## [An adaptive congestion\-aware graph neural routing framework with hybrid microcoded event\-driven control for network\-on\-chip systems](../publications/0001c63f6c59d1d15822.md)

sushmitha veeraragavan; R\. Manjith

Network\-on\-Chip \(NoC\) architectures have become a fundamental communication backbone for many\-core processors, artificial intelligence accelerators, edge\-computing platforms, and high\-performance embedded systems\. However, achieving efficient packet routing in large\-scale NoCs remains challenging due to dynamic traffic variations, congestion propagation, limited global network visibility, and stringent hardware constraints\. Conventional deterministic and heuristic routing algorithms suffer from reduced adaptability under non\-uniform traffic conditions, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning \(DRL\)\-based routers primarily rely on local state representations and finite\-state\-machine \(FSM\) controllers, limiting their scalability, topology awareness, and hardware deployability\. To address these limitations, this work proposes an Adaptive Congestion\-Aware Graph Neural Routing Framework with Hybrid Microcoded Event\-Driven Control for Network\-on\-Chip Systems\. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: \(i\) an Adaptive Congestion\-Aware Graph Neural Network \(ACA\-GNN\) encoder that generates compact topology\-aware embeddings by capturing local and multi\-hop congestion dependencies through congestion\-aware message propagation, \(ii\) a quantized Deep Reinforcement Learning \(DRL\) agent that performs low\-latency adaptive routing decisions using compact graph embeddings, and \(iii\) a Hybrid Microcoded Event\-Driven Controller \(H\-µEDC\) that replaces conventional FSM\-based control with programmable event\-triggered micro\-routines to ensure deterministic routing execution\. The proposed architecture is implemented on a Xilinx Zynq\-7000 FPGA and evaluated using BookSim2 cycle\-accurate simulation, Orion 3\.0 power modeling, synthetic traffic patterns, and PARSEC/Rodinia benchmark workloads\. Experimental results demonstrate up to 48% lower packet latency, and 31% lower energy per flit compared with state\-of\-the\-art heuristic and machine\-learning\-based routing approaches\. Hardware implementation further requires only 1\.2% LUTs, 1\.4% flip\-flops, three DSP blocks, one BRAM, and 0\.556 W power consumption while maintaining deterministic single\-cycle routing decisions using cached ACA\-GNN embeddings\. These results demonstrate that the proposed ACA\-GNN\-HµEDC framework effectively combines topology\-aware routing intelligence, congestion adaptivity, hardware efficiency, and scalability, making it a practical solution for next\-generation many\-core Network\-on\-Chip systems\.

## [Digital transformation of the ERP environment in company X using a Greenfield implementation of SAP S/4HANA](../publications/0005bd596e1722ecf247.md)

Nino Antonin Polajner

Digitalna preobrazba organizacij predstavlja enega ključnih izzivov sodobnega poslovnega okolja, pri čemer imajo celovite informacijske rešitve \(ERP\) pomembno vlogo pri povezovanju poslovnih procesov, izboljševanju učinkovitosti poslovanja in podpori odločanju\. Zaradi zaključka rednega vzdrževanja rešitve SAP ECC se številne organizacije soočajo s prehodom na rešitev SAP S/4HANA, ki predstavlja novo generacijo ERP rešitev in omogoča sodobnejšo arhitekturo, analitiko v realnem času ter podporo digitalni preobrazbi\. Magistrsko delo obravnava implementacijo ERP rešitve SAP S/4HANA s pristopom Greenfield\. V teoretičnem delu so predstavljeni razvoj ERP rešitev, primerjava sistemov SAP ECC in SAP S/4HANA, migracijski pristopi ter ključni dejavniki uspešne implementacije\. Posebna pozornost je namenjena metodologiji SAP Activate, konceptu Clean Core in platformi SAP Business Technology Platform\. Empirični del temelji na študiji primera podjetja X, ki izvaja prehod z rešitve SAP ECC na SAP S/4HANA\. Analiza je pokazala, da uspešna implementacija ni odvisna zgolj od tehnične izvedbe projekta, temveč predvsem od učinkovitega upravljanja organizacijskih sprememb, aktivnega vključevanja ključnih uporabnikov, standardizacije poslovnih procesov in omejevanja nepotrebnih prilagoditev sistema\. Ugotovitve potrjujejo, da pristop Greenfield skupaj z metodologijo SAP Activate in načelom Clean Core predstavlja ustrezno podlago za dolgoročno vzdržnost ERP rešitve ter učinkovitejšo digitalno preobrazbo organizacij\.

## [PharmAI: domain\-specific QA generation by adaptive learning and fine\-tuning of small language models](../publications/00062578d7d037501886.md)

Shenbagarajan Anantharajan; Saranraj Loganathan; Rajkumaran Soundarraj; E Emerson Nithiyaraj

Background Domain\-specific medical question\-answering \(QA\) models face bottlenecks due to scarce labeled data, specialized terminology, and constrained computational hardware\. Objectives The study aims to develop an efficient pharmaceutical question\-answering \(QA\) system that can be trained and deployed on consumer\-grade hardware using Small Language Models \(SLMs\)\. Materials and methods The pipeline processes four pharmaceutical textbooks containing 3,977 total pages, producing 7,370 semantically similar text chunks and 2,144 synthetic QA pairs under four questioning categories: definition, mechanism, comparison, and clinical application\. Three Small Language Models \(SLMs\), namely SmolLM2\-1\.7B\-Instruct, Qwen2\.5–1\.5B\-Instruct, and Llama\-3\.2–1B\-Instruct, are fine\-tuned under the same QLoRA \(Quantized Low\-Rank Adaptation\) configurations and then evaluated with retrieval metrics \(Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank\) and generation metrics \(ROUGE\-1/2/L, Semantic Similarity, BERTScore\)\. Architectural decisions including NF4 4\-bit quantization, CPU\-based FAISS indexing, and completion\-only loss masking are implemented due to hardware constraints and validated via ablation analysis\. Results SmolLM2\-1\.7B\-Instruct, Qwen2\.5–1\.5B\-Instruct, and Llama\-3\.2–1B\-Instruct demonstrated identical retrieval performance, achieving a Recall@1 of 0\.517, Recall@3 of 0\.732, Recall@5 of 0\.797, and an MRR of 0\.628\. Similarly, the generation performance evaluation revealed that Qwen2\.5–1\.5B FT outperformed the other fine\-tuned SLMs, achieving the highest scores across all metrics \(ROUGE\-1 = 0\.47, ROUGE\-2 = 0\.25, ROUGE\-L = 0\.38, and BERTScore = 0\.72\)\. In comparison, SmolLM2\-1\.7B FT and Llama\-3\.2–1B FT exhibited comparable performance, with ROUGE\-1 scores of approximately 0\.35, ROUGE\-2 scores of 0\.16–0\.17, ROUGE\-L scores of 0\.25–0\.26, and BERTScores of 0\.66, indicating lower lexical and semantic alignment with the reference outputs than Qwen2\.5–1\.5B FT\. Conclusion We evaluate retrieval and generation performance using comprehensive metric suites, incorporating a category\-wise breakdown that reveals comparison questions to be the most challenging for single\-passage retrieval architectures\.

## [Marked preoperative regression of biopsy\-diagnosed microsatellite instability\-high colon adenocarcinoma with a small residual traditional serrated adenoma: A case report](../publications/00159b07a301772e433d.md)

Kazuhito Minami; Hiroki Funakoshi; Kazuhito Minami; Yumi Oshiro; Yoshiaki Nozaka; Shinjiro Egashira

Introduction: Marked regression of colorectal cancer before surgery is extremely rare\. Microsatellite instability\-high \(MSI\-high\) tumors are characterized by a high neoantigen burden and pronounced immunogenicity\. Biopsy\-associated tissue injury may induce local inflammatory and reparative responses; whether these responses can augment antitumor immunity in an immunogenic tumor microenvironment remains uncertain\. We report a case of MSI\-high colorectal adenocarcinoma that markedly regressed after biopsy, with no residual carcinoma identified in the resected specimen\. The temporal and histopathologic findings raise the possibility of an interplay between biopsy\-associated tissue injury and the intrinsic immunogenicity of an MSI\-high tumor\. Case Report: Initial colonoscopy in a man in his 70s identified an ascending colon lesion consisting of a protruded component and a shallow depressed component\. Magnifying endoscopy demonstrated irregular vascular and surface patterns corresponding to Japan NBI Expert Team \(JNET\) type 2B, together with a type Vi pit pattern, raising suspicion of submucosal invasion\. Biopsy specimens obtained from the lesion revealed moderately to well\-differentiated adenocarcinoma\. Polymerase chain reaction \(PCR\)\-based MSI testing of the biopsy specimen demonstrated MSI\-high status\. Follow\-up colonoscopy performed 36 days later showed regression of the protruded component\. Laparoscopic ileocecal resection \(LIR\) with lymph node dissection was performed 77 days after the initial diagnosis\. Macroscopically, only a small protruded lesion measuring approximately 3 mm remained at approximately the same longitudinal level as the tattoo but several centimeters away along the colonic wall\. Histopathologic examination revealed a 3\-mm traditional serrated adenoma \(TSA\) with low\-grade dysplasia, accompanied by prominent submucosal fibrosis in the presumed tumor bed\. No viable adenocarcinoma was identified despite extensive additional sectioning\. Moderate lymphocytic infiltration accompanied by lymphoid follicle formation was observed within the presumed tumor bed\. Conclusion: Although the underlying mechanism cannot be definitively established, the interval endoscopic regression observed after biopsy and the absence of residual carcinoma in the resected specimen are consistent with a possible regression process\. However, complete mechanical removal of the malignant component during biopsy or changes resulting from procedure\-related tissue injury cannot be excluded\. The MSI\-high status and lymphocytic infiltration with lymphoid follicle formation provide a plausible immunologic context, but the contribution of an immune\-mediated mechanism remains speculative\.

## [KRIPTO\-AKTIVLAR AYLANMASI VA MAYNING SOHASIDAGI JINOIY QILMISHLAR SUBYEKTIV TOMONINING XUSUSIYATLARI](../publications/001a884a3a6760bf9109.md)

Baxtiyor Primov

Mazkur maqolada O‘zbekiston Respublikasi Jinoyat kodeksining 2788\-moddasi \(kripto\-aktivlar aylanmasi sohasidagi qonunchilikni buzish\) va 2789\-moddasida \(mayning faoliyatini qonunga xilof ravishda amalga oshirish\) nazarda tutilgan jinoyatlar subyektiv tomonining nazariy va amaliy xususiyatlari tadqiq etilgan\. Jinoyat kodeksining 21\-moddasi hamda mazkur moddalar dispozitsiyalarining tuzilishi tahlili asosida ushbu jinoyatlar formal tarkibli bo‘lib, faqat qasddan sodir etilishi, ularda egri qasd va ehtiyotsizlik shakllari istisno etilishi asoslab berilgan\. Jinoyat huquqi doktrinasidagi klassik va intellektual\-texnologik yondashuvlar hamda «texnik ehtiyotsizlik» modeli qiyosiy o‘rganilgan, «kod hukmronligi» \(Rule of Code\) g‘oyasini jinoiy qasdni isbotlashga mexanik ravishda tatbiq etish tanqidiy baholangan\. Anonim kripto\-aktivlar va yashirin mayning belgilarining subyektiv tomondagi aksi ochib berilib, muallifning «Ikki bosqichli intellektual ayb» \(Two\-tier Digital Culpability\) konsepsiyasi ilgari surilgan\. Shuningdek, jinoiy qasdni isbotlovchi intellektual\-vositaviy yuridik markerlar tizimi ishlab chiqilgan, aybsiz holda zarar yetkazishni \(kazusni\) jinoiy qasddan ajratish mezonlari hamda JK 2788\-moddasini takomillashtirish bo‘yicha taklif asoslab berilgan\.

## [A framework for assessing quality indicators in animal cancer registries: a case study](../publications/001d0088abc724b49dd6.md)

Marta Cresci; Francesca Cito; Antonio Petrini; Giovanni Di Teodoro; Marina Baffoni; Giuseppe Ru; Maria Ines Crescio

Introduction Animal cancer registries \(ACRs\) are becoming increasingly important in veterinary oncology and within the One Health framework\. However, no standardized framework currently exists to assess their quality comprehensively\. This study developed a structured quality assessment framework by adapting internationally recognized standards for human cancer registries with the aim of providing data managers of animal cancer registries, as well as those involved in establishing new ACRs, with a tool to support the evaluation of registry activities\. Methods A systematized literature review identified 16 quality indicators organized into six domains: registry organization, data sources, comparability, validity, timeliness, and completeness\. As a proof of concept, the framework was applied to the Abruzzo \(Italy\) ACR\. Results All indicators were measurable using routinely collected registry data, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed approach and enabling a comprehensive evaluation of registry performance across all six quality domains\. Discussion Although further validation in different registry configuration is warranted, this framework provides a practical foundation for standardized quality assessment, benchmarking, and the harmonization of animal cancer registries\.

## [RCNNricePPI: leveraging deep learning to predict rice protein\-protein interactions for climate\-responsive agriculture](../publications/0039d8fd305f19dcb89b.md)

Neeraj Budhlakoti; Nitesh Kumar Sharma; Sharanbasappa D Madival; Anshuman Singh; Sudhir Srivastava; Dwijesh Chandra Mishra; Mahender Kumar Singh; Atul Kumar; Girish Kumar Jha

Protein\-protein interactions \(PPIs\) are fundamental to cellular regulation, metabolism and stress\-response pathways in rice, but experimentally characterized interaction networks remain incomplete\. Here, we present RCNNricePPI, a sequence\-based deep learning framework for rice PPI prediction that combines word2vec\-derived amino acid embedding with a Siamese recurrent convolutional neural network integrating convolutional and bidirectional gated recurrent units\. Rice PPIs data were curated from publicly available interaction resources, followed by removal of self\-interactions, redundant pairs and low quality sequence\. To reduce protein\-level information leakage, model development and evaluation were performed using a protein\-aware partitioning strategy, including protein disjoint five\-fold cross\-validation and an independent held\-out test set\. At a classification threshold of 0\.40, RCNNricePPI achieved an accuracy of 0\.8996, balanced accuracy of 0\.7451 and AUROC of 0\.8295, compared with a baseline logistic regression values of 0\.6459, 0\.6964, 0\.7820 respectively\. Performance was further assessed based protein novelty, with AUROC values of 0\.9259, 0\.7995 and 0\.7340 for both\-seen, one\-unseen and both\-unseen protein pairs, respectively\. Architectural ablation and conventional machine learning comparisons further supported the contribution of the integrated architecture\. RCNNricePPI is implemented as an accessible web\-based resource and provides a framework for prioritizing candidate interactions for subsequent experimental investigation\. The RCNNricePPI is freely available at riceppi\.biodb\.in \.

## [Reuse of rod spatial structures for children’s playgrounds betterment](../publications/004013d6ecd4a2c1db89.md)

Erik Schneider; Lyazzat Tuleuvna Nurkusheva; Turar Uzakbayev; Bolat Kuspangaliyev; Константин Самойлов

The disadvantage of most of children&\#x27;s playgrounds is the inability to fully use them during afternoon sun and in the rain\. Frequently used small gazebos and canopies only allow you to hide from the rain or the sun\. A full\-fledged game is impossible\. The optimal solution, apparently, is to build pavilions that are high enough for a full\-fledged game and provide a roof over most of the playing space\. An analysis of various solutions has shown that recombined elements of disassembled collapsible rod spatial structures can used for this purpose\. These widespread structures used in large\-span buildings and usually fail after several cycles of operation\. The proposed continuation of their use increases their asset turnover\. Pavilions built from these structures provide an opportunity to continue the games in the afternoon sun and in the rain\. The strength and spatial rigidity of these structures makes it possible to attach various amusement rides and lighting equipment to them\. The article presents a conceptual design solution\. This solution solves some of the problems of ensuring sustainable development by saving energy and reducing costs, as it ensures the reuse of dismantled structures\. The solution is almost universal for different regions\. The proposed solution should be seen as a conceptually new application of existing systems\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NA APRENDIZAGEM BASEADA EM PROBLEMAS \(PBL\) NA EDUCAÇÃO MÉDICA: EVIDÊNCIAS DE UMA REVISÃO NARRATIVA](../publications/004c01a764f108a3f054.md)

Letícia Jochem

Introdução e objetivo: A Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas \(PBL\) é amplamente utilizada na educação médica por favorecer o raciocínio clínico, a aprendizagem autodirigida e a resolução de problemas\. Entretanto, sua implementação demanda tempo e preparo docente para elaboração de casos e condução das tutorias\. Nesse contexto, a inteligência artificial \(IA\) generativa emerge como ferramenta capaz de apoiar a construção de cenários clínicos, oferecer feedback em tempo real e ampliar as possibilidades de aprendizagem¹,²\. O objetivo deste trabalho foi sintetizar as evidências disponíveis sobre o uso da inteligência artificial generativa na Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas \(PBL\) na educação médica, destacando seus potenciais benefícios, desafios e implicações para a formação de estudantes de medicina e médicos residentes\.Método: Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura\. Foi realizada busca estruturada na base de dados PubMed, utilizando os descritores “Artificial intelligence”, “medical students” e “Problem\-based learning”, combinados pelo operador booleano AND\. A busca foi realizada em junho de 2026, com recorte temporal a partir de 2020\. Foram identificados 93 estudos, dos quais 11 atenderam aos critérios definidos e compuseram a análise\. Foram incluídos estudos relacionados à aplicação de IA na Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas \(PBL\) ou em outras metodologias ativas, com foco em estudantes de medicina ou residentes, sendo excluídos aqueles sem relação com educação médica ou PBL, além de trabalhos estritamente técnicos e duplicados\.Resultados: A análise dos 11 estudos identificou evidências de que diferentes modelos de IA generativa, como ChatGPT e DeepSeek, podem favorecer o desempenho acadêmico e o raciocínio clínico de estudantes de medicina\. Alguns estudos, desenvolvidos em áreas como hematologia e nefrologia, demonstraram que estudantes que utilizaram apoio de IA apresentaram melhores resultados em avaliações teóricas e maior desempenho no julgamento clínico quando comparados aos métodos tradicionais¹,²\. Além disso, um dos estudos sugeriu redução das diferenças de desempenho entre estudantes com distintos níveis de conhecimento prévio³\. Por outro lado, também foram identificados desafios relacionados ao uso dessa tecnologia\. Em alguns contextos, os estudantes utilizam a IA de forma passiva, apenas para obter respostas prontas, reduzindo o esforço cognitivo e podendo comprometer o processo de aprendizagem⁴\. Assim, o uso adequado da IA no PBL depende de uma abordagem ativa, que estimule o debate e o raciocínio crítico\. Também foi observado que o ensino sobre ética em IA contribui para que os estudantes compreendam as limitações da tecnologia, incluindo possíveis erros, vieses e respostas imprecisas, promovendo uma postura mais crítica e segura em sua utilização na prática médica⁵\.Conclusão: A IA generativa apresenta potencial para qualificar o PBL, favorecendo o desempenho acadêmico, o raciocínio clínico e a personalização da aprendizagem\. Entretanto, sua utilização deve ocorrer de forma ética e supervisionada, de modo a estimular o pensamento crítico e evitar a dependência tecnológica\. Estudos adicionais são necessários para avaliar seus impactos a longo prazo na formação médica\.

## [Size and geometry effects on the flow\-rate–torque trade\-off of a drainage impeller in a submerged mechanical defoamer](../publications/0054454f53a2044af979.md)

Fan Wang; Youqiang Jiang; Youjie Qiu; Wei Liu; Yangyang Huai

Abstract Rotating drainage impellers must balance suction\-driven flow against shaft loading, yet which geometric parameters govern this flow\-rate–torque trade\-off remains poorly established\. This work addresses this question for the drainage impeller of a submerged mechanical defoamer, focusing on the single\-phase hydrodynamics underlying froth capture rather than directly modelling foam rupture\. Thirty configurations spanning four geometric parameters — blade number Z, impeller diameter D, impeller height H and blade outlet angle β — were generated by maximin orthogonal Latin hypercube sampling and evaluated by three\-dimensional steady\-state CFD for drainage flow rate and torque\. Gaussian\-process surrogates with leave\-one\-out cross\-validation then supported conditional\-response analysis, Sobol sensitivity indices and surrogate\-based multi\-objective Bayesian optimization\. The results show that impeller diameter dominates the dimensional responses, with first\-order Sobol indices of 0\.91 for flow rate and 0\.96 for torque\. After dimensional normalization removes the leading size\-scaling effects, diameter still governs the flow coefficient, whereas impeller height emerges as the principal secondary factor for the torque coefficient, indicating that size mainly sets the operating point while the residual geometry modulates the normalized loading\. A representative Pareto compromise design \(Z = 8, D = 81\.11 mm, H = 30 mm, β = 120°\) was verified by CFD within 6% of the surrogate predictions; relative to the original impeller it raises the flow rate by 25\.5%, a gain attributable mainly to the enlarged diameter rather than to improve dimensionless flow capacity\. Water experiments at 1000 rev/min confirmed the CFD predictions for both impellers, with flow\-rate deviations within 5% and torque deviations within 10%\. Flow\-field analysis relates the higher throughput to an enlarged suction\-related low\-pressure region, smoother blade\-passage flow and reduced local wake dissipation\. The framework provides a practical basis for drainage\-impeller design and, more generally, for separating size and geometry effects in CFD\-based optimization under limited simulation budgets\.

## [DeciCAD: Harness\-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents](../publications/0060aaefb0733994053b.md)

Yufeng Peng; Yixin Zhang; Ziyi Liu; Zhikun Xu; Jiarong Yang; Sijie Wang; Wenjie Feng; Qiyu Kang

Large Language Model agents operate through closed\-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness\. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer\-aided design \(CAD\), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long\-horizon procedures\. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain\-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision\-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions\. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine\-tuning \(SFT\) and geometry\-grounded online reinforcement learning \(RL\)\. Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union \(IoU\) while reducing model\-output tokens by 45\-\-88% relative to a general\-purpose coding harness\. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0\.6883 to 0\.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66\.5% to 73\.5% and F1 to 0\.7880\. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD\.

## [Developing Criteria and Indicators for Assessing Students’ Knowledge in a Digital Educational Environment](../publications/0061b49c74aeb2d17f36.md)

Urmat Moldosanov

The digital transformation of higher education requires the development of assessment systems capable of measuring not only the amount of knowledge acquired by students but also their ability to understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, and create information in technology\-mediated contexts\. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing criteria and indicators for assessing students’ knowledge in a digital educational environment\. The study employs systematic analysis, comparison, classification, synthesis, and pedagogical modelling\. The proposed framework includes six assessment criteria: conceptual knowledge, comprehension and interpretation, practical application, analytical and problem\-solving ability, knowledge integration and creation, and reflective and self\-regulated learning\. Each criterion is operationalised through measurable qualitative and quantitative indicators\. A four\-level assessment scale — advanced, proficient, developing, and insufficient — is introduced to improve transparency and consistency\. The article also proposes a weighted formula for calculating an integrated student knowledge score\. Particular attention is given to validity, reliability, fairness, transparency, accessibility, academic integrity, and the pedagogically responsible use of learning analytics and artificial intelligence\. The findings indicate that digital assessment becomes educationally meaningful when assessment tasks are aligned with learning outcomes, indicators are observable and measurable, students receive timely feedback, and automated data are combined with professional teacher judgement\. The proposed framework may be adapted to different university disciplines, learning management systems, and blended or fully online educational programmes\.

## [TransCRC\-XAI: Source Code and Jupyter Notebook for Colorectal Cancer Molecular Stratification and Biomarker Discovery](../publications/006bd5115a741beb324f.md)

Waleed Mahmoud Ead

This repository provides the Python implementation and Jupyter notebook associated with TransCRC\-XAI, an explainable machine learning framework developed for patient\-specific transcriptomic analysis, molecular stratification, and biomarker discovery in colorectal cancer \(CRC\)\. The framework integrates paired tumor normal gene expression analysis, patient\-specific differential expression, a Transition Stability Score \(TSS\), dimensionality reduction, molecular transition phenotype \(MTP\) discovery, and explainable machine learning to investigate heterogeneous molecular alterations associated with colorectal cancer\. The computational workflow includes data preprocessing, paired expression\-difference construction, stability\-based feature assessment, molecular phenotype identification, predictive modeling, and SHAP\-based feature interpretation\. The framework also incorporates a Patient Molecular Transition Score \(PMTS\) and pathway\-level analysis to support the biological interpretation of patient\-specific molecular alterations\. The research workflow is designed around two publicly accessible transcriptomic datasets: GSE44076: Discovery dataset containing matched colorectal tumor and adjacent\-normal expression profiles\. GSE39582: Independent external dataset intended for evaluating the generalizability of selected transcriptomic signatures\. The repository is intended to support methodological transparency, reproducibility, and further research in explainable artificial intelligence, computational oncology, precision medicine, and transcriptomic biomarker discovery\. Keywords: Colorectal Cancer; TransCRC\-XAI; Explainable Artificial Intelligence; Transcriptomics; Biomarker Discovery; Molecular Stratification; Patient\-Specific Analysis; SHAP; Machine Learning; Precision Oncology\.

## [Public Sector Reforms and Sustainable Enterprise Development: Nigeria’s Quest for Sustainable Economic Development](../publications/0083ebf481a6fbd65fa7.md)

Chibuzo Charles Nwosu; Dike C\. Obalum; Mathias Ozoemena Ananti

Public sector reform is essential for fostering sustainable enterprise development and inclusive economic growth in developing economies, particularly in Nigeria\. Various reform initiatives have aimed to enhance institutional effectiveness, regulatory efficiency, public service delivery, and create a better environment for business and investment\. However, persistent challenges such as policy inconsistency, weak institutional capacity, corruption, and inadequate funding hinder successful reform implementation and enterprise sustainability\. This study explores the relationship between public sector reform and sustainable enterprise development in Nigeria by examining historical reform efforts, institutional changes, and contemporary governance initiatives\. Guided by Institutional Theory, it posits that strong, transparent, and accountable public institutions are crucial for nurturing sustainable business ecosystems and economic resilience\. The study highlights the impact of public sector reforms on enterprise sustainability and development\. In conclusion, it emphasizes that effective public sector institutions and governance reforms are vital for sustainable development and competitiveness, recommending policy continuity, capacity strengthening, enhanced transparency, institutional autonomy, and sustainable financing mechanisms\.

## [Analisis Sentimen Program MBG Sebelum Dan Sesudah Implementasi Pada Platform X Dan Tiktok Menggunakan SVM](../publications/009880608be0522ba4de.md)

Ismail Akbar Rosiqin; Deni Arifianto; Reni Umilasari

Program Makan Bergizi Gratis \(MBG\) merupakan kebijakan pemerintah Indonesia untuk menanggulangi stunting melalui penyediaan asupan gizi\. Sebagai program nasional, MBG memunculkan beragam respons publik yang banyak disampaikan melalui media sosial\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis perubahan sentimen publik sebelum dan setelah implementasi MBG pada platform X dan TikTok, serta mengevaluasi kinerja metode Support Vector Machine \(SVM\)\. Data dikumpulkan melalui scraping menggunakan tagar \#MakanSiangGratis, \#MakanBergiziGratis, dan \#MBG, dengan total 4\.000 data pada masing\-masing platform untuk periode sebelum dan sesudah implementasi\. Tahapan penelitian meliputi pelabelan sentimen, preprocessing, pembobotan TF\-IDF, dan klasifikasi menggunakan SVM dengan evaluasi K\-Fold Cross Validation\. Hasil menunjukkan perbedaan pola sentimen setelah implementasi\. Pada platform X, sentimen negatif meningkat dan positif menurun, sedangkan di TikTok sentimen positif tetap dominan meskipun netral dan negatif meningkat\. Secara keseluruhan, SVM menunjukkan kinerja yang baik dan stabil dengan tingkat akurasi tinggi, serta memberikan kontribusi akademik dalam kajian analisis sentimen kebijakan publik di media sosial\.Kata kunci: Analisis Sentimen; MBG; Platform TikTok; Platform X; Support Vector Machine

## [A Systematic Intracranial Exposure‐Response Evaluation of Brain‐Penetrant Inhibitors: Informing Dose Selection for Brain Metastases](../publications/009dfec40e33e81f9d66.md)

Yuqian Zhao; Weize Huang

ABSTRACT Brain metastases \(BMs\) represent a major clinical challenge due to their high incidence in cancers such as non‐small cell lung cancer \(NSCLC\) and breast cancer, and the limited efficacy of systemic therapies resulting from inadequate drug penetration across the blood–brain barrier\. Although several brain‐penetrant tyrosine kinase inhibitors \(TKIs\) have been developed, the quantitative relationship between intracranial drug exposure and intracranial clinical response has not been well established, leaving an important gap in dose selection strategies\. In this study, we systematically evaluated the intracranial exposure‐response relationship across brain‐penetrant small‐molecule TKIs\. Fourteen TKIs were identified based on guideline‐recommended therapies for BMs\. For each drug, plasma and cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) pharmacokinetic profiles were simulated using published population pharmacokinetic models, with CSF exposures extrapolated using known unbound plasma fractions and CSF‐to‐plasma unbound concentration ratios \( K p,uu,CSF \) in humans\. Key intracranial exposure metrics, including the CSF steady‐state trough and average concentrations relative to IC 50 \( C min,ss /IC 50 and C ave,ss /IC 50 \) and the percentage of the steady‐state dosing interval during which CSF concentrations remained above IC 50 \(T% &gt; IC 50 \), were derived and correlated with intracranial outcomes from published clinical studies\. Overall, significant positive correlations were observed between intracranial exposure metrics and both intracranial objective response rate \(ORR\) and complete response rate \(CR\)\. Greater exposure coverage above IC 50 was associated with improved intracranial efficacy\. This work demonstrates a positive intracranial exposure‐response relationship across brain‐penetrant TKIs and provides a quantitative benchmark to inform dose selection beyond traditional plasma exposure metrics\. These findings highlight the importance of achieving sufficient CNS drug concentrations to optimize the therapeutic effect in patients with BMs\.

## [Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence\-Assisted Metaphase Finder for Clinical Cytogenetic Application](../publications/00a4bdfd5c06ff1cd02a.md)

Bilinda J\. Dawson; Christy A\. Prongay; Tori B\. Strapp; Lynne S\. Rosenblum

Background/Objectives: Clinical cytogenetics has benefited from artificial intelligence \(AI\) integration into digital karyotyping systems for segmentation and classification of chromosomes\. Metaphase image identification and capture utilize traditional metaphase finder classifiers whose specificity can be improved, especially where lowered detection thresholds for low\-mitotic\-index specimens result in higher debris selection\. Use of AI to reliably detect metaphases at 10× magnification may resolve this issue\. This study compares a new AI\-based metaphase finder algorithm to the conventional non\-AI classifier\. Methods: G\-banded slides from 105 normal and abnormal peripheral blood \(PB\) and bone marrow \(BM\) specimens were scanned at 10× magnification and images were captured at 100× using the HiBand system \(Applied Spectral Imaging\), once with the automatic metaphase finder and again using the AI\-assisted algorithm\. The number of real metaphases versus debris, for up to 100 captured images per slide, and quality metrics were compared using both applications\. Results: True metaphase detection in BM specimens averaged 77\.3 ± 21\.6 versus 82\.5 ± 19\.9 \(6\.3% increase\) for normal cases and 72\.1 ± 18\.5 versus 89\.7 ± 14\.2 \(14\.6% increase\) for abnormal cases comparing the non\-AI and AI classifiers, respectively\. There was no difference for normal PB cases \(97\.6 ± 1\.5 versus 97\.1 ± 2\.9\) and a 2\.6% decrease for abnormal PB cases \(97\.9 ± 2\.2 versus 95\.4 ± 4\.2\) between the two classifiers\. All cases demonstrated comparable image quality\. Conclusions: This study demonstrates that the AI\-assisted metaphase finder improves true metaphase capture compared to the non\-AI classifier for BM while maintaining high fidelity for PB specimens\. These findings contribute to the expanding literature on integration of AI in clinical cytogenetics\.

## [Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality](../publications/00a5dc3f051185c18880.md)

Niclas Göring; Shuofeng Zhang; Branton DeMoss; Ard A\. Louis

We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on their last hidden layer representations\. By evaluating representation quality with a parameter\-free $k$\-nearest\-neighbor \($k$\-NN\) classifier, our certificate avoids traditional parameter\-space complexity measures, KL divergences to a posterior, weight norms, and compression\. The bound is tight: trained from scratch, it reaches an 8\.0 percentage point gap to test error on CIFAR\-10 \(ResNet\-18\) and yields the first non\-vacuous certificates we are aware of on CIFAR\-100; with frozen DINOv2 representations, it certifies at 1\.4\\% on CIFAR\-10 and 23\.1\\% on 1,000\-class ImageNet\. It decomposes additively into three empirical, independently measurable quantities: local class geometry \($k$\-NN decoder error\), decoder\-network agreement, and training stability\. This allows the bound to act as a diagnostic tool: we demonstrate that actively destroying local class geometry eliminates generalization while leaving dataset memorization intact, identifying class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization\. Finally, we show that learned representations are significantly less sensitive to weight noise than linear readouts, suggesting why parameter\-space certificates often struggle to remain tight\.

## [Where Does the AI Time Dividend Go? Generative AI, Work Intensification, and Work\-Life Balance](../publications/00ac5271b43ea48c7bfc.md)

Dong Yao

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) can accelerate knowledge\-work tasks, but task\-level efficiency does not necessarily translate into shorter working hours or improved employee welfare\. This article proposes an AI time\-dividend allocation framework that separates the creation of saved time from its subsequent use\. Drawing on the job demands–resources perspective, it examines a resource pathway through perceived time savings and work–life balance alongside a competing demand pathway through work intensification\. The reported three\-wave observational survey comprises 472 complete cases\. Standardized ordinary least squares models with HC3 robust standard errors indicate that GenAI use intensity is associated with perceived time savings \(β = \.495, p &lt; \.001\)\. Time savings is positively associated with work–life balance \(β = \.255, p &lt; \.001\), whereas work intensification is negatively associated with work–life balance \(β = −\.443, p &lt; \.001\)\. Reported bootstrap indirect effects are positive through time savings \(0\.126, 95% CI \[0\.079, 0\.176\]\) and negative through time savings and work intensification \(−0\.036, 95% CI \[−0\.059, −0\.015\]\)\. Performance pressure is positively associated with intensification, but its proposed interaction with time savings is not statistically significant\. The findings are consistent with competing allocation pathways; given the observational design, they should not be interpreted as causal effects\. The article identifies time\-dividend allocation as a consequential dimension of AI\-enabled work design\.

## [EFEITO DO ÓLEO A BASE DE CANABIDIOL SOBRE COMPORTAMENTOS TIPO DEPRESSIVOS E NEUROPROTEÇÃO EM ANIMAIS SUBMETIDOS A ESTRESSE NA INFÂNCIA](../publications/00adc7a74effaa30c7be.md)

Nicoly Glembotzky; MAIQUELI EDUARDA DAMA MINGOTI; KELLI MARIA KREUZ; AMANDA GOLLO BERTOLLO; Marieli Philippsen; Hans Fiedler Bastos Rievers; Rafaella Peixoto Abreu da Silva; FERNANDA PILATTI; Laysa Anacleto Schuh; ZULEIDE MARIA IGNÁCIO

O Transtorno Depressivo Maior \(TDM\) está associado à exposição ao estresse durante o desenvolvimento, podendo provocar alterações comportamentais e neurobiológicas persistentes\. Este estudo investigou o efeito do canabidiol \(CBD\) sobre comportamentos tipo depressivos e os níveis de BDNF no hipocampo de ratos machos submetidos à privação maternal \(PM\) e ao isolamento social \(IS\)\. Foram utilizados ratos Wistar distribuídos em grupos controle, estresse \+ veículo, estresse \+ escitalopram \(10 mg/kg\) e estresse \+ CBD \(30 mg/kg\), tratados por gavagem durante 14 dias\. Os comportamentos foram avaliados pelos testes de campo aberto e natação forçada, enquanto os níveis de BDNF foram analisados no hipocampo\. O estresse promoveu aumento significativo do tempo de imobilidade no teste de natação forçada \(F = 4,503; p = 0,0062\), indicando comportamento tipo depressivo\. O tratamento com CBD reduziu significativamente a imobilidade, sem alterações na atividade locomotora\. Entretanto, os níveis de BDNF foram reduzidos no grupo estressado tratado com veículo em comparação ao controle \(p = 0,0164\), e nenhum tratamento promoveu reversão significativa\. Os resultados indicam que o CBD apresenta potencial efeito tipo antidepressivo diante do estresse precoce, embora seus mecanismos neurobiológicos ainda necessitem de investigação\.

## [Strategi Operasi Keamanan Laut di Selat Malaka Melalui Peningkatan Maritime Domain Awareness dalam Rangka Mendukung Tugas TNI AL](../publications/00bd6522d47fef24ef2d.md)

Achmad Muzakki; Baharudin Anwar; Jamroji Dwi Wahono; Tohonan Evangelista Siagian

Selat Malaka merupakan jalur pelayaran internasional bernilai strategis tinggi yang kerap dihadapkan pada tingginya potensi kejahatan lintas negara dan modus dark vessels, sehingga menuntut keterpaduan deteksi serta efisiensi pengerahan unsur patroli TNI AL\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merumuskan strategi operasi keamanan laut di Selat Malaka melalui peningkatan Maritime Domain Awareness \(MDA\) guna mendukung tugas TNI AL\. Penelitian kualitatif deskriptif ini mengintegrasikan analisis perangkat lunak NVivo 12 Pro dan pemetaan matriks berbasis data wawancara mendalam dengan Narasumber yang berasal dari Kotama hingga Lanal\. Hasil pengolahan data NVivo 12 Pro mengungkap fenomena bahwa keberhasilan operasi sangat bergantung pada penguatan jaringan sensor pangkalan \(Koarmada, Kodaeral dan Lanal\), efektivitas analisis data Puskodal, serta kesiapan operasional unsur KRI/KAL\. ## [Study buddy learning is associated with academic success in undergraduate science courses](../publications/00c9790f1aea03fb2b98.md)

Achol Jones; Gabrielle Reznik; Al Rohet Hossain; Veronica Dudarev; Bowen Hui; Patrice Belleville; Warren Williams; Eden Fussner; James T\. Enns

for undergraduate science students\. The study tested three hypotheses: \(i\) Do students benefit academically from a formalized study buddy peer learning program? \(ii\) Do mentors and protégés benefit equally from participation in the study buddy program? \(iii\) Does heterogeneity in group members&\#x27; initial academic performance have an effect on benefits from participation in the study buddy program? To test these hypotheses, we implemented a cohort\-based study buddy program in which high\-scoring students \(mentors\) and lower\-scoring peers \(protégés\), following their first assessment scores in a given course, were invited to form study groups\. We compared the performance of participants versus non\-participants on subsequent assessments, while examining separately the effects for mentors and protégés\. Results showed \(i\) significant grade benefits for participants over non\-participants, \(ii\) similar participation benefits for students in mentor and protégé roles, and \(iii\) no interaction of competence\-based heterogeneity on these effects\. Although this study design was unable to assess the nature of the study buddy interactions, the grade performance data highlight the program as a cost\-effective and scalable approach to enhance students&\#x27; educational experiences\. The data also emphasize the value of reducing barriers to collaborative learning in higher education\.

## [Online prediction of fresh concrete workability via machine learning\-based assessment of mixing power curves](../publications/00cb49faa126c2794a9b.md)

Alexander Teichmann; M Haist

Concrete production control relies largely on operator expertise and manual material testing, which delivers results only after mixing, when adjustments are very limited\. This approach becomes insufficient for low\-CO 2 mixes and recycled aggregates, whose variable water demand increases rejection risk\. Consequently, online quality assessment based on process information acquired during mixing is required\. A signal readily available in modern plants is the mixer’s power draw over time, i\.e\., the mixing power curve \(MPC\), which reflects rheology\-related transitions and homogenization behavior\. However, current practice reduces this to a single end\-of\-mixing value, ignoring the information contained in the temporal evolution\. This study therefore proposes a long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) model to predict slump flow from the MPC augmented by mix composition data before the end of mixing\. The model was trained on a synthetic dataset comprising 500 randomized mix designs with mixing curves generated according to an empirically supported six\-stage mixing model\. Slump flow was assigned using a heuristic rule combining empirical relationships with mix proportions and an MPC\-derived process\-state descriptor\. Across all evaluated scenarios, the LSTM maintained high accuracy \( R 2 &gt; 0\.925 \)\. Without water\-content information, it retains an MAE of 1\.2 cm, 4\.1 cm lower compared to a baseline regression model, highlighting the information contained in the MPC beyond mix proportions and single end\-of\-mixing power values\. Within the simulated framework, the results show that the LSTM can reliably estimate fresh concrete workability during mixing, supporting its use as a soft sensor for online quality assessment based on the already available mixing power signal\.

## [Investigating Pedestrian Safety Near Transit Bus Stops](../publications/00d523a546b944953ff4.md)

Tolulope Oke

This research examined how road and bus stop design and characteristics influence pedestrian safety, shaping both user perceptions and behaviors, and affecting crash outcomes near transit stops\. A three\-stage methodology integrated quantitative analysis with empirical field research\. The first stage involved a macro\-level quantitative analysis of factors contributing to pedestrian crashes, fusing together data on historical crash records, transit operations, demographic data, road inventories, and vehicle counts, and capturing over 300 crash\-relevant features\. Traditional and machine learning models were applied to classify bus stops and predict crash occurrence and severity\. The second stage focused on human factors through a micro\-level qualitative investigation, collecting public perceptions of safety through electronic surveys and comparing them with objective risk measures\. The third stage consisted of systematic field observations documenting pedestrian behaviors and assessing how environmental and design characteristics influence these behaviors\. By integrating objective crash modeling, subjective user perceptions, and observed behavior, the study developed a comprehensive framework for enhancing pedestrian safety\. The findings inform actionable design guidelines and policy recommendations, supporting Vision Zero objectives and guiding transit agency standards, municipal complete streets policies, and national street design manuals\.

## [When school feels unsafe: bullying victimization, school climate, and adolescent emotional well\-being](../publications/00d58d0b5eac89c93d20.md)

Millicent Aziku

The aim of the current study is to examine the relationships among bullying victimization, school safety, school belonging, teacher support, and emotional well\-being using data from the Programme for International Student Assessment \(PISA\) 2022 with 135,348 adolescents across 15 education systems\. The study utilized survey\-adjusted hierarchical regression analyses incorporating Balanced Repeated Replication \(BRR\) weights\. Results indicated that bullying victimization was significantly and negatively associated with adolescents’ emotional well\-being and perceived school safety\. Additionally, school safety and teacher support were positively correlated with school belonging, while school safety, school belonging, and teacher support were positively associated with emotional well\-being\. Regarding gender differences, the interaction analyses indicated that the association between bullying victimization and school belonging was stronger among female than male adolescents, while the bullying\-emotional well\-being association did not differ significantly by gender\. The findings emphasize the importance of fostering safe, supportive, and inclusive school environments in relation to adolescents’ emotional well\-being and experiences of bullying\.

## [Memória, prática pedagógica e identidade: uma análise bibliográfica da formação de professores que ensinam Matemática](../publications/00dd048975b04501a488.md)

Marisa de Oliveira Bruchez; Lucí Teresinha Marchiori dos Santos Bernardi

This study examines the relationship between memory, pedagogical practice, and identity, especially in the context of training teachers who teach mathematics in the early years of schooling\. It aims to analyze how individual and collective memories, constructed in childhood, school trajectory, and professional training, influence the constitution of pedagogical practice and the teaching identity of teachers who teach mathematics in the early years of schooling\. Methodologically, this is a qualitative, bibliographical, and analytical research\. The results indicate that memory, when problematized in formative processes, is configured as a relevant dimension in the constitution of professional identity and favors the construction of more reflective, empathetic, and committed pedagogical practices towards inclusive mathematics education in the early years of schooling\. It concludes that the critical incorporation of individual and collective memories in formative processes broadens the understanding of pedagogical practice and strengthens the construction of a more conscious, collaborative, and committed teaching practice in mathematics\.

## [Active Learning: A Strategy to Improve the Quality of Mathematics Learning](../publications/00e8a5c3530ac5e2e3c0.md)

Miyejav Ramos; Clarissa Anella Gravi

Active learning is often associated with increased student participation, yet its contribution to mathematics learning quality depends on whether participation generates substantive mathematical thinking\. This conceptual review develops an integrative framework explaining how active learning can support higher\-quality mathematics learning\. Relevant literature on active learning, mathematical activities, student engagement, teacher facilitation, and mathematics learning quality was synthesized to identify their conceptual relationships\. The synthesis conceptualizes active learning as a pedagogical orientation enacted through purposeful mathematical activities involving problem solving, representation, reasoning, communication, and reflection\. Student engagement functions as the core mechanism through which these activities become meaningful learning experiences, while teacher facilitation operates as a cross\-cutting condition that designs, supports, monitors, and adapts learning processes\. Mathematics learning quality is conceptualized as an emergent consequence reflected in deeper understanding, mathematical reasoning, problem solving, communication, representation, and meaningful application of knowledge\. The resulting framework integrates five interrelated components and five conceptual propositions\. Rather than proposing a fixed causal sequence, it represents a dynamic pedagogical system in which purposeful activity, sustained engagement, and responsive facilitation interact to create conditions for meaningful mathematical learning\. The framework offers a conceptual basis for designing active mathematics learning and guiding future empirical investigation\.

## [Beyond doomsday and infinity: reaching human boundaries in the age of AI: a viewpoint contribution for Kybernetes](../publications/00f46882d3b31f6a8045.md)

Stefan Güldenberg

Purpose This viewpoint contribution revisits Heinz von Foerster&\#x27;s famous “Doomsday” article in the context of the twenty\-first century transition toward artificial intelligence \(AI\), demographic stagnation and planetary boundaries\. While von Foerster, Mora and Amiot \(1960\) projected a singularity of population growth for the year 2026, the world has instead entered an age of AI characterized by declining population growth, diminishing human intelligence, decreasing productivity and increasing ecological as well as social stress\. This article argues that the contemporary challenge is no longer one of uncontrolled population expansion, but rather one of maintaining human flourishing, resilience, longevity and organizational intelligence\. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on second\-order cybernetics, systems theory, intellectual capital theory, organizational learning and humanistic management, the article proposes a shift from the industrial paradigm of quantitative growth toward a post\-industrial paradigm of qualitative growth and human flourishing\. Findings Human beings and human intelligence increasingly represent the scarcest resource in developed societies\. This paper develops three interrelated arguments: First, humanity in the age of AI is experiencing not only ecological boundaries but also human, institutional, social and societal boundaries\. Second, AI challenges simultaneously human intelligence as well as organizational productivity\. Third, future longevity depends less on maximizing efficiency and more on cultivating attentiveness, system thinking, organizational learning and human flourishing\. The paper concludes that von Foerster&\#x27;s legacy remains highly relevant because it redirects attention from deterministic forecasting towards system thinking and scenario planning\. Originality/value In the age of AI, the decisive question is no longer whether humanity reaches “doomsday,” but whether humanity can develop sufficiently intelligent organizations to avoid creating its own self\-fulfilling catastrophes\.

## [Machine learning om de prognose van multiple sclerose patiënten te modelleren](../publications/00f881432218299d9d80.md)

Robbe D’hondt

Multiple sclerosis is a neurological autoimmune disorder with onset typically in young adulthood, affecting millions of individuals worldwide\. Despite the existence of several disease\-modifying therapies, multiple sclerosis can still result in a severe reduction in quality of life\. This could be mitigated by administering the right treatment with appropriate efficacy to a patient as soon as possible, as early treatment can delay or even prevent long\-term disability accrual\. However, finding this patient\-treatment match is challenging, as the disease course is very heterogeneous and unpredictable, and the optimal treatment might not even exist yet\. Although several data\-driven prognostic models have been proposed, the field often focuses only on a single patient outcome represented in a binary classification problem\. Additionally, explainability and interpretation remains underexplored, which are crucial in the medical domain for trust in the system and accountability of decisions\. In this thesis, we aim to develop novel approaches for modeling prognosis in multiple sclerosis on the patient, group and population level\. On the patient level, we advance personalized prognosis for patients, by investigating alternatives to the currently dominant binary classification paradigm predicting whether patients will worsen in a fixed number of years\. On the group level, we investigate outcome\-informed patient stratification based on multiple time\-to\-event patient outcomes\. On the population level, we improve model and disease understanding, by using explainability techniques and interpreting their results\. Three new learning frameworks were developed\. First, we propose a multi\-target binning approach for modeling sparse sporadically observed time series with different lengths of follow\-up, as typically encountered in retrospective observational chronic care datasets\. Second, we conduct an extensive comparison of the binary classification paradigm to a survival analysis alternative for time\-to\-worsening, for multiple sclerosis and beyond\. Third, we extend a survival analysis outcome\-informed clustering algorithm to the multi\-event setting and apply it to composite scores in multiple and systemic sclerosis, achieving methodological and external validation\. Explainability and domain knowledge interpretations are interwoven throughout the development of these three methods\. However, we also specifically develop a dashboard to explain individual predictions of random forest\-based models for the expert end user\. Our findings indicate that survival analysis is a valuable replacement for the binary classification paradigm\. When thresholded at a specific point in time, the single threshold\-agnostic survival analysis model performs equally well as a binary classification model trained for that specific threshold\. This observation holds true for a variety of benchmark datasets from different domains: without compromises, a single survival model on the full prediction horizon matches the performance of the specialized binary classification model\. For multiple sclerosis, post\-hoc explainability techniques applied to the time\- to\-worsening model showcase that the model uncovered interesting variable interaction patterns\. Likewise, the inherent explainability of the multi\-event survival\-informed clustering algorithm allowed us to identify clusters with higher risks of worsening for some patient outcomes but lower risks of worsening for other outcomes\. These explanations are partly corroborated with the domain literature, but also partly remain potential research hypotheses\. In conclusion, we have extensively advocated and motivated the competitive performance and increased expressiveness of survival analysis over binary classification for worsening in multiple sclerosis\. When integrated together with the multi\-target binning approach and local explainability dashboard into a clinical decision support system, this paves the way for personalized medicine\. These alternative paradigms allow clinicians to get a more comprehensive view on the future progression of the individual patient, easing the treatment selection process\. Additionally, since many patient outcomes are naturally represented as a time\-to\-event, the proposed multi\-event survival\-informed clustering algorithm is also broadly applicable for patient stratification purposes\. When developing novel treatments, this algorithm can be used to split the candidate cohort for a clinical trial into more homogeneous subgroups\. More homogeneous means equal statistical power for lower sample sizes, and thus overall more cost\-effective drug trials\. Finally, we show how explainability techniques can be applied and interpreted to increase model and disease understanding\. These explanations could generate scientific hypotheses to be tested, as we showcased for the prognostic relevance of a biomarker called CHIT1\.

## [Author\-in\-the\-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference](../publications/0104bc55b4dc8a51f6b1.md)

Yukun Dong; Linjun Zhang; Tian Zheng

Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors&\#x27; code is expected to reproduce\. We present an author\-in\-the\-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent&\#x27;s investigation and assessment\. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two\-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment\. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved\. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review\. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases\. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent&\#x27;s investigation and assessment\. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing\. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers\.

## [Causal Value Attribution of Marketing Labels in LLM\-Generated Ads: A Deconfounder Approach](../publications/0107fb099e7fd2aab09b.md)

Danhong You; Wei Jiang;  Zhiqiang;  Zheng

As AI\-generated content becomes commoditized, economic value increasingly shifts from final artifacts to the upstream expertise used to specify inputs that steer LLM generation\. Yet organizations lack methods for valuing this expertise and identifying which individual skills or configurations causally improve performance\. This study examines generative marketing, where structured expert labels serve as skill primitives conditioning LLM\-generated advertisements\. Estimating their causal effects is difficult because outcomes reflect stochastic LLM mediation, high\-dimensional label interactions, and multimodal confounding\. This study proposes D\-VAE \(Deconfounder Variational Autoencoder\), a counterfactual\-inference framework integrating a multi\-treatment deconfounder with causal representation learning\. D\-VAE recovers causally disentangled expert\-labeling logic and derives PAC\-based bounds on omitted\-variable bias from single\-treatment confounders\. Applied to 29,177 foundation\-makeup ad creatives, D\-VAE outperforms state\-of\-the\-art benchmarks\. A field experiment shows that recommended configurations increase engagement by 32\.7% and perform statistically indistinguishably from human experts, while a simulation study confirms causal attribution under complex confounding and treatment interactions\. Overall, the study shifts value assessment from AI\-generated products to skills, providing a foundation for pricing and optimizing AI\-augmented skill portfolios\.
