## [A comprehensive review of underground CO2 storage and associated risks](../publications/0122bb5d89ba6205d11b.md)

Bomi Kim; Yongho Seong; Qingquan Liu; Kun Sang Lee

Geological carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) storage has emerged as one of the most promising technologies for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and achieving global carbon neutrality\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of CO 2 geological storage with emphasis on storage formations, trapping mechanisms, storage capacity assessment methods, monitoring techniques, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and the key factors governing long\-term storage security\. Major geological storage formations—deep saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, unmineable coal seams, and basalt formations—are compared in terms of storage capacity, injectivity, containment, and technological maturity; and the fundamental CO 2 trapping mechanisms \(structural, residual, solubility, and mineral trapping\) are examined together with their contributions to long\-term storage permanence\. Storage\-capacity assessment methods are critically evaluated within the Carbon Sequestration Leadership Forum \(CSLF\) Theoretical–Effective–Practical–Matched Capacity framework, including the volumetric equations used for saline aquifers and depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs and their associated sources of uncertainty\. The discussion is grounded in seven representative operating and demonstration CCS projects \(Sleipner, In Salah, Quest, Illinois Basin–Decatur, Otway, Carbfix, and Gorgon\), illustrating how storage capacity, monitoring, and risk\-management decisions have been implemented in practice\. Storage risks are organized within an integrated Source–Pathway–Receptor \(SPR\) and Hazard–Failure–Consequence \(HFC\) framework, and their evolution and coupling are traced across the injection, operational, and post\-injection stages of a storage project\. Corresponding monitoring technologies and preventive and corrective mitigation strategies are reviewed and explicitly linked to the specific risks they are designed to detect or control\. Finally, recent advances in coupled thermo\-hydro\-mechanical\-chemical \(THMC\) modeling, digital twins, machine\-learning surrogates, and distributed fiber\-optic and AI\-based monitoring are discussed as emerging tools for reducing uncertainty and improving real\-time risk management\. Overall, this review offers an integrated, stage\-aware framework for understanding and managing geological CO 2 storage risk, together with perspectives for improving storage reliability and accelerating the large\-scale deployment of carbon capture and storage \(CCS\)\.

## [Does digital transformation of high\-carbon emission enterprises promote green technological innovation quality? —The moderating role of executive green awareness and corporate social responsibility](../publications/013229c67d43e4cf5fe9.md)

Chenchen Ye; Deqiang Deng; Zhechao Xiong

High\-carbon industries face immense pressure to achieve substantive green innovation\. While digital transformation \(DT\) is a potential catalyst, its impact on the quality of green technological innovation \(GTI\) remains unclear\. Using panel data from 291 Chinese A\-share listed firms in high\-carbon sectors, this study employs fixed\-effects models to investigate whether DT promotes GTI quality\. We further examine the moderating roles of executive green awareness \(EGA\) and corporate social responsibility \(CSR\), and the boundary condition of the emission trading scheme \(ETS\) policy\. The fixed\-effects models reveal that: \(1\) DT significantly improves GTI quality, with persistent effects\. \(2\) EGA and CSR positively moderate this relationship, strengthening the link between DT and high\-quality GTI\. \(3\) Heterogeneity analysis shows DT’s effect is more significant among enterprises in ETS pilot regions and those with high carbon emissions\. This study shifts the focus from innovation quantity to quality in a critical context\. Its originality lies in revealing the synergistic effects of digital resources with internal governance \(EGA\) and strategic orientation \(CSR\), and providing novel evidence on ETS policy as a boundary condition for unlocking DT’s green potential\. We conclude that DT’s effectiveness in driving quality green innovation is contingent on proactive green awareness, social responsibility, and supportive carbon pricing\. These findings provide contextual insights into how policy\-driven digital transformation interacts with environmental governance to enhance green innovation, offering actionable references for emerging economies undergoing similar low\-carbon transitions\.

## [Future anxiety and psychological wellbeing among sport management students: the indirect role of mental toughness and the joint moderating role of age and family economic status](../publications/013b318314e4cf36f547.md)

Seda Nur Turhal; Faik Öz; Oğuzhan GÜL; Yunus ŞAHİNLER; Ismail Belli; Mehmet Bayansalduz

Introduction This study examined the association between future anxiety and psychological wellbeing, the indirect association through mental toughness, and the joint moderating role of age and family economic status in the relationship between future anxiety and mental toughness among sport management students\. Methods A cross\-sectional correlational design was used with 367 students enrolled in sport management departments at four public universities in Türkiye\. Data were collected using the Future Anxiety Scale for University Students, the Mental Toughness Inventory, and the Psychological Wellbeing Scale\. Pearson correlation, observed\-variable path analysis, and three\-way interaction analysis were conducted\. Results Future anxiety was negatively associated with psychological wellbeing \( r = −0\.40, p &lt; 0\.001\) and mental toughness \( r = −0\.35, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas mental toughness was positively associated with psychological wellbeing \( r = 0\.75, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The indirect association between future anxiety and psychological wellbeing through mental toughness was statistically significant \( β = −0\.240, 95% BCa bootstrap CI \[−0\.336, −0\.160\]\), while the direct association remained significant \( β = −0\.165, p &lt; 0\.001\), indicating that mental toughness accounted for part of the association\. The three\-way interaction among future anxiety, age, and family economic status was statistically significant in predicting mental toughness \( B = 0\.550, p = 0\.006\)\. Future anxiety was negatively associated with mental toughness across all age and family economic status groups\. The largest observed negative slope was found among students aged 22 years or older whose family income was lower than their family expenses \( B = −0\.620, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas the smallest observed negative slope was found among students aged 18–21 years in the same economic group \( B = −0\.180, p = 0\.041\)\. Discussion These findings identify mental toughness as an important psychological resource associated with psychological wellbeing and indicate that age and family economic status jointly condition the strength of the relationship between future anxiety and mental toughness\. Given the cross\-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than evidence of causal relationships\.

## [Examining intersections of biographies &amp; biologies: Diversity &amp; outcomes of people with multiple sclerosis in Canada \(iBio2Div\-MS\) protocol](../publications/013ccee3121a76b71862.md)

Ruth Ann Marrie; Kaarina Kowalec; Afolasade O\. Fakolade; John Fisk; Sarah J\. Donkers; Colleen Jean Maxwell; Penelope S\. Smyth; Christina M\. Wolfson; Marcia L\. Finlayson

BACKGROUND: Although advances have been made in understanding multiple sclerosis \(MS\) disease etiology and developing new therapeutics, the benefits of these advances have been distributed inequitably across population groups\. Persons with MS \(PwMS\) who are racialized, men, of lower social position, or living in rural areas experience worse outcomes for reasons yet to be fully elucidated\. OBJECTIVE: We designed a prospective three\-year longitudinal study to assess the individual and joint effects of contextual, biographical, and biological factors \(e\.g\., sex, age, and genetics\), on performance\-based and patient\-reported outcomes among groups under\-represented in MS research\. METHODS: We will enroll 500 PwMS and 100 individuals without MS who are aged ≥18 years, resident in Canada, able to complete interviews in English, commit to three years of participation, and self\-identify as belonging to ≥1 of these groups: men, racialized, immigrant within the last ten years, 2SLGBTQI\+, rural resident \(population &lt;10,000\) or living with moderate\-to\-severe disability\. Following e\-consent, participants will provide a saliva sample for DNA collection and complete four telephone interviews over three years \(at baseline and yearly thereafter\)\. CONCLUSIONS: This study will provide insight into the joint contributions of contextual, biographical, and biological factors to health outcomes among underrepresented groups with MS\.

## [High\-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel\-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques](../publications/0157ddbdcc8037cd855a.md)

Roberto Colonna; Carolina Filizzola; Vita Elena Di Leo; Iacopo Mancusi; Mariano Lisi; Valerio Tramutoli

High accuracy in burned area \(BA\) mapping is desirable for many fire\-related applications\. Most operational products are based on coarse\-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m\. The use of higher\-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager \(MSI\) on board Sentinel\-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods\. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications\. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products\. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique \(RST\) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel\-2 images within Google Earth Engine\. Test results from two complete region\-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97\.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi\-source validation framework, with an area\-based commission error of 1\.38% and omission error of 0\.60%\. Missed detections documented by the Regional Spatial Data Infrastructure \(RSDI\) amounted to 10\.60 ha, corresponding to approximately 0\.9% of the burned area reported by RSDI over the tested periods\. Polygon\-level intercomparison with RSDI and the European Forest Fire Information System \(EFFIS\) yielded Intersection over Union \(IoU\) values of 0\.69 and 0\.83, respectively\. The proposed approach mapped larger burned areas than those reported by both RSDI \(\+48%\) and EFFIS \(\+143%\) as well\.

## [THE SCIENTIFIC DISCOURSE ON PHARMACOLOGY AND BIOINFORMATIC ANALYSIS IN MODERN DRUG DESIGN: FROM TARGET DISCOVERY TO TRANSLATIONAL OPTIMIZATION THROUGH INTEGRATED MOLECULAR, COMPUTATIONAL, STRUCTURAL, SYSTEMS AND PRECISION MEDICINE APPROACHES](../publications/015cd2663e7820822792.md)

Nodar Sulashvili; Margarita Beglaryan; Nana Gorgaslidze; Naira Chichoyan; Vira Kravchenko; Marika Sulashvili; Nato Alavidze; Ia Egnatievi; Manana Giorgobiani; Magda Davitashvili; Irina IMERLISHVILI; MARINA GIORGOBIANI; Ігор Сенюк; Lali Patsia; Olga Shapoval; NATIA KVIZHINADZE; Lasha Tchelidze; David Aphkhazava

Drug discovery has evolved from a largely empirical discipline into a knowledge\-intensive enterprise that depends on the integration of pharmacology, structural biology, computational chemistry, and bioinformatics\. Modern pharmacotherapeutic design is no longer satisfied by the demonstration that a molecule binds a macromolecular target\. Instead, a candidate must be considered within a broader context that includes disease mechanism, network position of the target, tissue expression, structural tractability, off\-target liabilities, pharmacokinetic behavior, and the probability of translation from preclinical systems to humans\. Bioinformatic analysis has become central to this process because it enables the organization and interpretation of genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, phenotypic, and chemical data at a scale that cannot be managed by traditional reductionist workflows alone\. Pharmacology remains equally indispensable because the relevance of computational outputs depends on mechanistic interpretation, exposure\-response understanding, and a realistic view of efficacy and safety in complex biological systems\. This review examines how pharmacology and bioinformatic analysis jointly inform contemporary drug design across the discovery pipeline\. It discusses target identification and validation, structural bioinformatics, structure\-based and ligand\-based design, network pharmacology, multi\-omics analysis, ADMET prediction, and pharmacokinetic\-pharmacodynamic modeling\. It also addresses the increasing role of machine learning, not as a replacement for experimental science, but as a tool for prioritization, pattern recognition, and iterative decision support\. Particular emphasis is placed on the limitations of current approaches, including database incompleteness, bias in training sets, uncertain biological annotation, and the common error of overinterpreting docking scores or predictive probabilities as proof of therapeutic success\. The central argument is that the most reliable drug design strategies emerge when computational breadth is combined with pharmacological depth\. In that integrative framework, bioinformatics helps define what should be tested, while pharmacology determines what the resulting signals actually mean for drug action, safety, and translation\.

## [Presenting ReadingFood and its infrastructure](../publications/016170f6acfeff997784.md)

Diana Santos; Michael Preminger; Elizaveta Khachaturyan; Åse Kristine Tveit; Slav Petrov

In this paper, we provide general information on the ReadingFood project, discussing its architecture and infrastructure choice\(s\)\. After presenting the CorpusEye environment, we give some “appetizers” of the diverse studies that can be done with this system\. First, we present a taxonomy developed to cover food and drink in the three languages, and we explain the need to disambiguate for a fine\-grained classification in this domain\. We then illustrate different kinds of studies that ReadingFood allows, namely a\) lexical semantics of container words in Italian, b\) changes in drinking habits in Norway, and c\) differences between Portuguese and Brazilian societies in what concerns drinking\. We finish by a short discussion on how other infrastructural challenges for other parts of the project can be solved\.

## [INTEGRATION OF AUTOMATION SYSTEMS INTO CRITICAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE: CYBERSECURITY AND RESILIENCE CHALLENGES](../publications/01695198a554c0bfa95a.md)

Andrii Shcherba

Purpose\. The purpose of this study is to examine the cybersecurity and resilience challenges associated with the increasing integration of supervisory control and data acquisition \(SCADA\) and programmable logic controller \(PLC\) systems into critical energy infrastructure\. Particular attention is given to automation systems deployed across energy, transport, and gas supply facilities, where improvements in operational efficiency are accompanied by an expanding attack surface available to malicious actors\. Methodology\. The study applies an analytical and synthesis\-based approach to the current body of knowledge on industrial control system cybersecurity\. The analysis encompasses SCADA\-related cyber threats, applicable cybersecurity standards and frameworks, including IEC 62443 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, resilience architecture design, and documented incident patterns across offshore extraction platforms, gas pipelines, and fuel storage facilities\. The findings derived from the literature are synthesised to establish the conceptual and structural basis for assessing cyber\-physical resilience maturity\. Results\. The analysis identifies a persistent pattern of reactive rather than proactive security governance, insufficient segmentation between information technology \(IT\) and operational technology \(OT\) networks, and inadequate industrial control system \(ICS\)\-specific incident response planning across documented cases\. Based on these findings, the study develops the Cyber\-Physical Resilience Maturity Model \(CPRMM\), a four\-level, four\-domain assessment framework designed to enable operators and regulators to systematically evaluate and benchmark the cybersecurity posture of industrial control system environments\. Practical implications\. The CPRMM translates conceptual findings from the cybersecurity literature into a structured, practitioner\-oriented scoring tool that can support operators and regulators in identifying cybersecurity weaknesses and assessing the maturity of cyber\-physical resilience measures\. The findings further indicate that addressing existing deficiencies requires both technical investment and a fundamental shift in organisational security culture\. Value/originality\. The principal original contribution of the study is the development of the Cyber\-Physical Resilience Maturity Model as an integrated framework for the systematic assessment and benchmarking of cybersecurity and resilience within industrial control system environments\. By combining four maturity levels with four assessment domains, the CPRMM provides a structured mechanism for translating established cybersecurity knowledge into an operational assessment instrument applicable to critical infrastructure\.

## [Determinizm Termo\-Algorytmiczny w Hyperscale AI: Modelowanie i proaktywna kontrola nieliniowej propagacji anomalii hydrodynamicznych obiegów mCDU do warstwy wykonawczej obliczeń rozproszonych\.](../publications/0169d4dd2d1dc09d039b.md)

Rajmund Olszewski

Determinizm Termo\-Algorytmiczny w Hyperscale AI: Modelowanie i proaktywna kontrola nieliniowej propagacji anomalii hydrodynamicznych obiegów mCDU do warstwy wykonawczej obliczeń rozproszonych Streszczenie: Wraz ze skalowaniem klastrów obliczeniowych sztucznej inteligencji \(AI/HPC\) powyżej gęstości mocy 100 kW na szafę rackową, dotychczasowy paradygmat ścisłej separacji infrastruktury mechaniczno\-hydraulicznej \(HVAC/mCDU\) od warstwy wykonawczej oprogramowania ulega całkowitemu załamaniu\. Niniejsza rozprawa doktorska wprowadza i formalizuje pojęcie Determinizmu Termo\-Algorytmicznego – teorii stanowiącej, że w architekturach wielkowęzłowych proces obliczeniowy jest zdarzeniem ściśle termodynamicznym, w którym fizyka płynu bezpośrednio modyfikuje czas trwania cyklu zegara procesora oraz determinuje łączny czas egzekucji algorytmu \(t\_exec\)\. Głównym celem badawczym pracy jest sformułowanie, numeryczne rozwiązanie oraz empiryczna walidacja modelu nieliniowej propagacji zaburzeń hydraulicznych ze skali makroinstalacji obiegów wtórnych mCDU do skali mikro \(mikrokanały zimnych płyt GPU o wymiarach 100–200 µm\), a ostatecznie do logiki sterowania częstotliwością taktowania krzemu w trybie DVFS i orkiestracji barier synchronizacji klastrowej \(NCCL Ring\-AllReduce\)\. W ramach pracy wyprowadzono Sprzężony Układ Równań Stanu \(0D Lumped\-Parameter DAE System\), wiążący w jedną pętlę sprzężenia zwrotnego: Kinematykę taktowania zegara PMIC w dziedzinie cykli obliczeniowych: dC\(t\) / dt = f\(T\_j\(t\)\) Bilans cieplny złącza krzemowego \(T\_j\) uwzględniający dodatnie sprzężenie zwrotne z wykładniczo rosnącymi prądami upływu I\_leak\(T\_j\) oraz załamanie konwekcyjnego współczynnika przejmowania ciepła h\_conv na skutek uwięzionej fazy gazowej alpha\_void: C\_th \* \(dT\_j\(t\) / dt\) = P\_total\(f\(t\), V\(t\), T\_j\(t\)\) \* S\(t\) \- h\(alpha\_void\(t\)\) \* A \* \(T\_j\(t\) \- T\_fluid\(t\)\) gdzie P\_total\(f, V, T\_j\) = P\_dyn\(f, V\) \+ V \* I\_leak\(T\_j\), a S\(t\) = 1 / \[1 \+ exp\(k \* \(t \- t\_exec\)\)\] stanowi gładką sigmoidalną funkcja przejścia w stany spoczynku C\-state\. Stochastyczną inercję hydrodynamiki dwufazowej, opisującą desorpcję gazów obcych z płynu zgodnie z Prawem Henry’ego oraz lokalne mikro\-wrzenie \(flash evaporation\) wywołane zapaścią ciśnienia statycznego np\. \(P\_stat &lt; 30 PSIG / 2\.07 bar g\): tau\_void \* \(d alpha\_void\(t\) / dt\) = G\_eq\(Q\_dot\(t\), m\_dot\(t\), Delta P\_micro\(t\)\) \- alpha\_void\(t\) W odpowiedzi na zidentyfikowany problem opóźnienia klasycznych czujników \(1–10 Hz\) opracowano cyber\-fizyczny algorytm kontroli TACE\-Alg, wykorzystujący telemetrię piezoelektryczną 100 Hz\. Pomiary ruchomej wariancji szumu ciśnienia różnicowego sigma^2\_DeltaP pozwalają na estymację ułamka fazy gazowej alpha\_void\(t\) = min\(0\.05, gamma \* sqrt\(sigma^2\_DeltaP\(t\)\)\) oraz proaktywną modyfikację pracy pomp VFD lub zaworów bypass na 300–800 ms przed krytycznym skokiem temperatury krzemu T\_j, trwale eliminując powstawanie lokalnych maruderów \(Straggler Effect\) w synchronicznych operacjach rozproszonych\. Rozprawa rozszerza uniwersalny model teoretyczny na dwie zaawansowane domeny technologiczne: Obliczenia Post\-CMOS \(Part V\): Zastosowanie predykcyjnych materiałów zmiennofazowych \(PCM\), falowodów fononowych oraz ciekłych metali sterowanych magnetohydrodynamicznie \(MHD\) w stykach gęstości mocy przekraczających 500 W/cm²\. Autonomiczne Systemy Kosmiczne \(Part VI\): Załamanie konwekcji swobodnej w warunkach mikrograwitacji \(g \-&gt; 0\), potęgowanie zjawiska przywierania pęcherzy \(alpha\_void &gt; 0\), dysypacja radiacyjna Stefana\-Boltzmanna w próżni kosmicznej oraz kointegracja ciepła odpadowego z układami podtrzymywania życia załogi \(ECLSS\)\. Opracowanie wieńczy zestaw rygorystycznych procedur odbiorowych QA/QC \(dwuetapowa deaeracja próżniowa, kalibracja poduszki azotu np\. 25 PSIG przy bezwzględnie wyzerowanym przyłączu cieczowym 0\.0 PSIG oraz „Test Neodymowy”\), stanowiący bezpośrednie wdrożenie inżynieryjne wyników badań do praktyki komisjonowania najnowocześniejszych centrów danych Hyperscale AI\. Title: Thermo\-Algorithmic Determinism in Hyperscale AI: Modeling and Proactive Control of Non\-Linear Hydrodynamic Anomaly Propagation from mCDU Loops to the Execution Layer of Distributed Computing Abstract: With artificial intelligence and high\-performance computing \(AI/HPC\) clusters scaling beyond power densities of 100 kW per rack, the traditional paradigm of strictly isolating mechanical\-hydraulic facility infrastructure \(HVAC/mCDU\) from the software execution layer completely collapses\. This doctoral dissertation introduces and formalizes the concept of Thermo\-Algorithmic Determinism—a theory establishing that in multi\-node architectures, the computational process is fundamentally a thermodynamic event wherein fluid physics directly modulates the CPU clock cycle duration and determines total algorithm execution time \(t\_exec\)\. The primary research objective of this work is to formulate, numerically solve, and empirically validate a model describing the non\-linear propagation of hydraulic disturbances from the macro\-scale of secondary mCDU cooling loops down to the micro\-scale \(microchannels of GPU cold plates measuring 100–200 µm\), and ultimately to the silicon clock frequency control logic in DVFS mode and cluster synchronization barrier orchestration \(NCCL Ring\-AllReduce\)\. As part of this research, a Coupled Lumped\-Parameter Differential\-Algebraic System of Equations \(0D DAE System\) was derived, binding into a closed feedback loop: PMIC Clock Kinematics in the computational cycle domain: dC\(t\) / dt = f\(T\_j\(t\)\) Silicon Junction Thermal Balance \(T\_j\) incorporating positive feedback from exponentially growing leakage currents I\_leak\(T\_j\) and the collapse of the convective heat transfer coefficient h\_conv caused by trapped gas void fraction alpha\_void: C\_th \* \(dT\_j\(t\) / dt\) = P\_total\(f\(t\), V\(t\), T\_j\(t\)\) \* S\(t\) \- h\(alpha\_void\(t\)\) \* A \* \(T\_j\(t\) \- T\_fluid\(t\)\) where P\_total\(f, V, T\_j\) = P\_dyn\(f, V\) \+ V \* I\_leak\(T\_j\), and S\(t\) = 1 / \[1 \+ exp\(k \* \(t \- t\_exec\)\)\] represents a smooth C\-state transition function\. Stochastic Two\-Phase Hydrodynamic Inertia, describing foreign gas desorption from the coolant under Henry&\#x27;s Law and localized flash evaporation caused by static pressure collapse e\.g\. \(P\_stat &lt; 30 PSIG / 2\.07 bar g\): tau\_void \* \(d alpha\_void\(t\) / dt\) = G\_eq\(Q\_dot\(t\), m\_dot\(t\), Delta P\_micro\(t\)\) \- alpha\_void\(t\) To address the response latency inherent in conventional temperature and pressure sensors \(1–10 Hz\), a cyber\-physical control algorithm \(TACE\-Alg\) was developed utilizing 100 Hz piezoelectric telemetry\. Real\-time measurements of the moving variance of differential pressure noise sigma^2\_DeltaP enable estimation of the void fraction alpha\_void\(t\) = min\(0\.05, gamma \* sqrt\(sigma^2\_DeltaP\(t\)\)\) and proactive adjustment of VFD pumps or bypass valves 300–800 ms prior to critical silicon junction temperature spikes \(T\_j\), permanently mitigating local straggler generation \(Straggler Effect\) in synchronous distributed operations\. The dissertation extends the theoretical framework across two advanced technical frontiers: Post\-CMOS Computing \(Part V\): Integration of predictive Phase Change Materials \(PCM\), phononic waveguides, and magnetohydrodynamic \(MHD\) liquid metal loops for extreme heat fluxes exceeding 500 W/cm²\. Autonomous Deep\-Space AI \(Part VI\): Breakdown of buoyancy\-driven convection in microgravity \(g \-&gt; 0\), amplification of bubble pinning \(alpha\_void &gt; 0\), Stefan\-Boltzmann radiative vacuum dissipation, and enthalpy harvesting for Environmental Control and Life Support Systems \(ECLSS\)\. The work concludes with a comprehensive suite of QA/QC commissioning protocols \(including two\-stage oil\-free vacuum degassing, nitrogen precharge calibration at e\.g\. 25 PSIG exclusively with a zeroed 0\.0 PSIG liquid connection, and the &quot;Neodymium Test&quot;\), providing direct engineering implementation of the research findings into Hyperscale AI data center commissioning practices\.

## [Assessment of change in drug\-induced parkinsonism in daily\-life gait using vision\-based machine learning](../publications/0173ce992a586dec9e37.md)

Benjamin Filtjens; Vida Adeli; Soroush Mehraban; Andrea Sabo; Babak Taati; Andrea Iaboni

Drug\-induced parkinsonism is a potentially reversible movement disorder that may be subtle and difficult to monitor in residential dementia care\. Vision\-based machine learning analysis of gait may provide unobtrusive longitudinal monitoring around medication changes\. We conducted a two\-center cohort study of 61 residents with dementia receiving psychotropic medication\. Hallway gait sequences were recorded using ceiling\-mounted cameras and converted to three\-dimensional body pose\. A TabPFN classifier estimated UPDRS\-III item 29 gait severity for each walk\. We evaluated associations between acute antipsychotic \(AP\) and antidepressant \(AD\) dose reduction/cessation \(≥50% dose reduction or cessation, 0\-21 days after change\) and daily mean predicted gait severity using linear mixed\-effects models in ever\-exposed participants, with complementary equal\-weight paired analyses among participants observed in both medication states\. In mixed\-effects models, acute AP dose reduction/cessation was associated with lower predicted gait severity \(β=\-0\.127, p = 0\.022\), whereas AD dose reduction/cessation was not \(β=\-0\.060, p = 0\.210\)\. Equal\-weight paired analyses found no statistically significant participant\-average within\-person change among paired participants \(AP mean change = 0\.031, 95% CI \[\-0\.114, 0\.176\], p = 0\.653; AD mean change =\-0\.021, 95% CI \[\-0\.098, 0\.056\], p = 0\.575\), consistent with heterogeneous individual responses\. Vision\-based monitoring captured within\-participant gait variation around psychotropic dose\-reduction periods, but findings are associative\. Larger prospective studies with documented reasons for medication changes are needed before using such monitoring to guide medication decisions\.

## [Zr‐Al‐C MAX Phases Stabilized by Carbon Vacancies](../publications/0174305c511ad52bca46.md)

Nick Goossens; Cesare Roncaglia; Daniele Passerone; Michael Stuer

ABSTRACT Extreme service environments demand the engineering of innovative high‐performance materials, with high purity as a critical design requirement\. Zirconium‐based MAX phases are touted for their radiation tolerance, favorable neutronics, and liquid metal compatibility\. Accordingly, they are proposed as highly promising candidates to replace corrosion‐sensitive zircalloy coatings for accident‐tolerant fuels in Gen‐III/Gen‐IV nuclear reactors\. However, their potential has never materialized due to their poor synthesizability and thus low purity\. The inevitable and poorly understood competing formation of ZrC during synthesis severely compromises their thermomechanical integrity and radiation response\. This work combines complementary insights into theoretical phase stability and experimental synthesizability of and \. Carbon vacancies are predicted to adversely affect stability, whereas moderate \(5–10 at\.%\) carbon deficiency improves stability\. Reactive spark plasma sintering /Al/C powder mixtures of varying stoichiometry validated these trends: only forms substantially when using stoichiometric or carbon‐excessive feedstocks, whereas formation is highly sensitive to carbon‐deficient feedstocks: carbon‐stoichiometric or ‐excessive \(25 at\.%\) feedstocks do not yield appreciable quantities of \. Defect engineering thus emerges as a powerful alternative strategy for enhancing MAX phase stability and synthesizability without compromising their chemical integrity, opening new avenues for their design and application\.

## [GraphBEAT: Graph\-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers](../publications/018eb36afc1f4c731eed.md)

Leo Y\. Li\-Han; Chris Varghese; Elizabeth B\. Habermann; Mark J\. Truty; William R\. G\. Perry; Cornelius A\. Thiels; Hojjat Salehinejad

Longitudinal electronic health records \(EHRs\) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health\. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling\. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT \(Graph\-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time\), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient\-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers\. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events\. A context\-aware, time\-decay message\-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi\-head attention pooling to generate patient\-level representations\. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi\-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12\-, 24\-, and 36\-month diagnostic lead times\. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks \(GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN\) and sequence modeling approaches \(Transformer and long short\-term memory \[LSTM\]\)\. GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating\-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines\. These results support GraphBEAT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach for cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous longitudinal health records\.

## [Knowledge Transfer in Early Modern England: The Role of Culinary Collections and Household Investigation Using THE WASPAS Method](../publications/018f250fb203c02abbf0.md)

Muniyammal Sakthivel; M\. Ramachandran; Arunambigai Ramesh

This study examines the progress of English agriculture during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, focusing on labor productivity, grain yields, and the expansion of farm size\. Using estate surveys, land tax assessments, and Arthur Young’s data, it explores how larger farms improved labor efficiency and contributed to agricultural transformation\. The research also compares English agricultural performance with French and Russian agriculture, highlighting international differences in farming practices and productivity\. Furthermore, the study evaluates five varieties of English, namely Old English, Middle English, King James Bible English, Colonial American English, and Scots English, using the WASPAS method\. Four evaluation parameters—rich vocabulary, historical importance, complex grammar, and obsolete vocabulary—are considered to assess their relative significance\. The findings indicate that Colonial American English achieved the highest ranking, whereas Old English received the lowest\. Colonial American English demonstrated the highest preference value under the WASPAS approach\. These results illustrate the usefulness of multi\-criteria decision\-making methods in comparative linguistic evaluation and provide insights into the historical development and distinctive characteristics of English language varieties\.

## [Intraoperative asymmetry of thalamic stimulation mapping in Essential Tremor: specificity of first hemisphere implantation and transitory lesioning effect](../publications/01a4fc4e64cff9b77c4a.md)

Vittoria Bucciarelli; Dorian Vogel; J\. Coste; Rémi Chaix; Simone Hemm; Jean‐Jacques Lemaire

Introduction Deep Brain Stimulation \(DBS\) effectively reduces symptoms in Essential Tremor \(ET\)\. Clinical benefit depends on modulation of distributed neural circuits with still undeciphered mechanisms\. Furthermore, the lesioning effect observable intraoperatively following the implantation of the DBS lead in the first brain hemisphere has received little attention\. We hypothesize that hemispheric differences exist in the spatial organization of improvement and adverse effects, related to the sequential implantation of electrodes and a transitory lesioning effect\. Methods We investigated this hemispheric asymmetry with a data\-driven, probabilistic mapping approach, linking simulated stimulation volumes \[Volumes of Tissue Activated \(VTAs\)\] to symptom improvement \(imp\) and side effects \(se\) for each hemisphere\. Intraoperative data from 23 ET patients undergoing DBS lead implantation in the ventrointermediate nucleus of thalamus \(Vim\) were retrospectively analyzed\. The left hemisphere was systematically implanted first\. Stimulation spots \(positions\) were categorized using therapeutic window values and side effect occurrence\. Hemisphere\-specific probabilistic effect volumes of imp \(PVimp\) and se \(PVse\) derived from VTAs, and clusters of stimulation spots grouped by category were computed\. They were topographically analyzed in relation to structures of the Vim region, and compared within hemispheres and across hemispheres\. Results In the first implanted hemisphere, PVimp was in the infero\-posterior part of Vim reaching the subthalamic tegmental fields, whereas the PVse was above, posterior and lateral to the PVimp, spanning Vim and the ventrocaudal nucleus of thalamus \(VC\)\. In the right one, PVimp and PVse overlapped, intersecting Vim and VC, in the intermediate part of both\. The stimulation spots clusters, in the left hemisphere, were located around the intermediate part, slightly lateral of Vim and VC to a lesser extent\. In the right one, they were located in the intermediate and superior parts of Vim\. Discussion Significant hemispheric asymmetries were observed, revealing a lesioning effect subsequent to the first DBS lead implantation in the left hemisphere\. This led to a broader distribution of optimal positions with a larger PVimp largely overlapping with the PVse in the contralateral right hemisphere\. The combined mapping and categorization framework yields hemisphere\-specific insights on the transitory lesioning and bi\-hemispheric modulation which could guide future DBS strategies\.

## [¿Tienen los bebés la capacidad de leer mentes?](../publications/01aab5cc1ea23b4c4fad.md)

Ányerson Stiths Gómez Tabares

La lectura de mentes es la capacidad de atribuir y responder a los estados mentales de los demás\. Tradicionalmente, se ha considerado que la lectura de mentes requiere de la posesión de conceptos mentales y emerge en niños de cuatro años\. Sin embargo, los estudios recientes han mostrado que los bebés tienen una comprensión implícita de los estados mentales, lo que sugiere que esta capacidad surge tempranamente en el neurodesarrollo\. Los hallazgos y la interpretación de la lectura de mentes en bebés han sido cuestionados\. En este artículo se debate si la lectura de mentes implícita es realmente lectura de mentes, o si refleja procesos de submentalización\. Para ello, se analiza el carácter conceptual de la controversia entre las explicaciones mentalistas y submentalistas, y se destaca la dificultad de encontrar una solución empírica\. También se discuten los supuestos de la teoría de lectura de mentes como posesión de conceptos y se analizan los argumentos centrales de las teorías submentalistas y mentalistas\. Se presentan argumentos en contra de la tesis de que la lectura de mentes implícita involucra la representación de conceptos mentales\. Se propone que los bebés tienen una capacidad preconceptual que se enriquece con los procesos de intencionalidad compartida para rastrear las intenciones que subyacen al comportamiento social\. Se introduce la noción de protoconcepto para caracterizar la naturaleza relacional y no conceptual de la lectura de mentes implícita\. Se argumenta que los bebés emplean los protoconceptos para identificar expresiones faciales, verbales y conductuales en los demás y vincularlas con estados mentales\.

## [SMART CITY 5\.0 ЯК КОНЦЕПЦІЯ ЛЮДИНОЦЕНТРИЧНОГО МІСЬКОГО РОЗВИТКУ: СИНЕРГІЯ ІНТЕРНЕТУ РЕЧЕЙ ТА ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ](../publications/01ad139b299500aa8c3f.md)

OLEG PUNCHENKO; Nataliia Punchenko

Устатті досліджено концептуальні та методологічні засади формування Smart City 5\.0 на основі синергії технологій Інтернету речей \(IoT\) та штучного інтелекту \(AI\)\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена прискоренням цифрової трансформації міст, поширенням технологій Інтернету речей \(IoT\), штучного інтелекту \(AI\), великих даних та інтелектуальних цифрових платформ, які докорінно змінюють способи функціонування міської інфраструктури та управління міськими процесами\. Метою статті є концептуалізація ролі Інтернету речей та штучного інтелекту у формуванні Smart City 5\.0 як нової людиноцентричної, інтелектуальної та стійкої моделі розвитку міста, а також визначення синергетичного характеру їх взаємодії у забезпеченні ефективного управління міськими процесами, підвищенні якості життя громадян та формуванні цифрового міського середовища\. Результати дослідження\. Обґрунтовано, що перехід від традиційної моделі Smart City до Smart City 5\.0 означає не лише технологічну модернізацію міської інфраструктури, а й формування людиноцентричної, інтелектуальної, сталої та адаптивної екосистеми міського розвитку\. Розкрито роль IoT у створенні розгалуженої системи збору, передачі та моніторингу даних про функціонування міського середовища, а AI визначено як інструмент їх інтелектуального аналізу, прогнозування та підтримки управлінських рішень\. Доведено, що синергія IoT та AI створює технологічне підґрунтя для підвищення ефективності управління енергетикою, транспортом, екологією, безпекою, комунальними послугами та якістю життя населення\. Запропоновано концептуальну модель Smart City 5\.0 «людина – IoT – AI – дані – міське управління – суспільство», яка орієнтована на інтеграцію цифрових технологій із соціальними, екологічними та гуманістичними цілями розвитку міста\. Особливу увагу приділено питанням цифрової довіри, етичної відповідальності, кібербезпеки, захисту даних та недопущення технологічної дискримінації\. Визначено перспективи застосування моделі Smart City 5\.0 в Україні в контексті цифрової трансформації, повоєнного відновлення, підвищення стійкості міської інфраструктури та забезпечення сталого розвитку територіальних громад\. Висновок\. Практична реалізація концепції Smart City 5\.0 в Україні має розглядатися не лише як цифровізація міської інфраструктури, а як формування людиноцентричної, безпечної, стійкої та інтелектуальної екосистеми міста, у якій IoT, штучний інтелект, Big Data та цифрові платформи забезпечують нову якість управління\.

## [Engineered probiotic\-mediated palmitoylethanolamide biosynthesis protects against colitis\-associated liver injury](../publications/01b0aa4aecd843d476fe.md)

Irene Palenca; Silvia Basili Franzin; Giovanni Sarnelli; Giuseppe Esposito

Chronic colitis promotes secondary liver injury through disruption of the gut–liver axis, whereby intestinal barrier breakdown enables portal translocation of microbial products that activate hepatic inflammatory and fibrogenic pathways\. Palmitoylethanolamide \(PEA\), an endogenous ALIAmide acting primarily via PPAR\-α, exerts anti\-inflammatory and barrier\-protective effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor oral bioavailability\. We investigated whether mucosa\-targeted, probiotic\-mediated, in situ PEA biosynthesis could attenuate liver injury associated with chronic colitis\. Male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to chronic dextran sulfate sodium \(DSS\) colitis and treated with an engineered Lactobacillus paracasei F19 strain expressing human NAPE\-PLD \(pNAPE\-LP\) plus ultra\-low\-dose palmitate, a control strain \(pLP\), or pNAPE\-LP combined with the PPAR\-α antagonist MK886\. pNAPE\-LP significantly increased colonic PEA levels and elevated circulating and hepatic PEA, confirming effective local production with systemic distribution\. Treatment ameliorated colitis severity, restored tight\-junction protein expression, and reduced endotoxemia\. Importantly, pNAPE\-LP attenuated colitis\-associated liver injury by decreasing histological damage and collagen deposition, lowering transaminase levels, and reducing hepatic neutrophil infiltration\. These effects were accompanied by the suppression of the hepatic TLR4/NF\-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, reduced caspase\-1 activation, decreased IL\-1β, TNF\-α, and IL\-6 levels, restored PPAR\-α expression, and reduced Bax expression\. The control strain was ineffective, and PPAR\-α inhibition abolished both intestinal and hepatic protection\. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that engineered probiotics acting as “living drug factories” can target the gut–liver axis via localized PEA biosynthesis, restoring barrier integrity and limiting hepatic inflammatory and fibrogenic signaling in chronic colitis\.

## [SportRGDET: Scene prior and relation graph enhanced detection transformer for sports scenes](../publications/01b4abd2637fe5dd49f4.md)

Qingya Ouyang; Chaoyi Su; Qingyuan Li

Object detection in sports videos holds significant application value in tactical analysis, athlete tracking, and intelligent broadcasting\. However, existing methods face two key challenges when processing sports scenes: on one hand, target distribution in sports footage is strictly constrained by field boundaries, yet generic detectors uniformly allocate detection resources across the entire image, causing frequent false detections in off\-field regions due to the visual similarity between spectators and athletes; on the other hand, objects such as athletes, balls, and referees in sports scenes form stable spatial co\-occurrence patterns governed by game rules, yet existing methods predict each object independently, failing to leverage cross\-category relational cues to assist the detection of difficult targets\. To address these issues, this paper proposes SportRGDET \(Sport Relation\-Graph DEtection Transformer\), a framework that achieves accurate detection through two core modules: the Scene Prior Guided Module \(SPGM\) jointly estimates the spatial probability distribution and boundary gradient map of the field region from multi\-scale encoder features, fuses them to generate a hierarchical field confidence mask, and performs spatial modulation on the deformable self\-attention weights of the encoder, which reallocates attention resources toward the effective field area and progressively suppresses off\-field interference across layers, thereby reducing false detections while incurring only moderate additional computation; the Relation Reasoning Enhancement Module \(RREM\) treats each candidate object as a node during the detection decoding stage, adaptively learns inter\-node association strengths through a relation encoder based on category embeddings and relative spatial positions of node pairs, constructs a dynamic relation graph, and bidirectionally propagates contextual information across nodes via graph attention mechanisms, enabling difficult targets to refine their predictions by leveraging positional and categorical cues from surrounding identified objects, enhancing detection robustness under occlusion and blur conditions\. Experimental results demonstrate that SportRGDET achieves significant performance improvements on multiple sports detection benchmark datasets, validating the effectiveness of scene prior and relation reasoning mechanisms in sports scene object detection\.

## [WikiPlanner: wiki\-derived temporal monitors for safe LLM agent planning \- a medical\-domain proof of concept](../publications/01c93f2e8eb9200b930d.md)

Bailing Zhang

Large language model \(LLM\) agents in high\-stakes sequential planning may produce locally reasonable steps whose overall sequence violates domain constraints; single\-step filters cannot detect such cross\-step temporal violations\. We present WikiPlanner, which extracts temporal constraints from domain wikis, structures them via a typed Temporal Constraint Intermediate Representation \(TC\-IR\) with seven constraint labels compiled to six Linear Temporal Logic over finite traces \(LTLf\) templates, and instantiates them as parallel runtime monitors\. The two\-stage pipeline \- TC\-IR extraction followed by deterministic template compilation \- isolates LLM extraction uncertainty from formal compilation\. We evaluate every stage on a medical planning benchmark of 45 constraints and 236 test plans \(137 aligned, 99 natural\)\. A dual\-annotator audit of the 220 raw extractions \(κ = 0\.451, adjudicated\) places semantic extraction precision at 25\.9%; an automated check finds 79\.5% of these records structurally well\-formed \(90\.1% on a held\-out nursing corpus\); invented orderings, state\-vs\.\-action confusion, and silent parse loss from output truncation are the dominant error classes\. Plan validation achieves F1 = 0\.920 \(95%CI: 0\.873\-0\.956\) on the aligned set and F1 = 0\.582 \(95%CI: 0\.447\-0\.701\) on the natural set; the gap is attributed primarily to constraint\-library coverage and symbol grounding, as wiki\-derived constraint symbols and generator vocabulary form largely disjoint namespaces\. Latency scales linearly with library size \(0\.006\-0\.059 ms\)\. Single\-pass template repair resolves 39\.1% of violation plans \(mean 1\.30 word\-level edits per success\); local post\-trigger repairs substantially outperform pre\-trigger modifications\. Results are a single\-domain proof of concept, and symbol grounding is the main obstacle to natural\-plan deployment\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Supply Chain Management: Applications, Evidence, Implementation Constraints, and Future Directions](../publications/01d1834f3e1c5cf85156.md)

Joel Mtango; Hemant Kumar Watts

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) are increasingly investigated as decision\-support technologies for supply chain management \(SCM\), yet their value depends on the nature of the decision, data availability, organisational capability and the methods used to evaluate outcomes\. This critical narrative review examines applications across demand forecasting, inventory planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, risk management and sustainability\. It brings together relevant peer\-reviewed reviews, conceptual contributions and empirical studies, and distinguishes evidence from operational deployments from results reported in literature syntheses or simulations\. The literature supports the practical relevance of data\-driven prediction, pattern detection and decision augmentation, but it does not establish uniform improvements in cost, forecast accuracy, resilience or environmental performance across settings\. Reviewed research also identifies integration costs, fragmented data, process misalignment, model drift, limited transparency and governance concerns as barriers to realising benefits\. Recent work on generative AI broadens possible applications to document\-intensive processes, synthetic scenarios and interactive decision support, while indicating that field\-based validation remains limited\. A process\-oriented framework is proposed in which analytics inform planning, procurement, manufacturing, distribution and inventory decisions under continuous human oversight\. The review argues that useful evaluations should compare AI\-supported decisions against relevant operational baselines, account for service levels and cost trade\-offs, and document transferability across sectors and resource settings\. Future research should prioritise longitudinal field studies, cross\-organisational coordination, responsible deployment and context\-sensitive applications in emerging economies\.
