## [Assessing Behavioral and Environmental Facets of Obesity Unobtrusively Utilizing Digital Tools: Introducing the BETTER4U Indicators](../publications/01d8c1675a544d7a6ee9.md)

Chrysa Episkopou; Dimitrios Aletras; Afroditi Kita; Aleksandra Łuszczyńska; Maria Kafyra; Eva Karaglani; Yannis Μanios; Maira Bes‐Rastrollo; Anna E Ek; Ioannis Ioakeimidis; Ioanna Panagiota Kalafati; Ana Isabel Rito; Alexis Kyriacou; Anestis Dougkas; Julie‐Anne Nazare; Louise Seconda; Gillian Santorelli; Vassilios Fanos; Karri Silventoinen; Terho J\. Lehtimäki; George V\. Dedoussis; Anastasios N\. Delopoulos

Understanding obesity involves evaluating numerous contributing factors\. Collecting the necessary data for this can impose a significant burden on both research participants during clinical studies and real\-life deployments of digital tools aiding obesity management\. The BETTER4U project \(European Union&\#x27;s Horizon Europe, Grant Agreement ID 101080117\) introduces 36 behavioral and 9 living environment indicators designed to unobtrusively and efficiently capture daily life through passive monitoring using market\-available smartphones and smartwatches while accounting for environmental confounders\. This concise set, intended for dietitians, physical activity experts, and healthcare professionals as a standard for assessing obesity\-related behavior, summarizes the behavioral and environmental profile of a person with obesity/overweight\. We present the selected indicators, their selection and implementation methodology and the high\-level plan for their verification, describing their conceptual foundations and technical realization\. These indicators can be deployed in a modular framework: by transforming raw sensor data into structured, interpretable measures they provide a scalable foundation for long\-term monitoring of obesogenic behaviors, individual assessment, and evaluation of interventions targeting physical activity, diet, stress, and sleep\. The indicators are intended for an expert\-facing dashboard within the BETTER4U Intervention Platform, a participant\-side interface within the BETTER4U application, and as input to the BETTER4U AI\-based causal model, supporting relationship modeling between behavior, environment, and obesity outcomes to inform personalized interventions\. This work lays the basis for data\-driven validation of these indicators following the &quot;BETTER4ALL Pilot Study&quot; \(ClinicalTrials\.gov ID: NCT07120802\), ahead of their use in the BETTER4U RCT among individuals with obesity/overweight\.

## [Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query\-Template Identification](../publications/01d8fb4a30ee331230b7.md)

Paulo Pintor; Rogério Costa; José Moreira

Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection\. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution\. This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query\-template identification\. We construct query\-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple\-level Lineage and Why\-provenance across entire query results\. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors \(PSD\), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features\. We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \\\(12\{,\}500\\\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC\-DS query templates\. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available\. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test\-processing cost\.

## [Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu](../publications/01e285f14851474fc054.md)

Rakesh Kumar Sundararajan; Thangasundari Ramasamy

Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder\-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu\. Digital transformation and artificial intelligence \(AI\) offer promising solutions to persistent challenges, including inadequate cold\-chain infrastructure, limited traceability, intermediary\-dependent marketing and certification workflow inefficiencies\. This systematic review draws on evidence from 30 peer\-reviewed and institutional publications\. These sources were identified through a PRISMA\-compliant search of Scopus, Elsevier, Taylor &amp; Francis, Web of Science, IEEE, MDPI, Wiley, FAO, and government databases\. The findings indicate that AI\-enabled precision farming, machine learning\-based demand forecasting, Internet of Things\-enabled cold\-chain monitoring, and blockchain\-supported traceability improve production efficiency, market access and organic supply chain transparency\. However, widespread adoption is constrained by inadequate rural connectivity, limited digital literacy, incompatibility between digital platforms and Participatory Guarantee System certification workflows, and weak first\-mile infrastructure\. This review proposes the Digital Transformation and AI Readiness Framework for Organic Supply Chains \(DARF\-OSC\)\. DARF\-OSC is a five\-stage conceptual model that integrates Diffusion of Innovations theory with the Resource\-Based View\. Also, this review identifies five key research gaps and tiered policy recommendations for South Tamil Nadu\.

## [A comprehensive scientific overview of cement stabilization additives for oil wells](../publications/01e44f35105d129a7312.md)

Ageu da Silva Monteiro Freire; José Valderisso Alfredo de Carvalho; Carlos Eduardo de Araújo Padilha; Renata Martins Braga; Júlio Cézar de Oliveira Freitas

Abstract Additives play a fundamental role in the cementing of oil wells by enhancing the physical and chemical properties of cement slurries\. Thus, this study conducts a bibliometric analysis of scientific articles on oil well cementing over recent decades\. The bibliometric analysis was performed in the Scopus database, with 586 articles, of which only 218 were evaluated after a review process\. China, in addition to being the country with the highest number of publications, also boasts the journal and research institution with the most contributions\. Synthetic additives are utilized in 87% of the papers, natural additives in 11%, and a combination of natural and synthetic additives in 2%\. The primary natural additives include cellulose, lignin, and residues from rice and sugarcane\. The most frequently reported functions of additives in the literature are filtrate loss control, expansion agent, and set retarder\. Class G cement is predominant in the studies\. The main tests performed in the studies include compressive strength, rheological properties, thickening time, static fluid loss, and free fluid tests\. Among the natural additives, cellulose derivatives were the most widely investigated and demonstrated the greatest improvements in fluid\-loss control, rheology, and mechanical performance\. Lignin derivatives and biomass ashes, particularly rice husk ash, also stood out for increasing compressive strength, reducing permeability, and offering sustainable low\-carbon alternatives\. It is concluded that studies on natural additives for cement slurries still need to advance, as few works address their use, especially given the volume of waste generated worldwide\.

## [Digital\-green coupling coordination and firm labor productivity: evidence from Chinese listed companies](../publications/01e5af5fd1d07939f29f.md)

Juhao Lai; Guangxing Hu; Bin Li

Introduction This study examines whether the coordinated development of firms’ digital and green subsystems is associated with labor productivity\. Methods Using an unbalanced panel of Chinese A\-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we construct amultidimensional digital‐green coupling coordination \(DGCC\) index and estimate firm and year fixed‐effects models\. Results Higher DGCC is associated with higher labor productivity, and the result remains stable across alternative measures, fixed‐effects structures, inference procedures, additional controls, temporal‐ordering tests, and medium\-horizon changes\. The evidence further associates DGCC with a more highly educated workforce, a greater relative allocation of employees to technical functions, and a smaller administrative\-employment share\. The relationship varies with labor\-cost pressure, human‐capital levels, and routine‐task intensity\. Further analysis links DGCC to lower expense intensity and stronger cash realization\. Discussion These findings highlight the workforce, organizational, and operating adjustments that accompany firms’ coordinated digital and green development\.

## [Towards consumer\-oriented smart grids : investigating consumer perspectives on the adoption of smart technologies and services](../publications/01edca01b14769e8bb99.md)

Petteri Siitonen

Consumers are expected to play a central role in smart grids, and therefore, it is becoming increasingly important to identify and understand factors that influence consumer engagement in them through various smart grid technologies and services\. This dissertation focuses on investigating consumer opinions, awareness, and experiences of key smart grid technologies and services, as well as on analysing factors and variables that influence their adoption\. By providing insights for both theory and practice, the research carried out in this dissertation aims to support the development of consumer\-oriented smart grids and to inform efforts to promote the adoption of smart grid technologies and services\. The research conducted in the dissertation adopts both qualitative and quantitative methods\. First, consumer perspectives towards demand response are investigated using a systematic review and thematic synthesis of previous European demand response projects\. Secondly, to improve the understanding of the roles of trust and technological knowledge in affecting technology adoption in the smart grid context, a cross\-sectional online questionnaire survey of Finnish consumers is carried out, and the data are analysed using path analysis\. Lastly, a machine learning\-based social media sentiment analysis is conducted to examine how consumer opinions of various smart grid technologies and behaviours have changed in response to the 2022 energy crisis\. This dissertation contributes to the smart grid literature in several ways\. Firstly, by highlighting the importance of incorporating consumer perspectives into the design of demand response programs, this work provides insights that can inform the development of smart grid services that are compatible with consumers’ preferences\. Secondly, the research elucidates the mechanisms by which trust and technological knowledge may influence the adoption of smart grid technologies and discusses the potential implications for future research and practice\. Lastly, to shed light on how times of crisis can change public opinion on smart grids, it is investigated how the 2022 energy crisis affected Finnish consumers’ awareness and opinions of smart grid technologies and services\. The results of this dissertation can serve both researchers and practitioners in the development of consumer\-oriented smart grids and in informing efforts to increase the adoption of smart grid technologies and services\.

## [O prompt cego: um limite anterior à resposta da inteligência artificial no aconselhamento relacional](../publications/01ef2955b27fb267b85e.md)

Marcos Temistocles Duarte

Introdução: Pessoas em sofrimento relacional recorrem cada vez mais à inteligência artificial generativa para interpretar conflitos, redigir mensagens e decidir sobre separações\. A discussão atual enfatiza respostas incorretas, riscos de validação excessiva e a entrada de uma “terceira voz” nas relações, mas considera menos uma limitação anterior à resposta: o usuário só consegue incluir no prompt aquilo que está disponível à sua própria compreensão naquele momento\. Objetivo: Propor, como formulação teórico\-clínica, o conceito de prompt cego e discutir sua utilidade em psiquiatria e psicoterapia\. Método: Ensaio teórico\-clínico ilustrado por vinheta inteiramente fictícia, não derivada de paciente identificável\. Resultado: O prompt cego descreve perguntas estruturadas por omissões clinicamente relevantes que o usuário não reconhece, não mentaliza ou não consegue formular sob intensa ativação afetiva\. Propõem\-se quatro tipos heurísticos de ponto cego: não formulado, contraditório, relacional e dependente do estado\. Mesmo coerente com o problema apresentado, a resposta da inteligência artificial pode reforçar fechamento decisório prematuro, atribuições unilaterais ou redução de um conflito diádico a traços individuais\. Propõe\-se que o clínico examine a função, o enquadramento, as ausências e os efeitos posteriores da consulta\. Conclusão: O limite clínico pode surgir antes da resposta\. O prompt deve ser tratado como material clínico e como mapa provisório do que o paciente consegue e ainda não consegue pensar\.

## [Route\-Dependent Correction and Credibility Curvature in Online Electric\-Vehicle Misinformation: A Computational Test of Quantum Sociodynamics](../publications/01f409be0dc842d39751.md)

Muhammad Talut

Corrections to electric\-vehicle \(EV\) misinformation are usually analysed as functions of content, source credibility or timing, yet the same correction can be read differently depending on the relation through which it travels\. This article develops Quantum Sociodynamics \(QSD\), a gauge\-covariant formulation in which actor orientations are complex states, relations are directed symbolic transporters, response is signed, and inconsistency between communication routes is represented by holonomy around closed cycles\. It then asks two deliberately separate questions\. Stage A tests whether a reduced QSD estimator recovers three signed couplings, relational memory, institutional\-shock magnitude and a baseline response\. Recovery is assessed across 80 baseline replicates and an additional stress grid spanning higher observation noise, shorter panels, fewer actors, missing phase observations, uncertain shock timing, heterogeneous memory, weak couplings and structural misspecification\. Stage B is an explicitly exploratory analysis of 101 EV\-related historical Birdwatch/Community Notes linked to 75 posts, 3,999 aggregate ratings, 145 status milestones and 139 cited\-source records\. Because closed directed cycles are not observable in these data, formal holonomy is not measured\. Stage B instead evaluates a clearly labelled provenance\-memory inconsistency index constructed from cited\-source entropy, author\-history mismatch and source\-type count, together with a full weight\-sensitivity grid and a component decomposition\. Sparse\-event estimation uses Firth penalised logistic regression with cluster bootstrap stability intervals, and inference is reported with effect sizes, confidence intervals and false\-discovery\-rate control rather than binary support labels\. Baseline synthetic recovery was strong \(true\-estimated correlations 0\.986 to 0\.998; parameter RMSE 0\.005 to 0\.032; coupling sign recovered in every replicate\) and degraded in an interpretable way under stress\. Empirically, longer notes were associated with higher odds of platform resolution and greater cited\-domain count with lower odds; the inconsistency index was associated with lower aggregate rating weight but not with greater reason\-tag disagreement\. Repeated grouped and rolling\-origin cross\-validation, benchmarked against an explicit prevalence model, showed no predictive gain from the index over a simpler provenance\-memory specification\. QSD is therefore computationally recoverable but empirically undecided in its distinctive claim: deciding it requires individual ratings, authentic exposure sequences and complete directed cycles\. The contribution is a methodological boundary analysis for relational models of low\-carbon technology communication, not a predictive instrument for platform governance\.

## [Effect of Digital Project Management Practices on Project Delivery Success: A Case of Rusumo Cross\-Border Market Project in Kirehe District Under Rwanda Transport Development Agency](../publications/01faa2e2cc62a7601820.md)

Karemera Nathalie; Sam Bazimya

The study examined the effect of Digital Project Management \(DPM\) Practices on Project Delivery Success, focusing on the Rusumo Cross\-Border Market Project in Kirehe District under the Rwanda Transport Development Agency \(RTDA\)\. The study was guided by four objectives: to evaluate the effect of digital planning and scheduling practices on project delivery success; to examine how digital collaboration and communication platforms influence stakeholder coordination and delivery outcomes; to assess the effect of digital risk management practices on project success; and to analyze how digital monitoring and control dashboards affect timeliness, cost management, and overall project delivery success\. The study was anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\), Resource\-Based View \(RBV\), and Stakeholder Theory, which collectively explain technology adoption, organizational capability utilization, and stakeholder engagement in project environments\. A mixed methods approach employing descriptive and correlational research designs was adopted\. The target population comprised 251 project stakeholders, including project managers, engineers, technicians, supervisors, and traders’ representatives\. Using the Taro Yamane formula, a sample size of 154 respondents was determined and selected through stratified and purposive sampling techniques\. Data were collected using structured questionnaires, structured interviews, and documentary review\. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analysis with SPSS, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically\.

## [LONG\-DISTANCE WRITING EXPERIMENT: MAPPING MAKASSAR IN HUMAN LITERARY CREATION AND GENERATIVE AI TEXTS THROUGH A HYBRID AUTHORSHIP FRAMEWORK](../publications/01fce52c7241de190e7b.md)

Faisal Oddang

Penelitian ini menyajikan eksperimen penulisan jarak jauh untuk menganalisis secara komparatif representasi kota Makassar dalam dua korpus sastra yang berbeda: karya yang ditulis oleh manusia dan teks yang dihasilkan oleh Kecerdasan Buatan \(AI\)\. Maraknya penggunaan AI dalam produksi kreatif memicu pertanyaan epistemologis mendasar mengenai kepengarangan dan kapasitas mesin untuk menggambarkan entitas budaya\. Makassar, dengan karakteristik sosio\-spasialnya yang unik, berfungsi sebagai studi kasus untuk menguji perbedaan antara representasi yang didorong oleh pengalaman manusia dan yang berasal dari algoritma\.Dengan memanfaatkan Large Language Models \(LLMs\) seperti ChatGPT menggunakan perintah yang identik dan dirancang dengan cermat, penelitian ini akan mengumpulkan korpus AI untuk disandingkan secara langsung dan kritis dengan korpus sastra yang sudah ada yang ditulis oleh manusia\.Dengan menerapkan analisis teks komputasi tingkat lanjut \(pemodelan topik, stilometri, analisis sentimen/leksikal\) bersamaan dengan pembacaan cermat \(close reading\) secara kualitatif, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membedakan pola tematik, stilistik, dan linguistik yang unik di dalam masing\-masing korpus\. Temuan yang diantisipasi akan menjelaskan kemampuan dan keterbatasan generatif AI dalam memproduksi konten yang bernuansa budaya, mengungkap potensi bias dalam data pelatihan, dan berkontribusi secara substansial pada konsep kreativitas dan representasi urban digital yang terus berkembang, terutama di bidang Humaniora Digital dan estetika komputasional\.

## [Beyond Forecast Accuracy: A Responsible AI Framework for Provenance\-Aware Fine Jewelry Retail Planning](../publications/020c8e88600372129451.md)

James Hutson2 Katayoun Kiarsi1\*

Fine jewelry retailers must reconcile uncertain demand, high\-value inventory, complex material histories, and expectations of responsible sourcing\. This article develops a responsible artificial intelligence framework that connects demand forecasting, provenance evidence, and governance within retail planning\. A conceptual framework\-development approach informed by design\-science research combines a targeted literature update through October 9, 2026, with descriptive analysis of published market statistics and an external retail forecasting benchmark\. The analysis distinguishes original design propositions from empirical findings reported by other researchers; no retailer\-level experiment or environmental impact assessment was conducted\. Three sourced bar charts illustrate changing gold jewelry consumption and the methodological relevance of inventory\-based model evaluation\. The resulting architecture integrates data inputs, predictive analytics, provenance and traceability, ethical governance, and human\-reviewed decisions with feedback\. Five design principles and five testable propositions specify how forecasts can inform assortment, replenishment, allocation, and sourcing while preserving evidence quality and accountability\. The framework shifts evaluation from forecast accuracy alone toward decision quality under explicit operational and provenance constraints\. It also separates inventory efficiency, sourcing documentation, and environmental outcomes, preventing improvements in one category from being misrepresented as proof of another\. Managerial implications include staged implementation, evidence\-qualified sourcing rules, meaningful review authority, and documented overrides\. Future validation should compare complete decision policies, preserve temporal information boundaries, measure calibrated reliance, and assess environmental consequences independently\. The article contributes a sector\-specific architecture and evaluation agenda for accountable retail intelligence without claiming that the integrated framework has already demonstrated operational or sustainability benefits across fine jewelry businesses and markets\.

## [The Application of Time Series Forecasting Model for Carbon Emissions Prediction in Electrical Grid: A Step Toward Climate Action](../publications/0216e09d2b7f2479b27e.md)

Keat Soon Tioh; Khim Chen Jason Tan

This study evaluates the forecasting performance of three models of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average \(ARIMA\), Prophet, and Bi\-directional Long Short\-Term Memory \(BiLSTM\) in predicting CO2 emissions from the electricity grid in the United States\. Using a real dataset from the California Independent System Operator \(CAISO\) that records CO2 emissions at five\-minute intervals between 2018 and 2020, the data underwent preprocessing steps including outlier removal, missing value imputation, and feature selection before model training\. ARIMA parameters were determined using statistical tests such as ACF, Partial Autocorrelation Function \(PACF\), and Augmented Dickey Fuller \(ADF\), while Prophet addressed seasonality and calendar effects\. BiLSTM, a deep learning model, was applied to capture complex temporal dependencies and non\-linear relationships in the dataset\. The models were evaluated using Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\) and Root Mean Square Error \(RMSE\) metrics\. The results show that BiLSTM achieved the lowest error values \(MAE: 266\.726; RMSE: 429\.228\), outperforming ARIMA \(MAE: 1728\.797; RMSE: 2203\.464\) and Prophet \(MAE: 831\.346; RMSE: 1102\.884\)\. These findings indicate that BiLSTM is more effective in modeling and forecasting highly variable and long\-term CO2 emission data\. The study provides valuable insights for researchers and energy sector practitioners by demonstrating that machine learning\-based forecasting can support carbon reduction initiatives and improve decision\-making for electricity grid management\. Moreover, the inclusion of a near\-real\-time alert system and dashboard design enhances the study’s practical relevance\. Despite being limited to U\.S\. grid data, this research underscores the potential of BiLSTM models in achieving environmentally sustainable energy operations through accurate and timely CO2 emission forecasting\.

## [Comparison of Three Techniques for Donor Site Coverage after Vascularized Free Fibula Flap \(VFFF\) and Radial Forearm Free Flap \(RFFF\): A Retrospective Study](../publications/022382473013d31abd19.md)

Sara Silvestri; Federica Sobrero; Michela Omedè; Giorgia Cigna; Massimo Fasolis

The vascularized free fibula flap and radial forearm free flap are two workhorse flaps in head and neck reconstruction\. This study compared functional and aesthetic outcomes for donor site closure after harvesting radial forearm or fibula free flaps\. In a retrospective analysis of 45 patients, three techniques were evaluated: a full\-thickness skin graft, a mono\-layer Integra® dermal substitute plus a split\-thickness skin graft, and a double\-layer Integra® with a deferred split\-thickness graft\. Patient satisfaction scores were significantly higher for the full\-thickness graft and the double\-layer Integra® technique compared to the mono\-layer Integra®\. The surgeon’s evaluation found superior aesthetic results for the full\-thickness graft over the mono\-layer Integra®\. Analysis of functional outcomes using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand \(DASH\) score and the Foot and Ankle Disability Index \(FADI\) score showed no significant differences among the three techniques; however, these functional analyses were exploratory, with DASH available for 34 patients and FADI for only 11, so the absence of significant differences should be interpreted as &quot;no difference detected&quot; rather than as demonstrated equivalence\. Therefore, while functional recovery was comparable across these techniques, the full\-thickness skin graft provided the most favorable aesthetic result for donor site reconstruction in this cohort\.

## [Gratitude and happiness among university students: a cross\-sectional study in teacher education](../publications/0228b41ce974b927d66b.md)

Hernán Vicente Rojas\-Moscoso; Adrián Orlando Manrique\-Rojas; Naylea Nayeli Velasquez Cutipa; Pilar Valeria Zapana\-Aguilar; Kevin Mario Laura\-De La Cruz

Introduction This study examined the association between gratitude and happiness among education students at a public university in Tacna, Peru, including four dimensions of happiness: positive sense of life, life satisfaction, personal fulfillment, and joy of living\. Methods A quantitative, non\-experimental, cross\-sectional correlational design was used\. Participants were 507 students \(313 women and 194 men\) aged 18–37 years\. Gratitude and happiness were assessed using the Lima Gratitude Scale and the Lima Happiness Scale\. Internal consistency and associations were examined using Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha, model\-based omega, Spearman&\#x27;s rho, bootstrap confidence intervals, and Holm\-adjusted p \-values\. Results Internal consistency was good for gratitude \(α = 0\.807, 95% bootstrap CI \[0\.777, 0\.831\]; ω = 0\.823\) and excellent for happiness \(α = 0\.942, 95% bootstrap CI \[0\.933, 0\.950\]; ω = 0\.943\)\. Gratitude was positively associated with overall happiness, Spearman&\#x27;s ρ = 0\.447, 95% bootstrap CI \[0\.368, 0\.519\], p &lt; 0\.001\. Dimension\-specific correlations ranged from ρ = 0\.351 for personal fulfillment to ρ = 0\.420 for joy of living; all remained significant after Holm adjustment\. Excluding the participant with one reconstructed item response produced a similar overall correlation \(ρ = 0\.448\)\. Discussion Gratitude showed a robust, moderately sized positive association with happiness and its four dimensions among teacher education students\. However, the cross\-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the single\-institution convenience sample limits generalizability\. Longitudinal and multi\-institutional studies are needed to determine the temporal direction and broader applicability of these associations\.

## [Causal analysis of Alzheimer’s disease molecular data](../publications/022983e160e1d8bcecd8.md)

Rebecca Ting Jiin Loo; Enrico Glaab

Abstract Background Genome\-wide studies have revealed many molecular associations with Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\), but association alone does not identify cause, mechanism, or treatable target\. This review surveys methods used to infer causal relationships from AD molecular data and assesses their core findings\. Main body We reviewed causal\-inference work applied to AD genetics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, covering Mendelian randomization, probabilistic graphical and Bayesian network models, causal reasoning over knowledge graphs, time\-resolved methods including Granger causality, and mediation analysis\. Genetic\-instrument and network methods have identified candidate causal molecules, mapped pathways, and supported some drug targets\. However, several associations reported in observational studies have not been supported by genetic analyses, and apparent disagreements between studies often reflect differences in the estimand, the tissue from which genetic instruments are derived, or assumptions of the methods used\. Conclusion Brain\-relevant genetic instruments, longitudinal multi\-omics, single\-cell resolution, and triangulation across methods are needed to separate cause from consequence and to prioritize intervention targets for experimental validation\.

## [THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL IMAGING TECHNOLOGY IN THE UNIVERSITY FINANCIAL REIMBURSEMENT PROCESS: A CASE STUDY OF UNIVERSITY N](../publications/023811493d5cc66be535.md)

Tian Shen; XiaoYing Liao; JiaJia Zhu; Ting Pu; KeWei Liu

Faculty members and students at many newly established universities often find the reimbursement process confusing, and repeated errors end up slowing down the entire procedure\. Drawing on the actual situation at University N, this study looks closely at where its financial reimbursement system falls short and proposes a set of concrete measures to improve it, in the hope of offering a workable reference for the digital transformation of reimbursement work at similar institutions\. The core idea is to use AI video generation tools to produce short demonstration clips of the reimbursement workflow, and to examine whether artificial intelligence and digital imaging technologies can make university reimbursement more intuitive, more carefully managed, and more intelligent\. The findings indicate that these technologies do help: they raise reimbursement efficiency, bring down operating costs, and strengthen the control of compliance risks\.

## [A Machine Learning Framework for Objective Definition and Projection of Meteorological Seasons: An Application to the Indian Subcontinent](../publications/024175a8d2bbc344171f.md)

Jacopo Grassi; Elisa Palazzi; Jost von Hardenberg; Paolo Davini

Abstract Meteorological seasons are typically defined through fixed calendar intervals or region‐specific thresholds, yet such approaches fail to capture the actual variability of the annual cycle\. Here we present a machine learning framework that objectively detects meteorological seasons and projects their future evolution\. The method combines Radially Constrained Clustering \(RCC\) to identify seasons from reanalysis data with a supervised Multinomial Logistic Regression Classifier \(MLRC\) that allows these definitions to be applied also to climate model projections\. We use the Indian subcontinent as a detailed proof of concept region since it has established operational references for monsoon onset and withdrawal, and it includes contrasting seasonal regimes, from monsoon dominated lowlands to high mountain regions influenced by winter disturbances\. The RCC‐derived seasons recover the main operational seasonal phases adopted by the India Meteorological Department, while also providing consistent definitions of transition periods\. Evaluation against a CMIP6 multi‐model ensemble shows that models capture the seasonal cycle with high skill in Central and Southern India, but exhibit lower performance in complex mountainous regions\. Future projections indicate a robust lengthening of the monsoon season, primarily due to delayed withdrawal, and a concurrent shortening of winter, driven by the loss of days in December–January\. These findings highlight the asymmetric nature of seasonal shifts under global warming and demonstrate the potential of data‐driven approaches to provide objective and reproducible definitions of seasonality\.

## [Prediction of Material Removal Rate for Chemical Mechanical Planarization using Bayesian Additive Regression Trees](../publications/02462d7cca87310cffd7.md)

Han Bao; Xiyuan Qian

Chemical Mechanical Planarization \(CMP\) is a critical surface processing technique in semiconductor manufacturing, where the Material Removal Rate \(MRR\) plays a vital role in determining process quality\. Traditional physics\-driven MRR models based on Preston&\#x27;s Equation have difficulty capturing the complex nonlinear relationships and high\-order interactions present in CMP data\. This paper applies Bayesian Additive Regression Trees \(BART\) to CMP MRR prediction\. BART uses a Bayesian sum\-of\-trees framework to model nonlinear effects and interactions while providing posterior uncertainty estimates and variable\-importance information\. Quantitative comparisons on the validation set show that BART achieves the best predictive performance, outperforming the strongest baseline model by 11% in terms of RMSE\. Model reliability and interpretation are examined through residual diagnostics, MCMC convergence checks, hyperparameter\-sensitivity analysis, omnibus covariate testing, and variable\-importance analysis\. These results indicate that BART is effective for CMP MRR prediction and can help identify process variables that warrant monitoring and diagnostic attention\.

## [AXBOROT MAYDONI GLOBALLASHUVINING SHAXS MA’NAVIY MADANIYATI SHAKLANISHIGA TA’SIRI](../publications/0253f39dd6f8c59a633e.md)

ZAMIRA BAXTIYOROVNA RAXMATOVA

This article examines the impact of the globalization of the information sphere on the formation of an individual’s spiritual culture\. It analyzes the interrelation among globalization, spirituality, and culture, and discusses the significance of factors that emerge in connection with mass culture, individualism, and egocentrism—phenomena inherently linked with globalization\. Reflections are offered on their role in contemporary sociocultural development\.

## [DDoS HUJUMLARINI ANIQLASHDA SUN&\#x27;IY INTELLEKT MODELLARI VA ALGORITMLARI](../publications/025449aa28567334b00b.md)

Aliboyev Farrux Sa&\#x27;dulla o&\#x27;g&\#x27;li

Mazkur maqolada taqsimlangan xizmat ko&\#x27;rsatishni rad etish \(Distributed Denial of Service — DDoS\) hujumlarini aniqlashda sun&\#x27;iy intellekt, mashinali o&\#x27;qitish va chuqur o&\#x27;qitish modellaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi\. ## [Accounting and analytical systems as a tool to support management decisions in the context of digital business transformation](../publications/025eeada7e4cc8fe47ec.md)

Halyna Matskiv; Наталія Райтер

У статті досліджено теоретичні, методичні та практичні аспекти функціонування обліково\-аналітичних систем як інструменту підтримки управлінських рішень в умовах цифрової трансформації бізнесу\. Обґрунтовано, що цифровізація економіки та розвиток інформаційно\-комунікаційних технологій змінюють роль обліково\-аналітичних систем, які трансформуються з інструмента обліку в інтегровану інформаційну платформу, здатну забезпечувати формування, накопичення, обробку, аналіз, прогнозування та візуалізацію даних для прийняття оперативних, тактичних і стратегічних управлінських рішень\. Узагальнено наукові підходи до визначення сутності обліково\-аналітичної системи та визначено її місце в системі управління підприємством\. Досліджено вплив цифрової трансформації на розвиток обліково\-аналітичних систем і доведено необхідність інтеграції фінансової та нефінансової інформації в єдиному цифровому середовищі\. Встановлено, що використання ERP\-систем, Business Intelligence, Big Data, штучного інтелекту, хмарних технологій, роботизованої автоматизації бізнес\-процесів та електронного документообігу підвищує оперативність, достовірність і аналітичну цінність інформації для управління\. Запропоновано авторську концепцію інтегрованої обліково\-аналітичної системи підтримки управлінських рішень, що ґрунтується на взаємодії інформаційного, облікового, аналітичного, інтелектуального та управлінського рівнів\. Визначено основні напрями розвитку обліково\-аналітичних систем, серед яких інтеграція інформаційних потоків, розвиток прогнозної аналітики, автоматизація облікових процесів, посилення інформаційної безпеки, використання системи ключових показників ефективності та розвиток цифрових компетентностей персоналу\. Запропоновано систему показників оцінювання ефективності обліково\-аналітичної системи, яка дає змогу комплексно оцінити її вплив на якість інформаційного забезпечення, швидкість обробки даних, рівень автоматизації бізнес\-процесів, обґрунтованість управлінських рішень і результативність діяльності підприємства\.

## [Regime\-Dependent Systematic Risk of Sustainability\-Oriented Investments: Evidence from Borsa Istanbul](../publications/02667a1e40725fbfb94b.md)

Tutku ÜNKARACALAR

This study examines whether the systematic\-risk exposure of sustainability\-oriented investments varies across market states in Borsa Istanbul\. Rather than treating sustainability as an unconditional source of superior performance or financial resilience, the analysis focuses on the regime dependence of market sensitivity\. A two\-state Markov Regime\-Switching Model combined with a Regime\-Switching Capital Asset Pricing Model \(CAPM\) is applied to an equally weighted, dynamically updated sustainability\-oriented portfolio over January 2015–December 2025\. Portfolio and market returns are expressed as U\.S\. dollar\-denominated excess returns\. The results identify two persistent market states with markedly different volatility characteristics\. The sustainability\-oriented portfolio exhibits a beta of 0\.81 in the low\-volatility regime and 1\.18 in the high\-volatility regime, corresponding to a point\-estimate increase of 0\.37\. The high\-volatility state is also characterised by negative average excess returns and a return variance 8\.5 times that of the low\-volatility state\. These findings provide evidence that the systematic\-risk exposure of sustainability\-oriented investments is strongly regime\-dependent\. However, because portfolio composition and other firm characteristics cannot be fully separated from sustainability status, the findings are interpreted as regime\-dependent associations rather than as evidence of a causal sustainability\-induced resilience effect\. The study complements recent regime\-switching evidence from Borsa Istanbul by emphasising dynamic portfolio membership, portfolio\-construction sensitivity, and a more conservative interpretation of sustainability\-related risk dynamics\.

## [From Webinar Participant to EFL Lecturer: Identity Construction through Pedagogy, AI, and Research](../publications/026d7cff6d491536d420.md)

Endah Kurtianti

Professional identity has been widely examined in language teacher education, yet little is known about how sustained participation in webinar ecosystems integrates pedagogical learning, artificial intelligence \(AI\) literacy, and research engagement during the transition from master’s student to lecturer\. This narrative inquiry explored how webinar\-based professional development contributed to the professional identity construction of Nada \(pseudonym\), an Indonesian EFL lecturer who began attending webinars as a master’s student in 2020\. Data were collected through three in\-depth narrative interviews and supporting documents and were analyzed using thematic narrative analysis\. The findings show a cumulative identity trajectory\. First, self\-directed webinar participation expanded from thesis\-related learning into sustained professional learning, networking, and academic socialization\. Second, exposure to lecturer\-development and research communities enabled Nada to anticipate academic responsibilities and reposition herself from a participant to a lecturer\. Third, pedagogical learning, AI literacy, and research engagement became mutually reinforcing identity resources, reflected in more concise online teaching, greater confidence in AI\-assisted material preparation, publication activity, and the acquisition of a competitive early\-career research grant\. The study offers an original temporal account of webinars as digital communities of practice in which professional learning, possible future selves, and academic recognition jointly support identity negotiation\. It highlights the value of webinar\-based development for preparing EFL educators for integrated teaching, technological, and research roles\.

## [Where Latents Belong and How They Flow: Joint Identification of Structural Roles](../publications/02814e749791f1830293.md)

Xintong Li; Kun Zhang; Yujia Zheng

Latent factors in dynamical systems can play different roles across observations and time\. For example, an idea in a group meeting may be expressed by only some participants, inherit information from earlier discussions, and shape what is said next\. We formalize this notion as the structural role of a latent factor, describing where it is expressed, whether it receives influence from the past, and whether it transmits influence to the future\. The main challenge is correspondence, since the three structures may be identified under different permutations, while a structural role is defined only when they are aligned to the same latent coordinate\. We show that, under suitable structural and variability conditions, all three roles are jointly identifiable under a common permutation at each time point\. Guided by this theory, we develop RoleTrace, a framework that traces structural roles in a shared latent coordinate system\. Synthetic experiments validate structural recovery, while experiments on multiparty meetings examine the identified roles in real sequential interactions\.

## [A game\-level difficulty\-aware curriculum learning framework for progressive graph neural network training in distribution network fault diagnosis](../publications/0283331d183a2f280ce4.md)

Tianxiao Peng

Abstract Graph neural networks \(GNNs\) have shown considerable potential for distribution network fault diagnosis; however, conventional empirical risk minimization with randomly ordered samples may lead to unstable convergence and substantial performance degradation when complex network topologies and severely corrupted measurements are introduced during the early stages of training\. To address this issue, this paper proposes a game\-level difficulty\-aware curriculum learning framework for progressive GNN training\. The framework first performs offline sample difficulty evaluation by combining degree\-distribution entropy, which characterizes topological complexity, with inverse signal\-to\-noise ratio \(SNR\), which represents measurement corruption\. The resulting coupled difficulty score is then used by an online pacing function to progressively introduce training samples from easy to hard\. Dynamic loss reweighting is further incorporated to balance previously learned easy samples and newly introduced difficult samples throughout training\. The framework is evaluated on seven\-category fault diagnosis datasets generated using the IEEE 33\-bus and IEEE 123\-bus distribution systems under different measurement noise levels, transition resistances, load variations, and missing\-data conditions\. On the IEEE 33\-bus system at 20 dB SNR, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 91\.55% and a Macro\-F1 score of 91\.20%, outperforming the standard GCN by 11\.10 and 11\.32% points, respectively\. It also enters a relatively stable loss region approximately 25 epochs earlier than standard GCN training and maintains improved diagnostic performance when up to 30% of the nodal measurements are missing\. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the accuracy, convergence stability, and robustness of GNN\-based distribution network fault diagnosis\. The present SNR\-based difficulty measure uses clean reference signals available in controlled simulations; practical black\-box deployment therefore requires estimated noise indicators, such as filtering residuals, blind SNR estimation, or model\-based predictive uncertainty\.

## [CD38\-targeted therapies in kidney disease: evidence maturity, disease\-stage dependence, and biomarker\-guided retreatment](../publications/029323b7a2512f21a9d8.md)

Peidong Feng; Xiaoyong Yu

CD38 targeting can reach antibody\-secreting cells that persist after B\-cell depletion, along with selected natural killer\-cell and other immune\-cell subsets\. This narrative review examines CD38\-targeted antibodies in immune\-mediated and monoclonal immunoglobulin\-related kidney diseases and kidney transplantation\. It asks what clinical studies establish, how disease stage may affect response durability, and whether biomarkers can guide retreatment\. Evidence differs by agent, regimen, and outcome\. The most mature randomized evidence with kidney\-organ outcomes comes from daratumumab\-based combination therapy in immunoglobulin light\-chain \(AL\) amyloidosis, a plasma\-cell disorder\. In other kidney and transplant indications, early\-phase randomized trials and uncontrolled studies show immunologic, tissue, or proteinuria responses, but long\-term kidney or graft benefit remains unproven\. Disease duration, previous treatment, and residual tissue injury may help explain variable responses, although treatment selection by disease stage has not been validated\. Biomarkers measure distinct aspects of response and can support monitoring; changes alone do not establish pathogenic\-cell depletion or justify retreatment\. Biomarker\-guided dosing was feasible in a selected transplant cohort and requires comparative validation\. Clinical interpretation must remain specific to the studied antibody and regimen\. Research priorities include trials with kidney and graft outcomes, prospective patient selection, comparisons of treatment strategies, validation of biomarker\-guided retreatment, and cumulative safety during repeated therapy\.

## [Trustworthy intelligent automation for human\-automation teaming in flight operations](../publications/029fde1248be35047cba.md)

Cho Yin Yiu

Automation has been extensively used in flight operations to enhance work efficiency and alleviate the cognitive workload of operators during demanding tasks such as manual flying\. As automation has become increasingly reliable in the past decades, pilots are now supervisors of automation rather than operators\. However, pilots might experience a decline in vigilance over time and eventually become delinked from the control loop, posing a significant safety threat to flight operations\. Hence, identifying human out\-of\-the\-loop \(OOTL\) in the cockpit efficiently is critical to ensure flight safety while not overloading human operators\. Therefore, this thesis seeks an integrated cockpit automation solution with neuroergonomics, cockpit/air\-ground interaction, and artificial intelligence \(AI\) to achieve human\-automation teaming \(HAT\) through balancing human and task performance with a minimal trade\-off in cognitive workload\. The first study of this thesis focuses on an integrated empirical appraisal of human and task performance of pilots using electroencephalography \(EEG\), reaction time, and NASA Task Load Index \(TLX\)\. Twenty\-four cadet pilots were recruited to accomplish a flight task on an Airbus A320 flight simulator with different levels of automation \(LOA\)\. The results from the EEG indicated that partial automation raises pilots&\#x27; engagement and reduces pilots&\#x27; drowsiness\. The reaction time was also significantly shorter, with a nonsignificant increase in the NASA\-TLX score\. Furthermore, a Neurobehavioural Performance Index \(NBPI\) for automation was proposed and validated to evaluate human and task performance and understand human OOTL through the underlying cognitive mechanisms\. The results suggested that future cockpit automation designs should consider an effective task distribution for HAT\. The second study of this thesis proposes an adaptive automation framework based on EEG spectral features and spatiotemporal deep learning with 2D/3D Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\) and Long\-Short Term Memory \(LSTM\) to keep pilots in the loop\. Our results indicated that the proposed two\-stage 2D CNN\-LSTM model with stacked images yields a test accuracy of 0\.9918\. To ensure safe applications in high\-stakes domains like aviation, the Shapley additive explanations were adopted to strengthen the interpretability of the model\. High delta and theta waves with low beta and gamma waves were found contributing positively to the OOTL state\. It indicates that the classification aligns with the theoretical background and is trustworthy\. The trustworthy adaptive deep learning model supports the dynamic automation configuration for improving human\-automation collaboration in cruising flights\. The model designed can support adaptive and dynamic automation configuration that tunes the level of automation to improve the human\-automation collaboration in cruising flights\. The third study of this thesis further advances intelligent automation through analysing the radio communication between pilots and air traffic controllers \(ATCOs\) using speech recognition and the reasoning capabilities of large language models \(LLMs\)\. For mutual verification, pilots are required to read back the instructions and clearance from ATCOs in a timely manner to mitigate communication errors\. Hence, speech recognition was utilised to transcribe radio communication in the readback procedure to text and identify vocal cues of human OOTL with the reasoning ability of LLMs\. Fine\-tuning was performed to enhance the aviation\-specific knowledge of the LLMs\. Furthermore, a chain\-of\-thought \(CoT\) and fault\-tolerant approach is adopted to design prompts to enhance the explainability for trustworthy applications of the model in safety\-critical domains\. To validate the framework in real\-time, a case study with ten pilots is conducted on an Airbus A320 simulator\. Our model successfully achieved an accuracy of 0\.8722 and 0\.8144 in offline and real\-time OOTL detection, respectively\. Based on dynamic automation tuning, the proposed Voice2Vigilance framework contributes by offering a trustworthy, non\-intrusive, and cockpit\-ready solution to achieve HAT in flight operations\. Summing up, this thesis examines human OOTL from multiple perspectives, including neuroergonomics, behaviour, and communication\. It contributes to safer flight operations with AI\-driven intelligent automation to keep pilots in the loop\.

## [Identification of Novel Raf\-kinase Inhibitors Using in Silico Virtual Screening for Targeted Cancer Therapy: In Silico Discovery of Novel RAF Kinase Inhibitors](../publications/02a76b22e179e81ec5d3.md)

Derouicha Matmour; Mimouna BEKKADOUR; Mohamed Salah Eddine Sahnine; Abderrahmane Maafa; Dalila MIRAOUI; Saliha BENABDI; Chahrazed Kandouci; Yassine Merad

Cancer has long been a major health problem; the overexpression of a protein kinase in cell signaling pathways is a common cause of it\. Targeted therapy has become a more popular focus of research due to its specificity towards particular protein kinases, compared to conventional chemotherapy, which does not differentiate between normal and cancerous cells\. B\-Raf is one such protein kinase that is commonly mutated in various types of cancer, including melanoma, colorectal cancer, and prostate cancer\. The objective of this study is to identify new inhibitors or candidates for anti\-protein kinase drugs targeting the Raf\-B protein using the dual strategy of screening novel compounds and repurposing drugs\. This research focused on using in silico drug design tools, such as Autodock vina, for virtual screening\. We docked and studied 13 candidates that had not yet passed the preclinical phase, and repurposed 29 medications that already had a temporary authorization for use for a different target\. This allowed us to predict their physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties, as well as their binding energies with the B\-RAF protein kinase \(ID: 6M3M\)\. Our results were promising, yielding three candidates with an excellent binding energy above \-10\.2 kcal/mol, with candidate 8b \(\-10\.7 kcal/mol, 6\-\(4\-\{\[\(phénylamino\)\(sulfanyl\) méthyl\]amino\}sphényl\)\-2\-phényl\-2,3,4,5\-tétrahydropyridazin\-3\-ol\) being the most promising\. We also found five molecules from the repurposing with a binding energy above \-9\.4 kcal/mol, with Uprosertib \(\-10\.3 kcal/mol, N\-\[\(2S\)\-1\-Amino\-3\-\(3,4\-difluorophenyl\)\-2\-propanyl\]\-5\-chloro\-4\-\(4\-chloro\-1\-methyl\-1H\-pyrazol\-5\-yl\)\-2\-furamide\) having the highest binding energy, it used in trials studying the treatment of Cancer, Melanoma, Solid Tumours, Cervical Cancer, and HER2/Neu Negative, among others\. Importantly, none of these candidates were predicted to pass the blood\-brain barrier, making them harmless to the central nervous system\. A QSAR study is recommended to provide valuable insights into the ligand\-protein interactions and potentially optimize the design of these promising molecules with enhanced potency and selectivity\. Also, it is important to conduct further in vitro and in vivo studies to verify their efficacy and safety\.

## [Robust Federated Learning with Integrated Access Control for Distributed Edge Cloud Big Data Systems](../publications/02ac0f8d1684c18133a3.md)

Vinod K\. Barupati; Shivshankar M Nagrik

Federated learning is a distributed machine learning paradigm in which participating devices or edge nodes train a shared model without transferring their raw data to a central repository\. This property makes federated learning attractive for edge cloud big data environments where data are geographically distributed, continuously generated, heterogeneous, and subject to privacy requirements\. However, decentralization also introduces security and governance challenges\. An attacker may impersonate a participant, submit poisoned model updates, exploit weak permissions, infer private information from model updates, or compromise an edge node\. Robust federated learning therefore requires more than an aggregation algorithm; it requires coordinated access control, privacy protection, participant validation, secure communication, and resilience against malicious behavior\. This review examines the integration of federated learning with access control for distributed edge cloud big data systems\. It discusses the foundations of federated learning, edge intelligence, role based and attribute based access control, threat models, robust aggregation, secure aggregation, privacy preservation, communication efficiency, scalability, and application requirements\. The review also compares major security mechanisms and identifies research directions for adaptive authorization, decentralized trust, privacy preserving identity management, resource aware robustness, and explainable security decisions\. An integrated architecture is proposed in which identity, role, attributes, device state, data sensitivity, and training behaviour are jointly considered before model updates are accepted\. Such an approach can provide a practical security layer for collaborative learning while retaining the principal benefit of federated learning: keeping sensitive data close to their source\.

## [The impact of digital technology on green economies](../publications/02ac94b16541f9a9bcd0.md)

Botond Géza Kálmán; Zsuzsanna Szeiner; Szilvia Valéria Módosné Szalai

Introduction Digital agriculture is regarded as an important instrument for achieving green economies, with the potential to raise productivity while reducing environmental impacts\. This study explores how digitalization in agriculture affects greenhouse gas emissions, pesticide use and productivity\. Methods The research uses a mixed\-methods design\. Quantitative analysis draws on international environmental and economic indicators for approximately 180 countries between 2000 and 2023 \(415 country\-year observations\), combining Spearman correlations, regression models with GDP interaction terms, and K\-means cluster analysis\. A qualitative case study of digital agriculture in Latin America complements the statistical findings\. Results Digital infrastructure is strongly associated with the adoption of agricultural digital technologies, and smart farming investment is associated with better economic performance of the agricultural sector\. Investment in digital agriculture shows a positive association with both emissions and pesticide use, while the interaction with GDP is negative and significant\. Cluster analysis confirms that countries with higher GDP and stronger digital infrastructure achieve more balanced environmental outcomes\. Discussion The environmental benefits of digital agriculture are conditional on economic capacity\. In economically advanced settings, digital technologies reduce resource use, waste and emissions; in economically constrained regions, higher output can offset the environmental gains\. Digital agricultural transformation therefore offers opportunities for sustainable development, but its success depends on equitable access to digital technologies and on policy support that mitigates the trade\-off between productivity and environmental protection\.

## [Mortalidad infantil y residuos sólidos en los cantones del Guayas, Ecuador \(2016\-2023\)](../publications/02b0b9f80ed9f6067b4f.md)

Cinthya Succety Patiño Rojas; Carmen Graciela Urgilés Carabajo

The study analyzes the socio\-environmental and economic determinants of infant mortality in the 25 cantons of the province of Guayas between 2016 and 2023\. The research is based on the persistence of territorial inequalities in child health associated with solid waste management and local economic capacity\. The study uses a longitudinal ecological design based on panel data for the cantons, combining descriptive statistics, thematic mapping, and the estimation of a fixed\-effects model with robust standard errors grouped by unit\. The model specification was tested using heteroscedasticity, autocorrelation, and cross\-sectional dependence tests to ensure the consistency of the estimates\. The results show that the rate of solid waste per capita is positively and significantly linked to income\-related infant mortality, while cantonal GDP shows a similarly significant negative relationship\. Taken together, these associations suggest that children&\#x27;s health is determined both by exposure to degraded environments and by the economic capacity of the territories\. Hence, the priority is to strengthen waste management, investment in sanitation, and institutional capacities to reduce health gaps between cantons\. It is also proposed that future research incorporate microenvironmental variables and spatial indicators to better understand how environment, territory, and child health are intertwined\.

## [Personal Hygiene Behaviors and Socioeconomic Determinants of Child Undernutrition: A National Cross\-Sectional Study in Indonesia](../publications/02b77c31b628aed612d1.md)

Yoyok Bekti Prasetyo; Rendy Kavalera Hakim; Wan Marina Wan Ismail; Haliza Hasan; Nur Melizza; Henny Dwi Susanti; Ika Rizki Anggraini

Background\. Child undernutrition remains a major public health concern in Indonesia\. Evidence on the roles of household environmental and socioeconomic factors, based on nationally representative data analyzed using appropriate complex survey methods, remains limited\. This study examined the associations between these factors and stunting, wasting, and underweight among Indonesian children under five years\. Methods\. A cross\-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the 2022 Indonesian Nutrition Status Survey \(SSGI\), which represents approximately 17\.1 million children under 5\. Survey\-weighted descriptive statistics, Rao\-Scott adjusted χ² tests, and multivariable logistic regression accounting for the complex sampling design were performed to estimate adjusted odds ratios \(AORs\) and 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\)\. Results\. Regional disparities and parental socioeconomic characteristics were consistently associated with all three forms of undernutrition\. Compared with Eastern Indonesia, children living in Western Indonesia had lower odds of stunting \(AOR=0\.63, 95% CI: 0\.57\-0\.69\), wasting \(AOR=0\.56, 95% CI: 0\.50\-0\.62\), and underweight \(AOR=0\.58, 95% CI: 0\.51\-0\.66\)\. Low parental education and parental unemployment were independently associated with higher odds of all three outcomes \(all p&lt;0\.01\)\. Unimproved sanitation and inadequate solid waste management were associated with stunting, whereas unimproved sanitation was also associated with wasting\. Conclusion\. Child undernutrition in Indonesia is independently associated with regional inequalities, parental socioeconomic disadvantage, and selected household environmental conditions\. Multisectoral interventions that target disadvantaged regions, improve parental socioeconomic conditions, and strengthen sanitation infrastructure are needed to reduce child undernutrition\.

## [Digital Revolution, AI and the Future of Human Translation: From Translator to Cultural Guarantor](../publications/02bca8cd9056e8caa2fe.md)

Ferial FILALI\-FELLAH

The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is transforming Translation Studies \(TS\)\. This article adopts a historical and critical approach, based on a literature review from 1954 to 2024, from Statistical Machine Translation to Generative AI\. While Generative Translation \(GT\) achieves unprecedented fluency and terminological consistency, it still fails to render cultural depth, ethical nuance and spiritual meaning\. Through examples such as the translation of 仁 \(Ren\) and رحمة \(Rahma\), the study argues that the translator&\#x27;s role is evolving from a linguistic transferer to a cultural guarantor and strategic curator of meaning\. The paper concludes that Human Translation is not doomed, but its survival depends on integrating AI mastery with intercultural mediation, in line with the Global Civilization Initiative\. Article submitted to Frontiers \(ID 2030041\) on 15\-10\-2026\. Deposited on Zenodo in Restricted Access for author copyright protection\.

## [Corrosion and Wear Behaviour of Eggshell\-Derived CDHA\-GNP Coatings on Ti\-6Al\-4V and Ti\-6Al\-7Nb Alloys by Low\-Temperature Pack Cementation](../publications/02d1da7a200976b98b61.md)

Chandra Shekar Beera; Ramanaiah Nallu

Abstract Titanium alloys are widely used for orthopaedic and dental implants, yet surface wear and electrochemical degradation remain important performance concerns\. This study evaluates eggshell\-derived calcium\-deficient hydroxyapatite \(CDHA\) and 0\.5 wt\.% graphene nanoplatelet \(GNP\)\-reinforced CDHA coatings deposited on Ti\-6Al\-4V and Ti\-6Al\-7Nb by low\-temperature pack cementation at 800 °C for 2 h under argon\. Surface morphology, phase constitution, composition, Raman features, and supporting surface characteristics were examined\. Under dry sliding conditions, the CDHA\-GNP\-coated specimens exhibited lower specific wear rates than the untreated, oxidized, and CDHA\-coated specimens for both Ti\-6Al\-4V and Ti\-6Al\-7Nb alloys\. A further reduction in specific wear rate was observed under saline sliding in 0\.9 wt\.% NaCl, demonstrating the favourable wear response of the GNP\-containing coatings under both sliding environments\. SEM examination of the worn surfaces showed comparatively reduced surface damage and more compacted wear regions for the CDHA\-GNP coatings\. These observations are consistent with the lower material removal observed for the GNP\-containing coatings and indicate their improved resistance to sliding wear under both dry and saline conditions\. While the potentiodynamic polarization in 3\.5 wt\.% NaCl\. For the CDHA\-GNP condition, I\_corr decreased from 8\.822 to 5\.275 µA cm⁻² for Ti\-6Al\-4V and from 7\.974 to 4\.489 µA cm⁻² for Ti\-6Al\-7Nb, corresponding to reductions of 40\.2% and 43\.7%, respectively\. The corresponding corrosion rates decreased from 0\.0782 to 0\.0467 mm y⁻¹ and from 0\.0692 to 0\.0390 mm y⁻¹, representing reductions of 40\.3% and 43\.6%\. The results demonstrate the measured wear and electrochemical responses under the investigated laboratory conditions, while adhesion, fatigue, long\-term stability, and biological performance require further validation\.

## [DeepSwarm\-DBSCAN: Deep Learning and Swarm Intelligence for Automated Density\-Based Clustering](../publications/02d2645e62f0023b2173.md)

Asma Khazaal Abdulsahib; Mohammad Ali Balafar; Ali Jameel Hashim

Density\-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise is widely used for unsupervised clustering due to its ability to identify arbitrarily shaped clusters and handle noise\. However, its effectiveness strongly depends on appropriate hyperparameter selection, which becomes challenging and computationally expensive for high\-dimensional data\. This study aims to address this limitation by proposing an automated and scalable optimization framework\. The proposed DeepSwarm\-DBSCAN framework integrates deep neural networks with an enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\) algorithm to automatically determine optimal DBSCAN hyper\- parameters\. Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\) and Autoencoders \(AE\) learn compact and meaningful feature representations, projecting high\-dimensional data into lower\-dimensional latent spaces\. An adaptive PSO strategy then searches this reduced space to optimize clustering validity metrics efficiently\. Experimental evaluations on MNIST and CIFAR\-10 datasets demonstrate that DeepSwarm\-DBSCAN outperforms conventional DBSCAN, achieving clustering accuracies of 92%, 91%, and 94%—with a silhouette coefficient of 0\.7 on MNIST—indicating strong cluster coherence\. Additionally, the proposed approach reduces hyperparameter optimization runtime by approximately 30% compared to traditional grid search methods\. Conclusion: The results confirm that combining deep representation learning with swarm\-based optimization provides an effective solution for DBSCAN hyperparameter tuning\. DeepSwarm\- DBSCAN offers a robust, scalable, and efficient clustering framework suitable for real\- world high\-dimensional data analysis across diverse application domains\. The results confirm that combining deep representation learning with swarm\-based optimization provides an effective solution for DBSCAN hyperparameter tuning\. DeepSwarm\-DBSCAN offers a robust, scalable, and efficient clustering framework suitable for real\-world high\- dimensional data analysis across diverse application domains\.

## [Physics\-constrained generative digital twin for early leakage detection in nitrogen accumulators in governor control systems at hydroelectric power plants](../publications/02d31a46de509a2519f5.md)

Taha Selim Ustun; Pampa Sinha; Mehmet Akif Bütüner; Erkan Koç; Doğan Gezer

Abstract Nitrogen pre\-charge loss in hydropower governor accumulators is a slow but critical degradation process that weakens hydraulic energy storage, reduces pressure\-retention time, increases pump cycling, and accelerates thermal–mechanical stress\. Conventional pressure\-threshold SCADA alarms can miss the early stage because oil pressure may remain inside the operating band while waveform dynamics deteriorate\. This paper proposes a SCADA\-calibrated physics\-constrained generative digital twin for early nitrogen leakage diagnosis\. Limited anonymized field\-SCADA observations are used only as calibration anchors for pressure set\-points, pump\-ON duration, pump\-OFF retention, temperature range, and the fast\-rise/slow\-decay waveform; they are not presented as a complete labeled leakage dataset\. The evaluation uses 80,000 physics\-constrained synthetic training records and 20,000 independently generated synthetic test records per run, balanced across eight degradation months\. Train and test records are produced with disjoint seeds and no shared cycles or residual draws\. Across five independent generation\-and\-training runs, Random Forest gives the best pressure\-prediction performance, with R 2 = 0\.999731 ± 0\.000004, MAE = 0\.0856 ± 0\.0007 bar, RMSE = 0\.1074 ± 0\.0007 bar, and 96\.78 ± 0\.18% of samples within 1% of the 23\-bar operating span \(0\.23 bar\)\. The corrected health index is bounded by 1\.0, and cycle\-level indicators identify the Month\-4 warning transition before a conventional pressure\-threshold response\. The framework therefore supports earlier inspection and nitrogen\-recharge planning, helping operators reduce avoidable pump cycling, maintenance escalation, and the risk of unplanned governor\-system outages, while explicitly distinguishing SCADA calibration from synthetic diagnostic evaluation\.

## [Safety and Efficacy of Lutein and Zeaxanthin in the AREDS2 Formulation for Age\-Related Macular Degeneration](../publications/02df05638e85ba1f1e0a.md)

Haryo Dimasto Kristiyanto; Amaze Grace Sira; Yosafat Reza Herlambang Wibisana; Haryadi Aristo Tamma; Made Anom Danuartha

Age\-related macular degeneration \(AMD\) is a progressive degenerative disease of the central retina and is a leading cause of vision loss among older adults worldwide\. The original Age\-Related Eye Disease Study \(AREDS\) supplement formula reduced the risk of progression to advanced AMD\. However, the beta\-carotene in this formula was associated with a higher risk of lung cancer in current and former smokers\. AREDS2 evaluated lutein and zeaxanthin as safer substitutes for beta\-carotene\. These macular carotenoids have antioxidant effects and a better safety profile\. Studies show that lutein and zeaxanthin help slow AMD progression through antioxidant effects and retinoprotective mechanisms\. Researchers have also studied genetic factors, including complement factor H \(CFH\) and age\-related maculopathy susceptibility 2 \(ARMS2\)\. However, current evidence is not strong enough to support individualized treatment based on these factors\. Overall, lutein and zeaxanthin appear to provide a favorable balance of efficacy and safety as replacements for beta\-carotene in the AREDS2 formulation\.

## [Spivak, Ihor: Who Sees Through Our Eyes? A Hypothesis on the Fundamental Nature of Individual Consciousness](../publications/02e6776e7809285769a8.md)



This paper presents an independently formulated scientific and philosophical hypothesis proposing that consciousness may be a fundamental property of the Universe and that individual consciousness may exist independently of the biological brain\. The model proposes the existence of distinct, persistent structures of individual consciousness, termed clusters\. Each cluster is assumed to possess a stable individual identity while retaining the capacity to accumulate information through experience\. The brain is considered a biological interface through which a cluster may interact with the physical world\. Such interaction is proposed to depend on the compatibility of the respective characteristics of the cluster and the nervous system\. The hypothesis allows for the possible persistence of individual consciousness after biological death and its subsequent interaction with another compatible nervous system, without requiring the transfer of a previous human personality\. The paper discusses conceptual parallels with other approaches to consciousness, unresolved scientific questions and possible avenues for empirical investigation\. The proposed model has not been experimentally confirmed and is presented for critical scientific and philosophical examination\. \(direct link \)

## [&quot;D³: Arquitetura Tecnológica de Inteligência Espacial, Processamento e Transmissão para Previsão de Inundações, Detecção de Manchas d&\#x27;Água e Monitoramento de Cobertura Vegetal via Satélite Brasileiro&quot;\.](../publications/02f5703c074a773496ff.md)

Mauro Roberto Pena Pena; Pena

Esta é uma proposta para o edital AI4SDGs 2026\. A D³ \(Dados, Dimensão e Decisão\) é uma arquitetura tecnológica de pré\-processamento, codificação e transmissão para satélites brasileiros, voltada à previsão de inundações, à detecção de manchas d&\#x27;água e ao monitoramento de cobertura vegetal\. Ela parte da premissa de que o gargalo da inteligência artificial embarcada está no dado, e não no modelo: transmitir e processar matrizes radiométricas de 10 a 16 bits consome banda, energia e capacidade de dissipação térmica, recursos escassos em plataformas de órbita baixa\. A proposta binariza índices espectrais \(NDVI/NDWI\) calculados a partir do sensor WFI dos satélites Amazônia\-1 e CBERS\-4A e converte blocos de 5 bits em índices compactos da lista mplex \(Base 32\), com complemento f\(x\) = 31 − x\. Essa estrutura fornece redundância implícita, permite detecção de erro por consistência sem bits de paridade e alimenta modelos de IA leves, executáveis em FPGA\. O downlink fica restrito aos vetores de alteração e alerta \(Δx\)\. As metas de projeto, a serem validadas e não medidas, são: redução de downlink ≥ 70%, redução de cerca de três ordens de grandeza na energia por inferência e IoU ≥ 0,87 na segmentação de água\. O documento detalha o protocolo de validação, os critérios de Go/No\-Go, a análise de riscos com contingências e o roadmap de maturação \(TRL 3 a 8\)\. A base algébrica está registrada no Folding Effect \(Preprints\.org, ID 238109\)\. As listas mplex e mpcolex constituem avanço autoral e exploratório sobre esse registro\. This is a proposal for the AI4SDGs 2026 call\. D³ \(Data, Dimension and Decision\) is a technological architecture for preprocessing, encoding and transmission on Brazilian satellites, aimed at flood forecasting, water\-body detection and vegetation cover monitoring\. It starts from the premise that the bottleneck of onboard artificial intelligence lies in the data, not in the model: transmitting and processing 10\- to 16\-bit radiometric matrices consumes bandwidth, energy and thermal dissipation capacity, which are scarce resources on low Earth orbit platforms\. The proposal binarizes spectral indices \(NDVI/NDWI\) computed from the WFI sensor of the Amazônia\-1 and CBERS\-4A satellites and converts 5\-bit blocks into compact indices of the mplex list \(Base 32\), with complement f\(x\) = 31 − x\. This structure provides implicit redundancy, allows error detection by consistency without parity bits, and feeds lightweight AI models that can run on FPGAs\. The downlink is restricted to change and alert vectors \(Δx\)\. The design targets, which are yet to be validated and are not measured results, are: downlink reduction ≥ 70%, a reduction of about three orders of magnitude in energy per inference, and IoU ≥ 0\.87 in water segmentation\. The document details the validation protocol, the Go/No\-Go criteria, the risk analysis with contingency plans and the maturation roadmap \(TRL 3 to 8\)\. The algebraic basis is registered in the Folding Effect \(Preprints\.org, ID 238109\)\. The mplex and mpcolex lists constitute an authorial and exploratory advance built on that registration\.

## [Prevalence and associated factors of vitamin B12 deficiency among Vietnamese patients with type 2 diabetes receiving metformin therapy: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/02ffca69853e06ec29ce.md)

Thị Kim Dung Nguyễn; Thi Lan Anh Ke; Pham Van Linh; Xuan Thuy Tran; Thanh Binh Vu

Background/objectives This study examined serum vitamin B12 status and associated clinical factors among Vietnamese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) receiving metformin\. Methods This hospital\-based cross\-sectional study included 400 eligible patients treated with metformin for at least 6 months and recruited by non\-probability convenience sampling at two hospitals in Thai Binh, Vietnam\. The study\-defined outcome was serum vitamin B12 &lt;300 pg/mL, comprising absolute deficiency \(&lt;200 pg/mL\) and marginal status \(200 to &lt;300 pg/mL\)\. Associations were examined using univariable analysis and the reported exploratory multivariable logistic regression model\. Results Overall, 103 participants \(25\.75%\) met the combined threshold: 29 \(7\.25%\) had absolute deficiency and 74 \(18\.50%\) had marginal status\. In the reported adjusted model, metformin use &gt;5 years \(adjusted odds ratio \[AOR\] = 1\.84; 95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 1\.07\-3\.18\) and anemia \(AOR = 3\.43; 95% CI: 1\.62\-7\.23\) were associated with the outcome\. The macrocytosis estimate was highly imprecise\. Conclusions Low serum vitamin B12 was common in this hospital\-based sample\. Periodic assessment merits consideration during prolonged metformin therapy, with use &gt;5 years serving as a pragmatic prompt rather than a validated testing threshold\. Unexplained anemia or neuropathic symptoms warrant assessment when deficiency is suspected, regardless of treatment duration\. The adjusted findings remain exploratory and do not establish causality or model robustness\.

## [How Learning to Write Helped Me Learn to Think](../publications/0308756438c0fe8dc5d6.md)

Nicholas D\. J\. Strzalkowski

Write without stopping for five minutes, whatever comes to mind\. This simple task transformed how I write and teach writing in my undergraduate science classroom\. Scientists can spend their whole careers without thinking deeply about writing\. I was this scientist\. I was a mimic without my own voice\. Learning freewriting expanded my view of writing from a means of communication to a method of exploration\. Writing freely for oneself reveals what is known and unknown\. It makes thinking visible and creates a powerful classroom and scholarly practice for generating and refining ideas\. In this reflective essay, I describe how learning freewriting through a faculty community of practice transformed my identity as a writer, scientist, and educator\. I discovered that writing is more than a means of communication—it is a valuable process for developing and refining understanding\. As AI\-assisted writing becomes more pervasive, preserving writing as a tool for thinking, understanding, and developing voice is increasingly important\. I present a framework that positions freewriting along a spectrum from introspection and reflection to creation and dissemination\. Freewriting, across this spectrum, helps writers develop understanding before feeling the pressure to communicate it\.
