## [Structure\-based computational prioritization of Emodin\-8\-glucoside as a candidate ligand for the VEGFR1 kinase domain in the context of placenta previa](../publications/03164d7c5307b9b54cb8.md)

Deniz inan; Sinan KARAGECILI; Nouman Safdar Ali

Placenta previa is a serious obstetric condition associated with abnormal placental implantation and hemorrhagic complications, for which no targeted pharmacological therapy is established\. This study applied an integrated structure\-based computational workflow to explore the intracellular VEGFR1 kinase domain as a candidate molecular target\. Twenty\-one phytochemicals were screened using AutoDock Vina and MOE, with Emodin\-8\-glucoside consistently prioritized among the highest\-ranked compounds\. Redocking of the co\-crystallized ligand 8ST reproduced its experimental pose with a heavy\-atom RMSD of 1\.465 Å\. Comparative 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations showed persistent binding\-site association of Emodin\-8\-glucoside and the 8ST control\. End\-point energy estimates were method dependent, with MM\-GBSA yielding a negative mean estimate while MM\-PBSA yielded a near\-zero estimate with substantial variability\. DFT analysis produced a HOMO\-LUMO gap of 0\.13204 Hartree \(approximately 3\.59 eV\)\. SwissADME and ProTox 3\.0 identified low gastrointestinal absorption, P\-glycoprotein substrate behavior, high polarity, and several predicted toxicity liabilities\. Overall, Emodin\-8\-glucoside represents an in\-silico\-prioritized exploratory candidate requiring biochemical, selectivity, placental\-cell, and pregnancy\-safety validation\.

## [Modelo MNAR: Mediación Neurodidáctica del Saber Pedagógico en Actividades Rectoras de Transición Rural](../publications/031b499a6d38bd04f08f.md)

Sully Johanna Calixto Pedraza

In rural Colombian early childhood education there is a persistent gap between the pedagogical knowledge teachers build through practice and their access to neurodidactic principles that could guide the design of core activities: play, art, literature and exploration of the environment\. This article presents the MNAR Model \(Neurodidactic Mediation of pedagogical knowledge in core activities of rural kindergarten\), formulated through a qualitative study grounded in the socio\-critical paradigm and an action research design, conducted with kindergarten teachers from three rural schools in Oicatá, Soracá and Sotaquirá \(Boyacá, Colombia\)\. Data were produced through semi\-structured interviews and participant observation recorded in field journals during an eight\-meeting professional development process \(January–June 2025\), and were analysed through open and axial coding in Atlas\.ti and triangulation\. The diagnosis identified 79 codes grouped into seven subcategories: teachers displayed reflective pedagogical knowledge oriented towards innovation and socio\-emotional development, together with limited conceptual knowledge of neurodidactics and adverse conditions \(multigrade classrooms, lack of materials, weak family support\)\. During the intervention, changes were recorded in teachers&\#x27; discourse and planning: they moved from describing their practices as intuitive to grounding them, and they designed sequences and materials with neurodidactic intent\. On this basis, the MNAR Model was formulated, articulating four guidelines that correspond to the study categories and two emergent cross\-cutting guidelines: the pedagogy of love and teachers&\#x27; socio\-emotional competence\. The model is a situated conceptual proposal; its effect on classroom practice and children&\#x27;s learning was not evaluated and requires further research\.

## [DIGITAL PEDAGOGY IN HIGHER EDUCATION: DEVELOPING 21ST\-CENTURY CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS](../publications/031dfad098a58e8817a2.md)

Abdusalomova Barchinoy Jo&\#x27;rabek qizi; Xudoyqulov Abdulla Eshquvvatovich

Digital pedagogy has become an essential component of higher education, offering new opportunities to develop students’ critical thinking, analytical reasoning, problem\-solving, and independent learning skills\. This article examines how digital learning environments and technology\-enhanced teaching strategies can support the development of critical thinking among university students\. Particular attention is given to blended learning, problem\-based learning, collaborative digital platforms, and artificial intelligence\. The discussion draws on existing research and identifies practical approaches for integrating digital tools into higher education\. The article argues that technology alone does not guarantee improved learning outcomes; effective digital pedagogy requires purposeful instructional design, active student participation, and continuous feedback\.

## [BEYOND SOLVENTS: SOLID\-STATE ENGINEERING STRATEGIES FOR SOLUBILITY ENHANCEMENT OF POORLY WATER\-SOLUBLE DRUGS](../publications/0322c5731298c963c990.md)

Anjani Kumar Dwivedi; Ritesh Kumar Tiwari

Background: Poor aqueous solubility of active pharmaceutical ingredients remains a major challenge in pharmaceutical development, as it can lead to slow dissolution, inadequate drug absorption, variable bioavailability, and reduced therapeutic performance\. Conventional solubility enhancement techniques, including micronization, solvent\-based solid dispersion, and the use of solubilizing agents, may involve limitations related to solvent consumption, processing complexity, physical instability, and environmental sustainability\. Mechanochemistry has emerged as a promising solid\-state engineering approach that uses mechanical energy to modify the physicochemical properties of drug substances, often with reduced or no solvent use\. Objective: This review aims to explore mechanochemical approaches for enhancing the solubility and dissolution performance of poorly water\-soluble drugs\. It emphasizes the fundamental mechanisms, major processing technologies, formulation strategies, and recent developments that support the application of mechanochemistry in pharmaceutical formulation development\. Methods: The review examines mechanochemical techniques, including mortar–pestle grinding, ball milling, liquid\-assisted grinding, mechanochemical cocrystallization, co\-amorphization, and polymer\-assisted solid\-state processing\. It discusses the influence of drug properties, polymeric carriers, coformers, drug\-to\-carrier ratios, and processing parameters on formulation performance\. Analytical and characterization techniques, including Fourier\-transform infrared spectroscopy, powder X\-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, and microscopic methods, are considered alongside solubility measurements, dissolution testing, and physical stability assessment\. Results: Mechanochemical processing offers considerable potential for improving the apparent solubility and dissolution rate of poorly water\-soluble drugs through particle\-size reduction, crystal lattice disruption, defect formation, amorphization, and modification of drug–excipient interactions\. The effectiveness of these approaches depends on formulation composition, processing conditions, and the physical properties of the resulting solid\. The review also highlights challenges associated with recrystallization, moisture sensitivity, process reproducibility, and the translation of laboratory\-scale methods to industrial manufacturing\. Emerging applications of process analytical technology, predictive modelling, and continuous processing provide opportunities to improve process control and scalability\. Conclusion: Mechanochemistry represents a versatile and potentially sustainable strategy for improving the pharmaceutical performance of poorly water\-soluble drugs\. Its advantages include the potential to reduce solvent consumption, minimize waste, and enable targeted solid\-state modifications\. However, successful implementation requires systematic formulation optimization, comprehensive characterization, long\-term stability evaluation, and reliable scale\-up strategies\. Further research into standardized protocols, quality control, and industrial processing is essential to establish mechanochemistry as a reproducible and practical platform for pharmaceutical development\.

## [Примена алата заснованих на вештачкој интелигенцији у реинжењерингу информационих система](../publications/0323da3129f49e919642.md)

Анастасија Савић

This paper presents the process of re\-engineering a hospital information system using artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based tools\. The research involves the application of an AI assistant \(Google Gemini\) and an AI agent \(OpenAI Codex\) in the phases of source code analysis, unified modeling language \(UML\) model generation, database reengineering, and application layer modernization\. The presented results demonstrate the potential of AI tools for documentation reconstruction, system modeling, and supporting various phases of the re\-engineering process, while emphasizing the necessity of expert verification of the generated results\.

## [PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer\-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas](../publications/0325383c2918163124ef.md)

Haoming Li; Defu Cao; Xu Hu; Yingtao Luo; Yiyang Wang; Xianghe Xu; Jiashu He; Wanting Jiang; Yifan Zhang; Yunhan Zhao; Siyang Wu; Chen Yang; Haixin Wang; Zheyuan Deng; Taoran Li; Jingwen Zhang; Zhejian Peng; Shushu Liang; Yue Zhao; Bingzhe Li; Feng Chen; Yifan Wang; Jintao Huang; Yijun Wang; Yuexing Hao; Xiaomin Li

Computer\-use agents \(CUAs\) are commonly evaluated against fixed task specifications, but users may omit requirements, add constraints, or require approval before consequential actions\. Completing the benchmark instruction does not guarantee serving the person who asked\. We introduce PersonaCUABench, which holds 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks\. A persona agent, playing one of 44 personas in four groups, rewrites each instruction in that user&\#x27;s own words and answers the CUA&\#x27;s questions, while the CUA sees only the dialogue, never the profile or the original instruction\. Across nine backbones \(3,330 runs\), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests\. The losses have two sources: in 59\.9% of cells that lose points, the agent engages with what the user asked for and still gets it wrong, and 11\.2% are stops the user requested that the checker scores as failures\. Even when a persona request is fully completed, the user gives the top satisfaction rating in only 62\.7% of cells, against 84\.1% for the original requests\. CUAs should therefore be evaluated not only on task completion but also on whether they meet the requirements and constraints users express\. Code: https://github\.com/MatrAIx\-ai/PersonaCUABench\. Project page: https://matraix\.ai/research/persona\-cua\.html

## [Embodiment\-Classifier Guidance: Transferring Frozen VLAs Across Robot Dynamics without Demonstrations](../publications/0325e885bf5024bfb601.md)

Devin Han; Hershraj Niranjani

Flow\-based policies such as $π\_0$ are trained on a fixed set of embodiments, and transferring them to new ones is an open problem\. To adapt a frozen $π\_0$ to a new embodiment without additional demonstrations or parameter updates, we train a lightweight embodiment classifier to distinguish successful action chunks on the source body from those on the target body, using a few calibration tasks\. On transfer tasks that $π\_0$ saw on its source body but the classifier was never trained on, we nudge each denoising step of $π\_0$ with the classifier&\#x27;s gradient, which estimates the direction from the distribution of successful actions on the source body toward that on the target body\. On the LIBERO simulation benchmark with four modified controllers, embodiment\-classifier guidance raises $π\_0$&\#x27;s average success on the target bodies from 72% to 80% across 12 suite\-controller pairs, with a 31% relative reduction in failures \(11 of 12 gain; 5 significant after Holm correction\)\. In simulation, guidance is data\-efficient, needing few target\-body rollouts per task, which makes it promising for sim\-to\-real transfer, where rollouts are costly\. Guidance is mixed on weak wrists and harmful on a locked wrist, when the classifier lacks data or favors infeasible motions\. Collecting more target\-body data with guided $π\_0$ can fill such gaps: on one weak\-wrist arm, guided $π\_0$ solved a task on which unguided $π\_0$ had zero successes in the original data, and retraining the classifier on the guided successes raised success from 52\.5% to 70\.7%\.

## [Unsteady MHD transport of a tangent\-hyperbolic ternary hybrid nanofluid over a permeable stretching surface with variable thermal conductivity and nonlinear radiation](../publications/032a846cc6a787ed256d.md)

Abanti Datta; Amitava Dutta; Arka Banerjee; Sayantan Mukherjee

This work is a numerical exploration of the unsteady MHD transport of a ternary hybrid nanofluid of tangent\-hyperbolic flow over a permeable stretching surface\. The working fluid consists of \[Formula: see text\] Cu, and \[Formula: see text\] nanoparticles dispersed in ethylene glycol\. The model includes nonlinear radiation, variable thermal conductivity, Joule heating, and Darcy\-Forchheimer porous effects\. The governing equations of partial differential equations are reduced to similarity equations of ordinary differential equations and solved by MATLAB BVP5C\. Simulations show that an increase in the Weissenberg number and Forchheimer parameter decreases the velocity field because of the increase in elastic and inertial resistance and the energy dissipation elevates the fluid temperature\. The variable thermal conductivity will greatly enhance thermal gradients near the wall and increase the performance of heat transfer\. Moreover, increased concentrations of nanoparticles enhance skin\-friction coefficients, Nusselt and Sherwood numbers\. The ternary hybrid nanofluid is better than mono and binary systems due to synergistic interactions of the nanoparticles that promotes thermal conductivity and mass diffusion\. The findings indicate that the Nusselt number decreases up to 92\.14% with increasing magnetic parameter and decreases to about 95\.93% with increasing thermal radiation, which shows a high level of suppression of heat transfer\. Conversely, the stretching parameter augments the skin friction and mass transfer by approximately 42\.48 and 11\.47% respectively, whereas thermophysical parameters augment the Nusselt number by up to 286\.9%\. Comprehensively, the numerical analysis shows, quantitatively, the competing interplay of electromagnetic, thermal and diffusive processes in dictating transport behaviour in ternary hybrid nanofluid flow\. These results demonstrate the possibilities of tangent\-hyperbolic ternary hybrid nanofluids in the advanced cooling and thermal management processes with intricate rheological and electromagnetic interactions\. The soundness and correctness of the numerical framework is validated against existing literature\.

## [Green English language teaching approach to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls](../publications/0333c48142b8a8a53494.md)

نوفه المواضية

The present study examined the effect of using green English pedagogy to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls\. Sixty Jordanian grade 9 EFL students participated in the present study\. They were enrolled in the Serfa secondary school for girls, education directorate of Lwa&\#x27;a Al\-Qasr\. The participants were assigned as control and experimental groups\. The elicitation of data relied on three instruments, namely critical reading test, perception questionnaire and environmental awareness checklist\. The current study employed the pre\-and\-posttest research design\. It made use of the mixed method in analyzing the collected data both quantitatively and qualitatively\. The findings indicated that green English instruction positively helped to develop the critical reading skills of Jordanian EFL grade 9 students\. The present study recommended that curriculum planning and design of English syllabi for Jordanian secondary school should incorporate green English\-based learning materials and should train Jordanian EFL teachers to employ the green English instruction with the classroom parameters\.

## [Impatiens lianchengensis \(Balsaminaceae\), a new species from southeastern China](../publications/033840292000d5e3ff46.md)

Jiedong Lin; Junlong Li; Boheng Li; Xinjie Jin; Meizhen Wang; Pan Li

A new species, Impatiens lianchengensis J\. D\. Lin &amp; P\. Li, sp\. nov \., from a moist valley on Mt\. Guanzhai, Liancheng County, Fujian Province, southeastern China, is described and illustrated\. It resembles I\. huangyanensis X\. F\. Jin &amp; B\. Y\. Ding and I\. tainingensis J\.\-D\. Lin &amp; P\. Li in gross morphology but differs in numerous features\. The molecular phylogeny of Impatiens indicated that I\. lianchengensis is closely related to I\. kuocangshanica , I\. wuyiensis , I\. platysepala , and I\. tainingensis based on plastome and ITS sequences\.

## [PHARMACOLOGY OF RECEPTORS AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF DRUG SEARCHING: INTEGRATED CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, PHARMACODYNAMIC, PHARMACOKINETIC, PHARMACOTHERAPEUTIC, PHARMACOGENOMIC, THERAPEUTIC DRUG MONITORING, EVIDENCE\-BASED, AND PRECISION MEDICINE APPROACHES](../publications/033ea8335436941bc62a.md)

Nodar Sulashvili; Margarita Beglaryan; Nana Gorgaslidze; Naira Chichoyan; Vira Kravchenko; Marika Sulashvili; Nato Alavidze; Ia Egnatievi; Manana Giorgobiani; Magda Davitashvili; Irina IMERLISHVILI; MARINA GIORGOBIANI; Ігор Сенюк; Lali Patsia; Olga Shapoval; NATIA KVIZHINADZE; Lasha Tchelidze; David Aphkhazava

Receptors are dynamic macromolecules that transduce chemical signals into biological responses and serve as the principal targets of modern therapeutics\. This review surveys current concepts in receptor pharmacology and their application to drug discovery and development\. Receptor\-mediated signal transduction is examined across the major receptor families, including G protein–coupled receptors, ligand\-gated and voltage\-gated ion channels, nuclear receptors, and receptor tyrosine kinases, with emphasis on the second messengers, kinase cascades, and transcriptional programs that they engage\. Classical receptor theory is reviewed alongside modern extensions that incorporate receptor efficacy, constitutive activity, receptor reserve, allosteric modulation, and biased agonism\. Intracellular signal propagation is discussed as a network\-level phenomenon shaped by cross\-talk, feedback regulation, scaffold proteins, and compartmentalised signalling, providing the conceptual basis for network pharmacology\. Drug\-discovery strategies are then considered, from target identification and validation, high\-throughput and phenotypic screening, and structure\-based and fragment\-based design to computational approaches, medicinal\-chemistry optimisation, and the management of resistance, tolerance, and translational risk\. Emerging modalities — allosteric modulators, agonists, targeted protein degraders \(PROTACs\), molecular glues, and covalent inhibitors — are discussed alongside the integration of receptor pharmacology with systems biology, biomarker\-guided therapy, and personalised medicine\. The review concludes that progress in receptor pharmacology will depend on controlling receptor conformational states, pathway selectivity, and tissue context rather than on maximising target affinity alone\.

## [Navigating Sprawl\-Induced Lifestyle Shifts: The Impact of Architectural Standards on Energy Consumption in High\-Rise Residential Building Typologies in Erbil, Iraq](../publications/03472a42022d8d0357bc.md)

Sarko Hassan Sleman; Shad Sherzad Jawhar; Cemil Atakara

Urban sprawl across the Middle East has restructured residential living patterns, accelerating the transition from traditional courtyard dwellings to high\-rise apartment typologies and exposing systemic gaps between architectural design standards and as\-built practice\. This study, framed explicitly as a Post\-Occupancy Evaluation \(POE\), investigates the relationship between three micro\-level architectural standards — building orientation, thermal insulation quality, and window\-to\-wall ratio \(WWR\) efficiency — and the macro\-level energy consequences of sprawl\-induced lifestyle change in post\-2010 high\-rise residential buildings in Erbil, Iraq\. The research foregrounds human\-building interaction and the perceived performance of architectural standards over physical building\-physics measurement, and adopts a cross\-sectional quantitative design using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) in SmartPLS 4\. Technical envelope constructs are operationalised via occupant\-observable symptoms — perceived drafts, solar glare, HVAC dependency — that act as latent\-variable proxies for architectural adherence\. The conceptual model specifies four exogenous architectural constructs, one moderating sprawl\-lifestyle construct, and two endogenous outcomes \(Perceived Thermal Comfort and Perceived Energy Performance\) tested through six directional hypotheses\. The findings indicate that sprawl\-induced lifestyle change is the strongest predictor of perceived energy performance, that envelope compliance and thermal insulation quality most strongly shape perceived thermal comfort, and that perceived thermal comfort mediates the influence of envelope parameters on energy performance, while building orientation shows only a weak effect and the moderating role of lifestyle change is limited\. The model explains approximately 60% of the variance in perceived energy performance and 52% in perceived thermal comfort\. The study delivers a first\-of\-its\-kind POE\-grounded PLS\-SEM model for Iraq&\#x27;s residential stock and evidence\-based recommendations for architects, engineers, and policymakers\.

## [Digital Health Ecosystems and Community Wellness: A Socio Technological Framework for Public Health Innovation](../publications/034a77db405983df5b7d.md)

Bindu Madhavi Mangalampalli; Sreoshi Dasgupta; K\. ARPITHA; Gowhar Rashid Bhat; Piyal Roy; Saptarshi Kumar Sarkar

Digital health ecosystems are transforming the nature of healthcare delivery by integrating innovative technology, healthcare stakeholders and community resources to drive community health and population wellness\. The present study examines the idea of digital health ecosystems to aid socio\-technological systems of innovation in the domain of population health\. The interpretivist philosophy, deductive approach, descriptive research design and secondary data collection methodology are embraced and applied in the study\. To investigate the interplay of technological infrastructure, stakeholder engagement, governance mechanisms, and healthcare results, academic journals, healthcare reports, policy documents, and publications by international health organizations were used to gather data\. The results indicate that digital health technologies, telemedicine, electronic health records, mobile health applications, wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing, have the potential to significantly enhance healthcare access, efficacy, and communication with patients\. The analysis also shows that the stakeholder collaboration between the healthcare providers, policy formulators, technology innovators and communities results in an enhanced health awareness, disease prevention, management of chronic diseases and the quality of life in general\. However, the challenges of digital inequalities, cyber threats, privacy, lack of proper infrastructure, and digital illiteracy also exist as issues to the effective implementation\. The paper provides a socio\-technological model integrating technological innovation, social and organizational variables to enhance sustainable healthcare change\. Under the framework, the most significant elements in promoting the best benefit of community health are governance, community\-related participation, and responsible digital health\. Overall, the research concludes that the digital health ecosystems represent a promising path to creating more accessible, resilient, and patient\-centered healthcare systems and improving long term community health and innovation in population health\.

## [التأهيل الأكاديمي ومتطلبات الممارسة المهنية لدى خريجي الإعلام في ليبيا دراسة نوعية في خبرات الانتقال من الجامعة إلى سوق العمل](../publications/0359f94d7d43319cf119.md)

محمد البكاي

ملخص: هدفت هذه الدراسة النوعية إلى استكشاف الخبرة المعاشة لخريجي كليات وأقسام الإعلام في ليبيا خلال انتقالهم من التأهيل الأكاديمي إلى الممارسة المهنية، مستندة إلى المدخل الظاهراتي الوصفي، ومتخذة نظرية التنشئة المهنية إطارًا تفسيريًا\. واعتمدت الدراسة المقابلات الفردية شبه المقننة المتعمقة مصدرًا رئيسًا للبيانات، لدى عينة قصدية بلغت 18 مشاركًا من خريجي الإعلام العاملين فعليًا في المجال، واستعانت بملاحظة ميدانية غير مشاركة ومراجعة وثائق مهنية مختارة للتحقق من اتساق التفسير لا لتوليد بيانات مستقلة، وحللت البيانات وفق خطوات كولايزي السبع، ونظم الترميز ووثق باستخدام برنامج NVivo، وخضعت عينة من المادة المرمزة لمراجعة محلل نوعي ثاني مستقل، وكشفت النتائج أن الانتقال إلى سوق العمل لا يمثل غيابًا للمعرفة، بل إعادة تركيب لها في بيئة سريعة التغير، إذ يؤدي التأهيل الجامعي وظيفة تأسيسية في بناء اللغة المهنية والأطر المعرفية، بينما تتركز الفجوة الفعلية في سرعة الأداء وتعدد الأدوار والعمل متعدد المنصات، كما تبين أن التعلم الذاتي يتحول تدريجيًا إلى مكون أصيل من الهوية المهنية للخريج، وتقترح الدراسة نموذجًا تفسيريًا بعنوان \(دورة إعادة تشكيل الجاهزية المهنية\)، يعيد قراءة مراحل التنشئة المهنية بوصفها دورة متكررة لا مسارًا خطيًا ينتهي بالتمثل، وتخلص الدراسة إلى توصيات عملية لتعزيز الصلة بين التأهيل الأكاديمي ومتطلبات الممارسة المهنية الفعلية\. الكلمات المفتاحية: التأهيل الأكاديمي، الممارسة المهنية، التنشئة المهنية، الخبرة المعاشة، البحث الظاهراتي، خريجو الإعلام، ليبيا\.

## [Cradle\-to\-gate life cycle assessment of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan identifies environmental hotspots and improvement opportunities](../publications/035dcd459dcef32ca960.md)

Narges Samanian; Mohammad Ali Hesarinejad; Ulugbek Sadullayev; Dilfuza Egamberdieva

Dairy production is an important component of Uzbekistan&\#x27;s food system but is associated with environmental burdens\. This study presents a cradle\-to\-gate life cycle assessment \(LCA\) of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan to quantify environmental impacts, identify hotspots, evaluate uncertainty, and assess environmental improvement options\. A case\-based inventory informed by farm records and national production data was developed for 1000 kg of pasteurized milk at the factory gate, covering feed production, dairy farming, transport, processing, and packaging\. Environmental impacts were assessed using ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint \(H\)\. Global warming potential \(GWP\), characterized water consumption, terrestrial acidification, freshwater eutrophication, and fossil resource scarcity were 1537\.8 kg CO 2 \-eq, 1509\.5 m 3 , 13\.40 kg SO 2 \-eq, 0\.775 kg P\-eq, and 158\.1 kg oil\-eq, respectively\. Dairy\-farm activities were the largest GWP contributor \(46\.6%\), while feed production accounted for all characterized water consumption and dominated freshwater eutrophication \(81\.8%\)\. Feed production and dairy\-farm activities contributed 52\.9% and 47\.1% of terrestrial acidification, respectively, whereas packaging dominated fossil resource scarcity \(65\.8%\)\. Monte Carlo analysis quantified model uncertainty, while sensitivity analysis identified methane/manure emissions as the main GWP uncertainty driver, irrigation demand for water consumption, fertilizer nutrient losses for acidification and eutrophication, and packaging factors for fossil resource scarcity\. The integrated inventory\-level sustainability scenario reduced GWP, water consumption, acidification, eutrophication, and fossil resource scarcity by 23\.9%, 47\.5%, 25\.0%, 25\.0%, and 4\.5%, respectively\. These findings support impact\-specific strategies for improving the environmental sustainability of the assessed dairy production system and provide evidence relevant to dairy\-sector improvement in Uzbekistan\.

## [Progress in research on RAAS inhibitors regulating inflammatory responses and oxidative stress: from molecular mechanisms to clinical evidence](../publications/03626be0528e209f04fd.md)

Hongtao Yin; Mengdi Yang; Shiming Zhang; Qiong Li; Donghu Zhen; Xulei Tang

The renin\-angiotensin\-aldosterone system \(RAAS\) inhibitors serve as cornerstone pharmacotherapies for chronic conditions including hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease\. Accumulating evidence over recent years has demonstrated that their target organ\-protective effects cannot be fully attributed to blood pressure\-lowering actions alone; instead, the modulation of inflammatory responses and oxidative stress emerges as a core mechanism underpinning their extra\-antihypertensive benefits\. However, systematic comparisons of such effects across distinct classes of RAAS inhibitors and integration of the latest evidence remain lacking\. This review focuses on the molecular regulatory network of the dual RAAS axes, systematically dissecting the specific molecular mechanisms by which the canonical ACE\-AngII\-AT1R axis mediates tissue injury—via activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, NADPH oxidase, and NF\-κB signaling pathways—while the protective ACE2\-Ang\(1–7\)\-MasR axis exerts anti\-inflammatory and antioxidant effects\. A cross\-class comparison is conducted to evaluate the divergent effects of five clinically prevalent RAAS inhibitor classes \(ACE inhibitors \[ACEI\], angiotensin receptor blockers \[ARB\], direct renin inhibitors \[DRI\], angiotensin receptor\-neprilysin inhibitors \[ARNI\], and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists \[MRA\]\) on the regulation of inflammation and oxidative stress\. By synthesizing the latest evidence from basic science and clinical studies over the past decade, we summarize the distinct organ\-protective profiles of these agents across various target organs affected by cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, pulmonary disorders, neurological conditions, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoporosis\. Finally, addressing the limitations and inconsistencies within existing literature, this article proposes future research directions, strategies for optimizing combination therapies, and refined clinical trial designs to enhance the clinical application of RAAS inhibitors and facilitate the development of novel organ\-protection paradigms\.

## [O‘ZBEKISTONDA SUN’IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA SAVDO HAJMI VA ISTE’MOLCHILAR TALABINI PROGNOZLASH](../publications/03771c15fd35b636b962.md)

Shadmanov\.X\.N\.

Mazkur maqolada O‘zbekistonda savdo hajmi va iste’molchilar talabini sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalari asosida prognozlashning nazariy, metodologik va amaliy jihatlari tadqiq etiladi\. Savdo korxonalarida talabning mavsumiyligi, narxlarning o‘zgarishi, aksiyalar, bayramlar, hududiy xususiyatlar, iste’molchilar xulq\-atvori va raqamli savdo kanallarining rivojlanishi prognozlash jarayonini murakkablashtiradi\. An’anaviy statistik usullar ayrim holatlarda samarali natija bersa\-da, katta hajmdagi ko‘p omilli ma’lumotlar va murakkab nochiziqli bog‘liqliklarni tahlil qilishda mashinaviy o‘qitish algoritmlaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari kengaymoqda\. Tadqiqotda O‘zbekiston Milliy statistika qo‘mitasining elektron tijorat va chakana savdo bo‘yicha ochiq ma’lumotlari tavsifiy\-statistik tahlil qilindi, prognozlash usullarini qiyoslash uchun metodologik yondashuv ishlab chiqildi hamda savdo korxonalarida sun’iy intellektni joriy etishning bosqichlari belgilandi\. Rasmiy ma’lumotlarga ko‘ra, O‘zbekistonda elektron tijorat savdo hajmi 2024\-yildagi 15,2 trillion so‘mdan 2025\-yilda 31,6 trillion so‘mga yetgan\. Ushbu dinamika raqamli savdo ma’lumotlarini tahlil qilish va prognozlash tizimlarini rivojlantirish dolzarbligini ko‘rsatadi, biroq o‘z\-o‘zidan sun’iy intellekt modelining samaradorligini isbotlamaydi\. Maqolada ARIMA, gradient boosting, tasodifiy o‘rmon, rekurrent neyron tarmoqlar va gibrid modellarni qo‘llash imkoniyatlari ko‘rib chiqiladi\. Prognoz sifatini baholash uchun MAE, RMSE, WAPE va boshqa ko‘rsatkichlardan foydalanish taklif etiladi\. Shuningdek, ma’lumotlar sifati, algoritmik xatoliklar, shaxsga doir ma’lumotlarni himoya qilish va model natijalarini inson nazorati ostida qo‘llash masalalari yoritiladi\. Tadqiqot natijalari O‘zbekiston savdo korxonalarida ma’lumotlarga asoslangan boshqaruvni rivojlantirish va talab prognozlarining amaliy ahamiyatini oshirishga qaratilgan\.

## [LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT: NEOLOGISMS IN CONTEMPORARY ENGLISH](../publications/038575b538682d0c6b35.md)

Xudayqulova Nigina Faxriddinovna; Dildor Urolovna Eshmuratova

Language development is a continuous process shaped by social transformation, technological innovation, cultural interaction, and changes in human communication\. One of the most significant manifestations of this process is the emergence of neologisms, which are newly created words or expressions, as well as existing words that acquire new meanings\. In contemporary English, neologisms emerge in response to developments in digital technology, artificial intelligence, social media, science, popular culture, and global communication\. This article examines the role of neologisms in the development of modern English, focusing on their formation, classification, dissemination, and influence on vocabulary expansion\. Particular attention is given to word formation processes such as compounding, blending, affixation, abbreviation, borrowing, and semantic change\. The article also considers the role of digital communication in popularising new lexical items and discusses the challenges associated with their interpretation, standardisation, and long\-term acceptance\. The analysis demonstrates that neologisms reflect the changing needs of English speakers and contribute significantly to the flexibility and expressive potential of the language\.

## [Wettability alteration of CO2\-water\-shale system: state of the art and future directions](../publications/03aaa9ef47a15410697b.md)

Chao Luo; Xin Yin; Biying Zeng; Jialin Yuan; Xinlei Huo; Hun Lin; Nanxin Yin

Wettability serves as a fundamental petrophysical property governing hydrocarbon recovery efficiency and determining the geological storage security of injected CO 2 within shale formations\. This work systematically reviews the recent advances in wettability alteration \(WA\) of shale induced by CO 2 flooding\. First, the classification criteria of reservoir wettability are summarized, and the respective merits and limitations of prevailing experimental and numerical characterization approaches for wettability quantification are critically discussed\. Thereafter, key controlling factors encompassing in\-situ reservoir conditions, formation water salinity, inherent mineralogy, total organic carbon \(TOC\) content and geochemical interactions are elaborated, with detailed assessment on how these variables modulate the WA behaviors of CO 2 \-brine\-shale ternary systems\. On this basis, the urgent research demands toward multi\-scale quantitative characterization and in\-depth mechanistic exploration of WA are highlighted\. Additionally, the pivotal role of WA in guiding CO 2 storage site screening and long\-term geological safety evaluation is emphasized\. This comprehensive review clarifies current research bottlenecks and delivers instructive references for preferential formation optimization and subsequent feasibility evaluation of field\-scale CO 2 geological sequestration projects in shale reservoirs\.

## [การเปลยนแปลงและปรบตวของตลาดนำในยค Ai \- Robotic : กรณศกษาตลาดนำในจงหวดสมทรสงคราม](../publications/03b0317a646b6cbefd5a.md)

Supakarn Siripaisarn; Anyamanee Chumanee; Apichat Maharachsena; Watcharee Arunrach; Thanyachanok Poolsawat

This research article aimed to 1\) study the background and development of floating markets in Samut Songkhram Province, 2\) examine changes and adaptations of floating markets in economic, social, cultural, and environmental aspects, and 3\) study guidelines for developing floating markets for sustainable tourism\. This qualitative study purposively selected two study sites: Amphawa Floating Market and Tha Kha Floating Market in Samut Songkhram Province\. Data were collected through document review, field surveys and observations, in\-depth interviews, and focus group discussions\. The data were analyzed using content analysis, and the findings were presented through analytical description\. The findings revealed that 1\) both floating markets evolved from riverside communities that used rivers and canals for transportation and trade into cultural tourism destinations\. Amphawa Floating Market has been revitalized and has developed diverse tourism activities, while Tha Kha Floating Market continues to preserve its distinctive boat\-based trading and traditional orchard\-farming way of life\. 2\) Changes in transportation systems, economic structures, tourism promotion, and technological advancement have led communities to adapt their occupations, trading practices, and tourist services\. Social media and digital technologies are used for publicity, communication, and payments, creating both economic opportunities and challenges for the preservation of community ways of life and the environment\. 3\) Guidelines for sustainable floating market development should emphasize the conservation of local identity and wisdom, the promotion of community and stakeholder network participation, the development of entrepreneurs&\#x27; capacities, and the appropriate application of digital technologies, including consideration of the use of artificial intelligence to support tourism management and services in the future, in order to achieve a balance among economic, social, cultural, and environmental dimensions\.

## [The Pemberdayaan Komunitas Kreatif Kampung Batik Semarang Melalui Edukasi AI Motif Batik Berbasis Kearifan Lokal](../publications/03b2a482fe05718be8a6.md)

Bernadeta Lenny Setyowati; Peter Ardhianto; Ekawati Marhaenny Dukut; Krismalita Sekar Diasti

This community service program aims to empower batik artisans, particularly female MSMEs in Kemijen and Kampoeng Batik Semarang, by educating them on utilizing Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) as an assistive technology to design Semarangan batik motifs based on local wisdom\. An interdisciplinary team spanning Communication Science, Cultural Studies, English, and Visual Communication Design implemented this program\. The execution methods included conceptual counseling, practical training on generative AI, project\-based creative mentoring, and design evaluations\. The results demonstrated a significant increase in digital literacy: 100% of participants understood AI&\#x27;s role as an assistive design tool, and practical AI operational skills rose to 86%\. The program successfully produced more than 5 collaborative batik motif prototypes \(e\.g\., Warak Ngendog, blekok, and tamarind tree\) and digital promotion copywriting in English\. Program outputs include an ISBN\-registered interdisciplinary educational module, an Intellectual Property Rights \(IPR\) registration draft for the educational model, and a scientific article draft submitted to a national Sinta 5 accredited journal\. In conclusion, utilizing AI as an assistive technology accelerates visual design exploration without diluting local cultural philosophy and authenticity, thereby strengthening the economic resilience and digital capacity of female batik MSMEs in the creative industry\. Keywords\-\-\- Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Semarangan Batik, female MSMEs, local wisdom, community empowerment\.

## [Next‐Generation Integrated Pest Management in Oilseed Rape and Canola: can new approaches solve the age‐old problem of IPM delivery?](../publications/03b4d553b317ee035edb.md)

S\. M\. Cook; Kevin M\. King; Michael Rostás; M\. Jędryczka

1 INTRODUCTION Integrated pest management \(IPM\) is a decades\-old concept, but has failed to reach its potential in offering agriculture efficient and cost\-effective crop protection using a diversity of approaches\.1 This is mainly due to the cheapness and ease\-of\-use of synthetic insecticides, with IPM becoming more of an ‘integrated pesticide management’ system \(rotate crops, monitor pests; if populations exceed threshold, then apply pesticides\) than the ‘real’ IPM intended\. However, public lobbying for pesticide reductions, the revocation of several key pesticides including neonicotinoid insecticidal seed treatments by the European Union in 2014, and the widespread resistance of pests to most of the commonly used pesticides have driven research towards the diversity of approaches first imagined\. Arguably, the clearest example of this is in Brassica napus, for which, particularly in Europe, few, if any, synthetic control options are commercially available, particularly for insect pests\. B\. napus is grown around the world as an important source of food\-grade oil and as food stock for biofuel, with meal used for animal feed\. Two major forms of B\. napus are grown: oilseed rape \(OSR\) and canola\. OSR is winter hardy, and therefore autumn\-sown with yields benefitting from the long growing period; it represents the dominant form used in Europe\. The spring\-sown form is widely grown in Australia, Canada, China, the USA and other southern regions where the growing season is shorter; it is commonly known as canola\. A dearth of synthetic control options and the pressure to conserve biodiversity through pesticide reduction have stimulated the evolution of ‘next\-generation’ IPM tactics for systems that are less reliant, if not completely unreliant, on synthetic toxicants\. These approaches are the subject of this Special Issue\. Like our last Special Issue of Pest Management Science, ‘Integrated Pest Control in Oilseed Crops’ \(Volume 80, Issue 5\),2 this Issue was inspired by a meeting of the International Organization for Biological Control&\#x27;s Working Group on ‘Integrated Control in Oilseed Crops’, which was held in Dresden, Germany \(10–11 September 2024\)\.3 This working group comprises an entomology and a pathology subsection\. Meetings are very friendly and effective in fostering a community of researchers that stimulates research and drives forward the science\.

## [Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Binary Classification of Heart Disease: A Cross\-Validated Analysis of a Clinical Dataset](../publications/03b7bd0eaabb9a1a30fd.md)

Taniya Mondal; Durjodhan Mondal

Machine learning \(ML\) algorithms are increasingly used to classify heart disease using routinely collected clinical variables\. This study compared nine supervised classifiers to identify the best\-performing model for binary heart disease classification\. A secondary analysis was conducted using a dataset of 303 observations, 13 predictors, and a binary outcome\. Data completeness and outcome distribution were assessed, and no missing values were identified\. The dataset included 165 positive cases \(54\.5%\) and 138 negative cases \(45\.5%\)\. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, radial\-basis\-function Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), K\-Nearest Neighbors \(KNN\), Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Decision Tree were evaluated using five\-fold stratified cross\-validation\. Numerical predictors were standardized, and categorical predictors were one\-hot encoded within preprocessing pipelines\. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1\-score, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve \(ROC\-AUC\)\. Logistic Regression achieved the highest reported accuracy \(86\.5%\), precision \(85\.2%\), sensitivity \(90\.9%\), specificity \(81\.2%\), F1\-score \(88\.0%\), and ROC\-AUC \(0\.914\)\. Random Forest and AdaBoost achieved ROC\-AUC values of 0\.901, while Extra Trees achieved 0\.896\. Decision Tree performed least effectively, with an accuracy of 74\.3% and ROC\-AUC of 0\.739\. Logistic Regression emerged as the strongestperforming classifier in this comparison and represents a reasonable baseline for further investigation\. However, the findings remain preliminary because confidence intervals, formal paired comparisons, nested hyperparameter tuning, calibration assessment, and independent external validation were unavailable\. Further research should reproduce the analysis using the raw dataset and evaluate model generalizability before considering clinical applications\.

## [РОЗВИТОК ТЕХНІЧНИХ ЗАСОБІВ ВИЗНАЧЕННЯ ШВИДКОСТІ ТРАНСПОРТНИХ ЗАСОБІВ ПІД ЧАС ЕКСПЕРТИЗИ ДТП](../publications/03bfcf43dd8d39d8d519.md)

Наталія Семченко; Антон Павлович Руденко

Досліджено розвиток технічних засобів визначення швидкості транспортних засобів під час проведення експертизи дорожньо\-транспортних пригод\. Розглянуто еволюцію методів установлення швидкості від аналізу матеріальних слідів гальмування та деформацій транспортних засобів до застосування радіолокаційних і лазерних вимірювачів, систем відеофіксації, цифрової фотограмметрії, бортових реєстраторів даних і програмних комплексів реконструкції ДТП\. Систематизовано сучасні технічні засоби за принципом дії та характером отримуваної інформації, визначено їхні переваги й обмеження щодо використання в експертній практиці\. Проаналізовано особливості використання даних реєстраторів подій транспортних засобів для перевірки результатів розрахунків\. Встановлено, що достовірність визначення швидкості залежить від якості вихідних даних, метрологічних характеристик вимірювальних засобів, точності визначення просторових і часових параметрів, повноти матеріалів ДТП та обґрунтованості застосованих методик\. Обґрунтовано доцільність комплексного використання незалежних джерел інформації, стандартизації процедур відеоекспертного аналізу, експериментальної перевірки програмного забезпечення та застосування засобів штучного інтелекту як допоміжного інструменту експертного дослідження\. Запропоновано перспективні напрями вдосконалення методів визначення швидкості транспортних засобів для підвищення точності, об&\#x27;єктивності та доказової обґрунтованості результатів автотехнічної експертизи\.

## [Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA\-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy](../publications/03ca3d8cb3dafe4ef4ac.md)

Mohamed Kassar; Jaixi Hu; Isabel Rauscher; Carlos Vinícius Gomes; Thomas Wendler; Sibylle Ilse Ziegler; Ali Afshar‐Oromieh; Wolfgang A\. Weber; Axel Rominger; Nassir Navab; Matthias J\. Eiber; Robert Seifert; Kuangyu Shi

Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration\. Therefore, vision–language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning\. Prostate\-specific membrane antigen \(PSMA\)–targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well\-established treatment for metastatic castration\-resistant prostate cancer \(mCRPC\), but it is still not known which patients will be good long\-term responders\. Therefore, this study proposes a physician\-inspired visual question answering \(VQA\) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA\-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication\. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either \[177Lu\]Lu\-PSMA I&amp;T or \[177Lu\]Lu\-PSMA\-617\. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3\-dimensional image encoder, the domain\-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross\-modal transformer to process baseline and interim \(after 2 cycles\) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query\. The model was trained to predict 24\-mo survival, and performance was compared with state\-of\-the\-art approaches\. External validation was performed with the \[177Lu\]Lu\-PSMA\-617 cohort\. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state\-of\-the\-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query\-free attention multimodal fusion model\. Specifically, it achieved 81\.8% accuracy \(95% CI, 0\.52–0\.95\) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate\-specific antigen measurements\. External validation of the VQA showed 71\.9% accuracy \(95% CI, 0\.53–0\.86\) after few\-shot fine\-tuning, with further improvement over all state\-of\-the\-art approaches in survival stratification\. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground\-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed \(log\-rank test, P = 0\.76\)\. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve \(0\.75\) among the evaluated models\. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance\. Conclusion: By adopting a physician\-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning\. The preliminary results indicate that VQA\-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy\.

## [The association of cognitive behavioral intervention with caregiver burden and quality of life among family caregivers of cancer recurrence patients](../publications/03d14867ee012de84de8.md)

Zhan Zhang; Han Zhou; Xiaoyu Guo; Bo Zheng

Objective This study aimed to evaluate the immediate and 3\-month follow\-up associations of cognitive behavioral intervention \(CBI\) on caregiver burden and quality of life \(QOL\) among family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer\. Methods A quasi\-experimental study was conducted among 87 family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer who completed the study at a tertiary hospital in China\. Participants were recruited from two inpatient wards within the same oncology department, with one ward assigned to the intervention arm \(n=43\) and the other to the control arm \(n=44\)\. The intervention group received an 8\-week structured CBI alongside routine care, while the control group received routine care alone\. Outcomes were measured using the Zarit Burden Interview \(ZBI\) and the World Health Organization Quality of Life\-BREF\-Chinese Version \(WHOQOL\-BREF\-CV\), which were administered at baseline \(T 0 \), immediately post\-intervention \(T 1 \), and 3\-month post\-intervention follow\-up \(T 2 \)\. Results Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in total caregiver burden at both T 1 \(MD = \-8\.27, 95% CI: \-10\.39 to \-6\.16; d = \-1\.66\) and T 2 \(MD = \-4\.66, 95% CI: \-6\.92 to \-2\.40; d = \-0\.88\)\. Significant improvements were also observed in overall QOL at T 1 \(MD = 3\.39, 95% CI: 1\.46 to 5\.32; d = 0\.75\) and T 2 \(MD = 3\.91, 95% CI: 1\.83 to 5\.99; d = 0\.80\), as well as in the physical domain at T 1 and T 2 , and in the psychological domain at T 1 \. However, the psychological\-domain difference at T 2 was less robust in post hoc multiplicity\-adjusted sensitivity analyses\. However, between\-group differences in the social relationships and environmental domains were not statistically significant at T 2 \( p &gt; 0\.05\)\. The control group showed no significant longitudinal changes in caregiver burden; however, significant within\-group fluctuations were observed in several QOL domains over time\. Conclusions The findings suggest that CBI may be associated with reduced caregiver burden and improved QOL among family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer over the immediate and 3\-month follow\-up period\. Further large\-scale, multi\-center studies with extended follow\-up are recommended to confirm the sustainability of these effects and the generalizability of the intervention\.

## [Autentisk ledelse utvikles mellom mennesker: Sosiokulturell læring og GenKI som supplerende kulturelt redskap](../publications/03d2664514af43bd5f31.md)

June Borge Doornich

Forskning på autentisk lederutvikling er hovedsakelig forankret i erfaringsbasert læring og vektlegger individuell refleksjon og utprøving\. Denne studien undersøker hvordan pedagogiske metoder forankret i sosiokulturell læring bidrar til læring og utvikling av autentisk ledelse, og drøfter generativ kunstig intelligens \(GenKI\) muligheter og begrensninger i slike læringsprosesser\. Studien er en kvalitativ, eksplorativ enkeltcasestudie av et emne i autentisk ledelse i en siviløkonomutdanning\. Analysen viser at kulturelle redskaper og språk gjorde studentenes fortolkninger tilgjengelige for respons og videreutvikling i sosial samhandling\. Læringsprosessen fremmet særlig selvbevissthet, balansert prosessering og relasjonell orientering, mens autentisk atferd var mindre tydelig dokumentert\. Studien fremmer dermed autentisk lederutvikling som en kulturelt mediert og sosialt forankret læringsprosess\. På dette grunnlaget forstås GenKI som et supplerende kulturelt redskap for faglig og individuell bearbeiding, men ikke som en erstatning for menneskelig samhandling\. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Authentic Leadership Develops Between People: Sociocultural Learning and GenKI as a Supplementary Cultural Tool Research on authentic leadership development is largely grounded in experiential learning and emphasizes individual reflection and experimentation\. This study examines how pedagogical methods grounded in sociocultural learning contribute to authentic leadership learning and development and discusses the opportunities and limitations of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) in such processes\. The study is a qualitative, exploratory single\-case study of an authentic leadership course in a business program, based on students’ written reflection assignments\. The analysis shows that cultural tools and language made students’ interpretations available for feedback and further development through social interaction\. The learning process particularly fostered self\-awareness, balanced processing, and relational orientation, while authentic behavior was less clearly documented\. The study thus promote authentic leadership development as a culturally mediated and socially embedded learning process\. Accordingly, GenAI is understood as a supplementary cultural tool for conceptual learning and individual reflection, but not as a substitute for human interaction\.

## [Is a Linear Probe Evidence of a Linear Representation?](../publications/03d6cd68fd25ac09e9c9.md)

Nadir Kutluozen; Christian Internò; David Klindt

The linear representation hypothesis holds that pretrained vision models encode generative factors as linearly decodable directions in feature space, and comes with a standard methodology: train a linear probe, declare a factor represented if accuracy is high\. We show this test is too permissive\. Asymptotically, any sufficiently rich feature map, including a random one, admits a linear readout, so high probe accuracy is consistent with two very different geometries: a true linear world model, where the latent\-aligned subspace dominates the representation, or a kernel machine, where the latents lie linearly inside a much larger curved manifold\. This distinction matters because the curved structure orthogonal to the probe is relevant for out\-of\-distribution generalization, robustness, and compositional transfer\. We propose three asymmetric diagnostics that distinguish the two cases: reverse predictivity, spectral concentration, and out\-of\-distribution generalization\. We validate them in a fully observed simulation where ground truth is known\. Applied to six pretrained vision transformers on SVG\-World, our deterministic generative benchmark with paired visual styles, and to two of them on CelebA, they show pretraining produces structure beyond a random kernel but well short of a linear world model\. On dSprites, 3D Shapes and MPI3D, forward decodability and latent\-aligned variance dissociate\. Thus, forward decoding alone does not show that the probed factors align with the dominant geometry of the representation\. In summary, our work cautions about the success of linear probes as opposed to truly linear and low dimensional representations\.

## [Continuous Learning and Multimodal Techniques for Next\-Generation Spam Detection Systems](../publications/03e8a660a6c1340b2ce9.md)

Maria Qamar; Nilesh Jain

The problem of email spam is still extremely topical since the unsolicited bulk messages change in both content and method\. This essay examines machine learning\-based spam filters on a test email dataset that consists of spam and valid \(ham\) emails\. We use four classifiers, namely Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), Random Forest and Logistic Regression and compare them in terms of measures of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1\-score\. The models are all high in spam detection accuracy \(greater than 90 percent\), with SVM being a little better in the overall accuracy \(approximately 95\.5 percent\) and accuracy\. Naive Bayes has the best spam recall \(around 94\.2\) but with a more significant number of false positives and a trade\-off between spam captures and legitimate email loss\. We use extensive text preprocessing \(tokenization, stop\-word elimination, stemming\) and make comparisons of feature representations: word embeddings vs\. term frequency\-inverse document frequency \(TF\-IDF\)\. TF\-IDF features performed better on this dataset than the average word embeddings on this dataset\. In the fight against constantly evolving spam techniques, we consider the use of continuous learning approaches that dynamically update the filter to overcome concept drift, and we consider multimodal approaches that use textual and image data or link analysis to detect material that the purely textual filter fails to detect\. As we have found, it is indeed true that using fixed machine learning models is effective in detecting spam and doing it with a high level of accuracy, however next\-generation systems do need to constantly learn and make use of several data modalities to serve as a resource to robust and adaptive spam filtering in dynamic real\-life scenarios\.

## [Astrophysical Parameters of 5056 Open Star Clusters from Bayesian Nested Sampling with PARSEC Isochrones](../publications/03e993bb89710e57f6d7.md)

O\. Plevne; Furkan Akbaba

Abstract We present a homogeneous catalogue of ages, metallicities, distances, and reddenings for 5 056 open clusters in the Unified Cluster Catalogue \(UCC\), derived uniformly from Gaia Data Release 3 \(DR3\) colour–magnitude diagrams via Bayesian nested sampling with PARSEC isochrones\. Unlike previous large\-scale catalogues, metallicity is fitted as a free parameter for every cluster rather than fixed or adopted from the literature: where available, Gaia XP spectrophotometric metallicities inform the fit \(1 201 clusters\), while the remaining clusters are constrained by broad priors from Gaia parallaxes and the Schlegel–Finkbeiner–Davis dust map\. No cluster is anchored to an external open\-cluster parameter catalogue, and no per\-cluster manual intervention is applied\. A fit\-quality metric, ηfit, identifies 3 807 clusters \(75 per cent\) with reliable colour–magnitude solutions, spanning ages of 0\.004–5\.9 Gyr and distances out to 17 kpc\. We validate the resulting parameters against six literature catalogues and, more critically, against independent high\-resolution spectroscopic metallicities from OCCAM DR19: for 132 clusters in common we find a median absolute deviation of only 0\.054 dex \(−0\.021 ± 0\.132 dex mean offset\), comparable to the intrinsic systematic uncertainty of isochrone\-based metallicities\. As a direct consequence of this fidelity, the radial metallicity gradient recovered from our XP\-informed clusters \(−0\.064 dex kpc−1\) steepens towards the spectroscopically calibrated value \(−0\.079 dex kpc−1\) for the highest\-quality subset – demonstrating that a purely photometric pipeline, built without reference to spectroscopy, recovers a physically meaningful abundance scale\. The full catalogue and posterior chains are publicly released\.

## [Development of a Novel Non\-Invasive Blood Pressure Measurement Technique Using Near\-Infrared Spectroscopy and Deep Neural Networks](../publications/03ec0e6679ffca5c0af7.md)

Roya Kheyrkhah Shali; Seyed Kamaledin Setarehdan; Behjat Seifi

Non\-invasive monitoring of blood pressure is essential for health management in daily life, particularly for elderly individuals and patients with autonomic dysfunction\. However, conventional cuff\-based sphygmomanometers are uncomfortable and provide discontinuous monitoring\. In this study, we propose a novel non\-invasive technique for blood pressure change assessment based on prefrontal near\-infrared spectroscopy \(NIRS\) and deep neural networks\. Unlike existing approaches that rely primarily on electrocardiography or photoplethysmography signals, the proposed method independently utilizes prefrontal NIRS signals to capture optical responses associated with postural changes\. This enables early prediction of blood pressure changes following standing\. NIRS is a non\-invasive, real\-time, portable, high temporal resolution, and cost\-effective in comparison with other brain monitoring modalities\. NIRS signals were collected from 40 healthy adults \(aged 19\-39 years\) as test and training groups, 40 entirely new volunteers as an independent evaluation group, and during sit\-to\-stand transitions using a two\-channel system, while reference blood pressure measurements were obtained using an automatic sphygmomanometer\. An adaptive filtering framework was applied to suppress physiological noise, and multiple deep learning architectures were evaluated for regression analysis\. A hybrid convolutional neural network\-gated recurrent unit \(CNN\-GRU\) model achieved the best performance, yielding root mean square errors of 1\.95 mmHg and 1\.75 mmHg for systolic and diastolic blood pressure, respectively\. The results demonstrate that prefrontal NIRS combined with deep learning provides a reliable and accurate framework for non\-invasive blood pressure change monitoring\. This technique shows strong potential for wearable applications in elderly populations and individuals at risk of orthostatic hypotension, and it establishes a foundation for future clinical deployment\.

## [Managers&\#x27; Freelancer Mindset Orientation and relational evaluations as drivers of pay decisions for external workers](../publications/03f1f33d1ed102f91fe0.md)

Hilla Peretz; Aharon E\. Tziner; Cristinel Vasiliu; Andreea Saseanu

Purpose Organizations increasingly rely on freelancers, yet pay parity between freelancers and comparable employees varies widely\. This study introduces Freelancer Mindset Orientation \(FMO\), managers&\#x27; perception of freelancing as a legitimate, attractive, and personally resonant career mode, and examines how it shapes pay equality decisions for external workers through relational evaluations and organizational inclusion practices\. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 353 managers recruited via the Prolific platform were analyzed using path analysis in Mplus 9, with bias\-corrected bootstrapped confidence intervals \(5,000 resamples\) to test mediation and moderation hypotheses\. Findings Managers&\#x27; Freelancer Mindset Orientation \(FMO\) was positively associated with pay equality for freelancers and with more favorable relational evaluations of freelancers \(perceived fit, commitment/loyalty, and trustworthiness\)\. Relational evaluations were, in turn, positively associated with pay equality and partially explained by the FMO\-pay association\. The positive association between FMO and pay equality was stronger among managers reporting higher organizational inclusion of freelancers\. Inclusion also strengthened the association between FMO and relational evaluations, whereas the association between relational evaluations and pay equality did not vary significantly across inclusion levels\. Research limitations The cross\-sectional design limits causal inference\. Future research should employ longitudinal designs, multi\-source data \(payroll records, freelancer reports\), and cross\-national samples\. Practical implications Organizations can promote pay fairness by developing managerial FMO through training, building trust\-based manager\-freelancer relationships, and implementing inclusive practices that integrate freelancers into organizational workflows\. Originality/value This study introduces FMO as a novel identity\-based micro\-level construct and provides the first empirical test of how managerial career orientations, relational evaluations, and inclusion practices jointly determine pay equality for external workers\.

## [AI chatbot integration in fashion e\-retail: consumer behaviour shifts and pathways to organizational change](../publications/04034e18075092a34352.md)

Ying Wu; Malcolm Stewart; Fred A\. Yamoah; Fahima Alam

Purpose AI chatbots are increasingly embedded in customer\-facing retail operations, yet research has examined them mainly as tools of individual adoption\. This study positions consumer attitudinal and behavioural responses to chatbots in fashion e\-retail as micro\-level foundations that may create pressures and capabilities for organisational change\. Design/methodology/approach Integrating TAM, TRA, TPB and the Uses and Gratifications Theory, an integrative model links technology readiness \(TR\), perceived adaptiveness \(PA\), hedonic motivation \(HM\), symbolic and social value and subjective norms \(SN\) to attitude and behavioural intention, tested with PLS\-SEM on survey data from 776 UK consumers and bias\-corrected bootstrap mediation analysis\. Findings HM and PA emerge as dominant antecedents of attitude \(R2 = 0\.736\), which strongly predicts behavioural intention \(ß = 0\.829, R2 = 0\.699\)\. Attitude mediates the effects of perceived usefulness \(PU\) and HM on intention; PA mediates the TR pathway\. Research limitations/implications The cross\-sectional, consumer\-side design limits causal and organisational inference; longitudinal and cross\-industry replication are priorities for future work\. Practical implications Managers should treat chatbots as experience\-design assets, reconfigure service KPIs around hedonic and adaptive value and address workforce implications of redistributed emotional labour\. Social implications This study highlights the societal implications of AI\-enabled service transformation, including risks of digital exclusion, job transformation, deskilling and the redistribution of emotional labour\. As chatbots become embedded in organisational service infrastructures, firms should balance automation with inclusive, human\-centred design\. The findings emphasise accessible, ethically governed and culturally responsive AI systems that support equitable participation across diverse user groups while preserving appropriate opportunities for human interaction\. Originality/value Recasting fashion e\-retail as a distinctive, identity\-driven site for theorising AI\-enabled change, the study specifies three pathways through which chatbot integration may contribute to organisational change: demand\-side expectation shifts, data\-enabled organisational learning and the reconfiguration of service work\.

## [Intraoperative OCT observation of incision\-related descemet membrane detachment during implantable collamer lens implantation](../publications/0404aa856744ca33c466.md)

Jiao Xie; Nian Guan; Ying Liu; Zhenwen Zheng; Xing He; Zhengwei Shen

Purpose The occurrence of Descemet membrane detachment \(DMD\) during each surgical step of implantable Collamer lens \(ICL\) surgery for phakic eyes using intraoperative OCT navigation microscope, and to analyze the factors influencing DMD\. Methods The single\-center retrospective case series included 100 eyes of 50 patients aged 21 to 38 years with refractive errors from July to October 2024, and all patients underwent ICL surgery with a 3\.0 mm steep\-axis surgical incision\. During the operation, the intraoperative OCT navigation microscope was used to observe at each step whether the DMD occured at the incision site and whether the range of detachment changed in subsequent steps\. Results All procedures were completed successfully without intraoperative complications\. No DMD was detected by the end of incision creation\. The cumulative number of eyes in which DMD had been detected increased to 21 \(21%\) by the end of ICL insertion, 34 \(34%\) by the end of ICL positioning, and 45 \(45%\) by the end of irrigation/aspiration of the viscoelastic agent\. In the mixed\-effects analysis accounting for the correlation between fellow eyes, lower preoperative intraocular pressure was associated with higher odds of DMD occurrence \(odds ratio per 1\-mmHg increase, 0\.77; 95% CI, 0\.61–0\.97; P = 0\.03\)\. None of the evaluated factors was significantly associated with DMD extent\. Conclusion Intraoperative OCT enabled real\-time detection of incision\-related DMD developing or extending during ICL surgery\. The cumulative occurrence of DMD increased as the procedure progressed, supporting careful instrument manipulation and minimization of repeated contact with the corneal incision throughout surgery\.

## [Explainable machine learning with a graphical user interface for estimating compressive strength and life cycle assessment based embodied carbon of rice husk ash concrete](../publications/040681d4ef40287959e4.md)

Stephen Adeyemi Alabi; Ibrahim A\. Tijani; Alireza Moghayedi; Jeffrey Mahachi; Samson Olalekan Odeyemi

Meeting the growing demand for concrete while reducing its environmental impact remains a crucial challenge for the construction industry\. Although rice husk ash \(RHA\) offers substantial potential as a supplementary cementitious material to lower cement\-related emissions, its widespread adoption is constrained by uncertainty in achieving a performance\-environmental efficiency trade\-off between mechanical performance and embodied carbon reduction\. This paper proposes an explainable machine learning \(ML\) framework for the evaluation of compressive strength of RHA\-based concrete across various curing stages, complemented by life cycle assessment \(LCA\) based embodied carbon evaluation\. A refined database compiled from existing studies was adopted to train and optimise eight different ML models\. The models were optimised using Optuna and assessed using multiple performance metrics, while SHapley Additive exPlanation \(SHAP\) was adopted to quantify global and local feature contributions\. To support practical deployment, the best performing models were incorporated within an interactive decision support interface facilitating real time, coding free compressive strength prediction together with LCA\-based embodied carbon calculation; thereby supporting performance\-based mix design and accelerating the sustainable use of agricultural waste derived cementitious materials\.

## [More is not necessarily better: A comparison of 2\-mA and 4\-mA prefrontal cortex anodal tDCS on endurance performance, head oxygenation, cognition, and psychophysiological responses in cyclists](../publications/0407820f3eefa7912604.md)

Everton Borges da Silva; Mércia Jaynne Leandro de Melo; Matheus Alves Mendonça; Daniel de Medeiros Leiros; Ehsan Amiri; Heloiana Faro; Daniel Gomes da Silva Machado

A single session of 2 mA anodal tDCS produced small, practically relevant improvements in endurance performance relative to sham alongside intensity\-dependent changes in prefrontal head oxygenation, with the largest performance benefit associated with poorer baseline cognitive performance; 4 mA did not differ from sham on either outcome\.
