## [Gender Differences in Information Systems Research: Representation and Productivity](../publications/0408e8b64543a4465520.md)

Aaron M\. French; Amy B\. Woszczynski; Yuanxia Li; Carole L\. Hollingsworth; John D\. Rusk

This research evaluates gender differences in information systems \(IS\) research among the Senior Scholars’ Basket of 8 \(SB8\)\. Using an archival research method, we collect and analyze all research publications over the first two decades of the 21st century to assess gender differences in research publications and the representativeness of women in IS research\. Our analysis reviews 5,080 published articles, 5,606 unique authors, and 13,692 author listings in the journal list\. Findings reveal that women comprise 26\.85% of unique authors, which is representative of the field of IS, reported at 28%\. The quantity of publications differs, with men significantly outperforming women \(23\.13% of all author listings\)\. Furthermore, only 14 women appear on the top 100 scholars in the field of IS over the two\-decade period\. While women are proportionately represented in the field of IS, they are underrepresented at the highest levels of research productivity\. The findings call for further investigation into the causes of these disparities and suggest that increased mentorship and networking opportunities for women may help address the gap in research output\. We conclude with insights and recommendations for future research and advancing gender equity in the field of IS\.

## [Deportation, Displacement, and Reintegration: Pakistani Migrant Workers Returning from the UAE Amid Geopolitical Crisis](../publications/040935583d6dda7aa1ae.md)

Zubair Butt Hussain; Muhammad Munib Khalid; Ihtisham Ullah; Agustino Silverius Mbunda; Saeed Agha Ahmadzai

This article examines the reported deportation and crisis\-driven return of Pakistani migrant workers from the United Arab Emirates \(UAE\) during the 2026 regional crisis and considers its implications for reintegration in Pakistan\. Drawing on qualitative critical\-interpretive document analysis, the study reviews event\-specific journalistic reporting, Pakistani migration\-governance documents, material on Gulf labor regimes, and scholarship on deportation and reintegration\. The analysis does not find sufficient publicly available evidence to establish that the UAE implemented a formally documented policy of sectarian deportation against Pakistani Shi’a workers\. Rather, it identifies a politically sensitive context in which routine immigration enforcement, reported experiences of discretionary suspicion, and the structural deportability of temporary migrant workers appeared to converge\. Reported accounts indicate possible disruption to employment, access to savings, personal belongings, and future migration plans; read alongside reintegration scholarship, these accounts point to plausible economic, social, and psychosocial risks after return to Pakistan\. The article develops the concept of securitized labor governance to explain how temporary labor regimes may become more security\-inflected during geopolitical crisis without necessarily constituting a formal discriminatory policy\. It concludes by recommending a coordinated, district\-linked crisis\-returnee response in Pakistan, including registration, consular case documentation, legal referral, psychosocial support, and livelihood assistance\.

## [Ayurvedic Gastronomy of Kṛtānna Varga: The Process of Food Preparation in the Light of Modern Nutrition and Food Science](../publications/0410e9d98f9c0110fee9.md)

Disha Gupta; Samhita Hegde

Background: Ayurveda gives great importance to Āhāra \(food\) and also has an extensive list of food preparations called Kṛtānna Varga\. Various processes, like washing, boiling, milling, roasting, frying, drying, and mixing of ingredients are involved in the process of preparing these foods\. This may have an effect on the digestibility, nutritional profile, and sensory quality of the food that is prepared\. Modern food science offers a platform for studying these changes in terms of starch, protein, lipids, phytochemicals, and products of processing\. Objective: To review the selected Kṛtānna Varga products in terms of modern nutrition and food chemistry, especially with regard to gelatinisation of starch, digestibility of proteins, variations in anti\-nutritional factors, lipoxidation and Maillard reactions\. Methods: The study consisted of a literature review of the available Ayurvedic sources combined with contemporary sources on rice, wheat, pulses, milk, ghee, ginger, turmeric, and reactions in food processing during heating\. Results: From the reviewed literature, it is clear that cooking procedures related to Kṛtānna Varga could be linked to many possible changes in the characteristics of the foods\. Cooking of rice through boiling can cause starch gelatinization, while cooking of rice with pulses can affect protein digestibility and lower the presence of some antinutritional components\. Heat treatment of milk causes denaturation of proteins and may encourage the reaction of lactose and lysine\. Ghee is prone to lipid oxidation if heated excessively\. Likewise, browning and frying of wheat products can cause Maillard reactions and, under certain circumstances, acrylamide production\. Conclusion: The ways of preparation explained in Kṛtānna Varga can serve as good reference points in studying the link between traditional food processing and nutritional/chemical modifications of products\. But still, the effects on nutrition or medicine need to be explored more by employing standardized recipes and processing techniques\. Keywords: Ayurveda, Kṛtānna Varga, Āhāra, rice, wheat, ghee, starch gelatinisation, protein digestibility, glycaemic response, food processing

## [Artificial intelligence empowered NB\-IoT systems: architectures, advances, and future perspectives](../publications/04132d18d3c08b35100e.md)

Rakesh K\. Kadu; Lalit Agrawal; Pratik K\. Agrawal; Shivam Sham Agrawal; Manoj Sheshrao Sonune; Madhusudan B\. Kulkarni; Manish L\. Bhaiyya

Abstract With an increasing number of devices being installed in agriculture, factories, hospitals, and cities, the need for intelligent, trustworthy, and energy\-efficient communication systems is rising\. This is one such system: Narrow Band Internet of Things, or NB\-IoT, which connects devices at a long range with low\-power consumption\. But it also has a poor reaction time and is not adaptable to changing situations\. This review discusses how artificial intelligence \(AI\), including machine learning \(ML\), deep learning, and other intelligent methods, are making NB\-IoT more adaptable and predictive\. By deploying lightweight AI models and edge computing—that is, processing locally on a device—systems are able to better manage wireless signals, save battery life, and improve overall performance\. It also discusses several related real\-world applications in the area of agriculture, healthcare, industry, and smart cities and achieves benefits such as saving water, early disease diagnosis, predictive machine maintenance, and environmental monitoring\. The integration of AI with NB\-IoT fosters digital solutions toward sustainability, security, and being human\-centric\. All the progress made thus far will be of immense utility to decision\-makers, engineers, planners of smart cities, and service providers who look to smarter, more affordable, privacy\-friendly technology for the future\.

## [Spin\-Transfer Torque MRAM \(STT\-MRAM\) and Spin\-Orbit Torque \(SOT\) In\-Memory Computing: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy, Crossbar Arrays, and Deep Learning Accelerators](../publications/04134f9c78e331932c19.md)

Harsh Kumar Verma, Aditya Dattarwal, Dr\. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr\. Akhil Pandey

The insatiable memory bandwidth demands of deep learning foundation models and edge artificial intelligence are bottlenecked by the Von Neumann bottleneck: the continuous energy\-prohibitive shuttling of weights and activations between off\-chip dynamic RAM \(DRAM\) and processor arithmetic logic units \(ALUs\)\. Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory \(MRAM\), anchored by magnetic tunnel junctions \(MTJs\) exhibiting Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy \(PMA\), establishes a non\-volatile, radiation\-hardened, and virtually wear\-out\-free memory technology capable of high\-density integration alongside sub\-5nm CMOS logic\. By exploiting Spin\-Transfer Torque \(STT\) and emerging three\-terminal SpinOrbit Torque \(SOT\) switching mechanisms, MRAM enables ultra\-fast write speeds \(\~ns\) and zero standby leakage power\. Furthermore, integrating MTJ crossbar arrays into non\-volatile In\-Memory Computing \(IMC\) architectures allows matrix\-vector multiplications \(MVM\)—the dominant workload in neural network inference—to be executed natively inside memory via Ohm&\#x27;s and Kirchhoff&\#x27;s laws with sub\-nanosecond latency and massive energy reduction\. However, translating spintronic devices into production in\-memory computing systems introduces severe physical and circuit bottlenecks: stochastic thermal switching jitter, limited tunneling magnetoresistance \(TMR\) ratios restricting multi\-bit precision, IRdrop voltage drops across dense crossbar lines, and write\-read disturbance errors\. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of STT\-MRAM and SOT\-MRAM in\-memory computing architectures\. We formalize spin\-transfer torque switching dynamics via the Landau\-Lifshitz\-GilbertSlonczewski \(LLGS\) equation, derive crossbar non\-volatile dot\-product transfer functions, and model stochastic thermal stability factors under PMA scaling\. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SPICE and hardware\-in\-the\-loop testbed evaluating 64Mb STT\-MRAM macro arrays and 3\-terminal SOT\-MRAM neuromorphic inference accelerators across Vision Transformers and ResNet workloads\. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our SOT\-MRAM in\-memory accelerator achieves an energy efficiency of 142\.6 Tera\-Operations per Second per Watt \(TOPS/W\)—a 14x improvement over 4nm digital GPU SRAM caches—while sustaining a sub\-nanosecond MVM latency and 98\.4% image classification accuracy\. Finally, we formulate open challenges in ultra\-dense 3D vertical MTJ integration, all\-spintronic non\-volatile spiking logic, and quantum\-resistant spintronic PUFs\.

## [Cross\-Embodiment Causal Transfer from Human Videos to Robot Manipulation](../publications/041561c4263289c77924.md)

Xingyu Zhang; Yingchao Li; Peizheng Guo; Jie Hu; Changwen Zheng; Wenwen Qiang

Scaling robot manipulation models requires large amounts of interaction data, yet collecting diverse real\-robot experience remains costly\. Human manipulation videos, in contrast, provide abundant and diverse task experience that could potentially benefit robot learning\. However, differences in morphology, action spaces, and control mechanisms make human motions unsuitable as direct supervision for robot actions, raising a scientific question: what knowledge in human videos should be transferred across embodiments to robot manipulation? To address this question, we analyze subtask transfer through the lens of causal beams, focusing on which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies should be retained to support local task effects\. Based on this perspective, we propose Causal\-Beam\-Guided Subtask Transfer \(CBST\)\. CBST learns manipulation\-related representations from human videos and grounds them in task\-level semantic variables using robot demonstrations\. Within a predefined manipulation model, causal\-beam constraints guide contextual information selection by requiring retained assignments to sustain local mechanism outputs while preserving nontrivial responsiveness to retained inputs\. The selected semantic information conditions a world\-action model, allowing the robot to generate actions from its own observations without requiring human\-robot motion correspondence\. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show improvements in task success over the corresponding world\-action model baselines\.

## [Random Forest makine öğrenme yöntemiyle GRACE verisinin mekânsal çözünürlüğünün artırılması: Bursa ili için uydu destekli yeraltı suyu tahmini](../publications/0416ee0d102ed771b997.md)

Ali Ünver

Bu çalışmada, GRACE uydularından elde edilen düşük mekânsal çözünürlüklü toplam su depolama anomalisi \(TWSA\) verilerinin yerel ölçekte kullanımını geliştirmek için Random Forest \(RF\) tabanlı bir ölçek küçültme yaklaşımı uygulanmıştır\. Bursa ili için 2002–2024 dönemindeki GRACE Mascon TWSA verileri; CHIRPS yağış, GLDAS toprak nemi, MODIS evapotranspirasyon, gündüz yüzey sıcaklığı, NDVI ve mevsimsel bileşen ile Google Earth Engine ortamında bütünleştirilmiştir\. Bu süreçte 1 km çözünürlükte yıllık yeraltı suyu depolama anomalisi \(GWSA\) haritaları üretilmiştir\. Model, GRACE’in uzun dönemli eğilimlerini güvenilir biçimde yeniden üretmiş; açıklanan varyans %91,65 ve RMSE 3,60 cm olarak belirlenmiştir\. Mekânsal analizler, İznik–Gemlik–Orhangazi hattında belirgin azalışlar; Mustafakemalpaşa–Karacabey ovalarında ise görece durağan veya artış eğilimleri göstermiştir\. Değişken önem analizinde mevsimsel bileşen en yüksek katkıyı sağlamış, yağış ve toprak nemi de temel girdiler olarak öne çıkmıştır\. RF sonuçları, SYGM yeraltı su kütleleriyle yüksek uyum göstermiş ve resmî envanterde tanımlanmayan alanlar için ek mekânsal bilgi sunmuştur\.

## [Pedagogical conditions for forming the readiness of future teachers at the university to use modular e\-learning technology](../publications/041c4e99aec76a9e4ca0.md)

Bayan Kylyshpai; I Yusupova; Raikhan Skakova; Kenzhekhan Medeubayeva; Salima Seitenova

The study aims to determine the impact of the use of modular e\-technology on the level of formation of motivational\-value, cognitive and activity\-practical components of readiness of students of the pedagogical university\. The study is based on a quasi\-experimental design of “pre\-testing with a control group”\. The sample was formed by 162 students of pedagogical specialties of 2–4 years, evenly distributed between the experimental \(n = 81\) and control \(n = 81\) groups\. The diagnostic complex consisted of the author&\#x27;s questionnaire RMETQ, the knowledge test KMELT and a practical task with the analytical rubric ARMECD\. Statistical analysis consisted of MANOVA, ANCOVA, dependent and independent t\-tests, correlation analysis \(Pearson/Spearman\) and effect size estimation\. The results indicated the superiority of the experimental group in all components of readiness \(p &lt; \.001; d = 1\.77–2\.58; η²p = \.439–\.622\)\. The greatest increase was recorded for the activity\-practical component \(\+103\.8%\)\. In the experimental group, an integrated structure of readiness with strong intercomponent correlations \(r = \.61–\.72\) was formed, in contrast to weak connections in the control group \(r = \.27–\.33\)\. The results determined the feasibility of introducing modular e\-technology into the system of pedagogical university training\.

## [Two\-Dimensional Memristors: Materials, Switching Physics, Architectures, and Computing Applications](../publications/0420f7c3e20cf5d12c45.md)

Rajesh Kumar Jha

Abstract For the upcoming generation of non\-volatile memory, neuromorphic computing, and in\-memory artificial intelligence \(AI\) hardware, two\-dimensional \(2D\) material\-based memristors have emerged as a promising device type\. Their van der Waals \(vdW\) interfaces, atomic\-scale thickness, and tunable electronic characteristics enable remarkable control over resistive switching mechanisms\. They have an advantage over conventional bulk oxide memristors in terms of device uniformity, scalability, and power efficiency\. An overview of recent developments in 2D memristive technologies is provided in this review, which also discusses material systems like black phosphorus, hexagonal boron nitride, graphene derivatives, transition metal dichalcogenides, and new 2D ferroelectrics\. Additionally, it covers important resistive switching mechanisms such as interface\-modulated switching, electrochemical metallization, defect and vacancy migration, and phase\-transition\-driven behavior\. The effectiveness of various device architectures, such as planar and vertical structures, vdW heterostructures, and large\-scale crossbar arrays, for in\-memory computing is examined\. Furthermore, neuromorphic characteristics such as very low\-energy matrix\-vector multiplication, spiking neural networks, analog weight modulation, and synaptic plasticity are emphasized\. Important problems pertaining to endurance, environmental stability, variability, and large\-area growth are explored, along with fresh approaches to these problems\. Finally, future directions that highlight the revolutionary potential of 2D memristors for AI, edge computing, and next\-generation memory technologies are described, including 3D integration, atomically engineered defects, and ultra\-flexible neuromorphic systems\.

## [Deep learning\-based predictions and analysis of Norovirus dynamics using a fractional\-order mathematical model](../publications/0424fed08b1ff0fb6759.md)

Basit Rehman; Akhtar Ali

Norovirus, which is extremely contagious and has a significant impact on the gastrointestinal tract, has also been one of the main potential threats to health in the population\. The use of fractional calculus has received much interest in the past few years with regard to the modeling of infectious diseases, especially because it allows modeling the memory and nonlocal processes in a dynamic system\. In this study, a mathematical model is developed to investigate the transmission dynamics of norovirus\. The proposed model consists of five epidemiological compartments: susceptible, exposed, infected, vaccinated, and recovered populations\. The existence and uniqueness of the mathematical model are proven by a fixed\-point theorem\. The findings demonstrate that the sustainability of the disease\-free equilibrium increases with a decrease in fractional order\. In order to observe the effects of the fractional order on the dynamics of disease, numerical simulations are carried out based on the three\-step Adams\-Bashforth procedure, which supports the theoretical results with graphical illustrations\. Moreover, the results are validated through the comparison with deep neural networks\. The comprehensive nature of numerical simulations carried out at different fractional orders and transmission parameters indicates that the dynamics of fractional orders are effective in describing memory and heterogeneity of the disease transmission, which are characterized by classical integer\-order models only to a limited extent\. The results also indicate that the high coverage of vaccination and improvement in the effectiveness of treatment will greatly decrease the prevalence of infections\. Further, the model has been demonstrated to be numerically stable and positive in real parameter disclosures\. Altogether, this study provides a reliable mathematical approach and better understanding for analyzing disease dynamics and may be extended to other applications in epidemiology and related scientific fields\.

## [Northoff, Georg &amp; Gouveia, Steven S\.: Does artificial intelligence exhibit basic fundamental subjectivity? A neurophilosophical argument](../publications/0426d9d693fff9188a8b.md)



\_Phenomenology and the Cognitive Sciences\_ 23 \(5\):1097\-1118\. 2024Does artificial intelligence \(AI\) exhibit consciousness or self? While this question is hotly debated, here we take a slightly different stance by focusing on those features that make possible both, namely a basic or fundamental subjectivity\. Learning from humans and their brain, we first ask what we mean by subjectivity\. Subjectivity is manifest in the perspectiveness and mineness of our experience which, ontologically, can be traced to a point of view\. Adopting a non\-reductive neurophilosophical strategy, we assume that the point of view exhibits two layers, a most basic neuroecological and higher order mental layer\. The neuroecological layer of the point of view is mediated by the timescales of world and brain, as further evidenced by empirical data on our sense of self\. Are there corresponding timescales shared with the world in AI and is there a point of view with perspectiveness and mineness? Discussing current neuroscientific evidence, we deny that current AI exhibits a point of view, let alone perspectiveness and mineness\. We therefore conclude that, as per current state, AI does not exhibit a basic or fundamental subjectivity and henceforth no consciousness or self is possible in models such as ChatGPT and similar technologies\. \(direct link \)

## [Multi\-sourced AI Tutor for Non\-Native English Speaker Students](../publications/043bd131c63cf6f7f3ff.md)

Yiyin Shen; Xinyi Ai; Weibing Wang; Rogers Jeffrey Leo John; Meenakshi Syamkumar

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions\. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non\-native English speaker \(NNES\) students face in computing courses due to language barriers\. To aid such students, we developed a general\-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages \(currently focused on Mandarin\) and provide bilingual responses\. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension\. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries\. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83\.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner\. The tutor also provided high\-quality translations for 76\.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64\.47% of them\. Our findings underscore the potential of multi\-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non\-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course\.

## [External cervical spine joint moments in pilots during high \+Gz real–flight: a biomechanical analysis using individual opensim models](../publications/043d8526cc696f4aab87.md)

Fabian Göll; Bjoern Braunstein; Rene Lingscheid; Roland Nüsse; Dana Hartmann; Robert Rein; Kirsten Albracht

Abstract The cervical spine of fast jet pilots is exposed to high \+Gz accelerations during large range of head movements which may lead to biomechanical impairments\. The objective of this study therefore was to quantify and analyze the resulting external cervical spine joint moments experienced by fast jet pilots during standardized head movements in real–flight during \+5Gz, \+7Gz and \+9Gz maneuvers\. The in– flight helmet orientation recordings and additional ground based motion capture recordings of isolated head movements of seven Eurofighter pilots were processed using a custom made pipeline\. Subsequent inverse kinematics and inverse dynamics simulations of the in–flight head movements using individual OpenSim pilot models showed a significant reduction in the head extension angle with increasing \+Gz acceleration\. Cervical spine joint moments did not change significantly with increasing \+Gz acceleration\. However, theory–based model analysis indicated that constant head positions under higher \+Gz acceleration would lead to an increase in joint moments\. The pilots seemed to exhibit reduced head extension at higher \+Gz levels, while external joint moments remained relatively constant\. Furthermore, the designed pipeline may support individual cervical spine health assessment and monitoring, as well as to inform strength training or rehabilitation programming\.

## [Thinking Beyond the Tool: Misuse of ChatGPT and the Future of Student Cognition](../publications/0445690f3f54295a93da.md)

Intakhab Alam Khan

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly ChatGPT, has rapidly transformed education by providing immediate information, personalized learning support, academic writing assistance, language learning opportunities, and research support\. However, growing concerns exist regarding excessive reliance on AI\-generated content and its potential effects on cognitive development\. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the educational benefits and cognitive risks associated with ChatGPT using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA 2020\) guidelines\. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, PubMed, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2022 and June 2026\. Following systematic screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 27 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis\. Five major themes emerged: educational benefits, cognitive offloading, critical thinking, creativity, and teacher perspectives\. Findings indicate that ChatGPT supports personalized learning, feedback, academic writing, language learning, coding, and research productivity\. Conversely, excessive dependence may contribute to cognitive offloading, weaker memory retention, reduced analytical reasoning and critical thinking, superficial learning, diminished creativity, and academic integrity concerns\. Teacher guidance and ethical AI practices are essential for safeguarding cognitive development\. The review concludes that ChatGPT should enhance rather than replace students’ cognitive activities, supporting critical thinking, creativity, ethical responsibility, and lifelong learning\.

## [An Interpretable Machine Learning Model for 90\-Day Mortality After Major Head and Neck Surgery](../publications/045588a2a0014fa7c95f.md)

Linxin Jiang; Junlin Huang; Daniel Ralph Reissmann; Deborah Kreher; Gerhard Schmalz; Simin Li; Liben Xie

Introduction and aims Head and neck surgery carries substantial perioperative mortality, yet existing risk models lack head\-and\-neck specificity and interpretability\. We aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for 90\-day all\-cause mortality after major head and neck surgery using LASSO, Boruta, and SHAP\. Methods This study conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients \(≥18 years\) undergoing major head and neck surgery between 2015 and 2020 in the INSPIRE database\. LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm were applied for feature selection\. Five classifiers—LASSO, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and AdaBoost—were trained and compared under repeated stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation\. SHAP analysis of the Boruta–XGBoost model provided individualized interpretation of nonlinear prediction drivers\. Results Among 15,694 patients, 90\-day mortality was 0\.44% \(n = 69\)\. At the natural outcome prevalence, LASSO showed the numerically highest discrimination \(AUC 0\.83, 95% CI 0\.77\-0\.89\), sensitivity \(0\.79, 95% CI 0\.70\-0\.88\), and F1 score \(0\.028, 95% CI 0\.025\-0\.032\)\. The AUCs of CatBoost, AdaBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM were 0\.81 \(95% CI 0\.75\-0\.87\), 0\.80 \(95% CI 0\.74\-0\.86\), 0\.78 \(95% CI 0\.72\-0\.84\), and 0\.77 \(95% CI 0\.70\-0\.84\), respectively; however, the confidence intervals overlapped substantially\. Within the Boruta–XGBoost model, SHAP analysis identified preoperative CRP \(mean \|SHAP\| = 1\.050\), albumin \(0\.524\), phosphate \(0\.419\), sodium \(0\.419\), lymphocyte count \(0\.348\), ASA class \(0\.323\), preoperative MACE within 30 days \(0\.317\), platelet count \(0\.271\), ALP \(0\.246\), BUN \(0\.235\), and troponin \(0\.154\) as dominant predictors\. Elevated inflammatory and metabolic markers and depleted nutritional and haematologic reserves shifted predictions toward higher mortality\. Conclusions An interpretable machine learning framework integrating LASSO, Boruta, and SHAP identified parsimonious, biologically plausible predictors of 90\-day mortality after head and neck surgery\. Clinical significance SHAP\-based individualized risk explanations translate algorithmic outputs into modifiable preoperative targets—inflammation, nutrition, electrolyte balance, and cardiovascular reserve—supporting personalized risk stratification, informed consent, and targeted prehabilitation in this high\-risk surgical population\.

## [Evaluating the Performance of LDPC Decoders Using the Sum\- Product and Minimum\-Sum Algorithms in 5G Communication Networks](../publications/045a130ae10d19facbae.md)

Efiyeseimokumo S\. Ikeremo

In need to offer multiple services, wireless mobile communication demands a huge amount of data capacity\. Peak throughput, low latency, and substantial speed are delivered by 5G networks\. Wireless communications increasingly depend on channel coding\. Channel coding for the 5G communication networks is facing a fresh difficulty and Sum product algorithm \(SPA\) is the significant breakthrough in this area\. This research evaluates performance of LDPC of Sum product algorithm \(SPA\) and LDPC of Min\-Sum algorithm \(MSA\) as in channel coding contenders for the 5G communication networks for different coding rates of ½ and 2/3 and at the same block length of 1024\. The simulations are implemented using MATLAB R2018b\. As the quality criterion of a channel code, FER and BER of the coding schemes is displayed versus SNR for the same block lengths \(L=1024\) and different code rates of 1/2 and 2/3 correspondingly\. The evaluations and comparisons are conducted in terms of FER and BER for the same block length \(L=1024\) and differing code rates of 1/2 and 2/3\. It is evident from the results that the SPA surpasses the other rival algorithm for nearly in all code rates\. Also, there is no error floor in case of SPA\. Therefore, choice for faster algorithm which are sought for the 5G communication networks because its characteristic of Enhanced Mobile Broadband \(eMBB\), Ultra\-Reliable Low Latency Communications \(URLLC\), and Massive Machine Type Communications \(mMTC\)\. Although SPA has demonstrated their potential, faster decoding performance enhancement for tiny block lengths is still an unresolved subject\. Channel coding for 5G is a dynamic investigation area as to tackle various outstanding tasks in future\.

## [Physics\-Informed Explainable Hybrid Machine Learning and True Pareto\-Optimal Inverse Design for Strength–Conductivity Optimization of High\-Performance Cu–Cr–X Copper Alloys](../publications/0467c9c93711b794177e.md)

Aswin Karkadakattil

High\-performance Cu–Cr–X copper alloys face an inherent trade\-off between mechanical strength and electrical conductivity\. This study develops a physics\-informed, interpretable machine\-learning framework for their optimization and inverse design\. A literature\-derived dataset of 3017 experimental records was compiled, with 2302 records retained after preprocessing and reliability filtering\. Metallurgically motivated descriptors, including Aging Severity, Cold Work Index, Cr–Aging interaction, Zener\-pinning and Hall–Petch proxies, and source reliability, were incorporated\. Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and CatBoost were evaluated using a leakage\-free 10\-fold out\-of\-fold stacking framework\. The stacking model achieved R 2 = 0\.895, MAE = 17\.3, and RMSE = 48\.7, compared with R 2 values of 0\.781, 0\.802, 0\.837, and 0\.857, respectively, for the four base learners\. SHAP analysis highlighted Cu, Cr, source reliability, aging\-related variables, and precipitation\-related descriptors as important predictors\. Pareto\-based inverse screening identified candidates with predicted Strength Index values exceeding 520 and approaching 580, with conductivity reaching approximately 95 %IACS\. The framework provides a data\-driven route for narrowing the Cu–Cr–X design space, while the predicted candidates require experimental validation\.

## [Post\-traumatic headache as a window into persistent brain dysfunction after traumatic brain injury: an opinion article](../publications/046f71324dac4fc27b50.md)

Denise Franco de Almeida Duarte; Jader Vinicius Da Silva Rocha; Fernanda Moura Vargas Dias; Micheline Henrique Araújo da Luz Koerich; Vitória Caroline Reinoso de Almeida; Rodrigo Freire de Almeida; Walter Gomes da Silva Filho; Fernando Zanela da Silva Arêas

Traumatic brain injury \(TBI\) remains a major cause of death and disability worldwide, particularly among young adults and individuals of working age \(1,2\)\. Advances in prehospital care, neurosurgery, and intensive care have improved survival after TBI, increasing attention to the persistent symptoms and functional limitations that may affect long\-term recovery and quality of life \(1,2\)\.Post\-traumatic headache \(PTH\) is a secondary headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head, including TBI, and is among the most frequent neurological symptoms reported after TBI \(3\)\(4\)\(5\)\(6\)\. In this article, we specifically address PTH occurring in the context of TBI rather than the broader category of headache attributed to head injury without established TBI\. Consistent with the International Classification of Headache Disorders, PTH that persists for more than three months is referred to here as persistent PTH \(3\)\. Persistent PTH may coexist with fatigue, cognitive complaints, sleep disturbances, anxiety, depression, and limitations in daily activities \(4\)\(5\)\(6\), contributing to the complexity of long\-term clinical recovery\.Conventional measures of initial TBI severity, including the Glasgow Coma Scale \(GCS\), pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings, remain essential for acute assessment and prognosis\.However, the relationship between the extent and characteristics of the initial injury and persistent symptoms is not straightforward, and individuals with apparently similar acute injury characteristics may follow different long\-term recovery trajectories \(4\-6, 11, 12\)\. This variability has increased interest in biological and functional processes that may persist or evolve after the acute injury \(7\)\(8\)\(9\)\.Against this background, we propose the hypothesis that persistent PTH may serve as a clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction after TBI\. This concept does not imply that persistent PTH is itself a biomarker or that it demonstrates the presence of a specific underlying mechanism\. Rather, we propose that its persistence may serve as a clinical signal warranting investigation of functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully characterized by conventional structural assessment\. This hypothesis is considered across the TBI severity spectrum\. However, the evidence discussed in this article derives from heterogeneous populations, including mild TBI and moderate\-to\-severe TBI, and findings from one severity group should not be assumed to generalize to another\. Furthermore, evidence directly obtained from patients with persistent PTH remains more limited than evidence derived from broader TBI populations\. Throughout this article, we therefore distinguish PTH\-specific findings from mechanisms that remain biologically plausible on the basis of the broader TBI literature\.Acute TBI severity remains a major determinant of early clinical outcomes\. Measures such as the GCS, pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings are strongly associated with mortality and functional disability and remain fundamental for clinical decision\-making and prognostic assessment \(1,2,10\)\. However, these measures were primarily developed to characterize the initial injury and estimate acute outcomes, and their ability to account for persistent symptoms and heterogeneous longterm recovery trajectories is more limited \(11,12\)\.Patients with apparently similar initial injury characteristics may experience markedly different longterm outcomes, including persistent headache, fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life \(11,12\)\. This variability suggests that the extent and characteristics of the initial injury alone do not fully capture the processes associated with long\-term recovery\.TBI initiates a cascade of biological events that may extend beyond the acute phase \(7\-9\)\. Among these processes, neuroinflammation has been extensively investigated\. Acute activation of microglia and astrocytes contributes to tissue responses following injury, whereas sustained or dysregulated inflammatory activity has been associated with blood\-brain barrier alterations, persistent inflammatory signaling, and changes in neuronal function \(7\)\(8\)\(9\)\(17\)\(18\)\(19\)\. Importantly, evidence of persistent neuroinflammation after TBI derives predominantly from experimental studies and broader TBI populations and should not be interpreted as evidence that neuroinflammation directly causes persistent PTH\. Rather, it provides a biologically plausible framework that requires specific validation in patients with persistent PTH\.Altered nociceptive processing may represent another relevant mechanism\. Central sensitization should be distinguished from nociplastic pain and other forms of altered nociceptive signaling because these concepts are related but not interchangeable \(20,21\)\. PTH\-specific studies have identified sensory abnormalities, including cephalic allodynia, hyperalgesia, and altered pain modulatory responses, supporting abnormal nociceptive processing in at least a subset of patients with persistent PTH \(22\)\. Experimental evidence of hypersensitivity to calcitonin gene\-related peptide \(CGRP\) further supports the involvement of CGRP\-related nociceptive pathways \(23\)\. However, these findings neither establish central sensitization as a universal mechanism nor demonstrate a single pathophysiological pathway underlying persistent PTH\.A complementary perspective is provided by network neuroscience, which conceptualizes neurological dysfunction as potentially arising from disturbances in interactions among distributed brain networks rather than exclusively from focal structural damage \(13\)\(14\)\(15\)\. TBI studies have demonstrated persistent structural network abnormalities during recovery \(24\), while PTH\-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in resting\-state functional connectivity involving pain\-processing, painmodulatory, and affective networks \(25,26\)\. These findings provide more direct, although still limited, evidence that persistent PTH may be associated with alterations in brain network function\.Persistent PTH also frequently co\-occurs with fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life \(4\)\(5\)\(6\)\. Rather than representing different expressions of a single persistent biological condition, these manifestations may arise from partially overlapping, independent, or mutually reinforcing mechanisms\. Their co\-occurrence therefore underscores the heterogeneity of post\-traumatic recovery and the need to investigate how different biological and functional processes contribute to individual symptom profiles\.Within the framework proposed here, persistent PTH is considered a potential clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction rather than a validated biomarker, prognostic indicator, or surrogate measure of an underlying biological process\. We use the term clinical window to describe an observable clinical feature whose persistence may signal the need to investigate ongoing functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully captured by conventional structural assessment\. Thus, persistent PTH is proposed primarily as a clinical signal for further investigation, not as evidence that a specific pathophysiological process is present\.We use the term persistent brain dysfunction as an umbrella concept encompassing ongoing abnormalities in neural function or biological processes after TBI, including altered nociceptive processing, disturbances in brain network function, and potentially persistent inflammatory activity\. This definition does not imply a single mechanism, nor does it assume that these abnormalities are present in all individuals with persistent PTH or that persistent PTH is caused by any one of them\.The distinction is important because the evidence supporting these potential mechanisms varies substantially\. PTH\-specific neuroimaging studies have demonstrated alterations in resting\-state functional connectivity involving pain\-processing and pain\-modulatory networks, including periaqueductal gray\-related connectivity, with some alterations associated with headache burden or the subsequent development of persistent PTH \(25,26\)\. By contrast, evidence for persistent neuroinflammation and several other chronic neurobiological abnormalities derives predominantly from broader TBI populations\. These mechanisms should therefore be regarded as biologically plausible contributors requiring direct investigation in persistent PTH rather than as established pathophysiological correlates of the condition\.Persistent PTH may also reflect greater overall symptom burden rather than a distinct biological state\.Headache commonly co\-occurs with sleep disturbance, fatigue, cognitive complaints, anxiety, depression, and other post\-traumatic symptoms \(4\-6\), and these factors may independently influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function\. Pre\-existing headache disorders, injury severity, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and psychological and behavioral factors may further contribute to clinical heterogeneity\. Consequently, the presence or severity of persistent PTH cannot currently be assumed to indicate the presence, type, or magnitude of persistent brain dysfunction\.Testing the proposed clinical\-window hypothesis will therefore require prospective studies that combine detailed headache phenotyping with objective measures of brain function and biology while accounting for relevant confounding factors\. Quantitative electroencephalography, neuroimagingderived connectivity measures, and molecular or inflammatory measures are candidate approaches that could be evaluated in this context \(24,27,28,31\)\. Artificial intelligence and machine\-learning methods may complement these measures as analytical approaches for identifying multidimensional patterns or patient phenotypes, rather than representing biological or functional measures themselves \(29,30\)\.At present, none of these candidate approaches can be considered a validated biomarker of persistent PTH\. Their value lies in testing whether persistent PTH is systematically associated with measurable patterns of post\-traumatic dysfunction beyond headache severity and overall symptom burden\.The hypothesis proposed in this article should be interpreted within several important limitations\. First, evidence directly linking persistent PTH to measurable ongoing brain dysfunction remains limited\.Although PTH\-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in functional connectivity \(25,26\), much of the evidence supporting persistent neuroinflammation, neurophysiological abnormalities, and other chronic biological processes derives from broader TBI populations\. Extrapolation of these findings to persistent PTH therefore requires caution, and associations observed after TBI should not be assumed to represent mechanisms of persistent PTH\.Second, persistent PTH is clinically and biologically heterogeneous\. Headache phenotype, pre\-existing headache disorders, TBI severity, sleep disturbance, fatigue, psychological symptoms, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and other post\-traumatic symptoms may influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function\. These factors provide alternative or complementary explanations for associations between persistent PTH and biological or functional abnormalities\. Consequently, future studies should determine whether such associations remain after appropriate characterization and adjustment for relevant confounding factors\.The proposed clinical\-window hypothesis also generates testable predictions\. If persistent PTH is associated with ongoing post\-traumatic dysfunction beyond overall symptom burden, individuals with persistent PTH should demonstrate reproducible functional or biological abnormalities when compared with appropriately matched TBI survivors without persistent PTH\. These associations should remain detectable after accounting for injury severity, pre\-existing headache, headache phenotype, psychological symptoms, sleep disturbance, medication use, and other relevant clinical factors\.Longitudinal studies should further determine whether changes in headache frequency, intensity, or disability are accompanied by changes in candidate neurophysiological, neuroimaging, or molecular measures\.Conversely, failure to identify reproducible associations between persistent PTH and objective measures of post\-traumatic dysfunction, particularly after controlling for symptom burden and relevant confounders, would argue against the proposed clinical\-window hypothesis or restrict its applicability to specific patient subgroups\. This possibility is important because the framework proposed here should be considered a testable hypothesis rather than an assumption that persistent headache necessarily reflects ongoing brain dysfunction\.Future research should therefore prioritize prospective longitudinal designs with detailed headache phenotyping and appropriate comparison groups\. Studies comparing TBI survivors with persistent PTH, TBI survivors without persistent PTH, and, where appropriate, individuals with primary headache disorders may help determine which findings are related specifically to persistent PTH, to TBI more broadly, or to chronic headache irrespective of trauma\. Stratification by mild TBI and moderate\-to\-severe TBI will also be necessary because mechanisms and recovery trajectories may differ across injury severity\.Multimodal studies integrating clinical phenotyping with neuroimaging, quantitative electroencephalography, and molecular measures may help determine whether reproducible patterns of dysfunction can be identified in specific persistent PTH subgroups\. Artificial intelligence and machine\-learning approaches may support the analysis of these multidimensional datasets and the identification of patient phenotypes, but their role is analytical and depends on the quality and validation of the underlying clinical and biological measures \(24,\(27\)\(28\)\(29\)\(30\)\(31\)\. Candidate measures should not be considered biomarkers until their reproducibility, specificity, longitudinal behavior, and clinical relevance have been established in persistent PTH populations\.Ultimately, the value of the proposed framework will depend on whether persistent PTH provides clinically meaningful information beyond established measures of injury severity and overall posttraumatic symptom burden\. Prospective validation is therefore required before persistent PTH can be used to identify individuals for additional biological assessment, prognostic stratification, or mechanism\-based interventions\. Persistent PTH may provide a clinically accessible signal for investigating ongoing functional or biological abnormalities after TBI, but this relationship remains hypothetical and should not be interpreted as evidence that persistent headache is itself a biomarker of brain dysfunction\.Distinguishing PTH\-specific findings from abnormalities associated with TBI more broadly, controlling for alternative explanations and confounding factors, and prospectively testing the proposed associations will be essential to determine the validity and clinical relevance of this framework\.

## [APLICAÇÃO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL COMO FERRAMENTA DE APOIO À IDENTIFICAÇÃO DE OPORTUNIDADES DE MELHORIA CONTÍNUA EM PROCESSOS INDUSTRIAIS](../publications/0478d28d1996d8533527.md)

Amanda Lima; Ana Moura; Isabela Antunes; João Silva; Mariana Costa; Mikael Silva

O aumento da competitividade global e a complexidade das cadeias produtivas exigem que as organizações industriais promovam o aprimoramento contínuo de seus processos e a redução de desperdícios por meio de metodologias de gestão consolidadas, notadamente o Lean Manufacturing e o Kaizen\. Com a consolidação da Indústria 4\.0 e a proliferação de sistemas ciberfísicos, a geração de dados fabris cresceu expressivamente\. Esse fenômeno inviabilizou análises diagnósticas manuais, criando um cenário de saturação informacional que demanda a adoção de tecnologias analíticas avançadas\. Nesse contexto, a Inteligência Artificial \(IA\) desponta como ferramenta algorítmica fundamental para identificar padrões e anomalias multivariadas\. Contudo, o grande desafio científico e prático reside em integrar o poder computacional dessa tecnologia às rotinas de gestão do chão de fábrica para apoiar decisões operacionais, valorizando o conhecimento tácito dos profissionais e mitigando a sobrecarga cognitiva associada à interpretação de falhas\. Essa premissa fundamenta\-se nos preceitos da Indústria 5\.0, que reposiciona o fator humano no centro da governança sistêmica\. Diante desta problemática, o objetivo principal desta pesquisa consiste em propor estratégias organizadas para utilizar a Inteligência Artificial como suporte analítico e decisório na identificação proativa de oportunidades de melhoria contínua\. Para tal, adotou\-se uma metodologia aplicada, exploratória e descritiva, com abordagem mista\. A partir da revisão bibliográfica, elaborou\-se um framework conceitual estruturado em sete etapas que conectam a extração de dados digitais, a modelagem analítica e a execução de ações de melhoria\. A validação exploratória, conduzida com cinco especialistas seniores em engenharia de processos, confirmou a elevada aderência prática e relevância do modelo\. Os resultados demonstraram que, embora a tecnologia processe a complexidade dos dados operacionais com precisão, a validação contextual e a priorização de intervenções permanecem como prerrogativas essencialmente humanas\. Conclui\-se que a IA atua como um catalisador da inteligência humana, e o framework desenvolvido contribui para sistematizar essa simbiose sociotécnica em prol da excelência operacional sustentável\.

## [Legal status, gender, and the division of household labour among African couples](../publications/047bea8c12a418ba5a47.md)

Nicole Kreisberg; Hannah Persaud

Legal status is a pivotal axis of stratification in the United States\. Yet individuals do not migrate alone\. Two\-thirds of migrants are married, and migrant spouses receive a separate – and often dependent – legal categorization from that of their husband or wife\. International student visa dependents, for instance, are legally tied to their spouse, and they cannot work or attend school full\-time themselves\. These constraints raise important theoretical questions about how immigration laws, via dependent visas, contribute to gender inequalities in migrant households\. Drawing on 52 in\-depth interviews with members of 26 African student visa couples, this article illustrates how dependent visas produce different household divisions of labour depending on the dependent visa holder&\#x27;s gender\. Women on dependent visas maintain traditional domesticated roles, blaming their lack of agency on US law\. Men, by contrast, respond to visa restrictions in one of two ways\. Some men resist domesticated household roles, leaving their full\-time student wives to pick up the ‘second shift’ at home\. Others adjust to household responsibilities by invoking their agency over the adjustment, rather than the law’s – masculinising their domesticity through language of self\-sacrifice\. The law interacts with gender ideology and individual agency to structure household labour decisions\.

## [Cities and urban areas are central to global decarbonization pathways](../publications/0482b429a59996090104.md)

Diego Manya; Mark Roelfsema; Yuetong Zhang; Ying Yu; Gunnar Luderer; Pascal Weigmann; Angel Hsu

Cities and subnational governments are increasingly adopting mitigation targets and plans toward net\-zero goals, yet the global pathways used to assess decarbonization remain too spatially coarse to directly evaluate their contribution\. Here, we develop a policy\-compatible framework that links Current Policies \(Medium\) and below\-2 °C \(Low\) pathways from the IMAGE integrated assessment model \(IAM\) to dynamically changing urban administrative units through a Kaya\-based downscaling approach\. We find that urban administrative areas account for most modeled emissions and mitigation under both scenarios, with their share remaining high across regions despite substantial and heterogeneous spatial restructuring over time\. Integrating pledges from 1363 subnational entities across 48 countries, we estimate that by 2050 these commitments could deliver additional mitigation beyond those already accounted for under national policies, equivalent to 14\.6–15\.9% of the global urban Medium pathway and 17\.5–18\.4% across the G20\. If fully implemented, these commitments would bring participating jurisdictions collectively close to the Low pathway, but would remain insufficient on their own to shift the overall global emissions trajectory onto a pathway likely to keep warming below 2 °C\. Our findings demonstrate the potential significance of subnational action while highlighting the need for coordinated mitigation across multiple levels of government\.

## [Intrapartum ultrasound parameters within prediction models for mode of birth in nulliparous women: a scoping review](../publications/04833e57e5ca173d9f9b.md)

Yanwen Li; Lin Rao; Linglin Pan; Peimin Xie; Wenlin Zhou; Hong Li

Intrapartum ultrasound \(IPUS\) provides objective measurements of foetal head descent and position\. This scoping review mapped how IPUS parameters have been incorporated into prediction models for mode of birth in nulliparous women, the performance and validation reported by the included studies, and the evidence relevant to obstetric nursing and midwifery\. We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and PRISMA\-ScR\. Ten English\- and Chinese\-language databases were searched until February 2026\. Eligible studies developed or validated a prediction model that included at least one IPUS parameter for a mode\-of\-birth outcome in nulliparous women\. Two reviewers independently screened the records, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias using PROBAST\. The findings were synthesised narratively and stratified according to clinical timing\. Comparison with clinical\-only models was outside the review scope\. Nineteen cohort studies \(14 prospective and 5 retrospective; 2011–2026; 64–1,020 women\) were included\. Sixteen studies used logistic regression, two used machine\-learning approaches and one used only time\-to\-event modelling\. The angle of progression and head–perineum distance were the most frequent sonographic predictors\. Study authors reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0\.75–0\.99; within\-study comparisons sometimes showed higher discrimination after ultrasound parameters were added, but comparator definitions and modelling methods varied\. All studies had a high risk of bias, none reported external validation and none evaluated implementation outcomes\. Included studies reported potentially useful discrimination, but this review cannot establish incremental value over clinical\-only models\. Evidence for routine IPUS use in obstetric nursing and midwifery is insufficient\. Future research should prioritise multicentre external validation, standardised measurement timing, direct comparison with clinical\-only models, and co\-designed implementation studies examining workflow, acceptability and woman\-centred outcomes\. Not applicable\.

## [Same Spectrum, Harder First\-Order Training: Phase\-Locking in Single\- versus Multi\-Qubit Re\-Uploading Circuits](../publications/0490b79b096469461b47.md)

Michael Poppel; David Bucher; Maximilian Zorn; Markus Baumann; Sebastian Wölckert; Claudia Linnhoff\-Popien; Philipp Altmann; Jonas Stein

Angle\-encoded variational quantum circuits implement truncated Fourier series\. For one\-dimensional inputs, a single\-qubit re\-uploading \(serial\) circuit represents every function that a multi\-qubit circuit with the same encoding budget $E$ can; we find that this exchange of width for depth is not free in first\-order training\. Because its state lives on the Bloch sphere, all parameters of the serial circuit move the state, at each input, along one complex direction, which we call \\emph\{phase\-locking\}\. We prove that this costs no Fourier direction but leaves no direction to spare: however many parameters it has, the serial circuit has at most $2E\+2$ tangent directions, one more than its $2E\+1$ Fourier coefficients need, while a two\-qubit control with the same encoding budget and model class generically has at least $6E\+6$\. The cost in training is measured against this control, as the number of runs out of 100 that reach the optimum within a fixed step budget\. On an exact loss with flat\-spectrum targets the gap grows with $E$; at $E=32$ the serial circuit converges in 3, 53 and 83 runs under gradient descent, Adam and Levenberg\-\-Marquardt, the control in 99, 100 and 100\. On three real\-world series, at matched parameter counts, the serial circuit reaches the least\-squares optimum in at most 9 runs under Adam and in 32 to 93 under Levenberg\-\-Marquardt, the control in at least 98 and in all 100; its held\-out error is up to about $1\.5$ times that of the control under Adam, but no larger in the typical run under Levenberg\-\-Marquardt\.

## [Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open‐Mouth Proton‐Density‐Weighted MRI](../publications/04911ca288b95eba3369.md)

Kotaro Ito; Hirotaka Muraoka; Satoshi Tokunaga; Kohei Otsuka; Tomohiro Komatsu; Yuta Kohinata; Shoya Hirohata

BACKGROUND: The temporomandibular joint \(TMJ\) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function\. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction\. OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance \(MR\) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once \(YOLO\) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction \(DDwR\) and disc displacement without reduction \(DDwoR\)\. METHODS: This study included 237 patients \(48 males, 189 females; age range, 19\-83 \[mean, 44\.73 ± 18\.3\] years\) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings\. After exclusion, 439 proton density\-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training \(280 images\), validation \(71 images\) and test \(88 images\) datasets\. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle\. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR\. RESULTS: The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements\. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0\.983, 0\.988 and 0\.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns\. CONCLUSION: The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images\.

## [Silveira, David: Conscious Electromagnetic Organization in an Eternalist Block Universe](../publications/04a3a222e65f1131259a.md)



Electromagnetic theories of consciousness propose that conscious experience may be physically realized through organized electromagnetic activity generated by nervous systems\. McFadden’s conscious electromagnetic information \(CEMI\) field theory identifies consciousness with physically integrated, causally active information instantiated in the brain’s endogenous electromagnetic field\. If this proposal is correct, consciousness\-realizing electromagnetic organization is not a separate substance or physical force\. It is a particular organization of ordinary field activity\. The component premises examined here are not themselves proposed as new\. CEMI supplies the conditional model of consciousness, ordinary relativistic physics supplies the electromagnetic energy\-momentum and matter\-field dynamics, and eternalism supplies the temporal ontology\. The paper’s contribution is a synthesis developed from their conjunction\. It distinguishes the temporal and phenomenal boundary of consciousness\-realizing organization from the wider physical causal history in which that organization participates\. Interactions occurring while a configuration is consciousness\-realizing can alter physical conditions that enter successor configurations and further causal chains after the organization required for consciousness has ended\. The argument is placed within a block\-universe framework that combines eternalism with the further treatment of the complete spacetime history as a four\-dimensional physical whole\. Within that framework, locally emergent consciousness\-realizing regions, their physical predecessors, and later configurations partly shaped through their activity occupy different regions of one complete history\. Temporal emergence therefore does not exclude constitutive physical membership\. The distinctive point is not that physical processes leave consequences, but that a bounded phenomenal organization can occur within a physical causal history whose consequences extend beyond that phenomenal boundary without extending the consciousness itself\. This does not establish that consciousness created, sustains, grounds, or retrocausally influences the universe\. It raises a further conditional question\. Membership in the complete block does not by itself imply explanatory importance, but if the block ultimately depends upon deeper relations among its physical contents, consciousness\-realizing regions and physical histories partly shaped through them cannot be excluded merely because consciousness emerges late in chronology\. Whether those histories actually possess any deeper constitutive role remains open\. CEMI supplies the specific electromagnetic case, while the relation among phenomenal boundaries, physical causal descent, temporal emergence, and global constitution is broader than that model\. Keywords: consciousness; electromagnetic field; CEMI theory; eternalism; block universe; stress\-energy; physicalism; energy\-momentum; spacetime; global constitution\.

## [Brain\-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies](../publications/04a45d20e9ed587676b6.md)

Renana Oz Rokach; Odeya Marmor; Yoav Levy; Ariel Gilad

It is long thought that higher\-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location \(i\.e\., ‘what’ and ‘where’ streams\)\. Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain\-wide \(beyond cortex\) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters\. We combine simultaneous brain\-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus\. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance\. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain\-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively\. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history\. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location\. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration\. Neural mechanisms underlying optimal sensory integration are not fully understood\. Here authors show that there exist two subnetworks spanning across many cortical and subcortical areas when the mouse performs whisker\-dependent ‘what’ and ‘where’ tasks\. Furthermore, the recruitment of either frontal or posterior subnetwork is determined by the internal behavioral strategy of the mouse\.

## [A hybrid deep compression model for enhanced classification of high\-dimensional image data](../publications/04ad67ec4d6fc5ffa664.md)

T\. Srinivasarao; Yanda Nagamani; Saraswatula Venkata Suryanarayana; Venubabu Rachapudi; Raju Anitha; Ravi Teja Gedela

Abstract High\-dimensional image data often contain redundant pixel\-level information, leading to increased computational complexity and reduced learning efficiency in machine learning models\. To address this challenge, we propose a Hybrid Compressive Feature Reduction Model \(HCFRM\) that achieves an effective trade\-off between computational efficiency and classification accuracy on challenging large\-scale datasets such as CIFAR\-10, using CSV\-shaped image representations\. The proposed HCFRM framework employs an optimized configuration consisting of 100 PCA components, a 64\-dimensional Autoencoder latent space, and the top 32 Mutual Information\-selected features to achieve an effective balance between dimensionality reduction and classification performance\. This optimized HCFRM configuration was adopted throughout all experiments to ensure consistent and reproducible evaluation across the benchmark datasets\. This adaptive tuning ensures robust performance on flattened high\-dimensional representations, demonstrated on CIFAR\-10, medical imaging, and hyperspectral datasets, highlighting the model’s flexibility and applicability to various image domains\. The decision\-making process is guided by the analysis of the expected values of feature vectors projected into a reduced coordinate space through a hybrid sensor processing pipeline\. Experimental results demonstrate that HCFRM achieves a 74% reduction in feature dimensionality while providing approximately 28–38% faster training compared with PCA\+Autoencoder and Autoencoder\-only baselines\. Despite aggressive parameter\-space compaction, the proposed model attains a classification accuracy of 74%, indicating effective class separability under reduced computational cost\. These findings confirm that HCFRM is an efficient and scalable solution for learning large\-scale, high\-dimensional image data, making it well suited for memory\-efficient and high\-performance visual learning systems\. The proposed framework further enables efficient processing of high\-dimensional visual representations for 3D scene reconstruction and volumetric modeling, supporting enhanced computer vision performance\. The modular and compressive design of HCFRM makes it suitable for scalable and cluster\-based visual learning systems\.

## [True Digital Poiesis: A Conceptual Framework and Interface Design for Generative AI in the Humanities](../publications/04b9be64c13cd095d875.md)

Will Hasty; Mark Law; Daniel Maxwell; Lauren Dulick; Ying Xiao; Markus Pope; Idalis Villanueva; Stephan Kory

This article introduces True Digital Poiesis \(TDP\), a conceptual pedagogical framework and proposed interface design for engaging generative AI in the Humanities\. Drawing on experiential learning theory and grounded in the humanistic preoccupation with alterity — the otherness of history — TDP proposes the use of AI to simulate premodern events while foregrounding the active interpretive effort involved in constructing the past\. The framework envisions the design of a digital prompt\-builder, the Event Cruncher Stylus \(ECS\), and a structured critical review process, both of which are designed to support student engagement with the complexities of historical construction\. In presenting the theoretical foundation, practical applications, and interface design of TDP, this article argues that precise and responsible use of AI in historical simulation — ranging from non\-immersive to fully immersive simulative modes — requires a systematic, embodied method for engaging the alterity of the past\. As a conceptual proposal grounded in hermeneutic theory and experiential learning research, TDP is presented here as a framework whose empirical evaluation through classroom implementation and outcome assessment is a primary objective of ongoing and future research\.

## [German Relative Clauses \(Relativsatz\) and Their Indonesian Equivalents in NADI Magazine: A Contrastive Syntactic Analysis](../publications/04ca6f1306ab20cc5cde.md)

Pratomo Widodo; Wening Rahayu; Sulis Triyono; Tyas Gita Atibrata

Relative clauses constitute an important grammatical device for establishing cohesion and reference in discourse\. However, German and Indonesian differ significantly in the way relative meanings are encoded because German is an inflectional language with a rich system of relative pronouns and adverbs, whereas Indonesian relies primarily on the relative marker ‘yang’ and other lexical strategies\. This study aims to describe the differences in the syntactic structures of German and Indonesian; the word order in German and Indonesian sentences; and the functions and meanings of Relativsatz in both languages\. The research method employed is descriptive qualitative\. This study adopts a document or text study approach, which emphasizes contrastive analysis and the interpretation of written materials based on their context\. The data consist of German texts and their Indonesian translations published in NADI magazine \(2020–2022\)\. The data collection technique used in this study is the observation and note\-taking method, which was carried out by carefully reading all data sources\. The findings indicate that Relativsatz in German and Indonesian sentences share both similarities and differences in their functions and meanings\. These differences are primarily due to the distinctive use of exophoric references in German Relativsatz, whereas Indonesian tends to employ endophoric references\. Additionally, the findings reveal that German Relativsatz are predominantly realized through the relative pronouns der, die, and das, while Indonesian commonly uses yang, appositive constructions, coordination, and discourse\-based strategies\. Overall, the study shows that German grammatical relativization is frequently transformed into lexical or discourse\-based constructions in Indonesian while preserving meaning, highlighting the importance of typological awareness in translation and foreign\-language pedagogy\.
