## [Paggamit ng Canvas LMS sa paglinang ng pagsulat ng posisyong papel sa Filipino 12](../publications/04ce67cc9b8e8ec5d440.md)

Mary Cris L Talledo

Nilayon ng pag\-aaral na ito na masuri ang kabisaan ng paggamit ng Canvas Learning Management System \(LMS\) bilang interbensiyon sa paglinang ng kasanayan sa pagsulat ng posisyong papel sa asignaturang Filipino sa Piling Larang \(Akademik\) ng mga mag\-aaral sa Grade 12\. Sinuri rin nito ang pauna at panghuling pagganap ng mga mag\-aaral batay sa linaw ng posisyon, mahahalagang punto, at tono, gayundin ang epekto ng paggamit ng Canvas Learning Management System sa kanilang interes at retensiyon sa pagkatuto\.Gumamit ang pag\-aaral ng pre\-test\-post\-test experimental design\.Ang mga kalahok ay binubuo ng animnapung \(60\) mag\-aaral ng Grade 12 mula sa University of Cebu\-Lapu\-Lapu and Mandaue Senior High School sa taong panuruan 2025\-2026\.Gumamit ng rubric\-based performance test at talatanungan sa interes at retensiyon bilang mga instrumento\.Natuklasan na ang paunang pagganap ng mga mag\-aaral sa pagsulat ng posisyong papel ay nasa katamtamang antas, samantalang ang panghuling pagganap matapos gamitin ang Canvas LMS ay umabot sa mahusay hanggang napakahusay\.Lumabas din na may makabuluhang pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng pauna at panghuling pagganap\.Nagtamo rin ang mga mag\-aaral ng mataas na antas ng interes at retensiyon, na nagpapakita ng positibong epekto ng paggamit ng Canvas LMS sa kanilang pagkatuto\.Napagpasyahan na ang paggamit ng nito ay isang mabisang estratehiya sa pagpapahusay ng kasanayan sa pagsulat ng posisyong papel at sa pagpapaunlad ng interes at retensiyon ng mga mag\-aaral\.Batay sa mga natuklasan, inirerekomenda ang paggamit ng nabuong Lesson Exemplar bilang awtput ng pag\-aaral upang magsilbing gabay ng mga guro sa pagtuturo ng pagsulat ng posisyong papel sa Filipino 12 gamit ang Canvas Learning Management System\.

## [Affective symptoms in focal epilepsy: A scoping review of localization and lateralizing findings](../publications/04d9bfc9bdf592074c27.md)

Sofía S\. Sánchez; A\. Lagunas; Emily K\. Acton; S\. Guevara‐Lazo; Enrique J\. Carrazana; Brin E\. Freund; Fábio Augusto Nascimento; Sándor Beniczky; William O\. Tatum

Emotional experiences during focal seizures are often misinterpreted as psychiatric disorders\. We aimed to evaluate symptoms involving affective symptoms at seizure onset\. We aimed to identify the most prevalent affective symptoms at seizure onset and characterize their localizing and lateralizing value\. We performed a scoping review based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta\-Analyses\-extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines\. A systematic search identified records from 4 databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL \(via EBSCOhost\), and Web of Science\. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts; discrepancies were resolved by consensus\. This review focused on patients with focal seizures, as affective symptoms may occur in generalized epilepsies\. The affective symptoms: fear, anxiety, panic, sadness, mystic, ecstatic, sexual, and mirth were identified, and semiology was evaluated in accordance with ILAE guidelines\. Symptom onset, frequency, brain localization, and video\-EEG monitoring technique were evaluated to assess localization and lateralization of regional networks\. Scalp EEG, invasive EEG recordings, and electrical stimulation were analyzed\. A total of 1276 documents were identified, with 98 studies included for review\. Fear was the most frequently reported ictal emotion, identified in 274 patients \(66%\), predominantly in temporal lobe epilepsy\. Sadness and sexual, ecstatic symptoms were also consistently associated with temporal networks\. Mirth was more frequently reported with frontal onset seizures\. Evidence, primarily from Class IV studies, reported right hemispheric predominance for ecstasy, mystic, and sexual symptoms at seizure onset\. Ictal affective symptoms at seizure onset yield localizing information\. The limbic system, especially the temporal lobe, followed by the frontal lobe, was the most common site of origin\. Fear was the most common spontaneous and electrically elicited symptom, followed by anxiety\. While bi\-hemispheric lateralization occurred, right lateralization predominated\. Recognizing paroxysmal affective symptoms as ictal phenomena may reduce misdiagnosis and aid presurgical evaluation in drug\-resistant focal epilepsy\.

## [Generiranje distorzijsko popravljenih BOLD fMRI slik brez prisotnosti slik magnetnega polja](../publications/04d9d39d8a36af8b88d3.md)

Ivan Nikolov

Susceptibility\-induced distortions degrade EPI image quality and can misalign functional images with anatomical scans\. Correcting these distortions is therefore important for reliable downstream analysis\. Classical correction methods require additional acquisitions, such as field maps or reversed phase\-encoding images, which are often unavailable in legacy datasets or time\-constrained clinical settings\. This thesis investigates whether deep learning can correct susceptibility\-induced distortions from a single distorted image and a T1\-weighted anatomical scan\. We compare several neural network architectures using data from three Human Connectome Project cohorts\. We then evaluate the selected MedNeXt v1 Medium model in a complete 4D fMRI pipeline\. The proposed approach achieves the best RMSE, SSIM, and NMI across all cohorts\. It outperforms the uncorrected baseline, SynBOLD\-DisCo, and a topup\-refined variant of itself\. It performs well across all evaluated phase\-encoding directions\. Inference requires only a single feed\-forward pass and can run on a standard CPU without a dedicated GPU\.

## [How Murky Before a VLM Knows It Cannot See? Accuracy, Confidence and Abstention on a Physical Visibility Axis](../publications/04e31cf8db48ba022a99.md)

Mochamad Rizal Fauzan; Irgi Surya

Robustness studies of vision\-language models \(VLMs\) grade degradation on nominal severity scales \(&quot;level 1\-5&quot;\) that carry no physical units, and they rarely ask whether a model&\#x27;s confidence follows the loss of visibility\. We measure accuracy, internal \(token\-probability\) confidence, verbalized confidence and an explicit abstain option on a visibility axis in metres: fog follows the Koschmieder model, an underwater arm scales the absorption spectrum of pure water, both are applied with a monocular metric depth map, and the visibility range V is swept over eight log\-spaced levels from 250 m to 1\.95 m\. On 1000 COCO scenes and five small open VLMs \(2\-5 B parameters\), accuracy on a boxed\-object identification task falls from near its clean value to chance within a narrow band \(half\-way visibility V\_acc of 12\.1\-15\.9 m in fog and 20\.5\-38\.6 m under water\) while, for the four models that are confident on clean images, the confidence stays high: at V=1\.95 m in fog their accuracy is at chance but their mean internal confidence is 0\.68\-0\.84 and their verbalized confidence 0\.61\-1\.00, a blind\-spot width W=log10\(V\_acc/V\_aware\) of at least 0\.79 decades, i\.e\. a factor of 6\.2 in visibility\. The remaining model is under\-confident throughout and its internal confidence follows accuracy\. An explicit abstain option follows accuracy when it names the reason \(W from \-0\.21 to \-0\.06 in fog\) but, for one model, lags with a generic &quot;I don&\#x27;t know&quot; \(W up to 0\.18\)\. ImageNet\-C fog severities 1\-5 correspond to only 55\-110 m of physical visibility, outside the failure band, and leave the accuracy of the models within 5 percentage points of its clean value\. Blank\-image and shuffled\-image controls, a prior\-matched answer set and a 200\-image pilot that preceded the study are reported\. Findings are descriptive: one draw of 1000 images, depth of assumed scale, and models of 2\-5 B parameters\.

## [Deep protected habitats in the Gulf of Cádiz reveal an overlooked Iberian distribution of Pagurus chevreuxi \(Bouvier, 1896\) \(Decapoda, Paguridae\)](../publications/04ec3e465fec1cedfd68.md)

Isabel Muñoz; Sara Roman; Carlos Caro; Jose Antonio Cuesta; Luis Miguel Fernández\-Salas; Carlos Farias; Miriam Sayago; Raúl Jiménez\-Romero; Juan Gil; Yolanda Vila; Marina Delgado

We report Pagurus chevreuxi \(Bouvier, 1896\) for the first time from Spanish waters of the Gulf of Cádiz, filling a gap in this species’ documented distribution along the Iberian Atlantic margin\. The specimen was collected at 418 m depth on Gazul mud volcano during the CIRCASUR2025 survey and identified using diagnostic morphological characters and mitochondrial 16S rRNA sequence data\. This find represents the deepest confirmed record of the species, which was previously regarded as predominantly inhabiting shallow water\. The new record also provides new evidence that the geographic and bathymetric distribution of P\. chevreuxi may be broader and more continuous than currently documented across its known range\.

## [IntelliLayer: A Deep Learning Architecture for Dynamic Decision Intelligence](../publications/04ed4e21c521b9c95700.md)

Gundeti Mounika; Vimula Shwetha; Dr K Sridhar

Organizations increasingly use data\-driven systems to support operational decision\-making in dynamic environments\. However, many existing deep learning models focus primarily on predicting outcomes rather than recommending reliable actions\. These models often provide limited information about prediction confidence, may experience performance degradation when data patterns change, and offer insufficient explanations for their decisions\. Previous studies have addressed these challenges independently through improved prediction models, uncertainty estimation, calibration techniques, data drift detection, and explainable AI methods\. To address these limitations, this paper introduces IntelliLayer, a five\-layer deep learning architecture that combines these capabilities within a unified decision\-making framework\. The proposed architecture integrates static data and sequential events using Transformer encoders and a learnable gated fusion mechanism\. It estimates calibrated outcome distributions through a deep ensemble and selects actions based on expected utility, while uncertain cases are referred to human reviewers\. To handle changing data patterns, the framework employs adaptive windowing for drift detection and updates the model using replay techniques and elastic weight consolidation\. Additionally, integrated gradients are used to explain individual predictions, and an audit record is maintained for every decision to support transparency and accountability\. The paper describes the architecture of each layer, outlines the online decision\-making algorithm, and presents a reference implementation stack\. It also defines a reproducible evaluation framework covering predictive performance, calibration, decision\-making costs, selective prediction coverage, recovery from data drift, and processing latency\. Since experimental results have not yet been obtained, the proposed evaluation protocol and results template provide a structured basis for future validation of the IntelliLayer architecture\.

## [From digestion to inflammatory signaling: the Postprandial Bioactive Exposure Axis as a compartment\-based conceptual model for mechanistic nutrition research](../publications/04f118c58c41705c8bfd.md)

Abdulmannan Fadel; Yazan Ranneh

Mechanistic nutrition research often moves from what a meal contains to what it is claimed to do without clearly defining the exposure steps between ingestion and biological response\. This becomes problematic when studies use causal or quasi\-causal language about inflammation, barrier function or systemic effects\. Digestion, intestinal interaction, epithelial uptake, enterocyte metabolism, microbial conversion, portal or lymphatic transport and post\-absorptive handling can each alter the chemical form, concentration, timing and site of action of food\-derived molecules\. This article proposes the Postprandial Bioactive Exposure Axis, or PBEA, as a compartment\-based model for organizing these steps in mechanistic nutrition research\. The model separates four operational fractions: bioaccessible, intestinally bioactive, absorbed and systemically relevant\. These fractions are levels of exposure inference, not discrete biological compartments\. The aim is to help authors match claims to the compartment actually measured\. The PBEA adds value by separating luminal availability from local intestinal action, and absorption from systemic relevance\. It also helps prevent common overinterpretations, including equating intake with exposure, micellarisation with bioavailability, plasma detection with physiological relevance and indirect blood markers with direct evidence of altered barrier function\. The model is intended as a practical tool for study design, model selection, temporal interpretation and more cautious mechanistic claims\.

## [Environmental factors and polygenic risk score for psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders in children with dyslexia](../publications/04f1d09de548a7469ae8.md)

Haoxue Wang; Hong Fan; Rundong Liu; Kaiheng Zhu; Zhen Xiang; Shuai Zhao; Qianhui Chen; Jiao Zhang; Tianchun Wang; 梁希 Liang Xi; Ranran Song

Developmental dyslexia \(DD\) impacts learning achievement and psychosocial development and is associated with various environmental factors and also genetic factors\. Here, we conducted a multi\-center case\-control study by screening 29,820 primary school students between 2–6 grades in four cities in China and enrolled 948 dyslexia cases who meet the criteria of dyslexia and 948 controls with matching age and sex\. We comprehensively investigated the environmental factors using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) machine learning model and Shapley additive explanations \(SHAP\) algorithm\. The most important risk factors in dyslexia are the proactive learning habit, the age of child’s literacy, maternal education level, out\-migrant workers, and prolonged screen exposure during pregnancy\. The home literacy environment accounted for most of the variance within both groups\. Then we examined shared polygenic risks between DD, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorders, schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and bipolar disorder using polygenic risk score \(PRS\) analyses\. The results showed that the highest PRS DD quartile had a 2\.13\-fold risk than the lowest quartile with risk factors adjusted \(95% CI: 1\.08, 4\.18\)\. The individuals with the highest PRS ASD quartile and PRS SCZ quartile \(OR: 2\.13; 95% CI: 1\.14, 3\.98 and OR: 2\.41; 95% CI: 1\.23, 4\.72\) were associated with increasing dyslexia risks\. This study identified the importance of screening personalized environmental factors among dyslexia and highlighted the shared genetic architecture between dyslexia and other disorders\. These findings offered novel insight into the etiology of dyslexia, contributing to the advancement of early prevention strategies\.

## [Toxic concentrations of glutamate induce ferroptosis without affecting mitochondrial respiration in rodent brain slice cultures](../publications/04f5d1ada1f5e9b1d162.md)

Annette Vaglio\-Garro; Marco Theuermann; Katharina E\. Sweis; Sergejs Zavadskis; Márton Kokas; Zsuzsanna Környei; Miriam Karas; László Tretter; Tímea Komlódi; Adelheid Weidinger; Andrey V\. Kozlov

Many neuronal disorders are characterized by glutamate toxicity, which is closely associated with mitochondrial and neuronal dysfunction\. The aim of this study was to investigate the link between mitochondrial function and mechanisms of cell death induced by glutamate\. The study was carried out on male \(C57BL/6\), male Sprague Dawley acute brain slice \(ABSs\), male and female organotypic brain slice \(BSCs\)\. Mitochondrial respiration, activities of tricarboxylic acid \(TCA\) cycle enzymes, and the cell death rate \(assessed by lactate dehydrogenase \(LDH\) release and histological analyses\) were determined\. Memantine was used to inhibit excitotoxicity, while Ferrostatin\-1, rosiglitazone and deferoxamine were used as inhibitors of ferroptotic pathway\. In astrocytes, pyruvate dehydrogenase complex \(PDHC\) and oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex \(OGDHC\), showed less than 1% of the enzymatic activity observed in whole brain tissue\. In BSCs, glutamate exposure induced a marked increase in oxidative phosphorylation\-linked mitochondrial respiration, which was independent of OGDHC activity and disappeared when BSC homogenates were analysed\. Glutamate\-induced cell death was not alleviated by memantine but was significantly reduced by ferrostatin\-1\. The activation of ferroptosis by glutamate was also observed in ABSs, as well as the inhibition of lipid peroxidation induced by ferrostatin\-1, rosiglitazone and deferoxamine\. Ferrostatin\-1, and rosiglitazone additionally inhibited cell death, while deferoxamine did not\. The unusual response to deferoxamine requires further elucidation\. In summary, our data suggest that elevated glutamate levels enhance neuronal energy metabolism in brain slices, compensating glutamate\-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and reduce excitotoxicity\. In contrast, persistently elevated levels of extracellular glutamate impair the cystine/glutamate antiporter, leading to ferroptosis\. Significance Statement Excessive extracellular glutamate is a hallmark of many neurodegenerative and ischemic conditions\. This study reveals that toxic glutamate concentrations in BSCs, modelling brain tissue, intensify neuronal energy metabolism without rescuing cells from death, shifting the predominant mechanism from excitotoxicity to ferroptosis\. Such phenomenon was not observed in studies on neuronal cell cultures, also including our previous studies\. These results suggest that targeting ferroptosis may offer therapeutic potential in neuronal disorders traditionally attributed to excitotoxic damage\.

## [Bibliometric Analysis of Studies Published in the Ankara University Faculty of Educational Sciences Journal of Special Education](../publications/050d25d07565ec2a079e.md)

Ufuk Özkubat; Onur Erdoğan; Fatih Koçak; Furkan Akdağ; Mehmet Emin Kalaylı; Mehmet İnce

Introduction: The number and diversity of academic studies in the field of special education are steadily increasing\. Understanding the developmental trajectory of the field requires examining the publication structure of scientific journals, their citation relationships, and the collaboration networks among researchers\. Bibliometric analyses make it possible to evaluate these processes systematically and thereby offer a holistic view of the scientific development of the field\. The aim of this study is to examine the bibliometric characteristics of the studies published in the Ankara University Faculty of Educational Sciences Journal of Special Education between 2006 and 2025 in terms of publication performance, citation structure, co\-authorship networks, and thematic orientations\.Method: The bibliometric analysis method was used in this study\. A total of 406 publications indexed in the Web of Science database and published from 2006, when the journal was included in the Web of Science Emerging Sources Citation Index \(ESCI\), through the end of 2025 were analyzed\. The data selection and reporting process was carried out in line with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and the reliability of the data extraction and coding stages was ensured through the evaluations of two independent researchers\. Performance analysis and science mapping techniques were applied together in the analysis process\. Within the scope of performance analysis, publication counts and citation indicators were evaluated\. In the science mapping process, citation analysis, co\-authorship analysis, and keyword analysis were conducted\.Findings: The findings reveal a marked upward trend in the journal&\#x27;s publication output, particularly after 2016\. Citation analyses show that the influential studies are concentrated on the themes of early literacy, parent education, autism spectrum disorder, and inclusion practices\. An examination of the collaboration networks among authors and institutions indicates that certain researchers and universities play central roles in knowledge production\. Keyword analyses reveal that autism, intellectual disability, and inclusion are the most prominent research areas\.Discussion: The upward trend in the journal&\#x27;s publication output indicates that academic interest and research activity in the field of special education are strengthening\. An examination of the thematic distribution shows that autism, intellectual disability, and inclusion practices are among the most prominent research topics in the literature\. In addition, the presence of topics such as early literacy and parent education among the cited studies underscores the importance of these themes for both practice and research\. The concentration of author and institutional collaboration networks around certain researchers and universities indicates that knowledge production within the field is shaped by particular academic centers\. In this respect, by revealing the journal&\#x27;s thematic orientations and academic collaboration structure in the field of special education, the study contributes to an understanding of the field&\#x27;s developmental dynamics\.

## [The Impact of Cybersecurity Risks on Electronic Auditing Quality at Jordanian Banks](../publications/050f25c192204df3e687.md)

رشا الغزي

هدف هذا البحث الى بيان أثر مخاطر الأمن السيبراني بأبعاده \(مخاطر أمن المعلومات، المخاطر التكنولوجية والتشغيلية، مخاطر الأداء\) في جودة التدقيق الالكتروني في البنوك الأردنية، تم استخدام المنهج الوصفي التحليلي من خلال توظيف الاستبانة واستخدام عدد من الأساليب الإحصائية كالمتوسط الحسابي والانحراف المعياري ومعامل الانحدار المتعدد، وبرنامج spss لتحليل البيانات واختبار الفرضيات، تمثلت العينة في العاملين في الدوائر \(المالية والتدقيق الداخلي وتكنولوجيا المعلومات\) في البنوك الأردنية، مع تضمين المدققين الداخليين والمحاسبين والتقنيين في هذه الأقسام، ولهذا فقد قام الباحثان بتوزيع \(180\) إستبانة إلكترونياً وتم استرجاع \(167\) استبانة، جميعها صالحة للتحليل\. أظهرت نتائج الدراسة وجود اثر إيجابي ذو دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى معنوية \(0\.05 ≥a\) لمخاطر الأمن السيبراني بأبعاده في جودة التدقيق الالكتروني، وأوصت الدراسة بالاستمرار على العمل في تمتين الضوابط الأمنية السيبرانية اللازمة للحد من تأثير المخاطر على جودة التدقيق الإلكتروني وضرورة التطوير المستمر ببرامج تدريب الموظفين حول مخاطر أمن المعلومات\. الكلمات المفتاحية: مخاطر الأمن السيبراني، جودة التدقيق الالكتروني، البنوك الاردن

## [Early Manifold Shaping: A Relational Account of Infant Pre Conceptual Experience](../publications/050f6bbc6452e3e1e39b.md)

Denis Bailey

Early Manifold Shaping presents a relational account of infant pre‑conceptual experience, reframing early development as a process of directional and tonal structuring rather than cognition or object perception\. Before infants can recognize caregivers, perceive objects, or form expectations, they inhabit a continuous multimodal manifold composed of skin, visual, auditory, proprioceptive, vestibular, visceral, and endocrine signals\. Repeated directional shifts within this manifold generate patterned contours that are felt rather than recognized\. These contours carry warm \(settling\) and cool \(alerting\) tonalities that precede emotion and valence\. Through repetition, tonalities stabilize into strekions—recurring relational shapes that orient the infant without memory or representation\. As strekions cluster, the infant encounters proto‑objects, not as entities but as persistent relational contours that “return” within experience\. Orientation emerges as the infant leans toward familiar warm contours and away from familiar cool ones, establishing the earliest sense of “where” before space, objecthood, or self\. This relational model dissolves the assumption that infants begin with cognition and instead shows how meaning, valence, and proto‑objecthood arise from directional structure\. The framework provides a generative foundation for later perception, attachment, and agency, and offers a developmental instantiation of Relational Structuralism \(RS\)\.

## [Feedback mit Haken: Was Schüler:innen aus dem KI\-Netz fischen](../publications/0511985a54914951e6b8.md)

Lena Bukmakowski; Carolyn Blume

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) promises to make it possible to get immediate and personalized formative feedback and correction for grammar and structure in written texts\. In this contribution, an exploratory case study examines to what extent the coordination between the technology and the learners fosters a strategic development of the writing process\. After first describing the principles of feedback delivered by generative AI, the ways in which learners utilize an illustrative AI\-based tool to revise foreign language texts will be analyzed\. It becomes clear that the writers intermittently use the feedback to apply metacognitive strategies\. At the same time, opaque and vague feedback leads to a rejection of some suggestions\. Finally, these findings will be examined in the context of their implications for supporting process\-oriented writing in foreign language instruction\.

## [Sağlıkta Yapay Zekâ Kullanımı](../publications/0513852380e237c831d5.md)



Sağlıkta Yapay Zekâ Kullanımı isimli kitap, yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin sağlık alanındaki uygulamalarını farklı disiplinlerin bakış açısıyla ele alan kapsamlı bir eserdir\. Dijital dönüşümün hız kazandığı günümüzde yapay zekâ; tanı ve tedavi süreçlerinden hasta bakımına, klinik karar desteğinden sağlık hizmetlerinin yönetimine kadar pek çok alanda önemli bir yer edinmektedir\. Bu kitap, söz konusu gelişmeleri bilimsel bir çerçevede değerlendirmek amacıyla hazırlanmıştır\. Eserde, yapay zekânın sağlık alanındaki kullanımına ilişkin farklı konuları ele alan bölümler yer almaktadır\. Her bölüm, alanında deneyimli akademisyenler tarafından güncel literatür ışığında kaleme alınmış olup teknolojinin sunduğu olanakları, uygulama örneklerini ve karşılaşılan güçlükleri dengeli biçimde ortaya koymaktadır\. Kitapta ayrıca yapay zekâ kullanımının etik, hukuki ve mesleki boyutlarına dikkat çekilmesi hedeflenmektedir\. Kitap, sağlık alanında eğitim gören lisans ve lisansüstü öğrenciler, bu alanda çalışan akademisyenler, araştırmacılar ve sahada görev yapan sağlık profesyonelleri için değerli bir başvuru kaynağı niteliği taşımaktadır\. Sağlıkta Yapay Zekâ Kullanımı, sağlık profesyonellerinin yapay zekâ okuryazarlığının gelişmesine katkı sunmayı, yeni araştırmalara temel oluşturmayı ve teknolojinin sağlık hizmetlerine güvenli ve etkin biçimde entegre edilmesine ışık tutmayı amaçlamaktadır\.

## [Data\-Driven Governance and Digital Learning Systems as Catalysts for Safeguarding Democracy in Africa](../publications/0519309f91437a074712.md)

Philip Okposo

Africa’s democratic systems are increasingly influenced by digital technologies, data infrastructures, social media, and artificial intelligence\. These developments provide opportunities to improve electoral administration, evidence\-based governance, civic education, and citizen engagement, while also creating risks related to misinformation, exclusion, surveillance, and declining public trust\. This study examines how data analytics and Learning Management Systems \(LMS\) can work together to support electoral integrity and responsible citizenship without replacing established democratic institutions\. The study adopts a documentary secondary\-data research design, drawing on peer\-reviewed studies and authoritative institutional evidence\. Selected democratic, digital access, and electoral participation indicators are examined descriptively to identify key democratic pressures and their relationship to potential technological interventions\. The findings indicate a significant gap between democratic aspirations and citizens’ experiences\. Across 39 African countries, 66% of citizens express a preference for democracy, while 45% describe their countries as mostly or completely democratic and 37% report satisfaction with how democracy works\. Although 75% support fair, open, and honest elections, only 39% report trust in their national electoral commission\. Internet use in Africa reached 38% in 2024, highlighting both the potential reach and limitations of digital interventions\. Electoral participation also varies considerably across selected countries\. These findings do not establish a causal relationship between digital learning and electoral participation but demonstrate the importance of context\-sensitive approaches\. The study therefore proposes the Data\-Driven Democratic Resilience Framework \(DDDRF\), comprising data acquisition, analytics and assurance, LMS\-enabled civic learning, citizen feedback, and safeguards relating to privacy, transparency, accessibility, human oversight, and redress\. The study contributes an information\-systems perspective to research on African democracy by integrating data governance and civic learning within a common framework for strengthening democratic resilience\.

## [Embedded Morgan Fingerprints for More Efficient Molecular Property Predictions With Machine Learning](../publications/051bb6e83ef5c3de10ce.md)

Emilio Nuñez\-Andrade; Isaac Vidal; Rafael Gómez‐Bombarelli; James William Ryan; Francisco J\. Martín‐Martínez

High\-dimensional data arrays in molecular representations pose some significant challenges for Machine Learning applications, including overfitting and computational inefficiency during training\. This is particularly relevant for Morgan Fingerprint \(MFP\), widely used for tasks such as classification and property prediction, when dealing with large and complex molecular datasets\. This article introduces embedded Morgan Fingerprint \(eMFP\), a method for dimensionality reduction of MFP, while preserving the key structural information of the encoded molecule\. The implementation of eMFP offers an improved data representation that mitigates the risk of overfitting while enhancing model performance\. Our results demonstrate that eMFP outperforms standard MFP in regression models, including Random Forest \(RF\), Multi\-layer Perceptron \(MLP\), K\-Neighbors Regressor \(KNR\), Gradient Booster Regressor \(GBR\) and a Deep Neural Network \(DNN\), across three different databases \(RedDB, NFA, and QM9\), with optimal compression sizes of q = 16, q = 32 and q = 64\. These findings highlight the potential of eMFP as a faster and often superior alternative to MFP, offering more efficient hyperparameter optimization in regression models for molecular property predictions, and improved performance with large datasets where high\-dimensional categorical data is encoded\.

## [Meaning\-Full Leadership: Meaning\-Making Discourse in Christian Leadership Development Conferences in the United Kingdom and the United States of America](../publications/052129a31fe17e80cd24.md)

John D\. Coggin

This thesis explores the social construction of leadership through meaning\-making discourse at Christian leadership development conferences \(LDCs\)\. Existing research into leadership development, which is predominantly functionalist in approach, has largely overlooked the ways in which LDCs serve as meaning\-making sites and through their discourse construct concepts of leadership that affect personal identity, organisational structure, and social control\. This thesis recovers and develops Peter L\. Berger’s concept of plausibility structures as an analytical tool to describe how logics from various meaning\-making sources are utilised by speakers to construct an identity of ‘meaning\-full’ leadership at LDCs\. Using critical discourse analysis, it explores how social understandings of leadership were cultivated through the content of three LDCs hosted in 2022 by faith\-based groups\. These LDCs were held for in\-person audiences in the United Kingdom and the United States of America and broadcast around the world through streaming platforms and local screenings\. The thesis examines the ways in which transnational understandings of leadership were framed in conversation with neoliberal understandings of leadership, forged through grappling with the personal and organisational impacts of the COVID\-19 pandemic, and honed through developing strategies for church leaders to conceive of and exert power over their organisations and wider society\. It finds through this analysis that the task of leadership in the context of LDCs extends beyond the cultivation of practical skills for organisational management and constitutes an important aspect of personal identity\. It concludes that the model of ‘meaning\-full’ leadership advanced by the LDCs has simultaneously empowering and anxiety\-producing valences, with implications not only for the identity management of individual leaders but also for the lived social realities of the organisations they lead\.

## [Multivariable Look\-up Table Construction for Aerodynamic Prediction Discrepancy Model Using Nested Grid Optimization of Linear and Nonlinear Methods with Non\-smoothness Penalty](../publications/05269f2591c5bb4fc02f.md)

Suk Young Jung; Hyunjae Nam; Kyungjin Yim

A technique was developed for multivariable look\-up table construction to make aerodynamic prediction discrepancy model, which represents differences between predicted and measured aerodynamic parameter, by using a nested process of linear method such as least squares and gradient\-based nonlinear optimization for coefficients and grid points of the look\-up table, respectively\. Test data covered only part of the multi\-dimensional variable space and were distributed unevenly across the grid cells, so the optimization process had high probability of being ill\-posed problem\. To cope with this problem, non\-smoothness penalty methods were introduced to consider variance error as well as bias error, one was ridge regression technique combined with the linear method and the other was curvature\-based non\-smoothness penalty involved into the loss function for the nonlinear grid optimization\. First, a parameter study was conducted with the coefficient optimization by the linear method with a fixed and equally spaced grid to investigate effects of a weighting factor for the ridge regression and to acquire Pareto front for $$\{R\}^\{2\}$$ and smoothness of optimized solutions for the various weighting factor values\. Second, based on this parameter study results, a decision could be made about another weighting factor for the non\-smoothness penalty term in the grid optimization\. This two\-step approach for the grid and coefficient optimization of multivariable look\-up table was proved to work effectively and efficiently for the metamodel construction by appropriate trade\-off between the bias and variance errors through a demonstration using real flight test data\.

## [Research trends and hotspots in colorectal cancer screening](../publications/052c7c88348b25f5b0f6.md)

Jinkai Zhou; He Zhou; Jiayu Xu; Maohua Wang; Lei Liu; Xiaolong Tang

BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer \(CRC\), is a highly prevalent malignant tumor worldwide, and early screening is key to improving its prognosis\. Currently, CRC screening research is growing exponentially, but its core research hotspots, evolutionary trends, and interdisciplinary features are not clear\. In this study, we used bibliometric analysis to analyze the distribution of literature, research hotspots, and cutting\-edge developments in the field of CRC screening worldwide, and to provide a scientific basis for optimizing screening strategies\. METHODS: Publications on CRC screening from 2015 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection\. VOSviewer \(v1\.6\.20\), RStudio \(v4\.4\.1\), and CiteSpace \(v6\.4\.2\) were used for bibliometric and visual analyses\. The main analyses included publication trends, countries, authors, journals, references, and keywords\. RESULT: A total of 3245 publications were included in the analysis\. Global publications on CRC screening showed a steady upward trend over the past decade, with an annual growth rate of 2\.17%\. The United States contributed the highest number of publications, and the University of North Carolina ranked as the most productive institution\. GASTROENTEROLOGY and GUT were the most frequently cited journals in this field\. Lansdorp‑Vogelaar I was among the most prolific authors\. The most cited article was &quot;CRC screening for average\-risk adults: 2018 guideline update from the American Cancer Society\.&quot; Keyword analysis showed that the research hotspots in this field included colonoscopy, biomarker, adenoma detection rate, artificial intelligence, etc\. CONCLUSION: Current research in CRC screening focuses on traditional screening methods, population\-related factors, and emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence\. Stronger international collaboration and interdisciplinary studies are needed to advance the field\.

## [Prostate cancer screening with MRI: insights from the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group](../publications/0541db0fa7eed1b2fa7f.md)

Giorgio Brembilla; Emanuele Messina; Tristan Barret; Iztok Caglič; Renato Cuocolo; Maarten de Rooij; Roberto García Figueiras; Rossano Girometti; Adalgisa Guerra; Charlie Alexander Hamm; Guglielmo Manenti; Andrea Ponsiglione; Raphaële Renard Penna; Jonathan Richenberg; Evis Sala; Harriet Thoeny; Ahmet Tuncay Turgut; Joan Carles Vilanova; Sam J\. Withey; Jeries Paolo Zawaideh; Jelle O\. Barentsz; Valeria Panebianco; on behalf of the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group

Prostate\-specific antigen \(PSA\)\-based screening for prostate cancer \(PCa\) remains controversial due to uncertain long\-term benefits, overdiagnosis, and overtreatment of indolent disease\. Magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) has transformed the diagnostic pathway of PCa and is increasingly explored as a screening tool\. This special report from the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group provides an overview of current evidence and insights into the potential role of MRI in PCa screening\. MRI\-based screening strategies appear to improve detection of clinically significant PCa while reducing unnecessary biopsies and diagnoses of non\-significant disease, though long\-term outcome data, including mortality impact and interval cancer rates, remain limited\. Biparametric MRI is particularly suited for screening due to its shorter acquisition time, reduced operational complexity, and lower costs compared with multiparametric MRI\. Two main implementation approaches have emerged: MRI\-first pathways, which maximise detection but require substantial resources, and risk\-stratified strategies, in which MRI is used after initial assessment \(e\.g\. PSA\), potentially offering greater feasibility and cost\-effectiveness\. Evidence from large trials supports integrating MRI into screening pathways, particularly as a reflex test after PSA screening, although uncertainties remain regarding optimal protocols, interpretation thresholds, follow\-up strategies, and long\-term outcomes\. Key barriers include limited MRI capacity, economic considerations, and the need for standardisation and quality assurance\. Advances in artificial intelligence may further enhance efficiency\. Overall, MRI has the potential to improve the balance between benefits and harms in PCa screening, but further evidence is required to define its optimal implementation\. KEY POINTS: Question Can prostate MRI be effectively integrated into population\-based prostate cancer screening pathways? Findings MRI\-based screening improves detection of csPCa while reducing unnecessary biopsies; biparametric MRI should be the protocol of choice to enhance feasibility, although optimal implementation and long\-term outcomes remain uncertain\. Clinical relevance MRI may overcome key limitations of PSA\-based screening by enhancing the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer while reducing harms such as overdiagnosis and unnecessary biopsies\.

## [Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To](../publications/0542e703c6325efdf525.md)

Uriel Dolev; Idan Schwartz; Yoav Goldberg

Chain\-of\-thought \(CoT\) controllability, the ability of reasoning models to control properties of their CoT, is consequential for both their usefulness and reliable oversight\. Recent work evaluates this capability by measuring whether models follow CoT constraints given in the user prompt, and reports very low controllability across models\. We argue that this low controllability may not reflect an inherent inability of reasoning models to control their CoT, but instead result from naively specifying constraints in the user prompt\. To test this, we introduce Self\-Instructed CoT Controllability: a complementary evaluation that places the constraint as a self\-instruction inside the model&\#x27;s CoT and measures its ability to follow it\. We show that, under self\-instruction, models achieve significantly higher controllability than with standard user instructions\. Even a generic reminder to follow the user&\#x27;s constraint substantially improves controllability\. Moreover, effective self\-instructions can be bootstrapped into the reasoning through a simple instruction in the user prompt, enabling improved control even without access to the reasoning channel\. Finally, using self\-instruction, we demonstrate in a realistic monitoring setup that CoT controllability can be leveraged for monitor evasion, posing a risk to CoT monitorability\.

## [Inclusive electroencephalography practices for Black and Muslim participation in a White non\-Muslim\-majority country: A co\-produced tutorial](../publications/0547df51e2471642fd68.md)

Damian Cruse; Ilham Razaie; Nyamesumpa Abbey; Natasha Bradbury; Yasmin Darawil; Hana Eldessoky; Fatima Farooq; Olivia Francis; Romy Froemer; Dorinda Lokko; Esther Nwakor; Amaliah\-Saffron Odutola; Andrew Quinn; Nishita Sujan; Malaika Zabair

Most electroencephalography \(EEG\) research is conducted in White\-majority Western countries by White researchers\. EEG practices therefore often explicitly and implicitly exclude minoritised groups, leading to low diversity in EEG data samples that deepens biases in interpretation and clinical utility\. Because EEG electrodes must contact the scalp, Black people and Muslim women who wear a hijab \(or, Hijabis\) are two systematically excluded groups\. As a group of EEG researchers, Black people, and Hijabis, here we describe co\-produced practical approaches to overcoming EEG participation barriers, from recruitment to data collection, and provide co\-produced text, photographs, and videos designed to break down these barriers\. These approaches provide further tools for the EEG community to tackle systemic exclusion and foster better, more representative neuroscience\.

## [Hälterlein, Jens: Imagining and governing artificial intelligence: the ordoliberal way—an analysis of the national strategy ‘AI made in Germany’](../publications/054abbbc68e60808059e.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 40 \(3\):1749\-1760\. 2025National Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) strategies articulate imaginaries of the integration of AI into society and envision the governing of AI research, development and applications accordingly\. To integrate these central aspects of national AI strategies under one coherent perspective, this paper presented an analysis of Germany’s strategy ‘AI made in Germany’ through the conceptual lens of ordoliberal political rationality\. The first part of the paper analyses how the guiding vision of a human\-centric AI not only adheres to ethical and legal principles consistent with Germany’s liberal democratic constitutional system but also addresses the risks and promises inherent to the ordoliberal problematization of freedom\. Second, it is scrutinized how the strategy cultivates the fear of not achieving technological sovereignty in the AI sector\. Thereby, it frames the global AI race as a race of competing \(national\) approaches to governing AI and articulates an ordoliberal approach to governing AI \(the ‘third way’\), according to which government has to operate between the twin dangers of governing too much and not governing enough\. Third, the paper analyses how this ordoliberal proportionality of governing structures Germany’s Science Technology &amp; Innovation Policy\. It is shown that the corresponding risk\-based approach of regulating AI constitutes a security apparatus as it produces an assessment of fears: weighting the fear of the failure to innovate with the fear of the ramifications of innovation\. Finally, two lines of critical engagement based on this analysis are conducted\. \(direct link \)

## [Development Of an Adaptive Leadership Model for Enhancing the Learning Adaptability of Students Majoring in Advertising Design at Vocational Colleges of Guangdong Province, China](../publications/054abc8ee0328a92e170.md)

Liandi He; XiaoShu Xu; Yin Yun Wei

This study aimed to \(1\) identify the core dimensions of adaptive leadership and learning adaptability among advertising design students in vocational colleges in Guangdong Province, China; \(2\) assess their current levels; \(3\) examine the predictive effect of adaptive leadership on learning adaptability; \(4\) develop an adaptive leadership model to enhance learning adaptability; and \(5\) evaluate the model’s effectiveness\. A mixed\-methods research design was employed\. Questionnaires were distributed to 290 students, of which 270 valid responses were retained for quantitative analysis\. Descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis were used to examine students’ levels and the predictive relationships between variables\. Expert consultation informed model development, and a 16\-week quasi\-experimental intervention involving 82 students was evaluated using paired\-samples t\-tests\. The findings revealed that students demonstrated moderate levels of adaptive leadership and upper\-moderate levels of learning adaptability, with Change\-Coping and Autonomous Learning Adaptability representing the weakest dimensions\. Adaptive leadership significantly and positively predicted learning adaptability, explaining 51% of its variance\. Change\-Coping was the strongest predictor, followed by Problem\-Solving, Self\-Awareness, and Interpersonal Relationships\. Based on these findings, a localized three\-stage cyclical adaptive leadership cultivation model was developed\. The quasi\-experimental evaluation involving 82 students demonstrated significant improvements across all dimensions of learning adaptability following the intervention\. This study contributes localized empirical evidence to vocational advertising design education in Guangdong Province and provides a systematic, practical framework for enhancing students’ learning adaptability and employability in the AIGC\-driven creative industry\.

## [Mitochondrial Quality Control in Degenerative Musculoskeletal Diseases: Signaling Networks and Therapeutic Landscapes](../publications/054d0a3db1a5de81c7a0.md)

Haiyang Gao; Zhangrong Cheng; Xianglong Chen; Wenbo Wu; Wu Wang; Zimu Yu; Yang Cao; Yukun Zhang

Degenerative musculoskeletal disorders, including osteoarthritis \(OA\), intervertebral disc degeneration \(IVDD\), and osteoporosis \(OP\), are increasingly viewed as disorders of mitochondrial quality control \(MQC\) rather than passive mechanical wear\. The MQC network, comprising mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy\-biogenesis coupling, and inter\-organelle communication, organizes the aging\-inflammation\-metabolism axis\. Its collapse releases mtDNA fragments that act as damage\-associated molecular patterns \(DAMPs\) activating innate immunity via cGAS\-STING, and metabolic intermediates that remodel the epigenome through histone lactylation, potentially locking acute stress into a &quot;metabolic memory&quot;, although the mtDNA\-methylation component remains hypothesis\-level\. Multi\-omics and cell\-free mtDNA liquid biopsy underpin a proposed subtyping into bioenergetic failure, immuno\-inflammatory activation, and senescent cell accumulation, still a within\-OA hypothesis pending independent and cross\-disease validation\. Therapy is shifting from symptom management toward organelle medicine, including cardiolipin stabilizers, PROTAC\-mediated protein degradation, mitochondrial base editing, and engineered mitochondrial transplantation\. Metformin has randomized trial evidence in knee OA pending confirmation, NAD\+ precursors are in early clinical testing, and SS\-31 holds accelerated approval only for Barth syndrome; other strategies remain preclinical\. Delivery barriers and disease heterogeneity require precision stratification, biomimetic models, and AI\-driven decision\-making\. This review delineates the shared molecular logic of the three diseases and proposes a prototype subtyping\-to\-treatment roadmap pending validation\.

## [From gut microbiome to aging brain: Butyrate as a neurogeroscience effector](../publications/054d65960f2fe677c4c0.md)

Laura Mitrea; Lavinia\-Florina Calinoiu; Gheorghe\-Adrian Martau; Bernadette\-Emoke Teleky; Ana\-Maria Cocean; Răzvan Odocheanu; Bianca\-Eugenia Stefanescu; Dan\-Cristian Vodnar

Aging\-related cognitive decline is increasingly linked to disruption of the microbiome\-gut\-brain axis, in which age\-associated dysbiosis progressively reduces butyrate production, a short\-chain fatty acid and central neuroactive metabolite generated by bacterial fermentation of dietary fiber\. Experimental studies indicate that butyrate can influence multiple processes relevant to brain aging, including histone deacetylase activity, neuroinflammatory signaling, microglial phenotypes, blood\-brain barrier integrity, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis\. Through these mechanisms, butyrate may modulate several molecular and cellular processes involved in brain aging, although evidence for direct causal effects in the human brain remains limited\. Preclinical studies report neuroprotective effects across several models of aging and neurological disease; however, direct evidence in humans remains limited and largely associative or indirect\. Therefore, this review critically synthesizes current evidence on microbiome\-derived butyrate in brain aging, encompassing its microbial production and age\-related alterations, molecular and cellular mechanisms, associations with neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric conditions, and emerging strategies for therapeutic modulation and delivery\. It examines emerging biotechnological strategies \- including prodrug design, nanoparticle\- and liposomal\-based delivery systems, gut\-targeted formulations, and microbiome engineering \- all developed to overcome the blood\-brain barrier and restore therapeutically relevant butyrate concentrations in the aging brain\. By bridging fundamental microbiome biology and translational neuroscience, this review positions butyrate as a mechanistically grounded neurogeroscience effector and charts a roadmap for its application in promoting brain health across the aging continuum\.

## [Machine Learning\-Based Evaluation of Tower Foundation Frost Jacking in the Marginal Permafrost of Northeast China](../publications/05560a235f3375971f21.md)

Juncen Lin; Guoyu Li; Kai Gao; Dun Chen; Yapeng Cao; Alexander N\. Fedorov

Rapid localized permafrost degradation heightens geological risk and threatens the long\-term stability of transmission towers in cold regions\. Based on systematic field investigations of 336 towers in the marginal permafrost of Northeast China, thirteen conditioning factors were incorporated to evaluate five machine learning models \(Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Logistic Regression\) for foundation frost jacking susceptibility assessment, with SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) and Geographical Detector \(GeoDetector\) used to quantify factor contributions and interactions\. Results show that differential frost jacking poses the greatest structural hazard\. Peat\-rich wetland geohydrological settings constitute the highest\-risk terrain for foundation uplift\. Random Forest achieved the highest area under the curve of 0\.987 and showed competitive performance across multiple evaluation metrics\. Ground ice content was the most influential predictor, followed by land cover, soil type, and surface water\. Ice content and land cover exhibited the strongest explanatory power \(q = 0\.78\)\. These findings provide a quantitative and interpretable basis for frost\-jacking susceptibility assessment and preliminary engineering screening within the investigated transmission corridor\.

## [When Does &quot;Post\-Call&quot; Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings\-Call NLP Benchmarks](../publications/05615d3606f5357313f1.md)

Xiaoyu Ma; Kelvin J\. L\. Koa; Yuncong Liu; Ke\-Wei Huang

Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high\-frequency return intervals\. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within\-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete\. Chronological train\-\-test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples\. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence\. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms\. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call\-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance\. At this baseline, moving from the call\-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9\.4% of calls\. Holding completion\-clock cutpoints fixed, 28\.3% change quintile\. In an independent release\-session analysis of a public earnings\-call volatility benchmark, shifting before\-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three\-day mean squared error by 18\.1\-21\.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged\. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable\. The Availability Contract makes this assumption explicit and ties post\-input claims to the available timing evidence\.

## [FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds](../publications/0565ad4e4ad0689378de.md)

Ching\-Heng Cheng; Chia\-Ming Lee; Ming\-Ching Chang; Xin Li; Yu\-Lun Liu; Chih\-Chung Hsu

Single\-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture\. It is inherently interactive: users try many focal points and blur strengths on one image, so each edit should be fast and change only the blur\. Recent generative methods, however, rerun large diffusion models for every edit\. We observe that the two sub\-problems differ in kind: recovering the all\-in\-focus image is ill\-posed and needs a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane\. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders every edit with a lightweight network\. To address the ill\-posed restoration, a one\-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality\. For precise control, the renderer is conditioned on an explicit defocus map and uses defocus\-bias attention, which lets pixels at similar defocus share information without interference from pixels at other depths; in\-focus content stays unchanged, and editing the map yields tilt\-shift and two focal planes\. To further test generalization to unseen cameras, we collect 3CReal, a three\-camera benchmark of 89 pairs\. FlashReFocus achieves the best perceptual fidelity for zero\-shot bokeh rendering on EBB\! and 3CReal, refocuses 148\.3x faster than GenRefocus, and takes about half a second per further edit, 462x faster\.

## [TRANSFORMAÇÃO DIGITAL NA GESTÃO PÚBLICA: SÍNTESE DAS INOVAÇÕES EM SERVIÇOS DIGITAIS AO CIDADÃO NOS CONCURSOS DA ENAP \(2021–2023\)](../publications/056d3fe8396a19fc89d8.md)

Jacinalva Vieira da Silva Santana; Solange Antonio Rocha; Eduardo César Dechechi; Elías García

A transformação digital consolidou\-se como eixo estratégico da administração pública brasileira, especialmente noâmbito federal, diante da demanda crescente por serviços mais eficientes, acessíveis, transparentes e centrados nocidadão\. Nessa perspectiva, este estudo analisa as iniciativas premiadas nos Concursos de Inovação no Setor Públicoda Escola Nacional de Administração Pública \(ENAP\), no período de 2021 a 2023, com foco na categoria Inovaçãoem Serviços ou Políticas Públicas no Poder Executivo Federal\. A pesquisa adota a abordagem qualitativa, denatureza aplicada e caráter descritivo, fundamentada em análise documental dos relatórios oficiais da ENAP e emrevisão bibliográfica sobre inovação pública, governo digital e transformação digital\. Os projetos inovadoresexaminados foram as iniciativas como PIX, Conecta gov\.br, Prova de Vida Digital, Recomendação de Serviços nogov\.br com uso de inteligência artificial e a plataforma SOUGOV\.BR\. Os resultados evidenciam padrõesconvergentes de inovação, destacando a integração e interoperabilidade de sistemas, o uso de tecnologiasemergentes, a simplificação de processos, a melhoria da experiência do usuário e o fortalecimento da transparência edo controle social\. Conclui\-se que a administração pública federal brasileira avança para uma transformação digitalestrutural, na qual a tecnologia atua como instrumento de inovação institucional e geração de valor público,contribuindo para uma gestão mais eficiente, responsiva e orientada ao cidadão, além de oferecer subsídiosrelevantes para a formulação de políticas públicas e futuras agendas de pesquisa\.

## [Prioritizing quality of life determinants for sustainable development goals in rural India: an integrated ISM\-fuzzy TOPSIS approach](../publications/0570e45042bc6a59247b.md)

Wen\-Kuo Chen; Venkateswarlu Nalluri; Sai Manideep Appana; Yogesh Vinayak Hadole; Madhavaiah Chendragiri

Improving Quality of Life \(QoL\) and achieving Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\) in rural regions of developing nations such as India poses notable challenges\. This study aims to identify and prioritize the key factors affecting QoL among rural communities in India, providing actionable insights for policymakers\. Using a hybrid Interpretive Structural Modelling \(ISM\) and the Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution \(Fuzzy TOPSIS\) approach, we created a model that illustrates the relationships among the QoL affecting criteria identified through literature review, while Fuzzy TOPSIS ranks them, accommodating the uncertainty and subjectivity inherent in expert assessments\. The major findings underline three critical areas for rural development: cultural preservation \(corresponds to SDG 11\), transparency and accountability \(corresponds to SDG 16\), and agricultural innovation \(corresponds to SDG 2 and 9\) for enhanced QoL in rural India\. The combined application of ISM and Fuzzy TOPSIS offers a thorough analytical approach, permitting an in\-depth examination of the intricate interconnectedness of various socio\-economic elements\. This paper adds to the conversation on sustainable development by providing a detailed understanding of what influences QoL in rural areas and suggesting practical recommendations for policymakers\. The techniques adopted are effective tools for evaluating rural development projects and aligning them with SDGs, thus fostering a more inclusive and fair growth path for India’s rural territories\. Thereby, this study fulfills its central aim of prioritizing the key challenges in enhancing QoL in rural India through SDGs\.

## [Cascaded 2\-stage 3D U\-Net for Couinaud hepatic segmentation](../publications/0592480a3c712f672f99.md)

En este trabajo se propone un enfoque basado en aprendizaje profundo para la segmentación automática del hígado y de sus ocho segmentos anatómicos según la clasificación de Couinaud utilizando un esquema de aprendizaje en cascada\. El enfoque propuesto descompone la tarea de segmentación en dos etapas secuenciales\. En primer lugar, un modelo 3D U\-Net binario identifica la región hepática dentro del volumen de CT abdominal\.
