## [ShiftQAT: Quantization\-Aware Training for the Numerical Contract of a Fixed\-Function Edge CNN Accelerator](../publications/059fe6630cd36b60ab7a.md)

Oguzhan Buyuksolak; Osman Erman Okman; Mehmet Gorkem Ulkar

Fixed\-function CNN accelerators make edge inference fast and energy\-efficient, but they execute only networks that obey a precise numerical contract\. On the MAX7800x family, this contract requires power\-of\-two, per\-tensor, symmetric scales, 8\-bit activations and biases, integer\-only arithmetic, and one statically configured shift per layer\. We present ShiftQAT, the quantization\-aware training \(QAT\) flow we developed for this family, which produces networks satisfying the contract by construction\. It is the default training path of ai8x\-training, the family&\#x27;s open\-source training toolchain\. ShiftQAT resolves residual, concatenation, and weight\-sharing dependencies so that activation scales propagate statically and each layer&\#x27;s requantization reduces to one offline\-configured shift\. It also trains weights and biases on a joint power\-of\-two grid that fits the 8\-bit bias budget\. Among the compared methods, only ShiftQAT satisfies all of the contract&\#x27;s scaling constraints, including signed 8\-bit activation storage\. Even so, on ImageNet it matches the W8A8 accuracy drop of less constrained QAT methods and stays within 2\.9 percentage points of FP32 at W4A8\. On MAX78002 silicon, ShiftQAT\-trained MobileNetV2 and ResNet\-18 classify ImageNet images in 14\.6 and 8\.4 ms at 5\.1 and 2\.8 mJ per inference\.

## [Generative adversarial networks with Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification for structural health monitoring: Fibre Bragg grating data augmentation comparison in Hawk T1A aircraft](../publications/05bbe732e0f658b30403.md)

Alvaro Peiro; Marios Impraimakis

The signal generation capabilities of a novel data augmentation framework are examined in aerospace structures\. First, the framework learns class\-conditional temporal and spectral characteristics of the measured structural responses\. It uses conditional generative adversarial network training and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification as a Bayesian approximation\. This step enables stochastic signal synthesis and uncertainty quantification\. Second, the generated responses are rigorously compared against experimental measurements across time, frequency, uncertainty, variability, and feature domains to assess physical realism, statistical consistency, and distributional fidelity\. Finally, the synthetic data are evaluated to determine whether they should be incorporated into a supervised damage classification workflow\. The framework is validated on the full\-scale benchmark dataset from a BAE Systems Hawk T1A aircraft tested at the University of Sheffield&\#x27;s Structural Dynamics Laboratory for Verification and Validation\. The test involves acceleration, fibre Bragg grating strain, and nonlinear dynamic response measurements\. The results demonstrate that the model accurately captures dominant structural dynamics, it guides on signal use for classification improvement based on uncertainty characteristics, and it provides meaningful uncertainty estimates linked to signal complexity and excitation characteristics\. Importantly, the framework offers a realistic generative modelling plan as a robust digital twin component for data\-driven structural health monitoring, supporting resilient decision\-making for condition assessment in safety\-critical aerospace systems\.

## [د\. هبه منصور توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في خدمة علم أصول الفقه](../publications/05c198158a9e711db835.md)

هبه منصور

الملخص تدور هذه الدراسة حول موضوع مهم من موضوعات علم أصول الفقه، حيث ظهرت في زماننا المعاصر تقنيات حديثة متعلقة بالذكاء الاصطناعي فكان لا بد من دراسة متخصصة تبين مدى إمكانية توظيف هذه التقنيات في تجديد علم اصول الفقه وخدمة مباحثة وأصوله، وتضع الضوابط لهذا التوظيف وتدرس المجالات المتعلقة بهذا السياق\. هدفت الدراسة إلى بيان مفهوم تجديد علم اصول الفقه والذكاء الاصطناعي وتأصيل المراد بتوظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تجديد علم أصول الفقه، ووضع ضوابط لهذا التوظيف ورسم حدود ومجالات هذا التوظيف\. اتبعت الباحثة المنهج الاستقرائي وذلك من خلال استقراء نصوص الاصوليين للوقوف على مفهوم تجديد علم أصول الفقه ومفهوم الذكاء الاصطناعي، والمنهج التأصيلي لتأصيل المراد بتوظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في تجديد علم أصول الفقه، والمنهج الاستنتاجي للوقوف على ضوابط ومجالات التوظيف\. خلصت الدراسة إلى أن المراد بتوظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في تجديد علم أصول الفقه بأنه توجيه أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي الحديثة، والعمل على إدماجها واستخدامها في خدمة وإحياء مباحث علم أصول الفقه، بما يسهم في تنظيم مادتها وتحليل النصوص الأصولية وتحسين فهم النصوص الشرعية، بما يواكب المستجدات المعاصرة في إطار الضوابط الشرعية، وبما لا يمس بقداسة النص الشرعي وثوابته ومقاصده\.

## [Unravelling the deprotonation isomers of sulfobenzoic acid produced via electrospray ionization: A combined infrared spectroscopy and quantum chemical study](../publications/05cbf12383e2f0b8132a.md)

Sarah Wilson; Caroline Dessent; TOON PONGWORASUWANNA; Giel Berden; Jos Oomens

Mass spectrometric identification of the regioisomers of Sulfobenzoic acid \(SBA\), an important chemical intermediate, is complicated by the system containing both sulfonic acid and carboxylic acid deprotonation sites\. Here, we apply infrared multiple\-photon dissociation \(IRMPD\) spectroscopy for the first time to ortho\-, meta\-, and para\-SBA deprotonated molecules, \[SBA\-H\]\-, formed via electrospray ionization, to determine the identity of the deprotonation isomers\. IRMPD spectra were acquired over the fingerprint region \(800 – 2000 cm\-1\) at the FELIX free\-electron laser, with experimental measurements being interpreted with the aid of quantum chemical calculations at the CAM\-B3LYP/6\-311\+\+G\(2d,2p\) level\. For all three regioisomers, the IRMPD spectra are consistent with deprotonation occurring only at the sulfonic acid group with characteristic sulfonate stretches observed \(\~1220 and 1060 cm\-1, for the symmetric and asymmetric stretches\)\. Importantly, we find no spectroscopic evidence for the presence of carboxylate deprotomers\. Our spectroscopic results are fully consistent with the quantum chemical predictions of the relative deprotomer energies of the \[SBA\-H\]\- anions, since the meta\- and para\-\[SBA\-H\]\-, gas\-phase sulfonate deprotomers are calculated to be substantially lower in energy than the corresponding carboxylates \(by 65\.6 and 73\.3 kJ/mol, respectively\)\. The ortho\-\[SBA\-H\]\- regioisomers optimizes to a single structure, where the sulfonate group is deprotonated and forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond with the \-OH group of the adjacent carboxylic acid\. We discuss the collision\-induced dissociation patterns of the \[SBA\-H\]\- regioisomers, and present a full interpretation of the observed fragmentation pathways consistent with the electrosprayed anions corresponding solely to sulfonate structures\.

## [Improving deep neural network prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure in hydrate\-bearing sediments through feature engineering and architecture search](../publications/05d0321225d0873c030e.md)

Thi Huynh Ho; Thuat Thanh Trinh

Abstract Accurate prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure \( $$P\_b$$ \) in natural gas hydrate\-bearing sediments provides screening\-level support for laboratory\-scale hydraulic fracturing design in NGH\-bearing sediments\. This study demonstrates that systematic feature engineering and neural architecture search yield substantial improvements for predicting $$P\_b$$ on a 114\-sample published dataset\. The framework first expands the feature space from 12 to 208 variables via polynomial transformations, interaction terms, and domain\-specific features, followed by deduplication\. Multi\-method feature selection identifies a 14\-feature subset, and extended evaluation identifies a verified 12 $$\\times $$ 32 model as the best\-performing saved configuration\. The reproducible\-by\-retraining reference is R $$^2$$ $$\\approx $$ 0\.87; the verified 12 $$\\times $$ 32 saved model achieves R $$^2$$ = 0\.92 on its original held\-out split and is reported as an upper bound on the dataset\. The best of 60 retraining runs reaches 0\.85—none reproduces 0\.92, confirming that 0\.92 is a saved\-artifact result, not a reproducible target\. The verified 12 $$\\times $$ 32 model reduces MSE from 19\.34 to 8\.22 MPa $$^2$$ and MAE from 3\.16 to 2\.14 MPa compared to the best prior reported result \(R $$^2$$ = 0\.81\)\. Feature importance and SHAP analysis show that the model assigns highest importance to stress\-composition interactions and stress\-derived statistical terms, consistent with known geomechanical controls on fracture initiation\. Generalization is modest \(CV mean R $$^2 \\approx $$ 0\.50\), and simpler models \(RandomForest, SVR\) are recommended as production\-ready baselines; the 12 $$\\times $$ 32 DNN is retained as the best verified saved artifact\. These findings confirm that the dataset contains untapped predictive capacity, and that methodological refinement through domain\-informed feature engineering combined with systematic architecture search provides an effective pathway for improving prediction fidelity in small\-sample geomechanical problems\.

## [TD\-interpreter: enhancing the understanding of timing diagrams with visual\-language learning](../publications/05dc0c419f54c89e5a5c.md)

Jie He; Vincent Theo Willem Kenbeek; Zhantao Yang; Meixun Qu; Ezio Bartocci; Dejan Ničković; Radu Grosu

Abstract We introduce TD\-Interpreter, a specialised machine learning \(ML\) workflow that assists engineers in understanding complex timing diagrams \(TDs\), originating from a third party, during their design and verification process\. The outcome of this workflow is a visual question\-answer environment which allows engineers to input a set of TDs and ask design and verification queries regarding these TDs\. To address limited training data availability, we developed a synthetic data generation pipeline that aligns visual information with its textual interpretation\. We then implemented TD\-Interpreter using a lightweight 7B Multimodal Large Language Model \(MLLM\), guided by both supervised fine\-tuning \(SFT\) and reinforcement learning \(RL\)\. We also developed extensive TD\-reasoning benchmarks from simple retrieval tasks to complex reasoning problems in the real world\. Our experimental results show that TD\-Interpreter substantially outperformed both the untuned base model, and commercial MLLMs \(GPT\-5\.2\), on the evaluated benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed workflow\.

## [Osmanlı Vakıf Sistemi İçinde Avarız Vakıfları: Üsküdar ve Galata Örnekleri](../publications/06034682311cc00a93e4.md)

Nejla Doğan

Osmanlı mahkeme kayıtları, dönemin toplumsal yapısı hakkında önemli bilgiler sunmakta olup, bu bilgiler arasında vakıflar özel bir yer tutmaktadır\. Vakıf çalışmalarında mahkeme sicillerinin taşıdığı önem dikkate alınarak, bu araştırmada temel arşiv kaynağı olarak mahkeme kayıtları tercih edilmiştir\. Çalışma, 17\. yüzyıl ile sınırlı olup, Üsküdar ve Galata mahkeme kayıtlarına yansıyan vakfiyeler üzerinden avarız vakıflarını ve işleyişlerini incelemektedir\. Bu araştırma, avarız kapsamına giren çeşitli vergileri ödemekte güçlük çekenlere yardım amacıyla kurulan vakıfların kayıtlarını ele alarak, mevcut literatüre katkıda bulunmayı amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırmada, avarız vakıflarının kuruluş amaçları, mevkufat türleri, işleyiş ve tevliyet biçimleri ile vakıf kurucularının toplumsal profilleri gibi temel karakteristik özellikler ele alınmıştır\. Bu sayede, avarız vakıflarının dönemin sosyal ve ekonomik yapısındaki önemi ortaya konulmuş ve sistemin ne kadar esnek ve döneme göre uyarlanabilir olduğu gösterilmeye çalışılmıştır\.

## [Physical activity, mental health, and healthy development in adolescents: mechanisms and implications for intervention](../publications/060470db3e0f06f4b7e8.md)

Liang Rui; Junming Zhang; Sa Li

Adolescence combines heightened neurobehavioral plasticity with a steep rise in the incidence of depressive and anxiety disorders\. Habitual physical activity, by contrast, begins to fall much earlier, from about age seven, so adolescents enter the years of peak diagnostic risk already substantially less active than they were as children\. That offset, rather than a coincidence of two curves, is the premise of this review\. Meta\-analytic syntheses report moderate improvements in depressive \(SMD = −0\.45, 95% CI −0\.59 to −0\.31\) and anxiety symptoms \(SMD = −0\.39, 95% CI −0\.61 to −0\.17\) after exercise interventions in samples aged 5 to 18 years, yet several large pragmatic trials have detected no benefit\. This mini review synthesizes recent evidence on these effects, the mechanisms proposed to explain them, and why the evidence base remains internally inconsistent\. We argue that the contradiction is largely resolvable: efficacy estimates come from a heavily overlapping pool of trials and are inflated by unblinded designs, self\-reported outcomes, and passive comparators, whereas universal school\-based trials recruit predominantly asymptomatic students and deliver far less activity than prescribed\. Mechanisms span three nested levels, neurobiological, psychosocial and behavioral, but most mediation evidence is concurrent rather than temporally ordered\. Read through self\-determination theory and acceptance\-based accounts of distress tolerance, tolerable difficulty appears to be part of how participation confers benefit, with implications for injury, dropout and elite youth sport\. Priorities include adequately powered trials with active controls and process evaluation, compositional analysis of movement behaviors, and temporally ordered mechanistic designs\.

## [Learning the control\-of\-variables strategy through self\-generated and vicarious errors: the mediating roles of affect, motivation, cognitive load, and error awareness](../publications/06086c68fb6c281ae8b8.md)

Linda Hämmerle; Shelbi L\. Kuhlmann; Theresa Krause\-Wichmann; Andrea Möller

Abstract Controlled experiments are essential for causal reasoning, yet students struggle with the control\-of\-variables strategy \(CVS\)\. Self\-generated errors, vicarious errors, or a combination could provide learning opportunities; however, error awareness, motivation, affect, and cognitive load may shape whether students benefit from different types of errors\. This study examines the effect of self\-generated, vicarious, combined, or no errors on CVS learning, and investigates affect, motivation, cognitive load, and error awareness as potential mediators\. 255 seventh\- and eighth\-grade students \(40% female\) participated\. In an experimental intervention study with three experimental groups and one control group, students engaged with experiments before receiving instruction and error\-reflection prompts, following a problem\-solving prior to instruction approach\. We assessed CVS skills, affect, cognitive load, motivation, and error awareness\. Analyses included ANCOVA, ANOVA, and path models\. The self\-generated errors group scored highest on the CVS\-posttest, followed by the no\-errors, vicarious errors, and combination groups\. Group differences in CVS performance were not statistically significant, although all groups improved from pre\- to posttest\. No mediation effects were found for affect, motivation, or cognitive load\. Error awareness positively predicted posttest performance, but negatively mediated the effect of self\-generated errors on learning\. Different types of errors and error\-free examples were all associated with CVS learning gains, even though the different types did not differentially affect CVS learning outcomes when controlling for prior knowledge\. Error awareness showed a complex pattern, being positively associated with performance while marginally negatively mediating the effect of self\-generated errors\. These findings highlight the need for further research to better understand the complex role of errors in science learning\.

## [One Oral GLP\-1 Receptor Agonist, Three Gateways: What a Nonpeptide Metabolic Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/0609db99d3f9b1189441.md)

Riddhi Rohan Moradiya; Aditi Shivakumar Hipparagi; Peivand Pirouzi

Oral, nonpeptide small\-molecule glucagon\-like peptide\-1 \(GLP\-1\) receptor agonists represent a significant pharmaceutical innovation within an already well\-established therapeutic mechanism, offering the metabolic benefits long associated with injectable peptide GLP\-1 agonists through a once\-daily tablet formulation\. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of an oral GLP\-1 receptor agonist candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014\. Because this candidate&\#x27;s nonpeptide, small\-molecule chemical format places it under each region&\#x27;s conventional small\-molecule nonclinical framework rather than the biologics\-specific framework governing its peptide\-based predecessors, the comparison also addresses a regulatory\-classification question of direct practical relevance: how chemical format, not shared pharmacological mechanism, determines which nonclinical and administrative conventions actually apply in each of the three jurisdictions\. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to this program, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing oral metabolic drug candidates across Canada, the United States, and the European Union\.Keywords: oral GLP\-1 receptor agonist; obesity; type 2 diabetes; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [DEMOCRATIC ACCOUNTABILITY ON PAPER AND IN PRACTICE: A SCOPING REVIEW OF EU AND US ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE POLICY, WITH A CONCLUDING WORD FOR INDIA](../publications/06156c35b7a747d21598.md)

Mangal Deo; Medhavi Gupta

The artificial intelligence policy secures democratic accountability has become almost a ritual opening line in both Brussels and Washington, and it is a claim this paper has set out to test rather than repeat\. Through a scoping review of the primary legal instruments in force between 2023 and 2026, together with the peer\-reviewed and specialist\-professional commentary written on them, democratic accountability has been operationalised along three variables: binding regulatory red lines, transparency in AI\-enabled political campaigning, and the robustness of public oversight institutions once a system is already in the field\. The European Union, it is found, has legislated all three dimensions in explicit statutory language — and has, in the same breath, generated a literature preoccupied with the gap between what Parliament authorised and what administration has actually delivered\. The United States has moved the other way, from a voluntary risk\-management posture toward a strategy of executive\-led federal preemption that several scholars read not as deregulation but as a redistribution of who gets to regulate\. Neither trajectory, the paper argues, offers India a template that can simply be imported; each offers a caution worth absorbing before, rather than after, India&\#x27;s own institutions harden into their final shape\.

## [CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre\-Registered Study of 465 Agent\-Authored Pull Requests](../publications/061870a2bf2eb42b9831.md)

Lo Gullstrand Heander; Markus Borg; Emma Söderberg; Christofer Rydenfält

Context: Organizations increasingly delegate code review to multi\-agent large language model \(LLM\) pipelines billed per token\. Low code quality raises human maintenance effort, but its effect on agent review cost has not been measured\. Objective: We test whether baseline CodeHealth predicts the token cost of agentic review and fix beyond pull request \(PR\) footprint\. Method: In a pre\-registered observational study, we sampled 465 agent\-authored PRs from 246 repositories in AIDev, jointly stratified by CodeHealth and footprint under repository caps\. A frozen five\-agent review\-and\-fix pipeline processed every PR with three different LLMs\. Per LLM, we fitted a mixed model of log tokens on CodeHealth and log PR footprint, with a repository random intercept\. Results: For all three LLMs the CodeHealth coefficient was negative, with 95% CI excluding zero; each CodeHealth point was associated with 3\.5% to 6\.1% lower token cost\. CodeHealth was unrelated to PR footprint, so PR size does not explain the association\. Two of three registered smells predicted fix cost; batch fixing left median CodeHealth unchanged\. Exploratory analyses located the association in the review stage, where agents iterated more on unhealthy code without writing more comments\. Adjusting for the size of the scored files absorbed the association, which we interpret as mediation by file size\. Conclusions: A quality metric calibrated against human maintainability also predicts the inference cost of multi\-agent review and fix\. The effect is modest per point and not carried by PR size, so the refactoring case extends to agent\-reviewed code when it changes structure and file size, not only the score\. Data Availability: https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.22127920

## [Adaptive deanonymization of blockchain transactions leveraging integrative neural architectures in decentralized networks](../publications/0618a9f68fda634927ad.md)

Rohit Saxena; Brijesh Kumar Chaurasia; Abhinav Awasthi; Lav Upadhyay

Abstract The pseudonymous nature of decentralized networks like Bitcoin presents tremendous obstacles for regulatory compliance, forensic auditing, and cybercrime investigation\. Traditional heuristics and single\-modality machine learning \(ML\) frameworks provide partial transparency but usually suffer from the modality isolation problem, which fails to consider spatial graph structure, temporal transaction velocity, and local metadata patterns simultaneously\. To break these limitations, in this paper, we propose an adaptive behavioral deanonymization method for blockchain transactions at the entity level based on an integrative neural architecture \(CNN → LSTM → GNN\) that dynamically focuses on spatial, temporal, and structural signals based on the behavior of the entity\. The integrative neural uses a Disjoint Set Union \(DSU\) algorithm to combine temporary address artifacts into 140,235 resolved actor clusters, lowering ledger noise by 67\.2%\. The proposed architecture uses 1D\-Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\) for extracting local structural fingerprints, Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) networks for capturing temporal sequence velocity, and Graph Neural Networks \(GNN\) over a dynamic k\-Nearest Neighbor \(k\-NN\) adjacency matrix for aggregating neighborhood context\. The architecture uses cost\-sensitive learning \(weighted cross\-entropy\) to tackle the significant class imbalance \(1:500\) to maintain analytical authenticity and forensics standards without synthetic distortion\. The proposed architecture is assessed on a sample of a dataset of 427,625 transactions, achieving an overall classification accuracy of approximately 97%, which is better than the baseline models, and generating a transparent, explainable audit trail using SHAP and LIME feature attribution\.

## [GenOpt\-FedGNN: GAN\-Augmented Federated Graph Learning with GWO and ASIO\-Inspired Adaptive Aggregation for Imbalanced Fraud Detection](../publications/061b4455953726e1a3bc.md)

Narayan Patil; Sheela Hundekari; Sagar Dhanraj Pande

Detecting fraud in distributed financial transaction systems is challenging\. It is extremely rare to find a fraudulent record\. The interactions among transactional records have a relational structure and the data can’t be stored centrally by every participating institution\. The paper introduces the federated graph learning framework i\.e\. GenOpt\-FedGNN\. The framework combines Generative Adversarial Network \(GAN\) with client local learning, graph neural classification, and the aggregation of the trained models through adaptive process of Grey Wolf Optimization \(GWO\) and Asteroid Satellite Inspired Optimization \(ASIO\)\. Each client preprocesses their own transactions independently, produces more minority fraud samples to train a class weighted Graph Neural Network \(GNN\), and builds a transaction graph\. Each client sends updates regarding model and validator to the server\. The framework is tested with a set of 200,000 PaySim transactions\. Transactions were randomly sampled and distributed among the five distributed clients with 30 communication rounds\. Six configurations \(FedAvg, GWO and ASIO with and without GAN augmentation\), have been compared by Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1\-score, ROC\-AUC, PR\-AUC, Specificity, False Positive Rate, False Negative Rate and Confusion\-matrix measures\. The ablation analysis demonstrated that GAN augmentation doubled local fraud training samples and reduced class\-imbalance ratio\. But, the local fraud data has been extremely imbalanced\. Overall, at the final round, the accuracy was highest with ASIO\-GAN \(96\.40%\), the specificity \(96\.41%\), precision \(1\.58%\), F1\-score \(3\.11%\), and the lowest False Positive Rate \(3\.59%\)\. The best Balanced Accuracy \(94\.16%\) was found for FedAvg\-GAN, and the best PR\-AUC \(60\.02%\) was found for ASIO\-NoGAN\. The GWO GAN\-based configurations got best PR\-AUC of 59\.20%\. The ablation results on the other hand further showed that using GAN for augmentation resulted in a consistent increase in the Accuracy, Precision, F1\-Score, Specificity and false alarm control compared to using it without GAN\. So augmentation with GAN and aggregation with Adaptive Aggregation can affect the sensitivity–specificity trade\-off but not necessarily all the other aggregation metrics\. The proposed framework is reproducible and data local to the raw data for the graph\-based fraud detection application which features extreme class imbalance\.

## [Advancing vision\-language understanding through fine\-grained perception and long\-range modeling](../publications/062d44e8618fd5c8d4fc.md)

Tanveer Hannan

Human perception is not a passive recording of the world\. It is an active, selective process of anchoring meaning within an overwhelming perceptual stream—sustaining the identity of objects through occlusion, locating moments of relevance within hours of experience, and extracting structure from dense, heterogeneous information\. This dissertation asks whether vision–language systems can do the same\. We argue that the central failure of current architectures is not insufficient scale, but insufficient selectivity: the inability to maintain stable, semantically persistent representations—perceptual anchors—across the noise of dynamic scenes and the vastness of long\-range multimodal contexts\. A model that cannot preserve what it has seen will hallucinate; a model that cannot manage what it is shown will be overwhelmed\. Both failures are architectural, and both are addressable through principled inductive biases rather than brute\-force capacity\. This dissertation develops a unified framework in which perceptual anchors are established, selectively propagated, and recursively retrieved across increasing scales of complexity—from object instances in short video clips, to temporal events in hour\-long videos, to semantically coherent regions in multimodal documents\. Five contributions instantiate this framework, each addressing a distinct manifestation of the same underlying problem: how to sustain grounded, fine\-grained understanding across time, language, and scale\. From this progression, three principles crystallise\. Perception is selective: reliable understanding requires that representations be propagated conditionally, not uniformly\. Grounding is unified: retrieving a relevant anchor and understanding why it is relevant are not two tasks but one\. Scaling is recursive: an unbounded perceptual world is navigated not by expanding memory, but by learning to search\. Together, these principles converge on a single insight: that to know the world is not to contain it, but to attend to it—selectively, persistently, and with the willingness to revise what has faded and release what no longer serves\. What this dissertation instantiates computationally, the philosophy of mind has long theorised as the structural condition of cognition: that understanding is not the accumulation of all available information, but the principled, selective engagement with what endures\.

## [Inteligencia artificial y marketing digital: reflexiones comparadas entre Colombia y panamá a partir del periplo internacional 2025](../publications/0631dd4d7fdc9ec4a862.md)

Angélica María Corrales Castiblanco

La inteligencia artificial \(IA\) ha dejado de ser una herramienta emergente, para consolidarse como un motor central de innovación tecnológica en el marketing digital; a nivel global, este sector proyecta superar los 107\.500 millones de dólares en 2028, con un crecimiento sostenido impulsado por algoritmos predictivos, automatización y personalización\. Sin embargo, la adopción en América Latina presenta matices, en Colombia, cerca del 59 % de los consumidores interactúa cotidianamente con aplicaciones de IA, mientras que en Panamá el avance ha sido mayor debido a la inversión en infraestructura digital y políticas de innovación\. Este ensayo analiza la relevancia de la IA en el marketing digital desde un enfoque comparativo, integrando cifras recientes, estudios de caso y reflexiones críticas; donde se plantea que, aunque la IA fortalece la personalización, la eficiencia y la optimización de campañas, su impacto depende de superar retos organizacionales, culturales y éticos\.

## [Anxiety Symptoms Assessed by the Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale, Lifestyle Habits, and Cardiometabolic Risk in Spanish Workers](../publications/0634c06d7bf38fc3fbbe.md)

Lucía Garrido Sepúlveda; Pedro Juan Tárraga López; María Teófila Vicente\-Herrero; Jose Alberto Garrido; Ángel Arturo López‐González; José Ignacio Ramírez‐Manent

Background: Anxiety has been increasingly recognized as a relevant contributor to cardiometabolic dysfunction through neuroendocrine, inflammatory, and behavioral mechanisms\. However, evidence evaluating the relationship between anxiety symptoms, lifestyle habits, and cardiometabolic risk in large occupational populations remains limited\. This study aimed to analyze the association between Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale \(GADS\) scores, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic risk factors in a large cohort of Spanish workers\. Methods: A cross\-sectional observational study was conducted in 119,336 Spanish workers undergoing routine occupational health examinations between 2021 and 2023\. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the GADS\. Lifestyle variables included smoking status, physical activity assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire \(IPAQ\), and adherence to the Mediterranean diet evaluated through the Prevention with Mediterranean Diet \(PREDIMED\) questionnaire\. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, lipid profile, fasting glucose, obesity, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome were analyzed\. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios \(ORs\) for cardiometabolic abnormalities according to anxiety status and lifestyle factors\. Results: Elevated GADS scores were significantly associated with worse cardiometabolic profiles in both sexes, including higher blood pressure, triglycerides, fasting glucose, body mass index, waist circumference, and lower high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations\. Workers with elevated anxiety presented markedly higher prevalences of hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, impaired fasting glucose, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome \(all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. After multivariable adjustment, elevated anxiety remained independently associated with hypertension \(OR 6\.48; 95% confidence interval \(CI\) 5\.89– 7\.09\), hypertriglyceridemia \(OR 5\.31; 95% CI 4\.60–6\.02\), and impaired fasting glucose \(OR 5\.23; 95% CI 4\.64–5\.83\)\. Physical inactivity and low adherence to the Mediterranean diet were associated with a less favorable cardiometabolic profile among participants with elevated anxiety scores\. Elevated GADS scores were independently associated with all major cardiometabolic outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with the strongest associations observed for hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and impaired fasting glucose\. Conclusions: Elevated GADS scores are strongly associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles in Spanish workers, particularly when combined with unhealthy lifestyle behaviors\. These findings support the integration of mental health assessment and lifestyle interventions into occupational cardiometabolic prevention strategies\.

## [INSTRUCTIONAL DESIGN OF A WORKPLACE\-ORIENTED GENERAL AIGC COURSE IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE](../publications/063bcdf1d55325bc8e24.md)

Yishen Liao; Lei Shu; 赵爱华; Yun Zhang; Hejie Yu

In the era of digital intelligence, artificial intelligence generated content \(AIGC\) has become deeply integrated into workplace workflows\. However, a growing gap has emerged between corporate demand for AIGC\-driven productivity and the lag in talent development\. Current introductory AIGC courses suffer from fragmented content, superficial assessment methods, and limited adaptability\. To address these challenges, this study proposes a holistic instructional design framework based on the &quot;structural reconstruction, capability building, and closed\-loop evaluation&quot; model, featuring an 8\-hour modular curriculum: prompt engineering \(2 hours\) to establish foundational concepts for cross\-domain transfer, core tool mastery \(4 hours\) covering four mainstream AI platforms \(ERNIE Bot, DeepSeek, WPS AI, and Doubao\), and role\-specific applications \(2 hours\) offering tailored practical exercises across five key professions \(finance, education, software development, copywriting, and design\)\. The framework employs a hybrid assessment model combining self\-evaluations, instructor feedback, and AI\-driven evaluations to target real\-world problem\-solving skills and adaptability to new tools, while a data\-driven feedback loop enables continuous optimization of both course content and personalized learning interventions\. Ultimately, this study provides a scalable, iterative system framework for empowering today&\#x27;s AI\-driven workforce\.

## [Auditing Audiovisual Correspondence in Generative AI Coursework with Frozen Multimodal Encoders](../publications/063fcba35e2d25b08b83.md)

Gang Xu; Xiaojing Qin; Weitao Liu

Computational evaluation of generative artificial intelligence coursework requires distinguishing audiovisual correspondence from creative achievement\. We conducted a retrospective computational measurement audit of 49 archived student submissions containing 58 videos\. Frozen CLIP and CLAP representations were queried with paired event and affect descriptions\. Five fixed anchor configurations and a pretrained AudioCLIP comparator were evaluated through original\-pair retrieval, temporal and coordinate controls, blur and noise transformations, teacher judgments, and selected cases\. The primary configuration achieved a mean reciprocal rank of 0\.179, compared with 0\.093 for the designated AudioCLIP comparator; its advantage over other temporal anchor configurations remained uncertain\. Temporal and anchor\-index disruptions reduced discrimination, while perturbations could increase matched scores despite poorer retrieval\. During revision, two teachers independently rerated all submissions after calibration on separate examples and rubric freezing\. Total\-score agreement was ICC\(A,1\) = 0\.970 and ICC\(A,2\) = 0\.985, but the primary diagnostic’s association with their mean total was near zero \(Spearman ρ = 0\.020\)\. A few adjusted dimension\-level associations did not retain significance in the non\-silent sensitivity analysis\. Selected cases exposed unverified semantic responses and nonzero outputs from silent audio\. The workflow supports inspectable correspondence diagnostics; artistic grading and educational usefulness require further validation\.

## [Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests](../publications/064a190e47b03f3291c9.md)

Yuxin Qiao; Jianquan Liu; David P\. Edwards

Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear\. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest\-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna\. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon\-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3\.5% and 1\.6% of forest globally, respectively\. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests\. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health\.

## [Multimodal eye\-tracking reveals impaired inhibitory control and reduced preparatory pupil dilation in essential tremor](../publications/064b4f7459f90d00498e.md)

Chien‐Tai Hong; Jui\-Tai Chen; Audrey Yong; Ta\-Liang Chen; Kevin S Xu; Chin‐An Wang

Abstract Essential tremor is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving cerebello\-thalamo\-cortical and autonomic processes beyond tremor itself\. Oculomotor, pupillary, and blink signals provide complementary physiological readouts of these distributed systems, yet they have largely been studied in isolation\. Here, we used video\-based eye tracking during an interleaved pro\- and anti\-saccade task to characterize oculomotor performance, pupil dynamics, blink behavior, and trial\-by\-trial cross\-domain coupling in 45 essential tremor patients and 46 controls\. Essential tremor showed impaired inhibitory oculomotor control, reflected by increased direction errors, prolonged anti\-saccade reaction times, extended voluntary override time, and reduced generation of express saccades\. Preparatory pupil dilation was attenuated and constriction timing delayed despite preserved tonic baseline\. In contrast, blink dynamics were largely preserved\. Trial\-by\-trial pupil–saccade coupling was also largely preserved, indicating maintained cross\-domain coordination despite reduced preparatory autonomic modulation\. Exploratory machine\-learning analyses suggested that combined pupil–saccade features may capture aspects of clinical heterogeneity, particularly early\-onset status, although these findings did not survive permutation testing\. Together, these results indicate that essential tremor is associated with selective impairment of inhibitory oculomotor control and preparatory autonomic responses, with preserved cross\-domain coordination\. Multimodal eye tracking may therefore provide a scalable, non\-invasive framework for characterizing the heterogeneous physiological expression of essential tremor\.

## [Renewable Energy Integration for Enhanced Power System Stability Under Large Disturbances](../publications/06692f8e0c9e4f120acf.md)

Moussa Bakdi; Rachid Taleb; Asma Toualbia; Hacene Mellah; Maamar Souaihia; Hakima Mostefaoui

The Large\-Scale integration of renewable energy sources fundamentally alters the dynamic behavior of modern power systems, presenting both critical challenges and unprecedented opportunities for stability enhancement\. This paper investigates the dual\-edged impact of wind power, via Doubly\-Fed Induction Generators, and solar photovoltaic systems on power system stability during severe contingencies\. While the inherent intermittency of these sources characterized by fluctuating wind speeds and partial shading of PV arrays introduces significant operational uncertainties, their advanced power electronic interfaces offer a pathway for intelligent grid support\. This work proposes a novel control framework that leverages the fast\-acting reactive power capability of DFIGs and the active power modulation of solar PV inverters to provide synthetic inertia and voltage support, thereby improving the system&\#x27;s transient stability\. Concurrently, a small\-signal stability analysis is conducted using eigenvalue and modal decomposition techniques to evaluate the impact of these RESs on the system&\#x27;s damping characteristics and oscillatory modes\. The efficacy of the proposed strategy is validated through time\-domain simulations on a modified IEEE test system\. Results demonstrate a marked improvement in rotor angle stability and critical fault clearing time, alongside enhanced damping of inter\-area oscillations\. This research establishes that, when equipped with suitable grid\-forming controls, renewable energy sources are not merely a source of instability but a crucial asset for bolstering overall grid resilience against large disturbances\.

## [A Fundamental and Human Right: Addressing Basic Needs in Higher Education](../publications/066e832c711b075d9e9a.md)

April Lopez

Resumo indisponível na fonte\.

## [A Multivariate Analysis of Teacher Self\-Efficacy and Cognitive Load in Scripted Instructional Programs](../publications/068ad4c04a01b2221677.md)

Tameka A Bonner

This quantitative, non\-experimental, multivariate comparative study examined whether statistically significant differences existed in teacher self\-efficacy and teacher cognitive load between Title I and non–Title I elementary school teachers who implement scripted instructional programs\. The study addressed a gap in the literature by simultaneously examining these constructs across differing school settings\. The final analytic sample consisted of 169 elementary school teachers employed in Title I and non\-Title I schools within a suburban public school district in the southeastern United States\. Data were collected using the Teacher Sense of Efficacy Scale \(TSES\), the NASA Task Load Index \(NASA\-TLX\), and a demographic questionnaire administered via an electronic survey platform\. A one\-way multivariate analysis of variance \(MANOVA\) was conducted to examine differences between the two groups\. The results indicated no statistically significant difference in teacher self\-efficacy between Title I and non\-Title I teachers; however, a statistically significant difference in teacher cognitive load was found by school designation\. These findings demonstrate that while teachers maintained similar levels of confidence in their instructional abilities, the mental demands associated with implementing scripted instructional programs differed between Title I and non\-Title I school contexts\. Future research should replicate this study using more diverse populations, longitudinal designs, and additional contextual variables to examine further factors influencing teacher cognitive load and self\-efficacy within scripted instructional environments\.

## [Responsive pedagogy in higher education block delivery: a collaborative autoethnography](../publications/069a47430bd998a02187.md)

Adeline Muscat; Samara Van Toledo; Bec Marland; Sara Gaul\-Mckee

Widening participation in higher education has contributed to increasingly diverse student populations, highlighting the need for responsive teaching practices\. While research on block model delivery has examined student outcomes and experiences, less attention has been given to how responsive pedagogy is enacted in everyday teaching\. This study examines responsive pedagogy within block model delivery at an Australian university characterised by a diverse student population\. Using collaborative autoethnography, four teacher\-researchers engaged in vignette writing, collaborative dialogue, reflective writing, and recursive analysis to examine their responses to varied student learning needs\. Informed by rhizomatic theory, the analysis identified temporality, scaffolding, and differentiation as interconnected dimensions of responsive practice\. Findings reveal how these practices are relationally enacted and shaped by the temporal and structural conditions of intensive delivery\. The study conceptualises responsive pedagogy in block model higher education as structurally enabled, temporally reconfigured, and relationally enacted, contributing a practice\-centred understanding of pedagogical responsiveness in diverse higher education classrooms\.

## [Uncertainty\-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search](../publications/06a26db3f16d0aca080b.md)

Jianguo Huang; Zhiyi Lyu; Fuxiang Zhang; Yanchen Deng; Deheng Ye; Bo An

Tree search enhances multi\-step reasoning in large language models \(LLMs\), yet prevailing methods expand every step with a fixed budget, irrespective of the marginal utility of expansion\. We first show, across existing search algorithms, that continuations sampled from a shared intermediate state are largely duplicates and collapse to a few distinct answers\. Critically, we find that the semantic dispersion of sibling actions predicts the redundancy of their downstream continuations, permitting a subtree&\#x27;s budget to be fixed before expansion\. An information\-theoretic analysis motivates this: treating the per\-step budget as the Monte Carlo sample size for estimating a step&\#x27;s residual answer entropy, we derive a sufficient budget that shrinks with sibling dispersion\. We accordingly propose $\\textbf\{Uncertainty\-Aware Allocation\}$ \(UAA\), a training\-free framework that decouples value from uncertainty: values determine which candidates are promising, while uncertainty, estimated from sibling dispersion at no additional model cost, determines how many merit expansion, via uncertainty\-aware pruning and uncertainty\-aware budgeting\. Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reduces token usage by up to $90\\%$ and latency by up to $9\\times$ at comparable accuracy, generalizing across four tree search algorithms and both open\- and closed\-source LLMs\.

## [Social pressure: stress responses to virtual humans in immersive virtual job interviews](../publications/06a83fbf9ba0e7038327.md)

Celia Kessassi; Cédric Dumas; Caroline G\. L\. Cao; Mathieu Chollet

Abstract Prior research suggests that the attitude of virtual humans, in situations such as job interviews, can influence users’ stress levels\. However, the mechanisms through which designers can precisely modulate stress levels in these settings remain unclear\. We propose a mechanism for modulating users’ stress levels through multimodal social interactions with virtual humans\. These interactions are modulated along two dimensions: friendliness \(friendly vs\. hostile\) and dominance \(dominant vs\. non\-dominant\)\. To test this mechanism, we conducted two studies in which participants interacted with virtual humans that varied in friendliness and dominance\. Friendliness was expressed through cues of appreciation or dislike, such as facial expressions \(e\.g\., smiling or frowning\) and speech content \(e\.g\., “that’s good\!”\), whereas dominance was expressed through cues of control or lack of control, such as social rank \(i\.e\., supervisor vs\. subordinate\) and assertiveness \(i\.e\., giving instructions vs\. asking permission\)\. The results indicate that the behavior of the virtual humans plays a role in shaping stress responses; however, the findings reveal a complex relationship and therefore need to be interpreted with caution\. In particular, the findings showed that the dominant virtual human was perceived as less friendly than the non\-dominant virtual human\. Future research should further investigate this effect and consider alternative models that provide more clearly distinguishable and independent control parameters for modulating stress responses in social virtual environments\.

## [Synchronization of complex networks: Prescribed performance\-based event\-triggered impulsive control](../publications/06a85f69abcef87992f9.md)

Beiyang Kang; Jun\-Guo Lu; Jiarong Li; Juan Yu; Jinling Wang; Cheng Hu

To improve both transient and steady\-state performance in the synchronization process of complex networks, this paper proposes two novel event\-triggered pulse control schemes incorporating prescribed performance constraints\. First, an event\-triggered impulsive control based on a prescribed performance function is designed, which achieves practical synchronization of the complex network and ensures that synchronization errors remain strictly within a tunable range\. The proposed triggering mechanism is proven to effectively eliminate Zeno behavior\. Additionally, to achieve complete synchronization, forced pulses are incorporated into the control scheme\. By combining an error transformation function and using Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions for complete synchronization are derived, while Zeno behavior is also eliminated\. Finally, numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of both strategies, demonstrating the advantages of the proposed methods in terms of performance tuning and resource conservation\.

## [Observation Window Design Outweighs Architectural Complexity in Deep Learning for Sepsis Mortality Prediction](../publications/06b046c7be860c3caee8.md)

Irawan Irawan; Siti Nurmaini; Rossi Passarella; Jasmir Jasmir

Deep learning models for predicting sepsis mortality often obscure which design choices genuinely improve performance\.We developed a sequential model using 19,902 Sepsis\-3 patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV \(MIMIC\-IV\), processing hourly physiological sequences via convolutional and bidirectional recurrent layers alongside static patient features\.Under matched conditions, sliding\-window augmentation improved discrimination by 0\.033 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\), of which repeated training examples accounted for the larger share\.The static feature pathway contributed 0\.061, whereas the convolutional block had no measurable effect\.On a held\-out test set the model reached an AUROC of 0\.902; gradient boosting, a bidirectional long short\-term memory network, and a Transformer encoder reached 0\.865, 0\.855, and 0\.851 under an identical protocol and tuning budget\.When all features were restricted to the information available at each prediction time, discrimination fell to 0\.807 at six hours and 0\.839 at twelve, so shorter horizons carry a substantial cost\.These results suggest that in this task, input representation and observation length mattered more than architectural complexity\.

## [Real\-world clinical outcomes under intravenous and subcutaneous esketamine protocols for treatment\-resistant depression: a multicenter, retrospective study](../publications/06b4de799545cf7df325.md)

Gilberto Sousa Alves; Humberto M\. M\. Dos Santos; Samira D Damasceno; LAURA MARIANE SILVA MACIEL; Otavio Andre Farias Sousa da Silva; Ciro Sousa de Moura Fe; Jilmario Gomes de Santana; Mariélia Barbosa Leal de Freitas; André Férrer Carvalho; Dennison Monteiro

Background Esketamine is a promising therapeutic option for treatment\-resistant depression \(TRD\)\. Intravenous \(IV\) administration is the most extensively studied parenteral route\. However, subcutaneous \(SC\) administration may offer simpler, more scalable delivery\. Multicenter real\-world evidence comparing IV and SC routes of administration remains limited\. Objective To report clinical outcomes and tolerability of parenteral esketamine protocols for TRD at three Brazilian advanced\-care centers\. Methods This multicenter retrospective chart review study \(2023–2025\) included 72 outpatients aged 18–65 years who received esketamine 2 to 3 times weekly via IV \(n = 26; 6 sessions\) or SC \(n = 46; 12 sessions\) administration\. Data were analyzed in RStudio 2026\.01\.0 Build 392 using R 4\.5\.2\. The primary outcome was categorical response on the Beck Depression Inventory\-II \(BDI\-II\) at the shared 6\-session milestone and at each protocol\-specific endpoint\. Secondary outcomes included continuous changes in BDI\-II and Beck Anxiety Inventory \(BAI\) scores in the full sample, tolerability and documented adverse events, and exploratory factor analysis of baseline symptom dimensions\. Results After six sessions, BDI\-II response distribution favored the IV protocol, although the between\-group difference was not statistically significant \(Pearson’s chi\-square = 5\.661; p = 0\.059; odds ratio, 3\.06; 95% CI, 1\.22–8\.00\)\. At the protocol\-specific endpoints, categorical BDI\-II response did not differ significantly between groups \(Pearson’s chi\-square = 1\.227; p = 0\.541; odds ratio, 1\.44; 95% CI, 0\.57–3\.73\)\. No serious adverse events or adverse\-event\-related discontinuations were reported; dissociation was more frequent with IV than with SC treatment \(53\.8% vs\. 13\.0%; p = 0\.001\), whereas nausea and mild transient blood pressure increases did not differ significantly\. BDI\-II factor analysis identified cognitive\-affective and somatic\-neurovegetative dimensions\. Conclusions The IV protocol showed a more favorable BDI\-II response distribution at the shared 6\-session milestone, whereas SC esketamine achieved statistically comparable categorical outcomes at its 12\-session protocol\-specific endpoint\. Route selection should consider speed of response, tolerability, dosing, operational complexity, and access\. SC esketamine may be a feasible option where simplicity, tolerability, and access are priorities\. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the retrospective, observational study design\.

## [Treatment Sequencing With Biologic Switching, Staged Excision, and Split‐Thickness Skin Grafting for Extensive Hidradenitis Suppurativa](../publications/06d2a157638552bff84d.md)

Shunki Hashizumi; Ko Kagoyama; Hiroaki Ishida; Teruhiko Makino; Tadamichi Shimizu

Treatment of extensive multiregional hidradenitis suppurativa requires sequencing biologic therapy and surgery when active inflammation and irreversible structural disease coexist\. A 58\-year\-old Japanese man with Hurley Stage III disease had inadequate overall control with adalimumab\. At the assessment before medial\-thigh surgery, the International Hidradenitis Suppurativa Severity Score System score was 48\. Because he sought prompt relief from painful drainage and daily wound care, bilateral scarred and tunnel\-bearing lesions were excised and reconstructed by staged split\-thickness skin grafting while adalimumab was continued\. Local control was achieved, but disease persisted elsewhere, prompting a switch to bimekizumab\. Inflammatory lesion counts decreased, but Hidradenitis Suppurativa Clinical Response was not achieved at week 16 and extensive gluteal scars and draining tunnels remained\. Bilateral gluteal excision and staged grafting were therefore performed during continued bimekizumab treatment, without postoperative infection, bleeding, or graft failure\. Six months after reconstruction, the severity score was 9 and the clinical response criterion was met, reflecting both decreased inflammatory activity during bimekizumab treatment and surgical removal of structural lesions\. Gluteal local control persisted through 15 months\. This case illustrates sequencing biologic switching and regional surgery according to inflammatory activity, persistent structural disease, and the need for prompt symptom relief\.

## [CareBridge AI: A Unified Web\-Based Healthcare Assistance Platform](../publications/06d3f42106e7f8ef6fd7.md)

Saniya Javid Shaikh; A\. N\. Pawar

Healthcare\-support information is often spread across separate services for treatment\-cost planning, government assistance discovery, hospital location search, and medical\-document review\. This can make navigation difficult for patients and families, particularly those seeking affordable care\. This paper presents CareBridge AI, a web\-based prototype that organizes selected healthcare\-support functions in one interface\. Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the prototype provides interfaces for medical\-bill information, a funding\-gap calculator, medical\-report text review, scheme discovery, a hospital finder, and chat\-style support\. The funding\-gap module estimates the remaining amount from user\-entered treatment cost, available funds, expected assistance, and other contributions\. The current implementation uses browser\-side logic and demonstration storage\. It does not demonstrate a trained or clinically validated AI/ML model, a production\-grade patient database, or an IoT deployment\. A qualitative comparison identifies integration and navigation as the main design opportunity\. A proposed evaluation plan covers calculation correctness, official\-link validity, usability, privacy, and future AI validation\. No clinical or performance improvement is claimed without measured testing\.

## [Self\-relevance dynamically biases exploration and exploitation in value\-based decisions](../publications/06da9c29d4e8a8130c6a.md)

Esther S Selvaraj; Marius Golubickis; Siobhan E\. Caughey; Parnian Jalalian; Yadvi Sharma; Srishti Khasa; Leoni S\. Masroujah; C\. Neil Macrae

While adaptive decision\-making requires balancing exploration and exploitation, dominant accounts often treat this trade\-off as independent of social context\. Drawing on theories of self\-function and motivated cognition, we tested whether deciding for oneself versus others alters exploration\-exploitation dynamics\. Across two experiments, participants completed a restless multi\-armed bandit task for themselves or a close friend under gain \(Experiment 1\) and loss \(Experiment 2\) conditions\. Results indicated that self\-other differences in choice behavior emerged dynamically over time rather than reflecting a static bias\. An additional computational modeling analysis revealed that self\-relevance was associated with increased sensitivity to value differences \(i\.e\., inverse temperature\), consistent with more deterministic choice \(i\.e\., exploitation\)\. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that self\-relevance does not merely influence learning but dynamically shapes decision policies over time\. More broadly, the results highlight the importance of motivational context in regulating how individuals balance information gain and reward during value\-based decisions\.

## [ACEdit: Stable Multi\-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning](../publications/06e43b6503af4e069c85.md)

Sara Dorfman; Nir Goren; Gal Barak; Daniel Cohen\-Or; Or Patashnik

Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns\. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor&\#x27;s original training and multi\-turn inference\. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi\-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift\. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self\-Forcing to image editing\. The main challenge is that self\-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground\-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable\. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs\. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction\. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi\-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence\.

## [Scoping One Health Foresight Collaboration among EU Agencies](../publications/06e57b7a6110f8aa04dc.md)

Ariana Ferrari; Susanne Giesecke; Totti Könnölä A

This working paper constitutes the first deliverable under the EFSA contract RTD/2023/OP/0011 – Lot 1 on Foresight on Demand in Science, Technology, Research and Innovation Policy, implemented within the framework of multi\-agency foresight on One Health and authorised by the European Commission, DG Research &amp; Innovation, G1 – Common R&amp;I Strategy and Foresight Service\. It examines the relevance of the One Health approach for a broad range of European institutions and agencies and argues that One Health has become an increasingly important framework for addressing the complex and interdependent challenges facing the European Union\. These challenges include emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial and antifungal resistance, environmental pollution, climate change, food insecurity, mental health pressures, and widening social inequalities, all of which cut across traditional sectoral and institutional boundaries\. The report situates One Health within its broader conceptual and policy context\. It shows that the approach has evolved from earlier biomedical understandings centred on zoonotic disease and veterinary\-public health cooperation into a wider framework linking human, animal, plant, and environmental health\. In line with the recommendations of the European Commission’s Group of Chief Scientific Advisors, the report adopts the OHHLEP definition of One Health as an integrated and unifying approach aimed at balancing and optimizing the health of humans, animals, plants, and ecosystems\. At the same time, it underlines that important ambiguities remain concerning the interpretation, scope, and operationalisation of the concept, especially in the context of European governance\. The report therefore not only maps One Health as a thematic field but also examines how it can serve as a practical basis for stronger coordination among EU agencies and institutions\. A central finding is that One Health is already relevant to a wide constellation of EU bodies, even if this relevance is not always explicitly recognised or institutionally coordinated\. The report highlights the roles of DG SANTE, DG ENV, DG CLIMA, DG AGRI, and the Joint Research Centre, as well as agencies such as EFSA, EMA, ECDC, EEA, ECHA, EUDA, EU\-OSHA, Frontex, EIGE, and ETF\. These actors contribute complementary expertise across food safety, infectious disease monitoring, environmental protection, chemical safety, medicines regulation, occupational health, social inequalities, and preparedness\. The report notes that cooperation has already advanced through initiatives such as the ONE Conference, the cross\-agency One Health task force, and joint work on zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance\. However, it also finds that collaboration remains uneven, fragmented, and often dependent on issue\-specific rather than strategic coordination\. Existing efforts show strong potential, but the absence of a fully integrated governance architecture continues to limit the EU’s capacity to translate One Health into a genuinely shared and anticipatory policy framework\. On this basis, the report develops a broad and integrated overview of the main scientific themes currently shaping the One Health agenda\. These include infectious diseases and health security, veterinary medical products, antimicrobial and antifungal resistance, environmental and climate\-related health risks, animal health and welfare, public health and disease prevention, sustainable food systems, inequalities and governance, digitalisation and health, and education and training\. A major contribution of the report is that it expands the One Health agenda beyond its more established focus on zoonoses and AMR\. It argues that issues such as chemical pollution, microplastics, PFAS, unsafe food systems, occupational health, illicit drugs, mental health, militarization, nuclear risks, and the health implications of geopolitical change must also be considered within a One Health framework because they arise from and reinforce the interdependence of environmental, animal, and human health\. The report therefore presents One Health not as a narrow technical field, but as a broader framework for understanding and governing systemic and interacting risks\. The report also emphasizes that the One Health perspective is closely aligned with broader EU strategic priorities\. It shows that One Health contributes not only to public health protection, but also to goals related to sustainable prosperity, food security, preparedness, climate resilience, social fairness, and democratic legitimacy\. In this sense, One Health is framed as a governance approach capable of linking prevention, resilience, and sustainability across domains that are too often treated separately\. The report repeatedly stresses that challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, environmental degradation, food insecurity, and health inequalities cannot be addressed adequately through isolated policy responses\. Rather, they require integrated surveillance, coordinated foresight, and stronger institutional mechanisms capable of connecting evidence, preparedness, and action across sectors and scales\. A further important conclusion is that One Health must be treated as both a scientific and institutional innovation agenda\. The report identifies the need for stronger inter\- and transdisciplinary collaboration, improved data sharing, harmonised surveillance systems, and clearer coordination mechanisms at EU level\. It supports the view that the European Union should adopt a more coherent One Health strategy, backed by adequate resources, shared infrastructures, and long\-term political support\. Education and training are also identified as crucial pillars\. One Health concepts should be integrated into academic, professional, and public learning environments, while digital tools, artificial intelligence, and data systems should be developed in line with ethical, inclusive, and sustainable principles\. At the same time, the report warns that digitalisation, if poorly governed, may reproduce inequalities, deepen data divides, and generate new environmental burdens\. In its final section, the report moves from thematic mapping to strategic foresight\. It identifies a series of emerging and cross\-cutting areas that merit particular attention in future collaboration\. These include cross\-border health threats and joint preparedness, chemicals and environmental exposures, illicit drugs and their environmental and social dimensions, climate change and health inequalities, social determinants of health, mental health, digitalisation, and militarization\. Across all these areas, the report underscores the need for strengthened multi\-agency collaboration and more systematic data sharing\. It argues that the EU already possesses many of the institutional building blocks required for a stronger One Health approach, but that these assets need to be connected more effectively through coordinated foresight, shared analytical tools, and common strategic priorities\. Overall, the report presents One Health as a necessary and forward\-looking framework for European governance\. It shows that the health of people, animals, plants, and ecosystems is increasingly shaped by interconnected pressures that no single institution, sector, or Member State can manage alone\. By embedding One Health more firmly in research agendas, legislative initiatives, surveillance systems, education, and inter\-agency cooperation, the European Union can improve its capacity to anticipate and respond to multidimensional threats while also advancing sustainability, equity, and resilience\. In this sense, One Health is not merely a conceptual lens, but a practical foundation for future European collaboration in science, regulation, and strategic policy development\.

## [Towards a comprehensive landscape and mechanism understanding of virus\-disease associations](../publications/06e7d97fe195c0deb1d3.md)

Yifan Wu; Ruina You; Yang Feng; Shangwen Lu; Chen Siang; Ping Fu; Zhaozhong Zhu; Congyu Lu; Zhiyuan Zhang; Lihua Xu; Huiru Li; Xinglian Wang; Xinyi Wang; Qian Huang; Xun Liu; Zhuoya Xu; Guolin Dong; Shiqing Li; Xiaowen Hu; Zefeng Xiang; Yixuan Hu; Longfei Mao; Zhichao Miao; 祥贤 孟; Yousong Peng

Viruses are linked to human diseases through complex molecular mechanisms, yet a comprehensive investigation of virus\-disease associations and their molecular basis remains lacking\. We curated 3,555 high\-confidence virus\-disease associations involving 267 viruses and 954 diseases through text\-mining over 28 million PubMed abstracts followed by rigorous manual verification, establishing the most comprehensive resource in this field to date\. We then developed AVD, a user\-friendly online database to store, visualize, and analyze these associations and their molecular mechanisms\. Our analysis revealed that virus\-disease association patterns are significantly influenced by viral taxonomy, phenotype, and key biological traits such as transmissibility, transmission routes, and tissue tropism\. Molecular analysis identified a core set of bridging genes involved in the majority of virus\-disease associations\. Notably, these bridging genes were extensively involved in viral infections and diseases, and exhibit distinct characteristics, including a high proportion of secreted proteins, elevated expression across human tissues, and high centrality in the human protein\-protein interaction network\. Furthermore, we developed a machine\-learning model capable of accurately predicting virus\-disease associations\. Collectively, this study provides a valuable data resource and analytical framework for studying virus\-disease relationships and offers novel insights into their molecular mechanisms\. In this manuscript the authors analyze viral\-disease associations and identified that virus\-disease associations are significantly influenced by viral taxonomic, phenotype, and their biological traits\. Genes that may mediate the viral\-disease associations are also discovered\. A database called AVD \(Association of Virus and human Diseases\) is also constructed to facilitate the storage and convenient analysis of the associations\.

## [Effects of Hypoxic Adipose\-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome on Type II Collagen Expression in a Rabbit Model of Disc Degeneration](../publications/06f042a9306e5d7e4f20.md)

Romaniyanto Romaniyanto; Dykall Naf&\#x27;an Dzikri; Daffa Sadewa; Muhammad Setya Fachreza

Introduction: Intervertebral disc \(IVD\) degeneration is a major cause of low back pain, and is characterized by the loss of extracellular matrix, particularly type II collagen\. Regenerative therapies using mesenchymal stem cells \(MSCs\) and their secretome have shown promise, but their comparative effects on type II collagen expression require further investigation\. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the effects of allogeneic hypoxic adipose\-derived mesenchymal stem cells \(Ad\-MSCs\) and their secretome on type II collagen expression in a rabbit model of IVD degeneration\. Methods: A true experimental study was conducted on 18 New Zealand White rabbits\. Degeneration was induced by needle puncture\. Subjects were divided into three groups: control \(fibrin glue\), P1 \(hypoxic Ad\-MSC\), and P2 \(secretome\)\. After 8 weeks, type II collagen expression was analyzed using immunohistochemistry\. Results: Both P1 and P2 showed significantly higher type II collagen expression than the control \(p = 0\.001 and p &lt; 0\.001, respectively\)\. The secretome group \(P2\) showed significantly higher expression than the Ad\-MSC group \(P1\) \(p = 0\.039\)\. These findings suggest that the secretome may provide a greater stimulatory effect on type II collagen expression than direct cell administration\. Conclusion: The hypoxic Ad\-MSC\-derived secretome resulted in higher type II collagen expression than hypoxic Ad\-MSCs administration in this rabbit model\.

## [Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF\-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis](../publications/06f0b1df2c8503506970.md)

Agata Kurowski; Bohan Zhu; Yifei Sun; Paul R\. Sargunas; Nimisha Jain; Ashley Chan; Lahouaria Hadri; Yi Shi; Martin J\. Walsh; Sai Ma

UHRF1 is a chromatin\-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood\. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells \(ESCs\) and embryos\. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near\-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1\-null embryos developed normally until E8\.5 and then failed to develop further by E9\.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss\. Single\-cell multi\-omic \(ME\-seq\) profiling of E8\.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture\. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF\-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis\-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP\-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations\. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis\. The authors show that loss of UHRF1 disrupts DNA methylation, CTCF\-associated chromatin organization and gene regulation during early mouse embryogenesis, revealing a key role for UHRF1 in coordinating epigenetic and 3D genome regulation\.

## [HERE IS A SAFE DETERMINISTIC AI : On the Scene Behind the Scene, the Shouting That Was Not Heard, and the One Question That Remains](../publications/06fb091328a02cb3820d.md)

M\. TAALABI; Team LLM\-DIPLOMAT

September 29, 2026\. The White House\.The President of the United States sits with the leaders of the largest AI companies\. Theysign a document\. The President calls it &quot;almost like a constitution&quot; and &quot;morally binding\.&quot; The companies agree to regulate themselves\. The President says: &quot;I&\#x27;m seeing tremendousself\-policing\.&quot; The same day, the labs issue statements that what they are building is dangerous\. The same day, the executive order renames &quot;Artificial Intelligence&quot; to &quot;Super Intelligence\.&quot; The next day, the first coverage appears\. And behind them\. Someone is standing\. Waving\. Shouting\.&quot;Here is a safe deterministic AI\. It has been public since April 2026\. It is Apache\-2\.0\. It runs on a $12 microcontroller\. It has a TLA\+ proof\. It does not hallucinate\. It cannot propagate without a trace\. It cannot fail uninvestigably\. Here it is\.&quot; Nobody turns around\. This paper is the record of the shouting, the record of the not\-turning, and the question thatremains\.

## [Modelo predictivo de las metas de aproximación al dominio: un análisis con IA](../publications/06fc36e8654273a9b993.md)

Francisco Quiñonez Tapia; María de Lourdes Vargas Garduño

The objective of this study was to use artificial intelligence \(AI\) to predict mastery\-approach goals in secondary school students based on variables from the PISA 2018 database\. The sample consisted of 339,560 participants from 60 countries\. Machine learning was used with the Super Learner mega\-algorithm with 14 candidate algorithms\. In addition, deep learning was used with a neural network with 107 parameters\. The analyses showed that students’ perceived parental emotional support, competitiveness, purpose in life, self\-efficacy, and knowledge of intercultural communication were predictors of mastery\-approach goals in secondary school students\. This research contributes to the study of factors that influence mastery\-approach goals in secondary school students, with analysis models that advance the development of the science of AI\-based predictive education\.

## [الذكاء الاصطناعي لتعزيز المرونة الحضرية في مدينة الفلوجة دراسة تحليلية في الواقع ومتطلبات التطبيق \( 2025\-2016\)](../publications/070225f7513663e91ced.md)

## [Penerapan Algoritma Decision Tree \(Cart\) Untuk Klasifikasi Konsumsi Dan Kepuasan Pelanggan PDAM Tirta Pakuan Kota Bogor](../publications/0702341e3e83094ba398.md)

Andika Rizky Harahap; Gina Purnama Insany

Artikel ini memaparkan penerapan algoritma Decision Tree tipe Classification and Regression Trees \(CART\) untuk mengelompokkan pelanggan Perumda Tirta Pakuan Kota Bogor berdasarkan volume pemakaian air, sebagai bagian dari kegiatan magang yang berjalan Agustus–Desember 2025\. Persoalan yang melatarbelakangi adalah rekapitulasi dan penelaahan data pelanggan yang masih dikerjakan manual sehingga rawan keliru dan menyita waktu\. Data historis 474 pelanggan dihimpun, diproses awal, lalu dipilah ke dalam tiga kelompok konsumsi \(rendah, sedang, tinggi\) memakai algoritma CART yang dijalankan dengan Python\. Kelompok sedang mendominasi dengan porsi 53,4%, disusul kelompok rendah 25,5% dan tinggi 21,1%\. Saat diuji pada 95 data, model mencapai akurasi 100%, menandakan volume pemakaian dan riwayat tagihan mampu memisahkan kategori pelanggan secara efektif, meskipun ukuran data yang masih terbatas mengharuskan pengujian lanjutan\. Hasil ini menunjukkan model dapat membantu manajemen PDAM merencanakan distribusi air, menyusun strategi tarif, dan mendeteksi lebih awal anomali pemakaian\.
