A qualitative approach with a case study design was used in the implementation of this research, involving the main subjects: religious education teachers, mosque administrators, and sixth\-grade students\. Data collection was carried out through the application of participatory observation techniques, in\-depth interviews, and review of documentation of various religious activities\. The results of the study indicate that this collaboration does not occur incidentally, but rather takes the form of institutional, structured, and integrative through the optimization of three dimensions of the mosque: management of idarah, imarah, and maintenance of ri&\#x27;ayah\. Religious education teachers consistently play a role as conceptors and pedagogical companions who implement structured habituation strategies from the preparation stage of purification to the implementation of dhikr\. The research conclusion confirms that religious character is effectively formed through the process of observation, imitation of social behavior models, and direct experience involvement in the school ecosystem\.

## [E\-Government Maturity Analysis: Realizing Advanced and Adaptive Digital Transformation of the Central Java Provincial Government](../publications/08c70925ddbb46844698.md)

Muhammad Nurul Huda; Muhammad Samsuri; Azzahra Novita Rahma; Titin Purwaningsih; Mohammad Jafar Loilatu

This research aims to evaluate the maturity level of e\-government in the Central Java Provincial Government using a maturity model adapted to the local context\. The e\-government maturity model developed consists of four main dimensions: technology, organization, environment, and economy\. This maturity model divides the maturity levels into five levels: initial, developing, defined, managed, and optimizing\. The method used in this study is a qualitative approach, collecting primary data through interviews with policymakers and validating it using secondary data sourced from official government documents and other reliable sources\. The research results show that overall, the level of e\-government maturity in Central Java is at level 4 \(managed\), which means the e\-government system of the Central Java Provincial Government is fully integrated across services and well\-managed\. Despite significant progress, there are still areas requiring immediate improvement, such as ICT infrastructure, human resource development, and community participation\. This research recommends that local governments continue to expand the equitable distribution of ICT infrastructure to rural and remote areas, strengthen measurable human resource training programs to improve employee technical skills, and implement educational programs to increase community participation in e\-participation platforms to support more advanced and adaptive e\-government sustainability in the future\.

## [Helping Clients Regulate Emotions and Develop Effective Coping Skills](../publications/08c7315337c738b32a3f.md)

Derek J\. Lee

Helping Clients Regulate Emotions and Develop Effective Coping Skills is a step\-by\-step clinical guide to understanding emotion regulation, developing tools to measure and monitor emotion regulation, and creating individualized and personalized coping tools for clients\. The book explores and explains concepts that are often discussed, but rarely defined, and it teaches techniques that are currently not published\. The chapters outline a model for defining mood and consistent scaling that can be used as a treatment tool, providing direction for care and measurables that can be included in clinical notes and for insurance purposes\. This book also provides a step\-by\-step framework that clinicians can use to teach clients how to regulate their emotions and utilize their natural support systems\. Counselors, social workers, psychologists, therapists, and other professionals will come away from this workbook with a deep understanding of what coping is and why it is effective\. They’ll also develop a toolbox of techniques that they can use for helping clients develop their own coping skills\.

## [Physics\-guided data\-driven learning with active learning for slope stability analysis considering spatial variability](../publications/08d4843b34cd448a67be.md)

Xitailang Cao; Ren Jianxi; Miao Dong; Shan Lin; Hongwei Guo; Hong Zheng

The spatial variability of soil properties significantly affects slope stability and failure mechanisms, introducing uncertainties in the factor of safety \( F s \), deformation responses, and critical slip surfaces \(CSS\)\. Traditional Monte Carlo\-based random field methods are computationally expensive, while passive sampling\-based machine learning models often suffer from inefficient data utilization\. This study develops a physics\-guided data\-driven learning framework with active learning \(PGDAL\) for spatially variable slope stability analysis\. The framework integrates MNMM\-based high\-fidelity simulations, active learning\-based sample selection, and CNN/U\-Net surrogate models\. Spatially varying soil properties are represented as image\-based inputs, while F s , displacement fields, strain fields, and CSS information obtained from MNMM simulations are used as learning targets\. Four query strategies, including LCUS, margin sampling, entropy sampling, and maximum standard deviation sampling, are compared to evaluate their effects on model performance\. The proposed framework enables multi\-response prediction by learning the nonlinear relationship between random field inputs and slope responses, and further identifies smooth CSS through predicted deformation fields\. Results demonstrate that PGDAL achieves higher prediction accuracy and faster convergence than passive sampling while requiring fewer high\-fidelity samples\. The proposed framework provides an efficient surrogate modeling approach for intelligent slope stability analysis considering spatial variability\.

## [Hazards monitoring in confined spaces: a comprehensive review, trends, challenges, and future directions](../publications/08da86783002380e3703.md)

Rogério Antônio Casagrande; Cristian Cechinel; Roberto Muñoz

Confined spaces account for a significant portion of occupational fatalities worldwide due to their inherent atmospheric hazards and limited access for emergency response\. This paper proposes a comprehensive systematic review of the literature on remote monitoring of confined spaces to enhance worker safety from atmospheric hazards\. It highlights the use of the PRISMA methodology to examine studies employing wireless technology to prevent occupational deaths\. The paper identifies confined\-space hazards such as flammable or toxic gases and low oxygen levels\. The review analyzed 146 studies from the past 10 years, with 32 meeting the inclusion criteria for in\-depth analysis\. Findings indicate that industries like mining, oil and gas, and civil construction have invested heavily in safety technologies, including wireless sensor networks for monitoring, big data for storage, and machine learning to improve decision\-making\. However, many other sectors still need to adopt real\-time monitoring technologies to reduce work\-related accidents\. The results present risk management strategies for confined spaces, including training, regulations, and technology investments tailored to specific operational areas and confined\-space types\. Additionally, the review emphasizes that atmospheric hazards in confined spaces require greater attention to reduce fatalities, given the complexity and diversity of gases present\. Implementing risk management techniques in confined spaces is essential to prevent serious injuries and deaths, expanding mitigation efforts beyond atmospheric hazards to include physical, biological, and ergonomic risks\.

## [Structured Data Preprocessing Techniques for a Multilingual Healthcare Dataset in Machine Learning Applications](../publications/08dc330ed60926f6d14b.md)

Choo‐Yee Ting; Md\. Abu Nishan; Chih\-Yang Pee; Helmi Zakariah; Thanh\-Trung Nguyen

Data preprocessing is a foundational stage in any machine learning \(ML\) workflow, especially when dealing with complex, multilingual, and real\-world healthcare datasets\. The quality, consistency, and structure of input data strongly influence the accuracy, fairness, and interpretability of predictive models\. This paper presents a comprehensive and structured preprocessing framework designed for a large multilingual healthcare dataset containing 19,536 patient records with 67 features encompassing demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic information\. The framework systematically addresses data heterogeneity, linguistic diversity, and structural inconsistencies through multiple stages of cleaning and transformation\. The preprocessing process includes translation of Malay text into English to ensure linguistic uniformity, standardized handling of missing values using transparent placeholders, and column splitting of composite attributes to improve granularity and feature representation\. Outlier detection was performed using statistical approaches such as Interquartile Range \(IQR\) and Z\-Score methods to identify and remove extreme or erroneous values, thereby improving data integrity and model stability\. Furthermore, categorical variables were converted into numerical form using one\-hot encoding, ensuring compatibility with diverse ML algorithms while preventing artificial ordering and bias\. An experimental evaluation using a Random Forest classifier demonstrated that these preprocessing techniques substantially enhanced predictive performance\. Model accuracy improved from 72\.4% to 86\.7%, while the area under the curve \(AUC\) increased from 0\.78 to 0\.92, indicating more robust classification and generalization\. The resulting dataset is cleaner, more consistent, and better suited for downstream ML applications\. Overall, this study provides a reproducible and practical framework for managing multilingual healthcare data, underscoring that systematic preprocessing is not merely a preliminary task but a critical foundation for building reliable, transparent, and interpretable machine learning solutions in healthcare and other data\-intensive domains\.

## [Taşkın Potansiyelinin Belirlenmesinde Temel Bileşen Analizi Destekli Morfometrik Bir Yaklaşım: Şiro Çayı Havzası Örneği \(Pütürge/Malatya, Türkiye\)](../publications/08dea2bd88b4b497fafb.md)

Fatih Ocak; Serkan Gürgöze

Taşkınlar, küresel ölçekte ciddi kayıplara yol açan önemli hidrometeorolojik tehlikeler arasında yer almaktadır\. Bu nedenle taşkın riskinin olası zararlarını azaltabilmek amacıyla taşkın potansiyelinin belirlenmesine yönelik analizler büyük önem taşımaktadır\. Bu çalışmanın amacı, Malatya Pütürge’deki Şiro Çayı Havzası&\#x27;nda yer alan 15 alt havzanın \(AH\) taşkın potansiyelini morfometrik analizler ile Coğrafi Bilgi Sistemleri \(CBS\) tabanlı Normalize Morfometrik Taşkın İndeksi \(NMFI\) ve Temel Bileşen Analizi \(PCA\) yöntemleri kullanılarak belirlemektir\. Bu kapsamda 5 m çözünürlüklü Dijital Yükseklik Modeli \(DEM\) kullanılarak alt havzaların çizgisel, alansal ve rölyef özelliklerini temsil eden 16 adet morfometrik gösterge hesaplanmış ve daha objektif olması için parametreler NMFI yöntemiyle normalize edilmiştir\. Normalize edilen parametreler arasında korelasyon kurulmuş ve taşkın potansiyelini temsil eden baskın değişkenleri belirlemek amacıyla PCA uygulanmıştır\. NMFI ve PCA yöntemleriyle belirlenen taşkın potansiyeli, alt havzalarda genellikle benzer sınıfsal dağılımlar göstermiştir\. Her iki yöntemde de AH\-4, AH\-5, AH\-13, AH\-14 ve AH\-15 alt havzaları yüksek rölyef özellikleri, iyi gelişmiş drenaj ağı ve kısa akış süresi nedeniyle yüksek taşkın potansiyeli sınıfında; AH\-6, AH\-8, AH\-9, AH\-10 ve AH\-12 alt havzaları ise daha dengeli morfometrik özelliklere sahip oldukları için orta düzey taşkın potansiyeli sınıfında yer almıştır\. Çalışma sonuçları morfometrik analiz temelli yaklaşımların çeşitli yöntemlerle entegre edilmesinin havzaların taşkın potansiyelinin belirlenmesinde etkili bir yöntem olduğunu göstermektedir\.

## [Stimulus over expertise: what governs clinical visual attention in early health\-vocational students](../publications/08e5de64dff8d4717951.md)

Burcu Yüksel; Begüm Çapa Tayyare; Nurullah Eryılmaz

Introduction Eye tracking is increasingly used to investigate how health\-profession students allocate visual attention to clinically critical regions of diagnostic and therapeutic images\. However, whether disciplinary training produces a perceptual advantage for images within students&\#x27; own fields remains unclear\. This study examined whether students preferentially attended to critical regions in images from their own discipline compared with those from an unfamiliar discipline\. Methods A within\-stimulus 2 × 2 mixed design was employed involving 34 Medical Laboratory Techniques \(MLT\) students and 29 Occupational Therapy \(OT\) students\. Participants viewed clinical images from both disciplines while their eye movements were recorded\. Within each image set, own\-discipline and visiting viewers were compared on attention to predefined critical regions and related fixation and timing measures\. The potential predictive roles of academic standing and cognitive and learning\-style variables were also examined\. Results No consistent own\-discipline advantage was observed across the eye\-tracking measures\. Attention to critical regions did not favour students from the corresponding discipline in either image set, and statistically significant differences, where observed, favoured visiting rather than own\-discipline viewers\. In contrast, image identity consistently exerted a substantial effect on visual attention across all conditions\. Neither academic standing nor cognitive or learning\-style variables predicted attention to critical regions\. Discussion The findings challenge the assumption that enrolment in a health\-profession programme necessarily confers discipline\-specific perceptual expertise\. Instead, visual attention appears to be influenced more strongly by stimulus characteristics than by disciplinary background at this stage of training\. These results suggest that discipline\-specific perceptual expertise may develop through accumulated, deliberate clinical exposure rather than through programme enrolment alone\.

## [Atopic Dermatitis in the Era of Exposome and Artificial Intelligence](../publications/08ecb9c18ff5ecca9595.md)

Sara Manti; Federica Li Pomi; Luca Gammeri; Francesco Borgia; Giuseppe Murdaca; Sebastiano Gangemi

Atopic dermatitis \(AD\) is a heterogeneous, relapsing inflammatory skin disease in which epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, microbial imbalance, genetics, and the environment interact continuously over time\. Although a substantial body of literature has linked AD with air pollution, weather, allergens, stress, infections, sleep disturbance, skin care practices and microbial perturbation, most studies have assessed single exposures in isolation\. This reductionist approach only partially reflects the real\-world biology of AD, where patients experience dynamic combinations of external and internal exposures whose effects are non\-linear, cumulative and modified by age, phenotype, treatment and susceptibility\. The exposome paradigm offers a broader conceptual lens by considering the totality of exposures over the life course\. However, exposomic research in AD is methodologically challenging because the data are multimodal, high\-dimensional, time\-dependent, and often incomplete\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) can help address this complexity by integrating heterogeneous data layers, modelling temporal dependencies, discovering latent patterns, and generating individualized predictions\. This narrative review examines current evidence and proposes a theoretical framework that integrates AI and the exposome in AD\. We define the principal domains of the AD exposome, describe a multilevel analytical architecture spanning environmental, clinical, behavioural, microbiome, and multi\-omics data\. We distinguish applications evaluated in AD studies from exploratory analyses and proposed objectives: prediction of annual flare burden remains exploratory, whereas exposome\-informed short\-term flare alerts are proposed applications\. Although selected AI applications have been evaluated in AD, the added predictive value of exposure data and the clinical utility of a fully integrated exposome–AI system remain to be established\. We also outline key methodological and translational priorities, including exposure assessment, temporality, treatment\-confounding, interpretability, fairness, data governance, and external validation\. The proposed framework offers a structured basis for future research, with clinical translation dependent on prospective validation and evidence of benefit to patient care\.

## [Characterization of KPC\-287 conferring high\-level ceftazidime–avibactam resistance in an ST11\-KL64 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate](../publications/08fa3c2bea23465807ce.md)

Yue Gong; Yanlei Shen; Junru Lu; Yan Li; Shangshang Qin; Xiufang Shi; Xin Tian

Background Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major global public health threat because of its increasing antimicrobial resistance and capacity for dissemination\. Ceftazidime\-avibactam \(CAZ/AVI\) is a key therapeutic option for infections caused by KPC\-producing Enterobacterales , but emerging KPC variants compromises its efficacy\. Here, we characterized multidrug\-resistant K\. pneumoniae isolate KP22\-83 and investigated the contribution of KPC\-287 to antimicrobial resistance, bacterial fitness, and virulence\. Methods KP22\-83 was characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole\-genome sequencing, resistance and virulence gene annotation, KPC phylogenetic analysis, and structural analysis\. The bla KPC\-287 gene was cloned into pUC19 and introduced into Escherichia coli DH5α and K\. pneumoniae ATCC 13883 for functional validation\. Growth, motility, in vitro competition, and biofilm formation assays were performed to evaluate fitness\-associated phenotypes associated with KPC\-287 carriage\. The transferability and retention of bla KPC\-287 were examined by conjugation assay and serial passage with or without CAZ/AVI\. Virulence was evaluated using a Galleria mellonella infection model\. Results KP22\-83 belonged to ST11\-KL64 and exhibited multidrug\-resistance\. Whole\-genome sequencing identified bla KPC\-287 together with 11 additional antimicrobial resistance\-associated genes and 34 virulence\-associated genes\. KPC\-287 clustered close to KPC\-155 and differed by P168Q and A242del while retaining a highly conserved predicted global fold\. Introduction of pUC19\-KPC\-287 increased the CAZ/AVI MIC to 64/4 mg/L in both E\. coli DH5α and K\. pneumoniae ATCC 13883, demonstrating that bla KPC\-287 conferred high\-level CAZ/AVI resistance\. In contrast, meropenem MICs were not substantially altered\. KPC\-287 carriage caused modest reductions in growth, motility, and competitive fitness, together with greater crystal violet\-stained biofilm biomass than the corresponding empty\-vector controls\. The bla KPC\-287 was detected in transconjugants together with IncFII and IncR replicon markers and remained detectable after 30 passages with or without CAZ/AVI\. Furthermore, KP22\-83 caused substantial larval mortality, whereas KPC\-287 acquisition did not markedly affect virulence in K\. pneumoniae ATCC 13883\. Conclusion This study provides a systematic functional characterization of KPC\-287 in an ST11\-KL64 K\. pneumoniae clinical isolate in China\. KPC\-287 confers high\-level CAZ/AVI resistance with limited fitness cost and bla KPC\-287 is transferable in an IncFII/IncR plasmid background and remains detectable during serial passage\. These findings highlight the need for continuous genomic surveillance and functional characterization of emerging KPC variants\.

## [Kathy: Expert System for the Optimization of Nutritional Strategies in the Female Hormonal Regulation](../publications/08fbdfa51bd334078272.md)

Verónica López\-Marsico; Carolina Uesato; Antonio Quintero\-Rincón

Más del 26 % de la población mundial menstrúa sin una guía fiable para gestionar las fases hormonales del ciclo\. Este trabajo presenta a Kathy, un sistema experto de asesoramiento nutricional adaptado al ciclo menstrual femenino\. Implementado en SWI\-Prolog y Python, utiliza inferencia avanzada sobre una base de conocimiento estructurada dentro de una interfaz conversacional basada en consola\. La base de conocimiento contiene 164 hechos y 23 reglas lógicas específicas del dominio, basadas en la literatura científica, que formalizan las cuatro fases del ciclo menstrual \(menstrual, folicular, ovulatoria y lútea\) y generan recomendaciones personalizadas basadas en la evidencia\. El sistema se describe mediante autómatas finitos y una máquina de Turing abstracta, lo que permite analizar su complejidad computacional\. Kathy mejora el acceso al conocimiento basado en la evidencia para optimizar las estrategias de apoyo alineadas con los ciclos fisiológicos naturales del cuerpo femenino, un campo que tradicionalmente ha dependido de costosas consultas profesionales\. Los experimentos demuestran una mayor eficiencia algorítmica, con tiempos de respuesta que van desde los 2,3 ms para consultas directas hasta los 123,8 ms para la optimización multiobjetivo compleja\. El sistema alcanza una precisión del 95 % en el contexto de recomendaciones de carácter básico y del 88 % en la fase de optimización heurística integral\.

## [Temporally Correlated Stochastic Spiking Neural Networks Enabled by 2D Ferroelectric Synapse‐Neuron Integration](../publications/0903691bde01f34cf300.md)

Hanseo Jeon; Ui Do Ji; Sangmin Lee; Sangmin Lee; Gihyeon Bhin; Chang Yong Park; Ji‐Sang Park; Byung Chul Jang; Sungjoo Lee; Sungjoo Lee

ABSTRACT Stochastic neural computation is essential for probabilistic inference and brain‐inspired information processing\. However, most hardware stochastic neurons generate statistically independent spikes and fail to reproduce the temporal correlations observed in biological neurons\. We demonstrate an integrated hardware synapse‐neuron consisting of a FeFET synapse and a CulnP 2 S 6 neuron, where the neuron exhibits temporally correlated stochastic spiking\. The spike probability is continuously tuned by synaptic weight through voltage modulation, enabling hardware stochastic neural computation\. Electrical measurements reveal voltage‐dependent stochastic firing accompanied by leaky‐integration‐firing dynamics\. Structural and polarization analyses reveal differences in Cu‐related atomic contrast and partially retained polarization states, suggesting a history‐dependent internal state\. Autocorrelation and inter‐spike interval analyses reveal temporal dependencies between successive stochastic spikes, which are consistent with the evolution of this retained state, with the strongest correlation emerging in the intermediate stochastic regime\. The proposed stochastic spiking neural network achieves an inference accuracy of approximately 90% and maintains over 87% accuracy under severe noise conditions, demonstrating the computational advantages of temporally correlated stochastic spiking for robust probabilistic neural computation\. This work demonstrates a class of 2D ferroelectric neuromorphic hardware that inherently incorporates intrinsic temporal dynamics, providing a pathway toward next‐generation neuromorphic and probabilistic computing\.

## [Economic impacts of subsea cable deployment](../publications/090d04277cc545352fa2.md)

Wolfgang Briglauer; Raúl Katz; Monika Köppl\-Turyna; Juan Jung

This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of the economic impact of submarine cable \(SMC\) infrastructure, which is critical for global digital connectivity and carries almost all intercontinental data traffic\. Despite their fundamental role in the digital economy, robust evidence on the economic returns of SMC investments is very scarce\. To address this, we use a panel dataset of developed countries and causal identification strategies, such as two\-way fixed effects models and instrumental variables exploiting exogenous variation from factors like a country&\#x27;s coastline length and legacy market competition\. In our empirical analysis we first describe how international bandwidth \(IBW\) can be used as a proxy for SMC capacity and examine how it affects domestic broadband quality levels\. We then quantify the impact on broadband demand, finding distinct yet robust demand elasticities for mobile and fixed services\. We find that a 1% increase in IBW drives an increase in mobile broadband adoption between 0\.049% and 0\.081%, while the increase for fixed broadband adoption ranges between 0\.056% and 0\.061%\. Finally, we translate these estimates into a simple cost\-benefit framework using an illustrative transatlantic cable project connecting Ireland and the United States\. This analysis shows that the substantial GDP spillovers overwhelmingly exceed the total private deployment costs\. Our findings affirm that SMC deployments generate significant positive externalities and high social returns\. While it has been argued in the previous literature that these effects are critical to developing nations lacking infrastructure, our findings indicate this effect is also applicable to advanced economies\. Consequently, we argue that policymakers in coastal nations, regardless of their level of development, have a strong economic incentive to facilitate private investment by reducing regulatory barriers and transaction costs associated with, for example, cable permits and landing stations\.

## [Associations Between Conventional Breast MRI Signal Characteristics and Immunohistochemical Biomarkers in Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Exploratory Study](../publications/090d109d918cad158428.md)

Uğurcan Balyemez; Sinan Akay; Hatice Tuba Sanal; Mustafa Taşar

BACKGROUND/AIMS:This study investigates whether quantitative magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\)\-derived signal measurements are associated with immunohistochemical biomarkers in breast cancer, extending beyond morphological assessment to signal\-based imaging characteristics\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:The study retrospectively included 63 patients with 66 breast cancer lesions, selected from an initial cohort of 415 patients based on specific inclusion criteria\.MRI scans were performed using a standardized protocol, and quantitative MRI signal measurements were extracted and analysed\.Histopathological data\-including estrogen receptor \(ER\), progesterone receptor, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 status, and Ki\-67 proliferation index\-were also evaluated\.Statistical analyses, including correlation and regression tests, were conducted to assess associations between MRI features and immunohistochemical biomarkers\.RESULTS: Weak associations were observed between pre\-contrast T1 signal intensity \(SI\) and ER expression, and between T2 SI and the Ki\-67 proliferation index \(Spearman&\#x27;s ρ=\-0\.17 and 0\.25, respectively\); neither remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons nor after adjustment for within\-patient lesion clustering\.A more robust positive association was observed between the initial enhancement ratio \(IER\) and Ki\-67 \(ρ=0\.39,95% confidence interval: 0\.16\-0\.57,p=0\.001\), which remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction \(corrected p=0\.016\) and in both a single\-lesion\-per\-patient sensitivity analysis and a cluster\-robust regression\. CONCLUSION:The association between IER and Ki\-67 remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons and after accounting for within\-patient lesion clustering, suggesting that it may represent a comparatively robust exploratory imaging correlate of tumor proliferation\.Associations involving T1 SI and T2 SI were weak and did not survive correction\.These findings are preliminary and hypothesisgenerating, underscoring the need for further studies with larger datasets to clarify the clinical relevance of quantitative MRI analysis in breast cancer evaluation\.

It also considers issues of increasing the effectiveness of language learning through the use of innovative methods and information technologies in the educational process\.

## [Artificial intelligence and machine learning in contemporary neuroeconomics: Data analysis and modeling of economic behavior](../publications/09226efd40f95f676995.md)

Maxim V\. Fedorov; Ольга Юрьевна Клевцова; Сергей Александрович Игнатьев

Aim\. To systematize contemporary understandings of neuroeconomics as an interdisciplinary field of research, and to determine the role of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning technologies in analyzing economic behavior based on a comparison of international and Russian studies\. Objectives\. To trace the genesis and key theoretical models of neuroeconomics; to characterize the state and specifics of neuroeconomic research by Russian scholars; to systematize the main research directions on individual, social, and financial economic behavior conducted by international authors; to examine the forms of AI application both as a data analysis tool and as an independent computational model of decision\-making; to compare the degree of maturity and institutional support of the areas under consideration\. Methods\. A qualitative comparative\-analytical review of peer\-reviewed international and Russian research on neuroeconomics, computational neuroscience, behavioral economics, and the application of AI in the analysis of economic behavior is employed\. The sources were selected by the authors according to their relevance to three thematic blocks: theoretical and methodological foundations of neuroeconomics, empirical studies of the neural mechanisms of choice, and works on the application of machine learning to the analysis and modeling of economic behavior\. The comparison of international and Russian directions is conducted according to the criteria of theoretical foundation, empirical methods, and the degree of integration of AI and machine learning\. Resul ts It is established that neuroeconomics is emerging as an independent discipline that explains decision\-making through the interaction of automatic and controlled neural processes\. International researchers take into account social preferences and financial behavior, while Russian authors focus predominantly on social influence, conformity, rehabilitation neurotechnologies, and are still weakly integrated into economic theory\. The dual role of AI as a data analysis tool and a computational model of choice is demonstrated, and the ethical frameworks for the application of neurotechnologies and AI in economic research are examined \. Conclusions\. Neuroeconomics represents a mature interdisciplinary field with a pronounced asymmetry between international and Russian research in terms of integration into economic theory\. AI enhances the analytical capabilities of neuroeconomics but requires methodological caution and institutional ethical regulation\. A promising direction for development is the creation in Russia of specialized interdisciplinary programs that combine economics, neuroscience, and data analysis

## [Marketing misinformation in the age of AI](../publications/092ad73211f8d501dd31.md)

Gita Venkataramani Johar; Amna Kirmani

Abstract We shine a spotlight on marketing misinformation—claims about products and brands that contradict or distort verifiable facts\. Misinformation may be created unintentionally or intentionally by companies, competitors, customers, or third parties seeking to harm companies or consumers\. We focus on the role of AI in creating, obfuscating, and disseminating misinformation in the form of text, audio, images, and videos generated using large language models\. This type of information can pose a substantial risk for brand safety\. Consumers may be aware that AI can generate misinformation but may lack the ability to guard against it\. We discuss how different stakeholders in the information ecosystem can help in the prevention and correction of misinformation and propose a future research agenda in this critical and fast‐growing area\.

## [Tracking crop evapotranspiration and water stress across seasons using multi\-sensor UAV observations](../publications/092de35a046ab53511e0.md)

Jordan Bates; Carsten Montzka; Harry Vereecken; François Jonard

Abstract\. Field\-scale estimation of evapotranspiration \(ET\) using high\-resolution data supports water conservation and yield optimization by enabling localized water use monitoring and early detection of crop stress\. This study applies the Priestley–Taylor Two\-Source Energy Balance \(TSEB\-PT\) model at 15 cm resolution using unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\) data over a 10\-hectare field across three seasons: sugar beet \(2021\), potato \(2022\), and winter wheat \(2023\)\. Key inputs included thermal infrared \(TIR\) for land surface temperature \(LST\), multispectral \(MS\) and LiDAR data for canopy characterization, and a fusion of MS derived green area index \(GAI\) and LiDAR derived plant area index \(PAI\) to derive the fraction of green LAI \(fg\)\. Model outputs were validated against eddy covariance \(EC\) flux data using footprint modeling\. Results showed high sensitivity to LST, emphasizing the importance of accurate thermal calibration\. While both GAI and PAI provided comparable LAI inputs during peak growth, GAI better captured functional canopy decline during stress and senescence, especially in winter wheat, where dense structure led to cooling effects unrelated to transpiration\. Dynamic fg improved ET accuracy across all crops, particularly under declining canopy function\. Overall, TSEB\-PT showed strong agreement with EC measurements \(RMSE = 0\.14 mm/h, R² = 0\.49; R² = 0\.81 excluding senescence\)\. UAV TIR based ET maps also revealed early stress signals prior to changes in MS or LiDAR based metrics\. This study demonstrates the value of integrating very\-high\-resolution UAV data with the TSEB\-PT model for multi\-crop and season\-long ET monitoring and early stress detection\.

## [Open\-vocabulary Object Detection for Open\-pit Mining Equipment: A Case Study of Prompt Formulation, Model Scale and Object Size Effects on Zero\-shot Accuracy](../publications/0938118b689776551140.md)

Refka Ghodhbani; Taoufik Saidani

Camera\-based detection in mines depends on site\-specific annotation\.Open\-vocabulary detectors take class names as text at inference time and could remove this step\.This case study evaluates seven text\-prompted detectors from four families on one open\-pit machinery collection of 171 images and seven classes, prompted with class names, mining vocabulary or descriptive phrases, with bootstrap confidence intervals on the principal results\.The best zeroshot configuration, OWLv2 with plain class names, reaches 21\.9% AP50, against 57\.9% for a YOLO11s detector finetuned on 111 images and selected on a separate validation split\.Descriptive phrases lower AP50 by up to 13\.2 points\.With one prompt per class, mining terms score clearly below plain names for three detectors and level with them for the two Grounding DINO models\.Larger checkpoints give no consistent gain\.Most errors confuse machine types, and about fourteen annotated images match the best zero\-shot result\.

## [A Literature\-calibrated Digital Twin\-inspired Framework for Secure and Predictable IoT Smart Homes](../publications/09393a4430b61330040c.md)

Ibtehal Shakir Mahmoud; H A Abdulkareem

Smart homes are expected to be reliable, secure, and predictable at once, yet most existing systems address these goals in isolation\.This paper introduces a literature\-calibrated, digital\-twin\-inspired simulation framework that integrates network behaviour, biometric authentication, and failure prediction within one environment\.Rather than assuming independent device failures, the framework models failures as a consequence of a slowly varying networkhealth state, allowing a leakage\-controlled classifier trained only on pre\-execution signals to achieve moderate predictive discrimination\.The framework&\#x27;s automatic retry mechanism raises the full system&\#x27;s mean command success rate to 96\.2% \(mean network\-command latency 110\.9 ms, reported alongside the closest published figures for context\); a separate resource\-constrained ablation isolates the risk scores&\#x27; specific contribution, showing that risk\-guided retry allocation preserves 90\.7% success under a matched \~50% retry budget, versus 88\.4% for random allocation\.A STRIDE threat model with CVSS scoring assigns low or very low modelled residual risk to five of six identified threats, leaving traffic analysis as a medium residual risk\.Ablation experiments show retry is the dominant driver of reliability, with risk\-guided prediction adding further benefit once retry capacity is constrained\.

## [A Dual‐Excitation Light‐Harvesting System Based on a Flexible Silicon Composite Containing Ca 2 Sr\(PO 4 \) 2 : Ce 3\+ , Sm 3\+ , Designed for Multimodal Anti‐Counterfeiting and Secure Information Encryption](../publications/094510707e83ea78f3cb.md)

Marek Adaszyński; Kacper Adamczak; Dagmara Stefańska

ABSTRACT Advanced anti‐counterfeiting technologies require luminescent materials capable of generating dynamic and difficult‐to‐reproduce optical responses\. The research focuses on a dual‐excitation light‐harvesting system based on flexible silicone composites containing Ca 2 Sr\(PO 4 \) 2 : Ce 3\+ , Sm 3\+ phosphors, designed for multimodal anti‐counterfeiting protection and secure information encryption The co‐doped phosphate exhibits excitation‐dependent emission resulting from efficient Ce 3\+ → Sm 3\+ energy transfer and multisite occupation of dopant ions, enabling tunable luminescence under different excitation wavelengths\. Temperature‐dependent studies additionally reveal a phonon‐assisted energy transfer process leading to enhancement of Sm 3\+ emission\. The combination of excitation‐ and temperature‐controlled luminescence enables reversible color switching and generation of complex optical signatures that are difficult to counterfeit\. As a proof of concept, the phosphor is incorporated into a flexible silicone security label displaying distinct emission patterns observable using a simple UV source and camera detection\. Furthermore, a novel encoding platform is proposed, enabling message encryption through the selection of material composition and controlled excitation conditions\. The developed dual‐excitation composite represents a promising strategy for next‐generation flexible anticounterfeiting systems, adaptive optical labels, and secure data encryption technologies\.

## [Defining the Clinical Indication for Real‐Time Artificial Intelligence–Assisted Ultrasound in Breast Lesions with Low Suspicion of Malignancy](../publications/0957cf44a8113c89013c.md)

Jeeyeon Lee; Bora Yang; Won Hwa Kim; Jaeil Kim; Ho Yong Park; Byeongju Kang; Joon Suk Moon; HAI LIN PARK

Objectives To evaluate whether real‐time artificial intelligence \(AI\) breast ultrasound \(US\) can identify a subgroup of breast imaging reporting and data system \(BI‐RADS\) category 4A lesions without suspicious mammographic \(MMG\) findings in whom unnecessary biopsy may be safely avoided\. Methods This retrospective analysis of single‐center biopsy registry included 641 consecutive US BI‐RADS 4A lesions that underwent vacuum‐assisted breast biopsy\. Before conducting biopsy, the lesions were reassessed using a real‐time AI US system \(CadAI‐B®\), and MMG findings were classified as suspicious or non‐suspicious based on formal reports\. Seven prespecified biopsy‐decision strategies were evaluated, including 3 AI‐only strategies, 3 mammography‐gated AI strategies, and the current standard strategy of biopsy all BI‐RADS 4A lesions\. The primary outcomes were biopsy reduction rate, missed cancers, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy, with final pathology as the reference standard\. Results Among 641 cases of US BI‐RADS 4A lesions, 26 cases of malignancies \(4\.1%\) were identified, including 14 cases of ductal carcinoma in situ \(DCIS\), 11 cases of invasive ductal carcinomas, and 1 case of apocrine carcinoma\. AI reassigned 289 cases of lesions \(45\.1%\) to BI‐RADS categories 1–3\. AI‐only biopsy‐deferral strategies missed 30\.8% and 38\.5% of malignancies when biopsy was deferred for AI BI‐RADS ≤2 and ≤3 lesions, respectively, with DCIS accounting for most missed cancers\. In contrast, among lesions without suspicious MMG findings, no malignancies were observed in AI BI‐RADS 1–3 lesions\. The sequential strategy of deferring biopsy only for lesions with AI BI‐RADS ≤3 and non‐suspicious MMG findings reduced biopsies by 43\.5% \(279/641\) while maintaining 100\.0% sensitivity \(95% CI, 87\.1–100\.0%\) and increasing specificity to 45\.4% \(95% CI, 41\.4–49\.4%\)\. Conclusion Real‐time AI breast US alone could not safely support biopsy deferral in US BI‐RADS 4A lesions\. However, after suspicious MMG findings had been excluded, AI identified a low‐risk subgroup in whom unnecessary biopsy could be substantially reduced without compromising cancer detection\. These findings suggest that the clinical utility of real‐time AI breast US lies in patients without suspicious MMG findings\. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation\.

## [Automated Inventory Management and Quality Assessment of Ornamental Nursery Crops Using End\-to\-End Deep Learning](../publications/0958841b6bced329cd02.md)

Hamid Habib Syed; Faraz Ahmad; Md\. Hasibur Rahman; Mohtasim Hadi Rafi; Jeremy Pickens; Tariq Rehman

Abstract Purpose Ornamental crop production is a rapidly developing sector of US agriculture\. Accurate inventory management and quality assessment are critical tasks for monitoring sales, yield, space requirements, production timing, and quality improvements of ornamental nurseries\. Current inventory practices rely on manual counting, which is labor\-intensive and often inaccurate\. This study develops an automated system for plant counting and quality assessment of container nursery stock\. Methods An unmanned teleoperated ground vehicle, “NurseryBot,” was developed for plant counting and quality assessment of container nursery stock\. The NurseryBot utilized RGB cameras to collect video data from a downward\-facing perspective\. A deep learning framework based on YOLOv11 model variants was trained and tested on a panoramic dataset to detect and segment plants efficiently\. Cross\-species knowledge adaptation approaches were explored to improve segmentation generalization\. Morphological parameters, including area, perimeter, eccentricity, and circularity, were extracted to systematically evaluate plant quality using image\-based parameters\. Results The YOLOv11\-m instance segmentation model showed the highest precision, recall, and counting accuracy among the evaluated variants for plant detection and segmentation\. For bounding boxes, the model attained precision, recall, and mAP50 values of 0\.971, 0\.970, and 0\.941 for azalea and 0\.968, 0\.966, and 0\.915 for sunshine, respectively\. For mask segmentation, the model achieved precision, recall, and mAP50 values of 0\.969, 0\.968, and 0\.901 for azalea and 0\.967, 0\.966, and 0\.907 for sunshine, respectively\. The proposed system achieved counting accuracies of 95\.59% for azalea plants and 95\.37% for sunshine plants\. Conclusions This study demonstrates an end\-to\-end robotic and deep learning\-based system for automated inventory counting and plant quality assessment in container nurseries\. The proposed approach provides an accurate alternative to manual inventory practices under the nursery conditions evaluated in this study\. This technology provides growers and researchers with an efficient way to accurately maintain inventory counts and assess plant quality\.

## [Physics\-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real\-Time Edge Inference](../publications/095ed2123891e867cce0.md)

Vlad Alexandru Sănduleac; Shahariya Rasheed Rayamarakkarveettil Puthanpurayil; Noman Khan; Remus Teodorescu

Grid foundation models \(GridFMs\) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power\-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver\. Their size, however, targets data\-centre inference, whereas low\-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor \(PMU\) reporting frame\. We distil a 20\.1M\-parameter, 12\-layer GridFM teacher into a 0\.62M\-parameter, 6\-layer student, a $32\.5\\times$ parameter reduction at half the message\-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power\-flow loss with output, physics\-residual, latent\-state and attention transfer\. The physics\-residual term, which matches the teacher&\#x27;s power\-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power\-grid graphs\. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118\-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional \(synchronous\) generators are replaced by inverter\-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive\-power limits \(IEEE 1547\), giving $97\\,529$ physically valid \(AC\-OPF\-feasible\) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately\. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\\%$ on active\-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive\-power dispatch\. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term\. The physics\-residual term, in the layer\-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus\-level residual field\. The resulting student is $32\.5\\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message\-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge\-device benchmarking\.

## [Pemanfaatan Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif dalam Meningkatkan Produktivitas Belajar Mahasiswa Program Studi Bisnis Digital](../publications/096272018cc167a699fd.md)

Amelia Putri utami; Yadi Maryadi

Perkembangan teknologi digital telah mendorong pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) dalam berbagai aspek kehidupan, termasuk dunia pendidikan\. Berbagai aplikasi seperti ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, dan Claude mulai dimanfaatkan mahasiswa sebagai pendukung proses pembelajaran, mulai dari mencari referensi, memahami materi perkuliahan, menyusun ide, hingga membantu penyelesaian tugas akademik\. Di Program Studi Bisnis Digital, penguasaan teknologi digital menjadi salah satu kompetensi utama yang harus dimiliki mahasiswa agar mampu beradaptasi dengan perkembangan dunia bisnis berbasis teknologi\. Oleh karena itu, pemanfaatan GenAI menjadi topik yang penting untuk dikaji\. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran Generative Artificial Intelligence dalam meningkatkan produktivitas belajar mahasiswa Program Studi Bisnis Digital melalui pendekatan studi literatur\. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi literatur dengan mengkaji berbagai jurnal ilmiah, prosiding, dan publikasi akademik yang membahas penerapan Generative AI dalam pendidikan tinggi\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa GenAI mampu meningkatkan efisiensi proses belajar, mempercepat pencarian informasi, membantu pengembangan ide, meningkatkan kreativitas, serta mendukung pembelajaran mandiri\. Namun demikian, penggunaan GenAI juga menghadirkan tantangan berupa ketergantungan teknologi, potensi penyalahgunaan dalam penyelesaian tugas akademik, serta isu etika dan integritas akademik\. Berdasarkan hasil kajian, pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence perlu diimbangi dengan kemampuan berpikir kritis, literasi digital, dan etika akademik agar teknologi tersebut dapat dimanfaatkan secara optimal sebagai pendukung proses pembelajaran tanpa mengurangi kualitas kompetensi mahasiswa\.

## [POTENCIAL TERAPÊUTICO ANTIDEPRESSIVO DO ÓLEO DE CANNABIS SATIVA DE ESPECTRO COMPLETO EM MODELOS ANIMAIS](../publications/096a9d83ec15ed8293bf.md)

Marina Kipper; MAIQUELI EDUARDA DAMA MINGOTI; Maria Franciely Paz Araújo Albuquerque; Joana Perardt; Camila Ferreira Puntel; ÉRIC GABRIEL SERPA BRUNHARA; Luiz Martins Freitas da Silva; Catharine Bomfim Santos; CLENEIDE PICININ WEBLER PICININ WEBLER; Zuleide Maria Ign´acio

O Transtorno Depressivo Maior pode estar relacionado a situações de estresse vividas no início da vida, que também podem interferir na resposta aos antidepressivos\. O estudo avaliou o potencial terapêutico do óleo de Cannabis sativa de espectro completo em ratos Wistar machos submetidos à privação maternal e ao isolamento social\. Foram utilizados 40 animais, divididos em quatro grupos: controle, estresse, estresse tratado com escitalopram \(10 mg/kg\) e estresse tratado com óleo de espectro completo \(1 mg/kg\)\. Após os protocolos de estresse e 14 dias de tratamento, os animais foram avaliados nos testes de campo aberto e natação forçada\. Não foram observadas alterações significativas na atividade locomotora e exploratória\. No teste de natação forçada, os animais submetidos ao estresse apresentaram maior tempo de imobilidade\. O escitalopram reduziu significativamente esse comportamento\. O óleo de espectro completo também apresentou redução na média de imobilidade, porém sem diferença estatisticamente significativa\. Assim, nas condições avaliadas, não foi possível confirmar efeito tipo antidepressivo significativo do óleo\.

## [Intellektual texnologiyalar sharoitida sanoat klasterlarida logistik infratuzilmani rivojlantirishning iqtisodiy ahamiyati](../publications/097999fad00a30fb001f.md)

## [LIBERO\-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation](../publications/0979e7e5e265ef51edf6.md)

Zhixu Li; Keqian Tang; Litian Gong; Jingyu Yao; Wenqian Zhang; Tianze Xu; Zehao Wang; Yuping Wang; Junge Zhang; Jiachen Li

Personalization is essential for general\-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality\. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation \(PeRM\) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction\. We introduce LIBERO\-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents\. LIBERO\-PeRM studies five questions: 1\) how policies follow preferences in zero\-shot settings; 2\) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3\) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4\) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5\) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts\. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user\-profile choices\. This formulation is restricted to language\-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks\. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences\. We create five task suites \(312 tasks\) with high\-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference\-satisfaction metrics\. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero\-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable\. Mixed training achieves better no\-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference\-only training, but can weaken motion\-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult\. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero\-perm\.github\.io/\.

## [CF\-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test\-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets](../publications/097c7aa24f836b828aca.md)

Sabarish G; Deepak Parashar

Automated fundus\-based diabetic retinopathy \(DR\) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source\-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations\. Existing test\-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams\. These mechanisms can reinforce confidently incorrect predictions and break down when clinical images arrive independently\. We introduce CF\-NODE, a novel counterfactual test\-time adaptation framework for cross\- domain DR grading\. Instead of trusting prediction confidence or estimating a target distribution, CF\-NODE asks how each prediction responds under a controlled intervention on the evidence supporting it\. CF\-NODE ranks internal spatial nodes using model\-derived attention, feature magnitude, and node\-set similarity, progressively attenuates the highest\-ranked nodes, and uses the stability of the resulting expected\-grade response to apply a bounded calibration of the predicted grade distribution\. The framework is fully frozen and adapts every image independently using only geometric views and a fixed source\-derived prior, requiring no target\-derived information or model updates\. We evaluate CF\-NODE on five external DR datasets under repeated\-seed evaluation against TENT, EATA, SAR, and T3A\. CF\-NODE outperforms all four methods with statistically significant improvements over the second\-best method, improves AUC on every target domain, and attains the highest average AUC and macro\-F1, delivering stronger grade discrimination together with more balanced recognition across DR severity levels\. These results demonstrate that counterfactual intervention sensitivity provides consistent and deployment\-ready domain robustness for single\-image clinical inference\.

## [Comparative evaluation of regulatory framework of european union and India for its possible application in tanzania for medical devices](../publications/0980ed4673cc9088eb4b.md)

Shivani Jani

Medical devices are essential components of contemporary health systems, but their safety, performance and availability depend on an effective regulatory system operating throughout the product life cycle\. Regulatory approaches differ across jurisdictions according to national legislation, institutional capacity, risk classification, conformity assessment arrangements and post\-market surveillance mechanisms\. This review compares the current regulatory frameworks for medical devices in the European Union \(EU\) and India and examines their possible relevance to Tanzania\. The analysis uses current legislation, regulatory guidance and official information from the European Commission, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization \(CDSCO\), the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority \(TMDA\) and the World Health Organization \(WHO\)\. The EU framework is based principally on Regulation \(EU\) 2017/745 on medical devices \(MDR\) and Regulation \(EU\) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices \(IVDR\), while India regulates medical devices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Medical Devices Rules, 2017\. Tanzania regulates medical devices through TMDA under the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Act, Cap\. 219 and associated regulations and guidelines\. All three systems use risk\-based concepts, although the classes, regulatory pathways and conformity assessment mechanisms are not identical\. Tanzania already has a structured framework, including risk classification, registration or notification, quality\-system requirements, post\-market surveillance and online regulatory processes\. The principal opportunity is therefore not to replicate another jurisdiction, but to strengthen implementation through risk\-proportionate review, regulatory reliance, technical capacity, digital information systems, post\-market surveillance and stakeholder coordination\. The comparison provides a basis for practical, context\-sensitive recommendations for strengthening Tanzania’s medical device regulatory system\.

## [Del grafiti urbano a la animación digital: evolución de una expresión visual contemporánea](../publications/0985ec4babc56aba3c6d.md)

José Said Arceo Arias; Francisco Jesús Kantún Hernández; Johrel Cuevas Moreno; Francisco Manuel Pool Rosado

El grafiti se consolidó como un medio de expresión artística dentro del espacio urbano y atravesó diversos contextos sociales\. Surgió como una manifestación visual asociada a la protesta, la identidad y la apropiación del espacio público\. El presente artículo tuvo como objetivo analizar sus orígenes, su evolución histórica y su adaptación a los recursos digitales contemporáneos, así como examinar su incorporación en la animación digital y los medios audiovisuales\. Se planteó como hipótesis que el grafiti logró reinventarse sin perder su carácter crítico al integrarse a nuevas plataformas tecnológicas\. La investigación se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cualitativo, mediante revisión documental y análisis de literatura sobre arte urbano y en medios digitales como videojuegos o películas\. Resultados de la investigación indican que la digitalización ha ampliado su alcance, lo que fortaleció su visibilidad global y diversificar sus formatos expresivos\. Esto mismo permitió que nuevas formas de representarse se crearán para el grafiti sin desvincular la esencia urbana\. Contrastando con investigaciones previas que lo situaban únicamente como práctica marginal, la información indica su consolidación como lenguaje visual legítimo dentro de la cultura contemporánea\. Se concluye que el grafiti ha sabido adaptarse a los cambios tecnológicos sin perder su función expresiva y crítica\.

## [Ritmos cerebrais, fadiga cognitiva e desempenho operacional em missões espaciais de longa duração: indicadores eletroencefalográficos e implicações neuroéticas](../publications/098696a6eb6f381f960b.md)

Marina Corrêa Freitas; Michele Aparecida Cerqueira

Introdução: Missões espaciais de longa duração combinam microgravidade, isolamento, confinamento, alterações do ciclo claro\-escuro, carga de trabalho e maior autonomia operacional, fatores que podem modificar o sono, a atividade elétrica cerebral e o desempenho cognitivo\. Objetivo: Analisar as evidências sobre ritmos cerebrais e indicadores eletroencefalográficos associados à fadiga cognitiva e ao desempenho de astronautas, discutindo as limitações técnicas e as implicações neuroéticas do monitoramento de neurodados em voo\. Método: Realizou\-se revisão integrativa, com busca estruturada em PubMed/MEDLINE e ScienceDirect, complementada por rastreamento de referências e documentos institucionais\. O processo de seleção foi apresentado conforme as etapas de identificação, triagem, elegibilidade e inclusão do PRISMA 2020\. Quinze publicações compuseram a síntese qualitativa\. Resultados: Os estudos identificaram alterações de potência e conectividade nas bandas alfa, beta e teta, mudanças em potenciais relacionados a eventos e associações entre sono insuficiente, estresse, lentificação cognitiva e desempenho visuoespacial\. Entretanto, pequenas amostras, artefatos, heterogeneidade analítica e baixa especificidade impedem que um único parâmetro de eletroencefalograma \(EEG\) seja considerado biomarcador operacional validado\. Conclusões: O EEG apresenta potencial como componente de sistemas multimodais e personalizados de vigilância neurocognitiva, desde que os resultados sejam interpretados por profissionais, associados a medidas comportamentais e fisiológicas e submetidos a regras de consentimento, privacidade mental, limitação de finalidade, segurança cibernética e revisão humana\.

## [Implementasi Sistem Monitoring Kualitas Udara Pada Dinas Komunikasi Informatika Dan Statistik Lampung](../publications/098c7b2ce194f40a3323.md)

Ni Made Deni Arini; Retno Dwi Handayani

Kualitas udara dalam ruangan merupakan faktor penting yang mempengaruhi kesehatan dan produktivitas kerja, namun monitoring masih banyak dilakukan secara manual dan belum realtime\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengimplementasikan sistem monitoring kualitas udara berbasis Internet of Things \(IoT\) yang terintegrasi dengan website\. Sistem menggunakan ESP8266 NodeMCU dengan sensor DHT11, MQ\-135, dan GP2Y1010AU0F untuk mengukur suhu, kelembaban,respon gas, dan partikulat debu\. Data dikirim ke Firebase Realtime Database dan ditampilkan pada dashboard web dashboard\. Hasil pengujian transmisi menunjukkan rata\-rata delay sebesar 1,9 detik \(\)\. Pengujian kalibrasi relatif pada 990 data sampel secara kuantitatif terbukti meningkatkan kestabilan pembacaan sensor dengan menekan rentang data ekstrem pada suhu \(dari 11,40 °C menjadi 2,70 °C\), kelembaban \(dari 59,00% menjadi 15,00%\), gas \(dari 11,62 menjadi 3,30\), dan debu \(dari 92,52 menjadi 35,20\)\. Visualisasi grafik dan penyimpanan data historis memfasilitasi analisis fluktuasi lingkungan kerja di Ruang Rapat DISKOMINFOTIK Provinsi Lampung\. Dengan demikian, sistem ini efektif mendukung pemantauan kualitas udara secara realtime dan responsif\.

## [Food additives at the intersection of food safety, freshness, and human health: a comprehensive review](../publications/099fd90e1e5bdf69f2f2.md)

Mikru Belachew; Mesenbet Kassa; Eshetie Erku; Desye Teferi; Desalew Ayalew

Food additives are vital tools in the modern global food supply chain to ensure microbiological safety, enhance shelf life and maintain sensory attributes\. But the rising consumption of highly processed foods has raised concerns about the long\-term physiological impact of prolonged exposure to chemicals\. Critical gaps in cumulative risk assessments are identified by analysing the regulatory frameworks of the European Food Safety Authority and the Food and Drug Administration\. The goal of this review is to focus on the paradigm shift toward clean\-label alternatives, offering a roadmap for balancing technological necessity with consumer health longevity\. The review’s results support the current dual paradigms of food additives’ unquestionable efficacy in reducing foodborne pathogens and chemical degradation, in contrast to recent clinical and preclinical data linking specific synthetic agents to metabolic disruption, systemic inflammation, and gut microbiota symbiosis\.

## [Aspiration\-line pressure stability in Venturi and peristaltic pump configurations during phacoemulsification: an in vitro study](../publications/09b05d2c6436475cb248.md)

Tomoyuki Kunishige; Hisaharu Suzuki; Fumiki Okamoto

This in vitro study descriptively evaluated aspiration\-line pressure waveforms between Venturi and peristaltic pump configurations and their associated tubing systems using two Stellaris systems and a KITARO artificial anterior chamber model\. VAC200 and VAC400 represented 200\- and 400\-mm Hg vacuum settings in the Venturi configuration and vacuum limits in the peristaltic configuration, with peristaltic flow settings of 20 and 35 mL/min, respectively\. Pressure was recorded at 0\.1\-s intervals and analyzed during the stable 30\- to 50\-s period after activation\. Only one continuous run was performed per condition\. Reported standard deviations \(SDs\) represent within\-run temporal fluctuation, not between\-run variability\. Mean pressure, SD, and transient fluctuations of 10 mm Hg or greater were evaluated\. At VAC200, mean pressure was − 10\.40 ± 0\.53 mm Hg in the Venturi configuration and 11\.02 ± 2\.99 mm Hg in the peristaltic configuration\. At VAC400, values were − 70\.90 ± 1\.06 and − 50\.97 ± 2\.54 mm Hg, respectively\. Descriptive analysis suggested greater pressure fluctuation in the peristaltic configuration at both settings\. Intermittent transient fluctuations of 10 mm Hg or greater occurred only in P\-VAC400\. These findings describe aspiration\-line pressure waveforms under the tested in vitro conditions\.

## [THE EFFECT OF STUDY HABITS AND DISCIPLINE ON ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION LEARNING OUTCOMES \(SURVEY OF STUDENTS OF SDN GANDARIA UTARA 03 SOUTH JAKARTA\)](../publications/09b95328403b57132241.md)

Muhammad Ma’mun; Nur Irsyadiah; Madian Muhammad Muchlis

The background of this study stems from the anomalous fluctuations in student grades, which consistently remain below the minimum completion standard, despite the school reporting a very high level of attendance discipline and assignment completion routines\. This research aims to evaluate and measure the magnitude of the partial and simultaneous influence of study habits and discipline variables on the achievement of final learning outcomes in Islamic Religious Education\. The researcher designed an empirical quantitative approach through a correlational survey method on a representative sample of 35 upper\-grade students at SDN Gandaria Utara 03, South Jakarta\. Field metric data collection utilized a closed\-ended Likert\-scale questionnaire instrument and documentation of academic grade reporting\. The researcher then analyzed the data using multiple linear regression testing techniques based on statistical software programs\. Quantitative data processing revealed empirical findings that the study habits and discipline variables simultaneously failed to have a significant impact on student academic achievement, recording a significance value of 0\.958\. The multiple regression analysis recorded a very low coefficient of determination, at only 0\.3%\. The research conclusion clearly declares the collapse of the conventional paradigm that glorifies compliance with physical regulations as a guarantee of high academic intelligence in students\.

## [AI content detection in student text assignments, false positive rates, and academic integrity](../publications/09c812b3ba75b95e9f02.md)

Mohammad Reza Maghami; Chin Kuan Ho; Camilleri Patrick

Universities increasingly use AI content detection tools to identify student assignments potentially produced by generative AI, yet concerns remain regarding their reliability and false\-positive classification of human\-written work\. This systematic review examines the causes, consequences, and mitigation of false\-positive AI detection in academic contexts\. The review covers literature published between 2020 and 2026 and includes 90 eligible studies, comprising 81 Scopus\-indexed publications and nine studies identified through Google Scholar\. Bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer was combined with Structural Topic Modelling to examine keyword relationships, latent research themes, and temporal development, while qualitative synthesis identified major causes, impacts, and mitigation strategies\. The findings reveal three broader themes concerning academic integrity and student assessment, plagiarism and responsible AI governance, and detection accuracy, reliability, and false positives\. False\-positive outcomes vary substantially across tools and evaluation settings, limiting direct quantitative comparison\. Major contributing factors include algorithmic and language bias, limited contextual understanding, surface\-level linguistic features, and insufficiently diverse training data\. The evidence further highlights risks to assessment fairness, student confidence, and institutional decision\-making\. Effective responses therefore require transparent detection practices, human review, AI literacy, clear institutional policies, and accessible appeal procedures\.

## [ABC transporter genetic polymorphisms in cancer therapy: implications for anticancer drug disposition, efficacy, and toxicity](../publications/09cbdac48a29913d8aaf.md)

Christine Barrett; Marina Gálvez‐Peralta

Introduction Pharmacogenetics has emerged as an important component of precision medicine in oncology\. Although clinical implementation has primarily focused on established biomarkers, such as DPYD, UGT1A1, TPMT, and NUDT15, data suggests that genetic variations in ATP\-binding cassette \(ABC\) drug transporters may also affect the disposition and clinical effects of anticancer therapies\. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the contribution of ABCB1, ABCC1, and ABCG2 polymorphisms to anticancer therapy’s efficacy and toxicity\. Methods and Materials A narrative review of the published pharmacogenetic and pharmacokinetic literature was conducted, focusing on studies evaluating germline polymorphisms in ABC transporter genes and their associations with anticancer drug disposition, treatment efficacy, and adverse events\. Results ABC transporter polymorphisms have been associated with clinically relevant variability in anticancer drug efficacy and toxicity\. The effects of variants in ABCB1 , particularly C1236T, G2677 T/A, and C3435T, on taxane\- and anthracycline\-induced toxicity and treatment response have been extensively studied\. ABCC1 variants have been associated with vincristine\-induced peripheral neuropathy and with hematologic, gastrointestinal, hepatic, and cardiac toxicities following anthracyclines and other chemotherapy regimens\. ABCG2 polymorphisms, particularly C421A, have demonstrated associations with drug exposure and toxicity for selected tyrosine kinase inhibitors, among other therapies\. Conclusion Variations in ABC transporter genes represent a potentially important factor that contributes to variability in anticancer drug response and toxicity\. Our heterogeneous findings emphasize that transporter\-mediated drug disposition is multifactorial; therefore, future research should prioritize the use of polygenic models that integrate pharmacogenomics with other tumor\- and patient\-specific factors to better understand the relationship between ABC transporter polymorphisms and anticancer drugs, and how these genetic variants affect drug efficacy and toxicity\.

## [ZAMONAVIY ADABIYOTDA INSON VA SUN&\#x27;IY INTELLEKT MUNOSABATI TALQINI](../publications/09e2cd09d0609598e28a.md)

Анализируется, почему произведение называют первым узбекским интеллектуальным триллером\. ## [Technology\-Based Innovations and Tax Compliance in Nigeria](../publications/09eda46655e2b0a9c0e3.md)

Edu Uju Juliet; Joseph O\. Udoayang; Dorathy C\. Akpan; Sunday Asukwo Okpo

The inadequacies in Nigeria&\#x27;s traditional tax administration system have posed significant challenges to tax revenue generation, including inefficiencies, corruption, and lack of transparency, ultimately resulting in low tax revenue generation\. This study was therefore conducted to examine the effect of that technology\-based innovations on tax compliance cum revenue generation in Nigeria\. The study was anchored on four technology\-based innovation variables, namely, e payment of taxes, e\-processing of VAT returns, e\-filing of PAYE returns and e\-personal assessment\. The study adopted descriptive survey research design, while data were obtained through questionnaires administered to selected personnel of the Federal Inland Revenue Service now known as the Nigerian Revenue Service and relevant tax practitioners\. Out of one hundred and fifty \(150\) questionnaires administered, one hundred and forty\-four \(144\) respondents correctly completed and returned for analysis\. Descriptive statistics, model summary, analysis of variance and multiple regression analysis were employed for analysis with the aid of SPSS\. The findings revealed that, e\-payment of taxes, e\-processing of VAT returns, e\-filing of PAYE returns and e\-personal assessment had positive and significant relationships with tax revenue generation in Nigeria\. The study concluded that technology\-based innovations jointly enhance tax compliance and tax revenue generation in Nigeria\. It was recommended that the Nigerian Revenue Service should strengthen digital tax platforms, improve user support and awareness, expand secure e\-payment channels, automate VAT and PAYE return processing and simplify electronic personal assessment systems in order to improve voluntary compliance and revenue collection\.

## [Admission\-time prediction of 7\-day mortality in clinician\-attributed hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage: development and external validation against the ICH score](../publications/09eeb1a83772f1a181a6.md)

Qingwen Chen; Tao Zhong; Jian Liu; Dawei Feng; Han Gao

Early mortality after intracerebral haemorrhage remains difficult to estimate at admission\. We developed models for recorded mortality within 7 days after admission in two retrospective cohorts of clinician\-attributed hypertensive intracerebral haemorrhage\. Qingyuan records \( n = 1,433; 369 events\) were used for grouped nested cross\-validation, and Yunfu records \( n = 924; 182 events\) for external validation\. The models used 28 admission\-time predictors\. Predictions were averaged across 20 imputation\-specific pipelines\. Elastic\-net logistic regression was selected from the development data\. Its development and external areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0\.848 and 0\.893, respectively\. In external validation, the ICH score had an area under the curve of 0\.860, giving a difference of 0\.0324 \(95% CI 0\.0126–0\.0523; DeLong P = 0\.00135\)\. The external Brier score was 0\.103, with a calibration intercept of − 0\.504 and slope of 1\.149\. At the development\-selected threshold of 0\.1976, sensitivity was 0\.901 and specificity was 0\.706\. The model modestly improved discrimination over the ICH score, but overprediction, differences between centres, and unavailable treatment and outcome\-ascertainment details limit clinical interpretation\.

## [Rutin interferes with hnRNP L phase separation and modulates the PKM2–lactate–H3K9la axis in pulmonary fibrosis](../publications/09f21acf687fed91e655.md)

Jianlin Luan; Yi Wang; Mengqi Jiang; Haitong Zhang; Changjun Lv; Jinjin Zhang; Xiaodong Song

Background Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic and progressive lung disease with limited treatment options; it is urgent to develop new drugs\. Purpose This study investigated the anti\-pulmonary fibrosis effects and mechanism of rutin, and sought to provide a potential lead compound for further development of anti\-pulmonary fibrosis agents\. Methods The anti\-pulmonary fibrosis effect of rutin was assessed using Cell Counting Kit\-8 \(CCK\-8\), real\-time cell proliferation analysis and scratch wound healing assay in Transforming Growth Factor\-β1\(TGF\-β1\)\-stimulated Medical Research Council cell strain\-5 \(MRC\-5\) cells, along with lung function tests, MicroCT imaging, Hematoxylin and Eosin \(H&amp;E\) and Masson staining in mice with induced pulmonary fibrosis\. The mechanism of rutin was explored through molecular docking, the surface plasmon resonance assay, the cell thermal shift assay \(CETSA\), droplet formation observation, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, transcriptome sequencing, Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay \(ELISA\), Co\-immunoprecipitation \(Co\-IP\) and Chromatin Immunoprecipitation\-Polymerase Chain Reaction \(ChIP\-PCR\)\. Results Rutin inhibited fibroblast\-to\-myofibroblast differentiation, myofibroblast proliferation and migration, and extracellular matrix deposition\. Moreover, rutin effectively improved lung function, including forced vital capacity, dynamic lung compliance and total lung capacity\. Additionally, rutin markedly alleviated fibrotic features, such as honeycomb lung reduction, preserved alveolar structure and thinned alveolar walls\. Mechanistically, our data support a model in which rutin may interfere with hnRNP L phase separation, and this interference is associated with reduced PKM2 generation, decreased lactate production and subsequent loss of H3K9la\. The reduced H3K9la, in turn, correlated with suppressed PKM2 transcription, suggesting a self\-limiting regulatory circuit\. Conclusion Our findings suggest that rutin may interfere with the regulatory interplay involving hnRNP L phase separation, PKM2 alternative splicing, lactate, and H3K9la, which is associated with the attenuation of pulmonary fibrosis\. While these data reveal a potential mechanistic framework, definitive causality at each step of this regulatory axis remains to be established\. Further studies are warranted to validate this model and to optimize the bioavailability of rutin for therapeutic application\.
