## [Primary tracheal lymphoepithelioma\-like carcinoma in a young non\-smoking male: a case report highlighting the diagnostic value of flow\-volume loop](../publications/0a102af8572384ea6ce7.md)

Shan Xiao; Sida Chen; Jintao Ou; Yan Shen

Background Primary tracheal lymphoepithelioma\-like carcinoma \(LELC\) is an extremely rare malignancy \(&lt;2% of tracheal tumors\) strongly associated with Epstein–Barr virus\. Tracheal tumors can mimic asthma due to dynamic airway obstruction, often leading to diagnostic delay\. The flow\-volume loop provides critical clues to central airway obstruction but is frequently overlooked\. Case Presentation We report a 30\-year\-old non\-smoking male initially misdiagnosed with asthma, whose refractoriness to inhaled corticosteroids prompted spirometry\. The flow\-volume loop revealed a plateau pattern in both inspiratory and expiratory limbs, consistent with fixed upper airway obstruction which guided chest computed tomography \(CT\) and bronchoscopy to identify a tracheal polypoid mass\. Pathological examination confirmed LELC with positive EBV\-encoded small RNAs \(EBER\) in situ hybridization\. The patient underwent endoscopic resection followed by video\-assisted thoracoscopic surgery \(VATS\) tracheal resection\-anastomosis with lymphadenectomy\. Postoperative pulmonary function testing at 1\-year follow\-up demonstrated complete normalization of the flow\-volume loop morphology, with FEV 1 \(Forced expiratory volume in 1 s\) improved from 0\.91L to 3\.62L\(\+298%\) and PEF \(peak expiratory flow\) from 2\.03L/s to 6\.76 L/s \(\+233%\)\. The patient remained asymptomatic without recurrence at 1\-year follow\-up\. Conclusion This case underscores that, in young patients with asthma\-like symptoms refractory to conventional therapy, flow\-volume loop analysis should not be deferred, as it can unmask central airway obstruction and expedite the diagnosis of rare tracheal malignancies\.

## [Data, Artificial Intelligence and Content as Levers of Sales Growth in Digital Marketing](../publications/0a153bdadd4633d2fc23.md)

Tais Fraile; Thiago Anderson Lira Clemente

Abstract: The availability of customer data, the advance of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and the growing importance of digital content and influencers have changed the tools that firms can use to increase sales\. This narrative review examines how these three levers—data and analytics, AI\-enabled personalization, and content and influencer marketing—contribute to sales growth, and under which conditions they generate results\. Peer\-reviewed studies and reference works published up to 2023 were analyzed qualitatively\. The literature indicates that marketing analytics improves decisions on targeting, pricing and resource allocation; that AI supports personalization at scale, from mechanical automation to analytical and feeling\-oriented applications; and that content and influencer marketing build engagement, trust and purchase intention when they are relevant and credible\. Generative AI, which gained prominence in 2023, expands content production and customer interaction capabilities but also raises concerns regarding accuracy, transparency and ethics\. The review concludes that these levers produce the greatest effect when combined in an integrated system in which data informs content and personalization, and results are measured and fed back into decisions\. It also emphasizes that privacy, trust and human judgment remain essential conditions for sustainable sales growth\.

## [Mesoscopic learning dynamics of extensive\-width neural networks](../publications/0a1ff6d6877a7eaef437.md)

Shu Zhou; Jean Barbier; Sebastian Goldt

Understanding how stochastic gradient descent learns internal representations in wide neural networks trained on rich target functions is a central problem in machine learning\. We study this question in two\-layer neural networks learning target functions represented by networks of the same architecture, with arbitrary nonlinearity, and with network width and input dimension growing proportionally\. In this regime, standard approaches for describing the learning dynamics require tracking a diverging number of overlaps, which measure correlations between learned and target features, leaving no obvious description in terms of a few order parameters\. Here, we develop a mesoscopic description of learning by characterizing the distribution of overlaps\. In the early stages of learning, we find that a Gaussian description of overlap statistics reduces the learning dynamics to a few collective variables that track learning of the target function&\#x27;s linear and quadratic components\. We then estimate the timescale of specialization, when Gaussian closure breaks down and individual learned features begin to strongly correlate with specific target features\. We find that specialization in extensive\-rank networks is accelerated via a quadratic shielding mechanism, whereby learning the linear and quadratic components of the target function filters gradient fluctuations\. We finally describe how the activation function determines the pattern of specialization and characterize the subsequent refinement of learned features\. Together, these results show how collective learning gives way to individual feature discovery and clarify when learning in large neural networks admits a simple statistical description\.

## [CIIR \- Class\-Indexed Interface Representation Learning](../publications/0a26b55057c317121244.md)

Doo Yon Kim; Christian Wallraven

Multimodal learning commonly assumes paired or synchronized observations, yet independently collected datasets rarely provide such correspondence\. We introduce CIIR, a modular encoder\-\-decoder framework that connects heterogeneous datasets through a class\-indexed address space while preserving each dataset&\#x27;s native input format and output module\. A known local index selects address $k$, and an input\-dependent 128\-dimensional address representation Z\_k\(x\) is written to that address\. To demonstrate CIIR, we learn this address space from handwritten digits, clothing images, spoken\-digit spectrograms, and hand signs without synchronized or instance\-matched samples\. Newly trained label\-free receivers recover the requested addresses with 94\.7% macro\-average Address Realization Accuracy\. We then attach the unseen SVHN dataset after freezing the base address space and train only lightweight adapters, achieving 90\.2% MNIST&gt;SVHN and 82\.3% SVHN&gt;MNIST end\-to\-end Address Transfer Accuracy without target\-side decoder labels\. To demonstrate generalizability of CIIR, we reuse the ten addresses as code elements in collision\-free arithmetic and hierarchical address codes for all 100 CIFAR\-100 classes and evaluate direct arithmetic\-code realization through the existing receivers\. These results establish CIIR as a compact interface for modular cross\-dataset communication and post\-hoc dataset attachment without exhaustive paired multimodal supervision\.

## [Gut microbiota in patients receiving dialysis: Mechanisms, complications and the road to personalized microbiome‑based care \(Review\)](../publications/0a33e87b0b9661d17681.md)

Chenxia Jin; Yanping Wang

Gut dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a potential contributor to poor outcomes in patients receiving dialysis, yet its mechanistic complexity and therapeutic implications remain incompletely understood in clinical practice\.The uremic environment, dietary restrictions, polypharmacy and dialysis modality\-specific factors collectively reshape the gut microbial ecology, promoting the overproduction of deleterious metabolites such as indoxyl sulfate, p\-cresyl sulfate and trimethylamine n\-oxide while depleting protective short\-chain fatty acids\.These alterations compromise intestinal barrier integrity, fuel systemic inflammation through endotoxemia and NOD\-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome activation and have been associated with cardiovascular disease, immune dysfunction, peritonitis, protein\-energy wasting and cognitive impairment\.although probiotic, prebiotic, synbiotic and dietary interventions show promise, heterogeneous responses across trials underscore the inadequacy of one\-size\-fits\-all strategies\.Multi\-omics profiling has revealed substantial interindividual variability in microbial composition and metabolic capacity, providing a rationale for personalized approaches\.The present review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms underlying dysbiosis and complications in patients receiving dialysis and proposes a roadmap toward personalized microbiome\-based care to improve clinical outcomes\.Contents 1\. introduction 2\. Drivers and landscape of gut dysbiosis in dialysis 3\. Pathophysiological mechanisms linking gut dysbiosis to systemic complications 4\. Major complications associated with gut dysbiosis in dialysis 5\. Therapeutic modulation of the gut microbiome in dialysis: current evidence 6\. Multi\-omics approaches to characterizing dysbiosis in dialysis 7\. Toward personalized microbiome\-based care in dialysis 8\. Future perspectives 9\. conclusions

## [From Technology to the Development of Competence \. AI as a resource of teaching English: A Review of University\-Level Foreign Language Instruction](../publications/0a37f300c4ff73343e77.md)

Ketty Zoraida Vergara Mendoza; Mariana Marisol Briones Zambrano

El rápido desarrollo de las herramientas de inteligencia artificial \(IA\) generativa, entre ellas los chatbots conversacionales, los sistemas de tutoría inteligente y las plataformas de evaluación automatizada de la escritura, ha transformado la manera en que se desarrollan las competencias comunicativas y lingüísticas en las aulas universitarias de lenguas extranjeras y segundas lenguas \(L2\)\. Este artículo revisa la literatura empírica y teórica reciente \(2023\-2026\), además presenta un resultado cuantitativo de 238 estudiantes sobre la enseñanza de lenguas mediada por IA y sitúa los hallazgos en el marco de los modelos de competencia comunicativa de Hymes \(1972\) y de Canale y Swain \(1980\)\. Las investigaciones muestran que los chatbots de IA pueden aumentar la disposición de los estudiantes a comunicarse y reducir la ansiedad al hablar en una lengua extranjera, y que la retroalimentación escrita generada por IA puede mejorar la precisión gramatical y los hábitos de revisión\. Sin embargo, las mejoras en la competencia lingüística no siempre se traducen en un mayor desarrollo de habilidades comunicativas o críticas de orden superior, y persisten preocupaciones relacionadas con la dependencia excesiva, la integridad académica y el acceso equitativo\. El artículo concluye con implicaciones pedagógicas que plantean la IA como un andamiaje, y no como un sustituto de la interacción mediada por el docente, así como con líneas para futuras investigaciones\.

## [From Me to We: The Pivotal Role of Self‐Determination Profiles in Cooperative Learning](../publications/0a3cf672d15deada324f.md)

Berna Yüner; Fulya Barış Pekmezci

ABSTRACT This study aims to identify different latent profiles based on psychological needs and examine their moderating role in the link between self‐regulation and cooperation\. The study sample consists of 560 undergraduate students from diverse class levels\. The Student Perceptions of Knowledge‐Building scale and the Activity‐Feeling States scale were used\. For the latent profiles, autonomy, competence, and relatedness were used, and two significantly different profiles named as The Achievers and The Connectors were determined\. The moderation analysis revealed that the Achievers profile significantly moderated the effect of self‐regulation on cooperative learning, while it is insignificant in the Connectors profile\. The results highlighted the critical role of self‐regulation on collaborative dynamics, serving as a vital prerequisite for effective group work\.

## [Journalism Transformation in the Digital Era: Data, Algorithms, and Audiences](../publications/0a4114d141b66ec646ae.md)

Haikha

Although digital journalism has received considerable scholarly attention, the relationships among data practices, audience metrics, algorithmic visibility, platform dependence, media power, and professional accountability remain insufficiently integrated\. This study examines how these dimensions interact in the transformation of digital journalism and their implications for journalistic quality and public responsibility\. Adopting a qualitative interpretive approach, the study draws on books, journal articles, and academic book chapters selected for their relevance, recency, and theoretical contribution\. Thematic analysis involved identifying key ideas, organizing them into four analytical dimensions, and synthesizing their interrelationships\. The findings indicate that digital technologies expand capacities for information gathering, analysis, and presentation, while audience metrics and algorithmic distribution shape news visibility and editorial priorities\. These processes intersect with platform dependence, commercial pressures, and media ownership structures, creating challenges for editorial independence and professional accountability\. By integrating these dimensions into a common analytical framework, the study advances an interconnected understanding of digital journalism\. It concludes that journalistic quality depends on critical interpretation of evidence, independent editorial judgment, and clear responsibility for published content\. The findings suggest that news organizations should use audience metrics as supporting information, critically evaluate data and AI\-assisted outputs, and maintain transparent editorial practices\. Further empirical research could examine how Indonesian newsrooms navigate these pressures across different organizational and ownership contexts\.

## [Towards Implementing Indicative Planning Methods in the Management of the Russian Economy](../publications/0a45b869a587c5ab230a.md)

Gligich\-Zolotareva V\. M\.

In the modern world, mixed forms of economic development planning – where economic coordination mechanisms incorporate elements of both market self\-regulation and state regulation – are increasingly common\. Indicative planning, which relies heavily on state programs for socio\-economic development, is one such transitional form\. In the Russian Federation, the entire system of state programs is geared toward achieving national goals, and a unified plan for their attainment has been approved\. To establish a management and monitoring system for this unified plan, integrate it into the public administration framework, and facilitate decision\-making based on monitoring results, the Government of the Russian Federation issued Decree No\. 761 on June 19, 2026\. This decree approved the Regulation on the management system for the unified plan to achieve the Russian Federation’s national development goals, as well as the plan’s functional management structure\. The document introduces several fundamental innovations to the domestic socio\-economic development planning system – discussed in this article – including: defining the unified plan’s management structure with clearly delineated functions, powers, and responsibilities for all participants; managing the plan \(formation, maintenance, updating, and monitoring\) in a digital format, including through the use of artificial intelligence; establishing procedures for managing operational and strategic risks, as well as incidents and issues regarding target achievement identified during implementation; assessing the plan’s implementation effectiveness; and fostering extensive inter\-agency and cross\-sectoral collaboration among participants, including state corporations, development institutions, and expert or other organizations\. The article concludes that this mechanism for implementing the unified plan can be viewed as an element of indicative planning for the Russian economy at both federal and regional levels\.

## [Response\-Informed Value Estimation for Cost\-Aware Multi\-Turn LLM Routing](../publications/0a48b03b836ecb656257.md)

Haotian Yan; Jiaqi Liu; Bingyi Jing; Tianjun Yao

Multi\-turn LLM routing selects a model at every turn before its response is available, yet task success is revealed only when the interaction ends, leaving each intermediate choice without a label of its own\. Logged trajectories, however, retain the response each call produced, which exposes what each turn required and how well the chosen model served it, evidence that outcomes alone hide\. We introduce RIVET \(Response\-Informed Value Estimation for Turn\-Level Routing\), which exploits this post\-call evidence during training while keeping routing strictly pre\-call at deployment\. RIVET jointly trains two value estimators over a shared state\-model representation: a deployable Routing Value Estimator that scores candidate models from pre\-call information, and a training\-only Response\-Informed Value Estimator that additionally observes the realized response\. Conditioning on the response turns response\-induced return variation from residual noise into an observed covariate, and we show that this reduces the leading asymptotic estimation error of the shared representation\. On the MINT benchmark, RIVET solves more held\-out tasks than the strongest multi\-turn baseline while using 74\.7% less total call cost\.

## [The Evolutionary Stress Framework: A Field Guide](../publications/0a4d3d0a868495f26923.md)

Lori Hogenkamp

The Evolutionary Stress Framework: A Field Guide provides a plain\-language map of the Evolutionary Stress Framework \(ESF\), a conceptual and research\-generating framework developed by Lori Hogenkamp at the Center for Adaptive Stress\. ESF examines health, disability, and neurodivergence as emergent patterns in interacting brain\-body\-environment systems rather than as isolated defects or single\-cause outcomes\. It brings together allostasis and allostatic load, predictive processing and interoception, neurodiversity, person\-environment fit, energy constraints, and complex\-systems science\. This Version 1\.0 record contains the canonical Field Guide and three public companion resources: the ESF Translation Map, the ESF Canonical Terminology and Boundary Map, and The 14 Core Claims of the Evolutionary Stress Framework\. Together, the materials explain what the framework is, how its disciplinary languages connect, what its central terms mean, and what propositions the framework commits itself to\. The Translation Map is supplied in PDF and PNG formats, and a ZIP archive contains the same five public files as a single downloadable package\. The guide distinguishes regulatory architecture, developmental calibration, and expressed profile; defines Regulatory Bandwidth as present coordinated regulatory capacity under perturbation; separates Regulatory Bandwidth from Regulatory Margin; and incorporates the published non\-scalar measurement analysis by treating capacity as a conditional perturbation\-response profile before scalarization\. It distinguishes established foundations, strong convergent support, ESF syntheses, active empirical hypotheses, and methodological implications, while reporting publication status separately\. Interactive companion: The ESF Rosetta Map is a living evidence architecture showing how interdisciplinary sources contribute to, support, constrain, refine, or challenge the framework: https://lorihogenkamp\-ops\.github\.io/esf\-rosetta\-map/ \(archived baseline: Zenodo DOI 10\.5281/zenodo\.23422797\) These materials are living public references\. Later revisions will be issued as new versions of this Zenodo record rather than silently replacing Version 1\.0\. Version 1\.0 has not been peer\-reviewed and is not medical advice, diagnostic guidance, or a validated clinical model\. AI language tools supported drafting, editing, figure development, and document preparation under the author&\#x27;s direction and review\. The author is responsible for the framing, claims, citations, and conclusions\. This document is part of the Evolutionary Stress Framework \(ESF\) public library of the Center for Adaptive Stress\.

## [A Hybrid EfficientNet\-B0 and Machine Learning Framework for Multi\-Class Retinal Disease Classification on RFMiD](../publications/0a52f46891be00d38949.md)

Md\. Alam Hossain; Paritosh Chandra Ray; Md\. Mehedi Hasan; Abdul Al Mahin; Ferdowsi Khatun

Automated analysis of retinal fundus images can support scalable screening, but multi\-disease classification remains difficult because retinal abnormalities may exhibit overlapping visual characteristics and clinically important classes are often underrepresented\. This paper investigates a four\-class retinal image classification framework using a strictly filtered subset of the Retinal Fundus Multi\-Disease Image Dataset \(RFMiD\)\. The considered classes are No\_Disease\_Risk, diabetic retinopathy, age\-related macular degeneration, and macular hole\. Images with multiple disease labels, unselected diseases, or inconsistent annotations were excluded, resulting in 855 training, 294 validation, and 305 test images\. Training data were balanced to 401 entries per class through sampling with replacement and stochastic augmentation\. A pretrained EfficientNet\-B0 with frozen parameters was used to extract a 1,280\-dimensional representation from each image\. Support vector machine, Random Forest, K\-nearest neighbors, XGBoost, and CatBoost classifiers were subsequently evaluated\. On the official test subset, CatBoost attained the highest accuracy of 0\.9016, weighted F1\-score of 0\.9022, and macro\-ROC\-AUC of 0\.9842\. SVM achieved the highest macro precision and macro F1\-score, at 0\.9075 and 0\.8628, respectively, while XGBoost produced the highest macro recall of 0\.8774\. Grad\-CAM visualizations were generated for selected test images to examine the retinal regions associated with the model predictions\. The results show that fixed deep representations can support effective retinal image classification with conventional learners, although the small number of unique ARMD samples limits the statistical reliability and generalizability of the findings\.

## [Reconstructing National Memory in the Digital Age: Documentary Film, Audionarratives and Digital Visual Art in Ukraine](../publications/0a556b1f5334883eb6ec.md)

Tetiana Hyrina; Alina Zadorozhnia; Lidiya Koval; Ангеліна Трегуб; Liudmyla Cherniavska\-Lomakina

The article examines the specifics of the transformation of Ukrainian national memory in the digital era from the perspective of documentary film, audio narratives and digital visual arts\. The aim of the study is to determine the role of digital cultural practices in the preservation, representation and actualization of historical experience, the formation of cultural identity, social consolidation and international representation of Ukraine\. The methodology is based on an interdisciplinary approach and combines methods of analysis and synthesis, comparative, systemic, content, discursive, visual and audiovisual analysis\. We demonstrate that digitalization transforms national memory from a mostly institutional model into a network, multimodal and participatory system, in which documentary, audio and visual formats serve complementary functions\. They become particularly relevant in the Russian\-Ukrainian war, as they enable quick documentation of events, preservation of personal testimonies, symbolic formulation of traumatic experience and its international communication\. The main risks of digital memory are identified: disinformation, decontextualization, platform dependence, privacy violations, and technological obsolescence\. The study emphasizes the need for systematic verification of digital materials, standardization of metadata, backups, open formats, and the creation of a reliable institutional framework for digital archiving\.

## [Rational structure\-guided identification of a Bcl\-2\-targeting peptide with antiproliferative effects on colorectal cancer cells](../publications/0a63385a526498dab5f1.md)

Xing Jin; Shudan Yang; Qianqian Wang; Shutong Chen; Yinan Wang; Yang Yang

Bcl\-2 is critical for tumour survival and serves as a promising anticancer drug target\. Herein, a series of novel Bcl\-2\-targeted peptides were identified through structure\-based virtual screening and systematic biological validation\. Four candidate peptides were selected from the peptide library\. MST results demonstrated that Peptide 1 exhibited the strongest apparent binding affinity towards Bcl\-2 \(Kd = 0\.51 ± 0\.03 μM\), superior to VS\-9 and other screened peptides\. Molecular dynamics simulation, free energy landscape analysis, and MM/GBSA calculation further supported the predicted conformational features of the Bcl\-2–Peptide\-1 complex\. MTT assays demonstrated that Peptide\-1 markedly inhibited the proliferation of HT29 and Colo320HSR colorectal cancer cells, while showing limited effects on normal NCM460 cells\. Bcl\-2 knockdown attenuated the bioactivity of Peptide\-1, and RT\-qPCR and ELISA analyses revealed that Peptide\-1 modulated Bax/Bcl\-2 expression at both transcriptional and protein levels\. Peptide\-1 represents a promising Bcl\-2\-targeting peptide with antiproliferative activity against colorectal cancer cells\.

## [The Self\-Improvement Problem](../publications/0a63d9de18bc1aa895b5.md)

Brian B\. Moser; Stanislav Frolov; Tobias C\. Nauen; Federico Raue; Andreas Dengel

With the rise of large language models, agentic systems are becoming increasingly autonomous, as they write code, call tools, revise prompts, and propose modifications to their own components\. This autonomy raises a fundamental question for safe self\-improvement: can an automated gate like a reward model or an automated reviewer reliably decide whether a proposed update should be accepted? The difficulty is structural\. The gate must be a terminating, computable procedure, while the property we ultimately care about, namely whether an update is a genuine semantic improvement, depends on potentially unbounded program behavior\. We formalize this mismatch by modeling agents as programs and defining improvement in terms of a semantic score that need not be computable\. We study two evaluation abstractions\. The first is a certifier that approves or rejects an update\. The second is a search procedure that, given access to a proposal generator, attempts to output some improving candidate if one exists\. We show that, in the fully general setting, no terminating procedure can simultaneously guarantee reliability \(never accepting a non\-improvement\) and non\-conservatism \(never missing an available improvement\): self\-referential constructions can force any such gate or searcher to fail\. Randomized gates with bounded error face the same limit\. We then identify a standard decidable regime used in practice \(bounded evaluation and a finite proposal budget\) under which exhaustive simulation yields a terminating search procedure with the desired guarantees\. We also show the limit of this recovery: a chain of accepted updates can raise the bounded score in every round while the true score falls\. Our results draw a boundary between unbounded, universal settings where correctness guarantees collapse and bounded settings where they can be recovered by design\.

## [Comparison between Cervical Epidural and Stellate Ganglion Block in Management of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome of the Upper Limb: A Prospective Comparative Study](../publications/0a65a677384cd944f0ca.md)



Complex Regional Pain Syndrome \(CRPS\) is a neuropathic pain syndrome resulting from complex pathophysiological mechanisms affecting multiple levels of the nervous system\.This work aimed to evaluate two regimens \(cervical epidural block and stellate ganglion block\) efficacy of treatment in easing chronic refractory pain in cases had upper limb CRPS after orthopedic trauma\.Prospective comparative study included 90 patients with upper limb CRPS admitted to Pain Clinic, Tanta University Hospitals\.The cases were divided into 2 equal groups: Group 1: Ultrasound \(U/S\) guided stellate ganglion block and group 2: C\-arm guided unilateral cervical epidural block\.Brief Pain Inventory short form was significantly decreased immediately after injection, at 3 and 6 months than baseline BPISF in both group 1 \(from 8 \(7\-9\) at baseline to 1 \(0\-2\) at 6 months\) and group 2 \(from 8 \(7\-8\) at baseline to 1 \(0\-1\) at 6 months\) \(P\.value &lt;0\.05\)\.BPI\-SF was insignificantly different at baseline, immediately after injection, at 3 and 6 months between both groups\.Pregabalin total dose was significantly decreased at 3 and 6 months than baseline dose in group 1 and group 2 \(P&lt;0\.05\)\.There was an no significant difference between both groups regarding pregabalin total dose at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months\.Both cervical epidural block and stellate ganglion block are safe and effective for pain control in upper limb CRPS, with no significant difference between techniques\.

## [Connectivity Marketing Mix Integration and Digital Capabilities in Traditional Food Micro\-Enterprises: A Case Study of Tempe Producers in Indonesia](../publications/0a71339d7d98f31dd9bc.md)

Enny Segarahati Barus; Muhammad Nakula Ramadani; Anda Subrata; Dina Arfianti Siregar; Bernadetta Anita Jerry Simbolon; Iqbal Mustaqim Nasution; Amrin

Objective: To analyze the 4Ps marketing mix at Tempe Pandawa and formulate a gradual digital transition suitable for its limited resources Theoretical framework: Integrates the marketing mix, word\-of\-mouth communication, brand visibility, and digital transition perspectives\. Literature review: Previous studies show that traditional food micro\-enterprises rely on product quality, affordable prices, proximity\-based distribution, and interpersonal promotion, but often have limited brand visibility and digital market access Methods: An exploratory single\-case study was conducted through semi\-structured interviews with one owner and four customers, supported by business documentation from January to May 2026\. Data were analyzed using a deductive 4Ps matrix and thematic comparison\. Results: Tempe Pandawa maintains product quality, affordable pricing, and proximity\-based distribution, while promotion remains dependent on direct communication and word\-of\-mouth\. The findings reveal an asymmetrical marketing mix in which product, price, and place are established, but promotion has not translated local trust into broader brand visibility\. Implications: Digital transition can be implemented gradually through stronger packaging identity, WhatsApp Business catalogs, point\-of\-sale mapping, simple digital content, and distribution expansion trials\. Novelty: The study proposes a gradual digital transition framework that builds digital visibility and market access from existing marketing practices and local customer trust\. Given the single\-case design and five informants, the findings are analytically rather than statistically generalizable\.

## [Single\-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross\-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis](../publications/0a73396b4f3a6d01465d.md)

Thanh\-Hong Nguyen; Tuan\-Dinh Nguyen; Tuan\-Dinh Nguyen; Tuan\-Dinh Nguyen; Oanh\-Thi Hoang; Thuy\-Thu T\. Can; Minh\-Huyen T\. Nguyen; Mai\-Hoang Tran; Hieu\-Chi Chu; Dinh\-Van Nguyen

Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages\. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue\-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response\. Single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor\-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context\. This review critically examines recent single\-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis\. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross\-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment\-response, and functional evidence\. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine\-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal\-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell\-state and regulatory\-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain\. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA\-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue\-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis\. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single\-cell\-derived biomarkers\. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation\. Together, these advances position single\-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches\.

## [Attention over noisy examples: generalization and memorization in the exponential Hopfield network](../publications/0a75f62cda344430fcdb.md)

Francesco Alemanno

In Hebbian learning from examples a Hopfield network of $N$ neurons is not supplied with the $K$ archetypes it has to retrieve but with $M$ blurred examples of each, of quality $r$, and whether it can infer them depends on the load $α=K/N$ \(interference among them\) and on the dataset entropy $ρ=\(1\-r^2\)/\(Mr^2\)$ \(how little the examples say about them\)\. We transfer this protocol to the exponential Hopfield model, whose zero\-temperature update is a step of softmax attention with the unlabelled examples as keys\. A signal\-to\-noise analysis gives in closed form the overlap between the output and an unseen archetype, $m^\{\(1\)\}=\{\\rm erf\}\(1/\\sqrt\{2ρ\_\{\\rm eff\}\}\)$: the majority\-rule law of the pairwise model at small load, with $ρ$ replaced by an attention entropy $ρ\_\{\\rm eff\}$ built from the weight the softmax gives to the correct class and the number of examples it spreads it over\. Two consequences follow\. First, in a window of inverse temperatures $β$ that widens as $\\sqrt N$ the interference between archetypes is exponentially small in $Nβ$: the load drops out and the number of archetypes that can be learnt grows as $\\exp\(c\\sqrt N\)$\. Second, learning fails differently: in the pairwise model through a spin\-glass phase, in the exponential model through memorization: the softmax concentrates its weight on the training example closest to the input and returns it in place of the archetype\. Seen from the input the softmax weights are those of the random energy model, and memorization is its freezing transition, at $β\\sqrt\{N\(1\-r^2\)\}\\simeq\\sqrt\{2\\ln M\}$; it is measurable on a head whose keys are examples as the number of examples carrying weight\. On MNIST the diagnostic follows the random\-energy prediction; on fashion\-MNIST it detects sub\-clusters in the classes, and the best accuracy lies beyond the memorization threshold, where the softmax reads out a local sub\-prototype\.

## [Retos de la evaluación del aprendizaje en la educa\-ción superior: hacia una evaluación formativa y transparente\.](../publications/0a77410df202e926dac7.md)

Msc\. Roxana Magaly Herrera Aguayo

La evaluación del aprendizaje en educación superior enfrenta una tensión estructural entre modelos tradicionales centrados en la certificación y las demandas contemporáneas de una formación orientada al desarrollo de competencias\. La masificación de las aulas, la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial y la persistente subjetividad en la calificación configuran un escenario que exige repensar los dispositivos evaluativos\. Esta revisión sistemática se propone analizar los principales retos de la evaluación en educación superior y sistematizar las características de un modelo formativo\-transparente que responda a dichos desafíos\. Siguiendo las directrices PRISMA 2020, se realizó una búsqueda en las bases de datos Redalyc, Dialnet y Google Scholar, abarcando publicaciones entre enero de 2015 y diciembre de 2023 en español e inglés\. Tras el cribado de 300 registros iniciales, se seleccionaron 15 estudios empíricos que aplicaran estrategias de evaluación formativa en contextos universitarios\. Los resultados evidencian que la coevaluación \(40%\), la autoevaluación \(30%\) y la evaluación entre pares \(20%\) constituyen las estrategias más documentadas, mientras que el uso sistemático de rúbricas aparece en menor proporción \(10%\) \. Se identifica una brecha persistente entre el discurso institucional sobre evaluación formativa y su implementación efectiva, condicionada por la carga docente, la falta de formación específica y la pervivencia de culturas evaluativas sumativas\. La revisión concluye que la transición hacia un paradigma formativo\-transparente requiere articular criterios negociados, instrumentos diversificados y un feedback dialógico sostenido, condiciones que trascienden la mera adopción de técnicas y demandan una reconfiguración de las relaciones pedagógicas en la universidad\.

## [Transformation of the Locus of Control When Working with Generative Neural Networks in Art and Pedagogical Education: From External Attribution to Informed Management](../publications/0a9266596d53d84e8644.md)

M\. N\. Serebryakov

Aim \. To provide a theoretical substantiation of the psychological and pedagogical mechanism of transforming external locus of control into internal one when working with generative neural networks in art and pedagogical education\. Methodology \. The research is based on a theoretical analysis and synthesis of the principles of psychological theories that determine the dynamics of locus of control, as well as on the methods of interpretation and modelling\. Results \. A three\-stage model of locus of control transformation \(external attribution – competence crisis – conscious management\) has been developed\. It is grounded in dialectical logic and the dynamics of cognitive, activity\-based, and motivational\-meaning dimensions\. Research implications \. An approach to integrating neural networks into art and pedagogical education is proposed, considering the psychological mechanisms that determine the trajectory of mastering this technology\. Pedagogical recommendations for implementing this approach are formulated\.

## [Classification Matters: Divergent Estimates of Dementia Risk Factors in the Health and Retirement Study](../publications/0aa2bab3bb0e3f20b303.md)

Gina E\. Nam; Junxian Liu; Suhani Amin; Karla Renata Flores Romero; Zachary J\. Kunicki; M\. Maria Glymour; Kaitlin Blackstone Casaletto; Jacqueline M\. Torres; Eleanor Hayes‐Larson

Clinical dementia diagnosis requires substantial expertise and is complex and costly\. Therefore, large population\-based studies often lack gold\-standard longitudinal diagnoses and instead use classification algorithms employing cognitive, functional, and health\-related measures to identify dementia\. We evaluated whether algorithm choice affects conclusions regarding dementia risk in the nationally representative Health and Retirement Study \(HRS; 2010\-2020\)\. We constructed four algorithm\-specific samples of participants age 70\+ without dementia in 2010: Langa\-Weir \(n=6,498\), Hudomiet \(n=6,556\), Expert \(n=5,751\), and Wu \(n=5,935\)\. Participants were followed until first dementia classification, death, or censoring\. We estimated dementia incidence rates \(IRs\) and used adjusted Cox models to estimate hazard ratios \(HRs\) for known risk factors\. Dementia IRs per 1000 person\-years meaningfully varied across algorithms, from 26\.5 \(95% CI 24\.5\-28\.5, Hudomiet\) to 62\.8 \(59\.9\-65\.8, Expert\)\. Sociodemographic risk factor associations also varied substantially\. HRs for education \(&lt; vs\. ≥high school\) ranged from 1\.36 \(1\.19\-1\.54, Hudomiet\) to 2\.22 \(1\.98\-2\.50, Langa\-Weir\), and HRs non\-Hispanic Black vs\. non\-Hispanic White ranged from 1\.86 \(1\.53\-2\.27, Expert\) to 2\.74 \(2\.40\-3\.12, Langa\-Weir\)\. Differences were less pronounced for health\-related risk factors\. In the absence of gold standard longitudinal diagnosis in HRS, researchers should examine the robustness of findings across multiple algorithms\.

## [Exploring immune\-endothelial interactions in neuroinflammation and vascular dysfunction](../publications/0aa647bec445dc04d490.md)

Zitian Wang; Zezheng Kang; Lei Wu; Jinglin Hu; Xinhua Chen; Tuoxian Tang

Neuroinflammation and cerebrovascular endothelial dysfunction are traditionally studied as parallel processes confined to individual disease categories\. Yet a growing body of evidence indicates that they operate as components of a tightly coupled, self\-amplifying circuit: the immune\-endothelial\-neural axis\. Within this axis, the peripheral immune system, cerebrovascular endothelium, and neural networks continuously modulate one another across disease contexts\. This Review summarizes current knowledge on the bidirectional immune\-endothelial interactions that underlie blood\-brain barrier disruption and neuroinflammation across cerebrovascular disorders, neuroimmune diseases, and neurodegenerative conditions\. A systems\-level comparison across disease categories identifies shared pathological hallmarks alongside disease\-specific signatures of tempo, vascular scale, and regional vulnerability\. Emerging therapeutic strategies are considered along the three limbs of the axis: immunomodulation, endothelial protection and barrier stabilization, and neural recovery, including traditional Chinese medicine as a multitarget approach\. By framing neurological disorders through the immune\-endothelial\-neural axis, this Review proposes a unifying framework that bridges disease boundaries and identifies common mechanistic targets for future translational research\. The framework is offered as a testable proposition in which the relative contribution of each limb differs between disorders\.

## [BMuon: Budgeting Muon&\#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility](../publications/0aa722a70d2dfe7377da.md)

Rida Assalouh; Tom Jacobs; Rebekka Burkholz; Yani Ioannou; Umut Şimşekli

Muon has emerged as a strong optimizer for neural network training and admits an interpretation as steepest descent under a spectral\-norm geometry\. Yet we find that Muon\-trained Transformers can degrade sharply when their MLP hidden channels are pruned after training\. To reconcile Muon&\#x27;s optimization performance with structured compressibility, we introduce Budget Muon \(BMuon\), which modifies Muon&\#x27;s spectral geometry so that hidden channels across blocks compete for a shared allocation budget\. The resulting oracle is exactly normalized steepest descent under a family of norms that interpolate between Muon&\#x27;s geometry and structured sparse geometries\. Our principal sparsity control is an interpretable global channel\-allocation budget, rather than a setting\-dependent sparsity\-penalty coefficient\. For linear factorization models, we show that Muon admits minimum\-cost exact representations with redundant hidden width, whereas under the BMuon oracle geometry and a sufficiently scarce budget, every minimum\-cost representation is width\-minimal\. For practical training, we derive a minorization\-maximization surrogate for the exact allocation problem\. On ImageNet\-1K with ViT\-S/16, BMuon improves over Muon under gradual structured MLP pruning, and its learned allocations provide a more effective pruning criterion than weight magnitude\. On a 1B\-parameter LLaMA\-style model trained on FineWeb, BMuon improves over Muon under post\-training MLP channel pruning\.

## [Enhanced Medical Intelligence Process Using Data Visualization](../publications/0ab98d39a80364966062.md)

Rosetta Duru

This paper focused on developing an expert system for health sector that uses intelligent agent to guide doctors in accurately carrying out disease control procedures\. Therefore, knowledge sharing across board for medical practitioners\. Also, the ontology\-based data integration \(OBDI\) and virtual data integration \(VDI\) approaches appear as a promising way to resolve semantic issues in information interoperability in medical record management\. the system developed was used to manage a disease registry that consists of the concepts of the domain, the attributes characterizing each disease, the different symptoms, and treatments\. Also, a relational database for storing and tracking disease outbreak and control using ontology\-based data integration \(OBDI\) was achieved\. A platform for Virtualized Data Access – Connect to different data sources and make them accessible from a common logical data access point was created which integrated an intelligent agent that uses case\-based reasoning for determining the disease control procedure to be applied to patient treatment for effective control of the disease\. The system achieved integration of various patients’ medical records from different hospitals using ontology based and virtual data integration technique that will allow clinic data of one patient collected together to form a combinational resource, and could be accessed by physician if authority is assigned to the physician\. ## [XAI\-driven analysis of influencing factors in streamflow\-based flood forecasting via fine tuned MTV19Anet](../publications/0abd2b0841092a9bf82a.md)

A\. Shashank; P\. Geetha; G\. Jyothish Lal; Sankaran Rajendran

An accurate and timely flood prediction that relies on streamflow information is important for developing an early warning system to minimize the negative effects of floods\. This paper proposes a new Steam flow\-based Flood prediction model using a Fine\-tuned MTV19ANet architecture \(SFFPM\-FTA\)\. The novelty of proposed model integrates an Enhanced Normalization Technique \(enNormT\) that effectively reduces the impact of large outliers\. It also employs an improved entropy\-based feature extraction method to enhance prediction robustness\. The hyperparameters are optimized using an Improved Wolverine Optimization Algorithm \(IWoOA\) with SHAP, an explainable AI technique to insights into model interpretability\. The study also includes the visual representation of steam flow, where normal flow and flooded flow are visually represented over river areas\. The experimental analysis shows that the proposed SFFPM\-FTA model obtains high performance compared to other prediction models with respect to various error measures\. The proposed model demonstrates minimal errors in streamflow\-based flood forecasting through improved normalization during preprocessing and enhanced entropy\-based feature extraction\. Compared with other baseline methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance, with reductions of 55\.26% in MAE, 64\.56% in MAPE, 83\.45% in MSE, and 57\.30% in RMSE, respectively\. In addition, the model achieves NSE of 0\.988, KGE of 0\.963, and R² of 0\.986, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately capturing streamflow dynamics\. Overall, the proposed SFFPM\-FTA improves flood forecasting accuracy and provides reliable and interpretable streamflow predictions\.

## [Psychometric evaluation of the 240\-item Farsi temperament and character inventory\-revised \(TCI\-R\) in an Iranian community sample](../publications/0ac19646c212b3e4b089.md)

Maryam Moghadasin; Danilo Garcia; Claude Robert Cloninger

Abstract This study evaluated the psychometric properties of the authorized full\-length Farsi version of the Temperament and Character Inventory\-Revised \(TCI\-R; 240 items\) in a large non\-clinical Iranian adult sample \( N = 1,316\) drawn from 13 cultural\-linguistic regions\. Participants completed the TCI\-R\. A subsample \( n = 50\) completed the NEO\-PI\-R, and another \( n = 80\) completed the TCI\-R again after eight weeks\. We examined the factorial structure using principal axis factoring \(PAF\) with Promax rotation and confirmatory factor analysis \(CFA\)\. Additionally, we evaluated internal consistency \(Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega\), construct reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, test\-retest reliability, and measurement invariance across gender\. Exploratory and confirmatory analyses supported the expected four\-factor temperament and three\-factor character structures, with acceptable though not uniformly strong fit for a complex multidimensional personality instrument\. Internal consistency was acceptable to high at the dimension level, although several four\-item subscales showed lower reliability\. Test–retest correlations indicated strong short\-term stability in the undergraduate retest subsample\. Construct reliability was generally satisfactory, while AVE values were lower for Novelty Seeking and Cooperativeness, indicating weaker latent\-level convergence for these two dimensions\. Preliminary correlations with NEO\-PI\-R traits \( n = 50\) supported external convergent validity and should be interpreted with caution\. Self\-Transcendence showed a differentiated relationship with Openness facets, overlapping most strongly with Feelings and more modestly with Aesthetics, Ideas, and Fantasy, whereas Values showed a small negative association\. The intercorrelation between Harm Avoidance and Self\-Directedness was somewhat stronger than typically reported in international validations\. Measurement invariance analyses supported configural and metric invariance across gender, with partial scalar invariance adopted for both the temperament and character models after freeing one intercept \(RD4\) for temperament and five \(SD3, SD5, CO2, ST2, ST3\) for character\. The Farsi TCI\-R provides initial psychometric support for use in non\-clinical Iranian community research, with caution regarding specific subscales, Novelty Seeking and Cooperativeness latent convergence, and gender\-based mean comparisons\. The differentiated Self\-Transcendence–Openness facet pattern and relatively strong Harm Avoidance–Self\-Directedness association, interpreted within Cloninger’s dynamic\-systems framework, represent theoretically meaningful findings that warrant cross\-cultural replication\.

## [The Real Impact of AI and ML on Enterprise Problem\-Solving: Beyond the Hype](../publications/0ac78f242f2f891c7b11.md)

David Ohnstad

Some shifts arrive quietly\. They don&\#x27;t make a dramatic entrance, and they certainly don&\#x27;t wait for an industry white paper to declare their importance\. They weave their way into daily routines – a small shortcut here, a smoother workflow there Full article: https://davidohnstad\.net/the\-real\-impact\-of\-emerging\-tech\-trends\-on\-everyday\-problem\-solving/

## [Shortening the Life Determination Period in LEDs Using TRIZ Methodology](../publications/0acb97955bd4c7d54ad6.md)

Çiğdem Cengiz

This study goes beyond simple optimization approaches for LED aging and lifespan estimation by using the TRIZ methodology as an innovative solution\. A fundamental technical paradox in the TRIZ approach is that accurate LED lifespan estimation requires lengthy aging tests, which delay time\-to\-market, reducing both time and efficiency\. A similar physical paradox arises from the need for long test times for accuracy, while short times are necessary for rapid market launch\. To address these paradoxes, the decomposition principles of TRIZ are utilized\. Accelerated aging tests are performed using a time\-based decomposition approach, followed by simultaneous tests under different environmental and operating conditions using a spatial decomposition approach\. Furthermore, principles such as inhibitory effect, viscosity change, and acceleration, which are among the 40 innovative principles of TRIZ, are used to improve the efficiency of LED aging processes\. Thus, the temperature\-dependent aging behavior and lifespan estimation of LEDs are analyzed within the framework of TM\-21 and LM\-80 standards\. The TRIZ methodology significantly reduces the differences between accuracy and test time thanks to its systematic problem\-solving approach\.

## [Olfactory Epithelium as a Model for Human Neural Regeneration](../publications/0ad77bd097fe9623fa4d.md)

Ziyad Matrouk Almeshrigi

The olfactory epithelium is a privileged region in terms of neurogenesis and repair mechanisms that can be studied through its regeneration capability at any age\. The present article provides an insight into the current understanding of the regenerative potential of the olfactory epithelium from multiple angles, including cellular composition and diversity, modes of regeneration, molecular regulators, comparative and experimental approaches, and therapeutic implications\. The review focuses on the value and limitations of the olfactory epithelium as a model for studying human neural regeneration and discusses the existing evidence from studies of human tissue, animal models, single\-cell technologies, and stem\-cell biology\. It aims to provide a comprehensive view of the regenerative processes by describing the function of particular cells and the modes of their interactions in the context of the entire system\. The findings on the functional diversity of olfactory sensory neurons and supporting cells and their connections with stem cells, growth factors, and biomaterials are presented\. The article also highlights the differences between the regenerative response in various animal models and the response of the human olfactory epithelium to injury\. Finally, the review concludes with a discussion of the therapeutic implications of the study of olfactory epithelium regeneration\. The study provides a valuable insight into the mechanisms and points to the importance of additional preclinical and clinical research in multiple areas related to neural regeneration\. Moreover, it highlights the complexity of extrapolating the results from animal experiments to humans and the uniqueness of the human olfactory epithelium, which may hinder the translation of the findings and require additional considerations\.

## [Trust Cultures and the Politics of Relational Legitimacy](../publications/0adbf7f6118acadf1c89.md)

Karl Patrick Regala Mendoza

Moving beyond conventional understandings of trust as an individual attitude or institutional outcome, Trust Cultures and the Politics of Relational Legitimacy develops the concept of trust cultures to explain how historically and culturally situated publics learn to navigate uncertainty, recalibrate expectations, and sustain democratic life despite persistent institutional fragility\. Trust is understood not simply as confidence in institutions but as part of a broader relational process through which legitimacy is continually negotiated, contested, repaired, and reconstituted\. Drawing on interpretive analyses of public health controversies, local governance, political scandals, and everyday democratic life in the Philippines, the book develops an interconnected conceptual vocabulary—including relational legitimacy, democratic ambivalence, scandal constructivation, accrued damage, fragile repair, and moral coordination —to demonstrate that democratic endurance depends less on institutional perfection than on the relational capacities through which citizens continue inhabiting imperfect institutions\. Rather than treating the Global South as a site for applying theories developed elsewhere, this book advances it as a site of theory generation\. It argues that postcolonial democracies illuminate broader dynamics of legitimacy, uncertainty, and democratic endurance that increasingly characterize political life across the contemporary world\. Bringing communication research into conversation with cultural sociology, political sociology, democratic theory, and interpretive social science, this book offers a relational account of democracy in which trust is understood not as the absence of uncertainty but as one of the relational infrastructures through which democratic societies learn to live together despite it\. This work is essential for scholars, researchers, and practitioners in political communication, sociology of emotions, trust studies, and Southeast Asian/Global South studies\. It speaks to those grappling with the challenges of disinformation, affective polarization, and the erosion of institutional legitimacy in fractured democracies, offering a Global South\-rooted perspective that redefines trust as a relational, emotional, and ethical dynamic\.

## [IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE HUMAN ROLE IN THE FUTURE STOCK MARKET THEORETICAL AND IDEOLOGICAL EXPECTATIONS FOR UZBEKISTAN](../publications/0adc761b469053f41047.md)

Alisher Shavkidinov

Artificial intelligence can reduce the cost of processing financial information, yet its contribution to stock market development depends on the institutions that govern data, decisions and accountability\. This article examines that relationship for Uzbekistan through a critical synthesis of financial economics, research on human reliance on algorithms, international governance frameworks and national policy documents\. It distinguishes established findings from conditional expectations and develops a framework in which automated analysis remains subject to accountable human authority\. The central argument is that market quality depends on complementary investment in disclosure, professional competence and supervisory capacity\. An ideological comparison identifies tensions between technological efficiency, developmental objectives and investor autonomy\. Two analytical tables specify responsibilities and measurable criteria for future evaluation\. The proposed framework yields testable propositions concerning disclosure quality, meaningful review and common dependence on model providers\. For Uzbekistan, the defensible sequence begins with verified information and supervised analytical applications, followed by limited deployment only after independent validation\. These conclusions are theoretical; the article reports no original trading experiment or estimated investment returns\.

## [A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On\-Policy Bidirectional Distillation](../publications/0adc9734dd592b53ed79.md)

Haoyu Chen; Jun Bai; Yang Liu; Jianfei Zhang; Wenge Rong

Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards \(RLVR\) has substantially improved Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) LLMs, but its outcome\-level rewards provide only sparse supervision\. On\-Policy Distillation offers dense token\-level feedback, yet requires a stronger compatible teacher, while on\-policy self\-distillation relies on hand\-designed privileged information\. We observe that the MoE architecture itself offers a way to resolve this dilemma, as increasing the activation budget per token exposes latent expert capacity and yields a potentially stronger teacher within the model\. However, naive expansion degrades performance because newly co\-activated experts are not optimized to work together\. We therefore propose MoEvolve, a bidirectional distillation framework following a recovery\-then\-improvement strategy: we first restore the activation\-expanded high\-$k$ model and further strengthen it by exploiting its additional active capacity, then reverse the direction of distillation to transfer the enhanced capabilities back into the original low\-$k$ configuration, retaining its inference\-time activation budget\. Across diverse MoE models and benchmarks, MoEvolve improves the initial models by up to $22\.2$ domain\-average points and outperforms same\-budget RLVR baselines by up to $6\.5$ points\. Notably, the final low\-$k$ models often surpass their activation\-expanded teachers\.

## [“Boiled Water Softens the Potato But Hardens the Egg”: Perceived Utility of Mindfulness and Reappraisal Strategies and Relations to Compliance In Situ](../publications/0ae7837fd9e3aa7ee16b.md)

Almaz Mesghina; Lindsey E\. Richland

Abstract Objectives Individuals in laboratory settings frequently do not comply with instructed emotion regulation \(ER\) strategies as stressor intensity increases—sometimes not using ER at all, often switching from reappraisal to strategies like mindfulness\. Though some have explored predictors of ER choice, few have done so in situ as individuals regulate responses to self\-relevant, ongoing stressors, nor directly asked how individuals perceive the utility of ER strategies after instruction\. Methods In total, 290 American undergraduates from two large, minority\-serving institutions were assigned to regulate their COVID\-19 pandemic\-related distress using mindfulness or reappraisal\. Previously, research found that participants’ compliance was imperfect, especially for reappraisal\. In the present study, we qualitatively analyzed participants’ responses to an item asking why they believed their strategy was/was not useful and analyzed whether these themes predicted compliance\. Results Most participants expressed ambivalence about their strategy\. Mindfulness noncompliers were more likely to mention context and individual differences themes as important for the utility of their strategy\. Controlling for mindfulness condition and pandemic\-related distress, which both positively predicted compliance, mentioning individual differences predicted a 69% decrease in the likelihood of compliance \(OR 0\.31, 95% CI \[0\.13, 0\.75\], p = 0\.009\)\. Conclusions Though mindfulness had higher compliance when compared to reappraisal, their compliance narratives tended to focus on utility limits: elucidating under which contexts and for whom mindfulness would be further useful\. We underscore the importance of research on ER choice in situ, including continued investigation of reasoners’ perceptions of and compliance to their real\-life emotion regulatory opportunities\. Preregistration The analyses reported here were not preregistered\. However, they use previously unanalyzed and unreported data from Mesghina et al\. \(2021; Study 2\), which was pre\-registered \(osf\.io/kq9gp\)\.

## [Tecnologías de la información y la comunicación: impacto en niños y adolescentes](../publications/0afe336f838d48d2f48d.md)

Maritza Padrón\-Nieves; Alicia Ponte‐Sucre

La vida social y responsable, así como el funcionamiento de todas las sociedades humanas, se asientan en el uso de códigos para expresar ideas; por ello, surge la definición de la comunicación como el acto mediante el cual un individuo establece contacto con otro para transmitir información\. A lo largo de la historia de la humanidad se evidencia cómo el hombre ha buscado herramientas que le permitan progresar, y cada nuevo paso ha traído consigo cuestionamientos éticos acordes con la complejidad de dichas herramientas\. Con el desarrollo de las Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación \(TIC\), se tienen al alcance equipos, sistemas y programas para encontrar soluciones a diversos problemas; sin embargo, la velocidad del avance tecnológico hace reflexionar sobre la importancia de su uso adecuado\. En la primera parte de este artículo se describen las características de las TIC y las regulaciones vigentes, y en la segunda se desarrolla una de las consecuencias del uso masivo de estas herramientas: su impacto en la niñez y la adolescencia\.

## [Evaluating Semantic and Relational Knowledge Preservation under Fair\-budget Multi\-document Compression](../publications/0b01ccd5df62dbb67090.md)

Shaufiah Abdullah Junaidi; Yuefeng Li; Richi Nayak

Compressing multi\-document text before structured\-knowledge extraction can reduce processing cost, but it can also remove relation\-bearing evidence\.This study evaluates how a frozen topic\-pattern extractive selector differs from fair\-budget comparators in preserving semantic and relational information under matched word budgets\.The selector combines latent dirichlet allocation topic relevance, FP\-Growth lexical\-pattern support, and a redundancy penalty\.A 120\-configuration validation search was completed before definitive test analysis; Run82 \(α=0\.30,β=0\.70, δ=1\.00, 15 sentences, 25 topics\) was then frozen and transferred unchanged to held\-out evaluation\.On 5,621 Multi\-News test clusters, Run82 produced statistically reliable but small improvements in concept F1 \(0\.4550 vs\. 0\.4405\) and relation F1 \(0\.4395 vs\. 0\.4251\), while exact\-triple F1 was effectively unchanged \(0\.3994 vs\. 0\.3990\)\.A prespecified 500\-cluster PRIMERA comparison under the same exact word budget produced lower dependency\-based structured\-preservation scores than both Run82 and Lead\-W, but an independent 500\-cluster REBEL analysis reversed the Run82\-Lead\-W ordering \(exact\-triple F1 0\.1779 vs\. 0\.4094\), demonstrating extractor sensitivity\.Independent WebNLG verification reproduced the same component\-composition gap: subject, object, and predicate coverage improved, whereas complete semantic\-triple recovery did not\.Across 100 alternative WebNLG regroupings, subject, object, and predicate effects remained positive in every regrouping, whereas complete semantic\-triple effects were smaller and less consistently significant\.Preservation also declined sharply with increasing compression severity and source\-graph size\.Ablation further showed non\-uniform component contributions and budget\-length trade\-offs\.Across both datasets, improvements at the concept and relation\-vocabulary levels did not propagate to argument pairing or complete triple recovery\.We therefore characterize the component\-structure preservation gap as a pipelineconditional empirical pattern rather than a universal hierarchy\.

## [Barriers to comprehensive fertility counseling among persons living with HIV/AIDS in Ghana](../publications/0b2d19dae665825293a7.md)

Priscilla Asantewaa Boadi; Victor Luckyboy Dzramado

Introduction Persons living with HIV/AIDS \(PLWHA\) in Ghana increasingly express the wish to have children, yet little is known about whether routine HIV care delivers fertility counseling that extends beyond prevention of mother\-to\-child transmission to the safer conception, individualized planning, and onward referral that comprehensive counseling requires\. This study explored the barriers to comprehensive fertility counseling experienced by PLWHA receiving antiretroviral therapy at a district hospital in the Ashanti Region of Ghana\. Methods A qualitative interpretive phenomenological design was used\. Twelve purposively selected adults living with HIV, comprising nine women and three men aged 26–49 years, attended the antiretroviral therapy clinic at St\. Michael&\#x27;s Hospital, Pramso, and took part in in\-depth semi\-structured interviews between August and October 2024\. Interviews were audio\-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed manually through an inductive interpretive phenomenological process that moved from meaning units to situated interpretation and then to essential themes\. Trustworthiness was supported through reflexive journaling, documented positionality, participant validation of preliminary interpretations, and an audit trail\. Results Three essential themes captured how healthcare experiences shaped fertility counseling and decision\-making, namely quality of reproductive health counseling and education, healthcare provider attitudes and support, and access to comprehensive reproductive health services\. Participants valued prevention of mother\-to\-child transmission education and the relational warmth of providers, yet described counseling that was generic rather than tailored to their circumstances and that seldom addressed protection of an HIV\-negative partner during conception\. No participant reported being offered or receiving a referral, preconception consultation, or structured reproductive plan when personal barriers such as absence of a partner stood in the way of childbearing\. One participant had received no fertility counseling at all\. Discussion These accounts left participants holding reproductive hopes they could not translate into plans\. The findings suggest that at this facility fertility counseling is routinely delivered but, as experienced by these participants, incompletely comprehensive, and that structured individualized planning, provider capacity in safer conception, and clearly communicated referral pathways deserve attention\.

## [An artificial intelligence framework for end\-to\-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models](../publications/0b3774430ba6d27ddec4.md)

Cathy Shyr; Yan Hu; Rory J Tinker; Thomas A\. Cassini; Kevin Byram; Rizwan Hamid; Daniel Fabbri; Adam Wright; Josh F\. Peterson; Undiagnosed Diseases Network; Lisa Bastarache; Hua Xu

Phenotyping is fundamental to rare disease diagnosis, but manually curating structured phenotypes from clinical notes is labor intensive and difficult to scale\. Existing artificial intelligence \(AI\) approaches optimize individual components of phenotyping but generally do not operationalize the full workflow of extracting features from clinical text, standardizing them to Human Phenotype Ontology \(HPO\) terms, and prioritizing rare disease\-relevant HPO terms\. We developed RARE\-PHENIX, an end\-to\-end AI framework for rare disease phenotyping that integrates large language model\-based phenotype extraction, ontology\-grounded standardization to HPO terms, and supervised ranking of HPO terms\. We trained RARE\-PHENIX using data from 2671 patients across 11 Undiagnosed Diseases Network clinical sites, and externally validated it on 16,357 real\-world clinical notes from 143 patients at Vanderbilt University Medical Center\. Our findings suggest RARE\-PHENIX generates structured, prioritized HPO terms highly concordant with clinician curation, demonstrates potential downstream disease\-prioritization signal, and may support human\-in\-the\-loop rare disease phenotyping in real\-world settings\.

## [The coral settlement\-sphere: microenvironments that shape reef restoration in the Anthropocene](../publications/0b3d46e630d792f1190f.md)

Sarah Ling Romero; Peter L\. Harrison; Alexandra Ordoñez Alvarez; Tom Shlesinger; Adi Khen; Yossi Loya; Jennifer E\. Smith; Daniel Wangpraseurt

Accelerating losses of reef\-building corals are driving steep declines in coral recruitment, imperiling the biodiversity and long\-term resilience of reef ecosystems worldwide\. Here, we review the mechanisms underlying coral recruitment success through a critical – yet largely overlooked – microenvironmental lens relevant to the scale of microscopic coral larvae\. We introduce the concept of the “settlement\-sphere”, which encompasses the physical, biochemical, and microbial microhabitat properties that govern successful coral larval recruitment\. We then examine how anthropogenic stressors erode this settlement\-sphere by diminishing essential chemical cues, reducing microhabitat complexity, and altering key physico\-chemical conditions \(e\.g\., hypoxia\), ultimately leading to recruitment failure\. Finally, we argue that advancing a collective understanding of the settlement\-sphere is essential for developing actionable strategies to restore degraded coral reef systems\. Such strategies include augmenting reef microhabitats with chemical cues and advanced materials that promote coral recruitment, thereby supporting genetic diversity, enhancing resilience, and enabling the restocking of coral populations\.

## [Design Strategies for Multi\-Agent Systems: Lessons from Four Implementations](../publications/0b42b03433728a80acd4.md)

Lucía Covarrubias; Tomás Rivero; Ignacio Bosch

La orquestación de sistemas multiagente exige decisiones de diseño\. Componentes como la generación aumentada por recuperación \(RAG\), herramientas externas, memorias heterogéneas, políticas de seguridad y protocolos como Model Context Protocol \(MCP\) deben integrarse de forma coherente\. Esto plantea interrogantes concretas: qué base de datos vectorial utilizar, cuándo delegar tareas entre agentes y cuándo exponer un agente como herramienta de otro\. Este trabajo presenta un análisis retrospectivo de cuatro sistemas implementados en distintos entornos: NeuroHire, Doki, MateApp y Ciruelito\. En estos sistemas se exploraron distintas formas de orquestación con el OpenAI Agents SDK y el framework LangChain\. A partir del análisis se observaron diez estrategias de diseño, entre las que se destacan: la delegación jerárquica entre agentes, RAG con umbralización y conversión explícita de distancia a similitud en FAISS, Quota\-Driven Degradation con degradación a un modelo más económico tras superar el límite de uso, y MCP Tool Filter para reducir la superficie de ataque\. Estas estrategias abordan problemas observados durante el desarrollo: contexto irrelevante en RAG, gestión de costos en entornos multi\-tenant, seguridad en la integración de herramientas, aislamiento de datos y mejora de la mantenibilidad mediante encapsulación y guardrails técnicos\.

## [Clinical characteristics and pharmacovigilance signals of immune checkpoint inhibitor\-associated cystitis and ureteritis: analysis of FAERS reports and published cases](../publications/0b4528e304fc0b35cbb5.md)

Yuanyuan Zhang; JiaJin Yang

Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor \(ICI\)\-associated cystitis and ureteritis are uncommon urinary immune\-related adverse events that are difficult to distinguish from infection or other urinary tract complications\. Their clinical phenotype and pharmacovigilance signal remain incompletely defined\. Methods We combined a pooled analysis of published cases with a FAERS disproportionality analysis from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1\. Published cases were reviewed for clinical presentation, treatment, rechallenge, and time\-to\-onset\. FAERS reports were deduplicated at the CASEID level\. A broad cystitis\-inclusive definition included IMMUNE\-MEDIATED CYSTITIS, CYSTITIS NONINFECTIVE, URETERITIS, and CYSTITIS; a high\-specificity definition excluded the nonspecific Preferred Term CYSTITIS\. Disproportionality was assessed using reporting odds ratios \(RORs\), proportional reporting ratios, chi\-square statistics, and information components\. Results Twenty\-eight reports comprising 45 unique patients were included\. The median age was 56 years, and lung cancer was the most common malignancy\. Published cases commonly showed urinary frequency, dysuria, hematuria, leukocyturia, inflammatory imaging or cystoscopic abnormalities, and corticosteroid responsiveness\. Upper urinary tract involvement was documented in 13 of 33 patients with available CT data\. Median time\-to\-onset was 62 days among 24 evaluable cases, and recurrence occurred in 5 of 9 rechallenged patients\. In FAERS, 20,257,224 deduplicated CASEIDs were analyzed\. The broad cystitis\-inclusive definition identified 397 ICI\-associated cases and showed only a weak signal \(ROR, 1\.12; 95% CI, 1\.02–1\.24\), whereas the high\-specificity definition identified 151 cases and yielded a stronger signal \(ROR, 9\.04; 95% CI, 7\.63–10\.70\)\. Class\-level signals were also observed, and the overall high\-specificity signal remained positive across sensitivity analyses\. Conclusion These findings support ICI\-associated cystitis and ureteritis as an uncommon urothelial inflammatory irAE spectrum\. Phenotype\-aware outcome definition is important in pharmacovigilance because nonspecific cystitis coding may dilute the reporting signal\.

## [Cognition, oversight, and the safety case for documentation AI](../publications/0b4a34a056bd7af007e5.md)

Fahad Wali Ahmed; Fauwad Ahmed

Large language models \(LLMs\) can now draft hospital discharge summaries\. Reported hallucination rates vary by measurement context, from about 1%\-2% in structured summarisation to over 60% under provocation testing\. The common argument that LLMs outperform a tired resident treats a high\-stakes clinical and legal document as a text\-quality problem\. We argue that a potentially underappreciated concern is the weakening of clinician oversight when reviewing fluent machine\-generated text, and that the joint clinician\-AI system is central to safety\. We propose a Clinician\-AI Oversight Model with four safeguards: bounded autonomy, structured verification, error\-signal monitoring, and longitudinal evaluation of cognitive effects\.
