A drought mitigation strategy stimulates denitrification could therefore trade water\-stress resilience against climate burden\. No N2O flax data accompany the current work, and in our view no scald application should be contemplated until the NosZ\-to\-NirK balance and the resulting N2O:N2 product ratio are measured directly in soil\.The gap between these results and agricultural practice is substantial, and we think it should be started plainly rather than bridged rhetorically\. Persistence is the first obstacle: naphthalene\-derived acids are readily biodegraded from common soil bacteria and sorb strongly to organic matter and clays, so the effective rhizosphere concentration of an applied dose is unlikely to resemble that achieved in controlled systems\. Soil type, pH, temperature and moisture regime will all modulate this, and more has been varied systematically\.Second, ecological selectivity is unproven at community scale\. Applying an aromatic acid to soil may preferentially favor aromatic\-degrading taxa, some of which are opportunists, and could shift community structure in ways that are unhelpful or difficult to reverse\. Third, the biosafety and regulatory position of applying a naphthalene derivative to agricultural soil is not trivial and has not been addressed\. Fourth, the economics of synthesizing and delivering a defined metabolite at field scale, alongside a live inoculant with its own formulation and shelf\-life constrains, remain unexplored\.These considerations argue for two parallel and non\-exclusive strategies\. The more immediately actionable is restoration of soil microbial diversity through reduced tillages, cover cropping, diversified rotation and organic amendment, supporting the endogenous capacity for 2\-NA\-mediated recruitment\.The more speculative is targeted co\-application of a metabolite with a compatible keystone strain as a biostimulant, which should be treated as research program rather than a near\-term product\. Progress of both will depend on standardized multi\-omics frameworks capable of linking microbial community composition to function across sites and seasons, an area where methodological harmonization remains a recognized bottleneck \(Kumar et al\., 2023\)\.Chen et al\. \( 2026\) provide the latest mechanistic framework to date of how resident microbial diversity conditions a plant&\#x27;s chemical recruitments of beneficial partners under drought\. We found it as evidence that diversity is a functional prerequisite for practice host signaling, and that individual exudates can be multifunctional in ways that classical signal\-versus\-substrate distinctions do not capture\.\. The priorities we would set are correspondingly modest and testable, identification and genetic validation of the 2\-NA biosynthesis pathway; measurement of exudation kinetics under realistic, fluctuating drought rather than imposed step changes; determination of the fate, half\-life and sorption behavior of 2\-NA across contrasting soils; assessment of community\-level and N2O consequences; and examination of whether diversity\-conditioned signaling operates in cereals and other legumes \(Gahlot, 2026\)\. Multi\-side field evaluation should follow, not precede, these steps\. Framed this way, the contribution of this work is conceptual rather than immediately applied\. It does not yet deliver droughtsmart agriculture but clarifies what such a strategy would need to be built upon and it suggest that protecting the diversity already present in agricultural soils may be a more reliable investment than engineering it\. However, this study further opens new dimension of research on diversity\-dependent chemical ecology of drought adaptation in soybean that incorporated plant metabolomics, bacterial sensor biology and N biogeochemistry, which merely resolves a long\-standing gap in our understanding of diversity function relationship in the rhizosphere but also microbiome\-assisted climate\-smart crop improvement\.

## [Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling\-Law Prediction](../publications/0b726beb53b474e1f3e9.md)

Aishwarya Wesanekar; Sheng\-Tao Yang; Jiawei Zhang; Flavio Sales Truzzi; Chen Chen; Nader Beigiparast; Shengyuan Huang; Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam; Vitor Cid; Colin Clement; Vinayak Thapliyal; Sebastian Ament; Jihao Andreas Lin; Vincent Huang; Kai Han; Boyi Jiang; Wenlin Chen; Chaorong Chen; Ashwin Kumar; Maximilian Balandat; David Eriksson; Yifei Zhang; Pan Zhong

Evaluating candidate changes \(hypotheses\) to recommendation models requires full\-scale training runs consuming thousands of GPU\-hours, severely limiting the hypothesis space engineers can feasibly explore\. We introduce Predictable Scaling \(PS\), a systematic framework that exploits empirically verified regularity conditions to predict full\-scale model performance from small\-scale proxies\. PS constructs scaled\-down variants via composable scaling functions along distinct resource axes, and projects metrics to the target scale via curve fitting with calibrated uncertainty estimates\. We compare three prediction strategies of increasing expressiveness: even the simplest \(raw proxy\) achieves prediction error within the empirical noise floor of repeated\-run variance; the most expressive \(Gaussian Process\) provides an indicative 15% relative MAE improvement and calibrated uncertainty\. Evaluation on two ranking models of increasing complexity\-\-\-a task\-specific model and a foundation model\-\-\-demonstrates that PS correctly ranks actionable hypotheses across diverse hypothesis types at 79\-88% compute reductions\.

## [Case Report: Improvement in neurologic symptoms and remission following non\-operative management of locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck following cemiplimab therapy: two cases](../publications/0b8adf6c2e5259d222a5.md)

Elijah Lee; Wolfram E\. Samlowski; Brandon Reynolds; Kaviyon Sadrolashrafi

Background Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common skin malignancy in aging populations\. Surgical resection and radiotherapy can result in significant morbidity, as well as functional and cosmetic impairments\. PD\-1 antibodies are promising treatments for locally advanced disease\. Case presentation Two elderly men \(aged 71 and 73\) with locoregionally advanced head and neck tumors received neoadjuvant treatment with cemiplimab \(350 mg IV every 3 weeks\)\. Both patients presented with neurologic symptoms concerning for nerve involvement; however, perineural spread could not be identified radiographically or by limited biopsies\. Both patients achieved a significant clinical response after only four doses of cemiplimab\. After 4 additional doses, both patients underwent elective treatment discontinuation and surgery and radiotherapy were omitted\. With over 12\-month follow\-up, both patients remained free of recurrence\. Treatment was well\-tolerated with only Grade 1 pruritus\. Conclusion These observations are promising and suggest the feasibility of response\-adapted management following cemiplimab therapy in selected patients with advanced squamous cell skin cancer with resolution of neurologic symptoms\. This approach may allow for omission of surgery and radiotherapy in selected patients\. Further investigation to define appropriate candidates for this approach appears warranted\.

## [Multi\-tissue transcriptional profiling resolves opposing acute and chronic host\-response programs along the bone marrow–to–periphery axis in bacterial pneumonia](../publications/0b95d05e4ac26657fc18.md)

Xiaoyu Xiang; Zhongxue Feng; Tingting Li; Zhiwen Gong; Lietao Wang; Jing Yang; Lijun Wang; Wei Zhang

Background Whether the host response to severe bacterial pneumonia is shared across pathogens or tailored to the infecting organism is unresolved, yet it bears directly on host\-directed therapy and on risk stratification in the critically ill\. Methods Matched murine models of acute and chronic intranasal infection with Staphylococcus aureus \(Gram\-positive\) and Klebsiella pneumoniae \(Gram\-negative\) were established, and bulk ribonucleic acid \(RNA\) sequencing was performed on bone marrow, blood, spleen and lymph node\. Genes differentially expressed between the marrow and the peripheral compartments were intersected across pathogens to define core mobilization signatures\. These were scored by single\-sample gene set enrichment analysis \(ssGSEA\) in four independent animal datasets, five human infection cohorts and three murine datasets containing infected lung tissue, and were refined into compact panels by four\-algorithm machine learning and weighted gene co\-expression network analysis\. Results The host response resolved into two distinct transcriptional programs organized along the bone marrow to periphery axis\. Acute infection engaged a conserved 32\-gene mobilization core, anchored by a densely interconnected 10\-gene hub and enriched for tumour necrosis factor \(TNF\), interleukin\-17 \(IL\-17\), leukocyte transendothelial migration and efferocytosis signalling, that was shared between Gram\-positive and Gram\-negative pneumonia and preferentially active in peripheral blood\. This acute signature marked an effector\-mobilization cellular ecology\. It was elevated across bacterial, viral and fungal disease, was conserved from mouse to human, and in five human cohorts increased with sepsis severity, scaled with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment \(SOFA\) organ\-failure score, and independently stratified 28\-day mortality \(hazard ratio \[HR\] 2\.33\)\. In published murine datasets it was also induced in infected lung by both pathogen classes and rose with progression to sepsis\. Chronic infection instead engaged a smaller, pathogen\-restricted 14\-gene program with tissue\- and time\-dependent dynamics that defined a regulatory, exhausted and myeloid\-inflammatory state and carried no prognostic information\. Orthogonal machine\-learning and co\-expression analyses nominated compact 10\-gene acute and four\-gene chronic candidate panels\. Conclusion The transcriptional response to bacterial pneumonia is a coordinated bone marrow to periphery process rather than a set of isolated tissue reactions\. The conserved acute axis is a severity\- and outcome\-associated, pathogen\-agnostic signature and a rational substrate for broadly applicable host\-response biomarkers and host\-directed therapy in severe infection\.

## [Business Analytics for Cybersecurity Vulnerability Prioritization in Banking: Evidence from EPSS, CVSS, and CISA KEV](../publications/0b99e59ff53ca49c295c.md)

Raguvaran V

The fast increase in the number of cyber threats faced in today&\#x27;s banking sector calls for smart algorithms capable of prioritizing the detected vulnerabilities timely and accurately\. This paper proposes a business analytics model that utilizes the evidence from Exploit Prediction Scoring System \(EPSS\), Common Vulnerability Scoring System \(CVSS\), and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency&\#x27;s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities \(CISA KEV\) catalogue for enhanced decision\-making in managing the vulnerabilities in the banking environment\. The central component of the proposed model is represented by the hybrid algorithm architecture that uses the representation learning power of the Heterogeneous Graph Transformer \(HGT\) along with the clustering capacity of the Self\-Organizing Map \(SOM\) and the ability of the Isolation Forest to detect anomalies\. By combining the advantages of all these approaches, the model obtains a good combination of the capacity to model the relational dependencies between vulnerabilities, to detect latent patterns and the ability to isolate anomalous signals\. Experimental analysis performed using the real\-world banking datasets shows the high accuracy of 97\.40%, which proves the efficiency of the model for ranking and prioritizing the vulnerabilities that require urgent addressing\. Besides its efficiency, the proposed business analytics model makes an important contribution to the field\. The proposed model shows how machine learning can be made consistent with the business goals so that limited resources are allocated to those vulnerabilities that are most likely to be exploited\. In essence, such a solution makes business analytics a bridge between technical assessment and executive decision\-making in the banking field\.

## [Research on a production plan\-driven multi\-objective inventory\-to\-sales ratio optimization model for cigarettes](../publications/0ba6127d9be7daa1bedc.md)

Qi Sun; Wanjiang Wang; Wei Jian; Feng Zhao; Mingjun Wang; Huihui Gao; 蒋柳燕; Donghong Liu; Renwang Li

The cigarette industry faces persistent conflicts between rigid production quotas and volatile market demand, often resulting in suboptimal inventory structures and frequent stockouts or overstocking\. To address this, we propose a production plan\-driven multi\-objective optimization model that explicitly integrates the inventory\-to\-sales ratio \(ISR\) as a feasibility constraint rather than an objective\. The model simultaneously optimizes inventory turnover, production smoothness, total cost, and service level, subject to capacity, safety\-stock, and annual quota constraints\. An enhanced NSGA\-II is developed, featuring hierarchical constraint handling, equipment\-plan coupled encoding, and demand\-responsive mutation, to efficiently explore the constrained search space\. Simulation experiments on five cigarette brands demonstrate that the improved algorithm outperforms the conventional NSGA\-II, reducing IGD by 38\.6%, increasing Hypervolume by 56\.1%, and lowering Spacing by 80\.2%, while ensuring all Pareto solutions are strictly feasible\. Three preference schemes—cost\-priority, market\-priority, and balanced—yield distinct production plans with clear trade\-offs between cost and turnover\. The results confirm that the proposed framework provides actionable decision support for inventory\-production coordination under plan\-driven manufacturing environments\.

## [Who will replace their phones? An explainable machine learning approach using large\-scale telecom behavioral data](../publications/0badce516bd4e3bb2b48.md)

Yulin Zhu; Sen Xia; Feng Qiu; Benjiang Lu

Purpose Rapid technological innovation has accelerated the diffusion of mobile phones and communication networks, making phone replacement an important consumer behavior in the telecommunications market\. However, limited research has examined the determinants of phone replacement decisions using large\-scale behavioral data from telecom operators\. This study aims to identify the key predictive factors influencing users&\#x27; phone replacement behavior and develop a predictive framework for telecom operators\. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from approximately 400,000 telecom users, this study develops a prediction framework based on the XGBoost machine learning algorithm\. The model incorporates large\-scale behavioral data, including users&\#x27; demographic characteristics, phone attributes and mobile communication behaviors\. To enhance model interpretability, SHAP analysis is employed to assess the importance and interaction effects of predictive features\. Findings The results show that historical phone replacement behavior is the strongest predictor of future replacement decisions\. Brand prominence of the currently owned phone is negatively associated with replacement likelihood, suggesting that users with well\-known brands tend to retain their devices longer\. In addition, communication demand indicators, such as call duration and SMS usage, positively influence phone replacement probability, with heterogeneous effects across different user groups\. Originality/value This study integrates large\-scale telecom behavioral data with explainable machine learning techniques to predict consumer phone replacement behavior, providing a transparent analytical framework and practical insights for telecom operators to design personalized marketing strategies\.

## [Application of Machine Learning for Defect Mitigation and Roughness Estimation in EHLA AM Process](../publications/0bb20ddb593cf7ded797.md)

Jeferson T\. Pacheco; Lucas Weihmann; Murilo de Souza Ribeiro; Oksana Kovalenko; Tiago Vieira da Cunha

Abstract This study presents a data\-driven methodology for optimizing Extreme High\-Speed Laser Cladding \(EHLA\) processing parameters with the aim of identifying defect\-free conditions and controlling surface roughness\. The proposed approach combines experimental analysis, machine learning and experimental validation\. In the first stage, classification algorithms were evaluated to identify processing conditions associated with defect\-free coatings\. The Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\) provided the best overall classification performance and was used to support the screening of feasible processing conditions\. Correlation analysis identified process speed, overlap and mass flow rate as the parameters most associated with defect occurrence, while stand\-off, overlap, process speed and laser power showed the strongest relationships with surface roughness\. In the second stage, regression models were developed using a reduced parameter space comprising laser power, process speed and overlap\. The MLP provided the best predictive performance for surface roughness among the evaluated models\. Experimental validation confirmed the formation of defect\-free coatings under the selected processing conditions, although prediction errors increased for some less\-represented or extreme conditions\. Multilayer deposition further demonstrated stable roughness and defect\-free coating formation under the selected conditions\.

## [Laboratory\-measured functional abilities and refereeing quality in elite football referees](../publications/0bb9633742dfb4acdf73.md)

Ivan Krakan; Josip Tomaško; Ivan Belčić; Dario Novak

Introduction The aim of this study was to determine whether functional abilities are associated with the quality of refereeing in elite football referees\. Methods Seventeen referees from the highest Croatian national competition represented the complete referee list for the 2022/2023 season\. One referee sustained an injury during sprint testing and did not complete the physiological assessment\. The final analytical sample consisted of 16 referees\. Laboratory testing was performed in January 2023, between the first and second parts of the competitive season\. The analysed variables were maximal treadmill speed, speed at the ventilatory threshold, maximal heart rate, heart rate at the ventilatory threshold, absolute and relative maximal oxygen uptake, and relative oxygen uptake at the ventilatory threshold\. Refereeing quality was determined from official supervisor grades across the season, including the subsequent review of those grades by the national Referees Committee\. Results Mean relative maximal oxygen uptake was 51\.71 ± 4\.28 mL/kg/min, maximal treadmill speed was 18\.50 ± 1\.03 km/h, and the mean refereeing quality grade was 8\.21 ± 0\.26\. No statistically significant association was found between the examined functional variables and season\-long refereeing quality\. The full\-sample Spearman analysis showed the same overall pattern\. Discussion The small analytical sample limits the detection of weak and moderate associations\. The study hypothesis was not supported\.

## [Relationship Between Motives and Satisfaction in Using Chatgpt as a Medium Sharing Feeling](../publications/0bbc83e785e6359f3f04.md)

Risa Eryanti; Ratih Pandu Mustikasari

Many people are now turning to AI chatbots as conversational companions\. This trend is reflected in the finding that 73\.8% of respondents reported having used ChatGPT as a medium for expressing their feelings or confiding personal problems\. This emerging form of interaction between humans and artificial intelligence systems suggests that AI technology functions not only as an information retrieval tool but also as a communication space where Generation Z can express their emotions and personal experiences\. Therefore, understanding the motives that drive Generation Z to use ChatGPT and the level of satisfaction they obtain has become a relevant area of study, particularly from the perspective of the Uses and Gratifications Theory\. This study employed a quantitative correlational method using an online questionnaire distributed to respondents who met the predetermined criteria\. Data were analyzed through validity testing, reliability testing, classical assumption tests, and Spearman’s Rank correlation analysis using SPSS software\. The findings indicate a significant relationship between the motives and satisfaction of Generation Z in using ChatGPT as a medium for confiding personal problems\. Information motive emerged as the most dominant indicator, with respondents using ChatGPT to obtain information, explanations, advice, and new perspectives that helped them better understand and cope with the problems they were experiencing\. Meanwhile, cognitive needs gratification was identified as the most dominant satisfaction indicator, as respondents reported gaining greater understanding, useful information, and new perspectives regarding the issues they faced\. Keywords: Gen Z, Uses and Gratification, Artificial Intelligence, ChatGPT

## [Exploring collaborative problem\-solving in AI\-assisted robotics education](../publications/0bbf76848bd5e7caea0c.md)

Christian Basil Omeh; Elias Oupa Mashile

Prompt engineering \(PE\) involves creating, improving, and deploying prompts to improve large language model \(LLM\) performance\. Despite its increasing importance, many students lack skills in this area\. Although frameworks for prompt design and process exist, theory\-based instructional tools for improving prompt engineering skills are uncommon for developing collaborative problem\-solving \(CPS\) skills in Robotics Education\. This study adopted a PE strategy in AI\-assisted robotics education, particularly for developing CPS\. PE has four scaffolding stages: Alignment, Adaptation, Autonomy, and Innovation, and was analysed through four PE codes: Alignment Specification, Adaptive Refinement, Auditing, and Innovation\. This study adopted a non\-randomised, multi\-site, criterion\-group comparative design, with 243 undergraduate students categorised according to their ability group\. This study used epistemic network analysis \(ENA\) to identify the co\-occurrences of PE and CPS skills and examine the differences in conversation patterns among ability groups\. The findings revealed distinct PE–CPS discourse configurations across ability groups\. These results underscore the pedagogical value of scaffolding in developing PE skills and fostering students’ productivity in a synergetic learning environment\.

## [Slow Frontal Spindle Activity and Declarative Memory Retention During Daytime Naps](../publications/0bc75c48c457cff7bb0f.md)

Vaishali Mutreja; Prakriti Gupta; Ovidiu Lungu; Latifa Lazzouni; Arnaud Boutin; Ella Gabitov; Madeleine E\. Sharp; Julie Carrier; Julien Doyon

Memory consolidation refers to how newly encoded memories are strengthened and retained over time, and ample evidence indicates that sleep supports this process for both procedural and declarative memories\. Although sleep spindles during non\-rapid eye movement \(NREM\) sleep have been associated with consolidation, it remains unclear whether all spindle types contribute equally\. Spindles vary in frequency and topography, slow spindles \(≤ 12\.5 Hz\) predominating frontally, fast spindles \(&gt; 12\.5 Hz\) parietally and recent work suggests that procedural memory consolidation relates to the temporal organization of spindles in &\#x27;trains&\#x27; \(events occurring &lt; 6 s apart\)\. We investigated whether a similar mechanism operates for declarative memory during daytime naps\. Participants \(Nap, N = 23; No\-Nap, N = 15\) completed an object\-location task involving 36 item\-location associations, tested immediately after learning and again following a 90\-min nap opportunity or an equivalent wake period\. The Nap group exhibited significantly better delayed memory, measured by combined recall\-associative recognition scores and a greater proportion of nappers maintained or improved performance\. Within the Nap group, memory was positively associated with local spindle density at frontal and parietal sites and with the proportion of slow frontal spindles clustered in trains during NREM2\. Contrary to our expectations, however, these associations did not reach significance under two\-tailed testing, possibly reflecting the limited sample size and thus lack of statistical power for an experimental design based on naps\. Together, our results demonstrate a robust behavioural benefit of daytime naps for declarative memory retention and, more tentatively, point to slow frontal spindle activity as a candidate correlate for future work\.

## [Machine Learning to Distinguish Physiologic Causes of Hypoxemia After Bidirectional Glenn Using Bedside Markers](../publications/0bca16c5727311813b04.md)

Fabio Savorgnan; Paola Pilla; Sarah Visokay; Kaitlin Ness; Thomas J\. Fiedorek; Saúl Flores

Background: Hypoxemia after bidirectional Glenn palliation can result from distinct physiological mechanisms that may produce similar arterial oxygen saturation\. We evaluated whether routinely available bedside markers could recover physiological states encoded in a mechanistic virtual\-patient model\. Methods: A steady\-state zero\-dimensional closed\-loop model generated five causes of Glenn hypoxemia: elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, veno\-venous collateral shunting, pulmonary gas\-exchange impairment, increased metabolic demand, and ventricular dysfunction\. Hidden physiological variables were withheld from the classifier; inputs were SpO2, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, hemoglobin, Glenn/SVC pressure, and SVC oxygen saturation\. Because bedside patterns arise downstream from prespecified equations and phenotype perturbations, classification was interpreted as internal mechanistic recoverability rather than clinical diagnostic performance\. Results: Of 150,000 generated states, 127,162 passed broad physiological criteria and 66,269 met strict hypoxemia/hemodynamic criteria\. After balancing, 26,400 virtual patients were analyzed \(5280 per mechanism; 19,800 training and 6600 held\-out testing\)\. SpO2 alone achieved 26\.1% accuracy \(macro\-AUROC 0\.580\); the primary bedside model achieved 56\.1% accuracy \(95% CI 55\.0–57\.4%\) and macro\-AUROC 0\.845 \(95% CI 0\.840–0\.851\)\. Elevated PVR was the most readily recovered phenotype\. Glenn/SVC pressure and SVC saturation provided the largest incremental contributions, while broader measurement\-error assumptions substantially reduced performance\. Conclusions: Within this mechanistic simulation, multivariable bedside patterns allowed partial recovery of physiological states encoded by the model\. Because phenotypes and their observable consequences were generated from prespecified assumptions, the reported performance quantifies internal recoverability under those assumptions and should not be interpreted as diagnostic accuracy or as independent evidence of bedside information content in patients\. The model identifies testable physiologic signatures and areas of overlap for prospective clinical validation\.

## [Topology\-mediated deformation and failure mechanisms in heterogeneous cellular SiCp/Al composites revealed by mesoscale finite element analysis](../publications/0bd6c311903442823036.md)

Haipeng Chen; Zhong Zheng; Bo Yuan; Sainan Ma; Likun Wang; Bowen Gong; Wenting Ouyang; Dongming Chen; Cheng Liu; Xiang Gao

Introduction The spatial heterogeneity of reinforcement distribution strongly influences the mechanical response of particle\-reinforced metal matrix composites \(PRMMCs\)\. However, the respective roles of local reinforcement concentration and network connectivity in deformation and failure remain unclear\. Methods In this study, two\-dimensional mesoscale finite element models of SiCp/6061Al composites with identical global SiC volume fraction but distinct cellular architectures were developed\. By varying local SiC volume fraction and reinforcement\-rich region connectivity, the effects of heterogeneous particle distributions on stress transfer, strain localization, crack initiation and propagation were investigated\. Results The results demonstrate that moderate reinforcement localization enhances tensile strength by improving stress transfer efficiency, whereas excessive localization accompanied by network discontinuity deteriorates macroscopic load\-bearing capability\. Furthermore, local SiC concentration primarily determines damage initiation through intensified deformation incompatibility, while reinforcement network connectivity governs subsequent crack propagation behavior\. A continuous particle\-rich framework promotes efficient load transfer but accelerates crack transmission after damage initiation, whereas a disconnected network enhances crack deflection but reduces strengthening efficiency\. Discussion These findings establish a topology\-based design principle for heterogeneous SiCp/Al composites, emphasizing that reinforcement connectivity is essential for achieving a favorable balance between strength and damage tolerance\.

## [Spatiotemporal differentiation and determinants of abandoned farmland utilization in the Yangtze River Economic Belt](../publications/0bd7c6ee5c11f4851210.md)

Zhe Zhu; Shiwen Chen; Leyi Shao; Ping Li; Heran Zou; Yilong Sheng

As a stabilizer safeguarding China’s food security, the Yangtze River Economic Belt is troubled by farmland abandonment and inefficient utilization of abandoned farmland\. Therefore, clarifying the spatiotemporal differentiation and determinants of abandoned farmland utilization is critical to addressing challenges in cultivated land protection\. Based on the China Land Cover Dataset \(CLCD\), this study adopts land\-use trajectory analysis, kernel density analysis, and spatial autocorrelation analysis to explore core issues of abandoned farmland utilization from three dimensions: scale, efficiency and stability\. The results show that: \(1\) Since 2022, abandoned farmland utilization policies have raised the annual utilization rate by an average of 2\.5 percentage points\. Historical abandoned land stocks are absorbed evenly each year, shifting governance from clearing accumulated abandoned land arrears to regularly controlling newly abandoned farmland\. \(2\) Abandoned farmland utilization shows a striking west\-high and east\-low spatial agglomeration gradient: HH clusters distribute in the upper reaches and LL clusters in the lower reaches, with the upper and middle reaches achieving a 10\-percentage\-point 4\-year growth in utilization rates\. Utilization stability follows the middle reaches \(91\.12%\), upper reaches \(90\.28%\), and lower reaches \(85\.36%\)\. \(3\) Natural geography, economic levels, labor composition and institutional policies cause these disparities\. This research provides theoretical and practical support for differentiated regional governance of abandoned farmland and consolidated national food security\.

## [Interpretable MSME Credit Risk Prediction Through XGBoost Feature Selection and LSSVM Classification](../publications/0bdaf8029789e00f9d7f.md)

Sharmila Jeyarani S\.; Sanjay Raj J\.; Rajamannar N\.G\.; Sabari Anandh M\.

This research work proposes an interpretable hybrid ML approach to credit risk evaluation of MSMEs in supply chain financing, combining feature selection using XGBoost with classification using RBF\-LSSVM\. The credit information of the multi\-sourced variety is standardized into a common set of financial and operational variables followed by stratification, training normalization, and class balance through SMOTE technique to minimize the impact of minority class bias while maintaining test set independence\. Using the XGBoost classifier with TreeSHAP analysis of features selects the relevant predictors that are further classified using the RBF\-LSSVM classifier with calibrated probability estimation and optimized decision threshold for risk\-aware classification\. This proposed approach achieves 97\.96% accuracy, 94\.52% precision, 97\.43% recall, and 95\.95% F1\-score on the held\-out evaluation set\. SHAP and counterfactual explanations offer feature level interpretations of the risk assessments\.

## [Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection](../publications/0bde6218077551a3bd8c.md)

Kajaree Das; Oliver Böse; Subarnaduti Paul; Gabriel Storch; Martin Mundt

Deepfake detectors safeguard against misinformation, rendering their failures as much a societal as a technical concern\. As generators constantly evolve, detectors trained on static datasets miss newly arising threats, while progressive training interferes catastrophically\. Yet, mitigating forgetfulness in terms of accuracy, the prevalent focus of continual learning \(CL\), is insufficient to reflect real\-world impact\. We therefore scrutinize the effects of CL methods with respect to evolving fairness\. To this end, we analyze four dimensions of fairness across diverse demographics for detectors trained progressively on a chronological sequence of 11 real\-world deepfake generation methods\. Tracking fairness metrics over time, we expose non\-trivial interplays between performance and fairness that depend on both the choice of CL algorithm and demographic intersections\. We find accuracy degradation to typically exacerbate unfairness and, conversely, fairness improvements to remain scarce over time\. Dissecting the CL method families \(rehearsal, prompts, regularization\), we observe that inequitable forgetting is not explained by underrepresentation alone, but likely entangled with representation learning\. We thus issue a call to action for CL methods to take social outcomes into account when balancing the stability\-plasticity tradeoff\.

## [DRONES NA RECUPERAÇÃO DE BACIAS HIDROGRÁFICAS IMPACTADAS: REVISÃO DA AMOSTRAGEM HIDROQUÍMICA E DO REPOVOAMENTO ÍCTICO COMO PILARES OPERACIONAIS](../publications/0be322abfe8a8b5a7f59.md)

Christiano Pedro Guirlanda; Gabriela Luiza Almeida Silva; Ana Clara Cassin Cordeiro; Helen Martins Marques; Diego Fernandes Almeida Silva; Artur Jesus Araujo; Juan Canellas Bosch Netto

A recuperação de bacias hidrográficas impactadas por desastres de mineração depende de duas operações de campo onerosas, arriscadas e de baixa resolução espaço\-temporal: o monitoramento hidroquímico e o repovoamento íctico\. Os veículos aéreos não tripulados \(VANTs\) emergiram, na última década, como plataforma capaz de transformar ambas, deslocando o paradigma da observação passiva para a intervenção física\. Esta revisão adota desenho híbrido, com revisão sistemática \(PAGE et al, 2020\) para a amostragem de água por drone e análise prospectiva estruturada para o peixamento por drone\. Os achados evidenciam assimetria acentuada\. A amostragem hidroquímica por VANT é campo consolidado e estatisticamente validado, porém concentrado em corpos lênticos e incipiente em rios de fluxo rápido, nos quais a hidrodinâmica, a vegetação ripária e a perda de sinal GNSS impõem barreiras não resolvidas\. Em contraste, o peixamento por drone permanece praticamente ausente da literatura revisada por pares, embora a soltura aérea tripulada tenha décadas de uso e sobrevivência superior à dos métodos terrestres\. Argumenta\-se que essa lacuna é uma fronteira de engenharia, e não uma inviabilidade, e propõe\-se um arcabouço que integra amostragem, análise e liberação de alevinos em uma única cadeia de recuperação, ilustrada pela bacia do Rio Doce após o desastre de Fundão\.

## [IoT tabanlı içilebilir su kalitesi izleme sistemi](../publications/0be3f6bec2d44f36c86f.md)

Ali KAVURUR

Su kaynaklarının yerinde ve sürekli izlenmesi amacıyla, pH, bulanıklık, toplam çözünmüş katı madde \(Total Dissolved Solids:TDS\) ve sıcaklık parametrelerini eş zamanlı olarak takip eden, Wemos D1 Mini ESP32 mikrodenetleyicisi tabanlı düşük maliyetli ve gerçek zamanlı bir Nesnelerin İnternetini \(Internet of Things :IoT\) kullanan su kalitesi izleme sistemi geliştirilmiştir\. Sistemin temel amacı; yüksek işlem gücü, yoğun bellek ve enerji tüketen karmaşık Yapay Zeka \(YZ\) algoritmaları yerine, matematiksel Su Kalitesi İndeksini \(Water Quality Index: WQI\) doğrudan donanım üzerinde çalıştırarak anlık ve verimli bir değerlendirme ortaya koymaktır\. Sensörlerden alınan analog ve dijital veriler, Wemos D1 mikrodenetleyicisi bünyesinde işlenerek anlık olarak WQI skoruna dönüştürülmekte ve suyun içilebilirlik durumu yerel bir OLED ekran üzerinde gecikmesiz olarak gösterilmektedir\. Sistem, anlık takibin yanı sıra verileri gelecekteki tahmine dayalı analizler, geniş ölçekli veri madenciliği ve makine öğrenmesi çalışmaları için bulut tabanlı ThingSpeak platformuna aktarmaktadır\. Geliştirilen bu yaklaşım, donanım kaynaklarını asgari düzeyde tutarak gerçek zamanlı ve düşük maliyetli su kalitesi değerlendirmesi yapabilen, enerji verimli ve sürdürülebilir bir IoT mimarisi sunmaktadır\.

## [The Extent to which Heads of Schools Ensure Professional Development for Teachers in Integration of Digital Technologies into Teaching in Public Secondary Schools in Moshi Municipality Tanzania](../publications/0be43977f577c2fadc9b.md)

Carolie D\. Lucas; Eugene Lyamtane; Victorini Salema

This study examined the extent to which heads of schools ensure professional development for teachers in integration of digital technologies into teaching in public secondary schools in Moshi Municipality, guided by UTAUT Theory\. The study used a convergent mixed\-methods design to collect and integrate quantitative and qualitative data\. The study employed a convergent design under a mixedmethods research approach\. The target population was 718 individuals\. A sample of 147 respondents was selected through stratified random and purposive sampling, comprising 137 teachers and 5 Heads of Schools from five schools\. Instruments were validated by 3 research experts from the Department of Education Planning and Administration at Mwenge Catholic University\. The study collected quantitative data using questionnaires and qualitative data through an interview guide and an observation guide\. Data collection instruments were pilot\-tested in one public school\. Reliability for Likert\-type items was ensured using Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha coefficient, whereby alpha of 0\.923 was obtained from questionnaires for teachers\. The trustworthiness of qualitative data collection instruments was ensured through peer debriefing and triangulation techniques\. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics \(frequencies, percentages, and means\) via SPSS Version 27, while qualitative data were analysed thematically\. Ethical guidelines were observed through informed consent, anonymity and confidentiality\. The study finding show that Heads of Schools play an important role in ensuring professional development for teachers in the integration of digital technologies into teaching\. However, available training focuses mainly on basic computer literacy rather than pedagogical integration; inadequate subject\-specific professional development, and digital technology programs are not included in school development plans or annual calendars, make it difficult to allocate resources and monitor teachers’ progress\. The study concluded that the availability of digital resources alone does not ensure sustained pedagogical utilisation\. Consequently, effective digital technology integration requires not only strong school leadership but also sustainable and diversified mechanisms for teachers&\#x27; professional development, mobilising financial, infrastructural to ensure teachers&\#x27; technical support\. The study recommends strengthening practical teacher training, providing digital resources, integrating ICT into classroom supervision, and involving teachers in technology\-related decisions\.

## [Intelligent MPPT in PV Systems using metaheuristic\-optimised deep neural networks](../publications/0beb416d960221794ab2.md)

M\. Sheela; O\.V\. Gnana Swathika

Solar photovoltaic \(PV\) systems face problems with multiple local maxima, poor tracking efficiencies and unstable maximum power point tracking \(MPPT\) when the irradiance changes rapidly or when there is partial shading on the panels\. Traditional MPPT methods including Perturb and Observe \(P&amp;O\) and Incremental Conductance display slow convergence and oscillation around the steady state in the changing environment\. This paper proposes a Digital Twin\-based Grey Wolf Optimization \(GWO\-Deep Neural Network\) intelligent MPPT system for solar PV systems to overcome these two issues\.This paper proposes a hybrid Grey wolf optimization –Deep neural Network \(GWO\_DNN\) based MPPT technique for photovoltaic systems\. The comparison between hybrid deep neural network \(DNN\)\-based controllers for maximally tracking MPPs through Grey Wolf Optimisation \(GWO\), Golden Eagle Optimisation \(GO\) and Moth\-Flame Algorithm \(MFA\) are evaluated by comparing relative effectiveness based upon converging performance, prediction accuracy, computational efficiency and stability\. The proposed method improves tracking efficiency, reduces steady\-state oscillations and achieves faster convergence under varying irradiance conditions\. Computational models show GWO\-DNN controllers achieving lower test mean absolute distance from the true MPP compared to the other controllers with mean absolute mean square errors \(MAE\) reported as 0\.6138 V \(GWO\-DNN\), 0\.3506 V \(MFA\-DNN\) and 0\.4978 V \(GO\-DNN\)\. The GWO\-DNN controllers also have a lower degree of oscillation in steady\-state conditions, showing faster convergence than all other controllers as well as significantly lower prediction errors\. In contrast, Moses\-DNN performs more reliably with respect to optimal positioning, but its predictive capabilities will limit its effectiveness for practical real\-time implementation\. Although GO\-DNN provides lower inference time than both the GWO app and MFA model as is a whole, the standard deviation of how far down the MPP would be estimated will increase for the time taken to make the prediction\. A traditional CNN\-LSTM model has demonstrated to consistently underperform under dynamic operating conditions\. Thus, the results demonstrate that GWO\-DNN represents a superior balance of MPPT controller characteristics across dynamic operating ranges, as such, GWO\-DNN will provide the most robust and predictable MPP capability for use in smart solar energy applications\. This initiative helps meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals through the past improvements made in renewable energy extraction efficiency, the creation of more intelligent energy infrastructure and ultimately the contribution to greater levels of solar energy production, while also reducing wasted energy through better designs\. Specifically, it contributes to SDG7 \- Affordable and Clean Energy; SDG9 \- Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; and SDG13 \- Climate Action by facilitating the creation of sustainable, resilient and low\-carbon energy systems\.

## [Peningkatan Kesadaran Hukum Warga Terhadap Perlindungan Data Pribadi dan Konsekuensi Hukumnya di Era Digital](../publications/0bf618adf13f58962e46.md)

Syukron Abdul Kadir; Noor Rahmat; Bhenu SE Artha; Amirudin Amirudin; Sumantri Sumantri

The rapid development of information technology has led to an increased risk of personal data misuse in society\. A lack of understanding regarding the legal basis and methods for protecting personal data often leaves the general public vulnerable to cybercrimes, such as online fraud and illegal commercial lending\. This community service activity aims to provide education and legal counseling regarding the protection of personal data, the legal framework governing it, and the legal consequences for violators\. The method used was legal counseling in the form of interactive lectures and question\-and\-answer sessions\. The event was held on Friday, August 7, 2026, in the Celeban area, Umbulharjo District, Yogyakarta City, and was attended by 11 local residents\. The results of this activity showed an increase in residents’ understanding of the importance of maintaining the confidentiality of personal data, such as the National Identity Number \(NIK\) and the photo on their ID card, as well as an understanding of the legal protection mechanisms stipulated in Law No\. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection \(PDP Law\)\.

## [Growth mindset as a structural link between parental support and academic stress among mathematically high\-achieving elementary students with gifted education experience](../publications/0bf98ab98886b1c9dfc8.md)

Yile Wu; Doehee 안도희Ahn

Introduction Mathematically high\-achieving elementary students with gifted education experience may experience academic stress\. This study examined structural associations among perceived parental support, growth mindset, self\-regulated learning, and academic stress, with supplementary exploratory comparisons of latent means across gender\. Methods Cross\-sectional data from the second wave of the Korean Education Longitudinal Study 2013 \(KELS 2013\) were analyzed for 238 sixth\-grade students who had participated in gifted education programs and answered at least 22 of 25 items correctly on a mathematics basic competency assessment\. After testing measurement invariance across gender, latent mean differences were examined\. Structural equation modeling controlling for gender and 5,000 bias\-corrected bootstrap resamples were used to estimate direct and indirect associations\. Results Parental support was positively associated with growth mindset and self\-regulated learning, and growth mindset was positively associated with self\-regulated learning and negatively associated with academic stress\. The direct paths from parental support and self\-regulated learning to academic stress were not significant\. A significant negative indirect association between parental support and academic stress through growth mindset was found\. Supplementary gender comparisons indicated higher perceived parental support among boys and higher academic stress among girls\. Discussion A negative indirect association between perceived parental support and academic stress through growth mindset was observed in this sample\. The measures assessed general beliefs and academic experiences\. The cross\-sectional findings do not establish mathematics\-specific processes, temporal ordering, or causal mechanisms\.

## [Valorization of cotton waste into cellulose nanocrystals and their incorporation into electrospun poly \(vinyl alcohol\) nanofibrous membranes with enhanced thermal and structural properties](../publications/0bff6ef4fba083352b9a.md)

Wael Dagher; Abeer Alassod; Mhd Firas Al Hinnawi; Ibrahim Alghoraibi; Eyad Abdur\-Rahman

Cellulose nanocrystals \(CNCs\) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis\. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration from 40% to 62% was associated with an increase in CNC yield from approximately 19\.20 ± 3\.9% to 41\.30 ± 3\.1%, indicating the influence of acid concentration on the recovery of the nanocrystalline fraction under the conditions employed\. Energy\-dispersive X\-ray spectroscopy \(EDX\) showed carbon and oxygen as the predominant elements, at 62\.39 and 34\.33 wt%, respectively, with trace amounts of sulfur and sodium\. Scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\) revealed snowflake\-like aggregated structures composed of branched rod\-like features, with an average width of 56\.5 ± 8\.7 nm \. Atomic force microscopy \(AFM\) showed broadly consistent nanoscale morphological features, with snowflake\-like structures ranging from approximately 120–200 nm and protruding branches of approximately 63\.2 ± 10\.9 nm in diameter\. Fourier\-transform infrared spectroscopy \(FTIR\) showed characteristic cellulose bands, including the band at 872\.9 cm⁻¹ associated with β\-\(1→4\)\-glycosidic linkages\. CNCs were incorporated into poly \(vinyl alcohol\) \(PVA\) nanofibrous membranes at concentrations of 0–40 wt% via electrospinning\. Field\-emission scanning electron microscopy \(FESEM\) of the 40 wt% CNC membrane revealed a relatively uniform fibrous network with a mean fiber diameter of 104\.3 ± 38\.6 nm, with CNCs distributed on the fiber surfaces\. FTIR analysis of the prepared nanofibers showed the characteristic 916 cm⁻¹ band, supporting the presence of the cellulose component\. Thermogravimetric analysis \(TGA\) showed an increase in residual mass with increasing CNC content, from 1\.28% for the neat PVA membrane to 24\.88% for the 40 wt% CNC membrane\. Derivative thermogravimetry \(DTG\) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content\. The 40 wt% CNC formulation exhibited the highest residual mass among the studied formulations\. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes\.

## [CNN\-Based Target Detection Under Domain\-Mismatched and Low\-SNR Sub\-THz Radar Conditions](../publications/0c0fbfb8e1492a2b45b8.md)

Subhankar Shome; Suman Das; Vandana Yadav; Saumya Das; Sushmita Chaudhari

Abstract Sub\-THz radar systems enable high\-resolution sensing, which is critical for next\-generation intelligent sensing applications, but can suffer from poor performance in low\-SNR conditions, waveform distortion, phase instability, and non\-stationary clutter conditions\. A lightweight CNN framework is proposed in this article based on the domain of spectrogram to detect targets in sub\-THz sensing environments with degraded and mismatching environment\. In the framework proposed here, realistic sensing errors due to the stochastic variability of the clutter, impulsive interference, spreading of the spectrum and distortion of the phase and mismatch of the waveform when the data sets are generated are taken into account\. To enable the CNN to learn the distributed statistical target features in a cluttered environment, received radar signals are mapped into time\-frequency spectrogram representations using Short\-Time Fourier Transform \(STFT\)\. The robustness of operation can be tested by deliberately introducing a mismatch between training and testing environments, such as changes in the waveforms and noise background\. The proposed detector is compared to the conventional Matched Filter and spectral CA\-CFAR baselines in terms of ROC\-AUC, probability of detection and low\-false alarm\. The experimental results show that a CNN\-based framework can provide better robustness in low SNR and distorted sensing conditions, and it also showed that the proposed CNN framework outperforms conventional model\-driven detectors in terms of detection performance\. The results demonstrate the practicability of deep learning for the spectrogram space in a realistic non\-ideal sensing scenario for practical target detection in sub\-THz radar\.

## [Persistence of soil profile carbon fractions after ten years of tillage, crop rotation and residue management practice in a Haplic Plinthosol of South Africa](../publications/0c105d2d4d241bd42fab.md)

Sifundo November; Alen Manyevere; Dimpho Elvis Elephant; Adornis D\. Nciizah

Introduction Conservation agriculture \(CA\) has emerged as a sustainable farming practice for improving soil health and preserving soil organic carbon \(SOC\) fractions\. However, most studies in South Africa have focused on short\-term impacts and surface soil layers, leaving the long\-term effects of CA on SOC distribution throughout the soil profile poorly understood\. This study evaluated the persistence and distribution of SOC fractions after 10 years of CA implementation under different tillage, crop rotation, residue management, and soil depth treatments\. Methods The study was conducted on a long\-term field experiment established in 2012 using a randomized complete block design with a strip\-split\-split plot arrangement\. Treatments included no\-till \(NT\) and conventional tillage \(CT\), four crop rotations \(MFM, MFS, MWM, and MWS\), crop residue retention \(R\+\) and removal \(R−\), and three soil depths \(0−20, 20−40, and 40−60 cm\)\. Soil samples collected during the 2022 cropping season were analyzed for SOC, SOC stocks, particulate organic matter \(POM\), permanganate\-oxidizable carbon \(POXC\), total extractable carbon \(TEC\), humic acid \(HA\), fulvic acid \(FA\), and related humification indices\. Results No\-till \(NT\) increased SOC by 0\.64%, representing a 14\.06% improvement over conventional tillage \(CT\), with greater carbon sequestration in the 0−20 cm soil layer\. Crop rotation and residue retention enhanced particulate organic matter, particularly in the 0−20 and 20−40 cm depths\. Conventional tillage increased humic acid concentrations by 25\.40%, while NT increased fulvic acid concentrations by 41\.67% in the surface layer\. Principal component analysis identified SOC, HR, and TEC as the major drivers of SOC stock variability\. Discussion Conservation agriculture, particularly NT combined with crop rotation and residue retention, improved SOC and carbon quality indicators in the topsoil\. However, limited changes were observed in the 20−60 cm soil layers after 10 years, suggesting that longer\-term implementation and monitoring are required to achieve substantial subsoil carbon sequestration and stabilization\.

## [Has GPT\-6\-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?](../publications/0c18022a46fbe6082799.md)

 SenseNova; Joint Research Team;  :; Zhongang Cai; Ziang Cao; Tailai Chen; Han Chong Chua; Linjun Dai; Hanming Deng; Hokin Deng; Haiwen Diao; Chenjing Ding; Weichen Fan; Xiao Fu; Zerui Gong; Chenyang Gu; Zexin He; Zhi Hou; Bo Li; Qinyue Li; Quanzhou Li; Xiaowan Li; Zhichao Liao; Dahua Lin; Zilong Lin; Bo Liu; Chunxiao Liu; Pengfei Liu; Tianqi Liu; Ziwei Liu; Chen Change Loy; Lewei Lu; Jiapeng Luo; Yuexiao Ma; Liang Pan; Xingang Pan; Oscar Qian; Ziyi Shang; Yuyao Shao; Dawei Su; Dacheng Tao; Qingyi Tao; Quan Wang; Ruisi Wang; Xiaogang Wang; Ziyi Wang; Beichen Wen; Donghao Wu; Jiaxu Wu; Silei Wu; Xiaoming Wu; Zhonghua Wu; Hongcan Xiao; Weiye Xu; Atsushi Yamashita; Lei Yang; Zhe Yang; Baiqiao Yin; Wanqi Yin; Hanfei Zhao; Tianbo Zhong; Long Zhuo; Jing Zuo

GPT\-6\-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments\. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT\-6\-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field\. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT\-6\-Astra\. We conduct a large\-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands\. Under a unified protocol that allows in\-context learning \(ICL\) from training\-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT\-6\-Astra achieves unprecedented performance \(Fig\. 1\)\. Future research may focus on improving 1\) the generality of ICL 2\) cost and execution time, 3\) physical\-state verification, 4\) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5\) long\-horizon preservation of progress\. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control\. We identify that close\-loop coordination between a high\-level &quot;System 2&quot; reasoner \(i\.e\., GPT\-6\-Astra\) and a low\-level &quot;System 1&quot; controller \(e\.g\., π0\.5\) is costly but effective\. Third, we examine GPT\-6\-Astra on real\-world deployment\. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1\) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2\) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints\. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks\. We develop a prototype that 1\) derives tasks from real\-world needs, 2\) provides no in\-domain demonstrations, and 3\) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate\. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT\-6\-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence\.

## [Moderating roles of strategic innovation compensation effect on new quality productive forces and firm performance: Evidence from Chinese A\-share listed companies](../publications/0c182e569f21048c3fd3.md)

Kai Jiang; Haslinah Binti Muhamad; Mohammad Noor Hisham Osman

New Quality Productive Forces \(NQPF\) have become China’s primary policy imperative to drive high\-quality development of its economy\. However, empirical evidence on the effects of NQPF on firm performance and the conditions that strengthen such effects is limited\. Building upon the resource\-based view and innovation compensation theory \(Barney, 1991; Porter &amp; van der Linde, 1995\), this study explores the link between NQPF and firm value and the moderating role of the innovation compensation effect \(ICE\)\. Using two\-way fixed effects and instrumental variable \(IV\) analysis, the study examines a panel dataset of 4,256 Chinese A\-share listed companies between 2015 and 2024\. It finds that NQPF has a positive and significant effect on the long\-term value of firms\. Although the ICE \(measured as the invention patent ratio\) does not directly increase the value of a firm, it significantly increases the positive effect of NQPF on firm performance\. Furthermore, this moderating role is significantly stronger in non\-state\-owned enterprises, high\-tech industries, and companies in the Eastern and Central regions of China\. The results contribute to the existing evidence on NQPF, as they provide micro\-level evidence on the value creation mechanism of NQPF and have practical implications for policymakers and firms\.

## [The Navier\-Stokes equations blow up, and planes still fly](../publications/0c1c9815c35b3750cffd.md)

Amin Doostmohammadi

An AI system reports a proof that the Navier–Stokes equations can produce infinite velocities in a finite time\. For pure mathematics, this could be a major event\. For physics, it changes much less, and it gives no reason to doubt the equations that we use every day to fly aircraft, forecast the weather, and treat patients with cardiovascular disease\.

## [Artificial intelligences, their policies and regulations and criteria of technological sovereignty](../publications/0c1ec057f25a0ca9fea7.md)

Ariel Hernán Vercelli

Las inteligencias artificiales \(IA\) han dejado de ser una promesa\. Nada parece escapar a sus procesos de eficientización, a esta nueva traducción digital del mundo: optimización del tiempo, aprovechamiento del espacio y control estricto tanto de las conductas humanas como de las no\-humanas\. El rápido crecimiento mundial de las IA trajo todo tipo de declaraciones, estrategias, políticas y leyes\. En pocos años las regulaciones sobre las IA se transformaron en un tema central de la geopolítica mundial\. Ahora bien, ¿qué ocurrió con estas políticas y regulaciones sobre IA en la República Argentina \(tanto a nivel nacional como sub\-nacional\)? Aunque Argentina todavía no sancionó leyes sobre IA a nivel nacional, sí es posible identificar tanto iniciativas nacionales como numerosas políticas y decretos a nivel sub\-nacional\. Entre otras preguntas, estas iniciativas ¿cómo protegen \(o no protegen\) los intereses nacionales / provinciales? ¿Qué valores, principios y modelos se han tomado en cuenta? ¿Qué ha ocurrido con la soberanía tecnológica en materia de IA? En la ponencia, al igual que en el proyecto de investigación mayor, se analiza el concepto de soberanía tecnológica, sus complejidades y los criterios a la hora de evaluar y fortalecer las políticas y regulaciones sobre IA\.

## [Towards Reconstructing Geographically Diverse Architecture with 3D Foundation Models](../publications/0c20b05632f546100ae5.md)

Nicky Kriplani; Yiwen Zhang; Angelina Wang; Hadar Averbuch\-Elor

Internet\-scale photo collections of real\-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models \(3DFMs\) that estimate scene structure in a single feed\-forward pass\. In this work, we introduce ArchWorld, a benchmark of 3D architectural landmarks with high geographic coverage and rich metadata\. We use this benchmark to conduct a thorough error analysis of current 3DFMs to understand where they fall short and how they can be improved\. We examine socially relevant disparities in model error and find that model performance varies by geographic region; however, unlike typical fairness regimes, the trends only partially match training data representation\. Our investigation reveals that the observed geographic disparities reflect not only differences in data representation and scene size but also differences in region\-specific architectural features and background distractors that make scenes from different regions inherently vary in difficulty\. Leveraging insights from these model failings, we introduce an intervention scheme that improves 3DFM performance while simultaneously reducing geographic disparities\.

## [Calibrated Probabilistic Predictions for Phishing Email Detection Using Sentence\-BERT with Machine Learning Models](../publications/0c20df5e7c8edd4c4029.md)

Oluwasegun Abiodun Abioye; Abraham Eseoghene Evwiekpaefe; Philip Oshiokhaimhele Odion

Phishing email detection poses a critical challenge in cybersecurity, and addressing it requires integrating calibrated probabilistic predictions with advanced semantic embeddings from Sentence\-BERT \(SBERT\)\. Phishing remains a persistent threat, exploiting deceptive emails to obtain sensitive information\. Although many detection models focus on maximizing accuracy, they often disregard probability calibration, which is essential for trustworthy decision\-making\. To improve reliability, the all\-mpnet\-base\-v2 SBERT model was employed to capture deep semantic representations of emails, strengthening the distinction between phishing and legitimate messages\. Nine machine learning and deep learning classifiers, including tree\-based ensembles \(Extra Trees, Random Forest, LightGBM\), linear \(Logistic Regression\), probabilistic \(Gaussian Naïve Bayes\), instance\-based \(k\-Nearest Neighbors\), neural networks \(Multi\-Layer Perceptron, Gated Recurrent Unit\), and kernel\-based \(Support Vector Machine\) were tested on a balanced dataset enhanced with SMOTE\. Evaluation metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, and the Brier score, which measures calibration quality\. Results show that although most classifiers achieved strong accuracy, their calibration performance varied\. LightGBM, MLP, GRU, and SVM produced superior calibration with lower Brier scores, delivering more reliable probability estimates for phishing risk assessment\. Conversely, Gaussian Naïve Bayes showed weaker calibration, reflecting the limitations of conditional independence assumptions with complex embeddings\. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of combining robust semantic feature extraction with calibrated probabilistic predictions to improve both effectiveness and trustworthiness in phishing detection systems\. This integrated approach strengthens cybersecurity operations by enabling more nuanced, confidence\-aware decision\-making\.

## [AI赋能在地国际化：宁波港口文化融入跨文化教学的实践路径](../publications/0c30a92779db9eb7b6fc.md)

Luo Jun

在地国际化是地方高校提升人才培养质量与服务区域开放能级的重要路径，但当前跨文化教学仍面临本土文化缺位、技术赋能浅表化及国际传播实践能力薄弱等困境。本研究以宁波港口文化为载体，构建“AI赋能\+在地文化\+跨文化能力”三维融合的课程改革模式。通过生成式AI实现文化资源的双语转化与知识图谱构建，设计涵盖AI角色扮演、人机协同创作及数据驱动评价的沉浸式教学闭环，推动文化认知向跨文化交际与国际传播实践转化。基于《跨文化能力发展》课程的实证表明，该模式可显著提升学生的跨文化敏感度、语用适切性及外语叙事能力，并建成可复用的AI辅助教学资源库。研究验证了AI在深化在地国际化教学中的增量价值，为地方高校依托区域特色开展数智化跨文化育人提供了可迁移范式与伦理反思路径。

## [Globally guided multi\-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning](../publications/0c30bbdf1357f2b65cef.md)

Xu Wang; Qi Liu; Haotian Li

Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles \(UAVs\) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments\. Existing multi\-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning\. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Globally Guided Decoupled\-Critic Multi\-Agent Soft Actor\-Critic algorithm \(GDC\-MASAC\)\. RRT $$^\*$$ \-based global guidance provides reference waypoints for the leader UAV, reducing inefficient exploration and local deadlocks\. Three decoupled Critic branches separately evaluate target navigation, formation maintenance, and safety objectives, while an environment\-aware formation reward adjustment relaxes formation tracking near obstacles according to the distance to obstacle boundaries\. Experiments under different obstacle densities and swarm sizes show that GDC\-MASAC improves mission completion, collision avoidance, and formation coordination\. In a scenario with 12 obstacles and 3 UAVs, GDC\-MASAC achieves a mission success rate of 86%, whereas the baseline methods achieve success rates below 50%\. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GDC\-MASAC for cooperative multi\-UAV path planning in cluttered environments\.

## [Really Need Recursion? Revisiting One\-pass Registration with Multi\-level Multi\-space Contextual Guidance](../publications/0c38ad11852ff5db03eb.md)

Yue Lin; Shenghai Wu; Mingyuan Meng

Deformable image registration is a fundamental challenge in medical image analysis\. Recent deep learning\-based methods typically adopt either one\-pass architectures that complete registration in a single network iteration, or recursive architectures that refine registration through multiple passes\. While recursive methods often improve accuracy, they incur substantial computational overhead and slower inference speed\. In this paper, we challenge the necessity of recursion for high\-performance deformable registration and propose M2CG, a one\-pass registration network with Multi\-level Multi\-space Contextual Guidance\. It performs multi\-step progressive pyramid registration within a single iteration, guided at each step by contextual cues from three levels \(previous, current, and subsequent steps\) and four spaces \(image space, image feature space, segmentation space, and segmentation feature space\)\. Our M2CG supports both unsupervised \(without any labels\) and semi\-supervised \(with segmentation labels for partial training data\) registration, and has achieved state\-of\-the\-art performance across two well\-benchmarked inter\-/intra\-patient medical registration tasks with eight public datasets\. Our findings suggest that the current reliance on recursion may stem from the absence of sufficient contextual cues that comprehensively characterize the remaining distance to the target alignment\.

## [GRU\-KAN: A Hybrid Recurrent–Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for Low\-latency 3D Hand Gesture Classification Using Direct Kinematic Features from Skeletal Data](../publications/0c575828bb42f5f43cd1.md)

Israa F\. Fatih; Wisam S\. Hacham; Muhannad K\. Sabir

The conventional hand\-gesture recognition method is based on complicated signal processing, such as Kalman filtering and Fast Fourier Transform \(FFT\), and the Electromyography \(EMG\) / Inertial Measurement Unit \(IMU\) based method has the disadvantages of handcrafting and latency\.In this paper, a vision\-based framework is proposed that operates directly on raw 3D skeletal streams, avoiding the classic pre\-processing steps, and allows the extraction of 14 kinematic descriptors in a lightweight manner\.To achieve gesture recognition, a hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit\-Kolmogorov\-Arnold Network \(GRU\-KAN\) architecture is proposed in which the temporal model is built using a Gated Recurrent Unit and the non\-linear classification model is a Kolmogorov\-Arnold Network, whose learnable B\-spline activations do not cause vanishing gradients when using skip connections\.The model achieves a test accuracy of 90\.0% on a held\-out test set of 70 sequences \(10 per gesture\), drawn from a total dataset of 350 sequences across seven gestures\.The latency\-optimized CPU configuration achieves this accuracy with an inference latency of 57\.06 ms per pre\-segmented sequence, suitable for edge deployment\.The proposed GRU\-KAN outperforms a controlled GRU\-MLP baseline \(85\.71%\) by \+4\.29 percentage points under identical encoder and training conditions\.On the FPHA public benchmark \(45 classes, 1,175 sequences, variable\-length\), GRU\-KAN achieves 66\.81% versus 64\.68% for the matched GRU\-MLP baseline, confirming the KAN classifier&\#x27;s consistent advantage under an identical recurrent encoder and training protocol\.The results demonstrate that GRU\-KAN exhibits better convergence stability and classification accuracy than a matched GRU\-MLP baseline under identical encoder and training protocols\.

## [Scalable long\-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling](../publications/0c6802ec3fe3d83e2897.md)

Yicheng Chen; Xiaoyun Yu; Hyejeong Song; Xintian Wang; Zihui Li; Zixi Xia; Junmin Chen; Peichen Zhong

Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long\-range electrostatics and electrical\-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first\-principles methods\. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine\-learning interatomic potentials \(MLIPs\)\. Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long\-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation\. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long\-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges \(BECs\) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges\. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions\. Implemented as DPA4C\-LR on the \\texttt\{nvalchemi\} platform, the framework scales to 5\.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short\-range backbone\. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C\-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field\-dependent infrared spectra of water\. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \\ce\{Pb\(Mg\_\{1/3\}Nb\_\{2/3\}\)O3\}, which is obscured by finite\-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room\-temperature field\-driven ionic conductivity of $6\.8 \\pm 0\.7$\~mS/cm in amorphous \\ce\{Li\_\{0\.9\}NbO\_\{0\.9\}Cl\_\{4\.1\}\}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab\-corrected electrostatics\. By combining long\-range physics, electrical\-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device\-relevant length scales\.

## [Unravelling the planetary health diet index\-depression nexus: utilisation of network and machine learning approaches](../publications/0c6b69c86c62109d0aad.md)

Jiaci Lin; Bo Hu; Liuna Geng

Adherence to the planetary health diet index \(PHDI\) is associated with health benefits, but its relationship with depression, particularly the roles of dietary components and symptoms, remains poorly understood\. We aimed to \(1\) compare PHDI component interrelationships between individuals with and without depression; \(2\) identify PHDI components most predictive of depression using machine learning and \(3\) identify bridge nodes connecting PHDI components with depressive symptoms\. This cross\-sectional study analysed data from 25 542 adults in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005\-2018\. The PHDI was calculated from two 24\-h dietary recalls\. Depression was assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire\-9 with scores ≥10 indicating depression\. We employed network analysis to compare dietary structures, an extreme gradient boosting \(XGBoost\) model interpreted using shapley additive explanations \(SHAP\) values to identify predictors and bridge network analysis to identify bridge nodes connecting the PHDI and depressive symptom communities\. The PHDI network in the non\-depressed group was more densely connected than in the depressed group\. SHAP analysis of the XGBoost model identified non\-starchy vegetables \(PHDI2\) and added sugars \(PHDI14\) as the most important predictors, with higher component scores associated with a lower predicted probability of depression\. In the bridge network analysis, appetite problems \(PHQ5\) and depressed mood \(PHQ2\) emerged as the strongest bridge nodes between the PHDI and depressive symptom communities\. A structured, plant\-forward dietary pattern was associated with lower depression levels, with appetite problems and depressed mood identified as the bridge nodes between the PHDI and depressive symptom communities\.

## [Цифровая трансформация туристической отрасли как драйвер изменения требований к компетенциям персонала](../publications/0c724cd8bdc51aed9615.md)

Natal&\#x27;ya V\. TROFIMOVA; Э\. Р\. Мамлеева; Marina Sazykina; М\.А\. Ризванова

В статье анализируется влияние цифровой трансформации туристической отрасли России на требования к компетенциям персонала\. На основе статистических данных и отраслевых отчётов за 2024–2025 гг\. выявлены ключевые тренды: интеллектуализация гостиничного бизнеса, внедрение искусственного интеллекта, развитие государственных цифровых платформ\. Показано, что цифровизация ведёт к автоматизации рутинных операций, появлению гибридных функций и новых профессиональных ролей\. Систематизированы цифровые компетенции \(базовые, продвинутые, специализированные\)\. Оценено соответствие образовательных программ запросам рынка, выявлены региональные диспропорции\. Предложены направления модернизации профессионального образования\. The article analyzes the impact of digital transformation of the Russian tourism industry on the requirements for personnel competencies\. Based on statistical data and industry reports for 2024–2025, key technological trends are identified: intellectualization of the hotel business, introduction of artificial intelligence, development of government digital platforms, and import substitution of IT solutions\. It is shown that digitalization leads to automation of routine operations, emergence of hybrid job functions and new professional roles\. The demanded digital competencies are systematized into three levels: basic, advanced, and specialized\. The compliance of existing higher and secondary vocational education programs with current labor market demands is assessed, and regional disparities and content gaps in personnel training are identified\. Based on the obtained data, directions for modernizing the vocational education system in the digital economy are proposed\.

## [THE RELATIONS BETWEEN LANGUAGE AND THOUGHT](../publications/0c7aba655848146b4e91.md)

Jasmina Jamshidovna Dusaliyeva; Khadicha Mamatkulova

This article synthesizes key theoretical and empirical perspectives on the relationship between language and thought across linguistics, psycholinguistics, and cognitive science\. Examining contributions from Humboldt, Sapir, Whorf, Vygotsky, Piaget, and Chomsky alongside modern empirical studies, it demonstrates that language and thought continuously interact, shaping human perception, categorization, and executive cognition\.

## [PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence\-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents](../publications/0c8d4b1836117d96c28e.md)

Hamed Khosravi; Xiaoming Huo

LLM agents are used to check records against an organization&\#x27;s requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation\. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator\-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link\. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed\. We introduce PRIME \(Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence\)\. Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified\. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify\. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself\. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger\. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion\. On 480 public\-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26\.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none\. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30\.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59\.2 out of 100\.

## [The New Southbound Aesthetic: Artistic Collaboration and Talent Cultivation Between Taiwan and India](../publications/0c8f62356e1127300e4d.md)

Rachana Ahire

Contemporary Asian painting is experiencing a significant ontological transformation, shifting from exclusively physical media to digital\-hybrid practices\. In Taiwan and India, artists increasingly combine traditional media, including gouache, ink, and folk motifs, with digital tools, E\-Ink displays, and generative processes\. This technological integration functions as a form of postcolonial resistance to geopolitical instability and essentialist identities\. This study examines how digital\-hybrid painting serves as a mechanism for envisioning resilient, non\-essentialist futures, with particular attention to the concepts of &quot;precarious intelligence&quot; in Taiwan and &quot;diasporic flux&quot; within the Indian diaspora\. The research also evaluates the significance of artistic collaboration between these two nations within the framework of the New Southbound Policy\. Employing a qualitative, comparative analytical framework based exclusively on secondary data, the study conducts a thematic synthesis of exhibition catalogs \(including the 2025 Venice Biennale Pavilion\), museum records from the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts, artist statements, and scholarly articles published between 2024 and 2026\. The findings indicate that, despite differing sources of instability cross\-strait tensions and environmental uncertainty in Taiwan, and fractured belonging in the Indian diaspora both contexts utilize digital hybrids to reclaim cultural agency\. Taiwanese artists employ these mediums to articulate a democratically paradoxical identity and resist authoritarian narratives\.
