In contrast, Indian diaspora artists reconfigure historical elements, such as Mughal miniatures, to challenge colonial visual regimes and ethnic commodification\. The study concludes that digital\-hybrid painting creates a critical &quot;third space&quot; that dismantles traditional boundaries and establishes essential pathways for technological and artistic collaboration between Taiwan and India, thereby resisting global hegemonies in a precarious international context\.

## [The Illusion of Reality: From The Truman Show to Social Media\-The New Prisoners of Consumer Society](../publications/0ca642d38489301d923a.md)

Nargis Özgen; Sena CONKOĞLU

Since its emergence, capitalism has functioned not only as an economic formation but also as a political and ideological order\. What is distinctive today is that these effects have become more visible and data\-driven within digital environments\. The dynamics of the consumer society ensure that individuals are positioned not only as consumers but also as marketing objects\. In this context, cinema stands out as a critical tool that makes visible the effects of the capitalist system on individuals\. This study semiotically analyzes the effects of the capitalist system on individuals and the functioning mechanisms of the consumer society through Peter Weir’s The Truman Show \(1998\) within the framework of Peirce’s triple sign model and Barthes’s semiotic framework\. The study analyzes the semiotic codes of the film and examines the control mechanisms of the capitalist order on the individual\. In the film, the artificial world in which Truman lives is constructed as a symbolic model of the modern consumer society and a critical narrative is presented about the position of the individual within the system\. Truman’s process of awareness allows the individual to question the concepts of freedom and reality and offers a criticism of the invisible limits of today’s consumer society\. The main research problem of the study is to reveal how the voluntary participation of today’s individuals in surveillance and consumption mechanisms is represented in the movie\. The findings show that today’s individuals live in a system like Truman; however, today, individuals voluntarily turn into marketing objects\. Today’s digital content producers are active participants in the system by turning their own lives into commodities through social media and digital platforms\. In this context, The Truman Show is not only a work of cinema, but also a critical narrative that discusses the impact of the capitalist order on the individual and the invisible boundaries of modern consumer culture\.

## [Next Token or Vector? Learning How Far to Decode](../publications/0ca6f3a4fe5aa483be03.md)

Sai Sreenivas Chintha; Chidera Biringa; Rishab Sharma; Anusha Agrawal; Prachi Badarayani; Gemma Zhang; Nigel Boachie Kumankumah; Marco Ayala; Sulaiman Vesal

Standard autoregressive decoding advances one token at a time, even when several upcoming tokens can be predicted together\. We propose CADENCE \(Context\-Adaptive DEcoding\), a generation method that learns both what to draft and how far to draft\. Gaussian prediction heads represent future spans as continuous latent vectors, and a shared decoder converts the selected vector into token predictions in parallel\. A learned router selects the prediction length from the model&\#x27;s own hidden states and predicted Gaussian parameters, adapting generation granularity to the current context with single\-token generation as a fallback\. The backbone verifies each proposed continuation and retains the prefix that matches its greedy predictions\. Experiments with Llama\-3\.1\-8B\-Instruct on Alpaca, GSM8K, and HumanEval show that router\-selected positions yield higher draft acceptance than applying the corresponding prediction length everywhere\. CADENCE achieves up to 1\.3x higher generation throughput than standard greedy decoding\.

## [Memory Reconstruction in Complex PTSD: A Case Illustration of Guided Imagery in Metacognitive Interpersonal Therapy](../publications/0cac3c4741d0d22852de.md)

Félix Inchausti; Nancy V\. García‐Poveda; Marta Pérez‐Jiménez; Roberto Maluenda\-Gatica

This article describes the use of guided imagery within Metacognitive Interpersonal Therapy \(MIT\) in the treatment of a woman with a history of relational trauma and severe emotional dysregulation\. The case of Alicia, a 49\-year\-old patient with disorganized attachment and longstanding interpersonal difficulties, is presented to illustrate how imagery\-based interventions can facilitate emotional processing and change\. Treatment focused on helping Alicia understand and manage intense emotional reactions that were often experienced as overwhelming and confusing\. In one key session, a panic episode occurring in a supermarket\-whose origins were traced to earlier experiences of humiliation and threat\-was explored using guided imagery\. The intervention aimed to help her remain present, access a sense of safety, and develop a more adaptive response to the situation\. A session transcript shows how grounding, therapist attunement, and imagery work supported Alicia in moving from a state of helplessness to a sense of stability and control\. Over the course of treatment, she showed improvements in emotional awareness, interpersonal functioning, and overall distress\. This case highlights how guided imagery can be used within MIT to help patients access emotionally meaningful experiences and develop new ways of understanding and responding to them\.

## [Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes](../publications/0cadab476d004a543662.md)

Camille Brouillon; Alina Pushkarev; Marjorie A\. Liénard; Songhwan Hwang; Arno Munhoven; Richard J McDowell; Robert James Lucas; Megan L\. Porter; Han Sun; Peter Hegemann

Stomatopod crustaceans \(mantis shrimps\) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear\. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning\. Two mid\-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long\-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red\-sensitive animal rhodopsins\. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception\. Row\-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far\-red spectrum\.

## [How Veterans with PTSD Experience Symptom Improvement from Social Support](../publications/0caf8b2ac1d437d6b9b9.md)

Patti &quot;Lori&quot; Beisner

Social support is a concept that is simple to grasp, yet subjective in nature and difficult to describe\. Current research abounds reporting the positive impact of social support upon veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\)\. However, few studies describe the phenomenon of social support for combat veterans, which they attribute to PTSD symptom improvement\. The purpose of this study was to address this gap in research by exploring the lived experiences of veterans who have improved symptoms that they attribute to support they have received\. Semi\-structured interviews were conducted with eight combat veterans who self\-reported PTSD symptom improvement due to social support and were 18 years old or older\. Descriptive phenomenological analysis was utilized to extract themes from the experiences of the participants\. Twelve themes emerged from the research: coming alongside, remaining and being there through it all, shared knowledge or went through similar experiences, individualized, no surprises or judgement, essential or critical, life\-sustaining, safety, camaraderie, normalized, relief/peace/decreased guilt, and providing alternative perspective\. These themes were discussed from the perspective of the cognitive model of PTSD\. The findings of this research demonstrate how social support can manifest from the perspective of the veteran\. Furthermore, the results provide a deep and rich illustration of social support from which supporters can emulate in their interactions with veterans they care about for the purpose of alleviating their PTSD symptoms\.

## [AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions](../publications/0cb755e191154bd6ac78.md)

Alexey A\. Bokov; Ivan I\. Panin; Nikolay B\. Nechaev; Mikhail Yu\. Valkov; Valeria Yu\. Chernina; Natalia Gombolevskaya; Ayyaz Hussain; Vladimir M\. Agafonov; Victor A\. Gombolevskiy; Aleksandr V\. Nesterov; Iaroslav R\. Bespalov; Ivan V\. Oseledets; Dmitry V\. Dylov

Large language models \(LLMs\) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe\. We developed a multidimensional benchmark using 300 diagnostically resolved NEJM\-\-MedQA cases: 110 for physician reference ratings and Judge calibration and 190 for held\-out evaluation\. Eight single\-model pipelines generated independent role\-specific opinions and interactive\-consilium reports under free\-form and structured clinical\-reasoning conditions\. A physician\-calibrated LLM Judge evaluated 3,040 final reports and the corresponding structured primary\-role outputs\. Model identity separated report quality more strongly than response format\. Structured final reports had higher overall mean scores in seven of eight model pipelines, with their clearest advantage in management \(2\.740 vs\. 2\.436\)\. Compared with the structured pre\-consilium primary\-role opinion, the complete structured synthesis had higher pooled scores across all five shared criteria, with the largest increases in problem prioritization, factual grounding, and reasoning coherence\. GPT\-5\.6\-Sol led every evaluated component and reached consensus in the fewest review rounds\. These findings show that the benchmark can distinguish model capability, the contribution of multidisciplinary synthesis, criterion\-specific effects of response structure, deliberation dynamics, and inference requirements within one common\-case evaluation\.

## [Semiotic Landscapes of Deli Serdang Traditional Markets: Linguistic, Visual, Material, and Spatial Expressions of Cultural Identity and Local Wisdom](../publications/0cc7dbbf43d5316b1a0d.md)

Ely Ezir; Apriliyanti Apriliyanti; Devi Anisa Marpaung; Muhammad Ali Pawiro; Dedy Suhery; Mohd Hamid Raza

Traditional markets represent important cultural semiotic spaces where linguistic, visual, material, and spatial signs reflect social interaction, cultural identity, and local wisdom within community life\. This study aims to examine the semiotic landscapes of traditional markets in Deli Serdang, Indonesia, focusing on how multimodal signs express and negotiate cultural identity and local wisdom\. The study employed a qualitative semiotic approach grounded in Scollon and Scollon’s geosemiotics and Kress and van Leeuwen’s multimodal theory\. The research was conducted in selected traditional markets in Deli Serdang Regency, North Sumatra, involving traders, buyers, and market administrators as participants\. Data were collected through visual documentation, participant observation, in\-depth interviews, and field notes\. The analysis focused on market signage, vendor–customer interactions, spatial arrangements, and culturally significant artefacts\. The findings reveal that traditional markets function not only as economic and communicative spaces but also as cultural texts that encode communal values such as reciprocity, mutual trust, and social cohesion\. Identity negotiation is reflected through the use of vernacular languages, hybrid linguistic forms, and culturally embedded interactional practices that demonstrate continuity and adaptation amid modernization\. Local wisdom is maintained through symbolic artefacts, ritualized practices, and moral values embedded in everyday market transactions\. The study concludes that traditional markets in Deli Serdang constitute dynamic semiotic spaces that actively preserve cultural identity and local wisdom while strengthening cultural resilience and social harmony\.

## [A Cluster\-Based Technology Roadmapping Approach for Strategic Management of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare](../publications/0cd097b59f5914ab95a6.md)

Şakire Nesli DEMİRCİOĞLU; Serkan Altuntaş; Turkay Dereli

Technology roadmapping is a key strategic concern for companies\. The aim of this study is to propose a cluster\-based technology roadmapping approach using patent documents\. The proposed approach is applied to artificial intelligence \(AI\) technology\. The proposed approach provides evidence\-based decision\-making in healthcare management by identifying and prioritizing artificial intelligence \(AI\) technology domains with high long\-term success potential\. Unlike existing studies in the literature, the proposed approach integrates weighted evaluation criteria with market trends and product feature characteristics, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of technological relevance from a managerial perspective\. The applicability of the proposed approach is demonstrated through an empirical case study on AI applications in the healthcare domain\. The findings suggest that medical image processing, diagnosis and treatment support systems, electronic communication technologies, interactive robotic systems, and acoustic and haptic feedback technologies are expected to play a significant role in the long\-term development of healthcare services\.

## [For Patients With Sequelae From Bell&\#x27;s Palsy, Electrical Stimulation May Cause Increased Synkinesis When Aggressively Applied in the Acute Phase of Recovery](../publications/0cdb8e76b2edb0513025.md)

Soyeon Jung; Ji Hae Lee; Jun Sung Sur; Min Young Kwak; Jae‐Joong Kim

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the phase\-specific impact of cumulative nonselective electrical stimulation \(ES\) on long\-term functional sequelae and subsequent botulinum toxin \(BoNT\) therapeutic durability in patients with severe Bell&\#x27;s palsy\. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 317 patients with severe unilateral Bell&\#x27;s palsy \(predominantly ≥ 90% ENoG degeneration, all ≥ 80%\) who developed clinically confirmed facial synkinesis were analyzed\. Patients were stratified based on ES onset timing \(acute &lt; 1 month, subacute 1\-6 months, and chronic &gt; 6 months\) and cumulative duration\. Outcomes were assessed using the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System, Synkinesis Assessment Questionnaire \(SAQ\), and BoNT durability \(duration of effect\)\. Age\-adjusted analysis \(ANCOVA\) and machine\-learning\-based decision tree regression were employed to identify prognostic thresholds\. RESULTS: ES exposure was significantly associated with increased synkinesis \(9\.32 vs\. 8\.27, p = 0\.007\) and reduced BoNT durability \(3\.15 vs\. 4\.51 months, p &lt; 0\.001\) compared to the non\-ES group\. A critical safety threshold for cumulative ES was identified at 4\.64 h, beyond which synkinesis scores deteriorated by 35\.7% and BoNT durability decreased by 23\.8%\. Notably, ES showed a strict phase\-dependent dichotomy: acute\-phase ES correlated with the highest synkinesis \(p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas chronic\-phase ES was associated with significantly lower synkinesis \(6\.11 ± 2\.05\) and superior functional recovery compared to both acute\-phase and non\-ES cohorts \(p = 0\.015\)\. CONCLUSIONS: The impact of ES on facial nerve recovery is highly phase\-specific\. While chronic\-phase application offers therapeutic potential, excessive acute\-phase ES correlates with exacerbated synkinesis and reduced BoNT durability\. Our data suggest a cumulative safety threshold of 4\.64 h, emphasizing the need for a judicious, time\-dependent approach to ES during the acute phase of nerve regeneration\.

## [The Impact of Problem\-Based Learning \(PBL\) on Intellectual Indicators: A Comparative Analysis of STEM and Humanities Disciplines](../publications/0ce562d8604960a089eb.md)

Алишер Эрназаров

This study investigates the influence of problem\-based learning \(PBL\) on students&\#x27; intellectual development, comparing its effects within STEM and humanities disciplines\. The paper reviews contemporary experimental, quasi\-experimental, and mixed\-methods approaches to measuring cognitive and metacognitive change, describes the adaptation of PBL to the specific demands of STEM and humanities coursework, and outlines a prospective research design—including growth\-curve and hierarchical Bayesian modeling—for tracking long\-term cognitive outcomes\. The findings indicate that PBL meaningfully strengthens critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and independent problem\-solving in both fields, with STEM disciplines showing a stronger effect on logical and systemic reasoning and humanities disciplines showing a stronger effect on critical interpretation and reflective ability\. Implementation challenges, limitations, and directions for future research are discussed, and recommendations are offered for institutions seeking to adopt PBL in a discipline\-sensitive manner\.

## [Anterior\-to\-Posterior vs Direct Posterior Fixation of the Posterior Malleolus in Weber Type C Trimalleolar Ankle Fractures](../publications/0cec75a8d6428f18c54e.md)

Ahmet Polat; Mustafa Polat; Enes Başer; Yasin Kılıc; Osman Yüksel YAVUZ

Objective: To compare early and 1\-y outcomes after anterior\-to\-posterior screw fixation and direct posterior fixation of the posterior malleolus in Weber type C trimalleolar ankle fractures\. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 183 patients: 78 treated with anterior\-to\-posterior fixation and 105 with direct posterior fixation\. The visual analog scale \(VAS\), Olerud\-Molander Ankle Score \(OMAS\), and American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society \(AOFAS\) ankle\-hindfoot score were assessed at 3 mo and 1 y\. Radiological alignment, residual posterior step\-off, ankle motion, and return to work were also compared\. Results: At 3 mo, posterior fixation was associated with lower VAS scores \(mean \[SD\], 0\.99 \[1\.07\] vs 2\.09 \[1\.14\]\), higher OMAS \(mean \[SD\], 82\.11 \[6\.68\] vs 72\.76 \[8\.78\]\), and higher AOFAS scores \(mean \[SD\], 85\.19 \[6\.82\] vs 76\.78 \[7\.87\]; all P &lt; \.001\)\. These scores did not differ significantly at 1 y\. Syndesmotic screw fixation was less frequent after posterior fixation \(4\.8% vs 94\.9%; P &lt; \.001\)\. Residual posterior step\-off was slightly lower after posterior fixation \(mean \[SD\], 0\.06 \[0\.14\] mm vs 0\.09 \[0\.13\] mm; P = \.01\), with all values below 2 mm\. Mortise alignment, final ankle motion, and return\-to\-work time were comparable between groups\. Conclusions: Direct posterior fixation was associated with better early pain and function and less frequent syndesmotic screw fixation\. Clinical outcomes converged and were similar at 1 y\. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether these associations are causal\.

## [GatewayBench: Unified Capability and Security Evaluation Platform for MCP Gateways](../publications/0cf5872e8e38d57c7dfd.md)

Yitian Zheng; Zhaorun Chen; Haoyu Li; Bo Li

AI agents have increasingly interacted with external environments by invoking tools, with Model Context Protocol \(MCP\) emerging as a standard interface for connecting agents to heterogeneous tools and services\. As organizations deploy agents at scale, MCP gateways have become a critical middleware layer for aggregating, governing, and shaping the tool surface exposed to agents\. Despite the growing importance of MCP gateways in agentic systems, no prior work has systematically studied how gateway design affects agent capability, efficiency, and security\. To address this gap, we introduce GatewayBench, the first unified evaluation framework and benchmark for MCP gateways\. We characterize gateway architectures into two major paradigms: flattened gateways and hierarchical gateways\. GatewayBench comprises 524 tasks across six domains, together with a pool of 11,118 real\-world tools from 251 authentic MCP servers\. To emulate large\-scale deployments, we systematically inject task\-irrelevant tools sampled from this pool into each agent environment, enabling controlled evaluation as the accessible tool surface scales\. Based on GatewayBench, we conduct extensive experiments across seven widely deployed MCP gateways and diverse agent configurations, covering both benign and adversarial tasks\. Our results reveal substantial differences across gateway designs in task completion, tool\-use efficiency, and resilience to attacks, and further demonstrate that these effects interact strongly with the underlying model and agent harness\. These findings highlight the MCP gateway as a consequential yet underexplored component of the agentic AI stack\. By enabling controlled evaluation of gateway architectures under realistic tool ecosystems, GatewayBench provides both practical guidance for MCP gateway design and a rigorous testbed for developing more capable, efficient, and secure agentic systems\.

## [Regulatory Oversight and Audit Failures: A Study of Ghana’s Audit Quality Review Process](../publications/0cf87fadb88dbf0bb429.md)

Samuel Antwi; Evans O\. N\. D\. Ocansey

Purpose: This study investigates the Ghanaian audit quality review process as both an institutional practice and a regulatory mechanism\. Specifically, the study evaluates how oversight is operationalized, the extent to which it mitigates audit failures, and the institutional factors that shape its effectiveness\. Methods: This study uses exploratory qualitative research design, consistent with Logie and Maroun to examine the regulatory oversight and audit failures in Ghana’s audit quality review process implemented through Act 1058\. Data was sourced from Audit Quality Review reports published by Institute Chartered Accountants\-Ghana \(ICAG\) for 2023 and 2024\. Findings: Study reveals that the dual role of ICAG as both custodian and disciplinary authority raises concerns of soft regulatory capture, where enforcement may prioritize visible infractions over systemic quality failures\. The findings underscore the need for a shift from rule\-based inspections to risk\-based, capacity\-building oversight\. The findings further suggest that resource constraints, the potential for institutional decoupling, and possible regulatory capture associated with ICAG’s dual role as professional body and regulator may limit enforcement effectiveness and hinder the development of a sustainable audit quality culture in Ghana\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice, and Policy: The study integrates institutional, legitimacy, and regulatory theories to explain the coexistence of improved formal compliance and persistent technical deficiencies in audit practice\. It also provides evidence that highlights the need for risk\-based reviews, stronger internal quality management systems, competency\-based continuing professional development, and targeted technical support for audit firms\. This study advocates greater autonomy and independence for audit quality monitoring, and a shift towards enforncement that evaluates the sufficiency of audit evidence, professional judgment, and actual audit performance rather than procedural compliance alone\.

## [Human\-Computer Interaction](../publications/0d033de5f99e63ecfff3.md)

Alan Dix

Digital technology shapes our daily lives, from smartphones to autonomous cars, and human\-computer interaction \(HCI\) focuses on understanding and enhancing how we interact with these systems\. Human–Computer Interaction: The Basics provides a concise and accessible introduction to the foundational principles, practical applications, and contemporary challenges of this dynamic and diverse field\. This book begins by exploring key topics such as understanding the human context in which systems are deployed, applying design and evaluation methods, and building and deploying human\-focused software\. Later chapters examine the social and ethical implications of digital technology and underlying theory and research, incorporating insights from psychological and social science perspectives\. For those aiming to understand how the systems around them have been designed, or are seeking guidance to improve design processes, this book offers valuable insights to support the creation of better, more effective systems\. An essential read for newcomers and first\-year students, this book is ideal for those undertaking or considering courses related to HCI, including interaction design, user experience \(UX\) design, user interface design, and human\-centred systems, as well as interdisciplinary fields like the digital humanities\. It also offers insights and inspiration for more experienced readers\.

## [Reconstructing Lost Urban Memory with Generative AI: An Oral\-History Prompt\-Engineering Framework](../publications/0d0be33dcbd7fe83351f.md)

Özlem Kevseroğlu; İrem Yaşar; Vildan Yıldırım

Urban transformation processes not only destroy the physical fabric of historic neighbourhoods but also erode the collective memory and everyday life practices embedded within them\. This study addresses this spatial memory loss by employing generative AI to visually reconstruct the lost atmospheres of Cumhuriyet Neighbourhood within the outer walls of Kayseri Castle, Turkey\. Drawing on oral history interviews conducted as part of a TÜBİTAK\-funded project, narrative data from 5 former residents were transformed into structured seven\-category prompts and fed into Google Gemini\- Nano Banana 2 pro, OpenAI GPT\-Image\-1, and XAI Grok\. A 30\-member residents panel evaluated the outputs\. Tool G \(Google Gemini\) achieved the best overall ranking \(M = 1\.77\)\. The findings confirm that human curatorial oversight and iterative community feedback remain essential for culturally authentic AI\-generated heritage visualisations\.

## [An interpretable machine learning framework for SDG 7 electricity access forecasting and policy scenario analysis in sub\-Saharan Africa](../publications/0d0d749eff37ebff803c.md)

Sena Gemechis File

Abstract Universal electricity access by 2030 \(Sustainable Development Goal 7, SDG 7\) remains far off track in Sub\-Saharan Africa \(SSA\), where approximately 565 million people lacked access in 2023\. This study proposes an interpretable framework that integrates forecasting, explainability, and policy scenario analysis into a reproducible workflow, demonstrated on a World Development Indicators panel of 45 SSA countries \(2001–2023; 1035 observations\) with Ethiopia as the case study\. Linear Regression \(LR\), Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM are compared under leave\-one\-country\-out and temporal\-split validation\. With path dependence represented through a lagged access feature, LR achieves the lowest error: a mean absolute error \(MAE\) of 1\.93 percentage points across the 45 held\-out countries \(2\.04 for Ethiopia\) and 1\.33 for Ethiopia in the temporal split\. LR improves on a persistence baseline in 33 of 45 countries \(median MAE improvement 15\.9%\)\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) show that prior\-year access dominates predictions, as expected under the autoregressive specification and consistent with infrastructure path dependence\. SHAP informs the diagnostic assessment of the predictive structure, while multicollinearity screening, coefficient\-sign verification, and scenario\-sensitivity checks determine the selection of LR as the scenario model\. Under Slow, Business\-as\-Usual, and Accelerated scenarios, Ethiopia is projected to reach 67\.5–69\.9% access by 2030, leaving a gap of 30–32 percentage points\. Within the socioeconomic scenarios represented, macroeconomic improvements alone are unlikely to close this gap; structural interventions such as grid extension, lower connection costs, and off\-grid solar deployment are needed\. The framework is open and potentially transferable, pending validation elsewhere\.

## [Genesis 11:1\-9 and Technological Self\-Totalization: A Theological Critique of Uncontrolled AI Ambition](../publications/0d19aa06eae7c2fdbae5.md)

Ragil Kristiawan; Sungduk Yun; Zinzendorf R\. A\. Dachi

The uncontrolled development of Artificial Intelligence raises fundamental questions about human limits and divine sovereignty\. This article analyzes the Tower of Babel narrative in Genesis 11:1\-9 as a theological critique of uncontrolled AI ambition\. Using a historical\-grammatical exegetical method with attention to the Hebrew text, this study identifies four patterns of human ambition that parallel contemporary AI development, namely autonomy from God, centralized control, technological self\-totalization, and self\-glorification\. The findings show that God&\#x27;s intervention at Babel was not merely punitive but redemptive, establishing limits that preserve authentic human flourishing\. The article argues that the crisis posed by AI is not merely ethical but spiritual, touching the core of what it means to be human before God\. The theological and pastoral implications include recovering a theology of limits, cultivating humility, replacing fear with trust, embracing diversity, and living with creaturely dependence on God\. This study contributes to the development of an Evangelical theological response to AI that is attentive to the Asian context\.

## [The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Primary School Chinese Language Teaching: An Analysis from Teachers&\#x27; Perspectives](../publications/0d1fe8e59217bedbf42e.md)

李乃麟

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) has entered Chinese primary education faster than curricula, assessment systems and teacher preparation have adapted to it\. While a growing body of Chinese scholarship explores how GenAI can “empower” yuwen \(Chinese language\) teaching, considerably less attention has been paid to the disruptive effects that frontline teachers must absorb in daily practice\. This article offers a qualitative, interpretive analysis of how AI affects primary school Chinese language teaching when viewed from the teacher’s position\. Rather than collecting new empirical data, it analyses three bodies of material: national and international policy documents on GenAI in schools, Chinese and international research on AI in language and primary education, and published expert commentary on Chinese language education in the AI era\. Read through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) framework, the analysis identifies four interrelated areas of impact: the erosion of foundational literacy practices such as character writing and sustained reading; a crisis of authorship in writing instruction, in which teachers are pushed from cultivating expression towards verifying authenticity; the reconfiguration of teachers’ professional roles and identities; and institutional ambiguity arising from gaps between national policy, school practice, assessment and home use\. The article argues that the central difficulty is not technological access but a misalignment between AI\-saturated learning environments and product\-oriented teaching and assessment traditions\. Implications are drawn for process\-oriented writing pedagogy, assessment reform, teacher professional development and home–school collaboration\.

## [Examining children’s sensitivity to morphologically\-marked focus in the comprehension of question sentences: evidence from quantifier comprehension in child Turkish](../publications/0d3152d8afdfb1feffd4.md)

Münir Özturhan; Utako Minai

This study investigated the role of morphologically\-marked focus in child language comprehension\. The Turkish question particle \(QP\) mI typically appears at the end of a question sentence, but can also appear in other positions, attaching to an element to be focalized and marking it as the most important information conveyed in the sentence\. For example, if a question sentence meaning “ Is the child holding a balloon? ” has the QP on the subject noun \(“ the child ”\), it is focalized, rendering an interpretation similar to a cleft construction \(e\.g\., “ Is it the child that is holding a balloon? ”\)\. We investigated whether Turkish\-speaking preschool\-age children can incorporate focus marked by QP placement by testing sentences containing a universal quantifier her \(“every”\) in two conditions: questions with the QP appearing sentence\-finally \(yielding a reading like “ Is every child holding a balloon? ”\), and those with the QP on the universally\-quantified subject, focalizing it \(yielding an “ Is it every child that is holding a balloon? ” reading\)\. We presented the sentences along with an “extra object” picture depicting children holding a balloon each and an extra balloon held by nobody, a context known to elicit “q\-spreading” \(erroneous “No” answers attributed to the presence of the extra balloon\), to examine whether focus\-marking on the subject would facilitate adult\-like interpretation \(“Yes” answers verifying the children all have balloons\)\. Children indeed exhibited significantly less q\-spreading when the quantified subject contained focus\-marking, suggesting that children utilize morphologically\-marked focus during comprehension, consistent with “full competence” approaches to focus and quantification\.

## [Preschool teachers’ emotions relate to racialized perceptions of Black and White children’s behaviors](../publications/0d478835391f7da57eb8.md)

Kamilah B\. Legette; Elizabeth King

Abstract Through a mixed\-methods approach, the current study examined preschool teachers’ feelings about and perceptions of children’s non\-compliant behaviors, their assessments of children’s behaviors by child race, and their acknowledgement of racial inequity in classrooms\. Teachers reported emotional responses to child behavior \(via vignettes and interviews\) and reported their perceptions of the behavior as severe, representative of a behavioral pattern, and inappropriate\. Results indicate that teachers described being frustrated, angry, and overwhelmed in response to children’s non\-compliance\. Additionally, findings indicate that racialized perceptions related to teachers’ emotions; when teachers reported feeling frustrated or concerned, the association between frustration, concern and perceived severity of the behavior was stronger for Black compared to White children\. We found a discrepancy between teachers’ emotional responses to children’s behaviors \(quantitative data\) and what they described in interviews, such that teachers were unlikely to acknowledge racial inequity or describe differential perceptions of children’s behavior by child race\. Results indicate a need for greater attention to teachers’ racial biases in behavior management\.

## [Mitigating Demographic Disparities in Explanation\-Human Alignment via Rationale Regularization](../publications/0d4b04f7a3b00c074406.md)

Suryansh Talukdar; Taha Sarwat; Jonathan Rusert

We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection\. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups\. Using the HateXplain dataset, we introduce Plausibility\-EFG, a metric that measures the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups by comparing model\-generated token attributions with human\-annotated rationales\. We evaluate BERT, RoBERTa, and ADV\-RoBERTa, an adversarially trained model, using Integrated Gradients and SHAP\. Our results show that ADV\-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups\. These improvements are observed with both attribution methods and remain consistent across training, validation, and test splits\. We also show that reducing prediction\-level bias alone does not eliminate disparities in explanations, suggesting that predictive fairness and explanation fairness are related but distinct objectives\. Finally, our fairness\-performance analysis shows that stronger adversarial regularization can further reduce Plausibility\-EFG, although it may cause a small decrease in macro\-F1\. Overall, this work presents explanation fairness as an important objective in hate speech moderation and introduces Fair\-REF, a framework designed to reduce disparities in model explanations across demographic groups\.

## [Teaching with AI, Not Against It: A Thinking Partner Framework for Working Adult Learners in Compressed Online Formats](../publications/0d4c4ed23b0552e96627.md)

Abbot L\. Packard; Ryan Fuller; Glen A\. Holmes; Bryce Platt Kayanuma

Working adult learners in online graduate programs face challenges that make strict AI bans both impractical and unhelpful\. This paper introduces the Thinking Partner Framework, a practical approach to AI integration developed and refined across six semesters of graduate research methods courses serving approximately 440 K\-12 educators\. Instead of treating AI as a problem to be detected, the framework positions AI as a Socratic partner that helps students learn while still requiring them to think for themselves\. Five design principles—transparency, process documentation, authentic assessment, scaffolded autonomy, and metacognitive reflection—guide the framework’s implementation\. The paper includes practical tools such as sample prompts, documentation templates, and examples illustrating the difference between using AI for answers and using it as a thinking partner\. Observations from practice, including a 96% checkpoint completion rate and evidence of students transferring Socratic techniques to their own classrooms, suggest promise, though more rigorous research is needed\. This framework gives distance education administrators a practical option beyond simply banning or allowing AI\. Keywords: artificial intelligence, adult learning, distance education, Socratic method, academic integrity, compressed courses

## [Spin Potential and Thermal Regularization in the Two‐Flavor Nambu–Jona‐Lasinio Model](../publications/0d4c7ff16a556b8cce53.md)

William R\. Tavares; Ricardo L\. S\. Farias

ABSTRACT Recently, the spin potential has been proposed as a new thermodynamic quantity that quantifies the degree of spin alignment of quark matter along a preferred direction in lattice quantum chromodynamics \(LQCD\)\. By using this quantity, one can explore the behavior of different aspects of the QCD phase diagram and connect them with future LQCD and experimental results\. Since it is a natural quantity to investigate within effective models, in this work we introduce the spin potential in the context of the two‐flavor Nambu–Jona‐Lasinio model at finite temperature and study its dependence on whether or not one regularizes the thermal contributions, an issue that has been discussed over the years in connection with the behavior of thermodynamic observables and the recovery of the Stefan–Boltzmann limit at high temperatures\. To investigate these effects, we evaluate the effective quark masses as well as the pressure of the model for different spin potential values using two different prescriptions for the regularization of the thermal contributions\.

## [تجربة الأمهات في توظيف أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي كوسيلة للتكيف والدعم في رعاية الأطفال ذوي اضطراب فرط النشاط وتشتت الانتباهADHD دراسة نوعية](../publications/0d4d425273ef07a0e86f.md)

الدكتورة\. أماني محمد بوخمسين

على الرغم من تزايد الاهتمام العلمي باضطراب فرط الحركة وتشتت الانتباه Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder \(ADHD\)، فإن الدراسات التي تتناول تجارب الأمهات من منظور تحليلي معمق لا تزال محدودة، ولا سيما فيما يتعلق بفهم أدوارهن التربوية وممارسات التأقلم اليومية في سياق الرعاية المستمرة\. كما تفتقر الأدبيات إلى دراسات نوعية تستكشف الخبرات الشعورية والاجتماعية للأمهات عند استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي لمواجهة تحديات تربية الأطفال ذوي اضطراب فرط الحركة وتشتت الانتباه\. وانطلاقا من هذه الفجوة، هدفت الدراسة إلى استكشاف خبرات الأمهات في رعاية أطفالهن ذوي الاضطراب، وتحليل آليات التأقلم والاحتواء التي يتبعنها، وفهم دور أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي في دعم ممارسات الرعاية اليومية\. اعتمدت الدراسة المنهج النوعي، من خلال عينة قصدية مكونة من خمس أمهات لأطفال في مرحلة رياض الأطفال مشخصين باضطراب فرط الحركة وتشتت الانتباه\. وجمعت البيانات باستخدام المقابلات شبه المنظمة، ثم حللت وفق منهج التحليل الموضوعي Thematic Analysis، مع الاستفادة من أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي بوصفها أدوات مساعدة في تتبع الأنماط اللغوية والانفعالية في البيانات، مع الحفاظ على الدور التفسيري للباحثة في قراءة المعاني وبناء الثيمات\. أظهرت النتائج أن استخدام الأمهات للذكاء الاصطناعي لم يكن مجرد ممارسة تقنية، بل جاء بوصفه جزءا من استراتيجيات أوسع للتكيف النفسي والتربوي\. فقد استخدمت الأمهات تطبيقات تنظيم الروتين اليومي، وتتبع السلوك، والمراقبة الانفعالية، والمساعدات الصوتية، والمنصات التعليمية التفاعلية؛ بهدف تنظيم حياة الطفل اليومية، وتقليل الاحتكاك المباشر، وفهم الأنماط السلوكية والانفعالية بصورة أكثر وعيا\. كما أسهمت هذه الأدوات في تعزيز شعور الأمهات بالكفاءة الذاتية ومنحهن إحساسا أكبر بالسيطرة على متطلبات الرعاية اليومية\. وكشفت الدراسة عن عدد من التحديات، من أبرزها الحواجز اللغوية والتقنية، ومحدودية المحتوى العربي المتخصص، وارتفاع تكلفة بعض التطبيقات، والخوف من التبعية التقنية، إضافة إلى مقاومة بعض أفراد الأسرة لاستخدام التقنية في التربية\. وخلصت الدراسة إلى أن الذكاء الاصطناعي لا ينبغي أن ينظر إليه بوصفه بديلا عن دور الأم أو عن التدخل المهني المتخصص، وإنما موردا داعما تتحدد فاعليته بمدى حساسيته للسياق الثقافي والاجتماعي، وإتاحته بصورة عادلة، واستخدامه ضمن إطار تربوي واع\. وتوصي الدراسة بتطوير أدوات ذكاء اصطناعي عربية حساسة للسياق الثقافي والاجتماعي، وبناء برامج إرشادية تساعد الأمهات على الاستخدام الآمن والفعال لهذه الأدوات، مع الحفاظ على البعد الإنساني والعاطفي في الرعاية الأسرية\.

## [Practical Prescribed‐Time Control for Strict‐Feedback Nonlinear Systems Subject to Sensor Faults and Input Saturation](../publications/0d52935da5055e29b009.md)

Mingjun Chen; Jieqing Tan; Peng Chen; Yangang Yao; yan Yao; Lianglei Fan

ABSTRACT This article proposes a novel and practical prescribed time control \(PPTC\) method for strict feedback nonlinear systems \(SFNSs\) subject to input saturation and sensor faults\. This method fills the research gap in existing literature, which only addresses a single constraint \(either input saturation or sensor faults\) rather than their simultaneous occurrence\. By constructing a novel time‐varying scaling transformation function \(STF\), a new practical prescribed‐time stability \(PPTS\) criterion is established\. The designed decoupling control parameter mechanism can directly preset the upper bound of the convergence time and independently adjust the control accuracy, thus overcoming the limitations of traditional fixed‐time control \(FxTC\)–namely, the ambiguous correlation between control parameters and convergence time, as well as the difficulty in presetting the convergence time explicitly\. Meanwhile, the proposed method circumvents the singularity problem and the defect of excessive initial control input in the prescribed time control \(PdTC\)\. The algorithm does not require an accurate mathematical model of the system&\#x27;s nonlinear components\. Instead, it addresses unknown nonlinearity via fuzzy logic systems \(FLSs\) and enhances system robustness by integrating fault‐tolerant design with saturation compensation mechanisms\. Stability analysis demonstrates that all signals of the closed‐loop system are bounded within the practical prescribed time, sensor faults are effectively compensated, and the tracking error is constrained within the preset range\. The simulation results verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme\.

## [METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING INFORMATION AND ANALYTICAL COMPETENCE OF FUTURE LIBRARY, INFORMATION, AND ARCHIVAL PROFESSIONALS THROUGH GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE](../publications/0d65b17b92ea1858fed4.md)

Tur O\.; Shabunina V\.

The study examines the impact of global oil volatility on the financial performance of banks in Kazakhstan\. The aim of the study is to assess the sensitivity of key indicators of the financial stability of the banking sector, such as ROA, ROE, and CAR, to changes in oil volatility\. This study uses data from the banking sector, obtained through manual collection from the financial statements of 16 banks in Kazakhstan for the period from 2002 to 2024\. This issue is studied using the Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity model \(hereinafter – GARCH\), as well as Fixed or Random Effects models \(hereinafter – FE or RE models, respectively\)\. ## [Is \(AI\-guided\) coronary CT angiography ready for prime time in diabetes care and research?](../publications/0d66d0c0798aa2dce0e7.md)

Nordin M\.J\. Hanssen; Cheyenne Y Y Beverloo; Saloua El Messaoudi; Richard A\. P\. Takx; Nick S\. Nurmohamed

Abstract Due to its increasing prevalence, the burden of diabetes\-attributable cardiovascular disease is projected to increase substantially\. At the same time, there is a growing need to better identify patients at the highest cardiovascular risk and to optimize the use of increasingly available—but costly—weight\-, glucose\-, and lipid\-lowering therapies\. We postulate that coronary computed tomography angiography \(CCTA\), potentially enhanced by novel artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based image analysis, could serve as a valuable tool for diabetologists to more accurately assess atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk\. With ongoing reductions in cost and radiation exposure, CCTA has become a more feasible modality to quantify coronary artery disease burden, particularly in patients with diabetes, who represent one of the highest\-risk populations\. AI\-guided analysis may further enhance scalability by reducing radiologist workload and improving reproducibility\. In this perspective, we discuss both the promise and the current limitations of this approach, including questions surrounding whether to use intravenous contrast, and the management of incidental findings or clinically significant stenoses\. We also explore the potential role of CCTA\-derived endpoints in clinical trials for anti\-atherosclerotic therapies, which could complement or partially replace traditional major adverse cardiovascular event outcomes that increasingly require large sample sizes due to declining event rates\. A trial design combining non\-inferiority on hard endpoints with superiority on CCTA measures may reduce costs while accelerating evidence generation\. Ultimately, integrating AI\-guided CCTA into clinical care and research may enable more precise and scalable cardiovascular risk stratification in diabetes care\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI CAUSAL ENTROPIC BOUND FOR AUTONOMOUS LEARNING SYSTEMS \(ECB\)](../publications/0d683ed54da85812c50b.md)

m el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Causal Entropic Bound \(ECB\) introduces a fundamental thermodynamic law governing autonomous learning, transcending statistical machine learning\. It addresses a critical physical reality: discovering true causality requires breaking time\-reversal symmetry\. By integrating the Crooks Fluctuation Theorem with Causal Algorithmic Complexity, the ECB proves that extracting pure causal information necessitates minimum entropy production strictly exceeding the classical Landauer limit\. The framework establishes an absolute, dimensionally consistent lower bound on energy dissipation for any system to distinguish causal mechanisms from spurious correlations\. Formulated as S\_dot &gt;= \(k\_B / tau\) \* \(I\_causal \+ beta \* K\_c\(G\)\), it defines the average entropy production rate required to acquire a total causal information load over timescale tau\. This paradigm redefines intelligence as a thermodynamically constrained ability to uncover reality&\#x27;s causal fabric, setting the ultimate theoretical benchmark for next\-generation neuromorphic hardware, quantum learning, and Artificial General Intelligence\.

## [Scaling Innovation: How Entrepreneurial Leadership Drives Sustainable Corporate Growth](../publications/0d6a4d7f693351f4ce42.md)

Shaurya Gupta

In the current dynamic business environment where competition is very stiff, it has become imperative for businesses to always come up with innovations as a way of ensuring growth and keeping a competitive advantage \[1\]\. While technology and other factors have increased the need for innovations in businesses, the success of scaling innovations could also depend on the kind of leaders in an organization \[2\]\. Entrepreneurial leadership can thus be defined as an approach that utilizes visioning, opportunity seeking, risk taking and organizational flexibility in order to ensure continuous innovation and corporate growth \[3\]\. Many research studies have been carried out in order to understand the relationship between leadership and innovation but not many have been done about the role of entrepreneurial leadership in scaling innovations and sustaining corporate growth across diverse industries\. Qualitative multiple\-case study method will be utilized to explore the role of entrepreneurial leadership in shaping innovation and sustainable growth and performance of the organization\. The research makes use of the secondary data sources including academic journals, company reports, leadership insights and case\-studies of global organizations who have become successful through innovations\. We analyze the data using thematic analysis, identifying the repeating themes of effective behavior for leaders, organization capabilities and strategy involved in scaling innovation\. The findings show the way in which entrepreneurial leadership helps create an organizational culture that values creativity, adaptability, learning, empowerment of employees and innovation\-oriented approach toward customers \[3\]\. Moreover, ambidexterity of the organization as part of transformation and sustainable growth as a result of innovation becoming an integral part of strategy and being facilitated by adaptive leadership is also considered in alignment with the results of the research\. Thus, the research, by bringing together different perspectives from various theoretical frameworks as well as practical organizational phenomenon through corporate examples, contributes to the existing literature on forming the above\-mentioned connection between entrepreneurial leadership and its ability to scale innovation for sustainable growth\. It further offers implications to practice where business leaders can shape resilient, future\-ready organizations\.

## [Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in answering patient\-oriented questions about coronary artery bypass grafting: An expert\-based cross\-sectional study](../publications/0d73c255b95e09381cf1.md)

Hakan Baltacı; Yusuf Taşpınar; Üzeyir Yılmaz

Objectives: Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used by patients to obtain information about high\-risk procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting \(CABG\)\.This study aimed to compare expert evaluations of responses generated by ChatGPT \(GPT\-5\.5 Instant, OpenAI\) and Gemini \(Gemini 3\.5 Flash, Google\) to frequently asked patient\-oriented questions about CABG\. Patients and methods:In this expert\-based cross\-sectional study, responses generated by ChatGPT and Gemini to 29 frequently asked CABG\-related questions developed by cardiovascular surgeons were evaluated\.The questions were submitted in English to both models through free, publicly available web interfaces using a standardized prompt\.Each question was entered in a separate new chat session, and only the first generated response was recorded\.Optional web search and Deep Research features were not manually enabled\.After model identities and model\-specific elements were removed, the responses were presented separately in randomized order\.Five cardiovascular surgeons independently rated the responses using a five\-point Likert scale that jointly assessed clinical accuracy and usefulness\.In the primary paired analysis, the sum of the five evaluators&\#x27; ratings for each question was used, yielding 29 paired questionlevel observations\.Results: Both models received high scores\.The mean question\-level total score was 23\.31±1\.54for ChatGPT and 23\.00±1\.31for Gemini\.The mean paired difference was 0\.31 points \(bootstrap 95% confidence interval \[CI\], \-0\.07 to 0\.69\) and was not statistically significant \(Wilcoxon signed\-rank test, W=60\.0; p=0\.129; matched\-pairs rank\-biserial correlation=0\.37\)\.At the individual\-rating level, 97\.2% of ratings were 4 or 5 for each model\.The average\-measures absolute\-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient was 0\.50 \(95% CI, 0\.13\-0\.74\)for ChatGPT and 0\.15 \(95% CI, \-0\.49\-0\.56\)for Gemini\.Conclusion: Under the reported evaluation conditions, responses generated by ChatGPT and Gemini received similarly high combined ratings for clinical accuracy and usefulness\.These findings reflect the expert\-rated clinical appropriateness of model responses generated at a specific time point; they do not establish guideline concordance, within\-model reproducibility, patient comprehension, or clinical benefit\.LLM\-generated CABG information may have a supportive role in patient education; however, this possibility requires validation in patient\-based studies\.These tools should not replace individualized physician\-led counseling\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Readiness Among Paramedics at the Saudi Red Crescent Authority: A Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/0d79e1aaa18ec32ede4a.md)

Mohammed Jamaan Alsahli

Objective: To evaluate AI readiness among paramedics working within the Saudi Red Crescent Authority \(SRCA\) and examine demographic and professional characteristics related to their readiness\.Methods: This cross\-sectional study was conducted among SRCA paramedics\. Data were collected through a structured online questionnaire covering demographic and professional features and the validated Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale for Medical Students \(MAIRS\-MS\), which assesses four dimensions: Cognition, Ability, Vision, and Ethics\. Comparisons between groups were performed with the Mann\-Whitney U and Kruskal\-Wallis tests, while correlations were assessed using Spearman&\#x27;s rank correlation, and a multiple linear regression model examined factors independently related to AI readiness\.Results: A total of 262 paramedics participated\. The mean overall AI readiness score was 72\.55 \(SD 21\.79\) on the 110\-point scale, reflecting a moderate degree of readiness\. The Ethics and the Cognition domains had the highest \(3\.57/5\) and the lowest \(3\.15/5\) mean item scores, respectively\. Participants reported greater confidence in AI&\#x27;s ethical and practical aspects than in understanding AI concepts and terminology\. Prior AI training was the only factor independently associated with higher AI readiness \(B=10\.13, 95% CI 3\.45–16\.81; P=\.003\)\.Conclusion: SRCA paramedics demonstrated moderate AI readiness, with greater confidence in AI&\#x27;s ethical and practical application than in its conceptual and technical foundations\. Prior AI training was the only independent factor associated with higher readiness, highlighting the potential of structured AI education before the broader implementation of AI in EMS\.

## [Shape‐Based Classification and Anatomical Localization of Phalanges in Hamdani Sheep and Hair Goats](../publications/0d81e9da779e81caadf4.md)

Hadji Chiuta Salimu; Nedžad Hadžiomerović; Ozan Gündemir

ABSTRACT Reliable identification of isolated sheep and goat phalanges is challenging because of the close skeletal similarity between these species and the repeated arrangement of homologous digital bones across the forelimbs, hindlimbs, and medial‐lateral positions\. This study evaluated three‐dimensional phalangeal shape for discrimination between 12‐month‐old male Hamdani sheep and Hair goats and for localization among the sampled anatomical positions\. Proximal phalanx \(P1\), middle phalanx \(P2\), and distal phalanx \(P3\) from 30 male Hamdani sheep \( Ovis aries \) and 30 male Hair goats \( Capra hircus \), all 12 months of age, were analysed\. Bone‐specific configurations of 60, 77, and 60 surface pseudolandmarks were used for P1, P2, and P3, respectively\. Three‐dimensional shape provided substantially greater diagnostic information than centroid size\. Shape‐only species classification reached 98\.3% for P1, 98\.3% for P2, and 100% for P3, whereas forelimb‐hindlimb classification reached 100%, 98\.3%, and 96\.2%, respectively\. P1 provided the strongest discrimination among the four sampled compound anatomical positions, achieving 91\.1% internal classification accuracy\. Size‐only classification accuracy ranged from 48\.5% to 58\.6%, compared with 98\.3–100\.0% for shape‐only models\. P2 showed the largest adjusted breed‐species effect in the animal‐mean analysis \(partial R 2 = 0\.421\), whereas P3 yielded the highest internal species‐classification accuracy \(100\.0%\) and the largest descriptive sheep‐goat mean‐shape distance within its own phalanx‐specific shape space\. Importantly, P3 showed no significant interspecific centroid‐size difference despite perfect shape‐based species classification, demonstrating that its diagnostic signal was primarily geometric rather than size‐dependent\. Overall, the results revealed a phalanx‐specific diagnostic pattern within the present reference sample: P3 yielded the highest observed breed‐species classification accuracy, whereas P1 provided the strongest discrimination of limb region and the four sampled compound anatomical positions\. These findings support discrimination within the present modern reference sample; independent validation across other breeds, both sexes, different ages, and archaeological specimens of molecularly confirmed taxon is required before routine application\.

## [Women’s voice in the South African entrepreneurial ecosystem: implications for support interventions](../publications/0d820bb9624329781424.md)

Sinqobile Joseph Mkhwanazi; Reward Utete

Introduction While there are numerous claims that women entrepreneurship is in a precarious state after the recent upheavals, the situation of their businesses has not been sufficiently examined\. Despite the subject&\#x27;s pertinence, to the best of the authors&\#x27; knowledge, the existing literature gives scant attention to the current situation of women entrepreneurs in South Africa in the post\-pandemic era\. Grounded in Resource\-Based Theory and Institutional Theory, this study empirically investigates the current state of women entrepreneurs in Durban\. Methods Adopting the quantitative research approach, data were collected using a closed\-ended questionnaire, of which 349 SMEs&\#x27; responses were subjected to both descriptive and inferential analysis\. Exploratory Factor Analysis \(EFA\) using Principal Axis Factoring with Promax rotation identified the underlying constructs, followed by reliability and multiple regression analyses\. Results Entrepreneurial Constraints \(EC\), Entrepreneurial Support \(ES\), Entrepreneurial Participation \(EP\), and Business Environment and Regulatory Climate \(BERC\) emerged as the key constructs\. The findings reported low satisfaction with entrepreneurial support, particularly financial, infrastructural, training and guidance support\. EC was the most prominent challenge, with inadequate capital, skills deficits and low profitability being highly reported\. Regression analysis showed that ES and BERC were positively associated with EP, while EC was negatively associated with EP\. Collectively, the predictors explained 46\.3% of the variance in EP\. Discussion The findings indicate that women’s entrepreneurial participation is shaped by the interaction of resource availability and institutional conditions\. Strengthening financial assistance, skills development, mentorship, infrastructure, guidance and the regulatory environment may address the multidimensional barriers affecting women entrepreneurs\.

## [From information to action: exploring the relationship between fair\-trade message informativeness and consumer behavioral intentions](../publications/0d8718172a201d1b4ee5.md)

Rithika Jeethu Suvarna; Kavitha T C; Parthesh R\. Shanbhag; M\. Swathi Poojary

Sustainability encompasses more than environmental protection, acknowledging the societal context in which it operates\. It simultaneously expresses concern for individuals\. Fair\-trade products have garnered significant interest, particularly within agrifood systems and consumer intention toward fair\-trade items has been widely studied\. However, limited attention has been given to how fair\-trade advertisements, as a distinct stimulus, shape consumer perception and subsequently influence their behavioral intention\. Underpinning the Stimulus\-Organism\-Response model, this study investigates the influence of informativeness on fair\-trade practices on purchase intention, word\-of\-mouth and willingness\-to\-pay through mediating role of ad attitude using survey responses\. The study employed an accidental sampling technique for collecting data from Indian Gen\-Z consumers\. The study reveals the positive impact of informativeness on ad attitude and a significant influence of ad attitude on word\-of\-mouth, purchase intention and willingness\-to\-pay, depicting the consumers’ social and monetary preferences\. This encourages future research to explore the interrelationships between factors such as perceived value, skepticism, product quality and their potential in understanding consumer intentions toward fair\-trade practices and framing of effective marketing strategies\.

## [Scalable and Trustworthy Machine Learning for Spatiotemporal Events: From Neural Point Processes to Foundation Models](../publications/0d89e0164d1a152acf0c.md)

Zihao Zhou

Spatiotemporal events, such as earthquakes and aftershocks, epidemic case reports, geotagged social activity, and vehicle trajectories, are discrete occurrences in continuous space and time\. They arrive at irregular intervals, interact across space, and depend strongly on their history, properties that defeat models built for regularly\-sampled data\. This dissertation develops machine learning methods for such events across two eras of the field, unified by a single concern: trustworthiness in both models and evidence\. In the first era, neural point processes faced a fundamental obstacle: the likelihood contains an intractable integral of the intensity over space and time, and approximating it numerically places error inside every gradient step\. This dissertation refuses that compromise\. DeepSTPP sidesteps the integral by design, decoding a deep latent process into a kernel\-mixture intensity whose integral is available in closed form, which accelerates training by two orders of magnitude over Neural\-ODE baselines\. Auto\-NPP computes temporal likelihood integrals exactly for free\-form neural intensities through automatic integration: parameterize the antiderivative and recover the intensity by differentiation\. Its spatiotemporal extension, AutoSTPP, reduces the volume integral to line integrals\. Under the stated regularity and identifiability conditions, the derivative\-network class retains its approximation capacity, and maximum\-likelihood estimation consistently recovers the true influence function\. In the second era, foundation models arrived, shifting the bottleneck from model construction to evidence about capability\. A controlled, hypothesis\-driven study of large language models in time series anomaly detection tests several standing conjectures\. For most tested anomaly types, models detect anomalies more accurately from plots than from numeric text; chain\-of\-thought prompting does not improve detection; and the tested repetition\- and addition\-based accounts do not predict the observed behavior, which varies sharply across model families\. STEventsBench then provides the first standardized benchmark for anomaly detection on irregular\-interval spatiotemporal events, aggregating more than 45 million public records across nine public datasets with controlled anomaly injection and unified evaluation\. Exact event models and anomaly detectors can therefore be compared under one protocol\. Together, these contributions argue that trustworthy machine learning for spatiotemporal events rests on exact likelihoods for models and controlled, reproducible measurement for claims\.

## [Come evitare la &quot;sommersione&quot;? Intelligenza artificiale e diritto pubblico](../publications/0d8da3bc000d3e43f6ad.md)

Vasco Pereira Da Silva

This article examines the impact of artificial intelligence on constitutional and administrative law, arguing that digital technologies challenge traditional legal categories, public power, democratic governance, and fundamental rights\. ## [Da resposta da IA ao julgamento próprio: pensamento crítico e autonomia do estudante](../publications/0d908d643b88225595ad.md)

Juan de Jesús Alvarado Ortiz; Oralia Mercedes Moguel Morales; Francisco Jesus Vieyra Gonzalez; Onelia Hernández Torres

Introduction: The growing integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has transformed the way students access, process, and produce information, creating new learning opportunities while also raising risks associated with cognitive dependence\. The objective of this study was to analyze the relationship between the use of generative artificial intelligence, critical thinking, and student autonomy, identifying the conditions that foster independent judgment and those that may promote excessive delegation of reasoning\. Materials and methods: A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, considering publications from 2021 to 2026 in high\-impact academic databases\. After the identification, screening, and eligibility stages, 24 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis\. The results revealed four main thematic areas: AI as cognitive support, critical thinking and evaluation of AI\-generated responses, self\-regulation and student agency, and cognitive dependence or cognitive offloading\. Conclusions: It is concluded that AI does not automatically strengthen or weaken student autonomy; its effect depends on the degree of cognitive control retained by the learner\. When AI\-generated responses are contrasted, verified, and critically reflected upon, AI can enhance learning; when they are accepted uncritically, the risk of dependence and loss of independent judgment increases\.

## [CHARACTERIZATION OF DOPPLER SPECTROSCOPY ASSOCIATED WITH DEVELOPMENTAL COMPETENCE OF IN VITRO\-PRODUCED PIG EMBRYOS](../publications/0d9afb538849714e7e62.md)

Kayode Babatunde Balogun

One of the major unsolved challenges in assisted reproductive technology \(ART\) to date is the prediction of embryo viability before transfer\. While conventional morphological grading does not require contact with embryos, it is also evaluator\-dependent, subjective, and intrinsically limited, assessing only shape and symmetry, and not the actual signature of the physiological processes that take place inside an embryo\. Two embryos that are identical under a microscope, and judged to be viable based on morphology, can have a very different underlying metabolic behavior and cytoskeletal activity\. Those underlying characteristics, not only gross appearance, are what consequently determine whether an in vitro\-produced embryo can develop suitably to a blastocyst that is transferable, or whether it finally ceases development and fails\. The present dissertation aims to further address the above\-mentioned lack of a quantitative and objective approach to viability assessment of porcine embryos by developing and validating a biodynamic imaging \(BDI\)\-based approach\. It comprises three studies, which are presented sequentially and are each a step towards the larger problem\. The first was to establish the culture infrastructure to link a single optical measurement to the eventual fate of an embryo; the second was to show with the original BDI instrument that its spectral output really reflects viability; and the third was to re\-engineer the imaging instrument itself to a more stable, physiologically interpretable configuration that is the system&\#x27;s future\.The first study was a foundation, testing that in vitro\-produced \(IVP\) porcine embryos can be cultured in the Well\-of\-the\-Well \(WOW\) microwell culture system\. In contrast to conventional group culture, which uses 10 or more embryos in one droplet of medium, the WOW dishes allow each embryo to be cultured in a separate microwell in a single droplet of medium, yet preserving the autocrine and paracrine benefits of group culture\. This was a prerequisite for a subsequent study to correlate BDI spectral reading with the actual developmental result of an embryo\. In a first experiment, cumulus\-oocyte complexes under standardized in vitro maturation \(IVM\) and in vitro fertilization \(IVF\) conditions were allocated to five culture conditions, including individual microwell culture and two group culture conditions at different medium volumes, and a conventional dish control \(500 embryos\)\. This was followed by a second experiment \(350 embryos\), in which the best of the above tests was isolated and compared with a conventional control\. There were no differences in the cleavage rates among any of the conditions examined, suggesting that the microwell effect is not due to early developmental competence and therefore occurs later in development\. By contrast, blastocyst formation was significantly and consistently higher in embryos cultured individually in 50 μL WOW microwells compared to any of the grouped or conventional culture conditions \(42\.0% vs\. 13\.0 – 29\.0%, P &lt; 0\.001 in Experiment 1; 37\.9% vs\. 28\.1%, P = 0\.040 in Experiment 2\), and the blastocysts formed under the WOW microwells were of higher quality based on the number of nuclei \(38\.97 vs\. 33\.21, P = 0\.017\)\. These results not only report that the development of porcine IVP embryos in microwells is enhanced, but they also show that embryo quality is not compromised\. In addition, individual embryo traceability was made possible, which is crucial for the remaining parts of the dissertation\.The second study, building on the findings of the first, is a non\-contact, label\-free optical system using Doppler spectroscopy that characterizes the embryo viability signal using a original Biodynamic Imaging system\. The BDI was able to assess embryo intracellular motion without disrupting the developmental trajectory and generate a 128\-point spectral profile of each embryo in approximately three minutes\. Porcine embryos were individually measured once per experimental session \(13 independent sessions\), distributed to the WOW microwells, and cultured to a developmental endpoint of expanded/hatched blastocyst stage at day 7, for a total of 199 individually tracked porcine embryos \(104 identified as viable and 95 identified as non\-viable\)\. Nine biomarkers were extracted from each spectral profile, ranging from the low\-frequency plateau, the mid\-spectrum knee, the high\-frequency Nyquist region, their running\-mean equivalents, dynamic range, backscatter brightness, particle count, and normalized standard deviation\. Five of these nine biomarkers significantly separated viable from nonviable embryos: four spectral\-amplitude biomarkers spanning the plateau, knee, and Nyquist regions showed uniformly elevated values in viable embryos \(Cohen&\#x27;s d = 0\.42–0\.48\), and particle count showed a smaller but still significant elevation \(d = 0\.31\)\. Significant separation was observed at all 128 spectral indices tested, with no evidence of a localized change in spectral shape, as there was no significant difference between viable and nonviable embryos in dynamic range\. The nine\-biomarker Linear Discriminant Analysis \(LDA\) classifier yielded an AUC of 0\.645 in the training set, and an AUC of 0\.550 ± 0\.091 in five\-fold cross\-validation\. This confirmed that the signal in the original BDI system is a viable signal that is indeed meaningful from a biological point of view\. The discriminative value of this signal was relatively weak, indicating the need for a more stable and more physiologically specific measure to further refine this classification\.The third study partially addresses the need identified in the second study by re\-engineering the optical configuration of the BDI\. The configuration of the original BDI’s two\-arm interferometer was changed to a common\-path Fresnel biprism configuration where the reference beam and the object beam both share the same optical elements, instead of traveling two different paths\. This makes the system more stable against long\-time exposures to vibration and path\-length drift\. This system recorded backscattered light from 4\-cell stage IVP porcine embryos and then numerically reconstructed it into holograms and optical coherence images\. Temporal Fourier transforms of the pixel\-wise intensity time series were then used to produce Doppler power spectra\. It was possible to fit the spectra with a single physiologically interpretable parameter, the knee frequency describing a qualitative difference between diffusive and actively driven intracellular transport\. While dead embryos were entirely devoid of any knee, living embryos consistently exhibited a knee, clustering around approximately 0\.5 Hz, making the difference between the two more of a categorical distinction than only a statistical one, and indicating complete cessation of active, energy\-dependent intracellular transport at death\. The knee frequency was then monitored continuously over a period of 45 minutes in the living embryos, revealing a progressive decrease in the frequency over time, thus achieving a snapshot of the loss of metabolic vigor that would never have been seen on a single snapshot measurement\.Each of these three studies describes a clear progression: A validated culture platform that enables the tracking of individual\-embryo viability, validation of BDI\-derived spectral viability biomarkers that are globally distributed, and a re\-engineered, more stable Fresnel biprism instrument that can generate a single physiologically interpretable biomarker of embryo viability, usable to classify viability and track its decline continuously over time\. When viewed in the context of the entire dissertation, this series points to the direction of success in achieving a quantitative, physiologically inspired, machine\-learning\-based approach to predicting the viability of early embryos in a porcine model\.
