## [FDE\-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery](../publications/0da13841ce76627a9ec5.md)

Dongxu Yang; Hongda Yan; Renxin Wang; Baoli Zhang; Haojia Zuo; Ying Zhao; Youmin Chen; Xiaojian Liao; Congming Gao; Tianyang Jiang; Yixiao Chen; Qing Wang; Zhiguo Yu; Xiaqing Li; Yuhao Zhang; Jiawen Sun; Renzhe Xu; De Mi; Tiancheng Wu; Xianya Fu; Xuanlu Zhao; Bo Feng; Meixuan Ren; Guanming Lin; Ziheng Zhou; Xinhua Wang

Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well\-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets\. Real\-world customer delivery is different: forward\-deployed engineers \(FDEs\) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints\. We introduce FDE\-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end\-to\-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real\-world delivery projects\. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production\-like systems to deliver working solutions\. FDE\-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer&\#x27;s own success metric, normalized between 0 \(unchanged system\) and 1 \(reference solution\), with penalties for stakeholder interactions \(messages, trial runs, and waiting time\)\. An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria\. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers\. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE\-Gym score of 0\.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks \(a score of at least 0\.8 with no incident\)\. Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance\. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0\.8 or above on only 10\. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well\-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers\.

## [Case Report: Diagnostic dilemma: rebound thymic hyperplasia mimicking mediastinal relapse following chemoimmunotherapy in pediatric jejunal Burkitt lymphoma](../publications/0daf89fcbbfdef468e22.md)

Meifang Lin; Zengwang Zhang; Hao Zhang; Dongdong Zhang

Background Pediatric sporadic Burkitt lymphoma \(BL\) typically presents with gastrointestinal involvement; primary mediastinal disease is exceedingly rare\. Rebound thymic hyperplasia \(RTH\) is a benign regenerative process following chemotherapy that can radiologically mimic mediastinal relapse, creating significant diagnostic challenges in post\-treatment surveillance\. Case presentation An 8\-year\-old male was diagnosed with St\. Jude stage III Burkitt lymphoma \(BL\) following the emergency resection of a jejunal mass\. After receiving risk\-adapted chemoimmunotherapy, he achieved a complete metabolic response\. Three months post\-treatment, routine surveillance computed tomography \(CT\) revealed a new anterior mediastinal soft tissue mass, magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) revealing T2 hyperintensity in the anterior mediastinal lesion without restricted diffusion, while subsequent PET/CT demonstrated mildly increased FDG uptake, raising immediate clinical concern for disease relapse\. To rule out malignancy, a CT\-guided percutaneous biopsy was performed\. Histopathological analysis revealed normal thymic microarchitecture containing Hassall’s corpuscles\. The final imaging and pathological findings supported a diagnosis of chemotherapy\-induced rebound thymic hyperplasia \(RTH\)\. Conclusion Cytotoxic therapy induces profound thymic involution, often followed by striking regenerative expansion upon treatment cessation\. Recognizing RTH is paramount to avoid misdiagnosing neoplastic recurrence and administering unwarranted therapies\. This case highlights need to integrate advanced imaging and tissue biopsy when evaluating new mediastinal opacities in pediatric lymphoma survivors\.

## [Unifying Embodied Foundation Models via a Model\-to\-Policy Formulation](../publications/0dafb41c77d0665d03fb.md)

Xinyi Hong; Mingyang Ren

Vision\-language\-action \(VLA\) models and world\-action models \(WAMs\) have emerged as promising approaches to robot learning and control\. These models integrate multimodal perception and action generation, but differ in their architectures, output representations, and learning objectives\. In this paper, we present a unified, architecture\-agnostic probabilistic formulation for embodied foundation models based on stochastic kernels\. Our formulation has two key components: \(i\) we characterize embodied foundation models through conditional output distributions and action\-realization kernels, which together induce task\-conditioned robot policies; and \(ii\) we connect pretraining and post\-training to policy deployment, accommodating model\-specific pretraining objectives and offline or online post\-training strategies\. We instantiate the formulation for OpenVLA and DreamZero, covering autoregressive action\-token prediction and joint video\-action generation\.

## [Hybrid Supervised\-unsupervised Learning Framework for Financial Data Analysis Enhanced by Quantum\-inspired Computing](../publications/0db18d28fbf1b91a7a7f.md)

Praneeth Reddy Amudala Puchakayala; Poonam Ghule; Vijay Vaswani; Jeevith S H

Financial time\-series analysis poses some difficulties, due to the non\-stationarity of data, its distribution is heavy\-tailed, the regime structure in financial time\-series is latent, and there are few labelled training signals available\.These models are highly sensitive to unexpected trade\-offs and limited out\-of\-distribution generalisation, and unsupervised models, on their own, are unable to directly inform tradeable decisions\.This paper proposes a framework named Quantum\-Inspired Hybrid Supervised\-Unsupervised Learning \(QIHSL\) consisting of three tightly\-integrated modules: \(1\) Quantum\-Inspired Feature Transformation \(QFT\) module that maps the financial features into amplitudeand phase\-encoded qubit\-state analogues, and generates the cross\-feature interaction terms inspired by entanglement;\(2\) Quantum\-Inspired K\-Means \(QI\-KMeans\) clustering module that uses the quantum fidelity based distance metric to learn the regime \(bull, bear, sideways\) of the data in an unsupervised manner; and \(3\) a Quantum\-Inspired Support Vector Machine \(QI\-SVM\) regime\-gated ensemble for robust and regime\-aware return\-direction prediction with QI\-SVMs that specialise in predicting the return direction in different market regimes\.The experiments on a comprehensive benchmark dataset of 4,950 synthetic daily observations from the S&amp;P 500 index, used to capture the statistical properties of equity markets, namely Student\-t distributed returns \(ν = 5\), three\-state regime switching and nineteen technical indicators, show that QIHSL achieves an accuracy of 0\.4913, a precision of 0\.5538, a recall of 0\.2588, an F1\-score of 0\.3527 and an AUC of 0\.5029 on the hold\-out test set, outperforming the baseline SVM by 5\.92 percentage points in precision\.It represents the best of all six comparison methods \(Table 2\) and for all the architectures in the matched\-condition comparison \(Table 7\) is an advantage \(not a finding\) of precision for two instances of the simulation and does not necessarily mean that they are more likely to forecast than others\.The controlled ablation study \(Table 3\) also shows that a component\-level benefit for quantum\-inspired feature enrichment can be measured by the QFT module&\#x27;s accuracy of \+2\.0 pp and F1\-score of \+11\.9 pp over the SVM baseline \(A2 vs\. A1\)\.Five\-fold stratified cross validation gives a stability of AUC = 0\.4987 ± 0\.0095\.An ablation study shows that the QFT module contributes the largest single\-step accuracy gain \(\+2\.0 pp\) and F1\-score gain \(\+11\.9 pp over A1\); adding regime gating further improves accuracy \(\+0\.95 pp\) but reduces F1 \(\-0\.0786\) and AUC \(\-0\.0123\) relative to QFT alone\.The reported AUC \(around 0\.5\) is at chance level, and no pairwise McNemar comparison is significant at alpha = 0\.05 \(the smallest p = 0\.2433\), which is consistent with the almost efficient nature of the synthetic benchmark\.Combined, results show no statistically relevant predictive value for the synthetic benchmark\.The most interesting aspect of QIHSL is its highest precision \(0\.5538\) of all methods compared, which could have some relevance to conservative trading, but not to proven practical forecast effectiveness\.

## [Music Therapy and community participation: Selfhood and artistic citizenship within and beyond the clinic](../publications/0db7862d397c67c6ddda.md)

Brynjulf Stige

Music therapy practices evolve in specific contexts, which suggests that the conceptual and theoretical claims we make should be continuously challenged by practical realities\. In this paper, I challenge tendencies to polarize clinical music therapy and community music therapy, by elaborating on two main themes: a\) Possibilities and limitations of connecting community music therapy and cultural participation in music therapy within mental health clinics; b\) Ways of relating to the argument that, as professionals, music therapists must heed established models of thinking in the clinic\. This theoretical article takes inspiration from two integrative metatheoretical traditions; the bioecological and sociocultural tradition and contemporary enactivist perspectives\. The examples that I present in this paper are based in practice contexts within mental healthcare in Bergen, Norway\. A “Three\-Stage Model” is outlined, with emphasis on the ecological transitions from i\) clinical music therapy, to ii\) municipal follow\-up services, to iii\) independent cultural participation in the local community\. The affordances and limitations of the notion of artistic citizenship in relation to the Three\-Stage Model are explored and related to the notions of personhood and selfhood\. The relationships between the Three\-Stage Model and organisational culture of mental health clinics in Norway are discussed, and areas of future research indicated\.

## [Clinical Performance of the IWGDF Risk Stratification System for Diabetic Foot Ulceration: A Gender\-Disaggregated Study of 713 Patients](../publications/0dc04850086634cd8b9a.md)

Fatimah Z Alenazi; Thamer Alslamah; Basmah F\. Alharbi; Wafa Ibrahim Alotaibi; Metab Algeffari; Yasir Alsalamah; Faisal I\. Almohaileb; Mirna Awni Fawaz; António Raposo

INTRODUCTION: Diabetic foot ulceration \(DFU\) is a major complication of diabetes and is a leading cause of lower\-extremity amputation\. This study evaluated the cross\-sectional discriminative performance of the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot \(IWGDF\) risk classification for prevalent active DFU, described gender\-disaggregated ulcer prevalence, and identified factors independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk in a specialist diabetes center\. METHODS: In this retrospective cross\-sectional study, 713 adults with diabetes mellitus who attended the diabetic foot service of a university diabetes center were classified according to the IWGDF risk system\. The prevalence of active DFU was compared across risk categories using the Cochran\-Armitage trend test\. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk and active DFU\. RESULTS: Active DFU was present in 21 patients \(2\.9%\), with no significant difference between men \(3\.8%\) and women \(2\.1%\)\. Overall, 17\.3% of the patients were classified as having moderate or high risk\. Ulcer prevalence increased progressively across the IWGDF categories, from 0\.0% in the very\-low\-risk group to 38\.5% in the high\-risk group \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The IWGDF classification showed excellent cross\-sectional discrimination for prevalent active DFU \(c\-statistic 0\.938\), with 90\.5% sensitivity and 99\.7% negative predictive value at the moderate/high\-risk threshold\. Older age and higher glycated hemoglobin \(HbA1c\) levels were independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk, whereas gender was not\. CONCLUSION: The IWGDF classification showed excellent cross\-sectional discrimination for prevalent active DFU\. Older age and poorer glycemic control, but not gender, were independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk\. These findings support routine IWGDF\-guided risk stratification in specialist diabetes care, although prospective studies are required to establish its performance in predicting future ulceration\.

## [Undergraduate students’ mastering of fragmentary technical translation using artificial intelligence](../publications/0dcb78503c2744c57300.md)

Roman Konstantinovich Chalov

The purpose of this study is to provide a theoretical foundation for and develop a technology for the integrative training of future translators – undergraduate students – in fragmentary technical translation \(FTT\) using artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools\. The main content of the article includes an analysis of the specifics of FTT, a classification of AI tools, and a description of four conceptual levels of integration \(discursive, speech\-cognitive, speech\-activity, and subject\-linguistic\)\. The scientific novelty lies in providing a theoretical justification for the didactic functions of the four levels of AI integration in FTT activities, developing a matrix for the distribution of functions between the student translator and AI as a pedagogical support tool \(“scaffolding”\), as well as in the didactic specification of the principle of “verifiable assistiveness”, which defines the boundaries of delegating translation tasks to AI in order to preserve the learner’s regulatory function\. The results of theoretical modeling suggest that the integration of AI into the learning process, provided that the student exercises reflective control, creates conditions for reducing cognitive load, stimulating speech\-thinking activity, and developing the strategic flexibility necessary for translation work within modern information flows in a corporate setting\.

## [OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence](../publications/0dfd3a837b538247395b.md)

Hongchen Wei; Daohong Ying; Zhi Hong; Aidan Wu; Bei Liu; Ruichun Ma; Yifan Yang; Qi Dai; Kai Qiu; Rui Xu; Dongdong Chen; Zhenzhong Chen; Chong Luo

AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables\. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments\. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work\. From a natural\-language description of an organization&\#x27;s purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables\. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do\. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning\. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain\-expert feedback\. Frontier\-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom\. Supervised fine\-tuning and on\-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3\.5\-9B on external professional\-work benchmarks, including GDPval\. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal\-\-assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single\- and multi\-agent baselines tested\. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work\-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents\.

## [The EU AI Act and the Polish Legal Order: Constitutional Framework, Regulatory Architecture, Policy and Implementation Gaps](../publications/0e00841fd367e1f12dd0.md)

Michał Jackowski

This article examines Poland’s implementation of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act from constitutional, legislative, institutional, and policy perspectives\. It analyses the Polish AI ecosystem, constitutional protections for dignity, privacy, informational autonomy, compensation, and appeal, and the evolving national regulatory framework\. ## [Deterministic fixed point inference with tiled parallelism for ASIC implementation of human activity recognition](../publications/0e0117abe0dc97a0ae40.md)

M\. Madhushankara; H Muralikrishna; Ananthakrishna Thalengala

Abstract Deploying machine learning models on hardware platforms requires careful handling of numerical precision, limited resources, and predictable execution\. In practice, mismatches between floating\-point software models and their register\-transfer level \(RTL\) implementations can lead to inconsistent inference results\. In this proposed work, a hardware–software co\-designed methodology that ensures bit\-accurate and deterministic inference across floating\-point and RTL implementations is proposed\. A fully connected neural network with a 64–64–6 architecture is trained on the UCI human activity recognition \(HAR\) dataset and mapped to a hardware\-friendly fixed\-point representation\. An application specific integrated circuit \(ASIC\)\-oriented RTL design is developed and validated against a cycle\-accurate Python fixed\-point model to ensure consistency between software and hardware execution\. To improve the performance, a tiled parallel multiply–accumulate \(MAC\) architecture with $$\\textit\{PAR\}=8$$ is employed, enabling higher throughput without significantly increasing hardware complexity\. The model achieves $$93\.24\\%$$ accuracy in floating\-point and $$92\.66\\%$$ after fixed\-point and RTL implementation, with a reduction of 0\.58 percentage points following quantization\. The RTL outputs match the fixed\-point model across all evaluated samples, confirming its deterministic behavior\. Synthesis using the TSMC 12 nm technology achieves a compute energy of 30\.33 pJ per inference and a total inference energy of 170\.67 pJ, demonstrating the suitability of the proposed methodology for edge AI applications\.

## [Case Report: A germline SDHB c\.268C&gt;T \(p\.Arg90Ter\) variant in a family with very\-early\-onset colorectal neoplasia](../publications/0e029d4400295495347b.md)

Chang Liu; Dayang Zhou; Wenjing Xu; Hai Pan; Xiang Ji; Jian Huang; Zhu Zhu

Background Very\-early\-onset colorectal cancer \(CRC\), particularly when clustered within a family, raises concern for an inherited cancer predisposition\. However, the contribution of germline SDHB variants to CRC susceptibility remains uncertain\. We report a family in which two sisters developed colorectal carcinoma before 25 years of age and in whom a known pathogenic germline SDHB variant was identified\. Case presentation A 22\-year\-old woman presented with a 3\-year history of intermittent hematochezia\. Complete colonoscopy identified an ulcerated lesion in the rectosigmoid region approximately 15 cm from the anal verge\. Endoscopic biopsy showed high\-grade intraepithelial neoplasia with focal intramucosal carcinoma\. The patient underwent laparoscopic rectal resection with lymph\-node dissection and sigmoidorectal anastomosis\. The surgical resection specimen demonstrated moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3N0M0, stage IIA, with no metastatic involvement in 14 examined lymph nodes\. Germline testing identified SDHB NM\_003000\.3:c\.268C&gt;T \(p\.Arg90Ter\)\. Her elder sister had developed rectal adenocarcinoma at 19 years of age, whereas their father had two rectal polyps measuring approximately 0\.6 and 0\.8 cm, with histopathology demonstrating tubular adenoma\. The same germline SDHB variant was detected in the proband, her elder sister, and her father\. In the proband’s tumor, the SDHB variant showed a VAF of 20\.75%, SDHB protein expression was retained, and no biallelic SDHB inactivation was demonstrated\. The tumor additionally harbored a somatic TP53 frameshift alteration and SMAD4 copy\-number loss\. Conclusions This family demonstrates remarkable clustering of very\-early\-onset colorectal neoplasia together with a known pathogenic germline SDHB variant\. However, the available segregation, molecular, and immunohistochemical evidence is insufficient to establish SDHB as a CRC susceptibility gene or to demonstrate an SDHB \-driven tumor mechanism\. This observation should therefore be considered hypothesis\-generating and warrants validation in additional families, larger cohorts, comprehensive genomic analyses, and CRC\-specific functional studies\.

## [Methodological concerns restrict generalizations about children’s overimitation](../publications/0e0686cd05336d99ecfb.md)

Ashley B\. Marin; Rebekah A\. Richert; Frankie T\. K\. Fong

Overimitation has been studied and theorized as a key social learning mechanism that drives cultural transmission\. Despite notable theoretical advancements, methodological inconsistencies and ecological gaps have made it difficult to draw broad conclusions about the nature and function of overimitation\. These differences create confounding explanations for both the factors that influence overimitation, as well as the developmental and cultural functions of overimitation, leaving gaps in what either individual studies or the collective body of work can reliably say about the causes and purposes of overimitation\. That is, certain effects may be partly, and unintentionally, shaped by specific methodological or procedural details\. In this article, we discuss how variations in design components from existing studies create tensions for explanations and conclusions\. We focus on the experimental tasks themselves, the behavioral coding schemes used to evaluate overimitation, and how experiments are set up\. We conclude by proposing approaches that place both the research question and the cultural context at the forefront, enabling scholars to more accurately study and/or compare children’s imitative behaviors across cultures and contexts\.

## [Low\-Level Laser Therapy in Dentistry: Biological Effects, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives](../publications/0e06e255dc279ae10e15.md)

Akshay Ashok Katara; Rajendra Avhad; Saloni Kanodia; Vishwabharati I Tayade; Sameer Chauhan; Priyanka Bind; Pratik Surana

Low\-level laser therapy \(LLLT\), also referred to as photobiomodulation therapy \(PBMT\), is being integrated into dental treatment progressively\.It has biological effects through light exposure, modulating cellular activity, helping to reduce pain, control inflammation, and heal tissue\.LLLT has been demonstrated to have potential uses in periodontal therapy, endodontics, oral surgery, implantology, orthodontics, temporomandibular disorders \(TMDs\), and pediatric dentistry\.However, considerable variations in laser parameters and treatment protocols limit the comparability of findings across studies and make it difficult to draw definitive conclusions\.This review highlights the biological mechanisms, clinical application, current evidence, safety, limitations, and future perspectives of LLLT for dental purposes\.

## [Workplace Safety Judgment from Images: Comparing AI Assistants Across Five Occupational Contexts](../publications/0e0ca380c4390455c062.md)

Mehmed Zahid Çögenli; Yılmaz Karadaş

This study compared the image\-based workplace safety judgments of three general\-purpose AI assistants across five occupational contexts\. Fifteen workplace images representing construction, workshop/manufacturing, maintenance/technical service, warehouse/logistics, and laboratory settings were evaluated by ChatGPT GPT\-5\.5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3\.5 Flash\. Each model completed 15 single\-image assessments and five within\-context relative\-ranking tasks, yielding 60 outputs\. Two occupational safety specialists independently rated the outputs on five 0–5 dimensions and six binary error patterns\. The raters showed exact or near\-exact score agreement in 81\.8% of the ordinal ratings; pooled quadratic weighted agreement was moderate, κ = 0\.479, 95% CI \[0\.340, 0\.595\]\. Agreement was complete for pairwise ranking accuracy and exact final ordering\. Based on the two\-rater means, ChatGPT led in visible evidence coverage \(4\.37\), visual fidelity \(4\.43\), prioritization \(3\.73\), and uncertainty discipline \(4\.70\), whereas Claude obtained the highest descriptive control\-guidance mean \(4\.40\)\. Between\-model differences were statistically significant in the other four dimensions but not in control guidance\. No rater\-confirmed problematic control recommendation was observed\. All three models achieved the same final\-match performance: four of five context rankings were fully correct and 14 of 15 pairwise relations were correct\. The shared failure occurred in the workshop/manufacturing context, where the image containing a visible person at height was ranked below a dusty but static scene\. The findings support supervised first\-pass use of AI assistants but not autonomous workplace safety evaluation\.

## [Delivering online cognitive behavioral therapy to address mental health challenges in correctional workers: a randomized controlled trial](../publications/0e12e4e21ae6f53c06d8.md)

Christina Holmes; Gilmar Gutiérrez; Callum Stephenson; Elnaz Moghimi; Niloufar Malakouti; Jasleen Jagayat; C\. B\. Patel; Alexander I\. F\. Simpson; Cory J\. Gerritsen; Michael Martin; Mark Fitzpatrick; Jazmin Eadie; Anika Agrawal; Vineeth Jarabana; Kimia Asadpour; Ferwa Khan; Dianne Groll; Mohsen Omrani; Nazanin Alavi

Background Correctional workers \(CWs\), are frequently exposed to traumatic workplace events, placing them at higher risk of experiencing mental health disorders, including major depressive disorder \(MDD\), generalized anxiety disorder \(GAD\), and posttraumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\)\. Despite high prevalence of mental health challenges, CWs underutilize mental health services due to stigma, irregular work schedules, and accessibility issues\. While cognitive behavioral therapy \(CBT\) is effective, it poses accessibility challenges\. Electronic CBT \(eCBT\) offers a scalable, accessible alternative, but use among CWs remains underexplored\. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of diagnosis\-specific eCBT programs designed for CWs in reducing symptoms of MDD, GAD, and PTSD compared to treatment as usual \(TAU\)\. Methods A randomized controlled trial \(RCT\) was conducted with 84 CWs in Ontario, assigned to either eCBT \(n=40\) or TAU \(n=44\)\. The eCBT program provided diagnosis\-specific modules with synchronous personalized feedback from care providers over 12\-weeks via the Online Psychotherapy Tool \(OPTT\)\. Symptom severity was measured at baseline, week\-6, and post\-treatment using validated scales for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and quality\-of\-life\. Data analysis included paired samples t\-tests, mixed linear models, and effect size calculations \(Cohen’s d\)\. Results The eCBT group exhibited significant reductions in symptom severity for depression, anxiety, and PTSD from baseline to post\-treatment compared to TAU \(p&lt;0\.01\), with a moderate effect size \(Cohen’s d=0\.68\)\. Symptom severity decreased by 61\.37% for eCBT versus 23\.29% in TAU\. Mixed linear models confirmed a significant treatment\-by\-time interaction, favoring eCBT \(p&lt;0\.01\)\. However, no significant differences in quality\-of\-life improvements were observed between groups\. Conclusions Diagnosis\-specific eCBT programs are effective in reducing symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD for CWs\. The asynchronous, accessible format of eCBT addresses current key barriers\. Future research should explore strategies to improve adherence and increase the accessibility of services for CWs\.

## [Ontology\-Grounded RAG with SPARQL and Local Language Models for Technical Documentation](../publications/0e1ace538ce267c24e4d.md)

Julián Rafael Coronel Andrade; Edwin Alexander Siguenza Siguenza; Andrew Sebastian Cantos Vasquez; Pablo Sebastián Vélez Mejía; Marcos Orellana

This paper presents LIDI\-AI, a Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) system whose knowledge base consists of technical documentation for the LIDI\-AI Research Assistant, a web\-based data analysis application developed at Universidad del Azuay\. The runtime architecture integrates two complementary knowledge sources: an OWL 2 ontology \(artifact version 2\.0\) with six classes and twenty\-five properties \(nine object and sixteen datatype properties\) that models the five\-stage pipeline, the accepted file formats, the statistical analysis types, and the system errors, and a SPARQL 1\.1 query layer for structured intent resolution\. A Prolog knowledge base built on an Object\-Attribute\-Value \(OAV\) representation, comprising 172 facts, 17 inference rules, and three diagnostic engines, is formally specified and validated as a symbolic reasoning layer, although it is not yet callable from the Python orchestrator at runtime\. A lexical retrieval module selects ontology fragments as grounded context for a locally hosted language model, specifically Llama\-3\.2\-3B deployed via the Ollama framework with Q4\_K\_M quantization\. Evaluation on ten queries from real users shows that seven were resolved with high precision via SPARQL\-grounded retrieval, two were resolved via lexical fallback with ontology traceability, and one out\-of\-domain query received an explicit knowledge\-limit acknowledgment, yielding an appropriate response rate with zero hallucinations\.

## [Multidimensional evolutionary paths in agricultural resilience research: a bibliometric analysis based on citespace and SciMAT](../publications/0e1b15a297f3186c9e9d.md)

Wenyu Song; Siyu Gong; 于志岗

Agricultural resilience refers to the capacity of agricultural systems to respond to extreme weather events while maintaining food security and system stability, and it has become an important topic in sustainability research\. Although the literature on agricultural resilience has expanded rapidly, comprehensive bibliometric assessments of this field remain limited\. Based on 3221 articles published in the Web of Science Core Collection between 2003 and 2025, this study applies CiteSpace and SciMAT to systematically map the development of agricultural resilience research\. This study assesses national research output, institutional contributions, collaboration networks, and keyword co\-occurrence to map the knowledge structure and evolution\. The results show that agricultural resilience research has progressed through three main stages: initial theoretical exploration, mid\-term practical application, and recent integrative studies\. Current research focuses on adaptability, ecosystem services, and integrated analytical frameworks\. Despite this progress, challenges remain, including the absence of standardized measurement indicators and pronounced regional imbalances in research attention\. Future studies should foster interdisciplinary collaboration, integrate technological innovation with policy analysis, and develop multi\-scale assessment frameworks\. These steps will guide region\-specific adaptation strategies under climate uncertainty\.

Yunran Wang; Cheng Shi

With the development of new media technology, the important mission of inheriting China&\#x27;s traditional music culture is facing great challenges, including the influence of multiculturalism and the insufficient utilization of technical resources\. In this context, it is very important to explore effective communication strategies in the new media environment for the preservation and innovation of traditional music culture\. This paper discusses the opportunities and challenges of social media and big data in spreading traditional music culture\. The proposed strategies include building an online education platform, optimizing the teaching system, enriching the cultural database and establishing a technology\-integrated museum\. In addition, improving students&\#x27; media literacy and expanding multimedia platforms can significantly enhance cultural communication\. By exploring concept innovation, resource mining, field expansion and integration with market economy, this study provides implementation strategies for promoting traditional music culture in the university environment\.

## [Scene Reconstruction Using Ubiquitous Wireless Signals via Diffusion Posterior Inference Over physics\-Grounded Representations](../publications/0e2279ee9ddfcc4036b4.md)

Vahid Yazdnian; Yasaman Ghasempour

Knowing the layout of the physical world matters for many applications, yet the sensors we rely on for it \(e\.g\., cameras and LiDAR\) can fail in darkness, in adverse weather, or behind walls\. Wireless signals do not face these limitations: every link between a base station and a user is shaped by the buildings it passes, reflects from, or is blocked by, leaving information about the surrounding scene embedded in the wireless channel measured at the endpoints\. However, mapping channel measurements to the environment is a severely ill\-posed problem: a measurement records only the structures that interact with the transmitted electromagnetic waves along its propagation paths, and even these observations can often be explained by multiple plausible scenes\. We therefore formulate wireless scene reconstruction as posterior inference and develop a hierarchical framework with two complementary stages to approach this problem\. A wireless foundation model, pretrained to respect propagation physics, transforms each channel measurement into a representation of the scene structure that shaped the observation\. A diffusion model then jointly integrates representations from multiple measurements to model and sample the posterior over building occupancy, with consensus over samples producing the final reconstruction\. We demonstrate that the framework can accurately recover building footprints from wireless channel measurements alone and show that its performance depends critically on both design components: physics\-grounded representations expose scene\-relevant information, while joint posterior inference coherently integrates complementary observations\.

## [Intelligent Field‐Adaptive Electrohydrodynamic Printing for Curved Conformal Electronics](../publications/0e2827334d29dd220ae9.md)

C X Liu; Yiwen Feng; Xu Chen; Kaiwen Chen; Ran Zhang; Xiaopeng Zhang; Liujia Suo; Xiangji Chen; Zefei LI; Fengshu Wang; Ruixuan Xu; Shuaiwu Liu; Shiwen Liang; Lingjie Kong; Dazhi Wang

ABSTRACT Curved conformal electronics are increasingly important for wearable devices, biosensing, and advanced communication systems, requiring high‐resolution and high‐precision manufacturing on complex surfaces\. Electrohydrodynamic printing is a promising method for fabricating conformal electronics, but its application on curved insulating substrates is hindered by local electric‐field disturbances arising from residual charge accumulation and spatial variations, leading to poor dimensional control\. To address this challenge, an intelligent field‐adaptive electrohydrodynamic printing framework is established, in which alternating‐electric‐field modulation reduces the effects of residual charge, the equivalent electrical gap quantitatively characterizes spatially varying electric‐field conditions, and machine learning‐based parameter regulation compensates for local electric‐field variations\. Based on this framework, a machine‐learning and alternating‐electric‐field synergistic modulated electrohydrodynamic printing approach is developed to achieve stable printing and precise line‐width control on curved substrates\. The approach rapidly optimizes parameters for target line widths, achieving average relative errors around 10% or lower at the initial printing position, and further reduces average relative line‐width errors by up to 7\.24 percentage points through adaptive regulation during curved‐substrate printing\. Diverse high‐precision patterns are printed, and the conformal frequency‐selective surface and antenna with excellent electromagnetic performance are fabricated, demonstrating the potential of this framework for advancing curved conformal electronics manufacturing\.

## [Tren Penelitian Kecemasan Matematika \(Mathematics Anxiety\) dan Strategi Pembelajaran untuk Mengatasinya](../publications/0e302f5a915d07f67b6c.md)

Rapsi Anggira Anjuni; Khathibul Umam Zaid Nugroho; Musdalipa Musdalipa; NURHADI NURHADI; Finta Rahmawati

This study aims to map research trends on students&\#x27; mathematics anxiety from 2020 to 2026, identify its effects on learning processes and outcomes, and synthesize learning strategies used to address it\. The method used was a Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) based on the procedural framework\. Literature searches were conducted through Google Scholar, Publish or Perish, ResearchGate, DOAJ, SINTA, and Scopus\. Of 38 identified articles, 19 met the selection criteria and were analyzed\. The findings show that publications on mathematics anxiety tended to increase during 2024–2026\. Mathematics anxiety was associated with reduced concentration, lower self\-confidence, avoidance of mathematics learning, and lower academic achievement and problem\-solving performance in several studies\. The identified strategies included contextual learning, cooperative learning, concrete media and educational games, positive reinforcement, psychological support, and the development of mathematical resilience and self\-regulation\. The study concludes that mathematics anxiety is a multidimensional issue and its mitigation should be adapted to students&\#x27; characteristics and learning contexts\. Keywords: Learning strategies; Mathematics anxiety; Mathematics learning; Students; Systematic Literature Review\.

## [Matching developmental timelines of fish, frog, mouse and human brains](../publications/0e3fa987f526f657e374.md)

Hyun Jung Park; 정호성

The overall structure and development of the central nervous system \(CNS\) are highly conserved among vertebrates\. Peak neurogenesis generally precedes the main wave of astrogliogenesis; exuberant synapses are formed and pruned during critical periods; and the neurotransmitter gamma\-aminobutyric acid \(GABA\) shifts from depolarizing to hyperpolarizing as the brain matures\. The sequence of these key developmental events is broadly similar across vertebrate model organisms, including mouse, Xenopus, and zebrafish\. Despite this overall similarity, the relative duration of each event varies substantially, and key events such as live birth in mammals do not occur in fish or frogs\. These differences must be considered when translating findings from one species to another\. In this review, we compare several developmental events that are relevant to modeling human diseases in animal models, including microglial colonization and blood–brain barrier formation\. We also present comparative developmental timelines as a resource for translational neuroscience research\.

## [Environmental Chemistry in higher education across Europe](../publications/0e4fb466238dd6e6b849.md)

Ivana Ivančev\-Tumbas; Ester Heath; Gerhard Lammel

In the academic year 2024/25, the EuChemS Division on Chemistry and the Environment \(DCE\) conducted a Europe\-wide survey of higher education programmes that include Environmental Chemistry, either as the principal discipline or as embedded content in interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary curricula\. Information on 300 programmes was collected from universities in 31 countries, i\.e\. 113 at the 1st, 156 at the 2nd and 31 at the 3rd study level\. Respectively, 42%, 35% and 19% of the programmes shared details on the contents, teaching tools used, needs and future plans, while the rest of the responding programmes shared only basic information\. With basic information on additional 159 1st and 2nd study level programmes based on web search by the authors \(mostly for non\-responsive countries\), in total, 428 programmes at the 1st and the 2nd study level were identified\. Since response rate varied dramatically across countries, the representativeness was severely undermined the findings for Europe as a whole\. From the information collected from programmes which responded, it was found that multidisciplinary and/or environmental compartment\-related approaches are present in programmes&\#x27; design early, even from 1st level of education and more diverse at the 2nd level\. Environmental Chemistry is taught in science programmes containing the terms &\#x27;environment\(\-al\)&\#x27;, &\#x27;Chemistry&\#x27;, &\#x27;Geoscience&\#x27; and &\#x27;Toxicology&\#x27;, but also quite frequently in engineering programmes\. The water, climate, protection and sustainability themes are very common\. A wide variety of programmes clearly reflects the importance of knowledge about the behaviour and effects of chemicals \(including accompanying substances and waste products\) in the environment for the training of experts in a variety of professions and occupational fields\. The analysis of the contents of programmes with Environmental Chemistry as their principal discipline suggests that there is no uniform understanding of what exactly constitutes the discipline as a main or important topic within an interdisciplinary curriculum, most probably as a consequence of very broad discipline&\#x27;s boundaries\. Greater consistency and better comparability of the content, skills and qualifications offered by degree programmes to be acquired therein could be achieved through a coordinated effort which would better define core contents\.

## [ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ ПОТЕНЦИАЛА ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА ДЛЯ ПОВЫШЕНИЯ КАЧЕСТВА ПРОЕКТИРОВАНИЯ ЗДАНИЙ](../publications/0e517bf24a70b59dbbe2.md)

МИХАИЛ ЮРЬЕВИЧ ВИРЦЕВ; АРТЕМ ИГОРЕВИЧ МАЧУЛЬСКИЙ; АЛЕКСАНДР МИХАЙЛОВИЧ ВИРЦЕВ

Интеграция искусственного интеллекта в процесс архитектурно\-строительного проектирования предоставляет беспрецедентные возможности для совершенствования инженерных и дизайнерских аспектов\. Это позволяет достигать оптимальных решений, существенно улучшать эксплуатационные характеристики и долговечность зданий, а также повышать их экологическую устойчивость\. Искусственный интеллект представляет собой совокупность систем, наделенных способностью воспроизводить функции человека\. Они, в свою очередь, включают, но не ограничиваются, идентификацией визуальных повторяющихся элементов, процессом принятия решений и приобретением новых знаний\. С помощью генеративных инструментов, работающих на искусственном интеллекте, можно быстро получить множество различных вариантов дизайна или проекта\. Эти варианты будут точно соответствовать всем вашим условиям и ограничениям\. Предложенная методология предполагает развитие творческих способностей и способствует повышению эффективности временных затрат при проектировании\. Использование методов машинного обучения в сочетании с инструментами искусственного интеллекта открывает широкие возможности для проведения комплексного анализа всех данных\. Результатом такой стратегии является оптимизация пространственной конфигурации застройки, обеспечивающая повышение энергетической автономности зданий и сооружений\. Использование технологий машинного обучения обеспечивает эффективную обработку данных, полученных из сенсорных систем и прогностических моделей\. Это позволяет нам идентифицировать закономерности и тенденции, характерные для архитектурного проектирования\. Использование аналитической базы информации обеспечивает принятие решений, при этом повышая их качество и эффективность\. Стремительный прогресс в области искусственного интеллекта открывает беспрецедентные перспективы для инноваций в проектировании различных зданий и сооружений\.

## [Machine learning integration of Sentinel\-1 SAR and ground\-based measurements for soil moisture estimation in temperate forested landscape of Somogy County, Hungary](../publications/0e54c77a4a8ffb53938c.md)

Study region Somogy County is located in south\-western Hungary \(45\.95°–46\.50°N, 17\.40°–18\.00°E\) and covers 6065 km²\. The region includes temperate forests, intensive agricultural land, and wetlands developed on diverse soils, including Eutric Luvisols, Cambisols, Albeluvisols, Acid Gleysols, and Aquic Gleysols\. The climate ranges from subhumid to humid\. Regional SWC maps were generated at 10 m resolution and further analysed using a Forest Vulnerability Index and a five\-level management priority classification\. New hydrological insight for the region Station\-scale model performance was strong \(R² = 0\.866–0\.913; RMSE = 0\.018–0\.022 m³ m⁻³; NSE = 0\.838–0\.891\), while regional predictions showed moderate accuracy \(R² = 0\.532–0\.648; RMSE = 0\.033–0\.041 m³ m⁻³\), with KNN providing the best spatial transferability among the three models tested, though absolute spatial transferability remained limited under station\-holdout cross\-validation\. Given the three\-station, two\-summer observation network, these county\-scale maps serve as a pilot regional extrapolation rather than a fully validated product\. VV backscatter, antecedent SWC, and saturated water content were the main predictors\. Spatial patterns revealed higher drought sensitivity in sandy lowlands and greater moisture retention in silt\-loam uplands, with a marked drying trend between 2024 and 2025, particularly in northern forest areas\.

## [An interpretable machine learning risk stratification model for the imaging burden of cerebral small vessel disease: integrating echocardiography, carotid ultrasound, and serological indicators](../publications/0e643b2fc4cd9a5232ed.md)

Huilan Tan; Houwei Li; Chulin Deng; Sisi Liang; 蓝家富

This study enrolled 401 subjects, who were stratified according to the total imaging burden score of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease \(CSVD\) and divided into a training set \(280 cases\) and a validation set \(121 cases\) at a ratio of 7:3\. Six variables—age, left ventricular posterior wall end\-diastolic thickness, E/e′ ratio, maximum carotid plaque thickness, history of hypertension, and low\-density lipoprotein cholesterol—were included, and Logistic regression, K\-nearest neighbor, and partial least squares models were separately constructed\. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity, and decision curve analysis\. The results showed that the K\-nearest neighbor model achieved the best performance in the validation set \(AUC 0\.869, accuracy 82\.6%, sensitivity 65\.0%, specificity 95\.1%\)\. SHAP analysis clarified the contribution of each feature, with E/e′ being the strongest predictor \(mean absolute SHAP value 0\.194\), followed by maximum carotid plaque thickness and age \(0\.085 and 0\.062, respectively\)\. Decision curve analysis showed that the model yielded the greatest net benefit at a disease\-risk threshold of 35%\. With a specificity of 95\.1%, the model performed prominently in risk stratification of CSVD patients, could effectively identify low\-risk populations and reduce unnecessary imaging examinations, but its sensitivity was relatively low \(65\.0%\), making it more suitable for clinical secondary diagnosis\.

## [Online forecasting for financial time series](../publications/0e6c8bf163b42804062e.md)

Nikolas Michael; Mihai Cucuringu; Sam Howison

We introduce OFTER \(online forecasting via temporal embedding regression\), a time series forecasting pipeline tailored for financial problems centered on mid\-sized multivariate time series\. OFTER utilizes the non\-parametric models of k\-nearest neighbors and generalized regression neural networks, integrated with a dimensionality reduction component\. To circumvent the curse of dimensionality, we employ a weighted norm based on a modified version of the maximal correlation coefficient\. The pipeline we introduce is specifically designed for online tasks, has an interpretable output, and is able to outperform several state\-of\-the\-art baselines\. The computational efficacy of the algorithm, its online nature, and its ability to operate in low signal\-to\-noise regimes, render OFTER an ideal approach for financial multivariate time series problems, such as daily equity forecasting\. Our work demonstrates that while deep learning models hold significant promise for time series forecasting, traditional methods carefully integrating mainstream tools remain very competitive alternatives with the added benefits of scalability and interpretability\.

## [Relationship Between Osteoarthritis and Metabolic Diseases: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis](../publications/0e6fcbbe368cb321dd86.md)

Yunping Weng; Junyan Wu; 谢水兰; Zhang Yumin

Background/Aims: To map global research on osteoarthritis \(OA\) and metabolic diseases, separately examining individual metabolic diseases and metabolic syndrome \(MetS\), and identify gaps and emerging frontiers\. Materials and Methods: Web of Science Core Collection publications \(2009–2025\) were retrieved on February 22, 2026\. Co\-authorship and keyword co\-occurrence networks, Louvain clustering \(modularity and silhouette evaluation\), burst detection, and keyword\-cluster visualization were performed\. Betweenness centrality assessed country collaboration\. Chord diagrams and temporal streamgraphs mapped pairwise disease co\-study patterns and trajectories\. GLP\-1 receptor agonist \(GLP\-1RA\) trends were assessed using 24 predefined terms\. Results: We included 10,217 articles from 1582 journals by 38,665 authors\. Annual output rose 4\.4\-fold between 2009 and 2025\. The United States \(33\.4%\), China \(15\.0%\), and the United Kingdom \(9\.3%\) were the leading contributors\. Ten major themes were identified: progression, arthroplasty, physical activity, inflammation, prevalence, Mendelian randomization, meta\-analysis, knee OA, body mass index, and hip\. Obesity and type 2 diabetes were the most frequently co\-studied conditions\. Obesity showed the strongest sustained growth, whereas nonalcoholic fatty liver disease \(NAFLD\) received limited attention\. Inflammation and risk were the strongest burst terms\. OA\-related GLP\-1RA publications increased 9\.7\-fold after 2021\. Conclusion: OA\-metabolic disease research is expanding rapidly\. NAFLD, hyperuricemia, and MetS remain underexplored, while GLP\-1RA is a major emerging frontier\. Cite this article as: Weng Y, Wu J, Xie S, Zhang Y\. Relationship Between Osteoarthritis and Metabolic Diseases: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis\. ArchRheumatol\. Published online October 14, 2026\. doi: 10\.5152/ ArchRheumatol\.2026\.26556\.

## [The Serotonergic and Cholinergic Signaling Pathways Drive Gastric Precancerous Lesions and Its Potential Mechanism](../publications/0e781d998ad57800b48e.md)

Shengli Gao; Xufei Feng; Nana Zhang; Jia Su; Yuyan Wang; Linghan Kong; Jianing Zhou; Hui Dong; Feifei Guo

Gastric cancer \(GC\) is a leading lethal malignancy globally\. Gastric precancerous lesion \(GPL\) represents a critical step in GC, but its neural regulatory mechanisms remain largely unclear\. We combined bioinformatics, patch\-clamp recording, immunofluorescence, and chemogenetics to investigate serotonergic and cholinergic signaling in GPL\. An N\-methyl\-N\-nitrosourea \(MNU\) \-induced mouse model was used for in vivo validation\. High 5\-HTR1D expression correlated with poor survival in gastric adenocarcinoma patients and was upregulated in AGS and MKN45 cells, as well as in gastric tissues of GPL mice\. 5\-HT evoked non\-selective cation currents involving 5\-HTR1D and TRPV4 in gastric epithelial and cancer cells, as supported by both pharmacological inhibition and siRNA\-mediated TRPV4 knockdown\. Blockade of 5\-HTR1D or TRPV4 attenuated intestinal metaplasia and dysplasia, and this improvement was accompanied by reduced AKT/mTOR activation in GPL mice\. Increased gastric M3R/5\-HT co\-localization was associated with elevated acetylcholine and overactivated cholinergic neurons in the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus \(DMV\)\. Chemogenetic inhibition of DMV cholinergic neurons decreased ChAT and 5\-HT levels and alleviated gastric pathology in GPL mice\. These findings suggest that 5\-HT/5\-HTR1D signaling may promote TRPV4\-involved cation currents, contributing to mucosal pathology and intestinal metaplasia in GPL model mice, whereas DMV cholinergic neurons projecting to the stomach may facilitate gastric 5\-HT secretion and thereby potentially contribute to GPL progression\. This work establishes a novel neuro\-epithelial network linking vagal cholinergic output to serotonergic signaling that may be involved in GPL progression, providing potential targets for prevention and intervention\.

## [Love of variety? An experimental study of heterogeneous responses to foreign brands in the marketplace](../publications/0e7c77daa26c55a77c22.md)

Valentina González‐Rostani; Jude C\. Hays

Abstract Do everyday encounters with foreign brands shape political attitudes? We argue that brand origin cues activate national identities, producing different responses among nationalists and cosmopolitans\. In an online shopping experiment, U\.S\. participants were randomly assigned to compare American \(control\), European, or Asian \(treatment\) sport utility vehicles without explicit mention of brand origin\. Exposure to foreign brands increased opposition to trade and immigration and support for Donald Trump among nationalists\. Cosmopolitans generally showed little change\. These effects are not reducible to partisanship, revealing within\-coalition divides among Republicans and among Democrats and Independents\. Our findings show that subtle consumer experiences spill over into politics, creating a bottom\-up channel of polarization that links nationalism and populism to support for neomercantilist and nativist policies\.

## [A hybrid QSPR\-MCDM framework for ranking organic acids using topological indices](../publications/0e7e121323fdd241e0c3.md)

Zhihong Xue; Shamaila Yousaf; Waheed Khalid; Ferdous M\. O\. Tawfiq; Keneni Abera Tola

Organic acids are industrially and pharmaceutically important compounds, yet selecting the most suitable acid for a given application is complicated by the need to reconcile multiple, often conflicting physicochemical properties\. This study develops and validates a hybrid framework that integrates Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship \(QSPR\) modeling with Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making \(MCDM\) to systematically rank twenty organic acids\. Thirteen degree\-based topological indices were computed from the hydrogen\-suppressed molecular graphs of the acids and used as structural descriptors to build linear QSPR models for five key physicochemical properties: boiling point, molecular weight, enthalpy of vaporization, flash point, and density\. All five models were statistically significant \( \\\(p &lt; 0\.001\\\) \), with leave\-one\-out cross\-validated \\\(Q^2\\\) values ranging from 0\.52 to 0\.77, confirming genuine predictive capability\. The QSPR\-estimated properties then constituted the decision matrix for the MCDM stage\. Three MCDM methods \(TOPSIS, VIKOR, and SAW\) were combined with four weight\-allocation approaches \(Point Allocation, Mean Weight, Standard Deviation, and Entropy\), yielding twelve distinct ranking scenarios that were subsequently integrated into a single composite ordering via rank\-average aggregation\. Unlike earlier applications of MCDM in chemical graph theory, where topological indices themselves served as criteria, the present framework employs indices exclusively as structure descriptors within the QSPR stage, ensuring that the final ranking reflects predicted chemical behavior rather than abstract graph\-theoretic quantities\. The results demonstrate strong robustness at the extremes of the ranking: Ascorbic acid and Gallic acid consistently occupy the top two positions across all twelve scenarios, while Tetraacetic acid is uniformly ranked last\. In contrast, mid\-tier acids such as Citric acid, Tartaric acid, Phthalic acid, and EDAHA display considerable rank variability, reflecting more balanced property profiles that are sensitive to weighting choices\. Spearman rank correlation between individual scenarios and the composite ranking ranged from \\\(\\rho \\approx 0\.87\\\) to \\\(\\rho \\approx 0\.99\\\) , with differentiated weighting schemes \(PA, SD, E\) agreeing more closely with the composite than the equal\-weight scheme\. The proposed QSPR\-MCDM framework offers a robust, objective, and adaptable tool for holistic compound assessment and rational selection in chemical, material, and pharmaceutical applications, moving beyond single\-property prediction toward informed multi\-criteria decision\-making\.

## [Beyond Leaf Images: A Personalized Multimodal Temporal AI Framework for Pre\-Symptomatic Plant Health Monitoring and Disease\-Risk Early Warning](../publications/0e8ffa60c5ae8f18f8ec.md)

Rupali Prakash Kolamkar; Rupali Prakash Kolamkar; Kshitij Shantaram Doundkar; Neha Waychol; Sunil P Mahajan

Artificial intelligence has advanced plant disease recognition, mainly through image\-based deep learning\. Its weakness is timing: a camera records a visible symptom, a model matches it to a known class, and a label is returned\. This confirms disease but says little about the earlier period, when a plant is already changing yet shows no clear lesion\. This paper proposes PlantPulse, a personalized multimodal temporal framework for that pre\-symptomatic window\. It draws on environmental, soil, optional electrophysiological or impedance, thermal and volatile organic compound signals, together with periodic RGB images\. Rather than judging every plant against a population model, PlantPulse learns a reference pattern for each plant during a healthy period, scores new observations against it, and uses a temporal anomaly layer to detect departures\. A risk layer then uses environmental and physiological context to separate normal variation, plausible abiotic stress, possible disease risk and cases in which the evidence is insufficient, while an uncertainty layer allows the system to abstain rather than mislabel unusual signals as disease\. The paper defines a common data representation, candidate statistical and deep learning models, three multimodal fusion strategies and an evaluation protocol built around warning lead time, false alarm burden, calibration, missing modalities, cross\-environment testing and leakage control\. PlantPulse is presented as a research design rather than a validated system; its value must be established through longitudinal trials with independent ground truth\. The aim is continuous monitoring in which images remain important but are no longer the only evidence\.
