## [Integrating bulk and single\-cell RNA sequencing to identify mitochondrial quality control\-related key genes in rheumatoid arthritis](../publications/0e961be187ebe618a7e9.md)

Yuting Xiao; Jiayou zhang; Jing Su; Jing Wu

Mitochondrial quality control \(MQC\) dysfunction contributes to rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\), but MQC\-related genes in RA remain incompletely characterized\. We integrated two bulk blood transcriptomic datasets and one peripheral blood mononuclear cell \(PBMC\) single\-cell RNA\-sequencing dataset \(248 RA and 88 control bulk samples; 11,719 cells from 3 RA and 3 healthy donors\)\. Weighted gene co\-expression network and differential expression analyses, combined with three machine\-learning algorithms, identified candidate genes\. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory network, single\-cell, cell–cell communication, pseudotime, metabolic, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction \(RT\-qPCR\) analyses were performed\. Nine MQC\-related candidate genes were identified; CDC42 and RBBP7 emerged as key genes, with CDC42 upregulated and RBBP7 downregulated in RA\. Gene set enrichment analysis \(GSEA\) linked CDC42 to JAK–STAT signaling, while translation initiation showed opposite enrichment patterns\. After multiple\-testing correction, 15 immune\-cell subsets differed between RA and controls; monocytes positively correlated with CDC42 and negatively with RBBP7\. Single\-cell analysis showed relatively high RBBP7 expression in B cells, motivating exploratory analyses of B\-cell trajectories, metabolism, and predicted CCL5–CCR1 communication with monocytes\. RT\-qPCR confirmed the mRNA expression patterns\. These findings identify CDC42 and RBBP7 as MQC\-related key genes associated with distinct immune and metabolic features in blood\-derived samples from patients with RA\.

## [Development and Preliminary Reliability Assessment of a Standardised Tool for Meda Sāra Parīkṣā](../publications/0ea327094df206bacbf0.md)

P\. S\. Muktha; T\. Saritha; Prasanna N Mogasale; Nagaraj S\.

Introduction: Daśa Vidha Parīkṣā is an important Ayurvedic diagnostic tool used to assess Āyu Bala, Ātura Bala, and Vyādhi Bala, thereby guiding appropriate treatment planning\. Meda Sāra, one of the Aṣṭa Sāra, reflects the excellence of Meda Dhātu and is associated with Snigdhatā, Sthairya, softness, and nourishment; however, its clinical utility is limited due to the lack of standardized assessment criteria\. Objectives: To study the parameters of Meda Sāra Puruṣa, develop and standardize assessment criteria based on classical Ayurvedic texts, and clinically evaluate these parameters\. Materials and Methods: An observational cross\-sectional study was conducted on 50 apparently healthy volunteers aged 18–40 years, of either gender, were recruited by consecutive sampling, using a structured proforma based on the Meda Sāra Lakṣaṇa described by Ācārya Caraka and Ācārya Suśruta\. Participants were assessed through history, physical, psychological, and functional evaluations and screened using the WHOQOL\-BREF questionnaire\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha\. Results: In the present study, the majority of participants belonged to the Madhyama Meda Sāra category \(74%\), followed by Pravara Meda Sāra \(24%\) and Avara Meda Sāra \(2%\), indicating moderate expression of Meda Sāra Lakṣaṇa among healthy individuals\. Conclusion: The developed tool demonstrated preliminary reliability and provides a structured approach for Meda Sāra assessment; however, further studies are required for wider validation and clinical applicability\. Keywords: Meda Sāra, Meda Dhātu, Sāra Parīkṣā

## [Between the Lines: Decoding Signaling Differences in Public and Private Sector Job Advertisements](../publications/0ea6eba41a6b7672a380.md)

Nico Gießmann; Nicolas Drathschmidt

ABSTRACT To compete in the “war for talent,” public sector employers must demonstrate advantages over private employers\. While public service motivation \(PSM\) predicts sector preference, scholars disagree on whether public employers \(can\) effectively signal PSM in job advertisements\. Consequently, this article examines how public and private job advertisements differ in language\. We collected 5000 advertisements from both sectors and performed natural language processing \(NLP\) and qualitative content analysis\. Both sectors use specialized language that can narrow the applicant pool\. PSM signals appear more often in the public sector, but affective motives are rarely communicated; instead, self‐sacrifice is framed as a legal obligation\. Public sector advertisements adopt a rational tone instead of explaining purpose and societal value\. Legally mandated, saturated signals may be perceived as low‐cost and ineffective\. The findings explain the mixed results concerning PSM signaling and underscore the gap between theory and practice in PSM‐related recruitment efforts\.

## [Adaptación de la consulta ortodóntica para un adulto con trastorno del espectro autista: reporte de caso](../publications/0eab57553509bda21a9b.md)

Brayan Condolo Bravo; Gerson Cabezas Bernhardt; Ana Maria Cabezas Espinosa

El trastorno del espectro autista \(TEA\) es una condición del neurodesarrollo que afecta la comunicación, la interacción social y el comportamiento\. Estas características pueden influir significativamente en la salud oral debido a dificultades en la higiene bucal por sus perfiles sensoriales, patrones alimenticios atípicos, ansiedad y miedo ante procedimientos dentales y dificultades sensoriales, lo que plantea retos adicionales para el tratamiento odontológico y ortodóncico\. Reportamos el caso de un paciente masculino de 20 años de edad, estudiante de Ingeniería Civil en la Universidad San Francisco de Quito, diagnosticado con Trastorno de espectro autista Nivel 1, según la clasificación DSM\-5 por su nivel de necesidades de acompañamiento\. El paciente presentó una relación esqueletal Clase I, con biprotrusión maxilo\-mandibular, así como apiñamiento moderado en el sector anterior\. Este reporte describe la planificación y el manejo de un tratamiento ortodóncico correctivo en un paciente con diversidad funcional, destacando las adaptaciones clínicas y comunicacionales necesarias para favorecer la cooperación y minimizar el estrés durante el tratamiento\. Se discuten las principales dificultades que enfrentan las personas autistas al someterse a terapia ortodóncica, incluyendo la sensibilidad sensorial, la tolerancia a los aparatos y la adherencia a las indicaciones, subrayando la importancia de un enfoque interdisciplinario y personalizado\.

## [Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges](../publications/0eaccb74ed11b58dd5e3.md)

Qianqian Liu; Chaojie Wang; Zeyi Zhang; Ming Xiao; Xiaokai Hao; Kunzhe Wang; Liguang Wang

ABSTRACT Designing high‐performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade‐offs\. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial‐and‐error approaches\. Recent advances in machine learning \(ML\) are transforming electrolyte research into a data‐driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery\. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design\. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry\. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi‐objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development\. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism‐informed and transferable ML frameworks\. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next‐generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high‐performance rechargeable batteries\.

## [Influence of PVA Concentration on the Properties of Lontar Palm Leaf‐Sugarcane Bagasse Hybrid Biocomposite Films](../publications/0ec36a8850d2d114be71.md)

Emmidia Djonaedi; Mochamad Chalid; Dedi Priadi; Nurul Asni; Heribertus Rudi K; Deli Silvia; Duwi Putri; Hammam Alfarizi; Ramdhani Harjo

ABSTRACT Natural fiber‐reinforced bioplastics represent a viable strategy for valorizing agricultural waste; however, the combined reinforcement of lontar palm \( Borassus flabellifer \) leaf and sugarcane bagasse fibers in a polyvinyl alcohol \(PVA\) matrix remains underexplored\. This study investigates the effects of varying PVA concentrations \(15, 30, and 45 wt%\) on the physical, mechanical, thermal, and interfacial properties of hybrid biocomposite films\. Extracted cellulose fibers served as structural reinforcement\. Tensile strength increased with higher PVA loading, peaking at 1\.79 MPa at 45 wt% PVA, while elongation reached an optimal 43\.36% at 30 wt\.% PVA\. Physical characterization revealed a maximum swelling of 70\.3% at 45 wt\.% PVA, whereas water solubility decreased from 63\.54% at 15 wt\.% PVA to a minimum of 55\.30% at 45 wt\.% PVA\. The 45 wt\.% formulation also exhibited superior structural and thermal stability, showing the lowest soil‐burial degradation \(36\.80%\) and minimal heat‐induced weight loss \(8\.99% at 120°C\)\. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed robust interfacial bonding via hydrogen linkages \(3500–3200 cm − 1 \) and prominent C─O/C─O─C vibrations \(1200–1000 cm − 1 \) between the cellulose fillers and polymer chains\. Overall, balancing PVA concentration with hybrid fiber reinforcement is critical to tailoring mechanical strength, water affinity, and degradation resistance in biodegradable films

## [Inter\-rater reliability of needle EMG pattern classification among physicians](../publications/0ec39b26316b2c8cc4ea.md)

Селиверстова Екатерина Геннадьевна; Artem Pyatkov; Mariya Kovalchuk; Evgenia Druzhinina; Mikhail Sinkin

Objective To evaluate the inter\-rater reliability of needle electromyographic \(EMG\) assessment among 19 physicians with varying clinical experience and specialties using a consensus standard as reference\. Methods The study followed the GRRAS guidelines\. First, four EMG experts agreed on classifying thirty EMG recordings as normal, myogenic, or neurogenic and referred to as a consensus standard \(CS\)\. Second, those anonymised recordings were independently classified by 19 non\-expert physicians\. Thereafter, Cohen’s kappa \(κ\) was calculated for each physician against the CS\. Fleiss’ κ was used for multi\-rater agreement\. Category\-specific \(one\-vs\-rest\) κ, sensitivity and specificity were computed\. Subgroup analyses by experience and specialty were performed\. Post\-hoc power analysis was used for the specialty comparison\. Results The mean κ versus the consensus standard across all physicians was 0\.688 \(median 0\.747, SD 0\.172; range 0\.287–0\.900\)\. Overall multi\-rater agreement \(Fleiss’ κ\) was 0\.581\. Category\-specific κ values were: neurogenic 0\.723, normal 0\.368, myogenic 0\.334\. Sensitivity/specificity: neurogenic 94\.6%/87\.1%, myogenic 69\.7%/96\.1%, normal 78\.2%/88\.9%\. Agreement with the CS increased with experience: mean κ rose from 0\.365 \(group 1, ≤1 year\) to 0\.798 \(group 4, &gt;10 years\)\. No significant difference was found between neurologists and clinical physiologists \(Mann–Whitney U, p = 0\.174\); post\-hoc power was low \(≈45%\), thus non\-significance should not be interpreted as equivalence\. EMG experts showed almost perfect agreement \( κ = 0\.85–0\.95\)\. Conclusion In this exploratory study, physicians demonstrated moderate to substantial agreement with a CS standard in EMG classification\. Neurogenic changes are identified most reliably, whereas differentiation between normal and myogenic changes remains challenging\. Greater experience was associated with better agreement in our sample, but this finding requires confirmation in larger studies\. No statistically significant difference was found between neurologists and clinical physiologists, although the analysis was underpowered\. Individual competency varied widely within specialties, suggesting that objective, competency\-based qualification may be more relevant than specialty alone\.

## [Fostering Academic Reading Proficiency through Independent Learning in a Higher Education Context](../publications/0ec3ff2b331f19d7dd1b.md)

Rizka Patrika Rizal; Lego Prayogo; Imam Khasbani

Academic reading proficiency is essential for academic and professional development in higher education, as it enables individuals to access, comprehend, and critically engage with scholarly resources\. However, empirical evidence on the effectiveness of structured independent learning programs for improving academic reading proficiency among higher education learners remains limited, particularly in the Indonesian context\. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an independent learning program in fostering academic reading proficiency among participants in a higher education context\. This study involved 26 participants from a university in Jakarta\. A quantitative pre\-experimental design employing a pre\-test and post\-test approach was used to assess participants’ reading performance before and after the intervention\. The program provided flexible and self\-paced learning opportunities through guided academic reading materials and structured learning activities\. Data were collected from reading assessment scores and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics using descriptive statistics and a paired\-samples t\-test to determine the extent of improvement\. The findings revealed a positive increase in participants’ academic reading proficiency following their participation in the independent learning program, indicating enhanced comprehension of academic texts and improved reading performance\. The paired\-samples t\-test indicated that the improvement was statistically significant, t\(\[df\] = \[t\-value\], p &lt; \.05 and Cohen’s d = X\. These results suggest that independent learning can be an effective strategy for developing academic reading skills among adult learners in higher education settings\. The study underscores the importance of self\-directed learning in supporting continuous professional development and academic literacy while offering a flexible and sustainable approach to English language improvement\.

## [Uncertainty\-Aware Digital Twin Framework for Resilient Low\-Carbon Port Infrastructure under Electrification and Sensor Degradation](../publications/0ec70a1feb0f49ff285e.md)

Seyed Reza Samaei; K\.S\. Reddy; James Riffat

The electrification of port operations is reshaping the technical relationship between logistics performance, energy demand, infrastructure condition and data reliability\. Although digital twins are increasingly used for port monitoring and decision support, many frameworks continue to assume clean sensing, synchronised data streams and stable observability\. This study develops an uncertainty\-aware digital twin framework for resilient low\-carbon port infrastructure under electrification and sensor degradation\. A synthetic reference container terminal with 4\.5 million TEU/year throughput, six berths, twenty\-two quay cranes, 58,000 TEU yard capacity, 120 monitoring channels, 55 MW grid\-import capacity, 28 MW renewable capacity and 60 MWh battery storage is simulated for one year at a 5 min update interval\. Fifty paired stochastic replications are analysed after a 14\-day warm\-up period\. Under compound stress comprising 35% sensor loss, 5% measurement noise, 10 min synchronisation delay, 90% electrification, 25% higher latent vessel\-arrival demand intensity before application of the approach\-channel cap, 25% lower renewable availability and 12% lower equipment productivity, the framework yields 10\.5 h mean completed\-vessel waiting delay, 5\.7% energy shortfall, 0\.27 infrastructure\-health risk, 0\.31 uncertainty index, 14\.6 h recovery time and a resilience index of 0\.64\. Relative to a conventional digital twin, completed\-vessel waiting delay decreases by 18\.0%, energy shortfall by 32\.1%, uncertainty index by 29\.5% and recovery time by 26\.3%\. Paired replication\-level tests remain significant after Holm adjustment, with large paired effect sizes for the principal operational, energy, uncertainty and resilience outcomes\. The results show that resilient electrified\-port operation depends not only on installed electrical capacity, but also on temporal alignment, probabilistic state estimation, energy flexibility, health\-aware operation and explicit representation of degraded information quality\.

## [“All the World is a \(Debate\) Stage”: College Debates as a Form of Civic Engagement](../publications/0ecc20fa6a293361c96f.md)

Sara Sepanski Whipple; Valentina Dimitrova\-Grajzl; Kim Connolly

Political division and self\-censorship in the United States have risen considerably in recent years\. One means of countering such divides and siloed dialogue is through civil discourse that exposes people to diverse viewpoints\. In an effort to bridge partisan divides, the Braver Angels Organization developed a debate format centered on these principles\. Virginia Military Institute is one college campus that has adopted such debates as a form of civic engagement\. In this paper we describe the development of the VMI College Debates and Discourse Program which has become a leading community of practice in civil discourse and engagement across college campuses, elaborating on the program’s initiatives, approach, and objectives\. The paper also provides an overview of the Braver Angels debate structure and how such debates promote open dialogue\. The paper concludes with qualitative and quantitative evidence for the program’s effectiveness as well as advice for those interested in pursuing similar programs at their home institutions\.

## [NEUROBIOLOGIA DA DEPENDÊNCIA QUÍMICA: mecanismos cerebrais, consequências e perspectivas de tratamento](../publications/0ecf59b6c8ac3f71e0f3.md)

Dagma Aparecida Ribeiro Rocha; Hugo Christiano Soares Melo

Este trabalho teve como objetivo analisar os principais avanços da neurociência na compreensão da dependência química, com ênfase nos mecanismos cerebrais envolvidos, nas alterações comportamentais decorrentes e nas implicações para o desenvolvimento de abordagens terapêuticas mais eficazes\. A relevância do tema pode ser observada pela magnitude do consumo de drogas no cenário mundial: segundo o World Drug Report 2024, aproximadamente 292 milhões de pessoas entre 15 e 64 anos utilizaram drogas em 2022, enquanto cerca de 64 milhões apresentavam transtornos relacionados ao uso de drogas\. Trata\-se de uma pesquisa de natureza qualitativa, desenvolvida por meio de revisão narrativa da literatura, com base em publicações científicas de 2016 a 2026, obtidas em bases como Google Acadêmico, SciElo e PubMed\. Os estudos analisados indicam que o uso de substâncias psicoativas promove intensa ativação do sistema de recompensa, envolvendo alterações na neurotransmissão dopaminérgica e na atribuição de saliência aos estímulos relacionados à droga\. Evidenciou\-se também que processos de neuroplasticidade produzem modificações duradouras nos circuitos neurais envolvidos na recompensa, no controle executivo e na regulação emocional, favorecendo comportamentos compulsivos e dificultando o controle inibitório\. As consequências incluem abstinência, craving, vulnerabilidade à recaída e manutenção de alterações neurobiológicas mesmo após períodos de abstinência\. Os achados reforçam a necessidade de estratégias terapêuticas integradas, baseadas em evidências, que considerem os mecanismos neurobiológicos associados à dependência e articulem intervenções psicológicas, farmacológicas e psicossociais\.

## [A Conceptual Framework for Scaling Technical Leadership and Mentorship in Remote Software Engineering Teams](../publications/0ed693eeee0c80841308.md)

Oluwasanmi Segun Adanigbo

The rise of remote work has revolutionized software engineering, presenting both unique challenges and significant opportunities for technical leadership and mentorship\. As organizations increasingly adopt remote work models, it is crucial to scale leadership and mentorship practices to ensure the continued development of teams\. This paper presents a conceptual framework for scaling technical leadership and mentorship within remote software engineering teams\. The framework addresses key challenges such as communication barriers, maintaining consistent quality, and preventing burnout, while proposing strategies like clear communication channels, structured mentorship programs, and the effective use of collaborative tools\. It emphasizes the integration of leadership development, mentorship structures, and technology to support both the technical and interpersonal growth of team members\. ## [EMERGING HEPATOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES FOR LIVER DISEASE: CURRENT PROGRESS AND FUTURE DIRECTION](../publications/0eebcfe3d5640cf1b85d.md)

2Anvesh Sharma and 3Shubhanshu Soni 1\*Kashish Rajput

Due to their complex and multifaceted character, liver diseases represent a huge global health burden and contribute considerably to morbidity and mortality globally\. Although the liver is essential for detoxification, protein synthesis, metabolic equilibrium, and biochemical regulation, it is extremely vulnerable to damage due to ongoing exposure to chemicals, medications, and infections\. Hepatocellular carcinoma, alcoholic liver disease, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\), and cirrhosis are among the liver diseases that frequently proceed asymptomatically and are identified at advanced stages, which limits the effectiveness of treatment\. Interconnected processes including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, apoptosis, fibrosis, and immunological dysregulation are involved in the pathogenesis of liver injury\. The main goals of conventional therapy approaches, such as liver transplantation, medication, and lifestyle changes, are to control symptoms and halt the course of the disease\. However, they are not very effective at correcting extensive liver damage and may have negative side effects\. Emerging hepatoprotective treatments that target several molecular pathways have been made possible by recent developments\. Targeted pharmacological medicines \(such as PPAR, FXR, and thyroid hormone receptor\-β agonists\), natural bioactive substances, drug delivery methods based on nanotechnology, gene and RNA\-based therapies, stem cell\-based regenerative techniques, immunotherapy, and gut microbiome modification are some of these\. When assessing these treatments, experimental models such as those caused by CCl₄, paracetamol, alcohol, and diet\-induced liver impairment are crucial\. Furthermore, despite ongoing obstacles like a lack of trustworthy biomarkers, translational gaps, high prices, and regulatory restrictions, clinical trials and translational research are crucial for confirming their safety and efficacy\. In order to improve therapeutic outcomes, future hepatoprotective techniques will prioritize multi\-targeted approaches, personalized medicine, and the integration of omics technology and artificial intelligence\. Despite tremendous advancements, more study and interdisciplinary cooperation are needed to get past current obstacles and provide medicines that are accessible, safe, and effective\. All things considered, new hepatoprotective treatments have great potential to improve liver regeneration, restore hepatic function, and lower the prevalence of liver illnesses worldwide\.

## [Development and Evaluation of Vision\-Language Models for Ergonomic Physical Exposure Assessment in Occupational Manual Material Handling](../publications/0ef369a6d69d3379b2d1.md)

Mohammad Sadra Rajabi

Work\-related musculoskeletal disorders remain a leading cause of lost workdays and substantial costs for workers and employers, and manual material handling \(MMH\) tasks are a major contributor to the physical exposures that drive this risk\. Existing physical exposure assessment methods, including self\-reports, systematic observation, and direct measurement, are often labor\-intensive, costly, or impractical for use in real work environments\. Vision\-language models \(VLMs\), which combine visual encoders with large language models to jointly process video and text, offer a potentially non\-invasive and scalable alternative for quantifying physical exposures from regular RGB video\. This dissertation developed and evaluated VLM\-based methods for physical exposure assessment during MMH tasks using three sequential studies\. The first study evaluated the use of VLMs to classify eight MMH tasks and specific task conditions \(hand configuration and lift origin\), and to temporally segment task start and end times\. The work achieved task classification accuracies of \~82–85%, lift\-origin classification accuracies of \~94–98%, and errors in mean absolute start and end time of &lt;0\.5 seconds\. The second study assessed the feasibility of using two VLM\-based pipelines to estimate horizontal \(H\) and vertical \(V\) hand distances required by the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation \(RNLE\)\. Using a segmentation\-based, multi\-view pipeline consistently yielding the smallest errors \(mean absolute errors of \~6–8 cm for H and \~5–8 cm for V\)\. The third study evaluated a VLM\-based pipeline for estimating dynamic, triaxial, bilateral external hand forces during MMH tasks\. Root mean square errors of \~4\.7–5\.6 N were obtained for the horizontal and mediolateral force components and \~10\.6–11\.0 N for the vertical component\. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of VLM\-based methods as objective, scalable, and minimally intrusive tools for quantifying physical exposures during MMH tasks, supporting their continued development toward practical, video\-based occupational physical exposure assessment\.

## [Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association](../publications/0ef408fd609dad2f6516.md)

Mulubrhan F\. Mogos; Susan E\. Maynard; Stacy M Perrin; Mai N\. Nguyen‐Huynh; Mona N\. Bahouth; Catherine Torrington Eaton; Iris Z\. Feinberg; Joyce Sampson; Jared W\. Magnani; Kiffon Marie Keigher

Health literacy is a critical component of high\-quality stroke care\. Across the continuum from prevention through recovery, health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke\-related morbidity\. Despite its importance, it is often overlooked, leaving patients and caregivers overwhelmed by communication demands that exceed their capacity\. These mismatches are especially pronounced among individuals with stroke\-related cognitive or language impairments, limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, or limited digital literacy\. This scientific statement synthesizes current evidence on the role of health literacy and communication within stroke systems of care and identifies nurse\-led opportunities to advance equity and patient\-centered outcomes while recognizing this as a shared interprofessional responsibility\. Nurse\-led interventions, including teach\-back\-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, have demonstrated improvements in stroke knowledge, self\-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness\. However, the literature is marked by methodological heterogeneity\. Many studies are underpowered and infrequently use validated health literacy or communication measures\. Future directions include standardized assessment of health literacy; literacy\-sensitive, nurse\-led, and interprofessional care models; workforce training in plain\-language and culturally responsive communication; and organizational health literacy principles\. Emerging technologies, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, offer promise for improving communication and personalization but require rigorous evaluation to minimize bias and ensure equity and usability\.

## [Fluorescence Encoding\-Enabled Multiplexed Droplet Digital Recombinase Polymerase Amplification\-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Rapid Screening of Lower Respiratory Tract Infection\-Associated Bacterial Pathogens](../publications/0f29043f64118c8a4f09.md)

Yifan Wang; Enqi Huang; Ziyi Zhang; Xicong Zhu; Ting Zhang; Na Yang; Zhenhua Chen; Dongyang Cai; Dayu Liu

Abstract Digital RPA\-CRISPR/Cas12a assays enable accurate nucleic acid quantification; however, their multiplexing capacity is inherently limited by signal confounding arising from the promiscuous trans\-cleavage activity of Cas12a effectors\. To overcome this limitation, we developed a fluorescence encoding\-enabled multiplexed droplet digital RPA\-CRISPR/Cas12a \(FLEMD\-CRISPR\) assay that integrates combinatorial fluorescence encoding, deterministic droplet pairing within a calabash\-shaped microwell array, and a machine learning\-assisted decoding pipeline\. In FLEMD\-CRISPR, small\-volume fluorescence\-encoded CRISPR/Cas12a droplets, each assigned a unique spectral signature corresponding to a specific crRNA, are one\-to\-one paired with large\-volume RPA droplets\. Following RPA amplification and droplet merging, Cas12a\-mediated reporter cleavage occurs only in droplets containing target amplicons\. The decoding pipeline then localizes droplets, classifies their colors to assign crRNA identities, and finally detects positive signals, enabling high\-throughput, hands\-off analysis of the entire droplet array\. FLEMD\-CRISPR enabled simultaneous quantification of nucleic acid targets from eight major lower respiratory tract infection\-associated bacterial pathogens, showing strong linear correlation \(R2 = 0\.9987–0\.9998\) and consistent detection efficiency \(slopes = 0\.9849–1\.0198\) relative to single\-plex digital PCR\. The complete workflow, from sample preparation to final readout, can be completed within 2 h\. Clinical validation using 30 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples showed that the bacterial detection outcomes of FLEMD\-CRISPR were highly concordant with standard\-of\-care culture, achieving 100% \(20/20\) positive percent agreement and 99\.1% \(218/220\) negative percent agreement\. By enabling panel reconfiguration through simple modifications of the droplet encoding library, FLEMD\-CRISPR provides a flexible platform for the development of highly multiplexed digital CRISPR assays\.

## [GenAI\-Powered Smart Traffic Assistant: A Multimodal AI Framework for Real\-Time Traffic Prediction, Route Recommendation, and Explainable Urban Mobility](../publications/0f2ab313a06e64e92bdb.md)

Naganaboyina Vinod Kumar; Ch\. Hema Vardhan; Gattu Mohan Goud; M\. Mohan Krishna Reddy; U\. Devendra

Urban traffic management increasingly requires systems that can reason over heterogeneous, time\-varying information rather than rely only on static maps or historical averages\. This paper presents the GenAI\-Powered Smart Traffic Assistant, a prototype intelligent transportation platform that combines real\-time location, traffic and weather inputs, historical traffic data, machine\-learning\-based congestion prediction, computer\-vision vehicle detection, route recommendation, alerts, explainable AI \(XAI\), and role\-aware dashboards in a unified workflow\. The system is derived from a semester project report and its associated prototype deployment\. The design follows a layered client\-server architecture with a web/mobile oriented interface, application services, machine\-learning components, and persistent traffic data\. A structured development methodology is used to integrate data collection, preprocessing, prediction, recommendation, visualization, security, and maintenance\. Rather than claiming benchmark accuracy that is not reported in the source project, the paper evaluates the prototype through functional coverage, architecture consistency, safety constraints, and explicit non\-functional targets\. The resulting framework provides a practical foundation for multimodal traffic assistance and a pathway toward live CCTV integration, IoT sensing, adaptive signal control, continuous model learning, and smart\-city interoperability\.

## [A Preliminary Study of Mobile\-Based CBT for Anger Management in Individuals With ASD Without Intellectual Disability](../publications/0f2fc37d92a98ed7c565.md)

So Yeong Choi; Kyong‐Mee Chung

This study examined the preliminary efficacy of HARU ASD, a mobile\-based cognitive behavioral therapy program \(mCBT\), for anger management in adolescents and young adults with autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability\. Thirty participants \(intervention group n = 16, waitlist control group n = 14\) and twenty\-five caregivers \(intervention group n = 14, waitlist control group n = 11\) were included in the final analysis\. Self\-report, caregiver\-proxy questionnaires \(9 subscales each\), and direct behavioral observations \(5 domains\) were administered before and after the intervention\. After Holm–Bonferroni correction, only the caregiver\-proxy reported direct anger\-out remained significant, suggesting reduced direct verbal and behavioral anger expression in the intervention group\. These findings suggest the limited effectiveness of the HARU ASD for managing anger among individuals with ASD without ID, although larger trials with prespecified primary outcomes are needed\. ## [Herb\-Drug Interaction Safety: Clinical Implications, Molecular Mechanisms, and the Future of Integrated Medicine](../publications/0f3fd8f8c5e2f762ec8e.md)



Background: The concurrent use of herbal medicines and conventional pharmaceuticals has become a global health phenomenon, driven by a cultural shift toward holistic wellness and the pervasive misconception that &quot;natural&quot; products are inherently devoid of risk\.This integration creates a complex pharmacological landscape where bioactive phytochemicals can significantly alter the therapeutic efficacy and safety profiles of prescription drugs\.Objectives: This review aims to delineate the mechanistic underpinnings of Herb\-Drug Interactions \(HDIs\), evaluate the clinical implications for high\-risk patient populations, and assess current methodological advancements in risk prediction and surveillance\.Methods: A multi\-tiered framework is explored, encompassing pharmacokinetic \(ADME\) modulationspecifically involving Cytochrome P450 \(CYP\) enzymes and P\-glycoprotein \(P\-gp\) transporters\-and pharmacodynamic pathways of synergy and antagonism\.The role of in silico modeling, Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), and &quot;herbovigilance&quot; systems is evaluated as a modern strategy for mitigating iatrogenic harm\.Results: Evidence suggests that HDIs pose the greatest threat to patients on Narrow Therapeutic Index \(NTI\) medications, such as anticoagulants and immunosuppressants\.Pharmacokinetic induction, exemplified by St\. John&\#x27;s Wort \(Hypericum perforatum\), can lead to sub\-therapeutic plasma levels and therapeutic failure, while irreversible inhibition, such as the furanocoumarin effect in grapefruit, may precipitate systemic toxicity\.Furthermore, host\-specific factors like age\-related physiological decline and the extreme phytochemical variability of non\-standardized herbal products exacerbate these risks\.Conclusion: HDIs represent a paramount safety challenge in contemporary integrated medicine\.To ensure patient safety, a paradigm shift is required that reclassifies herbal products as active pharmacological agents\.This necessitates rigorous standardized labeling, mandatory clinical screening protocols, and the deployment of AIdriven predictive tools to bridge the existing &quot;communication chasm&quot; between patients and healthcare providers\.

## [Transformer\-based Digital Biomarker Identification for Early Neurological Assessment](../publications/0f49b6717e44ac9a01ca.md)

Zahraa Naser Shahweli; Areej Hameed Al\-Anbary; Ahmed Saeed Obied

The objective assessment and differential diagnosis of movement disorders, particularly Parkinson&\#x27;s disease \(PD\) and Essential Tremor \(ET\), remain challenging due to the subjectivity and limited temporal coverage of conventional in\-clinic clinical assessments\.Although consumer\-grade smartphones equipped with inertial sensors provide a practical platform for continuous movement monitoring, existing deep\-learning approaches remain constrained by their dependence on large, expertly annotated clinical datasets and their limited ability to learn generalized temporal representations\.To address these challenges, this study proposes a self\-supervised, patch\-based Transformer framework that identifies clinically consistent candidate digital features from smartphone inertial timeseries data\.The proposed framework employs a two\-stage training strategy in which the Transformer encoder is first pre\-trained using masked autoencoding on millions of unlabeled inertial sensor samples from the crowdsourced mPower dataset to learn robust latent representations of human movement\.The pre\-trained encoder is subsequently fine\-tuned using a subject\-wise protocol on the Mobile Device Tremor Dataset for multi\-class tremor classification\.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a multi\-class classification accuracy of 95\.85% and a macro F1\-score of 95\.52%, consistently outperforming fully supervised 1D Temporal Convolutional \(1D\-TCN\) and BiLSTM\-Attention baselines\.Instead of relying on handcrafted features, the proposed framework identified discriminative movement patterns that aligned with established neurophysiological tremor frequency ranges \(4\-6 Hz and 8\-12 Hz\) in an automated, end\-to\-end manner, bridging self\-supervised deep representations with physical diagnostic criteria\.These findings demonstrate the potential of self\-supervised Transformer models to enable scalable, objective, and clinically interpretable decision support for early neurological assessment in mobile sensor environments\.

## [The role of tumor biopsy in children with obstructive hydrocephalus treated with endoscopic third ventriculostomy: a single\-center experience](../publications/0f4a124b2f31c34ddabd.md)

Ryszard Sordyl; Natalia Wyroba; Justyna Karliczek; Wiktoria Pniok; Marek Mandera

PURPOSE: We aimed to present and analyze our institutional experience with endoscopic third ventriculostomy \(ETV\), performed alone or in combination with simultaneous tumor biopsy, for the management of obstructive hydrocephalus in pediatric patients\. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted of the medical records of pediatric patients with tumor\-related obstructive hydrocephalus who underwent ETV between 2013 and 2024\. RESULTS: Thirty\-five children underwent ETV at a mean age of 9\.2 years\. Hydrocephalus was most commonly associated with lesions located in the tectal plate \(65\.7%\)\. In 12 cases \(34\.3%\), ETV was combined with an endoscopic tumor biopsy\. Over a median follow\-up of 3\.3 years, the overall ETV effectiveness was 82\.9% \(n = 29\)\. Postoperative complications occurred in 7 patients \(20\.0%\), with the most frequent being transient cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) leakage from the surgical wound \(n = 3; 42\.9%\)\. Histological results of endoscopic tumor biopsy were successfully obtained from 10 of 12 \(83\.3%\) samples\. No statistically significant differences in rates of reoperation, shunt implantation, or tumor resection were observed between patients with ETV alone and those with ETV with biopsy\. CONCLUSIONS: ETV is an effective treatment for tumor\-related obstructive hydrocephalus in children that may be safely combined with endoscopic tumor biopsy in selected cases, enabling early histopathological diagnosis and timely initiation of oncological treatment while potentially reducing the need for subsequent open surgical procedures\.

## [Patterns of travel preferences in China and their relationship with the Big Five personality traits](../publications/0f4d3384dbc0c48696cd.md)

Wendi Ji; Mao Mao; Vesselin Popov; Shiling Chen; Luning Sun

Identification of patterns of travel preferences enables personalised services in the hospitality and tourism sectors\. Previous research has indicated links between patterns of travel preferences and personality traits but has mostly focused on isolated segments of a traveller’s journey, such as hotel or destination selection\. The current study, based on the Big Five personality traits, extends this line of research using a large\-scale empirical dataset \(N = 979\) in China that spans multiple aspects of travel behaviour\. K\-means clustering identifies four distinct groups, Experience Seekers, Convenience &amp; Low\-Cost Seekers, Quality &amp; Status Seekers, and Easy\-Goers, which differ in their patterns of preferences as well as their demographic and personality profiles\. Logistic regression and random forest analyses reveal Extraversion and Openness to Experience as the most significant predictors of travel preferences\. The results provide insights for the hospitality and tourism industry and suggest that incorporating personality traits can support more effective customer understanding and service design\.

## [Leading Together through Co\-digitizing: The Creative Practices of Young People and their Teachers](../publications/0f51085601c52a9b1aa5.md)

Juan Carlos Castro; Kit Grauer; Joanna Black; Michael Emme; Moniques Richard; Ching\-Chiu Lin

Recently, educational policymakers have responded to young people&\#x27;s digital media practices through increasingly restrictive bans and controls\. Drawing on over forty years of collective research, we argue that art educators are positioned to lead through this moment of moral panic by co\-digitizing, that is, participating with young people and their digital practices\. We share how art educators have cultivated learning networks where knowledge is assembled through relations among people, tools, and contexts\. As a result, we call for pedagogical leadership that reconnects schooling with young people&\#x27;s digital lives\.

## [Infrastructural tinkering and the everyday governance of water in Pumwani, Nairobi](../publications/0f5d8fcc0e90ec6721d7.md)

Martin Grau

In Southern cities, residents carry out continuous acts of tinkering through which they negotiate access to water despite the characteristic unreliability of the formal system\. While Urban Political Ecology \(UPE\) and Science and Technology Studies \(STS\) have shown how governance emerges through situated socio\-material practices, they have paid less attention to the recurring dynamics through which these practices reproduce or reorganise urban order\. Drawing on Varela and colleagues enactive account of coupling and co\-dependent arising, this paper conceptualises infrastructural tinkering as an iterative mode of governance through which embodied dispositions are continually reproduced or reorganised in response to failure\. The argument is developed through qualitative interviews conducted at nine water points in the neighbourhood of Pumwani, in Nairobi\. The analysis identifies six patterns that reveal distinct modes of orienting action in recursive socio\-material engagements\. While most patterns reproduce conditions of urban capture by reinforcing historically inherited relations, autonomous forms of tinkering demonstrate how recurrent engagement may also reorganise governance through situated negotiation\. The paper argues that tradition and transformation are not opposing pairs but emerge from the same dynamics that produce constraints\. In doing so, it contributes towards a relational account of governance that explains how urban order is continually reproduced andreorganised through everyday infrastructural practice\.

## [Embodied Performance Adaptation in Precision Sport – A Multimodal Study of Cognitive, Autonomic, and Motor Integration in Refining Dexterity](../publications/0f6c4370804e83fdd225.md)

Rajan Sathish; Gintare Dauksaite

Background: Self\-regulation under performance pressure is critical in precision sports such as shooting and archery\. Prior research has examined cognitive, physiological, and motor processes independently, leaving limited evidence on their integrated adaptation within an embodied performance framework\. Methods: Eight trained precision sport athletes \(seven men, one woman; age 31\.2 ± 15\.0 years\) completed a longitudinal within\-subject repeated\-measures design with assessments at baseline, after Training Block 1 \(mid\-assessment\), and after Training Block 2 \(final assessment\)\. Cognitive efficiency was assessed with the Automated Neuropsychological Assessment Metrics, fine motor control with the Analyser of Dynamic Parameters of Human Hand and Leg Movements, and autonomic regulation with heart rate variability \(HRV\)\. A controlled auditory pressure constraint \(countdown beep\) was introduced during the final assessment\. Results: From baseline to final assessment, reaction time decreased by 8\.40% \(W = 36, p = \.008, rrb = 1\.00\), motor variability decreased by 25\.19% \(W = 33, p = \.039, rrb = 0\.833\), throughput increased by 24\.32% \(W = 0\.0, p = \.008, rrb = −1\.00\), maximum movement speed increased by 34\.26% \(W = 0\.0, p = \.008, rrb = −1\.00\), and spatial accuracy error decreased by 11\.79% \(W = 36, p = \.008, rrb = 1\.00\)\. Under the auditory pressure condition, spatial accuracy improved further relative to post\-training baseline \(W = 33, p = \.039, rrb = 0\.833\) without significant HRV deterioration\. Spearman’s correlations linked reaction time with temporal inconsistency \(rs = \.777\), spatial accuracy with throughput \(rs = −\.802\), temporal inconsistency with HRV \(rs = −\.709\), and motor variability with shooting performance \(rs = −\.714\) \(W, Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank Test statistic; rrb, rank\-biserial correlation effect size; rs, Spearman’s rank\-order correlation coefficient\)\. Conclusion: Multimodal training was associated with coordinated cognitive, motor, and autonomic adaptation in precision sport athletes, consistent with performance stability under externally imposed pressure and an embodied, system\-level account of precision sport performance\. Keywords: Dexterity, cognition, archery, shooting, expert performance

## [Research attitudes through the COVID\-19 pandemic](../publications/0f8bcee6f0e0b9b76e60.md)

Sarah K\. Schlund; Dan K\. Hoang; Amy Kind; Joshua D\. Grill; Daniel L\. Gillen

Introduction Identifying the factors that influence attitudes toward biomedical research is essential for improving public engagement and participation\. The COVID\-19 pandemic offers a unique opportunity to assess how a public health crisis shapes perceptions of clinical research\. We investigated whether attitudes toward biomedical research differed across phases of the COVID\-19 pandemic\. Methods We analyzed data from 5,098 adults enrolled in the UC Irvine Consent\-to\-Contact \(C2C\) registry, an online voluntary recruitment registry in Southern California, between June 2016 and August 2025\. Research attitudes were assessed with the validated 7\-item Research Attitudes Questionnaire \(RAQ\) at enrollment and annually thereafter\. Scores were analyzed continuously \(7 \-35\) and dichotomously, with &gt;28 defined a priori as high\. COVID\-19 periods were defined a priori as: P1 \(before March 13, 2020—the U\.S\. national emergency declaration\), P2 \(March 13 to December 11, 2020—prior to COVID\-19 vaccine approval\), and P3 \(after December 11, 2020—post\-vaccine approval\)\. Cross\-sectional analyses included all participants; longitudinal analyses were limited to 1,388 participants who enrolled before March 2020 and had ≥3 assessments\. Results Our sample of 5,098 adults was predominantly non\-Hispanic White \(70\.2%\), female \(65\.7%\), highly educated, and over age 50 \(66\.7%\)\. Participants enrolling during P2 had 60% higher odds of a high RAQ score \(&gt;28\) compared with P1 \(aOR 1\.60; 95% CI: 1\.07, 2\.40; p =0\.022\)\. Longitudinally, the mean within\-subject RAQ score was significantly higher during P2 versus P1 \(Est\. 0\.37; 95% CI: 0\.08, 0\.66; p =0\.011\), and the odds of a high RAQ score were 24% higher in P2 \(aOR 1\.24; 95% CI: 1\.09, 1\.39; p &lt;0\.001\) compared to P1\. Discussion These findings suggest that awareness of urgent medical issues, such as the COVID\-19 pandemic, may affect attitudes toward research\.

## [Anxiety\-Driven Hemodynamics in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: A Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/0f906dd61478d23b654a.md)

Latha Sambatra; Veeresh Kademani; Sheryl Fernandes

Objectives Coronary angiography \(CAG\) is an essential diagnostic procedure for coronary artery disease \(CAD\); however, patients frequently experience pre\-procedural anxiety, which may affect physiological stability\. Therefore, this study aimed to assess pre\-procedural anxiety and its impact on hemodynamic parameters among patients undergoing CAG\. Material and Methods A descriptive study was conducted from October 2024 to July 2025 among 58 patients undergoing CAG at a tertiary care hospital in Mangalore, India\. Participants were selected using convenience sampling\. Data were collected using a demographic proforma, the State\-Trait Anxiety Inventory \(STAI\), a sphygmomanometer, and a pulse oximeter\. Eligible participants were aged 30–65 years, while those with prior angiography, anxiolytic use, cognitive or psychiatric disorders, hypertensive conditions, or critical illness were excluded\. Data were analysed using SPSS v20\. Results Among 58 participants, 65\.5% were males, with a mean age of 58\.39 ± 8\.10 years\. The STAI results showed that 68\.97% of the patients experienced moderate anxiety and 31\.03% had mild anxiety, with no cases of severe anxiety\. Hemodynamic findings demonstrated elevated mean systolic \(142\.93 ± 14\.26 mmHg\) and diastolic blood pressure \(87\.93 ± 9\.78 mmHg\) values among the participants\. The mean heart rate was 89\.32 ± 11\.49 beats per minute, reflecting a moderately elevated heart rate\. Oxygen saturation remained within the normal range \(96\.53 ± 3\.17%\)\. Conclusion Patients undergoing CAG experienced mild to moderate anxiety accompanied by elevated blood pressure and a modest increased heart rate, highlighting the importance of assessing and managing anxiety to maintain physiological stability and improve procedural outcomes\.

## [Persepsi Mahasiswa Terhadap Penggunaaan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pembelajaran](../publications/0f97ea9dae66d8a0200d.md)

Nazwa Pahira Dongoran

Perkembangan teknologi Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) telah memberikan berbagai kemudahan dalam proses pembelajaran, khususnya bagi mahasiswa dalam mencari informasi, memahami materi, dan menyelesaikan tugas akademik\. Penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran dapat memberikan manfaat, tetapi juga menimbulkan berbagai persepsi yang perlu dikaji lebih lanjut\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui persepsi mahasiswa terhadap penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran serta mengidentifikasi faktor\-faktor yang mendasari persepsi tersebut\. Penelitian dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner yang terdiri atas 20 pernyataan kepada 76 responden\. Data yang diperoleh dianalisis menggunakan Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\), dengan tahapan pengujian kelayakan data melalui Kaiser\-Meyer Olkin \(KMO\) dan uji Bartlett, ekstraksi faktor, serta rotasi Varimax untuk memperoleh struktur faktor yang lebih mudah diinterpretasikan\. Hasil pengujian awal menunjukkan nilai KMO sebesar 0,906 dan uji Bartlett yang signifikan dengan nilai p &lt; 0,001, sehingga data memenuhi indikasi awal untuk dilakukan analisis faktor\. Berdasarkan kriteria nilai eigen lebih dari satu, diperoleh tiga faktor awal yang selanjutnya dianalisis untuk mengetahui pengelompokan pernyataan berdasarkan korelasi antarvariabel\. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat memberikan gambaran mengenai dimensi\-dimensi persepsi mahasiswa terhadap penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran serta menjadi bahan pertimbangan dalam pemanfaatan AI secara efektif dan bertanggung jawab di lingkungan akademik\.

## [The Impact of a Career\-Connected Convergent Inquiry Project on High School Students’ Knowledge and Information Processing Competency in English Education](../publications/0f98277d4d693bfcb878.md)

Whyun Young Choi

This study explored the impact of a career\-connected convergent inquiry project on high school students’ knowledge and information processing competency in English education\. An explanatory sequential mixed\-methods design was employed with 148 students over 17 weeks, encompassing topic selection through final presentation\. Quantitatively, pre\- and post\-surveys using a validated competency instrument were analyzed using paired\-samples t\-tests and effect size calculations\. Qualitatively, semi\-structured interviews with nine students were thematically analyzed to explore learning experiences\. Quantitative results showed statistically significant improvements across all competency domains and sub\-elements, with relatively large effect sizes in “scope setting” and “production\.” Qualitative findings revealed that students perceived English as a “tool for career exploration” rather than an “assessment object,” developing confidence in authentic contexts\. Career contexts functioned as “critical filters” for prioritizing information\. Students transitioned into knowledge producers through reconstructing information into outputs, while generative AI and digital tools served as “cognitive and affective scaffolding” that reduced linguistic barriers and enabled focus on information processing activities\. This study provides empirical evidence that career\-connected convergent inquiry projects constitute an effective pedagogical model for cultivating knowledge and information processing competency in English education, offering concrete foundations for process\-tracking assessment systems, stage\-specific AI integration, and teacher professional development\.

## [Skill\-Decoupled On\-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision\-Language Models](../publications/0fb4e34f11b72eb11e98.md)

Yuqi Xiong; Chunyi Peng; Zhipeng Xu; Qing Yang; Zhenghao Liu; Zulong Chen; Yu Gu; Ge Yu

Reinforcement learning \(RL\) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision\-language models \(VLMs\), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross\-capability gradient conflicts\. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward\-hacking biases\. This paper proposes Skill\-Decoupled On\-Policy Expert Distillation \(SCOPED\), which trains capability\-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward\-guided reflection\. During on\-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time\. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed\-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill\-decoupled on\-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities\. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task\-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student\. All code and data are available at https://github\.com/NEUIR/SCOPED\.

## [Analysis of Flavonoid Bioactives in Combating HPV Infection: Potential for the Development of Cervical Cancer Therapy](../publications/0fbd0790af1947f9e416.md)

Alwi Rahman Simamora; Adryano Samuel Gurning

Introduction: Human Papilloma Virus \(HPV\) infection is the main cause of cervical cancer and ranks fourth most common cancer in women worldwide\. The high incidence rate and current limitations of treatment are the basis for studying the potential of flavonoid compounds which are natural resources of Indonesia as an alternative anti\-HPV therapy\. Method: The method used is a narrative literature review with literature collection carried out through the PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases\. The selected articles were those published in the last ten years \(2014\-2024\) and are available in abstract and full text\. Results: Flavonoids have significant potential as anti\-HPV agents with mechanisms involving apoptosis induction and inhibition of oncoprotein pathways, such as E6 and c\-Myc, in cervical cancer cells\. Several natural sources such as banana peel with a content of 20\.76 mg qe/g, seeds of the fruit of the boils with a content of 423\.60 mg qe/g, and leaves of the matoa with a content of 15\.884 mg qe/g are proven to be rich in flavonoids and offer opportunities for the development of HPV infection treatment therapy\. Conclusion: Flavonoids have good potential as anti\-HPV in preventing cervical cancer with different mechanisms according to the type of compound\. Flavonoid content can be found in banana peel, seeds of the fruit of the boils, red onion waste, and matoa\.

## [Profiling the MMP family genes as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma: from computational discovery to clinical validation in a South Indian cohort](../publications/0fc3de8c5c7c56a9bd31.md)

P\. Sakthi Subhashini; T\. Bharanidharan; D\. Suresh Kumar; S\. Asha Devi

Background Over the past decade, lifestyle\-related habits and environmental exposures have substantially increased the global incidence of Oral squamous cell carcinoma \(OSCC\)\. This trend underscores the importance of early screening to improve patient treatment outcomes, as delayed diagnosis severely reduces survival chances\. Matrix metalloproteinases \(MMPs\) are a family of zinc\- and calcium\-dependent proteolytic enzymes that degrade the components of extracellular matrix, thereby promoting tumor progression, invasion and metastasis\. Despite their well\-established roles in OSCC, the overall clinical relevance of MMPs remains unclear\. Methods This study systematically investigates the transcriptional expression landscape of all 23 human MMPs to determine their prognostic relevance in OSCC\. Through an integrated analysis of the Gene Expression Omnibus and The Cancer Genome Atlas databases, six overlapping differentially expressed genes of MMP family were identified from the human oral tissue transcriptomic datasets\. Prognostic relevance of these MMPs were examined by receiver operating characteristic curves, survival analyses, and predictive nomograms\. Results Computational analysis revealed that the prediction model achieved optimal accuracy when the six selected MMPs \(MMP\-1, MMP\-10, MMP\-3, MMP\-12, MMP\-13, and MMP\-9\) were combined with Tumor\-Node\-Metastasis staging system\. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis demonstrated that the MMPs were associated with metabolic reprogramming and proliferation\-related signaling pathways, highlighting their contribution towards oral tumor progression\. To validate the in silico transcriptomic findings, we performed an enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay to quantify the serum levels of MMP\-1, MMP\-10, and MMP\-9 in South Indian OSCC patients\. These proteins were significantly elevated in OSCC patients than healthy control samples \( p &lt; 0\.0001, p &lt; 0\.0001 and p = 0\.0002\) respectively\. Conclusion This study reveals that the elevated serum levels of MMP\-1, MMP\- 10 and MMP\-9 can serve as minimally invasive prognostic biomarkers for OSCC in the South Indian cohort\.

## [Overcoming Challenges in Carbon Credit Verification for Solar PV Projects in Nigeria: An ICT\-Driven Approach](../publications/0fd9fbd4cfe529881db4.md)

Prosper Oghenemaro Ugbehe; Olokpa Evworhovwo Favour; Omon Louis Erugba; Idibie Emmanuel Emuesiri; Ogbodogbo Oghenevwogaga Precious; Aruoriwo Godstime Ugbehe; Etaredafe Aghogho Faith

The feasibility of carbon credits for solar photovoltaic \(PV\) projects in Nigeria is faced with major setbacks, including data inaccuracy, high verification costs, limited transparency, and inadequate institutional capacity\. These challenges affect project developers from adequately examining carbon markets and undermine the reliability of emissions reduction claims\. This study analyzes an ICT\-driven method to manage these barriers, emphasizing on the mobilization of digital monitoring, reporting, and verification \(MRV\) systems to suit the Nigerian context\. By incorporating Internet of Things \(IoT\) devices, blockchain technology, and cloud\-based platforms, the suggested solution improves data trustworthiness, decreases transaction fees, and impacts stakeholder trust\. Case studies of already operating solar PV programs in Nigeria are assessed to find the feasibility and effect of such technological solutions\. The study concluded that capitalizing on ICT can tremendously refine carbon credit verification processes, improve scalability of renewable energy \(RE\) projects, and allow wider inclusion in global carbon markets\. Recommendations are suggested for policymakers, builders, and investors to aid the use of ICT tools for sustainable carbon finance in Nigeria’s energy sector\.

## [Enterovirus D68 infection causing plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia: a case report and literature review](../publications/0fdf0416e7719b78c8d1.md)

Chenxi Lin; Tingting Tian; Zhiyan Hao; Ying Huang; Weimin Tian

Background Plastic bronchitis \(PB\) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree\-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life\-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed\. Enterovirus D68 \(EV\-D68\) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure\. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV\-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported\. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV\-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV\-D68\. Methods We report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection\. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026\. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”\. Case description This case involved an 11\-year\-old girl with previously good health\. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day\. Chest CT showed patchy increased\-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased\-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening\. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage \(BAL\) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation\. Targeted next\-generation sequencing \(tNGS\) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid\(BALF\) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus\. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti\-inflammatory therapy were also administered\. By hospital day 10, the patient&\#x27;s condition had stabilized;Follow\-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high\-density opacities with re\-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high\-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion\. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection\. The patient was discharged with medication\. At 6 days post\-discharge, follow\-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery\. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days\. Conclusion EV\-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children\. In addition to direct pathogen\-mediated tissue injury, immune\-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms\. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti\-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes\.

## [Indian Philosophy: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern World: Critical Epistemology, Comparative Thought, and Contemporary Applications](../publications/0fe1954e697413a458a9.md)

Ras Bihari Sharma; Smt\. Anuradha Kumari

Indian Philosophy: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern World explores the major traditions, concepts, and debates of Indian philosophical thought and their relevance to contemporary intellectual life\. It examines classical Indian systems through critical epistemology, comparative philosophy, logic, metaphysics, consciousness, ethics, and contemporary applications\. The book covers the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy, heterodox traditions including Buddhism, Jainism, and Charvaka, theories of knowledge \(pramana\), logical reasoning, language and meaning, the nature of the self, consciousness, karma, dharma, and liberation\. It also compares Indian and Western philosophical perspectives and discusses connections with artificial intelligence, ecology, sustainable living, democracy, and social justice\. Designed for students, teachers, researchers, and general readers, this book provides a structured introduction to Indian philosophical traditions, their historical development, internal debates, and continuing significance in the modern world\. Publisher: Geh Press Edition: First edition, 2026 ISBN: 978\-81\-68406\-53\-7

## [Sosyal Adalet Arayışında Evrensel Temel Gelir ve Atâ Sistemi: Karşılaştırmalı Bir İnceleme](../publications/0fed795765eecc8e718a.md)

Burak Vural; Öznur Özdemir

Evrensel Temel Gelir \(ETG\) kavramı, herhangi bir koşula bağlı kalmadan tüm vatandaşlara devlet tarafından düzenli nakit ödemeyi taahhüt eden, bu yolla temel insani ihtiyaçları karşılamayı hedefleyen bir sosyal politika önerisidir\. Atâ sistemi ise VII\. yüzyılda İslam toplumu içinde ortaya çıkan ve ihtiyaç sahiplerine beytülmâlden yapılan düzenli ödemeleri içeren bir sistemdir\. Günümüzde hâkim ana akım iktisat politikalarının gelir eşitsizliği ve yoksullukla mücadele noktasında yetersiz kalışı karşısında ETG bir çözüm yolu olarak görülmektedir\. Bu sebeple ETG ve tarih boyunca ortaya konulan benzer politikalar araştırmalara konu olmuştur\. Şimdiye kadar olan çalışmalarda ETG birçok farklı açıdan incelenmiş olmasına rağmen kavramı İslam iktisadı çerçevesinde ele alan çalışmalar oldukça sınırlı ve yüzeysel kalmıştır\. Bu uygulamanın İslam iktisadı perspektifinden ele alınması için İslam tarihinden benzer örneklerin incelenmesi gerekmektedir\. Bu çalışmada temel gelir kavramının tarihsel geçmişi, özellikleri ve günümüz uygulamaları açıklanarak Hz\. Ömer döneminde sistemleştirilen atâ ödemelerinin evrensel temel gelir kavramı ile karşılaştırması yapılacaktır\. Çalışmada İslam tarihi kaynaklarının yanı sıra modern dönemde yazılmış birçok kaynağa da başvurularak hem ETG tarihi seyrinde incelenmiş olacak hem de Hz\. Ömer dönemindeki atâ uygulaması ile benzerlikleri ortaya konulmuş olacaktır\. Böylece ETG, sosyal adalet kavramı çerçevesinde İslam tarihindeki somut bir uygulamayla karşılaştırılacak, servetin adil dağılımı, kamu kaynaklarındaki ortak hak ve temel ihtiyaçların güvence altına alınması gibi İslam iktisadının temel prensipleri açısından değerlendirilmiş olacaktır\.

## [Map Before Machine™: Engineering Pre\-AI Sense\-Making in Copilot Systems \(CognitionX Emirates 2026\)](../publications/100ab8d1e7748992315f.md)

Devika Toprani

Presented at CognitionX Emirates 2026 \(Dubai Technology Entrepreneur Center, Dubai, UAE\), Map Before Machine™: Engineering Pre\-AI Sense\-Making in Copilot Systems addresses a critical vulnerability in Human\-AI Interaction: because every AI interface opens directly into a prompt box, users bypass independent reasoning, demonstrating that automation bias is a problem of sequence rather than trust, with the most skilled AI users proving the worst at spotting AI errors \(Fernandes et al\., 2026\)\. To resolve this, Devika Toprani \(Toprani, 2026\) introduces four proprietary, patent\-pending architectures: \(1\) the Somagraphic Learning™ Framework, a human\-first, 3\-stage visual\-cognitive sequence \(Attempt → Map → Refine\) that anchors human reasoning before AI enters at the Refine stage\. \(2\) Shape\-Emotion Grammar™, an inclusive, pre\-verbal structure utilizing shapes, motion, and perceptual salience to build conceptual meaning before language or AI arrives for multilingual, neurodiverse, ELL, and visual thinkers\. \(3\) Map Before Machine™, an analog\-first AI literacy mechanism requiring users to generate a timestamped cognitive artifact prior to AI engagement, deployable via Pen &amp; Paper thinking cards, LMS\-ready modules, or a software\-level Pre\-AI UX Onboarding Layer \(Pre\-AI Prompt Gateway\)\. \(4\) Somatic AI Literacy™, the capacity to establish embodied conceptual orientation before AI interaction begins\. Built via Somagraphic Learning™ in April 2026\. Absent from AI literacy frameworks, UNESCO, CSTA, OECD, ISTE, U\.S\. Department of Labor, etc, which focus on post\-AI interaction, as of April 2026\. ## [YOLO11\-DAL a multi\-scale fusion network for target detection in UAV\-based power line inspection](../publications/1010fef3ef0069c6517a.md)

Taotao Wu; Zhonghua Liu

Abstract Reliable detection of transmission\-line components and defects in unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\) imagery supports preventive maintenance\. Repeated downsampling, however, removes fine spatial detail, while limited interaction between feature levels hinders small\-object detection\. We developed YOLO11\-DAL, a compact detector based on YOLO11n, to address these limitations\. C3k2\-LEGM integrates local structure with global context in two lower\-backbone blocks\. Attentional Scale Sequence Fusion \(ASF\) aggregates P2–P5 features, while a Dynamic Aligned Head \(DAH\) coordinates classification and localisation\. On a seven\-class UAV power\-line dataset, YOLO11\-DAL achieved 86\.2% mAP50 and 57\.7% mAP50:95\. These values exceeded the YOLO11n baseline by 3\.3 and 2\.5% points, respectively\. The parameter count decreased from 2\.58 million to 2\.34 million\. A prototype using a ZED camera and Jetson TX2 integrated image acquisition, inference and result visualisation\. End\-to\-end latency was not measured, so the prototype establishes functional integration rather than verified real\-time performance\. The results support coordinated feature fusion and task\-specific prediction as a practical design for compact UAV inspection detectors\.

## [Strategies for Mitigating Anti‐Nutritional Factors in Legumes: A Review of Traditional and Innovative Processing Techniques for Enhanced Bioavailability](../publications/1012e472e7fbc20d2720.md)

Diana Kavaya; Muhammad Siddiq; Leonard MP Rweyemamu; Lilian Daniel Kaale

ABSTRACT Legumes \(family Fabaceae\) are vital, nutrient‐dense global resources rich in proteins, complex carbohydrates and micronutrients\. Although offering agronomic benefits like nitrogen fixation, their dietary utilization is often constrained by anti‐nutritional factors \(ANFs\) such as phytates, tannins, lectins and oligosaccharides, which reduce bioavailability and cause gastrointestinal discomfort\. This review examines the dual nature of ANFs, highlighting their ecological roles and medicinal benefits alongside their inhibitory nutritional effects\. It evaluates traditional processing methods like soaking, boiling and spontaneous fermentation against modern techniques including controlled fermentation, extrusion cooking and chemical modification\. Through specific case studies, the review explores how soaking and boiling common beans \( Phaseolus vulgaris \) influence nutritional properties and consumer acceptability\. It discusses how bacterial and fungal fermentation, alongside extrusion, enhance the sensory, nutritional and structural qualities of soybeans \( Glycine max \) for industrial product development\. Additionally, sprouting in cowpeas \( Vigna unguiculata \) is highlighted as an effective strategy for preserving heat‐sensitive nutrients\. The review demonstrates how independent variables like hydration, heat and chemical agents \(e\.g\., sodium bicarbonate\) affect the composition, concentration and bioavailability of nutrients and ANFs\. Although heat‐based treatments impact water‐soluble and heat‐labile compounds, nonheat treatments like hydropriming enhance enzyme activity and mobilize nutrient reserves\. Each method presents unique trade‐offs regarding nutrient retention, structural quality and sensory attributes\. Ultimately, this study emphasizes the necessity of optimizing processing techniques to mitigate ANFs while maintaining overall nutritional value, thereby supporting the global shift toward sustainable, plant‐based diets\.

## [Detection and Classification of Email Phishing using CNN\-BiLSTM Model](../publications/101930e6a867de5712ed.md)

Aminu Kabir; Olufunmi Atoyebi Temitope; Prema A\. Kirubakaran; Joshua Abah; Abubakar Mukhtar Ammani

Phishing emails remain one of the most prevalent cybersecurity threats, exploiting users through deceptive messages that mimic legitimate communication\. Traditional detection techniques such as blacklist filtering, rule\-based systems, and signature\-based methods are increasingly ineffective against evolving phishing strategies\. This study proposes an intelligent deep learning\-based approach for the detection and classification of email phishing using a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(CNN–BiLSTM\) model\. The model leverages CNN for automated feature extraction and BiLSTM for capturing contextual and sequential dependencies in email text\. A labeled dataset consisting of 50,000 phishing and legitimate emails was preprocessed using text cleaning, normalization, tokenization, and encoding techniques to enhance model performance\. The proposed model was trained and evaluated using standard performance metrics\. Experimental results demonstrate that the CNN–BiLSTM model achieves superior performance compared to traditional and machine learning\-based approaches, effectively identifying complex phishing patterns\. The proposed model attained an accuracy of 98\.42%, a precision of 97\.85%, a recall of 96\.93%, an F1\-score of 97\.38%, and an AUC\-ROC of 0\.992, while maintaining a practical inference time of 42 ms\. While the model demonstrates robust classification capabilities, limitations remain regarding dataset diversity and deployment context\. The findings highlight the potential of deep learning techniques to improve email security and mitigate phishing attacks\. This study contributes to the development of intelligent cybersecurity systems capable of adapting to the dynamic nature of phishing threats\.

## [Optimalisasi Code Mixing dan Code Switching dalam Pembelajaran pada Program Studi Non\-Bahasa Inggris](../publications/101d3ec4153a695fc03b.md)

Rimma Sianipar

Penelitian ini mengeksplorasi bagaimana code mixing dan code switching memengaruhi proses belajar mahasiswa dalam lingkungan kelas multibahasa\. Selain itu, sebanyak 80% responden atau 80 mahasiswa menyatakan merasa lebih nyaman ketika dosen sesekali menggunakan bahasa ibu sebagai sarana penjelasan, sedangkan aspek kepercayaan diri diukur melalui indikator yang berbeda\. Pada aspek partisipasi, sebanyak 68% responden atau 68 mahasiswa melaporkan bahwa mereka merasa lebih leluasa untuk berkontribusi dalam diskusi kelas dan mengajukan pertanyaan\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa mahasiswa mempersepsikan penggunaan strategi kebahasaan yang fleksibel sebagai salah satu bentuk dukungan dalam memahami materi dan berpartisipasi dalam pembelajaran\.

## [Analysis of clinical feature differences and influencing factors between children with peptic ulcer and healthy children](../publications/102c267ba6a1e1c56cbb.md)

Caiyan Chen; Huiying Qiu

This study conducted a retrospective analysis of clinical data from 92 children with peptic ulcer admitted to a tertiary hospital in the past 5 years and 92 healthy children in the same period, systematically exploring differences in clinical manifestations, laboratory indicators, lifestyle habits, and psychological status between the two groups\. Multivariate logistic regression models were employed to identify independent risk factors for pediatric peptic ulcer\. Results showed that the incidence of abdominal pain \(82\.6% vs\. 15\.2%\), vomiting \(63\.0% vs\. 8\.7%\), and melena \(19\.6% vs\. 0%\) was significantly higher in the patient group than in the healthy group \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Helicobacter pylori \(Hp\) infection rate \(63\.0% vs\. 8\.7%\) and anemia incidence \(45\.7% vs\. 12\.0%\) were also markedly elevated\. Gastroscopy revealed that ulcers predominantly occurred in the duodenal bulb \(68\.5%\) and gastric antrum \(23\.9%\)\. Regarding lifestyle habits, the patient group exhibited significantly higher proportions of boarding school attendance \(77\.2% vs\. 28\.3%\), high\-sugar diet \(56\.5% vs\. 28\.3%\), family history of digestive system diseases \(30\.4% vs\. 8\.7%\), and psychological disorder prevalence \(63\.0% vs\. 9\.8%\) compared to the control group \( P &lt; 0\.01\)\. Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that Hp infection \(OR = 4\.23\), high\-sugar diet \(OR = 2\.89\), family history \(OR = 3\. 17\), boarding school attendance \(OR = 2\.41\), and psychological disorders \(OR = 6\. 11\) were independent risk factors for pediatric peptic ulcer\. This study provides evidence\-based support for early identification and intervention of pediatric peptic ulcer, suggesting that clinical practice should strengthen screening for high\-risk children and implement comprehensive interventions to improve prognosis\.
