## [AI GOVERNANCE AND FINANCIAL RISK : DISCLOSURE BASED AI READINESS INDEX FOR INDIAN BANKS](../publications/10383f4d8677e7f289c3.md)

Snehitha Bommidi; Golli Mohan

Indian banks have been moving rapidly towards the use of artificial intelligence, but there is still no consensus on the best way to assess how well they govern it\. In this paper, a disclosure\-based AI\-Readiness Index is developed and tested for Indian banks, employing sixteen indicators divided into four categories: governance and oversight, risk management, capability and adoption, and transparency and ethics\. Each indicator is assigned a score from 0 to 2 according to the actual information that the bank provides in its FY2025–26 annual report\. Fifteen listed banks were assessed in this manner—five being public\-sector and ten private\-sector—resulting in an overall score out of 100\. HDFC Bank achieves the highest score at 90\.6 and Yes Bank comes second at 84\.4; in both cases these are the only two banks that explicitly link their AI policies to the RBI&\#x27;s Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of AI \(FREE\-AI\), which was issued in August 2025\. SBI is next at 81\.3\. Canara Bank is at the lowest level with a score of 25\.0\. The index is statistically robust \(with a Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha of 0\.87\) and the ranking remains almost unchanged when different weighting methods are applied—whether equal weights, entropy weights or TOPSIS all show very similar results\. A k\-means clustering method divides the banks into three broad groups that correspond to the categories of adopters as described by the Diffusion of Innovation theory: Leaders, Followers and Laggards\. On average private banks score higher than public\-sector banks \(61\.3 compared to 48\.8\), although with only five public\-sector banks in the sample this difference does not reach statistical significance\. The correlations between the index and financial\-risk indicators—NPAs, ROA, CRAR—are weak and inconclusive, and the paper states this clearly rather than presenting the figures in a more favourable light\. What the study provides is a practical, regulator\-linked method of measuring AI governance readiness, directly aligned with the structure of FREE\-AI, thus addressing a gap that is not covered by any of the studies reviewed here: an index of this kind, designed for Indian banks, tested against real risk outcomes after the FREE\-AI framework had been introduced\.

## [АНАЛІЗ СУЧАСНОГО СТАНУ ТА МЕТОДІВ ІМІТАЦІЙНОГО МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ АВТОНОМНИХ СИСТЕМ ТА ТРАНСПОРТНИХ ЗАСОБІВ](../publications/10522cb8b2fa808740d2.md)

Олексій Коломійцев; Станіслав Сергійович Довбій; Ірина Ячна; Володимир Олександрович Комаров; Albert Katunin; Іван Цебрюк; Володимир Миколайович Кібальник; Руслан Миколайович Шупило; Віктор Іванович Сапон; Mykola Bahlai; О\.П\. Марценяк; Тарас Анатолійович Співак

У статті проведено аналіз сучасного стану та методів імітаційного моделювання автономних систем та транспортних засобів\. Сучасні автономні транспортні засоби вимагають високої точності, швидкості та безпеки прийняття рішень у реальному масштабі часу\. Відомі алгоритми пошуку шляху або геометричні методи часто мають високу обчислювальну складність або не здатні ефективно адаптуватися до динамічного міського середовища\. Використання моделей машинного навчання у бортових комп’ютерних системах дозволяє прогнозувати поведінку інших учасників дорожнього руху та знаходити оптимальні траєкторії автономним транспортним засобам в умовах невизначеності\. Розроблено рекомендації\.

## [Correlation between systemic branched\-chain amino acid metabolism and tear fluid inflammation with visual quality of life in patients with dry eye disease](../publications/1052903b347d656f683d.md)

YingMing Wang; Lijuan Que; Zhengtai Sun; Lei Zhong; Xuepei Zhang

Background Dry eye disease \(DED\) is a common multifactorial ocular surface disorder characterized by tear film instability, inflammation, and visual impairment, with rising global prevalence affecting quality of life\. While inflammation is central to DED pathophysiology, the role of systemic metabolic dysregulation in modulating local ocular surface inflammation remains unclear\. This study investigates the correlation between systemic branched\-chain amino acid \(BCAA\) metabolism and tear inflammatory markers as well as visual\-related quality of life \(VR\-QOL\) in DED patients\. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 111 DED patients and 64 healthy controls from a single center \(2022–2024\)\. In the pilot phase, tear samples from 26 DED and 22 controls underwent untargeted metabolomics using UPLC\-MS to identify differential metabolites and pathways\. In the serum\-based sequential exploratory phase, serum BCAA levels \(leucine, valine, ILE\) were measured in 85 DED patients \(stratified by severity\) and 42 controls\. Tear inflammatory factors \(IL\-1β, IL\-6, IL\-8, hs\-CRP, TNF\-α\) were quantified by ELISA/immunofluorescence\. Pearson correlation analyzed associations between serum BCAAs and ocular surface sign parameters \(Schirmer’s test, corneal staining\), and inflammatory markers\. Receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the apparent discriminative ability of serum BCAAs for suboptimal visual quality of life in patients with dry eye disease \(DED\)\. Results Untargeted metabolomics revealed 15 significantly altered tear metabolites in DED \(8 upregulated, 7 downregulated\)\. Enrichment analysis revealed a suggestive trend toward enrichment of the BCAA biosynthesis pathway \(Raw P = 0\.016; after Benjamini–Hochberg correction, FDR Q = 0\.058, which did not meet the significance threshold of Q &lt; 0\.05\.\)\. In this study, pathways with raw P &lt; 0\.05 but corrected Q ≥ 0\.05 were defined as exhibiting a “suggestive enrichment trend” and were not considered as definitive conclusions, warranting further targeted validation\. Serum levels of leucine, valine, and ILE were significantly elevated in both mild\-to\-moderate and severe DED groups versus controls \(all P&lt;0\.05\), but did not differ by severity\. Positive correlations were found between each BCAA and specific tear inflammatory factors \(IL\-1β, hs\-CRP, TNF\-α; r=0\.35–0\.66, all P&lt;0\.05\), while no significant associations emerged with IL\-6, IL\-8, or clinical signs\. ROC analysis revealed notable associations between serum BCAAs and poor VR\-QOL, with AUCs of 0\.916 \(leucine\), 0\.837 \(valine\), and 0\.886 \(ILE\)\. These exploratory findings suggest a potential link between BCAA levels and vision\-related quality of life, but do not establish clinical utility as biomarkers\. Conclusions Untargeted tear metabolomics in a small cohort revealed BCAA\-related metabolic alterations in DED\. Sequential exploratory analysis of an independent large\-sample serum cohort further demonstrated that elevated serum Leu, Val, and ILE, which correlated positively with tear IL\-1β, hs\-CRP, and TNF\-α at the population level\. These findings provide exploratory evidence linking serum BCAAs to DED\. However, given the use of two distinct matrices without paired sampling and the control group sample size n = 42 during the serum association exploratory phase being modestly lower than the predetermined goal—potentially compromising the statistical power of some tests—the results only support population\-level cross\-biofluid associations and do not confirm individual\-level coupling\.

## [Differential Privacy Synthetic Tabular Data Generation for Federated Learning](../publications/1089a5ee63184ae9ad31.md)

Mariona Almató\-Baucells; Carla Lázaro; Cecilio Ángulo

Machine learning in healthcare struggles for one main reason: good data are hard to come by\. Medical records are sensitive, and the rules on sharing them between hospitals are strict\. A common workaround is the use of synthetic data, that is, artificial records that copy the statistics of real ones; however, on its own, such use offers no real privacy guarantee, and earlier studies show it can still leak details about the patients behind it\. We introduce an approach tackling both problems at once\. It builds on a previous UMAP\-based generator methodology and extends it so several hospitals can work together without sharing raw records, in a federated learning form\. Then, the proposed methodology adds differential privacy so every shared quantity carries a formal \(εDP,δ\) guarantee, holding by construction for the fully synthetic variant and under a bounded\-input assumption for the partially synthetic one, tracked by a custom privacy accountant\. Two versions of the methodology are tested: apartially synthetic one, where a reference hospital validates the others’ rows, and a fully synthetic one, where each centre builds its own data from aggregated cluster statistics\. Both are evaluated on four publicly available healthcare tabular datasets spanning prostate cancer \(PI\-CAI, CIA\), breast cancer \(BC\-MLR\), and cardiovascular disease \(fiv\-CardioDB\), to test whether the observed trends generalize beyond a single clinical domain\. As a key takeaway, it is demonstrated that going federated barely affects quality, but the privacy cost depends strongly on the moment in the procedure when the noise is injected, and this pattern holds consistently across all four datasets\.

## [Current Applications and Emerging Horizons of Artificial Intelligence in Temporal Bone Computed Tomography](../publications/108c81c46987dbcf7b81.md)

Yue Cheng; Ning Xu; Pengfei Zhao

The temporal bone has intricate anatomy\. CT examinations can clearly depict fine anatomical structures and subtle lesions, providing indispensable imaging evidence for diagnosing otologic diseases and planning surgical procedures\. However, image interpretation has several inherent limitations, including subjectivity, substantial interobserver variability, and heavy reliance on physician experience, all of which can compromise clinical decision\-making and lead to inconsistent patient management\. In recent years, AI\-driven approaches have made significant progress in this field, particularly in optimizing image quality, identifying key anatomical structures, and assisting in the diagnosis of common otologic diseases\. These advances span multiple tasks and have gradually narrowed the performance gap between automated tools and expert readers\. Despite encouraging results in research settings, AI tools continue to encounter multiple obstacles in the transition from algorithmic validation to routine clinical use\. These challenges include insufficient and imbalanced training data, limited generalizability across diverse populations and imaging protocols, and a persistent lack of clinician trust arising from the &quot;black\-box&quot; nature of these models\. Moreover, the absence of standardized benchmarks and prospective clinical trials further impedes the deployment of these technologies in routine otologic practice\. This paper comprehensively reviews current AI applications in temporal bone CT imaging and discusses related emerging technologies, aiming to provide new perspectives and methods for clinical practice\.

## [Phones away: a mixed methods study exploring secondary school pupil and staff perspectives on tighter mobile phone restrictions](../publications/10920efce36d4f3ecd38.md)

Keely Pridden

There has been much debate in the last five years about the use of mobile phones in schools\. Many secondary schools across the world have been introducing mobile phone bans\. In the UK, numerous schools have considered further restrictions since the government published guidance in February 2024 which recommends against the use of mobile phones during the school day\. However, at present approaches to mobile phone use in schools have been inconsistent and there is a lack of empirical evidence as to the impact of mobile phone restrictions have on a range of factors thought to be influenced by mobile phone use\. This research investigated the impact of tighter restrictions on mobile phone use in a secondary school, looking at factors such as attention/concentration in class, behaviour, wellbeing, cyberbullying, physical activity, screen time and social interactions in school\. A pre\- and post\- measure survey was completed by pupils in school, to look at their views before and after mobile phone policy changes\. Focus groups with staff and pupils were then conducted to gather their views on the use of mobile phones in school and their perspectives on the findings from the survey\. Descriptive statistics were produced for the survey data, and a thematic analysis was used to analyse data gathered from the focus group\. Findings showed that most pupils do not feel that mobile phone restrictions have made a difference to factors investigated\. School staff were predominately against the use of mobile phones in schools with concerns about safety and classroom distraction\. Whereas pupils mostly felt that mobile phones should be used in school within reason\. The difference in staff and pupil perspectives highlights the importance of involving the views of pupils in policy formation\. Future research could look at longer follow\-up periods to review impact and involve parent views\.

## [A lightweight residual multilayer perceptron method for geomagnetic matching navigation](../publications/109c7421f89ef919be1b.md)

Songnan Yang; Haoxuan Tang; Yu Yuan; Wenqi Bai; Yan Yan; Yong Huang; Shiliang Zhang

Abstract To address the inherent challenges of localization in regions with weak or ambiguous magnetic gradients, this paper proposes a lightweight residual multilayer perceptron \(MLRP\) method for geomagnetic matching navigation\. By establishing an accurate nonlinear mapping between geomagnetic vectors and spatial coordinates, the proposed method prevents gradient degradation and the consequent decline in accuracy and stability observed in existing geomagnetic matching methods\. Furthermore, the MLRP method employs an efficient network architecture, achieving a balance between efficiency and accuracy on resource\-constrained mobile platforms, making it suitable for long\-distance navigation missions\. Simulation results demonstrate that, under varying noise conditions, MLRP achieves the lowest mean route\-level error among the evaluated methods\. In one measured route in Xi&\#x27;an, MLRP reduced J\_MAD by 13\.94% relative to ICCP and achieved a batch\-one latency of 1\.7706 ms on an NVIDIA Jetson TX2, confirming the practical feasibility of achieving high\-precision autonomous navigation in GNSS\-denied environments using the MLRP method\.

## [Not All Test\-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model\-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning](../publications/109ef0629d04c81b5e15.md)

Ming Shen; Tianjun Yao

Test\-time scaling methods implicitly assume that additional computation from the same model provides independent evidence\. We show that this assumption fails within a single reasoning model: errors are correlated across repeated samples, across reasoning depth, and in the model&\#x27;s own self\-evaluation, so more compute from the same model is not more evidence\. We introduce DIA \(Disagreement\-triggered Independent Arbitration\), which treats disagreement between an intermediate\-stage and the final\-stage prediction as a per\-question signal of reasoning instability and resolves it by asking a small panel of heterogeneous models to solve the question independently, without seeing either candidate, and aggregating their answers directly\. Across seven benchmarks and two base models, DIA outperforms full chain\-of\-thought in 12 of 14 settings, including a 7\.00% gain on MuSiQue, while activating on only $\\sim 17\\%$ of examples and using up to 47\.2% fewer tokens than a multi\-agent baseline\. Ablations show that both independent solving and solver heterogeneity are necessary for these gains\.

## [CAT\-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty](../publications/10a18b121df3063925e5.md)

Yuan\-Chen Chang; Niklas Herbster; Gauthier Gidel; Tommaso Tosato

Large language models \(LLMs\) are becoming prevalent in scenarios where honesty is critical\. However, despite alignment training, these models still exhibit dishonest behaviour, such as outputting claims that contradict some knowledge or are not supported by what is accessible in context\. We introduce Continuous Adversarial Training for Consistent Honesty \(CATCH\), inspired by a method originally developed to robustly refuse harmful queries\. CATCH trains the model towards an honest answer and away from a dishonest one while maintaining the model&\#x27;s capabilities\. We evaluate two architectures \(Llama\-3\.3\-70B\-Instruct and Qwen3\-3\.6\-27B\)\. We show that trained with only hundreds of targets built from self\-reporting scenarios, CATCH learns an honest behaviour that robustly generalizes and transfers across distinct benchmarks\. It consistently reduces dishonesty under pressure on MASK, increases confessions in the multi\-agent game of Among Us, and improves the discovery rates of the model&\#x27;s hidden behaviours in AuditBench\. We show that CATCH outperforms prompting and supervised fine\-tuning in improving honesty, and it is on par with state\-of\-the\-art honesty activation steering\. However, CATCH surpasses honesty steering in maintaining utility, thanks to a novel choice of utility data\.

## [Service Shitshows Delivery Prevention: Live\-Action Role\-Playing \(LARP\) Bad Service](../publications/10c757b4fa75ce8647cd.md)

Arch George Woodside; Rouxelle de Villiers; Pedro Mir Bernal

Frontline service workers and/or their supervisors delivering clearly inaccurate, bad, and/or unlawful service to customers or other “persons of interest” \(POI\) that causally precedes negative outcomes is one category of shitshow service\-failure performance\. The study presents both case studies and findings from national data showing that shitshow service enactments by performing professional public servants \(PPSs\) occur daily and more frequently in the U\.S\. than in other economically developed nations\. Substantial case evidence supports the view that shitshow performances readily occur even when service protagonists have decades of job experience and/or have trained newly hired professional public servants\. “Professional public servants” \(PPS\) includes employees working in various government agencies, departments, and branches \(e\.g\., clerks in a branch of the U\.S\. Postal Service, a frontline service provider in a state department of motor vehicles, public libraries, and local/state/federal police officers\)\. This study proposes “LARP” \(i\.e\., live\-action role\-playing\) by PPSs as actors with protagonists, POI \(i\.e\., “person of interest”\), and additional collaborative roles\) in face\-to\-face enactments in recorded, actual shitshow performances \(i\.e\., the psychological equivalent of a live virus immunization\) provides the emotional heat needed to help prevent subsequent real\-life shitshow reenactments\.

## [Sinemada Seyir Deneyiminin Sanal Gerçeklik Teknolojisiyle İlişkisini Sorgulamak](../publications/10caaa4913d00075e1cd.md)

Berceste Gülçin Özdemir; Simge ŞİŞMAN BAL; Derya Gül Ünlü; Özge Gürsoy Atar

Bu çalışmanın kuramsal çerçevesini oluşturan ana eksen, sinemanın başlangıcından bugüne kadar ortaya çıkan yeni iletişim teknolojileri bağlamında sinemanın gelişimiyle ilişkili seyir deneyimini tartışmaya açmaktadır\. Araştırmanın amacı, sinema izleyicisinin sinema perdesindeki iki boyutlu seyir deneyimi ile sanal gerçeklik gözlükleriyle izlenebilen 360 derece görüntü sunan üç boyutlu film anlatılarındaki seyir deneyimi pratiğini karşılaştırmalı incelemektir\. Bu amaç doğrultusunda çalışma, iki aşamadan oluşmaktadır\. İlk aşamada kesitsel desen ile veri toplanarak nicel bir araştırma yöntemi tercih edilmiş katılımcılara \(N=214\) çevirim içi olarak Katılımcı Bilgi Formu ile Sinema Alışkanlıklarını Değerlendirme Anketi uygulanmıştır\. Çalışmanın ikinci aşamasında ise, odak grup çalışması \(N=42\) yürütülerek nitel bir araştırma yöntemi tercih edilmiştir\. Odak grup katılımcılarına aynı kısa metraj film, iki boyutlu sinema perdesi ve sanal gerçeklik gözlükleri ile 360° görüntünün sunduğu üç boyutlu film formatı olmak üzere iki farklı boyutta izletilmiş ve ardından çalışmanın amacına yönelik oluşturulan yapılandırılmış araştırma soruları derinlemesine görüşme yöntemlerine uygun olarak sorgulanmıştır\. Çalışmanın her iki aşamasından elde edilen bulgular, sinemada seyir deneyiminin yeni iletişim teknolojileriyle teoride ve pratikte değişimin ve dönüşümün gerçekleşebileceğini göstermektedir\. Bu doğrultuda, mevcut çalışma sinema sahasında seyir deneyim pratiğine ilişkin değişim öngörüsü ile sinema teorilerinde güncel tartışmaların da yapılmasının önünü açmaktadır\.

## [FederatedBytes: Tokenizer\-Free, Byte\-Level Small Language Models for Efficient Multimodal Federated Learning](../publications/10da182fff6e3eacf772.md)

Ali Sarabadani; Massimo Piccardi; Mehran Abolhasan; Farzad Tofigh; Ian Zhou; Justin Lipman

Federated Learning \(FL\) is a powerful machine learning framework that allows building a global model from the contributions of multiple, distributed clients, while ensuring the privacy of their local data\. However, its heavy computational and communication overheads challenge its use for contemporary AI workloads such as natural language processing \(NLP\) and multimodal analysis\. For this reason, this paper presents a novel small language model that leverages byte\-level text and multimodal data processing, enhanced by a linear attention mechanism, to enable manageable Federated Learning of NLP and multimodal analysis tasks\. The proposed model, nicknamed FederatedBytes, manages to process text and any other data types, including images, by treating its input as a mere sequence of bytes, while its lean linear attention mechanism allows abating the overall memory and computational footprint\. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed model we have carried out an extensive performance evaluation on sentiment analysis tasks in multilingual and multimodal settings over the Multilingual Amazon Reviews and ScienceQA datasets\. The experimental results show that FederatedBytes has been able to outperform comparable models such as ByT5 and LSTM, achieving higher accuracy while significantly reducing memory and communication overheads\.

## [Safeguarding Childhood: A Comprehensive Review of Child Abuse in Pakistan](../publications/10ec3ab36f7b9d09ca4a.md)

Zohra Asad; Khadija Khaja

Child abuse is a phenomenon that has affected children from every country, culture, or socio\-economic class\. Children who are abused or neglected may be more likely to repeat the cycle of violence by entering violent relationships as teens and adults, or with some abusing their children\. This paper aims to explore child abuse in Pakistan, the incidence of child abuse, and ways to address it\. This academic article seeks to investigate and examine the patterns of child abuse in Pakistan\. This report offers insights into the prevalence, types, risk factors, and effects of child abuse in Pakistan by reviewing the relevant literature, statistical data, and research studies\. The current judicial system, societal attitudes, and difficulties in resolving child abuse are also addressed\. The results of this review highlight the urgent need for all\-encompassing initiatives to prevent child abuse and protect children&\#x27;s rights and welfare in Pakistan, including awareness campaigns, regulatory changes, and multi\-sectoral partnerships that help reduce child abuse\.

## [Noise\-shaped Sampling and Annealing for Scalable On\-the\-edge Training of Binary and Ternary AI Models](../publications/10edb69fae7a48bcf595.md)

Zihao Chen; Zhili Xiao; Rui\-Jie Zhu; Yipeng Wang; Jason Eshraghian; Shantanu Chakrabartty

The training loss of binary and ternary neural networks, expanded as a multilinear polynomial over the discrete weights, is structurally equivalent to the energy of a hierarchical high\-order Ising model\. We exploit this equivalence to apply Ising solvers to discrete\-weight network training, while accounting for a fundamental difference in objectives: an Ising solver seeks the ground state of a fixed energy function, whereas training seeks solutions that generalize to unseen data\. Our key contribution is $ΣΔ$\-Sampler, an optimizer that reconciles these objectives by embedding a stochastic sampling\-and\-annealing step as a noisy quantizer inside a first\-order $ΣΔ$ noise\-shaping loop\. The loop pushes noise from weight quantization, high\-order frustration, and mini\-batch sampling out of the low\-frequency adaptation band, so that discrete weight updates follow the smooth descent trajectories embedded in the rugged loss landscape\. We validate the framework on a planted quadratic unconstrained binary optimization \(QUBO\) benchmark with a known minimizer; on CIFAR\-10, where a $13$M\-parameter ternary model comes within $1\\%$ of full\-precision accuracy; on ImageNet\-1k, where a ternary ResNet\-18 comes within $0\.4\\%$ Top\-5 accuracy of a ternary baseline; on class\-incremental continual learning, where prior\-task accuracy is preserved; and on MatMul\-free language models up to $2\.7$B parameters, where it outperforms a straight\-through\-estimator baseline under matched continued pre\-training\. Compared with standard quantization\-aware training, $ΣΔ$\-Sampler reduces the training memory footprint by over $50\\%$, delivers an order\-of\-magnitude speed\-up, and reduces weight\-update memory traffic by four orders of magnitude, making it attractive for on\-device training and fine\-tuning of large binary and ternary models\.

## [A machine learning framework for predicting the fire response of concrete\-filled steel plate composite walls](../publications/10ee5a8dc219a11080ed.md)

Nav Raj Bhatt; Huu‐Tai Thai; Brian Uy; Tuan T\. Ngo

Finite element \(FE\) modelling of concrete\-filled steel plate composite \(CFSPC\) walls under fire is computationally demanding, while experimental data remain limited because of the cost and complexity associated with fire testing\. This study presents a machine learning \(ML\) framework for predicting the fire response of axially loaded CFSPC walls subjected to two\-sided ISO 834 standard fire exposure\. As part of dataset development, 255 additional FE simulations were generated using the validated FE model and combined with existing data to form an augmented dataset of 490 cases\. The predictive framework operates in two stages\. First, the fire resistance period \(FRP\) is predicted using ML algorithms\. Then, axial displacement–time curves are predicted in the next stage using a characteristic point\-based method and a principal component analysis \(PCA\)\-based method\. Support Vector Regression \(SVR\) achieved the highest accuracy for Stage 1 FRP prediction, with a test R 2 of 0\.987, while the PCA\-based approach achieved superior accuracy for Stage 2 curve reconstruction, with a mean NRMSE of 0\.231\. Finally, the trained models were implemented in a web\-based prediction application, providing an efficient surrogate tool for rapid prediction of both FRP and deformation response of CFSPC walls under fire within the investigated parameter range\.

## [Improving English Communication Skills for Non\-English Major EFL Students Using a Self\-Developed Website \- Speakee](../publications/10ef569d430e17763247.md)

Le Nguyen Nguyen; Thi Phuong Uyen Nguyen; Uyen Nu Thuy Nguyen

The study examined the effects of a self\-developed website – Speakee on developing English communication skills among non\-English major students at the University of Da Nang\. It also examined how students perceived the use of the website as a tool for improving their English communication skills\. Speakee is an AI\-powered role\-play platform developed to provide contextualized speaking practice and delayed feedback, which was designed based on Task\-Based Language Teaching and Situated Learning Theory\. The study adopted a mixed\-methods quasi\-experimental design\. Datawere gathered through English speaking tests during pre\- and post\-intervention and semi\-structured interviews\. The results indicated that students using Speakee demonstrated significant improvement in their overall English\-speaking performance\. Interview findings further suggested that students perceived several benefits from using the platform, particularly in pronunciation practice, vocabulary development, speaking confidence, and opportunities for additional speaking practice\. Nevertheless, several technical limitations related to speech recognition accuracy, AI interaction quality, and long\-term engagement were also reported\.

## [Electromagnetic pulse as a security threat: impacts on critical infrastructure and protection options](../publications/111a55cf30ba685f1307.md)

Jon Štular

Diplomsko delo obravnava elektromagnetni pulz \(EMP\) kot sodobno varnostno grožnjo ter analizira njegove možne vplive na kritično infrastrukturo in možnosti zaščite pred njegovimi posledicami\. EMP lahko povzroči motnje ali odpoved delovanja elektronskih, komunikacijskih in elektroenergetskih sistemov, pri čemer največje tveganje predstavljajo verižne posledice, ki se zaradi medsebojne povezanosti kritične infrastrukture lahko razširijo na več ključnih družbenih sistemov\. Posebej pomembna sta elektroenergetski in informacijsko\-komunikacijski sektor, saj omogočata delovanje številnih drugih infrastrukturnih in družbenih dejavnosti\. Na podlagi izvedene analize literature je mogoče ugotoviti, da je EMP kompleksna tehnološka in varnostna grožnja, ki je lahko posledica jedrskih, nejedrskih ali naravnih pojavov\. Posebni pravni okvirji, namenjeni izključno elektromagnetnim grožnjam, večinoma ne obstajajo, vendar so ukrepi za zmanjševanje tveganj vključeni v širše sisteme zaščite kritične infrastrukture, kriznega upravljanja in zagotavljanja nacionalne odpornosti\. Ključna ugotovitev diplomskega dela je, da popolne zaščite pred elektromagnetnim pulzom ni mogoče zagotoviti\. Z ustreznimi tehničnimi, organizacijskimi in mednarodnimi ukrepi pa je mogoče bistveno povečati odpornost kritične infrastrukture ter zmanjšati posledice morebitnih elektromagnetnih dogodkov\. Učinkovito obvladovanje elektromagnetnih groženj zato temelji na celostnem pristopu, ki združuje zaščito kritične infrastrukture, krizno upravljanje, mednarodno sodelovanje in krepitev odpornosti družbe\.

## [Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation](../publications/111e09484963cc0e6e7c.md)

Niamjit Das; Kevin Andrew

Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience\. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land\-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high\-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models\. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry \(DTF\) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty\-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support\. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer\-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks\. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine\-learning surrogates\. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi\-temporal observations and dynamic model states\. Results reveal uneven biome representation, with tropical and boreal forests underrepresented compared to temperate zones, underscoring equity concerns in biodiversity\-rich regions\. While most forestry digital twins remain at prototype or early operational stages, continuous coupling of sensing platforms to models demonstrates the potential for near\-real\-time forecasting that extends beyond static inventories\. Future priorities include physics\-informed machine learning, FAIR\-compliant cloud\-native workflows, and expanded monitoring in underrepresented ecosystems\. Embedding biodiversity and resilience monitoring into near\-real\-time, uncertainty\-aware workflows will be critical, enabling DTF to evolve into operational systems that provide adaptive, policy\-relevant decision support for climate\-resilient forest management\. This review offers an integrative roadmap for advancing DTF, contributing to global sustainability and supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including Climate Action \(SDG 13\) and Life on Land \(SDG 15\)\.

## [Prospects of Integrating New Digital Technologies and Evaluation Techniques for Enhanced Business Education Curriculum Implementation in Universities in South\-East Nigeria](../publications/112997e8159d3d416208.md)

Chika Chukwuma\-Nosike; Patience Osebhakhomen Imeokparia

This descriptive survey investigates the prospects of integrating new digital technologies and evaluation techniques to enhance Business Education curriculum implementation in universities in South\-East Nigeria\. Two research questions guided the study\. The population comprises all 203 Business Education lecturers in public universities in South\-East Nigeria offering Business Education\. The multi\-stage, cluster, purposive, and simple random sampling techniques were employed to select a sample of 102 lecturers from six public universities across three states in the South\-East, Nigeria, out of a total of five states in the zone\. The study used a two\-section rating scale with twenty \(20\) items titled Prospects of Integrating New Digital Technologies and Evaluation Techniques for Enhanced Business Education Curriculum Implementation \(PINDTETBECI\) for data collection\. The instrument was validated by three specialists in Business Education, Measurement and Evaluation, and Curriculum Studies\. The reliability of the instrument was determined using Cronbach’s Alpha reliability statistics, and coefficient indices of 0\.83 and 0\.78 were obtained\. The research questions were answered using the mean/pooled mean and standard deviation\. The findings showed that new digital technologies and evaluation techniques such as LMS, Simulation tools, and virtual defence can enhance Business Education curriculum implementation, with a high mean score range of 3\.6 to 3\.8\. It also highlighted the prospects of integrating these new technologies and evaluation techniques, as indicated by items with a high mean range of 3\.8, showing that digital technology\-powered learner\-centred approaches enhance students’ active participation and enable adequate curriculum content coverage during Business Education curriculum implementation in universities in South\-East Nigeria\. Based on the findings, some recommendations were proffered towards effective integration of the new digital technologies and evaluation techniques for enhanced Business Education curriculum implementation in universities in South\-East Nigeria\.

## [Predicting Urban Growth and Future Land Use/Land Cover Change Using GeoAI A Case Study of Indore District, Madhya Pradesh, India](../publications/11306aeae94fbea5e1d4.md)

Bhawna Dandotiya; Suresh Awase

1\. Abstract Rapid urbanisation is transforming the spatial structure of Indore and its surrounding peri\-urban landscape\. This proposed study aims to develop a GeoAI\-oriented framework for analysing historical urban expansion and predicting future land\-use/land\-cover \(LULC\) change\. The study will integrate Earth\-observation data, GIS layers, demographic information, accessibility variables, terrain characteristics, environmental constraints, and machine\-learning methods within a reproducible spatial workflow\. Verified secondary evidence indicates that Indore district covers 3,898 km² and had a population of 3,276,697 in 2011, including 2,427,709 urban and 848,988 rural residents\. Published analysis of the Indore urban/peri\-urban area reports an increase in built\-up area from 15\.30 km² in 1991 to 63\.57 km² in 2001 and 158\.11 km² in 2011\. These trends demonstrate the need for spatially explicit urban\-growth modelling\. The proposed study will identify the principal spatial drivers of urban expansion, classify historical LULC, develop and validate a GeoAI\-based prediction model, and generate a future urban\-growth probability surface for a selected prediction year, such as 2035 or 2045\. Final satellite\-derived LULC areas and model accuracy statistics will be calculated from the selected datasets and independent validation samples before the study is presented as a completed empirical analysis\.

## [Model of internal and external determinants of affiliation motivation among elementary school teacher education students in ethnoscience\-based inquiry learning](../publications/114ff237059383eaf74e.md)

Aisyah Ali; Akhmad Kadir; Ria Ristiani; Suwita Suwita; Lely Yustina Wati; Endriani Endriani

This study examined individual, relational, and classroom\-level factors associated with affiliation motivation among Elementary School Teacher Education students participating in ethnoscience\-based inquiry learning\. A cross\-sectional explanatory survey involved 173 students drawn from four classes randomly selected from eight eligible classes\. Self\-efficacy, goal setting, social needs, sense of belonging, teacher\-student relationships, peer support, recognition and appreciation, classroom climate, and affiliation motivation were measured at one time point and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling\. The eight predictors jointly explained 55\.8% of the variance in affiliation motivation\. All structural associations were positive and statistically significant \(β = \.128–\.187, p = \.004–\.041\), although individual effect sizes were small \(f² = \.026–\.053\)\. The findings indicate cumulative contributions of individual, interpersonal, and classroom\-level resources to affiliation motivation\. Because the study was cross\-sectional, self\-reported, and conducted at one institution, the findings should not be interpreted causally and should be generalized cautiously\.

## [Note on Stochastic Vehicle Routing With Delivery Choice Under Recourse Options](../publications/115426a9865c5c364771.md)

Prahalad Venkateshan; Kamlesh Mathur

ABSTRACT In this paper, we consider the stochastic vehicle routing problem with delivery choice, where, upon reaching a particular customer, the driver has the choice of how much to deliver once the customer demand is revealed\. In our earlier work, a basic version of the problem was considered, in which the driver cannot return to the depot midway in a route to replenish the cargo on board \(see Venkateshan and Mathur 2025\)\. In the present work, we expand on the choices that the driver has by allowing the driver to return to the depot to replenish before returning to the same customer or to proceed to the next customer\. We prove the optimality of different threshold‐based fulfillment policies\. Tests show that these policies significantly reduce the computational effort needed to determine the optimal fulfillment policy along a route, as well as its associated expected profit\. We also show that a single‐vehicle tour that visits all customers is optimal even if multiple vehicles are allowed\.

## [Ecological benefit evaluation and design optimization of urban architectural complexes based on fuzzy logic](../publications/116363d81b6405487843.md)

Zhengjia Xu; Sun Yong

Assessing ecological advantages and refining urban architectural designs are essential for sustainable urban growth\. A lot of study has been done on energy efficiency, resource conservation, and green materials, but there is still no complete framework for systematic ecological assessment and improvement\. This paper presents the Fuzzy Logic\-Based Ecological Design Optimization Framework \(FLEDOF\), which amalgamates environmental, economic, and social sustainability while tackling the uncertainties intrinsic to urban design\. FLEDOF gathers information about energy use, carbon emissions, air quality, and the effects on ecosystems\. It then uses fuzzy multi\-criteria decision\-making methods to rank and improve design options\. The simulation findings show that energy efficiency has improved by 8–10% compared to traditional approaches, carbon emissions have gone down, and resources have been used more efficiently\. The accuracy of data processing has even gone up to 98\.5% under different building situations\. The framework gives architects, urban planners, and policymakers useful information, such as ecological scores, performance measures, and implementation plans, so they may make smart choices\. FLEDOF uses advanced fuzzy logic, iterative optimization, and multi\-database integration to create a methodical, data\-driven way to construct cities that will last\. Its practical consequences support eco\-friendly urban infrastructures and align with global sustainability goals, providing a strong basis for assessing and improving the ecological performance of urban architectural complexes\.

## [Syntropic Horizons of Hope — Conscience, Obligation, and Answerable Action](../publications/11662f05323f9e24fffd.md)

Rubens Turci

Human responsibility cannot be reduced either to compliance with established obligations or to fidelity to personal conviction\. Both individuals and institutions can recognize genuine demands of responsibility, and both can misunderstand the realities to which they respond\. This essay develops a philosophy of syntropic praxis in which conscience is understood as a situated, fallible, and cultivable capacity for recognition and judgment\. Its exercise depends on disciplined attention, public inquiry, legitimate authority, the claims of others, and responsiveness to consequences\. Through encounters with fallibilism, social epistemology, practical wisdom, conscientious objection, civil resistance, epistemic injustice, and artificial intelligence, the essay argues that corrigibility must be cultivated personally and organized institutionally\. Syntropic praxis names neither a privileged form of conduct nor a guarantee of moral truth, but an orientation toward more coherent, justifiable, and responsible participation in shared reality\.

## [Organizational AI Readiness Maturity Model \(AIRMM\): A Conceptual Framework Bridging AI Readiness and Maturity Perspectives](../publications/1167fe73d7ab5a263776.md)

Zineb Benabbou; Med Achraf Nafzaoui

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption requires more than technological availability; it depends on organizational conditions related to strategy, resources, knowledge, culture, data, and processes\. Existing AI readiness frameworks primarily identify these conditions, while AI maturity models generally assess the sophistication of AI capabilities and use\. This study addresses the conceptual space between these two perspectives by proposing an Organizational AI Readiness Maturity Model \(AIRMM\)\. Drawing on organizational readiness theory, AI readiness research, and maturity\-model literature, the AIRMM conceptualizes organizational preparedness as a progressive and multidimensional construct\. The proposed framework comprises six dimensions—strategic alignment, resources, knowledge, culture, data, and process readiness—and four maturity levels ranging from Fragmented to Institutionalized\. Rather than treating organizations as simply ready or not ready, the model assesses the degree to which readiness conditions are developed, formalized, integrated, and institutionalized\. The AIRMM contributes to the literature by introducing a developmental perspective on organizational AI readiness and distinguishing readiness maturity from broader AI maturity\. As a conceptual framework, it also provides a basis for organizational diagnosis and future empirical validation\.
