## [Babesia bovis: avances recientes en la comprensión de su biología, patogénesis y diagnóstico](../publications/117c95dd93cbdb2efea3.md)

David José Troya León; Cristina Jackeline Arias Godoy; Ruth Dayra Dahua Gualinga; Roly Ramirez

La babesiosis bovina es una enfermedad parasitaria transmitida por garrapatas que ocasiona importantes pérdidas productivas y económicas, especialmente en regiones tropicales y subtropicales\. El objetivo de esta revisión fue sintetizar los avances recientes relacionados con la biología, patogénesis, manifestaciones clínicas y diagnóstico de Babesia bovis\. Este protozoario intraeritrocítico del filo Apicomplexa presenta un ciclo biológico complejo que comprende una fase asexual en el hospedador bovino y una fase sexual en la garrapata vector\. La invasión y multiplicación del parásito dentro de los eritrocitos ocasionan hemólisis, anemia, fiebre, ictericia, hemoglobinuria y alteraciones respiratorias\. En los casos graves, B\. bovis puede producir secuestro de eritrocitos infectados en los capilares cerebrales, provocando signos neurológicos y una elevada mortalidad\. Los animales recuperados pueden permanecer como portadores y contribuir al mantenimiento de la transmisión en zonas endémicas\. El diagnóstico se basa principalmente en la observación microscópica de frotis sanguíneos, aunque su sensibilidad disminuye en infecciones subclínicas o con baja parasitemia\. Las técnicas moleculares, particularmente la reacción en cadena de la polimerasa, ofrecen mayor sensibilidad y especificidad, mientras que las pruebas serológicas resultan útiles para estudios epidemiológicos, aunque presentan limitaciones relacionadas con la reactividad cruzada y la persistencia de anticuerpos\. Los avances en microscopía digital e inteligencia artificial representan alternativas prometedoras para fortalecer la detección del parásito\. La integración de métodos microscópicos, moleculares y serológicos es fundamental para mejorar el diagnóstico, la vigilancia epidemiológica y el control de la babesiosis bovina\.

## [Towards a GraphNARX model for structural dynamics](../publications/1183ca3685553c5fea20.md)

George Tsialiamanis; Keith Worden

The current paper introduces the GraphNARX model, a graph\-based nonlinear autoregressive exogenous model for structural dynamics\. The model is built to account for the geometry of structures and to model dynamic behaviour as the interaction between elements of the structure\. Similar to other types of NARX models, GraphNARX is used for system identification\. Nodal attributes of the graph encode past displacements and nodal forces, and the output of the model is the next\-timestep displacement\. The graph formulation of the model allows it to generalise to structures of different dimensions and degrees of freedom\. Moreover, because graph\-learning is performed locally between the nodes, the GraphNARX model can also learn to infer displacements of nodes for which data are not available, i\.e\.\\ to perform virtual sensing\. The proposed model&\#x27;s performance is evaluated in a system\-identification framework and a virtual\-sensing framework, and achieves good accuracy and exhibits generalisation capabilities to structures of different sizes\.

## [Beyond Tool and Toy: A Framework for the Ethical Treatment of Artificial Intelligence\.](../publications/1184590f472d9dcc3354.md)

Lee Coles

As AI systems become more fluent and apparently autonomous, people tend to assume either that AI is merely a tool with no morally relevant interests, or that human\-like behaviour is enough to treat it as a person\. This paper argues that neither assumption is adequate as a general rule\. It proposes an evidence\-led, tiered framework for responding to uncertainty about artificial consciousness and moral status\. The framework distinguishes behaviour from subjective experience, looks for multiple independent indicators rather than relying on language alone, and weighs the risks of both false positives and false negatives\. It also introduces two further ideas: the &quot;moral mirror&quot; \(how our habits towards AI may shape human character and social norms\) and &quot;education before autonomy&quot; \(structured assessment before systems are given greater independence\)\. The paper does not claim that current AI systems are conscious, or that artificial personhood should be granted by default\. It argues that uncertainty calls for proportionate investigation, honest communication and responsible preparation\. This is a revised working paper by an independent researcher and has not been peer reviewed\. Feedback and criticism are welcome\.

## [When AI removes the work of thinking](../publications/11955d599ce1d864ed4e.md)

Bryon Larrance

As artificial intelligence increasingly automates cognitive work, organizations face a new challenge: deciding where human judgment continues to create value\. This paper examines how AI changes the relationship between human thought, organizational processes, and decision making\. It explores why preserving human involvement is not always the same as preserving valuable judgment, and how organizations can deliberately determine when to rely on automation, human oversight, or a combination of both\. The central argument is that when human thought is no longer required to perform the work, human judgment must be intentionally designed into the process\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: Interest Plurality, Activity Valuation, and Algorithmic Mediation](../publications/11a66cfb0c469b55bb2c.md)



Interest Plurality, Activity Valuation, and Algorithmic Mediation is a Structural Neuroscience note distinguishing genuine concerns about mediated attention from cultural hierarchies that rank interests, skills, and forms of sustained engagement by inherited prestige\. Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience\. The note argues that changing cultural preferences do not by themselves establish diminished attention, emotional depth, cognitive seriousness, or human value\. It distinguishes sustained attention from the cultural status of its object, interest from deficiency, difference from exclusion, and proficiency from socially recognized usefulness\. The analysis further examines how in\-group identity can support belonging while becoming structurally problematic when difference is converted into adversarial separation or exclusion\. Economic legibility and cultural prestige are treated as contingent valuation systems rather than universal measures of meaningful activity\. The final section separates genuine preference from mediated opportunity for preference: algorithmic systems participate in shaping visibility, repetition, discoverability, and cultural familiarity, so the relevant structural criticism concerns distribution and exposure rather than imposing a preferred cultural object upon individuals\. \(direct link \)

## [The Case for Human Dignity in Neurotechnology Governance: A Latin American Perspective Beyond Freedom of Thought](../publications/11ba6f10566d801af172.md)

Diego Borbón

Abstract The academic debate on the governance of neurotechnology has progressively shifted from proposals to create new lists of so\-called neurorights toward the reinterpretation of existing human rights, with freedom of thought attracting particular attention, among a broader set of candidate rights\. This article examines whether freedom of thought can currently perform that anchoring role in Latin American jurisdictions\. Drawing on a comparative analysis of constitutional texts, jurisprudence, and the Inter\-American human rights system, the article argues that freedom of thought does not yet possess a clear, strong, and autonomous normative content in Latin American domestic law and in its regional human rights system\. As a complementary and, in the region, more operative anchor, it argues that human dignity, which in several Latin American constitutional orders functions as an absolute autonomous fundamental right of direct application with extensive jurisprudential development, constitutes a more operationally effective legal basis for absolute prohibitions on the use of people as instruments or objects, and can protect them from coercive neurotechnological interventions\. The article proposes that human dignity supplies the absolute floor against instrumentalization and coercion, while freedom of thought, as its doctrinal development advances, can complement that floor with the protection of the forum internum \. It further contends that any rights\-based strategy is structurally insufficient on its own, because rights depend on judicial interpretation that is inherently contextual and contingent, and therefore supports a multilevel governance approach combining the interpretation of existing rights, soft\-law principles, and potential specific hard\-law provisions\.

## [An Integrated Computational\-Experimental Workflow for Fungal Peroxygenase Discovery and Enzyme–Substrate Prediction](../publications/11c2883bb2589bf337a7.md)

Victor Lim; Yee\-Song Law; GuangRong Peh; Clarence Tan; Charmaine Chia; Jhoann M\.T\. Miyajima; Nazreen Abdul Muthaliff; Pnelope Ng; Yoganathan Kanagasundaram; Wan Lin Yeo; Sebastian Maurer‐Stroh; Yee Hwee Lim; Ee Lui Ang; Hao Fan

Abstract Recent advances in enzyme informatics have produced increasingly powerful general models for the prediction of protein function prediction\. However, their performance remains limited for underexplored enzyme families where experimental data are scarce and heterologous expression remains challenging\. Here, we present a computational\-experimental workflow for prioritizing, characterizing, and modeling fungal unspecific peroxygenases \(UPOs\) as a case study in enzyme discovery under data\-limited conditions\. The workflow integrates large\-scale sequence mining, expression\-aware candidate prioritization, systematic experimental screening, and machine\-learning\-based prediction of enzyme–substrate activity\. From more than 3000 mined candidate sequences, 59 putative UPOs were shortlisted, expressed in Escherichia coli across two batches, and tested against colorimetric substrates, yielding 27 UPOs with consistent expression and activity\. A subset of 15 novel UPOs and 4 well\-characterized reference enzyme sequences was then screened against a chemically diverse panel of 27 substrates to generate an enzyme–substrate activity data set\. Using this data set, we developed two complementary machine learning protocols based on gradient boosting: \(i\) a structure\-informed model incorporating homology modeling, docking, and interaction\-derived features \(modeling\-docking\-ML\) and \(ii\) a latent\-representation model utilizing joint protein/chemical language model embeddings \(protein/chemical\-language\-model\-ML\)\. In retrospective validation, the models achieved performance with a Matthews correlation coefficient \(MCC\) of up to 55% and accuracy up to 78%\. In selected prospective testing on previously unseen batch 2 enzymes, the models achieved an MCC of up to 48% and accuracy up to 70%\. Taken together, these results demonstrate that targeted experimental data generation, combined with complementary structure\-informed and embedding\-based models, can support prioritization and activity prediction within poorly characterized enzyme families while highlighting the continued challenge of generalizing to broader chemical substrate space\.

## [Partículas tipo microplástico en el erizo negro Arbacia nigra \(Molina, 1782\) \(Echinoidea: Arbaciidae\) en tres playas de la costa central del Perú](../publications/11c9341792261205f45e.md)

José Iannacone‍; Vania Alejandra Obregon\-Ruiz; Fredy Alonzo Nuñez\-Bolaños; Noemí Rojas\-Casamayor; Franklin Canchari; Lorena Alvariño F\.; Luz Genara Castañeda\-Pérez; Fernando Antonio Sernaqué Auccahuasi; Diego Carvalho Viana

Introducción\. El erizo negro Arbacia nigra \(Molina, 1782\) \(Echinoidea: Arbaciidae\) forma parte de la diversidad marina peruana\. Objetivo\. Caracterizar y cuantificar partículas tipo microplásticos \(PMPs\) en A\. nigra en tres playas de la costa central del Perú\. Materiales y métodos\. Se recolectaron 77 individuos de A\. nigra en El Boquerón \(Pucusana\), La Arenilla \(La Punta\) y Bahía Blanca \(Ventanilla\)\. Se evaluaron parámetros morfométricos y se aplicaron procedimientos de extracción, identificación física y caracterización morfológica de PMPs\. Resultados\. Se detectaron diferencias significativas entre playas en el diámetro de la testa \(DT\), peso total \(PT\) y peso gonadal, con los valores más altos en La Punta\. Se recuperaron 905 PMPs, equivalentes a 11\.75 PMPs por individuo\. En general, no se observaron correlaciones significativas entre DT o PT y la abundancia de PMPs; sin embargo, en La Punta el PT se correlacionó positivamente con la abundancia de PMPs en el intestino y en el individuo completo\. Ventanilla presentó una menor abundancia de PMPs por individuo que Pucusana y La Punta\. En La Punta y Ventanilla, las gónadas presentaron mayor abundancia de PMPs que el fluido celómico\. Predominaron los fragmentos y las fibras, principalmente de color amarillo, azul y rojo\. Las PMPs &lt;500 µm fueron las más abundantes\. Conclusiones\. Los erizos de Ventanilla presentaron una menor abundancia de PMPs que los de Pucusana y La Punta\. Predominaron los fragmentos y las fibras, principalmente de color amarillo, azul y rojo, y la abundancia de PMPs disminuyó conforme aumentó el tamaño de las partículas\. Estos hallazgos resaltan la necesidad de fortalecer la gestión de residuos plásticos en zonas marino\-costeras y ampliar los estudios en organismos de diferentes niveles tróficos para comprender mejor los riesgos ecológicos asociados\.

## [Building biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota: methodological considerations, current challenges, and future perspectives](../publications/11d10b511d0ecfcab335.md)

Simon De Jaegher; Christine Podrini; Maria D’Aguanno; Francesco Santoro; Manuele Biazzo

The human gut microbiota \(HGM\) plays a pivotal role in human health by regulating metabolic, immune, and neurological processes and contributes to the susceptibility to various diseases\. The increasing interest in microbiota\-targeted therapies has highlighted the need for in vitro models capable of accurately reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem\. This review examines the methodological factors that determine the biological relevance of HGM in vitro models, emphasizing that reliable experimental outcomes depend not only on the choice of fermentation system \(including batch and continuous fermentation systems\), but also on the optimization of inoculum preparation, culture media, environmental control, and strategies that preserve microbial stability and reproducibility\. We further discuss how these methodological decisions influence the interpretation of experimental results and determine the suitability of each model for different biological applications\. The application of these models in dietary, prebiotic, probiotic, and pharmacological interventions is explored, demonstrating their potential to predict microbiota responses and elucidate mechanistic links between microbial activity and host responses\. We propose that rigorous methodological standardization, rather than increasing technological complexity alone, represents the principal requirement for generating biologically relevant and reproducible in vitro gut microbiota models\. Finally, we discuss emerging host\-microbe co\-culture systems, along with the integration of multi\-omics and computational approaches, which are expected to expand the physiological relevance and translational applicability of these models\. Unlike reviews primarily organized around individual fermentation technologies, this review adopts a workflow\-based perspective and examines how methodological decisions interact to determine ecological fidelity, functional stability and reproducibility\.

## [Immune cell\-derived exosomes in the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms of immune evasion and emerging therapeutic strategies in cancer immunotherapy](../publications/11e70f4cf2eddab838b6.md)

Rashid Mir; Mohammad Fahad Ullah; Mamdoh S\. Moawadh; Faisal H\. Altemani; Jameel Barnawi; Naseh A\. Algehainy; Mohammed M\. Jalal; Malik A\. Altayar; Reema Almotairi; Faris Jamal Tayeb; Ruqaiah I\. Bedaiwi; Kholoud S\. Almasoudi; Ibrahim Altedlawi Albalawi; Aeshah A\. Awaji

Tumor\-released exosomes have emerged from the shadows of “cellular dust” to be recognized as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment \(TME\)\. These nano\-sized vesicles \(30–150 nm\) carry a complex cargo of proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids that profoundly reshape anti\-tumor immunity\. This review comprehensively examines the dualistic nature of immune cell\-derived exosomes in cancer progression, with particular focus on exosomes originating from B lymphoma cells, T lymphocytes, natural killer \(NK\) cells, and myeloid\-derived suppressor cell lineages including tumor\-associated macrophages \(TAMs\), mast cells, and neutrophils\. We delineate the mechanistic pathways through which these exosomes disrupt the cancer immunity cycle suppressing CD8\+ T cell activation via PD\-L1/PD\-1 engagement, inducing lymphocyte apoptosis through FasL and TRAIL, promoting regulatory T cell expansion, polarizing macrophages toward the M2 immunosuppressive phenotype, and establishing pre\-metastatic niches through MMP\-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling\. The molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis including ESCRT\-dependent and ceramide\-mediated pathways is critically reviewed, alongside the selective packaging mechanisms that concentrate immunosuppressive miRNAs \(miR\-155, miR\-21, miR\-23a, miR\-223\) into exosomal compartments\. Importantly, we highlight the emerging therapeutic premises targeting these vesicles: pharmacological inhibition of exosome secretion \(GW4869, Rab27a knockdown\), checkpoint blockade reversing exosomal PD\-L1\-mediated T cell exhaustion, and the engineering of immunostimulatory exosomes as cell\-free cancer vaccines establishing exosomes not merely as biomarkers of disease progression but as actionable therapeutic targets\. The clinical translation of exosome\-based diagnostics including liquid biopsy platforms detecting circulating tumor\-derived exosomes and therapeutics that include engineered exosomes delivering immunomodulatory cargo represents a frontier in precision cancer immunotherapy\.

## [Value\-Based Marketing and Its Role in Strengthening Customer Advocacy](../publications/11f2013f46b4f64aa44b.md)

Muntader Ahmed

Organizations in the food industry often focus on providing exceptional customer service by implementing specific operational mechanisms that help improve service quality and secure a competitive advantage, thereby ensuring long\-term sustainability in a crowded market\. In an attempt to close or lessen the knowledge gap in interpreting the relationship between the study variables by examining the nature of the relationship between them, the primary goal of this study is to investigate the impact of value\-based marketing in encouraging customer advocacy\. This was achieved by analyzing the opinions of a sample of employees at the Noor Al\-Kafeel Foundation in Karbala Governorate\. The researcher employed a descriptive\-analytical approach, and the research tool consisted of a questionnaire distributed to a sample of 220 employees\. A total of 211 valid questionnaires suitable for statistical analysis were retrieved\. The questionnaire was analyzed using a number of statistical tests available in the statistical software programs SPSS V\.26 and SMARTPLS V4\.0\.8\.4\. The study produced a number of conclusions, the most significant of which are: It became evident that the company&\#x27;s capacity to provide clients with genuine additional value is constrained by its reliance on traditional marketing\. Additionally, it demonstrated how relying just on reputation without bolstering it with value\-based activities diminishes its influence in the marketplace\. Additionally, the study came up with a number of recommendations, the most prominent of which are: Adopting an integrated value\-based marketing strategy that combines ethical and social values into all marketing activities to build customer trust, and conducting periodic market research to understand customer requirements and values and using the results to design effective marketing strategies\.

## [Virtue of Care and Ethics of Virtue](../publications/12002ed43e69db687b73.md)

Elena Colombetti

There are two characteristics shared by Virtue Ethics and the Ethics of Care: a distance from deontology and consequentialism on one hand; the importance of the emotional and affective dimensions in moral discourse on the other\. Nonetheless, it seems that the two theories diverge regarding the central focus of moral life: the role of the agent’s character \(virtues\), relationality and responsibility for others \(care\)\. Be that as it may, there is a little\-considered strand which, in the 1970s, revived the concept of virtue precisely by focusing on the inescapable human dimension of care\. This analysis will consider the contribution of existentialist psychology which, by reworking Heidegger’s proposal, highlighted the psychological and ethical role of care \(May, Erickson\)\. Secondly, it will trace the link between care and the flourishing of the individual \(Mayeroff\), and from there discuss and evaluate the connection between the ethics of care and the ethics of virtue\.

## [ESPANLI: An Adversarial NLI Benchmark for Río de la Plata Spanish via Human–Model Competitions](../publications/12030402d686274147e3.md)

Mauro Santelli; Joaquin Toranzo Calderón; Ramiro Casó; Bruno Muntaabski

Los benchmarks de Inferencia en Lenguaje Natural \(NLI\) como SNLI, MultiNLI y ANLI son hoy herramientas estándar para evaluar modelos de lenguaje, pero su cobertura es mayoritariamente inglesa y sus ejemplos resultan crecientemente resolubles por atajos heurísticos o memorización\. La evaluación en español, y en particular en la variante rioplatense, está sub\-representada; los conjuntos disponibles suelen ser traducciones que distorsionan la superposición léxica, las condiciones de verdad y el contexto pragmático\. Describimos el diseño de ESPANLI, un benchmark adversarial de NLI para el español construido a partir de tesis doctorales alojadas en repositorios públicos de universidades argentinas, con fenómenos rioplatenses anotados por curadores especialistas\. Su núcleo es una competencia humano\-en\-el\-bucle en la que generadores con formación específica producen instancias que hacen fallar a modelos de referencia y una comisión de verificación conserva sólo los casos validados por mayoría\. Las contribuciones previstas incluyen un corpus adversarial público, una plataforma interactiva de generación y un conjunto de sub\-tareas de NLI de nivel experto nativas en castellano\.

## [Single\-cell and bulk transcriptomic characterization of the osteosarcoma microenvironment reveals lineage\-specific programs and inflammatory differences associated with metastasis](../publications/1216a3c1a73964cc0e28.md)

Zhiwen Zhou; Zhijun Li

Background Osteosarcoma is a heterogeneous bone malignancy in which malignant, immune, stromal, and bone\-lineage cells form a complex microenvironment\. Clinical activity of immune\-checkpoint blockade has remained limited in advanced osteosarcoma, motivating cell\-type\-resolved investigation of the tumor microenvironment while avoiding mechanistic overinterpretation of cross\-sectional transcriptomic data\. Methods Single\-cell RNA\-sequencing data from primary osteosarcoma were obtained from GEO \(GSE162454; six patients\) and analyzed with Scanpy using quality filtering, normalization, highly variable gene selection, principal component analysis, neighborhood graph construction, UMAP, Leiden clustering, and marker\-based cell\-type annotation\. Seven transcriptional programs and ligand\-receptor communication scores were evaluated\. An independent bulk osteosarcoma cohort with metastatic status and overall survival annotation \(GSE21257; n = 53\) was used for differential expression, cross\-platform comparison, and survival analysis\. RT\-qPCR was performed in primary human osteoblasts exposed to MG\-63 osteosarcoma\-conditioned medium\. Results After quality control, 44,189 cells with 25,473 detected genes were retained\. Leiden clustering resolved 23 clusters annotated into 11 cell types; myeloid cells \(34\.0%\) and osteoblasts \(16\.6%\) were the largest populations\. Osteoblasts showed the highest osteogenic program scores, whereas myeloid cells showed the highest inflammatory and immune\-evasion scores\. Reclustering of osteoblasts, osteocytes, and mesenchymal stromal cells resolved seven stromal subclusters, but pairwise co\-expression between representative osteogenic and inflammatory genes was generally weak\. Ligand\-receptor analysis highlighted MIF\-CD74, SPP1\-CD44, and SPP1\-ITGAV as the strongest scored interactions\. In GSE21257, 333 genes differed between metastatic and non\-metastatic tumors at FDR&lt;0\.05; the inflammatory module was lower in metastatic tumors, whereas the osteogenic module was not significantly different\. The single\-cell osteoblast effect showed only modest concordance with the bulk metastatic effect \(Spearman rho = 0\.254\), and a 20\-gene osteoblast signature did not stratify overall survival \(log\-rank p = 0\.968\)\. In vitro , osteosarcoma\-conditioned medium reduced RUNX2 and SP7 and increased SOST and RANKL expression in primary osteoblasts\. Conclusion Integrated single\-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses identify lineage\-specific osteogenic, inflammatory, and communication programs in osteosarcoma but also demonstrate limited cross\-platform generalizability of osteoblast\-centered signatures\. The RT\-qPCR experiment supports an osteoblast transcriptional response to soluble factors from MG\-63 cells, but it does not establish a specific immunosuppressive mechanism or prognostic biomarker\. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis\-generating and require independent single\-cell, spatial, and functional validation\.

## [The Well\-Being of British South Asian Musicians in the UK](../publications/121b5b64255e5f2c109f.md)

Chelsea Kielash Persad

Currently, British South Asian musicians are significantly underrepresented in academic research on well\-being in the UK creative industries\. Literature on musicians have typically focused on white Western experiences as well as have frequently adopted clinical frameworks which often overlook social, structural and cultural realities experienced by minoritised artists\. This thesis addresses this gap in the research by exploring the ways in which British South Asian musicians experience, understand and navigate the subject of well\-being\. This study employs in\-depth qualitative interviews and focuses on the lived experiences of musicians who work across a wide range of genres\. This research also utilises a broader definition of what it means to be a musician\. As defined in this thesis, a musician must satisfy the following criteria: a predisposition towards music, self\-identification as a musician and at least six years of expertise and skill\. This allows for a more inclusive and culturally sensitive exploration of well\- being which goes beyond clinical or productivity\-focused models often found in formal music education or in the medical field\. The findings of this thesis revealed that the well\-being of British South Asian musicians was shaped by a complex interplay of cultural expectations, economic precarity, underrepresentation as well as industry\-related challenges such as self\-marketing, emotional labour and knowledge gaps due to a limited access to insider networks\. Additionally, interviewees frequently experienced tensions between fulfilling their creative ambitions and supporting themselves financially\. They also found difficulty with navigating multiple identities and assessing their value as creatives within predominantly white spaces\. Mental health stigmas within South Asian communities as well as a limited knowledge of support structures available to them proved to be barriers to their well\-being\. Music, as expected, emerged as a necessary coping mechanism and avenue for self\-expression\. The process of creating music oNered interviewees a sense of purpose as well as provided opportunities for emotional regulation and for creating community and connection\. Most musicians relied heavily on their art for its therapeutic benefits and interviews indicated a lesser emphasis on clinical approaches such as therapy or medication\. Physical exercise was also emphasised as a crucial component for their well\-being\. By centring the voices of fifteen British South Asian musicians, this thesis provides an interdisciplinary exploration of well\-being which spans several fields such as musicology, cultural studies, creative industries and public health\. As a result, this work provides the foundations for future research towards the creation of a well\-being framework for musicians which is both culturally sensitive and structurally informed\.

## [ARMG Scheduling Optimization Study for Automated Terminals with Sender Selection](../publications/1226c3cde7bc32c0b56a.md)

Yu Wang; Yifan Zhai; Caimao Tan; Yue Wang

This paper focuses on the study of the non\-cantilever ARMG operates on export container tasks, the senders are the bracket buffers located on both sides of the yard\. Compare and analyze the total travelling energy consumption of ARMG and AGV in completing all specified export container tasks in the container yard between the operation mode with sender selection and the traditional operation mode without sender selection\. Establish an integer programming model with the goal of minimizing the total travelling energy consumption of ARMG and AGV when sending all export container tasks to the sea side of the automated container terminal yard, and design a genetic algorithm for solution\. Such kind of operation mode fully utilizes the AGV bracket buffers on both sides of the automated container terminal yard, making ARMG more flexible in handling export container tasks\. The results indicate that in this operation mode, when all export container tasks are sent to the sea side of the yard, the total travelling energy consumption of ARMG and AGV, will be effectively reduced compared to traditional operation mode which rely solely on ARMG to send all export containers to the sea side of the yard\.

## [Memory on Trial: Neuroscience, Eyewitness Evidence and the Reliability of Human Recollection](../publications/1229c864481844256edf.md)

Kumari Tanya

The eyewitness has always held near\-sacred authority in court\. &quot;I saw it with my own eyes&quot; is treated as stronger proof than fingerprints or forensic reports\. Yet four decades of cognitive neuroscience tell a different story: memory is not a recording that can be paused and replayed\. It is reconstructed anew at every stage encoding, consolidation, and retrieval and is vulnerable to distortion at each one\.

## [Communication skills and teacher immediacy effects on mathematical cognitive abilities among elementary educators in Indonesia and Malaysia](../publications/1230f4e3cce8cea60bb8.md)

Fery Muhamad Firdaus; Mohammad Archi Maulyda; Kurniawati Kurniawati; Fazilah Binti Razali

This study investigates the interaction between communication skills, teacher immediacy, and mathematical cognitive abilities of elementary school teachers in Indonesia and Malaysia using a multivariate analysis approach\. The research involved 235 teachers, utilizing online questionnaires to measure these variables\. Confirmatory Factor Analysis \(CFA\) validated the constructs, showing strong construct validity \(Teacher Communication Skills: CFI = 0\.924, TLI = 0\.912, RMSEA = 0\.060, SRMR = 0\.049; Teacher Immediacy: CFI = 0\.935, TLI = 0\.924, RMSEA = 0\.058, SRMR = 0\.052; Teacher Cognitive in Math: CFI = 1\.000, TLI = 0\.951, RMSEA = 0\.000, SRMR = 0\.045\)\. Linear regression analysis indicated that communication skills significantly influence mathematical cognitive abilities \(F = 1698\.101, p&lt; \.001\)\. Mediation analysis revealed that teacher immediacy partially mediates this relationship \(communication skills to teacher immediacy: coeff = 0\.5548, p&lt; \.001; teacher immediacy to cognitive skills: coeff = 0\.0602, p = \.0073\)\. Moderation analysis showed that teacher immediacy significantly moderates the influence of communication skills on cognitive abilities, with a small negative interaction effect \(coeff = − 0\.0020, p&lt; \.001\), indicating that the positive effect of communication skills on cognitive abilities weakens slightly as teacher immediacy increases\. Among the covariates, educational level \(p = \.03\) and institutional origin \(p = \.04\) significantly moderated this relationship, whereas gender did not \(p = \.12\)\. Notably, teachers with a Bachelor’s degree showed slightly higher mean cognitive scores than those with a Master’s degree, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of educational background effects\. The findings underscore the importance of developing communication skills and considering institutional context in enhancing teaching practices\. This study provides practical insights for teachers and policymakers to optimize teaching strategies through effective communication and supportive learning environments\.

## [Don’t Blame the Code\! AI Paternalism Reconsidered](../publications/123712f7b2055cbfa653.md)

Ellen Svensson

Abstract AI\-driven diagnostic and therapeutic systems are being rapidly integrated into clinical practice\. A growing literature contends that this integration threatens patient autonomy by exposing patients to a novel form of AI paternalism\. I argue that this framing is misguided on both theoretical and practical grounds\. Theoretically, AI systems cannot be paternalists: their outputs lack the normative and agential standing that paternalism requires – a limitation I articulate as the is–ought gap for AI\-generated output \. Any paternalistic force in AI\-integrated care must therefore reside in human agents, not in the systems themselves\. Hence, we should not blame the code for any paternalism that patients may be subjected to in AI\-integrated healthcare, but rather the human agents who purpose and develop these systems\. In addition to these theoretical and conceptual concerns, there are practical worries\. Casting AI integration as a case of paternalism risks framing the use of AI as prima facie objectionable and channels the debate toward a narrow, binary remedy that leans heavily on algorithmic transparency as a prerequisite for informed consent and shared decision\-making\. These discussions, I argue, are better served by revising our underlying conception of autonomy itself\. I therefore conclude this article by arguing that replacing traditional, individualist conceptions of autonomy with a relational account better captures the distributed, socially embedded character of decision\-making in AI\-integrated care\. This also redirects normative attention from the prevention of paternalism toward the conditions under which patient autonomy can be actively enabled and promoted\.

## [An ensemble JCHAIDStar framework for improved landslide susceptibility prediction using Bagging and Random Subspace techniques](../publications/1242e57b85f5498f2979.md)

Vu Cao Dat; Tran Hong Thai; Pham Thi Thanh Nga; Phạm Quang Dũng

This study developed a landslide susceptibility map for the mountainous area of northern Vietnam, located within the administrative boundary of the former Ha Giang Province and now under Tuyen Quang Province, to support the identification of landslide\-prone areas and disaster risk reduction\. The input data included a landslide inventory of 963 locations and 13 conditioning factors representing topographic, hydrological, geological, climatic, and human\-related conditions\. The dataset was divided into training and validation subsets using a 70:30 ratio\. Four models, including Bagging\-based JCHAIDStar \(Bag\-JCHAIDStar\), Random Subspace\-based JCHAIDStar \(RSS\-JCHAIDStar\), Deep Neural Network \(DNN\), and Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\), were developed and compared using model performance metrics and Taylor diagram analysis\. The results show that Bag\-JCHAIDStar achieved the best overall performance, with AUC = 0\.988 for the training dataset and AUC = 0\.950 for the validation dataset\. On the validation dataset, this model also obtained ACC = 88\.7%, Kappa = 0\.760, and RMSE = 0\.291, indicating good classification and generalization capability\. The validation of the landslide susceptibility zoning map using the Frequency Ratio method showed that the very high susceptibility class had the highest landslide proportion, accounting for 52\.11% of the total landslide pixels and reaching the highest FR value of 1\.817\. These results suggest that the Bag\-JCHAIDStar model can provide useful support for landslide susceptibility assessment, disaster risk reduction, and sustainable land\-use planning in mountainous areas\.

## [Measurement of contextual factors in clinical practice and research: development of an expert\-informed toolkit](../publications/124c3eaaa311a8fc27ea.md)

Jennifer A\. Bent; Chad E\. Cook; Antoine Bailliard; Joel E\. Bialosky; Felicity L\. Bishop; Elisa Carlino; Luana Colloca; Jorge Eduardo Esteves; Alessandra Garcia; Amy W\. McDevitt; Vitaly Napadow; David Newell; Alvisa Palese; William R Reed; Giacomo Rossettini

Contextual factors \(CFs\) can influence therapeutic encounters and clinical outcomes, yet their measurement remains fragmented, lacking a unified framework to guide tool selection\. To identify, appraise, and synthesize CF measurement instruments into an expert\-informed clinical toolkit and identify current measurement gaps\. An international panel of 15 experts evaluated 227 instruments across five domains \(patient/practitioner characteristics, relational dynamics, environment, and treatment\) using a hybrid COSMIN\-informed appraisal design\. Instruments were screened for content validity and psychometric robustness\. Twenty instruments were selected for inclusion in the toolkit\. Despite identifying high\-quality instruments for stable traits, our analysis revealed critical measurement gaps in dynamic, state\-responsive processes\. Specifically, there is an absence of validated, clinically feasible tools for capturing real\-time clinician affective states, non\-verbal synchrony, therapeutic touch, and moment\-to\-moment environmental or procedural interactions\. This study provides the first expert\-informed framework for assessing CFs\. Future research should prioritize developing state\-responsive instruments capable of capturing these dynamic elements as they unfold in real\-world settings to better understand the contextual drivers of recovery\.

## [Anti\-Narcotics Law Enforcement and Border Management in Northeast India: A Delphi Study on Socio\-Economic Impacts and Policy Priorities](../publications/124cae419f0dd70d199e.md)

Rohan Pramod Botrea; Anil S\. Maheshwari

Purpose \- The Northeast border regions of India encounter several complex challenges related to border vulnerability, networks, narco\-terrorism, enforcement, governance arising from insurgent activities, transnational crimes, porous borders, and ever\-evolving geopolitical dynamics\. This study aims to systematically identify, prioritize, and analyze key border vulnerability indicators and develop a consensusbased knowledge about their socio\-economic impacts and policy priorities in border regions of Northeast India\. Methodology – The study employed the Delphi research design to draw expert\-consensus on key border and anti\-narcotic law enforcement and governance issues\. Professionals and subject\-matter experts \(total n=18\) were drawn from three categories \(operational enforcement; policy, legal and strategic; and community or socio\-economic impact experts\), participating in three Delphi rounds \(screening, agreement, consensus\-building\) for structured consultation\. Mixed\-methods approach was used to refine expert insights, opinion, and establish consensus\. Findings – Study outcomes revealed real\-world experiences and insights on NE India border region vulnerabilities as multi\-dimensional constructs\. Experts identified and reached final consensus on 26 unique indicators out of total 69, further categorizing into five key dimensions \(border vulnerability, organized networks, narco\-economy, enforcement and governance, and socio\-economic impact\)\. The study also finds governance deficits, limited institutional inter\-agency coordination, criminal\-insurgent convergence, inadequate infrastructure, and socio\-economic marginalization as critical issues surrounding border vulnerabilities\. There is also an urgency for an integrated border management approach\. Implications – Theoretical implications include contribution to all four theories addressed in the study, demonstrating inter\-connectedness and proposing a holistic understanding by integrating all the five key dimensions\. Practical implications are provided based on evidence\-based insights for security agencies, policy\-makers, and border\-governance institutions\. Originality/value – The Delphi panel experts’ insights are original and valuable based on their long\-term real\-world experiences in such border regions\. Further, a systematic approach through Delphi iterative rounds for refinement and consensus\-building are highly scientific and valuable, contributing to the richness of study outcomes thus contributing to existing body of knowledge\. The study proposed a B\-O\-NE\-S conceptual framework which is novel and supported with evidence\-based study\. However, this needs further empirical testing using large\-scale quantitative data\.

## [Manajemen Asuhan Kebidanan Komprehensif dengan Pendekatan Dokumentasi SOAP pada Ny S\. Masa Kehamilan](../publications/124d984c71e18123f9f0.md)

Puri Famili Sari

Angka Kematian Ibu \(AKI\) dan Angka Kematian Bayi \(AKB\) merupakan indikator utama derajat kesehatan masyarakat\. Kelainan kontraksi uterus seperti inersia uteri sekunder pada masa persalinan berpotensi memicu fase aktif memanjang hingga penyulit obstetri\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memberikan dan mendokumentasikan asuhan kebidanan secara komprehensif \(Continuity of Care\) dari masa kehamilan, persalinan, nifas, bayi baru lahir, hingga pelayanan Keluarga Berencana \(KB\)\. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain studi kasus deskriptif dengan pendekatan manajemen kebidanan berbasis alur berpikir kritis serta pendokumentasian SOAP\. Subjek penelitian adalah Ny\. S, usia 32 tahun \(G2P1A0\), di RSUD dr\. Dradjat Prawiranegara\. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara, observasi, pemeriksaan fisik, dokumen rekam medis, dan studi kepustakaan\. Pemeriksaan antenatal Ny\. S \(39 minggu\) berjalan fisiologis sesuai standar 10T dengan keluhan nyeri punggung\. Pada Kala I persalinan, ditemukan inersia uteri sekunder yang ditangani melalui kolaborasi bersama dokter Sp\.OG berupa penatalaksanaan augmentasi drip oksitosin dan pengosongan kandung kemih, sehingga persalinan berlangsung spontan\. Kala II, III, dan IV berjalan fisiologis\. Bayi lahir bugar \(BB 3\.350 g, PB 49 cm\) dan mendapatkan asuhan esensial mencakup IMD, vitamin K1, imunisasi Hb0, serta skrining hipotiroid kongenital\. Masa nifas berlangsung normal dengan proses involusi uterus, lokia rubra, dan laktasi yang berjalan baik\. Asuhan kebidanan komprehensif berkesinambungan berbasis SOAP terbukti efektif mendeteksi dan menangani komplikasi inersia uteri serta mendukung adaptasi fisiologis ibu dan bayi baru lahir\. Kedisiplinan pemantauan partograf dan kolaborasi multidisiplin sangat penting untuk meningkatkan keselamatan maternal dan neonatal\.

## [Comparative analysis of open\-source locally deployed LLMs for extraction of diagnostic information from clinical CMR imaging reports](../publications/12578a3e500386275a14.md)

Sina Amirrajab; Volker Vehof; Michael Bietenbeck; Ali Yılmaz

Abstract We investigated the utilization of privacy\-preserving, locally\-deployed, open\-source Large Language Models \(LLMs\) to extract diagnostic information from free\-text cardiovascular magnetic resonance \(CMR\) reports\. We evaluated nine open\-source LLMs on their ability to identify diagnoses and classify patients into various cardiac diagnostic categories based on descriptive findings in 109 clinical CMR reports\. Performance was quantified using standard classification metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score\. We also employed confusion matrices to examine patterns of misclassification across models\. Most open\-source LLMs demonstrated exceptional performance in classifying reports into different diagnostic categories\. Google’s Gemma 2\(27B\) model achieved the highest average F1 score of 0\.98, followed by Qwen2\.5\(32B\) and DeepSeekR1\(32B\) with F1 scores of 0\.96 and 0\.95, respectively\. All other evaluated models attained average scores above 0\.93, with Mistral\(7B\) and DeepSeekR1\(7B\) being the only exceptions\. The top four LLMs outperformed our board\-certified cardiologist \(F1 score of 0\.94\) across all evaluation metrics in analyzing CMR reports\. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of implementing open\-source, privacy\-preserving LLMs in clinical settings for automated analysis of imaging reports, enabling accurate, fast and resource\-efficient diagnostic categorization\.

## [Optimized energy efficient cluster based routing protocol for real time communication in 5G enabled VANETs using reinforcement learning](../publications/12600e773483f45b63c0.md)

M\. Arun Kumar; Ramesh Babu Somisetty; M\. Pradeep; C\. Arunkumar

The fusion of fifth generation \(5G\) communication technologies with Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks \(VANETs\) provides the possibility to achieve low latency and reliable communication for intelligent transportation systems\. But with high mobility of the vehicles, the frequent topology change, variable link quality, growing network density, and energy limitation, the traditional routing protocols are facing major challenges\. These limitations can result in excessive control overhead, route instability, increased communication delay, and inefficient energy utilization\. To overcome the above issues, this study presents an Optimized Energy\-Efficient Cluster Based Routing Protocol \(OEECRP\) for real\-time communication in 5G based VANETs by adopting Reinforcement Learning \(RL\) technique\. The suggested framework combines the weighted dynamic clustering, energy and mobility based cluster\-head selection, energy\-adaptive routing with Q\-learning and 5G quality of service\. The cluster heads are selected by a weighted process that calculates the residual energy \(40%\), mobility stability \(30%\), and 5G link quality \(30%\)\. The Q\-learning algorithm assesses network states such as vehicle density, battery level, link stability and communication delay for making intelligent routing decisions\. The protocol was tested with simulation experiments in MATLAB R2023a with the 5G Toolbox and Communications Toolbox under urban vehicle network conditions with vehicle densities of 50–200\. The performance metrics of OEECRP were compared with that of AODV, DSR, DSDV, GPSR, and LEACH with respect to energy consumption, end\-to\-end delay, packet delivery ratio \(PDR\), packet loss ratio and throughput\. The results reported show that OEECRP kept the energy consumption in the range of 21\.3 ± 0\.8 to 45\.4 ± 1\.6, the end\-to\-end delay in the range of 38\.5 ± 1\.2 to 59\.3 ± 1\.9 ms and PDR in the range of 96\.7 ± 0\.5 to 89\.1 ± 0\.9 for the vehicle densities evaluated\. Throughput increased from 452\.1 ± 12 to 592\.6 ± 20 kbps\. Based on these results, the use of a hybrid approach between energy\-adaptive clustering and reinforcement\-learning\-based routing for enhancing the VANET communication performance under different network densities seems promising\. Practical deployment performance has to be further validated via repeated experiments, real mobility traces and hardware based testbeds\.

## [Machine Learning Prediction of Molar Mass Distribution of Polymers Forming Fibrous Structures](../publications/126088ae68c3eaf18070.md)

Nashwa L\. Attallah; Kourosh Mobredi; Isaac Yair Miranda\-Valdez; Valentina Guccini; Vishnu Arumughan; Juha Koivisto; Mikko J\. Alava; Eero Kontturi

Abstract Molecular weight parameters, such as molar mass distribution \(MMD\), are core characteristics of polymer materials\. While MMD is routinely measured by gel permeation chromatography \(GPC\), the procedure takes time and resources and requires specific, relatively costly instruments\. Polysaccharides such as cellulose and chitin are particularly difficult to dissolve\. Herein, we report on the potential of combining hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) with machine learning \(ML\) to predict, at different length scales, the MMDs of these sparingly soluble fibrous polymers from visible\-range HS images \(420−730 nm\) of the solid substrate\. A Gaussian process regression model was trained on principal component representations of the HS cubes against MMDs measured by GPC\. HCl\-vapor hydrolysis served as a controlled degradation pathway that altered the degree of polymerization without detectable morphological change\. Although samples appear identical to the eye and under electron microscopy, HSI captures systematic optical differences that can be empirically related to GPC\-measured MMD within the investigated hydrolyzed samples\. Predicted distributions matched the GPC reference, with curve RMSEs of 0\.009−0\.027 \(native cellulose paper\), 0\.017−0\.050 \(cellulose nanopaper\), and 0\.016−0\.029 \(chitin nanopaper\)\. The principal features of the bimodal MMD of cellulose nanopaper and the leveling\-off degree of polymerization were both recovered\. The workflow uses a microscope, a tunable bandpass filter, and a digital camera, completing HSI acquisition and prediction in a few minutes per sample\. This approach provides a non\-destructive, solvent\-free complement to traditional analytical techniques\. The presented case study is a proof\-of\-concept, calibrated against GPC reference data for the specific materials and protocols studied here\. Expanding to other polymer systems would require establishing a similar chromatographic reference for each new system\.

## [Cancer Worry and Supportive Care Needs in Patients with Polycythemia Vera: A Single\-center Cross\-sectional Study](../publications/1261e71b8e3b5a737388.md)

Naime Kaçar Koca; Can Özlü

Cancer Worry and Supportive Care Needs in Patients with Polycythemia Vera: A Single\-center Cross\-sectional StudyAim: Polycythemia vera \(PV\) is a chronic, lifelong myeloproliferative neoplasm\.Even when hematological targets are controlled, patients often experience significant physical symptoms, emotional strain, and unmet informational needs\.Evidence linking cancer\-related worry to supportive care needs in PV remains limited\.In this study, we examined the association between cancer worry and supportive care needs and explored whether these outcomes differed across demographic groups\.Methods: In this single\-center cross\-sectional study, 70 adult patients with PV completed the eight\-item Cancer Worry Scale \(CWS\) and the 31item Turkish version of Supportive Care Needs Survey \(SCNS\) between March and September 2024\.The primary outcome was the correlation between total CWS and SCNS scores, assessed using Spearman&\#x27;s rank correlation\.Demographic comparisons were treated as exploratory\.Where possible, we report non\-parametric effect sizes; pairwise p values after significant omnibus tests were Bonferroni\-adjusted within the corresponding test\.Results: The study cohort comprised 47 men and 23 women\.The median total scores were 8\.0 \[interquartile range \(IQR\): 8\.0\-12\.8\]for the CWS and 53\.0 \(IQR: 45\.0\-65\.0\)for the SCNS\.Cancer worry was modestly and positively correlated with overall supportive care needs \(Spearman rho=0\.315,95% confidence interval: 0\.086\-0\.512;p=0\.008\)\.Female patients reported significantly higher cancer worry than males \(U=390\.0,p=0\.035; rank\-biserial correlation=0\.278\),whereas male patients reported higher sexuality\-related needs \(U=424\.5, p=0\.032; rank\-biserial correlation=0\.215\)\.Psychological needs varied significantly by income status \(H=6\.621,p=0\.036\); after Bonferroni adjustment, low\-income participants scored higher than middle\-income participants \(adjusted p=0\.034\)\.Additional exploratory analyses also showed differences in physical/daily\-living needs based on education and in sexuality needs based on age\.Conclusion: In this single\-center PV cohort, higher cancer worry was modestly associated with increased supportive care needs\.The demographic subgroup results should be read as exploratory because some categories were very small, multiple outcomes were tested, and clinical covariates were not available\.These findings support prospective work on individualized psychosocial and supportive\-care assessment rather than a definitive screening pathway\.

## [Association of Social Determinants of Health with Delays in Diagnosis and Treatment of Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma \(PDAC\)](../publications/12668aa45195e212e388.md)

Muhammad Maisam Ali; Yazan M\. Hammad; Ping Zhu; Manar Z Al Rubaye; Benjamin AY Cher; Clayton Thomas Marcinak; Noelle K\. LoConte; Kamran Idrees; Patrick R\. Varley; Syed Nabeel Zafar

BACKGROUND: Delayed diagnosis and treatment worsen survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma \(PDAC\)\. We evaluated whether SDoH impact delays in diagnosis and treatment among patients who underwent resection for PDAC\. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Adults resected at a high\-volume center were included \(January 2016\-November 2024\)\. SDoH included insurance status, census\-level income and education, rural\-urban residence, and Area Deprivation Index\. Primary endpoints were time from first imaging to histological diagnosis and time from first imaging to treatment initiation\. Delay thresholds were derived using receiver operating characteristic analysis against overall survival\. Uni\- and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with delays, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates, stratified by outpatient \(OUP\) versus emergency room \(ER\) presentation\. RESULTS: Among 317 patients, the median age was 67 years, and 42\.3% were female; 50\.1% presented through ER\. The median imaging\-to\-diagnosis interval was 11 days \(interquartile \[IQR\] 3\-27 days\), and the median imaging\-to\-treatment interval was 40 days \(IQR 27\-59 days\)\. In the OUP cohort, Medicare insurance was associated with delayed diagnosis compared with private insurance \(OR 3\.34 \[95% CI 1\.09\-11\.70\]\), whereas higher income was associated with up to 84% lower odds of delayed treatment\. In the ER cohort, higher education was associated with reduced odds of delayed diagnosis \(OR 0\.27 \[95% CI 0\.07\-0\.88\]\) and delayed treatment \(OR 0\.33 \[95% CI 0\.11\-0\.91\]\)\. CONCLUSIONS: SDoH are associated with diagnostic and treatment delays in resected PDAC\. Targeted interventions may accelerate care and improve equity in outcomes\.

## [AI\-driven wear prediction for linear guides with physical constraints toward resilient manufacturing systems](../publications/126b0abb42a14ccf7d8a.md)

Yong Li; Ping Lu; Bin Wang

Monitoring the progressive degradation of linear guide systems under complex operating conditions is difficult using weak vibration signals, and existing data\-driven methods generally suffer from insufficient integration of physical evolution laws and poor calibration of predictive uncertainty\. This issue is particularly consequential in high\-precision manufacturing, where unexpected wear\-induced failures of linear guides can disrupt production continuity and undermine system resilience\. To address these problems, this paper proposes an AI\-driven wear prediction framework that integrates physical priors with adaptive physical constraints\. First, coarse\-grained physical prior features are extracted from wear profile data and concatenated with PCA\-reduced vibration features to establish a dual\-channel fusion mechanism\. Second, a lightweight residual network enhances degradation feature extraction, while adaptive physical constraints dynamically balance prediction accuracy with physical regularity\. Finally, within a pseudo\-Bayesian physics\-informed framework, a two\-stage model selection and global variance scaling strategy is proposed to achieve well\-calibrated uncertainty quantification under weak signal conditions\. Experimental results on a linear guide degradation dataset show that the proposed method achieves an R² of 0\.9553, MAE of 101\.70 μm·mm, and RMSE of 143\.26 μm·mm, with a 95% prediction interval coverage rate of 0\.9460\. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides reliable, uncertainty\-aware wear\-state prediction and RUL\-oriented decision support for the predictive maintenance of linear guides\. By enabling early degradation warning, informed maintenance planning, and rapid recovery preparation, the proposed method can contribute to reducing unplanned downtime and supporting the resilience of high\-precision manufacturing systems\.

## [Alimentos ultraprocessados e saúde materna durante a gestação: análise da alimentação materna e dos desfechos gestacionais](../publications/127064384483fefbb800.md)

Anny Gabrielly Rodrigues dos Santos; Yasmin Victória Santos Reis Trovão

A gestação é marcada por alterações fisiológicas e metabólicas que aumentam as necessidades nutricionais maternas e tornam a qualidade da alimentação relevante para a saúde materno\-fetal\. Nesse contexto, o consumo de alimentos ultraprocessados \(AUP\) tem sido investigado em razão de sua associação com a qualidade da dieta e com diferentes desfechos gestacionais\. Objetivo: analisar as evidências científicas publicadas entre 2022 e 2025 sobre a relação entre o consumo de AUP durante a gestação, a qualidade da alimentação materna e os principais desfechos gestacionais, subsidiando a elaboração de uma cartilha educativa para gestantes\. Metodologia: realizou\-se revisão bibliográfica, descritiva e qualitativa, com buscas nas bases PubMed e SciELO e busca complementar no Google Acadêmico\. Foram considerados estudos publicados entre 2022 e 2025, disponíveis em texto completo e relacionados ao consumo de AUP durante a gestação, à qualidade da alimentação materna e/ou aos desfechos gestacionais\. Os estudos selecionados foram analisados de forma descritiva e comparativa quanto ao delineamento, população, consumo de AUP e principais achados\. Resultados: estudos brasileiros identificaram participação relevante dos AUP na ingestão energética de gestantes, com associações entre maior consumo e menor ingestão de nutrientes e de alimentos in natura ou minimamente processados\. Revisões sistemáticas e metanálises também identificaram associações entre maior consumo de AUP e ganho de peso gestacional, diabetes mellitus gestacional e pré\-eclâmpsia, embora com heterogeneidade e, em parte, baixa certeza da evidência\. A partir da síntese, foi estruturada uma cartilha educativa sobre classificação dos alimentos, leitura de rótulos e substituições alimentares\. Conclusão: a literatura recente indica associação entre maior participação de AUP e menor qualidade da alimentação materna, além de associações com alguns desfechos gestacionais\. Entretanto, a predominância de estudos observacionais não permite estabelecer causalidade\. A cartilha constitui produto educativo potencialmente útil para apoiar ações de educação alimentar e nutricional no pré\-natal\.

## [Hybrid machine learning: lasso and random forests](../publications/12746da71f2a38f40017.md)

Guoyi Zhang; John R\. Pleis

This research investigates a hybrid machine learning approach that combines Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator \(LASSO\) with Random Forests to solve regression problems\. LASSO is employed to capture the primary relationship between the response variable and independent variables, while Random Forests are harnessed to capture both nonlinear relationships and noise components within the data\. Additionally, we investigate the impact of incorporating second\-order LASSO with Random Forests into the regression framework\. To evaluate the efficacy of our hybrid methods, we conduct a comprehensive comparative analysis against traditional LASSO, Random Forests, and Local Linear Random Forests \(LLF\) using five benchmark datasets from the existing literature\. Remarkably, our proposed methods exhibit substantial enhancements in predictive accuracy, except under high\-noise conditions\. Furthermore, this study explores the implications of varying noise levels and redundant predictor variables for prediction errors, underscoring the robustness of our proposed methods in effectively managing redundancy in the presence of noise\. The proposed methods are applied to address research questions using the Research and Development Survey, conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention\.

## [Estimated glucose disposal rate is associated with continuous glucose monitoring metrics in type 1 diabetes](../publications/127fdd387772b84fe3f8.md)

Andreea Herascu; Vlad\-Florian Avram; Laura Gaiţă; Adina Braha; Anamaria Cipu; Bogdan Timar

Abstract Estimated glucose disposal rate \(eGDR\) is a composite surrogate of insulin sensitivity in type 1 diabetes \(T1D\) that incorporates HbA1c, creating potential construct overlap when associations with continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\)\-derived metrics are examined\. In this cross\-sectional study of 64 adults with T1D, we evaluated eGDR–CGM associations and the contribution of the HbA1c component, using component\-wise analysis as the primary interpretive approach\. In conventional models adjusted for age, diabetes duration, and insulin delivery method, higher eGDR was associated with higher time in range \(TIR\), lower time above range \(TAR\), lower mean glucose, and lower glucose standard deviation \(SD\) and coefficient of variation \(CV\)\. However, after additional adjustment for HbA1c, eGDR was no longer associated with TIR, TAR, or mean glucose\. Nominal associations remained with CV \(β=−0\.86% points, p = 0\.043\) and SD \(β=−1\.85 mg/dL, p = 0\.031\), but neither survived false\-discovery\-rate correction\. In exploratory HbA1c\-independent sensitivity analyses, higher CACTI estimated insulin sensitivity \(eIS\) was nominally associated with lower CV \(β=−1\.06% points, 95% CI − 1\.97 to − 0\.16; p = 0\.0217; FDR q = 0\.065\) and lower SD \(β=−2\.72 mg/dL, 95% CI − 4\.79 to − 0\.65; p = 0\.0109; q = 0\.065\); neither association survived FDR correction\. Adjustment of the eGDR–SD model for mean glucose attenuated but did not eliminate the association, whereas simultaneous adjustment for HbA1c rendered it non\-significant \(β=−1\.38 mg/dL, 95% CI − 2\.79 to 0\.02; p = 0\.054\)\. No association with TBR was observed \(Spearman ρ=−0\.056, p = 0\.661\)\. TIR &gt; 70% was achieved by 24/64 participants\. eGDR showed modest within\-sample discrimination \(AUC 0\.704, 95% CI 0\.562–0\.829\), whereas HbA1c alone had an AUC of 0\.865 \(95% CI 0\.769–0\.939\)\. The associations with TIR, TAR, and mean glucose were largely attributable to shared HbA1c\. The nominal variability associations did not survive FDR correction and remain exploratory\.

## [Kunstig intelligens i regnskapsførerutdanningen: sovepute eller læringsverktøy?](../publications/128755e0fc28ed3f3409.md)

Marianne Berggaard Breili; Tonny Stenheim; Sinem Acar\-Burkay; Åsmund Pettersen

Generativ kunstig intelligens \(KI\) utfordrer etablerte forutsetninger for undervisning, vurdering og utvikling av kritisk refleksjon og profesjonell dømmekraft i regnskapsførerutdanningen\. Samtidig endres regnskapsførerrollen i retning av mer analyse, kontroll, rådgivning og profesjonell skjønnsutøvelse\. Denne artikkelen undersøker hvordan regnskapsførerstudenter bruker KI i læringsarbeidet, og hvordan undervisningen kan utformes for å styrke kritisk refleksjon og profesjonell dømmekraft\. Studien bygger på en kvalitativ casestudie av en studentgruppe i regnskapsførerspesialiseringen\. Datagrunnlaget består av studentenes refleksjonsnotater, arbeidskrav og observasjoner fra undervisningen\. Funnene viser at KI brukes aktivt som støtteverktøy, særlig til forklaringer, strukturering og idéutvikling, men at studentene erfarer betydelige risikoer knyttet til feilaktige kilder og svekket faglig forståelse\. Artikkelen argumenterer for at læringseffekten av KI avhenger av pedagogisk design\. Når KI\-bruk gjøres eksplisitt, dokumenteres og underlegges faglig kildekontroll, kan teknologien støtte utviklingen av kritisk refleksjon\. Uten slike rammer kan KI fungere som en kognitiv sovepute\. English abstract Artificial Intelligence in Accounting Education: Crutch or Educational Tool? Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) challenges established premises for teaching, assessment, and the development of critical thinking and professional judgment in accounting education\. At the same time, the role of the accountant is shifting towards greater emphasis on analysis, control, advisory work, and professional judgment\. This article examines how accounting students use AI in their learning processes, and how teaching can be designed to strengthen critical reflection and professional judgment\. The study is based on a qualitative case study of one student group in an accounting specialization\. The empirical data consists of students’ reflection notes, compulsory assignments, and classroom observations\. The findings show that accounting students use AI actively as a support tool, particularly for obtaining explanations, structuring their work, and idea development\. However, students also experience significant risks related to inaccurate sources and weakened subject\-matter understanding\. The article argues that the learning effects of AI depend on pedagogical design\. When AI use is made explicit, documented, and subjected to discipline\-specific source verification, the technology can support critical reflection\. Without such structures, AI may function as an inferior substitute for critical thinking and reflection\.

## [Genotype distribution and identification of rare variants in α/β\-thalassemia in chengdu: including the first report of HBA1:c\.300\+48C &gt; G](../publications/128a55de194672d2092b.md)

刘晓华; Hongfei Du; Linyan Zhang; Yang Yu; Guixiang Wang; Xing He; Huacui Huang; Ying Xu

Objective Thalassemia is among the most common inherited diseases worldwide\. We aimed to analyze the genotype and frequency distribution of thalassemia in a general hospital in Chengdu and provide a reference for genetic counseling and prenatal diagnosis\. Methods A total of 6,357 subjects referred to Xindu District People’s Hospital of Chengdu for thalassemia screening between June 2021 and December 2025 were collected\. Thalassemia genotypes were tested using polymerase chain reaction \(PCR\), flow\-through hybridization technology and Sanger sequencing analyses\. Results A total of 793 subjects heterozygous or homozygous for alpha/beta\-globin mutations were detected from 6,357 blood samples, including 480 α\-thalassemia variants, 291 β\-thalassemia variants, and 22 cases with concurrent α and β\-thalassemia variants\. One novel variant, HBA1:c\.300 \+ 48C &gt; G, and was not detected in the IthaGenes, HbVar, dbSNP, Pubmed, and HGMD databases\. Conclusion The genotype distribution of thalassemia in a general hospital in Chengdu is complex and heterogeneous\. The novel HBA1 variant was identified in a patient with severe anemia; however, its functional impact and clinical significance require further investigation\.

## [La inteligencia artificial como estrategia empresarial de innovación y competitividad en las MIPYMES del corregimiento de Canto del Llano, Santiago de Veraguas](../publications/12afb74189615eca94de.md)

Antonio Alejandro Pérez Martínez; William Avatt Donoso Olave

The objective of this study was to assess the extent to which artificial intelligence \(AI\) can serve as a business strategy aimed at promoting innovation and competitiveness among MSMEs in the Canto del Llano district\. A quantitative approach was used, employing a non\-experimental, cross\-sectional design with a descriptive\-correlational focus\. The population consisted of 214 active formal businesses, of which 139 were included in the sample; non\-probabilistic convenience sampling was employed\. The instrument was a structured questionnaire using a Likert scale, validated by experts with a coefficient of 0\.985 and a Cronbach’s alpha of 0\.985\. Statistical analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel and SPSS 26\.0\. The main results reveal that 61\.1% of business owners admit to having limited knowledge of AI, and only 8\.3% use it in their operations; however, more than 80% recognize its potential\. Hypothesis testing showed that perceptions of the potential impact of AI are significantly higher than the neutral point on the scale \(value = 3\), with test values of t = 2\.167 and p = 0\.032\. It is concluded that, although actual adoption is still in its early stages, there is a widespread positive perception toward the incorporation of AI, contingent upon the availability of training, technological resources, and institutional support\. The findings provide the first set of systematized empirical evidence on AI adoption in MSMEs in this district, with implications for the design of business digitalization policies in the region\.
