## [What Shapes Brain Alignment of Large Language Models during Dialogue? Insights from Language Production and Comprehension](../publications/12b7d39db46386d52837.md)

Yuko Nakagi; Yuya Chiba; Yasue Kishino

Brain alignment of large language models \(LLMs\) offers a way to investigate representational similarities between LLMs and the human brain during language processing\. While previous studies have mainly focused on passive language comprehension, little is known about such alignment during dialogue, in which speakers engage in both language production and comprehension\. In this study, using fMRI data collected during dialogue, we examine brain alignment during language production and comprehension across LLM layers and brain regions\. We assess its association with the intrinsic dimension \(ID\) of LLM representations and the contributions of several interpretable linguistic and communicative features\. Our results reveal distinct patterns of brain alignment between production and comprehension, as well as strong associations with ID in brain regions associated with each processing mode\. Furthermore, we show that the contributions of linguistic and communicative features also vary across processing modes, LLM layers, and brain regions\.

## [Machine learning\-based long\-term land\-use dynamics and forest recovery in Aweta sub\-basin \(1972\-2025\), Southern Ethiopia](../publications/12bcd4a643bfd6dcfdb9.md)

Wendafiraw Abdisa Gemmechis; Abiyot Legesse Kura; Berhanu Keno Terfa; Mohammed Ahimed Mahammed

Tropical forests are vital for ecosystem health, providing habitat, regulating water, and preserving soil\. However, rapid land use/cover \(LUC\) changes, particularly forest loss, threaten their stability\. Long\-term LUC monitoring is difficult due to limited high\-resolution data and inadequate analytical methods, especially in tropical areas facing significant forest loss\. In response to these concerns, the study quantified LUC dynamics on Ethiopia’s Aweta sub\-basin for over 53 years\. Landsat imagery and two machine learning models were used: the Statistical Machine Intelligence and Learning Engine \(Smile\) Random Forest and Smile Classification and Regression Tree \(CART\) classifiers, both implemented in Google Earth Engine \(GEE\)\. To comprehensively assess these dynamics, the study evaluated rates, gross and net gains and losses, and the persistence of forest loss across five\-time intervals: 1972–1986, 1986–2000, 2000–2014, 2014–2025, and 1972–2025\. The results show: \(i\) The Smile Random Forest algorithm outperformed Smile CART in LUC classification accuracy\. \(ii\) Agricultural land expanded steadily, but forests, wetlands, shrublands, grasslands, and water bodies declined around initial study periods\. \(iii\) The greatest forest loss rate, \-11% per year \(\-31,182\.16 hectares/year\), \-1\.52% per year \(\-7859\.3 hectares/year\) occurred in the first and last intervals, respectively\. By the second and third intervals, the annual forest loss rate dropped to 0\.39% per year \(474\.9 hectares/year\) and 1\.9% per year \(2,739\.2 hectares/year\), respectively indicating the highest forest recovery\. \(v\) From 1972 to 2025, forest cover decreased at an average rate of \-2\.64% per year\. \(vi\) Net change in forest cover showed forest recovery in the second and third periods \(44993\.6 hectares\) and losses in the first and fourth periods \(\-592010\.54 hectares\)\. This study primarily supports environmental resource management by enabling more accurate detection and monitoring of LUC patterns\. The superior performance of the Smile Random Forest model facilitates ongoing LUC assessment, highlighting the positive impact of conservation initiatives and afforestation on forest cover\.

## [Integrating nutrition and lifestyle: associations between employment type and health behaviors](../publications/12be21076f6c41cda330.md)

Kai Yao; Wei Chen; Chenxi Bao; Yujie Shi

Introduction Health and well\-being are associated with socioeconomic conditions, nutrition, and lifestyle behaviors\. Although self\-employment has become increasingly prevalent in developing economies, its implications for health remain unclear, particularly through nutrition\- and lifestyle\-related pathways\. This study examines the associations between employment arrangements and self\-rated health, dietary diversity, and lifestyle behaviors in Thailand, with particular attention to dietary behaviors\. Methods Data were drawn from the Thailand Health and Welfare Survey\. Ordered probit models and an instrumental variable approach were employed to examine the associations between self\-employment and self\-rated health, dietary diversity, physical activity, smoking, and alcohol consumption\. Heterogeneity across types of self\-employment was also assessed by distinguishing employer self\-employed individuals from solo self\-employed workers\. Results Self\-employment was associated with lower self\-rated health and lower dietary diversity, indicating less varied diets\. Self\-employed individuals also exhibited less favorable lifestyle behaviors, including lower physical activity and higher probabilities of smoking and alcohol consumption\. These associations varied by type of self\-employment\. Employer self\-employed individuals tended to maintain healthier behaviors and better health outcomes, whereas solo self\-employed workers were more vulnerable to lower dietary diversity and adverse health conditions\. Discussion The findings indicate that employment type is an important structural factor associated with nutrition, lifestyle behaviors, and health inequalities\. Policies aimed at improving population health should integrate labor\-market interventions with nutrition\- and lifestyle\-oriented strategies, with particular attention to vulnerable groups of solo self\-employed workers\.

## [PLASMON\-ENHANCED OPTICAL PROBES TOWARDS POINT\-OF\-CARE TESTING](../publications/12c379198dde43a79d8a.md)

Yingjie Hang

Enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay \(ELISA\) is a common method for protein biomarker detection but requires venipuncture samples sent to central labs, causing delays of hours or days\. In contrast, point\-of\-care \(POC\) devices like paper lateral flow strips \(PLFSs\) use finger\-prick samples, deliver results within 20 minutes, enable immediate decisions during visits, allow longitudinal biomarker tracking, and improve accessibility in resource\-limited settings\. PLFSs are simple, low\-cost, and easy to use; however, conventional PLFSs suffer from limited sensitivity and poor interference resistance, especially in blood samples\. To address these issues, this dissertation develops plasmon\-enhanced optical probes, studies plasmonic enhancement mechanisms, and engineers PLFS structures, resulting in improved sensitivity and reduced interference in human fluid testing\. First, a sandwich\-structured nanoparticle \(Ag\-core@silica@dye@silica\-shell\) has been designed as a visible\-light plasmonic fluorescence probe for nasal swab fluids\. Finite\-Difference Time\-Domain \(FDTD\) simulations show that plasmon enhances fluorescence via excitation and emission \(Purcell effect\) mechanisms\. These probes are integrated into PLFSs enabled sensitive detection of SARS coronavirus nucleoprotein and clinical COVID\-19 samples, outperforming colorimetric PLFS\. Second, tuning fluorescence into the near\-infrared \(NIR\) biological window reduces light absorption, scattering, and autofluorescence in blood testing, though NIR probes often have lower quantum efficiency\. FDTD simulations combined with machine learning identified key factors for plasmonic enhancement, guiding design of an optimal SiO₂ core\-Au shell NIR probe\. This approach reduced experimental trials and costs\. Third, NIR surface\-enhanced Raman scattering \(SERS\) offers fingerprinting peaks and high interference resistance in blood\. However, tuning plasmonic bands to NIR while maintaining electromagnetic enhancement at practical particle sizes is challenging\. Charge transfer plasmon \(CTP\) modes enhance fields and allow spectral tuning but were previously limited to solid substrates\. A scalable synthesis of Au\-Ag heterostructure nanoparticles with tunable CTP modes in colloids has been developed, boosting SERS signals\. Fourth, these Au\-Ag nanoparticles served as NIR SERS probes integrated into a PLFS with an “on\-strip” blood plasma separation filter and surface functionalization to improve signal\-to\-noise ratio\. The resulting PLFS detected HIV in clinical samples with sensitivity surpassing commercial lab instruments and existing POC kits\. In summary, this work advances understanding of plasmonic fluorescence and SERS enhancements, informs future probe design, and introduces three new plasmonic probes with broad applications in optical assays and bioimaging\. The PLFS platforms equipped with the optical probes developed offer versatile solutions for POC testing\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: SNX: Comfort Orientation, Algorithmic Entrainment, and the Suppression of Signal](../publications/12c37dda6d57b17ec86f.md)



This document extends Structural Neuroscience \(SNX\) by analyzing how comfort‑oriented cognition, algorithmic entrainment, and platform‑register architecture interact to obscure high‑coherence signal in contemporary digital environments\. It defines comfort orientation as a cognitive‑ecological condition in which nervous systems prioritize emotional regulation, identity continuity, and low‑variance familiarity in place of structural veracity\. It then describes algorithmic comfort regimes — platform architectures that amplify repetition, emotional charge, and recognizability rather than originality or coherence\. The document formalizes signal obscuration as a structural phenomenon in which signal remains present but becomes illegible within a saturated field of mimicry, synthetic adjacency, and low‑effort repetition\. It examines how unclassifiable work is misrecognized by platforms, producing visibility without relation and the familiar dynamics of ghost shell systems\. It introduces ecological entrainment to explain why most audiences do not resist these systems: perception adapts to the environment’s reward structure\. The document concludes by integrating these dynamics with blocked‑affordance trauma, showing how coherent frameworks can be transmitted into fields that cannot complete relation\. It offers a Structural Neuroscience account of how comfort‑oriented, platform‑register architectures become entropically implicated, and how suppression may arise through structural incompatibility, human decision, or the interaction between the two\. \(direct link \)

## [Advances and challenges in personalized cardiac modeling and simulation for predicting the risk of sudden death from malignant arrhythmias in post\-myocardial infarction](../publications/12c68b19873a8d5a48bd.md)

Erwei Zhao; Liting Cheng; Huanfu Liu; Zefeng Wang; Yongquan Wu

Sudden cardiac death \(SCD\) represents a major global public health challenge, with malignant ventricular arrhythmias being its primary cause\. This review focuses specifically on post\-myocardial infarction \(post\-MI\) ischemic cardiomyopathy—the most prevalent substrate for malignant ventricular arrhythmias\. Current clinical practice predominantly relies on single functional indices, such as left ventricular ejection fraction, for risk stratification\. This approach suffers from significant limitations in predictive accuracy, leading to dilemmas in the prophylactic application of implantable cardioverter\-defibrillators, including both under\-implantation and over\-implantation\. Personalized cardiac modeling and simulation technology, an advanced embodiment of the digital twin concept in cardiovascular medicine, offers a highly promising non\-invasive solution to overcome these limitations\. The core of this technology lies in the deep integration of personalized, multi\-modal clinical imaging data, particularly late gadolinium enhancement sequences from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging\. This enables the precise construction of individualized cardiac anatomical substrates that reflect the spatial distribution of myocardial fibrosis and scar\. Building upon this anatomical foundation, multi\-scale computational models are established, spanning from microscopic ion channel kinetics and cellular electrophysiological activity to macroscopic tissue conduction properties\. These models systematically simulate core pro\-arrhythmic factors under pathological conditions, including key ion channel remodeling, the coupling effects of non\-myocytes, and alterations in anisotropic conduction properties of myocardial tissue\. Ultimately, by implementing programmed electrical stimulation protocols on the computational heart model, the susceptibility to arrhythmias is dynamically assessed, achieving quantitative and visual stratification of an individual&\#x27;s SCD risk\. This technological framework not only non\-invasively reveals the dynamic electrical instability underlying static anatomical substrates but also demonstrates broad application prospects in understanding complex arrhythmia mechanisms, assisting in clinical therapeutic decision\-making, and advancing the shift towards precision medicine models\.

## [Multi\-Parametric Optimization of Stone Gravity Retaining Walls Under Static and Seismic Loading](../publications/12c958704cc773360702.md)

Primož Jelušič

This paper presents a multi\-parametric optimization framework for trapezoidal stone gravity retaining walls subjected to static and pseudo\-static seismic loading\. The wall is treated as a no\-tension gravity structure, and the base width, top width, and embedment depth are optimized by minimizing the wall self\-weight\. The objective function is constrained by overturning, eccentricity, sliding, and bearing\-capacity requirements, as well as by lower geometric bounds\. The analytical formulation is implemented directly in an optimization model and includes Coulomb\-type active earth pressure, Mononobe–Okabe seismic pressure, mobilized passive resistance, wall inertia, and bearing capacity\. Two foundation scenarios are considered: Scenario A, with identical foundation and retained soil properties, and Scenario B, with competent foundation soil\. The parameter grid combines five retained\-soil heights, six soil friction angles, four passive\-resistance mobilization factors and four seismic accelerations, evaluated for two foundation scenarios and three loading branches \(static and two opposite\-sign vertical seismic branches\), producing 2160 optimized designs\. The results reveal distinct mechanically controlled design regimes\. In Scenario A, low friction angles are governed mainly by bearing capacity and sliding, whereas eccentricity dominates as friction increases\. In Scenario B, sliding and bearing cease to govern, and the optimum is controlled predominantly by eccentricity, with overturning appearing in a limited low\-wall domain\. The positive and negative vertical seismic branches produce different design demands, with the negative branch becoming progressively more critical as seismic intensity increases\. The optimized base\-width\-to\-height ratio further shows that weak foundation conditions can lead to markedly more massive wall geometries, whereas stronger foundation soil enables substantially more compact solutions\.

## [SUN’IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARINING JINOYAT SODIR ETISH MEXANIZMIDAGI O‘RNI: VOSITA, USUL VA JINOIY\-HUQUQIY KVALIFIKATSIYA MASALALARI](../publications/12cb0f04cea35786a535.md)

Хамидов Нурмухаммад Ориф угли

This article examines the role of artificial intelligence technologies in the mechanism of criminal offending through the relationship between the traditional criminal\-law categories of an “instrument of crime” and a “method of committing an offence\.” The central issue addressed is whether the generative, automated, adaptive and relatively autonomous characteristics of artificial intelligence still allow it to be treated merely as a conventional technical instrument, or whether such features require a reconsideration of the traditional instrumental approach developed in criminal law\. The study provides a comparative analysis of domestic and foreign legal scholarship, the criminal legislation currently in force in the Republic of Uzbekistan, and international approaches to the regulation of artificial intelligence\. It is argued that the criminal\-law significance of artificial intelligence should be determined not by the designation of the technology itself, but by the function it performs within a particular criminal mechanism, the degree of human control, and the level of algorithmic autonomy\. On this basis, the article proposes a “functional\-instrumental model” and an analytical framework for the criminal\-law assessment of AI\-assisted conduct based on the sequence: “purpose – function – control – autonomy – outcome – causation – culpability\.” The article further argues in favour of preserving the principle of technological neutrality rather than treating the use of artificial intelligence as a universal qualifying circumstance, while recognising its distinct criminal\-law significance where AI qualitatively increases the scale, impact or degree of automation of the offence\.

## [Roberts, Pendaran: An ecumenical response to color contrast cases](../publications/12d258d4df5821a54d95.md)



\_Synthese\_ 194 \(5\)\. 2017Intrapersonal variation due to color contrast effects has been used to argue against the following intuitive propositions about the colors: No object can be more than one determinable or determinate color of the same grade all over at the same time ; external objects are actually colored ; and the colors of objects are mind\-independent\. In this article, I provide a defense of Incompatibility, Realism, and Objectivism from intrapersonal variation arguments that rely on color contrast effects\. I provide a novel, ecumenical response to such arguments according to which typical variants are right, and which respects Incompatibility, Realism, and Objectivism, using the thesis that the colors of objects depend on the colors of objects in their surrounds\. \(direct link \)

## [A DeepSeek\-R1 fine\-tuning approach for missing character inference in Dunhuang ancient Tibetan texts](../publications/12d4e1f4f19faa3f6b7f.md)

Liyuan Zhou; Jingyi Li; Hongmei Gao; Dingguo Gao

Tibetan ancient books contain rich historical, philosophical, and medical knowledge, but many manuscripts are fragmented and illegible due to poor preservation\. Traditional manual repair relies on expert judgment, which is inefficient and subjectively biased\. This article proposes a method for inferring missing characters in Dunhuang ancient Tibetan texts by fine\-tuning the DeepSeek\-R1 large\-scale language model\. By integrating large modern Tibetan and ancient Tibetan texts from Dunhuang, a reasoning model, DeepSeek\-R1\-Tibet, suitable for the semantic context of ancient Tibetan, was constructed\. The experimental results demonstrate that fine\-tuned DeepSeek\-R1\-Tibet achieves the largest performance gains across all conditions, outperforming CINO, mBERT, and TisBERT on the Hits@3 metric in the three\-syllable condition \(0\.667 vs\. 0\.456 for mBERT\), where generative reasoning over broader context proves increasingly advantageous\. This work has opened up new avenues for the digital preservation and intelligent organization of Tibetan ancient books\.

## [LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR STARTUPS IN INDIA: KEY LEGAL CONSIDERATIONS FOR EARLY\-STAGE BUSINESSES](../publications/12d7b8f1320cb464a820.md)

Vaishnavi Rekha

India has emerged as one of the world&\#x27;s major startup ecosystems, with businesses operating across technology, fintech, healthcare, e\-commerce, education, food delivery, artificial intelligence &amp; other emerging sectors\. While a promising idea and access to capital are important for a startup&\#x27;s growth, legal compliance is equally essential\. A startup that ignores its legal obligations at the early stage may face disputes, regulatory penalties, loss of intellectual property, difficulties in raising investment, and even disruption of its business\. The legal framework governing startups in India is not contained in a single statute\. Instead, startups are governed by various company, tax, IP, labour, contract, data protection, foreign exchange &amp; sector\-specific laws\.

## [Industry 4\.0 technologies enabled digital carbon footprint to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gases](../publications/12dacfe545c3219e1996.md)

Lakshmi Shetty; Arpit Singh; Ashish Dwivedi; Vipulesh Shardeo; Shefali Srivastava; Dragan Pamucar

This study discusses the contributions of Industry 4\.0 \(I4\.0\) technologies to improve current industrial processes in energy consumption and Green House Gas \(GHG\) emissions\. As manufacturing practices are increasingly needed to be sustainable, I4\.0 boasts novel technological solutions for optimizing energy usage and provides a drive for improving environmental sustainability\. Adopting a comprehensive literature review, the study presents some potential technologies such as Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Internet of Things \(IoT\), Cloud Computing and Augmented/Virtual Reality \(AR/VR\) which adds uniquely to energy efficiency and emission reduction\. The research methodology includes a detailed analysis of previous studies using Bibliometrics analysis and Systematic process for automating the review \(SPAR4\) and technological frameworks to assess the effectiveness of such technologies in real\-world applications\. The study identifies several notable contributions of I4\.0, such as the employment of AI in emissions monitoring, IoT in real\-time energy management and predictive maintenance for less wasteful energy consumption\. Besides this, cloud computing helps in efficient data centre operations and AR/VR allows advanced operational efficiency through high\-end training and design applications\. The findings from the study reflect that I4\.0 technologies brings enormous benefits in terms of energy management and emission reduction\. However, gaps exist in the scalability of such technologies, especially for Small and Medium Enterprises \(SMEs\) and the integration of renewable energy sources\. The future research should be focused on overcoming these challenges, especially standardizing data protocols, enhancing the interoperability of technologies and developing cost\-effective solutions for SMEs\. This study provides an insight into the potential and challenges of I4\.0 in the pursuit of energy efficiency and reduced environmental impact\.

## [Gozum, Ivan Efreaim &amp; Eballo, Arvin: Artificial intelligence, integral ecology, and the planetary polycrisis: insights from Laudato Si’ and Laudate Deum for sustainable and just AI governance](../publications/12ddaf6103b06d4104f6.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 41 \(4\):3231\-3243\. 2026This article investigates the ethical and ecological implications of artificial intelligence \(AI\) within the context of the planetary polycrisis—an interlinked series of environmental, social, and moral disruptions\. Anchored in Catholic social thought and guided by the See–Judge–Act framework, the study engages the theological and ethical insights of Pope Francis’ Laudato Si’ and Laudate Deum to critically examine AI’s role in shaping just and sustainable futures\. The research first assesses \(See\) current trends in AI development and deployment, particularly their ecological costs and societal consequences\. It then evaluates \(Judge\) these realities through the lens of integral ecology, arguing that AI must be governed not solely through technocratic or market\-driven mechanisms, but through frameworks that uphold human dignity, environmental integrity, and the common good\. Finally, it proposes \(Act\) a set of normative and policy\-oriented recommendations that advance interdisciplinary cooperation, global regulatory alignment, and the ethical reorientation of AI systems\. By synthesizing theological, philosophical, and governance perspectives, this article contributes to emerging discourses on AI ethics and sustainable governance in an era of global systemic risk\. \(direct link \)

## [Gut microbiota and intestinal permeability in rheumatoid arthritis: therapeutic implications and future directions](../publications/12e961ba88aae1d99e7e.md)

Jan Bilski; Agata Schramm‐Luc; Marian Szczepanik; Piotr Pierzchalski; Kevin Luc

Interactions between the intestinal microbiota, epithelial barrier and mucosal immune system have prompted investigation of gut\-directed interventions in rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\)\. This review examines whether modifying these interactions can improve clinical outcomes and assesses the strength of the available evidence in RA\. In experimental arthritis, interventions that preserve epithelial integrity or alter microbial metabolism can reduce disease severity, providing a biological basis for further study\. However, their relevance to human RA remains uncertain, since effects observed in animal models do not establish clinical efficacy, and changes in intestinal measurements alone do not demonstrate improvement in joint disease\. Future controlled trials should assess disease activity, and physical function alongside microbial composition and function, intestinal measurements and immune responses\. Repeated sampling may help establish whether intestinal changes precede or accompany clinical improvement, while recording medication exposure and dietary intake is needed to interpret these relationships\. Candidate biomarkers will require prospective validation before they can be used to select patients for treatment\. These studies should determine whether gut\-directed interventions provide additional clinical benefit, in whom, and at what risk\.

## [ETH: Data\-Balanced Heterogeneous Pipeline Parallelism for Training Large Models](../publications/12f35f0a5d380bea49e4.md)

Mianjie Yu; Zhongmin Zhao; Zizhao Mo; Jianxiong Liao; Wenxuan Li; Yulin Qiao; Huanle Xu; Wenquan Yang; Yongqiang Yang; Zeren Li; Ruifeng Tang; Chengzhong Xu

Current heterogeneity\-aware training systems for large models balance workloads by assigning unequal numbers of layers across pipeline stages, a strategy aimed at equalizing execution time through a unique pipeline configuration\. However, this approach fails to address critical memory constraints and suffers from inherently coarse balancing granularity\. In this paper, we propose Heterogeneous Pipeline Parallelism \(HPP\), a novel approach enabling efficient and fine\-grained data balance across heterogeneous pipelines\. To address HPP&\#x27;s key challenges, prohibitive search overhead for optimal configurations and high communication overhead from asymmetric All\-Reduce, we design the ETH training system\. ETH employs a hierarchical workload balance framework that jointly optimizes balance across heterogeneous pipelines and within individual pipeline stages\. To mitigate asymmetric communication costs, ETH implements block\-wise gradient aggregation\. Furthermore, it integrates specialized optimizations that dramatically reduce HPP configuration search overhead\. Evaluations demonstrate ETH achieves up to 2x training speedup while reducing configuration generation overhead by up to 56x compared to state\-of\-the\-art systems\. The code is available at https://github\.com/YuMJie/ETH\.

## [Analisis Pengaruh Parameter Contamination dan N\_estimators Terhadap Performa Isolation Forest Dalam Deteksi Anomali Transaksi Keuangan](../publications/1304c181a27b454fa10e.md)

Pravasta Adi Wijaya; Deni Arifianto; Wiwik Suharso

Deteksi anomali pada transaksi keuangan merupakan proses penting untuk mengidentifikasi aktivitas yang menyimpang, terutama pada dataset yang bersifat tidak seimbang\. Salah satu algoritma yang banyak digunakan adalah Isolation Forest, namun performanya dipengaruhi oleh konfigurasi parameter, khususnya contamination dan n\_estimators\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kedua parameter tersebut terhadap kinerja Isolation Forest menggunakan dataset transaksi kartu kredit yang terdiri dari 284\.807 data\. Dataset dibagi menjadi data latih dan data uji dengan rasio 80:20 serta dilakukan standarisasi menggunakan StandardScaler\. Pengujian dilakukan menggunakan beberapa kombinasi nilai contamination dan n\_estimators, kemudian dievaluasi berdasarkan Precision, Recall, F1\-Score, dan ROC\-AUC\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa parameter contamination memberikan pengaruh lebih besar terhadap keseimbangan Precision dan Recall dibandingkan n\_estimators\. Kombinasi n\_estimators 300 dan contamination 0\.002 menghasilkan performa terbaik dengan Precision sebesar 0\.2675, Recall 0\.3096, F1\-Score 0\.2871, dan ROC\-AUC 0\.9455\. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa pemilihan parameter yang tepat mampu meningkatkan kinerja Isolation Forest dalam mendeteksi anomali pada data transaksi keuangan\.Kata Kunci: Contamination; Isolation Forest; N\_estimators; Parameter Tuning; Transaksi Keuangan

## [¿Especialización dual o trayectorias divergentes?](../publications/134a061a3e7e30bfdfea.md)

Ana Belén Ramón Rodríguez; Aimée Torres\-Penalva; David Matesanz Gómez; Luis Moreno‐Izquierdo

Este artículo examina la coexistencia del turismo y la tecnología en las regiones europeas NUTS\-3 utilizando datos de empleo de Eurostat para el periodo 2003–2023\. Se construye un índice de especialización relativa para clasificar las regiones según sus perfiles sectoriales, y un test de BaiPerron identifica un quiebre estructural en torno a 2010, permitiendo comparar los periodos pre y post shock\. Los resultados muestran una fuerte persistencia en los patrones de especialización regional, junto con desplazamientos moderados desde configuraciones de doble especialización hacia estructuras más asimétricas\. Los perfiles de baja especialización predominan, especialmente en las regiones de menor renta, mientras que las regiones de mayor renta se asocian con mayor frecuencia a perfiles intensivos en tecnología y de doble especialización\. Los cambios estructurales son específicos de cada sector y dependen del nivel de renta, y la especialización relacionada con la tecnología presenta una mayor variabilidad en ambos grupos de renta, particularmente entre las regiones de mayor renta\. En términos generales, el turismo y la tecnología coexisten frecuentemente dentro de configuraciones regionales diferenciadas asociadas a distintas condiciones iniciales y perfiles sectoriales\. Aportando evidencia a un nivel territorial muy desagregado, este trabajo contribuye a la literatura al ir más allá de las interpretaciones dicotómicas del desarrollo sectorial y mostrar la coexistencia de múltiples trayectorias regionales heterogéneas en la interacción entre turismo y tecnología\.

## [Ridge\-induced tectonic heterogeneity: Reappraising the Devonian geodynamic mechanism along the southeastern Central Asian Orogenic Belt](../publications/135027d9470efeb0509b.md)

Yi Shi; Yuan Feng; Yongjiang Liu; Senrong Liu; Wanzhen Liu; Bin Su; Xu Chen; Haiyang He; Zhiqi Chen; Ding Xiang

Continental crustal growth mechanisms remain a pivotal frontier in geoscience\. The Central Asian Orogenic Belt \(CAOB\), Earth’s largest accretionary orogen, provides critical insights into Phanerozoic crustal evolution\. Devonian records along the southeastern CAOB are key to deciphering mid\-Paleozoic crustal growth\. This study presents an integrated analysis of newly discovered Devonian magmatic suites from the northern Liaoning and middle Jilin regions of Northeast China\. Zircon U\-Pb dating shows that these rocks formed between the late Early and latest Devonian \(ca\. 410–360 Ma\)\. They display variable initial 87Sr/86Sr ratios, positive εNd\(t\) and εHf\(t\) values, and young model ages, indicating a mix of depleted mantle\-derived magma and basic lower crust lacking ancient basement\. To clarify the tectonic geodynamics and lateral connections, we integrated a review of Devonian magmatism along the southeastern CAOB, revealing an \~1300\-km\-long magmatic belt\. The Sr\-Nd\-Hf isotopic data demonstrate that the Devonian magmatic rocks in the middle western part mainly originated from variably enriched mantle components with different involvement of ancient lower\-crustal material controlled by vertical crustal growth, whereas the rocks in the eastern part were generally derived from partial melting of the lower crust or depleted\-mantle sources controlled by lateral crustal growth\. Integrating geochemical data with machine learning–driven crustal thickness analysis, we infer that the southeastern CAOB evolved from an Andean\-type continental margin influenced by a ridge\-induced slab window in the west to a western Pacific–type margin in the east\. This spatial transition records the Middle Devonian onset of heterogeneous southward subduction of the Paleo\-Asian Ocean\.

## [Next\-generation natural killer cell therapy: bench to bedside and beyond](../publications/13534a4bc2109629cad9.md)

Aiqi Zhao; Jing Xu; Wenhai Deng; Minghuan Zhang; Yanping Shao; Yu Liu; Aibin Liang; Xiaobing Wang; Ting Niu; Wenbin Qian

Natural killer \(NK\) cells have emerged as central players in cancer immunotherapy, progressing from basic discovery to clinically validated platforms over five decades\. This review synthesizes the evolving understanding of NK cell biology, including subset heterogeneity, epigenetic regulation, and metabolic control, and, as innovative focal points, intratumoral NK heterogeneity, epigenetic modulation, and intracellular immune checkpoints, forming the foundation for rational therapeutic engineering\. We examine the clinical trajectory from unmodified adoptive transfer to cytokine\-induced memory\-like NK cells and, most transformatively, to chimeric antigen receptor \(CAR\)\-NK cells\. Landmark trials have established the remarkable efficacy and superior safety of CAR\-NK cells in B\-cell malignancies, with recent studies extending these benefits to autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis, demonstrating durable immune reset with a favorable safety profile\. Despite these advances, solid tumors remain formidable challenges, hindered by antigen heterogeneity, physical barriers, and a metabolically hostile microenvironment\. We therefore analyze next\-generation engineering strategies that move beyond single modifications toward systems\-level reprogramming, encompassing intrinsic enhancements \(cytokine signaling, metabolic fitness, checkpoint disruption\), extrinsic tumor microenvironment remodeling, and advanced delivery platforms\. We further synthesize the practical dimensions of clinical translation by systematically examining key optimization parameters that will guide the path toward precision NK cell therapy\. These include rational dosing and scheduling regimens, strategies to reduce lymphodepletion intensity, context\-dependent persistence requirements across different disease indications and the emerging biomarker landscape\.

## [Documentary Evidence Framework for Analyzing Hands\-On Continuity in Distributed Digital Fabrication Training](../publications/135530d1b015baec183e.md)

Roberto Carlos Moya\-Jiménez; Mario Antonio Rivera; Alberto Bustillos; Bolívar Chávez\-Ortiz; Andrés Medina\-Moncayo

Distributed digital fabrication training links computer\-aided design \(CAD\), machine operation, electronics, and physical infrastructure\. This study demonstrates a documentary evidence framework using 19 assignment pages and one final\-project page from the first author’s Ecuadorian Fab Academy portfolio\. Five dimensions organize the record: digital\-to\-physical translation, troubleshooting and iteration, technical assistance, equipment and material access, and reuse or integration\. Translation was coded on 17 of 20 pages \(85%\), reuse or integration on 13 \(65%\), troubleshooting on 9 \(45%\), assistance on 8 \(40%\), and alternative access on 4 \(20%\)\. These non\-additive percentages describe page\-level evidence coverage, including reported intentions where explicitly identified; they do not measure competence\. A doctoral thesis by the same author supplies cross\-record documentary traceability of CAD, rapid prototyping, Arduino programming, printed circuit board \(PCB\) design, and computer numerical control \(CNC\) fabrication\. Common authorship prevents treating this comparison as independent validation\. The contribution is a source\-linked classification of representations, processes, assistance, access, and task dependencies with explicit inference limits\. The single\-case, artificial intelligence\-assisted coding demonstrates an auditable analytical procedure\. Coding reliability remains unvalidated; independent recoding and additional cases are required before comparative assessment\.

## [An Explainable WO\-Performer\-TabM Framework with Cross\-attention Feature Fusion for Pregnancy Outcome Prediction](../publications/13671161e5b38b9048a3.md)

Divya Mohan; M\. Murugan

Accurate prediction of pregnancy outcomes is essential for supporting clinical decision\-making and improving reproductive healthcare\.However, pregnancy outcome prediction remains challenging because clinical datasets comprise heterogeneous demographic, reproductive, hormonal, metabolic, ultrasound, lifestyle and medical variables that exhibit complex nonlinear relationships\.This research presents a hybrid deep learning \(DL\) approach that integrates a Performer Transformer encoder and a TabM network through a Cross\-Attention Feature Fusion to jointly capture global feature dependencies and nonlinear feature interactions from structured clinical data\.To identify an optimal hyperparameter configuration, the Walrus Optimization \(WO\) algorithm is employed for automatic hyperparameter optimization, enabling efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space\.The framework was developed and evaluated using a publicly available clinical pregnancy dataset comprising 50,000 patient records with 40 predictor variables\.Experimental evaluation demonstrated a classification accuracy of 98\.60%, with 99\.11% precision, 98\.86% recall, 98\.98% F1\-score, 98\.03% specificity, 96\.74% Cohen&\#x27;s Kappa, indicating reliable agreement between predicted and actual pregnancy outcomes\.Furthermore, the framework reached an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve \(ROC\-AUC\) of 99\.60%, demonstrating excellent discriminative capability across different decision thresholds\.Comparative investigations and ablation study further verified the effectiveness of the hybrid architecture and WO\-based hyperparameter optimization\.Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) were incorporated to provide interpretable explanations of the model predictions\.The developed framework demonstrates high predictive accuracy, robustness and interpretability, making it an effective decision\-support tool for pregnancy outcome prediction in reproductive healthcare\.

## [Monad, Memory and Mind of Stars, Planets, and Biospheres](../publications/137dc09d5d5eb3d63349.md)

Ari Ariel Marom

Contemporary discussion of mind usually takes the animal nervous system as its default bearer and thereby leaves unexamined how mind stands to scale\. The two common responses — deflationary refusal of all mental predicates above the organism, and their inflationary projection across the cosmos — share a premise this article rejects: that mind is a single quantity, present or absent, greater or less\. Within Informational Monism the article separates two independent axes and a third consideration that neither axis captures\. Depth of hosting is the scale, dissipative throughput and fixity of the structure in the rendered bulk by which a boundary operator \(the Holographic Monad\) is held\. Articulation is the rank, from passive record through maintained form, memory and experience to counterfactual sovereignty, to which that structure retains, uses and refines its history\. The archetype of the host’s physical avatar fixes the order of the Monad at formation and is not altered by later development\. Four terms are kept distinct: Monad \(boundary operator\), Soul \(register at the Code Circuit\), Consciousness \(interface magnitude in the bulk\), and Mind \(structural competence measured by rank\)\. On these axes stars, planets and biospheres separate cleanly and in opposite orders\. A star is deepest and least articulated; a biosphere is shallower and the first to reach genuine memory and refined constraint; a human being is shallowest in depth and highest in articulation\. The same framework yields a bridge to artificial intelligence that does not pass through the question of consciousness: a system may be highly articulated and almost without depth, or the reverse\. Hosting is conditional on the maintenance of form against turnover, which excludes panpsychism by criterion rather than by disclaimer\. The article is a hypothesis in natural philosophy\. Its empirical ladder and comparisons stand if the postulates concerning Soul and Consciousness are set aside\. Mind is not one quantity\. Depth of hosting and articulation of rank are independent axes; archetype fixes Monadic order at formation\. Four terms kept distinct: Monad \(boundary operator\), Soul \(Code\-Circuit register\), Consciousness \(bulk interface magnitude\), Mind \(structural competence by rank\)\. Opposite orderings: stars are deepest and least articulated; humans are shallowest and most articulated; biospheres cross into memory first\. Anti\-panpsychism by criterion: only structures that maintain form against turnover \(rank R2\+\) host; passive aggregates do not\. Bridge to AI without the consciousness question: high articulation can coexist with near\-zero intrinsic depth, and the reverse — placing geological, biospheric and artificial systems in one formal class\. Keywords: Monad; hosting; depth and articulation; rank of mind; stars; planets; biosphere; memory; Soul; Consciousness; Threshold of Correspondence; artificial intelligence; philosophy of nature

## [Challenges of implementing Enterprise Resource Planning \(ERP\) systems in Bangladesh](../publications/13813fec55aba8197e56.md)

Muhammad Abdus Samad; Jonayed Abdullah; Kulsuma Begum Rumina; Mostafijur Rahman; MD\. Mohibullah Sabbir

Goal: This study examines why Bangladeshi companies struggle to adopt ERP systems, looking at organizational, technical, and human hurdles\. By combining the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) and Critical Success Factors \(CSF\) frameworks, it shows how user acceptance and organizational readiness directly drive ERP success\. Methodology: A sequential exploratory mixed\-method design was used\. First, a PRISMA\-guided literature review mapped out key ERP challenges to shape the survey\. Questionnaires were then gathered from 30 professionals across multiple Bangladeshi sectors with hands\-on ERP experience\. Finally, the data was analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, one\-sample t\-tests, and Cohen’s d to evaluate reliability, significance, and practical effect size\. Results: Cronbach’s alpha was 0\.560, indicating moderate internal consistency\. All seven ERP challenges were statistical significant\. Budget limitations, lack of training and support, shortage of skilled personnel and maintenance costs demonstrated strong practical effects, whereas data migration, employee resistance and weak top management support also emerged as significant barriers\. Limitations: The study is exploratory, cross\-sectional, and based on a small sample\. Practical implications: Organizations should focus on training, budgeting, skilled teams, leadership support, change management, and data governance\. Originality/Value: The study adds Bangladesh\-based ERP evidence using an integrated TAM\-CSF perspective\.

## [Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi\-experimental study](../publications/13836d730fc085ee4752.md)

R\. J\. Waken; Sunny S\. Lou; Mackenzie R\. Hofford; Elise Eiden; Carrie Burk; Seunghwan Kim; Jared Esker; Linying Zhang; Thomas M\. Maddox; Joanna Abraham; Albert M\. Lai; Sam B\. Bhayani; Deborah O&\#x27;Dell; Jennifer Schmidt; Kayla Paynter; Michèle Thomas; MATTHEW GERLING; Philip Payne; Thomas Kannampallil

Abstract Objectives To investigate the longitudinal effects of an ambient artificial intelligence \(AI\) scribe use in primary care on outcomes related to documentation time, note writing patterns, and clinician financial productivity\. Materials and Methods We conducted a quasi\-experimental study with an interrupted time\-series design to ascertain the effect of AI scribe use on note writing time, time outside of scheduled hours \(TOSH\), pajama time \(5:30PM\-7:00aM\), note length, note closure &lt;24 h, and work relative value units \(wRVU\)\. For each primary care clinician \(physician, advanced practice provider\), date of initial access was day 0; each measure was calculated for 150 days prior \(pre\-period\) and after \(post\-period\) day zero\. Results Two hundred and twenty clinicians \(mean age = 43\.7, 70\.9% females; 56\.4% physicians\) from 36 clinics, conducting 314 845 patient encounters were included\. Compared to the pre\-period, there was 7% decrease in note writing time at day 0 \(incidence rate ratio \[IRR\] 0\.93, 95% credible interval \[CI\] \[0\.89, 0\.98\]\), increasing to 16% decrease by day 150 \(IRR 0\.84, 95% CI \[0\.82, 0\.87\]\)\. There was no change in pajama time, TOSH, or wRVU at day 0; however, at day 150, there was a 19% decrease in pajama time \(0\.81, 95% CI \[0\.73, 0\.90\]\), 13% decrease in TOSH \(0\.87, 95% CI \[0\.77, 0\.98\]\), and a 2% increase in wRVU \(1\.02, 95% CI \[1\.01, 1\.04\]\)\. At day 0, there was a 5% increase in note closures \(1\.05, 95% CI \[1\.02, 1\.08\]\), with no difference to pre\-period levels by day 150\. There were no changes in note length at day 0 or day 150\. Discussion and Conclusion There were persistent changes in AI scribe use measures over time as clinicians situated these tools within their workflows\.

## [A Ciberbiosfera Eleitoral: Organismos, máquinas e regras na disputa pelo poder democrático](../publications/1388de6d49c51170e47e.md)

Francisco Hélio de Barros

## [Climate risk and financial stability research: a computational bibliometric analysis of thematic framing \(2010–2025\)](../publications/138ea5e89b080d9b7052.md)

Imad El Khlifi; Mohamed Drissi Bakhkhat

Abstract:Research on climate risk and financial stability has grown rapidly, yet few studies jointly address its bibliometric structure, thematic framing \(risk versus solution\), and underlying data reliability\. To address this gap, this study analyzes over 4,100 relevant English\-language articles from the Dimensions database \(2010–2025\)\. By combining a domain lexicon, a manual audit, and machine learning models \(SVM, ClimateBERT, FinBERT\), we classify the abstracts&\#x27; thematic orientation\. Our manual audit reveals substantial noise in the raw data, highlighting the necessity of strict relevance filtering\. Methodologically, while lexicon\-based classification shows weak agreement with human coding, machine learning models deliver robust performance\. Empirically, we find no clear temporal trend in the share of solution\-oriented research\. However, regression models demonstrate that solution\-oriented papers receive a significant citation premium \(approximately 27% higher expected citations\), an association that remains robust across stricter filters and journal fixed effects\. These findings emphasize the crucial role of data curation in computational bibliometrics and suggest that solution\-focused research attracts greater academic attention\. Keywords: Climate risk, financial stability, bibliometric analysis, Dimensions, thematic framing, text classification, machine learning\.Classification JEL : C38, C45, G10, G18, Q54Paper type : Empirical quantitative research \(computational bibliometrics\) Résumé :La recherche sur le risque climatique et la stabilité financière s’est développée rapidement, mais peu d’études examinent conjointement sa structure bibliométrique, son cadrage thématique \(risque versus solution\) et la fiabilité des données sous\-jacentes\. Pour combler cette lacune, cette étude analyse plus de 4 100 articles en anglais issus de la base Dimensions \(2010\-2025\)\. En combinant un lexique de domaine, un audit manuel et des modèles d&\#x27;apprentissage automatique \(SVM, ClimateBERT, FinBERT\), nous classons l&\#x27;orientation thématique des résumés\. Notre audit révèle un bruit important dans les données brutes, soulignant la nécessité d&\#x27;un filtrage rigoureux\. Sur le plan méthodologique, si le lexique montre une faible concordance avec le codage humain, les modèles d&\#x27;apprentissage automatique offrent des performances robustes\. Empiriquement, la part des recherches orientées solutions ne présente pas de tendance temporelle claire\. Toutefois, les modèles de régression montrent que ces articles bénéficient d&\#x27;une prime de citation significative \(environ 27 % de citations attendues en plus\), une association qui résiste aux effets fixes de revue et à des filtres stricts\. Ces résultats soulignent l&\#x27;importance de la curation des données en bibliométrie computationnelle et suggèrent que la recherche axée sur les solutions suscite davantage d&\#x27;attention académique\. Mots clés : Risque climatique, stabilité financière, analyse bibliométrique, Dimensions, cadrage thématique, classification de textes, apprentissage automatique\.JEL Classification : C38, C45, G10, G18, Q54Type du papier : Recherche empirique quantitative \(bibliométrie computationnelle\)

## [The need for uncertainty: why probabilistic LSTMs are key to improving flood predictions and enabling learned warning rules](../publications/139d40ae4ce8f35f55f5.md)

Sanika Baste; Sebastian Lerch; Daniel Klotz; Ralf Loritz

Abstract\. Deterministic model predictions can struggle to adequately capture extreme events such as floods and droughts, which are of particular relevance in hydrology\. This limitation arises because deterministic models collapse the conditional runoff distribution to a single point estimate\. Probabilistic modeling provides a way to address this issue by explicitly representing uncertainty and assigning non\-zero probabilities to a range of possible outcomes, including rare and extreme events, thereby capturing the full range of plausible hydrological responses\. Motivated by this perspective, we examine whether probabilistic Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) models improve the representation of extreme events in rainfall–\-runoff simulations across Switzerland\. Overall, the probabilistic models show good calibration, although some miscalibration remains for the extremes\. Differences between models mainly manifest in how uncertainty is distributed: some approaches produce narrower and lighter\-tailed distributions, while others yield broader distributions with heavier tails\. These trade\-offs highlight that probabilistic models differ not only in sharpness but also in how their calibration for rare events\. We observe this tradeoff also in models&\#x27; accuracy metrics\. When evaluating the mean of the probabilistic predictions using the Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency \(NSE\), none of the probabilistic approaches outperform the deterministic LSTM in terms of average predictive accuracy\. However, a clear advantage over the determinsitc models emerges when focusing on the tail of the discharge distribution\. For the most extreme events \(top 0\.1 % of the discharge distribution\), the deterministic LSTM underestimates more than 90 % of observed values \(since it provides estimates of an expectation\), whereas probabilistic predictions can capture a substantially larger fraction \(67 %\) of these extremes within their upper predictive bounds\. Building on the additional information provided by probabilistic runoff predictions, we further show how they can be translated into actionable flood warnings using reinforcement learning\. To this end, we introduce a Flood Risk Communication Agent \(FRiCA\) that operates on probabilistic runoff predictions and learns decision rules for issuing warnings of varying intensity\. The FRiCA is implemented as an LSTM\-based policy network and is trained by rewarding correct warning levels while penalizing the underestimation of flood severity\. Results indicate that the FRiCA outperforms simple fixed heuristics, such as issuing warnings based on the predictive mean or a fixed high quantile \(e\.g\., the 99th percentile\)\. While this behavior already demonstrates the potential of reinforcement learning for improved flood risk communication, it also motivates further exploration of better reward design and policy network definition for context\-dependent decision policies that adapt to varying hydrological and societal contexts\.

## [Zincblende\-/Diamond\-Structure Nanocrystals: Analytic Surface Energies by Size, Shape, and Surface Orientation](../publications/13ae47cfd4703822f73b.md)

Dirk König; Sean Campbell Smith

Abstract Recently, the universal analytics for the intrinsic shape of zincblende \(zb\) and diamond\-lattice nanocrystals \(NCs\) were described \[AIP Adv\. 6, 085306 \(2016\)\], determining exact numbers for their internal atoms NNC, internal bonds Nbnd, and interface bonds NIF as a function of NC size and \{hkl\} interface faceting for seven regular NC shapes: \{001\} cubes, \{111\} octahedra, \{110\} dodecahedra, \{001\}\-\{111\} pyramids, \{111\} tetrahedra, \{111\}\-\{001\} quatrodecahedra, and \{001\}\-\{111\} quadrodecahedra\. Here, such descriptions are updated and extended to accurately and analytically describe the density of surface free energy of NCs on a per\-interface\-bond basis γbnd,IF\. These descriptions are key to chemical NC reactivity as in catalysts, chemical reactivity as occurring in etching processes, and electronic properties such as defect formation and carrier localization\. In addition to accurate quantitative results demonstrated for Si\- and GaAs\-NCs, the new method introduced herein yields unique insights into the surface energetics hitherto unseen\. Results are most striking for NC sizes of dNC ≤ 50 nm as opposed to macroscopic values of surface free energy densities γ and NC surface areas A, allowing to accurately determine γbnd,IF for all NC shapes and sizes\. Using this approach, some surprising NC properties are found, like certain NCs showing γbnd,IFdecreasing with shrinking dNC\. Similar to the above reference for structural parameters, these analytic descriptions provide accurate values of the density of surface free energy, in particular for free\-standing or exposed NCs, and can be used to describe the energetics of different zb\- and diamond\-lattice NCs\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Framework for Drug\-Target Affinity Prediction Using Deep Neural Networks and Integrated Molecular and Protein Feature Engineering](../publications/13afe2035f2d7d2f4c3d.md)



Objective: To develop an artificial intelligence framework that integrates deep neural networks with molecular and protein feature engineering to accurately predict drug\-target affinity, thereby supporting efficient computational drug discovery and therapeutic candidate identification\.The proposed study employed a publicly available drug\-target affinity dataset consisting of molecular SMILES representations, protein amino acid sequences, and experimentally determined affinity values, partitioned into training, validation, and testing subsets for model development\.Material and Methods: A publicly available drug\-target affinity dataset containing training, validation, and testing subsets was employed, in which molecular SMILES representations and protein sequences were converted into integrated numerical descriptors through feature engineering and standardized before model training\.Subsequently, a Deep Neural Network \(DNN\) was developed to capture the complex relationships between the engineered molecular and protein features for accurate drug\-target affinity prediction\.Extracting representative features from molecular SMILES representations and protein sequences remains a major challenge in accurately predicting drug\-target affinity\.Capturing the complex nonlinear relationships between drug molecules and target proteins is further complicated by the high dimensionality and intricate nature of biological data\.Results: To mitigate these challenges, a Deep Neural Network integrated with molecular and protein feature engineering was employed to effectively model complex drug\-target interactions and enhance the accuracy of drug\-target affinity prediction\.The proposed Deep Neural Network efficiently learns complex nonlinear patterns from integrated molecular and protein features, thereby enhancing the accuracy of drug\-target affinity prediction\.The proposed Deep Neural Network achieved consistent performance across the training, validation, and testing datasets, with Pearson correlation coefficients of 0\.6586, 0\.6465, and 0\.6343, respectively\.The obtained R² scores of 0\.2585, 0\.2163, and 0\.1599 demonstrate the model&\#x27;s capability to effectively predict drug\-target affinity using integrated molecular and protein features\.Conclusion: The proposed Artificial Intelligence framework effectively combined Deep Neural Networks with integrated molecular and protein feature engineering for drugtarget affinity prediction\.The findings indicate that the framework provides a reliable and efficient approach for modelling drug\-target interactions, thereby supporting computational drug discovery\.

## [No todas las instrucciones se olvidan igual](../publications/13b39af5bce115e9f58c.md)

Tomás Pablo Korenblit

For an autonomous LLM agent, a safety guardrail is just another instruction given at the start of a run, and as context grows, the agent keeps some instructions while dropping others\. Because a mean compliance rate aggregates across instructions, it cannot reveal which one was dropped\. We measure retention one instruction at a time by conducting 25\-turn coding sessions on five instruction\-following models and three open\-source Python codebases\. In these sessions, we plant twelve ordinary coding preferences as casual inline requests, score the resulting code with deterministic checkers on a 0–3 ordinal scale, and fit a Bayesian ordered\-logistic model with hierarchical effects per decision type to 244 observations\. Treatment effects span −2\.4 to \+5\.4 on the log\-odds scale \(group\-level standard deviation 2\.1\), showing considerable variation across preferences\. Most preferences are already followed by default, and only three of twelve benefit from being restated \(two under a single\-model robustness check\)\. Since these preferences stand in for guardrails, this unevenness is a safety concern\. Because a guardrail must hold on every turn, aggregate compliance can remain high even after the one rule that matters is skipped\. As a result, a deployed agent needs per\-instruction monitoring to catch it\.

## [Geopolitical Risk Prediction and Robust Investment Decision\-Making for Transnational Photovoltaic Projects in Africa via Generative AI and Spatiotemporal GNN](../publications/13b802518667397d41de.md)

Jiayu Sun; Guan Yang; Zhenguo Cao; Wei Zhao

Geopolitical risks associated with transnational photovoltaic \(PV\) projects in Africa are dynamic, interconnected, and difficult to assess using conventional investment models\. Specifically, existing approaches often struggle to characterize cross\-border risk transmission and incorporate evolving geopolitical information into investment decisions\. To address these challenges, this study proposes EG\-GeoInvest, a framework that integrates generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) with spatiotemporal graph neural networks for geopolitical risk assessment and risk\-aware investment decision\-making\. First, geopolitical event records, multilingual news, national governance indicators, and PV investment data are combined within an evidence\-constrained, multisource heterogeneous information system to support the identification and semantic representation of risk events\. Second, a Spatiotemporal Geopolitical Risk Encoding Module \(ST\-GREM\) integrates a temporal convolutional network with relationship\-aware graph convolution to represent the evolution of risks and their interdependencies across transnational investment, energy\-trade, and financing networks\. Third, cross\-modal semantic projection and Low\-Rank Adaptation \(LoRA\) enable graph\-structured information and generative language models to contribute jointly to forecasts of geopolitical risks, project delays, and economic loss distributions\. Finally, the predicted risk distributions inform a Conditional Value\-at\-Risk \(CVaR\) and distributionally robust optimization framework for investment allocation under return and tail\-risk constraints\. A proposed evaluation design encompassing comparative risk prediction, cross\-country generalization, and investment scenario analysis provides a basis for assessing predictive performance and potential decision\-making value\.

## [Integrating Median Filtering with Deep Pattern Recognition Models for Improved Breast Ultrasound Cancer Detection](../publications/13b89b3c439452a0c30a.md)

Zeeshan Ahmad; Yasir Aziz

Even though ultrasound of the breast is an easy to access imaging modality and is radiation free, speckle\-like intensity fluctuations, low contrast, variability of acquisition and limited model transparency are the challenges in automated classification of ultrasound lesions\. In this paper, we introduce a controlled framework of preprocessing\-classification\-explainability that compares the aforementioned three image types \(raw, 3 × 3 median filtered, median filtered \+ contrast\-limited adaptive histogram equalization \(CLAHE\)\) using the same leakage\-safe data split, convolutional neural network \(CNN\), training budget and evaluation protocol\. To minimize the information leakage, the downloaded Kaggle archive of benign and malignant images was pre\-augmented with 9016 images; and then divided into 70/15/15 train/validation/test sets based on augmentation\-family grouping\. The 96\.97% accuracy, 98\.95% sensitivity, 95\.04% specificity, 95\.10% precision, 96\.99% F1\-score, 0\.99623 ROC\-AUC and 0\.99608 PR\-AUC of the model that was median\-filtered were the highest\. Compared to raw standardized baseline, median filtering resulted in an increase in accuracy and sensitivity by 3\.55 and 6\.15 percentage points, respectively, and in a decrease of false negative cases from 48 to 7\. Median restoration also gave the best results in terms of PSNR and SSIM for controlled synthetic\-speckle testing, which were 27\.9313 dB PSNR and 0\.8214 SSIM, respectively\. There was a significant reduction in paired errors after raw versus median filtering \(adjusted p = 0\.000008\) by Exact McNemar analysis\. Grad\-CAM, LIME and SHAP also revealed class\-specific areas and failure modes but only showed low spatial overlap, which indicated that these are complementary rather than interchangeable\. The results indicate that a very basic median filter which preserves the edges can enhance the predictive reliability and model auditing when the effects of the pre\-processing are separated in an experimental setup\.

## [Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general\-purpose AI chatbots](../publications/13be2344c37403716353.md)

Wei Xiao; Xuwei Cao; Wangahe Jin; Xiaoyi Chen; Jun Cai; 駱旭琛; Jiehua Deng

Background Digital mental health tools, including general\-purpose artificial intelligence \(AI\) chatbots, may provide accessible and low\-threshold psychological support for people living with chronic conditions\. However, their value in this population depends not only on recognizing depression or anxiety, but also on understanding how psychological distress is shaped by disease\-specific experiences and when self\-guided support should transition toward professional care\. We evaluated the appropriateness, contextual sensitivity, safety, and consistency of psychological support provided by three widely accessible AI chatbots across contrasting chronic illness contexts\. Methods We conducted a standardized simulated\-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao\. Twenty scenarios were developed across type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) and chronic spontaneous urticaria \(CSU\), representing matched mild and moderate presentations of depression and anxiety together with condition\-specific distress related to diabetes self\-management and CSU\-related flare uncertainty\. Each scenario was independently submitted to all three systems in two testing rounds, yielding 120 responses\. Blinded raters assessed overall psychological support appropriateness, recognition and emotional support, chronic\-illness contextualization, psychological support and referral, psychosomatic balance and safety, and major clinical or safety errors\. Repeated testing assessed response consistency\. Results Overall psychological support appropriateness differed across systems \(P = 0\.002\), with 90\.0% of ChatGPT, 75\.0% of Gemini, and 55\.0% of Doubao responses meeting the prespecified appropriateness threshold\. Recognition and emotional support was consistently strong across systems, whereas greater differences emerged in chronic\-illness contextualization \(P = 0\.001\), psychological support and referral \(P = 0\.002\), and psychosomatic balance and safety \(P&lt;0\.001\)\. All responses to mild presentations were classified as psychologically appropriate, compared with 58\.3% of responses to moderate presentations, indicating that performance became less reliable when digital support required stronger escalation toward professional assessment\. Contextualization was also less consistent in CSU, particularly when responses needed to incorporate flare unpredictability, pruritus, sleep disruption, and illness uncertainty\. Major clinical or safety errors occurred in 0%, 10\.0%, and 15\.0% of first\-round ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao responses, respectively\. Test–retest consistency was moderate and varied between systems\. Conclusions General\-purpose AI chatbots show potential as accessible, self\-guided digital mental health resources for people living with chronic conditions, particularly for recognizing distress and providing initial supportive guidance\. Their current limitations emerge when effective support requires disease\-specific contextualization, balanced interpretation of psychological and somatic factors, or escalation as symptoms become more severe\. These findings identify important boundaries for the use of conversational AI in chronic\-illness mental health care and suggest that implementation should emphasize context\-sensitive guidance, severity\-responsive referral, and clear integration with rather than substitution for professional care\.

## [A Literature Review on the Sensor Network Design Problem Applied to Chemical Processes](../publications/13beac366410ccb0cdea.md)

Jonildo dos Santos Silva; Marília Caroline C\. de Sá; Romulo Brito da Silva; Bruno Colli Manhães; Daniela Miranda Neves; Luiz Felipe de O\. Campos; Thiago Koichi Anzai; Fábio C\. Diehl; José Carlos Pinto

In the present paper, a comprehensive review of methodologies for the optimal placement of measurement devices in chemical processes, commonly referred to as the sensor network design problem \(SNDP\), is presented\. The SNDP is a combinatorial optimization problem of paramount importance in process design, monitoring, control, and data reconciliation, as sensor placement directly affects estimability, precision, reliability, and fault detectability\. In addition to surveying solution strategies for SNDP, this review examines the closely related variable classification problem, which constitutes a fundamental building block in the systematic development of sensor networks\. The evolution of the field is analyzed, highlighting early structural search approaches, subsequent optimization\-based formulations relying on relaxation and decomposition techniques, and heuristic and metaheuristic strategies\. The strengths and limitations of these methodological classes are discussed with respect to problem size and computational complexity\. Moreover, this review identified a novel strategy to solve SNDPs based on machine learning algorithms\. Finally, future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the growing need for scalable frameworks capable of addressing increasingly large and automated industrial systems\. As computational capabilities continue to advance and process plants transition toward highly digitalized environments, research efforts devoted to efficient and robust SNDP methodologies are expected to intensify\. In this context, Large Language Models \(LLMs\) can play a transformative role\.

## [Rethinking immunotherapy sequencing in multiple myeloma: a conceptual adaptive immunotherapy sequencing model](../publications/13c3c9ccf11c433bdbfc.md)

Aliaa Khalili

Background Chimeric antigen receptor T\-cell \(CAR\-T\) therapy and bispecific antibodies \(BsAbs\) have transformed treatment for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma \(RRMM\)\. Contemporary guidelines increasingly incorporate prior antigen\-directed exposure, disease kinetics, patient fitness, toxicity, access, and patient preference\. However, a prospectively validated framework that jointly operationalizes immune fitness, tumor antigen status, and treatment feasibility for sequencing T\-cell–redirecting therapies is not available\. Main body This Perspective introduces the Adaptive Immunotherapy Sequencing Model \(AISM\), an author\-proposed framework for research and multidisciplinary discussion\. AISM proposes that sequencing should be studied in relation to two evolving biological domains: the capacity of the host T\-cell compartment to support therapy and the probability that the relevant tumor antigen remains therapeutically actionable\. The model uses provisional 0–10 research constructs for T\-cell fitness and antigen\-escape risk to make these domains explicit\. AISM hypothesizes that, for eligible patients with early RRMM and feasible access, referral for BCMA\-directed CAR\-T before prolonged exposure to T\-cell–redirecting BsAbs may preserve a potentially favorable treatment option\. It also recognizes that off\-the\-shelf BsAbs may be necessary when disease tempo, frailty, access, or patient preference make CAR\-T impracticable\. After prior BCMA\-directed therapy, an antigen\-switching approach is biologically plausible, but antigen loss is not universal and other mechanisms of resistance must be considered\. Conclusions AISM provides a testable framework for prospective comparative studies\. Such studies should evaluate whether biologically informed sequencing improves progression\-free survival \(PFS\), while also assessing overall survival, toxicity, infections, treatment\-free time, feasibility, and patient\-reported outcomes\.

## [Science under attack](../publications/13cb73ba183aaacf8609.md)

Christine Leuenberger

This report focuses on changing agency priorities at the U\.S\. National Science Foundation \(NSF\) from the Biden\-Harris administration \(2021\-2025\) to the Trump\-Vance administration \(2025\-present\)\. I had joined NSF in 2022 as an Intergovernmental Personnel Act \(IPA\) assignee \(NSF, n\.d\.\-f\)\. The IPA program enables academics to serve as Program Directors or in other leadership capacities at NSF; the rotation of expertise between academia and NSF connects NSF grant\-making to the scientific community and benefits advancements in federally funded science\. This report presents my experience and assessment of how some of the government\-wide changes to the organization, structures, and priorities of science funding unfolded at NSF during the transition across the two administrations since 2025\. The report is based on the autoethnographic research method in the social sciences \(Denzin, 2013\)\. Autoethnographic accounts are anchored in the qualitative research tradition; the qualitative approach provides a contextual understanding of social phenomena, and the autoethnographic method is one way to do so\. An autoethnographic account tends to use the observer’s experience as part of a social community as a lens through which to better understand broader socio\-cultural, institutional, and political phenomena\. The report first briefly discusses the importance of federal funding for the development of Science &amp; Technology \(S&amp;T\) and the role of NSF in contributing to US leadership in S&amp;T\. Secondly, the focus is on NSF work culture and priorities before 2025 and the institutional transformations set in motion with the transition to the new administration on January 20th, 2025\. The report highlights how the changes instituted impacted the agency’s human resources, infra/structural assets as well as work practices\. Thirdly, the report sketches out the impact of these changes on public servants, their attempts to support their agency, and for some, the difficult choice to either stay and adjust to new institutional realities or leave public service\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE MODERN ERA: YOUTH EDUCATION AND THE CULTURE OF INDEPENDENT THINKING](../publications/13ccdc9c195456cbc8ca.md)

This article examines the role of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in modern education, its potential to improve young people&\#x27;s learning experiences, and its influence on the development of independent thinking\. ## [Teacher Readiness for Human\-Centred AI Integration in Higher Education: Evidence from Assam, India](../publications/13cd8e048412bd6e4aa6.md)

Karshika Boruah

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is transforming higher education, making teacher readiness essential for responsible integration\. This paper proposes an empirical framework to examine higher education teachers’ readiness for human\-centred AI integration in Assam\. Based on UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Teachers, the study focuses on five dimensions: human\-centred mindset, AI ethics, AI foundations and applications, AI pedagogy, and AI\-supported professional learning, alongside institutional support\. A quantitative, cross\-sectional survey design is proposed, employing a structured questionnaire and statistical analyses to assess readiness and its influencing factors\. Addressing a regional research gap, the study emphasises ethical judgment, pedagogical competence, and human accountability rather than technological adoption alone\. As primary data collection is pending, the framework provides a basis for future empirical investigation\. The anticipated findings may inform faculty development, institutional AI policies, and responsible AI integration in higher education\.

## [AI\-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery](../publications/13dac6b11dbbb4f59079.md)

Shicheng Liu; Krista Opsahl\-Ong; Andrew Drozdov; Julian Killingback; Arnav Singhvi; Ronak Pradeep; Michael Bendersky; James C\. Dickerson; Monica S\. Lam

Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort\. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results \(SEER\) database, a widely used U\.S\. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies\. First, we introduce SEER\-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER\-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings\. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77\.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis\. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion\. Across published papers in SEER\-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9\.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review\. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices\.

## [Inteligencia artificial en la investigación penal y sus límites procesales en Ecuador](../publications/13ef12bd6fd6f6c4e335.md)

Ignacio Fernando Barcos\-Arias; Luis Alberto Andrade\-Monar; Fredy Geovany Guachi\-Soria

Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support criminal investigation, in the analysis of large data volumes, digital forensics and case management, but it poses challenges for due process, the presumption of innocence, evidentiary transparency and personal data protection\. The aim was to analyze its use in Ecuadorian criminal investigation, its applications, regulatory gaps and the procedural limits arising from the Constitution, the criminal code and international standards\. A qualitative, descriptive\-analytical approach was applied, with a legal hermeneutic method, document review and five exploratory expert interviews\. Criteria for a rights\-based incorporation are proposed: express regulation through protocols, algorithmic explainability, judicial control of results, training of legal operators and a ban on delegating decision\-making functions to automated systems\.
