Арайлым Тұрусбекова; Arailym Turusbekova; S\. G\. \(Seydalieva\) Omarovna

Abstract\. The article discusses the influence of the &quot;inverted class&quot; model, enhanced by artificial intelligence tools in teaching English as a foreign language, on mastering the lexical stock\. The focus on three\-stage learning, which is based on independent repetition using artificial intelligence after lessons, recognizing new vocabulary before class, actively using it in the classroom in a semantic context, rather than the model of memorizing words a traditional lesson\. The methodological basis of the study was a comparative analysis of the works of Kazakhstani and Russian researchers published in 2023\-2025, systematization of the didactic activities of digital tools and pedagogical design of Model tasks for the EFL lesson\.The result of the analysis showed that artificial intelligence is more productive as a means of connecting pre\-training, level adjusting training, instant feedback and interval repetition than as a separate technology that automatically &quot;trains&quot; vocabulary\.In the practical part, samples of identifying new words from the text,creating context, conducting a microdiologue with AI\-chat,comparing incorrect answers, forming an individual dictionary map snd deferred verification were presented\.

## [Charakteristika, Behandlungsprozesse und klinischer Outcome von Patienten mit Schlaganfallbeginn im Krankenhaus und anschließender Verlegung zur endovaskulären Thrombektomie in einem telemedizinischen Schlaganfallnetzwerk](../publications/13f3ec1781b86dcb3d83.md)

Miriam Leitner

In dieser Dissertation liegt der Fokus auf denjenigen Patienten, die einen In\-Hospital\-Stroke \(IHS\) in einem ländlichen Krankenhaus erleiden und anschließend zur endovaskulären Thrombektomie \(EVT\) in ein Schlaganfallzentrum verlegt werden\. Zu dieser Patientengruppe gibt es bisher nur wenige Studien\. IHS treten häufig auf und unterscheiden sich in einigen wichtigen Merkmalen von Schlaganfällen außerhalb des Krankenhauses, sogenannten Out\-of\-Hospital\-Strokes \(OHS\)\. IHS sind zudem mit Verzögerungen in der Behandlung sowie mit einem schlechteren klinischen Outcome assoziiert\. Die EVT wird seit dem Jahr 2015 zunehmend in der Schlaganfallversorgung angewendet, wird jedoch überwiegend von spezialisierten Neuroradiologen in Schlaganfallzentren durchgeführt, was die Diskrepanz in der Schlaganfallversorgung zwischen Ballungszentrum und dem ländlichen Raum verstärkt\. Die Interhospitalverlegung in ein Schlaganfallzentrum und die damit verbundene Zeitverzögerung stellt einen weiteren Risikofaktor für einen schlechteren klinischen Outcome dar\. Eine genauere Untersuchung dieser besonders vulnerablen Patientengruppe ist daher notwendig\. Bei dieser Dissertation handelt es sich um eine registerbasierte retrospektive Analyse von prospektiv gesammelten Daten\. Die Studienpopulation umfasst 49 IHS\-Patienten und 274 OHS\-Patienten aus 14 ländlichen Kliniken des telemedizinischen Schlaganfallnetzwerks Südostbayern \(TEMPiS\), die in ein Schlaganfallzentrum verlegt und mittels EVT behandelt wurden\. Patienten, die zwischen dem 01\.02\.2018 und dem 31\.07\.2020 behandelt wurden, wurden in die Analyse eingeschlossen\. Baseline\-Charakteristika, Behandlungsprozesse sowie klinische Outcomes wurden zwischen IHS\- und OHS\-Patienten verglichen\. Darüber hinaus wurden die Einweisungsdiagnosen der IHS\-Patienten analysiert\. Der primäre Endpunkt war der Wert auf der modified Rankin Scale \(mRS\) drei Monate nach dem Schlaganfall\. IHS\-Patienten waren signifikant häufiger an Vorhofflimmern \(55\.3% vs\. 35\.9%, p= \.012\) und Diabetes mellitus \(36\.2% vs\. 21\.1%, p= \.024\) vorerkrankt und nahmen signifikant häufiger orale Antikoagulanzien ein \(44\.7% vs\. 20\.8%, p&lt; \.001\)\. Der NIHSS\-Score war in beiden Studiengruppen vergleichbar \(NIHSS\-Mittelwert: 16\.13 vs\. 14\.67, p= \.152\)\. Die Zeitintervalle von Symptombeginn bis zur Durchführung der EVT waren für IHS\-Patienten signifikant kürzer\. Trotzdem war ihr klinischer Outcome signifikant schlechter als bei OHS\-Patienten: 59\.8% der IHS\-Patienten vs\. 28\.8% der OHS\-Patienten verstarben innerhalb der ersten drei Monate nach dem Schlaganfall \(p&lt; \.001\)\. Nur 20\.4% der IHS\-Patienten erreichten einen guten bis moderaten klinischen Outcome \(mRS 0\-3\) nach drei Monaten, während dies bei 39\.8% der OHS\-Patienten der Fall war \(p&lt; \.010\)\. In den durchgeführten logistischen Regressionsanalysen war IHS mit einem signifikant schlechteren klinischen Outcome \(adjustierte Odds Ratio \(aOR\): 3\.04, 95%\-Konfidenzintervall \(KI\): 1\.57\-6\.04, p&lt; \.001\) und einem höheren Mortalitätsrisiko \(aOR: 3\.99, 95%\-KI: 1\.84\-8\.92, p&lt; \.001\) assoziiert\. In dieser Dissertation wurden die IHS\-Patienten schneller mittels EVT behandelt, wiesen eine vergleichbare Rate an sicheren und erfolgreichen Interventionen auf, hatten einem ähnlichen Schlaganfall\-Schweregrad sowie nur geringe Baseline\-Unterschiede\. Trotzdem war insbesondere die Sterblichkeit der IHS\-Patienten sehr hoch und nur wenige IHS\-Patienten erreichten einen guten klinischen Outcome nach drei Monaten\. Nur ein kleiner Anteil der IHS\-Patienten scheint daher von der Verlegung zur EVT zu profitieren\. Weitere Studien sind erforderlich, um diese Patientengruppe genauer zu charakterisieren und alternative Behandlungsstrategien zu evaluieren\.

## [Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book II: Coherence Geometry and Modern Machine Learning\. A Source Theory of Learning Systems](../publications/13fa84dd43fe1856ec6d.md)

B\. Petersen

Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book II: Coherence Geometry and Modern Machine Learning\. A Source Theory of Learning Systems develops the source\-to\-endpoint bridge of the Coherence\-Driven Intelligence \(CDI\) framework\. The book presents a finite coherence\-memory Source description of learning systems and shows how familiar machine\-learning objects and architectures may arise as endpoint projections of retained Source structure\. It develops Source presentations, local coherence views, closure maps, target geometry, basin readout, projection equivalence, and projection loss, and uses these structures to distinguish the organization of memory from its downstream endpoint representation\. The framework is applied across a broad range of contemporary learning systems, including deep and recurrent networks, convolution, attention, transformers, mixture\-of\-experts architectures, associative and energy\-based models, autoencoders, diffusion models, self\-supervised and contrastive learning, graph neural networks, retrieval\-augmented systems, state\-space models, reinforcement learning, continual learning, meta\-learning, and composite AI systems\. The volume also develops source\-transparent memory operations including replay, editing, seam and margin diagnostics, growth, pruning, repair, and reclosure\. The later part of the book moves beyond architecture\-by\-architecture catalogue coverage and develops a finite structural grammar for learning operations\. It culminates in the Finite Machine\-Learning Projection Theorem, which establishes finite representational universality for the stated class of finite typed machine\-learning systems: their operational structure can be realized within the finite CDI framework and their declared endpoint observables recovered through projection\. The result does not, by itself, assert complete\-Source representability, complete\-Source dynamical descent, persistent admissible Source lifting, or equal efficiency or utility across architectures\. This volume is Book II of the Coherence\-Driven Intelligence series\. Book I develops the mathematical foundations of CDI, while Book III constructs source\-explicit intelligent systems directly through the WaveModules reference realization\. This release is a Working Reference Text, Version 0\.1, and has not undergone external editorial or peer review\. CGI Internal ID: CGI\-BKS\-0006

## [Social Justice, Technology, and the Canadian Engineering Profession&\#x27;s Statutory Public Interest Mandate](../publications/13fece566bfe180799b6.md)

Mic Liu

Engineered systems govern ordinary life long before a court, regulator, or complaint process becomes involved\. They influence whether drinking water remains protected, whether a public building can be used safely and with dignity, and whether technical information can be understood and challenged\. A design may satisfy a minimum technical requirement while still placing a patterned and uneven burden on a structurally marginalized public\. This thesis asks how the public\-interest mandate in the provincial and territorial laws that regulate professional engineering across Canada should apply when engineering work creates or significantly shapes that kind of risk\. I argue that the mandate requires role\-specific due care for a material disparate\-impact risk when six cumulative conditions are met\. The first three ask whether the risk is more than remote or minor, whether it may impair a public\-facing interest, and whether its burden is patterned and uneven\. The remaining three ask whether engineering work creates or significantly shapes the risk, whether a competent actor could know of it through ordinary diligence within role, and whether an actor has authority to respond\. The thesis develops that argument through interdisciplinary legal and engineering analysis\. It interprets statutes, regulations, and cases governing professional authority, then connects those sources to engineering ethics and science and technology studies\. Scholarship on equality and disability helps identify evidence that conventional technical routines may miss\. Work on Indigenous knowledge and epistemic injustice adds questions about authority, credibility, and excluded forms of knowledge\. Three recurring examples test the framework at different distances from licensed practice\. Site 41, a proposed Ontario landfill, is the engineering\-heavy example because hydrogeology and groundwater modelling were central to the dispute\. Technical transparency and distributed public authority were also central\. Public washrooms provide an ordinary code\-mediated example in which fixture calculations, mechanical systems, and accessibility can affect equivalent access\. Artificial intelligence and large language model system integration provide the boundary example, showing how professional engineering may govern a defined technical use while other legal and institutional actors govern the wider technology ecosystem\. The thesis makes three connected contributions\. First, the cumulative threshold test identifies when an equality\-facing concern becomes relevant to professional engineering responsibility\. Second, the actor\-authority map locates the person or institution that can investigate or change the relevant work\. It also identifies who can approve the decision or receive an escalation\. Third, the Public\-Interest Impact Assessment translates those findings into a process of identify, assess, and respond\. The assessment connects evidence to engineering judgment, assigns a response within authority, and records the conditions that require later review\. The goal is to contribute to technological accountability by making professional decisions more attentive to affected publics, more transparent about uncertainty, and more reviewable when a material disparate\-impact risk is known or reasonably knowable\. This account places defined duties on engineering actors while preserving the separate authority of Indigenous legal orders, public bodies, and human\-rights institutions\. Employers and other regulators retain the authority assigned to them by law or organizational role\. \-\- Bien avant qu&\#x27;un tribunal, un organisme de réglementation ou un mécanisme de plainte intervienne, les systèmes issus du génie organisent déjà la vie quotidienne\. Ils influencent la protection de l&\#x27;eau potable, l&\#x27;accès sûr et digne aux bâtiments publics ainsi que la possibilité de comprendre et de contester une décision technique\. Une conception peut respecter une exigence technique minimale tout en imposant, selon un schéma récurrent, un fardeau inégal à un public structurellement marginalisé\. Cette thèse examine la manière dont le mandat d&\#x27;intérêt public prévu par les lois provinciales et territoriales qui encadrent la profession d&\#x27;ingénieur au Canada devrait s&\#x27;appliquer lorsqu&\#x27;un travail de génie crée ou façonne de façon importante un tel risque\. Je soutiens que ce mandat exige une diligence adaptée au rôle lorsqu&\#x27;un risque important d&\#x27;effets négatifs structurés et inégalement répartis satisfait à six critères cumulatifs\. Les trois premiers demandent si le risque dépasse le stade lointain ou mineur, s&\#x27;il peut compromettre un intérêt dont le public doit pouvoir bénéficier concrètement et si le fardeau se répartit de manière structurée et inégale\. Les trois autres portent sur le lien avec le travail de génie, les connaissances accessibles à un acteur compétent dans l&\#x27;exercice de son rôle et le pouvoir d&\#x27;intervenir\. La thèse développe cet argument au moyen d&\#x27;une analyse interdisciplinaire du droit et du génie\. Elle interprète les lois, les règlements et la jurisprudence qui encadrent l&\#x27;autorité professionnelle, puis met ces sources en relation avec l&\#x27;éthique du génie et les études sociales des sciences et des technologies\. Les travaux sur l&\#x27;égalité et le handicap aident à repérer les éléments de preuve que les routines techniques peuvent laisser de côté\. Les savoirs autochtones et les travaux sur l&\#x27;injustice épistémique soulèvent aussi des questions d&\#x27;autorité, de crédibilité et d&\#x27;exclusion des connaissances\. Trois exemples récurrents éprouvent le cadre selon des liens plus ou moins étroits avec l&\#x27;exercice réservé du génie\. Le site 41, un projet de lieu d&\#x27;enfouissement en Ontario, constitue l&\#x27;exemple où le génie occupe une place centrale parce que l&\#x27;hydrogéologie et la modélisation des eaux souterraines étaient au coeur du différend\. Les toilettes publiques fournissent un exemple courant de conception encadrée par les codes du bâtiment, où le calcul des appareils sanitaires, les systèmes mécaniques et l&\#x27;accessibilité peuvent influer sur l&\#x27;égalité d&\#x27;accès\. L&\#x27;intégration de systèmes d&\#x27;intelligence artificielle \(IA\), notamment de grands modèles de langage \(GML\), sert d&\#x27;exemple frontière où la responsabilité professionnelle dépend du travail précis et de l&\#x27;autorité réellement exercée\. La thèse propose trois contributions liées\. Premièrement, un test de seuil cumulatif précise le moment où un enjeu lié à l&\#x27;égalité devient pertinent pour la responsabilité professionnelle en génie\. Deuxièmement, une cartographie des acteurs et de leurs pouvoirs situe la personne ou l&\#x27;institution qui peut enquêter sur le travail ou le modifier\. Elle indique aussi qui peut approuver la décision et à qui le risque doit être signalé\. Troisièmement, l&\#x27;évaluation des incidences sur l&\#x27;intérêt public \(Public\-Interest Impact Assessment ou PIIA\) traduit ces constats en trois étapes : identifier, évaluer et intervenir\. L&\#x27;évaluation relie les éléments de preuve au jugement de génie, attribue une réponse dans les limites de l&\#x27;autorité et consigne les circonstances qui exigent une réévaluation\. La thèse cherche ainsi à contribuer à la responsabilisation technologique en rendant les décisions professionnelles plus attentives aux publics touchés, plus transparentes quant à l&\#x27;incertitude et plus faciles à examiner lorsqu&\#x27;un risque important d&\#x27;effets négatifs structurés et inégalement répartis est connu ou devrait raisonnablement l&\#x27;être\. Le cadre attribue des responsabilités précises aux acteurs du génie tout en respectant l&\#x27;autorité distincte des ordres juridiques autochtones, des organismes publics et des organismes de protection des droits de la personne\.

## [Uric acid\-to\-HDL\-cholesterol ratio and incident carotid atherosclerosis: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/14099519d4b7ce868316.md)

Hezhi Wen; Kaiyang Shao; Yaling Li; Ruyi Cai; Ting Sun

Background The uric acid\-to\-HDL\-cholesterol ratio \(UHR\) has been proposed as a composite cardiometabolic biomarker, but prospective evidence linking UHR to incident carotid atherosclerosis remains limited\. Methods In a retrospective cohort of 16,572 adults from a tertiary health examination center in Zhejiang, China, we examined the association between baseline UHR and incident carotid artery lesions using Cox proportional hazards regression\. Incremental predictive performance was evaluated using C\-statistic, integrated discrimination improvement, continuous net reclassification improvement, median improvement in individual predicted event probabilities, and decision curve analysis\. Results Over a mean follow\-up of 2\.7 years, 4,454 incident events occurred\. Each 1\-SD increment in baseline UHR was independently associated with a 6% higher hazard of incident carotid artery lesions \(HR 1\.06, 95% CI 1\.01–1\.11; p = 0\.015\)\. In exploratory sex\-stratified analyses, the association was statistically significant in males \(HR 1\.07, 95% CI 1\.02–1\.12; p = 0\.010\) but not in females \(HR 0\.98, 95% CI 0\.93–1\.04; p = 0\.524\), though the formal interaction test was not significant \( p = 0\.261\)\. UHR did not improve discrimination \(ΔC = 0\.0003\) or net clinical benefit despite significant changes in individual predicted event probabilities in males \( p = 0\.008\)\. Conclusion Higher baseline UHR was independently associated with short\-term carotid atherosclerotic progression\. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible sex difference, but this requires confirmation in adequately powered studies\. While UHR provides independent prognostic information, it does not meaningfully improve risk stratification beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors in health examination populations\.

## [PREVALÊNCIA DE COMPROMETIMENTO COGNITIVO RASTREADO PELO TESTE DO DESENHO DO RELÓGIO EM IDOSOS COMUNITÁRIOS](../publications/140e65c597d7b98b77d5.md)

Alicia Pedrini Tachini; Eloisa Gilli Longen; Francieli Battiti; Vitoria Vicentini Silva; Caio Bechert de Modesti; Daniele Coelho; Djenifer Cristy Carneiro Fortunato

O envelhecimento populacional amplia a relevância do rastreio cognitivo precoce na comunidade\. Este estudo teve como objetivo estimar a prevalência de comprometimento cognitivo rastreado pelo Teste do Desenho do Relógio \(TDR\) em idosos comunitários e analisar sua relação com o sexo, a faixa etária e o nível de atividade física\. Estudo transversal e descritivo, com amostra por conveniência de idosos \(≥60 anos\) participantes de grupos de convivência\. O TDR foi pontuado de 0 a 10 e classificado em desempenho normal \(9\-10 pontos\), suspeita de alteração \(6\-8 pontos\) ou alteração cognitiva \(≤5 pontos\)\. A atividade física autorrelatada foi categorizada em menos de 150 minutos semanais, 150 minutos semanais ou mais e sedentarismo\. Utilizaram\-se os testes de Mann\-Whitney, Kruskal\-Wallis com pós\-teste de Dunn, exato de Fisher\-Freeman\-Halton e regressão logística ajustada por idade e sexo \(α=5%\)\. Entre os 184 participantes \(85,9% mulheres; mediana de idade de 74 anos\), 72,3% apresentaram desempenho normal, 15,2% suspeita de alteração e 12,5% alteração cognitiva, totalizando 27,7% com rastreio alterado\. Não houve diferença entre os sexos \(p=0,500\)\. O desempenho diferiu entre as faixas etárias \(p=0,026\), sendo pior entre 70 e 79 anos em comparação a 60 e 69 anos \(p=0,023\)\. A atividade física não se associou ao desempenho cognitivo nas análises bruta \(p=0,662\) e ajustada, embora os sedentários fossem mais velhos \(p=0,006\)\. Cerca de um em cada quatro idosos comunitários apresentou rastreio cognitivo alterado, o que reforça a utilidade do TDR como triagem rápida e de baixo custo na comunidade, associada a encaminhamento para avaliação complementar\.

## [Desarrollo de un agente conversacional con RAG para el apoyo en la toma de decisiones en la empresa Acopio, Beneficio y Torcido de Tabaco Granma](../publications/1410d3bcae31d8ef772a.md)

Marcos Antonio Lozada Pérez; Juan Antonio Plasencia Soler

This research addresses the challenges of decision\-making in the area of ​​quality control for exported hand\-rolled tobacco at the company &quot;Acopio, Beneficio y Torcido de Tabaco Granma,&quot; where the growing volume of production data hinders efficient analysis\. The main objective of this paper is to develop a conversational agent based on Recall Augmented Generation \(RAG\) technology, integrating a linguistic rule generation module capable of leveraging local knowledge bases to provide reliable, evidence\-based responses\. The study focuses on generative artificial intelligence applied to quality management\. The methodological strategy combined theoretical methods such as analytical\-synthetic, inductive\-deductive, and document analysis, along with empirical methods such as interviews\. The system was designed using the Scrum agile approach, incorporating design patterns, modular architecture, and coding standards\. The results obtained demonstrate that the conversational agent improves efficiency and objectivity in decision\-making by transforming historical data into structured and understandable information through linguistic summarization and rules\. The tests conducted, along with expert validation, confirmed the solution&\#x27;s effectiveness\.

## [Influence of intrinsic factors on at\-sea behavior of late chick\-rearing emperor penguins \(Aptenodytes forsteri\) at Cape Crozier, Antarctica](../publications/14175de4e507bb0ccb40.md)

Parker Forman; David R\. Thompson; Kimberly T\. Goetz; Markus Horning; Matthew H\. Pinkerton; Birgitte I\. McDonald

Intrinsic differences among individuals can shape how marine predators forage in heterogeneous environments\. For emperor penguins at Cape Crozier, the southernmost breeding colony in the Ross Sea and a potential climate refuge, the influence of sex, size, and body condition on at\-sea behavior during late chick\-rearing is unknown\. Using data from eight emperor penguins, we identified two behavioral groups through cluster analysis; both traveled comparable distances from the colony but differed in dive depth, dive rate, and the use of the seafloor\. Group membership was associated with sex but not defined by it, as behavioral grouping and sex explained different aspects of trip behavior\. A Hidden Markov Model \(HMM\) further showed that a simpler parameter set based on horizontal movement \(step length, turning angle\) effectively classified key at\-sea behaviors \(Rest, Foraging, and Transit states\), and revealed that adding dive depth as a parameter did not improve foraging state discrimination\. Penguin dive patterns suggest sex\-based differences: females had higher stroke rates and dived more frequently but shallower, while males dived less frequently but deeper\. Dive depth showed a nonlinear relationship with body condition, with individuals in intermediate condition reaching the greatest depths, while body mass had no detectable effect\. Together, our results provide an initial description of variation in late chick\-rearing foraging behavior at Cape Crozier\. The findings suggest that emperor penguins exhibit different foraging strategies influenced by sex and physical condition, which produces variation in dive behavior and use of bathymetric features\. Such differences could affect how individuals exploit a dynamic marine environment and provide a foundation for understanding the factors that shape emperor penguin foraging behavior\.

The study analyzes the didactic potential of the Internet of Things, sensor monitoring, GIS, remote sensing, artificial intelligence, smart irrigation and digital data analytics\.

## [Tohârlar Üzerine Bir İnceleme](../publications/142326af0bb93e5987e7.md)

Ahmet Yılmaz; Ali TORAMAN

Tohârlar meselesi, Orta Asya ile uzaktan veya yakından belli ölçüde ilgilenen bütün araştırmacıların, ilgisini çeken bir konudur\. Mevzuya duyulan ilgi ve meraktan ötürü hemen hemen herkes Tohârlar hakkında kendince bir şeyler ifade etmiştir\. Bunun nedeni Tohârların, Orta Asya’daki Indo Germen’lerin öncüleri arasında kabul edilmesinden kaynaklanmaktadır\. Esasınsa Tohâr bölge ve millet adı, çok eskilere kadar uzanan bir tabir değildir\. Yüeçih’lerin batıya taraf göçleri esnasında görülen bu deyim, farklı görüşlere neden olmuştur\. Konunun mültaleasından da anlaşılacağı veçhile Tohârların farklı yönlerden ele alınması gerekmektedir\. Nitekim son zamanlarda Tohâristan, Tohârlar ve Tohârca hakkında farklı ülkelerde çok sayıda araştırmacı inceleme yapmaya ve değişik fikirler öne sürmeye başladı\. Konuyla ilgi çalışma yapan tarihçiler için en büyük sorunlardan biri; Tohârlar hakkındaki eski Grek\-Roma kaynaklarında yer alan parça parça sınırlı bilgilerin, Çin yıllıklarındaki bilgilerle birleştirilmesi ve bunların Tohâr diliyle olan bağlarının belirlenmesidir\. Bilâhare, Tohârlar olarak tanımlanan üzerinde tam anlamıyla fikir birliğine varılamayan meseleyi aydınlatacak elle tutulur bir sonuca ulaşılamadı\. Tohâr meselesi bir bütün olarak sınırlı sayıdaki materyale dayanmaktadır ve tespitlerin çoğu geçici hipotezlere sahiptir\. Evvel emirde mevsuk kaynaklardaki bilgilere göre; Tohâr\-Yüeçih ilişkisinin analizi yapılmadıkça, Tohâristan coğrafyasının sınırları belirlenmedikçe, Batı kaynaklarının aktardığı karmaşık ve taraflı bilgiler tekrar ele alınmadıkça, Tohârların dili ve kökenleri hakkındaki fikirler ikna edici olmayacaktır\. Bu çalışmada Tohârların menşei, ilk görüldükleri havali, Yüeçih’ler ile olan münasebetleri ve zamanla tarih sahnesinden çekilmeleri üzerinde durulacaktır\.

## [Wood\-Based Hybrid Construction and Circular Economy: A Three\-Level Framework for Component, System, and Building Design](../publications/143bc2df3d93e471876d.md)

Markku Karjalainen; Hüseyin Emre Ilgın; Teemu Hirvilammi; Sami Pajunen

Hybrid construction is a key strategy for increasing the use of wood in contemporary buildings while meeting structural and regulatory requirements, particularly as building\-level carbon reporting and embodied\-carbon requirements are becoming increasingly important in Finland and other regulatory contexts\. This study aims to examine how wood\-based hybrid construction can be systematically structured to support low\-carbon and circular building practice, distinguishing single component level, system level, and building level strategies\. This research builds on a research, development, and education learning materials project at Tampere University and adopts a qualitative, non\-experimental methodology based on a structured synthesis of peer\-reviewed literature, technical sources, and documented application examples\. The main contribution of this study is a three\-level decision\-support framework that clarifies how wood\-based hybridization can be evaluated across different design scales in relation to structural performance, circular economy mechanisms, and early\-stage design decision\-making\. The results suggest that hybridization effectiveness is scale\-dependent, that higher hybridization levels may provide broader strategic opportunities for regulatory alignment and lifecycle\-oriented design when supported by appropriate system configuration, and that circular economy performance depends on connection logic, adaptability, and material separability rather than material choice alone\. The findings provide a practical reference for architectural design, professional practice, and education\.

## [Inclusion, Exclusion and Flourishing: The Role of Social Pain and Related Emotions](../publications/144786f232838bd1c084.md)

Marco Meneghin

This paper argues that human flourishing is not merely individual but interrelational\. While recent debates emphasise positive affect or individual capacities in well\-being, they tend to underexplore the regulatory role of negatively valenced experiences\. Focusing on social pain—the distress associated with social exclusion and disrupted social bonds—I draw on neuroscientific and psychological evidence showing its affective overlap with physical pain as a shared alarm system\. I argue that this system signals threats to relational conditions fundamental to agency and well\-being\. On this view, social pain plays a central regulatory role, parallel to that of physical pain: it tracks social damage, motivates responses primarily oriented towards repair and reintegration, and operates with social and moral emotions that shape norm\-sensitive interactions\. On this basis, I defend a conception of flourishing as essentially interrelational, in which the maintenance and restoration of social inclusion are structurally central to well\-being and moral agency\.

## [Digital Identity in the Age of Generative AI: A Conceptual Comparative Analysis of the UK, Italy and Poland](../publications/144d27eb08723dcae705.md)

Malgorzata Sulimierska; Ashwinth Sankar; Agata Kocia

Purpose: Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) weakens the assumed link between authenticated identity and reliable organisational evidence\. This conceptual paper reconceptualises digital organisational identity as governance infrastructure that links actors, organisational authority, economic substance, and AI\-mediated evidence in business, accounting and assurance\. Design/Methodology/Approach: The paper adopts a conceptual methodology that combines critical literature synthesis, comparative analysis, and model construction\. Guided by Power’s Audit Society framework, it integrates digital identity, accounting, and AI\-governance literature and compares the UK Trust Framework, Italy’s SPID and Poland’s mObywatel to identify key constructs and map their relationships within an identity–evidence trust\-chain model\. Findings: The model shows that authentication does not establish organisational authority or economic substance; GenAI adds provenance risk by enabling credible\-looking evidence to become detached from its underlying event\. Original/Value of the Paper: The paper connects previously separate literatures and integrates four evidentiary construct’s identity, organisational authority, economic substance and AI provenance with second\-order auditability as a mechanism for preserving accountable professional judgement in business\. Research Limitations/Implications: The framework is conceptual and requires empirical validation\. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence Digital Organisational Identity Digital Identity Governance Accounting Evidence Audit Society Professional Judgement National Digital Identity Regimes Assurance Citation: Sulimierska, M\., Sankar, A\. S\. and Kocia, A\. \(2026\): Digital Identity in the Age of Generative AI: A Conceptual Comparative Analysis of the UK, Italy and Poland\. World Journal of Science, Technology and Sustainable Development \(WJSTSD\), Vol\. 21, No\. 6, pp\. 565\-580\.

## [Patient‐Reported Outcome Measures in Musculoskeletal Oncology: Current Concepts, Barriers, and the Future](../publications/144db838c43d267f3d9f.md)

Shujaa T Khan; Rowan J Barker\-Clarke; Brian Benyamini; Zachary D\. C\. Burke; Nathan W\. Mesko; Lukas M\. Nystrom

Patient\-reported outcome measures \(PROMs\) remain underutilized in musculoskeletal oncology, with only 4\.9% of tumor\-focused articles incorporating them\. This review synthesizes current PROM instruments\-including Toronto Extremity Salvage Score, PROMIS, and emerging tools such as the Sarcoma Assessment Measure\-and identifies barriers unique to this population, including psychological distress, workflow complexity, and disease heterogeneity\. Future directions include flexible baseline collection, EHR\-integrated dashboards, national registry linkage, wearable technology, and AI\-driven processing to increase PROMs utilization\.

## [Education System Based on Algorithm \(ESBOA\): Design and Simulation\-Based Evaluation of an Algorithmic Framework for Teaching, Learning, Assessment, and Educational Management](../publications/14508d210af755c1c77d.md)

Sayed Mohammad Kazim Rajaee; Musawer Hakimi

Universities have teaching, assessment, feedback, and management, yet these parts are rarely joined into one explicit and repeatable process\. This paper presents the Education System Based on Algorithm \(ESBOA\), a framework that treats the educational lifecycle as an algorithm: Input, Objective, Instructions, Teaching, Learning, Assessment, Feedback, and Output, with planning, monitoring, reporting, and improvement running through every stage\. The study has three distinct parts\. First, framework development: using a design\-science approach, recurring problems of traditional teaching were traced to six governing principles, an eight\-stage architecture, an input–process–output model, and pseudocode for a bounded corrective\-learning loop with teacher referral\. Its contribution is not a new learning theory but an explicit, auditable procedure that joins objective\-level assessment, a capped feedback cycle, and management reporting, which mastery learning, outcome\-based education, adaptive systems, and learning analytics each address only in part\. Second, computational verification: because the planned pilot has not yet taken place, the loop was verified in a Monte Carlo simulation of 200 synthetic students over 500 replications, followed by sensitivity analyses of feedback gain, ability, difficulty, cycle cap, assessment error, forgetting, and objective dependency\. Under assumed parameters, simulated mean mastery was 0\.57 in a single\-pass course, 0\.83 with the feedback loop, and 0\.86 with student\-level analysis added; these values follow from the model’s assumptions and are not independent evidence of effectiveness\. The benefit of the loop disappeared when feedback carried no information, and the loop required about 2\.3 to 2\.4 corrective cycles per student\. Third, educational effectiveness has not been tested\. A twelve\-month pilot roadmap, evaluation indicators, a risk register, and ethical safeguards are proposed for computer science courses\. The findings support the conceptual and computational feasibility of ESBOA only; whether it improves learning must be established empirically\.

## [DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery](../publications/14516922384f71c31705.md)

Yuxing Chen; Zhisheng Zhang; Cheng Tang; Wei Li; Minghui Zhang; Ziyan Huang; Shaocong Wei; Jiawei Chen; Junru Hu; Hongze Zhu; Jianghan Shen; Min Cen; Xinyuan Zhu; Yaxue Zhao; Jubo Wang; Yuqiang Li; Chun\-Mei Feng; Zongyuan Ge; Rui Su; Jie Xu; Yirong Chen; Xi Xu; Ming Hu

Computational drug discovery requires agents to compose scientific operations and adapt to changing evidence and constraints\. Here we introduce DrugHarness, an evolvable agent harness coupling composable scientific execution with conditional skill induction\. Its environment integrates over 80 scientific operations, biomedical resources and task\-specific code, preserving associations among candidates, results and artifacts\. From execution trajectories and outcome feedback, DrugHarness induces action hypotheses with observable applicability conditions, recommended actions and supporting evidence\. An independent review agent evaluates candidate skills derived from these hypotheses through source verification and, when needed, targeted execution trials\. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks and are revised through feedback\. Evaluation on MolBench and SMDD\-Bench demonstrates capabilities in molecular screening, optimization and constrained design\. Without evolution, DrugHarness exceeds reported MolClaw\-CC results by 10\.8 percentage points in affinity\-comparison accuracy and 55% in mean top\-three active hits on MolBench\. Retrospective evaluation on skill\-development tasks shows that evolution increases Qwen&\#x27;s affinity\-comparison accuracy from 62\.2% to 81\.1% and optimization success from 79\.5% to 87\.2%\. In a prospective HPK1 study, DrugHarness achieves a more favorable median docking score than Biomni among system\-specific candidates\. A synthesized compound achieves a cellular IC50 of 14\.19 nM, a 2\.64\-fold potency improvement over the best input reference, with activity competitive with two selected compounds designed by experienced medicinal chemists\. These results support conditional skill evolution for scientific agents and demonstrate a workflow connecting computational drug design with experimental validation\.

## [AI‑Driven Meta‑Governance: How Autonomous Systems Can Govern Other AI Models in Real Time](../publications/1451a1b0a77ab9c442c5.md)

Sharanya Varatharajan

The increasing deployment of autonomous artificial intelligence \(AI\) systems has created a need for governance mechanisms capable of monitoring, evaluating, and controlling AI behavior in real time\. Traditional governance approaches often rely on predefined policies, periodic audits, and human supervision, which may be insufficient for complex, rapidly evolving, and multi\-agent environments\. This paper examines AI\-driven meta\-governance, an emerging approach in which autonomous supervisory systems oversee other AI models and agents to enforce policies, detect risks, and support responsible decision\-making\. It proposes a layered conceptual framework integrating continuous monitoring, policy\-as\-code, automated risk assessment, adaptive enforcement, auditability, and human oversight\. The framework considers governance performance across cybersecurity, healthcare, enterprise digital twins, and decentralized AI ecosystems\. Key evaluation dimensions include policy compliance, violation\-detection accuracy, response latency, scalability, transparency, and accountability\. The study also examines challenges involving cascading failures, conflicting policies, adversarial manipulation, excessive autonomy, and the reliability of AI\-based supervisory decisions\. It argues that effective meta\-governance requires a balance between autonomous enforcement and human control, supported by clear accountability structures, independent validation, and transparent intervention mechanisms\. By connecting AI governance principles with operational control architectures, this study contributes a conceptual foundation for developing adaptive, secure, and trustworthy governance systems for increasingly autonomous AI ecosystems\.

## [Wisdom as Infrastructure: A New Architecture for Longevity and Regeneration](../publications/14591f412bc26252561d.md)

Desiree C\. T\. Cox

Longevity science and regenerative medicine have moved the limits of translational medicine\. The sciences of aging and age\-related diseases, cell and gene therapies, biomaterials, digital phenotyping, and artificial intelligence are expanding what can be measured and modified across the life course\. Yet the field’s decisive bottleneck may no longer be discovery alone\. Technical capacity is advancing faster than the institutional capacity to decide what should count as progress, how uncertainty should be governed, and how biological gains become durable and equitably distributed human benefit\. This perspective advances the proposition that wisdom is infrastructure\. Wisdom is defined here not as intuition or individual authority, but as the organized capacity to integrate heterogeneous evidence, deliberate explicitly about values, anticipate consequences across time, and implement innovation with the people and systems it will affect\. The perspective situates this proposition within a broader architecture of human flourishing and proposes a translational human flourishing framework comprising six integrative and interdependent domains: biological integrity and plasticity; functional capacity and resilience; agency, purpose, and meaning; social connection and participation; enabling environments; and ethical governance and equity\. The framework does not displace mechanistic, disease\-specific, or regulatory endpoints\. It connects them to the full causal pathway through which an intervention becomes meaningful in a human life\. A research agenda is proposed around multidomain outcomes, longitudinal trajectories, implementation and equity, governance indicators, learning health systems, and place\-based translational ecosystems\. The central claim is deliberately ambitious but empirically bounded: longevity and regenerative medicine will fulfill their promise only when the infrastructures that accelerate innovation are matched by infrastructures that give innovation direction, legitimacy, memory, and human purpose\.

## [An Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Short\-Range Rainfall Forecasting in Mumbai’s Monsoon Regime](../publications/145af559894ac3e2490b.md)

Manpreet Kaur Aiden; Sanjeev Thakur; Kasimahanthi Amar Jyothi; Manmeet Singh; Deepti Mehrotra

Abstract Short\-range rainfall forecasting in tropical coastal megacities is a formidable challenge owing to the nonlinear dynamics, strong seasonality, and pronounced interannual variability that characterise monsoon precipitation regimes\. This study develops and evaluates deep learning frameworks for multi\-lead\-time \(D\+1 to D\+4\) daily rainfall forecasting over Mumbai \(72\.88°E, 19\.07°N\), India, a densely populated coastal metropolis where accurate precipitation prediction is directly consequential for flood early warning\. Six forecasting systems namely Random Forest, XGBoost, a one\-dimensional CNN, a Transformer, and two metaheuristically tuned variants of a novel Conv1D–CBAM–BiLSTM–attention Enhanced Hybrid architecture \(GA\-Hybrid and PSO\-Enhanced\) are benchmarked against persistence and climatology references\. The PSO\-Enhanced ensemble is the strongest system at every lead, attaining R² = 0\.636 \(RMSE = 8\.97 mm day⁻¹\) at D\+1 and 0\.454, 0\.373 and 0\.399 at D\+2–D\+4, ahead of the GA\-Hybrid \(0\.626, 0\.428, 0\.352, 0\.385\), the strongest gradient\-boosting benchmark XGBoost \(R² ≤ 0\.561\), persistence \(R² = 0\.572 at D\+1, declining to 0\.049 by D\+4\), and climatology \(R² = 0\.327, lead\-independent\)\. Recurrent\-memory architectures outperform the memoryless CNN and Transformer at every lead, indicating that sequential dependence, rather than attention alone, carries most of the exploitable predictive signal\. For detection of rainfall exceeding the 95th percentile, the two optimised hybrids achieve the highest critical success index at every lead \(up to 0\.403 at D\+1\), considerably exceeding persistence, whose detection skill collapses beyond D\+2\. SHAP attribution shows that D\+1 skill rests chiefly on rainfall persistence and 850–500\-hPa moisture, whose combined importance nearly halves by D\+2\. Benchmarked against GraphCast and NOAA GFS for June–September 2019, the PSO\-Enhanced framework trails the global systems at short lead but attains higher correlation with observations by D\+4 \(r = 0\.61 versus 0\.32 and 0\.25, respectively\), indicating a comparative advantage of the localised, predictor\-rich statistical approach at longer point\-forecast horizons\.

## [Thermal\-inertia Aware Load Balancing with Energy\-memory in Distributed Cloud Systems](../publications/145dd003c2bbc110c9bd.md)

Zryan Najat Rashid

Distributed cloud systems now are used to run data\-intensive, IoT, and real\-time applications, yet the rising computational load presents significant energy and thermal\-management challenges\.It is important to note that existing load\-balancing techniques are based on the instantaneous utilization or power measured and ignore recent history of energy consumption, and delayed behavior of heating and cooling,\.In this work, a lightweight online scheduling framework, Energy\-Memory and Thermal\-Inertia Aware Load Balancing \(EMTI\-LB\), is proposed to include energy use history, first\-order thermal modeling, and energy estimation of tasks, while also accounting for thermal risk and scheduling delay in a single function\.For every incoming task, EMTI\-LB computes the cost of all candidate nodes and selects the node with the lowest predicted cost to which to assign the task\.The O\(N\) scheduling complexity per task is for the method where N is the number of candidate nodes\.The evaluation of EMTI\-LB has been done in CloudSim 5\.0 with 10 different heterogeneous VMs and 500 dynamically\-arrived cloudlets\.Each experiment was run 30 times with EMTI\-LB compared to Random, Round\-Robin and conventional Energy\-Aware scheduling\.EMTI\-LB consumed 125 kWh, achieving energy reductions of approximately 7\.4% compared to Energy\-Aware scheduling \(135 kWh\), 13\.8% compared to Round\-Robin \(145 kWh\), and 21\.9% compared to Random scheduling \(160 kWh\)\.It also lowered thermal violations from 4\.5 \(Energy\-Aware\), 6\.0 \(Round\-Robin\), and 8\.0 \(Random\) to 2\.0 per 100 tasks \(reductions of 55\.6%, 66\.7%, and 75\.0%, respectively\), and reduced SLA violations from 10\.1% \(Random\), 7\.5% \(Round\-Robin\), and 5\.0% \(Energy\-Aware\) to 3\.1%, representing reductions of 69\.3%, 58\.7%, and 38\.0%, respectively\.The results of the ablation showed that the energy needs were higher for both with the removal of thermal inertia \(132 kWh\) and energy memory \(137 kWh\)\.The results show that using energy memory with thermal inertia can enhance energy efficiency, maintain thermal stability and ensure the quality of the service, without requiring the usual training and computationally intensive optimization\.

## [การใชแอปพลเคชน Quizlet เพอพฒนาความสามารถในการอานออกเสยงและการจำความหมายคำศพทภาษาองกฤษของนกเรยนชนมธยมศกษาปท 2](../publications/146199cc23b26e997416.md)

This study aimed to 1\) examine students&\#x27; English vocabulary pronunciation and meaning retention, 2\) compare these abilities before and after using the Quizlet application, and 3\) investigate students&\#x27; satisfaction with the intervention\. The target population comprised 16 eighth\-grade students at Ban Fang Teun School, Phan District, Chiang Rai Province, during the second semester of the 2024 academic year, selected through purposive sampling\.
