## [Scalable Levenberg\-Marquardt Training Framework for Deep Learning](../publications/146831d4cf850c05fca5.md)

Xianghao Wang; Johan Barthélemy; John Taylor

The Levenberg\-Marquardt \(LMA\) algorithm is a widely used nonlinear least\-squares solver known for its rapid convergence\. For small\-scale neural networks, LMA provides better convergence and architectural robustness than first\-order optimizers like Adam\. However, LMA imposes prohibitive memory and computational costs\. These costs are primarily from the Jacobian matrix, whose dimensions scale with both the number of samples and parameters\. This bottleneck prevents its use in large\-scale neural networks\. Recent efforts scale LMA using preconditioned conjugate gradient \(PCG\) solvers to avoid materializing the Jacobian\. However, PCG only approximates the solution, requiring many network propagations and a task\-specific preconditioner\. Other studies optimize LMA to reduce costs, but they restrict their methods to specific tasks or network architectures\. As a result, LMA remains impractical for training general large\-scale neural networks\. In this paper, we propose LeMA, a distributed LMA algorithm for large\-scale neural network training on multi\-GPU platforms\. Our contributions are twofold: First, an exact dual formulation of LMA removes the memory dependence on the parameter dimension\. Second, a Jacobian sharding strategy computes Jacobian shards on the fly and in parallel to avoid materializing the full Jacobian\. For large\-scale neural networks, LeMA reduces the memory footprint of LMA from quadratic in the number of parameters to quadratic in the batch size\. This makes exact LMA steps feasible for billion\-parameter models without approximate PCG solves\. Furthermore, for a convolutional neural network with 1,000,022,632 parameters on an 8\-GPU node, LeMA achieves a 7\.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to a 99\.7% strong scaling efficiency\.

## [Penerapan Clay Art dan Painting Therapy dalam Kegiatan Penguatan Kesehatan Mental Mahasiswa](../publications/146b1e1b507c60166bb6.md)

Silfia Mona Aryani; Nadhifia Iryadini Rohadatul &\#x27;Aisy; Ambar Mulyono; Ayu Fibramantya Adi; Lulu Purwaningrum; Anugrah Aji Pratama; Retno Pangestuti; Kusnul Rosita

One in eight people worldwide suffers from a mental disorder\. This condition also appears at the university level, as students experience increased academic pressure\. Negative perceptions of mental disorders lead to shame, fear, or reluctance among sufferers to seek help\. Educational institutions are expected to provide therapies such as assertiveness training and relaxation training\. This article discusses community service activities in the form of clay art and painting therapy to raise awareness of student mental health\. The activities provided participants with the opportunity to create clay works and watercolor paintings while expressing their mental distress\. The art therapy concluded with counseling between participants and therapists from the Surakarta Psychology House\. Participants found art therapy to be highly beneficial in helping them reduce anxiety, leading to feelings of greater relaxation, well\-being, and happiness\. Despite remaining concerned about the outcome and the judgment of others, this activity taught participants to enjoy the process, be grateful for everything they&\#x27;ve gone through, calm themselves, and appreciate the result, as the process is what matters most\. Participants also found the art therapy activity enjoyable and a welcome distraction from their busy student schedules\. The experience was deemed highly engaging, as participants learned various ways to manage stress, anxiety, and other negative feelings through art therapy, and found it a way to release negative emotions\.

## [UN SDG WITHIN CONTEMPORARY CORPORATE FINANCE: THE GAP BETWEEN DISCLOSURE AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION](../publications/14760945872aa8c64c50.md)

Glib Aleksin; С\.А\. Лубковський; Вікторія Віталіївна Чепка

Problem setting\. A decade after the adoption of the 2030 Agenda, companies have embedded sustainability principles into mainstream corporate reporting, while the financial effects of this transition remain considerably less certain\. The growing financing needs associated with the Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\), together with the recent weakening of several sustainable finance indicators, make it increasingly important to distinguish between declared corporate commitment and actual capital allocation\. Aim\. This study aims to assess this divergence, focusing on the relationship between SDG\-related corporate commitments and observable financing and investment outcomes in contemporary corporate finance\. Methodology\. The study applies documentary, comparative, and structural\-dynamic analysis to aggregate open\-source data for 2015\-2025 and examines five interconnected layers, namely, corporate disclosure, labelled debt issuance, sustainable fund flows, pricing signals, and real investment\. Results\. The results show that sustainability reporting has become near\-universal among the world’s largest companies – 96% of the G250 report on sustainability; among G250 companies that report on sustainability or ESG matters, 74% use the SDGs\. At the same time, sustainable bond issuance declined by 19% in 2025 to approximately USD 866 billion, while total global bond issuance increased by almost 11% to more than USD 10 trillion\. Sustainable funds recorded USD 84 billion in net outflows in 2025, while SDG\-related FDI in developing economies fell by 26% in 2024\. Annual labelled issuance is equivalent in scale to approximately 20\-25% of the estimated USD 4 trillion annual SDG financing gap, although this comparison does not measure actual gap coverage\. The findings demonstrate a descriptive divergence between mature sustainability communication and several downstream indicators of financing and investment\. Practical value\. This study demonstrates that corporate treasurers, investors, regulators, and development finance institutions should assess disclosure, labelled instruments, investor commitments, and real investment separately when evaluating the financial contribution of business to the SDGs\.

## [Distinguishing FDA Expedited Program Designations from Marketing Authorization: Orphan Drug, RMAT, and Priority Review in a Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Cell Therapy](../publications/147651c12e477940e177.md)

Mudra Gautamkumar Naik; Mansi Ketankumar Patel; Peivand Pirouzi

A persistent source of confusion in rare disease drug development, among sponsors, investors, and the public alike, is the conflation of expedited\-program designations with marketing authorization itself: a product can hold Orphan Drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, Priority Review, and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations simultaneously, none of which constitutes or guarantees approval, and each of which serves a distinct and limited regulatory function\. This article uses an allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) to disentangle these designations precisely, with particular attention to the frequently misunderstood distinction between Priority Review, which shortens an agency&\#x27;s target review timeline, and Accelerated Approval, which permits approval based on a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; the product under review holds the former but has never been eligible for the latter, since no accepted surrogate exists for its mechanism\. The article develops this product&\#x27;s full designation and regulatory history as a worked example, proposes a real\-world evidence strategy appropriate to a product advancing entirely on traditional approval standards, and closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals communicating designation status accurately to internal and external stakeholders\.Keywords: expedited programs; Priority Review; Accelerated Approval; Orphan Drug designation; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [THE HUMAN SPECIFIES THE MACHINE EXECUTES : On AI Successionism, the Arithmetic That Forbids It, and the Architecture of the Signer](../publications/147ded8970350b549ebb.md)

M\. TAALABI; Team LLM\-DIPLOMAT

A thesis is circulating in technology, in the longtermist community, and in the marketinglanguage of the AI industry\. It has several names\. The most direct is successionism\. The claim: AI is the successor to humanity\. Not &quot;AI is a tool\.&quot; Not &quot;AI is a mirror\.&quot; Not &quot;AI is a category of system we must govern\.&quot; But:AI is what comes next\. The next dominant intelligence\. The next stage\. This paper argues that the claim fails on two independent grounds: First — the architectural ground\. Succession requires a stable object, a direction, aspecification, and a trust root\. A stochastic system has none of these\. A successor cannotbe signed\. The architecture of every certifiable system already answers the question: thehuman specifies, the machine executes\. Second — the arithmetic ground\. Even if the architectural question were set aside, thescaling path that successionism depends on is bounded by physical constants\. The energytable is not a forecast\. It is a ratio\. The successor cannot be built\. Two arguments\. Both close the same door\. From different directions\. Neither depends on the other\. The paper also names the actor who is proceeding anyway — on the record, with a factory — and states what the response is, and what it is not\.

## [Students’ experiences of supplemental instruction and self\-reported academic performance in Physics within the bachelor of radiography and extended curriculum programme](../publications/1482eb891a9d85bd5d40.md)

Nape Matheko Phahlamohlaka; Vukani Siphesihle Ncwane

Introduction Supplemental instruction \(SI\) in higher education is a co\-curricular activity that supports student learning and improves academic performance in high\-risk modules at the South African University of Technology\. However, there is limited empirical evidence regarding SI and student academic performance in modules such as Physics\. This study aimed to examine students’ satisfaction with SI facilitation, differences in self\-reported academic performance, and factors associated with performance among students participating in SI in the Physics module of the Bachelor of Radiography \(BRad\) in Diagnostics and Extended Curriculum Programme \(ECP\)\. Methods A quantitative, retrospective, observational research design comparing two sequential self\-reported assessment categories among students participating in SI was used\. A convenience sample of 183 students was approached from an eligible population of 350\. Data were collected from April to June 2025 using structured questionnaires available in paper\-based and online formats\. Assessment grades were self\-reported\. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics with a 95% confidence interval, and significance was set at p &lt; 0\.05\. The findings were interpreted through Vygotsky&\#x27;s sociocultural theory of learning\. Results Of the 183 students approached, 81\.42% responded \( n = 149\), after one age\-based exclusion, 148 were included in the analysis\. Among the 108 participants with matched Test 1 and Test 2 data, the median self\-reported grade category was one category higher in Test 2 than in Test 1 \(95% CI: 0–1; Z = −5\.941, p &lt; 0\.001\), with a large effect size \( r = 0\.57\)\. Lecture attendance was moderately associated with Test 1 grades \(rho = 0\.336, p &lt; 0\.001\) and weakly associated with Test 2 grades \(rho = 0\.239, p = 0\.012\)\. Supplemental instruction attendance showed a weak association with Test 2 grades \(rho = 0\.191, p = 0\.048\)\. Furthermore, 91 respondents \(70\.5%; 95% CI: 62\.0%–77\.8%\) agreed that the SI content was aligned with the Physics lecture material\. Conclusion This study found favourable student satisfaction with SI facilitation and positive perceptions of alignment between SI sessions and scheduled Physics lecture content\. The results support the continued provision of SI as a student\-support strategy in the Physics module for the BRad programme and ECPs at the South African University of Technology\.

## [IMPACTO DA SELEÇÃO DE EMBRIÕES EUPLOIDES POR PGT\-A NOS DESFECHOS DA FERTILIZAÇÃO IN VITRO: REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA E META\-ANÁLISE SOBRE IMPLANTAÇÃO, PERDA GESTACIONAL E NASCIMENTO VIVO](../publications/148352b8e9613e0dadf7.md)

Gabriela Tofoli Vieira Machado; Lígia Quintino de Castro; Camila Uler Lavorato; Camila Beatriz Silva Resende Alves; GABRIELLI JOÃO DOS SANTOS; Beatriz Freiria Cabrini; Lara Claudino Fiaschi; Anayara Suzini Francisco; Lívia de Oliveira Alves; Rafaella Michellis

O teste genético pré\-implantacional para aneuploidias \(PGT\-A\) é utilizado na fertilização in vitro \(FIV\) para auxiliar na seleção de blastocistos classificados como euploides\. Este estudo teve como objetivo avaliar o impacto do PGT\-A sobre implantação, perda gestacional e nascimento vivo, comparando\-o à seleção embrionária convencional baseada em avaliação morfológica\. Foi realizada revisão sistemática com síntese quantitativa, seguindo as recomendações PRISMA, nas bases MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, CINAHL e no registro internacional de ensaios clínicos da Organização Mundial da Saúde, considerando estudos publicados até abril de 2026\. Foram identificados 136 estudos, dos quais 120 foram excluídos e 16 incluídos na síntese final, sendo seis ensaios clínicos randomizados e dez estudos de coorte\. Os resultados indicaram maior taxa de implantação por transferência com PGT\-A e menor frequência de perda gestacional clínica\. Em um grande ensaio clínico randomizado, a perda gestacional clínica cumulativa foi de 8,7% no grupo PGT\-A e 12,6% no grupo de FIV convencional\. Entretanto, não foi demonstrado aumento consistente do nascimento vivo cumulativo por paciente ou ciclo iniciado\. Nos pacientes com falha recorrente de implantação, os resultados permaneceram inconclusivos\. Conclui\-se que o PGT\-A pode melhorar determinados desfechos relacionados à transferência embrionária, mas seu impacto sobre o nascimento vivo cumulativo permanece variável e deve ser interpretado considerando as características clínicas e metodológicas dos estudos\.

## [Polar coordinate transformations for machine learning based dark matter subhalo detection in strong gravitational lenses](../publications/149e8a56bf4534f5e17e.md)

J CAMPBELL; Simon Dye; Emma Chapman; Adam Moss

Abstract Strong gravitational lensing provides a powerful probe of dark matter, particularly on small scales where the gravitational effects of dark matter subhalos within galaxies can manifest as perturbations within the extended arcs of gravitationally lensed sources\. We investigate whether transforming lensed images into polar coordinates improves the ability of convolutional neural networks to infer subhalo mass\. We introduce a machine learning architecture that outputs a prediction uncertainty alongside a mass prediction to enable assessment of network reliability\. Using simulated Hubble Space Telescope observations, we compare our models trained on Cartesian and polar representations under different initialisation schemes, noise levels, and subhalo concentrations \(c = 60, c = 30\)\. We find that polar\-transformed inputs consistently yield higher subhalo detection fractions than standard Cartesian images across all tested masses\. For subhalos with mass 109M⊙ ≤ M ≤ 109\.5M⊙, the fraction of subhalos the network is able to detect increases by \~15 per cent\. Pretrained networks outperform randomly initialized networks, and the polar transform consistently improves network performance in both low signal\-to\-noise data and for lower\-concentration subhalos\. These results demonstrate that presenting strong lensing images in a polar representation provides a computationally inexpensive way of improving CNN\-based subhalo detection\.

## [Robotic airship for measurement and validation of a CERN detector stray magnetic field](../publications/14ac70635de6f48aa11c.md)

Francesco Mazzei; Paolo Francesco Scaramuzzino; Luca Bernardi; Fabio Curti; Corrado Gargiulo

The detector caverns of the Large Hadron Collider \(LHC\) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research \(CERN\) are harsh environments for robotic operation: confined, without satellite navigation, close to fragile hardware, and permeated by intense stray magnetic fields that can disturb onboard electronics, actuators, and sensors\. Characterising these fields is a prerequisite for deploying robots in the caverns, and is also relevant to detector operation, since anomalous fringe fields can affect the surrounding infrastructure and particle tracking\. Yet conventional approaches based on fixed sensors, mechanical systems, or manual surveys provide only sparse spatial coverage\. This paper presents a robotic airship that combines a three\-axis Hall\-effect sensor with ArUco marker\-based visual localisation to measure the three\-dimensional stray field in the ALICE \(A Large Ion Collider Experiment\) detector cavern\. Two campaigns were conducted with the magnets at nominal current: static measurements at twenty known positions, isolating sensor accuracy from localisation uncertainty, and dynamic flights over the same instrumented region\. The measurements were compared with an electromagnetic simulation through a dedicated uncertainty\-propagation framework\. The simulation reproduces the transverse field components well \(R 2 = 0\.86–0\.98\), whereas the vertical component shows a lower agreement \(R 2 = 0\.75–0\.79\) and a systematic positive bias of 0\.65–1\.12 mT, more consistent with simplifications in the electromagnetic model than with measurement uncertainty\. These results demonstrate the feasibility of aerial robotic platforms for stray field characterisation in large experimental facilities and lay the groundwork for a fully autonomous survey system\.

## [From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media](../publications/14ae0e4e8b1fde4432d0.md)

Chacko P\. George

Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation\. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system\. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer \(AL\), the Deliberate Layer \(DL\), and the Cultural Language Layer \(CL\)\. In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally\-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response\. Based on a multi\-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group\-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture\. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL\-directed reaction and limit DL\-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation\. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding\.

## [Diabetes‐Related Foot Disease as the Principal Reason for Hospital Admission: 5 Years of Data From a Major Tertiary Hospital in Aotearoa New Zealand](../publications/14b608df6deb68f3e6a1.md)

Michele Garrett; Rinki Murphy; Arier Chi\-Lun Lee; Peter Anthony Lazzarini; Timothy W Kenealy

OBJECTIVE: To examine hospitalisations caused by diabetes\-related foot disease \(DFD\) at the largest tertiary hospital in Aotearoa New Zealand\. METHODS: We analysed hospital admission data for DFD\-caused hospitalisations from Auckland City Hospital \(ACH\), from 1 July 2014 to 30 June 2019, for people 15 years or older, using ICD10\-AM discharge codes and amputation procedure codes\. DFD\-caused hospitalisations were defined where DFD was the principal reason for admission\. Demographic variables and length of stay were also collected\. RESULTS: During the study period, out of the total 11,222 hospitalisations in persons with diabetes, 1605 \(14\.3%\) were DFD\-caused hospitalisations, which included 265 \(16\.5%\) minor amputations and 94 \(5\.9%\) major amputations\. There were a total of 71,033 hospital bed days in persons with diabetes, of which 16,992 \(23\.9%\) hospital bed days were due to DFD\. Median length of stay in days was 4 \(IQR: 1\-8\) for persons with diabetes; 7 \(3\-14\) for DFD\-caused hospitalisations, 13 \(8\-22\) for minors and 17 \(13\-26\) for major amputations\. The DFD\-caused hospitalisation rate per 1000 persons with diabetes increased by 86% from 6\.2 \(95% CI: 5\.2, 7\.2\) in 2014/15 to 11\.5 \(10\.2, 12\.8\) in 2018/19 and combined minor and major amputation rates increased 82% from 1\.1 \(0\.7, 1\.5\) to 2\.0 \(1\.4, 2\.5\)\. The rate of first DFD\-caused hospitalisation was highest for Māori at 7\.5 \(5\.8 9\.5\), followed by Pacific at 5\.3 \(4\.5, 6\.2\) and lowest for European/Other at 3\.7 \(3\.3, 4\.1\) per 1000 person\-years with diabetes\. CONCLUSION: DFD\-caused hospitalisations and amputations made up nearly a quarter of all hospital bed days used by people with diabetes and nearly doubled over 5 years\. The highest rates were found in adults of Māori and Pacific ethnicity\. Most DFD\-caused hospitalisations did not involve amputations \(78%\)\. The high and increasing burden of DFD\-caused hospitalisations suggest surveillance could monitor necessary changes to preventative foot care services\.

## [General Foundation Programs in Oman: A Comparative Study of Standards and Outcomes](../publications/14bdf9dfe7fc302f55d9.md)

Mohamed Elamin

This study primarily aims to compare the Oman Academic Standards for General Foundation Programs \(OASGFPs\) with the draft of the Oman Core Academic Learning Outcomes \(OCALOs\), identifying their similarities and differences and exploring their implications for the expectations and positioning of General Foundation Programs \(GFPs\) in the Oman Qualifications Framework \(OQF\)\. Using a qualitative document analysis approach, the study compares key elements of the two frameworks, including learning outcomes, curriculum structure, subject requirements, and international English language proficiency standards\. The findings suggest that OCALOs can be viewed as a developmental extension of OASGFPs, introducing refined learning outcomes and curriculum innovations, including emerging topics like artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. However, several issues require further consideration, including inconsistencies in specifying instructional time across subjects and the extent of institutional flexibility\. The study also highlights the need to review the targeted international English language proficiency levels to ensure alignment with entry\-level and current postgraduate admission requirements\. Given that OCALOs remain in draft form, the observations presented may assist policymakers, higher education institutions, and GFP educators in refining national foundation program policies and practices in Oman\.

## [İbtidai təhsildə şagirdlərin yaş və fərdi xüsusiyyətlərinə uyğun pedaqoji yanaşmaların təşkili](../publications/14be1455c5df1f4611c9.md)

Leylan Əsgərova

Bu məqalədə ibtidai təhsil mərhələsində şagirdlərin yaş və fərdi xüsusiyyətlərinə uyğun pedaqoji yanaşmaların təşkili məsələsi nəzəri və praktik aspektlərdən təhlil edilmişdir\. Araşdırmada göstərilir ki, ibtidai sinif şagirdlərinin psixoloji, idrak və emosional inkişaf xüsusiyyətləri onların təlim fəaliyyətinə birbaşa təsir göstərir və bu xüsusiyyətlərin nəzərə alınması təlim prosesinin effektivliyinin artırılmasında mühüm rol oynayır\. Məqalədə qeyd olunur ki, şagirdlərin öyrənmə tərzləri, maraq dairələri və fərdi inkişaf tempinin müxtəlifliyi vahid pedaqoji yanaşmanın tətbiqini qeyri\-effektiv edir və diferensiallaşdırılmış təlim strategiyalarının zəruriliyini ön plana çıxarır\. Tədqiqat çərçivəsində diferensiallaşdırılmış təlim yanaşmasının mahiyyəti, onun əsas komponentləri və ibtidai siniflərdə tətbiq imkanları geniş şəkildə izah edilmiş, müxtəlif praktik nümunələr əsasında bu yanaşmanın üstünlükləri əsaslandırılmışdır\. Eyni zamanda inklüziv təhsil prinsiplərinin tətbiqi kontekstində müəllimin pedaqoji fəaliyyətinin daha çevik və fərdiləşdirilmiş şəkildə qurulmasının vacibliyi vurğulanmışdır\. Xüsusi təhsil ehtiyacları olan şagirdlərin ümumi təhsil mühitinə inteqrasiyası zamanı diferensial metodların tətbiqinin əhəmiyyəti xüsusi qeyd edilmişdir\. Nəticə olaraq müəyyən edilmişdir ki, şagirdlərin yaş və fərdi xüsusiyyətlərinə uyğun pedaqoji yanaşmaların sistemli şəkildə tətbiqi onların akademik nailiyyətlərinin yüksəlməsinə, motivasiyasının artmasına və sosial bacarıqlarının inkişafına müsbət təsir göstərir\. Məqalədə həmçinin müəllimlərin peşəkar inkişafı, tədris materiallarının təkmilləşdirilməsi və qiymətləndirmə üsullarının fərdiləşdirilməsi istiqamətində elmi cəhətdən əsaslandırılmış bir sıra təkliflər irəli sürülmüşdür\.

## [Air quality index forecasting under seasonal and long\-term environmental dynamics](../publications/14cec2a88e470a4b8fe4.md)

Shivani Jain

The Air Quality Index \(AQI\) indicates air pollution levels and their associated risks to human health and the environment\. Factors influencing AQI include temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation, air pressure, seasonal variations, changes in industrial and urbanization patterns, and major pollutants such as PM2\.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, and O3\. This paper discusses AQI geography and timing, as well as the relationship between air pollution and climate systems\. It gives special attention to seasonal fluctuations and regional differences in pollution, dispersion, radiative forcing, short\-lived climate pollutants, deforestation, and urbanization\. The study also addresses seasonal and long\-term environmental variations that affect pollutant levels and AQI\. The study recognizes the importance of AQI forecasting for pollution assessment, public information, health protection, resource allocation, enforcement, location ranking, trend analysis, and timely assessment\. The assessment also highlights key challenges, including potential variation in pollutant locations, monitoring difficulties, data reliability, the lack of direct studies on air quality indexes, and limited validation for real\-time applications\. To develop efficient air\-quality management plans and provide precise, trustworthy air\-quality forecasts, it is crucial to understand these environmental and temporal factors\.

## [ANALISIS FAKTOR\-FAKTOR YANG MEMPENGARUHI IMPLEMENTASI SEABED WARFARE DALAM MENGHADAPI ANCAMAN MULTIDOMAIN DI INDONESIA](../publications/14d2b09e2b6686b1a1aa.md)

Azi Wardiana; Goki P\. Sihombing; Manahan Budiarto Pandjaitan

Perkembangan karakter ancaman multidomain telah menempatkan dasar laut sebagai ruang strategis yang semakin penting dalam keamanan maritim\. Infrastruktur kritis bawah laut, khususnya kabel komunikasi dan pipa energi, memiliki nilai strategis tinggi karena gangguan terhadapnya dapat menghasilkan dampak berantai terhadap komunikasi, ekonomi, komando dan kendali, serta ketahanan nasional\. Dalam konteks Indonesia sebagai negara kepulauan dengan posisi geografis strategis dan kepadatan jalur konektivitas bawah laut, kemampuan seabed warfare menjadi bagian penting dari kesiapan operasi laut\. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis faktor\-faktor yang memengaruhi implementasi seabed warfare di Indonesia berdasarkan rumusan masalah kedua penelitian\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan memanfaatkan hasil wawancara, observasi, studi dokumentasi, serta analisis faktor internal\-eksternal melalui SWOT yang terdapat dalam Taskap\. Kerangka teoritis menggunakan teori implementasi George C\. Edwards III, Mazmanian dan Sabatier, Merilee S\. Grindle, teori strategi Arthur F\. Lykke, serta perspektif perlindungan infrastruktur kritis dan keamanan maritim\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi seabed warfare dipengaruhi oleh faktor internal dan eksternal yang saling berinteraksi\. Faktor internal utama meliputi keterbatasan Underwater Domain Awareness \(UDA\), belum tersedianya jaringan sensor dasar laut tetap yang terintegrasi, belum optimalnya doktrin dan konsep operasi, keterbatasan kemampuan dibandingkan luas wilayah laut, belum adanya satuan respons cepat khusus, belum real\-time\-nya data hidro\-oseanografi, serta fragmentasi koordinasi antarlembaga\. Faktor eksternal meliputi perkembangan teknologi UUV, sensor akustik dan kecerdasan buatan, peluang kerja sama dan transfer teknologi, penguatan industri pertahanan, kebutuhan regulasi perlindungan Critical Underwater Infrastructure \(CUI\), dinamika geopolitik Indo\-Pasifik, serta meningkatnya ancaman sabotase dan aktivitas wahana bawah laut asing\. Analisis SWOT menempatkan posisi TNI Angkatan Laut pada Kuadran II dengan skor sumbu X \-0,21 dan sumbu Y 0,04 sehingga strategi yang relevan adalah turn around strategy, yaitu memanfaatkan peluang eksternal untuk mengatasi kelemahan internal\. Implementasi seabed warfare dengan demikian memerlukan pendekatan terintegrasi yang menggabungkan teknologi, doktrin, sumber daya manusia, tata kelola, koordinasi sipil\-militer, dan sistem informasi maritim\.

## [Martha C\. Nussbaum’s Public Ethics: Lyric Opera and the Dignity of Emotions](../publications/14e061dcc6b0ddfd367a.md)

Fabrizia Abbate

The aim of this contribution is to shed light on the public role of emotions as it emerges from Martha C\. Nussbaum’s philosophical and political reflections\. Democratic and just societies are not solely reliant on laws and institutions; they are also contingent on the collective emotions that underpin their public values\. Shared feelings are needed to unite citizens, ensuring cooperation and respect\. However, alongside positive emotions such as civic love, critical patriotism and social gratitude, there is a risk of negative emotions that are destructive in the public sphere, such as fear, disgust, anger\. Our contribution examines the research conducted by the American philosopher over the past decade, focusing in particular on works such as Upheavals of Thought and Political Emotions, while awaiting the publication of her new book on the connection between social emotions and lyric opera \(forthcoming 2026\)\. Our goal is to reflect on the dignity of emotions through her philosophical and moral interpretation of Operas\.

## [Associations and Additive Interaction of Childhood Trauma and Psychological Resilience With Depression Among Vocational College Students](../publications/14f55a7df807c3dfb8a5.md)

Jiacun Tian; Xiaoping Chen; Danwen Huang; Xiaoyan Qiu

Background: To observe the effects of childhood trauma and psychological resilience on depression in vocational college students, as well as their additive and interactive effects\. Methods: From November 2023 to November 2024, 992 college students from a higher vocational and technical college in Shaoxing were selected using cluster sampling\. An online survey was conducted using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale \(CES\-D\), the 10\-item Connor\-Davidson Resilience Scale \(CD\-RISC\-10\), and the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire\-Short Form \(CTQ\-SF\)\. According to the presence or absence of depressive symptoms, the students were divided into a depressive symptom group and a non\-depressive group\. CTQ\-SF scores, CD RISC\-10 scores, and general characteristics of were compared between the two groups to analyse factors associated with depressive symptoms among higher vocational college students\. The additive interaction between CTQ\-SF and CD\-RISC\-10 scores in relation to depressive symptoms was also analysed\. Results: Among the 992 vocational college students, the incidence of depressive symptoms was 19\.86% \(197/992\)\. The CTQ\-SF score was higher in the depressive symptom group than in the non\-depressive group \(p &lt; 0\.05\), and the CD\-RISC\-10 score was lower in the depressive symptom group than in the non\-depressive group \(p&lt; 0\.05\)\. The depressive symptom group was older than the non\-depressive symptom group and had higher proportions of students with monthly living expenses &lt;1000 yuan, average or poor relationships with classmates, and divorced or widowed parents \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that age \(odds ratio \(OR\) = 1\.179, 95% confidence interval \(CI\): 1\.072–1\.295\), average or poor relationships with classmates \(OR =3\.197, 95% CI: 2\.038–5\.015\), and having divorced or widowed parents \(OR = 3\.208, 95% CI: 1\.788–5\.756\) were risk factors for depressive symptoms among vocational college students \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Monthly living expenses \(OR = 0\.264, 95% CI: 0\.168–0\.416\), sexual orientation \(OR = 0\.740, 95% CI: 0\.551–0\.993\), and CD\-RISC\-10 score \(OR = 0\.306, 95% CI: 0\.187–0\.502\) were protective factors for depression symptoms among vocational college students \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The additive interaction analysis yielded relative excess risk due to interaction \(RERI\) =–0\.001, attributable proportion due to interaction \(AP\) =–0\.002, and synergy index \(S\) = 1\.003, indicating no additive interaction between CTQ\-SF and CD\-RISC\-10 scores in relation to depressive symptoms among vocational college students\. Conclusions: CTQ\-SF and CD\-RISC\-10 scores showed no additive interaction in relation to depressive symptoms among vocational college students\.

## [Large\-scale functional overlap between dorsal and ventral object\-responsive networks](../publications/14f8851c58b80b3d24ca.md)

Claire Simmons; Marlene Behrmann; Vladislav Ayzenberg

The processes of acting on and recognizing objects have traditionally been attributed to dorsal and ventral visual pathways, respectively\. Although extensive evidence suggests that the two pathways interact, the extent and the strength of these interactions across whole\-brain networks remain unclear\. In two experiments, we characterized the whole\-brain network connections of object\-selective regions in each pathway using functional magnetic resonance imaging data acquired while participants viewed objects\. Here, we show substantial spatial overlap in connectivity networks generated from the dorsal and the ventral seed region—with greater similarity between object networks within an individual than each network shows across individuals\. This overlap persists across viewing of tools and non\-tools and even after controlling for the shared variance between pathways\. Together, these findings reveal that dorsal and ventral pathways form highly overlapping and distributed networks in the service of object perception\.

## [Observed readmission timing and diagnostic profiles among high\-risk adolescents and general child and adolescent inpatients: a 10\-year cohort study](../publications/14fbde9f35651d62de5b.md)

Gyula Sófi

Background Rehospitalization is a key indicator of clinical instability in child and adolescent psychiatric populations, yet most studies focus on its occurrence rather than its timing and diagnostic context\. It remains unclear whether high\-risk adolescents and general child and adolescent inpatient populations show distinct patterns of clinical instability beyond differences in rehospitalization frequency\. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a 10\-year inpatient dataset from a national child and adolescent psychiatric center\. A general inpatient cohort \(N = 4016\) was compared with a high\-risk cohort \(N = 570\) defined by at least one police\- or justice\-related admission during the observation period\. Rehospitalization rates, observed time to first readmission, length of stay, and diagnostic categories were examined\. Results Admission\-frequency distributions were broadly comparable between cohorts and did not differ significantly overall\. Among rehospitalized patients, the median observed time to first readmission was 19 days in the high\-risk cohort and 190 days in the general inpatient cohort\. Length of stay was comparable between cohorts\. Diagnostic\-category distributions differed significantly between cohorts \(χ²\(3\) = 2038\.04, p &lt; 0\.001; Cramér’s V = 0\.667\), with externalizing and substance\-related disorders predominating in the high\-risk cohort \(76\.7%\) and developmental–emotional disorders predominating in the general inpatient cohort \(66\.7%\)\. Conclusions The two clinically defined inpatient cohorts showed different patterns of rehospitalization and diagnostic characteristics\. Among rehospitalized patients, the observed median interval to first readmission was shorter in the high\-risk cohort; however, this descriptive difference should be interpreted in the context of substantial baseline age differences and unequal opportunities for observing readmission within pediatric psychiatric care\. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of considering observed readmission timing alongside diagnostic characteristics, while recognizing the limitations of unadjusted retrospective comparisons\.

## [Therapeutic role of norepinephrine infusion and 28\-day mortality in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: A pharmaco\-epidemiological cohort study with overlap weighting](../publications/14fc994efd4e71b205d8.md)

Peng Xue

Abstract: Background: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage \(aSAH\) is frequently complicated by hemodynamic instability and impaired cerebral perfusion, which may require vasoactive support\. However, the association between norepinephrine \(NE\) exposure and short\-term mortality in aSAH remains uncertain\. Objectives: To evaluate the association between NE infusion and 28\-day all\-cause mortality among patients with aSAH treated with endovascular embolization, while accounting for baseline severity and measured confounding\. Methods: This single\-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with aSAH who underwent endovascular embolization at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, China, from January 1, 2022 to August 31, 2025\. Patients were classified according to NE administration during the acute hospitalization\. The primary outcome was 28\-day all\-cause mortality\. Survival was compared using Kaplan\-Meier curves and log\-rank tests\. Cox proportional hazards models were fitted in crude, adjusted and fully adjusted forms\. Propensity score\-based overlap weighting was applied as a sensitivity analysis to improve covariate balance; balance was evaluated using standardized mean differences \(SMDs\)\. Results: A total of 259 patients were included in this study, of whom 67 received norepinephrine\. The 28\-day mortality rate was higher in the NE group than in the non\-NE group \(47\.8% vs\. 15\.7%, P&lt;0\.001\)\. After full adjustment for laboratory and other relevant covariates, NE use remained associated with an increased risk of 28\-day mortality \(HR=2\.892, 95% CI: 1\.566\-5\.338, P&lt;0\.001\)\. Consistent results were observed in the overlap\-weighted \(OW\) analysis \(HR=2\.211, 95% CI: 1\.218\-4\.015, P=0\.009\)\. No significant interactions were identified in the subgroup analyses\.Conclusion: NE infusion was associated with higher 28\-day mortality in patients with aSAH\. Because NE use may also indicate severe hemodynamic instability, these findings should be interpreted as an association rather than proof of causality\. Prospective studies with detailed dose\-duration data are needed\.

## [Quality, Reliability, and Safety of a Commercial Evidence\-Grading Artificial Intelligence System for Cardiovascular Decision Support: An Independent Proof\-of\-Concept Evaluation Using Simulated Cases](../publications/15011b9ec213040cdd06.md)

Ayşe Hüseyinoğlu Aydın; Fatih Aydın

This dataset accompanies a vignette\-based evaluation of AI\-generated responses to 40 simulated cardiovascular cases covering coronary artery disease, heart failure, and arrhythmias\.The Excel file contains case identifiers, age, sex, disease category, clinical severity category, age group, and individual scores from three cardiologist raters across eight evaluation domains: medical accuracy, factual accuracy, completeness, clarity, urgency, language quality, absence of false claims, and absence of harm\. It also includes individual Global Quality Scores \(GQS\), calculated mean scores, and binary harmfulness assessments\.The accompanying vignette document provides the clinical scenarios used in the evaluation\. Case identifiers correspond across the files, enabling linkage between each vignette and its associated ratings\.All cases are simulated and contain no identifiable patient information\. Column abbreviations ending in R1, R2, and R3 denote the three raters; columns ending in Mean contain the corresponding average scores\.

## [Stewards of Data: A Practical Handbook for Undergraduate Researchers in Engineering and Applied Sciences](../publications/150feb2951aba244f50e.md)

Şenay Purzer; Wei Zakharov; Carla Zoltowski

Filled with actionable guides and real\-world examples, Stewards of Data: A Practical Handbook for Undergraduate Researchers in Engineering and Applied Sciences allows readers to utilize the provided templates and guides almost immediately\. In today’s world, data is ubiquitous and AI is growing exponentially\. Practicing ethical data management is, therefore, crucial\. Ensuring that data is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable is essential\. This book is an interdisciplinary effort aimed at embedding ethical data life\-cycle management education into undergraduate research\. The authors present a Data Steward Framework, which serves as a guide for undergraduate researchers, the graduate students who mentor them, postdocs, and faculty\. The toolkit prompts mentors and undergraduates to reason through ethical considerations, future consequences, and trade\-off decisions as they plan, collect, describe, manage, visualize, curate, and share their data\.

## [Digital educational games in veterinary education: a scoping review with comparison to human medical education](../publications/1511163efbe95d28f996.md)

Ingrid Toftaker; Karin Berggren; Lena‐Mari Tamminen

Inroduction Game\-based learning, including approaches such as serious games and gamification, is used to enhance engagement and learning in education\. While its use in medical education has been reviewed, its application in veterinary education remains underexplored\. This scoping review summarizes the use of digital game\-based learning in veterinary medicine\. Methodology Searches of Web of Science, Medline, and Scopus were conducted, following the Population/Concept/Context framework and PRISMA\-ScR guidelines\. Thirteen veterinary education publications were identified and compared to 177 human medical education articles\. Results In both fields, games were mainly used in clinical sciences, with common types including simulations and case\-based learning covering diverse topics\. Ten veterinary studies included evaluations, with six assessing learning outcomes, and eight examining affective outcomes such as motivation and confidence\. Cognitive findings were mixed, while some studies reported positive effects on learning outcomes, others found no significant differences, and one study reported lower scores in part of the assessment for the intervention group\. Control groups that did not interact with the game were included in only two of the veterinary studies and only one used a systematic allocation procedure\. Access to games was often poorly documented\. Discussion Overall, the included studies suggest that game\-based learning is generally well\-received and may enhance learning, although one study reported low uptake of the game activity\. However, further research is needed to determine the conditions that optimize its effectiveness\. Systematic review registration https://osf\.io/cnpk5/overview \.

## [Tezepelumab alters airway epithelial transcriptional responses and epithelial–smooth muscle signalling in uncontrolled asthma](../publications/151df57c5a3274ef6a97.md)

Sangeetha Ramu; Sara Vázquez‐Mera; Mandy Menzel; Samuel Cerps; Juan José Nieto‐Fontarigo; Morten Winther Hvidtfeldt; Celeste Michala Porsbjerg; Asger Sverrild; Lena Uller

Background Tezepelumab is a monoclonal antibody that targets thymic stromal lymphopoietin \(TSLP\)\. It reduces airway hyperresponsiveness, eosinophilia, mucus plugging, and asthma exacerbations, which are commonly caused by viral infections\. Although clinical TSLP blockade attenuates virus\-induced IL\-33 and T2 cytokines in human bronchial epithelial cells \(HBECs\), the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood\. Aim The aim of this study was to identify transcriptomic changes modulated by tezepelumab in HBECs and determine their downstream remodelling\-related effects on bronchial smooth muscle cells \(BSMCs\)\. Methods HBECs from patients with uncontrolled asthma before and after 12 weeks of tezepelumab \( n = 13\) or placebo \( n = 13\) were expanded in vitro as submerged monocultures and subsequently exposed to poly\(I:C\)\. Transcriptomic profiling was performed, and selected targets were validated at mRNA and/or protein levels\. Conditioned media from HBECs were applied to BSMCs to assess the expression of remodelling\-associated mediators\. Results Tezepelumab treatment downregulated S100A8 and S100A9 expression in unstimulated HBECs\. Following poly\(I:C\) stimulation, exploratory transcriptomic analysis identified enrichment of TNF\-α/nuclear factor kappa B \(NF\-κB\)\-related pathways in placebo\-treated HBECs compared with tezepelumab\-treated HBECs\. Validation analyses showed variable responses across the cohort, with attenuation observed primarily in patients with higher baseline inflammatory responses\. In separate gain\-of\-function experiments, recombinant TSLP enhanced poly\(I:C\)\-induced expression of S100A8, S100A9, TNFSF15, and TRAF1, together with increased NF\-κB activation\. Furthermore, conditioned media from poly\(I:C\)\-stimulated HBECs collected after tezepelumab treatment induced lower TGF\-β2 gene expression in BSMCs than conditioned media from placebo\-treated HBECs\. Conclusion Clinical TSLP blockade by tezepelumab was associated with altered epithelial transcriptional responses and reduced TGF\-β2 gene expression in BSMCs exposed to epithelial conditioned media\. These findings are hypothesis\-generating and provide transcriptional insight into the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic benefits in asthma management\.

## [User experience and early adoption of an artificial intelligence application: a mixed\-methods sentiment analysis of DeepSeek reviews on Google Play](../publications/1522c1474e2e579372ee.md)

Amrollah Shamsi; Ting Wang; Sarah Abou Karroum; Narayanaswamy Vasantha Raju

Purpose The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence \(AI\) chatbot applications has transformed digital information access, yet the theoretical understanding of how users evaluate new AI tools during early adoption remains limited\. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model and Expectation Confirmation Theory, the study aims to address a conceptual gap regarding mixed sentiment and explore how demographic factors, such as gender, shape user experience during early adoption\. Design/methodology/approach A mixed\-methods approach was used to analyze 1,000 Google Play Store reviews\. Reviews were categorized by sentiment: positive, negative, mixed \(both positive and negative statements\) or neutral\. Gender predictions were also made from usernames to explore demographic differences in sentiment\. Findings Of the 1,000 reviews, 487 were mixed reviews \(48\.7%\), 373 were negative reviews \(37\.3%\), 139 were positive reviews \(13\.9%\) and one was neutral \(0\.1%\), indicating that mixed and negative sentiment predominated\. Users were mostly satisfied with DeepSeek’s usability and output quality, but criticized its performance and stability issues\. Female users gave more negative reviews than male users \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Research limitations/implications The analysis was conducted on a stratified sample of 1,000 “most relevant” Google Play reviews from a short early adoption period, which may not accurately represent later user experiences or experiences on other platforms\. Only reviews from phone users were included, and the neutral sentiment category contained too few cases for comparison\. Gender inference was based on usernames and reflects predicted rather than self\-identified gender\. Therefore, the results should be interpreted as indicative of early user perceptions rather than long\-term attitudes\. Practical implications The findings indicate that infrastructure reliability is the primary determinant of early user satisfaction\. Transparent communication about service limitations is recommended prior to large\-scale deployment\. For policymakers, the equity implications of performance\-unstable free AI services warrant attention, particularly for users with limited access to alternatives\. Originality/value The mixed\-methods analysis of early DeepSeek user reviews, which distinguishes between mixed sentiment and positive and negative feedback, and incorporates a gender\-based comparison, provides timely insight into user expectations and challenges during early adoption, supporting the development of more user\-centered and stable AI systems\.

## [Bağlanma stilleri ile sosyal medya bağımlılığı arasındaki ilişkide duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve FoMO’nun seri aracı rolleri](../publications/152b39f14bd19e9c6b06.md)

Şahabettin MUTLU; Sevgi Bayazit; Eşref Enes Kuyumcu

Bağlanma stilleri, duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve gelişmeleri kaçırma korkusunun \(FoMO\) sosyal medya bağımlılığıyla ilişkili olduğu bilinmekle birlikte, bu değişkenlerin söz konusu ilişkide birlikte nasıl bir örüntü gösterdiği yeterince açıklığa kavuşmamıştır\. Bu doğrultuda, araştırmada bağlanma stilleri ile sosyal medya bağımlılığı arasındaki ilişkide duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve FoMO üzerinden tanımlanan ayrı ve seri dolaylı ilişkiler incelenmiştir\. Araştırma, uygun örnekleme yöntemiyle ulaşılan 425 yetişkin katılımcı ile kesitsel ve ilişkisel desende yürütülmüştür\. Veriler Üç Boyutlu Bağlanma Stilleri Ölçeği, Duygu Düzenleme Güçlüğü Ölçeği\-Kısa Form \(DDGÖ\-16\), Sosyal Medyada Gelişmeleri Kaçırma Korkusu Ölçeği ve Bergen Sosyal Medya Bağımlılığı Ölçeği kullanılarak toplanmıştır\. Verilerin analizinde Pearson korelasyon analizi ve Hayes PROCESS Macro \(Model 6\) seri aracılık analizi kullanılmış; yaş ve cinsiyet kontrol degişkeni olarak dahil edilmiştir\. Bulgular, her üç bağlanma stili ile sosyal medya bağımlılığı arasındaki ilişkide duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve FoMO üzerinden tanımlanan ayrı dolaylı ilişkilerin anlamlı olduğunu göstermiştir\. Bunun yanında, duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve FoMO üzerinden tanımlanan seri dolaylı ilişkiler güvenli bağlanma \(%95 GA \[−0\.084, −0\.024\]\), kaçıngan bağlanma \(%95 GA \[0\.009, 0\.045\]\) ve kaygılı\-kararsız bağlanma stilleri \(%95 GA \[0\.032, 0\.092\]\) için de anlamlı bulunmuştur\. Her iki aracı değişken modele dâhil edildiğinde ise bağlanma stilleri ile sosyal medya bağımlılığı arasındaki doğrudan ilişkiler anlamlı bulunmamıştır\. Bulgular, bağlanma stilleri ile sosyal medya bağımlılığı arasındaki ilişkinin anlaşılmasında duygu düzenleme güçlüğü ve FoMO’nun birbiriyle ilişkili değişkenler olarak birlikte değerlendirilmesinin önemine işaret etmektedir\.

## [Predicting Length of Hospital stay for patients undergoing discectomy surgery using clinical and surgical parameters via machine learning](../publications/15357141a612f36dea5a.md)

Faezeh Mehdipour; Behzad Imani; Alireza Jafarkhani; Samad Moslehi; Ebrahim Rafiei

As one of the most frequent spine procedures, discectomy significantly impacts healthcare systems by extending postoperative length of stay \(PLOS\), which affects both patient recovery and resource management\. This study evaluated machine learning models to identify key clinical predictors and accurately estimate hospital stay duration following discectomy\. Potential factors influencing length of stay were initially gathered from existing literature and verified by a clinical expert panel\. Medical records of 400 patients who underwent discectomy across three medical centers in Tabriz were analyzed\. To address missing data \(&lt; 3\.5%\), simple imputation was applied after removing cases with high missingness\. Data were partitioned into an 80% training set \( n = 320\) and a 20% independent hold\-out test set \( n = 80\), with 5\-fold cross\-validation applied strictly during training\. Six predictive algorithms—Linear Regression, LASSO Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\), and Deep Neural Network \(DNN\)—were developed and evaluated\. Model interpretability was further examined using global SHAP analysis\. Postoperative blood loss, intraoperative blood loss, body mass index, age, duration of surgery, surgical instrumentation, and procedure location emerged as the highest\-ranked predictors, whereas blood transfusion had the lowest impact\. On the unseen test dataset, tree\-based ensemble models achieved superior predictive accuracy compared to linear and deep learning approaches\. The Random Forest model demonstrated the best overall performance \(Mean Squared Error: 0\.452, Explained Variance Score: 0\.874, \\\(\\:\{R\}^\{2\}\\\) : 0\.874\), closely followed by XGBoost \( \\\(\\:\{R\}^\{2\}\\\) : 0\.858\), while LASSO \( \\\(\\:\{R\}^\{2\}\\\) : 0\.129\) and linear baseline models yielded lower performance due to non\-linear clinical feature interactions\. Tree\-based machine learning models, particularly Random Forest, offer promising capabilities for predicting hospital length of stay after discectomy\. Identifying these key perioperative drivers can support clinical discharge planning, optimize bed capacity allocation, and improve hospital resource management\.

## [Materiovigilance in India: Current Status and Future Perspectives](../publications/154486210c52dfda8fad.md)

Akash Kumar; Yusra Ahmad; Hiba Parveen; Pragati Bailwal

The systematic efforts to prevent and mitigate the dangers posed by medical devices are one of the principal functions of materiovigilance\. MvPI&\#x27;s inception under the Pharmacovigilance Programme in India was a significant milestone in enhancing the management of medical devices and regulatory intervention for the devices\. The paper explores the roles of some members of the multidisciplinary healthcare team \(physicians, nurses, biomedical engineers, pharmacists, &amp; technical staff\) and the potential device\-related risk\. The paper also explores the influence of maternal vigilance on the regulatory cycle \(recalls &amp; alerts, redesign &amp; modification, &amp; control\) on the Medical Device Rules \(MDR 2017\)\. The paper also explores the current PMS in India and the positive indicators such as the rise in reporting centres, the growing number of reports submitted digitally, and the use of real\-world data\. India has made progress on Reporting Centre closure, Reporting Centre underuse, Reporting Centre untraceability, Reporting Centre manufacturer unaccountability, and Reporting Centre poor hospital culture weak Reporting Centre\. India&\#x27;s progress has been compared to that of other countries in order to highlight India&\#x27;s progress\. This comparison shows that India has made progress in reporting\. ## [Estimating Parameters of Gamma Distribution Using Neural Network](../publications/15555bb6dfa7538bdfb9.md)

Rasha Mohamed Mandouh; Mahmoud Riad Mahmoud; Ehab Rasheedy Ali

Widely used in scientific and engineering domains, the Gamma distribution provides an essential framework for describing waiting\-time mechanisms and positively skewed patterns\. Achieving accurate parameter estimates is therefore critical for maintaining the reliability of statistical inference and improving predictive performance\. In this paper, the classical methods for estimating the gamma distribution are assessed in comparison to a new method of estimation using neural networks\. The integration of Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\) into the estimation process enabled the development of a streamlined yet robust neural architecture capable of simultaneously inferring the key parameters of the Gamma distribution\. This design leverages the ANN’s ability to learn complex nonlinear relationships within the data, allowing the model to capture the underlying distributional structure and perform joint parameter estimation more efficiently than traditional analytical methods\. The ANN neural network uses the concept of matching theoretical and sample quantities to estimate gamma parameters using mean, standard deviation, median, skewness and kurtosis\. An extensive simulation study was conducted to demonstrate the power of the proposed ANN\-based method\. Then, the results of the proposed method were compared to MLE and moment\-based methods\.

## [Fractional\-Order Advection–Diffusion Equations: A Critical Review of Physical Origins, Analytical and Numerical Methods, and Applications](../publications/1557c87a95f10f0268ca.md)

Weiguang Huang

The advection–diffusion equation is the canonical continuum description of transport, yet it fails for a broad class of systems in which particle motion is non\-Fickian\. Fractional\-order advection–diffusion equations replace integer derivatives with operators of non\-integer order and, in doing so, encode long\-range spatial jumps and long\-memory waiting times that classical models discard\. This review provides a critical, evidence\-based synthesis of the field from its foundations in continuous\-time random walks and Lévy motion through the mathematical and numerical landscape\. We first examine the family of fractional operators and the physical meaning of their kernels\. We then trace the micro–macro derivations that connect fractional advection–diffusion equations to anomalous transport, mobile–immobile systems, tempered and variable\-order processes\. Analytical methods and the now\-mature toolbox of finite difference, finite element, spectral, meshless and lattice\-Boltzmann discretizations are appraised for accuracy, stability and computational cost\. Inverse problems and parameter estimation, which decide whether such models earn their extra complexity, are reviewed next\. Applications in hydrology, porous media, plasmas, space physics, heat and mass transfer, biology and finance illustrate both success and unresolved tension\. Throughout, we identify trends—rising use of non\-singular\-kernel operators, machine\-learning solvers and realistic benchmarking—and we flag persistent gaps: inconsistent operator conventions, sparse validation against real data, and scarce higher\-dimensional and multiscale results\. We close with a concrete research agenda for making fractional advection–diffusion models predictive rather than descriptive\. Keywords: fractional calculus; anomalous diffusion; advection–diffusion equation; Lévy motion; Caputo derivative; mobile–immobile transport; finite difference methods; inverse problems\.
