## [Neuromorphic Computing with Interfacial Dynamics in Electrolytic Memristive Synapse](../publications/1579ddfc8396ec9eaaa1.md)

Yi‐Tong Xu; 李明鎬; Chuanjie Yao; Xingyuan Xu; Yijing Cai; Suhang Liu; Lukang Gao; Qiao‐Ping Wang; Xinshuo Huang; Jianing Wu; Hui‐Jiuan Chen; Shudong Yu; Xi Xie

ABSTRACT Brain‐inspired computing demands devices that operate at biological voltages and embody biological principles\. Existing liquid‐based memristors offer ion‐mediated computation yet exceed physiological levels and require rigid matrices\. Here, we report a hydrogel‐confined electrolytic memristive synapse \(EMS\) that leverages reversible Ag/AgCl interfacial electrochemistry for synaptic modulation and reservoir‐state encoding at only 100 mV\. The device exhibits chloride‐ion‐dependent memristive hysteresis and emulates fundamental synaptic learning rules\. Such dynamics provide the short‐term memory and nonlinearity used in a simulated reservoir‐computing framework, achieving 95\.05% accuracy in handwritten‐digit classification and exhibiting good performance under noise and mechanical deformation\. The device conformability and the design flexibility of the electrochemical interface offer new opportunities toward bio‐integrated systems, promising for adaptive human‐machine computing architectures\.

## [A hybrid CNN–BiLSTM network with additive attention for automated four\-stage classification of Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease from brain MRI](../publications/15847b9773e5abacea2b.md)

T\. Deenadayalan; S\. P\. Shantharajah; Swarna Priya Ramu

AD is a progressive and irreversible neurodegenerative disorder\. Because the structural changes that accompany the earliest stages of the disease are subtle and easily overlooked, manual interpretation of MRI is time\-consuming and prone to inter\-observer disagreement\. This study presents an end\-to\-end deep learning framework that fuses spatial and sequential reasoning to classify brain MRI into four clinically meaningful stages: Person with no dementia, Person with very mild dementia, Person with mild dementia, and Person with moderate dementia\. An additive attention mechanism subsequently weights the most informative positions before a compact dense head produces the final decision\. Class imbalance is addressed by capped oversampling of real minority slices combined with residual cost\-sensitive weighting, applied to the training fold only; pixel\-space SMOTE is deliberately avoided because interpolating between two unregistered MRI slices produces images without an anatomical referent\. Exact\-duplicate screening is applied prior to partitioning, and a quantitative near\-duplicate audit is reported for the fixed folds\. Trained on 6,400 grayscale MRI slices under a stratified 70/15/15 protocol, the proposed CNN–BiLSTM–Attention model attains a test accuracy of 95\.94%, a balanced accuracy of 96\.08%, an MCC of 0\.9334, a Cohen&\#x27;s kappa of 0\.9325 and a macro\-averaged one\-vs\.\-rest AUC of 0\.9954, on a slice\-level held\-out test fold\. Per\-class analysis shows strong sensitivity and specificity for the three better\-represented stages; the extremely rare Person with moderate dementia class \(nine test images\) shows a favorable point estimate but is too small to support a claim of robust detection on its own\. Attention maps and Grad\-CAM overlays localize the evidence the network uses, and an error\-structure analysis shows that no misclassification spans more than two stages\. Because the corpus carries no subject identifiers, patient\-grouped partitioning is not possible and the reported accuracies should be interpreted as an upper bound attainable under a slice\-level split; this constraint is quantified explicitly and motivates the external\-validation study outlined in the manuscript\. Overall, the results highlight the methodological value of coupling convolutional feature extraction with bidirectional sequence modeling and additive attention under a leakage\-aware, imbalance\-aware evaluation protocol for multi\-stage AD staging\.

## [The design–stewardship disconnect in urban greening governance: a structured evidence synthesis](../publications/1584dec447b6ff71106d.md)

Xiaoyan Ye; Yian Xu; Jinyuan Tu

While global investments in urban green infrastructure \(UGI\) are accelerating, the long\-term performance of these nature\-based solutions is increasingly compromised by a critical disconnect between initial design and post\-construction stewardship\. To unpack this governance blind spot, this study analyzes 62 peer\-reviewed publications\. Operating under a specific methodological boundary condition, we applied a threshold\-based selection criterion focusing exclusively on high\-impact \(Q1\) journals\. Consequently, this study is explicitly positioned as a structured synthesis of the mainstream theoretical discourse shaping current global UGI policy, rather than a globally exhaustive empirical census\. Records were coded across five critical dimensions: funding, governance, aesthetics, equity, and technology\. Our synthesis reveals frequent co\-occurrences of governance and funding deficits, particularly exacerbating technology gaps and spatial inequity\. Crucially, we identify a structural paradox: capital\-intensive designs frequently intersect with profound institutional and financial barriers, whereas naturalized designs recurrently face strong esthetic friction\. We conceptualize this phenomenon as the “CAPEX\-OPEX divide” in urban environmental governance\. Based on these systemic associations, we advance a comprehensive framework comprising three core stewardship propositions—administrative under\-resourcing, esthetic conflict, and unequal stewardship burdens\. This synthesis shifts the academic and policy focus from mere UGI creation to sustainable, equitable long\-term maintenance\.

## [Integrating hippopotamus optimization algorithm into machine learning frameworks for predicting suspended sediment concentrations](../publications/158fb3c0967ae27a8873.md)

Mohsen Nasrabadi; Yaser Mehri; Ali Abdolrazaq Sabbar; Mohammad Javad Nahvinia; Mohammad Hosein Omid

Abstract The vertical distribution of sediment concentration is a fundamental component of sediment transport hydraulics, directly impacting the estimation of sediment loads in riverine and channel systems\. Therefore, accurate characterization of this distribution remains a critical challenge in hydraulic engineering\. To address this, advanced intelligent modeling techniques offer a robust pathway for reliable prediction\. This study evaluates the performance of six distinct modeling approaches—ORELM, ORELM\-HOA, GPR, GPR\-HOA, GMDH\-ANFIS, and GMDH\-ANFIS\-HOA—to predict the relative sediment concentration distribution \(C/C a ​\)\. Results indicated that the integration of meta\-heuristic optimization significantly enhances the predictive precision of the GMDH\-ANFIS, ORELM, and GPR frameworks\. Comparative analysis reveals that the GMDH\-ANFIS\-HOA model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an RMSE of 0\.0434 and R 2 of 0\.9747 during the training phase, and an RMSE of 0\.0424 and R 2 of 0\.9727 during the testing phase\. The GPR\-HOA model followed as the second\-best performer\. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identified the relative depth \(y/D\) as the most dominant factor influencing model accuracy\. These findings demonstrate that the optimized GMDH\-ANFIS\-HOA model provides a reliable and efficient computational tool for engineers and hydrologists, facilitating improved design and management of irrigation canals, river engineering projects, and sediment\-related environmental assessments\.

## [The Evolution of Biotechnology: Historical Discoveries, Major Milestones, and Recent Advances: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/1591037a5e088c29f174.md)



Biotechnology has evolved from ancient fermentation practices and the domestication of plants and animals into a multidisciplinary field that integrates molecular biology, genetics, engineering, and computational sciences\.This review presents a comprehensive overview of the historical evolution of biotechnology, highlighting the major scientific discoveries, technological milestones, and recent advances that have shaped its development\.Early contributions by Robert Hooke, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, Louis Pasteur, Gregor Mendel, and Karl Ereky established the foundations of cell biology, microbiology, genetics, and industrial biotechnology\.Subsequent breakthroughs, including the elucidation of the DNA double helix, recombinant DNA technology, recombinant human insulin, the Human Genome Project, and CRISPR\-Cas9 genome editing, revolutionized biological research and enabled transformative applications in medicine, agriculture, and industry\.The review further discusses advances in genome engineering, viral and non\-viral gene delivery systems, synthetic biology, regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, bioprinting, biofortification, cellular agriculture, and sustainable biomanufacturing\.Recent innovations involving high\-throughput sequencing, multi\-omics technologies, messenger RNA therapeutics, artificial intelligence, protein structure prediction, and computational protein design have accelerated biological discovery and expanded the capabilities of precision medicine and biotechnology\.The review also examines the emergence of biotechnology regulation, the development of the bioeconomy, and the growing importance of ethical, safe, and sustainable implementation of biotechnology\.Collectively, these developments demonstrate the remarkable progression of biotechnology from traditional biological practices to advanced genome engineering and AI\-driven innovation, emphasizing its critical role in addressing global challenges in healthcare, agriculture, environmental sustainability, food security, and industrial development\.

## [Inteligencia artificial para predecir patrones epidemiológicos: revisión sistemática](../publications/15aa973fa524124eca2d.md)

Estefanny Mishell Santa Cruz\-Alvarez; Valentina Dayanara Rodríguez\-Anangonó; Humberto Alexander Cárdenas\-Villa; Bolívar Fernando Mena Hidalgo

Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre el uso de la inteligencia artificial para predecir patrones epidemiológicos, con énfasis en la salud bucal\. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO \(2012\-2025\); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, análisis de carga de enfermedad, estudios de pronóstico, un ensayo aleatorizado y estudios de predicción\. Resultados: el aprendizaje automático permitió pronosticar el dengue con datos climáticos, y los modelos de proyección estimaron la carga futura del cáncer bucal y cervicouterino\. En odontología, el aprendizaje profundo mostró buen desempeño para detectar caries en radiografías y fotografías\. Conclusión: la inteligencia artificial es útil para la vigilancia y la predicción epidemiológica, pero requiere validación externa, datos representativos y reporte estandarizado\.

## [Psychometric properties of a short knowledge test to evaluate awareness of external ventricular drain care practices among Chinese nurses: a Rasch model analysis of an efficient 7\-item self\-reported assessment tool](../publications/15ab6ddacab123fd7a66.md)

Linlin Wen; 孙媛媛; Xue Du

Background External ventricular drainage \(EVD\) is an important intervention in the management of patients with severe neurological conditions, and standardized nursing care is essential for preventing complications and ensuring patient safety\. Nurses’ knowledge of recommended EVD care practices is an important foundation for safe and evidence\-based care\. However, existing instruments for assessing EVD\-related nursing knowledge are often lengthy or have limited psychometric validation, which may restrict their use in routine clinical assessment and large\-scale training\. Therefore, a brief, reliable, and psychometrically robust instrument is needed to efficiently assess nurses’ knowledge of EVD care practices and identify areas requiring targeted education\. Aim To translate and culturally adapt the Short Knowledge Test to Evaluate Awareness of External Ventricular Drain Care Practices and evaluate its psychometric properties among Chinese nurses using the Rasch model, thereby providing a reliable tool for the rapid assessment of nurses’ self\-reported knowledge of recommended EVD care practices and the identification of targeted training needs\. Method The original scale was translated and culturally adapted into Chinese using the Brislin forward–backward translation method, resulting in the Chinese version of the Short Knowledge Test to Evaluate Awareness of External Ventricular Drain Care Practices \(C\-SKT\-EVD\)\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted among clinical nurses recruited from First Affiliated Hospital of Jinzhou Medical University, Liaoning Province, mainland China\. 242 valid participants included in the final analysis\. Descriptive statistics were performed using SPSS version 26\.0, and the psychometric properties of the scale were evaluated using the Rasch Rating Scale Model in Winsteps version 3\.72\.3, focusing on unidimensionality, item fit, category functioning, item–person distribution, test information function, separation indices and reliability, and differential item functioning \(DIF\)\. Results The empirical variance explained by the measures was 55\.1%, and the eigenvalue of the first contrast was 1\.4, supporting the unidimensionality of the C\-SKT\-EVD\. The Infit mean\-square \(MNSQ\) values for the seven items ranged from 0\.94 to 1\.16, while the Outfit MNSQ values ranged from 0\.94 to 1\.07, all indicating acceptable fit to the Rasch model\. The point\-measure correlation coefficients \(PT\-Measure Corr\.\) ranged from 0\.63 to 0\.70, suggesting good alignment between the items and the underlying latent construct\. The observed average measures across the five rating categories increased monotonically, and the category thresholds were ordered sequentially\. The category probability curves also showed clearly defined peaks, indicating that the rating categories functioned well and that no category collapsing was required\. The item difficulty distribution was generally well matched to the respondents’ levels of self\-reported EVD care knowledge, and the test information function indicated higher measurement precision around the average level of the measured construct, with relatively less information provided for respondents with extremely high or low levels of the latent trait\. Conclusion The C\-SKT\-EVD demonstrated generally acceptable Rasch measurement properties in the present sample of Chinese nurses, providing preliminary evidence for its use as a brief screening and educational assessment tool for self\-reported knowledge of recommended EVD care practices\. However, these findings do not establish comprehensive validity or objective clinical competence\. Further multicenter studies in diverse nursing populations are needed to confirm its broader applicability\.

## [Shift\-Reliance Alignment: Ranking Vision\-Language Models by the Cues They Trust](../publications/15accaefe869d94aa982.md)

Faisal Mohammad; Mohamed Younis

Vision\-language models \(VLMs\) are usually chosen from leaderboards, which give one ranking for every application\. On questions about objects that a scene suggests but does not contain, however, the model with the lowest error on the POPE hallucination benchmark is not the one with the lowest error on such questions\. For yes/no questions about object presence, we show that the best model for a target domain can be predicted without running any candidate on that domain, given 650 to 1,200 labeled target items that calibrate a detector\. We measure each model&\#x27;s reliance on a cue, a feature such as scene context or text in the image, by editing 100 labeled source images so that the cue suggests the wrong answer, and comparing with a matched control edit\. Reliance predicts which VLMs are misled by physical sticker attacks \(Spearman \.93 on nine models not used to design the score\) and which hallucinate on unedited COCO photographs, beyond what their tendency to answer yes explains\. Shift\-Reliance Alignment \(SRA\) scores a model by its source error on the labeled source questions plus its reliance multiplied by the shift\. The shift is the proportion of target questions on which the cue misleads, and a detector estimates it on the unlabeled target images\. SRA selects the model with the lowest score\. In pre\-registered tests on new images where most questions mislead, it lowered the error of the selected model from 30\.4% under selection by source error to 18\.8% on Objects365 and OpenImages but, against its prediction, not on COCO\. On CueDial, a benchmark we release that varies how often a cue misleads, selection by model confidence falls more than 40 percentage points behind the best model when overlaid text denies a visible object, and SRA stays within 3 points\.

## [AI anxiety among university librarians in Bangladesh: A multidimensional assessment using the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale](../publications/15ae798e6fb802e5c61c.md)

Md\. Sakib Biswas; Zakir Hossain; Panorea Gaitanou

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) becomes increasingly integrated into library services, understanding librarians’ psychological responses to this technological transformation has become an important research priority\. This study investigates AI anxiety among university librarians in Bangladesh and examines whether anxiety levels vary across demographic and professional characteristics\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted using the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale \(AIAS\)\. Data were collected from librarians employed in public and private universities in Bangladesh through convenience sampling\. Following data\-quality screening, 138 valid responses were retained for analysis\. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, and one\-way analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) with Bonferroni post hoc tests were employed to examine patterns of AI anxiety and group differences\. Overall, university librarians reported a moderate level of AI anxiety \(M = 3\.00\)\. Anxiety levels were broadly comparable across dimensions, although Sociotechnical Blindness recorded a slightly higher mean score than the remaining dimensions\. Educational qualification and professional experience showed limited overall associations with AI anxiety, while gender, age, and professional designation demonstrated little variation\. The findings suggest that concerns regarding governance, transparency, professional identity, and organizational readiness may be more salient than technological learning challenges\. The study extends research on AI anxiety to a Global South library context and contributes evidence that AI anxiety among university librarians is well understood as an interrelated socio\-professional and organizational phenomenon\. The findings highlight the importance of professional development, institutional support, and responsible AI governance in academic libraries\.

## [Compiling Multi\-Threshold Operators for Quantized Non\-Monotonic and Fine\-Granular Activations in Custom\-Tailored DNN Accelerators](../publications/15c0fbb1ea9f570defb0.md)

Christoph Berganski; Felix Jentzsch; Marco Platzner

Aggressive quantization of neural networks can expose activation functions as bottlenecks for efficient hardware acceleration\. Implementing quantized activations as multi\-threshold operations has been shown to be a promising optimization, allowing for efficient hardware implementation of few\-bit activations\. However, current implementations are limited to monotonically increasing functions, quantization schemes with one\-dimensional \(per\-channel\) granularity and a small set of predefined activation\-quantizer combinations\. We formalize the multi\-threshold representation to extend it to non\-monotonic functions and fine\-granular parameters, i\.e\., multi\-dimensional thresholds\. For automated conversion of quantized function compositions into threshold representation, we propose a systematic approach via algebraic rules integrated into the ONNX\-based compiler infrastructure\. We experimentally validate our solution on a selection of monotonic and non\-monotonic functions by extending the binary search based multi\-threshold operator that is integrated into the FINN framework for end\-to\-end synthesis of custom\-tailored FPGA accelerators\. The cost of hardware support for non\-monotonicity and fine\-granularity is characterized in comparison to an alternative approach utilizing existing operators via graph\-level decomposition\. We compare our method to prior work as well as the approach taken by the hls4ml framework\. As an outlook, we demonstrate the prospects of using the multi\-threshold representation during the training of a neural network as a form of quantization aware training\.

The author engages in scientific polemics with Western and Eastern scholars regarding repressive approaches, corporate criminal liability, and the specific objects of crypto\-theft\. ## [Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty](../publications/15d96124c54379a8c0e0.md)

Chengze Xie; Xuan Wang; Ying Ding; Hairong Wang; Yan Li

We develop a robust reinforcement learning \(RL\) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics\. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes\. Applying our framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer in a simulator calibrated to clinical data, we obtain generalizable and robust policies that substantially outperform the existing adaptive therapy method\. In particular, we attain robustness with almost no loss of performance when the biomarker is accurate and the disease evolves as anticipated, and find that the resulting policy Pareto\-dominates the existing method across a diverse array of scenarios\. Our findings suggest that robust RL holds great promise as a principled methodology for learning reliable adaptive treatment policies\.

## [Phenotyping of the post\-traumatic immune response and therapeutic strategies in a refined murine two\-hit trauma model](../publications/15e36e9febe6265bd3c9.md)

Christina Sophia Schwenk

Trauma and its consequences are one of the leading causes of death among young patients\. The reasons for mortality vary depending on when they occur\. Especially in the later stages of care \(days to weeks after the trauma\), death is often caused by immunological complications\. The two\-hit hypothesis offers an explanation for this\. It classifies the initial trauma as the “first hit” for the immune system, triggering a systemic immune response\. Hereby, the systemic inflammatory response \(SIRS\) and its compensatory mechanism \(CARS\) stand in a fragile balance\. This is significantly influenced by regulatory T cells \(CD4\+ Tregs\) and the interplay between immune cells and platelets\. This delicate balance can be destabilized by “second hits” occurring during trauma therapy \(e\.g\. surgery, reperfusion events, or ICU stay\)\. This promotes complications, with sepsis being one of the most dangerous in this context\. Sepsis is a complex syndrome that includes different immunological phenotypes\. It is currently defined as life\-threatening multiple organ failure based on an infection\-triggered, misdirected systemic immune response\. The treatment of immunological trauma consequences is presently \(2026\) based on a symptomatic approach, as despite extensive research, no causal treatment options have yet been successfully applied and approved in humans\. For this reason, there is still a great need for research to gain a better understanding of the immunological consequences of trauma and thus be able to test targeted causal immunomodulatory treatment options\. This study aimed to model the post\-traumatic immune response, including the development of sepsis, by using a murine two\-hit trauma model, to further investigate it and to examine immunomodulators as potential treatment options\. The animal model consisted of a standardized 3rd\-degree scalding of 20 % of the body surface, followed by sepsis induction via Cecal Ligation and Puncture \(CLP\)\. Due to its classification as a severely stressful animal experiment, the model was optimized in accordance with the 3R principles to minimize stress on the mice\. As promising immunomodulators, the fibrinogen\-splitting enzyme ancrod and the versatile compound curcumin, combined with piperine \(C\+P\), were tested\. It was demonstrated that C\+P significantly improves survival in the two\-hit model\. No corresponding advantage was observed for ancrod compared to the untreated control group\. The comprehensive immunomodulatory properties of C\+P therapy may explain the improved survival rate\. It was shown that C\+P, among other things, influences various T lymphocytes and platelets\. CD4\+ Tregs appeared to be primed for further activation, while pro\-inflammatory signals were reduced by downregulation of CD8\+ T cell and platelet activity\. In addition, the release of predominantly anti\-inflammatory cytokines was increased \(e\.g\. IL\-10\), while some pro\-inflammatory cytokines were found to be diminished \(e\.g\. IL\-6\)\. Under the influence of C\+P, end\-organ damage was also reduced\. Overall, the impression is that C\+P may be able to stabilize the post\-traumatic immune response and thus possibly contribute to maintaining the balance between SIRS and CARS\. With the refined protocol in hand, the two\-hit burn/CLP model was successfully applied to provide initial insight into the therapeutic immunomodulatory potential of C\+P in trauma treatment\. The exact mechanisms and causal relationships remain unclear and shall therefore become the subject of further research\.

## [Front\-resolved mode\-II–III nominal driving\-force evolution and group\-validated machine\-learning prediction for high\-speed railway wheel\-tread cracks](../publications/15eb4d183def300e9233.md)

Closed wheel\-tread cracks can remain compression\-dominated during rolling contact while sustaining substantial in\-plane and out\-of\-plane shear\. A closure\-aware nominal driving force combines event\-paired differences in the mode\-II and mode\-III stress\-intensity factors\. Four arc\-length descriptors summarise its front distribution: mean, peak, peak coordinate and coefficient of variation\. Controlled comparisons evaluate initial crack size and orientation, axle load, speed and wheel–rail friction\. Thirty Latin\-hypercube finite\-element conditions provide 4,272 front points for condition\-grouped machine\-learning validation\. ExtraTrees achieves a case\-macro cross\-validation RMSE of 16\.9587 MPa·mm1/2\. Four held\-out numerical conditions, comprising 579 front points, give a pointwise RMSE of 8\.5794 MPa·mm1/2\. Front coordinate and initial orientation have the largest mean absolute SHAP contributions\. The predicted terminal profiles quantify differences in driving\-force magnitude and localisation across conditions within the sampled domain\.

## [Teachers’ Digital Competence for Multimodal Learning Environments: A Comparative Study Across Educational Levels in Galicia \(Spain\)](../publications/15f8dad157eeba0449af.md)

Carmen Fernández\-Morante; Beatriz Cebreiro\-López; Antonio Palacios‐Rodríguez; Lorena Casal Otero

The assessment of teachers’ digital competence has become a key challenge for educational systems seeking to foster effective multimodal, online, and blended learning environments\. This study examines the level of self\-perceived digital competence and educators’ readiness to design, implement, and support multimodal learning experiences across all educational levels in Galicia, Spain\. A descriptive cross\-sectional study was conducted using the DigCompEdu Check\-In questionnaire with a sample of 1550 teachers\. The findings reveal a generally intermediate level of digital competence across educational levels, with significant differences between educational stages in several dimensions of the DigCompEdu framework\. Teachers reported stronger competences in professional engagement and digital resources, while lower levels were observed in learner empowerment and the facilitation of students’ digital competence\. These results suggest that, although teachers possess a solid foundation for the use of digital technologies, important challenges remain regarding their preparedness to promote active participation, autonomy, and digital engagement in multimodal learning environments\. The dimensions most closely associated with the design and facilitation of multimodal educational experiences, particularly digital resources, teaching and learning, learner empowerment, and the development of students’ digital competence, highlight the need for targeted professional development initiatives\. The study provides a comprehensive baseline for evaluating teachers’ readiness for multimodal online and blended learning before the full implementation of the European Digital Education Action Plan 2021–2027\. Consequently, it offers valuable evidence for assessing the future impact of European policies aimed at strengthening digital education and supporting innovative multimodal teaching practices\.

## [“Kendini Bir İşle Meşgul Et, Şeytan Geldiğinde Seni Çalışırken Bulsun”: Erken Modern Dönem İspanya’sında Tembellik Algısı](../publications/15fc0d773a839514dcda.md)

Mehmet Talha Kalkan

XVI\. yüzyılın sonlarından itibaren İspanya’da yaşanan iktisadi, demografik ve kültürel krizler, tembelliğin yalnızca bireysel bir zaaf değil; aynı zamanda, devletin çöküşünü hızlandıran yapısal bir tehdit olarak görülmesine yol açmıştır\. Gaspar Gutiérrez de los Ríos, Francisco de Luque Fajardo ve Pedro de Guzmán gibi yazarlar, tembelliği kumar, oyun, tiyatro ve eğlence üzerinden eleştirerek onun toplumsal düzeni bozduğunu ve Tanrı’nın lütfundan uzaklaşmaya yol açtığını savunmuşlardır\. Ayrıca José Pellicer de Ossau Salas y Tovar, Jerónimo Ardid, Sancho de Moncada, Miguel Caja de Leruela ve Luisa de Padilla gibi düşünürler ise tembelliği üretim kaybı, yabancıların İspanyol pazarlarında kurduğu hâkimiyetin ve soyluların yaşadığı yozlaşmanın nedeni olarak göstermiştir\. Sonuç olarak tembellik, İspanyol düşüncesinde “şeytani” bir alışkanlık ve bütün günahların kaynağı olarak konumlanmış, devletin bekasını tehdit eden ahlaki ve siyasal bir meseleye dönüşmüştür\. Bu çerçevede çalışma, tembellik karşıtı söylemlerin nasıl bir toplumsal eleştiri aracına dönüştüğünü ortaya koymuştur\.

## [Design and Experimental Validation of a Low\-Cost, IoT\-Enabled Smart Power Meter for Low\-Voltage DC Systems](../publications/16171dea71f9aefee0c5.md)

Obiora Emeka Okoye; Ernest Chidi Okoro; Ezeuzo Chinyere Perpetua

This paper presents the design and experimental validation of a low‑cost Internet of Things‑enabled smart power meter for low‑voltage direct‑current applications\. The prototype integrates an ESP32 microcontroller, INA219 high‑side current and voltage sensor, SSD1306 OLED display, Wi‑Fi connectivity, and Blynk cloud telemetry\. The system was evaluated using a 9 V battery source and different LED load configurations\. Under the baseline test condition, the prototype measured a bus voltage of 8\.94 V, load current of 15\.10 mA, and power consumption of 0\.13 W\. During a 60‑second discharge test, the measured voltage decreased from 8\.94 to 8\.80 V, while current decreased from 15\.10 to 14\.40 mA\. Comparative LED testing produced current values between 14\.80 and 16\.50 mA, demonstrating the ability to distinguish small load‑current variations\. Local OLED readings were also transmitted to the Blynk dashboard at nominal one‑second intervals\. The proposed meter provides an inexpensive and replicable platform for educational laboratories, low‑power DC energy auditing, and preliminary monitoring of decentralized renewable‑energy systems\.

## [Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome \(PRES\) associated with imatinib: A case report and literature review of PRES associated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors](../publications/1626baa061a4df1372bb.md)

Prachi Mohapatra; Priyanka Vasist; Ajay Kumar Garg; Divyani Garg; Achal Kumar Srivastava; Shailesh  B Gaikwad; Ayush Agarwal

Early recognition of drug\-induced posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome \(PRES\) is crucial, as timely discontinuation of the offending agent and supportive management typically result in rapid and complete recovery\. We have presented a case of imatinib induced PRES after 5 weeks of therapy for a gastrointestinal stromal tumour in a 38\-year\-old woman highlighting the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for new\-onset neurological symptoms in patients receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors \(TKIs\), even those not primarily targeting vascular endothelial growth factor \(VEGF\) pathways\.

## [Crafting Resilient AI policies for Education](../publications/1629d465d3e21b12389d.md)

Delight Ejiaka; Miranda Hannasch; Branden Cunningham

The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence into academic spaces requires a shift from passive restriction to resilient, active pedagogical frameworks\. This virtual panel explores actionable strategies to protect academic integrity, promote deep critical thinking, and manage AI use, particularly in foundational courses\. Panelists will discuss the implementation of high\-engagement classroom interventions\. The will offer frameworks for transparent student disclosure practices\. Attendees will leave with practical templates for syllabus policies, assignment rubrics, and disclosure benchmarks designed to foster a culture of transparency and process\-oriented learning in an AI\-permeated landscape\.

## [Repairing LLM\-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis](../publications/162caca66409150e19ea.md)

Giovanni Vaccarino; Emanuele La Malfa; Dehai Min; Hanrong Zhang; Pier Luca Lanzi; Lu Cheng; Michael J\. Wooldridge; Philip S\. Yu; Sara Bernardini

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification\. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver\-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds\. Purely LLM\-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11\.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments\. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism\-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference\-free acceptance predicate\. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning \(SMT\-LIB2\), constraint programming \(MiniZinc\), and planning \(PDDL\), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1\.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12\.9 percentage points over zero\-shot formalization and 8\.7 percentage points over LLM\-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks\. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% \(3,086 instances\) of its floor\-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split\.

## [The Impact of Technology Dependence on Students&\#x27; Critical Thinking Skills in Digital Learning](../publications/162d4510419243f74fd7.md)

Charles Samuel Albert; Muh\. Zuhdy Hamzah; Tedy Haryadi; Saepullah Saepullah; Achsanul Fiqri

This study aims to analyze the impact of technology dependence on students’ critical thinking skills in digital learning\. The study employs a library research approach by examining books, journal articles, previous studies, scientific reports, and other relevant scholarly literature\. The collected data were analyzed using content analysis to identify patterns, relationships, and significant information concerning technology dependence, critical thinking, and digital learning\. The findings indicate that technology provides substantial benefits by facilitating information access, supporting academic tasks, and improving learning efficiency\. However, excessive dependence on technology may encourage cognitive offloading, in which students delegate certain cognitive processes to technological systems\. This condition may reduce students’ direct engagement in analyzing information, evaluating evidence, drawing conclusions, and developing independent reasoning\. Therefore, technology use in digital learning should function as a supporting instrument rather than a substitute for students’ cognitive processes\. Digital learning practices emphasizing verification, reflection, source evaluation, and evidence\-based argumentation can help maintain and strengthen students’ critical thinking skills while maximizing the educational benefits of technology\.

## [Deep Learning\-Driven Assessment of Adolescent Emotional Intelligence and Psychological Well\-Being Using Optimized Feature Selection](../publications/162d456e0569284d924b.md)

Krishnamoorthy Nandhini; S\. Muthukumaran; Gnanasankaran Natarajan; Rathinaramasamy Balamurugan; Sabapathy Nagasundaram

Background: Emotional Intelligence \(EI\) is an important factor that affects adolescents&\#x27; academic performance, social behavior, psychological health, and life resilience\. Identifying the major emotional intelligence factors that affect adolescent behavior in colleges can help teachers and psychologists design effective intervention strategies\. However, the EI datasets contain many emotional and behavioral features that require feature selection and classification methods to improve prediction accuracy\. This research recommends a Hybrid Feature Selection\-based Emotional Deep Learning \(HFS\-EDL\) Framework for estimating adolescents&\#x27; emotional intelligence at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels in Tamil Nadu\. Methods: The survey was carried out using a questionnaire with 3510 students across five districts of Tamil Nadu\. The dataset includes 25 attributes; age group is the target variable\. After data preprocessing, the most significant EI factors were selected using two techniques: Chi\-Square and Mutual Information \(MI\)\. Three deep learning models, namely Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\), Recurrent Neural Network \(RNN\), and Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), were then used to classify the selected features\. Model performance was measured using accuracy, recall, precision, specificity, and error rate\. Results: The experimental results showed that the feature selection method performs better than the full feature set\. Mutual Information is most effective with ANN and RNN models, while Chi\-Square feature selection is most effective with LSTM\. Conclusion: Overall, the proposed HFS\-EDL framework demonstrates the capability to successfully recognize important emotional intelligence factors and improve classification accuracy in predicting an adolescent&\#x27;s emotional intelligence\.

## [Systematic Review Using Artificial Intelligence: From Planning to Evidence Synthesis](../publications/163050db44837a9f90ee.md)

Zen Revista

Systematic reviews are widely regarded as the cornerstone of evidence\-based medicine and decision\-making, providing structured, transparent, and reproducible syntheses of the available research evidence on a given question\. However, traditional systematic review methodologies were developed in an era of comparatively modest scholarly output and now face an evidence base that doubles in size at intervals of less than a decade\. The average review requires well over a year of collaborative work, involves screening thousands of records, and relies on manual, cognitively demanding procedures that scale poorly with the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of contemporary scientific literature\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly machine learning, natural language processing, and, more recently, large language models \(LLMs\), has emerged as a promising response to this challenge of scale\. This thesis presents a comprehensive, end\-to\-end examination of the application of AI throughout the systematic review lifecycle, structured around the four canonical phases of the review workflow: planning; search and study selection; data extraction and critical appraisal; and evidence synthesis and reporting\. Drawing on more than two hundred primary sources, including methodological standards established by Cochrane, the PRISMA 2020 statement, five decades of AI research, and empirical studies on the automation of evidence synthesis published between 2006 and 2025, this thesis examines the capabilities and limitations of different classes of AI methods at each stage of the review process\. Classical machine learning approaches to relevance screening, supported by two decades of evaluation evidence and shown to reduce screening workload while maintaining high recall, are distinguished from prompt\-based LLM approaches\. The latter offer broader capabilities, including search query formulation, data extraction, and risk\-of\-bias assessment, but their reliability remains insufficient to support unsupervised deployment in rigorous evidence synthesis\. The thesis develops a unified analytical framework that maps AI capabilities onto the different phases of systematic reviews; consolidates empirical evidence concerning performance, workload reduction, and failure modes; situates these technologies within Cochrane&\#x27;s methodological standards, the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework, and emerging guidance on the responsible use of generative AI in research; and examines the ethical, epistemological, and organisational implications of delegating knowledge\-related tasks to machines\. The findings indicate that AI is neither a substitute for the methodological rigour required by systematic reviews nor merely a peripheral convenience\. Rather, it constitutes a potentially transformative assistive infrastructure whose safe and effective implementation depends on human\-in\-the\-loop architectures, phase\-specific validation, transparent reporting of automation procedures, and the preservation of human judgement as the ultimate authority in evaluating and substantiating knowledge claims\. The thesis concludes by presenting structured recommendations for systematic review teams, technology developers, academic journals, and policymakers\. It also proposes a research agenda for the emerging field of AI\-native evidence synthesis, emphasising the need for rigorous evaluation, methodological transparency, responsible governance, and the continued integration of human expertise into increasingly automated research workflows\.

## [Thermo\-diffusive Response in Generalized Thermoelastic Medium Having Spherical Cavity](../publications/163b4f6a6f667c9834d5.md)

Soumen Shaw; Nikos Mastorakis

The present study examines the thermo\-diffusive response of a homogeneous, isotropic, semi\-infinite medium subjected to a finite rotational field\. The analysis is carried out within the framework of the generalized theory of thermoelasticity incorporating mass diffusion, which accounts for finite thermal wave speeds and diffusion effects\. The coupled governing equations describing displacement, stress, temperature, and concentration fields are formulated and solved analytically\. To infer the physical behavior of the medium, a complex quartic characteristic equation is derived and solved using Descartes’ algorithm in conjunction with the irreducible Cardan’s method\. Numerical computations are performed to illustrate the theoretical developments\. The effects of rotation and thermo\-diffusion on displacement components, stress distribution, and temperature variations are presented graphically and investigated\. The results reveal significant influences of rotation and diffusion parameters on the thermoelastic response\. The present investigation is expected to be useful in understanding thermo\-diffusive phenomena arising in geophysical and engineering applications\.

## [AI\-driven early warning of psychological crisis in college students using network theory and few\-shot learning through survey\-parameterized simulation](../publications/16497d216df59f30a33d.md)

Yilin Ren; Jienan Wu

Psychological crises among college students are often detected too late because current practice relies on periodic screening that is passive and infrequent\. This paper proposes an AI\-driven early\-warning framework that organizes multi\-source campus behavioral traces into a three\-layer student–behavior–space–time heterogeneous dynamic graph\. A heterogeneous graph neural network with hierarchical and temporal attention detects behavioral\-pattern drift preceding a crisis, while graph contrastive pre\-training and few\-shot fine\-tuning yield a student\-specific dynamic behavioral representation from scarce crisis\-positive labels; the risk score is decomposed into behavioral\-dimension attributions for counselors\. Evaluation uses a survey\-parameterized simulation: eight thousand synthetic student records generated from distributions calibrated to the desensitized behavioral records of 316 real students, with a field\-survey\-parameterized crisis\-generating mechanism applied to sixty designated cases\. The method achieves an AUPRC of 0\.249, recall of 0\.607, and average lead time of 2\.79 weeks, ahead of all baselines; ablation attributes most gain to contrastive pre\-training and heterogeneous representation\. Against stronger competitors the advantage narrows, and against four additional crisis\-generating mechanisms evaluated with the model frozen, it persists when the signature carries relational and directionally persistent structure but disappears otherwise\. An information\-flow audit shows discriminative ability persisting to roughly two weeks ahead and flooring beyond three, indicating detection of ongoing deterioration rather than forecasting of future decline\. At recall 0\.700 the alert load reaches 8\.2 per counselor per week; the framework is accordingly a methodological contribution, not a validated system for real crises\.

## [Mechanonociceptive tactile feedback enhances prosthetic grasp control during repeated human\-in\-the\-loop interaction](../publications/164a14b76c482441f66f.md)

Elif Hocaoğlu

Upper\-limb prosthetic systems continue to face a fundamental challenge in providing sensory feedback that remains functionally effective during repeated interaction\. This study investigates innocuous painful feedback \(IPF\), a controlled mechanonociceptive tactile modality intended to provide salient error\-related information during human\-in\-the\-loop prosthetic interaction\. A custom experimental platform was developed to emulate prosthetic grasping conditions in healthy participants, enabling systematic evaluation of IPF across feedback modality, stimulation frequency, temporal modulation strategy, and spatial configuration\. IPF was associated with lower grasp\-position errors than visual\-only and visual\-plus\-force feedback, supporting its potential as a corrective sensory feedback modality for boundary\-constrained grasp control\. Within the tested frequency range, high\-frequency stimulation produced the lowest error levels, demonstrating that the functional effectiveness of IPF depends on stimulation frequency\. Progressive frequency modulation generally maintained lower error levels than fixed\-frequency stimulation across repeated interaction, while sequential dual\-site stimulation yielded lower overall participant\-level errors than repeated single\-site stimulation, although the magnitude of this difference varied across the trial sequence\. Collectively, these findings indicate that the behavioral effectiveness of mechanonociceptive feedback depends not only on feedback modality, but also on its temporal and spatial organization\. As a proof\-of\-concept study conducted in neurologically intact participants using a virtual prosthetic\-like grasping paradigm, these findings provide a basis for subsequent validation with individuals with upper\-limb amputation and physical prosthetic devices\.

## [Occupational disease compensation claims in Italy: an epidemiological analysis of national insurance data with predictive insights](../publications/164c8f2bd9a384968ee9.md)

Martina Padovan; Alessandro Palla

Introduction\. Occupational diseases remain an underreported public health problem\. In Italy, national insurance claims provide a useful view of recognized occupational diseases, although they do not measure the full burden of disease in the workforce\. Few studies have combined descriptive analysis of insurance claims with predictive modelling to assess factors associated with recognized impairment\. Methods\. We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 310,189 occupational disease claims from the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work \(INAIL\) open data, covering the period 2020 to 2024\. Multivariable linear regression was used to estimate associations between demographic, clinical, and occupational factors and the degree of impairment\. Neural\-network models with embedding layers were developed to classify claims with recognized impairment \(&gt;0%\) and to predict impairment severity\. Results\. Musculoskeletal disorders represented the largest share of claims, whereas neoplasms and asbestos\-related diseases were associated with the highest impairment\. Diagnostic category and causal agent were the strongest predictors of severity among claims\. The classification model achieved 98\.15% accuracy and 99\.99% sensitivity for recognized impairment\. The regression model attained a mean absolute error of 2\.31% and R2=0\.71, outperforming the linear regression baseline R2=0\.55\)\. Conclusion\. Combining descriptive epidemiology with machine learning yields actionable insights for prioritizing high\-risk claims and supporting administrative decision\-making in occupational health surveillance\. These findings represent a proof of concept given inherent administrative data limitations, including underreporting, lack of workforce denominators, and potential data bias\. Future developments should incorporate explainable artificial intelligence techniques to bridge the gap between predictive performance and clinical interpretability\.

## [Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism &amp; Its Impact on Purchase Intention](../publications/16515496555b93813d6c.md)

Humna Hamad Butt; Maha Gul; Umme Rehma; Rukhba Ather Zia; Asma Nisar

The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models\. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain\. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular\. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4\. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted\. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention\. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools\. ## [Examining the Effect of Global Supply Chain Disruption on the Trade Market for Automobiles in Zambia](../publications/1662180a1f5eb0423275.md)

Brian Silomba

The coronavirus disease \(COVID\-19\) pandemic caused major global supply chain disruptions\. However, this study examined the effect of global Supply Chain disruption on the automobile trade market in Zambia\. It incorporates comparative data spanning pre\-pandemic \(2016\-2019\) and pandemic \(2020\-2022\) periods, providing insights into key performance shifts\. The automobile industry&\#x27;s adoption of alternative logistics routes and enhanced supplier relationships demonstrates practical applications of theories in under\-researched Zambian territories\. The resource dependence theory \(RDT\), Institution theory \(IT\), and Contingency theory \(CT\) were incorporated\. The research study relies on a qualitative research design, and the primary data were gathered from automobile dealer companies within Lusaka, Zambia\. The data were gathered from surveys, questionnaires, interviews, and observations from different automobile organizations in Zambia\. The targeted automobile companies were Ford Zambia \(cfao mobility\), Toyota Zambia, and Southern Cross Motors\. A total of 115 people were interviewed from Procurement, Logistics, Facilities, and warehouse / Stores department amongst the three automobile dealer companies within Lusaka, Zambia\. The research findings identified several key metrics on the trade market for the automobile industry utilized to monitor and assess global supply chain disruptions on trade, particularly in response to the challenges posed by the COVID\-19 pandemic\. However, these findings underscore the need for continuous improvement of resilient supply chain strategies, particularly in a global landscape marked by frequent disruptions\.

## [WebMCP: A Browser\-Native navigator\.modelContext Standard for Agentic Web Automation](../publications/1673c918746ab45df99a.md)

Harsha Nooka; Suhas Madupuri

Purpose: This paper examines WebMCP, a proposed browser\-native web platform standard that lets websites expose explicit, schema\-described tools to large language model agents, as an alternative to actuation, in which an agent simulates the clicks, keystrokes, and navigation a human would perform\. Methodology: The paper analyzes WebMCP, incubated within the World Wide Web Consortium&\#x27;s Web Machine Learning Community Group and implemented as an origin trial in the Chrome browser beginning with Chrome 149\. We describe WebMCP&\#x27;s architecture, including the browser\-mediated JavaScript interface navigator\.modelContext and a declarative HTML annotation form, and its relationship to Anthropic&\#x27;s Model Context Protocol; analyze its security and permission model; place it within a comparative design\-space taxonomy alongside DOM automation, computer\-use agents, and server\-side Model Context Protocol integrations; and examine the emerging standardization landscape, including browser vendor positions and adjacent efforts such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol\. A generalized use case illustrates how a composite retail website might expose search, filtering, and checkout tools under this model\. All sources and data referenced in this manuscript are dated on or before June 30, 2026\. Findings: WebMCP allows a website to register tools that an agent invokes directly rather than inferring actions from pixels or DOM structure, with a security model built on origin isolation, a dedicated Permissions Policy directive, and a human\-in\-the\-loop confirmation mechanism for consequential actions\. Open problems remain in cross\-site tool discovery, adversarial tool poisoning, and the evaluation of agent\-web interaction quality\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: For theory, the paper contributes a comparative design\-space taxonomy that positions browser\-native, declarative agent integration against actuation\-based and server\-side approaches\. For practice, it gives web developers and agent builders a technical account of WebMCP&\#x27;s registration mechanisms, security model, and interaction flow\. For policy, it informs browser vendors and standards bodies through its analysis of the standardization landscape and a research agenda for browser\-native agent integration standards as this area continues to develop\.

## [Green Chemistry Strategies for the Synthesis of Fluorinated Bioactive Molecules: Recent Advances and Future Directions](../publications/167e09aef123b2b7a747.md)



Fluorination of bioassay molecules has proven to be a unique strategy in recent drug discovery, agrochemical, and materials sciences\.The unique properties of fluorine, such as its high electronegativity, small atomic size, and high bond energy of the C\-F bond, bring remarkable metabolic stability, increased membrane permeability and pharmacokinetic optimization to drug candidates\.But the existing methods of fluorination suffer from the use of dangerous reactants, volatile organics as solvents, extreme reaction temperatures, and good amount of chemical waste, which would bring critical environmental and safety issues\.The principles of green chemistry, as stated by Anastas and Warner, are a very good guiding tool to design alternative approaches to fluorination chemistry that are more environmentally friendly while not compromising on synthetic efficiency and yields\.This review brings together all the key approaches that have been applied to the design and synthesis of fluorinated bioactive molecules in a panoramic way\.Solvent\-free fluorination reactions, aqueous\-phase fluorination strategies, photocatalytic, electrochemical, renewable fluorine sources, biocatalytic C\-F bond formation, microwave\-and flow chemistryassisted fluorinations and computational tools for designing greener fluorination processes are discussed\.Besides that, we explore the concepts of atom economy, catalytic fluorination and waste minimization in the synthesis of pharmacologically significant scaffolds of fluorine\.Recent developments in the introduction of PET imaging 18Fradiolabeling under green conditions, sustainable trifluoromethylation reactions, and incorporation of machine learning for prediction of optimal green pathways for fluorination reactions will receive special attention\.The review presents and summarises the evidence that sustainable industry development for pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals is possible with green fluorination chemistry while simultaneously being economically viable and technologically cutting\-edge\.

## [Empowering risky choices: care ethics and risk management in participatory immersive performance](../publications/16837df6723e579c7079.md)

Melissa Bondar

This article examines audience engagement in immersive theatrical productions, focusing on why some participants thrive while others feel fearful or reluctant\. It critiques traditional risk management systems for overlooking psychological and social risks in participatory art\. Using insights from Joan Tronto’s care ethics and Paul Slovic’s risk perception, this study proposes that grounded risk management in care ethics can enhance audience experiences\. By focusing on developing tools to help address unintentional discomfort, the article suggests that a reimagined approach to risk assessment could foster deeper engagement and emotional resilience in immersive performances\.

## [Sustainable Solutions through Self\-Sufficient Energy Houses Powered by Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems](../publications/16909a99d4c2098fac29.md)

Jorge Contreras; Carlos Armenta\-Déu

This article analyzes the energy self\-sufficiency in a paired house using a hybrid renewable energy system installed in one house and using the second house for a null energy balance\. The article searches for sustainable systems reducing energy dependence on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions\. The study is based on the application of the fundamental equations of energy, thermal, and electrical balance for a domestic installation\. This system integrates a domestic wind turbine and a photovoltaic array, assisted by a battery bank as an energy storage system to compensate for energy imbalances during a power outage\. The proposed design relies exclusively on electricity to meet all thermal and electrical demands, including heating, domestic hot water, air conditioning, appliances, and lighting\. The design employs an air source heat pump for domestic hot water, heating, and air conditioning; this unit directly connects to the hybrid renewable energy system, and the battery bank assists the hybrid system when needed\. The battery is charged and discharged according to the daily energy balance\. A simulation is performed under various operating conditions to evaluate the proposed design feasibility\. The study includes experimental tests to verify the simulation’s validity and the reliability of the system design\. Experimental tests show good agreement between simulation and actual performance, with an accuracy higher than 99% \( σ ave = 2\.126\), and demonstrate the feasibility of energy self\-sufficiency in housing with hybrid renewable energy sources\. Sustainable energy installations require highly efficient systems to supply thermal energy, such as high\-performance aerothermal heat pumps\.

## [Dynamic adaptation of attentional control across bilingual interactional contexts](../publications/16957c439d88323a89e5.md)

Min Li; Xiangyu Shi; Qinghong Xu; Jie Li

Background/objectives Bilingual experience is thought to shape cognitive control via adaptive attentional reorganization, yet the neural mechanisms by which different interactional contexts dynamically modulate attentional control remain unclear\. This study used EEG to examine how Chinese monolingual, English monolingual, bilingual, and voluntary naming contexts influence attentional control in Chinese–English bilinguals\. Methods Thirty\-five bilinguals completed picture\-naming tasks in different contexts, followed by an antisaccade task with concurrent EEG\. We analyzed reaction time, ERPs, frontal and parietal delta/theta power, and frontoparietal functional connectivity \(wPLI\)\. Results Bilingual and voluntary naming contexts shortened antisaccade reaction times \(all p &lt; 0\.01\)\. No significant main effect of context was found on N2 amplitudes \( p = 0\.615\)\. Both contexts reduced parietal delta and theta power relative to the English monolingual context \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Exploratory connectivity analysis initially suggested bilingual\-context effects, but this finding did not survive homologous ROI validation\. These preliminary sensor\-level findings await validation by source\-localized EEG or fMRI\. Conclusions These findings suggest that bilingual and voluntary naming contexts may facilitate attentional control through adaptive reorganization of the attentional system rather than through enhancing a specific inhibitory process\. This pattern is consistent with the adaptationist perspective on bilingual cognition and provides preliminary neural evidence for the language mode theory\.

## [HIGHER EDUCATION TEACHING PROFESSION: TRAINING, PRACTICES, AND INNOVATION](../publications/169ad5f03a78ead2e0c4.md)

Alcimar de Lima Marques Filho; Angela Monteiro Simão; Diego Macedo Almeida; Anna Cristhina Barbosa Massulo; Lena Marina Moreira Puga Barbosa; Valdenilson de Souza Ribeiro; Silvya Karen de Carvalho Martins; Aylin Cynthia de Carvalho Lopes

This article analyzes how teacher education, pedagogical practices, and innovation interact in the reconfiguration of the teaching profession in higher education\. It is a qualitative theoretical\-conceptual study supported by structured bibliographic research and an audit of the references used\. The corpus comprises seminal works, reviews, meta\-analyses, empirical studies, and institutional documents addressing teacher professionalism and identity, professional development, pedagogical practices, digital competence, and generative artificial intelligence\. The interpretive synthesis indicates that disciplinary expertise, although indispensable, does not exhaust the competence required for teaching; professional development depends on the interaction among education, experience, reflection, and context; and pedagogical innovation should not be equated with technological novelty\. The analysis also shows that digital competence involves pedagogical judgment and that the diffusion of generative artificial intelligence adds new demands related to verification, contextualization, ethics, and learning mediation\. As a theoretical contribution, the article proposes the Integrative Model for the Reconfiguration of University Teaching \(MIRDU\), which organizes education, practice, reflection, and innovation as recursive components of professional development, conditioned by institutional, pedagogical, and technological factors\. The model is presented as a conceptual proposition to be empirically validated in future studies\.

## [Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta&\#x27;s End\-to\-End Co\-Design for High\-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs](../publications/16aa712ef986c2001088.md)

Haoyu Zhang; Arshad Rahman; Adnan Aziz; Ajith Prabhudev; Amin Farmahini; Ben Rhoads; Benson Ma; Brian Shi; Cen Zhao; CK Luk; Dingming Wu; Emad El\-Haraty; Eric Chen; Frank Li; Gary Huang; Gefei Zuo; Haoran Zhang; Hiwot Kassa; Hongyi Zeng; Jack Taylor; Jeremy Hadidjojo; John Donati; Jonathan Sheffield; Julio Machado Silva; Karthik Ganesan; Kent Russell; KR Kishore; Lei Tian; Liu Ke; Muhammad Osama; Peng Chen; Rakesh Hemnani; Ryan Swann; Saleel Kudchadker; Shankar Yanamandram; Shobhit Kanaujia; Shucai Xiao; Srinath Bayareddy; Srinivas Vaidyanathan; Sudharssun Subramanian; Supadchaya Puangpontip; Taylor Robie; Tianhao Huang; Tyler Hart; Viswesh Sankaran; Weijun Jiang; Wenkai Du; Xiaodong Wang; Xiaohu Guo; Yao Rong; Yinbin Ma; Yue Dong; Yuzhen Huang; Yvonne Liu; Zhan Shu; Dan Rabinovitsj; Ajit Mathews; Chunqiang Tang

Meta deploys a heterogeneous fleet comprising NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators to reduce costs and mitigate vendor lock\-in\. However, the extensive history of NVIDIA\-specific optimizations hinders performance portability to other hardware\. This paper presents our methods for optimizing alternative accelerators, using AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation model training as a case study\. We propose three reusable principles\. First, hardware\-model co\-design is essential: rather than directly porting models from NVIDIA GPUs, revising model structures and software recipes allows full exploitation of accelerator\-specific strengths \(e\.g\., MI350X&\#x27;s 1\.6x HBM capacity relative to B200\)\. Second, our analytical performance model enables zero\-warmup optimal kernel selection across diverse datatypes and matrix shapes in production models, drastically simplifying tuning\. Third, increasingly mature agentic workflows have lowered the barrier to porting from the CUDA ecosystem; we extend these workflows for microarchitecture\-aware kernel optimizations and custom shim generation\. Compared to the directly ported baseline, these methods deliver up to 1\.5x improvement in end\-to\-end training throughput\. To our knowledge, this is the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large\-scale training\. Our contributions have been upstreamed to the open\-source PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm ecosystems\.

## [CBS Yöntemleriyle Alakır Çayı Havzası’nın Morfometrik Özelliklerinin Analizi](../publications/16ac82a54b2cff30cf22.md)

Nuran Göral; Mehmet Ali Özdemir

Bu çalışma, Alakır Çayı Havzası’ndaki hidrolojik süreçlerin ve havza yönetimine yönelik fiziksel altyapının anlaşılmasına katkı sağlamak amacıyla, havzanın morfometrik özelliklerini nicel verilerle ortaya koymayı hedeflemektedir\. Analizler kapsamında, Coğrafi Bilgi Sistemleri \(CBS\) ve 5 m çözünürlüklü Sayısal Yükseklik Modeli \(SYM\) verileri kullanılarak; çizgisel, alansal ve relief morfometrisi gruplarında toplam 22 parametre hesaplanmıştır\. Elde edilen bulgular; şekil faktörü \(0\.212\), dairesellik oranı \(0\.143\) ve uzama oranı \(0\.52\) değerleri ile havzanın belirgin biçimde uzun, dar ve eliptik bir morfolojiye sahip olduğunu kanıtlamaktadır\. Drenaj yoğunluğu \(1\.64 km/km²\) ve akarsu sıklığı \(2\.45 adet/km²\) değerleri, yüzey akışının havza genelinde etkin bir şekilde organize olduğunu ve drenaj ağının alansal olarak iyi geliştiğini göstermektedir\. Havza reliefi \(2949 m\), relief oranı \(48\.7 m/km\) ve engebelilik değeri \(4\.84\), topoğrafik enerjinin ve dikey gelişimin oldukça yüksek olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır\. Hipsometrik integral değerinin \(0\.39\) ve hipsometrik eğrinin genel formunun işaret ettiği &quot;olgunluk&quot; evresi, havzada flüvyal aşınım süreçlerinin aktif biçimde devam ettiğini ve topoğrafyanın denge profiline doğru ilerlediğini yansıtmaktadır\. Sonuç olarak bu çalışmada elde edilen morfometrik göstergeler, Alakır Çayı Havzası’nın hidrolojik davranışının değerlendirilmesinde ve fiziksel çevreye dayalı havza planlama ile yönetim stratejilerinde kullanılabilecek güvenilir ve bütüncül bir veri seti sunmaktadır\.
