## [Latent class analysis identifies three biologically distinct phenotypes among patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy: a derivation and temporal validation study](../publications/18391a7482e23a42a662.md)

Li\-Li Yang; Chao Chen; Lili Sun; Mengxia Li; Li Han

Background Despite successful vascular recanalization, approximately half of patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy \(EVT\) fail to achieve functional independence at 3 months\. The biological determinants of this heterogeneity remain poorly characterized\. Methods Latent class analysis \(LCA\) was applied to 825 consecutive EVT\-treated patients \(development cohort, January 2021–December 2024\) using 12 routine post\-procedural clinical and laboratory indicators\. Phenotype associations with favorable 3\-month outcome \(modified Rankin Scale 0–2\) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression\. Reproducibility was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort \( n = 211\)\. Results LCA identified three phenotypes\. The Low\-burden phenotype \(Class 1, 44\.4%\) had the lowest inflammatory and coagulatory burden and achieved favorable outcome in 70\.8% of patients\. The Metabolic phenotype \(Class 2, 42\.7%\), characterized by hyperglycemia and elevated neutrophil\-to\-lymphocyte ratio, had a favorable outcome rate of 44\.9% and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage \(sICH\) rate of 7\.1%\. The hypercoagulable phenotype \(Class 3, 13\.0%\), defined by markedly elevated D\-dimer and atrial fibrillation, had a favorable outcome rate of 40\.2% and sICH rate of 8\.4%\. After multivariable adjustment, both Class 2 \(OR 0\.49, 95% CI 0\.35–0\.69\) and Class 3 \(OR 0\.41, 95% CI 0\.25–0\.67\) were independently associated with unfavorable outcome \(both p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Class distribution and outcome associations were reproduced in the validation cohort\. Conclusion LCA identified three biologically distinct phenotypes among EVT\-treated patients with divergent functional outcomes\. Multicenter prospective validation is needed before these findings can inform clinical practice\.

## [The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks](../publications/183d424998fafcf36645.md)

Niclas Göring; Shuofeng Zhang; Roi Holtzman; Yoonsoo Nam; Ard A\. Louis

Every neuron in a trained network outputs a number that can be separated into its sign \(positive or negative\) and its magnitude \(absolute size\)\. We call the set of all neuron signs the \\textit\{sign code\}\. This raises a key question: does classification depend more on the sign code or on the magnitudes? For overparameterized vision classifiers with sign\-preserving activations, the answer is overwhelmingly the sign code\. A $k$\-nearest neighbor classifier operating only on this binary sign code achieves accuracy comparable to the full model across different architectures, activation functions, and datasets\. Moreover, replacing all magnitudes in every layer with random noise while keeping the original signs barely changes residual network performance\. In contrast, flipping just 20\\% of the signs reduces accuracy to chance\. Models generalize well when same\-class inputs share similar sign codes\. When this overlap is disrupted by a regularizer, training accuracy remains high, but test performance collapses\. A margin decomposition helps explain these results: the sign\-only contribution to each logit grows as $\\sqrt\{d\}$ in network width, dominating the magnitude residual\. The natural unit of analysis for these networks may not be through their continuous weight space but instead through their discrete sign codes\.

## [Virology\-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp\-centered benchmarking](../publications/1848c0839746afca211f.md)

Luis Ruben Ramos\-Cortes; Alan Orlando Santos\-Mena; Luis Enrique Flores\-Padilla; Kevin Paul Miranda\-Lizárraga; David Mauricio Cañedo\-Figueroa; Luisa Fernanda Ontiveros\-Zúñiga; Flor Itzel Lira\-Hernández; Juan Fidel Osuna‐Ramos; Saúl Noriega; Jaime Cardoso‐Ortiz; Vanessa Alcalá\-Ramírez; Luis Adrián De Jesús‐González

Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage\. RNA\-dependent RNA polymerases \(RdRps\) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\), machine learning \(ML\), deep learning \(DL\), geometric deep learning \(GDL\), and generative molecular design are increasingly used to accelerate antiviral discovery, yet their performance is often inferred from general protein\-ligand benchmarks dominated by non\-viral targets\. This review argues that respiratory RNA virus polymerases are a high\-value but comparatively underrepresented class of antiviral targets and a complementary test case for evaluating AI\-guided drug discovery\. We synthesize current approaches in computer\-aided drug design \(CADD\), molecular docking, ML\-assisted virtual screening, molecular representations, pose\-generation models, generative AI, and protein\-ligand affinity benchmarking\. We emphasize that docking scores, predicted affinity, and root\-mean\-square error \(RMSE\) values are insufficient unless linked to target engagement, enzymatic inhibition, cell\-based antiviral activity, cytotoxicity, resistance, and pharmacological feasibility\. We propose an RdRp\-centered AI pipeline that integrates curated polymerase structural ensembles, leakage\-resistant benchmarking, antiviral\-specific evaluation tasks, ADME/Tox filtering, biochemical validation, cell\-based infection assays, resistance profiling, and iterative model refinement\. Moving beyond docking scores requires benchmarking models under virologically realistic conditions and validating whether computational prioritization enriches compounds with experimentally actionable antiviral activity\.

## [Multi\-environment evaluation and decision\-level analysis of clinical prediction models under dataset shift](../publications/18499f8a091e8f5ba911.md)

Jorge Robalino\-Díaz; Alejandro Cabrera‐Andrade; Ana Karina Zambrano; William Eduardo Villegas\-Ch

Clinical machine\-learning models are often evaluated within a single dataset, although deployment occurs across heterogeneous institutions and measurement processes\. We evaluated Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting for ICU hospital\-mortality prediction across MIMIC\-III Demo and eICU using a 24\-h landmark design, explicit feature mappings, and predictors retained only when sufficiently observed in both domains\. A decision\-level diagnostic analysis examined how predicted\-probability distributions interact with a fixed 0\.5 threshold\. The primary cohort contained 110 MIMIC and 1,324 eICU ICU episodes\. In eICU\-to\-MIMIC transfer, AUC\-ROC was 0\.598 for Logistic Regression, 0\.642 for Random Forest, and 0\.613 for Gradient Boosting\. Random Forest generated no positive predictions, a threshold failure already visible during internal eICU validation\. Logistic Regression retained partial sensitivity with substantial false\-positive burden, whereas Gradient Boosting detected only two deaths\. These findings show that clinical model evaluation should examine calibration, threshold behavior, feature harmonization, and source\-to\-target operating\-point stability, not only aggregate discrimination\.

## [Enhancing Sustainable Agriculture in China Through Capital Investment, Environmental Balance, and Natural Resource Productivity](../publications/184d41e401db6a21e079.md)

Tang Yuhong; Yimin Liu

ABSTRACT Rapid population increase and resource scarcity require a sustainable agricultural system that will provide for productivity, environmental sustainability, and farmers&\#x27; livelihoods\. Despite the productivity of modern agricultural methods, they have led to soil degradation, ecological imbalance, and regional differences\. This study analyzes the association between initial capital investment, sustainable agricultural practices, environmental sustainability, natural resource productivity, and regional economic development\. A mixed‐methods design was used, in which quantitative data were collected through purposive sampling of 668 respondents \(332 agricultural researchers and 336 Chinese farmers\), while semi‐structured qualitative interviews were also conducted with 72 participants\. Quantitative data analysis was performed using SPSS for descriptive screening, SmartPLS for PLS‐SEM measurement, and AMOS for confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling\. Qualitative analysis was done using NVivo\. Results revealed a considerable indirect relationship between initial capital investment and improved natural resources due to productivity \( B = 0\.057, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Sustainable agriculture is positively associated with environmental and ecological balance \( B = 0\.289, p &lt; 0\.001\) and enhanced natural resource conservation \( B = 0\.173, p = 0\.002\)\. Enhancement of agricultural tools and resources was positively associated with sustainable agriculture \( B = 0\.355, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Simultaneously, sustainable agriculture was also positively associated with regional economic development \( B = 0\.260, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. This study provides empirical evidence for a framework linking capital investment, sustainability, and socio‐economic outcomes\. These findings offer crucial guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to promote agricultural development with environmental resilience and economic inclusivity\.

## [Ets2 Is an Activity‐Dependent Transcriptional Regulator of a Fast‐Twitch Muscle Program](../publications/1850ad71aeae85d3a737.md)

Zaheer A\. Rana; Jo C\. Bruusgaard; Jens R\. Wendland; Ivan Myhre Winje; Ingrid Marie Egner; Irina D\. Karavanova; Einar Eftestøl; Detlef Vullhorst; Kristian Gundersen; Andres Bounanno

The functional properties of excitable cells, including skeletal muscle, are regulated by electrical activity\. Distinct motoneuron firing patterns control contraction speed, strength, and endurance of fast\- and slow\-twitch myofibers by activating transcriptional programs that specify contractile and metabolic protein isoforms\. Although transcriptional regulators of slow muscle adaptation are well characterized, less is known about activity\-dependent mechanisms controlling expression of fast muscle genes\. We previously showed that the quail fast troponin I \(TnIf\) intronic regulatory element \(FIRE\) is both necessary and sufficient for fast\-muscle\-specific transcription and responds selectively to brief, high\-frequency \(150 Hz\) stimulation rather than to sustained low\-frequency \(20 Hz\) activity\. In this study, using mRNA microarray analysis of muscles subjected to different stimulation patterns, we identified E26 transformation\-specific homolog 2 \(Ets2\) as a transcription factor rapidly and selectively induced by fast\-patterned activity\. Ets2 accumulates in nuclei of slow soleus muscle following fast, but not slow, stimulation, and it is expressed more abundantly in fast muscle\. Ets2 binds a consensus Ets site within the TnIf FIRE, and mutation of this site abolishes enhancer activation by fast\-patterned activity\. Furthermore, Ets2 knockdown reduces transcription from both a trimerized Ets2\-responsive reporter and a TnIf FIRE reporter specifically in fast muscles\. To our knowledge, these findings identify Ets2 as the first transcription factor shown to selectively promote fast muscle gene expression in response to fast\-patterned activity\. Together with NFATc1, Ets2 may contribute to a dynamic regulatory mechanism that enables skeletal muscles to adapt their functional properties to changing physiological demands\.

## [Factors Worsening the Bipolar Disorder: A Systemic Review](../publications/1854ff2510839098186f.md)

Sabitri Pradhan

Introduction: Bipolar disorder \(BD\) is a severe psychiatric condition characterized by extreme mood fluctuations, ranging from manic episodes to depressive states\. Despite the advancements in understanding the pathophysiology of BD, numerous factors continue to worsen the course and prognosis of the disorder\. Objectives: This systematic review aims to explore the literature on various factors that exacerbate the symptoms and progression of BD, such as effect of melatonin, solar light, biological clock, genetics, nor\-adrenaline and dopamine reductase, reductase in tyramine containing diet\. These factors are crucial for identifying individuals at higher risk for adverse outcomes to improve treatment adherence, enhance mood stabilization and reduce relapse rates\. Methods: Various literature search was carried out from different databases such as Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar and ScienceDirect to cover this review\. Conclusions: The findings underscore the need for a comprehensive, multidimensional approach to managing Bipolar Disease, focusing not only on pharmacological interventions but also on psychosocial support and personalized care\.

Brooks; Francisco Javier Castander; T\. Claybaugh; S\. Cole; Andrei Cuceu; Kyle Dawson; Axel de la Macorra; Biprateep Dey; P\. Doel; Ann Elliott; N Emas; Simone Ferraro; Andreu Font\-Ribera; J\. E\. Forero\-Romero; C\. García\-Quintero; ENRIQUE GAZTAÑAGA; Satya Gontcho A Gontcho; Gaston Gutierrez; J\. Guy; K\. Honscheid; Dragan Huterer A; Mustapha Ishak; Shahab Joudaki; R\. Joyce; R\. Kehoe; David R\. Kirkby; Theodore Kisner; Anthony Kremin; Alex Krolewski; Ofer Lahav; C\. Lamman; Martin Landriau; Laurent Le Guillou; Michael Levi; Marc Manera; Paul Martini; Aaron Meisner; R\. Miquel; John Moustakas; Eva\-Maria Mueller; S\. Nadathur; J\. A\. Newman; Gustavo Niz; N\. Palanque‐Delabrouille; Will Percival; Claire Poppett; A\. Wechsler; Pauline Zarrouk; Rongpu Zhou; Hu Zou

Abstract We present constraints on cosmic structure growth from the analysis of galaxy clustering and galaxy–galaxy lensing with galaxies from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument \(DESI\) Data Release 1\. Our analysis includes four samples drawn from the Bright Galaxy Survey \(BGS\) and the luminous red galaxy \(LRG\) target classes\. Projected galaxy clustering measurements from DESI are supplemented with lensing data from the Dark Energy Survey \(DES\), the Kilo\-Degree Survey \(KiDS\), and the Hyper Suprime\-Cam \(HSC\) survey around the same targets\. Our method relies on a simulation\-based modeling framework using the AbacusSummit simulations and a complex halo occupation distribution model that incorporates assembly bias\. We analyze scales down to 0\.4 h −1 Mpc for clustering and 2\.5 h −1 Mpc for lensing, leading to stringent constraints on S 8 = σ 8 Ω m / 0\.3 and Ω m when fixing other cosmological parameters to those preferred by the cosmic microwave background\. We find S 8 = 0\.79 7 − 0\.024 \+ 0\.023 and Ω m = 0\.292 ± 0\.011 when using lensing measurements from DES and KiDS\. Similarly, for HSC, we find S 8 = 0\.79 1 − 0\.021 \+ 0\.020 and Ω m = 0\.300 ± 0\.009 when assuming the best\-fit photometric redshift offset suggested by the HSC collaboration\. ## [‘It’s Becoming a Privilege to Own a Pet’ – Pet Acquisition Experiences for Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino Families in Four U\.S\. Cities](../publications/1869f7a5cf3f39d61671.md)

Sloane M\. Hawes; Lexis H\. Ly; Diana Beltrán; Celeste Morales; Jada Ford; Valli\-Laurente Fraser\-Celin

Introduction: Pet ownership has benefits for human and animal well\-being\. However, Black, Indigenous, and People of Color \(BIPOC\) in the United States \(U\.S\.\) face systemic and institutional barriers to acquiring pets\. Current literature on pet acquisition largely overlooks BIPOC families’ experiences\. This study aimed to explore BIPOC families’ experiences, challenges, and priorities regarding pet acquisition in four U\.S\. cities \(Atlanta, Miami, and Minneapolis, Philadelphia\)\. Methods: Focus groups were conducted with 26 pet owners who identify as Black/African American or Hispanic/Latino\. Participants were asked about their perceptions of and experiences with various pet acquisition sources \(animal shelters and rescues, professional or licensed breeders, and family members, friends, or neighbors\) and suggestions to improve the pet acquisition process\. The data were analyzed inductively through rapid qualitative analysis\. Results: Participants reported varied experiences across pet acquisition sources\. Barriers to shelter and rescue adoption included experiences of judgment, lengthy or intrusive screening processes, and a lack of cultural responsiveness\. Some participants described experiences of discrimination from shelters and rescues, particularly related to race and income\. Many relied on friends, family, and neighbors to acquire pets due to convenience, trust, and affordability\. Conclusion: The Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino pet owners in this study encountered structural and interpersonal barriers to pet acquisition that influence their source of pet acquisition\. The participants’ experiences suggest that managing bias and removing barriers to pet acquisition may expand access to the human–animal bond and decrease animal shelter overpopulation and euthanasia\.

## [Enhancement without a rationale? Black pepper extract \(piperine\) in dietary supplements and the future of formulation: a perspective from Japan](../publications/1877fc53a82be90f57c4.md)

Masaki Kaneko

Bioavailability enhancers, most notably black pepper extract \(piperine\), are increasingly added to dietary supplements with claims of “improved absorption\.” Piperine raises systemic exposure to co\-administered compounds not by enhancing absorption but mainly by inhibiting drug\-metabolizing systems, including CYP3A4, CYP2C9, and P\-glycoprotein, and can therefore alter concentrations of concomitant medications, including drugs with a narrow therapeutic index\. This Perspective argues that piperine is frequently included in multi\-ingredient products without a defensible formulation rationale and, in the author&\#x27;s observation, now appears in Japan&\#x27;s practitioner\-exclusive \(clinic\-dispensed\) supplement market\. A structured summary of 22 human pharmacokinetic studies shows that reports of enhanced nutrient absorption derive from manufacturer\-affiliated studies of a few chemical forms; that trials without piperine\-manufacturer involvement have not confirmed enhancement for curcumin or resveratrol at supplement doses; and that interaction studies with prescription drugs, mostly from groups with no commercial interest, repeatedly demonstrate altered drug exposure\. This asymmetry is compounded by inadvertent supplement–supplement combinations and reports of turmeric–piperine\-associated liver injury\. The conditions under which piperine is a rational formulation choice are defined, and label warnings are endorsed as necessary but insufficient\. “Practitioner\-exclusive” labeling does not guarantee a sound formulation, and the good manufacturing practice requirements mandatory for Foods with Function Claims in Japan since September 2026 address manufacturing quality, not formulation appropriateness\. Supplement formulation should be a deliberate, expert\-driven discipline rather than an accumulation of trending ingredients; formulation rationale and interaction risk, not manufacturing quality alone, should become explicit considerations for clinicians, regulators, and industry\.

## [Comparative Evaluation of Different Types of Remineralizing Toothpastes on White Spot Lesions: An In Vitro Study](../publications/187b63d8ed6b68616542.md)



Background: White spot lesions \(WSLs\) are a frequent complication of fixed orthodontic treatment due to plaque accumulation and enamel demineralization\.Aim: To compare the remineralization efficacy of different commercially available toothpastes on WSLs using surface microhardness analysis\.Materials and Methods: Sixty extracted human premolars were demineralized and divided into four groups: artificial saliva \(control\), Sensodyne ProEnamel, Vantej \(nano\-hydroxyapatite\), and Amflor \(amine fluoride\)\.Surface microhardness \(VHN\) was measured at baseline, post\-demineralization, and post\-remineralization\.Statistical analysis included ANOVA and Tukey&\#x27;s post hoc test\.Results: Significant reduction in microhardness occurred after demineralization \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\.Maximum remineralization was observed with Amflor \(94\.7%\), followed by Vantej \(57\.6%\) and Sensodyne \(29\.6%\)\.Conclusion: Amine fluoride toothpaste showed superior remineralization potential and can be recommended for prevention of WSLs in orthodontic patients\.

## [AUTOMATION OF JUDICIAL DECISIONS BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS CONSTITUTIONAL LIMITS](../publications/188ee176955ddbf4a88f.md)

José Ferreira Neto

This article analyzes the constitutional limits of the automation of judicial decisions via Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), investigating its impact on the reasoning and impartiality of the Brazilian Judiciary\. Faced with a litigation crisis and a massive volume of lawsuits, technology has been adopted to ensure procedural speed\. However, the study examines the risks of automation bias and algorithmic opacity, which threaten to transform the law into a statistical system and undermine due process\. Methodologically, the research is based on a review of literature and documents, grounded in legal doctrine and Resolution No\. 332/2020 of the National Council of Justice \(CNJ\)\. The study argues that technological efficiency cannot supersede fundamental guarantees, making it imperative to maintain a &quot;human reserve&quot; at the core of the decision\-making process\. It concludes that AI should serve strictly as a tool for procedural management, preserving the human—and non\-delegable—prerogative of the act of adjudication\.

## [Analysis of subjective complexity through managerial situations throughout the trajectory of projects in SMEs](../publications/1891b9db80c83105337f.md)

Joseph Gniaka Kama

Although project management literature has extensively documented the objective dimensions of complexity, it does not enough explain how complexity is subjectively constructed and transformed by stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle\. In particular, research largely ignores the role of managerial situations\. This research attempts to address this gap by using projects within SMEs as its empirical context\. Based on a questionnaire survey of 154 stakeholders involved in SME projects in France, this research employs factor analysis, analysis of variance, chi\-square tests, and TwoStep classification, conducted using SPSS and XLSTAT software\. The results reveal that the nature of managerial complexity varies depending on the project phases\. Situations of ‘ambivalent’ complexity, the most destabilizing one, are primarily observed during the emergence and implementation phases, while situations of ‘imposed’ complexity are more concentrated in the upstream feasibility and design phases\. Conversely, perceived and routinized forms of complexity appear more frequently during the termination phase, suggesting an evolving dynamic in the manifestations of complexity throughout the project phases\. The study contributes to understanding how the perception of the complexity of managerial situations varies according to the phases of a project by proposing appropriate managerial support to manage them effectively\.

## [Improved YOLOv26\-ACearly\-ASPPdeep for citrus disease and pest detection](../publications/1893d5e7ba0aa0f9d4b6.md)

Huiling Li; Xiaoxia Fang; Yufeng Shu; Yichun Zhan; Jiankai Chen

This study addresses early and accurate detection of citrus diseases and pests under complex orchard conditions, which is essential for timely intervention and yield protection\. The results indicate that depth\-aware AdaptiveConv\-ASPP coupling provides a practical accuracy\-efficiency trade\-off for smart citrus disease and pest surveillance\.

## [Solvent Polarity\-Dependent In Vitro Antioxidant and Enzyme Inhibition Profile of Heracleum persicum: A Preliminary Comparative Screening](../publications/18980042424939aca692.md)

Fatih Dönmez; Hüsniye Kayalar

Heracleum persicum, an aromatic Apiaceae species rich in phenolic compounds, has attracted growing interest, yet comparative data on solvent\-dependent bioactivity remain limited\. In the present study, the aerial parts of Heracleum persicum were subjected to maceration with solvents of graded polarity \(water, ethanol, methanol, and n\-hexane\), and the resulting extracts were evaluated for antioxidant capacity and for inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase \(AChE\), butyrylcholinesterase \(BChE\), and urease\. Antioxidant activity was determined by the ABTS, FRAP, and CUPRAC assays\. All measurements were performed in triplicate \(n = 3\) and expressed as mean ± standard deviation\. Data were compared by one\-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, while Pearson correlation analysis and principal component analysis \(PCA\) were employed for exploratory purposes\. Polar extracts exhibited markedly higher antioxidant activity; the aqueous extract showed the strongest urease inhibition, whereas the n\-hexane extract was most active against AChE\. These findings demonstrate that solvent polarity is a decisive determinant of the antioxidant and enzyme inhibitory profile of Heracleum persicum extracts and provide a rational basis for selecting solvent systems in subsequent bioactivity\-guided studies\.

## [A Review of Machine Learning Applications in Assessing Emotional Intelligence across Social and Professional Domain](../publications/18990d2a01e1ff560639.md)

M\. Karthi P\. Manju

Emotional Intelligence \(EI\) has emerged as a critical determinant of success in both social interactions and professional environments\. Recent advancements in Machine Learning \(ML\) and Data Mining have enabled researchers to move beyond traditional psychometric analysis toward predictive behavioral modeling\. Some of the algorithms implemented according to specific research questions that were applied, were the classification algorithms \(ID3 and J48\) for the production of decision trees, regarding the four more general factors \(welfare, self\-control, emotionality and sociability\) and in overall emotional intelligence\. The results obtained, after weighing and criteria basis, present consumers&\#x27; rates, which in turn analyze the degree of emotional intelligence\. ## [Dijital Etkileşimde İtibar Akışı: İki Aşamalı İletişim Modelinde Sosyal Medya Fenomenlerinin Kurumsal İtibar Algısına Etkisi \(Z Kuşağı Örneği\)](../publications/189ac0f54a385d6c10c3.md)

Mehmet Yalçınkaya

Dijital iletişim çağında sosyal medya fenomenlerinin yükselişi ve Z kuşağının dijital platformlarla kurduğu yoğun ilişki, kurumlar ve markalar için itibar yönetimini köklü bir biçimde dönüştürmüştür\. Bu çalışma, sosyal medya fenomenlerinin algılanan niteliklerinin \(fenomenin algılanan uzmanlığı, fenomenle parasosyal ilişki, fenomenin güvenilirliği ve fenomeni tavsiye etme niyeti\) Z kuşağı bireylerinin kurumsal itibar algısı üzerindeki etkisini incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Aynı zamanda, sosyal medya kullanım yoğunluğunun bu ilişkilerdeki düzenleyici rolü de araştırılmıştır\. Araştırmanın teorik temelini, fenomenleri dijital kanaat önderleri olarak konumlandıran İki Aşamalı İletişim Modeli oluşturmaktadır\. Nicel araştırma yaklaşımı benimsenen çalışmada, sosyal medya kullanıcısı olan 538 Z kuşağı katılımcıdan toplanan veriler analiz edilmiştir\. Veri analizi sürecinde, temel hipotezlerin test edilmesi amacıyla Yapısal Eşitlik Modellemesi \(YEM\) kullanılmıştır\. Ek olarak, sosyal medya kullanım yoğunluğuna göre \(düşük ve yüksek kullanım grupları\) bu ilişkilerin farklılaşıp farklılaşmadığını belirlemek için çok gruplu yapısal eşitlik modeli \(Çok Gruplu YEM\) analizi gerçekleştirilmiştir\. Bulgular, fenomenin algılanan uzmanlığı, fenomenle parasosyal ilişki, fenomenin güvenilirliği ve fenomeni tavsiye etme niyeti boyutlarının tamamının Z kuşağı katılımcılarının kurumsal itibar algısını pozitif ve anlamlı yönde etkilediğini göstermektedir\. Bu sonuçlar, dijital kanaat önderlerinin, özellikle Z kuşağı için, geleneksel medyanın doğrudan etkisinden çok daha güçlü bir itibar aktarımı aracı olarak işlev gördüğünü desteklemektedir\. Çok Gruplu YEM analizinden elde edilecek sonuçlar ise, sosyal medyayı yoğun kullanan Z kuşağının, fenomenler aracılığıyla iletilen kurumsal mesajlardan farklılaşan düzeylerde etkilenip etkilenmediği konusunda değerli yönetimsel çıkarımlar sunacaktır\. Dolayısıyla çalışma, İki Aşamalı Akış Modeli&\#x27;nin dijital geçerliliğini test etmesi ve sosyal medya kullanım yoğunluğunun modere edici etkisini Yapısal Eşitlik Modeli ile derinlemesine incelemesi açısından literatüre önemli bir katkı sağlamaktadır\.

## [Machine Learning\-assisted Antenna Design and Optimization: A Comprehensive Review of Surrogate Modeling, Active Learning, and Intelligent Optimization](../publications/18a1c7db3ebc2076689e.md)

Mitesh Upreti; Sanjay Mathur

The rapid development of wireless communication systems has created an increasing demand for compact, broadband, high\-performance, and application\-specific antennas\. Conventional antenna design approaches generally rely on analytical formulations, empirical relationships, parameter sweeps, and repeated full\-wave electromagnetic \(EM\) simulations, which become computationally expensive as the number of design variables increases\. To address these challenges, metaheuristic optimisation techniques such as Genetic Algorithm \(GA\) and Particle Swarm Optimisation \(PSO\) have been widely investigated for exploring complex antenna design spaces\. More recently, machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) approaches have been introduced for antenna performance prediction, inverse design, and surrogate\-assisted optimisation\. These approaches can reduce the computational burden associated with repeated EM simulations; however, their effectiveness often depends on sufficiently large and representative simulation datasets\. Hybrid ML–metaheuristic approaches further improve the optimisation process by combining predictive models with intelligent search algorithms, while Active Learning enables the selective acquisition of informative simulation samples\. This review presents the evolution of computational antenna design from conventional and metaheuristic approaches to ML\-based, hybrid, and Active Learning\-driven methodologies\. The reviewed studies are critically examined with respect to their design strategies, optimisation techniques, simulation requirements, data dependence, and computational efficiency\. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of surrogate modelling and adaptive sample selection in reducing expensive full\-wave simulations\. The review identifies the limitations of existing approaches and highlights the need for autonomous, data\-efficient, and simulation\-efficient frameworks for high\-dimensional microstrip antenna optimisation\.

## [Edit Discovery in Human\-AI Interactions](../publications/18b5d1560d49653cb3c8.md)

Alireza Mirrokni; Shayan Kiyani; George Pappas; Hamed Hassani

Human\-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected\. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly\. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information\. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool\-use overhead\. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization \(EDO\), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions while controlling unnecessary confirmations and respecting an editor\-cost budget\. We characterize the population\-optimal policy and show that it takes the form of a cost\-adjusted threshold on the posterior probability of an edit\. Building on this structure, we develop EDIT \(Edit Discovery via Iterative Thresholding\), an online algorithm for the partial\-feedback setting in which edit labels are revealed only for selected interactions\. EDIT combines an adaptive edit score, a confirmation\-control threshold, and a cost\-aware selection rule; it satisfies the editor budget at every round and controls the average confirmation rate up to a vanishing finite\-horizon term, without distributional assumptions on the interaction stream\. Across four reasoning and factual question\-answering benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade\-off between editor cost, Type\-I error, and Type\-II error than direct LLM\-based batch selection\.

## [Understanding Disruptive Innovation as Business Model Transformation: The Roles of Entrepreneurial Orientation, Digital Affordances, and Failure Learning](../publications/18ba90a0026736063f7e.md)

Dwi Kartika; Mar&\#x27;atus Solikhah

Purpose – This study aims to examine the conceptual development of Disruptive Innovation \(DI\) by addressing ongoing debates regarding its definition, underlying mechanisms, and boundary conditions\. The research seeks to explain how disruptive innovation emerges and how incumbent firms respond to disruptive forces through the integration of entrepreneurial, technological, and organizational perspectives\. Design/Methodology/Approach – This study employs a Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) approach by analyzing ten high\-quality Q1/Q2 journal articles published between 2020 and 2025\. The review is complemented by the theoretical foundations of Mazzarol and Reboud \(2020\)\. The study synthesizes three main theoretical perspectives: Entrepreneurial Orientation \(EO\), Digital Technology Affordances, and Failure Learning, to develop a conceptual understanding of disruptive innovation mechanisms\. Findings – The findings indicate that Disruptive Innovation is primarily a business model phenomenon rather than solely a technological advancement\. DI emerges through the interaction of Entrepreneurial Orientation, digital technology affordances \(including artificial intelligence\), and dynamic capabilities involving sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring\. Failure Learning serves as an important moderating factor that transforms entrepreneurial intentions into sustainable disruptive outcomes\. The review also reveals that faster innovation adoption by incumbent firms positively affects market value, while delayed responses increase vulnerability to disruptive threats\. Originality/Value – This study contributes to disruptive innovation literature by integrating multiple theoretical streams into a unified conceptual framework\. The proposed framework and four theoretical propositions provide directions for future empirical research, particularly in emerging markets where institutional conditions create both challenges and opportunities for disruptive innovation\. The study also advances understanding of DI as a strategic business model transformation rather than merely a technological disruption\.

## [Geographic distribution of physicians and teachers in Japan – what might we learn from the contrast between two workforce allocation systems?](../publications/18c4a4bd828244247488.md)

Aikyo; Matsumoto

INTRODUCTION: Equitable access to health care and education is recognised as a core human right in both the Constitution of Japan and international frameworks\. However, the geographic distribution of professionals providing these services is governed by different institutional arrangements\. METHODS: This descriptive study used data from the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare&\#x27;s Statistics of Physicians, Dentists and Pharmacists 2020; the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology&\#x27;s School Basic Survey 2023; and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications&\#x27; Basic Resident Register 2023\. The database linked the Japanese population with the number of physicians and teachers in 1896 municipalities across Japan\. Municipalities are classified into four administrative categories \(metropolis, centre city, other city, and town/village\) and are also grouped into four quartiles based on population density\. These government\-mandated censuses comprehensively cover practising physicians and schools, including private institutions, throughout Japan\. Population\-standardised indicators were used to compare geographic distribution patterns\. RESULTS: The total numbers of physicians and teachers analysed in this study were 339,623 and 894,940, respectively\. Physicians were more concentrated in metropolitan areas, whereas teachers were distributed more evenly or were relatively more numerous in less densely populated areas\. The number of physicians per 100,000 people in metropolises was more than double that in towns and villages\. In contrast, the number of teachers per 10,000 children in towns and villages was 1\.4 to 1\.6 times higher than in metropolises\. Similar contrasting patterns were observed when areas were classified by population density quartiles\. CONCLUSION: This contrast highlights how different workforce allocation systems may shape the geographic availability of essential services\. These findings should not, however, be interpreted as implying that one profession is more socially responsible than the other\. The findings suggest that institutional arrangements, including public employment, assignment mechanisms, professional mobility, and financing structures, have a central role in shaping geographic workforce distribution\. Although the teacher allocation framework cannot be directly applied to health care, it offers useful institutional points of comparison for health workforce policy\.

## [Skorburg, Joshua August &amp; Sinnott\-Armstrong, Walter: The alignment problem&\#x27;s problem](../publications/18cc2e59fed4fa3aee87.md)



The GPT\-4o incident can be seen as a natural experiment, of sorts, in AI alignment\. It showed what can happen when user preferences – what users say they like, what their feedback signals reward – are taken as the target of alignment\. Aligning AI to user preferences seems more likely to give us systems that agree with us, rather than systems that get things right\. We argue that this situation vindicates a philosophical position that has been too hastily dismissed\. Namely, that a proper target of AI alignment is idealized preferences\.

## [Large Language Model–Assisted Qualitative Analysis: A Case Study of Medical Students with Academic Difficulties](../publications/18e252e7e9e88fe4aa04.md)

Xiaohan Zhang; Shaohua Li

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet practical accounts of how they can be incorporated without displacing human interpretation remain limited\. This study presents a researcher\-supervised workflow for processing and analysing semi\-structured interviews with medical students experiencing academic difficulties\. Thirty interviews were transcribed, checked against recordings, de\-identified, and analysed through three stages: event/theme identification, element\-level examination of focal events, and cross\-event interpretive construction\. The workflow identified recurring difficulties involving unclear learning goals, limited learning resources, professional\-identity tension, and family expectations\. LLMs supported the organisation of long transcripts and the comparison of related experiences; researchers verified outputs, retained contextual qualifications, and developed the final interpretation\. The findings illustrate that LLMs can make qualitative analysis more traceable and efficient when their outputs are treated as provisional analytic material rather than authoritative conclusions\. We propose practical safeguards for transcription, privacy, validation, and documentation\. This case study offers a concise, reproducible pathway for using LLMs to assist—not replace—qualitative inquiry\.

## [Can LLMs predict the outcomes of machine learning experiments?](../publications/18eed7231f6cb31520b9.md)

Ayush Bansal; Aldo Pareja; Sean Klein; Serge Didenko; Artem Lukoianov

Recent advances in AI make Recursive Self\-Improvement \(RSI\) increasingly plausible\. Large Language Models \(LLMs\) can already propose, select, and run Machine Learning \(ML\) experiments\. However, the space of possible design choices in ML is vast\. An LLM that proposes an experiment needs a reliable intuition of whether it is worth running given the timing constraints of long training runs\. In this work, we measure such intuition in current frontier LLMs by evaluating how accurately they predict the impact of self\-generated ML experiment ideas before these are put into training runs\. To this end, we construct a dataset of 288 LLM\-proposed ideas on eight MLE\-bench tasks\. We then prompt five frontier LLMs \(GPT\-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5\.5, Claude Fable 5\.1, Kimi K3, and GLM\-5\.3\) to predict the impact of each idea and compare their predictions with the actual outcomes after training\. We report four main findings\. First, LLM predictions are substantially better than random chance but far from accurate: even the best model, Claude Opus 5\.5, explains only half of the variance in outcomes \(R^2 = 0\.49\)\. Second, we notice that all tested models systematically underestimate the magnitude of the changes\. Third, prediction quality varies widely across tasks\. Finally, the choice of the coding harness that actually implements the ideas has little effect on outcomes, and we find no evidence of self\-preference\. Higher reasoning settings and additional context lead to modest gains\. Overall, our results show that current LLMs have useful but limited intuition about which ML ideas will work\. We release our dataset to support further study\.

## [P2\-YOLO12: Small Polyp Detection in Colonoscopy via Endoscopic Image Preprocessing and a High\-resolution Detection Head](../publications/18f02ba97da0dc6bb318.md)

Samsul Arifin; Nanik Suciati; Daffa Muhamad Azhar

Accurate polyp detection during colonoscopy is crucial yet challenging because polyps are often small, lowcontrast, and irregularly shaped\.This study proposes P2\-YOLO12, a polyp\-detection framework that couples an integrated endoscopic image preprocessing pipeline with an architecture tailored to small objects\.The pipeline sequentially applies Zero\-Reference Deep Curve Estimation \(Zero\-DCE\) to correct low illumination, Specular\-Aware Inpainting \(SAI\) to remove endoscopic light reflections, and Discrete Wavelet Transform \(DWT\) to suppress noise while preserving polyp edges\.For detection, a P2 detection head was added to the standard YOLO12 heads \(P3, P4, P5\); its higher\-resolution feature map \(stride 4\) better captured the fine details and boundaries of small polyps\.The method was evaluated on a leakage\-controlled split of 3,837 in\-distribution images \(3,322 polyp\-containing and 515 polyp\-free frames; 3,681 polyp boxes\) drawn from Kvasir\-SEG, CVC\-ClinicDB, and PolypGen, grouped by sequence for CVC\-ClinicDB and PolypGen and split at the image level for Kvasir\-SEG, with the fully held\-out ETIS\-LaribPolypDB dataset \(196 images, 208 boxes\) reserved for out\-of\-distribution testing\.Across twenty\-eight scenario ablations over four YOLO generations, the proposed P2\-YOLO12 achieved a precision of 95\.80%, recall of 93\.15%, F1\-score of 94\.46%, mAP50 of 97\.25%, and mAP50\-95 of 71\.85%, outperforming the YOLO12 baseline \(mAP50 of 87\.76%\)\.Size\-stratified evaluation showed that the P2 head raised the small\-polyp average precision \(AP\_small\) from 35\.12% to 55\.40% relative to the baseline\.On the fully held\-out, out\-of\-distribution ETIS\-LaribPolypDB dataset, P2\-YOLO12 retained an mAP50 of 85\.25%, a 12\.3% relative drop from in\-distribution performance compared with a 22\.0% drop for the baseline, whereas AP\_small more than doubled from 18\.75% to 43\.75% relative to the baseline\.These results indicate that integrating image preprocessing with the P2 detection head improves detection sensitivity, localization accuracy, and generalization to an unseen dataset for small, low\-contrast polyps that are most prone to being missed in clinical colonoscopy\.

## [Fuzzy\-Based Cross\-Cultural Validation of a Serious Game Model: 34 Nations](../publications/1916cfb35487cae7a9c1.md)

Mei Kurniawan; M Suyanto; Ema Utami; Kusrini Kusrini

Purpose: This study examines whether the DEGREE \(Digital Educational Game Review and Evaluation Engine\) model demonstrates stable conceptual suitability and global applicability across diverse cultural contexts\. It responds to the need for scalable validation methods for Serious Games evaluation models beyond local psychometric testing\. Methodology: A cross\-sectional single\-click expert\-validation design was combined with fuzzy set theory\. A total of 385 screened expert responses from 34 countries were analysed\. Likert\-scale judgments were converted into triangular fuzzy numbers and defuzzified using the centroid method to derive regional and global conceptual\-suitability scores\. Findings: The model achieved a high global Fuzzy Mean of 0\.84\. Regional results showed Very High suitability in Asia\-Pacific \(0\.91\) and High suitability in Europe \(0\.82\), North America \(0\.79\), and South America and Others \(0\.75\), indicating broad agreement with moderate regional variation\. Originality: The study advances prior DEGREE research by shifting from local instrument validation to global expert\-based conceptual validation\. It introduces a scalable, language\-independent validation paradigm that combines minimal\-interaction expert judgment with fuzzy modelling\. Impact: The findings support the use of DEGREE as a globally adaptable conceptual framework for Serious Games evaluation and provide a rapid validation strategy that can inform intelligent educational technologies, adaptive learning systems, and future user\-based empirical studies\.

## [Growth, Methodological Evolution, and Clinical Maturity of Artificial Intelligence Research in Major Medical Journals, 2018–2025: A Longitudinal Bibliometric Study](../publications/191cb08838c4f56b855d.md)

Abdulraoof Alsaeedi; Norah AlQarni; Ibrahim Rozi; Mohamed Ibrahim

Objectives: To quantify changes in the volume, methods, and clinical maturity of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) research in major medical journals from 2018 through 2025\.Methods: We conducted a longitudinal bibliometric study of PubMed\-indexed records from 99 leading clinical and general medical journals\. The search was conducted on July 2026\. Records were deduplicated and classified as empirical AI/ML research, evidence synthesis, AI discourse, or unclassified\. Empirical studies were categorized by model family and clinical maturity\. Journal\-year Poisson generalized estimating equations used total substantive publications as an offset and clustered observations by journal\.Results: Among 6,891 unique publications, 4,205 \(61%\) were empirical AI/ML studies\. Empirical articles increased from 213 in 2018 to 903 in 2025\. The adjusted publication rate rose by 20\.5% annually \(incidence rate ratio, 1\.205; 95% confidence interval, 1\.166–1\.245; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Blinded validation yielded 92\.7% agreement \(Cohen&\#x27;s kappa, 0\.854\)\. Traditional ML remained dominant, while transformer, large language model, and generative AI studies rose sharply after 2022\. Overall, 81\.9% of empirical studies were retrospective development studies, and 17\.4% reached external validation, prospective evaluation, or real\-world deployment\.Conclusion: The AI/ML research became a larger component of major\-journal output, but clinical translation lagged behind publication growth\. Progress should be assessed through external validation, prospective evaluation, real\-world effectiveness, equity, and transparent reporting\.

## [Optimizing the Privacy Accuracy Trade\-off in Data Stream Mining Using Random Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition](../publications/1929b83d9f8865f9ccf3.md)

Anita A\. Parmar; Chirag A\. Patel

Data stream mining has become increasingly important as a result of the continuous generation of data in real world applications including healthcare monitoring, sensor networks, transportation systems and online services\. While stream classification techniques provide strong predictive performance, publishing or processing such streams raises serious privacy concerns\. Perturbation based privacy preserving data stream mining \(PPDSM\) methods address this issue by adding noise to the data before it is analyzed\. Cumulative noise addition accumulates noise across a fixed\-size cycle of records give a favourable privacy–accuracy trade\-off compared with independent noise addition\. However, a fixed cycle size introduces a predictable and periodic structure in the perturbation process\. This paper proposes Random\-Cycle Cumulative Noise Addition \(RC\-CNA\), a perturbation mechanism that adds noise to random cycle sizes instead of fix\-cycle size\. RC\-CNA is evaluated against the fixedcycle model\. The proposed method raises classification accuracy, lowers privacy breach probability, and achieves the overall Privacy–Accuracy trade\-off\. Proposed method indicates that randomizing the cycle size, combined with the modulation, is a practical improvement that simultaneously strengthens privacy protection and improves classification utility\.

## [Machine\-Learning\-Assisted Tuning of Exchange–Correlation Functional Parameters for the eXact\-Integral Simplified Tamm\-Dancoff Approximation Method](../publications/192d45d41d6bc2b345f3.md)

Sheng\-Rui Wang; Dongyi Xiao; Qiu Fang; Xiang‐Yang Liu; Ganglong Cui

Abstract Here, we improve the accuracy of eXact\-integral simplified Tamm–Dancoff approximation \(XsTDA\) excitation energies through reference\-guided and machine\-learning\-assisted molecule\-specific tuning of exchange–correlation functional parameters in the XsTDA response calculation\. Using DLPNO\-STEOM\-CCSD excitation energies for 55,624 organic molecules, we systematically tune one exchange–correlation functional parameter for four hybrid functionals: the exact\-exchange fraction ax for PBE0 and M06–2X, and the range\-separation parameter ω for CAM\-B3LYP and ωB97X\-D\. Two objectives are considered, targeting either the first 10 singlet excited states or only S1\. With the standard functional parameters, XsTDA yields 10\-state MAEs of 0\.61–0\.97 eV relative to DLPNO\-STEOM\-CCSD, whereas molecule\-specific tuning reduces these errors to 0\.19–0\.28 eV\. The two objectives reveal a clear one\-parameter trade\-off: S1\-specific tuning provides the highest S1 accuracy but compromises higher excited states, whereas 10\-state tuning gives more balanced multistate performance\. To enable practical application to new molecules, five machine\-learning architectures are trained to predict the tuned parameters directly from molecular structure, yielding held\-out\-test MAEs of 0\.21–0\.30 eV for the 10\-state objective and 0\.13–0\.16 eV for the S1\-only objective\. Among the models, a directed message\-passing neural network shows the strongest overall transferability; combined with ωB97X\-D, it yields MAEs of 0\.23 and 0\.24 eV for the 10\-state and S1\-only objectives on the 32\-molecule subset derived from the original XsTDA benchmark\. These results establish ML\-assisted molecule\-specific parameter tuning as a practical route to improve XsTDA excitation energies while retaining its computational efficiency\.

## [Müller, Jean Moritz &amp; Naar, Hichem: Can Emotions Be Rational?](../publications/192f4854d278a6629cca.md)



\_Philosophy Compass\_ 21 \(5\):e70127\. 2026Do emotions belong to the class of rationally assessable phenomena or should they be classified as arational reactions? This article provides an overview of the debate on this question, focusing on contemporary attempts to show that emotions are rationally assessable\. We look at these attempts through the lens of the prominent distinction between a structuralist and a substantivist conception of rationality\. According to the structuralist view, rationality requires coherence among our mental states\. By contrast, on the substantivist view, it requires responsiveness to reasons\. Whereas the most explicit contemporary defenses of emotional rationality endorse structuralism, we explore in detail the case for the view that emotions are substantively rational\. Topics addressed include how we should construe the claim that emotions are rational, whether reasons\-talk is intelligible in the case of emotions, candidates for normative reasons for emotion, and whether emotions can be genuine responses to reasons\. \(direct link \)

## [A comparative analysis of the effect of different drying treatments on the volatile organic compounds of polygonati odorati rhizoma](../publications/19317aa937827b2eb223.md)

Haili Tang; Shijia Zhang; Ziran Yu; Qiuye Liu; 左亚杰

Introduction Polygonati Odorati Rhizoma \(POR\) is a widely recognized functional food, volatile organic compounds \(VOCs\) as one of their main active metabolites\. Drying is a crucial link in the front\-end of the product production chain\. There have been no comparison investigations on the effects of different drying methods on the VOCs of POR\. Methods Gas chromatography\-ion mobility spectrometry \(GC\-IMS\) was utilized to detect and analyze the VOCs of POR samples treated with vacuum freeze\-drying \(VFD\), vacuum drying \(VD\), sun drying \(SD\), hot\-air drying \(HAD\), and microwave drying \(MD\)\. Analytical methods including Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\), Cluster Analysis \(CA\), and Partial Least\-Squares Discriminant Analysis \(PLS\-DA\) were used\. Results A total of 56 VOCs were detected\. Principal component analysis \(PCA\), cluster analysis \(CA\), and partial least\-squares discriminant analysis \(PLS\-DA\), consistently showed that the VOCs of VFD\- and MD\-treated samples were the closest to those of SD samples, whereas VD and HAD differed more markedly\. Representative drying\-specific markers tentatively identified as \(E\)\-2\-heptenal and ethyl hexanoate in SD, 2,5\-dimethyl thiophene in HAD, \(E\)\-2\-butenal in MD, 2\-butanol in VD, and 3\-methyl\-3\-buten\-1\-ol in VFD were observed\. Conclusions These results indicate that different drying methods significantly affect the VOC profile of POR\. VFD and MD are promising for VOC retention\.

## [Institutionalizing Eco\-ELT in an Indonesian Boarding School: A Qualitative Case Study](../publications/1933d5bf6493b84241b7.md)

Arif Bulan; Titi Pujiarti; Diana Purwati; Rusdin Rusdin; Nur Wahyuni; Baharudin Baharudin; Yana Karisma; Ana Joana Dos Reis

This study investigates the institutionalization of Ecological English Language Teaching \(Eco\-ELT\) within an Indonesian boarding school context\. Moving beyond viewing Eco\-ELT as a pedagogical innovation, the study conceptualizes it as an institutional process shaped by leadership, organizational culture, and structural mechanisms\. Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through semi\-structured interviews with the principal and English teachers, classroom observations, and document analysis of school policies and sustainability programs\. The data were analyzed thematically to identify patterns related to institutional framing, pedagogical enactment, and sustainability challenges\. The findings reveal that Eco\-ELT is legitimized through alignment with the school’s ideological vision of character formation and sustainability, and embedded within what the institution terms a “life curriculum\.” Leadership plays a central role in articulating moral direction, while teachers function as mediating agents who translate institutional discourse into classroom practice\. Structural supports, including language policies and environmental routines, reinforce the continuity of sustainability integration beyond formal instruction\. However, the institutionalization process remains partially reliant on normative leadership and organizational culture, with limited formal codification in written policy frameworks\. This study contributes to the emerging discourse on Eco\-ELT by reframing sustainability\-oriented language education as an institutional project rather than merely a curricular adaptation\. The findings highlight the importance of ideological coherence, distributed leadership, and structural alignment in sustaining environmental integration within English language teaching\.

## [Criminalization of Indian Politics: Causes, Consequences, Electoral Trends, Judicial Responses and the Need for Electoral Reforms](../publications/194681d153778157ecdd.md)

Abhay Korde; Adv\. Tanoj Joshi

The criminalization of politics has emerged as one of the most significant threats to India&\#x27;s democratic system\. The increasing participation of individuals with criminal antecedents in electoral politics undermines the principles of constitutional democracy, rule of law, transparency, accountability, and good governance\. Although India possesses an independent judiciary, an autonomous Election Commission, and comprehensive electoral laws, the persistence of candidates facing serious criminal charges in legislative bodies reflects systemic weaknesses in electoral governance and political accountability\. The phenomenon has expanded due to multiple factors, including excessive election expenditure, delayed judicial processes, political patronage, weak enforcement of electoral laws, identity\-based politics, and the growing nexus among politicians, criminals, bureaucrats, and business interests\. This study critically examines the historical evolution of criminalization in Indian politics and analyzes its constitutional, legal, political, and socio\-economic dimensions\. It evaluates the effectiveness of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, constitutional provisions, and the role of the Election Commission of India in addressing the issue\. The paper further examines landmark judgments of the Supreme Court that have strengthened electoral transparency through mandatory disclosure of criminal antecedents and immediate disqualification upon conviction in specified cases\. The study also presents a comparative analysis of political parties and states with respect to elected representatives having criminal backgrounds, using data compiled by the Association for Democratic Reforms \(ADR\) and the Election Commission of India \(ECI\)\. It explores the phenomenon of political horse trading, misuse of constitutional offices, and the erosion of democratic ethics resulting from criminal influence in politics\. The research concludes that criminalization has become institutionalized within India&\#x27;s electoral system due to structural deficiencies and political incentives\. Comprehensive electoral reforms, judicial efficiency, police reforms, transparent political funding, stronger accountability mechanisms for political parties, and enhanced voter awareness are essential to preserve the integrity of Indian democracy\.

## [Rituximabe e caplacizumabe no tratamento da púrpura trombocitopênica trombótica adquirida](../publications/19558eff3155ba3496f6.md)

Junko Sakamoto; Janaina Pereira Dina Toreli; Beatriz da Costa Aguiar Alves; Gláucia Luciano da Veiga; Edimar Cristiano Pereira; Thaís Moura Gascón; Fernando Luiz Affonso Fonseca

Objetivo: avaliar sistematicamente a eficácia e a segurança do rituximabe e do caplacizumabe no tratamento da púrpura trombocitopênica trombótica adquirida \(PTTa\), com ênfase nos seus efeitos sobre a recuperação plaquetária, necessidade de troca plasmática, hospitalização, exacerbações, recidivas e eventos tromboembólicos\. Métodos: foi realizada uma revisão sistemática de estudos publicados em língua inglesa entre 2016 e 2024 para avaliar o uso de rituximabe e/ou caplacizumabe em pacientes com PTTa\. A busca na literatura foi realizada nas bases PubMed, ScienceDirect e Wiley\. Foram considerados elegíveis estudos que investigaram o uso terapêutico do rituximabe e/ou caplacizumabe e relataram desfechos clínicos em pacientes com PTTa\. Registros duplicados e artigos de revisão foram removidos, e os estudos remanescentes foram triados de acordo com os critérios de elegibilidadepreviamente definidos\. Foram excluídos estudos não relacionados ao tratamento da PTTa ou que estavam fora do escopo da revisão\. Os estudos elegíveis foram submetidos à extração sistemática dos dados e à síntese qualitativa, com foco na recuperação plaquetária, necessidade de troca plasmática, tempo de hospitalização, exacerbações, recidivas e eventos tromboembólicos\. Resultados: um total de 14 estudos atendeu aos critérios de inclusão e foi incluído na revisão sistemática final\. A busca nas bases de dados identificou inicialmente 365 registros, sendo 22 no PubMed, 174 no ScienceDirect e 169 na Wiley\. Após a remoção de 2 registros duplicados e 103 artigos de revisão, 260 estudos permaneceram para triagem\. Destes, 246 foram excluídos por não estarem relacionados ao tratamento da PTTa ou por não atenderem aos critérios de elegibilidade previamente definidos, resultando nos 14 estudos incluídos naanálise final\. O caplacizumabe, quando associado à troca plasmática e à terapia imunossupressora, esteve relacionado à recuperação plaquetária mais rápida, menor número de sessões de troca plasmática e menor tempo de hospitalização\. O rituximabe, um anticorpo monoclonal anti\-CD20 que promove a depleção de células B e reduz a produção de autoanticorpos anti\-ADAMTS13, demonstrou benefício clínico quando introduzido precocemente e em pacientes com doença refratária ou recidivante\. A abordagem terapêutica combinada esteve associada à redução de exacerbações, recidivas e eventos tromboembólicos\. Conclusão: O rituximabe e o caplacizumabe representam estratégias terapêuticas eficazes para a PTTa, proporcionando benefícios complementares por meio de mecanismos de ação distintos\. As evidências disponíveis apoiam sua utilização nas estratégias terapêuticas contemporâneas,tanto no tratamento inicial quanto no manejo da doença refratária ou recidivante\.

## [Asian new regionalism revisited: ASEAN–China interactions in the 21 st century](../publications/195b76b0542ceb307656.md)

Hong Liu; Mengting Lyu; Dharendra Wardhana

ASEAN–China interactions constitute a critical site for reassessing the contemporary dynamics of new regionalism in the 21st century\. While scholarship has moved beyond state\-led and Eurocentric paradigms, gaps remain in understanding how new regionalism evolves in Asia\. This article revisits Asian new regionalism and reconceptualises it as a pluralistic, multi\-actor, multi\-layered, and rule\-shaping form of regional configuration engulfed by internal and external challenges\. As demonstrated by ASEAN–China interactions, this process unfolds across digital, financial, and strategic domains and develops through regional agency under great\-power pressures and the new geopolitics\. This article addresses three core questions: What defines the contemporary characteristics of Asian new regionalism? How do these interactions shed new light on its changing forms and modalities? What shapes its trajectories toward integration, fragmentation, or reconfiguration? Drawing on empirical analyses of ASEAN–China interactions, the article highlights the interplay of the state and non\-state actors, the rise of regulatory governance in emerging sectors, and the region’s adaptive responses to internal and external changes\. As a rework of Asian new regionalism, this essay offers an empirically grounded and theoretically informed account of the Global South’s changing role in regional and global governance\.

## [Digital Evidence and the Enforcement of Cybercrime Law in Tanzania: Legal and Investigative Challenges](../publications/195e37f0ac0aebaf2e91.md)

Kennedy Gwakisa Mlawa

The increasing reliance on information and communication technology \(ICT\) has significantly transformed social, economic, and government activities, while also leading to a rise in cybercrime that requires effective legal and institutional responses\. The Cybercrimes Act of 2015 \(Cap\. 443 R\.E\. 2023\) is Tanzania&\#x27;s primary legislation for addressing cybercrimes and overseeing the collection and use of digital evidence in criminal investigations\. However, law enforcement agencies face legal, procedural, and technical obstacles in investigating cybercrimes and managing digital evidence, which hamper full enforcement of this law\. The study used doctrinal legal research methods and qualitatively analysed primary and secondary sources\. Primary sources included the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, statutes, court cases, and relevant international and regional agreements\. Secondary sources comprised books, journal articles, reports, and other literature on cybercrime, digital evidence, and forensic investigation procedures\. The research identified several legal, procedural, and technical challenges in investigating cybercrimes and enforcing the Cybercrimes Act, 2023 in Tanzania\. It showed that, despite a comprehensive legal framework, Tanzania faces significant hurdles, including the lack of specific laws for emerging technologies, insufficient digital forensics infrastructure, limited capacity, procedural issues in preserving electronic evidence, institutional problems, and difficulties in international investigations\. These challenges hinder effective cybercrime investigations, weaken prosecution efforts, and impact the admissibility of digital evidence in court\.

## [What Does School\-Based Nutritious Meals Program Reveal about Nutritional Status and Micronutrient Biomarkers in School\-Aged Children? Implications for Indonesia’s MBG Program](../publications/1960a1cb89b3d3d06e51.md)

Asriyanti Asriyanti; Rudi Saputra; Meiliati Aminyoto

Nutritional problems among school\-aged children in Indonesia continue to reflect a double burden of malnutrition, marked by the coexistence of undernutrition, overweight, and micronutrient deficiencies\. In response, the Free Nutritious Meals \(Makan Bergizi Gratis/MBG\) Program was introduced as a cross\-sectoral initiative that provides daily balanced meals designed to meet children’s energy, protein, and essential micronutrient requirements\. Existing studies consistently suggest that school feeding interventions are associated with improvements in anthropometric indicators, including weight\-for\-age, height\-for\-age, and body mass index\-for\-age, as well as favorable changes in micronutrient biomarkers such as hemoglobin, ferritin, and serum vitamin A\. These outcomes are supported by physiological mechanisms related to adequate intake of animal\-based protein, iron, zinc, and vitamin C, which are essential for growth, cognitive function, and immune competence\. Nevertheless, implementation quality influences program effectiveness, including food safety, menu diversity, consistency of meal provision, and intersectoral coordination\. Limited local biomarker data remain a key challenge, underscoring the need for longitudinal evaluations to assess MBG&\#x27;s biological impact\. Overall, the MBG Program has the potential to contribute to improving the nutritional status of school\-aged children and supporting Indonesia’s long\-term human capital development\.

## [BUB signaling in cancer and molecular insights into targeted therapies](../publications/1967b2c4376c4946b3da.md)

Bhavika Baweja; Camille Saini; Prerna Vats; Rashi Soni; Kritika Jangir; Prachi Patidar; Ashok Kumar; Rajeev Nema

The Spindle Assembly Checkpoint \(SAC\) is vital for proper chromosome segregation during cell division and for maintaining genomic integrity; its disruption can cause aneuploidy and tumors\. The BUB gene family ensures SAC fidelity by regulating kinetochore\-microtubule attachments and mitotic progression\. Dysregulation leads to chromosomal instability \(CIN\), contributing to cancer progression, heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance\. Beyond mitosis, BUB proteins influence DNA repair, chromatin remodeling, transcription, and immune responses\. They interact with cell cycle and genome stability pathways, impacting cancer prognosis and therapy response\. Research is ongoing to validate BUB proteins as biomarkers and develop inhibitors, possibly combined with immunotherapies or DNA\-damaging agents for resistant tumors\. This review summarizes their functions, highlighting their potential in personalized cancer treatment\.

## [Beyond Disclosure: Sustainable Finance Regulation and the Pricing of ESG Performance in Mature Capital Markets](../publications/196fd2d3dd86a259deda.md)

Nicola Del Sarto

ABSTRACT This study examines whether and under what conditions Environmental, Social, and Governance \(ESG\) performance becomes financially meaningful in mature capital markets\. Using a longitudinal transatlantic panel of large firms listed in the EURO STOXX 50 and S&amp;P 100 over the period 2015–2024, we analyse the within‐firm association between lagged ESG performance, market valuation, and accounting profitability\. We further examine whether this relationship changes around the 2018 EU Action Plan on Financing Sustainable Growth and the 2021 implementation of the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, and whether ESG controversies moderate the financial relevance of ESG performance\. Firm and year fixed‐effect models show that improvements in ESG performance are positively but only weakly associated with Tobin&\#x27;s Q , whereas no systematic relationship emerges with accounting profitability\. Policy interaction models and a dynamic event study provide no evidence of a discrete strengthening of the ESG–valuation relationship for EU‐domiciled firms relative to US‐domiciled firms following the selected regulatory milestones\. ESG controversies are directionally associated with weaker ESG value relevance, although the evidence is more pronounced for profitability than for market valuation\. Moreover, the Environmental, Social, and Governance pillars are not statistically distinguishable from one another\. Among large and highly visible firms, sustainable finance regulation may operate as institutional codification and credibility infrastructure rather than as an abrupt valuation shock, although the evidence is equally consistent with limited statistical power and with measurement error in a domicile‐based indicator of regulatory exposure\. The results highlight the conditional and statistically fragile nature of ESG value relevance and should be generalized cautiously beyond institutionally mature capital markets\.

## [A CURADORIA ALGORÍTMICA COMO METODOLOGIA ATIVA: A INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NO DESENVOLVIMENTO DO PENSAMENTO CRÍTICO E NA AVALIAÇÃO ESCOLAR \- UMA BREVE REVISÃO](../publications/19738478be38f84d06b5.md)

Cecília Tavares Neves Braga

O avanço progressivo da Inteligência Artificial Generativa \(GenAI\) e dos Grandes Modelos de Linguagem \(LLMs\) no ecossistema educacional tem redefinido as dinâmicas de ensino, aprendizagem e avaliação\. Contudo, o uso não mediado dessas tecnologias suscita preocupações acerca do descarregamento cognitivo passivo e do enfraquecimento do pensamento crítico discente\. Este artigo de revisão bibliográfica tem como objetivo analisar o conceito de curadoria algorítmica como uma metodologia ativa de aprendizagem, capaz de transformar a interação com a GenAI em um processo reflexivo de auditoria e avaliação formativa\. A fundamentação teórica ancora\-se nos pressupostos do letramento em dados e tecnologia de Luckin \(2018\), Selwyn \(2019, 2022\) e Bender et al\. \(2021\), articulados às abordagens de metodologias ativas propostas por Moran \(2015\)\. A análise aponta que a transição de um modelo centrado na entrega de produtos finais para um processo baseado na formulação iterativa de comandos \(prompts\), verificação de fatos e análise de vieses favorece o protagonismo estudantil e fortalece o julgamento epistemológico\. Conclui\-se que a curadoria algorítmica se consolida como uma práxis pedagógica viável para mitigar a dependência cognitiva, oferecendo caminhos para uma integração ética, crítica e emancipatória da inteligência artificial na educação básica e superior\.
