## [Machine Learning Explicable \(XAI\) en Sistemas de Software Inteligentes: Un Enfoque para Mejorar la Confiabilidad](../publications/1989f25bb440a9a85386.md)

Maria Teodolinda Ortega Ovalle

The increasing integration of Machine Learning models into intelligent software systems has driven significant advances in automation, prediction, and decision\-making\. However, the inherent complexity of many algorithms, particularly those based on deep learning, has raised concerns regarding reliability, transparency, and accountability in critical contexts\. Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) is an essential response to these limitations, providing mechanisms to interpret, justify, and audit model behavior\. This article examines the main XAI approaches applied to intelligent systems, including local and global explanation methods, surrogate models, feature decomposition techniques, and visualization tools\. It also analyzes current challenges in explanation evaluation, integrating XAI into software architectures, and balancing interpretability with predictive performance\. The results show that systematically incorporating XAI enhances system reliability, strengthens decision\-making, and facilitates the adoption of ML models in regulated sectors such as healthcare, finance, and security\. Finally, the paper proposes a conceptual framework to guide the implementation of XAI in intelligent systems, ensuring transparency, robustness, and algorithmic responsibility\.

## [AVC\-Reward: Event\-Centric Audio\-Video Consistency Evaluation](../publications/198b134c27192ca31ff1.md)

Yuruo Wu; Kaihang Pan; Kai Shen; Jiacheng Li; Shuyuan Tu; Jisheng Dang; Li Tuoyu; Juncheng Li; Siliang Tang

As joint audio\-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio\-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi\-event composition, multi\-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross\-modal relations\. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks\. They typically evaluate an audio\-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes\. We propose an event\-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross\-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse\-to\-fine, three\-level consistency metric\. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event\-level temporal synchronization, and fine\-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio\-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross\-modal relations\. We instantiate the metric as AVC\-Reward, a trainable audio\-video reward model\. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC\-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio\-video generation models\. AVC\-Reward achieves state\-of\-the\-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio\-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement\-learning signal\. Project page: https://tsuki0512\.github\.io/AVC\-Reward\.github\.io/

## [Retrospective discriminative performance of an exploratory modified early obstetric warning score for identifying critical obstetric conditions in pregnant and puerperal women](../publications/198f501151c87982103f.md)

Jiali Shen; 沈利萍; Qiong Sun

Objective: To compare the retrospective discriminative performance of the modified early warning score \(MEWS\), modified early obstetric warning score \(MEOWS\), and an exploratory modified MEOWS \(MMEOWS\) for identifying critical obstetric conditions in pregnant and puerperal women\. Methodology: This single\-center retrospective study included 5,867 women hospitalized from January 2023 to December 2024 at Huzhou Maternal and Child Health Hospital\. Participants were classified according to the occurrence of critical obstetric conditions during hospitalization\. MEWS, MEOWS, and MMEOWS were calculated using the most abnormal values recorded during hospitalization\. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to assess area under the curve \(AUC\), optimal cutoff values, sensitivity, and specificity\. Results: Of 5,867 participants, 1,050 \(17\.9%\) met the composite definition of critical obstetric conditions\. MEWS, MEOWS, and MMEOWS scores were significantly higher in the critical group \(all P&lt;0\.001\)\. The AUCs were 0\.817 \(95% CI, 0\.803–0\.830\), 0\.882 \(0\.870–0\.894\), and 0\.911 \(0\.901–0\.922\), respectively\. At the optimal cutoff, MMEOWS showed 80\.76% sensitivity and 88\.15% specificity\. At predefined clinical thresholds, MEOWS had the highest sensitivity but low specificity, whereas MMEOWS showed a more balanced sensitivity\-specificity profile\. Conclusion: All three scores discriminated critical from non\-critical obstetric cases in this retrospective cohort\. MMEOWS showed the highest retrospective discriminative performance, but its prospective early\-warning value requires validation using predefined early assessment time points\.

## [The Effect of Multisensory\-Based Materials on the Reading Skills of Children with Learning Disabilities](../publications/199573372a1a77cbe7ca.md)

Rabia Kural; Zehra Esra Ketenoğlu Kayabaşı

Reading material that appeals to multiple senses can provide readers with an interactive, active reading and learning environment\. This study investigates the effectiveness of reading activities with multisensory materials on the fluent reading skills of students diagnosed with specific learning disabilities\. For this purpose, the students were asked to use the material by first listening, then reading, then acting out the story with puppets, and finally rereading it with the book “My Book, My Friend”, a material developed using a multisensory method\. The study was designed using a qualitative approach and conducted through action research\. Five students and three teachers included in the study were given a material book developed based on multisensory concepts to practice in the support education room in general education schools and were asked to use it\. Then, the LAB \(Literacy Assessment Battery\) was applied to determine the effectiveness of the material\. As a result of the research, it was observed that using multisensory materials improved students’ reading, reading comprehension and writing\.

## [Trans\-anethole attenuates streptozotocin\-induced cognitive dysfunction by modulating oxidative stress and cholinergic activity](../publications/199a2e7a9ee3b9b98c61.md)

Shruti S\. Mole; Prarambh S\. R\. Dwivedi; Wilona Loren Lobo; C\. S\. Shastry; Pukar Khanal

Introduction Cognitive impairment is a neurological disorder defined as an inability to learn, think, judge, remember, and make decisions\. The primary cause of chronic, age\- related cognitive decline is Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\), which is frequently studied as a representative model\. The current therapies for AD provide only symptomatic relief, which necessitates the need for safer, multi\-target treatments\. Trans\- anethole, the primary constituent of Illicium verum , Pimpinella anisum , and Foeniculum vulgare , is an aromatic molecule that possesses several pharmacological activities, including anti\-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which may have neuroprotective benefits\. Methods The current study integrated in silico , in vitro , and in vivo approaches to examine the neuroprotective potential of trans\- anethole\. In silico studies were carried out to find out the potential molecular targets and pathways associated with the effects of trans\-anethole against AD\- related cognitive dysfunction\. Cytotoxicity, antioxidant activity, and cholinesterase inhibition were assessed in vitro on BV2 cells\. Intracerebroventricular \(ICV\) administration of streptozotocin \(STZ: 3 mg/kg\) in rats induces an insulin\-resistant brain state leading to progressive cognitive and memory impairment, a condition that closely relates to sporadic Alzheimer’s disease\. ICV\-STZ\-induced Wistar rats were used to assess the effect of trans\- anethole on AD\-related cognitive dysfunction through behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological assessments\. Results A total of 174 common targets were identified, enriching pathways including apoptosis, AGE\-RAGE, TNF, and PI3K\- Akt signaling\. Stable interactions were observed in molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations\. Trans\-anethole demonstrates moderate cholinesterase inhibition and antioxidant activity in BV2 cells\. Comparing STZ\- treated rats to disease control, trans\-anethole at doses of 100 mg/kg and 400 mg/kg significantly reduced lipid peroxidation, restored antioxidant enzyme levels, and attenuated cholinergic dysfunction\. Histopathological findings showed qualitative preservation of hippocampal neuronal morphology\. Discussion Overall, these findings suggest that trans\-anethole may represent a potential neuroprotective preclinical candidate for further investigation in Alzheimer’s disease\-related cognitive dysfunction\.

## [“Russian Socrates”: M\.K\. Mamardashvili and V\.V\. Bibikhin](../publications/19a008c583d0f6141c3f.md)

О\. В\. Зарапин; О В Зарапин

В отечественной философской культуре М\.К\. Мамардашвили и В\.В\. Бибихин – знаковые фигуры, олицетворяющие философский профессионализм в преодолении академических барьеров, в открытости к жизни, интеллектуально связывающей людей друг с другом\. Яркое выражение этого – в педагогике, в курсах лекций, следующих образцу преподавания философии как живого философствующего самосознания на виду у всех\. Автор статьи исходит из того, что действенность этого образца раскрывается вовсе не в силе харизматического самосознания, вызывающего аудиторию к соприсутствию и ответу\. Его тезис состоит в том, что такой образец воплощает уже известную форму действия, которая реализуется в виде публичного чтения классического философского текста и в нацеленности на то, чтобы «узнать себя в Другом»\. Эту форму можно назвать сократической\. В статье она реконструирована на материале учебных курсов М\.К\. Мамардашвили «Кантианские вариации» и В\.В\. Бибихина «Чтение философии»\. В курсах согласуются: избранный лектором способ чтения текста, заложенная в этот способ идея самосознания, средства поддержания контакта с аудиторией\. Автор статьи подчеркивает, что педагогическое наследие отечественных философов выражается в неосократизме, особо востребованном в цифровую эпоху\. Он представляет собой реальную и действенную оппозицию популяризируемой практике общения с обученной нейросетью, способной внушить пользователю представление о том, что самосознание личности есть совокупность переживаний индивида, ценный и интересный элемент его приватной интеллектуальной жизни\.

## [Perceived readiness for self\-directed e\-learning in undergraduate physiotherapy education: Insights for future curriculum development](../publications/19b1ccfdff053f842ed4.md)

Anri Human; M Cochrane\-Boeyens

Background\. Self\-directed learning \(SDL\) is an essential competency for health sciences students, particularly as higher education increasingly integrates blended\- and e\-learning approaches\. In South Africa where students enter tertiary education from diverse socioeconomic and educational backgrounds, the readiness of physiotherapy students to engage in SDL within e\-learning environments remains underexplored\. Objectives\. To investigate the perceived readiness of undergraduate physiotherapy students to participate in self\-directed e\-learning at a South African tertiary institution\. Methods\. A descriptive, cross\-sectional study was conducted among first\- to fourth\-year physiotherapy students \(N=217\)\. Participants voluntarily completed the UniSIM questionnaire, a validated tool assessing 10 SDL readiness domains\. Responses were rated on a 7\-point Likert scale, with descriptive statistics used for analysis\. Results\. A total of 94 students \(43%\) completed the questionnaire\. Most reported readiness in key SDL areas, including motivation and planning \(85\.80%\), comprehension competence \(95\.45%\), time management \(79\.17%\) and online learning proficiency \(72\.27%\)\. However, only 52\.27% felt confident managing tests and examinations, and 71\.82% reported difficulty managing stress\. Despite overall readiness for SDL, 76\.89% preferred guided learning formats, such as lectures\. Conclusion\. Undergraduate physiotherapy students demonstrated overall readiness for self\-directed e\-learning, particularly in areas critical for academic autonomy\. However, stress management emerged as a notable barrier, and the preference for guided instruction suggests a need for structured support\. Future initiatives should incorporate strategies to strengthen emotional resilience and gradually foster SDL competencies across all years of study\.

## [Fuel load and potential fire behavior vary seasonally and across grassland plant communities](../publications/19b56ec9beecfef71038.md)

Lina Aoyama; Katharine N\. Suding; Advyth Ramachandran; Jordan T\. Lee; Paul Dennison; Thomas K\. Merchant; Jonathan J\. Henn

Abstract Grassland fuels can be patchy across space and time, especially on landscapes where multiple grassland plant communities co\-occur\. However, the standard fuel models inadequately capture the spatiotemporal variability in grassland fuels for local, strategic planning of fuel treatments\. We aimed to better understand the seasonal variation in grassland fuels and fire behavior across grassland types\. Here, we developed remote sensing\-based grassland fuel maps using multispectral satellite data \(10\-m resolution\) from Sentinel\-2, compared seasonal fire behavior across grassland types, and performed a sensitivity analysis of fire behavior models to changes in litter, dead 1 h, and live herbaceous loads, and fuelbed depth estimates\. We were able to best predict live herbaceous load \(R2 = 0\.85\), followed by fuelbed depth \(R2 = 0\.81\), dead 1 h fuel load \(R2 = 0\.76\), and litter load \(R2 = 0\.67\) based on remotely sensed predictors\. Our spatially predicted grassland fuel maps showed seasonal variability in fuel loads in different places, reflecting the varying timing of curing by grassland types\. In particular, we observed more accumulation of dead 1 h load between August and October in early senescing mixedgrass prairies than later senescing tallgrass prairies\. We found an overall faster modeled rate of spread in smooth brome\-dominated, invasive grasslands and native tallgrass prairies compared to mixedgrass and prairie dog\-dominated grasslands\. From the sensitivity analysis, we found that modeled fire behavior model is most sensitive to dead 1 h fuel load and least sensitive to litter load in this grassland system\. At a time when grassland fires are increasing and resources for fuel management are limited, remote sensing approach to grassland fuel modeling may help land managers make decisions about where and when to prioritize fuel treatments to mitigate the risk of catastrophic wildfires\.

## [Principal Component Analysis of Barriers to Smart Mining Technology Adoption in Hard\-Rock Mining](../publications/19b866c4a142a8e94868.md)

Olusegun Aanuoluwapo Oguntona; Chijioke Emmanuel Emere; Clinton Ohis Aigbavboa

The transition toward smart mining technologies \(SMTs\), spanning automation, artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and digital twins, is reshaping safety, productivity and sustainability outcomes across the global extractive sector\. Yet, their adoption within South Africa’s hard\-rock mining industry remains slow, fragmented and empirically under\-theorised\. Drawing on diffusion of innovation and socio\-technical systems perspectives as interpretive lenses, this exploratory study investigates the barriers to SMT adoption as perceived by mining professionals\. A quantitative research design was adopted, using a structured questionnaire administered to 80 mining professionals across South Africa’s Northwest, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces\. Data were analysed through a three\-stage process comprising reliability and validity testing, descriptive statistics, and principal component analysis \(PCA\)\. PCA of the twenty\-one barriers identified in the literature extracted four components that jointly explained 62\.05% of the total variance\. Nineteen barriers met the loading criteria for assignment to these components: Adoption Risk and Workforce Barriers; Organisational and Stakeholder Readiness Barriers; Technological Awareness and Change Barriers; and Institutional and Environmental Sustainability Barriers\. The findings suggest that, as perceived by the respondents, barriers to SMT adoption extend beyond technological limitations to include regulatory ambiguity, financial constraints, workforce readiness and weak institutional support\. Given the modest, non\-probability sample, the component structure is exploratory and preliminary\. It requires confirmatory testing in larger, independent samples before it is extended to other capital\-intensive, safety\-critical and regulation\-heavy industries\. The study concludes with practical, policy, and theoretical implications for mining firms, technology providers, regulators, and researchers seeking to accelerate safe, sustainable, and intelligent digital transformation\.

## [Metagenomic characterization of microbial communities associated with alphaherpesvirinae detection in magnificent frigatebirds from French Guiana](../publications/19bb36b3d766b7a34fbd.md)

Ilaria Di Bartolo; Manrico Sebastiano; Gabriele Vaccari; Elisabetta Suffredini; Arianna Boni; David Costantini; Luca De Sabato

Introduction A population of Magnificent Frigatebirds \(Fregata magnificens, Suliformes\) inhabiting French Guiana has been under investigation since 2005 due to high chick mortality rates associated with nodular proliferative skin lesions, characterized by featherless areas on the body\. An initial study conducted in 2009 reported the presence of an alphaherpesvirus detected in a crust from a single individual in the same frigatebird population\. However, the cause of the outbreaks and the associated high mortality in the frigatebird population remained undetermined\. Methods Almost 15 years later, in 2024, we collected beak swabs, cloacal swabs, and blood samples from 14 animals\. Six animals were clinically healthy, while eight showed clinical signs including skin crusts, hyperkeratosis on the eyes, corneal thickening, and signs of distress\. To investigate the potential causes of those signs, we screened the samples for herpesviruses\. To characterize bacterial and viral communities and investigate potential co\-infections, we selected four beak swabs for metagenomic analysis: two from herpesvirus\-positive individuals and two from herpesvirus\-negative controls \(one healthy and one with clinical signs\), and sequenced them using metagenomic Next Generation Sequencing \(NGS\)\. Results and discussion Two individuals tested positive for herpesviruses in beak swabs, one healthy and one with clinical signs\. Analysis of the bacterial community revealed that the most abundant phyla were Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, and Fusobacteria, which typically inhabit the gut microbiota\. All reported bacterial phyla were detected in every sequenced sample\. At the viral level, among non\-bacteriophage viruses, Orthoherpesviridae showed the highest abundance in PCR\-positive animals, followed by Adenoviridae\- and Hepadnaviridae\-related sequences\. Sequence analysis of the DNA\-directed DNA polymerase \(DdDp\) region of Orthoherpesviridae identified two sequences: one with 98\.1% nucleotide identity to sequences reported in the same geographic area in 2005, and the other with 72\.1% identity to a vulture herpesvirus from India\. The bacterial and viral populations detected were largely similar between animals with and without clinical signs\. Due to the limited sample size, it was not possible to determine whether the detected microorganisms were associated with the observed clinical signs\.

## [Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study](../publications/19c583b7a40a95dc4388.md)

Yixing Li; Dehui Liu; Ruixue Qin; Xingchang Li; Mei Li

Background Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects\. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level\. Objectives Age\-standardized thyroid cancer incidence was the prespecified primary outcome\. We aimed to \(1\) build machine learning models predicting country\-level thyroid cancer incidence from dietary and socioeconomic features, \(2\) quantify confounder\-adjusted dietary associations with incidence, including prespecified sensitivity analyses of the iodine\-rich food availability index, and \(3\) identify key dietary predictors through explainability analyses and a descriptive decomposition of the development pathway\. Mortality was analyzed only as a secondary outcome in order to evaluate whether the incidence patterns could be attributed to differential cancer detection rather than to differences in disease occurrence\. Methods We integrated GLOBOCAN 2022 \(cancer outcomes\), FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets \(113 food items, 2010–2022; primary exposure 2015–2019 mean\), the UNDP Human Development Report 2025 statistical annex \(HDI 2023 and its life expectancy, education, and income sub\-indices\), and WHO obesity prevalence \(2022\) across 163 countries, yielding 155 harmonized variables and 150 numeric predictors\. All modeling was performed inside a nested cross\-validation framework: multiple imputation by chained equations, standardization, four\-method consensus feature selection, and hyperparameter search were fitted exclusively on the training partition of each outer fold \(10 folds × five repetitions\), and performance was summarized from pooled out\-of\-fold predictions with 95% confidence intervals obtained by resampling countries \(2,000 bootstrap replicates\)\. Three analyses separated dietary signal from confounding: block\-wise models comparing socioeconomic\-only, diet\-only and combined feature sets; leave\-one\-region\-out validation across six world regions; and confounder\-adjusted partial correlations under a basic \(HDI, obesity\) and an extended adjustment set \(HDI, obesity, the three HDI sub\-indices, and region fixed effects\), with Benjamini–Hochberg and Bonferroni correction applied across all comparisons\. Iodine\-related exposure was represented by an iodine\-rich food availability index constructed from seafood, dairy, and egg supply; its construction was interrogated in four sensitivity analyses in which the components were entered separately and jointly, four weighting schemes were compared, total animal protein supply was added to the adjustment set, and an iodine\-poor animal\-origin food index was used as a specificity control\. Binary classification and all mortality analyses were secondary\. Results Regression on incidence was the primary task\. Stacking ensemble performed best, with a pooled out\-of\-fold R ² of 0\.613 \(95% CI \[0\.510, 0\.726\]\), RMSE = 3\.04, MAE = 1\.82, and Spearman ρ = 0\.901 \(95% CI \[0\.862, 0\.924\]\); random forest \( R ² = 0\.609\), bagging \( R ² = 0\.599\), and KNN \( R ² = 0\.580\) followed, and a high\-dimensional deep tabular model \(DynaTab\) was statistically comparable \( R ² = 0\.626\)\. Predictive accuracy was, however, almost entirely socioeconomic: nine development variables alone gave R ² = 0\.609, 140 dietary variables alone gave 0\.284, and the incremental contribution of the dietary block was –0\.048 \(95% CI −0\.169 to \+0\.034\), \+0\.021, and \+0\.017 across model families\. Under leave\-one\-region\-out validation, the rank ordering of countries was largely preserved \(pooled ρ = 0\.813\), but the level was not\. Unadjusted associations with incidence were positive for the iodine\-rich food availability index \( ρ = 0\.234\), total energy \( ρ = 0\.230\), seafood \( ρ = 0\.219\), and the animal\-to\-plant protein ratio \( ρ = 0\.221\)\. After adjustment and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, seafood supply, dairy supply, the iodine\-rich food availability index, the animal\-to\-plant protein ratio, and mollusks remained significant under the extended adjustment set \(seafood partial r = 0\.196, q = 0\.031; iodine\-rich food availability index 0\.224, q = 0\.026\), whereas plant protein did not \(–0\.095, q = 0\.309\)\. In sensitivity analyses, the index association was carried by seafood \(0\.196, q = 0\.017\) and dairy \(0\.198, q = 0\.017\) but not eggs \(0\.065, q = 0\.411\), was stable across equal\-weighted, z\-score, and iodine\-content\-weighted constructions \(0\.238–0\.256\), survived further adjustment for total animal protein supply \(0\.203, q = 0\.032\), and was not reproduced by an iodine\-poor animal\-origin food index \(0\.102, q = 0\.198\)\. Path decomposition attributed 50\.2% of the seafood–incidence correlation to the HDI pathway \(95% bootstrap CI 16%–90%\)\. In the secondary mortality analysis, the dietary ordering was preserved, but associations with the mortality\-to\-incidence ratio were close to zero \(HDI ρ = 0\.053; seafood ρ = 0\.065\), and in the sensitivity classification analysis, Extra Trees reached AUC = 0\.932 \(95% CI \[0\.893, 0\.964\]\) at the median split\. Conclusions With all model construction confined to training folds, machine learning models built from national food supply and socioeconomic data explain a moderate share of the between\-country variation in thyroid cancer incidence, but that predictive accuracy is carried by development indicators rather than by diet\. The availability of iodine\-rich food groups, seafood supply, and the animal\-to\-plant protein ratio nevertheless retained positive ecological associations with incidence after adjustment for development and metabolic confounders and after correction for multiple comparisons, and the index association proved robust to how the index was constructed and specific to iodine\-rich rather than to animal\-origin food groups in general; plant protein showed no association once multiplicity was controlled\. Roughly half of the seafood–incidence correlation tracks the development pathway, and the secondary mortality analysis is consistent with a substantial contribution from differential detection\. These findings are ecological associations with the availability of iodine\-rich food groups, not with measured iodine intake or exposure; they generate testable hypotheses for individual\-level studies with measured iodine status and do not establish causation\.

## [Task Allocation and Improvement of Collective Work Efficiency in Swarm Robotics Using Autonomous Decentralized Algorithms](../publications/19cbbff926b3b855654f.md)

Taiki Watanabe; Yuki Tanigaki; Tomohiro Hayakawa; Fumitoshi Matsuno; Ryusuke Fujisawa

This study proposes a decentralized, dynamic task allocation algorithm for swarm robotics to enhance efficiency in multi\-foraging tasks\. Inspired by the adaptive foraging behavior of social insects, the proposed method introduces a utility\-based metric called &quot;Umami,&quot; which evaluates food sources based on their quantity and distance from the nest\. Each robot dynamically transitions between three roles—Searcher, Picker, and Carrier—based on local information and threshold\-based switching\. Simulation experiments conducted under various environment sizes and robot densities demonstrated that the proposed integrated model achieved notably higher foraging efficiency, especially in large\-scale environments\. These findings suggest that the proposed approach offers a scalable and adaptable solution for efficient task execution in swarm robotic systems\.

## [Diminished ovarian reserve in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical, immunological, viral, and therapeutic determinants in a 24\-month prospective study](../publications/19d0c0a700ff12667f58.md)

Margherita Rizzo; Silvia Beltrami; Francesca Ruffilli; Carlo Garaffoni; Ettore Silvagni; Daria Bortolotti; Giorgia Cianci; Maila Galloppa; Beatrice Maranini; Marcello Govoni; Roberta Rizzo; Alessandra Bortoluzzi

Background and objectives Systemic lupus erythematosus \(SLE\) predominantly affects women of reproductive age; however, the impact of the disease, chronic inflammation, and its treatments on ovarian reserve remains insufficiently characterized\. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve in SLE and to evaluate the longitudinal associations of clinical characteristics, therapeutic exposures, and herpesvirus serologies with Anti\-Müllerian Hormone \(AMH\) levels\. Methods This observational prospective monocentric study followed 80 premenopausal women \(18–45 years\) with SLE for 24 months\. Clinical data, treatments, AMH levels, and herpesvirus serologies were collected every 6 months\. Patients were stratified by diminished ovarian reserve \(AMH &lt;1 ng/mL\)\. Longitudinal AMH trajectories and the impact of covariates were evaluated using repeated\-measures analyses and linear mixed\-effects models\. Results The cohort exhibited a high prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve \(45% of the study population\), associated with older age \(37 ± 7 vs\. 34 ± 7 years, p = 0\.041\), longer disease duration \(14 ± 9 vs\. 10 ± 6 years, p = 0\.026\), higher cumulative damage \(p = 0\.007\), and lupus anticoagulant positivity \(14% vs\. 39%, p=0\.009\)\. Disease activity was comparable across groups\. Hydroxychloroquine use was more frequent in women without diminished ovarian reserve \(89% vs 69%, p = 0\.033\)\. Over 24 months, AMH levels remained stable with no progressive decline\. Belimumab exposure did not adversely affect AMH trajectories, and viral serologies showed no direct long\-term impact on AMH levels\. Conclusions This prospective longitudinal study highlights that diminished ovarian reserve is common in women with SLE\. AMH levels remained stable over 24 months, with no adverse longitudinal association with belimumab exposure\. Hydroxychloroquine use was associated with a lower prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve and warrants further investigation\. Serial AMH assessment may support personalized reproductive counselling in women with SLE\.

## [Immune\-checkpoint blockade and candidate predictive biomarkers in HIV\-negative Kaposi sarcoma: current evidence and a practical research framework](../publications/19d0d10a189a8847308f.md)

Yang Song; Yan Fang; Lin Zeng; Hua Guan

Kaposi sarcoma \(KS\) is a KSHV/HHV\-8\-driven vascular neoplasm with heterogeneous HIV\-negative epidemiological settings\. Immune\-checkpoint blockade is biologically plausible, but direct clinical evidence remains limited to a small, non\-comparative phase II cohort of pembrolizumab in classic or endemic KS\. Its 71% best objective response rate is a signal that warrants confirmation, not comparative evidence or a basis for biomarker\-guided treatment\. This narrative review distinguishes established clinical observations from candidate translational hypotheses, appraises analytical and biological limitations of proposed markers, and outlines requirements for prospective subtype\-stratified validation\. PD\-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden, and KSHV DNA should not be used as stand\-alone selection or exclusion tests in routine care\.

## [Genetic associations in the gut–lung axis: a Mendelian randomization study and in vitro assessment of sodium butyrate in non\-small cell lung cancer](../publications/19d37f16210e1e008e1d.md)

Weili Yi; Li Qin; Dongning Huang; Fang Wu

Background The gut microbiota may influence host immunity, but the relationship between specific microbial genera and non\-small cell lung cancer \(NSCLC\) risk remains uncertain\. We evaluated genetically proxied microbial abundance and conducted separate exploratory experiments with sodium butyrate \(NaB\)\. Methods Two\-sample Mendelian randomization \(MR\) used genus\-level MiBioGen summary statistics and FinnGen/OpenGWAS NSCLC data \(finn\-b\-C3\_LUNG\_NONSMALL; 1,627 cases and 217,165 controls\)\. Instruments were selected at P &lt; 1 × 10 −5 with linkage disequilibrium clumping \(r 2 &lt; 0\.001; 10,000 kb\) and F &gt; 10\. Inverse variance weighting \(IVW\) was the primary estimator; Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate \(BH\-FDR\) correction was applied across 119 genera\. Sensitivity analyses included MR\-Egger, weighted median, mode\-based methods, heterogeneity, pleiotropy and leave\-one\-out analyses\. NaB, used as a representative microbial metabolite rather than a taxon\-specific product, was evaluated at 1 mM for 24 h in tumor\-conditioned medium \(TCM\) experiments\. Results Six genera showed nominal inverse IVW associations with NSCLC risk \(P = 0\.0120–0\.0498\): Alistipes, Methanobrevibacter, Bacteroides , Ruminococcus gauvreauii group, Ruminococcus 1 and Peptococcus \. None survived BH\-FDR correction \(q = 0\.6072–0\.9819\)\. Sensitivity tests did not detect heterogeneity or directional pleiotropy for these genera, but alternative estimators and leave\-one\-out analyses did not consistently retain nominal significance\. In THP\-1\-derived macrophages, NaB treatment altered polarization\-associated transcripts, reduced the TCM\-associated CCK\-8 signal and increased acetylated histone H3 \(Ac\-H3\) relative to TCM alone\. Conclusion The MR analysis identifies six suggestive microbial associations with NSCLC risk that require independent replication\. Complementary NaB experiments show changes in macrophage\-associated transcripts, metabolic viability and histone acetylation, providing a basis for further study of microbial metabolites in the tumor microenvironment\.

## [Metaheuristic Hyperparameter Optimization of Machine Learning Models for Diabetes Prediction](../publications/1a0151960b026b2b8d90.md)

Halim Dayanan; Ali Akdağlı; Timur Lale

This study investigates the effect of metaheuristic hyperparameter optimization on machine learning\-based diabetes prediction using a unified experimental framework\. Five classifiers—Logistic Regression, K\-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost—were optimized using the Dhole Optimization Algorithm \(DOA\), Grey Wolf Optimization \(GWO\), Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\), and RIME\. After removing duplicate records, 96,146 observations were retained and divided into stratified training and independent test subsets\. Hyperparameter tuning was conducted only on the training data using five\-fold cross\-validation, while model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, Matthews correlation coefficient, ROC\-AUC, and PR\-AUC\. Among the 20 model\-optimizer combinations, XGBoost\-PSO achieved the highest test F1 score of 0\.8119, whereas XGBoost\-GWO produced the highest ROC\-AUC of 0\.9781 and PR\-AUC of 0\.8849\. Decision Tree also showed competitive performance, while Random Forest\-RIME achieved the highest recall but with lower precision and F1 score\. At the optimizer level, GWO provided the strongest average predictive performance, whereas DOA offered the greatest computational efficiency\. Cross\-validation and independent test results were generally consistent, indicating satisfactory generalization\. Correlation and permutation feature importance analyses identified HbA1c level and blood glucose level as the most influential predictors\. Overall, the findings show that model and optimizer selection should jointly consider predictive performance, generalization, interpretability, and computational efficiency\.

## [Norman, John Mark: The BAL\-Looping Framework in a Nutshell: A Standalone Diagram](../publications/1a0611012f7629ede91e.md)



This single diagram is presented as a standalone item intended to accompany any of the papers on the BAL\-looping framework\. It shows the framework&\#x27;s bare\-bones architecture, omitting much of the terminology and detail developed in the papers, such as the brain at large \(BAL\), the proxy transfer device \(PTD\), neuronal proxies, the internal model of the environment, and other elements that flesh out the framework\. It also leaves aside important conceptual distinctions, such as the fact that gist is not linguistic in nature but is the very stuff of subjective experience, in all its modes\. Some functional relationships, such as the resonance between the output and input channels during looping, are not explicitly labeled but are readily discernible from the diagram\. While examining the diagram, the reader thus closes certain gestalts, a process that can contribute both to understanding and to memory\. \(Updated October 17, 2026 – Added a second page containing a detailed textual description of the diagram for blind and visually impaired readers, followed by the original legend\. The diagram and its explanation remain unchanged\.\)

## [Human Presence Verification in the Age of Artificial Intelligence](../publications/1a172e3cb98066f88e25.md)

Tennessee Lantuas

Human Presence Verification in the Age of Artificial Intelligence A Preliminary Scientific and Philosophical Exploration Dear Members of the International Scientific Community, This video presents a preliminary interdisciplinary reflection on one of the emerging challenges of digital communication: How can we reliably distinguish human participation from autonomous artificial intelligence in online interactions? As conversational AI systems become increasingly sophisticated, the distinction between a human\-authored message, an AI\-assisted communication, and a fully automated response becomes progressively less apparent\. Our research proposal explores the potential of a multimodal human\-presence verification framework combining several technological approaches: \- Real\-time visual presence verification\. \- Smartphone motion sensors, including accelerometers and gyroscopes\. \- Cryptographic device attestation\. \- Time\-sensitive verification challenges\. \- Privacy\-preserving certification mechanisms\. The central hypothesis is that combining independent verification signals could strengthen confidence in the physical presence of a human participant\. However, verifying human presence does not necessarily establish human authorship\. A verified individual may subsequently delegate communication to an autonomous AI agent\. This distinction represents a fundamental scientific and philosophical question\. The mathematical examples presented in this preliminary work are illustrative models rather than experimentally validated findings\. They are intended to support discussion and identify directions for future research\. Further investigation would require controlled experiments, statistical validation, cybersecurity assessments, accessibility evaluations, and rigorous privacy analysis\. Research Ethics and Transparency This project was initiated through human reflection and developed with the assistance of ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence system created by OpenAI\. The human contributor directed the conceptual exploration, identified the research questions, and remains responsible for reviewing and validating the publication\. AI assistance contributed to structuring the scientific discussion, formulating illustrative mathematical models, and developing the explanatory text\. This collaboration is disclosed intentionally because transparency regarding human and artificial contributions is itself central to the research question\. Conclusion The objective of this proposal is not to establish that machines cannot imitate humans, but to investigate how digital systems might provide meaningful, voluntary, and privacy\-respecting evidence of human presence\. As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly capable of communicating on our behalf, the challenge is not merely to identify who is speaking, but to understand who is present, who is responsible, and what constitutes authentic participation\. We invite researchers in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital identity, philosophy, and human–computer interaction to examine, challenge, and further develop these preliminary ideas\. Research status: Independent conceptual proposal — preliminary, non\-peer\-reviewed work\. Contributor: Tennessee Lantuas AI assistance: ChatGPT \(OpenAI\) Date: October 15, 2026

## [Relation\-aware dynamic knowledge subgraph enhanced large language models for medical multiple\-choice question answering](../publications/1a345c40102118957c0a.md)

Yu Ma; Tianning Di; Jiangpeng Xu; Yue Wu

Medical multiple\-choice question answering requires models to simultaneously understand question semantics, candidate\-answer differences, and structured relations among medical entities in complex clinical contexts\. To address the limitations that existing knowledge\-enhanced methods often adopt question\-level unified modeling and thus struggle to characterize local relational differences among different candidate options, while conventional low\-rank adaptation lacks relation\-pattern adaptivity, this paper proposes a knowledge\-enhanced large language model framework that combines option\-level knowledge subgraph representation fusion with relation\-aware dynamic LoRA adaptation\. The proposed method first constructs a local medical knowledge subgraph for the question stem and each candidate answer separately, and then injects structured knowledge into candidate representations through a graph encoder and gated fusion mechanism\. Subsequently, multiple learned LoRA expert branches are dynamically combined through candidate\-conditioned routing based on the relational information encoded in the enhanced candidate representations, enabling the model to obtain more suitable parameter update paths\. The experimental results are reported as the mean and standard deviation over three random\-seed runs\. On the MedQA dataset, the proposed method achieves Accuracy scores of 62\.90%±0\.82% and 62\.84%±1\.04%, together with F1\-Score values of 62\.97%±1\.07% and 62\.79%±0\.78%, using Llama3 8B and Qwen 7B, respectively\. On the MedMCQA dataset, the corresponding Accuracy scores are 61\.04%±0\.30% and 58\.59%±0\.65%, while the F1\-Score values reach 61\.21%±0\.54% and 57\.77%±0\.57%, respectively\. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve knowledge understanding, candidate discrimination, and reasoning stability in medical multiple\-choice question answering\.

## [Measuring the local shape of learning\-rate transfer curves](../publications/1a3b4e19fa42682fbec8.md)

Satoki Ishikawa; Rio Yokota; Ryo Karakida

Understanding the learning\-rate \(LR\) dependence of trained model performance is essential for better optimization of neural networks, but the appropriate size of the LR depends on learning dynamics, architecture, and their hidden biases, and thus our understanding of this complex dependence remains limited\. The behavior of the loss curve as a function of the LR has recently been observed in extensive experiments on LR transfer across different settings, such as model sizes, and it is becoming more important to explore methodologies for quantitatively characterizing the shape of this LR curve\. In this work, we provide two relational equations that give a good empirical explanation of the gradient of the LR transfer curve, i\.e\., the LR gradient\. One is a theoretical formula that holds at the edge of stability, and the other is an approximate expression obtained by naively treating this gradient as a hyper\-parameter gradient\. Using these two relational equations in a complementary manner, we show a lower bound on the gradient of the curve and a zero gradient under specific conditions for normalization layers in theory\. The approximate expression also applies to a wide range of experimental settings and allows us to decompose the LR gradient into layer\-wise components and quantify the strong contribution of specific layers to the curve shape\. Thus, this serves as a foundation for better understanding the internal mechanisms of LR dependence\.

## [DESIGN A SECURE CLOUD STORAGE FOR DATA PRIVACY USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE](../publications/1a42751e286f07d65c13.md)

VIKAS GAUND; VINAY KUMAR; Richa Pandey

Storing information with an outside cloud vendor gives users flexible, pay\-as\-needed capacity, yet it also puts privacy, confidentiality, integrity and access control at risk\.This paper describes the design of a cloud storage platform that pairs cryptographic protection with machine intelligence to keep user files safe\.The planned architecture is built from six tiers: the user interface, authentication and authorization, activity monitoring, AI\-based detection, encryption with storage, and a security response tier\.Every file is encrypted before it is saved and is decrypted only once the requester passes authorization\.A machine learning module studies how users behave, labels each session as normal or suspicious, and raises alerts or demands extra verification when something looks wrong\.The work follows an experimental design\-and\-development approach in which the AI model is trained and tested on its own prior to integration\.The intended result is a functioning prototype that shows encrypted storage together with AI\-driven threat detection\.

## [Peripheral blood CD34\+ peak during mobilisation as an additional parameter to assess PBSC inoculum adequacy autologous HSCT](../publications/1a45edd68d1ae35d42f5.md)

Giuseppe Milone; Giuseppe Milone; Emanuele Martorana; Maria Grazia Camuglia; Salvatore Leotta; Andrea Spadaro; Giulia Giuffrida; Gaetano Moschetti; Federica Galbo; Paola Scire; Giulio Antonio Milone; Giulio Antonio Milone; Giordana Brunetti; P\. Castorina

Background After autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation \(HSCT\), the infused CD34\+ cell dose is usually considered essential for assessing the adequacy of the peripheral blood progenitor cells \(PBSC\) inoculum\. Methods In a cohort of 302 patients who underwent autologous haematopoietic transplantation, we investigated whether the peak peripheral blood CD34\+ cell count during mobilisation could predict neutrophil engraftment\. Results In the overall cohort, the mean time to neutrophil engraftment was 12\.2 days, and the mean infused CD34\+ cell dose was 5\.1 × 10^6 CD34\+ cells/kg\. In univariate analysis, the CD34\+ cell dose \(p=0\.005\), the PB CD34\+ peak during mobilisation \(p=0\.0002\), the number of performed apheresis \(p=0\.03\), and the use of G\-CSF \(p=0\.001\) were significantly associated with time to neutrophil engraftment\. When factors were evaluated in multivariate analysis, the PB CD34\+ peak and use of G\-CSF remained significant\. In a ROC analysis, the PB CD34\+ peak predicted delayed engraftment with an AUC of 0\.695 \(95% CI, 0\.599\-0\.791\)\. Joint stratification by PB CD34\+ peak and infused CD34\+ dose identified subgroups at high risk of delayed engraftment\. Conclusion In patients treated by autologous HSCT and receiving an adequate dose of infused CD34\+ cells, the PB CD34\+ peak during mobilisation is independently associated with post\-transplant neutrophil engraftment\.

## [Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing](../publications/1a4b09a3439f77f4d5bf.md)

Irina A\. Kerle; Oleksandr Husak; Thomas Gross; Andreas Hartig; Rebecca Prause; Daniela Richter; Sascha Brückmann; Maximilian Werner; Anja Kögler; Dorothea Hanf; Lino Möhrmann; Doreen William; Karsten Wendt; Nicole Pfarr; Carolin Mogler; Daniela Ellen Aust; Evelin Schröck; Christoph Heining; Hanno Glimm

Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy\. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events\. To address this, we developed a machine learning \(ML\) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program\. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition\. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN\-deleted and wild\-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry\. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild\-type by TSO500; 75% \(15/20\) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression\. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods\.

## [Model Business Intelligence Berbasis Explainable AI dan Analisis Ketidakpastian untuk Rekomendasi Strategi Penjualan UMKM](../publications/1a4bf05b86de1fcf4fc1.md)

Karanita Karanita; Andi Rahma Nur Alam; Arwinda Arwinda

Penelitian ini mengembangkan model Business Intelligence yang mengintegrasikan Explainable AI dan analisis ketidakpastian untuk mendukung keputusan penjualan UMKM Coppo Awi\. ## [An academic chatbot with hybrid retrieval and local large language models](../publications/1a4c851b56234d9d9aba.md)

Jhon Paúl Guadalupe Andrade; Blanca Topón\-Visarrea; Christian Iza

Higher\-education institutions devote a substantial share of their staff time to answering queries whose answers are already set out in institutional regulations\. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an academic chatbot based on retrieval\-augmented generation that lets users query those documents in natural language and receive grounded answers in Spanish\. The system combines a structure\-aware ingestion pipeline, a hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic search and lexical search through reciprocal rank fusion, and a locally hosted large language model\. A distinguishing goal is data sovereignty: every component runs on institutional hardware, so no data is sent to external services\. Quality is evaluated with the RAGAS framework over five regulatory documents: the corpus\-wide set attains a global score of 0\.90, with faithfulness of 0\.97\. The acceptance criterion is not met, however, under its conjunctive reading: answer relevancy stays below its threshold across all sets, and p95 latency reaches 6\.47 seconds against a 5\-second target\. Quality further degrades on long, heavily cross\-referenced regulations\. A contrast questionnaire administered to nineteen users places the perception index at 3\.64 out of 5 and exposes a relevant discrepancy: only 57\.9% agree that the system does not produce fabricated information, against the faithfulness the automatic judge assigns it\.

## [Data\-Driven and Physics\-Informed Machine Learning for Geotechnical Engineering Practice: A Systematic Review, Mathematical Formulation, and Comparative Case Study Analysis](../publications/1a54c464535c47a4e400.md)

Godfrey Jaja; Horace Jaja

Geotechnical engineering practice has traditionally relied on empirical and semi\-analytical correlations that struggle to represent the non\-linear, spatially variable behaviour of soils and rocks\. This paper synthesizes evidence from 221 peer\-reviewed studies \(2020\-2026\) on the application of machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) to soil mechanics, rock mechanics, and earth structures, and formally derives the governing mathematical formulations of the principal algorithm families, including ensemble trees, artificial neural networks, and physics\-informed neural networks \(PINNs\)\. Secondary quantitative synthesis of the reviewed corpus shows ensemble methods such as extreme gradient boosting achieving coefficients of determination of 0\.90\-0\.96 for geomaterial property prediction, compared with 0\.65\-0\.75 for conventional correlations\. Three operational case studies from Singapore, Hong Kong, and China illustrate measurable safety and economic gains from field deployment\. The review concludes that physics\-informed, ensemble\-based ML constitutes a statistically and practically significant advance over classical empirical methods, while data scarcity, interpretability, and cross\-site transferability remain the principal barriers to unconditional adoption in regulated design practice\.

## [Enhancing Dropshipping Performance Through Hybrid Recommendation Engines](../publications/1a55d52d095181d178b0.md)

Mehmet Shala; Zana Shala Krasniqi; Edmond Hajrizi

Small dropshipping stores often present the same popular products to all customers rather than providing personalised recommendations\. Personalisation, however, represents one of the few aspects of the shopping experience that such stores can directly control\. This study presents a lightweight hybrid recommendation engine that combines content\-based filtering, item\-based collaborative filtering, and trend signals under the budget and infrastructure constraints of small businesses\. The system was evaluated using the public Amazon Beauty dataset, comprising 1\.35 million ratings from 883,753 users across 23,838 products, and compared with tuned ItemKNN, PureSVD, and Bayesian Personalized Ranking \(BPR\) baselines using a temporal train–test split and full\-catalogue ranking\. Introducing item\-based collaborative filtering increased NDCG@10 from 0\.0029 to 0\.0418, while the best\-performing hybrid configuration, with weights of 10% content, 70% collaborative, and 20% trend, achieved an NDCG@10 of 0\.0425 ± 0\.0013 and significantly outperformed the individual components\. Although statistically reliable, the resulting improvement was small in practical terms, corresponding to approximately one additional successful recommendation per 862 recommendation lists\. The relative advantage increased to 52% when only one\-quarter of the training data was available but reversed for users with longer interaction histories\. Content\-based recommendations derived from product attributes provided the weakest signal, challenging the assumption that attribute similarity is particularly effective for beauty products\. This finding was consistent across the metadata configurations evaluated, including the product\-type field, which was the only fully reliable product attribute available in the dataset\. The collaborative neighbourhood model achieved approximately twice the ranking performance of the latent\-factor baselines while requiring approximately one\-fiftieth of their training time\. On commodity hardware, the deployed system generated recommendations with a median latency of 34 ms and required approximately 25 s for an offline rebuild\. Six propositions with explicit boundary conditions are formulated to characterize the observed relationships between data sparsity, evidence distribution, and recommendation accuracy\. The central proposition is that accuracy under sparse conditions depends more strongly on the alignment between model parameters and the locations of available evidence than on model sophistication alone\. As the evaluation is limited to offline experiments, future work should assess whether these improvements translate into changes in customer engagement and conversion through live A/B testing\.

## [Что\-то происходит: Теория происходящего\. Финитарный актуализм происходящего, внутренне присущее математическому процессу происходящее, эволюционный космогенез и действительность сознательного переживания](../publications/1a58c6514d95dad9923b.md)

Chris Bartlett

В этой работе ставится вопрос о том, что могло бы означать, что реальность действительно происходит\. Любое полное сознательное переживание ставит два вопроса\. Как появилась его структура, включая информацию в мозге и теле? И благодаря чему эта структура действительна и переживается сейчас, а не просто где\-то описана как переживаемая? Теория происходящего, предложенная в этой работе, предлагает ответ на каждый из них, исходя из одного отправного положения: что\-то действительно происходит\. Финитарный актуализм происходящего, её ядро, принимает за аксиому, что по меньшей мере один базовый процесс просто происходит, без начала и конца\. Если всё существующее математично, база представляет собой математическую структуру \(конечное правило и его состояния\), а её происходящее есть выполнение этой структуры без конца, не требующее движущей силы и не встречающее сопротивления\. Если предположить, что ничто бесконечное никогда не существует как завершённое целое, существование базы не является отдельным фактом наряду с её происходящим; этот аспект ядра в работе называется внутренне присущим математическому процессу происходящим\. У базы есть «сейчас», но нет часов: процедурное изменение происходит без конца\. Связанный с этим, но независимый математический результат, структурированная нулевость, показывает, что нечто может в сумме составлять ровно ноль, не будучи пустым\. Высказывается предположение, что это может отчасти объяснить, почему вообще что\-либо существует\. Предлагается считать, что из этого происходящего процесса возникает более богатая структура\. Предлагается считать, что реальность представляет собой иерархию всё более сложных уровней, начинающуюся с простого базового слоя, причём носителем каждого уровня служит деятельность ниже него; наша Вселенная была бы одним миром среди многих на одном из этих более высоких уровней\. База, процесс которой происходит без конца, могла бы обеспечивать квазибесконечное изобилие и никогда не прекращающееся изменение: достаточно случайной изменчивости, чтобы отбор мог создавать структуры для копирования, памяти и восстановления\. То, что создаёт отбор, затем в конечном счёте стало бы создавать новые миры, вслепую или по замыслу, что в работе называется эволюционным космогенезом\. Наконец, предлагается считать, что то же происходящее делает вещи действительными, давая нам самое глубокое ощущение того, что действительно есть «сейчас»\. Конечные случаи происходящего, включая наши жизни, представляют собой организованные части этого происходящего базового процесса\. Структура определяет, каково переживание, но именно то, что оно составляет часть происходящего базы, делает его действительно переживаемым, и в этой работе это называется действительностью сознательного переживания\.

## [Methodology for the application of generative artificial intelligence tools in higher design education](../publications/1a621dcefed4ea0c3a74.md)

Naila Huseynova; Sevinj Hasanova; Aysel Abasova

The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\) technologies across both theoretical and practical domains is fundamentally transforming the epistemological and pedagogical foundations of higher design education\. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the methodological integration of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and DALL·E, in fostering creative thinking, critical analysis, and practical skills among design students in higher education institutions\. The research examines the transition of studio pedagogy from traditional forms toward hybrid and dialogical models, the reinterpretation of Donald Schön’s concept of reflection\-in\-action within algorithmic environments, and the evolving role of the educator in AI\-assisted learning processes\. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a modified Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) framework and a four\-component Information and Communication Competence \(ICC\) model\. The findings indicate that the systematic and purposeful implementation of GAI tools can increase students’ visual design production and productivity by approximately 14%; however, it may also lead to reduced diversity of ideas and an overreliance on algorithms for cognitive functions\. To mitigate these risks, the study proposes the concepts of epistemic vigilance and process\-oriented hybrid assessment mechanisms as essential components of contemporary design education\.

## [Case report: When encephalitis is not an infection: two cases of autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy mimicking infectious encephalitis](../publications/1a66fba22c681bbf2616.md)

Gabriela Trojan; Ngoc Hoang Anh Than; Abisha Senthilkumar; Faith Emmanuel; Anna M\. Moniuszko\-Malinowska; Piotr Czupryna

Background Autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein \(GFAP\) astrocytopathy is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disease of the central nervous system that frequently mimics infectious meningoencephalitis\. Because its clinical presentation, cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) findings, and inflammatory markers often resemble central nervous system infection, diagnosis may be delayed, postponing appropriate immunotherapy\. Case Presentation We describe two women with markedly different clinical presentations of GFAP astrocytopathy who were initially managed as suspected infectious meningoencephalitis\. Both patients presented with inflammatory CSF findings, negative extensive microbiological investigations, and initial empirical antimicrobial treatment\. In the first case, persistent aseptic meningitis with recurrent symptoms prompted autoimmune testing after repeated negative infectious work\-up\. In the second case, rapidly progressive encephalopathy requiring intensive care initially suggested severe infectious meningoencephalitis\. In both patients, neuronal surface and paraneoplastic antibody testing was negative, whereas indirect immunofluorescence detected GFAP\-IgG, supporting the diagnosis in the context of the clinical, CSF, neuroimaging, and microbiological findings\. Both patients subsequently received corticosteroid treatment and experienced clinical improvement, although residual neurological symptoms persisted in the first patient\. Conclusion These cases highlight the broad clinical spectrum of GFAP astrocytopathy and its potential to closely mimic infectious central nervous system disease\. Earlier recognition of GFAP astrocytopathy may facilitate timely consideration of immunotherapy and help reduce diagnostic delay and unnecessary antimicrobial exposure in patients with inflammatory meningoencephalitic presentations and negative infectious investigations\.

## [Disaster Management Skills Scale Development Study for Schools](../publications/1a6c09d63ec036f9fb0d.md)

Abdulvahap Doğan; Tuncay Yavuz Özdemir

This research aimed to psychometrically validate an instrument, based on teachers’ perspectives, to assess the disaster management skills of school administrators\. The study employed an exploratory sequential mixed\-methods design integrating qualitative and quantitative approaches\. During the qualitative phase, literature and documents on school\-based disaster management were analyzed through document analysis to generate an initial item pool\. These items were evaluated by experts for content validity and refined through a pilot study\. The quantitative phase involved independent samples of teachers from school settings in Elazığ\. Specifically, data from 301 teachers were used for the Exploratory Factor Analysis \(EFA\), while responses from another 300 were analyzed through Confirmatory Factor Analysis \(CFA\)\. The EFA results identified a four\-factor structure consisting of 28 items: Risk Reduction, Pre\-Disaster Preparedness, Disaster Response, and Post\-Disaster Recovery\. This structure was tested using the independent sample for construct validity\. The CFA findings indicated that the proposed model demonstrated high goodness\-of\-fit indices\. Ultimately, the findings suggest the Disaster Management Skills for Schools is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing school administrators’ competencies, providing a useful tool for educational research and professional practice\.

## [Disease Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks](../publications/1a719b9160418698b196.md)

B\.J\. Luckyn; OCHINDO CONFIDENCE T\.

In recent times, the medical world has been dealing with a very serious challenge detecting diseases early enough before they become life\-threatening\. Many patients, especially in developing countries like Nigeria, only come to know they have a chronic disease when it has already progressed to an advanced and harder\-to\-treat stage\. This is mostly because traditional methods of diagnosis rely heavily on doctors and laboratory technicians manually reviewing test results, a process that can be slow, expensive, and sometimes prone to human error, especially in environments with limited medical personnel or equipment\. This work investigates how Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\), which is a core technique in the field of machine learning and artificial intelligence, can be trained to automatically predict whether a patient has diabetes based on certain routine medical examination inputs\. The work makes use of the widely accepted Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset, which contains the medical records of female patients of Pima Indian heritage, including features such as glucose concentration, blood pressure, body mass index \(BMI\), age, insulin level, skin thickness, number of pregnancies, and a diabetes pedigree function score\. The ANN model was designed with three hidden layers, batch normalization, and dropout regularization to ensure it generalized well on unseen data\. After complete training and evaluation on the test portion of the dataset, the model achieved a Test Accuracy of 73\.38%, Precision of 59\.70%, Recall \(Sensitivity\) of 74\.07%, an F1\-Score of 66\.12%, and an AUC\-ROC score of 0\.798\. The relatively high Recall score is especially important in a medical context because it means the model successfully identified the majority of actual diabetic patients\. These results confirm that Artificial Neural Networks are a highly promising tool for disease prediction and early diagnosis in clinical settings\. The simulation was implemented entirely in Python using TensorFlow and Keras, and all results are verifiable from the charts included in this report\.

## [Artificial Intelligence for Magnetic Resonance Imaging\-Based Diagnosis of Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease](../publications/1a8b6b5e6b486b074770.md)

Walaa M\. Alsharif

Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder requiring timely diagnosis\. This structured narrative review examines artificial intelligence \(AI\) and deep\-learning applications \(DL\) for MRI\-based diagnosis of AD and mild cognitive impairment \(MCI\)\. PubMed and Web of Science were searched between April\-June 2026; Scopus and ScienceDirect supported supplementary discovery\. Studies were purposively selected using predefined eligibility criteria, with 42 primary studies summarized\. Convolutional neural networks, transformers, transfer learning, and multimodal approaches frequently reported promising classification performance\. However, findings varied across datasets, tasks, validation procedures, and populations, while high accuracies were often derived from curated datasets and internal validation\. Limited external and prospective validation, potential over fitting or data leakage, class imbalance, and insufficient demographic and scanner diversity restrict clinical generalizability\. Independent multicenter and real\-world assessments are required prior to routine clinical adoption\.

## [Genome\-wide association analysis identifies candidate loci associated with hydroxycinnamic acid accumulation in sweetpotato](../publications/1a9165b033ca72b4fdff.md)

Yiren Su; Lingxiao Zhao; Shizhuo Xiao; Xibin Dai; Zhilin Zhou; Qinghe Cao

Hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds are important phenolic bioactive constituents in sweetpotato storage roots and play important roles in quality formation and abiotic stress responses\. In this study, the contents of 33 hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds were determined in 229 sweetpotato germplasm accessions grown in three agroecological regions\. Genome\-wide association analysis \(GWAS\) was conducted to identify candidate genes, and the relationships of these genes with hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds accumulation and abiotic stress responses were further investigated\. The results showed that the 33 hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds exhibited extensive natural variation within the population\. Comprehensive evaluation identified several high\-accumulation accessions, including BZ13, BZ31, BZ19, BZ20, and BZ30\. GWAS identified 4,938 significant SNP–trait associations\. Stable signals for FA\-4\-O\-GlcA and isoFer\-C1\-GlcA were detected in the 19\.71–21\.09 Mb interval on Iba\_chr05a, whereas recurrent signals on Iba\_chr10a were concentrated in the 24\.88–25\.10 Mb and 25\.54–26\.14 Mb intervals\. Candidate gene analysis identified genes encoding caffeoylshikimate esterase \(CSE\), UDP\-glycosyltransferases \(UGTs\), ATP\-binding cassette transporters \(ABC transporters\), and several transcription factors\. Transcriptome analysis under stress conditions further showed that several candidate genes were differentially expressed under drought, heat, and cold stresses, indicating that they may also participate in abiotic stress responses in sweetpotato\. Overall, this study revealed the natural variation and genetic basis of hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds in sweetpotato and identified candidate loci and genes associated with both hydroxycinnamic acid\-related compounds accumulation and abiotic stress responses, providing candidate loci for subsequent molecular marker development and useful genetic resources for functional quality improvement and stress\-tolerant breeding in sweetpotato\.

## [From Chronology to Physiology: A Critical Translational Assessment of Artificial Intelligence for Precision Healthspan Measurement](../publications/1aa319f8da6834b71a8b.md)

Timur M\. Saliev; Prim B\. Singh

Healthspan, the period of life free from major chronic disease and disability, is a central geroscience outcome, yet its prediction remains difficult due to its multidimensional and heterogeneous nature\. In this review, we synthesize advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) for precision healthspan assessment, shifting from chronological age estimates toward physiologically grounded, individualized health trajectory forecasting\. We examine supervised, deep, self\-supervised, and reinforcement learning approaches, alongside AI\-based biomarkers of aging, including epigenetic, proteomic, imaging, and wearable\-derived digital biomarkers\. We also discuss multimodal AI integrating multi\-omic, imaging, and sensor data, explainable AI for clinical translation, and key issues in validation, regulation, ethics, bias, privacy, and equitable access\. We critically appraise the level of validation supporting each major technology, distinguish biological\-age estimation from true healthspan prediction, and separate predictive performance from demonstrated clinical utility\. In this review, we conclude that AI\-powered healthspan algorithms hold promise for shifting healthcare from reactive disease management to proactive, personalized aging management, but current evidence remains strongest for prediction and weakest for clinical utility; translation will require rigorous external and prospective validation, standardized outcomes, robust ethical and regulatory frameworks, and equitable implementation\.
