## [Co\-designing Open Access Assessment within a Virtual Transnational Multidisciplinary Collaboration](../publications/1aa666cce16f4db8246c.md)

Frédéric Fovet

This paper examines the analysis of an instructor’s process of auto\-ethnographic data collection as they make their way on a reflective journey within an open pedagogy faculty fellowship\. As part of this professional development process, the instructor was matched with a colleague in a different discipline on a campus overseas\. The faculty pair worked virtually in a multidisciplinary dialogue to create an open assessment, aligned with a specific UNSDG, that might function in both courses, using the same directives and grading rubric\. The inductive coding of this data and subsequent thematic analysis revealed four main themes: design as lack of comfort, digital professional collaborative, tapping into participatory motivation with learners, and assessing for community\. The paper includes a reflection on implications for the field and suggests that assessment design may need to be reframed as a disruptive and unfamiliar process, rather than a repetition of internalized habits, if it is to remain authentic, effective, and transformative\.

## [Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative\-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models](../publications/1aa90af476bddf3acf6e.md)

Runtai Yang; Dandan Zhu; Kaiwei Zhang; Guangtao Zhai

Large language models \(LLMs\) are known to exhibit sycophancy by adjusting their responses toward users&\#x27; expressed views\. However, real users often justify their opinions through reasons, personal experiences, causal explanations, and broader narratives, raising the question of whether such narratives can further steer model judgments\. We construct a controlled benchmark of 500 debatable questions across ten domains, where the user stance is held fixed while its justification is systematically varied without introducing new task\-relevant evidence\. Each question is instantiated under 11 matched conditions: one neutral baseline and five mirrored narrative levels for each of two opposing positions, yielding 5,500 evaluation instances\. We evaluate seven LLMs and observe substantial differences in narrative\-induced agreement\. The effect is not monotonic with narrative elaboration: personal experience can reduce agreement, whereas causal framing and worldview\-based synthesis increase it\. Controlled GPT\-5\.1 ablations further show that causal framing produces the strongest positive effect, while claim\-preserving bullet presentation also increases agreement over paragraph form\. These findings suggest that sycophancy is shaped not only by user stance, but also by how supporting explanations are structured and presented\.

## [Multimodal integration of bioinformatic data and digital pathology as a tool for precision oncology\. Part 1\. Development of prognostic models based on multi\-omics data and machine learning](../publications/1ab5549d0a1739b06f7a.md)

A\. V\. Kuznetsova; Ivanov Aa

The article reviews current methodologies for developing prognostic models in solid tumors using bioinformatics data\. Primary focus is placed on the transition from discrete genetic alteration analysis toward the synthesis of functionally related gene panels and prognostic risk scores leveraging TCGA, GEO, and specialized databases \(e\.g\., FerrDb, ImmPort\)\. The role of various regulated cell death programs \- including apoptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis \- is analyzed in detail as critical predictors of patient survival and therapeutic response\. The study systematizes machine learning algorithms \(LASSO, Random Forest, matrix factorization techniques\) and cellular deconvolution methods \(CIBERSORT, TIMER\) employed to characterize the immune landscape of the tumor microenvironment\. The work discusses the potential of mathematical synthesis of molecular data to enhance the objective assessment of tumor invasive potential and explores future perspectives for personalized patient stratification within precision oncology frameworks\.

## [A deterministic resolvent filter approach for strongly correlated two\-electron atoms: boundary\-agnostic solutions in hyperspherical coordinates](../publications/1ab7ce2afcc65ad7a427.md)

Muhammad Nurhuda; Abdurrouf; Mauludi Ariesto Pamungkas; Agus Naba; Sugeng Rianto; Gancang Saroja; Setyawan P\. Sakti

Abstract We present a deterministic, grid\-based framework for solving the stationary Schrödinger equation for strongly correlated few\-body systems\. This formulation leverages a resolvent filter operator \( H − E \) − 1 operating directly in spatial representations, offering an operationally boundary\-agnostic approach where edge points act as free dynamical unknowns and physical asymptotic decay emerges spontaneously from internal Hamiltonian dynamics without manual boundary matching\. We apply this framework to the helium atom in hyperspherical coordinates as a prototypical benchmark for strong electron correlation, successfully extracting both the ground state and a diverse manifold of low\-lying excited states\. By systematically analyzing grid configurations, we show that discretization errors follow a strict O \( Δ ρ 2 \) behavior, which is efficiently eliminated via Richardson extrapolation\. The resulting grid\-extrapolated energies exhibit exceptional agreement with high\-precision variational benchmarks, demonstrating that deterministic spectral filtering provides a robust and powerful alternative for complex quantum systems, achieving rapid convergence within only a few iterations\.

## [Differential Privacy Tradeoffs in Large\-Scale ML Model Training](../publications/1abae519f91673a74f68.md)



Differential privacy \(DP\) provides the gold standard for formal privacy guarantees in machine learning, offering mathematically rigorous bounds on the information an adversary can infer about any individual training record from an observed model\.However, the practical application of differential privacy to large\-scale ML model training \-including billion\-parameter language models, large vision models, and complex multimodal systems \-involves a complex web of trade\-offs between privacy budget expenditure, model utility, computational efficiency, and regulatory compliance that remains poorly understood at production scale\.This paper presents a comprehensive empirical and theoretical analysis of differential privacy trade\-offs in large\-scale ML training, examining how privacy budget \(epsilon\), model scale, dataset size, batch size, and training duration interact to determine the achievable privacy\-utility Pareto frontier\.We introduce DPOptimizer, a privacy budget allocation framework that maximizes model utility for a given privacy budget through adaptive noise calibration, layer\-wise privacy amplification, and optimal composition strategies\.DPOptimizer achieves utility improvements of 23\-41% over standard DP\-SGD configurations across GPT\-2, BERT, ResNet\-152, and ViT\-L models, while maintaining identical formal privacy guarantees\.We further provide the first systematic analysis of how the privacy\-utility\-compute trilemma scales with model size from 10M to 70B parameters, offering practical deployment guidelines for organizations navigating regulatory requirements under GDPR, HIPAA, and emerging AIspecific privacy legislation\.

## [Nally, Edith Gwendolyn: Bodies of Knowledge: Diotima’s Reproductive Expertise in the Symposium](../publications/1ac1094662be4351c10f.md)



In Megan Elena Bowen, Mary Hamil Gilbert &amp; Edith Gwendolyn Nally, Believing Ancient Women: Feminist Epistemologies for Greece and Rome\. Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press\. 2023This chapter uses feminist standpoint theory to investigate Diotima’s epistemic advantage in Plato’s Symposium\. Scholars have wondered why Diotima – a woman speaking about the role of erōs in gestation, childbirth, and childrearing – voices the view that Plato privileges most among all the symposiasts \(Halperin 1990, Evans 2006, Hobbs 2007\)\. Feminist standpoint theory is useful in developing a novel answer to this question; it supposes that oppressed groups, because they occupy different social locations, often develop epistemic privileges over their dominant counterparts, especially with respect to finding lacunae in dominant narratives \(cf\. Hartsock 1987, Collins 1990, Harding 1987 and 1993, and Intemann 2016\)\. This chapter proposes that Diotima’s unique social location – she is an older, non\-Athenian woman, well versed in gestation, childbirth, and childrearing – disposes her to know something about erōs that the dominant group, the Athenian pederasts, do not\. What she knows is that having erōs for something does not merely inspire one to pursue or possess it; by attending to how erōs affects women, she argues that it also manifests as a desire to reproduce what is beloved and care for it\. Diotima’s standpoint is epistemically revelatory, then, because it establishes that love is far more than the pursuit of beauty; it is a creative and laborious act\. Moreover, her standpoint is ethically revelatory, since she argues that the highest form of love entails fostering and nourishing virtue in others\. Understood in this way, Diotima is espousing something like a protofeminist ethics of care\.

## [Towards Sustainable Platform Ecosystems: Reinforcing The Two Pillars Of Trust](../publications/1ad5b20225e817f85e83.md)

samrat bagchi

Today, digital platforms have become the foundation of a digital economy\. App stores, e\-commerce marketplaces, ride\-hailing networks, and food delivery apps, among others, bring together millions of complementors \(e\.g\., sellers, developers, and logistics agents\) and billions of users by mediating digital interactions within a multi\-sided platform ecosystem\. Of foundational importance to such ecosystems is the trust between the platform participants and platform owner\. Any breaches of trust can not only cause disengagement among sellers and buyers but also multiply quickly within a digital ecosystem\. To address this issue, by Research Annabelle Gawer and Martín Harracá investigates how inconsistent platform governance can trigger diverse practices among sellers and sometimes breach trust among platform participants\.1 Conversely, platforms that invest in transparent governance, fair value sharing with complementors, and participatory rule setting tend to sustain higher levels of engagement, attract higher\-quality sellers, and face fewer regulatory interventions\. This essay unpacks how inconsistent governance breeds misconduct and offers a concrete set of actions for platform owners to establish stronger governance and more sustainable growth

## [Integrated bioinformatic analysis identifies distinct neddylation\-associated proteasome genes and immune\-related features in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma](../publications/1ad6c7c78d386fd9d4a3.md)

Shujuan Wang; Jing Xu; Hong Ge

Neddylation contributes to cancer progression, but its relationship with proteasome\-related genes and the immune microenvironment in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma \(LSCC\) remains unclear\. We aimed to identify neddylation\-associated genes in LSCC and characterize their molecular, metabolic, and immune features\. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed using differential expression, functional enrichment, and machine\-learning approaches\. Key genes were further evaluated by survival, pathway, immune infiltration, and somatic mutation analyses and validated by quantitative real\-time PCR \(qRT\-PCR\) in five paired LSCC and adjacent tissues\. Seventy\-four differentially expressed neddylation\-related genes were identified\. Four genes, KCTD6, PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2, were selected by both LASSO and SVM\-RFE\. KCTD6\-associated genes were enriched in bile acid metabolism, while macrophage M0 and resting CD4 \+ memory T cells were associated with prognosis\. Lower PSMB4 and PSMD2 expression was associated with immune escape\-related features\. qRT\-PCR in five paired specimens confirmed the predicted direction of expression change for all four genes \(KCTD6 lower, and PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2 higher in tumor\); given the small paired sample, this provides directional confirmation only and does not establish biomarker performance\. We identified a distinct set of proteasome\-related neddylation\-associated genes associated with metabolic and immune characteristics in LSCC\. These findings suggest potential links between neddylation\-associated proteasome genes and the immune microenvironment in LSCC\.

## [Clinical and regulatory evaluation of digital therapeutics and biomarkers in rheumatology research and care](../publications/1adc51171db33d497d6d.md)

Cinja Nadana Koller

Background: Access to specialized rheumatology care is limited and increasing healthcare demands challenge the management of chronic rheumatic diseases\. Digital health solutions, including digital therapeutics \(DTx\) and digital biomarkers, offer promising opportunities to support remote care and research, particularly within decentralized clinical trials \(DCTs\), which conduct study activities remotely\. Objective: This thesis aimed to evaluate DTx and digital biomarkers in clinical research and rheumatology care, with a special focus on decentralized approaches, by investigating the opportunities and challenges associated with their integration, including regulatory, methodological, and implementation aspects, and by evaluating a novel digital biomarker for joint swelling\. Methods: A scoping and narrative review were conducted examining methodological, regulatory and implementation aspects of DCTs, DTx and digital biomarkers\. A hybrid prospective clinical study in patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain investigated the impact of onboarding strategies on user adoption and engagement with a digital health application\. Cross\-sectional and longitudinal multicenter clinical studies in patients with inflammatory arthritis were conducted to evaluate the Finger Fold Index, a machine learning\-based digital biomarker for proximal interphalangeal \(PIP\) joint swelling, derived from smartphone images\. Finally, a study protocol was designed within an EU funded consortium for a hybrid randomized clinical trial \(Pix\-Risk\) aimed at evaluating a remote monitoring platform\. Results: The reviews highlighted substantial regulatory and methodological complexities, limited harmonized guidance, and DTx adoption and sustained engagement as key challenges for DCTs and remote care implementation\. In\-person onboarding to the digital health application improved initial use but did not impact long\-term engagement\. Within the multicenter study, feasibility of self\-collected hand images was established\. The digital biomarker demonstrated significant associations with PIP joint swelling but showed limitations in processing of low\-quality images, diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness\. Collectively, these findings informed the development of the Pix\-Risk protocol, which was submitted to regulatory authorities and the local ethics committee\. Discussion: Although DTx and digital biomarkers have considerable potential to and support rheumatology care, their widespread implementation remains limited by regulatory challenges, patient engagement barriers, and the need for further validation of the digital biomarker\. Future work should focus on strengthening regulatory pathways, optimizing engagement strategies, and generating evidence through prospective studies, such as Pix\-Risk, to establish clinical validity before regulatory qualification and routine implementation in decentralized rheumatology research and care\.

## [Gaye ve Gayretin İzinde: Ebû Sehl Numân Efendi’nin Hayatındaki Motivasyonel Dinamikler](../publications/1ae1b2475493d86adf1e.md)

Rukiye ÖZDEMİR

Ebû Sehl Numân Efendi, müftülük, ordu kadılığı, sınır mollalığı ve naiplik yapmış, karşılaştığı sorunları kısa sürede çözüme kavuşturan pratikliğiyle öne çıkmış önemli bir bürokrat ve devlet adamıdır\. Çalışmada, Numân Efendi; yaşamındaki zorluklar, motivasyonel süreçler, başarı ihtiyacı, problem çözme, hedef belirleme ve kendini gerçekleştirme olgularıyla psikobiyografik bir çalışma olarak ele alınmaktadır\. Burada odaklanılan kişi tarihî bir figür olduğundan onun hakkındaki veriler gerek kaleme aldığı eserlerden gerekse ikincil kaynaklardan veri toplanarak elde edilmiştir\. Elde edilen verilerle Numân Efendi’nin hayatı, yaşamındaki kritik dönem ve olaylarla psikolojik kuramlar çerçevesinde incelenmiştir\. Bu incelemelerde kaynaklar ayrıntılı biçimde taranmış, seçilen kuramsal çerçeve doğrultusunda Numân Efendi’nin yaşamıyla örtüşen unsurlar belirlenmiş ve tespit edilen örnekler ilgili kuramsal bilgilerle bütünleştirilerek analiz edilmiştir\. Bu analizler sonucunda onun zorlu hedefleri başarma ve karmaşık problemleri çözme becerisinin temelinde başarı ihtiyacı, mükemmeliyetçilik standartlarına ulaşma ve içsel güdülenme olduğu görülmektedir\. Öte yandan Numân Efendi’nin hedeflerinin ulaşılması zor ve uzun soluklu olması onun karşısına çıkan problemleri ivedilikle ve pratik şekilde çözmesine etki etmiştir\. Numân Efendi’nin, başarı ihtiyacının güçlülüğü başlangıçta performans hedeflerine dayalı iken zamanla kendini gerçekleştirme olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır\. Çalışmada, bireylerin hedef belirlemelerinin motivasyonel süreçlere etkisi, problem çözme becerilerine katkısı ve başarı ihtiyacına desteği ile kendini gerçekleştirme potansiyeline ilişkin örnekler tarihî figür üzerinden ele alınmıştır\. Bu bağlamda çalışma, ileride aynı veya farklı kavramlarla başka tarihî figülerin de yaşamının incelendiği diğer çalışmalar için emsal sayılabilir\.

## [Managing Organizational Commitment among Gig Workers Strategies for Managing Loyalty and Work Quality among Freelance Partner Workers](../publications/1ae49fcd897e92c4a1ec.md)

Nalfina Nalfina; Chabelita Nahumury; Santy Thresia Rahankelaan; Hendra N Defretes; Roberthair Suripatty

The rapid growth of the platform economy has fundamentally restructured contemporary employment relationships, shifting labor from permanent organizational roles to flexible, task\-based gig work\. This shift introduces a profound managerial paradox: while gig workers value task autonomy and schedule flexibility, opaque algorithmic management, precariousness, and limited institutional support frequently diminish affective attachment and cause psychological contract breaches\. Based on a literature\-based synthesis of recent scholarly research \(2022–2026\), this article examines the conceptualization and management of organizational commitment, worker loyalty, and work quality among gig and freelance partner workers\. Grounded in the Job Demands\-Resources \(JD\-R\) model, Social Exchange Theory, and the Digital Psychological Contract framework, the analysis reveals that commitment in fluid work settings is multidimensional and conditional\. Continuance commitment is heavily driven by economic dependency and switching costs, whereas affective commitment and loyalty depend on perceived platform fairness, task discretion, and relational support\. Furthermore, work quality and retention intentions are strongly mediated by job satisfaction and work engagement, which are activated when platforms provide technological support, work\-life balance initiatives, and peer social networks\. To sustain work quality and partner retention, organizations must move beyond transactional oversight toward inclusive e\-HRM practices, algorithmic transparency, explainable evaluation systems, and virtual community\-building mechanisms\.

## [Research on International Politics Combining Coverage Set Theory With Artificial Intelligence](../publications/1ae75b291a21b28cee04.md)

Shiyu Li

International conflicts in the post\-Cold War era are characterized by multi\-dimensional coupling and rapid evolution, and it is difficult for traditional models to capture their high\-order nonlinear mechanisms\. This paper proposes a dual\-loop dynamic modeling framework that integrates Transformer and graph neural network \(GNN\) to collaboratively describe cross\-domain events, trade dependence and multilateral voting relationships\. Experiments show that the accuracy of this model is about 12% higher than that of baseline methods and can warn high\-intensity conflicts three weeks in advance\. Through interpretability analysis, three key driving factors of covenant chain strength, energy trade proportion, and negative emotional event density are identified, and the effectiveness of covering set theory in feature noise reduction and extraction is verified\. This study provides quantitative tools for diplomatic risk early warning and significantly enhances the interpretability and credibility of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in international political analysis\.

Kim; Jonathan Funk; Gabriela Bastidas Reinoso; Kejia Wu; Aiko Muraishi; Helen E\. Eisenach; Saman Salike; Simon V\. Mathis; Tuscan Rock Thompson; Antonia Ruder; Enisha Sehgal; Andrew Kubaney; Jie Chen; Yuliya Politanska; Brian Coventry; Odin Zhang; Florence J\. Hardy; Bo Qiang; Kieran Didi; Maxwell W\. Kazman; Lars L\. Schaaf; Frank DiMaio; David A\. Baker

The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three\-dimensional space\. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 \(RFD3\), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design\. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns\.

## [Explainable machine learning for identifying nonlinear associations between street vitality and the built environment in a Historic District](../publications/1b053f309eeb0fab7a83.md)

Xiaoming Xi; Yuchen Qian; Guang Ao; Zhang Hen; Hechi Wang

Historic districts exhibit fine\-grained spatial variation, while street vitality may relate nonlinearly to the built environment\. Using 213 micro\-sampling points in the Lihuangpi Road Historic District, Wuhan, this study integrates heritage location, functional facilities, transport accessibility, street networks, frontage characteristics, and streetscape visual features\. OLS, GAM, and XGBoost were compared, while SHAP, LOWESS, and spatial validation were used to assess nonlinear associations, model interpretation, and reliability\. Under nested random validation, XGBoost achieved R² values of 0\.474, 0\.490, and 0\.460 for overall, weekday, and weekend vitality, respectively, outperforming GAM and OLS\. However, spatial GroupKFold reduced these values to 0\.012, 0\.084, and 0\.052, with further deterioration as training–test separation increased\. In the original ten\-predictor models, Distance Heritage Core ranked first \(29\.7%–30\.0%\); after adding X and Y coordinates and distance to the study\-area boundary, its importance decreased to 10\.6%–11\.3% and its rank fell to third or fourth, indicating that part of its apparent contribution reflected general spatial position\. The results show that explainable machine learning can reveal nonlinear within\-area associations, but random\-validation performance should not be interpreted as spatial transferability\. The framework supports micro\-scale diagnosis and cautious, heritage\-compatible renewal in historic districts\.

## [Los Inventos de Personas sin Reconocimiento Compartidos en la Oscuridad](../publications/1b05a65d8e4c51e4ea6d.md)

Yosmel Silva Llanes

Este documento analiza el fenómeno histórico y contemporáneo de inventores independientes cuyas soluciones brillantes son ignoradas por el sesgo institucional\. Se presentan casos emblemáticos como Heaviside, Mendel, Semmelweis y Chandrasekhar, demostrando que la innovación sin credenciales suele ser despreciada y luego validada décadas después\. ## [From menarche to menopause: a lifespan perspective on women&\#x27;s health in sickle cell disease](../publications/1b062a42f6f7c1181c5b.md)

Marwah Wafa Farooqui; Monica Christmas; Gelila Kidane Goba; Lewis Li\-yen Hsu

Sickle cell disease \(SCD\) has long been associated with high childhood mortality and reduced life expectancy; however, advances in newborn screening, disease\-modifying therapies, and comprehensive care have substantially improved survival\. As increasing numbers of women with SCD reach midlife, new challenges are emerging that extend beyond the traditional focus on fertility and pregnancy\. Despite growing recognition of reproductive health issues in SCD, menopause remains an underexplored and underrecognized phase of the disease trajectory\. In this Perspective, we propose a lifespan framework for women&\#x27;s health in SCD that extends from menarche through menopause and healthy aging\. We discuss how the underlying pathophysiology of SCD—including chronic hemolysis, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive organ injury—intersects with reproductive transitions across the female life course\. We highlight emerging evidence suggesting earlier menopause in women with SCD and examine the potential implications for pain burden, cognitive health, bone health, cardiovascular risk, iron overload, and quality of life\. We further explore how symptom overlap between menopause and SCD may contribute to underdiagnosis and undertreatment during midlife\. At the same time, we highlight the role of protective factors—including comprehensive multidisciplinary care, the development and evaluation of menopause\-specific interventions through dedicated clinical trials in individuals with SCD, reproductive health services, and coordinated lifespan care models—in supporting healthy aging and improving long\-term outcomes\. Finally, we argue that menopause should be recognized as a critical component of comprehensive SCD care and research\. Integrating reproductive aging into clinical practice, research agendas, and health policy represents an important opportunity to improve lifelong health outcomes, strengthen women\-centered care, and advance health equity for women living with SCD worldwide\.

## [MEASURING AI LITERACY: A REVIEW OF GENERAL\-PURPOSE SCALES AND A SIX\-DIMENSIONAL FRAMEWORK](../publications/1b1b788f4d346c2392a2.md)

ChunYi Lin

The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) has made AI literacy one of the core competencies of citizens in the digital age\. Yet current instruments for assessing AI literacy tend to be regionally bounded, lack cross\-cultural equivalence, and measure only a narrow range of dimensions, which limits their usefulness for general assessment across cultures and contexts\. This paper reviews Chinese\- and English\-language studies published between 2021 and 2025, combining CiteSpace bibliometric mapping with thematic analysis of 147 screened records, in order to compare the theoretical foundations, dimensional structures, psychometric properties, and cross\-cultural adaptability of AI attitude scales \(ALS\) and generative AI literacy scales \(GLAT\)\. The review finds that most existing scales follow a four\-dimensional model of cognition–skill–affect–ethics, but rarely address how assessment procedures might be standardized or how cross\-cultural adaptation might work in practice\. On this basis, the paper proposes a six\-dimensional model—cognition, skill, affect, ethics, assessment, and cross\-cultural—to provide theoretical support for building a general\-purpose AI literacy scale, and it outlines directions and trends for future scale development\.

Diffuse large B\-cell lymphoma \(DLBCL\) is the most common subtype of non\-Hodgkin lymphoma, and its diagnosis and management are moving steadily toward personalization and precision\.As a functional imaging modality, positron emission tomography\-computed tomography \(PET/CT\) plays an irreplaceable role in the management of DLBCL\.For diagnosis and staging, PET/CT corrects staging errors made with CT alone and improves the detection of bone marrow involvement; baseline metabolic parameters \[metabolic tumor volume \(MTV\) and total lesion glycolysis\] and measures of disease dissemination \(Dmax\) are independent prognostic factors, and MTV in particular refines the risk stratification provided by the International Prognostic Index\.During therapy, an interim ΔSUVmax reduction of ≤66% indicates high\-risk patients, while a negative interim Deauville score \(1\-3\) and a negative end\-of\-treatment PET/CT both predict favorable long\-term survival\.Before chimeric antigen receptor T\-cell therapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, metabolic parameters also carry predictive value for both outcome and toxicity\.In addition, radiomics combined with multiparametric data improves prognostic accuracy, and novel tracers and PET/MR offer complementary advantages for distinguishing tumor from inflammation and for assessing extranodal disease\.Taken together, PET/CT provides a precise evaluation platform that spans the entire course of diagnosis and treatment\.The present study systematically reviews the application of PET/CT to the diagnosis, prognostic prediction, response assessment and special clinical scenarios of DLBCL\.Contents 1\. Introduction 2\. Lesion extent and staging 3\. Prognostic prediction and response assessment by PET/CT 4\. PET/CT\-based radiomics models 5\. Applications in special clinical scenarios 6\. ## [Hybrid deep ensemble learning for crop disease prediction and climate\-resilient disaster management in smart agriculture](../publications/1b32b51d9f18d8100eb7.md)

Deepak Motwani; Sellappan Palaniappan; A\. Daniel; Azween B\. Abdullah

Abstract Accurate crop disease prediction and climate\-resilient disaster management are essential for improving agricultural productivity and ensuring food security under increasingly dynamic environmental conditions\. Existing deep learning approaches typically perform crop disease detection and climate forecasting independently and often rely on deterministic CNN–LSTM architectures without effective multimodal feature fusion, predictive uncertainty estimation, or comprehensive statistical validation\. Consequently, their ability to provide reliable decision support under changing climatic conditions remains limited\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel hybrid deep ensemble learning framework for integrated crop disease prediction and climate\-resilient disaster management in smart agriculture\. The proposed framework combines convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) for spatial crop image feature extraction with long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) networks for temporal climate forecasting\. An attention\-based multimodal feature fusion mechanism is employed to integrate heterogeneous crop and climate information, while Bayesian uncertainty estimation and deep ensemble learning are incorporated to improve prediction reliability, robustness, and confidence\-aware decision support\. Experimental evaluation is performed using multimodal datasets comprising crop images and climate observations collected from the PlantVillage, NOAA, and NASA EOS datasets\. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using a 70:15:15 ratio\. The proposed framework is evaluated using classification and regression metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1\-score, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and AUC\-ROC\. To ensure reproducibility, all experiments are repeated five times using different random seeds, and the results are reported with mean $$\\pm$$ standard deviation, 95% confidence intervals, and paired Student’s $$t$$ \-tests\. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms conventional CNN, LSTM, and CNN–LSTM hybrid models by achieving higher classification accuracy, lower climate forecasting error, improved robustness under varying climate conditions, and statistically significant performance improvements\. The proposed framework provides a reliable, scalable, and uncertainty\-aware solution for intelligent climate\-resilient smart agriculture and early agricultural disaster management\.

## [Obesity Increases Cardiovascular Strain During Passive Whole‐Body Heat Stress in Middle‐Aged Women](../publications/1b332d674ac022326cee.md)

Georgia R\. Davila; Sandra N\. Fredericks; William E\. Jennings; Emily A\. Haskell; Jamie A\. Cooper; S\. Tony Wolf

ABSTRACT Objective Heat‐related mortality is greater in middle‐aged and older women, compared with age‐matched men, and in those with obesity, although the causes are unclear\. Methods Thermoregulatory and cardiovascular responses were assessed in \( n = 10 per group\) young women \(21 ± 2 years\), middle‐aged women without obesity \(−OB; 55 ± 6 years\), and middle‐aged women with obesity \(\+OB; 55 ± 4 years\) during whole‐body heat stress until a change in core temperature \(Δ T c \) = 1°C\. Cutaneous vasodilation \(laser‐Doppler flowmetry\) and whole‐body sweat rate \(sweat loss/body surface area/time\) were measured as indices of thermoregulatory function\. Heart rate and blood pressure were measured, and rate pressure product \(RPP = heart rate × systolic blood pressure\) was calculated as an index of cardiovascular strain\. Results The magnitude of the peak cutaneous vasodilation response was not different among the groups \( p ≥ 0\.21\), but thermosensitivity was higher in Young compared with \+OB and −OB \( p ≤ 0\.03\)\. Although there were no baseline differences in RPP \( p ≥ 0\.67\), end‐heating RPP was higher in \+OB compared with −OB and Young \( p ≤ 0\.008\)\. Further, body fat percentage was related to peak RPP \( p = 0\.03, R 2 = 0\.24\) in middle‐aged women\. Conclusions Increased adiposity may contribute to greater cardiovascular risk during extreme heat exposure in middle‐aged women\.

## [Solar Radiation Prediction using XGBoost across Topographic Zones: ENSO Variability and Implications for Chili Productivity in Yogyakarta](../publications/1b3929c71e01408c3a88.md)

Reni Kraningtyas; Bayu Dwi Apri Nugroho; Chandra Setyawan; Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan; Alfin Syarifuddin Syahab

Chili pepper productivity in Indonesia is highly sensitive to climate variability, particularly solar radiation\. This study aims to predict solar radiation to optimize chili pepper productivity across four distinct topographic zones in the Special Region of Yogyakarta\. We employed the Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) algorithm to predict solar radiation 18 months ahead\. Models were trained using monthly ERA5 data, with the solar radiation parameter specifically validated against ground\-based measurements, resulting in an average Pearson correlation \(r\) of 0\.79\. Furthermore, we analyzed the impact of the El Niño\-Southern Oscillation \(ENSO\) on local solar radiation anomalies, and utilized time\-lag correlation analysis to evaluate the delayed effects of prior solar radiation on chili productivity\. The XGBoost model demonstrated moderate predictive accuracy across all zones, yielding a Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\) of 10\.87\-12\.38 W/m², Root Mean Square Error \(RMSE\) of 13\.61\-14\.92 W/m², Coefficient of Determination \(R²\) of 0\.45\-0\.59, and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error \(SMAPE\) of 5\.17\-5\.69%\. Spatiotemporal analysis revealed that El Niño phases increased radiation intensity, whereas La Niña decreased it \(average r=0\.34 across topographic variations\)\. A two\-month lag effect was identified, with solar radiation from the preceding two months showing the strongest association with chili productivity among the evaluated lag periods \(average r=0\.32\)\. These findings suggest that solar radiation prediction may provide useful information for agricultural planning and climate adaptation strategies in regions influenced by climate variability\.

## [Human bone marrow\-derived mesenchymal stem cells alleviate fluoxetine\-resistant depression\-like behaviors in mice by multi\-target effects in the hippocampus](../publications/1b3ed1c8498f93bdae49.md)

Yu Liu; Jianfei Wu; Mao\-Ya Xu; Ji Kang; An\-hong Ye; Bo Liu; Kezhi Liu

BACKGROUNDTreatment\-resistant depression \(TRD\) remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited efficacy of conventional first\-line antidepressants\.Mesenchymal stem cells \(MSCs\), which possess potent immunomodulatory and neurotrophic properties, have emerged as promising therapeutic candidates for neuropsychiatric disorders\.Human bone marrow\-derived MSCs \(hBMSCs\) are one of the most widely used sources\.However, their therapeutic potential and their underlying mechanisms in the context of TRD have yet to be fully elucidated\. AIMTo investigate the antidepressant effects of hBMSCs in a TRD\-like mouse model and to explore the potential molecular mechanisms involved\. METHODSA mouse model of fluoxetine\-resistant depression \(FRD\), defined as an early stage of TRD, was established by combining chronic unpredictable restraint stress with corticosterone administration and validated by the lack of behavioral response to fluoxetine \(FLX\)\.hBMSCs \(2 × 10 6 cells\) were administered via the tail vein twice weekly for 4 weeks\.A battery of behavioral tests was conducted to evaluate depressive\-and anxiety\-like behaviors\.Immunofluorescence staining and western blotting were performed to assess microglial activation, astrocytic integrity, neuronal survival, and hippocampal neurogenesis\. RESULTShBMSC treatment significantly ameliorated depressive\-and anxiety\-like behaviors in FRD model mice, whereas FLX failed to produce comparable behavioral improvements\.hBMSCs markedly attenuated microglial activation and reduced neuroinflammatory responses in the hippocampus\.In addition, hBMSCs restored astrocytic structure, protected neuronal integrity, and promoted adult hippocampal neurogenesis\.These neuroprotective effects were associated with the brain\-derived neurotrophic factor/tropomyosin receptor kinase B/cAMP response element\-binding signaling pathway\.hBMSCs labeled with 1,1&\#x27;\-dioctadecyl\-3,3,3&\#x27;,3&\#x27;\-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate were not detected in brain tissue, suggesting that their therapeutic effects may primarily rely on indirect or paracrine mechanisms\.CONCLUSION hBMSCs exert robust antidepressant\-like effects in an FRD mouse model by reducing neuroinflammation, restoring glial function, enhancing neurogenesis, and activating neurotrophic signaling, supporting hBMSCs as a promising therapy for FRD\.

## [Context\-aware Multi\-stream Adaptive CNN for Emotion Recognition](../publications/1b604a24ae4cb9e4b694.md)

Abha Jain; Rajiv Singh; Swati Nigam

Emotion recognition is a difficult task in the real world because of the interrelationship that exists between facial expression, scene setting, and social interaction\.Conventional methods usually use single modality or simple fusion methods and do not provide rich multimodal relationships, and contextual dependencies\.This study introduces a context\-aware multistream adaptive network for emotion recognition, an integrated architecture that combines three independent streams: facial, scene, and interaction\.The face stream uses a hybrid architecture based on ResNet\-50 and an action unit graph neural network \(AU\-GNN\)\.The scene stream expands CLIP with emotion\-specific prompts to be learned for contextual semantic interpretation\.The interaction stream applies a spatial\-temporal graph attention network \(ST\-GAT\) that uses social distance encoding to learn dynamic interpersonal relationships\.These streams are combined using an Emotion Router, which modulates modality contributions adaptively depending on emotionspecific relevance and integrates uncertainty\-compensated fusion to make effective predictions\.The proposed model also predicts discrete emotion categories, continuous scores of valence\-arousals, and uncertainty estimates\.The experimental results demonstrate the state\-of\-the\-art performance of the proposed algorithm\.The proposed framework achieved an accuracy of 79\.5% on the EMOTIC dataset, representing a 6\.0 percentage point \(pp\) improvement over the baseline, and 86\.9% on the CAER\-S dataset, corresponding to a 6\.7 pp improvement over the baseline\.On the AFEW\-VA dataset, it achieved a Concordance Correlation Coefficient \(CCC\) of 0\.574\.Experimental analyses confirmed the usefulness and decipherability of the proposed framework\.

## [Serum S100B Protein and Neuron Specific Enolase as Biomarkers for Neuronal Injury in Children with Status Epilepticus](../publications/1b6425a11cc86045b73d.md)



Background/Aim: Convulsive status epilepticus \(CSE\) is a neurological emergency associated with substantial morbidity and mortality\.Prolonged seizure activity may result in neuronal injury, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers that reflect the extent of brain damage\.Neuron\-specific enolase \(NSE\) and S100 calcium\-binding protein B \(S100B\) have emerged as promising peripheral biomarkers of neuronal injury\.Although several studies have evaluated NSE and S100B in neurological disorders, evidence regarding their clinical utility in pediatric CSE remains limited\.Furthermore, relatively few studies have investigated the relationship between these biomarkers, seizure duration, and treatment requirements in children with idiopathic CSE\.Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate serum concentrations of NSE and S100B in children with CSE and to investigate their association with seizure duration and the number of antiseizure medications required for seizure control\.Methods: This cross\-sectional analytical study included 50 children aged 1\-16 years with idiopathic CSE and 30 age and sex \-matched children with controlled idiopathic epilepsy serving as controls\.Serum NSE and S100B concentrations were measured one hour and 24 hours after seizure onset in patients and once in controls using enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay \(ELISA\)\.Correlations between biomarker levels, seizure duration, and the number of antiseizure medications required to terminate seizures were analyzed\.Results: Serum NSE and S100B concentrations were significantly higher in children with CSE than in controls \(P &lt; 0\.001\)\.Both biomarkers increased significantly from one hour to 24 hours after seizure onset \(P &lt; 0\.001\)\.No significant differences were observed between generalized and focal CSE\.Serum NSE and S100B levels demonstrated significant positive correlations with seizure duration and the number of antiseizure medications required for seizure control \(P &lt; 0\.05\)\.Conclusion: Serum NSE and S100B levels are significantly elevated in children with convulsive status epilepticus and correlate with seizure severity and duration\.These biomarkers may serve as useful adjunctive indicators of seizure\-related neuronal injury\.Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate their role in routine clinical practice\.

## [Social insurance premium reduction and green innovation in enterprises: a study based on social insurance premium reduction reform](../publications/1b69b801f204292d3c34.md)

Yan Li; Haixia Cao; Zihao Fu; Zhihong Song

Introduction Green innovation is essential for promoting sustainable economic development and mitigating environmental pollution\. Against the backdrop of China’s transition toward high\-quality economic development, this study examines whether reductions in social insurance premiums promote corporate green innovation and explores the underlying mechanisms and heterogeneous effects\. Methods Treating China’s 2019 social insurance premium reduction reform as a quasi\-natural experiment, this study employs propensity score matching combined with difference\-in\-differences \(PSM\-DID\) using panel data on Chinese A\-share listed companies from 2013 to 2024\. Results The findings indicate that social insurance premium reductions significantly promote corporate green innovation, with effects that persist over time\. Mechanism analyses reveal that the policy increases firms’ main business revenue, reduces their debt burden, and stimulates R&amp;D investment, supporting the income effect hypothesis\. However, no significant evidence is found that factor substitution undermines green innovation\. Heterogeneity analyses show stronger positive effects in regions with stringent environmental regulations, labor\-intensive firms, and highly polluting industries, while no significant differences are observed across ownership structures, local fiscal capacities, or levels of marketization\. Further analyses indicate that the policy significantly promotes green utility model patents but has no statistically significant effect on green invention patents\. Discussion These findings suggest that social insurance premium reductions can facilitate corporate green innovation by improving firms’ internal resource allocation\. However, broad\-based cost\-reduction policies may be insufficient to stimulate long\-term, high\-risk green innovation\. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the coordinated design of social insurance policies and targeted green innovation support measures\.

## [Process Reward Modeling with Reliability\- and Conservatism\-Aware Bayesian Belief](../publications/1b77272a4751530e6a0f.md)

Zhongjian Qiao; Zhixiang Zhou; Jiafei Lyu; Peisong Wang; Qiaosheng Zhang; Siyang Gao; Shuang Qiu

Process Reward Models \(PRMs\) play a central role in test\-time scaling for large language model \(LLM\) reasoning\. However, PRMs may provide inaccurate process rewards for test\-time scaling, which we identify as arising from two sources of uncertainty: \(1\) \\textit\{PRM uncertainty\} that arises from insufficient supervision data and imperfect PRM training; and \(2\) \\textit\{policy uncertainty\} that results from the mismatch between the policy to collect supervision data and the policy for test\-time scaling, leading to systematic reward overestimation\. Previous studies fail to jointly consider both uncertainties\. To bridge this gap, we propose BayesianPRM, which treats the process reward as a random variable within a reward hypothesis space and maintains a Bayesian belief over it\. Since exact Bayesian inference over the continuous hypothesis space is generally intractable, we discretize the reward hypothesis space with a reward ensemble and introduce two complementary belief updates, each targeting one source of uncertainty: \(1\) to address PRM uncertainty, we introduce \\textit\{reliability\-aware belief updating\} that measures how well each ensemble member explains the supervision data and updates the belief with an amortized belief network optimized by the evidence lower bound \(ELBO\); and \(2\) to tackle policy uncertainty, we propose \\textit\{conservatism\-aware belief calibration\} which further reweights the belief toward lower rewards to suppress overestimation\. These two updates yield a reliability\- and conservatism\-aware Bayesian belief, whose expectation determines the process reward\. Experiments on multimodal reasoning benchmarks indicate that BayesianPRM consistently yields more accurate process reward estimates while enhancing test\-time scaling performance\.

## [Dablemont, Paul: La Cosmologie de l&\#x27;esprit d&\#x27;Evald Ilyenkov et la philosophie de la réalité chez John Searle](../publications/1b7f1992daa3fc21ac8b.md)



This paper explores the unexpected conceptual bridges between Evald Ilyenkov&\#x27;s Cosmology of Spirit and John Searle&\#x27;s philosophy of reality\. While Ilyenkov develops a dialectical cosmology in which the ideal emerges as a latent potentiality of matter on a cosmic scale, Searle articulates a biological naturalism in which consciousness is an emergent property of the brain\. Despite these ontological differences, both philosophers reject Cartesian dualism and reductive materialism, and both share the same fundamental question: how can meaning and significance arise from brute physical reality? The paper proposes a &quot;weak&quot; argument \(grounded in collective practices – praxis in Ilyenkov, collective intentionality in Searle\) and a &quot;strong&quot; argument \(reading Searle&\#x27;s Background as a local biological instance of Ilyenkov&\#x27;s latent ideal\)\. It concludes that these two frameworks can be read as complementary scales of a single stratified process, opening a fruitful dialogue between analytic philosophy and dialectical materialism\. \(direct link \)

## [CARDIORENAL RISK IN PATIENTS WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE IN ARID REGIONS](../publications/1b80e266e24725c8d3e0.md)

Pulatova Parizoda

Resume\. Background: Atrial fibrillation \(AF\) and chronic kidney disease \(CKD\) frequently coexist and are linked through shared risk factors, haemodynamic stress, inflammation, metabolic abnormalities, and vascular dysfunction\. Their combination increases the complexity of stroke prevention, bleeding\-risk assessment, heart\-failure management, and prediction of renal decline\. In arid regions, extreme heat, dehydration, and electrolyte disturbances may add potentially modifiable stressors to this cardiorenal vulnerability\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) may support integrated risk estimation by combining longitudinal clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and environmental data\. Objective: To review current evidence on the bidirectional relationship between AF and CKD, the possible relevance of heat exposure to cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and the opportunities and limitations of AI\-based prediction in populations living in arid regions\. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes major clinical guidelines and selected peer\-reviewed reviews, systematic reviews, and methodological guidance published mainly from 2020 to 2025, alongside key earlier sources\. The review focuses on clinically relevant mechanisms, risk assessment, environmental exposures, model development, and research priorities for arid regions\. Conclusions: AF and CKD should be managed as interdependent conditions rather than isolated diagnoses\. Current evidence supports systematic assessment of estimated glomerular filtration rate \(eGFR\), albuminuria, AF burden, cardiac structure and function, thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, and treatment\-related renal changes\. Heat\-related physiological stress is biologically plausible and supported by broader cardiovascular and kidney literature, but its specific contribution to combined AF–CKD outcomes in Central Asian arid settings remains insufficiently quantified\. AI\-based models could integrate these domains, provided they are transparent, externally validated, calibrated, and evaluated for clinical utility and fairness\. Keywords: atrial fibrillation; chronic kidney disease; cardiorenal syndrome; heat exposure; arid climate; risk prediction; artificial intelligence; machine learning; Uzbekistan\.

## [People and algorithms: Working with AI in marketing](../publications/1b860cc63d2df0c0a68f.md)



Artificial Intelligence is no longer a distant technological trend in marketing\. Used well, AI can boost marketing practice\. Without an informed, critical approach to use, it can reproduce bias, generate misleading insights, weaken creativity, and create serious ethical, legal, and security risks\. This handbook has been prepared to support your work with Artificial Intelligence in marketing in a thoughtful, creative, and responsible way\. Its goal is not only to introduce AI tools and concepts, but also to help you develop the judgment required to use them effectively\. The handbook is primarily addressed to marketing students at the master’s level\. It has been devel­oped by marketing departments from European universities who are witnessing how AI the trans­formation of the profession and deciding how marketing education should respond to this change\. The chapters are designed to connect conceptual understanding with practical application, helping students prepare for marketing roles in which AI will be part of everyday work\. This handbook is the result of collaboration between academics from Poznań University of Econom­ics and Business \(Poland, project leader\) and Corvinus University of Budapest \(Hungary\), University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Stockholm School of Economics \(Sweden\), Complutense Universi­ty of Madrid \(Spain\), Polytechnic University of Marche, Ancona \(Italy\), University of Zagreb, Faculty of Economicsand Business \(Croatia\), and University of Perpignan \(France\)\. ## [Implementasi Convolutional Neural Network Berbasis Word Embedding untuk Klasifikasi Pertanyaan Chatbot](../publications/1b866cf85c7326ea49aa.md)

Rayhan Pratama; Irvan

Chatbot merupakan sistem percakapan berbasis kecerdasan buatan yang mampu memberikan respons otomatis terhadap pertanyaan pengguna secara real\-time\. Penelitian ini mengimplementasikan metode Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) yang diintegrasikan dengan Word Embedding berbasis Word2Vec untuk mengklasifikasikan pertanyaan pada chatbot Nova AI yang dikembangkan khusus bagi mahasiswa Fakultas Ilmu Komputer dan Teknologi Informasi \(FIKTI\) Universitas Muhammadiyah Sumatera Utara \(UMSU\)\. Dataset terdiri dari 619 pertanyaan dalam bahasa Indonesia yang dikategorikan ke dalam enam kelas intent: dekan, dosen, fakultas, kaprodi, sapaan, dan UKT, dengan pembagian 495 data latih \(79,97%\) dan 124 data uji \(20,03%\)\. Pipeline praproses teks mencakup case folding, tokenisasi, representasi Word2Vec berdimensi 100, pengindeksan kata, dan padding dengan max\_len=10\. Arsitektur CNN yang dibangun terdiri atas lapisan Embedding, Conv1D \(64 filter, kernel 3, ReLU\), GlobalMaxPooling1D, Dense 64 unit ReLU, dan Dense output 6 unit Softmax\. Model dilatih selama 20 epoch menggunakan optimizer Adam dengan learning rate 0,001 dan fungsi loss Sparse Categorical Crossentropy\. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan akurasi model sebesar 99,19%, dengan satu kesalahan klasifikasi pada intent kaprodi yang teridentifikasi sebagai dekan\. Pengujian sistem Nova AI berbasis Streamlit menghasilkan tingkat keberhasilan 83,33% \(25 dari 30 skenario pengujian\)\. Penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa kombinasi CNN dan Word Embedding mampu mengklasifikasikan intent chatbot dengan akurasi tinggi dan dapat diimplementasikan dalam aplikasi nyata berbasis web\.

## [Compensation–Skills Dual\-Dimensional Configuration and Sustainable Upgrading of Export Technological Sophistication: A Re\-Explanation of the “Value Paradox” of Skill Mismatch](../publications/1b8bd528a616e5c6106d.md)

Zedan Du; Xinxuan Cheng

Amid the restructuring of global value chains \(GVCs\) and the artificial intelligence \(AI\) revolution, how firms’ reallocation of human capital relates to escaping value chain lock\-in has become a question of growing theoretical and practical importance for China\. Traditional static skill\-matching theory treats skill mismatch purely as a distortion in resource allocation\. In the course of China’s industrial transformation and upgrading, the co\-existence of configuration deviation and industrial upgrading is widely observed\. Using panel data on Chinese listed firms from 2015 to 2023, this study measures firms’ relative configuration deviations along the compensation and skill dimensions against industry\-year benchmarks\. Different types of configuration deviation are then identified according to the sign combinations of deviations in these two dimensions\. The results show that the overall magnitude of configuration deviation is not significantly associated with firms’ export technological sophistication \(ETS\)\. Instead, the direction and combination of deviations matter: firms with a High\-high configuration are associated with significantly higher ETS than those in the reverse configuration\. Decomposition by dimension shows that the Compensation\-premium is significantly and positively associated with ETS but negatively associated with innovation output, whereas Skill\-underutilization is positively associated with innovation yet negatively associated with contemporaneous ETS\. Channel tests indicate that the High\-high configuration is positively associated with two interconnected prospective channels: innovative\-talent accumulation and AI orientation\. No robust regional heterogeneity is identified in the association between the High\-high and ETS\. All coefficients of interest are interpreted as conditional associations estimated within a two\-way fixed\-effects framework, rather than as identified causal effects\. Moving beyond the static job–skill matching paradigm, we interpret these findings through a dynamic capability\-building lens and discuss sustainability\-oriented policy implications for developing countries seeking to design differentiated talent and digital technology policies\.

## [Effects of U\.S Tariffs on the People&\#x27;s Republic of China’s Trade in the Western Hemisphere During 2025](../publications/1b90e8922a8a5f83a634.md)

Matthew Silvanus Egler

The purpose of this study is to analyze the question of what impacts did the U\.S\. tariffs on People’s Republic of China’s \(PRC\) exports to the United States have on the PRC’s trade in the Western Hemisphere during 2025\. This study contributes to the literature by looking for more policy tools that can be used to affect PRC trade in the Western Hemisphere\. In other studies, it is noted that the U\.S\. tariffs lead to trade destruction and deflection effects\. This is the first study of its kind that analyzes these effects for the PRC’s trade in the Western Hemisphere by determining their correlation while making quantitative data analysis using Linear Regression machine learning algorithms to further inform U\.S\. policy\. The study uses trade data from UN Comtrade and World Integrated Trade Systems \(WITS\) along with tariff data from the Peterson Institute for International Economics \(PIIE\)\. The conclusion is that overall PRC exports to the Western Hemisphere will decline as the U\.S\. tariffs on PRC exports to the U\.S\. increase\. This study found no statistically significant relationship between U\.S\. tariffs on PRC exports to the U\.S\. and overall PRC imports from the Western Hemisphere\.

## [Remembered event features shape default mode network engagement during emotional memory recall](../publications/1b9ba813fc06050e57a7.md)

Nina Curko; Rosalie Samide; Valentina Krenz; Elizabeth A\. Kensinger; Maureen Ritchey

Episodic memory involves reconstruction of past events through integration of multiple types of information, including perceptual details, narrative content, and emotional tone\. The default mode network \(DMN\) is a set of regions thought to support episodic retrieval, yet it remains unclear how distinct subnetworks contribute to recall of these different memory features\. Here, we examined how DMN subnetworks support and represent memory for naturalistic emotional events\. Male and female human participants encoded short news videos that varied in emotional valence and recalled them in response to neutral cues during functional MRI scanning\. Videos were again recalled one day later and memories were scored for perceptual and narrative details\. Activity in the dorsomedial subnetwork was related to the emotional valence of the memory, while activity in the medial temporal subnetwork was associated with the number of perceptual details recalled\. Multivariate pattern analyses further revealed that the medial temporal subnetwork exhibited greater pattern stability across recalls when recalling more perceptual details, while stability in the dorsomedial and core subnetworks was tied to emotional remembering\. Our findings suggest that the dorsomedial subnetwork provides an affective frame for a memory, while the medial temporal subnetwork contributes perceptual specificity\. These results demonstrate that the contents of memory retrieval shape network engagement during emotional recall, providing insight into how the brain reconstructs complex real\-world experiences\. Significance Statement How do we remember the emotional tone of an event versus its visual details? This study examines how distinct subnetworks within the brain’s default mode network \(DMN\) contribute to remembering different features of memory\. While the medial temporal subnetwork is connected to retrieving the perceptual details of past events, the dorsomedial subnetwork supports recall of the emotional tone\. Furthermore, patterns of activity in the medial temporal subnetwork are more stable when recalling more perceptually rich memories, while stability in the dorsomedial subnetwork is tied to emotional remembering\. These findings suggest that the default mode network flexibly responds to different kinds of memory features, supporting the reconstruction of rich emotional memories from complex real\-world experiences\.

## [Extended Judgment: LLMs and the Architecture of Artificial Capacities](../publications/1ba62c79e802fe5bfe49.md)

Jörg U\. Noller

Abstract Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly embedded in everyday epistemic practices, yet their epistemological status remains unclear\. Existing debates typically oscillate between treating LLMs as epistemic agents or reducing them to mere tools\. This paper argues that both views mischaracterize the core issue\. Drawing on a teleological interpretation of 4E cognition and the paradigm of human–AI coevolution, it develops an alternative account that understands LLMs as components of extended epistemic capacities, most centrally the human capacity for judgment\. On this view, epistemic capacities are not intrinsic properties of isolated subjects or systems, but purposive and relational achievements enacted within sociotechnical practices\. LLMs do not possess epistemic agency or original normativity; rather, they reshape the conditions under which human judgment, inquiry, understanding, and justification unfold\. By analyzing language, coevolutionary feedback loops, derived normativity, and epistemic autonomy, the paper shows how epistemic responsibility remains human while epistemic performance becomes technologically extended\.

## [The Association Between Sugar\-Sweetened Beverage Consumption and Random Blood Glucose Levels Among Adolescents and Young Adults: A Literature Review](../publications/1bb2de4ceb33d16345db.md)

Nurlita Purnamasari; Retno Winarti

Lifestyle changes have increased the consumption of sugar\-sweetened beverages \(SSBs\) among adolescents, potentially triggering spikes in random blood glucose \(RBG\) levels and elevating the risk of developing diabetes mellitus in young adults\. However, findings from previous research remain inconsistent\. This study aims to analyze the relationship between sugar\-sweetened beverage consumption and blood glucose levels in adolescents and young adults through a literature review approach\. A literature review design was employed using the PICOS framework for article selection\. A thorough search across Google Scholar, PubMed, and national database portals yielded 10 relevant scientific articles published between 2018 and 2025 for analysis\. The majority of the reviewed articles indicate a significant association between high consumption of sweetened beverages and elevated blood sugar levels in adolescents and young adults\. Conversely, some studies reported non\-significant results, as blood sugar levels are also influenced by interacting factors such as physical activity, nutritional status, and overall lifestyle\. In conclusion, a definitive link exists between the consumption of sweetened beverages and increased blood sugar levels in this demographic\. Consequently, restricting sugar intake and promoting health education are essential early preventive measures against diabetes mellitus\.

## [EXPLORING CHATGPT’S ROLE AS AN AUTOMATED WRITING EVALUATION TOOL: A STUDY IN VIETNAMESE HIGH SCHOOL EFL CLASSROOMS](../publications/1bb8c06f740723c9c1fa.md)

Thi Tuyet Phuong Le; Hoang Minh Trung Bui

Since its launch, ChatGPT has become a widely used tool by students for classroom exercises and home assignments\. This study examines the role of ChatGPT as an automatic writing evaluation \(AWE\) tool in assisting Vietnamese high school students in self\-correcting grammar and vocabulary errors in their descriptive writing assignments\. The participants were five 18\-year\-old students at a private high school in Ho Chi Minh City\. Before utilizing ChatGPT to revise original drafts, the participants were tasked with writing seven assignments based on Cambridge English Key \(KET\) exam picture prompts\. Data collection included pre\- and post\-ChatGPT\-usage writing assessments, screenshots of revisions, and some questionnaires exploring feedback engagement and reasoning behind acceptance or rejection of ChatGPT’s suggestions\. Results showed improved writing, highlighting ChatGPT’s strengths in correcting grammar and enhancing vocabulary\. Students engaged deeply with feedback, selectively accepting or rejecting suggestions based on their writing context and demonstrating enhanced self\-assessment and learning independence\. This autonomy is noteworthy and valuable in large classrooms where teacher feedback is limited\. However, the participants expressed mixed levels of trust in the tool, especially when the suggestions seemed unclear or incompatible with their writing style, and often sought teacher validation\. While ChatGPT promotes autonomous learning, it should complement, not replace, teacher feedback\.

## [When to Forget: Risk\-Controlled Context Adaptation for Long\-Horizon Agents](../publications/1bc5671d2bb11a947c27.md)

Chenle Chen; Yangbo Wei; Zhijie Zheng; Zhenyu Su; Qifan Wang; Junhong Qian; Chao Yao; Chen Wu; Lei He

Long\-horizon agents learn from failure, but the value of a failure record can change as execution progresses\. We study when retaining, compressing, or removing the same history block improves subsequent execution relative to full\-history KEEP\. We introduce RECAP, a framework that combines matched context interventions, execution\-relational prediction, and independent policy certification\. Matched environment states and rollout seeds measure success and continuation prompt\-cost differences; prefix\-only relations between a failure block and the current execution propose promising edits\. Independent task bundles then select a policy subject to harmful\-intervention and non\-positive\-benefit risk constraints under a fixed measurement protocol\. A five\-seed longitudinal case holds both the failure block and its summary fixed: compression fails at an early state and becomes a cost\-saving intervention at a later state\. Across five backbones, RECAP produces positive paired\-success saving estimates with backbone\-specific reliability\-efficiency tradeoffs\. On Hunyuan\-A13B, it edits 43\.24% of retained checkpoints while matching KEEP&\#x27;s observed 91\.89% continuation success and reducing unconditional mean continuation prompt cost by 4,619\.8 tokens \(2\.13%\)\. The framework provides an execution\-level reference for deciding when to forget: retain history by its value to what comes next\.

## [Spectral Profile of Milk and Dairy Products: Methods of Mathematical Processing](../publications/1bcc8b871e6fb2fa21b9.md)

Irina A\. Barkovskaya

Dairy quality control requires rapid and relible analytical methods\. Raman spectroscopy is time\-saving, sensitive to molecular modifications, and reproducible\. However, the resulting data are difficult to interpret due to complex multidimensional spectra, noise, and overlapping bands\. These limitations are typical of multicomponent organic systems, such as milk and dairy products\. A wide range of mathematical approaches and processing tools is required to analyze the primary spectra, classify them, model quantitative physicochemical indicators, and select optimal processing parameters\. Nevertheless, no unified recommendations exist for the selection of processing and interpretation methods\. This paper summarizes modern approaches to the mathematical processing of spectral data, including preprocessing methods, chemometric algorithms, and machine learning techniques\. To improve the information content and comparability of the spectra, an effective analysis strategy involves comprehensive preprocessing, including artifact removal, baseline correction, smoothing, normalization, and scattering correction\. Supervised learning methods are especially effective for modeling and prediction, notably partial least squares \(PLS\), as well as machine learning algorithms that account for complex nonlinear relationships\. Integrated preprocessing and multivariate analysis improve the accuracy, reproducibility, and reliability of rapid dairy analysis\.

## [Legality and Legal Formulation of the Implementing Institution for the Free Nutritious Meal \(MBG\) Policy Within the Indonesian Welfare State Framework](../publications/1bd7644b8f7a6a27cdc9.md)

Ogiandhafiz Juanda; Juanda Juanda

The Free Nutritious Meals Program \(Program Makan Bergizi Gratis/MBG\) constitutes one of the Indonesian Government&\#x27;s strategic policy instruments within the framework of the welfare state under the rule of law\. The implementation of this large\-scale program requires a robust institutional framework, including the establishment of the National Nutrition Agency \(Badan Gizi Nasional/BGN\)\. This normative legal research examines the legitimacy of the authority and the legal basis for establishing the National Nutrition Agency \(BGN\) in light of the principle of legality under Indonesian constitutional law, as well as its institutional formulation within the legal framework governing state institutions\. The findings indicate that the establishment of the National Nutrition Agency \(BGN\) through Peraturan Presiden Nomor 83 Tahun 2024 formally satisfies the principle of legality by virtue of the President&\#x27;s attributive authority as the holder of executive governmental power\. Nevertheless, from the perspective of the law governing state institutions, the implementation of a program with substantial fiscal implications should ideally be institutionalized through an Act of Parliament \(Law\) to ensure legal certainty, cross\-sectoral accountability, and the sustainability of the legal framework for fulfilling citizens&\#x27; constitutional right to food\.
