## [Where Does the Performance Go? Understanding and Recovering Performance Regressions in C\-to\-Rust Translation](../publications/1bee68ddbf9575f13079.md)

Zhiqiang Yuan; Chong Wang; Zhenhao Zhou; Junwei Liu; Xin Peng

Rust is increasingly adopted as a memory\-safe successor to C, and transpilers such as \\crust\{\} can migrate entire C projects while preserving their behavior\. Preserving behavior, however, does not guarantee preserving performance\. We study this gap on 20 real\-world C projects and their \\crust\{\} translations\. On the eight projects used for analysis, the translated Rust is more than 3\\% slower than the original C on 12 of 19 operations, by up to 62\.2\\%\. By comparing execution\-cost profiles, optimized LLVM IR, and compiler optimization remarks across each C\-\-Rust pair, we trace these slowdowns to nine recurring performance issues, spanning residual runtime work, missed compiler optimizations, and C\-style source patterns, and derive an optimization direction for each\. We then present \\ourtool\{\}, an LLM\-based approach that encodes these issues as reusable optimization rules to recover the performance of translated Rust\. \\ourtool\{\} profiles each project to locate hot functions and matches them against rule\-specific patterns\. The LLM then checks each rule&\#x27;s rewrite preconditions against the project context before rewriting, and a rewrite is kept only if it passes both functional and performance validation\. On 41 operations from twelve held\-out projects, \\ourtool\{\} preserves C outputs on all tested workloads and speeds up 40 operations over the \\crust\{\} translations, 18 of which end up faster than the original C\. It outperforms the general\-purpose coding agent \\codex\{\} on 31 of the 37 operations where both preserve C outputs, and outperforms its own variant without rule guidance on 34 of the 41 operations\.

## [Novel grazing strategies increase milkweed \(Asclepias spp\.\) availability and monarch \(Danaus plexippus\) abundance in rangelands](../publications/1bf1066596f0c34fdc0e.md)

Ellysa R\. Johnson; Emma C\. Donahey; Katherine C Kral\-O’Brien; Jason P\. Harmon; Kevin K K Sedivec; Torre J\. Hovick

Introduction Monarch butterfly \( Danaus plexippus \) populations are declining, emphasizing the need for conservation throughout their range\. An understudied and underutilized area for conservation includes rangelands managed with livestock grazing\. Although this region is on the edge of the eastern monarch population range, rangelands can provide billions of milkweed \( Asclepias spp\.\) stems, the host plant for monarch butterflies\. A better understanding of the dynamics between milkweed, monarchs, and grazing strategies are necessary, especially since previous research has shown how milkweed stem abundance changes based on grazing management\. Our objectives were to 1\) quantify the influence of three livestock grazing strategies on milkweed and flowering forbs and 2\) determine how adult and juvenile monarch abundance is influenced by milkweed and flowering forbs\. Methods Our study was conducted at the Central Grasslands Research Extension Center in North Dakota from 2021\-2022\. We examined three grazing strategies that varied in their spatial and temporal disturbance patterns \(modified twice\-over rest\-rotation \[MTORG\], patch\-burn grazing \[PBG\], and season\-long grazing \[SLG\]\)\. Results We found higher milkweed abundance in MTORG compared to PBG and SLG, and milkweed abundance was not impacted by drought during the study\. Floral resources were generally more abundant in MTORG, but we detected a significant interaction between year and grazing regime\. Floral resources declined dramatically in PBG in 2021 because of the drought but recovered quickly the following year and matched floral resource availability in the MTORG strategy in 2022\. Both adult and juvenile monarch abundance were positively correlated with milkweed abundance\. Discussion Despite adult monarchs needing both milkweed for reproduction and nectar resources for fueling adult flight, the best explanation for changes in adult monarch abundance was milkweed abundance\. Overall, we found rangelands can benefit monarchs, both during juvenile and adult life stages, by providing vital plant resources\. However, the magnitude of benefit will depend on the spatial and temporal influence of grazing disturbance on host plant availability\.

## [Integrating ventilation assessments with IoT monitoring to evaluate indoor air quality in elementary schools of San Luis Potosí, México](../publications/1bf3823805ebbeec3110.md)

Salvador Ruíz\-Correa; Rubén López‐Revilla; Lina R\. Riego‐Ruiz; Gladys Diaz; Khaled Boussetta; Nicolás Gómez‐Hernández; Abdulhalim Dandoush; Lamine Amour; Francisco J\. Marmolejo\-Cossío; Cresencio Hernández Rosales; Marco Cardenas‐Juarez; Janeth Gabriela Rivera\-Aguilar

Indoor air quality \(IAQ\) is often neglected in schools of the Global South\. Carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) and fine particulate matter \(PM 2\.5 \) serve as key indicators of ventilation and exposure risk\. This study employed a two\-pronged approach to evaluate IAQ in elementary schools of the San Luis Potosí Metropolitan Area, Mexico\. Ventilation rates were quantified in 106 spaces across 53 schools\. Continuous IAQ monitoring \(CO 2 , PM 2\.5 , temperature, relative humidity\) was conducted using low\-cost Air Sentinel monitors in a convenience sample of 11 schools during cold and hot seasons\. Machine learning models forecasted CO 2 concentrations one hour in advance, and the Wells\-Riley model estimated airborne infection probability \(AIP\)\. IAQ was classified as poor, acceptable, and excellent in 1\.3%, 31\.5%, and 67\.2% of classrooms, respectively\. During the cold season, 97\.7% of classrooms maintained CO 2 within 400–1000 ppm; in the hot season, 67\.7% fell within this range and 1\.2% exceeded 2000 ppm\. The strongest CO 2 forecasting performance occurred in the hot season, while PM 2\.5 forecasts failed in both seasons, AIP increased monotonically during the first two hours of class in both seasons\. We conclude that integrating ventilation assessments with continuous IoT monitoring provides a comprehensive approach to characterizing IAQ in resource\-constrained settings\.

## [Trust in Physicians Exceeds Trust in Social Media, Family, and Friends for Health Information Among Adult Social Media Users](../publications/1c1b853fa4ea5f736155.md)

Matthew Jervis; France Nguyen\-Grozavu; Aaron Jacobs

Social media has dramatically expanded access to health information beyond traditional clinical settings\.Patients increasingly turn to digital platforms for immediate health\-related information\.While this democratization of information has possible benefits, such as increased health literacy, it also raises concerns about misinformation and erosion of trust in healthcare professionals trained to address these questions\.The primary objective of this study is to quantify levels of trust in differing sources of health information among adult social media users in the US\.We additionally evaluate whether time spent on social media is associated with trust in physician\-delivered health information\.We hypothesize that physicians remain the most trusted source of health information among the three sources evaluated\.Additionally, we hypothesize that greater time spent on social media is associated with lower trust in physicians\.A cross\-sectional survey study was conducted among adults 18 years or older who reported social media use within the past seven days and had visited a physician in the US within the past one year\.Social media use was limited to the following platforms: Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Twitter/X, Reddit, LinkedIn, and Instagram\.Among the 65 participants, most were female, White, held a bachelor&\#x27;s degree, and were between 25 and 30 years of age\.Trust in health information differed significantly across information sources\.Participants reported the greatest trust in physicians, followed by family or friends, and the lowest trust in social media \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\.No significant differences were observed between users and non\-users of each social media platform with regards to trust in physician\-delivered health information\.Additionally, time spent on social media was not associated with trust in physician\-delivered health information\.Despite widespread social media use among participants, physicians remained the most trusted source of health information\.This underscores physicians&\#x27; enduring role as a trusted source in the digital age\.Future research can investigate the factors that sustain this trust and further influences on health\-related decisionmaking and behaviors\.

## [Efektivitas Modul Etika Digital Berbasis Fikih Terhadap Perilaku Bermedia Sosial Siswa Madrasah Ibtidaiyah: Studi Pilot Kuasi\-Eksperimental](../publications/1c1e5f69fe5afc43391b.md)

Jimi Harianto; Shela Imelda; Elsya Putri; Haniah Putri; Nadia Dwi Lestari; Fitria Nur Aini; Gus Maftuh Ihsan

Penelitian pilot kuasi\-eksperimental ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi efektivitas modul etika digital berbasis fikih terhadap perilaku siswa Madrasah Ibtidaiyah \(MI\) di media sosial\. Desain penelitian menggunakan one\-group pretest\-posttest design dengan partisipan sebanyak 60 siswa kelas 4A dan 4B di MIN 11 Labuhan Dalam, Bandar Lampung\. Intervensi dilaksanakan selama enam minggu melalui pertemuan mingguan yang mencakup pembelajaran fikih kontekstual, praktik membaca berulang \(Arab/Inggris\), penguatan ritual, serta kegiatan experiential learning untuk fikih Ibtidaiyah experiential Instrumen pengukuran perilaku berupa tes tertulis dan lembar observasi perilaku yang diisi oleh guru dan orang tua, yang diberikan pada tahap pretest dan posttest, serta didukung oleh analisis artefak siswa\. Hasil analisis kuantitatif menunjukkan peningkatan skor perilaku bermedia sosial secara signifikan \(M pre\-test = 58,2; M post\-test = 79,4; \*p\* &lt; 0,01; N\-gain = 0,51, kategori sedang\)\. Selain itu, data observasi dari guru dan orang tua mengonfirmasi adanya perubahan perilaku positif yang konsisten, seperti peningkatan kesantunan dalam berkomentar, pengurangan penyebaran konten yang tidak bermanfaat, serta peningkatan kesadaran akan dampak konten digital\. Analisis tematik terhadap artefak siswa, seperti tulisan refleksi dan hasil diskusi kelompok, juga memperkuat temuan bahwa modul dapat membantu menginternalisasi nilai\-nilai fikih dalam konteks interaksi digital sehari\-hari\. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa modul etika digital berbasis fikih efektif sebagai sarana intervensi awal di tingkat MI\. Penelitian lanjutan dengan skala yang lebih luas, kelompok kontrol, serta instrumen pengukuran yang lebih terstandar dan tervalidasi sangat direkomendasikan untuk menguji generalisasi dan validitas internalisasi nilai\-nilai tersebut\.

## [The Vanishing Ground: Link Rot, Source Spoofing, and the Epistemic Fragility of Web\-Grounded AI](../publications/1c23867328885d241e7e.md)

Jace \(Jeong Hyeon\) Kim

Abstract Web\-grounded artificial intelligence systems increasingly rely on online information to retrieve evidence, generate answers, and support knowledge\-intensive tasks\. Yet the web is neither a stable archive nor a uniformly trustworthy evidentiary environment\. Sources may disappear, change without notice, become inaccessible, or be deliberately manipulated\. These conditions create an epistemic vulnerability that extends beyond model\-level errors: even a capable system may produce unreliable conclusions when the evidence available to it is incomplete, altered, or inauthentic\. This paper develops a multidisciplinary narrative review of three interrelated vulnerabilities: link rot and content drift, selective information disappearance, and source spoofing or data manipulation\. Drawing on research in digital preservation, information science, cybersecurity, political communication, and social epistemology, it examines how changes in the availability and integrity of online evidence can affect web\-grounded AI systems\. Existing research documents substantial rates of digital decay and demonstrates the feasibility of certain attacks on web\-scale training datasets\. However, these findings do not establish the prevalence or coordinated deployment of comparable attacks against contemporary AI search and retrieval systems\. The paper distinguishes source unavailability from source falsity, and technical susceptibility from demonstrated exploitation\. It argues that epistemic reliability should be evaluated not only in terms of answer accuracy, but also through the availability, authenticity, temporal stability, and traceability of the evidence supporting an answer\. It proposes a research agenda centered on source provenance, temporal verification, archival preservation, retrieval integrity, and systematic testing of how source changes affect generated outputs\. The central claim is that the reliability of web\-grounded AI depends partly on the survival and integrity of its evidentiary environment, not solely on the capabilities of the model processing it\. Keywords: web\-grounded AI; link rot; content drift; source spoofing; data poisoning; retrieval\-augmented generation; epistemic reliability; digital preservation Disclaimer This paper presents a multidisciplinary narrative review and a conceptual framework for examining the epistemic vulnerabilities of web\-grounded artificial intelligence\. It does not claim that the prospective scenarios discussed have occurred at scale, that source disappearance necessarily indicates deliberate manipulation, or that any specific organization is responsible for coordinated interference\. Throughout the text, demonstrated technical vulnerabilities, reported cases, theoretical risks, and proposed safeguards are strictly distinguished\. Furthermore, the psychological literature is utilized to contextualize potential effects on memory and reasoning, rather than to establish a direct causal relationship between web instability and individual or collective memory distortion\. Accordingly, the claims concerning downstream effects on AI\-generated knowledge should be understood as foundational research questions that require further empirical validation\. Author’s Note This paper examines the evidentiary instability of the online environment on which web\-grounded artificial intelligence partly depends\. It brings together research on link rot, content drift, source impersonation, selective information removal, and data manipulation to examine how changes in accessible evidence may affect the reliability and later verifiability of AI\-generated claims\. The argument does not assume a coordinated campaign by any particular corporation, government, or other actor\. Source disappearance, content revision, ordinary technical failure, institutional decisions, and deliberate manipulation are distinct processes that may produce superficially similar outcomes\. None, by itself, establishes malicious intent or demonstrates that an AI\-generated error resulted from external interference\. Claims about intent, prevalence, and causation require evidence beyond the observation of a missing, altered, or inconsistent source\. Research on human memory provides a relevant but limited point of comparison\. Studies of misinformation and its continued influence show that inaccurate information can affect later recollection and reasoning under particular conditions \(Loftus, 1992; Walter &amp; Tukachinsky, 2020\)\. These findings do not establish that the disappearance of digital sources necessarily distorts memory, that inaccessible records cause people to accept false accounts, or that such effects occur uniformly\. The relationship between source instability, individual recollection, and the reconstruction of shared accounts remains an empirical question\. The paper’s narrower purpose is to make the evidentiary dependencies of web\-grounded AI more explicit\. A plausible or even currently accurate answer is not necessarily one whose supporting evidence can be independently recovered and checked later\. Evaluating reliability therefore requires attention not only to answer quality, but also to source availability, content integrity, provenance, and the possibility of reconstructing the evidentiary path\. The proposed safeguards and evaluation framework are research directions rather than established solutions\. The aim is to make claims about evidence loss testable without presuming either systematic manipulation or inevitable failure\.

## [Age\-associated radiomic phenotyping in mice using multi\-energy photon\-counting and preclinical CT: an exploratory study](../publications/1c3a2b0f15bc08b345ce.md)

Noah A\. Castioni; Carmen Wängler; Carolin Mogler; Björn Wängler; Caroline Cassia; Henning Rudolf; Matthias Frank Froelich; Stefan Oswald Schoenberg; Alexander Hertel

To investigate whether CT\-derived radiomic features capture imaging patterns associated with chronological age groups in mice and to assess the influence of imaging platform and photon\-counting CT reconstruction strategy on classification performance\. Female C57BL/6NRj mice from three chronological age groups \(28, 88, and 99 weeks; n = 11\) underwent clinical photon\-counting CT \(PCCT\) and preclinical Albira II CT\. Heart, liver, and spleen were segmented and radiomic features were extracted\. The individual mouse was defined as the independent biological unit\. Model development and evaluation used nested leave\-one\-mouse\-out cross\-validation with all preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and, where applicable, reconstruction\-energy selection restricted to the respective training folds\. Organ\-level class probabilities were averaged to generate one mouse\-level prediction\. Monoenergetic PCCT reconstructions from 40 to 180 keV were evaluated, including a fully nested energy\-and\-pipeline selection analysis\. A grouped mouse\-level permutation analysis with 200 permutations was performed for the primary monoenergetic workflow\. Albira II correctly classified 5/11 mice \(45\.5%; 95% CI, 21\.3\-72\.0%\), whereas PCCT\-SPP correctly classified 10/11 mice \(90\.9%; 95% CI, 62\.3\-98\.4%\)\. The fully nested monoenergetic PCCT workflow correctly classified 9/11 mice \(81\.8%; 95% CI, 52\.3\-94\.9%; balanced accuracy, 83\.3%; macro\-F1, 83\.3%\)\. Energy\-specific performance varied considerably: 110 keV showed the highest accuracy \(81\.8%\) and was selected in 7/11 outer folds, whereas the highest macro one\-vs\-rest AUC occurred at 130 keV \(0\.867\)\. None of the 200 permuted analyses reached the observed fully nested monoenergetic accuracy \(plus\-one corrected Monte\-Carlo p = 0\.005\)\. CT\-derived radiomic features showed chronological age\-group\-associated patterns in this exploratory murine cohort, with classification performance varying substantially across imaging platforms and reconstruction strategies\. PCCT\-SPP showed the numerically highest performance, while monoenergetic PCCT demonstrated pronounced energy dependence without evidence for a universally optimal reconstruction energy\. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts and correlation with independent biological\-aging reference measures\.

## [Rautenberg, Niclas: Artificial intelligence, calculative reason, and technical domination: lessons from Husserl, Heidegger, and Marcuse](../publications/1c62047520e52af81063.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 41 \(9\)\. 2026The run on artificial intelligence \(AI\) is also a race for rendering world and mind calculable\. As has recently been observed, the ultimate goal of Silicon Valley and its copycats is ‘to capture the planet in a computationally legible form’ \(Crawford 2021\)\. This endeavor and thus contemporary forms of AI, as revolutionary as they may seem, are not entirely new; in fact, machine learning algorithms and generative AI are only the newest expression of a drive towards mathematization and control whose origins reach back to antiquity\. This paper redirects and re\-actualizes the phenomenological analyses of Edmund Husserl and Martin Heidegger to bring into relief the genealogical origins and the attitudinal patterns underlying contemporary AI and the calculative thinking that it embodies\. With Husserl, we see that the technology is a tool to mathematize the world\. Moreover, Heidegger shows how contemporary AI becomes both expression and tool for a \(self\-\)alienating thirst for domination that reduces human beings themselves to mere ‘stock’, ready to be controlled, computed, and exploited\. Yet, drawing on these two authors does not suffice to fathom AI’s sociotechnical embeddedness\. Instead, following Herbert Marcuse, it is necessary to reveal calculative reason’s relation to capitalist modes of production\. These insight into AI’s socio\-historical conditions of possibility is crucial\. Technology is never purely scientific nor technical; it is an inherently political matter\. As such, it also requires a political response—even from academics\. \(direct link \)

## [Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models](../publications/1c63d80646b45e355e7b.md)

Chenyi Shi; Xihua Wang; Y\. Jun Xu; Xingyu Zhu; Shunqing Jia; Zejun Liu; Boyang Mao; Yan Dai; Yanxin Rong; Qinya Lv; Xuming Ji; Chengming Luo

Leveraging its capability for large\-scale, repeated monitoring, remote sensing has increasingly supported nitrogen and phosphorus estimation in surface waters\. However, the evolution of this field from proxy\-based nutrient retrieval to integration with process\-based models remains insufficiently synthesized\. Here we review remote sensing approaches for estimating aquatic nutrients, with emphasis on their roles in supporting process\-based modeling, and compare their methodologies, applications, and limitations\. At the watershed scale, remote sensing supports land use mapping and pollution load estimation, identifying nutrient sources and constraining transport simulations\. At the lake scale, it provides continuous observations and water quality products that inform hydrodynamic and water quality models\. At the field and interface scales, remote sensing helps identify hotspots of nutrient loss by capturing the heterogeneity of management practices\. Despite these advances, nutrient estimation remains constrained by proxy relationships and spatial scale\. Future research should integrate remote sensing with hydrodynamic and biogeochemical models to constrain nutrient fluxes and improve mechanistic understanding of aquatic nutrient cycling\. At the watershed scale, remote sensing maps land use and estimates pollution loads; at the lake scale, it provides water quality data for models; at field and interface scales, it identifies nutrient\-loss hotspots, based on a review of remote sensing to approaches aquatic nutrients\.

## [DHEE AND DHRITI: CLASSICAL WISDOM TO COGNITIVE SCIENCE](../publications/1c7261ed521dd15c8cb2.md)

Arunkumar B Arali; Dr\. Sinchana D\. Nanda; Pratibha V Kulkarni

Background: Cognition enables understanding, retention, decision\-making and behavioural regulation\. Ayurveda describes these functions through Prajna, expressed by three interdependent faculties: Dhee, Dhriti and Smriti\. Their integrated role provides a basis for understanding cognition within Ayurveda and exploring its relevance to contemporary cognitive science\. Objective: To examine the roles of Dhee and Dhriti in cognition and explore their relevance to contemporary cognitive science\. Materials and Methods: Classical Ayurvedic texts, including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, along with their authoritative commentaries, were reviewed\. Relevant contemporary literature on cognition, executive function, and self\-regulation was also examined\. A qualitative conceptual review was undertaken by analysing the Ayurvedic concepts of Jnanotpatti, Triguna, Tridosha, Vibhramsha, and Prajnaparadha and correlating them with contemporary understanding of cognitive functions\. Results and Conclusion: Dhee represents active examination and discrimination, while Dhriti represents sustaining and regulatory capacity supporting appropriate action\. Their disturbance may contribute to Prajnaparadha and Sarvadosha Prakopa\. Functionally, Dhee relates to attention, reasoning and decision\-making, while Dhriti relates to inhibitory control, persistence and self\-regulation\. These are functional parallels rather than direct anatomical or neurobiological equivalences\. Ayurveda therefore presents cognition as an integrated process linking mental function, behaviour and health\.

## [Extra hidden states under emission misspecification in hidden Markov models](../publications/1c7676cac3a816d831bb.md)

Aurélien Nicosia

Abstract Additional states in a hidden Markov model \(HMM\) can compensate for restrictive emission distributions without representing additional scientific regimes\. We study this distinction using the established representation of mixture components as refined states\. Under compactness, mixture identifiability and positive aggregate transitions, we prove that a simple‐emission HMM with too few components has an observed‐law Kullback–Leibler loss that grows at least linearly with sequence length\. An exact refinement, or an aggregate HMM with mixture emissions, removes this approximation gap\. Simulations illustrate the resulting incentive to add states\. An analysis of tumor allele fractions on chromosome 1 then compares five Gaussian states with three regional profiles containing five Gaussian components\. The fitted emissions and regional assignments are nearly the same after grouping the Gaussian states, while the mixture model uses 14 fewer parameters\. This example illustrates how additional states can describe variation within a regional profile rather than additional regional regimes\. The number of fitted states alone therefore does not determine the number of scientifically distinct regimes\.

## [Institutional support, relationships, and multicultural participation: response surfaces of university belonging and sociocultural engagement](../publications/1c7ce1f7093bf0b74403.md)

Siyuan Luo; Hui Qu

Introduction Universities are cultural settings in which institutional arrangements and interpersonal recognition jointly condition participation and belonging\. Methods This open\-data secondary analysis examined how perceived supportive campus environment and relationship quality combined in relation to university belonging and sociocultural engagement among health\-professions students at a culturally diverse university in the United Arab Emirates\. The released dataset contained 683 records; 661 complete cases entered both polynomial models\. Predictors were transformed to proportion\-of\-maximum\-possible scores\. Inference combined 2,000 bootstrap resamples, HC3 heteroskedasticity\-robust standard errors, duplicate\-record checks, and Cook&\#x27;s D influence sensitivity\. Results The models explained 47\.3% of belonging and 25\.6% of sociocultural engagement\. The joint\-resource slope was positive for belonging \[a1 = 3\.159, 95% bootstrap CI \(2\.596, 3\.602\)\] and sociocultural engagement \[a1 = 1\.721, CI \(1\.233, 2\.133\)\]\. Curvature, directional difference, and mismatch curvature were not consistently supported\. Removing two exact duplicate records or 41 observations above Cook&\#x27;s D &gt;4/ n retained the positive joint\-resource pattern\. Discussion Thus, stronger institutional support and relationships were jointly associated with both campus belonging and multicultural participation, without evidence for a unique matching effect\. The cross\-sectional measures do not directly observe identity co\-construction, so the contribution is a bounded quantitative account of conditions associated with culturally situated participation and belonging\.

This single\-center retrospective observational study included 28 patients with surgical conditions and confirmed COVID\-19\. The small sample size limited the statistical power to detect a significant reduction in mortality among patients treated with higher\-dose colchicine; nevertheless, a trend toward lower mortality was observed\. Colchicine treatment was associated with a statistically significant reduction in serum ferritin levels, accompanied by trends toward lower CRP and D\-dimer levels\. ## [The glymphatic connectome: a hypothesis for how metabolic waste accumulation may contribute to preferential network degeneration](../publications/1c8d716fc24fd3136b53.md)

Khaled A\. Abdel\-Sater

Background Neurodegenerative diseases exhibit selective vulnerability, with preferential involvement of highly connected brain regions\. This review explores how glymphatic dysfunction and impaired extracellular waste removal may contribute to network\-specific degeneration\.Methods Narrative review of 2000–2026 literature \(PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar\), integrating connectome neuroscience, network analysis, glymphatic physiology, neurovascular biology, and proteinopathy research\.Results Hub regions show greater amyloid\-β and tau accumulation, suggesting metabolic demand, vascular regulation, and clearance efficiency shape regional vulnerability\. Glymphatic transport patterns resemble pathological deposition patterns, supporting a role for impaired clearance in disease progression\. Connectome features—centrality, modularity, resilience—may index cumulative molecular, cellular, and vascular dysfunction\.Conclusion The Brain Waste Fingerprint hypothesis proposes neurodegeneration arises from interactions among impaired clearance, vascular dysfunction, protein accumulation, and connectome reorganization\. ## [Case Report: Pallister\-Hall syndrome associated with a previously unreported de novo GLI3 frameshift variant and diagnostic insights from the Middle East](../publications/1c95d09fdbafc099061c.md)

Gessila Khalil; Ihab K\. Hemieid; Elie G\. Malki

Pallister–Hall syndrome \(PHS\) is a rare GLI3 \-related disorder characterized by hypothalamic hamartoma and mesoaxial polydactyly\. We report an infant from the West Bank, Palestine, with these cardinal findings, imperforate anus, rhizomelic limb shortening, right renal agenesis, choanal atresia, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect\. Whole\-exome sequencing identified a previously unreported heterozygous GLI3 frameshift variant, NM\_000168\.6:c\.2410del \(p\.Val804SerfsTer5\), absent in both parents and therefore presumed de novo \. The variant lies in the middle\-third PHS\-associated region and was provisionally classified as likely pathogenic\. At the last documented assessment on day 89 of life, no seizures or biochemical evidence of pituitary dysfunction had been identified\. Comparison with regional and molecularly relevant reports showed that neurological and endocrine severity varied among patients with truncating variants in this region\. This case documents a previously unreported likely pathogenic GLI3 variant in an established PHS phenotype and supports age\-appropriate neurological and endocrine surveillance\.

## [Decomposing multi\-scale dynamic regulation from single\-cell multiomics with scMagnify](../publications/1c95d19d170929b3d917.md)

Xufeng Chen; Xi Yan; Bihan Shen; Heqi Wang; Z Tang; Yan Zang; Ping Lin; Haibing Zhang; Yu Li; Hong Li

Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology\. However, capturing the multi\-scale time\-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging\. Here we present scMagnify, a deep\-learning\-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi\-scale gene regulatory networks \(GRNs\)\. Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify’s favorable performance\. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time\-lags\. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage\-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions\. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify’s intercellular communication module mapped key signaling\-to\-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes\. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi\-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease\. Chen and colleagues present scMagnify, a framework that uses single\-cell multi\-omic data to reconstruct and decompose time\-lagged gene regulatory networks\. The study analyses regulatory programs associated with development and disease\.

## [Concept before capability \- a validity\-led approach to AI in OSCEs](../publications/1c97eb41512bd4fe378c.md)

Jack Amiry; James Benjamin Galloway; S\. Helen Oram

Objective Structured Clinical Examinations \(OSCEs\) remain central to the assessment of clinical competence, yet the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) into assessment design, delivery, and scoring raises a fundamental question: what evidence of competence are OSCEs intended to generate? This paper argues that AI should be evaluated through the lens of OSCE validity, with particular attention to how it may strengthen or weaken the interpretive chain linking observed performance to assessment decisions\. Drawing on Messick&\#x27;s unitary conception of validity and Kane&\#x27;s argument\-based framework, we examine how AI may introduce distinct threats across the scoring, generalisation, extrapolation, and implication inferences that underpin OSCE interpretation\. We argue that generative AI \(genAI\) creates a particular risk of construct drift, whereby plausible assessment materials or scoring processes gradually reward observable proxies rather than the underlying clinical capabilities they are intended to assess\. To translate this validity perspective into practice, we propose a framework that maps AI applications across the OSCE workflow according to their proximity to candidate consequences and the evidential burden required to justify their use\. Lower\-risk applications, such as design support and post\-hoc analytics, may strengthen assessment when accompanied by construct\-focused review and human oversight, whereas higher\-risk uses, including AI\-mediated candidate encounters and automated summative scoring, require substantially stronger validity evidence\. We conclude that AI should be adopted according to the principle of concept before capability: assessment communities must first establish what clinical competence means and what evidence should count before deciding where AI has a legitimate role in high\-stakes assessment\.

## [Agronomic performance of canola and carinata under nitrogen sources in northwestern Rio Grande do Sul](../publications/1c99ecf235a90c766bca.md)

Júlia Sarturi Jung; Ivan Ricardo Carvalho; Antônio Carlos Pappis; Cristhian Milbradt Babeski; Willyan Júnior Adorian Bandeira; GGabriel Mathias Weimer Bruinsma

Canola \(Brassica napus L\. var\. oleifera\) and carinata \(Brassica carinata A\. Braun\) are economically important oilseed crops, driven by the demand for biofuels and the diversification of winter cropping systems in southern Brazil\. Nitrogen fertilization is one of the main factors influencing the growth and yield of these species\. The objective of this study was to evaluate the agronomic performance of canola \(Diamond and Nuola 300\) and carinata \(Nujet 350 and Nugreen 60\) cultivars under different nitrogen sources \(liquid urea and ammonium sulfate\), in addition to a control without supplementary nitrogen\. The experiment was conducted in Ijuí, RS, in 2025, in a randomized complete block design in a 2 × 3 factorial scheme, with four replications\. Morphological variables \(plant height and height of insertion of the first silique\) and yield components \(number of siliques per plant, number of grains per silique, grain weight per plant, and grain yield per hectare\) were evaluated\. In canola, nitrogen sources significantly influenced plant height and the height of insertion of the first silique, with greater growth under liquid urea, without a significant effect on yield\. For carinata, there was no effect of nitrogen sources on yield components, only differences between genotypes for plant height and height of insertion of the first silique\. Under the edaphoclimatic conditions of the study, agronomic performance was more associated with the intrinsic characteristics of the species than with the nitrogen source applied\.

## [In silico design and molecular docking evaluation of antisense oligonucleotides targeting IDO1 mRNA in the context of depression](../publications/1ca0d1c2b33255b04cff.md)

Hao Lin; Kexin Liu; Yuan Xue; Xiaopeng Wei; Rui Guo

Depression is a prevalent mental disorder worldwide, often accompanied by severe complications that significantly impair patients&\#x27; daily lives\. Indoleamine\-2,3\-dioxygenase 1 \(IDO1\), a key metabolic enzyme in the kynurenine pathway, is considered a promising therapeutic target for depression treatment\. Antisense oligonucleotides \(ASOs\) are small nucleic acid drugs characterized by high specificity, high potency, minimal drug\-drug interactions, a prolonged duration of action, and a low risk of off\-target activity, making them effective tools for targeting molecules previously considered undruggable\. Consequently, this study designed a novel ASO targeting the IDO1 gene using a computational approach as a fundamental basis for further investigation\. Based on rational design criteria, five candidate ASOs were screened and utilized for molecular docking simulations with their corresponding IDO1 mRNA fragments\. Furthermore, the intermolecular interactions and binding affinities of the resulting complexes were comprehensively evaluated\. The results demonstrated that strong interactions were established across the five complexes\. Among them, ASO1 displayed the strongest binding affinity\. Notably, its binding site is located within the coding region \(CDS\) of the mRNA, suggesting its potential to effectively inhibit IDO1 gene expression and exert therapeutic efficacy for depression\.

## [Development and external validation of an AI pipeline for automated estimation of a radiographic DMFT \(rDMFT\) score from panoramic radiographs: a feasibility study](../publications/1ca5a35b3670f21bed3e.md)

Babak Saravi; Veronika Shavlokhova; Ashraf Türky; Daman Deep Singh; Felix Schrader; Andreas Vollmer; Norbert R\. Kübler; Christoph K\. Sproll; Lara Schorn

OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of estimating a radiographic Decayed\-Missing\-Filled\-Teeth score \(rDMFT\), a proxy for the clinical DMFT index, from a single panoramic radiograph with a position\-aware deep\-learning pipeline\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A tooth\-status detector and a tooth\-numbering detector \(32 FDI positions\), trained on DENTEX 2023, were combined in a position\-aware read\-out \(one tooth per FDI position, third molars excluded, missing teeth = 28 \- occupied positions\) and validated on 100 panoramic radiographs from an independent hospital against a two\-dentist, radiograph\-based reference \(intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC; mean absolute error, MAE; Bland\-Altman analysis\)\. RESULTS: Against the reference, the pipeline reached an ICC of 0\.84 \(95% CI 0\.74 to 0\.90\) and an MAE of 2\.38, below the between\-dentist agreement in point estimate \(ICC 0\.88, MAE 2\.13\), with larger errors against each dentist alone \(MAE 3\.00 and 2\.73\) and a bias of \+ 1\.14 units from caries over\-detection; agreement was highest for filled \(r 0\.90\) and lowest for decayed teeth \(r 0\.34; dentists 0\.16\)\. In the 26 radiographs with missing teeth the missing count was exact in 42% \(62% within ± 1 tooth\), and missing teeth were over\-called in 15 of 74 complete dentitions; tooth loss was no longer overlooked \(26 of 26 detected\), but the overall ICC was 0\.84 versus 0\.90 without numbering\. CONCLUSIONS: Automated rDMFT estimation is feasible, but agreement was lower in point estimate than between two dentists, with larger errors against each dentist\. The missing component now responds to actual tooth loss but remains imprecise and is over\-called in some complete dentitions; the decayed component is unreliable\. The pipeline is a research building block, not a decision\-support or triage tool\. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: rDMFT is a radiographic proxy, not a clinical measure, and the pipeline is not proposed for clinical use; any application would first require validation in unselected cohorts against clinically determined reference standards\.

## [Texture Analysis of Tumor Spect Images Using Tumorotropic Radiopharmaceuticals](../publications/1caa32267326d785fcf9.md)

Николай Александрович Николов; Sergiy Makeyev; Tatiana Novikova; Denis Myronchuk; Yevhen Rozum; Iryna Kozubska

Background\. Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography \(SPECT\) is one of the most sensitive methods for investigating brain tumors\. Processing and analyzing 3D images require specific segmentation methods, resource\-intensive calculations, and specialized software\. Today, the most popular strategy for solving these problems is the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. At the same time, training AI requires hundreds to thousands of cases in databases, which makes correct training and validation of segmentation methods impossible due to data scarcity\. One solution to the problem of insufficient data is augmentation and artificial generation of images with the requisite properties\. However, quantitative criteria for the adequacy of texture properties of model SPECT images have not yet been defined\. Objective\. The aim of this work is the texture analysis of brain tumor SPECT images and the determination of their main quantitative characteristics for the subsequent assessment of the correctness of artificial tumor generation or augmentation methods\. Methods\. Brain SPECT studies were performed using 99mTc\-pertechnetate and 99mTc\-MIBI\. A total of 94 tumor cases were analyzed, including anaplastic astrocytoma \(n=11\), glioblastoma \(n=22\), metastases \(n=12\), meningioma \(n=4\), and others\. Texture analysis included geometric, statistical \(independent voxel intensity\), and topological \(voxel relationships\) metrics, as well as indices dependent on background cutoff level\. Approximately 45 parameters were calculated per region of interest\. Results\. The data presented in this work systematize the list of texture characteristics of tumor SPECT images using tumorotropic radiopharmaceuticals\. The presented mean values, data dispersion levels, mutual correlation, and regression analysis of these indices allow for a comprehensive evaluation of the adequacy of model 3D SPECT tumor images\. Conclusions\. Quantitative texture characteristics of brain tumor SPECT images were obtained\. To quantitatively assess the degree of neoplasm perfusion and contour indistinctness, a number of new indices were proposed, based on: comparing radiopharmaceutical activity in the tumor with the confluens sinuum area; and evaluating the characteristics of the sigmoid function approximation of parameters dependent on the α background cutoff level\. It was shown that the vast majority of quantitative texture characteristics of tumor SPECT images using tumorotropic agents significantly correlate with the corresponding values of conditionally undamaged tissues\. This relationship is interpreted as being influenced by image quality and the proximity of tumors and the symmetrical control zone to areas with high radiopharmaceutical uptake, particularly skull regions\. For a correct comparison of regions of interest, index normalization accounting for such a correlation is proposed\.

ABSTRACT The quest for better and advanced materials that comply with economic and environmental sustainability principles has led to the development of several materials, including geopolymers\. Derived from aluminosilicates and acid/alkali activators, geopolymers have proven to be a good alternative to several materials, to be environmentally benign and cheap to produce as they can be produced from valorizing waste\. It is therefore necessary to know more about geopolymers to facilitate their industrial application and commercialization\. In this regard, the paper reviews the physicochemical characteristics of geopolymers to fine‐tune them to specific applications, especially in wastewater treatment\. ## [Chinese High\-Level Comprehensive Universities’ Participation in Science Teacher Education in the AI Era: Policy Design, Implementation Status, and Sustainable Mechanisms](../publications/1cd2c9a1c9a9d0f39ba5.md)

Tao Deng; Yilong Zhang; Boyang Deng

Artificial intelligence is reshaping science education, intensifying demands for high\-quality science teachers\. In 2023, China launched the National Excellence Program to promote the institutionalized participation of high\-level comprehensive universities in teacher education\. Drawing on policy analysis, fieldwork across 12 pilot universities, and the case of Northeast Normal University, this study examines the program’s policy design, implementation status, and sustainable mechanisms in the AI era\. The findings show that while the initiative drives a transition toward an open, multiactor collaborative model, disciplinary and technological resources do not automatically translate into teacher education capacity\. Pilot universities still confront unstable participation incentives, fragmented collaboration, fragile institutional guarantees, and unsystematic evaluation\. Moving from project\-based participation to institutionalized implementation therefore requires sustained organizational translation\. The study proposes a four\-dimensional integrated framework comprising Composite Driving, Collaborative Implementation, Multi\-Dimensional Guarantee, and Effect Evaluation mechanisms to support the transformation of disciplinary and technological resources into stable teacher education capacity and cultivate scholar\-like science teachers with academic literacy, educational literacy, and digital\-intelligence mastery\.

## [A novel biomarker combination of adenosine deaminase and total bile acids for predicting 3\-year coronary artery disease risk in middle\-aged and older hospitalized patients](../publications/1ce8c9baf744494a4073.md)

Tao Yang; Wenchao Ou; Sisi Ling; 靳立军; Zechang Lu; Hongquan Liao; Shao\-Jun Liu; Benrong Liu

Coronary artery disease \(CAD\) onset is a leading cause of mortality and morbidity\. Short\-term risk assessment, which generates greater urgency than long\-term estimates, can prompt immediate preventive actions\. However, validated biomarkers and tools for near\-term prediction are scarce\. This study aimed to identify and validate novel biomarkers for predicting 3\-year incident CAD to facilitate timely and targeted risk management\. This retrospective cohort study included 353 patients without history of CAD in the index hospitalization\. Based on follow\-up coronary angiography results, patients were classed into CAD \(incident CAD within 3 years following their index hospitalization, n = 130\) and control groups \( n = 223\)\. Cox regression, restricted cubic splines \(RCS\), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\) machine learning \(ML\) modeling were used to identify and validate biomarkers and construct a risk predictive ML model\. Elevated baseline plasma adenosine deaminase \(ADA\) and total bile acids \(TBA\) levels were significantly associated with a higher risk of CAD onset within 3 years\. Multivariable Cox regression confirmed baseline ADA \( HR = 1\.525, 95% CI 1\.246–1\.867, P &lt; 0\.0001 \) and TBA \( HR = 1\.253, 95% CI 1\.055–1\.489, P = 0\.01 \) as independent predictors of 3\-year CAD risk\. RCS analysis revealed linear dose\-dependent relationships between both biomarkers and CAD risk\. Combining ADA and TBA \(cutoff &gt; 12\.25\) enhanced risk stratification, with the high\-risk group exhibiting a 2\.795\-fold increased relative risk and an elevated hazard ratio of 3\.11 \(95% CI 1\.985–4\.878\) in the fully adjusted Cox model\. Subgroup analyses confirmed consistent associations across all strata\. An XGBoost model incorporating seven biomarkers, including ADA and TBA, achieved excellent predictive performance with an AUC of 0\.846 \(95% CI 0\.803–0\.888\) for the full dataset\. SHAP analysis identified ADA and TBA as the most influential predictors\. Survival analysis demonstrated that patients identified as high risk by the XGBoost model faced a nearly eightfold higher CAD incidence within 3 years compared to low\-risk individuals \(HR = 7\.97\)\. ADA and TBA serve as potential biomarkers for predicting 3\-year CAD risk in middle\-aged and older adults, and their incorporation into an XGBoost model yields superior predictive performance\.

## [Spelling error patterns in the co\-occurrence of reading and spelling difficulties among Chinese children](../publications/1cef02d2eadc1bf4a5ae.md)

Jiuqing Tang; Zujun Song; Zebo XU; Yanjun Wei; Zhenguang Garry Cai; Jingjing Zhao

Abstract Reading difficulties \(RD\) and spelling difficulties \(SD\) frequently co\-occur in children and are associated with persistent spelling problems\. However, little is known about spelling error patterns in Chinese among children with RD, SD, or their co\-occurrence \(RDSD\)\. The current study investigates spelling error patterns of Chinese RD, SD, and RDSD children, together with the cognitive\-linguistic factors associated with these patterns\. We recruited a total of 360 Chinese primary school students aged 8 to 11 years, with 26 meeting criteria for RD only, 32 for SD only, 25 for RDSD, and 118 typically developing children serving as controls\. These children handwrote a character according to a dictation prompt\. Phonological awareness \(PA\), rapid automatized naming \(RAN\), verbal short\-term memory \(vSTM\), morphological awareness \(MA\), and orthographic awareness \(OA\) were assessed to examine cognitive\-linguistic factors associated with spelling error patterns\. Compared with the typical controls, all atypical groups produced more lexical\-level phonological errors, such as writing a homophonic character in place of the target character, with no significant differences among the RD, SD, and RDSD groups\. Across all four groups, poorer vSTM and RAN predicted lower overall spelling performance\. In particular, poorer vSTM was associated with increased lexical\-level phonological errors\. Such increased lexical\-level phonological errors may reflect difficulties in selecting the correct orthographic form among multiple homophonic alternatives in Chinese and may be associated with deficits in the retrieval and temporary maintenance of phonological information\.

## [Archaeal methanogenesis in a deep terrestrial aquifer driven by Methanothermobacter tomskensis sp\. nov\.](../publications/1cf6d8846ffa7df72888.md)

V\. E\. Trubitsyn; I\. I\. Rusanov; Viktoria I\. Rechkina; Vitaly V\. Kadnikov; Daria N\. Zasko; Alexey V\. Beletsky; N\. V\. Pimenov; Nikolai V\. Ravin; Viktoria A\. Shcherbakova; Olga V\. Karnachuk

Methanogenic archaea, capable of producing organic matter from hydrogen and CO 2 emanating from the mantle, constitute one of the key functional groups of microorganisms in the deep subsurface\. Although the diversity of methanogenic inhabitants of the deep biosphere has been studied in detail, the activity of methanogens in these biotopes remains virtually uncharacterized\. We have measured the rate of hyrogenotrophic methanogenesis in water from the model borehole 3P \(2\.7 km deep\), located near the small town of Parabel in the Tomsk Region\. The potential rate of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis, measured using 14 C\-labeled sodium bicarbonate, was 5\.45 ± 0\.528 nmol CH 4 /dm 3 /day \(0\.00545 ± 0\.0005 nmol CH 4 /cm 3 /day\) \- a value compatible to the methanogenic archaeal activity known for anaerobic sediments of surface water bodies\. The 16S rRNA gene profiles of water from well 3P were dominated by s single phylotype assigned to the genus Methanothermobacter ; it accounted for 25\.54% of the total microbial community\. A MAG \(metagenome assembled genome\) designated 3P\-20\-051 and belonging to the genus Methanothermobacter was assembled from the water metagenome of well 3P\. According to GTDB taxonomy, this MAG represents a novel species within the genus\. The closest validly described relative of MAG 3P\-20\-001 was Methanothermobacter marburgensis with an ANI of 92\.66%\. Following the characterization of this MAG, a strain of methanogenic archaea designated as K4 T was isolated in pure culture\. Morphological, physiological, genotypic, and phylogenetic data indicate that this strain represents a new species of the genus Methanothermobacter, for which we propose the name Methanothermobacter tomskensis sp\. nov\. Comparison of the strain K4 T genome with MAG 3P\-20\-051 showed that they were nearly identical: the ANI value was 99\.96%\. Thus, M\. tomskensis sp\. nov\. indeed, represents a dominant methanogenic lineage revealed by metagenomics\. Strain K4 T is characterized by an obligately hydrogenotrophic metabolism and possibly represents the main producer of organic matter in the deep horizons of the thermal aquifer\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and Entrepreneurial Marketing in SMEs in Edo State, Nigeria: A Critical Secondary\-Data Analysis and Capability\-Based Framework](../publications/1cf73efdfab61b34ed94.md)

Kingsley Akabuokwu; Anthony Iyekekpolor

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly accessible to small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) through cloud software, generative AI, social\-platform analytics, automated advertising, recommendation systems and conversational agents\. Yet access to a tool is not equivalent to possession of an organisational capability\. This article examines how AI can strengthen entrepreneurial marketing and SME performance in Edo State, Nigeria, while identifying the conditions under which adoption may produce weak, unequal or harmful outcomes\. The study uses a critical secondary\-data design that triangulates official Nigerian and Edo State policy and economic documents, national MSME statistics, peer\-reviewed theory, and published Edo\-focused survey results\. It re\-analyses reported descriptive statistics and regression outputs rather than fabricating primary observations\. The evidence indicates that Edo SMEs perceive substantial performance benefits from AI\-enabled outputs: a published 2024 survey reports approximately 70\-72% agreement that AI improves decision quality, speed, customer service and opportunity identification\. In the same study, data readiness explained 15\.5% of reported performance variance and computational readiness explained 12\.6%\. A separate 2025 Edo\-Delta study ranked ICT platforms as the strongest of three digital\-transformation predictors, ahead of digital human resources and finance for technology\. However, serious methodological weaknesses in the local evidence—including inconsistent sample counts, self\-reported performance, non\-probability sampling, cross\-sectional designs and questionable model diagnostics—prevent strong causal conclusions\. The article therefore advances an AI\-enabled entrepreneurial marketing capability framework in which data quality, affordable compute, owner\-manager competence and responsible governance enable AI to amplify seven entrepreneurial\-marketing behaviours: proactiveness, opportunity focus, calculated risk\-taking, innovativeness, customer intensity, resource leveraging and value creation\. The central finding is that AI is best understood as an amplifier, not an autonomous source, of competitive advantage\. It creates value when embedded in rapid market learning, disciplined experimentation and trusted customer relationships; it can also scale misinformation, bias, privacy violations and inefficient routines\. The study concludes with a staged adoption pathway and policy recommendations for Edo State, business associations, universities, financial institutions and SME owner\-managers\.

## [Hierarchical affective predictive imbalance in adolescent borderline personality disorder: task\-evoked fMRI evidence from multimodal machine learning](../publications/1cff233eacca89101df5.md)

Min Ma; Xueying Wang; Zeming Tan; Jun Liu; Qian Xiao; Ting Hu; Alessandro Grecucci; Xiaoping Yi

Background Predictive\-processing accounts of BPD, including the hierarchical\-prior\-imbalance account proposed by Herzog, offer a framework for interpreting affective instability and impulsivity\. The present task\-fMRI study evaluates whether discriminative task\-evoked patterns are consistent with this framework; because it does not directly estimate prediction errors, precision weighting, or hierarchical belief updating, it is not a mechanistic test of predictive processing\. Methods To evaluate this question, this study developed a leakage\-controlled multimodal machine learning framework for individualized classification of adolescents with BPD and healthy controls based on emotional Go/No\-Go task\-fMRI activity\. Three feature domains were constructed: functional connectivity \(FC\), task\-evoked general linear model \(GLM\)\-derived temporal features, and clinical variables\. Seven feature settings, including single\-modality, dual\-modality, and full multimodal combinations, were evaluated using multiple conventional machine learning classifiers, including logistic regression, support vector machine, k\-nearest neighbors, Gaussian naive Bayes, multilayer perceptron, random forest, and XGBoost or gradient boosting\. Results The results showed that task\-evoked GLM\-derived features provided the strongest single\-modality discriminative information \(AUC of 0\.881 ± 0\.055\)\. SHAP analysis confirmed the predominance of GLM\-derived features, accounting for 83\.1% of total model attribution, compared to 9\.5 and 7\.5% for functional connectivity and clinical variables, respectively\. At the neural level, discriminative features were distributed across visual/perceptual regions \(calcarine, cuneus, occipital cortex\), temporoparietal/default\-mode hubs \(angular and supramarginal gyri\), frontal control regions \(inferior frontal gyrus\), and subcortical structures \(putamen\)\. This distributed pattern aligns with a hierarchical organization spanning perceptual input, contextual/self\-referential processing, and top\-down inhibitory control systems, consistent with the proposed model of hierarchical affective predictive imbalance\. Conclusion Task\-evoked GLM\-derived features were the primary source of discriminative information for adolescent BPD, with functional connectivity and clinical variables providing modest additional value\. The resulting classification pattern is consistent with hierarchical predictive\-processing accounts but does not establish a specific predictive\-processing mechanism\. The same regional pattern may also reflect visual attention, salience processing, and executive inhibitory control\.

## [From Digital Provision to Quality Improvement: A Resource\-to\-Capability Framework for Institutional Digital Ecosystems in Vocational Education and Training](../publications/1cff68ba92b1b2b48da1.md)

Mounaim EL HAYANI; Fatiha Benamar

Abstract Purpose — This conceptual article considers how vocational education and training \(VET\) institutions may convert digital provision into capabilities that support pedagogical quality, rather than treating equipment or technology adoption as evidence of quality improvement\. Design/methodology/approach — An interpretive synthesis connects research on digital transformation, organizational capabilities, VET teaching and process\-based evaluation\. It distinguishes resource availability, orchestration, capability enactment and quality evidence\. Findings — A four\-stage framework specifies digital provision, institutional resource orchestration, quality\-enabling capabilities and pedagogical process quality, with external occupational interfaces and feedback cycles as boundary conditions\.
