## [Segmented or Integrated? Volatility Connectedness between Commodity Futures and Cryptocurrencies](../publications/1d04d887c55d9cda4e49.md)

Yusuf AKGÜL

This study examines whether commodity futures and cryptocurrency markets constitute a single integrated risk system or remain largely segmented in terms of volatility\. Using daily data on six commodity futures contracts \(gold, silver, copper, WTI crude oil, natural gas, wheat\) and four cryptocurrencies \(Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Litecoin\) over 25 August 2016 – 30 June 2026 \(2,471 trading days\), conditional volatilities estimated by GARCH\(1,1\) are embedded in a ten\-variable VAR, and spillovers are measured with the Diebold–Yılmaz connectedness framework\. The central contribution decomposes total connectedness into within\-block and cross\-block components, complemented by DCC\-GARCH return correlations\. Total connectedness is 28\.7%, yet 61\.4% occurs within the crypto block and 34\.9% within the commodity block, leaving only 3\.6% to cross\-block transmission\. Natural gas \(\+20\.4\) and Ethereum \(\+8\.5\) are the leading net transmitters and gold the largest net receiver \(−18\.7\)\. Commodity–crypto correlations remain low and inert \(0\.040–0\.123\), and the segmentation is robust to the forecast horizon, VAR lag length, window width, return frequency, volatility measure, sample period and data source\. The findings indicate distinct shock sources and durable diversification; aggregate connectedness can conceal block structure\.

## [Silent Fractures, Severed Lines: Measuring the Impact: A Closer Look at Traumatic Cranial Nerve Injuries](../publications/1d0548666ac10070f5fd.md)

Kaleemuddin Shaik; Satyanavamani Gali

Objectives: Traumatic cranial nerve injuries \(TCNIs\) are an under\-recognized yet significant cause of long\-term neurological disability following head trauma\. Cranial nerves are particularly vulnerable to acceleration– deceleration forces, skull base fractures, and direct compressive injuries, resulting in sensory, motor, visual, auditory, and facial functional deficits\. Although the reported incidence of cranial nerve injury ranges from 5% to 23% among patients with traumatic brain injury \(TBI\), most available literature focuses on severe head injury, with limited data addressing mild to moderate trauma\. Early diagnosis is often challenging because cranial nerve deficits may be masked by associated injuries or may present in a delayed fashion\. Functional outcomes vary considerably depending on the nerve involved\. This study was undertaken to evaluate the incidence, pattern of involvement, management, and outcomes of TCNIs in patients with mild to moderate head injury at our institution and to compare the findings with published literature\. To study the incidence, clinical pattern, management, and outcomes of TCNIs in patients with mild to moderate head injury and to compare the findings with established published series\. Material and Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and Dec 2025 at Government General Hospital \(GGH\), Guntur\. During the study period, 1050consecutive patients with mild to moderate head injury \(Glasgow Coma Scale \[GCS\] score 9–15\) were screened, among whom 70 patients identified to have traumatic cranial nerve injury were included for Detailed clinical assessment; comprehensive cranial nerve examination, computed tomography \(CT\) of the brain, and relevant neuroimaging studies were performed\. Patients were followed periodically to assess neurological recovery\. Outcomes were compared with published studies and recent Indian prospective studies\. Results: Young adult males constituted the majority of patients\. Road traffic accidents were the most common mechanism of injury\. Isolated cranial nerve involvement was more frequent than multiple cranial nerve involvement\. Facial nerve injury was the most common cranial neuropathy, followed by oculomotor, optic, abducens, olfactory, and trochlear nerve injuries\. Most patients were managed conservatively, while surgical intervention was required only in selected cases with compressive bony fragments or associated lesions\. Functional recovery was more favorable in facial and abducens nerve palsies, whereas optic and olfactory nerve injuries demonstrated poorer recovery rates\. The incidence of traumatic cranial nerve injury in our study and other contemporary series \(15%\)\. Similar to previous studies, there was a predominance of young adult males, with road traffic accidents being the commonest mode of injury\. The facial nerve was the most frequently involved cranial nerve, followed by the oculomotor and optic nerves\. Most patients had a favorable outcome with conservative management, whereas optic nerve injuries were associated with poorer visual outcomes, consistent with findings from the International Optic Nerve Trauma Study\. Conclusion: Our institutional experience demonstrates that TCNIs, although relatively uncommon, contribute significantly to morbidity following mild to moderate head injury\. The pattern of involvement is comparable with major published series, with young males, road traffic accidents, and facial nerve palsy predominating\. Optic and olfactory nerve injuries are associated with poorer prognosis and require careful patient counseling\. Routine cranial nerve screening and structured follow\-up should be incorporated into standard head injury assessment protocols to facilitate early diagnosis and optimize outcomes\.

## [Emergence and development of observation practices in AI\-assisted plant adaptation learning](../publications/1d0d84ac9b24620cf31e.md)

Widi Purwianingsih; Pipih Nurhayati; Ari Widodo; Achmad Samsudin; R Riandi

Observation is a fundamental scientific practice in science learning, particularly for understanding gradual biological phenomena such as plant adaptation\. Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education, limited research has examined how AI\-supported tools influence students&\#x27; observation practices during authentic scientific inquiry\. This study investigates the emergence and development of students&\#x27; observation practices during plant adaptation learning supported by an AI\-based identifier\. A six\-week mixed\-methods exploratory study was conducted with 84 middle school students\. Learning activities were organised into four phases: orientation, initial observation, AI\-assisted identification, and re\-observation and validation\. Data were collected through observation sheets, students&\#x27; observation notes, reflective journals, group discussions, and records of AI use\. Quantitative analysis revealed significant differences in observation orientations across learning phases \(Friedman test, p &lt; \.001\), indicating changes in observation practices over time\. Qualitative findings showed that students initially relied on AI\-generated cues to guide their observations\. Over time, however, observation practices shifted toward direct empirical observation and peer\-supported validation through repeated comparisons of plant characteristics across environmental conditions\. The findings reveal a developmental trajectory from AI\-reliant observation to direct observation and collaborative validation, accompanied by a gradual reduction in dependence on AI\-generated outputs\. These findings suggest that AI may function as an initial observational scaffold, while more sophisticated observation practices emerge through repeated engagement with phenomena and collaborative reasoning\.

## [Self\-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness\-Policy Optimization](../publications/1d18b6bb54ad847ab372.md)

Zhepei Wei; Wenlin Yao; Baolin Peng; Danqing Wang; Qianhui Wu; Hao Cheng; Yu Meng; Jianfeng Gao

Large language model \(LLM\) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment\. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal\-\-\-a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness\. In light of this, we propose Self\-HPO, a recursive self\-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer\. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates \(H\-step\)\. The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning \(RL\) under the selected harness \(P\-step\), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy&\#x27;s evolving failure modes\. Across three coding benchmarks, Self\-HPO consistently outperforms harness\-only and policy\-only baselines, improving Qwen3\.5\-35B\-A3B&\#x27;s average resolve rate from 57\.8% to 64\.8%, with gains generalizing to out\-of\-distribution settings\. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains\. Self\-HPO also improves reliability \(Pass@1\) and expands the capability frontier \(Pass@k\) over the base agent\. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model \(e\.g\., Opus 4\.8\) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost\.

## [Dietary Artificial Sweeteners: From Chemical Transformation in Food to Gut Microbial Processing](../publications/1d1ba5a8e57558207198.md)

Jürgen Lassak; Michael Hellwig

ABSTRACT Research on artificial sweeteners faces diverse challenges—ranging from long‐term health effects and technological and regulatory questions to environmental aspects—and requires an interdisciplinary approach\. Currently, 10 individual substances are approved as artificial sweeteners in the European Union\. In this brief review, we demonstrate how these substances are chemically stable under food processing and storage conditions both within and beyond the scope of their approved applications, and we address their stability in ecosystems\. Individual degradation products have been described for all sweeteners; however, data on the occurrence and toxicity of these compounds are scarce\. Limited stability is particularly evident for peptide‐based sweeteners such as aspartame under acidic conditions\. Furthermore, we describe how certain artificial sweeteners \(e\.g\., cyclamate, acesulfame K\) can be metabolized by microbiota‐relevant microorganisms, and that other sweeteners \(e\.g\., saccharin, sucralose\) can alter the composition of the microbiota\.

## [Impact of matched samples on domain harmonization in cross\-cohort NMR metabolomics](../publications/1d28853f3825388c0fe5.md)

Aigar Ottas; L\. Goldoni; A\. Armirotti; S\. Decherchi

INTRODUCTION: Machine learning models trained on metabolomics data frequently show reduced performance when applied to independent cohorts because of domain shifts introduced by differences in analytical platforms, sample handling, storage conditions, and metabolite quantification procedures\. Robust approaches for harmonizing metabolomics datasets across cohorts are therefore needed to improve model transferability and reproducibility\. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of matched samples on domain harmonization and cross\-cohort prediction performance in NMR metabolomics data, and to compare multiple harmonization strategies for improving model generalization across independently acquired datasets\. METHODS: A machine\-learning framework was developed to classify ICD\-10 code I50\.9 \(unspecified heart failure\) using plasma NMR metabolomics data from the Estonian Biobank\. Models were trained on a source dataset comprising 12,000 samples measured at Nightingale Health and evaluated on an independently measured destination dataset of 295 samples acquired on a different NMR platform\. Harmonization approaches included within\-domain normalization, Optimal Transport, Bridge mapping, and Empirical Bayes correction\. The effect of matched samples was assessed using up to 108 duplicated biospecimens measured in both datasets\. Additional validation was performed using independently generated human gestational diabetes and mouse diabetes metabolomics datasets from Metabolomics Workbench\. RESULTS: Domain harmonization generally improved cross\-cohort prediction compared with unaligned data, particularly when matched samples were available\. Predictive performance increased as the number of matched samples used for calibration increased, although gains varied across methods\. Nevertheless, simple within\-domain normalization consistently provided strong performance and often matched or exceeded more complex alignment approaches\. External validation using fully unmatched human and mouse metabolomics datasets demonstrated that harmonization strategies improved classification performance relative to raw data, supporting the broader applicability of the framework\. CONCLUSION: Matched samples substantially enhance domain harmonization and improve the transferability of metabolomics prediction models across analytical platforms and cohorts\. However, robust normalization remains a strong baseline, and the benefits of more sophisticated alignment methods depend on the availability and representativeness of matched reference samples\. These findings provide practical guidance for developing reproducible cross\-cohort metabolomics machine\-learning models while preserving biologically relevant signals\.

## [Advances in immunotherapy for gastrointestinal malignancies](../publications/1d2b01606ce3e37ac8a4.md)

Bo Liu; Lei Wang; Yuehan Ma; Weijie Xu; Xinting Chen; Zhaocheng Chi; Bao\-Cheng Xing

Gastrointestinal malignancies remain leading causes of cancer mortality, yet their sensitivity to immunotherapy differs sharply across anatomical sites, histologies, molecular subtypes, and disease stages\. Immune checkpoint blockade has established durable clinical benefit in microsatellite instability\-high colorectal cancer, advanced gastric and esophageal cancers, hepatocellular carcinoma, and biliary tract cancer, while pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and microsatellite\-stable colorectal cancer remain largely refractory\. Recent phase III trials have moved immunotherapy into perioperative treatment\. Concurrently, claudin 18\.2\-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells, T\-cell receptor\-engineered cells, bispecific antibodies, personalized vaccines, and oncolytic viruses are converting previously speculative strategies into clinically testable platforms\. This review integrates contemporary trial evidence with mechanisms of immune escape, biomarker development, and combination toxicity\. The resulting framework prioritizes evidence maturity across diverse gastrointestinal tumor types worldwide\.

## [An automated EEG–ECG framework for CAP–HRV analysis: enabling brain–heart coupling studies in sleep disorders](../publications/1d2db7bfaea72f245fa4.md)

Shaween Shukir; Mostafa Mohamed Moussa; Yahya Alzaabi; Ahsan Habib Khandoker; Zbigniew R\. Struzik

Background Multimodal sleep analysis typically requires separate processing pipelines for electroencephalography \(EEG\) and electrocardiography \(ECG\), which complicates joint investigation of sleep microstructure and autonomic regulation\. Cyclic alternating pattern \(CAP\) scoring and heart rate variability \(HRV\) analysis are routinely performed in different software environments, limiting temporal alignment, reproducibility, and scalability\. Methods We present an open\-source MATLAB framework that integrates rule\-based CAP A1 detection and HRV feature extraction within a single, time\-synchronized workflow\. The pipeline performs standardized EEG and ECG preprocessing, rule\-based CAP A1 detection during slow\-wave sleep \(SWS\) implementing the Terzano scoring criteria, R\-peak detection via the Pan–Tompkins algorithm, and computation of time\-domain, frequency\-domain, and nonlinear HRV features by calling the open\-source PhysioZoo/mhrv toolbox directly\. CAP annotations are aligned with 5\-minute ECG epochs through the shared polysomnography \(PSG\) time base\. The complete code is released as an open\-source repository to support reuse and extension\. Results Because HRV features are computed by calling the PhysioZoo/mhrv toolbox directly, the pipeline introduces no reimplemented HRV routine and inherits that toolbox’s validated feature definitions\. CAP A1 detection is provided as a rule\-based implementation of published criteria and has not yet been benchmarked against expert manual scoring\. A worked example on the OSAD\+ subgroup \(n = 18\) demonstrates pipeline output across CAP and non\-CAP epochs, and a healthy\-sleep A1\-event HRV reference is reported from the public CAP Sleep Database \(15 controls, 785 A1 epochs\) as a descriptive cross\-database reference\. Conclusion The framework provides a reproducible, rule\-based, and modular tool for integrated EEG–ECG analysis of sleep microstructure and autonomic dynamics\. By enabling synchronized CAP–HRV feature extraction in a single environment, it lowers the engineering barrier to brain–heart coupling research during sleep and provides a foundation for future extensions, including validated CAP detection, a matched\-control study, a Python port, and cloud\-based deployment\.

## [Federated digital twin framework for spectrum handover management in vehicular THz ORAN](../publications/1d367b2bd9ce0d469e46.md)

Akanksha Gupta; Amira Nisar; Mumtaz Ahmad Khan

Vehicular Terahertz \(THz\) Open Radio Access Networks \(ORAN\) face severe challenges due to ultra\-high mobility, rapid channel dynamics, spectrum scarcity, and frequent handovers, which limit the effectiveness of existing reactive and centralized management strategies\. This paper proposes a Federated Blockchain\-Assisted Digital Twin framework for proactive spectrum sharing and seamless handover in vehicular THz ORAN systems\. The framework employs a Contrastive Denoising Spatio\-Temporal Autoencoder \(CD\-STAE\) to refine multi\-source telemetry while preserving transient anomalies, followed by a Federated Multi\-View Neural State\-Space Twin \(FMNSS\) that constructs a privacy\-preserving digital replica of the network\. A Spatio\-Temporal Transformer with Heteroscedastic Uncertainty \(ST\-TrH\) enables confidence\-aware forecasting of load, interference, and mobility\-driven congestion, while On\-Chain Verifiable Reward Shaping \(OVRS\) integrates blockchain\-derived trust scores into federated aggregation and proactive spectrum leasing\. Building on these predictions, a Reinforced Graph Trajectory Encoded DiffNet \(R\-GTEDiffNet\), comprising EM\-ST\-GAT, Causal Trajectory Encoder \(CTE\), and Differentiable Handover Cost Layer \(DHCL\), is introduced to perform mobility\-aware spectrum slicing and predictive handover optimization\. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance over state\-of\-the\-art models, achieving up to 94\.1% spectrum utilization, 6\.2 ms leasing delay, 10\.5 ms handover latency, 1786 Mbps throughput, and an average classification accuracy of 98\.68%, showing the framework’s strength in high\-speed vehicular THz ORAN scenarios\.

## [Time series regression network using exogenous variables for missing effective ion charge reconstruction in EAST tokamak](../publications/1d61bb52c459cc5b3847.md)

K\. Jia; Zong Xu; Zhenwei Wu; Wei Gao; Minrui Wang; Ang Ti; Hailin Zhao; Xiaohe Wu; Zhen Zhou; Kaibo Nan; Zhe Yuan Si; Zichao Lin; Juan Huang

Abstract The effective ion charge \(Zeff\) is a key parameter for characterizing plasma impurity levels and is important for investigating impurity transport and assessing discharge conditions in tokamaks\. However, diagnostic system failures can lead to missing or incomplete Zeff signals\. Accurate reconstruction remains challenging because Zeff is related to multiple plasma parameters and exhibits temporal dependencies\. In this study, a time series regression network was developed to reconstruct missing Zeff values from exogenous plasma parameters in EAST\. The model employed a sequential CNN\-BiGRU\-Transformer encoder architecture, in which the CNN extracted local temporal features, the BiGRU captured bidirectional temporal information, and the Transformer encoder modelled dependencies across different timescales through multi\-head self\-attention\. The model was trained and validated using a dataset comprising 1566 EAST discharges\. The results show that the average similarity between the reconstruction and experimental data is 90\.3%, while the average coverage probability is 91\.4%, indicating that most reconstruction values fall within the standard deviation error range of the experimental results\. Overall, this study presents a feasible offline signal reconstruction method to maintaining the integrity of Zeff signals in EAST and provides a useful reference for reconstructing missing diagnostic data in future fusion devices\.

## [Genetic Algorithm\-Based Feature Selection and Random Forest Modelling of Agricultural Biotechnology Adoption and Crop Yield in Tamil Nadu](../publications/1d61c20d191562f8739e.md)

Priya K; Aji Jovitha A\. T; Manimannan G

This research paper attempts to identify the Biotechnology inputs such as tissue\-culture seedlings, improved seed, microbial biofertilisers and bio pesticides are promoted widely in Tamil Nadu, yet their combined association with crop performance is seldom examined across many crops at once\. This study analyses 6,500 farm\-level records covering 38 districts, 14 crops and the years 2021–2025 \(a simulated research dataset\) and introduces a relative yield index \(RYI\) that expresses each yield as a ratio to its crop median, so that crops with very different absolute yields can be compared\. A genetic algorithm \(GA\) searches the space of 41 candidate predictors, using cross\-validated Random Forest accuracy with a small size penalty as fitness, and a final Random Forest is trained on the selected subset\. The GA retained 23 predictors \(a 43\.9% reduction\) and reached a hold\-out R² of 0\.382 and RMSE of 0\.140, against 0\.367 and 0\.141 for a Random Forest on all predictors; gradient boosting scored highest \(R² = 0\.418\)\. Tissue\-culture seedlings \(\+10\.1%, Cohen d = 0\.58\) and improved seed \(\+7\.2%, d = 0\.40\) were linked to a higher RYI, whereas farmer training showed no detectable effect\. Irrigation source was the dominant predictor: drip or sprinkler farms exceeded rain fed farms by 27%\.

## [Mühendislikte Bilgisayar Destekli Modelleme, Analiz ve Kontrol Uygulamaları](../publications/1d67d80a91e79c8d9642.md)



Bu kitap, mühendisliğin farklı alanlarında kullanılan bilgisayar destekli yöntemleri modelleme, veri analizi ve kontrol açısından ele almaktadır\. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol, sürü robotiği ve hidroloji araştırmaları üzerinden hesaplamalı yaklaşımların temel ilkelerini, uygulama koşullarını ve değerlendirme ölçütlerini bir araya getirmektedir\. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol bölümünde, derin öğrenme tabanlı görsel muayene sistemleri; kusur tespiti, görüntü segmentasyonu ve anomali tespiti yöntemleriyle birlikte incelenmektedir\. Veri sınırlılıkları, görüntüleme donanımı ve gerçek zamanlı üretim hattı entegrasyonu ele alınmaktadır\. Sürü robotiği bölümünde, çok robotlu sistemlerin koordinasyon ve kontrol problemleri değerlendirilmekte; farklı kontrol yaklaşımları ölçeklenebilirlik, haberleşme gereksinimleri, hesaplama yükü ve arıza toleransı bakımından karşılaştırılmaktadır\. Hidroloji bölümünde ise bilimsel yayınlardan araştırma eğilimlerinin belirlenmesi amacıyla konu modelleme yöntemleri uygulanmakta; gizli anlamsal analiz, gizli Dirichlet tahsisi ve negatif olmayan matris ayrıştırması karşılaştırılmaktadır\. Kitap, yöntemlerin kuramsal temelleri ile uygulamadaki gereksinimleri arasındaki ilişkiyi vurgulayarak araştırmacılara, lisansüstü öğrencilere ve mühendislik uygulayıcılarına disiplinler arası bir bakış sunmaktadır\.

## [Stretchable h‐BN/TPU Fibers for Passive‐Active Dual‐Mode Thermal Management and Wearable Haptic Interfaces](../publications/1d6f892e165a0a51a319.md)

Yiwei Zhou; Shanshan Long; Bo Chen; Maohua Li; Linhong Li; Yue Qin; Rongjie Yang; Hanxi Chen; Cheng‐Te Lin; Yixiang Xu; Kean How Cheah; Nan Jiang; Jinhong Yu

ABSTRACT Wearable thermal interfaces require rapid, spatially confined thermal feedback together with mechanical compliance, yet existing passive thermal‐management textiles and active thermal‐haptic devices remain largely separate\. Here, a stretchable h ‐BN/TPU composite fiber is developed by coupling microfluidic spinning with non‐solvent‐induced phase separation\. Rectangular‐channel confinement aligns hexagonal boron nitride plates within a microporous thermoplastic polyurethane matrix, constructing directional heat‐conduction pathways while preserving large deformation\. The optimized 30 wt\.% h ‐BN/TPU fiber achieves a dry‐state thermal conductivity of 2\.08 and 4\.14 W·m −1 ·K −1 under humid conditions, together with 9\.67 MPa tensile strength and 422% elongation at break\. Pareto‐front analysis identifies the 30 wt\.% composition as the thermal‐mechanical knee, arising from the coupled effects of filler orientation, low void fraction, and deformable TPU domains\. Woven h ‐BN/TPU fabrics provide passive thermal management, reducing surface temperature by 5\.7°C under simulated solar irradiation and maintaining performance after 2000 bending cycles\. When integrated into a thermal feedback glove, the fabric enables localized fingertip actuation with a heating rate of \+29\.55°C·s −1 and a thermal relaxation time of ∼20 s \(returning below the warm perception threshold of 35°C\)\. This fiber platform bridges passive heat regulation and active thermal haptics for next‐generation thermally interactive wearables\.

## [The psychology of fate: patterned constraint, situated freedom, and algorithmic prediction](../publications/1d7324b6495228657433.md)

Adrienne Incze; Tamás Treuer

This Conceptual Analysis rehabilitates fate as a boundary concept for theoretical and philosophical psychology\. It does not treat fate as metaphysical predestination or as a new causal mechanism\. Instead, fate is defined as the lived convergence of patterned constraints that organize possibility before reflective choice begins\. Four features distinguish fate\-like experience: temporal recurrence, pre\-reflective organization of action, a felt quality of necessity, and partial rather than absolute openness to transformation\. Using a transparent, targeted theory\-synthesis method, the article places depth psychology in dialogue with attachment and infant research, ecological and enactive accounts of agency, predictive processing and active inference, phenomenology and Daseinsanalysis, critical and narrative psychology, and contemporary work on algorithmic mediation\. The analysis clarifies that human agency is neither isolated nor exclusively internal: bodies, relationships, institutions, stories, and technological systems participate in shaping fields of action\. Non\-human systems may mediate and redistribute agency without thereby acquiring the same phenomenological or moral status as persons\. The central construct of situated freedom names the capacity to recognize, reinterpret, resist, and transform patterned constraints by changing both one&\#x27;s relation to them and, where possible, the environments that sustain them\. A multilevel practical heuristic is proposed for clinical, everyday, social, and algorithmic contexts\. The paper also specifies limitations: fate is culturally variable, should not be used diagnostically, and must never naturalize oppression or engineered technological constraints\.

## [A novel load balancing algorithm for task allocation in fog\-enabled healthcare systems](../publications/1d741a9d11f29f5b57a6.md)

Ahmad Naseem Alvi; Bakhtiar Qutub Ali; Haider Ali; Abdul Khader Jilani Saudagar

Timely intervention is critical for saving a patient’s life\. To monitor vital signs, various health monitoring sensors are placed on the patient’s body, collecting data at regular intervals\. However, the limited computational capacity of these health monitoring sensor nodes prevents them from analyzing the data independently\. By integrating sensors with Internet of Things \(IoT\) nodes, the collected data can be offloaded to nearby fog nodes for processing\. A challenge arises when certain fog nodes receive a disproportionate number of healthcare data tasks compared to others, necessitating an efficient load balancing mechanism to process these time\-sensitive tasks promptly\. In this work, we propose an Intelligent Task Offloading Scheme for Healthcare Data Analysis \( ITOS HDA \)\. The scheme consists of two key algorithms: \(1\) a load balancing algorithm that employs the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution \(TOPSIS\) method to allocate offloaded tasks efficiently among fog nodes, and \(2\) a task execution algorithm that uses the 0/1 Knapsack approach to prioritize tasks based on their deadlines\. The performance of ITOS HDA is evaluated against state\-of\-the\-art schemes, demonstrating its superiority in handling varying numbers of fog nodes and offloaded tasks\. Experimental results confirm that ITOS HDA outperforms existing algorithms in terms of efficiency and scalability\.

## [Recent advances in coarse\-grained simulations of nucleic acid condensation](../publications/1d771cca5755f463f144.md)

Jessica Fong Ng; Shanlong Li; Jianhan Chen

Biomolecular condensates, formed through phase separation of multivalent biomolecules, play essential roles in cellular processes such as stress response, RNA processing, transcriptional control, and genome organization\. Nucleic acids are increasingly recognized as important drivers and regulators of condensate formation and dynamics\. This review examines recent advances in coarse\-grained molecular simulations of dynamic nucleic acids and their phase transitions\. We survey established computational frameworks validated against experimental data and discuss emerging applications that address increasingly complex systems\. Existing studies reveal that base\-mediated interactions emerge as dominant drivers in homotypic nucleic acid condensation and that simulation resolution fundamentally determines which physical phenomena are accessible and observable\. We underscore that different modeling approaches at various resolutions provide complementary insights into nucleic acid condensation mechanisms and the driving forces\. We emphasize the opportunities and challenges in extending these frameworks to capture the complexity of nucleic acid\-mediated phase separation in biological contexts, while identifying important gaps in current modeling capabilities\. Overall, molecular simulations at multiple scales have proven to be powerful tools for elucidating the mechanistic principles underlying nucleic acid condensates and their cellular functions\.

## [Methodology and methods for studying the image of the future state](../publications/1d832985b33d1e5e8386.md)

Aleksandr A\. Grebenyuk; Ирина Волкова

This article presents an attempt to generalize methods for analyzing images of the future, in particular, the image of the future state as a complex and largely irrational construct of collective consciousness recorded in textual, graphic, audio, or numerical format\. It examines the specific features of multilevel methodological approaches to analyzing images of the future \(thematic analysis, comprehensive socio\-humanitarian analysis, causal\-level analysis, and linguopolitical prognostics\), as well as the possibilities of applying selected sociological and psychological methods, hermeneutics, semiotics, archetypal analysis, cognitive science, and cybermetrics, using domestic and foreign studies as examples\.

## [When the clinician becomes the manager: safety planning as intrapsychic enactment and a testable Internal Family Systems reframing of suicide\-specific care](../publications/1d94138eb61112ac2cef.md)

Jörg E\. Strobel

Safety planning depends on disclosure\. Yet many suicidal patients conceal their suicidal intent from clinicians, often fearing the consequences of disclosure\. Critics of contemporary suicide\-prevention frameworks increasingly warn that a detection\-and\-containment approach may foster a defensive, algorithmic practice, but an encounter\-level account of how such an approach may become counter\-therapeutic has remained underdeveloped\. Drawing on Internal Family Systems \(IFS\) theory, we propose one such account\. We argue that suicidality is often best understood as a protective response to unbearable distress, conceptualized within IFS as a “firefighter” stance: a protective action whose catastrophic outcome nonetheless serves a function\. More novelly, we suggest that containment\-oriented safety planning can recruit the clinician into the \`manager&\#x27; role within the patient’s internal system, recreating within the therapeutic dyad the very manager–firefighter polarity that may contribute to the crisis\. From this follows a specific paradox: a system that depends on disclosure may, under certain conditions, suppress the very disclosure on which it relies\. The contribution of this paper is neither the functional interpretation of suicidality nor the critique of containment\-oriented care, both of which are well established in the literature\. Rather, it is the proposal that the clinical encounter itself may operate as an enactment of the patient’s own manager–firefighter polarity, and that it may create a concealment mechanism through which suppression\-oriented care may undermine its own aims\. From this account, we derive a falsifiable prediction that distinguishes it from alliance\- and autonomy\-based explanations: a containment\-oriented approach should produce selective concealment of suicidal intent despite preserved engagement—a dissociation between sustained alliance and concealed suicidal intent that those explanations do not predict\. Conditions for disconfirmation are specified\.

## [Learning Changes the World and Then What Was Learned has Changed: Training and Deploying Neural Networks in the Control Loop](../publications/1d9c6ed9e4c0c15ca489.md)

Vittorio Lippi

Neural networks offer critical adaptability for controlling complex systems where nominal modeling proves intractable\. However, when offline\-trained neural networks are deployed within closed\-loop control systems, their actions fundamentally alter the state distribution upon which they were trained\. This paper introduces a unified taxonomy to categorize these sequential failure modes: the initial Closed\-Loop Identification Error, the deployment\-induced Action Error, and the continuous Tracking Error\. Through discrete\-time sensitivity analysis, this work formalizes how offline\-learned parameters locally guarantee a trajectory divergence upon deployment, degrading performance due to local loss geometry\. To mitigate this distribution shift, we propose actionable design policies centered on time\-scale separated online adaptation\. These mechanisms are validated through ablation studies on a nonlinear Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that bounded continuous learning successfully mitigates trajectory divergence whereas static deployments fail, offering concrete guidelines for practitioners deploying machine learning components in safety\-critical feedback systems\.

## [Investigação Sobre Diplomacia Pública na Public Relations Review \(2000–2024\): Uma Revisão Sistemática de 25 Anos](../publications/1da3aafce3e176fadbd3.md)

Álvaro Elgueta\-Ruiz; Carmen Lucía Domínguez Aguila; Daniela Bento Almeida

Over the past two decades, public diplomacy \(PD\) has consolidated its position as a strategic field of communication and a central instrument of countries’ foreign policy, drawing increasing attention in international public relations scholarship\. However, despite the growing body of literature and academic interest in these areas, systematic approaches to PD research remain limited\. To address this gap, the present study examines the state of research in this field through qualitative and quantitative content analysis of all articles on PD published in Public Relations Review between 2000 and 2024 \(n = 52\), out of 1,991 articles published during this period\. This analysis identifies the main authors and their affiliated universities, the networks they form, their objectives, research questions, hypotheses, the methodologies employed, the types of studies conducted, and the theories, findings, and conclusions presented, among other relevant aspects\. Finally, the study discusses the theoretical and practical implications of PD research for the broader field of public relations and related areas\.

## [An explainable machine learning framework with trend\-sensitive features for predicting high\-potential merchants in mobile payment ecosystems](../publications/1da608c1e33ed48b61c8.md)

JrJung Lyu; Chun\-Hung Hsieh

Mobile payment platforms face a persistent decision\-support challenge: payment service providers \(PSPs\) must identify high\-potential merchants from large merchant bases without relying solely on retrospective transaction scale\. This study develops an explainable decision\-support framework for merchant prioritization by combining growth\-trajectory feature engineering, XGBoost classification, and SHAP\-based interpretability\. Using 61,280 merchant\-month records from 3,939 merchants of a leading payment service provider between January 2022 and March 2025, the framework predicts merchant potential while translating model outputs into decision\-usable explanations\. Merchant potential is operationalized through a polar\-group label: merchants in the top 20% of cumulative future gross merchandise value \(GMV\) over the prediction horizon are treated as high\-potential and those in the bottom 20% as low\-potential, so the term “high\-potential” denotes this top\-quantile future\-GMV definition rather than current transaction size\. To establish methodological rigor, the framework is benchmarked against rule\-based, linear, ensemble, and stacking baselines, and a feature\-group ablation is conducted to isolate the contribution of trend\-sensitive variables\. The proposed framework attains strong predictive performance on the held\-out test set \(AUC = 0\.841; AP = 0\.868; F1 = 0\.783; Precision@100 = 0\.91; Lift@40% = 1\.61\) while outperforming logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, raw\-GMV XGBoost, and rule\-based screening on operational precision\. SHAP analysis indicates that the nine\-month GMV trend slope and the six\-month average GMV jointly shape merchant potential, with growth trajectory providing incremental predictive value beyond static scale\. The study contributes to merchant analytics by reframing explainability as a structured, auditable decision\-support layer rather than as a supplementary visualization\. For PSPs, the proposed framework supports transparent merchant prioritization, internal auditability, and targeted resource allocation while avoiding overdependence on opaque prediction scores or simple GMV\-based heuristics\. As boundary conditions, the results are drawn from a single PSP and a polar\-group \(top\-versus\-bottom\-quantile\) sample rather than the full merchant population, and the decision\-support layer is assessed structurally through mapping consistency and rank stability rather than through user studies, formal audits, or measured business outcomes\.

## [ENSEMBLES DE DEEP LEARNING NO DIAGNÓSTICO DE LESÕES ENDOSCÓPICAS](../publications/1da85b35c4bbf05617aa.md)

Breno Augusto Tamanini; Danilo Maia de Oliveira; Marcos Raffael Almeida Amorim; Felipe da Costa Mota; José Leal Rodrigues; Genilson Vieira Martins

Lesões gastrointestinais representam um relevante problema de saúde pública, cuja detecção precoce reduz a mortalidade, apesar da subjetividade da análise manual de imagens endoscópicas\. Este trabalho propõe o DeepEnsemble\-Endo, um ensemble de weighted soft voting com pesos otimizados via grid search\. Após avaliar 11 CNNs pré\-treinadas por transfer learning e selecionar as cinco melhores \(DenseNet121, ResNet50, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB2\), os pesos foram sistematicamente otimizados, alcançando 96,63% de acurácia e 97,25% de F1\-score \- superandos ensembles simples da literatura e evidenciando o potencial da abordagem como suporte automatizado à decisão clínica\.

## [Closed\-Loop, Event\-Driven Machine Learning for Autonomous Triage of Single\-Photon Emitters](../publications/1dacc1b882911e11b88e.md)

Tanvir M\. Mahim; Md Nahin Islam; M\. Mosaddequr Rahman; Abu S\. M\. Mohsin

Abstract Identifying which candidate sites on a solid\-state sample are single\-photon emitters requires a Hanbury Brown–Twiss \(HBT\) measurement of the second\-order correlation function g\(2\)\(τ\), which is slow because photon coincidences accumulate at a rate proportional to the square of the detected count rate\. We examine how much of this time can be saved by deciding while the coincidences are still accumulating and by adapting the exposure of each site\. A spiking neural network reads the coincidence record in short time slices and updates, after every slice, its estimate of the probability that the site hosts a single emitter; a reinforcement\-learning controller decides, site by site, whether to expose longer, certify, or reject; and a graph that encodes the electronic level structure of each emitter class conditions one estimator on the class being measured\. All components are trained on simulated data from a standard three\-level photon\-counting model, which we validate against the exact master\-equation solution before use\. In simulation, the event\-driven estimator reaches 90% balanced accuracy with 6 times less acquisition time than a multistart least\-squares fit, typically committing to a decision 312 ms into a 1 s exposure, and adaptive exposure screens simulated 48\-site fields 1\.7 times faster than fixed\-dwell scanning at matched precision and recall\. Applied without retraining to published experimental HBT data from an InGaAs/GaAs quantum dot, a network trained only on simulated pulsed\-excitation histograms estimates g\(2\)\(0\) from 30 s records with half the error of peak\-area analysis of the same records\. The closed\-loop results are obtained in simulation only\. The code, data, and trained models are openly available\.

## [Physics\-Informed Vector LSTM for Multi\-Horizon Hub\-Height Wind Speed Forecasting Across Multiple Sites](../publications/1db42edc0bab574a8964.md)

Jianguo Yan; Zhe Li; Chuangye Li; Zhihua Ding; 黄翔超; Guohua Ke; Wenzhe Zhang; Bin Song; Shifeng Ding

Accurate hub\-height wind\-speed forecasting is a prerequisite for the safe and economical integration of wind power into the electricity grid, because forecasting errors propagate directly into imbalance penalties, reserve sizing, and turbine wear, and short\-term predictions \(one to twenty\-four hours ahead\) are of direct operational value\. The literature on wind\-speed and, more broadly, multivariate time\-series forecasting has advanced through three overlapping waves, namely classical statistical and physical models, shallow machine\-learning regression, and deep sequence models, which share a common trajectory of replacing hand\-crafted meteorological relationships by data\-driven estimators\. Four shared limits recur across this work: deep architectures treat covariates as exchangeable tokens and under\-use the physically grounded relationships among synchronous variables; they optimize pure accuracy without a mechanism that keeps the forecast physically consistent with the atmosphere; evaluations concentrate on generic benchmarks where the short\-term optimum is often a linear or persistence baseline, so the benefit of complex inductive biases at operational horizons is unclear; and wind\-speed studies seldom isolate an explicit physical prior from the recurrent or attention backbone\. This work contributes \(a\) a reproducible multi\-site benchmark of eight forecasting strategies, namely persistence, ARIMA, gradient\-boosted trees, a plain LSTM, and four further deep architectures including PatchTST, DLinear, iTransformer, and the proposed physics\-informed PIV\-LSTM, evaluated at five horizons on four real sites; \(b\) a physics\-informed vector \(PIV\) that augments the network input with an ordinary\-least\-squares linear reconstruction of the target from its known covariates, and regularizes training with a decaying consistency loss, implemented on an LSTM backbone \(PIV\-LSTM\); and \(c\) an ablation that quantifies where the physical prior helps and where it does not, together with an honest assessment of the results, including where a classical model remains competitive and the long\-horizon regime in which every model loses skill\.

## [Multi\-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation](../publications/1db8fdb5e9b4861858b0.md)

Yiming Lu; Tingyu Lu; Di Zhang; Lili Ye; Hao Li

Aluminum nanoparticles \(ANPs\) are among the most energy\-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive\. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum\-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales \(&lt;500 atoms, picoseconds\), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments\. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human\-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task\-specific machine learning potential \(MLP\) more traceable and auditable\. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model\-use decisions under researcher control\. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near\-linear scalability\. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature\-regulated dual\-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic &quot;gatekeeper,&quot; regulating oxidation through a &quot;breathing mode&quot; of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a &quot;rupture mode&quot; leads to shell failure and rapid combustion\. Importantly, we resolve a decades\-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude\. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human\-audited agentic workflows can make domain\-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible\.
