## [Digital Transformation in Religious Public Administration: Policy Innovation for Inclusive Services](../publications/1dd7668ef763f90460b2.md)

Muhibbatul Laili; Yayah Dwi Hayatun; Singh Dhepa Manggala

Digital transformation can expand access to public services, yet fragmented administrative responsibilities and unequal digital capabilities may prevent users from benefiting from these changes\. This study examines how policy innovation can connect institutional coordination and responsiveness to diverse user needs to support inclusive services in religious public administration\. Adopting an interpretive approach, the study employs qualitative conceptual synthesis of theoretical contributions and published empirical research selected for their conceptual and substantive relevance\. Analysis involves repeated reading, thematic interpretation, and comparison of concepts and arguments, guided by collaborative governance and public service logic\. The synthesis indicates that policy innovation can support coordination by clarifying responsibilities, aligning procedures, and establishing arrangements for resolving problems across administrative units\. Alongside these organizational arrangements, responsiveness requires attention to users’ ability to complete service processes and their opportunities to influence service decisions through accessible participation and appropriate assistance\. Bringing these dimensions together suggests that identified barriers can inform procedural adjustment when connected to institutions with the authority and capacity to respond\. Moreover, experiences of unsuccessful access provide relevant input for policy revision alongside feedback from users who complete services\. The study proposes a conceptual model linking organizational capacity with user inclusion and offers guidance for reviewing service responsibilities, participation arrangements, and support mechanisms\. These relationships remain propositions for empirical examination within public institutions administering religious affairs\.

## [Forensic Evidence Integrity in Jordan: Strengthening Prosecutorial Oversight and Digital Governance](../publications/1ddad27891afa49f17bd.md)

Mohammed Bany Taha; Malek Hamad; Dhya Numan

This study examines whether the Jordanian public prosecutor&\#x27;s supervisory powers are sufficient to protect forensic evidence from contamination, undocumented handling, technical error, and chain\-of\-custody weaknesses, and asks how contemporary forensic standards and digital technologies can be incorporated into prosecutorial oversight without shifting scientific decision\-making from forensic specialists to legal authorities\. Using qualitative doctrinal, comparative, and standards\-based analysis, the study analyses Jordanian criminal\-procedure regulations and assesses them against international forensic and digital\-evidence standards using six analytical dimensions: legality, identity, continuity, scientific reliability, traceability, and accountability\. The findings indicate that Jordanian law provides meaningful prosecutorial authority and recognizes the evidentiary value of scientific expertise\. Nonetheless, the legal and institutional materials examined reveal deficiencies in standardized lifecycle documentation, digital chain\-of\-custody controls, technical traceability, validation records, exception reporting, and auditable prosecutorial review\. Drawing on these legal and forensic findings, the study proposes the Prosecutorial Integrity and Digital Evidence Governance \(PIDEG\) Model, which integrates unique evidence identification, digital chain\-of\-custody documentation, technical metadata, validation controls, exception alerts, access restrictions, audit trails, and defined prosecutorial review\. Academically, the study contributes a legal\-technological governance framework for Jordan that integrates prosecutorial oversight, forensic quality assurance, and digital evidence governance within a coherent evidentiary framework\. Under this model, prosecutors function as procedural and governance overseers responsible for legality, documentation, accountability, and review, while forensic scientists remain independent professionals responsible for scientific validation and interpretation\.

## [Identification of Transcriptional Signatures Associated with COPD in Immune and Epithelial–Stromal Cells Using Machine Learning Methods](../publications/1ddc82cebeaee1e66227.md)

Jingxin Ren; Jingjing Fan; YuSheng Bao; Wei Guo; Kaiyan Feng; Jerry Hu; Wenran Zhou; Deling Wang; Lin Lü; Tao Huang; Yu‐Dong Cai

In the context of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\), understanding gene expression patterns across various cell types is pivotal for disease comprehension, therapeutic development, and enhancement of patient prognosis\. Nevertheless, the intricate interplay between immune and structural cells, along with their significance in COPD pathogenesis, remains only partially understood\. This research employed multiple machine learning techniques to pinpoint marker genes exhibiting pronounced alterations between COPD patients and healthy individuals\. We utilized six feature selection algorithms \(LASSO, LightGBM, MCFS, RF, CATboost, and XGBoost\) and three classification methods \(DT, KNN, and RF\) to analyze single\-cell patient data\. Cells were bifurcated into two subsets: immune cells and epithelial–stromal cells\. Each cell, encompassing 21,237 genes, was labeled either as a healthy control or COPD\. We identified a number of promising genes, such as FKBP5, which encodes a protein crucial for stress response regulation, and SCGB3A1, which is predominantly expressed in the respiratory tract and critical for regulating lung function\. Both genes exhibit strong correlations with COPD\. The study also underscored the potential roles of HLA\-DRB1 and HSP90AA1 in COPD pathogenesis\. Our findings underscore the unparalleled potential of machine learning in identifying genetic markers for intricate diseases like COPD, paving the way for targeted therapeutic advancements\.

## [Integrated haematological, inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers in steady\-state and vaso\-occlusive crisis of sickle cell disease: a case\-control study in Benin City](../publications/1de64f4e84821b9b74b6.md)

Babatunde Ishola Gabriel Adejumo; Nnagbo Nonso Udemezue; Margaret Oyarazi Adebowale; Usman Itakure Abdukaldir; Olayemi Feyisayo Aiyesoro; Nkechi Augustina Olise; Afolabi Adiru Adegboye; Angela Maria Chidera Obiajunwa; Olufunke Deborah Abolarin; Uteno Itanyi Drisu; Kenneth Echezona Ilekuba; Benson Benjamin Osayetin Ebhohimhen; Andre Julin\-Paulidor Kamdem; Prasad Babu Dasari; Abdulhameed Aliu

Integrated evidence on haematological, inflammatory, and endothelial biomarker profiles across clinically distinct sickle cell disease \(SCD\) states remains limited in African populations\. This study evaluated these biomarkers among individuals with steady\-state SCD, vaso\-occlusive crisis \(VOC\), and healthy controls in Benin City, Nigeria\. This case\-control study included 89 participants: 20 with steady\-state SCD, 32 presenting with VOC, and 37 healthy controls\. Haematological parameters, complete blood count\-derived inflammatory indices, C\-reactive protein \(CRP\), interleukin\-6 \(IL\-6\), and soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule\-1 \(sVCAM\-1\) were assessed\. Between\-group differences and the within\-cohort discrimination of VOC from steady\-state SCD were evaluated using conventional and exploratory multivariable approaches\. Participants with VOC showed greater haematological abnormalities and inflammatory and endothelial activation than those in steady state\. Among individual markers, NLR, CRP, IL\-6, and sVCAM\-1 showed comparatively strong within\-cohort discrimination of VOC status, with AUCs of 0\.816, 0\.857, 0\.882, and 0\.901, respectively\. An integrated biomarker model yielded an AUC of 0\.938, although performance was estimated within the same modest SCD cohort\. Inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers differed across SCD clinical states and showed potential as adjunctive markers of disease activity\. Larger prospective studies accounting for treatment exposure and providing independent validation are required before clinical application\.

## [HiPredict: Predicting the missing HiRISE RED4 spectral channel with machine learning](../publications/1de9a21806540c0dfa55.md)

Ardan Suphi; Ben Moseley; Gareth S Collins; Valentin T Bickel; Vidhya G Rangarajan

The High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment \(HiRISE\) onboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter \(MRO\) acquires imagery of Mars at 25\-\-30 cm/pixel, supporting studies of martian geology, climate history, and landing\-site characterization\. Its 14\-detector focal plane assembly includes several overlapping detectors that enable the acquisition of three\-channel colour\-infrared images, which are important for identifying compositional variations and studying active surface processes\. In 2023, a detector in the center of the focal plane assembly \(RED4\) began failing intermittently, creating a gap in acquired imagery and reducing the instrument&\#x27;s colour\-imaging capability by half\. The HiRISE processing pipeline provides a synthetic red \(SYN4\) channel obtained by linearly scaling the co\-located infrared \(IR10\) channel\. However, this approach cannot capture observed non\-linear relationships between the colour channels, limiting its accuracy and applicability\. Here, we present HiPredict, a machine\-learning framework that reconstructs RED4 from co\-located IR10 and blue\-green \(BG12\) imagery, neighbouring red\-channel observations, and acquisition metadata\. The model employs a U\-Net architecture to learn non\-linear spatiotemporal\-spectral relationships between these inputs and is trained on 81,717 training samples, representing 13,625 observations\. Evaluated on 23,348 test samples, representing 3,892 pre\-failure observations, HiPredict reconstructs RED4 with a Normalised Mean Absolute Error of 1\.1%, substantially outperforming SYN4 \(3\.1%\)\. The reconstructed products improve colour image recovery and more closely represent features of interest such as icy craters, stratigraphy exposed along ridge crests and chloride deposits\. We release HiPredict as an open software tool\. This work demonstrates the potential of machine learning to mitigate data loss as planetary missions age and naturally degrade\.

## [Prism\-1: Position\- and Rival\-Independent Scoring for System One Models](../publications/1e0f67c054943857f044.md)

Yao Long Teng; Jianguo Huang; Jiayi Cai; Yanchen Deng; Bo An

Given a state and a set of options, such as intents, tools or interface elements, System One decision models return a distribution over the options in one forward pass, without generated reasoning\. Web systems increasingly build them by reading decisions from language models\. Two axioms of rational choice are natural requirements for such decisions, because in web systems the listing and the option set are determined by other components and can change or be manipulated: the order in which the options are listed should not matter, and adding an option should not change the relative odds of the others \(Luce&\#x27;s choice axiom\)\. We test the standard reads, namely single\-choice question \(SCQ\) prompting, with shuffled\-order training, order averaging or sorted options, and invariant set architectures, and find that each violates at least one axiom: one shuffle changes 12\-20% of SCQ answers, sorting only freezes an arbitrary convention, and a well\-chosen added option steers 4\-34% of decisions\. By Luce&\#x27;s theorem, a read satisfies both axioms only if it is a softmax over scores that each depend on one option alone, so in a transformer they hold by construction only if no token that scores an option sees another\. We implement this as Prism\-1 \(Position\- and Rival\-Independent Scoring for System One Models\): every option is read in its own block at shared positions, with the model&\#x27;s usual left\-to\-right attention, in one forward pass\. On five benchmark sets with Qwen3\-8B and Gemma 4 12B, SCQ prompting trained on the same data still changes 7% of its answers under one shuffle, and an added irrelevant option steers 12% of its decisions\. Prism\-1 stays within one point of that baseline&\#x27;s accuracy and is 2\-4 points more accurate once only answers that survive a reordering are counted, while no shuffle changes any of its answers and no added irrelevant option moves its choice among the others\.

## [PREVALÊNCIA DE ANSIEDADE EM ADULTOS ATENDIDOS NA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA À SAÚDE](../publications/1e1aaecb231ee3606364.md)

Natan Zanella; Ivana Loraine Lindemann; Gustavo Olszanski Acrani

Os transtornos de ansiedade constituem importante problema de saúde pública e representam uma das principais causas de incapacidade\. Este estudo objetivou estimar a prevalência de ansiedade e avaliar sua associação com características sociodemográficas, comportamentais e condições de saúde em adultos atendidos na Atenção Primária à Saúde \(APS\)\. Trata\-se de um estudo epidemiológico transversal realizado com 908 indivíduos de 20 a 59 anos atendidos nas unidades urbanas da APS de Passo Fundo, Rio Grande do Sul, entre julho e dezembro de 2025\. O desfecho foi definido pelo diagnóstico médico autorreferido de ansiedade, e as associações foram avaliadas pelos testes do qui\-quadrado de Pearson ou exato de Fisher\. A prevalência de ansiedade foi de 54,8% \(IC95 52–58\), sendo significativamente maior entre mulheres, indivíduos com depressão, em acompanhamento psicológico ou psiquiátrico, portadores de multimorbidades, usuários de medicação contínua e pessoas com obesidade \(p&lt;0,001\)\. A prevalência observada foi superior à descrita em estudos populacionais, possivelmente em razão do perfil da amostra, composta predominantemente por adultos em idade economicamente ativa e com doenças crônicas\. Os achados evidenciam a ansiedade como importante problema de saúde na APS e reforçam a necessidade de rastreamento, diagnóstico precoce e acompanhamento longitudinal para qualificar a assistência em saúde mental\.

## [ANÁLISIS MULTIVARIADO DE EMULSIONES AGUA\-CBD EMPLEANDO TENSOACTIVOS DE GRADO COSMÉTICO](../publications/1e20a0ab0428c9ca344e.md)

Hugo Solis Garcia; Ricardo A\. Valdez; Andrés de la Rosa Martínez; Stalin Suntaxi Crisanto; Alba Cabrera Torres; Vinicio Ramiro Benalcázar\-Rojas

Los tónicos faciales a base de cannabidiol \(CBD\) han ganado popularidad en la industria cosmética por sus propiedades antiinflamatorias, antioxidantes y calmantes, el uso de tensoactivos es fundamental, ya que estabilizan la emulsión y favorecen la dispersión del CBD mejorando su absorción cutánea al facilitar la penetración del compuesto a través de la matriz acuosa\. Esta investigación evaluó emulsiones de CBD en agua para tres tipos de productos cosméticos: agua micelar \(MW\), agua de rosas \(RW\) y tónico facial \(FT\), utilizando tres tensoactivos: SA1 \(Tween 20\), SA2 \(lecitina natural\) y SA3 \(Tween 80\), en diferentes concentraciones y temperaturas\. Se realizaron mediciones cuantitativas para determinar la viscosidad y cambios de pH, también mediciones cualitativas para la coloración como son los indicadores de degradación en las emulsiones\. El análisis estadístico incluyó métodos exploratorios, descriptivos e inferenciales, también se empleó el análisis de correspondencias múltiples para identificar asociaciones entre categorías\. Adicionalmente, se desarrolló modelos para la predicción del pH utilizando técnicas estadísticas y de aprendizaje automático\. Se demostró que la emulsión del tónico facial mostró mayor estabilidad en las 14 semanas de almacenamiento, y no presentó signos de degradación en el rango de temperatura evaluado\. La formulación mediante el uso de los tensoactivos SA1 y SA3 se consideró la más adecuada para uso cosmético\. El modelo de predicción más adecuado fue la regresión lineal múltiple, con un R² de 0\.7045 y un error cuadrático medio de 0\.1786\. El presente estudio aportó criterios técnicos para el desarrollo de formulaciones cosméticas con CBD\.

## [Pandemic Preparedness and Public Health Policy Reform in the 21st Century](../publications/1e312c3f6aebc1e8d865.md)



Background: The Public Health, Government, community, and Economy are challenged during times of Pandemics\.The crises in the last few years have exhibited the necessity for a strong surveillance system of illness outbreaks, efficient public contacts, a sound health care system, technological advancement and good evidencebased public health policies\.The gains of pandemic preparedness need to be more coordinated institutional change and trust, civic engagement/cooperation with other countries\.Objective: We aimed to understand the public opinion on pandemic preparedness and the necessity for 21st\-century public health policies\.It also explored the interconnections of all of these aspects of healthcare preparedness, disease surveillance, healthcare communication, government leadership, policy reform, community engagement, technology, international cooperation and the effectiveness of overall pandemic response\. Methods:The type of research design applied was quantitative \-cross\-sectional\.A series of data collection instruments was used in data collection, including a structured questionnaire made up of 62 items in 5 point likert scale, together with five open\-ended questions, including demographic questions; of which 310 respondents were used\.The statistical analysis of the data used was descriptive statistics, normality analysis, Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha test, Kaiser\-Meyer\-Olkin test, Bartlett&\#x27;s Test of Sphericity, independent\-samples t\-test, one\-way ANOVA, Kruskal\-Wallis test, Chisquared test, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis\.The criterion of statistical significance used was a level of 0\.05\.Results: The reliability of the questionnaire was quite excellent, and the Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha was obtained as 0\.969\.Construct validity was supported by a KMO value of 0\.953 and a significant Bartlett&\#x27;s test, χ² \(1891\) = 13,595\.931,p &lt; 0\.001\.No significant differences were found between males and females or among the age groups after the pandemic, but significant differences were found among residents of various geographical areas and previous experience with a pandemic\.Each of the study constructs had positive and statistically significant relationships\.Overall Assessment had the highest correlation of r = \.581,p &lt; 0\.001, with Public Health Policy Reform\.The regression model was statistically significant, F \(4,305\) = 99\.058,p &lt; 0\.001, with an R² of 56\.5% explaining the overall variance of the model\.Positive significant factors were: Public Health Communication, Policy Reform, Pandemic Preparedness and Technology and Innovation\. Conclusion:The results show that community engagement and collaboration globally, having the hospitals ready, investments in technology, communication with all stakeholders and multiple changes in the public health system are all part of what became a successful response to the pandemic\.Governments have a responsibility to hear and pay heed to lessons learned in their policies, ensure equitable resource allocation so no one is forgotten, enhance surveillance and prepare now for epidemics\.

## [24\-Hour Movement Behavior Reallocations and Glycemic Variability in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Longitudinal Isotemporal Substitution Analysis](../publications/1e3212fe55df631924e3.md)

Pei Chen; Bingqian Zhu; Chang Park; Mia Cajita; Minsun Park; Lisa K\. Sharp; Cynthia Fritschi; Ali Çınar; Laurie Quinn

Background: Glycemic variability \(GV\) is an important cardiometabolic risk marker in adults with type 1 diabetes \(T1D\)\. We estimated the effects of reallocating time among sleep, sedentary behavior, light physical activity \(LPA\), and moderate\-to\-vigorous physical activity \(MVPA\) on six GV outcomes in adults with T1D\. Methods: This secondary analysis included 23 adults contributing 102 days with concurrent accelerometer\-based activity monitoring and continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\)\. Compositional rescaling was applied to ensure a 24\-h in total\. Isotemporal substitution models with linear mixed\-effects regression were used to estimate associations of 30\-min reallocations among behaviors \(e\.g\., from sleep to LPA\) with GV outcomes, including standard deviation of glucose \(SD\), coefficient of variation \(CV\), large amplitude of glycemic excursions \(LAGE\), mean amplitude of glycemic excursions \(MAGE\), continuous overlapping net glycemic action with a 60\-min lag \(CONGA\-60\), and time in range \(TIR\), while adjusting for covariates\. Results: Participants had a mean age of 32\.6 years, BMI of 28\.2 kg/m 2 , and diabetes duration of 16\.3 years\. Reallocating 0\.5 hours from sleep to sedentary time, LPA, or MVPA significantly reduced CV \(estimate range: −14\.4 to −15\.2, all p &lt; 0\.05\) and TIR \(estimate range: −3\.6 to −3\.6, all p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Replacing sedentary time with LPA significantly reduced LAGE \(estimate = −3\.4, p = 0\.035\)\. No significant associations were found for SD, MAGE, or CONGA\-60\. Conclusion: These findings highlight that optimizing glycemic stability in adults with T1D requires a nuanced consideration of how reallocations between sleep, sedentary time, LPA, and MVPA differentially affect GV, TIR, and LAGE\.

## [Microcontroller\-Based Automated Drug Infusion and Monitoring System for Critical Care](../publications/1e37aa6a027fc0c7ea0f.md)



In critical care, the accurate delivery of drugs through vias is absolutely essential \-failure to set the right occlusion time or to accurately recognise the period may generate a serious threat if the flow isn&\#x27;t completely released and is not delivered correctly, or if there is a programming error\.This mini project is an Automatic infusion and automatic monitoring system using microcontroller which can be used as an academic prototype/single channel syringe\-pump system\.The clinician enters in a volume, concentration, a rate and volume to be infused, a safety controller validates the parameters entered by the clinician by comparing the parameters with the clinician&\#x27;s database of programmable drugs, and a stepper motor actuator is then enabled to work\.All inputs \-such as pressure, syringe position, delivered\-volume, door, air\-in\-line and battery and optional physiological\-monitor inputs \-are sampled continuously\.The embedded software features deterministic state machine, independent watchdog supervision, alarm latching, alarm/event logging and fail\-safe motor shutdown\.This programmed flow rate as a function of motor displacement is mathematically modeled, and volume being provided is calculated\.These techniques will be validated in a usability review and calibration will be performed at the various flows, fault injection, power outage recovery and plausibility check of the sensors\.This sample simulation was performed and a mean absolute flow error of less than 2 percent, for four nominal test flow rates, was achieved as well as all critical fault injections directed to a safe state\.The values are provided for interesting purposes only and for demonstration of the project and are not to be interpreted as clinical value statements\.The work focuses on the fact that although automation can help reduce repetitive programming and increase traceability, it can be utilized in conjunction with, but not as a replacement for, prescription verification, expert clinical judgment, formal risk management, electrical\-safety testing, software validation and regulatory clearance\.

## [Competition and Diversity in Generative AI](../publications/1e3d2ce9a125a9e5aed1.md)

Manish Raghavan

Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced\. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? Our work begins with a simple observation: content producers do not act in isolation\. Instead, they compete with one another \(e\.g\., for customers or attention\)\. We explore the impact competition has on both content diversity and overall social welfare when producers use generative AI\. Through a formal game\-theoretic model, we show that competitive markets select for diverse AI models, mitigating monoculture\. We further show that a generative AI model that performs well in isolation \(i\.e\., according to a benchmark\) may fail to provide value in a competitive market\. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating generative AI models across the breadth of their output distributions, particularly when they will be deployed in competitive environments\. We validate our theoretical results with a series of experiments involving generative text and image models\. Overall, our results suggest that homogenization due to generative AI is unlikely to persist under strong competition\. This paper was accepted by Itai Ashlagi, market design, platform, and demand analytics\. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi\.org/10\.1287/mnsc\.2025\.02761 \.

## [Effectiveness of Implementing Blended Learning Model with SMART BADMINTON ZR Application in Badminton Learning in Physical Education](../publications/1e3ffe1da96d053e9e42.md)



This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of implementing a blended learning model using the SMART BADMINTON ZR application on improving student performance in basic serving and smashing techniques in badminton courses\.Method: This study used a quasi\-experimental design with a pretest\-posttest control group\.A total of 64 Physical Education students from Dharmas Indonesia University participated and were divided into an experimental group \(n=32\) that used the blended learning model based on the SMART BADMINTON ZR application, and a control group \(n=32\) that used conventional face\-to\-face learning methods\.The intervention was carried out over 16 meetings\.Student performance was measured using a serve and smash technique test with a 1\-4 scale process\-work rubric\.Data were analyzed using paired\-samples t\-test and independent\-samples t\-test with a significance level of α = 0\.05\.Results: The results showed a significant improvement in both skills \(serve and smash\) in the experimental group compared to the control group \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\.The experimental group showed an average posttest score of 45\.88, higher than the control group with an average of 40\.78\.Conclusion: The integration of technology through a blended learning model with the SMART BADMINTON ZR application has been proven effective in improving students&\#x27; understanding, motor performance, and engagement in sports learning\.Flexibility in independent learning, better visualization of techniques, quick feedback, and increased motivation are key factors in the success of this approach\.

## [An interventional study on enhancing print awareness in senior kindergarten children through gamified picture book teaching](../publications/1e47b2f396162f0e2375.md)

Jun Zhang; Jiakuo Liu; Yaoyao Xu; Shangqing Yuan; Tie Sun; Deqiang Wang

Print awareness, encompassing children&\#x27;s understanding of the functional, formal, and rule\-based aspects of written language, is a critical precursor to early literacy\. Despite growing interest in picture\-book interventions, few studies have systematically examined classroom\-based gamified approaches to enhancing print awareness among Chinese kindergarten children\. This study investigated the effects of a six\-week gamified picture book intervention on print awareness within the Chinese logographic writing system\. Fifty senior kindergarten children \(aged 5–6 years\) from two intact classes in an urban kindergarten in China participated in the study\. Using cluster randomization at the classroom level, one class was assigned to the experimental group \( n = 25\) and the other to the control group \( n = 25\)\. Children in the experimental group participated in weekly gamified picture\-book activities, whereas those in the control group received regular picture\-book instruction\. Print awareness was assessed before and after the intervention across three dimensions: Print Function, Print Form, and Print Rules\. Mixed ANOVA revealed significant main effects of Time for all three dimensions, indicating that children in both groups improved from pre\-test to post\-test\. Significant main effects of Group were observed for Print Function, F\(1, 48\) = 4\.68, p = 0\.033, η p 2 = 0\.04, and Print Form, F\(1, 48\) = 4\.32, p = 0\.040, η p 2 = 0\.04, with the experimental group showing higher overall scores than the control group\. No significant group difference was found for Print Rules, and no significant Time × Group interactions were observed for any dimension\. These findings suggest that gamified picture\-book teaching may provide additional support for children&\#x27;s Print Function and Print Form awareness, while the observed improvements over time likely reflect general developmental progress rather than accelerated growth resulting from the intervention\. The study highlights that different dimensions of print awareness may respond differently to classroom instruction and provides practical implications for designing developmentally appropriate, gamified early literacy activities within Chinese kindergarten settings\.

## [‘Bringing natural behaviour into the laboratory’: international networks, aggression research, and Czechoslovak psychopharmacology in the 1970s](../publications/1e4e8009430f4c77f487.md)

Jakub Střelec

This article explores the development of ethological research on aggression in late socialist Czechoslovakia, focusing on the work of pharmacologist Miloslav Kršiak \(1939\-2016\) at the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences\. Drawing on archival records, personal correspondence, and institutional sources, it examines Kršiak&\#x27;s international networks and shows how he sustained collaborations with colleagues abroad, as well as the strategies he adopted to navigate the political setting of the Normalization period\. The study also demonstrates how ethological approaches were adapted to meet state socialist research priorities, particularly in the study of addiction to over\-the\-counter analgesics\. It suggests that, although pharmacological research on aggression drew on a shared transnational repertoire of methods, its development and uses were shaped by the political structures, institutional routines, and public health priorities of late state socialism\. By tracing both transnational exchange and local adaptation, the article contributes to a more differentiated history of Cold War science and to a broader understanding of how biological approaches to aggressive behaviour took shape in different post\-war settings\.

## [Establishing Diagnosis Models for Autism Spectrum Disorder With Auditory Brainstem Response Using Machine Learning Methods](../publications/1e4f47abff668c5f3a87.md)

Chunmei Ren; Qingjie Zhang; Xianrong Liang; Guojun Yun; Kanglong Peng

This study aimed to develop and validate models built using machine learning methods for the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\)\. A total of 851 children with suspected ASD were enrolled\. Related features were acquired using the Autism Behavior Checklist and Auditory Brainstem Response \(ABR\) outcomes\. The Shapley additive explanation \(SHAP\) values were used to explain the feature impact used in the models with the best performance\. In addition, different methods were used to depict group differences\. Our study found that significant results in ABR outcomes among children with different phenotypes mainly depend on stimulation intensity\. The predominant finding is that signal conduction from the cochlear nerve to the inferior colliculus in children with ASD may be associated with autistic behaviors in a way that displays region\-specific \(e\.g\., cochlear nerve, olivary\) and intensity\-dependent \(e\.g\., 45, 65 dB\) complexity\. The XGBoost models outperformed the other candidates, with the highest prediction accuracy \(85\.9%\) and AUROC \(0\.779\)\. Wave III and V were identified as the features with largest impact\. These findings highlight atypical ABR patterns in ASD and their association with autistic behaviors, contributing to the growing literature on understanding alterations in bioelectrical performance in children with ASD\.

## [The Hasse Principle Analogy in Physics\-Informed Machine Learning: From Local Failure to Global Success via Adaptive Normalization and Multi\-Task Learning](../publications/1e54f629025f0fed586c.md)

MOHAMMED TAHAR SAIM

We investigate an analogy between the Hasse Principle from arithmetic geometry and transfer learning in physics\-informed machine learning\. Using five topological insulator models \(SSH, Haldane, Kane\-Mele, BHZ, and Weyl\), we train models on 3,000 synthetic samples and examine cross\-model transfer\. FINDINGS:\(1\) Global\-to\-Local transfer \(restriction\) outperforms Local\-to\-Global transfer \(lifting\), with F1 scores of 0\.70 vs\. 0\.62\.\(2\) An adaptive normalization scheme improves Global\-to\-Local transfer from F1 = 0\.70 to 0\.92\.\(3\) Multi\-Task Learning with a model\-type auxiliary task achieves F1 = 0\.99 across all models\. CAUTION:The connection to the Hasse Principle is HEURISTIC, not a formal mathematical equivalence\. The observed asymmetry is consistent with a statistical interpretation \(distribution shift\); its resemblance to arithmetic obstructions remains a suggestive but UNPROVEN analogy\. This work is a starting point for interdisciplinary investigation, not an established mathematical bridge\.

## [Urolithin A pretreatment protects against seizures through IGF\-1R Tyr1166/1167 phosphorylation inhibition and enhances the antiseizure effect of valproic acid](../publications/1e60d11e8e10e4e02459.md)

Ming Li; Jiabin Zong; Yu Zhang; Minghua Zou; Fu Lu; Songqing Pan; Lily Zhang; Liu Yang; Heyang Qin; Zhouhua Li; Haiyan Wen; Wanbin Huang; 肖哲曼

Abstract Urolithin A \(UA\), a metabolite derived from gut microbiota that originates from ellagitannins found in pomegranate, berries, and walnuts, has emerged as a promising postbiotic exhibiting mitophagy\-inducing and neuroprotective properties\. This study examined the antiseizure effects of UA pretreatment and its potential to enhance the efficacy of valproic acid \(VPA\), a first\-line antiseizure medication, using a pilocarpine\-induced status epilepticus \(SE\) rat model\. UA significantly reduced seizure stage, prolonged latency, shortened duration, and decreased incidence of seizures, while alleviating SE\-induced behavioral and cognitive impairments\. Network pharmacology revealed insulin\-like growth factor 1 receptor \(IGF\-1R\) as a critical target of UA\. Subsequent experiments demonstrated that UA exerts its therapeutic effects by inhibiting the phosphorylation of IGF\-1R\. Importantly, the combination of UA and VPA yielded enhanced antiseizure effects compared to either treatment alone in mitigating seizures and behavioral comorbidities\. These findings suggest that UA may serve as a valuable adjuvant to conventional antiseizure therapy\. Additionally, this study elucidates the antiseizure potential of UA as a pomegranate\-derived postbiotic, providing experimental evidence from an animal model to support a UA\-VPA combination strategy aimed at improving the efficacy of epilepsy treatment\.

## [Where&\#x27;s the Indirect Evidence? Investigating Grammatical Generalization with Influence Functions](../publications/1e6506045c75cc0bc236.md)

William Dai; Zhenghao Herbert Zhou; Maya Viswanathan; Robert Frank

Language models generalize beyond their training corpus to learn linguistic phenomena \(Patil et al\., 2024; Misra and Mahowald, 2024\), showing that there exists indirect evidence driving learning\. Prior work has inferred that indirect evidence exists without identifying its character or considered specific hypotheses about what it might be\. We explore an alternative bottom\-up method for identifying indirect evidence\. We use influence functions \(Koh and Liang, 2017\) to measure how individual training sentences affect model predictions in 15 grammatical phenomena from BLiMP \(Warstadt et al\., 2020\)\. We filter out a phenomenon&\#x27;s direct evidence using hand\-constructed rules and take the 60,000 most influential remaining sentences as indirect evidence\. This indirect evidence substantially affects learning: retraining without it lowers held\-out accuracy more than removing a matched random group for every phenomenon across five models \(by a median of 12 points\)\. We characterize the indirect evidence by its similarity to our direct evidence filters: it \(partially\) meets the filters&\#x27; structural conditions at a median of 4\.7 times the rate of a matched random group\. Finally, clustering phenomena by indirect\-evidence overlap recovers three of the five BLiMP categories that include multiple phenomena, suggesting that this method can reveal linguistic relationships\.

## [A metadata deduplication framework associated with metadata placement and retrieval in edge\-cloud using Adaptive Capsule Neural Network \(A\-CNet\)](../publications/1e74bd455f8e55cd6c11.md)

Radha V; R\. Anitha

With the rapid digitization and smart industrial systems, the volume of metadata stored in the edge\-cloud has grown exponentially\. Factors such as global connectivity and seamless access to information have further accelerated this growth\. At the same time, many organizations collect and process vast amounts of data from multiple sources\. Meanwhile, this growth leads to an increase in data redundancy, especially in edge\-cloud storage that impacts data storage and analysis\. For minimizing the duplicate metadata in edge\-cloud, the proposed model employs a machine learning\-based metadata deduplication technique\. In this research study, a new metadata deduplication mechanism in the edge\-cloud using machine learning is developed to eliminate duplicate metadata\. At first, the metadata deduplication is done in the edge\-cloud by the Adaptive Capsule Neural Network \(A\-CNet\) model\. The performance of this network is enhanced using the Improved Black\-Winged Kite Algorithm \(IBKA\) that fine\-tunes the relevant parameters\. Another major challenge faced by geographically distributed edge\-cloud storage systems is existing metadata placement methods often lead to high latency and increased security risks during data transmission and data access\. To address this issue, the optimal metadata placement in the edge device is done by the developed IBKA\. Before placing the metadata, the encryption process is performed using Elliptic Curve Cryptography \(ECC\) to protect the metadata from unauthorized access\. The data location is identified, and the corresponding metadata is stored on an edge server associated with the node that is closest to the data’s virtual location in the spatial domain\. The objective function, namely Euclidean distance between nodes is considered during metadata placement\. Then, the data retrieval process is done by the Data Retrieval Protocol \(DRP\) approach, which helps in extracting the essential information based on the user query\. Finally, the retrieved metadata is decrypted using the ECC algorithm\. The overall performance of the developed method is evaluated with other techniques and encryption methods to validate its efficacy\.

## [Study on microgrid \- strength parameters of the soil\-geosynthetic interface based on direct shear tests](../publications/1e77e55477b79269d444.md)

Thiago de Sá Sena; Ana Karine Santiago Bessa; Anderson Borghetti Soares; Marcos Fábio Porto de Aguiar

Soil reinforcements positively influence the mechanical behavior of soil by inserting external elements, such as geosynthetics, which improve strength and reduce deformability of the composite\. Over the years, new geosynthetics have been developed and upgraded\. In the last decade or so, microgrids have emerged as an appropriate choice for strengthening and separating soil layers\. This research aimed to evaluate the strength parameters of the soil‒microgrid interface using direct shear tests under different testing conditions and to compare the results with those for other geosynthetics \(geomembrane and geotextile\)\. The support base type \(rigid and soil\) for the geosynthetics was varied in the direct shear tests\. When a soil base was used beneath the microgrid, performance was more efficient than with a rigid wooden base due to the higher soil friction angle\. The results for all soil–geosynthetic interface strength parameters obtained using the rigid base indicated that the microgrid exhibited higher strength than the geomembrane and comparable strength to the geotextile, though slightly lower\.

Сайфуллаева Венера Ниматжоновна

In the realm of information security, artificial intelligence is utilized not only for real\-time operations, attack prediction, threat prevention, and the automation of authentication processes but also serves as a primary tool for cybercriminals\. The development of artificial intelligence has significantly altered the information security landscape; the use of AI for international criminal purposes such as deepfake\-enabled fraud, online human trafficking, blackmail and extortion, cracking encrypted passwords via malware, orchestrating virtual attacks through automated hacking, cyberterrorism, phishing, and more is rapidly expanding, creating an urgent need to strengthen information security measures\. ## [Effect of Mirror Therapy Combined with Conventional Physiotherapy on Upper Limb Motor Recovery in Individuals with Stroke](../publications/1e8a78b170ca343f6052.md)



Background: Stroke is the main cause of long\-term disability, which affects mainly the upper limb and results in motor impairment and limits independence in daily activities\.Mirror therapy uses visual feedback to facilitate motor recovery through neuroplastic changes\.Which is a simple and cost\-effective rehabilitation approach; because of this, it has gained attention in treatment therapy\.Objective: To determine the effectiveness of mirror therapy in improving upper limb motor function in individuals with stroke when used along with conventional physiotherapy\. Methods:A pre\-and post\-interventional study was conducted on 30 individuals with subacute and chronic stroke presenting with upper limb motor impairment\.Mirror therapy in addition to conventional physiotherapy was given to participants for 12 weeks \(30 minutes per session, five sessions per week\)\.Motor recovery and functional performance both before and after the intervention were assessed using the Fugl\-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity \(FMA\-UE\) and the Action Research Arm Test \(ARAT\)\.The paired t\-test was used for statistical analysis, and the significance level was set at p &lt; 0\.05\. Results:Both outcome measures showed statistically significant improvements following the treatment\.The mean FMA\-UE score increased from 28\.6 ± 5\.4 to 42\.1 ± 4\.9 \(p &lt; 0\.001\), which indicates enhanced motor recovery\.Similarly, Action Research Arm scores improved from 19\.8 ± 4\.3 to 33\.5 ± 5\.1 \(p &lt; 0\.001\), resulting in better functional use of the affected upper limb\. Conclusion:It was observed that mirror therapy, along with conventional physiotherapy when given in upper limb motor impairment after stroke is effective and a good practical intervention for improvement\.It is suitable for both clinical and home\-based rehabilitation because of simplicity and low cost\.Further studies with larger samples and controlled designs are needed to strengthen the evidence\.

## [Integration of Generative AI in the Recruitment ProcessCost Efficiency vs\. Algorithmic Bias Risks in Tech](../publications/1e93ca95dea63af51fc0.md)

Rois Rois; Beny T\. Ritto; Sofyan Solissa; Saskia Fugida

The adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) and Large Language Models \(LLMs\) in Human Resource Management \(HRM\), particularly within recruitment and talent acquisition, has accelerated rapidly across global and national technology companies\. This study critically analyzes the dialectic between the cost efficiency and process efficiency offered by GenAI versus the risks of algorithmic bias, transparency hurdles, data privacy vulnerabilities, and fairness in candidate evaluation\. Utilizing a Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) methodology guided by PRISMA standards across 23 peer\-reviewed academic studies and reputable reports published between 2022 and 2026, this paper reveals that GenAI integration such as LLM\-based semantic resume parsing, automated job description generation, and conversational chatbots can reduce time\-to\-hire by 40–60% and significantly lower operational hiring costs\. However, GenAI models remain vulnerable to reproducing historical bias, engaging in proxy discrimination, triggering candidate information hallucinations, and creating opaque decision\-making processes \(black\-box problem\)\. This article formulates an ethical governance framework grounded in Human\-in\-the\-Loop \(HITL\) oversight, regular algorithmic bias audits, data anonymization \(blind screening\), and Explainable AI \(XAI\) to ensure that operational speed does not compromise workforce diversity, equal opportunity, and workplace equity\.

## [Development of IoT Systems for Real–Time Assessment of Vibration Signals in a Generator](../publications/1e95c33fc75af8a17cc6.md)

Sylvester Chukwutem Onwusa, Oghenerukevwe Omovigho Prosper, Oderhowho Nyorere, Okoye, Peter Izuoba, Usikpedo Charles Olordo and Uyeri Oghenerobo Cyril

The assessment of vibration signals in automotive generators is crucial for ensuring operational efficiency, reliability and predictive maintenance\. Excessive vibrations can lead to mechanical failures, energy losses and reduced generator lifespan\. However, traditional vibration monitoring methods often rely on periodic manual inspections, which are time\-consuming, expensive and inefficient for real\-time diagnostics\. To address this issue, this study focuses on the development of an IoT\-based system for real\-time vibration signal assessment in automotive generators\. The methodology involves designing and implementing a wireless sensor network integrated with microcontrollers and accelerometers to capture vibration signals continuously\. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud\-based platform for real\-time processing and analysis using machine learning algorithms\. The system employs edge computing techniques to enhance data processing speed and reduce latency\. A prototype is tested in a controlled environment to evaluate its performance in detecting abnormal vibration patterns and predicting potential faults\. The justification for this study lies in the increasing demand for intelligent and automated monitoring solutions in modern automotive power systems\. By leveraging IoT technology, this research provides a cost\-effective, scalable, and efficient alternative to conventional vibration monitoring techniques, contributing to improved energy efficiency and reliability of generators\. The results demonstrate that the developed IoT system effectively detects and analyzes vibration anomalies in real time, enabling early fault detection and reducing maintenance costs\. In conclusion, the proposed system enhances the predictive maintenance capabilities of automotive generators, ensuring longer operational life and reduced downtime\. It was recommended that future research explore the integration of advanced artificial intelligence models for more accurate predictive analytics and the implementation of this system in real\-world automotive applications to validate its robustness and scalability\.

## [Lethe: Link Inference Attacks For Evaluation of Edge Unlearning Methods](../publications/1eabe7965cff30d85348.md)

Andrea D&\#x27;Angelo; Francesco Gullo; Davide Mottin; Sayan Ranu; Giovanni Stilo

Graph Unlearning \(GU\) aims to remove the influence of specific training data from a Graph Neural Network without retraining anew\. While most methods address removal of nodes and features, Edge Unlearning \(EU\), aiming at forgetting edges, has recently attracted dedicated attention as a standalone problem due to the hardness of completely removing the impact of an edge in the model\. Despite this, no dedicated benchmark for EU exists besides isolated evaluations on feature\-rich datasets such as Cora and Citeseer where GNNs exploit node features rather than graph structure\. As such, we show two systematic limitations in existing evaluations: dedicated EU methods can be slower than retraining anew, and accuracy metrics are uninformative due to the negligible impact of edge removal\. To address this gap, we introduce Lethe, the first comprehensive benchmark for Edge Unlearning, featuring 15 methods and 8 datasets\. Our benchmark emphasizes large graphs, introduces evaluation tasks of varying difficulty, and proposes empirical measures based on link inference attacks rather than proxy accuracy metrics\. We provide a comprehensive empirical analysis, demonstrate the shortcomings of current evaluations, and release Lethe as a reproducible, extensible benchmark\.

## [Pleasure, Pain, and Authenticity in Pornography](../publications/1eb9051bda1920850cc6.md)

Eran Shor

This book explores the role of positive emotions such as pleasure, affection, satisfaction, and the intersection of these emotions with pain and authenticity in today’s pornographic industry\. It offers surprising insights into the relationship between gender and pleasure\. Readers will be able to gain a better understanding of the role and historical development of positive emotions in mainstream pornographic videos and of pornography viewers’ attitudes and perspectives regarding these emotions\. These insights rely on a systematic content analysis of more than 600 mainstream online pornographic videos, as well as more than 300 in\-depth interviews with a diverse sample of frequent viewers of mainstream pornography\. The book is written primarily for scholars, including professors, graduate students, and advanced undergraduate students in the social sciences and humanities\. It will also be of interest to various non\-academic audiences, including feminist and religious activists, educators, parents, and pornography consumers\. The book is written in accessible language and avoids technicalities, making it approachable to these wider audiences\.

## [PM\-USHA International Conference Series – जञनसत \(Jñānasetu\): The Bridge of KnowledgeARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE FUTURE OF COMMERCE](../publications/1ed429cbab03dc8c38e7.md)

Krupa Bhatt; Sakshi Saxena

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is becoming an important force in the transformation of contemporary commerce\. Its applications now extend across marketing, retail, e\-commerce, customer service, forecasting, decision support, supply chain management, and business operations\. This paper examines the role of AI in shaping the future of commerce by synthesising existing academic literature on AI\-enabled commercial transformation\. The study adopts a conceptual and descriptive approach based on a narrative review of peer\-reviewed secondary literature\. The review focuses on five interrelated themes: personalisation and consumer engagement, predictive decision\-making, intelligent automation, AI\-mediated customer experience, and responsible AI governance\. The synthesis indicates that AI is shifting commerce from standardised to increasingly personalised interactions, from reactive to predictive decision\-making, and from predominantly manual processes towards human\-AI collaboration\. These developments can improve efficiency, relevance, convenience, innovation, and competitiveness\. At the same time, expanded use of consumer data and algorithmic decision\-making creates significant concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accountability, consumer autonomy, and workforce transformation\. The paper argues that technological capability alone is insufficient to create sustainable commercial value\. The future of commerce is likely to depend on the ability of organisations to combine AI capabilities with human judgement, consumer trust, ethical governance, and sustainability considerations\. A conceptual framework is proposed in which AI\-enabled capabilities influence commerce transformation and commercial outcomes, while responsible governance acts as a critical enabling condition\. The paper concludes that competitive advantage in an AI\-enabled economy will depend not merely on the speed of AI adoption, but on how effectively and responsibly organisations integrate AI into commercial systems and stakeholder relationships\.

## [Deterministic Bounds on Accuracy and Stability of Metric\-Space Regression and Classification](../publications/1ed738b414fe4e1867bf.md)

Nina Maria Gottschling; Jakob Gawlikowski; Michele Caprio

Data\-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data\. While best\-fit machine learning methods can accommodate such noise through uncertainty estimates, they are prone to overfitting and it is challenging to quantify ambiguity of the relation between inputs and targets\. We introduce a geometric framework that quantifies this ambiguity through the average kernel size, computed with data\-dependent, i\.e\. model\-independent, feasible sets derived from worst\-case input and target noise\. The framework provides computable, deterministic, non\-asymptotic bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy for a finite, constructed dataset, independent of the predictive model class, and applies to regression and classification with pseudo\-metric input spaces and metric target spaces\. The ambiguity of the input\-target relation implies three consequences: an empirical error floor, an accuracy\-stability trade\-off, and, under standard probabilistic assumptions, a strictly positive distribution\-training error gap when training below the accuracy bounds\. Under standard Borel assumptions for Euclidean norms, the distributional analogue of the average kernel size is related to Bayes risk as it reduces to the optimal distribution root\-mean\-squared error times the square root of two\. Experiments spanning tabular regression, image regression and classification datasets yield nontrivial bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy on a constructed dataset, alongside descriptive comparisons with model performance on the original datasets\. The bounds provide a computable, model\-independent reference scale on the constructed dataset and comparisons with model performance on the original dataset are descriptive\.

## [DeepHopping\-LTE: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Adaptive Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum \(FHSS\) in Dense 4G Cellular Networks](../publications/1ee366533b459a8bd2ca.md)

Nkechinyere Eyidia; Smiles Chiweikpe Obiajunwa

The rapid growth of mobile devices and dense 4G deployments has intensified interference and congestion, challenging network reliability, spectrum efficiency, and quality of service\. This study proposes DeepHopping\-LTE, a deep reinforcement learning\-based adaptive frequency hopping framework designed to dynamically optimize frequency selection in dense cellular networks\. By leveraging a deep Q\-network \(DQN\), the framework balances exploration and exploitation using an epsilon\-greedy policy, converging to optimal hopping sequences to minimize interference while maximizing throughput\. Simulations and field data from two urban locations demonstrated that DeepHopping\-LTE significantly outperforms traditional static FHSS and heuristic frequency hopping methods\. The framework achieved a stable signal\-to\-interference\-plus\-noise ratio \(SINR\) averaging 15–17 dB, compared to 5 dB for static methods, more than doubling spectrum efficiency to 5\.5 bits/s/Hz under high load conditions\. Packet delivery ratio also improved dramatically, ranging from 94% to 98%, while traditional FHSS averaged 75%, reflecting superior reliability and quality of service\. Throughput improvement ratios reached 1\.6 under peak user density, and interference reduction ranged from 40% to 70%, confirming effective mitigation of environmental noise\. Additionally, the adaptability index reached 0\.95, demonstrating near\-instantaneous response to dynamic network changes, whereas heuristic and static methods lagged at 0\.65 and 0\.15, respectively\. The results validate that reinforcement learning can transform frequency hopping from a static approach into an intelligent, adaptive solution capable of optimizing network performance in real\-time\. By continuously observing network states and selecting optimal channels, DeepHopping\-LTE not only mitigates interference but also enhances spectrum utilization, reliability, and user experience\. These findings provide a practical foundation for policy implementation in dense urban networks, supporting guidelines for adaptive frequency management, interference monitoring, and reinforcement learning deployment in 4G and future 5G environments\. In conclusion, DeepHopping\-LTE addresses the critical challenges of dense cellular networks, offering a scalable, intelligent, and resilient framework that surpasses traditional methods, enabling efficient and reliable communication in high\-density mobile ecosystems\.

## [Disrupted fear regulation in insomnia disorder revealed by arousal estimation from skin conductance](../publications/1ee4bb980768ecd96a95.md)

Tianyu Hwang; Saman Khazaei; Edward Franz Pace\-Schott; Ryan M\. Bottary; Rose T\. Faghih

Insomnia disorder \(ID\) is a common sleep\-wake disorder marked by persistent dissatisfaction with sleep quality or quantity\. Previous studies have shown that sleep plays a critical role in emotion regulation, particularly in fear extinction\. This study aims to characterize ID using estimates of the sympathetic arousal state derived from skin conductance \(SC\)\-based observations, and to compare two observation models: the marked point process \(MPP\) model and the MPP coupled with continuous \(MPP\+Cont\) model\. We utilize SC data from a fear conditioning and extinction procedure involving 24 individuals with ID and 24 good sleepers \(GS\)\. The SC measurements are deconvolved to extract autonomic nervous system \(ANS\) activations and the tonic component\. The MPP observation model uses only the extracted ANS activations, while the MPP\+Cont model incorporates both ANS activations and the tonic component\. Both models are employed to estimate the underlying arousal state over time and compute a high arousal index \(HAI\)\. We compare the estimated arousal states and HAI between the ID and GS groups to assess alterations in arousal associated with ID\. Our results reveal that ID may be associated with impaired fear extinction learning and recall\. Notably, the distinction between ID and GS emerges only under the MPP\+Cont model, indicating the critical role of the tonic component in arousal estimation\. Overall, this study highlights the potential of arousal state estimation for understanding autonomic dysregulation in ID, thereby supporting interventions for fear\-centered comorbidities and improving quality of life\.

## [Greening the Chain: Supplier Emission Reductions From Focal Firm Green Bonds](../publications/1ee5243a7069f315bfc9.md)

Zhiping Zhang; Yirui Zhang; FU Guang\-xin; Zhangxin Frank Liu; Sirimon Treepongkaruna

ABSTRACT Green bonds have emerged as a significant financial instrument for sustainable development\. Grounded in stakeholder theory, institutional theory, and signaling theory, this study contributes to the sustainable development literature by exploring how focal firms&\#x27; green bond issuance influences green supply chain sustainable governance\. Using 2132 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms during 2016–2023, the study employs a fixed‐effects model to examine the relationship between focal firms&\#x27; green bond issuance and supplier carbon emissions\. The empirical results indicate that focal firms&\#x27; green bond issuance reduces supplier carbon emissions, with supplier green innovation and analyst attention serving as two key mediating mechanisms\. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis reveals that this emission reduction effect is more pronounced for suppliers that are state‐owned, smaller, or operating in more competitive industries\. This study reveals the broader environmental governance effects of green bonds from the perspective of suppliers, providing practical implications for government green finance policy formulation and corporate supply chain decarbonization strategies\.

## [Darwin\-Claw: Environment\-Adaptive Experience Consolidation for Recursively Self\-Evolving Agents](../publications/1f052a558ea2479a339e.md)

Mingze Yin; Xiaohan Wang; Dian Li; Longfei Luo; Jiahong Yan; Yiheng Zhu; Chang\-Yu Hsieh

While Large Language Model \(LLM\) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across complex tasks, they predominantly operate in isolated sessions, lacking the ability to continually learn from historical interactions or adapt to user\-specific environments\. Existing self\-evolution paradigms often indiscriminately inject raw interaction trajectories into memory or skill modules, leading to obscured behavioral patterns and compromised update controllability\. Furthermore, as foundational LLM reasoning improves, the bottleneck for agentic evolution shifts from accumulating generic knowledge to effectively managing situational experience\. To address this, we propose Darwin\-Claw, an environment\-adaptive self\-evolving framework that systematically distills episodic experiences to drive the comprehensive evolution of operational skills and durable memory\. Theoretically grounded in an iterative agent\-actor and evolver\-critic co\-adaptation, Darwin\-Claw introduces a Hierarchical Experience Consolidation System that extracts fine\-grained error attributions and generalizes them into dynamically updated prototype vectors\. This structured situational experience serves as interaction patches for context\-sensitive perception and explicit optimization signals for skill refinement\. Practically, Darwin\-Claw is a readily deployable, automated framework compatible with mainstream agent systems without requiring manual curation\. Extensive experiments on WildClawBench demonstrate that Darwin\-Claw yields substantial performance improvements, establishing a controllable and stable pathway for the continual, user\-centric adaptation of autonomous agents in real\-world ecosystems\.

## [Autophagy\-lysosome pathway dysfunction in MASLD progression: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targets](../publications/1f22ba9168b5bd4d58cb.md)

Shuaibing Cao; Xinyue Cheng; Yi Yang; Baoping Lu; Shan Li; 黄春田; Mingyu Ba; Lei Luo; Changpu Zhao

Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide, yet no standardized pharmacotherapy has been approved for clinical use\. The autophagy–lysosome pathway \(ALP\) serves as an essential intracellular degradation and recycling machinery that sustains hepatic metabolic homeostasis via modulation of lipid turnover, mitochondrial quality surveillance, and hepatocellular detoxification\. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that ALP impairment acts as a core pathogenic factor across all stages of MASLD progression\. This review systematically elaborates the molecular framework of the ALP and its multifaceted physiological functions in the liver, with special attention to the central pathogenic mechanisms underlying ALP impairment in MASLD: lysosomal dysfunction, defective autophagosome–lysosome fusion, dysregulation of key transcriptional and epigenetic regulators, and impaired subtypes of selective autophagy\. ALP activity displays stage\-specific characteristics across MASLD progression, featuring compensatory activation in simple hepatic steatosis but functional suppression in metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatohepatitis \(MASH\)\. Hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells exert opposing autophagic activity during liver fibrogenesis\. We further summarize existing therapeutic strategies targeting the ALP, which fall into three categories: pharmacological agents \(ALP agonists, lysosomal modulators, natural bioactive compounds, and nano\-drug delivery systems\), non\-pharmacological interventions \(dietary adjustment, physical exercise, and lifestyle modification\), and gut–liver axis regulatory approaches\. Finally, we address the primary translational bottlenecks and prospective avenues for converting these mechanistic findings into viable clinical therapies\.

## [MEDICINA DE PRECISIÓN EN ENFERMEDADES CARDIOVASCULARES: INTEGRACIÓN DE BIOMARCADORES, DATOS CLÍNICOS E INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL PARA LA TOMA DE DECISIONES](../publications/1f27c3a455c111de798a.md)

Vanesa Paola Gallo Morales; Janina Gissela Pilco\-Díaz; Marco Vinicio Flores Blacio; Arnulfo Pazos Rodriguez

La medicina cardiológica de precisión intenta mejorar los enfoques basados en la población mediante la aplicación de biomarcadores multiómicos, datos clínicos y inteligencia artificial \(IA\)\. Recopilar y analizar sistemáticamente la evidencia disponible sobre modelos basados en inteligencia artificial que incorporen, como mínimo, dos de los siguientes factores: biomarcadores multiómicos, datos clínicos o imágenes cardiovasculares/fenotipos vasculares, aplicables a personas de edad adulta con enfermedad o riesgo cardiovascular\. Se realizó una búsqueda en PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science y ScienceDirect \(1 de enero de 2020\-31 de marzo de 2026\) de acuerdo con los criterios PRISMA 2020\. Se extrajo información sobre los estudios primarios incluidos que cumplían los criterios de inclusión, y se evaluaron su validez y los riesgos de sesgo utilizando PROBAST\+AI\. La certeza de la evidencia se evaluó utilizando el GRADE adaptado a los modelos pronósticos\. Se identificaron tres estudios que cumplían los criterios de inclusión\. El estudio «CardiOmicScore» \(Luo et al\., 2026\) informó de un C\-index para ProScore de entre 0,69 y 0,82, y para MetScore de entre 0,64 y 0,74 en la predicción de seis enfermedades cardiovasculares \(ECV\), y una ganancia de entre 0,005 y 0,102 al combinarse con datos clínicos\. El estudio «Queen of Hearts» \(Carvalho et al\., 2026\) obtuvo una AUC de 0,94 \(intervalo de confianza del 95 %: 0,92\-0,95\) en un registro retrospectivo multicéntrico de 1 032 pacientes para la detección de oclusión miocárdica \(OMI\)\. El modelo de predicción de ictus basado en imágenes de la retina \(Govindaiah et al\., 2025\) informó de una AUC de 0,83 para un ictus a los cinco años y de 0,79 a los diez años\. La certeza de la evidencia se clasificó como muy baja para todas las variables de resultado\. Existe escasez de estudios que utilicen criterios de inclusión ambiciosos\. La evidencia disponible no permite conclusiones definitivas sobre la eficacia del uso de la IA para mejorar la medicina de precisión cardiovascular\. Es necesario disponer de más información sobre la validación cruzada de estos modelos en poblaciones diferentes, incluida la evaluación de la calibración y los resultados centrados en el paciente\.

## [Blue Economy Development in ASEAN: Opportunities, Challenges, and Pathways Toward Ocean Sustainability](../publications/1f2aedaf99fbf4c56569.md)

Rogelio A\. Cruz; Maria Elena P\. Santos

The blue economy has emerged as a strategic framework for reconciling ocean\-based economic development with marine ecosystem conservation and social well\-being, particularly in maritime regions such as Southeast Asia\. As one of the world’s most ocean\-dependent regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations \(ASEAN\) possesses extensive marine resources that support fisheries, marine tourism, shipping, offshore energy, and emerging marine biotechnology industries\. This review critically synthesizes the development, governance, challenges, and future prospects of the blue economy across the ten ASEAN member states\. A total of 40 peer\-reviewed journal articles published between 2010 and 2024 were systematically reviewed and organized into four thematic areas: \(i\) the sectoral composition and economic contribution of blue economy activities; \(ii\) policy, institutional, and governance frameworks; \(iii\) environmental and socioeconomic constraints; and \(iv\) emerging pathways toward sustainable and inclusive ocean\-based development\. The synthesis indicates that ASEAN’s ocean\-based sectors collectively generate an estimated USD 360–380 billion annually, demonstrating their substantial contribution to regional economies\. However, their long\-term sustainability remains constrained by fragmented governance, marine ecosystem degradation, unsustainable resource exploitation, uneven institutional capacity, and inequitable distribution of economic benefits\. Significant differences among member states further highlight the need for context\-specific national strategies supported by stronger regional coordination\. Future blue economy development should prioritize integrated ocean governance, sustainable blue finance, technological innovation and transfer, ecosystem\-based management, and meaningful participation of coastal communities\. Strengthening these mechanisms would enable ASEAN to move beyond sector\-driven ocean exploitation toward a more resilient, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable blue economy while accelerating progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 14 \(SDG 14: Life Below Water\) and the broader 2030 Agenda\.

## [O&\#x27;ZBEK TILI MILLIY KORPUSIDA LINGVISTIK GESHTALTNI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH VA ULARNING KOGNITIV\-SEMANTIK ONTOLOGIYASINI YARATISH](../publications/1f2e012a5e9f7c8c9008.md)

Niyozova Gulhayo Erkinovna

Annotatsiya\. Ushbu maqolada O‘zbek tili milliy korpusi ma’lumotlari asosida lingvistik geshtaltlarni avtomatik aniqlash va ularning kognitiv\-semantik ontologiyasini yaratish usullari ko‘rib chiqiladi\. Tadqiqotda korpusdagi katta matnlar bazasidan statistik va kollokatsion ko‘rsatkichlar yordamida markaziy so‘zlar atrofidagi turg‘un birikmalar va iboralarni avtomatik ajratib olish algoritmi ishlab chiqilgan\. Shuningdek, ajratilgan geshtaltlarni sun’iy intellekt va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash tizimlari uchun bilimlarni rasmiylashtirish muhitida ontologik model ko‘rinishiga keltirish yo‘llari ko‘rsatilgan Kalit so‘zlar: lingvistik geshtalt, o‘zbek tili milliy korpusi, kognitiv\-semantik ontologiya, tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, kollokatsiya, semantik model\. Аннотация\. В данной статье рассматриваются методы автоматического извлечения лингвистических гештальтов и создания их когнитивно\-семантической онтологии на основе данных Национального корпуса узбекского языка\. В исследовании разработан алгоритм автоматического выделения устойчивых словосочетаний и фраз вокруг ключевых слов из больших текстовых массивов корпуса с использованием статистических и коллокационных показателей\. Также предложены способы представления выделенных гештальтов в виде онтологической модели в среде формализации знаний для систем искусственного интеллекта и обработки естественного языка\. Ключевые слова: лингвистический гештальт, Национальный корпус узбекского языка, когнитивно\-семантическая онтология, обработка естественного языка, коллокация, семантическая модель\. Abstract\. This article examines methods for automatically extracting linguistic gestalts and building their cognitive\-semantic ontology based on data from the Uzbek National Corpus\. The study presents an algorithm that utilizes statistical and collocational metrics to automatically extract stable collocations and phrases surrounding core words from large corpus text datasets\. Additionally, it demonstrates ways to represent the extracted gestalts as an ontological model within a knowledge formalization environment for artificial intelligence and Natural Language Processing systems\. Keywords: linguistic gestalt, Uzbek National Corpus, cognitive\-semantic ontology, Natural Language Processing, collocation, semantic model\.
