## [Familiarity and Liking in Classroom Networks: A Multilayer Analysis of Rated Peer Relations](../publications/1f3ed2c4976cf8294d4c.md)

Cheng\-Han Leng; Ulf Böckenholt

Many social network datasets consist of ordinal ratings exchanged among the same set of individuals on multiple relational dimensions\. Such data are common in educational and behavioral research but pose challenges due to ordinal measurement, asymmetric sender and receiver roles, and dependence within and across relations\. We analyze classroom network data from Taiwanese senior high schools, in which students provided ratings of familiarity and liking, to examine relational dimensionality, reciprocity, cross\-relational overlap, and individual characteristics\. To this end, we develop and apply a latent\-space rated\-network model that accounts for ordinal rating scales, sender and receiver heterogeneity, and higher\-order interaction structure\. The model allows familiarity and liking to be treated either as a single relational dimension or as distinct but interdependent layers and decomposes within\- and cross\-layer dependence into interpretable, role\-specific components linked to classical network summaries, such as reciprocity and multiplexity\. In application, the model shows that high descriptive overlap between familiarity and liking does not imply a common generative process\. Latent interaction patterns are shared across relations, but differences emerge in dispersion of latent positions, particularly by gender\. Moreover, familiarity ratings are associated with both sender and receiver personality traits, whereas liking ratings are primarily associated with receiver traits\.

## [A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria](../publications/1f50b056c1df1dbac5cf.md)

Satya Prakash; Clenira Varela; Mark D\. Walsh; Roberto Galizi; Mark Isalan; Alfonso Jaramillo

Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate\. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory\. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 \+ P2 plasmid pool\. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction\. Across single\-strain trajectories, combined plate\-reader and flow\-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity\- and variance\-dependent weight change\. At the single\-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary\. In mixed populations and co\-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic\-tac\-toe lessons\. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co\-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear\-classifier architectures\. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights\.

## [Climate Change in the State Executive Agenda](../publications/1f5421491c56803bcb43.md)

Chris J\. Koski; Owen Wegner

ABSTRACT State of the state \(SOTS\) speeches represent an annual opportunity for governors to identify issues they intend to prioritize in the coming year\. The speeches represent a finite agenda space directed at lawmakers as well as the general public\. In this paper, we use SOTS speeches to assess the attention American governors directed toward climate change from 2020 to 2024\. Climate change is a particularly useful topic to explore substantively because of the outsized role states play in climate policy in the United States\. We address three research questions\. \(1\) What role does gubernatorial party have in determining the agenda presence of climate change? \(2\) What is the influence of legislative control versus divided government on climate agenda presence? \(3\) To what extent is climate change associated with other issues in SOTS speeches? Our dataset contains 60,801 manually coded quasi‐sentences from 235 speeches\. We find that Democrats mention climate change more than Republicans, that this difference is greatest between government trifectas, but that Democratic and Republican governors speaking to divided legislatures shape their message to meet the partisan split\. We also find that climate change is associated with a host of other issues, but that Democratic governors associate climate change with a broader range of issues than Republicans\. Our work contributes to gubernatorial politics, climate politics, and agenda‐setting scholarship\.

## [Life cycle assessment of a cyanobacterium\-based biofertilizer produced from brewery wastewater: a low\-carbon alternative to NPK fertilizers for barley \(Hordeum vulgare\) production in Passo Fundo, Brazil](../publications/1f66e7ed1669b5b9c191.md)

Paula André da Silva; Arthur Lima e Silva; Daniel Kurpan; Breno Berardo Monteiro; Tácila Oliveira Pinto de Freitas; Bruna de Lemos Novo; Raphael de Oliveira Ribeiro; Anna A\. Sher; Bettina Susanne Hoffmann; Denise Maria Guimarães Freire; Anita Ferreira do Valle

Climate change mitigation requires solutions that reduce greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions, especially in the agricultural sector, which is responsible for most of Brazil&\#x27;s emissions\. Synthetic fertilizers contribute to GHG emissions due to their production, transportation, and use processes\. This work quantified and compared the environmental impact associated with replacing synthetic fertilizers imported by Brazil with a biofertilizer produced from the cultivation of Limnospira sp\. in brewery effluent\. The resulting biomass was used to produce a cyanobacterium\-based biofertilizer, which was later applied to the cultivation of barley \( Hordeum vulgare \), adopting the concept of circular economy\. The life cycle assessment \(LCA\) used a software database \(Open LCA and Ecoinvent 3\.8\) to quantify GHG emissions in the production and transportation of the biofertilizer and a chemical fertilizer \(NPK 5\-20\-20\)\. The LCA demonstrated that the biofertilizer had a 2\.7\-fold reduction in global warming impact relative to the NPK fertilizer, with emissions of 485\.84 kg CO 2 \-eq/ton vs\. 1,312\.75 kg CO 2 \-eq/ton\. A sensitivity analysis was performed using fertilizer substitution scenarios of 50% and 75%, indicating emission reductions of 1\.46 and 1\.89 times, respectively\. These findings indicate that total and partial replacements benefit the environment and strengthen sustainability in the agricultural and industrial sectors\.

## [An evaluation guided multiagent framework for generating floor plans that comply with municipal building regulations](../publications/1f6d6a61d87244444e44.md)

Aarnav Kembhavi; Aryan Rai; Prakhar Parashar; Ananmay A Lohia; Mihir Arya; T Padmashree

Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules\. In architectural layout generation, balancing geometric intuition with regulatory compliance remains a persistent challenge, as current frameworks routinely fail to conform to local building laws\. This paper proposes LayoutGen, a multi\-agent neuro\-symbolic framework coupling probabilistic generation with deterministic verification in an evaluation\-guided refinement loop\. LayoutGen employs a four\-phase retrieval\-driven pipeline \(spatial reasoning, coordinate mapping, vector rendering, and iterative refinement\) powered by a dual retrieval engine leveraging architectural precedents and legislative laws\. An Evaluation Engine scores the generated 2D Scalable Vector Graphics \(SVG\) layouts and returns a graded, itemised report\. Every scored quantity is computed by deterministic geometric checks over the generated coordinates against a structured rule repository; the Large Language Model \(LLM\) is confined to spatial planning, coordinate proposal, and the natural language feedback that drives refinement, together with an advisory Vaastu commentary that does not enter the grade\. Evaluated on single\-storey residential configurations drawn from the RPLAN and MSD datasets, spanning studio to 3BHK typologies and represented as axisaligned rectangular rooms, the full pipeline reduces detected violations from 3\.7 to 0\.3 per plan across n =200 runs, a 92% reduction relative to an unretrieved, unrefined single\-shot baseline using the same backbone model\. Violations are counted across the three error categories the Evaluation Engine checks: topological, geometric, and the encoded dimensional provisions of minimum room area, minimum room width and critical width\. The regulatory component of that count covers only provisions decidable from single\-floor room geometry; setbacks, floor area ratio, egress, staircase geometry, parking and ventilation are present in the repositories but checked outside the generation loop\. Component ablation isolates the contribution of each pipeline stage, and the same architecture runs unchanged across three Indian municipal rule repositories \(BBMP, CMDA, GHMC\) through structured rule replacement alone, without retraining or prompt redesign\. These three regimes express their dimensional provisions in a common form, so this establishes portability within that family rather than generality across regulatory systems\. The framework also integrates Server\-Sent Events \(SSE\) for real\-time design streaming\.

## [Student use of generative AI and perceived institutional support across three linguistic contexts](../publications/1f6d9839f338c66a7cc9.md)

Deddy Gusman; David Sulistiawan Aditya; Dhita Widya Putri; NUR DAMAYANTI; Nurmalina Nurmalina; Gyöngyi Bujdosó

Student use of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) raises questions about how everyday academic practices relate to perceived institutional support\. This exploratory cross\-sectional survey used Indonesian, English, and Hungarian questionnaire versions sharing a common set of core items\. The harmonised dataset included 186 respondents, mainly residents of Indonesia and Hungary\. Overall, 78\.0% reported using AI several times per week or daily \(95% CI \[71\.5, 83\.3\]\), 96\.8% reported using ChatGPT \(95% CI \[93\.1, 98\.5\]\), and 79\.6% reported perceived learning improvement \(95% CI \[73\.2, 84\.7\]\)\. Institution\-funded access and clearer policies were the most frequently requested forms of support\. In the full sample, the Indonesia–Hungary contrast was larger for professor encouragement \(\|r rb \| = 0\.549\) than for perceived learning improvement \(\|r rb \| = 0\.050\)\. However, governance\-related contrasts attenuated in the small English\-language subsample\. Country, language, recruitment route, and response timing overlapped, and measurement invariance was not established\. These findings describe sampled students’ perceptions and do not identify independent country effects, institutional policy quality, or a temporal lag between practice and governance\. We use practice\-governance decoupling as an interpretive description of the coexistence of routine reported use and uneven perceived support\. A four\-component heuristic distinguishes survey findings from literature\-informed interpretation and proposed outcomes for future evaluation\.

## [Redox\-Responsive Curcumin\-Loaded Polymeric Nanoparticles for Targeted Therapy of Parkinson’s Disease\-Associated Neuroinflammation](../publications/1f711f812bf13aac129a.md)

Vishal Kumar yadav; Upendra Kumar; Akash Rameshwar Thombre; Sugandha G\. Chaudhari; Mohammad Asad Alam; Mohd Wasiullah; Tej Pratap Singh; Alka Singh

Parkinson’s disease \(PD\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, oxidative stress, and chronic neuroinflammation\. The present study focuses on the development of redox\-responsive curcumin\-loaded polymeric nanoparticles as a targeted therapeutic strategy for PD\-associated neuroinflammation\. Curcumin was encapsulated within biodegradable PLGA/PEG\-based nanoparticles incorporating disulfide linkages to enable reactive oxygen species \(ROS\)\-triggered drug release\. The formulated nanoparticles were evaluated for physicochemical properties, in vitro drug release behavior, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, anti\-inflammatory activity, oxidative stress modulation, and in vivo neuroprotective efficacy\. The nanoparticles exhibited uniform nanoscale size distribution, high encapsulation efficiency, and stable surface charge, indicating suitability for brain\-targeted delivery\. In vitro studies demonstrated controlled drug release under physiological conditions and significantly enhanced release under oxidative environments, confirming redox responsiveness\. Cellular studies in microglial and neuronal models showed improved uptake, minimal cytotoxicity, and significant reduction in ROS levels and apoptosis\. Anti\-inflammatory assays revealed suppression of pro\-inflammatory cytokines \(TNF\-α, IL\-1β, IL\-6\) and inhibition of microglial activation\. Furthermore, oxidative stress markers were significantly reduced with a concomitant increase in antioxidant enzyme activity \(SOD, CAT, and GSH\)\. In vivo results in toxin\-induced PD models demonstrated improved motor coordination, enhanced neuronal survival, and reduced neuroinflammation\. Overall, the developed nanocarrier system effectively enhances curcumin bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy, offering a promising multifunctional approach for the management of Parkinson’s disease\.

## [Integración de tecnologías digitales en la educación superior: análisis del ecosistema tecnológico de la Universidad Estatal Amazónica\.](../publications/1f721e174fdbfac6b29f.md)

Edwin Gustavo Fernández Sánchez; Lineth del Rocío Fernández Sánchez; Katherine Estefania Coro Villarreal; V\. Morales

La integración de tecnologías digitales constituye un componente estratégico para la transformación de los ambientes educativos en la educación superior\. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar la integración de tecnologías digitales en la Universidad Estatal Amazónica mediante la caracterización de la infraestructura, conectividad, plataformas institucionales, recursos digitales y estrategias de capacitación docente que conforman su ecosistema tecnológico educativo\. Se desarrolló una investigación cuantitativa, descriptiva, no experimental, documental y de corte transversal\-retrospectivo, sustentada en registros e información institucional\. Se analizaron las pantallas interactivas instaladas en los ambientes educativos, la conectividad a Internet, el Entorno Virtual de Aprendizaje \(EVA\), Microsoft 365, las bibliotecas virtuales y los procesos de capacitación docente\. Los resultados evidenciaron un ecosistema articulado en tres niveles: infraestructura y acceso, servicios y recursos digitales, y desarrollo de capacidades\. Se concluye que la UEA presenta una integración estructural y funcional sustentada en la articulación de infraestructura, conectividad, servicios digitales y capacitación docente\. Esta configuración transforma las condiciones tecnológicas de los ambientes educativos y proporciona una base institucional para la integración progresiva de tecnologías digitales, sin que los datos permitan inferir efectos causales sobre el aprendizaje o el rendimiento académico\.

## [Oil Rents, Economic Growth and Human Development in OPEC Countries: Panel Data Evidence from AMG and PMG Estimations](../publications/1f79e08345dc75e850fb.md)

Fatma Fehime AYDIN

The natural resource reserves of countries can offer important opportunities for countries to achieve their economic growth and development targets\. However, due to mistakes in the way they are managed, their impact on economic growth and development may sometimes not be at the expected level, and even negative effects, called the resource curse, may occur\. Therefore, analyzing natural resource reserves’ relationship with economic growth and development is an important issue\. Using data from 11 OPEC countries for the period 2003\-2020, the study analyses the relationship between oil rents’ \(OR\) economic growth \(EG\) and human development \(HDI\)\. Westerlund panel cointegration test, Dumitrescu &amp; Hurlin panel causality test, Augmented Mean Group \(AMG\), and Pooled Mean Group \(PMG\) estimators are applied in this study\. According to the findings obtained from the Westerlund panel cointegration test, the results provide limited evidence of a long\-run association between OR and HDI, with the bootstrap\-adjusted evidence being marginally significant at the 10% level but not at the 5% level\. According to the AMG and PMG methods, OR has a positive association with both EG and HDI\. The panel causality test by Dumitrescu &amp; Hurlin found no statistically significant causal relationship between OR and EG, while a bidirectional causal relationship exists among OR and HDI\. Overall, the findings suggest that the development benefits of oil revenues can be enhanced by channeling them into human capital, healthcare, infrastructure, and productive investment; at the same time, excessive dependence on oil can be reduced through economic diversification, and the transparency and efficiency of resource management can be improved\.

## [Developing stacking models for interacting biopolymers using quantum mechanical calculations and machine learning](../publications/1f7cf757fcf88a243b39.md)

Anik Brinckerhoff; Malav Champaneria; Creston A\. Singer; Julie Nguyen; Sheikh Rabiul Islam; David Salas‐de la Cruz; Hong Fang

Biopolymers are long\-chain molecules with significant potential for developing sustainable, renewable, and environmentally friendly materials\. Agarose, a biopolymer derived from red algae, is widely used in bioengineering and biomedical applications because of its biocompatibility and biodegradability\. Understanding how agarose chains interact and assemble is essential for explaining its gelation behavior and material properties\. For decades, scientists have debated whether agarose chains primarily form double\-helical structures or other arrangements\. In this study, researchers used high\-throughput quantum mechanical calculations and machine\-learning models to investigate the interactions between agarose chains\. Their results show that stacked configurations are energetically and statistically more favorable than the traditionally proposed double\-helix structure\. The study also identifies simple interatomic interactions and distances between specific atomic species as effective descriptors for predicting the assembled structures\. These findings resolve a long\-standing controversy and provide valuable insight into agarose structure, gelation, and the design of advanced biopolymeric materials\.

## [Human\-Ecosystem Coupling Mechanisms and Data\-Driven Spatial Optimization in Urban Green Infrastructure](../publications/1f823d8d8f95eb3fa328.md)

Ye Wen

High\-density urban construction continuously alters land cover, hydrothermal cycles, and habitat patterns, significantly impacting residents&\#x27; well\-being through heat exposure, air quality variations, activity opportunities, and nature contact\. Urban green infrastructure, relying on vegetation, water bodies, and soil processes to buffer built\-up environmental stressors, serves as a crucial link between ecological resilience, public health, and spatial governance\. From a socio\-ecological coupling perspective, this paper outlines the complex interaction chain between built\-up environmental pressures, ecological process responses, resident exposure, and governance feedback, systematically analyzing the synergy, trade\-offs, and equity differences of multifunctional services\. Based on this framework, it discusses the advanced integration of remote sensing, street view imagery, spatial machine learning, multi\-objective optimization, and urban digital twins in state identification, priority area determination, scheme generation, and dynamic feedback\. Existing evidence suggests that green infrastructure performance is jointly shaped by ecological structure, urban morphology, population activity, and governance conditions\. Ultimately, spatial optimization for high\-density cities requires a fundamental shift from static green volume assessment to dynamic decision\-making that comprehensively combines ecological processes, actual exposure, equitable allocation, and long\-term feedback mechanisms to ensure sustainable urban development and enhanced community well\-being across diverse socio\-economic contexts\. Furthermore, addressing these challenges necessitates interdisciplinary collaboration to bridge the gap between theoretical models and practical urban planning implementations\.

## [Generative Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: Redefining Business Leadership, Marketing Excellence, and Governance Practices](../publications/1f862892075f9b14bd30.md)

Santanu Roy; Dr\. R Ganesh Kumar; Prof\. Abhijeet Wairagade; Dr\. Panduarng Sudamrao Dabhade; Ajay Bhushan Prasad

The advent of generative AI is having a profound impact on entrepreneurial strategy, organizational innovation, leadership, and long\-term competitive performance\. This study explored the impact of the adoption of artificial intelligence on the process of entrepreneurial transformation toward sustainability in terms of leadership support, business model innovation, sustainable competitive advantage, institutional support, cost effectiveness, and firm performance\. The study adopted a quantitative secondary\-data design and had a managerial dataset of 325 observations\. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling was utilised to assess the measurement reliability, construct validity, structural linkages, explanatory power, and indirect effects\. It was discovered that the measurement model had acceptable Average Variance and Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha values over 0\.80\. extracted values greater than 0\.65, demonstrating convergent validity and adequate dependability\. The structural results indicated that the use of AI had significant impacts on business model innovation, sustainable competitive advantage, and firm performance\. The top direct result of business model innovation was that it created a firm&\#x27;s strongest direct link to its performance, followed by sustainable competitive advantage\. AI adoption was strongly encouraged by leadership support, and government support had positive impacts on AI adoption, leadership support and cost effectiveness\. Important indirect effects also suggested that AI has impacts on organizational performance via innovation and sustainable competitive capability\. The overall results indicate that the strategic contribution of AI is highly reliant on leadership, innovation, institutional support, and responsible organizational practices\.

## [MusselFinder : Automated dreissenid mussel density estimation via robotic benthic imaging](../publications/1f8b6ba389481cd9c8b6.md)

Angus Galloway; Peter C\. Esselman; Anthony J Geglio; Shadi Moradi; Jennifer M\. Morris; Joseph Geisz; Magdalena K\. Sobol; Graham W\. Taylor

Abstract Despite the widespread need to map the abundance of invasive quagga and zebr mussels \( Dreissena spp\.\) in lakes and reservoirs worldwide, current methods remain limited by data collection and analysis bottlenecks\. Autonomous underwater vehicles \(AUVs\) combined with machine learning \(ML\) offer a scalable remote sensing approach for estimating mussel density \(individuals m −2 \) across large spatial domains and a range of habitats that are difficult to sample with current techniques\. We present MusselFinder: a deep neural network \(DNN\)‐based pipeline that detects and enumerates live mussels in AUV‐collected benthic images\. MusselFinder estimates live mussel percent cover and density in nadir monocular images captured at known altitudes above the lakebed\. In images of suitable clarity, MusselFinder achieved strong pixel‐level localization \(mussel‐class Intersection over Union \[IoU\] &gt; 0\.76\) and density prediction \(log‐density R 2 = 0\.79–0\.95\) over a variety of bottom types\. AUV‐based image acquisition is more than three orders of magnitude faster than physical sampling by divers or ponar grabs, and DNN‐based analysis can proceed at rates comparable to image acquisition\. We used MusselFinder to analyze over 50,000 spatially referenced images at a spawning reef in Lake Michigan, representing a shift from small‐scale, diver‐collected datasets to large‐scale monitoring in unconstrained environments\. The method can be adapted to new imaging conditions using a modest training set and a user‐friendly point‐labeling technique, supporting broader‐scale monitoring of one of the world&\#x27;s most invasive invertebrates\.

## [Selection of Electric Vehicles within the Framework of Consumer Preferences: A SWARA\-CODAS Application on the Turkish Market](../publications/1f8c084363fb5620272c.md)

Murat Kurnuç

The rapid growth of the electric vehicle market in recent years has made it essential, from a marketing perspective, to understand which criteria are decisive in evaluating these vehicles and how the available options are positioned with respect to these criteria\. Accordingly, this study aims to reveal the relative weights of the prominent criteria in the electric vehicle evaluation process and to comparatively rank the competing models in the Turkish market within the framework of these criteria\. In determining the criteria, economic, technical, and usage\-based dimensions were taken into consideration\. A two\-stage approach was adopted in the analysis process; the criteria weights were calculated using the SWARA technique, while the performance ranking of the alternative models was conducted using the CODAS technique\. The findings indicate that the most decisive factor in the evaluation process is driving range, followed by purchase cost, power consumption, and battery warranty period\. In the ranking of alternatives, it was observed that brands offering technical superiority and comprehensive warranty advantages came to the forefront rather than the models with the highest market share\. In addition to contributing to the marketing literature, the study offers various insights and recommendations for manufacturers and distributors\.

## [Bridging scales: a perspective on macro\-to\-micro transfer for microscopy foundation models](../publications/1f8f8118b10523859ed7.md)

Yuanjie Gu; Yiqun Wang; Jun Zhang; Zhi Lü; Biqin Dong

Foundation models \(FMs\) are transforming artificial intelligence for science, but microscopy FMs remain constrained by limited, heterogeneous, and information\-sparse data\. We propose a Macro\-to\-Micro paradigm in which large\-scale macroscopic pretraining establishes a broad visual representation, followed by microscopy\-specific adaptation that introduces biological specificity and modality\-dependent imaging knowledge\. This staged strategy enables scarce microscopy data to specialize a mature representation rather than build one from scratch\. Combined with domain\-aware adaptation and a coordinated microscopy data ecosystem, Macro\-to\-Micro provides a data\-efficient roadmap toward foundation models that ground general visual intelligence in biological knowledge and the physics of image formation\.

## [Decision tree classification of academic success in a first\-year human anatomy course at a South African university](../publications/1f9160c9fcc1471d05d0.md)

E Bruwer; Nicolene Jooste

Background\. Human anatomy is a fundamental subject in health sciences education, yet academic success in this topic is often hindered by various challenges, including the extensive module content, complex concepts and reduced instructional time\. Identifying students at risk of underperformance early in the module can facilitate timely interventions\. Objective\. To develop a classification scheme to predict academic success in a first\-year human anatomy module in South Africa using admission\-stage data, including South Africa’s National Senior Certificate \(NSC\) subjects and qualification enrolment\. Methods\. Data from 196 students enrolled in Optometry, Nursing and BSc Life and Environmental Sciences programmes \(2017 \- 2018\) were analysed\. A decision tree classification model \(J48 algorithm\) was applied to identify key predictors of student success, categorised as failed, passed or distinction\. Results\. Results indicated that qualification enrolment and the NSC subjects Home Language, Mathematics and History were the most informative predictors\. The model demonstrated a 55\.6% overall accuracy, with the highest classification success for the ‘passed’ category \(93/165\) but limited predictive power for ‘failed’ and ‘distinction’ classifications\. The kappa value \(0\.1083\) and mean absolute error \(0\.1606\) indicated moderate agreement and acceptable accuracy\. These findings highlight the complexity of predicting academic performance in the study of human anatomy and suggest that although admission data may provide some insights, additional factors \(e\.g\. learning strategies and motivation\) could play crucial roles\. Conclusion\. Mathematics at secondary\-school level played a key role in distinguishing students likely to pass human anatomy modules, across all degree programmes that were analysed\. Furthermore, the study findings underscore the need for supplementary assessment tools and support mechanisms to enhance student success\. Future research should explore the integration of cognitive and behavioural predictors alongside academic metrics to improve classification models\.

## [Epidemiology and clinical outcomes of filler\-related complications among transgender women in Mexico](../publications/1f9cbe68004c3570ed9a.md)

Karen Marañón; Mariana Velez\-Pintado; América Sarahí Martínez\-Frías; Esmeralda Román\-Mar; Mitzi Zaira Fong\-Ponce; Montserrat Staeps\-Gordoa; Juanita Lastra\-Torres; Elizabeth Vancini\-Nieto; María Eugenia Zghaib\-Rivero; Paula Viveros\-Wacher; Álvaro López\-Íñiguez; Alfredo Ponce‐de‐León; María Fernanda González\-Lara

Abstract Filler\-related complications \(FRC\) arise from the injection of high\-density substances used to modify the body in order to harmonize gender identity and/or gender expression and represent an emerging public health problem\. Among transgender women, limited access to gender\-affirming healthcare, together with other psychosocial, structural, and social factors, may contribute to the use of body modification practices intended to harmonize gender identity and gender expression, including the use of injectable materials\. We conducted a retrospective analytical study among transgender women with a history of filler injections receiving care at three public referral centers in Mexico City between September 2024 and July 2025\. Participants were identified through review of available clinical records and transgender care registries\. Transgender identity was determined based on self\-identified gender documented in the clinical record and confirmed through clinical chart review\. Demographic, clinical, and social variables were collected to characterize FRC and associated factors\. FRC were defined as documented inflammatory, infectious, migratory, or mixed manifestations temporally associated with prior filler exposure and attributed by the treating clinical team to filler injections\. A total of 222 transgender women were included, with a median age of 45 years \(IQR 38–52\)\. Overall, 99 participants \(44\.5%\) were classified as having FRC, most commonly inflammatory or mixed presentations\. Materials referred to as “biopolymers” were the most frequently reported injected substances, followed by injectable oils, and among participants with available information, 93% of injections were performed by non\-medical personnel\. The time between filler injection and symptom onset exceeded 5 years in 54% of participants with FRC\. More than one\-third of affected participants required hospitalization attributable to FRC\. Nearly half of transgender women with prior filler injections experienced complications, underscoring the substantial morbidity associated with filler injections performed outside supervised medical care\. These findings highlight the multifactorial structural and social context surrounding non\-medically supervised filler use, including barriers to gender\-affirming healthcare, and the need for multidisciplinary care pathways for FRC\. Because this retrospective study was conducted at referral centers, severe complications may be overrepresented\.

## [What AI training data sells for: a sourced index of public prices, 2023 to 2026](../publications/1f9eaef28c17a02e6a27.md)

Yuma Heymans

Training data for machine learning is bought and sold without an exchange or a posted price list\. This paper assembles the public record of its prices: 1,022 observations for nine kinds of data, read from 735 source documents between 11 and 17 October 2026, 1,009 of them dated 2023 or later\. Each observation keeps the figure as published, the side of the market where the money moves \(paid to makers, offered to holders, asking price, made to order, completed sale, cost to produce\) and a conversion to a common unit by stated arithmetic, with ranges entered as geometric midpoints\. Medians in each kind&\#x27;s main unit run from $0\.525 per image to $316,228 per company archive, and within a main unit the upper quartile is 2\.0 to 37\.8 times the lower\. The side of the market moves prices as much as the kind of data does\. For agent\-training tasks, the median price buyers pay for collection to order is 9\.5 times the median paid to the people who make them\. For company records, the median published offer to holders is 11\.2 times the median of the four completed sales with a stated amount\. Completed sales are 73 of the 1,022 observations, and only 11 observations come from court filings\. We describe the disclosure, promotion, concentration and survivorship biases of a public\-record compilation and state the method so that every figure can be recomputed\. JEL codes: D40, D83, L14, L86, O33 Keywords: training data; data markets; price index; data licensing; artificial intelligence; market transparency; posted prices Use of AI: this paper was prepared with generative AI tools, which compiled and analysed the open datasets and drafted the text\. The author takes responsibility for its content\. Competing interests: the author is CEO of AIData\.Broker, which acts for companies that license their data to AI developers and publishes the open datasets the paper draws on\. Also at aidata\.broker/research/paper\-prices\.

## [Stylistic Imitation and Peer\-Based Intervention in Thai EFL Writing Classrooms: A Qualitative Study of Learners’ Writing Development](../publications/1fa52d74bd22b4774d02.md)

Lindren Oliver; Mille Stutgart; Jemima Mai

Writing remains challenging for EFL learners because it requires the simultaneous management of ideas, organization, language, cohesion, and genre conventions\. Although model\-text instruction and peer feedback have independently received considerable attention\. This qualitative descriptive study investigated the extent to which stylistic imitation implemented through peer\-based intervention supported Thai EFL learners’ writing and explored learners’ perceptions of its contribution to drafting, feedback, revision, and writing independence\. Participants were five EFL teachers and 23 learners involved in academic writing classes at secondary schools in Thailand\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews and non\-participant classroom observations and analysed through data condensation, thematic display, and conclusion drawing and verification\. The findings indicated that model texts reduced drafting uncertainty and made paragraph structure, cohesion, transitions, and rhetorical development more visible\. Peer review helped learners identify unclear ideas, organizational weaknesses, and missing explanations, while repeated feedback cycles encouraged substantive revision and greater confidence\. However, improvements were less apparent in grammar and vocabulary, and several learners remained uncertain about peer\-feedback accuracy or dependent on model structures and teacher confirmation\. The intervention therefore supported writing to a meaningful but differentiated extent, with its strongest contributions occurring at the discourse and writing\-process levels\. The study concludes that stylistic imitation and peer intervention can function as mutually reinforcing pedagogical practices when supported by clear models, focused rubrics, feedback training, teacher monitoring, and gradual withdrawal of scaffolding\.

## [RETHINKING TRANSLATOR TRAINING AS A CROSS\-CUTTING TECHNOLOGICAL WORKFLOW](../publications/1fa6d205600259d097c7.md)

Yu\. V\. Kondratenko; L\. O\. Hastynshchykova

Modern translator training faces a structural mismatch: technology is typically taught as a set of isolated modules, one tool per topic, while professional translation practice treats these same tools as an interconnected workflow in which a single instrument routinely performs functions attributed to several distinct stages\. This article reframes the transla\- tion process as a technological chain comprising four interrelated components – pre\-translation analysis, CAT\-assisted translation supported by an AI agent, quality management, and file preparation – and argues that these components are better represented as a network of overlapping actions than as a linear sequence of self\-contained stages\. Drawing on both theoretical models of translator competence \(PACTE’s instrumental competence, the EMT framework\) and empirical studies of specific tools and stages, the article identifies a gap between well\-established theoretical support for cross\- cutting technical competence and its still\-fragmented empirical and classroom validation\. The study demonstrates, through classroom examples – including the pre\-editing of auto\-generated video subtitles using regular expressions and a compar\- ative analysis of PDF\-document translation across several CAT environments – that a single technological action routinely crosses the boundaries between the four proposed stages, undermining the pedagogical logic of modular instruction\. The article proposes a network model of the translation technological chain, in which the four components function as condi\- tional nodes connected by feedback and cross\-cutting links rather than fixed sequential order, and grounds this model in the broader concept of a translator’s digital literacy\. The findings support a concrete pedagogical principle: technical com\- petence formation should be organized around cross\-cutting, project\-based assignments that require students to move across several nodes of the model, rather than around isolated tool\-specific modules\. The article concludes by identifying directions for further research, including the applicability of the proposed model to team\-based translation workflows and an unresolved gap between the documented professional importance of quality\-management tools and students’ compar\- atively modest perception of their value\.

## [Estrategias neuroeducativas para favorecer la autorregulaciónen la primera infancia: revisión sistemática en contextos latinoamericanos](../publications/1faaacb781286c89de87.md)

Paula Vanessa Benavides\-Garzón; Karem Vásquez\-Rendón; Juan Felipe Torres\-Garzón; Steve Fernando Pedraza Vargas

Introduction: Self\-regulation is a fundamental process for cognitive and socio\-emotional development during early childhood\. Educational neuroscience proposes pedagogical strategies grounded in knowledge of brain functioning to foster self\-regulation; however, evidence from Latin America remains fragmented\. Methodology: A systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines and the SPIDER framework\. Six databases were searched, and studies published between 2019 and 2024 addressing neuroeducational strategies to promote self\-regulation in preschool children from Latin America were selected\. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool \(MMAT\)\. Results: Of the 951 records identified, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria\. Five categories of neuroeducational strategies were identified: play\-based activities, neuromotor stimulation, emotional and metacognitive education, multisensory approaches, and teacher training with technology integration\. Overall, the studies reported improvements in executive functions, attention, inhibitory control, and emotional regulation\. Discussion: The evidence supports the use of neuroeducational strategies to promote self\-regulation; however, descriptive and quasi\-experimental designs with methodological limitations predominate\. Conclusions: Neuroeducational strategies show promising results for strengthening self\-regulation in early childhood\. Nevertheless, longitudinal studies with more rigorous method ological designs are needed to strengthen the evidence in Latin American contexts\.Received: 06/07/2026 \- Approved: 02/08/2026

## [MANAGEMENT OF ORGANIZATIONAL MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITALIZATION: AN INTEGRATED APPROACH](../publications/1fb9baefb2dfa34d5e08.md)

Ірина Іванівна Білик; Наталія Косар; Ю\. Т\. Савченко

The article examines an integrated approach to managing organizational marketing communications under digital transformation\. It substantiates that digitalization changes traditional communication models, expands stakeholder interaction channels, and increases the need to combine analytical and generative tools\. The purpose of the study is to analyze the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of integrated marketing communication management in public administration bodies and nonprofit organizations, including sports organizations\. The study analyzes Big Data, CRM systems, social media, AI\-generated content, and chatbots in communication activities\. The study compares objectives, audiences, channels, digital tools, challenges, and ethical risks\. The components of an integrated approach are proposed: consistency of information messages, multichannel communication, orientation toward target audience needs, and continuous feedback\. It is established that CRM systems support stakeholder relationship management, personalized interaction, and communication performance analysis; Big Data expands opportunities for audience segmentation and behavioral analysis; and generative artificial intelligence facilitates adaptive content creation and communication automation\. Digital integration increases audience trust and engagement, optimizes expenditures, and enables faster responses to environmental changes\. The effectiveness of integrated communications depends on the consistency of messages across different channels and their adaptation to the specific needs of stakeholder groups\. The systematic combination of digital technologies with traditional communication tools is substantiated as a basis for organizational resilience in a dynamic environment\. Ethical, reputational, institutional, and resource\-related challenges associated with disinformation, non\-transparent use of AI, personal data protection, unequal digital skills, and limited resources are systematized\. The scientific novelty lies in conceptualizing an integrated approach as a universal yet sector\-differentiated model for managing organizational marketing communications\. The practical value lies in applying the model to improve communication strategies\.

K\. Priyanka; N\. Chandrakala; Padmavathi Nakka

Road traffic accidents are one of the main causes of death and serious injury worldwide and delays in the response of emergency services may often increase the risk of death and permanent disability\. Sensors such as accelerometers, gyroscopes, GPS, and cameras can be used to constantly monitor the vehicle dynamics\. Real accidents, normal driving situations and false alarms can be correctly discriminated by machine learning algorithms from real time data\. When an accident is detected the system automatically detects the exact location, records important incident information and sends alerts to emergency services, local hospitals and designated emergency contacts, all without human intervention\. The proposed framework is designed to reduce the response time, increase the accuracy of accident detection and improve the efficiency of emergency management\. The system is able to provide reliable data transmission and continuous monitoring in various road conditions via cloud Based communication and intelligent decision making\. The experimental evaluation shows that the proposed approach can significantly reduce the delay of notification and improve the reliability of detection and support of timely medical assistance, thus increasing the chances of survival and decreasing the severity of accident\-related consequences\. &quot;The smart solution is a practical step forward in the development of safer transportation systems and smart city infrastructures by integrating real time analytics, automation and connected technologies for effective accident management\.

## [O potencial da Inteligência Artificial para a Gestão do Conhecimento na Petrobras](../publications/1fcb5be773b88e8935d9.md)

Arturo Cavalcanti Catunda; Tayane Cristina Mattera Souza

This article discusses the growing importance of knowledge as an organizational asset and the integration between Knowledge Management \(KM\) and Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\. This integration can enhance KM processes, while consistent KM practices provide high quality data for intelligent algorithms\. The purpose of this study is to present how Petrobras is structuring itself to apply AI in its KM processes\. This is a case study based on content analysis of documents \(internal reports, consulting reports, event materials\), interviews with the company’s KM team, and a literature review\. The study contributes to the field by highlighting Petrobras’ journey as a complex and regulated organization\. This journey involved combining agile methods, experimentation, international scouting, and other strategies to meet business requirements aligned with organizational needs, expanding the benefits of this technology\. As a result, in addition to the strong ROI potential and the intangible benefits associated with applying AI to KM processes, the study concludes that this innovation represents a strategic step for Petrobras\. However, success will depend on the combination of technology and human factors, ensuring that the established governance enables proper data curation and mitigation of risks associated with this emerging technology\.

## [THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHING AND LEARNING](../publications/1fd3e0bd48169459a9d7.md)

Husenova Nargiza

In recent years, artificial intelligence \(AI\) has become one of the most influential technologies in the field of education, particularly in foreign language teaching and learning\. The integration of AI tools into English language education has created new opportunities for both teachers and students by providing personalized learning experiences, immediate feedback, and access to various digital resources\. This paper examines the impact of artificial intelligence on English language teaching and learning, focusing on its advantages, applications, and possible challenges\. AI\-based technologies such as language learning applications, automated assessment systems, virtual assistants, and conversational tools help students improve their vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and communication skills\. Moreover, AI allows learners to study independently according to their individual needs and learning pace\. For teachers, artificial intelligence provides support in lesson planning, creating educational materials, and evaluating students’ progress\. However, despite its benefits, the use of AI also presents certain challenges, including dependence on technology, data privacy issues, and the need for teachers to develop digital competencies\. The study concludes that artificial intelligence can significantly enhance English language education when it is used effectively and combined with traditional teaching approaches\. AI should be considered not as a replacement for teachers, but as a powerful tool that supports more effective, interactive, and learner\-centered language instruction\.

## [Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Multi\-Lesion Detection in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening from Fundus Photographs with Ophthalmologist Benchmarking](../publications/1fe5587886e6a2ca21c2.md)

Aninda Paul Antor; Nandan Kushum Das; Bidith Ranjan Deb; Nasrin Afrose; Md Kamrul Islam Chowdhury; Md Bazlur Rahman; Marwa Islam; Subarna Roy

Background: Diabetic retinopathy is among the leading preventable causes of blindness worldwide, but the shortage of trained ophthalmologists and the growing burden of screening still remain a considerable challenge, particularly in resource\-constrained settings\. Purpose: The aim of this study was to assess the diagnostic accuracy of a deep learning algorithm for detecting multiple retinal lesions associated with diabetic retinopathy in fundus photographs and to compare its performance with that of ophthalmologists\. Methods: This retrospective analytical study used a combined dataset of approximately 38,788 annotated colour fundus photographs drawn from the publicly available EyePACS and APTOS 2019 datasets\. A deep learning model based on EfficientNet\-B4 was developed using supervised learning\. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing sets\. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), sensitivity, specificity, and F1\-score\. A subset of test images was independently assessed by ophthalmologists for benchmarking\. Findings: The deep learning model achieved a mean AUC of 0\.92 across five categories of retinal lesions\. The highest performance was observed for hard exudate detection \(AUC = 0\.96\) and retinal haemorrhage detection \(AUC = 0\.94\), with relatively lower performance for neovascularization \(AUC = 0\.87\)\. The model performed similarly to ophthalmologists and demonstrated higher sensitivity in detecting hard exudates\. Conclusion: Deep learning algorithms are capable of high diagnostic accuracy in multi\-lesion detection of diabetic retinopathy in fundus photographs and represent a promising adjunct to ophthalmologist\-led screening; however, prospective real\-world validation and further work on model interpretability are needed before routine clinical deployment\. J\.Natl\.Inst\.Ophthalmol\.2025;8\(1\): 56\-62

## [Machine\-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3\-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors](../publications/1fe6ff390b0faf150da4.md)

Víctor Puig\-I\-Laborda; Jorge Carrasco Muriel; Andrea Castañeda Tena; Teddy Groves; Johan le Nepvou de Carfort; Ulrich Krühne; Krist V\. Gernaey; Cees Haringa; Ignasi Puig‐de‐Dou; Lars Keld Nielsen

Abstract High\-fidelity computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred\-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application\. We developed surrogate models trained on $$760$$ 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3\-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions \(e\.g\., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio\-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration\), and local spatial descriptors \(e\.g\., distance to the feeding point\)\. Among various methods, attention\-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy \(test $$\{\{\{\\rm\{R\}\}\}\}^\{2\}\\approx 0\.91$$ R 2 ≈ 0\.91 \), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond\-scale inference—up to a million\-fold speed\-up compared to CFD\. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real\-time optimization and digital\-twin frameworks in bioprocessing\. Our results demonstrate that data\-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control\.

## [A Lifelong Neuro\-Symbolic Explainable AI Twin for Zero\-Touch 6G IoE Management Under Non\-Stationary Network Dynamics](../publications/1fe8f604e48846ae02b3.md)

Walaa M\. Alayed; Hassam Ahmed Tahir; Waqar Ul Hassan

Future sixth\-generation \(6G\) Internet of Everything \(IoE\) networks require zero\-touch management systems capable of autonomously allocating communication and computational resources, satisfying service\-level constraints, and providing transparent explanations for their decisions\. Existing neuro\-symbolic explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\) twins improve interpretability by coupling neural prediction with symbolic reasoning; however, most rely on statically engineered causal graphs, fixed rule sets, and immutable knowledge bases\. Such closed\-world assumptions are unsuitable for non\-stationary 6G environments in which radio conditions, mobility patterns, interference relationships, and service requirements continuously evolve\. To address this limitation, this paper proposes LL\-NS\-XAI, a Lifelong Learning Neuro\-Symbolic XAI Digital Twin for zero\-touch 6G IoE management\. The framework integrates three tightly coupled planes: an online implicit learner at the physical edge for time\-varying service association and uplink/downlink resource allocation; a dynamic explicit learner in the virtual core for directed acyclic graph \(DAG\)\-based Bayesian reasoning, most\-probable\-explanation inference, and explainable trust scoring; and a meta\-cognitive layer that monitors reasoning residuals, detects parameter drift, structural drift, and ontological emergence, and autonomously revises the causal graph, probabilistic rule sets, conditional probability tables, and knowledge base\. Unlike static neuro\-symbolic twins, LL\-NS\-XAI treats realized post\-decision outcomes, including achieved channel quality indicator \(CQI\), measured end\-to\-end delay, and throughput, as interventional evidence for online causal\-model adaptation\. Experimental evaluation using a non\-stationary 5G\-derived dataset with injected parameter drift, structural drift, and emergent IoE service classes demonstrates that LL\-NS\-XAI maintains higher long\-term trustworthiness, lower reasoning residuals, and bounded performance degradation compared with static XAI twins, non\-stationary bandits, and pure continual\-learning baselines\. The framework additionally accommodates a previously unseen IoE service class through autonomous causal\-graph expansion, recovering near\-oracle performance without offline retraining\. These results demonstrate that lifelong causal adaptation can improve the robustness, explainability, and autonomy of AI\-enabled zero\-touch management in evolving 6G IoE networks\.

## [Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of ecological risks in the Wujiang River Basin over the past four decades](../publications/1feb43629d2361205290.md)

Wei Li; Xiao Jiang; Liang Huang; Sisi Lv; Weiquan Zhao; Jianfeng Wu

Elucidating the spatiotemporal changes in ecological risk is theoretically and practically significant for advancing regional ecological civilisation development and achieving watershed ecological security\. A landscape ecological risk \(LER\) assessment model based on land use data spanning eight periods from 1990 to 2023 was established for the Wujiang River Basin\. Through this model, the spatiotemporal differentiation and evolutionary characteristics of the intrabasin LER were systematically analysed\. By integrating spatial autocorrelation analysis with the optimal parameterised geographic detector method, the dominant drivers of global and local spatial differentiation in ecological risk were identified\. Between 1990 and 2023, the Wujiang River Basin LER was significantly positively spatially correlated with the drivers, demonstrating overall risk reduction\. The high/medium–high\-risk area proportion decreased from 11\.48 to 4\.02%\. The low\-risk area proportion increased from 5\.75 to 52\.68%\. Temporal analysis revealed three distinct phases of ecological risk evolution: disturbance \(1990–2000\), reduction \(2000–2015\), and stabilisation \(2015–2023\)\. Landscape pattern changes influenced risk across phases\. Socioeconomic factors dominated the spatial pattern of ecological risk\. The combined effect of multiple drivers was greater than the effects of individual factors\. This study provides systematic references and decision\-making support for establishing ecological barriers, managing ecological risks, and optimising ecological spatial patterns in the upper Yangtze River territorial space\.
