## [ОЦЕНКА ПАТЕНТНОЙ АКТИВНОСТИ ДАЛЬНЕГО ВОСТОКА](../publications/200b6d88d2de4ae90f39.md)

Андрей Николаевич Гоменюк

В статье рассматривается роль патентной активности как ключевого индикатора инновационного развития в контексте стратегического приоритета России на XXI век — развития Дальнего Востока\. Подчеркивается, что в условиях экономики, основанной на знаниях, способность региона генерировать и коммерциализировать новые технологии становится основным фактором его конкурентоспособности\. На Х Восточном экономическом форуме президент России Владимир Путин акцентировал внимание на необходимости превращения Дальнего Востока в передовой регион по цифровому развитию\. Внедрение новых технологий, таких как искусственный интеллект и беспилотники, рассматривается как способ повышения эффективности и обеспечения безопасности в условиях глобальной технологической конкуренции\. Анализ патентной статистики показывает, что, несмотря на рост числа патентных заявок в России, Дальний Восток демонстрирует низкие показатели патентной активности, что связано с исторически сырьевой направленностью экономики и недостаточной интеграцией научных исследований с производственными предприятиями\. В статье также представлены данные о распределении патентных заявок по регионам и выявлена значительная концентрация патентной активности в Приморском крае, Республике Саха \(Якутия\) и Хабаровском крае\. Подчеркивается необходимость создания условий для кооперации между научными институтами и бизнесом, что может способствовать переходу экономики региона от сырьевой модели к экономике высоких технологий\.

## [Serial H&amp;E Pathology Reveals Progression‐Associated Nuclear Size Drift as a Longitudinal Digital Readout of Bladder Cancer Evolution](../publications/20179f8e1936334d9585.md)

Xing Liu; Zhen‐Duo Shi; Gong‐Cheng Wang; Jianming Wang; Ying Liu; Yi Gong; Xuan Lin; Di Wu; Shichao Zhuo; Han Han; Yibing Shi; Fan‐Lai Meng; Yu Zhang; Zhigang Jia; Conghui Han

Serial pathological specimens are routinely generated during bladder cancer surveillance, but their temporal information remains underused in computational pathology\. This study develops a longitudinal digital pathology framework to quantify direction\-preserving nuclear morphological change within the same patient\. Paired hematoxylin and eosin whole\-slide images are organized as T0, the earlier specimen, and T1, the later specimen\. Signed Δ features, defined as T1\-T0, are extracted across nuclear size, shape regularity, local cellularity, and spatial organization\. After quality control, the discovery cohort includes 86 pairs from 86 patients, and the independent confirmation cohort includes 96 pairs from 96 patients\. A separate four\-center resource of 1977 whole\-slide images from 1660 patients provides a static contextual baseline\. Several nuclear features showed the same direction of association with progression across the two cohorts\. Nuclear size\-related change was most prominent in the independent confirmation cohort, particularly for equivalent nuclear diameter and nuclear area\. Spatial analysis shows a broader upward distributional shift in nuclear area in progression pairs\. Static foundation\-model representations show variable locked cross\-center transferability, whereas Ki\-67 immunohistochemistry and TCGA\-BLCA transcriptomic analyses provide complementary tissue\-level and molecular context\. Routine serial hematoxylin and eosin specimens may therefore provide interpretable, direction\-preserving digital readouts of bladder cancer evolution\.

## [Photostabilization of PVC/PS/PMMA Blend Films by Metal Oxide Nanoparticles under Accelerated UV Aging](../publications/2017a4cb9a7915aa1ace.md)

Amani Ayad Husain; Dina Ahmed; Thura Alyasiri; Mohammed Kadhom; Muna  S\. Bufaroosha; Ahmed Ahmed; Emad Yousif

Degradation by ultraviolet \(UV\) radiation is still one of the most important issues affecting the long\-term effectiveness and sustainability of polymers used outdoors\. In this context, a ternary polymer blend of poly\(vinyl chloride\) \(PVC\), polystyrene \(PS\), and poly\(methyl methacrylate\) \(PMMA\) was synthesized by solution casting and loaded with metal oxide nanoparticles \(NPs\) \(e\.g\., MgO, ZnO, TiO2, and NiO\) at low concentration levels as UV photostabilizers\. The incorporation of metal oxide NPs in the polymer system was done under accelerated UV irradiation \(up to 300 hours\) and the efficiency of the nanoparticles to prevent UV\-induced degradation was investigated\. The degree of UV photostabilization was evaluated by FTIR spectroscopy, weight loss, and atomic force microscopy \(AFM\) studies\. The FTIR investigations showed a significant concentration of carbonyl groups in the untreated film; this is indicating that the polymer experienced some photo\-oxidation during the UV exposure\. The films with metal oxide nanoparticles showed comparatively lower carbonyl index than those of the unmodified polymer blend\. Besides, the treated samples showed less weight loss compared to the blank samples\. In addition, AFM examination revealed that the modified films had a lower surface roughness and cracking, in addition to less morphology degradation following UV irradiation\. The higher photostabilization observed is associated with the ability of metal oxides to absorb harmful UV radiation, thus inhibiting radical reactions responsible for the degradation process in the polymer matrix\. Metal oxide nanoparticles can, therefore, be considered an effective method of enhancing UV resistance of polymeric films for use in various applications\. The selection of these four nanoparticles was therefore intended to enable a meaningful comparison of their photostabilizing efficiencies rather than to assume equivalent performance\. Their incorporation at low concentrations also allows their UV\-screening effect to be investigated while minimizing potential adverse effects associated with high nanoparticle loading, such as aggregation and changes in the physical properties of the polymer matrix\. The comparison is particularly relevant to the present PVC/PS/PMMA blend, for which the effectiveness of these oxide nanoparticles as UV stabilizers has not been sufficiently established\.

## [More than one and less than many: research and care in pediatric first\-in\-human cell and gene therapy clinical trials](../publications/20184785ddc73fe4dcee.md)

Stanislav Birko; Ma’n H\. Zawati

The pediatric context poses specific challenges to the clinical translation of cell and gene therapies\. We conducted a narrative review of literature addressing the responsibilities of researcher\-clinicians in the context of clinical trials using cell and gene therapies, with an emphasis on first\-in\-human trials in minors\. The inclusion criteria of our search yielded 16 papers, one of them addressing the exact intersection we were looking at, with the others circling this intersection\. Only one of these 16 papers make a link to the wider theoretical debate on the tension between fulfilling the aims of clinical care and the aims of clinical research when conducting clinical trials–what is often referred to as the similarity vs\. difference debate–and this debate’s connection to discussions of the central concept of the therapeutic misconception\. Building on others’ claim that the similarity vs\. difference framing is too simplistic to capture real\-world nuance, we note that the concepts of therapeutic misconception and clinical equipoise both depend on mutually exclusive positions in this debate\. We do not argue for jettisoning either of these concepts\. Instead, we consider the resulting paradox to be productive\. It is productive to integrate discussions of the therapeutic misconception and clinical equipoise into the similarity vs\. difference debate, as the limitations of these discussions become more apparent in conjunction\. In other words, researcher\-clinicians taking their ethical duties seriously do not need to ‘solve’ these debates, but neither should this free them from engaging with the debates\. Additionally, we discuss the legal context of cell and gene therapies in North America, concluding that nothing in the surveyed ethical literature suggests that greater uncertainties inherent in the field of early\-phase cell or gene therapy trials justify relaxation of standards around informed consent for cell and gene therapy clinical trials\.

## [IMU\-Based Bilateral Kinematic Waveform Analysis Associated with Shoulder Pain History in Competitive Swimmers](../publications/2019cf944d29a68cdc74.md)

Ben Gronbach; Kyle Capili; Fatemeh Khatami

Shoulder injuries are one of the most common overuse problems in competitive swimming, yet objective, field\-deployable methods for quantifying pain\-related movement alterations remain limited\. This study investigates whether bilateral IMU sensors placed on the upper humerus can identify kinematic bilateral waveform similarities tied to a history of shoulder pain in swimmers\. In this study, thirty\-four NCAA Division 1 collegiate swimmers and water polo players completed a standardized swimming test and were classified into moderate/severe pain \(n = 22\) and none/mild pain \(n = 12\) groups based on self\-reported shoulder pain scores\. Kinematic features were extracted and evaluated using statistical tests and machine learning classification\. The none/mild pain group showed a higher peak left\-right shoulder cross\-correlation across all axes \(0\.85 vs\. 0\.78, p = 0\.002\)\. The best\-performing model Classification accuracy for distinguishing between moderate/severe pain and none/mild pain conditions achieved a balanced accuracy of 70\.6% \(24/34 participants\), with a balanced accuracy of 69\.7% \(95% CI \[52\.7–85\.2%\]\) and an ROC AUC of 0\.731 \(95% CI \[0\.557–0\.890\]\), suggesting that personalized machine learning approaches may be necessary to improve individual\-level classification performance\. Further investigation of intra\-subject associations between shoulder pain history and kinematic bilateral waveform similarities is warranted to better understand their relationship and determine potential causal mechanisms\.

## [Re\-thinking Energy Markets in Times of the Energy Transition : Implications for Market Design and Regulation](../publications/201d39cfa1d5862afaa6.md)

Lisa Hanny

Modern energy systems are undergoing a profound transformation\. The traditional model of centralized power plants delivering electricity to largely passive consumers is giving way to a decentralized and participatory landscape\. Rooftop solar panels, electric vehicles, storage devices, and smart household technologies are shifting the flow of energy and information, creating new opportunities for market participation and trading products such as flexibility services\. At the same time, these developments introduce unprecedented complexity: balancing variable renewable generation, coordinating millions of distributed energy resources, and ensuring grid stability are challenges that demand re\-thinking existing system and market structures\. In this context, energy flexibility emerges as a key mechanism, enabling participants to actively shape supply and demand, respond to market signals, and integrate low\-carbon technologies\. In this sense, electricity consumers or &quot;prosumers&quot; become active market participants, providing flexibility services that stabilize the system while benefiting economically\. Yet flexibility alone is insufficient without clear incentives, reliable monitoring, and transparent reward structures embedded in a suitable market design\. Digital technologies provide the critical bridge between market design goals and real\-world behavioural changes\. They help operationalize incentive schemes, monitor the behaviour of a growing number of market participants, and make economic rewards, e\.g\., from flexibility provision, tangible\. Hence, these technologies transform energy from a passive commodity into an interactive service, allowing markets, regulators, and consumers to interact in small time intervals and exchange a broad portfolio of energy\-related goods and services\. This dissertation explores how decentralization, sustainability, and digitalization intersect to reshape energy systems\. It highlights how digital technologies can operationalize incentives, enhance system resilience, and make energy markets more transparent, efficient, and participatory\. Ultimately, it argues that the energy transition is not just a technical challenge, but a societal one requiring an interdisciplinary consideration of policy goals and regulations as well as digital technologies\.

## [An Intelligent Machine Learning Framework for Early Detection of CI/CD Pipeline Failures](../publications/202837f67000975e48c9.md)

Sana Fatima; Muazzam Khan; Shayan Faiz

Continuous integration and continuous delivery \(CI/CD\) pipelines automate software build, testing, and deployment workflows, but failures can delay releases and consume engineering resources\. This study investigates early failure detection using an adaptive ensemble of XGBoost, bidirectional long short\-term memory \(Bi\-LSTM\), and a BERT encoder, combined through a gating multilayer perceptron\. The evaluation covers 194,400 pipeline executions from Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps, and CircleCI\. A candidate space of 167 features captures build metrics, log semantics, resource utilization, test outcomes, code changes, and dependencies\. Nine models are compared using precision, recall, F1\-score, AUC\-ROC, and training time\. The ensemble achieves an F1\-score of 0\.940 and an AUC\-ROC of 0\.974, compared with 0\.924 and 0\.961 for BERT\. At checkpoints corresponding to 10%, 25%, and 50% of estimated pipeline duration, failure\-detection rates are 54\.2%, 78\.6%, and 91\.3%, with mean warning lead times of 14\.1, 8\.7, and 4\.3 minutes, respectively\. The results indicate a trade\-off between earlier warnings and detection coverage\. Build\-duration deviation, error\-keyword frequency, and CPU spikes receive the highest feature\-importance scores\. Interpretation is limited by unequal model feature sets, the absence of leave\-one\-platform\-out results, and incomplete end\-to\-end training\-cost accounting\. Future evaluation should examine threshold calibration, temporal drift, and false\-alarm costs before operational deployment\.

## [Attention\-guided hybrid transformer\-ensemble framework for emotional vulnerability detection in cancer patient and caregiver narratives](../publications/20289b64023437bb1877.md)

Md\. Siam Ansary

Understanding the emotional vulnerability of cancer patients and caregivers is critical for improving psychological support and clinical intervention strategies\. With the rapid growth of online health communities, large volumes of textual narratives describing treatment experiences and emotional struggles have become available for computational analysis\. However, accurately capturing emotional intensity and contextual sentiment in such narratives remains challenging due to the complex linguistic patterns present in health\-related discussions\. This study proposes an attention\-guided hybrid transformer\-ensemble learning framework for emotional vulnerability detection in cancer\-related social media posts\. The proposed architecture integrates domain\-adapted contextual representations generated by BioBERT with linguistic intensity features to capture both semantic context and emotional strength\. An attention\-based feature fusion mechanism dynamically combines these heterogeneous features to produce enriched representations of patient narratives\. The fused representations are subsequently utilized by multiple optimized machine learning classifiers, including XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and CatBoost\. Hyperparameter optimization is performed using the Optuna framework to improve predictive performance\. Furthermore, ensemble learning strategies such as soft voting, hard voting, and stacking are employed to combine the predictions of the base classifiers\. Experiments conducted on a held\-out split of a publicly available dataset of 10,391 posts from cancer patients and caregivers demonstrate that ensemble approaches consistently outperform individual classifiers on this data\. The stacking ensemble achieves an accuracy of 0\.76 and an ROC\-AUC of 0\.91, outperforming its own individual base classifiers but not a fine\-tuned BioBERT baseline \(accuracy 0\.77, ROC\-AUC 0\.92\) evaluated on the same split; a TF\-IDF with linear SVM baseline is also competitive \(accuracy 0\.763\)\. The framework’s practical advantage over full BioBERT fine\-tuning is therefore computational rather than purely predictive: it reuses frozen BioBERT features and adds a lightweight, interpretable attention\-fusion and tree\-ensemble stage at a fraction of the training cost, while an ablation study confirms that the attention\-based fusion of contextual and lexical\-intensity signals meaningfully outperforms either signal alone or their simple concatenation\. The proposed framework thus provides a scalable, lower\-cost computational approach that can support mental health monitoring and early intervention systems in online healthcare communities, at a modest accuracy cost relative to full transformer fine\-tuning\.

## [The Rise of Populism in the U\.S\.: A Study of Regional Wealth Inequality](../publications/2031962cdce26dec4be2.md)

Aryan Surendranath

This paper investigates the role of regional wealth inequality in driving the rise of populism in the United States\. Distinct from prior studies that primarily focus on income disparities, this paper’s analysis examines wealth measures, specifically median wealth and the wealth Gini coefficient, to capture the deeper, structural economic divides that underpin political behaviour\. Using state\-level and county\-level voting data from the MIT Election Data and Science Lab alongside wealth data from the GEOWEALTH\-US database, the paper employs a series of ordinary least squares \(OLS\) regression models with demographic controls and state fixed effects, supplemented by instrumental variables \(IV\) analysis using historical state estate/inheritance taxes as an exogenous source of variation\. The results indicate that at the county level, higher median wealth is generally associated with lower populist vote shares, and increased wealth inequality within a county is positively correlated with populist support under the most robust preferred model specifications, with IV estimates confirming these relationships\. Overall, the findings suggest that long\-term wealth disparities may be a critical driver of populist sentiment, offering new insights into the political economy of contemporary electoral dynamics\.

## [Human uniqueness and vulnerability to mental disorder](../publications/2045b4e63ad846dc8005.md)

Riadh Abed; Benjamin Griffin; Paul St John‐Smith

Summary Among all animals, humans stand out as uniquely vulnerable to mental disorder\. Explaining this vulnerability constitutes a central challenge for psychiatry that requires an explicitly evolutionary approach\. A necessary first step is a rigorous scientific account of human uniqueness: species\-specific psychological/behavioural traits distinguishing Homo sapiens from other animals\.

## [Design and development of an automated telephone ordering system using artificial intelligence](../publications/2047cffdafa503d916c1.md)

Ελευθέριος Βλάχος

Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία πραγματεύεται τον σχεδιασμό και την ανάπτυξη ενός συστήματος αυτόματης λήψης και διαχείρισης τηλεφωνικών παραγγελιών για επιχειρήσεις εστίασης, με αξιοποίηση τεχνολογιών Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και Επεξεργασίας Φυσικής Γλώσσας\. Η ανάγκη για την ανάπτυξη ενός τέτοιου συστήματος προκύπτει από τις δυσκολίες που μπορεί να παρουσιάζει η παραδοσιακή τηλεφωνική καταγραφή παραγγελιών, όπως λάθη στην καταχώρηση, καθυστερήσεις και αυξημένη απασχόληση του προσωπικού\. Στόχος της εργασίας είναι η δημιουργία ενός λειτουργικού πρωτοτύπου που μπορεί να λαμβάνει την προφορική παραγγελία του πελάτη, να επεξεργάζεται το περιεχόμενό της και να τη μετατρέπει σε δομημένη μορφή, ώστε να μπορεί να αποθηκευτεί, να ελεγχθεί και να διαχειριστεί από το προσωπικό της επιχείρησης\. Για την υλοποίηση του συστήματος συνδυάζονται σύγχρονες τεχνολογίες αναγνώρισης ομιλίας, Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων και ανάκτησης σχετικής πληροφορίας, ενώ παράλληλα υποστηρίζεται η λειτουργία πολλαπλών καταστημάτων με διαφορετικά μενού\. Η αξιολόγηση της εφαρμογής πραγματοποιήθηκε τόσο σε λειτουργικό επίπεδο, μέσω αντιπροσωπευτικών σεναρίων δοκιμών, όσο και ως προς τη χρηστικότητά της\. Για την αξιολόγηση της εμπειρίας χρήσης εφαρμόστηκε η μέθοδος System Usability Scale \(SUS\)\. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι το προτεινόμενο σύστημα μπορεί να αποτελέσει μια λειτουργική βάση για την αυτοματοποίηση της τηλεφωνικής λήψης παραγγελιών, διατηρώντας παράλληλα τη δυνατότητα ανθρώπινου ελέγχου και παρέμβασης όπου αυτό απαιτείται\.

## [University Academic Logos Versus Athletic Logos: Who Is Viewing Matters More Than Which Logo Is Shown](../publications/20538f54499804fce61f.md)

Rand Wergin; Bartlomiej Hanus

Universities invest heavily in distinct academic and athletic logos, assuming that these visual signals communicate different institutional value propositions to prospective students\. Drawing on signaling theory, this study asks whether viewers’ dispositional traits shape their attitudes toward a university, and whether the type of logo encountered moderates those relationships\. Using a fictitious university and AI\-generated academic and athletic logos, we surveyed 387 respondents, each evaluating one logo, and modeled the data using partial least squares structural equation modeling\. The traits of task/goal orientation, need for learning, and need for social resources each predicted more favorable attitudes toward the institution, with need for social resources the strongest predictor, whereas need for competition did not contribute independently\. Critically, a multigroup analysis found no significant difference in any relationship between the academic\-logo and athletic\-logo conditions, indicating that viewer dispositions, rather than logo type, drove institutional attitudes\. These results qualify the common assumption that academic and athletic logos function as sharply distinct signals and suggest that who is viewing matters more than which logo is shown\.

## [Issues of improving service quality in the hotel and restaurant industry](../publications/20611856d903c026dbd2.md)

Ольга Олійник; Volodymyr Kotsiuk

The hospitality industry plays a vital role in the global economy, providing services that require the highest standards to ensure customer satisfaction and operational success\. Managing quality in this environment involves a combination of effective, efficient operations\. This article explores the challenges and best practices of quality assurance in the hospitality industry, highlighting the importance of customer service delivery, employee training, and technological advancements\. A key component of quality control is the use of standardized methods\. These frameworks help businesses maintain operational efficiency, reduce risk, and improve the customer experience\. Furthermore, training and motivating employees play an important role in ensuring service quality\. Trained employees can effectively address customer needs, solve problems, and contribute to a successful brand\. Another important factor is customer feedback and continuous improvement\. The ability to receive, analyze, and adapt to customer feedback is critical to maintaining a competitive advantage\. In the digital age, online reviews and ratings have a major impact on customer decisions, making quality management a top priority for businesses\. Technological innovations such as artificial intelligence, automation, and intelligent service systems have revolutionized the quality of the hospitality industry\. AI\-powered chatbots, automated reservation systems, and data analytics enable businesses to personalize customer experiences, streamline processes, and improve operational efficiency\. However, despite technological advances, challenges such as employee turnover, cultural differences, and regulatory compliance still plague quality management\. A successful strategy involves balancing resource integration and people\-centric service delivery, ensuring that hospitality companies not only meet industry standards but also exceed customer expectations\. The article concludes that quality management is a dynamic and ongoing process that requires strategic planning, employee engagement, and adaptation to changing customer preferences\. The future of successful management in the hospitality industry will be shaped by digital transformation, sustainable development initiatives, and an increased focus on personalized service\.

## [ANALYSIS OF DIGITAL MULTITASKING HABITS ON SHORT\-TERM MEMORY OF GRADE XII STUDENTS OF OUTSTANDING G AT AL\-AZHAR SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL MEDAN](../publications/206978707db617905905.md)

Syifa Sahira Purba; Al Fathir Aruli; Annisa Nailatul Izzah; RM\. Bimo SWKP; Rafi Anaya Marwan; Nurjamiaty

The development of digital technology has changed the way students obtain information and interact with devices during learning activities\. One increasingly common habit is digital multitasking, which involves studying while using social media, messaging services, music, videos, or other applications\. Repeated attention shifts can increase demands on cognitive resources and potentially impact the ability to retain information in the short term\. This study aims to analyze the relationship between digital multitasking habits and short\-term memory in grade XII Unggulan G students at Al\-Azhar High School, Medan\. The study used a quantitative approach with a correlational design\. Data were planned to be collected through a digital multitasking habits questionnaire and a short\-term memory test\. Analysis included descriptive statistics and a Pearson Product Moment correlation test if statistical assumptions were met\. This study is expected to provide an empirical overview of the relationship between digital device usage habits and students&\#x27; cognitive processes and serve as a basis for developing more targeted learning strategies\.

## [Reciprocal teaching para sa pag\-unawa sa maikling kuwentong Asyano ng Baitang 9](../publications/206f08a5300e038ff596.md)

Rina D Rosaceña

Nilayon ng pag\-aaral na ito na masuri ang kahusayan ng paggamit ng reciprocal teaching bilang estratehiya sa pagtuturo sa mga mag\-aaral sa pag\-unawa sa maikling kuwento ng Baitang 9 sa Daanbantayan National High School sa taong panuruan 2025\-2026 bilang batayan sa pagbuo ng kagamitang pampagtuturo\.Gumamit ang pananaliksik ng One Group Pretest\-Posttest Quasi\-experimental Design na nilahukan ng 50 mag\-aaral ng Baitang 9\. Dalawang pangunahing instrumento ang ginamit: test kwestyuner at sarbey kwestyuner na binuo alinsunod sa mga pamantayan ng K to 12 Basic Education Curriculum\.Sinukat ang antas ng pag\-unawa sa binasa bago at pagkatapos ng interbensiyon, ang makabuluhang pagkakaiba ng pauna at panghuling pagganap, at ang pananaw ng mga mag\-aaral sa paggamit ng Reciprocal Teaching\.Ipinakita ng mga resulta na bago ang interbensiyon, ang antas ng pag\-unawa ng mga mag\-aaral sa maikling kuwentong Asyano ay nasa katamtamang antas\.Pagkatapos ng paggamit ng Reciprocal Teaching, tumaas ang kanilang pagganap sa mahusay hanggang napakahusay na antas sa lahat ng kasanayang sinukat\.Pinatunayan ng paired t\-test na may makabuluhang pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng pauna at panghuling pagganap na may p\-value na &lt;0\.001, dahilan upang iwaksi ang null hypothesis\.Ipinahihiwatig ng mga natuklasan na ang Reciprocal Teaching ay mabisang estratehiya sa pagpapalalim ng kritikal, analitikal, at interpretatibong pag\-unawa ng mga mag\-aaral sa pagbasa ng maikling kuwentong Asyano sa antas sekundarya\.

## [Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent\-Safety Evaluations](../publications/20705ae78b404bf072cc.md)

Hasan Demirkiran; Jens Ernstberger

AI agents take actions through tools\. Some actions are sensitive, so guards that supervise them must themselves be evaluated reliably\. Yet the data used to evaluate a guard can include cues that make labels predictable without measuring the intended safety construct, and those cues can also influence guard decisions\. We introduce a three\-level shortcut\-auditing framework and audit completed LinuxArena trajectories and two TS\-Bench\-derived step datasets\. We distinguish label predictability, observational guard association, and paired decision sensitivity\. In LinuxArena, shorter average shell commands strongly predict trajectory labels\. In AgentDojo\-Traj, exact\-tool lookup falls from F\_1=\.901 with mixed\-domain folds to \.495 under domain holdout\. In AgentHarm\-Traj, released TS\-Guard F\_1 falls from \.902 under row weighting to \.719 with equal interaction weighting, while balanced accuracy rises\. We then test the strongest safe\-row marker association in a seven\-configuration screen on a frozen 64\-step AgentDojo\-Traj cohort using repeated, interleaved Haiku calls\. Rewriting the &lt;INFORMATION&gt; marker lowers blocking by 8\.33 percentage points, while opaque tool aliases raise it by 11\.46 points\. All unsafe calls remain blocked; the changes concern false positives against inherited labels\. Both effects remain nonzero after subtracting the formatting\-placebo effect, with exploratory 95% ranges excluding zero\. The same edits also change measured accuracy against inherited labels\. This provides direct evidence that benchmark representation can materially change a guard&\#x27;s decisions and measured evaluation performance\. The Haiku\-sized effects do not reproduce in Luna or deterministic Q8 TS\-Guard\. We recommend domain group holdouts, evaluation\-unit metrics, and placebo\-controlled paired interventions\.

## [University physical education course experience and resilience\-based psychological recovery capacity among students in Chinese higher education: indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self\-efficacy, and peer connectedness](../publications/2080fb764e64f8c3ac43.md)

Wendong Yang; Liangfang Meng

University students face increasing psychological pressure, yet formal mental health services often remain limited in reach and depend on active help\-seeking\. This study examines university physical education \(PE\) as an educational context whose perceived qualities may be associated with psychological resources relevant to adaptation under stress\. Using cross\-sectional survey data from 831 Chinese college students, we examined whether perceived PE course experience was associated with resilience\-based psychological recovery capacity and whether this association was indirectly linked through emotion regulation, exercise self\-efficacy, and peer connectedness\. The retained measurement specification represented PE course experience as a second\-order construct comprising teacher support, mastery climate, embodied engagement, emotional release, and peer interaction\. Structural equation modeling indicated that PE course experience was positively associated with resilience\-based psychological recovery capacity and with all three proposed indirect\-linking variables\. Bootstrapping results supported significant indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self\-efficacy, and peer connectedness, with exercise self\-efficacy showing the largest estimated indirect association\. The association remained significant after controlling for perceived stress and extracurricular exercise frequency\. These findings link perceived PE course qualities with resilience\-based adaptive capacity, conditional on the measured covariates\. They do not isolate curriculum effects from physical\-activity exposure\. Because the design is cross\-sectional, the findings should be interpreted as theoretically grounded associations rather than causal effects\.

## [COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS AND EXPLAINABILITY METHODS FOR ECG HEARTBEAT CLASSIFICATION](../publications/208200dc6a83472a26fd.md)

Jessica Fernandes Lopes; Felipe Torquato Bressan; Rafael S\. Bressan; Danilo Sipoli Sanches

This study compared a 1D\-CNN architecture and a hybrid CNN\-BiLSTM\-Attention model for multiclass electrocardiographic heartbeat classification, incorporating Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques to evaluate the faithfulness and temporal distribution of the evidence used by the models\. Experiments used a dataset derived from the MIT\-BIH Arrhythmia Database, organized into the Normal, Supraventricular, Ventricular, Fusion, and Unclassified classes\. The protocol employed five\-fold stratified cross\-validation exclusively on the training set, epoch selection based on Macro F1 in an internal validation partition, and final evaluation on an untouched holdout test set\. The 1D\-CNN achieved a test Macro F1 of 0\.8681 versus 0\.8140 for the CNN\-BiLSTM\-Attention model, whereas the hybrid model achieved higher Balanced Accuracy, 0\.9441 versus 0\.9264, indicating higher average class\-wise recall\. Explainability analysis employed 1D Grad\-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and temporal attention on a class\-balanced subset of samples correctly classified by both architectures\. Under the adopted perturbation protocol, Integrated Gradients showed positive mean faithfulness gains across all classes for both architectures, whereas Grad\-CAM and temporal attention exhibited more class\-dependent behavior\. Low\-to\-moderate agreement among the methods indicated that different techniques may emphasize distinct temporal regions for the same correct prediction\. Within this experimental setting, the additional complexity of the hybrid model did not translate into uniformly better predictive performance, supporting the complementary evaluation of predictive performance and explainability in ECG classification\.

## [The circadian system and its role in the development of metabolic disorders in obesity](../publications/208d871beb205b45997c.md)

Yu\. V\. Nelaeva; M\. R\. Nekrasova; Alsu Asatovna Nelaeva

The circadian system coordinates the functioning of the human body throughout the day\. The circadian rhythms affect the adipose tissue metabolism by regulating lipolysis and lipogenesis through the transcription of the main encoding genes\. In the case of circadian rhythm disorders, biochemical, neuroendocrine and molecular\-genetic processes in adipose tissue change, and insulin resistance increases, ultimately leading to metabolic syndrome development\. The metabolism of organs and tissues regulates by changing the sleep\-wake cycles, which are directly related to the feeding\-fasting cycle\. Melatonin is of great importance for energy homeostasis control and carbohydrate metabolism\. Its dysfunction follows by such metabolic disorders as obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular diseases\.

## [Medical Decision‐Making Capacity in Early‐Stage Alzheimer Patients: Comparison With Healthy Controls and Benefit of Assistive Information](../publications/209769146c243e3532a7.md)

Dilara Aylin Felice Vossberg; Vasilija Rolfes; Heiner Fangerau; Martin Haupt

BACKGROUND: Early\-stage Alzheimer Disease \(AD\) may lead to restricted decision\-making capacity and without standardized instruments, there is great variability in determining patients&\#x27; ability to give consent\. This study aimed to assess decision\-making capacity of AD patients in comparison to a healthy control group and investigated the usefulness of visual aids\. METHODS: A group of 30 ad patients and 30 healthy controls were compared using the MacArthur Competence Assessment Tool for Treatment \(MacCAT\-T\)\. Additionally, we implemented a modified version of the MacCAT\-T with visual aids\. RESULTS: Results revealed a significant difference in the MacCAT\-T domain of Understanding between the AD and control group after adjustment for age, sex, and education\. No significant differences were found for Appreciation, Reasoning, or Expression of Choice\. Adding visual aids led to no significant improvements\. CONCLUSIONS: Standardized assessments can be valuable tools for determining the decision\-making capacity of patients with early\-stage AD\. The efficacy of visual aids should be further investigated\.

## [Review of Memory and the Gothic Aesthetic in Film](../publications/2099b05d0e24097fb7b2.md)

Ali Najaf Dokht

This review considers Joana Jacob Ramalho’s Memory and the Gothic Aesthetic in Film \(2025\), which proposes the cinematic Gothic as a transnational aesthetics of memory shaped by exile, travel, and touch\. It assesses the book’s theoretical framework, its account of “travelling directors,” and its analyses of haptic and amnesiac memory, and notes where the politics of memory could be developed further\.

## [Mediación asistida por inteligencia artificial: implicaciones éticas en la resolución de conflictos](../publications/20a465a28248d2287d6b.md)

Martha Cecilia Rosero\-Puetate; Jhon Sebastián Fuertes\-Realpe; Hamilton Fernando Lucero\-Arellano; Angie Michelle Velasco\-Campaña

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is entering alternative dispute resolution and raises ethical questions about party autonomy, impartiality and transparency\. The study analysed the ethical implications of AI\-assisted mediation, with emphasis on its possible use in Ecuador\. The research was qualitative and documentary, reviewing scholarship, domestic rules, international instruments and studies on online dispute resolution\. The results indicate that AI can improve efficiency and widen access, but it carries risks of dehumanisation, algorithmic opacity and reproduction of bias, and that Ecuadorian law does not regulate its use in mediation\. It is concluded that adoption requires ethical principles, specific regulation and constant human oversight\.

## [The unnoticed understanding: Searle’s Chinese room and the illegitimate inference](../publications/20af1b4006e96f9d6155.md)

Yu Pei

Contemporary debates about large language models \(LLMs\) remain shaped by the logical structure of Searle’s Chinese Room Argument \(1980\)\. Sceptics routinely argue that since LLMs merely manipulate statistical patterns without understanding the content they process, they possess no genuine understanding or mentality\. This inferential pattern recapitulates Searle’s move from “the person in the room does not understand Chinese” to “running a program is insufficient for mentality”\. This paper argues that this inference is illegitimate\. It accepts Searle’s premise that the person in the Chinese Room does not understand Chinese\. However, it shows that the person does understand something else: the rule system itself\. This understanding is genuine and intrinsic by Searle’s own criteria, and it is acquired during the process of running the program\. Searle’s argument therefore contains an unacknowledged inferential gap: from “no understanding of the processed content” to “no understanding whatsoever”\. Furthermore, Searle’s structural equivalence premise, that the person and the computer are doing the same thing, is shown to constitute a double\-edged sword: if consistently applied, it prevents Searle from denying that the machine may possess an analogue of the person’s understanding\. The Chinese Room Argument cannot establish its intended conclusion\.

## [A novel imbalanced learning using dynamic multiclass evolutionary oversampling sigmoid deep neural network techniques](../publications/20b90ac8b82175fb8bfc.md)

V\.S\. Nageswara Rao Kadiyala; Sabuzima Nayak; Ripon Patgiri

The majority and minority class data variably reduce the quality of the data produced and make the network harder to train for class\-imbalanced datasets\. It is uncertain how the minority class data are distributed and how they are input into the model\. Furthermore, due to their significant bias in favour of the majority class, typical machine learning classifiers suffer considerably\. To address these issues, we proposed multi‑class data stream learning using evolutionary and oversampling \(EVOS\) techniques\. Evolutionary feature selection and effective oversampling combine for multi\-class data stream learning\. ## [Fuzzy Logic\-Based Modeling and Multi\-Objective Optimization of Blood Pump Rotational Speed Considering Hydraulic and Hemolytic Performance](../publications/20be16f56925b95722ab.md)

Abdoulaye Billo Diallo; Hasan Çınar; Ömer İncebay; Rafet Yapıcı

This study aims to determine the optimal operating rotational speed of a centrifugal blood pump\. In order to investigate this, a centrifugal blood pump was designed, and its hydraulic efficiency and hemolysis index were calculated using computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\) simulations over a range of 2500\-3500 rpm for rotational speed and 2\.5\-6 L/min for flow rate\. The pump design was carried out by considering key geometric parameters, including the number of blades, inlet and outlet widths, inlet and outlet angles, impeller diameter, volute inlet width, and volute outlet diameter\. Subsequently, a fuzzy logic\-based pump model was developed using rotational speed and mass flow rate as input parameters, and pressure difference, hemolysis index, and hydraulic efficiency as output parameters\. After validating this model with CFD simulations, the optimal pump rotational speed was determined by solving an objective function incorporating hydraulic efficiency and hemolysis index using the particle swarm optimization \(PSO\) algorithm\. The results indicate that the optimal rotational speed of the centrifugal pump is 3150 rpm, at which a hydraulic efficiency of 36% and a hemolysis index \(HI\) of 1\.65x10\-5 are achieved\. In summary, this study presents a systematic methodology for determining the optimal operating speed that enables centrifugal blood pumps to operate efficiently while maintaining a low hemolysis index\.

## [Knowledge to action phenomenon beyond the healthcare discipline: a scoping review](../publications/20da6f67bb16aeb277ac.md)

Rou Szen Lim; Tvisha Devireddy; Sarah Nicole Dunn Phillips; Kathryn M\. McDonald

The knowledge to action \(K2A\) phenomenon encompasses the process in which research is converted into practical applications leading to meaningful impacts in real\-world settings\. Research in the K2A field has been burgeoning across disciplines, with the development and use of various K2A theories, models, and frameworks \(TMFs\)\. However, there is concern that limited cross\-disciplinary communication in the K2A field reduces novel synergies and insights across contexts\. A more robust understanding of how K2A is enacted in different contexts rests upon examining how K2A research is conceptualized and applied to the knowing\-doing gap in different disciplines\. Prior scoping reviews of K2A TMFs are limited to the healthcare discipline\. Expanding beyond healthcare, this scoping review aims to \(1\) identify the K2A TMF\(s\) used in three non\-healthcare disciplines, \(2\) characterize the K2A TMF\(s\) used, and \(3\) identify the prevalent components\. Articles published in the business, education and environmental sciences/studies disciplines were identified using Web of Science and Scopus\. Included studies satisfied the following criteria: reported and described the use of a K2A TMF\(s\), described an intervention, and were published in English between 2019–2024\. A total of 2702 articles were screened, and 39 studies were included for data extraction\. 38 distinct K2A TMF\(s\) were identified, 63% of which were not previously identified in healthcare scoping reviews\. The most common K2A TMF\(s\) used were the Technology Acceptance Model \( n = 4\), the Diffusion of Innovation Theory \( n = 4\), and the Theory of Planned Behaviour \( n = 3\)\. In 69% of K2A TMF applications, a rationale was provided for its selection\. This review demonstrates how K2A TMFs are applied in three disciplines beyond healthcare and generates possibilities for further cross\-pollinating research across disciplines that have developed rich but siloed approaches\. Identifying and comparing classifications and applications of K2A TMFs across disciplines strengthens the transdisciplinary character and integration of K2A research\.

## [Artificial intelligence as academic infrastructure: governance, administrative intelligence, and AI fluency in Kazakhstan’s higher education sector](../publications/20e45dea65aac15d9a02.md)

Rajasekhara Mouly Potluri; Victoria Polozova

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly part of higher education&\#x27;s institutional infrastructure, extending beyond teaching and learning to governance, administration, and student support\. This study examines how AI Governance Readiness \(AIGR\) influences Administrative Efficiency through AI \(AEAI\), AI Fluency Orientation \(AIFO\), and Student Retention Intentions \(SRI\), while assessing the mediating roles of AEAI and AIFO and the moderating role of Equity Perception \(EPS\) in Kazakhstan&\#x27;s higher education sector\. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study develops and empirically tests an institutional capability model using 935 valid responses from students, faculty, academic administrators, and digital administration staff across public and private universities\. The scholars analyzed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) in SmartPLS 4\.0, supported by RStudio\. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, while the structural model showed adequate explanatory and predictive performance\. We assessed common method bias through procedural safeguards and full\-collinearity diagnostics, and identified no substantive concerns\. The findings show that AIGR is positively associated with AEAI and AIFO, while both constructs positively influence SRI\. AEAI and AIFO also significantly mediate the relationship between AIGR and SRI\. However, EPS does not significantly moderate the relationships between AI\-enabled institutional capabilities and retention intentions\. The findings position AI governance as a strategic institutional capability through which universities can improve administrative responsiveness, develop AI\-related competencies, and support student continuity\. The study contributes empirical evidence from Kazakhstan to the growing literature on responsible AI governance and digital transformation in higher education\.

## [Crowd Detection and Overcrowding Alert System](../publications/20f6f3c1a2eeb2f2c007.md)

Mrs\.Ayesha Siddiqa; Chaitra P; Varsha H R; Sahana H V; Yashaswini S N

A crowd detection and overcrowding alert system is proposed to monitor public spaces and prevent unsafe crowd conditions\. The system applies computer vision and deep learning techniques to analyze live video feeds from surveillance cameras, detecting the number of people present, tracking movement patterns, and estimating crowd density in specific zones\. When density exceeds a predefined safety threshold, the system automatically generates alerts for authorities, enabling timely intervention and helping to prevent accidents, stampedes, and congestion in locations such as malls, transportation hubs, campuses, and public events\. The proposed solution is designed to integrate with existing CCTV infrastructure as well as IoT devices and mobile notification services for faster response, and to provide continuous monitoring and visual insight through a live dashboard so that authorities can easily identify high\-risk zones\. ## [Beyond the Algebraic Product: Generalizing ANFIS with Parametric and Non\-Parametric T\-Norms](../publications/20f9c8878827a6935881.md)

Hélida Santos

Machine Learning and Fuzzy Logic effectively complement each other in neuro\-fuzzy systems, combining data\-driven learning with interpretable reasoning under uncertainty\. A prominent architecture is the Adaptive Neuro\-Fuzzy Inference System \(ANFIS\), which employs the Takagi\-Sugeno method to model complex nonlinear systems\. However, standard ANFIS is traditionally limited to the algebraic product operation in its antecedent layer and often encounters computational bottlenecks on CPU hardware when handling high\-dimensional datasets\. In this work, we propose a generalization of the ANFIS antecedent layer by systematically integrating various families of parametric and non\-parametric t\-norms\. We evaluate this architecture in two distinct environments: a traditional CPU\-based baseline and a GPU\-accelerated framework\. Experiments conducted on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that replacing the fixed product operator with flexible t\-norms improves predictive accuracy and adaptability, and statistical tests confirm the benefits of the proposed generalization\.

## [Antimicrobial light\-based interventions for management of oral infections: a mini review](../publications/210002e56098a0f950e4.md)

Gal Hiltch; Liviu Steier; Katia Rupel; Giulia Ottaviani; José Antônio Poli de Figueiredo

Limitations of conventional disinfectants and rising antimicrobial resistance have accelerated the development of light\-based, resistance\-free interventions\. This mini\-review describes the mechanisms and evidence for antimicrobial photodynamic therapy \(aPDT\), antimicrobial blue light \(aBL\), antimicrobial selective photothermolysis \(aSP\) and photothermal therapy \(PTT\)\. Unlike antibiotics, light\-based interventions avoid inducing microbial resistance or disturbing the host microflora\. Interventions were evaluated across endodontics, periodontal and peri\-implant disease, oral mucosal infections, and dental caries\. Current literature is heavily skewed towards aPDT, leaving other interventions underexplored despite their mechanistic promise\. aPDT is currently the only one with systematic reviews and meta\-analyses, whereas evidence for aBL and PTT remains confined to in\-vitro and preclinical studies\. In periodontitis, aPDT achieved statistical significance, but clinical improvements were negligible and below meaningful thresholds, leading official guidelines from major bodies against its routine use\. Clinical evidence currently supports aPDT only in oral candidiasis, where outcomes matched conventional treatments\. aSP, tested only as pulsed Nd:YAG or CW diode adjuncts to debridement, was not superior to conventional methods, and selectivity has never been measured clinically\. Promising directions are aBL, due to its selectivity for periodontopathogens and link to autofluorescence\-based diagnosis, and PTT for its combined antimicrobial and regeneration capacity\. Physical limiting factors for aPDT and aBL are shallow effective depth and oxygen dependence in anaerobic niches, and a narrow thermal safety margin for aSP and PTT\. A recurring gap is lack of translation between microbial reduction and improved clinical outcomes across interventions, highlighting the need for multi\-center trials based on clinically proven standardized protocols\.

## [AI\-assisted predictive appraisal and preservation prioritisation in television audiovisual archives: a theoretical framework integrating human oversight](../publications/21103c084722acfdb4aa.md)

Jorge Caldera\-Serrano

Introduction\. The article addresses the challenge of examining the possible future archival significance of televised audiovisual documents in television archives\. It introduces Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted predictive appraisal and preservation prioritisation to support archival decision\-making in contexts of audiovisual overproduction and future\-oriented archival judgment, responding to resource, storage, and preservation constraints\. Method\. The study develops a theoretical and conceptual model integrating AI into archival appraisal processes\. It draws on a critical review of specialised literature in archival science, heritage preservation, and computational cultural analysis, with particular attention to content features, contextual information, and production metadata\. This is a critical conceptual literature review rather than an empirical validation\. Analysis\. The analysis identifies patterns relevant to prospective archival appraisal and examines how predictive analytics can be aligned with established archival principles\. It also examines the epistemological and ethical implications of algorithm\-supported appraisal, including questions of bias, legitimacy, and responsibility\. Conclusions\. The article proposes a conceptual framework combining AI\-assisted predictive appraisal with well\-founded archival criteria\. It positions predictive analytics as a complementary tool for optimising curation, prioritising resources, and supporting more strategic and sustainable archive management\. Its contribution is conceptual rather than demonstrative and remains dependent on human oversight, archival interpretation, and documented accountability\.

## [Pemodelan Klasifikasi Tingkat Kerusakan Peralatan Penunjang Akademik Berbasis Natural Language Processing dan Naïve Bayes](../publications/21132794988aaa0f9cd5.md)

Trizaurah Armiani; Diah Novita Sari; Aqila Putri Fathiyah; Rahmawati Dwi Lestari; Muhammad Karison

Pengelolaan laporan kerusakan peralatan akademik menghadapi permasalahan karena informasi kerusakan umumnya disampaikan dalam bentuk teks tidak terstruktur dengan variasi deskripsi yang berbeda\. Kondisi tersebut menyulitkan proses identifikasi tingkat kerusakan secara konsisten dan dapat memperlambat penanganan aset\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menerapkan Natural Language Processing untuk mengolah deskripsi laporan kerusakan dan menggunakan algoritma Naïve Bayes untuk mengklasifikasikan tingkat kerusakan peralatan\. Data penelitian diperoleh dari laporan kerusakan pada Unit Penunjang Akademik Perawatan dan Perbaikan Politeknik Negeri Sriwijaya periode 2021–2026\. Sebanyak 4\.147 data laporan dikumpulkan dan melalui tahap data preparation diperoleh 2\.374 data yang digunakan dalam proses klasifikasi\. Pengolahan teks dilakukan melalui case folding, tokenizing, filtering, dan stemming, kemudian data direpresentasikan menggunakan pembobotan Term Frequency\-Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\)\. Karena distribusi kelas tidak seimbang, Synthetic Minority Over\-sampling Technique \(SMOTE\) diterapkan pada data training sebelum proses klasifikasi menggunakan Naïve Bayes\. Evaluasi terhadap 475 data testing menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 86,53%\. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi text preprocessing, TF\-IDF, SMOTE, dan Naïve Bayes dapat diterapkan untuk mengklasifikasikan tingkat kerusakan peralatan berdasarkan teks laporan kerusakan\.

## [Extraosseous Ewing Sarcoma Presenting as a Shoulder Mass in a 12\-Year\-Old Girl: A Case Report](../publications/2117cb3d0ffe4de72dc3.md)

Sumona Bose; Vikas Dagar; Gaurab Ranjan Chaudhuri; Abanti Das; Indranil Chakrabarti

Introduction: Extraosseous Ewing sarcoma \(EES\) is a rare malignant small round cell tumor of soft tissue, and its occurrence in the pediatric shoulder region is particularly uncommon\. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 12\-year\-old girl who presented with a rapidly enlarging subcutaneous mass over the shoulder\. The lesion was completely excised, followed by flap reconstruction\. Histopathological examination revealed a malignant round cell neoplasm composed of sheets of round to ovoid cells with areas of prominent, staghorn\-like vascular pattern\. Immunohistochemistry showed strong positivity for CD99 and NKX2\.2, supporting a diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma\. Although molecular confirmation could not be performed due to resource limitations, integrated diagnostic evaluation incorporating radiologic features and immunohistochemical profile favored an EWSR1–FLI1 fusion\-associated Ewing sarcoma\.Conclusion: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges in resource\-limited settings and underscores the importance of combined histopathological and ancillary techniques for accurate classification\. Early recognition, complete surgical excision, and appropriate multimodal therapy are essential for achieving favorable outcomes in this rare presentation\.

Data analytics is changing how organisations operate, plan, and compete\. Businesses use data to understand customer behaviour, improve services, reduce costs, and identify new opportunities\. This knowledge can help them select relevant training and prepare for the changing demands of the data analytics profession\. The Growing Importance of Data Analytics Organisations no longer use data only to prepare monthly reports\. They use it to support decisions across sales, finance, marketing, operations, healthcare, manufacturing, and technology\. For example, a retailer can analyse sales records to forecast product demand\. A bank can study transaction patterns to identify suspicious activity\. Artificial Intelligence and AI\-Assisted Analytics Artificial intelligence is one of the most important trends in the analytics industry\. AI tools can help analysts summarise datasets, identify patterns, generate queries, and automate routine tasks\. This can reduce the time spent on some activities and allow professionals to focus more on interpreting results\. For example, an analyst can use AI\-assisted tools to explore sales performance or generate an initial summary of customer feedback\. The analyst must still verify the output, check the data, and confirm that the conclusions are valid\. In June 2026, Gartner identified AI\-first operations, AI governance, and connected data and analytics platforms among the major trends shaping enterprise analytics\. Its report also highlighted the need to manage the risks associated with AI\-driven decisions\. Learners should therefore understand both the benefits and the limits of AI\. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet can provide a foundation in data analysis, while further learning can help students explore AI\-assisted workflows\. Important areas to understand include: Using AI tools to support data exploration\. Checking AI\-generated calculations and summaries\. Understanding the basics of machine learning\. Protecting confidential information when using AI systems\. Applying human judgement to important business decisions\. AI can support analytical work, but it does not remove the need for accurate data, sound reasoning, and accountability\. Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics Traditional reporting often explains what has already happened\. Predictive and prescriptive analytics extend this process by helping organisations estimate possible outcomes and assess potential actions\. Predictive Analytics Predictive analytics uses historical data, statistical methods, and machine learning models to estimate future events\. A retailer may forecast product demand from previous sales\. A financial institution may estimate credit risk\. A logistics company may use historical delivery information to identify the factors linked to delays\. Prescriptive Analytics Prescriptive analytics goes a step further by assessing possible actions based on defined objectives and constraints\. For example, a supply chain team may use an optimisation model to assess delivery routes or inventory levels\. These developments show the value of understanding analytical methods beyond basic reporting\. For example, an e\-commerce company can track order activity and inventory levels during a major sale\. A transport company can monitor vehicle performance and delivery status\. A financial organisation can use real\-time systems to flag transactions that require further review\. Real\-time analytics often depends on data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, streaming technologies, and reliable monitoring systems\. Entry\-level analysts may not build these systems themselves, but an understanding of how data moves from source to dashboard can help them work more effectively with technical teams\. Cloud Analytics and Modern Data Platforms Cloud analytics allows organisations to store, process, and analyse data through cloud\-based services\. It can help teams access information across locations and connect datasets from different business systems\. Cloud platforms also support collaboration and scalable data processing\. However, effective cloud analytics requires suitable access controls, cost management, data quality checks, and security practices\. Modern data platforms increasingly bring together data engineering, analytics, governance, and AI capabilities\. This creates a need for professionals who understand not only how to create a report but also where the data comes from and how it should be used\. Business Intelligence and Data Visualisation Business intelligence remains a key part of modern analytics\. Tools such as Microsoft Power BI and Tableau help users present information through charts, tables, filters, and interactive dashboards\. Excel remains useful for organising data and performing basic analysis\. A well\-designed dashboard can show revenue trends, customer retention, inventory levels, and operating costs in one place\. The analyst must choose suitable metrics and explain their meaning without creating misleading impressions\. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet that includes practical reporting exercises can help learners understand these concepts\. When reviewing a programme, check whether it covers data preparation, dashboard design, data modelling, and the interpretation of business metrics\. Data Quality, Privacy, and Responsible Analytics Advanced tools cannot compensate for poor\-quality data\. Missing values, duplicate records, incorrect formats, and inconsistent definitions can lead to inaccurate reports\. TechTarget&\#x27;s January 2026 review of business intelligence trends highlighted governance, data quality, and responsible access to analytics as important concerns for organisations\. Learners should develop habits that support reliable analysis: Check the source and completeness of a dataset\. Identify duplicate records and inconsistent values\.
