## [Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China](../publications/2124595185dd7d34d37d.md)

Wang Wen\-quan; Ting Du; Jiangxia Ye; Xiaohong Huang; Yangyang Li; Zhonghe Zhang; Lei Shi

BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease \(PWD\), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus \(PWN\), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China\. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single\-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species\-specific contributions\. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species\-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities\. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis\. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios\. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors\. GeoDetector revealed substantial interspecific variation in explanatory power for PWN suitability, with Pinus massoniana, P\. thunbergii, and Monochamus alternatus showing the highest q\-values \(0\.78, 0\.77, and 0\.79, respectively\)\. All host\-vector combinations explained PWN suitability better than either species alone\. CONCLUSION: PWD risk in China cannot be inferred from host or vector availability alone, but is shaped by stronger abiotic constraints on PWN and host\-vector interactions\. Climatically marginal regions with suitable hosts and vectors should be prioritized for surveillance, and species with high q\-values warrant further investigation\. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry\.

## [Toponymic knowledge infrastructures in five\-state Middle Asia: linguistic transformation, manuscript cartography, and historical\-geographical reconstruction](../publications/213bb143859b6afb1112.md)

Bibaisha Iliasovna Nurdauletova; Sholpan Saparbaikyzy; Ж\.О\. Артыкбаев; Tursynkhan Zakonuly Kairken; Saltanat Spatayeva; Elizabeth Shilunga

Toponymic records embedded in Arabic, Persian, and Chinese manuscript traditions provide evidence for reconstructing the historical geographies of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan\. This review uses a structured narrative and conceptual\-synthesis methodology to compare place\-name transmission across languages, scripts, manuscript genres, and political regimes\. A diachronic framework separates pre\-Islamic external attestations, medieval Arabic\-Persian documentation, early\-modern cartography, imperial and Soviet standardisation, and post\-Soviet renaming rather than treating linguistic layers as synchronous\. Direct evidence from the five\-state core is distinguished from supporting evidence from neighbouring transmission corridors and comparative regions\. Micro\-cases of Koneurgenish/Gurganj, Dargan/Dargan\-Ata, hydronymic compounds, and political renaming are combined with explicit cross\-script harmonisation rules and spatial\-chronological triangulation\. Toponymy is operationalised as a sociopolitical knowledge infrastructure when names function as repeatable identifiers linking routes, jurisdictions, administrative records, gazetteers, and maps\. Digital approaches extend this framework through georeferenced historical gazetteers, variant\-name alignment, route modelling, and confidence\-ranked reconstruction\. Reliable interpretation depends on preserving source provenance, separating transliteration from phonological reconstruction, and distinguishing linguistic change from administrative replacement\.

## [Responsible integration of generative AI and LLMs in higher education: Empirical insights and a framework for teaching and learning](../publications/215ba433382dafd3c32a.md)

Jose A\. Diaz\-Garcia; Roberto Morcillo\-Jiménez; Bartolomé Ortiz\-Viso; Maria Dolores Ruiz

Generative AI \(GenAI\) tools are rapidly reshaping university learning environments, yet pedagogical and ethical frameworks have not developed at the same pace as their adoption\. Adopting a multidisciplinary approach, this study combines empirical evidence from a survey of 117 undergraduate Engineering and Health Sciences students with the pedagogical perspectives of university lecturers\. It examines how students currently use GenAI and how these tools can be meaningfully integrated into teaching and learning\. Findings show that students’ first exposure to GenAI is mainly driven by informal social media channels rather than institutional guidance, resulting in uneven and often unguided adoption\. The study also identifies a “contradictory profile” in 11% of the sample: students who perceive GenAI use as a form of cheating while also expressing a strong demand for formal training on its academic integration\. From the lecturers’ perspective, GenAI offers opportunities to support content creation, assessment design, and instructional workflows, provided that human\-led teaching remains central\. By integrating observed student behaviors with expert recommendations, this research proposes an ethical framework and practical guidelines for the responsible integration of GenAI in higher education\. The study highlights the urgent need for institutional policies that address emerging socio\-ethical tensions and ensure that GenAI enhances, rather than circumvents, foundational knowledge, academic integrity, and critical thinking\.

## [Physics\-guided explainable machine learning for predicting temporal scour evolution around hybrid spur dikes under unsteady flood hydrographs](../publications/215c8e3b7583734395fa.md)

Mehdi Daryaee; Laleh Divband Hafshejani; Seyed Mahmood Kashefipour; Amirreza Shahriari

Accurate prediction of local scour around river\-training structures during flood events remains a major challenge because scour evolution is governed by highly nonlinear interactions among hydraulic conditions, structural permeability, sediment transport, and time\-dependent bed morphology\. Although machine learning has recently improved scour prediction, existing studies have primarily focused on equilibrium scour under steady flow conditions and have largely treated predictive models as black boxes, limiting physical interpretation\. This study develops an explainable physics\-guided machine learning framework for predicting the temporal evolution of normalized scour depth around hybrid spur dikes \(Bandal\-like\) under unsteady flood hydrographs\. A laboratory dataset comprising 1,308 observations collected under nine hydrograph scenarios with different peak discharges, hydrograph durations, and permeability ratios was used to train and evaluate four regression algorithms, including Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, and CatBoost\. Hyperparameters were optimized using GridSearchCV with five\-fold cross\-validation, and a physics\-guided cumulative\-maximum constraint was incorporated to maintain temporal consistency of the predicted cumulative scour envelope by preventing nonphysical decreases\. Among the investigated models, CatBoost achieved the highest predictive performance on the independent testing dataset, with \\\(\{R\}^\{2\}=0\.9110\\\) , RMSE = 0\.0504, and MAE = 0\.0343, and successfully reproduced the principal characteristics of temporal scour evolution across the investigated flood hydrographs\. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses using CatBoost Feature Importance, Permutation Feature Importance, and SHAP consistently identified relative time \( \\\(t/\{T\}\_\{b\}\\\) \) as the dominant predictor, followed by structural permeability \( \\\(\{R\}\_\{a\}\\\) \), while SHAP interaction analysis revealed nonlinear and condition\-dependent relationships among hydrograph position, relative discharge, flow depth, and structural permeability\. In particular, the predictive contribution of relative discharge became more pronounced near peak\-flow conditions, while the influence of permeability varied with hydraulic loading and hydrograph stage\. The proposed framework combines predictive performance with interpretable model\-based insights and physics\-guided temporal consistency, providing a complementary approach to conventional scour assessment within the investigated experimental domain\.

## [Vaccination and Economic Recovery](../publications/216af45e005866885613.md)

Yimin Wang

ABSTRACT The COVID‐19 pandemic severely hampered human mobility and disrupted a series of economic activities\. In this study, I examine the impacts of vaccine coverage on mobility and several other economic indicators in the US\. I construct a novel shift‐share instrument that leverages the strong correlation between vaccination rates and demographic composition by sex and age group to address endogeneity concerns\. Using high‐frequency data, I find strong evidence that higher vaccine coverage increased mobility, reflected in more trips taken and a lower likelihood of staying at home\. I then assess the effects of vaccination on multiple economic indicators\. I find modest evidence that higher vaccine coverage increased labor market participation and employment rate, while the effects on new business applications and home mortgage applications are limited\.

## [Generative artificial intelligence and managerial cognition in turbulent supply chains: a real\-time empirical analysis](../publications/216d54d589ba9e10e9ee.md)

Augustine Nnoruka Okeke; Ifeanyi Ugbebor

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) promises to transform supply chain disruption management, yet its cognitive benefits and associated governance tensions remain insufficiently understood\. This study conceptualises and empirically examines a cognitive paradox whereby GenAI accelerates managerial sensemaking, expands response options, and facilitates adaptive reframing while increasing verification demands, accountability uncertainty, and coordination difficulties\. Using a scenario\-based mixed\-methods design, the research integrates an experiment with 200 senior supply chain managers randomly assigned to GenAI\-supported and unsupported decision environments and 25 executive interviews\. The study examines cognitive agility, operationalised through rapid reframing, information integration, and evaluative flexibility, as the managerial mechanism linking GenAI support to disruption\-response effectiveness\. Experimental findings associate GenAI support with greater cognitive agility and improved decision accuracy, adaptability, and timeliness\. Exploratory Bayesian network analysis identifies complementary probabilistic dependencies without establishing causality\. Qualitative evidence demonstrates that these benefits depend on data integration, verification practices, calibrated trust, managerial competence, and explicit decision rights\. The study contributes to supply chain scholarship by establishing cognitive agility as a microfoundation of GenAI\-enabled disruption response and identifying governance maturity as a boundary condition distinguishing cognitive augmentation from accelerated error, accountability ambiguity, and coordination failure\.

## [Artificial intelligence in the hiring process: transforming hr practices through opportunities, challenges and ethical aspects](../publications/2171c96b41e42719748c.md)

Urška Horvat

Magistrsko delo obravnava vpliv umetne inteligence \(AI\) na proces zaposlovanja, pri čemer se osredotoča na njeno uporabo v kadrovskih procesih, priložnosti za večjo učinkovitost, etične dileme, zaznano pravičnost, preglednost postopkov in spreminjanje vloge kadrovskih strokovnjakov\. Uporaba AI v zaposlovanju postaja vse pomembnejša, saj organizacijam omogoča hitrejšo obdelavo informacij, podporo pri administrativnih nalogah, pripravo vsebin, oblikovanje povzetkov, transkripcijo razgovorov in bolj strukturirano izvedbo posameznih faz selekcijskega postopka\. Ugotovitve so pokazale, da AI v kadrovskih procesih najpogosteje nastopa kot podporno orodje, ki razbremenjuje kadrovske strokovnjake pri ponavljajočih se, administrativnih in časovno zahtevnih nalogah\. Njena uporaba lahko prispeva k večji učinkovitosti, hitrejšemu odzivanju kandidatom, boljši organizaciji informacij in bolj strukturirani pripravi zaposlitvenih postopkov\. Vpliv AI na kakovost izbire kandidatov pa je bolj posreden, saj AI sama po sebi ne zagotavlja izbire najboljšega kandidata, temveč lahko kakovost postopka izboljša predvsem z boljšo pripravo, doslednejšimi kriteriji in hitrejšim dostopom do pomembnih informacij\. Pomemben del ugotovitev se nanaša na etična vprašanja, povezana z uporabo AI v zaposlovanju\. Med najpomembnejšimi tveganji so pristranskost algoritmov, nepreglednost delovanja orodij, varovanje osebnih podatkov, možnost napačnih sklepov in nevarnost prevelikega zaupanja v rezultate AI\. Zato je pri uporabi AI v kadrovskih procesih ključnega pomena, da organizacije zagotovijo pregledno komunikacijo s kandidati, ustrezno varstvo podatkov, človeški nadzor in kritično preverjanje rezultatov\. Sklepne ugotovitve so pokazale, da AI ne nadomešča kadrovskih strokovnjakov, temveč spreminja njihovo vlogo\. Kadrovski strokovnjaki se zaradi uporabe AI lahko bolj osredotočajo na vsebinsko presojo kandidatov, sodelovanje z vodji, kandidatovo izkušnjo in strateške naloge\. Hkrati pa uporaba AI zahteva nova znanja, predvsem podatkovno in AI\-pismenost, razumevanje omejitev orodij, varno ravnanje s podatki in sposobnost kritičnega vrednotenja rezultatov\. AI lahko pomembno izboljša kadrovske procese le, če je uporabljena odgovorno, pregledno in pod nadzorom človeka\.

## [MEN’S WRESTLING AT THE OLYMPIC GAMES, 1896–2024: A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF MEDAL DISTRIBUTION, COMPETITIVE CONCENTRATION, AND HISTORICAL TRANSFORMATION](../publications/217fa920384a12c22cd9.md)

Mehmet Yıldız

The aim of this study was to examine the historical development of men’s Greco\-Roman and freestyle wrestling competitions from the 1896 Athens Olympic Games to the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, the medal performances of Olympic delegations, and changes in the concentration of medal success over time\. The study was designed as descriptive research based on the historical research method and secondary data analysis\. Data on Olympic wrestling competitions were compiled from historical results published by United World Wrestling \(UWW\)\. Results from men’s Greco\-Roman and freestyle wrestling competitions were evaluated by Olympic year, wrestling style, and Olympic delegation\. Historical performance rankings were determined primarily according to the number of gold medals, followed by silver and bronze medals\. The Herfindahl–Hirschman Index \(HHI\), normalized HHI, Four\-Delegation Concentration Ratio \(CR4\), and Gini coefficient were used to assess concentration and inequality in medal distribution\. The main quantitative analyses were restricted to official editions of the Olympic Games; the 1906 Athens Intercalated Games were excluded from the primary analyses\. The findings indicate that medal success in men’s Olympic wrestling was concentrated among a limited number of delegations during the early periods, whereas competition gradually expanded to a broader international base as the number of medal\-winning countries increased over time\. In the historical ranking based on gold medals, the Soviet Union ranked first, while the United States recorded the highest total number of medals\. Türkiye also ranked among the leading delegations in terms of historical gold\-medal success\. Long\-term changes in the HHI, normalized HHI, and CR4 indicate that medal concentration, particularly in the modern period, declined compared with the early Olympic Games\. Nevertheless, periodic fluctuations demonstrate that the transformation of the competitive structure was not linear\. In conclusion, medal success in men’s Olympic wrestling became distributed across a broader group of countries over approximately 130 years, while certain countries maintained their historical prominence\. By evaluating the history of Olympic wrestling through the combined use of long\-term medal data and competitive concentration indicators, this study is expected to contribute to the literature on sport history and sport management\.

## [At peace with results: Navigating results in Swedish peacebuilding support](../publications/2184250255dd68860869.md)

Janet Vähämäki; Fredrik Söderbaum; Annika Hilgert; Susanna Alexius

Abstract Motivation This study contributes to the literature on the conditions under which results‐based management \(RBM\) practices enhance or undermine development policy implementation, and research on how aid bureaucrats respond to competing institutional demands\. Purpose The case of the Folke Bernadotte Academy \(FBA\), the Swedish government agency for peace, security, and development, contributes to the relatively limited literature on RBM in peacebuilding contexts\. Approach and methods The analysis of FBA&\#x27;s responses to competing results demands is based on a qualitative research design combining document analysis, focus group interviews, and in‐depth semi‐structured interviews with staff across organizational functions\. The analytical framework centres on institutional logics and strategic responses to conflicting institutional demands, and an ideal‐typical model is developed representing two co‐existing institutional logics for results: a Public Administration \(PA\) logic associated with requirements of upward accountability, precise measurement requirements and a Field‐based \(FB\) logic rooted in demands for adaptive, partner‐oriented implementation practices\. Findings At FBA, results are predominantly interpreted in line with the FB logic, and few tensions between the logics are found\. The less internally represented demands aligned with the PA logic on RBM are strategically redefined and decoupled from core operations using pragmatic bureaucratic skills, specifically a response we define as reversed commensuration \. The case also reveals the use of proper organization proxies \(legitimate structures, processes, and methods\) to signal adherence and future results on the way\. Policy implications Contrary to hegemonic beliefs in the field, the findings indicate that the tensions and adverse consequences commonly associated with RBM are not inevitable\. The FBA case demonstrates how agencies can mitigate the dynamics of “result fetishism” by strategically mediating competing results demands while sustaining flexibility and responsiveness to partner priorities and avoiding hyper bureaucracy\.

## [EXPRESS: A novel mouse model of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis based on photochemical\-induction combined with in situ injection](../publications/218e789e22ff0cda8c99.md)

Chengbin Zhou; Chengbin Zhou; Huimin Jiang; Yifan Zhou; Weiyue Zhang; Hui Li; Wei Ma; Lu Liu; Xiao Xue; Chunxiao Lu; Xiaoming Zhang; Zilin Xu; Ran Duan; Feng Qian; Liuguan Bian; Xunming Ji; Chen Zhou; Chen Zhou

Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis \(CVST\) is a distinct cerebrovascular disorder characterized by impaired venous drainage and blood\-brain barrier dysfunction, yet its pathophysiology remains poorly understood due to a lack of refined experimental models\. We developed a novel, clinically relevant mouse model of CVST by integrating localized intraluminal induction with photochemical occlusion of the superior sagittal sinus \(SSS\)\. Model fidelity was validated using laser speckle contrast imaging, MRI, and histological analysis\. Our approach produced consistent, spatially restricted SSS thrombosis, resulting in pronounced acute\-stage brain edema and venous infarction\. Notably, MRI combined with TTC staining identified a peri\-infarct region suggestive of a venous penumbra\. Functional assessments revealed significant acute motor deficits followed by recovery at day 7, whereas cognitive impairments persisted longer\. Compared with conventional FeCl₃ or systemic Rose Bengal photothrombosis models, this integrated method exhibited superior anatomical specificity and minimized off\-target tissue injury\. This study introduces a reproducible CVST model that successfully recapitulates the key hemodynamic and pathological features of human venous stroke, providing a robust platform for mechanistic investigations and the evaluation of targeted therapeutic interventions\.

## [Loss of Fmr1 causes subnucleus\-specific decreases in dendritic complexity in mediodorsal thalamus](../publications/218ec41743ac67581b50.md)

Alena Kizimenko; Polina N\. Lyuboslavsky; Audrey C\. Brumback

In the mediodorsal thalamus \(MD\), neurons of the medial \(MD\-M\) and lateral \(MD\-L\) subnuclei project to the medial prefrontal cortex \(mPFC\) to control complementary aspects of behavior, with MD\-M supporting more of the social/emotional domain and MD\-L promoting cognitive functions\. Our recent work shows that MD\-M and MD\-L have differences in hyperpolarization\-activated, cyclic nucleotide\-gated \(HCN\) pacemaker channels that may enable their distinct roles in behavior\. Low HCN channel activity in MD\-M neurons makes them relatively sensitive and responsive to inputs, while higher HCN channel activity makes MD\-L neurons more specific and selective for which inputs it transforms into outputs\. Knockout \(KO\) of the fragile X syndrome\-related gene Fmr1 decreased the activity of HCN channels in MD\-L but not MD\-M neurons, making MD\-L neurons more like MD\-M cells physiologically\. We sought to understand if these Fmr1\-related changes in MD function were accompanied by changes in subcellular structure\. Here, we assessed the dendritic morphology of MD neurons in adult Fmr1 KO and wildtype \(WT\) littermate mice\. In acute ex vivo brain slices, we filled MD neurons with biocytin via whole cell recording pipettes\. We used Neurolucida to trace the dendrites, performed quantitative analysis of dendritic architecture, compared MD\-M and MD\-L neurons in wildtype mice, and compared WT to KO mice for each subnucleus\. In WT mice, MD\-M neurons showed more distal dendritic branching compared with MD\-L neurons\. In Fmr1 KO mice, MD\-M neurons lost their distal dendritic branching and exhibited significant reductions in multiple measures of dendritic complexity compared to WT controls \(total dendritic length, number of nodes, and number of terminals\), while MD\-L neurons showed no morphological differences between WT and KO animals\. Notably, these morphological changes show a double dissociation with our previous physiological findings: MD\-M neurons exhibit structural but not functional changes, while MD\-L neurons show functional but not structural changes in Fmr1 KO mice\. Together, these findings suggest that FMRP regulates structure and function through independent, circuit\-specific mechanisms in thalamocortical neurons, with implications for understanding the diverse cellular and network consequences of Fmr1 loss in fragile X syndrome\.

## [Hyperspectral imaging, processing, and new challenges: a comprehensive review](../publications/21a4036bb1c4ec70a83c.md)

Xiaoyan Luo; Lei Zhang; Jialie Shen; Yinqiang Zheng; You Yang

Hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) captures rich spectral information across hundreds of contiguous narrow wavelength bands, enabling fine\-grained material characterization beyond conventional imaging modalities\. With the rapid development of sensor technologies and data\-driven algorithms, HSI has been widely adopted in diverse scientific and engineering fields while also facing fundamental challenges arising from high\-dimensional nonlinear spectral mixing, severe scarcity of labeled data, cross\-sensor and cross\-domain variability, and growing demands for real\-time processing and scalable multimodal integration\. We present a comprehensive review of hyperspectral imaging from the perspectives of imaging principles, system calibration and preprocessing, and image processing methodologies\. In particular, we systematically review core hyperspectral image processing tasks, including spectral mixture analysis and unmixing, dimensionality reduction, classification, and segmentation, as well as detection\-related tasks, and summarize representative methods and their technical evolution across different analytical objectives\. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are discussed, with a focus on data annotation scarcity, multimodal integration, real\-time processing, and the emerging impact of large models and generative artificial intelligence on hyperspectral image analysis\. We aim to provide a structured reference and a holistic understanding of current progress and future directions in hyperspectral imaging and processing research\.

## [Analisis Literasi Digital Lansia Dalam Mengidentifikasi Penipuan Berbasis Kecerdasan Buatan di Whatsapp Pada Komunitas Santa Monika Bekasi](../publications/21b3902100285e891d9f.md)

Nataliani Suseno; Yulianti Fajar Wulandari; Cindya Yunita Pratiwi

This study aims to examine artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based scams on WhatsApp within the Santa Monika Bekasi Community\. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the research explores the characteristics of older adults as social media users in the digital era\. It also investigates the rapid development of communication technology and its influence on how older adults receive, interpret, and process information\. WhatsApp is one of the most widely used communication platforms across different age groups\. Digital media, commonly referred to as new media, enables information to be disseminated through digital technologies\. Although these technologies provide convenient access to information, they have also created opportunities for increasingly prevalent online scams\. In this context, enhancing digital literacy and raising awareness among older adults are essential to helping them identify suspicious messages, recognize potential AI\-based scams on WhatsApp, and take appropriate measures to avoid becoming victims of digital fraud\.

## [PROMPT LITERACY У НАВЧАННІ ЯПОНСЬКОЇ МОВИ: МОДЕЛЬ GPT\-ОПОСЕРЕДКОВАНОЇ МОВЛЕННЄВОЇ ДІЯЛЬНОСТІ](../publications/21b3dad725c938eb0496.md)

А\.В\. Гілевич; Yulia BORYSHPOLETS

У статті теоретично обґрунтовано prompt literacy як перспективний компонент сучасної іншомовної комунікативної компетентності у навчанні японської мови та визначено його місце в середовищі взаємодії «людина – генеративний AI»\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена переходом від використання генеративного штучного інтелекту як допоміж\- ного цифрового інструмента до GPT\-опосередкованої мовленнєвої діяльності, у якій результат залежить не лише від можливостей мовної моделі, а й від здатності здобувача освіти формулювати, контекстуалізувати, уточнювати та кри\- тично оцінювати запити\. Матеріалом дослідження стали 14 сучасних праць японських, корейських, американських, британських та індонезійських дослідників, присвячених prompt literacy, prompt engineering, AI literacy і використанню генеративного AI в іншомовній та японськомовній освіті\. Застосовано критичний і порівняльний аналіз наукових дже\- рел, концептуальний аналіз ключових понять, систематизацію та теоретичне моделювання\. Уточнено співвідношення понять prompt engineering, prompt literacy та AI literacy й обґрунтовано специфіку Japanese\-language prompt literacy, що передбачає врахування комунікативної мети, рівня володіння мовою, соціальних ролей, регістру, прагматичної доречності та культурного контексту\. Авторами запропоновано модель GPT\-опосередкованої мовленнєвої діяльності із сімома взаємопов’язаними компонентами: комунікативна мета, контекст, рольова рамка, мовні обмеження, формат результату, критичне оцінювання AI output та ітеративне вдосконалення prompt\. Визначено методичні принципи фор\- мування цієї компетентності, запропоновано типи навчальних завдань і п’ять вимірів її подальшої операціоналізації\. Зроблено висновок, що prompt literacy доцільно розглядати не як суто технічну навичку, а як точку перетину мовної, прагматичної, стратегічної, цифрової та критичної компетентностей\. Перспективою подальших досліджень визначено емпіричну перевірку запропонованої моделі на матеріалі університетського навчання японської мови\.

## [Konstruksi Nilai Etika Bisnis Islam Dalam Pemikiran Rafik Issa Beekun: Analisis Tauhid, Keadilan, Kebebasan, Tanggung Jawab, dan Ihsan Serta Relevansinya Terhadap Bisnis Kontemporer](../publications/21e855e79b28180c0490.md)

Kuat Kuat; Arfan Arfan; Hidayat Jayamiharja

Artikel ini menganalisis lima prinsip fundamental etika bisnis Islam dalam pemikiran Rafik Issa Beekun, yaitu unity \(tauhid\), equilibrium \(keadilan\), free will \(kebebasan\), responsibility \(tanggung jawab\), dan benevolence \(ihsan\), serta merekonstruksi hubungan fungsional antarlima prinsip tersebut dalam pengambilan keputusan bisnis etis\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif berbasis penelitian kepustakaan \(library research\) dan penelitian konseptual \(conceptual research\), dengan analisis isi, analisis konseptual, dan analisis tematik terhadap karya primer Beekun dan literatur akademik yang relevan\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tauhid berfungsi sebagai orientasi moral, keadilan sebagai keseimbangan etis, kebebasan sebagai agensi moral, tanggung jawab sebagai akuntabilitas, dan ihsan sebagai keunggulan moral\. Kelima fungsi tersebut direkonstruksi menjadi Model Integratif Pengambilan Keputusan Etis dalam Bisnis Islam dengan pola Tauhid → Keadilan → Kebebasan ↔ Tanggung Jawab → Ihsan → Keputusan Bisnis Etis\. Kebaruan penelitian tidak terletak pada penemuan prinsip etika baru, tetapi pada rekonstruksi hubungan fungsional lima aksioma Beekun menjadi kerangka evaluasi keputusan yang mengintegrasikan orientasi moral, keseimbangan etis, agensi moral, akuntabilitas, dan keunggulan moral\. Model tersebut relevan untuk menganalisis persoalan bisnis kontemporer, termasuk pemasaran digital, fake review, dark patterns, penggunaan data konsumen, algoritma, kecerdasan buatan, hubungan stakeholder, dan tanggung jawab sosial perusahaan\. Penelitian ini berkontribusi secara konseptual dengan menjembatani prinsip normatif etika bisnis Islam dan proses pengambilan keputusan serta menyediakan dasar bagi pengembangan kerangka evaluasi etis dalam bisnis kontemporer\.

## [An automata\-machine learning integrated framework for intelligent mental health diagnostics](../publications/220c9df2a31661ce99b2.md)

Lokesh Pawar; Rohit Bajaj; Yohannes Mengist; Nitin Kumar; Ruby Pant; Ajay Kumar; Purnendu Shekar Pandey

Depression among the students has critical impact on student’s life and it needs to be predicted at an early stage\. The unstructured nature of self\-emotions are going to undetected and emerged as a critical mental health concern\. Integration of machine learning \(ML\) with behavioural modelling address the concern and connects with student emotional state and helps to predict the depression among students at early stage\. An automata\-machine learning integrated approaches including ensemble of lazy and eager classifiers, behavioural modelling, minimization of finite automata are evaluated and compared in three scenarios where in the first case predictive performance on original dataset is evaluated\. The second case in sighting the real life scenario student specific emotions are extracted with automata\-based behavioural states to generate meaningful patterns and feature vectors for each student and these automata generated features are statistically tested and signified then embed with original dataset\. Further the ML feature selection Gini index applied on automata integrated dataset to select the prominent features to enhance the predictive performance\. In the third case automata based feature merging is applied which maintain the credibility of each feature and merged systematically with related features and preserve the equivalence and reduce the feature redundancy\. Unlike the traditional ML based feature selection, Automata based feature merging retains the interpretability and behavioural traceability of all features\. Lastly, eager learning \(random forest\) and lazy Learning \(kstar\) are ensemble and deployed to take advantage of the automata based optimized feature sets\. The automata assisted scenario performs well and improves the accuracy with 14\.86% where the baseline accuracy is 82\.02% evaluated with random forest classifier and the accuracy with automata based behavioural modelling is recorded 96\.88% and shows proposed framework is an interpretable, dynamic solution for mental health interventions in educational settings\. The main contributions of the proposed framework is to extract automata based features that behaviourally connects to student emotions and mental state\. The minimization of finite automata reduces the redundant factors and maintained the credibility of each feature\. Further multi\-metric statistical validation determines the applicability of automata extracted features\.

## [Advancing health equity in cancer care through collaborative research agenda development: a provincial workshop guided by patient\-oriented research in Alberta, Canada](../publications/220e38fc4cfbf38f0de7.md)

Anna Pujadas Botey; Harkeert Judge; Paula J\. Robson; Anna Santos Salas

Health inequities in cancer care persist, indicating that advancing equity requires not only understanding inequities but also transforming how cancer research is developed and conducted\. Although equity\-oriented and community\-engaged approaches have advanced important principles for research, there is limited understanding of the conditions and processes required to translate these principles into practice within cancer care systems, including how research agendas can be collaboratively developed to reflect community and health system needs\. This Perspective describes the co\-design and implementation of a provincial Health Equity Workshop in Alberta, Canada, as a practice\-based example of how a cancer care system operationalized Patient\-Oriented Research principles to support equity\-oriented research agenda development\. Guided by Patient\-Oriented Research and informed by the Health Equity Implementation Framework, the initiative involved a twelve\-member working group comprising people with lived experience of cancer, representatives of community organizations, health system leaders, and researchers who co\-designed and facilitated a two\-day workshop involving 43 participants\. Reflections from the initiative highlighted relational, organizational, and practical conditions that shaped equity\-oriented engagement, including trust\-building, shared leadership, compensation and resource supports, institutional commitment, and attention to system\-level barriers affecting participation\. The workshop demonstrated how co\-design can embed equity from the earliest stages of research agenda development by bringing together diverse forms of expertise to shape what research is needed and how it should be conducted\. This Perspective offers practical insights for researchers, health systems, and community partners seeking to advance equitable cancer research and care\.

## [Assessing the Impact of Digital Business Models on the Performance of Commercial Banks](../publications/2213f112edb5e6020e7e.md)

Jurayev Jahongir Bahodir ugli

The article assesses the impact of digital business models on the performance of commercial banks\. It compares the traditional branch\-based banking model with platform, open\-banking and ecosystem\-based digital models, and identifies the advantages \(lower costs, financial inclusion, new revenue streams\) and the risks \(cyber threats, technology and talent dependence, intensified competition, the digital divide\) of the transition\. The current state, regulatory framework and potential of digital business models in Uzbekistan&\#x27;s commercial banks are analysed, and recommendations for their development are proposed\.

يقدم البحث \(توظيف أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي في ترجمة وتحليل النصوص الأدبية الكلاسيكية &quot;تمور ونخيل العراق القديم&quot;\) دراسة تحليلية مقارنة للأوصاف التي قدمها المؤرخ الروماني بليني الأكبر \(23\-79 م\) عن نخيل وتمور العراق القديم، الواردة في كتابه &quot;التاريخ الطبيعي&quot;\. تعد النخيل شريان الحياة الاقتصادية والاجتماعية عند سكان بلاد الرافدين، وهي حقيقة موثقة في كتابات المؤرخين والجغرافيين الكلاسيكيين \(الإغريق والرومان\)\. تكمن أهمية هذه الدراسة في استقصاء النصوص اللاتينية القديمة التي وثّقت البيئة الزراعية لحضارة العراق القديم، ونظرًا لتعقيد هذه النصوص وكثافتها، يستخدم هذا البحث تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي، اداة \(Google Gemini\) كأداة منهجية لجمع النصوص وترجمتها وتحليلها، مما يُسهم في فك رموزها واستخلاص رؤى علمية

## [From single\-atom to multi\-metallic composite systems: Rational design and mechanistic insights of metal\-nitrogen\-carbon catalysts for oxygen reduction reaction](../publications/221b904ad8f82aab0936.md)

Chunxu Lai; Dai Dang; Dustin Banham; Bin Liu; Tiejun Wang

Abstract Atomically dispersed M\-N\-C catalysts have been demonstrated as one of the most promising non\-precious metal catalysts for proton exchange membrane fuel cells \(PEMFCs\) and zinc\-air batteries \(ZABs\), owing to their excellent performance in the oxygen reduction reaction \(ORR\)\. To date, diverse M\-N\-C catalysts have been developed for the ORR\. This review comprehensively summarizes the optimization strategies for M\-N\-C catalysts, progressing from single\-atom catalysts to composite structures, including dual\-atom sites, multi\-atom sites, and architectures integrated with clusters and particles\. Furthermore, it explores the differences in activity and stability among various types of M\-N\-C catalysts and analyzes their potential for transition from laboratory to industry, highlighting key considerations in this process\. Finally, the review emphasizes persisting challenges and proposes three critical aspects warranting further attention in the future development of M\-N\-C catalysts, aiming to provide constructive perspectives for the sustainable advancement of clean energy technologies\.

## [Avaliação do comportamento térmico e eficiência energética em processos de cozedura cerâmica](../publications/221bbcd34048f3963069.md)

Diogo Alexandre Oliveira Costa

A presente dissertação investiga o comportamento térmico e energético de um forno industrial do setor cerâmico, recorrendo à aplicação de técnicas de análise de dados e metodologias de exploração estatística orientadas para a eficiência operacional\. O estudo surge no contexto da crescente importância da Ciência de Dados na Indústria 4\.0, onde a otimização de processos térmicos e a redução do consumo energético assumem um papel central para a sustentabilidade e competitividade do setor\. A investigação fundamentou\-se inicialmente numa análise sistemática do estado da arte, que demonstrou o papel crucial da Ciência de Dados na análise preditiva e na expansão das capacidades de Avaliação de Ciclo de Vida \(ACV\)\. Este processo permitiu o levantamento de requisitos técnicos e a identificação de variáveis\-chave \(como a composição da pasta, tempos de ciclo, fluxos de exaustão e consumos energéticos\) essenciais para que modelos de Machine Learning possam apoiar decisões sustentáveis\. A base experimental assentou em dois conjuntos de dados distintos: o primeiro exploratório, que permitiu compreender o contexto produtivo e as relações fundamentais entre variáveis térmicas e energéticas; e o segundo mais completo, que suportou a análise aprofundada do funcionamento real de um forno de produção de chacota ao longo de sete meses\. A metodologia adotada incluiu limpeza e preparação dos dados, deteção de outliers, segmentação por curvas de produção, análise temporal, correlações e criação de variáveis derivadas\. Os resultados evidenciaram padrões de funcionamento coerentes com o processo produtivo, bem como fenómenos relevantes para a eficiência térmica, incluindo oscilações antes de quebras, assimetrias entre zonas do forno e efeitos de inércia térmica\. Verificou\-se que a curva de 13 horas funciona como padrão operacional eficiente, enquanto a curva de 16 horas revela maior potencial energético quando aplicada estrategicamente\. Conclui\-se que a integração de ferramentas de análise de dados, apoiadas por softwares multidisciplinares e bases de dados ambientais identificadas na literatura, permite não só diagnosticar o estado real do processo como identificar oportunidades de otimização energética e bases para o desenvolvimento de modelos preditivos num contexto industrial real\.

## [The Role of Amyloid\-Beta Plaques in Disrupting Neural Communication in Alzheimer’s Disease](../publications/222072f9ae4d865dfb8a.md)

Aditya Reddy

Alzheimer’s Disease \(AD\) is defined as a particular onset and course of cognitive and functional decline\. Central to AD pathology is the abnormal processing of amyloid precursor proteins \(APPs\), which produces amyloid\-beta \(Aβ\) peptides prone to misfolding and aggregation\. Soluble Aβ oligomers are now also recognized as the earliest and most potent disruptors of synaptic communication, leading to the impairment of receptor function and long\-term potentiation\. These amyloidogenic events serve as an upstream trigger for the hyperphosphorylation and aggregation of tau\. As Aβ accumulation progresses, it activates kinases that drive tau hyperphosphorylation, misfolding, and neurofibrillary tangle formation\. These effects destabilize microtubules and interrupt axonal transport\. The combined effect of Aβ\-induced synaptic toxicity, tau\-mediated structural breakdown, and chronic neuroinflammation leads to the progressive loss of neural connectivity characteristic of Alzheimer’s Disease\. This paper will examine how Aβ plaques create disruptions in neural signaling, enabling the transition of tau from a microtubule\-stabilizing protein to a neurotoxic aggregate\. By evaluating Aβ as the initiator of synaptic stress and tau as the primary driver for structural neurodegeneration and clinical decline, this review aims to show that the loss of neural connectivity in AD is the result of this interdependent proteinopathy, which is further exaggerated by chronic neuroinflammation\.

## [Oral Actinomyces Species Exposure is Associated with Anxiety‐Like Behavior, Mitochondrial Remodeling, and Altered GABAergic Pathways](../publications/22326e2dcd750287241d.md)

Tabinda Salman; Zhenwu Luo; Douglas E\. Johnson; Arshad Ali Noorani; Zhuang Wan; Bogdan Bordieanu; Zhiwei Ye; Rachel D\. Penrod; Hongxu Xian; Sylvia Fitting; Peter W\. Kalivas; Wei Jiang

INTRODUCTION: The human oral microbiome is increasingly recognized as a contributor to brain health, yet its mechanisms remain unclear\. We previously found an enrichment of oral Actinomyces species in chronic cannabis smokers\. METHOD: Wild\-type C57BL/6 mice were orally inoculated with Actinomyces species following antibiotic preconditioning and assessed using behavioral assays, multi\-tissue cytokine profiling, single\-cell RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and biochemical analyses\. Selected metabolites were tested in neuronal cells in vitro\. RESULTS: Oral inoculation with cannabis use\-associated Actinomyces species, especially A\. meyeri, in mice was accompanied by anxiety\-like behaviors, alterations in mitochondrial pathways, and reduced GABAergic markers, without evidence of bacterial brain translocation, changes in the canonical proinflammatory cytokines measured in this study, or memory decline\. Notably, integrated oral and brain metabolomic analyses prioritized arginine and argininosuccinate as candidate mediators associated with Actinomyces exposure for further investigation\. Selected metabolites associated with Actinomyces exposure altered mitochondrial function and oxidative stress in neuronal cells in vitro, supporting their potential role in mediating the observed molecular changes\. CONCLUSION: Together, these results suggest that oral microbiome\-associated metabolites may contribute to behavioral alterations through mechanisms involving mitochondrial remodeling and altered GABAergic pathways, supporting further investigation of the oral\-brain metabolic axis in neuropsychiatric disorders\.

## [Multiscale surface\-texture characterisation of heritage paintings using reflectance transformation imaging and completed local binary patterns](../publications/2232a18052fc414a8612.md)

Yun Zhou; Bin Gao; Weiping Zeng

Reflectance transformation imaging provides a non\-contact means of recording the illumination\-dependent appearance of cultural heritage objects and can assist in the visual examination of brushwork, cracks, surface irregularities, and material\-texture variations\. However, the large number of directional\-light images produced during RTI acquisition creates challenges for extracting stable and interpretable surface\-texture information\. This study presents a multiscale computational framework for characterising the visible surface features of heritage paintings using physically acquired RTI image sequences\. The proposed framework first normalises the directional\-light observations and generates relightable representations under controlled illumination directions\. Discrete wavelet transform \(DWT\) is subsequently employed to decompose the RTI observations into multiscale frequency components representing coarse surface structures and fine textural variations\. Completed local binary patterns \(CLBP\) are then extracted from the wavelet sub\-bands to describe local intensity differences, neighbourhood relationships, and directional texture characteristics\. The resulting descriptors are combined to produce surface\-detail maps and quantitative texture representations for different regions of the paintings\. The framework is evaluated using real multi\-light RTI datasets and compared with conventional local binary patterns, wavelet\-only descriptors, gradient\-based methods, and standard texture\-analysis approaches\. Evaluation considers descriptor repeatability across lighting directions, texture separability, edge preservation, local contrast, computational cost, and robustness to illumination variation\. The framework is intended for computational surface visualisation and texture characterisation\. The study provides a reproducible and physically grounded approach for analysing visible painting\-surface characteristics from real RTI measurements and establishes a basis for subsequent evaluation with conservator\-annotated heritage datasets\.

## [Navigating tensions: an empirical study of ELF teachers’ AI literacy and emotionally mediated responses to artificial intelligence in a Chinese university](../publications/223687970864a3c89cc1.md)

Ping Wang

The emergence of generative AI \(GenAI\) like ChatGPT constitutes a paradigm shift for language education, particularly for English as a Lingua Franca teachers in China, who face top\-down mandates to adopt it\. This mixed\-methods study of 52 Chinese university teachers examined the interplay between their AI literacy, emotional responses, and professional identity\. Findings reveal high awareness but a critical deficit in pedagogical and critical AI literacy\. Teachers experienced profound ambivalence, simultaneous enthusiasm and existential anxiety as they grappled with a displaced identity as knowledge authorities\. Emotions actively mediated their engagement, leading to defensive, performative, or transformative stances, often exacerbated by institutional ‘AI evangelism\.’ The study concludes that support must extend beyond tool training to foster collaborative spaces for ethical sense\-making and identity renegotiation, advocating a ‘pedagogy of integrity’ centred on process\-oriented assessment and critical human\-AI collaboration\.

## [AI\-enabled social media: implications for salespeople, sales leadership, and sales organizations](../publications/2238318bb6d6f2fd7d73.md)

Vishag A\. Badrinarayanan; Christine Lai\-Bennejean; Adam A\. Rapp; Laurianne Schmitt; Arun Sharma

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) becomes embedded within social media, AI\-enabled social media is increasingly changing how salespeople, sales leaders, and sales organizations engage with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders\. Yet, sales research has largely focused on how sales actors use traditional social media with little emphasis on the implications of AI, a notable gap that also remains in the rapidly evolving research on AI in B2B sales\. Thus, there is limited understanding of how embedding AI within social media alters the action possibilities available to sales actors\. Drawing on affordance theory, we define AI\-enabled social media and examine how AI alters and extends traditional social media affordances across external social media and enterprise social media \(ESM\), with implications for salespeople across the sales process, sales leadership across key leadership roles, and sales organizations across key organizational domains\. We then discuss theoretical and managerial implications and develop a research agenda for advancing knowledge of AI\-enabled social media in B2B sales\.

Therefore, in our view, it is more appropriate to approach the issue of valency by considering not only the grammatical characteristics of words but also their semantic properties\.Based on the description of word relationships provided by A\.A\. Ufimtseva and V\.G\. Admoni, the combinatory potential of various parts of speech has been investigated by examining the completeness or incompleteness of their lexical content, while also taking into account the concepts of sentence constituents and syntactic relations\. The grammatical potential of words was studied in conjunction with their lexical semantics\. ## [From Statutory Mandate to Strategic Capability in Public Institutions: Repositioning the Kenya School of Government within a Changing Public\-Sector Environment A Conceptual Review Based on Desktop Analysis](../publications/22537c7d31d283a68fec.md)

Mbatha N\. Januaris; Annastacia Mwende Mwova

This paper investigates how statutory public institutions can convert mandate\-based institutional advantages into strategic capabilities that maintain relevance and performance amid evolving operating environments, using the Kenya School of Government \(KSG\) as a case study\. Employing Strategic Fit Theory, the Resource\-Based View, and dynamic capabilities frameworks, the study conducts a conceptual desktop review of institutional documents, national policy frameworks, and strategic management literature, supplemented by environmental, SWOT, and TOWS analyses\. The findings indicate that KSG has substantial institutional resources, including statutory legitimacy, specialized public\-sector expertise, national reach, institutional knowledge, and established government relationships\. Nevertheless, fiscal constraints, technological advancements, the emergence of alternative service providers, and shifting stakeholder expectations increasingly challenge the institution’s ability to convert these resources into sustained strategic value\. Four interconnected capability domains are identified as critical for institutional repositioning: digital capability, financial resilience, research and knowledge differentiation, and strategic partnerships and institutional reach\. The paper contends that statutory mandate, while fundamental for institutional legitimacy and positioning, does not ensure sustained strategic relevance\. Rather than replacing existing institutional strengths, effective strategic repositioning requires intentional integration, adaptation, and renewal in response to environmental change\. This study offers a capability\-oriented perspective on public\-sector strategic management by distinguishing mandate\-based institutional advantage from capability\-driven strategic positioning, with implications for Schools of Government and similar public institutions\.

## [Spatial structure and heterogeneous drivers of city\-level CO2 emission in China: Insights from geographically weighted spatiotemporal decomposition method](../publications/22572aac8e74d8fa1e3a.md)

Yue Wang; Huijie Wen; Peipei Qiu; Xuesong Wang; Wenbo Xue; Yixuan Zheng; Gang Yan; Yuanhang Zhang

Anthropogenic carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) emissions in China have risen persistently, making effective mitigation policies critical for achieving carbon peak and neutrality\. Such policies must be regionally tailored, given the large disparities in emission patterns, socioeconomic drivers, and decarbonization potentials across China\. Most studies of differentiated emission mitigation concentrate on strategy design but neglect the rationality and accuracy of spatial management units, serving as the spatial objects for policy implementation\. The scientific identification of spatial management units is the key to improving the effectiveness of mitigation measures\. This study applies the Geographically Weighted Rotation Empirical Orthogonal Function \(GWREOF\) to anthropogenic CO 2 emissions across 337 Chinese cities from 1990 to 2020, identifying 20 geographically contiguous spatial modes that characterize the spatial structure of China’s CO 2 emissions\. These 20 modes are then used to delineate 20 spatially continuous management units for anthropogenic CO 2 emissions \(i\.e\. carbon emission zones\)\. We then analyze the disparities of carbon emission, carbon balance capacity, economic output and energy intensity among different zones and establish the indicator matrix to divide them into eight types\. The results show that mitigation priorities differ by zone types: Economically Developed High\-Emission Zones and Low\-Carbon Sustaining Medium\-Emission Zones should prioritize energy decarbonization and low‑carbon tertiary industries\. Resource\-Dependent High\-Emission and Transition\-Pressured Medium\-Emission Types require stringent coal controls and ecological restoration\. Low\-Carbon Developing Medium\-Emission Type needs green manufacturing upgrades\. Energy Optimization Medium\-Emission Type should improve coal structures in heating and industry, and Ecologically Prioritized Low\-Emission Type should monetize clean energy and forest sinks through compensation\. Combining spatially‑based zoning reflecting emission heterogeneity with factor‑based classification reflecting driver heterogeneity, this research improves targeted and systematic governance of anthropogenic CO 2 emissions in China at the national level\.

## [The Loss or the Architecture? What Matters in Survival Analysis with Competing Risks](../publications/226026081d61f250aa57.md)

Julie Alberge; Gaël Varoquaux; Judith Abécassis

Often, \\emph\{eg\} in healthcare and predictive maintenance, what matters is which of several competing causes will strike first, and with what probability: survival analysis with competing risks\. Corresponding deep learning methods are developed as bundles: a new architecture together with a new training loss, tested on one to five datasets against a handful of baselines\. Thus, a state\-of\-the\-art result cannot be attributed to the architecture, the loss, or the evaluation protocol\. The coupling is not accidental: with one incidence curve per cause, a network&\#x27;s head is tied to the losses expressible on it\. We vary the two axes independently, three losses, two of them strictly proper, on four backbones, across two modalities that tease the axes apart: 20 tabular and 3 pathology\-image datasets\. One loss wins in both: modelling cumulative incidence directly under censoring weighting\. It brings twice as much as benefits a good choice of backbone on competing\-risks data, and no more than it on single\-event data: the loss is decisive for competing risks\. The backbone matters too, and must match the modality: tabular networks lead on tables, pretrained vision encoders on images\. The two choices compound rather than substitute\. Proper scoring rules reveal these dynamics; the concordance index \(C\-index\), which is not proper, does not separate models: neither axis moves it, not even tuning on the loss built to improve it\. This is an avenue of progress: composed, the two give a model nobody has tried, RealMLP or TabM trained with the cumulative\-incidence loss, which takes the best Brier score in our benchmark\.

## [The Role of the Father in Child Development](../publications/2265a155ab515f8579f1.md)



Comprehensive scholarship on fatherhood from evolutionary, physiological, and psychological perspectives Now in its Sixth Edition, The Role of the Father in Child Development remains the authoritative reference on paternal influences across cultures and contexts\. Edited by Michael E\. Lamb, whose research has shaped family law and policy internationally, this volume synthesizes recent scholarship from evolutionary biology, physiology, psychology, and sociology to provide a rounded understanding of contemporary fatherhood worldwide\. This edition presents up\-to\-date summaries of fatherhood research, including a chapter from leading psychologist James Rilling, whose specialized work on evolutionary and neurological bases of paternal behavior reaches a broader audience here\. The volume examines father\-child relationships across diverse family structures, including post\-divorce arrangements, foster care, adoption, and LGBTQ\+ parenting contexts\. The book also covers: Cross\-cultural perspectives on father involvement and paternal roles across diverse societies and family structures around the world Evolutionary and physiological foundations of fathering behavior drawn from current biological anthropology and neuroscience research findings Research\-based guidance for legal practitioners working on custody evaluations, divorce proceedings, and family court matters Evidence informing policy decisions on fostering, adoption, and diverse family arrangements including same\-sex and LGBTQ\+ parenting Multidisciplinary frameworks integrating psychology, sociology, and family social science perspectives on contemporary paternal engagement Essential for scholars, researchers, and advanced students in developmental psychology and family studies, The Role of the Father in Child Development also serves practitioners in psychology, social work, and criminology\. Legal professionals handling family and custody matters, custody evaluators, and policy makers will find authoritative evidence to inform their work with fathers and families\.

## [SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On\-Policy Distillation](../publications/226adcd415937738916c.md)

Kai Tang; Xing Zheng; Haobo Wang; Guangcheng Zhu; Shenzhi Yang; Zhengqing Zang; Yingfan Ma; Bowen Song; Weiqiang Wang

A key challenge in on\-policy distillation \(OPD\) is extracting effective supervision from teacher knowledge\. Supervision from token probabilities may underutilize internal knowledge, while direct hidden\-state matching forces the student to shift to the teacher&\#x27;s feature space and complicates cross\-architecture transfer\. Inspired by contrastive learning&\#x27;s use of relationships between instances, we propose \\textbf\{SimOPD\} to transfer teacher internal knowledge through response similarities\. Specifically, SimOPD uses paired memory banks of student\-generated responses to extract supervision from the teacher&\#x27;s internal representations as similarity distributions\. The student then matches these distributions within its own representation space, retaining representational freedom and removing the need for cross\-model projection\. Extensive experiments show that SimOPD improves the overall average over the strongest baselines by up to 2\.6 and 3\.1 percentage points in same\- and cross\-architecture settings\.

## [Human Interventions as Labels: Localizing, Steering, and \(Sometimes\) Editing the Computations Behind LLM Agent Failures](../publications/22922e9f979a87fc87d5.md)

Cesare Zavattari; Alessandro Tommasi; Giuseppe Prencipe

When an LLM agent misbehaves, a human steps in, and that intervention is usually discarded or replayed as training data\. We treat it instead as a measurement: a label pointing at the internal computation that failed\. We study it in a controlled agent environment, on one failure \(asking a clarifying question when the request was already unambiguous\), with labels from a rule\-based overseer validated against blind human judgment\. Claims cover eligible models, which both over\-ask and sometimes act on matched unambiguous requests: five of thirteen qualified \(Qwen2\.5\-3B, gemma\-2\-2b, OLMo\-3\-7B, Mistral\-Nemo\-12B, Phi\-4\)\. Four findings\. First, the ask\-vs\-act decision is causally localizable in every eligible family: a direction learned from intervention labels flips 72\-100% of held\-out over\-asks at a definite residual\-stream depth, with site and dose chosen on training data, and random directions under the same procedure flip at most one episode\. Second, over\-asking has two mechanistic signatures: in four families the model demonstrably knows the request is unambiguous \(the belief is decodable, causally inert and orthogonal to the decision\) and asks anyway; in the fifth, the rare over\-asks track different world\-representations\. Third, steering gated on a probe readout removes most of the simulated oversight burden while legitimate questions survive \(bootstrap 95% intervals exclude zero\); a prompt instruction makes it worse\. Fourth, consolidating the fix into the weights yields a map, not a rule: on one model a LoRA confined to the causal band passes every criterion fixed in advance while behavior cloning on identical data breaks retention; on three families the reverse holds; on the fifth the outcome crosses the boundary across seeds\. A geometric rule written down in advance to predict the regime failed on two out\-of\-family tests; we report the failure and stop rather than fit a replacement\.

## [Analisis Tren dan Bias Etis Penggunaan Generative Ai dalam Pendidikan Tinggi: Sebuah Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis \(2022–2026\)](../publications/22a5277110c6752da726.md)

Anjelina Br Sembiring; Yunita, Lilis; Prodi D\-III Keperawatan Sintang, Poltekkes Kemenkes Pontianak, Pontianak; Paramita Larasmahesa

Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence \(Generative AI\) telah membawa perubahan dalam pelaksanaan pembelajaran, penilaian, penelitian, dan pengelolaan akademik di perguruan tinggi\. Teknologi ini menawarkan kemudahan dalam menghasilkan teks, merangkum informasi, memberikan umpan balik, serta mendukung pembelajaran yang lebih personal\. Namun, penggunaannya juga menimbulkan persoalan etis, seperti bias algoritmik, ketidakakuratan informasi, pelanggaran integritas akademik, risiko privasi data, ketimpangan akses, dan rendahnya transparansi dalam penggunaan kecerdasan buatan\. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis tren penggunaan Generative AI dalam pendidikan tinggi, mengidentifikasi bentuk bias dan risiko etis yang muncul, serta menguraikan strategi penerapan teknologi yang bertanggung jawab berdasarkan literatur ilmiah periode 2022–2026\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui sintesis tematik terhadap literatur yang relevan\. Pembahasan mencakup kajian mengenai perkembangan penggunaan Generative AI, integritas akademik, keadilan algoritmik, perlindungan data, dan tata kelola institusi\. Hasil sintesis menunjukkan bahwa Generative AI berpotensi meningkatkan efisiensi pembelajaran dan mendukung aktivitas akademik, tetapi manfaatnya bergantung pada literasi AI, pengawasan manusia, transparansi, dan kesiapan kebijakan institusi\. Bias dalam keluaran AI juga berpotensi memperkuat stereotip, menghasilkan informasi yang tidak seimbang, serta merugikan pengguna dengan latar belakang bahasa dan budaya tertentu\. Oleh karena itu, perguruan tinggi perlu mengembangkan pedoman penggunaan AI yang jelas, memperkuat kompetensi digital sivitas akademika, dan menerapkan sistem evaluasi yang berorientasi pada keadilan serta akuntabilitas\. Kajian ini juga menemukan perlunya penelitian empiris lebih lanjut mengenai bias Generative AI dalam konteks pendidikan tinggi Indonesia\.

## [Predictive Modeling of Urban Heat Stress Using Machine Learning: A 2050 UTCI\-Based Assessment](../publications/22ae1d8d19f8fbbfc127.md)

Ninitha Arumugakani; Madhumathi Anbu; Hourakhsh Ahmad Nia; Ranjitharamasamy Sudhakara Pandian

Urban heat islands and increasingly severe thermal stress pose critical challenges to sustainable urban development, yet physics\-based simulation tools remain computationally expensive and ill\-suited to early\-stage climate\-responsive design\. This study applies machine learning to predict outdoor air and surface temperature using 20 years \(2005\-2025\) of daily maximum temperature data ranging from 15°C to 40°C\. Four algorithms were evaluated: Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XG Boost\)\. Gradient Boosting achieved the best performance with RMSE = 1\.869, MAE = 1\.405, and R² = 0\.708, indicating robust predictive ability across diurnal temperature and seasonal patterns\. 2050 projections, based on direct extrapolation of the trained model&\#x27;s seasonal temperature pattern, show a shift toward moderate\-to\-strong Universal Thermal Climate Index \(UTCI\) heat stress conditions across the majority of the year, underscoring the need for climate\-responsive urban design even under conservative, non\-scenario\-scaled projections\. The results strengthen the acceptance of data\-driven ML frameworks for the application in urban planning and climate\-responsive architectural design practice\.

## [A Protocol for Developing Q\-SOFT Instructional Design: Process, Components, and Implementation Guidelines](../publications/22b41c910ab0cd9a4a27.md)

Soft skills refer to the skills that support individuals’ functioning in interpersonal, emotional, and cognitive domains\.
