## [Do Malaysian Newsrooms Jump on the AI Bandwagon? Empirical Evidence From Journalists’ Perspectives](../publications/22ba6156cdbf2e70aed2.md)

Jiankun Gong; Yu Zuo; Izzati Aziz; Mumtaz Aini Alivi; Kunjin Luo; Yuqing Lin

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly promoted as a transformative force in journalism, yet most research on newsroom AI adoption remains concentrated in Western and other well\-resourced media settings\. This study examines how AI is interpreted, organized, and used in Malaysian newsrooms, offering insight from an emerging Southeast Asian media context\. Drawing on semi\-structured interviews with 20 journalists across six Malaysian news organizations, the article investigates how national AI governance signals are translated into newsroom norms, how organizational resources and managerial priorities shape uptake, and how AI is incorporated into everyday reporting, editing, and verification\. The analysis shows that AI adoption in Malaysian newsrooms is uneven and selective rather than uniform\. First, national AI momentum has not yet produced strong newsroom\-level governance; instead, the practice remains shaped by limited written rules, selective disclosure, and strong human accountability\. Second, organizational capacity is patchy, with uneven access to tools, training, and infrastructural support across organizations and roles\. Third, AI is used mainly in bounded, assistive tasks such as transcription, translation, summarization, and headline generation, while verification labor is redistributed rather than reduced\. The findings identify a typology of newsroom responses—cautious minimalists, experimental pragmatists, and human\-gated adopters—showing that Malaysian newsrooms are not simply “jumping on the AI bandwagon,” but engaging AI pragmatically under uneven governance and resource conditions\.

## [Artificial Intelligence for Engineering\-Grade Parametric CAD: A Critical Review of Representations, Large Language Models, and Agentic Design Systems](../publications/22bf63d72dc1c5162daf.md)

Jihad Rishmany; Rodrigue Imad; Rabih Kahaleh

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is rapidly expanding computer\-aided design \(CAD\) from shape generation toward generative, conversational, and agentic engineering\. However, most AI–CAD evaluations remain dominated by geometric similarity and execution success, while industrial CAD depends on editable parameters, design intent, stable feature histories, manufacturing constraints, and downstream CAD/CAE reuse\. This structured critical review synthesizes 107 sources, principally from 2020–2026, across constrained sketches, boundary representations \(B\-Reps\), parametric sequences, executable CAD programs, large language and multimodal models, CAD agents, commercial\-CAD integration, and CAD–CAE\. Rather than organizing the field only by model family, the review compares methods through the engineering information preserved and the behavior of generated models after modification\. The synthesis identifies a consistent evidence gap: geometric validity and program execution are increasingly strong, whereas native feature\-tree robustness, persistent references, design\-intent preservation, and downstream verification remain weakly benchmarked\. To address this gap, we propose the engineering\-grade AI–CAD \(EG–CAD\) framework, in which geometric validity and executability are mandatory gates followed by parametric editability, constraint/design\-intent preservation, feature\-history robustness, engineering compliance, and downstream usability\. A reference agent architecture and staged roadmap connect these criteria to CAD/CAM/CAE and smart\-manufacturing workflows, reframing AI–CAD as an engineering automation problem rather than a shape\-generation task\.

## [Efficacy of prophylactic tranexamic acid in preventing postpartum hemorrhage following repeat cesarean sections: a retrospective matched\-cohort study](../publications/22d94386604b7252e06e.md)

Xiaodan Di; LI Xiaojun; Zheng Zheng; Lanlan Guo; Taowei Dong; Qiaozhu Chen

Background Postpartum hemorrhage \(PPH\) is a leading cause of maternal mortality, and women with repeat cesarean sections are at high risk\. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of prophylactic tranexamic acid \(TXA\) in preventing PPH among women undergoing repeat cesarean sections\. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted including women with repeated cesarean sections at a tertiary obstetrical center in South China between July 2016 and December 2023\. Patients were divided into the TXA group and the control group according to intraoperative prophylactic TXA administration\. Given the imbalance in baseline characteristics, 1:2 propensity score matching \(PSM\) with a caliper of 0\.01 was performed to balance confounding variables\. The primary outcome was PPH incidence\. Secondary outcomes included estimated blood loss, hemoglobin decline, additional uterotonic use, and blood transfusion rate\. Results After 1:2 PSM, 2,777 women in the TXA group were matched with 5,554 women in the control group, with baseline characteristics well balanced\. The incidence of PPH was significantly lower in the TXA group than in the control group \(11\.09% vs\. 17\.03%, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The TXA group also demonstrated less calculated estimated blood loss, smaller hemoglobin reduction \(12\.06% vs\. 18\.44%, P &lt; 0\.001\), and lower requirements for additional uterotonic agents \(26\.90% vs\. 29\.80%, P = 0\.006\)\. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that prophylactic TXA was an independent protective factor against PPH \(OR 0\.620, 95% CI 0\.540\-0\.712, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. No significant difference was observed in blood transfusion rates \(1\.55% vs\. 2\.09%, P = 0\.089\)\. Conclusion Prophylactic TXA use was associated with a lower incidence of PPH and the need for additional uterotonics in women undergoing repeat cesarean sections\. Randomized trials in this specific population are needed\.

## [Entrepreneurial Performance and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: A Review of Psychological, Individual, Organisational and Environmental Determinants](../publications/22de12afe88774970a4c.md)

B Pathinettampadiyan; G Kingsly; H\. Samuel Thavaraj

Entrepreneurial performance is a multidimensional phenomenon that is influenced by the psychological attributes, individual competencies, organisational capabilities, financial resources, technological developments and environment\. This is crucial for fostering entrepreneurship effectiveness and sustainable entrepreneurship development as these determinants are interrelated\. The key factors affecting the performance of entrepreneurs are explored, focusing on emotional intelligence, entrepreneurial orientation, education, the digital transformation, financial capabilities, institutional support and sustainability\. The review brings together literature on psychological and individual factors, entrepreneurial orientation and competency building, digital transformation and financial skills, as well as environmental, institutional and sustainable entrepreneurship\. The reviewed studies have identified emotional intelligence as a salient psychological factor that facilitates emotional control, making decisions, coping with adversity, interpersonal relationships, leadership, and flexibility in the face of unpredictable business environments\. The other factors that contribute to opportunity recognition, innovation, entrepreneurial intention, and venture development are entrepreneurial education, experiential learning, digital competencies and entrepreneurial orientation\. Digital technologies and artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital platforms and other technologies offer opportunities to enhance resource mobilisation, market access and organisational performance, but face issues of digital inequality, ethical governance and technological capacity\. Entrepreneurial development and the ability to embrace sustainable business practices are also affected by financial literacy, access to finance, saving patterns and green finance\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Quality Assurance: Applications, Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Perspectives](../publications/22e81007fd252e175c88.md)

Ankita Roy

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly influencing pharmaceutical manufacturing and quality management by enabling data\-driven process monitoring, prediction, automation, and decision support\. This narrative review examines the application of AI across major pharmaceutical manufacturing operations and within quality assurance \(QA\) and quality control \(QC\)\. The review focuses on machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, predictive analytics, Internet of Things \(IoT\)\-enabled monitoring, robotics, and digital\-twin technologies\. Potential applications include raw\-material inspection, dispensing and weighing, granulation, blending, tablet compression, capsule filling, coating, packaging, warehouse management, predictive maintenance, documentation review, deviation management, corrective and preventive action \(CAPA\), validation support, risk assessment, visual inspection, laboratorydata interpretation, stability studies, and process analytical technology \(PAT\)\. AI can improve speed, consistency, traceability, and early detection of process or quality problems; however, these benefits depend on data quality, appropriate validation, cybersecurity, system integration, human oversight, and regulatory acceptability\. Current regulatory activity, including the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration&\#x27;s discussion paper on AI in drug manufacturing, demonstrates the growing importance of risk\-based approaches to AI adoption\. Overall, AI should be viewed as an enabling technology that augments, rather than replaces, pharmaceutical professionals\. Responsible implementation combining validated digital systems with human expertise may support safer, more efficient, and more reliable pharmaceutical manufacturing\.

## [Tourism, Hospitality and Digital Transformation in India: Economic Contributions, Employment, and Pathways to Sustainable Growth](../publications/22ef2f7c4f24309fe855.md)

Parul Gupta and  Partho Pratim Seal

Tourism and hospitality contribute significantly to India&\#x27;s economic development through employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment, entrepreneurship, and demand in other industries\. Other factors also influence the sector&\#x27;s contribution to development\. Digital transformation, enabled by online travel agencies, mobile money, artificial intelligence \(AI\), analytics, CRM, and smart destination technologies, offers opportunities to reduce transaction costs, expand market reach, improve productivity, and enhance visitor experiences\. However, challenges such as limited digital skills among small businesses, platform dependence, cyber threats, privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and job losses must be addressed\. This paper analyzes the tourism and hospitality sector&\#x27;s impact on the Indian economy and how technology affects the sector&\#x27;s growth and development\. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach with secondary data from government publications, policies, and academic literature, the paper discusses the significance of productivity, employment, inclusiveness, technology, and resilience\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Alternative, Nonformal, and Adult Learning in the Global South: Protocol for a Mixed\-Methods Systematic Review](../publications/22f1b2c2da4e4718a8a0.md)

Cyrus Pontawe Casingal

ABSTRACT: Background: Research on artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education has expanded rapidly, yet it remains concentrated in higher education and formal schooling in high\-income countries\. Alternative, nonformal, and adult learning programs, which serve out\-of\-school youth and adults across the Global South, are largely absent from this evidence base\. No systematic synthesis has examined how AI is used in these programs, what outcomes it produces, and what conditions shape its adoption\. Objective: This protocol describes a mixed\-methods systematic review that will identify, appraise, and synthesize empirical evidence on AI use in alternative, nonformal, and adult learning programs in low\- and middle\-income countries \(LMICs\)\. Methods: The review follows the JBI methodology for mixed\-methods systematic reviews and is reported according to PRISMA\-P\. Searches will cover Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ERIC, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, four regional databases, and grey literature sources for studies published from January 2015 onward\. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and appraise quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool\. Quantitative findings will be synthesized narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta\-analysis \(SWiM\) guideline, with meta\-analysis where at least three comparable studies exist\. Qualitative findings will be synthesized thematically\. Both strands will be integrated through a convergent segregated approach, and certainty of evidence will be rated with GRADE and GRADE\-CERQual\. Discussion: The review will provide the first consolidated synthesis of AI use in second\-chance and adult learning in the Global South\. Its findings will inform program managers, teacher developers, and policymakers responsible for programs such as the Philippine Alternative Learning System \(ALS\)\. Keywords: artificial intelligence; generative AI; nonformal education; adult learning; Alternative Learning System; Global South; systematic review protocol

## [Perceived Artificial Intelligence Skill Demand Across the Construction Project Lifecycle: Evidence from the Rwandan Construction Industry](../publications/22f609ea58971a90716d.md)

OLUWASEUN SUNDAY DOSUMU; Christine Musanase; Ryan Tumusiime Kaganga; Dieudonne Ahishakiye; Eric Iradukunda

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly transforming construction processes, yet limited empirical evidence exists on the skills required by professionals across different stages of the construction project lifecycle, particularly in developing economies\. This study evaluates the perceived demand for AI skills across the eight stages of the Royal Institute of British Architects \(RIBA\) Plan of Work in the Rwandan construction industry\. A quantitative cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 174 construction professionals representing architecture, engineering, quantity surveying and construction management\. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring the perceived demand for AI\-related skills across the eight lifecycle stages\. Descriptive statistics were used to assess and rank skill demand, while the Kruskal\-Wallis H test examined differences among professional groups, and the Friedman test assessed differences across lifecycle stages\. The findings show moderate\-to\-high demand for AI skills across all lifecycle stages\. The use stage recorded the highest overall demand, followed by strategic definition, and manufacturing and construction, while handover recorded the lowest\. Significant differences across lifecycle stages were identified using the Friedman test \(χ² = 19\.162, p = 0\.008\), although the practical effect was very weak \(Kendall&\#x27;s W = 0\.016\), indicating modest variation in relative intensity\. Most individual skills did not differ significantly across professional groups, suggesting a substantial common set of AI competencies alongside selected discipline\-specific requirements\. The study’s findings provide evidence for the development of targeted, stage\-specific construction education, professional development and workforce strategies in Rwanda and comparable developing economies\.

## [Do nominal formations retain their spatial distinctiveness during attacking sequences ending in goals? A spatiotemporal analysis of the 4\-2\-3\-1, 4\-3\-3, and 4\-4\-2 formations](../publications/230379b877aa2152ff46.md)

Onur Tütüncü; Yiğit Bartık; Saumya Mehta; Daniel Memmert

The objective of this study was twofold: firstly, to examine whether nominally distinct tactical formations remained spatially distinguishable or progressively converged towards similar collective spatial configurations as an open\-play goal approached; and secondly, to determine how the spatial organisation of each formation changed relative to its own match\-average configuration over the same pre\-goal period\. The data were obtained from 306 Bundesliga matches \(2016–17\), comprising 247 open\-play goal\-scoring sequences\. The final 60\-s prior to each goal were divided into four consecutive 15\-s intervals\. Spatial configurations were examined across these intervals, at the goal moment, and relative to each team&\#x27;s match\-average spatial configuration\. Spatial similarity was quantified using normalised Euclidean distances and panel data models\. In addition, supervised machine learning was employed to assess whether nominal formations remained distinguishable based solely on spatial configurations\. The spatial similarity of the match\-average configurations of formations varied markedly across the pre\-goal period\. At the moment of the goal, similarity reached only \.14 for the 4\-2\-3\-1, \.10 for the 4\-3\-3, and \.00 for the 4\-4\-2 \(p &lt; \.001\)\. The formations showed limited spatial distinguishability\. Accuracies were below 60%, with the lowest value of 29% observed between the 4\-3\-3 and 4\-4\-2 formations\. Only one formation demonstrated 71% accuracy\. Overall, machine learning revealed that there was limited spatial distinguishability among the nominal formations\. In summary, the reduced distinguishability between nominal formations may indicate a tendency towards greater structural similarity in goal\-scoring situations\. These findings provide a novel perspective on the conceptualisation and interpretation of tactical formations in modern football\.

## [The Cognitive Cost of LLM Writing: A Reading\-Time Comparison with Human Text](../publications/231094b5f28f9a49a9e6.md)

Kamer Cekini; Elisabetta Biondi; Chiara Boldrini; Andrea Passarella; Marco Conti

Although linguistic differences between human\-written and Large Language Model \(LLM\)\-generated texts have been extensively studied, their implications for the cognitive effort involved in reading remain less explored\. In psycholinguistics, reading time is commonly used as an indirect measure of cognitive processing effort\. Building on this perspective, we investigate whether human\-written texts and their LLM\-generated rewrites exhibit differences in predicted reading time that may reflect differences in processing demands for readers\. To this end, we introduce RoBERTa\-RT, a model trained on human eye\-tracking data to predict word\-level reading times\. We evaluate the model on both internal and external test sets, construct a paired dataset of 496 human\-written articles and their LLM\-generated rewrites, and apply RoBERTa\-RT to compare their predicted reading times\. Our findings show that LLM\-generated rewrites tend to be shorter and have slightly lower predicted total reading times, while exhibiting higher predicted reading times per word\. These differences are associated with systematic linguistic changes, including longer and less frequent words, greater lexical diversity, and higher contextual predictability\. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that LLM\-generated writing may redistribute reading demands: reducing the amount of text to process while increasing the predicted processing effort associated with individual words\. This highlights the importance of considering not only the linguistic characteristics of machine\-generated content, but also its potential implications for human cognitive processing\.

## [A blueprint for future press legislation protecting every element of the media in the use of information technology](../publications/2314b75fa2129a7cd4db.md)

Muhammad Dicky Khairil; Achmad Faishal; Saprudin Saprudin

Law Number 40 of 1999 on the Press has never once been amended, while the responsibility of digital platforms rests only in a presidential regulation and the use of artificial intelligence only in an institutional regulation\. This study formulates future press legislation capable of protecting every element of the media in the use of information technology\. It is normative legal research, descriptive, analytical and prescriptive in character, employing statutory, conceptual, comparative and case approaches, and analysed deductively against a coherence criterion of legal truth\. The result is a blueprint for new press legislation comprising ten principal substances: expanded definitions of the press following the journalistic function; a guarantee of press freedom in both its negative and positive dimensions; a mandatory tiered mechanism of dispute resolution; strengthening of the Press Council; a chapter on the responsibility of digital platform companies; a chapter on artificial intelligence; a journalistic exemption in personal data protection; verification of press companies and protection of citizen journalists; content moderation under judicial supervision; and a harmonising lex specialis clause\. The blueprint is crowned by an original theoretical construction, the Theory of Dignified Press Coherence, built on four axioms, five dimensions of coherence and five propositions\. The article concludes that the core problem of Indonesian press law is incoherence, and that its remedy is coherence embodied in certain statutory norms\.

## [Why Interfacial Electric Fields May Appear Weaker: An Electron\-Density\-Based Study of the Flat Air–Water Interface](../publications/232893845a2fa8ad542a.md)

Gabriele Amante; Giuseppe Cassone

Abstract The catalytic properties of water microdroplets are often attributed to strong interfacial electric fields, yet the nature of these fields remains debated\. Here we combine quantum data\-driven many\-body molecular dynamics, ab initio resampling, and spatially resolved electric field evaluations to rigorously assess intermolecular electrostatics at the flat air–water interface\. The calculated local intermolecular quantity may be viewed as a microsolvation electric\-field descriptor of the environment experienced by a molecular species approaching or residing near the interface\. By classifying molecules using two complementary interface definitions and going beyond classical partial\-charge methods, we obtain field maps directly from the electronic charge density\. Similarly to recent experimental findings, the bulk and interfacial field distributions overlap strongly, while their mean values exhibit a modest interfacial reduction of ∼10%\. Correlations with the density profiles obtained from different reference frames indicate that density depletion near the surface contributes to this attenuation\. Beyond offering an electron\-density\-based methodology for evaluating local electric fields, these findings suggest that exceptionally strong local fields alone may not fully account for the enhanced reactivity reported in microdroplets\.

In this study, we reviewed the distribution of alien\-dominated and co\-dominated plant communities in Italy\. We updated a former syntaxonomic scheme based on the Italian Vegetation Prodrome and also produced a syntaxonomic scheme based on FloraVeg\.EU\. For the first time, a cartographic synthesis has been produced\. Mapping outputs were standardised using the European Environmental Agency 10 km × 10 km grid\. In total, 1,566 occurrences of alien\-dominated or co\-dominated plant communities were verified and recorded based on 170 bibliographical sources, 147 of which are georeferenced\. ## [BRUTE FORCE LOGIN DETECTION: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF IPBASED, ACCOUNT\-BASED, MACHINE LEARNING\-BASED, AND HYBRID APPROACHES](../publications/232ad7e47ad71d8b235f.md)



Brute force login attacks remain a persistent threat, and detection research has split into IP\-based, account\-based, machine learning\-based, and hybrid approaches that are rarely compared on common terms\.This paper reviews 18 papers published between 2006 and 2026, classifies them by the component that makes the detection decision, and compares them on reported accuracy, resilience to IP rotation and low\-rate attacks, computational overhead, real\-time suitability, dataset realism, and deployment complexity\.No experiments are run, and all numerical results are as reported by the authors of the cited works\.Accuracy figures are plentiful but not directly comparable: nine studies report values from 94\.3% to 99\.995%, mostly on public benchmarks, and only four papers use production data\.Evasion is tested directly in three papers, overhead is measured in four, and SSH dominates protocol coverage\.Account\-based methods have the thinnest evidence, while hybrid methods carry the strongest evidence on distributed and low\-rate attacks\.The paper closes with criteria\-based deployment recommendations and a call for a shared benchmark that includes evasion scenarios\.

## [Exploring generative AI appropriation in Colombian adults’ informal English learning](../publications/23312e30193d41a857b0.md)

Mariana Mora Gaitán; Jenny Catalina Loaiza Fuquen

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is transforming the possibilities for informal language learning by providing immediate feedback, conversational interaction, and potentially personalized learning experiences\. However, its use does not necessarily entail greater learner autonomy, self\-regulation, or agency\. This study aimed to understand how Colombian adults configure their informal English learning practices through GenAI tools, with particular attention to decision\-making processes, self\-regulation, evaluation of AI\-generated responses, and the articulation of GenAI with other learning resources\. Adopting a qualitative, exploratory, and interpretive approach, the study involved four Colombian adults with diverse linguistic, educational, and GenAI\-use trajectories\. Data were generated through participant characterization forms, GenAI interaction records, semi\-structured interviews, and, when available, documentary evidence of participants’ interactions with the technology\. A predominantly inductive thematic analysis generated four interconnected categories: negotiating control over the learning interaction; constructing and calibrating trust in AI\-generated feedback; experiencing personalization through responsive interaction; and reconfiguring the broader learning repertoire\. Findings show that participants assumed, negotiated, and delegated control in different ways and developed varying criteria for accepting, questioning, or verifying GenAI\-generated responses\. They also selectively integrated GenAI with other digital and human learning resources\. Based on these findings, the study conceptualizes GenAI appropriation as a form of situated orchestration through which learners coordinate technological affordances with their purposes, prior knowledge, evaluative criteria, and broader learning repertoires\. The findings suggest that GenAI does not automatically produce learner autonomy or agency; rather, it creates new spaces in which these may be exercised, negotiated, or delegated\.

## [Beyond Latent Personalization: Integrating HRV\-Conditioned Personalization via LLM for Interpretable Stress Detection](../publications/23325f498b575cfa6091.md)

Wei\-Hsiang Ma; Ya\-Tse Wu; Hsing\-Hang Chou; Chi\-Chun Lee

Stress detection based on heart rate variability \(HRV\) has received increasing attention\. However, existing personalized approaches integrate personal attributes with HRV through latent representations, limiting the interpretability of their interactions\. In this work, we propose an LLM\-enhanced personalized stress detection framework that integrates HRV features and personal attributes through LLM\-based semantic interpretation\. The proposed framework achieves a 29\.9% relative MCC improvement over the strongest baseline on TILES\-2018 while providing human\-readable descriptions of individual physiological responses\. The results highlight the potential of LLM\-based semantic interpretation for achieving both effective and interpretable personalized stress detection\.

## [Supply Chain Management and Business Performance of Agri\-Farm Businesses in the Province of Rizal](../publications/233a62c44f4e4fd47c8d.md)

Krizzia Ann Camille Soriano

Agricultural enterprises in the Province of Rizal face persistent supply chain challenges, including fragmented supplier networks, inadequate post\-harvest infrastructure, and limited coordination across production and distribution stages\. This study assessed supply chain management \(SCM\) practices and their relationship with the non\-financial business performance of agri\-farm businesses in Rizal\. Specifically, it examined SCM implementation using the Supply Chain Operations Reference \(SCOR\) Model dimensions of Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, and Return, alongside business performance indicators comprising cost efficiency, operational efficiency, and customer satisfaction\. Employing a quantitative descriptive\-correlational research design, the study involved 342 respondents, consisting of 57 agri\-farm owners, managers, and supervisors and 285 customers selected through stratified sampling\. Data were collected using a validated five\-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed through weighted means, analysis of variance \(ANOVA\), and Pearson&\#x27;s correlation coefficient\. Findings revealed that SCM practices were implemented to a high extent, with Source receiving the highest assessment and Return the lowest\. Business performance was likewise rated high, particularly in customer satisfaction\. ANOVA indicated no significant differences in SCM assessments across demographic profiles, while significant differences emerged between respondent groups regarding business performance evaluations\. Pearson correlation established a significant positive relationship between SCM practices and business performance, with Deliver and Return demonstrating the strongest associations with cost efficiency\. The findings highlight the importance of delivery reliability and reverse logistics in improving agribusiness performance\. The study provides a SCOR\-based framework to guide agri\-farm operators, cooperative managers, and policymakers in strengthening supply chain efficiency, operational competitiveness, and sustainable agricultural business development within the province\.

## [A plataformização da leitura: uma análise documental do Leia Paraná](../publications/233f5e2889be78df4c30.md)

Suelen Ariane Campiolo Trevizan

A plataforma Leia Paraná foi implantada em 2023 como política pública de incentivo à leitura, consolidando\-se o modelo de plataformização do ensino \(Van Dijck; Poell, 2018\) em meio a um contexto de reforma empresarial da educação \(Freitas, 2018\)\. Passados três anos, ainda se sabe pouco sobre seu funcionamento além dos indicadores quantitativos divulgados pela propaganda oficial\. Diante dessa escassez de informações, este artigo procura descrever criticamente a plataforma, analisando sua contratação, arquitetura, funcionalidades, acervo e objetivos institucionais\. A análise se baseia em levantamento de dados sobre a implementação disponibilizados pela SEED\-PR, pelo Portal da Transparência e pelo TCE\-PR, complementados pela observação da interface, pela catalogação do acervo e pela comparação dessas características com as metas estabelecidas pelo governo\. Conclui\-se que seus objetivos são atendidos apenas parcialmente\. Embora haja a oferta de obras acessíveis e potencialmente atraentes para os estudantes, apresenta limitações quanto à transparência dos dados coletados, ao diagnóstico qualitativo dos resultados e ao desenvolvimento da cultura digital\.

## [Ultrafast Laser Micro/Nano Processing of GaN for Next‐Generation Microelectromechanical Systems \(MEMS\) Applications](../publications/2348624bdcfe76677888.md)

Rizwana Bibi; Yang Li; Muhammad Farhan; Rui Wen; Zhi Wang; Lan Jiang; Youqi Zhu; Xiaodong Li; Tai Peng; Xueqiang Zhang

ABSTRACT Gallium nitride \(GaN\) has established itself as a wide‐bandgap semiconductor, driving advances in radio‐frequency devices, solid‐state lighting, and high‐power electronics\. Its chemical stability, strong piezoelectric properties, and biocompatibility have turned GaN into a crucial candidate for next‐generation microelectromechanical systems \(MEMS\), including sensors, resonators, and energy harvesters operating in harsh environments\. However, GaN&\#x27;s transition from planar devices to 3D MEMS structures is limited by its hardness, brittleness, and chemical inertness\. Conventional fabrication methods induce heat‐affected zones, lattice damage, and micro‐cracks, significantly reducing device yield and performance\. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of ultrafast laser micro/nano processing as a transformative, non‐contact manufacturing paradigm to overcome these limitations\. We first elucidate the fundamental mechanisms of laser–material interactions, distinguishing between picosecond \(ps\) and femtosecond \(fs\) regimes, with attention to non‐linear absorption, ionization dynamics, and non‐thermal ablation enabling submicron resolution with minimal collateral damage\. We investigate laser methodologies including maskless direct writing, laser lift‐off \(LLO\), and laser‐induced periodic surface structures \(LIPSS\), highlighting their integration into high‐performance GaN MEMS devices for enhanced sensitivity\. We explore hybrid integration with complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor \(CMOS\) technology and artificial intelligence \(AI\)‐driven optimization to address throughput challenges, offering pathways toward wafer‐scale manufacturing of next‐generation GaN MEMS\.

## [The trade\-off between minimal instability and larger improvements over deferred acceptance](../publications/2352b36c13f3163a4df9.md)

Taylor Knipe; Josué Ortega

The celebrated Efficiency\-Adjusted Deferred Acceptance mechanism \(EADA\) improves the efficiency of the DA algorithm via consented priority violations\. Notwithstanding its many merits, we show that EADA can improve only two students when an alternative mechanism that Pareto\-dominates DA could benefit all but one student\. This shortfall in the number of students improved is not exclusive of EADA but extends to all setwise minimally unstable mechanisms, i\.e\. those that generate a set of blocking pairs that is never a strict superset of that of another mechanism\. The incompatibility between number of students improved and minimal instability disappears when blocking pairs are compared cardinally rather than by set inclusion\. In some problems, EADA can be doubly dominated: improving fewer students while generating more blocking pairs\.

## [XAI and its Applications in Decision Support System](../publications/23570c0514394af30bfc.md)

Gitin Garg; Kiya Jain; Vishal Shrivastava; Akhil Pandey

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has transformed decision\-making across various industries by enabling systems to analyse large volumes of data and provide intelligent recommendations\. However, many modern AI models, particularly deep learning algorithms, function as &quot;black boxes,&quot; making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are generated\. This lack of transparency limits the adoption of AI in critical domains such as healthcare, finance, law, and business\. Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) has emerged as a promising solution that improves transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI systems\. Decision Support Systems \(DSS\) assist decision\-makers by combining data, analytical models, and domain knowledge\. Integrating XAI into DSS enables users to understand AI\-generated recommendations, thereby improving confidence and accountability\. This review paper explores the concepts of XAI, different explanation techniques, and their applications in DSS\. The paper also discusses recent research, challenges, limitations, and future research directions

## [Integración de modelación matemática y control estadístico en la formación técnico\-profesional de gastronomía: un estudio de caso en la producción de cheesecake semifrío](../publications/235c40fb9d99fa2b8bd3.md)

Paula Isidora Mora Caballero; Valeria Edith Araujo de la Cruz; Sandra Rusbeli Lugo Caraballo; Joaquín Emerson Gutiérrez Muñoz; Victoria Eglee Cedeño Artigas; Diego Javier Moya Rojas; Gloria Estrella Tapia Rivas; Antonio de la Hoz Saldaña

Este estudio formaliza la receta técnica de un cheesecake semifrío mediante el uso de herramientas de modelación lineal para optimizar su escalado industrial\. El objetivo principal es transformar una receta empírica tradicional en un sistema físico\-matemático reproducible\. Se definen funciones lineales para el consumo de insumos y se establece una constante de rigidez estructural \(R = 2\.2\) para garantizar la estabilidad mecánica de la base\. Los resultados del modelo proyectado demuestran que la aplicación de razones de proporcionalidad y control estadístico reduce las mermas en un 78 % y disminuye la varianza de peso en el producto final, asegurando uniformidad y alta calidad en la producción a gran escala\.

## [Komparasi Algoritma Machine Learning Untuk Klasifikasi Risiko Serangan Jantung Di Indonesia](../publications/235cc67ffd9b72d527fa.md)

Rizal Maulana; Ahmad Al Kaafi; Rizka Dahlia

Serangan jantung merupakan salah satu penyebab kematian tertinggi di Indonesia sehingga diperlukan upaya deteksi dini untuk mengidentifikasi individu yang berisiko mengalami kondisi tersebut\. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan performa algoritma Decision Tree, Random Forest, dan Gradient Boosting dalam klasifikasi risiko serangan jantung di Indonesia, serta menganalisis pengaruh feature selection terhadap performa model\. Penelitian menggunakan dataset Heart Attack Prediction in Indonesia yang diperoleh dari Kaggle, yang terdiri atas 158\.355 data individu dan 28 atribut\. Data tersebut mencakup karakteristik individu dan faktor yang berkaitan dengan risiko serangan jantung, seperti usia, jenis kelamin, hipertensi, diabetes, kadar kolesterol, obesitas, kebiasaan merokok, aktivitas fisik, tekanan darah, serta riwayat penyakit jantung sebelumnya\. Tahapan penelitian meliputi data cleaning, transformasi data menggunakan one\-hot encoding, feature selection menggunakan metode Gain Ratio, serta pembagian data menjadi 80% data latih dan 20% data uji\. Performa model dievaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1\-score\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Gradient Boosting memperoleh akurasi tertinggi sebesar 73,6%, diikuti Decision Tree sebesar 72,2% dan Random Forest sebesar 71,2%\. Feature selection menghasilkan 9 atribut terpilih tanpa memberikan peningkatan performa yang berarti\. Dengan demikian, Gradient Boosting merupakan algoritma dengan performa terbaik dalam klasifikasi risiko serangan jantung pada penelitian ini\.

## [Integration of Hadith Values into the Islamic Education Curriculum](../publications/237938a0e9683509487b.md)

Ismail Pane; Hasan; Siti Aisyah; Syarifah Laili; Sustikasari

This study aims to analyze the integration of hadits values into the Islamic education curriculum as an effort to develop learners with strong character, noble morals, and a balanced spiritual, intellectual, and social personality\. The rapid advancement of technology, globalization, and social transformation requires the Islamic education curriculum to emphasize not only knowledge acquisition but also the internalization of prophetic values derived from the Qur’ân and Hadits\. This study employed the Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) method by examining relevant scholarly articles, books, and academic documents related to Islamic education, curriculum development, and the implementation of hadits values\. The data were analyzed through the processes of identification, selection, synthesis, and interpretation to obtain a comprehensive understanding of the integration model of hadits values within the Islamic education curriculum\. The findings reveal that hadits values can be integrated through four main dimensions: the development of educational objectives oriented toward character and moral formation, the strengthening of learning content based on prophetic values, the implementation of teaching strategies that emulate the educational methods of Prophet Muhammad \(peace be upon him\), and an assessment system that balances cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains\. Furthermore, the successful implementation of hadits value integration requires exemplary educators, a religious school culture, and the wise utilization of digital technology as a learning medium\. This study proposes the Hadits Values Integrated Islamic Curriculum \(HVIIC\) as a conceptual framework that positions Hadits as the philosophical, pedagogical, and ethical foundation for Islamic curriculum development\. The proposed model is expected to strengthen the quality of Islamic education by enabling it to respond to contemporary challenges while preserving the authentic values of Islamic teachings\.

## [Cyperus flavicomus \(Cyperaceae\), long misnamed C\. macrostachyos: a comprehensive taxonomic reassessment with annotated synonymy and voucher\-backed global distribution](../publications/23983d83e2a4aff6df60.md)

Aidan D\. Ross; Jason Keith Norsworthy

The pantropical annual flatsedge widely known as Cyperus macrostachyos Lam\. \(Cyperaceae; Cyperus subg\. Cyperus, former segregate genus Pycreus\) has been described under no fewer than 30 names over the past two centuries, variously treated as one or two species, with no substantive consensus on circumscription or nomenclature\. In North America, the species is instead recognized as C\. flavicomus Michx\. To resolve these discrepancies, we examined the protologues and, where available, original type material for all names currently or historically synonymized with C\. macrostachyos s\.l\., supplemented by an extensive survey of digitized collections ascribed to the species and of broader Pycreus material from Africa and South Asia \(ca\. 2,000 specimens from 130 herbaria in total\)\. We report three principal findings\. First, the morphological variation historically used to separate the species into two taxa is attributable to characters that are either environmentally plastic or maturity\-dependent, and does not warrant recognition of more than one species\. Second, examination of the holotype and holotype fragment of C\. macrostachyos reveals that the material is not conspecific with the pantropical species to which it has been applied since Hooper and Raynal \(1969\), but corresponds in all observable characters to the South Asian endemic C\. puncticulatus Vahl\. The “Ex Africa” locality cited by Lamarck \(1791\) could not be corroborated by any material among the extensive African collections surveyed; we render the type citation as “Uncertain locality \(‘Ex Africa’ teste Lamarck 1791\)” to reflect this\. Third, the correct name for the pantropical species is C\. flavicomus Michx\. \(1803\)—first reinstated by Tucker \(1985\), here independently confirmed and extended to encompass the full synonymy\. Conservation of C\. puncticulatus Vahl against C\. macrostachyos Lam\. is recommended under Art\. 14 of the ICN; a formal proposal will be submitted to Taxon\. An annotated synonymy, revised description, and voucher\-backed global distribution for C\. flavicomus Michx\. and lectotype designations for eleven names are provided\.

## [PROOF\-THEORETIC RELATIONS BETWEEN HIGMAN’S AND KRUSKAL’S THEOREM, AND INDEPENDENCE RESULTS FOR TREE\-LIKE STRUCTURES](../publications/239a9e8a2dc9b01fc7fc.md)

Gabriele Buriola; Andreas Weiermann

Abstract Higman’s lemma and Kruskal’s theorem are two of the most celebrated results in the theory of well quasi\-orders\. In his seminal paper G\. Higman obtained what is known as Higman’s lemma as a corollary of a more general theorem, dubbed here as Higman’s theorem\. While the lemma deals with finite sequences over a well quasi\-order, the theorem is about abstract operations of arbitrarily high arity\. J\. B\. Kruskal was fully aware of this broader framework: in his seminal paper, he not only applied Higman’s lemma at crucial points of his proof but also followed Higman’s proof schema\. At the conclusion of the article, Kruskal noted that Higman’s theorem is a special case—restricted to trees of finite degree—of his own tree theorem\. Although he provided no formal reduction, he included a glossary translating concepts between the tree and algebraic settings\. The equivalence between these versions was later clarified by D\. Schmidt and M\. Pouzet\. In this work, we revisit that equivalence to illuminate the proof\-theoretical relationships between the two theorems within the base system RCA 0 $\_0$ Subscript 0 of reverse mathematics\. Moreover, some independence results over first\- and second\-order theories are treated\. In particular, tree\-like structures, involving either Ackermannian terms or exponential expressions, are studied unveiling well\-foundedness properties that are independent from Peano arithmetic and relevant fragments of second\-order arithmetic\.

## [BMP4 and WIF1 expression in mother–child pairs in relation to anorectal malformations and maternal reproductive history](../publications/239d3a637bfcfeedc999.md)

Maleha Asim; Amena Rahim; Mudassar Fiaz; Anoshia Javed; Waqar Ahmed Awan

Anorectal malformations \(ARM\) result from disrupted embryonic hindgut development, with both genetic and environmental factors contributing to disease pathogenesis\. However, the relationships among maternal molecular alterations, reproductive history, and offspring gene expression remain poorly understood\. This hospital\-based case–control study evaluated BMP4 and WIF1 expression in peripheral blood from 182 biological mother–child pairs, comprising 83 children with ARM and 99 controls\. Gene expression was quantified by quantitative real\-time PCR and expressed as ΔCt, with 2⁻ΔΔCt used to describe relative expression\. Consanguineous marriage was more frequent among mothers of children with ARM than controls \(67\.5% vs\. 40\.4%; odds ratio 3\.06, 95% CI 1\.66–5\.63\) and was included as a covariate in adjusted analyses\. Children with ARM showed markedly reduced BMP4 expression compared with controls \(0\.44\-fold, 95% CI 0\.33–0\.59\), a difference unaffected by adjustment for consanguinity; BMP4 expression was similarly, though more modestly, reduced in their mothers \(0\.77\-fold, 95% CI 0\.63–0\.95\)\. Child WIF1 expression did not differ between groups, and evidence for altered maternal WIF1 expression was inconclusive\. In multivariable regression, ARM status was the only independent predictor of child BMP4 ΔCt \(B = 1\.24, 95% CI 0\.77–1\.72, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Maternal miscarriage history significantly moderated the association between ARM status and child WIF1 ΔCt \(FDR\-adjusted P = 0\.001 for miscarriage group; P = 0\.004 for recurrent miscarriage\)\. These findings support an association between reduced BMP4 expression and ARM in both children and their mothers and suggest that maternal reproductive history may modify child WIF1 expression\. Prospective and functional studies are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these associations\.

## [Dexmedetomidine versus Lidocaine for Intubation in Traumatic Brain Injury: A Double\-Blind Randomized Trial with Post Hoc Equivalence Analysis](../publications/23a37a4713008e8b2fc0.md)

Shallahudin; Aswoco Andyk Asmoro; Ristiawan Muji Laksono; Buyung Hartiyo Laksono

Background\. Laryngoscopy\-induced pressure surges and induction\-related hypotension threaten the injured brain\. Dexmedetomidine and lidocaine blunt the intubation response, but their relative effect in traumatic brain injury \(TBI\) is uncertain\. Objective\. To estimate the difference in the mean arterial pressure \(MAP\) response to intubation between the two agents and to define, post hoc, the differences excluded\. Methods\. In a double\-blind randomized trial, 71 adults with TBI received dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg over 10 min \(n = 37\) or lidocaine 1\.5 mg/kg over 2 min plus an 8\-min saline sham \(n = 34\) before standardized induction; lidocaine ended about 11 min before laryngoscopy\. The primary outcome was the change in MAP from baseline to 1 min after intubation\. The trial was not registered\. Analyses included Welch estimation, post hoc two one\-sided tests \(TOST\), ANCOVA and exact tests\. Results\. MAP fell by 11\.5 mmHg with lidocaine and 12\.8 mmHg with dexmedetomidine; no pressor response occurred\. The difference \(dexmedetomidine − lidocaine\) was −1\.30 mmHg \(95% CI −4\.14 to 1\.54; p = 0\.365\); adjusted, −1\.66 mmHg \(−4\.31 to 1\.00\)\. Post hoc, differences beyond ±4 mmHg were excluded \(TOST p = 0\.031\)\. Heart rate did not differ \(Holm p = 1\.000\)\. Ephedrine was needed in 3/37 versus 2/34 and atropine in 2/37 versus 1/34 \(both p = 1\.000\)\. Conclusion\. In adults with predominantly mild\-to\-moderate TBI, MAP responses to intubation with the two agents differed by about 4 mmHg or less post hoc, with infrequent rescue therapy\. Without a placebo arm, neither agent’s own effect can be quantified\.

## [IoT\-Integrated Intelligent Platform for Biomedical Waste Classification and Hazardous Emission Alerts](../publications/23aacdf2329ca9a961a4.md)

Jaswanth R\.; Ramya K\.L\.; Shruthi S\.; Archana T\.; Anusuya K\.

Improper handling of biomedical and bio\-waste can result in exposing health care professionals and the surrounding environment to dangerous infections and emission of dangerous gases\. Manual sorting and monitoring of waste is also time\-consuming and cannot give real\-time data on the state of stored waste\. This research study proposes an IoT\-integrated smart biowaste management system which incorporates waste identification using camera, waste classification using machine learning, gas sensing, and alerts generation\. An image of the waste that is placed in the collection device is taken by the camera, while image preprocessing and machine learning is performed for the identification of the category of the waste\. Along with this process, the MQ\-2 sensor measures the condition of the gas in the surroundings of the collected waste and makes a comparison with the predefined threshold\. A microcontroller controls the processing of the image as well as the sensor and sends the processed information to the cloud platform\. Upon detecting any abnormal gas condition, the system triggers a local buzzer as well as remote alerts\.

## [ПРЕЦЕДЕНТНІ ФЕНОМЕНИ ЯК КОГНІТИВНІ МЕХАНІЗМИ ФРЕЙМУВАННЯ В АНГЛОМОВНОМУ МЕДІАДИСКУРСІ](../publications/23aba1fddb53e8377aaa.md)

Ирина Архипова

У статті здійснено лінгвокогнітивний аналіз прецедентних феноменів у сучасному англомовному медіадис\- курсі\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням ролі медіакомунікації у формуванні суспільних уявлень та інтерпретацій соціальної реальності, а також необхідністю комплексного вивчення мовних механізмів когні\- тивного впливу на адресата\. Особливу увагу приділено аналізу прецедентних феноменів як культурно зумовлених мовних одиниць, що апелюють до колективної пам’яті мовної спільноти та спільного фонового знання\. Метою дослідження є виявлення когнітивних механізмів актуалізації прецедентних феноменів у сучасному англомовному медіадискурсі та з’ясування їх ролі у процесах фреймування, оцінювання й інтерпретації соціаль\- ної реальності\. Методологічну основу роботи становить лінгвокогнітивний підхід, у межах якого мова розгля\- дається як інструмент концептуалізації знань та формування інтерпретаційних моделей реальності\. У дослі\- дженні використано методи когнітивно\-дискурсивного аналізу, контекстуальної інтерпретації та елементи якісного корпусного аналізу\. Матеріалом дослідження слугували тексти сучасних англомовних засобів масової інформації, зокрема аналі\- тичні та інформаційні статті провідних міжнародних онлайн\-видань\. Результати дослідження засвідчують, що прецедентні феномени виконують функцію когнітивних тригерів, які активують культурну пам’ять та сприяють формуванню інтерпретаційних рамок медіаповідомлень\. Встановлено, що прецедентні імена, висло\- ви, тексти та ситуації активно використовуються для імпліцитної передачі оцінних значень, емоційного впливу та переконування адресата\. Їх актуалізація забезпечує швидке залучення спільного фонового знання аудиторії та сприяє формуванню певних моделей інтерпретації подій\. Доведено, що прецедентні феномени виступають важливим інструментом когнітивного структурування інформації та формування смислів у сучасному медіа\- дискурсі\.

## [Institutional capacity, FTA network breadth, and trade efficiency in China’s aquatic\-product imports: evidence from a true random\-effects stochastic frontier gravity model](../publications/23aecefbfe4cfc44762f.md)

Wei Yang; Kunlin Tang

China’s rapidly expanding aquatic\-product imports raise an important economic question: how fully do established supplier relationships realize the trade capacity supported by market scale, production capacity, and institutional conditions? Using a balanced panel of 16 major suppliers over 2013–2022, this study estimates a true random\-effects stochastic frontier gravity model that separates persistent supplier heterogeneity from time\-varying trade inefficiency\. The results identify two distinct margins\. China’s fishery\-sector scale and supplier total aquatic\-animal production expand the conditional import frontier, while stronger China\-side logistics\-service competence and broader supplier external FTA networks are associated with lower trade inefficiency and stronger frontier realization\. The FTA\-network relationship remains particularly consistent across alternative time controls, LPI annualization, supplier economic and governance controls, and broader PPML samples\. Mean JLMS trade efficiency rises from 58\.00% in 2013 to 89\.21% in 2022\. In 2022, observed imports of USD 18\.41 billion correspond to a conditional frontier of approximately USD 20\.65 billion, leaving a USD 2\.24 billion conditional gap concentrated in a small number of large\-frontier relationships\. An efficiency–frontier matrix further distinguishes core high\-realization suppliers, large\-frontier relationships with greater room for realization, and efficient smaller suppliers that contribute diversification\. These findings show that trade\-capacity formation and trade\-capacity realization are complementary dimensions of resilient aquatic\-food supply chains\.

## [Extraction, Characterization and Application of Essential Oil from Lemon \(Citrus Limon \(L\.\) Osbeck\) Peel](../publications/23af817d0d8769fea192.md)



Essential oil was extracted from lemon \(Citrus limon \(L\.\) Osbeck\) peel by steam distillation and characterized to evaluate its potential industrial applications\.The oil was recovered in a yield of 0\.38%, within the range reported for citrus peel oils\.It was colourless, soluble in organic solvents and insoluble in water, with a specific gravity of 0\.450\.Chemical characterization gave an acid value of 7\.59 mg/g, an iodine value of 11\.35 mg/g, a saponification value of 100\.70 mg/g and an ester value of 93\.11 mg/g\.The low iodine value classified the oil as non\-drying, while the low saponification value indicated a non\-saponifying oil, consistent with the terpenoid\-dominated composition typical of citrus peel oils\.The extracted oil was subsequently incorporated as a fragrance ingredient in the formulation of liquid soap, demonstrating a practical route for valorizing lemon\-peel waste into a value\-added consumer product\.

## [बकग एव वततय कषतर म कतरम बदधमतत: अवसर, चनतय एव भवषय क सभवनए](../publications/23b32e0d95f5efdd8e96.md)

किशोरी लाल अहिरवार

शोध सारांश पिछले कुछ वर्षों में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence—AI\) का उपयोग बैंकिंग, बीमा, निवेश तथा फिनटेक \(वित्तीय प्रौद्योगिकी\) के क्षेत्रों में तेजी से बढ़ा है। भारत में डिजिटल बैंकिंग के विस्तार ने वित्तीय सेवाओं को अधिक सुलभ और सुविधाजनक बनाने में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है। जहाँ पहले बैंकिंग सेवाओं के लिए ग्राहकों को लंबी कतारों में खड़ा होना पड़ता था, वहीं आज डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म के माध्यम से अनेक वित्तीय कार्य कम समय में पूरे किए जा सकते हैं। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता आधारित प्रणालियाँ ऋण आवेदनों के मूल्यांकन, धोखाधड़ी की पहचान, ग्राहक सहायता, जोखिम विश्लेषण तथा निवेश संबंधी निर्णयों में सहयोग प्रदान कर सकती हैं। इससे वित्तीय संस्थानों की कार्यक्षमता बढ़ाने, समय की बचत करने और ग्राहकों को बेहतर सेवाएँ उपलब्ध कराने की संभावनाएँ विकसित हुई हैं। प्रस्तुत शोध में भारतीय बैंकिंग एवं वित्तीय क्षेत्र, विशेष रूप से शेयर बाजार में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के उपयोग का अध्ययन किया गया है। इसमें AI के प्रमुख लाभों, व्यावहारिक चुनौतियों तथा भविष्य की संभावनाओं का विश्लेषण किया गया है। इसके साथ ही डेटा की गोपनीयता, साइबर सुरक्षा, एल्गोरिदमिक पक्षपात, निर्णय प्रक्रिया में पारदर्शिता तथा तकनीक पर अत्यधिक निर्भरता जैसी चुनौतियों पर भी ध्यान केंद्रित किया गया है। वित्तीय क्षेत्र में AI के उपयोग को जिम्मेदार और सुरक्षित बनाए रखने के लिए भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक \(RBI\) तथा भारतीय प्रतिभूति और विनिमय बोर्ड \(SEBI\) जैसी नियामक संस्थाओं की भूमिका भी अध्ययन का महत्त्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है। अध्ययन का उद्देश्य यह समझना है कि कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता किस प्रकार भारतीय बैंकिंग एवं वित्तीय सेवाओं को अधिक प्रभावी, सुरक्षित और सुलभ बनाने में योगदान दे सकती है तथा इसके उपयोग से उत्पन्न जोखिमों को किस प्रकार कम किया जा सकता है। निष्कर्षतः, वित्तीय क्षेत्र में AI का सफल उपयोग तकनीकी नवाचार के साथ\-साथ मजबूत साइबर सुरक्षा, डेटा संरक्षण, पारदर्शिता, उचित नियामक निगरानी और मानवीय पर्यवेक्षण पर निर्भर करता है। इन पहलुओं पर ध्यान देकर कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के माध्यम से भारत के वित्तीय क्षेत्र में अधिक समावेशी, कुशल और विश्वसनीय सेवाओं के विकास को प्रोत्साहित किया जा सकता है।

## [Longitudinal single\-cell RNA\-seq profiling of lung cell phenotypes, signaling, and cross\-talk during fibrosis resolution](../publications/23b9cf73299c9b91e2c8.md)

Jennifer M\. Speth; Vivian T Wong; Steve D\. Guzman; Natalie Walker; Yang Liu; Rachel L\. Zemans; Timothy S\. Blackwell; Carlos A\. Aguilar; Marc L\. Peters\-Golden; Sean M\. Fortier

Resolution of fibrosis following lung injury is distinguished from persistent/progressive parenchymal scarring through the timely clearance of aberrant cell types, removal of excess collagens, and regeneration of alveolar structure\. The requisite signaling pathways, cellular cross\-talk, and phenotypic shifts associated with, and required for, resolution of established lung fibrosis have not been well characterized\. To address this critical knowledge gap, we performed longitudinal single\-cell RNA sequencing of whole mouse lung digests obtained during spontaneously resolving fibrosis\. We observed a fibrosis\-associated macrophage and an ECM\-secreting Csmd1\+ fibroblast population emerging during peak fibrosis and undergoing partial clearance during resolution\. Our study also revealed conspicuous shifts in well\-established pathways associated with tissue repair and fibrosis among immune, mesenchymal, and epithelial cells during spontaneous resolution\. In addition to a decline in pro\-fibrotic driver pathways, the putative anti\-fibrotic pathways cAMP, HGF/MET, and TWEAK were enriched in several cell types during spontaneous resolution\. CellChat analysis was used to predict the cellular senders and recipients of each pathway and characterize their longitudinal changes\. Our characterization of the cellular and molecular dynamics in whole lungs during spontaneous fibrosis resolution provides a foundation for the identification of endogenous pathways that might be leveraged to treat pulmonary fibrosis\.

## [Adaptive stewardship of understanding: Artificial intelligence and intergenerational governance in mining](../publications/23d0a33b624f7d573ab8.md)

Priscilla P\. Nelson

Mining stewardship has traditionally focused on the governance of physical assets, operational performance, environmental impacts, and organizational decision\-making\. While these responsibilities remain essential, they assume that the understanding supporting stewardship is comparatively stable\. In reality, understanding continually evolves as new observations emerge, assumptions are revised, stakeholders change, institutions adapt, and stewardship extends across increasingly long temporal horizons\. Artificial intelligence further transforms this process by participating in how observations are integrated, interpretations are developed, assumptions are reinforced or challenged, and institutional knowledge is preserved and communicated\. Stewardship must therefore address not only what decisions are made, but also how understanding itself is created, maintained, questioned, and renewed\. This paper proposes adaptive stewardship as a framework for governing an evolving ecology of understanding throughout the mine life cycle and beyond closure\. The framework distinguishes understanding from observation, examines the lifecycle of assumptions, introduces the concepts of time windows of understanding and observation boundaries, and argues that governance must preserve the conditions under which understanding can continue to improve across generations\. Within this ecology, artificial intelligence is treated not as an autonomous decision\-maker but as an evolving participant whose value depends upon transparent governance that maintains visibility of assumptions, uncertainty, evidence, and human judgment\. The paper concludes that the long\-term objective of stewardship is not to preserve today&\#x27;s knowledge, but to preserve society&\#x27;s continuing capacity to develop better understanding as mining systems, environmental conditions, technologies, institutions, and societal expectations evolve\.

## [A corpus linguistics enhanced hybrid deep learning for semantic\-driven emotion detection on textual data](../publications/23d480b390767fbce109.md)

Noah N\. Alsager; Mohammad Mahzari; Haroon Nasser Alsager

Corpus linguistics offers a structured approach to assess huge set of texts \(corpora\) to uncover language patterns, structural relationships, and semantic interpretations\. Within text\-based emotion recognition \(TER\), corpus linguistics facilitates the identification of linguistic features that show underlying emotional expressions\. However, the existing machine learning\-based models often struggle to learn subtle semantic relationships, contextual relationships, and differences in emotional expression across textual content\. Recent advancements in deep learning have demonstrated excellent capabilities for contextual and relational representation learning, yet accurate and robust multi\-class emotional classification remains challenging\. Therefore, this study proposes a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Semantic\-driven Emotion Detection \(HDLF\-SED\) on Textual data, aiming to improve learning representation and the accurate separation of multi\-class emotional categories\. To achieve this, the model uses RoBERTa\-Large as a feature embedding technique to learn subtle linguistic patterns and contextual relationships to produce discriminative feature representations for further analysis\. The model employs hybrid learning by integrating a temporal convolutional network with a multi\-head attention mechanism to jointly capture sequential and local contextual patterns and selectively focus on emotion\-relevant features to perform accurate multi\-class emotion classification\. Furthermore, the RAdam optimization algorithm is used to facilitate more stable and effective optimization during model training and improve classification accuracy\. Experimental evaluation is carried out using two benchmark datasets across various performance measures; these results highlight that the proposed HDLF\-SED model demonstrates the potential of combining contextual embedding with hybrid learning for more accurate and reliable motion detection and performs multi\-class classification\.
