## [Subjektive Leistungsbewertung: Chancen, Verzerrungen und der Einfluss narzisstischer Führungskräfte auf die Mitarbeiterbeurteilung](../publications/23dd966b6cda93b2e0d0.md)

Miriam K\. Maske; Stefanie Neumeister; Matthias Sohn

Subjektive Leistungsbeurteilungen sind ein unverzichtbarer Bestandteil moderner Performance\-Management\-Systeme, da zentrale Leistungsdimensionen nicht vollständig objektiv messbar sind\. Die verhaltensorientierte Forschung zeigt jedoch, dass Leistungsurteile durch persönliche Wahrnehmungen und psychologische Bewertungsverzerrungen beeinflusst werden können\. Zwei Online\-Experimente verdeutlichen, dass narzisstische Mitarbeitende trotz identischer objektiver Leistung unterschiedlich bewertet werden, je nachdem, wie stark der Narzissmus der beurteilenden Führungskraft ausgeprägt ist\. Entscheidend ist dabei die wahrgenommene psychologische Nähe zwischen Führungskraft und Mitarbeitenden\. Für Unternehmen ergibt sich daraus die Notwendigkeit, subjektive Bewertungsprozesse kritisch zu reflektieren und mögliche Verzerrungen aktiv zu begrenzen, um faire und valide Leistungsbeurteilungen sicherzustellen\.

## [Child and adolescent mental health in South Tyrol, Italy: A narrative synthesis of the Corona and Psyche – South Tyrol \(COP\-S\) survey series, 2021–2025](../publications/23e9d4fa79e992d5fe44.md)

Verena Barbieri; Giuliano Piccoliori; Doris Hager von Strobele Prainsack; Christian Josef Wiedermann

Background: Five years after the onset of the COVID\-19 pandemic, mental health indicators in children and adolescents have not returned to pre\-pandemic levels\. This narrative synthesis of the Corona and Psyche – South Tyrol \(COP\-S\) study series, conducted in a bilingual Alpine region of Northern Italy, summarizes the course of youth mental health, its correlates, and prevention implications\. Methods: Findings from four cross\-sectional COP\-S survey waves between 2021 and 2025 were synthesized and contextualized by one external comparison with the neighboring Austrian Tyrol\. Waves covered children aged 7–10 years \(6–10 years in 2025; parental proxy\) and adolescents aged 11–19 \(proxy and self\-report\)\. Validated instruments assessed mental health outcomes—emotional and behavioral difficulties, anxiety, depressive symptoms, psychosomatic symptoms, quality of life, and eating\-disorder risk—and correlates including social support, resilience, health literacy, problematic Internet use, sleep, physical activity, school stress, family affluence and subjective financial strain\. Results: The gender gap was pronounced for anxiety, where higher scores in girls were largely independent of covariates\. The leading correlates shifted from pandemic\-related fears to school stress, problematic Internet use, poor sleep and subjective financial strain\. School\-language differences were not driven by home–school language mismatch\. Parental health literacy was associated with proxy reporting in younger children\. Perceived social support and resilience related to outcomes through parallel rather than sequential pathways\. Eating\-disorder risk was marked by widespread body dissatisfaction and a treatment gap, without difference in SCOFF screening between questionnaire languages\. Outcomes were broadly similar in South Tyrol and neighboring Austrian Tyrol\. Discussion: The mental health burden in South Tyrolean youth in 2025 reflects persistent everyday stressors rather than the acute pandemic\-related factors\. Prevention can combine school\-based reduction of academic stress, age\-appropriate digital\-media policies, sleep measures, and joint social\-support and resilience interventions\. Anxiety\-specific approaches for female adolescents, parental health\-literacy education and family\-level economic support may complement universal measures\.

## [Intuitionistic Fuzzy Multi\-Attribute Group Decision Making Using CoCoSo Technique](../publications/23f4caaa691c8847640a.md)

Mingyue Zhang; Dan Zeng; Wei Ji

The evaluation of the quality of integrating traditional Chinese culture into multicultural classroom teaching can help standardize pathways for cultural integration, mitigate cross\-cultural teaching conflicts, support the inheritance of Chinese cultural heritage and the cultivation of intercultural competence, improve the multicultural classroom evaluation system, and provide a foundation for enhancing teaching effectiveness and quality of culture\-based education\. The teaching quality evaluation in rural multicultural classrooms through Chinese traditional culture incorporation represents a significant MAGDM\. In this research, we propose a method termed Intuitionistic Fuzzy CoCoSo, grounded in the DSM \(IF\-DSM\-CoCoSo\), designed to efficiently address MAGDM tasks that involve IFSs\. Then, the IF\-DSM\-CoCoSo framework provides a robust scheme for assessing teaching quality in rural multicultural classrooms, incorporating traditional Chinese culture\. In addition, a numerical evaluation is performed to examine teaching quality and to confirm the validity of proposed model in practice\.

## [Perioperative nutrition\-related laboratory profiles predict outcomes after digestive procedures in patients with gastrointestinal cancer](../publications/23f5b142b8426146c741.md)

MengHui Zhang; Liangliang Hui; Jialing Zhang; Chengran Wang; Fan Xu; Guoquan Tao; Honggang Wang

Routine laboratory measurements may capture nutritional, inflammatory, and organ\-function vulnerability in patients with gastrointestinal cancer\. We developed nested logistic regression models using INSPIRE v1\.4\.2 and evaluated a portable model in MIMIC\-IV v3\.1\. The original INSPIRE cohort comprised 11,471 operations among 10,728 patients, with 893 deaths within 365 days\. Patients were allocated to development and held\-out test sets\. For 365\-day mortality, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\) was 0\.783 \(95% CI 0\.752–0\.811\) for clinical variables, 0\.843 \(95% CI 0\.820–0\.868\) after adding laboratory variables, and 0\.856 \(95% CI 0\.834–0\.879\) for the full perioperative model\. Patient\-level full\-pipeline bootstrap analysis yielded an optimism\-corrected AUROC of 0\.837\. External AUROC was 0\.676 \(95% CI 0\.663–0\.688\) for 365\-day mortality and 0\.724 \(95% CI 0\.692–0\.754\) for recorded hospital death after harmonizing CRP units\. Calibration drift was substantial, and hospital\-death discrimination was sensitive to laboratory timing\. Corrected operation\-linked risk tertiles showed graded mortality and lower albumin and hemoglobin levels in higher\-risk groups\. Perioperative nutrition\-related laboratory profiles provided additional discrimination for 365\-day mortality beyond clinical variables, although limited external performance and calibration drift warrant further validation before clinical use\.

## [Distopías fílmicas sobre inteligencia artificial: Reflexión e impacto emocional suscitado en universitarios](../publications/24000b1ad6fd4b57d747.md)

María Esther del Moral Pérez; Jonathan Castañeda Fernández; Nerea López‐Bouzas; M\. Carmen Bellver Moreno

Esta investigación, derivada del Proyecto ETIC\-IA, utiliza como catalizador de la reflexión crítica tres tecno\-distopías fílmicas \(orwelliana, kafkiana y huxleyana\), que plasman imaginarios sociales y preocupaciones contemporáneas sobre la vigilancia, deshumanización, control y tecnificación extrema de la vida cotidiana\. El objetivo es analizar cómo impactan emocionalmente estas narrativas en futuros educadores \(N = 425\), y cómo se relaciona su actitud hacia la IA con su preocupación o cambio de percepción sobre sus consecuencias, así como con la reflexión suscitada\. Los resultados evidencian que los universitarios usan la IA en tareas académicas, la consideran útil y muestran una actitud positiva\. Sin embargo, tras el visionado de tecno\-distopías se observa un cambio de percepción sobre la deshumanización atribuida a los algoritmos y la transferencia de responsabilidades a las máquinas\. Una actitud negativa hacia la IA se relaciona con mayor frustración, inquietud y miedo ante las consecuencias de su empoderamiento y el riesgo de la anulación humana\. Las mujeres manifiestan una mayor preocupación y declaran haber cambiado su percepción ante los dilemas presentados\. La tecno\-distopía orwelliana, donde se legitima la vigilancia extrema y la intimidad desaparece, les genera mayor inquietud\. Les preocupa que la IA despersonalice decisiones críticas y excluya consideraciones éticas\. En conclusión, se subraya el potencial pedagógico de estas narrativas distópicas para promover la reflexión crítica sobre cómo los sistemas inteligentes pueden reconfigurar –de manera opaca, coercitiva o seductora– la experiencia humana y el progreso social\.

## [From Science Fiction to Science Faction: Interrogating Posthuman Assemblage in Bollywood Science Fiction Film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya](../publications/2405bbc87a29db725ede.md)

Dilpreet Kour; Sadaf Shah

In an era marked by ever\-increasing integration of humans with artificial intelligence \(AI\), popular culture predominantly Bollywood, functions as a reflective canvas that shapes and mirrors society’s growing reliance on technology\. In this context, Bollywood Science fiction film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya emerges as a significant cultural text that portrays the intricacies of human\-AI relationship\. The study contextualizes film within the framework of Posthumanism\. The study draws from Posthumanist theorist, Stefan Herbrechter’s concept of “Science faction” along with Rosi Braidotti’s posthumanist philosophy, while incorporating the foundational concepts of film theorists, Rosie Thomas’ moral universe and Ranjani Mazumdar’s techno\-urbanism\. It provides a methodological bridge to examine shifting and evolving paradigms of human\-machine relationships within Indian cinema\. Employing close textual analysis, the paper argues that the film presents human\-AI interaction not as a distant fantasy but as an imminent “Science Factional” appraisal of a near\-future reality\. By examining a non Western film, the paper offers a localized departure from Western centric AI narratives\. It highlights that Bollywood not only reflects society’s technological anxieties but also offers a framework for understanding global technological evolution in a posthuman world, where coexistence of human and AI is mediated through cultural kinship\. As Bollywood significantly influence the societal narratives, the analysis of a non Western film contributes to the contemporary discussions about global cinematic portrayal of human\-machine relationships as well as Bollywood’s role in shaping these intertwined realities\. By blending scientific and fantastical elements, the study provides an ideal platform for exploring Bollywood’s engagement with Science faction and demonstrates how cinematic form interacts with theoretical frameworks, leading to a richer understanding of the evolving posthuman condition\.

## [Artificial Intelligence\-Driven Decision Business Management: A Conceptual Study of Innovation, Efficiency and Competitive Advantage](../publications/240c256f943fb740cc04.md)

Vinod Kumar Sahu; Siva Sai Prasanna Kumar Jittuga; Sanjana M; Sumit Kumar; Ashish Jha

Organizations increasingly face volatile markets, abundant data and pressure to decide quickly\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is widely presented as a way to meet these demands, yet the scholarly picture of how it affects management is spread across many sectors, methods and vocabularies\. This conceptual study synthesizes twenty recent sources on AI in business management and decision\-making in order to explain how AI is linked to innovation, operational efficiency and competitive advantage\. Using a structured narrative review, the paper identifies five recurring themes: the improvement of decision quality and speed, efficiency gains from automation and prediction, AI\-enabled innovation and new business models, the strategic alignment of AI with organizational goals, and the ethical and governance conditions that determine whether benefits last\. Building on these themes, the paper proposes an integrative framework in which AI capabilities influence decision processes, decision processes generate efficiency and innovation, and these outcomes support competitive advantage, with strategic alignment, human–AI collaboration, organizational readiness and responsible governance acting as conditioning factors\. Six propositions are advanced for later empirical testing\. The paper contributes a consolidated reading of a fragmented literature and offers practical guidance for managers, while acknowledging that its conclusions rest on the reviewed sources and require validation in future studies\.

## [Atypical chromoblastomycosis in a renal transplant recipient: Dermoscopic features and response to super\-bioavailable itraconazole](../publications/24116779c4e9114d4e75.md)

Shivangi Singh; Navya Pedapalli; Priyanka Arun Kowe; Prashant Ramteke; Gobinda Murmu

Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic subcutaneous mycosis caused by dematiaceous fungi, including Fonsecaea pedrosoi, Phialophora verrucosa, Fonsecaea compacta, and Cladophialophora carrionii\.It typically follows traumatic inoculation in tropical regions and predominantly affects immunocompetent individuals, with rare occurrence in immunosuppressed hosts, particularly solid organ transplant recipients\.\[1,2\]

## [Disentangling Propagation Effects from the Spectro\-Temporal Properties of Fast Radio Bursts](../publications/2422105d407577a6c828.md)

Aishwarya Kumar

Fast Radio Bursts \(FRBs\) are energetic radio\-frequency transients with no established progenitor model despite nearly two decades of observations\. Their observed spectro\-temporal properties provide insights into the emission mechanism but can be significantly modified by dispersion and scattering\. This thesis investigates how these two propagation effects alter the sub\-burst slope law derived within the Triggered Relativistic Dynamical Model \(TRDM\)\. This law describes an inverse relation between sub\-burst slope and duration, with a proportionality constant A characterizing the emission process\. We present a modified law incorporating the scattering timescale and residual dispersive delay, together with a methodology to recover these quantities alongside the intrinsic parameters\. We test our methodology using simulated FRBs generated within the TRDM using superradiance as the emission mechanism, with a range of scattering strengths and residual dispersion offsets introduced into the bursts\. The modified sub\-burst slope law approaches different limiting regimes depending on the observing frequency and the relative strength of the propagation effects\. At high frequencies, the TRDM slope law is recovered, whereas at low frequencies propagation effects dominate the relation\. Simulations recover the scattering timescale with high precision, while residual dispersion is less reliably recovered because of its degeneracy with A\. Applying our methodology to observations of FRB 20121102A yields a scattering timescale of \~2\.4 ms at 1 GHz when the 400\-800 MHz CHIME observation is included\. Excluding this measurement leaves the scattering timescale unconstrained at its lower bound\. These results demonstrate that broad frequency coverage is essential for separating intrinsic and extrinsic contributions, with high\-frequency observations constraining the intrinsic emission behavior and low\-frequency observations providing strong leverage on propagation effects\.

## [Digital Biofeedback–Based Nursing Program for Improving Physiological Regulation, Anxiety, Sleep Quality, and SelfManagement among Patients with Heart Failure](../publications/2425ced0abeabee1f339.md)

Nevin Adel Amer; Hanan Mohamed Safar; Iman Abd\-Elmoaty Mohamed; Rania Reafaat Abdelkader Atia; Bahaa Eldin Abdellatif Ali Ali; Reham AbdElhamed AbdElmawla Elsaid; Samah Zidan; Manal Ahmed Mohamed Ismail; Eman Ali Metwaly Badr; Yasmin Mohamed Ali

Background: Heart failure is a complex chronic condition characterized by impaired cardiovascular function and persistent physiological stress, often accompanied by anxiety, poor sleep quality, and difficulties in maintaining effective self\-management\. Digital biofeedback may provide patients with real\-time physiological information that supports relaxation, symptom awareness, behavioral regulation, and active participation in disease management\. Aim: To evaluate the effect of a digital biofeedbackbased nursing program on physiological regulation, anxiety, sleep quality, and self\-management among patients with heart failure\. Subjects and Methods: A quasi\-experimental one\-group pretest–posttest design was used\. A purposive sample of 100 adult patients diagnosed with heart failure was recruited from the cardiac and medical outpatient clinics of Sohag University Hospitals\. Data were collected using a structured patient assessment questionnaire, a physiological regulation assessment, the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale \(GAD\-7\), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index \(PSQI\), and a heart failure self\-management assessment scale\. The nursing program incorporated digital biofeedbackassisted breathing and relaxation exercises, physiological monitoring, symptom recognition, medication and dietary adherence, sleep\-management strategies, and individualized self\-management education\. The intervention was implemented through structured sessions with digital biofeedback Digital Biofeedback–Based Nursing Program for Improving Physiological Regulation, Anxiety, Sleep Quality, and Self\-Management among Patients with Heart Failure practice and follow\-up support\. Results: Following implementation of the program, patients demonstrated significant improvement in physiological regulation, with greater ability to recognize and control physiological responses\. Anxiety levels decreased significantly, while sleep quality improved\. A significant improvement was also observed in patients’ self\-management behaviors, including medication adherence, symptom monitoring, dietary and fluid management, physical activity, and appropriate responses to worsening symptoms\. Significant differences were observed between pre\- and post\-intervention measurements \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion: The Digital Biofeedback–Based Nursing Program was effective in improving physiological regulation and reducing anxiety while enhancing sleep quality and self\-management among patients with heart failure\. Recommendations: Digital biofeedback should be incorporated into nursing\-led heart failure management programs as a supportive strategy for physiological regulation, psychological well\-being, sleep improvement, and long\-term self\-management\.

## [Bipolar Disorder as Oscillatory Regime Instability](../publications/243b439913517237f4de.md)

Ari Ariel Marom

Energetic Switching, Affective Threshold Dynamics, and the Breakdown of Mood\-State Constraint within Informational Nosology Bipolar disorder is clinically defined by recurrent episodes of mania or hypomania and depression, with intervening periods of variable stability\. Existing accounts correctly emphasize circadian vulnerability, reward hypersensitivity, monoaminergic dysregulation, and kindling over successive episodes\. What they often leave under\-specified is the systems\-level architecture that makes a brain capable of crossing, locking into, and later exiting radically different affective operating regimes\. This monograph formalizes bipolar disorder within Informational Nosology as an oscillatory regime\-instability problem rather than as a simple excess or deficit of mood\. The core claim is that bipolar illness reflects failure of the constraints that normally keep affective state transitions bounded, reversible, and metabolically affordable\. Under converging circadian, sleep, energetic, and stress loads, the system becomes prone to threshold crossings into high\-gain expansive regimes and low\-gain depleted regimes\. Mania is read as a high\-throughput, low\-inhibition operating mode with compressed valuation and accelerated commitment; depression as a protective or exhausted low\-throughput mode with narrowed affordance and elevated withdrawal\. The disease process is therefore not only episodic content, but progressive alteration of switching thresholds, recovery capacity, and inter\-episode stability\. The account is non\-substitutive\. It does not displace lithium\-response biology, circadian medicine, or clinical staging\. It relocates them within one dynamical language used across the Nosology corpus: energetic headroom, threshold mechanics, noise, precision, and the maintenance of operational constraint\. Bipolar disorder is demarcated from schizophrenia by the preservation of a different relation between uncertainty and rigid crystallization, from autism by its acquired episodic switching architecture, and from unipolar depression by the bipolar capacity for high\-gain expansive departure\. Empirical signatures and falsification criteria are stated explicitly\. Highlights: Bipolar disorder is formalized as oscillatory regime instability, not merely as alternating excess and deficit of mood\. Core mechanism: failure of constraints that keep affective transitions bounded, reversible, and metabolically affordable\. Mania and depression reinterpreted as distinct operating regimes — high\-gain expansive versus low\-throughput depleted — with progressive threshold and recovery effects\. Clear demarcation from schizophrenia, autism, unipolar depression, and the gradual neurodegenerative portals\. Non\-displacement stance: circadian, pharmacological, and staging evidence remain intact; the contribution is a unifying dynamical architecture\. Keywords: bipolar disorder; mania; depression; circadian rhythms; energetic switching; threshold dynamics; mood instability; informational nosology; systems neuroscience; kindling

## [An IoT digital twin framework for smart waste and energy management optimazation in Maiduguri](../publications/2441d37d4ef642cb86b8.md)

Aishatu Ibrahim Birma; Abdulmuminu Shamsudeen; Raihanatu Mohammed Hamid

The rapid pace of urban development in cities like Maiduguri, Nigeria, brings significant operational challenges to municipal waste collection and energy distribution\. This study presents a six\-layer Digital Twin \(DT\) architectural framework designed for resource\-constrained urban environments that integrates resilient Internet of Things \(IoT\) sensing, machine learning \(ML\) forecasting, and agent\-based co\-simulation\. During a six\-month pilot deployment, data was obtained from 10 smart waste bins with ultrasonic sensors, servo actuators, and GSM modules, and 3 distribution\-node energy meters\. To predict bin fill levels and energy demand without future information data leakage, time\-series forecasting models including Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) networks, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using 5\-fold rolling\-origin cross\-validation\. The LSTM model gave the best predictive accuracy \(R²=0\.92, RMSE = 4\.8%\)\. The forecasted horizons were fed into an AnyLogic agent\-based simulation with Ant Colony Optimisation \(ACO\) for dynamic collection vehicle routing\. Across 30 stochastic simulation runs, the proposed DT framework achieved an 18\.2% pm 1\.4% reduction in total collection distance \(and 15\.4% pm 1\.1% reduction in fuel consumption\), a 41\.8% pm 3\.1% reduction in potential waste overflow events, a 10\.3% pm 0\.8% reduction in fleet CO₂ emissions, and an 11\.6% pm 1\.1% improvement in peak load\-balancing efficiency relative to the current static baseline\. The architecture uses local buffering in EEPROM to ensure data continuity even when network connectivity is intermittent\. The results provide a proof\-of\-concept for moving from reactive municipal scheduling to data\-driven decision making in infrastructural fragile environments\.

## [Conformal Prediction for Distribution\-Free Uncertainty in Machine Learning Models](../publications/24421cb064cfcc2f3352.md)

Mini T\. V

A point prediction says nothing about how far it might be wrong\. Conformal prediction repairs that with very little machinery: hold out some labelled data, score how badly the model misses on it, and widen each new prediction by a quantile of those scores\. The resulting set contains the true label with a chosen probability, for any model and any data distribution, provided the data are exchangeable\. This review reads the literature with one question in mind, namely what exactly is promised and under which assumption\. We go through the split recipe and the adaptive scores built for regression and classification, then the limits of the guarantee, which is marginal and not per individual\. Most of the article concerns what happens when exchangeability fails: covariate and label shift, drifting streams, time series\. We close with risk control, counterfactual inference and generative language models, and with a short list of checks a practitioner should run before trusting a reported coverage figure\. No new experiment is reported; every number quoted is a theoretical bound taken from the cited source\.

## [The ipsilesional DTI\-ALPS index provides modest incremental prognostic value beyond clinical models for 90\-day outcome in patients with acute MCA occlusion treated with intravenous thrombolysis: a prospective exploratory cohort study](../publications/24447444476f4dffd1b7.md)

Lu Shen; Bo Ye; Jingye Lu; Chengying Yin; Huiqun Lu; Xiaojie Xu; Beijia Qin; Caixia Xu; Peng Yu

Background and purpose Impaired perivascular fluid dynamics may contribute to secondary brain injury after acute ischemic stroke, yet its prognostic relevance remains uncertain\. We investigated whether the Diffusion Tensor Image Analysis along the Perivascular Space \(ALPS\) index—a quantitative MRI marker of perivascular fluid dynamics—provides incremental predictive value for long\-term functional outcomes in patients with acute middle cerebral artery occlusion \(MCAO\) treated with intravenous thrombolysis\. Methods In this prospective observational cohort study, 128 patients underwent multimodal brain MRI within 24 h of admission, and the ALPS index was calculated in the hemisphere ipsilateral to the occlusion \(ipsilesional ALPS\)\. Favorable outcome at 90 days was defined as modified Rankin Scale \(mRS\) 0–2\. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, with covariates \(admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale \[NIHSS\] score, LDL cholesterol, and smoking status\) prespecified on clinical grounds rather than selected by univariate screening\. Incremental discriminative value was assessed by comparing nested models using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis and the likelihood\-ratio test \(LRT\), which is preferable to DeLong’s test for nested models\. Calibration \(Hosmer–Lemeshow test, Nagelkerke R 2 \) and internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples \(optimism\-corrected AUC\) were performed\. Interpretation Lower admission NIHSS score \[adjusted odds ratio \(aOR\) per 1\-point increase: 0\.890, 95% CI: 0\.813–0\.976; p = 0\.013\] and lower LDL cholesterol \(aOR per 1 mmol/L: 0\.660, 95% CI: 0\.472–0\.923; p = 0\.015\) were independently associated with favorable outcome, whereas the ipsilesional ALPS index showed a directionally consistent, non\-significant association \(aOR per 0\.1\-unit increase: 1\.525, 95% CI: 0\.948–2\.454; p = 0\.082\)\. Adding the ALPS index to a base model containing NIHSS and LDL yielded a modest but significant improvement in discrimination \(AUC 0\.681 to 0\.699; ΔAUC = 0\.018; LRT p = 0\.042\); calibration was adequate \(Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0\.31 and 0\.28\), and the gain persisted after bootstrap optimism correction \(ΔAUC = 0\.013\)\. Conclusion In this exploratory cohort, the ipsilesional ALPS index showed a consistent directional association with 90\-day functional outcome and provided a modest but significant incremental improvement in discrimination beyond NIHSS and LDL cholesterol; the magnitude of this gain is small and requires external validation\.

## [Estimating bilateral hand kinetics from upper\-limb kinematics in sprint front crawl: a subject\-wise validation of an artificial neural network](../publications/2458e72b0d56d35d8549.md)

Tianyi Gao; Shang Qi; Jiawen Li; Dongxiang Huang; Kaiqi Zheng; 李海侠; Jie Gao

Objective Hand force contributes substantially to front crawl performance, but measuring it requires hand\-worn hardware\. We tested whether an artificial neural network driven only by three\-dimensional upper\-limb kinematics can reconstruct bilateral hand kinetics recorded by a hand\-force device, and at which level of the signal \(waveform, discrete descriptors, between\-swimmer and inter\-limb differences\) the estimates agree\. Methods Twenty\-four male competitive swimmers performed maximal 50\-m front crawl without breathing while wearing eo SwimBETTER handsets; 14 upper\-body markers were tracked by underwater motion capture at 100 Hz\. For each swimmer, the underwater phase \(fingertip entry to exit\) of each hand was analysed\. A laterally mirrored multilayer perceptron using 197 trunk\-frame features estimated six targets per hand under subject\-wise six\-fold cross\-validation, with architecture, regularisation and smoothing selected inside each fold\. It was compared with four alternative learned models and two baselines \(a scalar group\-mean null model and a phase\-conditioned mean\-waveform template\), and uncertainty was estimated with participant\-cluster bootstraps\. Results For resultant force, root\-mean\-square error was 24\.5 ± 6\.1 N \(left\) and 23\.3 ± 9\.9 N \(right\), per\-window correlations were 0\.85 and 0\.84, and ICC\(A,1\) was 0\.70 and 0\.64\. The network was comparable to gradient boosting and coordinate\-only models but was not more accurate than the template \(template RMSE 21\.8 and 21\.2 N; left\-hand difference 2\.7 N, 95% CI 0\.9–4\.5\)\. Between\-swimmer correlations of measured and estimated peak force, impulse and mean force ranged from −0\.36 to 0\.27, and the estimated inter\-limb symmetry index did not agree with the measured one \(r −0\.23 to −0\.10; the dominant side was matched in 50%–58% of swimmers\)\. Left\-hand peak force was underestimated by 32\.6 N, and the absolute error in time to peak averaged 12%–13% of the underwater phase\. Modelling both hands in every window, a broader definition that includes each hand’s recovery and entry, inflated apparent accuracy \(left RMSE 21\.6 N, r 0\.89\)\. Conclusion In a device\-on protocol, kinematics\-driven estimation recovered the group\-typical force–time pattern but added little to a phase template and did not resolve differences between swimmers or between limbs\. It cannot yet replace hand\-force measurement for individual assessment\.

## [A hybrid reinforcement learning and Harris Hawks Optimization framework for multi\-objective resource management in IIoT](../publications/2459275db699ce7d955a.md)

Suresh Dara; Mourad Elloumi; Mohan Allam; Visalakshi Annepu; VenkataSeshaiah Banka; Ezzeddine Touti

The Industrial Internet of Things \(IIoT\) is revolutionizing industrial processes by interconnecting sensors, machines, and computing resources to enable intelligent automation, real\-time monitoring, and predictive maintenance\. Despite its potential, efficient allocation and management of resources in IIoT networks remain a significant challenge due to the dynamic, heterogeneous, and large\-scale nature of industrial environments\. Traditional static or heuristic resource allocation methods often fail to satisfy conflicting objectives such as minimizing latency, maximizing throughput, ensuring energy efficiency, and maintaining system reliability\. To address these challenges, this paper presents the design and development of an AI\-based multi\-objective resource management system for IIoT systems\. The system integrates reinforcement learning \(RL\) for adaptive, real\-time decision\-making with Harris Hawks Optimization \(HHO\) for multi\-objective optimization, balancing competing performance metrics across sensing, communication, computing, and control layers\. The RL agent predicts system states and dynamically adjusts resource allocation, while HHO fine\-tunes the solutions to achieve optimal performance under multiple constraints\. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms conventional static and heuristic approaches, achieving higher efficiency, faster adaptability, and improved scalability\. By intelligently managing resources and optimizing system behavior, this system enhances overall operational reliability and Quality\-of\-Service in IIoT networks\. The results indicate that combining AI\-driven decision\-making with advanced nature\-inspired optimization provides a robust and efficient solution for next\-generation industrial applications, paving the way for more intelligent, resilient, and resource\-efficient IIoT systems\.

## [Analyse multivariée des signatures spatiales et différenciation des profils urbains et environnementaux des six arrondissements d&\#x27;Antananarivo Renivohitra](../publications/2486b60ec9f45642ad1f.md)

RAKOTOARIVELO José Alain Pachou; TOVONIRINA Mamiharizo Jackie; Rakotoson Andriatiana Tolontsoa

Cette étude analyse les signatures spatiales et la différenciation des profils urbains et environnementaux des six arrondissements d’Antananarivo Renivohitra à partir d’une approche multivariée intégrant topographie, bâti, réseau routier, végétation et hydrographie\. L’analyse en composantes principales montre que les deux premiers axes expliquent 63,8 % de la variance totale, avec 43,7 % pour PC1 et 20,1 % pour PC2, tandis que les trois premiers axes atteignent 80,2 %\. L’analyse factorielle multiple confirme cette structuration, avec 42,9 % de variance expliquée par MFA1 et 19,3 % par MFA2\. Les corrélations de Spearman révèlent une forte association entre le bâti et le réseau routier \(ρ = 0,74\), alors que la proximité hydrographique est négativement corrélée au réseau routier \(ρ = –0,42\) et à la végétation \(ρ = –0,35\)\. Les profils standardisés mettent en évidence un 1er arrondissement fortement urbanisé, tandis que le 6e se distingue par une forte influence hydrographique\. Les distances euclidiennes confirment cette différenciation, avec une proximité minimale entre les 3e et 5e arrondissements \(2,00\) et un contraste maximal entre les 3e et 6e \(4,46\)\. Ces résultats révèlent une organisation territoriale fondée sur des gradients urbains, topographiques et environnementaux complémentaires\.

## [Suriye Devrimi Edebiyatında Muâraza Şiirleri](../publications/24886aa3ff4913e728be.md)

Ahmet Onur

Suriye devrimi olaylarına şiirde canlı bir hareket eşlik etti\. Şairlerin çoğu devrime katılmış veya devrimin sesini susturmak için her türlü yolu kullanan rejimin suçları nedeniyle devrimin trajedilerini yaşamıştı\. Muâraza \(nazîre\), bu şiirin bir biçimiydi; Suriye devrimi edebiyatında hem eski hem de modern edebiyattan şiirlere birçok muâraza vardır\. Bu çalışma, devrimci şiirin genel olarak Arap şiirine nasıl yaklaştığını anlamak için bu muârazaları ele almayı ve incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Çalışmanın önemi, geçen yılın sonlarında zafer kazanan Suriye devriminin şairlerinin sunduğu ve yaklaşık on dört yıl süren çağdaş bir deneyimi oluşturan yaratıcı üretimin öneminden kaynaklanmaktadır\. Bu süre zarfında, sanatsal nitelik açısından zengin bir yaratıcılık ortaya çıkmıştır ve bilimsel çalışmalarda ortaya çıkarılıp dikkate alınmalıdır\. Çalışma, devrimin birçok şairinin dikkatini çeken olguyu, çok sayıda örneğini analiz ederek tanımlamak için betimleyici ve analitik yaklaşıma dayanmıştır\. Çalışma, muâraza şiirlerinde, çoğu çağdaş deneyimin gerçekliğine göre önceki metni zenginleştiren yeni bir ses oluşturan çeşitli imgeler ortaya koymuştur\. Ayrıca, önceki metinle diyaloğa dayanan veya devrimden ilham alarak onu yaratıcı bir şekilde tamamlamaya çalışan muârazalar da vardı\. Çoğu muâraza şiirleri, ölçü, uyak ve asonansla temsil edilen biçimsel muâraza unsurlarını korurken, bazı muâraza şiirleri bunlardan uzaklaşmıştır\.

## [Differences in income\-related health inequalities in Brazil and the USA: a comparative cross\-sectional study](../publications/24a3b0c4bffe03fea0da.md)

Stefano Zapperi; José S\. Andrade; Humberto A\. Carmona; Antonio S\. Lima Neto; Caterina A\. M\. La Porta

Introduction Health inequality is a persistent, policy\-relevant problem shaped by multiple socioeconomic factors, among which income and healthcare policy are especially prominent and often vary substantially between countries\. The goal of the present study is to quantify the relationship between income and health in two countries with different healthcare systems, Brazil and the USA\. Methods We compared health conditions in relation to income in Brazil and the USA through cross\-sectional, nationally representative, household\-based surveys using data from the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde \(PNS\) for Brazil and the Panel Study of Income Dynamics \(PSID\) for the USA collected in 2019\. We used survey\-weighted logistic regression with cluster\-robust standard errors, adjusted for urban/rural residence, sex, education, and age\. Results Both countries showed income\-related health inequality, with lower\-income groups generally reporting worse self\-rated health\. A formal test of the country\-by\-income interaction showed a significantly steeper income gradient in the USA than in Brazil for diabetes and obesity and a significant reversal in the direction of the association for psychiatric conditions, with higher income associated with higher prevalence in Brazil but lower prevalence in the USA\. No significant cross\-country difference was found for hypertension, self\-rated health, or cancer diagnosis\. Geographically, a north\-south divide in inequality is apparent in Brazil, while income disparities are less uniform in the USA\. States with a larger share of low\-income people experience worse health conditions in the USA, while this effect is less visible in Brazil\. Discussion Taken together, income\-related health inequality is more pronounced in the USA than in Brazil for several, though not all, of the conditions examined\. This pattern may be associated with differences in healthcare systems and lifestyles between the two countries, although the cross\-sectional design does not permit causal inference\.

## [Medication\-related knowledge and behavior profiles are generally favorable, but counseling needs remain among pregnant and postpartum women in Taiyuan, China: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/24a548ed56333379346f.md)

Chaolong Zhang; 何荧居; Yuanyuan Yang; Li Zhang; Wenfei Zhang; Liuye Yang; Mengyao Ma

Objective To characterize medication\-related Knowledge\-Attitude\-Practice \(KAP\) risk profiles, pregnancy\- and lactation\-specific medication familiarity, and demographic correlates among pregnant and postpartum women in Taiyuan, China\. Methods We conducted a hospital\-based cross\-sectional survey at Taiyuan Taihang Hospital from July to October 2024 using convenience sampling and an adapted medication\-related KAP questionnaire\. Higher knowledge\-, attitude\-, and behavior\-risk scores indicated less favorable profiles, whereas higher familiarity scores indicated greater self\-rated familiarity\. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s α\. Associations were examined using Pearson correlations, Welch’s analysis of variance with Games\-Howell post hoc tests, and multivariable ordinary least\-squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors\. Results Of 500 returned questionnaires, 497 were analyzed\. Cronbach’s α ranged from 0\.808 to 0\.957\. Mean knowledge\-risk and behavior\-risk scores were 59\.78 ± 18\.99 and 57\.22 ± 11\.29, respectively, both within the prespecified good category; the mean attitude\-risk score was 37\.34 ± 7\.94, within the pass category\. For attitude risk, 59\.0% were classified as pass, 16\.1% as fail, and 24\.9% as good or excellent\. Knowledge risk was inversely correlated with attitude risk \( r = −0\.258\) and positively correlated with behavior risk \( r = 0\.275\), while attitude risk was weakly positively correlated with behavior risk \( r = 0\.118; all p ≤ 0\.009\)\. In the adjusted behavior\-risk model, higher scores were observed among participants aged 35–49 years and those with other insurance or self\-payment\. The overall adjusted association between monthly income and behavior risk was not statistically significant \(Wald p = 0\.098\); an isolated contrast between the 4,000–6,000\-yuan and below\-2,000\-yuan groups reached nominal statistical significance and was treated as exploratory\. Familiarity scores across five pregnancy\- and lactation\-specific topics ranged from 2\.46 to 2\.60 on a five\-point scale\. Conclusion Favorable knowledge\- and behavior\-risk profiles coexisted with less favorable attitude\-risk classifications and limited topic\-specific familiarity\. Broad medication\-safety counseling should be integrated into antenatal and postpartum care, with proactive medication review considered for women aged 35–49 years, those with other insurance or self\-payment, and those with complex medication needs\. The income finding should be regarded as exploratory\. Multicenter prospective studies are needed to assess generalizability and evaluate this service approach\.

## [Statistical analysis of Hoek\-Brown shear strength properties for single and multiple intact rock units](../publications/24a9bf214676cbc84155.md)

Esteban Hormazabal; Carlos Carranza\-Torres

In the practice of geotechnical mining, the shear strength of intact rock is typically characterized using the Hoek\-Brown failure criterion\. The presence of veinlets, micro\-defects and/or a stockwork texture of tested rock specimens, a common feature of mineralized rock, leads to variability of results from strength testing, resulting in the need to carry out regression analysis of the test results to find a best fit Hoek\-Brown failure curve\. This paper presents a way of accounting uniaxial compression tests separately from triaxial tests, so to decrease the biasing towards one type of testing in particular\. This alternative form of doing the regression analysis may be applicable when the quality of uniaxial compression tests is known to be of similar good quality as triaxial tests, as could be the case in some mining projects\. In the proposed methodology, a measure of the quality of the fit of the Hoek\-Brown failure curve is obtained by computation and interpretation of a correlation factor\. For cases in which several intact rock units are being characterized, a global correlation factor for all geotechnical units considered together is proposed\. To further quantify the variability of results obtained from laboratory testing, a probability analysis of the Hoek\-Brown properties is also presented\.

## [Spatiotemporal training‐free LiDAR denoising and hybrid pedestrian detection on airport aprons: Focus on low‐speed and stationary targets](../publications/24c1977b50a3bdf47abc.md)

Ihn\-Sik Weon; Yoosoo Jang; Beomchan Park

Abstract LiDAR sensors in apron environments enable detailed monitoring of aircraft, vehicles, and pedestrians, but their clouds points often contain irregular noise from reflections, clutter, and dynamic interference\. This study proposes the density and temporally aware filter \(DTF‐Filter\), which combines local density‐adaptive thresholding with temporal consistency across consecutive frames\. A multi‐stage pedestrian recognition pipeline integrates adaptive ground segmentation, density‐based clustering, and a hybrid classifier of traditional machine learning and a lightweight deep learning model\. On real‐world apron data \(15 000 frames\) and KITTI, DTF‐Filter achieves a mean outlier reduction of 78\.0% ± 4\.2% \(max: 95\.2%\) versus 48\.3% ± 6\.1% for statistical outlier removal \(SOR\) \( p &lt; 0\.001\) and improves the pedestrian detection ‐score from 0\.891 ± 0\.023 to 0\.952 ± 0\.012 \( p &lt; 0\.001\), with consistent performance across weather conditions \(clear: 0\.961 ± 0\.009, fog: 0\.943 ± 0\.015, rain: 0\.937 ± 0\.018\)\. The method provides a computationally efficient \(11 ± 1\.2 ms/frame on CPU\), training‐free solution for real‐time LiDAR perception of stationary and low‐speed targets in safety‐critical apron environments, intended to complement higher velocity perception modules\.

## [Dual\-Release Gastro\-Resistant Platforms Using Tablet\-in\-Tablet Drug Delivery Systems: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/24c1e03970cbae45558c.md)

D\. Rajesh; M\. Muthukumaran; Abu Thahir; P\. Senthil; L\. Tharini

Oral drug delivery systems remain the most widely used pharmaceutical dosage forms due to their convenience, cost\-effectiveness, and high patient compliance\. However, conventional oral formulations often fail to provide sitespecific drug delivery and controlled drug release required for optimal therapeutic outcomes\. Tablet\-in\-tablet \(TNT\) drug delivery systems have emerged as an innovative strategy that enables sequential, delayed, or dual drug release within a single dosage form\. These systems incorporate an inner core tablet surrounded by an outer tablet layer, allowing the delivery of multiple drugs or release phases\. In particular, dual\-release gastro\-resistant platforms have gained significant attention because they protect acid\-labile drugs from degradation in the gastric environment while ensuring targeted drug release in the intestinal region\. The use of pH\-dependent enteric polymers enables selective drug release in the gastrointestinal tract\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of tablet\-in\-tablet technology, focusing on the design principles, formulation approaches, manufacturing techniques, and drug release mechanisms involved in dual\-release gastro\-resistant platforms\. The review also discusses commonly used polymers, evaluation parameters, advantages, limitations, and pharmaceutical applications of TNT systems\. Furthermore, recent technological advances including 3D printing, smart polymers, and nanotechnology\-based strategies are highlighted\. The future potential of tablet\-in\-tablet drug delivery systems in developing advanced oral dosage forms and personalized medicine is also explored\.

## [Recognising University Students with Criminal Justice Experience](../publications/24c96a9ddfecb61eb1ea.md)

Helena Gosling; Sarah Maclennan

Exploring how students with criminal justice experience access higher education, experience university life, and navigate barriers while building support, this book offers rare insight into an often\-overlooked dimension of widening participation, equity and justice in UK universities\. Drawing on existing literature, empirical evidence and an analysis of regulatory tools, this book explores how students with criminal justice experience are often positioned within universities and how this framing can shape their engagement with higher education\. It presents a complex and layered account that recognises the intersection of external social pressures, sector\-wide priorities, institutional dynamics, and everyday interactions and invites readers to reflect critically on what they know, what they assume and how they might work to disrupt the status quo\. This must\-read text raises a series of fundamental questions about who the sector recognises as worthy recipients of initiatives to improve access and participation in higher education, as well as how it can modernise attempts to better serve its diverse, global community\. It offers practical pathways for change, making it especially valuable to universities, regulators, and practitioners seeking to embed justice\-conscious support within everyday higher education practices\.

## [Springbok Optimization Algorithm: A Nature\-inspired Metaheuristic for Global Optimization and Engineering Design Problems](../publications/24d04df95b4a1cbaab9e.md)

Zeinab Montazeri; Mohammad Dehghani; Raed Abu Zitar; Omar Almomani; Kei Eguchi

Metaheuristic algorithms are used in optimization problems due to their ability to solve very complex problems; however, striking the right balance between exploration and exploitation remains a significant challenge\.In this study, the Springbok Optimization Algorithm \(SOA\) is introduced as a swarm\-based method that is inspired by the Springbok spatial structure switching between aggregation and dispersion and adjusting the position relative to the nearby members of the group\.In SOA, the dispersion behavior is modeled to increase the diversity and coverage of the search space in the exploration phase, while the use of local promising members to refine suitable solutions constitutes the exploitation phase\.The performance of SOA is evaluated using 10 fixed\-dimensional multimodal test functions, including F1\-F10, and four engineering design problems including tension/compression spring design, welded beam design problem, speed reducer design problem, and pressure vessel design problem\.The performance of SOA is compared with 9 metaheuristic algorithms, and the results are analyzed with the mean, best, worst, std, median, and rank indices\.The results show that SOA achieves the first\-best optimizer rank in all 10 benchmark functions and provides 100% successful and competitive performance\.Also, SOA has provided 100% successful performance in all four engineering design problems by providing more optimal solutions than the compared algorithms\.The quantitative and qualitative analysis of the results, along with boxplots and convergence curves, shows the appropriate and stable quality and stability of the solutions obtained by SOA\.The findings of this study indicate that SOA, with its high ability to balance exploration and exploitation, is an effective and powerful optimizer for a wide range of optimization problems in science and real\-world applications\.

## [Perceived AI Anthropomorphism and Brand Loyalty in Generative AI Services: The Roles of Confirmation, Brand Trust, Satisfaction, and Continuance Intention](../publications/24d50725c83b59cc4039.md)

Gamze EREN; Erkan Gülter; Muhammed Fatih Cevher

Generative artificial intelligence services combine functional performance with humanlike interaction, yet it remains unclear whether perceived humanlikeness contributes directly to post\-use satisfaction or is associated primarily with more proximal performance and relational appraisals\. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, anthropomorphism theory and the Computers Are Social Actors perspective, the Expectation\-Confirmation Model, and consumer–brand relationship research, this study examines perceived AI anthropomorphism \(PAIA\), confirmation, brand trust, satisfaction, continuance intention, and brand loyalty\. Survey data were obtained from 555 ChatGPT users in Türkiye and analyzed using PLS\-SEM\. PAIA was strongly associated with confirmation \(β = 0\.624\) and brand trust \(β = 0\.578\), whereas its direct association with satisfaction was small \(β = 0\.081\)\. Confirmation and brand trust were positively associated with satisfaction \(β = 0\.581 and β = 0\.306\), satisfaction was strongly associated with continuance intention \(β = 0\.705\), and brand trust, satisfaction, and continuance intention were each positively associated with brand loyalty\. Exploratory factor analysis, HTMT diagnostics, and confirmatory comparisons of alternative measurement structures showed substantial overlap between confirmation and satisfaction\. The six\-construct model fit better than the more parsimonious alternatives examined, but conclusions that depend on separating these two constructs are treated as tentative\. Overall, PAIA was strongly associated with post\-use and relational appraisals, but whether its association with satisfaction runs mainly through confirmation could not be established with confidence\. Because the design is cross\-sectional, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects\.

## [CoLU: Confidence\-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models](../publications/24d75543d70d0c11ac50.md)

Jingkai Guo; Ziyi Zhao; Chaitali Chakrabarti; Deliang Fan

Large language model \(LLM\) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch\. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine\-tuning, while FOM\-UL explores selective layer updates\. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge\. This trade\-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss\. In this work, we propose Confidence\-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning \(CoLU\), which combines a novel confidence\-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning\. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening \(BLS\), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting\-retention \(NFR\) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs\. BLS pre\-selects top\-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis\. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60\.2\-79\.7% with almost the same performance\. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA\-based FOM\-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings\. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods\. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date\. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77\.4% to 79\.5% lower than full\-model unlearning\.

## [Türkiye Sermaye Piyasası Alt Sektörlerinde Piyasa Etkinsizliğinin Değerlendirilmesi: AMIM Perspektifi](../publications/24fc02a692ffe58be2b0.md)

Emrah Öget

Bu çalışmanın amacı, Borsa İstanbul’da yer alan seçilmiş 10 alt sektörün piyasa etkinliğini, krizler bağlamında 1997\-2025 dönemi için AMIM \(Adjusted Market Inefficiency Magnitude\) ölçütü ile analiz etmektir\. Çalışmada öncelikle kriz dönemleri belirlenmiş, ardından sektörlerin etkinsizlik düzeyleri kriz ve toparlanma süreçleri bağlamında değerlendirilmiştir\. Bulgular, sektörlerin piyasa etkinliklerinin zaman içinde değişkenlik gösterdiğini ve piyasanın tamamen etkin veya etkinsiz bir yapıda olmadığını ortaya koymaktadır\. Kriz dönemlerinde daha sık etkinlik gözlemlenen sektörlerin İletişim, Metal Ana, Elektrik, Ticaret ve Ulaştırma olduğu; kriz dışı dönemlerde ise İletişim, Ticaret ve Ulaştırma sektörlerinin etkinliğini görece istikrarlı biçimde koruduğu tespit edilmiştir\. 2024 sonrası dönemde, Bankacılık sektörünün etkinsizliği tarihsel olarak en yüksek seviyeye çıkmıştır\. Bu durum sıkı para politikası, düzenleyici kısıtlamalar, düşük likidite ve artan politika belirsizliğiyle açıklanabilmektedir\. Bulgular genel olarak, piyasa etkinliğinin ekonomik koşullar, bilgi akış hızı ve yatırımcı davranışlarına bağlı olarak değişkenlik gösterdiğini ve Adaptif Piyasalar Hipotezi ile tutarlı dinamik bir yapı sergilediğini ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Case Report: Intentional massive melatonin ingestion \(450 mg\) in an adolescent female](../publications/250a4f958c61f2c831f9.md)

Sepehr Miran; Bahar Amiri; Peyman Astaraki; Arian Karimi Rouzbahani

Over\-the\-counter \(OTC\) melatonin is widely perceived as benign, yet its unregulated, high\-dose formulations create an accessible means of self\-harm for adolescents, and reports of intentional overdose have risen alongside a well\-documented surge in pediatric exposures\. We report a 16\-year\-old female who intentionally ingested 450 mg of melatonin \(90 × 5 mg tablets\), a 90\-fold supratherapeutic dose, and synthesize this case against the published literature on melatonin overdose, suicidality, and toxicokinetics\. She presented 2\.5 h post\-ingestion with marked somnolence \(Glasgow Coma Scale 13/15\) and heart rate of 62 beats/min\. Venous blood gas showed a mild, respiratory\-compensated metabolic acidosis \(pH 7\.34, HCO3 15\.6 mmol/L\), with mild hyponatremia and stress leukocytosis\. Hepatic, renal, and coagulation studies and a 12\-lead electrocardiogram were normal, and a comprehensive toxicology screen was negative, consistent with an isolated exposure \(Poison Severity Score Grade 1, Minor\)\. She was medically cleared within 14\.5 h of ingestion but, given persistent suicidal ideation on psychiatric evaluation, was transferred to inpatient psychiatric care at 20\.5 h post\-ingestion\. This case, together with a review of published case reports, cohort data, and toxicokinetic evidence, indicates that massive isolated melatonin ingestion typically produces self\-limited sedation, consistent with saturable hepatic CYP1A2\-mediated clearance, alongside mild, transient metabolic derangement without organ injury\. Population\-level and case\-level evidence converge, however, on a critical message for clinicians: low physiological toxicity does not indicate low psychiatric risk, and every adolescent presenting after intentional OTC chronobiotic ingestion warrants formal psychiatric evaluation regardless of how benign the medical course appears\.

## [Advanced drug delivery and PBPK modelling as translational tools for precision therapies in juvenile idiopathic arthritis](../publications/250b2431e2f46ec85c2e.md)

Marina Cuquerella\-Gilabert; Cristina Martín‐Sabroso; Javier Zarzoso\-Foj; Juan Aparicio\-Blanco; Alejandro Balsa; Ana Isabel Torres‐Suárez; Victor Mangas Sanjuan; Carlos Rodríguez‐Nogales

Patients with persistent forms of juvenile idiopathic arthritis \(JIA\) often report limited therapeutic benefit from currently available treatments\. Despite substantial advances in the management of rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) and related disorders over recent decades, treatment strategies for JIA remain insufficiently defined\. The application of advanced drug delivery systems holds promise in addressing these limitations by enabling controlled and sustained drug release over extended periods\. Other integrative approaches such as novel physiologically based pharmacokinetic \(PBPK\) modelling have demonstrated to be a critical tool in optimizing pharmacotherapy in pediatric populations, particularly by improving dose selection and predicting drug disposition\. This review summarizes current disease\-modifying antirheumatic drugs \(DMARDs\) for JIA management and critically examines the current, still largely prospective, integration of emerging drug delivery systems with PBPK modelling, highlighting existing translational examples alongside key opportunities and challenges for precision therapies in this field\.

## [Drug–Drug Interactions vs\. Therapeutic Combinations in Patients with Congestive Heart Failure and Diabetes: An Ambispective Real‐World Study](../publications/250d677a09d7a78c29ff.md)

Navakanth Raju Ramayanam; Bhawarlal Kavitha; Chitthi Babu Prathisha; Dharmaraj Samundeeswary; Bharath Kumar Mamilla Mugaiahgari; Bayapa Reddy Narapureddy; Sarad Pawar Naik Bukke

Concomitant congestive heart failure \(CHF\) and diabetes mellitus \(DM\) patients frequently are treated with polypharmacy, thus potentially increasing the risk of drug\-drug interactions \(pDDIs\)\. Conventional DDI screening methods often fail to distinguish clinically significant interactions from recommended therapeutic combinations\. This study assessed the prevalence, severity, and clinical consequences of pDDIs in hospitalized patients with CHF and DM\. This ambispective, cross\-sectional study included 144 hospitalized patients with CHF and DM\. We used the Micromedex and Lexicomp databases to check prescriptions\. We classified clinically relevant DDIs and therapeutic combinations requiring routine monitoring by severity\. 207 pDDIs were identified, of which 84\.1% were moderate and 15\.9% severe\. Polypharmacy was a major risk factor for the DDI burden, and over seven drugs were associated with significantly more interactions than fewer drugs \(P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Polypharmacy was an independent predictor of clinically significant DDI \(AOR 3\.42; 95% CI 1\.78\-6\.59\) in the multivariate analysis\. The most commonly seen combinations \(statin\-ezetimibe and sulfonylurea\-metformin therapy\) are guideline\-recommended and do not need to be avoided\. Clinical pharmacists and prescribing clinicians performing context\-aware interpretation of DDI alerts by differentiating between guideline\-recommended therapeutic combinations requiring monitoring and truly actionable interactions can reduce alert fatigue, preserve evidence\-based therapy, and support safe prescribing in complex CHF\-DM patients\.

## [External validation and comparative performance of four risk scores for acute kidney injury in critically ill adults](../publications/2516bc7bc342e65b926b.md)

F Liu; Linpei Jia; Jing Wang; Lanjing Wang; Wang Zheng; Dandan Zhu; Meng Wang; Zhi Liu; 李思杰

Background Several parsimonious scores predict acute kidney injury \(AKI\), but their comparative performance in critically ill adults is uncertain\. We hypothesized that the ICU\-derived UCSD\-Mayo score would show higher discrimination than three scores developed in broader acute\-care populations\.Methods This single\-center retrospective validation study included 1,723 emergency ICU patients admitted from 2014 to 2021\. We compared the UCSD\-Mayo, AKI\-RiSc, Bell, and APS scores for in\-hospital AKI, AKI within 7 days, and stages 2 and 3 AKI\. Analyses included AUROC with paired DeLong comparisons, cross\-validated local recalibration, calibration plots, IDI, categorical NRI at the event rate, decision\-curve analysis, and prespecified sensitivity analyses\.Results In\-hospital AKI occurred in 406 patients \(23\.6%\), 281 \(16\.3%\) developed AKI within 7 days, and 169 \(9\.8%\) developed stages 2 and 3 AKI\. UCSD\-Mayo had the highest observed AUROC for in\-hospital AKI \(0\.713, 95%CI 0\.685–0\.740\), 7\-day AKI \(0\.690, 0\.658–0\.723\), and stages 2 and 3 AKI \(0\.706, 0\.665–0\.746\)\. Its 7\-day AUROC did not differ significantly from AKI\-RiSc \(difference 0\.029, 95%CI −0\.006 to 0\.064; p = 0\.103\)\. Reclassification and net benefit varied by outcome and threshold; sensitivity analyses did not materially change the overall pattern\.Conclusions In this single\-center Chinese emergency ICU cohort, UCSD\-Mayo showed the highest observed discrimination, but improvements were modest and were not uniform across all outcomes, metrics, or decision thresholds\. These scores may support risk awareness and monitoring but should not be used as stand\-alone treatment rules\.

## [Gated bidirectional cross\-modal attention framework with domain generalization for multimodal fake news detection](../publications/251beb65b8022db61f76.md)

Sapana Yakkundi; Rudragoud Patil; Aijazahamed Qazi; T Manoj

Abstract The rapid proliferation of multimodal misinformation on social media necessitates systems that identify fake news across domains\. Existing studies rely on simple concatenation\-based fusion, exhibiting poor generalization across heterogeneous platforms with varied content patterns and visual semantics\. To address this, this study presents Gated Cross Balanced Attention Network \(GCBA\-Net\), a novel framework that enhances fake news detection, robustness and domain adaptability\. GCBA\-Net employs an adaptive gating to independently weight textual and visual inputs\. To assess architectural design choices on detection performance, four variants of GCBA\-Net were developed varying in dimensionality, projection strategy, gating function, feed\-forward activation, attention head count, and attention type\. Domain generalization is achieved through Gradient Reversal Layer \(GRL\) and Maximum Mean Discrepancy \(MMD\) techniques\. Evaluation on Weibo and Fakeddit datasets demonstrates GCBA\-Net variants consistently outperform state\-of\-the\-art baselines\. The best variant on the Weibo achieved nearly 0\.99 accuracy, improving over the EANN baseline\. Performance improved from 0\.77 for the existing fusion model to over 0\.98 accuracy on Fakeddit, with precision, recall, and F1\-score exceeding 0\.97\. GCBA\-Net v1, v3 and v4 showed strong performance, while GCBA\-Net v2 yielded moderate results\. These findings demonstrate that GCBA\-Net is an adaptable, effective framework for detecting multilingual fake news in real\-world scenarios\.

## [Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Time Series Isolation Slicing and Multi\-domain Feature Fusion](../publications/251f945c424be682fb6f.md)

Wuchu Tang; Guofu Wu; Jiawei Yang; Wenxin Dong

To address the potential data leakage associated with overlapping slicing and the limited generalization capability of rolling bearing fault diagnosis models under strong noise, small\-sample, and class\-imbalanced conditions, a parallel CNN–BiLSTM–CBAM method based on time\-isolated slicing and multi\-domain feature fusion is proposed\. A time\-isolated data construction strategy is adopted, in which continuous vibration records are first partitioned into independent temporal segments and then sliced separately, thereby reducing the risk of cross\-subset information leakage caused by overlapping windows\. In addition, −2 dB noise and class\-imbalance processing are introduced to simulate complex operating conditions\. A dual\-branch EWT–CWT mechanism is constructed to collaboratively extract multi\-domain time–frequency features, and a gated adaptive fusion module is designed to dynamically estimate channel weights, thereby enhancing fault\-sensitive features while suppressing noise interference\. A parallel network is employed to capture local impulsive characteristics and bidirectional temporal dependencies, while CBAM further refines critical fault information\. The parameter sizes and training times of different models are also preliminarily compared\. The proposed method is evaluated on a self\-developed bearing test rig under multiple coupled speed–load conditions and on the public CWRU dataset\. Experimental results indicate that overlap\-first sampling followed by random partitioning may lead to overestimated test accuracy, whereas time\-isolated partitioning provides a more reliable indication of model performance on temporally independent test data\. Conflict of Interest Statement The authors declare no conflicts of interest\.

## [Estimation of glomerular filtration rate by standard renal CT imaging](../publications/2520ee1eec6a3a8305d1.md)

Kristoffer N\.D\. Huitfeldt Sola; Helena Genberg; Joshua Webster\-Ford; Anders Ullén; Torkel B\. Brismar

Abstract Objectives To develop and evaluate a method to predict glomerular filtration rate \(GFR\) from clinical renal CT\. Materials and methods Medical records of adult living kidney donors operated between 2013 and 2022 and patients considered for neoadjuvant cisplatin prior to cystectomy between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed\. Inclusion criteria were \(1\) renal CT obtained at 100 or 120 kVp before and 5–15 min after contrast administration, and \(2\) iohexol clearance test within 2 months of imaging\. The iohexol clearance test was performed on the same day as the cystatin C and creatinine measurements\. Estimated GFR values included cystatin C–based eGFR \(eGFR cystatin C \), creatinine\-based eGFR using the Cockcroft–Gault formula \(eGFR Cockcroft\-Gault \), and eGFR using the Revised Lund–Malmö formula \(eGFR LMR18 \), which is based on both creatinine and cystatin C\. Manual and automatic segmentations of the renal pelvis and bladder were performed in both the excretory and unenhanced phases\. Results In total, 139 patients were included in the analysis \(mean age 52 ± 13 years; 60% women\)\. Multivariate linear regression analysis combining the segmentation\-derived variable with body surface area and age gave an adjusted R\-square of 0\.77 to mGFR iohexol \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. GFR CT had the strongest relationship to mGFR iohexol with a mean absolute error of 12\.8 mL/min, compared with 15\.6 mL/min for eGFR Cockcroft\-Gault , 14\.2 mL/min for eGFR cystatin C , and 13\.0 mL/min for eGFR LMR18 \. Manual and automatic segmentations had similar performance\. Patients evaluated for cisplatin treatment had greater variation in CT\-estimated split renal function than donors\. Conclusion Renal function can be estimated with high precision from clinical renal CT\. Key Points Question Accurate GFR assessment is critical, but current methods are either labor\-intensive or imprecise\. Can renal CT imaging provide a reliable alternative? Findings CT\-derived eGFR showed the strongest correlation with iohexol clearance \(R² = 0\.77\), with lower error compared to creatinine\- and cystatin C–based estimates\. Critical relevance statement Routine CT imaging can provide precise estimates of kidney function, supporting donor evaluations, chemotherapy dosing, and critical care decisions when accurate renal function is essential\.

## [A generative AI framework for preference\-driven indoor visualization: an exploratory questionnaire\-based approach](../publications/252f2c6f470e67d200a5.md)

Mohamed Nour; Osama Abo Eleinen; ashraf elmokadem; Basma N\. El\-Mowafy

Abstract Although residential spatial qualities are consistently recognized as a determinant of occupant spatial preference and perceptual experience, early\-stage practice lacks systematic, user\-centered mechanisms for capturing and translating individual preferences into design concepts\. This study aims to examine whether a structured, questionnaire\-driven generative AI framework can produce preference\-aligned residential interior visualizations, and which spatial preference dimensions are most reliably translated\. To address this aim, a 15\-item multiple\-choice questionnaire, grounded in eight environmental psychology and architectural theory frameworks, maps user responses through a predefined parameter layer into structured prompts, guiding Google Gemini&\#x27;s integrated generative pipeline to produce individualized interior visualizations across three residential typologies: living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices\. Evaluation by 122 participants across 25 countries employed four perceptual constructs — Atmospheric Coherence, Emotional Comfort, Overall Satisfaction, and Expectations Alignment — operationalized strictly as indicators of perceived design suitability and preference resonance, not as measures of psychological or mental health outcomes\. All four constructs exceeded the neutral midpoint at a Bonferroni\-corrected threshold with large effect sizes \(M = 4\.03–4\.61; d = 1\.20–2\.52\), and internal consistency of the multi\-item constructs was acceptable to good \(α = 0\.72–0\.84\)\. The theoretically predicted construct hierarchy — with atmospheric parameters translating most reliably and identity\-expressive parameters least — was preserved across all typologies and evaluative profiles, establishing preliminary feasibility of the framework as a preference\-elicitation and visualization instrument for early\-stage design\.

## [Designing Teaching Materials with GenAI: Perceptions of Cognitive Load and Learner Competencies in Higher Education](../publications/25876d9fbaca1ec1c3f3.md)

Cristina Navas Romero; GANNA ZAKHAROVA; Francisco D\. Guillén‐Gámez; Sara Cebrián Cifuentes

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is increasingly used to design instructional materials in higher education, yet limited evidence exists on students’ perceptions of the cognitive demands and learner\-related competencies involved\. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory, this study examined university students’ perceptions of GenAI\-supported instructional material design according to gender, age, and admission grade\. A quantitative, non\-experimental, ex post facto study was conducted with 451 university students enrolled in education\-related undergraduate and master’s programmes\. The instrument assessed perceived usefulness, beliefs concerning metacognitive practices, prior knowledge, and problem\-solving strategies, and perceived intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load\. Participants generally reported positive perceptions\. Female students reported significantly higher scores on the metacognitive skills, prior knowledge, and problem\-solving skills dimensions, although effect sizes were small\. These differences should be interpreted cautiously, given that female students represented 82% of the sample\. No statistically significant gender differences were detected in the cognitive load dimensions\. Age showed only a weak negative association with extraneous cognitive load, whereas admission grade was positively associated with metacognitive scores in both gender groups and with prior knowledge and problem\-solving scores among female students\. The findings describe students’ beliefs about the practices and cognitive demands associated with GenAI\-supported material design and may inform training in the critical review and pedagogical adaptation of AI\-generated teaching materials\.

## [Endüstri 5\.0&\#x27;da İnsan\-Makine İş Birliğinin Çevresel Performansa Etkisi: KOBİ&\#x27;ler Üzerine Sistematik Bir Derleme ve Çerçeve Önerisi](../publications/258ac80fd16fe9f9a470.md)

Fatma Didem Tunçez; Ali AYHAN

Bu çalışma, Endüstri 5\.0&\#x27;ın insan merkezli vizyonu çerçevesinde, işbirlikçi robotların \(cobot\), yapay zekânın \(YZ\) ve dijital ikizlerin imalat KOBİ&\#x27;lerindeki çevresel performans üzerindeki etkisini sistematik bir derleme ve kavramsal çerçeve geliştirme yaklaşımıyla incelemektedir\. Çalışmanın temel amacı; teknolojilerin kontrollü koşullardaki çevresel potansiyeli ile gerçek üretim sahasındaki performansı arasındaki farkı ampirik verilerle belgelemek, bu farkın arkasındaki sosyo\-teknik dinamikleri açıklamak ve uygulanabilir bir kapatma çerçevesi sunmaktır\. PRISMA 2020 protokolü izlenerek Web of Science \(WoS\) veri tabanında \(2020–2025\) taranan 35\.442 yayından; gerçek üretim sahasında uygulanmış ve ölçülebilir çevresel KPI&\#x27;lar \(enerji, emisyon, atık\) içeren 28 ampirik makale derinlemesine tematik analize tabi tutulmuştur\. Nitel bulgular frekans sayımı ve çapraz kaynak doğrulamayla sentezlenmiştir\. Bu bulgular doğrultusunda çalışma, Bütünleşik Çevresel Performans Çerçevesi&\#x27;ni \(BÇPÇ\) önermektedir\. Çerçevenin matematiksel yapısı üç varsayıma dayanmaktadır: çarpımsal mantık \(en zayıf halka ilkesi\), analitik bağımsızlık ve normalize değerler\.
