## [Robust Spam Email Classification Using an Ensemble of Traditional ML and BERT\-Based Deep Learning Models](../publications/2595ae9643ede359643f.md)

Mushtaq Talib Mahdi

Phishing and spam emails have become enormous cybersecurity threats that call for accurate and efficient identification processes\. A comparative study of classical machine\-learning and deep\-learning approaches is developed in this paper, where we also present a BiLSTM\-based model\. The textual data is preprocessed \(lowercased, punctuation, non\-alphanumeric characters and stop words removed\) followed by TF\-IDF feature extraction\. The obtained features are passed to MNB and SVM classifiers, whose probabilistic predictions are combined using soft voting\. Along these lines, fine\-tuned BERT and BiLSTM models are used to exploit the sequential and contextual dependencies in the text data\. Performance of the model is evaluated using Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 score\. All models are trained and evaluated on a single, publicly available spam\-classification dataset \(spam\.csv, 5,573 labeled messages categorized as spam or ham\) using a held\-out test split\. The proposed BiLSTM\-based model proved its competitive classification performance with moderate computational complexity: the accuracy of 98\.92% and F1\-score of 96\.03%\. These results suggest that BiLSTM can accommodate contextual dependencies in spam and phishing\-related text, while providing a trade\-off to handle predictive performance and computational resources effectively\. Hence, the proposed method provide a good foundation for text\-wise spam and phishing detection that is both effective and scalable\.

## [Automated Trash Bin](../publications/25979c96e805381adf9a.md)

Ivymae C\. Pautan; Josephine Gonzaga

This study developed and evaluated an automated trash bin designed to improve sanitation and waste disposal practices through sensor\-based technology\. Specifically, it assessed the functionality of the automated lid operation using ultrasonic sensing technology, the waste segregation system, the disinfectant spray mechanism for odor reduction, and the smartphone\-based notification system that alerted users when the bin reached full capacity\. A descriptive\-developmental research design was employed, with teachers and staff of B\.A\. Calamba National High School in Pangao\-an, Magpet, Cotabato serving as the respondents\. The functionality of the system was tested through ten experimental trials, while user acceptability was evaluated in terms of design, convenience, and safety\. Results indicated that most system features operated consistently and were rated as highly workable\. Although minor inconsistencies were observed in the waste segregation sensor, suggesting the need for further calibration and refinement, the overall performance of the automated trash bin remained reliable and functional\. Furthermore, respondents rated the innovation as highly acceptable across all evaluation criteria, demonstrating its effectiveness, safety, and user\-friendliness\. The study concluded that the automated trash bin provided a practical and innovative solution for enhancing sanitation, promoting proper waste management practices, and supporting public health and environmental cleanliness\. It recommended further improvement of the waste segregation sensor to optimize system performance and encouraged future studies to integrate additional smart technologies that could enhance the efficiency and sustainability of automated waste management systems\.

## [Systematic Review of AI\-Based PHM Frameworks for Ship Systems and Equipment](../publications/2598c89e128b99f1b19c.md)

Luis Fernando Mendoza Cardona; Joan Suarez Loaiza; E\. Castillo; Edwin Giovanny Paipa Sanabria; Juan Carlos Martínez\-Santos

Maritime operations require high levels of availability and safety under changing cargo, operational, and environmental conditions\. Therefore, anticipating degradation and failures in critical ship systems is an important operational requirement\.Although predictive maintenance has advanced rapidly through data\-driven approaches and artificial intelligence \(AI\), the available literature remains fragmented and does not consistently establish the relationships among the ship systems analyzed, the methodological approaches employed, and the conditions required for operational implementation\.This article presents a systematic literature review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA\) methodology to examine the development of AI\-based predictive maintenance for ship systems from a Prognostics and Health Management \(PHM\) perspective\. Scopus and Web of Science were searched, and predefined screening, eligibility, inclusion, and exclusion criteria were applied\.The findings show that research is strongly concentrated on propulsion systems, classified under Ship Work Breakdown Structure \(SWBS\) Group 200, and electric\-plant systems, classified under SWBS Group 300, with most studies focusing on detection and diagnosis\. Prognostic and prescriptive applications remain comparatively less developed\. Methodologically, the literature is dominated by machine\-learning and deep\-learning approaches using operational and condition\-monitoring variables associated with different operating regimes\.Overall, maritime PHM exhibits uneven levels of functional and implementation maturity\. Important challenges remain in model comparability, independent validation, and sustained onboard deployment, while opportunities persist for extending PHM to underrepresented ship systems and validating these approaches in real\-world fleet operations

## [Study on AI Education and Skill Development: NEP 2020 and AI Integration](../publications/259962ab32574af2f920.md)

Ms\. Zulfa Khan; Mr\. Tarkar Jeet Ravindranath

Abstract Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is becoming an important technology in transforming education and skill development\. The National Education Policy \(NEP\) 2020 emphasizes technology\-enabled learning, multidisciplinary education, vocational education, critical thinking, creativity, and the development of future\-ready skills\. The integration of AI into education can support these objectives by providing personalized learning, intelligent assessment, automated feedback, digital learning resources, and improved teaching and learning processes\. AI can help students learn according to their individual needs, improve academic performance, and access educational resources more effectively\. It can also contribute to the development of digital literacy, problem\-solving, creativity, communication, and other skills required in the changing world of work\. For teachers, AI can assist in lesson planning, assessment, feedback, and identifying students&\#x27; learning needs, thereby improving the overall efficiency of the education system\. However, the successful integration of AI also presents several challenges\. These include the digital divide, unequal access to technology, inadequate digital infrastructure, data privacy and security concerns, ethical issues, limited awareness, and insufficient training among teachers and educators\. Addressing these challenges is essential to ensure that AI benefits all learners equally and is used responsibly\. This study examines the role of AI in education and skill development and explores its alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020\. It focuses on the opportunities offered by AI, as well as the challenges involved in its implementation\. The study also suggests measures such as improving digital infrastructure, providing teacher training, promoting AI awareness, ensuring data privacy, and establishing ethical guidelines for responsible AI use\. Overall, the study highlights that the effective and responsible integration of AI can strengthen the objectives of NEP 2020\. By combining technological innovation with inclusive and learner\-centred approaches, AI can contribute to a more personalized, accessible, innovative, and future\-ready education system in India\. Keywords: AI Personalized learning, intelligent assessment, digital learning resources, language support, and improved teaching methods\.

## [Evolution and Classification of Solar Tracking Systems: From Fixed\-Mount to Dual\-Axis Configurations](../publications/259c3a9b733824864fb8.md)

Efosa EDEGBE; Ehimen Isibhakhomen IBHADODE

The energy delivered by a photovoltaic \(PV\) panel depends on how closely its surface stays perpendicular to the incident solar beam\. Solar trackers address this, but published energy\-gain figures vary widely \(about 10–100% across reviews, and 22–56% in a 2020 review\), and many historical and technical statements are repeated without primary sources\. This review addresses that inconsistency for readers who must choose or design a tracker\. Following a documented search protocol, it \(i\) traces PV and tracker development against verified sources, \(ii\) defines the azimuth, zenith/elevation and tilt conventions and the two incompatible azimuth conventions in use, \(iii\) classifies trackers by degrees of freedom, drive and control strategy, and \(iv\) synthesises reported gains from reviews and field studies\. Field studies in the set report dual\-axis gains of 30\.8–37\.2% over fixed mounts, and single\-axis gains of 10–24%, with wide variation in baseline, duration and climate; the extra gain of dual\-axis over single\-axis is only a few percentage points in the most comparable study\. Control strategy, land use and parasitic energy consumption affect the net benefit as much as the number of axes\. The review closes with recommendations for standardised reporting and states where its findings are useful

## [Clinical Characteristics, Disease Activity and Severity of Thyroid Orbitopathy at Presentation to a Tertiary Referral Center](../publications/25a0f7667f54758a2ec2.md)

Zeynep Akkul; Derya Doğanay; Burcu Kahkeci

Objectives: To present the clinical characteristics of patients with thyroid orbitopathy at initial presentation to a tertiary care center and to determine the disease activity and severity of thyroid orbitopathy at the time of referral\.Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 105 right eyes of 105 patients with thyroid orbitopathy \(TO\) presenting to our clinic between January 2024 and January 2026\. On inspection, eyelid retraction and lid lag were evaluated, and margin reflex distance 1 and 2 \(MRD1 and MRD2\) were measured\. Exophthalmometry was performed to determine the amount of proptosis\. The Clinical Activity Score \(CAS\) was calculated based on the presence of spontaneous retrobulbar pain or pain on eye movements, eyelid edema or hyperemia, conjunctival chemosis or hyperemia, and caruncle edema\. The EUGOGO classification attempts to assess both disease activity and disease severity\.Results: The study population consisted predominantly of female patients, with a comparable age distribution between sexes\. All patients had bilateral involvement\. Most patients had inactive disease according to the Clinical Activity Score \(CAS\)\. However, disease activity differed significantly between sexes, with male patients exhibiting a higher frequency of active disease than female patients\. According to the EUGOGO classification, mild disease was the most prevalent severity category, followed by moderate\-to\-severe and sight\-threatening disease\. Although sight\-threatening disease was numerically more frequent in male patients, no statistically significant sex\-related differences were observed across the EUGOGO severity categories\.Conclusion: Among TO patients, a substantial proportion of those referred to tertiary care centers had active disease, and male sex was found to be associated with higher clinical activity\. These findings emphasize the importance of early diagnosis and timely multidisciplinary evaluation which may aid to reduce disease\-related morbidity\.

## [СОЦІАЛЬНА РІВНІСТЬ У ЦИФРОВОМУ СУСПІЛЬСТВІ: МІЖ ГУМАНІЗМОМ І ТРАНСГУМАНІЗМОМ](../publications/25af331bbe6fd805be83.md)

Алла Анатоліївна Кравченко

У статті досліджено трансформацію соціальної рівності в умовах цифровізації та поширення практик технологічного вдосконалення людини\. Актуальність проблеми пов’язана з тим, що цифрові технології і штучний інтелект не лише нерівномірно розподіляють соціальні можливості, а й дедалі активніше впливають на когнітивні, професійні та потенційно біологічні спроможності людини\. Метою дослідження є концептуалізація змін соціальної рівності на перетині гуманістичної та трансгуманістичної парадигм і визначення нормативних критеріїв соціально справедливого технологічного розвитку\. Методологічну основу становлять концептуальний і порівняльний аналіз, нормативно\-етичний підхід та міждисциплінарний синтез\. Простежено ускладнення цифрової нерівності: від нерівності доступу і компетентностей до нерівності результатів, представленості в даних, взаємодії з алгоритмічними системами та можливостей використання штучного інтелекту\. Показано, що технологічне вдосконалення людини за умов нерівного доступу може сприяти закріпленню соціальних переваг у стійких відмінностях людських спроможностей\. Для концептуалізації цього ризику запропоновано поняття технологічно опосередкованої антропологічної нерівності\. Обґрунтовано нормативні умови, за яких технологічне розширення можливостей залишається сумісним із рівним моральним статусом, автономією, недомінуванням і соціальною справедливістю\. Проведений аналіз дає підстави розглядати соціальну рівність у цифровому суспільстві ширше, ніж рівність доступу до матеріальних або цифрових ресурсів\. Її нормативний зміст формується на перетині розподільного, спроможнісного та реляційного вимірів: важливими є не тільки справедливість доступу до суспільно значущих благ, а й реальна здатність людини використовувати їх для досягнення значущих цілей та збереження рівного морального і соціального статусу\. Такий підхід дозволяє оцінювати технологічні зміни не за самим фактом появи нових відмінностей, а за тим, як вони впливають на можливості людини, характер соціальних відносин і умови суспільної участі\. Практичне значення результатів полягає у можливості застосування запропонованих критеріїв для оцінювання соціальних наслідків високовпливових технологій\.

## [Deep\-Learning\-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives](../publications/25b31c9e87949c9fdd6c.md)

Xu Jianeng; Min\-Min Zhao; C\. J\. Xu; Xiang Wang; Zhe Dou; Yue Wang

Abstract The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases \(IREDs\) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds\. Herein, we report a machine learning \(ML\)\-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation\. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep\-learning\-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate\. Subsequent engineering using a few\-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N \(M6\) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface\. Kinetic analysis showed 156\-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72\-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild\-type \(WT\) enzyme\. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters\. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement\. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1\. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95\.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10\.5 g of enantiopure methyl N\-\(2\-methoxy\-2\-oxoethyl\)\-d\-alaninate \(1a\) in 75\.0% isolated yield with &gt; 99\.9% ee\. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML\-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability\.

## [HERO: a hierarchical attention and multi\-feature fusion framework for automated English essay scoring](../publications/25b670fd76a946463ac1.md)

Xiaoru Gou

Automated essay scoring \(AES\) has emerged as a crucial task in educational technology, aiming to replicate human evaluation of writing with speed, fairness, and accuracy\. This study proposes an advanced deep learning framework, HERO \(Hierarchical Essay Representation Optimizer\), that uses hierarchical attention mechanisms and multi\-feature fusion for holistic and grammar\-based essay scoring\. The proposed model employs a two\-level bidirectional LSTM with attention to capture contextual information at both word and sentence levels, while integrating auxiliary metadata features such as prompt ID, gender, and grade level to enhance prediction performance\. Experiments are conducted on the ASAP 2\.0 dataset containing nearly 12,000 human\-scored essays\. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance over baseline models, including MLP, KNN, and XGBoost, achieving a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0\.92, MAE of 0\.019, and CCC of 0\.91\. Comprehensive evaluation using error metrics, correlation measures, and statistical validation confirms the robustness and reliability of the model\. The findings indicate that the integration of hierarchical representation learning with feature\-level fusion significantly enhances essay scoring accuracy while supporting interpretability\. However, the fairness analysis was limited to aggregate evaluation on the available dataset, and subgroup\-level calibration was not comprehensively validated\.

## [2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenide \(TMD\) Memristive In\-Sensor Computing and Neuromorphic Vision Chips: Atomically Thin Photodetectors, Sub\-Nanosecond Optoelectronic Modulation, and Edge Visual Processing](../publications/25b9c68c8c090df1d239.md)

Ayush Gupta, Harshit Jain, Dr\. Rajeev Kumar Verma, Dr\. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr\. Akhil Pandey,   Er\.Ram Babu Buri

Autonomous vision systems, edge artificial intelligence, and real\-time robotics are fundamentally constrained by the energy\-prohibitive data transfer overhead between separated image sensors \(CMOS cameras\) and digital processing units \(GPUs, TPUs\)\. In\-Sensor Computing establishes a transformative paradigm shift that fuses optical sensing, non\-volatile memory, and neural computation directly into a single unified atomically thin hardware layer\. TwoDimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenides \(2D TMDs, such as MoS2, WSe2, and MoSe2\) provide an exceptional material platform for optoelectronic in\-sensor computing, featuring direct bandgaps, high optical absorption coefficients, pronounced excitonic effects, and memristive conductance switching via trap\-assisted charge\-trapping\. By integrating 2D TMD photodetectors with memristive crossbar arrays, artificial vision chips can capture visual inputs, store synaptic weights, and execute parallel matrix\-vector multiplications for feature extraction and pattern recognition natively at the optical focal plane with sub\-nanosecond latency and ultra\-low power dissipation\. However, translating atomically thin TMD optoelectronic devices from laboratory flakes into wafer\-scale in\-sensor vision chips introduces profound physical and manufacturing bottlenecks: high contact resistance at metal\-TMD interfaces, spatial variations in defect density causing conductance drift, sub\-bandgap trap relaxation kinetics limiting frame rates, and large\-scale 2D material growth uniformity\. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of 2D TMD memristive in\-sensor computing and neuromorphic vision chips\. We formalize optoelectronic photoconductive gain via trap\-assisted recombination models, derive crossbar in\-sensor dot\-product transfer functions, and model spatiotemporal spiking vision processing\. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise multi\-physics co\-simulation and physical wafer\-scale testbed evaluating 64x64 MoS2 optoelectronic memristive crossbar arrays across real\-time edge image classification \(MNIST, CIFAR\-10\) and optical pattern recognition\. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our 2D MoS2 in\-sensor vision chip achieves an energy efficiency of 342\.4 Tera\-Operations per Second per Watt \(TOPS/W\)—a 35x improvement over conventional CMOS camera\-GPU pipelines—while sustaining a sub\-nanosecond sensing\-computation latency and 97\.8% image classification accuracy\. Finally, we formulate open challenges in wafer\-scale 2D epitaxy, multispectral color filtering, and all\-optical reset mechanisms\.

## [Water Sensitive Urban Planning: Mapping Its Evolution](../publications/25bc6ff51a3c9c3727c4.md)

Abhishek Chhonkar; Rina Surana

Rapid urbanization, urban growth, and improvement in quality of life have led to an increase in freshwater demand globally, which, coupled with limited water resources, gives rise to challenges in the supply of water\.These challenges are further exacerbated by substandard infrastructure and the spiraling costs of inter\-basin transfers from sources beyond catchments and administrative limits of urban areas required by large urban centres\.Development of urban areas has often resulted in reduction of percolation sinks and blocking of urban drainage systems, causing waterlogging, flooding, and water pollution\.Rapid socioeconomic development and unchecked urban sprawl, despite the existing water scarcity, have frequently led to the mismanagement of urban water resources\.Physical planning is poorly integrated with water resources&\#x27; planning, promoting unsustainable growth\.Unsustainable and unregulated urban growth is being fostered in most cities because of a lack of integration between land use plans and water resource planning\.Leading research organizations and scholars in the field have addressed these issues from various angles in multiple directions with different priorities, concepts, and visions at different levels and scales\.In this study a systematic literature review is carried out to explore the integration of urban planning and urban water management\.Bibliometric analyses are conducted to identify key research areas, important keywords, and emerging research trends\.The findings indicated a rise in studies related to urban planning and urban water management since 2003\.The paper highlighted the need for a more integrated, water\-sensitive approach and interdisciplinary research to address the challenges of water scarcity and urbanization 1\.

## [Gut microbiota are linked to gastrointestinal symptoms and behavioral changes but not inflammation in autism spectrum disorder: a cross\-sectional analysis](../publications/25d8ddb330ce40bc9901.md)

Vaishali Harne; Nicole Y\. Fatheree; Angela V\. Serrano; Beanna Okeugo; Ana Fadhel Alvarez; Manouchehr Hessabi; Amirali Tahanan; Rosleen Mansour; Fernando Navarro; Essam M\. Imseis; Supriya Nair; Wallace A\. Gleason; Melissa R\. Van Arsdall; Tu Mai; Shabba A\. Armbrister; Salomea Giorgberidze; Mohammad Hossein Rahbar; Minjae Lee; Deborah A\. Pearson; Ruth Ann Luna; Yuying Liu; J\. Marc Rhoads

BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal \(GI\) symptoms are increased in children with autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\)\. We examined the relationship between ASD severity, intestinal inflammation, gut permeability, and dysbiosis\. METHODS: Our cross\-sectional study examined baseline data from a clinical trial and included stools from typically developing \(TD\) controls and siblings\. GI symptom severity was assessed using GI severity index \(GSI\) with Bristol stool scoring, while ASD symptoms were quantified using Social Responsiveness Scale \(SRS\-2\)\. Biomarkers including plasma zonulin, occludin, and S100A9, and fecal calprotectin levels, were measured to assess intestinal permeability and inflammation\. Fecal microbiota was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing\. RESULTS: Seventy\-two children with ASD were included for biomarker analysis, and 135 children&\#x27;s stools for microbiome analysis\. A statistically significant correlation was observed between GSI and SRS\-2 scores \(p = 0\.02\)\. GSI and SRS\-2 scores did not correlate with measured biomarkers, none of which were elevated above published normal values\. Children with ASD had reduced fecal richness and distinct clustering of organisms, with increased relative abundance of Fusicatenibacter, Blautia, Sarcina, and Eubacterium, compared to TD children\. CONCLUSIONS: Children with ASD who had GI symptoms had increased Bacteroides and Ruminococci\. Dysbiosis correlated with common GI symptoms, including flatulence, foul stools, and nighttime awakening\. IMPACT: Children with ASD who have more disturbed social awareness are prone to more severe GI symptoms, reduced fecal microbial diversity and abnormal fecal microbial composition\. Certain stool microbial taxa correlated with total GI symptom scores as well as with specific GI symptoms including flatulence, abdominal pain/irritability, and foul\-smelling stools\. However, we found no evidence of gastrointestinal or systemic inflammation, nor of increased gut permeability to explain the symptoms\.

## [Virus\-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses](../publications/25e0ed552cbfbcf284bf.md)

Zihan Zhang; Huiwen Zheng; Longding Liu

Introduction Virus\-like particles \(VLPs\) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication\-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity\. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood\.Areas covered This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen\-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition\. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen\-presenting cells and shape CD4\+ and CD8\+ T\-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell–B\-cell interactions within germinal centers\. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered\.Expert opinion The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses\. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure–immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability\. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high\-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism\-based optimization of VLP platforms\. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge\.
