## [Clinical and pathological analysis of invasive mucinous micropapillary carcinoma of the breast: a series of case reports](../publications/25e7d730c560cfbaa277.md)

Jiangjiang Zheng; Aimei Lu; Mengchao Fang

The aim of the study was to analyse the clinicopathological features of invasive mucinous micropapillary carcinoma \(MUMPC\), a rare breast cancer variant\. We retrospectively reviewed 7 MUMPC cases diagnosed in 2017–2024, evaluating clinical, imaging, histopathological, and immunohistochemical data \(including epithelial membrane antigen, hormone receptors, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, and Kiel 67 antigen\)\. The cohort comprised 7 female patients aged 40–77 years \(mean, 53\.8 years\)\. Tumour size range was 0\.9–6\.0 cm \(mean, 3\.4 cm\)\. Histologically, all tumours exhibited classic features: abundant extracellular mucin containing tumour cells arranged in micropapillary, glandular, and cluster patterns, with characteristic retraction\-like spaces\. Regarding nuclear grade, 5 cases showed low\-to\-intermediate\-grade nuclei, while 2 cases exhibited high\-grade nuclei\. Immuno\- phenotypically, 6 cases demonstrated strong positivity for oestrogen and progesterone receptors \(50–95% of cells\)\. The human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 status was negative \(score 0\) in 4 cases, equivocal \(2\+\) in 2 cases \(both confirmed to have amplification by fluorescence in situ hybridisation\), and positive \(3\+\) in 1 case\. Two patients had lymph node metastasis; 5 patients remained recurrence\-free at 60 months of follow\-up, 1 patient died at 17 months, and 1 patient was newly diagnosed\. Mucinous micropapillary carcinoma displays distinct clinicopathological and immunophenotypic features, suggesting potentially more aggressive behaviour than pure mucinous carcinoma\. Accurate diagnosis and individualised management are essential\.

## [Regulating Artificial Intelligence in Greece: Constitutional Principles and Administrative Safeguards Beyond the Impact of the AI Act](../publications/25f498d356cdddd5ce53.md)

Fereniki Panagopoulou; Stefanos Vitoratos

This article examines how artificial intelligence and Regulation \(EU\) 2024/1689 affect the Greek legal order\. It argues that the AI Act has not yet significantly reshaped Greek constitutional or legislative architecture, while AI systems already influence public administration, judicial processes, cybersecurity governance, and public\-sector capacity\. The analysis focuses on constitutional guarantees, Law 4961/2022, access to administrative documents, automated decision\-making, accountability, and digital transformation\. It concludes that the AI Act chiefly consolidates challenges already arising in practice and that effective governance depends on adapting and rigorously applying existing rule\-of\-law safeguards\. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; AI Act; Greece; Constitutional law; Administrative law

## [II\. Meşrutiyet Dönemi Edebî Tenkidinde Genç Kalemler ve Yeni Lisan](../publications/25f4c2eb48d4bd0f9254.md)

Tuba Dalar

Kendine özgü hatırlatma biçimleri içeren edebî metinler, toplumların kökleri ile kurduğu bağı kuvvetlendirerek ulusal kimliğe süreklilik kazandırır\. Dilin filolojik bir olgu olmanın ötesinde büyük oranda siyasal ve toplumsal bir olgu olduğunun bilincinde olan sanatçılar, milletlerin kolektif belleğini oluşturan kadim simgeler düzlemini, dağılmalara karşı koruma altına alırlar\. Yeni Lisan öncesi bazı muhtelif dergilerde ele alınan dilde sadeleşme, daha çok tasfiyeci bir perspektiften tanımlanmıştır\. Yeni Lisan hareketi ile de dil konusu, daha şuurlu ve sistematik bir şekilde incelenir ve sanatın seviyesi düşürülmeden dilde sadeleşmenin mümkün olabileceği ortaya koyulur\. Eleştiriye dair yöntemsel tartışmaların ötesinde olan bu çalışmada, dil ve edebiyat vasıtasıyla millî bir kültür, millî bir tefekkür inşa etme gayretinde olan millî edebiyat dönemi sanatçıları ile fikirsel düzlemde onlarla örtüşen ve onlardan ayrışan dönem sanatçıları arasında gelişen eleştiri metinleri ve polemikler değerlendirilerek dönemin eleştirel portresi çizildi\. Millet, kavim, ırk, millî edebiyat, kavmî edebiyat, millî dil, yeni insan, yeni hayat gibi kavramların etrafında kurgulanan millî bir edebî hareketin tanımı, amacı, ilkeleri ve ortaya koyduğu eserler üzerine dönemin muhtelif yayın organlarında pek çok eleştiri metni yayımlansa da bu çalışmada, Ali Canip Yöntem, Ömer Seyfettin ve Ziya Gökalp’in katkılarıyla 1911’de Selanik’ten yayın hayatına merhaba diyen Genç Kalemler’de çıkan yazılar değerlendirildi\.

## [Anxiety and depressive symptoms and health\-related quality of life in girls with central precocious puberty versus isolated premature thelarche: a comparative cross\-sectional study](../publications/25f79dc8691bc502bf82.md)

Burak Kamış; Semine Özdemir Dilek; Gürkan Tarçın

Introduction Previous studies have examined psychological symptoms and health\-related quality of life \(HRQoL\) in girls with central precocious puberty \(CPP\) and isolated premature thelarche \(IPT\), but findings from direct comparisons have been inconsistent\. We aimed to compare anxiety and depressive symptoms and HRQoL between girls with CPP and IPT and to examine associations between psychological symptom burden and HRQoL\. Methods This comparative cross\-sectional study included 50 girls \(mean age, 8\.33 ± 0\.23 years\), including 18 with idiopathic CPP and 32 with IPT\. Breast development had first been recognized before 8 years of age in all participants\. Psychological questionnaires were administered on the same day as the endocrinological evaluation\. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using SCARED, RCADS\-CV, and CDI, and self\-reported HRQoL was assessed using PedsQL 4\.0\. Between\-group comparisons incorporated Benjamini–Hochberg false\-discovery\-rate correction\. Spearman correlations and exploratory hierarchical linear regression were performed\. Results No between\-group differences in anxiety, depressive symptoms, or HRQoL remained statistically significant after FDR correction\. Clinically elevated SCARED scores occurred in 38\.9% of girls with CPP and 53\.1% with IPT \(p=0\.333\), while CDI scores ≥19 occurred in 11\.1% and 18\.8%, respectively \(p=0\.694\)\. In the combined sample, psychological symptom scores were inversely correlated with PedsQL total scores \(Spearman’s r s =−0\.568 to −0\.720; all p&lt;0\.001\)\. In exploratory regression adjusted for endocrine phenotype, BMI SDS, and symptom duration, SCARED \(β=−0\.382, p=0\.003\) and CDI \(β=−0\.481, p&lt;0\.001\) scores were associated with lower PedsQL total scores\. Discussion Higher anxiety and depressive symptom scores were associated with lower HRQoL in this clinical sample\. The absence of statistically significant CPP–IPT differences does not establish equivalence or exclude a contribution of endocrine factors\. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these associations\.

## [Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent\-Based Agro\-Ecological Model](../publications/25ff04fd0334741ff307.md)

Benjamin Pianet; Baptiste Lesquoy; Paul Saves; Benoit Gaudou; Jean Villerd; Nicolas Verstaevel; Olivier Therond

Agent\-based models are well\-suited for modelling agro\-ecological systems for decision\-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours\. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher\-level choice activates them\. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill\-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction\. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first\-class modelling object\. Using advanced surrogate modelling techniques, we encode the crop\-management itinerary of the high\-resolution agro\-ecological modelling platform MAELIA as a hierarchical design space featuring both categorical and numerical variables\. We propose a novel dedicated method to analyse this kind of hierarchical space, a random\-forest\-supervised HSIC\-ANOVA, which ranks main effects and interactions natively on the tree while placing rarely and always active decisions on an equal footing\. We show how, when applied to simulation outputs such as nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon variation, and yield predictions, it can deliver an interpretable, decision\-oriented reading\.

## [SBCA: cross\-modal gated actor\-critic with frozen BERT\-based sentiment features for multi\-asset portfolio optimization](../publications/2601921da2d790861541.md)

Jinfeng Pan; Mi Liu; 晓萍; Jiahao Chen

Portfolio optimization is constrained by linear assumptions and limited integration of multi\-modal information\. Throughout this study, BERT serves only as a text encoder producing a scalar sentiment score from headlines; it is fine\-tuned offline once and then held fixed, so its parameters are neither updated nor jointly optimized with the policy, and its scores are pre\-computed static inputs\. We propose a cross\-modal gated Actor\-Critic framework \(SBCA\) for multi\-asset portfolio optimization, addressing two gaps in deep reinforcement learning: reliance on a single affine concatenation layer for price\-text fusion, and the absence of downside\-risk and turnover penalties in reward designs\. SBCA learns gated cross\-modal interactions and embeds both penalties in its reward\. On 11 years of U\.S\. equity data, SBCA outperforms Equal Weight, Buy &amp; Hold, the Dow Jones index, MVO and PPO on all metrics in the 2\- and 4\-asset groups, and in the 6\-asset group trails only Equal Weight and MVO in absolute return\. Block\-bootstrap tests give exploratory, uncorrected evidence for the Actor\-Critic component over gated fusion in the 2\-asset group, though no component\-level comparison survives correction; cost sensitivity gives descriptive evidence of robustness\. SBCA thus combines offline text preprocessing with a jointly trained policy for dynamic portfolio decision\-making\.

## [Del eco algorítmico a la voz original: educación sensible y desfondamiento](../publications/260f07b5fef6707b71af.md)

Luis Manuel Martínez Domínguez

The massive irruption of generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) constitutes an ontological event that challenges contemporary education beyond mere technical efficiency or academic integrity\. This study justifies the critical urgency of addressing the structural &quot;groundlessness&quot; of the human person in the face of current algorithmic saturation and technological idolatry\. The main objective is to analyze, within the theoretical framework of Sensitive Education, the imminent risk of the &quot;synthetic echo&quot; supplanting the student&\#x27;s &quot;original voice,&quot; thereby atrophying their discursive agency and capacity for meaning\. A hermeneutic and phenomenological methodology is employed, articulating Leonardo Polo&\#x27;s transcendental anthropology, Hartmut Rosa&\#x27;s sociology of resonance, and the cultural criticism of authors such as Byung\-Chul Han and Éric Sadin\. The results reveal a deep existential fracture: AI imposes a &quot;perfect closure&quot; of data that collides with human &quot;radical openness,&quot; generating an alienation where discourse \(logos\) is traumatically dissociated from vital experience \(bios\)\. In conclusion, it is argued that true digital literacy requires a transition from the isolation of the digital &quot;false\-we&quot; towards a &quot;mature\-we&quot; capable of ethical resistance and real alterity\. Educational assessment must abandon the forensic approach to plagiarism to discern, through a &quot;resonant hearing,&quot; the vibratory authenticity of learning, thus guaranteeing the primacy of the spirit over automatism and restoring the classroom as an essential sanctuary of presence and listening\.

## [INTEGRATED COST\-SCHEDULE AND PROCUREMENT ANALYTICS FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY CHAINS IN SAUDI MEGA\-PROJECTS: ENHANCING FORECASTING AND PROJECT DELIVERY UNDER VISION 2030](../publications/261b036f929d2c11efee.md)

Amaan Ullah Sharif Mohammed

Saudi mega\-projects operate through dense networks of designers, contractors, manufacturers, logistics providers and specialist suppliers, so cost and schedule performance cannot be governed effectively as separate reporting streams\. Procurement commitments shape the timing and price of resources; schedule changes alter purchasing priorities and logistics demand; and commercial variations feed back into forecast completion cost\. This review develops an integrated framework for cost\-schedule and procurement analytics in construction supply chains, with particular relevance to Saudi Arabias Vision 2030 delivery environment\. Thirty peer\-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2025 were synthesised across artificial intelligence in construction management, project cost prediction, schedule forecasting, construction supply\-chain modelling, resilience and digital\-twin\-enabled control\. The evidence indicates that predictive value emerges when cost, schedule and procurement records share consistent identifiers, timestamps and decision horizons\. Machine\-learning and hybrid models can improve forecasting, but isolated accuracy is insufficient unless outputs expose uncertainty, identify drivers and trigger accountable management action\.

## [A Statistical Study of Ion\-scale Waves at 1 au Using Machine Learning](../publications/261b4a375c0672635dbf.md)

S\. Fordin; Michael A\. Shay; Lynn B\. Wilson III; Jaye L\. Verniero; Subash Adhikari; Manuel Andres Herrera Arias; Bilal Khan; Daniel O’Donnell; Barbara J\. Thompson

Abstract Circularly polarized waves at ion scales are thought to play vital roles in the heating and acceleration of coronal plasma, though the extent of their roles throughout the heliosphere remains an open question\. In this work, a 1D convolutional neural network trained to identify waves in magnetic field time\-series data is used to classify the Wind spacecraft data set at 1 au for the yr 2005–2024\. Approximately 1\.8 million intervals out of about one hundred million intervals are found to contain circularly polarized wave signatures with amplitudes &gt;0\.1 nT and spacecraft\-frame frequencies &gt;0\.16 Hz\. Wave intervals are observed most often in both the fast, hot wind and in slow Alfvénic wind\. The number of wave intervals per day fluctuates at frequencies that closely follow the harmonics of solar rotation, implying a connection between wave occurrence and large\-scale solar wind features\. Comparison of the measured temperature anisotropy and proton plasma beta in wave intervals to kinetic instability criteria shows a correlation between wave occurrence and the proton cyclotron and mirror instabilities\. However, local generation mechanisms associated with core proton temperature anisotropy instability only account for ≈30% of the identified waves\.

## [Cross\-domain signal grammars of transcription termination](../publications/261e71042556c693cfb9.md)

Shouqing Hou; Hongru Ma; Xuye Lang; Yuan Yao

Transcription termination establishes gene boundaries, recycles RNA polymerase, and prevents interference between neighboring transcription units\. Termination depends on cis\-acting elements, trans\-acting factors, and the susceptibility of the elongation complex to pausing, cleavage, destabilization, or release\. Predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase\-release regions are nevertheless often treated as measurements of the same event, which complicates mechanistic comparison and model development\. This review compares termination signals as context\-dependent rule systems in which sequence determinants, RNA structure and accessibility, and processing sites are interpreted through their order and spacing, molecular readers, conditional gates, and kinetic windows\. It examines bacterial intrinsic and Rho\-dependent termination, archaeal U\-rich and cleavage\-linked routes, PAS\-centered RNAPII termination, and nuclear Pol I, Pol III, and specialized RNAPII pathways, showing how shared kinetic constraints are met by divergent molecular solutions shaped by cellular organization\. Matching each signal feature to the measurement that supports it clarifies cross\-domain comparisons and guides transcriptome\-wide analysis, prediction, and terminator engineering in defined biological systems\.

## [E\-MDD: an evidence\-guided explainable framework for EEG\-based depression recognition](../publications/262a13a681dce137e9d2.md)

Huang Junfen; Zhuhuayang Zhang; YingYu Cao; Zhenxi Zhao; Liangfei Niu

Introduction An evidence\-guided explainable framework, E\-MDD, is developed to integrate high\-dimensional EEG representations, neurophysiological biomarkers, and large language models for the recognition of EEG\-based depression with concise and evidence\-based textual explanations\. Methods The proposed E\-MDD framework consists of three stages: classification, evidence construction, and evidence\-guided inference\. In the classification stage, two parallel feature extraction branches are employed to extract Electroencephalography latent features and neurophysiological biomarkers, which are subsequently fused and fed into a lightweight multilayer perceptron for the recognition of depression\. In the evidence construction stage, the latent feature dimensions of the EEG are aligned with neurophysiological biomarkers, and the model&\#x27;s decision basis is identified to construct structured evidence supporting the classification results\. In the evidence\-guided inference stage, structured evidence and the proposed evidence\-guided prompt are used to guide the large language model in generating concise textual explanations\. Results The experimental results on the Mumtaz dataset show that E\-MDD achieves an AUC of 0\.8472 and an F1\-score of 0\.8421\. Meanwhile, the generated short\-text explanations can effectively describe the basis of the model&\#x27;s decision\-making for its predictions, demonstrating a high degree of faithfulness\. The proposed framework also demonstrates consistent evidence\-guided explanation performance across EEGNet and EEGConformer\. Discussion Overall, this study proposes a neurophysiologically interpretable framework for EEG\-based deep learning models, which effectively enhances the interpretability of deep learning models for depression detection and provides a new perspective for understanding their decision\-making mechanisms\.

## [Multimodal AI refines EAU risk stratification in patients undergoing radiotherapy for prostate cancer](../publications/263269bf100686b014c4.md)

Andrea Camilloni; Chiara Micoli; Ugo Giovanni Falagario; Nita Mulliqi; Erik Everett Palm; Thorgerdur Palsdottir; Kelvin Szolnoky; Xiaoyi Ji; Sol Erika Boman; Andrea Discacciati; Lars Egevad; Henrik Grönberg; Kimmo Kartasalo; Tobias Nordström; Martin Eklund

Abstract The European Association of Urology \(EAU\) risk groups guide treatment decisions in prostate cancer using prostate\-specific antigen \(PSA\), ISUP grade, and clinical stage, but do not incorporate histopathological image information\. We evaluated a locked multimodal artificial intelligence \(AI\) model that integrates routinely available clinical variables \(age, PSA, and ISUP grade\) with deep\-learning features extracted from diagnostic biopsy whole\-slide images for predicting outcomes after radiotherapy \(RT\)\. The model was originally trained to predict biochemical recurrence \(BCR\) following radical prostatectomy and was applied without retraining to 353 patients from the population\-based STHLM3 trial \(ISRCTN84445406\) treated with RT\. Study endpoints included BCR \(Phoenix definition\), high\-risk BCR \(HR\-BCR\), and prostate cancer\-specific mortality \(PCSM\)\. Model performance was assessed using Harrell’s C\-index and cumulative incidence analyses and compared with EAU risk groups\. The continuous AI score showed C\-indices of 0\.65 \(95% CI 0\.55–0\.74\) for BCR, 0\.84 \(0\.72–0\.95\) for HR\-BCR, and 0\.81 \(0\.63–1\.00\) for PCSM, compared with 0\.60, 0\.82, and 0\.80, respectively, for EAU risk groups\. Although paired differences in C\-index between AI and EAU were not statistically significant, adding the continuous AI score to EAU classification improved model fit for BCR, HR\-BCR, and PCSM\. Exploratory AI risk stratification classified 18\.9% of EAU intermediate\-risk patients as AI high\-risk and 28\.2% of EAU high\-risk patients as AI low\-risk\. Within the EAU high\-risk group, patients classified as AI low\-risk \( n = 24\) experienced no BCR events during 10 years of follow\-up, compared with a 10\-year cumulative incidence of 28\.7% \(95% CI 17\.3–41\.2%\) among AI high\-risk patients \( n = 61\)\. These findings suggest that multimodal AI may refine EAU risk stratification by identifying distinct prognostic subgroups within established risk categories, although prospective validation is needed before its potential role in individualized treatment decision\-making can be established\.

## [Strategic Human Resource Management and Institutional Governance: Bridging Policy and Practice in the Gambian Public Sector](../publications/2636debc06864b1fc1b4.md)

Lamin Saidyjeng; Modou Lamin Fatajo

Public sector reforms in The Gambia have emphasized accountability, transparency, and good governance, yet gender disparities and patronage networks continue to undermine merit\-based recruitment and inclusion\. Women hold only 8\.6% of parliamentary seats and 31\.4% of senior management positions, while institutional support for marginalized groups remains inadequate \(Afrobarometer, 2022; Senghore, 2018\)\. Despite constitutional guarantees of equality, non\-discrimination, merit\-based appointments, and equal access to public service under Sections 33, 172, 174, and 220 of the 1997 Constitution, these principles remain insufficiently integrated into human resource management \(HRM\)\. Addressing the gap between constitutional law and strategic HRM, this study analyzes constitutional provisions, public service regulations, and governance practices through normative juridical and institutional approaches\. The findings reveal a gap between formal compliance and substantive implementation in recruitment, promotion, performance management, and leadership development\. The study proposes a constitutional compliance model of strategic HRM, which entails integrating equality, meritocracy, accountability, and transparency into recruitment and promotion, performance management, and leadership development systems\. This study contributes to interdisciplinary literature and provides practical recommendations for public sector reform by redefining constitutional governance as a management framework rather than merely a legal constraint\. The findings highlight the importance of aligning HR strategies with constitutional values to strengthen institutional legitimacy, employee engagement, and long\-term governance stability in emerging democracies\.

## [IMPACT OF CYBER\-SECURE BLOCK CHAIN SYSTEMS ON TRUST, REPAYMENT BEHAVIOUR, AND GOVERNANCE IN MICROFINANCE INSTITUTIONS](../publications/263dcbd9042b507dfc31.md)

Surekha Nadikuda

The study examines the impact of cyber\-secure Block chain systems on borrower trust, loan repayment behaviour, and institutional governance in microfinance institutions\. Using primary data collected from 425 respondents through purposive sampling, the study applied Chi\-square, Pearson correlation, ANOVA, and multiple regression analyses to test the proposed hypotheses\. The findings reveal that cyber security and Block chain transparency significantly enhance borrower trust, improve repayment behaviour, strengthen data protection and user confidence, and promote institutional governance and accountability\. Borrower trust was also found to play a significant mediating role between Block chain adoption and repayment performance\. The study concludes that integrating Block chain with robust cyber security mechanisms can improve transparency, operational efficiency, and the long\-term sustainability of digital microfinance services

## [Sinonasal Inverted Papilloma: Demographics, Recurrence Predictors, and Surgical Outcomes — A 10\-Year Retrospective Review at a Tertiary Center in Saudi Arabia](../publications/263f236173f52f43d683.md)

Ali Jaber Asiry; Majed A\. Alali; Nasir A\. Magboul; Salem A\. Alrasheed; Ibraheem M\. Alkanhal; Mohammed A\. Alabduljabbar; Raid H\. Almadi; Abdullah Saud AlDughaither; Faisal Salahaddin Alfawaz; Ali Majrashi; Saud Alromaih; Ghassan Alokby; Tamadar Aldoheyan

Objectives: To characterize the demographic, clinical, and radiological profile of patients with sinonasal inverted papilloma \(IP\) managed at a tertiary center in Saudi Arabia, to determine recurrence rates in primary versus revision cases, and to identify factors associated with recurrence\.Methods: This retrospective observational study included 59 adult patients with histopathologically confirmed sinonasal inverted papilloma \(IP\)\. Demographic, clinical, radiological, and surgical data were extracted from medical records\. Tumors were staged using the Krouse system\. Patients were stratified into primary or revision cases, and associations with recurrence were evaluated\.Results: Most patients were men \(72\.9%\) and older than 45 \(79\.7%\) years old\. All tumors were unilateral, most frequently arising from the maxillary sinus \(40\.7%\) or lateral nasal wall \(39%\); most were Krouse T2 \(45\.8%\)\. Hyperostosis was present in 52\.5% of cases\. Recurrence occurred in 23 patients \(39%\): 16\.7% in primary cases \(6/36\) and 73\.9% in revision cases \(17/23\)\. All 4 combined endoscopic\-external cases recurred, versus 34\.5% treated endoscopically\. Smoking, Krouse stage, anatomical site, hyperostosis, allergic rhinitis, and malignant transformation were not associated with recurrence\.Conclusion: In this Saudi Arabian cohort, revision status was the dominant correlate of sinonasal IP recurrence, and the surgical approach reflected disease complexity\. These findings support stratified postoperative surveillance and attachment\-oriented surgical planning, particularly for revision surgery\. Outcomes in primary cases were comparable to those reported in a contemporary endoscopic series\.

## [Spatio\-Temporal Analysis of Shoreline Change Along the Machilipatnam Coast Using Landsat Imagery and QGIS](../publications/26440a4822bf6b877240.md)

M\.L\. Sirisha; Subhashish Dey; Seelam Srikanth; G\.T\.N\. Veerendra

Shoreline analysis is an important aspect of coastal studies, as coastlines are continuously influenced by natural processes such as waves, tides, currents, and human activities\. Monitoring these changes is essential for effective coastal management, environmental protection and sustainable development\. This research work focuses on the analysis of shoreline characteristics along the Machilipatnam coast in Krishna District, Andhra Pradesh, using geospatial techniques\. Landsat ETM \+ satellite imagery for the period 2018 to 2022 was used as the primary data source\. The satellite data provides multispectral information with moderate spatial resolution, making it suitable for coastal analysis\. The images were processed using QGIS software, where band combination and colour composite techniques were applied to enhance the visual distinction between land and water features\. A layer stack approach was used to organize raster data for better interpretation\. The shoreline was identified based on textural variations and digitized as a vector line layer\. Additionally, the land and water regions were digitized as polygon layers to enable spatial analysis\. Various GIS tools were used to calculate shoreline length and area measurements, allowing for systematic comparison across multiple years\. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating remote sensing and GIS techniques for shoreline mapping and analysis\.

## [Disproportionality of Depressive Reactions and the Process of Change in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Depression](../publications/264b86f9ecf55711302e.md)

Samuel T\. Murphy; Iony D\. Ezawa; Benjamin J\. Pfeifer; Daniel R\. Strunk

BACKGROUND: The proportionality of depressive reactions to stress was long considered an essential feature of clinical depression\. Although judgments of the proportionality of depressive reactions have been effectively removed in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders \(5th ed\.\), important empirical questions remain about the information that such judgments might convey\. METHODS: In Study One, we tested the factor structure of a brief self\-report measure of disproportionality, the Proportionality of Depressive Reactions\-Self\-Report \(PDR\-S\) and evaluated its relationship with measures of adaptive and maladaptive coping in a sample of 616 undergraduate students\. In Study Two, we evaluated the role of disproportionality in understanding the impact of cognitive change procedures on client&\#x27;s experience of cognitive change\. We evaluated this in a sample of 126 clients participating in CBT for depression\. RESULTS: In Study One, evaluation of the PDR\-S revealed good model fit for a single factor solution\. The PDR\-S was positively related to cognitive reactivity and maladaptive coping responses; it was negatively related to adaptive coping\. Most relations were still significant when neuroticism and depressive symptoms were included as covariates\. In Study Two, disproportionality moderated the relation between cognitive change procedures and cognitive change, with a stronger positive relationship when participants self\-reported a more disproportionate depressive reaction\. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the use of the PDR\-S as a brief measure of disproportionality\. Initial evidence shows that the effect of cognitive change procedures on cognitive change is stronger among those self\-reporting a more disproportionate depressive reaction\.

## [Spatial divergence of climate–vegetation relationships in Florida: A 43\-year multi\-method analysis \(1982–2024\)](../publications/2657d795d7f141a90b2e.md)

Anil Kumar Mandal; Aman Kumar Thapa; Madan Thapa Chhetri; Hongbo Su; Yan Yong; Fred Bloetscher

Abstract Attributing long\-term vegetation change to climate is difficult in subtropical ecosystems, where temperature and precipitation act simultaneously, are confounded by abrupt disturbances, and where statewide averages can conceal offsetting associations\. Here we apply a multi\-method convergence\-of\-evidence framework to a sensor\-harmonized 43\-year record \(1982–2024\) of NOAA CDR NDVI, temperature, and precipitation across Florida, which spans cool temperate forests to warm subtropical wetlands\. Modified Mann–Kendall tests with false\-discovery\-rate correction detected monotonic trends; pixel\-level correlation, spatial\-error regression, and lagged cross\-correlation evaluated association strength, direction, and timing; Empirical Orthogonal Function decomposition of deseasonalized anomalies separated persistent climatic signals from episodic disturbance, with the leading mode \(58\.4% of variance\) tracking latitudinal warming and a lower\-order mode \(PC3\) tracking hurricane impacts\. Florida warmed by \+0\.033 °C yr⁻¹, significant in 99\.6% of land pixels, while precipitation showed no field\-significant trend\. The temperature–greenness association was positive across essentially the entire state, marginally stronger in the south; localized negative responses were confined to specific southern wetland and urban\-fringe pixels rather than forming a systematic north–south reversal\. The state\-mean precipitation–NDVI correlation was negative at zero lag and reversed from r = −0\.263 to r = \+0\.102 when incoming shortwave radiation was partialed out, consistent with cloud\-associated light suppression rather than water limitation—a phenomenon we term the Water Paradox\. SPI/SPEI–NDVI correlations were near zero, and Everglades water levels were largely decoupled from wetland greenness \(r = 0\.08, n\.s\.\), indicating that inundation acts as a localized threshold modifier rather than a dominant suppressor\. Climate–vegetation models for comparable high\-rainfall subtropical systems may therefore need to account for spatially divergent temperature sensitivities and treat precipitation as an energy constraint rather than a uniform benefit\.

## [Evolution of guideline\-based male infertility responses by large language models between 2025 and 2026: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Perplexity, and DeepSeek](../publications/26586bcb2691f6ac859d.md)

Burak Elmaağaç; Ali Yasin Ozercan; Murat Demir; Murat Gül

RéSUMé: CONTEXTE: Les grands modèles de langage \(LLM\) sont de plus en plus utilisés par les patients et les cliniciens pour obtenir des informations médicales, mais leurs performances peuvent évoluer au fil du temps à mesure que les modèles sont mis à jour\. L&\#x27;infertilité masculine est un domaine étroitement encadré par des recommandations, dans lequel des informations inexactes ou incomplètes peuvent influer sur l&\#x27;évaluation diagnostique, le conseil aux patients et les attentes thérapeutiques\. Cette étude a évalué l&\#x27;évolution, entre 2025 et 2026, des performances de ChatGPT, Perplexity et DeepSeek dans leurs réponses à des questions sur l&\#x27;infertilité masculine élaborées à partir de recommandations cliniques\. RéSULTATS: Au total, 528 réponses de chatbots ont été évaluées à partir de 88 questions sur l&\#x27;infertilité masculine issues des recommandations de l&\#x27;Association européenne d&\#x27;urologie \(EAU\), auxquelles ChatGPT, Perplexity et DeepSeek ont répondu en 2025 et en 2026\. En 2025, des différences significatives entre les modèles ont été observées dans les quatre domaines évalués: Perplexity a obtenu les meilleurs scores pour la qualité du contenu et l&\#x27;évaluation par les experts, tandis que DeepSeek affichait les performances les plus faibles\. En 2026, les scores DISCERN ont convergé entre les modèles, alors que des différences significatives persistaient en matière de lisibilité, de score global de qualité et d&\#x27;avis des experts\. ChatGPT s&\#x27;est significativement amélioré dans les quatre domaines évalués et a obtenu le meilleur score global de qualité en 2026\. DeepSeek a enregistré l&\#x27;amélioration la plus marquée, notamment pour les scores DISCERN et d&\#x27;avis des experts\. La lisibilité des réponses de Perplexity s&\#x27;est améliorée, mais cette évolution ne s&\#x27;est pas accompagnée d&\#x27;une amélioration parallèle du score global de qualité ni de l&\#x27;utilité clinique évaluée par les experts\. Des risques potentiels pour la sécurité des patients ont été relevés dans sept des 88 réponses fournies par DeepSeek en 2025, tandis qu&\#x27;aucun risque de ce type n&\#x27;a été constaté dans les réponses de 2026\. Aucune des 528 réponses ne contenait de recommandation explicite considérée comme susceptible de causer un préjudice immédiat ou grave aux patients\. CONCLUSIONS: Les performances ont évolué selon des modalités propres à chaque modèle, plutôt que de manière uniformément progressive\. Les résultats correspondent à un échantillon de réponses obtenues lors d&\#x27;une première interrogation à des questions clairement formulées et dérivées de recommandations, plutôt qu&\#x27;à des estimations robustes des performances ou de la reproductibilité des modèles\. Les grands modèles de langage \(LLM\) peuvent faciliter l&\#x27;accès aux informations sur l&\#x27;infertilité masculine, mais une vérification auprès de sources faisant autorité et une supervision humaine appropriée demeurent nécessaires\.

## [SDN\-Driven Bandwidth Allocation for Federated Learning of Driving Policies Across Autonomous Vehicle Swarms](../publications/265f67f785caa5e5fa37.md)

Maryam Jasim  Mohammed

This paper presents a joint bandwidth allocation and federated learning optimization framework for Software\-Defined Networking \(SDN\)\-assisted autonomous vehicular networks\. The framework addresses challenges such as dynamic channel conditions, mobility\-induced fading, and heterogeneous data by minimizing convergence bounds, latency, and energy consumption while maximizing fairness\. Using a multi\-objective optimization approach and Gaussian Process Regression for mobility prediction, the model enables proactive, channel\-aware resource management\. Three solvers—Sequential Quadratic Programming \(SQP\), Interior Point, and Active Set—are evaluated, with the Interior Point method showing the best performance in convergence and efficiency\. This work lays the foundation for future research into more complex resource management strategies in SDN\-enabled vehicular networks\.

## [Genetic evidence for the psychosis continuum: polygenic score analysis](../publications/26660840ca1430521945.md)

Senta M\. Haussler; Diana Pinto Prata; Matthew J\. Kempton; Vishal Bhavsar; Ryan Arathimos; Jonathan R\. I\. Coleman; Lucia Valmaggia; Stefania Tognin; Gemma Modinos; Paolo Fusar‐Poli; Diego Quattrone; Jim van Os; Bart P\. F\. Rutten; Gerome D\. Breen; Marta Di Forti; Craig Morgan; Cathryn M\. Lewis; Matthew H\. Hotopf; Philip K\. McGuire; Robin M\. Murray; Evangelos Vassos

Background The psychosis continuum conceptualises psychotic phenomena as existing on a spectrum from subclinical experiences to psychotic disorders\. Despite epidemiological and clinical evidence in support of this model, few studies have examined polygenic liability across the severity continuum: from subclinical experiences to first\-episode psychosis \(FEP\)\. Aims To map polygenic liability for schizophrenia \(SCZ\), bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder \(MDD\) across the psychosis continuum\. We hypothesised that schizophrenia polygenic scores \(SCZ\-PGS\) would track phenotypic severity most closely across this continuum\. Method We harmonised data from 5 south\-east London cohorts \( N = 1315; 860 European, 455 African ancestries\) across 4 ordered groups indicative of different levels of phenotypic severity: controls \( n = 647\), individuals with self\-reported psychotic experiences \( n = 89\), individuals at clinical high risk \(CHR\) that did not convert to psychosis \( n = 124\) and individuals with FEP \( n = 455\)\. We computed ancestry\-specific PGS for SCZ, bipolar disorder and MDD and compared these across groups using ordinal logistic regression\. Results In European ancestry participants, elevated SCZ\-PGS \(odds ratio 1\.72, p = 4\.57 × 10 −15 \), bipolar disorder\-PGS \(odds ratio 1\.56, p = 1\.03 × 10 −10 \) and MDD\-PGS \(odds ratio 1\.44, p = 4\.86 × 10 −8 \) were individually associated with increasing phenotypic severity\. SCZ\-PGS explained the largest variance \( R 2 = 0\.084\) across the psychosis continuum and showed pairwise differences between CHR and controls \( β = 0\.32, p = 0\.027\), and between FEP and CHR \( β = 0\.38, p = 0\.017\)\. Multivariable models, combining three PGS, outperformed univariable models \( R 2 = 0\.105\)\. Similar trends in SCZ\-PGS across the psychosis continuum phenotype were seen in African ancestry participants, but only controls and FEP groups differed significantly \( β = 0\.27, p = 0\.037\)\. Conclusions Our findings provide biological evidence supporting the psychosis continuum framework\. In European ancestry, SCZ\-PGS differences suggest that CHR who do not transition to psychosis have intermediate genetic vulnerability\. Multivariable models, utilising all three PGS, explained additional variance compared with univariable ones, supporting transdiagnostic genetic liability\. Improving PGS predictive power in African ancestry remains a priority\.

## [The pedagogical impact of AI\-Assisted idea generation on self\-efficacy and idea development skills in general foundation program students&\#x27; research\-based essay](../publications/266d8c8dd8cb350e3886.md)

Ahoud Yaqoob Al\-Kuwaili; Sheema Amtul Hai

Foundation Program students often struggle to generate research ideas and organise their thoughts when writing research\-based essays, which can undermine their confidence and academic performance\. Traditional assessment methods provide limited insight into students&\#x27; independent development of ideas\. However, recent advances in educational technology, particularly Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), offer new opportunities to support learning\. This study aims to investigate the pedagogical impact of AI\-assisted idea generation on General Foundation Program \(GFP\) students&\#x27; self\-efficacy and idea\-generating skills in research\-based essay writing\. The study adopts a quantitative research design using a single\-group pre\-test and post\-test approach\. The sample consists of 25 randomly selected GFP students\. The intervention is conducted over a period of 4\-6 weeks\. Students use ChatGPT as their primary AI tool for brainstorming, outlining, and refining ideas\. Students&\#x27; self\-efficacy is measured based on a structured questionnaire, while idea development skills are assessed through a writing rubric\. Data is analysed using paired\-sample comparison\. The results indicate improvement in both self\-efficacy and idea development\. The study highlights the importance of integrating AI tools into writing instruction to enhance student confidence and performance\.

## [Bayesian optimization\-driven machine learning for compressive strength prediction of hybrid fiber\-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete](../publications/267b1b1befe124b43ee6.md)

Li Chengjin; Runrun Dong; Jawad Tariq; Eugene Henry Rushema; Muhammad Awais Hussain; Muhammad Akbar; Masamba Pinto

The use of recycled coarse aggregate \(RCA\) in concrete provides a sustainable approach to reducing construction and demolition waste, but predicting its compressive strength \(CS\) is challenging due to complex interactions among binder composition, supplementary cementitious materials \(SCMs\), fibers, and mix proportions\. This study develops and compares seven Bayesian optimization \(BO\) based machine learning \(ML\) models to predict the CS of hybrid fiber\-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete \(HFRRAC\)\. A dataset of 281 experimental samples with 14 input variables, including OPC, FA, GGBS, water content, aggregate proportions, and fiber characteristics, was used for model training and evaluation\. Performance was assessed using R 2 , RMSE, MAE, and MAPE\. The results show that ensemble and boosting methods outperform the conventional approaches evaluated in this study\. On the held\-out testing subset, the best\-performing BO\-GP\-GBQR model achieved a training R 2 of 0\.9959 and a testing R 2 of 0\.9348, with a testing RMSE of 3\.5675 MPa, MAE of 2\.4883 MPa, and MAPE of 8\.03%\. SHAP analysis identified water content, OPC, and GGBS as the most influential parameters\. The proposed framework enables accurate and interpretable prediction of 28\-day CS and can support preliminary mixture screening for HFRRAC containing recycled coarse aggregate and hybrid fibers\.

## [Structural characterization and biological activity of 3,4\-dihydroxy\-1,6\-bis\(3\-methoxyphenyl\)hexa\-2,4\-diene\-1,6\-dione \(DBMPD\) isolated from vegetable seeds](../publications/267d95f587ec5b8c5950.md)

Venkatadri Babu; J Irshad Ahamad; Suriya Rehman; Irfan Ahmad Rather

The increasing demand for the production and consumption of vegetables as part of a balanced diet has resulted in significant plant\-based waste rich in phytochemicals, which has recently gained attention for its potential use as innovative ingredients in food, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals\. The current study presents the isolation and characterization of 3,4\-Dihydroxy\-1,6\-bis\(3\-methoxyphenyl\)hexa\-2,4\-diene\-1,6\-dione \(DBMPD\) from vegetable seed waste for evaluating its biological efficiency and applications\. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of DBMPD was performed through Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy \(FT\-IR\), UV\-Vis, and NMR techniques in conjunction with Gaussian 09 computation software\. Ground state molecular geometry, vibrational modes, and electronic orbital characteristics were derived through density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations employing the Becke, 3\-parameter, Lee\-Yang\-Parr \(B3LYP\) exchange\-correlation functional paired with the 6\-311\+\+G\(d,p\) basis set\. The resulting computational data were further applied to map the energy profile and evaluate the chemical reactivity descriptors of DBMPD\. In vitro antimicrobial activity of DBMPD was observed, with zones of inhibition of 17\.3±0\.5 mm and 19\.6±1\.1 mm against Proteus mirabilis \. Additionally, the compound demonstrated significant 2,2\-diphenyl\-1\-picrylhydrazyl \(DPPH\) scavenging activity \(21\.8±0\.6% to 45\.4±1\.5%\) at a concentration of 10µg/mL \( p = 0\.0079 \) and H 2 O 2 scavenging activity ranging from 22\.8±1\.6% to 45\.4±1\.5% at concentrations of 10µg/mL and 50µg/mL, respectively \(p=0\.005 , p&lt;0\.0001 \)\. Regarding antidiabetic effectiveness, DBMPD exhibited substantial glucosidase inhibitory activity at all concentrations \( p&lt;0\.001 \)\. Lastly, in silico molecular docking analysis, employing AutoDock software, revealed a binding free energy of −5\.6 Kcal/mol and a computed inhibition constant \(Ki\) of 77\.7347 M\. These docking outcomes confirm that DBMPD forms a stable complex with the 3S35 breast cancer target protein, highlighting its prospective value as a lead molecule in anticancer drug development\. Moreover, the observed antibacterial and antidiabetic activities highlight the potential of the bio/vegetable waste for applications in the pharmaceutical sector\.

## [Factors influencing future liver remnant hypertrophy after portal vein embolization: a mini review](../publications/2680693dae8057d1b5e7.md)

Yuxuan Lu; Hangcheng Liu; Boyang Wu; Canhong Xiang; Jianping Zeng; Quanyu Guo; Hongwei Lu; Shizhong Yang; Jitao Wang; Jiahong Dong

Background Portal vein embolization \(PVE\) promotes future liver remnant \(FLR\) hypertrophy before major hepatectomy, but the response varies substantially among patients\. This review summarizes determinants of post\-PVE FLR hypertrophy to support preoperative risk stratification and individualized planning\. Methods Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure \(CNKI\) through 26 August 2026 combined terms for PVE, liver regeneration or FLR hypertrophy, and predictors or associated factors\. Reference lists and the authors’ existing reference collection were also screened, and evidence was narratively synthesized across five domains\. Results FLR hypertrophy reflects multiple interacting determinants\. Advanced age, selected chemotherapy exposures, and liver fibrosis have been associated with weaker regenerative responses\. Elevated inflammatory markers and biliary infection may impair hypertrophy, whereas adequate embolization extent and appropriate embolic material selection may improve the response\. Conclusion FLR hypertrophy after PVE is determined by interacting demographic and clinical, laboratory, hepatic and biliary, tumor\-related, and procedure\-related factors\. Recognizing these determinants may improve patient selection, help predict insufficient hypertrophy, and guide individualized PVE strategies to increase the safety of major hepatectomy\.

## [Beyond Points and Badges: How Mobile\-Based Gamification Drives Multidimensional Engagement to Improve Learning Outcomes in Engineering Education](../publications/268997fc435bcd4bbcc7.md)

Jonni Mardizal; Doni Tri Putra Yanto; Herlin Setyawan; Stefanos Balaskas; Soha Rawas; Firas Tayseer Ayasrah

Gamification and mobile\-based learning have become popular innovative approaches in education\. However, empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness in engineering education, particularly in electrical engineering, remains fragmented, with a critical gap in understanding the mediating mechanisms through which gamification drives outcomes in this uniquely demanding context\. This study examines the impact of mobile\-based gamification \(MobGam\) on learning engagement \(LE\) and learning outcomes \(LO\) among electrical engineering students\. Research data were collected through standardized questionnaires from 121 students and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The results demonstrate that the Usage Intensity of MobGam \(UI\) has a positive and significant effect on all dimensions of students’ LE, namely Behavioral Engagement \(BE\), Cognitive Engagement \(CE\), and Emotional Engagement \(EE\)\. UI also positively associated with LO, as measured by perceived learning effectiveness \(PLE\) and perceived academic performance \(PAP\)\. Moreover, LE mediates the relationship between UI and LO\. Crucially, EE emerged as the strongest mediating pathway, underscoring the paramount importance of affective factors in overcoming the cognitive demands of engineering coursework\. Specifically, EE showed the most substantial mediating effect on PLE \(β = 0\.326\) and PAP \(β = 0\.314\)\. These findings extend beyond electrical engineering education by providing evidence that emotionally resonant gamification is associated with higher persistence and more positive perceived LO, particularly in contexts with high cognitive load\. This study offers a theoretically grounded, empirically validated model that redefines the success of educational gamification in electrical engineering education, shifting focus from mere usage to the cultivation of deep, emotionally resonant engagement\.

## [The Digital–Circular Economy Nexus in Supply Chains: Trends, Themes, and Insights from a Scientometric Perspective](../publications/269332012eafc93cab6a.md)

Muhammad Shoaib; Rongjian Yu; Hassan Ali; Muhammad Taha; Shoaib Ali

The growing urgency for sustainability in global supply chains, spurred by increasing demand, environmental degradation, and resource scarcity, has intensified academic and industrial focus on adopting circular economy \(CE\) principles\. Recently, digital technologies have become key enablers of this shift, facilitating improved supply chain resilience, efficiency, and environmental outcomes\. This study addresses a critical gap in the literature by systematically exploring the convergence of digitalization, supply chain management, and the circular economy\. A scientometric analysis of 628 peer\-reviewed articles published between 2010 and 2025 offers a comprehensive mapping of the intellectual structure and evolution of knowledge in this field\. The findings reveal a marked acceleration in publication volume in 2025 compared with previous years, particularly in journals focusing on environmental sustainability and technological innovation\. Citation and network analyzes indicate that China dominates research output, whereas the United Kingdom and India exhibit higher citation impact, reflecting their intellectual prominence in the field\. Content analysis reveals four core thematic clusters: the technological influence of digital tools such as blockchain, the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and machine learning; strategic approaches to strengthening supply chain resilience; emerging opportunities and innovation potential; and real\-world industrial deployment across various sectors\. These themes collectively underscore a growing scholarly consensus on the integrative role of digital technologies in advancing circular economy goals within supply chain systems\. By tracing the evolution of research and highlighting key authors, journals, and thematic trends, this study offers critical insights for both academia and industry\. This study is grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory \(DCT\), which explains how organizations purposefully identify opportunities, seize them, and reconfigure resources to sustain competitive advantage\. It provides a strategic foundation for practitioners to evaluate digital maturity and align technological adoption with circular\-economy objectives\. Ultimately, this study highlights the transformative role of digitalization in integrating circular principles into global supply chains, offering deeper insights into sustainable value creation in the digital era\.

## [Digital Empathy Scale: A Validity and Reliability Study](../publications/269ca70456373fcd8738.md)

Abdullah Yıldırmaz

Online communication platforms now constitute one of the principal arenas of interpersonal exchange; constraints on nonverbal signaling, asynchronous turn\-taking, and varying degrees of anonymity together reshape how individuals interpret others&\#x27; states and decide whether to act on them\. The present research developed and examined the psychometric properties of the Digital Empathy Scale \(DES\), a 12\-item instrument intended to capture empathic orientation in online contexts, using a sequential three\-phase design\. In the first phase \(N = 300\), a 29\-item pool was submitted to principal axis factoring; the analysis returned a one\-factor solution explaining 45\.6% of the total variance \(KMO = \.892; Bartlett χ²\(66\) = 1464\.63, p &lt; \.001; factor loadings \.57–\.68\)\. In the second phase \(N = 417\), confirmatory factor analysis on an independent sample supported the proposed structure \(CFI = \.945; TLI = \.928; RMSEA = \.072; SRMR = \.050\) and yielded external validity evidence \(general empathy r = \.599; digital well\-being r = \.367; social desirability r = \.164; α = \.929; split\-half r = \.871\)\. In the third phase \(N = 80\), the scale exhibited substantial temporal stability across a two\-week interval \(r = \.817, p &lt; \.001\)\. Taken together, the findings provide convergent psychometric evidence supporting the DES as a sound instrument for assessing empathy within digital communication settings\.
