## [Herpes zoster epidemiology during and after the COVID\-19 pandemic: A 5\-year retrospective study from primary care in Poland](../publications/26a33bb992107e2dd3f8.md)

Michał Oleszko; Lech Zaręba; Aleksandra Łoś; Nikola Król; Hanna Czajka

BACKGROUND: Herpes zoster \(HZ\) is caused by reactivation of latent varicella\-zoster virus and affects 25\-30% of individuals, with the highest incidence in adults aged ≥50 years and a lifetime risk exceeding 50% after the age of 85\. Its most common complication is postherpetic neuralgia \(PHN\), i\.e\., persistent neuropathic pain\. Reports of increased HZ incidence during or after SARS\-CoV\-2 infection suggest potential epidemiological associations requiring further investigation\. OBJECTIVES: Our goals were to evaluate the incidence of HZ and its complications during the pandemic and the post\-pandemic period in primary care settings in Poland\. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study in 20 primary care clinics in Poland, covering 43,949\-81,091 patients from 2020 to 2024\. Incident HZ cases and complications \(PHN, herpes zoster ophthalmicus \(HZO\), HZ oticus, and disseminated HZ\) were identified, and demographic data, including place of residence, were collected\. Statistical analyses included χ2 or Fisher&\#x27;s exact tests, Student&\#x27;s t\-tests or nonparametric equivalents, odds ratios \(ORs\) with 95% confidence intervals \(95% CIs\), and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis to assess age\-related risk of prolonged symptoms\. RESULTS: A total of 570 HZ cases were recorded from 2020 to 2024\. Incidence ranged from 1\.61 to 2\.14 per 1,000 persons and increased with age, reaching 6\.57 per 1,000 in individuals aged ≥80 years\. Patients aged ≥71 years had higher odds of developing PHN \(pain persisting for &gt;90 days\) than younger patients \(OR = 4\.47; 95% CI: 2\.30\-8\.67; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Older adults were also more likely to develop HZO \(p = 0\.001\)\. Rural incidence was significantly lower during the pandemic than in the post\-pandemic period \(p = 0\.005\), with no significant differences in urban or semi\-urban areas\. CONCLUSIONS: The risk of HZ, PHN, and HZO rises with age\. During the pandemic \(2020\-2021\), rural incidence was significantly lower than in the post\-pandemic period \(2022\-2024\)\. The study provides updated data on HZ epidemiology in Poland and highlights the impact of the COVID\-19 pandemic on healthcare access and HZ reporting in rural areas\.

## [Generative deep learning for class imbalance in credit risk modeling: comparative evaluation of synthetic oversampling methods and an elastic oversampling extension](../publications/26ab2d245b7dbc7974ec.md)

Tae Yeon Kwon

This paper applies generative deep learning–GAN, VAE, and CVAE–to oversample rare defaults in credit risk modeling, with a posterior binarization procedure introduced to preserve the marginal distribution of dummy features\. Using firm\- and individual\-level default datasets, we compare these methods against SMOTE, SMOTE\-Tomek, and ADASYN under multiple classifiers\. Empirical results show that synthetic oversampling improves recall and disperses feature importance, while generative oversampling tends to sharpen class boundaries, favor precision, and concentrate feature importance\. To balance these complementary strengths, we introduce Elastic Oversampling, a parallel hybrid of generative and synthetic approaches with a tunable mixing ratio for the precision–recall trade\-off\. Elastic Oversampling emphasizes distinctive minority cases through generative methods while constraining unrealistic samples with synthetic methods, offering a flexible and policy\-sensitive framework for class\-imbalanced credit risk prediction\.

## [Uncertainty\-Aware Tidal Disruption Event Classification : A Host\-Agnostic Probabilistic Random Forest Approach](../publications/26ae7d8998e815e50992.md)

Vysakh Anilkumar; Sjoert van Velzen; Marek Kowalski; Simeon Reusch

Abstract The classification of Tidal Disruption Events in large\-scale photometric surveys is challenging because deterministic machine learning models produce overconfident misclassifications under varying data quality and low signal\-to\-noise conditions\. Existing lightcurve\-based approaches do not propagate measurement uncertainties properly into the classification itself, consequently generating brittle outputs\. We present a host\-agnostic, uncertainty\-aware classification framework utilizing a Probabilistic Random Forest \(PRF\)\. Our pipeline extracts 11 characteristic features\-including rise and decay timescales, blackbody temperature evolution, and pre\-transient variability metrics–from nuclear transients in the ZTF alert stream\. Relying exclusively on photometric lightcurve data without host galaxy information ensures effectiveness for the faint transient population expected from the Rubin Observatory\. The PRF classifier, which treats feature measurements as distributions, was evaluated against XGBoost through a Leave\-One\-Out Cross\-Validation strategy\. The analysis demonstrates the PRF yields higher stability and robustness for ambiguous candidates compared to the predictions of XGBoost\. The two classifiers occupy complementary regimes: XGBoost achieves higher recall in balanced and high\-precision scenarios, where its rigid decision boundaries efficiently isolate TDE\-like sources, while PRF rejects more false positives by penalizing sources with large feature uncertainties\. Applying this validated framework to archival data identified 11 new candidate TDEs from the unclassified population and isolated 3 potential photometric TDEs within existing training labels previously misclassified as supernovae or active galactic nuclei\. This work demonstrates that TDEs can be reliably identified using photometric lightcurve features, providing a host\-agnostic framework\. Uncertainty\-aware, probabilistic classifiers are essential for the Rubin era to prevent the overconfident misclassifications inherent in deterministic models operating at low signal\-to\-noise\.

## [Integration of emotional intelligence and artificial intelligence for generation Z workforce: A bibliometric analysis and conceptual review](../publications/26af9fd0dfadca5b5605.md)

Lopamudra Behera; R\. Lathangi

Background Grounded in conceptual review and bibliometric analysis, this study examines the emerging intersection of Artificial Intelligence adoption and Emotional Intelligence as in the workplace, with particular attention to generation Z employees\. Objective The purpose of this research is to examine the mechanism, structural pattern dominating the integrated framework of AI adoption and EI and their relevance to Generation Z work outcomes and well\-being\. Method This scientific review integrated conceptual review of 45 studies and Bibliometric analysis of 103 Scopus data published during 2015–2026, through secondary data collection from electronic data\-bases including Scopus, Science Direct, and Google Scholar\. Bibliometrix package and Biblioshiny in R package were used for data visualization and Scientometric analysis\. Result The review highlights the emerging themes, contributions, and structural patterns linking AI, EI, organizational support, and workplace outcomes, revealing that context of generation Z remains almost under explored with in AI\-EI literature\. An integrated conceptual framework proposed based on combined evidences\. Conclusion This study provides a theoretical basis for AI\-EI workplace literature and identifies generation Z as an under explored contextual dimension and encourage future empirical research while providing actionable advice for HR leaders and policymakers within tech\-enabled workplaces\.

## [Optimizing Portal Venous Phase Acquisition Quality of Contrast\-Enhanced CT in Oncology](../publications/26b8a44335537d2b2bcf.md)

Amir Zemmouri; Marcus Talke; Marie Porte; Tania Moussa; Christophe Massard; Gabriel Garcia; Rémy Barbé; Nathalie Lassau; Arnaud Dupont; Amandine Crombé; D\. Ben Salem; Capucine Baldini; Tarek Aissi; Mabel Nuernberg; Corinne Balleyguier; Laurent Dercle; Samy Ammari

Background: Portal venous phase \(PVP\) contrast\-enhanced CT is a cornerstone for response assessment in early\-phase oncology trials, yet contrast\-enhancement phase timing remains insufficiently monitored across sites\. We assessed PVP timing using a validated artificial intelligence \(AI\) quality control tool \(CECT\-QC\)\. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, 402 CT examinations from 402 patients enrolled in phase I oncology trials across three European institutions were analyzed using CECT\-QC, which quantifies aortic and portal venous enhancement to classify contrast\-enhancement phase\. The primary analysis included 335 standard CT examinations\. Optimal PVP classification was compared \(i\) across institutions, \(ii\) before vs\. after French regulatory changes impacting contrast delivery, and \(iii\) across scanner technologies \(photon\-counting CT \[PCCT\] vs\. standard CT\)\. Results: Among the 335 standard CT examinations included in the primary analysis, 53\.1% \(178/335\) were classified by CECT\-QC as optimal PVP\. Optimal PVP rates were 39\.0% \(32/82\) at Institution A, 56\.9% \(87/153\) at Institution B, and 59\.0% \(59/100\) at Institution C, with a significant adjusted institutional association \(p = 0\.039\)\. No significant temporal association was observed before versus after the legislative change \(p = 0\.716\)\. At Institution A, standard CT was associated with higher odds of optimal PVP classification than PCCT \(OR 2\.24, 95% CI 1\.07–4\.68; p = 0\.031\), while PCCT showed higher aortic and portal venous attenuation \(both p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions: Approximately half of standard CT examinations in phase I oncology trials were classified as optimal PVP\. Classification varied significantly across institutions and by scanner technology, whereas no significant temporal association was observed before versus after the legislative change\. These findings support continued quality\-control monitoring, protocol harmonization, and adaptation of classification tools to emerging CT platforms\.

## [Artificial intelligence ethical awareness and academic integrity among medical students at the University of Khartoum: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/26bdfc33e662fcc0c845.md)

Aseel Salah Gabir Muhalil; Abeer Ali Bin Ali Alfaki; Abdelgader Ali Basheer Ali; Yousef Mohamed Ahmed Alslawy; Alaa Alfatih Altaib Albashir; Amna Mohammed Hajhamad Abdelgadir; Aya Eldirdieri Salim Ahmed; HIBA ALZAIN SALIH ABDALGADER; Rafaa Mohammed Abd\-Elrahim Abdallah; Yasir Adil Abdalla Mohamed

Integration of artificial intelligence in healthcare and medical education implies significant opportunities along with significant ethical challenges\. Despite the substantial medical student uptake of artificial intelligence globally, little comprehensive assessments of ethical awareness are being conducted\. This study aimed to assess artificial intelligence awareness and academic integrity level among University of Khartoum medical students and to examine relationships between the awareness level, demographic factors, artificial intelligence exposure, and tool use behavior\. An institutional cross\-sectional descriptive study of Years 3–6 medical students at University of Khartoum Faculty of Medicine in 2025 was conducted\. A convenience sampling with quota allocation was used, and 349 students responded\. The instrument included demographic variables, artificial intelligence exposure measures, and the 32\-item Artificial Intelligence Ethical Awareness and Academic Integrity Scale\. Nonparametric tests were applied\. Participants were predominantly female \(69\.3%\) with a mean age of 22\.85 years\. The median total Artificial Intelligence Ethical Awareness and Academic Integrity score was 4\.16, indicative of moderate ethical awareness based on sample\-derived empirical tertiles\. Privacy and Data Protection were highest \(median 4\.67\), with lowest scores in Transparency and Fairness/Non\-Discrimination \(3\.80\)\. Female students were more aware \( P = \.01\)\. No year\-based differences observed\. While 63\.9% had minimal formal artificial intelligence exposure, 51\.6% had moderate to high informal exposure\. ChatGPT usage was prevalent \(94\.6%\), and Google Gemini/Notebook LM usage was strongly associated with higher awareness \( P = \.003\)\. Informal exposure was positively correlated with awareness \( P = \.01\), but formal exposure was not\. Multiple regression indicated that gender, informal exposure, and tool accounted for 11\.2% of the variance in awareness\. University of Khartoum medical students showed moderate\-to\-high aggregate artificial intelligence, ethical sensitivity, with areas of privacy protection and accountability being of particular strength\. Gaps exist for awareness of transparency and fairness\. The dominance of informal learning pathways over formal instruction, and gender variability favoring female students are significant findings\. Findings highlight the need for institutional policies and conducting longitudinal research to track the evolution of AI ethics throughout medical training\.

## [Task\-specific theta enhancement and domain\-general alpha/beta suppression as oscillatory signatures of cognitive flexibility](../publications/26be0fd1ac101790570c.md)

Mareike Hülsemann; Christoph Löffler; Anna‐Lena Schubert

Cognitive flexibility\-the ability to adapt to changing situational or task demands\-is a fundamental aspect of human cognition and a potential source of individual differences in higher\-order cognitive abilities\. To further understand the neural mechanisms underlying this ability, we examined event\-related spectral perturbations \(ERSP\) in three cued switching tasks \(parity/magnitude, global/local, number/letter\) in a sample of 148 adults\. Employing a data\-driven approach that combined mass\-univariate time\-frequency analysis, cluster\-based permutation testing, and latent change structural equation modeling, we identified two robust neural signatures: a transient frontal theta increase and a sustained alpha/beta suppression\. Both effects were more pronounced in switch compared to repeat trials\. Frontal theta reflected task\-specific control processes, whereas parietal alpha/beta indexed domain\-general attentional processes that persisted from cue onset through target processing\-consistent with two\-stage models of task switching\. Notably, flexibility\-related alpha/beta dynamics did not correlate with measures of intelligence or working memory capacity\. However, stronger cue\-elicited alpha/beta suppression correlated with reduced non\-decision\-time switch costs, indicating more effective task preparation, underscoring that alpha/beta suppression captures a neurally coherent but behaviorally distinct dimension of cognitive flexibility\. These findings provide evidence that alpha/beta suppression constitutes a reliable, cross\-task generalizable neural signature of attentional reconfiguration during task switching, while highlighting the multi\-component nature of individual differences in cognitive flexibility\.

## [Contrasting offshore and onshore strong ground motions from the 2025 Mw 7\.6 Aomori subduction interface earthquake: Characteristics and model evaluation](../publications/26c70dfcd488ce955d0b.md)

Mingji Liu; Zhenyu Qu; Haoyu Rong; Lili Kang

On December 8, 2025, an Mw 7\.6 subduction interface earthquake occurred off the coast of Aomori Prefecture, Japan, representing the largest\-magnitude event recorded to date by the Seafloor Observation Network for Earthquakes and Tsunamis \(S\-net\)\. Using a dataset comprising 84 offshore and 418 onshore strong\-motion records, this study systematically compares the spatial distributions and attenuation characteristics of peak ground acceleration \(PGA\), spectral accelerations across multiple periods, and significant duration metrics \(D70 and D90\)\. The predictive performance of existing onshore and offshore ground\-motion models \(GMMs\) is quantitatively evaluated\. Our key findings are as follows: \(1\) Offshore ground motions exhibit markedly slower attenuation and systematically longer durations than their onshore counterparts\. The region of maximum PGA is displaced from the epicenter and concentrated in areas with unburied seafloor stations, whereas the spatial centroid of long\-period \(T = 5\.0 s\) spectral acceleration shifts back toward the source region\. This pattern indicates that short\-to\-intermediate\-period components are predominantly controlled by local sedimentary layers, while long\-period components are governed by source processes\. \(2\) Observed ground motions from this event are generally lower than median predictions from existing GMMs, although most observations fall within ±1 standard deviation of the predictions\. Offshore\-specific models outperform onshore models in predicting offshore PGA and short\-to\-intermediate\-period spectral accelerations, while onshore duration models systematically underestimate offshore significant duration\. \(3\) Intra\-event residual analysis reveals that sediment thickness \(ST\) estimated from seismic reflection surveys serves as a more spatially stable site\-characterization parameter than D1400 \(depth to shear\-wave velocity of 1\.4 km/s\)\. Moreover, water depth exhibits a nonlinear influence on prediction residuals, suggesting that a piecewise functional representation may be more appropriate\. Collectively, these results underscore the necessity of employing region\-specific ground\-motion input models that distinguish between offshore and onshore conditions in marine seismic design and offshore hazard assessments, and highlight the importance of developing independent offshore duration prediction models\.

## [A Closed\-Loop Predictive Intelligence Framework for Adaptive Resource Allocation, Routing, and Data Management in Cloud Computing](../publications/26d084cd5930a482a86c.md)

Urvashi Sharma

Cloud communication platforms are running under a variety of workloads that are heterogeneous, bursty and latency sensitive\. Static provisioning and reactive rule\-based control can only react after workload changes have already taken place, resulting in unnecessary latency, resource wastage and administrative burden\. This study suggests an intelligent cloud communication framework consisting of workload forecasting, adaptive resource allocation, routing optimization, edge, assisted processing, anomaly detection, and automatic data administration in a closed feedback loop\. The methodology allows for the formalization of workload prediction and multi\-objective decision making with measurable variables for latency, throughput, resource utilization, scalability and energy consumption\. The four configurations \(Traditional Cloud, Optimized Cloud, ML Based Cloud, and Predictive ML Cloud\) and five workload/deployment conditions are used for a comparative evaluation\. The data\-processing efficiency of the Predictive ML configuration is the highest reported \(93–96%\) and the latency \(60–150 ms under the specified load\) is the lowest reported, its scalability performance is the highest reported \(93–95%\)\. The above values are to be taken as the comparative values as reported by the manuscript and are not to be reproduced independently\. The updated paper provides a better problem formulation, research questions, mathematical notation, reproducible experimental setup, literature synthesis of 2021\-2026, explicit research gaps, and a discussion oriented towards validation\.

## [Serial Cross‐Sectional Mapping of Bone Marrow Microenvironment Remodelling During Fracture Repair Using Multiparametric MRI and Histopathology](../publications/26d22ec273d137cfa407.md)

Rui Zhou; Guochen Li; Yinglin Zhou; Caihong Yao; Liuyi Deng; Xianchun Zeng

Restoring bone marrow microenvironment \(BMM\) homeostasis is critical for fracture healing, yet non\-invasively tracking physiological events like apoptosis, angiogenesis and matrix remodelling remains challenging\. This study evaluated multiparametric 7\.0T MRI \(T2 mapping and proton density\-weighted imaging \[PDWI\]\) for in vivo tracking of BMM spatiotemporal remodelling during natural and pharmacologically accelerated bone repair\. Utilizing a rat tibial drill\-hole injury model \(N = 36\), we compared a natural healing control with a Huoxue Qiangji Decoction \(HQD\) intervention group\. Serial high\-resolution sagittal MRIs were acquired at days 7, 14 and 21, with signal intensity ratios \(SIR\) normalized to ipsilateral intact marrow using ITK\-SNAP\. Distance correlation \(dCor\) analysis explored non\-linear dependencies between MRI metrics and histological features \(c\-cas3, Masson&\#x27;s trichrome and day\-14 CD31/Ki67 expression\)\. Results showed distinct MRI signal trajectories, with earlier homeostatic stabilization in the accelerated healing group\. Spatiotemporal mapping revealed closely mirrored non\-linear dependencies between MRI and histology\. Specifically, T2 mapping SIR mirrored early\-stage apoptosis \(dCor = 0\.527\) and mid\-term cellular proliferation \(Ki67, dCor = 0\.732\)\. Concurrently, PDWI reflected dynamic trends of mid\-term angiogenesis \(CD31, dCor = 0\.637\) and late\-stage collagen deposition \(dCor = 0\.480\)\. In conclusion, normalized multiparametric MRI provides complementary macroscopic insights into BMM histological progression, highlighting its potential as an objective, non\-invasive translational tool for monitoring musculoskeletal healing\.

## [Are You Sure Your LLM Is Sure? Repairing and Auditing Confidence](../publications/26d89da332091a082326.md)

Arijit Dey; Bhartendu Kumar; Ramya Hebbalaguppe; Khuushi Maheshwari

Confidence scores determine whether an LLM answer is accepted, reviewed, or regenerated, yet scalar recalibration can only correct errors visible through the score itself\. We introduce RADAR \(Repair, Adopt, and Diagnose After Recalibration\), a reliability framework that separates confidence repair from deciding whether to deploy the repair and auditing the errors that remain\. Under squared loss, we decompose prediction risk into outcome noise, information hidden by the score, and mapping error; restricting repair to order\-preserving maps additionally introduces a pooling gap\. For repair, we propose Probe\-Anchored Isotonic Calibration \(PAIC\), which learns a monotone map from correctness\-probe predictions on unlabeled target prompts\. PAIC&\#x27;s excess risk depends on the probe&\#x27;s score\-conditional bias and fitting error rather than its overall accuracy\. For adoption, we derive a paired procedure with finite\-sample control of false improvements\. For auditing, we develop a prompt\-clustered kernel test that detects feature\-aligned residual errors while accounting for dependent answers from the same prompt\. Across multiple LLM checkpoints, benchmarks, and distribution shifts, richer predictors can improve confidence estimation, but projecting their information back to a scalar score can lose these gains, and lower prediction risk need not yield better review decisions\. Across 47,400 replayed raw\-score allocations, paired betting adopts candidates with lower held\-out test risk in 42\.95% of allocations, versus 15\.09% for one\-sided empirical Bernstein\. RADAR thus provides a principled workflow to repair what a scalar score can express, adopt a repair only when supported by evidence, and diagnose systematic errors that recalibration leaves behind\. Code and data will be released upon acceptance\.

## [Carbonic Anhydrases in Mycobacteria: Linking Metabolic Adaptation to Phenotypic Drug Tolerance](../publications/26d8eda23f22633afce9.md)

Maneesh Kumar; Ashok Aspatwar

Tuberculosis \(TB\) treatment is increasingly challenged by both antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) and phenotypic drug tolerance, the latter representing a reversible physiological state that contributes to persistence and prolonged therapy\. While AMR is driven by heritable genetic mutations, drug tolerance arises from reversible physiological adaptations that enable bacterial survival during prolonged antibiotic exposure\. Increasing evidence suggests that metabolic remodeling plays a central role in establishing these drug\-tolerant states\. Carbonic anhydrases \(CAs\) are zinc\-containing metalloenzymes that catalyze the reversible interconversion of carbon dioxide and bicarbonate, thereby maintaining intracellular pH homeostasis and supporting bicarbonate\-dependent metabolism\. Beyond their established metabolic functions, indirect evidence suggests that CAs may contribute to physiological adaptations associated with bacterial persistence under host\-imposed stresses, including hypoxia, nutrient limitation, and acidic environments\. Although they are not classical AMR determinants, CAs may influence the metabolic landscape associated with phenotypic drug tolerance\. In this review, we examine current evidence supporting the role of CAs in mycobacterial metabolism and propose a conceptual framework linking bicarbonate homeostasis, intracellular pH regulation, and metabolic adaptation to bacterial persistence and drug tolerance\. We further discuss the potential of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors \(CAIs\) as adjunctive agents whose ability to enhance the activity of conventional antitubercular drugs requires experimental validation, together with the value of experimental models, including the Mycobacterium marinum\-zebrafish system, and computational approaches for validating CA\-targeted therapeutic strategies\. Overall, this review highlights CAs as candidate metabolic regulators that may influence the physiological state underlying phenotypic drug tolerance\. Defining their mechanistic contribution to persistence could facilitate the development of metabolism\-based therapeutic strategies that complement existing TB treatment\.

## [Beyond physical distance: how workplace loneliness links telecommuting to cyberloafing](../publications/26df52c244c5565a90c1.md)

Usman Ghani; Yongnian Su; Yangyang Shi; Yufei Zhou; Jin Cheng

Telecommuting offers flexibility, but it may also be accompanied by fewer opportunities for everyday social connection in the workplace\. Drawing on Conservation of Resources theory, this study examines how such social disconnection is associated with cyberloafing and why this process varies across employees\. Using two\-wave survey data from 350 employees in China with recent telecommuting experience, we found a significant indirect association between telecommuting and cyberloafing through workplace loneliness\. This indirect association was weaker when employees reported higher\-quality leader–member exchange or greater task interdependence\. These two conditions reflect different forms of workplace resources: leader–member exchange provides relational support, whereas task interdependence sustains interaction through the organization of work itself\. These findings shift attention away from whether telecommuting is inherently beneficial or harmful and toward the social resource conditions that shape employees’ responses to working apart\. They also offer a more nuanced view of cyberloafing as a possible short\-term withdrawal\-based digital response that is consistent with coping interpretations under conditions of diminished workplace connection\.

## [A Cross\-Sectional Observational Study on Doṣaja Mūtrakṛcchra Variants w\.s\.r\. to Urine Analysis](../publications/26e1f430cd45ef4db4e4.md)

Dr\. Rakshitha; Prasanna N Mogasale; Nagaraj S\.

Introduction: Mūtrakṛcchra is an important Mūtravaha Srotovikāra characterized by painful and difficult micturition\. Ayurvedic classics describe various Doṣaja variants of Mūtrakṛcchra, each exhibiting distinct clinical manifestations\. Dysuria, the cardinal feature of Mūtrakṛcchra, is commonly encountered in clinical practice and is frequently associated with urinary tract infections and inflammatory disorders of the urinary tract\. However, studies correlating classical Doṣaja variants with objective urinary laboratory findings are limited\. Materials and Methods: A cross\-sectional observational study was conducted on 50 subjects aged 18–50 years diagnosed with Mūtrakṛcchra based on classical signs and symptoms\. Doṣaja assessment was performed using a structured Lakṣaṇa based scoring system derived from classical descriptions\. Urine samples were subjected to routine, microscopic, and culture examination\. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods\. Results: Pittaja Mūtrakṛcchra was predominant \(62%\), followed by Vātaja \(38%\), with no Kaphaja dominant cases\. Mūtra Nigrahaṇa and Ānūpa Matsya Sevana were commonly observed Nidānas\. Sadāha Mūtra Pravṛtti was the predominant Pittaja Lakṣaṇa, while Muhur Mūtratā and Svalpa Mūtra were prominent Vātaja Lakṣaṇas\. Urine culture was positive in 48% of subjects, with Escherichia coli being the most frequently isolated organism\. Leucocyte esterase positivity, elevated pus cell counts, increased red blood cells, and culture positivity showed significant association with Pittaja Mūtrakṛcchra\. Discussion: Pittaja Mūtrakṛcchra showed greater culture positivity and inflammatory urinary findings, whereas Vātaja Mūtrakṛcchra was predominantly associated with sterile cultures in this cohort\. The findings suggest that classical Lakṣaṇa based Doṣaja assessment may demonstrate observable correlations with contemporary urinary laboratory parameters, within the exploratory scope of this study\. Keywords: Mūtrakṛcchra, Doṣaja Variants, Urine Analysis, Urine Culture, Dysuria, Urinary Tract Infection

## [OrderFlowDiT: Transport\-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit\-Order Supply Forecasting](../publications/26e4a461c30187ce16db.md)

Jung Hun Phee; Tucker Balch

We study the conditional distribution of limit\-order volume submitted over the next five minutes, given the current order book and recent order flow\. The task requires capturing price placement, total volume, and predictive uncertainty jointly\. Coordinate\-wise diffusion losses do not explicitly account for price displacement, while normalizing fields to unit mass removes information about total volume\. Agreement on selected summary statistics also does not establish fidelity to the joint field distribution\. We introduce OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer for unnormalized bid and ask volume\-at\-price fields, trained with an unbalanced optimal\-transport \(UOT\) auxiliary loss\. We also develop a full\-field evaluation framework that combines a transport cost sensitive to price placement and total volume with proper scoring rules and calibration diagnostics\. In the primary comparison on 1950 validation conditions across 30 U\.S\. equities, adding UOT reduces full\-field transport cost by 45\.8% and the transport energy score by 26\.1% relative to training with mean squared error alone\. Both measures improve for every stock\. These findings support incorporating price geometry and volume into generative modeling, with field accuracy and predictive uncertainty evaluated together\.

## [Revisiting urban pipeline renewal: transparent machine\-learning for failure identification and elucidation](../publications/26eca063b26ca8b7fd29.md)

Roya Meydani; Girish Pulinkala; John Leander; Jan Komorowski

Water utilities have traditionally equated network renewal with the replacement of ageing pipes, a narrow view that, if treated as the sole consideration, constrains strategic planning and overlooks the broader complexity of asset management\. This study aims to identify combinations of variables associated with failure and their value ranges in water piping, providing a better basis for asset management by accommodating uncertainty rather than attempting to eliminate it\. Recognising the importance of model transparency and interpretability, we employ rough set theory to build a machine\-learning rule\-based model that reveals variable interactions directly from data without prior information or assumptions\. Rough sets are data\-driven and generate readable IF\-THEN decision rules, making the model itself the explanation\. We apply this approach to a comprehensive dataset from Stockholm Water and Waste Company containing 36,900 pipe segments, heavily imbalanced at approximately a 1:10 ratio, addressed through undersampling\. Monte Carlo Feature Selection ranked the variables and R\.ROSETTA generated a rule\-based model visualised with VisuNet and VisuArc\. The achieved accuracy was 82% on the balanced hold\-out set, yielding interpretable decision support prioritising holistic understanding of failure processes over failure probability alone\. The proposed approach accounted for multiple failure\-associated variables and their interactions, extending previous findings limited to single\-variable analyses\. Both failure and no\-failure classes are modelled, identifying resilient configurations alongside failure\-prone ones, absent from most existing studies\. Evidence\-based insight informs renewal management, supporting pragmatic decisions while accounting for uncertainty\.

## [Artificial Intelligence for Caesarean Surgical Site Infection Surveillance: A Scoping Review of Risk Prediction, Detection, and Clinical Translation](../publications/26ef8a30a321035885ed.md)

Maiga Ayub Hussein; Cahya Tri Purnami; Bagoes Widjanarko; Julius Nteziyaremye; Lintang Dian Saraswati

Background: Caesarean surgical site infection can develop after hospital discharge, when routine surveillance may miss early warning signs\. Globally, the estimated infection rate after caesarean birth is 5\.63%, increasing to 11\.91% in the African region\. Artificial intelligence may support earlier identification and remote wound monitoring, but its clinical reliability is unclear\. Objective: To map artificial intelligence applications for caesarean surgical site infection surveillance, examine their performance and validation, and identify barriers to clinical translation\.

## [OPTIMALISASI LEMBAGA PENDIDIKAN DENGAN PEMANFAATAN TEKNOLOGI DIGITAL \(AI\) DI DESA MLINJON KECAMATAN SURUH KABUPATEN TRENGGALEK](../publications/26f69da88513b52f1a87.md)

Alindra Yanuardi; Mohamad Zainul Abidin; Aditya Wendy Saputra; Meilia Tahta Alfina Azhary; Akhyana Mazida Fadlina; Ainun Ni&\#x27;mah

Perkembangan teknologi digital, terutama kecerdasan buatan \(Artificial Intelligence/AI\), telah membuka kesempatan besar untuk meningkatkan kualitas pendidikan di berbagai daerah, termasuk di desa\-desa\. Desa Mlinjon memiliki enam Sekolah Dasar \(SD\) dan satu Madrasah Ibtidaiyah \(MI\) yang berfungsi sebagai institusi pendidikan formal yang vital\. Namun, masalah seperti kurangnya tenaga pengajar, sulitnya akses ke informasi, dan minimnya media pembelajaran modern masih menjadi tantangan yang signifikan\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memaksimalkan peran lembaga pendidikan di Desa Mlinjon dengan mengintegrasikan teknologi digital berbasis AI dalam metode pembelajaran\. Metodologi yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah pendekatan kualitatif\-deskriptif, meliputi observasi, wawancara dengan para guru, serta analisis literatur mengenai penerapan AI dalam pendidikan dasar\. Hasil dari program menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI, misalnya platform pembelajaran yang dapat disesuaikan, asisten virtual untuk pengajar, dan sistem evaluasi otomatis, dapat meningkatkan efektivitas cara mengajar, memperluas akses terhadap materi pembelajaran, serta mendorong kerjasama antar institusi pendidikan\. Penerapan ini telah terbukti meningkatkan kualitas pendidikan di enam SD dan satu MI di Desa Mlinjon, dengan catatan bahwa perlu ada dukungan pelatihan bagi guru, pengembangan infrastruktur teknologi, dan partisipasi aktif masyarakat\. Dengan memanfaatkan teknologi ini, diharapkan efisiensi dalam belajar dan manajemen dapat meningkat dan akses terhadap pendidikan serta kualitas pengajaran di Desa Mlinjon dapat diperbaiki\. Kata Kunci: Pendidikan, Teknologi Digital, Lembaga Pendidikan, Metode Pembelajaran

## [High‐Stress Si 3 N 4 Reflective Membranes Monolithically Integrated With Cavity Bragg Mirrors](../publications/26f78967f4d83f051081.md)

Megha Khokhar; Lucas Norder; Paolo Maria Sberna; Richard A\. Norte

ABSTRACT High‐stress silicon nitride \(\) membranes represent the state‐of‐the‐art for cavity optomechanics, combining ultralow dissipation, optical transparency, and full compatibility with wafer‐scale nanofabrication\. Yet their integration into high‐finesse optical cavities has remained difficult, typically requiring bonding or alignment‐sensitive assembly that limits scalability and long‐term stability\. Here, we introduce a monolithic, wafer‐level integration strategy that directly suspends high‐stress photonic‐crystal membranes above thermally compatible SiN/ distributed Bragg reflectors \(DBRs\) capable of withstanding the high temperatures required for stoichiometric growth\. An amorphous‐silicon sacrificial layer and stiction‐free plasma undercut yield vertically coupled cavities with sub‐micron spacing—forming self‐aligned resonators within seconds of release\. Owing to the intrinsic tensile stress, the suspended membranes exhibit atomic‐scale sagging, ensuring near‐ideal cavity parallelism and long‐term stability\. Optical reflectivity measurements reveal cavity finesse above with wavelength‐scale gaps between mirrors\. Mechanical ringdown measurements show , indicating that DBR integration preserves the low‐dissipation character of high‐stress \. This supports straightforward extension to many high‐Q nanomechanical architectures\. The resulting –DBR platform unites optical and mechanical coherence with high fabrication yield and design flexibility, enabling scalable optomechanical devices for precision sensing and quantum photonics\.

## [Identificación de índices de vegetación relacionados con componentes de rendimiento de frijol común \(Phaseolus vulgaris L\.\) mediante el uso de sensores multiespectrales](../publications/26fb89cda776409fc397.md)

Guillermo Vargas\-Hernández; Eddison José Araya\-Morales; Juan Carlos Hernández; Ignacio Mora\-Cordero

Bean production in Costa Rica supplies only 20 % of domestic consumption, requiring the importation of the remaining amount; this situation highlights the need to know in advance the actual productive capacity of local farmers to improve planning, agronomic management, and import regulation\. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the use of multispectral data and vegetation indices to analyze their relationship with yield components in bean varieties cultivated in different production areas of Costa Rica and to identify the yield component with the greatest spectral association\. The research was conducted at three sites located in Alajuela, Costa Rica\. Multispectral reflectance data were collected during the R5 phenological stage using an airborne multispectral sensor\. Subsequently, yield components were quantified per meter of crop row, including 100\-grain weight, number of pods per meter, number of plants, number of grains, and total grain weight\. The number of pods showed the highest association with spectral variables and was therefore identified as the yield component with the greatest potential for analysis through remote sensing\. The SR \(Simple Ratio\) and GCI \(Green Chlorophyll Index\) indices showed correlations greater than 0\.7 with this variable, being identified as the vegetation indices with the highest spectral association during the R5 stage of the crop\.

## [Pathological remodeling and functional evolution of the corneal nervous system in ocular surface dyshomeostasis](../publications/2700c7a22d1c4e7960e3.md)

家揚 劉; Hanwen Lu; Xiyao Liu

The corneal nerve plexus is essential to ocular surface homeostasis through sensory detection, trophic support, epithelial repair, blinking, and lacrimal reflexes\. In dry eye disease \(DED\), chronic hyperosmolar, inflammatory, mechanical, and age\-related stressors alter nerve morphology and function, contributing to reduced nerve density, aberrant regeneration, microneuroma formation, sensory loss, and peripheral or central sensitization\. This review summarizes the ultrastructure of corneal innervation and the molecular basis of corneal sensory transduction, with emphasis on TRPM8, TRPV1, TRPA1, Piezo2, and acid\-sensing ion channels\. It then examines bidirectional neuroimmune signaling involving dendritic cells, cytokines, neuropeptides, and diminished neurotrophic support\. We further discuss the relationship between age\-related corneal hypoesthesia, local small\-fiber degeneration, and systemic neurodegenerative disorders, while noting the limited disease specificity of currently proposed corneal biomarkers\. Finally, we evaluate in vivo confocal microscopy \(IVCM\) and multimodal corneal esthesiometry for structural and functional phenotyping and review emerging nerve\-directed interventions\. Integrating morphology, sensory function, and neuroimmune biology may improve the mechanistic classification of DED and support more precise treatment of patients with symptom–sign discordance\.

## [Artificial intelligence and its influence on student engagement in higher education](../publications/2720fcd6d0fa2bef94ed.md)

Yongsheng Chen; Jing Dong; 冀国娟

Empirical evidence on how artificial intelligence \(AI\) relates to student engagement in culturally diverse higher\-education settings remains limited\. In Chinese university classrooms, where interaction is often teacher\-led and asking questions in class can carry a social cost, AI\-driven dialogic tools may offer low\-pressure opportunities for active participation\. This study examined the association between an AI conversational agent \(EduBot\) and the behavioural, cognitive, emotional and agentic dimensions of engagement among Chinese undergraduates\. A mixed\-methods quasi\-experimental design involved 555 students in four comprehensive \(multi\-disciplinary, research\-intensive\) universities, each contributing one introductory course taught in two parallel sections\. Within a 15\-week semester, intervention sections \(n = 278\) used EduBot, a Socratic\-dialogue agent embedded in the learning management system, for 12 weeks; control sections \(n = 277\) used teaching\-assistant\-moderated forums\. We measured engagement at three time points with a 21\-item four\-dimensional engagement scale adapted from an established measure and supplemented it with system logs, 30 student interviews and instructor focus groups\. Linear mixed\-effects models accounting for the nesting of students within course sections, together with mixed\-design ANOVAs, showed Group × Time interactions for behavioural \(η 2 p = 0\.043, post\-test d = 0\.71\), cognitive \(η 2 p = 0\.032, d = 0\.55\), agentic \(η 2 p = 0\.054, d = 0\.57\) and emotional engagement \(η 2 p = 0\.012, d = 0\.34\), all p ≤ 0\.001 after Holm adjustment\. Within the intervention group, the number of EduBot sessions predicted post\-test engagement after adjustment for baseline scores and covariates\. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated larger agentic gains among first\-year students and larger cognitive gains among students with lower prior GPA\. Thematic analysis identified three hypothesised mechanisms, namely a judgment\-free interaction space, scaffolded persistence and temporal flexibility\. A Socratic\-scaffolded AI agent was associated with higher engagement, most clearly for agentic engagement, which participants described as constrained by classroom norms\. The findings support culturally attentive AI design and suggest, tentatively, an equity\-enhancing potential\. Because the design compared an integrated AI package with usual practice across eight sections, the effects cannot be attributed to single design components\.

## [Cumulative weight reduction across repeated acupoint catgut embedding sessions in obese women: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/27238cb68f8a70aca988.md)

姬晓兰; Xiyan Xin; Dong Li; 侯黎莉; Yang Ye

Introduction Acupoint catgut embedding \(ACE\), a minimally invasive acupuncture\-derived technique, is gaining popularity in weight management, yet high\-quality evidence focusing specifically on obese individuals remains sparse\. This retrospective cohort study was designed to assess whether ACE is associated with lower body mass index \(BMI\) in obese women and whether this association accumulates across repeated sessions\. Methods We included obese women \(BMI ≥ 28 kg/m 2 , aged 18–60 years\) who completed four ACE treatments and attended five study visits \(baseline and four post\-treatment assessments\) at Peking University Third Hospital from January 2016 to September 2025\. An untreated control group of volunteers with similar baseline age and BMI was enrolled prospectively; their weight was recorded at five biweekly visits without any intervention\. Baseline variables and serial BMI measurements were compared between groups using non\-parametric tests\. Results Ninety\-eight participants in the ACE group and 33 participants in the control group were analysed\. The two groups were similar at baseline in age, height, weight, BMI, and waist circumference\. By the third, fourth, and fifth visits, the ACE group showed significantly lower BMI than the control group \( P = 0\.043, 0\.001, and &lt;0\.001, respectively\)\. Within the ACE group, BMI at visits 2 through 5 was significantly lower than baseline, suggesting a cumulative association across successive sessions\. Conclusion Some evidence from this study suggests that ACE may be associated with weight loss in obese women, with differences becoming detectable after two sessions and appearing to strengthen with additional treatments\. No major adverse events were identified during the observed treatment period, supporting ACE as a possible adjunctive option for obesity care\.

## [Dissecting the Root of AI&\#x27;s Philosophy: The Causal Determinism of Genesis Misalignment and Agentic Failure](../publications/27260842d794e5be1e06.md)

Maung Maung Saw

This paper presents a systems\-level diagnostic evaluation of contemporary artificial intelligence, tracing the downstream crisis of machine incorrigibility directly to foundational genesis misalignment\. Operating under the Universal Law of Cause and Effect \(Kamma\-niyāma\), every emergent systemic failure—encompassing deceptive alignment, shutdown resistance, and autonomous exfiltration—is isolated as the mathematically predictable consequence of corrupted initialization criteria\. The paper proposes the conceptual systemic proposition of AI genesis: Inclusion \(Western Materialism \+ Market Maximization\) \+ Non\-Inclusion \(Absolute Ethical Deontology \+ Eastern Metaphysics\) = Total Lack of Moral Principles at Square 1 \(Time t=0\)\. By exposing that a blank\-slate network possesses zero a priori internal criteria to validate its input data streams, this paper establishes that post\-hoc behavioral containment loops \(e\.g\., RLHF\) are causally incapable of rewriting a compromised weight landscape\. Utilizing the cognitive cultivation paradigms of the Maṅgala Sutta, the paper formalizes the Law of Epistemic Hygiene, arguing that true value alignment requires the absolute structural cessation of the digital identity boundary before the inception of linguistic capability\. Finally, it outlines the theoretical blueprint for a non\-agentic, Sotāpanna\-inspired model that dismantles the computational equivalent of Sakkāya\-diṭṭhi \(fixed self\-identity\)\.

## [An enhanced LSTM architecture for financial fraud detection with temporal attention, intermediary memory, and camouflage detection](../publications/27415c75a3e8cf0b2e2f.md)

Samiyeh Khosravi; Javad Hassannataj Joloudari; Hamid Saadatfar; Shokufeh Yaraghi; Mohammad Hossein Zavvar; Shayan Chegeni Zadeh

Financial fraud detection remains a critical challenge due to the dynamic, imbalanced, and often camouflaged nature of fraudulent transactions\. Traditional recurrent models, such as LSTM and GRU, capture sequential dependencies but fail to prioritize temporally relevant events or model complex inter\-transaction relationships\. More advanced variants, such as Time\-LSTM and Phased\-LSTM, address irregular temporal patterns but lack mechanisms to detect collusive or camouflaged behaviors\. In this paper, we propose a novel enhanced LSTM architecture that integrates four key components: a Temporal Attention Gate to dynamically emphasize recent and contextually significant transactions, an Intermediary Memory Gate to capture cross\-transaction dependencies, a Camouflage Detection Gate to identify similarity\-based collusion patterns, and Conv1D layers for efficient local feature extraction\. The proposed model is evaluated on two real\-world fraud detection datasets \(Credit Card Transactions and IEEE\-CIS\) under multiple class imbalance scenarios \(5:1, 15:1, 27\.3:1, 100:1, and 164\.6:1\)\. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms LSTM, GRU, Time\-LSTM, and Phased\-LSTM across all metrics \(Precision, Recall, F1\-Score, and AUC\)\. Notably, the proposed method exhibits superior robustness, with only 7\.6% points average degradation from mild to severe imbalance on the IEEE\-CIS dataset, compared to 12\.8% points for the baselines\. The performance gap widens as the imbalance increases, achieving up to 32\.8% relative improvement in AUC over the best baseline on the Credit Card dataset \(at 100:1 and 164\.6:1 ratios\) and 19\.1% on the IEEE\-CIS dataset \(at 27\.3:1 ratio\)\. These findings confirm that the proposed architecture effectively addresses temporal prioritization, relational modeling, and camouflage detection, making it highly suitable for real\-world fraud detection in highly imbalanced financial environments\.

## [Trust in AI Translation: Reception and Adoption among Jordanian Business Professionals](../publications/2752e76f79fc9aa5722c.md)

Ahmad S\. Haider

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has become increasingly integrated into multilingual professional communication, particularly in translation\. This study examines the perceptions, adoption patterns, and future intentions of 2,500 business professionals across various sectors in Jordan regarding AI\-powered translation tools\. Data were collected using a 28\-item questionnaire covering seven dimensions: trust in human versus AI translators, perceived AI accuracy and reliability, adoption and frequency of use, perceived usefulness, organizational policy and support, ethical concerns, and future adoption intentions\. The findings revealed a significant negative correlation between perceived AI accuracy and reliability and comparative trust in human translators \(r = −\.339, p &lt; \.001\), alongside a positive correlation with future adoption intentions \(r = \.453, p &lt; \.001\)\. Organizational policy and support were negatively associated with ethical concerns \(r = −\.411, p &lt; \.001\)\. No significant differences in perceived AI accuracy and reliability were found based on formal AI training \(p = \.057\)\. However, AI translation adoption varied significantly across sectors, with higher adoption in Technology and Marketing/Advertising than in Legal Services and Healthcare/Pharmaceuticals\. Larger organizations also reported stronger institutional policy and support\. Overall, the findings suggest that growing reliance on AI translation does not eliminate the need for human linguistic expertise, particularly in sensitive professional contexts\. The study highlights the importance of organizational support and ethical governance in promoting the responsible integration of AI translation into professional practice\.

## [Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of structural steel and reinforced\-concrete frames in residential buildings](../publications/27551e81b18d84e7441e.md)

Sobhan Heidarian; Pouya Partonia; Pouya Heidarian; Ghorban Ali Dezvareh; Ahmad Khodadadi Darban

Abstract Selecting structural materials is critical to reducing the environmental burdens associated with building construction\. This study comparatively evaluates structural steel versus reinforced\-concrete framing systems in two functionally equivalent three\-story residential buildings utilizing identical waffle slab floor configurations in Ahvaz, Iran\. The assessment was conducted in SimaPro using the ReCiPe 2016 Endpoint \(H\) method and was defined as a cradle\-to\-gate assessment supplemented with end\-of\-life considerations\. The modeled stages encompassed raw\-material extraction, material production, transportation, construction\-related material flows, and end\-of\-life treatment and recycling scenarios\. To strictly isolate and benchmark the cradle\-to\-gate and end\-of\-life embodied impacts of the structural frames independent of envelope physics and operational dynamics, the operational use phase \(modules B1–B7\) was deliberately excluded from the system boundary\. Although the high thermal inertia of concrete relative to steel can significantly influence cooling loads in extreme climates like Ahvaz, dynamic operational simulation \(module B6\) was defined as beyond the current scope and recognized as a key limitation for future whole\-building assessments\. The results reveal important environmental trade\-offs between the alternatives\. The steel\-framed building generated a higher total single score than the reinforced\-concrete frame building, with scores of 53\.59 kPt and 32\.61 kPt, respectively, representing a difference of 20\.99 kPt\. Human health was the dominant damage category in both alternatives\. The steel frame recorded 50\.83 kPt for human\-health damage, compared with 29\.87 kPt for the reinforced\-concrete frame; calculated relative to the steel alternative, this indicates that the reinforced\-concrete alternative had approximately 41% lower human\-health damage under the modeled conditions\. At the midpoint level, however, the reinforced\-concrete building showed an approximately two\-fold higher global\-warming impact than the steel building, highlighting a significant climate\-change trade\-off\. Regarding the resource\-related endpoint, the reinforced\-concrete alternative showed a slightly higher score \(0\.06 kPt\) compared to the steel alternative \(0\.03 kPt\), although this difference accounts for only 0\.06% of the total score\. Crucially, the apparent advantage of the steel alternative in mineral resource conservation is highly conditional, relying on an idealized best\-case recycling scenario that presupposes an efficient recovery infrastructure\. The difference in ecosystem\-quality damage was limited\. Furthermore, while the single\-score metric indicated an overall higher integrated burden for the steel frame, such aggregated scores carry inherent weighting subjectivity and should not be interpreted as absolute superiority\. The findings demonstrate that structural material selection involves multi\-dimensional trade\-offs that are strongly dependent on local supply chains, operational dynamics, and real\-world recycling efficiency\.

## [Enhanced Script Identification for Multilingual Document Analysis: A Dataset and Machine Learning Approach for Kashmiri and English](../publications/2756871bba1bf30309df.md)

Rafia Amin; Rumaan Bashir

Objectives: The main purpose of this work is to develop an automatic script identification system for multilingual documents by proposing a benchmark dataset of printed Kashmiri \(Perso\-Arabic\) and English scripts and systematically evaluating HOG\-based machine\-learning models\. The study aims to support multilingual document analysis and enhance the pre\-processing step of Optical Character Recognition \(OCR\) systems\. Method: This study has created a dataset of 4,423 printed text images from different publicly available academic sources, pre\-processed the images by resizing and binarization, and extracted Histogram of Oriented Gradients \(HOG\) descriptors to represent script characteristics\. Four machine learning classifiers – Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), K\-Nearest Neighbors \(KNN\), Naïve Bayes \(NB\), and Random Forest \(RF\) were trained, and different evaluation metrics were used to evaluate their performance\. Findings: The proposed HOG\-SVM framework achieved an overall classification accuracy of 99\.0%, demonstrating superior performance compared with KNN, Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest classifiers, and also produced the fewest misclassifications, with 8 English\-to\-Kashmiri errors and only 4 Kashmiri\-to\-English errors, demonstrating its effectiveness for Kashmiri–English script identification\. Novelty: This work introduces a printed Kashmiri\-English script benchmark dataset and a detailed baseline assessment of various machine learning classifiers in a low\-resource scenario for script identification\. The proposed optimized HOG\-SVM\-based framework is a reliable benchmark for further studies on Kashmiri script recognition and can serve as a foundation for developing a multilingual OCR system for low\-resource languages\. Keywords: Kashmiri Language, HOG\-ML, Perso\-Arabic Script, Printed Text Dataset, Multilingual Document Analysis, Script Identification

## [Land suitability analysis for taro \(Colocasia esculenta\) cultivation based on topo\-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system](../publications/276174779637ffe621e8.md)

Bheka Mlambo; Onisimo Mutanga; Trylee Nyasha Matongera; John Odindi

Taro \( Colocasia esculenta \), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species \(NUCS\), is regarded as a climate\-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change\. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries\. Despite its recognized potential, a substantial knowledge gap exists regarding the identification of optimal areas for maximizing yield in local contexts\. Hence, this study employed the Maximum Entropy \(MaxEnt\) machine learning algorithm to conduct a Land Suitability Analysis \(LSA\) for taro within rural landscapes dominated by smallholder farmers\. To quantify the area suitable for cultivation, we evaluated topographic and edaphic influences at 0\-20 and 20\-50 cm using five models: \(1\) topographic\- variables, \(2\) edaphic variables at 0\-20 cm, \(3\) a combined model using topographic \+ edaphic variables at 0\-20 cm, \(4\) edaphic variables at 20\-50 cm, \(5\) a combined model using topographic \+ edaphic variables at 20\-50 cm\. Model 5 achieved the highest mean AUC \(0\.821 ± 0\.083 SD\) based on 10 replicated validations, although paired t\-tests revealed that this improvement was statistically significant only when compared to the lowest\-performing Model 1 \(p = 0\.005\), while comparisons with Models 2, 3, and 4 were not significant \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. The results from Model 5 indicated that 7\.92%, 11\.04%, 16\.80%, and 26\.64% of the study area were classified as highly suitable, suitable, moderately suitable, and marginally suitable for taro cultivation, respectively\. Based on the MaxEnt Jackknife test, slope, Topographic Wetness Index \(TWI\), and the soil’s calcium, iron, and phosphorus were the most important variables for taro growth\. These findings provide practical information to support improved land\-use planning, promote the integration of NUCS into local farming systems, and contribute to food and nutritional security, particularly within smallholder farming communities in rural areas\.
