## [DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real\-World Autonomous Driving](../publications/2767107ad667922a9320.md)

Wei Wang; Yiru Veronika Wang; Yihan Wang; Zihao Li; Xiaohui Liang

Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources\. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving\. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements\. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation\. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance\. Action conditioned future prediction and risk sensitive planning connect this representation to driving decisions\. Its offline component reconstructs recorded scenes using neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting, then expands long tail conditions using generative models while restricting the use of generated content as geometric ground truth\. We specify data partitioning, sensor ablations, fault injection, paired closed loop testing, and real to simulation consistency assessment\. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence management can reduce dangerous false free space predictions and occlusion risk within a matched computational budget while retaining acceptable driving efficiency\. All performance claims remain subject to experimental validation\. Keywords: autonomous driving; 3D occupancy; sensor fusion; uncertainty; generative world models; NeRF; 3D Gaussian Splatting; closed loop simulation

## [Predictive Analytics for Diabetes Detection Using Advanced Machine Learning Models](../publications/27891d9aab93b5056231.md)



Despite its prevalence, diabetes can be managed and even reversed if caught in its early stages\.Using the dataset&\#x27;s precise diagnostic characteristics, we train a model for determining the likelihood of a patient receiving diabetes\.After that, we investigate several options for enhancing the model&\#x27;s precision and efficiency\.In this piece, logistic regression is utilized extensively, and the analysis is carried out using Python IDEs\.The experiment&\#x27;s primary data sources are a Vanderbilt dataset derived from a study of African Americans living in rural Virginia and NIDDK&\#x27;s PIMA Indians Diabetes dataset\.Two distinct methods exist for selecting functions\.The icing on the cake is that we use aggregation techniques, which boost performance by making more precise predictions with a single model\.We provide the accuracy and runtime of both the original datasets and datasets created later using feature selection and aggregation algorithms\.Also included with each case is a comparison\.Applying the aggregation strategy Maximum Voting yielded an accuracy of approximately 78% for dataset 1\.When maximum polling and stacking were applied together, the accuracy for dataset 2 reached a peak of around 93%\.Among the most effective algorithms for building predictive models is logistic regression\.

## [Notch signalling governs human enteric nervous system progenitor dynamics](../publications/279fe3017650ca830dc4.md)

Antigoni Gogolou; Nikolas Stefanidis; Fay Cooper; Guillaume Blin; Stanley E\. Strawbridge; Alexander George Fletcher; Anestis Tsakiridis

The enteric nervous system \(ENS\) is the main branch of the peripheral nervous system that innervates the gastrointestinal tract controlling vital functions\. It arises during embryogenesis via migration, proliferation and differentiation of neural crest\-derived ENS progenitors\. Perturbation of these processes, caused by mutations in key signalling pathway components and transcription factors, prevents progenitor colonisation of the distal gut causing aganglionic phenotypes and enteric neuropathies such as Hirschsprung \(HSCR\) disease\. While animal models implicate Notch signalling in ENS specification, its role in human ENS progenitor cell fate decisions remains unclear\. Here, we employ a human pluripotent stem cell\-based model to show that Notch signalling is a key regulator of human ENS progenitor dynamics\. Quantitative modelling of our in vitro data indicates that Notch inhibition accelerates progenitor differentiation without substantially altering neuronal versus glial lineage bias\. Furthermore, we establish that Notch signalling controls human ENS progenitor migration by influencing migration velocity and directionality\. Together, these findings provide mechanistic insights into how Notch signalling disruption may contribute to the pathogenesis of human intestinal aganglionosis\.

## [Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Menulis Teks Puisi dengan Menggunakan Media Audiovisual Peserta Didik Kelas VIII SMP Negeri 1 Wadaga, Kabupaten Muna Barat](../publications/27a00d3bcf5893cad4a6.md)

La Ode Adili

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kemampuan menulis puisi peserta didik kelas VIII melalui penerapan pembelajaran berbasis media audiovisual di SMP Negeri 1 Wadaga, Kabupaten Muna Barat\. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan peserta didik dalam menulis puisi, khususnya dalam menentukan tema, memilih diksi yang tepat, mengembangkan imaji, menggunakan bahasa figuratif, dan menyampaikan amanat\. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian tindakan kelas \(PTK\) yang mengadopsi model Kemmis dan McTaggart serta dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus\. Setiap siklus terdiri atas tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi\. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 22 peserta didik kelas VIII\. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes menulis puisi, observasi aktivitas guru dan peserta didik, dokumentasi, serta wawancara singkat\. Data tersebut selanjutnya dianalisis menggunakan teknik deskriptif kuantitatif dan kualitatif\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan hasil belajar peserta didik secara konsisten selama pelaksanaan tindakan\. Nilai rata\-rata meningkat dari 60,23 pada tahap pratindakan menjadi 72,73 pada siklus I, kemudian mencapai 82,73 pada siklus II\. Ketuntasan belajar meningkat dari 45,45% pada tahap pratindakan menjadi 81,82% pada siklus I, dan mencapai 100% pada siklus II\. Peningkatan juga terlihat pada seluruh aspek penilaian, yaitu tema, pemilihan diksi, imaji, bahasa figuratif, dan amanat\. Keterlibatan guru dalam pembelajaran meningkat dari 77,1% pada siklus I menjadi 95,8% pada siklus II, sedangkan partisipasi aktif peserta didik meningkat dari 68,8% menjadi 91,7%\. Pengintegrasian media audiovisual dengan pemodelan penggunaan diksi, pencatatan kata kunci secara terbimbing, serta pemberian bantuan bertahap dalam penyusunan larik membantu peserta didik dalam memunculkan ide, mengolah pengalaman indrawi, dan mengembangkannya menjadi bait\-bait puisi\. Secara keseluruhan, penerapan intervensi pembelajaran ini berhasil meningkatkan proses pembelajaran, keterlibatan peserta didik, dan kemampuan menulis puisi selama penelitian berlangsung\.

## [“Men of All Parties Are in Perfect Accord”: How the Catch\-All Argument for Chinese Exclusion of the Workingmen’s Party of California Became Bipartisan Consensus, 1872\-1883](../publications/27a77eadcc3821cb0b58.md)

Benjamin Jiang

The Workingmen’s Party of California \(WPC\) dominated California politics for three years from 1877 to 1880, with Chinese exclusion and anti\-monopoly as its core agendas\. The party significantly contributed to the California Constitution of 1879 and indirectly influenced the passage of the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882\. Yet, few historians have analyzed the WPC through political science frameworks, leaving an important historic case study out of the contemporary discussion on nativism populism and leaving relevant political theories unexamined by the WPC historiography\. Using contemporary political science theories, this paper will analyze the WPC as a nativist and populist party\. Furthermore, using qualitative and statistical analysis of historic newspapers, this paper will investigate the two main historiographical debates about the WPC’s ideology: whether anti\-monopoly or nativism was the WPC’s main ideology, and whether the ideology was artificially constructed or originated naturally\. This paper will first argue that the WPC’s most influential ideology was nativism instead of anti\-monopoly\. Then, this paper will define the WPC’s version of Chinese exclusion as undifferentiated, meaning that it was a catch\-all case amalgamating cultural, racial, anti\-slavery, and labor arguments against Chinese immigration\. Thus, this paper proposes that the WPC’s Chinese exclusion was an intentional, artificial strategy to consolidate a broad coalition\. Moreover, this paper proposes that the established parties of California, the Democratic and Republican parties, adopted the WPC’s undifferentiated ideology of nativism\. These findings will suggest that the nationalization of anti\-Chinese sentiments that led to the passage of the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 originated from political entrepreneurs, rather than from the populace\.

## [The afterlife of consent: rethinking temporality, human dignity, and structural harm in international human rights law](../publications/27ac4719111858b706e5.md)

Abubakar Muhammad Jibril; Tourkia Rebhi

Contemporary international human rights law faces a conceptual challenge from digital environments in which intimate material remains accessible, reproducible, and socially consequential long after disclosure\. Although scholarship addresses digital privacy, technology\-facilitated gender\-based violence, and platform governance, insufficient attention has been given to the temporal and relational implications of persistent exposure for consent and human dignity\. This article asks whether existing international human rights frameworks adequately conceptualise harm when initial consent acquires continuing consequences through digital infrastructures\. Employing qualitative doctrinal and interdisciplinary legal analysis, the study examines international human rights norms and regional jurisprudence through feminist relational autonomy, structural\-harm analysis, African relational conceptions of dignity, and decolonial approaches to international law\. The findings reveal unresolved tensions concerning consent, autonomy, responsibility, and remedy\. The article develops the concept of the afterlife of consent to capture the divergence between initial authorisation and transformed conditions of visibility, accessibility, and vulnerability\. It argues that relational dignity and structural\-harm perspectives enable nuanced interpretations of continuing digital exposure, while decolonial analysis broadens the conceptualisation of the human rights subject\. The study advances a framework for interpreting existing protections in response to persistent digital vulnerability without establishing an unlimited right to erasure, while preserving established human rights principles and addressing evolving digital realities\.

## [Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores](../publications/27b3a4d710e5b22c82c4.md)

LiWen Kang; Junjie Chen; Mingsheng Hong; Wei Wei; Zuofu Xiang; zejun Zhang

Olfactory receptor \(OR\) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation\. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear\. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches\. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species\. Notably, bamboo\-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans\. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints\. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals\.

## [Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics](../publications/27cbd3fc913cee30abde.md)

Jiaxin Li; Jianping Liu; Nan Wang; Keyi Zhang; Wen Zhang; Mengze Gao; Zhiguo Lu; Xiaoyuan Shawn Chen; Yan Li

ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles \(LNPs\) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA \(siRNA\) therapeutics\. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity\. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations\. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route\. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications\. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment\. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs\. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver\.

## [Dijital Dönüşüm Kıskacında Türk Vergi Yazını: Yapay Zekâ Odaklı Çalışmaların Sistematik Literatür İncelemesi](../publications/27cc837c8056e7ecc7f5.md)

Ercan YELMAN

Yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin vergi alanındaki kullanımı, dijitalleşme süreciyle birlikte önemli bir dönüşüm geçirmektedir\. Özellikle vergi denetimi, vergi uyumu, tahsilat süreçleri ve mükellef hizmetleri gibi alanlarda yapay zekâ uygulamaları büyük değişikliklere yol açmaktadır\. Bu çalışma, 2005–2025 yılları arasında Türkiye&\#x27;de gerçekleştirilen akademik yayınları bibliyometrik bir yöntemle incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırmada Google, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, YÖK Tez ve YÖK Akademik, vergikutuphanesi\.com gibi çeşitli veri tabanlarından elde edilen makale, bildiri, kitap ve kitap bölümü ve lisansüstü tezler değerlendirilmiştir\. Yayınların türü, yıllara göre dağılımı, kullanılan araştırma yöntemleri, tematik odaklar ve anahtar kelime trendleri gibi unsurlar üzerine detaylı bir analiz yapılmıştır\. Elde edilen bulgular, özellikle 2019 sonrasında yapay zekâ ve vergi alanına yönelik akademik ilginin belirgin bir şekilde arttığını göstermektedir\. Çalışmaların büyük bir kısmı makale formatında olup, çoğunlukla nitel araştırma yöntemleri tercih edilmiştir\. Tematik açıdan ise vergi denetimi ve vergi uyumu gibi konular ön plana çıkmaktadır\. Bu araştırma, Türkiye’deki yapay zekâ ve vergi alanındaki mevcut akademik literatürü ortaya koyarak, gelecekteki araştırmalar için kapsamlı bir rehber sunmaktadır\.

## [Decoding inflammation to target hybrid diabetes phenotypes](../publications/27cd3573cff1905da2ef.md)

Giada Rossi; Annalisa Terranegra; Maria Elena Lunati; Ida Pastore; LORENZO POZZI CANOVA; Loredana G Bucciarelli; Vincenzo Cimino; Cristian Loretelli; Moufida Ben Nasr; Paolo Fiorina; Francesca D’Addio

With the escalating global epidemic of overweight and obesity worldwide, metabolic abnormalities \(i\.e\., central obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia and hypertension\) are raising in patients with type 1 diabetes \(T1D\)\. On the other hand, data are emerging on the detection of autoimmune markers in obese individuals previously diagnosed with type 2 diabetes \(T2D\)\. These overlapping immune\-metabolic features, characterizing hybrid phenotypes of diabetes such as double diabetes \(DD\) and latent autoimmune diabetes in adults \(LADA\), add a new layer of complexity in the diabetes spectrum and increase the risk of diabetes\-related complications and mortality\. Low\-grade chronic inflammation is thought to play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of DD and LADA and may represent a major driver in β\-cell dysfunction and metabolic dysregulation\. However, the literature on the topic is still limited, as well as the availability of specific therapeutic clinical approaches\. This review aims to summarize current evidence on inflammatory and immune\-metabolic biomarkers for early detection and identification of DD and LADA as compared to other types of diabetes\. Novel diagnostic strategies, including genomics, miRNomics, metabolomics and microbiomics analysis, together with therapeutic options targeting metabolic and inflammatory pathways will be also explored\. Challenges, including disease heterogeneity will be discussed alongside future directions, emphasizing the need for personalized medicine and longitudinal studies to shed more light on this overlooked hybrid phenotypes of diabetes\.

## [Diagnostic Accuracy of Multidetector CT for Detecting Ampullary Carcinoma: A Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/27dafb1a2b9773e538b6.md)



Background Ampullary carcinoma is an uncommon gastrointestinal malignancy in which timely diagnosis is essential for curative treatment\.Although multidetector three\-dimensional computed tomography \(3D CT\) is routinely used for evaluating periampullary lesions, evidence regarding its diagnostic accuracy in South Asian populations remains limited\.This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of multidetector 3D CT for detecting ampullary carcinoma using histopathology as the reference standard\.Methods A cross\-sectional diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at the Department of Radiology, Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation \(SIUT\), Karachi, Pakistan\.A total of 186 consecutive patients with suspected ampullary carcinoma underwent contrast\-enhanced multidetector 3D CT followed by histopathological confirmation through endoscopic biopsy or surgical resection\.Diagnostic performance was assessed by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value \(PPV\), negative predictive value \(NPV\), overall diagnostic accuracy, likelihood ratios, diagnostic odds ratio, receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve, and Cohen&\#x27;s κ agreement\. ResultsHistopathology confirmed ampullary carcinoma in 43 \(23\.1%\)patients\.Multidetector 3D CT demonstrated a sensitivity of 90\.7% \(95% CI: 77\.9\-97\.4%\),specificity of 91\.6% \(95% CI: 85\.8\-95\.5%\),PPV of 76\.5%, NPV of 97\.0%, and overall diagnostic accuracy of 91\.4% \(95% CI: 86\.4\-94\.9%\)\.The positive and negative likelihood ratios were 10\.8 and 0\.10, respectively, while the diagnostic odds ratio was 106\.4\.ROC analysis demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an AUC of 0\.911 \(95% CI: 0\.864\-0\.958;p&lt;0\.001\)\.Agreement between CT and histopathology was substantial \(Cohen&\#x27;s κ = 0\.79, p&lt;0\.001\)\. ConclusionMultidetector three\-dimensional CT demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for detecting ampullary carcinoma and showed substantial agreement with histopathology\.Its high sensitivity, specificity, and particularly high negative predictive value support its role as an effective first\-line non\-invasive imaging modality for the evaluation and preoperative assessment of suspected ampullary carcinoma, especially in resource\-limited settings\.

## [A Human\-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K\-12 Education](../publications/27ea07a0b83dcf118586.md)

Avula Chandrakala

Artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance\. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access\. This exploratory cross\-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect\. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross\-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open\-ended responses\. Sixty\-four respondents \(97\.0%\) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant\. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 \(75\.8%\), while 48 \(72\.7%\) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit\. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect \(55; 83\.3%\), followed by creativity \(52; 78\.8%\), problem\-solving \(48; 72\.7%\), and decision\-making \(47; 71\.2%\)\. Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance\. Based on these findings and relevant literature, the article proposes a preliminary six\-principle Future Minds Framework\. The small exploratory sample and self\-reported data do not support generalization or causal conclusions about cognition\. Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes\.

## [The impact of social media use on appearance anxiety among college students —the chain mediating effect of upward social comparison and envy](../publications/27ed37273d2ea666dc6c.md)

Yongjian Lin; Zhihao Li; Luling Li; Zhen LV; Tianxiang Song; Xiujie Zhou; Jianchao Ni

Background The widespread adoption of digital media has reshaped young people’s aesthetic experiences\. The abundance of idealized and digitally enhanced appearance\-related content on social media has made appearance anxiety increasingly prevalent among university students\. However, the psychological pathways linking social media use to appearance anxiety require systematic examination\. This study examined the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety among university students and tested the chain mediating roles of upward social comparison and envy\. Methods Using convenience sampling, 1,640 university students in China completed the Social Media Use Intensity Scale, Appearance Anxiety Scale, Upward Social Comparison Scale, and Envy Scale\. Confirmatory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and PROCESS Model 6 analysis with 5,000 percentile bootstrap samples were used to examine the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety and the chain mediating effects of upward social comparison and envy\. All regression equations controlled for gender, educational level, and average daily social media use time\. Results \(1\) Social media use was significantly and positively associated with appearance anxiety among university students\. \(2\) Upward social comparison mediated the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety\. \(3\) Envy mediated the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety\. \(4\) Upward social comparison and envy showed a significant chain mediating effect in the relationship between social media use and appearance anxiety\. Conclusion This study provided preliminary cross\-sectional evidence for an appearance\-anxiety\-specific comparison–envy pattern linking social media use to appearance anxiety among university students\. The findings provide theoretical and practical implications for aesthetic education and media literacy education in higher education within the digital media environment\. They may also help guide university students toward more rational aesthetic perceptions, reduced appearance anxiety, and improved physical and mental well\-being\.

## [Impaired autophagy and lysosome function in human fibroblast aging](../publications/27ed9758a36d01736ebc.md)

Juan José Unzueta\-Mendoza; Ian García‐Aguirre; Mina Königsberg; Isabel Arrieta‐Cruz; Solangy Lizcano‐Meneses; Jonathan J\. Magaña; Adriana Alarcón‐Aguilar; Bulmaro Cisneros

Background Human aging is characterized by a progressive, time\-dependent deterioration in physiological and cognitive functioning\. Aging is driven by an array of interconnected cellular hallmarks, including genomic instability, mitochondrial dysfunction, telomere attrition, epigenetic alteration and dysfunctional autophagy\. Autophagy is a cytoprotective \(cellular degradation and recycling\) pathway that maintains homeostasis during starvation or stress, and whose activity is associated with extended lifespan\. This multi\-step process comprises autophagosome formation and maturation, autophagosome–lysosome fusion, and cargo degradation\. Thus, analysis of autophagy flux is necessary to precisely design therapeutic interventions aimed at restoring autophagy in aging\. Methods The autophagy flux was comprehensively analyzed in human skin fibroblasts from donors of different ages \(20–96 years old\), a cell system that retains age\-associated cellular and molecular signatures\. The subcellular localization and activity of the master transcription factor of autophagy and lysosome biogenesis, TFEB, was analyzed by confocal microscopy assays and transcriptional expression of TFEB target genes \(RT\-qPCR\) respectively\. The autophagy flux was evaluated by monitoring the autophagy markers LC3 and p62 by Western blotting and confocal microscopy analyses, using inhibitor drugs to block autophagy or lysosomal activity\. Autophagosome maturation and autophagosome\-lysosome fusion were analyzed by colocalizing LC3 with Sintaxin\-17 and LC3 with the lysosomal protein LAMP1 respectively, using inhibitor drugs and confocal microscopy assays\. The analysis of lysosomal morphology and function was evaluated by lysobrite dye staining and live\-cell confocal microscopy analysis\. Results The initial stages of autophagy, including activation of TFEB, and autophagosome formation, remained apparently functional in fibroblast aging\. In contrast, the rate of both autophagosome maturation and autophagosome\-lysosome fusion, as well as the lysosomal function appears to be altered in aged fibroblasts\. Specifically, enlarged dysfunctional lysosomes were identified as a hallmark of the fibroblasts of the 96\-year\-old donor\. This lysosomal dysfunction may lead to a reduced ability to degrade canonical autophagy markers, LC3\-II and p62, and the accumulation of lipofuscin\. Conclusion Overall, the results provide evidence that autophagy flux is impaired at the late stages in aged fibroblasts, specifically in autophagosome maturation and autophagosome\-lysosome fusion steps\. Furthermore, it was demonstrated that this failure correlates with the presence of enlarged dysfunctional lysosomes\. This study underscores the significance of enhancing lysosomal activity to counteract autophagy decline in aging\.

## [3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code](../publications/27edde89bdc01696bd23.md)

Yipeng Gao; Ziyao Zeng; Jinfa Huang; Yijiang Li; Haolin Xiong; Wang Qin; Xinlei Yu; Youheng Yao; Jie Zhang; Kun\-Yu Lin; Rong Liu; Yinyuan Zhao; Yajie Zhao; Meiqi Guo; Jiebo Luo; Lei Shu; Yunhao Ge; Xinyu Hu; Laurent Itti

We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale\. 3DCodeVerse comprises large\-scale, high\-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding\. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse\-2M, a large\-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code\. We build this corpus by collecting open\-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents\. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records\. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi\-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content\. It uses execution checks, spatial measurements, and visual feedback to automatically evaluate and revise generated programs without human feedback during generation\. Third, we conduct systematic empirical studies of 3D coding, establishing baselines with fine\-tuned open models and deriving practical guidance through component\-level analyses of our harness\. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine\-tuning on our dataset significantly improves the 3D coding capabilities of open\-source models\. Notably, our 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design \(3D Object\) in pairwise human evaluations, when both are utilized by Claude Opus 5\.5\.

## [Training overdamped dynamics](../publications/27f992dacc2cadf2c29b.md)

Marc Berneman; Daniel Hexner

In regimes where inertia is negligible, the temporal evolution is governed by overdamped dynamics\. This limit is particularly relevant in soft\-matter contexts, such as polymers, colloidal suspensions, and processes occurring at the cellular scale\. Being able to manipulate the dynamics of such many\-particle systems would enable control over rate\-dependent elastic responses, time\-dependent material properties, relaxation processes, and perhaps the hydrodynamics of suspensions\. In this work, we develop a framework for manipulating overdamped dynamics through local, physically motivated update rules\. Our approach is inspired by ideas from physical learning and directed aging, in which microscopic parameters adapt autonomously to endow a material with a desired function\. Using the Rayleighian formulation, whose minimization reproduces the overdamped equations of motion, we derive approximate directed\-aging and equilibrium\-propagation rules tailored to dissipative systems\. To demonstrate these ideas, we study a disordered Maxwell material that behaves elastically at short times but flows at long times\. By locally modifying the viscous damping, we show that one can tune the viscous Poisson&\#x27;s ratio and shape local mechanical responses\. These results illustrate how materials can be trained to exhibit targeted rate\-dependent elastic and viscous behaviors\.

## [The Maternal Blood Transcriptome Reflects Molecular Signatures Associated With Large Offspring Syndrome and Other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Cattle](../publications/27fa46b9e347e477d6f2.md)

Tatiane S Maia; María Belén Rabaglino; Rebecca Krisher; P\. Rodríguez\-Villamil; Jeniffer Pamela J\. Laguna; Jeniffer F\. Escoto; Yanping Zhang; Abigail J\. Sproull; Peter James Hansen

Large offspring syndrome \(LOS\) in cattle is a phenomenon characterized by fetal overgrowth that is largely associated with calves derived from in vitro produced embryos\. Here it was tested whether occurrence of LOS as well as two other adverse pregnancy outcomes, stillbirth and abortion, could be predicted using changes in the maternal blood transcriptome early in gestation\. Blood samples were collected from Holstein and crossbred heifers at 40\-50 days of gestation following embryo transfer of in vitro produced embryos\. A total of 203 samples were selected for RNA\-sequencing and used to compare recipients of embryos resulting in live\-born calves of normal birth weight \(control; n = 96\) with recipients of embryos resulting in LOS calves \(n = 15\), stillbirths \(n = 43\), and abortion before 210 days of gestation \(n = 49\)\. Large offspring syndrome was defined based on birth weights greater than 2 standard deviations from the mean\. The number of differentially\-expressed genes \(p &lt; 0\.01\) was 32, 176, and 100 for comparisons of control versus LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively\. Biomarkers were identified in a randomly selected, balanced training dataset using Random Forest after filtering for differential expression\. Markers were then tested in the held\-out dataset through 6 machine learning models\. The best biomarkers consisted of 26, 24, and 28 genes for LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively\. The accuracy of prediction ranged from 0\.91 to 0\.965 for LOS, 0\.73 to 0\.98 for stillbirth, and 0\.62 to 0\.96 for abortion\. Despite the relatively small sample size, the model demonstrated high sensitivity for LOS classification, supporting that the maternal blood transcriptome in early pregnancy reflects molecular alterations associated with fetal overgrowth that can be predictive of the condition\.

## [Tecnologías emergentes en odontología: revisión bibliográfica](../publications/28047611fc3a27e76ae0.md)

Paula Alejandra Erazo\-Romo; Mercy Estefanía Colcha\-Tuqueres; Adriana Katherine Quezada\-Quiñonez

Objetivo: describir las principales tecnologías emergentes en odontología, sus aplicaciones clínicas, sus beneficios y sus limitaciones\. Método: revisión bibliográfica narrativa en PubMed y SciELO; se analizaron 15 documentos publicados entre 2012 y 2025\. Resultados: los flujos digitales y el CAD/CAM redujeron las citas y el tiempo clínico en prótesis\. La imagen digital y la inteligencia artificial mejoraron el diagnóstico, aunque los modelos de inteligencia artificial muestran alto riesgo de sesgo\. El láser permitió procedimientos menos invasivos y la teleodontología amplió el acceso en zonas remotas\. La robótica y la odontología regenerativa siguen en desarrollo\. Conclusión: las tecnologías emergentes mejoran la precisión, la eficiencia y la experiencia del paciente, pero su adopción exige mejor evidencia clínica, formación profesional y atención a los costos\.

## [Hybrid modeling of grounding and collision risk for vessels not under command](../publications/280ee94fae8c288cd7cd.md)

Mehmet Kaptan

Although loss of control \(not under command, NUC\) is one of the leading triggers of maritime accidents, the quantitative role of human and organizational factors in the process by which it evolves into a risk of grounding and collision has been largely neglected\. Traditional approaches primarily treat this situation as a technical reliability issue; however, whether a loss of control leads to a disaster is often determined not by the failure itself, but by human and organizational performance in the first few minutes following the failure\. To address this gap, this study proposes an original hybrid methodological framework that combines LLM\-supported HFACS\-PV coding, Monte Carlo simulation, and decision tree analysis within a sequential and integrated data flow\. Within this framework the predictive and quantitative burden rests on the Monte Carlo simulation, while the decision tree contributes an interpretable, descriptive account of factor combinations; it is not presented as a validated predictive classifier\. NUC cases compiled from publicly available accident investigation reports were coded into five HFACS\-PV layers using a large language model\-supported protocol; the resulting layer load was converted into a human factor multiplier that scales the vessel’s time to regain power and fed into the probabilistic simulation as input\. The simulation predicts the likelihood of catastrophic outcomes following a loss of control and highlights how the critical time window for intervention narrows significantly—particularly in extreme scenarios—emphasizing the decisive role of initial response capacity\. A controlled sensitivity analysis shows that, when physical variables are held constant, the human factor significantly alters the probability of a catastrophic event; however, this effect acts as a conditional modulator dependent on the available time window\. Decision tree analysis reveals that the simultaneous occurrence of technology–interface failures and skill\-based errors is the pattern most strongly associated with catastrophic outcomes\. This decision\-tree finding is descriptive and exploratory in nature; under leave\-one\-out cross\-validation the model does not outperform the majority\-class baseline and is therefore not used as a predictive classifier\. Furthermore, deficiencies in organizational processes and safety management systems emerged as the dominant latent condition in the vast majority of cases, and independent cases outside the dataset also confirmed this trend\. The proposed framework offers a practical and comparative decision\-support tool that integrates text\-based human factor analysis with probabilistic risk modeling\.

## [Integration of augmented reality in construction practice in Enugu state, Nigeria](../publications/2810394d4afd22a5205c.md)

Emeka J\. Mba; Chinyelu D\.F\. Onyia; Peter I\. Oforji; Paul C\. Ogbuefi; Emmanuel C\. Ezefuna

Emerging digital technologies increasingly influence the construction sector in Nigeria; however, the adoption of Augmented Reality \(AR\) remains limited\. This study investigated the awareness and knowledge level, accessibility, and readiness for AR adoption in construction practice in Enugu Metropolis, Nigeria\. A quantitative cross\-sectional survey was adopted, and a structured questionnaire was administered to 247 participants, including architects, engineers, project managers, construction firm owners, and vendors of digital construction tools\. Descriptive and inferential statistics was used to analyze the results, which revealed patterns in awareness, perceived benefits, barriers to AR adoption, and exposure to pilot cases of AR application\. Findings revealed that while a majority of professionals are aware of AR \(65\.6%\), the respondents reported very low knowledge of AR applications \(18\.6%\)\. High costs \(37\.3%\), lack of technical expertise \(25\.9%\), and inadequate digital infrastructure \(19\.4%\) were identified as the major barriers hindering adoption\. Despite these challenges, respondents expressed strong support for future investment in AR, highlighting training \(35\.6%\), financial support \(30\.8%\), infrastructural improvement \(16\.6%\), and awareness campaigns \(6\.1%\) as necessary solutions\. The study contributes to AR adoption in construction practice by bringing to the fore perceived benefits, barriers, and how architects, engineers, project managers, construction firm owners, among others, may leverage AR for improved efficiency, communication, and collaboration\. The study recommends collaborative interventions between professional bodies, government, and relevant stakeholders in the construction industry to accelerate AR adoption in construction practice, positioning Enugu as a model for digital innovation in the built environment\.

## [Bio‐Inspired Nucleotide Electrolyte Engineering Enables Highly Reversible Zinc Anodes for Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries](../publications/2811f0c615484e947dfe.md)

Xinyu Lv; Xin  Yong Gu; 李凤春; Yu Chen; Yongjuan Chen; Jingya Wang; Jian Hua Yang; Mingbo Wu

ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries \(AZIBs\) are promising for large‐scale energy storage but suffer from Zn dendrite growth, water‐induced parasitic reactions, and interfacial instability\. Herein, inspired by natural nucleotide architectures, we introduce disodium inosinate \(IMP\) as a green multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Zn electrochemistry\. Its naturally preorganized nucleotide framework integrates chemically differentiated phosphate, hydroxyl‐rich ribose, and O/N‐containing heterocyclic regions, which exhibit distinct interaction preferences toward Zn 2 \+ , water molecules, and the Zn surface under different local electrochemical environments\. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that IMP participates in Zn 2\+ solvation and regulates the local water environment, while preferential multisite adsorption at the Zn interface homogenizes Zn 2\+ flux and promotes Zn\(002\)‐preferred deposition, enabling dense and dendrite‐suppressed Zn growth\. Consequently, Zn\|\|Zn cells achieve stable cycling for over 2000 h at 5 mA cm −2 and 2\.5 mAh cm −2 , while Zn\|\|Cu cells maintain an average Coulombic efficiency above 99\.8% over 3500 cycles\. Zn\|\|NVO full cells retain 87\.3% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 , and pouch cells demonstrate stable cycling for 300 cycles\. This work highlights how the intrinsic chemical differentiation of a naturally preorganized nucleotide architecture can translate into distinct molecular interactions across different electrochemical environments, providing a bio‐inspired strategy for sustainable aqueous electrolyte design\.

## [Traffic surveillance video\-based a unified road accident detection, classification, and vehicle tracking framework using an optimized spatio\-temporal attention mechanism](../publications/2814785f8b7f1b381af2.md)

Chokkakula Devi; Gowri S\.

In recent days, vehicular accident detection has materialized because of the unique and intriguing application potential in the evolution of Intelligent Transportation Systems \(ITS\)\. To monitor and respond to the event of a fatal accident, real\-world traffic surveillance footage requires continuous analysis\. In this research, the road accident from the traffic surveillance video is detected, classified, and vehicle tracked using an efficient and innovative model\. The surveillance videos are gathered from the CCTV Footage dataset, which is a publicly available dataset\. The gathered videos are directly applied to the Spatio\-Temporal Attention\-based Adaptive Yolov9 with SE\-InceptionNet and Deep SORT \(AYSIDSORT\) model for detecting, classifying and tracking traffic accidents very effectively\. The developed network allows accurate detection and tracking of vehicles in real\-time, which ensures the continuous traffic flow without losing moving objects\. The variables of the proposed AYSIDSORT model are tuned by the developed Generation Probability\-based Equilibrium Optimizer \(GP\-EO\) to improve the detection and classification performance\. The exact location of the accident is sent to the appropriate entities using an Internet of Things \(IoT\) platform to provide a timely rescue for the affected individual\. Here, the proposed framework acts as a computer vision\-based accident detection and tracking framework with potential IoT integration to find the exact location of the accident, which helps to provide a timely rescue for the affected individual\. The effectiveness of the offered approach is validated with various baseline detection models\. The accuracy of the suggested AYSIDSORT reaches to 95% in the 100th epoch, whereas there is a slight variation in the accuracy values when the batch size is varied from 4 to 128\. The outcomes show that the designed framework is better than existing methods\.

## [NETWORK TRAFFIC ANALYSIS FOR DETECTING CYBER ATTACKS \( October 2026\)](../publications/281a8596d96437320f25.md)

Praveen Kumar Mishra; Aastha Singh

Most attacks have to traverse a network at some point, and when they do so, they leave traces in the traffic\.This paper investigates how those traces can be collected, measured and turned into alerts\.We cover the most common ways to collect traffic data \(packet captures, flow records and logs\), the types of characteristics that are generally useful, and three main families of detection methods: signature\-based, statistical and machine learning\-based\.We also describe how several well\-known attacks \(port scans, denial of service, brute force and botnet command\-and\-control\) manifest themselves on the wire A step\-by\-step analysis pipeline is presented, as well as the most common public datasets used for evaluation and the corresponding metrics\.Finally, we discuss the major challenges that remain in this area: encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift and the gap between laboratory test results and real\-world network deployments\.The goal is to provide a clear, practical overview for students and junior security analysts rather than presenting a novel algorithm\.

## [A review of recent advances in privacy\-preserving federated learning for healthcare applications](../publications/281ede313ddf99c45c94.md)

Anik Sen; Swee‐Huay Heng; Shing\-chiang TAN1

The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in healthcare, driven by the increasing availability of electronic health records \(EHRs\), medical imaging systems, genomic data, and wearable devices, has created significant challenges related to patient privacy, data security, and regulatory compliance\. Traditional centralised machine learning \(ML\) approaches often require large\-scale data sharing, which increases the risk of sensitive medical information exposure\. Federated learning \(FL\) has emerged as a promising distributed learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training across multiple institutions without transferring raw patient data\. Recent advances in privacy\-preserving FL have further strengthened its applicability in healthcare through the integration of techniques such as differential privacy \(DP\), homomorphic encryption \(HE\), secure aggregation, blockchain\-assisted frameworks, and secure multi\-party computation\. This study critically reviews recent developments in privacy\-preserving FL for healthcare applications published between 2024 and early 2026, with particular emphasis on medical imaging, EHRs analytics, genomics, and wearable health monitoring systems\. In addition, major technical and security challenges, including non\-independent and identically distributed \(non\-IID\) data distributions, communication overhead, scalability issues, gradient leakage, model poisoning, and membership inference attacks, are comprehensively analysed\. Regulatory, ethical, and interoperability concerns associated with cross\-institutional collaboration are also discussed\. Finally, current research gaps, emerging trends, and future directions for developing secure, scalable, and trustworthy federated healthcare systems are identified\.

## [The Political\-Business Nexus Behind Priority Mining Area Allocations \(WIUPK\) for Religious Organizations: An Analysis of Government Regulation Number 25 of 2024](../publications/28218a1bbf7eb34b5083.md)

Khuzaeni Khuzaeni; Yuddy Chrisnandi

The allocation of Special Mining Business License Areas \(WIUPK\) to business entities owned by religious organizations under Government Regulation Number 25 of 2024 has generated debate regarding the interactions among state authority, political interests, civil society organizations, and business actors\. This study aims to examine the political process underlying the formulation of Government Regulation Number 25 of 2024, particularly Article 83A, and to analyze the relationships among state actors, political elites, religious organizations, and business interests through the theoretical perspectives of state capture, the business\-politics nexus, and civil society\. This study employed a qualitative approach using a document analysis design\. Data were collected from laws and regulations, official government documents, academic publications, institutional reports, and relevant media sources\. The data were analyzed using the interactive model developed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, supported by source and theoretical triangulation\. The findings reveal that Government Regulation Number 25 of 2024 was formulated through an executive regulatory process that combined provisions granting priority access to WIUPK for religious organizations with other provisions benefiting large\-scale mining license holders\. The study also identifies patterns of interest exchange among state actors, political elites, religious organizations, and business interests that exhibit characteristics consistent with state capture, although it does not establish definitive evidence regarding the motives of the actors involved\. This research highlights the importance of transparency, public participation, and stronger accountability mechanisms in the formulation of strategic natural resource policies\.

## [Design of periodic mesoporous organosilica catalyst bearing copper phthalocyanine and quaternary ammonium for CO 2 cycloaddition](../publications/282fe33786c75e303f05.md)

Xiufu Hua; Chunfang Lai; Mengchi Dai; Yue Yu; Zhongyuan Liang; Renbo Wei; Lingling Wang

Abstract The development of heterogeneous catalysts with high activity, stability, and co\-catalyst\-free operation remains a significant challenge for the sustainable conversion of CO2 into value\-added chemicals\. Herein, we report a novel periodic mesoporous organosilica \(PMO\) heterogeneously functionalized with copper phthalocyanine \(CuPc\) and quaternary ammonium salts \(CuPc\-UQA2\-PMO\)\. This catalyst integrates CuPc centers, hydrogen\-bond\-donating urea groups, and iodide\-releasing quaternary ammonium moieties within a highly ordered mesoporous silica framework via covalent anchoring, creating a synergistic trinity active site\. The resulting catalyst exhibits a well\-defined spherical morphology, uniform element distribution, and a BET surface area of 714 m2·g\-1\. Under cocatalyst\-free conditions \(100 oC, 2\.0 MPa CO2\), CuPc\-UQA2\-PMO achieves nearly 99% yield and 100% selectivity for propylene carbonate from the cycloaddition of CO2 and propylene oxide\. Density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations reveal the cooperative activation of epoxide by Cu2\+ and urea, along with the availability of I\- species from the quaternary ammonium moieties for ring\-opening initiation and the synergistic adsorption/polarization of CO2 by the π\-conjugated system and quaternary ammonium cation, significantly lowers the energy barrier \(24\.21 kcal·mol\-1 for the rate\-determining step\)\. Furthermore, the catalyst reveals excellent recyclability over five consecutive cycles without appreciable loss in activity or structural integrity, highlighting its great potential for practical applications in green carbon utilization\.

## [Bioreactor Optimisation Through Coupled Fluid–Structure Interaction and Data\-Driven Analysis: A Biomimetic Framework for Predicting Early Cell Attachment](../publications/2844704d9b61b2c8cb10.md)

Yuyang Wei; Weijie Fei; Jiarong Wang; Luzheng Bi

Early cell attachment sets the baseline for proliferation, matrix deposition and construct maturation in tissue engineering, yet conventional bioreactors deliver simplified, quasi\-static stimuli that poorly represent the multi\-axial mechanical environment of native tissue\. Here we reported a biomimetic computational–experimental framework for a humanoid\-robot\-driven perfusion bioreactor\. The framework coupled a high\-fidelity fluid–structure interaction \(FSI\) model of the culture chamber with a machine\-learning model in order to describe the initial 3 h attachment phase, which preceded the application of robotic multi\-axial loading\. All experimental data reported here were therefore acquired during the static and perfused seeding phase; robotic loading was applied subsequently and was not part of the present dataset\. Local mechanical and fluidic fields—wall shear stress, flow velocity, pressure, von Mises stress and scaffold strain—were mapped across ten scaffold subregions and paired with spatially resolved cell numbers obtained by PicoGreen double\-stranded DNA quantification\. Six regression algorithms were compared under identical conditions; a multilayer perceptron \(MLP\) gave the lowest mean absolute error \(13\.2%\)\. Permutation importance ranked flow velocity, wall shear stress, von Mises stress and pressure as the dominant correlates of early adhesion\. Parameter sweeps of perfusion rate and scaffold stiffness were model predictions rather than measured optima, and identified 1\.4–1\.6 mL/min and a moderately compliant scaffold as candidate operating points for experimental testing\. The framework provides a transferable route to rational bioreactor and scaffold tuning with reduced empirical trial and error\.

## [A integração da inteligência artificial às metodologias ativas: impactos na aprendizagem significativa de estudantes universitários](../publications/28463d116ee993b8dfb0.md)

Percília Augusta Santana da Silva Campelo; Kecyani Lima dos Reis; Cesar Mendel Fernandes Ferreira; Wanderson Thiago Santos Noleto; David José Oliveira Tozetto; Tatiana Teixeira de Castro Carvalho Beckemkamp; Maria Joana da Silva Pinto; Daiane Rodrigues De Oliveira; Cátia Irene Duarte Valente; Herick Pampolha Huet de Bacelar

Este estudo aborda a integração da Inteligência Artificial \(IA\) às metodologias ativas no ensino superior para a promoção da aprendizagem significativa\. O objetivo foi analisar, mediante revisão sistemática, as evidências científicas sobre os impactos dessa integração em estudantes universitários\. A metodologia seguiu as diretrizes PRISMA 2020 e a estratégia PICO, realizando buscas nas bases Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, MDPI, Frontiers e SciELO\. Após triagem e avaliação de elegibilidade, selecionaram\-se 14 artigos para a síntese qualitativa\. Os resultados indicam que o uso de chatbots, tutores inteligentes e sistemas adaptativos articulados a métodos como sala de aula invertida, aprendizagem baseada em problemas/projetos e gamificação favorece a compreensão conceitual, o pensamento crítico, a motivação, o engajamento e a autorregulação\. Contudo, emergem desafios referentes à formação docente, à integridade acadêmica, à privacidade de dados e aos vieses algorítmicos\. Conclui\-se que a IA potencializa as metodologias ativas para uma aprendizagem significativa, desde que haja fundamentação pedagógica sólida, ética, mediação docente intencional e suporte institucional com capacitação continuada\.

## [Case Report: Endometrial carcinoma harboring a rare POLE p\.T278K variant and dual MSH6 frameshift variants](../publications/284c10ee5f6df5446c3d.md)

Yuxuan Yang; Huimei Luo; Huixing Yan; Haoping Yu; Xinyue Ma; Qiuli Teng; Longxin Zhang; Jinwen Ye; Zeng Yuan; Qing Zhang

Background POLE \-mutated endometrial carcinomas are associated with an excellent prognosis and have become an integral component of the molecular classification of endometrial carcinoma\. However, the pathogenicity of many rare non\-hotspot POLE exonuclease\-domain variants remains uncertain, particularly when they occur in tumors harboring additional molecular alterations that may confound molecular classification\. Methods Histopathologic findings and immunohistochemical expression of mismatch repair proteins and p53 were evaluated\. Targeted next\-generation sequencing of tumor tissue was performed to characterize genomic alterations, microsatellite instability, tumor mutational burden, and the mutational spectrum\. The non\-hotspot POLE p\.T278K variant was evaluated using the León\-Castillo scoring framework\. MLH1 promoter methylation was assessed by methylation\-specific PCR to further characterize the subclonal MLH1/PMS2 loss\. Case summary A 59\-year\-old woman with endometrioid endometrial carcinoma underwent total hysterectomy with surgical staging\. Targeted next\-generation sequencing identified a rare non\-hotspot POLE exonuclease\-domain variant, c\.833C&gt;A \(p\.T278K\), together with two MSH6 frameshift variants, c\.3261del \(p\.F1088Sfs\*2\) and c\.3261dup \(p\.F1088Lfs\*5\)\. The tumor demonstrated an ultramutated genomic profile with a tumor mutational burden of 370\.0 mutations/Mb and an MSI\-H phenotype\. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated subclonal loss of MLH1, PMS2, and MSH6 with retained MSH2 expression; MLH1 promoter methylation was also detected\. Conclusion This case adds clinicopathological and molecular evidence supporting the biological significance of the rare POLE p\.T278K variant and illustrates a practical approach for interpreting uncommon POLE exonuclease\-domain variants in endometrial carcinomas with multiple molecular classifiers\. Accurate identification of the dominant molecular classifier is critical for appropriate molecular classification, prognostic assessment, and clinical management\.

## [Low\-grade fibromyxoid and sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma: distinct behaviour in the same spectrum of ultra\-rare sarcomas](../publications/2856442373080eb7a22a.md)

Beatriz Castanheira; Inês Soldin; Joana Vieira; Mariana Gomes Afonso; Sofia Conde; Augusto Moreira; Miguel Henriques Abreu

Introduction Low\-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma \(LGFMS\) and sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma \(SEF\) represent a molecularly related spectrum of ultra\-rare soft\-tissue sarcomas characterised by recurrent FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements and frequent MUC4 expression\. Despite sharing recurrent molecular alterations, their clinical behaviour differs markedly, positioning them at opposite ends of a biologically related spectrum with distinct clinical trajectories\. This study aimed to characterise the clinicopathological features, molecular profiles, treatment approaches, and outcomes across this spectrum\. Methods We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients with LGFMS or SEF at a national EURACAN\-designated sarcoma reference centre between 2013 and 2024\. Clinicopathological characteristics, molecular findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected and analysed descriptively\. Results Twenty patients were included: 11 \(55%\) LGFMS, six \(30%\) SEF and three \(15%\) hybrid tumours\. MUC4 was positive in 13 cases \(65%\)\. Molecular analysis was informative in 19 patients \(95%\), with FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements in 16 \(84%\)\. FUS predominated \(63%\); EWSR1 rearrangements were confined to SEF \(21%\)\. Nineteen patients \(95%\) underwent curative\-intent surgery\. Local recurrence occurred in two \(10%\)\. Distant metastases developed in three \(15%\), all with SEF or hybrid histology\. Metastatic progression was early \(median 6 months\), associated with high\-risk histological features and EWSR1 rearrangement\. SEF accounted for the only disease\-related death; median overall survival was not reached, with 95% of patients alive at last follow\-up\. Discussion These findings highlight the divergent clinical behaviour across the LGFMS–SEF spectrum and support closer surveillance of high\-risk tumours\.

## [SEMANTIC ANALYSIS OF UZBEK LANGUAGE TEXTS USING THE INCEPTION PLATFORM](../publications/28571a1b09b49c6ba61d.md)

Matyoqubova Shaydo Maqsud qizi; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre

This article examines the application of the INCEpTION platform to the semantic analysis of Uzbek\-language texts, emphasizing linguistic annotation, knowledge representation, and the development of computational language resources\. INCEpTION is a web\-based semantic annotation platform that supports collaborative annotation, knowledge\-assisted labeling, and machine\-learning\-assisted annotation workflows\. The study investigates how its functionalities can be adapted to the linguistic characteristics of Uzbek, an agglutinative Turkic language with extensive morphological variation and relatively flexible word order\. Particular attention is given to named entity recognition, semantic relation annotation, word sense disambiguation, and the identification of context\-dependent meanings\. The research adopts a descriptive and comparative methodological approach based on established studies in natural language processing, semantic annotation, and computational linguistics\. The article proposes an annotation framework for Uzbek texts and identifies methodological challenges associated with morphological complexity, contextual ambiguity, annotation consistency, and limited annotated resources\. The findings indicate that INCEpTION provides a technically suitable environment for organizing human\-supervised semantic annotation projects, although its effectiveness for Uzbek depends on the availability of appropriate linguistic guidelines, annotated datasets, and compatible language\-processing models\. The study contributes to the methodological foundations of Uzbek natural language processing and outlines practical directions for developing semantically annotated Uzbek corpora\.

## [Enhancing operational efficiency in resource\-constrained apparel SMEs through simulation\-based process standardisation](../publications/285b948614186b956ec0.md)

Cristopher Antonio Muñoz Ibáñez; Rogelio Zarza\-Díaz; Juana Isabel Méndez; Mariel Alfaro\-Ponce

This study examines Discrete Event Simulation as a strategic tool for operational optimisation in small and medium\-sized textile enterprises, focusing on a women&\#x27;s boxer shorts production line\. It addresses common inefficiencies in resource\-constrained, high\-variability environments: task fragmentation, unbalanced workloads, and excessive cycle\-time variability\. A validated simulation model was built in Arena® software using time and motion studies, probability distribution fitting, and field data\. Two improvement scenarios were tested: \(1\) adding auxiliary labour at bottleneck stations, and \(2\) standardising operating procedures to reduce both mean processing time and cycle\-time variability of critical operations\. Scenario 1 yielded negligible throughput gains, whereas Scenario 2 increased average shift production by 31\.7% over the simulated baseline of 398 pieces/shift \(\+26\.5% versus the observed 414 pieces/shift\), while reducing variability and improving stability\. Statistical significance was confirmed via ANOVA \(30 replications per scenario, p &lt; 0\.05\) with Tukey&\#x27;s test, and model validity by deviation within ±4% of real performance\. The standardisation strategy is also expected to yield sustainability benefits, raising good\-quality output from existing capacity and reducing waste, though these effects are inferred, not directly measured, and left to future work\. Overall, results highlight simulation&\#x27;s value for improving efficiency and competitiveness in modular textile manufacturing without major capital investment\.

## [Electrochemical Detection of PFAS Contaminants Across Environmental and Pharmaceutical Matrices:Sensing Mechanisms, Nanomaterial Platforms, Biological Monitoring, and Regulatory Convergence](../publications/287014f2a569a09fd421.md)



PFAS are a class of over 14,000 synthetic compounds characterized by a stable carbon\-fluorine bond that confers resistance to thermal and biological degradation, resulting in common contamination of various aquatic matrices at concentrations ranging from sub\-parts per trillion to parts per billion\.Demand for directly deployable sensitive quantification methods has been spurred by increasingly stringent regulatory responses such as the U\.S\. Environmental Protection Agency \(EPA\) proposed maximum contaminant levels of 4 ppt for PFOA and PFOS in 2024 under its third Fourth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule and sub\-parametric values recommended by the EU Drinking Water Directive\.Conventional liquid chromatography\-tandem mass spectrometry provides the required sensitivity but is still limited by centralized infrastructure and slow sample preparation that prevents point\-of\-care or real\-time surveillance\.Another critically understudied dimension includes pharmaceutical matrices, where PFAS can act as formulation excipients or derive from the synthesis of fluorinated active pharmaceutical ingredients and pharmacokinetically interfere with albumin binding and hepatic CYP450 activity in exposed populations\.The current review summarized the existing electrochemical sensing strategies, including molecularly imprinted polymers, aptasensors, and CRISPR\-Cas12a biosensors, and state\-of\-the\-art electrode structures, including metal\-organic frameworks, MXenes, and covalent triazine frameworks, for targeting PFAS in environmental and biological matrices\.While some of these can be implemented analytically with detection below 1 ppt, critical benchmarking using regulatory thresholds reveals that 10% of sensor studies validate their performance in non\-spiked field or clinical matrices\.This highlights the need for multi\-analyte array development to allow standardized sensor validation frameworks across environmental and pharmaceutical quality monitoring\.

Rice blast is one of the most destructive fungal diseases affecting rice cultivation, which causes large yield losses and creates a major risk to the world&\#x27;s food security\. In addition to early detection, accurate severity\-level assessment is crucial for effective disease management\. A hybrid deep learning method based on ConvNeXt and Vision Transformer \(ViT\) models is proposed for assessing rice blast disease severity in the present work\. A new well\-organised dataset comprising 1,440 rice leaf images annotated into seven severity levels ranging from 1–10% to 61–70% based on the lesion area coverage is utilised in the model\. The proposed hybrid ConvNeXt–ViT model has two parallel feature extraction branches, where ConvNeXt captures spatial and textural patterns, while ViT learns global contextual representations\. Complementary feature representations from both branches are fused through a unified classification head to enable fine\-grained severity prediction\. A series of tests was carried out to evaluate the effect of different fusion strategies, pre\-trained weights, patch sizes, and batch sizes on model performance\. The proposed approach demonstrates consistent training behaviour and generalisation across different configurations\. Comparative evaluation against state\-of\-the\-art CNN models such as ResNet, EfficientNet, VGG, MobileNet, and Xception, as well as a transformer\-based baseline shows that the proposed approach achieves superior performance\. ## [Analisis Tingkat Degradasi Minyak Transformator Daya 80 MVA Menggunakan Metode Health Index Multi\-Parameter](../publications/28757498438063a4148e.md)

Ananta Deka Ramadhani; Ali Nur Fathoni; Subuh Isnur Haryudo; Fendi Achmad

Minyak transformator merupakan bagian penting dari sistem isolasi yang berfungsi sebagai media isolasi listrik dan pendingin selama transformator beroperasi\. Penurunan kualitas minyak akibat panas, oksidasi, kelembapan, dan tekanan listrik dapat mempengaruhi keandalan transformator\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi kondisi minyak transformator menggunakan metode Health Index dengan mengintegrasikan parameter Dissolved Gas Analysis \(DGA\), Oil Quality, dan furan\. Data diperoleh melalui pengujian DGA, Breakdown Voltage \(BDV\), Water Content, Interfacial Tension \(IFT\), Acidity, Colour, dan 2\-FAL\. Setiap parameter diberikan skor dan bobot, kemudian dikonversi menjadi Health Index Factor \(HIF\) untuk memperoleh nilai Health Index secara keseluruhan\. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa kelompok DGA memiliki nilai HIF sebesar 3,33, Oil Quality sebesar 2,08, dan furan sebesar 4,00\. Nilai Oil Quality yang rendah terutama dipengaruhi oleh BDV sebesar 25 kV dan Water Content sebesar 40,4 ppm yang berada pada kategori D\. Sementara itu, nilai 2\-FAL sebesar 75,40 ppb berada pada kategori A dengan kondisi bagus\. Berdasarkan integrasi seluruh parameter, diperoleh nilai Health Index sebesar 76,05% yang termasuk dalam kategori Bagus\. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa kondisi transformator secara keseluruhan masih berada pada kondisi baik, dengan parameter BDV dan Water Content menjadi aspek yang perlu mendapat perhatian dalam kegiatan pemantauan dan pemeliharaan\.

## [AuditKIT: A Unified Evaluation Spine for Benchmarking, Judging, and Comparing Large Language Models and Agentic Systems](../publications/287d30d4ef2c639bf055.md)

Shreeyans Arora; Utsav Avaiya; Zera Lyngkhoi; Hem Gosalia; Ram Mohan Rao Kadiyala; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu; Pratinav Seth

Evaluating language models and agents requires combining benchmark accuracy, judge\-based assessment, runtime performance, tool\-use behavior, and retrieval quality\. Differences in interfaces, metric semantics, and trace formats complicate these comparisons and can hide failures in agentic workflows\. We present AuditKIT, a source\-available evaluation library that records these measurements in one result representation, with direction\-aware metric contracts, configuration fingerprints, and extensible metrics and backends\. For agents, it provides turn\-aware tool\-call matching, separates parallel from sequential execution, and distinguishes verified task outcomes from trajectory\-level diagnostics\. Missing or unobservable evidence is marked unscored rather than counted as failure\. For retrieval\-augmented generation, it combines ranked retrieval metrics, judged grounding, and deterministic evidence checks\. Seven case studies spanning model comparison, serving runtimes, retrieval, tool calling, and interoperability show how answer extraction, runtime behavior, and metric selection change evaluation outcomes\.

## [Newspaper Vendor Problem: Some Insights Concerning the Expected Value of Perfect Information](../publications/287e7b5d1241f3b60bac.md)

Thomas Wedel

The single\-period inventory problem with uncertain demand, also known as the Newspaper Vendor Problem, is a commonly encountered occurrence in industry and significant research literature exists on the subject\. The critical ratio or fractile method provides the decision maker with a method for quickly calculating the optimal stock quantity that either maximizes expected profit or minimizes the expected cost\. The critical ratio or fractile method is based upon the concept of finding the optimal balance between the opportunity costs of having excess inventory versus having a insufficient supply on hand\. Little research publication, however, exists concerning EVPI for the Newspaper Vendor problem\. This paper addresses that gap in literature\. Market research is often available to more accurately estimate next periods demand but usually it has an attached cost\. The Expected Value of Perfect Information \(EVPI\) represents the most that the decision maker would ever pay for market research\. It provides the scale for which all sources of information about future demand can be rated\. This paper demonstrates the procedure for finding EVPI for cases where demand is estimated by either a discrete or a continuous probability distribution\. Practical examples of both profit maximization and cost minimization are provided in the paper\.

## [Salloch, Sabine ; Kacprowski, Tim ; Balke, Wolf\-Tilo ; Ursin, Frank &amp; Benzinger, Lasse: Should Artificial Intelligence be used to support clinical ethical decision\-making? A systematic review of reasons](../publications/287f4e361b09a089e336.md)



\_BMC Medical Ethics\_ 24 \(1\):1\-9\. 2023BackgroundHealthcare providers have to make ethically complex clinical decisions which may be a source of stress\. Researchers have recently introduced Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-based applications to assist in clinical ethical decision\-making\. However, the use of such tools is controversial\. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the reasons given in the academic literature for and against their use\.MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, Philpapers\.org and Google Scholar were searched for all relevant publications\. The resulting set of publications was title and abstract screened according to defined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 44 papers whose full texts were analysed using the Kuckartz method of qualitative text analysis\.ResultsArtificial Intelligence might increase patient autonomy by improving the accuracy of predictions and allowing patients to receive their preferred treatment\. It is thought to increase beneficence by providing reliable information, thereby, supporting surrogate decision\-making\. Some authors fear that reducing ethical decision\-making to statistical correlations may limit autonomy\. Others argue that AI may not be able to replicate the process of ethical deliberation because it lacks human characteristics\. Concerns have been raised about issues of justice, as AI may replicate existing biases in the decision\-making process\.ConclusionsThe prospective benefits of using AI in clinical ethical decision\-making are manifold, but its development and use should be undertaken carefully to avoid ethical pitfalls\. Several issues that are central to the discussion of Clinical Decision Support Systems, such as justice, explicability or human–machine interaction, have been neglected in the debate on AI for clinical ethics so far\.Trial registrationThis review is registered at Open Science Framework \(https://osf\.io/wvcs9\)\. \(direct link \)

## [A deep reinforcement learning framework with hybrid actions and multi objective rewards optimizes E commerce personalized marketing](../publications/2885803698b088d11746.md)

Yiwei Bai

As the scale of e\-commerce platforms continues to grow and user behavior becomes more dynamic, generating effective personalized marketing strategies has become essential for improving conversion efficiency and increasing long\-term user value\. Traditional approaches struggle with adapting to changing user states, modeling long\-term returns, and supporting automated decision\-making\. To address these issues, this study develops a deep reinforcement learning framework for personalized marketing in e\-commerce\. The framework models user interactions as a Markov Decision Process and integrates user state representation, a hybrid action space, and a multi\-objective reward design into a unified optimization process\. The method adopts an improved Soft Actor\-Critic algorithm to learn marketing strategies in an end\-to\-end manner\. It introduces an adaptive temperature mechanism to balance exploration and exploitation, incorporates a constraint handling module to ensure business feasibility, and applies prioritized experience replay to improve sample efficiency and training stability\. These modifications allow the model to better capture complex user behavior patterns and produce more reliable decisions\. The experiments use an offline dataset that contains about 2\.7 million real transaction and behavior records from an e\-commerce platform\. Compared with SAC\-Base, SAC\-IM improves CTR, CVR, and LTV by approximately 5\.6%, 7\.2%, and 8\.3%, respectively\. In addition, we further compare SAC\-IM with advanced offline reinforcement learning baselines, including CQL, IQL, and TD3\+BC, and report inference time, training time, and representative best/worst cases\. These finding indicate that the method can balance short\-term performance and long\-term value, and demonstrate its effectiveness for large\-scale e\-commerce marketing tasks\.

## [Same organ, divergent immunity: T\-cell exhaustion versus stromal exclusion in hepatocellular carcinoma and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma](../publications/28890c90534b47ffe449.md)

YanXi Chen; Tao Peng; Hao Nie; Yan Hu

Although hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma \(iCCA\) arise in the same organ, they occupy distinct immune geographies within a shared barrier network\. HCC is relatively enriched for inflamed yet dysfunctional CD8 \+ T\-cell states, whereas iCCA is more often characterized by stromal\- and myeloid\-associated immune exclusion; both patterns can occur in either tumor, but differ in their relative predominance\. Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped the treatment landscape in primary liver cancer, but durable benefit remains limited and heterogeneous\. Here, we place the T\-cell landscape—not checkpoint expression alone—at the center of comparison, focusing on where tumor\-reactive cells reside, the states they occupy, and the factors that constrain their reactivation\. By integrating clinical and translational evidence across HCC and iCCA, and distinguishing throughout between mechanisms established in human tumors and those extrapolated from experimental models or from other malignancies, we propose that differences in the T\-cell landscape help explain divergent therapeutic responses and provide a testable framework for biomarker\-guided combination strategies\. The key question is therefore not simply whether to release the checkpoint, but what each tumor’s T\-cell ecosystem requires for effective reactivation\.

## [Computationally guided side chain optimization of nirmatrelvir for lead discovery against coronavirus main proteases](../publications/28922a623e7f0f2c905f.md)

Md Saidur Rahman; Shahidul M\. Islam

To optimize Nirmatrelvir as an inhibitor of the MERS\-CoV main protease \(Mpro\), we developed an automated RDKit\-based iterative scaffold optimization framework that integrated fragment replacement, combinatorial library enumeration, and chemical feasibility filtering to generate 15,744 drug\-like analogs through systematic substitutions at six positions on the Nirmatrelvir scaffold\. Based on the correlation between structural similarity and docking score of the modified molecules, a binding score \(BS\) approach was advanced to rapidly identify and rank promising lead compounds\.
