To assess the robustness of the BS approach, multiple computational methods were employed, including K DEEP , molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations, molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area \(MM/GBSA\) free energy calculations, and Boltz\-2\. The BS ranking showed strong agreement with all computational validation methods, consistently identifying compounds with enhanced binding affinities and stable protein\-ligand interactions\. The top\-ranked compounds, M1, M3, M5, and M6, identified by high Binding Score \(BS\) values \(9\.1–10\.2\), exhibited favorable MM/GBSA binding free energies ranging from − 31\.7 to − 42\.9 kcal/mol, K DEEP \-predicted binding affinities of − 9\.5 to − 10\.6 kcal/mol, and Boltz\-2 predicted pIC₅₀ values of 10\.0–11\.8\. Furthermore, for SARS\-CoV\-2 Mpro, BS scores also correlated well with available experimental half\-maximal inhibitory concentration \(IC 50 \) data and Boltz\-2 predictions for Nirmatrelvir analogues\. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the BS approach may serve as an efficient strategy for screening, prioritizing, and accelerating the discovery of next\-generation coronavirus Mpro inhibitors\.

## [The Role of Emerging Technologies in Shaping Modern Banking and Financial Services](../publications/289f12c2932fa19cbfbb.md)

Ms\. Ritika Anil Nandanwar

Emerging technologies are significantly transforming the landscape of banking and financial services, shifting the way institutions operate and how consumers engage with financial products\. Technologies such as artificial intelligence \(AI\), blockchain, big data analytics, and cloud computing have moved beyond theoretical concepts and are now at the core of innovation within the financial sector\. These tools are streamlining operations, enhancing customer service, improving security, and enabling the development of more inclusive and user\-centric financial services\. This paper explores how these technologies are making banking systems faster, smarter, more efficient, and accessible to a broader population\. AI is being used for fraud detection, predictive analytics, and virtual customer assistance\. Blockchain is enabling secure, decentralized financial transactions with increased transparency\. Big data is helping institutions understand customer behavior and tailor services accordingly, while cloud computing allows for more agile and scalable infrastructure, enabling banks to respond more quickly to market changes\. While the benefits of these advancements are substantial, they also come with a new set of challenges\. Issues such as cybersecurity vulnerabilities, regulatory compliance, data privacy, and digital inclusion must be carefully addressed to ensure that technological progress does not come at the cost of trust, safety, or accessibility\. Furthermore, as financial services become increasingly digitized, the digital divide may widen, potentially excluding certain populations from the benefits of modern banking\.

## [First record of the non\-native leafhopper Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 \(Hemiptera, Cicadellidae, Deltocephalinae, Opsiini\) in Bulgaria](../publications/28a1e7b0b3637cf2be17.md)

Ilia Gjonov; Radost Angelova; KATIA TRENCHEVA

We report Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 from Bulgaria for the first time\. We collected 36 specimens, including a nymph, at eight localities in six widely separated cities\. All records originated from urban parks and gardens\. Identification was based on external morphology and the male genitalia\. The broad geographic spread of the records, from the Black Sea coast and southern Bulgaria to the Danube region in the north\-west, suggests that this adventive East Asian leafhopper is already more widely distributed in Bulgarian urban areas than currently documented\.

## [Elevated prenatal IL\-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage](../publications/28a555394ecd5c18907a.md)

Genni Desiato; Edoardo Fraviga; Thomas Cassani; Riccardo Grassi; Martina Vitali; Francesca Fanuele; Filippo Mirabella; Clara A\. Amegandjin; Federica Ruggeri; M\. Cremonesi; David Andruszewski; Andrea Contestabile; Laura Cancedda; Riccardo Fesce; Graziella Di Cristo; Ilgiz A\. Mufazalov; Marinos Kallikourdis; Michela Matteoli; Sebastiano Bariselli; Davide Pozzi

Abstract Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation\. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined\. Maternal immune activation \(MIA\) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders\. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin\-6 \(IL\-6\) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation\. By triggering a STAT3\-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL\-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch\. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA\-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders\.

## [Modern non\-invasive methods for the diagnosis of scoliosis in children](../publications/28b7f6a4a42b97e13943.md)

Andrey I\. Perepelkin; Е\. В\. Власова; Ahmed Ghulam

Scoliosis is the most common orthopedic disease in childhood, affecting 3–5 % of children and adolescents\. Traditional radiography, despite its status as the “gold standard”, is associated with cumulative radiation exposure, which is particularly significant for the growing organism\. Over the past decades, numerous diagnostic methods that do not use ionizing radiation \(hereinafter referred to as radiation\-free\) have been developed, but their clinical application remains limited\. The aim of the study: To conduct a systematic analysis of modern non\-invasive methods for diagnosing scoliosis in children, evaluate their diagnostic accuracy, clinical effectiveness, advantages and limitations, and determine prospects for implementation in clinical practice\. Research methodology: An analysis of domestic and foreign literature from 1973 to 2025 was conducted\. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and eLibrary\.ru databases\. The review includes data from randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta\-analyses, and clinical guidelines\. The results of the research: The review includes relevant sources covering the epidemiology, etiopathogenesis, and classification of scoliosis\. The main non\-invasive diagnostic methods are analyzed: low\-dose radiography \(EOS\), ultrasound \(Scolioscan\), surface topography \(including moiré topography, raster stereography, and computer optical topography\), 3D scanning, magnetic resonance imaging, as well as neurophysiological methods\. According to recent meta\-analyses, ultrasonography demonstrates the highest degree of correlation with radiography, while surface topography also shows consistently high agreement of results\. Conclusion: Modern methods that do not use ionizing radiation represent an effective alternative to traditional radiography, especially for screening examinations and dynamic monitoring\. Ultrasonography and surface topography are the most promising radiation\-free methods\. Further development of artificial intelligence technologies will improve the accuracy and reproducibility of these methods and expand their availability for widespread clinical practice\.

## [The Personalistic Norm and the Author&\#x27;s Code of Ethics in the Context of the Development of the Virtual Environment](../publications/28b887cb77b62e0e749d.md)

Sławomir Chrost

Technological development manifesting itself mainly through the virtual environment and AI creates a fundamental challenge for the modern world\. In the era of the so called industrial and technological revolution and the rapid AI development moral and ethical dilemma occur\. In that context a new teaching objective appears, such as understanding the ethical implications of automation and AI; the ability to foresee the unintentional consequences of technology; making decisions that take into account diversity and inclusion or responsibility for the long\-term impact of technological decisions\. The paper aims to formulate a code of ethics in the context of the development of virtual environments \(and particularly artificial intelligence\) within the framework of theistic personalism\. The article presents and explains ten detailed principles \(The principle of personal dignity, The principle of freedom and self\-determination, The principle of responsibility, The principle of safety, control and criticism, The principle of multidimensional being and multidirectional development, The principle of the primacy of spirituality over technology, The principle of primacy of personal relationships, The principle of truth, The principle of good, The principle of beauty\)\. The primary research method was an analysis of sources and relevant literature \(desk research\)\. Procedurally, the analysis proceeded in three stages\. The first involved formulating the fundamental ethical dilemmas related to human development in the context of the virtual environment\. The second stage included an anthropological and ethical analysis of these dilemmas in light of the ethics of personalism, particularly the personalist norm\. The third stage consisted of a theoretical synthesis leading to the formulation of an original code of personalist ethics in the context of the development of the virtual world, based primarily on the personalist norm\.

## [Telemedicine in Retinopathy of Prematurity: A Review of Current Evidence and Clinical Outcomes](../publications/28c7a9048b4157b4b048.md)

Ilinca\-Medeea Iftime; Andreea Ramona Treteanu; Andreea Pușcașu; Mihai Craiu; Octaviana Cristea; Alina Angelica Ciolpan

Background/Objectives: Retinopathy of prematurity \(ROP\) is a leading cause of preventable childhood visual impairment, particularly in settings where access to specialized ophthalmologic care is limited\. Telemedicine offers an alternative approach to ROP screening and monitoring through remote retinal imaging and expert interpretation\. This narrative review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance, clinical benefits, implementation challenges, and future perspectives of telemedicine in ROP screening and management\. Methods: A narrative literature review was conducted with consideration of the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles \(SANRA\) criteria\. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched in August and August 2026 for relevant publications from January 2000 to the search date\. Two authors independently screened titles and abstracts, followed by full\-text assessment according to predefined eligibility criteria\. A total of 143 scientific articles and other high\-quality sources were included in the final narrative synthesis\. Evidence was evaluated qualitatively, without a formal risk\-of\-bias assessment\. Findings: The reviewed literature indicates that telemedicine can expand access to ROP screening, facilitate remote specialist consultation, support longitudinal disease monitoring, and improve the triage of infants requiring urgent assessment\. In selected settings, remote retinal image interpretation has demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to conventional examinations for clinically significant and vision\-threatening ROP\. Artificial intelligence\-based assessment and smartphone\-based retinal imaging represent promising approaches to improving screening accessibility and workflow efficiency, particularly in resource\-limited settings\. However, implementation remains constrained by equipment costs, infrastructure limitations, image quality, workforce training requirements, and ethical and legal considerations\. Conclusions: Telemedicine represents a promising complementary strategy for ROP screening and management, with the potential to improve access to timely specialist assessment and help prevent ROP\-related visual impairment\. Its successful integration into clinical practice requires sustainable infrastructure, standardized protocols, trained personnel, and reliable referral pathways that ensure timely in\-person examination and treatment when indicated\. Further research is needed to establish the effectiveness, cost\-efficiency, and long\-term sustainability of different telemedicine\-based approaches across diverse healthcare settings\.

## [PLANT\-BASED GREEN NANOTECHNOLOGY: ADVANCES IN THE BIOSYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND BIOLOGICAL APPLICATIONS OF NANOMATERIALS](../publications/28d306eeac91eb5abe2f.md)

Pratibha Tabaji Kurkute; Padmaja; Subash Chandra Sahu

Nanotechnology has developed very rapidly and has had a great impact on a number of sciences, in particular biomedicine, agriculture and environmental remediation\. The production of nanomaterials by traditional techniques relies on physical and chemical procedures that are efficient but use toxic reducing agents, produce toxic by\-products and need large amount of energy\. Over the last few years, plant\-based green nanotechnology has been identified as a revolutionary, eco\-friendly and sustainable alternative to these traditional techniques\. Plant extracts including flavonoids, polyphenols, terpenoids, and alkaloids exhibit an extensive phytochemical diversity, which enables scientists to efficiently reduce metal ions and stabilize the generated nanoparticles simultaneously through an environmentally friendly process\. This peer\-reviewed article reviews comprehensively the recent progress in the biosynthesis of plant\-mediated nanomaterials, especially metallic and metal oxide nanoparticles including silver, gold, copper and zinc oxide\. It also gives detailed information on the essential techniques used to characterize nanoparticles in terms of their shape, size and structure such as UV\-Vis, FTIR, XRD and SEM\. Note that this review extensively discusses the biological uses of these biogenic nanoparticles with special focus on their potential antimicrobial, anticancer, antioxidant and targeted drug delivery capabilities\. This paper reveals the revolutionary potential of plant\-based green nanotechnology in modern science by integrating fundamental mechanisms and practical applications and addressing the current challenges in scalability and standardization\.

## [A formação do enfermeiro para a educação em saúde: desafios e estratégias no ensino de graduação — uma revisão integrativa](../publications/28f6231edc7e59d130d6.md)

Beatriz Caroline Lodete; Milena Farias Santos; Rafaela Dávila Da Cruz dos Santos Botelho; FABRÍCIO SIDNEI DA SILVA; Rauer Ferreira Franco; Livia Moreira Da Silva

A educação em saúde constitui dimensão inerente ao trabalho do enfermeiro e exige competências que ultrapassam a transmissão de informações, incluindo comunicação, letramento em saúde, planejamento educativo, diálogo, avaliação de necessidades e promoção da autonomia\. Este estudo objetivou analisar como a formação de graduação em Enfermagem tem preparado estudantes para a atuação em educação em saúde, identificando estratégias pedagógicas, resultados e desafios\. Realizou\-se revisão integrativa da literatura, com estudos publicados entre janeiro de 2020 e agosto de 2026, localizados em MEDLINE/PubMed, Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde, LILACS/BDENF e SciELO, além de rastreamento complementar de referências\. Vinte estudos compuseram a síntese\. As estratégias incluíram simulação, pacientes padronizados, Teach\-Back, aprendizagem baseada em serviços, trabalho em equipe, role\-play, intervenções digitais, e\-books interativos e uso supervisionado de inteligência artificial\. Os achados indicaram melhora de conhecimentos, letramento em saúde, autoconfiança, comunicação e competências para educação do paciente, sobretudo quando ensino explícito foi combinado a prática, feedback e situações autênticas\. Persistiram lacunas curriculares, heterogeneidade das intervenções, avaliações predominantemente autorreferidas e escassez de acompanhamento longitudinal\. Conclui\-se que a competência educativa deve ser desenvolvida longitudinalmente na graduação, articulada ao SUS, à promoção da saúde, à educação popular e a experiências práticas com avaliação formativa\.

## [How national missions reshape policy networks: evidence from China’s STI policy\-making collaborative network, 1978–2023](../publications/290ac3d98408c640e535.md)

Lupeng Zhang; Yulin Chang; Wenbo Chen

Science, technology and innovation \(STI\) policy in China is made jointly by many government agencies, so the way those agencies collaborate bears on what innovation governance can achieve\. This study examines that collaborative network, drawing on 1010 STI policy documents issued jointly by central government agencies between 1978 and 2023\. Policy network theory and the mission\-oriented innovation policy framework are combined with multi\-period social network analysis to trace how the network expanded and how the position of individual agencies changed\. Three findings emerge\. The network expanded in an orderly way across five stages, growing from 8 to 73 participating agencies, while the cohesion index stayed above 0\.68 throughout and reached its highest value in the most recent stage, so growth in scale did not come at the cost of cohesion\. Agency roles moved from a single dominant core towards a differentiated division of labour, and four role types can be distinguished, namely Agenda Leader, Boundary Spanner, Innovation Seed and Resource Hub\. Successive upgrades in national science and technology missions coincided closely with these changes in structure\. The trajectory observed here departs from the movement from policy community to issue network that Western policy network theory anticipates, and may mark a third path of mission\-driven orderly expansion, although a descriptive design supports association and not causal attribution\. The findings bear on how policy network theory might be extended to state\-led innovation systems\.

## [An Explainable Federated Vision–Language Learning Framework for Privacy\-Preserving Automated Medical Report Generation Across Distributed Healthcare Institutions](../publications/2919a7651a243fe72d2f.md)



Automated generation of medical reports using AI can help speed up diagnosis and reduce doctor workload, but currently, the most efficient forms of automation use centralized training, which requires hospitals to share sensitive patient data\. This raises concerns about the privacy and regulatory issues of sharing patient information to generate reports\. In addition, clinicians have difficulty trusting AI\-assisted diagnosis because the visionlanguage models used for automated report generation are not easily interpretable\. To tackle these issues, an Explainable Federated Vision\-Language Learning Framework \(EFVLL\) has been created to generate automated medical reports that preserve patient privacy through distributed healthcare institutions\. Hospitals can use federated learning to build a collaborative global vision\-language model without having to share raw patient information\. The EFVLL framework also includes an explainable attention mechanism that will help clinicians understand how specific areas of the image and text are related to the report being generated, increasing the transparency and interpretability of automated reports\. Further, the EFVLL will improve generalization across non\-homogenous datasets and comply with data privacy and regulatory requirements\. The EFVLL framework has been validated with multiple large standard datasets \(e\.g\., RSNA\), and therefore it is suitable for implementation and use in a distributed healthcare environment\.

## [Escaping Rounding Barriers in Large Language Model Quantization via Transverse\-Field Ising Optimization](../publications/29220ed6822bd0df5850.md)

Anh Nguyen Duc; Linh Ngo Van; Sang Dinh Viet; Hoang Ta Duy; Tung Nguyen Son; Canh Dinh The; Tu Vu Van

Weight\-only post\-training quantization \(PTQ\) pipelines such as AWQ ultimately commit to a deterministic rounding decision for every scalar weight, and recent discrete coordinate\-descent quantizers refine those decisions one weight at a time\. We show that both are blocked by the same obstacle: correlated activation channels create multi\-spin energy barriers in the discrete rounding landscape — configurations in which no single rounding flip helps, yet a small group of coordinated flips strictly reduces the layer reconstruction error\. We characterize these barriers exactly under the empirical activation metric and prove that they arise only from frustration between local quantization fields and cross\-channel couplings\. Building on this analysis we propose Transverse\-Field Ising Correction \(TFIC\), a barrier\-aware discrete optimizer that post\-processes any AWQ\-style pipeline\. TFIC casts fixed\-grid rounding as a classical Ising ground\-state problem, selects the spins near a rounding boundary as a mobile pool, drives that pool to a single\-flip local minimum by exact coordinate descent, and then crosses barriers with cluster moves that flip small groups of coupled spins together\. Every accepted move is scored against the exact reconstruction energy, and a robust per\-layer noise\-floor acceptance rule prunes flips whose apparent gain is within calibration\-estimation noise; together these guarantee that each layer’s calibration reconstruction error is monotonically non\-increasing\. TFIC requires no gradients and no architectural changes\. On Mistral\-7B and Llama\-3\-8B, applying TFIC on top of a 4\-bit AWQ baseline consistently reduces WikiText\-2 and C4 perplexity, at a per\-layer cost of tens of seconds and with no inference\-time overhead\.

## [Cath, Corinne ; Wachter, Sandra ; Mittelstadt, Brent ; Taddeo, Mariarosaria &amp; Floridi, Luciano: Artificial intelligence and the ‘Good Society’: the US, EU, and UK approach](../publications/29252acf4ea0513c8036.md)



\_Science and Engineering Ethics\_ 24 \(2\):505\-528\. 2018In October 2016, the White House, the European Parliament, and the UK House of Commons each issued a report outlining their visions on how to prepare society for the widespread use of artificial intelligence\. In this article, we provide a comparative assessment of these three reports in order to facilitate the design of policies favourable to the development of a ‘good AI society’\. To do so, we examine how each report addresses the following three topics: the development of a ‘good AI society’; the role and responsibility of the government, the private sector, and the research community in pursuing such a development; and where the recommendations to support such a development may be in need of improvement\. Our analysis concludes that the reports address adequately various ethical, social, and economic topics, but come short of providing an overarching political vision and long\-term strategy for the development of a ‘good AI society’\. In order to contribute to fill this gap, in the conclusion we suggest a two\-pronged approach\.

## [Effects of violet light exposure on aging dogs: a pilot study](../publications/293107d748cfa0130447.md)

Kana MIYAMOTO; Nanami Ono; Shinichiro Kondo; Yukihiro Miwa; Kazuo Tsubota; Makiko Ozawa; Takefumi Kikusui

Aging in dogs is known to induce various physical and brain alterations similar to dementia in humans\. Concurrently with the recent extension of canine life expectancy, these age\-related changes have imposed growing burdens on both dogs and their owners, emerging as a significant social issue\. However, no curative treatment has yet been established, and the current mainstay of management focuses on improving the quality of life through symptomatic therapies, such as environmental modifications and pharmacotherapy\. This study focused on violet light, which has suggested efficacy against such age\-related changes\. We developed a novel violet light irradiation device and evaluated its efficacy and safety in elderly dogs as a pilot study\. An intra\-individual comparison using an ABA design was employed with geriatric dogs aged 14 to 16 years housed in a senior dog care facility \(two of which discontinued midway\)\. The study design consisted of a one\-month violet light exposure phase preceded and followed by two\-week non\-exposure periods\. Physical activity levels were measured using accelerometers and cognitive function was assessed using the DISHAA and CCDR\. To evaluate the safety, general physical and ophthalmic examinations were conducted by veterinarians\. As a result, no significant overall effect was found on activity levels \(Daytime: x 2 = 4\.22, p = 0\.12; Nighttime: x 2 = 1\.58, p = 0\.45\)\. Similarly, no significant overall effects were observed for either the DISHAA or the CCDR \(DISHAA: x 2 = 1\.60, p = 0\.45; CCDR: x 2 = 1\.56, p = 0\.46\)\. However, a trend toward cognitive improvement was observed in six out of seven dogs and an upward trend in activity levels\-indicating physical function improvement\-was noted in two out of seven dogs\. Regarding safety, no overt clinical abnormalities associated with violet light irradiation were identified\. This pilot study demonstrated no clear overall effect, though some individuals showed signs of improvement\. Future research should consider large\-scale trials controlling for various variables\.

## [An integrated AI\-IoT framework for urban pollution source detection and sustainable Smart\-City Governance](../publications/2943adee0ef0bf1a7db8.md)

Abubakar Ahmad; Mazlina Binti Abdul Majid; Murizah Binti Kassim

Urban air pollution remains a major challenge to sustainable city development because traditional monitoring systems have limited capacity to address complex and dynamic urban environments\. Although Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Internet of Things \(IoT\) technologies have demonstrated considerable potential for environmental monitoring, existing approaches often emphasize individual technical capabilities while giving limited attention to governance transparency, ethical deployment, and sustainability alignment\. This study proposes an integrated AI\-IoT conceptual framework for urban pollution source detection and sustainable smart\-city governance\. The framework integrates multi\-source environmental sensing, data processing, AI\-driven forecasting and pollution source attribution, intelligent decision support, ethical AI governance, and Sustainable Development Goal \(SDG\) alignment within a unified six\-layer architecture\. Its conceptual grounding is assessed through structured literature mapping, comparative analysis of existing AI\-based urban monitoring frameworks, and case\-study mapping using a published IoT\-enabled environmental monitoring application\. The framework establishes an end\-to\-end pathway connecting environmental observations with pollution intelligence, policy\-oriented decision support, responsible governance, and measurable sustainability outcomes\. It also identifies key implementation challenges involving data privacy, algorithmic bias, explainability, interoperability, scalability, and deployment constraints\. The proposed architecture provides a structured foundation for future implementation and empirical evaluation of intelligent, ethical, and sustainability\-oriented urban pollution management systems\.

## [Real\-Time Sign Language Recognition System: A Computer Vision\-Based Approach for Accessible Human–Computer Interaction](../publications/294ac3a57d27dc78c426.md)

Sakshi Bhong

This paper, titled “Real\-Time Sign Language Recognition System: A Computer Vision\-Based Approach for Accessible Human–Computer Interaction,” proposes a camera\-based system for recognizing hand gestures and converting supported signs into readable text\. The proposed system uses a modular processing pipeline consisting of video acquisition, hand detection, landmark and feature extraction, gesture classification, temporal smoothing, and text output\. Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and a machine\-learning classifier are suggested as potential implementation technologies\. The system is designed to capture live video frames, identify hand landmarks, normalize coordinates, extract relevant features, classify supported gestures, and display the predicted sign\. Confidence thresholds and temporal smoothing can help reduce unreliable or inconsistent predictions\. The design also supports future extensions such as speech output, dynamic gesture recognition, and expanded sign vocabularies\. The paper describes the proposed architecture, system modules, processing algorithm, implementation approach, evaluation plan, limitations, and future scope\. Potential evaluation measures include classification accuracy, per\-class precision and recall, inference latency, and processing frame rate\. This work presents a proposed software\-system design intended to improve communication accessibility through computer vision and machine learning\. Experimental performance results are not claimed in the current paper; implementation and testing are required to validate the system&\#x27;s effectiveness\.

## [Forensic investigation of drones: tools, methods, and open issues](../publications/294e508ed3b5f424cee6.md)

Manisha Wadhwa; Kanishk Aneja; Sakshi; Pankaj Sharma

The growing adoption of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles \(UAVs\) across civilian, commercial, and security sectors has introduced new challenges for digital forensic investigations, particularly in incidents involving unauthorized surveillance, privacy violations, and cyberattacks\. The recovery and analysis of UAV\-generated evidence remain challenging due to heterogeneous platform architectures, proprietary and encrypted data formats, and the absence of standardized forensic procedures\. This paper presents a PRISMA\-based systematic review of more than 70 peer\-reviewed studies, organized into six research themes: forensic frameworks and standardization, evidence acquisition and analysis, forensic tool evaluation, cybersecurity and anti\-forensics, AI\-assisted investigations, and application\-oriented studies\. Unlike previous surveys that primarily examine individual aspects of drone forensics, this review brings together technical, operational, and legal perspectives to identify common challenges and their implications for practical investigations\. The findings reveal persistent gaps in tool interoperability, forensic readiness, evidence preservation, real\-world validation, and legal admissibility\. Emerging technologies, including machine learning, digital twins, cryptanalysis, and Large Language Models \(LLMs\), offer opportunities to improve evidence correlation, incident reconstruction, anomaly detection, and forensic reporting\. However, their practical adoption requires careful consideration of explainability, reproducibility, data privacy, and the reliability of AI\-generated findings\. Based on the identified gaps, the review proposes future research directions emphasizing standardized evidence acquisition, forensic\-ready UAV architectures, interoperable tools, and verifiable AI\-assisted analysis\. The study provides practical insights for forensic investigators, policymakers, and tool developers toward establishing more reliable, scalable, and legally defensible UAV forensic practices\.

## [К вопросу о внедрении технологий искусственного интеллекта для рассмотрения обращений граждан в органах Роспотребнадзора](../publications/2951656b9a444e009511.md)

Л\.И\. Спирина; Р\.А\. Краснова

В статье рассматривается проблема повышения эффективности работы с обращениями граждан в условиях цифровой трансформации деятельности органов государственной власти\. Актуальность обусловлена наличием дисбаланса между растущим потоком электронных обращений граждан и ограниченными кадровыми ресурсами органов государственной власти\. Цель исследования разработать мероприятия по оптимизации административных процессов посредством внедрения технологий искусственного интеллекта для автоматизации классификации, маршрутизации и подготовки ответов на типовые обращения\. The article discusses the problem of increasing the efficiency of working with citizens&\#x27; appeals in the context of digital transformation of the activities of public authorities\. The relevance is due to the presence of an imbalance between the growing flow of electronic requests from citizens and the limited human resources of public authorities\. The purpose of the study is to develop measures to optimize administrative processes through the introduction of artificial intelligence technologies to automate the classification, routing and preparation of responses to standard requests\.

## [A Kaizen perspective for managing human\-technology continuous improvement in the digital age](../publications/295328d2f282cc7ae00f.md)

Francesco Caputo; Cristina Cervino; Maria Giovanna Corrado; Giuseppe Maria Russo

Purpose The paper examines how digital technologies are transforming continuous improvement \(CI\) by altering the cognitive and relational dynamics that have long underpinned Kaizen\-oriented learning\. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual approach, drawing on insights from CI, organizational learning and digital transformation\. It establishes an interpretive framework focusing on cognitive offloading as a pivotal mechanism connecting technology adoption with the decline of participatory improvement routines\. Findings Digital technologies can significantly speed up decision\-making and streamline processes\. However, there is a downside: their widespread use may reduce our ability to reflect, learn from experience and solve problems\. When we start relying too much on technology for cognitive tasks, we risk becoming efficient in a procedural sense but socially vulnerable\. This can weaken human skills that are essential for viable improvement\. Practical implications The paper presents a conceptual model and practical guidelines for managers interested in developing CI systems that focus on maintaining discretion, fostering a strong learning environment and encouraging collective sense\-making instead of merely optimizing execution\. Originality/value Thanks to the adoption of Kaizen principles, the paper advances the discussion on CI by highlighting the fact that cognitive offloading poses a risk not only to individuals but also to organizations, particularly in environments that rely heavily on digital technology\.

## [The image of scientists among neurodivergent children: a pilot study](../publications/295b8c45e343690e6b3e.md)

Antonia Maria Alves da Silva; Ygor Raphael Gomes Eloy; Henrique Luis do Carmo e Sá; Adriana Rolim Campos

Abstract This pilot study aimed to explore how a specific group of neurodivergent students in the 4th and 5th grades of elementary school represent scientists through drawing\. To this end, the Draw\-a\-Scientist Test \(DAST\) was administered to 7 neurodivergent children with a diagnosed Autism Spectrum Disorder \(ASD\) who participated in the Young Scientists Project\. The analysis of the drawing data was conducted using a multimodal vision\-language model \(ChatGPT, GPT\-4o version\) with the prompt “Evaluate the drawings using the Draw\-a\-Scientist Test checklist”, followed by independent researcher review to ensure consistency and contextual interpretation\. Within this small pilot cohort \( n = 7\), the drawings predominantly contained visual features commonly associated with traditional representations of scientists, featuring laboratory instruments, a predominantly laboratory environment, and male figures in 6 of the 7 drawings\. Representations of scientists in diverse real\-world contexts, or utilizing digital technology, books, or chemical formulas, were absent\. While strictly illustrative and limited by the small sample size, these preliminary observations suggest a reliance on conventional perceptions of scientific figures among these participants\. These preliminary observations warrant further investigation using larger cohorts to evaluate whether tailored, inclusive pedagogical strategies can broaden perceptions of science\.

## [Internet of Things: Embedded Technologies, Smart Applications, and Future Directions](../publications/295ee5c4f16688673e11.md)

Prof\. N\. M\. Kolhe Sonwane Vishakha; Dr\. H\. B\. Jadhav Prof\. D\. S\. Kshirsagar

The Internet of Things \(IoT\) connects physical objects through sensors, embedded processors, and communication interfaces\. These devices can collect and share data, helping systems respond automatically to changing conditions\. This review offers a structured overview of IoT’s development, enabling technologies, practical applications, and the challenges that affect reliable deployment\. It draws primarily on a review article by Yalli, Hasan, and Badawi, which explores IoT’s evolution and its connections to wireless sensor networks, cloud and edge computing, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain\. The paper follows the flow of a typical IoT system, from sensing and communication to data processing and action\. It discusses applications in smart homes, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, education, and energy management, as well as practical challenges such as limited device resources, network delays, compatibility between systems, privacy, cybersecurity, and maintenance\.

## [CIDADES INTELIGENTES E INFRAESTRUTURA SUSTENTÁVEL: APLICAÇÕES DA ENGENHARIA DE DADOS, INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL E ENERGIAS RENOVÁVEIS](../publications/296cb97fa3ec410ab900.md)

As cidades concentram a maior parte da demanda por energia, mobilidade e serviços e, por isso, tornaram\-se o principal laboratório de soluções digitais voltadas à sustentabilidade\. Este artigo analisa como a engenharia de dados, a inteligência artificial \(IA\) e as energias renováveis podem ser articuladas na construção de infraestruturas urbanas sustentáveis\. Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa de literatura, de abordagem qualitativa, apoiada em quinze fontes entre artigos científicos internacionais, relatórios técnicos e documentos normativos brasileiros publicados entre 2014 e 2025\. A análise organiza o tema em cinco camadas \(coleta, engenharia de dados, modelos de IA, operação e governança\) e discute ganhos reportados, barreiras e implicações para o contexto brasileiro\. Os resultados indicam que o desempenho das aplicações de IA depende menos do algoritmo isolado e mais da qualidade e da interoperabilidade dos dados, da previsibilidade da oferta renovável e de arranjos institucionais capazes de orientar a tecnologia para finalidades públicas\. Conclui\-se que a vantagem brasileira em matriz elétrica renovável só se converterá em cidades mais eficientes e justas se vier acompanhada de investimento em dados, governança e participação social\.

## [A Study on the Current Status of Cash Logistics and Future Analysis Based on Artificial Intelligence and Industry 5\.0](../publications/2972f67e9de772161c90.md)

Mahmut Sayar; Ozan ATEŞ; Tuğbay Burçin Gümüş; Gözde Ulutagay

The significance of logistics and SCM has grown due to intense global competition, disaster and the future pandemics\. Additionally, the high cost of logistics processes is also increasing the cost and environmental impact of production\. This study analyses the current state of research in the field of cash logistics and identifies future development trends based on methodological findings\. In the course of the present study, a total of 78 academic articles published between 2006 and 2024 and retrieved from the WoS, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases were examined\. The primary analytical approach employed was bibliometric mapping and thematic content analysis, supported by MAXQDA and VOSviewer\. The findings indicate that the literature focuses primarily on operations research, constrained vehicle routing, AI\-based ATM demand forecasting, and the optimization of physical security risks\. The analysis results demonstrate that ML and ANN have a significant impact on cost minimization and operational accuracy\. In view of these findings, specific recommendations have been developed for industry research and applications\. In accordance with the points, it is recommended that human\-machine collaboration be strengthened within the framework of Industry 5\.0\. Furthermore, dynamic optimization algorithms such as deep reinforcement learning, blockchain\-based security protocols, and autonomous vehicle systems should be integrated into cash networks\.

RII used to Quantifies perceived factor importance for Maps structural dependencies and hierarchy ISM is used\. Fuzzy DEMATEL Identifies direct or indirect causal drivers despite expert ambiguity\. ## [A GB\-SAR slope displacement interval prediction method based on FA\-VAG feature transfer and an improved sparrow search algorithm](../publications/298d9b3a5df908ca53d2.md)

Y\. Dai; ZiWei Zhao; XiaoDong Gan; Songlin Liao

Slope displacement interval prediction quantifies uncertainty in future deformation and supports slope monitoring and early warning\. This study extends the point\-prediction FA\-VAG backbone previously reported by Gan et al\. rather than presenting that backbone as a new model\. The new contribution is an interval\-prediction layer that transfers the pretrained FA\-VAG hidden states, reduces them by Principal Component Analysis \(PCA\), fuses them with multi\-step point forecasts, and maps the fused representation to non\-crossing bounds using a Random Vector Functional Link Network \(RVFLN\)\. A prior\-informed improved Sparrow Search Algorithm \(SG\-ISSA\) then optimizes the RVFLN output weights\. For the prespecified target point 7, the framework achieved PICP/MPIW/CWC values of 0\.90/5\.97/5\.97 for five\-step prediction and 1\.00/8\.74/8\.74 for seven\-step prediction\. Independent external validation yielded 0\.90/58\.82/58\.82 for five\-step prediction\. These results support the interval\-extension framework on the two evaluated datasets; additional probabilistic baselines and harmonized reruns of the ablation study remain necessary\.

## [Simplification and LLM\-assisted reworking: A modular prompting approach for the comprehension of expository texts](../publications/298fbb66c7b61c1deb64.md)

Verónica Sofía D’Angelo

La comprensión de textos expositivos académicos constituye un desafío persistente en el ámbito universitario, en parte debido a rasgos como la alta densidad informacional, la complejidad sintáctica y estructuras lingüísticas abstractas —nominalizaciones, construcciones impersonales—\. A partir de aportes de la psicología cognitiva y la psicolingüística, este trabajo sostiene que la dificultad de los textos no reside únicamente en su complejidad conceptual, sino en la forma en que ese contenido se codifica lingüísticamente: las estructuras agente\-acción\-objeto, alineadas con el orden de los eventos, facilitan el procesamiento, mientras que las nominalizaciones, la voz pasiva y la sintaxis densa incrementan la carga inferencial, especialmente en lectores novatos\. Retomando marcos recientes de caracterización del prompting en contextos académicos, se propone un protocolo modular de simplificación asistida mediante modelos de lenguaje generativos\. El protocolo comprende cinco módulos de transformación —desnominalización de procesos, explicitación de agentes, segmentación sintáctica, explicitación relacional e integración de ejemplos disciplinares— y un módulo transversal de metacomprensión que visibiliza las transformaciones realizadas\. Cada módulo se organiza en torno a un fundamento teórico, un rasgo objetivo, una regla de transformación, criterios de control y una instrucción operativa\. Se ilustra la aplicación mediante cuatro casos disciplinares \(sociología, biología, economía, derecho\)\. El enfoque distingue complejidad conceptual de complejidad discursiva, ofreciendo una alternativa sistemática y flexible a la simplificación automática tradicional\. Entre las limitaciones se destaca la ausencia de validación empírica con usuarios, señalada como línea prioritaria de investigación futura\.

## [A deep feature\-based approach for classifying flue gas pollutants and hazard identification using pyramid\-dilated temporal convolution networks](../publications/2991cdd4e886b68da239.md)

Nowadays, real\-world monitoring and accurate prediction for toxic gas concentration have gained much attention from researchers, as it provides great work in emergency validation situations and rescue works\. But, choosing the best design and also validating the most suitable safety measures are difficult due to the lack of execution of the important field examinations under emission regulations\. So, a deep learning\-based flue gas analysis model is implemented for hazard detection\. Here, required samples are gathered from benchmark resources and features are extracted through Convolutional\-Autoencoder with Spatial–Temporal Attention \(CA\-STA\)\. The flue gas classification is performed using a Pyramid Dilated\-based Adaptive Temporal Convolution Network \(PD\-ATCN\), where the extracted features are given as inputs\. The flexibility of the suggested approach is enhanced by fine\-tuning the parameters of PD\-ATCN using Improved Random Variable\-based Cray Fish Optimization \(IRV\-CFO\)\. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated through diverse performance metrics, which show higher robustness\. In the accuracy analysis, the developed IRV\-CFO\-PD\-ATCN gained superior typical flue gas pollutants classification and hazards identification outcome as 95\.11% for dataset 1 and 92\.6% for dataset 2, compared to baseline approaches\. ## [Thirty\-Two Theses and What Would Refute Them](../publications/2998978a41105b3b25c9.md)

Dirk de Pol

Abstract This register deposits thirty\-two theses on the Omegacene, a condition without precedent in which intelligent systems, biological and artificial, are beginning to read and deliberately rewrite their own foundations: genes, neural states, and program code\. Developed as part of the Omegacene project at omegacene\.com, these theses establish a framework for examining the emerging transformation of intelligence, life, and civilization\. They concern the concepts through which this condition can be understood, the six political spaces in which its future is being decided, the technologies driving it, and the institutions and social orders that must respond\. Each thesis is explained so that it can be understood without prior knowledge and carries four test entries: what it rests on, what would support it, what would refute it, and by when an answer seems possible\. Each is also classified according to whether future developments can decide its validity\. Cases known at the date of deposit serve to formulate the hypotheses; subsequent developments provide the basis for testing them\. For the first thesis to fall due, a prediction about Germany by the end of 2028 is deposited in advance, including case selection, measures, and decision rules\. The purpose of this deposit is to establish a timestamped record of the Omegacene&\#x27;s testable claims\. Two theses fall due in 2028, three by 2030 or 2032, nine by 2035, three by 2040, two by 2045, and one by 2046\. Four are observed continuously, one of them without scoring\. Eight carry no deadline because no period is known within which they could be decided\. The reckoning will be published on the stated dates, including results that contradict the author&\#x27;s expectations\. The register is part of the broader intellectual undertaking documented at omegacene\.com\. Its purpose is not to predict a predetermined future, but to make claims about the Omegacene explicit, traceable, and open to correction as that future unfolds\.

## [Singh, Mayank: There Is No Ultimate Foundation: There Is Only Depth to Dive \(A Phenomenological Inquiry into Seeing, Existence, Process, and the Imagination of Separation\)](../publications/299985e636e4ca9ad8ef.md)



Human beings continually search for foundations that can explain existence, reality, consciousness, and being\. This search often assumes that whatever exists must ultimately depend on an internal principle, an external cause, an absolute beginning, or a final reality\. This paper questions that assumption through a phenomenological inquiry into seeing, experience, thought, and the continuity of existence\. Its central proposition is that there is no ultimate foundation to be established; there is only the depth of what is, and without seeing, there is no diving into that depth\. Existence is approached not as a completed object requiring a final explanation, but as what is already happening through connection, separation, creation, dissolution, and transformation\. These processes are neither denied nor reduced to illusion\. Instead, the paper questions whether their occurrence requires an ultimate ground outside or beneath them\. It further examines how thought transforms distinctions into ideas of absolute separation, how the observer imagines a position outside what is observed, and how concepts such as zero, infinity, oneness, and ultimate reality can become imagined foundations when treated as final metaphysical answers\. The inquiry also distinguishes direct seeing from the recognition and interpretation shaped by prior knowledge, social conditioning, and inherited beliefs\. Seeing is not presented as a technique for attaining an ultimate state or as another philosophical doctrine\. Rather, it concerns the encounter with what is happening before an explanation is mistaken for the whole of what is\. The paper concludes that the absence of an ultimate foundation does not end inquiry\. It leaves inquiry open to depth without a predetermined destination\. \(direct link \)

## [GOVERNING INNOVATION: POLITICAL INSTITUTIONS, BUSINESS STRATEGIES, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT IN THE ERA OF INTELLIGENT TECHNOLOGIES](../publications/299a36933b4188fff593.md)

Ahmad Reshad Rahimi; Fazel Rabi Mohammad Naser; Mohammad Hanif Rasekh; Abdull Samim Adib

Globally, smart technologies, particularly artificial intelligence \(AI\) is proliferating quickly and reshaping political institutions, business practices, healthcare delivery systems, and civil infrastructure development\. This review discusses how governments, organizations, health systems, and infrastructure planners are adjusting governance, strategic frameworks, and engineering practices to embrace AI\-enabled innovation, while managing risks\. We used a narrative review methodology, synthesizing peer\-reviewed literature, policy reports, and institutional publications published between 2016 and 2026 obtained from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases\. The review identifies five interconnected themes: \(1\) The changing role of political institutions in regulating AI through policy frameworks and digital governance initiatives; \(2\) Business adoption strategies for AI integration, including automation of decision\-making and transformation of the workforce; \(3\) AI applications in healthcare systems, including diagnostics and patient care, along with ethical and equity concerns; \(4\) Integration of intelligent systems in civil engineering and infrastructure, including smart construction, structural health monitoring, and resilient urban planning; and \(5\) Broader social implications such as algorithmic bias, labor displacement, and digital inequality\. Findings suggest that while intelligent technologies produce significant efficiency and innovation gains across sectors, fragmented regulatory approaches and uneven institutional capacity create governance gaps that are disproportionately borne by vulnerable populations and under\-resourced infrastructure systems\. The review finds that effective governance of AI requires coordinated multi\-stakeholder frameworks that include political oversight, responsible business practices, equitable healthcare policy, and resilient infrastructure planning\. Future research should explore comparative cross\-national governance models and longitudinal assessments of AI’s socioeconomic and infrastructural impact\.

## [Facial sentiment and verbal content in harmony: theory and evidence](../publications/29aad68c0ad78b20ea35.md)

Seongeun Bae; Youngjae Shim; Sihyun An; Joonkyo Shim; Hyunsoo Yoon; Kwangwon Ahn

Identifying the sentiment in policy announcements helps analyze shifts in underlying stances and signals embedded in policy announcements\. Previous studies have mainly focused on either text\-based approaches or non\-verbal cues in relation to housing policies, resulting in a limited comprehension of interactions between them\. This study aims to examine the relationship between the facial sentiment of housing policy announcers and the quantitative features of their speech transcripts\. We first utilize a deep learning model to extract the facial sentiment embedded in housing policy announcers\. Subsequently, we calculate the scaling exponent and employ the controlled growth process model to extract a text cohesion from policy announcers’ transcripts\. Lastly, we examine how both verbal and non\-verbal cues interact with each other in terms of housing policy announcements\. This study exhibits three notable findings: \(1\) the facial sentiment of policy announcers varies in accordance with the heterogeneity in policy stances, \(2\) the quantitative features of policy transcripts also reflect the heterogeneous policy stances; and therefore, \(3\) there is a macroscopic interaction between housing policy announcers’ facial sentiment and their verbal contents\. Agents can benchmark the research framework to establish a structured approach to effectively analyze the far\-reaching effects of housing policies\. Policymakers can utilize our approach to quantitatively assess current policy stances by exploring the paths of implemented policies\. Additionally, market analysts can leverage these insights to track policy consistency over time, improving their understanding of regulatory trends and enhancing their comprehension of the government’s policy trajectory\.

## [VPS13A Disease \(Chorea‐Acanthocytosis\) in Puerto Rico; New Genetic and Clinical Observations](../publications/29b34d4ef5e984538271.md)
