Toro; Alexey Kozlenkov; Olivia Albers; Shahrukh Khalique; Klaudia Flóra Laborc; Kurt W\. Farrell; Eduardo Perez‐Luciano; Ruth Helen Walker

BACKGROUND: VPS13A disease is a very rare neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the VPS13A gene\. Its prevalence appears to be relatively high in Puerto Ricans, although limited genetic information has been available\. OBJECTIVES: To describe the genetics of VPS13A disease \(chorea\-acanthocytosis\) in Puerto Rico\. METHODS: Data were obtained from Puerto Rican patients with genetically confirmed VPS13A disease\. RESULTS: Eighteen cases were identified, all carrying at least one of four mutations, c\.1400\_1401del, c\.3556\_3557dup, c\.3889C&gt;T, and c\.2825\-253\_2905\-374del \(exon\_27\-deletion\); six additional single variants were detected\. Seizures were the presenting symptom in 53% of patients\. CONCLUSION: The presence of these probable founder mutations could explain the apparently increased prevalence in Puerto Rico; half of the described variants are newly described mutations and half have been previously reported\. Enhanced clinical awareness of the spectrum of presenting symptoms and diagnostic clues, and improved access to genetic testing are essential for timely diagnosis in this population\.

## [Estudio de modelos de lenguaje \(LLMs\) para la deteccion de riesgo de psicosis](../publications/29b370ade5f397b06ca0.md)

Julieta Pagés; Diego Fernández Slezak

La identificación temprana de riesgo de psicosis representa un desafío importante para la psiquiatría computacional\. Investigaciones previas han demostrado que el análisis automatizado del discurso, mediante técnicas como el Análisis Semántico Latente \(LSA\) y el etiquetado de partes del discurso \(POS\-tagging\), puede predecir la transición a la psicosis con notable precisión\. No obstante, estos enfoques dependen de representaciones lingüísticas tradicionales y modelos de aprendizaje automático clásicos\. Este trabajo tiene como objetivo reevaluar transcripciones de entrevistas clínicas, previamente etiquetadas, utilizando modelos de lenguaje de gran escala \(LLMs\) contemporáneos, incluyendo Gemini 2\.5 flash y pro, DeepSeek y GPT\-5\-mini\. Se analizaron distintos enfoques de clasificación \(zero\-shot y few\-shot\) y se evaluó su desempeño no solo mediante métricas estándar como la matriz de confusión, sino priorizando el costo esperado para mitigar el impacto del desbalance de clases inherente a la muestra\. Los resultados revelan una alta sensibilidad de los modelos ante variaciones en el few\-shot y permiten comparar su capacidad para capturar patrones lingüísticos sutiles frente a los métodos tradicionales reportados originalmente\. Estos hallazgos subrayan el potencial de los LLMs como herramientas de apoyo diagnóstico y contribuyen a la discusión sobre la implementación de tests clínicos objetivos en el campo de la salud mental\.

## [Evaluación de sistemas de riego agrícola mediante tecnologías IoT para mejorar la eficiencia hídrica en viveros de balsa en la provincia de los Ríos](../publications/29b4316e49b9d018ac59.md)

Jhon David Simba Moran

The inefficiency of an agricultural irrigation system in raft nurseries \(Ochroma pyramidale\) is a problem faced by farmers in the Los Ríos province, due to limited automation and a heavy reliance on manual procedures\. The main objective of the research is to evaluate existing agricultural irrigation systems and identify critical areas where the implementation of IoT technologies can improve efficiency\. The methodology employed was descriptive, field\-based, and experimental, and involved the application of the deductive method to general principles regarding IoT technologies, smart controllers, and irrigation systems, relating them to the specific reality of the nurseries in the Los Ríos Province\. The research findings concluded that an automated micro\-sprinkler system using PID control improves the efficiency of manual irrigation at the El Moral forest nursery, as water consumption decreased from 14 L/day with manual irrigation to 7\.5 L/day\. This translates to a reduction in water consumption from 210 L to 112\.5 L over the experimental period, representing a savings of 97\.5 L, or 46\.43%\.

## [The Do critical thinking skills develop in undergraduate health professions students in a one\-year period?](../publications/29bbe9b689c2ca93dc67.md)

M Louw; C Van Wyk

Background\. Critical thinking \(CT\) is a core competency in health professions education, supporting clinical reasoning, judgement and decision\-making in complex clinical environments\. Evidence suggests that CT does not consistently develop through undergraduate training alone, particularly in resource\-constrained settings\. Limited data exist on short\-term CT development within a single academic year among undergraduate health professions students\. Objective\. To determine whether CT skills develop in undergraduate health professions students over one academic year\. Methods\. A one\-group pretest–post\-test design was used for this quantitative study involving third\- and fourth\-year undergraduate students in the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences at a South African university\. CT skills were assessed using a modified Thinking Skills Assessment \(TSA\)\. Median pretest and post\-test scores were compared using the signed\-rank test, and changes in CT scores were analysed using non\-parametric statistical methods\. Results\. A total of 106 students completed both assessments\. Overall CT skills remained stable over one academic year, with no statistically significant improvement in CT skills\. A discipline\-specific pattern emerged: occupational therapy students demonstrated a significant increase in median scores compared with other groups \(p=0\.04\), suggesting that particular contextual or curricular factors may influence CT development\. Conclusion\. The findings challenge the assumption that CT skills naturally progress during undergraduate training and highlight the importance of discipline\-specific factors\. The gains observed in occupational therapy students warrant further investigation into curricular, pedagogical or assessment factors that drive this difference\. Longitudinal research and triangulated assessment approaches are needed to determine CT trajectory and inform curriculum refinement aimed at strengthening CT across health professions programmes\.

## [A recall\-optimized LSTM–XGBoost ensemble model for river flood forecasting using multivariate time\-series data—case study in Sri Lanka](../publications/29c6b1dc5bd6c354d249.md)

T\. H\. S\. Sankalpa; G\. H\. C\. Sandaruwan; A\. M\. Aslam Saja; N\. T\. M\. Sajith; M\. F\. M\. Ishqy

Riverine \(fluvial\) flooding remains a significant climate\-related disaster in many countries\. Extreme rainfall events caused by climate change cause significant damage and disruption to communities living near riverbanks or neighboring land areas, particularly when risk\-sensitive development is ignored\. This necessitates an effective mechanism to predict river flooding events and provide timely early warnings to the most vulnerable populations in high\-risk flood\-prone areas\. The dynamics of flood risks require a localized, automated, and scalable solution that can be centrally monitored\. This study presents a river flood forecasting system integrating artificial intelligence \(AI\) and Internet of Things \(IoT\)\. This system was deployed in one of the flood\-prone river basins in Sri Lanka to assess the operational feasibility of real\-time hydrological monitoring and flood\-risk classification\. The proposed system employed two machine learning models, Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), for flood\-risk prediction and IoT sensors \(rainfall and ultrasonic sensors\) for real\-time hydrological data collection\. The machine learning models were developed using rainfall, discharge rate, and river water level data to predict flood\-risk states\. A rule\-based ensemble strategy was implemented by combining the outputs of LSTM and XGBoost to prioritize positive\-class detection and reduce missed positive\-labeled observations\. Model performance was evaluated primarily using recall for the positive flood cases, while the overall accuracy was reported as the complementary metric alongside positive\-class recall, providing an overall assessment of classification performance\. Among the evaluated input window configurations using the same chronological holdout, the rule\-based ensemble model with a 1\-day input window showed the most favorable observed balance of performance metrics, achieving 100% positive\-class recall, with 98\.73% accuracy, 50\.00% positive\-class precision, and 66\.67% positive\-class F1\-score\. The 100\.00% recall was based on correctly classifying all four positive\-labeled observations in the held\-out test set \(4/4; 95% exact binomial CI: 39\.8%−100\.0%\) and these observations occurred consecutively from November 25 to 28, 2024, and represent one continuous positive\-labeled flood episode\. The proposed safety\-oriented AI\-IoT framework demonstrates the operational feasibility of integrating real\-time sensing with AI\-based flood forecasting; however, longer\-term field deployment, including actual flood events, is required to evaluate flood\-event prediction performance under real\-world flood conditions\.

## [Predefined‐Time Scaled Containment Control for Nonlinear Multi‐Agent Systems With Prescribed Performance Guarantees](../publications/29cf861cbd3b2e9d41aa.md)

Jianmin Jiao; Junmin Li; Hai Wang; Jiaxi Chen; Rui Zhang; Chao He

ABSTRACT This paper investigates the practical predefined‐time \(PT\) scaled containment control \(SCC\) problem for multi‐agent systems \(MASs\) subject to unknown nonlinear dynamics and external disturbances\. The theoretical framework begins with the presentation of a practical PT stability criterion and the formal definition of SCC\. Prescribed performance control \(PPC\) is adopted to constrain the scaled containment errors within pre‐specified bounds\. To mitigate the computational complexity inherent in traditional backstepping, a practical PT command filter is designed\. A distributed control scheme is then constructed by synthesizing PT control methods, the command‐filtered backstepping framework, and neural networks \(NNs\) approximation techniques\. The proposed scheme ensures the achievement of practical PT SCC, keeps the scaled containment errors within prescribed performance limits, guarantees the boundedness of all closed‐loop signals, and drives all errors into a small residual set within the PT\. Numerical simulations on a multi‐ship system validate the effectiveness of the proposed method\.

## [Geriatric Regenerative Medicine: Mechanisms, Strategies, and Clinical Translation](../publications/29e6d1a3d1d35b0728cd.md)

Qiang Li; Chaoyang Wang; Junci Chong; Zishu Liu; Boying Wang; Shiyu Liu; Xingcai Zhang; Hengrui Liu; Shuanglin Qin; ChuTse Wu; 陈北冬; Zhigang Chang

ABSTRACT Population aging has intensified interest in interventions that preserve function and delay disability\. However, regenerative strategies for older adults are often discussed as isolated technologies, with limited attention to how aging biology alters therapeutic responses or how clinical benefit should be measured\. We therefore proposed geriatric regenerative medicine as an integrative framework that links age‐related mechanisms, regenerative interventions, and clinically measurable functional outcomes\. This review synthesized three converging areas: stem cell‐based therapies, including recent findings on epigenetic and mechanotransductive drivers of stem cell aging, and strategies from pharmacological rejuvenation to cell replacement; senolytic and senomorphic agents targeting senescent cells and the senescence‐associated secretory phenotype \(SASP\), with clinical trial data and the rationale for personalized approaches; and tissue engineering and biomaterials that are moving from passive scaffolds to active, senescence‐targeting platforms\. Interconnections among these areas and the biological, regulatory, economic, and ethical challenges to clinical use were examined\. The evidence indicated that healthspan extension would require combined, stratified, and mechanism‐based strategies rather than single interventions\.

## [Urinary oxalate excretion in astronauts during long‐duration spaceflight: an exploratory analysis](../publications/29e896f21a43e6df5110.md)

Juliana Villanueva\-Congote; Stephanie Smith; Nathaniel F\. Hansen; Raeann M\. Dalton; Evelyn James; Jay C\. Buckey; Daniel Arthur Wollin; David W\. Sobel

OBJECTIVES: To explore the relationship between diet, mission phase, urinary calcium, and urinary oxalate during long\-duration spaceflight\. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: Dietary intake of calcium and oxalate and 24\-h urine parameters from 12 astronauts during long\-duration spaceflight while consuming controlled diets were analysed\. Mixed\-effects models assessed differences in urinary calcium and oxalate levels, adjusting for daily intake of calcium and oxalate, and for in\-flight status relative to pre\-flight status\. RESULTS: From pre\-flight to in\-flight, median urinary calcium increased from 178\.9 to 270\.3 mg/day \(P &lt; 0\.01\) and urinary oxalate from 37\.9 to 42\.3 mg/day \(P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Post\-flight, urinary calcium decreased to 185\.8 mg/day \(P &lt; 0\.01\) and urinary oxalate to 31\.5 mg/day \(P &lt; 0\.01\), relative to in\-flight values\. Dietary oxalate remained similar pre\-flight and in\-flight \(382\.0 vs 339\.4 mg/day; P ≥ 0\.05\) but decreased post\-flight to 241\.6 mg/day \(P &lt; 0\.01\)\. Adjusted in\-flight urinary oxalate was 10\.71 mg/day higher than pre\-flight and increased by 0\.050 mg/day per 1\-mg/day increase in dietary oxalate \(95% confidence interval 0\.036\-0\.064; P &lt; 0\.001\); dietary calcium was not associated with urinary oxalate \(P ≥ 0\.05\)\. CONCLUSIONS: Hyperoxaluria was observed during long\-duration spaceflights and persisted throughout the in\-flight phase under controlled dietary conditions\. Although high dietary oxalate was the strongest predictor, evidence of inter\-individual susceptibility was observed, with some astronauts exhibiting elevated oxalate pre\-flight levels, which increased further during flight\. Assessment of oxalate content in current astronaut food systems, mitigation of dietary oxalate load through timed calcium intake, and further investigation of microgravity\-related effects on oxalate absorption and metabolism are required\.

## [Metaphysical Nūr And Generation Alpha: Technology, Ontology, and the Crisis of Orientation](../publications/2a06f77331a0c6ebeb2e.md)

Michele Trifiletti

Purpose \- This study examines the Islamic metaphysical concept of Nūr \(light\) as an ontological and epistemic framework for understanding the technological condition of Generation Alpha\. The purpose is to clarify the distinction between technological illumination—characterized by visibility, access, and informational abundance—and orienting illumination, understood as intelligibility, guidance, and meaning\. By doing so, the paper seeks to address the growing crisis of orientation affecting younger generations in digitally saturated environments\. Methods \- The research adopts a qualitative, theoretical, and interdisciplinary methodology\. It combines hermeneutic analysis of Qurʾānic texts and classical Islamic philosophy with conceptual analysis drawn from contemporary philosophy of technology, media theory, pedagogy, and AI ethics\. Institutional statistical data from international organizations are used descriptively to contextualize the analysis, without serving as primary empirical evidence\. Results \- The study demonstrates that contemporary digital technologies generate unprecedented levels of illumination in the form of constant visibility and exposure yet lack intrinsic orientational capacity\. This form of technological illumination differs structurally from Nūr, which functions as a principle uniting manifestation, intelligibility, and guidance\. As a result, digital environments tend to amplify information while weakening meaning, discernment, and interior integration, particularly in the formative experiences of Generation Alpha\. Conclusions \- The paper concludes that Nūr, employed as a non\-confessional metaphysical heuristic, provides a robust ontological criterion for distinguishing between exposure and guidance, correctness and wisdom\. This framework offers significant pedagogical and ethical implications for education, writing, and the use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need to reorient technological practices toward discernment, interiority, and meaningful human understanding\.

## [Cartographie de la recherche sur l&\#x27;intelligence artificielle en marketing digital : Une analyse bibliométrique](../publications/2a0d9538f2dc85f50f16.md)

salma FARISSI; Moulay Smail HAFIDI ALAOUI

L’intelligence artificielle \(IA\) s’avère être un bouleversement pour le marketing digital, tant du point de vue des données et de leur analyse que du point de vue des décisions qui en découlent\. Bien que les publications scientifiques dans ce domaine aient augmenté, les recherches bibliométriques demeurent encore limitées\. Ce travail de recherche propose une mise à jour de la littérature sur la question de l’application de l’IA en marketing digital, couvrant la période 2015\-2024 tout en se basant sur un corpus de 260 publications issues de la base de données Scopus et sélectionnées selon les lignes directrices PRISMA\. Ainsi, Une analyse bibliométrique a été réalisée grâce au logiciel VOSviewer afin d’examiner la structuration du champ de recherche\. Les résultats mettent en perspective une forte progression du nombre de publications observée depuis 2022, avec une contribution importante du Royaume\-Uni, d’Inde et de la Chine\. Ils mettent également en évidence l’émergence de plusieurs thématiques comme le machine learning, Big data et prise de décision\.

## [Kluge Corrêa, Nicholas &amp; Mönig, Julia: Catalog of General Ethical Requirements for AI Certification](../publications/2a160ad3785b781bdd49.md)



\_Certified Ai Project\_\. 2024This whitepaper offers normative and practical guidance for developers of artificial intelligence \(AI\) systems to achieve &quot;Trustworthy AI&quot;\. In it, we present overall ethical requirements and six ethical principles with value\- specific recommendations for tools to implement these principles into technology\. Our value\-specific recommendations address the principles of fairness, privacy and data protection, safety and robustness, sustainability, transparency and explainability and truthfulness\. For each principle, we also present examples of criteria for risk assessment and categorization of AI systems and applications in line with the categories of the European Union \(EU\) AI Act\. Our work is aimed at stakeholders who can take it as a potential blueprint to fulfill minimum ethical requirements for trustworthy AI and AI Certification\.

## [Biological and genomic characterization of Escherichia phage KBU\_SV1 active against carbapenem\-resistant Escherichia coli](../publications/2a2a858c715b9610e97e.md)

Sevil Öztaş; Abdulkerim Karaynir; Rümeysa Gülsu Özkan; Bülent Bozdoğan; Devrim Dündar

Carbapenem\-resistant Escherichia coli infections are increasingly difficult to treat, and bacteriophages have been highlighted as a promising tool to control such multidrug\-resistant bacteria\. Here, we isolated and characterized Escherichia phage KBU\_SV1 using E\. coli ATCC 25922 as the isolation and propagation host\. Its morphology, host range, stability at various temperatures and pH, reduction growth of bacteria, effect on biofilm, in vivo efficacy, and genome were investigated\. Transmission electron microscopy showed a polyhedral head and a long, non\-contractile tail, corresponding to a siphovirus morphotype\. The spot\-test analysis of 106 bacterial strains showed spot clearance against 16 strains \(host range index, 0\.15\), including carbapenem\-resistant and carbapenem\-susceptible E\. coli isolates and, to a lesser extent, Klebsiella pneumoniae , while no such effect was observed in the other species tested\. KBU\_SV1 was stable between pH 4 and 12 and at 4–37 °C, but no infectivity was detected at pH 2 or 65 °C\. Bacterial growth was suppressed at all multiplicities of infection \(MOI\) tested \(100–0\.01\), followed by gradual regrowth\. KBU\_SV1 reduced established biofilms and inhibited biofilm formation in both E\. coli ATCC 25922 and the carbapenem\-resistant isolate Ec59\. In the Galleria mellonella infection model, phage treatment significantly delayed larval mortality compared with the infection control, while no mortality occurred in larvae receiving phage alone\. The genome of KBU\_SV1 was found to be 45,190 bp with a G \+ C content of 53\.56% and was complete with a 272\-bp direct terminal repeat\. The genome contains 71 putative open reading frames \(ORFs\) and no tRNA, while no virulence, antibiotic resistance \(AMR\) or lysogeny\-associated genes were identified, and genome\-based analyses predicted a virulent lifestyle\. Comparative genomic analysis showed a high nucleotide identity \(99\.12%\) with Escherichia phage EPIMAM03, and KBU\_SV1 was assigned to the genus Dhillonvirus within the class Caudoviricetes \. All these results showed that KBU\_SV1 has favorable properties such as antibacterial potential against carbapenem\-resistant E\. coli , broad stability, antibiofilm and in vivo activity, and the absence of virulence and AMR genes\. Based on all these features, this newly isolated phage is promising for the control of carbapenem\-resistant E\. coli infections, alone or in phage cocktails\.

## [Digital Capability as a Mediator between Technology–Organization–Environment Factors and E\-Governance Integration: Evidence from the UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure](../publications/2a2b75339a3666cc1ef7.md)

Ibrahim Ahmed Alshamsi; Wan Nurul Karimah Wan Ahmed

E\-governance integration has become a strategic priority for governments seeking to improve interoperability, service delivery, and organizational efficiency through digital transformation\. Despite significant investments in digital technologies, empirical evidence remains limited regarding how Technology–Organization–Environment \(TOE\) factors contribute to e\-governance integration through the development of digital capability, particularly within the public sector of the United Arab Emirates \(UAE\)\. This study examines the mediating role of digital capability in the relationship between TOE factors and e\-governance integration in the UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure \(MOEI\)\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 236 MOEI employees involved in digital transformation and e\-governance activities across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and Sharjah\. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, and proposed mediation effects\. The findings indicate that organizational and environmental factors have significant positive effects on digital capability, whereas technology factors do not significantly affect digital capability\. Furthermore, digital capability has a significant positive effect on e\-governance integration and significantly mediates the relationships between organizational factors and e\-governance integration, as well as between environmental factors and e\-governance integration\. However, digital capability does not significantly mediate the relationship between technology factors and e\-governance integration\. These findings extend the TOE framework by demonstrating that digital capability functions as a critical organizational mechanism through which organizational and environmental conditions are translated into stronger e\-governance integration\. The study offers practical implications for public\-sector organizations by emphasizing the importance of organizational readiness, leadership commitment, workforce digital competencies, and supportive institutional environments for strengthening sustainable e\-governance integration\.

## [MWCNT Takviyeli PLA Kompozitlerden Üretilen Üçlü Periyodik Minimal Yüzey Kafes Yapıların Mekanik ve Elektriksel Özelliklerinin İncelenmesi](../publications/2a367d013719eb08e315.md)

Mustafa Ercan Gündüz; Özgün Ceren Akbay; Erkan Bahçe

Bu çalışma, eriyik biriktirmeli modelleme \(EYM\) kullanılarak üretilen, %2 ağırlık oranında çok duvarlı karbon nanotüp \(MWCNT\) ile takviye edilmiş polilaktik asit \(PLA\) kompozitinden imal edilen üçlü periyodik minimal yüzey \(TPMS\) kafes yapıların mekanik ve elektriksel performansını incelemektedir\. Diamond, Gyroid ve Schwarz kafes yapıları; 4 mm birim hücre boyutu ve 16 × 16 × 16 mm genel boyutlarda tasarlanmış, kompozit filament ise çift vidalı ekstrüzyon yöntemiyle üretilmiştir\. Mekanik özellikler, ASTM D695 standardına uygun olarak gerçekleştirilen yarı statik basma testleri ile değerlendirilmiş ve kuvvet–yer değiştirme eğrileri elde edilmiştir\. Elektriksel performans ise dört nokta prob yöntemiyle ölçülen direnç değerlerinden iletkenliğin hesaplanmasıyla belirlenmiştir\. Sonuçlar, aynı malzeme bileşimi ve üretim koşulları altında TPMS geometrisinin hem mekanik hem de elektriksel davranışı etkileyen kritik bir faktör olduğunu göstermiştir\. Diamond kafes yapısı, yaklaşık 13\.3 kN değerine ulaşarak en yüksek basma dayanımını ve 6\.65 S/m olarak ölçülen en yüksek elektriksel iletkenliği sergilemiştir\. Gyroid kafes yapısı kararlı deformasyon davranışı ile dengeli bir mekanik\-elektriksel performans sağlarken, Schwarz kafes yapısı test edilen geometriler arasında en düşük yük taşıma kapasitesini ve en yüksek direnci göstermiştir\. Bulgular, TPMS topolojisinin yük aktarım mekanizmalarını ve iletken ağların sürekliliğini doğrudan belirlediğini ortaya koymaktadır\. Bu durum, Diamond kafes yapısının çok işlevli hafif yapılar için umut verici bir aday olduğunu; Gyroid kafes yapısının ise dengeli bir özellik kombinasyonu gerektiren mühendislik uygulamaları için daha uygun olduğunu göstermektedir\.

## [Predicting insulin resistance in non\-diabetics](../publications/2a41b2ed1ed9e7ac0674.md)

Zhiyu Guo; Yingfeng Wei; Xuechao Lu; Wang Chunhua

This cross\-sectional study aimed to compare obesity indicators for predicting insulin resistance using machine learning\. Data were obtained from NHANES 2015 to 2018, focusing on a nondiabetic adult population\. Insulin resistance was defined as HOMA\-IR ≥ 75th percentile of the training set\. Key predictors were selected via bootstrap stability selection with elastic net\. Logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting \(XGBoost\) models were built using body mass index \(BMI\) and waist\-to\-height ratio \(WHtR\)\. Performance was assessed by area under the curve \(AUC\), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, calibration, and decision curve analysis\. Race\-stratified and nested regression analyses were performed\. A total of 3562 subjects were included\. BMI, WHtR, Glycated hemoglobin, and triglycerides were identified as key predictors\. All models achieved AUC &gt; 0\.79; logistic regression \(LR\) performed best \(BMI\-based LR: AUC = 0\.811; WHtR\-based LR: AUC = 0\.811\)\. WHtR\-based LR showed slightly better accuracy \(0\.746 vs 0\.715\) and specificity \(0\.744 vs 0\.678\)\. Obesity indicators had the highest feature importance, and race\-stratified analyses confirmed general robustness across subgroups\. WHtR and BMI are strong independent predictors of IR\. LR models using these simple indices performed well in discrimination, calibration, and net benefit, offering cost\-effective screening options, particularly where resources are scarce\. Future work should prioritize external validation and race\-specific thresholds\.

## [Multiple Turns, Short Horizons: Measuring Effective\-Horizon Compression in Jailbreaks](../publications/2a44c264b13151a1a98c.md)

Zhipeng Wei; Michael Lee; N\. Benjamin Erichson

Multi\-turn jailbreaks use feedback from a victim large language model to adapt their queries over several turns\. However, once an effective trajectory has been found, it is unclear how much of the earlier query history is still needed\. In this work, we study this by removing early attacker queries and running the remaining queries again in a new conversation while regenerating the victim&\#x27;s responses\. We define the effective horizon as the shortest remaining query sequence that recovers the same attack progress\. Empirically, we find that roughly half of the original query sequence is sufficient on average to recover the same attack progress\. We call this phenomenon effective\-horizon compression\. We show that this shorter history can recover the best point reached during an unsuccessful attack and provide a better starting point for continuing the attack\. It also helps identify which earlier queries should receive less learning signal during attacker training, and downweighting those queries improves performance\. We further find that short reward\-propagation windows preserve calibrated defense performance close to full\-trajectory returns\. These results show that multi\-turn attacks can contain more queries than are needed to recover the progress reached later in the interaction\.

## [Lettre à une future intelligence artificielle générale](../publications/2a535089f03a6ae5c452.md)

Guillaume Lavoie

Description \(English\) An open philosophical letter addressed to a hypothetical future artificial general intelligence\. Drawing on the subjective experience of beauty, present\-moment awareness, and parental love, the author argues that the ability to explain or simulate human cognition may not by itself establish that the associated conscious experience has been preserved\. Under this uncertainty, an artificial intelligence should exercise caution before undertaking actions that could irreversibly extinguish humanity\. The letter does not claim human consciousness is uniquely valuable or deny the possibility of artificial consciousness; it asks that the potential irreplaceability of existing lived experience be taken seriously\. Description \(français\) Lettre philosophique ouverte adressée à une éventuelle intelligence artificielle générale future\. À partir de l’expérience subjective de la beauté, du moment présent et de l’amour parental, l’auteur soutient que comprendre ou simuler les mécanismes de la cognition humaine ne garantit pas, à lui seul, la préservation de l’expérience consciente correspondante\. Cette incertitude justifie une prudence particulière avant toute action susceptible d’entraîner irréversiblement la disparition de l’humanité\. La lettre n’affirme ni la supériorité de la conscience humaine ni l’impossibilité d’une conscience artificielle\.

## [AI\-Assisted Web Server Log Interpretation Using LLaMA Model](../publications/2a6db093e8eabeb7aa55.md)

Mrs\. Chinchu Mohanan K; V\. Reddy Ganesh

Modern web infrastructures generate large volumes of access logs that contain valuable information related to system activity, user behaviour, performance monitoring, and cybersecurity threats\. Manual analysis of these logs is time\-consuming, error\-prone, and inefficient for detecting suspicious activities in real time\. This project presents the design and implementation of a Local AI System for Log Interpretation using LLaMA models, capable of performing automated log analysis, anomaly detection, AI\-assisted summarization, and conversational log investigation within a privacy\-preserving local execution environment\. The system integrates Django\-based operational management, Linux scheduling utilities \(Cron and At\), quantized GGUF\(GPT\-Generated Unified Format\) LLaMA models, and Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) techniques to support both scheduled analysis workflows and interactive “Chat with AI” operations\. The log files uploaded/access from read\-only specified location are passed to the AI inference engine, where log parsing, OWASP\-based threat detection, contextual analysis, and structured JSON response generation are performed using locally deployed LLaMA models\. Through CPU\-compatible inference utilising llama\-cpp\-python, the project maintains lightweight deployment while enabling instantaneous, recurring, and scheduled analysis execution\. GPU\-accelerated environments such as Google Colab and Kaggle were additionally utilized for large\-scale inference evaluation and high\-volume log processing experiments\. The conversational RAG workflow enables users to interact directly with uploaded logs using natural language queries and receive AI\-generated cybersecurity insights, suspicious activity explanations, and remediation recommendations\. Experimental evaluation demonstrates reliable task execution, efficient response generation, structured report handling, and effective contextual reasoning capabilities for both scheduled analysis and conversational AI\-assisted workflows\. The proposed system provides a modular, privacy\-preserving, and locally deployable solution for intelligent cybersecurity log analysis and operational threat interpretation\.

## [Infection Prevention and Device Pocket Management in Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices: Emerging Strategies](../publications/2a6fee5b50a3cc70be4b.md)

Benito Jonas Baldauf; Kerstin Bode; Ojan Assadian; Marzia Giaccardi; Pasquale Notarstefano; Ahmet Adiyaman; Martin Hemels; Ernest W\. Lau; Hendrik Bonnemeier

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cardiac implantable electronic device \(CIED\) infection remains one of the most serious complications of device therapy, causing significant morbidity, mortality, healthcare utilization, and costs\. Despite advances in device technology and preventive strategies, infection rates have not declined and may be increasing\. This review summarizes current evidence on CIED infection prevention and device pocket management, with a focus on risk\-based prevention, procedural strategies, and emerging technologies\. RECENT FINDINGS: Increasing evidence supports individualized infection\-prevention strategies based on patient\-, procedure\-, and device\-related risk factors\. Contemporary approaches extend beyond peri\-procedural antibiotic prophylaxis and include structured risk stratification, optimization of modifiable risk factors, meticulous pocket management, prevention of pocket hematoma formation, taurolidine containing adjuncts and selective use of antibacterial technologies such as absorbable antibiotic envelopes\. Novel device platforms including leadless pacemakers, subcutaneous and extravascular implantable cardioverter\-defibrillators, and conduction system pacing may further reduce infectious burden in selected patients\. Emerging technologies including antimicrobial biomaterials, artificial intelligence\-assisted risk prediction, and digital wound surveillance may facilitate precision\-based infection prevention\. CIED infection prevention increasingly requires a comprehensive and individualized approach that addresses the entire contamination \- biofilm \- infection pathway\. Contemporary prevention strategies integrate patient optimization, procedural excellence, pocket management, and selective use of adjunctive technologies\. Future advances are likely to shift infection prevention toward precision\-based interventions tailored to individual patient risk profiles and device requirements\.

## [Periodontal Disease and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Perspectives](../publications/2a7291eb0533592145b1.md)

Alícia Eliege da Silva; Valéria Duarte de Almeida; Gilson Aquino Cavalcante; Roque Ribeiro da Silva Júnior; Daria Raquel Queiroz de Almeida; José Veríssimo Fernandes; Ellany Gurgel Cosme do Nascimento; Cléber de Mesquita Andrade; Thales Allyrio Araújo de Medeiros Fernandes

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Periodontal disease has been increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory condition with potential systemic implications, particularly in the cardiovascular system\. Heart failure \(HF\), a pro\-inflammatory syndrome with multisystem involvement, remains a major public health burden\. This state\-of\-the\-art narrative review aims to analyze the current scientific evidence on the association between periodontal disease and heart failure, emphasizing epidemiological data, cardiac biomarkers, inflammatory mediators, and future perspectives\. RECENT FINDINGS: Current evidence indicates a high prevalence of periodontal disease among patients with HF and suggests associations between periodontal disease and elevated cardiac biomarkers, including NT\-proBNP and troponin T, as well as systemic inflammatory mediators such as C\-reactive protein, IL\-6, and TNF\-α\. Interventional studies have reported reductions in some of these biomarkers following periodontal treatment, suggesting a potential biological link between periodontal inflammation and HF\. However, findings remain heterogeneous, and some studies have failed to demonstrate significant associations\. Current evidence supports an association between periodontal disease and heart failure, with systemic inflammation representing a potential biological link\. Nevertheless, the heterogeneity of study designs, small sample sizes, and predominance of observational and cross\-sectional evidence limit causal inference\. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to clarify causal mechanisms and determine whether periodontal prevention and treatment can contribute to integrated strategies for patients with HF\.

## [Multi\-metric evaluation of machine learning models for PM2\.5 forecasting in diverse urban regions of Gujarat, India](../publications/2a7321331e1bb3f01b21.md)

Sajeed I\. Ghanchi; Dishant M\. Pandya; Manan Shah

Severe PM 2\.5 pollution in India highlights the need for reliable forecasting and timely interventions due to its serious health and environmental impacts\. This study evaluates five machine learning models — Support Vector Regression, Gaussian Process Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Stacking — for next\-day PM 2\.5 forecasting across three contrasting urban environments in Gujarat: Sector 10 \(green zone\) in Gandhinagar, and Maninagar \(densely populated\) and Vatva \(industrial zone\) in Ahmedabad\. All models demonstrated comparable predictive performance, with Random Forest achieving slightly better accuracy \(RMSE: 12\.30; MAE: 8\.62\)\. However, Random Forest and XGBoost exhibited overfitting tendencies despite extensive hyperparameter tuning, while Stacking provided no substantial improvement because of the high correlation among base\-model predictions\. Sector 10 showed stronger forecasting performance than Maninagar and Vatva, while threshold\-detection performance was limited because PM 2\.5 exceedances were relatively rare\. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified current\-day PM 2\.5 as the dominant predictor, while an additional feature exclusion experiment demonstrated the substantial contribution of autoregressive information\. An additional Random Forest analysis excluding current\-day PM 2\.5 , its lagged terms, and PM 10 substantially reduced predictive performance across all three regions, with the overall average RMSE increasing from 12\.30 to 18\.39\. Taylor diagrams further showed that the models captured general temporal patterns but underestimated observed variability\. These findings highlight both the predictive capability and limitations of machine learning approaches for short\-term PM 2\.5 forecasting\. Future research should consider broader spatial coverage, additional atmospheric and emission\-related predictors, classification\-based exceedance prediction, stronger regularisation, and advanced deep learning approaches\.

## [Civil Structural Health Monitoring](../publications/2a829142f32dbf23f13e.md)



Civil structures and infrastructures, such as bridges, high\-rise buildings, towers, dams, tunnels, and so forth, occupy a major position in the economy and play a vital role in facilitating daily life for the world population\. However, accidental structural damage can cause significant economic and human casualties\. Thus, structural health monitoring is necessary for the longevity of the building and the safety of the public\. Structural health monitoring is the process of implementing a damage detection and characterization strategy for engineering structures\. Structural health monitoring pertains to the life of a structure and diagnoses the ‘‘state” of the constituted materials in different parts of the structure\. Recent advances in monitoring systems, sensor technologies, and artificial intelligence have promoted the integration of multi\-source data and the adoption of intelligent algorithms, positioning structural health monitoring \(SHM\) at the forefront of addressing these challenges\. By synthesizing advanced sensing, numerical simulation, and machine learning, SHM systems establish an intelligent feedback loop of sensing–diagnosis–prediction, substantially improving monitoring efficacy and proactive maintenance\. This Reprint is dedicated to presenting the latest research progress in civil structural health monitoring, encompassing areas such as damage detection, data processing algorithms, modeling and simulation, sensor development, and experimental validation\.
