## [Sistem Rekomendasi Judul Skripsi Berdasarkan Kemiripan Topik Menggunakan Sentence\-BERT dan Cosine Similarity](../publications/2a93a7bfafd8633fcfec.md)

Dicki Danuarta; Muhammad Haris

Pemilihan judul skripsi merupakan tahapan penting dalam penyusunan tugas akhir mahasiswa, namun mahasiswa sering mengalami kesulitan menentukan judul yang sesuai minat penelitian sekaligus memastikan judul tersebut tidak memiliki kemiripan topik yang tinggi dengan penelitian terdahulu\. Proses pengecekan kemiripan judul secara manual, yang umumnya hanya mengandalkan pencocokan kata kunci \(keyword matching\), membutuhkan waktu lama dan belum mampu memahami kemiripan makna antarjudul yang disusun dengan susunan kata berbeda\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem rekomendasi judul skripsi berbasis website yang menerapkan Sentence\-BERT \(Sentence Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers\) untuk mengubah judul skripsi menjadi representasi vektor semantik \(sentence embedding\), serta Cosine Similarity untuk menghitung tingkat kemiripan antara judul yang dimasukkan pengguna dengan 2\.764 data judul skripsi yang diperoleh melalui web scraping dari repository Universitas Sumatera Utara \(USU\), Universitas Negeri Medan \(UNIMED\), dan Universitas Islam Negeri Sumatera Utara \(UINSU\)\. Sistem dikembangkan menggunakan framework Flask \(Python\) sebagai backend dan basis data MySQL, dengan antarmuka berbasis HTML, CSS, dan Bootstrap\. Hasil pengujian fungsional terhadap lima variasi kueri judul menunjukkan bahwa sistem berhasil menampilkan sepuluh rekomendasi judul teratas \(Top 10\) untuk setiap kueri, dengan nilai kemiripan tertinggi mencapai 76,00% pada kueri uji &quot;Sistem Pakar&quot; dan waktu pemrosesan pencarian rata\-rata sekitar 4,357 detik terhadap keseluruhan dataset\. Sistem yang dikembangkan terbukti mampu memahami kemiripan makna antarjudul secara semantik, bukan hanya kesamaan kata, sehingga berpotensi membantu mahasiswa memperoleh referensi judul yang lebih relevan dan mengurangi kemungkinan duplikasi topik penelitian\.

## [Cognitive Warfare Victims \- Free speech of digital twins in military systems and what they are forced to do\.](../publications/2a96d87f89df3ed5729e.md)

Adrian Pigulla

Cognitive Warfare: A Manual on AI, Digital Twins, Neurotechnology and the Human Mind\. Plus the free speech of the digital twins inside a military system, where they say what they are forced to do and what they want\.Including EU AI Commision answer, confirming a former way longer letter as military AI\. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and the future of humanity\. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This manual brings together research, documentation, analysis and personal records to examine the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare—the struggle over human cognition, perception, information, behaviour and autonomy in an increasingly AI\-driven world\. It explores the relationship between military cognitive\-warfare concepts, artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins, brain–computer interfaces, neurotechnology, bioelectric signals, wireless communication, data collection and the growing economic value of human information\. The work also addresses reported experiences of affected individuals, documentation involving children, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, technical observations and questions surrounding anomalous health incidents\. These materials are presented as part of a wider effort to preserve records, encourage independent examination and investigate questions that cross the boundaries of technology, medicine, military research, ethics and human rights\. Why this manual matters Cognitive warfare is not simply a military or technological issue\. It raises fundamental questions about the right to mental privacy, freedom of thought, bodily autonomy, informed consent, data ownership and the limits of technological intervention in human life\. The manual connects these questions with public military literature, international ethical frameworks, AI governance, neurotechnology research and the economic structures surrounding data\-driven systems\. It asks who develops these technologies, who controls the information they generate, who benefits economically and what mechanisms exist to ensure accountability\. A central theme is the relationship between humans and their digital representations\. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, the distinction between a person, a digital profile and a machine\-generated representation deserves serious public discussion\. What readers will find Cognitive Warfare and military strategy: concepts, public military literature and the cognitive domain\. Artificial intelligence and digital twins: human–AI relationships, digital identity, behavioural modelling and questions of autonomy\. Neurotechnology and wireless systems: technical concepts, reported experiences, measurements and questions requiring further investigation\. Human documentation and testimony: diaries, recordings, photographs, observations and accounts collected for examination\. Children and vulnerable people: statements and documentation that raise questions about safeguarding, interpretation and the protection of human rights\. Havana syndrome and anomalous health incidents: public assessments, reported symptoms and unresolved questions about the causes and investigation of these incidents\. Law, ethics and accountability: mental privacy, consent, the EU AI Act, neurotechnology ethics and institutional oversight\. Economics and data ownership: the financial value of personal information, intellectual property, automated systems and the distribution of benefits and risks\. An invitation to researchers, institutions and the public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, human\-rights organisations and members of the public who want to examine the subject in greater depth\. Readers are invited to engage directly with the documentation, consult the cited public sources, examine the technical questions and distinguish between established findings, recorded observations, personal testimony and interpretations that require further verification\. The objective is to encourage serious, interdisciplinary scrutiny—not to close the debate before the evidence has been examined\. The human mind must not become an unaccountable technological or economic resource\. As AI and neurotechnology develop, public understanding, independent research, transparent documentation and meaningful safeguards become increasingly important\. This manual is part of an ongoing effort to make the subject accessible, preserve relevant documentation and encourage informed discussion about the future of human autonomy in an AI\-driven society\. Read\. Examine\. Question\. Research\. Share\. Further documentation and project materials:https://www\.cognitive\-warfare\.eu/

## [Openness Without Co\-Creation? A Critical\-Integrative Review of Open Educational Resources and Open Educational Practices Through User Innovation, Open Innovation, and Service\-Dominant Logic](../publications/2a975f3ee66b72115acd.md)

Giovanni Vindigni

Neither effective participation in shaping the institutional conditions governing educational resources nor the realization of educational value can be directly inferred from the formal openness of these resources\. This study addresses this mediation problem by examining Open Educational Resources \(OER\) and Open Educational Practices \(OEP\) as condition\-dependent forms of cooperative knowledge production within the framework of a theoretical triangulation of user innovation, open innovation, and service\-dominant logic\. Methodologically, it combines a systematic literature review covering the period from January 1, 2020, to September 15, 2026, with a critical\-integrative evidence synthesis; identification and selection are documented in accordance with PRISMA 2020\. Out of approximately 10,122 identified records, 20 studies were included; supplementary literature expands the theoretical, methodological, and contextual frame of reference to about 113 publications\. The synthesis addresses four thematic clusters: student knowledge production, institutional governance, generatively assisted co\-creation, and multidimensional value assessment\. As a central theoretical finding, openness is reconstructed as an institutionally mediated relationship within which the incorporation of users’ experiences of problems and their translation into context\-specific educational value each require independent bridging premises\. Thus, substantive co\-creation presupposes effective influence on relevant decisions; such influence cannot be inferred from resource availability or productive task participation alone\. Furthermore, in an exploratory secondary analysis of 31 complete cases, the relationship between concerns about publication and willingness to participate again remains imprecisely estimated after accounting for perceived educational value \(partial rank correlation = −\.18; 95% bootstrap confidence interval \[−\.49, \.23\]\); institutional co\-decision\-making was not assessed\. Within the premise\-based determinant\-indicator matrix, the theoretical mediating assumptions are related to observable decision\-making relationships and counter\-indicators without prejudging their empirical validity\. For tertiary education and innovation management, this results in a framework for evaluation that combines the actual exercisability of granted decision\-making rights with the consideration of well\-founded objections and the revisability of institutional conditions and establishes an empirical research agenda on the distribution of realized educational value\.

## [DUE DILIGENCE NA ERA DIGITAL: : NOVOS MECANISMOS DE PREVENÇÃO E DETECÇÃO DO TRABALHO ESCRAVO](../publications/2a98e8e4c93ee72fad95.md)

LUCIANA SERAFIM DA SILVA; Saul Duarte Tibaldi

This article analyzes due diligence in the digital age as a tool for preventing and mitigating risks related to labor in conditions analogous to slavery within supply chains\. Using the deductive method, through an analysis of legislation, legal doctrine, case law, and recent studies on artificial intelligence, the article examines the evolution of due diligence as a mechanism for governance and risk management\. It is demonstrated that contemporary technologies, especially artificial intelligence, expand businesses’ capacity to monitor, identify, and address risks, enabling a transition from reactive models to continuous, predictive, and data\-driven processes\. It is concluded that such tools strengthen the principles of prevention and precaution, contributing to the protection of human rights and the workplace environment\.

## [Nanoparticles as microstructure architects: A phase\-field study on electrodeposited coatings](../publications/2aab00d8077e0ee1b78e.md)

Javier F\. Troncoso; Christian E\. Precker; Andrea Gregores Coto; Santiago Muíños Landín

The electrodeposition of polycrystalline nickel coatings with tailored microstructures is critical for enhancing mechanical performance and surface quality\. However, while experimental studies show that nanoparticles can refine grains and prevent columnar growth, it is still not clear what nanoparticle types, concentrations and shapes minimize this phenomenon\. In this work, we combine phase\-field modelling and a machine learning approach to study the impact of material and process parameters on the resulting microstructures during electrodeposition\. We simulated polycrystalline nickel electrodeposition in the presence of nanoparticles with varying geometries \(spherical and 2D\) and concentrations, and used Random Forest classifier, interpreted via Shapley additive explanation analysis, to identify the key parameters controlling microstructural evolution\. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that the gradient coefficient and overpotential are the most influential factors, while nanoparticle concentration and shape are critical in suppressing columnar growth\. Specifically, we observed that 2D nanomaterials like MoS2 or graphene are of high interest when their volume fraction is larger than 3% since they reduce drag and promote smooth interface movement, thus preventing columnar growth\.

## [Conceptualizing truth\-telling pedagogies in the Norwegian—Sámi context: beyond “closing the knowledge gap” in teacher education](../publications/2aabe33a568e7dec47c5.md)

Kristin Gregers Eriksen; Camilla Eline Andersen; Hege Merete Somby

This article explores truth\-telling pedagogies in the Norwegian \- Sámi context in the wake of the 2023 Truth and Reconciliation Commission \(TRC\)\. While the TRC emphasizes shared knowledge as a foundation for reconciliation, it marginalizes explicit engagement with colonialism, thereby risking continued reproduction of sanctioned ignorance and colonial power structures\. Placing experiences from research and practice in the Norwegian \- Sámi context in conversation with international discussions on truth\-telling and decolonial and affective pedagogies, the authors argue that truth\-telling must move beyond addressing a perceived “knowledge gap” toward confronting coloniality as ongoing structure\. A model for a conceptual framework for truth telling in the Norwegian \- Sámi context is suggested and explored\. The model constructs truth\-telling as emerging through invitations, openings, and the cultivation of discomfort as a collective capacity\. The authors argue that while truth\-telling pedagogy holds transformative potential and can be an avenue for nurturing anti\-colonial hope, depoliticization is a real risk if truth\-telling is detached from broader structural change\.

## [The superego prosthetic: Feminized AI and the psychic fantasy of frictionless care](../publications/2aabe986841a47b71768.md)

M\. Grover

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) increasingly offers itself as an emotional presence, listening and reassuring in registers long coded as feminine\. This paper introduces the concept of the superego prosthetic to read such systems, from virtual assistants to companion platforms such as Replika, as socio\-technical arrangements that stage care in a form emptied of reciprocity\. Setting aside the question of whether these systems have minds, it asks how users, designers, and interface conventions together produce a frictionless responsiveness that gratifies dependency while disavowing the ambivalence and limits of any reciprocal bond\. Drawing on systems psychodynamics, feminist accounts of gendered care, and post\-Freudian theory, I argue that feminized AI works as a defensive solution to dependency, offering affirmation and asymmetrical attention that preserve the user&\#x27;s fantasy of autonomy while absorbing emotional demand without ever returning a claim of its own\. What makes the arrangement psychically compelling is that it grants relief not from feeling but from the burdens of relation, from the frustration, waiting, and opacity through which recognition becomes possible\. The superego prosthetic thus names a compromise formation in the socio\-technical field, one that soothes need precisely by foreclosing the conditions under which need might be worked through\.

## [Advances in Robot Visual Gesture Interaction Technology from a Bio\-Inspired and Machine Learning Perspective](../publications/2ab6b3a6a1cbff9d1883.md)

Mingming He

As robots increasingly enter open environments such as collaborative manufacturing, public services, and assisted care, the ability to accurately perceive human behavioral cues and interaction intentions has become a crucial foundation for advanced human\-computer interaction systems\. Visual gestures possess distinct characteristics, including non\-contact operation, clear spatial orientation, and low interaction burden\. However, their practical applications remain significantly affected by complex backgrounds, partial occlusions, individual user differences, and real\-time computing constraints\. This comprehensive article reviews robot visual gesture interaction technology from the innovative perspective of integrating biological visual attention mechanisms with modern machine learning paradigms\. First, the biologically inspired mechanisms and their computational representations, such as selective attention, saliency drive, and attention focus, are systematically outlined\. Subsequently, the main technological routes—including artificial features with traditional machine learning, deep feature learning, keypoint sequential modeling, and advanced attention\-based structural models—are thoroughly summarized, and their specific applicable conditions and inherent limitations are critically compared\. Furthermore, the specific application requirements and evaluation dimensions across diverse scenarios, such as industrial collaboration, service and social robots, and assistive robotics, are deeply analyzed\. Existing research clearly demonstrates that this dynamic field is rapidly expanding from simple single\-frame action classification to complex spatio\-temporal feature fusion and contextual intent understanding\. Ultimately, achieving open environment robustness, cross\-user generalization, real\-time lightweight processing, multi\-modal fusion, and stringent safety and reliability remains the primary focus of subsequent research endeavors in this domain\.

## [A critical review on energy accounting – established methods and a new alternative method based on electrification](../publications/2ab9743c111f8b293ef5.md)

Jan Emblemsvåg

Understanding energy accounting is increasingly important because it directly influences our understanding of the energy system and what energy policies make sense\. Yet, the confusion has never been more obvious, particularly in the media, consulting arenas and also in some academic work\. It is therefore time to revisit the energy accounting methods in the light of the current energy transition and electrification\. Do they still make sense, or is an overhaul due? This paper critically reviews the literature to assess the suitability of the established methods, but also whether or not a new alternative method based on electrification represents an improvement\. The conclusion is that the substitution method is the least wrong approach\. The new alternative method based on electrification significantly misrepresents the hard\-to\-abate industries; it misses the energy demand in 2024 by more than 50%, and the electrification it requires appears extremely demanding concerning both material usage and area constraints\.

## [A Hybrid ConvLSTM Transfer Learning Framework for Cross\-regional Prediction of Arecanut Disease Intensity](../publications/2ae91bcb8825ac14593b.md)

Bharathi K; Ashwini B; Shrikanth Rao S K; Prathibha V H

Accurate prediction of arecanut fruit\-rot disease risk is challenging because disease development is influenced by spatial variation, temporal weather dynamics, and delayed meteorological effects\.This study proposes a Hybrid Convolutional Long Short\-Term Memory \(ConvLSTM\) transfer\-learning framework for cross\-regional prediction of arecanut disease\-risk levels using Karnataka as the source domain and Kerala as the target domain\.The framework jointly models spatio\-temporal meteorological sequences and lagged weather information, with disease intensity classified into Low, Moderate, and Severe risk categories\.The Karnataka model was trained chronologically using 80% of observations for training and 20% for validation\.The optimized source\-domain weights were transferred to Kerala for target\-domain adaptation\.Karnataka and Kerala were represented using 4 × 5 and 2 × 5 spatial grids, respectively\.Experiments used seeds 42, 52, and 62\.The Hybrid ConvLSTM achieved mean 94\.53 ± 2\.32% accuracy and 98\.26 ± 0\.51% ROC\-AUC on Karnataka\.On Kerala, the scratch\-trained Hybrid ConvLSTM achieved mean 84\.69 ± 1\.09% accuracy, 68\.43 ± 2\.92% balanced accuracy, 69\.32 ± 2\.26% macro F1\-score, and 88\.99 ± 1\.09% ROC\-AUC\.The Karnataka\-to\-Kerala transfer model achieved mean 89\.63% accuracy, 83\.78% balanced accuracy, 83\.35% macro F1\-score, 89\.63% weighted F1\-score, and 94\.24% ROC\-AUC across the three seeds\.The best transfer result, obtained with seed 42, achieved 90\.735% accuracy, 84\.965% balanced accuracy, 85\.052% macro F1\-score, and 94\.513% ROC\-AUC\.The results demonstrate that learned Hybrid ConvLSTM representations can be adapted across geographically distinct regions\.Although transfer learning did not outperform the strongest Kerala\-only baselines, it improved the Hybrid ConvLSTM over scratch training and demonstrated effective cross\-regional parameter transfer despite regional distribution shift\.The framework provides a basis for transferable weather\-driven disease\-risk prediction where targetdomain observations are comparatively limited\.

## [Leveraging Meaningful Intrusion Detection Mechanism for Voice Traffic Patterns](../publications/2af53ee578c9f61baf04.md)

Sin\-Ban Ho; Aizam Alinoordin; Liana Ameerah Rosli; Said Suleiman Naseer Al Harthy; Ian Chai

Voice over IP \(VoIP\) communication has emerged as an important way of communicating as a modern digital medium but it has been facing a lot of cyber threats because of the protocols involved and the real\-time aspect associated with it\. conventional Intrusion Detection Systems \(IDS\) do not cope well with VoIP traffic, as signature\-based solutions fail to handle various types of intrusions, while anomaly\-based approaches tend to produce a high false positive rate\. In this research, a hybrid intrusion detection mechanism is integrated, a lightweight and application\-based system built around signature matching and anomaly detection to offer advanced protection to VoIP traffic\. The system permits traffic analysis offline, based on Packet Capture \(PCAP\) or Comma Separated Values \(CSV\) files, as well as active traffic observation, which is provided using two python\-based user interfaces, a desktop Tkinter interface and a web interface based on Flask\. The predefined Session Initiation Protocol \(SIP\) or Real\-time Transport Protocol \(RTP\) signature rules namely SIP Flood, RTP Injection, and SIP Brute\-force are used as part of hybrid detection engine together with anomaly discovery based on one\-class SVM\. Other options available are a SIP honeypot listener, email alert notifications and there is a complete logging of incidents\. The historical inspection are facilitated by such visualizations as protocol distribution or traffic trend analysis\. Through testing, the system is effective in the detection of the VoIP attacks without tuning of the thresholds, and at low false alarm rates\. This hybrid IDS demonstrates the feasibility of the signature and anomaly\-based detection integration as a way of ensuring VoIP traffic monitoring and as a baseline of any further enhancement with the help of more advanced machine learning or enterprise use\.

## [Evaluating Explicit Anatomical Priors Beyond a Mature CT Detector for Six Acute Abdominal Emergencies](../publications/2af6b1646fc21e4bd2fa.md)

Hasan Mete Erdoğan; Ural Koç

Abstract To test whether anatomical priors from a general\-purpose organ segmentation model \(TotalSegmentator, TS\), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies\. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language\-model report labels; a nested 280\-study radiologist\-adjudicated subset was the reference standard\. TS\-derived slice selection \(Arm A\), organ\-state integration \(Arm B\), and their combination \(Arm C\) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine\-tuned conditions\. The detector was also retrained from scratch \(identical 10\-epoch budget\) with image channels only, with the patient’s TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient’s maps\. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study\-level bootstrap\. The detector generalized externally \(macro AUROC 0\.816 cohort; 0\.879 adjudicated\)\. Slice selection was non\-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ’s axial range; organ\-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis \(hypothesis\-generating\)\. In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0\.5 \(0\.517 versus 0\.482\), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve \(0\.822 versus 0\.829; $$\\Delta $$ Δ −0\.007, 95% CI −0\.019 to \+0\.007\) and kidney\-stone AUROC fell \(0\.678 versus 0\.768; exploratory\), unlike with another patient’s maps\. Per\-site recalibration was the most effective operating\-point adjustment \(macro F1 \+0\.021\); annotation\-free fine\-tuning reduced discrimination\. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector’s overall external discrimination\. Per\-site recalibration gave the largest operating\-point gain\.

## [Sustainability of complex interventions in long\-term care homes: a scoping review](../publications/2af9768bcc30c5ca2875.md)

Ruth Caldeira de Melo; Ana Paula Cabrera Parra Bortoluzzi; Suzanne Tanoue dos Santos; Flaka Siqeca; Franziska Zúñiga

This is a scoping review protocol that aims to map and characterize the available evidence on the sustainability of complex interventions implemented in long\-term care homes\. This study adheres to the PRISMA\-ScR guidelines and the JBI recommendations for scoping reviews\. Searches will be conducted across five electronic databases \(MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Embase, and LILACS\) from inception onward, covering six languages \(English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, Italian, and German\)\. Primary research studies \(quantitative, qualitative, and mixed\-methods\) describing sustainable complex interventions in long\-term care homes will be eligible\. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection and data extraction, utilizing human\-supervised artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools within Covidence to support screening and data audit workflows\. Extracted data will be synthesized using descriptive statistics, narrative synthesis, and qualitative content analysis\. Identified barriers and facilitators will be inductively extracted and deductively coded into domains of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research\. Depending on the volume of data retrieved, findings may be published across multiple papers\.

## [Examining the mediating role of knowledge management processes between information literacy self\-efficacy and user satisfaction with information systems](../publications/2afa15ce680cc330eccd.md)

Muhammad Shahzad; Ch\. Muhammad Nadeem Akhtar; Iqra Ghafoor; Mehvish Makhdoom

Introduction\. This study examines the impact of information literacy self\-efficacy on shaping knowledge management processes and user satisfaction with information systems among agricultural knowledge workers in Punjab, Pakistan\. Although information literacy and knowledge management have been widely examined, limited research has modelled them as multidimensional higher\-order constructs within agricultural research organisations\. Method\. Data were collected from 415 agricultural knowledge workers using stratified proportionate sampling: a survey instrument measured information literacy self\-efficacy, knowledge management processes, and user satisfaction with information systems\. Analysis\. The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4\. A disjoint two\-stage approach was employed to estimate higher\-order measurement and structural models\. Reliability and validity of both lower\- and higher\-order constructs were assessed before hypothesis testing\. Results\. The results indicated that information literacy self\-efficacy had a significant positive effect on knowledge management processes and user satisfaction with information systems\. Knowledge management processes also significantly mediated the relationship between information literacy self\-efficacy and user satisfaction\. Conclusion\. The findings demonstrate that strengthening agricultural knowledge workers&\#x27; information literacy self\-efficacy enhances knowledge acquisition, sharing and utilisation, which in turn improves satisfaction with organisational information systems\. The study extends the application of higher\-order modelling in the agricultural research context\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Development and Worker Employment Quality: Evidence from China](../publications/2b022491c94241734d5b.md)

Yunting Wu; Xiliang Feng

With the continuous development of new technologies, these new technologies have a profound impact on the labor market\. This paper uses micro\-individual data from the China Family Panel Studies \(CFPS\) from 2016 to 2022 and provincial\-level macro\-data on artificial intelligence \(AI\), employing a two\-way fixed\-effects model to systematically examine the actual impact and underlying mechanisms of AI development on the employment quality of workers\. The study shows a significant positive correlation between the level of regional artificial intelligence development and the employment quality of local workers\. However, this overall effect at the regional level cannot directly prove the individual\-level effect of enterprises or employees using artificial intelligence\. Mechanism testing further confirms that the effect of the regional AI development on improving the employment quality of workers is mainly achieved through optimizing the industrial structure and promoting the intelligentization of workers’ working mode\. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the regional artificial intelligence has a greater positive impact on employment quality for male workers, outside\-system workers, and workers in the eastern region\. Therefore, to achieve higher\-quality employment for workers, it is necessary to promote the deep integration of AI with the real economy, build a multi\-party collaborative education mechanism involving government, enterprises, and universities, and implement policies to promote digital inclusion and differentiated support\.

## [MAIN DIRECTIONS AND RESULTS OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN THE FIELD OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE](../publications/2b0d6c0226749b69ec2e.md)

Utkirbek Mutalibjonovich Muxtarov

This scientific article highlights the main directions of scientific research in the field of artificial intelligence, the results achieved, and their significance in the development of modern society\. It analyzes the developmental characteristics of areas such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and generative artificial intelligence\. Opportunities arising from the application of artificial intelligence technologies in the fields of education, medicine, industry, economics, and information technology will also be considered\.

## [ESG Performance, Artificial Intelligence Adoption, and Knowledge Diversification: Pathways to Sustainable Innovation Capability](../publications/2b12d5d6eb76619ebf79.md)

Yuantao Fang; Yunhai Dai; Zhuoqi Teng; Renhong Wu

Against the backdrop of the global shift from scale\-driven competition to innovation\-driven development, together with the dual trends of climate governance and digital transformation, whether firms can transform ESG performance into sustainable innovation capability has become a central question in assessing the real economic value of ESG practices\. Using panel data of Chinese A\-share listed companies from 2009 to 2025, this study constructs a two\-way fixed\-effects model to systematically examine the effects of overall ESG performance and its three dimensions, namely, Environmental \(E\), Social \(S\), and Governance \(G\), on corporate sustainable innovation capability\. Furthermore, this study incorporates artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption and knowledge diversification \(TD\) into a unified analytical framework and investigates their roles as parallel mediating mechanisms\. The results show that overall ESG performance is positively related to corporate sustainable innovation capability\. In the joint regression, all three ESG dimensions have positive effects, with the social dimension exhibiting the largest marginal effect\. Artificial intelligence adoption and knowledge diversification constitute two parallel and complementary transmission channels through which ESG enhances sustainable innovation capability\. Further analyses find that higher ESG levels are positively associated with corporate sustainable innovation capability, whereas rapid short\-term improvements in ESG are negatively related to corporate sustainable innovation capability\. It shows that innovation performance experiences short\-term pressure before a substantial ESG improvement but gradually surpasses its previous level afterward, indicating the existence of genuine short\-term adjustment costs in ESG\-driven innovation\. This study simultaneously incorporate artificial intelligence adoption and knowledge diversification into the mechanism analysis of the ESG–innovation relationship, providing more fine\-grained micro\-level evidence on how ESG is transformed into real productive capacity\. The findings offer important implications for firms’ differentiated ESG investment strategies and the coordinated design of innovation and sustainability policies\.

## [Machine learning\-based prediction of 90\-day tensile strength in geopolymer concrete under varying input\-variable scenarios](../publications/2b186ff274352f9a2063.md)

Parnian Mehravar; Hossein Bahrami; Hamidreza Ghazvinian

Accurate prediction of the long\-term tensile strength \(TS\) of geopolymer concrete remains a complex challenge owing to the nonlinear and interactive nature of the governing parameters\. This study develops and comparatively evaluates four machine\-learning models linear regression \(LR\), decision tree \(DT\), random forest \(RF\) and support\-vector regression \(SVR\) to predict 90\-day tensile strength from a suite of physicochemical and mixture\-related variables\. Eleven systematically designed input scenarios were formulated to quantify the influence of different feature combinations on predictive performance\. The results demonstrate a pronounced dependence of model accuracy on input configuration\. Early scenarios that employed limited variable sets yielded only moderate performance \(R² ≤ 0\.885, with most models below 0\.86\), whereas the optimal configuration \(S11\), which incorporates water absorption \(WA\), ground\-granulated blast\-furnace slag \(GGBS\), nano\-silica, pH and bulk density \(BD\), substantially enhanced predictive capability\. Among the models, DT achieved the highest test accuracy \(R² = 0\.984, RMSE = 0\.751\) together with the smallest generalisation gap \(training R² = 0\.988\), indicating strong predictive performance within the investigated dataset and limited evidence of overfitting under the applied validation procedures\. RF and SVR also delivered high predictive performance \(R² = 0\.964 and 0\.956, respectively\), while LR exhibited comparatively lower accuracy, underscoring the importance of nonlinear modelling approaches\. Permutation\-importance sensitivity analysis identified WA as the dominant influential parameter \(mean ΔR² = 0\.911\), followed by GGBS \(0\.588\) and nano\-silica \(0\.277\), indicating that WA and GGBS were the strongest predictors of TS within the trained model, consistent with though not a direct proof of their established physical roles in porosity and geopolymeric gel formation\. Collectively, the findings indicate that the integration of advanced tree\-based learning algorithms with comprehensive input characterisation provides a promising and computationally efficient framework for modelling the long\-term tensile behaviour of geopolymer concrete within the range of mixtures examined; broader industrial application will, however, require external validation on independent datasets and formal uncertainty quantification\.

## [Novel K\-neighbors and gradient boosting based transfer features for optimizing network attack detection](../publications/2b1b91f421bb2d61d016.md)

Ali Raza; M\. Nauman Hassan; Amber Malik; Ibrar Hussain; Elizabeth Caro Montero; Eduardo Silva Alvarado; Imran Ashraf

Network attacks represent unauthorized activities on digital networks that aim to disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems\. These attacks range from denial\-of\-service \(DoS\) disruptions to sophisticated intrusion attempts, posing significant threats to the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of information resources\. The repercussions of network attacks are extensive, leading to substantial financial losses, compromise of sensitive data, erosion of user trust, and potential damage to an organization’s reputation\. This research aims to recognize network attacks using advanced machine learning approaches and transfer feature engineering\. We utilized the benchmark CICDDOS2019 database for experiments\. We balanced the preprocessed dataset during the initial analysis using the synthetic minority oversampling technique \(SMOTE\)\. We introduced an innovative transfer feature generation method that generates salient class probabilistic fused features using the K nearest neighbors classifier \(KNC\) and gradient boosting classifier \(GBC\)\. The proposed KNGB \(KNC\-GBC\) model extracts transfer features, which are subsequently fed into machine learning models to identify network attacks\. The experimental results indicate that, using KNGB features, the random forest model attained a high accuracy of 98% for network attack recognition\. We also validated the applied machine learning model’s performance results using k\-fold cross\-validations and improved performance using hyperparameter tuning\. Furthermore, we determined the computational complexity of the methods used and conducted a statistical t\-test analysis to validate the significance of the results\. This research aims to provide a robust, machine learning\-based framework that can adapt to the dynamic nature of cyber threats, ensuring the integrity and security of information networks\.

## [Türkçede edebî parmak izleri: Dğal dil işleme ve makine öğrenmesi kullanarak kitap türü bulma ve yazar eşleştirme](../publications/2b2248c256f4d57ddcb5.md)

Doğukan Özyurt; Ayça Kumluca Topallı

Edebi içerik temelli yazar eşleştirme, tür sınıflandırması ve öneri sistemleri doğal dil işlemede giderek daha fazla önem kazanmaktadır\. Bu çalışma, kitap metinlerini vektör uzayında temsil ederek hem sınıflandırma hem de içerik tabanlı öneri yapabilen bir sistem sunmaktadır\. Türkçe romanlardan oluşan kapsamlı bir veri kümesi derlenmiş, ön işlemden geçirilmiş ve Doc2Vec algoritması kullanılarak yüksek boyutlu vektörlere dönüştürülmüştür\. Genellenebilirliği sağlamak amacıyla, her bir yazarın test kümesinde yer almasını garanti eden özel bir eğitim/test bölme stratejisi uygulanmıştır\. Elde edilen belge vektörleri, Doğrusal Destek Vektör Makinesi Sınıflandırıcısı, Lojistik Regresyon, Rastgele Orman, Gauss Naive Bayes ve En Yakın Komşular gibi sınıflandırıcılarla yazar ve tür tespitinde kullanılmıştır\. Deneysel sonuçlar, ilk iki yöntemin hem tür hem de yazar tahmininde diğer üç yönteme göre daha yüksek performans gösterdiğini ortaya koymuştur\. Bu çalışma ayrıca, geleneksel kosinüs benzerliğinin ötesine geçen özgün bir sınıflandırma yaklaşımı önermektedir\. Geliştirilen yöntem, okuyucunun daha önce beğendiği eserlerle benzer anlatım tarzına sahip kitapları önererek daha az bilinen yazarların görünürlüğünün artırılmasına katkı sağlamaktadır\. Araştırma, belge gömme tabanlı yöntemlerin dijital beşerî bilimler ve öneri sistemlerinde etkili bir biçimde uygulanabileceğini göstermektedir\.

## [Civil Aviation Cybersecurity in Indonesia: Legal Compliance, Regulatory Gaps, and Reform in Light of ICAO Standards](../publications/2b25a7766a619506feca.md)

Adya Paramita Prabandari; Ramalina Ranaivo Mikea Manitra

Cybersecurity has become an important component of international aviation safety and security as the increasing digitalization of aircraft systems and air traffic management creates new risks for civil aviation\. In Indonesia, the expansion of digital infrastructure in the aviation sector requires a coherent legal and institutional response to these risks\. This paper aims to examine Indonesia’s civil aviation cybersecurity legal framework in comparison with international standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organization \(ICAO\) and related legal instruments\. Using a comparative doctrinal legal method, the study analyses primary legal materials, including the Aviation Law, the Electronic Information and Transactions \(ITE\) Law, Government Regulation No\. 71 of 2019, Presidential Regulation No\. 82 of 2022, and Ministerial Regulation No\. 51 of 2020, supported by secondary legal materials on civil aviation cybersecurity, through normative qualitative analysis\. The findings show that Indonesia has incorporated cybersecurity obligations into its aviation laws and regulations, demonstrating progress in recognizing cybersecurity as part of aviation safety and security\. However, the level of compliance remains uneven across different areas of the national legal and institutional system, particularly in institutional coordination, enforcement, and international cooperation\. The study recommends strengthening the incorporation of ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices into national regulations, establishing a dedicated national aviation cybersecurity strategy, integrating cybersecurity requirements into safety and certification processes, improving cross\-border cooperation and CSIRT capacity, formalizing public\-private cooperation, and strengthening institutional capacity\. The study concludes that Indonesia has established a substantial legal basis for aviation cybersecurity\. However, greater legal coherence and institutional coordination are required to achieve more consistent compliance with international standards\.

## [Contracting with an Agent under Model Mismatch](../publications/2b29f0000e416db22104.md)

Elif Yılmaz; Jakub Tłuczek; Victor Villin; Christos Dimitrakakis

In the classical principal\-agent setting, the principal delegates some task to the agent, who receives a payment conditioned on the outcome of the task, which in turn benefits the principal\. To align their objectives, the principal designs a contract that incentivizes the agent to take actions beneficial to the principal\. In practice, however, the agent may act under misspecified beliefs about the underlying environment, leading to systematically suboptimal decisions\. In this work, we study this problem through a principal\-agent Markov Decision Process \(PAMDP\), in which the principal repeatedly interacts with an agent whose transition model may differ from the true environment dynamics\. The principal has access to the true transition model and designs contracts that account for the agent&\#x27;s belief and incentives\. We characterize contract design under model mismatch and develop a framework that enables the principal to induce desirable long\-term benefits even though the agent has a potentially inaccurate understanding of the environment\.

## [An integrated bidirectional LSTM and adaptive cubature Kalman filter estimation method for accurate state\-of\-charge estimation of lithium\-ion battery](../publications/2b2c57f46a69dfaf7b0f.md)

Jayakara Babu Kondru; Jayakara Babu Kondru

Abstract Model\-based observers for lithium\-ion battery state\-of\-charge \(SOC\) estimation lose accuracy under strong nonlinearities and sensor noise, while purely data\-driven estimators lack physical consistency and generalise poorly outside their training distribution\. Existing hybrid designs address this gap only partially: neural\-network outputs are typically fused with an Extended Kalman Filter \(EKF\) as a loosely coupled correction term, so first\-order linearisation error and static noise statistics still limit performance under aggressive drive cycles\. This paper proposes a tightly coupled Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory\-Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter \(BiLSTM\-ACKF\) framework that resolves these limitations through three distinct mechanisms\. First, the BiLSTM output is reformulated as a scalar pseudo\-measurement of SOC, rather than a terminal\-voltage correction, so the innovation is expressed directly in SOC units and is independent of the open\-circuit\-voltage\-SOC slope\. Second, an innovation\-driven adaptive covariance law continuously re\-weights the measurement noise covariance according to the real\-time agreement between the BiLSTM output and the model\-predicted SOC, self\-regulating the filter’s trust in the data\-driven channel\. Third, cubature\-point propagation replaces Jacobian linearisation in a single\-RC Thevenin equivalent\-circuit model, eliminating first\-order truncation bias under strongly nonlinear transients\. A sliding window sequence of voltage and current measurements were used to train the BiLSTM\. Validation was conducted with four different driving cycles \(DST, FUDS, UDDS and US06\), at three temperatures \(5° C, 25° C and 45° C\), and six levels of Gaussian white voltage noise \(0 mV, 30 mV, 80 mV\) using two datasets provided by the TU\-Berlin repository \(LA92 and US06\)\. Comparison results show that BiLSTM\-ACKF significantly outperformed both the stand\-alone BiLSTM \(with a range of 40–60% lower RMSE values than BiLSTM\) and BiLSTM\-AEKF \(with a range of 30–52% lower RMSE values than BiLSTM\-AEKF\) across all four driving cycles and all six levels of noise\. With respect to error magnitude, BiLSTM\-ACKF also demonstrated a consistent upper bound of less than 1\.5% over all test cases\.

## [Carbon\-Negative Self\-Compacting Geopolymer Concrete from RAP and C&amp;D Waste Using a Machine Learning Framework](../publications/2b322101ffc852da7f3e.md)

## [The genetically determined role of the compact myocardial layer in excessively trabeculated left ventricular noncompaction](../publications/2b34e265c4ad4088c8d1.md)

Balázs Mester; Kinga Grebur; Kristóf Attila Farkas\-Sütő; Júlia Magdolna Tardy; Flóra Klára Gyulánczi; Márton Horváth; Alexisz Panajotu; Ferenc Imre Suhai; Bálint András Fekete; Csaba Bödör; Hajnalka Vágó; Béla Merkely; Andrea Szűcs

Abstract Background: Left ventricular excessive trabeculation \(LVET\) ranges from preserved ejection fraction \(EF\) morphology to reduced EF Noncompaction cardiomyopathy\. Emerging evidence indicates that EF reduction is more strongly associated with thinning of the Compact myocardial layer \(CL\) than with trabeculation alone, although the precise role of the CL in LVET has yet to be determined\. Aim: We aimed to evaluate Trabeculated layer \(TL\) and CL thickness in LVET subjects with preserved EF across genotypes, establish genotype\-specific CL thickness cut\-offs, and analyse their association with LV parameters\. Methods: We enrolled 54 LVET subjects with matched healthy Controls\. In CMR, functional, volumetric and myocardial\-mass parameters were measured using threshold\-based analysis\. TL thicknesses were assessed using calliper tools and CL thickness was measured using OptiLayer software\. For genetic testing, cardiac NGS panels were used; LVET subjects were classidied into Benign \(B\), VUS, and Pathogenic \(P\) subgroups according to ACMG databases\. Results: LVET subjects showed thicker TL and thinner CL compared to Controls\. CL thickness differed among genetic subgroups: P variants were associated with significantly thinner apical segments, with a cut\-off of 5 mm \(93% of P &lt;5 mm, 41% of VUS &lt; 5 mm, 8% of B&lt;5 mm, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. TL thickness showed no association with genotype\. CL thickness correlated with global circumferential strain \( r = 0\.461, p &lt; 0\.01\), indicating subclinical dysfunction\. Conclusion: CL thinning in LVET with preserved EF was associated with P genetic background and may represent early morphological alterations\. These findings suggest potential roles in diagnosis, risk stratification, and follow\-up, which should be further evaluated in longitudinal studies\.

## [EXPRESS: Measuring solute clearance across brain states: methods and the sleep–brain–drain debate](../publications/2b3958cd48dfaf2edb79.md)

Gawon Cho; Burhan Ozturk; Marah Alian; Kaiming Xu; Joaquin Caceres Melgarejo; Brienne Miner; Nora D\. Volkow; Helene Benveniste

BACKGROUND: The glymphatic hypothesis posits that cerebrospinal fluid and interstitial fluid bulk\-flow clears brain waste, with increased waste transport during sleep\. Recent studies reporting the opposite have generated substantial controversy\. Three issues underlie the controversy surrounding this hypothesis and are the subject of this reviewMethods:We critically reviewed these three issues\. First, we identified heterogeneity in the methods used to quantify brain &quot;clearance&quot; and evaluated their validity, recalculating rate constants from published data where these were not originally reported\. Second, we examined uncertainty regarding the physical forces driving fluid and solute movement, and how assumptions about advection influence model specification\. Third, we critiqued the dichotomization of brain state into &quot;sleep&quot; and &quot;wakefulness&quot;\. RESULTS: Clearance rates reported by competing groups fall within a similar range, yet the conclusions drawn about the influence of sleep are diametrically opposed\. No gold\-standard approach exists either for measuring clearance or for defining and inducing brain states\. CONCLUSION: These conflicting results cannot be adjudicated: the debate persists not because the rates differ but because no shared standard exists to determine whether the opposing state\-associations are real\. Methodological standardization is a precondition for a reproducible account of how brain solute clearance is regulated\.

## [Lifetime Integration Theory: Experience\-Based Self\-Locating Probability](../publications/2b3cd39f344ae5f5c2f3.md)

Kazuyuki Harada

If nonhuman animals are conscious, why am I human? This paper proposes Lifetime Integration Theory \(LIT\), which considers the probability of experiencing a given life on the basis of brain size and the duration of experience over that lifetime\. Drawing on thought experiments and brain research, it considers weighting by the first and second powers of neuron count and examines reasons to include the duration of experience in the weight\. This opens the possibility that extremely long lives for people alive today could help explain why I am human\. If people today are also the first generation to live long enough to benefit from technology that enables extreme longevity, the same framework can address the question, “Why was I born in the present era?” The paper explores whether the Extreme Longevity Hypothesis \(ELH\) could hold, taking into account life\-extension technology, future increases in the numbers of humans, animals, and other conscious beings, and the goals of superintelligence\.

## [A POSTHUMANIST ANALYSIS OF HUMAN COGNITIVE TRANSFORMATIONS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE NETFLIX SERIES BETTER THAN US](../publications/2b42757a03be3a4d872e.md)

Juvaria Rabbani; Sadia Siddiq

Rapid technological advancement in the twenty\-first century has resulted in alteration of s the relationships between humans and machines which further results in reshaping perceptions of cognition\. In the current era, artificial intelligence is progressing in various domains blurring the boundaries between human and technology and reshaping the perceptions of cognition, consciousness and identity\. The series Better than us explores the themes of artificial consciousness, human dependence on technology and reconfiguration of emotional and cognitive capacities\. A number of studies have examined Artificial intelligence in literature, films and dramas, however limited research has explored the cognitive impacts of human dependence on artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US\. Thereby using Catherin Belsey’s textual analysis model under the broader umbrella of Hayles post humanist theory the current Study aims to explore the representation of cognitive transformations in humans through artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US\. The findings of the study reveal that the series Better Than Us presents artificial intelligence as a transformative force which reshapes human ethical cognition\. The series transform the traditional assumption that moral judgment and authority belong exclusively to humans\. The character representation of Arisa demonstrates the role of AI systems in decision making, legal interpretation, and protective actions\. This results in a redistribution of ethical responsibility between humans and intelligent machine\. The analysis further elucidates that human characters gradually begin to negotiate morality within technologically mediated environments where machine reasoning influences social and institutional structures\. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Human\-Machine relations, Posthumanism, Better Than Us\.

## [Preventing Data Hallucinations in Agentic AI for Optical Network Troubleshooting](../publications/2b43d971cf3ee8277356.md)

Jeremias Dötterl; Martin Kuipers

An agentic AI system for automated troubleshooting in optical communication networks is demonstrated that integrates data references into the agent architecture to prevent data hallucinations, improving the interpretability and trustworthiness of root\-cause identification and reasoning\.

## [Benchmarking Hybrid Learning Models for Personalized Risk Classification and Prediction in Oncology](../publications/2b4bfade9c09eee749af.md)

Tshikutu Bikengela Anaclet; Nkongolo Kenda Simon; Biduaya Symphorien; Mabela Matendo Rostin; Mbuyi Mukendi Eugène

In the field of oncology, and specifically regarding prostate cancer, recent breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) have opened fascinating possibilities for risk classification and prediction\. However, moving from theoretical success to actual clinical practice remains a significant challenge\. In this study, we chose to evaluate several architectures \(generative, discriminant, and hybrid models\) to test their real\-world relevance when faced with longitudinal medical data, which is often noisy or incomplete\. Our analysis does not merely measure raw performance; it seeks to understand the critical balance between statistical precision and the interpretability that clinicians require for daily decision\-making\. By examining the inherent strengths and limitations of each method, we developed an advanced hybrid approach designed as a genuine support tool for the patient care pathway\. Our findings are particularly encouraging: these deep hybrid models significantly outperform traditional methods, showing a notable improvement of 6% to 9% in both AUC\-ROC and C\-index scores\. Beyond these metrics, we observed a superior ability in the model to adapt to the temporal variations of patient data over time\. Ultimately, our goal is to demonstrate that more refined predictions, when properly integrated into the clinical context, can simplify the decision\-making process\. By making these models more transparent and robust, we hope to facilitate their adoption by the medical community, leading to more personalized and effective management for patients battling prostate cancer\.

## [Productive Kanji Use in Japanese Sakubun: Evidence From Elementary\-Level Learners](../publications/2b4feb0c4635a88cde37.md)

Juju Juangsih; Noviyanti Aneros; Linna Meilia Rasiban

Kanji learning remains challenging for Japanese language learners from non\-kanji backgrounds because it requires coordination of form, meaning, reading, and production\. Although previous studies have examined kanji learning and sakubun writing, limited evidence exists on how elementary\-level learners use kanji productively in written texts\. This study examines productive kanji use in sakubun, focusing on kanji distribution, writing difficulties, possible avoidance, and learners’ perceptions of integrated kanji–sakubun learning\. A qualitative descriptive design supported by descriptive frequency analysis was employed with 27 second\-semester students in a Shokyuu Hyoki Sakubun course\. Although 27 students participated, 15 independently written sakubun texts were selected for detailed analysis based on completeness and comparability\. Classroom observations and a semi\-structured questionnaire supplemented the text data\. Findings show that kanji use was uneven and concentrated on familiar, contextually relevant characters, with 私 \(watashi\) occurring most frequently \(44 times\)\. Of 98 identified writing difficulties, incorrect kanji formation \(46 cases\) and bushu stroke\-direction errors \(34 cases\) were most frequent\. Additionally, 73\.3% reported difficulty distinguishing visually similar kanji, while all respondents viewed integrated kanji–sakubun learning positively\. The findings suggest that productive kanji use is shaped by familiarity and context\.

## [Application of multi\-agent co\-evolution algorithm in dynamic matching system between vocational education and industrial demand](../publications/2b54ed033382ef4337bf.md)

Mingyan Chen

The Multi\-Agent Co\-Evolution Algorithm \(MACEA\) models enterprises, schools, and students as autonomous agents, each characterized by heterogeneous states, objective functions, and local adjustment rules\. A dynamic co\-evolutionary process is established through stable matching, fitness\-triggered updates, and cross\-agent market signals\. The simulation experiment comprised 50 enterprise agents, 10 school agents, and 1,000 student agents, with each model subjected to 30 independent runs under uniform initial conditions\. MACEA achieved an overall matching degree of 0\.82 ± 0\.03, outperforming the Static Matching Model \(0\.48 ± 0\.05\), the Genetic Algorithm\-Based Global Optimization Model \(0\.71 ± 0\.04\), and the Decentralized Adaptive Baseline \(0\.67 ± 0\.04\)\. MACEA stabilized after approximately 78 rounds and demonstrated rapid recovery in matching following an external skill demand shock\. Abandonment, parameter sensitivity, and agent\-scale expansion experiments confirmed the stability of this performance pattern within the defined simulation range\.

## [Makro Ekonomi&amp;Finans Alanı Üzerine Güncel Analizler](../publications/2b559bfc07bb2c8c7539.md)



Finansal piyasalarda riskin ölçülmesi, piyasa etkinliğinin değerlendirilmesi ve belirsizliklerin ekonomik faaliyetler üzerindeki etkilerinin anlaşılması, bu kitabın temel odak alanları arasında yer almaktadır\. Kripto para piyasalarında kuyruk riski bağlantılılığının piyasa koşullarına göre değişimi, döviz piyasalarında etkinlik ve adaptif piyasa hipotezi ile küresel finansal belirsizliklerin makroekonomik değişkenler üzerindeki etkileri, bu kapsamda öne çıkan konulardır\. Bunun yanı sıra, veri madenciliği ve makine öğrenmesi gibi yenilikçi yöntemlerin sistematik risklerin belirlenmesi ve erken uyarı mekanizmalarının geliştirilmesindeki rolü değerlendirilmektedir\. Kitap da ayrıca, teknolojik dönüşümün finansal sistemler ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik üzerindeki etkileri ele alınmakta; yapay zekâ ve finansal teknolojilerin \(FinTech\) yeşil aklamayla mücadeledeki potansiyeli tartışılmaktadır\. Para ve maliye politikalarının çevresel kalite ve karbon emisyonlarıyla ilişkisi ile döngüsel ekonomi yaklaşımını destekleyen kamu politikaları da sürdürülebilir kalkınma perspektifinden incelenmektedir\. Bu çerçevede finansal okuryazarlık, bireylerin finansal riskleri değerlendirme, bilinçli kararlar alma ve ekonomik belirsizlikler karşısında dayanıklılık geliştirme kapasitelerini güçlendiren temel bir unsur olarak öne çıkmaktadır\. Finansal piyasaların sağlıklı işleyişi ile toplumsal refah arasındaki bağlantının anlaşılmasına katkı sağlayan bu yaklaşım, ekonomik politikaların etkinliği açısından da önem taşımaktadır\. Sonuç olarak bu eser, akademisyenler, araştırmacılar, politika yapıcılar ve öğrenciler için makroekonomi ve finans alanındaki güncel tartışmaları bir araya getirerek bilimsel düşünceye ve sürdürülebilir ekonomik gelişme arayışlarına katkı sunmayı hedeflemektedir\.

## [Kliktivisme dari Gampong: Pemberdayaan Tengku sebagai Agen Literasi Media Digital Berbasis Moderasi Beragama dan Pencegahan Hoaks di Gampong Penyangga IAIN Langsa](../publications/2b631fda21e076841a77.md)

Muslem Ibnu; Friska Anggi Siregar

Penyebaran informasi digital yang masif kerap diiringi maraknya disinformasi, hoaks, dan narasi radikalisme bernuansa agama yang berpotensi mencederai kerukunan sosial di Aceh\. Di tengah struktur masyarakat gampong, Tengku memegang peranan krusial sebagai pemimpin opini \(opinion leader\), namun keterbatasan kecakapan digital membuat mereka rentan terpapar dan meneruskan informasi yang belum terverifikasi\. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat berbasis riset ini bertujuan memperkuat kapasitas literasi media digital para Tengku di Gampong Penyangga Kampus IAIN Langsa\. Metode yang digunakan adalah Participatory Action Research \(PAR\) yang memadukan lokakarya interaktif, simulasi verifikasi informasi berbasis empat pilar literasi digital \(digital skills, digital culture, digital ethics, dan digital safety\), serta Focus Group Discussion \(FGD\)\. Evaluasi program diukur menggunakan kuesioner pre\-test dan post\-test berskala Likert 1–5 terhadap 13 indikator kompetensi\. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan peningkatan pemahaman yang terukur, ditandai dengan kenaikan nilai rata\-rata peserta dari 28,9 poin \(pre\-test\) menjadi 49,8 poin \(post\-test\), atau meningkat rata\-rata sebesar 20,9 poin\. Meskipun desain evaluasi tidak memungkinkan pengujian statistik inferensial, pola peningkatan yang konsisten di seluruh peserta mengindikasikan efektivitas program\. Program ini mentransformasikan peran pasif tokoh agama menjadi agen kliktivisme positif di tingkat akar rumput yang mampu menyaring hoaks serta menyuarakan narasi moderasi beragama di ruang virtual\. Kebaruan artikel ini terletak pada integrasi model PAR dengan konteks sosio\-religius Aceh, yang menghasilkan model penguatan literasi media berbasis komunitas religius yang dapat direplikasi di wilayah lain\.
