For chest abnormality classification, this study uses visual deep neural network architectures as Swin Transformer, ConvNeXt, EfficientNet, and ResNet\. This research utilizes ViT\+BART, ViT\+GPT\-2, Swin\+BART, and Swin\+GPT\-2 for the input image to generate report\. The performance of visual classifiers is measured in Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and Macro F1\-score\. The generated reports are evaluated by BLEU, ROUGE\-1, ROUGE\-2, ROUGE\-L, and BERT\-F1\. Swin Transformer achieved an accuracy of 0\.77, while ViT\+BART achieved BLEU, ROUGE\-1, ROUGE\-2, ROUGE\-L, and BERT\-F1 scores of 0\.13, 0\.42, 0\.17, 0\.33, and 0\.89 respectively

## [Die Veränderung von dysfunktionalen Erwartungen bei Menschen mit depressiven Störungen und Symptomen – Kognitive, affektive und verhaltensbezogene Mechanismen](../publications/2d314db137cc2e51bdea.md)

Edith Rapo

Im Rahmen dieses Dissertationsvorhabens wurde mittels fünf wissenschaftlicher Artikel untersucht, welche Mechanismen die Erwartungsveränderung bei Menschen mit depressiven Störungen und Symptomen begünstigen beziehungsweise hemmen\. Es wurde ein experimentelles Paradigma entwickelt, in welchem positive Erfahrungsberichte über Psychotherapie genutzt wurden, um die Erwartungen bezüglich positiver versus negativer Lebensereignisse und die Behandlungserwartungen zu modifizieren\. Es wurde an einer kleinen klinischen Stichprobe \(N = 17\) auf Machbarkeit überprüft \(Artikel 1\) und an einer großen klinischen Stichprobe \(N = 156\) angewendet\. Die Erfahrungsberichte verbesserten die Erwartungen signifikant\. Der Einfluss von kognitiver Immunisierung auf die Erwartungsveränderung konnte nicht nachgewiesen werden \(Artikel 2\)\. Menschen mit persistierender depressiver Störung \(n = 54\) verbesserten ihre Therapieerwartungen weniger stark als Menschen mit episodischer depressiver Störung \(n = 102\), besonders wenn kognitive Immunisierung experimentell gefördert wurde \(Artikel 3\)\. Zudem wurde an einer klinischen Stichprobe \(N = 80\) der Einfluss von State Affekt auf die Erwartungsveränderung nach positivem versus negativem Leistungsfeedback untersucht\. Affekt hatte keinen signifikanten Einfluss auf die Erwartungsveränderung \(Artikel 4\)\. Abschließend wurde an zwei Stichproben \(N = 149 und N = 212\) untersucht, wie der Schweregrad depressiver Symptome mit der Inkongruenz zwischen Selbst\- und erwarteter Fremdwahrnehmung \(Metawahrnehmung\) und dem Feedbacksuchverhalten zusammenhängt\. Mit steigendem Schweregrad wich die Selbstwahrnehmung zunehmend negativ von der Metawahrnehmung ab\. Außerdem zeigte sich ein negativer Zusammenhang zwischen dem Schweregrad und dem Feedbacksuchverhalten, der jedoch nicht durch Valenz des Feedbacks oder Inkongruenz zwischen Selbst\- und Metawahrnehmung erklärt werden konnte \(Artikel 5\)\.

## [A novel approach for testing water safety using deep learning inference of microscopic images of unincubated water samples](../publications/2d35afb3e40ea91474f7.md)

Sanjay Srinivasan

Abstract Fecal\-contaminated water causes diseases and even death\. Current microbial water safety tests require pathogen incubation, taking 24–72 h and costing $20\-$50 per test\. This paper presents a solution \(DeepScope\) that classifies microscopic images of unincubated water samples by a composite water\-safety determination, meeting UNICEF’s ideal Target Product Profile numerical performance thresholds for presence/absence testing, with an estimated per\-test cost of $0\.44\. By eliminating the need for pathogen incubation, DeepScope reduces testing time by over 98%\. In DeepScope, a dataset of microscope images of bacteria and water samples was assembled from the public DIBaS bacterial image collection and water samples from multiple source types, with labels cross\-validated using color\-change coliform tests\. A novel tile\-swap augmentation technique was developed to expand dataset diversity and mitigate overfitting, swapping random tile pairs to preserve bacterial morphology while producing a large space of augmented images\. Four convolutional neural network models \(ResNet\-18 and ResNet\-50 backbones, with and without dropout regularization\) were developed using transfer learning, then evaluated on a field\-test dataset comprising 100,000 microscope images of unseen, real\-world water samples collected from fourteen different water sources across Sammamish, WA\. On the 160 original microscope acquisitions underlying this dataset, the DeepScope model \(ResNet\-50 with dropout\) achieved 96\.88% accuracy, 98\.61% recall, and 94\.67% precision, corresponding to a 1\.39% false\-negative rate and a 4\.55% false\-positive rate\. A larger field test was then carried out on the 100,000 augmented images derived from these acquisitions, with the operating threshold set to fix precision at 90%\. Under these conditions the model achieved recall of 94\.48% ±0\.11%, accuracy of 92\.79% ±0\.08%, and F1 of 92\.19% ±0\.09%—a 5\.52% false\-negative rate, well below UNICEF’s 10% ceiling and competitive with membrane filtration and color\-change coliform tests without requiring pathogen incubation\. The DeepScope model was tested in a web server environment using mobile applications for Android and iOS\. The testing validated Internet\-based or smartphone\-based water safety testing, with results obtained in seconds\.

## [An Exploration of Approaches to Contextual Teaching in Elementary School Music Education from the Perspective of Authentic Learning](../publications/2d3767c34765c319c48a.md)

Taotao Jin

To implement the requirement in the Compulsory Education Arts Curriculum Standards \(2022 Edition\) to link contextual teaching with life experiences, integrating the concept of authentic learning into elementary school music classrooms holds significant practical value\. In response to current issues in music classroom situational teaching\-such as fragmented tasks, overly formalized scenarios, and superficial learning outcomes\-this study clarifies the theoretical similarities and differences between authenticity\-based learning and situational teaching\. By addressing practical needs such as classroom scenario creation, task design, and learning experiences, it constructs a teaching pathway driven by real\-world projects, featuring embodied participation, and incorporating authenticity\-based assessment throughout\. The study also proposes optimization strategies in three areas: identifying authentic problems, leveraging digital technology, and expanding resources and learning environments\. This exploration offers insights for conducting more vivid and in\-depth situational teaching in elementary school music classrooms, helping students develop musical literacy through authentic experiences\.

## [Path to Prior\-Data Fitted Relational Models via Learned Latent Multi\-table Representations](../publications/2d45b3c077d1b22413ca.md)

Mohammad Sadeq Abolhasani; Viswanath Ganapathy

Prior\-data fitted networks \(PFNs\) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine\-tuning\. This paradigm is effective for transformer\-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB\-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph\-based relational models built on message passing\. We pretrain the graph\-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer\-based relational learners, also improves message\-passing representations\. Rather than fine\-tune on downstream tasks, we use the pretrained encoder as a general\-purpose relational representation learner and pass its latent representations to a frozen in\-context predictor \(\\ticl\{\}\); no component is trained on the target task\. On 16 real\-world relational classification tasks, evaluated over five seeds against raw\-feature and untrained\-encoder baselines, a purely synthetic curriculum that begins with schema\-guided data and continues with schema\-agnostic data gives the strongest frozen in\-context performance\\rev\{, outperforming real\-data\-only pretraining and every unordered single\-stage mixture of the corpora; when appended after real\-data pretraining, it yields the best encoders overall\}\. These results provide initial evidence that PFN\-style synthetic pretraining transfers to graph\-based relational foundation models\.

## [Hybrid experimental–numerical methodology for the mechanical analysis of mortars containing recycled polymer inclusions](../publications/2d49dc552b88799bcffc.md)

Melany Isabel Pinilla\-Hernandez; María Eugenia Maciá Torregrosa; Roberto Alonso González Lezcano

Abstract This investigation presents a hybrid experimental–numerical methodology for evaluating the mechanical behavior of mortars containing recycled polymer inclusions\. Mortar mixtures incorporating recycled polyethylene terephthalate \(PET\) and polyamide 6 \(PA6\) at replacement levels of 10 \[%\] and 20 \[%\] were produced and experimentally characterized through compressive and flexural strength tests\. In addition, the elastic modulus and deformation capacity of the mixtures were determined to assess the influence of recycled polymers on mortar performance\. The experimental results were subsequently used to calibrate and validate finite element models developed in SolidWorks Simulation\. The numerical analyses enabled the evaluation of stress distributions, deformation patterns, and critical regions associated with damage initiation, providing additional insight into the mechanical response of the investigated mortars\. The comparison between experimental measurements and numerical predictions demonstrated satisfactory agreement, confirming the suitability of the proposed modeling approach\. The results indicate that the incorporation of recycled polymer inclusions modifies the stiffness and deformation capacity of the mortar while maintaining acceptable mechanical performance\. PA6 inclusions promoted a more deformable response through a reduction in elastic modulus, whereas PET inclusions maintained mechanical strengths comparable to those of the reference mortar\. The proposed methodology provides a reliable and reproducible framework for the characterization and numerical assessment of sustainable mortars containing recycled polymer materials and contributes to the development of environmentally friendly cement\-based composites\.

## [ANÁLISE DOS ANÁLOGOS DE GLP\-1 NA MODULAÇÃO DO COMPORTAMENTO ALIMENTAR E NA RELAÇÃO COM A COMIDA](../publications/2d4e899a25e559a83e93.md)

Beatriz Leal Silva Xavier; Emily Vitória Melo de Sousa

A ingestão alimentar é regulada por diversos mecanismos complexos que compõem o controle homeostático e o sistema de recompensa alimentar, no qual o peptídeo semelhante ao glucagon tipo 1 \(GLP\-1\) tem um papel fundamental em enviar sinais de saciedade\. Este estudo teve como finalidade analisar os efeitos dos análogos de GLP\-1 na modulação do comportamento alimentar, considerando aspectos fisiológicos e comportamentais\. Dessa forma, foi conduzida uma revisão integrativa da literatura, com busca na base de dados PubMed \(Medline\), incluindo artigos originais e revisões publicadas nos últimos cinco anos\. A análise dos resultados indica que os fármacos como a liraglutida, semaglutida e tirzepatida promovem uma redução significativa do apetite e da percepção de saciedade\. Observou\-se ainda que esses análogos influenciam na modulação de aspectos hedônicos, reduzindo o desejo por alimentos altamente palatáveis, e interferindo em comportamentos como o comer emocional e a alimentação por recompensa\. A discussão ressalta que, embora apresentem eficácia, as respostas ao medicamento podem variar de acordo com os indivíduos, conforme o padrão alimentar, tornando indispensável o acompanhamento nutricional e multiprofissional\. Conclui\-se que os análogos de GLP\-1 contribuem positivamente para a relação do indivíduo com a comida, mas são necessários mais estudos para avaliar seus efeitos e repercussões nutricionais a longo prazo\.

## [Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges](../publications/2d66463ea41fcf67aa99.md)

Yian Li; Xiaoyu Guo; Hao Zhang; Jiayu Chen; Shuiwang Li; Xiaowei Dai

Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired\. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks\. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision\. This definition distinguishes active observation acquisition from processing fixed inputs and guides the selection of representative literature\. Within this scope, this review develops an analytical framework organized around four questions\. It begins with what evidence the task requires, examines which actions can obtain that evidence and how a candidate observation should be valued, and considers how the next sensing action should be selected and executed\. New observations then update the perceptual state and guide subsequent decisions, forming a closed loop that provides a common basis for comparing methods across applications\. To examine how their benefits can be demonstrated, this review assesses whether existing datasets support observation selection, how interactive environments enable controlled comparisons, and what physical platforms reveal about execution feasibility\. It further examines how baseline comparisons can establish whether adapting observations is necessary and whether informed selection offers benefits beyond simpler sensing strategies\. These considerations underpin an evaluation framework that links improvements in visual evidence to downstream task outcomes while accounting for acquisition costs and risks\. Its core value is to help isolate the contribution of sensing decisions and determine whether their benefits justify the resources required\. The analysis concludes that predicted observation value does not guarantee that useful evidence can be acquired through feasible actions, while task success alone cannot establish the benefit of active observation selection\. Further progress requires reliable value estimation and planning over longer decision sequences under physical and resource constraints\. It also requires grounding semantic reasoning in acquired evidence and maintaining effective collaboration under imperfect communication, with these capabilities verified through reproducible evaluation of the complete perception and action loop\.

## [Reconsidering pathways to global shipping decarbonization: idealism vs\. realism](../publications/2d71f5ddc88e9304e468.md)

Wenwen Li; Yizhou Sun; 胡正良 Hu Zhengliang

Introduction The 2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships and its 2025 Draft Net\-Zero Framework exhibit evident features of idealism\. These instruments have not fully considered vessels’ long\-term asset cycles, technological bottlenecks for zero\-carbon marine fuels, cross\-country disparities in shipping development, and safety constraints related to green maritime infrastructure\. Methods This study integrates legal realism, resource dependence theory, and securitization theory into a climate\-realism framework\. It uses doctrinal legal analysis, qualitative policy evaluation, and a Norway–China comparative case study\. Results The limitations of the IMO Draft Net\-Zero Framework are dissected across four dimensions: transition costs, technological maturity, carbon\-pricing fairness, and infrastructure security\. The Norway–China comparison shows that a one\-size\-fits\-all aggressive pathway cannot reconcile industry survival with climate governance goals, whereas a gradual, inclusive, and technology\-neutral route is more sustainable\. Discussion To reconcile idealism with reality, global shipping decarbonization governance should establish a dynamic adjustment mechanism matched to technological iteration, implement differentiated carbon pricing, and build a transnational risk\-sharing system for green infrastructure\. This would balance development rights and maritime economic security while steadily promoting shipping decarbonization\.

## [The Effect of the Peer Tutoring Learning Model on Student Learning Outcomes Regarding Matrices in Senior High School](../publications/2d7abba6f69c13a20e77.md)

Nur Huda Adam; Evi Hulukati; Hasan S\. Panigoro

This study aims to analyze the impact of the Peer Tutoring learning model on students&\#x27; mathematics learning outcomes regarding the topic of matrices at SMA Negeri 1 Tapa\. The primary issue underlying this research is the low level of active student engagement in conventional instruction and the failure of learning outcomes to meet the minimum mastery criteria\. The study employed a quasi\-experimental design, specifically a pre\-test and post\-test control group design involving 38 Grade XI students selected via simple random sampling\. The research instrument consisted of an essay test with established validity and reliability\. Data were analyzed using the Independent Sample t\-test and an effect size test\. The results indicate a significant difference in learning outcomes between the experimental and control groups; the experimental class achieved an average score of 90\.00, far surpassing the control class\. Hypothesis testing yielded a t\-value of 5\.300 \(exceeding the critical value of 1\.688\), with an effect size of 4\.884, indicating a very high impact of the Peer Tutoring model\. These findings confirm that the Peer Tutoring model is effective in enhancing students&\#x27; conceptual understanding through mechanisms of learning\-by\-teaching and metacognitive dialogue\. The study highlights the importance of adopting peer\-tutoring\-based cooperative learning models as an adaptive instructional solution to optimize student academic achievement in high schools\.

## [Generative AI in Accounting Policies and Estimates: Safeguarding Professional Judgment and Addressing Managerial Bias](../publications/2d7b858f30b40c07943d.md)

Radosveta Krasteva\-Hristova; Rayna Petrova; Silviya Petrova Chukanska

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is increasingly used in corporate reporting, where accounting policies and estimates require professional judgment\. The central risk examined is not automated error but automated advocacy: a fluent, standard\-referenced justification for a preferred treatment can now be obtained in seconds, making biased judgment a governance problem before it is an accounting problem\. Using theory adaptation, this conceptual study integrates research on professional judgment, motivated reasoning, and automation reliance\. It identifies five bias\-amplification mechanisms: anchoring, automation bias, outcome\-directed prompting, unverified justification, and diffusion of responsibility\. It develops TRACE, a proposed framework comprising task boundary, regulatory grounding, alternative assessment, challenge and contradiction, and evidence trail\. Its intended operation is illustrated using four constructed IFRS cases \(IAS 8/IAS 16, IAS 36, IAS 37, IFRS 15\) and a boundary\-condition variant in which TRACE does not resolve the disagreement\. The AI proposals are stylised illustrations, not model outputs or empirical data\. GenAI appears most defensible when used to generate alternatives and challenge a preferred treatment, and least defensible when asked to select or justify a conclusion\. TRACE may make AI\-assisted judgments more attributable and contestable, but it has not been empirically validated and cannot guarantee unbiased outcomes\.

## [Artificial intelligence–enabled nursing surveillance for pediatric cancer immunotherapy: integrating biomarkers, patient\-reported outcomes, and long\-term toxicity management](../publications/2d7fef6649c6154216dd.md)

Yi Peng; Qiong Kou; Sihong Guo; Jia Xu; Lijuan Wang; Xiaoyan Chen

Pediatric cancer immunotherapy has expanded from anti\-GD2 antibodies and bispecific T\-cell engagers to immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T\-cell therapy\. These treatments can produce rapid, nonlinear, and partially overlapping toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell\-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, infection, prolonged cytopenia, B\-cell aplasia, and organ\-specific immune\-related adverse events\. Nurses provide the highest\-frequency clinical observations across inpatient, ambulatory, and home settings, yet conventional monitoring often fragments laboratory data, vital signs, neurologic findings, caregiver observations, and patient\-reported outcomes\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) offers a means to fuse these longitudinal signals into individualized risk trajectories\. The clinically relevant mechanism, however, is not autonomous prediction; it is a nurse\-in\-the\-loop system in which AI improves temporal sensitivity and prioritization, while nurses verify signal quality, interpret age\- and development\-specific context, reconcile child–caregiver discordance, activate protocol\-based escalation, and maintain accountability\. This Mini Review examines how biomarkers, continuous physiological monitoring, electronic patient\-reported outcomes, and caregiver\-reported behavioral changes can support AI\-enabled nursing surveillance during acute immunotoxicity and long\-term survivorship\. We propose a three\-layer framework linking immune\-toxicity biology, a multimodal digital phenotype, and nursing counter\-regulation\. We also discuss workflow integration, alert fatigue, model drift, bias, privacy, and the need for prospective pediatric validation\. AI should augment not replace specialist pediatric oncology nursing judgment and should be evaluated by whether it improves timely intervention, symptom burden, family experience, and long\-term safety\.

## [Structural, Optical, and Magnetic Properties of Mn x Fe 3‐x O 4 Ferrofluids Derived From Iron Sand for Energy Harvesting Application](../publications/2d8b5b316408133ab62d.md)

Sri Rahmawati; Babita Tripathi; Yap Wing Fen; Arif Hidayat; Nurul Hidayat; Anindya Bella Monica; ST\. Ulfawanti Intan Subadra; Munasir; Ahmad Taufiq

ABSTRACT In this research, we report the synthesis of iron sand‐based Mn x Fe 3‐x O 4 ferrofluids along with the characterization of their structural, optical, and magnetic properties, as well as their energy harvesting performance\. The Mn x Fe 3‐x O 4 nanoparticles in the ferrofluids constructed an inverse spinel structure, with their diffraction peaks shifting to lower angles as the Mn 2\+ content increased\. FTIR spectra showed the Fe‐O and Mn‐O stretching detected at wavenumbers of 430–521 cm −1 and 411 cm −1 , respectively\. The magnetic nanoparticles tended to agglomerate with particle sizes ranging from 24\.0 nm to 39\.6 nm\. The bandgap energy increased as the Mn 2\+ content increased\. Furthermore, the energy harvesting performance was represented by voltage values in the range of 16\.17–96\.20 µV as a function of Mn 2\+ content\. Although the voltage was relatively low, the obtained results indicate promising potential for future energy harvesting applications\.

## [Validation and Pilot testing of Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Anxiety and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy](../publications/2d8c95660c50e3b09a23.md)



Background: One of the most prevalent mental health issues, anxiety disorders have a substantial impact on a person&\#x27;s quality of life\.Understanding public awareness and behaviors related to anxiety and its management is essential for designing effective interventions\.Aims: The goal of this study is to assess the levels of knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding anxiety among people in the Rampur region\.Materials and Methods: A self\-developed KAP questionnaire consisting of 34 items was designed and validated using content validity index \(CVI\) and internal consistency measures\.A pilot cross\-sectional study was conducted among 60 participants\.Results: The knowledge section revealed mixed awareness levels, with several participants demonstrating good understanding of anxiety symptoms and impacts, such as its effect on sleep, concentration, and daily functioning \(up to 80%\)\.Attitude findings indicated a generally positive outlook towards anxiety management, with 80\-84% of participants expressing willingness to discuss anxiety\.Practice\-related results showed encouraging trends, with the majority engaging in adaptive coping strategies such as relaxation\.Conclusion: The questionnaire demonstrated excellent content validity and strong internal reliability, confirming its suitability for use in future research\.

## [Seismic – Gravimetric analysis of the Algeciras fault system \(Colombia\): spatio\-temporal correlations from GRACE and GNSS\-InSAR](../publications/2dad46d7718f5965b789.md)

Edwin Mauricio Pinzon Monroy; Carlos A\. Vargas

Integrating seismological, gravimetric, and geodetic observations provides a complementary framework for investigating spatiotemporal relationships among seismic activity, mass redistribution, and surface deformation in active fault systems\. This study investigated these associations in the Algeciras Fault System \(AFS\) by integrating seismic records, monthly gravimetric observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment \(GRACE\) and GRACE Follow\-On \(GRACE\-FO\) missions corrected for hydrological effects using the Global Land Data Assimilation System \(GLDAS\), and surface deformation observations derived from Global Navigation Satellite System \(GNSS\) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar \(InSAR\)\. Cross\-correlation analysis between temporal gravity variations and GNSS displacements identified positive and inverse associations with correlation coefficients ranging from 0\.0001 to 0\.61, time lags of up to 45 months, and heterogeneous spatial patterns along the AFS corridor\. In addition, the integrated analysis of gravimetric variations and InSAR\-derived vertical displacements identified areas where simultaneous decreases in gravity and elevation accounted for approximately 99% of the total seismic energy released, compared with areas corresponding to the other relationships evaluated between the two variables\. A fluctuation was also observed in the GRACE\-derived gravimetric time series during the period surrounding the 2019 Mesetas earthquake \(Mw 6\.0\)\. Overall, the proposed methodology provides an exploratory and replicable approach for analyzing the associations observed among the different sources of information and offers complementary analytical insights for future research on seismic hazard and surface dynamics in tectonically active regions\.

## [The Influence of Perceived Training Effectiveness, Talent Management, and Leadership on Organizational Citizenship Behavior Through Organizational Commitment to Al\-Amanah Al\-Gontory Islamic Boarding School Teachers](../publications/2db42044ee7b3048b5be.md)

Diwa Haikal Adittya; Dewi Susita; Widya Parimita

Organizational citizenship behavior \(OCB\) among teachers plays a crucial role in enhancing the effectiveness and sustainability of educational institutions, particularly Islamic boarding schools \(pesantren\), where teachers frequently contribute beyond their formal responsibilities\. This study aims to examine the effects of perceived training effectiveness, talent management, and leadership on OCB, with organizational commitment serving as a mediating variable among teachers at Al\-Amanah Al\-Gontory Islamic Boarding School\. The study employed a quantitative, associative research design involving 124 teachers from a population of 179, with the sample size determined using Slovin’s formula\. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on a five\-point Likert scale and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) using a two\-stage approach\. The results indicate that perceived training effectiveness has significant positive effects on both OCB and organizational commitment, while leadership significantly influences organizational commitment\. Furthermore, organizational commitment has a significant positive effect on OCB and mediates the relationship between perceived training effectiveness and OCB\. Conversely, talent management has no statistically significant effect on either OCB or organizational commitment, while leadership has no significant direct effect on OCB\. Additionally, organizational commitment does not significantly mediate the relationships between talent management and OCB or between leadership and OCB\. These findings underscore the importance of effective training programs and strong organizational commitment in fostering teachers’ discretionary contributions and promoting positive organizational behavior within pesantren\-based educational institutions\. The study offers practical implications for strengthening human resource management strategies through competency\-based training, initiatives to enhance organizational commitment, and more systematic talent management practices\.

## [Heterogeneous graph transformer with slot\-based message passing for node classification](../publications/2dca11f054872e26732b.md)

Yanqi Xie; Weipeng Zheng; Yu Ming; Kaibiao Lin; Baisen Xiong

As a widely utilized data structure, heterogeneous graphs can accurately model complex structures and multi\-typed relationships, finding extensive applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, and biomedical analysis\. Node classification supports these applications by identifying entity categories or functional roles\. However, during the message\-passing process, mapping different types of nodes into a unified representation space often leads to cross\-type feature confusion, resulting in the loss of type\-specific semantic information\. To address this issue, this paper proposes the HGT\-Slot model\. First, the model employs a type\-aware Slot initialization to construct type\-specific representation spaces for different node types, preserving their unique semantic attributes\. Subsequently, a Slot attention mechanism is employed during the message\-passing phase to preserve heterogeneous semantic information through different Slot channels\. Meanwhile, the Transformer architecture is leveraged to enhance interactions among node representations, thereby improving the representation capability of the model\. Finally, a Slot aggregation mechanism integrates the Slot representations for local prediction, which is fused with the global prediction from the Transformer branch for classification\. Experiments on three datasets show that HGT\-Slot achieves the best mean Macro\-F1 and Micro\-F1 scores among the compared methods for node classification\.

## [The Ultimate Deduction of AI‑Driven Civilization Transition: The Collapse of the 200‑Year‑Old Industrial System, Deadlock of Interests and Risks of Historical Emergence\(V1\)](../publications/2dce2e17c50fcce61baf.md)

XiangKun Wang

Ninety\-nine percent of modern human social forms are transitional byproducts of the 200\-year industrial era, not eternal configurations of civilization\. Education, law, working hours, professions, class structures, trade, finance, and currency all serve solely to facilitate industrial labor division; they can only buffer contradictions, not eradicate inequality at its root\. AI represents the first comprehensive cognitive substitution revolution in millennia—sufficient to dismantle the 200\-year industrial system and overturn the millennia\-old axioms of human labor value\. The velocity of AI iteration far outpaces the speed of institutional correction, causing the window for civilizational transition to shrink rapidly while urgency reaches critical levels\. The primary bottleneck in the transition between civilizations is not a technical barrier, but a structural deadlock of wealth and power, where the entrenched system lacks any intrinsic motivation for active reconstruction\. The two productivity leaps of the industrial age both achieved order reconstruction through world wars; today&\#x27;s underlying contradictions are a complete recurrence of historical patterns\. While structural contradictions exist with absolute certainty and continue to accumulate, history possesses inherent randomness and emergence, rendering the final outcome unpredictable\. No one desires turmoil, yet no one can arrest the natural release of historical laws and systemic potential energy\. Humanity is entering an era of ultimate AI transition: a total paradigm shift, an intractable deadlock of interests, and a future rendered completely unpredictable\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Epidemiology and Public Health: Measurement, Evidence, and Population Consequences](../publications/2dd1a022fda925d90a96.md)

Pietro Corona

This scholarly monograph examines how artificial intelligence has developed within epidemiology and public health, which computational methods have been most frequently documented, how applications have evolved across scientific and geographical contexts, and what the available evidence establishes about their consequences for research, services and population health\. The investigation integrates historical reconstruction, quantitative evidence mapping, source\-based methodological appraisal, selected comparative analyses and conceptual synthesis\. Its analytical corpus comprises 4,752 retained research reports spanning 1993 to 2026, with the final year incomplete\. The study documents the coexistence and evolution of neural networks, tree\-based approaches, statistical learning and other computational methods, while examining geographical patterns, classification uncertainty and the emergence of contemporary AI\-enabled workflows and operational systems\. The monograph investigates applications across infectious\-disease surveillance and forecasting, genomic epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance, environmental exposure estimation, wastewater monitoring, population registries, organised screening and preventive health services\. Comparative analyses examine measurement validity, predictive performance, external validation, causal interpretation, screening completion, service productivity, implementation, economic consequences and equity\. Favourable outcomes are considered alongside null, adverse, mixed and uncertain findings, with explicit attention to study design, comparators, analytical populations and outcome definitions\. An original contribution is the identification and empirical investigation of underascertainment in the classification of environmental research functions\. The broader synthesis examines how AI changes the production of epidemiological knowledge, how observation and measurement shape scientific conclusions, and why improvements in prediction or operational performance cannot automatically be interpreted as attributable improvements in population health\. Organised into 18 chapters and five methodological appendices, with 44 original scientific illustrations and 25 tables, the book provides an integrated international perspective on the methodological evolution, documented contributions, limitations and emerging directions of artificial intelligence in epidemiology and public health\. The work is intended for epidemiologists, public\-health researchers, computational scientists, health\-services researchers, methodologists, policymakers and advanced students\.

## [Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long\-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries](../publications/2dea376a1f6caa3dddef.md)

Anikait Singh; Teresa Zhang; Yoonho Lee; Roshen Sanjay Nair; Aviral Kumar; Chelsea Finn

Reasoning over long document contexts remains a challenge for large language models \(LLMs\)\. Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross\-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics\. Instead, can we allow agents to perform anticipatory directed curation: learning to proactively reorganize unstructured corpora prior to inference to efficiently serve diverse future queries\. We build on a key asymmetry in modern agentic harnesses \(e\.g\., Claude Code\): while LLM agents are adept at navigating existing filesystems to solve an immediate task, they are rarely trained to construct reusable workspaces for future use\. To instantiate this capability, we introduce Librarian Agents, a framework in which a builder agent transforms raw documents into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links, which forms a workspace tailored for a downstream answering agent\. We formulate workspace construction as a Markov decision process and optimize the builder policy via reinforcement learning to directly maximize downstream answering accuracy\. Empirically, Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp\-Plus, amortizes upfront construction costs across repeated queries, and generalizes zero\-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31\-point average accuracy improvement\.

## [Sustainable Supply Chain Management, Green Operations, and Circular Economy Practices: A Theoretical Framework for Organizational Sustainability](../publications/2dfd0d59fd03dece46c7.md)

Marimuthu Kn; K\. Rajamannar

Sustainable Supply Chain Management \(SSCM\), green operations, and circular economy \(CE\) practices have become fundamental pillars of modern organizational sustainability\. Escalating environmental concerns, resource scarcity, climate change, and increasing stakeholder expectations have compelled organizations to transition from traditional linear business models to sustainable and regenerative operational systems\. This theoretical study synthesizes contemporary literature to develop an integrated framework explaining the interrelationships among sustainable supply chain management, green operations, and circular economy practices\. Drawing upon the Natural Resource\-Based View \(NRBV\), Stakeholder Theory \[1\], Institutional Theory, Triple Bottom Line \(TBL\), and Circular Economy Theory \[2\], the study proposes a comprehensive conceptual model illustrating how sustainable procurement, green manufacturing, reverse logistics, resource efficiency, ecoinnovation, and circular resource flows collectively contribute to environmental, economic, and social sustainability\. The paper further identifies research gaps and develops a conceptual foundation for future empirical investigations\. The proposed framework provides strategic insights for managers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to improve organizational resilience and long\-term sustainable competitiveness\. Keywords: Sustainable procurement; reverse logistics; eco\-innovation; resource efficiency; organizational resilience

## [Tracing Geopolitical Change Through Documents: A Comparative Content Analysis of Germany’s Arctic Policy Guidelines \(2013–2024\)](../publications/2dfde8dd02693c62f7c7.md)

Hasan Fatih Seval

Research on Arctic securitization centers on the Arctic states; non\-Arctic observers have received less systematic attention\. This article examines Germany, an Arctic Council observer since 1998, and asks how its official framing of the Arctic changed between 2013 and 2024\. It applies qualitative comparative content analysis in MAXQDA to Germany’s three Arctic Policy Guidelines \(2013, 2019, 2024\)\. Barry Buzan’s five sectors of security serve as the main codes, supplemented by thematic and perceptual codes; the documents are compared through coverage and normalized co\-occurrence densities\. The analysis identifies two shifts of different kinds\. Between 2013 and 2019, opportunity framing fell from 19 to 8 percent of the text, while threat framing and the military sector barely moved\. The balance between threat and opportunity thus tipped two and a half years before Russia’s full\-scale invasion of Ukraine\. Between 2019 and 2024, military coverage rose from 6 to 15 percent, and its framing moved from preventing an arms race to deterrence\. The documents tie only this second shift to the war\. Environmental security remained the largest sector throughout\. The article adds an observer\-state case to Arctic securitization research and shows how measurement separates changes that a before\-and\-after reading runs together\.

## [Digital transformation of outpatient care: physicians’ expectations and barriers to implementing telemedicine and artificial intelligence technologies\.](../publications/2e2693a1b2f525e7c876.md)

E\. N\. Morozova; Шинкарева Наталья Владимировна; N\. V\. Eckert; A\. V\. Ferjaoui; Р\. В\. Горенков

Background\. In the context of healthcare digital transformation, telemedicine \(TM\) and artificial intelligence \(AI\) are being integrated into clinical practice; however, the pace of their implementation outpaces the analysis of their impact on workflows, workload, and physicians’ psychological acceptance\. Studying systemic barriers and the human factor is essential for the successful scaling of digital tools in primary care\. Objective: to assess real\-world experience, identify key barriers, and determine the relationship between physicians’ expectations and practical challenges of implementing TM and AI in the activities of outpatient medical professionals\. Materials and methods\. A cross\-sectional study was conducted using an anonymous online survey of 897 medical professionals from outpatient clinics in the Moscow region\. The questionnaire covered socio\-demographic and professional characteristics, frequency and formats of TM, AI and EHR use, as well as perceived barriers and risks\. Statistical analysis employed descriptive statistics and Pearson’s χ² test \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Results\. Daily TM consultations are conducted by 49\.7% of physicians, predominantly in audio format \(46\.5%\)\. Despite recognizing TM effectiveness for chronic patient follow\-up \(63\.3%\), 30\.6% report increased workload, and 38\.3% consider no more than two consultations per day optimal\. The main TM barriers are technical failures \(29\.3%\) and low patient digital literacy \(16\.2%\)\. Regarding AI, a gap was revealed: readiness for use is 55%, while 60\.5% have no practical experience; 50\.1% fear degradation of their diagnostic skills\. Major systemic issues include insufficient interoperability \(43\.6%\) and lack of training \(22\.8%\)\. Statistical analysis confirmed significant associations between AI use and expectations \(p &lt; 0\.05\), and between training needs and AI readiness \(χ² = 23\.979; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion\. A persistent gap was identified between positive perceptions of digital technologies’ potential and the real challenges of their integration\. The barriers – technical, organizational, and psychological – are systemic and require comprehensive solutions: specialized training, minimization of technical failures, ensuring information systems interoperability, and revision of workload standards considering the time spent on TM consultations\.

## [Physics\-Informed AI for Defect Prediction in WAAM for Space Systems \(Academic Edition\)](../publications/2e3075cfa0d73b85fe0b.md)

Sangat Naik

Physics\-Informed AI for Defect Prediction in WAAM for Space Systems \(Academic Edition\) This book explores the integration of physics\-informed artificial intelligence with Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing \(WAAM\), focusing on defect prediction and its potential applications in space manufacturing systems\. The work examines the fundamental physics of WAAM, defect formation mechanisms, computational modeling, machine learning, physics\-informed neural networks, and hybrid predictive architectures\. Particular attention is given to challenges associated with data scarcity, process uncertainty, microgravity, and autonomous manufacturing\. The book also introduces a proposed Physics\-Informed WAAM Intelligence Framework and identifies research opportunities for improving manufacturing reliability in demanding environments\. Intended for researchers, engineers, and graduate students, this academic edition provides a foundation for further investigation into intelligent additive manufacturing, materials engineering, and future space technologies\. This edition is made available for academic reference, research, and citation\.

## [Generative Value Classifier](../publications/2e3baadeceaa5b7f0a0c.md)

Alexander Swerdlow; Perry Dong; Chelsea Finn

Q\-learning is premised on learning a function to predict the value of a state\-action pair, with the goal of using such a function to guide policy improvement\. Most approaches learn this function from scratch using scalar or distributional return targets\. This discriminative approach leaves another source of supervision for learning representations unused: the actions themselves\. Rather than directly predict the return of a state\-action pair, we ask the reverse question: how likely is the action under each possible return? This perspective provides a critic whose generative component is a return\-conditioned policy, which can share the actor&\#x27;s architecture\. Training this policy supervises the critic with every action rather than with returns alone, and a squared\-error loss anchors the critic&\#x27;s Q\-value to the bootstrapped target\. We evaluate our approach on both offline and online RL tasks and show gains over leading discriminative methods, including distributional RL methods\.

## [Cross‐Scale Integrated Photonic Convolver Based on Conjugate‐Symmetric Interference](../publications/2e3cdf6030dee4d35a9d.md)

Yixuan Zheng; 张姝然 Zhang Shuran; Jiajia Wang; Yifu Xu; Yunping Bai; Xingyuan Xu

ABSTRACT Photonic hardware offers a promising route to high‐speed and energy‐efficient convolution computing beyond the bandwidth and power limitations of conventional electronic platforms\. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a cross‐scale integrated photonic convolver \(CSIPC\) that enables cross‐scale feature extraction through a single training process\. Implemented on a hierarchically coupled finite‐impulse‐response \(FIR\) photonic chip, the CSIPC exploits the propagation of conjugate‐symmetric interference‐weight relations through the coupling network, together with the spatiotemporal interleaving induced by serial‐to‐parallel conversion\. A single set of trained chip weights can be mapped at different output ports into a family of equivalent convolution kernels with distinct effective tap numbers and temporal intervals\. By selecting the output port and tuning the input symbol rate, 2 × 4, 2 × 2, and 2 × 1 two‐dimensional convolution kernels can be realized on the same chip\. We experimentally validate multifunctional cross‐scale image feature extraction and achieve a maximum single‐mode equivalent computing throughput of 0\.276 TOPS\. These results provide a route toward cross‐scale photonic convolution using a single device and a single training process, while improving functional integration density and enabling the reuse of trained weights and hardware resources\.

## [Intelligent Cyber Attack Detection through Machine Learning](../publications/2e552afe34603e2edd88.md)

S\. Sireesha; A\. Ramaswami Reddy; D V V Deepthi

Internet of Things \(IoT\) Connection encouraged new technology solutions for public safety in the city by integrating the transportation, healthcare and environment sectors into smart services\. The variety of devices and continual chug of information makes these interdependent systems effective for both improving operational effectiveness and enhancing quality of life, but provides cybercriminals with a broad attack surface\. Existing methods of security are simply not up to the task of addressing realtime, complex threats\. In this work, we present a novel machine learning\-based approach to detect a cyber attack in Internet of Things \(IoT\) powered smart cities\. This proposed solution would be based on the analysis of network traffic and activities of the devices to determine whether the activity is normal or not\. In the data preparation section, unimportant features are removed, missing values are filled, scaling and filters of features are applied on the data to improve the accuracy of the model\. Various approaches are implemented and explored to find the best machine learning approach for detecting cyberattacks\. Generally, accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and confusion matrix analysis are used to evaluate the performance\. Its aim is to keep the computational efficiency, increase early Cyber intrusion detection and decrease false alarms\. The patterns learnt may be finding an abnormal behaviour in historic activity that can be used to detect Denial of Service \(DoS\), probing, access or data manipulation attacks\. The results of the experiment highlight an immense improvement in the time taken for the detection of threats, from nearly real\-time time to almost instant time, with the use of machine learning threat detection technology, which greatly improves the security of the IoT infrastructure\. The study results underline the importance of Smart City Security Systems\. The proposed architecture is flexible and extendable with the number of urban services and in the future it will offer cyber resilience capabilities to the IoT based system\.

## [QuAD: Quantitative Assessment via Distribution\-Alignment for Qualitative Data Quality Enabled by a Content\-Aware Multi\-Agent System](../publications/2e62bbd2c4e64ffd3915.md)

Wenshuo Zhang; Leixian Shen; Qiqi Zhou; Shuchang Xu; Feiyang Hao; Huamin Qu; Haobo Li; Zhao Chen; Lin\-Ping Yuan

Assessing whether qualitative responses collected from semi\-structured questions are ready for a particular analysis goal is a persistent challenge\. Manual qualitative analysis is interpretive and labor\-intensive, while existing automated methods often lack a dataset\-level perspective for deciding whether a response set supports a researcher\-selected analytical lens\. We introduce QuAD, a framework for quantitative pre\-analysis assessment of qualitative response datasets\. QuAD compares a reconstructed intrinsic cluster distribution reconstructed from responses with an extrinsic, researcher\-defined analytical lens derived from metadata\. QuAD is structured into a four\-quadrant assessment whose metrics are read jointly, from lens\-level relations to within\-cluster variation, to provide fitness\-for\-purpose signals for revealing general patterns and unique insights\. Because this assessment relies on lens\-conditioned inter\-response dissimilarity, we propose a content\-aware multi\-agent system with two\-stage instruction generation and adaptive anchors to improve scoring consistency\. We validate QuAD through controlled experiments on synthetic data, including robustness and baseline comparisons, and a real\-world social survey case study\. The case study shows how QuAD quantitatively assesses whether a selected analysis axis is promising and also surfaces representative or unusual responses for human interpretation\.

## [Wi\-Fi 7 Streaming Stability: A Multi\-Band, Multi\-Bitrate Performance Assessment](../publications/2e62f5acf687c9596966.md)

Nurul I\. Sarkar; Sonia Gul

Wi\-Fi 7 \(IEEE 802\.11be\) introduces key physical and medium access control \(MAC\) layer advancements, including wider channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, 4096\-QAM modulation, preamble puncturing, and tri\-band operation across 2\.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz to support high\-bandwidth and low\-latency wireless applications\. Despite these advances, the application\-level streaming behavior of Wi\-Fi 7 networks under realistic multi\-factor conditions remains insufficiently characterized in the literature\. This paper presents an empirical and simulation\-based evaluation of Wi\-Fi 7 streaming stability, assessing, with one variable changed at a time, the separate effects of received signal strength \(RSS\), codec bitrate, frequency band, network layer protocol, media type, and network contention on playback delay for MP3 audio and MP4 video streams\. A physical testbed comprising a Wi\-Fi 7 access point and client devices is used to conduct controlled experiments across varying signal and network conditions, complemented by OMNeT\+\+ simulation to assess MAC layer scalability under higher client densities\. Each band was evaluated independently with Multi\-Link Operation \(MLO\) disabled, so the results characterize single\-link operation on Wi\-Fi 7 hardware rather than coordinated 802\.11be MLO; the codec bitrates tested \(192–320 kbps\) are low relative to the link capacity, so link saturation was not exercised in the testbed\. Results show that RSS degradation non\-linearly increases playback delay in the pooled results\. Pooled across the conditions tested, not as a strong\-signal subset, the bands rank as follows by mean playback delay: 2\.4 GHz \(7\.05 s\), 5 GHz \(5\.21 s\), and 6 GHz \(4\.26 s\)\. Higher codec bitrates were associated with lower playback delay, most plausibly because VLC’s pre\-buffering threshold is filled sooner at higher bitrates on an unsaturated link\. Network layer protocol \(IPv4 vs\. IPv6\) showed no material difference in mean playback delay\. Network contention, modeled through increasing concurrent client counts, increased playback delay from one to three testbed clients, and simulated network\-layer delay increased from 40 to 80 clients\. These findings provide a descriptive, multi\-parameter, single\-link performance baseline for Wi\-Fi 7 audio and video streaming, providing practical guidance for network deployment and serving as a reference for future benchmarking of next\-generation Wi\-Fi 8 \(IEEE 802\.11bn\) networks\.

## [Sibirya’nın Tarihî ve Kültürel Bir Mirası: Saha \(Yakut\) Bıçağı](../publications/2e688b58c3b4aadbdfdd.md)

Recep Efe Çoban

Sibirya’da yaşayan Saha Türklerinin en önemli kültür unsurlarından biri olan Saha bıçağı, çok soğuk iklimlerde dahi kolayca kullanabilen; ağaç oyma, et dilimleme, buz kırma ve avcılık sırasındaki pek çok görevi başarıyla yerine getirebilen dünyaca tanınmış bir bıçak türüdür\. Saha bıçağı, karakteristik olarak namlunun sağ yüzeyinde bulunan ve Sahaca üös \(үөс\) olarak adlandırılan büyük oluk ile sol yüzeyindeki dışbükey geometrisi ile tanınmaktadır\. Bu asimetrik namlu kesitiyle Saha bıçağı, Saha toplumunun zorlu Sibirya koşullarında hayatta kalma ekipmanlarının başında yer almakta, bu yüzden Sahalar tarafından “üçüncü el” olarak adlandırılmaktadır\. Çalışmamız, temelde, başta Saha Türkleri olmak üzere, Sibirya’nın diğer toplulukları ve komşu kavimler tarafından büyük önem atfedilen bu bıçak türünü ele almaktadır\. Zira özellikle Türkçe literatür değerlendirildiğinde, Sahaların bu kadim kültürel mirasının Sahaları ele alan geniş çaplı çalışmalarda kısıtlı olarak ele alındığı, müstakil olarak Saha bıçağını konu edinen bir çalışmanın yapılmadığı görülmektedir\. Bu bağlamda makalemiz, Sibirya’nın çetin koşullarında yaşam süren Sahalar için işlevsel bir kesici alet olmanın ötesinde kültürel ve tarihî açıdan kadim bir miras hüviyeti taşıyan Saha bıçağını bütüncül bir bakış açısıyla ele almayı ve gelecekte yapılacak daha detaylı araştırmalar için temel oluşturmayı hedeflemektedir\.

## [Shaping the Future of Accounting Education](../publications/2e6cd14e44764b0006c2.md)

Vanissla Hutzli; Catherine Equey Balzli; Giulia Ortoleva; Mireille Bétrancourt

The rapid development of digital technologies is transforming the accounting profession and the competencies required to practise it\. Consequently, higher education institutions face increasing pressure to prepare students and graduates for evolving professional roles and to align accounting curricula with changing labour market expectations\. Identifying the competencies required in a technology\-enabled accounting profession is therefore particularly relevant to the preparation and professional development of future and early\-career accounting professionals\. This study identifies the competencies associated with the Accountant 4\.0 and examines how frequently they are identified in academic and professional literature\. A structured literature review was conducted, including 47 academic publications and documentary sources associated with 14 professional accounting organisations\. The findings reveal differences in the frequency with which competencies are identified across the two bodies of literature\. Academic publications most frequently identify general technological skills and understanding, problem\-solving, communication, and teamwork\. The professional corpus covers a broader range of competencies, with technical accounting competencies, general technological skills and understanding, data analytics, ethics, integrity and professionalism, and analytical reasoning among the most frequently identified\. Communication and teamwork are among the competencies frequently identified across both academic and professional sources\. By integrating and systematically comparing academic and professional perspectives, this study provides a consolidated overview of Accountant 4\.0 competencies and identifies areas of convergence and divergence between the two bodies of literature\. The findings provide a basis for reflecting on how accounting education can support the competency development of students, graduates, and early\-career professionals as they prepare for a profession increasingly shaped by digital transformation\.

## [Association of endoscopic and CT response with pathological response after preoperative FLOT\-based therapy for gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/2e7254315844cf7ca59d.md)

Hüseyin Gencer; Gökhan Uçar; Efnan Algın; Mehmet Ali Nahit Sendur; Erdal Birol Bostancı

Background Pathological response to preoperative chemotherapy is prognostically relevant in gastric cancer, but reliable estimation before surgery remains challenging\. We evaluated the relationship between routine endoscopic and computed tomography \(CT\) response assessments and major pathological response \(MPR\) after FLOT\-based therapy\. Methods In this retrospective, single\-center cohort study, 450 institutional records were screened and 47 patients with gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer who underwent gastrectomy after FLOT\-based therapy and had evaluable pre\- and post\-treatment endoscopy were included; 37 also had comparable paired CT assessments\. Endoscopic and CT responses were classified as complete, partial, stable, or progressive\. Pathology reports were harmonized into complete, near\-complete, partial, and poor/no response, and MPR was defined as complete or near\-complete response\. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis, and paired endoscopy and CT areas under the curve \(AUCs\) were compared using the DeLong test\. The combined endoscopy\-plus\-CT model was exploratory\. Results MPR occurred in 17 of 47 patients \(36\.2%\), including pathological complete response \(pCR\) in 10 \(21\.3%\)\. In the full cohort, endoscopy had an AUC of 0\.619 \(95% CI, 0\.466\-0\.771\) for MPR\. In the paired cohort, AUCs were 0\.561 \(95% CI, 0\.379\-0\.743\) for endoscopy and 0\.675 \(95% CI, 0\.501\-0\.848\) for CT \(difference, 0\.114; p=0\.35\)\. The combined model yielded an apparent AUC of 0\.692 \(95% CI, 0\.511\-0\.873\)\. Both patients with endoscopic complete response had pCR, although this category identified only 2 of 10 pCRs\. Conclusions Routine endoscopic response showed limited discrimination for MPR\. CT had a numerically higher AUC, but the paired comparison was inconclusive, and combining the modalities did not materially improve discrimination\. Given the small paired cohort and heterogeneous pathology reporting, these findings are hypothesis\-generating\. Standardized prospective assessment is required before endoscopic or CT response can be used to estimate pathological response with clinical confidence\.

## [Spatially Integrated Intercalation–Conversion Hybrid Cathode for Durable, High‐Capacity Lithium Metal Batteries](../publications/2e8802fba74b486cfa25.md)

Sang Gu Yeo; Kenneth Liem; Zongfu An; Keon‐Han Kim; Soochan Kim

ABSTRACT The fundamental trade‐off between structural stability and high capacity remains a key challenge in Li‐ion battery cathode design, especially in cost‐sensitive, large‐scale applications\. Here, we present a spatially integrated intercalation–conversion hybrid cathode that combines LiFePO 4 and sulfur‐based materials within a monolayer architecture\. This earth‐abundant composition synchronizes Li‐ion intercalation with the solid‐liquid sulfur conversion reaction: LiFePO 4 serves as a mechanically robust Li host and a chemical regulator that suppresses polysulfide shuttles, while sulfur‐based materials provide high specific capacity\. By rationally tailoring the cathode composition and electrolyte solvation chemistry, we reveal how electrolyte–cathode synergistic interactions govern active material utilization, interfacial kinetics, and long‐term stability\. The optimized Li‐metal battery delivers stable cycling over 3000 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0\.016% per cycle at 5 C and also demonstrates stable cycling under practical asymmetric cycling protocols\. This work provides a new design principle for hybrid cathodes, offering a scalable pathway toward ultra‐durable and high‐capacity Li‐metal batteries\.

## [Estrategias de afrontamiento al estrés competitivo y su relación con el rendimiento deportivo en futbolistas universitarios del club ESPE](../publications/2e8c10b4108bdb9c3fd0.md)

Billy Xavier Ligña Zambrano; Elva Katherine Aguilar Morocho

El presente estudio exploratorio tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre las estrategias de afrontamiento al estrés competitivo, las fuentes de estrés y el rendimiento deportivo en futbolistas universitarios del Club ESPE, así como describir los síntomas de estrés presentes en esta población\. Se realizó un censo poblacional con la totalidad de la plantilla oficial, conformada por 25 jugadores masculinos entre 18 y 25 años \(M = 22\.4, DE = 1\.66\)\. Se adoptó un diseño cuantitativo, descriptivo\-correlacional y transversal\. Se aplicó una adaptación de 30 ítems del Cuestionario de Fuentes de Estrés, Síntomas y Estrategias de Afrontamiento en el Deporte \(FUSIES\), con validación de contenido por juicio de tres expertos\. La confiabilidad obtenida en JASP 0\.18\.3 en la muestra final fue: Fuentes α = \.71 \(IC95% \.52\-\.90\), Síntomas α = \.85 \(IC95% \.77\-\.92\) y Afrontamiento α = \.90 \(IC95% \.81\-\.99\), con un alfa total de \.81\. Los coeficientes de consistencia interna oscilaron entre niveles aceptables y altos\. El rendimiento fue evaluado por el director técnico mediante una escala unidimensional de cinco puntos\. Los resultados no evidenciaron diferencias estadísticamente significativas en el rendimiento según la posición de juego, ni asociaciones significativas entre las variables psicológicas y el rendimiento\. Se observó únicamente una tendencia positiva de magnitud moderada entre afrontamiento y rendimiento que no alcanzó significancia estadística \(rho = \.347, p = \.089\)\. En esta muestra no se encontraron asociaciones estadísticamente significativas entre las variables psicológicas evaluadas y el rendimiento deportivo\. Los resultados deben interpretarse considerando el carácter exploratorio del estudio, el tamaño reducido de la población y la medición subjetiva del rendimiento\.

IgA nephropathy is a common cause of glomerular disease that may result in kidney failure\. Until recently, angiotensin blockade using angiotensin converting enzyme \(ACE\) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers \(ARB\) were the main treatment options for patients with IgA nephropathy\. Newer drugs such as sodium\-glucose co\-transporter 2 \(SGLT2\) inhibitors, endothelin angiotensin receptor antagonists \(DEARA\), endothelin receptor antagonists \(ERA\), complement inhibitors, targeted release formulation glucocorticoids, and a proliferation\-inducing ligand \(APRIL\) and B cell activation factor \(BAFF\) inhibitors have shown promise in reducing proteinuria and delaying the progression of IgA nephropathy\. In this review, we will explore the latest pharmacological options, their efficacy, and when they should be considered in adult patients with IgA nephropathy\.

## [Can AI Forecast the Extremes? Evaluating Probabilistic Weather Models on Tropical Cyclones](../publications/2ea548b975376d5cf276.md)

Nathan Chalumeau; Xavier Renard; Remi Meynadier; Hugo Rakotoarimanga; Marcin Detyniecki; Emmanuel de Bezenac

Weather prediction is undergoing an important shift, with data\-driven AI models outperforming leading numerical weather prediction systems on average at a fraction of the computational cost\. Yet, whether this success extends to extreme events remains contested\. Earlier evaluations have exposed important shortcomings, but have largely focused on deterministic models and metrics, leaving the capabilities of the latest probabilistic models less understood\. We conduct an extensive benchmark of tropical cyclone forecasting, comparing GenCast, FourCastNet 3, and FGN with ECMWF&\#x27;s operational physics\-based ensemble, IFS\-ENS\. We develop a suite of probabilistic metrics and diagnostic analyses to assess cyclone tracking, intensity biases, uncertainty, and the wind\-pressure relationship that characterizes storm structure\. We find that, despite remaining limitations in intensity and ensemble spread, leading AI models substantially outperform IFS\-ENS in cyclone tracking: FGN achieves better probabilistic location scores for 90% of evaluated storms in 2025\. Further analyses reveal model\-specific failure modes and suggest a lingering influence of pretraining data, pointing to opportunities for targeted improvement\. Nonetheless, these results suggest that AI models are capable of capturing physical relationships that remain predictive well beyond typical weather conditions, motivating further investigation into how these capabilities emerge and how to strengthen them\.
