## [Clitoria ternatea as a phytopharmacological resource: plant metabolites, mechanistic evidence, translational prospects, and safety considerations](../publications/2eb236b65195aa46eefb.md)

Dharmasoth Rama Devi; Salapu Neelima Maheswari; Rajana Krishna Saranya; Surisetty Aashritha; Nooka Gouri Sankar; Nissi Abigail Gurrala; Prithviraj Karak; Sayandeep K\. Das

Clitoria ternatea L\. \(Fabaceae; butterfly pea\) is used in traditional medicine and is increasingly developed as a food colorant, functional beverage, botanical preparation, and source of peptide scaffolds\. Previous reviews have separately emphasized ethnomedicine, flower extraction, anthocyanins, or cyclotides; however, the evidence has rarely been integrated according to preparation identity, study design, bioavailability, safety, and translational readiness\. This structured critical narrative review updates the literature through 8 August 2026\. PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched using species\-name and domain\-specific terms\. Primary studies were prioritized, and evidence was stratified as chemical/analytical, in silico , isolated\-target or cell\-based, animal, and human\. Study interpretation considered taxonomic authentication, plant part, extraction and chemical characterization, dose, controls, duration, model relevance, adverse\-event reporting, and exposure plausibility\. The principal metabolite classes are ternatin anthocyanins, flavonol glycosides, phenolic acids, triterpenoids, sterols, and cyclotides\. Chemical assays such as DPPH and ABTS support redox characterization but do not establish pharmacological or therapeutic efficacy\. Neurobehavioral, anti\-inflammatory, metabolic, antimicrobial, organ\-protective, and cytotoxic signals are reported mainly in preclinical models, often using incompletely standardized extracts\. Human evidence is restricted to small acute crossover studies and exploratory adjunctive studies, including a 2026 study of flower tea in people with type 2 diabetes and diabetic distress\. Intact ternatins are orally absorbed in rats, but systemic exposure is modest and human pharmacokinetic data are unavailable; metabolite exposure, formulation effects, chronic toxicity, reproductive safety, cyclotide immunogenicity, and botanical\-drug interactions remain insufficiently defined\. Recent genomic and peptide studies strengthen the biotechnology relevance of cyclotides and butelase\-1 but should not be conflated with the efficacy of crude botanical preparations\. Overall, C\. ternatea is a promising source of defined food, botanical, and peptide products, but therapeutic claims require authenticated materials, marker\-based standardization, exposure\-linked pharmacology, and adequately controlled clinical trials\.

## [New strategies for the treatment of tuberculosis: research progress and clinical translation in immune modulation and inflammation control](../publications/2ebf13d17f7e0548c0b2.md)

Shihao Du; Lulu Zhen; Ji Zhou; Di Deng

Tuberculosis \(TB\) remains a major global public health challenge, with treatment complicated by drug resistance, adverse effects, and suboptimal host immune responses\. Whilst conventional anti\-TB drugs are effective bactericidally, their immunomodulatory effects may, in certain contexts, contribute to immune imbalance and affect treatment outcomes\. Host\-directed therapy \(HDT\), which aims to modulate the host immune response to enhance pathogen control and limit immunopathology, has emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy\. This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence for HDT in TB, focusing on immunosenescence, trained immunity, cytokine and lipid mediator networks, immunometabolic reprogramming, neuroendocrine regulation, and repurposed drugs including metformin and statins\. Importantly, we distinguish between evidence derived directly from TB models \( in vitro , animal, and clinical studies\) and evidence extrapolated from other diseases, highlighting knowledge gaps and areas requiring further investigation\. We propose that future progress depends on evidence\-based stratification of HDT candidates, rigorous clinical trial design, and a personalised approach that accounts for patient comorbidities and immune status\. This review aims to provide a balanced framework for advancing HDT from bench to bedside in TB therapy\.

## [Ciddiyet Karnavalı: İroni, Mizah ve Kayıtsızlığa Dair Bir İnceleme](../publications/2ec18bbf405ca4bf5d01.md)

Adem Yılmaz

Bu yazı bir mizah, ironi ve klişe kavramları üzerinden çağdaş deneyimlerimize dair bir eleştiri getirmeyi hedeflemektedir\. Mizah, etkin bir varoluşun, kişinin kendisiyle barışık olmasının ifadesiyken bugün, farklı adlar altında ötekini, kendinden olmayanı alaya almakla bir tutulmaktadır\. Mizahın bu şekilde algılanışın ardında yaşamın klişeleşmesi, eyleme gücünden yoksunluk yer almaktadır\. Yazı, bu güçsüzlük halinin, onu göz ardı etmeyi amaçlayan bir ciddiyet perdesi altına gizlendiğini belirtirken bu ciddiyetinin en aşikâr görünümünün aşırı bir kayıtlılık hali olduğunu iddia edecektir\. Bu iddiasını da Arendt, Adorno, Deleuze ve Kierkegaard ile Comte\-Sponville’in analizleri ile birlikte sunacak olan yazı, yaşantının klişeleşmesi, aşırı etkileşim ve mizahın yaşadığı dönüşüm arasında bir bağ kuracaktır\. Mizahın kendi koşulunu yitirerek ironileştiğini ifade eden yazı, onun eleştirdiği koşul ve süreçleri üreten bir yapıya büründüğüne işaret etmektedir\. Bunun yanında mizahın, politik ve toplumsal güçsüzlüğün gramerine ve daimî bir kayıtlılık hâliyle işleyerek bir kavrayış formuna dönüştüğünün altı çizilecektir\.

## [Development of Moodle\-Based Web\-Based Learning with the Concept of Staged Learning Flow to Improve Learning Outcomes of Junior High School Students](../publications/2ec48713a78432de512d.md)

Asroninaldi; Alwen Bentri; Abna Hidayati; Nofri Hendri; Rayendra Rayendra

Informatics learning at the junior high school \(SMP\) level still faces various challenges, especially in the use of the Learning Management System \(LMS\) which is generally only used as a medium for distributing materials without managing the learning flow systematically\. This research aims to develop Moodle\-based web\-based learning that integrates the concept of Staged Learning Flow to improve the quality of Informatics learning\. The research uses the Research and Development \(R&amp;D\) method with the ADDIE model which includes the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages\. The research subjects consisted of material experts, media experts, linguists, Informatics teachers, and students of grade VII of junior high school\. Data were collected through observation, interviews, questionnaires, and learning outcome tests, then analyzed descriptively and inferentially using eligibility percentage, Paired Sample t\-test, and Normalized Gain \(N\-Gain\)\. The results showed that the product obtained a validity level of 94\.18% with the very valid category, a practicality level of 95\.50% based on the teacher&\#x27;s assessment and 94\.92% based on the response of students with the very practical category, and effectively improved the learning outcomes of students as shown by an increase in the average score from 56\.87 to 85\.73, the significance value of the Paired Sample t\-test of 0\.000 \(p &lt; 0\.05\), and an N\-Gain value of 0\.67 which included Medium category\. The findings of the study show that the integration of the Staged Learning Flow concept into Moodle is able to create more structured learning, increase student engagement, and support improved learning outcomes\. Thus, the Moodle\-based web\-based learning developed is declared valid, practical, and effective to be used as an Informatics learning medium in junior high schools\.

## [Detection Pyramid Reconstruction for Fine\-grained Rice Grain Impurity Detection Using YOLO11s](../publications/2ec74a6afeaaa0ec3b0a.md)

Sunitha N V; Pradeep B S

The Impurity detection in rice grains plays an important role in assessing the quality and food safety as well as automation\.Unfortunately, most object detectors are built for general purposes and work badly for fine\-grained object detection since their design involves low\-resolution prediction layers\.Our work introduces the strategy of Detection Pyramid Reconstruction \(DPR\) of YOLO11s by substituting P5 prediction layer with high\-resolution P2 prediction layer to enhance detection of rice grains and impurities of small and medium sizes while preserving lightweight architecture\.The model was tested on the custom dataset with 195 images and 13,343 annotations of whole rice, broken rice, husk, and stones using five\-fold cross\-validation\.Precision of the model reached 0\.9190 ± 0\.0247, recall 0\.9115 ± 0\.0297, mAP@50 0\.9516 ± 0\.0134 and mAP@50\-95 0\.5040 ± 0\.0078\.The relative improvement of mAP@50\-95 was 4\.98% while decreasing number of trainable parameters by 41\.8% compared with YOLO11s\.Analysis of results obtained from comparisons of YOLOv8s, YOLOv10s and RT\-DETR\-L, together with ablation studies, revealed that the DPR strategy enhances detection performance and computation efficiency\.Additional evaluation on the VisDrone dataset offered supplementary validation besides the rice dataset\.

## [AI Hermeneutic Competence in Qur’anic Exegesis](../publications/2ed7e479efc6c1312eed.md)

Indra Wahyuddin

The development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has significantly transformed various fields of knowledge, including Qur’anic exegesis\. AI can rapidly process Islamic data, analyze language, connect classical and contemporary tafsir sources, and present interpretive information systematically\. These advances have raised scholarly debates concerning whether AI possesses the hermeneutic competence required to interpret the Qur’an\. This study examines AI’s hermeneutic competence by evaluating it against the qualifications of a mufassir within the tradition of ‘ulūm al\-Qur’ān\. It employs a qualitative library research approach\. The findings reveal that AI demonstrates considerable strengths in processing large datasets, retrieving references, recognizing linguistic patterns, and organizing interpretive information efficiently\. Nevertheless, these capabilities remain technical and computational rather than epistemological\. AI cannot fulfill the essential qualifications of a mufassir, including spiritual maturity, religious experience, scholarly intuition, contextual understanding of socio\-religious realities, and ethical responsibility in interpreting divine revelation\. Consequently, AI should not be regarded as a replacement for human mufassirs, but as a complementary tool that supports research, documentation, and access to tafsir sources\. This study argues that the integration of AI into Qur’anic exegesis must remain grounded in the epistemological principles of ‘ulūm al\-Qur’ān\. Maintaining a balance between technological innovation and authoritative interpretive methodology is essential to ensure that Qur’anic interpretation remains academically rigorous, contextually sound, ethically responsible, and faithful to the intellectual tradition of Islamic scholarship\.

## [Spermidine combined with resistance exercise ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction via AMPK\-SIRT1\-PGC\-1α in D\-galactose\-induced aging rats](../publications/2ee9549e9831c2afc37b.md)

Kunda Yang; Lili Sun; Yu Cheng; Kunxiang Liang; Nixi Huang; Yunshuang Liu; Yewenqian Zhang; Chuangye Liu; Lina Peng

Age\-related decline in myocardial structure and function is closely linked to dysregulated mitophagy, impaired mitochondrial biogenesis, and elevated apoptosis\. Spermidine \(SPD\), a naturally occurring polyamine, and resistance exercise \(RE\) are both known to induce autophagy and exert cardioprotective anti\-aging effects\. In the present study, we investigated whether combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction in D\-galactose\-induced aging rats, and explored the underlying mechanisms\. With the exception of a control group, all rats received 6 weeks of daily intraperitoneal D\-galactose injections to induce aging\. Successful model establishment was verified by quantifying expression of the senescence\-associated genes p53, p21, and p16, and by conducting hematoxylin–eosin \(H&amp;E\) and Masson’s trichrome staining\. Following model validation, rats in the aging cohort were assigned to three intervention groups treated for 8 weeks: RE alone, RE \+ vehicle \(VRE\), and SPD \+ RE\. Myocardial tissues were assessed using H&amp;E staining, Masson’s trichrome staining, and transmission electron microscopy\. Myocardial levels of adenosine triphosphate \(ATP\), citrate synthase \(CS\), cytochrome c oxidase subunit I \(COX I\), and mitochondrial membrane potential \(MMP\) were quantified\. Markers of mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, and apoptosis were also quantified\. Molecules of the AMPK\-SIRT1\-PGC\-1α pathway were measured using reverse transcription\-quantitative polymerase chain reaction \(RT\-qPCR\), Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry\. Combined SPD \+ RE intervention significantly ameliorated pathological myocardial structural alterations, mitochondrial morphological abnormalities, and functional impairment\. It elevated myocardial ATP, CS, COX I, and MMP levels, and activated the AMPK\-SIRT1\-PGC\-1α pathway\. Specifically, it upregulated p\-AMPK, SIRT1, PGC\-1α, NRF1, and TFAM to promote mitochondrial biogenesis\. Enhanced mitophagy was confirmed by an increased LC3B\-II/LC3B\-I ratio and reduced p62 expression, while suppressed apoptosis was verified by upregulated Bcl\-2 and downregulated Bax\. In conclusion, combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates age\-related myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction by activating the AMPK\-SIRT1\-PGC\-1α signaling pathway, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy, and inhibiting apoptosis\.

## [Worker and Organizational Factors Associated with Safety Outcomes in Construction Projects in Iba, Zambales: Basis for a Construction Safety Enhancement Plan](../publications/2eef4694c10bc2830b96.md)

Marko Antonio Fernandez

Construction safety remains a significant concern due to the hazardous nature of construction work and the complex interaction of workers and organizational factors that influence safety outcomes\. This study examined worker\-related and organizational factors associated with safety outcomes in construction projects in Iba, Zambales and served as the basis for a proposed Construction Safety Enhancement Plan \(CSEP\)\. A quantitative descriptive\-correlational research design was employed involving 140 construction personnel from selected construction projects in Iba, Zambales\. Data were gathered using a validated structured questionnaire with an overall pilot\-test reliability coefficient of α = \.89\. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, multiple regression, and Structural Equation Modeling \(SEM\) were used to analyze the data\. Findings revealed generally favorable worker behaviors \(M = 3\.42\), attitudes \(M = 3\.71\), and perceptions \(M = 3\.68\), as well as positive assessments of workplace influence \(M = 3\.63\), safety policy effectiveness \(M = 3\.52\), resource availability \(M = 3\.61\), communication and management support \(M = 3\.58\), and safety training effectiveness \(M = 3\.84\)\. Safety outcomes in terms of policy quality \(M = 3\.45\), compliance \(M = 3\.63\), incident rate \(M = 3\.48\), and policy and training refinement \(M = 3\.66\) were likewise rated favorably\. However, SEM results revealed weak and statistically nonsignificant relationships among worker\-related factors, organizational factors, and safety outcomes, indicating limited explanatory power of the proposed model\. Based on the findings, a six\-component Construction Safety Enhancement Plan was developed focusing on safety leadership, hazard management, competency development, communication and participation, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement\. Construction safety is influenced by multiple interacting factors that extend beyond the variables examined in the study\. The proposed CSEP offers a practical framework for strengthening safety culture and supporting continuous safety improvement in construction projects\.

## [RL\-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual\-Channel Retrieval in Long\-Horizon Agent Memory](../publications/2efa138ca5755ac03763.md)

Dabin Sheng; Zhe Wu; Jinming Zhao; Junliang Xing; Yuanchun Shi

Time\-aware retrieval is crucial for long\-horizon LLM agents to effectively leverage ever\-growing long\-term memory\. Existing methods focus on lexical or semantic similarity, leading to target memories being crowded out by temporally mismatched yet semantically similar candidates\. Even time\-aware approaches inject temporal cues only during memory organization or answer generation, overlooking temporal constraints at the retrieval stage, where candidate selection occurs \- the root cause of the displacement\. Inspired by the temporal contiguity effect in human episodic memory, we propose TIDER \(Temporal Interval\-driven Dual\-channel Evidence Retrieval\), a time\-aware agentic retrieval framework\. Central to TIDER is a reinforcement learning \(RL\)\-trained temporal interval locator that infers the temporal windows in which the evidence lies\. RL optimizes window localization as a discrete, non\-differentiable retrieval decision, using composite rewards to convert sparse answer supervision into fine\-grained retrieval feedback\. These temporal windows first define the temporal retrieval channel; the retrieved candidates are then merged with results from the semantic channel and reranked by proximity to the windows\. This temporal grounding enables TIDER to retrieve temporally aligned evidence that would otherwise be drowned out by the volume of semantically similar yet temporally mismatched memories\. With a lightweight 1\.7B locator, TIDER achieves state\-of\-the\-art accuracy on both long\-horizon memory benchmarks \- 61\.52% on LifeBench \(\+8\.82%\) and 78\.96% on LoCoMo \(\+3\.66%\) \- which indicates that temporal cues are crucial for pinpointing target evidence amid a vast pool of semantically similar historical events in long\-term daily\-life memory\.

## [ResQNet: A Crowdsourced Disaster Preparedness and Real\-Time SOS Mesh Network Using Wi\-Fi Direct MANET, Delay Tolerant Networking, and Artificial Intelligence](../publications/2efed33e15e183a08eb9.md)

Hitha Sundar P S; Huma Anjum; Karan Vivek; Roshan Kumar B K; Divyashree

Natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods, cyclones, landslides, and wildfires frequently damage cellular towers and internet infrastructure, leaving victims unable to contact rescue teams and depriving responders of real\-time situational information\. This paper presents ResQNet, a crowdsourced, infrastructure\-independent disaster communication system that uses Wi\-Fi Direct\-based Mobile Ad Hoc Networking \(MANET\) and Delay Tolerant Networking \(DTN\) to relay SOS alerts between nearby smartphones without relying on cellular or internet connectivity\. Each smartphone in the network functions simultaneously as a sender, relay, and store\-and\-forward node: SOS packets, tagged with a unique identifier, timestamp, GPS coordinates, hop count, and time\-to\-live \(TTL\), are propagated hop by hop until they reach an internet\-enabled gateway device or a rescue authority\. Duplicate packet suppression and TTL\-controlled flooding are used to keep the network efficient under heavy load\. ResQNet further incorporates artificial intelligence for emergency severity classification, location\-based clustering of victims, accessibility analysis, and hotspot identification, together with voice\-triggered SOS activation for hands\-free operation\. A web\-based dashboard visualizes live SOS alerts, victim clusters, and priority levels on a map to support rescue coordination\. Simulation\-based evaluation of packet delivery ratio, latency, and message loss indicates that the proposed architecture can sustain reliable emergency communication even when conventional networks fail, offering a scalable and low\-cost foundation for future disaster\-response systems\.

## [Global Research Trends and Emerging Themes in Poultry Coccidiosis: A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis of PubMed Literature](../publications/2f05300052c93fced63a.md)

thousand and five hundred nine articles from 2019 to 2026 were searched using the Bibliometrix package via the Biblioshiny interface\.The outcomes showed that there was a very strong and steady growth of scientific production, with the growth rate of 49\.04% per annum, which demonstrates the fast developing research interest\.It was seen that the research environment was very collaborative, with an average of 7\.17 co\-authors per document and 29\.65% international collaboration\.Poultry Science and Veterinary Parasitology were the few specialized journals in the publication scene, which is predictable according to the law of Bradford\.There was a law of productivity of authors that emphasized the role of a few active researchers\.Themes and key word analysis revealed key research areas such as Eimeria biology, anticoccidial drugs, vaccine development, and gut health\.It is interesting to note that the development of new themes, including microbiota control and phytogenic feed additives, can be viewed as the evolution of a new paradigm of sustainable and integrative disease control\.The analysis of collaboration networks also showed that there were well\-developed clusters of research with the focus on the necessity of multidisciplinary approaches\.Although the study has certain restrictions associated with the utilization of one database and decreased citation indicators, this research acts as a valuable resource of information about the intellectual framework and development of poultry coccidiosis studies\.The results show that the field is dynamic and provides a direction of future studies to conduct especially on how to achieve sustainable and innovative control measures in order to enhance poultry health and productivity\.

## [Early childhood teachers’ practices and perspectives on the integration of smart devices in children’s learning environments](../publications/2f1029a83be1caa32983.md)

Ali Ahmad Al‐Barakat; Rommel Mahmoud AlAli; Sarah Bader Alotaibi; Amal Aboras; Ali Khalifa Atwa Abdullatif; Ashraf Mahrous Nour Zaher

Abstract Digital technology is increasingly used in early childhood education to support children’s engagement, interaction, and learning\. However, limited research has examined how teachers interpret and integrate smart devices into classroom practice, particularly in underrepresented contexts such as Saudi Arabia\. This study explores early childhood teachers’ perceptions and practices regarding the integration of smart devices in children’s learning\. A qualitative research design was employed with 63 early childhood teachers in Al\-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia\. Data were collected through classroom observations and semi\-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis\. The findings revealed four interconnected domains of practice concerning teachers’ integration of smart devices in early childhood settings: children’s digital self\-regulation, guidance for technology use, digital collaboration and social interaction, and digital creativity and innovation\. The findings suggest that smart\-device integration is shaped by teachers’ intentional decisions, pedagogical guidance, and attention to children’s learning needs\. The study contributes context\-sensitive evidence to the literature on digital technology in early childhood education by providing an empirically grounded account of interconnected pedagogical practices within the Saudi Arabian context\. It also highlights the role of teachers in creating meaningful digital learning experiences in which smart devices complement, rather than replace, meaningful interaction and other age\-appropriate learning opportunities\.

## [The Pampa del Indio Project: long\-term variations of Trypanosoma cruzi infection in Triatoma sordida, a non\-target invasive vector](../publications/2f1367f7e0845627b871.md)

Marta Victoria Cardinal; S\. Piñero; Gustavo Fabián Enriquez; M\. S\. Gaspe; Natalia Paula Macchiaverna; A\. Alvedro; R\. E\. Gürtler

Introduction The Gran Chaco region still faces vector\-borne transmission of Trypanosoma cruzi by the main vector, Triatoma infestans \. In Pampa del Indio, a municipality belonging to the Argentinian Chaco, a long\-term research and intervention program achieved the quasielimination of T\. infestans from rural houses and halted the domestic vector\-borne transmission of T\. cruzi \. Here, we evaluate the occurrence and distribution of T\. cruzi infection in Triatoma sordida sensu lato , a secondary species that frequently invades rural domiciles and colonizes the peridomestic environment, over 2007\-2016\. Based on the prevalence of infection reported across the Gran Chaco region in the absence of T\. infestans and given the limited sensitivity of optical microscopy, we hypothesized that T\. cruzi infection in T\. sordida post\-intervention would be higher than in our previous reports \(0\-6%\)\. Methods and results Of 10,728 T\. sordida collected at 528 premises along the intervention, we examined 1,946 specimens by OM or vkDNA\-PCR and found a naïve prevalence of T\. cruzi infection of 1\.44% \(95% CI: 0\.10% –2\.07%\)\. The mean number of infected T\. sordida per house was 1\.12 \(SD = 0\.33\)\. Infection was higher in adults rather than nymphs; maximal in domiciles, intermediate in peridomestic kitchens, storerooms and granaries, and minimal in other peridomestic sites\. Spatial analysis identified an infection hotspot in the northwestern section of the municipality\. By means of single\-season occupancy models, we estimated that the detection probability of T\. cruzi infection was method\-dependent, with OM detecting at most 73% of the truly infected T\. sordida \(assuming 100% detectability with vkDNA\-PCR\)\. Across nearly a decade of vector surveillance and control, T\. cruzi infection in T\. sordida remained &lt;2%, and ≤5% of the houses harboring T\. sordida exhibited infected specimens\. Discussion We report relatively low levels of T\. cruzi infection, one component of Chagas disease transmission risk, in the currently most abundant triatomine vector in Pampa del Indio\. Given the enzootic nature of T\. cruzi transmission cycles, our imperfect knowledge on how they function, and the finding of infected T\. sordida throughout the post\-intervention phase, sustained surveillance within an adaptive management scheme is needed to guarantee long\-term vector\-borne transmission control\.

## [From Billion\-Scale to Million\-Scale Language Models: Operational Capabilities for Embedded Post\-Exploitation](../publications/2f17b2e03c8c2da6b914.md)

Gabriel Hortea; Simon Pietro Romano; Juan Tapiador; Mario Varlese

Small Language Models \(SLMs\) are increasingly attractive for resource\-constrained environments due to their low computational footprint\. These characteristics also make them candidates for future autonomous malware, where connectivity, latency, privacy, or operational constraints may preclude cloud\-based inference\. Yet the ability of ultra\-compact models to support malware during post\-exploitation remains poorly understood\. We systematically evaluate seven open\-source SLMs \(20M\-1\.5B parameters\) on two post\-exploitation code\-generation tasks: Directory Enumeration and Backdoor Generation\. We compare Python \(high\-resource\) and Lua \(low\-resource\) across prompting strategies, task formulations, iterative reasoning, grammar\-constrained decoding, and execution\-feedback loops\. Results show that offensive code\-generation capabilities do not increase linearly with model size\. Successful execution depends on the interaction of model capacity, task formulation, and prompting strategy, with task formulation exerting a greater influence than prompt engineering alone\. Algorithmic formulation combined with few\-shot prompting enables Qwen2\.5\-Coder 1\.5B to reach Pass@5 of 100% in both Python and Lua for Directory Enumeration, 100% in Python for Backdoor Generation, and 99\.2% in Lua\. Although the evaluated models remain too computationally demanding for widespread deployment in contemporary malware, rapid progress in compact models may reduce this barrier\. These findings help anticipate AI\-assisted malware and inform future countermeasures\.

## [A Comparative Study of Client\-Level Stabilization Techniques in Federated Learning for Robust Plant Disease Recognition](../publications/2f17e10f342b104c2944.md)

Aurora\-Felicia Cristea; Ciprian Dobre

The successful integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) algorithms in precision agriculture provided farmers with the means to identify potential issues, such as early disease detection or pest infestations, by making crop\-related predictions\. The new technological developments in this field improve the functioning of traditional agriculture by reducing the dependence on specialized human expertise and facilitating greater access to diagnostic procedures\. However, most studies conducted in this area rely on centralized training of AI models, which leads to increased costs and raised privacy\-related concerns\. Federated learning \(FL\) offers a compelling framework for collaboratively training machine learning \(ML\) models on distributed datasets without centralizing the data owned by each participant\. FL offers significant advantages in the preservation of data privacy, facilitates the collaborative exploitation of geographically distributed data sources, and reduces the risks associated with centralized collection\. In this paper, we investigate the current limitations and performance boundaries of existing Federated and privacy\-preserving learning in distributed sensing systems for plant disease detection, in scenarios that closely resemble real\-world conditions\. Our analysis specifically examined how FL aggregation algorithms, such as FedAvg, FedAvgM and FedProx, work in a custom multi\-client experimental setup where data is partitioned so that each participant observes only those symptom patterns associated with specific environmental and climatic conditions\. We propose further partial aggregation of the local model, an approach where we send only the model backbone to the central server, while the classification head of each participant remains strictly on the client side\. The construction of environmentally heterogeneity is combined with a globally representative stabilizer node designed to preserve knowledge across disease classes that may be absent from certain clients\.

## [Στρατηγικές για λογοθεραπεία σε παιδιά με δυσαριθμησία](../publications/2f1aec02583beabf6735.md)

ΧΑΡΑΛΑΜΠΟΣ ΓΕΩΡΓΙΑΔΗΣ

Σκοπός της παρούσας μελέτης ήταν η διερεύνηση των στρατηγικών λογοθεραπείας που εφαρμόζονται σε παιδιά με δυσαριθμησία, καθώς και η αξιολόγηση της στάσης των εκπαιδευτικών και λογοθεραπευτών απέναντι σε αυτά τα παιδιά\. Η μελέτη περιέλαβε τη συλλογή ποσοτικών και ποιοτικών δεδομένων μέσω ερωτηματολογίων και παρατηρήσεων σε 10 εκπαιδευτικούς και 10 λογοθεραπευτές του Δημοτικού Σχολείου «Πέταρ Μπερόν»\. Τα αποτελέσματα ανέδειξαν τη σημασία της εξατομικευμένης παρέμβασης, της συνεργασίας μεταξύ σχολείου, λογοθεραπευτή και οικογένειας, καθώς και της χρήσης πολυαισθητηριακών και βιωματικών τεχνικών για την ανάπτυξη αριθμητικών δεξιοτήτων\. Επιπλέον, διαπιστώθηκε ότι η ενεργή συμμετοχή των γονέων και η θετική στάση των εκπαιδευτικών συμβάλλουν στη μείωση του μαθηματικού άγχους και στη βελτίωση της αυτοεκτίμησης των παιδιών\. Συμπερασματικά, η λογοθεραπευτική παρέμβαση, όταν είναι συστηματική και εξατομικευμένη, υποστηρίζει τόσο τις μαθηματικές δεξιότητες όσο και τη συνολική γνωστική και ψυχοκοινωνική ανάπτυξη των παιδιών με δυσαριθμησία\.

## [The synergistic potential of combining PD\-1/PD\-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapies in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma](../publications/2f1cbff63cab15f428e5.md)

RuYan Li; Zihao Heng; Xi Cheng

Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma \(ESCC\) is associated with a poor prognosis, and the efficacy of conventional therapies \(chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery\) remains limited\. The advent of programmed death 1 \(PD\-1\)/programmed death\-ligand 1 \(PD\-L1\) inhibitors has substantially altered the treatment paradigm for ESCC\. The combination of these immune checkpoint inhibitors \(ICIs\) with conventional treatments demonstrates significant synergistic potential\. Standard oncological regimens often center on chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or various combinations thereof\. This synergy stems from complementary mechanisms: conventional therapies can induce immunogenic cell death, release tumor antigens, and remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby laying the groundwork for immunotherapy\. In turn, PD\-1/PD\-L1 inhibitors work by releasing the “brakes” on T cells, activating and enhancing the host anti\-tumor immune response\. This facilitates the elimination of residual cancer cells and establishes long\-term immune surveillance\. In conclusion, the combination of PD\-1/PD\-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapy achieves a greater\-than\-additive \(“1 \+ 1&gt;2”\) effect and has evolved into a standard first\-line treatment strategy for advanced/metastatic ESCC, substantially improving patient outcomes\. Future research will focus on optimizing combination protocols, overcoming resistance, and precisely identifying patient populations most likely to benefit\.

## [Data Science: from stochastics to machine learning with Python](../publications/2f217c8027f73fcbe199.md)

Konrad Voelkel

An undergraduate introduction to data science that begins with stochastics and ends with machine learning without leaving a gap in between\. The estimators and learning algorithms — k\-means, principal component analysis, regression, expectation maximization — are reimplemented rather than called\. Thirty chapters covering probability spaces, random variables and distributions; expected value, variance and the central limit theorem; vectorised computation with Numpy and Scipy; exploratory data analysis with Pandas and Matplotlib; multivariate statistics, covariance and relative entropy; statistical models, maximum likelihood, tests and model selection; and data protection under the GDPR\. The English edition of the lecture notes used in the computer science bachelor&\#x27;s programme at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf\. Published as a website and as a 318\-page PDF; sources, including every notebook, at github\.com/konradvoelkel/ds\-en\.

## [Narrative Voice, Memory, and Postcolonial Identity Formation: A Comparative Analytical Study of Lyrical Storytelling in the Select Novels of Arundhati Roy and Kiran Desai](../publications/2f2e17b71849afd11b56.md)

Abhimanue Yadav; Shikha Dutt Sharma

The rise of the postcolonial narratives has predicted the intricacies of fractured identities informed by the past, displacement and cultural ambivalence\. Nevertheless, the significance of lyrical narrative voice as a memory creating and mediating mechanism is under\-researched\. This paper examines the interplay of narrative voice and memory to construct postcolonial identity in these two novels that were chosen Arundhati Roy and Kiran Desai\. Through the application of qualitative comparative textual analysis based on the postcolonial and memory theory, the paper examines how the two authors employ lyrical narratives told through non\-linear storytelling, remembrance imagery and rhythmic language in re\-creating personal and community experiences\. It is argued in the analysis that the role of the lyrical narrative voice is a compelling discursive tool wherein fragmented identities are researched, which enables characters to power brokering trauma, belonging, and cultural dislocation\. Although the narrative style of Roy is more intimate and localized in terms of memory and emotional richness, the one of Desai is indicative of the general diasporic conflicts and national identity construction\. This study can help to better explain how modern Indian English fiction can be articulated by focusing on the issues of memory, voice, and postcolonial subjectivity\.

## [ECLIPSE v2\.0: a reproducible scaffold for severe confirmatory testing through preregistration, single\-shot validation, and static\-analysis screening](../publications/2f3b8874bc89b5926ecb.md)

Camilo Alejandro Sjöberg Tala

Abstract The replication crisis has exposed systematic methodological weaknesses across the empirical sciences, yet existing infrastructure offers little technical enforcement and few reproducible tools for assessing rigor\. We propose ECLIPSE v2\.0, a computational scaffold combining preregistration, cryptographically verified data splitting \(SHA\-256\), single\-shot holdout validation, integrity scoring, anomaly screening and static analysis into an auditable workflow for confirmatory testing\. Three instruments are introduced, each an operational tool rather than a definitive measure: the Eclipse Integrity Score, a heuristic operationalization of protocol\-level integrity across five dimensions; the Standardized Test\-set Discrepancy Score, a descriptive signal flagging holdout results unusually good relative to cross\-validation folds, screened against empirically derived cutoffs rather than nominal significance levels; and an Automated Code Auditor screening scripts for protocol violations\. Controlled construct checks demonstrate component non\-redundancy and ranking stability under the synthetic generator and weighting schemes used, but not external validity\. No retrospective corpus can validly compute the score alongside replication outcomes, so we pre\-specify a prospective test of incremental validity over binary preregistration and cite evidence that broad methodological\-quality indicators track external\-validation performance in clinical prediction models, which is indirectly relevant rather than a validation of those dimensions\. ECLIPSE is offered as a scaffold, not a guarantee of compliance\.

## [DESAFÍOS EDUCATIVOS FRENTE A LOS RESULTADOS DE PISA EN ESTUDIANTES DE EDUCACIÓN MEDIA DE PARAGUAY: PERSPECTIVAS DE DOCENTES, FAMILIAS Y ESTADO](../publications/2f3eb4a327b11f262ed7.md)

Juana Domínguez de Mora

Los resultados de Paraguay en el Programa para la Evaluación Internacional de los Estudiantes \(PISA\) 2022 evidencian importantes desafíos en los aprendizajes de los estudiantes de 15 años\. Solo el 15 % alcanzó al menos el nivel 2 de competencia en Matemática, frente al 34 % en Lectura y el 29 % en Ciencias \(OECD, 2023\)\. Estos resultados constituyen un punto de partida para analizar las condiciones que intervienen en el proceso educativo y los aspectos que requieren fortalecimiento\. El presente trabajo analiza esta realidad desde tres dimensiones relacionadas: la práctica docente, el acompañamiento familiar y las políticas y condiciones educativas promovidas por el Estado\. Desde un enfoque descriptivo y documental, se revisan resultados de PISA, documentos oficiales, investigaciones y aportes de organismos vinculados con la educación, complementados con una reflexión sobre el contexto educativo paraguayo\. En la práctica docente se consideran la formación disciplinar y pedagógica, la actualización profesional, las estrategias de enseñanza, la evaluación formativa y las condiciones laborales\. En el ámbito familiar se abordan el acompañamiento del aprendizaje, los hábitos de estudio, la comunicación con la institución y la corresponsabilidad educativa, considerando las asociaciones identificadas por PISA entre determinadas formas de participación familiar y las actitudes y estrategias de aprendizaje \(OECD, 2024\)\. Finalmente, se examinan políticas relacionadas con equidad, formación docente, infraestructura, recursos, conectividad, convivencia escolar y seguimiento\. El análisis evidencia que la mejora de los aprendizajes constituye un desafío multidimensional que requiere articulación entre docentes, familias, instituciones y políticas educativas\.

## [Behavioral\-metabolic phenotypes and differential risks of diabetic kidney disease and peripheral neuropathy in type 2 diabetes: a latent class analysis](../publications/2f425ba6c45d1e146cd3.md)

Yue Wang; Zijian Liu; Zhang Zhengshan; An Hu; Lin Liu; Shuanghui Zeng; Ping Liu; Yahui Wang; Sun Luying

Background Behavioral and metabolic risk factors frequently coexist in type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\), but their combined patterns and associations with microvascular complications remain insufficiently characterized\. Methods This cohort study included 706 individuals with T2DM\. Outcome\-specific risk sets were established by excluding participants with prevalent diabetic kidney disease \(DKD\) or diabetic peripheral neuropathy \(DPN\) at baseline\. Behavioral and metabolic factors were classified using latent class analysis\. Multinomial logistic regression and Cox models, alongside socioeconomic status \(SES\)\-stratified analyses, assessed associations among phenotypes, SES, and incident complications\. Results Three behavioral\-metabolic phenotypes were identified: the Behavioral\-Visceral Adiposity \(BVA\) phenotype \(14\.3%\), characterized by unhealthy lifestyle behaviors, lower BMI, and higher visceral adiposity; the Obesity\-Related Metabolic Risk \(OMR\) phenotype \(39\.8%\), characterized by obesity, physical inactivity, insulin resistance, and suboptimal blood pressure control; and the Low\-Risk \(LR\) phenotype \(45\.9%\)\. Compared with the LR phenotype, the OMR phenotype showed increased risks of incident DKD \(HR = 2\.01; 95% CI = 1\.32–3\.04\) and DPN \(HR = 2\.06; 95% CI = 1\.18–3\.58\)\. The BVA phenotype was associated with increased risk of DPN \(HR = 2\.47; 95% CI = 1\.19–5\.12\)\. SES was independently associated with phenotype membership\. Associations between the OMR phenotype and DKD or DPN were mainly observed among individuals with low SES, whereas the association between the BVA phenotype and DPN was mainly observed among individuals with high SES\. Conclusions Three distinct behavioral\-metabolic phenotypes were identified among individuals with T2DM and showed differential associations with DKD and DPN risks\. Integrating behavioral patterns, metabolic profiles, and socioeconomic context into risk stratification strategies may enhance early identification and individualized prevention of microvascular complications\.

## [Smart Framing Through IoT Sensors](../publications/2f4c38c6578f544d1eed.md)

Abhishek Srivastva; Prabhash Chandra Pathak

Currently, farmers assess their soil and crops by walking through the fields occasionally\. This paper describes a more efficient method: small sensor units positioned in the soil which transmit data to the phone or computer all day\. We describe the setup of this system including the soil moisture, soil temperature, soil pH, nutrient and weather sensors and the way that they are used to identify when to water and fertilize\. We explain the system components, discuss the major sensors and wireless communications, and provide a simple testing plan\. Previous field trials show that watering based on sensor data can save 20\-50% of water without compromising yield and issues can be detected in minutes and not days\. We also discuss difficulties \(cost, limited network coverage, sensor degradation over time and security concerns\), and how we might see things evolve in the future\. Overall, sensor\-monitoring is practical and can be used to reduce waste in farming\.

## [Sample\-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Policy Improvement via Flow\-Reversed Action Anchors](../publications/2f5f7789295259117ad6.md)

Carl Qi; Weijun Dong; Xiaojie Wang; Peiyi Chen; Rahul Sajnani; Mingyuan Zhang; Amy Zhang; Jose Barreiros; Manikatan Nambi; Lillian J\. Ratliff; Dylan Randle

Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment\-level reliability and throughput remains difficult\. Reinforcement learning \(RL\) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction\. Existing methods adapt frozen flow\-matching policies by treating noise space as a continuous action space\. We show that this behaviorally unstructured space makes exploration inefficient, often preventing these methods from extracting meaningful learning signals on challenging tasks\. We introduce AnchorQ, which enables coarse\-to\-fine policy improvement through a structured, refinable latent action representation\. At each decision step, AnchorQ uses flow reversal to map reference behaviors to state\-conditioned latent anchors, samples local particles around those anchors, and applies value\-guided sampling to explore promising refinements\. Our analysis shows that anchors reduce identification complexity at the cost of support bias; particle refinement trades this bias against action\-class complexity; and critic accuracy determines the reliability of KL\-regularized, value\-guided selection\. Across simulated and real\-world manipulation tasks, AnchorQ outperforms state\-of\-the\-art post\-training baselines in sample efficiency, delivering a 37% improvement in real\-world success rate and 97% higher simulated task throughput under the same interaction budget\. Additional visualizations are available on our website https://anchorq\-rl\.com/\.

## [INNOVATIVE LENDING AS A TOOL FOR THE POST\-WAR MODERNIZATION OF UKRAINE&\#x27;S ECONOMY](../publications/2f65cdb7c19bb03af92e.md)

Віолетта Харабара

The prospects for the development of innovative lending in Ukraine depend to a large extent on the state’s ability to establish effective mechanisms for providing financial support to businesses that implement technological innovations\. Among such mechanisms, the ‘Affordable Loans 5\-7\-9%’ programme holds a special place, having proven its effectiveness in the challenging macroeconomic conditions of martial law\. Expanding this programme involves not only increasing the volume of budgetary funding for interest rate compensation, but also differentiating lending conditions depending on the nature of the innovation project, its degree of technological complexity, and its potential impact on the competitiveness of the national economy\.

## [A bioinspired conceptual framework for adaptive university press management](../publications/2f72530ea676947a181a.md)

Ángel Torres\-Toukoumidis; Saúl Fernando Pesántez Vicuña; Esteban Inga; Monica Rodas

University presses face converging pressures from scholarly quality, peer\-review integrity, reviewer scarcity, Open Science, artificial intelligence, international visibility, and economic sustainability\. This article proposes Epigenetic Editorial Intelligence, a bioinspired conceptual framework that represents stable institutional rules as Editorial DNA and models operational adaptation through epigenetic regulation, an Artificial Immune System, organizational memory, human–AI collaboration, and multiobjective optimization\. Nine operational indicators are formalized and aggregated into a Global Editorial Intelligence Index \(GEII\)\. Internal model behavior is examined through paired synthetic ablations that disable one mechanism at a time, using 200 Monte Carlo repetitions, common random\-number streams, 95% confidence intervals, alternative weighting schemes and 1000 Dirichlet weight perturbations\. Results are interpreted as structural\-consistency diagnostics rather than empirical validation\. This work provides a reproducible conceptual and mathematical foundation for subsequent implementation and testing with real editorial records\.

## [Artificial intelligence application in predictive maintenance for industrial systems](../publications/2f7811fd87f3573bd2a5.md)

Σοφία Παπαδοπούλου

Στο σύγχρονο βιομηχανικό περιβάλλον, οι απρόβλεπτες βλάβες του εξοπλισμού προκαλούν υψηλό οικονομικό κόστος, καθώς και σοβαρούς κινδύνους για την ασφάλεια και το περιβάλλον\. Για την αντιμετώπιση αυτού του προβλήματος, η Προβλεπτική Συντήρηση \(Predictive Maintenance \- PdM\) αποτελεί την πιο αποδοτική στρατηγική\. Σε αντίθεση με τις παραδοσιακές πρακτικές συντήρησης, οι οποίες εφαρμόζονται ετεροχρονισμένα ή με σταθερά χρονοδιαγράμματα, η Προβλεπτική Συντήρηση βασίζεται στη συνεχή παρακολούθηση της πραγματικής κατάστασης των μηχανημάτων \(Condition\-Based Maintenance\)\. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία αξιολογεί τη χρήση αλγορίθμων Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης \(ΤΝ\) για εφαρμογές Προβλεπτικής Συντήρησης στη εποχή του Industry 4\.0 και των Κυβερνο\-φυσικών Συστημάτων \(CPS\)\. Η μεθοδολογία περιλαμβάνει μια εκτενή βιβλιογραφική ανασκόπηση σε τέσσερις βασικούς τομείς: Ενέργεια, Μεταποίηση, Μεταφορές και Βαριά Βιομηχανία\. Οι επιλεγμένες μελέτες αναλύθηκαν με βάση την πρακτική τους εφαρμογή, την απόδοση των αλγορίθμων και την επικαιρότητά τους\. Τα ευρήματα τεκμηριώνουν ότι οι αρχιτεκτονικές Βαθιάς Μάθησης, ιδιαίτερα τα δίκτυα LSTM για εκτίμηση Εναπομένουσας Ωφέλιμης Ζωής \(RUL\) και τα CNN για εικονοβασισμένη διάγνωση βλαβών, υπερτερούν των κλασικών αλγορίθμων Μηχανικής Μάθησης σε συνθήκες επαρκών δεδομένων, επιτυγχάνοντας ακρίβεια έως 99% σε επιλεγμένες εφαρμογές\. Οι υβριδικές προσεγγίσεις, που συνδυάζουν φυσικά μοντέλα \(physics\-based\) με δεδομενοκεντρικούς αλγορίθμους, αποδεικνύονται ανθεκτικότερες σε μεταβαλλόμενες συνθήκες λειτουργίας και ανεπαρκή ιστορικά δεδομένα\. Διατομεακά, αναδεικνύεται ότι τα κυριότερα εμπόδια για τη βιομηχανική υιοθέτηση της ΤΝ δεν είναι πλέον αλγοριθμικά, αλλά επιχειρησιακά, όπως η σπανιότητα επισημασμένων δεδομένων αστοχίας, η αδιαφάνεια των μοντέλων Βαθιάς Μάθησης και απουσία τυποποιημένων πρωτοκόλλων αξιολόγησης\. Η εργασία καταλήγει ότι η ερευνητική προτεραιότητα της επόμενης δεκαετίας έγκειται στην ανάπτυξη Ερμηνεύσιμων \(XAI\), ανθεκτικών και υπολογιστικά αποδοτικών συστημάτων PdM βιομηχανικής κλίμακας, μέσω της διεπιστημονικής συνεργασίας μηχανολόγων, επιστημόνων δεδομένων και ρυθμιστικών αρχών\.

## [A comprehensive examination of the current AI landscape in ocean sciences: applications, challenges, and emerging trends](../publications/2f8053e99d82cc4a9326.md)

Tiara Mulder; Spencer Bialek; Shen Molloy; Alexi Baccardax Westcott; Shayla Fitzsimmons

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) are increasingly used in ocean sciences to analyze large, complex, and unevenly sampled datasets from satellites, autonomous platforms, sensors, vessels, and genomic tools\. This review examines how AI and ML are being applied across major areas of ocean research, including physical oceanography, coastal hazards, marine biogeochemistry, ecology, remote sensing, acoustics, marine geology, and applied ocean engineering\. Using a literature\-synthesis workflow supported by Schlitsummarizer and full\-text extraction methods, this paper identifies key applications, emerging trends, research gaps, and limitations in ocean\-based ML\. The review shows that ML is particularly useful for predicting surface currents, reconstructing subsurface ocean conditions, forecasting waves, estimating biogeochemical variables, classifying marine organisms and habitats, improving remote\-sensing products, and supporting autonomous observing systems\. Emerging trends include the growth of deep learning, physics\-informed machine learning, explainable AI, data integration across observing platforms, and management\-focused applications related to climate adaptation, coastal planning, fisheries, and environmental monitoring\. However, major challenges remain, including sparse and biased ocean observations, limited data from deep\-ocean and polar regions, validation bias, poor model transferability, class imbalance in ecological datasets, black\-box model behavior, and uncertainty under changing climate conditions\. Overall, this review argues that AI and ML are valuable tools for expanding ocean observation and prediction, but they must be used alongside oceanographic knowledge, careful validation, and transparent interpretation to ensure reliable scientific and management outcomes\.

## [Structural optimization in TensErLEED using a parameter tree and R\-factor gradients](../publications/2f8444ec4a25a458b7c0.md)

Alexander M\. Imre; Paul Haidegger; Florian Kraushofer; Ralf Wanzenböck; Tobias Hable; Sarah Tobisch; Marie Kienzer; Florian Buchner; Jesús Carrete; Georg K\. H\. Madsen; Michael Schmid; Ulrike Diebold; Michele Riva

Abstract Quantitative low\-energy electron diffraction \[LEED I \( V \)\] is a powerful method for surface\-structure determination, based on a direct comparison of I \( V \) data between experiment and computations for a structure model\. As the diffraction intensities I are highly sensitive to subtle structural changes, local structure optimization is essential for assessing the validity of a structure model and finding the best\-fit structure\. Even when using the tensor\-LEED approximation—which accelerates optimization by applying a perturbative treatment of small deviations from a reference structure—the optimization process is computationally expensive\. In the new tensor\-LEED implementation presented in this work, the problem of surface\-structure optimization is reformulated using a tree\-based data structure, which helps to avoid redundant function evaluations\. Intensities are computed on the fly, eliminating limitations of previous algorithms using grid\-based search with precomputed values\. This enables the use of state\-of\-the\-art optimization algorithms\. Implemented in Python with the JAX library, the method provides access to gradients of the R factor and supports execution on graphics processing units \(GPUs\)\. These developments reduce the computing time by more than an order of magnitude\.

## [Métodos diagnósticos para la detección de infecciones por Helicobacter pylori: una revisión sistemática](../publications/2f87cbdc201c2e4ff47a.md)

Karla Lizeth Lascano Salazar; Francisco Javier Ustáriz Fajardo

Introducción\. La infección por Helicobacter pylori, es un problema de salud pública a nivel mundial por su alta incidencia y patologías gastrointestinales asociadas\. Actualmente, los métodos diagnósticos se clasifican en invasivos y no invasivos con diferentes desempeños de validez y sin consenso de aplicación clínica\. Objetivo\. Comparar la precisión diagnostica de métodos invasivos y no invasivos para la detección de infecciones por H\. pylori, basándose en evidencia científica sobre sensibilidad\-especificidad\. Metodología\. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de evidencia según las directrices PRISMA 2020, centrada en Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, empleando términos controlados MeSH, descriptores como: Helicobacter pylori, diagnosis, diagnostic methods, detection, sensitivity, specificity, combinados mediante operadores booleanos\. Seleccionándose, estudios primarios de precisión diagnóstica; la calidad metodológica y riesgo de sesgo se evaluó mediante QUADAS\-2\. Resultados\. El análisis comparativo mostró que métodos invasivos \(histología, prueba bioquímica para detectar la actividad ureasa y reacción en cadena de la polimerasa en tiempo real en biopsia\), alcanzaron valores máximos de sensibilidad y especificidad\. Entre los métodos no invasivos \(prueba de liento con urea marcada con Carbono\-13 y prueba de reacción en cadena de la polimerasa fecal\) mostraron rendimientos de validez equivalentes a los métodos invasivos, constituyéndose como alternativa diagnóstica para H\. pylori\. Conclusión\. La evidencia disponible sugiere que los métodos invasivos presentan la mayor precisión diagnóstica; sin embargo, las técnicas y modalidades emergentes y la instauración de sistemas de inteligencia artificial al diagnóstico de H\. pylori se dirigen hacia estrategias combinadas que logren integrar métodos no invasivos de alta precisión\. Área de estudio general: Laboratorio Clínico\. Área de estudio específica: Salud y Bienestar\. Tipo de estudio: Revisión sistemática\.

## [SIT\-Eval: Situation\-Based Interactive Turn\-by\-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents](../publications/2f9190e5be9994f8ad60.md)

Ravil Mussabayev; Saveliy Zavertyaev; Dmitriy Parpulov; Andrey Savchenko

The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects\. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations\-\-\-a critical safety gap, as low\-probability events become frequent failures at production scale\. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage\. We introduce SIT\-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation\-based conversational agents\. We formalize an agent&\#x27;s desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q\. At each conversation turn, an LLM\-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation\. A context\-aware LLM\-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent&\#x27;s reply for that situation\. The judge is validated using human\-verified synthetic golden dialogues\. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules\. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning\.

## [Estabilización y control de un sistema de levitación magnética de segundo orden utilizando diseñosde control basados en Lyapunov](../publications/2f9a6dff117bd187ad72.md)

Oscar Danilo Montoya; Walter Gil\-González; Luis Fernando Grisales Noreña; Oscar Danilo Montoya

This paper presents a Lyapunov\-based control framework for stabilizing a second\-order magnetic levitation system \(MLS\)\. The study explores three distinct candidate Lyapunov functions—exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric\-quadratic—to derive nonlinear controllers ensuring asymptotic stability\. The proposed control laws are designed to regulate the levitating mass position while minimizing control effort\. A systematic tuning process using particle swarm optimization \(PSO\) is employed to optimize control parameters based on performance indices, including ITAE, IAE, ITSE, and total control energy\. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the control strategies, showing that all controllers successfully stabilize the MLS while exhibiting different transient responses and energy consumption levels\. The logarithmic Lyapunov\-based controller demonstrates superior performance in terms of precision, response speed, and energy efficiency\. Future work aims to extend these methods to handle parameter uncertainties and disturbances while exploring machine learning\-based control optimization\.

## [ASSESSMENT OF AVOIDABLE MORTALITY IN UKRAINE: ADAPTATION OF AN INTERNATIONAL METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK](../publications/2fa1b4c167a26e01116b.md)

Lekhan Vn; Mykola I\. Zaiarskyi

Introduction\. Assessment of avoidable mortality is widely used to characterize potentially avoidable health losses and certain aspects of health system performance\.Aim\. To develop and pilot a reproducible methodology for adapting the approach of the Organisation for Economic Co\-operation and Development and European Statistical Office \(OECD/Eurostat\) to the assessment of avoidable mortality using official statistical data from Ukraine\.Materials and methods\. The OECD/Eurostat methodology \(2022 version\), including the list of preventable and amenable causes of death, corresponding ICD\-10 codes, and an age limit of 0–74 years, was used as the methodological basis\. An algorithm was developed to harmonize data from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine for 2018–2020, including classification of harmonization mapping types, direct age standardization using the OECD 2015 Standard Population, assessment of statistical uncertainty, and sensitivity and robustness analyses under the Base\-case and Extended harmonization scenarios\.Results\. Of the 93 OECD/Eurostat harmonization units, 81 showed full or practically full correspondence with the Ukrainian data, whereas 12 had methodological limitations\. In 2020, under the Base\-case scenario, the total avoidable mortality rate was 467\.1 per 100,000 population, exceeding the reference levels reported for the OECD and European Union \(EU\), but falling within the range observed in some Central and Eastern European countries\. Ischemic heart disease accounted for 50\.6% of deaths classified as total avoidable mortality in the Base\-case scenario\. For 2018–2020, the preventable\-to\-amenable mortality ratio was 1\.15 in the Base\-case scenario and 1\.38 in the Extended scenario, compared with 1\.81 in the EU\. The male\-to\-female ratio for total avoidable mortality was 2\.44 and 2\.50, respectively\. Inclusion of harmonization units with methodological limitations increased the total avoidable mortality rate by 14\.6%, with the largest increase observed for preventable mortality \(\+26\.6%\), whereas amenable mortality increased by 4\.9%\.Conclusions\. The developed algorithm yielded reproducible and epidemiologically plausible estimates of avoidable mortality, demonstrating its applicability to official Ukrainian mortality data\. Absolute estimates, particularly for preventable mortality, were sensitive to the harmonization scenario, whereas the main structural patterns and sex differences remained robust\.

## [A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Customer Churn Predictive in e\-Commerce](../publications/2fa4c280fdc66fb94cff.md)

Lew Sook Ling; Yi Qi Tan; Ram Avtar

Customer churn rate is one of the main challenges that e\-Commerce businesses must address, as it may affect revenue and long\-term growth\. In this paper, predictive analysis was used to identify potential customers who would be lost\. It uses two different types of data to evaluate and compare the performance of five Machine Learning \(ML\) models, namely logistic regression, decision tree, support vector machine, gradient boost and random forest\. Accuracy, precision, recall rate and F1 score are used as indicators of model performance\. Among them, random forest achieved the highest performance across both datasets, demonstrating superior predictive power and consistency\. By validating results on multiple datasets, this paper not only ensures reliability but also highlights the stability of churn prediction models across varying data conditions\. The findings indicate that effective churn prediction can support proactive customer retention strategies, enabling e\-Commerce businesses to minimize losses and promote sustainable growth\. The use of two datasets represents a notable contribution, as it provides a stronger basis for assessing model generalizability and avoiding bias toward a single data source\. The findings indicate that accurate churn prediction can support proactive retention strategies, enabling e\-Commerce businesses to reduce churned customers, enhance loyalty, and maintain a competitive advantage\. Overall, this paper underscores the value of data\-driven approaches, demonstrates the benefits of employing multiple datasets for model validation, and provides actionable insights for businesses aiming to implement effective and sustainable customer retention strategies\.
