## [Direct probabilistic IMPT treatment planning with setup and range errors for neuro\-oncological patients](../publications/2fbb43ce35664d323a75.md)

Jelte R\. de Jong; Sebastiaan Breedveld; Steven Habraken; Mischa S\. Hoogeman; Jenneke I\. de Jong; Danny Lathouwers; Zoltán Perkó

Abstract Objective \. To show computational feasibility of a previously proposed probabilistic planning approach on a neuro\-oncological patient group, we compared probabilistic plans with \(automated\) robust plans for one patient \(group A\) that could achieve sufficient clinical target coverage and for four patients \(group B\) where target coverage had to be compromised due to organ\-at\-risk \(OAR\) dose constraints\. Approach \. The probabilistic approach is percentile\-based and uses the fact that a \(dose\) percentile can be approximated as a linear combination of its expected value and standard deviation\. This allows us to formulate objectives and constraints with patient\-specific acceptance probabilities\. The optimization has a nested structure: the inner optimization optimizes the beam weights for a given percentile estimate, while an outer loop iteratively updates and improves the accuracy of the percentile estimate\. For every outer iteration, the optimization is warm\-started from the previous iteration\. Percentiles are efficiently calculated by sampling a polynomial chaos expansion of the dose\-influence matrix\. Main results \. The patient in group A achieved cumulative OAR dose reductions \(of OAR\-related DVH\-metrics\) of 23\.1 GyRBE, for identical target coverage\. Target coverage improved for all patients in group B \(the 10th percentile of D 99\.8 % increased up to 0\.61 GyRBE\), at the same time reaching cumulative OAR dose reductions \(of OAR\-related DVH\-metrics\) up to about 40 GyRBE\. Probabilistic plans were optimized in 44 h to 226 h\. For two representative patients, eliminating warm\-starting \(i\.e\. the outer loop\) from the approach reduced total optimization times to below 10 h \(which took originally 80 h and 141 h\)\. Significance \. Compared to robust optimization methods, the probabilistic approach achieves improved trade\-offs between probabilistic target coverage and OAR sparing, potentially leading to better treatments\.

## [Physicochemical quality and irrigation suitability of groundwater resources in the Feija aquifer \(southeastern Morocco\)](../publications/2fbc4fcaac449062e104.md)

Hamid Nadi; Fathalah Elwahab; Hicham Ouhakki; Mehdi Boudraine; Marjaa Hanae; Nabila Auajjar; Naima Dohou; Khalid Yamni; Moulay Laarbi Ouahidi

Groundwater is the primary water resource in the arid Feija plain \(Zagora, Morocco\), but its quality is increasingly threatened by climate change and intensive agriculture\. This study assessed the physicochemical quality and irrigation suitability of the Feija aquifer\. Over three years \(2022–2024\), 96 groundwater samples were collected from eight wells \(P1–P8\) in all four seasons to assess spatial and temporal variability\. Physicochemical parameters, including pH, electrical conductivity \(EC\), and major ions, were analysed\. The results indicate high mineralisation, with a mean EC of 2934\.14 µS∙cm−1 and significant spatial heterogeneity\. Correlation analysis and principal component analysis \(PCA\) identified two dominant processes: a salinity gradient driven by natural water–rock interactions and evaporative concentration, and a pollution gradient linked to diffuse agricultural inputs \(nitrates and bicarbonates\)\. Seasonal box plots identify summer as a critical period, with nitrate concentrations frequently exceeding the 50 mg∙dm−3 drinking\-water threshold and EC values peaking in autumn\. High sodium and chloride concentrations indicate a sodium–chloride hydrochemical facies, with agricultural intensification contributing to groundwater degradation\. Irrigation\-suitability indices calculated from the mean ionic composition \(sodium adsorption ratio, SAR ≈ 3\.4; permeability index, PI ≈ 67%\) indicate a high to very high salinity hazard \(Richards’ USSL classes C3–C4, based on measured EC\), a low sodium hazard \(class S1\) and a permissible to good permeability class \(Doneen class II\)\. Salinity, rather than sodicity, is therefore the main constraint on irrigation use\.

## [Lysosomal exoglycosidases as biomarkers of systemic diseases – what’s new?](../publications/2fbc54d8852ae3eec6dd.md)

Iwona Ptaszyńska\-Sarosiek; Weronika Wiktoria Sarosiek; Gabriela Iga Sarosiek; Anna Charuta; Mateusz Maciejczyk

Numerous studies suggest that lysosomal exoglycosidases can be utilised in the diagnosis and monitoring of various diseases\. This paper summarises recent reports on the clinical use of N\-acetyl\-β\-D\-hexosaminidase \(HEX\), β\-glucuronidase \(GLU\), β\-galactosidase \(GAL\), α\-mannosidase \(MAN\) and α\-L\-fucosidase \(FUC\) in systemic diseases\. The clinical relevance of exoglycosidases has been demonstrated in liver disease, alcohol use disorder \(AUD\) in adults, nicotine addiction, kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, nasopharyngeal disease and musculoskeletal disorders\. Exoglycosidase activity correlates with disease severity and is characterised by high sensitivity, though low specificity\. However, lysosomal exoglycosidases may have a particular application in addiction medicine\. Compared to routine biomarkers, they are more sensitive and specific to alcohol\-induced damage\. Importantly, lysosomal exoglycosidases \(especially HEX and its isoenzymes\) show a greater correlation with acute ethanol exposure and are less dependent on individual factors \(age, gender, comorbidities\)\.

## [A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THRESHOLD, REFERENCE AND MACHINE\-BASED APPROACHES TO ASSESSING THE CORRECTNESS OF REHABILITATION EXERCISES](../publications/2fbcb44d0d3db078d08a.md)

Mariia Korostylova; Oleg Kobylin; Ilya Kobylin

The task of automatically assessing the correctness of rehabilitation exercise performance based on key body points extracted from video is considered\. Three approaches — threshold\-based, reference\-based \(dynamic time warping, DTW\) and machine\-based \(Random Forest\) — are compared on the REHAB24\-6 dataset for three exercises \(arm abduction, leg abduction, squats\)\. Group cross\-validation by participant and McNemar&\#x27;s exact test are applied; the results are compared against trivial baseline classification levels\. A useful predictive signal is shown not to be present for all exercises: for arm abduction the machine\-based approach achieved an accuracy of 82\.1 % against a baseline of 56\.2 %, whereas for squats no approach exceeded the baseline\. The advantages and limitations of each approach for use in home telerehabilitation systems are identified\.

## [Hydroglyphus hamulatus \(Gyllenhal, 1813\) \(Coleoptera, Dytiscidae\), a predaceous diving beetle species new to the Czech Republic](../publications/2fbcf6a4ac24671b8d90.md)

Michal Straka; Andrea Zapriháčová; Emil Janeček; Jaroslav Šťastný; Jiřı́ Hájek

We report the occurrence of the predaceous diving beetle Hydroglyphus hamulatus \(Gyllenhal, 1813\) in the Czech Republic\. Specimens were collected between 2021 and 2024 at post\-mining lakes Most and Milada, with an additional record from 1986\. These data raise the number of Czech diving beetles to 127 confirmed and eight questionably present species\. The new records likely reflect a recent European migration wave and highlight the conservation value of post\-mining lakes, a habitat resembling northern European oligotrophic lakes that are rare in Central Europe\.

## [Keterkaitan antara Hambatan Adaptasi Dengan Homesickness Pada Mahasiswa Rantau Dari Luar Pulau Jawa di Universitas Islam Sultan Agung Semarang](../publications/2fc402d1c5b63caf8951.md)

Kaori Latifah; Laily Rahmah

Mahasiswa rantau dari luar Pulau Jawa kerap menghadapi hambatan adaptasi di lingkungan baru yang dapat berpotensi memunculkan homesickness sebagai bentuk tekanan psikologis dan memengaruhi proses penyesuaian diri dan kesejahteraan psikologis mahasiswa\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui keterkaitan antara hambatan adaptasi dengan homesickness pada mahasiswa rantau dari luar Pulau Jawa di Universitas Islam Sultan Agung Semarang\. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling\. Subjek penelitian merupakan mahasiswa aktif Universitas Islam Sultan Agung Semarang yang berasal dari luar Pulau Jawa\. Metode pengumpulan data menggunakan dua skala psikologi, yaitu skala homesickness dengan koefisien reliabilitas sebesar 0,929 serta skala hambatan adaptasi dengan koefisien reliabilitas sebesar 0,876\. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan teknik Pearson Correlation\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terdapat hubungan positif antara hambatan adaptasi dengan homesickness pada mahasiswa rantau luar Pulau Jawa dengan nilai korelasi sebesar R = 0,649 dan nilai F hitung = 28,106 dengan signifikansi p &lt; 0,05\. Dengan demikian, hambatan adaptasi memiliki peranan penting terhadap munculnya homesickness pada mahasiswa rantau dari luar Pulau Jawa di Universitas Islam Sultan Agung Semarang\.

## [A Model for Descriptive Answers Evaluation Using Word2Vec Neural Network Architecture](../publications/2fd6188a7eede2beca7c.md)

Ekanem Bassey Asuquo; Irikefe Eti Friday; Nwanze Ezeamaka David

The increasing popularity and acceptance of CBE \(Computer\-based Examination\) systems by examination bodies and institutions of learning globally for evaluation of multi\-choice answers have unveiled the need for similar systems for descriptive answers evaluation\. In this study, Word2Vec Neural Network architecture, specifically CBOW \(Continuous Bag\-of\-Words\) was used to build an ML model for descriptive answers evaluation\. The corpus for training the model were of two categories namely: model answers to exam questions and answers by examinees\. Five hundred and twenty five \(525\) instances of answers from 105 examinees in 5 questions from the course, Introduction to computing were used\. 80% of the dataset were used for model training while 20% was for the validation process\. Also, answers from examinees were manually graded by three experts in the area and used to compare and evaluate the model performances in two instances of 40% and 50% as pass marks\. In the case of 40% pass mark, F1 scores of 0\.92 for Class 1 \(i\.e\. pass class\) and 0\.91 for Class 0 \(fail class\) were obtained which reflect a strong, balanced ability to identify actual cases \(high recall\) and avoid false alarms \(high precision\) for both classes\. With respect to 50% pass mark, F1 scores of 0\.82 and 1\.0 were obtained for failed and pass classes respectively indicating that the model is slightly better at identifying and classifying instances of pass class compared to fail class\. The model overall accuracy of 0\.9 shows its potentials to correctly evaluate descriptive answers\.

## [Enhancing Electric Vehicle Battery Management Efficiency: Integrated Thermal Control, State Estimation, and Cell Balancing](../publications/2fe8f5dbfe57a513e647.md)

Ghongade Prashant

Electric vehicle \(EV\) battery management systems \(BMS\) critically influence range, safety, and lifecycle cost through their impact on thermal regulation, state estimation accuracy, and cell balancing efficiency\. This paper presents an integrated framework for improving BMS efficiency by co\-optimizing battery thermal management strategies, advanced state\-of\-charge \(SoC\) and state\-of\-health \(SoH\) estimation algorithms, and adaptive cell balancing techniques\. We review recent advances in liquid, hybrid, and AI\-enabled thermal management; evaluate machine learning–enhanced SoC/SoH estimators against conventional observers; and propose a hierarchical control architecture that minimizes auxiliary energy consumption while maintaining cells within optimal operating windows\. Simulation and experimental benchmarks indicate that integrated strategies can reduce thermal management energy use by 6–9%, improve SoC estimation RMSE to below 1\.5%, and enhance pack\-level energy throughput by up to 8% over rule\-based baselines\. The findings provide actionable design guidelines for next\-generation efficient BMS in EVs\.

## [Exploring Patients&\#x27; Care Needs in Digital Free‐Text Messages During Cancer Treatment: Qualitative Analysis Guided by the Fundamentals of Care Framework](../publications/2fec39afd5cb042a4286.md)

Marie\-Therése Crafoord; Maria Fjell; Tina Gustavell

AIM: To describe the content of patients&\#x27; free\-text messages submitted within a digital symptom\-monitoring system during cancer treatment, and to explore how these messages reflect relational, integrated, and contextual care needs as conceptualised in the Fundamentals of Care Framework, and to generate implications for the future development of digitally mediated cancer care\. DESIGN: Exploratory qualitative study using inductive and deductive content analysis\. METHOD: Free\-text messages \(n = 2097\) from 180 patients receiving treatment for breast, prostate, or pancreatic cancer were analysed\. These messages were collected between 2013 and 2017 within three clinical trials, in which intervention\-group participants used a symptom\-reporting app and could submit free\-text messages alongside their reports\. Summative counts and inductive qualitative content analysis were conducted first, followed by a deductive interpretation using the Fundamentals of Care Framework to examine how communication reflected relational, integrated, and contextual care needs\. RESULTS: Three interconnected categories were identified: navigating uncertainty and taking an active role, reassurance and confirmation, and going beyond predefined symptom ratings\. These formed the overarching theme of expressing experiences and negotiating shared care\. Patients used free\-text messages to seek clarification, describe symptoms and contextual factors, articulate self\-care efforts, set boundaries for communication, and maintain relational continuity with nurses\. Deductive interpretation suggested that patients actively contributed to sustaining therapeutic relationships, integrating symptoms with everyday life experiences, and managing substantial self\-care responsibilities\. CONCLUSION: Free\-text communication enabled patients to articulate needs not captured in structured symptom questionnaires, supporting more person\-centred and contextually informed assessment\. Implications for the profession and patient care: Future digitally mediated cancer care should not only monitor symptoms but also support relational continuity, preserve integrated patient narratives, and facilitate collaborative sense\-making around self\-care and symptom management\. WHAT PROBLEM DID THE STUDY ADDRESS?: Structured questionnaires do not fully capture patients&\#x27; experiences or care needs or the relational and contextual dimensions of care during cancer treatment\. WHAT WERE THE MAIN FINDINGS?: Patients used free\-text messages to negotiate shared care, contextualise symptoms, maintain relational contact with nurses, and support self\-care decision\-making during cancer treatment\. IMPACT: Findings inform the future development of digitally mediated cancer care by highlighting the importance of supporting patients&\#x27; relational work, preserving integrated patient narratives, and enabling collaborative sense\-making around self\-care\. NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC INVOLVEMENT: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting\. REPORTING METHOD: The Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research \(SRQR\)\. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials\.gov identifier: NCT02479607; NCT02477137\.

## [Epistemic Possibility and Textual Source Voice in AI Technology Journalism: A Corpus\-Assisted Case Study of May, Might, Could, and Likely, 2022–2026](../publications/2ff3264ce9a3c7f55107.md)

Asjad Balla

AI journalism often couples statements about current technical capability with predictions whose realization is uncertain\. This exploratory, corpus\-assisted case study investigates may, might, could and likely in 20 criterion\-based TechCrunch AI articles, chosen as two eligible articles from two fixed 14\-day windows each year, 2022–2026\. On October 4, 2026 a script was executed to audit the captured canonical pages, raw html, cleaned editorial text and verification logs\. Case\-insensitive, whole\-word searches in headlines and editorial bodies yielded 40 target tokens\. Was was the most frequent form \(n = 16, 40\.0%\) and occurred in nine articles, but only 7 of the 16 occurrences \(43\.8%\) were epistemic; the other nine were capacity or affordance\. Epistemicity was found in 10 of the 12 may tokens \(83\.3%\) and all the might and likely tokens\. Of these, 29 \(72\.5 %\) were epistemic\. One watermarking article in 2023 accounted for 8 of the 40 tokens, so removing it dropped the proportion of all target tokens in 2023 from 22\.5% to 3\.1%\. Two blinded machine\-assisted coding passes agreed on 35 of 40 semantic codes \(87\.5%; κ = \.679\)\. This is an algorithmic audit diagnostic, not human inter\-rater reliability\. The findings are descriptive, entirely auditable, and limited to this small, purposively bounded corpus Keywords: epistemic modality, uncertainty, artificial intelligence, technology journalism, corpus\-assisted discourse studies,modal verbs, source attribution

## [Harnessing large\-scale genomics\-based screening for the identification of expansin genes responsive to abiotic stress in Peucedanum praeruptorum](../publications/2ff36d4b0fdc584d4450.md)

Canguang He; Modan Qi; Xueru Li; Jun Dai; Cheng Song

Introduction Expansins are crucial for cell wall relaxation and significantly impact plant growth and development\. However, the expansin gene family in Peucedanum praeruptorum remains to be systematically characterized\. Methods Here, we systematically identified expansin genes in P\. praeruptorum and analysed their molecular characteristics, evolutionary patterns, and expression profiles in response to methyl jasmonate \(MeJA\)\. Subcellular localization prediction, gene structure analysis, chromosomal localization, collinearity analysis, and cis\-acting element analysis were performed\. Based on cis\-element screening, PpdEXPA01, PpdEXPA10, PpdEXPA13, PpdEXPB1, and PpdEXPB2 were selected to validate their expression under exogenous MeJA stress\. Results A total of 39 PpdEXP genes were identified and classified into four subfamilies: EXPA \(24 genes\), EXPB \(9 genes\), EXPLA \(2 genes\), and EXPLB \(4 genes\)\. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that all members are localized in the cell wall, and all expansin proteins are hydrophilic\. Gene structural analysis showed that the number of introns ranged from one to four and that all genes contained two conserved domains: DPBB\_EXPA\_N and Expansin\_C\. Chromosomal localization analysis showed that the 39 PpdEXP genes were distributed across 11 chromosomes, with tandem duplication events occurring on chromosomes 3, 4, and 7\. Collinearity analysis indicated that segmental and whole\-genome duplication were the main driving forces behind the expansion of the expansin gene family\. Analysis of cis\-acting elements revealed 1,237 elements in total, which were primarily classified into three categories: hormone response, light response, and stress response\. Expression profiling revealed that PpdEXP genes exhibit significant tissue specificity\. The five selected genes had significant tissue\- and time\-specific expression patterns in roots, stems, and leaves under exogenous MeJA stress\. Discussion This study systematically elucidated the molecular basis and expression regulation patterns of the P\. praeruptorum expansin family, providing a foundation for further functional characterization of PpdEXP genes and their potential roles in growth, development, and stress responses\.

## [Amygdala neurofeedback as an adjunct to residential dialectical behavior therapy for borderline personality disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial](../publications/2ffb723ce49bfc396f85.md)

Miroslava Jindrová; Philip Santangelo; Nikolaus Kleindienst; Christian G\. Schmahl; Christian Paret

BACKGROUND: Borderline personality disorder \(BPD\) is characterized by affective instability and amygdala hyperreactivity\. Although dialectical behavior therapy \(DBT\) reduces symptoms and amygdala\-related abnormalities, many patients show only partial remission\. Real\-time functional magnetic resonance imaging \(fMRI\) amygdala neurofeedback \(amy\-NF\) directly targets hyperactive limbic responses and has shown promise in uncontrolled trials\. We examined whether amy\-NF adds benefit to inpatient DBT\. METHODS: Thirty\-six mid\-therapy people with BPD and clinically significant residual symptoms \(BSL\-23 &gt; 1\.5\) were randomized to DBT plus amy\-NF \(n = 23\) or DBT alone, termed treatment as usual \(TAU = 13\)\. Post\-treatment assessments were completed by 15/9 \(amy\-NF/TAU\), with 15/8 and 12/7 completing the 3\- and 6\-month follow\-ups\. Ecological momentary assessment \(EMA\) of daily\-life affective instability served as the primary outcome\. Secondary outcomes included self\-reports, amygdala responses during two fMRI tasks, and resting\-state fMRI\. Assessments occurred at pre\-, post\-, 3\-, and 6\-month follow\-up\. RESULTS: Participants successfully downregulated amygdala activity during neurofeedback\. EMA showed improvements in negative affect, inner tension, and affective instability over time, without consistent superiority of amy\-NF\. Self\-reports likewise showed no additional benefit of amy\-NF, and BSL\-23 scores increased after discharge in both groups\. Amy\-NF was associated with transient pre\-post reductions in amygdala activity during both viewing and regulation in the emotion regulation task, and with more stable amygdala reactivity over time than TAU in the faces task\. Resting\-state analyses showed transient pre\-post increases in amygdala connectivity with precuneus and dorsomedial frontal regions in amy\-NF\. CONCLUSIONS: Amygdala neurofeedback is feasible and reduced amygdala activity in BPD, but did not yield additional clinical benefit when delivered alongside intensive residential DBT, although the small sample may have limited power to detect such effects\. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was preregistered 2020/03/26 on ClinicalTrials\.gov and received the ID NCT04333888\.

## [Asymptotic mixed graph convolutional with trend\-aware self\-attention networks for traffic flow forecasting](../publications/2fffa8ef4cb8a91d0d61.md)

Hongyan Wang

Accurate traffic flow forecasting plays a critical role in enhancing the efficiency and safety of transportation systems\. Nevertheless, this task remains challenging due to the complex spatio\-temporal correlations embedded in traffic data\. Existing adaptive\-graph\-based methods usually learn graph structures during training, making them insufficiently responsive to testing\-phase traffic states\. Consequently, their forecasting performance may deteriorate under unexpected fluctuations and irregular traffic variations\. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a novel Asymptotic Mixed Graph Convolutional with Trend\-Aware Self\-Attention Network \(AMG\-TSA\)\. By learning trend similarities among traffic nodes, AMG\-TSA constructs an asymptotic adjacency matrix to support both asymptotic structure\-aware graph convolution and asymptotic dynamic graph convolution, enabling synchronized modeling of dynamic spatial dependencies\. Meanwhile, a trend\-aware self\-attention module is introduced to capture local contextual patterns and nonlinear temporal dependencies, while dilated causal convolution enlarges the temporal receptive field and supports long\-range temporal dependency modeling\. Experiments on two real\-world traffic datasets show that AMG\-TSA consistently outperforms representative baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness in traffic flow forecasting\.

## [NestedVLA: Learning to Consolidate and Generate Skills for Vision\-Language\-Action Models](../publications/300119a8a5f89aba9477.md)

Guodong Du; Wanyu Lin

Vision\-\-Language\-\-Action \(VLA\) models promise generalist robotic agents, yet consolidating skills learned across heterogeneous tasks and environments remains difficult: training data is fragmented across platforms, joint multi\-task training suffers from interference, and model merging tends to introduce parameter conflicts or require architectural changes\. We instead advocate a paradigm in which skills are first learned independently and then consolidated post hoc\. To this end, we propose NestedVLA, which replaces parameter aggregation with parameter generation: a nested hypernetwork, conditioned on the target task, synthesizes task\-adaptive action\-expert parameters that compose with a frozen base VLA\. Task\-specific compressed VLM residuals are retained separately\. This formulation enables flexible task\-conditioned skill reuse while mitigating interference\. Across three RL benchmarks \(MetaWorld, ManiSkill, CALVIN\), NestedVLA outperforms the strongest model\-merging baseline by 41 pp on average, matches per\-task fine\-tuning within 1 pp on ManiSkill, and substantially closes the gap on CALVIN, pointing toward a storage\-efficient route to skill consolidation\. Code is available at https://github\.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026\-NestedVLA\.

## [The Weight of Tomorrow: Future Anxiety as a Mediator Between Self\-Efficacy and Depression Among Final\-Year University Students](../publications/300c2e1bc15d702f8eb7.md)

Tazkiya Saidah; Onny Fransinata Anggara

As graduation approaches, senior students face academic pressure and uncertainty about the future, which increases their vulnerability to anxiety and symptoms of depression\. This study aims to examine the mediating role of future anxiety in the relationship between self\-efficacy and symptoms of depression among senior undergraduate students\. This quantitative study included 302 final\-year students from University X, who were sampled purposively\. The data were gathered by utilizing the General Self\-Efficacy Scale \(GSES\), the Dark Future Anxiety Scale \(DFAS\), and the Patient Health Questionnaire\-9 \(PHQ\-9\)\. Analysis of mediation was conducted using the medmod module in Jamovi\. The outcomes confirmed that future anxiety significantly mediates the relationship between self\-efficacy and depressive symptoms \(indirect effect: β = \-0\.121, p = 0\.005, 95% CI \[\-0\.029, \-0\.044\]\)\. These current findings highlight that future anxiety functions as a key psychological mechanism linking higher self\-efficacy to lower depressive symptoms\. These findings also emphasize the importance of interventions that strengthen self\-efficacy while reducing future anxiety to promote psychological well\-being among senior college students\.

## [Automating carbon risk assessment of residential buildings using scalable energy and emissions data in city information models](../publications/30203d84b289fbd2d00b.md)

Peter Oluwadamilola Akinde; Nils Seifert; Matthias Hümmer

The residential building sector accounts for approximately 17\-20% of global CO₂ emissions, making it a critical target for decarbonization efforts aligned with the Paris Agreement&\#x27;s 1\.5°C warming limit\. This study presents an automated framework for carbon risk assessment that integrates scalable energy and emissions data into City Information Models \(CIMs\), addressing the limitations of manual assessment tools that require extensive data input and lack scalability\. The framework leverages TABULA building archetypes and power law scaling \(optimal exponent b=0\.85\) to extrapolate energy demand and CO₂ emissions from minimal input data such as building geometry, address, heating system, and renovation status, thereby enriching CIMs with dynamic sustainability metrics\. Validation using 10 Bavarian residential buildings demonstrated robust predictive accuracy, with energy demand predictions achieving a Normalized Mean Bias Error \(NMBE\) of 4\.77% and CO₂ emissions an NMBE of 4\.17%, both within ASHRAE Guideline 14 thresholds \(±5%\)\. Strong correlations were observed \(Pearson&\#x27;s r=0\.825 for energy, 0\.774 for CO₂\), though stranding year predictions under the CRREM 1\.5°C energy reduction pathway showed deviations of up to four years, reflecting limitations from static decarbonization assumptions\. This also highlights the framework’s intended use as a portfolio\-scale screening tool for relative transition risk, rather than as a deterministic predictor of asset\-level compliance dates\. The framework quantifies excess carbon costs using EU ETS price trajectories, offering policymakers a scalable tool for prioritizing retrofits and mitigating stranded asset risks\. Future enhancements should integrate dynamic grid decarbonization, machine learning for occupancy modeling, and expanded validation across diverse climatic contexts to strengthen applicability for global sustainability initiatives\.

## [Digitally Mediated Thesis Writing Among ELT Undergraduates: Strategic Patterns of Multi\-Tool Integration Across Writing Stages](../publications/302114074a1cf152dead.md)

Sheila Agustina; Fika Megawati; Sandrina Bilqis; Nurkamilah Nurkamilah

The increasing integration of digital tools into academic writing has transformed how students compose, revise, and conceptualize scholarly work\. Existing research has examined artificial intelligence and writing support technologies in general classroom contexts, but limited attention has been paid to how undergraduate students employ these tools in high\-stakes academic tasks such as thesis writing\. This gap is particularly significant in English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) settings, where linguistic and rhetorical demands are intensified\. Accordingly, this study investigates how Indonesian undergraduate ELT students integrate digital tools into their thesis writing\. It focuses on the types of tools used, the stages of writing they support, students’ motivations, and patterns of integration\. Using a qualitative case study design, data were collected from 38 students through open\-ended questionnaires and analyzed thematically\. The findings reveal that students engage with a range of generative, translation, and language\-refinement tools across multiple stages of thesis writing, particularly during editing, literature review, and discussion development\. An iterative draft–consult–revise cycle also emerged as a central integration pattern\. It indicates that students maintain agency while coordinating digital mediation\. The study concludes that digitally mediated thesis writing reflects emerging forms of academic literacy, which underscore the need for structured digital literacy guidance within ELT writing pedagogy\.

## [From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology](../publications/30270b94efe2d051b805.md)

Letong Huang; Hongqin Sun; Yi Huang; Qingyi Gu; Hailong Zhang; Dingqin He; Wenyi Zhang; Siyu Chen; Delin Xu; Juanjuan Zhao

Two paradigms now drive the life sciences\. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence\. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis\-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high\-dimensional datasets of modern biology\. Each has delivered major advances on its own\. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry\. In this review we propose a three\-part taxonomy of integration strategies, namely AI\-accelerated mechanistic modeling, mechanism\-informed AI, and hybrid models spanning one\-directional sequential coupling and bidirectional iterative systems, and we survey their applications in systems and synthetic biology, pharmacology and drug discovery, epidemiology, and neuroscience\. We then examine seven challenges that stand in the way: interpretability, data sparsity, causality, identifiability, computational scale, multimodal integration, and validation and generalization, and we close with a view of biological digital twins, causal discovery engines, and automated science\. Our argument is that combining these approaches is the principal task for a new generation of interdisciplinary scientists who aim to build a predictive and mechanistic science of life\.

## [Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs](../publications/30298f0e3455b5352308.md)

Yang Ni

Learning causal structure from data requires assumptions about mechanisms, noises, observation schemes, and interventions\. Historically, causal discovery has relied primarily on conditional independence\. This review focuses on modern causal discovery methods that exploit properties of distributions beyond conditional independence\. Our organizing principle separates the source of identification from the statistical estimator and its computational implementation\. This perspective connects conditional\-independence methods with distributional asymmetries, conditional\-moment restrictions, and variation across environments or individuals\. We examine discovery under latent confounding and feedback, distinguishing causal information about observed variables from reconstruction of latent structure and emphasizing the additional semantics required by cyclic models\. We also distinguish population identification, frequentist and Bayesian consistency, uncertainty quantification, and algorithmic guarantees\. Throughout, examples show why the same observational distribution can support different conclusions under different model classes\. We conclude with guidance for comparing methods at their identifiable targets and a research agenda for uncertainty, heterogeneous populations, non\-scalar variables, and the intersection of discrete data, feedback, and hidden confounding\.

## [AI\-Driven Supply Chain Transformation in Bangladesh: An Integrated Multitech Approach and Empirical Evaluation of Readiness to Adopt](../publications/302b7c26057d725a2a62.md)

Tahmid Hossain

Abstract Bangladesh&\#x27;s industrial supply chains are spanning Ready\-Made Garments, pharmaceuticals, FMCG, logistics sectors continue to be hampered by structural bottlenecks, information asymmetry, and siloed operations, even as global markets shift toward Industry 4\.0/5\.0 digital integration\. While individual technologies such as Generative AI, blockchain, IoT, predictive analytics, and robotics have been studied separately, few frameworks integrate them into a single operational architecture, and no prior South Asian study has empirically compared adoption readiness across university students, academic faculty, and industry professionals\. This study addresses that gap using a cross\-sectional survey of 257 respondents, analyzed through the lens of the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) and Resource\-Based View \(RBV\)\. Results show high Perceived Usefulness \(cost reduction, M=3\.96; risk reduction, M=3\.79\) and strong Individual Readiness \(M=3\.99\), positively correlated with usefulness \(r=\.665, p&lt;\.001\)\. However, Organizational Readiness was markedly lower \(M=3\.26\), driven by talent shortages \(44\.4%\) and capital constraints \(36\.6%\) \- revealing an &quot;Awareness\-Execution Paradox&quot; between individual enthusiasm and institutional capacity\. Chi\-square tests confirmed significant perception gaps between professionals and students on local AI awareness \(p&lt;\.001\) and integration ease \(p=\.049\)\. The study proposes a five\-layer Unified Multitech Smart Supply Chain Framework and offers practical implications for academia, industry, and policymakers seeking to accelerate digital supply chain transformation in Bangladesh\.

## [IMPROVING THE CREDIT POLICY OF THE BANKING SECTOR OF THE REPUBLIC OF TAJIKISTAN IN THE CONTEXT OF FINANCIAL MARKET DIGITALIZATION](../publications/302cb39136a2f9bb8e22.md)

Joziba Abdulloeva

This article examines the current directions for improving the credit policy of the banking sector of the Republic of Tajikistan in the context of financial market digitalization\. The study analyzes the theoretical and methodological foundations of credit policy formation and explores its transformation under the influence of digital technologies\. Based on statistical data for 2024\-2025, the current state of bank lending in Tajikistan is assessed and the main challenges affecting the efficiency of credit policy are identified, including insufficient diversification of the loan portfolio, a limited level of digitalization of lending processes and persistent credit risks\. The paper proposes key directions for improving credit policy through the implementation of a risk\-oriented digital lending model, wider application of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data technologies, the development of an integrated digital information infrastructure and the enhancement of credit risk management mechanisms\. The findings of the study may be used by commercial banks and banking regulators in developing measures aimed at improving the efficiency and sustainability of the banking sector under conditions of financial market digitalization\.

## [Integrating deep learning signature from 2D spinal radiographs with clinical features: a machine learning model to predict structural spinal damage progression in axial spondyloarthritis](../publications/302d0c2fc3e729cc86f2.md)

Hexin Feng; Qingqing Zhao; Yang Zhao; Zhichang Liu; Wei Zhou; Shinong Pan

Abstract Background To develop a machine learning model that integrates a two\-dimensional deep learning \(DL2D\) signature derived from spinal radiographs with clinical features to predict the progression of structural spinal damage in axial spondyloarthritis \(axSpA\)\. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 277 axSpA patients from two centers and collected clinical and spinal radiograph data\. Clinical features were first screened using univariate regression followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\) regression\. Deep learning models were built on spinal radiographs using three architectures; the optimal model was selected to extract the DL2D signature, which was then integrated with clinical features to train support vector machine \(SVM\) and random forest \(RF\) models for predicting cervical and lumbar Modified Stoke Ankylosing Spondylitis Spinal Score \(mSASSS\) progression\. Model performance was assessed using mean squared error \(MSE\), mean absolute percentage error \(MAPE\), bias, coefficient of determination \(R²\), and Pearson correlation to assess linear agreement\. Subgroup analyses were conducted by follow‑up intervals\. Results Univariate analysis yielded 14 and 18 significant clinical features in the cervical and lumbar datasets, reduced to 9 and 10 by LASSO regression, respectively\. DenseNet121 was chosen for DL2D signature extraction due to its superior validation performance \(MSE: 0\.694 for cervical, 0\.663 for lumbar; MAPE: 0\.779 and 0\.742\)\. The combined model integrating the DL2D signature with clinical features consistently outperformed single‑modal models\. The RF‑based combined model showed strong generalization, with validation/test MSEs of 0\.539/0\.405 \(cervical\) and 0\.411/0\.293 \(lumbar\), MAPEs of 0\.540/0\.390 and 0\.438/0\.390, as well as higher R², stronger Pearson correlations, and lower bias than the other models\. Subgroup analysis confirmed better prediction for 1–4 years than for ≥ 4 years follow‑ups\. Conclusions The random forest model integrating the DL2D signature with clinical features accurately predicts short\-term \(1–4 years\) structural spinal damage progression in axSpA, which may facilitate risk stratification and timely intervention\.

## [ЗАРУБІЖНИЙ ДОСВІД УДОСКОНАЛЕННЯ УПРАВЛІНСЬКИХ ПРИНЦИПІВ РЕАГУВАННЯ НА НАДЗВИЧАЙНІ СИТУАЦІЇ В УКРАЇНІ](../publications/302dc3e130b75011583e.md)

В\. Ф\. Загурська\-Антонюк

Статтю присвячено аналізу сучасного стану, системних проблем та перспектив модер\- нізації системи публічного управління у сфері цивільного захисту й реагування на надзвичайні ситуації\. У дослідженні узагальнено міжнародний досвід правового регулювання та інсти\- туційного забезпечення антикризового менеджменту на прикладі США \(FEMA\), Німеччини \(BBK\), Японії, Італії та Великої Британії, а також окреслено трансформаційно\-інноваційні підходи країн ЄС та ООН \(зокрема застосування GIS, AI, систем раннього попередження та єдиних комунікаційних центрів\)\. На основі аналітичних даних критично оцінено ефективність функціонування сил цивіль\- ного захисту в Україні\. Виявлено ключові недоліки вітчизняної системи, зокрема: слабку між\- відомчу координацію, фрагментарність взаємодії, затримки у розгортанні органів управління \(комісій, штабів НС\) та надходженні інформації, низький рівень матеріально\-технічного забезпечення, а також відсутність чіткої моноцентричної ієрархії при ліквідації велико\- масштабних катастроф техногенного та природного характеру\. Окрему увагу приділено кадровому дефіциту та відсутності чітких кваліфікаційних вимог до керівників ліквідації НС і персоналу штабів\. Доведено, що в умовах реальних загроз функції управління фактично зміщуються на опе\- ративні сили ДСНС, що нівелює принципи гнучкості й стійкості системи\. Обґрунтовано рекомендації щодо законодавчого регулювання сфери, які передбачають: інституціоналізацію професійних менеджерів державного рівня з ліквідації НС із визначенням їхнього кваліфікацій\- ного коду; створення постійного штату таких службовців у профільному міністерстві для ліквідації криз регіонального та державного масштабів; законодавче унормування діяльності штабу з ліквідації НС як постійно діючого органу із широким застосуванням мобільних \(пере\- сувних\) пунктів управління\. За результатами дослідження запропоновано комплекс заходів державного регулювання та законодавчих змін\. Обґрунтовано необхідність формування інституту професійних мене\- джерів державного рівня з ліквідації НС із введенням відповідного коду професії, створення постійного штату таких фахівців у структурі ДСНС України, а також законодавчого унорму\- вання діяльності штабу з ліквідації НС як постійно діючого органу із впровадженням сучасних пересувних пунктів управління\.

## [Ứng dụng MaxEnt và SoilGrids trong định hướng bảo tồn tại chỗ loài Thất diệp nhất chi hoa ở tỉnh Điện Biên, Việt Nam](../publications/3034738743e75a841ee9.md)

Ngô Thị Linh; Lê Anh Thanh; Nguyễn Thị Hương Ly; Nguyễn Hồng Hải

Thất diệp nhất chi hoa hay Bảy lá một hoa \(Paris polyphylla hoặc Paris xichouensis hoặc Paris vietnamensis\) là loài thực vật có giá trị dược liệu quý đang nguy cấp do khai thác quá mức và suy thoái sinh cảnh\. Nghiên cứu nhằm lượng hóa yêu cầu sinh thái thổ nhưỡng và lập bản đồ sinh cảnh tiềm năng của loài tại tỉnh Điện Biên, Việt Nam\. Mô hình MaxEnt được tích hợp với dữ liệu thổ nhưỡng SoilGrids \(độ phân giải 250 m\)\. Dựa trên 40 điểm ghi nhận loài và 8 biến đặc điểm lý hóa lớp đất mặt \(0–15 cm\), mô hình dự báo với độ tin cậy rất cao \(AUC huấn luyện = 0,937; kiểm tra = 0,915\)\. Kết quả cho thấy phân bố của loài chịu chi phối mạnh bởi hàm lượng Nitơ tổng số \(25,1%\), tỷ lệ hạt sét \(16,1%\), dung trọng đất \(12,9%\) và pH \(11,0%\)\. Điều này phản ánh đặc tính sinh thái đặc thù của loài là sinh trưởng tốt trên đất giàu dinh dưỡng, tơi xốp, thoát nước tốt và tính axit nhẹ\. Về không gian, sinh cảnh phù hợp chỉ chiếm khoảng 10% diện tích toàn tỉnh \(962 km²\), phân mảnh hẹp, biệt lập trên địa hình núi dốc thuộc các xã Mường Tùng, Na Sang, Sín Thầu, Nậm Nèn và Mường Pồn\. Nhìn chung, việc tích hợp MaxEnt và SoilGrids thể hiện hiệu quả cao trong đánh giá sinh cảnh tiềm năng của loài, cung cấp cơ sở dữ liệu thiết yếu để hoạch định bảo tồn tại chỗ và phát triển canh tác dưới tán rừng\.

## [Advanced machine learning for predictive 2D and 3D abrasion modeling in sediment bypass tunnels](../publications/30354dc6177e6ebe3d8b.md)

Ahmed Emara; Sameh Kantoush; Mohamed Saber; Tetsuya Sumi; Emad Mabrouk

Sediment bypass tunnels \(SBTs\) are widely used to alleviate reservoir sedimentation; however, they are susceptible to hydro\-abrasive erosion, which can compromise their longevity\. Predicting spatial abrasion is challenging due to the complexity of flow–sediment interactions and the scarcity of data\. In this work, we synthesize recent advances in using machine learning \(ML\), specifically the XGBoost algorithm, to map abrasion patterns on SBT floors in both two\-dimensional \(surface damage/no damage\) and three\-dimensional \(damage depth\) contexts\. Utilizing high\-resolution laser\-scan data from the Koshibu SBT in Japan, we extract geometric \(e\.g\., distances along the tunnel and curvature\) and hydraulic \(e\.g\., flow velocity, discharge\) features for each surface point\. For 2D mapping, points were classified as “abraded” or “not abraded” based on a 2 cm depth threshold; for 3D mapping, the actual damage depth was predicted\. XGBoost was trained on 50% of the approximately 1\.16\-million\-point dataset and tested on the remainder\. The 2D classification model achieved an overall accuracy of 86\.4% \(with a sensitivity of 91\.9% and a specificity of 89\.6%\), successfully identifying four characteristic abrasion patterns in both straight and curved sections\. The 3D regression model achieved a correlation coefficient R of 0\.861 and Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency of 0\.748 between the predicted and measured depths \(exceeding 0\.90 and 0\.85 in some sections\)\. These results demonstrate that ML models can effectively capture complex abrasion behavior, though small\-scale “wave\-like” damage patterns remain challenging\. This integrated approach highlights the promise of modern ML techniques for predictive tunnel maintenance and sediment management in hydropower infrastructure\.

## [Mapping University Students Risk of Dependence on Generative Artificial Intelligence Using K\-Means Clustering](../publications/304224ecd72a10a479a6.md)

Hafiz Fadhillah; Taufiq Taufiq

The growing use of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) in higher education has changed how university students approach academic tasks\. Although these tools can support learning and improve efficiency, frequent reliance on them raises concerns about students&\#x27; ability to study and solve problems independently\. This study aims to identify patterns of GenAI use among university students and explore potential indicators of dependence through K\-Means clustering\. An exploratory quantitative approach was adopted, using questionnaire responses collected through 15 items measured on a five\-point Likert scale\. Of the 106 responses received, 104 met the inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis\. The data underwent screening, numerical encoding, and reverse scoring before being grouped using the K\-Means algorithm\. The appropriate number of clusters was selected by comparing Silhouette Scores across solutions containing two to seven clusters\. The analysis identified three student groups, with a Silhouette Score of 0\.2443\. The first group comprised 30 students \(28\.85%\) who showed relatively higher GenAI use and stronger indications of behavioral dependence\. The second group included 11 students \(10\.58%\) who reported lower GenAI use but demonstrated limitations in academic independence and understanding\. The remaining 63 students \(60\.58%\) formed a group characterized by moderate GenAI use\. These findings suggest that frequency of use alone does not adequately reflect the risk of dependence\. However, the relatively low Silhouette Score indicates limited separation between groups, meaning that the resulting profiles should be interpreted as exploratory rather than definitive\.

## [Prior\-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network \(PISA\-Net\) for multi\-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel\-2 imagery](../publications/3043ac159d4c022e595b.md)

Lin Wu; Yihang Duan; Yu Zhang; Yabo Huang; Duojia Yang; Wenfu Wu; Ning Li

Accurate retrieval of water\-quality parameters from remote\-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges\. This study proposes a Prior\-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network \(PISA\-Net\) for multi\-parameter water\-quality retrieval from Sentinel\-2 imagery in Poyang Lake\. PISA\-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge\-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate\-derived geographic priors\. A geographic soft\-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature\-wise Linear Modulation \(FiLM\), while a stop gradient consistency loss \(SG\-CL\) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation\. Chl\-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5\-fold spatial\-block cross\-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine\-learning, and deep\-learning baselines\. PISA\-Net achieved R 2 values of 0\.6113, 0\.5112, and 0\.5054 for Chl\-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D\-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29\.6%, 21\.4%, and 19\.0%\. An additional April 2018 cross\-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero\-shot transfer, whereas few\-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross\-season adaptability after limited local calibration\. Overall, PISA\-Net provides a prior\-informed spectral–spatial framework for water\-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi\-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability\.

## [Noise\-robust fault diagnosis of elastic ring\-supported rolling bearings using multi\-scale dilated convolution and multi\-head self\-attention](../publications/3047d0b23bafe7e75a6f.md)

Dawei Gu; Jia Li; Zhuo Xu; Kai Sun; Juan Wen; Guang Zhang; Baisong Pan; Bangchun Wen

Elastic ring\-supported rolling bearings are critical components in high\-end rotating machinery such as aero\-engines and gas turbines\. However, the vibration responses of such bearings are often affected by complex transmission paths, elastic\-support\-induced dynamic coupling, and strong background noise, which makes weak fault feature extraction and reliable diagnosis difficult\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a noise\-robust fault diagnosis method termed the multi\-scale dilated convolution and multi\-head self\-attention convolutional neural network \(MSDA\-CNN\)\. In the proposed framework, Z\-score normalization and variational mode decomposition \(VMD\) are used to preprocess raw vibration signals and construct multi\-channel inputs that retain fault\-related components in different frequency bands\. A multi\-scale dilated convolution module with parallel branches is then employed to extract complementary local and long\-range temporal features under noisy conditions\. Finally, a multi\-head self\-attention \(MHSA\) layer is introduced to enhance global feature interaction and improve class\-discriminative representation learning\. Experiments on a self\-built rotor\-bearing fault diagnosis platform and the public Paderborn University bearing dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves average diagnostic accuracies of 99\.86% and 98\.52%, respectively\. Under different Gaussian noise levels, MSDA\-CNN consistently outperforms MLP, 1D\-CNN, WD\-CNN, and MCL\-DRL\.

## [Decoding molecular heterogeneity in lupus nephritis: integrating single\-cell and spatial multi\-omics for endotype\-driven precision therapeutics](../publications/305dd2c3bc0bf205bdf8.md)

Jun Zhou; Wei Xiao; Hui Jian

Lupus nephritis \(LN\) develops in 40–60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus \(SLE\) and remains the leading cause of renal morbidity and progression to end\-stage renal disease \(ESRD\)\. While the upstream immunological events initiating LN—including loss of self\-tolerance, pathogenic autoantibody production, glomerular immune complex deposition, and type I interferon \(IFN\) activation—are broadly shared, accumulating evidence demonstrates that these convergent triggers give rise to molecularly heterogeneous tissue injury programs at the renal level\. This fundamental divergence provides a mechanistic explanation for the inconsistent therapeutic responses observed with standardized immunosuppressive protocols\. Advances in single\-cell transcriptomics, spatial gene expression mapping, CITE\-seq, and cross\-platform multi\-omic integration have deconvolved this heterogeneity into at least five recognizable tissue\-level injury programs: \(i\) an IFN\-γ\-polarized macrophage–tubular epithelial cell co\-activation circuit, \(ii\) a Tfh–B cell ectopic germinal center pathway, \(iii\) a neutrophil extracellular trap \(NET\)\-driven inflammatory cascade, \(iv\) a podocyte\-autonomous injury program, and \(v\) a TREM2\+ macrophage\-orchestrated fibrotic program\. Concurrently, multiplexed urinary biomarker platforms are under development as non\-invasive surrogates for tissue\-level pathogenic activity\. This review synthesizes current understanding of disease mechanisms, molecular profiling evidence, biomarker candidates, and mechanism\-directed therapies corresponding to each tissue injury program\. We map existing and investigational agents—including anifrolumab, obinutuzumab, voclosporin, CAR\-T cell therapy, and complement inhibitors—to their mechanistic targets and delineate the design requirements for prospective biomarker\-stratified trials essential to validating molecularly guided treatment selection\.

## [AI as a mediating quasi\-stakeholder: rethinking coopetition in hotel marketing consortia](../publications/30635313d1db11303646.md)

Sofia Almeida

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping inter\-organisational relationships in tourism and hospitality, yet its role within coopetitive networks remains underexplored\. This research letter develops a conceptual framework that positions AI as a mediating quasi\-stakeholder, extending Stakeholder Theory \(ST\) through the integration of Coopetition Theory \(CT\) and Actor–Network Theory \(ANT\)\. Using hotel marketing consortia \(HMCs\) as an illustrative context, we argue that AI\-enabled decision\-support systems actively mediate visibility, resource allocation, coordination, and value distribution through algorithmic processes, thereby influencing the balance between cooperation and competition among independent hotels\. The paper advances four theoretical propositions linking AI mechanisms, algorithmic mediation, coopetition outcomes, and algorithmic governance\. In doing so, it contributes to the emerging literature on AI\-enabled inter\-organisational relationships by introducing a novel conceptualisation of AI that moves beyond its traditional role as a technological resource\. The study also highlights the importance of algorithmic governance, emphasising transparency, explainability, fairness, and accountability as key mechanisms for sustaining trust and equitable value distribution within digitally mediated hospitality ecosystems\. Finally, the proposed framework provides a foundation for future empirical research across tourism and hospitality contexts where AI increasingly mediates strategic interactions\.

## [Role of scalp threads as a therapeutic armamentarium in the management of androgenetic alopecia](../publications/3063caa86ddc38a152e1.md)

Vaishnavi R\. Batchu; Megha Chandrashekar; Madura Chandu; BS Chandrashekar

Objectives: Androgenetic alopecia \(AGA\) is the most frequently encountered entity in clinical practice\. However, its treatment options like topical minoxidil often reach a response plateau, and few of them are non\-responders, complicating management\. Oral antiandrogens are limited by their potential side effects\. As a result, there is an increasing demand for supplementary therapies to enhance hair density\. One such approach is the thread embedding technique \(TET\), which is gaining relevance in managing pattern hair loss due to its ability to promote connective tissue remodeling\. Material and Methods: This prospective cohort study evaluated 17 patients \(13 males and 4 females, aged 25–40 years\) diagnosed with AGA\. Patients with Norwood–Hamilton grades 2–5 and Ludwig grades 2–3 were enrolled\. Baseline trichoscopic analysis was conducted before TET, measuring hair density, thickness, and anagen\-to\-telogen ratio\. The treatment area was mapped in a grid pattern, and the number of threads was planned accordingly\. Under topical anesthesia, Mint Mono ™ threads \(29 G, 30 mm or 30 G, 25 mm\) were inserted into the dermis\. Global photographs were taken before treatment and at 3 months\. 10 dermatologists assessed these images using a 7\-point scale \(from −3 = greatly decreased to \+3 = greatly increased\)\. Results: On average, 93% of patients showed overall improvement, with 38% rated as slight, 42% as moderate, and 12\.9% as great improvement\. The mean Visual Analog Scale score at 3 months was 6\.4 out of 10\. Reported side effects were minimal, including intraoperative pain \(2 patients\), post\-procedure itching \(1 patient\), and thread extrusion \(1 patient\)\. Conclusion: This study highlights the potential of TET as an effective and safe adjunctive treatment for pattern hair loss, particularly for patients unresponsive to conventional therapies\.

## [Examining child stress response, parenting and relationship\-related changes associated with a dyadic mindfulness and self\-compassion program](../publications/30769519bebc50b32fc0.md)

Christine Lathren; Jessica L\. Borelli; Rosemary Ellsworth; Elondra D\. Harr; Samantha DiMaio; Jamie Lynn Tatera; Veronica Diaz; Karen Bluth; Ryan J\. Herringa; Sara A\. Heyn

Introduction Interventions that dyadically equip families with self\-compassion skills represent a promising approach for addressing mental health challenges, particularly during the key transitional period of middle childhood\. This study examines changes and candidate processes associated with participation in the Mindfulness and Self\-Compassion for Children and Caregivers \(MSC\-CC\) course\. Methods Twenty\-three caregiver\-child dyads \(Child, M age =8\.78; Caregiver, M age =41\.2\) participated in MSC\-CC, delivered remotely over six weekly group sessions\. Pre\- and post\-intervention assessments included self\-report measures of parenting and relational closeness outcomes during a dyadic stressor task \(behavior, reflective functioning\[RF\], and physiology\)\. Analyses investigated pre\-post change in primary outcomes and linear mixed\-effects models estimated time\-related changes and baseline moderators of physiological change\. Significance tests identify pre\-post increases in parenting and emotion\-supportive beliefs\. Results and Discussion Physiologically, we detected significant decreases in child physiological arousal\. Exploratory moderation analyses suggest, among others, low levels of mindfulness and high RF at baseline predict the largest reductions in child stress physiology\. While uncontrolled, the MSC\-CC participation was associated with increases in mindful parenting and the caregiver\-child relationship and lower child physiological arousal during a dyadic challenge, most prominently in families with lower emotion\-supportive beliefs at baseline\. Altogether, this highlights candidate processes and moderators of efficacy to be confirmed in a fully powered randomized controlled trial\. Trial registration ClinicalTrials\.gov , Self\-Compassion for Children and Caregivers \(SCCC\) , NCT05818397, registration and study start on 2023\-10\-16\.

## [A Proposed Integrated Multi\-Signal Framework for Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Model\-Generated Text](../publications/307ad0457b7ebf725d2f.md)

Komal

The Large Language Model \(LLMs\) have proven to be extremely powerful in generating high\-quality fluent and informative responses to a wide range of prompts\. The main issue with such model is that they tend to generate hallucinated responses i\.e\. responses that contain information not supported by the context\. The issue with detecting hallucinations is that a response might sound reasonable, even if it contains irrelevant or incorrect information\. The prior work on the topic has had limited success, as the majority of it focuses on utilizing only one type of evidence to detect hallucination, which might be insufficient to capture the complexity of phenomenon\. This paper proposes a novel method for detecting hallucination in LLMs responses that utilize a hybrid of different signals to detect hallucinations\. This paper introduces a set of signals based on semantic consistency, semantic uncertainty, factual or contextual verification, prompt sensitivity and model variability that evaluate the responses from different angles to determine whether it contains any hallucinations\. The paper tests the model on the HaluEval dataset and compares it to individual signals to see whether the hybrid approach would perform better than any single signal\. It evaluates the performance using standard classification evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC\-AUC and PR\-AUC and performs an ablation study to assess the impact of each individual signal\. Overall, this paper aims to improve the current understanding of the hallucination detection task and the factors influencing it and provide an effective solution to the problem\.

## [Does the Higgs Have a Family? A Search for Charged Scalar Production via Vector Boson Fusion With the ATLAS Experiment](../publications/307b3d62a582e1d9d681.md)

T\. C\. Gosart

This dissertation presents a combined search for the production of singly\-charged \($H^\{\\pm\}$\) and doubly\-charged scalars \($H^\{\\pm\\pm\}$\) with the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider \(LHC\)\. The charged scalars are produced via vector\-boson fusion processes and decay into vector bosons, producing a final state with two jets and two vector\-bosons \($VVjj$\)\. The search is performed with 140 fb$^\{\-1\}$ of data collected at $\\sqrt\{s\} = 13$ TeV and 164 fb$^\{\-1\}$ of data collected at $\\sqrt\{s\} = 13\.6$ TeV with the ATLAS detector, corresponding to the 2015 \- 2018 and 2022 \- 2024 data taking periods at the LHC, respectively\. Results of this combined search are interpreted in the context of the Georgi\-Machacek \(GM\) model\. Three search strategies are presented\. The first reproduces cut\-based strategies from two prior ATLAS results, each of which observed small excesses of data\. The second attempts to improve upon the selection criteria used in the published $H^\{\\pm\\pm\}$ search\. The third, and most sensitive, strategy utilizes machine\-learning techniques, specifically gradient boosted decision trees \(BDTs\)\. Individual BDTs are trained for each search channel, and the models are further divided within each channel to provide sensitivity for specific ranges of masses of the charged scalars\. A total of 18 models are trained across the two channels\. For each strategy, limits are set on the primary GM model parameter and on the production cross\-section of each charged scalar\.

## [Türkiye’de Yerel Yönetimden Yerel Yönetişime: Kavramsal Çerçeve ve Pratikler](../publications/308b2bd4f66c69b0f8f9.md)

Erkan Dokuyucu

1980’li yıllarda benimsenmeye başlanan neoliberal politikalar sonucunda küreselleşme ve aynı zamanda yerelleşme politikalarının hız kazanmasıyla yeni bir süreç başlamıştır\. Bu durum devletlerin ve dolayısıyla yerel yönetimlerin yapısında ve işleyişinde değişikliğe sebep olmuştur\. Bu süreçte, neoliberal politikalarla birlikte kamu yönetimindeki yeni yaklaşımlar, yerel yönetimlerin sorunlarına eğilmede referans alınmaya başlanmıştır\. Buradan hareketle yerel yönetimlerin yetki ve kaynaklarının sınırlılığı, kapalı yapısı, hantal işleyişi, hizmet sunumu, personel yapısı, demokratikliği gibi pek çok alanda yaşadığı sorunların çözümü olarak yönetişim kavramı ileri sürülmüştür\. Pek çok ülkede olduğu gibi Türkiye’de de yönetişimin özellikleri olan, şeffaflık, katılımcılık, hesap verebilirlik, hukukun üstünlüğü, etkinlik, verimlilik, yerellik gibi ilkeler uygulamaya konulmak istenmiştir\. Bu doğrultuda çalışmanın temel amacı, Türkiye’de yerel yönetimden yerel yönetişime geçiş sürecini yasal düzenlemeler ve uygulama örnekleri çerçevesinde değerlendirmektir\. Çalışmada nitel araştırma yöntemi benimsenerek konu ile ilgili basılı ve elektronik kaynaklar taranmış, elde edilen veriler doküman analizi yöntemi kullanılarak yorumlayıcı bir yaklaşımla değerlendirilmiştir\. Sonuç olarak yasal mevzuatta yapılan değişiklikler ve ortaya çıkan kent konseyleri, kalkınma ajansları, yerel gündem 21, proje demokrasisi, halk günleri, e\-belediyecilik, bağımsız idari otoriteler, stratejik planlama ve katılımcı bütçeleme gibi örnekler yerel yönetişim ilkelerinin uygulanmasında Türkiye’de özellikle 1980 sonrasında yasal ve kurumsal düzeyde önemli çalışmalar yapıldığının göstergesidir\.

## [Hydrogeological Evaluation of Hydrological Data and Criteria Correlation Using GIS and AHP Methods in Hilvan District, Şanlıurfa, Türkiye](../publications/308c3d3a068a48a8cb80.md)

Veysel Aslan

This study evaluates the groundwater potential of the study area through the integrated analysis of key hydrogeological parameters\. Based on long\-term precipitation and groundwater level data, the mean annual precipitation was determined as 456\.23 mm, while groundwater levels ranged between 4\.2 m and 18\.7 m, with an average depth of 10\.3 m\. Water budget calculations indicate that approximately 3\.9 million m³ of water infiltrates into the aquifer annually\. A total of nine parameters—precipitation, aquifer characteristics, slope, drainage density, soil type, geology, land use, geomorphology, and land capability—were analyzed using Geographic Information Systems \(GIS\) in raster format\. The weights of these parameters were determined using the Analytic Hierarchy Process \(AHP\), and the consistency of the model was validated with a consistency ratio of CR = 0\.07\. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive relationships between precipitation and groundwater levels, as well as between permeability and groundwater potential \(r &gt; 0\.6\), while a significant negative correlation was observed between slope and groundwater potential \(r &lt; \-0\.5\)\. According to the Groundwater Potential Map, 10% of the study area is classified as “very good,” 20\.80% as “good,” 30\.56% as “moderate,” 18\.75% as “poor,” and 19\.89% as “very poor\.” The results indicate that approximately 22% of the area has high groundwater potential, making these zones priority targets for future well siting and sustainable groundwater resource management\.

## [Hijacking Developmental Immunity: Inflammation and Immune Dysregulation in Pediatric Brain Tumors](../publications/308c9c9252cc6d937c80.md)

Rajanya Roy; Kornelius Kerl

Pediatric brain tumors \(PBTs\) remain a leading cause of cancer\-related mortality in children, underscoring the need for more effective therapeutic strategies\. These tumors arise from disrupted neurodevelopmental programs and evolve within a developmentally constrained immune landscape that is tolerogenic, epigenetically plastic, and susceptible to tumor\-mediated co\-option\. Increasing evidence indicates that, besides molecular heterogeneity, the tumor immune microenvironment critically influences clinical outcomes\. Despite its therapeutic promise, immunotherapy has yet to demonstrate consistent clinical benefit in most PBTs, highlighting the need for rational multimodal strategies guided by deeper understanding of tumor\-immune interactions in the developing brain\. To provide a comprehensive perspective on fetal immune ontogeny and its tumor\-driven dysregulation we used medulloblastoma, pediatric gliomas, atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumors, and ependymoma as representative entities\. Drawing on insights from developmental neurobiology, tumor immunology, and emerging multi\-omic studies, we outline how PBTs exploit physiological immune maturation programs to establish immune evasion, sustain chronic inflammation, and promote therapy resistance\. We further discuss emerging multimodal immunotherapeutic strategies and next\-generation CAR T\-cell approaches currently under clinical investigation\. In addition, we highlight therapeutic avenues such as targeting tumor\-associated myeloid populations and key inflammatory regulators that may offer promising opportunities for future clinical translation\. We believe this Review will help address current limitations in preclinical models, improve patient stratification and guide rational design of therapeutic strategies\.

## [Digital\-Green Integration and Supply\-Chain Resilience in Bangladesh&\#x27;s Footwear Industry: The Mediating Role of Circular\-Economy Practices](../publications/3090c3d754ba3238e0e5.md)

Wasif Hammad; Shajjad Hossain; Ifrad Hossain; Masrur Sabih Mahir; Md\. Mehedi Raj

Bangladesh&\#x27;s footwear industry faces mounting pressure to strengthen environmental performance while maintaining continuity against supply\-chain disruptions, yet limited empirical evidence explains how digital and green capabilities jointly relate to resilience in this context\. Drawing on dynamic capability theory, this study examined the associations among digital technology adoption \(DTA\), green supply\-chain management \(GSCM\), and supply\-chain resilience \(SCR\) among managers and professionals in Bangladesh&\#x27;s footwear manufacturing and supply\-chain organizations\. A cross\-sectional survey of 47 valid respondents was analyzed using reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlation, and ordinary least squares regression with robust standard errors\. DTA was positively associated with GSCM \(r = \.446, p = \.002\)\. DTA and GSCM each showed a positive, statistically significant, and independent association with SCR, together explaining 54\.5% of the variance in resilience, with DTA showing the larger unique effect \(β = \.526 versus β = \.334 for GSCM\)\. Item\-level analysis further identified digital traceability and green purchasing as the two practices with the largest perceived implementation gaps in the sample\. Circular\-economy practices were measured but excluded from the confirmatory analysis and remain a direction for future research\. The findings suggest that digital and green capabilities each contribute distinctly to supply\-chain resilience and point to traceability and green sourcing as priority areas for footwear manufacturers and policymakers seeking to strengthen resilience in Bangladesh&\#x27;s footwear sector\.
