## [Holistic climate change education in Finnish lower secondary science: textbook representations and teachers’ perspectives](../publications/333b300e55f56820caa3.md)

Pilvi Sihvonen; Veera Uusi\-Äijö; Maija Katariina Aksela

Climate change education is widely promoted as a holistic and cross\-curricular goal\. The study examines, through Finnish textbooks and teachers’ perspectives, the opportunities and challenges of implementing holistic climate change education in lower secondary science\. The analysis combines textbook analysis, a teacher survey \(N = 66\), and interviews, guided by the UNESCO Greening Curriculum framework\. The findings show that teachers consider climate change highly relevant and demonstrate the knowledge and pedagogical capacity for holistic approaches, although these remain largely implicit\. However, three interrelated challenges constrain the implementation of these approaches\. Climate change is represented unevenly across textbook series, resulting in different learning pathways and potentially unequal opportunities for students\. Teachers report that textbooks provide insufficient support, particularly in physics and chemistry, and that their educational background has not adequately prepared them\. Therefore, they rely on self\-produced materials and continuous self\-directed learning, increasing workload\. Structural conditions of subject\-based schooling and the subject\-centred nature of teaching contribute to fragmented and teacher\-dependent practices, while school architecture shapes opportunities for teacher collaboration, and socio\-economic context and school culture influence how climate change is positioned in teaching\. The findings suggest that developing holistic climate change education requires a research\-informed understanding of how climate change concepts develop and how this understanding can be translated into practice\. This calls for closer integration of research and practice through collaborative approaches, such as co\-design, involving multidisciplinary actors and teacher\-researchers\. The results can inform curriculum, textbook, and teacher education development\. Without such efforts, fragmented practices are likely to persist\.

## [Medium\-Frequency Electrotherapy\-Driven Remodeling of Tumor Biology and Overcoming Treatment Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Integration](../publications/33404209003b1058c5d0.md)

Xiumin Wu; Yao Liu; Zhifei He; Hang Du; Hongzhi Ouyang; Huaiqing Luo; Yufei Li; Jun Huang; Yongguang Tao; Li Cong; Chen Yuanbing; Yiqun Jiang

Electrotherapy exerts antitumor effects by applying specific electric currents or fields to tumor tissues, inducing biological responses through thermal, non\-thermal, and electrochemical mechanisms\. In recent years, electrotherapy has emerged as a promising approach in cancer treatment\. Its therapeutic efficacy is largely determined by key physical parameters, including frequency, voltage, electric field strength, and exposure duration\. Among various electrotherapy modalities, medium\-frequency electrotherapy, which primarily operates through non\-thermal mechanisms, induces biological effects via coordinated regulation of multiple cellular processes, including membrane potential modulation, ion channel activity, and intracellular signaling pathways\. This category mainly includes pulsed electric fields and tumor treating fields\. This review systematically summarizes the historical development and evolution of electrotherapy, with particular emphasis on the regulatory effects of medium\-frequency electrotherapy on malignant tumor biology\. We further discuss the molecular mechanisms through which medium\-frequency electrotherapy, alone or in combination with surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, may overcome tumor treatment resistance\. By integrating recent clinical evidence regarding the application of medium\-frequency electrotherapy in combination with conventional anticancer therapies, this review proposes a &\#x27;physical energy\-biological effect\-clinical translation&\#x27; framework\. Through elucidating how electrotherapy reshapes tumor biology and attenuates resistance to established treatments, this review provides new insights into the development of multimodal therapeutic strategies for cancer\.

## [Identification of SGK1 as a candidate regulator associated with myeloid cell senescence in ME/CFS: An integrative transcriptomic and experimental study](../publications/3343bc04c67145460afd.md)

Yan Jin; Rui Qin; Wan Li; Jin Liu; Xinghua Chen

BACKGROUND: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome \(ME/CFS\) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding\. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored\. METHODS: A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed\. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577\. Weighted gene co\-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype\. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging\-related genes from the GenAge database\. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms\. Cell type\-specific expression was mapped using single\-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP\-1 cell senescence model\. RESULTS: Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes\. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation\. Single\-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern\. Single\-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function\. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D\-galactose\-induced senescent THP\-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53\. CONCLUSION: This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence\-related alterations in ME/CFS\. Integrated transcriptomic, single\-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging\-associated immune alterations\. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS\-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1\.

## [Is there scope for scope in morphophonological rule induction?](../publications/335060251bf66dc54bea.md)

Bert Vaux; Núria Bosch

In the context of finite input, learners are faced with a learnability problem: they must infer the full set contexts where a given rule or dependency applies, even if the input exposed contains only a limited set of tokens relevant to that given rule\. In order to make headway in situations of input sparseness, the learner is thus forced to extrapolate\. A key question in language acquisition, both phonological and morphosyntactic, remains which ‘extrapolation’ or, more precisely, evaluation metrics the learner uses in the task of inferring one linguistic system over other possible systems \(Gold, 1967\)\.

## [Politics as a Principal Instrument of Social Change](../publications/33572336c1d5058cf900.md)

Anokwuru  PhD Rev Fr Christian Uche

This paper examines politics as the primary instrument of social transformation and human advancement\. It argues that political participation is an essential aspect of human existence and collective development\. Drawing on the philosophical insights of Aristotle, John Locke, and Hannah Arendt, the study contends that politics is the framework through which societies translate ethical ideals into structures that sustain justice and order\. It further highlights how the deliberate engagement of citizens, especially young people, is central to the renewal of governance and the pursuit of social equity\. The discussion integrates classical thought with contemporary realities, showing how technology and civic awareness expand the possibilities of democratic participation\. By situating politics within the broader discourse of moral responsibility and social progress, the paper concludes that the true measure of any political system lies in its capacity to cultivate integrity, accountability, and community welfare\. Politics, therefore, remains the most vital means through which humanity organizes itself toward sustainable and inclusive development\.

## [Harmful Partial Interventions and Benign Leakage in Concept\-based Models](../publications/335a37e8f20a27bbaaf6.md)

Gregory Verghese; Christopher J\. Soelistyo; Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga; Alessandro Barp; Christopher R\. S\. Banerji

Artificial intelligence systems deployed in high\-risk settings increasingly require models that support meaningful human oversight\. Concept\-based models \(CMs\) offer a promising framework by enabling users to inspect and intervene on intermediate, human\-understandable concepts\. However, concept interventions can counterintuitively worsen downstream predictions, a failure mode we formalise as intervention harm\. We distinguish harm after all concepts have been intervened on from harm under partial interventions, the more likely practical use case\. Modern CMs often achieve high accuracy by encoding, or leaking, additional task\-relevant information in their intermediate concept representations\. Recent work argues that such leakage can be benign with respect to intervention harm when concept representations satisfy two conditions: sufficiency and localisation\. We prove that these criteria are not sufficient to guarantee that concept interventions improve downstream performance\. Across controlled and real\-world settings, we find that concept supervision incompleteness is associated with increased intervention harm\. Importantly, optimising the model when all concepts are intervened on, a previously proposed leakage mitigation objective, reduces endpoint harm but does not reliably prevent harmful partial corrections\. Hence, we introduce a complementary monotonic intervention objective that directly penalises increases in task loss along partial intervention trajectories\. Combining endpoint and monotonic intervention training substantially reduces the prevalence and magnitude of partial intervention harm while preserving concept and task predictive performance\.

## [Ferroptosis–pyroptosis crosstalk in neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: epithelial barrier failure, immune amplification, and precision targeting](../publications/335b8aef2fca6215543c.md)

Juan He; Yu Gu; Shanshan An; Liwei Yan; Xuhua Song

Necrotizing enterocolitis \(NEC\) is a rapidly progressive intestinal emergency of preterm infants in which epithelial injury, dysregulated innate immunity, microvascular failure and microbial translocation reinforce one another\. Ferroptosis and pyroptosis have emerged as complementary components of this process\. Ferroptosis is driven by iron\-dependent phospholipid peroxidation and failure of the SLC7A11–glutathione–GPX4 defense system, whereas pyroptosis is executed by inflammasome\-activated gasdermins with release of interleukin\-1β, interleukin\-18 and damage\-associated molecular patterns\. Recent NEC studies implicate epithelial ferroptosis, inflammasome–GSDMD activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immune\-cell death programs across epithelial, myeloid, lymphoid, and platelet compartments\. Current data support convergence through redox stress, mitochondrial injury, damage\-associated molecular patterns \(DAMPs\), and barrier failure; however, coexistence of ferroptotic and pyroptotic signals should not be interpreted as proven reciprocal crosstalk\. Direct causal coupling between these pathways in human NEC remains unconfirmed\. This Mini Review integrates epithelial, immune and vascular evidence; evaluates candidate biomarkers including HMGB1, intestinal fatty acid\-binding protein, S100A12, DEFA6 and lipopolysaccharide\-binding protein; and proposes a precision\-targeting framework\. Human milk–based supportive strategies are clinically relevant, whereas FXR/ACSL4 modulation, ferroptosis inhibitors, NLRP3/GSDMD blockade, and mitophagy\-directed interventions remain predominantly experimental in NEC\. Progress will require cell\-resolved human validation, longitudinal biomarker panels and developmentally appropriate combination strategies that interrupt the death–inflammation cycle without impairing host defense or intestinal maturation\.

## [Scaling transformer\-based abstractive multi\-document summarization to Arabic language](../publications/33671e10fc07d1516756.md)

Amer Al\-Dulame; Mohsen Kahani; Mohamed Allahbakhsh

The abstractive multi\-document summarization \(AMDS\) of the Arabic language is a daunting task because of the morphological richness of its language, the syntactic diversity, and the lack of task\-specific benchmarks\. We present Ara25, a Modern Standard Arabic multi\-document dataset, built upon more than a hundred news sources, and divided into 700\+ real\-world events, in this work, wherein each event contains several related articles, each with a single human\-written abstractive description\. Based on this resource, we construct and comparatively analyze five transformer\-based summarizers, mT5, Longformer EncoderDecoders \(LED\), AraT5, AarBERT and multilingual BERT, within a common long\-context fine\-tuning protocol that encodes and decodes multi\-article inputs with explicit article\-boundary markers\. We include Arabic conscious preprocessing and a full evaluation suite, consisting of ROUGE, BLEU, METEOR, chrF, BERTScore, MoverScore and human judgments of fluency, coherence, faithfulness, and coverage\. According to experimental results, long\-context abstractive models, especially those initialized with an XLSum\-tuned checkpoint, significantly outperform encoder\-decoder models on short contexts with respect to syntactic consistency and semantic adequacy, making them the best current baselines to date on Arabic AMDS on Ara25\. The combination of the dataset, modeling recipe and evaluation protocol gives a realistic benchmark and a reproducible reference point to future study on the abstractive multi\-document summarization in low\-resource languages\.

## [New Approach Methodologies \( NAMs \): Guiding Clinical Predictions through Human‐Relevant Evidence](../publications/33689143ca8d7b1efad8.md)

Aarzoo Thakur; Eric Chun Yong Chan; Mohamed A\. Elmeliegy; Karen Rowland Yeo

New Approach Methodologies \(NAMs\) encompass a growing family of non\-animal and human\-relevant tools designed to reduce, refine or replace traditional animal studies while generating evidence that is more translatable to human biology\. 1 However, NAMs are still often framed as alternatives to conventional animal studies\.This framing understates their broader and potentially more significant role in drug development\.The more pertinent question is not simply &\#x27;If a method is nonanimal or technologically novel?&\#x27;\.It is whether the method can generate human\-relevant evidence, demonstrate sufficient credibility for its intended use and support informed regulatory decisions\.This broader vision motivated the Clinical Pharmacology &amp; Therapeutics themed issue, &\#x27;New Approach Methodologies \(NAMs\): Guiding Clinical Predictions through Humanrelevant Evidence&\#x27; \.Numerous articles in this issue illustrate the translational utility of NAMs across the drug development continuum\.Together, they also show that experimental and computational NAMs are not competing but complementary components of translational pharmacology\.Experimental NAMs generate human\-relevant biological data\.Computational NAMs integrate these data into the context of whole\-body exposure, disease and population variability to generate quantitative predictions\.2 This interdependence is critical for improving the translation of safety and efficacy findings across drug development\.

## [Sliding Ferroelectric Metals: An Emerging Frontier](../publications/337167130a8c000d58a8.md)

Ying Yang; Zhenzhou Guo; Xia Cheng; Xiaotian Wang

ABSTRACT Sliding ferroelectric \(FE\) metals have emerged as a distinct paradigm in which interlayer sliding enables switchable out‐of‐plane polarization in a metallic state, overcoming the conventional incompatibility between FE switching and metallicity\. This Perspective traces the development of this field from its foundation in nonmagnetic systems, including 1T′‐WTe 2 and T d ‐MoTe 2 , in which switchable polarization coexists with metallic electronic states and enables Berry curvature memory and electrically controlled superconductivity\. Recent extensions to systems hosting compensated magnetic orders are also discussed\. Representative material platforms further reveal that these magnetic sliding FE metals can host triply‐coupled switching, sizable linear magnetoelectric coupling, and electrically tunable anomalous transport properties\. Critical challenges to translating these advances into practical applications are further identified, encompassing material discovery, experimental verification of triply‐coupled switching, and the development of spintronic devices\.

## [Smart Nanoformulations for Precision Medicine: Emerging Technologies, Therapeutic Applications, and Clinical Challenges](../publications/3378e92e8d8881381392.md)

A\. Helen Sonia; A\. Mohamed Ansar; D\.L\. Jayachandran; J\.L\. Arun; S\. Uma Maheswari; R\. Eshamugi; C\.J\. Shammah; P\. Sathiya; S\. Nagarajan

Smart nanoformulations have emerged as promising platforms in precision medicine by enabling controlled drug delivery, improved therapeutic targeting, enhanced bioavailability, and potential reductions in systemic toxicity\. Conventional drug delivery systems often encounter limitations associated with poor aqueous solubility, rapid clearance, inadequate tissue penetration, nonspecific biodistribution, and interpatient variability\. Recent advances have facilitated multifunctional carriers including polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, lipid nanoparticles, dendrimers, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, metallic nanoparticles, and biomimetic nanocarriers\. These systems can respond to endogenous stimuli such as pH, reactive oxygen species, enzyme activity, hypoxia, and redox conditions, or exogenous stimuli including light, magnetic fields, temperature, and ultrasound\. Integration with artificial intelligence, molecular imaging, genomic profiling, and theranostics offers opportunities for personalized therapy\. Applications span oncology, neurological and cardiovascular disorders, inflammation, infectious diseases, and nucleic acid therapeutics\. Although several nanomedicines have achieved regulatory approval, most complex stimuliresponsive and patient\-specific systems remain investigational\. Critical obstacles include biological heterogeneity, limited tissue accumulation, protein corona formation, immunogenicity, long\-term toxicity, manufacturing complexity, scale\-up, and regulatory requirements\. This review discusses major technologies, mechanisms, characterization approaches, therapeutic applications, clinical challenges, and future directions, emphasizing biomarker\-guided patient selection and clinical feasibility\.

## [Constructing t\-way test suites: a systematic survey and qualitative synthesis of the One\-Parameter\-at\-a\-Time approach](../publications/337cd0e1ffe94b5a9a28.md)

Muhammad Sabo Yahaya; Ahmad Sobri Hashim; Hussaini Mamman; Shamsu Abdullahi; Umama Umer; Dahiru Adamu Aliyu; Idrissa Mohammed Godowoli

Parameter interactions are a major source of software failures, yet the exponential growth of possible configurations makes exhaustive testing impractical\. Combinatorial Interaction Testing \(CIT\) is a highly effective sampling technique for identifying software defects caused by parameter interactions\. Over the past two decades, the One\-Parameter\-at\-a\-Time \(OPAT\) constructions paradigm has emerged as a cornerstone of CIT test suite generation\. Although numerous OPAT strategies have been proposed to optimize test suite size and execution speed, the literature remains fragmented, and direct side\-by\-side quantitative benchmarking has been impeded by a lack of open\-source tooling and standardized platforms\. To address this, this study presents a systematic survey and qualitative synthesis of 40 primary OPAT studies published between 2000 and 2026, retrieved from four major digital libraries\. Rather than attempting a direct quantitative benchmark comparison of execution times, which is shown to be mathematically invalid due to highly heterogeneous self\-reported hardware environments and the closed\-source nature of most academic tools, we establish a unified taxonomy that classifies OPAT research into five major categories: deterministic refinements, scaling and distribution strategies, advanced feature\-enhanced strategies, metaheuristic and hybrid strategies, and specialized OPAT adaptations\. Our analysis synthesizes qualitative trends, structural characteristics, parameter\-order growth mechanisms, and feature\-integration gaps across the literature\. We conclude with a critical assessment of the tooling and reproducibility challenges in the field, outlining vital future pathways, including diversified metaheuristic and hyper\-heuristic techniques, deterministic parallel algorithms, and AI\-driven adaptive test generation, to transition OPAT research into industrial\-grade, open\-source software engineering pipelines\.

## [Content Analysis in Counseling Research: A Meta‐Study of Methodological Components and Agreement Procedures](../publications/338335cd61993411f53f.md)

Edward Wahesh; William Bradley McKibben; Daniel Andrew DeCino; Lucy L\. Purgason; Phillip L\. Waalkes; Monica Maria Phelps‐Pineda; Avery Peffer

ABSTRACT This study examined content analysis \(CA\) reporting practices in counseling research, with emphasis on methodological reporting and coder agreement\. We analyzed 373 CA articles published from 1953 to 2024 across 28 counseling journals using a deductive coding framework based on Krippendorff&\#x27;s model of unitizing, sampling, recording, and reducing\. We also examined reporting of coder agreement procedures and interrater reliability \(IRR\)\. Most articles reported sampling procedures \(98%\) and a coding scheme \(80%\), whereas fewer reported coder preparation \(20%\) or pilot testing \(26%\)\. Only 37% reported a specific IRR index\. Reporting of coding schemes, pilot testing, use of multiple coders, and coding guides increased significantly across historical eras \( p s &lt; 0\.001\); reporting of coder agreement also differed significantly by era \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Findings suggest increased transparency over time but highlight persistent gaps in reporting practices, underscoring the need for clearer reporting standards that support evaluation of analytic procedures and reproducibility in counseling research\.

## [Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation](../publications/33892d1de6863834f006.md)

Weilin Ruan; Bohan Zhou; Jinghao Li; Yangkai Wei; Wenqian Li; Peiran Dong; Yingjie Xu; Leyi Wu; Haojian Huang; Binghui Xie; Han Yang; Kaiwen Zhou; Yinchuan Li; Ying\-Cong Chen; James Cheng

Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action\-relevant forms\. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs\. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence\. \(1\) Anvil\-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form\-specific generation, cross\-stage consistency verification, and failure\-driven recollection across 11 Ground\-\-Relation\-\-Act forms\. \(2\) Anvil\-Ben provides scene\-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene\-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation\. \(3\) Anvil\-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers\. Semantic\-first\-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student&\#x27;s earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths\. We construct 5\.8M source\-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held\-out evaluation and using the remaining 5\.22M records for training\. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil\-MOPD outperforms Qwen3\.5\-9B and RynnBrain\-8B by 9\.29 and 11\.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80\.67% on VABench\-Point\. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback\-guided repair as complementary framework components\.

## [The AI gaze and imagined places: Co\-creation and negotiation with the generative AI assemblage](../publications/338b002d786101041f43.md)

Michał Rzeszewski; Phil Jones; Maciej Główczyński; Tess Osborne

Generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) is increasingly used to produce images of places, yet how users negotiate representations of real locations remains understudied\. Building on the tourist gaze, we propose the AI gaze: a technologically mediated way of seeing place that is co\-produced through negotiation between users and the socio\-technical assemblage underlying GAI\. Combining semantic image analysis, interviews, and 523 prompts from 36 participants in Poznań and Birmingham, we show that these images reinforce stereotypical tropes, lack diversity, and include visual glitches\. We argue that the AI gaze is distinct because of how agency is distributed: the GAI\-assemblage seemingly resists attempts to align images with human understandings of place, while also enabling users to remix and challenge stereotypes\.

## [Stable, high\-temperature acoustic sonoluminescence using learning\-based control](../publications/339ae5c0129d82389dec.md)

Pablo Chehade; Nicolas Tomaselli; Eugenio Urdapilleta; Fabian Jose Bonetto

Abstract Achieving high collapse temperatures under stable operating conditions is a central challenge in acoustic cavitation and sonoluminescence, as instabilities typically limit energy focusing\. Conventional high\-amplitude, low\-frequency driving favors high collapse temperatures but simultaneously triggers shape instabilities that may destroy the bubble before extreme conditions are reached\. Here, we explore autonomous learning\-based control strategies to actively direct the dynamics of an acoustically driven cavitation bubble, with the dual objective of enhancing stability and maximizing collapse temperatures\. An adaptive agent, trained within a reinforcement learning framework, interacts with a numerical bubble model by modulating the amplitude and frequency of the driving acoustic field on a cycle\-by\-cycle basis, enabling the systematic discovery of time\-dependent excitation protocols beyond conventional approaches\. The control strategy is trained on a reduced\-order model combining the Keller\-Miksis equation with an ideal gas state description, and subsequently evaluated, once a stable strategy was obtained, on a more comprehensive and experimentally validated cavitation framework incorporating additional physical effects\. In contrast to standard stationary sinusoidal driving, which often leads to unstable dynamics and limited heating, the learned control policies identify simple, experimentally feasible excitation patterns that stabilize bubble dynamics while substantially increasing collapse temperatures\. Performance improvements of up to 7\- and 9\.5\-fold in the training and testing models, respectively, are observed, depending on the initial bubble radius\. These results highlight the potential of autonomous, learning\-based control as a general framework for cavitation management, providing a pathway to reliably access extreme conditions in sonoluminescence and enabling new opportunities in applications ranging from sonochemistry to biomedical technologies\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial – Educación](../publications/33ae60dd6b3d12a55200.md)

Juan Manuel Sarochar

This study investigates the approaches to analyzing the AI\-Education relationship and their relevance within the ecosystem of academic publications in Uruguay\. Through a systematic literature review, 67 documents published between 2021 and 2026 were selected and subjected to qualitative content analysis\. The results show that the predominant approach is AI in education, while AI technology education and AI ethics education are scarce\. Furthermore, the study found that AI and education are entirely absent\. While the findings are primarily analyzed from the perspective of Uruguay, they are also interpreted within the global context and from both academic and public policy perspectives related to AI\-Education\. The analysis of the study&\#x27;s results also leads to several key questions that are crucial to address in future research to further explore the findings\.

## [Sycophantic AI, critical\-feedback tolerance, and the case for productive friction in medical training](../publications/33b02aa8f6bafd862adc.md)

Zhi Chen; 贾波; 吉康祥; Huilin Sheng; Mengyun Sui; Long Xue

Concerns about generative AI in medical training often focus on eroded reasoning and deskilling\. Such competence\-based accounts are incomplete\. We identify a neglected casualty: critical\-feedback tolerance \(CFT\), the capacity to receive disconfirming evaluative feedback and remain productively engaged\. Affirmation\-optimized systems may lower CFT undetectably, surfacing only under authentic critique\. This conceptual Perspective defines CFT, differentiates it from six established constructs, specifies measurable facets, and states explicit refutation conditions\.

## [Assessment of Anxiety and Depression Symptoms Following Insulin Initiation in Type 2 Diabetes: A 6\-Month Prospective Observational Study](../publications/33b991f08bb27ee3cf30.md)

Cahit Uçar; Mehmet Emin Gerek; Adem Ay; Mustafa Turgut Yıldızgören; Hasan Esat Yücel

Objective: To compare 6\-month changes in anxiety and depression levels relative to metabolic trajectories between patients with type 2 diabetes newly initiated on insulin and an oral antidiabetic drug \(OAD\)–treated control group\. Methods: This prospective, observational study included 100 patients with type 2 diabetes: an insulin group \(n = 55; basal insulin added to OADs\) and an OAD control group \(n = 45\)\. Psychological distress was assessed at baseline and 6 months using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale \(HADS\) alongside HbA1c monitoring\. Trajectories were analyzed using 2×2 repeated\-measures ANOVA, and within\-group changes via paired t tests\. Standardized effect sizes \(Cohen d\) were calculated at 6 months\. Results: At baseline, diabetes duration and HbA1c levels were higher in the insulin group, while anxiety scores were higher in the OAD group \(P &lt; \.001 for all\)\. At 6 months, mean \(SD\) HbA1c decreased significantly in the insulin group \(from 9\.51% \[0\.72%\] to 7\.49% \[0\.78%\]; P &lt; \.001\) but remained stable in the OAD group\. Repeated\-measures ANOVA showed significant time × group interactions for anxiety \(F 1,98 = 69\.16; P &lt; \.001\) and depression \(F 1,98 = 85\.68; P &lt; \.001\)\. Within the insulin group, mean \(SD\) scores increased significantly for anxiety \(from 6\.98 \[2\.00\] to 11\.25 \[2\.74\]; P &lt; \.001\) and depression \(from 8\.25 \[2\.05\] to 12\.36 \[2\.26\]; P &lt; \.001\)\. At 6 months, between\-group differences reflected substantial clinical magnitudes favoring the control group for both anxiety \(Cohen d = 1\.14\) and depression \(Cohen d = 2\.29\)\. Conclusions: Insulin initiation was associated with increased anxiety and depression symptoms over 6 months despite improved glycemic control\. These findings underscore the need to integrate structured psychosocial support into clinical care during insulin transition\.

## [Correlation of Diffusion Upstream of Shocks with Their Magnetic Compression: An Application of IMAP’s Living Catalog of Interplanetary Shocks](../publications/33cc5a64cbe2c48f3078.md)

M\. E\. Cuesta; T\. S\. Horbury; Jamie S\. Rankin; Nibuna S\.M\. Subashchandar; Lingling Zhao; Drew L\. Turner; Savvas Raptis; Hameedullah A\. Farooki; Bishwas L\. Shrestha; David J\. McComas; Nathan A\. Schwadron; E\. R\. Christian; M\. Gkioulidou; Christina M\. S\. Cohen; Spiridon Kasapis; Leng Ying Khoo; Nehpreet Kaur Walia; Richa Naja Jain; Sungmin Pak; M\. M\. Shen; E\. J\. Zirnstein; Jamey R\. Szalay; G\. Livadiotis; N\. V\. Sarlis; John Grant Mitchell; Zigong Xu; Gabriel Domingo Muro; J\. Giacalone; William H\. Matthaeus; Gary Paul Zank

Abstract We apply an automated routine to detect and catalog interplanetary shocks observed by the Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe \(IMAP\)\. Using this catalog, we derive the upstream diffusion coefficient corresponding to 1 MeV protons along each shock’s normal direction using second\-order quasi\-linear theory and unified nonlinear transport theory to get the parallel and perpendicular components of the diffusion coefficient tensor, respectively\. We show that the magnetic compression, as a proxy for shock strength, of fast forward shocks is statistically correlated with the upstream diffusion coefficient \(Pearson correlation of 0\.81 ± 0\.13 and p \-value of 0\.014\), suggesting that magnetic compression is related to the processes governing particle acceleration and particle transport near interplanetary shocks\. This result is consistent with several possible interpretations, including changes in upstream turbulence, particle reflection, acceleration processes whose efficiency depends on shock compression and geometry, or a combination of these effects\. We host the interplanetary shock catalog on the IMAP mission’s publicly available webpage and plan to regularly update it for use by the heliophysics community\.

## [Rising Ozone Exposure and Future Public Health Risks in Germany and Neighboring Regions Revealed by Automated Machine Learning \(AutoML\)](../publications/33d279f1e86eae7ef0d6.md)

Jialing Qin; Zhonghua Zheng; Ye Tian; Haofan Wang; Junan Zhou; Mingliang Fang; Hongliang Zhang

Abstract Ground\-level ozone remains a major global health and environmental challenge, while climate change is expected to exacerbate ozone pollution\. However, chemical transport models \(CTMs\), such as the Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System \(CMAQ\), still suffer from systematic biases and limited predictive capabilities, highlighting the need for more accurate future projection models\. This study aims to develop an improved ozone projection framework by integrating Automated Machine Learning \(AutoML\) with CMAQ simulations that project future ozone concentrations in Germany and its neighboring regions under climate change scenarios\. Specifically, a fast and lightweight AutoML\-enabled framework was developed to optimize machine learning models based on CMAQ simulations, meteorological data, land use, and socioeconomic factors\. The model is trained using data from 2018 and validated against ground\-level ozone observations from 2019, showing substantial improvements over CMAQ simulations, with the average residual improved from −23\.54 μg/m3 to 1\.59 μg/m3\. According to projections for 2030 under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways \(SSPs\), summer ozone levels in Germany are expected to exceed the 2030 European Union \(EU\) air quality targets, particularly under high\-emission scenarios\. Health risk assessments also suggest an increase \(4% of overall exposure in SSP585 than in SSP126\) in ozone\-related health impacts\. Our findings highlight a simple yet effective approach for improving hybrid air quality modeling using AutoML\. They also provide an early warning for Germany and neighboring regions about the potential exceedance of the 2030 EU standard\. These results further underscore the associated public health risks and offer insights for future climate and air quality policy development\.

## [THE TALENT DEMAND STRUCTURE OF BIG DATA MANAGEMENT AND APPLICATION MAJOR UNDER THE BACKGROUND OF NEW\-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES](../publications/33d461f7a5fec82fde4a.md)

TongTong Sun; Pan Ou; Hao Pan

With the accelerated development of new\-quality productive forces, the talent demand structure for the Big Data Management and Application major is being reshaped\. Based on 2403 valid job postings collected from mainstream recruitment platforms and surveys on graduates’ professional competencies, this paper adopts statistical analysis and the LDA \(Latent Dirichlet Allocation\) topic model to explore the characteristics of industrial talent demand\. The study finds that bachelor’s degree serves as the mainstream academic threshold for the industry, and talent requirements are shifting from single\-task technical execution toward compound &quot;technology\-plus\-business&quot; capabilities\. Accordingly, this paper proposes constructing a curriculum system by leveraging the interdisciplinary strengths of economics and management\.

## [Local Level Resistance, Wickedness and State\-Mandated ICTD Programmes: A Case of Agriculture E\-Market Platform in Karnataka, India](../publications/33d5a4faa79a40d7d0ae.md)

Sanjay V\. Prabhakar; Amit Prakash

Situated in critical interpretivist traditions, this paper examines a state\-mandated programme to transform agricultural markets into E\-markets in Karnataka, India\. We problematise the top\-down, deterministic framing of this ICTD initiative, in which the state’s dominant success narratives marginalise local voices and explore how situated actors within the societal system perceive and respond to this transformation\. We undertake a layered analysis, first applying Scott’s counter\-discourse theory to establish a dissonance between state narratives and local realities\. This analysis serves as the foundation for a two\-pronged inquiry\. The first prong, informed by Scott’s resistance theory, demonstrates that dissonance with programme objectives leads local actors to adopt everyday resistance tactics such as foot\-dragging, false reporting, and false compliance, producing a condition of ‘cosmetic compliance’ amid low adoption\. The second prong, based on Rittel and Webber’s wicked problem lens, shows that the templated ICT intervention has deepened existing traits of wickedness and generated new ones rooted in resistance\. We argue that these new traits are not merely disruptive but reflect adaptive local agency and the evolving character of wicked problems\. The study challenges the top\-down orientation and epistemic preferences of state\-led development, advocating greater attention to indigenous practices, situated knowledge, and the evolving nature of wickedness in societal systems when designing ICTD strategies\.

## [Epithelial\-mesenchymal transition plasticity in breast cancer: regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic implications](../publications/33e050a518154ecf3ff2.md)

Chunlei Wang; Jie Cao; Bo Qin

Metastatic dissemination and therapeutic failure, the major determinants of breast cancer mortality, are fundamentally driven by epithelial\-mesenchymal transition \(EMT\) and its phenotypic plasticity\. This review comprehensively interrogates the regulatory logic of EMT plasticity in breast cancer, decoding the intricate interplay among transcription factor cascades, epigenetic landscapes, non\-coding RNA circuits, and microenvironmental cues that collectively sustain tumor cell adaptability\. We further delineate the translational frontier, summarizing recent advances in pharmacologically targeting EMT core regulators and discussing the promise and pitfalls of plasticity\-modulating therapeutic paradigms\. Ultimately, by integrating evolving knowledge from basic and translational research, we present a cohesive framework aimed at bridging mechanistic understanding with clinical decision\-making, with the goal of refining precision therapy for breast cancer patients\.

## [A comparative analysis of direct and indirect strategy\-based interventions for improving ESL learners’ speaking proficiency](../publications/33e729a25992fc977ac0.md)

S\. Mekala; R\. K\. Dharini; M\. P\. Shabitha

This study examines the impact of Direct and Indirect strategy\-based interventions on the speaking performance of ESL learners\. The participants are undergraduate students at Periyar Government Arts and Science College, Tiruchirappalli\. The study employs a quasi\-experimental design involving two experimental groups and a control group\. Data have been collected through questionnaires and speaking tasks, while classroom observations have also been recorded by the researcher to provide additional contextual information about learners’ participation and engagement\. The data have been analyzed using correlation analysis, one\-way ANOVA, and ANCOVA\. The results have shown significant improvements across the assessed dimensions of speaking performance following both Direct and Indirect strategy\-based interventions, with learners receiving the Indirect strategy\-based intervention showing greater gains\. Among them, cognitive, metacognitive, and social strategies have correlated well with speaking components, highlighting the vital role of these strategies in improving the learners’ speaking skill\. Within the context of the present study, these findings suggest that guided pedagogical intervention may play an important role in supporting improvements in ESL learners’ speaking performance across the aspects of fluency, coherence, grammatical acceptability, idea expansion and volume\. The study supports the inclusion of structured learning strategies in language instruction and reinforces the pedagogical shift towards learner\-centered, strategy\-informed teaching frameworks\.

## [डपफक, कतरम बदधमतत और लकततर: उभरत चनतय](../publications/33fac5d923611f317c7d.md)

अनिल हनवत

सारांश कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence—AI\) के तीव्र विकास ने सामाजिक, राजनीतिक और लोकतांत्रिक प्रक्रियाओं के स्वरूप में व्यापक परिवर्तन किए हैं। विशेष रूप से डीपफेक तकनीक ने कृत्रिम रूप से निर्मित वीडियो, ऑडियो और चित्रों के माध्यम से राजनीतिक सूचनाओं के निर्माण एवं प्रसार को अधिक प्रभावशाली बना दिया है। प्रस्तुत शोध\-पत्र का उद्देश्य डीपफेक, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता और लोकतंत्र के बीच संबंधों का विश्लेषण करना तथा लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था के समक्ष उत्पन्न होने वाली उभरती चुनौतियों का अध्ययन करना है। इस अध्ययन में राजनीतिक संचार, मतदाता व्यवहार, जनमत निर्माण, निर्वाचन प्रक्रिया, मानवाधिकार और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं की विश्वसनीयता को प्रमुख विश्लेषणात्मक आयामों के रूप में शामिल किया गया है। अध्ययन से स्पष्ट होता है कि डीपफेक तकनीक का उपयोग राजनीतिक नेताओं की छवि को प्रभावित करने, भ्रामक राजनीतिक संदेशों का प्रसार करने तथा मतदाताओं की धारणाओं को प्रभावित करने के लिए किया जा सकता है। इसके परिणामस्वरूप गलत सूचना, राजनीतिक ध्रुवीकरण और जनमत के कृत्रिम निर्माण की संभावनाएँ बढ़ जाती हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, डीपफेक सामग्री का व्यापक प्रसार नागरिकों में वास्तविक सूचनाओं के प्रति भी अविश्वास उत्पन्न कर सकता है, जिससे लोकतांत्रिक सूचना\-व्यवस्था और संस्थागत विश्वास कमजोर होने की आशंका रहती है। निर्वाचन के संदर्भ में यह चुनावी निष्पक्षता, राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धा और लोकतांत्रिक वैधता के लिए एक महत्त्वपूर्ण चुनौती प्रस्तुत करता है। साथ ही, डीपफेक तकनीक निजता, प्रतिष्ठा, व्यक्तिगत गरिमा और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित अनेक प्रश्न भी उत्पन्न करती है। अध्ययन का निष्कर्ष है कि डीपफेक से उत्पन्न चुनौतियों से निपटने के लिए केवल तकनीकी समाधान पर्याप्त नहीं हैं। इसके लिए डीपफेक की तकनीकी पहचान, तथ्य\-जाँच, प्रभावी कानूनी नियमन, निर्वाचन संस्थाओं की जवाबदेही, सोशल मीडिया मंचों की जिम्मेदारी तथा नागरिकों में डिजिटल साक्षरता को बढ़ावा देने वाले समन्वित प्रयास आवश्यक हैं। साथ ही, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के उपयोग में पारदर्शिता, मानवीय निगरानी और उत्तरदायित्व सुनिश्चित करना भी महत्त्वपूर्ण है। अतः लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों, मानवाधिकारों और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा करते हुए कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का संतुलित एवं उत्तरदायी उपयोग ही लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था की दीर्घकालिक विश्वसनीयता और सुरक्षा को बनाए रखने में सहायक हो सकता है। मुख्य शब्द: कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता, डीपफेक, लोकतंत्र, राजनीतिक संचार, गलत सूचना, जनमत निर्माण, निर्वाचन प्रक्रिया, डिजिटल साक्षरता, मानवाधिकार, सोशल मीडिया।

## [Automated Thyroid Disease Detection Using a Hybrid Autoencoder\-TabTransformer\-multi\-layer Perceptron Model](../publications/3403d59a873572f8f174.md)

Shibitha K P; P Manimeghalai; N\. Rajalakshmy; S\. Gnanasaravanan

Thyroid disorders constitute a major category of endocrine diseases globally, influencing metabolic homeostasis and overall physiological function\.Early and reliable diagnosis plays a critical role in effective disease management; however, clinical evaluation frequently depends on multiple biochemical markers and patient records, making manual interpretation challenging and susceptible to errors\.Conventional diagnostic approaches and traditional machine learning \(ML\) models frequently exhibit limitations to capture nonlinear relationships among heterogeneous clinical attributes and mixed data types\.To overcome these challenges, this research presents a hybrid Autoencoder\-TabTransformer\-Multi\-Layer Perceptron \(MLP\) model for automated thyroid disease detection from structured clinical and biochemical data\.The autoencoder component compresses numerical medical attributes into informative latent representations, while the TabTransformer captures contextual dependencies among categorical features using attention mechanisms\.The fused feature representation is subsequently processed by an MLP for final classification\.The effectiveness of the proposed architecture is assessed on a publicly accessible thyroid dataset containing demographic, medical history and hormonal measurements\.The original dataset containing 3,772 records was first stratified into training, validation and independent test subsets before any data\-dependent preprocessing\.Imputation parameters, categorical mappings, outlier thresholds and feature\-scaling statistics were derived exclusively from the training subset and subsequently applied unchanged to the validation and test subsets to prevent information leakage\.Following training\-set outlier removal, 1,790 samples were retained for model training, while the validation and independent test sets contained 755 samples each\.Experimental findings demonstrate that the hybrid model delivers an overall predictive accuracy of 98\.01%, with weighted precision, weighted recall and weighted F1\-score values of 97\.99%, 98\.01% and 98\.00%, respectively\.The model exhibits effective generalization and improved handling of heterogeneous tabular medical data through the complementary integration of latent feature learning and contextual modelling\.These outcomes demonstrate the predictive capability of the proposed hybrid architecture on the evaluated dataset, while further external and prospective validation is required to establish its clinical reliability and applicability to real\-world clinical decision\-support settings\.

## [Occupational Stress, Workload Burden, and Work–Family Conflict as Predictors of Physical and Mental Health Outcomes Among Nurses: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/34175a407618e85bdc9c.md)



The global healthcare architecture relies heavily on the functional capacity, cognitive precision, and psychological well\-being of the nursing workforce\.Operating as front\-line clinicians within high\-acuity environments, nurses face persistent challenges from structural understaffing, high patient volumes, intense emotional demands, and unpredictable shift schedules\.This comprehensive review synthesizes current empirical literature on how occupational stress, workload burden, and work\-family conflict \(WFC\) predict physical and mental health outcomes in the nursing profession\.Using established theoretical frameworks\-specifically the Job Demands\-Resources \(JD\-R\) model and the Effort\-Reward Imbalance \(ERI\) paradigm\-this paper examines the physiological and psychological pathways through which workplace strain leads to chronic systemic illness\.Epidemic levels of occupational burnout, major depression, clinical anxiety, and shift\-related sleep disorders are evaluated alongside physical conditions, including complex musculoskeletal disorders \(MSDs\), autonomic cardiovascular dysregulation, and metabolic changes\.The review also traces the bidirectional pathways of workfamily conflict\-including Work Interference with Family \(WIF\) and Family Interference with Work \(FIW\)\-to illustrate how professional resource depletion destabilizes personal and family systems\.Finally, by integrating multi\-level mitigation strategies, this paper provides an organizational blueprint for institutional, management, and individual interventions designed to protect the nursing workforce, improve patient safety, and strengthen global healthcare systems\.

## [Explainable Radiogenomic Fusion Links Mri\-derived Radiomic Phenotypes to Transcriptomic Molecular Subtypes in Breast Cancer](../publications/3431d39f4308cb76c391.md)

Sambhaji Balaso Thakar; Pradnya Sambhaji Thakar; Anil Sangle

Radiogenomics aims to use non\-invasive medical images to provide information about the molecular characteristics of tumors\. However, many radiogenomic studies focus mainly on prediction accuracy and provide limited explanation of which imaging features drive the predictions or how those features relate to tumor biology\. We developed an explainable radiogenomic framework for breast cancer that \(1\) compares machine\-learning models for predicting molecular subtype from MRI radiomic features, \(2\) uses bootstrap permutation importance to identify a compact and stable radiomic signature, and \(3\) examines correlations between the selected features and gene expression\. We first evaluated the workflow in a synthetic paired radiomics\-transcriptomics cohort of 300 samples\. Twelve MRI radiomic features and ten gene\-expression values were generated from shared estrogen\-receptor, HER2, and proliferation activity scores, providing a known ground truth for evaluation\. Five\-fold cross\-validation showed strong four\-class discrimination, with logistic regression achieving a macro\-average AUC of 0\.963\. Bootstrap analysis using 100 resamples and a 70% stability threshold identified six robust features: margin spiculation, enhancement heterogeneity, wash\-out ratio, shape irregularity, wash\-in slope, and peak enhancement\. The six\-feature signature preserved classification performance \(AUC = 0\.966\)\. Enhancement heterogeneity and margin spiculation were positively correlated with proliferation and basal markers and negatively correlated with estrogen\-pathway genes, whereas wash\-out ratio showed its strongest correlations with ERBB2 and GRB7\. The synthetic cohort provides a controlled proof of concept showing that the workflow can recover predefined imaging\-genomic relationships when a shared biological signal is present\. These associations should not be interpreted as newly discovered patient\-level biological findings\. Independent validation using real paired breast MRI and transcriptomic cohorts is required to establish generalizability and clinical utility\.

## [From Ethical Values to Organizational Transformation: The Emergence of Ethical\-Transformational Leadership Resonance in an Islamic Educational Context](../publications/3437c1533bf56df78ae2.md)

Moh Nadhif; Anas Tania Januari; Qisthi Efridita

This study explores how ethical and transformational leadership, through micro\-level practices, shapes teachers’ moral agency, organizational meaning\-making, and sustainable development\. Employing a qualitative single\-case study design, this research collected data through interviews, participant observation, and document analysis\. The study analyzed data using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by triangulation and member checking to ensure credibility and validity\. The findings indicate that leadership functions as relational praxis that connects ethical legitimacy, transformational influence, dialogue, participation, and trust\. Islamic values, including amanah, adl, integrity, responsibility, and ihsan, were embedded into everyday leadership practices and transformed into meaningful actions\. These practices generated Ethical\-Transformational Leadership Resonance through shared interpretation, collective commitment, and relational engagement\. This resonance enhanced teacher participation, professional involvement, and moral agency while strengthening shared organizational meaning and sustainable cultures grounded in trust and responsibility\. The study contributes a process\-based theoretical framework integrating ethical, transformational, relational, and sensemaking perspectives\. Practically, the findings suggest that leadership development should emphasize ethical reflection, relational competence, participatory decision\-making, and cultural responsiveness to support sustainable educational transformation\.

## [Fonksiyonel Sağlıktan Giyilebilir Kimliğe: Markaların Yaşam Tarzı Modasında Sağlık Anlatıları](../publications/3438404c71f1efd2297d.md)

Erdem Varol; Merve ÇELİK VAROL

Bu çalışmada, fonksiyonel sağlık, wellness, wellbeing ve longevity gibi kavramların günümüz yaşam tarzı giyim markalarının iletişim stratejilerinde nasıl bir dönüşüm yarattığını incelenmektedir\. Lululemon, Sporty &amp; Rich ve Alo Yoga gibi markaların sosyal medya içerikleri üzerinden yapılan betimsel içerik analizi ile sağlık kavramının yalnızca tıbbi bir olgu değil, aynı zamanda estetik, kültürel ve tüketim odaklı bir söylem haline geldiği ortaya konmuştur\. Bulgular, bu markaların aktif spor giyim \(athleisure\) ve giyimin bilişsel etkisi \(enclothed cognition\) yaklaşımlarını kullanarak sağlık temalı anlatıları giyilebilir bir kimlik unsuru olarak sunduklarını göstermektedir\. Bu sayede markalar, tüketiciyle duygusal bağ kurmakta, topluluk inşası gerçekleştirmekte ve sağlığı bir yaşam tarzı pratiğine dönüştürmektedir\. Lululemon, fiziksel performans ve zihinsel dengeyi gündelik yaşam pratikleriyle bütünleştirerek “zindelik” kavramını yaşam felsefesi hâline getirirken; Sporty &amp; Rich, geçmişten beslenen retro estetik, sade tasarımlar ve yavaş yaşam vurgusuyla minimalist bir zarafet sunmaktadır\. Alo Yoga ise yoga, meditasyon ve holistik wellness yaklaşımını merkezine alarak beden, zihin ve ruh arasındaki uyumu bütüncül bir denge anlayışıyla temsil etmektedir\. Lululemon, Sporty &amp; Rich ve Alo Yoga markalarının örneklem olarak seçilmesi, bu aktörlerin esenlik pratiklerini bütüncül bir yaşam tarzı anlatısına dönüştürmedeki stratejik öncüllüklerinden kaynaklanmaktadır\. Araştırma kapsamında, söz konusu markaların 1 Mayıs \- 31 Temmuz 2025 tarihleri arasındaki Instagram gönderileri incelenerek dijital sağlık söylemleri analiz edilmiştir\. Çalışmanın bu üç marka ve belirli zaman aralığıyla sınırlandırılması, lüks aktif giyim pazarının tamamına yönelik genelleme yapılmasını metodolojik olarak kısıtlamaktadır\. Bir başka deyişle, bu çalışma, sağlık anlatılarının modern tüketim kültüründeki rolünü disiplinler arası bir bakış açısıyla değerlendirmektedir\. Çalışma sonucunda; her üç markanın da athleisure tarzını yalnızca bir giyim biçimi olarak değil, kimlik ve aidiyet oluşturan bir kültürel pratik olarak konumlandırdıkları görülmektedir\.

## [THE ROLE OF LYMPHOCYTE IMMUNOPHENOTYPING IN IMMUNE\-MEDIATED INJURY TO A KIDNEY TRANSPLANT FROM A DONOR WITH DIAGNOSED BRAIN DEATH](../publications/343c395cd6076f97577b.md)

V\.M\. Torak

Immune\-mediated injury to a renal allograft remains one of the leading causes of graft loss in the late post\-transplant period\. Modern transplantation immunology considers rejection as a complex multilevel process involving cellular, humoral, and molecular mechanisms of the alloimmune response\. This paper reviews current literature on the role role of lymphocyte immunophenotyping in the diagnosis and prediction of antibody\-mediated and T\-cell rejection, evaluating the diagnostic and prognostic value of Treg, Breg, and NK cells, donor\-specific antibodies, updated Banff criteria, and immunological monitoring protocols\. The aim \- to review scientific sources on the current state of research regarding immune\-mediated kidney allograft injury, and to analyze the correlation of T\- and B\-cell immunophenotypes—particularly Treg and Breg subpopulations—with morphological data in recipients of kidney transplants from donors diagnosed with brain death \(DBD\)\. Conclusions\. Immune\-mediated allograft injury is a complex, stepwise process that includes cellular, humoral, and molecular mechanisms of the humoral response\. Modern dynamic immunological diagnostic monitoring opens up prospects for a personalized approach in transplantation\.

## [Diagnosing region\-specific flood influencing factors in a volcanic island using explainable machine learning](../publications/344974915a35e0daf7cf.md)

Hyeon‐Tae Moon; Gilho Kim; Kyungtak Kim

Abstract This study applies a grid\-based, explainable machine learning framework to identify dominant flood\-influencing factors under hydrologically heterogeneous conditions, using Jeju Island as a representative volcanic environment\. Historical flood trace maps were integrated with multi\-layer spatial datasets to classify flooded and non\-flooded grid cells at a 100 m resolution using five tree\-based algorithms\. The models achieved recall and F1\-scores of up to 0\.86 and 0\.78, respectively\. Feature\-importance and explainability analyses demonstrate that the dominance of flood\-influencing factors varies across spatial contexts, with hydrometeorological conditions acting as the primary drivers and spatial exposure and proximity\-based factors contributing in a region\-specific manner\. The results highlight diagnostic insights into the primary drivers of flooding and suggest that factors which may be underrepresented in conventional rainfall\-centric assessments can exert substantial influences on flood occurrence\.

## [A Structural and Behavioral Hybrid Framework for Detecting AI\-Generated Code in Programming Education](../publications/344bbde6201fc744a405.md)

Arockia Irudayaraja M\.; Rexton George R\.; Nishanth K\.; Sakthivel P\.

The Large Language Models \(LLMs\) for generating source code creates a need for code\-aware detection mechanisms capable of analyzing characteristics beyond token\-level statistics\. This research proposes CodeGuardX, a hybrid framework of structure and behavior, which combines Abstract Syntax Tree inspection, runtime sandboxing, and lexical stylometry in the detection of AI\-generated codes\. A vector of 33 dimensions containing 17 structural, 6 behavioral, and 10 stylometric features is used for classification using XGBoost with probability calibration and threshold optimization based on F1 metric\. Evaluation of the model is performed using 6,800 code samples from the domains of Python, Java, C, and C\+\+; a test set of 1,200 code samples is used for testing purposes\. CodeGuardX achieves an accuracy score of 93\.8% and F1 score of 92\.9%\. Ablation study demonstrates increasing F1 scores of 77\.8%, 87\.3%, and 92\.9%\. The combination of source code obfuscation, the framework retains 89\.4% F1\-score, demonstrating the robustness to lexical transformations\.

## [COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF CREDIT RISK AND LOAN DEFAULT PREDICTION MODELS BY MACHINE LEARNING\.](../publications/3457316d687755ffbf11.md)

Vuddagiri Lakshmi Jahnavi; Vittanala Gnana Sree; Gurala Lalithaditya Bulli Sri Amrutha; J\. Lalu Prasad

Identifying borrower default is a critical challenge in credit risk management, as inaccurate prediction can lead to financial losses and inefficient lending decisions\. This study presents a comparative machine learning approach for loan default prediction using the Home Credit Default Risk dataset, which contains financial, demographic, employment, and credit\-related information of loan applicants\. Four classification algorithms, namely Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, XG Boost and SVM, are evaluated for their ability to classify applicants according to default risk\. The proposed methodology involves feature selection, data preprocessing, median imputation for missing numerical values, categorical data handling, stratified data splitting, model training, and performance evaluation\. Fourteen predictive variables related to income, credit amount, annuity, employment, demographic characteristics, vehicle ownership, and external credit scores are considered\. The study also addresses class imbalance, as the underrepresentation of default cases may make accuracy alone insufficient for evaluating classification performance\. Therefore, accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, confusion matrix, and ROC\-AUC are considered for comprehensive model evaluation\. The comparative framework analyzes the performance of the selected classification techniques using consistent preprocessing and evaluation criteria\. By transforming applicant\-related financial and demographic information into predictive risk estimates, the proposed approach provides a systematic framework for loan default assessment\. The study demonstrates the applicability of machine learning\-based classification techniques to credit risk analysis and provides a structured approach for evaluating potential borrower default risk\. The findings can support data\-driven credit assessment and assist lending institutions in developing more systematic approaches to loan risk evaluation and decision\-making\.

## [The effect of cognitive biases and emotions on planning processes: a case study](../publications/34651d420e3f42376e00.md)

Lucia Dobrucká; Lenka Mynaříková

The planning discourse rarely focuses on emotions experienced by people who are expected to remain neutral, such as planners, public servants, and project managers, or on the cognitive biases that may affect both the emotions and the decision\-making throughout the whole planning process\. This paper discusses how rational considerations, as well as emotional assumptions and irrational cognitive biases among key actors, shaped one particular planning process, especially during a crisis\. Attention is paid in particular to the effect of emotions and cognitive biases on information processing, decision\-making, and judgment, as well as the rationalization of emotions\. The case study shows that cognitive biases and emotions played a significant role in shaping events and, moreover, influenced respondents’ long\-term interpretations of them\.
