## [Radiation\-induced oral mucositis as an immune hub: from innate immune sensing to adaptive immune dysregulation](../publications/3478dd6a367e3a8f0a73.md)

Xiaoguang Xue; Shenghong Qiu; Jianxiao Zheng; Yilin Kong; Lei Gao; Wenting Zhan; Weiwei Guo; Jixin Chen; Longmei Li

Radiation\-induced oral mucositis \(RIOM\) has traditionally been viewed as a cytotoxic injury to rapidly proliferating epithelial cells caused by radiotherapy\. Recent studies have revealed that RIOM is fundamentally a pivotal radiotherapy\-triggered, damage signal\-driven dysregulation event of local and systemic immune homeostasis\. The severity of RIOM dynamically and directly affects patients’ oral health\-related quality of life \(OHRQoL\), serving as an intuitive reflection of their local immune\-inflammatory status\. Key immunological events include the release of unique damage\-associated molecular patterns \(DAMPs\) by radiotherapy, which actively initiate and shape the intrinsic immune recognition program; functional shifts and imbalances in critical immune subsets such as neutrophils, macrophages, and T cells, forming the core circuitry of sustained injury and impaired repair; and the chronic immune microenvironment, which not only drives local pathology profoundly influencing systemic antitumor immune responses and long\-term complications\. This review aims to establish the emerging interdisciplinary framework of radioimmunomucosology, providing a novel perspective for optimizing comprehensive cancer therapy\. Additionally, systematic studies have revealed that radiotherapy induces predictable ecological dysbiosis in the oral microbiome, characterized by depletion of commensal bacteria and expansion of opportunistic pathogens\. This suggests that RIOM involves radiation\-triggered disruption or confrontation between host immunity and commensal microorganisms\.

## [Trump 2\.0 Desafíos geopolíticos globales 2025\-26](../publications/347c03199401cce3ff33.md)

Raúl Benítez Manaut

El presente artículo analiza cómo las fuerzas nacionalistas antiglobalizadoras van cobrando fuerza política en muchos países, como en Estados Unidos y Rusia\. Este país emprendió la guerra contra Ucrania en 2022 para recuperar su capacidad estratégica\. El ensayo se integra en ocho ejes temáticos\. Se aborda, como primer aspecto, el nacionalismo antiglobalizador\. El segundo apartado se dedica a cómo Estados Unidos, al llegar Donald Trump a la presidencia por segunda ocasión el 20 de enero de 2025, impulsa una guerra comercial con casi todos los países del mundo, sin importar si son aliados estratégicos o no\. En tercer lugar, se toma en cuenta la base material de los equilibrios entre los países, que se miden a través de su poder económico, demografía y geopolítica\. Como cuarto tema, se desprende que la autopercepción de Estados Unidos está en declive y se desarrolla el postulado de America First y sus consecuencias globales\. En quinto lugar, se analiza el desarrollo de la guerra de Ucrania tras cuatro años de combate, donde Rusia, encabezando un Polo Oriental de la geopolítica global, a pesar de su superioridad, no logra la victoria\. El Polo Occidental \(Europa y Estados Unidos\), a pesar de respaldar a Ucrania, tampoco tiene suficientes capacidades de sostener un conflicto prolongado\. En el sexto apartado, se hace un balance de la posesión de armas nucleares por nueve países, siendo este un indicador fundamental del poder de cada uno de ellos\. En séptimo lugar se estudia la “geopolítica en mutación”, donde los balances estratégicos entre los países se transforman, tomando también en cuenta el incremento de las tensiones en Medio Oriente\. Como octavo punto, se menciona el ascenso del poder de los países de Asia, principalmente de China y la India, siendo los países de mayor crecimiento económico a nivel mundial\. En las conclusiones, se menciona el momento geopolítico de gran crisis, por el desarrollo del conflicto en Gaza y el estallido de la guerra entre Estados Unidos, Israel y la respuesta de Irán durante la primera mitad de 2026\.

## [Authenticity across human and synthetic influencers: a configurational review of source evaluation and social influence](../publications/3480159ed4707e64c468.md)

Xiao\-Rui Lin; Amily Binti Fikry; Wei\-Guo Zhang; Kai Ding

Introduction Authenticity has become a central concern in social media influencer research, yet its construction is examined differently across human, virtual, and artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-mediated sources\. This study examines how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across these influencer contexts\. Methods This study conducted a corpus\-based review of 1,676 English\-language research articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus between July 2017 and March 2026\. BERTopic modeling was employed to identify recurring semantic topics, followed by an abductive, theory\-informed synthesis organized around source ontology and the dominant basis of authenticity construction\. Temporal changes in relative topic prevalence were examined across the eight complete calendar years from 2018 to 2025\. Results The synthesis identified four configurations: relational human authenticity, curated human authenticity, humanized synthetic authenticity, and governed synthetic authenticity\. Human\-influencer research emphasizes biography, accumulated interaction, commercial congruence, and motive transparency, whereas synthetic\-influencer research places greater weight on persona coherence, humanization, identity disclosure, ownership, automation, and accountability\. Credibility, trust, parasocial interaction, social presence, and engagement emerge as closely associated evaluative processes\. Temporal analysis revealed selective changes in relative topic prevalence, particularly concerning virtual\-influencer credibility, humanization, and tourism\-related applications, while most topics showed no clear linear trend\. Discussion The findings provide a corpus\- and method\-dependent framework for understanding how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across human and synthetic influencer contexts\. The framework highlights distinct evidential foundations underlying authenticity judgments and offers a basis for further research on source evaluation and social influence\.

## [Usability Evaluation of a Web\-Based Rabbit Reproduction Recording System for Smallholder Farmers: An ISO 9241\-11:2018 Approach](../publications/348aedbc75855c511c43.md)

Ivan Fahd Abidalbar Humaidi; Sri Minarti; Muhammad Halim Natsir; Osfar Sjofjan; Herman Tolle

Reproductive recording is essential for effective rabbit breeding management, yet manual systems often hinder breeding stock selection at the smallholder level\. This study developed a rabbit livestock recording website using The Five Planes framework and evaluated its usability under ISO 9241\-11:2018 across effectiveness \(success rate and error rate\), efficiency \(task completion time\), and satisfaction \(System Usability Scale/SUS\)\. Testing was conducted in two iterative phases involving animal science students and active rabbit farmers as respondents\. Phase I \(5 respondents\) yielded a success rate of 86\.25%, an error rate of 11%, an efficiency of 53\.05 seconds per task, and a SUS score of 63\.50 \(Marginal High\)\. Following interface improvements, Phase II \(20 respondents\) recorded a success rate of 74\.38%, an error rate of 12%, an efficiency of 66\.91 seconds per task, and a SUS score of 66\.13 \(Marginal High\)\. This decline is primarily attributable to the inclusion of farmer respondents with more heterogeneous digital literacy in Phase II, rather than a deterioration in system design\. These findings indicate that while The Five Planes framework produced a functionally robust recording website, further refinement is needed to improve usability for users with lower digital literacy before broader implementation in smallholder rabbit farming\.

## [Religious Regulation as Indirect Discrimination? Religious “Color‐Blindness” and Democratic Legitimacy Among Religious Majorities and Minorities](../publications/34976d7907c5a59a14ca.md)

Samuel Eisenkraft

ABSTRACT Background What is the impact of “colorblind” religious discrimination political attitudes of religious minorities? Cross‐national research exploring religious regulation&\#x27;s impact on democratic support among religious has given priority to the analysis of explicit forms of religious discrimination while also focusing exclusively on religious minorities as a subgroup\. This article addresses this gap in the literature by measuring how neutral regulation of religion drives divergent evaluations of state legitimacy and democracy in general between religious minorities and majorities\. Objective This study extends the literature on religious governance by examining the impact that colorblind religious discrimination has on divergences in political attitudes, particularly toward state legitimacy and evaluations of democracy, between religious communities\. Methods I apply multilevel ordinal logistic and linear regression models with cross‐level interactions on data from the World Values Survey \(WVS\) and the Religion and State \(RAS\) datasets\. Results Within countries with high levels of neutral restrictions on religion, evaluations of government and preferences for democracy diverge between religious majorities and minorities\. Above the 89th percentile of broad religious regulation, religious majorities are significantly more likely to give higher evaluations of the government\. Conversely, above the 74th percentile, religious minorities tend to view democracy significantly more favorably compared to majorities\. Conclusion From the analysis, I conclude that minorities perceive broad restrictions on religion as a “colorblind” form of discrimination which both disproportionately erode their confidence in the state at a greater rate compared to majorities while strengthening their affinity toward democracy\. On the majority side, I find that broad religious restrictions bolster the state&\#x27;s legitimacy among members of the religious majority, who themselves have a lower affinity toward democracy compared to minorities\.

## [A Survey of AI\-Based Visual Defect Detection Techniques for Automotive Manufacturing](../publications/3499273a87a94a30f2c3.md)

Rutvi Landge; Sakshi Barhate; Rutuja Kashid; Ritesh Kadam; Manisha Darak

Quality inspection is an essential process in automotive manufacturing, as defects in vehicle components can affect product quality, reliability, and production efficiency\. Traditional inspection methods often rely on manual examination, which can be time\-consuming and may produce inconsistent results under varying manufacturing conditions\. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Computer Vision have created opportunities for automated visual defect inspection\. This paper presents a survey of AI\-based visual defect detection techniques applicable to automotive manufacturing\. It examines approaches such as You Only Look Once \(YOLO\), image segmentation, and anomaly detection for identifying defects including scratches, dents, cracks, corrosion, and surface irregularities\. The survey aims to compare these techniques based on their reported capabilities, limitations, computational requirements, and suitability for industrial applications\. It also examines challenges related to dataset availability, class imbalance, changing environmental conditions, and deployment in real\-world manufacturing environments\. Based on the literature review, research gaps are identified to establish a foundation for Defect Lens, a proposed AI\-powered visual quality inspection platform for automotive manufacturing

## [Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy](../publications/34a8eb3bea85115a3b38.md)

Guoyong Ren; Chenyang Zhao; Yaxuan Sun

Background The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy \(EVT\) remains unclear\. Methods This retrospective single\-center reanalysis used a 2020–2022 registry\. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale \(NIHSS\) points from admission to the fixed 48\-h postoperative assessment\. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment\. A revision\-stage locked five\-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS\-only model serving as the comparator\. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples\. Results Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 \(23\.8%\) had END48\. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.651 and an optimism\-corrected AUC of 0\.601 \(0\.511 to 0\.723\)\. The corrected AUC difference vs\. the NIHSS\-only model was 0\.038 \(−0\.025 to 0\.171\)\. The corrected Brier score was 0\.180, compared to a prevalence\-only reference of 0\.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0\.9%\. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0\.731 \(0\.519 to 0\.892\)\. Incremental net benefit was −0\.015, 0\.036, and 0\.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero\. Post\-hoc Riley assessments across plausible model\-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development\. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation\. Conclusion Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain\. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required\.

## [Behaviorism, Cognitivism, and Constructivism: Implications for Mathematics Learning](../publications/34b581480ca34d259b34.md)

Tajina Bintay; Parama Chaborty

This study critically examines the complementary contributions of behaviorism, cognitivism, and constructivism to mathematics learning through an integrative literature review using a qualitative\-conceptual approach\. The analysis focused on four dimensions: theoretical foundations, learning mechanisms, pedagogical implications, and empirical support in mathematics education\. The synthesis reveals fundamental differences in how the three perspectives conceptualize learning and knowledge formation\. Behaviorism explains learning through observable behavioral change shaped by stimulus–response relations, practice, reinforcement, and feedback, making it particularly relevant to procedural accuracy and fluency\. Cognitivism emphasizes mental processing, prior knowledge, information organization, conceptual formation, representation, and knowledge reorganization, offering a stronger account of conceptual understanding and strategic thinking\. Constructivism emphasizes the construction and reconstruction of meaning through experience, exploration, interaction, negotiation, and reflection\. The findings indicate that no single perspective sufficiently explains the multidimensional character of mathematics learning\. Their pedagogical integration should therefore be selective and function\-based rather than eclectic, aligning theoretical principles with learning objectives, mathematical knowledge, task demands, and cognitive processes\. This study contributes a critical conceptual synthesis positioning the three theories as functionally differentiated yet complementary foundations for mathematics instruction that connects procedural fluency, conceptual understanding, reasoning, representation, and adaptive problem solving\.

## [Association of estimated plasma volume status with progression from stage 2 to stage 4 cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic syndrome: a cohort from the Tianjin region of China](../publications/34cba79c901898674d09.md)

Longrong Huang; Xiaofei Luo; Xiangqin Ou; Yu Liu; Lin Zhang; Qiang Xu

Introduction Cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic syndrome \(CKM\) is a systemicdisorder linked to insulin resistance\. The association between estimated plasmavolume status \(ePVS\) and progression from CKM stage 2 \(CKM2\) to stage 4\(CKM4\) remains poorly understood\. This study assessed the association betweenePVS and CKM2\-to\-CKM4 progression\. Methods A total of 36,505 hospitalized CKM2 patients from the TJHFIT cohortwere followed for 10 years, with 15,495 incident CKM4 events\. Cox proportionalhazards models, restricted cubic splines, and SHAP analyses were applied toestimate hazard ratios, nonlinear associations, and variable importance, adjustedfor demographics, medical history, laboratory parameters, and medications\. Results CKM4 patients had significantly higher admission and discharge ePVS thancontrols \(all P &lt; 0\.05\)\. In quartile\-stratified analyses, elevated risk of CKM4progression was independently observed only in the upper admission ePVS strata\(Q3 and Q4\), with no significant risk in the moderate stratum \(Q2\)\. For dischargeePVS, a significant risk signal emerged starting from Q2\. The highest admission ePVSquartile was associated with 43%, 88%, and 76% higher risks of CKM4, CKM4b, andheart failure versus Q1\. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a spoon\-shapednonlinear association between admission ePVS and CKM4, with an inflection point atapproximately 5\.14\. The association was stronger in patients aged &gt;60 years\. Discussion Higher admission ePVS \(Q3/Q4\) is independently associated with CKM2\-to\-CKM4 progression and may serve as a noninvasive risk biomarker particularly in older high\-risk populations\. External cohort validation is requiredbefore clinical application\. Trial registration The research has been registered \(ChiCTR2300077220\) with ethics approval \(TYLL2023\-K\-016\)\.

## [Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex](../publications/34cf222f82b6fad85072.md)

Sofia Raglio; Gabriele Di Antonio; Emiliano Brunamonti; Stefano Ferraina; Maurizio Mattia

Transitive inference \(TI\) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises\. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a &quot;mental line,&quot; a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks\. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex \(PMd\) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions\. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior\. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO ELETROCARDIOGRAMA PARA RASTREAMENTO DA DOENÇA DE CHAGAS: REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA E IMPLICAÇÕES PARA A SAÚDE PÚBLICA](../publications/34d76da6ef8f6b754ff2.md)

Kayki Saib Abi\-Habib Guerra; Isabella Rodrigues; Yasmin Guerra Saib Abi\-Habib; Davi Teixeira Poncio Vita

A doença de Chagas permanece subdiagnosticada, sobretudo em populações vulneráveis\. Objetivou\-se sintetizar o desempenho diagnóstico, a aplicabilidade e as implicações para a organização do rastreamento de modelos de inteligência artificial aplicados ao eletrocardiograma \(IA\-ECG\), tendo a infecção ou doença de Chagas como condição\-alvo e a sorologia ou referência clínica validada como padrão\. Realizou\-se revisão sistemática conforme PRISMA 2020 e PRISMA\-DTA\. PubMed, Europe PMC, BVS/LILACS Plus, SciELO e OpenAlex foram pesquisados até 1º de setembro de 2026; os anais CinC 2025 foram examinados em 30 de setembro\. Incluíram\-se 59 relatos, correspondentes a sete núcleos analíticos\. Alguns estudos pequenos e validações internas relataram acurácias de até 100%, porém apresentaram risco de sobreajuste e ausência de validação externa\. Em duas coortes externas, uma rede profunda obteve áreas sob a curva ROC de 0,68 e 0,59\. Em avaliação prospectiva na atenção primária, a combinação de IA\-ECG e variáveis epidemiológicas alcançou área sob a curva de 0,776, sensibilidade de 34,3% e especificidade de 91,6%\. A heterogeneidade impediu metanálise\. A IA\-ECG pode apoiar a priorização da sorologia, mas não substitui a confirmação laboratorial e exige validação regional, monitoramento de equidade e integração aos serviços de saúde\.

## [Machine learning\-based prediction of 30\-day outcomes after surgery for left\-sided infective endocarditis](../publications/34d8e74928da75abb409.md)

Hongtao Tang; Bo Wang; Tiange Li; Qi An; 唐梦琳; Yingying Ling

Surgery is often essential for patients with left\-sided infective endocarditis \(IE\)\. Accurate preoperative risk assessment remains challenging\. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning \(ML\) models to predict 30\-day postoperative mortality or major complications in patients undergoing surgery for left\-sided IE\. A retrospective analysis of adult patients between May 2009 and May 2025 was performed\. The primary outcome was a composite of all\-cause death or major complications within 30 days, including postoperative stroke, malignant arrhythmia, prolonged ventilation, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, shock, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome\. An ML\-based pipeline was used to select variables\. Eight ML algorithms were evaluated with 6 strategies to address class imbalance\. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and overall prediction error using out\-of\-fold \(OOF\) predictions in the training set, and the selected final model was subsequently evaluated in the test set\. Model interpretation was performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis, and an online tool was developed for clinical implementation\. Among the 992 included patients, 100 \(10\.1%\) experienced the primary outcome\. Ten predictors were selected for model development\. Of the 56 candidate models evaluated, 13 met the screening criteria based on OOF predictions\. The categorical boosting \(CatBoost\) model trained with random over\-sampling \(RO\) showed the lowest OOF Brier score and was selected as the final model\. In the test set, CatBoost\-RO achieved an AUC of 0\.814 \(95% CI: 0\.724–0\.904\), a calibration intercept of \-0\.036 \(95% CI: \-0\.474–0\.401\), a calibration slope of 0\.995 \(95% CI: 0\.658–1\.331\), and a Brier score of 0\.065 \(95% CI: 0\.053–0\.078\)\. SHAP analysis identified total bilirubin and N\-terminal pro\-B\-type natriuretic peptide as the most influential predictors\. The CatBoost model trained with RO showed favorable discrimination, calibration, and low prediction error for estimating the risk of 30\-day death or major complications after surgery for left\-sided IE, which may support preoperative risk stratification in this population, although external validation is warranted\.

## [Non\-destructive residual moisture measurement of lithium\-ion battery electrodes using near\-infrared spectroscopy](../publications/34dfcb8a0c5900c262d1.md)

Johannes Lindenblatt; MINGFEI MEI; Philipp Senft; Johannes Schachtl; Lovis Wach; Daub Rüdiger

The production environment accounts for a significant portion of the battery manufacturing costs\. Most manufacturing processes in battery production require a dry environment\. Otherwise, reactions between moisture and battery materials, especially active materials and electrolytes, can adversely affect battery life\. Current research focuses on smaller dry rooms to reduce costs\. However, with fully automated, digitized production processes, more inline measurement tools are needed to ensure quality and efficiency\. Residual moisture measurement during the battery production process is, therefore, crucial\. In this work, a contactless, non\-destructive method for determining residual moisture was developed\. Numerous experiments were conducted to examine potential influencing factors of electrode moisture\. Near\-infrared \(NIR\) spectroscopy was used to detect the residual moisture of electrodes\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) models were trained to predict residual moisture using a non\-destructive, inline\-capable hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) camera\. The true labels of the residual moisture content were determined based on Karl Fischer titration \(KFT\) results\. For data preprocessing, multivariate image analysis techniques were required to handle the large data sets generated by the HSI camera\. In the test data set, 84 % of the residual moisture predictions fell within the 1\-σ uncertainty band\. This scan\-level evaluation was subsequently complemented by a stricter, sample\-independent validation in which entire electrode samples \(rather than individual scans\) were withheld from training; under this stricter split, the coefficient of determination decreased from R 2 = 0\.66 to R 2 = 0\.39, while the model still outperformed a partial least squares \(PLS\) regression baseline evaluated under the same conditions, indicating both the promise and the current generalization limits of the approach\. The robustness of the predictive AI model was further tested by moving samples to align with the battery manufacturing environment\. The presented methodology enables inline residual moisture measurements integrated into the battery production process to monitor electrode moisture during cell assembly\.

## [Morphotectonic and topographic correlates of spring occurrence and perennial spring discharge in a forested catchment of the Garhwal Himalaya](../publications/34e128774fc84025473f.md)

Dharm Singh Meena; S\. S\. Rawat; Bhargabnanda Dass; D\. S\. Malik

Springs sustain domestic water supply across the Indian Himalaya, yet many are declining, and the landscape factors associated with their occurrence and discharge remain poorly quantified at the sub\-catchment scale\. This study examines the association of spring occurrence and dry\-season discharge with elevation, morphotectonic indices and land cover in the Henval River Catchment \(252\.71 km 2 \), Garhwal Himalaya, India\. Field surveys in 2024 mapped 82 springs, of which 74 were perennial, and the dry\-season \(March–April\) discharge of the perennial springs was measured by the volumetric method\. The spring data were integrated with DEM\-derived morphometric parameters, the Stream Length\-gradient \(SL\) index, the Valley Floor Width\-to\-Height ratio \(V f \), hypsometric analysis and Sentinel\-2\-based land\-use/land\-cover \(LULC\) data\. Spring occurrence was assessed with the Frequency Ratio \(FR\) method, and discharge with non\-parametric tests\. Of the 82 mapped springs, 87\.8% were nearest to high\-SL reaches \(SL &gt; 500; FR = 1\.58\), whereas low\-SL reaches \(SL &lt; 200\) were strongly under\-represented \(FR = 0\.08\)\. Of the perennial springs, 66\.2% lay within 200 m of reaches with SL ≥ 200, compared with 45% expected under a random distribution \(χ 2 = 13\.46, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The 1,400–1800 m zone contained 41\.9% of perennial springs and 59\.8% of total discharge\. Discharge differed among elevation zones \(Kruskal–Wallis H = 19\.86, p = 0\.001\) and showed a weak positive monotonic association with elevation \(Spearman ρ = 0\.314, p = 0\.007\)\. Vf class was not associated with spring occurrence \(FR ≈ 1\.0\) but springs near V\-shaped valleys \(V f &lt; 0\.5\) had higher median discharge than those near transitional valleys \(Mann–Whitney U = 907, p = 0\.018\)\. The hypsometric integral \(0\.44\) indicates a mature landscape with continuing incision\. Springs were over\-represented in forest relative to its areal extent \(FR = 1\.22\)\. These associations indicate that DEM\-derived indices, particularly the SL index, can help prioritise spring surveys and springshed protection in the Lesser Himalayas\.

## [Label‐Free YaxAB Nanopore Fingerprinting of Cancer‐Associated Single‐Residue Bcl‐xL Variants](../publications/34e2761b19c7225e6c45.md)

Minji Chung; Sohee Oh; Jin‐Sik Kim; 황성보; Ki‐Baek Jeong; Seung‐Wook Chi

Resolving cancer\-associated protein variants remains difficult when variants share similar molecular masses and folded structures\. Conventional assays often require labels or provide ensemble\-averaged readouts, limiting their ability to resolve subtle variant differences\. Here, a YaxAB nanopore workflow is presented for label\-free single\-molecule current fingerprinting of wild\-type Bcl\-xL and the cancer\-associated single\-residue variants N136K and R165W\. Individual Bcl\-xL proteins were electro\-osmotically trapped within the funnel\-shaped YaxAB lumen, where they generated characteristic ionic\-current events\. These events formed reproducible, analyte\-specific event populations in normalized current blockade and current noise space, resolving wild\-type Bcl\-xL, N136K, and R165W as distinct single\-molecule current fingerprints\. Wild\-type Bcl\-xL and N136K remained distinct despite a mass difference of only 14 Da, and the fingerprint separation was consistent with combined differences in excluded volume, net charge, and dipole moment\. Concentration\-dependent capture\-rate analysis further supported sub\-nanomolar to low\-nanomolar detection corresponding to protein amounts in the sub\-picomole to low\-picomole range, while capture\-rate normalization brought the estimated concentrations closer to the nominal concentrations\. These results present YaxAB nanopore sensing as a label\-free single\-molecule workflow for the current fingerprinting of cancer\-associated single\-residue Bcl\-xL variants, with low\-concentration detection as a supporting analytical capability\.

## [Oral microbial and metabolic alterations in acute exacerbations of COPD across fungal status](../publications/34e2852c7aa650629736.md)

Yanmei Feng; Fengjie Tang; Qihuan Ma; Zhi Ao; Qian Xiong; Wei Qin; Youjing Yang; Shasha Tao; Rui Guo

Background Oral dysbiosis has been associated with inflammatory processes in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(AECOPD\)\. However, whether Aspergillus\-associated or Candida\-positive status is associated with distinct oral multi\-omics profiles, and whether these profiles change following treatment, remains unclear\. Methods In this prospective cohort study \(August 2024 to July 2025\), 18 AECOPD patients were enrolled and stratified into non\-fungal exacerbators \(n=6\), Aspergillus \-associated AECOPD \(n=6\), and Candida \-positive AECOPD \(n=6\)\. Oral samples were collected before treatment and, where available, after treatment\. The primary analyses compared pretreatment microbial and metabolic profiles across fungal\-status groups, whereas longitudinal pre/post\-treatment analyses were secondary and exploratory and were performed only in groups with sufficient paired samples\. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups\. At pretreatment, Aspergillus\-associated AECOPD showed significantly reduced α diversity and distinct microbial community separation from non\-fungal exacerbators \(Bray–Curtis R = 0\.378, P = 0\.009\), whereas Candida\-positive AECOPD showed no significant global shift\. At the genus level, exploratory LEfSe analysis identified distinct subgroup\-associated candidate taxonomic signatures\. PICRUSt2\-based predicted functional profiles were broadly similar across groups\. Metabolomic profiling showed the most pronounced baseline differences in the Aspergillus\-associated group, with 11 upregulated and 90 downregulated metabolites versus the non\-fungal group\. Differential metabolites in this baseline comparison were predominantly mapped to sphingolipid metabolism, purine metabolism, one\-carbon metabolism, and cAMP/cGMP signaling pathways\. In secondary exploratory longitudinal analyses, metabolic shifts were observed in the non\-fungal group \(4 upregulated and 78 downregulated metabolites\) and the Candida\-positive group \(14 upregulated and 8 downregulated metabolites\)\. No formal longitudinal analysis was performed in the Aspergillus\-associated group because only two post\-treatment samples were available\. O2PLS identified shared cross\-omics variation distinguishing pretreatment Aspergillus\-associated from non\-fungal AECOPD, with several microbial and metabolite features contributing to the shared latent component\. Conclusion Compared with non\-fungal and Candida \-positive AECOPD, Aspergillus \-associated AECOPD showed the most pronounced pretreatment oral microbial dysbiosis and metabolic alterations\. These findings support the presence of a distinct oral microbial–metabolic phenotype associated with Aspergillus status and provide candidate signatures for future validation in larger longitudinal cohorts\. Clinical Trial Registration https://www\.chictr\.org\.cn/hvshowproject\.html?id=250288&amp;v=1\.0 , identifier ChiCTR2400083090\.

## [Using Machine learning To Predict Resource Demand in Smart Cities](../publications/34e859e138701e4198fe.md)

SAMI YASER ALI OTHMAN QASEM

Smart cities rely on efficient resource management to support urban sustainability and meet theneeds of growing populations\. Predicting future resource demand can help city planners makeinformed decisions about infrastructure and resource allocation\. Previous studies haveinvestigated machine learning methods for forecasting electricity consumption and waterdemand\. For example, Pesantez et al\. \(2020\) used smart meter data to develop and evaluatemachine learning models for hourly water demand forecasting\. Building on this research, thisproposal aims to investigate how machine learning can be used to predict electricity and waterdemand in smart cities\. The proposed methodology will involve analyzing historicalconsumption data, identifying relevant influencing factors, and comparing selected predictivemodels using appropriate evaluation metrics\. The study is expected to provide insights into thepotential benefits and limitations of machine learning for resource demand forecasting and itspossible role in supporting more effective urban resource planning\.

## [Physics\-guided machine learning fragility assessment of self\-centering\-braced RC bridges using CatBoost demand surrogates](../publications/34e8dd12a8dd6769704c.md)

Mohammad Hasan Gharavipour; Mohammadreza Ahadpour Khaneghah; Vahid Broujerdian

This study proposes a physics\-guided machine learning framework for the seismic fragility assessment of reinforced\-concrete bridges equipped with self\-centering braces \(SCBs\), with conventional restrainers used as the benchmark system\. Incremental Dynamic Analyses \(IDAs\) were performed in OpenSeesPy to build a demand\-capacity database covering eight engineering demand parameters \(EDPs\)\. Eight machine learning models, including artificial neural networks, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost \(CTB\), support vector regression, k\-nearest neighbors, and linear regression, were optimized using Optuna and compared in terms of predictive performance\. Among them, CTB provided the best overall accuracy, with cross\-validated mean R² values greater than 0\.97 for all EDPs\. The CTB\-based demand predictions were combined with lognormal capacity models to define probabilistic exceedance labels for different damage states\. These labels were then used to train a physics\-guided neural network \(PGNN\) for fragility curve generation\. The PGNN incorporates monotonicity and damage\-state ordering constraints into the loss function, together with gradient guidance derived from SHAP and ICE analyses, to produce smooth, monotonic, and non\-crossing fragility curves\. Component\-level fragilities were assembled into system\-level fragility curves using a series\-parallel OR/AND formulation\. At the system level, the median Sa\(1\.0 s\) for Slight damage increased from 0\.066 g for the restrainer bridge to 0\.219 g for the SCB bridge \(\+229\.5%\), while the Moderate\-state medians differed by only 1\.9%\. For Extensive damage, the SCB median intensity was 7\.7% lower than that of the restrainer bridge\. At Sa\(1\.0 s\) = 1\.5 g, the SCB configuration showed 15\.6% and 24\.2% higher exceedance probabilities at the Extensive and Complete damage states, respectively\. Overall, the proposed CTB\-PGNN framework reduces the limitations of fixed\-form regression models and provides physically consistent fragility estimates, offering a useful tool for retrofit prioritization and performance\-based seismic design\.

## [Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics](../publications/34ecc416d6bb59c98846.md)

Jian Gu; Hongyu Zhang; Chunyang Chen; Aldeida Aleti

The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream\. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does\. We argue that every hidden state has a native reference frame, induced by the layers that read it next and adaptive to the context\. Lexical reference frames approximate it by reading a state through the model&\#x27;s own remaining layers with a stated number of rounds of attention between positions and a typical attention output for the rest, without fitting to the model&\#x27;s output\. No lens, with fixed directions per layer, can exceed the square root of the native frame&\#x27;s coherence, 0\.30 and 0\.35 at mid\-depth of SmolLM3\-3B and OLMo3\-7B, whereas the first\-order frame, LexFrame\[1\], reaches 0\.97 and 0\.97 and reads a state within 0\.16 nats of the model&\#x27;s output\. Its coefficients attribute predictions more faithfully than attribution patching, its lexical basis steers a prediction while sparing other tokens, and its confident readings would let an early exit skip 0\.45 and 0\.42 of the layers, where lenses skip almost none\. In this way, lexical reference frames make every hidden state of the model readable, attributable and steerable\.

## [CORAL\-IDS: A Calibrated Risk Layer for Explainable, Open\-world Intrusion Detection](../publications/34fc323aa9b146c347e6.md)

Sarah Hikmat Khaled; Russl Hussein Hasan; Ali Talib Mohan; Ali saif aldeen Aubaid Khioon

Deep\-learning intrusion detection systems \(IDS\) tend to accumulate architectural components faster than evidence that those components help\.This paper takes the opposite route: starting from a rich candidate pipeline, additional retain only what survives paired statistical testing across five seeds, and report every rejected addition alongside its measured effect\.The result, CORAL\-IDS, is a plain 73\.518K\-parameter temporal Transformer wrapped in a Calibrated Operational Risk\-Assessment Layer: a class\-mean prototype memory that signals embedding\-space novelty, Monte Carlo Dropout predictive uncertainty, and a three\-term auditable risk score, with escalation thresholds calibrated as percentiles of verified\-benign validation traffic; SHapley Additive explanations \(SHAP\) accompany every alert as explanation only, without entering the decision path\.Six candidate additions \(isolation\-forest noise filtering, adaptive feature refinement, joint feature\-and\-temporal attention on raw features, prototype\-contrastive training, extreme\-value recalibration, and tenfold rare\-class oversampling\) were each fully implemented and evaluated: none improved closed\-set performance; joint feature\-and\-temporal attention consistently degraded it across all five paired seeds, and rare\-class oversampling lowered R2L recall\.On NSL\-KDD, the minimal detector reaches competitive accuracy and ranking quality under two disclosed evaluation protocols, at sub\-millisecond CPU inference; more importantly, the operational layer whose gains are deterministic for a fixed classifier recovers more than half of the attacks the classifier silently misses, at a precision where the majority of resulting escalations are genuine attacks\.External validation on UNSW\-NB15 shows the learned representation transfers well by ranking quality even as classification accuracy degrades under measured distribution shift, which this paper converts into a concrete deployment recalibration protocol\.

## [MatSegNet: A new boundary\-aware deep learning model for accurate carbide precipitate analysis in high\-strength steels](../publications/350f67e4e726178b99b4.md)

Xiaohan Bie; Manoj Arthanari; Evelin Barbosa de Mélo; Baihua Ren; Juancheng Li; Nicolas Brodusch; Stephen Yue; S\. Brahimi; Raynald Gauvin; Jun Jie Song

Lower Bainite \(LB\) and Tempered Martensite \(TM\) are two common microstructures in modern high\-strength steels\. LB and TM can render similar mechanical properties for steels, yet LB is often considered superior to TM in resistance to hydrogen embrittlement\. Such performance differences have conventionally been attributed to their distinction in certain microstructural features, particularly carbides\. The present study developed, MatSegNet, a new contour\-aware deep learning \(DL\) architecture\. It is tailored for comprehensive segmentation and quantitative characterization of carbide precipitates with complex contours in high\-strength steels, shown to outperform existing leading DL architectures\. Based on MatSegNet, a high\-throughput DL pipeline has been established for precise comparative carbide analysis in LB and TM\. The results showed that statistically the two microstructures exhibit similarity in key carbide characteristics with marginal difference, cautioning against the conventional use of carbide orientation as a reliable means to differentiate LB and TM in practice\. Through MatSegNet, this work demonstrated the potential of DL to play a critical role in enabling accurate and quantitative microstructure characterization to facilitate development of structure–property relationships for accelerating materials innovation\.

## [Mapping the research landscape of UAV\- and eVTOL\-enabled emergency medical services: a bibliometric analysis, scoping review, and policy tool assessment](../publications/35139927836e8781bbd7.md)

Zhiqiang Hao; Guoxuan Xu; Wei Zhuang; Liangru Xu; Tie Xu; Xingchen Zhu; Xianliang Yan

Background Electric vertical takeoff and landing \(eVTOL\) aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles \(UAVs\) are increasingly recognized as transformative technologies for emergency medical services \(EMS\)\. Despite a growing body of evidence on drone\-delivered automated external defibrillators \(AEDs\), blood product logistics, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations, no study has comprehensively mapped this interdisciplinary research landscape while simultaneously analyzing the policy frameworks that govern its implementation\. Methods We conducted a triple\-method study integrating bibliometric analysis, a scoping review following PRISMA\-ScR guidelines, and quantitative policy text analysis\. Bibliometric mapping covered 2015 to 2026\. The scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology with the PAGER \(Patterns, Advances, Gaps, Evidence, Recommendations\) synthesis framework, including 168 studies\. Policy analysis applied the Rothwell and Zegveld policy tool classification and the Policy Modeling Consistency \(PMC\) Index to 62 Chinese policy documents related to low\-altitude economy and emergency medical rescue \(2020–2025\), yielding 526 codable policy provisions\. Results The bibliometric analysis identified 683 publications across five thematic clusters, with exponential growth from 2022 onward\. The scoping review of 168 studies synthesized evidence showing drone\-delivered AEDs arrived before ambulances in 67% of cases \(median lead time 3 min 14 s\), blood product drone delivery reduced transport time by 61%, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations halved advanced life support response times\. All 964 modeled drone networks were cost\-effective under model assumptions, improving OHCA survival by 21%–46%\. Policy analysis of 62 Chinese documents revealed structural imbalance: supply\-side and environmental tools constituted 75\.3% of provisions while demand\-side tools accounted for only 24\.7%\. The mean PMC Index was 7\.46 \(SD = 0\.89\), with timeliness \(0\.73\) and policy measures \(0\.72\) as the weakest dimensions\. Conclusion The evidence base for UAV/eVTOL\-enabled emergency medical services is approaching the consistency needed to inform health systems planning, although no formal risk\-of\-bias appraisal was undertaken, and a critical disconnect persists between technological readiness and policy infrastructure\. We propose a “dual\-wheel drive, four\-chain integration” framework encompassing scenario implementation and ecosystem cultivation across infrastructure, industrial innovation, institutional policy, and human capital dimensions\. This framework offers a roadmap for translating fragmented pilot programs into sustainable, equity\-enhancing emergency medical service systems\.

## [Los neuroderechos en la Carta española de Derechos Digitales](../publications/3519a13eb7117628c21a.md)

José Manuel Sánchez Patrón

El Grupo de Investigación Neuroderecho \(GIN\) de la Universitat de València se presentó en octubre de 2022 como grupo multidisciplinar\. Reúne a juristas de distintas ramas y a especialistas de otras ciencias \(bioinformática, economía, filosofía, neurobiología, psicología, psicobiología, psiquiatría y sociología\) para estudiar los retos que las neurotecnologías plantean a la identidad, la autonomía, la dignidad y los derechos fundamentales\. Su trabajo se organiza en tres líneas, cada una constituida como grupo de trabajo: Neuroderecho, Psicología y Ética; Neurocriminología y Derecho procesal; y Neuroderecho e Inteligencia Artificial\. ## [Normalizing Flow Maps](../publications/35264cdfde1d9de3aa8a.md)

Francesco M\. Ruscio; Timothy James Hitge; Fred Zhangzhi Peng; Danyal Rehman; Zander W\. Blasingame; Nicholas M\. Boffi; Michael M\. Bronstein; Alexander Tong; Avishek Joey Bose

Scalable approaches to learning neural dynamical systems have placed diffusion, flow matching, and few\-step generators in flow maps at the forefront of generative modeling\. Such state\-of\-the\-art models have limited access to explicit model densities despite evolving from classical generative modeling approaches that leveraged tractable likelihoods, e\.g\., Normalizing Flows and Autoregressive models\. In this paper, we combine these threads of few\-step generation and tractable sample likelihoods and introduce Normalizing Flow Maps \(NFM\), a class of exactly invertible pushforward maps that generalizes normalizing flows and flow maps\. More precisely, NFMs learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system, but crucially, they provide efficient exact likelihood evaluation by construction\. To enable scalable training of NFMs, we derive two complementary axes of consistency inherent to NFMs that yield \(self\) distillation objectives: \(1\) pointwise matching, which unlocks $\\ell\_2$\-based flow\-map style regression losses, and \(2\) distributional matching, which matches pushforward distributions to the marginals of a prescribed forward process\. On conditional image generation on CIFAR\-10 and ImageNet\-64, NFMs achieve state\-of\-the\-art sample quality among parameter\-matched normalizing flows, while supporting likelihood\-based RLHF\. For equilibrium sampling in Boltzmann Generators, NFMs outperform prior state\-of\-the\-art normalizing flows on both single\-system and transferable peptide benchmarks\.

## [Perceived neijuan profiles and problematic short\-form video use among Chinese college students: indirect associations through anxiety and escape motivation](../publications/352c22d7cfb8ade1a949.md)

Luyang Pi; Xinxin Mo; Shishi Li; Ranran Wang; Huanhuan Shan; Jinyun Feng

Against a backdrop of intensifying competition, neijuan has become a common experience among college students and may be associated with problematic short\-form video use \(PSVU\)\. However, students may experience neijuan in different ways, and the associations between these patterns and PSVU remain unclear\. Drawing on the Interaction of Person\-Affect\-Cognition\-Execution \(I\-PACE\) model, this study identified latent profiles of perceived neijuan, compared PSVU across profiles, and examined indirect associations through anxiety and escape motivation\. A convenience sample of 818 college students completed the survey\. Latent profile analysis based on four dimension scores of perceived neijuan identified four profiles: low perceived neijuan \(6\.11%\), high competition with low burden \(7\.70%\), moderate perceived neijuan \(79\.71%\), and high perceived neijuan \(6\.48%\)\. Bolck–Croon–Hagenaars \(BCH\) analyses accounted for classification error in profile comparisons and in a cross\-sectional serial indirect\-effect model controlling for gender and grade\. PSVU was lower in the low perceived neijuan and high\-competition, low\-burden profiles than in the moderate and high perceived neijuan profiles, whereas the latter two profiles did not differ significantly\. Using the moderate profile as the reference, significant indirect associations with PSVU were observed for all three profile contrasts through anxiety, escape motivation, and the serial pathway from anxiety to escape motivation\. These findings suggest that perceived competition and subjective burden may combine in different ways, with these configurations showing different associations with PSVU, anxiety, and escape motivation\.

## [Exploration the influence of electron donor engineering on frequency\-dependent nonlinear optical properties of anthraquinone\-based chromophores: a DFT\-ML approach](../publications/352e7885cd05533b45ac.md)

Muhammad Adnan Asghar; Hafsa Sadiq; Muhammad Usman Khan; Amir Sohail; Norah Saad Alhokbany; Suvash Chandra Ojha

Recently, non\-linear optical materials \(NLO\) have gained significant attention due to their applications in photonics, optical communication, and signal processing\. Herein, anthraquinone core\-based chromophores \(APCD1–APCD7\) were designed via donor engineering for efficient nonlinear optical materials\. Their structural and optoelectronic properties were calculated by density functional theory and time dependent density functional theory \(DFT/TD\-DFT\) at M06/6\-311G \(d, p\) level\. The designed chromophores \(APCD1–APCD7\) showed red\-shifted absorption spectrum \(380\.89–466\.58 nm \) and reduced HOMO LUMO energy gap of 1\.99 − 3\.81 eV \. The density of states \(DOS\), transition density matrix \(TDM\) and natural bond orbital \(NBO\) analyses revealed efficient charge redistribution\. Moreover, the designed compounds exhibited enhanced NLO responses, with APCD1 showing the strongest second\-order NLO response, including β\(− 2ω;ω,ω\) of 7\.11 × 10⁻²⁷ esu , whereas APCD5 exhibited the most pronounced third\-order NLO response, with γ DFWM of 3\.10 × 10⁻³¹ esu and n₂ of 5\.01 × 10⁻¹⁴ cm²/W at 532 nm \. Machine learning analysis established the structure–property relationship of the energy gap, identifying PEOE VSA 11, EState VSA 10, and BCUT2D VSA 11 as the most influential descriptors\. Synthetic accessibility analysis indicates the practical feasibility of the designed chromophores, highlighting their potential for advanced photonic and optoelectronic applications\.

## [Extreme temperature, digital rural development, and grain production resilience in the Yellow River Basin](../publications/35440a0ce656f5fcc937.md)

Wenwen Wang; Yanru Yu; Yuanyi Yang; Yanwei Zhang

Introduction Severe temperature extremes are an increasingly dangerous threat to the resilience of grain production and sustainable food systems, particularly in climate\-sensitive river basins and large\-scale grain producers\. Though previous literature has considered the impact of climate change on crop yield and agricultural efficiency, there has been limited consideration of how extreme temperature events influence the multidimensional resilience of grain production systems and if digital rural development could enhance adaptive capacity\. The present study explores the association between extreme temperature events and resilience of the grain production in the Yellow River Basin, an important grain\-producing area of strategic significance with high climate sensitivity and ecological vulnerability, in China\. Methods On panel data of nine provinces from 2013 to 2022, we develop a grain production resilience index using resistance, recovery capacity, and transformation capacity and implement a two\-way fixed\-effect model, robustness test, endogeneity test, heterogeneity analysis, and a moderating effect model\. Results As shown by the results, extreme temperature events have a significant negative relationship with grain production resilience, and this result holds even when special samples are excluded and the estimation model is replaced, additional control variables are added, and the variables are transformed\. Analysis of heterogeneity shows that the negative correlation is more evident in non\-major grain\-producing areas and agricultural low\-consumption areas, suggesting that infrastructure conditions, economic capacity, and regional support systems may be associated with vulnerability of agricultural production to climate shocks\. The results of the moderating effect provide suggestive evidence that digital rural development may play a positive moderating role in the relationship between extreme temperature events and grain production resilience, which suggests that digital infrastructure, information services, and digital finance might be useful in mitigating climate\-related production risks\. Discussion These findings are valuable in the context of research on sustainable food systems as they connect the issues of climate adaptation, agricultural resilience, food security governance, and digital agriculture, and provide evidence that is policy relevant to improving the resilience of grain production in other climate\-sensitive river basins and grain\-producing regions\.

## [Multimodal Evaluation of Ouret lanata \(L\.\) Kuntze against Scopolamine\-induced Alzheimer’s\-like Neurocognitive dysfunction in Wistar Albino Rats](../publications/3545c89782cfb152690d.md)

A\. Thanga Thirupathi; A\. Shenbagavel; J\. Boopathy Rajakumar; J\. Ram Ganesh; M\. Bhavithra

Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder associated with cognitive decline, cholinergic dysfunction, oxidative stress, and neuronal damage\. The present study evaluated the neuroprotective and anti\-amnesic potential of Ouret lanata \(L\.\) Kuntze stem extracts against scopolamine hydrobromide\-induced AD\-like neurocognitive dysfunction in Wistar albino rats\. Petroleum ether, chloroform, ethanolic, aqueous, and total aqueous extracts were prepared and subjected to physicochemical, phytochemical, TLC, FTIR, and LC\-MS analyses\. In vitro acetylcholinesterase \(AChE\) inhibitory and DPPH radical\-scavenging activities were assessed\. Acute oral toxicity of the total aqueous extract was evaluated according to OECD 423\. Cognitive and behavioral functions were assessed using the Morris water maze, T\-maze, Y\-maze, novel object recognition, open\-field, and locomotor activity tests\. Brain AChE, lipid peroxidation, superoxide dismutase, and reduced glutathione were estimated, followed by hippocampal histopathological examination\. The total aqueous extract showed the highest extraction yield \(3\.48%\), while LC\-MS analysis identified several bioactive constituents in the ethanolic extract, including naringenin, catechin, acacetin, an isorhamnetin derivative, a kaempferol\-derived conjugate, and a rutin\-type glycoside\. The ethanolic extract exhibited strong AChE inhibition \(87% at 400 µg/mL; IC₅₀ 33\.04 µg/mL\), while ethanolic, aqueous, and total aqueous extracts showed antioxidant activity\. Treatment improved cognitive and behavioral performance and attenuated scopolamine\-induced alterations in AChE, lipid peroxidation, SOD, and GSH levels\. Histopathology further supported neuronal preservation\. Overall, Ouret lanata \(L\.\) Kuntze stem extracts, particularly the ethanolic and total aqueous extracts, demonstrated promising anti\-amnesic, antioxidant, and neuroprotective effects\.

## [Dzul Hori, Astrid: El cuerpo difuminado y la consciencia cuasiencarnada: dos imaginarios sociotécnicos de la inteligencia artificial en el cine ciberpunk](../publications/35493365a0a1cacf9b84.md)



\_El Oráculo de Silicio\. Reflexiones En la Era Algorítmica\_:131\-150\. 2026En este capítulo explico la relación entre el cuerpo y la inteligencia artificial en el cine ciberpunk, a partir de la propuesta de dos imaginarios sociotécnicos: el cuerpo difuminado y la consciencia cuasiencarnada\. Para ello, primero expongo qué es un imaginario sociotécnico y argumento por qué el cine ciberpunk mainstream puede producirlos\. Posteriormente, desarrollo la propuesta de los imaginarios sociotécnicos que denomino como “cuerpo difuminado” y “consciencia cuasiencarnada” a partir de la distinción entre cuerpo actual y cuerpo virtual de Don Ihde\. Finalmente, problematizo la relevancia otras formas de relacionar el cuerpo con la tecnología, frente a su institucionalización a través del cine\.

## [Understanding Consumer Perceptions of Online Sales Promotions: A Factor Analysis of Large Appliance Purchases in India](../publications/354cd0b73406cb67f9a3.md)

Supratim Pratihar; Manmath Nath Samantaray

This research investigates consumer attitudes toward online sales promotions in India, focusing on large appliances such as refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, and dishwashers\. The aim is to identify key factors shaping consumer perceptions, offering actionable insights for e\-commerce platforms to craft effective promotional strategies\. A quantitative methodology was employed, utilizing a survey of 467 Indian consumers with 17 Likert\-scale statements to capture perceptions\. Data reliability was validated through Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha, while factor analysis identified five core factors influencing attitudes\. These factors include Savings, emphasizing financial benefits and budget relief; Quality, which assures product excellence and brand upgrades; Convenience, highlighting ease and efficiency in purchases; Status, reflecting personal pride and emotional fulfilment from smart shopping; and Variety, offering access to diverse products and opportunities for brand exploration\. Together, these factors account for 73\.7% of the variance in consumer attitudes\. This study is novel in its focus on large appliances within the Indian e\-commerce context and introduces &quot;status&quot; and &quot;variety&quot; as new dimensions in understanding consumer perceptions, broadening established theoretical frameworks\. While its reliance on convenience sampling and specific product focus may limit generalizability, the findings provide critical insights for optimizing digital marketing strategies\. Practical implications include tailoring promotions to highlight savings, quality, convenience, and product diversity, particularly for price\-sensitive consumers\. Socially, the research underscores the role of online sales in enhancing accessibility to essential consumer durables, improving living standards, and promoting economic inclusivity in India

## [Identifying facilitators of and barriers to digital health literacy in pediatric rheumatic disease: A scoping review](../publications/354eef627053ec328dae.md)

Craig Eling; Alan M Rosenberg; Jennifer Stinson; Maryam Mehtar; Jasmin Bhawra; Roona Sinha; Donna M\. Goodridge

Digital health \(DH\) technologies have the potential to benefit pediatric patients with rheumatic diseases and their caregivers\. Digital health literacy \(DHL\) refers to the knowledge and skills necessary to use technology and the internet to manage and communicate about health\. The aim of this scoping review is to identify facilitators of and barriers to DHL and map them to the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation Model of Behavior \(COM\-B Model\) for children and adolescents with rheumatic diseases and their primary caregivers\. We searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, and ProQuest for English full\-text primary research studies\. Facilitators of and barriers to DHL identified were codified and mapped to the COM\-B Model\. This review adhered to the JBI scoping review framework and conformed to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA\)\-Scoping Review guidelines\. Of the 5789 unique records, 44 met inclusion criteria\. All the included studies did not explicitly address the concept and impact of DHL\. However, the studies identified promoting and detracting factors that matched the definition of DHL\. Thus, these were coded as facilitators of and barriers to DHL\. The COM\-B Model domain of psychological capability emerged as a major determinant of DHL\. The COM\-B Model domain of psychological capability emerged as a prominent source of facilitators of and barriers to DHL\. The design, function, language, and presentation of DH crafted to meet the developmental and educational needs of the user were essential to improving DHL\. Likewise, providers fostering quality communication and answering medical and technical questions arising from DH use fostered DHL in the domain of physical opportunity\. Addressing DHL requires consideration across clinical, administrative, design, and research contexts\. Recognizing low DHL and enacting educational interventions are essential to empowering digital health users\. Trial Registration Open Science Framework \(https://osf\.io/g4jbh/\)\.

## [University–Industry–Government Collaboration for Construction Materials Innovation: A Grant\-to\-Commercialization Model from Uzbekistan](../publications/355bd282667e8688e766.md)

Igamova Shakhinya Zikrilloyevn

This study develops a regional grant\-to\-commercialization model for construction\-materials innovation in Uzbekistan\. It combines legal and policy analysis, official statistics for 2020–2026, recent university–industry collaboration research, and benchmarking of commercialization programmes in Finland, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union\. Uzbekistan already permits local authorities to finance innovation, technology transfer and commercialization, and recent reforms have strengthened sector–enterprise–university–research linkages\. Yet an institutional “last\-mile” gap remains: public research funding is not systematically organized around regional, sector\-specific joint applications in which firms host industrial pilots and commercialization expertise is funded from the outset\. The paper proposes Regional Construction Materials Innovation and Commercialization Funds \(RCMICFs\), accessible only to university–enterprise consortia\. Each funded team must include an experienced commercialization manager and a market specialist, while at least 35–40% of eligible expenditure is devoted to commercialization preparation, certification, customer discovery and market validation\. Stage\-gated financing, enterprise co\-funding, independent review and outcome\-based KPIs are proposed to improve additionality, reduce capture risk and convert research into regional industrial value\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial y la transformación de la empleabilidad en el trabajo del futuro](../publications/355dcdacaceef9b5514a.md)

Angela Luciana Laura Vega; Daniel Josué Yataco Blas; Jorge Andrés Tipiani Yactayo; Ruth Gissela Perez Cabrejos

The objective of this research was to analyze the impact of artificial intelligence in the labor field, in order to determine whether it represents a risk or an opportunity for the future of employment, as well as to evaluate the transformation of the labor market in the face of the growing presence of this technology\. A systematic literature review was conducted based on a structured process that included the identification, selection, and evaluation of scientific studies, starting from a set of 350 research articles obtained from recognized academic databases, published between 2020 and 2025\. After a rigorous exclusion process, which involved the analysis of titles, abstracts, removal of duplicates, and the exclusion of studies not related to the variable of interest, 40 articles were selected for analysis\. The results showed that artificial intelligence improved efficiency and optimized processes, although it also raised concerns about the possible displacement of jobs\. Likewise, it was evidenced that the development of digital competencies and soft skills contributed to mitigating the risks of unemployment and promoting the creation of new jobs\. In this sense, artificial intelligence represents an opportunity if strategies are implemented to strengthen employability and facilitate adaptation to technological changes\.

## [Distinguishability and Recovery for a Doubly Sparse Spiked Wigner Model](../publications/355ffc1f73cd89e00088.md)

Ioana Dumitriu; JD Flynn; Zhichao Wang

We study distinguishability and recovery of a sparse rank\-one signal in a spiked Wigner model with independently sparse noise through a variety of algorithms and parameter regimes\. The signal and noise have separate sparsity parameters, while the signal\-to\-noise ratio \(SNR\) remains of constant order as the matrix size grows\. For sub\-Gaussian noise and spikes whose nonzero coordinates are bounded away from zero, a leave\-one\-out quadratic thresholding procedure \(a generalization of Ding et al\., 2024\) identifies the support\. Sign synchronization yields exact recovery for a Rademacher spike, and spectral refinement yields strong recovery\. The quadratic thresholding search parameter gives an explicit tradeoff between signal sparsity, noise sparsity, and computational cost\. We also study extensions to sub\-Gaussian spike priors through diagonal and quadratic thresholding\. For Rademacher spikes with continuous nonzero noise, we develop an identical search algorithm that exploits unblurred signal entries, the existence of which permits distinguishability; connectivity of the graph they reveal provides a sufficient condition for exact recovery\. These guarantees do not require moment assumptions on the continuous noise distribution\. Together with our previous PCA results \(Dumitriu et al\., 2026\), our analysis covers almost the entire space of parameters and regimes for distinguishing and recovering in our doubly sparse spiked Wigner model\.

## [Teachers’ Professional Development And Its Relationship With The Implementation Of Development Education Programs In Lapu\-Lapu City Schools](../publications/35618cb520bc8392c633.md)

Stiffany Ruth Borinaga

Public schools provide continued professional development, but there are still gaps between policy goals and classroom practice\. This study determined the implementation of Development Education programs along objectives and content integration, teaching strategies, instructional materials and monitoring evaluation and mechanisms in selected public schools in Lapu\-Lapu City\. The study used a mixed\-methods approach, obtaining quantitative survey data and qualitative interview data\. The quantitative results indicated that the program implementation was “Fully Implemented” in terms of objectives \(M=3\.3206\), teaching techniques \(M=3\.3016\) and monitoring mechanisms \(M=3\.3778\) but was hampered by instructional resources which were only “Much Implemented” \(M=2\.8825\)\. The overall competency profile of teachers leans toward “Proficient” \(M = 3\.1318\), leaning on peer\-led Learning Action Cells \(M = 3\.3300\) and mentorship from master teachers \(M = 3\.4000\) than self\-directed research \(M = 3\.1667\)\. Inferential research revealed three institutional dynamics: training\-driven \(Marigondon\), structural compliance \(Babag\) and decoupling policy\-practice \(Maribago\)\. The qualitative results showed several major obstacles such as excessive ancillary workloads, limited time and obsolete textbooks\. Consequently, program sustainability requires ecosystem\-specific, resource\-supported interventions rather than one\-size\-fits\-all training, serving as the basis for a proposed enhanced professional development plan\.

## [Face\-to\-face videolaryngoscopy for tracheal intubation in microgravity](../publications/357dafe237a2791afa6c.md)

Ron Birnbaum; Nicolas Bertrand; Séamus Thierry; Khoubeyb Abdelhafidh; Gilles Dhonneur

Abstract Long\-duration space missions will require crews to manage medical emergencies autonomously, including airway management in microgravity\. In weightlessness, the lack of gravitational reference alters operator–patient orientation and may complicate procedures such as tracheal intubation, particularly for operators with limited airway experience\. We conducted a crossover study during parabolic flights generating repeated periods of microgravity\. Six novice operators performed 135 tracheal intubation attempts on an airway manikin using either a face\-to\-face Airtraq® videolaryngoscopy configuration \(AIR\-F2F\) or a conventional behind\-the\-head McGrath® videolaryngoscopy approach \(MG\-CONV\)\. Outcomes were analyzed using mixed\-effects models accounting for repeated measurements\. AIR\-F2F achieved a higher success rate than MG\-CONV \(90\.3% vs\. 63\.0%\)\. The odds of successful intubation were significantly higher with AIR\-F2F \(odds ratio 6\.4, 95% CI 2\.3–18\.0; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Intubation was faster and perceived as less difficult with AIR\-F2F, whereas glottic visualization was similar between techniques\. These findings suggest that operator–patient orientation may influence airway management performance in microgravity and could inform the design of airway management procedures for future autonomous space missions\.

## [Neural network methods for two\-dimensional finite\-source reflector design](../publications/35861cb87b4590123cc1.md)

Roel Hacking; Lisa Kusch; Koondanibha Mitra; Martijn Anthonissen; Wilbert L\. IJzerman

Abstract We address the inverse problem of designing two\-dimensional reflectors that transform light from a finite, extended source into a prescribed far\-field distribution\. We propose a neural\-network parameterization of the reflector height and develop two differentiable objective functions: \(i\) a direct change\-of\-variables loss that pushes the source distribution through the learned inverse mapping, and \(ii\) a mesh\-based loss that maps a target\-space grid back to the source, integrates over intersections, and remains continuous even when the source is discontinuous\. Gradients are obtained via automatic differentiation and optimized with a robust quasi\-Newton method\. As a comparison, we formulate a deconvolution baseline built on a simplified finite\-source approximation: a one\-dimensional monotone mapping is recovered from flux balance, yielding an ordinary differential equation solved in integrating\-factor form; this solver is embedded in a modified Van\~Cittert iteration with nonnegativity clipping and a ray\-traced forward operator\. Across four benchmarks\-\-\-continuous and discontinuous sources, and with and without minimum\-height constraints\-\-\-we evaluate accuracy by the ray\-traced normalized mean absolute error\. Our neural\-network approach converges faster and achieves consistently lower errors than the deconvolution method, and handles height constraints naturally\. On our two main benchmarks the neural network reduces this error to $2\\times 10^\{\-5\}$ for a continuous source and $5\\times 10^\{\-5\}$ for a discontinuous source within a few seconds of wall\-clock time on a single GPU, against $4\\times 10^\{\-3\}$ and $5\\times 10^\{\-2\}$ for the deconvolution baseline after several hundred seconds\-\-\-two to three orders of magnitude lower error at two orders of magnitude less wall\-clock time\. We discuss how the method may be extended to rotationally symmetric and full three\-dimensional settings via iterative correction schemes\.

## [Gaze and Instrumental and Affective Communication in Doctor\-Patient Interactions](../publications/3586cfc0ab8b43436c84.md)

Nadine Bol; Debby Damen; Hugo P\. Aben; Carla Anne Roos; Rabia R\. Chhangur; Gijs A\. Holleman

This wearable eye\-tracking study investigated the social and clinical context in which patients’ and a clinician’s gaze and verbal behaviours occurred during medical consultations at an outpatient neurology clinic\. We analysed gaze behaviour and instrumental and affective communication of patients and a neurologist in selected consultations \(n = 12\), representing different consultation compositions \(i\.e\., the social context: one\-on\-one, one\-on\-two, one\-on\-many\) and consultation activities \(i\.e\., the clinical context: discussing scan results, performing a neurological examination\)\. In\-depth analyses of mutual and joint gaze in relation to verbal utterances were explored in a smaller subset \(n = 3\), providing detailed descriptions of patient\-neurologist gaze and verbal communication while considering the social and clinical context of these consultations\. Results showed that both patients and the neurologist predominantly gazed at each other’s faces but also looked at other locations and objects\. Individual, mutual, and joint gaze patterns at faces, the screen, and companions varied across social and clinical contexts\. Instrumental and affective communication were intertwined and co\-occurred with patients’ and the neurologist’s mutual and joint gaze states\. These findings underscore that doctor\-patient communication is shaped by what is said and how attention is jointly managed within the broader social and clinical context of doctor\-patient communication\.
