## [A phase\-velocity\-based 3D ray tracing method for transversely isotropic media](../publications/359133c1c3e92ee13b87.md)

Jianen Xiao; Ning Qin

Seismic anisotropy is common in subsurface media and significantly affects seismic wave propagation, and although ray tracing provides direct access to kinematic quantities such as ray paths and traveltimes, conventional anisotropic ray\-tracing methods often require repeated stiffness\-tensor rotations and Christoffel eigensystem calculations that increase their algebraic and implementation complexity\. To address this, we propose a phase\-velocity\-based 3D ray\-tracing method for qP waves in transversely isotropic \(TI\) media, in which the ray equations are constructed directly from the qP\-wave phase velocity and its spatial and directional derivatives, thereby avoiding repeated Bond transformations and Christoffel eigensystem calculations, and the resulting equations are integrated using a fourth\-order Runge–Kutta scheme\. Numerical experiments using homogeneous, layered, and structurally complex models show good agreement with analytical solutions, fast\-marching results, and simulated qP\-wavefronts\. These results demonstrate the accuracy and applicability of the proposed method for 3D qP\-wave ray tracing in TI media\.

## [Cross\-Domain Fake News Classification via RoBERTa Fine\-Tuning on Hybrid LIAR\-FakeNewsNet Corpus with Deployable Web Inference](../publications/3592217c8c9ea65b3ca9.md)

J\. Balaraju; Karthik Jilla

The rapid spread of misinformation on social media platforms escalates a serious threat to world socio\-political stability, health and financial security\. While current automated fake news detection models boast impressive accuracy scores, these are often due to memorisation of the training domain rather than genuine generalisation to unseen examples\. This study tackles the pressing need for domain\-robust misinformation and disinformation detection through the creation of a highly adaptive and deployable classification system\. The challenge stems from the severe drop in performance when exposed to the domain shift, especially with the emergence of generative language models that can perform style\-based attacks\. The proposed solution employs a RoBERTa\-base transformer model, fine\-tuned on a large, multi\-domain corpus of 37,143 instances\. This dataset mixes the short, politically focused statements of the LIAR dataset with the long, multi\-topic articles from the FakeNewsNet dataset and ensures cross\-domain generalisation\. Using full\-parameter fine\-tuning and evaluation across different domains, the model attained 86\.7% accuracy, 87\.3% macro precision and 86\.4% macro F1\-score on a diverse test corpus, surpassing traditional baselines\. Importantly, the assessment unveiled a conservative labelling tendency with a 90\.4% precision in detecting fake news and a 93\.1% recall in detecting genuine news which prevents the severe consequences of mistakenly accusing legitimate news\. Moreover, the design breaks out of research\-only models with its integration into a real\-time web service \(based on Flask\), providing sub\-second inferences with confidence scores\. This approach simultaneously addresses the problem of cross\-domain vulnerability of state\-of\-the\-art natural language processing models and demands deployable interpretability, setting a new benchmark for the implementation of natural language processing models in the fight against advanced, online misinformation\.

## [From Rules to Autonomous Agents: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence, Human\-AI Integration, and the Governance of Agentic Systems\-A Review](../publications/35a8657259a452d591bc.md)

Loso Judijanto

Artificial intelligence has evolved from rule\-based symbolic systems into learning architectures capable of perception, prediction, content generation, reasoning, planning, tool use, and increasingly autonomous action\. This qualitative literature review examines this transition as more than a technological chronology\. It interprets AI evolution through five interrelated dimensions: technological evolution, capability expansion, changing human roles, human–AI integration, and governance\. Drawing on contemporary peer\-reviewed literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, the review identifies seven thematic developments\. AI has progressed from encoded rules toward learned representations and goal\-directed action; generative AI has expanded AI into a general\-purpose content collaborator; agentic AI adds planning, memory, tool use, and iterative task execution; human roles increasingly shift from operator toward collaborator, delegator, and governor; human–AI complementarity remains conditional rather than automatic; effective deployment requires calibrated rather than maximal trust; and governance requirements increase as AI systems acquire greater operational agency\. The article proposes the Evolution–Capability–Role–Integration–Governance \(ECRIG\) framework to explain these relationships\. The framework suggests that sustainable benefits from advanced AI emerge when technological capability, human role allocation, interaction architecture, and governance mechanisms develop jointly\. The review concludes that the central challenge of the agentic\-AI era is not choosing between humans and machines, but designing accountable systems in which increasingly capable artificial agents remain aligned with meaningful human goals, authority, and oversight\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: Neurotect: The Centropic Cognitive Architecture of Structural Coherence](../publications/35c18a261cef93b2cefe.md)



Neurotect designates the centropic cognitive operating system within the Structural Neuroscience framework\. It stands alongside three other named neurotypes: the neurotypical \(belonging‑oriented\), the neurodivergent \(coherence‑seeking\), and the neurovenator \(power‑oriented\)\. Whereas neurotypical cognition optimizes for social belonging and neurodivergent cognition optimizes for independent verification, neurotect cognition optimizes for structural coherence, transparency, and lattice‑scale integrity\. In contrast, neurovenator cognition optimizes for strategic dominance and fragmentation‑based control\. The Neurotect perceives the geometry of systems, engineers coherence, and constructs environments where transparency dissolves predatory advantage\. This report formalizes the Neurotect architecture, distinguishes it from both neurodivergent coherence‑seeking and neurovenator exploitation, and situates it as the cognitive‑architecture expression of the high‑centropic Architect configuration described in SN03\. It establishes the Architect / Predator axis as a primary diagnostic structure within Structural Neuroscience and completes the four‑architecture model of human cognition\. \(direct link \)

## [Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework](../publications/35c6e6a83fc66ef155e8.md)

Yanyang Xiao

Neural networks often learn low\-frequency components before high\-frequency ones \-\-\- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F\-principle\. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it\. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: \(1\) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; \(2\) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; \(3\) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; \(4\) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite\-domain Fourier analysis; and \(5\) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks\. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series \(GFS\) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient\-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations\. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture\.

## [Clinical significance and discriminatory performance of the serum KL\-6 level as a biomarker for severe Chlamydia pneumoniae infection in children](../publications/35d541784c56966c8b8b.md)

Lei Ding; Sufang Chen; Huafeng Song; Shuting Cheng; Meng Shao; Hongyan Zhang; Jun Hua; Fei Gao; Junchi Xu

Objective To characterize the expression and evaluate the clinical utility for assessing disease severity of the serum Krebs von den Lungen\-6 \(KL\-6\) level in children with mild and severe acute Chlamydia pneumoniae \( C\. pneumoniae \) infection\. Methods A total of 68 hospitalized children with acute lower respiratory tract infection caused by C\. pneumoniae \(48 mild cases and 20 severe cases\) who were admitted to Children’s Hospital of Wujiang District from May 2024 to April 2025 were enrolled, with 19 healthy children included in the control group\. Serum KL\-6 levels, C\. pneumoniae \-IgM levels, and routine laboratory indicators were measured\. The correlation between the KL\-6 level and clinical features was analyzed, and discriminatory performance of the KL\-6 level for identifying severe C\. pneumoniae infection was assessed using ROC curves\. Results Serum KL\-6 levels were significantly higher in the severe group than in the mild group \[303\.00 \(227\.75, 328\.25\) U/mL vs\. 146\.50 \(133\.50, 164\.25\) U/mL, P &lt; 0\.001\]\. Binary logistic regression analysis indicated that KL\-6 was independently associated with severe C\. pneumoniae infection in children \(P &lt; 0\.001\), and the area under the curve \(AUC\) for differentiating severe infection from mild infection was 0\.951 \(95%CI=0\.880\-0\.997, P&lt;0\.001\)\. Further analysis revealed that the KL\-6 level was positively correlated with the number of pulmonary lesions, the number of hospitalization days, and C\. pneumoniae \-IgM levels but not with other indicators\. Conclusion The serum KL\-6 level can effectively reflect the degree of pulmonary parenchymal injury in children with C\. pneumoniae infection and can serve as an independent biomarker for severe C\. pneumoniae infection\. It demonstrates high discriminatory ability for identifying severe cases and may serve as an auxiliary biomarker for assessing pulmonary parenchymal injury\.

## [Coeckelbergh, Mark: Artificial Intelligence, Responsibility Attribution, and a Relational Justification of Explainability](../publications/35d75e3f3c27c9e51913.md)



\_Science and Engineering Ethics\_ 26 \(4\):2051\-2068\. 2020This paper discusses the problem of responsibility attribution raised by the use of artificial intelligence technologies\. It is assumed that only humans can be responsible agents; yet this alone already raises many issues, which are discussed starting from two Aristotelian conditions for responsibility\. Next to the well\-known problem of many hands, the issue of “many things” is identified and the temporal dimension is emphasized when it comes to the control condition\. Special attention is given to the epistemic condition, which draws attention to the issues of transparency and explainability\. In contrast to standard discussions, however, it is then argued that this knowledge problem regarding agents of responsibility is linked to the other side of the responsibility relation: the addressees or “patients” of responsibility, who may demand reasons for actions and decisions made by using AI\. Inspired by a relational approach, responsibility as answerability thus offers an important additional, if not primary, justification for explainability based, not on agency, but on patiency\. \(direct link \)

## [One Lipid\-Modifying Mechanism, Three Gateways: What a CETP Inhibitor Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/35d889d32ca67e77fce4.md)

Avinash Dundigalla; Afeefa Mahmood; Kritica; Daxaben Jigneshkumar Patel; Peivand Pirouzi

Cholesteryl ester transfer protein \(CETP\) inhibitors are a class of oral small\-molecule agents under continued clinical development for hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia, acting by inhibiting the transfer of cholesteryl esters from high\-density lipoprotein to lower\-density lipoprotein particles\. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of a CETP inhibitor candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\), and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency \(EMA\) under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014\. All three jurisdictions rely on the harmonized Common Technical Document \(CTD\) structure, under which Modules 2 through 5, covering quality, nonclinical, and clinical evidence, are substantially portable across regions, while Module 1 and its regional equivalents remain jurisdiction\-specific\. The article presents each region&\#x27;s legal framework, review timeline, and administrative content, develops a three\-way comparison table, and then turns to the practical challenges a sponsor managing this triad of filings actually faces and the specific ways artificial intelligence tools are being used, and can responsibly be used, in regulatory document preparation, administration, and quality control across all three jurisdictions\. The analysis closes with concrete recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing parallel CETP inhibitor trials, and more generally for any oral small\-molecule cardiometabolic candidate filed simultaneously in Canada, the United States, and the European Union\.Keywords: CETP inhibitor; dyslipidemia; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; Common Technical Document; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Where AI enters the product development process: Task orientation, human identity threat, and purchase intention](../publications/35e7dfd2902991e3c041.md)

Ju Yeun Jang; Kyuree Kim

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly moving beyond analytical retail functions into product development, raising new questions about how consumers respond depending on where AI is positioned within the process\. Across three studies with U\.S\. consumers in fashion\-related contexts, this research examines how the task AI performs and how its role is framed shape consumer responses to products developed with AI involvement\. Study 1 maps consumers’ perceptions of fashion\-related tasks along a logic–intuition continuum and identifies trend forecasting as a logic\-oriented task and design as an intuition\-oriented task\. Study 2 compares AI involvement in these two contrasting product\-development tasks and finds lower purchase intention when AI is involved in design rather than trend forecasting, with heightened human identity threat accounting for part of this difference\. Study 3 focuses on the intuition\-oriented design context and shows that framing AI as complementing rather than replacing human designers is associated with lower identity threat and higher purchase intention\. Together, the findings suggest that consumer responses depend not only on whether AI participates in product development, but also on where AI is positioned within the process and how its contribution relative to human creativity is framed\. This research advances understanding of task\-dependent responses to AI by identifying human identity threat as a mediator linking AI involvement to purchase intention and by showing how role framing can shape purchase intention when AI participates in creative work\.

## [Allocentric navigation is computationally universal](../publications/35ea0186191c2e4c8903.md)

Gualtiero Piccinini

I present three proofs that idealized neurocomputational architectures capable of navigation guided by allocentric maps with landmark structure can be computationally universal\. Navigation may occur online, in the environment, or offline, in the animal&\#x27;s head\. The first proof encodes the counters of a two\-counter machine as positions of movable markers on orthogonal axes\. The second directly simulates a one\-tape Turing machine using a writable tape\-path embedded in the map\. The third realizes the tape\-path&\#x27;s predecessor/successor relation through local cues at a two\-row landmark track rather than through a globally indexed path primitive\. I establish universality in two senses: each class of navigation models is Turing\-complete, and each contains a single machine that simulates every machine in its class\. These constructions are mathematically close to classical graph\-based models, including Kolmogorov\-Uspensky machines, storage\-modification machines, and graph Turing machines, so the bare computability results are unsurprising\. My contribution is to reconstruct them explicitly within an allocentric cognitive\-map architecture whose representational and computational primitives are drawn from empirical and theoretical work on spatial navigation and cognitive control\. This shows that an allocentric navigation\-based architecture can be computationally universal and opens the possibility of reconstructing aspects of biological cognition, including symbolic processing, in navigation\-based terms\.

## [Examining Essential Requirements for a Smart Grid Evaluation Framework Tailored for low Resource Settings](../publications/35eddf7586128c6e3644.md)

Abdu Karim Jjumba; Evelyn Kahiigi; Drake Patrick Mirembe; Jane Namaganda\-Kiyimba

Significant research has been done regarding frameworks for evaluation of smart grids in a bid to assess their efficiency, reliability, and impact\. However, the frameworks are mainly targeting developed grids, adapting these frameworks to low\-resource settings present significant challenges due to limited infrastructure, constrained budgets, inadequate technical expertise, regulatory gaps, and unreliable power supply\. Albait the automation of the said evaluation frameworks has also not been given enough attension\. This study employs a combined User\-Centered Design \(UCD\) and Quality Function Deployment \(QFD\) approach to examine in detail and identify, prioritize, and translate user requirements into technical specifications for designing an automated tailor\-made smart evaluation framework tailored for resource\-constrained environments\. A mixed\-method research design, including literature reviews, interviews, and surveys, was used to gather responses from smart grid users in Uganda and Kenya\. According to the findings ease of integration scored \(15\.2%\), localization scored \(15\.0%\), and environmental adaptability returned \(14\.2%\) and these turned out to be the most important technical requirements\. This meant that there is need for automated smart grid evaluation frameworks that seamlessly integrate into existing grid and at the same time adapt to the local contexts\. Additionally, modularity scored 9\.2%, offline capabilities returned 8\.8%, and resource efficiency scored 8\.4%\. Users emphasized these requirements to ensure ease of growth and resilience in environments with poor connectivity and power stability\. User requirements such as reliable data acquisition, resilience to intermittent internet connectivity, power outage readiness, and big data management were notably preffered\. The study further indicated that the users focus was mainly on energy efficiency metrics, resource conservation, and grid infrastructure robustness\. On the other hand, regulatory compliance was recognized but rather ranked lower in importance\. This study provides a data\-driven foundation for developing automated scalable, adaptive, and locally relevant smart grid evaluation frameworks for low\-resource settings, ensuring sustainability, accessibility, and operational resilience\. Future work in this series will look at development of a prototype, its validation, and real\-world implementation to enhance the practical impact of these findings\.

## [A study of the impact of AI\-employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior](../publications/35f327750f7b4dea4fc7.md)

Yan Guanyu; Niu Chenchen

Introduction With the deep integration of digitalization and generative artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence has transformed from a mere technical tool into a core collaborative partner within modern workplaces and human‑resource management\. As an interdependent human‑AI working mode characterized by complementary task division, joint task accomplishment, complementary decision‑making, and continuous iterative interaction between employees and AI agents, AI‑employee collaboration is conceptually distinct from simple AI adoption, instrumental AI use, and AI‑assisted technical systems\. Drawing on social cognitive theory, the present study aims to investigate how AI‑employee collaboration predicts employee innovation behavior, alongside the mediating role of self‑efficacy and the moderated‑mediation boundary condition of servant leadership\. Methods Three‑wave time‑lagged questionnaire data were collected from 259 employees working in internet‑service, finance, and catering industries across Beijing and Jinan\. Hierarchical regression and bootstrap approaches were adopted to test the proposed moderated‑mediation model\. Results The results show that AI‑employee collaboration exerts a significant positive predictive effect on employee innovation behavior\. Self‑efficacy partially mediates the relationship between AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation behavior\. Moreover, servant leadership positively moderates the link between AI‑employee collaboration and self‑efficacy and further strengthens the indirect predictive effect of AI‑employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior through self‑efficacy\. Discussion This research enriches existing literature by providing incremental empirical evidence for the internal cognitive mechanism and contextual boundary of AI‑driven employee innovation\. Theoretically, it unpacks the cognitive “black box” connecting AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation and identifies servant leadership as a key situational contingency factor\. Practically, these findings deliver concrete, actionable managerial insights for digitally transforming organizations to leverage AI tools and unlock employees’ innovative potential\.

## [Measuring a scaffold from inside: an operator\-authored self\-measurement harness for a constitutional runtime over a hosted language model](../publications/35f6af41941254e3dd82.md)

Richard Dobson

Interactive intelligent systems constructed over hosted large language models cannot retrain the substrate on which they depend, and so their designers enforce a named epistemology at the surrounding scaffold layer\. A difficulty follows that has received little methodological attention: when quality regresses, the regression frequently belongs to the scaffold rather than the substrate, and identifying it requires instruments that measure the scaffold itself rather than the model beneath it\. This article reports one such instrument set, added to a live constitutional runtime between 17 and 18 July 2026 and extended with a production drift observer on 19 August 2026, and situates it as a reusable design pattern\. The layer comprises six components—operator\-authored adversarial batteries held as versioned regression fixtures, deterministic pattern screens encoding named defects, an emission quarantine that retains failure evidence as a first\-class object, an instrument\-health monitor issuing autonomous handoffs, continuous\-integration delivery tripwires, and an observe\-only production drift detector that accumulates a hand\-labelling corpus from live traffic without altering any replies\. Eight falsifiable harness predictions are stated \(H1 through H8\), each named against a specific runtime carrier—a code path, a database table, or a typed field—and each paired with an explicit falsification condition; their relationship to the eight pre\-registered outcome predictions \(F1 through F8\) of a companion architecture paper is stated in a dedicated reconciliation section, since the harness reported here is the instrument set on which those outcome predictions depend\. Of the eight, five \(H1, H2, H3, H5, H7\) carry dated on\-platform observations and are reported in a dedicated observed subsection; three \(H4, H6, H8\) are prospective—predictions about experiments that have not yet occurred—and are reported separately under that label, so that no reader mistakes the distribution of evidence\. The predictions are offered for adversarial replication under an honest empirical frame rather than as settled results: the batteries were authored by the platform’s operator, classification is not independent, and the number of platforms studied is one\. The discussion states a narrow priority claim, distinguishes the enforcement point of composition\-time assertion from adjacent techniques, extends the pattern to the governance of learning loops—a scaffold that adapts must be measured by the same discipline that measures a scaffold that enforces—and argues that the interaction properties a reader encounters, an observation lock and per\-turn provenance grounding, become testable precisely because they are structurally enforced\.

## [Inteligencia artificial y aprendizaje significativo de las Ciencias Naturales: estrategias pedagógicas innovadoras desde Educación Inicial hasta Bachillerato General Unificado](../publications/35f788d1c1041ec36dc0.md)

Evert Francisco Salvador García; Johanna Leticia Macas Quezada; Jenny Rocio Arias Blacio; Cristhian Álvaro Quinteros Posligua; Elsa Janeth Magno Arboleda; Arturo Zuñiga

La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos representa una oportunidad para transformar las prácticas pedagógicas y fortalecer el aprendizaje significativo de las Ciencias Naturales en los diferentes niveles de escolaridad\. Sin embargo, su integración plantea desafíos relacionados con la formación docente, la pertinencia didáctica, la equidad tecnológica y la adaptación de los recursos digitales a las características cognitivas y evolutivas del estudiantado\. La presente investigación tiene como objetivo analizar la evidencia científica sobre la aplicación de la inteligencia artificial como estrategia de innovación pedagógica en la enseñanza de las Ciencias Naturales, desde Educación Inicial hasta Bachillerato General Unificado, considerando las particularidades del sistema educativo ecuatoriano\. Metodológicamente, se propone una revisión sistemática de la literatura, orientada por las directrices PRISMA 2020, mediante la identificación, selección y evaluación crítica de publicaciones científicas indexadas en Scopus, Web of Science y SciELO, correspondientes al período 2020\-2026\. El análisis contempla categorías relacionadas con el aprendizaje personalizado, la gamificación inteligente, la retroalimentación formativa, las simulaciones interactivas y el desarrollo del pensamiento científico\. Asimismo, examina las condiciones pedagógicas, tecnológicas y éticas que pueden favorecer o limitar su implementación\. Se espera que la sistematización de la evidencia permita identificar estrategias pertinentes para cada nivel educativo y reconocer vacíos de investigación\. El estudio busca aportar fundamentos científicos que orienten la integración responsable de la inteligencia artificial en las Ciencias Naturales, priorizando la mediación docente, la inclusión educativa y la construcción activa del conocimiento\.

## [Knowledge and Implementation of Perioperative Safety Standards Among Perioperative Nurses in a Nigerian Teaching Hospital: An Observational Study](../publications/36058dbb89a3e4835569.md)

The Operating Room Global \(TORG\); Dorcas Iyanuoluwa Odunlade; Myada A\. Ibrahim

Introduction: Surgical safety remains a critical concern globally due to the significant risk of adverse events during operative procedures and perioperative nurses play an important role in ensuring safe surgical care through adherence to these established safety standards\. Objective: The study assessed knowledge, and level of implementation of perioperative safety standards in the operating theatre of UNIOSUN Teaching Hospital, Osogbo, Osun State\. Method: An observational study design using a quantitative research method was used\. Data was collected using a self\-designed questionnaire developed by the World Health Organization \(WHO\) safety checklist and Association of Perioperative Nurses \(AORN\) guidelines\. Data was collected from 14 participants that represented both the sample size and target population\. Data was analyzed using descriptive statistics\. Results were presented in frequency tables, percentages and charts\. Results: Findings revealed that all participants \(14, 100%\) had good knowledge of perioperative safety standards\. 12\(85\.7%\) participants demonstrated a high level of implementation while 2\(14\.3%\) demonstrated low level\. Although high implementation was reported for several safety practices, the WHO surgical safety checklist and surgical smoke evacuation showed areas requiring improvement\. Conclusion: This study suggests that perioperative nurses had high formal exposure, strong knowledge of perioperative safety standards, and high self\-reported implementation, indicating a favorable foundation for safe surgical nursing practice\. However, published literature consistently shows that knowledge alone does not guarantee sustained compliance, and that stronger outcomes usually require continuing education, supportive leadership, teamwork, adequate resources, and audit\-based monitoring\. Keywords: Perioperative Nurses, Perioperative Safety Standards, Knowledge, Implementation\.

## [Participatorna priprava strategije za mlade z akcijskim načrtom avstrijske Štajerske](../publications/360a85945c43f40b06e9.md)

Martin Auferbauer; Arno Heimgartner; Thomas Lederer\-Hutsteiner

The Styrian Youth Strategy was developed through a participatory and evidence\-based process to provide a strategic framework for improving the living conditions of young people in Styria, Austria\. ## [Context\-Aware And Explainable Hate Speech Detection In Iraqi Social Media: A Framework For Parliamentary And Policy Analysis](../publications/360e4adb6efc7bf18c68.md)

Ali N\. Al\-Saadi

Overview: Concerns about hate speech and its implications for social cohesion, public discourse, and the safety of targeted communities have been intensified by the rapid expansion of social media, particularly in Iraq owing to its social, cultural, and linguistic diversity, as well as its experience of severe sectarian conflict and communal violence during 2006–2007\. Hence, it is important to examine social cohesion and harmful intergroup discourse in contemporary digital environments without assuming a direct causal relationship between past conflict and present\-day online hate speech\. Gap: Machine learning and Transformer\-based hate\-speech detection frameworks have significantly advanced in recent times; however, the reliable identification of hate speech in Iraqi social\-media discourse remains challenging since online communication in the country often involves dialectal variation, informal and non\-standard spelling, code\-mixing, sarcasm, implicit and coded expressions, and deliberate linguistic obfuscation\. These context\-dependent and dialect\-sensitive characteristics may not be adequately captured by generic language representations, and classification performance alone may fail to provide enough insight into model explainability, generalization across different forms of Iraqi online discourse, and robustness to linguistic manipulation\. Hence, there is a need for a framework that can combine contextual understanding, dialect sensitivity, explainability, and robustness for the Iraqi context\. Contributions: A context\-aware and explainable hate\-speech detection framework has been proposed in this study for deployment across Iraqi social media; the methodology of the proposed framework dynamically combines contextual and dialect\-specific information for hate\-speech classification by integrating Iraqi\-aware text preprocessing, contextual Transformer representations, dialect\-sensitive feature learning, and an adaptive fusion mechanism\. The system also incorporates Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) for identifying the linguistic elements contributing to model predictions; robustness analysis evaluates model behavior under realistic linguistic variations and obfuscation strategies\. In addition to the computational contribution, an interdisciplinary AI–policy framework is also incorporated, wherein anonymized and aggregated hate\-speech patterns can provide empirical evidence for parliamentary and public\-policy analysis\. The legislative and oversight role of the Iraqi Council of Representatives in addressing online hate speech was also examined in consideration of freedom of expression, privacy, explainability, responsible digital governance, and human oversight\. Conclusion: An integrated approach that connects Iraqi\-contextualized hate\-speech detection with explainable and robust artificial intelligence and parliamentary policy analysis has been proposed in this study, wherein AI is positioned as an empirical research and decision\-support instrument rather than a mechanism for automated censorship, punishment, or legal determination\. A combination of linguistic adaptation, contextual modeling, explainability, robustness assessment, and aggregated policy\-oriented evidence in the proposed methodology provides an experimentally testable and socially responsible foundation for analyzing hate speech in Iraqi social media and supporting evidence\-informed parliamentary and public\-policy analysis\.

## [Climate finance and SME environmental performance: testing adaptive green finance effectiveness theory under FinTech inclusion and policy uncertainty in Sri Lanka](../publications/361cd8a205cdd34d9b9a.md)

vidura perera; P\.M\.C\. Thilakerathne; Wasanthi Madurapperuma

Green finance has emerged as an important instrument for promoting sustainable development and supporting corporate environmental performance \(CEP\)\. However, its effectiveness remains uneven across developing economies, where financial constraints, limited technological capabilities, and economic policy uncertainty \(EPU\) may constrain firms’ ability to translate green financial resources into environmental outcomes\. Despite growing research on green finance, limited empirical evidence explains how technological capabilities, innovation mechanisms, and policy conditions jointly shape its effectiveness, particularly among small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) in developing countries\. To address this gap, this study develops and empirically tests the Adaptive Green Finance Effectiveness Theory \(AGFET\), which conceptualizes green finance effectiveness as a conditional resource\-conversion process shaped by technological enabling capabilities, innovation, and the policy environment\. Using primary cross\-sectional survey data collected from Sri Lankan SMEs operating in the manufacturing and service sectors, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\) to examine the relationships among green finance, CEP, green innovation, FinTech inclusion, and perceived economic policy uncertainty\. The findings reveal a significant positive association between green finance and CEP, both directly and indirectly through green innovation\. FinTech inclusion positively moderates the relationship between green finance and CEP, indicating a stronger positive association at higher levels of digital financial inclusion\. Conversely, perceived economic policy uncertainty negatively moderates this relationship, indicating that the positive association between green finance and CEP becomes weaker under greater perceived policy uncertainty\. Given the cross\-sectional and self\-reported nature of the data, these findings are interpreted as theory\-consistent associations rather than definitive causal effects\. Overall, the results provide empirical support for the conditional relationships proposed by AGFET and suggest that green\-finance effectiveness varies according to firms’ technological capabilities, innovation mechanisms, and perceived policy conditions\. The study contributes to sustainable finance research by advancing a context\-dependent explanation of green\-finance effectiveness and provides implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and SME managers in developing economies\.

## [Safe and sustainable by design \(SSbD\) for nanotechnology: scientific foundations, global policy perspectives, and industrial practice](../publications/3620a97a46523c855d5e.md)

Zayakhuu Gerelkhuu; Angela Serra; Seung\-Geun Park; Ishita Virmani; Aline Maria Zigiotto de Medeiros; Ariadna Acedo\-Terrades; Fotini Nikiforou; Achilleas Karakoltzidis; Seong\-Kwan Kim; Hyeonsoo Eom; Martin Himly; Dimitris G\. Mintis; Vasileios Minadakis; Dimitra‐Danai Varsou; Spyros Karakitsios; Dimosthenis Andreas Sarigiannis; Giusy del Giudice; Marcella Torres Maia; Michele Fratello; Anastasios G\. Papadiamantis; Panagiotis Isigonis; Anna Pohl; Sang Lee; Byung\-Tae Lee; Yang\-won Suh; Candida Lorusso; Francesco Dondero; Steffi Friedrichs; Antreas Afantitis; Haralambos Sarimveis; Eva‐Kathrin Schillinger; Peter Wick; Diego Stéfani T\. Martinez; Iseult Lynch; Thomas E\. Exner; Tommaso Serchi; Tae Hyun Yoon; Dario Greco

Safe and Sustainable by Design \(SSbD\) is emerging as a transformative framework for integrating safety and sustainability with functionality in nanotechnology\. This review provides a unified perspective on SSbD, bridging its scientific foundations, global policy developments, and industrial implementation\. We highlight how advances in mechanistic understanding of nanomaterial\-biological interactions enable earlier and more predictive safety assessment, supporting informed material design\. At the policy level, evolving regulatory and governance approaches across regions are shaping the integration of sustainability and safety requirements\. From an industrial perspective, SSbD is driving innovation in material substitution, process optimization, and lifecycle\-oriented design\. Despite this progress, challenges remain in standardization, data integration, and alignment between regulatory frameworks and industrial practice\. This work positions SSbD as a central paradigm for enabling responsible innovation and accelerating the transition toward safer and more sustainable nanotechnologies\.

## [A Leakage\-aware Cross\-dataset Evaluation Framework for IoT Intrusion Detection: BPSO Feature Selection, CORAL, and Bidirectional Transfer Analysis](../publications/36251903c7fdf97e6c09.md)

Karrar Imran Ogaili; Sundos F\. Jabbar; Asraa A\. Abd Al\-Ameer

Machine learning\-based intrusion detection systems \(IDS\) for the Internet of Things \(IoT\) are commonly evaluated using within\-dataset protocols that can conceal benchmark\-specific fitting, leakage, and failures under distribution shift\.This study presents a leakage\-aware, transfer\-aware, and reproducible evaluation framework combining duplicate and leakage auditing, train\-only preprocessing, mutual\-information \(MI\) ranking, binary particle swarm optimisation \(BPSO\), validation\-based threshold tuning, strict eight\-concept cross\-dataset mapping, optional correlation alignment \(CORAL\), and paired repeated\-seed analysis\.Five independent stratified holdout seeds were evaluated on resource\-bounded real\-data samples from Bot\-IoT and UNSW\-NB15\.On Bot\-IoT, near\-perfect accuracy and attack\-class F1 coexisted with much lower and unstable macro\-F1 because each test split contained only six or seven normal records; mean macro\-F1 ranged from 0\.6871 ± 0\.1314 for LR with MI\+BPSO to 0\.8590 ± 0\.0683 for RF\.On UNSW\-NB15, XGBoost \(0\.9219 ± 0\.0013\) and RF \(0\.9182 ± 0\.0031\) outperformed LR with MI\+BPSO \(0\.8738 ± 0\.0039\)\.No within\-dataset comparison was significant after Holm adjustment in the exploratory five\-seed Wilcoxon analysis\.Multiclass results further showed that the MI\-only feature pool outperformed the BPSO subset on both datasets\.Strict cross\-dataset macro\-F1 was substantially lower than within\-dataset performance\.Source\-only results ranged from 0\.3186 to 0\.4060 for Bot\-IoT to UNSW\-NB15 and from 0\.3009 to 0\.4457 in the reverse direction; CORAL improved macro\-F1 only for RF in the Bot\-IoT\-to\-UNSW\-NB15 direction and degraded macro\-F1 in the other five model\-direction comparisons\.Mean end\-to\-end single\-record latency was 8\.108 ms on Bot\-IoT and 5\.385 ms on UNSW\-NB15\.These findings support the methodological contribution: IoT\-IDS claims should be based on leakage\-controlled, class\-aware, uncertainty\-qualified, and transfer\-aware evidence rather than headline accuracy alone\.

## [Unraveling the K\+ transporter gene family in rice: evolution, subcellular localization, K\+ uptake activity, and transcriptional responses to salt stress](../publications/3634ecf28ff3eda6c235.md)

Tongyuan Yu; Jiadong Ren; Yue Yuan; Yuan Xue; Jie Liang; Zheyu Xu; Kejia Zhu; Mengying Jiang; Yunxia Fang; Xiaoqin Zhang; Yijun Meng; Zhonghua Chen; Quanxiang Tian; Dawei Xue

Rice is a global staple food crop, and its yield is seriously limited by soil salinity\. The high\-affinity K \+ transporter/K \+ uptake permease/K \+ transporter \(HAK/KUP/KT\) family of potassium transporters plays a pivotal role in K \+ homeostasis and plant salt tolerance\. However, their systematic characterization and functional relevance to salt tolerance in rice have not been clarified\. Here, we conducted genome\-wide identification and structural characterization of the HAK/KUP/KT family, assessed their expression profiles under salt stress, and examined their K \+ transport function\. In total, 27 OsHAK genes were identified in the rice genome, most of which exhibited salt\-responsive expression\. Yeast functional complementation assays confirmed that OsHAK11, OsHAK13, OsHAK23, OsHAK24, OsHAK25, and OsHAK26 can mediate K \+ absorption\. Among them, OsHAK11 and OsHAK25 showed relatively strong K \+ uptake ability\. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that OsHAK11 and OsHAK25 were located in the plasma membrane\. Our research systematically analyzed the sequence characteristics of the rice HAK gene family, examined their transcriptional responses to salt stress, and further evaluated the K \+ uptake capacity of HAK proteins\. These results provide a foundation for further elucidating the function of OsHAKs in plant salt tolerance\.

## [A RAG\-enhanced multi\-agent LLM/VLM framework for auditable and region\-aware structural health monitoring of a historic masonry structure](../publications/364803b875da4a7ae176.md)

Kemal Hacıefendioğlu; Volkan Kahya; Tunahan Aslan

Abstract Historic masonry structures require monitoring workflows that are non\-destructive, interpretable, and robust to field variability\. This paper presents a proof\-of\-concept, RAG\-enhanced structural health monitoring \(SHM\) workflow demonstrated on a single historic masonry minaret case study, in which a manager–orchestrator coordinates signal analysis, visual analysis, and cross\-modal fusion\. Vibration data from four sensors installed on this minaret are processed through a reproducible pipeline that includes data cleaning, PSD\-based baseline characterisation, adaptive windowing, robust normalisation, and anomaly screening with a 1D convolutional autoencoder trained on healthy reference data \(Measurements 1–12\), followed by evaluation on Measurements 13–20\. Localisation is strengthened through relation\-based autoencoders on sensor pairs and sensor\-to\-zone damage mapping\. In parallel, a VLM analyses sensor\-linked inspection images from the same case study, while a curated retrieval\-augmented structural memory package for the monitored minaret \(geometry, materials, baseline dynamics, FE notes, and inspection playbook\) supports context\-aware interpretation\. A three\-agent decision layer \(Agent A: LLM\+RAG, Agent B: VLM\+RAG, Agent C: fusion \+ RAG\) reconciles agreements and conflicts between signal\- and image\-derived evidence to produce case\-specific global and zone\-level risk assessments\. The study compares with\-RAG and without\-RAG analysis modes within this single deployment and reports structured, traceable outputs, including JSON artefacts, per\-image findings, per\-sensor summaries, narrative reports, and final risk maps\. Its main contribution is to demonstrate how signal\-derived anomalies, image\-derived evidence, and retrieval\-grounded structural memory can be combined within a traceable multi\-agent SHM workflow for one monitored historic masonry minaret\.

## [Risk Visualization With Petal\-X and Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Support Person\-Centered Care and Lifestyle Change in Cardiovascular Prevention: Qualitative Descriptive Study](../publications/36483e1ccfd3ad94590b.md)

Adrijana Svenšek; Diego Rojo; Mateja Lorber; Zalika Klemenc–Ketiš; Lucija Gosak; Katrien Verbert; Gregor Štiglic

Background: Cardiovascular diseases \(CVDs\) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality\. In primary prevention, effective communication of individual risk and support for behavior change are crucial\. Interactive risk visualizations can enhance understanding and engagement, while continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\) offers immediate feedback on the physiological effects of daily choices\. Objective: This study aimed to explore how patients at increased CVD risk and family medicine nurses perceive CVD risk visualization \(Petal\-X\) and the integration of real\-time glucose monitoring, with a focus on perceived person\-centered care \(PCC\), motivation, and lifestyle change\. This manuscript reports the qualitative phase of a larger sequential mixed methods study; the quantitative randomized controlled trial is reported separately\. Methods: Using total population \(census\) sampling within a closed, predefined trial cohort, we invited every eligible patient who had completed the intervention arm of a parallel randomized controlled trial and every eligible registered nurse providing preventive consultations at the same single community health center in central Slovenia who had been familiarized with the intervention and with the Petal\-X dashboard; 6 patients at increased CVD risk who had used the Petal\-X dashboard in combination with CGM, and 6 nurses familiar with the intervention, took part, and interviews were conducted between September and December 2024\. Data were collected through individual, face\-to\-face semistructured interviews that explored perceptions of the visualization, real\-time glucose monitoring, and lifestyle change\. Interviews were audio\-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed by inductive qualitative content analysis within a qualitative descriptive design; coding continued until code saturation and data adequacy were judged to have been reached\. Results: The analysis produced 11 subcategories, which were grouped into 4 categories, with an overarching theme running across them: visualization and digital tools as support for PCC to enhance motivation and lifestyle change in individuals at risk of CVD\. Patients and nurses reported that personalized visual displays improved understanding of risk factors, facilitated dialogue and shared decision\-making, and increased patients&\#x27; sense of involvement, responsibility, and control, although the 2 groups differed in emphasis: patients foregrounded personal meaning and self\-regulation, whereas nurses foregrounded communication and fit with the consultation workflow\. CGM was perceived as particularly motivating by linking behavior \(food, activity, and stress\) to real\-time glucose changes, encouraging dietary and activity adjustments that some participants maintained after the intervention\. Key barriers included variable digital literacy \(especially among older users\), fear or mistrust of technology, the attentional burden of continuous monitoring, potential information overload, workflow integration needs, and affordability or accessibility of CGM\. Conclusions: Interactive CVD risk visualization Petal\-X, especially when complemented by CGM, was perceived as a meaningful support for PCC and a driver of motivation and lifestyle change in primary prevention\. Implementation should address training, usability, integration into routine workflows, and equity of access\.

## [AI literacy in student translation practices: evidence from ChatGPT use in Hong Kong](../publications/365813feee4030ab24fb.md)

Hao YIN; Liu Jian\-wen; Mengyao Qi; Zeping Huang

The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\), such as ChatGPT, is reshaping translation practices by enabling dynamic human–AI interaction and placing new demands on users\. However, less is known about how students develop the competencies required to critically and responsibly engage with GenAI in translation contexts\. This study investigates students’ AI literacy through a multidimensional framework comprising knowledge, usage, evaluation, affect, and ethics\. A mixed\-methods design was employed, combining questionnaire data from 146 university students in Hong Kong with semi\-structured interviews with 10 participants\. Quantitative results indicate a generally positive but uneven AI literacy profile: students report high levels of usage, knowledge, and affect, relatively lower evaluation competence, and relatively low score of ethics dimension\. Correlation analysis further reveals a clustered structure among knowledge, usage, evaluation, and affect, whereas ethics is weakly associated with all other dimensions\. Qualitative findings further illuminate this imbalance\. While students actively integrate ChatGPT into translation tasks and demonstrate strong emotional engagement, their evaluative practices are mediated by prompt design and prior knowledge\. More critically, ethics emerges as the least internalized dimension, characterized by a gap between awareness and actual implementation in practice\. This study contributes to AI literacy research by demonstrating its structurally uneven and partially decoupled nature in AI\-mediated translation\. It further reconceptualizes ethics as a structurally under\-integrated dimension and highlights the interactional and input\-dependent nature of evaluative competence\.

## [Diagnostic Delay of Thoracic Meningiomas Due to Anchoring Bias Toward Lumbar Degenerative Disorders](../publications/36697d79f27f8a56f510.md)

Fatih Çalış; Naci Balak

In recent years, the frequency of surgery due to lumbar degenerative disorders has increased\. Thoracic spinal tumors are susceptible to delayed diagnosis because their symptoms often overlap with those of lumbar degenerative disorders\. Studies have shown that the time from symptom onset to diagnosis in intraspinal meningiomas averages 6\-23 months, with delays of up to 14 years reported\. Similarly, we observed delayed diagnosis in four female patients with thoracic intraspinal masses in the past year\. Two patients were 75 years old, and the others were 71 and 57 years old\. Their symptoms had been present for 1, 2, 3, and 6 years, respectively\. Since spinal meningiomas occur more frequently in women, typically between the ages of 49\-54, and predominantly in the thoracic region, careful history taking, physical examination, and appropriate radiological evaluation in elderly female patients with back pain and lower extremity symptoms may help avoid overtreatment\.

## [Enabling Efficient Serverless Inference Serving for LLM \(Large Language Model\) in the Cloud](../publications/3676796d576daa1d7f68.md)

Himel Ghosh

This review report examines the problem of cold\-start latency in serverless inference for large language models \(LLMs\) and surveys recent systems that address it, with a particular focus on ServerlessLLM\. In serverless environments, loading multi\-hundred\-gigabyte LLM checkpoints and initializing GPU resources can dominate end\-to\-end latency, making real\-time applications such as conversational agents and translation services difficult to deploy cost\-efficiently\. The report first summarizes the cold\-start problem and common mitigation strategies in today&\#x27;s Function\-as\-a\-Service \(FaaS\) platforms, including container warming, host\-side checkpoint caching, and cluster\-level storage servers\. It then reviews the design of ServerlessLLM, which exploits underutilized multi\-tier storage in GPU servers, a loading\-optimized checkpoint format, live inference migration based on token\-level state transfer, and a startup\-time\-aware model scheduler\. Additional methods from recent literature, such as RainbowCake&\#x27;s layered container caching, and the cold\-start handling mechanisms of major cloud providers are also discussed\. Drawing on the evaluation presented in the original work, the report highlights that multi\-tier checkpoint loading and live migration reduce model startup time by up to 6\-8× compared to conventional formats, and deliver up to 28× lower startup latency than Ray Serve for large models in realistic traces\. The review concludes by outlining open challenges and future directions, including integrating model compression, multi\-level inference pipelines, and advanced memory\-offloading techniques to further improve the scalability and efficiency of serverless LLM inference\.

## [Non\-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems](../publications/367b40860663e25822c6.md)

Mohsen Amidzadeh; Lauri Viitasaari; Mario Di Francesco

Stochastic optimization \(SO\) plays a central role in decision\-making under uncertainty\. Among SO problems, time\-varying stochastic optimization \(TV\-SO\) is particularly important due to its applications in adaptive control and machine learning\. Non\-parametric approaches have been proposed for time\-varying deterministic optimization; however, they have not been developed for their stochastic counterparts\. This work addresses that gap by developing a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus\. This framework yields non\-parametric optimality conditions for SO problems with stochastic decisions and supports the design of a scalable deep\-learning algorithm that is insensitive to the parameterization dimension\. This algorithm, called the Stochastic Path Follower \(SPF\), is applied to two important problems under distribution drift, namely least\-squares recovery and logistic regression\. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state\-of\-the\-art learning\-based and gradient\-based methods in both performance and scalability\.

## [Molecular detection and multilocus genotyping of Toxoplasma gondii in archived stray\-cat fecal DNA from central and western Thailand](../publications/367fd3f3335a2bfd789a.md)

Ruenruetai Udonsom; Aongart Mahittikorn; Tanjila Hasan; Yoshifumi Nishikawa; Supaluk Popruk

Background and Aim: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally important zoonotic protozoan, and felids serve as definitive hosts\. Although molecular studies have demonstrated substantial genetic diversity of T\. gondii in feline populations, information from Thailand remains limited, particularly for stray cats in central and western regions\. This retrospective study aimed to determine the prevalence of T\. gondii DNA and characterize multilocus genotype profiles in archived DNA extracted from stray\-cat fecal samples collected in Nakhon Nayok and Kanchanaburi provinces, Thailand, in 2013\. Materials and Methods: A total of 120 archived fecal DNA samples were analyzed, comprising 80 samples from Nakhon Nayok and 40 from Kanchanaburi\. Conventional polymerase chain reaction \(PCR\) targeting the B1 gene was used for molecular detection\. Positive amplicons were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and compared with GenBank reference sequences using Basic Local Alignment Search Tool\. Sequence\-confirmed samples were subsequently analyzed using multilocus nested PCR\-restriction fragment length polymorphism \(Mn\-PCR\-RFLP\)\. Reference strains RH, PRU, and VEG represented clonal types I, II, and III, respectively\. Differences in PCR positivity between provinces were assessed using Fisher’s exact test\. Results: Thirteen of 120 samples \(10\.8%\) were positive for T\. gondii DNA, including 8/80 \(10\.0%\) from Nakhon Nayok and 5/40 \(12\.5%\) from Kanchanaburi; the difference was not significant \(p = 0\.758\)\. B1 sequences showed 94\.52%–98\.70% identity with reference sequences\. Multilocus genotyping was successful in four of 13 positive samples \(30\.8%\)\. Two type I profiles and one type III profile were identified in Kanchanaburi, whereas one probable type II profile was identified in Nakhon Nayok\. No mixed, atypical, or ToxoDB\#9 profiles were detected among the four successfully characterized samples\. Conclusion: This study provides preliminary historical molecular evidence of classical T\. gondii clonal\-lineage profiles in stray\-cat fecal DNA from central and western Thailand\. However, the limited genotyping success prevents estimation of genotype frequencies or regional distribution\. Detection of T\. gondii DNA in feces should not be interpreted as evidence of viable oocysts, active shedding, infectivity, or current public health risk\. Larger prospective studies using fresh samples, quantitative PCR, and higher\-resolution genotyping are warranted\. Keywords: archived DNA, feline toxoplasmosis, molecular epidemiology, multilocus genotyping, stray cats, Thailand, Toxoplasma gondii, toxoplasmosis\.

## [Advanced Herbal Approaches to Diabetes and Metabolic Disorders: Current Status and Future Prospects](../publications/369094125a8b64b69ca5.md)

Ajita S\. Kesharwani; Palak Ghanshyam Rahangdale; Rashmi Khanijau; Naveen Jain; Hriddhi  Chakraborty

Diabetes and related metabolic issues are major health problems around the world\. In many cases, blood sugar is not well controlled\. Insulin may not work as it should\. Levels of fats in the blood can also become abnormal\. Over time, oxidative stress builds up\. Mild inflammation tends to continue too\. Many people do benefit from common drug therapy\. Even so, some medicines lead to side effects\. In other cases, the response is not strong enough\. Because these conditions come from more than one cause, interest in herbal options has grown\. Researchers are examining plant compounds as possible supportive choices\. This review explains the current status of herbal approaches\. It also looks at what might happen next\. Topics include the main chemicals found in these plants\. It covers possible ways those chemicals may act in the body\. It then summarizes what clinical studies report and how ready the evidence is for everyday use\. The review also groups plant chemical types into several categories\. The review covers both lab work and tests in people\. It looks at medicinal plants as well as specific plant chemicals\. Absorption is a key focus\. Safety is discussed too, including side risks and possible clashes between herbs and drugs\. Product strength is another concern\. Extracts can differ a lot between one batch and the next\.New ways to deliver these compounds are also included\. The text mentions nanoparticles, phytosomes, liposomes, and other carriers\. These systems may improve water solubility\. They may also help compounds stay stable\. Better uptake in the body is another point\. If uptake improves, the effects in treatment could be stronger\.For future work, the authors highlight multi target strategies\. They also bring up metabolomics and plans that can be adjusted for each person\. They suggest that artificial intelligence could aid trial design and data review\. They emphasize the need for products that stay consistent and are well standardized\. More toxicology studies are needed\. More work on pharmacokinetics is also important\. Finally, clinical trials should be planned better so herbal options for metabolic problems can be judged with solid evidence\.

## [Sueño y dolor lumbar crónico: una dimensión clínica infravalorada con implicaciones pronósticas y terapéuticas](../publications/369bfdf970033b15d167.md)

Juan Fernando García Henares; Cristian Sánchez\-Barros; Erika Torres San Narciso; Carlos Morales; Manuel Alejandro Sánchez\-García

Background: Chronic low back pain \(CLBP\) is the leading cause of years lived with disability worldwide\. Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent among patients with CLBP and may contribute to pain persistence, disability, and poorer treatment outcomes\. Despite this, sleep remains an underrecognized component of routine clinical assessment\. Objective: To review the available evidence on the relationship between sleep and CLBP, their shared pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical relevance, and implications for assessment and management in pain units\. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar\. Systematic reviews, meta\-analyses, clinical trials, observational studies, and clinical practice guidelines addressing the relationship between sleep and CLBP, underlying mechanisms, and therapeutic strategies were included\. Results: Sleep disturbances affect up to 73 % of patients with CLBP\. Poor sleep quality is associated with worse clinical outcomes, greater disability, and a higher likelihood of central sensitization\. The relationship between sleep and pain is bidirectional and involves alterations in endogenous pain modulation, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis dysregulation, and neuroinflammatory processes\. Systematic assessment of sleep using structured clinical interviews and validated questionnaires may help identify patients with more complex clinical profiles\. Among available interventions, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia \(CBT\-I\) has the strongest supporting evidence\. Several pharmacological treatments may improve sleep\-related outcomes; however, their direct analgesic effects in CLBP appear limited\. Conclusions: Sleep represents a clinically relevant dimension with important prognostic and therapeutic implications in CLBP\. Routine assessment of sleep may help identify patients with greater clinical complexity and support a more individualized multimodal treatment approach\. Integrating sleep evaluation into the routine management of CLBP may contribute to improved clinical and functional outcomes\.

## [Physical education and the formation of al\-Insān al\-Kāmil: integrative frameworks in classical islamic philosophical thought](../publications/369e0310f6a834cb7364.md)

Refat Asaad Fathy Hodwa Eid; Zi Jian Zhao

Abstract Physical education has rarely been examined through the perspective of classical Islamic philosophy\. Although Muslim philosophers did not develop physical education as a separate academic discipline, they discussed bodily cultivation within broader accounts of ethics, medicine, and human development\. This study explores how these discussions can contribute to contemporary thinking about physical education\. The study uses qualitative conceptual analysis and textual interpretation of selected classical Islamic philosophical works\. It draws on primary Arabic sources and established scholarly translations, focusing on the writings of Ibn Sina, Al\-Razi, Al\-Farabi, Al\-Kindi, Ibn Miskawayh, and Nasir al\-Din Al\-Tusi\. The analysis identifies recurring concepts related to the body, health, moral development, and education, and compares them with contemporary discussions in physical education and educational philosophy\. The findings suggest that two concepts, Iʿtidāl \(balance and moderation\) and Takāmul \(integration or wholeness\), play a central role in the classical Islamic understanding of human development\. Across the texts examined, physical activity is connected not only to health but also to character formation, self\-discipline, and social responsibility\. The study also identifies several points of comparison with contemporary ideas such as physical literacy, holistic education, and values\-based learning, while recognizing important differences in their philosophical foundations\. This study offers a theoretical framework for understanding physical education through a neglected strand of the Islamic philosophical tradition\. Rather than presenting empirical findings, it highlights concepts that may broaden current discussions about the aims of physical education and provide a basis for future research, particularly in culturally diverse and Muslim\-majority educational contexts\. It should be noted that classical Islamic philosophers did not develop a theory of physical education as a discrete institutional field\. Rather, this study reconstructs a coherent philosophical framework for bodily cultivation from texts in which physical practice was embedded within broader accounts of ethics, medicine, and human formation\.

## [HERStory: development and process evaluation of a manualized drama therapy intervention for women with breast cancer](../publications/369f8fdf6d076e2caec7.md)

Katrin Röhlig; Christina Vedar de Abreu; Cinzia Rosati; Dilem Doruk Becerik; Susann Kobus

Abstract Despite increasing recognition of creative arts therapies within psycho\-oncology, manualized drama therapy interventions remain scarce\. This article introduces HERStory, a six\-session drama therapy group intervention for women with breast cancer, combining the Heroine’s Journey with role work, dramatic enactment, embodiment\-oriented techniques, and resource\-oriented approaches, and presents an initial process evaluation\. The HERStory study was conducted as a prospective, non\-randomized study with a pre–post–post design\. Process evaluation used the newly developed Drama Therapy Process Observation Instrument \(SK\-BTP\), a 43\-item observer\-rated instrument assessing eight dimensions of drama therapy group processes\. Ratings were completed by an independent drama therapist\. Descriptive analyses included 14 participants completing the intervention\. Overall process quality demonstrated a positive trajectory\. Mean scores increased from M = 3\.56 to M = 4\.31 in Group 1 and from M = 3\.63 to M = 4\.51 in Group 3, whereas Group 2 maintained consistently high scores \(M = 4\.19–4\.30\)\. Process openness reached relatively high levels early, whereas role flexibility, thematic development, and symbolic depth increased across sessions\. The findings provide preliminary insights into the implementation of HERStory and the development of core drama therapy processes across the six sessions\. The manual offers a transparent and reproducible intervention for future research and clinical practice\. Further studies with larger samples and controlled designs are warranted to evaluate its effectiveness and applicability in other populations\. Trial registration : German Clinical Trials Register \(DRKS\), DRKS00036673, registered 15 April 2025\.

## [Using active acoustics from an underwater glider to investigate the relationship between acoustic target locations and coastal ocean fronts off the Pacific Northwest coast](../publications/36b0f743662aa3605dea.md)

Otavio A\. P\. Mendes; John A\. Barth; A\. Erofeev; Jace Marquardt; Brian K\. Wells; David D\. Huff; Anthony M\. Cossio

Traditional ship\-based sampling has provided valuable information about marine ecosystems\. However, repeated high\-resolution measurements are increasingly necessary to capture dynamic biophysical processes\. In this study, we used active, multi\-frequency acoustics from an autonomous underwater ocean glider to examine diel vertical migration and the relationship between zooplankton and fish aggregations to coastal fronts off the coast of Washington in the Pacific Northwest\. The objectives of this study were: \(1\) to examine the reliability of glider acoustics by comparing it with acoustic data from a ship; \(2\) to assess diel migration patterns over the continental shelf; \(3\) to relate the spatial and temporal distributions of zooplankton and fish to frontal positions\. Sampling occurred in late spring/early summer across both coastal upwelling and buoyancy\-driven freshwater fronts\. A Slocum glider, equipped with sensors for conductivity, temperature, depth, bio\-optical properties, including chlorophyll and colored dissolved organic matter \(CDOM\) fluorescence, dissolved oxygen, and multi\-frequency acoustics \(67, 120, 200 kHz\), completed 10 cross\-front transects over 1–2 weeks\. One cross\-shelf transect was sampled concurrently with the NOAA Ship Bell M\. Shimada to enable direct comparison of active acoustic profiles\. The glider\- and ship\-based acoustic observations were consistent \(R 2 = 0\.87\), confirming the glider system’s reliability\. Diel vertical migration was not clearly resolved, mainly due to limitations of frequency differentiation; however, distinct vertical partitioning was evident, with “fish” targets occupying the upper water column and “zooplankton” the deeper layers\. Both groups were predominantly distributed offshore of the upwelling front\. This study demonstrates the potential and challenges of using multi\-sensor autonomous underwater vehicles in upwelling regions to resolve fine\-scale biophysical patterns, highlighting their value as a complementary tool for traditional ship surveys\.

## [Towards a Relational Sociology of Law: Rethinking Practical Experience and Institutional Design in Asia](../publications/36b76591135693bbb01d.md)

Weidong Ji

As is well known, the cornerstone of modern Western jurisprudence is the autonomous individual\.The intellectual origins of the concept of individuality can be traced back to ancient Greek philosophy, particularly to the ontological distinction between &quot;matter&quot; and &quot;consciousness,&quot; as well as Socrates&\#x27; sceptical differentiation between earthly, imperfect knowledge \(doxa\) and heavenly &quot;true knowledge&quot; \(epistēmē\), which together form a realist category of binary opposition\.Since the Renaissance, this line of thought gradually evolved into Descartes&\#x27; mind\-body dualism and the principle of subjectivity in the bourgeois revolutions\.Following a reductionist methodology, it gave rise to an atomistic view of the individual, liberal ideas, the legal principle of party autonomy, and a series of institutional designs and axiomatic systems of law aimed at safeguarding natural and fundamental rights inherent in human beings\.In sharp contrast, the fundamental principle of traditional Chinese order lies in the unity of Heaven and humanity \(tian ren he yi\) and reciprocity in social intercourse \(li shang wang lai\), giving rise to a so\-called relation\-based society that transcends the dichotomies of matter and consciousness, object and subject\. 1 Although the global movement of &quot;law and modernization&quot; and &quot;law and development&quot; made individual rights a basic goal of social transformation in China and other Asian societies, with far\-reaching influence, Clifford Geertz argued that this Western conception of the individual also draws boundaries around the person, reducing him to an atomistic particle set in opposition to the natural and social background\.Thus, however powerful this individualism may be, from the perspective of the world&\#x27;s major civilizations and diverse cultures, it remains, after all, a particularistic idea \(see Geertz, 1974, p\. 31\)\.The emergence of this view marks the self\-reflection of 20th\-century academia \(not limited to anthropology and sociology\) on the Enlightenment movement that had surged since the 17th century, as well as its search for new ideals of social justice and more inclusive institutional arrangements\.For the simple sum of individual rationalities does not lead to collective rationality; indeed, negotiation aimed at maximizing individual interests often excludes the most reasonable public choices from the set of options\.It is therefore necessary to break down individual boundaries and, by redefining the status and role of the individual, achieve other\-oriented and collectively oriented communicative rationality, as well as social cooperation based on the principle of reciprocity and mutual benefit\.

## [Structural Evolution in Paraelectric–Antiferroelectric Phase Transitions of Tungsten Bronze\-Type K2NdNb5O15](../publications/36d1801aad57fa8b4648.md)

Hodaka Abe; Sou Yasuhara; Takuya Hoshina

Abstract Tungsten bronze \(TB\)\-type K2RNb5O15 \(R: rare\-earth element\) compounds exhibit antiferroelectric \(AFE\) properties and are promising for energy\-storage and high\-voltage applications\. However, the structural origin of their antiferroelectricity remains unclear, hindering the establishment of rational design principles\. Here, we investigated the structural evolution of K2NdNb5O15 from its aristotype P4/mbm phase to the AFE phase by combining high\-resolution synchrotron X\-ray and neutron powder diffraction experiments with machine\-learning\-assisted molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations\. The diffraction data revealed three successive phase transitions between 300 and 600 K, with a previously undetected intermediate phase lying between the aristotype P4/mbm and AFE phases\. The MD simulations and Rietveld analysis consistently identified the soft modes that drive the structural phase transitions from the P4/mbm phase to the AFE phase\. Condensation of a NbO6 octahedral tilting mode gives rise to the intermediate phase, whereas out\-of\-phase twisting of NbO6 octahedra and antipolar displacements of Nd and Nb cations emerge together at the transition to the AFE phase\. These findings resolve the multiple structural distortions responsible for the antiferroelectricity in K2NdNb5O15 and provide microscopic insight into the design of TB\-type AFEs\.

## [Attention\-based and contrastive deep learning models for real\-time anomaly detection in Edge\-IIoT networks](../publications/36d61b8f9c89a8232690.md)

Ahmad Reda Alzighaibi; Adam Marks; Abdullateef I\. Almudaifer; Hossam Magdy Balaha; Nadhir Ben Halima; Mostafa A\. Elhosseini

The rapid expansion of Industrial Internet of Things \(IIoT\) systems has increased the cyber\-attack surface of critical infrastructure, requiring intrusion detection systems \(IDS\) that are accurate, robust, and efficient under resource\-constrained edge environments\. Traditional approaches suffer from limited generalization, poor handling of class imbalance, and lack of statistical reliability and interpretability\. This paper proposes a modular deep learning framework integrating TabTransformer, Variational Autoencoder, and contrastive learning, combined through multi\-trial training \(N = 10\), statistical aggregation, and F1\-weighted ensemble fusion\. Experiments on the Edge\-IIoTset dataset \( $$\\approx $$ 1\.9M samples, 15 classes\) achieve 97\.60% accuracy and 83\.42% F1\-score, with multi\-trial aggregation reducing the uncertainty associated with single\-run reporting\. From a computational perspective, training is performed using large\-batch optimization \(batch size = 16,384\) with early stopping \(patience = 50\), while inference requires a single forward pass per model followed by constant\-time fusion\. The framework operates on compact tabular inputs \( $$\\approx $$ 96 features\), resulting in a lightweight memory footprint \(on the order of a few megabytes per model\) and enabling efficient deployment\. The inference pipeline processes batches in a few milliseconds on GPU\-class hardware, ensuring real\-time responsiveness for high\-throughput IIoT traffic streams while maintaining low computational overhead and energy demand\. Ablation analysis shows that removing ensemble fusion reduces F1\-score by approximately 1%:2%, while eliminating multi\-trial aggregation significantly increases variance, highlighting the importance of statistical robustness\. Furthermore, SHAP\-based explainable AI \(XAI\) provides insight into feature\-level contributions, enhancing transparency and supporting human\-in\-the\-loop security operations\. Overall, the proposed framework achieves a balanced trade\-off between predictive performance and computational efficiency, delivering a reproducible, interpretable, and deployment\-oriented IDS solution for real\-time IIoT environments\. Practical deployment considerations, including model export to ONNX format and quantization for edge hardware, are outlined as immediate next steps\.

## [Cross\-Border Gathering of Electronic Evidence in Criminal Cases: The Experience of the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China](../publications/36debc571c8332a979d0.md)

Natalia Olegovna Nikuradze

Over the past few years, the introduction of digital technologies into various areas of governance has accelerated markedly\. The development and improvement of the legal framework governing international cooperation among the BRICS countries on cross\-border gathering of electronic evidence is of strategic importance in combating transnational IT crime, which poses a threat to their economic and national security\. This article examines legal mechanisms for crossborder access to and collection of electronic evidence in criminal proceedings in the light of China’s experience, and on this basis proposes ideas for standardizing a single cooperation mechanism responding to requests for mutual legal assistance in cross\-border access to electronic evidence within the BRICS\.
