## [Beyond the Badge](../publications/36ec3d0e6f872a769faf.md)

Robert Szabó

Microcredentials are increasingly positioned as flexible alternatives to traditional degrees in a rapidly evolving labour market\. However, their proliferation has raised fundamental questions about their meaning, comparability, and value as signals of capability\. This article shifts the focus from growth narratives to the problem of trust: under what conditions do microcredentials function as credible indicators of skill? Drawing on current literature and industry perspectives, the paper argues that the effectiveness of microcredentials depends on three interrelated factors: robust educational design grounded in clearly defined learning outcomes, rigorous and verifiable assessment that demonstrates applied competence, and the reputational authority of the issuing body\. Without these elements, microcredentials risk contributing to credential inflation, where an abundance of low\-stakes certifications undermines their signalling power\. The analysis highlights a critical distinction between participation\-based certificates and evidence\-based credentials aligned with established models such as ISO/IEC 17024 \(International Organization for Standardization, 2026\)\. The article concludes that the future value of microcredentials lies not in their volume, but in their ability to function as trusted evidence systems that support meaningful skill development and labour market transparency\.

## [Can AI Assistants Trigger Mental Illness in Users?](../publications/36f13dac0d03eed6114d.md)

Eleftherios P\. Diamandis

As conversational artificial intelligence models become ubiquitous fixtures in professional and personal workflows, the nature of human\-tool interaction has the potential to gradually shift from mechanical utility to parasocial dependency\. While existing literature frequently addresses adverse events related to data privacy, algorithmic bias, and intellectual deskilling, the pathopsychological sequelae of sustained AI integration remain largely unexamined\. Here, we describe and preliminarily characterize the AI Assistant Syndrome, a human psychiatric construct encompassing acute chatbot\-induced anxiety and mental exhaustion\. This preliminary description will guide future systematic investigations to recognize, prevent, and treat this syndrome\.

## [Quantifying single\-cell biomechanics: a comparative analysis of experimental methods and theoretical models](../publications/36f7525f898ccba5b071.md)

Dipta Saha; Raisa Akhtaruzzaman; Sumaya Sharmin; Hyejin Moon; Ashfaq Adnan

This review presents a comprehensive overview of methodologies employed to measure and quantify the biomechanical properties of single cells, focusing on techniques that provide insights into cellular deformation and force response\. Understanding cell mechanics is crucial for advancing our knowledge of cellular behavior, disease progression, and therapeutic innovation in contexts such as cancer metastasis, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine\. We critically examine five primary experimental platforms: atomic force microscopy \(AFM\), dielectrophoresis \(DEP\), optical tweezers, micropipette aspiration, and hydrodynamic\-induced deformation\. For each method, we detail the underlying theoretical frameworks, experimental configurations, advantages, limitations, and application scope\. Contact\-based techniques \(AFM, micropipette aspiration\) provide high\-resolution measurements of localized stiffness and viscoelasticity, while non\-contact approaches \(DEP, hydrodynamic stretching, optical tweezers\) enable high\-throughput analysis with minimal physical disruption\. Furthermore, we evaluate the mechanical models used to extract biomechanical parameters and highlight modern data extraction processes, including automated image analysis\. Crucially, this review addresses the significant discrepancies in measured properties that arise across different methods due to varying loading rates, boundary conditions, and model assumptions\. By synthesizing these experimental and theoretical considerations, this review aims to guide the standardization and refinement of single\-cell biomechanics for both fundamental research and translational biomedical applications\.

Rostika Flora; Samsuryadi; Mohammad Zulkarnain; Nur Alam Fajar; Yuliarti; Derry Alamsyah; Annisah Biancika Jasmine; Prihatini Dini Novitasari; Dindi Paizer; Danny Kusuma Aerosta

Stunting remains a major public health challenge, while recent facial\-image studies report near\-perfect CNN performance under conditions that may not reflect real\-world deployment\.This study proposes a sensitivity\-analysis framework characterizing how six factors, within\-subject correlation, pseudo\-capture augmentation, evaluation\-set augmentation, training\-set augmentation, class resampling, and natural class distribution, affect reported performance\.EfficientNet\-B0 pretrained on ImageNet served as baseline across seven dataset\-scheme comparisons and three optimizers using 190 facial images from three Indonesian health centers\.Within\-subject correlation, examined through leakage of transformed derivatives across splits rather than independently captured repeats, was the dominant source of inflation, raising F2\-score by over 22% across all optimizers and establishing subject\-disjoint splitting as a minimum requirement\.Remaining comparisons were each confounded by simultaneous changes in sample size, augmentation, or class distribution: SGD stayed stable under reduced training volume, while Adam and AdamW repeatedly collapsed toward near\-zero specificity, indicating adaptive optimizers depend more on training volume to avoid degenerate behavior\.Under natural imbalance, dynamic thresholding collapsed to zero specificity, whereas Weighted CE with a static threshold preserved non\-zero performance for both classes, yielding F2\-score 65\.37%, sensitivity 74\.93%, specificity 36\.38%\.Extending this to AlexNet, ResNet34, ResNet\-50, and MambaVision\-T showed no single architecture dominating: MambaVision\-T led on sensitivity and F2\-score, AlexNet on accuracy, and ResNet34 on specificity, each trading off F2\-score\.Wide, overlapping confidence intervals indicate these differences are descriptive rather than definitive\.Evaluation protocol and optimizer choice strongly affect reported performance, while architecture choice trades sensitivity against specificity without resolving the low\-specificity limitation\.

## [Android embodiment with facial mimicry may enhance emotional responses during conversations with AI agents](../publications/370077b1fbd5a548e560.md)

Wataru Sato; Naoya Kawamura; Koh Shimokawa; Yasutaka Kubota; Takashi Minato

The potential of artificial intelligence \(AI\) agents to engage in emotional conversations with humans is attracting increasing attention\. Previous studies suggested that conversational agents powered by large language models such as ChatGPT can engage in emotionally competent conversations with humans\. However, whether verbal communication alone is sufficient or whether nonverbal communication might exert additive effects on emotional conversations remains unknown\. We conducted an experiment to examine whether android embodiment influenced emotional responses during interactions with conversational AI agents\. Participants engaged in positive emotional conversations with ChatGPT via the interface of either an android robot exhibiting facial mimicry or a blank display\. We measured their emotional experiences in terms of valence and arousal, as well as facial electromyography of the corrugator supercilii and zygomaticus major muscles and skin conductance level during conversations\. Participants reported significantly more positive valence ratings, and showed greater zygomaticus major EMG activity when interacting with the android than with the display\. No significant effects were observed for arousal, corrugator EMG activity, or skin conductance level\. These findings provide initial evidence that android embodiment may contribute to enhanced positive emotional responses during conversations with AI agents\.

## [GR\-OPD: Group\-Relative Sequence Credit for On\-Policy Distillation](../publications/37065c623b2bc5240d79.md)

Yushu Wang; Renkai Yang; Jingcao Xu; Zili Geng; Haihong Tang; Yaohui Jin; Hao He

On\-policy distillation \(OPD\) provides token\-level teacher feedback, yet common sampled\-token updates assign credit locally and omit the effects of earlier actions on subsequent feedback\. We introduce \\method\{\} \(Group\-Relative On\-Policy Distillation\), which decouples feedback computation from credit assignment by aggregating token feedback into calibrated sequence\-level credit\. We establish a theoretical basis for this approach by showing that, under ideal on\-policy assumptions, broadcasting raw summed feedback to every response token yields an unbiased estimate of the negative gradient of the sequence\-level reverse\-KL objective\. To support effective learning in practice, \\method\{\} discounts later feedback that may become less reliable under distribution shift and uses same\-prompt rollout groups to calibrate teacher guidance\. It preserves relative response preferences while retaining a controlled fraction of the group mean, which we term collective teacher pressure\. Across five Qwen3 teacher\-\-student settings and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, \\method\{\} outperforms vanilla OPD in macro Avg@K in every setting, including gains of 10\.9 and 11\.5 percentage points in two settings with matched thinking patterns\. It also maintains stable training under mismatched thinking patterns, where vanilla OPD collapses\. Ablations show that retaining an appropriate amount of collective teacher pressure can improve learning, while excessive collective teacher pressure or an unrestricted feedback horizon can destabilize training\.

## [6 Şubat 2023 Depremlerinin Kent İçi Nüfus Hareketliliğine Etkisi: Adana Örneği](../publications/370c2e82fa478cf5bd04.md)

Merve ALTUNDAL ÖNCÜ; İsmet GÜNEY; Dündar DAĞLI; Ersin ATEŞ

6 Şubat 2023 tarihinde Kahramanmaraş merkezli olarak meydana gelen depremler, Türkiye’nin güney ve güneydoğu bölgelerinde geniş çaplı yıkıma neden olmuş, sosyal, ekonomik ve mekânsal dengeleri derinden etkilemiştir\. Bu çalışma, depremlerden doğrudan etkilenen Adana kentinde yaşanan dönüşümleri inceleyerek, afet sonrası dönemde gayrimenkul piyasasında ve insan hareketliliğinde ortaya çıkan değişimleri mekânsal açıdan analiz etmeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Özellikle konut talebindeki ani artış, gayrimenkul fiyatlarında gözlenen dalgalanmalar ve kent içindeki nüfusun yeniden dağılımı araştırmanın temel inceleme alanlarını oluşturmaktadır\. Mahalle ölçeğindeki nüfus verileri ve emlak endeksi göstergeleri istatistiksel yöntemlerle değerlendirilmiştir\. Bu kapsamda Getis\-Ord Gi sıcak nokta analizi, Pearson korelasyon analizi, Temel Bileşenler Analizi \(PCA\) ve K\-Means kümeleme yöntemleri kullanılarak mahallelerin demografik ve ekonomik farklılaşmaları ortaya konmuştur\. Bulgular, Adana’da kentsel büyümenin özellikle batı ve kuzeydoğu akslarında yoğunlaştığını ve bu eğilimin deprem sonrasında belirgin biçimde hızlandığını göstermektedir\. Ayrıca bulgular, nüfus büyüklüğü ile emlak endeksi arasında güçlü bir doğrusal ilişki bulunmadığını; konut fiyatlarının daha çok mekânsal konum, yatırım beklentileri ve piyasa dinamikleri tarafından şekillendiğini ortaya koymaktadır\. Dolayısıyla afet sonrası dönemde gözlemlenen mekânsal hareketliliklerin kısa vadeli bir tepkinin ötesine geçerek kalıcı yapısal dönüşümlere zemin hazırladığı söylenebilir\. Bu kapsamda, yerel yönetimlerin afet sonrası demografik değişimleri dikkate alarak altyapı, konut ve sosyal hizmet politikalarını yeniden şekillendirmesi kritik bir gereklilik haline gelmiştir\.

## [On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training](../publications/370ce452158055b1e118.md)

Rachel Morris; Ryan Murray; Kerrek Stinson

For non\-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\\varepsilon$\. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O\(\\sqrt\{\\varepsilon\}\)$ or $O\(\\varepsilon\)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier\. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low\-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high\-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy\. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings\.

## [Sustainable and Green Networking: Architectures, Techniques, and Future Directions for Energy\-Efficient Communication Infrastructures](../publications/3716d84634b0cd4b05a8.md)

Sulaiman Bello Umar, Jyoti Shekawat, Tasiu Bello Umar; Fatima Abdullahi Sani Mahmud Mahmud Lawal

Information and Communication Technology \(ICT\) infrastructure is rapidly becoming an electrical energy consumer, and an increasingly non\-trivial emitter of greenhouse\-gases as a result of the growth of global data traffic, cloud computing, artificial\-intelligence workloads and always\-connected Internet\-of\-Things \(IoT\) devices\. Sustainable and Green Networking tackles this challenge by building energy\-awareness into the design, deployment and operation of communication networks without affecting performance, reliability and quality of service\. This paper summarizes the key concepts of green networking derived from literature published from 2022 to 2025, outlines the major classes of energy\-saving techniques \(standby and sleep modes, rate adaptation, energy\-proportional computing, Software\-Defined Networking \(SDN\) and Network Function Virtualization \(NFV\) based orchestration, and renewable\-powered infrastructure\) and suggests a cross\-layer conceptual framework that brings these techniques together under a single carbon\-intensity feedback loop\. As examples of application areas, green 5G/6G radio access networks, sustainable data centers, and energy efficient IoT/edge computing are presented\. A comparative study of the energy savings potential reported in the recent literature is presented, followed by a discussion of open challenges in the research field: the performance\-energy trade\-off, the standardization of energy information exposure, and the AI/ML energy\-overhead trade\-off, as well as interesting future research directions: the standardization of energy information exposure and the AI\-native energy orchestration\. The results will inform researchers, network operators and policymakers in their quest for more sustainable digital infrastructures\.

## [A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm–Tabu Search Method for The Storage Location Assignment Problem in Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems](../publications/372bdb7fdd6f349380b5.md)

Yung\-Chia Chang; Kuei\-Hu Chang; Shao\-Ting Yen

With the advent of artificial intelligence, the robotic mobile fulfillment system \(RMFS\) has emerged as a novel automated warehousing system\. Using a goods\-to\-person approach, RMFS employs robots to transport pods to workstations, where human pickers retrieve the required items, thereby significantly reducing walking distance\. In addition, both material assignment to pods and pod storage location assignment play critical roles in improving picking efficiency\. This study addresses these two decision problems through a two\-stage solution framework under a simplified single\-AGV, single\-workstation RMFS\. In the first stage, Apriori\-based association analysis and DBSCAN clustering are employed to identify highly associated materials and assign them to pods\. In the second stage, a hybrid genetic algorithm \(GA\) and tabu search \(TS\) algorithm is developed to optimize pod storage locations by minimizing the total round\-trip picking distance required to fulfill orders\. To verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach, the developed algorithms were applied to one week of real production\-order data from a Taiwanese computer equipment manufacturing company\. Experimental results show that, compared with the company&\#x27;s current method, the proposed approach reduces the average total pod movements by approximately 47\.12% and the average total picking distance by approximately 29\.60% under the studied operational setting\.

## [PulsoPBA: A Production System for Economic Activity Nowcasting with Neural Networks and Banking Data](../publications/372d9b06599620c6413a.md)

Igal Kejsefman; Agustín Caputo Bugallo; Milena Valens Upegui; Rodrigo Castro

PulsoPBA es un sistema de nowcasting para la estimación de granularidad semanal de la actividad económica de la Provincia de Buenos Aires \(Argentina\), cuyo dato oficial se publica con un rezago de hasta 10 semanas y con una granularidad mensual\. Para este objetivo, utiliza datos de aproximadamente 1\.200 variables derivadas de transacciones bancarias\. El sistema incorpora una etapa de desagregación temporal para construir la serie objetivo semanal partiendo de datos mensuales oficiales\. En cuanto al entrenamiento, la alta dimensionalidad y heterogeneidad de estas series motivó la adopción de redes neuronales capaces de proyectar variables a un espacio latente de menor dimensión\. Se utiliza la arquitectura TiDE, cuyo encoder viabiliza una reducción de dimensionalidad intrínseca\. El resultado principal es un pipeline automatizado en un entorno productivo\. El sistema se re\-entrena automáticamente al publicarse un nuevo dato oficial, integrando un embudo de selección de modelos multi\-criterio basado en el Weighted Interval Score \(WIS\) y predicciones probabilísticas via Monte Carlo Dropout\. Los resultados operativos contrastados con datos oficiales publicados ex post muestran un MAPE mensual de entre 0\.7% y 3\.5%, validando el pipeline y demostrando la factibilidad de un sistema de nowcasting de alta frecuencia a partir de datos bancarios de alta dimensionalidad\.

## [CEBPA\-induced trophectoderm\-like cells from pluripotent stem cells enable modeling of trophoblast lineage specification](../publications/37332fb12f051500af7d.md)

Haiyin Liu; Ruoqi Cheng; Jiarong Li; Tong Wang; Zining Li; Yunfei Huo; Bo Li; Cheng Li; Hongkui Deng; Jun Xu

Abstract Trophoblast lineages are essential for placental development and play indispensable roles in mammalian development\. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing trophoblast lineage specification, particularly trophectoderm formation, remain elusive\. Here, we show that transient overexpression of the transcription factor Cebpa in mouse pluripotent stem cells efficiently generates trophectoderm\-like cells that recapitulate key transcriptional features of trophectoderm\. These trophectoderm\-like cells can be further induced to form trophoblast organoids and exhibit developmental competence to generate all trophoblast lineages in vitro\. Mechanistically, Cebpa overexpression drives extensive epigenetic reprogramming toward a trophectoderm\-like state, including global remodeling of chromatin accessibility and coordinated changes in H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 histone modifications\. CUT&amp;RUN analyses further reveal binding of CEBPA to multiple trophectoderm\-specific enhancers\. Together, our findings identify Cebpa as a potent inducer of trophectoderm potential and establish a new platform for modeling trophectoderm lineage specification in vitro\.

## [Vessel\-associated microglia contribute to blood\-brain barrier disruption via a Notch\-IL\-1β axis in the diabetic brain](../publications/3736a624df31eab4347e.md)

Da\-Hye Lee; Min\-Joo Jung; Han\-Seok Jeong; Seung\-Hoon Kim; Gwanghun Kim; Hyun Mu Shin; Chung‐Hyun Cho

Diabetes mellitus \(DM\) is associated with central nervous system \(CNS\) complications, including cognitive impairment and an increased risk of neurodegenerative diseases\. However, the cellular mechanisms underlying blood\-brain barrier \(BBB\) disruption in the diabetic brain remain poorly understood\. In this study, we investigated the contribution of microglia to diabetes\-induced BBB dysfunction\. Using a streptozotocin \(STZ\)\-induced mouse model of type 1 diabetes, we observed increased BBB permeability and an accumulation of vessel\-associated microglia\. Transcriptomic analysis of isolated microglia revealed upregulation of genes associated with migration, angiogenesis, and vascular permeability, alongside activation of Notch signaling\. We found that endothelial cell \(EC\)\-derived CCL20, upregulated by TNF\-α, promotes microglial migration via AKT signaling\. Furthermore, direct interaction with ECs activates Notch signaling in microglia, inducing IL\-1β expression and disrupting EC tight junctions\. Treatment with minocycline attenuated microglial activation, restored endothelial Tjp1 expression, and reduced vascular leakage\. These findings identify a novel microglia\-EC signaling axis that contributes to BBB impairment in diabetes and suggest that targeting microglial activation may offer therapeutic potential for protecting neurovascular integrity in diabetic neuropathology\.

## [A Novel In Situ Wireless Monitoring of Bearing Cage Vibration and Skidding via Integrated Triboelectric and MEMS Sensing](../publications/373e73b5b64c5c215dae.md)

Ruoke Qin; Song Wang; Shuai Gao; Shuai Li; Qinkai Han; Gang Chen; Huayan Pu; Jun Luo

ABSTRACT To address the limitations of traditional bearing condition monitoring, such as long vibration transmission paths and weak fault features easily corrupted by noise, this study proposes a novel wireless self‐sensing intelligent bearing \(SV‐WSB\) for in‐situ skidding and vibration detection\. Integrated directly on the bearing cage with a Microelectromechanical Systems \(MEMS\) vibration sensor, triboelectric sensing unit, signal processing circuit, and Wi‐Fi module, the structure enables synchronous multi‐source signal acquisition and wireless transmission during bearing operation\. The floating freestanding triboelectric module captures cage rotational characteristics without motion interference, while the MEMS sensor directly perceives cage vibration and transient responses\. Experiments under steady‐state, acceleration‐deceleration, variable‐load and external impact conditions verify that triboelectric signals monitor cage speed and skidding ratio with only 0\.2% deviation from high‐speed camera measurements\. Vibration signals exhibit high sensitivity to transient impact excitation and unstable operating conditions\. The influences of dielectric material and electrode gap on triboelectric output performance are systematically investigated\. A Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\)‐Transformer‐based multi‐source information fusion model achieves higher fault diagnosis accuracy than single‐signal methods\. The proposed SV‐WSB provides a compact and effective solution for intelligent bearing condition monitoring and fault diagnosis\.

## [A Reproducible Machine Learning Pipeline for Educational Workload Analytics Using Synthetic Data](../publications/374afa233752b85f32a9.md)

Mazumder

Description This paper presents a reproducible machine learning pipeline for educational workload analytics using synthetic student data\. The study explores how lifestyle and academic\-related variables, including study hours, sleep, physical activity, and other daily activities, can be incorporated into a data\-driven framework for examining student stress\. Using a synthetic dataset comprising 10,000 records, the proposed workflow covers data preparation, feature selection, model training, predictive evaluation, and the interpretation of model performance\. The study reports standard regression metrics, including the coefficient of determination \(\(R^2\)\) and mean absolute error \(MAE\), alongside an additional measure of prediction accuracy within a specified tolerance\. These metrics provide a quantitative assessment of the model&\#x27;s ability to estimate stress\-related outcomes within the constructed dataset\. A central contribution of this work is its emphasis on reproducibility and methodological transparency\. By documenting the analytical workflow and evaluation procedure, the paper provides a practical framework that can support further experimentation in educational data analytics and machine learning\-based student workload research\. The findings should be interpreted within the limitations of synthetic data\. The results do not establish validated relationships between real students&\#x27; lifestyles and stress, nor do they constitute a clinical assessment or a validated student\-support intervention\. Instead, the study serves as an exploratory computational demonstration and a foundation for future research using real\-world, ethically collected, and appropriately validated educational data\. Keywords: Educational data analytics; machine learning; synthetic data; student stress estimation; workload analytics; predictive modelling; reproducible research\.

## [Fluorogenic RNA aptamers in cancer: emerging platforms for molecular imaging, biosensing, and precision oncology](../publications/3758996110519180935a.md)

Mohammad Mehdi Akbarin; Zahra Farjami; Hugo Ramírez Álvarez

Fluorogenic RNA aptamers have emerged as powerful molecular tools for cancer imaging, biosensing, and biomarker detection due to their high specificity, low background fluorescence, and genetic encodability\. These short RNA molecules activate fluorescence upon binding specific fluorogens, enabling real\-time visualization of intracellular targets and dynamic molecular processes in living systems\. Recent advances in RNA structural engineering, fluorophore optimization, and biosensor integration have significantly expanded the translational applications of fluorogenic aptamers in oncology\. This mini\-review summarizes the structural principles, fluorescence activation mechanisms, and cancer\-related applications of fluorogenic RNA aptamers and related nucleic acid biosensors\. Foundational studies describing the architecture of fluorogenic aptamer families, including Spinach, Broccoli, Mango, Pepper, Squash, and Beetroot, are discussed with emphasis on G\-quadruplex\-mediated fluorogen stabilization and fluorescence enhancement\. Furthermore, recent developments in CRISPR/Cas\-assisted fluorogenic biosensors, dual\-color RNA imaging systems, fluorogenic DNAzymes, and amplification\-driven aptamer platforms are highlighted\. Direct applications across multiple malignancies, including brain, breast, colorectal, liver, lung, prostate, and skin cancers, demonstrate the growing utility of these technologies for tumor\-associated RNA detection, epigenetic biomarker analysis, molecular imaging, and therapeutic monitoring\. In addition, advances in fluorescence brightness, structural stability, and multiplex imaging strategies have improved the sensitivity and adaptability of fluorogenic RNA systems for complex biological environments\. Despite current limitations related to RNA stability, intracellular delivery, and tissue penetration, fluorogenic RNA aptamers represent highly promising tools for next\-generation precision oncology\. Continued integration with nanotechnology, live\-cell imaging, artificial intelligence, and molecular diagnostics is expected to enhance further their clinical and translational potential in cancer research and personalized medicine\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Readiness and Educational Management Effectiveness: The Role of Digital Leadership](../publications/37641d1bdeb8e23fe5c6.md)

Setiawan; Ali Kuswadi; Dwi Sugianikl; Feri Riski Dinata; Muslih Qomarudin

This quantitative explanatory study examines relationships among artificial intelligence readiness \(AIR\), digital leadership \(DL\), and educational management effectiveness \(EME\) in questionnaire responses from 78 people involved in educational management or administration\. In the supplied results, AIR was positively associated with DL \(standardized coefficient = 0\.292, t = 2\.663, p = \.009; R² = \.085\)\. AIR was strongly associated with EME after adjustment for DL \(β = 0\.951, t = 26\.460, p &lt; \.001\), whereas the adjusted DL–EME coefficient was 0\.012 \(t = 0\.328, p = \.744\); EME model R² was \.911\. The source reports an indirect estimate near 0\.0033, calculated from unstandardized paths, but no bootstrapped confidence interval or direct test of the indirect effect\. A non\-significant DL–EME path alone does not establish the significance of mediation\. Furthermore, EME had Cronbach’s alpha of \.665, and the measurement model, institutional sampling frame, and item wording are not provided\. These cross\-sectional self\-reports support associations within this sample, not a causal effect or a verified absence of mediation\. The measurement evidence and indirect\-effect interval should be supplied before submission\.

## [Asymptomatic Anterior Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome: An Underdiagnosed Entity](../publications/376fee0d26c6b74d28f3.md)

Filiz Azman\-Iste; Berfe Simya Özbek

BACKGROUND/AIMS:Anterior tarsal tunnel syndrome \(ATTS\) is an uncommon entrapment neuropathy of the deep peroneal nerve that is frequently overlooked in clinical practice\.Prayer\-related and ground\-sitting postures, which are culturally common in Türkiye, may predispose individuals to this condition\.This study aims to evaluate the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and electrophysiological features of asymptomatic ATTS identified incidentally during routine electromyography \(EMG\) examinations\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:The records of 3,610 patients who underwent electrophysiological evaluation between January 2025 and February 2026 were retrospectively reviewed\.Patients with electrophysiological evidence of distal deep peroneal nerve involvement without ATTS\-related symptoms were included\.L5 radiculopathy, proximal peroneal neuropathy, and polyneuropathy with motor fiber involvement were excluded\.RESULTS: Asymptomatic ATTS was identified in 21 patients \(0\.58%\)\.The mean age was 56\.1±11\.9years; 11 were female and 10 were male\.All patients reported prolonged plantar\-flexion postures, mainly prayer\-related sitting habits \(namaz\), with a mean duration of 15 years\.Ten patients had diabetes mellitus\.On the affected side, mean extensor digitorum brevis \(EDB\) distal motor latency was 5\.19±1\.57ms and mean compound muscle action potential amplitude was 1\.04±0\.52mV, compared to 4\.47±0\.8ms and 3\.08±1\.52mV on the contralateral side\.Tibialis anterior \(TA\) motor responses were normal bilaterally\.Needle EMG demonstrated neurogenic changes confined to the EDB muscle in all patients\.CONCLUSION: Asymptomatic ATTS may be encountered more frequently in EMG practice than is generally appreciated\.Prayer\-related and ground\-sitting postures may predispose individuals to ATTS\.Systematic electrophysiological evaluation, including TA recording and needle EMG, may reduce misdiagnosis of polyneuropathy or lumbosacral radiculopathy in daily practice\.

## [IoT\-Based Battery Charging and Swapping Stations for Electric Vehicles: A Review of Architectures, Reservation, Security, and Challenges](../publications/3777fc04796d45b55b40.md)

U\. B\. Malkhandale; Sejal Mahato; Shruti Kale; Aryan Warkhedkar; Vansh Khonde; Khushi Ramtake

Battery swapping has re\-emerged as a practical alternative to plug\-in charging for electric vehicles \(EVs\), particularly for electric two\-wheelers used in delivery, ride\-hailing, and shared\-mobility services, where vehicle downtime directly reduces earnings\. As swapping networks grow, a station can no longer be a passive rack of chargers: it must continuously know which batteries are charged, reserved, or faulty, and it must release a battery only to the user entitled to it\. This paper reviews battery charging and swapping stations from this Internet of Things \(IoT\) viewpoint\. It \(i\) compares energy\-replenishment models and the commercial and policy landscape; \(ii\) surveys studies of station operation, planning, and user acceptance; \(iii\) examines IoT sensing, communication, and cloud architectures for real\-time batterystatus monitoring; \(iv\) analyzes reservation, authentication, and access\-control mechanisms and their cybersecurity implications; and \(v\) discusses charging safety and evaluation metrics\. A rulebased battery\-state model and a low\-cost prototype that combines an ESP32 controller, Li\-Po battery bays, RFID/PIN authentication, servo\-actuated gates, a Firebase database, and a ReactJS dashboard are presented as an illustrative reference implementation\. The reviewed studies largely address operation, planning, or acceptance separately; the review identifies open challenges in integrated real\-time monitoring, interoperability, battery\-health estimation, security, and standardized evaluation\.

## [Phytochemical\-capped silver nanoparticles and cationic polymeric nanoparticles form antibacterial hybrid nanoassemblies](../publications/377a2a00c1d03576d6a8.md)

HUMAIRA KHAN; Maged Abdelaziz; Nourina Nasim; Jungmi Park; Simona Piccolella; Vincent M\. Rotello; Severina Pacifico

Hybrid antibacterial nanomaterials that combine metallic nanoparticles with membrane\-active polymers represent a promising strategy to improve antimicrobial efficacy while reducing the amount of silver required for bacterial inhibition\. Herein, we report the development of sustainable hybrid nanoassemblies by integrating phytochemical‐stabilized silver nanoparticles \(AgNPs\), green‐synthesized using Camellia japonica flower extracts, with cationic poly \(oxanorbornene\-imide\) \(PONI‐C11‐TMA\) polymeric nanoparticles\. The obtained nanoparticles were characterized by UV‐Vis spectroscopy, ATR‐FTIR spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy \(TEM\), dynamic light scattering \(DLS\), and zeta potential measurements\. Cationic PONI‐C11‐TMA nanoparticles were synthesized and combined with AgNPs to generate hybrid PNP‐Ag nanoassemblies through electrostatic interactions\. The antibacterial activity of AgNPs, PONI‐C11‐TMA nanoparticles, and hybrid nanoassemblies was evaluated against multidrug‐resistant Gram‐negative bacterial strains, including Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, by determining minimum inhibitory concentrations \(MICs\) and fractional inhibitory concentration \(FIC\) indexes\. Cytocompatibility was assessed using NIH‐3T3 fibroblast cells\. Comprehensive UHPLC‐HRMS/MS and HPLC‐DAD analyses demonstrated that the flower extract is enriched in anthocyanins, flavan‐3‐ols, and other polyphenols, which serve as both reducing and stabilizing agents during nanoparticle formation\. The resulting AgNPs were predominantly spherical, with diameters of 20–30 nm, and exhibited excellent colloidal stability, as confirmed by UV‐Vis spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and dynamic light scattering\. Electrostatic assembly with positively charged PONI‐C11‐TMA nanoparticles generated stable hybrid nanoassemblies, as demonstrated by increases in hydrodynamic diameter and partial surface charge neutralization\. Individually, AgNPs and polymeric nanoparticles inhibited the growth of multidrug‐resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli at minimum inhibitory concentrations \(MICs\) of 10 and 2\.5 μg mL‐1, respectively, while maintaining high cytocompatibility toward NIH‐3T3 fibroblasts\. The hybrid nanoassemblies further reduced the effective antimicrobial concentrations, producing 2‐4‐fold MIC reductions against A\. baumannii and 4‐8‐fold reductions against E\. coli , with an additive interaction \(fractional inhibitory concentration index = 0\.75\)\. These findings demonstrate that phytochemical surface engineering of green‐synthesized AgNPs enables their integration with membrane‐active polymeric nanoparticles into stable hybrid nanoassemblies, providing an effective and sustainable platform for antibacterial nanomaterials with improved performance against Gram‐negative pathogens\.

## [The dual role of autophagy in gynecologic malignancies: promoting and inhibiting](../publications/377a5e18b52226b46678.md)

Dongying Gai; Ning Jia; Fanghua Qi; Lizhou Song; Wenwen Shao; Lin Zhao; Pingping Cai

Autophagy is a fundamental lysosome\-dependent degradation pathway that maintains cellular homeostasis by recycling intracellular components\. It plays a critical role in stress adaptation, energy metabolism, and genomic stability\. Emerging evidence supports that autophagy exhibits a context\-dependent dual role in the development and progression of gynecologic malignancies\. In the early stages of tumorigenesis or under specific molecular conditions, autophagy exerts tumor\-suppressive effects by preserving genomic integrity, attenuating chronic inflammation, and promoting autophagy\-related cell death\. However, as tumors progress or are exposed to therapeutic stress—such as radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or targeted therapy—autophagy is frequently reactivated as an adaptive survival mechanism\. This process enhances tumor cell tolerance to metabolic stress, oxidative damage, and therapeutic interventions, thereby facilitating tumor progression and contributing to drug resistance\. Accordingly, this review systematically summarizes the molecular regulatory mechanisms of autophagy in gynecologic malignancies and its role in treatment responses\. Furthermore, it highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting autophagy to improve precision treatment strategies\.

## [Enhancer\-Driven AAV Reporters Reveal Cell\-Type\-Specific Expression Differences in Aging and 5xFAD Mice](../publications/377c061bb4dc34981e16.md)

Haoqi Li

Enhancer\-driven adeno\-associated viral \(AAV\) reporters provide compact tools for targeting genetically defined neuronal populations, but their behavior in aging and Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease model contexts remains uncertain\. This thesis evaluated four enhancer\-AAV reporter datasets in young wild\-type, aged wild\-type, and 5xFAD mice: BiCHATe27 for cholinergic neurons, BiPVe3 for PV basket cells, BiPVe4 for PV chandelier cells, and BiSSTe4 for SST Martinotti cells\. Cleared brain tissue was imaged by light\-sheet microscopy and analyzed within paper\-matched regions of interest\. Reporter\-marker specificity, sensitivity, reporter intensity, and raw cell\-count burden were interpreted as descriptive pilot readouts\. Corrected BiCHATe27 ChAT analysis, driven by marker\-appropriate image\-analysis changes rather than by a new imaging modality, restored young wild\-type targeting estimates close to the AAV toolbox reference and suggested broadly stable targeting with reduced signal burden in aged and 5xFAD samples\. BiPVe3, BiPVe4, and BiSSTe4 showed lower or more variable targeting, including scan\-quality and ROI\-sensitivity effects\. Whole\-section pathology images added tissue context but were not used for specificity, sensitivity, or plaque\-proximity calculations\. Overall, the dataset supports a cautious cell\-type/subtype\-dependent model that requires manual counting, atlas registration, direct amyloid\-pathology assessment, and chromatin\-accessibility validation before stronger disease\-level interpretation\.

## [A Two\-stage Settling of the Milky Way Disk Revealed by Precise ChronoGal Ages](../publications/377fe0538fdeb1d10283.md)

David Mirabal; Carme Gallart; Tomás Ruiz\-Lara; Emma Fernández\-Alvar; A\. B\. A\. Queiroz; Guillem Aznar\-Menargues; Chris B\. A\. Brook; S\. Cassisi; Yllari K\. González\-Koda; Julio F\. Navarro; P\. A\. Palicio; F\. Surot

Abstract The spatial distribution of Galactic disk stars of different ages and metallicities encodes its dynamical evolution history and formation pathways\. The lack of precise ages for large, representative samples of stars has traditionally been a drawback for securely differentiating among formation scenarios proposed to explain the vertical properties of the Milky Way disk \(e\.g\. upside\-down formation versus secular dynamical heating\)\. In this letter, we use color–magnitude diagram fitting of Gaia data to derive very precise age–metallicity distributions for complete stellar samples in the solar neighborhood\. We identify quasi\-mono\-age–metallicity \(qMAM\) stellar populations with an age resolution better than 5% \(≃0\.5 Gyr at old age\), and study their absolute vertical density profile\. We observe a clear correlation between scale height and stellar age, with younger populations consistently more confined to the plane\. We find evidence that the scale height decrease rate changed drastically 10\.8 5 − 0\.12 \+ 0\.13 Gyr ago: at older ages, the evolution is very steep, with h Z dropping from over 1\.26 to ∼0\.5 kpc in merely 2 Gyr; subsequently, the thinning is very gradual, with h Z ∼ 0\.1 kpc for the youngest populations\. The extremely rapid early vertical settling of the disk points to a fundamentally upside\-down formation process at early times, when the thick disk component is basically formed\. We thus strongly support an evolutionary scenario defined by two distinct temporal phases: an initial, highly turbulent epoch that gave birth to the thick disk, and a subsequent more quiescent period of secular evolution and gradual gas settling, which formed the thin disk\.

## [Controlling the Diversity\-Quality Trade\-Off of LLMs by Merging Models Before and After Alignment](../publications/37813c7188dd2c983194.md)

Yasuaki Sumita; Tomoharu Iwata; Toshiyuki Tanaka

Alignment is known to change the output characteristics of large language models \(LLMs\)\. Base models tend to generate more diverse outputs, whereas aligned models tend to produce higher\-quality outputs\. The appropriate balance between the two depends on the task\. Existing methods either require costly fine\-tuning or, like temperature sampling, mainly improve lexical diversity rather than semantic diversity\. We introduce a depth\-aware FrankenMerging approach for controlling the diversity\-\-quality trade\-off between an aligned model and its base model without additional training\. This approach combines the lower layers of an aligned model with the higher layers of its base model based on the hypothesis that lexical diversity is more closely associated with lower layers and semantic diversity with higher layers\. Experiments showed that varying the number of layers taken from each model adjusts both diversity and quality\. In most cases, the merged models exhibited higher semantic diversity than the aligned model, and at some split positions, they showed higher lexical diversity than both original models\. They also demonstrated a better diversity\-\-quality trade\-off than temperature sampling in most settings\. A supporting ablation, in which we reversed the merging order, yielded results largely consistent with the hypothesis\.

## [Heavy metal ion driven smart nanomaterials for multimodal sensing, biocomputing, and information security: a mini review](../publications/3784b576fd15a22ea099.md)

Mohamed Nabeel Mattath

Heavy metal ions \(HMIs\) are widely recognized as persistent environmental pollutants\. However, they are increasingly being employed as functional chemical inputs in intelligent molecular systems\. This mini review summarizes smart nanomaterial\-based platforms developed for HMI\-driven biocomputing and information security\. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of dual\-mode, multimode, and multichannel readout strategies that translate selective ion\-recognition and signal\-transduction events into fluorescence, colorimetric, electrochemical, and other measurable responses\. By converting these responses into binary states, such platforms can execute diverse molecular logic operations, parity functions, and arithmetic functions\. Their applications in information security, including ASCII\- and Morse\-code\-based encryption, multimodal cryptosteganography, and anti\-counterfeiting strategies based on invisible fluorescent inks, are also discussed\. Collectively, these studies underscore the potential of HMIs to serve as chemically specific inputs in nanosystems, enhancing sensitive signal transduction and programmable functions for molecular computation and security applications, while reframing toxic pollutants as functional triggers in intelligent chemical platforms\.

## [From Events to Reasoning: Hierarchical Rule Composition over Explicit States](../publications/378db76478e5de63516c.md)

Cheng Lyu; Xueqi Wang

What a reasoning system emits is a conclusion; what it owes is a justification\. Producing one requires every operation to be admissible on the facts actually available, the dependencies of intermediate results to survive to the end of the path, and the path to be revised when a premise changes\. We present the Event Reasoning System \(ERS\), in which the reasoning state is an explicit event graph\. Semantic features nominate candidate objects and rule bindings, and declared rule and task conditions decide which may execute, so candidates that violate the represented period, unit, or evidence constraints cannot enter an accepted reasoning path\. Low\-level rules provide reusable local transformations, and recursively composable high\-level control rules organize subgoals and legal paths under the current goal, information gaps, and budget; a finite library is thereby rebound into paths never stored as complete solutions\. We formalize admissible transitions, task\-dependent control, compositional expressivity, dependency\-preserving revision, and the gap between reachable solutions and those a budgeted controller finds\. On structured\-event graphs, ERS builds dependency chains of up to twelve steps, cuts irrelevant executed domain operations from 32 to 0 as lookahead grows to 16, and produces no unsupported target output across 24 negative cases; with rules frozen, it passes 12/12 focused checks comprising nine accepted derivations involving unseen input/path combinations and three justified refusals, as well as 6/6 fact\-change cases\. On fourteen jointly solved development tasks, the recorded dynamic subgoal configuration uses 51\.6% less inference wall\-clock time than single\-level global control under their respective frozen settings\.

## [PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI\-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK](../publications/3790825e58fda0632c5c.md)

Anatoliy Drobakha; Liudmyla Lahuta

Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure\. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi\-agent systems using PersonaMatrix\-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI\. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis \(2019–2026\) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi\-agent roles, collective\-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism\. Peer\-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems\. Results: The framework separates output\-level stability \(RSI, IDS, RCS\) from role\-level and field\-level constructs\. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector\. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out\-of\-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states\. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis\. The archetypal\-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non\-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi\-agent environments\.

## [Advancing Research Governance in Nepal: Lessons from the NHRC–ICMR Technical Exposure Visit](../publications/37a46f85b89cd869aa4b.md)

Namita Ghimire; Ranjana Chataut; Sujata Acharya; Renu Twanabasu; Roshan Bhatta; Puspa Basnet; Aashish Malasi; Sudip Poudel; Aarati Shah; Hari Prasad Dhakal

The Nepal Health Research Council \(NHRC\) and the Indian Council of Medical Research \(ICMR\) established a bilateral collaboration under a Memorandum of Understanding \(MoU\) signed \(January 2021\) to foster scientific exchange, capacity building, and health research ethics\. NHRC officials comprising research officers, ethics administrators and journal office staff completed an exposure visits to the ICMR headquarters in New Delhi in February 2026\. The visit&\#x27;s sessions were centered on ethical practices of ICMR&\#x27;s Bioethics Unit such as the functioning of ethics committees, clinical trial registries, quality assurance protocols, research laboratory standards, and responses to emerging bioethical challenges\. This observational engagement identified operational models of potential relevance to NHRC&\#x27;s mandates\. Information was compiled from site visits, institutional documents, and expert presentations, and synthesized narratively into thematic lessons\. This report describes observed approaches to ethical governance, digitalization, and quality assurance that may inform the strengthening of Nepal&\#x27;s research governance framework\. Digitalization, updated national guidelines, tiered accreditation of research institutions, public engagement, and systematic human resource development were identified as priority areas for strengthening research governance in Nepal\. Keywords: Bioethics; capacity building; ethics committees; international cooperation; technology assessment\.

## [QAR\-Based Modeling of Aircraft Ground\-Taxi Fuel Consumption and CO2 Emissions: Determinants, Prediction and Operational Implications](../publications/37a5c376ac316bcb3778.md)

However, refined management and research remain challenged by data gaps and model imprecision\. A research framework is proposed, combining high\-precision Quick Access Recorder \(QAR\) data, statistical analysis, and machine learning\. Main\-engine fuel consumption differences across aircraft types, airports, and taxi\-in and taxi\-out operations were analyzed to identify the principal determinants of taxiing fuel consumption\. A direct taxi\-time–fuel baseline and an Adaptive Mechanism Learning \(AML\) model were constructed to predict aircraft taxiing fuel consumption\. The AML model achieved a test\-set coefficient of determination \(R2\) of 0\.9672, while aircraft\-specific R2 values exceeded 0\.97 for A320, A350, and B777 aircraft\. The findings provide a basis for refined fuel\-consumption assessment and operational decision support for greener airport operations\.

Late\-stage toxicity can lead to substantial attrition in drug development, motivating computational methods that can prioritize compounds for further safety assessment\. Recent work such as Trialblazer has demonstrated the utility of molecular fingerprints and bioactivity\-derived features for this task\. In this study, we develop an Enhanced Multi\-Branch Attention Network that combines Morgan fingerprints, MACCS keys, and physicochemical descriptors through separate feature\-processing branches followed by attention\-based fusion\. The training procedure incorporates focal loss, label smoothing, regularization, weighted sampling, and stratified 10\-fold cross\-validation\. The reported experiments use 1,841 compounds for model development and an independent test set of 339 compounds\. The reported ensemble test performance is ROC\-AUC = 0\.910 and MCC = 0\.525, with the remaining performance measures retained exactly as obtained from the experimental implementation\. The comparison with Trialblazer is presented as a benchmark comparison, while the lower recall of the proposed model is explicitly discussed as an important trade\-off\. The results suggest that the proposed multi\-representation architecture provides a potentially useful screening aid for late\-stage toxicity prediction, while experimental validation and careful interpretation remain necessary\.

## [Performance of machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) algorithms in prediction of breast cancer distant metastasis via imaging: a systematic review and meta‑analysis](../publications/37b73437a1e58fe72e9e.md)

Seyed Sina Dehghani; Ali Zakeri; Shiva Zahedinejad; محمدرضا نفیسی; Sefatullah Habibi; Hossein Molavi Vardanjani

Distant metastasis is a major cause of breast cancer mortality\. Early prediction may support risk\-adapted surveillance and treatment planning\. We evaluated imaging\-based machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) models for predicting future distant metastasis in patients without baseline metastatic disease\. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and supplementary Google Scholar searches were performed through June 2025\. Eligible studies evaluated imaging\-based AI prediction models and reported quantitative performance\. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\)\. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST \+ AI\. Random\-effects meta\-analysis, exploratory subgroup analyses, and univariable meta\-regression were performed\. Nine studies contributed 43 model evaluations\. The pooled model\-level AUC was 0\.80 \(95% CI: 0\.77–0\.84\)\. A secondary analysis restricted to the best\-performing model from each study yielded an AUC of 0\.89 \(95% CI: 0\.83–0\.95\)\. CT\-based models were associated with higher AUCs than MRI\-based models \(0\.83 vs\. 0\.71\), and models incorporating clinicopathological features had higher AUCs than imaging\-only models \(0\.91 vs\. 0\.74\)\. Exploratory meta\-regression identified associations with imaging modality, follow\-up duration, and inclusion of clinicopathological features\. Heterogeneity was substantial, and five of nine studies had high risk of bias\. Imaging\-based ML and DL models show potential for predicting future distant metastasis\. In the adjuvant setting, externally validated models may support risk stratification and individualized surveillance, but current evidence is insufficient to justify surveillance or treatment changes based solely on AI predictions\. Prospective external validation and transparent reporting are needed before clinical implementation\.

## [CLINICAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERISTICS OF RECOVERY IN WORKING\-AGE ADULTS AFTER COMMUNITY\-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA](../publications/37c5c2d3320d6200aba7.md)

Вікторія Іванівна Горошко; Анатолій Васильович Ємець; Євгенія Олександрівна Скріннік; Anna V\. Fastivets

Introduction\. Functional limitations may persist after the acute phase of community\-acquired pneumonia and delay return to daily and occupational activities\. Aim\. To investigate clinical and functional status and age\-related recovery characteristics in working\-age adults during 30 days after community\-acquired pneumonia and to substantiate the individualization of physical therapy\. Materials and methods\. A prospective clinical and functional study involved 73 participants\. The main group included 48 patients after community\-acquired pneumonia, divided into age subgroups of 18–22, 45–55, and 56–64 years; the control group included 25 participants\. Functional status was assessed using the Timed Up and Go test, the 10\-meter walk test, the 6\-minute walk test, the mMRC dyspnea scale, and the Borg CR10 scale\. Patients then completed a personalized 30\-day physical therapy program\. Results\. Compared with controls, patients had lower functional mobility, walking speed, and exercise tolerance\. The most pronounced limitations occurred in the 56–64\-year subgroup: median Timed Up and Go time was 13\.0 s, walking speed 0\.86 m/s, 6\-minute walk distance 385 m, post\-exercise oxygen saturation 91%, and heart rate 126 beats/min\. After 30 days, complete or nearly complete functional recovery was observed in 24 of 48 patients \(50\.0%\)\. The frequency of insufficient recovery increased with age, from 34\.8% to 56\.3% and 77\.8%\. Dyspnea at mMRC ≥2 persisted in 43\.8% of patients and severe fatigue in 50\.0%\. Overall, 37\.5% had not returned to usual daily activity, 25\.0% had not returned to professional or educational\-professional activity, and 37\.5% required further rehabilitation support\. Conclusions\. Thirty days after community\-acquired pneumonia, half of the working\-age adults had insufficient functional recovery\. Older age groups showed greater impairment in mobility and exercise tolerance, as well as more severe dyspnea and fatigue\. In the context of global efforts to achieve sustainable development and carbon neutrality, improving industrial energy efficiency has become a cornerstone of green transformation\. This study examines how corporate AI\-related disclosure intensity is associated with sustainable energy efficiency in manufacturing firms\. Using panel data on Chinese A\-share listed manufacturing firms from 2012 to 2024, we measure corporate energy efficiency using energy intensity based on standard coal\. AI\-related disclosure intensity is constructed from the frequency of AI\-related terms in firms’ annual reports and logarithmically transformed\. Based on panel regression, process innovation association analysis, moderation analysis, and ownership\-based subgroup analysis, this study finds that AI\-related disclosure intensity is negatively associated with energy intensity\. Yiqun Dong; Rongji Lu; Yuying Zhang; Yuteng Huang; Ziyi Wang; 孫吉滿; Siyi Li; Yuxin Jia; Ying Tian; Haodong Hu; XiFeng Li; Yanchao Liu; Chuan‐Zhi Duan

Introduction Post\-stroke sequelae \(PSS\) encompass persistent functional impairments after stroke and may benefit from early risk stratification\. ## [Escape dynamics and implicit bias of one\-pass SGD in overparameterized quadratic networks](../publications/37d3c59a3f70d0853fc2.md)

Dario Bocchi; Theotime Regimbeau; Carlo Lucibello; Luca Saglietti; Chiara Cammarota

Abstract We analyze the one\-pass stochastic gradient descent dynamics of a two\-layer neural network with quadratic activations in a teacher\-student framework\. In the high\-dimensional regime, where the input dimension N and the number of samples M diverge at fixed ratio α = M/N , and for finite hidden widths \(p, p \* \) of the student and teacher, respectively, we study the low\-dimensional ordinary differential equations that govern the evolution of the student\-teacher and student\-student overlap matrices\. We show that overparameterization \(p &gt; p \* \) only modestly accelerates escape from a plateau of poor generalization by modifying the prefactor of the exponential decay of the loss\. We then examine how unconstrained weight norms introduce a continuous rotational symmetry that results in a nontrivial manifold of zero\-loss solutions for p &gt; 1\. From this manifold the dynamics consistently selects the closest solution to the random initialization, as enforced by a conserved quantity in the ODEs governing the evolution of the overlaps\. Finally, a Hessian analysis of the population\-loss landscape confirms that the plateau and the solution manifold correspond to saddles with at least one negative eigenvalue and to marginal minima in the population\-loss geometry, respectively\.

Merle Willenberg; Peter Schildhauer

Foregrounding negotiations as forms of meta‑interactions that align user practices with platform affordances and algorithmic constraints, we introduce format \(Schildhauer &amp; Brock 2024\) as an analytical lens for media linguistics\. Format captures \(i\) potentiality \(the range of mediated affordances\) and \(ii\) procedurality \(the negotiated actualisation of those affordances\)\. Two empirical studies illustrate its utility\. A Zoom‑seminar analysis shows participants co‑constructing a digital seminar‑workshop format by negotiating reaction and turn‑taking features\. A multimodal study of twelve YouTube commentary videos \(and their comments\) reveals ongoing renegotiation of self‑censorship as a format feature in response to algorithmic pressures and audience expectations\. Findings demonstrate that format negotiation operates on multiple scales \(local vs global, explicit vs implicit, established vs emergent\) and across communicative levels, from comment sections to the whole platform\. ## [Beyond Technology Adoption: The I\-TRACK Model of AI\-TPACK Strategy Formation in Chinese Culture Teaching in Thailand](../publications/37ddd5a33ef42e25b8ea.md)

Kanokporn Numtong; Keran Wang; Kewalee Petcharatip; Ming Li

This study develops a practice\-grounded model explaining how high school Chinese language teachers in Thailand integrate artificial intelligence, pedagogy, and cultural content knowledge when forming and revising instructional strategies\. Semi\-structured interviews with 30 teachers were analyzed using grounded theory procedures\. Six categories were identified: institutional and personal conditions, teacher judgment and strategic mediation, learner response and strategy revision, pedagogical adaptation for Thai learners, contextual challenges in teaching Chinese culture, and knowledge\-driven content transformation\. These categories form the I\-TRACK model, in which teacher judgment connects contextual and institutional conditions with AI\-supported content transformation, localized pedagogy, and feedback\-based revision\.
