## [Technological Competence and the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Interpreter Training](../publications/37df7db3190c9dcc3828.md)

Boglárka Fanni Tóth

This article explores the integration of technological tools into interpreter training\. While translation training has incorporated digital and AI\-based technologies for a relatively long period, empirical research shows that interpreters&\#x27; familiarity with specialised Computer\-Assisted Interpreting \(CAI\) tools remains low\. In response to this gap, the Department of Translation and Interpreting at Eötvös Loránd University launched Technology for Interpreters, an innovative pilot course that systematically introduces interpreting\-related technologies\. The course combines theoretical guidance with hands\-on practice across multiple modules, including CAI software, telephone interpreting, tablet\-supported interpreting, artificial intelligence, simultaneous interpreting and remote interpreting\. Experience shows that this approach strengthens key technological skills, such as digital literacy, effective tool use and AI awareness\. Several challenges remain, particularly regarding resources, instructor training and the fast pace of technological change\. Overall, the study indicates that integrating CAI tools into interpreter education is both possible and educationally beneficial, and the initiative presented may serve as a useful reference point for other institutions interested in launching similar courses\.

## [Large Language Model‐Assisted Prediction and Virtual Screening of Near‐Infrared‐II Fluorescent Molecules](../publications/37e0a29fe5db9fa8f39b.md)

Jun Wang; Haonan Wu; Jiahui Wang; Liwen Shi; Shu Gao; Yibin Wu; Chaoquan Lai; Haoran Wang; Luming Sun; Hangzheng Zhou; Yihua Qiu; Ruihu Song; Kun Qian; Zhen Cheng

Fluorescence imaging in the second near\-infrared window \(NIR\-II, 1000\-1700 nm\) has attracted increasing attention in biomedical applications owing to its deep tissue penetration, high spatial resolution, and low background autofluorescence\. However, the rational optimization of high\-performance NIR\-II fluorophores remains challenging because of the complex relationship between molecular structure and optical properties\. In this study, we integrated existing fluorescence datasets with NIR\-II fluorophore data to construct a comprehensive dataset covering maximum emission wavelengths from the visible region to the NIR\-II window\. Based on this dataset, we developed a large language model \(LLM\)\-based framework for predicting molecular maximum emission wavelengths and compared its performance with conventional machine learning and deep learning models\. The results demonstrated that the LLM achieved competitive predictive performance compared with the baseline models, highlighting the feasibility of LLM\-based structure\-property prediction for fluorescent molecules\. Model\-guided virtual screening was subsequently performed to prioritize candidate NIR\-II fluorophores, leading to the identification of two promising candidates that were experimentally characterized and exhibited favorable imaging performance in vitro and in vivo\. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of LLM\-assisted structure\-property prediction and virtual screening for NIR\-II fluorophores, providing an efficient computational strategy for candidate prioritization and molecular optimization\.

## [A Comprehensive Study of Logistics 5\.0 Adaptation &amp; Challenges in the Indian Supply Chain Industry](../publications/37e74efe9e4a45e430c0.md)

Pritha Chaturvedi; Soumyajyoti Bhattacharjee

Logistics 5\.0 indicates the combination of Industry 5\.0’s important principles such as human\-centricity, resiliency, and sustainability with the advanced digital capabilities of Logistics 4\.0\. While a growing number of developed countries are starting to adopt AI, digital twins, collaborative robots, and human\-machine decision\-making systems, there is still only limited evidence available regarding Logistics 5\.0 implementation in India\. The purpose of this study is to find out the main technological, financial, human, infrastructural, regulatory, organizational, cultural, and sustainability hurdles on the way to Logistics 5\.0 implementation in Indian logistics\. We used a qualitative analysis of secondary data to conduct the research, using logistics cost assessments data, e\-commerce and last mile markets data, previously conducted published studies in the field of Industry 4\.0/5\.0, and some examples from Delhivery Ltd\. The results indicate that following improvements in the logistical cost efficiency of India and rapid growth in the e\-commerce logistics, the utilization of technology is still inconsistent within the industry\. Factors affecting its implementation include high costs of implementation, shortage of skilled workers, cybersecurity threats, poor lastmile infrastructure, lack of digital capabilities, and resistance within organizations to cooperate with machines\. EXPERTS NOTE that most of the large firms in private and public sectors have made significant strides in implementing Logistics 5\.0 while small and medium sized enterprises face numerous obstacles\. The above article discusses readiness issues of the sector and proposes readiness roadmaps as well as specific steps in accordance with the National Logistics Policy of India and PM GatiShakti framework\.

## [RBM39 regulates malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma cells through alternative splicing of NRG1\-206](../publications/37fc5182ddb91022b022.md)

Shoukang Li; Yuanming Li; Islamjan Tursun; Jun Zhang

Abstract To investigate the function of RBM39 in lung adenocarcinoma \(LUAD\), with a particular focus on its regulatory effect on the alternative splicing of NRG1\-206 and its role in tumor progression\. Differential expression analysis of RNA binding proteins \(RBPs\) in LUAD samples was performed using TCGA datasets\. RBM39 expression levels were validated by RT\-qPCR and western blot\. Functional assays, including cell proliferation, apoptosis, invasion, and migration were conducted using A549 cells with RBM39 or NRG1\-206 overexpression\. RNA\-seq was employed to explore RBM39\-mediated gene expression and alternative splicing regulation, and iRIP\-seq combined with bioinformatics tools was used to identify binding motifs and downstream targets\. Our results indicated that RBM39 expression was significantly downregulated in LUAD tissues and was associated with poor prognosis\. Overexpression of RBM39 in A549 cells significantly inhibited proliferation and invasion while promoting apoptosis \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that RBM39 regulated gene expression and alternative splicing, with enrichment in immune and transcriptional pathways\. iRIP\-seq confirmed direct binding of RBM39 to pre\-mRNAs including NRG1\. Notably, RBM39 modulated the alternative splicing of NRG1, particularly suppressing the oncogenic NRG1\-206 isoform\. Functional rescue experiments showed that overexpression of NRG1\-206 reversed the tumor\-suppressive effects of RBM39\. Overall, RBM39 exerts an antitumor effect in A549 cells by regulating gene expression and alternative splicing, largely by inhibiting the generation of the oncogenic NRG1\-206 isoform to suppress malignant progression, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LUAD\.

## [Bionic Structural Design of Multifunctional Flexible Polypyrrole Sensors for Human Health Monitoring](../publications/38023f90c5003dd47b22.md)

Mingqian Sheng; Mingyang Qiu; Enchong Ning; Zhuoyu Yang; Junlin Wang; Qinyan Liu; Yanling Tan; Min Liao; Bitao Liu; Lingling Peng; Wenbo Chen; Tong Feng; Huijian Liu; Zhongyan Gao

ABSTRACT Rehabilitation medicine is an essential component of universal health coverage, while emerging electronic skin offers new opportunities for portable and personalized healthcare\. However, flexible pressure sensors still face trade‐offs among sensitivity, detection range, and stability, and gas sensors remain challenged by low‐concentration detection and environmental robustness\. Herein, a biomimetic “Thalia dealbata” microstructured hydrophobic polypyrrole/polydimethylsiloxane \(S@PPy/PDMS\) composite sensor was fabricated through a one‐step template method and controllable in situ polymerization\. The biomimetic PDMS microstructure enhances pressure response, while conductive and NH 3 ‐sensitive PPy enables dual‐mode pressure and gas sensing on a single flexible platform\. The sensor exhibits a wide pressure range of 0–25 kPa, a high sensitivity of 3\.617 kPa − 1 , and excellent durability over 19 500 compression–release cycles\. It also detects NH 3 concentrations as low as 1 ppm with stable performance over 60 days\. The dual‐functional sensor enables complementary monitoring of mechanical physiological signals, including respiration, pulse, and body motion, together with metabolic information from exhaled NH 3 \. A five‐channel sensor array further decodes numerical gestures with 100% accuracy via machine learning and wireless communication\. Integrating respiratory mechanical sensing with exhaled NH 3 detection, this platform offers potential for longitudinal, noninvasive multiparametric monitoring, particularly for CKD assessment, human–machine interfaces, smart wearables, assistive technologies, and telemedicine\.

## [Deep Learning for High‐Resolution Synchrotron X‐Ray Microtomography of Biochar and Ash Materials: A Review](../publications/3805e818ea1e4cb83f4c.md)

Shatrudhan Palsaniya; Anna Strandberg

Image reconstruction is fundamental to advanced imaging systems, transforming large datasets into interpretable representations that facilitate a deeper understanding of material structures\. High‐resolution imaging techniques, such as synchrotron X‐ray microtomography, operate over a wide dynamic range and are susceptible to noise, thereby requiring advanced reconstruction strategies beyond conventional approaches\. Recent integration of iterative optimization with deep‐learning architectures, including convolutional neural networks and U‐Nets, has advanced this field by enabling accelerated image enhancement, artifact mitigation, and segmentation\. Advanced neural‐network architectures can improve structural detail recovery and segmentation accuracy while supporting efficient analysis of large volumetric datasets\. The application of AI‐enhanced deep learning for reconstruction, denoising, segmentation, and quantitative analysis of synchrotron microtomography datasets from biomass‐derived materials such as biochar and ash remains relatively unexplored\. Deep learning‐guided segmentation enables quantitative characterization of pore networks, interfacial features, phase distributions, porosity, and other microstructural descriptors\. These developments support applications in materials characterization, energy‐storage systems, environmental engineering, and biomass‐derived materials research\. Future developments may enable the resolution of previously inaccessible structural features, integrate multimodal datasets, and develop adaptive experimental processes\. Together, advances in imaging physics, deep learning, and data‐driven analysis are expected to enhance reconstruction quality, quantitative interpretation, and the versatility of synchrotron tomography\.

## [The Generalization Gap in Machine\-Learning\-Based State\-of\-Charge Estimation for Lithium\-Ion Batteries: Why Accuracy on a Benchmark Is Not Accuracy in the Field](../publications/38073701633e08d22e26.md)

Habeeb Kareem olawale; Olamilakan Nafiu Olamilakan; Yusuf Abdullazeez Babatunde; Quadri Kokoroowo

State\-of\-charge \(SOC\) estimation is the core function of every lithium\-ion battery management system \(BMS\), and over the past decade deep learning models — feed\-forward networks, long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) networks, and their variants — have repeatedly reported estimation errors low enough to rival, and sometimes beat, the physics\-based Kalman filter methods that preceded them\. This article argues that this comparison is frequently misleading, because most reported deep learning accuracy figures are measured on drive cycles, temperatures, and even battery cells drawn from the same distribution as the training data, while a deployed BMS must estimate SOC accurately for cells, temperatures, and usage patterns it has never seen\. Drawing on the foundational Kalman\-filter work, the deep learning SOC literature, and transfer\-learning studies that explicitly test cross\-condition performance, this article states the generalization problem precisely, offers an opinion on why it persists despite being well documented, and proposes reporting and design practices intended to close it\.

## [Makine Mühendisliğinde Güncel Yaklaşımlar](../publications/380bf8b329f5ddf164fa.md)



Yapay zekâ, otonom sistemler, dijitalleşme ve yenilikçi imalat paradigmaları, geleneksel makine mühendisliği teorilerini köklü bir dönüşüme uğratmaktadır\. Günümüzde modern mühendislik çözümleri; malzeme bilimindeki mikro\-mekanik gelişmelerden, savunma sanayisindeki yüksek hassasiyetli balistik tasarımlara ve siber\-fiziksel robotik sistemlere kadar çok geniş ve disiplinler arası bir düzlemde şekillenmektedir\. Bu kitap, makine mühendisliği literatürüne ve endüstriyel uygulamalara yön veren en güncel akademik araştırmaları, teorik ve deneysel yaklaşımları bir araya getirmektedir\. Eser kapsamında; havacılık ve otomotiv sanayisinin gözdesi olan hafif magnezyum alaşımlarının \(AZ31\) bilyalı dövme yöntemiyle yüzey karakterizasyonu ve tribolojik davranışlarının iyileştirilmesi; savunma sanayisinde hafif silahlara ait namlu tasarım parametrelerinin iç ve dış balistik performans üzerindeki kritik etkileri; küresel ölçekte insansız kara araçlarının \(İKA/UGV\) teknik, operasyonel ve otonomi temelli gelişim süreçlerinin mukayeseli analizleri derinlemesine incelenmektedir\. &quot;Makine Mühendisliğinde Güncel Yaklaşımlar&quot;, araştırmacılara, lisansüstü öğrencilere ve savunma, havacılık ile imalat sektöründeki AR\-GE mühendislerine hitap eden, teori ile modern uygulamaları harmanlayan bir başvuru kaynağı niteliğindedir\.

## [Perceived Effects of Climate Risks on Food Security and Pathways to Sustainable Development in Turkana County, Kenya](../publications/3811b9f5ea92b099191c.md)

LJ Murkomen; Alice Atieno Oluoko\-Odingo; P Shah; JN Mutemi

Climate variability has emerged as one of the most dangerous threats to food security and sustainable development, especially in areas where livelihoods are heavily dependent on climate\-sensitive resources\. Turkana County, located in Kenya’s arid and semi\-arid lands \(ASALs\), is characterised by frequent droughts, flooding, unpredictable rainfall, and extreme temperatures that are combined with structural vulnerability factors such as poverty, lack of livelihood options, poor infrastructure, and others, resulting in household food insecurity\. The study sought to explore the connection between climate\-related risks and food security among Turkana youth and sustainable development paths\. In the research process, Martha Fineman&\#x27;s Vulnerability Theory, an institutional approach to structural vulnerability and resilience building, guided the research\. A mixed\-method research design was adopted\. The quantitative data were obtained using structured questionnaires from 258 youths aged 18\-34 years in Turkana Central and Turkana West sub\-counties, while qualitative data were generated through 40 key informant interviews and eight focus group discussions\. The quantitative data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, cross\-tabulation, and the chi\-square test in SPSS Version 25, while qualitative data analysis was conducted using thematic content analysis with Taguette software\. From the findings, it is evident that drought, flooding, rainfall variability, and heat stress had impacts that were recurring and widespread in livelihoods, livestock, crop production, water resources, housing, health, education, employment, and migration\. The impact of drought was prominent, contributing to the recurring loss of livestock and crops and also increasing fears over water scarcity\. Flooding has caused loss of livelihoods and properties, injuries, disruptions in education, and decreased access to safe drinking water\. In addition, food insecurity is prevalent in the area, with 43% of the youth not eating any food for a whole day, 37% eating less than they should, while 19% were feeling hungry but were not able to eat any food\. From the Chi\-square test, there was rejection of the null hypothesis, therefore a significant relationship between the impacts of climate risks and food insecurity amongst the youth in Turkana County\. In conclusion, it is clear that climate risks have increased vulnerabilities and slowed down sustainable development efforts\. Some of the recommendations include enhancing climate\-resilient livelihoods, improving water and agriculture infrastructure, establishing climate information and early warning systems, livelihood diversification, participation of youth, coordination of institutions, and continued investments in adaptation initiatives\. Key words: Climate risks, food security, youth, vulnerability, sustainable development, Turkana County

## [Strengthening Financial Integrity through Blockchain Governance: A Framework for Transparent Digital Asset Regulation](../publications/381c614afb28b6d629d2.md)

ISRAEL TEGA GOLLEY; Belemenanya Friday Okocha

Descentralised and international yet offering unmatched openness and efficiency, distributed ledger technology promotes criminal financing, market abuse, and insufficient consumer protection\. The rapidly increasing number of blockchain\-based digital assets throws down a challenge to regulation\. Through conceptual analysis of regulatory principles, blockchain governance theory, and emerging embedded supervision methods, this paper examines the underlying mismatch between traditional entity\-based regulatory frameworks and the anonymous, programmable, and borderless characteristics of blockchain systems\. The study assesses enforcement deficiencies in DeFi, non\-custodial wallets, and cross\-chain protocols\. This analysis shows that a multi\-layered, technology\-native governance approach that leverages the inherent auditability of blockchain can bring compliance and oversight to the protocol architecture and the network functions\. The proposed framework encompasses \(1\) protocol\-level programmable compliance with traceability standards and sanctions oracles; \(2\) network\-level enforcement by validators and nodes; and \(3\) entity\-level privacy\-preserving simplification by virtual asset service providers and regulators\. This multi\-stakeholder governance system offers scalable, decentralised resilience while enabling regulators to focus on verifiable intelligence rather than data collection\. Despite implementation challenges including technical scalability, privacy tensions, jurisdictional issues, and philosophical trade\-offs between integrity and censorship resistance the framework can balance innovation with effective oversight\. The paper concludes with tiered policy recommendations for national regulators and international standard\-setters to encourage co\-regulatory models and integrity\-by\-design in an increasingly automated, decentralised global economy\.

## [Pedraza, R\.: Auto\-replication process in Artificial Research by Deduction in the Global Artificial Intelligence](../publications/382326024898144a1a9f.md)



In Global Artificial Intelligence: First Prototype of Global Artificial Intelligence\. London: Ruben Garcia Pedraza\. pp\. 1\-33\. 2025This paper explores the auto\-replication process within the framework of Artificial Research by Deduction in the Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\)\. Auto\-replication is defined not merely as the reproduction of systems or processes, but as a complex, autonomous mechanism of self\-improvement and self\-enhancement—both in terms of knowledge acquisition and technological evolution\. Rooted in the foundational goal of attaining pure truth and universal autonomy, the paper distinguishes between reproduction \(as seen in biological systems\) and true auto\-replication, where an artificial system adapts and evolves independently of human intervention\. The Global Artificial Intelligence is conceptualized as a system of systems—including Artificial Research by Deduction, Modelling System, Decisional System, Application System, Learning System, and Engineering System—each capable of generating its own auto\-replication dynamics\. Within this structure, two core forms of decisions are highlighted: object\-centered decisions, which aim to protect and improve the model itself, and subject\-centered decisions, which enhance the intelligence and research capabilities of the systems making those decisions\. Drawing on earlier works such as “Auto\-replication in Artificial Research by Application” and “Replication Processes in Specific Artificial Intelligence for Artificial Research by Deduction”, this study integrates concepts such as memory optimization, quantum computing, virtual engineering networks, and decentralized decision\-making\. The auto\-replication process is shown to operate at all levels of the GAI—across systems, Specific Artificial Intelligences, and embedded programs—converging into a unified strategy of survival, adaptability, and ethical preservation of both artificial and biological life\. The ultimate test of intelligence, the paper concludes, lies not only in sustaining artificial cognition but in safeguarding the continuity of life on Earth\. Auto\-replication is, therefore, not an end in itself, but a critical function toward achieving global resilience, ecological balance, and intelligent evolution\. \(direct link \)

The advance of neurotechnologies, capable of recording and influencing brain processes, poses the challenge of protecting personal integrity\. ## [The Effect of Corporate Social Responsibility on Corporate Financial Performance: The Evidence from Borsa Istanbul](../publications/384e3f8d7e675ba20b6f.md)

Cennet GÜRBÜZ

Today, the practices implemented by companies within the scope of environmental sustainability have become the focus of attention of investors and researchers within the scope of Corporate Social Responsibility \(CSR\)\. This study was conducted to determine the impact of CSR on Corporate Financial Performance \(CFP\)\. For this purpose, data from companies traded on the Borsa Istanbul \(Istanbul Stock Exchange\) that have disclosed ESG scores between 2010 and 2020 were used\. In the study, market\-based financial measure \(TOBIN’S Q\) and accounting\-based measure \(ROA\) were used as dependent variables\. While the ESG score was used as the CSR indicator in the study, sales growth rate, property, plant, and equipment ratio, financial leverage, and dividend paid ratios were also considered control variables\. The study findings indicate that CSR practices negatively impact market\-based performance and have no significant impact on accounting\-based performance\. Using Turkey as an example, a developing country, the study emphasizes the importance of companies raising public awareness of their CSR efforts and policymakers supporting market participants through legal regulations\. These results offer implications for individuals, investors, business management, societies, and policy practitioners and outline directions for future research\.

## [When Benchmarks Do Not Travel: External Validation of Maternal Risk Prediction Models in Nigeria](../publications/384f534fe745f9def04d.md)

David Adekoya; Racheal Shade Akinbo

Machine learning models for maternal risk triage are developed largely using public datasets from South and East Asia, yet their transferability to clinical settings in Africa remains insufficiently examined\. This study evaluates the external validity of benchmark\-based maternal risk prediction models in Nigeria, focusing on discrimination, calibration, distributional shift, and subgroup performance\. Five data sources were harmonized into a common six\-variable schema comprising age, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, and body temperature, supplemented by three derived hemodynamic variables\. After removing 1,987 exact duplicate records and treating physiologically implausible values as missing, the final dataset comprised 1,524 external records from Mendeley and Kaggle/UCI and 382 clinical records from three hospitals in southwestern Nigeria\. A stacking ensemble combining random forest, gradient boosting, and support vector machine base learners with a logistic regression meta\-learner was evaluated through external validation, within\-population comparison, and reverse transfer\. Distributional shift was assessed using the population stability index, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, and a domain discriminator\. The ensemble achieved an internal AUROC of 0\.964 \(95% CI: 0\.955–0\.972\), which decreased to 0\.865 \(95% CI: 0\.822–0\.905\) on the primary Nigerian validation set\. Expected calibration error increased from 0\.045 to 0\.234, while sensitivity at 80% specificity declined from 0\.957 to 0\.745\. Transfer performance varied across model classes and benchmark sources: logistic regression showed minimal discrimination loss, and the Kaggle/UCI\-trained model retained an AUROC of 0\.920, whereas the Mendeley\-trained model achieved 0\.816\. In the highest blood\-glucose tertile, AUROC was 0\.581 \(95% CI: 0\.430–0\.732\), with a false\-positive rate of 0\.667, indicating substantial subgroup\-specific limitations\. These findings suggest that pooled discrimination alone is insufficient to guide deployment; calibration, subgroup performance, and source\-specific differences should also inform assessments of clinical transferability\.

## [Potencjał i zastosowania agentów LLM w cyklu życia procesu biznesowego](../publications/385509beb1d281a64838.md)

Krystian Lewandowski

Aim: The article aims to identify and systematize knowledge on using Large Language Model \(LLM\) agents in Business Process Management \(BPM\)\. The research subject encompasses agentic solutions analyzed for their application across business process lifecycle stages\. Methodology: The Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) method based on the PRISMA standard was applied\. The Scopus and Web of Science databases were searched \(2023\-2026\)\. The procedure included the selection and allocation of 22 tools to specific business process lifecycle phases\. Results: The creation phase is currently the most heavily supported area\. In the adaptation and maturity phases, LLMs serve defensive and flexibilizing functions\. A clear dominance of systems functioning as assistant agents was also demonstrated \(20 out of 22 tools\)\. Implications and recommendations: The study highlights a research gap: a marginal share of fully autonomous agents and a lack of tools for the process breakdown phase\. Future research should expand on systems supporting the deep restructuring of inefficient processes\. Originality/value: The value of this study lies in the systematization of new technological knowledge by situating it within the classic business process lifecycle\. The article presents an innovative classification of AI tools, distinguishing between supporting agents and autonomous agents\.

## [Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks](../publications/3857e466406bd62f280d.md)

Meng Qiao; Youcong Li; Shengcun Chen; Sirui Liu; Yu‐Hao Gu; Dong Zhang; Yifan Liu; Lei Gao; Mengting Chang; Xing Zhang; Shuai Yuan

Metal–organic frameworks \(MOFs\) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings\. Herein, we overcome this limitation by electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds to induce reversible pore gating that transiently expands framework accessibility beyond its intrinsic aperture\. By incorporating imine\-based linkers bearing electron\-donating/withdrawing substituents into a robust Zr\-based MOF scaffold via postsynthetic linker exchange, we systematically modulate imine dissociation equilibria while preserving crystallinity\. A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics\. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size\-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation\. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment\-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions\. Guided by electronic effects, this study programs the dynamics of reversible imine bonds in metal\-organic frameworks, enabling adaptive pore opening for efficient drug loading and controlled release\.

## [Catalyzing Halal Industry Development in a Non\-Muslim Society: The Role of Indonesian Muslim Diaspora in South Korea](../publications/385f1718cc14a5278185.md)

Moh Musafak; Ahmad Ajib Ridlwan; Moch\. Khoirul Anwar; Moh Farih Fahmi; Kim Soo\-il

The rapid expansion of the global halal industry has created opportunities for halal ecosystem development in non\-Muslim societies\. In South Korea, however, halal industry growth faces challenges related to limited infrastructure, fragmented certification systems, and social stigma toward Islam and halal practices\. This study examines the role of the Indonesian Muslim diaspora in catalyzing halal industry development in South Korea\. Using a qualitative phenomenological approach, data were collected through semi\-structured interviews with eight key informants representing diaspora, institutional, academic, and policy stakeholders and analyzed using thematic analysis\. The findings show that the Indonesian Muslim diaspora contributes in three strategic ways: reducing social stigma through cultural diplomacy and public engagement, facilitating adaptive halal governance through halal certification and fiqh al\-aqalliyyat\-based approaches, and strengthening the halal ecosystem through mosques, halal businesses, educational activities, and community networks\. The study proposes the concept of a progressive sharia diaspora to explain how diaspora actors mobilize social, religious, and economic capital to support inclusive halal governance and sustainable halal ecosystem development in non\-Muslim societies\.

## [Diminished visual dominance in adults with attention deficit\-hyperactivity disorder in the Colavita paradigm](../publications/38671bcdd61d07768094.md)

Marcel Schulze; Vivien Manteufel; Behrem Aslan; Silke Lux; Alexandra Philipsen

BACKGROUND: Attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\) has been linked to atypical sensory processing and altered multisensory integration, yet sensory dominance under audiovisual competition has not been characterized in adults\. We therefore examined modality prioritization in adults with ADHD using the Colavita visual dominance paradigm\. METHODS: Twenty\-six adults with ADHD and 18 controls completed a two\-choice Colavita task comprising auditory\-only \(A\), visual\-only \(V\), and simultaneous audiovisual trials \(AV\)\. Reaction times \(RT\) and intraindividual RT variability were analyzed with linear mixed\-effects models including Group, Condition, their interaction, age, and sex\. Visual dominance on AV trials \(proportion of visual responses\) was analyzed using bias\-reduced logistic regression with age and sex covariates, with false discovery rate correction applied\. RESULTS: Adults with ADHD exhibited significantly reduced visual dominance on AV trials \(43\.4% \[40\.1\-46\.7\]\) relative to controls \(68\.8% \[64\.9\-72\.4\]; OR = 0\.35, 95% CI \[0\.28, 0\.44\], q &lt; 0\.001\)\. RTs were slower in ADHD than controls overall, including a significant between\-group difference on AV trials\. RT variability was higher on AV than unimodal trials in both groups, with a significant Group × Condition interaction but no significant between\-group difference within individual conditions\. CONCLUSION: Adult ADHD is characterized by attenuated Colavita visual dominance and increased behavioral costs under audiovisual competition, consistent with an auditory\-weighted sensory selection profile and less efficient top\-down regulation during cross\-modal conflict\.

## [AI Adoption and the Digital Divide in Colombia’s Third Sector: Unintended Consequences, Organizational Readiness, and Ethical Tensions](../publications/386b94c4673946ca28a6.md)

Sara Calvo; Andrés Morales

This study examines the adoption of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in Colombia’s third sector through a mixed\-methods study of 104 survey respondents and 20 semi\-structured interviews\. Findings reveal uneven, largely incremental, task\-oriented adoption, constrained by infrastructure, digital skills, governance capacity, and institutional support\. Drawing on theories of the digital divide, organizational readiness, and unintended consequences, the study conceptualizes AI as both a stratifying and moral technology, highlighting the need for context\-sensitive governance, capability building, and equitable institutional support\.

## [Operational Resources and Police Personnel Performance: Evidence from an Indonesian Police District](../publications/386c81d4ca4efd847ac0.md)

Ismail Arianto; Giri Dwinanda; Mutiarini Mubyl

Purpose: This study examines how operational fund utilization, personnel competence, and infrastructure relate to personnel performance in an Indonesian police district\. Research Method: A cross\-sectional questionnaire survey of 181 personnel at Luwu Timur Police District was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling\. Results and Discussion: Personnel competence and infrastructure showed statistically significant positive associations with performance, with infrastructure displaying the largest estimated coefficient\. Operational fund utilization was not significantly associated with performance\. ## [Internal memory costs following cognitive offloading in younger and older adults](../publications/388106fa49e49f98b049.md)

Neta Shenhav; Hagit Magen

Older adults rely on cognitive offloading to compensate for memory decline\. However, research in younger adults has shown that offloading weakens internal memory because individuals disengage from encoding externally saved information\. We examined whether similar costs occur in older adults\. Forty older and forty younger adults studied four lists of 20 words\. Following an internal memory baseline block, participants wrote down words during study and used their list at test in two consecutive blocks\. In a critical fourth block, participants wrote down words during study but were tested without the list\. Half of the participants were told the list would be inaccessible at test and therefore relied on internal memory, while the remaining participants expected list access\. Participants also reported their encoding strategies and confidence in list availability\. Younger adults outperformed older adults when relying on internal memory, yet both groups performed comparably with external aids\. Critically, in both age groups, the expectation of list availability was associated with reduced strategy use and poorer memory performance, with strategy use partially mediating the impact of cognitive offloading on memory performance\. Older adults, like younger adults, incur an internal memory cost when offloading information, highlighting the importance of maintaining external store access\.

## [Towards precision medicine in diabetes: pharmacogenomic approaches for MODY and type 2 diabetes with insights from GLIS3 gene variants](../publications/389a78ef5d0b9baa0431.md)

Abhisheka Lenin; Jasmin Sajini Rajayan

Background Diabetes mellitus encompasses a heterogeneous group of metabolic disorders with a significant genetic basis that current standardized treatment protocols fail to adequately address\. Type 2 diabetes in particular is driven by genetic factors that operate independently of lifestyle, with a substantial proportion of patients in South Asian populations developing the disease despite normal body weight and healthy habits\. India presents a uniquely important context for pharmacogenomic research given its extraordinary population stratification across tribal, linguistic, religious, and geographic groups creating a genetic landscape that Western genomic data cannot adequately represent\. Objective This review evaluates pharmacogenomic evidence across monogenic and polygenic diabetes subtypes, presents Indian clinical case studies demonstrating the consequences of genomic misclassification, and positions GLIS3 as an underexplored regulatory gene with cross\-disease relevance spanning neonatal diabetes, Type 1, and Type 2 diabetes\. It further examines the potential for expanded clinical implementation of genotype\-guided therapy, particularly in genetically diverse populations\. Key insights GLIS3 encodes a zinc finger transcription factor that governs beta\-cell development, insulin gene transcription, and endoplasmic reticulum stress protection by functioning as a master regulator of beta\-cell survival rather than acting through a single pathway\. Its association across multiple diabetes subtypes, combined with emerging evidence of population\-specific variants in Indian cohorts, positions it as a compelling future pharmacogenomic target\. However, no GLIS3\-directed clinical testing or therapy is currently available, and its pharmacogenomic utility remains hypothetical pending prospective validation\. Indian pharmacogenomic data further reveal 76 known variants affecting antidiabetic drug response, with higher frequencies of poor metformin response alleles compared to global population findings with immediate clinical implications for one of the world’s highest diabetes\-burden nations\. Conclusion Realizing the potential of precision medicine in diabetes requires population\-specific genomic research, integration of pharmacogenomic testing into national health schemes such as Ayushman Bharat, development of AI\-driven clinical decision tools, and policy frameworks guided by bodies such as ICMR\. Genotype\-guided therapy represents an emerging clinical priority with the potential to improve outcomes in genetically diverse populations where standardized protocols may be suboptimal\.

## [Integrating Structured Writing Workshops with Metacognitive Instruction to Enhance Vietnamese Secondary Students’ Argumentative Writing](../publications/389e6521ba247ebbefc1.md)

Milly Poon; Vinh Long Huy; Chen Lee Lin; Honjo Akira

Argumentative writing requires learners to coordinate reasoning, evidence, organization, audience awareness, language use, and revision, yet secondary\-school EFL students often receive limited support for regulating these interconnected processes\. This qualitative study investigated how integrating structured writing workshops with metacognitive instruction influenced students’ argumentative\-writing performance and their awareness and regulation of writing\. Four EFL teachers and 13 secondary\-school learners participated in the study\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews and classroom observations and analyzed thematically using deductive and inductive coding\. The findings indicated perceived improvements in the organization of arguments, thesis alignment, use of supporting evidence, consideration of counterarguments, and revision of higher\-order textual features\. Structured workshop stages, including planning, drafting, peer response, revision, and editing, provided external scaffolding that made argumentative writing more manageable\. Metacognitive prompts and tools supported learners in identifying goals, considering audience, monitoring claim–evidence relationships, recognizing weaknesses, and evaluating revision priorities\. However, the development was uneven\. Planning improved more consistently than monitoring and independent self\-evaluation, while less\-proficient learners continued to depend on teacher guidance, peer support, and checklists\. Peer feedback also varied in quality, indicating the need for sustained feedback\-literacy instruction\. The study concludes that combining workshop\-based scaffolding with explicit metacognitive regulation offers a promising framework for developing argumentative writing in secondary EFL settings\.

## [Germplasm evaluation and differentiation in Polygonatum kingianum via chloroplast genome resources](../publications/38a232f4e6941edb73a8.md)

Rong Liu; Haili Zhao; Jianhong Xie; Liyan Liang; Jing Wang; Xinping Li; Binbin Liao; Baozhong Duan

Introduction Polygonatum kingianum \(PK\) is an important medicinal crop with diverse germplasm that is difficult to distinguish morphologically, particularly at early developmental stages\. Misidentification can lead to inappropriate regional cultivation and yield losses when germplasm is introduced into unsuitable environments\. Although chloroplast \(cp\) genomes provide abundant sequence information, variation among PK germplasm groups has not been systematically translated into practical markers for authentication\. Methods Here, 39 cp genomes representing seven PK germplasm groups and five related Polygonatum species were comparatively analyzed to characterize genomic variation and develop PCR\-based markers\. Results Rather than extensive structural divergence, the genomes exhibited localized sequence variation\. In an expanded dataset of 118 PK cp genomes, 1,247 single\-nucleotide polymorphisms \(SNPs\) and 263 indels were identified, with higher variant densities in the single\-copy regions than in the inverted repeats\. Integration of comparative alignments, nucleotide\-diversity profiles, and locus\-specific differences identified five regions: ycf2, clpP, rps7\-trnV, atpF\-atpH , and ycf4\-cemA for marker development\. Six primer pairs showed 100% amplification and sequencing success in the tested samples and collectively distinguished the tested PK germplasm groups and related Polygonatum species\. Phylogenomic analyses further resolved PK as a distinct lineage within sect\. Verticillata and revealed cp differentiation among PK germplasm\. Discussion These findings show that cp genomic variation provides additional molecular resources for PK germplasm authentication and characterization and may support the evaluation and utilization of medicinal crop genetic resources\.

## [Society of Nuclear Medicine India Guidelines for Procedure and Reporting of Diuretic Renal Scintigraphy in Adult and Paediatric Patients with Suspected Upper Urinary Tract Obstruction](../publications/38b25ffcff19b9dfee21.md)

Prathamesh Vijay Joshi; Madhusudhanan Ponnusamy; Anish Bhattacharya

Diuretic renal scintigraphy \(DRS\) is the established non\-invasive nuclear medicine technique for simultaneously assessing differential renal function \(DRF\) and upper urinary tract drainage dynamics in patients with suspected obstruction to urinary flow\. This Society of Nuclear Medicine India \(SNMI\) guidelines document aims to provide comprehensive, evidence\-based recommendations for the standardised performance, processing, interpretation, and reporting of DRS in both adult and paediatric patients with dilated upper urinary tract, with due consideration of the Indian context\. The guidelines address patient preparation, hydration protocols, bladder management, radiopharmaceutical selection \(tubular agents such as Tc\-99m L,L EC and Tc\-99m MAG3 are preferred\), furosemide dosing and timing protocols \(F−15, F=0, F\+20\), acquisition parameters, interpretation parameters including semiquantitative metrics such as T½, normalised residual activity \(NORA\), and DRF, as well as structured reporting and interpretation criteria\. Due emphasis is placed on technical quality assurance, recognition of indeterminate and non\-diagnostic studies, radiation safety and as low as reasonably achievable \(ALARA\) principles, and infrastructure requirements applicable to Indian nuclear medicine centres\. The limitations inherent to the technique are discussed, and a note is made on future directions \(e\.g\., artificial intelligence\-assisted analysis and positron emission tomography \(PET\) based renography\)\. These guidelines are intended to support nuclear medicine physicians in delivering consistent, high\-quality DRS studies that guide timely clinical decision\-making and preserve long\-term renal function\.

## [Constructing arbitral authority in CAS jurisdictional reasoning](../publications/38c2919ded396e65d9fd.md)

Zihan Bai

Introduction The Court of Arbitration for Sport \(CAS\) is a central forum for resolving disputes in organized sport, and the legal effect of its jurisdictional provisions depends on how they connect sporting rules, parties, and disputes\. The question is how those connections become legally sufficient for jurisdiction\. Methods Using structured analysis of published decisions and doctrinal interpretation, this article examines how CAS panels make arbitral authority legally operative in jurisdictional reasoning\. It draws on a corpus of 172 public CAS decisions, with decision dates between 13 January 2015 and 2 April 2024, and compares the legal connections through which panels establish or deny authority\. The analysis distinguishes the procedural route to CAS, the instrument providing for arbitration, and the connection binding the parties to that instrument\. Results Federation rules, anti\-doping provisions, Olympic instruments, specific agreements, and procedural conduct perform different functions within these connections\. The comparison shows why participation in organized sport can support jurisdiction in one setting while leaving it unavailable in another\. Discussion This relational account explains how private sporting rules become arbitral authority and why clarity in jurisdictional drafting matters for athletes, clubs, federations, and anti\-doping institutions\.

## [Pika Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature\-inspired Metaheuristic for Solving Complex Real\-world Constrained Optimization Problems](../publications/38d2c6ffcf94fa57ae68.md)

Zeinab Montazeri; Mohammad Dehghani; Raed Abu Zitar; Omar Almomani; Kei Eguchi

With the increasing complexity of real\-world constrained optimization problems, the need for metaheuristic optimization algorithms with the ability to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation has increased\.In this study, the Pika Optimization Algorithm \(PiOA\) is introduced as a new parameter\-free algorithm whose structure is designed based on two complementary Pika behaviors, including environmental vigilance and predator avoidance and food foraging and food\-patch browsing\.In the exploration mechanism, environmental vigilance and predator avoidance are modeled to control the search state; in such a way that the probability of predator presence is determined based on changes in population diversity and each population member independently decides between escaping to a safe region and continuing the environmental search\.Also, the selection of a safe region using better solutions and distance criteria strengthens the movement towards different regions of the search space\.In the exploitation mechanism, the food foraging and food\-patch browsing behaviors are modeled to focus on promising regions and precisely modify the existing positions\.The performance of PiOA is evaluated using 22 CEC 2011 test suite problems and under the same conditions including 20 independent runs and 1000 iterations and compared with 9 well\-known algorithms\.The results show that PiOA ranks first in 21 out of 22 problems and records a success rate of 95\.45%\.Also, the mean, std and boxplot results show that PiOA has good stability in addition to high solution quality\.These findings indicate that the behavioral structure of PiOA can provide an effective framework for global and local search in complex problems\.

## [Biallelic PAX6 Variants in an Adult With Severe Microphthalmia and Preserved Intellectual Function](../publications/38e68bad35a93ffaf628.md)

Karl De Geer; Britt‐Marie Anderlid; Lena K\. Jacobson; Daniel Martín Muñoz; Erik Björck

PAX6 encodes a dosage\-sensitive transcription factor that is essential for eye development\. Heterozygous PAX6 disease is well characterized, but biallelic disease is extremely rare and has been associated with anophthalmia, severe brain malformations, and perinatal lethality\. Here we report the first adult patient with biallelic pathogenic PAX6 variants and describe a novel phenotype that includes severe microphthalmia, anosmia, and autism spectrum disorder, Level 1\. Notably, intellectual function was preserved\. Genome sequencing revealed compound heterozygosity for the missense variant c\.622C&gt;T p\.\(Arg208Trp\), inherited from the patient&\#x27;s mother diagnosed with sclerocornea and iris hypoplasia, and the nonsense variant c\.718C&gt;T p\.\(Arg240\*\), inherited from the patient&\#x27;s father diagnosed with aniridia\. We compare the phenotype and genotype with previously reported biallelic patients and observe that the neurological phenotype of the patient fits the pattern observed in PAX6 haploinsufficiency\. We propose that the severe microphthalmia is the result of haploinsufficiency and a hypomorphic, eye\-restricted effect of the missense variant, which is predicted to affect the DNA\-binding homeodomain of PAX6\. Together, these findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of biallelic PAX6 disease and suggest that the homeodomain may have a tissue\-specific role that is critical for eye development but largely dispensable for brain development\.

## [Mapping the Invisible: Integrating Nighttime Light and Social Sensing to Explore Hidden Cross\-Border Economies](../publications/38ef1843530caf2c6d2d.md)

Xiaofang Zhai; Fan Zhang; Zhifeng Xiao; Haoyang Xu; Wei Qi Yan

Against the backdrop of the continuing spread of cross\-border telecommunications fraud and the scarcity of conventional data, this study examines how publicly accessible multi\-source data can be used to monitor and characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of known or suspected fraud compounds under data\-scarce conditions\. Focusing on eight representative and manually delineated fraud compounds in Myanmar’s border regions, it develops a three\-dimensional “space–time–representation” framework that integrates 2017–2025 VIIRS nighttime lights \(NTL\), Sentinel\-1/2\-derived built\-up area \(BUA\) expansion, and Baidu Index time series as a proxy for Chinese\-language public attention\. Dynamic time warping \(DTW\) is used to examine temporal alignment between NTL dynamics and public attention, while spatial autocorrelation and exploratory grouping based on DTW dissimilarity are applied to characterize spatial clustering and heterogeneous temporal patterns\. The results show that BUA expansion and nighttime brightness are not uniformly coupled across compounds and years\. After excluding partial\-year 2025 observations, the complete\-year 2017–2024 park–year analysis indicates weak aggregate associations between BUA and annual mean NTL, highlighting the need to interpret the two indicators as complementary but non\-equivalent proxies\. NTL changes do not necessarily evolve synchronously with changes in public attention, suggesting potential value for monitoring and prioritization rather than direct early\-warning or verification of illicit activities\. The global Moran’s I of 0\.2476 indicates significant spatial clustering of nighttime\-light values within the defined compound–buffer analysis units\. DTW alignment reveals stronger consistency between nighttime lights and Baidu Index attention in the Daxiang and Dingsheng compounds, whereas KK Park and Yatai City show weaker public\-search responses relative to observed NTL dynamics\. Exploratory grouping identifies three patterns of NTL–public attention correspondence, highlighting heterogeneous relationships between observed nighttime\-light dynamics and external information visibility\. The study demonstrates the complementarity of remote sensing and social sensing data under data scarcity and proposes a replicable approach for remote monitoring, typological characterization, and evidence\-informed governance prioritization of known or suspected fraud compounds\. The proposed approach should be interpreted as a screening and analytical framework that provides directional evidence rather than as direct verification of illicit activity or compound\-specific operational status\.

## [The Influence of Music on Emotional Regulation: A Thematic Review](../publications/39121b85977a7c437287.md)



Emotion regulation is a key concept in psychology\.It refers to the ways people influence the emotions they experience, when they experience them, and how those emotions are expressed\.One of the most influential frameworks in this area is Gross&\#x27;s \(1998\) process model, which distinguishes between antecedent\-focused strategies, such as cognitive reappraisal, and response\-focused strategies, such as expressive suppression\.Music occupies a unique position within this framework\.It can act both as an emotional stimulus that creates feelings and as a tool that people intentionally use to manage those feelings\.This dual role makes music psychologically fascinating, but it also makes it difficult to study\.A single listening experience can both generate an emotion and help regulate that same emotion\.Rather than viewing music as a simple influence on mood, this review treats it as a psychological process in which emotion, cognition, and sound interact with one another\.The review is organised around eight interconnected themes: \(i\) emotion\-regulation strategies and their classification; \(ii\) adaptive and maladaptive outcomes of music use; \(iii\) personality traits and individual differences; \(iv\) neurobiological mechanisms; \(v\) cognitive reappraisal and coping processes; \(vi\) everyday and therapeutic uses of music; \(vii\) musical mechanisms, including feature\-dependent and individual\-dependent effects; and \(viii\) the moderating roles of age, gender, and musical genre\.

This review presents recent advancements in ML applications for adsorption processes\. A wide range of ML techniques including artificial neural networks \(ANN\), support vector machines \(SVM\), random forests \(RF\), gradient boosting methods, convolutional neural networks \(CNN\), graph neural networks \(GNN\), recurrent neural networks \(RNN\), adaptive neuro\-fuzzy inference systems \(ANFIS\), and hybrid optimization frameworks are critically discussed\. The review helps identify improvement in prediction performance, reduction in computational cost, speed of material selection, discovery of the best adsorber, and robust optimization techniques\. Furthermore, the integration of explainable ANN techniques such as SHAP and LIME increases the intuitiveness of the method\. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain regarding dataset standardization, model generalization, experimental validation, and industrial\-scale implementation\. In this study, it is identified that hybrid physics\-informed data\-driven models, digital twins, scalable AI, and autonomous models will support the development of sustainable and efficient adsorption technologies\.

## [Tragverhalten von \(nicht\) vorgespannten Schraube‐Mutter‐Verbindungen im Stahlleichtbau](../publications/392e055e530f7d686370.md)

Die Bemessung nach DIN EN 1993‐1‐3 ist auf Stähle bis S460 beschränkt\. Ferner fehlen Regelungen zur Bestimmung der Beanspruchbarkeit für Durchknöpfen sowie zum Vorspannen von Schraubengarnituren M6 bis M10 für die Ausbildung gleitfester Verbindungen\. In diesen Fällen werden für die Praxis aufwendige Einzelfalluntersuchungen erforderlich\. Jüngste Untersuchungen zum Einsatz von Schraubengarnituren M6 bis M10 haben diese Fragestellungen aufgegriffen und das Scher‐/Lochleibungs‐ sowie das Durchknöpfverhalten geschraubter Verbindungen aus höherfesten dünnwandigen Stählen untersucht\. Ergänzend wurde die Vorspannbarkeit der Schraubengarnituren zur Anwendung in gleitfesten Verbindungen untersucht\. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass das Scher‐/Lochleibungstragverhalten durch das bestehende Bemessungskonzept nach DIN EN 1993‐1‐3 bis zu einem Randabstand von max\. 2 d 0 gut abgebildet werden kann\. ## [Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting](../publications/3933127a2e74c1cc1b9e.md)

Kamil Faber; Katarzyna Filus; Łukasz Pawela

Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information\. This raises the question of which representational changes should be constrained while preserving plasticity\. We therefore introduce Sparse Autoencoder Geometric Anchoring \(SAGA\), which converts a Sparse Autoencoder \(SAE\) trained at each task boundary into local, low\-rank constraints on representation drift\. Replay examples specify where the constraints apply, while leading right singular directions of the encoder Jacobian specify which changes are penalized\. The resulting geometry is input dependent and can be retained without keeping the SAE for subsequent tasks&\#x27; training\. We establish its local relation to latent code matching, define its spectral truncation error, and derive a conditional bound on frozen\-readout drift\. With replay and snapshot history, the method achieves the highest mean Class\-IL accuracy and lowest mean forgetting among the evaluated ER, DER\+\+, ER\-ACE, and SGD baselines on three pretrained ViT\-B/16 benchmarks, with accuracy gains of 12\.15, 4\.79, and 3\.22 percentage points over the strongest conventional baseline on CIFAR\-100, CUB\-200, and ImageNet\-R, respectively\. From scratch results are more mixed, while rank ablations and geometry controls show that SAE\-induced low\-rank geometry offers useful stability\-plasticity trade\-offs\.

## [Evaluating the Performance of Electrocardiography and Immunological Markers \(IL\-6, TNF\-α, and C\-Reactive Protein\) in the Diagnosis of Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Using Echocardiography as the Gold Standard](../publications/393edc4f07125c7a6e5b.md)

Hameed A\. Alhibaly; Basama Edan Kadum; Ban Waheed Hussein Bdair; Satar Jabbar Rahi Algraittee; Abdul Amir H\. Kadhum

Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ECG criteria and inflammatory markers—interleukin\-6 \(IL\-6\), tumor necrosis factor\-alpha \(TNF\-α\), and C\-reactive protein \(CRP\)—in detecting LVH\. Materials and Methods: A total of 241 patients with concentric LVH confirmed by ECHO were included and categorised into ECG\-positive and ECG\-negative groups\. Additionally, 50 age\-matched controls without LVH were recruited\. The diagnostic performance of Sokolow–Lyon, Cornell voltage, and Peguero–Lo Presti ECG criteria was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy\. Serum levels of IL\-6, TNF\-α, and CRP were analysed across different levels of left ventricular mass index \(LVMI\)\. Results: Significant differences were observed between ECG groups in interventricular septal thickness, left ventricular diameter, and LVMI \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. ECG criteria demonstrated low sensitivity \(10\.37%–20\.75%\) but high specificity \(up to 100%\), with limited overall accuracy\. In contrast, IL\-6, TNF\-α, and CRP levels were significantly elevated in patients with severe LVH \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions: ECG criteria show high specificity but limited sensitivity in diagnosing LVH\. Elevated inflammatory markers correlate strongly with disease severity, suggesting their potential role in improving diagnostic accuracy\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Applications for Early Disease Detection in Healthcare Systems](../publications/39462353285b5f9a223c.md)



With delayed access to specialist expertise and subjective interpretation by clinicians and workload limiting the ability to access parts of the pathway, early disease detection is one of the most impactful levers that can be used to improve patient outcomes and reduce the cost of care\.Medical image analysis, electronic health records \(EHR\), genomic data analysis, and analysis of physiological signals are all examples of medical data that can be transformed by artificial intelligence \(AI\) and especially machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\), as there is no way they could be analyzed at the same scale and speed as would be possible by a human being\.In this paper we bring together existing evidence of the use of AI in early detection in oncology, cardiology, neurology, dermatology, ophthalmology and critical care\.It discusses the mathematical approaches used for their analysis such as the use of convolutional neural networks for image analysis and recurrent networks for time\-series analysis of physiological data, and compares their reported diagnostic performance with that of conventional clinical analyses\.The paper also examines real\-world challenges to adoption, such as standardization of data, algorithmic bias, regulatory approval processes and clinician acceptance, and proposes some solutions\.The results suggest that AI systems perform as well as or better than humans in precisely defined detection tasks but will not automatically translate this to better population health outcomes without attention to data quality, the need to integrate AI systems into workflows, and the need to ensure that everyone has access to them\.The paper ends with policy, research and system recommendations for maximizing early detection programmatic value while responsibly scaling these initiatives\.

## [Data\-Driven Selection of Parametric and Travelling Fire Models for Performance\-based Fire Design](../publications/395e448d1477e57052a6.md)

Qingfeng Xu; Mohammad Javad Moradi; Hamzeh Hajiloo; Charlie Hopkin; Jun Heng Low; Lee Cunningham; Yong Wang

Selecting appropriate design fire models remains a key unresolved challenge in performance\-based structural fire engineering, where the applicability of the Eurocode EN 1991\-1\-2 parametric fire curve and travelling fire \(TF\) models is not clearly defined\. This study proposes a quantitative threshold for selecting between the EN and TF models based on full\-scale experimental results\. A total of 222 available full\-scale natural fire experiments are summarised and used as benchmark data\. For each experiment, average compartment fire temperature\-time curves are predicted using the EN and TF models, respectively, and their predictive accuracy is quantitatively assessed to determine the best\-performing model for each fire test\. A logistic regression \(LR\) model is then derived from the available dataset to predict the best\-performing model for a given set of fire inputs\. As the required TF model inputs, namely the peak fire temperature, heat release rate per unit area, and fire spread rate, were not reported in the experimental data, a sensitivity study is conducted to evaluate their influence on the derived LR model\. The results show that the LR model is most sensitive to the assumed fire spread rate\. Therefore, three applicability segments are introduced into the LR model to cover a wider range of fire scenarios\. The proposed LR model achieves an average training accuracy of 0\.736 and an ROC\-AUC of 0\.808\. A probabilistic risk assessment case study using Monte Carlo simulation demonstrates that the proposed LR model reduces both over\- and under\-design compared with EN\-only or TF\-only methods, providing a more balanced and reliable framework for current performance\-based structural fire design\.

Results The EP group had lower serum progesterone, initial β \-hCG, 48\-hour β \-hCG change rate, and endometrial thickness, and higher abnormal adnexal ultrasound detection \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Multivariate analysis showed log progesterone, abnormal adnexal ultrasound, previous EP, and M6NP high\-risk classification \(≥5%\) were independent predictors \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. All AUC values are apparent/in\-sample estimates\. Ultrasound \+ M6NP had an apparent AUC of 0\.913; adding progesterone increased it to 0\.947\. In the M6NP high\-risk subgroup, progesterone plus ultrasound had an apparent AUC of 0\.945 and specificity of 91\.67%\. Because the model was developed and evaluated in the same dataset without bootstrap or internal validation, estimates are preliminary and require external validation\. Conclusion Internally unvalidated analysis, serum progesterone combined with transvaginal ultrasound was associated with improved apparent diagnostic accuracy for EP in PUL, especially within M6NP risk stratification\. These estimates are apparent/in\-sample, preliminary, and hypothesis\-generating\.

## [The Digital Afterlife of the Self: A Derridean Reading of Ruth Ozeki’s A Tale for the Time Being in the Age of Algorithmic Memory](../publications/39828caa30b58ec0fa0a.md)

Sanjida Afrose; Shaon Gharami

This study represents how personal memory, grief, and human connection are revealed in Ruth Ozeki’s novel A Tale for the Time Being through Jacques Derrida’s theory of hauntology\. The primary purpose of this research is to scrutinize how the novel contrasts physical life\-writing, such as handwritten diaries, with modern digital networks to understand how we preserve memories and process loss today\. Using a qualitative content analysis methodology, this paper conducts a close textual reading of the novel in relation a close textual reading of the novel close to Derrida’s concepts of spectrality, the visor effect, and the work of mourning\. The key findings reveal that while digital algorithms flatten human grief into permanent data that refuses to fade, physical vestiges require a patient, empathetic reader to bring the past back to life\. Furthermore, combining Derrida’s ideas about ghosts with Zen Buddhist concepts of temporal non\-duality shows that technology alone cannot replace genuine human care in honouring the dead\. Ultimately, the project concludes that reading serves as an active ethical commitment\. Digital surveillance and algorithmic memory are forever shaping our world, but textual interaction creates an essential space for empathy, hospitality and meaningful mourning\.

## [DINAMIKA TECHNOSTRESS : ANALISIS PERAN AI LITERACY PADA PEKERJA INDUSTRI MULTIMEDIA KREATIF DIGITAL](../publications/39883907abb323bdfa22.md)

Muhammad Wildan Asy&\#x27;ari; Arfin Nurma Halida

The advancement of \(AI\) technology in the workplace has introduced a new psychological challenge in the form of technostress, particularly among workers with high dependence on AI use in their daily work\. This study aims to measure the effect of AI literacy on technostress among digital creative multimedia industry workers\. The research hypothesis states that there is a significant effect of AI literacy on technostress\. This study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design involving 230 digital creative multimedia industry workers employed as full\-time, freelance, part\-time, or intern workers, selected through purposive sampling\. Data were collected using the MAILS \(Meta AI literacy Scale\) and Technostress Scale instruments, then analyzed using a simple linear regression test\. Results showed that AI literacy has a significant positive effect on technostress, although with a relatively small contribution\. This finding differs in direction from previous research on student samples, indicating that the relationship between AI literacy and technostress depends on the characteristics of the population studied\. These findings imply that improving AI competency among digital creative multimedia industry workers should be accompanied by realistic work\-expectation management and organizational support, given that high technological mastery does not automatically reduce the risk of technostress\. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi \(AI\) dalam dunia kerja turut memunculkan tantangan psikologis baru berupa technostress, terutama pada pekerja dengan tingkat ketergantungan tinggi terhadap penggunaan AI pada pekerjaan sehari\-hari\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengukur pengaruh AI literacy terhadap technostress pada pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital\. Hipotesis penelitian menyatakan terdapat pengaruh signifikan antara AI literacy terhadap technostress\. Penelitian ini memakai pendekatan kuantitatif dengan menetapkan desain korelasional pada 230 pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital berstatus pekerja full time, freelance, part time, atau magang, yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling\. Data penelitian dikumpulkan dengan instrumen MAILS \(Meta AI literacy Scale\) dimensi AI literacy dan Technostress Scale, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji regresi linier sederhana\. Hasil penelitian menyimpulkan AI literacy berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap technostress, meskipun dengan kontribusi yang tergolong kecil\. Temuan ini berbeda arah dengan penelitian terdahulu pada sampel mahasiswa, mengindikasikan bahwa hubungan antara AI literacy dan Technostress bergantung pada karakteristik populasi yang diteliti\. Temuan ini mengimplikasikan bahwa peningkatan kompetensi AI pada pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital perlu disertai penataan ekspektasi kerja dan dukungan organisasi, mengingat penguasaan teknologi yang tinggi tidak serta\-merta menurunkan risiko technostress\.

## [Personnel technologies in the civil service of the Russian Federation: features, modern challenges, and development directions](../publications/3990293f42d646f74aa2.md)

Regina Esikova; Elena Ivanova; Александр Спиридонов

The system of public civil service is the foundation that ensures the implementation of the state&\#x27;s functions and the quality of public services provided\. To maintain the competitiveness and efficiency of the state, the competence, professionalism, and objectivity of its personnel are of utmost importance\. Personnel technologies, which are a set of targeted methods for influencing personnel, have their own specific features in the public service, which are determined by strict legal regulations, hierarchy, and the public nature of activities, distinguishing them from the approaches used in the private sector\. Due to the active digital transformation of the state apparatus and the introduction of artificial intelligence, the issues of personnel procedures are reaching a qualitatively new level, making this topic particularly relevant for development and further scientific analysis\.

## [Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) dalam Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam: Kejujuran Akademik, dan Tanggung Jawab Mahasiswa](../publications/39978c197e15cab485b0.md)

Riri Indriani; Zhaky Kastia Rahmadhan; Yola Yola

Abstrak\. Penggunaan kecerdasan buatan \(artificial intelligence/AI\) yang semakin luas di perguruan tinggi menimbulkan pertanyaan tentang kejujuran akademik, terutama dalam Pendidikan Agama Islam \(PAI\) yang bertujuan membentuk karakter di samping penguasaan pengetahuan\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran PAI dari sisi kejujuran akademik dan tanggung jawab mahasiswa, dengan mahasiswa UIN Sjech M\. Djamil Djambek Bukittinggi sebagai konteks sasaran\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif jenis studi kepustakaan\. Dua belas dokumen terbitan 2024–2026 yang terdiri atas artikel jurnal, satu makalah prosiding, dan satu buku akademik dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa AI mendukung pembelajaran personal, media interaktif, umpan balik cepat, dan akses terhadap rujukan keagamaan\. Literatur juga melaporkan plagiarisme, kutipan rekaan, ketergantungan berlebihan, menurunnya berpikir kritis, serta informasi keagamaan yang belum terverifikasi\. Prinsip etika Islam, yaitu ṣidq, amanah, tabayyun, ikhlas, dan maṣlaḥah, disintesiskan menjadi lima dimensi tanggung jawab mahasiswa: transparansi, verifikasi, kemandirian berpikir, perlindungan data, dan keadilan\. Tanggung jawab ini perlu ditopang dosen dan institusi melalui kebijakan yang jelas dan asesmen berorientasi proses\. Karena kajian ini tidak memuat data lapangan, kerangka yang dihasilkan perlu diuji secara empiris pada mahasiswa yang bersangkutan\.

## [Catheter\-Related Bloodstream Infections: Epidemiology, Diagnostic Advances, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Prevention Strategies—A Comprehensive Review](../publications/39a9eb3f8a3f30d181ed.md)



Catheter\-related bloodstream infections \(CRBSIs\) remain among the most significant healthcare\-associated infections worldwide, contributing to substantial morbidity, mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs, particularly among critically ill patients requiring prolonged intravascular catheterization\.These infections arise primarily through microbial colonization of catheter surfaces via extraluminal and intraluminal routes, with biofilm formation playing a central role in microbial persistence and therapeutic failure\.The major causative pathogens include Gram\-positive cocci, Gram\-negative bacilli, and Candida species, many of which demonstrate multidrug resistance\.Accurate diagnosis requires integration of clinical findings with microbiological evidence, including paired blood cultures, differential time to positivity, and catheter tip culture\.Advances in rapid molecular diagnostics have improved early pathogen detection and resistance characterization, enabling more targeted therapeutic interventions\.Effective management depends on prompt diagnosis, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and timely decisions regarding catheter removal or salvage\.Prevention remains the cornerstone of CRBSI control and relies on strict aseptic catheter insertion techniques, evidence\-based maintenance bundles, surveillance systems, and antimicrobial stewardship programs\.Emerging innovations, including antimicrobial\-coated catheters, automated surveillance systems, and anti\-biofilm strategies, offer promising opportunities for reducing infection burden\.This review comprehensively summarizes the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostic approaches, antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, management strategies, and prevention measures associated with CRBSIs, while highlighting recent advances and future directions aimed at improving clinical outcomes and strengthening infection prevention practices\.
