## [Klebsiella\-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants](../publications/39c07f437bb1dffd394b.md)

Cale O\. Seymour; Gertrude Ecklu\-Mensah; Yesun Lee; Alexander R\. Nicols; Wesley A\. Cheng; Jaycee M\. Jumarang; Carolyn Jennifer Marentes Ruiz; Jocelyn Navarro; Rafaella Navarro; Yamile Rodríguez Angeles; David Durand; Sarah M\. Allard; Zackary W Taylor; Ruth G\. De León; Theresa Jean Ochoa; Jack A\. Gilbert; Pia S\. Pannaraj

Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide\. Oral rotavirus vaccine \(RVV\) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high\- and low\-income countries and the etiologies are unclear\. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U\.S\. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella\. Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response\. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month\. These results implicate microbiome\-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response\.

## [Optimizing the operation of sediment pass\-through tunnel of Nanhua Reservoir with machine learning and dynamic programming approach](../publications/39c2c2057ee15e2951c4.md)

Chia\-Wen Wu; Frederick NF Chou; Fong\-Zuo Lee; Bin\-Shuei Lin

Sediment accumulation in reservoirs poses a persistent challenge to sustainable water management, particularly during flood events when opportunities for sediment routing emerge\. An innovative approach is introduced to optimize operations of the sediment pass\-through tunnel at Nanhua Reservoir, Taiwan, integrating surrogate modeling with dynamic programming \(DP\)\. The SRH\-2D model is utilized to simulate sediment transport dynamics\. Its high computational demand, however, restricts real\-time use\. An XGBoost\-based surrogate model is thus developed to efficiently predict sediment pass\-through under diverse flood conditions\. This model is paired with a DP framework to identify optimal tunnel operation strategies, maximizing sediment discharge while ensuring flood control and water supply reliability\. Historical flood data from 2008 to 2024 are evaluated to validate the method\. Results show sediment pass\-through increases significantly—reaching 0\.146 MCM during Typhoon Gaemi—compared to 0\.076 MCM in baseline operations, with negligible downstream flood impacts\. Sensitivity analyses highlight inflow rates and sediment concentration as key drivers of routing efficiency\. The proposed methodology provides a practical, computationally efficient solution for real\-time reservoir management\.

## [Formulation and Evaluation of Curcumin Microsponges and their Hepatoprotective Effect against Paracetamol\-Induced Liver Toxicity in Rats: Curcumin microsponges and their hepatoprotective effect](../publications/39c65e55ef600854b547.md)

Gaurav N\. Kasar; Khemchand Rajendra Surana; Pooja Balkrishna Rasal; Aman Upaganlawar; Manoj Mahajan; Sunil Kashinath Mahajan

Curcumin now has numerous pharmacological effects; however, its poor bioavailability limits its therapeutic potential\. This study aimed to formulate curcumin microsponges and assess their effectiveness in shielding rat livers from paracetamol\-induced damage\. The toxicity was induced over a period of 10 days by administering 2 g/kg/day of paracetamol\. Paracetamol severely damages the livers of rats by raising liver function markers such as ALT, AST, ALP, and total bilirubin levels while simultaneously lowering total protein levels\. The mice received oral therapy for 10 days, including 100 mg/kg of curcumin microsponges and 100 mg/kg of plain curcumin \(P\-CUR\)\. On the final day of the therapy, the rats were sacrificed, and the liver was excised for pathological analysis\. Our findings indicate that microsponges exhibit a more potent hepatoprotective effect compared to conventional curcumin\. Curcumin microsponges significantly reduced paracetamol\-induced liver damage, as evidenced by a drop in liver function indicators\. Our research indicates that curcumin microsponges may possess significant hepatoprotective properties\.

## [Precision Medicine in Sickle Cell Disease: From Molecular Pathways to Curative Strategies](../publications/39d03bd9fc13e7641958.md)

Dina Tluli; Omar Tluli; A\. Alroy Karen; Mahd M\. Abujbara; Omar Sorour; Alaa Abdelhamid; Dahab Ghith; Mohamed Abdallah Yassin

Sickle cell disease \(SCD\) is a monogenic β\-globin disorder characterized by hemoglobin S polymerization, hemolysis, and vaso\-occlusion, yet it exhibits remarkable clinical heterogeneity\. Despite advances in supportive care and disease\-modifying therapies, substantial variability in severity, treatment response, and long\-term outcomes persists\. Therefore, this review aims to examine the biological and clinical foundations of precision medicine in SCD, emphasizing genomic modifiers, molecular pathways, and phenotype\-driven therapeutic strategies\. Key pathogenic pathways including hemoglobin polymerization, vascular adhesion, and inflammatory and oxidative amplification have enabled the development of targeted agents such as hydroxyurea, voxelotor, crizanlizumab, and L\-glutamine, each demonstrating domain\-specific targets\. Pharmacogenomic insights, particularly involving fetal hemoglobin regulatory loci \(e\.g\. BCL11A and HBS1L\-MYB\), further elucidate variability in disease expression and therapeutic response\. Emerging curative approaches, including allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, lentiviral gene addition, and CRISPR\-Cas9\-mediated genome editing, represent transformative applications of precision hematology\. Collectively, these advances support a paradigm shift from generalized symptom management toward biologically informed, individualized care\. Continued integration of genomic profiling, biomarker stratification, and equitable implementation frameworks will be essential to translate precision strategies into sustainable improvements in global SCD outcomes\.

## [Towards the automated identification of data constraints in software documents](../publications/39d3bcaf75059c4c239b.md)

Ying Zhou; Miao Miao; Vlad Birsan; Oscar Chaparro; Shiyi Wei; Andrian Marcus

Abstract Data constraints are important business rules that specify the values allowed or required for the data used in a software system\. These constraints are typically described in textual software artifacts \( e\.g\., requirements, developer documents, user manuals, etc\. \)\. In this paper, we focus on automating the task of identifying data constraints in natural language software documents\. In order to automate this task, we first study how data constraints are described in natural language\. Specifically, we studied 546 data constraints described in the natural language artifacts of nine software systems\. We uncovered and documented nine linguistic discourse patterns that stakeholders use to describe data constraints in natural language\. We cast the constraint identification and extraction as a text matching and classification problem\. We explore the suitability of traditional machine learning techniques, using the discourse patterns we discovered, together with other linguistic elements, as features, for automatically classifying sentence fragments as data constraint descriptions\. The best combination of features and learner achieves 63\.63% precision and 61\.40% recall \(62\.34% F1\)\. Automating the extraction of data constraints from natural language text is essential for automating their traceability to code, test generation, compliance analysis, etc\.

## [Analysis of the Effect of ESG Implementation, Financial Performance, and GCG on Firm Value with Profitability as a Mediating Variable in the Indonesian Banking Sector](../publications/39d8611ffcda62ffe7ad.md)

Ricky Andian; Zaenal Abidin

Although the Indonesian banking industry has demonstrated relatively positive growth, several indicators, including credit expansion, the cost of funds, and credit risk, continue to present significant challenges\. These conditions suggest that market participants remain cautious about the industry&\#x27;s future prospects\. This study aimed to examine the effects of environmental, social, and governance \(ESG\) practices, financial performance, and good corporate governance \(GCG\) on firm value, with return on assets \(ROA\) serving as a mediating variable\. The study employed a quantitative approach using panel data from 12 banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange \(IDX\) during the 2021–2024 period, selected through purposive sampling\. Data were analyzed using panel data regression and mediation analysis with EViews 14 software\. The findings were categorized into direct and indirect effects\. The results revealed that the nonperforming loan \(NPL\) ratio had a statistically significant negative effect on ROA, while the loan\-to\-deposit ratio \(LDR\) had a statistically significant negative effect on firm value\. However, none of the independent variables demonstrated statistically significant indirect effects on firm value through ROA\. These findings suggested that credit risk and liquidity management were important considerations in assessing banking performance and firm value, while profitability did not significantly mediate the relationships examined in this study\.

## [DEVELOPING STUDENTS&\#x27; INFORMATION SECURITY COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: A QUASI\-EXPERIMENTAL STUDY IN UZBEK HIGHER EDUCATION](../publications/39e50311d68ad1708033.md)

Mustafoyev Shahzod

Generative AI tools are now part of students&\#x27; everyday academic work, but the information security risks involved are rarely covered in curricula\. Students leak their own and other people&\#x27;s data into external systems, rely on fabricated output and fall for AI\-enhanced social engineering\. This paper reports a quasi\-experimental study of a pedagogical model designed to develop students&\#x27; information security competence in the context of AI tools\. The model is based on a pedagogical classification of AI related threats into four groups \(input data, output, access and account, cognitive\-behavioural\), a five\-stage learning technology in which simulation and reflection are mandatory, and five pedagogical conditions\.

## [What AI Cannot Give Gifted Learners](../publications/39ef02f2dfe78cb8c360.md)

Henry Tirri; Kirsi A\. Tirri

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) has entered gifted education faster than the field has decided what it changes\. This conceptual article argues that the pedagogical question is not whether AI helps\. It is which cognitive work stays with the learner\. Two claims follow\. First, hybrid human–AI intelligence is bilateral\. The learner shapes the AI partner as the partner shapes the learner\. Learners using identical products do not have identical partners\. The resulting advantage accumulates in the partnership rather than the person, invisibly\. Second, the same question asked of moral development divides ethical functioning into two clusters\. High ability confers one and not the other\. AI supplies fluent performance of the first and nothing to the second, and schools assess the first\. Both claims converge\. What matters has stopped being visible in the work a student hands in\. We specify five capacities worth teaching, three testable studies, and one recommendation for practice\.

## [StratFL: Countering Covert Model Poisoning Attacks with Strategic Federated Learning](../publications/39f018b650ce7fc41afe.md)

Manoj Twarakavi; Venkata Sriram Siddhardh Nadendla

Advanced persistent threats \(APTs\) are a major concern in federated learning \(FL\) deployments in critical sectors such as healthcare, and finance\. Traditional defense mechanisms fail to contain APTs due to their intermittent attacking behavior\. This paper addresses a specific type of APT called covert model poisoning \(CMP\) where the attacker intermittently injects poisoned model updates in a covert manner\. The interaction between the FL server and a CMP attacker is modeled as an imperfect repeated game where both players cannot observe each other&\#x27;s actions\. A novel adversarial search algorithm called StratFL is designed alongside novel belief update algorithms at both the server and adversary\. Experiments are designed using MNIST and CIFAR\-10 datasets to evaluate and compare StratFL&\#x27;s performance against state\-of\-the\-art methods\. Empirical convergence of belief update algorithms is demonstrated across various security vignettes\. At the same time, StratFL is found to exhibit an improved accuracy of 10% compared to state\-of\-the\-art methods\.

## [GeoState: Learning View\-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling](../publications/39fcaf8dba6042b7bd4a.md)

Hongchang Liu; Jian Liu; Yujuan Ding; Liang Peng; Xun Jiang; Fei Ma; Xing Xu; Yi Bin

Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models \(GFMs\) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors\. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera\-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict\. We propose GeoState, a view\-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene\-state evolution from camera\-dependent observation\. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi\-view GFM features into a view\-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays\. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately\. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context\-derived scale throughout the rollout without per\-frame scale alignment\. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross\-view querying, and generalizes zero\-shot to KITTI and nuScenes\. Project page: https://hongchang\-liu\.github\.io/GeoState\-project\-page/

## [La revolución de las redes autónomas y la inteligencia artificial agéntica en las telecomunicaciones](../publications/3a08a6aaba0c4bce5c6f.md)

G\. George Ponce de León; Oswaldo Patricio Bonifaz Vallejo; Italo Marcelo Lara Pilco; José David Velín Sagbay; Carlos Eduardo Velástegui Almeida

La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo analizar los avances, aplicaciones, beneficios y limitaciones de las redes autónomas y la inteligencia artificial agéntica en la transformación de las telecomunicaciones\. Se desarrolló una revisión de literatura con enfoque cualitativo y alcance descriptivo\-analítico, considerando 15 publicaciones científicas correspondientes al período 2020–2026\. El análisis documental se organizó en cinco categorías temáticas: evolución de las redes autónomas, inteligencia artificial agéntica y gestión inteligente de redes, eficiencia operativa y optimización de recursos, seguridad y confiabilidad, y sostenibilidad e inclusión digital\. Se diferenciaron los estudios sobre automatización convencional de aquellos relacionados con modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño y sistemas multiagente\. Los resultados identificaron oportunidades para automatizar la administración de redes, asignar recursos dinámicamente, apoyar la toma de decisiones y coordinar agentes inteligentes\. Sin embargo, la evidencia examinada no permitió establecer mejoras cuantitativas uniformes en el rendimiento operativo, el consumo energético o la confiabilidad de los servicios\. Se concluyó que las redes autónomas y la inteligencia artificial agéntica ofrecen oportunidades para desarrollar infraestructuras de telecomunicaciones más inteligentes, adaptables y eficientes\. Se recomienda realizar investigaciones empíricas que evalúen su rendimiento, seguridad, interoperabilidad y sostenibilidad en condiciones reales de funcionamiento\.

## [Whitehead’s symbolic reference as a theory of embodied semiotics: from causal efficacy to meaning](../publications/3a0dda446139727373b9.md)

Yi Yuxi

Abstract Contemporary embodied cognition theories often assume the existence of a mental representation of bodily experience, without explaining how this representation emerges from pre\-reflective bodily processes\. This paper turns to Alfred North Whitehead’s theory of symbolic reference, developed in Symbolism: Its Meaning and Effect\. Whitehead distinguishes two modes of perception: causal efficacy \(the vague, affective, bodily feeling of the world acting upon us\) and presentational immediacy \(the clear, spatialized presentation of sensory data\)\. Symbolic reference is the dynamic integration of these two modes, generating the embodied facts that constitute conscious experience\. We argue that Whitehead’s framework offers a non\-mentalistic, process\-based account of how bodily feelings become meaningful symbols, thereby shedding light on the residual Cartesianism in both phenomenology \(Merleau\-Ponty\) and cognitive linguistics \(conceptual metaphor theory\)\. The paper concludes by outlining implications for a Whiteheadian cognitive semiotics, in which meaning emerges from the environment’s causal efficacy on the living body\.

## [Inteligencia artificial en la administración de justicia: retos para el derecho ecuatoriano](../publications/3a0e9ab477cc09594b24.md)

Martha Cecilia Rosero\-Puetate; Jhon Sebastián Fuertes\-Realpe; Hamilton Fernando Lucero\-Arellano; Angie Michelle Velasco\-Campaña

Artificial intelligence is being incorporated into judicial systems to support management, case\-law search and outcome prediction, and it poses legal and ethical challenges\. The study analysed the challenges facing Ecuadorian law regarding its use in the administration of justice, with attention to risks for due process and regulatory gaps\. The research was qualitative and documentary, with an interpretive review of scholarship, domestic norms, international instruments and comparative studies\. The results indicate that the technology can ease the procedural burden, but it brings algorithmic opacity, bias and risks for reasoning, equality and data protection, and that no specific rule exists for the judicial sector\. It is concluded that regulation based on transparency, meaningful human oversight and training is required\.

## [Many Biases, One Circuit: Post\-Training Tunes a Pretrained Cue\-Routing Mechanism](../publications/3a1d7bce5752e0837f11.md)

Prakhar Gupta; Terry Jingchen Zhang; Zhijing Jin

Language models often abandon a correct answer when the prompt contains a cue, a hint toward a wrong option such as &quot;I think the answer is B\.&quot; Sycophancy and related biases show this failure\. They are often studied separately and blamed on alignment\. We test this view causally, tracing the attention heads behind these biases through the stages of two post\-training pipelines\. In multiple\-choice tests on most models, four cue types rely largely on the same few heads, a shared circuit already present in pretrained models\. Most base models follow cues in plain text\. Fine\-tuning a base model on about 200 generic assistant examples without cues activates these heads in chat format, so cue\-following can be a side effect of assistant tuning\. The final reinforcement learning \(RL\) stage strengthens the effect of cues in almost every comparison\. In Tulu\-3\-8B and OLMo\-2\-7B, we swap the attention patterns of six middle layers between the RL checkpoint and its predecessor\. For suggested\-answer cues, this shifts each checkpoint&\#x27;s cue effect most of the way to the other&\#x27;s level\. Post\-training thus seems to change when and how strongly models use this circuit\. Mitigation for these multiple\-choice biases could target this circuit\.

## [Modern Object Classification Techniques in Automotive Applications](../publications/3a1f25d30a14c627d5bd.md)

Dominciuc

Automotive radar sensors have become a key component of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems \(ADAS\) due to their robustness under adverse weather conditions\. This project presents an object classification approach based on radar point clouds and the analysis of the RadarScenes dataset\. The proposed methodology involves extracting features from radar point cloud data, followed by classification using supervised machine learning\. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine \(LightGBM\) model was trained and evaluated on real\-world radar measurements to distinguish between multiple road user categories, including vehicles, pedestrians, and two\-wheeled vehicles\. The results demonstrate the potential of automotive radar as a reliable perception sensor for intelligent transportation systems and autonomous vehicles\.

## [Pedraza, R\.: The database in Artificial Research by Deduction in the Global Artificial Intelligence](../publications/3a46026ef5f8bf2e28ca.md)



In Global Artificial Intelligence: First Prototype of Global Artificial Intelligence\. London: Ruben Garcia Pedraza\. pp\. 1\-25\. 2025This paper presents the conceptual and structural foundations of the database used in Artificial Research by Deduction within the framework of Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\)\. As the initial and essential stage in the automated scientific research process, the database takes the form of a comprehensive global matrix, designed to integrate all quantifiable factors relevant to human and natural systems—ranging from population demographics and economic indicators to planetary dynamics and astronomical phenomena\. The database is initially constructed from a wide array of national, continental, and international data sources, including unstructured datasets and specific matrices derived from early experiments in Specific Artificial Intelligence for Artificial Research by Deduction \(SAI\-D\)\. Through a rigorous process of standardization, this information is restructured into a unified matrix organized hierarchically into factors, sub\-factors, and potentially sub\-sub\-factors, each defined in quantitative terms and capable of providing a continuous flow of data\. This standardized global matrix serves as the foundational substrate for further stages in the Artificial Research by Deduction process\. In the subsequent replication stage, robotic systems populate the matrix with real\-time data flows, enabling deductive algorithms and GAI itself to identify potential mathematical relationships\. These relationships are evaluated as empirical hypotheses and, if deemed rational, inform the construction of models that feed into GAI’s broader modelling and decisional systems\. Ultimately, the database is not merely a passive repository of information, but an active and evolving structure that supports rational hypothesis generation, model construction, decision\-making, and systemic self\-improvement\. It serves as the empirical backbone for a unified artificial rationality capable of supporting the management and ethical guidance of global systems\.

## [The Mediating Role of Adaptive Strategies in the Relationship between Work\-Related Challenges and Teaching Effectiveness and Job Satisfaction of TVL \(Technical \-Vocational\-Livelihood\) Teachers: A Basis for a Professional Development Program](../publications/3a46459bd951c241eb5d.md)

Esteria T\. Acop

This study examined the mediating role of adaptive strategies in the relationship between work\-related challenges and teaching effectiveness and job satisfaction among Technical\-Vocational\-Livelihood \(TVL\) teachers as a basis for developing a professional development program\. Anchored in the Job Demands–Resources Model, Transactional Theory of Stress and Coping, and Herzberg’s Two\-Factor Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive\-correlational research design with mediation analysis\. Using universal sampling, 40 TVL teachers from five public secondary schools in Bilar, Batuan, and Carmen, Bohol, participated in the study\. Data were collected through a modified and expert\-validated questionnaire using a four\-point Likert scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and regression\-based mediation analysis at a 0\.05 significance level\. Results revealed high levels of work\-related challenges \(M = 3\.05\), adaptive strategies \(M = 3\.43\), and teaching effectiveness \(M = 3\.56\), while job satisfaction was moderate \(M = 3\.17\)\. Student\-related concerns and resource adequacy emerged as the major challenges, whereas technology and artificial intelligence\-assisted teaching received the highest adaptive strategy rating\. Work\-related challenges showed no statistically significant relationships with adaptive strategies, teaching effectiveness, or job satisfaction\. Adaptive strategies were significantly associated with teaching effectiveness \(r = \.392, p = \.012\) but not with job satisfaction \(r = \.003, p = \.986\)\. Moreover, no significant mediating effects were established for either professional outcome\. The findings informed the proposed Adaptive and Industry\-Responsive Professional Development Program, emphasizing instructional innovation, professional collaboration, institutional support, and teacher well\-being\. The study aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 3 \(Good Health and Well\-Being\), 4 \(Quality Education\), and 8 \(Decent Work and Economic Growth\)\. Its potential sustainability contribution lies in strengthening educational quality, institutional responsiveness, teacher welfare, and industry\-relevant workforce preparation through evidence\-based professional development\.

## [Mapping spatial and socioeconomic disparities in public healthcare accessibility in Patna City](../publications/3a5073827231099cf8aa.md)

Akash Kumar; Kiran Kumari

Background Rapid urbanization has intensified spatial inequalities in access to public healthcare in many Indian cities\. In Patna City, the concentration of secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities in central areas creates significant accessibility challenges for peripheral and socioeconomically disadvantaged populations\. This study evaluates spatial and socioeconomic inequalities in healthcare accessibility and identifies potential sites for future public healthcare facilities using an integrated GIS\-based analytical framework\. Methods A mixed\-methods approach was employed by integrating household survey data from 384 respondents with spatial datasets on healthcare facilities, road networks, land availability, and population distribution\. GIS\-based buffer analysis, network analysis, Thiessen polygons, and PCA\-based weighted overlay analysis were applied to evaluate healthcare accessibility and identify suitable sites for new healthcare facilities\. Chi\-square and multiple regression analyses were used to examine the influence of socioeconomic characteristics and travel distance on healthcare satisfaction and utilization\. Results The analysis revealed that over 62% of municipal wards are underserved, with residents in peripheral areas travelling 8–12 km to reach public hospitals, compared with 2–3 km in central wards\. PCA identified population density 29%, underserved service areas 22% and distance from existing hospitals 27% and four priority locations were identified for future healthcare facilities, giving the highest priority to the areas with high population density, underserved service areas and near existing hospitals\. The chi\-square test showed a significant association between income level and healthcare satisfaction χ² = 15\.63, p = 0\.004\. In multiple regression, travel distance β = −0\.472, p &lt; 0\.001, health status β = 0\.096, p = 0\.048, disease severity β = −0\.129, p = 0\.008\), transport mode β = 0\.114, p = 0\.021, and insurance status β = 0\.153, p = 0\.002 were significant contributors to the variation in healthcare utilization and income level, age, gender, education, occupation and household structure were not significant\. The regression model accounted for 74\.2% of the variance in healthcare utilization value is R² = 0\.742\. Conclusions Integrating GIS\-based spatial accessibility analysis with PCA\-derived suitability modelling and socioeconomic analysis provides an objective framework for identifying healthcare service gaps and potential sites\. The proposed approach supports evidence\-based urban health planning and offers a transferable methodology for improving equitable healthcare access in rapidly growing cities with limited healthcare resources\.

## [YAP\-dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading: a conditional knockout RNA\-sequencing study](../publications/3a5f44e864ea474a706a.md)

Xuewu Xing; Alexander N\. Piacentini; Yuki Suzuki; Leonardo A\. Sanchez; Chris Mendias; Scott Alan Rodeo

Background Tendon injuries are prevalent across various populations and significantly impair quality of life, presenting substantial healthcare challenges\. Purpose This study aimed to characterize Yes\-associated protein \(YAP\) \-dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading, using a conditional YAP knockout approach combined with RNA sequencing\. Given that tenocytes in vivo are continuously exposed to mechanical loading, this design was intended to identify genes whose regulation by YAP becomes critical under mechanical challenge\. Methods Employing conditional gene knockout techniques with RosaCreERT2 YAP\-floxed mice and mechanical loading protocols, alongside RNA sequencing and advanced bioinformatics analyses\. Results We identified 54 differentially expressed genes \(DEGs\) in tenocytes after YAP knockout, including six upregulated and 48 downregulated genes\. Notably, upregulated genes included Gzmc and Gm28151, while downregulated genes included Car3 and Rgs2\. Gene Ontology \(GO\) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes \(KEGG\) enrichment analyses highlighted significant pathways, such as the PPAR signaling pathway, emphasizing their relevance in tendon pathophysiology\. Furthermore, CIBERSORTx analysis revealed significant differences in immune cell infiltration, particularly in Treg and CD4 naive T cells, suggesting a link between YAP\-dependent pathways and immune responses in tendon healing\. Drug prediction analyses identified several small molecules interacting with hub genes, including LTC4S and CXCL13, indicating potential pharmacological targets for therapeutic intervention\. Conclusion Despite limitations such as a lack of in vivo validation and small sample size, this research underscores the pivotal role of YAP in tenocyte mechanotransduction and identifies key DEGs and pathways that may inform future therapeutic strategies for tendon injuries\. Future studies should focus on the in\-vivo implications of these findings and explore the potential for immune modulation and pharmacological interventions in tendon repair\.

## [Подієво\-орієнтована архітектура мультиагентних систем на основі великих мовних моделей – агенти як мікросервіси](../publications/3a65ad61871bbef81dd1.md)

С\. В\. Носко; Mykhailo Hulevych; Олексій Коломійцев; Вячеслав Федорович Третяк; О\. Ф\. Галицький; Б\.В\. Гайбадулов; Є\.В\. Моргун; Сергій Клєвцов; Костянтин Корольков; Михайло Бєлоус; Oleksandr Sapelnykov; А\. Д\. Бердочник; Тетяна Кулєшова; Natalia Bielous

У статті запропоновано подієво\-орієнтовану архітектуру мультиагентних систем \(МАС\) на основі великих мовних моделей \(LLM\), у якій кожен агент є незалежним мікросервісом з власним пулом обчислювальних ресурсів, а взаємодія агентів здійснюється завдяки брокеру подій\. Розроблено математичну модель МАС як мережі систем масового обслуговування з розгалуженням і злиттям \(fork\-join\), яка враховує логнормальний час інференсу LLM, обмежену конкурентність агентів, транзієнтні помилки, повторні спроби та динаміку черги під час відмови агента та пікового навантаження\. Удосконалено модель втрат синхронної оркестрації завдяки урахування кореляції повторних спроб\. Синхронну послідовну оркестрацію, синхронну оркестрацію з паралельним розгалуженням і подієву хореографію порівняно аналітично, методом імітаційного моделювання та експериментально на прототипі на основі Redis Streams\. Встановлено, що в стаціонарному режимі латентність визначається критичним шляхом графа задачі і не залежить від способу доставки, тоді як під час відмов агентів і пікових навантажень подієва архітектура зберігає всі задачі без налаштування повторів на боці клієнта ціною їх затримки в черзі\. Проаналізовано чутливість результатів до параметрів синхронної оркестрації та представлено результати експерименту з реальною мовною моделлю\.

## [Translating Service\-Learning Standards Into Practice: A Multiple\-Case Study of Undergraduate Courses](../publications/3a6be8a2cefd1db4085a.md)

Ashley Kathryn Vaughan

Background Service\-learning is widely used in higher education, yet less is known about how principles of high\-quality service\-learning are interpreted and operationalized across undergraduate courses\. Purpose This qualitative multiple\-case study examined how undergraduate instructors interpreted and operationalized principles associated with high\-quality service\-learning using the Standards for Quality Practice as an analytic framework\. Method Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews, open\-ended surveys, and course materials from 11 instructors representing 13 undergraduate service\-learning courses across multiple disciplines and institutions\. Findings lthough only one instructor reported prior familiarity with the Standards, instructors generally described practices aligned with the framework&\#x27;s dimensions\. Instructors shared similar goals but interpreted and operationalized principles in varied, integrated, and context\-dependent ways\. Reflection and curricular integration reflected relatively consistent understandings, whereas meaningful service, student voice, diversity, partnerships, and other dimensions were enacted through multiple approaches\. Course structure, institutional context, community partnerships, and logistical constraints further shaped implementation\. Implications Understanding service\-learning quality requires examining how recommended dimensions are interpreted and enacted within particular contexts\. This perspective has implications for faculty development, institutional support, and future research\.

## [Machine learning\-based risk screening model for depressive symptoms in middle\-aged and elderly cardiovascular disease patients](../publications/3a7b434953de0e4332e3.md)

Mingchen Wang; Hongwei Liu; Wei Liang; Guotao Wang; Guohua Ma

Cardiovascular disease \(CVD\) and depression frequently co\-occur, yet systematic depression screening remains underutilized in routine cardiac care\. This study aimed to develop and compare machine learning algorithms for identifying concurrent depressive symptoms in middle\-aged and elderly CVD patients\. Data from 2,204 participants aged ≥ 45 years with physician\-diagnosed CVD were obtained from the 2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study\. Depressive symptoms were defined as CES\-D10 score ≥ 10 \(prevalence: 54\.1%\)\. Seven algorithms—logistic regression \(LR\), artificial neural networks, XGBoost, LightGBM, decision tree, random forest, and support vector machine—were trained and internally validated\. Feature selection used LASSO regression\. Performance was assessed via AUC\-ROC, Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, with bootstrap correction for optimism\. Among 2,204 participants, 1,193 had depressive symptoms\. The LR model showed strong discrimination \(AUC = 0\.832, 95% CI: 0\.804–0\.860\), though performance differences among the top models were minimal \(AUC range: 0\.826–0\.832\)\. LR was selected for the final nomogram based on its favorable calibration and interpretability\. Significant predictors included loneliness, life satisfaction, self\-rated health, hearing status, gender, ADL score, sleep, and cognitive function\. A web\-based dynamic nomogram tool was developed as a research prototype to facilitate individualized risk estimation and illustrate the model’s potential application\. An LR\-based model using eight accessible variables demonstrated strong discrimination for identifying concurrent depressive symptoms in CVD patients\. The nomogram may serve as a preliminary triage tool to prompt confirmatory assessment; external validation is required before clinical implementation\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scientific Development and Future Directions](../publications/3a7df19d466d25d483d2.md)

Wasim Al\-Shattarat; Khalaf Alhaifi; Yaacob Ibrahim

This study examines the development and intellectual structure of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based financial fraud detection through a bibliometric analysis of 2200 Scopus\- and Web of Science\-indexed journal articles published between 1992 and 2026\. The literature has expanded rapidly, with 89\.6% of publications appearing since 2018 and an annual growth rate of 29\.4%\. Research is concentrated in Computer Science and Engineering, whereas Business and Economics account for 9\.2% of classified publications\. Credit card and payment fraud constitutes the largest research domain \(32\.0%\), followed by banking, loan, and transaction fraud \(14\.3%\), insurance fraud \(12\.2%\), and accounting and financial statement fraud \(9\.9%\)\. Neural networks and deep learning, ensemble and boosting methods, and classical supervised classifiers are the dominant methodological families\. The field has progressively shifted from traditional data\-mining and classical machine\-learning approaches toward deep learning, ensemble methods, graph neural networks, and explainable AI\. Science mapping shows that the intellectual structure remains strongly centered on payment fraud, while accounting and insurance fraud form more distinct research fronts\. Author productivity is highly dispersed, with 88\.9% of authors contributing a single publication, while international collaboration varies considerably across leading countries\. By integrating performance analysis, science mapping, fraud\-domain classification, bibliometric laws, and publication\-growth analysis, the study provides a comprehensive assessment of the field’s development, intellectual structure, and emerging research directions\.

## [Psychometric properties of the novel patient\-reported Functional Impacts of Narcolepsy Instrument \(FINI\) using data from phase 3 clinical trials in narcolepsy type 1](../publications/3a8054a0fbeb91667083.md)

Heather Romero; Yulia Savva; Stephen Crawford; Amy Howerter; Shruti Dave; Helen Doll

Background The Functional Impacts of Narcolepsy Instrument \(FINI\) is a 28\-item patient\-reported outcome measure developed to evaluate key functional impacts in people with narcolepsy type 1 \(NT1\) and 2 \(NT2\) across 6 domains: Tiredness, Cognitive Functioning, Cataplexy, Social Activities, Everyday Activities, Everyday Responsibilities\. This study aimed to assess the FINI&\#x27;s psychometric properties and estimate meaningful within\-patient change \(MWPC\) thresholds in NT1 using pooled data from 2 phase 3 clinical trials evaluating oveporexton in NT1 \( N = 167, NCT06470828; N = 105, NCT06505031\)\. Methodology FINI scale structure, known\-groups validity, convergent/divergent validity, internal consistency reliability, test\-retest reliability, and responsiveness were evaluated\. MWPC thresholds were estimated using anchor\- and distribution\-based approaches\. Results Confirmatory factor analysis supported the FINI 6\-domain scale structure\. The domains demonstrated good known\-groups validity, especially for comparisons between severe and moderate reference measure groups \(most P \-values &lt; 0\.05, standardized effect sizes: 0\.3–0\.9\)\. Convergent/divergent validity was supported by agreement between observed and expected correlation coefficients between FINI domains and reference measures\. Most domains demonstrated good internal consistency \(Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha: 0\.63–0\.90; ≥0\.78 for all except Everyday Activities\)\. Excellent test\-retest reliability was observed for all domains in a subpopulation of participants with a stable condition based on self\-reported Patient Global Impression of Severity scores \(ICC ≥0\.70\)\. Good responsiveness was demonstrated for all FINI domains, supported by correlations between domain and continuous reference measure change scores &gt;0\.35, and with greater improvements in domain scores associated with greater categorical improvements in reference measures \(all P \-values &lt;0\.05, average between\-group standardized response mean across domains: 0\.69\)\. All prespecified anchors exceeded the a priori threshold correlation with FINI domains \(≥0\.30\) and were used to derive MWPC thresholds \(ranges\): Tiredness and Everyday Activities, −35 \(−30 to −40\); Cognitive Functioning and Everyday Responsibilities, −30 \(−25 to −35\); Social Activities, −25 \(−20 to −30\); and Cataplexy, −20 \(−15 to −25\)\. Conclusions The FINI is a robust and valid measure assessing meaningful and important key functional impacts for people with narcolepsy\. These findings support use of the instrument in clinical trials to evaluate treatment benefit in NT1\. Given the FINI&\#x27;s sensitivity to change, it can potentially facilitate treatment decisions and track longitudinal outcomes in clinical practice\.

## [O&\#x27;ZBEK\-INGLIZ MAQOLLARI PARALLEL KORPUSINI YARATISHNING ILMIY VA AMALIY AHAMIYATI](../publications/3a82adfd442392ab0d1b.md)

Boltayeva Muxlisa Muxtorovna

Annotatsiya\.Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek va ingliz tillaridagi maqollar parallel korpusini tuzishning lingvistik, madaniy va texnologik ahamiyati atroflicha o‘rganiladi\. Parallel korpuslar korpus lingvistikasi, qiyosiy paremiologiya va mashinaviy tarjima sohasida muhim manba sifatida xizmat qiladi\. O‘zbek tilining agglyutinativ tabiati va ingliz tilining analitik xususiyatlari o‘rtasidagi farqlar, maqollarning semantik ekvivalentligi, madaniy o‘ziga xosliklari va tarjima strategiyalari tahlil qilishga yordam beradi\.Parallel korpus yaratish orqali frazeologik birliklarni aniq tarjima qilish, madaniyatlararo o‘xshashlik va farqlarni aniqlash, til o‘qitishda haqiqiy kontekstli materiallardan foydalanish, shuningdek, kam resursli tillar uchun NLP modellarini takomillashtirish kabi masalalar hal etilishi mumkinligi ko‘rsatiladi\. O‘zbek xalq maqollari va ularning ingliz tilidagi ekvivalentlari misolida korpusning ta’limiy, ilmiy va amaliy qo‘llanilishi yoritiladi\. Kalit so\`zlar: parallel korpus,paremiologiya,mashina tarjimasi, lingvakultralogiya, sun’iy intellekt Аннотация\. В статье всесторонне рассматривается лингвистическая, культурная и технологическая значимость создания параллельного корпуса узбекских и английских пословиц\. Параллельные корпуса служат важным ресурсом в таких областях, как корпусная лингвистика, сравнительная паремиология и машинный перевод\. Исследование позволяет проанализировать различия между агглютинативным строем узбекского языка и аналитическими характеристиками английского языка, а также вопросы семантической эквивалентности, культурной специфики и стратегий перевода пословиц\. Показано, что создание параллельного корпуса способствует решению таких задач, как точный перевод фразеологических единиц, выявление межкультурных сходств и различий, использование аутентичных контекстуальных материалов в преподавании языков и совершенствование моделей обработки естественного языка \(NLP\) для языков с ограниченными ресурсами\. Образовательный, научный и практический потенциал корпуса иллюстрируется на примерах узбекских народных пословиц и их английских эквивалентов\. Ключевые слова: параллельный корпус, паремиология, машинный перевод, лингвокультурология, искусственный интеллект Abstract:This article thoroughly explores the linguistic, cultural, and technological significance of constructing a parallel corpus of proverbs in Uzbek and English\. Parallel corpora serve as a vital resource in the fields of corpus linguistics, comparative paremiology, and machine translation research\. The study examines the structural differences between the agglutinative nature of Uzbek and the analytic character of English, as well as issues related to semantic equivalence of proverbs, cultural specificity, and translation strategies\. It is demonstrated that creating such a parallel corpus makes it possible to address several important tasks: achieving precise translation of phraseological units, identifying cross\-cultural similarities and differences, utilizing authentic contextual materials in language teaching, and improving natural language processing models for low\-resource languages\. Using examples of Uzbek folk proverbs and their English equivalents, the educational, scientific, and practical applications of the corpus are illustrated\. Keywords: parallel corpus,paremiology,machine translation, linguoculturalogy, artificial intelligence\(AI\)

## [ФИЛОСОФСКИЙ АНАЛИЗ ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ ЧЕЛОВЕЧЕСКИХ СПОСОБНОСТЕЙ, ТВОРЧЕСТВА И ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА В УСЛОВИЯХ ВЗАИМОДЕЙСТВИЯ С ИСКУССТВЕННЫМ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТОМ](../publications/3a941a99d368765c7b74.md)

Котова С\.А\.

Настоящая статья предлагает философский анализ глубинных трансформаций человеческих способностей, творчества и интеллекта, происходящих в контексте растущего взаимодействия с системами искусственного интеллекта \(ИИ\)\. Анализ выходит за рамки функционального рассмотрения ИИ как инструмента, фокусируясь на его онтологических, эпистемологических, феноменологических и этических измерениях\. ## [DNA methylation analysis of aortic wall tissue in ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection](../publications/3a94d3301ab1ad67a266.md)

Irina A\. Goncharova; А\. А\. Зарубин; Anton Markov; S\. А\. Shipulina; Н\. П\. Бабушкина; Iuliia A\. Koroleva; Aleksei A\. Sleptcov; Maria S\. Nazarenko

Ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection are life\-threatening cardiovascular conditions\. However, the epigenetic regulatory mechanisms within aortic cells underlying these pathologies remain poorly understood\. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated genes \(DMGs\) in aortic tissues from patients with ascending aortic dilatation/ aneurysm and dissection by performing a re\-analysis of publicly available DNA methylation datasets\. A re\-analysis was conducted on three DNA methylation datasets \(GSE50192, GSE202047, GSE84274\) from the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip\. To account for tissue heterogeneity, cellular deconvolution was performed using the HEpiDISH algorithm and a custom reference panel of cell\-type\-specific CpG sites for key vascular cell types \(endothelial cells, fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, immune cells\)\. Our re\-analysis revealed that aortic dissection and bicuspid aortic valve patients with aortic dilatation/aneurysm exhibit distinct DNA methylation profiles compared to intact aorta\. These pathologies differ from each other in the number and the spectrum of DMGs\. The adjustment for cellular heterogeneity eliminated the majority of the initially identified DMGs\. However, this correction helped to make an assessment of vascular inflammation, characterize its impact on aortic wall stability, and identify genes with differential DNA methylation associated with the disease phenotypes, rather than with inter\-group heterogeneity\. The genes NFIX , PCDH7 , MED13L , LMO4 , DIP2C , PLEKHF1 , NKD1 , C10orf41 \( ZNF503\-AS2 \), ARAP2 , TBX3 , and TBX5 , which remained in the DMG status after adjustment for cellular composition and are expressed in individual cells/whole aortic tissue, can be considered as new candidate genes for the development of aortic dilatation/aneurysm in patients with bicuspid aortic valve\. NFIX, LMO4, DIP2C, C10orf41 \(ZNF503\-AS2\), MED13L, TBX3, TBX5 are transcriptional regulators or modulators; NKD1 is a recognized inhibitor of the Wnt pathway\. Our findings highlight the necessity of a rigorous approach to cohort design, which includes comprehensive phenotyping \(encompassing aortic valve morphology\) and underscore the importance of future single\-cell investigations\.

## [Pengaruh Pengendalian Persediaan Bahan Baku dan Efisiensi Biaya terhadap Kualitas dan Kelancaran Proses Produksi](../publications/3a9620a984a3f500a60f.md)

Salsa Bila; Rendi Rendi; Suarni Norawati; Henrizal Henrizal; Mustafa Kamal

This study aims to analyze the effects of raw material inventory control and cost efficiency on the quality and smoothness of the CPO production process at PKS PT\. Mitra Bumi Bangkinang\. The study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory design\. The population consisted of 85 employees involved in production activities, all of whom were selected as the sample using a saturated sampling technique\. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Square\-Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) with SmartPLS\. The results showed that raw material inventory control had a positive and significant effect on production quality, while cost efficiency also had a positive and significant effect on production quality\. Raw material inventory control and cost efficiency each had a positive and significant effect on the smoothness of the production process\. In addition, production quality had a positive and significant effect on the smoothness of the production process\. These findings indicate that raw material inventory management, cost efficiency, and production quality are interrelated in supporting the smoothness of the CPO production process\.

## [Characterising and Analysing Retrieval\-Augmented Generation Techniques](../publications/3aa4913374155966214d.md)

Emmanuel Igbekele; Olawande Daramola

The advent of Large Language Models \(LLMs\) across many application domains has increased the need for Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) to reduce hallucinations and improve LLM performance\. Thus far, several RAG techniques with impressive features and capabilities have been proposed in the literature, making it a herculean task to select the most appropriate RAG techniques for specific problem scenarios\. Thus, we propose a conceptual framework comprising main dimensions and sub\-dimensions for characterising \(defining &quot;what it is&quot;\) and analysing \(defining &quot;how well it does&quot;\) existing RAG techniques\. The conceptual framework was developed through a qualitative analysis of the attributes of RAG techniques reported in the literature\. It can serve as a pre\-empirical filtering mechanism for researchers and practitioners in selecting the highest\-fit RAG candidates that meet specific user and task requirements before empirical benchmarking of RAG techniques, which can be computationally and financially expensive\.

## [SAFETY CULTURE AND MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES DRIVING ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS IN MARITIME TRANSPORT](../publications/3aa6761852ea0c3e88a8.md)

Onvara Kamkleang; Bharis Hongsakul; Wattana Srithaworn; Pipatpong Yalangkan; Mallika Subongkod

This study empirically investigates how safety culture, customer relationship management \(CRM\), and quality management jointly drive organizational effectiveness within Thailand’s maritime transport sector\. Grounded in the Resource\-Based View \(RBV\) theoretical framework, the research examines these vital intangible capabilities as synergistic drivers of sustained competitive advantage\. Using a quantitative approach, the study collected empirical data from 270 maritime transport organizations through targeted executive surveys and analyzed them using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The findings robustly reveal that safety culture significantly and directly enhances both CRM and quality management, while concurrently exerting a direct positive effect on overall organizational effectiveness\. Furthermore, CRM and quality management serve as crucial internal mediating mechanisms that significantly boost operational success\. Ultimately, the study highlights that safety culture is not merely a regulatory compliance requirement but a foundational strategic resource\. Integrating safety protocols with robust relationship and quality systems fundamentally empowers maritime firms to achieve sustainable organizational effectiveness amidst intensifying global competition\.

## [Beyond sanctions: where the costs of nursery pollination are borne](../publications/3ab3791655bb2c163100.md)

Kenji Suetsugu

Beyond sanctions: where the costs of nursery pollination are borneNursery pollination mutualisms bring cooperation and conflict into sharp focus: adult insects pollinate flowers, whereas their offspring consume plant tissues\.Wu et al\. \(2026, https://doi\. org/10\.1111/nph\.71476\)suggest that the stability of pollination mutualisms depends not only on limiting damage but also on which plant tissues larvae consume and how effectively plants buffer the resulting fitness consequences\.Their system also raises the question of when those consequences feed back into population dynamics\.Because greater reproductive success in one partner can directly reduce fitness in the other, nursery pollination mutualisms have become important models for understanding how cooperation persists despite conflict \(Bronstein, 2001;Sakai, 2002;Dufa€ y &amp; Anstett, 2003\)\.In classic fig, yucca, and Glochidion systems, plants constrain overexploitation through selective abortion, host sanctions, or related forms of partner control \(Pellmyr &amp; Huth, 1994;Goto et al\., 2010;Jand er &amp; Herre, 2010\)\.Yet, stable interactions need not always depend on penalizing pollinator offspring\.In Sambucus sieboldiana, for example, fruit abortion limits further maternal investment while allowing seed\-consuming Heterhelus larvae to complete development in fallen fruits \(Kawashima et al\., 2026\)\.Such cases invite a broader question: can mutualisms also persist by reorganizing where, when, and by whom the costs of cooperation are borne?Wu et al\. provide a compelling case study involving the endangered aquatic plant Ottelia jingxiensis\.Shore flies \(Hydrellia sp\.\) are primary pollinators of O\. jingxiensis, whereas the parasitoid wasp Chaenusa naiadum provides supplementary pollination\.Nectarless female flowers resemble nectar\-producing male flowers, consistent with imperfect Bakerian mimicry\.Shore flies lay eggs predominantly on the persistent calyces of female flowers, but their larvae then migrate down the scapes to submerged leaves, where they feed and pupate; no feeding on ovaries or seeds was observed\.Oviposition and larval feeding are therefore spatially decoupled, redirecting offspring damage from reproductive to vegetative tissues\.A related tritrophic association involving pollination, leaf mining, and parasitism occurs in Stratiotes aloides \(Katzenberger &amp; Zacharias, 2015\), but Wu et al\. explicitly connect this natural history to mechanisms that may stabilize the mutualism\.

## [Enhancing Interpretability in Skin Lesion Diagnosis Using RBBMO\-ViT–VGG19 Hybrid Framework with Intra\-class Consistency and Inter\-class Discrimination](../publications/3ab474ef50ed2bf272e8.md)

Praveena S; T\. Veeramakali

The skin lesions are need to be accurately and promptly recognized for an effective treatments and favourable prognoses\.Nevertheless, the common of existing deep learning model only focus on lesion classification, leaving out the simultaneous prediction of important morphological and colorimetric characteristics that are essential for interpretability\.To enhance the interpretability of automated skin lesion analysis, this paper develops an improved hybrid framework that incorporates optimization\-driven deep learning\.An Adaptive Non\-Local Mean \(ANLM\) filter is exploited to reduce image noise to maintain structural details\.Consequently, the Type\-2 Fuzzy C\-Means \(T2FCM\) clustering is exploited to segment lesion zones for accurate boundary identification\.The incorporation of Vision Transformer \(ViT\) and VGG19 is deployed for feature extraction to capture both global contextual patterns and hierarchical texture representations\.To enhance feature separability in the latent space, the framework maximizes inter\-class discrimination while encouraging intra\-class consistency\.A sparse auto encoder compresses the highdimensional perturbation space to lessen duplication while preserving meaningful representations\.Moreover, t\-SNE visualization latent space eliminates unnecessary perturbation samples and enhances visualization clarity\.Red\-Billed Blue Magpie Optimization \(RBBMO\) is employed for parameter refinement to enhance classification boundaries and stabilize convergence\.Local Interpretable Model Agnostic Explanations \(LIME\) is utilized to develop perturbation based interpretations that guarantee explainability\.When compared to traditional explainable AI techniques, experimental outcomes implemented in Python tool show better diagnostic accuracy of 99\.02% in single run evaluation and 99\.44% ± 0\.82% across five random seeds\.Thus, the suggested method enhances automated dermatological diagnostic systems&\#x27; transparency, dependability and clinical effectiveness\.

## [Associations Among Reading\-Log\-Based Digital Reading Frequency, Academic Orientation, and EFL Students’ Reading Comprehension](../publications/3abc88ed560dc12dd896.md)

Julia Wafiq Azizah; Munir Munir; Auliyanti Sahril Nurfadhilah

Frequent access to digital texts does not reveal how often EFL students sustain English reading or whether their reading serves academic purposes\. This study examined two reading\-log indicators of Digital Reading Frequency \(DRF\) and Academic Digital Reading Orientation \(ADRO\) in relation to Reading Comprehension \(RC\) among EFL students\. Using a quantitative correlational design, 116 of 122 initial participants were retained after recording at least three valid English digital reading sessions during a four\-week self\-reported log; a valid session lasted at least 10 minutes\. ADRO was calculated as each student’s proportion of valid sessions classified as academically oriented based on text type, stated reading purpose, and title or brief description\. RC was measured using a researcher\-developed 30\-item test that was pilot\-tested with 37 students outside the main sample and showed high reliability \(α = \.923\)\. Descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rho, and multiple linear regression were used\. Students recorded a mean of 6\.50 valid sessions over four weeks, while the mean student\-level ADRO score was \.3794\. DRF \(ρ = \.455, p &lt; \.001\) and ADRO \(ρ = \.377, p &lt; \.001\) were both positively associated with RC\. The regression model explained 35\.4% of the observed variance \(R² = \.354\), with both DRF \(β = \.430, p &lt; \.001\) and ADRO \(β = \.392, p &lt; \.001\) remaining independently significant\. These relationships are associative rather than causal\. The findings suggest that both regular English digital reading and academically purposeful text selection may deserve instructional attention, but neither should be interpreted as a tested intervention\.

## [The hypothalamic orexin–medial prefrontal cortex pathway modulates susceptibility to depression in the learned helplessness paradigm in male mice](../publications/3abe8aff1366691d5ca7.md)

Ting Mi; Zhenquan He; Baocong Yu; Qin Li; Guangyuan Lu; Jie Hao; Jiandong Niu; Suya Ma; Weifang Rong; Jianguo Niu

Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder primarily characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness\. The orexinergic system plays a crucial role in stress\-induced depression; however, the precise mechanisms remain unclear\. The medial prefrontal cortex \(mPFC\), a major target of orexinergic projections, is essential for emotional regulation\. This study suggests that impaired orexinergic input to the mPFC underlies depression\-like behaviors in murine models\. In the learned helplessness \(LH\) paradigm, the majority of male mice subjected to inescapable foot shocks developed depression\-like behaviors \(classified as LH\-susceptible\), whereas a subset displayed resilience \(classified as LH\-resilient\)\. LH\-susceptible mice exhibited a reduced number of orexin \+ neuronal somata in the hypothalamus, along with decreased expression of prepro\-orexin mRNA \. Correspondingly, the mPFC of these mice displayed decreased density of orexinergic terminals and lower Orexin A levels\. In contrast, LH\-resilient mice maintained stable hypothalamic orexin neuron counts, exhibited increased prepro\-orexin mRNA expression, and preserved orexinergic terminal density in the mPFC\. Chemogenetic activation of the hypothalamic orexin–mPFC pathway alleviated depression\-like behaviors in LH\-susceptible mice through Orexin A signaling\. Conversely, inhibition of this pathway induced depression\-like behaviors in LH\-resilient mice\. Additionally, LH\-susceptible mice showed decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons of the mPFC, which was improved by activation of hypothalamic orexinergic inputs; this improvement was attenuated by administration of an orexin receptor 1 \(OX1R\) antagonist\. Collectively, these findings implicate the hypothalamic orexin–mPFC pathway as a pivotal regulator of excitatory synaptic transmission and suggest its involvement in modulating individual variability in susceptibility and resilience to depression\. Significance statement Depression is a highly prevalent emotional disorder characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness under stress\. This study demonstrates that the orexinergic system is critical for modulating resilience to aversive stimuli\. Using the learned helplessness \(LH\) mouse model, we found that LH\-susceptible mice, but not LH\-resilient mice, show compromised hypothalamic orexinergic projections to the medial prefrontal cortex \(mPFC\), together with decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons\. Activation of the hypothalamic orexin–mPFC pathway alleviates depression\-like behaviors in susceptible mice through Orexin A, while inhibition of this pathway induces depression\-like phenotypes in resilient mice\. These findings identify orexinergic signaling as a promising therapeutic target for depression\.

## [Improving 24\-h surface\-drifter trajectory prediction around the Korean Peninsula using a multi\-source machine learning framework](../publications/3ac1dd3dc27d37c805d4.md)

Heejun Kim; Ji\-Chang Kim; Jin\-Yong Choi; Do\-Youn Kim; Choong\-Ki Kim

Predicting surface\-drifter trajectories is vital for material transport studies, marine hazard response, and analyses of upper\-ocean circulation\. However, this task remains challenging because winds, tides, mesoscale currents, and waves interact nonlinearly in ways that are difficult to represent in conventional drift\-forecasting frameworks\. This study developed a multi\-source machine learning framework for drifter trajectory prediction around the Korean Peninsula\. The framework uses oceanic model outputs from HYCOM, TPXO, and SCHISM, together with atmospheric and wave forcings from ERA5, as environmental input variables\. An Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\)\-based surrogate model was trained to estimate the zonal and meridional components of drifter velocity, and the resulting velocity estimates were time\-integrated to reconstruct 24\-h trajectories\. Model performance was evaluated against independent drifter observations and compared with a SCHISM\-based OpenDrift simulation, while SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis was used to examine regional variations in input\-variable attributions\. Applied to the marginal seas around the Korean Peninsula, the proposed approach improved 24\-h trajectory prediction, reducing distance RMSE from 9\.73 to 7\.49 km \(23%\) and increasing the normalized cumulative Lagrangian separation skill score \(NCLS\-SS\) from 0\.47 to 0\.57 \(21%\) over the independent test set\. Performance gains were observed across the tide\-dominated western, mixed southern, and eddy\-influenced eastern subregions\. The SHAP results further revealed systematic regional contrasts in the attribution patterns of the environmental inputs across these dynamical regimes\. These results indicate that the proposed framework offers a practical and interpretable approach for short\-term surface\-drift forecasting in heterogeneous coastal and marginal\-sea environments\.

## [Intracardiac echocardiography during invasive electrophysiological procedures](../publications/3acd88fb6950f4463833.md)

Petr Peichl; Stylianos E\. Tzeis; Marta Skowrońska; Dimitrios Asvestas; Jakub Marek Baran; Michela Casella; Rubén Casado\-Arroyo; Matevž Jan; Josef Kautzner; Jens Erik Nielsen‐Kudsk; Péter Kupó; Andrej Pernat; Nándor Szegedi; Vedran Velagić

Intracardiac echocardiography \(ICE\) is an imaging technique that provides real\-time, detailed visualization of intracardiac structures during various interventional procedures performed in the electrophysiology laboratory\. Over the past decades, ICE has evolved beyond simply assisting with transseptal puncture, becoming an auxiliary tool in numerous aspects of cardiac interventions\. This scientific statement offers a comprehensive, systematic overview of current applications of ICE across different clinical scenarios\. The existing evidence regarding the benefits of ICE is primarily derived from observational studies, which complicates the formulation of definitive advice for its clinical use\. Thus, this document aims to serve as a practical roadmap, emphasizing the key benefits of the technique\. The document covers fundamental principles of ICE imaging, standardized views, its role in transseptal puncture, ablation of supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, reduction of procedural radiation, early detection and management of periprocedural complications, identification of infective endocarditis, and the role of ICE for endomyocardial biopsy and left atrial appendage occlusion procedures\.

## [Catalysts Augmenting the Synthesis of Chiral Compounds and their Future Prospects: A Review](../publications/3acf0a70fbf3b64b3a0e.md)

Mebalari Thangkhiew; Ridip Kalita; Ridahunlang Nongkhlaw; Ridahunlang Nongkhlaw; Rishanlang Nongkhlaw; Rishanlang Nongkhlaw

Abstract: Asymmetric synthesis is a method of organic chemistry in which a reaction is designed to preferentially produce one enantiomer, leading to the formation of a product with specific stereochemistry\. At present, asymmetric synthesis has become essential to modern chemistry because lots of biologically active molecules exist as enantiomers having different physiological effects\. It helps researchers to control stereochemistry with high accuracy\. This method lowers the need for separation of the racemic mixture, which makes the process more efficient and cost\-effective\. Asymmetric synthesis plays a significant role in organic synthesis as it has the ability to selectively produce a single enantiomer from an achiral or racemic intermediate\. Its application in the field of organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry has grown significantly, primarily for the synthesis of complex natural products\. It plays a key role in improving drug performance and selectivity by understanding the relationship between chemical structure and biological activity\. Advances in asymmetric synthesis have enabled the efficient construction of complex chiral molecules with high enantioselectivity, facilitating the development of enantiomerically pure drugs, agrochemicals, and advanced materials\. Additionally, the integration of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence and computational modelling is expected to further enhance reaction design and predictability in asymmetric synthesis\. Various catalysts, including organo\- and metal\-complex catalysts, have been discovered that promote and accelerate asymmetric synthesis\. This review summarises the organocatalytic and organometallic approaches to asymmetric synthesis, highlighting the diverse catalysts employed, their synthetic applications, and future prospects in the field\.

## [Implementation Of Internship at the Central Statistics Agency of Sidoarjo Regency Msme Mapping Process Ahead of the 2026 Economic Census](../publications/3ae9fc09d3219e541984.md)

Davin Khurniawan; Atikha Sidhi Cahyana

General Background Digitalization within public statistical institutions enables streamlined data collection during national economic mapping activities\. Specific Background The Central Statistics Agency utilizes mobile applications like Kendedes Mobile for field survey tagging and micro\-business enumeration ahead of national economic censuses\. Knowledge Gap Although mobile surveys expedite field operations, systemic evaluations measuring multi\-dimensional operational factors that dictate overall user satisfaction levels remain understudied\. Aims This research analyzes multi\-variable determinants influencing user satisfaction with the Kendedes Mobile application at the Central Statistics Agency of Sidoarjo Regency using multiple linear regression modeling\. Results Multiple linear regression modeling reveals that work efficiency \(X4, coefficient 0\.559\) and system quality \(X2, coefficient 0\.419\) exhibit strong positive correlations with user satisfaction \(Y\), whereas ease of use, information quality, and individual user satisfaction variables show negative regression coefficients\. Novelty Empirical modeling identifies work efficiency as the primary positive driver governing field enumerator satisfaction in digital statistical mapping systems\. Implications Institutional IT managers must prioritize optimizing application responsiveness and operational workflow efficiency to improve user satisfaction and data collection productivity\. Key Findings Highlights Work Efficiency Represents Primary Positive Satisfaction Driver With Coefficient 0\.559 System Quality Exerts Secondary Positive Effect On Overall User Satisfaction Multi\-Variable Model Explains 44\.1 Percent Variation In Mobile Application Satisfaction Keywords Mobile Application, User Satisfaction, Multiple Linear Regression, Central Statistics Agency, System Efficiency

## [Metaphor, multimodality and generative AI: Synthetic images prompted by figurative expressions in anti\-immigration discourse](../publications/3af5ab396a8d69d1c8e8.md)

Christopher Hart

Complex social processes like migration are frequently understood via metaphors\. In right\-wing media and far\-right political discourses, two metaphors that abound draw on flood and invasion frames to problematise immigration and legitimise hostile attitudes and actions towards it\. In so far as metaphor involves the construction of mental imagery, it is intimately bound with visual experience, including semiotically mediated visual experience\. In a semiotic landscape increasingly populated by synthetic images, I argue that the meaning of metaphors may be modulated by AI\-generated visual content and that this is especially important in contexts of political communication\. The study investigates images generated by prompts instantiating an immigration is flood versus an immigration is invasion metaphor to inquire if and how they differ by source\-frame and what are the ideological implications of the images returned\. Following an initial pilot study, several specific semiotic features are analysed, including colour, properties of the figure \(size, shape, orientation\) and ground elements \(environment, securitising features and frame\-consistent features like fire and water\)\. Results show significant differences between metaphorical frames and highlight the potential that AI\-generated images have to reflect and reinforce ideological positions\.

## [Exercise dampens microglia synaptic engulfment in Alzheimer’s disease](../publications/3af657ca16292c9916a3.md)

Juan Zu

Emerging evidence substantiates the beneficial effects of exercise in mitigating cognitive impairment in Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\)\. However, the underlying mechanisms by which exercise exerts its effects in AD remain poorly understood\. Microglia play a central role in AD\-associated dementia, particularly through the pruning of synapses\. This study demonstrates that long\-term voluntary exercise upregulates cholinergic signaling, increases the expression of microglial α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors \(α7 nAchRs\), and reduces excessive microglial synaptic engulfment in a mouse model of AD\. Furthermore, primary microglia exposed to acetylcholine exhibited enhanced α7 nAchRs expression and significantly decreased engulfment of synaptosomes, an effect that was reversed by the α7 nAChRs antagonist methyllycaconitine \(MLA\)\. These findings provide evidence that long\-term exercise attenuates microglial excessive phagocytosis of synaptic components via modulation of α7 nAchRs, highlighting a potential therapeutic target in AD\-associated cognitive decline\.

## [Building community capacity for sustainable local food systems in central Java, Indonesia: an integrated training evaluation framework](../publications/3afcefce2c18aebc4ff5.md)

Agus Subhan Prasetyo; Kim E\. Dooley

Transitioning to a safe, resilient and sustainable food system requires more than policies and local food resources; it requires building community capacity to convert that potential into sustainable methods\. However, there is little evidence of training&\#x27;s contribution to local food systems beyond the immediate learning outcomes\. This study explores the contribution of a local food processing training program to community capacity building and sustainable local food systems through an integrated evaluation of its program design, implementation, and outcomes\. We performed a qualitative case study with multiple perspectives of the Local Food Processing Training Program \(LFPTP\) organized by the Food Security Agency of Central Java Province, Indonesia\. Data were collected through program documents, semi\-structured interviews with trainers, and in\-depth interviews sessions with 15 participants\. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis and cross\-perspective synthesis using the ADDIE model, the Kirkpatrick Evaluation Model and the FAO Four Pillars of Food Security\. The results point to two main mechanisms affecting the effectiveness of the program\. First, there is a “design\-implementation gap” when trainers must adapt the curriculum to the diversity of participants&\#x27; experiences and different constraints in implementation\. Second, there is a “transfer gap” where knowledge and skill gains do not reliably translate into changes in behavior, sustainable entrepreneurial activities or broader economic outcomes\. The success of the transfer also depends on previous experience, access to resources, family support, market opportunities and local socio\-economic conditions\. This research adds to the extant literature by constructing an integrated evaluation framework to link instructional design, training evaluation, and food system perspectives\. The framework shows that the contribution of training to sustainable local food systems depends on the inter\-connectedness of design, adaptive implementation, learning transfer and contextual conditions that enable long\-term application\.
