## [AI Governance and Digital Reputation Risk: A Social Media Analysis of Consumer Responses to Toyota’s Recall](../publications/3b07d7d25a4079cf580f.md)

Mona Shehata; Omnia Mohamed Ahmed Salem; Akram Ramadan

The increasing integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and software\-driven technologies into corporate products has introduced new governance challenges and digital reputation risks\. When failures occur in software\-controlled systems, their impact often extends beyond technical disruption, particularly as consumers actively share experiences and interpretations across online platforms\. This study examines how technological product failures are reflected in consumer sentiment and how these reactions contribute to digital reputation dynamics\. Focusing on Toyota’s digital dashboard recall, the study analyses user\-generated discussions on Reddit to explore how online communities interpret and respond to technological malfunctions\. A qualitative text analytics approach was employed, combining sentiment analysis and topic modelling using the Orange Text Mining platform\. The findings suggest that online discussions are predominantly informational, yet accompanied by notable expressions of dissatisfaction, primarily related to service delays, communication challenges and uncertainty regarding technical resolution\. Topic modelling identifies five recurring themes, including technical failure, software updates, service inefficiencies, warranty processes and reputation\-related concerns\. Importantly, the results indicate that reputational impact appears to be shaped less by the technical malfunction itself and more by how the organisation responds to the crisis\. This study contributes to research on AI governance and digital reputation risk by providing an empirically grounded account of how technological failures are interpreted and amplified within digital environments\.

## [Synthesis of gem ‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation](../publications/3b22bee7682c2a98f0ed.md)

Meng‐Ling Pu; Heng Xu; An‐Jiu Wen; Yu‐Ting Yang; Chen Cheng; Li Li; Fei Ye; Zheng Xu; Fuk Yee Kwong; Li‐Wen Xu

ABSTRACT The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements\. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C\(sp 2 \)─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters\. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution \(DR\) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities \(up to 98:2 er\)\. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks\. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity\.

## [Explainable temporal deep learning for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using IoT sensor data](../publications/3b24e27ca53387ab900c.md)

Muhammad Shoaib; Adam Khan; Muhammad Ismail Mohmand

Concrete compressive strength is a fundamental indicator of structural performance, yet conventional destructive testing methods require 7–28 days, limiting timely decision\-making in construction projects\. This study presents an interpretable deep learning framework for early prediction of concrete compressive strength using real\-time multivariate Internet of Things \(IoT\) sensor data\. The proposed approach integrates internal curing conditions \(temperature and humidity\), ambient environmental variables, and mix design parameters to model early\-age hydration dynamics as a temporal learning problem\. A Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(Bi\-LSTM\) network with an attention mechanism is developed to capture both forward and backward temporal dependencies in the curing process while identifying the most influential time intervals\. To ensure interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) and attention\-based analysis are incorporated to quantify feature importance and reveal critical curing stages governing strength development\. The model is trained and validated using field data collected from real construction sites, enabling evaluation under realistic environmental variability\. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high predictive accuracy \(MAE = 1\.52 MPa, R 2 = 0\.94\), outperforming benchmark models including GRU, Temporal Convolutional Networks \(TCN\), and conventional machine learning approaches\. Unlike existing studies that primarily rely on laboratory\-controlled datasets or focus on prediction without early\-stage applicability, the proposed framework enables reliable estimation of 7\-day and 28\-day compressive strength within the first 24–48 h of curing\. This combination of real\-time IoT sensing, temporal deep learning, and explainable artificial intelligence provides a robust and practical decision\-support tool for smart construction systems, enabling improved quality control, optimized scheduling, and reduced reliance on destructive testing\.

## [Sentiment Analysis of Political Debates on YouTube: Comparative Performance of Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression](../publications/3b2b202a4597661453c1.md)

Lanny Sitanayah; Apriandy Angdresey; Indah Yessi Kairupan; Ignatius Lucky Henokh Tangka

The 2024 Indonesian Presidential Election aimed at electing the President and Vice President for the 2024\-2029 term\. Central to this election were candidate debates, critical moments for presenting their visions and enabling public evaluation\. These debates, accessible on platforms such as YouTube, facilitate public commentary and form the basis for sentiment analysis\. However, analyzing YouTube comments presents challenges due to the volume of data, language diversity, and varied expressions\. Sentiment analysis, essential for gauging public opinion of political figures, uses algorithms such as Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression\. While Naive Bayes assumes feature independence, facilitating rapid implementation in text analysis, Logistic Regression is a discriminative model that captures feature dependencies, allowing it to assign specific weights to words or phrases that strongly signal positive or negative political sentiment\. Applied to YouTube comments on the 2024 Indonesian Presidential debates, Logistic Regression demonstrated superior performance with an average accuracy of 90\.57% on the aggregated dataset of five debates, outperforming Naive Bayes, which achieved 85\.24% using a standard 80:20 train\-test split\. These findings validate the use of Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression for sentiment analysis during significant political events, confirming the efficacy of integrating advanced transformer models for automated data labeling with classical classifiers for robust, real\-time political sentiment analysis\.

## [Cross\-Task Consistency\-Guided Mean Teacher with Cross Pseudo Supervision for Semi\-Supervised Polyp Segmentation](../publications/3b2cafd40334d8c2fc5e.md)

Thao Tran Thi Phuong; Lam Tran Tung; Tu Nguyen Ba; Thao Tran Thi; Truong Pham Van

With the recent improvements in deep learning techniques, many polyp segmentation methods have become increasingly accurate, facilitating prompt diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer\. However, the scarcity of labeled datasets poses significant challenges for training and developing supervised learning methods, as annotating data is a time\-consuming and labor\-intensive task\. To address this problem, we propose CTC\-MT, a semi\-supervised framework for colorectal polyp segmentation based on Mean Teacher and Cross Pseudo Supervision, comprising a teacher and two students to utilize both limited labeled data and unlabeled data\. With the proposed framework, we aim to encourage the similarity between the predictions from each student and the pseudo\-label from the teacher for unlabeled input, and ensure the consistency between the predictions of the two students for the same input image\. Additionally, we improve PMFNet architecture as the backbone model by leveraging a spatial MoE block and adding a regression branch to learn boundary features through a signed distance map and cross\-task consistency\. The experimental results show that our framework achieves promising performance on Kvasir\-SEG, ETIS, CVC\-300, CVC\-ClinicDB, and CVC\-ColonDB datasets compared to other state\-of\-the\-art approaches\.

## [Development and evaluation of an intelligent pharmaceutical manufacturing curriculum module under industry–education integration: a quasi\-experimental study](../publications/3b3ecd0abca96be39d2f.md)

Yan Peng; 李梦琪

The digital transformation of pharmaceutical manufacturing has generated an urgent need for graduates who possess competencies in intelligent manufacturing, data\-driven process control, digital quality systems, regulatory compliance, and innovation\-oriented problem solving\. However, conventional pharmaceutical education often remains theory\-centered and insufficiently connected with real industrial scenarios\. This study developed and evaluated an Intelligent Pharmaceutical Manufacturing curriculum module under the framework of industry–education integration\. The module incorporated Quality by Design \(QbD\), Process Analytical Technology \(PAT\), Manufacturing Execution Systems \(MES\), electronic batch records \(EBR\), digital twins, virtual simulation, AI\-assisted process optimization, Good Manufacturing Practice \(GMP\) compliance, validation, and data integrity\. A four\-integration teaching model was proposed to connect curriculum content with industrial standards, classroom learning with production scenarios, physical practice with virtual simulation, and knowledge acquisition with innovation projects\. A quasi\-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was used to evaluate the module\. Students in the intervention group received the newly developed curriculum module, whereas students in the control group received conventional instruction\. Results showed that the intervention group achieved greater learning gains than the control group in knowledge acquisition, practical competency, digital manufacturing competency, and learning engagement\. The largest improvement was observed in digital manufacturing competency, suggesting that the module effectively addressed a key limitation of traditional pharmaceutical manufacturing education\. Qualitative feedback further indicated that students perceived the module as authentic, industry\-relevant, and beneficial for future professional development\. This study provides a transferable curriculum framework—centered on the proposed four\-integration teaching model and industry–education co\-cultivation mechanism—for cultivating pharmaceutical professionals capable of adapting to intelligent manufacturing, and offers practical implications for industry–education collaboration in higher education\.

## [AI\-Driven Fit Confidence in Fashion E\-Commerce: How Personalization, Transparency, and Privacy Concerns Shape Consumer Experience and Purchase Intention](../publications/3b40b411118c03d962f7.md)

Alexander Sánchez\-Rodríguez; Jesús Rodríguez\-Flores; Andrés Fernando Morocho Caiza; Alexis Cordovés\-García; Gelmar García\-Vidal; Reyner Pérez\-Campdesuñer

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is transforming fashion e\-commerce through personalized recommendations, virtual try\-on, size suggestions, and algorithmic decision support\. This study examines AI\-driven fit confidence as a fashion\-specific mechanism linking AI personalization quality, algorithmic transparency, trust in AI, consumer experience, and purchase intention, while considering privacy concern as a boundary condition\. Data from 400 Ecuadorian consumers with prior exposure to AI\-enabled recommendation or personalization features in fashion e\-commerce were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling\. AI personalization quality and trust in AI were positively associated with fit confidence, while algorithmic transparency was associated with trust in AI\. Fit confidence was strongly related to consumer experience but showed only a small direct association with purchase intention; its indirect effect through consumer experience was substantially larger, indicating complementary partial mediation\. Privacy concern had no significant direct relationship with fit confidence\. The interaction between privacy concern and personalization quality was negative, but evidence was mixed and sensitive to the bootstrap confidence\-interval method; H7 was not supported under the primary percentile\-bootstrap criterion adopted in this study\. Predictive analyses showed stronger out\-of\-sample performance for trust in AI and fit confidence than for purchase intention\. The study distinguishes trust in technology from confidence in anticipated product–consumer fit and supports explainable, privacy\-sensitive applications in fashion e\-commerce\.

## [Beyond Reward Scoring: Online Multi\-Agent Preference Learning for Multimodal Response Generation](../publications/3b623cdd5713d8a11f73.md)

Ziyun Zou; Jiwoo Hong; Yifan Lu; Shao Tang; Weiyi Wu; Aman Gupta; Jin Tian; Imran Razzak

Multimodal preference alignment often follows a score\-based RLHF pipeline: a reward model is first trained to learn human preferences, then used to score on\-policy responses and optimize the response model&\#x27;s generation\. This turns preference supervision into a scalar signal for generation: a model may learn to produce answers with higher preference scores, but is rarely trained explicitly to learn the reasons underlying human preferences\. We therefore ask whether making preference understanding an internal capability of the response model can improve its generation\. To investigate this question, we propose \\textbf\{PrefMind\}, an online dual\-agent reinforcement learning framework with two trainable agents: a response Generator and a preference Critic\. Given a pair of candidate responses, the agents analyze and discuss which response better aligns with human preference\. Human labels supervise their judgments and corrections\. For pairs on which both the Generator and revised Critic correctly identify the human\-preferred response, the Generator produces an improved answer, and the Critic compares it against the original preferred response to provide a generation reward\. Both agents are jointly updated from interactions sampled with their current policies\. Through this process, \\textbf\{PrefMind\} trains the Generator to understand human preferences via explicit judgment and correction, and to translate this understanding into better responses\. Experiments across three model scales show improvements in both standalone preference judgment and downstream response generation\.

## [Epidemiological patterns and psychosocial risk factors of suicide among university students in Bangladesh revealed by a retrospective news content analysis](../publications/3b6a7505ca1b8c81b93b.md)

Ahsanul Haque Rifat; M\. M\. Enamul Aziz; Md\. Reazul Islam; Sonya Farhana Sony; Md Saiful Islam; Md\. Golam Dostogir; Mahamudul Hasan; Sabina Sharmin

Abstract Background Suicide has become a public health concern among university students in Bangladesh\. However, there is a lack of systematic evidence because of the lack of national surveillance on suicide\. Objectives This study aimed to analyze the epidemiology, methods, socio\-demographic risk factors, and temporal trends of university student’s suicide in Bangladesh using a retrospective content analysis of online news reports\. Methods A retrospective observational study was used\. From January 2015 to May 2026, a total of 100 student suicides were found in 10 online news portals \(5 English\-language and 5 Bangla\-language outlets\) in Bangladesh\. Gender, age, academic level, type of institution, location of the institution, suicide method, psychosocial risk factors, suicide notes, social media activity, mental health diagnosis, and other key classifications were included as variables\. The data obtained were analyzed descriptively using SPSS 25\.0 and Microsoft Excel\. Results Among the 100 included cases, 63% were male, with the mean age being around 23\.1 years \(range 18–31\) among the 45 cases \(45\.0%\) for which age was reported\. The students of public universities experienced the highest number of suicide cases, mainly from the University of Dhaka, which contributed 27% of the incidents\. There was a marked rise in cases from 2022 onward, with the highest number of cases in 2023 \( n = 17\)\. The most common method was hanging \(80%\), primarily by ceiling fans in private, indoor locations \(84%\)\. Depression \(17%\), relationship problems \(16%\), and academic stress or failure \(14%\) were the most common psychosocial risk factors\. Only 19% of cases had a confirmed mental health diagnosis\. In 16% of cases, a suicide note was reported, and in 9% of cases, there was a pre\-mortem communication via social media\. Conclusions Male students at public universities are at the greatest risk of suicide due to various risk factors and mental health issues\. Given that a confirmed mental health diagnosis was documented in only 19% of cases, alongside the prominence of relationship distress, academic pressure, and familial or financial stress as reported precipitants, this study recommends improving mental health services on university campuses in Bangladesh as one of several complementary measures\. Additionally, it also highlights the need for resilience workshops, training programs, and stronger public awareness through digital media\.

## [Local Distance Seismic Source Discrimination in the United Kingdom Using P/S Amplitude Ratios and Machine Learning](../publications/3b6dfdfb080de361539d.md)

Max Merrett; David N\. Green; Stuart E\. J\. Nippress; Richard Luckett

ABSTRACT Seismic source discriminants comparing earthquakes and explosions have been validated for large\-magnitude events \(local magnitude, ML&gt;3\.5\) detected at regional and greater distances \(&gt;350 km\)\. However, there is less evidence that existing seismic source discriminants apply to small\-magnitude seismic events \(ML≤3\.5\), which are predominantly detected at local distances \(≤350 km\)\. In this study, we investigate the performance of a P/S amplitude ratio discriminant for 210 small\-magnitude seismic events in the United Kingdom \(UK\)\. High\-frequency \(&gt; 8 Hz\) network\-averaged P/S ratios can discriminate between earthquakes and explosions, whereas low frequencies \(2–4 Hz\) can separate offshore explosions and quarry blasts\. We derive a path and site amplitude correction model that reduces P/S ratio distribution variability, but using discrimination metrics we show that simple across\-network averaging is the most important step to allow effective discrimination\. We also applied a machine learning classification model, previously trained to discriminate earthquakes and explosions in France, to our dataset\. The model demonstrates high classification accuracy, likely due to similarities between geology and seismic sources in France and the UK\. When the predictions from the convolutional neural network are combined with high\-frequency P/S ratios, we are able to distinguish other seismic sources, such as longwall mining\-induced earthquakes\. These results suggest that P/S ratios can be considered a useful seismic source discriminant at local distances across the UK, and network\-averaging sufficiently accounts for non\-source factors\.

## [Naturalistic language assessment and brain\-network biomarkers in post\-stroke aphasia for precision neurorehabilitation](../publications/3ba0242f6951e1fd05ad.md)

Jiayi Xia; Song Pei; Song ZHOU; Yulong Bai

Advances in naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and brain\-network modeling are creating new opportunities to evaluate post\-stroke aphasia under conditions closer to real\-world communication\. Conventional aphasia batteries and isolated linguistic tasks remain essential for diagnosis, severity classification, and treatment planning, but they provide limited information about how language\-network activity supports communication in dynamic, naturalistic contexts\. This integrative review, informed by a structured literature search and descriptive thematic mapping, synthesizes evidence on connected speech, discourse production, narrative comprehension, interactive communication, and contextual reading after stroke\. We examine how multilevel features from these behaviors can be organized into graded, interacting dimensions of lexical\-semantic access, phonological encoding, grammatical organization, discourse processing, executive\-predictive control, and speech\-motor output\. We further review multimodal evidence from fNIRS, fMRI, EEG/ERP, lesion\-symptom mapping, structural connectivity, and functional connectivity, highlighting residual left\-hemisphere language networks, conditional right\-hemisphere support, bilateral reorganization, domain\-general control systems, and longitudinal recovery\. Portable EEG and fNIRS are considered complementary approaches for repeated assessment during less constrained language tasks, with distinct temporal, spatial, and practical trade\-offs\. Building on this evidence, we propose an operational ecological biomarker framework that links task choice, multilevel feature extraction, multivariate behavioral profiles, neural measures, prespecified clinical questions, and longitudinal outcomes\. This framework may support recovery prediction, rehabilitation stratification, neuromodulation target selection, individualized therapy planning, and monitoring of functional communication\.

## [Bifunctional applications of Laurus nobilis\-derived silver nanoparticles: From catalytic synthesis of aminoindolizines to cytotoxicity against breast cancer cells](../publications/3ba2f10a455227f7fe6e.md)

Shuai Wu; Hongyan Jia

We report the green synthesis and characterization of silver nanoparticles \(AgNPs\) mediated by Laurus nobilis leaf extract\. Comprehensive structural analysis \(UV\-Vis, transmission electron microscopy \(TEM\), field emission scanning electron microscopy \(FESEM\), energy dispersive X\-ray spectroscopy \(EDX\) confirmed the successful formation of a stable AgNPs/ L\. nobilis composite\. TEM analysis revealed the particle size being 25\-30 nm\. As a heterogeneous catalyst, the nanocomposite facilitated the efficient, high\-yield synthesis of aminoindolizines via A 3 \-coupling \(yield 90\-96%\), exhibiting excellent stability across 8 recycling runs\. Furthermore, the biomedical potential of the Ag NPs was evaluated against breast cancer models\. The nanoparticles demonstrated significant, dose\-dependent antiproliferative activity against Michigan cancer foundation \- 7 \(MCF\-7\) and M D Anderson \- metastatic breast – 231 \(MDA\-MB\-231\) cell lines \(IC50​: 197 and 205 µg/mL, respectively\) with negligible toxicity toward normal cells\. Complemented by potent antioxidant activity \(1,1\-diphenyl\-2\-picrylhydrazyl \(DPPH\) IC50​: 190 µg/mL\), these results highlight the dual utility of L\. nobilis \-derived AgNPs as efficient catalysts and promising anticancer agents\.

## [Relación del perfil blando facial con las diferentes maloclusiones esqueletales según el índice de maduración cervical en una base de datos radiológica en pacientes de 8 a 20 años de la ciudad de Cuenca en el periodo 2022\-2023](../publications/3ba750eae9eea69c8685.md)

Josue Fernando Galarza Ochoa; Lorena Gonzalez\-Campoverde

Introducción: El perfil blando es importante en ortodoncia porque influye en la apariencia y función del rostro, y conocerlo ayuda a planificar mejor los tratamientos\. Objetivo: determinar la relación del perfil blando facial con las diferentes maloclusiones esqueletales según el índice de maduración cervical en una base de datos radiológica en pacientes de 8 a 20 años de la ciudad de Cuenca en el periodo 2022\-2023\. Materiales y Métodos: Se trabajó con radiografías laterales de 416 pacientes de un centro radiológico en Cuenca, usando un software para medir características óseas y del tejido blando, así como para evaluar la maduración cervical\. Resultados: En Cs 1\-2, la mayoría de mujeres tenía 8 años y hombres 9 años\. En Cs 3\-4, mujeres de 13 y hombres de 14 años\. En Cs 5\-6, ambos a los 20 años\. La correlación entre CVM y edad fue muy baja e inversa, pero entre CVM y sexo fue directa y fuerte\. Conclusión: Aunque el perfil blando cambia según la edad y el género, no parece estar directamente vinculado con el tipo de maloclusión ósea\. Esto indica que el diagnóstico debe considerar varios aspectos para lograr un buen tratamiento, y abre la puerta para futuros estudios en esta población\.

## [Ekologi Media Linguistik Non\-Kekerasan: Negosiasi Empati dan Keamanan dalam Komunikasi Manusia\-AI](../publications/3baffeb879c6f215dc47.md)

Rafli Fauzan; S D Putri

Kecerdasan buatan generatif semakin menjadi mediator dalam komunikasi antarmanusia, menim bulkan pertanyaan mendasar tentang bagaimana teknologi ini mengelola makna, emosi, dan keamanan psikologis dalam ruang digital\. Penelitian ini mengkaji ekologi media linguistik non\-kekerasan yang muncul dari negosiasi empati dan keamanan dalam komunikasi manusia\-AI\. Menggunakan kerangka Coordinated Management of Meaning \(CMM\), yang mengidentifikasi tiga dimensi penting dalam dialog berkelanjutan koherensi \(pemahaman bersama\), koordinasi \(penyelarasan tindakan\), dan misteri \(pengakuan atas apa yang tidak dapat sepenuhnya dijelaskan\) penelitian ini mengeksplorasi bagaimana agen AI dapat berfungsi sebagai mediator dalam percakapan yang terfragmentasi secara emosional dan berpotensi konfliktual \. Pendekatan penelitian menggunakan studi kasus eksperimental pada dialog dengan topik sensitif secara politik dan budaya, dengan melibatkan agen AI yang dirancang berdasarkan prinsip CMM \. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa agen AI generatif dapat mengurangi hambatan emosional dan memfasilitasi dialog yang lebih hormat dan inklusif, terutama bagi pengguna yang tidak terbiasa dengan diskusi semacam itu\. Dengan menyempurnakan pernyataan pengguna secara strategis dan memodulasi nada berdasarkan gaya resolusi konflik, agen ini dapat mempromosikan pengakuan timbal balik dan meningkatkan kualitas wacana \. Namun, temuan juga menyoroti keterbatasan: penerapan strategi yang terlalu kaku atau penghalusan emosi yang berlebihan dapat mengurangi keaslian pembicara atau menghambat ekspresi kritis\. Penelitian ini juga mengungkap bahwa dalam konteks multibahasa, AI mengungkap dan menyembunyikan aspek makna budaya yang disebut sebagai &quot;misteri&quot; ketika berhadapan dengan topik\-topik sensitif secara sosial\. Ketika AI menerjemahkan atau memformat ulang pesan antar bahasa, terjadi negosiasi antara kejelasan dan ambiguitas, antara kenyamanan emosional dan akurasi faktual \. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa ekologi media linguistik non\-kekerasan memerlukan keseimbangan yang hati\-hati antara kenyamanan emosional, agensi ekspresif, dan adaptasi yang peka terhadap konteks dalam desain sistem AI komunikatif\. Implikasi temuan ini penting bagi pengembang AI, pembuat kebijakan, dan praktisi komunikasi dalam merancang sistem yang mendukung dialog yang aman dan empatik tanpa mengorbankan kebebasan berekspresi dan pemikiran kritis\. Ekologi media yang berkelanjutan menuntut AI yang tidak hanya efisien, tetapi juga peka terhadap kompleksitas komunikasi manusia\.

## [Global Leadership in the World of AI:](../publications/3bb3f707bf1796e66387.md)

Danielle Badgett; Michael King

Background: This poster offers a practical approach to global leadership when introducing artificial intelligence \(AI\) into culturally diverse organizations\. Methods/Approach: The approach draws from leadership theory, emerging research on AI in the workplace, and cross\-cultural communication theory\. Through this research, The Ethical AI Competency Model and AI Implementation Protocol were developed\. Objectives: The Ethical AI Competency Model highlights six interconnected competencies: Cultural intelligence, Ethical AI Stewardship, Sensemaking and Strategy, Human\-Oriented AI Application, Cross\-Cultural Communication, and AI Literacy \(Chee et al\., 2025; Hagerty &amp; Rubnov, 2019; Oh et al\., 2026; Passlack et al\., 2026; Yang et al\., 2025\)\. Results: Grounded in this competency model, the AI Implementation Protocol offers a seven\-step protocol to support responsible and culturally inclusive AI adoption\. Conclusions: At its core, the framework argues that successful AI implementation within global leadership necessitates human\-centered values, organizational transparency, and the willingness and knowledge to adapt across cultures \(Pillai, 2024; Rezaei et al\., 2024\)\.

## [Teaching critical thinking with artificial intelligence: An information literacy training model at the Library of the Faculty of Medicine, Public Health, and Nursing, Universitas Gadjah Mada](../publications/3bba1b9a65fa7ff07386.md)

Mohammad Riqzazulmi; Fitri Mutia; Sukirno; Tachiyya Nailal Khusna

Purpose\. This study investigates the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) into information literacy training in university libraries, focusing on how AI can foster critical thinking and ethical awareness among students and staff\. Methods\. The research employed a qualitative descriptive approach with data collected through interviews, observations, and documentation at the Faculty of Medicine, Public Health, and Nursing Library of Gadjah Mada University\. Thematic analysis was used to identify patterns in participants&\#x27; experiences and in librarians&\#x27; roles as facilitators\. Findings\. The training model consisted of three main components: introducing AI concepts and ethical considerations, practicing the use of generative AI tools for literature searching, summarisation, and academic writing, and critically evaluating AI outputs\. The training enhanced participants&\#x27; ability to locate relevant sources, generate summaries, and support administrative tasks\. It also highlighted challenges, including difficulties in formulating effective prompts and the need for librarians to upgrade their AI competencies continually\. The findings show that AI\-based literacy training not only improves technical proficiency but also nurtures reflective and critical engagement with digital tools\. Implications\. The study concludes that AI\-driven information literacy programs in academic libraries can serve as an innovative model for strengthening users&\#x27; critical thinking, ethical responsibility, and digital literacy\. Sustained librarian capacity\-building and continuous training are essential to maximize the long\-term benefits of AI integration in academic information services\.

## [Metodología de la investigación científica en énfasis en las ciencias empresariales](../publications/3bc7dd165badaef89ce0.md)

Luciano Fermín Tinoco Palacios; John Tarazona Jiménez; Leoncio Florentino Cochachín Sánchez

Metodología de la investigación científica con énfasis en las ciencias empresariales es una obra integral y eminentemente didáctica que tender un puente entre la fundamentación filosófica y la aplicación práctica de los métodos de investigación en el ámbito organizacional\. El texto guía gradualmente al lector desde los fundamentos de la gnoseología y la epistemología hasta la estructuración detallada de proyectos e informes de investigación con enfoques cuantitativo, cualitativo y mixto\. Su gran valor diferencial radica en la incorporación de un caso de estudio totalmente actualizado que analiza la incidencia de la Inteligencia Artificial y la analítica de datos en la auditoría financiera externa de las MIPYMES, demostrando con rigor metodológico cómo las herramientas tecnológicas modernas optimizan el examen contable y la mitigación del riesgo de fraude bajo la normativa internacional\.

## [Gut‑kidney axis in chronic kidney disease: Dysbiosis, uremic metabolites and therapeutic opportunities \(Review\)](../publications/3bcb71b975360044d320.md)

Yinding Wang; Hanyu Zeng; Na Liu; Dong Yang

Chronic kidney disease \(CKD\) poses a notable global health burden\.Beyond traditional pathways, the gut\-kidney axis has emerged as a potential contributor to disease progression\.In the present narrative review, current evidence on the role of intestinal dysbiosis, characterized by reduced microbial diversity, depletion of beneficial short\-chain fatty acid producers and expansion of uremic toxin\-generating bacteria, in the accumulation of nephrotoxic metabolites \(such as indoxyl sulfate, p\-cresyl sulfate and trimethylamine N\-oxide\) is summarized\.These toxins promote oxidative stress, inflammation and fibrosis, accelerating renal decline\.By contrast, microbially derived short\-chain fatty acids exert protective effects\.Although therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiome \(including probiotics, prebiotics and adsorbents\) and fecal microbiota transplantation \(targeting the gut microbiome\) exhibit potential in modulating toxin levels, evidence for clinical endpoint benefit remains insufficient\.In the present review, mechanistic insights were critically evaluated, clinical intervention studies are systematically summarized in tabulated form and a roadmap for personalized, microbiota\-informed therapeutic strategies is proposed\. ## [ПЕРСПЕКТИВЫ ВНЕДРЕНИЯ ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА В ОХРАНУ ПАМЯТНИКОВ КУЛЬТУРНОГО НАСЛЕДИЯ](../publications/3bf71806320a3964d98d.md)

Рахматова Мафтунахон Нусратходжа кизи

В статье рассмотрены перспективы применения искусственного интеллекта \(ИИ\) в мониторинге, исследовании и реставрации памятников культурного наследия\. Проанализированы возможности компьютерного зрения, нейронных сетей, предиктивной аналитики и цифровых двойников для выявления повреждений и поддержки проектных решений, а также методологические, технические и этические ограничения их применения\. Предложена поэтапная модель внедрения, сочетающая цифровой мониторинг с экспертной оценкой\. Показано, что своевременная диагностика продлевает жизненный цикл исторических зданий и снижает ресурсоёмкость вмешательств, что соответствует принципам «зелёной» экономики\.

## [BUILDING TRUST IN DIGITAL PAYMENTS: THE ROLE OF CYBERSECURITY ASSURANCE IN OVERCOMING CONSUMER SKEPTICISM](../publications/3bfe7118243abcbfb6f1.md)

Javeria Iqbal; Muhammad Hafeez; Ahras Rashid; Zainab Tayyab

The growing use of digital payment technologies has significantly changed the way consumers carry out financial transactions\. This shift is particularly evident among Generation Z, who are generally more comfortable with digital technologies and increasingly prefer cashless payment methods\. However, despite the rapid expansion of digital payment services, concerns regarding security, privacy, fraud, and trust remain important factors that may discourage users from fully adopting these technologies\. Much of the existing research on digital payment adoption has focused on factors such as perceived usefulness, ease of use, convenience, and technology acceptance\. Comparatively less attention has been given to how cybersecurity assurance and Institutional Trust can reduce users’ concerns and strengthen their confidence in digital payment systems\. This issue is particularly relevant in Pakistan, where the digital payment ecosystem is expanding rapidly, yet users may still have concerns about the security of their financial information, the reliability of digital platforms, and the institutions responsible for providing these services\. Therefore, this paper aims to assess the Cybersecurity Assurance and Institutional Trust on Digital Payment Usage among Generation Z consumers in Pakistan\. Understanding these relationships can provide valuable insights into how security measures and trust in financial institutions shape consumers’ willingness to use digital payment services\. The findings may help fintech companies, banks, and other financial institutions better understand the factors that influence digital payment behavior and develop strategies that improve users’ confidence in their services\. In particular, stronger cybersecurity practices, transparent security mechanisms, and greater institutional credibility may help address users’ concerns and encourage more frequent use of digital payment platforms\. By examining these factors within the Pakistani context, the study addresses an area that has received relatively limited attention in the existing literature and contributes to a broader understanding of digital payment adoption among Generation Z\. The findings may also provide useful recommendations for policymakers and regulatory authorities seeking to strengthen cybersecurity standards, promote institutional trust, and develop a safer, more reliable, and inclusive digital payment ecosystem in Pakistan\.

## [Analysing police in emergency response systems: a bibliometric review and mapping of global research trends](../publications/3bff5c968bed3184c22b.md)

Alok Kumar Gaurav; Astha Arora; Sunil Gupta; Saurabh Yadav; Santap Sanhari Mishra; Indra Pratap

Purpose This study systematically examines the intellectual structure, thematic development, collaborative patterns and current research trends in police emergency response systems research through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis\. Design/methodology/approach A total of 510 Scopus\-indexed publications were analysed using Bibliometrix \(R\-package\) and VOS\-viewer\. To explore the field&\#x27;s knowledge structure, bibliometric performance analysis and science\-mapping techniques are used, including citation analysis, co\-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, collaboration analysis, keyword co\-occurrence, thematic mapping and thematic evolution\. Findings Research output has grown considerably since 2015, with the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom as the top three contributors\. The intellectual foundations of the field were identified through citation and co\-citation analyses, and the transition from operational to multidisciplinary research, with a focus on inter\-agency cooperation, psychological resilience, interoperability, and technological capacity for emergency response, was examined through thematic analyses\. The future directions for research are highlighted, with AI\-related concepts, smart cities, responder well\-being, resilience and digital emergency management emerging as themes\. Research limitations/implications The analysis was restricted to Scopus\-indexed English\-language publications and to bibliometric methods, which cannot assess the methodological quality of every study and may overlook relevant studies published in other bibliographic databases and languages\. Practical implications The results offer policy recommendations and evidence\-based insights for policymakers, police organisations and emergency management agencies to enhance inter\-agency collaboration, technological integration, organisational resilience and evidence\-informed emergency response systems\. Originality/value In this study, performance analysis and science mapping were successfully complemented and combined with a framework of past, present, and future within the context of the systematic synthesis of the literature of police emergency response systems research to obtain a comprehensive synthesis of the literature that provides a structured understanding of the evolution of the research area, the state of the art, and its future research agenda\.

## [قصيدة بين ذكاءين قصيدة المتنبي \(صحب الناس قبلنا ذا الزمانا \) بين الذكاء الاصطناعي ChatGPT وDeepSeek دراسة في ضوء المنهج الأسلوبي](../publications/3c08848db60c4524c0a0.md)

## [Tele\-EEG and AI\-Enabled Digital Twins for Epilepsy: A Scoping Review](../publications/3c104710621d53801397.md)

Leonel Vasquez\-Cevallos; Sridevi V\. Sarma

Epilepsy digital twins require patient\-specific computational models that evolve with longitudinal observations and support prospective inference\. We conducted a scoping review of complementary patient\-specific modeling and longitudinal or remote EEG approaches, searching five databases with a publication cutoff of 26 August 2026\. Additional retrieval on 11 October 2026 yielded 42 of the 54 previously unavailable reports\. Following consistent eligibility reassessment, 68 reports were included, 22 were excluded after full\-text assessment, and 12 remained unretrieved\. Fourteen included reports were classified as C0, ten as C1, forty as C2, three as C3, and one as C4 using a review\-specific functional framework\. Three reports demonstrated repeated updating with prospective prediction or simulation, and one demonstrated experimental governed feedback\. This combined count does not establish four longitudinally updated digital twins\. No included report demonstrated the complete non\-invasive longitudinal architecture of observation, explicit patient representation, repeated updating, uncertainty\-aware prospective inference, and governed output\. Mechanistic and dynamic network models contributed individualized representations, while remote EEG and adaptive computation contributed observation and prediction\. Initial personalization was more common than repeated updating\. The original single\-reviewer workflow was supplemented by separate coauthor review of selection and functional classification\. Incomplete retrieval, omitted Embase coverage, interpretive coding boundaries, and non\-harmonized clinical descriptors still limit interpretation\. Functional codes do not establish etiological applicability or treatment benefit\. Progress requires population\-specific, prospective validation of integrated architectures\.

## [Carbon\-Negative Dual\-Source polygeneration integrating biogas combustion and geothermal energy for Water–Energy–Carbon Nexus; 5E \+ LCA assessment and Ridge Regression–ALA optimization](../publications/3c1b8b5d571f0998ea58.md)

Rongsheng Liu; 简辉华; Jinhua Xiao; Xuexuan Zhu; Ke Li

The pressing necessity to reduce carbon emissions and shift to sustainable energy systems stimulates the creation of innovative polygeneration technologies, maximizing resource productivity and reducing environmental impact\. This paper suggests and critically analyzes an innovative dual\-source multi\-generation system as a synergistic integration of biogas\-combustion flue gas, geothermal energy, and LNG regasification with cold\-energy recovery to co\-produce electricity, heating, cooling, liquid CO 2 , hydrogen, oxygen, and desalinated water\. This system has net carbon\-negative performance, and the global warming potential of the life cycle is −0\.09 kgCO 2 \-eq/kWh, which highlights its environmental excellence and compliance with the objectives of cleaner production\. Based on a comprehensive 5E \(Energy, Exergy, Economic, Environmental, and Exergo\-environmental\) analysis and the stepwise Life Cycle Assessment \(LCA\), the system has proven a baseline polygeneration energy efficiency of 50\.30% and a levelized cost of energy \(LCOE\) of 0\.23 $/kWh\. Moreover, an advanced machine learning and multi\-objective optimization \(ML\-MOO\) framework, based on the Ridge Regression surrogate modeling and Artificial Lemming Algorithm \(ALA\), leads to a significant improvement in the system performance, namely, an increase in polygeneration exergy efficiency to 28\.69% while reducing LCOE to 0\.210 $/kWh\. The work offers a validated, scalable template of sustainable energy integration within the water\-energy\-carbon nexus, and a technically viable, economically competitive, and environmentally transformative route to decarbonized multi\-generation\.

## [Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off\-Policy Degradation in Mixture\-of\-Experts Reinforcement Learning](../publications/3c28ecef985418984b32.md)

Liangyao Jin; Zhixin Wang; Liming Liu; Mingjun Zhang; Zhengzhou Zhu; Fangcheng Fu; Jinlong Hou; Yuan Cheng; Xiaohe Hu; Ping Zhang; Siyuan Feng

Reinforcement learning \(RL\) can become off\-policy due to training\-inference mismatch, mini\-batch updates, and asynchronous training\. The resulting mismatch is especially harmful in Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) models, where rollout\-training discrepancies can change routing decisions and lead to router drift\. Rollout Routing Replay \(R3\) mitigates this mismatch by reusing expert selections from the rollout stage during training\. Our analysis shows that routing replay introduces gradient bias by losing contributions from experts selected by the training router but not the rollout router\. To address this, we propose Router Drift Control \(RDC\), which uses routing disagreement between rollout and training as a signal of off\-policy staleness and selectively rejects high\-drift responses\. The sequence\-level filtering avoids gradient bias introduced by replay while preserving native expert selection and the associated learning signals for retained responses\. Experiments show that RDC achieves larger gains as policy staleness increases and remains effective in asynchronous RL\. In asynchronous training, RDC combined with Truncated Importance Sampling \(TIS\) improves the average peak validation accuracy across AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 by 5\.5 points over TIS and 4\.5 points over R3\.

Rizki Darmawan; Heru Agus Santoso; Abdul Syukur; Affandy

Maize genomic prediction can accelerate breeding by estimating phenotypic performance from genomewide markers, but conclusions can depend on the paired choice of learning model, SNP input, phenotype construction, and validation design\.This study benchmarks selected model\-representation configurations rather than estimating independent representation effects\.The initial Genomes to Fields \(G2F\) genotype resource contained 5,733 hybrids and 2,156 SNPs, while the primary pollen days\-after\-planting \(DAP\) benchmark used 4,767 phenotype\-matched hybrids\.Eight representation families generated nine evaluated feature matrices because PCA100 and PCA300 were treated as distinct inputs, and all 1,945 planned runs were completed\.Across ten common 80/20 holdouts, RF\-PCA100 achieved the lowest mean RMSE of 2\.3982 \(R2 = 0\.6411; Pearson = 0\.8019\), but corrected resampled tests with Holm adjustment found no significant RMSE difference from RF\-additive, RF\-MAF\-weighted, or RF\-recessive\.A fixedeffect phenotype sensitivity analysis changed the ranking: GBLUP\-additive led on adjusted BLUEs \(RMSE = 1\.0282;R2 = 0\.8516\), demonstrating sensitivity to target construction\.Mean R2 was negative for every evaluated parentdisjoint configuration\.HGB genomic\-plus\-environmental prediction achieved positive R2 in only 6/10 held\-out years, 17/41 locations, 64/217 location\-years, and 2/5 climatic regimes\.On the same 2024 yield test records, a historicallocation mean baseline \(R2 = 0\.0761; unseen hybrids = 0\.0700\) outperformed the best learned configuration \(\-0\.0244 and \-0\.0451\)\.These results support configuration\-level claims and emphasize phenotype sensitivity and distributionshift validation before operational use\.

The transformation of breast cancer pathology from a purely morphological, diagnosis\-based approach to an approach that incorporates a molecular framework, based on gene expression arrays, immunohistochemistry markers and NGS for the molecular classification of cancers, for more specific and individual treatment decision making is now moving beyond doubt\.Using intrinsic subtyping based on PAM50 and other classifiers, the traditional luminal, HER2enriched and basal\-like classifications have been improved, and this classification has found its way into clinically actionable therapy pathways\.HER2\-low and HER2\-ultralow disease has become a new biological entity made possible by the advent of ADC in addition to the development of the CDK4/6 inhibitor combinations in the hormone receptor\-positive disease, and the newly discovered subgroups of BRCA\-mutated and triple\-negative disease with PARP inhibitors and immune checkpoint blockade\.Digital pathology and AI based image analysis is a growing tool that complements genomic profiling tests such as Oncotype DX and MammaPrint, to further enhance prognosis and minimise overtreatment with chemotherapy\.Resistance, tumor heterogeneity and lack of equal access to molecular testing are still significant challenges to getting universal care\.Spatial transcriptomics combined with liquid biopsy monitoring and pathology aided by artificial intelligence is the next promising decade of breast cancer care\.

## [Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models with SHAP Explanations towards Transparent Fake News Detection](../publications/3c4eb96548f990cf3afa.md)

Ramoni Tirimisiyu Amosa; Adebanjo Adekiigbe; Fabiyi Aderanti Alifat; Olorunlomerue Adam Biodun; Adisa Solagbade Philip; Lawal Moshood Olatunji; Akanni Abideen Amosa

The generation of fake news on online platforms has grown into a serious problem, compromising public trust, public opinion and the possibility of information\-based decision making\. In this study, an intelligent Fake News Detection \(FND\) system to automatically classify news articles as fake or real was developed using techniques of Natural Language Processing \(NLP\), Machine Learning \(ML\) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\)\. A publicly available dataset consisting of 44,856 news articles from the LIAR data set and the Kaggle repository was used, of which 80% was used for training and 20% for testing\. The data preprocessing included the following steps: Removing punctuation, Lowercase, Stop\-word removal, Tokenization, Stemming, Lemmatization, and TF\-IDF \(Term Frequency – Inverse Document Frequency\) Feature Extraction\. The classification algorithms used were Logistic Regression \(LR\), Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), Random Forest \(RF\), Decision Tree \(DT\), and Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), which were trained and evaluated with accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, and AUC\-ROC\. Experimental results indicated that SVM outperforms the other models with respect to accuracy \(99\.21%\), precision \(99\.25%\), recall \(99\.23%\), F1\-Score \(99\.24%\) and AUC\-ROC \(99\.96%\)\. To make the classifications auditable, SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) was applied uniformly to all five trained models rather than to the best model alone, permitting a direct comparison of the lexical evidence on which each classifier relies\. The attributions converge: four of the five models rank the token “said” as the single most influential feature, and in every case, it shifts the prediction towards REAL, indicating that the models are detecting the attribution conventions of professional reporting rather than topic alone\. The results show that the proposed NLP\-ML\-XAI framework is accurate, interpretable, and reliable for automatic fake news detection, which could be deployed by media organizations, fact checkers, and digital platforms to prevent spreading fake news online\.

## [Bridging the Nonclinical\-to\-Clinical Translational Gap in FDA BLA Review: Surrogate Test Articles for an Allogeneic Cell Therapy in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/3c4ffa10230da5de9ac3.md)

Neel Sanjaykumar Kansara; Peivand Pirouzi

A recurring and underappreciated challenge in nonclinical development for allogeneic cell therapies is species mismatch at the level of the test article itself: when a human cellular product cannot be administered to an animal model without triggering immune rejection, sponsors often substitute an analogous cell product derived from the model species, and regulators must then decide how much nonclinical support that substitute product actually provides for the human product under review\. This article examines this translational gap through a representative allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\), whose nonclinical package relied on a murine surrogate cell product rather than the human clinical candidate itself, a substitution FDA concluded did not establish the human product&\#x27;s own mechanism of action\. The article situates this nonclinical gap alongside the clinical evidentiary dispute the same program later encountered, develops a real\-world evidence framework informed by both, and closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals designing nonclinical packages for allogeneic cell therapies that cannot be tested directly in a standard animal model\.Keywords: allogeneic cell therapy; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; nonclinical surrogate product; species mismatch; Biologics License Application; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Chronic circadian misalignment in military personnel: a potential contributor to neuroinflammation risk](../publications/3c5271ef87e472d7eeb0.md)

Attila Novak; Tímea Téglás

Circadian rhythm disruption is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to neurological disorders; however, its role is often viewed as a secondary consequence rather than a primary driver of brain dysfunction\. We argue that chronic circadian misalignment should be reconceptualized as a potential, modifiable contributor to neuroinflammatory risk, rather than viewed solely as a secondary consequence\. Military personnel represent a unique and underutilized human model in this context, as they are chronically exposed to predictable circadian stressors, including irregular training schedules, overseas travel, sleep restriction, and pre\-operational stress\. At the molecular level, circadian misalignment disrupts core clock gene regulation \(e\.g\., CLOCK, BMAL1\), leading to downstream alterations in mitochondrial function and redox homeostasis\. These changes promote a sustained pro\-inflammatory milieu, impair neuroimmune balance, and compromise synaptic plasticity and blood–brain barrier integrity\. We propose that these mechanisms collectively increase vulnerability to cognitive dysfunction and mood disturbances, even in otherwise healthy and physically fit populations\. Thus, circadian misalignment in military personnel is not merely a byproduct of performance demands, but a biologically plausible contributor to brain dysfunction that warrants targeted intervention and further mechanistic study\. Reframing circadian disruption as a potential, modifiable neurobiological risk factor has significant implications for both research and practice\.

## [Micro‐to‐Macro Gains From Regional Trade Agreements: Evidence From RCEP](../publications/3c5e6611815245d4e5bc.md)

Zhihao Wang; Zhiyuan Chen; Fuxin Zhai

ABSTRACT We assess how the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership \(RCEP\)—the Asia–Pacific&\#x27;s largest trade agreement—affects trade and welfare when firms differ in productivity\. Using a widely applied firm‐level trade framework, we quantify how lower tariffs and easier market entry reshape which firms export, the volume of trade and the gains for member economies\. Most benefits arise because more productive firms start exporting and expand, while less efficient producers shrink or exit\. This reallocation towards high‐productivity firms raises overall efficiency, with stronger effects in sectors that face limited import competition\. Beyond the familiar gains from higher trade volumes and better international prices, RCEP delivers additional benefits from greater product variety and from domestic productivity improvements driven by firm entry and exit\. Malaysia, Vietnam and Cambodia benefit the most from RCEP, with welfare gains of 22\.2%, 5\.73% and 2\.37%, respectively, while China, Japan and South Korea gain relatively less, at 0\.37%, 0\.50% and 0\.49%, respectively\. The magnitude of tariff reductions primarily underlies these welfare changes\. The shape parameters of productivity distribution also have a non‐negligible impact on welfare outcomes, and the relative productivity dispersion between domestic and foreign firms matters as well when the shape parameters are allowed to vary across countries\. Our results highlight that ignoring firm dynamics tends to understate the agreement&\#x27;s welfare effects\.

## [Multimodal Sensing and Machine Learning for Nondestructive Quality and Safety Assessment of Agricultural Products](../publications/3c625cf733162a83e449.md)

Zhecong Yuan; Xindong Wang; Xinxin Wu; Xinai Zhang

The demand for non\-destructive evaluation of agricultural products has stimulated the emergence of multimodal sensing technologies capable of integrating diverse quality\- and safety\-related information\. This review summarizes the principles, data\-processing strategies, and applications of multimodal sensing systems combining machine vision, visible\-near\-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, Raman and fluorescence techniques, electronic noses, and auxiliary information with ML algorithms\. The complementary capabilities of different sensing modalities for evaluating external appearance, internal quality, chemical composition, freshness, spoilage, and safety hazards are discussed\. Meanwhile, the roles of conventional ML and deep learning in feature extraction, pattern recognition, and multimodal data fusion are highlighted\. Although advanced algorithms and increased data dimensions improve analytical performance, reliable deployment requires robust datasets, effective calibration transfer, model interpretability, uncertainty assessment, and independent validation\. Future advances should prioritize self\-supervised and few\-shot learning, domain adaptation, physics\-informed models, lightweight edge intelligence, and standardized benchmarking to improve model reliability, transferability, and scalability\. These innovations will facilitate the deployment of intelligent sensing systems from laboratory environments to real\-world agricultural quality and safety management\.

## [Noise\-robust discrimination of incoherent point sources with spatial\-mode demultiplexing](../publications/3c748cc14b8e219a6a17.md)

Jian\-Qiang Liu; Chao\-Ning Hu; Jun Xin; Xiao\-Ming Lu

We theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate that a reduced spatial\-mode demultiplexing \(SPADE\) measurement using only the two lowest\-order Hermite\-Gaussian modes exhibits remarkable robustness against background noise in discriminating between a single source and two incoherent point sources\. We establish a theoretical framework incorporating uniform background noise and derive an analytical Chernoff exponent expression, showing that SPADE consistently outperforms direct imaging \(DI\) across all source separations\. ## [A Conceptual Model for Revenue Diversification and Return on Equity Optimization in Banking](../publications/3c7a4c1c0e4a34b96b1d.md)

Ifeoma Okoli

This paper presents a critical, theory\-grounded review of how revenue diversification shapes return on equity \(ROE\) in banking, and it develops an integrative conceptual model that links income mix, risk appetite, operating leverage, and institutional capability to sustainable performance\. Rather than treating diversification as uniformly beneficial, the review applies a structured thematic synthesis of 250 sources, spanning income diversification theory, economies of scope, modern portfolio theory, and agency theory, to a core empirical literature of bank revenue mix and profitability published through 2024, supplemented by evidence on digital banking, fintech, and risk governance\. The synthesis shows that non\-interest income raises ROE only when it is matched to a bank&\#x27;s operational capability, funded within its risk appetite, and supported by governance that prices the associated volatility; where these conditions are absent, fee and trading income concentration erodes rather than strengthens returns\. Beyond consolidating this evidence, the review&\#x27;s contribution is threefold: it reconciles the discrepant findings of the cross\-country diversification literature with the largely disconnected single\-market ROE\-determinants literature; it specifies the conditions, technological, governance, and capital, under which diversification converts into higher risk adjusted ROE rather than higher earnings volatility; and it translates these conditions into four testable propositions and a practical measurement agenda for banks and regulators\. Because the review is thematic rather than meta\-analytic, it does not estimate a pooled effect size; its value lies instead in mapping where the evidence agrees, where it conflicts, and what a bank or regulator should measure next\.

## [Scale‐space image analysis for mapping spotted knapweed in grassland ecosystems](../publications/3c7affa81137be423d28.md)

Shohreh Sahebi; David Hill

Premise: This study investigates the value of scale\-space representations of spatial features for the identification and mapping of invasive plants using high\-resolution multispectral imagery\. Scale\-space representations combine the two\-dimensional spatial domain with a third dimension representing spatial scale, such that features can be represented across both space and image spatial resolution\. Methods: Gaussian pyramids were constructed to create representations of the features across five image resolution levels \(between 3 and 46 cm\) within the scale space\. A case study was employed to evaluate the importance of features across the scale space for the identification and mapping of spotted knapweed in a grassland ecosystem using multispectral imagery acquired using a remotely piloted aircraft system \(RPAS\)\. Classification was performed using a random forest classifier that was constructed using a process that included feature and hyperparameter optimization\. Results: The results of this case study show that classifiers constructed with only high spatial resolution features were associated with better classification performance than those constructed with only lower spatial resolution features; however, the best classification is achieved by leveraging features from throughout the feature scale spaces\. Discussion: These findings suggest that optimization of the spatial scale at which features are computed can substantially improve remote sensing image analysis and potentially inform RPAS flight planning to improve mission efficiency\.

El pronóstico de la demanda eléctrica en entornos institucionales presenta desafíos particulares derivados de la irregularidad de los patrones de consumo, especialmente durante períodos de receso académico o ante cambios estructurales en la infraestructura eléctrica\. ## [Comprehensive Techniques for Intelligent Transportation Systems: Issues and Solutions using Wireless Sensor Networks](../publications/3c8ad86ea8e4d162897c.md)



Communication, cutting\-edge electronic and computer technologies, control, and detection are all related to the intelligent transportation system \(ITS\)\.WSN is a collection of minuscule, interconnected sensor nodes that can do the real\-time computation, wireless communication, and sophisticated sensing\.Through the transmission of real\-time information, it improves safety, effectiveness, and traffic situation\.The real\-time gathering of transportation data and communication between targeted nodes play a big part in all ITS applications\.It is exceedingly difficult and expensive to deploy a wired sensor for data collection and communication from a wide area\.Wireless sensor deployment offers an appealing platform for data gathering and dependable communication in ITS due to the cheap maintenance costs\.In this paper, the fundamental ideas and practical information needed to create an objective and routing protocol for WSNs are described\.The most important factors that may be used to classify ITS systems according to their primary function are road safety, traffic flow management, and reliable communication\.Nonetheless, network reliability and traffic flow control are partially connected\.For instance, a collision between two or more vehicles might result in a traffic jam\.This incident&\#x27;s details provide a safety warning for incoming drivers to be informed of the situation\.Information that may be used for a range of purposes and is transmitted over an ITS network with a solid infrastructure\.The network distribution in ITS using different WSN methodologies is also addressed, which can help different researchers understand different challenges in developing the WSN\-based ITS\.

## [DistLearn: Zero\-Order Decentralized Layer\-wise Training via Game\-Theoretic Block Coordinate Descent](../publications/3c8f8cfcbc2792e345fd.md)

Iván Jourdan

El entrenamiento de Redes Neuronales \(NN\) mediante backpropagation enfrenta desafíos significativos, tales como el desvanecimiento y la explosión del gradiente\. Además, el cálculo de gradientes globales exactos y consistentes presenta un alto costo computacional a medida que se profundiza la red\. Estos desafíos se ven acentuados si se propone aplicar en arquitecturas de dispositivos AD\-HOC de borde para procesamiento distribuido\. En este trabajo, se introduce DistLearn, un algoritmo de entrenamiento descentralizado por capas de Orden Cero\. Al formular la optimización de las capas de la NN como un Juego de Potencial Exacto, DistLearn evita la propagación del error hacia atrás, encapsulando a las capas como jugadores independientes\. Cada capa actualiza autónomamente sus parámetros, empleando filtrado particular en combinación con estrategias evolutivas basadas en matrices de covarianza \(CMA\-ES\) y macro\-gradientes subrogados\. Evaluaciones experimentales realizadas indican que DistLearn es capaz de sortear mínimos locales de manera efectiva\. En los experimentos realizados, DistLearn logró un éxito del 82 % en objetivos con un RMSE ≤ 0\.07 en una topología 1\-6\-4\-4\-1, en comparación con el desempeño del optimizador ADAM \(44 %\)\. Estos resultados sugieren que DistLearn pudiera ser una alternativa viable, libre de gradientes, para la optimización de problemas no convexos en arquitecturas profundas\.

## [Real\-Time UAV scheduling under hazardous weather conditions using an integrated fuzzy logic and machine learning framework](../publications/3c965fd339a9b59bafe2.md)

Ahmad B\. Alkhodre; Adnan Ahmed Abi Sen; Abdelouahab Abid; Nour Mahmoud Bahbouh; Adel Ben Mnaouer; Mohamed Benaida; Yazed Alsaawy; Hani Almoamari

The use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles \(UAVs\) in precision agriculture, specifically palm farm management, is perpetually challenged by dynamic and extreme weather\. From sudden wind gusts and thermal stress to destructive regional events like sandstorms and flash floods, these hazards severely constrict operational windows\. This paper proposes a robust, hybrid scheduling framework that integrates fuzzy logic inference with an ensemble of machine learning classifiers to enhance real\-time UAV flight reliability\. The primary novelty of this research lies not in a new mathematical paradigm, but in its specialized application: the holistic integration of region\-specific agricultural hazards into a real\-time, decision\-fusion architecture\. The framework classifies takeoff viability into three categories \(SAFE, CAUTION, and UNSAFE\) automatically issuing alerts to trigger preventative measures and preserve hardware\. By leveraging both short\-term farm datasets and a decade of historical weather records, the fuzzy logic component reacts to rapid environmental shifts while establishing safety baselines\. Simultaneously, tree\-based ensemble models \(Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost\) analyze non\-linear atmospheric interactions, achieving up to 99\.67% accuracy in predicting safe windows\. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses, including evaluations without SMOTE and seasonal temporal holdout validations, confirm the model’s robustness against class imbalance and unseen extremes\. Empirical benchmarking demonstrates the framework&\#x27;s superiority over existing hybrid approaches, highlighting the necessity of combining adaptive fuzzy reasoning with deep historical learning for smart farming\.

## [Agencia docente e inteligencia artificial generativa en educación: análisis bibliométrico y mapeo científico \(2022–2026\)](../publications/3cbe1aab33192eb94c18.md)

Oscar Antonio Martínez Molina; Ana María Villón Tomalá; Luís Enrique Hernández Amaro; Richard Antonio Martínez Villegas

Generative artificial intelligence has introduced new forms of assistance, automation, and co\-production in teaching, intensifying debates about teacher agency, pedagogical judgment, and professional autonomy\. This study aimed to characterize the evolution, thematic structure, and research fronts connecting teacher agency with generative artificial intelligence between 2022 and 10 September 2026\. An exploratory bibliometric analysis was conducted on a verified corpus of 30 DOI\-bearing publications retrieved through structured searches of open scholarly metadata and cross\-checked against publisher records\. Temporal productivity, source concentration, conceptual recurrence, and thematic relationships were examined\. Output was absent in 2022, incipient in 2023\-2024, and accelerated in 2025\-2026, which accounted for 80\.0% of the corpus\. Mapping identified four clusters: agency and professional judgment, teacher education, professional knowledge for AI integration, and assessment\-governance\. Recent literature shifts attention from technology adoption toward negotiated control, critical validation of algorithmic outputs, and preservation of professional responsibility\. The field is therefore in an early consolidation phase, characterized by fragmented authorship and increasing conceptual convergence around human\-AI relations\. Future research should expand longitudinal evidence, include Latin American contexts, and examine institutional conditions that strengthen or constrain teacher agency\.

## [Recent progress in physical properties and power electronic applications of ε\(κ\)\-Ga2O3](../publications/3cbe43843af3e321ab3e.md)

Yanfang Zhang; Jinggang Hao; Conggui Huang

Gallium oxide \(Ga2O3\) has emerged as a promising candidate for next\-generation power electronics due to its ultra\-widebandgap and superior critical breakdown field\. The emergent spontaneous polarization and ferroelectric characteristics of ε\(κ\)\-Ga₂O₃ are anticipated to enable the development of advanced power devices with both low power consumption and high efficiency\. In this review, we describe the development on the physical properties and power electronic device applications of ε\(κ\)\-Ga2O3, covering its crystal structure and polarization properties, optical characteristics, thermal transport behavior, and electrical properties\. Then, we highlight recent progress in ε\(κ\)\-Ga₂O₃\-based power electronic devices, with particular focus on Schottky barrier diodes, p\-n heterojunctions diodes, and metal\-oxide\-semiconductor field\-effect transistors\.
