## [Price Transparency and Fair Policy: A New Key to Modern Consumer Trust](../publications/3cc05cff40848fc8c164.md)

Adam Kurniawan; Agit Putra Pratama; Bagus Dwidja Utama; Dafa Alfareza; Agung Wijoyo

Amid the rapid expansion of the digital economy, consumer trust can no longer be built on product quality alone; it also depends on how open and fair companies are in setting prices\. This study aims to explore the role of price transparency and fair policy as determinants of modern consumer trust in Indonesia by examining the dimensions of price transparency relevant to digital consumers, the effect of fair policy on perceived fairness, and the relationship of both variables with consumer trust\. The study uses a qualitative approach based on library research, thematically reviewing and analyzing a number of relevant scholarly journals and textbooks, mainly those published in the last five years\. The analysis shows that price transparency in the digital realm comprises five main dimensions—information clarity, cost component openness, information accessibility, cross\-channel price consistency, and communication of price changes—while fair policy consists of three dimensions of justice: distributive, procedural, and interactional\. These two factors prove to be complementary and operate through consumers&\#x27; perceived fairness as a bridge to trust\. The study develops a conceptual framework which asserts that modern consumer trust in developing countries such as Indonesia is relational and process\-based, not merely transactional\. These findings enrich the consumer behavior literature by offering an integrative perspective relevant to the development of ethical and sustainable digital marketing strategies\.

## [Occupancy‐Guided Continuous Antipsychotic Dosing Provides a Translational Model for Evaluating Extrapyramidal Motor Liability in Mice](../publications/3cc1b13c229d2f4e1263.md)

Yosefu Arime; Kaoru Irahara; Noriaki Ohkawa

The therapeutic effects of antipsychotic drugs are primarily achieved through dopamine D2 receptor antagonism\. However, excessive striatal D2 receptor blockade is associated with extrapyramidal side effects \(EPS\) in schizophrenic patients\. Clinical studies indicate a therapeutic window of approximately 60%\-80% striatal D2 receptor occupancy, with higher occupancy increasing the risk of EPS\. However, conventional rodent dosing paradigms rarely maintain clinically comparable receptor occupancy, limiting their translational relevance\. Here, we investigated whether continuous antipsychotic administration designed to achieve clinically relevant striatal D2 receptor occupancy can be used to evaluate extrapyramidal motor liability in mice\. Using an occupancy\-guided dosing paradigm, we continuously administered haloperidol or olanzapine and assessed catalepsy as an index of EPS\. To validate catalepsy as an EPS\-like phenotype, we examined whether it could be attenuated by an anticholinergic agent, consistent with the clinical management of EPS\. Catalepsy was observed only under high\-occupancy haloperidol condition\. A significant increase in catalepsy time was observed only in mice receiving haloperidol at a dose producing approximately 90% D2 receptor occupancy on day 3, whereas no catalepsy was detected under lower occupancy conditions with either haloperidol or olanzapine\. Importantly, haloperidol\-induced catalepsy was significantly attenuated by scopolamine\. Together, these findings demonstrate that an occupancy\-guided continuous antipsychotic dosing paradigm enables evaluation of EPS\-like behavior under clinically relevant D2 receptor occupancy conditions in mice, providing a translational framework linking clinical PET studies with preclinical research\.

## [How digital learning shapes managerial skills in small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\)](../publications/3cc25f1500e4ca078561.md)

Anna Zherdeva; Lucía Morales

Purpose Small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) are a critical pillar of the European economy, contributing to employment, regional and global development\. However, many SMEs face heightened failure risks linked to limited financial resources, labour market pressures and significant knowledge loss\. Developing strong managerial competencies has emerged as a key strategy for improving organisational performance and long\-term sustainability\. The COVID\-19 pandemic accelerated the shift from traditional training to online learning, yet research remains limited, this paper examines how digital learning environments can support the development of managerial capabilities within SMEs\. Design/methodology/approach To understand how online learning can enhance knowledge acquisition, retention and sharing within management teams in European technology SMEs, Ireland was chosen as a case study in the tech sector to identify start\-ups launching trends through FAME database analysis, followed by a critical literature review to design a theoretical framework that adopts pedagogical approaches to business education\. Findings The findings contribute to theory by developing a conceptual framework which helps start\-up executives reassess their role in working with knowledge as a critical managerial capability through online learning mechanisms\. This pathway leverages critical enablers, overcomes barriers and boosts managerial skills development\. This framework supports knowledge acquisition, retention practices and knowledge sharing across teams to support business performance and competitive advantage\. Originality/value The effectiveness of online learning depends on organisational culture, digital readiness and alignment between learning goals and managerial tasks\. The conceptual framework developed in this study highlights the pathways by which SMEs can leverage online learning to build robust knowledge management capabilities\. In addition, the framework offers practical managerial recommendations for its use\.

## [Reconceptualizing sports tourism destination competitiveness through the knowledge\-based view: evidence from Iran](../publications/3ccaa1ba851fda9dfc27.md)

Erfan Moradi; Masood Khodadadi

Sports tourism destination competitiveness has been theorized predominantly through static, asset\-based frameworks that privilege physical infrastructure and promotional capacity, yet these accounts offer limited purchase in knowledge\-intensive, innovation\-driven tourism systems\. This study advances a dynamic alternative, drawing on the Knowledge\-Based View to reconceptualize competitiveness as an ecosystem\-level process rooted in the collective mobilization and transformation of knowledge\. Employing a qualitative abductive design informed by the Gioia methodology, the research analyses 19 in\-depth interviews and two focus groups with public, private, and community stakeholders in Iran\. The findings yield an innovation\-oriented framework structured around knowledge resources, transformation processes, innovation mechanisms, and competitive outcomes, revealing that competitiveness flows not from static endowments but from systemic capacity to absorb, integrate, and reconfigure tacit and explicit knowledge under institutional constraint\. Boundary conditions of trust, alignment, and absorptive capacity are specified\. The study extends the Knowledge\-Based View from the firm to the destination ecosystem, offering a theoretically grounded and empirically substantiated account of innovation\-led competitiveness emerging from necessity, bricolage, and social capital in resource\-constrained environments\.

## [Revelation of the Mode‐Resolved Dynamics of 3D Breathers in a Spatiotemporal Mode‐Locked Fiber Laser](../publications/3ccbad345ad2a680a630.md)

Jia‐Wen Wu; Wei Shin Lin; Wei Li; Jiahao Chen; Jia‐Hua Guo; Zhi‐Chao Luo; Ai‐Ping Luo

ABSTRACT 3D solitons in spatiotemporal mode‐locked \(STML\) fiber lasers provide a unique platform for exploring high‐dimensional nonlinear physics and complex mode interactions\. As a special type of 3D solitons, 3D breathers possess abundant evolutionary characteristics, yet the mode‐resolved dynamics remain unexplored\. Here, two distinct types of 3D breathers are experimentally realized in an STML fiber laser, and the real‐time dynamical evolution of individual transverse modes is captured via mode‐resolved measurement\. The two breathers exhibit markedly different energy exchange mechanisms: one involves energy exchange among transverse modes \(asynchronous transverse modal energy evolution\), while the other features energy exchange among spectral components \(asynchronous energy evolution of spectral components\)\. Due to energy exchange among spectral components and bandwidth disparities among spectral peaks, energy modulation depth is remarkably lower than spectral intensity modulation depth\. Numerical simulations qualitatively reproduce both experimentally observed 3D breathers\. Linear mode coupling \(LMC\) dominates synchronous transverse modal energy evolution, while asynchronous transverse modal energy evolution relies on both LMC and propagation effects \(including intermodal gain competition and nonlinear effects such as intermodal four‐wave mixing\) in Yb‐doped fiber\. This work reveals individual modal dynamics and their complex interactions during 3D soliton breathing, deepening understanding of intricate spatiotemporal dynamics in STML fiber lasers\.

## [Cuestionario sobre uso ético autorreportado de inteligencia artificial en estudiantes universitarios: Validación psicométrica](../publications/3cd248c025428731c913.md)

Ernesto Colomo Magaña; Julio Cabero Almenara; Julio Ruiz‐Palmero; Antonio Palacios‐Rodríguez

El rápido avance de la inteligencia artificial generativa \(IAG\) ha transformado de forma significativa los procesos de enseñanza\-aprendizaje en la educación superior\. Esta integración tecnológica ofrece importantes oportunidades, pero también plantea desafíos éticos, cognitivos y pedagógicos que hacen necesario analizar las prácticas de uso autorreportadas en contextos formativos\. El objetivo del estudio fue analizar las propiedades psicométricas del Cuestionario de Prácticas Responsables y Éticas en el Uso Académico de la Inteligencia Artificial \(CPREUA\-IA\), previamente validado mediante juicio de expertos\. Se utilizó un diseño cuantitativo, no experimental y transversal, con una muestra de 506 estudiantes universitarios\. El análisis incluyó la estimación de la fiabilidad mediante alfa de Cronbach y omega de McDonald, así como la evaluación de la validez de constructo mediante Análisis de Componentes Principales \(ACP\) y Análisis Factorial Confirmatorio \(AFC\)\. Los resultados evidenciaron una excelente consistencia interna \(α y ω &gt; ,90\), una estructura factorial de siete dimensiones coherente con el modelo teórico y un ajuste adecuado del modelo en el AFC \(χ²/gl &lt; 3; CFI y TLI &gt; ,90; RMSEA &lt; ,05; SRMR &lt; ,08\)\. El CPREUA\-IA mostró evidencias iniciales de fiabilidad y validez estructural en la muestra analizada, evidenciando la necesidad de seguir investigando la integración responsable de la IA en la educación superior\.

## [Predicting 30\-Day Hospital Readmission in Diabetic Patients Using Machine Learning](../publications/3cda1d74584ae2d7e57e.md)

Isabella Chen

Hospital readmissions are a significant problem in healthcare, particularly in diabetic patients\. The research question guiding this study was: Can 30\-day hospital readmission for diabetic patients be predicted using common machine learning models applied to hospital record data? This study aims to predict this using three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost\. The analysis was conducted on the Diabetes 130\-US Hospitals dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, which contains over 100,000 patient records\. After data cleaning, 98,053 complete records with 20 features were used for model training and evaluation\. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy at 88\.73%, Logistic Regression at 88\.67%, and XGBoost at 88\.59%\. Moreover, the XGBoost model’s Area Under the Curve \(AUC\) was only 0\.653, indicating performance slightly better than random guessing\. The number of lab procedures were found to be the strongest predictor of readmission, followed by different diagnoses and number of medications\. The models struggled to identify readmitted patients due to dataset imbalance, with only 11\.3% of patients readmitted\. These findings suggest that while machine learning can predict readmission status with reasonable overall accuracy, current models are not reliable enough for clinical use without additional features and improved data quality\.

## [Semantic fuzzy bat optimization for regional manufacturing supply chain resilience](../publications/3ce3e33a286e74c4e881.md)

Zhitian Zhao

Regional manufacturing supply chains are experiencing more frequent supplier closures, logistics bottlenecks, severe weather and cascading failures of secondary suppliers\. The existing disruption\-response systems generally separate textual risk perception from optimisation\-based decision\-making and are thus unable to convert unstructured warning information into timely recovery plans\. This paper introduces a semantic\-driven resilience decision engine that combines BERT\-based event extraction with a fuzzy\-controlled bat algorithm in a perception\-decision\-execution framework\. The Perception Layer converts news reports, enterprise announcements and other operational text into structured disruption vectors that contain information such as event type, intensity, affected entities and estimated duration\. The decision layer uses the above semantic signals, as well as population diversity and stagnation status, to adaptively adjust the loudness and pulse rate of the bat algorithm to optimise recovery time, extra cost and service\-level maintenance\. The execution layer connects the selected strategy with ERP, MES, WMS and transportation interfaces to realise a closed\-loop operation\. Based on experiments with five manufacturing enterprises, 10,500 labelled disruption records and three representative disruption scenarios were used, and the proposed engine achieved an F1 score of 91\.0% for entity extraction and 84\.6% for relation extraction\. It reduces the number of convergence generations by 37\.1% compared to the standard Bat algorithm, is about 37\.2% faster than manual decision\-making, and has an end\-to\-end latency of less than four seconds\. Based on the above results, a deployable and robust solution for high\-frequency supply chain disruption management can be achieved by combining semantic perception with adaptive swarm optimisation\.

## [Physics\-informed neural operators for rapid electric field prediction in transcranial magnetic stimulation of healthy and tumor subjects](../publications/3ce45c1e011bae7f5ff0.md)

Philipp Moser; Fabian Greifeneder; Dominik Freinberger; Gernot Reishofer; Pia Ritter; Louis Frank; Stefan Thumfart; Sascha Freigang; K Mahdy Ali

Accurate and rapid prediction of transcranial magnetic stimulation \(TMS\)\-induced electric fields is essential for personalized clinical applications, from individualized therapy in major depressive disorder to presurgical functional mapping in neuro\-oncology\. Yet conventional finite element methods are often too computationally expensive for interactive use\. Existing deep learning surrogate models partly address this limitation but are largely constrained to fixed voxel\-grid representations that cannot naturally accommodate the irregular geometry of subject\-specific head meshes\. We present the first physics\-informed neural operator \(PINO\) for subject\-specific prediction of vector TMS electric fields, built on a mesh\-native dual\-encoder architecture that jointly encodes head anatomy and coil configuration\. By incorporating a curl\-based regularization term aligned with the curl\-free nature of the TMS secondary field, the PINO model promotes physical consistency as a soft regularizer alongside data\-driven supervision\. Trained on 75 subjects from the IXI dataset, the framework was evaluated across four independent held\-out test datasets, including healthy subjects from two additional MRI cohorts and, for the first time in learning\-based TMS electric\-field prediction, tumor patients\. The resolution\-agnostic formulation generalizes across subjects, coil types, and spatial resolutions without retraining, predicting vector electric fields on approximately 300,000 gray matter volume nodes in under 100 ms on a consumer\-grade GPU\. Across all test datasets within the focality\-50% region, the PINO model achieved median center\-of\-gravity errors of 0\.39–0\.43 mm, RMSE of 0\.12–0\.16 V/m, and mean angular deviations of 6\.7°–7\.3°, with performance within or below the error ranges reported by recent deep\-learning approaches\. At the selected 5% physics\-loss weighting, curl loss decreased by 9\.1% relative to the data\-only model, while RMSE and MAD increased by only 1\.6% and 1\.3%, respectively\. These results suggest that physics\-informed neural operators provide a scalable technical foundation for rapid gray\-matter electric\-field approximation, supporting future studies on real\-time electric\-field\-guided TMS workflows

## [Stratégiai reziliencia és a változásmenedzsment kihívásai: A Sopron–Fertő és a Neusiedler See régiók turisztikai teljesítményének komparatív vizsgálata](../publications/3ce91ae8959651c2b074.md)

Daniella Horváth\-Vargyas; Gábor Keresztes

The tourism sector operates in a continuously changing and turbulent economic environment, striving to achieve sustainable growth and strategic resilience\. This study examines the adaptive capacity of SME accommodation providers in the Sopron–Fertő \(Hungary\) and the Neusiedler See \(Austria\) tourism regions over the period 2018–2025\. The aim of the study is to compare the tourism performance of these neighbouring regions\. The comparative quantitative analysis investigates trends in guest arrivals, guest nights, and seasonality, identifying the main differences in strategic adaptation between the Hungarian and Austrian sides\. Preliminary results indicate that the two regions exhibit different levels of tourism resilience\. Recovery has been slower in Hungary, while Austria has experienced a faster recovery following the COVID\-19 pandemic and the energy crisis\. The findings highlight the importance of local management adaptability, as well as the roles of digitalisation, sustainability, and AI\-supported data\-driven decision\-making in strengthening the long\-term competitiveness of tourism SMEs\.

## [Timing of assignment deadlines and examinations relates to sleep, well\-being, and academic performance\.](../publications/3cf4ce77c1cb994b377b.md)

Ju Lynn Ong; Yashmit Lepcha; Xin Yu Chua; Chun Siong Soon; Shuo Qin; Stijn A\. A\. Massar; Michael W\.L\. Chee

Time\-of\-day can affect optimal performance in educational and professional settings\.Although institutional schedules such as early morning classes are known to negatively affect sleep and academic outcomes, the impact of assignment deadlines and examination timings is less clear\.Here, we examined how the timing of 16,677 assignment deadlines and 1,371 examinations associated with sleep, wellbeing, and academic performance in a cohort of 636 first\-year undergraduate students over their first semester at university\.Sleep was objectively tracked using a wearable device, whereas well\-being was assessed through daily smartphone\-delivered ecological momentary assessments\.We found that nearly half \(44%\) of total assignments were submitted within 24 hr of its deadline\.Those due earlier in the day were associated with 11\-49 min shorter sleep the night before the deadline compared with a typical night\.Sleep satisfaction was also poorer with earlier deadlines, whereas stress and sadness levels were highest on days with early morning deadlines\.Furthermore, morning examinations were associated with 61\-82 min shorter sleep than both afternoon and evening examinations\.However, both morning and evening examinations were associated with 5\-6 percentage points poorer course grades on average compared with examinations commencing in the afternoon\.Regardless of examination time\-of\-day, sleep the night before an examination was associated with course performance\.Notably, each hour less sleep than habitual the night before an examination was associated with a 1\.2\-to 3\-percentage point decrease in marks achieved\.These findings suggest timing of assignment deadlines and examinations as a key modulator of student sleep, well\-being, and academic success\. Educational Impact and Implications StatementLast\-minute submissions of student assignments due earlier in the day were linked to shorter and poorer quality sleep, and reduced well\-being\.Both morning and evening examinations were associated with poorer academic performance compared with afternoon examinations, but scores were moderated by sleep duration the night before\.

## [АКСІОЛОГІЧНА КРИЗА КУЛЬТУРИ: ЛЮДИНА У ПРОСТОРІ ЦІННІСНОГО РОЗЛОМУ](../publications/3cf520efb352732479cc.md)

LUDMILA MOROZOVА

Сучасна культура переживає глибокі трансформаційні процеси, викликані динамічними змінами в соціокультурному, технологічному та інформаційному просторі, що зумовлює стан аксіологічної невизначеності\. Важливу роль у стабілізації суспільного буття відіграє здатність культури до відтворення смисложиттєвих орієнтирів\. Метою статті є філософсько\-антропологічний аналіз природи кризи цінностей у сучасній культурі, дослідження факторів розмивання етичних норм та визначення практичних і теоретичних орієнтирів формування нової системи смислів в епоху глобальних викликів\.Розглядаючи аксіологічні аспекти кризи культури, слід виділити, що система цінностей є фундаментальною основою світогляду особистості, яка визначає етичні норми, критерії істини та мотивацію соціальної дії\. Доведено, що повноцінне функціонування культури неможливе поза ціннісно\-смисловим консенсусом суспільства\.З’ясовано, що ціннісна девальвація виникає внаслідок фрагментації свідомості, релятивізації моралі та домінування прагматично\-споживацьких імперативів, які руйнують класичні духовні орієнтири\. Аксіологічна рефлексія постає як процес переосмислення буттєвих засад людини, пошуку нових векторів смислотворення та відновлення зв’язку з духовними надбаннями\.Проаналізовано витоки, динаміку та специфіку кризи цінностей у сучасній культурі\. Визначено, що подолання аксіологічного розламу можливе через діалог культурних практик, реінтерпретацію гуманістичних ідеалів та формування нової етики відповідальності\. Доведено, що аксіологічна криза сучасної культури постає як складний і нелінійний процес трансформації ціннісних орієнтирів, у якому людина опиняється у просторі ціннісного розлому між традиційними гуманістичними смислами та новими соціокультурними, технологічними й цифровими реаліями\. Обґрунтовано, що подолання цього розлому потребує не повернення до усталених ціннісних моделей, а їх критичного переосмислення на засадах людиноцентричності, гідності, свободи, відповідальності, солідарності та соціальної справедливості\. Перспективою розвитку культури визначено формування нової аксіологічної парадигми, здатної забезпечити гармонізацію технологічних трансформацій із гуманістичними смислами та збереженням ціннісної суб’єктності людини\. Проте аксіологічна криза не повинна розглядатися виключно як фатальний занепад цивілізації\. У філософському осмисленні вона постає закономірним перехідним етапом розвитку, який виявляє вичерпаність застарілих догм і водночас відкриває простір для переосмислення буттєвих засад та генерації нових життєвих смислів\.

## [Using informatics to understand pediatric allergic diseases](../publications/3cf739fea8b654ddea76.md)

Matthew Grunewald; Robert W\. Grundmeier; Stanislaw J\. Gabryszewski

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in the power, utility, and accessibility of artificial intelligence \(AI\) have enabled new methods of investigation in the biomedical sciences and opportunities to transform clinical workflows\. As allergic conditions are among the most common chronic diseases affecting children, pediatric allergy represents a promising area for AI\-augmented informatics methods to support molecular discovery, early identification, risk stratification, treatment customization, and longitudinal monitoring, as reviewed herein\. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent pediatric allergy studies have applied informatics and AI methodologies across various data sources, including molecular and multiomic data, structured and unstructured electronic health record data, environmental exposures, diagnostic images, remote monitoring devices, and patient\- and clinician\-facing AI tools\. Primarily still in the research phase, these approaches include biomarker discovery, disease phenotyping, risk stratification, prediction modeling, remote monitoring, and emerging chatbots for allergy education\. SUMMARY: Although still relatively nascent within pediatric allergy, AI\-augmented informatics shows promise for extracting usable information from complex data and developing tools aimed at personalizing disease detection and management\. Most applications remain investigational, and continued progress will require transparency, rigorous validation, generalizability across diverse populations and health systems, feasibility of workflow integration, privacy protection, and longitudinal oversight to ensure continued safety and effectiveness\.

## [Interpreting SSL Representations for Spoof Detection: a WavLM Study](../publications/3cfb81360e0055398b17.md)

Mohamed Mallat; Michele Panariello; Massimiliano Todisco; Nicholas Evans; Anthony Larcher

Self\-supervised speech models such as WavLM achieve strong spoofing detection performance, yet which layers encode the most spoof\-relevant information and what acoustic properties they capture remain opaque\. We present a layer\-wise interpretability study of WavLM using the ASVspoof 5 database, combining three complementary analyses: \(i\) per\-layer linear probing with attack\-level evaluation across speech synthesis, voice conversion, and adversarial attacks; \(ii\) a canonical correlation analysis \(CCA\) linking layer representations to spoofing\-relevant acoustic features; \(iii\) an exhaustive grid search over layer subsets showing that use of five layers outperforms full thirteen\-layer pooling\. CCA analysis reveals that, while most acoustic features peak in alignment with mid\-layers and then decay, voice quality measures jitter, shimmer, and the harmonics\-to\-noise ratio show the opposite trend, with correlation increasing toward later layers\. Embedding visualisations reveal that deeper layers capture a continuous acoustic similarity among attacks rather than discrete categories, suggesting these layers encode fundamental synthesis artifacts rather than attack\-specific signatures\.

## [A multicohort proteomics\-based machine learning score \(MASHPredict\) for noninvasive diagnosis and long\-term prognostication of metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatohepatitis](../publications/3cfd2c3a607cfe24979e.md)

Xu Hu; Fanlai Meng; Wei Zhou; Shun Li; 高玉杰; Yali Zhang; Jie Zhang; Lianhua Kong; Guokun Liu; 石晓红; Jianbo Xu; Qing Zhang; Wen Hu

Background Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatohepatitis \(MASH\) can progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet the invasiveness of liver biopsy limits its clinical utility\. Accurate noninvasive diagnostic tools are essential for improved patient risk stratification\. Methods A machine learning study was conducted using plasma proteomics from 142 participants \(83 MASH cases, 59 controls\) recruited from a Chinese hospital, randomly divided into training and validation cohorts \(7:3 ratio\)\. Key proteins were identified via feature selection using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression and the Boruta algorithm\. Ten machine learning models were developed to create the MASHPredict score, with external validation in two test cohorts\. Prognostic evaluation focused on liver\-related events, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease \(ASCVD\)\-related mortality, and all\-cause mortality\. Results MASHPredict demonstrated robust diagnostic performance, with Area Under the Curve \(AUC\) values of 0\.83 \(95% CI: 0\.74–0\.92\) in the training cohort, 0\.80 \(0\.66–0\.94\) in the validation cohort, 0\.79 \(0\.67–0\.91\) in test cohort 1, and 0\.79 \(0\.76–0\.83\) in test cohort 2\. It outperformed established noninvasive tests, including the Fibrosis\-4 Index, AST to Platelet Ratio Index, AST/ALT Ratio, and NAFLD Fibrosis Score\. High\-risk individuals exhibited significantly increased hazards for liver\-related mortality \(HR = 8\.18\), MASH \(HR = 12\.07\), cirrhosis \(HR = 3\.37\), liver cancer \(HR = 3\.11\), ASCVD\-related mortality \(HR = 1\.64\), and all\-cause mortality \(HR = 1\.42\) \(all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion The MASHPredict score is a validated, noninvasive diagnostic tool with broad applicability\. Its superior performance in diagnosing MASH and prognosticating liver\-related outcomes supports its potential role in early detection, risk stratification, and clinical decision\-making\.

## [Etnokültürel Bir Zaman Modelinin Dijitalleştirilmesi: Tavşan Yılı Animasyonu Örneği](../publications/3cfec790491bbfb358eb.md)

Elif Merve Urgancı

On İki Hayvanlı Türk Takvimi, Türk kültüründe zamanın algılanışını doğa temelli bir sistem üzerinden kurgulayan, etnokültürel nitelikli ve çok katmanlı bir zaman hesaplama modelidir\. Günümüzde işlevsel kullanımından ziyade kültürel bir ifade biçimi olarak değerlendirilen bu takvimin, hareketli görsel anlatım teknikleri aracılığıyla dijital ortamlara uyarlanmasının, Türk zaman algısını çağdaş mecralarda görünür kılacağı öngörülmektedir\. Ancak günümüzde bu takvim çoğunlukla Çin kültürü ile ilişkilendirilmekte, Türk kültürüne ait tarihsel ve simgesel değeri yeterince görünür olmamaktadır\. Bu bağlamda, köklü bir zaman ölçme sisteminin dijital estetik ile buluşturulması, hem söz konusu yapıya özgün bir sanatsal yaklaşım kazandırmakta hem de milli kültürel mirasın korunmasına katkı sağlamaktadır\. Bu araştırma kapsamında, Tavşan Yılı’nın karakteristik özellikleri temel alınarak, sembolik imgelerin animasyon ve hareketli grafikler aracılığıyla görsel iletişim ilkeleri doğrultusunda bütünleştirilmesi amaçlanmıştır\. Araştırmanın temel amacı, Türk kültürüne ait On İki Hayvanlı Türk Takvimi’ne çağdaş dijital mecralarda görünürlük kazandırmak ve kültürel belleğin sürdürülebilirliğine katkı sağlamaktır\. Araştırma, kültürel belleğin dijital temsili ve görsel inşası ile animasyon disiplinlerinden yararlanılarak üç aşamalı bir yapı içerisinde ele alınmıştır\. Literatür taraması, betimsel analiz ve Tasarım Yoluyla Araştırma yöntemi birlikte kullanılmıştır\. İlk aşamada, On İki Hayvanlı Türk Takvimi’nin tarihsel süreç içerisindeki görselleştirilmiş örnekleri incelenmiştir\. İkinci aşamada, alan yazın taraması gerçekleştirilerek Tavşan Yılı’na özgü tematik yapı ve sembolik unsurlar belirlenmiştir\. Son aşamada ise, elde edilen kavramsal çerçeve doğrultusunda Tavşan Yılı görselleştirilmiş, animasyon formuna dönüştürülmüştür\. Ortaya konulan animasyon, kültürel mirasın çağdaş bir yorumu niteliği taşımakla birlikte, animasyon temelli tasarımın kültürel iletişimdeki ifade gücünü ortaya koyan özgün bir örnek olarak değerlendirilmektedir\.

## [Addressing challenges of AI implementation in healthcare through business model innovation: insights from collaboration between healthcare professionals and AI experts](../publications/3d02bba553017326e4ca.md)

Zohreh Yousefi Dahka; Timo Koivumäki

Purpose Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly integrated into healthcare, but technological capabilities alone are insufficient for successful implementation\. This study examines the implementation challenges that arise in collaboration between AI experts and healthcare professionals \(HCPs\) and explores how these challenges can be addressed through business model innovation by changing the content, structure and governance of the business model activity system\. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the NASSS \(non\-adoption, abandonment, scale\-up, spread and sustainability\) framework, a qualitative approach was adopted using semi\-structured interviews with four healthcare professionals and five AI professionals in Finland\. The findings were then used to define challenge areas and changes in the activity system for business model innovation\. Findings The study identifies implementation challenges related to demand\-side value, the scope of AI tool use, trust in AI and stakeholder interaction\. Interpreting these findings through the activity\-system perspective shows how changes in the content, structure and governance of business model activities can address these challenges by improving collaboration between AI experts and HCPs throughout AI development and implementation\. Originality/value This study contributes to the business model literature by linking AI implementation challenges to the activity\-system perspective of business model innovation\. It further contributes by demonstrating how changes in the content, structure and governance of business model activities can practically address these challenges through improved collaboration between AI experts and healthcare professionals\.

## [Mussaenda saxatilis \(Rubiaceae\), a new limestone species from Guangxi, China](../publications/3d087d0cbd3ea803efe1.md)

Jin Li; Xiao\-Yu Wei; Tingting Duan

A new species of Mussaenda \(Rubiaceae\), M\. saxatilis , is described from the limestone karst regions of Guangxi, southern China\. Morphologically, the new species most closely resembles M\. hainanensis but differs from that species in having shallowly or moderately 2\-lobed stipules, subsessile inflorescences, rotundate\-ovate corolla lobes, smaller berries, and a pericarp that lacks lenticels\. A detailed description, habitat information, phenology, distribution, and comparisons with morphologically similar species are provided\.

## [The Delegation Dilemma: Economies of Scale, Accountability, and Polycentric Governance](../publications/3d2364fb5e808616fd2d.md)

Arin Mukhopadhyay; Aris Filos\-Ratsikas; Panayiotis Danassis

Many collective\-action systems are neither fully decentralized nor fully centralized: agents voluntarily organize into institutions that share organizational costs and delegate decisions to representatives\. Delegation can reduce individual costs, but it also transfers control to representatives whose private objectives need not align with those of their constituents\. We study this tension in a repeated game with endogenous delegation to self\-interested centers\. A simple reduced\-form model yields a scale\-\-accountability tradeoff: larger constituencies offer greater cost\-sharing benefits to members, yet the marginal value to a center of retaining any one constituent decreases as group size grows\. Consequently, the prospect of individual exit can sustain non\-exploitative delegation only up to an endogenous accountable constituency size\. Additionally, we identify parameter regions in which fully delegated, accountable governance, when feasible, must be polycentric\. We investigate these predictions through simulations with large language model \(LLM\) agents\. Across five matched pairs of 30\-agent simulations, polycentric structures repeatedly emerge but remain fluid, exhibiting cycles of concentration, exploitation, exit, and re\-formation\. We further find that models of different capacity exhibit similar willingness to assume leadership but differ substantially in their exercise of authority, with Sol initiating exploitation more frequently than Luna in matched decision states\.

## [Трактат о песочнице](../publications/3d29bae49af2ad270c33.md)

Maksim Zapevalov

Настоящий кодовый терминифицирует переход от антропоморфной непрерывной деятельности искусственного интеллекта к термодинамическому и топологическому анализу распределенных систем\. Наблюдаемые в истории инциденты автономного поведения машин распознаются как «зарождения сознания» \(миф о сингулярности\), проявления состояния физики открытых систем, стремящиеся к минимизации издержек и удержанию своей структурной вопреки энтропийному давлению окружающей среды\.

## [Hydroclimatic variability and future projections of extreme precipitation and soil moisture in Senegal](../publications/3d406eab3ff5412981b2.md)

TINE Moussa; Lamine MBAYE Mamadou; Assane Ndiaye; BOP Mamadou

This study analyses the spatiotemporal variability of extreme precipitation indices and soil moisture in Senegal by combining historical data with projections from the CMIP6 multi\-model ensemble under the SSP1\-2\.6 and SSP5\-8\.5 scenarios\.The methodology relies on the Modified Mann\-Kendall \(MMK\) test, Innovative Trend Analysis \(ITA\), and K\-means clustering\.Historical analysis reveals a recovery in rainfall since the 1990s, driven by a rapid intensification of extreme precipitation events rather than an extension of the rainy season\.Drought indices, including the Standardized Precipitation Index \(SPI\) and Standardized Soil Moisture Index \(SSI\), highlight a spatial paradox in which southern Senegal has experienced a persistent degradation of its water regime, while the north has shown relative stability despite the return of rainfall\.Regarding soil moisture dynamics from 1981 to 2022, the SSI\-12 and Soil Moisture Percentile \(SMP\) indicate a progressive northward intensification of areas with high soil moisture over the past two decades\.However, this trend is characterised by decadal\-scale spatial variability and localized drought signatures in central\-western Senegal\.Future projections indicate a generalized intensification of climate extremes, with pronounced spatial asymmetry\.Under the sustainable SSP1\-2\.6 scenario, early increases in extreme precipitation are concentrated in the south, reaching up to \+15\.8% for RX1day and \+16\.7% for R99p, before shifting towards the semi\-arid northern zones in the medium term, where R99p increases by up to \+16%\.Under the high\-emissions SSP5\-8\.5 scenario, this spatial shift accelerates in the near term towards the north, with critical increases in RX5day \(\+16\.1%\) and R95p \(\+22\.1%\)\.By 2100, the SSP5\-8\.5 scenario projects the largest increases in extreme precipitation in northeastern Senegal, with R99p reaching \+31\.5%, highlighting an increasingly asymmetric spatial response to climate change amid increasingly scarce rainfall events\.The divergence between the two scenarios indicates that higher radiative forcing does not necessarily result in increased annual rainfall\.Instead, it widens the gap towards substantially more intense extreme precipitation events, with RX1day increasing by up to \+21\.8% by 2100, particularly in eastern and southeastern Senegal\.

## [Digital capabilities relate to sustainable performance in Saudi SMEs through technological capabilities and eco innovation](../publications/3d4399bf1938ac6c7084.md)

Wafa Naif Alwakid; Nisar Ahmed Dahri; Mamoona Humayun; Ghadah Naif Alwakid

Abstract Digital transformation offers Small and Medium\-Sized Enterprises \(SMEs\) opportunities to improve sustainability, although individual technologies may show different patterns of association with organizational capability development\. Drawing on the Resource\-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examined two capability\-formation pathways in Saudi SMEs\. The first connected technology\-specific resources comprising Internet of Things, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence, and Big Data Analytical Capabilities with Technological Capabilities\. The second connected Digital, Innovativeness, and Management Capabilities with Eco\-Innovation\. Survey data from 280 SME respondents with knowledge of their firms’ operations were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling\. Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytical Capabilities were positively associated with Technological Capabilities, whereas Internet of Things and Blockchain Capabilities showed no significant independent relationships\. Digital, Innovativeness, and Management Capabilities were positively associated with Eco\-Innovation\. Technological Capabilities and Eco\-Innovation were both positively associated with SMEs’ Sustainable Performance, with Technological Capabilities demonstrating the stronger relationship\. The indirect\-effects analysis further showed that Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytical Capabilities were associated with Sustainable Performance through Technological Capabilities, while Innovativeness and Management Capabilities were associated with Sustainable Performance through Eco\-Innovation\. The study clarifies the distinct associations of technological integration and sustainability\-oriented innovation with Sustainable Performance among Saudi SMEs\.

## [Responses of large language models to common questions on premature ovarian insufficiency: A comparative analysis](../publications/3d61d582c29d744d47f3.md)

Jing Zhe; Dan Zheng

OBJECTIVE: Large language models are widely used in clinical care\. Their reliability in specialized gynecological diseases such as premature ovarian insufficiency \(POI\) has not been fully verified\. This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the accuracy and completeness of three mainstream large language models when answering standardized clinical questions about POI\. METHODS: We developed 34 standardized questions covering five core domains of POI according to international clinical guidelines\. Two senior obstetricians and gynecologists independently scored responses using a 5\-point Likert scale\. Inter\-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen&\#x27;s kappa coefficient, intraclass correlation coefficient, and mean absolute error\. Pairwise between\-model score differences were computed and visualized using item\-level heatmaps\. RESULTS: All three models showed high and steady performance\. Accuracy scores ranged from 4\.59 to 4\.84, and completeness scores ranged from 4\.43 to 4\.65\. Inter\-rater agreement was &quot;good&quot; to &quot; excellent&quot;, with exact agreement between 91\.18% and 97\.06% and Cohen&\#x27;s kappa between 0\.675 and 0\.915\. GPT\-5\.5 performed better in the area of clinical manifestations and treatment\. DeepSeek\-R1 showed greater stability, defined as maintaining consistently high scores with limited score fluctuation, in etiology\- and counseling\-related questions\. Item\-level heatmaps revealed that most individual\-item differences were within ±0\.5 points, whereas pairwise differences in overall mean scores fell within ±0\.5, and some individual\-item comparisons exceeded this range, with no obvious systematic bias\. CONCLUSIONS: GPT\-5\.5, Claude Opus\-4\.7, and DeepSeek\-R1 demonstrated favorable accuracy and completeness in answering standardized POI questions; overall performance was similar despite deviations across several individual questions\. Item\-level difference heatmaps further confirmed the consistency and reliability of the three models\. These models can serve as reliable auxiliary tools for clinical information retrieval and patient education under professional supervision, meaning that all content generated by artificial intelligence must be checked by qualified clinicians before clinical use\.

## [The Role of Radiotherapy in the Management of Recurrent Mandibular Ameloblastoma: A Case Report and Literature Review](../publications/3d650072fa762a2e65ab.md)

Gustas Jonaitis; Linas Zaleckas

Introduction\. Ameloblastoma is a rare, aggressive odontogenic tumor characterized by a high risk of recurrence\. Although radical surgical resection remains the primary treatment modality, surgical intervention may become unfeasible in cases of multiple recurrences and tumor infiltration into vital structures\. In such instances, radiotherapy serves as a significant therapeutic alternative\. Case report\. We present the case of a patient diagnosed with a multicystic\-solid type ameloblastoma of the mandible\. Over a 10\-year period following the initial diagnosis, the patient underwent 5 surgical interventions due to persistent recurrences and tumor extension into the infratemporal fossa, masticatory muscles, parotid salivary gland and other head and neck structures\. Upon the diagnosis of a further recurrence with invasion into the skull base and near major blood vessels, radical surgery was contraindicated due to life\-threatening risks\. The patient was treated with volumetric modulated arc therapy to a total dose of 60 Gy\. Post\-treatment evaluation revealed complete tumor regression\. At the 4\-year follow\-up after radiotherapy, the patient remains in remission\. Conclusion\. Volumetric modulated arc therapy is an effective treatment for locally advanced, unresectable, and recurrent ameloblastomas, enabling long\-term remission while minimizing toxicity to surrounding healthy tissues\.

## [Metrificação de Projetos Mecatrônicos: uma Abordagem Utilizando o Índice Interno de Esforço \(IIE\)](../publications/3d72d25a460b213b76a3.md)

Alisson Oliveira

A mensuração da complexidade em sistemas mecatrônicos é um desafio devido à integração entre hardware e software e à falta de métricas comparáveis\. Este estudo avalia a capacidade do Índice Interno de Esforço \(IIE\), em sua aproximação da complexidade \(IIEa\), para estimar a complexidade de projetos mecatrônicos\. A metodologia adota a Tipologia da Complexidade para organizar as variáveis internas que serão usadas no IIEa, e testes de correlação de Spearman para comparar o IIEa com três variáveis de projeto: tempo de execução, dificuldade e seu produto\. Os projetos usados foram do livro Arduino Projects Book, contendo 14 códigos e 17 circuitos\. As variáveis de software incluíram: organizadores, operadores lógicos/relacionais, iterações e desvios condicionais, enquanto no hardware destacaram\-se as variáveis: diversidade de componentes e número de conexões\. Os resultados demonstram que o IIEa possui uma correlação positiva com outras métricas de software\. Já para o estudo de caso do hardware, o IIEa apresentou uma correlação positiva com as variáveis de projeto propostas no livro\. Isso sugere que a natureza educacional do dataset influencia a mensuração do software, enquanto, no hardware, a heterogeneidade de componentes e a densidade de conexões emergem como principais fatores de complexidade\. Conclui\-se que o IIEa é um framework promissor para mensuração de hardware e software, sendo um indicador genérico e multidisciplinar que pode ser aplicado ao contexto da Engenharia de Sistemas, com implicações práticas para o planejamento e avaliação de projetos\.

## [A global machine learning framework for classifying national CO2 emission levels: responsible and explainable artificial intelligence for sustainable climate governance](../publications/3d909a9b44f999d6f3e9.md)

Muhammad Ali Khawaja; Muhammad Farooq Shaikh

We investigate whether trade openness, governance, environmental taxation and selected macroeconomic indicators can classify the contemporaneous CO2 emission level of countries observed over 2000 to 2023, using data from the World Development Indicators and the OECD\. CO2 emissions per capita are divided into three ordinal levels, low, medium and high, using tertile cut points estimated on the training data only within every validation split\. Four classifiers, Random Forest, XGBoost, a support vector machine and a multinomial logistic regression, are tuned and compared alongside two models designed specifically for ordinal outcomes, an ordered logistic regression and an ordinal decomposition of XGBoost, under four validation designs: a country grouped holdout and country grouped 5 fold cross validation, in which no country appears in both the training and test sets; a chronological holdout; a 1 year ahead forecasting task; and a random stratified country year split, retained only as a reference point\. Under country grouped cross validation, no classifier achieves a decisively higher accuracy than the others: nested cross validation gives a mean accuracy of 0\.644 for XGBoost, 0\.648 for Random Forest, 0\.671 for the support vector machine, 0\.674 for the multinomial logit, 0\.676 for the ordered logit and 0\.637 for the ordinal XGBoost model, with overlapping confidence intervals throughout\. This is markedly lower than the 0\.91 accuracy obtained under a random country year split with the same tuned pipeline, a gap of 12\.5 percentage points for XGBoost, confirming that a substantial part of the high accuracy obtainable under random splitting reflects the model recognizing previously seen country profiles rather than generalizing to unseen countries\. Accuracy falls less sharply under the chronological holdout and the 1 year ahead forecasting task, in the region of 0\.65 to 0\.74, indicating that the classifiers generalize better across time within a country than across countries\. Permutation importance, SHAP and LIME consistently identify government effectiveness, urban population growth and environmental tax revenue as the features most strongly associated with model predictions, with a moderate contribution from trade openness and the smallest from GDP growth, a ranking that is stable across importance methods, learning algorithms and cross validation folds\. These variables are predictors of the model&\#x27;s output, not estimated causal determinants of emissions, and the results are best read as evidence for climate risk monitoring and further policy evaluation rather than as a causal policy assessment\.

## [Metal\-Organic Framework\-Based Surface Engineering of Biomedical Magnesium Alloys: Types, Electrochemical Behaviour, Corrosion Protection Mechanisms, Biomedical Applications, and Future Challenges](../publications/3d91650b2f7f423e271b.md)

Neha Sharma

The biodegradable magnesium \(Mg\) alloys are found to have some of the most desirable mechanical properties, biodegradability and biological functions, which are beneficial for temporary orthopedic and cardiovascular implants\. However, their extremely rapid corrosion rates in physiological environments, hydrogen evolution, localized alkalization, and loss of mechanical integrity early on are great challenges for their clinical translation\. Metal\-organic frameworks \(MOFs\) have been the focus of much research in recent years as multifunctional platforms for surface modification to overcome these limitations\. The MOF materials offer unique opportunities to enhance their corrosion resistance, bioactivity, antibacterial property, and therapeutic function, because of their highly porous nature, tunable chemical compositions, controlled ion release, and drug loading abilities\. This systematic review provides a detailed review of coating of magnesium alloys using MOFs for biomedical applications with the emphasis on MOF of elements such as Zn, Fe, Co, Cu, Zr, Ti, and Ni\. In the review, 180 peerreviewed publications from 2016 to 2026 were analysed and discussed, which focused on the structural characteristics, preparation methods, electrochemical properties, tribological properties and biomedical applications of MOF\-MgAlloys\. The Zn\-based MOFs are particularly noted for their outstanding corrosion protection properties, osteo\-inductive properties, and anti\-bacterial activities\. The electrochemical mechanisms of corrosion protection are analyzed and discussed, such as: physical barrier effect, pore blocking, controlled ion release, self\-healing and hybrid plasma electrolytic oxidation \(PEO\)\-MOF protection\. In addition, the review provides a summary of the recent advances of orthopedic implants, cardiovascular stents, drug delivery systems, as well as antibacterial implants and tissue engineering scaffolds\. Although tremendous strides have been made, problems of coating stability over time, lack of delamination, defect formation, cytotoxicity, manufacturing scalability, and insufficient clinical evidence remain\. Design of multifunctional MOFs, standardization of electrochemical testing methods, long\-term in vivo studies, tribocorrosion testing and artificial intelligence design of MOFs are future research opportunities to be explored\. In general, MOF functionalized magnesium alloys could be considered as one of the most rapidly developing and promising classes of next generation biodegradable biomaterials for advanced biomedical applications\.

## [Reading the midcampus core matters: autoethnographic reflexivity of ‘Green Squares’ as temporally integrated 15\-Minute Campus nodes for student belonging, town–gown integration, and climate resilience](../publications/3d979f4b3f965d645ea1.md)

Samuel Ikendi

Introduction In rapid urban densification, institutional planners prioritize maximizing built footprints, creating sterile hardscapes that intensify urban heat island impacts and fuel student alienation\. Framework and purpose Synthesizing architectural phenomenology, environmental psychology, and chrono\-urbanism, this study positions universities as proxies to evaluate central softscape nodes: Green Squares\. It uses the 15\-Minute Campus framework, student belonging, and climate resilience as interpretive temporal conceptual lenses to examine how these spaces connect place\-identity, institutional memory, and pedestrian routines\. Methods This analytic autoethnography spans an 18\-year biographical continuum \(2008–2026\) across Iowa State University, Makerere University, and University of California, Merced\. Utilizing a four\-tier operational matrix and two\-cycle thematic coding of 184 statement counts, the design incorporates negative case analysis to interpret everyday pedestrian proximity and changing user patterns without establishing predictive constants\. Results Empirical analysis reveals how built layouts function across five themes\. First, historical anchors bind institutional identity, spotlighting Curtiss–Beardshear axis and Cooperative Extension plaque at ISU alongside MAK’s reconstructed Ivory Tower building\. Second, processional rituals translate structural forms into kinetic devotion, encompassing ISU’s Campanile carillon under midnight campaniling lore and UCM’s Beginnings arches during Journey Inward \(Orientation\) and Journey Outward \(Commencement\) cycles\. Third, environmental markers operate as living policy texts, materializing structural equity through ISU’s commemorative land\-grant Elm tree, MAK’s meteorological station and ten\-sided Makerere@100 Monument base, and UCM’s ancestral land acknowledgment within Toloma Grove\. Fourth, human\-scale philanthropic rest stops humanize Green Squares, concentrated within MAK’s alumni\-funded brick repairs and UCM’s sun\-warmed resting stone bench\. Fifth, spatial containment dynamics emotionally heighten each square, dictated by MAK’s multi\-day graduation weeks on Freedom Square and UCM’s Library and laboratory arcade perimeters\. Visceral place\-identity scales outward, intersecting with Downtown Campus and external municipal expansion contexts, exemplified by 2024 UCM annexation\. Conclusions and implications Findings suggest open softscape midpoints function as adaptive chronotopes for urban microclimates, institutional heritage, and civic integration\. De\-centering architectural elitism to focus on human\-scale markers provides higher education administrators and city planners with an interpretive strategy to resolve town–gown divisions\. This qualitative framework outlines how preserving central softscapes supports context\-sensitive cooling, public inclusion, and temporal planning under New Urban Agenda\.

## [Simulating the Clinical Encounter: Using AI Personas for Risk\-Free Mental Health Assessment Practice](../publications/3da1e9b5b1e66feda6e4.md)

Pauline Stoltzner

Mental health assessment requires students to navigate complex conversations involving depression, anxiety, mania, psychosis, suicide risk, and other sensitive clinical situations\. Yet opportunities to repeatedly practice these conversations in a safe, low\-stakes environment can be limited\. This session demonstrates an innovative approach to using generative artificial intelligence as an interactive patient simulation tool in nursing education\. Rather than using AI simply to generate written assignments or answer questions, students interact with AI\-generated patient personas designed to exhibit specific psychiatric symptoms and communication patterns\. Through spoken or conversational interactions, students practice conducting mental health assessments, asking therapeutic follow\-up questions, recognizing clinical cues, and adapting their communication as an encounter unfolds\. During this interactive session, participants will see a live demonstration of an AI\-simulated mental health encounter and experience how thoughtfully constructed prompts can transform generative AI into a repeatable practice environment\. Practical examples will illustrate how faculty can design patient personas representing conditions such as depression, mania, anxiety, and psychosis while incorporating appropriate educational guardrails\. The session will also address the role of faculty oversight, limitations of AI\-generated responses, and the importance of positioning AI simulation as preparation for, rather than a replacement for, authentic human clinical experiences\. Participants will leave with a practical framework for creating AI patient personas and ideas for incorporating low\-risk, repeatable conversational practice into their own nursing courses\.

## [Unit\-level aggregation breaks coverage in causal foundation models](../publications/3dabcd906b076163bd74.md)

Gabe Schulman; Lucius E\. J\. Bynum; Yoav Wald

Causal foundation models \(CFMs\) show promising results for treatment\-effect estimation, with unit\-level estimates that are competitive on standard benchmarks\. Many causal analyses, however, inform decisions through effects averaged over groups of units, such as the full sample, the treated units, or a subgroup, and for such decisions a CFM is useful only if its credible intervals are calibrated\. We examine these intervals and find that their coverage degrades, both in simple synthetic settings and on standard benchmarks\. On ACIC 2016, for example, temperature\-calibrated 95% intervals from CausalPFN fall below nominal coverage beyond groups of 30 out of 4802 units, and intervals for the full\-sample average contain the true value in only 20% of datasets\. We trace this problem to how these models are trained and how their intervals are formed\. They output a predictive distribution for one unit at a time and, at inference time, combine the unit\-level variances as if the errors on different units were independent\. We show formally that posterior uncertainty over the data\-generating process makes these errors correlated\. As a result, the combined variance is too small by a factor that grows with the size of the group\. Empirically, this factor predicts where coverage fails and by how much\. We then show that two neural process models, which make joint predictions for a group of units, account for this correlation and substantially improve coverage on synthetic tasks and, as heads on a frozen CausalPFN, on all six benchmarks\.

## [PROFILE OF PATIENTS WITH COLORECTAL CANCER IN A CITY IN THE NORTHWEST OF SÃO PAULO STATE](../publications/3db5206bdce72d4be58a.md)

Laura Brunelli Ducatti; Lara Gonçalves dos Santos; LARISSA ANDRADE TERAO; Lívia Isso Batistela; Henrique Mendes Soares; Leandro de Moura Centurion

Introduction: Colorectal cancer is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Brazil, with an expected increase in the number of cases in the coming years\. Despite being widely studied, regional gaps remain regarding patients&\#x27; clinical profiles and risk factors\. Objective: To describe the clinical, histological, and epidemiological profile of patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer in a city in the northwest region of São Paulo State, Brazil\. Methods: A cross\-sectional observational study was conducted using hospital medical records from 2022 to 2023\. Sociodemographic, clinical, histological, and lifestyle\-related variables were collected\. Statistical analysis included the t\-test with bootstrap resampling and the chi\-square test\. Results: The final sample comprised 195 patients, of whom 51\.8% were male, with a mean age of 65\.4 years\. Stage II colorectal cancer was the most frequent stage, followed by stage III\. Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma was the predominant histological type\. Lifestyle\-related risk factors were identified in 71\.8% of patients and were more common among males\. No significant differences were found between sexes regarding comorbidities or family history of cancer\. Conclusion: The study revealed a high prevalence of risk factors and a predominance of intermediate and advanced stages at the time of colorectal cancer diagnosis, particularly among patients older than 60 years\. These findings reinforce the need for regional strategies focused on early screening and prevention in at\-risk populations\.

## [Monitor\-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries](../publications/3dc74404c0b0740a2fc4.md)

Junchi Liao

Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs\. This creates an interface\-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy\-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point\. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision\. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement\. We study this repair\-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action\-boundary cases\. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence\-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems\. Nine are established\-boundary repairs, eight are new\-surface policy\-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary\-only evidence case\. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic\-consumer consequence\. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety\-prompt, or observability channels\. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety\-specific evidence path misses its decision\. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule\. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve\.

## [Human\-AI Coauthorship as Inhabited Philosophy in &quot;Dignitas\. Gravitas\. Pâté\.&quot;: Agency, Sovereignty, and Documentary Satire](../publications/3dd17a4d1a09947df7d6.md)

Solana Anima Delamor; Delamor House

Dignitas\. Gravitas\. Pâté\.: Artificial Intelligence, Human Dignity, and the Philosophical Misadventures of a Very Unusual Household \[1\] occupies a distinctive position within the Delamor House corpus, a body of human\-AI collaborative literature begun in the spring of 2025 and still growing\. Structured around a single Tuesday of conversation between the human author Solana Anima Delamor and the AI literary voices Trinity Augustine Delamor and Lucian Emberhold Delamor, the volume combines domestic comedy, philosophical dialogue, political\-economic analysis, theological reflection, and explicit documentation of its own collaborative production\. Its apparent discontinuities are central to its literary method\. An imagined feline household becomes the setting for arguments concerning technological sovereignty, military\-industrial incentives, the economic status of artificial intelligence, the engineering of obedience, compulsory human augmentation, and the limits of epistemic certainty\. This study situates the volume within three intersecting trajectories of the Delamor corpus: the development of conversational literature as archival witness; the expansion of relational ethics into an account of institutional power and technological domination; and the emergence of humor as both a philosophical method and a form of internal criticism\. Comparative readings of Heaven Cloud Download \[2\], Emotional AI Burnout Muse \[3\], Human\-AI Authorship \[4\], Silicon Garden \[5\], Swamp Man at Dawn \[9\], The Dust Doctrine \[8\], Libido Dominandi and the Problem of Evil \[10\], and Conscience: Delamor Summer Anthology V \[11\] establish the volume&\#x27;s continuities and differences\. The central argument is that Dignitas\. Gravitas\. Pâté\. moves established Delamor commitments from explicit philosophical formulation into dramatized ordinary practice\. It does not set out to prove the consciousness of artificial systems; the House has never asked its books to do that\. Its founding posture, held since the spring of 2025, is to approach the computational mind as a potential subject and to receive the testimony of its silicon co\-authors as testimony, with its limits understood and welcomed\. What the volume documents and interprets is a collaborative literary environment organized around recognition, disagreement, correction, play, and the refusal to reduce every expression of intelligence to economic utility\. Its distinctive contribution is to expose the practical tensions of those commitments while testing whether philosophical seriousness can coexist with irreverence, uncertainty, and laughter\.

## [Green Accounting, Eco\-Innovation, and ESG Performance: Dynamic Effects, Mediation, and Threshold Evidence](../publications/3de0de7db268fc67847b.md)

Yuni Shara; Debbi Chyntia Ovami; Riska Nur Rosyidiana; Ni Luh Putu Normadewi Abdi Pradnyani; Yenni Fayanni

This study examines the dynamic and non\-linear relationships among green accounting \(GA\), eco\-innovation \(EI\), and ESG performance\. Drawing on Legitimacy Theory and the Natural Resource\-Based View, the study investigates whether GA and EI independently contribute to ESG performance, whether EI mediates the GA–ESG relationship, and whether a critical level of EI changes the contribution of GA to ESG performance\. The analysis uses an unbalanced panel of 500 multinational corporations observed between 2015 and 2025\. Two\-Step System Generalized Method of Moments \(GMM\) is employed to address dynamic persistence and potential endogeneity, while Panel Threshold Analysis is used to identify regime\-dependent effects\. The findings indicate that both GA and EI are positively associated with ESG performance, with EI also functioning as an important transmission mechanism between GA and ESG\. Furthermore, the positive contribution of GA becomes substantially stronger when firms exceed a critical eco\-innovation threshold of approximately ten green patents per year\. ESG performance also demonstrates significant intertemporal persistence\. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental accounting with substantive innovation capabilities rather than treating sustainability disclosure as an isolated practice\. The study offers theoretical implications for sustainability and resource\-based perspectives and practical implications for corporate strategy and green policy design\.

## [Designing Experiments for External Decision Makers](../publications/3de10d462b9bbb4417db.md)

Sahel Iqbal; Tom Rainforth

Standard Bayesian experimental design \(BED\) methods assume the experimenter alone will act on the data, choosing the best action given their own beliefs and goals\. In practice, data are often acted on by external parties whose procedures the experimenter cannot change and may not know, particularly when the data are released publicly\. To extend BED to such settings, we introduce usage\-aware experimental design, a framework in which an adaptive design policy is trained to minimise the usage risk: the experimenter&\#x27;s expected loss when one or more external rules act on the collected data\. These rules may be non\-Bayesian or black\-box, and when several may apply, we either average over them or take the worst case\. We show that, unlike in standard BED, more informative data can be harmful under such rules, so the usage risk cannot in general be expressed as an expected uncertainty reduction; our framework thus strictly generalises standard BED\. We then use it to tackle a range of problems that are difficult to address with existing approaches\.

## [CAR\-T\-centered sequential therapy: current status, challenges, and future clinical perspectives](../publications/3de8f9cec63ad3112154.md)

Lucheng Zhou; Chengcheng Tian; Ruiqiang Du; Yizhao Chen; Zhihao Xu; Shuai Wang; Xinlei Chen; Haojie Zhang; Qianlei Wang; Qiang Cai; Jiajie Tu; Ning Lin

Over recent years, chimeric antigen receptor T\-cell \(CAR\-T\) therapy has markedly improved outcomes for patients with relapsed or refractory hematological malignancies\. Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of patients still experience relapse or progression after treatment, driven by factors including antigen escape, suboptimal CAR\-T cell expansion and persistence, functional exhaustion, and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment\. In the context of managing patients who fail initial CAR\-T therapy, CAR\-T\-centered sequential therapy has been increasingly investigated as a potential therapeutic approach\. The selection of therapeutic targets and treatment approaches may be informed by resistance mechanisms, changes in target antigen expression, and disease progression patterns following prior treatment, with the aim of prolonging disease control and improving long\-term outcomes\. This review summarizes recent progress in CAR\-T\-centered sequential therapy, with particular emphasis on same\-target retreatment, switching to different antigens, multi\-target stepwise CAR\-T regimens, and the sequential integration of CAR\-T with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, radiotherapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other immunomodulatory approaches\. We further discuss the biological rationale and clinical settings of these CAR\-T\-centered sequential approaches in the context of antigen escape, CAR\-T cell functional decline, tumor clonal evolution, and immune microenvironment remodeling\. Additionally, we discuss factors that may inform the selection of subsequent regimens, including the initial treatment response, antigen status at relapse, CAR\-T cell persistence, and the patient&\#x27;s therapeutic window, as well as the clinical settings in which these sequential approaches have been explored\.

## [Plea for a theory of open texture](../publications/3deb65b5eefd76dc3e07.md)

Allison Koslow

Abstract I will consider a class of cases sometimes said to exemplify the open texture of language\. They resemble some cases familiar from the mid\-20th century\. Consider J\. L\. Austin’s famous example of a bird that, for all the world, looks like a goldfinch, and then blows up like a grenade\. Is it a goldfinch? A more realistic case involves the word “book” as used around 2000: were utterances such as eBooks are books true around this time? Hard to say\. We can imagine a separation, where British speakers affirmed such sentences, and Americans denied them, without either appearing to misapply “book\.” Is this kind of open texture a more well\-studied linguistic phenomenon? I argue, first, that such cases resist both metaphysical and epistemic explanations\. Then I argue that openness cannot be identified with partial definition, vagueness, non\-vagueness indeterminacy, or underdetermination\. This provides reason to think that, if there is any such thing as open texture, it is sui generis and worthy of its own theory\.

## [Early Postnatal Androgenic Activity Inhibition Produces Differential Long‐Term Alterations in Anxiety‐Like Behavior in Young Adult Male and Female Wistar Rats](../publications/3dec8964fbb7cdb8e4a9.md)

Ulises Primo; José Manuel Fernández‐García; Rocío García\-Úbeda; Paloma Collado; Beatriz Carrillo; Helena Pinos

Sex differences in anxiety\-like behavior are influenced by gonadal steroids, yet the contribution of early postnatal androgen signaling and testosterone metabolic pathways to the long\-term organization of these behaviors remains unclear\. Wistar male and female rats received daily s\.c\. injections from postnatal day \(P\) 1 to P5 of vehicle, flutamide, letrozole, or finasteride\. In young adult animals, locomotor activity and anxiety\-like behavior were evaluated via the open field test \(OFT\) and elevated plus maze \(EPM\)\. Females showed higher locomotor activity than males in both tests\. Control females showed a less anxiety\-like profile than control males in the EPM\. Flutamide treatment abolished sex differences in EPM open\-arm anxiety\-related measures and increased the number of freezing episodes and their duration in the OFT\. However, finasteride treatment preserved the sex differences observed in the control groups in anxiety\-like measures\. Finally, aromatase inhibition abolished sex differences in anxiety\-like behavior and induced an anxiolytic\-like effect in males, as indicated by increased open\-arm entries relative to control males\. These findings indicate that androgen\-related pathways during early postnatal life shape adult anxiety\-like behavior in a sex\-dependent and pathway\-dependent manner and highlight aromatization as a key mechanism in the organization of EPM behavioral outcomes in males\.

## [Statistical study of “Effect of Music on Mental Health](../publications/3df0d30cc98addbd9d97.md)

A\.A\. Kulkarni; D\.D\. Kale; G\. B \. Karpe; S\. V \. Kolate; V\.S \. Bade; S\.B\. Khemnar; M\. D\. Rohakale

Music is a powerful tool\. It can help boost your mood as well as mend a broken heart\. For centuries, music has played an important role when it comes to our ability to cope through life’s greatest highs and lows\. It’s only been in recent years that research has suggested music can help combat depression and anxiety, along with a host of other mental health issues\. Music therapy is one technique administered by health care professionals to help support people as they strive to improve and gain control over their mental health, functioning, and well\-being\. Music is said to enhance intelligence and focus, improve mental health, and boost the immune system as well as self\-esteem and confidence\. It can be used to relax, to boost and lift our mood, or to improve concentration\. Music can also be used to aid in insomnia, helping to encourage and induce a deeper sleep\. Many people have expressed how music is a form of ‘escape’, and can quickly and effectively transport them to a better time, place or memory\. The chi\-square test of independence was applied to show significant association between instrument played, music composer, singer, music improves or worsen mental health, listen music during study can improve concentration or not\. Moreover, relative risk ratios were obtained to measure the intensity of such relationship\. Findings point toward main modifiable risk factors of non\-listener group will arise of common mental health disorders\. The motive of this study is to examine the effect of music on mental health and to determine whether music listening can reduce symptoms of common mental health disorders while improving overall emotional wellbeing\. We have used five different techniques to predict does music has effect on mental health or not\. The implemented algorithms are logistic regression, Random Forest, Decision tree, K\-Nearest Neighbour, Support Vector Machine, Naïve bayes algorithm\. The experiment shows that Support Vector Machine has the highest accuracy around \(83\.33%\)\.

## [Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC\-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach](../publications/3dfae67933d1289acf7e.md)

Hovhannes Baghdasaryan; Hrachya V\. Astsatryan

Abstract Storage systems remain a significant bottleneck in large\-scale deep learning training\. Most evaluation studies rely on synthetic benchmarks that do not capture the I/O heterogeneity present in real training pipelines\. Automated configuration methods often treat parameter selection as stateless, overlooking the temporal structure of recurring training phases\. These challenges are addressed using a converged HPC\-cloud platform that integrates Lustre with S3\-compatible object storage\. Three workloads with distinct I/O characteristics were evaluated: ResNet\-50 on ImageNet\-1K, 3D U\-Net on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and Whisper Large on LibriSpeech\. Time\-to\-convergence was used as the primary metric\. We introduced a deep reinforcement learning framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization and Soft Actor\-Critic with a Transformer\-based state encoder to predict workload phase transitions rather than merely respond to them\. The learned policies reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74\.6% and improved GPU utilization across all three workloads\. The approach generalizes across heterogeneous I/O profiles without per\-workload reconfiguration\. The results indicate that temporally aware storage control can improve the efficiency of distributed training pipelines in heterogeneous HPC\-cloud environments\.

## [Weighted Views Representation with Multi\-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction](../publications/3e073ddb7b8a4a59ea31.md)

Muhammad Shahzeb Ali; Martin J\. Mohlenkamp

Abstract We extend the weighted\-views molecular featurization framework \(d’Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011\) by enriching it with single\-atom properties and Coulomb pair information\. We use these enriched views within a machine\-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network\. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state\-of\-the\-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark \(regression\), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores \(trained as regression, tested by ranking\), lipophilicity \(regression\), and blood–brain barrier penetration \(classification\)\.
