## [Removing records on animals and nonhumans in Ovid Embase: a comparison of 11 filters](../publications/3f543a4bfa6da4da5090.md)

Helen Fulbright; Connor Evans

Objective: To understand and compare the impact of 11 filters to remove records on animals or nonhumans in Ovid Embase, which are routinely used despite there being no performance data for them\. To understand the indexing of relevant subject headings in Embase\. Methods: To assess filter performance, we screened and categorized 3,000 records as &\#x27;should be removed&\#x27; or &\#x27;should be retained&\#x27; and calculated the sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for each filter\. We also reported on the number of records with human participants or data that were incorrectly removed by each filter\. Results: Method 11 was the most sensitive, correctly retaining 90\.6% records, whereas method 3 had the highest specificity, correctly removing 71\.5% records\. Of the records incorrectly removed by each filter, method 11 removed the fewest records with human participants or data at 10\.9%, whereas method 3 removed the most at 14\.3%\. Filters that did not remove records indexed with &\#x27;nonhuman/&\#x27; had higher sensitivity\. Filter performance could vary by subject, publication type and language due to differences in indexing\. Conclusion: In choosing a search filter, information specialists and review teams should discuss whether animals or nonhumans could feature in relevant studies\.

## [Epidemiological evolution of repetitive strain injuries and work\-related musculoskeletal disorders in Brazil: comparative analysis between 1990 and 2025\.](../publications/3f6b7639ad8c62421e8c.md)

Paulo Roberto Zétola; Caroline Da Ros Montes D’Oca

The objective of this study was to analyze the evolution of the epidemiological profile of repetitive strain injuries and work\-related musculoskeletal disorders in Brazil, comparing the industrial and corporate scenario of the 1990s with national and regional data published between 2007 and 2025\. A literature review with comparative analysis of secondary data was conducted, using as historical reference the analysis of 125 repetitive strain injuries cases among workers in the electro\-electronic industry and, as a contemporary counterpart, studies based on data from Brazil&\#x27;s Notifiable Diseases Information System, the Department of Information Technology of the Unified Health System, and recent literature\. The historical sample showed a predominance of women \(73\.6%\) and workers aged 31 to 35 years \(28\.0%\), with initial emphasis on wrist tendinitis \(49\.6%\) and shoulder bursitis \(20\.0%\)\. At the end of follow\-up, chronic pain syndrome was recorded in 65\.6% of cases\. Contemporary data showed a higher case concentration in older age groups, especially between 40 and 49 years in the national study from 2007 to 2021 and between 40 and 59 years in the 2018\-2023 period\. In Paraná, between 2014 and 2023, 5,694 cases were recorded, with female predominance \(62\.5%\) and work shifts longer than six hours in 86\.8% of notifications\. The evolution of cases over time suggests greater clinical and occupational complexity of repetitive strain injuries and work\-related musculoskeletal disorders, underscoring the need for cautious interpretation of indicators and integrated preventive strategies\.

## [Digital attention disruption and academic impact in adolescents: a data\-driven network and machine learning analysis](../publications/3f7002fdb0f2de107498.md)

Yan Liu

Academic impact associated with digital media use is a topic of considerable concern in the fields of adolescent mental health and education; however, the role of attention status in this context remains largely unknown\. The present study aimed to systematically investigate the multidimensional association patterns between attention\-related characteristics and academic impact among adolescents using data mining approaches\. The data were derived from two publicly available cross\-sectional survey datasets, and a final sample of 799 adolescents aged 19 years and below was included after age screening\. The analytical framework integrated LASSO regression, regularized partial correlation network analysis based on EBICglasso, XGBoost predictive modeling with SHAP interpretation, and latent profile analysis\. Results showed that LASSO regression identified stress level \(coefficient = 0\.384\) and social media use duration \(coefficient = 0\.297\) as the strongest predictors of academic impact\. Network analysis revealed a three\-community structure, corresponding to the “digital distraction load,” “psychological\-academic exhaustion,” and “academic engagement” dimensions, with academic impact located at the intersection of the first two communities\. The XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0\.842, and SHAP dependence plots further revealed a nonlinear pattern with an inflection point at approximately 3\.5 hours for daily social media use duration and a nonlinear effect of stress level\. Latent profile analysis identified three subgroups, among which the “high stress\-exhaustion” group showed a probability of academic impact as high as 79\.4%\. These findings indicate that attention\-related characteristics can effectively predict academic impact status in adolescents, with stress level, social media use duration, and number of notifications constituting the most influential set of predictors\. The results provide data\-driven theoretical evidence and practical implications for the early identification and stratified intervention of academic impact in adolescents\.

## [Transcranial photobiomodulation reduces predator‐induced anxiety‐like behavior \(risk assessment\) in male Rattus norvegicus threatened by Bothrops jararaca pit vipers](../publications/3f7082a129509dad56b1.md)

Ohana Turcato Macacare; Gustavo de Oliveira Tunis; Paloma Molina Hernandes; Norberto Cysne Coimbra

Photobiomodulation, also known as low\-level laser therapy, uses specific wavelengths of light to stimulate biological tissues\. Evidence from the literature indicates that transcranial photobiomodulation can alter neurophysiological activity; however, studies investigating its effects on the neurobiology of emotions remain scarce\. Therefore, the objective of the present study was to investigate the effects of acute transcranial photobiomodulation administered at five irradiation sites using an 808 nm \(± 10 nm\) wavelength on anxiety\-like behavior in rodents \(Rattus norvegicus\) exposed to either a potential wild predator \(Bothrops jararaca\) or predator\-related cues \(snake odor\)\. Both the presence of the snake and exposure to its odor elicited anxiety\-like risk\-assessment behavior in the rodents\. In turn, photobiomodulation treatment significantly reduced both the frequency and duration of this behavior, suggesting a potential anxiolytic\-like effect\.

## [The combination of microbial agent, organic fertilizer, and silica powder enhances oat yield and quality through regulating rhizosphere processes](../publications/3f728d66c643072efcd6.md)

Ping Chen; Yuanyuan Luo; Lingfang Ma; Mengmeng He; hongxiu ma; Wenli Ma; Quan Sun

Aims Soil salinization is a global challenge for sustainable agricultural development\. Composite modifiers have the potential to boost the agricultural productivity of salinized soils\. However, it’s still unclear whether it outperforms single modifiers in regulating rhizosphere soil properties, microbial communities, and forage yield and quality of different oat varieties \( Avena sativa L\.\) and the mechanisms\. Methods In this field experiment in 2023–2024 in the arid western China, five modifier treatments, namely CK \(control group without any modifier\), TJ \(microbial agent\), TF \(organic fertilizer\), TG \(silica powder\), and TJFG \(microbial agent \+ organic fertilizer \+ silica powder\), were designed for two oat varieties \(TY 60, Tianyan 60; MST 2, Musite 2\)\. Then, their effects on salinized soil properties, rhizosphere microbial communities, and the interaction between soil nutrient cycling and microbial composition were explored\. Results The crude protein \(CP\) content of the two oat varieties peaked under the TJFG treatment\. The rhizosphere soil NH 4 \+ \-N, available phosphorus \(AP\), available potassium \(AK\), organic matter \(SOM\), and water content \(SWC\) of the TJFG treatment were significantly higher than those of CK, while the soil pH and NO 3 − \-N content were significantly lower\. In addition, the AP content of the TJFG treatment was 70\.17, 44\.91, and 66\.93% \(average over 2 years\) higher than that of the TJ, TF, and TG treatments, respectively\. Conclusion The application of TJFG improved the diversity of bacterial and fungal communities as well as the activities of phosphatase \(ATP\), urease \(UE\), and catalase \(CAT\), thereby promoting soil nutrient transformations and enhancing soil fertility, oat yield, and quality\. Chloroflexota and Ascomycota were the key microbial phyla to regulate oat yield\. Organic matter, AK, AP, and CAT activity were the main soil factors affecting yield\. Overall, MST 2 has greater growth potential and more value for promotion and application than TY 60\. This study provides an important reference for salinized land use, ecological health maintenance, and sustainable agricultural production in arid regions\.

## [An electric\-potential\-augmented benchmark dataset for electrical capacitance tomography: Electric\-potential supervision for future physics\-guided learning](../publications/3f729cc17199e38b97f9.md)

Xinqi Zhang; Qiming Ma; Lihui Peng

Abstract While deep learning has significantly advanced image reconstruction of electrical capacitance tomography \(ECT\), most public datasets retain only capacitance vectors and permittivity distributions and do not expose the excitation\-wise electric potential field, a physical intermediate in the forward mapping\. To address this, we present an electric\-potential\-augmented ECT benchmark dataset generated via a COMSOL\-\-MATLAB pipeline for a fixed eight\-electrode sensor\. The dataset comprises 20,000 randomized samples across four typical flow\-pattern families\. Alongside conventional capacitance vectors and permittivity images, each sample preserves eight spatially registered full\-field potential maps\. Governing equations and field\-perturbation visualizations characterize the relation between potential and dielectric structure\. As an initial use of this physical information, we introduce potential\-field intermediate supervision to guide representation learning in simple forward and inverse models\. Under sample\-disjoint independent and identically distributed \(IID\) and fully held\-out two\-bar out\-of\-distribution \(OOD\) evaluation, potential supervision reduces forward capacitance\-prediction mean squared error \(MSE\) by 56\.8\\% and 74\.6\\%, respectively, relative to a structure\- and capacity\-aligned control\. In an exploratory forward experiment, a low\-weight partial differential equation \(PDE\) residual yields 5\.3\-\-8\.3\\% lower mean potential\-prediction MSE\. For inverse reconstruction, the simple model reduces mean MSE by 14\.3\\% and 3\.0\\% on IID and OOD data, respectively, relative to the same control\. The more modest inverse gains are consistent with the difficulty of recovering dense potential maps from limited capacitance measurements\. These results provide initial controlled evidence for the value of potential\-field supervision\. The dataset and reference experiments together offer a foundation and methodological insights for developing more advanced field\-supervised, physics\-informed, and data\-consistent ECT methods\.

## [Performance of Claude 3\.5 Sonnet Compared to Human Readers of The New England Journal of Medicine Clinical Case Challenges](../publications/3f8043bf3890b2aeca81.md)

Jack Litwin; Daniel J\. Parente

Introduction: Large language models \(LLMs\) can pass the US medical licensing exam and outperform residents on the family medicine in\-training exam\. The diagnostic performance of LLMs when applied to more complex medical cases, however, remains unknown\.Methods: We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of Claude \(Anthropic\), an LLM, on 20 case challenges published in The New England Journal of Medicine \(NEJM\)\. For each case, we presented Claude 3\.5 Sonnet with multimodal input, including the text and all corresponding images from the cases\. Claude was instructed to give an answer among multiple choices\. We compared Claude’s diagnostic accuracy to human respondents on the NEJM website\.Results: Claude 3\.5 Sonnet diagnosed cases correctly about half the time, and at a significantly higher rate than NEJM readers \(beta\-binomial odds ratio 2\.79; 95% CI \[profile\-likelihood\] 1\.09–7\.01; P = 0\.031\)\. Claude was highly self\-consistent in repeated exposure to questions, with perfect accuracy \(100%\) in nine cases and no accuracy \(0%\) in 10 cases, with one case at 90% accuracy\. Human accuracy ranged from 9%–63% across cases\. Claude’s performance was better on easier cases \(ie, those with human accuracy &gt;25%\)\.Conclusions: Claude 3\.5 Sonnet demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy compared to medical journal readers, though with notable variability in performance\. Further research comparing consistency and reliability of artificially intelligent diagnostic capabilities to that of licensed physicians is needed\.

## [A Temporal–Graph Fusion Framework for Financial Distress Early Warning in Advanced Manufacturing Enterprises](../publications/3f93632001b7b51beeea.md)

Siwei Wang

Economic uncertainty and increasingly interconnected supply chains create challenges for identifying financial distress among advanced manufacturing enterprises, where risks may evolve over time and extend across firm relationships\. Conventional early warning approaches often have difficulty capturing both the temporal development of financial conditions and the structural dependencies through which vulnerabilities can spread\. This study proposes a temporal–graph fusion deep learning framework for financial distress early warning\. A dual\-channel analytical structure integrates financial reporting indicators and risk management information\. A gated temporal convolution module models changes in firm\-level financial characteristics, while a dynamic graph convolution module represents evolving inter\-firm relationships and potential channels of risk transmission\. Macroeconomic variables and cross\-environment regularization are incorporated to address distribution shifts across economic conditions\. SHAP\-based analysis is used to interpret the contribution of predictive features and to examine nonlinear patterns and interactions associated with financial vulnerability\. The reported empirical comparisons indicate that the proposed framework achieves favorable predictive discrimination, early warning performance, and stability relative to the evaluated baseline models\. The study thus presents a unified approach for integrating longitudinal financial data, inter\-firm network information, and interpretable machine learning into corporate financial distress assessment\.

## [Stability Analysis of a Liquid Oxygen–Methane Rocket Combustor Using Hybrid CFD–Machine Learning Approach](../publications/3f9b1dfde7ca977bfb27.md)

Arijit Bhattacharya; Abhishek Sharma; Sirshendu Mondal; Ashoke De

Modern rocket combustors are highly susceptible to thermoacoustic instability \(TAI\) due to the positive feedback between pressure and heat release oscillations that occurs inside the acoustically confined combustion chamber\. TAI in rocket combustors may result in structural damage and subsequent mission failure\. To avoid such an outcome, careful mapping of the stable and unstable regimes of the rocket combustors is typically undertaken during the design and development stages\. While experiments with industry\-scale rocket combustors are prohibitively expensive, large eddy simulation \(LES\) can greatly aid in understanding the stability characteristics of the combustor during the early stages of design\. However, LES of industry\-scale rocket combustors is itself computationally very expensive\. Therefore, we explore an alternative hybrid approach\. LES simulations of an industry\-scale LOX\-methane rocket combustor are run for a small set of operating points, and the obtained data are used to map the stable and unstable regimes of the combustor using a dynamics\-attuned data\-driven tool, namely the temporal convolutional network \(TCN\)\. TCN sensitivity to the approach of TAI is then bench\-marked against the 0–1 test and translational error analysis, two well\-known dynamics\-based tools that have previously been successfully applied in thermoacoustic instability characterization\. Among the methods explored, the TCN tool is seen to be most suitable for stability analysis of the rocket combustor, at least for capturing the dynamical transition observed in the present combustor configuration\. As the TCN tool is computationally cheap and inherently parallelizable, a hybrid LES\-TCN approach can significantly reduce the computational requirement for high\-fidelity simulation\-based stability analysis of rocket combustors\. Moreover, the results indicate that the TCN tool can also be used for early prediction of impending TAI on a real\-time basis\. However, the suitability of TCN for real\-time early detection remains to be validated experimentally\.

## [Differentially Private Statistical Learning: Uncertainty Estimation and Utility Preservation](../publications/3f9ef6dbdc4073f89517.md)

Cecilia Ferrando

Organizations increasingly rely on sensitive data for high\-impact decisions, making it essential to develop methods that ensure individual privacy while preserving the utility of downstream analyses\. Differential privacy \(DP\) has emerged as the gold standard for such guarantees\. This thesis contributes novel methods for differentially private statistical learning, with a focus on improving the usability of private inference through rigorous uncertainty quantification and the accuracy of private estimators via data\-dependent mechanisms\. First, we develop parametric bootstrap methods for DP confidence intervals, enabling uncertainty estimation through post\-processing while accounting for both sampling and privacy noise\. This approach avoids multiple accesses to the data and remains accurate even in small\-sample regimes\. Second, we propose data\-dependent sufficient statistic perturbation, a framework that applies private query\-answering algorithms to release sufficient statistics, improving estimation in both linear and logistic regression\. Third, we introduce a data\-dependent method for private multivariate Gaussian covariance estimation: instead of perturbing the entire matrix, we iteratively select the most informative covariance entries to measure under the privacy budget, then reconstruct the full positive semidefinite matrix via a maximum\-entropy completion\. By concentrating noise where it matters most, we show that this strategy yields high\-utility covariance estimates, paving the way for novel continuous synthetic data generation methods\. These contributions aim to bridge theory and practice, advancing the applicability of differential privacy in statistical machine learning\.

## [CNC toolpath\-driven thermal modeling of WAAM: thermal assessment and microstructural interpretation](../publications/3fb97288fd72c4148a57.md)

Theylor Andres Amaya Villabón; Andrés Fernando Gil Plazas; Julián David Rubiano Buitrago; Stefan Böhm; Liz Karen Herrera Quintero

Abstract Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing \(WAAM\) involves highly transient thermal cycles, repeated reheating, and strong spatial temperature gradients, all of which govern the final microstructure of the deposited material\. In this work, a three\-dimensional transient thermal model for WAAM of ER70S\-6 carbon steel was developed directly from the same processed CNC G\-code used to operate the experimental system\. This approach allowed the simulation to preserve the real deposition trajectory, torch motion, arc on/off sequence, and fan\-assisted interpass cooling intervals\. The computational workflow combined G\-code parsing, geometric reconstruction of the deposited wall and substrate, structured voxelization, progressive material activation, and explicit transient heat\-transfer solution\. The thermal problem was formulated considering conduction, convection, radiation, and a moving volumetric Gaussian heat source following the deposition path\. As a representative case study, the framework was applied to an eight\-bead thin\-wall deposition produced under a single controlled GMAW condition and compared with thermographic measurements acquired during processing\. The simulated temperature fields showed good qualitative agreement with infrared observations during both active deposition and interpass cooling\. Quantitative comparisons of maximum surface temperature and local temperature histories also showed that the model reproduced the main thermal evolution of the process, despite the saturation and spatial\-resolution limitations of the thermal camera\. The simulated thermal histories were interpreted alongside spatially corresponding metallographic observations along the build height\. Faster cooling near the substrate was associated with finer acicular ferrite, repeated reheating in the intermediate region promoted more homogeneous equiaxed polygonal ferrite, and slower cooling in the upper region preserved a coarser as\-deposited ferritic morphology\.

## [Process Simulation Framework for Optimizing Performance in Large\-Scale Natural Gas Processing Facilities](../publications/3fcd28e0d1be71a85571.md)

Eromosele Asibor

This paper develops a governed simulation lifecycle that connects model credibility, operating envelopes, process safety, reliability, and economic optimization\. The study responds to the problem that gas plants face changing feed composition, pressure, temperature, contaminants, throughput, equipment condition, utility limits, and product specifications\. It uses an integrative conceptual review of scholarly and professional literature published to date, drawing on process simulation, process systems engineering, natural\-gas processing, and process safety sources\. The framework organizes eight decision functions: model\-purpose definition, thermodynamic method selection, data reconciliation, calibration and validation, sensitivity analysis, optimization, dynamic scenario testing, model governance\. It applies those functions across inlet separation, acid\-gas removal, dehydration, hydrocarbon dew\-point control, compression, fractionation and utilities\. The analysis treats uncertainty, process safety, reliability, environmental performance, resource efficiency, economics, and organizational control as connected requirements\. The proposed architecture links a system definition, evidence register, model assumptions, intervention portfolio, verification plan, and learning cycle\. Its central proposition is that validated steady state and dynamic models support design, debottlenecking, control, energy efficiency, reliability, and safe operating decisions only when those decisions preserve traceability from measured conditions to selected actions and verified outcomes\. The paper offers testable propositions, an implementation roadmap, asset\-specific application protocols, and a research agenda\. The framework supports case\-study testing and quantitative extension without claiming universal performance before field validation\.

## [Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability](../publications/3fd62e8c92dc0e8bb0d8.md)

Qingshi Wang

Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence\. Existing large language models \(LLMs\) and Theory of Mind \(ToM\) methods primarily infer mental states from linguistic information, lacking unified mechanisms for subjective world construction, cognitive\-psychological interactions, dynamic evolution, and historical dependencies\. This paper introduces the Mental World Model \(MWM\) and its implementation, the Multi\-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture \(MMEA\), which explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models interactions between cognition and mental states, and simulates continuous mental evolution shaped by historical experiences\. On DynToM and RecToM, MMEA achieves 96\.48% and 94\.00% accuracy, respectively, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized ToM methods\. Additional experiments demonstrate improvements of 28\.7, 39\.3, and 16\.6 percentage points in mental state and behavior prediction, long\-sequence prediction, and implicit mental state inference, respectively\. The results demonstrate that MMEA provides an interpretable framework for continuous mental modeling, enabling AI to move beyond surface\-level semantic representations to infer individuals&\#x27; underlying mental states from linguistic information and dynamically simulate their internal cognitive processes and evolution over time\. MWM also provides a promising foundation for causal reasoning, personalized AI, sustained human\-AI interaction, and future advances toward artificial general intelligence \(AGI\)\.

## [Do machine learning models really encode cross\-cultural lifestyle\-health differences? A leakage\-free reanalysis of two university cohorts in India and Japan](../publications/3fdc84c887d6ad7ea114.md)

Eiko Takaoka; S\. Ruban; B\. Mohammed Siraj; Varenya Vinay; Hilda Shanthini; Akshay Dias

Introduction Machine\-learning \(ML\) studies increasingly compare feature\-importance rankings between small, unevenly sized cohorts and interpret the differences as evidence of culturally specific “risk architectures\.” We show that such comparisons can be highly misleading without leakage\-free evaluation, using a worked example from our own cross\-sectional lifestyle and health data collected during June\-August 2024 from two universities in India and Japan\. Three problems were identified in our preliminary analysis: \(1\) an outcome \(obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 25\) that was tautologically predicted by including BMI itself as a model input; \(2\) model evaluation without a held\-out test set; and \(3\) feature\-importance comparisons that ignored sampling variability from an eightfold difference in cohort size\. Methods We addressed each problem using penalized logistic regression, Random Forest, and gradient\-boosted trees with proper train/test splitting, held\-out permutation importance, and bootstrap confidence intervals\. We also ran a sensitivity analysis that repeatedly subsampled the Indian cohort down to the size of the Japanese cohort\. Results Removing body mass index \(BMI\) as a predictor collapsed obesity\-model discrimination from perfect \(AUC = 1\.00\) to chance level \(AUC = 0\.50\-0\.57\), confirming that the BMI\-obesity association was definitional rather than empirical\. Held\-out predictive performance for the remaining viable outcome, elevated self\-rated stress, was modest at best \(AUC 0\.49\-0\.71\)\. Critically, in the subsampling analysis, every feature\-importance value observed in the actual Japanese data fell within the range produced by sample\-size noise alone\. Discussion We present this analysis as a transparent, reproducible case study of specific, checkable pitfalls: label leakage, missing train/test evaluation, unadjusted small\-sample comparison, and mislabeled psychometric instruments\. These should be routinely screened for before ML feature importance is interpreted as evidence of population\-level or cultural differences in digital health research\.

## [Supporting Student Success Through an Interpretable Early Warning System in a First\-Year Statistics Unit](../publications/4012a7c074d071bc0116.md)

Bee Lam; Steven Richardson

Early identification of students experiencing academic difficulty is critical to supporting student success and retention in their first year of university\. This study examines an interpretable learning analytics framework designed to support timely intervention in a first\-year introductory statistics unit\. Data from 566 students across three cohorts were used to develop and evaluate predictive models using assessment results collected during the teaching period and enrolment characteristics\. The selected model demonstrated strong predictive performance and was validated on a subsequent cohort\. To support practical implementation, predictions were translated into a colour\-coded risk report that enables educators to quickly identify and prioritise students requiring academic support\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\)\-based explanations were incorporated to provide transparency and assist educators in understanding the factors contributing to individual risk classifications\. Findings indicate that formative assessments are the strongest indicators of academic success, highlighting opportunities for proactive and targeted intervention\. The framework demonstrates how interpretable learning analytics can support evidence\-informed decision\-making and student success in large first\-year units\.

## [Evacuation of Educational Institutions: A Predictive Analysis and Profiling Approach](../publications/401ef7b3110bdd12c468.md)

Kioumourtzi Maria; Klimis Ntalianis; Nikos E\. Mastorakis

The safe and efficient evacuation of educational institutes in emergency situations requires planning, coordination, and prioritization that takes into consideration the complexity of diverse populations and building structures\. Conventional methods of evacuation planning are usually static and do not consider dynamic situations like hazard progression, crowd density, and vulnerable populations\. Recent developments in predictive analysis algorithms offer an opportunity to predict and plan evacuations more effectively\. This paper aims to discuss the integration of predictive analysis and profiling techniques in planning evacuations, specifically in relation to “who goes first and why\.” Parameters like age, mobility, proximity to hazards, and other characteristics are considered, and existing literature shows that vulnerable populations are given priority in evacuation planning\. Ethical issues like data privacy are also considered in predictive analysis and its integration in planning evacuations\. Predictive analysis in planning evacuations is a transformative tool in ensuring safe evacuations in educational institutes\.

## [Development and validation of an artificial intelligence literacy scale for students](../publications/4020d62c914ef97d8759.md)

Esra Nur Demirtaş; Tuğçe Gamze İŞÇİ

In today’s technological age, artificial intelligence literacy \(AIL\) has become a critical issue in the field of education\. The ability to understand, use, and critically evaluate artificial intelligence \(AI\) technologies is recognized as a fundamental competency enabling students to actively participate in the digital age\. In this context, the aim of this study is to develop a valid and reliable scale to obtain accurate data on artificial intelligence literacy by examining the concept of artificial intelligence literacy\. The study sample consists of 870 students \(424 boys, 346 girls\) in grades 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 attending elementary and middle schools\. A pool of 50 items was created to measure students’ levels of artificial intelligence literacy\. Exploratory Factor Analysis \(EFA\) resulted in 22 items and 6 subscales\. The measurement model obtained from Confirmatory Factor Analysis \(CFA\) demonstrated good fit\. The Cronbach’s Alpha internal consistency coefficient for the scale was found to be 0\.857, while the internal consistency coefficients for the subscales ranged between 0\.81 and 0\.82\. The CR, AVE, MSV, and ASV values indicate that the scale possesses both discriminant and convergent validity\. In conclusion, the developed scale possesses sufficient characteristics to determine students’ levels of AIL\. This study will assist in the development, teaching, and learning of AIL, as well as in the evaluation of AI education\.

## [Descriptive morpho pathological lesions and surveillance baseline of mesenchymal tumors in some commercially important marine fish species from the Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia](../publications/40227c74780ac02c316a.md)

F\.A\. Al\-Hizab; Ibtesam S\. Al\-Dhuayan; Mahmoud A\. Mahmoud; Mustafa M\. Ibrahim

Mesenchymal neoplasms in marine teleosts provide valuable insights into individual pathological states; however, interpreting them as indicators of environmental integrity requires considerable caution, and documenting such tumors is essential for monitoring ecosystem stressors\. This study aimed to describe several types of mesenchymal tumors in four commercially important fish species caught in the Arabian Gulf in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia\. During routine veterinary inspections at landing stations and markets in Jubail in 2025, 1,850 fish samples were examined\. Samples included Lethrinus nebulosus , Carangoides gymnostethus , Lethrinus lentjan , and Siganus canaliculatus\. Gross pathological examinations were conducted, followed by histopathological assessment using hematoxylin and eosin \(H&amp;E\) and Masson’s trichrome \(MT\) stains\. Ten cases of neoplastic growths were identified, representing an overall observed frequency of 0\.54%\. Lipomas were diagnosed in L\. nebulosus and C\. gymnostethus , presenting as well\-circumscribed, greasy, white subcutaneous masses composed of well\-differentiated adipocytes\. Rhabdomyoma was observed in L\. lentjan and was characterized by solitary, pedunculated overgrowths of pleomorphic but benign skeletal muscle fibers exhibiting loss of normal myotome polarity\. Rhabdomyosarcoma was identified in S\. canaliculatus , with malignant features including poorly differentiated myocytes, cellular pleomorphism, hemorrhage, and infiltration into the abdominal cavity with displacement of visceral organs\. As tumorigenesis in aquatic organisms are indicators for many environmental pollutants and stress, further studies are required to confirm the potential etiologies of such lesions in this region\.

## [Analysis Of The Malfunction And Handling Of Flap Stuck On A Cessna 172s Trainer Aircraft](../publications/4024823efd91f846aa28.md)

Iswahyudi Iswahyudi; Muhammad Akbar Ansor; Ajeng Wulansari; Aydin Anar Babayev

The flap is a secondary flight control component that assists the primary flight control by increasing the aircraft&\#x27;s lift at low speed, so its reliability must be maintained to avoid compromising flight training safety\. During the study period, a Cessna 172S trainer aircraft registered PK\-BYJ was reported to experience a malfunction on both flaps, which failed to move during ground run up, potentially affecting the performance of the flight control surfaces\. This article aims to analyze the cause of the malfunction and document the repair process\. The method used was field observation and systematic troubleshooting referring to the Cessna 172S Aircraft Maintenance Manual \(AMM\) Chapter 27, consisting of disassembly, inspection, servicing, reassembly, and functional test stages\. The disassembly and inspection results on the flap motor showed that the component had malfunctioned and could no longer drive both flaps despite receiving an appropriate electrical supply\. The repair was carried out by replacing the flap motor in accordance with AMM Chapter 27 procedures, followed by reassembly and a functional test that showed both flaps could move normally again, so the aircraft was declared airworthy for flight training operations\. This case study emphasizes the importance of compliance with AMM procedures and technician competence in diagnosing electromechanical component failures in flight control systems to maintain the reliability and operational safety of trainer aircraft\.

## [Large language models for ADHD clinical label prediction via parent questionnaires: diagnostic performance, explanation groundedness, and failure modes a temporal validation study](../publications/4034544a11dcb68a604a.md)

Rongqi Jiao; Dandan Wu; Hongyan Zhang; Jinlei Sun; Jing Zhang

Large language models \(LLMs\) can process descriptions from parent\-completed questionnaires, producing risk estimates and auditable reasoning\. Psychiatric LLM evaluations have focused on accuracy alone, rarely examining whether explanations are grounded in input data or language behavior changes with errors\. We evaluated four LLMs across classification, explanation groundedness, language behavior during errors, and grey\-zone boundaries\. We analyzed 2,264 de\-identified cases from a single\-center child psychiatry clinic under temporal validation \(training n=1,268, test n=996\), with DSM\-5 attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\) diagnosis by attending psychiatrists as the reference standard; controls had no other primary psychiatric diagnosis\. Four LLMs received descriptions of the Conners Parent Rating Scale and Weiss Functional Impairment Rating Scale\. LASSO and XGBoost served as supervised baselines\. Rationales underwent rule\-based groundedness annotation with expert validation on 80 cases; grey\-zone stratification used LASSO composite scores with principal component analysis \(PCA\)\. Under the Elevated\-Item condition, the four LLMs achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) of 0\.803–0\.823 and Cohen&\#x27;&\#x27;s κ of 0\.470–0\.492; Claude Opus 4\.7 was within 0\.004 of the item\-level LASSO baseline \(κ=0\.488\)\. Rule\-based annotation identified 36\.2%–41\.7% of claims as not directly supported by input data; expert assessment on a subset found \~38% \(κ=0\.699\), matching the automated method\. In the grey zone \(\~38% of cases\), all methods performed poorly \(LLM κ 0\.105–0\.140; LASSO κ 0\.228\), and PCA sensitivity analysis improved but did not eliminate uncertainty\. Reasoning structure did not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect predictions\. LLMs extracted signals comparable to supervised machine learning while generating auditable rationales\. However, more than one\-third of their clinical claims were not directly supported by the input data \(36\.2%–41\.7% across models by rule\-based annotation, closely matched by expert assessment on a subset at \~38%\), language behavior did not reliably signal classification errors, and all methods performed poorly in the grey zone \(over one\-third of cases\), where the simpler, more transparent LASSO baseline was at least as accurate\. Because a fluent narrative may present limited evidence as coherent judgment, LLM explanations should be treated as auditable drafts, not diagnostic conclusions\. The four\-dimension framework offers a reusable template for psychiatric AI evaluation; clinical deployment is not supported\.

## [Flexible Insole with Soft, Integrated, Polymeric Pressure Sensors to Discriminate Different Types of Gaits Using Machine Learning Techniques](../publications/4035c17a51894bfcda7a.md)

Valentina Vit; Luca Liparulo; A\. Alam; Riccardo Pecori; Nicola Coppedé

Wearable sensors offer promising solutions for continuous gait monitoring in healthcare, rehabilitation, and sports\. In this paper, a novel, soft, flexible, and easily made wearable sensor to detect the pressure generated by human gait was developed\. The sensor consists of a soft polyurethane foam functionalized with a PEDOT:PSS aqueous solution designed to integrate the active material and develop a piezoresistive device\. Eight soft sensors have been integrated into an insole, with dedicated readout electronic circuitry, including an accelerometer, a gyroscope, and a Bluetooth communication tag\. Seven participants’ gaits were analyzed, and for each one, three types of walks were recorded: normal, prone, and supine\. The data were analyzed with Machine Learning \(ML\) techniques, combining plantar pressure, accelerometer, and gyroscope features, to validate the device in discriminating among the three types of gaits\. Ten supervised classifiers were assessed, such as Random Forest \(RF\), Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), Multi\-layer Perceptron \(MLP\), K\-Nearest Neighbors, and Gradient Boosting, using a sliding\-window feature extraction pipeline and a chronological, per\-recording train\-test split designed to avoid information leakage between overlapping windows\. Hyperparameter optimization was carried out via Randomized Search with a stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation protocol\. The device has turned out to be suitable for detecting the three types of gaits thanks to the good results obtained by leveraging ML algorithms, reaching a classification accuracy of 90\.38% on held\-out data in a user\-specific \(subject\-dependent\) setting\. In a stricter Leave\-One\-Subject\-Out evaluation on participants never seen during training, accuracy reached 67\.66%, about twice the chance level, without any labeled data from the new user\. These results demonstrate the proposed flexible pressure system’s capability for continuous gait monitoring and support its use in healthcare diagnostics, rehabilitation evaluation, and sports biomechanics\.

## [Chaotic slime mould metaheuristic with Chebyshev map for IoT service composition](../publications/403f3a6d20e7a51d64f8.md)

Amal Halfaoui; Hadjila Fethallah; Zeyneb ElYebdri

The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things \(IoT\) has led to a proliferation of services offering identical functionalities with heterogeneous capabilities and quality levels\. Efficiently composing these IoT services to satisfy user requirements while maintaining system performance under strict Quality of Service constraints, such as energy consumption, remains a challenging combinatorial optimization problem\. Metaheuristic algorithms have proven effective in addressing such large\-scale optimization tasks\. This paper first proposes an energy consumption model for IoT services\. It then proposes two novel discrete versions of the Slime Mould Algorithm \(SMA\) specifically designed for IoT service composition\. The first, called Discrete Slime Mould Algorithm \(DSMA\), adapts SMA to the discrete domain using adaptive fitness\-based weights, probabilistic gene copying from the best solution, and an adaptive mutation mechanism\. The second, called Chaotic Discrete Slime Mould Algorithm \(CDSMA\), further integrates Chebyshev chaotic maps for population initialization and weight updating to improve population diversity and accelerate convergence\. Experimental results show that CDSMA consistently outperforms DSMA and other classical metaheuristics\. CDSMA achieves an optimality rate of 96\.33% with a small population size and 99\.92% with a moderate population size\. Furthermore, extensive experiments over 30 independent runs confirm that both proposed algorithms significantly outperform classical metaheuristics\. CDSMA achieves 96\.46% \(±0\.65\) optimality, DSMA achieves 93\.75% \(±0\.75\), significantly outperforming SMA \(84\.74%\), GWO \(82\.54%\), HHO \(82\.87%\), and WOA \(80\.15%\) with statistical significance \(t\-test, p &lt; 10\-20\)\.

## [DOST MU DÜŞMAN MI? 6C ÇERÇEVESİ BAĞLAMINDA ÜRETKEN YAPAY ZEKA DESTEKLİ KONUŞMA ÖĞRETİMİNİN İNGİLİZCEYİ YABANCI DİL OLARAK ÖĞRENEN ÖĞRENCİLERİN KONUŞMA BAŞARISI, İKİNCİ DİL MOTİVASYONU VE ÜRETKEN YAPAY ZEKA KABULÜ ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİLERİNİN İNCELENMESİ](../publications/405e38e7e17a37d42eb3.md)

İrem Altunel

This study investigated the effectiveness of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\)\-assisted speaking instruction in enhancing EFL learners’ speaking achievement, L2 motivation and their GenAI acceptance through the lens of the 6Cs Framework\. Adopting a sequential explanatory mixed\-methods design, the study involved 50 EFL learners in two intact classes at a Turkish university\. The experimental group received GenAI\-assisted speaking instruction through ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode, while the control group received non\-GenAI\-assisted speaking instruction for eight weeks\. Quantitative data were collected through speaking achievement tests, L2 Motivation Scale, and GenAI Acceptance scale, while qualitative data were obtained through semi\-structured interviews with 10 experimental\-group participants\. The findings revealed that the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvement in speaking achievement than the control group\. Significant improvement was also found in overall L2 motivation, particularly in Ideal L2 Self, Language Learning Experience, and Intended Effort\. Learners also reported a high overall level of GenAI acceptance with the subdimensions of Performance Expectancy and Facilitating Conditions\. Qualitative findings further indicated that GenAI\-assisted speaking activities contributed to learners’ creativity, critical thinking, cultural awareness, personal growth, communicative competence, and collaborative learning\. Participants particularly valued personalized feedback, meaningful communication opportunities, and a supportive speaking environment, while also reporting several technical and interaction\-related challenges\. Overall, the findings suggest that pedagogically informed GenAI integration can complement EFL speaking instruction by providing meaningful, personalized, and interactive speaking opportunities while supporting learners’ linguistic, motivational, and broader competency development\.

## [From Technology Users to Sustainability\-Oriented Learning Designers: Developing Science Teachers&\#x27; STEM–IoT Competencies through Professional Development](../publications/406224bbb64489d8dbb7.md)

Diana Rochintaniawati; Rika Rafikah; Hanna Nurul Husna; Aay Susilawaty; Joey M\. Suba

Purpose: This study examined whether an integrated STEM–Internet of Things \(IoT\)–Education for Sustainable Development \(ESD\) professional\-development program was associated with differences in junior secondary science teachers’ competencies at the group level\. Methods: A quantitative, pre\-experimental repeated cross\-sectional pretest–posttest design analyzed 29 valid pretest and 33 valid posttest responses from the MGMP IPA teacher community in Sumedang, Indonesia\. A researcher\-developed assessment comprised 10 multiple\-choice items and five constructed\-response items \(maximum total score = 100\)\. Descriptive statistics, normalized gain based on group means, Welch’s independent\-samples t\-test, Mann–Whitney U, and Hedges’ g were reported\. Findings: The mean total score was higher at posttest \(83\.24, SD = 11\.07\) than at pretest \(59\.34, SD = 16\.22\); the descriptive normalized gain was 0\.588\. Welch’s t\(48\.49\) = 6\.682 \(p &lt; \.001\), and Hedges’ g = 1\.72 indicated a large group\-level separation\. The largest multiple\-choice differences concerned the Blynk platform and ESP8266/Wi\-Fi modules, whereas constructed responses showed higher scores for sensor\-data interpretation and IoT–ESD project design\. Implications: Integrated technical practice, data interpretation, and pedagogical design may provide a useful structure for science\-teacher professional development\. These cross\-sectional comparisons cannot establish within\-teacher growth, program causality, or transfer to classroom practice\. Originality: The study examines factual, interpretive, and design\-oriented competencies within a combined STEM–IoT–ESD teacher\-learning program\.

## [Pier, Jens: Apperception as Capacity, I as Act: Kant on Self\-Consciousness as the Constitutive Human Faculty](../publications/40687b089a06b1099d89.md)



\_Topoi\_\. forthcomingIn recent years, renewed attention has been paid to Kant’s concern with capacities and faculties of the mind\. His critical philosophy is frequently characterized as a “capacity\-first philosophy” or “capacitism\.” A common feature of these characterizations is that they frame this feature as a matter of optional choice or theory design\. This paper also characterizes Kant’s philosophy as capacitism, though I argue that, firstly, he ultimately focuses on but one single capacity—self\-consciousness or apperception\. Secondly, I resist the idea that this focus should fundamentally be seen as a matter of metaphilosophical choice or design\. It is rather an articulation or explication of something non\-optional: on my interpretation, Kant’s capacitism brings out and makes explicit apperception as the starting point and principle of transcendental philosophy\. It occupies this principal position because it is the constitutive human faculty: the faculty in light of which all other faculties must be made sense of\. I further argue that judgment or the “I think” is the paradigmatic act of this capacity, and suggest that ultimately, apperception ought to be regarded as identical to human spontaneity in general\. Kant’s philosophy should thus be characterized as an apperception\-first philosophy\.

## [A CRITICAL REVIEW OF DATA ANALYTICS APPLICATIONS FOR ENHANCING ACCOUNTABILITY AND OUTCOME MEASUREMENT IN U\.S\. CHILD WELFARE SUPPORT AND CARE SYSTEMS](../publications/407946f7cb5abb9c01b1.md)

Tinotenda Mukaira; Mary Magdalene Yeboah; Matthew Oman\-Amoako

This is a critical review that examines the current trends in applications of data analytics for accountability and outcome determination in U\.S\. child welfare models\. Analytics tools, such as data administrative dashboards, risk predictive models, and decision making support models, are gaining applicability by child welfare organization to enhance assessment of risk, performance stem surveillance, characterize service gaps, and for outcome tracking besides stability placement, reunification, readmission into care, and the maltreatment recurrence\. Nevertheless, the review purports that data analytics entirely cannot serve as a technical solution\. Child welfare information is determined by institutional processes, reporting trends, service levels, and outstanding demographic disparities and socioeconomic inequalities\. Analytical tools, if when not validated carefully, and thoroughly examined through microscopic review lenses, can multiply instead of mitigating the disparities that exists\. This paper is premised on privacy protection, transparency, accountability, expertise review, and family involvement as fundamental undertakings for responsible analytics applicability\. It is premised that meaningful accountability is essential for ethical governance, capacity for corrective action, and a recognition that analytics ought to support, not eliminate, professional judgment in children issues decisions making, agencies and families\.

## [Mitigating Volatility in P2E through Allowance Verification in Decentralized Platform](../publications/407e1a6f80dfb149e1d8.md)

Md Shariful Islam; Hye\-Young Kim

Play\-to\-Earn \(P2E\) game economies integrated with Automated Market Maker \(AMM\) protocols face persistent sustainability challenges driven by whale\-induced price volatility and the absence of effective token\-burning mechanisms\. These issues erode economic fairness and discourage long\-term participation within web\-based blockchain gaming platforms\. This paper proposes EG\-AMM \(Epoch\-Guarded Automated Market Maker\), a software engineering framework that adds a governance\-aware volatility protection layer to existing AMM\-based P2E infrastructures without modifying the underlying pricing model\. Inspired by circuit breaker mechanisms in traditional finance, EG\-AMM enforces per\-epoch dynamic swap allowances for individual players, computed from price impact tolerance and configurable through Decentralized Autonomous Organization \(DAO\) parameters\. The framework employs Merkle\-proof\-based cryptographic verification and on\-chain accounting to ensure allowance limits are transparent and tamper\-resistant\. Unlike existing pool\-level approaches such as static transaction caps or dynamic fee schedules, EG\-AMM operates at the individual player level, curbing whale dominance while preserving equitable market access for ordinary players and newcomers\. Preliminary analysis and game\-theoretic simulation confirm improvements in price stability, participation fairness, and economic resilience, offering a practical and deployable path toward sustainable token ecosystems in blockchain\-integrated gaming applications\.

## [Microvascular resistance reserve: insights into discordant resting and hyperemic epicardial coronary physiology](../publications/40aaf9e71d49b1a1b16c.md)

Aswin Babu; Isobelle Goldrick; Billy Broadbent; Rania Faeq; Charley Ann Budgeon; Roopa Krishnamoorthy; Primero Ng; Cara Barnes; D\. Sankhesara; Avadhesh Saraswat; I\. Shiekh; James Marangou; Richard F\. Alcock; Rachel C\. Orme; Carl Johann Schultz; Graham S\. Hillis; J\. Spiro

Introduction Discordance between resting and hyperemic epicardial physiology is commonbut mechanistically unclear\. Microvascular resistance reserve \(MRR\), a novelindex of vasodilatory capacity, may provide insight\. We aimed to characterizethe prevalence and microvascular substrate of FFR/RFR discordance, andwhether MRR is independently associated with discordant phenotypes\. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 891 vessels from 723 consecutive patients with paired resting full\-cycle ratio \(RFR\) and fractional flow reserve \(FFR\) measurements \(June 2018–October 2024\)\. Vessels were categorized as concordant or discordant\. An operator\-selected subset of 210 underwent coronary flow reserve \(CFR\), index of microvascular resistance \(IMR\), and MRR assessment\. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of each discordant phenotype \(FFR−/RFR\+ and FFR\+/RFR−\)\. Results Discordance was present in 195 vessels \(22%\); 121 \(13\.6%\) FFR−/RFR\+ and 74 \(8\.3%\) FFR\+/RFR−\. Discordance was more common in the LAD \(25% vs\. 17%, OR 1\.68, 95% CI 1\.20–2\.36, p = 0\.003\), driven predominantly by the FFR−/RFR\+ phenotype \(OR 2\.43, 95% CI 1\.56–3\.78, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. In the microvascular subset \( n = 210\), reduced CFR \(OR 0\.77, 95% CI 0\.59–0\.97, p = 0\.039\) and reduced MRR \(OR 0\.81, 95% CI 0\.65–0\.97, p = 0\.037\) were independently associated with the FFR−/RFR\+ phenotype, while neither predicted the FFR\+/RFR− phenotype\. However, among 45 discordant vessels with microvascular data, MRR provided greater discrimination than CFR \(AUC 0\.712, 95% CI 0\.539–0\.884 vs\. 0\.608, 95% CI 0\.434–0\.783, p = 0\.018\)\. Discussion These exploratory, hypothesis\-generating findings suggest that impaired microvascular vasodilatory reserve, expressed predominantly as elevated resting flow, may contribute mechanistically to the FFR−/RFR\+ phenotype\.

## [Securing Digital Governance: A Doctrinal and Empirical Analysis of the Legal Framework Governing e\-Government System Protection in Tanzania](../publications/40b6e2d57506c3c828b8.md)

Mary Juma

Tanzania has moved much of its public administration onto shared digital platforms, among them the Government Electronic Payment Gateway \(GePG\), the Government Enterprise Service Bus \(GovESB\) and the e\-Office system\. The legal protection of these platforms rests on Part VII of the e\-Government Act \[Cap 273 R\.E\. 2023\], supported by the Cybercrimes Act, the Electronic Transactions Act and the Personal Data Protection Act\. This article asks whether that framework secures government systems in practice or only on paper\. It combines doctrinal analysis of the statutes, as consolidated in the Revised Edition of 2023 and amended in 2024, with qualitative data from semi\-structured interviews with thirty respondents in Morogoro Region, comprising ICT officers, administrators, users, members of the public and legal practitioners\. It draws on Information Systems Security Theory, Deterrence Theory and Protection Motivation Theory\. The article finds that the statutes are broad in coverage but thin in enforceable detail\. Sections 37 and 38 of the e\-Government Act impose security duties on public institutions without an institutional sanction, a timeline for remedial action, or a defined threshold for reporting incidents, while criminal liability under section 57 falls on individuals even where the underlying failure is budgetary or structural\. Responsibility is spread across the e\-Government Authority, the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority and its national CERT, the Personal Data Protection Commission and the police, with no statutory rule on who leads when an incident touches all of them\. Courts still apply the electronic evidence rules unevenly, and a thin treaty base limits the practical reach of Tanzania&\#x27;s extraterritorial jurisdiction\. The article argues that effectiveness depends less on enacting further statutes than on precision, enforceability and coordination, and it proposes targeted amendments, an incident coordination protocol, standardised forensic rules and ratification of the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime, which Tanzania signed in October 2025\.

## [USING CONTEMPORARY ENGLISH\-LANGUAGE SONGS IN TEACHING ENGLISH AT SENIOR SECONDARY SCHOOL](../publications/40c2ae42d5c8d8ed581b.md)

Taisiia Gotthard; Oksana Sierhieieva

The article substantiates the systematic rather than occasional use of contemporary English\-language songs as authentic material in teaching English to senior secondary school learners \(grades 10\-11\)\. Cognitive, affective, and sociocultural evidence on the role of music in second language acquisition is reviewed, and nine criteria for selecting songs for this age group are formulated\. The core of the study is a mapping of song material onto the thematic units of the Ukrainian senior\-school foreign language syllabus, accompanied by an indication of the language focus that each song can service and of a corresponding productive task\. A three\-phase methodological model \(pre\-listening, while\-listening, post\-listening\) is described, together with a typology of tasks in which every deletion, transformation and discussion prompt is tied to an explicit language objective instead of to the song as entertainment\. A sample forty\-five\-minute lesson framework and guidance on formative assessment are supplied, and the practical limitations of the approach are examined — non\-standard grammar in lyrics, content vetting, copyright compliance, and the risk of overuse\. ## [Machine Learning and IoT Monitoring for Stream\-Level Nowcasting: Event\-Based Performance Assessment](../publications/40c2bff9db99938e0e4f.md)

Michele Calvello; Rosa Menichini; Gaetano Pecoraro

Machine learning \(ML\) models utilizing high\-frequency Internet of Things \(IoT\) monitoring data offer significant potential for stream\-level nowcasting\. The assessment of model performance is often a challenging task because conventional approaches are typically influenced by prevailing low\-variability baseline conditions and are unable to assess a model’s ability, or inability, to reproduce rare but critical stream\-level surges\. To address this limitation, this study proposes a framework combining standard and event\-based performance metrics\. Using two years of multi\-source observations \(i\.e\., stream level, volumetric water content, suction, and rainfall\) collected in a small catchment in southern Italy, a set of Random Forest \(RF\) models was developed to systematically investigate the effect of adopting alternative feature sets, calibration strategies, and target formulations\. The assessment of the calibrated models was performed considering 29 stream\-level surge events\. The results of the analyses revealed that better statistical accuracy over the entire validation period does not necessarily translate into better capability in reproducing critical event dynamics\. Three main findings emerged: \(i\) models predicting short\-term stream\-level variations consistently outperformed those directly predicting stream level; \(ii\) calibration using the complete continuous dataset produced more robust models than calibration based exclusively on surge events; and \(iii\) a reduced set of features provided the most favorable performance balance between predictive performance and model robustness among the tested configurations\. Overall, these results suggest that combining conventional and event\-based evaluation metrics can provide a complementary assessment of ML forecasting models, highlighting the importance of considering both overall predictive accuracy and event\-scale dynamics\.

## [Evaluation of the accuracy of AI\-based pellet size measurement using experimental data and Monte Carlo simulation](../publications/40c5325d9618be8a9710.md)

Bettina Fazekas; Zoltán Petrovics; Dorián László Galata; Orsolya Péterfi; Éva Pusztai; Nikolett Kállai‐Szabó; István Antal; Edit Hirsch; Zsombor Kristóf Nagy

The purpose of this work is to evaluate the capability of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based particle size measurement in the case of pellet coating\. We hypothesize that due to the large number of particles observed per minute, the technique should be able to give statistically significant results even for small diameter differences in the order of several μm\. Experiments were performed with samples taken during a pellet coating process, where each sample was found to be significantly different\. To overcome the limitations of experiments where it is not feasible to produce samples with arbitrarily small size differences, we performed simulations relying on the Monte Carlo method\. Based on the simulations and the observed number of particles per minute during the experiments, we found that in processes where the diameter increase rate of the particles is above 3\.30 μm/min, the current setup of AI\-based endoscopic imaging can be reliably used for process monitoring, because it can provide statistically significant results for the involved particle size changes\.

## [The Role of AI In Startup Resource Optimization: A Content\-Analytic Study Using Chi\-Square, ANOVA and Linear Regression](../publications/40c75ef4310522aac40e.md)
