## [Factors Influencing Consumer Adoption And Willingness\-To\-Pay for Assistive Technologies: A Case Study of Voice\-Controlled Devices for the Elderly in Vietnam](../publications/41f92dd9776a998ae71b.md)

Nguyen Ha Bao; Quan Nguyen

The Viet Nam is experiencing rapid population ageing, creating an increasing need for technologies that support older adults’ independence and ageing in place\. This study examines the factors influencing older Vietnamese consumers’ intention to adopt voice\-controlled devices \(VCDs\) and investigates whether adoption intention contributes to willingness to pay \(WTP\)\. Drawing on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 \(UTAUT2\) and gerontechnology research, the study develops a model incorporating performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, trust, privacy concern, and technology anxiety as determinants of adoption intention\. The model further proposes adoption intention as a mediator between these antecedents and WTP\. Data were collected through a cross\-sectional survey of 225 Vietnamese adults aged 60 years and above in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City\. The measurement and structural models were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The results show that facilitating conditions exert the strongest positive effect on adoption intention \(β = 0\.711, p &lt; \.001\), followed by effort expectancy \(β = 0\.235, p &lt; \.001\), trust \(β = 0\.145, p &lt; \.001\), social influence \(β = 0\.113, p = \.016\), and performance expectancy \(β = 0\.108, p = \.002\)\. Privacy concern negatively affects adoption intention \(β = −0\.230, p &lt; \.001\), while technology anxiety has a smaller but significant negative effect \(β = −0\.043, p = \.027\)\. Adoption intention strongly predicts WTP \(β = 0\.787, p &lt; \.001\)\. Furthermore, adoption intention significantly mediates the relationships between all seven antecedents and WTP\. The findings demonstrate that older consumers’ willingness to pay is closely connected to their readiness to adopt VCDs, while practical support and ease of use are particularly important for adoption in the Vietnamese context\. The study contributes to technology\-acceptance and assistive\-technology research by integrating enabling and inhibiting factors with WTP and provides implications for developers, retailers, families, caregivers, and policymakers seeking to promote age\-friendly voice technologies in Viet Nam\.

## [When voices can be cloned: vocal identity threat and occupational self\-efficacy among singers in the era of generative AI audio](../publications/41f99972d5e9dd96f8b7.md)

Jingjing Niu; Yinghao Qi; Xiaobin Li

Generative AI voice cloning has advanced rapidly, yet its psychological and professional implications for singers remain underexplored\. This review synthesizes empirical evidence concerning two central constructs: vocal identity threat, defined as the perceived erosion of the connection between voice and self, and occupational self\-efficacy, referring to confidence in maintaining professional competence and value under technological uncertainty\. Neurocognitive and behavioral evidence indicates that the human voice functions as a highly self\-relevant identity cue supported by self\-prioritized processing, body ownership, and multisensory integration\. As AI\-generated voice clones become increasingly humanlike, questions have emerged about how such technologies may affect singers&\#x27; perceptions of vocal identity and professional value\. Importantly, perceptual discrimination between human and AI\-generated voices remains dependent on stimulus characteristics, listener factors, and the availability of prosodic and expressive cues\. We argue that three distinctions are critical for interpreting the current evidence: timbral similarity should not be equated with artistic equivalence, increasingly humanlike output does not establish perceptual interchangeability, and the implications of AI may differ depending on whether it substitutes for identity\-bearing vocal labor or scaffolds human\-controlled performance and creation\. Current evidence therefore provides an empirical basis for investigating potential AI\-related threats to singers&\#x27; vocal identity and occupational confidence, but direct singer\-specific evidence remains unavailable\. Future research should prioritize singer\-specific quantitative studies employing longitudinal designs, ecologically valid voice\-cloning scenarios, comparison conditions, and direct measures of identity threat and occupational self\-efficacy\.

## [Learning Self\-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms](../publications/420221dcfa53cd8535f3.md)

Guowei Xu; Zhenting Qi; Amani Kiruga; Himabindu Lakkaraju; Yilun Du

The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate\. Yet existing multi\-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior\. We introduce market\-based post\-training \(MPT\), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self\-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms\. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit\. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt together without a central coordinating agent\. We evaluate MPT on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research\. Results show gains over monolithic post\-training and confirm that agent participation indeed evolves with learning\. With the same post\-trained action policies, learned self\-orchestration outperforms alternative coordination strategies\. Ablations show that both action and bidding benefit from learning, and that learned bids provide more effective action\-training signals\. Beyond the original training objectives, trained swarms adapt faster to related tasks and achieve better performance with larger populations at inference time\. Larger populations also suffer smaller performance losses under agent dropout, demonstrating that learned self\-orchestration supports reuse, scaling, and robustness in decentralized agent swarms\. Code and trained models are available at https://github\.com/Embodied\-Minds\-Lab/MPT\.

## [XAI\-SFD: an explainable artificial intelligence framework for intelligent digitalisation of shit flow diagrams and smart sanitation management in South Africa](../publications/4205ae4628f05c22a54f.md)

Rotimi\-Williams Bello; Roseline Oluwaseun Ogundokun; Pius Adewale Owolawi; Ratunku Gabriel Lekalakala; Lizzy Mpenyana\-Monyatsi; Brilliant Mareme Petja; Etienne Van Wyk

Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real\-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain\. Shit Flow Diagrams \(SFDs\) are among the tools that can be used for the presentation and analysis of the sanitation service chain as well as identification of potential risks in the sanitation systems; however, the creation of traditional SFDs is a manual process and leaves no space for continuous monitoring\. This paper proposes XAI\-SFD, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\)\-based solution for the intelligent digitalization of Shit Flow Diagrams \(SFDs\) and smart sanitation management in South Africa\. This approach is based on IoT data gathering, GIS\-based spatial analysis, data validation, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, sanitation service chain modelling, Digital Twin technology and dashboard decision\-making support\. Explainability provides transparency and allows the stakeholders to understand what influences the risk assessment and prioritization\. A proof\-of\-concept was carried out on a controlled municipality scale, using 247 monitoring stations of the Routine Inland Water Quality Monitoring network of the City of Cape Town\. A total of four clusters of spatial contexts were identified, with the selected clustering model providing a silhouette coefficient of 0\.3133 and Davies\-Bouldin index of 1\.3324\. As a result of the explained priority assessment, 25 monitoring stations \(10\.12%\) have been defined as belonging to the high\-priority class, 99 stations \(40\.08%\) belonging to the medium\-priority class, and 123 stations \(49\.80%\) belonging to the low\-priority class\. Because of the lack of sanitation flows outcomes and water quality monitoring results in the dataset on monitoring sites, it is possible to consider the results received as prototyping findings and not as the validation of sanitation risk prediction models\. In this regard, the proposed XAI\-SFD architecture may be used as the base for further creation of heterogeneous databases of sanitation and environmental data\.

## [Diet contributes to microbiome and niche differentiation among three sympatric cervids](../publications/421bc1ce34beee1521a0.md)

Yuxiang Liang; Wentao Zhang; Feifei Yang; Yilin Zhang; Ruitao Wei; Chenbing Chu; Jiale Sun; Heng Bao; Weiping Li

Background Niche differentiation is a fundamental mechanism facilitating the coexistence of sympatric species, yet the extent to which dietary partitioning is associated with gut microbial differentiation remains poorly understood in wild cervids\. Methods Here, we investigated winter dietary composition and fecal microbiome communities of three sympatric cervid species—moose \( Alces alces \), red deer \( Cervus elaphus \), and roe deer \( Capreolus pygargus \)—in Youhao National Nature Reserve, northeastern China\. A total of 55 fresh fecal samples were collected in January 2024, including 19 moose, 7 red deer, and 29 roe deer samples\. Dietary composition was characterized using rbcL DNA metabarcoding, while microbiome communities were assessed using full\-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing\. Results Our results showed the three cervid species exhibited distinct dietary patterns, moose showed a relatively narrow woody\-plant\-dominated diet, whereas red deer and roe deer exhibited higher dietary diversity, and roe deer exhibited broader use of shared plant resources; microbiome communities also differed significantly among host species, with moose showing the clearest separation from red deer and roe deer in community composition and predicted microbial metabolic potentials; Procrustes analysis revealed significant concordance between dietary composition and microbiome community, and redundancy analysis also indicated that dietary plant composition explained a significant proportion of variation in microbiome community\. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that trophic differentiation among sympatric cervids is accompanied by coordinated variation in gut microbial community structure and predicted functional potential\. The results support a close ecological association between dietary niche differentiation and host\-associated microbiome variation, while causal and directional mechanisms require confirmation through longitudinal, experimental, and direct functional studies\.

## [A Cross‐Modal Gated Fusion Network Synergizing Physical Priors and Deep Learning for Robust Bearing Fault Diagnosis](../publications/422afed440cfbf0ba507.md)

Yitong Liu; Xintian Liu; Zhiguo Zhang; Lixia Ma; Guoqiang Wang

ABSTRACT Reliable fault diagnosis in rotating machinery is often hindered by poor cross‐individual generalization and the inherent black‐box nature of data‐driven models\. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a hybrid diagnostic framework that synergizes explicit physical priors with deep spatiotemporal representations\. The proposed architecture employs a dual‐stream strategy, integrating a residual multi‐scale CNN‐BiLSTM branch with an expert knowledge feature stream through a cross‐modal gated fusion mechanism\. Unlike conventional concatenation, this gated module adaptively modulates the contribution of each feature stream, effectively resolving semantic inconsistencies between data‐driven and physics‐informed modalities\. Comprehensive evaluations on a rigorous cross‐individual bearing fault benchmark demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing deep learning models\. Further ablation studies and manifold visualizations confirm that the integration of physical priors enhances feature discriminability and model robustness\. Moreover, an analysis of the gated coefficients reveals that the model dynamically adjusts its reliance on different feature streams in alignment with the bearing degradation process, thereby providing enhanced interpretability and clear evidence of its diagnostic superiority\.

## [Prune the Leaky Neurons: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in Fine\-Tuned LLMs via Joint\-Embedding\-Guided Pruning](../publications/4247521785f3111f911e.md)

Mohamed Shaaban; Mohamed Elmahallawy

Fine\-tuning large language models \(LLMs\) on proprietary records enables domain adaptation but introduces two challenges: \(i\) privacy leakage of memorized private data, such as personally identifiable information \(PII\), and \(ii\) balancing private data removal with utility preservation\. Existing defenses, including data sanitization and differential privacy, often degrade performance, while privacy\-neuron editing lacks a PII\-free reference to distinguish identity\-specific neurons from those supporting useful text\. We propose JEPA\-Prune, a post\-hoc neuron pruning framework guided by a model trained exclusively on PII\-free views\. Alongside the fine\-tuned private model, JEPA\-Prune, trains a public model on surrogate and masked views of the same records using a joint\-embedding predictive architecture \(JEPA\), capturing domain knowledge without identifiers\. A cross\-model representation probe quantifies deviations between private representations of leaked records and this PII\-free reference\. Integrated gradients and a scale\-invariant specificity score then identify PII\-responsive neurons, which are pruned without retraining\. Experiments show that pruning just 1\.6% of neurons reduces PII inference accuracy by up to 7\.4x and PII extraction recall by up to 13\.9x, while keeping unseen\-text perplexity within 16% of that of the unpruned model for most LLMs\. In contrast, privacy\-neuron editing increases perplexity by at least 26x\.

## [Recent Advances in Cushioning Materials for Postharvest Application: Material Sources, Fabrication Techniques, and Mitigation of Mechanical Damage](../publications/424f6c4999646c09493d.md)

Nanfeng Tan; Zhenbiao Li; Wenmin Zhang; Weiting Yang; Zhaoyun Ma; Ye Song; Zisheng Luo; Yanqun Xu

Mechanical damage caused by vibration, impact, and compression during postharvest handling, transportation, and distribution is one of the main factors leading to losses and quality deterioration of fruits and vegetables\. Cushioning packaging has therefore become an effective strategy for mitigating mechanical damage and maintaining produce quality\. However, most conventional cushioning materials are petroleum\-based plastics\. With increasing environmental pollution and growing demands for sustainable development, the development of renewable and potentially lower\-impact cushioning packaging materials has become an important research focus\. This review provides an overview of recent advances in cushioning materials for fruit and vegetable transportation\. The physiological and biochemical changes and associated quality deterioration of fruits and vegetables under mechanical stress are analyzed, including bruising, firmness loss, water loss, metabolic disturbance, changes in bioactive compounds, and decay development\. The effectiveness of different cushioning systems in mitigating mechanical damage and maintaining postharvest quality is also discussed\. The major raw materials used in cushioning packaging are classified according to their plant\-based, animal\-based, synthetic, and inorganic origins, and their functional properties and roles within material systems are summarized\. In addition, the main fabrication methods are compared in terms of structure formation, mechanical performance, advantages, limitations, processing requirements, and industrial feasibility\. Current challenges related to production cost, scalability, humidity sensitivity, food\-contact safety, recyclability, regulatory requirements, and life cycle sustainability are further considered\. This review provides a theoretical basis and practical reference for the future development and customized design of cushioning packaging materials with improved performance\.

## [Trust in complex task environments: results of an agent\-based simulation on incomplete contracts](../publications/4254f2d55c2029aa1fb7.md)

Friederike Wall

Purpose Incentive contracts often do not govern all task elements for which a subordinate is responsible\. In these situations, trust among the contracting parties is crucial for the effort the subordinate exerts on non\-contracted task elements\. This paper aims to examine the emergence of trust and its performance effects, accounting for the complexity of the task environment and the different cognitive bases of trust\. Design/methodology/approach The paper employs an agent\-based simulation following the framework of NK fitness landscapes and builds on the integrated model of leader\-member exchange of Brower et al\. \(2000\)\. In the simulation model, artificial organizations search for superior organizational performance where decision\-makers&\#x27; contracts are incomplete, i\.e\. not governing all task elements contributing to organizational performance\. In the simulation experiments, the complexity of the task environment and the cognitive bases of trust\-building, especially on the superior&\#x27;s side, are varied\. Findings The simulation results suggest that the complexity of task environments plays a twofold role in trust\-building and its performance effects: first, as complexity increases, dynamics arising from interrelated feedback loops affect trust among contracting parties; and second, this, in turn, reinforces frequent intra\-organizational adjustments\. These effects are moderated by the cognitive bases of trust\-building\. Consequently, in highly complex task environments, higher trust among parties does not universally improve organizational performance\. Originality/value The paper contributes to the literature by analyzing the interplay between the complexity of an organization&\#x27;s task environment and the dynamics of reciprocal trust that unfold in pursuit of superior organizational performance\. Moreover, by using agent\-based simulation, the paper showcases how computational methods can further advance trust research in organizational contexts\.

## [Design and Implementation of a Unique Elements Finder Using Python Sets](../publications/42561069288ccc3322fe.md)

Lily Roslin

Unique Elements Finder project is a simple but interesting python project\. This project is useful to learn the implementation of set for the purpose of finding unique integers from a list\. This is done through the Unique Elements Finder project\. In both the field of data analysis and the field of programming, the use of duplicate values often results in redundancy and inefficiency\. This project is the solution to the problem identified by using the built\-in set data structure in python which automatically removes duplicates and only stores the elements which are unique to the set\. This program accepts a list of numbers as input and then converts the list to a set to get the unique numbers in an efficient and concise way\. Unlike manual methods this methodology minimises the amount of computational complexity that is involved and ensures processing is finished in a short amount of time even when dealing with extremely large datasets\. In the fields of data management, analytics and software development, the project shows how elementary concepts such as sets can be used to produce results that are realistic and applicable to the real world\. On top of this, it emphasises the importance of having a deep knowledge of Python’s data structures to be able to solve problems quicker and better\.

## [Forward\-Looking Financial Reporting Risk Screening in Saudi Listed Firms: Evidence from the Beneish M\-Score and Explainable Machine Learning](../publications/42652687955d9f854b06.md)

Ibrahim Sweiti

Most applications of the Beneish M\-Score are contemporaneous: they screen financial statements after a reporting year has ended\. This study asks whether the eight Beneish indicators measured in year t contain information about the following year&\#x27;s Beneish screening classification\. The analysis uses a balanced panel of 66 Saudi listed non\-financial firms from 2018 to 2025, yielding 528 annual financial statements and 462 M\-Score observations for 2019\-2025\. Under the primary M &gt; \-1\.78 rule, 66 of 462 firm\-years \(14\.3%\) generate a screening signal\. On the untouched 2025 holdout, logistic regression achieves ROC\-AUC = 0\.718 and average precision = 0\.371, while Random Forest achieves ROC\-AUC = 0\.684 and average precision = 0\.406 and produces the higher precision and F1 at the pre\-specified 0\.50 decision\-score threshold\. A rolling\-origin stability analysis across 2021\-2025 uses the continuous current\-year M\-Score as the benchmark: pooled ROC\-AUC is 0\.537 for M\_t, 0\.661 for logistic regression, and 0\.653 for Random Forest\. Firm\-cluster bootstrap inference indicates that both fitted models improve discrimination relative to M\_t, whereas their difference is not statistically distinguishable\. Unweighted refits produce similar ranking performance\. SHAP identifies TATA as the leading Random Forest feature, followed by DEPI, AQI, and DSRI\. The evidence supports explainable machine learning as a complementary prioritization tool rather than a calibrated fraud probability or a substitute for professional review\.

## [Evaluation of Local Language Models in a RAG System for Educational Assistance](../publications/427dc87ddc872aba9ce0.md)

Dami´an Barsotti; Luis Biedma; Manuel Diaz Ferreiro; Mariano Lescano; Nahuel Seiler

Este trabajo presenta el desarrollo colaborativo entre la Facultad de Matemática, Astronomía, Física y Computación \(FAMAF\) de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba y la empresa Procer Tecnologías S\.A\.S\. para construir un sistema de Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) de asistencia educativa\. El sistema está diseñado para ejecutarse en una computadora local a la que se conecta un dispositivo portátil de asistencia diseñado por la empresa, reemplazando el sistema RAG que tiene actualmente desplegado en la nube\. Su objetivo es mejorar el acceso autónomo a contenidos escolares para estudiantes con discapacidad visual, dislexia u otras barreras de aprendizaje\. La arquitectura implementada combina almacenamiento vectorial, búsqueda híbrida, proceso de reranking y generación de respuestas con modelos de lenguaje ejecutados localmente vía Ollama\. Se evaluaron 10 modelos reducidos utilizando un dataset de 396 pares pregunta respuesta en español, construido a partir de documentos y usuarios reales del servicio en la nube de la empresa\. Los resultados muestran que la búsqueda híbrida con reranking mejora consistentemente a la búsqueda vectorial pura en las cinco métricas y en todos los modelos evaluados\. Notablemente, los modelos evaluados son de tamaño reducido pudiéndose ejecutar en GPUs de uso hogareño, y aun así obtienen métricas competitivas tomando como referencia las respuestas del sistema que la empresa tiene actualmente\.

## [Niches in cancer: from primary tumors to metastatic disease](../publications/4285103b6ba1e6e90dba.md)

Zheng Chao; Xiaojing Wang; Zhihua Wang; Kongming Wu; Le Li

Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant\-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches\. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant\-cell behavior\. These local environments sustain stem\-like states, regulate immune surveillance and vascular remodeling, and influence dissemination and treatment response\. Tumor\-derived extracellular vesicles and other systemic signals connect primary tumors to distant organs, conditioning tissues before tumor\-cell arrival and subsequently modulating disseminated tumor\-cell seeding, dormancy, reactivation and outgrowth\. Cancer niches therefore operate across spatial scales and disease stages, shaping tumor behavior in ways that cannot be explained by tumor\-cell\-intrinsic properties alone\. Advances in single\-cell and spatial profiling, organoid systems and intravital imaging are revealing their cellular composition, local architecture and evolution\. In this review, we integrate primary, pre\-metastatic and metastatic niche biology, examine how local environments evolve and influence one another during cancer progression, compare organ\-specific metastatic niches and assess emerging therapeutic strategies\. Effective niche\-directed therapy will require identifying the interactions that sustain disease, showing that treatment disrupts them and determining which patients are most likely to benefit\. Greater spatial, temporal and functional resolution may reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities and create opportunities to prevent relapse and achieve more durable disease control\.

## [Predicting Mammal Species Suitable for Chagas Disease Spread Using a Machine‐Learning Framework](../publications/429258241d972aa17869.md)

Maya Rocha‐Ortega; Carezza Botto‐Mahan; Gemma Rojo; Alex Córdoba‐Aguilar

Understanding which mammalian species participate in the sylvatic cycle of Trypanosoma cruzi is vital for clarifying the ecological processes that maintain Chagas disease transmission\. Although more than 100 mammal species have been reported as naturally infected, the actual diversity of hosts is much broader\. In this study, we employed a trait\-based, machine\-learning framework to evaluate mammals associated with natural infection\. Data concerning life\-history traits, morphological characteristics, environmental factors, trophic ecology, habitat use, biogeographic distributions, and spatial overlap with triatomine vectors were compiled to model compatibility with T\. cruzi infection using extreme gradient\-boosted regression\. Our analysis indicates that triatomines overlap with 573 mammal species\. While triatomines are considered generalists, they also utilize mammal species with specific traits, such as den\-dwelling behavior, medium to large body size, and tolerance to habitat disturbance\. This approach offers a structured foundation for identifying potential host species and prioritizing field research in regions that are insufficiently studied\. By integrating ecological traits with geographic and behavioral data, the model enhances the understanding of host\-parasite interactions in sylvatic Chagas disease and supports targeted surveillance of predicted mammalian hosts\.

## [“Quality by Design Approaches in Intranasal Drug Delivery Systems: Current Progress, Challenges and Future Perspectives”](../publications/429c0907f11a365b6ca2.md)



Intranasal drug delivery has emerged as a highly promising administration route owing to its unique anatomical advantages rich vascularization, large mucosal surface area \(\~150\-180 cm²\), and direct olfactory/trigeminal access to the central nervous system \(CNS\) bypassing the blood\-brain barrier \(BBB\)\.Despite these advantages, mucociliary clearance, limited nasal volume \(\~20 mL per nostril\), enzymatic barriers, and inter\-individual physiological variability complicate reproducible formulation development\.Quality by Design \(QbD\), a science\-and risk\-based pharmaceutical development framework endorsed by ICH Q8, Q9, and Q10, provides a structured, systematic approach to address these challenges\.This review comprehensively examines QbD applications across intranasal dosage forms including nasal solutions, sprays, powders, mucoadhesive systems, thermosensitive in situ gels, nanoemulsions, polymeric nanoparticles, and lipid nanoparticles \(SLN/NLC\)\.Key QbD elements\-Quality Target Product Profile \(QTPP\), Critical Quality Attributes \(CQAs\), Critical Material Attributes \(CMAs\), Critical Process Parameters \(CPPs\), Design Space, and Control Strategyare systematically discussed\.Risk assessment tools \(Ishikawa diagrams, FMEA, Pareto analysis\) and Design of Experiments \(DoE\) strategies including Plackett\-Burman, Box\-Behnken, and Central Composite Designs with Response Surface Methodology are elaborated\.Special emphasis is given to nose\-to\-brain delivery for CNS disorders \(Alzheimer&\#x27;s, Parkinson&\#x27;s, epilepsy, migraine\) with supporting case studies\.Regulatory expectations \(FDA, EMA\) and emerging trends including AI\-assisted development, digital twins, continuous manufacturing, and personalized medicine are also addressed\.QbD is confirmed as essential to ensure strong, consistent, and compliant intranasal drug products\.

## [Deformation‐Tolerant Functional Elastomer Overlayers for Haze‐Assisted Light Extraction and Color Conversion in Stretchable Mechanoluminescent Films](../publications/42a16bdc9835ac0ae9ed.md)

Gi\-Hong Jeon; Seongkyu Song; Soon Moon Jeong; Na Young Ha

ABSTRACT Mechanoluminescence \(ML\), which converts mechanical stimuli into light without an external power supply, offers opportunities for self‐powered optical sensing, wearable displays, soft robotics, and adaptive light‐emitting systems\. ZnS:Cu particles embedded in a poly\(dimethylsiloxane\) matrix \(ZnS:Cu‐PDMS\) represent an attractive stretchable ML platform because they generate strong emission under mechanical deformation\. However, most strategies for improving ML performance rely on modifying the emissive composite itself, limiting independent control over postemission photon extraction and spectral conversion\. Here, a modular functional elastomer overlayer strategy is presented to decouple ML generation from photon extraction and color conversion in ZnS:Cu‐PDMS composite films\. Polyurethane \(PU\), nematic liquid crystal \(NLC\)‐loaded PU \(NLC‐PU\), 4‐\(dicyanomethylene\)‐2‐methyl‐6‐\(p‐dimethylaminostyryl\)‐4H‐pyran \(DCM\)‐doped PU, and DCM‐ and NLC‐loaded PU \(DCM‐NLC‐PU\) overlayers are integrated as independently tunable optical layers\. NLC‐PU forms birefringent NLC‐rich domains that provide visible‐range haze, strain‐responsive optical anisotropy, and broadband, nonresonant photon redistribution\. When applied to ZnS:Cu‐PDMS films, NLC‐PU enhances outwardly collected green ML while preserving the intrinsic emission spectrum\. DCM‐containing overlayers enable green‐to‐yellow‐orange color conversion, while DCM‐NLC‐PU combines spectral conversion with scattering‐assisted outward emission enhancement\. This overlayer architecture provides a deformation‐tolerant route for controlling brightness and color in stretchable ML platforms\.

## [Attention\-integrated hybrid CNN–vision transformer framework for robust multi\-class cervical cytology classification using liquid\-based cytology images](../publications/42a9ba516fe398ccfb26.md)

A\. Sathiya; R\. Madonna Arieth; C\. M\. Nalayini; V\. Balaji

The grading of cervical cytology images is a challenging task because some morphological changes are subtle, there are class imbalances and variability in staining of lesion grades\. In order to overcome such difficulties, this work suggests MAH\-CerviT, a Multi\-Scale Attention\-Guided Hybrid Cervical Transformer framework that combines dense hierarchical convolutional learning and window\-based contextual modeling\. In contrast to the traditional convolutional networks that mainly learn the local texture patterns, or the transformer\-based networks that only focus on the global attention mechanism to improve the model, MAH\-CerviT is a synergistic network with three major components: \(i\) a multi\-scale dense convolutional backbone to learn the hierarchical morphological feature aggregation, \(ii\) a sequential channel\-spatial attention refinement module to selectively enhance the diagnostically relevant cellular regions, and \(iii\) a Swin Transformer encoder to model structured contextual dependency\. The hybrid fusion approach allows to discriminate between morphologically similar classes like HSIL and LSIL in a balanced manner and keep the computational efficiency\. Massive experiments in 5\-fold stratified cross\-validation show that MAH\-CerviT has a total accuracy of 95\.92, macro F 1\-score of 95\.52 and macro\-AUC of 96\.40, significantly higher than DenseNet\-121, EfficientNet\-B4, ViT\-Base, and Swin Transformer baselines\. It is statistically proved that the increase in comparison to the strongest baseline is significant \(p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Ablation experiments demonstrate that multi\-scale aggregation, attention refinement and contextual encoding have a cumulative beneficial effect on the performance of the baseline convolutional model, which justifies the complementary role of each\. The robustness analysis also shows that the performance remains stable even when there are image corruptions and less data\. The suggested MAH\-CerviT framework provides an efficient trade\-off between the accuracy of the discrimination system and the computational efficiency, and it is a reliable and scalable tool to solve the automated cervical cancer screening application\.

## [Seasonal analysis of soil microbial diversity following the application of different fertilisation types](../publications/42b34a2aa54c1b827cfb.md)

Sergeja Lešnik

V letih 2024 in 2025 je bil na Fakulteti za kmetijstvo in biosistemske vede Univerze v Mariboru izveden poskus za oceno vpliva različnih načinov gnojenja na mikrobiološko aktivnost tal\. Namen raziskave je bil ugotoviti odziv izbranih mikrobnih skupin \(skupno število mikroorganizmov, aktinomicete, plesni in kvasovke\) na različna gnojila \(Tanagra G1500 in G500, Kalcevita ApM1500 in ApM500 ter NPK\) ter oceniti vpliv sezonskih nihanj\. Rezultati so pokazali, da se številčnost mikrobnih skupin razlikuje glede na vrsto gnojila in sezono\. Najizrazitejše razlike so bile ugotovljene poleti in jeseni pri vseh gnojilnih obravnavanjih, kar kaže na izrazit sezonski odziv tal po gnojenju\. Največje sezonske razlike v skupnem številu mikroorganizmov in aktinomicet so bile opažene po uporabi gnojila NPK\. Dodatek gnojila Kalcevita ApM1500 je povzročil statistično značilno povečanje vseh spremljanih mikrobnih skupin, posebej plesni in kvasovk, medtem ko je bil vpliv na aktinomicete izrazitejši pri gnojilu Tanagra G500\. Znotraj posameznih sezon statistično značilnih razlik med gnojilnimi obravnavanji ni bilo, čeprav so bili opaženi določeni trendi\. Jeseni je po gnojenju s Tanagro G1500 izstopalo skupno število mikroorganizmov in aktinomicet, poleti pa je bilo največ mikroorganizmov pri gnojenju z NPK, največ aktinomicet pri Tanagri G1500 ter največ plesni in kvasovk pri Kalceviti ApM1500\. Rezultati potrjujejo, da gnojenje pomembno vpliva na mikrobno dinamiko tal, pri čemer se odziv razlikuje med posameznimi skupinami mikroorganizmov\.

## [Free Nutritious Meal Program Implementation and Reported Learning Focus: A Qualitative Case Study in Bandung](../publications/42bc105b052a972c2be5.md)

Annisa Salsabila; Yulianah Yulianah; Dzikri Syahrul Syiam; Gathan Dwiyan Zonagi; Tebia Aditya Muharam

Purpose— This study examines how meal delivery, reported food\-consumption practices, and perceived classroom attention intersect in elementary schools implementing Indonesia&\#x27;s Free Nutritious Meal \(MBG\) Program\. Research Methodology— The original study describes a qualitative case study in Batununggal District, Bandung, using interviews with students, teachers, and program administrators, classroom and meal observations, and document review\. Results— The study account describes more regular school meals, acceptance of varied menus, and communal eating experiences\. It also reports teachers&\#x27; perceptions of fewer hunger\-related interruptions and more sustained classroom engagement\. Meal timing and menu appeal emerge as operational themes\. Research limitations/Implications— The interpretive design and the absence of independent attention measures preclude causal claims\. The documentation of participant selection, fieldwork, and thematic inference also requires verification\. School\-level monitoring should attend to delivery schedules and meal acceptability\. Originality— The paper relates local school\-meal implementation practices to reported learning experiences within a public\-service delivery context\.

## [Causal‐Aware Dynamic Knowledge Graph for Wind Turbine Fault Diagnosis: Integrating Domain Knowledge With SCADA Data](../publications/42d7ce275142be6f2b7d.md)

Yu Sun; Zhimin Cheng; Tianxiang Zhao; Zizhao Zhang; Zhuang Kang

ABSTRACT This paper proposes a Causal‐Aware Dynamic Knowledge Graph \(CA‐DKG\) framework that systematically fuses FMEA domain knowledge with data‐driven causal discovery from SCADA time series\. We first develop a heterogeneous knowledge graph construction method that unifies structured FMEA failure triples with sensor monitoring relationships, providing a unified representation framework for cross‐source fault information covering components, failure modes, root causes and operational variables\. A multi‐stage causal discovery pipeline is further designed, integrating the PCMCI algorithm, expert physical rule audit and VCDF multi‐window stability verification, which effectively filters spurious correlations and extracts high‐confidence directed causal edges from SCADA time series\. On this basis, a relational graph attention network embedded with EvolveGCN temporal modeling is constructed to learn dynamic graph representations, enabling interpretable causal link prediction and fault propagation reasoning instead of opaque black‐box fault detection\. Validated on 161 days of SCADA data from a 5 MW offshore wind turbine with 23 sensor variables including physics‐based thermal residuals, CA‐DKG achieves 0\.88 AUC and 0\.61 F1‐score for causal edge prediction, outperforming the topology‐based PageRank baseline by 20% in AUC, while VCDF retains 66\.7% of stable causal edges\. This work provides an explainable knowledge‐data integrated framework for wind turbine intelligent fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance, supporting trustworthy causal reasoning for maintenance decisions\.

## [Vocational self\-stigma and problematic smartphone use: self\-regulatory fatigue as an indirect pathway and professional identity as a second\-stage moderator](../publications/42f33fde0aaa75f90856.md)

Yong Chen; Xiaoxian Zheng; Yingping Yan

Problematic smartphone use is common among young people, and research on its antecedents has focused mainly on individual dispositions and transient emotional states\. Less is known about whether self\-stigma, a chronic and group\-based devaluation of the self, is linked to problematic smartphone use through self\-regulatory fatigue, and whether professional identity weakens that link\. We examined these questions in a cross\-sectional survey of 1,352 students at Chinese higher vocational colleges, whose educational track carries a persistent status penalty\. Vocational self\-stigma was associated with greater self\-regulatory fatigue, which in turn was associated with more problematic smartphone use \[indirect effect = 0\.127, 95% CI \(0\.099, 0\.157\)\]\. This indirect association was larger when measurement error was modeled, remained significant across alternative scale compositions, covariate sets, and analytic samples, and was smaller but still significant when differences between cities of response were held constant\. Professional identity moderated the second stage of the pathway: the association between fatigue and problematic use weakened as professional identity increased \[ B = −0\.142, 95% CI \(−0\.228, −0\.053\)\] but remained significant for nearly all students, including those with a strong professional identity\. The corresponding first\-stage interaction was close to zero \[ B = −0\.008, 95% CI \(−0\.068, 0\.053\)\]\. Items reflecting awareness of public devaluation and items reflecting self\-devaluation showed similar indirect associations\. The findings are consistent with a view of vocational self\-stigma as a source of regulatory strain and suggest that professional identity is related to how students act under that strain more than to how closely self\-stigma is tied to it\. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to establish the temporal order of these associations\.

## [Structural Evolution of the International Migration Network \(1990 – 2024\)](../publications/42f97907a44d010b0e1e.md)

Alejandro Blasco; Marco Canero; Evangelina Iodice; Juan Manuel Rodríguez Miguel; Viktoriya Semeshenko; Carlos Sarraute

Las migraciones internacionales configuran una red compleja de relaciones entre países que evoluciona a lo largo del tiempo\. En este trabajo analizamos la estructura y evolución del sistema migratorio mundial entre 1990 y 2024 modelando los stocks del dataset UN International Migrant Stock como un grafo dirigido y ponderado, donde los nodos son países y las aristas representan volúmenes de migrantes entre pares origen\-destino\. Mediante herramientas de ciencia de redes caracterizamos propiedades topológicas globales, estructura comunitaria y centralidad, y contrastamos cuatro hipótesis sobre los determinantes de la migración: proximidad geográfica, afinidad cultural y lingüística, asimetría económica y crisis forzadas\. Los resultados revelan un sistema que se globaliza progresivamente: las comunidades regionales persisten pero pierden cohesión, los corredores migratorios atraviesan cada vez más fronteras tradicionales y la proximidad geográfica pierde peso relativo como determinante principal\. La unidad lingüística emerge, en cambio, como el factor cultural más estable y consistente a lo largo de todo el período\. Las migraciones forzadas constituyen la excepción estructural más marcada: ante crisis políticas o humanitarias, la geografía recupera su rol y concentra desplazamientos masivos en países vecinos con independencia de otros factores\. En conjunto, estos hallazgos caracterizan un sistema migratorio global heterogéneo, jerárquico y en transformación, cuya dinámica responde a una combinación de fuerzas estructurales de largo plazo e impactos abruptos de corto plazo\.

## [Beyond Automation: Towards Human\-Centered Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management](../publications/42fd15ed29f97dfff359.md)

Prof Ketaki Kukde Ashwini Gajanan Dongarkar

The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is transforming Human Resource Management \(HRM\) across the employee lifecycle, including recruitment, selection, learning and development, performance management, employee engagement, workforce planning, and talent retention\. Existing discussions frequently emphasize the capacity of AI to automate repetitive activities, improve efficiency, process large volumes of data, and support predictive decision\-making\. However, the increasing use of algorithmic systems in decisions affecting employees also raises fundamental concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, accountability, employee trust, and the potential erosion of human interaction within organizations\. This creates an important paradox: technologies introduced to improve HR efficiency may either strengthen or weaken the humancentered nature of HRM\. This study examines the question: Can Artificial Intelligence make Human Resource Management more human? The paper adopts an analytical and conceptual research approach based on existing academic literature, institutional publications, and contemporary evidence concerning AI and the future of work\. Rather than viewing AI as either a replacement for HR professionals or merely an efficiency\-enhancing technology, the study investigates the conditions under which AI can support meaningful human–technology collaboration \.The analysis proposes the Human\-Centered AI Trust Framework, which argues that the effectiveness of AI\-powered HR depends on the interaction between technological capability and five critical governance dimensions: transparency, fairness, privacy, human oversight, and employee trust\. The study argues that AI does not inherently humanize or dehumanize HR\. Automation can free HR professionals from repetitive administrative activities and create greater capacity for employee interaction, empathy, relationship management, and strategic work\. Conversely, poorly governed AI can increase surveillance, reduce trust, reproduce bias, and create impersonal workplaces\. The paper concludes that the future of HR should not be understood as a competition between Artificial Intelligence and Human Intelligence\. Instead, sustainable HR transformation requires AI systems to be governed by human judgment, ethical responsibility, and employee\-centered values\. The most successful organizations may therefore be those that use AI not to remove humans from HR, but to enable humans to perform the aspects of HR that require them to be most human\.

## [Inteligencia artificial en ortodoncia, endodoncia e implantología: revisión sistemática](../publications/42fedf011602604f9fef.md)

Linda Brizeida Ruiz\-Sanchez; Sleyter Andrés Villegas\-Avila

Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre las aplicaciones y el rendimiento de la inteligencia artificial en ortodoncia, endodoncia e implantología\. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO \(2012\-2025\); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas con metaanálisis, revisiones de alcance, revisiones críticas y estudios de desarrollo de algoritmos\. Resultados: en ortodoncia, el aprendizaje profundo localizó puntos cefalométricos con precisión elevada y se aplicó a la decisión de extracciones y a la segmentación tomográfica\. En endodoncia, detectó lesiones periapicales en radiografías y tomografías con alta sensibilidad\. En implantología, la evidencia identificada fue escasa\. Conclusión: la inteligencia artificial es una herramienta prometedora de apoyo al diagnóstico, pero requiere validación clínica externa, estándares de publicación y supervisión profesional\.

## [PCOS discussions on a Turkish online forum: a qualitative netnographic study of concerns, peer advice, and information gaps](../publications/431ad9afc8eeb2f71956.md)

Ömercan Aksoy

Introduction Polycystic ovary syndrome \(PCOS\) is a multidimensional endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive condition, yet little is known about how related concerns and peer advice unfold within Turkish online forums\. This study examined initial concerns and associated peer\-response patterns in a publicly accessible Turkish forum\. Methods A qualitative netnographic study was conducted using 120 initial posts and 708 peer responses published between August 2025 and May 2026\. Initial posts were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and assigned one dominant theme for descriptive frequency analysis\. Peer responses were categorized by their dominant communicative function using qualitative content analysis\. Results Fertility, pregnancy, and motherhood anxiety was the most frequent initial concern \( n = 24, 20\.0%\), followed by treatment and medication\-related uncertainty \( n = 22, 18\.3%\)\. Among peer responses, incomplete or uncertain advice predominated \( n = 398, 56\.2%\), followed by biomedical guidance or normalization \( n = 137, 19\.4%\), practical navigation \( n = 50, 7\.1%\), and experiential advice \( n = 47, 6\.6%\)\. Cross\-tabulation demonstrated that incomplete or uncertain advice predominated across most initial concern categories\. Discussion Turkish PCOS forum discussions represent a mixed peer\-information environment in which reassurance, experiential knowledge, practical guidance, incomplete advice, non\-evidence\-based recommendations, and stigmatizing interactions coexist\. Healthcare professionals should address patients&\#x27; online information\-seeking and provide clear, person\-centered guidance on diagnosis, treatment, fertility, visible symptoms, and healthcare pathways\.

## [Amplitude source location for volcanic earthquakes using source location\-dependent amplification corrections: Application to Izu Oshima volcano, Japan](../publications/432ad636dd1862f702a7.md)

Novia Antika Anggraeni; Takeshi Nishimura; Hisashi Nakahara

Summary The amplitude source location \(ASL\) method has been widely applied to volcanic earthquakes that do not show clear wave onsets at active volcanoes\. To reduce the effects of shallow velocity structures just beneath seismic stations, observed amplitudes are generally corrected by using seismic coda waves of regional earthquakes\. However, even using such amplitude corrections, ASL may not accurately locate the source of volcanic earthquakes occurring in a strongly heterogeneous medium in volcanic regions\. To overcome this limitation, we propose a source location\-dependent amplitude correction method and introduce seismic velocity structure with a vertical gradient\. We analyze 339 volcano\-tectonic earthquakes \(VTs\) recorded by eight seismic stations deployed across the Izu Oshima volcano edifice\. Reference hypocenters are determined from manually picked P\- and S\-wave arrival times and used to evaluate the performance of the proposed amplitude\-based method\. We divide the VT dataset into two subsets, which are used as reference and test datasets\. The amplification factors, which are the ratio of observed to predicted amplitudes of known VTs, are calculated for the reference dataset\. The amplification factors are further interpolated onto a two\-dimensional grid using the ordinary kriging method with an exponential variogram model and then replicated at each depth level of the three\-dimensional grid\. Using interpolated source\-location dependent amplification factors \(SLAF\), we correct the observed amplitudes of VTs in the test dataset and estimate the source locations by minimizing the amplitude residual in a grid search scheme\. We use the 8\-16 Hz frequency band, a velocity gradient k of 0\.33 s−1 and v0 1\.5 km s−1, and a constant attenuation factor \(Q\) of 50\. The obtained source locations show good agreement with the locations determined from P\- and S\-wave onsets\. Median misfits are approximately 1\.1 km and 1\.0 km in the vertical and horizontal directions, respectively\. Meanwhile, the median misfits from conventional ASL are approximately 2\.2 km and 2\.3 km in the vertical and horizontal directions, respectively, with the estimated location concentrated close to the summit\. These results demonstrate that our proposed method substantially improves relocation consistency and reduces summit\-ward bias\.

## [Progress in NK cell\-based immunotherapy for solid tumors and an exploration of its cardiovascular safety](../publications/432d8a315be663486f52.md)

Jiaxin Chen; Juntong Shen; Xiaolin Fu; Min Jiang; Ruihao Liu; Qiang Qiao; Yizhe Hu

Natural killer \(NK\) cell\-based immunotherapy has become a research focus in cellular immunotherapy in recent years,which has advanced rapidly in the treatment of solid tumors\. NK cells are key effector cells of innate immunity and can kill abnormal target cells without prior sensitization\. A broad consensus holds that NK cell\-based immunotherapy may become a new strategy for solid tumor treatment with lower risk and lower cost than T\-cell\-based immunotherapy\. However, its translation from theory to clinical application remains constrained by relevant risks, and research on its cardiovascular safety is still largely absent\. This review summarizes the latest research progress of NK cell\-based immunotherapy in solid tumors and discusses its cardiovascular safety\.
