## [Lipid Nanoparticles for Drug and Gene Delivery: Advances, Limitations and Future Perspectives](../publications/432f2abc1387264e2a3e.md)

Gayathri A; Nafeesathul Misriyya; Ambadi Switha M S

Lipid nanoparticles \(LNPs\) have emerged as one of the most promising nanocarrier systems for the delivery of therapeutic agents, including conventional small\-molecule drugs, proteins, messenger RNA \(mRNA\), small interfering RNA \(siRNA\), DNA, and gene\-editing components\. Their growing importance is attributed to their biocompatibility, versatility, ability to encapsulate and protect sensitive therapeutic molecules, and potential to facilitate intracellular delivery\. LNPs generally consist of ionizable lipids, phospholipids, cholesterol, and polyethylene glycol \(PEG\)\-lipids, with each component contributing to particle formation, stability, biodistribution, cellular uptake, and therapeutic performance\. The development of ionizable lipids has been particularly important because these lipids facilitate nucleic\-acid encapsulation under acidic conditions while remaining relatively neutral at physiological pH, thereby reducing nonspecific interactions and toxicity\. The clinical success of mRNA\-LNP vaccines has provided strong evidence for the translational potential of this technology and has accelerated research into LNP\-based therapeutics for cancer, infectious diseases, inherited disorders, and other conditions\. Despite these advances, several challenges remain, including limited tissue\-specific delivery, instability, immunogenicity, toxicity, endosomal entrapment, PEG\-related limitations, manufacturing complexity, and regulatory requirements\. This review discusses the principles, composition, preparation methods, mechanisms, therapeutic applications, recent advances, limitations, and future perspectives of lipid nanoparticles for drug and gene delivery, with particular emphasis on nucleic\-acid therapeutics, targeted delivery, organ\-selective LNPs, and emerging technologies\.

## [Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4\.0 era: a TCCM\-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis](../publications/432f3bea9a2c20aa3554.md)

Amarnath Padhi; Anil Kumar; Manoj Kumar Mishra; Garima Mathur

This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management \(KM\) in the context of Industry 4\.0 \(I4\.0\) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory\-Context\-Characteristics\-Method \(TCCM\) framework\. Drawing on 93 peer\-reviewed articles from Scopus \(2018–2025\), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM\-based synthesis\. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies\. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross\-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited\. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped\. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability \(DKMC\) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology\-mediated capability shaped by human\-AI interaction, real\-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms\. The study provides a transparent, theory\-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI\-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments\.

## [Equity, Environmental Justice and Governance of Urban Green Spaces: A Bibliometric Review](../publications/43525473f2e73d33ba0c.md)

Wiliam Fernández Vásquez

This study describes the configuration and evolution of research on equity, environmental justice, and governance of urban green spaces\. A bibliometric review of documents indexed in Scopus and SciELO was conducted, complemented by descriptive analysis and science mapping with bibliometrix and VOSviewer\. The findings show accelerated growth and a concentration of scientific output in countries with high research capacity\. The thematic structure links themes of accessibility and spatial measurement with others concerning environmental justice, governance, and green gentrification\. Alongside distribution\-oriented approaches, the field includes perspectives that consider participation, recognition, and policy effects\. The limited Latin American presence constitutes a relevant geographic gap and highlights the need for broader comparative research across diverse urban contexts\.

## [Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis](../publications/4355698a744a55636610.md)

Po\-Chen Chen

Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis Po\-Chen Chen THE AMNIS, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kaohsiung, Taiwan Email:amnischenadrian@gmail\.com ——————————————————————————————————————— Abstract This paper examines the relationship between anthropomorphic narratives in artificial intelligence \(AI\), the technical capabilities of contemporary computational systems, and the material labor challenges facing the hospitality industry\. Through a fourfold conceptual analysis, the paper investigates how metaphorical representations of AI may influence public understanding of technological capabilities and expectations regarding the automation of physical service work\. First, it distinguishes the mathematical and statistical mechanisms underlying large language models from interpretations that attribute human\-like subjective experience to their outputs\. Second, it examines Dream\-RSI as a case study in the use of biological metaphors to describe computational processes, distinguishing replay\-based exploration\-policy improvement from human dreaming or subconscious reflection\. Third, it considers the physical and engineering constraints of AI infrastructure and discusses their implications for the deployment of robotic systems in hospitality environments\. Fourth, it explores how narratives of technological transformation may influence investment expectations and operational decision\-making in labor\-intensive industries\. The paper argues that technological capabilities should be evaluated according to demonstrated performance rather than anthropomorphic expectations\. It further identifies targeted mechanical automation, workforce development, and responsible international labor mobility as potential approaches to addressing hospitality labor shortages, while recognizing the need for context\-specific economic and empirical evaluation\. By connecting AI narratives with the material requirements of service delivery, this paper proposes a framework for examining the relationship between technological expectation, operational feasibility, and the future of human labor in hospitality\. Keywords: AI Anthropomorphism; Hallucination; Dream\-RSI; Hospitality Labor Crisis; Humanoid Robots; Migrant Workers; Capital Allocation\.

## [Engineering the FK228 biosynthetic gene clusters for high\-yield production](../publications/43575e4a2fb7ecaa1cf3.md)

Maoqin Wang; Xuexin Jia; Yunling Zhang; Junchi Ma; Youming Zhang; Jun Fu; Ruijuan Li

FK228 \(romidepsin\) is a potent HDAC inhibitor; however, its clinical application is severely constrained by low natural yields and the genetic intractability of its native producer\. Here, we leveraged the established Burkholderia chassis KOGC1 to develop a high\-performance platform for FK228 production\. Through systematic fermentation optimization, we addressed major production constraints including potential end\-product toxicity and precursor supply\. Specifically, the integration of XAD\-16 resin adsorption together with the combined feeding of key amino acids \(cysteine, valine, and threonine\) elevated the titer to 743\.5 mg/L\. Subsequent refactoring of the biosynthetic gene cluster and promoter engineering further increased the titer to 1109\.4 mg/L\. Furthermore, the engineered strain exhibited remarkable genetic stability over five generations without antibiotic selection, which may help address a key barrier to future scale\-up\. Overall, this study establishes a highly productive laboratory\-scale FK228 biosynthetic platform, providing a foundation for future process development of this important therapeutic agent\.

## [Impact of Radio Wave Refractivity on Mobile Network Portability Threshold in Bayelsa State, Nigeria](../publications/435e6e27ae83a73f0a4d.md)

Joyce Odu Okafor

This study investigates the influence of radio wave refractivity on mobile network portability thresholds in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, focusing on the effects of radio refractivity \(W\-unit\), atmospheric temperature \(K\), relative humidity \(%\), and atmospheric pressure \(hPa\) on mobile network signal strength\. A mixed\-methods approach was employed, combining field measurements and statistical analysis to assess the Quality of Service \(QoS\) of GSM network providers in Biogbolo and Etegwe, Yenagoa\. Data collection involved a Drive Test \(DT\) method using a vehicle\-mounted Radio Frequency \(RF\) measurement system to capture realtime signal strength variations\. Statistical analysis was conducted using MINITAB and Python software, generating time\-series graphs and interval charts to track network performance trends\. The results indicate a strong correlation between meteorological factors and signal strength across four major network providers—9Mobile, Airtel, MTN, and Glo\. In Biogbolo, signal strength improved steadily with increasing refractivity, temperature, humidity, and pressure, demonstrating a predictable positive correlation\. Conversely, in Etegwe, refractivity effects were non\-linear, with 9Mobile exhibiting signal degradation at extreme refractivity values, likely due to multipath interference and atmospheric attenuation\. Temperature fluctuations also influenced signal propagation, with minor instability observed in extreme heat conditions\. High humidity levels enhanced signal strength in Biogbolo but led to signal deterioration in Etegwe, particularly in 9Mobile, confirming humidity\-induced signal absorption effects\. Atmospheric pressure consistently improved signal reception across all networks, reinforcing its stabilizing effect on wave propagation\. The study concludes that region\-specific network adjustments are essential for optimizing mobile communication reliability in Bayelsa State, particularly in coastal regions prone to refractivity\-induced signal variations\. The study recommends the need for climate\-adaptive mobile network strategies, including dynamic frequency allocation, temperature\-sensitive power control, adaptive modulation techniques, and real\-time meteorological integration\.

## [СУТНІСТЬ ТА ЗМІСТ ФЕНОМЕНА МЕРЕЖЕВИХ ПЛАТФОРМ: СОЦІАЛЬНО\-ФІЛОСОФСЬКИЙ АНАЛІЗ](../publications/435ef9156e57f9d1ef30.md)

Mykyta Slyusar

У статті здійснено соціально\-філософський аналіз сутності та змісту феномена мережевих платформ як фундаментального прояву цифрової трансформації сучасного суспільства\. У контексті цифровізації суспільства виникла нова наукова проблема визначення сутності та змісту феномена мережевих платформ як соціально\-філософської категорії, що відображає новий тип взаємодії між людиною, цифровими технологіями та суспільством\. Мета статті полягає у здійсненні соціально\-філософського аналізу мережевих платформ як нового цифрового феномена, розкритті їхньої онтологічної, соціокультурної та комунікативної природи, а також визначенні їхньої ролі у трансформації соціальних відносин, способів взаємодії, влади та суб’єктності в умовах становлення мережевого суспільства\. Результати досліджень\. У статті концептуалізовано мережеві платформи як сучасний соціально\-філософський феномен, досліджено трансформацію соціальної взаємодії під впливом мережевих платформ\. Осмислено трансформацію суб’єктності людини в платформному середовищі та визначено перспективи розвитку мережевих платформ у контексті формування мережевої цивілізації\. Мережеві платформи розглядаються не лише як технологічна інфраструктура, а як гібридний, мережево\-онтологічний, алгоритмічно опосередкований, комунікативно\-конструктивістський та постцифровий феномен, що трансформує способи соціальної взаємодії, комунікації, самоорганізації та конструювання соціальної реальності\. Визначено суперечливу природу платформізації, що поєднує розширення цифрової свободи й посилення алгоритмічної залежності, демократизацію комунікації та концентрацію цифрової влади, персоналізацію та стандартизацію, автономізацію та платформну залежність\. Висновок\. Доведено, що мережеві платформи виступають одним із ключових механізмів переходу від індустріально\-ієрархічної до мережево\-цифрової моделі суспільства, у межах якої змінюються співвідношення «людина – технологія – суспільство»\. Запропоновано розглядати феномен мережевих платформ крізь призму цифрової онтології, мережевої раціональності, алгоритмічної влади, платформної суб’єктності, цифрової взаємозалежності та людиноцентричної цифрової трансформації\.

## [AI\-POWERED CLOUD COST OPTIMIZATION](../publications/436a43b59da1e31fae69.md)



Although cloud computing offers scalable and flexible infrastructure, but inefficient resource allocation can result in increased operational costs\.Over\-provisioning leads to unused capacity, while under\-provisioning can result in poor application performance\.Reactive autoscaling often responds to measured workload, whereas predictive resource allocation aims to forecast future demand and pre\-allocate capacity\.This study presents an AI\-driven cost optimization framework that combines historical workload data, machine\-learning\-based forecasting, and cost\-aware resource allocation\.The proposed framework considers CPU utilization, memory usage, request rate, network activity, timeseries characteristics, and previous resource usage to estimate future resource requirements\.Based on the predicted requirements, scaling decisions are made while ensuring performance objectives are met\.The framework&\#x27;s effectiveness is evaluated based on cost savings, resource utilization, prediction accuracy, response time, and scaling frequency\.The expected outcomes include improved resource utilization and reduced cloud spending without sacrificing acceptable service quality\.Additionally, this study identifies potential challenges and limitations \(e\.g\., prediction inaccuracies and rapid changes in workload\) and suggests implementing a hybrid predictive/reactive strategy for practical applications\.

## [DIDACTIC POSSIBILITIES OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN MOTHER TONGUE LESSONS](../publications/436aa90be1a694f30c05.md)

Qurolova Mohira Adxamovna

This article examines the didactic possibilities of using artificial intelligence technologies in the organization of mother tongue lessons, their role in the educational process, and their influence on the development of students&\#x27; knowledge\. It analyzes the opportunities offered by artificial intelligence tools for taking individual learning needs into account, differentiating language\-related tasks, developing written and oral communication skills, and assessing learning\. It also addresses pedagogical appropriateness, the reliability of information, and the need to maintain teacher oversight when introducing these technologies into mother tongue education\. The article substantiates that the effective use of artificial intelligence can increase students&\#x27; interest in language learning and help accommodate individual differences in the learning process\.

## [On the unfulfilled debate between D\.I\. Dubrovsky and E\.V\. Ilyenkov](../publications/43733c7024af22d33bb5.md)

А\. А\. Жудина; Anastasia A\. Zhudina

Статья посвящена анализу оснований для утверждения о существовании спора между Э\.В\. Ильенковым и Д\.И\. Дубровским относительно проблемы идеального\. В исследовательской литературе нередко говорится о «неоконченном споре» или «дискуссии» двух мыслителей, однако само наличие спора требует специальной проверки\. В статье реконструируются исходные философские установки Ильенкова и Дубровского – их понимание предмета философии, статуса категории идеального и характера связи сознания с материальной действительностью\. Показано, что расхождение между ними обнаруживается уже на уровне предварительных определений и затрагивает не отдельные тезисы, а сами основания постановки проблемы\. Особое внимание уделяется анализу интерпретации каждым из авторов положений марксистской традиции – например, формулы о «пересаженном в человеческую голову материальном»\. Рассматривается, каким образом различие в понимании идеального – как общественно\-исторической формы мышления и деятельности у Ильенкова и как субъективной реальности, обусловленной функционированием мозга конкретного индивида, у Дубровского – определяет различие их теоретических программ и уровней анализа\. Демонстрируется, что тексты мыслителей, традиционно воспринимаемые как взаимные отклики, не образуют спора в строгом смысле слова, поскольку между позициями отсутствует единое предметное поле и согласованное понимание самого предмета обсуждения\. Утверждается, что под формой дискуссии скрывается столкновение различных представлений о природе и задачах философии\. Рассмотренный случай позволяет уточнить характер расхождений внутри советской философии второй половины ХХ в\. и выявить различие между философской и натуралистической моделями осмысления проблемы идеального, что имеет значение для более точного понимания истории отечественной философской мысли\.

## [Peningkatan Kinerja Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Pengguna Aplikasi Dompet Digital Menggunakan Support Vector Machine Melalui Optimasi Seleksi Fitur Particle Swarm Optimization](../publications/4385838bcf444dfce640.md)

Tengku Hadi Somad Fuddin; Mahardika Abdi Prawira Tanjung

Pertumbuhan pengguna dompet digital di Indonesia memunculkan kebutuhan untuk memahami persepsi pengguna melalui analisis sentimen ulasan\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kinerja klasifikasi sentimen ulasan pengguna aplikasi dompet digital menggunakan Support Vector Machine \(SVM\) melalui optimasi seleksi fitur berbasis Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\)\. Data dikumpulkan dari Google Play Store sebanyak 10\.000 ulasan yang berasal dari lima aplikasi dompet digital, yaitu GoPay, OVO, Dana, LinkAja, dan ShopeePay, dengan masing\-masing 2\.000 ulasan per aplikasi\. Ulasan diklasifikasikan ke dalam tiga kelas sentimen: positif, negatif, dan netral\. Proses ekstraksi fitur dilakukan menggunakan Term Frequency\-Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\) yang menghasilkan 5\.000 fitur\. Selanjutnya, Binary PSO diterapkan untuk melakukan seleksi fitur dan berhasil mereduksi dimensi fitur menjadi 1\.326 fitur atau sekitar 26,52% dari total fitur awal\. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model SVM tanpa seleksi fitur memperoleh akurasi sebesar 88,00%, sedangkan model SVM dengan seleksi fitur Chi\-Square menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 91,00%\. Model SVM dengan seleksi fitur PSO menghasilkan akurasi tertinggi sebesar 93,75%, precision sebesar 93,86%, recall sebesar 93,75%, dan F1\-score sebesar 93,79%\. Dengan demikian, penerapan PSO berhasil meningkatkan akurasi sebesar 5,75 poin persentase dibandingkan model baseline\. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TF\-IDF, Binary PSO, dan SVM merupakan pendekatan yang efektif untuk analisis sentimen ulasan pengguna dompet digital\.

## [Intelligent Electrical Capacity Forecasting for AI Workloads in Modular Data Centre Expansion Planning](../publications/4389ec52029f52157733.md)

Pradeep Rao Vennamaneni; Sri Prudhvi Adusumilli; Naveen Shrivastava; Mahesh Marri; Sojy John; Venkata Phaneendra Reddi

As the number of workloads for AI training and inference grows at a rapid rate, hyperscale and modular data centres have experienced unprecedented volatility and variability in electrical demand profiles, which is threatening the traditional deterministic capacity expansion planning approaches\. This paper combines recent developments in electrical load forecasting, deep learning architectures, and risk\-aware infrastructure planning, and proposes an integrated framework for intelligent forecasting capability of electrical capacity in the context of AI\-workload based modular expansion of the data centre\. The framework integrates probabilistic time\-series forecasting models, such as long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) networks and temporal fusion transformers \(TFT\), with a conditional value\-at\-risk \(CVaR\) constrained optimization layer that maps in uncertain demand forecasts into capacity expansion decisions, done in steps and in sections\. When compared to other forecasting methods, the hybrid attention\-based models show mean absolute percentage errors of less than four percent, much lower than the mean absolute percentage errors of classical statistical baseline models that are typically over nine percent when applied to similar short\-term forecasting problems\. The analysis further shows that in successive phases of expanded use, the combination of forecast\-driven provisioning and on\-site renewable generation and energy storage can reduce the marginal carbon intensity by over 50% compared to the traditional static deterministic approach to provisioning, while also improving capital efficiency and grid resilience\. Comparative benchmarking is done to assess efficiency, cost, scalability, and regulatory dimensions, and shows several times greater growth in facility demand for AI workloads when compared to enterprise workloads in more traditional baselines\. However, the synthesis identifies longstanding issues such as congestion in interconnection queues, forecast uncertainty propagation, and harmonisation of data\-sharing processes between the operators of data centres and the operators of the transmission system\. The proposed framework provides planners with a repeatable, scientifically rigored and mathematically based approach that is applicable to the ever expanding and rapidly evolving electrical use of AI computing\.

## [Isolation and Characterization of Extracellular Lipase\-Producing Bacillus spp\. and Exploratory Application of a Freeze\-Dried Lipase Preparation from Phenotypically Identified Bacillus licheniformis NOS2 in Bread](../publications/43a6ef98ae1d23066356.md)

Dawrin Hawar Mohammed; Abduljabar Omer Quja

Background and Aim: Microbial lipases are established food\-biotechnology catalysts; however, performance in bread depends on preparation, dose, and formulation\. This study followed environmental lipolytic Bacillus isolates through phenotypic identification and quantitative enzyme selection to exploratory bread application of a freeze\-dried extracellular preparation from NOS2, phenotypically identified as B\. licheniformis using BD Phoenix M50 with 99% confidence\. Material and Methods: Thirty oil\-associated soil and oil\-cake samples were screened\. Bacillus isolates were characterized conventionally and phenotypically identified using BD Phoenix M50\. Tributyrin hydrolysis, submerged lipase production, protein\-normalized activity, assay pH and temperature, thermal pre\-exposure response, olive\-oil emulsion response, ATR\-FTIR, Sephadex G\-100 enrichment, and freeze\-drying were assessed\. The freeze\-dried NOS2 preparation \(PE\) and commercial technological comparator \(SE\) were added at equal powder mass \(0\.01 or 0\.03 g kg⁻¹ flour\), with or without 2% butter; they were not activity\-matched\. Each bread formulation was one dough batch; therefore, physical measurements were interpreted descriptively\. Results and Conclusion: Eleven isolates were phenotypically assigned to B\. licheniformis \(n=6\), B\. subtilis \(n=4\), or B\. cereus \(n=1\)\. LSSS1, NOS2, and NOSS1 showed crude specific activities of 4\.18, 3\.98, and 3\.31 U mg⁻¹, respectively, and highest measured immediate activity at pH 6 and 37 °C\. Thermal pre\-exposure resulted in a non\-monotonic apparent titrimetric response in crude preparations and was not interpreted as molecular thermostability\. Relative post\-lyophilization activity after reconstitution was 77\.42\-83\.56%, with NOS2 highest\. In the single\-batch bread trial, PE 0\.03 plus butter showed the highest observed mean specific loaf volume \(3\.191 ± 0\.033 mL g⁻¹\) and lowest observed fresh and day\-1 firmness \(119\.3 ± 11\.0 and 203\.7 ± 14\.3 g\)\. Sensory springiness differed among formulations after multiplicity correction, whereas overall acceptability did not show a confirmed preference hierarchy\. Bread findings require independent batch replication for generalizable treatment inference\. INTRODUCTION Microbial lipases \(EC 3\.1\.1\.3\) hydrolyze ester bonds in triacylglycerols and can catalyze esterification and transesterification under appropriate conditions\. Their extracellular production by many microorganisms, broad catalytic versatility, and compatibility with diverse process environments have made them important targets for food biotechnology and other industrial applications \[1\]\. Bacillus species are particularly relevant as extracellular\-enzyme producers because of their rapid growth, secretion capacity, ecological adaptability, and long history as microbial production platforms \[2,3\]\. Oil\-contaminated soils and oil\-cake residues from edible\-oil processing are rational sources for lipolytic microorganisms because these environments repeatedly expose resident populations to triglycerides and lipid\-derived compounds\. Lipase\-producing bacteria have been recovered from oil\-associated environments \[4,5\], while oilseed cakes retain residual lipid, protein, carbohydrate, fiber, and minerals that can support microbial growth \[6\]\. Environmental screening nevertheless has value only when plate hydrolysis is followed by quantitative enzyme production and biochemical characterization, because halo formation reflects growth, secretion, diffusion, and substrate accessibility rather than enzyme activity alone\. For food\-processing use, characterization must distinguish between immediate catalytic optima and tolerance to process stresses\. The pH and temperature that maximize a short assay do not necessarily predict persistence after prolonged heat exposure\. This distinction is particularly important for bakery applications, where an enzyme preparation may experience changing temperature, water distribution, and substrate accessibility before it is thermally inactivated\. Freeze\-drying also deserves attention because it can improve handling and storage of an enzyme preparation but may cause activity losses during freezing and dehydration \[14\]\. In breadmaking, lipase action can modify the lipid environment at gas\-cell interfaces and can be associated with interactions among lipids, starch, and gluten, thereby influencing dough handling, loaf expansion, crumb structure, and firming\. Recent studies have reported increases in specific volume and reductions in bread hardness under some lipase\-treatment conditions, but the magnitude and direction of the response depend on enzyme origin, dose, flour lipid composition, and the presence of added fat \[7,8,17,18\]\. These mechanisms are used here only as literature\-supported explanatory frameworks\. The present study did not directly quantify mono\-/diacylglycerols, free fatty acids, interfacial lipid distribution, starch\-lipid complex formation, or specific lipid\-gluten interactions; therefore, none of these pathways is claimed as directly demonstrated in the present bread system\. Recent studies illustrate two complementary parts of the field\. Environmental studies have recovered and optimized extracellular lipase production from oil\-associated Bacillus isolates \[4,5\], whereas bakery studies commonly evaluate commercial or already\-defined lipase preparations directly in bread formulations \[8,17\]\. These approaches answer different questions\. Following the same locally produced extracellular preparation from environmental recovery and quantitative selection through biochemical characterization, drying, and direct bread application can therefore provide useful source\-to\-application information without implying that the individual methods are themselves novel\. Accordingly, the present study is framed as an integrated source\-to\-application case study rather than as a claim of being the first study to combine these stages\. Oil\-associated Bacillus isolates were screened and ranked by quantitative extracellular lipase performance; selected preparations were characterized for immediate pH and temperature response, thermal pre\-exposure response, olive\-oil emulsion response, ATR\-FTIR profile, partial purification, and freeze\-drying; and the selected freeze\-dried crude preparation was then evaluated in wheat bread at two addition levels with and without 2% butter alongside a technological commercial comparator\. The objectives were to identify functional extracellular lipase producers, define the measured preparation\-level biochemical behavior, and examine whether the selected preparation showed formulation\-dependent patterns in bread quality under the stated exploratory design\. MATERIALS AND METHODS 2\.1\. Environmental Sampling and Isolation Environmental sampling was conducted in June 2024 in Erbil Governorate, Kurdistan Region, Iraq\. Samples were obtained from Zer Oil Factory in Erbil, Srushti Nwebunawa Oil Factory in Bnaslawa/Erbil, and a local family\-operated oil\-processing business in Qushtapa\. Thirty separately collected specimens comprising oil\-contaminated soils and oil\-cake residues associated with sunflower, olive, and coconut processing were obtained by purposive sampling\. Soil was sampled aseptically at approximately 5\-10 cm depth; approximately 50 g of material was placed in sterile containers, transported to the laboratory on the same day, and processed after approximately 24 h at room temperature\. Twenty\-four specimens yielded bacterial growth under the isolation conditions and were retained for isolate\-level testing\. In the laboratory coding system, labels without the suffix “S” denote soil samples, whereas labels containing the suffix “S” denote substrate/oil\-cake samples\. The complete 24\-record isolate\-level dataset is provided in Table 10\. For heat\-selective enrichment, 2 g of each sample was added to 10 mL sterile nutrient broth and heated at 90 °C for 10\-12 min\. This step was intentionally selective for heat\-tolerant and/or spore\-forming organisms and could exclude heat\-sensitive or non\-spore\-forming lipase producers; consequently, the recovered isolates should not be interpreted as representing the full microbial diversity of the source environments\. Enrichment cultures were incubated at 37 °C for 24\-48 h and streaked onto nutrient agar \(LAB, Lab M Limited, UK\)\. Plates were incubated aerobically at 37 °C for approximately 24 h, and morphologically distinct colonies were repeatedly re\-streaked until pure\. Routine cultures were maintained on nutrient\-agar slants at 4 °C; long\-term stocks were prepared in nutrient broth containing 30% glycerol and stored at \-20 and \-80 °C\. 2\.2\. Phenotypic Characterization and Identification Purified isolates were examined by Gram staining and endospore staining\. Motility, catalase, oxidase, citrate utilization, urease activity, indole production, and hemolysis on 5% sheep\-blood agar were evaluated using conventional procedures\. Mannitol Egg Yolk Polymyxin \(MYP\) agar \(Ibresco, Italy\) was used as an additional differential medium after cooling the basal medium to approximately 45\-50 °C before addition of egg\-yolk and selective supplements\. Colony color, mannitol\-related reactions, and egg\-yolk precipitation were treated as supporting characteristics rather than definitive species criteria\. Selected Bacillus isolates were subjected to automated phenotypic identification using the BD Phoenix M50 system \(BD, USA\) with PMIC/ID\-111 Gram\-positive panels\. Fresh pure growth was adjusted to approximately 0\.5 McFarland before panel inoculation\. Instrument\-generated species assignments were interpreted as phenotypic identifications and were considered together with microscopic, cultural, and conventional biochemical characteristics\. Phoenix confidence values for the 11 target isolates ranged from 90% to 99%; NOS2, subsequently used for the bread preparation, was identified phenotypically as Bacillus licheniformis with 99% confidence\. Sequence\-based confirmation was not p

## [Effect of Probiotic Supplementation on Glycemic Control in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Evidence\-Based Case Report](../publications/43aa09a6df398f04dec4.md)

Gisheila Ruth Anggitha; Diana Sunardi

Introduction: Type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) remains a global health challenge with rising prevalence and significant long\-term complications\. Emerging evidence highlights the role of gut microbiota in glucose metabolism, with probiotics proposed as a potential adjunctive therapy to improve glycemic control\. Methods: Literature searches were performed in PubMed, Cochrane, and Scopus for randomized controlled trials \(RCTs\) and meta\-analyses published within the last five years\. Studies were critically appraised using the Oxford Center for Evidence\-Based Medicine \(OCEBM\) tools and outcomes for fasting blood glucose \(FBG\), glycated hemoglobin \(HbA1c\), and HOMA\-IR were assessed\. Results: Six studies met the inclusion criteria, including one network meta\-analysis and five RCTs\. Probiotic supplementation, particularly multi\-strain formulations of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, significantly improved FBG and HbA1c and enhanced β\-cell function\. However, heterogeneity in strains, dosage, and intervention duration limited definitive conclusions\. Most studies reported that probiotic supplementation is well tolerated, with only mild and transient gastrointestinal side effects\. Conclusion: Probiotic supplementation, especially a multi\-strain combination of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, may be a safe additional therapy to improve blood sugar control in people with type 2 diabetes\. Larger clinical trials with stronger methodologies are still needed to determine the optimal dose, strain composition, and duration of supplementation\.

## [Kinetik Tipografide Anlam Aktarımı: Şahsiyet Dizisi Örneği](../publications/43ae861020b9dd80d405.md)

Ebru Küçükkeskin; Fatih Kurtcu

Kinetik tipografi, metni harekete geçirerek onu görsel bir anlatıya dönüştüren ve anlam aktarımında çeşitli grafik tasarım ögelerinden yararlanan bir anlatım biçimidir\. Kinetik tipografi çalışmalarında kullanılan grafik tasarım ögelerinin anlam aktarımına katkısını sistematik biçimde ele alan çalışmaların sınırlı olması, bu alanda kapsamlı bir inceleme ihtiyacını ortaya koymaktadır\. Bu araştırmanın amacı, kinetik tipografide anlam aktarımına yardımcı olan grafik tasarım ögelerini belirlemek ve bu ögelerin kullanım biçimlerini incelemektir\. Araştırmada literatür incelemesi doğrultusunda belirlenen grafik tasarım ögeleri, çeşitli kinetik tipografi örneklerinin betimsel analizi ve Şahsiyet dizisinden seçilen bir sahne için gerçekleştirilen uygulama çalışması üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir\. Çalışma kapsamında yazı karakteri, form, hareket, renk, görsel efektler, destekleyici imgeler, kamera hareketleri, ışık ve arka plan ögelerinin anlam aktarımındaki işlevleri ele alınmıştır\. Çalışma sonucunda, incelenen kinetik tipografi örneklerinde bu ögelerin anlam aktarımını desteklemek amacıyla çeşitli işlevlerle kullanılabildiği belirlenmiştir\. Bu çalışma ile kinetik tipografi uygulamalarında anlam aktarımına yardımcı olan grafik tasarım ögeleri ve bu ögelerin birer araç olarak kullanım biçimleri bütüncül bir çerçevede ele alınmıştır\.

## [Dablemont, Paul: Le réel du sujet – Désir, inconscient et subjectivité différentielle](../publications/43c403c99a751ea6616d.md)



This paper argues that the subject is not a stable substance, but a fragile fold stretched over the void, produced by a subjective meta\-machine that constantly territorializes the flow of desire\. By weaving together Deleuze \(surface effect\), Lacan \(lack\-of\-being\), Adorno \(social wound\), and Searle \(Background\), it shows that the subject is traversed by operators – desire, the unconscious, memory, identity – that give consistency to the void\. The cure does not aim for illusory healing, but for an ethics of &quot;sober lucidity&quot;: it deconstructs fixations through negative deterritorialization, then invents new forms of life through creative\-critical reterritorialization, thus learning to &quot;dance on the abyss&quot; in the face of threats from war, authoritarian language, and digital colonization\. \(direct link \)

## [Truck Platooning—An Overview Study with Time Constraints](../publications/43c41af605c4874ae57b.md)

Athira Mavoomkuttathil Sivachandran

The truck platoon has a significant impact on modern society\. As fuel costs increase daily,vehicles can be driven in a pattern to reduce fuel consumption\. Vehicle routing problem is discussed in literature with taking only single objective and not considering other objectives\.Multiple objectives are hard to solve\.If the environment changes then vehicle routine problem gets a new route hence problem becomes challenging\.In theory the data about customers and route to reach the customer will be known before but the real case scenario the request from customer changes so the environment is dynamic\.The dynamic vehicle routing problem is discussed in this study with time window where which customer has to visit in what time is included\.Multiple objectives such as the waiting time of the customer and minimizing routing distance to reach the customer are considered here\.Hence there are multiple objectives in the dynamic environment an ensemble learning to obtain an optimization problem is discussed here ie;EL\-DMOEA\.Other algorithms to solve vehicle routing problem along with their comparison additionally different types of platoons, comparison of platoon with other types of the transportation is also discussed in this report\.

## [Disclosing pathogenic processes of monkeypox \(MPOX\) and drug repurposing through host\-transcriptomics analysis](../publications/43c5388858d0aa0338bc.md)

Sabkat Mahmud; Alvira Ajadee; Md\. Ahad Ali; Md\. Feroj Ahmed; Reaz Ahmmed; Md\. Masud Rana; Tooba Noor; Md\. Fahim Faysal; Md\. Hadiul Kabir; Md\. Nurul Haque Mollah

Monkeypox \(MPOX\) virus infection outbreak in Africa in 2022 was initially considered a neglected tropical disease \(NTD\)\. Now it is recognized as a global health problem\. The recent global spread has emphasized the need for increased attention to combat MPOX\. Although there are some vaccines against MPOX, most people worldwide are still not vaccinated due to their unawareness or unavailability\. However, so far, there is no approved drug against MPOX yet\. Therefore, effective drugs against MPOX are also essential\. This study attempted to disclose pathogenic processes and therapeutic strategies of MPOX based on MPOX\-associated host key\-genes \(hKGs\)\. At first, three transcriptomic profile datasets were analyzed, identifying 166 common host differentially expressed genes \(hDEGs\) between MPOX patients and control groups, comprising 75 upregulated and 91 downregulated hDEGs\. Subsequently, six top\-ranked host key genes \(hKGs\): ALB, HSP90AA1, CDH1, PTPRC, IGF1, and ABL1, were identified as potential MPOX\-causing genes through protein\-protein interaction \(PPI\) network analysis\. Functional enrichment analysis of these hKGs revealed critical pathogenic processes of MPOX infection, including biological processes, molecular functions, cellular components, and KEGG pathways\. Regulatory network analysis involving transcription factors and miRNAs provided further insights into disease mechanisms\. Based on molecular docking analysis, five top\-ranked drug molecules Tecovirimat, Beclabuvir, Maraviroc, Raltegravir, and Brincidofovir were identified as potential repurposable therapeutics against MPOX\. ADME/T and drug\-likeness evaluations confirmed favorable pharmacokinetic properties for these candidates\. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations of the top three complexes \(ALB\-Tecovirimat, CDH1\-Maraviroc, and PPARG\-Beclabuvir\) demonstrated strong binding stability, supported by RMSD, RMSF, and MM\-GBSA results\. Therefore, the results provided in this study might be potential resources for diagnosis and therapies of MPOX patients\. However, the findings require experimental validation in wet lab for further confirmation\.

## [What Lies Beyond ‘Basic’ Literacy?](../publications/43c71890ebe8038ab088.md)

Norbert Griszbacher; Kitti Griszbacher

Technological advances, changing labour markets, and the growing accessibility of online learning have renewed debate over the value of education beyond the compulsory \(elementary\) school years\. This opinion paper examines the contribution of education once basic literacy and foundational knowledge have been established, particularly during adolescence and emerging adulthood\. We argue that its value extends beyond academic and vocational preparation: educational institutions across elementary, secondary, vocational, and higher education can support character development, social and ethical development, civic responsibility, and the acquisition of transferable competencies\. In addition, it provides social, mentoring, and developmental experiences that are difficult to replicate through independent learning or early employment\. While acknowledging concerns about costs, curriculum relevance, and employability, we conclude that these challenges call for reform rather than reduced participation\. Education should therefore strengthen character and transferable competencies alongside academic learning, preparing not only knowledgeable individuals but also adaptable, responsible, and socially engaged people capable of becoming the best versions of themselves and navigating the challenges of ‘real’ life\.

## [Varietal classification and morphological traits prediction of lettuce cultivar \(Lactuca sativa L\.\) based on RGB\-images and convolutional neural network](../publications/43ce61e9bbb4a32650b8.md)

Qian Gong; Yan Zhang; Muhammad Allam Daffa Alhaqi; Wahyu Nurkholis Hadi Syahputra; Heon‐Ho Jeong

This study evaluated five convolutional neural network \(CNN\) architectures for non\-destructive lettuce \(Lactuca sativa L\.\) phenotyping using RGB images\. A dataset of 388 plants representing four cultivars was used to predict leaf area \(LA\), canopy diameter \(D\), fresh weight \(FW\), and dry weight \(DW\), and to classify cultivar identity\. Images were split into training, validation, and test sets \(70/15/15%\) before training\-only augmentation\. An input\-representation ablation compared original RGB, background\-segmented RGB, and binary canopy masks\. The best regression results were obtained with InceptionResNetV2 using original RGB for FW \(R 2 = 0\.935, RMSE = 30\.65 g\) and D \(R 2 = 0\.892, RMSE = 2\.17 cm\), SimpleCNN using original RGB for DW \(R 2 = 0\.958, RMSE = 1\.02 g\), and InceptionResNetV2 using segmented RGB for LA \(R 2 = 0\.898, RMSE = 520\.73 cm 2 \)\. Cultivar\-classification accuracy ranged from 96\.55% to 98\.28% across architectures\. Five\-fold cultivar\-stratified cross\-validation using segmented RGB showed relatively stable regression performance across partitions\. Under the same data split, the best CNN configurations produced numerically higher R 2 values than feature\-engineered machine\-learning baselines, although the difference for LA was marginal\. These results demonstrate trait\-dependent effects of image representation and support RGB\-based CNNs as a practical approach for lettuce phenotyping\.

## [The impact of social media on e\-commerce purchase behavior in Türkiye](../publications/43eb53fb595f38e207f5.md)

Neda Alipour; Sema Nur Kayalı; Mustafa Ağaçkesen; Beyzanur Sivil; Merve Nur Yıldız; Didem TETİK KÜÇÜKELÇİ

Due to the increasing involvement of social media in e\-commerce, there is also a remarkable change in the consumer purchasing behavior\. The aim of this paper is to examine the influential factors of e\-commerce purchase behavior and also compare differences among demographics in the context of social commerce\. The research was performed using an online questionnaire survey with 407 social media users from Turkey\. One\-way analysis of variance, correlation analysis and independent samples t\-test were used for data analysis\.According to the study, influencer impact, effectiveness of campaigns/discounts, trust in user\-generated reviews, and exposure to e\-commerce content had a significant positive relationship with e\-commerce shopping behavior\. However, the study found no significant relationship between purchasing behavior and social media advertising trust\. In addition, there were significant differences in shopping behavior among genders and generations\.The study contributes to the social commerce literature because of its practical approach to the issue and analysis of factors affecting consumer online purchasing behavior\. The research shows that the traditional social media trust is not enough to change consumer buying behavior; hence, companies need to create more complex strategies for promoting products/services in social networks\.

## [A new machine learning based framework for seismic damage ratio prediction of building clusters using satellite remote sensing data](../publications/43ee539d129031334a6b.md)

Min Liu; Xiwei Fan; Jiwen An; Jing Wang; Wenyu Nie; Yuanmeng Qi; Fucun Lu; Nuoting Hou; Xuchuan Lin; Hong Chen

Seismic\-induced building damage prediction is essential for disaster mitigation and risk assessment\. However, traditional methods often require detailed structural parameters that are labor\-intensive to obtain, while post\-earthquake remote sensing is frequently hindered by data latency\. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework utilizing pre\-event multi\-source satellite data to predict damage, employing building height and construction period as proxies for structural types\. Taking the 2023 Türkiye Mw 7\.8 earthquake as a case study, we modeled the weighted building cluster damage ratio \(WBCDR\) using 26 predictors derived from remotely sensed building key attributes, seismic parameters, topography, and spectral\-textural features\. Random Forest \(RF\) and Support Vector Regression \(SVR\) models were evaluated at spatial scales of 300 m, 500 m, and 1 km\. RF outperformed SVR, with the best mean test performance at 500 m across ten splits \(R2 = 0\.8248, Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\) = 0\.0482, Root Mean Squared Error \(RMSE\) = 0\.0916\)\. Notably, Pseudo\-Spectral Acceleration at 0\.3 s \(PSA03\), Peak Ground Acceleration \(PGA\), and textural Dissimilarity were identified as dominant influencing factors\. The proposed framework enables rapid and effective large\-scale seismic building damage prediction in areas lacking detailed structural information, providing valuable support for seismic risk assessment and emergency response\.

## [Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte\-level models should spend compute](../publications/43f028c019c1a804054f.md)

Nicolás Vera Zúñiga

Byte\-level language models such as the Byte Latent Transformer \(BLT\) run their large global model once per patch and start a patch where a small model&\#x27;s next\-byte entropy is high\. This rule rarely starts a patch at in\-line computed results, such as the number after &quot;=&quot; in a worked solution, and accuracy on them collapses under tight patch budgets\. We propose novelty patching, motivated by LZ77\-style compression: start a patch where the upcoming bytes are unlikely to repeat the recent context\. The rule is a lookup table over the previous two bytes, fitted in seconds on raw text with no labels, reference model or losses\. In BLT\-style models trained from scratch on a 1\.9 GB math corpus at a matched \~11% patch rate \(3 seeds each\), it has no clear effect at 1M parameters, raises final\-answer accuracy from 47% to 72% at 12M, and at 50M raises computed\-result accuracy from 21% to 57% and final\-answer accuracy from 60% to 90%; a table fitted on the raw pretraining corpus keeps the gain\. Outside math the advantage shrinks: novelty lowers bits per byte on prose and ties entropy on source code and on synthetic execution traces\. An analysis of where boundaries fall explains the pattern\. Computed results have ordinary surprisal for the patcher&\#x27;s model, so surprisal\-seeking rules pass over them: entropy concentrates patch starts on high\-surprisal bytes most strongly of all rules \(boundary enrichment 1\.61\) and is the worst on computed results, while the best rules sit near chance enrichment\. Novelty works where new content begins at segment starts close to the computation, as in written math; a learned chunker \(H\-Net\) finds such structure on its own, in math and in code\. We also report what did not work: typed uncertainty as a training rule, switching rules after training, and a context\-aware novelty predictor\.

## [Characterization and regionalization of dry spells across Java\-Indonesia using relative frequency and fractional contribution to total duration](../publications/43f069acb612331fdd71.md)

Dinda Rosyia Wibawanty; Supari; I Putu Santikayasa

Dry spells represent an important dimension of rainfall variability because rainfall accumulation alone may not adequately capture the temporal distribution of rainfall and its associated impacts\. This study characterizes and regionalizes dry spells across Java, Indonesia, using relative frequency \(RF\) and fractional contribution to total duration \(FCTD\)\. Daily rainfall data from 771 BMKG stations across Java for 2010–2019 were analyzed to characterize dry\-spell duration\. RF and FCTD were calculated for different dry\-spell durations\. Principal component analysis \(PCA\) and K\-means clustering were subsequently applied to regionalize dry\-spell characteristics\. Short\-duration dry spells \(≤10 days\) exhibited the highest RF throughout Java, whereas FCTD revealed pronounced spatial variability\. Western Java was characterized by a greater contribution from short\-duration dry spells, while eastern Java showed a greater contribution from long\-duration dry spells \(&gt;10 days\)\. A distinct north–south gradient was also identified, reflecting the influence of local topography, with long\-duration dry spells contributing more substantially in northern regions\. Dry\-spell characteristics closely corresponded to the spatial distribution of mean annual rainfall, with wetter regions dominated by short\-duration dry spells and drier regions by long\-duration dry spells\. Mean annual rainfall showed a moderately strong positive correlation with the FCTD of short\-duration dry spells \(Pearson’s r = 0\.657\)\. Regionalization identified four clusters representing distinct dry\-spell regimes across Java\. The findings demonstrate that combining RF, FCTD, and multivariate clustering provides a physically meaningful framework for characterizing the spatial variability of dry spells across Java, capturing both the west–east rainfall contrast and the north–south topographic gradient\.

## [Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization](../publications/440aff99ddf85a1ad762.md)

Johannes Jakubik; Isabelle Wittmann; Zaheed Gaffoor; Gciniwe Simphiwe Baloyi; Craig Mahlasi; Etienne Vos; Thomas Brunschwiler; Daniel J\. Egger

The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm \(QAOA\) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems\. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution\. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit\. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles\. However, finding good angles is an instance\-specific and computationally expensive non\-convex classical optimization task\. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high\-quality QAOA angles\. Our learned models replace the per\-instance optimization, that we call the solver, with a single forward pass that is several orders of magnitude faster than the solver with a near identical quality\. Our models further generalize to unseen topologies such as Barabási\-Albert and 2D grid graphs\. Experiments on quantum hardware confirm that QAOA samples with angles produced by our open\-source models are indistinguishable from solver angles\. Crucially, models sensitive to the topology of the problem instance increase the quality of the QAOA angles\. Our work amortizes a major bottleneck in QAOA by an up\-front data generation and training cost\. Importantly, this cost can be amortized over time in settings where many similar problems are optimized on a regular basis, as is often the case in applications for industry\.

## [JAUNDICE FORM OF LEPTOSPIROSIS IN OBSTETRIC PRACTICE: A CLINICAL CASE OF MATERNAL DEATH](../publications/442ebd6404a30e6936fa.md)

Viacheslav M\. Husiev

Introduction\. The icteric form of leptospirosis in pregnant women is rare but severe, potentially leading to multi\-organ failure and a high risk of maternal and fetal death\. Clinical manifestations are often nonspecific and may mimic preeclampsia or other pregnancy complications, complicating early diagnosis\.Aim\. To increase medical professionals’ awareness of the clinical course and pathomorphological findings of icteric leptospirosis in pregnancy to support timely diagnosis and clinical management\.Materials and methods\. A retrospective analysis was conducted of a maternal death in a 25\-week pregnant woman with the icteric form of leptospirosis\. The study included anamnesis, clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and autopsy results, with macro\- and histological examination of the liver, kidneys, lungs, and placenta\.Results\. On admission, the patient had jaundice, hyperthermia \(39\.2 °C\), tachycardia, arterial hypotension, and oliguria\. Laboratory tests indicated severe liver and kidney injury \(bilirubin 175 µmol/L, ALT 86 U/L, AST 95 U/L, creatinine 149 µmol/L, urea 15\.8 mmol/L, thrombocytopenia 74×10⁹/L, leukocytes 15\.4×10⁹/L, C\-reactive protein 18 mg/L\)\. Despite intensive therapy, multi\-organ failure, disseminated intravascular coagulation \(DIC\), and septic shock developed, resulting in death\. Autopsy confirmed a severe infectious\-toxic process: focal hepatic necrosis, dystrophic and necrotic changes in the kidneys, venous congestion and pulmonary edema, and severe infectious\-inflammatory damage of the placenta with villous edema, trophoblast necrosis, and extensive hemorrhages\.Conclusions\. Clinical, laboratory, and morphological findings indicate a severe course of the icteric form of leptospirosis in pregnancy and confirm the link between systemic infection, impaired uteroplacental circulation, and maternal death\. Early involvement of an infectious disease specialist and intensive therapy is critically important\.

## [The Ephemeral Cost of Switching Optimizers Across LLM Training Stages](../publications/444299cd671504a9f5a8.md)

Xinyu Zhao; Davis Wertheimer; Ashutosh Sharma; Rameswar Panda; Paul Pu Liang

Recent work suggests that switching optimizers between pretraining and subsequent training stages incurs a performance cost, but systematic investigation of this phenomenon is lacking\. We study the mismatch between AdamW and Muon optimizers by pretraining 1\.2B Llama\-3 models from scratch while varying the proportion of updates taken with each optimizer, and similarly interpolating between the two optimizers during continued pretraining and supervised fine\-tuning \(SFT\)\. Surprisingly, we find little evidence of a meaningful optimizer mismatch penalty: final performance is largely explained by the independent effects of the pretraining and post\-training optimizers, with downstream performance generally improving as the proportion of Muon updates during SFT increases\. Although matching the pretraining optimizer can reduce forgetting during SFT, this does not translate into improved final benchmark performance\. We further evaluate AdamW and Muon for task\-general SFT of open\-weight models, across the Llama and Qwen families up to 14B parameters, where Muon remains competitive with AdamW, despite these models having been pretrained with AdamW\. Together, our results suggest that the choice of optimizer for post\-training can be made largely independently of the optimizer used during pretraining\.

## [Next‐Generation Seismic Performance Assessment Through Multi‐Component Ground Motion Compatible Intensifying Artificial Acceleration](../publications/44482db408d21d1b2dd2.md)

Mohammad Amin Hariri‐Ardebili; Giacomo Sevieri; Carlo Resta; Golsa Mahdavi; Anna De Falco; Siamak Sattar; Sissy Nikolaou

ABSTRACT Despite the crucial need for fully quantitative risk assessment of large‐scale structures, their performance is typically assessed through deterministic or semi‐quantitative approaches\. The main preventing factor is the computational burden of probabilistic seismic analyses\. This paper proposes a fast and accurate method that combines the capabilities of Incremental Dynamic Analysis \(IDA\) and endurance time methods\. The method is based on intensifying artificial acceleration \(IAA\), which is generated based on meta‐features such as spectral ordinates, nonlinear response, and hysteretic energy present in real ground motion\. The IAA aims to estimate the incremental response of the structure, similar to the IDA method, but using only a single simulation\. The proposed IAA method is applied to a benchmark dam and is compared to single‐record IDA for various types of foundation‐structure interaction assumptions, as well as for linear and nonlinear systems\. Differences between multicomponent IAA and IDA in terms of drift and damage index are quantified using ten similarity and distance metrics\. The findings demonstrate promising compatibility between IAA and IDA, while the former reduces computational time by up to 90%\.

## [An AI\- and IoT\-Enabled Smart Food Donation Management System with Explainable Food\-Risk Prediction, Safe\-Time Forecasting and Automated NGO Assignment](../publications/44508e9f5dea3f2bb4f4.md)

Dr\. Manoj Singh S\. Mathavencie Sudhakar

Surplus cooked food from restaurants, hotels and cafés is often discarded because donors cannot verify its safety or reach an NGO in time\. This paper presents a Smart Food Donation Management System that combines low\-cost IoT sensing, explainable machine learning and automated NGO allocation in one web platform\. An ESP32 node with DHT22 and MQ\-135 sensors streams storage conditions, and high gas readings flag or block spoiled food\. Six algorithms were compared with 5\-fold cross\-validation; the selected Gradient Boosting model classifies each donation as low, medium or high risk from temperature, humidity, food age and food type\. A safe\-time forecast estimates when food will become high risk, and exact Shapley values explain each prediction\. An allocation module offers each donation to one NGO at a time, filtering by remaining capacity and by whether the NGO can arrive before the food becomes unsafe\. On 600 heldout records the model achieved 97\.0% accuracy, a macro F1\-score of 0\.957 and 98\.7% high\-risk recall, with no high\-risk record classified as low risk\. In a 50\-day simulation the allocation method delivered 87\.2% of meals safely, against 83\.3% for nearest\-NGO allocation, and all 45 functional tests passed\.

## [Tool Recommendation for Multi\-Step Agents: Finding Every Tool a Task Needs](../publications/44692cc584ddc4dd244a.md)

Sam Partee; River Stevens; Thierry Damiba; Valerie Fanelle

A multi\-step agent task fails when a single tool it needs is missing, yet the tools an agent may need are too many to list: the roughly 8,200 tools on the platform we study have definitions that together exceed the context window of any model we evaluate\. We present Tool Recommendation, a deployed system that gives an agent all of them, hundreds of times more than a typical MCP server exposes, through a fixed interface of three tools\. It runs at the gateway between agent and tools, executing every call under the end user&\#x27;s own credentials and checking it against the user&\#x27;s consent for each service and the tools the agent may use\. We evaluate it on both a public retrieval benchmark and billed end\-to\-end session cost\. On ToolRet, Tool Recommendation places every tool a query needs in the top ten 57% more often than BM25, a lexical ranking that commercial tool search offers, and compares favorably with published systems up to nine times its size\. In paired multi\-step workflows, its first recommendation covered every required tool in 93% of Codex sessions, and against a fixed list of 100 tools it cut input tokens by 17% with Codex and 40% with Claude Code and the total bill in all 14 runs, by up to 40%, with no change in task completion\.

## [FAREF: Exploring Consolidation and Acquisition Effects of Procedural Scaffolding in Argument Evaluation](../publications/447586e5d0dd8d47a4ee.md)

Hori Rashid; Nawras Khudhur; Tola Abdulsattar Faraj; Tsukasa Hirashima

Despite extensive research on critical thinking instruction, approaches for supporting the maintenance of procedural argument\-evaluation performance, particularly among struggling learners, remain underexplored\. This exploratory study evaluated the Formalization and Argument Reasoning Evaluation Framework \(FAREF\), a flowchart\-guided procedural scaffold integrating the Triangular Logic Model\. In a quasi\-experimental pretest\-posttest design, 29 undergraduates received FAREF instruction \( $$n = 15$$ \) or conventional instruction \( $$n = 14$$ \)\. An omnibus item\-level analysis yielded a significant three\-way interaction between condition, initial skill, and pre\-test response state, $$\\chi ^2\(1\) = 4\.08$$ , $$p =\.043$$ , consistent with a consolidation\-specific benefit for lower\-skill learners; the interaction was fragile to single cases \(leave\-one\-out range: $$p =\.024$$ –\.127\) and marginal when initial skill was modeled continuously \( $$p =\.053$$ \)\. No acquisition effect was detectable, and an equivalence test showed the study was insensitive to effects smaller than $$\\pm\\;0\.10$$ on the proportion scale\. The pre\-test performance clustered near the chance level of the binary format, bounding all inferences\. The findings are hypothesis\-generating and motivate a powered, randomized replication with a validated instrument\.

## [Benchmarking deep learning\-based reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography with clinically relevant synthetic datasets](../publications/447adea92a0e34c00d5d.md)

Panpan Chen; Refik Mert Çam

Deep learning \(DL\)\-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography \(PACT\) have developed rapidly in recent years\. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality \(IQ\) metrics that may lack clinical relevance\. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT\. A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open\-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL\-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT\. The datasets each include over 11,000 two\-dimensional \(2D\) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity\. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task\-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility\. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework&\#x27;s utility by comparing DL\-based and physics\-based reconstruction methods\. The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL\-based methods\. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions\. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task\-based assessments\. The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL\-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT\. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT\.

## [New approach to training personnel for Russian industry](../publications/44875f687ca8065ed395.md)

Т\.Д\. Ушкац

The article is devo ted to the study of modern approaches to the training of qualified personnel for Russian industry, taking into account the context of the digital economy and technological sovereignty\. The current reforms in higher and secondary vocational education, as well as federal projects and programs focused on practical training and employer involvement in the educational process, are analyzed\. Based on the systematization of data on personnel provision, regional labor market specifics, and existing barriers, recommendations for improving personnel training mechanisms are formulated\. A set of measures is proposed, including the creation of a national digital database of competencies, the development of university alliances and cluster models, as well as methods of long\-term workforce planning\. ## [Agentic Displacement in Second Language Writing: The Acquisitional Consequences of Delegating Writing to Autonomous AI Browsers](../publications/449e1cc3577176151064.md)

Hala Fawzi

Autonomous AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet and Copilot Mode in Microsoft Edge can receive a writing assignment, draft a response, and submit it with little language produced by the learner\. To explain what this means for second language \(L2\) writing, this conceptual paper introduces the term agentic displacement\. Full delegation transfers planning, writing, and revision to the agent, removing opportunities for the learner to produce language and regulate the writing process\. The paper argues that this loss may limit language development\. Delegation is a continuum; the paper traces its extreme, full replacement, through production\-based accounts of acquisition\. No empirical data are reported; the paper offers a framework, five testable propositions, and three dimensions of teacher practice: recognizing displacement, auditing tasks for delegability, and using pedagogical judgment to recover the learning a task was meant to produce\. The central risk is developmental, not only ethical or procedural\.

## [Towards Understanding Tinnitus Symptom Dynamics During Treatment](../publications/44a57997f0955c33988c.md)

Milena Engelke

Tinnitus is defined as the conscious perception of a tonal or composite noise for which there is no identifiable corresponding external sound source\. In its severe form, also referred to as tinnitus disorder, it is accompanied by emotional distress, cognitive dysfunction, and autonomic arousal\. While the percept itself affects approximately 14\.4% of adults, severe tinnitus is present in about 2\.3% of adults and is associated with reduced quality of life, fear, constant awareness, annoyance, concentration difficulties, and mental diseases\. Yet, the substantial heterogeneity in tinnitus phenotypes and aetiologies hinders the development of effective treatments\. Promising treatment outcomes often lack replication, and in many clinical trials, only a subset of patients respond\. Current clinical tinnitus research largely relies on aggregated data collected before and after treatment providing little insight into the temporal dynamics of symptom change\. The ubiquitous use of smartphones makes them well suited for regular symptom monitoring during treatment, which might shed light on unseen symptomatic patterns or dynamics during treatment, which could help to explain treatment heterogeneity\. To date, the potential of methods such as Ecological Momentary Assessment \(EMA\) remains underexplored in clinical tinnitus research\. In this thesis, I explore the potential of daily symptom monitoring across different tinnitus treatments to investigate symptom changes and dynamics\. The introduction first provides a clinical overview of tinnitus, followed by an introduction to EMA, its methodological foundations, and its current applications in health research and tinnitus studies\. The first study examines different analytical methods for quantifying treatment effects using EMA data and compares them with established patient\-reported outcome measures\. The second study investigates in greater detail how clinical improvement manifests in EMA\-derived symptoms and whether patterns of symptom fluctuation can predict treatment effects\. The third study addresses heterogeneity in symptom trajectories using latent class analysis\. In the final section the results are discussed across shared conceptual and methodological themes such as symptom dynamics, methodological innovations in EMA analysis, and the balance between idiographic and nomothetic approaches\.

## [Impact of AI‐Assisted Endoscopy on Secondary Review and Referral Decisions in Gastric Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Real‐World Study](../publications/44b5c65155d11e8c59d4.md)

Sachiyo Onishi; Seiji Adachi; Masahito Shimizu

OBJECTIVES: Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted endoscopy may support gastric cancer screening, but its impact on structured secondary human review remains unclear\. We evaluated secondary review modifications and referral decisions before and after AI implementation\. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 5013 screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy examinations performed before \(n = 2021\) and after \(n = 2992\) AI implementation\. The primary outcome was secondary review modifications\. Secondary outcomes included referral for further diagnostic evaluation\. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, Helicobacter pylori eradication status, prior\-year endoscopy, and endoscopist experience were performed\. Interaction analyses according to endoscopist experience and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses were conducted\. No external reference standard was available to verify secondary\-review modifications or referral decisions\. RESULTS: Secondary review modifications increased from 1\.2% in the pre\-AI period to 3\.7% in the AI period \(p &lt; 0\.01\)\. A significant interaction was observed between AI implementation and endoscopist experience \(p for interaction &lt; 0\.01\), with increased modifications primarily among nonexpert endoscopists\. Cancer\-related modifications remained uncommon but increased after AI implementation \(0\.6% vs\. 0\.2%, p = 0\.04\)\. Referral rates decreased from 4\.9% to 2\.8% \(p &lt; 0\.01\), and AI implementation was independently associated with lower odds of referral \(adjusted OR = 0\.53; 95% confidence interval = 0\.36\-0\.77\)\. CONCLUSIONS: AI\-assisted endoscopy was associated with lower referral rates; however, secondary review modifications persisted after AI implementation, particularly among nonexpert endoscopists\. These findings describe workflow changes and do not establish the clinical validity of the modifications or the appropriateness of referral decisions\.
