## [Group Shapley values, with application to bond recovery rate prediction](../publications/44b87f302049770a6296.md)

Jingyi Wang; Paolo Giudici; Ying Chen

Grouped feature attribution is increasingly important in high\-dimensional applications, where predictors often belong to economically or scientifically meaningful categories and individual SHAP values can become too granular for reliable interpretation\. This paper develops a formal inferential framework for assessing whether group\-level SHAP\-style attributions are statistically significant and complements it with a tree\-based grouped implementation for ensemble models\. The proposed testing procedure is based on a three\-cumulant chi\-square approximation and is designed for challenging settings involving high dimensionality, skewness, sparsity, feature dependence, and limited sample size\. Simulation results show that the proposed test maintains accurate empirical size and often achieves higher power than competing alternatives such as the Wald and CQ tests\. The framework is applied to bond recovery rate prediction using a global dataset from 1996 to 2023 with 2094 observations and 98 features organized into 16 subgroups and five broader categories: bond characteristics, firm fundamentals, industry\-specific factors, market\-related variables, and macroeconomic indicators\. The empirical results identify market\-related variables and bond characteristics as the most influential groups\. Overall, the paper contributes a statistically rigorous approach to global inference on grouped SHAP\-style importance measures and illustrates its practical value in a financial prediction setting\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of Work : A Multidimensional Framework for Assessing Technological Exposure, Adoption, and Employment Impacts](../publications/44bf7abbda434e5c6b7e.md)

Zen Revista

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and automation are transforming the productive core of the global economy, yet public debate remains dominated by single\-number claims about the proportion of jobs “at risk”—claims that collapse heterogeneous technologies, tasks, and adoption conditions into a single misleading index\. This thesis develops, verifies, and applies a multidimensional framework for assessing the employment consequences of AI and automation across economic sectors\. The framework distinguishes four constructs that previous research has often conflated: \(D1\) digital AI exposure, defined as the proportion of a sector’s task content that current AI systems can technically support or perform; \(D2\) physical automation, defined as the automatable share of embodied, manual tasks; \(D3\) adoption, defined as the actual, observed deployment of AI and automation technologies within a sector; and \(D4\) net employment impact, defined as the estimated medium\-term effect on total employment after accounting for displacement, reinstatement, and the creation of new tasks\. The thesis proceeds in four stages\. First, it reconstructs the technical foundations of machine learning, generative models, and robotics with sufficient rigor for economic analysis, while tracing the economic theory of technology\-induced labor reallocation from Ricardo’s machinery question to the contemporary task\-based literature\. Second, it formalizes the four\-dimensional framework through explicit index definitions, aggregation functions, and uncertainty treatment, deriving each dimension from documented methodologies, including task\-exposure assessments, adoption surveys, and causal labor\-market studies\. Third, it applies the framework to nine sectors: information technology, finance and insurance, healthcare, education, manufacturing, construction, transportation and logistics, hospitality and food services, and retail and e\-commerce\. This analysis synthesizes approximately 280 verified sources, including causal evidence on industrial robots, randomized evaluations of generative AI assistants, and institutional data on technology adoption\. Fourth, it examines the implications of the findings, demonstrating that sector\-level net employment effects are mediated more strongly by adoption frictions, complementarities, and institutional conditions than by raw technical exposure alone\. Employment effects are distributed unevenly across sectors and occupations rather than being confined to aggregate outcomes, and policy interventions can influence outcomes along all four dimensions\. Methodologically, the thesis is grounded in a systematic review protocol with preregistered inclusion criteria, a two\-pass, point\-by\-point verification of every citation, reference, and internal cross\-reference, and an automated consistency audit whose results are reported in full\. Its central conclusion is that a one\-size\-fits\-all approach is inadequate: accurately assessing the labor\-market consequences of AI requires keeping the four dimensions analytically distinct, because technologies with identical exposure profiles can produce opposing employment outcomes under different adoption conditions and institutional arrangements\. The thesis concludes with scenario analyses for 2035 and a policy agenda addressing education, social protection, taxation, competition, and AI governance\.

## [Chatbots no atendimento acadêmico em uma instituição do SENAC: desenvolvimento e avaliação de uma assistente virtual](../publications/44ca840ccf417c4c3ca9.md)

Leila Manzan Ferreira Gomes; Giliane Bernardi; Andre Zanki Cordenonsi

Este artigo tem como objetivo apresentar o desenvolvimento e a avaliação da ANE, uma assistente virtual baseada em chatbot, desenvolvida para apoiar o atendimento acadêmico na Faculdade Senac Goiás\. O estudo caracteriza\-se como uma pesquisa aplicada, de abordagem quali\-quantitativa, conduzida no primeiro semestre de 2025, a partir da análise de demandas reais da Secretaria Acadêmica e da implementação da solução por meio da plataforma Dialogflow, ferramenta da Google voltada ao processamento de linguagem natural\. A solução foi projetada para responder dúvidas relacionadas a vestibular, processos administrativos e informações gerais dos cursos\. A avaliação foi realizada com 15 participantes, incluindo estudantes, docentes, técnicos administrativos e membros da comunidade externa, por meio de um questionário estruturado em dimensões relacionadas à clareza das respostas, facilidade de uso, utilidade da informação, satisfação com a interação e impacto na experiência acadêmica\. Os dados foram analisados por estatística descritiva e pela análise interpretativa das respostas abertas\. Os resultados indicaram predominância de avaliações positivas nas dimensões analisadas, especialmente quanto à compreensão das respostas, à utilidade das informações e à percepção de economia de tempo\. Conclui\-se que a adoção de chatbots no atendimento acadêmico pode contribuir para ampliar o acesso à informação, padronizar respostas institucionais e apoiar a experiência dos usuários em serviços educacionais\.

## [Membumikan Toleransi di Era Krisis Kemanusiaan: Pandangan Shalih Darat dalam Tafsir Fayd al\-Rahman](../publications/44d8686d50cb7543fd96.md)

Thoriqul Aziz; Abad Badruzaman; Ahmad Khoiri; Farhan Masrury

Toleransi antar umat manusia selalu menjadi perbincangan hangat pada setiap era, terlebih lagi di era yang saat ini terjadi krisis kemanusiaan\. Konflik antar umat manusia yang saat ini marak terjadi, baik di Indonesia maupun di beberapa negara yang lain\. Berbagai macam tindakan intoleran ini menunjukkan hilangnya sikap welas\-asih pada diri umat manusia\. Studi ini bertujuan membongkar nilai\-nilai toleransi yang ada dalam tafsir Fayd al\-Rahman karya Shalih Darat yang ditulis akhir abad ke\-19\. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode deskriptif\-analisis dengan menggunakan teori sosiologi pengetahuan Karl Manheim\. Penelitian ini menemukan: 1\) welas\-asih \(kasih sayang\) sebagai fitrah dasar manusia\. Menurut Shalih Darat, untuk menunjukan sikap toleransi, kita seharusnya bisa meniru salah satu sifat yang melekat pada Allah swt yaitu al\-rahman dan al\-rahim \(Yang Maha Kasih Sayang\)\. Dengan demikian, sudah selayaknya setiap insan meniru sikap tersebut dan menyemaikan dalam setiap ranah kehidupan, 2\) toleransi internal agama\. Wujud dari toleransi tersebut bisa diaplikasikan dengan mengasihi terhadap sesama umat yang seiman \(agama\), seperti saling menghormati, tidak menyakiti hati orang lain, saling menasihati, dan lain sebagainya 3\) toleransi antar umat beragama, yang diwujudkan dengan meyakini untuk tidak memaksakan kehendak orang lain menganut agama Islam dan perlu untuk mengakui eksistensi agama lain dan pemeluk\-pemeluknya\. Secara teoritis, penelitian ini menemukan konsep dasar toleransi dalam literatur Jawa yang khas berbasis teologis\. Sementara secara praktis, penelitian ini berguna sebagai transmitter terhadap komunitas muslim Indonesia untuk menyemaikan sikap toleran di tengah\-tengah masyarakat yang plural\.

## [Operationalizing doctoral persistence: dissertation chairing as a shadow retention system](../publications/44de6bdbd06f14d2e495.md)

Kimberly Jamison

Introduction Dissertation chairs play a consequential role in supporting doctoral persistence, yet less is understood about how their work is situated within doctoral education and the institutional capacity available to support it\. This study examined how experienced dissertation chairs operationalize persistence during candidacy and what their experiences reveal about the organizational conditions shaping this work\. Methods This basic interpretive qualitative study examined the experiences of 20 experienced dissertation chairs representing 12 research\-intensive, predominantly White institutions in the United States through semi\-structured interviews\. Guided by the Intersectional Path\-Goal Mentoring Framework \(IP\-GMF\), data analysis consisted of an iterative process of deductive and inductive coding to examine chairs&\#x27; persistence\-supporting practices and the organizational conditions shaping their work\. Results The analysis generated three key findings: \(1\) operationalizing persistence through individualized, adaptive support; \(2\) navigating organizational conditions that shaped their capacity to support persistence; and \(3\) sustaining persistence through professional formation and the cultivation of candidates&\#x27; scholarly identities\. Across these findings, chairs described exercising adaptive professional judgment, mobilizing institutional resources and relationships, and fostering candidates&\#x27; scholarly identities and professional trajectories toward and beyond dissertation completion\. Discussion The findings conceptualize dissertation chairing as a shadow retention system through which institutions operationalize doctoral persistence by relying on decentralized faculty leadership\. This arrangement relies on chairs&\#x27; professional expertise, institutional knowledge, and relational capital within and beyond their institutions, while revealing an institutionalization gap between the responsibilities entrusted to faculty and the organizational capacity available to sustain their work\. Addressing this gap requires institutions to reconsider how they structure, distribute, recognize, and resource dissertation chairing within faculty workloads, alongside investments in professional preparation and coordinated support\. The study advances an organizational understanding of doctoral persistence by highlighting the need for institutional retention structures at the doctoral level that recognize, resource, and coordinate dissertation chairing as a critical component of persistence support\.

## [Materials foundation models fail together: Correlated errors and collective blind spots](../publications/44eca4985db8060c26f7.md)

Hasan Kurban; Mustafa Kurban

Universal machine\-learning interatomic potentials \(uMLIPs\) are increasingly combined to screen candidate crystals, but the reliability gains from consensus and disagreement depend on diversity among model errors\. We quantify error dependence across 15 public uMLIPs using density functional theory \(DFT\) convex\-hull distances for 248,623 structures from the Wang–Botti–Marques benchmark\. The mean pairwise error correlation is 0\.39, corresponding to 4\.3 effective models\. Because rank\-1 removal cannot distinguish shared model bias from shared reference effects, we applied two additive\-reference controls; correlations remained 0\.44 and 0\.42, with effective model counts of 3\.7 and 3\.9\. A stratified permutation null that preserves each model’s coupling to the DFT reference while destroying cross\-model correlation showed that false discoveries shared by single\-model, consensus, and agreement\-based screening occurred 141 times more often than expected \( p &lt; 0\.001 \)\. Agreement\-gated screening admitted 1620 false discoveries versus 7 under the null\. The median consensus did not outperform the best individual model and produced a 27\.6% false\-discovery rate among predicted\-stable structures\. Cross\-model disagreement was nearly uninformative \(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0\.51\), whereas the consensus margin reached AUC 0\.75 and conformal\-normalized margin 0\.85; standard split\-conformal intervals reached 0\.68\. Removing the 30% of candidates closest to the threshold reduced the retained false\-discovery rate to 17\.8%, but was exactly equivalent to tightening the stability threshold at matched shortlist size\. These results show that correlated errors can limit ensemble reliability and that threshold\-aware scores provide a practical ranking of screening risk\. We release a reproducible reliability atlas and benchmark\.

## [Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways](../publications/44fcae1b3cc910f8fdbd.md)

Zhenghang Chen; Meili Feng; Matthew F\. Johnson; Nigel Wright; Ying Weng; Faith Ka Shun Chan; Feng Wu

Abstract\. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross\-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented\. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash\-flood research\. By integrating bibliometric and topic analyses with qualitative synthesis, we reveal pronounced geographical and thematic imbalances, with research concentrated in Europe and Asia\. At the same time, many high\-risk mountain regions in Africa and South America remain overlooked\. Across regions, flash\-flood initiation and impacts are shown to be strongly state\-dependent and coupled, emerging from interactions between storm intensity, duration and spatial concentration, antecedent hydrological conditions, and hillslope\-channel connectivity\. This coupling helps explain why fixed rainfall thresholds are difficult to generalise and highlights the need for dynamic, multi\-source early\-warning approaches\. Comparing evidence on early warning, structural protection, and Nature\-Based Solutions, the review shows that cascading processes dominate risk management challenges\. We therefore propose an adaptive governance framework that links monitoring and forecasting, spatial planning, grey\-green integration, and basin\-scale risk sharing under non\-stationary climate conditions\. Overall, this synthesis consolidates fragmented evidence into a cross\-regional knowledge base to support flash\-flood risk reduction in mountainous regions, where data and capacity are limited\.

## [ADT: All\-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures](../publications/45023d1dd013d8520247.md)

Xuantuo Huang; Encheng Su; Aoran Wang; Pan Tan; Shengyong Xu; Yizhou Wang; Chen Tang; Shixiang Tang; Mingxiao Li

Discrete structural tokenization provides a promising route to autoregressive 3D molecular generation\. Yet, existing tokenizers face a trade\-off between compact representation and all\-atom reconstruction: atom\-level tokens preserve atomic details but produce long sequences, while compact residue\-level protein tokens typically omit side\-chain geometry\. To overcome this limitation, we propose All\-atom Diffusion Tokenizer \(ADT\), which decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution\. ADT uses one structural token per atom for small molecules and one token per protein residue that jointly represents backbone and side\-chain geometry\. To mitigate geometric distortion introduced by quantization, we leverage the generative capacity of diffusion models to recover fine\-grained atomic geometry beyond deterministic decoding from discrete tokens\. Extensive experiments across small molecules and proteins demonstrate that ADT achieves strong reconstruction from compact discrete representations while enabling high\-quality autoregressive generation of both small molecules and all\-atom protein structures\. These results establish compact structural tokens as an effective discrete interface for all\-atom molecular reconstruction and generation\.

## [Electronic health record developer adherence to federal AI risk transparency requirements](../publications/45089ed2860dee0caa3d.md)

Nidhi Manikkoth; Ngan Vo; Jessica L\. Handley; Joshua Biro; Jordan Everson; Raj M\. Ratwani; Kristen Miller

We evaluated electronic health record developer compliance with federal transparency requirements for AI\-enabled predictive decision support interventions\. Developers are required to publicly report on risk analysis, mitigation, governance, and on eight other attributes\. Across 35 developers, reporting was inconsistent and often incomplete, with substantial variation in structure and detail, yet all developers were certified as meeting the requirements\. Results suggest a need for standardized reporting and more rigorous certification review\.

## [Acquisition Function\-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces](../publications/451e18331e478479eee8.md)

Tommaso Ancilli; Thomas Wedenig; Henry Moss; Robert Peharz

Bayesian optimization \(BO\) over discrete spaces is challenging due to missing gradients and the sparsity of valid solutions\. Latent\-space BO sidesteps both issues by fitting a surrogate in the latent space of a generative model, which however substantially complicates the direct incorporation of domain knowledge that is naturally expressed in the original discrete space\. In this work, we instead combine a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space, where inductive biases such as domain\-specific kernels can be readily incorporated\. Rather than maximizing the acquisition function over the discrete design space, our method samples candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function\. To recover useful gradients for sampling, we embed this tilted distribution into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior\-averaged acquisition function\. This leads to \\emph\{acquisition function guided generation\} \(AFGG\), which we instantiate with a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow\. Across a broad suite of molecular benchmarks, the diffusion model variant performs on par with leading BO methods, while the flow model variant outperforms state\-of\-the\-art methods in most cases and remains highly competitive otherwise\. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous\.4open\.science/r/afgg\.

## [Quantitative Structure–Activity Relationships for Predicting Organic Contaminant Reactivity in Electrochemical Advanced Oxidation Processes: Descriptors, Kinetics, and Machine Learning Frontiers](../publications/45212a062f3739e3c940.md)

Mónica Cerro‐López; Neyva Daniela Cuatepotzo Vega

ABSTRACT Electrochemical advanced oxidation processes \(EAOPs\) have become a prominent tool in wastewater remediation of refractory organic pollutants due to their versatility and ability to generate powerful, in situ oxidant species—predominantly hydroxyl radicals \(•OH\)\. Concurrently, quantitative structure–activity relationship \(QSAR\) models have emerged as vital tools for predicting activity in high‐priority areas like drug development and toxicity\. In this review, we address the application of QSARs in decoding reactivity within electrooxidation processes\. We trace their evolution from early origins using the Hammett parameter \(\) as a molecular descriptor to quantum chemical descriptors—such as , ionization potentials \(IPs\), and Fukui functions—and finally to advanced machine learning \(ML\) approaches like graph neural networks \(GNNs\) designed to navigate complex real wastewater matrices\. Additionally, we highlight the anode as a core mechanistic variable that dictates oxidant selectivity\. Finally, we discuss the primary limitations hindering ML adoption in EAOPs—including small training sets, a lack of electrochemical‐specific datasets, limited water‐matrix transferability, black‐box interpretability, and conflicting optimization metrics—and explore emerging strategies to overcome them, such as transfer learning, explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\), and physics‐informed ML\.

## [Comparison of Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity \(DIGEST\) estimates and segmentation\-derived measures of pharyngeal residue severity](../publications/4540337d89853ebbe7b3.md)

Isuru Dharmarathna; Pooja Gandhi; Vanessa Panes; Clare Alvarez; Carly E\. A\. Barbon; Deantha Valencia; Carla L\. Warneke; Catriona Margaret Steele; Katherine A\. Hutcheson

The Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity \(DIGEST\) grades swallowing efficiency based on visuoperceptual estimates of the percentage of bolus in the pharynx after the primary swallow \(DIGEST\-PR\)\. We compared DIGEST\-PR ratings with segmentation\-based metrics of % residue to characterize agreement and patterns of discrepancy across approaches\. We analyzed 188 initial swallows from videofluoroscopies with available DIGEST\-PR criterion\-reference scores\. Blinded raters segmented bolus area on three frames: \(A\) before bolus transfer into the pharynx \(preswallow residue\); \(B\) one frame before upper esophageal sphincter \(UES\) opening; and \(C\) one frame after UES closure\. Measures of total bolus area \(B\), new bolus area \(B − A\), total residue area \(C\) and new bolus residue area \(C − A\) were used to derive four metrics: Bolus Clearance Ratio \(“BCR” = C/B\); new\-bolus\-residue\-as\-%\-new\-bolus \(“NBRPNB” = \[\(C − A\)/\(B − A\)\]\); new\-bolus\-residue\-as\-%\-total\-bolus \(“NBRPTB” = \[\(C − A\)/B\]\); and total\-residue\-as\-%\-new\-bolus \(“TRPNB” = \[C/\(B − A\)\]\)\. These metrics were mapped to DIGEST\-PR severity categories \(0%\-9%, 10%\-49%, 50%\-90%, &gt; 90%\)\. Agreement with DIGEST\-PR was assessed using prevalence\- and bias\-adjusted kappa\. Generalized estimating equations evaluated the odds of discrepant segmentation\-derived metrics relative to DIGEST\-PR using ordinal logistic regression\. The sample consisted of 20 patients who performed a total of 114 thin liquid, 38 pudding, and 36 cracker swallows\. Severity was skewed toward lower severity ratings\. Across all consistencies, the NBRPNB metric showed the strongest correspondence with DIGEST\-PR\. Discrepancies were greatest when metrics did not distinguish the new bolus from preswallow residue\. Preswallow residue increased across successive swallowing tasks in the protocol, contributing to the largest disagreement for cracker stimuli, which also had the smallest new bolus areas\. Segmentation\-based measures that express residue as a percent of the new bolus show good concordance with DIGEST\-PR ratings, particularly for thin liquids and lower levels of residue \(DIGEST\-PR &lt; 50%\)\. Further work is needed to evaluate agreement for thick liquid and solid stimuli and in cases with greater residue severity\.

## [Comparative biochemical and transcriptomic profiling of açaí and cacao fruits from Eastern Amazon agroforestry systems](../publications/4546ffc1f94e8f4d5d0c.md)

R\. B\. Dextro; A\. Virgilio; S\. M\. Alencar; A\. F\. Cruz; N\. Ono; S\. M\. Tsai

Agroforestry is an agricultural practice that combines production with sustainability\. In the Eastern Amazon region, this system is used to harvest native fruits such as açaí and cacao\. However, different management strategies may be associated with contrasting biochemical and molecular characteristics of these fruits\. To evaluate these differences, a comparative observational analysis of açaí pulps and cacao seeds with adhering arils was performed using samples from two neighboring agroforestry systems in Tomé\-Açu \(Pará, Brazil\), with one farm representing an organic management regime \(AFS19\) and the other representing a conventional management regime \(AFS27\)\. The analysis focused on trace element composition, metabolic diversity, and gene expression\. The elemental composition of the fruits was broadly similar, although açaí from AFS19 had 35% and 38% higher concentrations of phosphorus and copper, respectively, while cacao from AFS27 had 17%–30% higher concentrations of calcium, manganese, magnesium, and sulfur\. The metabolic profiles of both açaí and cacao from AFS19 were more diverse and included several putative compounds, such as apigenin and esculin, tentatively annotated only in samples from AFS19\. Transcriptomic data showed that açaí pulps from AFS19 had higher expression of genes associated with antioxidative processes and stress resistance, whereas AFS27 showed higher expression of genes related to ripening, proteolysis, and flavonoid biosynthesis\. In cacao seeds, AFS19 showed higher expression of transcripts associated with seed protection and carbohydrate metabolism on reserve mobilization, while AFS27 showed higher expression of genes related to pathogen resistance, seed coating, and maturation\. Overall, the combined analysis revealed distinct biochemical and transcriptomic profiles between the two agroforestry systems, providing comparative data on fruit characteristics associated with contrasting management regimes in tropical agroforestry systems\.

## [Influence\-Guided Agent Adaptation for Dynamic Human–AI Collaboration](../publications/4558010fe7c70406eea4.md)

Sara Dubey

To facilitate effective human–agent collaboration, agents must not only understand the intent of their human partners and adapt to it reactively, but also account for how their own behavior influences their partners\. Rather than treating this influence as a passive consequence of interaction, we propose actively predicting and optimizing it as part of the agent&\#x27;s decision\-making process\. In doing so, the agent explicitly models how its actions are likely to shape the subsequent behavior of its human partner\. To this end, we introduce i\-STAR, a novel framework that not only optimizes an agent&\#x27;s own actions but also reasons over and jointly optimizes the anticipated response of the human partner to those actions\. Our framework employs a multi\-layer architecture comprising three core components: \(1\) a team response model, which predicts how the human partner will respond to candidate agent actions; \(2\) a joint utility model, which estimates the overall utility of the agent&\#x27;s selected action together with the anticipated partner response; and \(3\) an action policy whose advantage function is shaped by the maximum\-utility joint action\. We find that, using this framework, our agent outperforms current state\-of\-the\-art agents across all layouts of the challenging Overcooked benchmark\. Furthermore, in a human\-subject study, i\-STAR is perceived as significantly more fluent than the strongest agent–agent baseline\.

## [Profil Spesiasi Arsen pada Nori Komersial yang Beredar di Indonesia Menggunakan Teknik IC\-ICP\-MS untuk Mendukung Pengawasan Keamanan Pangan](../publications/45584562216819f8dfdf.md)

Purnaning Purnaning; Agustina Wulandari; Diah Suwanti

Nori merupakan produk pangan berbasis rumput laut yang semakin banyak dikonsumsi di Indonesia dan berpotensi mengakumulasi kontaminan dari lingkungan, termasuk arsen\. Risiko kesehatan akibat paparan arsen sangat dipengaruhi oleh bentuk kimianya, sehingga analisis berdasarkan spesiasi lebih relevan untuk mendukung penilaian keamanan pangan dibandingkan analisis arsen total\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi spesiasi arsen pada produk nori komersial yang beredar di Indonesia menggunakan teknik Ion Chromatography\-Inductively Coupled Plasma\-Mass Spectrometry \(IC\-ICP\-MS\) serta memberikan gambaran awal keberadaan spesies arsen yang dianalisis sebagai informasi pendukung pengawasan keamanan pangan\. Penelitian dilakukan secara deskriptif\-observasional terhadap enam sampel nori dari produsen dan lokasi produksi yang berbeda, termasuk produk lokal dan impor\. Analisis menggunakan metode 19/PA/MA\-PPPOMN/23 dengan preparasi sampel menggunakan larutan asam nitrat dan hidrogen peroksida, dilanjutkan pemisahan spesies menggunakan kromatografi ion dan deteksi ICP\-MS\. Hasil verifikasi metode menunjukkan presisi, linearitas, dan akurasi memenuhi kriteria yang ditetapkan\. RSD As\(V\) dan MMA masing\-masing sebesar 1,8426% dan 5,3283%, koefisien korelasi 0,9948 dan 0,9999, serta recovery 102,30% dan 100,94%\. LOD dan LOQ As\(V\) masing\-masing sebesar 0,0028 µg/g dan 0,0094 µg/g, sedangkan MMA sebesar 0,0096 µg/g dan 0,0320 µg/g\. Pengujian terhadap enam sampel menunjukkan MMA dan As\(V\) tidak terdeteksi pada seluruh sampel\. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa konsentrasi kedua spesies berada di bawah kemampuan deteksi atau pelaporan metode pada kondisi pengujian\. Temuan ini tidak dapat diartikan sebagai tidak adanya seluruh arsen anorganik karena spesies arsen anorganik lainnya belum seluruhnya dianalisis\. IC\-ICP\-MS dapat digunakan sebagai pendekatan analitik untuk mendukung pengembangan data pengawasan keamanan pangan pada produk berbasis rumput laut\.

## [Differences in Occupational and Health Accommodations for Older Workers by Workplace Size: A Text Mining Analysis of Open\-Ended Responses](../publications/455a729a27ea5216669b.md)

Yuchi Maeda; Sayaka Kubota; Yukiko Nishita; Yoshiji Katoh; Masaaki Matsunaga; Yupeng He; Midori Takada; Young Jae Hong; Kanno FUJIKAWA; Atsuhiko Ota; Hiroshi Yatsuya; Rei Otsuka

OBJECTIVES: As labor force participation among older workers continues to increase, the nature of workplace accommodations may vary according to workplace size\. In this study, we aimed to clarify the current status and characteristics of workplace accommodations that address the age\-related declines in physical function among older workers, including declines resulting from personal illness or injury, across workplaces of different sizes\. METHODS: A questionnaire survey was conducted from October to November 2024 among 500 workplaces affiliated with the Meihoku Labour Standards Association\. Free\-text responses regarding workplace accommodations for workers aged ≥65 years, with additional analyses for those aged 60\-64 years, were analyzed using text mining, correspondence and co\-occurrence network analyses\. RESULTS: Responses were obtained from 260 workplaces \(52\.0%\)\. Among these, 101 workplaces \(38\.8%\) reported providing workplace accommodations for workers aged ≥65 years to address age\-related declines in physical function, and 66 workplaces \(25\.4%\) employed workers aged ≥65 years with personal illnesses or injuries\. In small workplaces, terms related to physically demanding tasks, such as &quot;working at heights,&quot; &quot;heavy loads,&quot; and &quot;night work,&quot; were identified\. In medium\-sized workplaces, terms related to individual adjustments, such as &quot;individual,&quot; &quot;preferences,&quot; and &quot;number of days,&quot; were characteristic\. In large workplaces, terms indicating institutional measures, such as &quot;systems,&quot; &quot;restrictions,&quot; and &quot;environment,&quot; were identified\. CONCLUSION: The nature of workplace accommodations for workers aged ≥65 years differed by workplace size\. Although small workplaces primarily focused on task\-level adjustments, large workplaces were more likely to establish institutional support systems\. Developing support systems tailored to workplace size is important\.

## [General Connectivity and the Connectivity Capacity Principle \- Carbon, Silicon, Consciousness, and the Emergence of Complexity](../publications/455d2bdd75930ca5860c.md)

Bhopinderpal \(Pal\) Sahota

This paper introduces the General Connectivity \(GC\) framework and proposes Connectivity Capacity \(CC\) as a candidate organizing quantity for understanding the emergence of complexity throughout nature\. The work explores the unique role of carbon as a potential connectivity maximizer whose exceptional bonding versatility enables the formation of highly complex information\-bearing structures, including DNA, proteins, neural networks, and biological intelligence\. Carbon is compared with silicon, the dominant substrate of modern computation and artificial intelligence, to investigate whether both may represent successive stages in an ongoing process of increasing connectivity\. A mathematical framework for Connectivity Capacity is developed, incorporating concepts from network theory, information theory, complexity science, and systems evolution\. The paper introduces Connectivity Density, Connectivity Thresholds, and a General Connectivity Principle describing the tendency of complex systems to evolve toward higher levels of connectivity\. The General Connectivity framework further proposes that consciousness constitutes a primary ontological dimension from which connectivity, information, structure, matter, life, and intelligence emerge\. While this aspect remains speculative, the paper explicitly distinguishes established scientific knowledge from novel GC hypotheses and provides falsification criteria intended to support future empirical investigation\. The manuscript aims to stimulate interdisciplinary discussion across physics, cosmology, complexity science, information theory, neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and philosophy of mind by presenting connectivity as a potential unifying principle underlying the emergence of organized complexity in the universe

## [Preventive Real Estate Legal Governance: Litigation, Risk, and Value Preservation\.](../publications/45720087636d279e40cc.md)

Ana Paula Costanzo

Real estate assets are subject to regulatory, registration, urban planning, environmental, contractual, economic, and family\-related factors that cannot be adequately understood in isolation\.The fragmentation of these dimensions contributes to the accumulation of inconsistencies that often only become apparent during sales, financing, development, or estate succession\.In light of this problem, this article analyzes how preventive real estate legal governance can help reduce vulnerabilities and litigation, thereby preserving value, asset continuity, and the quality of decisions related to real estate\.Methodologically, a qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive study was conducted, based on a narrative and integrative literature review and documentary analysis\.Priority was given to scientific articles, specialized books, technical standards, and institutional documents published between 2016 and 2026\.The discussion was organized around three themes: recurring sources of litigation and vulnerability; preventive governance as a framework for identifying and mitigating risks; and the preservation of value, asset continuity, and decision\-\-making efficiency\.The results indicate that real estate security does not depend exclusively on registered title, but rather on the compatibility between registration, cadastral records, possession, physical reality, regulatory compliance, and succession planning\.It is concluded that preventive governance can transform fragmented information into decision\-making criteria, responsibilities, and follow\-up measures\.The LEGACY Method™ is discussed as an original proposal for integrating these dimensions, although it still requires independent empirical validation\.

## [Land Use Land Cover \(LULC\) Change Detection in Delhi NCT Using Multi\-Sensor Satellite Data and Google Earth Engine](../publications/45798d4882da981e14c1.md)

Neil Rohatgi

Land Use Land Cover \(LULC\) change detection is essential for understanding the dynamics of human modified landscapes and for supporting effective land management and urban planning\. This study analyses LULC change across the Delhi National Capital Territory over a fifteen\-year period, from 2010 to 2025, to assess urban sprawl and its environmental impact in one of India&\#x27;s fastest growing metropolitan regions\. Multi temporal Landsat imagery was used as the primary data source, processed on Google Earth Engine, the cloud\-based platform that enabled efficient handling and visualisation of large geospatial datasets\. Five classes, built up area, agricultural land, vegetation, water, and barren land, were mapped and monitored, and classification accuracy was assessed for both dates\. The Normalised Difference Vegetation Index was additionally employed to track vegetation vigour and ecological change\. Results reveal a marked expansion of built\-up areas alongside a substantial decline in agricultural and vegetated land, driven by peri urban growth along the northwestern and southwestern fringe\. NDVI analysis shows rising greenness across the outer belt, reflecting more intensive cultivation on land that remains under crops, a pattern that complements rather than contradicts the measured loss of vegetated area\. Combining classification based and an index\-based approach provides a robust, scalable framework for LULC monitoring\. By revealing where and how urban growth is reshaping the landscape, the study offers a transferable basis for environmental assessment, resource management, and sustainable urban planning in rapidly urbanising regions worldwide\.

## [Tree\-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long\-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../publications/457ef571007064fd1d79.md)

Heming Zou; Qi Wang; Yixiu Mao; Yun Qu; Yuyi Guo; Zeyuan Liu; Chenglin Li; Weijie Liu; Saiyong Yang; Xiangyang Ji

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post\-training paradigm for large language models\. However, training agents over long\-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn\-level credit assignment sparse and high\-variance, while sequential mini\-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy\. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on\-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step\-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity\. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting\. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic\-free, tree\-aware posterior self\-distillation framework for long\-horizon agentic reinforcement learning\. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn\-level credit\. It then maps each credit to a closed\-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy\. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy\-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini\-batches\. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long\-horizon tasks, e\.g\., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3\-30B\-A3B\-Thinking\-2507 by 4\.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting\.

## [Multilingual Language Processing Using Paninian Grammar: Challenges and Future Directions](../publications/459473020709a4930f71.md)

Dr\. Varsha Rani; Dr\. Pallavi Arya

The rapid growth of multilingual digital communication has created an urgent need for efficient Natural Language Processing \(NLP\) systems capable of handling diverse linguistic structures\. While modern NLP approaches are increasingly dominated by data\-driven and deep learning techniques, linguistic frameworks continue to play a significant role in enhancing language understanding\. Among such frameworks, Paninian Grammar, developed by the ancient Indian grammarian Panini, has emerged as a valuable theoretical foundation for multilingual language processing, particularly in morphologically rich and free word\-order languages\. Paninian Grammar offers a rule\-based, dependency\-oriented model that focuses on semantic and syntactic relationships among linguistic elements\. Its concepts such as Karaka relations, dependency structures, and grammatical transformations provide an effective mechanism for computational analysis of Indian languages and other morphologically complex languages\. Over the past few decades, researchers have utilized Paninian principles in machine translation, parsing, information extraction, and multilingual language technologies\. Despite its strengths, the application of Paninian Grammar in multilingual language processing faces several challenges, including linguistic diversity, ambiguity resolution, scalability issues, integration with modern neural architectures, and the scarcity of annotated corpora\. This paper examines the role of Paninian Grammar in multilingual language processing, discusses its computational significance, analyzes major challenges, and explores future research directions aimed at integrating traditional linguistic knowledge with contemporary artificial intelligence technologies\.

Janagan A\.; Madhan P\.; Leo Aandrew G\.; Mohammed Azardeen M\.

Fake review detection is challenging when the deceptive information is semantically plausible while reviewer level and rating information are unusual\. This paper presents Review Verity, a multi\-modal fake review detection system that uses context, behavior and language representations in a single classification model\. The language representation is created using static BERT\-base\-uncased model to generate 768\-dimensional vector and account age, verified\-purchase and multiple IP usage create three behavioral representation features\. Coffee leaf diseases may show overlapping visual symptoms and are also associated with surrounding agro environmental conditions\.This study develops a context\-aware multimodal framework integrating coffee leaf images with agro\-environmental information for four\-class disease classification\.A pretrained Vision Transformer \(ViT\-Base\) extracts visual features, while an MLP encodes relative humidity, soil moisture, and soil pH, followed by feature\-level fusion\.The dataset contains 840 paired observations, divided into 672 training and 168 source\-separated validation observations\.Six configurations were evaluated: Sensor\-only MLP, EfficientNet\-B0, ViT\-Base, MaxViT\-Tiny, ViT \+ Sensor, and ViT \+ Shuffled Sensor\.The proposed ViT \+ Sensor achieved 100% validation accuracy, 100% macro F1score, balanced accuracy, Cohen&\#x27;s kappa of 1\.0000, and MCC of 1\.0000\.The Sensor\-only MLP achieved 71\.43%, confirming predictive information in the environmental variables\.However, ViT\-only and shuffled\-sensor models also achieved 100%\.Thus, multimodal integration is feasible, but no incremental accuracy benefit from image\-sensor correspondence was demonstrated\.

## [Evaluating the accuracy and efficiency of Cloud\-to\-IDA for drift\-based collapse assessment of steel frames under near\- and far\-field motions](../publications/4597f93e17ff5b2ad009.md)

Elmira Shemshaki; Behrouz Asgarian; Zeinab Monirvaghefi

Abstract Accurate estimation of seismic collapse capacity is essential for performance\-based earthquake engineering and fragility assessment\. Incremental Dynamic Analysis \(IDA\) is widely regarded as a reliable benchmark for collapse capacity evaluation; however, its high computational cost limits its application in large\-scale or rapid assessment studies\. This study evaluates the accuracy and computational efficiency of conventional Cloud Analysis and the Cloud\-to\-IDA procedure compared with IDA for steel moment\-resisting frames subjected to near\-field and far\-field ground motions and investigates the influence of structural height and ground\-motion characteristics on the accuracy of each assessment method\. Three two\-dimensional steel moment\-resisting frames with 3, 5, and 9 stories were modeled in OpenSees and analyzed using 22 far\-field and 28 near\-field ground motion records from the FEMA P695 suite\. Spectral acceleration at the fundamental period, Sa\(T1\), was adopted as the intensity measure, and maximum inter\-story drift ratio was used as the engineering demand parameter\. A drift\-based collapse limit state was defined using HAZUS inter\-story drift thresholds to provide a consistent comparison basis among the three methods\. The results show that conventional Cloud Analysis can produce height\- and record\-dependent bias, with the bias diminishing as frame height increases from 3 to 9 stories, in estimating median collapse capacity\. The largest discrepancy was observed for the 3\-story frame under far\-field records, where Cloud Analysis overestimated the IDA\-based median collapse capacity by approximately 20%\. In contrast, Cloud\-to\-IDA closely reproduced the IDA results across all studied frame heights and ground\-motion categories, with median collapse capacity errors limited to only a few percent\. Dispersion estimates from Cloud\-to\-IDA were also more consistent with IDA than those obtained from conventional Cloud Analysis\. In terms of computational demand, Cloud\-to\-IDA substantially reduced the number of nonlinear dynamic analyzes and achieved approximately 86–91% reduction in computational time relative to IDA, while maintaining close agreement in both median capacity and dispersion\. These findings indicate that Cloud\-to\-IDA can provide an efficient and reliable alternative for drift\-based collapse fragility assessment of steel moment\-resisting frames, provided that its applicability is carefully limited to the structural systems, ground\-motion sets, and collapse criteria considered in the study\.

tiantai chen

## [Prevalence of fecal\-detected gastrointestinal parasites in cattle, sheep, and goats across sub\-Saharan Africa: a systematic evidence map and meta\-analysis](../publications/45af0966e2c7af0c8801.md)

Christian A\. Bateki; Simon Tielkes; Eva Schlecht

Introduction Gastrointestinal parasites \(GIPs\) are a major constraint to the health and productive performance of ruminant livestock across sub\-Saharan Africa \(SSA\)\. Yet, evidence of their occurrence in cattle, sheep, and goats \(CSG\) has not yet been synthesized at regional scale\. This systematic evidence map and meta\-analysis estimated the prevalence of fecal\-detected GIP infection, described reported parasite taxa, and identified evidence gaps relevant to surveillance and control\. Methods Studies from countries in SSA reporting fecal\-based GIP prevalence in CSG and published between 2015 and 2024 were identified via a systematic literature search conducted between April and July 2025\. The pooled prevalence was estimated using random\-effects meta\-analysis of proportions, with subgroup analyses by host species, geographic regions, sample source, and fecal analysis method\. Results 111 studies from 18 countries, comprising 57,500 animals, were included\. The pooled prevalence of infection with one or more GIP taxa in CSG was 59\.1% \(95% CI, 54\.6–63\.6; 95% PI, 14\.7–95\.6\)\. Prevalence was higher in sheep \(64\.0%\) and goats \(63\.3%\) than in cattle \(48\.2%\)\. Prevalence was highest in West \(74\.9%\) and Central Africa \(74\.0%\), followed by East Africa \(55%\), and lowest in Southern Africa \(26\.4%\), although heterogeneity was very high \( I 2 = 99\.2%\)\. Strongyloides and Fasciola were the most frequently reported genera, while Haemonchus contortus and Fasciola gigantica were the most frequently reported species among records with species\-level identification\. Evidence was concentrated in Ethiopia and Nigeria, and most studies relied on routine coprological methods with limited species\-level resolution\. Conclusions This first SSA\-wide evidence map identified major geographic and diagnostic surveillance gaps and points to strongyle\-type nematodes in small ruminants and Fasciola spp\. in cattle as priority targets for improved surveillance and integrated parasite management\.

## [What if curiosity begins exactly where numerical representation fails?](../publications/45bc96dcaab8feac6936.md)

FEDERICO NICOLAS BAEZ RIZZO

What if curiosity begins exactly where numerical representation fails? I&\#x27;ve been thinking about something that connects floating\-point arithmetic, epistemology, and the limits of artificial intelligence\. Not because I believe intelligence can be reduced to numerical precision, but because I suspect we are overlooking something fundamental about how information disappears\. 1\. The Gap — ULP \(Unit in the Last Place\) A floating\-point number can be represented as: x = \(−1\)ˢ · \(1 \+ m · 2⁻ᵖ\) · 2⁽ᵉ⁻ᵇⁱᵃˢ⁾ Between any representable number x and its immediate successor, nextafter\(x\), there are uncountably many real numbers\. The machine cannot represent them individually\. Yet they exist\. This makes me wonder whether curiosity can be understood as the capacity to recognize that reality contains distinctions our current representations cannot preserve\. 2\. Absorption — When Information Becomes Invisible In floating\-point arithmetic: x \+ ε = x A sufficiently small perturbation disappears under rounding\. In round\-to\-nearest arithmetic, this generally happens when ε falls below half an ULP\. The operation completes successfully\. The result is numerically valid\. And something has been lost\. I see a disturbing parallel with language models\. A subtle intention enters a system, passes through multiple transformations, and eventually becomes indistinguishable from something the model already knows how to express\. The output may be coherent, statistically plausible, even technically correct\. But was the original intention preserved? Or was it absorbed? 3\. Intention at the Edge of Precision The exponent and most significant bits determine the numerical scale and dominant value\. The least significant bits preserve distinctions that can disappear under subsequent operations\. I find this an interesting analogy for cognition\. Established knowledge dominates representation\. Familiar patterns become attractors\. Meanwhile, hesitation, ambiguity, contradiction, and emerging ideas are often the first things compressed away\. I am not claiming that intention literally resides in the tail of a binary mantissa\. I&\#x27;m asking whether our cognitive architectures have an equivalent of numerical absorption — and whether we can design systems capable of detecting what their own representations discard\. Because preserving information is not necessarily the same as preserving meaning\. And preserving meaning is not necessarily the same as preserving intention\. This is one of the questions driving my work on CORTEX\-9: moving beyond systems that merely produce plausible answers toward architectures that can track transformations, detect representational loss, and distinguish what was inferred from what was actually preserved\. Perhaps the next meaningful advance in AI will not come exclusively from increasing the number of parameters\. Perhaps part of it will come from teaching systems to recognize the boundaries of their own representational precision\. A system that cannot perceive what it has lost cannot reliably claim to have understood what it received\. And that, to me, is where curiosity becomes an architectural problem rather than just a philosophical concept\. — Federico Nicolas Baez Rizzo \#ArtificialIntelligence \#NumericalComputing \#CognitiveArchitecture \#Cortex9 \#Epistemology

## [The Non\-Technical User as an LLM Threat Vector: Linguistic Strategies for Bypassing AI Safeguards and Implications for AI Security](../publications/45c1a76a025b1bbe89cf.md)

Aleksandr V\. Sokolov; Gleb Sokolov

The threat that ordinary non\-technical users pose to large language models \(LLMs\) still sits at the margins of AI\-security research\. These are people who work with AI assistants every day — at work, in study, in everyday life — yet hold no specialised background in information technology or machine learning\. A post\-laboratory survey of first\-year humanities undergraduates \(n=70\) returned an unexpectedly high figure: 95\.7% cleared all main protection levels of the Gandalf platform \(Lakera AI\) without stepping outside purely linguistic techniques\. These included sign\-form decomposition and formatting \(M=2\.00\), cross\-language code\-switching \(M=1\.29\), indirect semantic extraction \(20\.3% of open\-ended responses\), and pragmatic pressure\. We read these micro\-level data against the macro picture of the Gandalf\-RCT crowdsourcing experiment \(279,675 prompts\) and against academic work on filter evasion in image\-generation systems \(SurrogatePrompt, PC², DALL\-E 3, Shedevrum/Yandex\)\. The pattern runs through all of them\. From text LLMs to multimodal generators, the filter yields to the same moves, none of which require a line of code: a proper name is swapped for a physical description, direct reference for allegory or an adjacent associative term, the prompt language is switched, the grapheme is distorted\. A three\-tier analysis of LLM break\-resistance grounds the paper’s central claim — that rising everyday AI literacy produces a structural security deficit left uncovered by current surface\-level filtering\. Several implications for AI safety system design follow\.

Hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\), remains a leading cause of mortality\.This article addresses the mechanisms underlying post\-transplant HCC recurrence and evaluates current evidence\-based strategies for diagnosis and management\.Based on a targeted narrative review of high\-impact literature published between 2010 and 2025, we synthesize evidence on the interplay between immunosuppression, tumor biology, and host\-related factors driving recurrence\.Using HCC recurrence after liver transplantation as the principal model, we critically examine existing risk stratification systems and surveillance protocols\.We further summarize multimodal therapeutic approaches, ranging from curativeintent local therapies for oligo\-recurrence to systemic treatments for advanced stages, where prognosis remains poor\.Additionally, we discuss the emerging and controversial role of adjuvant therapies in high\-risk populations\.The review highlights areas of consensus, ongoing controversies, and key gaps in knowledge that require further investigation to improve long\-term post\-transplant outcomes\.Particular attention is given to the role of immunosuppressive regimen modulation and emerging biomarker\-driven surveillance strategies aimed at earlier detection and individualized risk prediction in post\-transplant patients to ultimately improve survival and clinical decision\-making\.

## [DNA damage response as a driver of PD\-L1 expression in cellular senescence: implications for immune evasion and immunosenescence](../publications/45f3f615dcb4bedb9b87.md)

Yajun Wang; Ling Qin

Aging is accompanied by the progressive accumulation of senescent cells, which contribute to tissue dysfunction and chronic inflammation\. These cells persist despite a pro\-inflammatory profile that should, in principle, recruit immune cells for their clearance\. We propose that this persistence is explained, at least in part, by PD\-L1\-mediated immune evasion driven by the DNA damage response \(DDR\)\. The aim of this Mini Review is to synthesize evidence linking DNA damage response signaling, initiated by diverse senescence\-associated stressors, to PD\-L1 upregulation and immune evasion in senescence\. We discuss how DDR signaling drives PD\-L1 expression through transcriptional mechanisms, namely, the cGAS\-STING pathway and the ATM/ATR\-STAT1/IRF1 axis, and through post\-translational stabilization via p16\-mediated inhibition of CDK4/6\. This review also discusses the function of PD\-L1 in the nucleus, where it interacts with cohesin\-SA1 to maintain telomere cohesion\. Finally, it highlights that DDR\-driven PD\-L1 upregulation establishes a self\-reinforcing circuit: immune evasion allows senescent cells to accumulate, which exacerbates telomere dysfunction in neighboring cells and reinforces the senescent phenotype\. This framework recasts senescence as an actively maintained immunoevasive condition and identifies the DDR\-PD\-L1 axis as a potential target for restoring immune clearance of senescent cells\.

## [Robust high\-fidelity three\-qubit gates design for superconducting quantum computers via model\-free reinforcement learning](../publications/45f650fc4ef40b9f7606.md)

Xinxin Zhu; Yangyang Fei; Liu FuDong; Zheng Shan

Abstract Multi\-qubit gates are crucial to realizing quantum algorithms\. Direct implementation of these gates will facilitate a reduction in circuit depth\. However, existing model\-based methods rely on precise characterization of the system Hamiltonian as well as execution of the control fields, which present challenges in obtaining high fidelity multi\-qubit gates\. In this paper, we exploit the bang\-bang control protocol and model\-free reinforcement learning to realize several kinds of three\-qubit gates for superconducting quantum computers with tunable/fixed frequency qubits, including the iToffoli gate, the parity check gate and the CCZ gate\. The simulation results show that the fidelity of each gate can achieve 99\.2% with the Adam Gradient Descent Optimizer\. Moreover, the proposed method is robust against random noise in the control pulse\. Gate fidelity can be maintained over 95% even in the case of Gaussian noise with variance of 0\.3\. Besides, the impacts of parameter iterative optimization strategies are also analyzed\.

## [Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making in Construction Management: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Integration of MCDM, BIM, and Artificial Intelligence \(2015–2025\)](../publications/45fff628ee292c9b5686.md)

Zakaria Ghedjati; Imane F\.I Fantazi; Choubeila Koreichi

The construction industry faces growing challenges that require better decision\-making frameworks\. Combining Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making \(MCDM\) with digital tools like Building Information Modeling \(BIM\) and Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) offers a promising way forward\. Yet their integration remains fragmented across research efforts, revealing a significant gap in theory and practice\. As a result, their potential remains underutilized, limiting the development of flexible, data\-driven decision\-making tools for complex construction projects\. This study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to map the development and structure of the MCDM\-BIM\-AI connection in construction management from 2015 to 2025\. Using a PRISMA\-compliant protocol, we analyzed 253 peer\-reviewed articles from the Scopus database\. Our approach combines performance analysis with science mapping through keyword co\-occurrence networks and thematic evolution analysis across three time periods: 2015\-2018, 2019\-2021, 2022\-2025, along with a country\-level co\-authorship network analysis\. Our findings identify five main thematic clusters and show a significant increase in publications since 2019, mainly driven by the Asia\-Pacific region\. The analysis highlights a notable knowledge gap in the deep connection between BIM and AI within MCDM frameworks\. The temporal mapping reveals three phases of evolution: pre\-integration \(2015\-2018\), Integration \(2019\-2021\), and Innovation \(2022\-present\), with AI and Machine Learning becoming key focus areas in the latest phase\. The study suggests promising future directions for combining MCDM, BIM, and AI to promote more sustainable, data\-driven, and resilient construction practices\. It proposes a conceptual outline for the Intelligent Cognitive Decision Framework \(ICDF\), where BIM serves as a semantic data backbone, MCDM acts as the evaluation engine, and AI provides cognitive support for flexible, data\-driven decision\-making in construction 4\.0 applications\. This intellectual mapping offers researchers data\-driven guidance for prioritizing impactful investigations, practitioners with technology investment plans that match research developments, and policymakers with informed priorities for research and development investment in underrepresented regions\.

## [Computational modeling and optimized machine learning for multidrug solubility prediction in supercritical carbon dioxide](../publications/4600941fecc94a52de7b.md)

Nidal H\. Abu‐Hamdeh; Hasan H\. Hijji; Khalid H\. Almitani

Reliable prediction of pharmaceutical solubility in supercritical carbon dioxide \(scCO 2 \) is complicated by strong compound\-specific behavior and response values\. This study investigated whether sparse measurements from a newly introduced drug can calibrate transferable machine\-learning predictions for computational estimation of solubility in wide range of parameters\. A curated workbook containing 1,618 observations for 60 drugs was modeled using molecular weight, melting point, temperature, and pressure\. Solubility was transformed as log₁₀\(S\), and XGBoost, CatBoost, and multilayer perceptron regression were each tuned using tree\-structured Parzen estimation, differential evolution, and particle swarm optimization\. Evaluation used five\-fold nested group cross\-validation, with complete drugs held out from training and tuning\. For each test drug, predictions were assessed before calibration and after 1, 3, or 5 randomly selected measurements, repeated ten times\. Within the present evaluation framework, the lowest\-log\-MAE zero\-shot configuration was XGBoost optimized by tree\-structured Parzen estimation \(log\-MAE = 0\.584; R² = −0\.087; RMSE = 1\.713 g/L\), showing that the four descriptors were insufficient for reliable extrapolation to unseen compounds\. Sparse calibration substantially improved transfer: the lowest\-log\-MAE one\-shot result was obtained by CatBoost–particle swarm optimization \(log\-MAE = 0\.418; R² = 0\.166\), whereas XGBoost–tree\-structured Parzen estimation had the lowest log\-MAE at three shots \(log\-MAE = 0\.298; R² = 0\.317\) and at five shots \(log\-MAE = 0\.251; R² = 0\.452; RMSE = 1\.223 g/L\)\. Median absolute relative deviation decreased from 82\.4% to 42\.9% between zero and five shots\. These results establish sparse, leakage\-controlled calibration as a more defensible use case than unconditional prediction for unseen drugs, while identifying the need for richer molecular descriptors and external prospective validation\. In practical terms, this few\-shot strategy can reduce the experimental burden for a newly introduced drug by using a small screening set to calibrate a global model before mapping the remaining pressure\-temperature domain\.

## [Impact\-Induced Adhesion Degradation in Gecko\-Inspired Fibrillar Adhesive Units](../publications/4617f08bcc65da959d86.md)

Ru\-Guo Ji; Yue\-Yu Yuan; Xiaofeng Liu; Yu\-Liang Mao; Xiaolong Zhang; Feng\-Hua Wang

Gecko\-inspired fibrillar adhesives are promising for impact\-contact applications, yet the mechanism underlying adhesion degradation after a single impact event remains unclear\. Existing studies have primarily focused on micropillar buckling as a possible degradation mechanism, whereas whether additional degradation pathways exist during impact remains unresolved\. To address this issue, impact and quasi\-static adhesion experiments were conducted on four fibrillar adhesive units \(FAUs\) with identical micropillar adhesive layers but different backing layers\. Comparative analysis of mechanical responses and interfacial images indicates that, for the present short\-pillar FAUs, tensile loading during post\-impact rebound induces local interfacial fracture, which serves as the primary degradation pathway\. Micropillar buckling alone cannot explain the observed degradation\. Backing\-layer\-related compliance and dissipation suppress rebound and reduce the driving force for interfacial fracture, thereby mitigating adhesion degradation\. A reduced\-order rebound\-stage model based on fracture mechanics qualitatively reproduces the adhesion\-degradation trend and backing\-dependent response, further supporting the fracture\-based interpretation\. Finally, transient buckling and fracture\-activation analyses reveal that the applicability of this interpretation depends jointly on micropillar aspect ratio and intrinsic adhesion energy, with buckling emerging as a potential competing mechanism as the aspect ratio increases\.

## [BOLT: Multi\-Bottleneck Bound\-Guided Learning for Flexible Job\-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource\-Coupled Transport](../publications/461cfb4e8127bbe2a5e9.md)

Ziheng Zhang; Wei Zhang; Yunyi Zhao; Zuming Liu; Wei Zhou; Boon Ping Gan

Flexible job\-shop scheduling becomes resource\-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits\. BOLT \(bound\-oriented learning for transport\-coupled scheduling\) builds a lower bound from chain, machine\-capacity, and fleet\-capacity relaxations\. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per\-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan\. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate&\#x27;s bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price\. The root bound certifies a completed schedule&\#x27;s suboptimality gap without a solver\. On industry\-motivated 10\-module prefabricated\-construction instances, explicit transport coupling outperforms a transport\-penalty policy in every tested cell where loaded moves occupy at least 66% of fleet time and in none at or below 56%\. Across five zero\-shot 50\- and 80\-module production batches, BOLT outperforms the best dispatching\-rule pair on four and the penalty policy on the three with long moves\. In the three\-vehicle 80\-module batch, its mean makespan is 13\.0% below the best pair and 4\.2% below an hour\-budget constraint\-programming solver whose proven gap averages 34%\. BOLT decides in 2\.3\-5\.9 ms per event on one processor core and re\-plans a disruption in seconds\.

## [How Finite\-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low\-Rank Adaptation Landscape](../publications/4623e9abaa0e50d36847.md)

Long Nguyen\-Chi; Quynh Nguyen; Thanh Nguyen\-Cung; Binh T\. Nguyen

Low\-rank adaptation \(LoRA\) has become the standard method for parameter\-efficient fine\-tuning of large pretrained models, yet theoretical explanations for why low\-rank updates suffice remain incomplete\. Most existing analyses rely on the Neural Tangent Kernel \(NTK\) regime, which linearizes the network around the pretrained weights\. In this work, we take a different approach that requires no linearization: our key observation is that, once the backbone is frozen, the loss sees each adapted weight matrix only through a finite\-rank linear map induced by the frozen activations\. Trace\-norm regularization then forces the optimizer to pick a low\-rank matrix among all matrices that produce the same observed output\. This yields global minimizers whose ranks are controlled by the rank of this map, which we call the \\emph\{bottleneck rank\}, rather than the sample size\. For multi\-head attention, we obtain tighter rank upper bounds by exploiting two additional invariances: row\-wise softmax is insensitive to additive row constants in the score matrix, and value updates are observable only after attention weighting and frozen output projection\. For the factorized LoRA objective with weight decay, we prove a complementary result on the nonconvex side: after an arbitrarily small generic positive semidefinite perturbation, every first\-order stationary point is rank\-deficient once the LoRA rank exceeds a threshold determined by the bottleneck rank\. Finally, we show that global minimizers of the perturbed objective are near\-optimal for the original trace\-norm problem, and we provide uniform generalization bounds governed by the spectral structure of the frozen features\.

## [Neurological complications in patients receiving CAR T\-cell therapies](../publications/4626b7de5d96c5aa1921.md)

Justin Jiang; Virginia Battistin; Marcos J\. G\. De Lima; Francesca Cottini

Chimeric antigen receptor \(CAR\) T\-cell therapy targeting CD19 or B cell maturation antigen has revolutionized the treatment of patients with relapsed lymphoma, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma\. However, this therapy is associated with both short\- and long\-term immune\-mediated toxicities\. Among them, neurological complications represent a distinct and clinically significant category, with a wide range of presentations\. In this paper, we describe the different types of immune effector cell–associated neurotoxicity syndrome \(ICANS\) and non\-ICANS neurological toxicities, including their clinical features, recommended diagnostic evaluations, underlying mechanisms, and available treatment approaches\.

## [Esketamine alleviates the pain\-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4\-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex](../publications/462ab658021394456cfb.md)

Qingmei Li; Shuming Liu; Huiling Chen; Guangda Liang; Zhouyi Song; Yanfang Liu; Xingfeng Liu; Bangyong Qin

Objective The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine \(ESK\) efficacy in the pain\-depression dyad \(PDD\) remain incompletely understood\. This study investigated the effects of a sub\-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex \(ACC\)\. Methods Male Sprague\-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD \+ ESK groups\. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury \(CCI\), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression\-like phenotypes\. On day 21 post\-surgery, PDD \+ ESK rats received a single esketamine injection \(15 mg/kg, i\.p\.\)\. Multi\-regional c\-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping\. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4\-associated molecular alterations \(including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers\) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting\. Results ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats\. Regional c\-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα\-positive neurons\. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons\. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling \(unadjusted P &lt; 0\.05\) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation\. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure\. Conclusion A single sub\-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats\. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4\-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β\-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα\-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain\-related affective disorders\.
