## [Can Artificial Intelligence Hear a Litigant Within the Meaning of Article 6 ECHR?](../publications/464d8eacf85955bd832b.md)

Andreea Elena Tabacu

The increasing use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in judicial systems raises a fundamental question under Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights \(ECHR\): can an AI system genuinely fulfil a litigant’s right to be heard? This article develops a functional account of that right as a multifaceted guarantee requiring the opportunity to present and challenge relevant material, effective examination of decisive submissions, clarification where necessary, contextual and normative evaluation, reasoned decision\-making, and responsibility for the outcome\. Using doctrinal, comparative, and normative methods, the study examines these requirements in relation to risks associated with judicial AI, including opacity, algorithmic bias, hallucinated outputs, limited explainability, and automation bias\. The analysis is situated within the EU AI Act, the GDPR, the CEPEJ Ethical Charter, Romanian civil procedure, and comparative administrative\-law cases\. The article finds that AI may legitimately assist courts through transcription, translation, legal research, document organization, and non\-binding summaries or drafts\. However, under current legal and technological conditions, AI cannot autonomously perform the hearing in its entirety\. Compliance with Article 6 therefore requires transparency, contestability, independent judicial verification, and meaningful human oversight\. Final adjudicative authority, reasoned judgment, and responsibility must remain with an independent and accountable human judge\.

## [The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence](../publications/46503499ba04c749e578.md)

ADRITA SHANNIGRAHI

Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation\. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions\. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle\. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both\. India doesn&\#x27;t have any regulatory framework on AI\-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions\. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI\-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them\. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works\.

## [Actual Infinity, God, and the Limits of Formal Verification: A Gödelian Critique of Mathematical Reductionism](../publications/465e082c7026eba33657.md)

Sameer Al\-Khawaja

Debates over actual infinity sometimes compare its acceptance with belief in God on the grounds of finite verifiability and observability\. Taking Doron Zeilberger’s ultrafinitist position as a point of departure, this article distinguishes a local methodological restriction on what mathematics should admit from a global verificationist claim about what may count as real, meaningful, or worthy of rational inquiry\. It argues that the second claim does not follow from the first and should not be attributed to Zeilberger without independent evidence\. Gödel’s incompleteness theorems are examined under their specific technical conditions to clarify the limits of provability within consistent, effectively axiomatizable systems sufficiently strong to express arithmetic\. These results neither refute finitism nor establish the existence of actual infinity or God; rather, they show why mathematical truth in the standard interpretation cannot be identified with provability within any fixed system of the relevant kind\. The discussion then draws on scientific realism, theoretical indispensability, and interventionist entity realism to show that direct observability is not a universal prerequisite for justified ontological commitment in science, without transferring scientific standards uncritically to metaphysics\. The article concludes that the infinity–God analogy is not inherently a category mistake\. A category mistake arises more specifically when rules governing admissibility within a mathematical framework are treated as though they determined the meaning, truth, or epistemic legitimacy of metaphysical claims\. Thus, finitist restrictions may remain coherent within mathematics while leaving substantive questions about God open to philosophical examination\.

## [Wavelet\-based adaptive image fusion of CT and MRI with local neighborhood variance for nasopharyngeal carcinoma](../publications/46625eb01cbeb4522508.md)

Xinjian Qin; Haojiang Li; Shanshan Liu; Pengxing Huang; Lizhi Liu; Hong\-Bo Chen; Xin Nian Yang

Multimodal imaging of nasopharyngeal carcinoma \(NPC\) requires complementary representation of CT\-derived bony anatomy and MRI\-derived soft\-tissue contrast\. Existing fusion methods may fail to preserve both structural detail and soft\-tissue information in a transparent and reproducible manner\. We present a wavelet\-based fusion framework that employs local neighborhood variance for adaptive weighting\. This interpretable variance\-driven strategy selectively integrates CT bony structures and MRI soft\-tissue textures according to regional information content\. The neighborhood configuration was selected through an ablation analysis of 232 clinical cases\. Quantitative evaluation showed improved image\-quality performance over the selected comparison methods across entropy, spatial frequency, average gradient, standard deviation, and edge information preservation factor, with respective gains of approximately 5\.5%, 2\.4%, 6\.7%, 5\.1%, and 3\.2% relative to the best\-performing baseline for each metric\. These findings support the proposed method as an image fusion methodology for preserving complementary multimodal information; direct effects on target delineation, workflow efficiency, or dosimetric outcomes require future clinical validation\.

## [Conventional alumina to advanced functional materials: Evolution, surface engineering, and emerging applications in separation science and beyond](../publications/46761acd3501ecb9770a.md)

Krishna Radheshyam Gupta; Monali Rushi Dakhole; Amruta Selote; Milind Janrao Umekar

Alumina \(Al₂O₃\) is a versatile inorganic oxide that has evolved from a conventional industrial material into an engineered functional platform for chromatography, catalysis, adsorption, environmental remediation, sensing, energy\-related technologies, and advanced ceramics\. Its broad utility arises from its diverse crystalline phases, tunable surface chemistry, high thermal stability, mechanical strength, controllable porosity, and capacity for surface modification\. Historically, activated alumina served as an important polar adsorbent and chromatographic stationary phase, while the Bayer process dominated industrial alumina production\. Advances in precipitation, sol–gel, hydrothermal, template\-assisted, and combustion methods subsequently enabled greater control over crystal phase, morphology, surface area, and pore architecture\.This review critically examines the evolution of alumina from conventional and industrial forms to porous, mesoporous, nanostructured, chemically functionalized, polymer\-coated, and hybrid materials\. Particular emphasis is placed on how polymorphism, surface hydroxylation, pore architecture, particle morphology, and functional groups govern adsorption and separation performance\. The development of alumina\-based chromatographic stationary phases, from activated alumina to chemically bonded and polymer\-modified systems, is discussed alongside emerging applications in catalysis, environmental remediation, sensing, and multifunctional composites\.The review further addresses sustainability challenges associated with conventional alumina production, including bauxite residue generation, and explores waste\-derived alumina and circular material strategies\. Key challenges include surface heterogeneity, reproducibility, phase stability, mass transfer, scalability, regeneration, and environmental impact\. Future directions encompass hierarchical pore engineering, application\-specific surface design, multifunctional hybrids, sustainable\-by\-design processing, advanced characterization, and data\-driven materials development\.

## [Rethinking Successive Rejects Algorithms](../publications/4677369e09695c8f3acf.md)

Mohamed Khair; Junpei Komiyama

In the best\-arm identification problem, an algorithm adaptively selects arms to find the arm of the largest mean reward\. Successive Rejects \(SR\) is a simple fixed\-budget best\-arm identification algorithm that eliminates one candidate arm at each phase\. At first glance, SR seems to have limited adaptivity, since it follows predetermined phase lengths\. However, for Gaussian arms with common variance, SR&\#x27;s worst\-instance error exponent normalized by the popular complexity measure $H\_1\(P\)$ is optimal up to a constant factor, which partly explains why SR&\#x27;s performance is competitive compared with state\-of\-the\-art adaptive sampling algorithms\. In this paper, we extend the framework of SR by optimizing its predefined schedule of phase lengths\. We formulate phase\-schedule design as an optimization problem for the normalized error exponent\. Then, we introduce a version of SR with the optimized schedule, which we call $H\_1$\-balanced Successive Rejects \($H\_1$\-SR\)\. This schedule is optimal within the class of SR\-type algorithms with deterministic equal\-count schedules\. For Gaussian arms with common variance, $H\_1$\-SR achieves at least $11/12$ of the optimal normalized rate over all adaptive algorithms for every $K\\ge2$, and this approximation ratio converges to one as $1\-O\(1/\\log K\)$ as $K\\to\\infty$\. This is a significant improvement over original SR, whose corresponding fraction of the optimal normalized rate converges to $1/4$\. Finally, experiments on ten synthetic instances and two dataset\-derived Gaussian benchmarks compare the optimized schedule with original SR at finite horizons\. They show substantial gains on many instances while also exposing a regime in which more aggressive early elimination is costly\.

## [Metaheuristic and Nonlinear Optimization for Intelligent Energy and Environmental Systems: A Review of Renewable Generation, Smart Metering, Networks and Environmental Monitoring](../publications/467e9ed585f9ab1fe358.md)

Kennedy R; Santhalakshmi M; Balamurali S

Energy and environmental systems are full of decisions that must be tuned under uncertainty: how much power to draw from a solar panel, how to bill and balance consumption on a smart grid, how to share spectrum in a wireless network and how to read a biosensor in the field\. Computing itself is part of the problem, since data centres, web services and smartphones draw a growing share of electricity\. Many of these decisions have no closed\-form solution because the underlying models are nonlinear, noisy or only partly known\. Metaheuristic search, fuzzy reasoning, nonlinear analysis and data\-driven forecasting are now used to find good settings, but studies are spread across power engineering, networking and environmental science\. This chapter reviews optimization and learning methods for five groups of problems: renewable generation and grid interfacing, smart metering and energy forecasting, resource allocation and energy\-aware computing in communication and IoT systems, environmental and agricultural monitoring, and the approximation of nonlinear physical models\. The review finds that hybrid metaheuristics, such as grey wolf optimization with opposition\-based learning, improve tracking and control in renewable systems, that tree ensembles and regression models are standard for consumption forecasting, that fuzzy optimization handles uncertainty in network resource allocation, that signal\-aware transfer scheduling and green design guidelines reduce the energy used by smartphones and web services, and that neural approximation can stand in for expensive solvers of nonlinear equations\. Few studies, however, compare methods on shared benchmarks or report computation cost\. Future work should use common test systems, report run time next to solution quality and link optimization with forecasting in one loop\.

## [A multi task deep learning framework for automated health condition prediction from retinal fundus images using hybrid attention and explainable AI](../publications/467fc7f7a7245247c6e6.md)

Ravi Kumar Tenali; Anitha Potnuri

Abstract Although retinal fundus imaging is a non\-invasive tool to assess systemic and fundus pathology, current deep learning algorithms are mostly single\-task, lack clinical interpretability and are unable to handle acquisition variation between different domains\. These constraints limit their clinical utility: when a patient comes to the clinic for fundus screening, they could also be diabetic, have glaucoma, AMD, and increased cardiovascular risk, with each disease having retinal vascular biomarkers that require a patient to be tested for in the clinic, which must be managed within a framework of common, interpretable, and generalizable models rather than a pipeline of independent models\. To solve these problems, we suggest a multi\-task deep learning network that simultaneously classifies DR severity \(five\-class\), glaucoma likelihood \(binary\), AMD stage \(four\-class\) and cardiovascular risk \(binary\) from a single retinal fundus image using a single forward pass\. It adopts an EfficientNet\-B4 convolutional backbone pretrained on the ImageNet dataset, a six\-layer multi\-head self\-attention Transformer encoder \(d\_model = 512, h = 8\), a novel dual\-branch spatial\-channel attention module that builds on, but significantly expands, the CBAM module, and four task\-specific output heads that are optimized using the homoscedastic uncertainty\-weighted multi\-task loss following the formulation of Kendall et al\. Per\-task anatomical explanations are produced by back propagating the CNN backbone via Grad\-CAM in the anatomical space\. The proposed model was evaluated on EyePACS, APTOS 2019, Messidor\-2 and RIM\-ONE v3 and achieved an accuracy of 94\.7%, AUC = 0\.978, sensitivity = 93\.2% and specificity = 95\.8% while being statistically better than all single task models \(DeLong test, p &lt; 0\.01, Bonferroni corrected\)\. Under the reported experimental setting, the zero\-shot cross\-dataset evaluation achieves AUC ≥ 0\.951, which is promising for its performance across datasets\. Grad\-CAM saliency maps are anatomically similar to established clinical grading criteria for each disease\. The four task\-specific heads share a single architecture and produce four outputs in one forward pass, but no individual patient in the training corpora had verified ground\-truth labels for all four conditions simultaneously; the model is trained on partially labelled, multi\-source data via a masked multi\-task loss, and the cardiovascular output is an AVR\-derived image\-based surrogate rather than a validated clinical cardiovascular diagnosis\. This proposed framework could be considered for an additional potential step toward the future when it comes to multi\-disease fundus screening with an interpretable single\-model solution, if it is assessed and approved at an independent multi\-centre level and by regulatory bodies\.

## [Legal Aspects of Artificial Intelligence in India](../publications/46963bd161c19edcb150.md)

Adv\. Nitesh Madhavi

Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used in India in areas ranging from financial services and healthcare to education, advertising, policing and content creation\. The legal difficulty is that AI systems do not fit neatly within one existing legal category\. They may process personal data, generate content, influence decisions, create cybersecurity risks and cause harm without a clear human actor at the point where the harm occurs\. India currently addresses these issues through a combination of general statutes, sectoral regulation, judicial principles and policy initiatives rather than through one comprehensive AI statute\. This paper examines the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, constitutional rights, intellectual property, intermediary responsibility, contractual and consumer liability, deepfakes and automated decision\-making\. It argues that although India&\#x27;s existing legal framework can address many individual harms, important questions concerning accountability, transparency, attribution and human oversight remain without a single, predictable legal standard\.

## [LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing](../publications/46a4d769a89e16c1821f.md)

Yuyan Zhou; Zeyuan Yang; Yuxuan Song; Zhicheng Cai; Hongli Yu; Weiying Ma; Hao Zhou; James Kwok

Diffusion large language models \(dLLMs\) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive language models, enabling non\-autoregressive text generation through parallel decoding\. Existing dLLMs can be broadly categorized into two families: masked diffusion models \(MDMs\) and uniform diffusion models \(UDMs\) In this work, we theoretically show that MDMs are easier to optimize due to their mask\-based transition schedule but have lower computational expressivity, whereas UDMs enable iterative state revision and greater expressivity but are substantially harder to train\. This trade\-off raises a natural question: can we obtain the expressivity of iterative revision without giving up the simple, easy\-to\-optimize transition schedule of MDMs? Motivated by this analysis, we propose Lookahead Editing \(\\ours\{\}\), which augments masked diffusion decoding with a rewritable proposal state\. At each decoding step, the model performs several lookahead updates to iteratively refine future predictions in this proposal state before committing tokens to the masked sequence\. This design introduces a rewritable proposal that uses additional compute to improve expressivity while keeping the simple mask\-based transition schedule of MDMs\. We fine\-tune Qwen2\.5\-7B and Qwen3\-8B to obtain LED\-\\texttt\{7B\} and LED\-\\texttt\{8B\}, respectively\. Across eight benchmarks, LED SFT yields average gains of $\+11\.4$ and $\+7\.7$ points over standard MDM SFT\. Moreover, using SFT alone, LED\-\\texttt\{8B\} outperforms LLaDA2\.1\-16B Q\-mode, which is trained with continued pre\-training, supervised fine\-tuning, and reinforcement learning\.

## [Prevalence and Antibacterial Susceptibility Pattern of Bacterial Isolates from Patients with External Ocular Infections in Three Tertiary Hospitals in Anambra State, Nigeria](../publications/46a62dfd549ce618aa95.md)



The human eye serves as the main sensory organ for vision, enabling perception of the world in remarkable detail\.Ocular infections are common and their morbidity can vary from mild, self\-limiting to sight\-threatening infections\.These infections have been known to cut across various age groups and gender\.The study aimed to determine the prevalence and antibacterial susceptibility pattern of bacterial isolates from external ocular infections in three tertiary hospitals in Anambra State, Nigeria: A hospital based cross\-sectional study was conducted at three tertiary hospitals in Anambra State\.A total of 384 ocular specimens were collected\.The bacteria were isolated using culture methods and identified by biochemical and molecular methods\.Antibiotic susceptibility test was carried out using disc diffusion techniques\.A structured questionnaire was used to obtain socio\-demographic characteristics of the patients\.Demographic distribution revealed that bacterial isolation was statistically significant in gender, residence and occupation but not significant across the different age groups\.Bacterial isolates were identified as Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella variicola and Escherichia coli\.Staphylococcus aureus was the most prevalent pathogen \(47\.3%\) and conjunctivitis was the most common bacterial external ocular infection \(43\.6%\)\.The antibacterial susceptibility test revealed that the S\. aureus and S\. epidermidis were 100% sensitive to vancomycin, chloramphenicol and cefotaxime\.E\. coli was 100% sensitive to all tested antibacterial drugs except chloramphenicol, ceftriaxone and cefotaxime and K\. variicola was 100% sensitive to all except vancomycin and ciprofloxacin\.The prevalence of ocular infection was high with Conjunctivitis being the dominant\.Gram positive bacteria accounted for 82% of isolates with S\. aureus being the predominant isolate\.Vancomycin, chloramphenicol and cefotaxime were most effective against gram positive isolates while the penicillins, aminoglycosides and levofloxacin were most effective against gram negative isolates\.Routine bacterial diagnosis using culture, biochemical and molecular tests is essential for guiding empirical and definitive treatments and limiting antibiotic resistance in external ocular infections\.

## [The influence of AI adoption on decision making, forecasting, and performance: Evidence from solar and telecommunication sectors in Pakistan and China](../publications/46a97b23902c61bcf3f9.md)

Maureen Quaid

This study investigates how Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) adoption builds sustainable supply chain performance in the renewable energy and telecommunications sectors, focusing on the mediating mechanisms of decision\-making and forecasting\. Using a comparative design, data was collected from 214 companies in Pakistan and China\. The proposed model was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\), integrating the Technology\-Organization\-Environment \(TOE\) framework and Resource\-Based View \(RBV\)\. Results confirm a fully mediated pathway, AI adoption is positively associated with decision making and forecasting capabilities, which are positively associated with operational and financial performance, and are associated stronger supply chain performance\. A key finding is that these capabilities exert no direct effect, revealing that AI&\#x27;s sustainability impact is realized indirectly through core business outcomes\. The comparative analysis highlights contextual influence, with China&\#x27;s mature ecosystem fostering deep AI integration and Pakistan&\#x27;s emerging context showing reliance on external tools\. This study provides a novel, integrated TOE\-RBV model that unpacks the &quot;black box&quot; of AI&\#x27;s impact on sustainability\. It offers unique empirical evidence from contrasting emerging economies, demonstrating that the path to AI\-driven sustainable supply chains is mediated and context\-dependent\. For managers, embedding AI into core processes is critical for sustainability gains\. For policymakers, strategies must be context\-specific, focusing on foundational digital infrastructure in emerging economies and advanced innovation ecosystems in mature ones\.

## [A Generalized Framework for Multivariate Predictive Regressions](../publications/46ac51a4bd9d9fa9afc9.md)

Xiaoquan Jiang; Qiang Kang

ABSTRACT Predictive regressions are subject to small‐sample bias when innovations in persistent predictors are correlated with predictive errors\. One approach to bias reduction is the multi‐predictor augmented regression method \(mARM\), which augments the predictive regression with bias‐corrected proxies for predictor innovations\. We extend this framework to allow for first‐order autocorrelation in predictive errors, first‐order autocorrelation in predictor innovations, and contemporaneous correlations between shocks to the two processes\. Simulations show that the mARM estimator can exhibit substantial bias, whereas our proposed extended mARM estimator significantly reduces bias relative to both mARM and ordinary least squares\. Looking at predictive regressions of stock returns on several widely used financial ratios, we find that the mARM approach yields spurious statistical significance for some predictive coefficients, which is not observed with the proposed extended mARM\.

## [Learning to Be Guided: Shaping Latent Geometry for Classifier\-Free Guidance](../publications/46b1be18de611fc2c67d.md)

Haoming Liu; Junhao Zhu; Shaoyi Zheng; Yuanhe Guo; Jinnuo Liu; Shenji Wan; Hongyi Wen

Classifier\-free guidance \(CFG\) is a standard component of conditional diffusion models, and guided generation performance has become the \\textit\{de facto\} measure of state\-of\-the\-art models\. Recent work on latent diffusion models seeks to learn latent spaces that are easier to model with diffusion\. However, under CFG, generation additionally depends on how conditions are arranged in the latent space\. We study this arrangement under discrete class conditions, termed \\emph\{class geometry\}, and investigate what class geometry allows a latent space to work well with CFG\. Under a Gaussian class model, we show that shifting variance from intra\- to inter\-class at fixed total variance makes classes more distinguishable under noise, and derive a noisy posterior objective whose per\-sample descent direction is proportional to the oracle CFG correction\. Based on the analysis, we propose Prototype Regularization \(PR\), a lightweight surrogate for the intractable noisy posterior objective, which applies a cosine prototype classifier to spatially pooled latents\. With a controlled training budget \(20 epochs for VAE, 80 epochs for DiT\), adding PR to an LDM baseline reduces guided gFID on ImageNet from 3\.31 to 2\.28, surpassing a DINOv3\-aligned VA\-VAE \(2\.44\) with negligible overhead\. We further demonstrate that PR generalizes to pseudo\-labels derived from clustering, continuous text\-embedding conditions, and video latents\. Together, our findings highlight class geometry as a critical factor in guided generation and take a first step toward CFG\-compatible representation learning\. Our project page is available at: https://maps\-research\.github\.io/cfg\-geometry/\.

## [Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β\-oxidation enables growth\-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty\-alcohol production](../publications/46b30d46f73e2f0ae6dc.md)

Bridgie Cawthon; Aidan E\. Cowan; Zen Yoshikawa; Kenneth Low; Justin J\. Baerwald; Nawa Raj Baral; Matthew R\. Incha; Jennifer  W\. Gin; Yan Chen; Christopher J\. Petzold; Edward E\. K\. Baidoo; Emine A\. Turumtay; Corinne D\. Scown; Adam M\. Feist; Jay D\. Keasling

Abstract Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing\. In this work we replace canonical mixed\-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation \(rBOX\) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation\. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux\. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold \(110 ± 0\.15 mg/L/hr\) and titer more than threefold up to 4\.0 ± 0\.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain\. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes\. These results establish redox\-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway\.

## [A Remotely Delivered Exercise\-Based Rehabilitation Program for Patients with Persistent Chemotherapy\-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy \(EX\-CIPN\): A Phase I Feasibility Trial](../publications/46b4a7578240ade8418f.md)

Eric Antonen; Michelle B\. Nadler; David Michael Langelier; Kristin L\. Campbell; David Flamer; Jang Hyuk Cho; Scott J\. Capozza; Lisa M\. Avery; Kelcey A\. Bland; Scott Leatherdale; Jackie Manthorne; Muna Al\-Khaifi; Jennifer Michelle Jones

Background: Chemotherapy\-induced peripheral neuropathy \(CIPN\) affects two\-thirds of patients who receive neurotoxic chemotherapy\. In almost half of these patients, CIPN is persistent, with limited treatment options\. Exercise\-based rehabilitation shows promising results in improving CIPN\-related outcomes, but high\-quality research is needed with CIPN symptoms and disability as primary endpoints\. Methods: We conducted a phase I single\-arm, multi\-method pilot study of a 10\-week remotely delivered exercise\-based rehabilitation program \(EX\-CIPN\) for adult \(≥18\-years\) cancer survivors experiencing CIPN symptoms ≥6 months post\-chemotherapy\. Primary outcomes were feasibility \(accrual, retention, and adherence\), acceptability \(interviews and surveys\), and safety \(CTCAE v5\)\. Secondary outcomes included pain, CIPN symptoms, CIPN\-related disability, and physiologic assessments\. Assessments were conducted at baseline \(T1\), post\-program \(T2\), and 3 months post\-program \(T3\)\. Post\-program feedback surveys were completed at T2 and semi\-structured qualitative video interviews were completed between T2 and T3\. Results: In total, 36 participants \(median age: 59, 83% female\) consented to participate in the study\. T1 retention rate \(90%\), adherence rates \(77–96%\), and no reported serious adverse events \(Grade 3 CTCAE v5\) supported study feasibility and safety\. Interviews and surveys supported intervention acceptability\. Retention rates at T2 \(68%\) and T3 \(63%\) did not reach feasibility targets\. CIPN symptoms and CIPN\-related disability showed significant improvement at T3 \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions: Results suggest that EX\-CIPN has encouraging feasibility outcomes and is acceptable and safe\. Preliminary clinical outcome results are promising\. Based on these study results, we can proceed to test this intervention, with a few modifications, in a prospective randomised trial with a CIPN\-related primary outcome\.

## [Genome\-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth’s oligotrophic depths](../publications/46c25d0313e3b3e6d70f.md)

Xiaonan Wan; Wenlu Feng; Yang Zhang; Tom A\. Williams; Gergely J\. Szöllősi; Hongyu Dang; Xuejun Yan; James M\. Tiedje; Jizhong Z\. Zhou; Xun Qian

Abstract Deep soils represent one of Earth’s largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood\. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China\. Despite its genome reduction \(average size \~2\.9 Mb\), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources\. Cellular, genomic, and metatranscriptomic evidence, including small cell and genome sizes, host\-associated metabolism, and the active expression of attachment\- and attack\-associated surface structures such as Tad pili and pore\-forming toxins, indicate a predatory lifestyle in Aridivitia\. Ancestral genome reconstruction reveals that Aridivitia originated as free\-living mixotrophs, but subsequently lost the ability to fix carbon as they evolved a predatory lifestyle\. Collectively, Aridivitia exemplifies a unique evolutionary strategy that reconciles genome reduction with functional versatility, expanding our understanding of microbial adaptation and evolution at the energetic limits of life\.

## [Modelos de Linguagem e Educação a Distância: Revisão Sistemática da Literatura Sobre o Uso Ético e Pedagógico no Ensino Superior](../publications/46c50b414cbf135ce6f7.md)

Rafael Alves Lozano; Guilherme da Cunha Mendonça; Janaina Kawata de Alencar; Thomaz Augusto Ferreira Assis; Francisca Miquelle Siqueira Cardoso; Karina Valdivia Delgado

A adoção de modelos de linguagem de grande escala \(LLMs\) na educação a distância \(EaD\) tem crescido rapidamente no ensino superior, porém, seus impactos pedagógicos e éticos ainda são pouco explorados de forma integrada na literatura\. Esta revisão de escopo teve como objetivo mapear as evidências disponíveis sobre o uso de LLMs na EaD no ensino superior, identificando aspectos éticos, benefícios, limitações e papel pedagógico dessas ferramentas\. Foram elegíveis artigos empíricos e teóricos que abordassem o uso de LLMs no contexto da EaD no ensino superior, com análise de dimensões éticas, pedagógicas ou de impacto na aprendizagem, publicados em inglês ou português\. A busca foi conduzida nas bases Scopus e Web of Science, seguindo o protocolo PRISMA\-ScR, na qual foram identificados 229 artigos na Scopus e 136 na Web of Science, totalizando 365; após a remoção de 92 duplicatas e a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade, 55 artigos foram incluídos na análise final\. Os resultados evidenciam que o uso de LLMs pode fortalecer a aprendizagem na EaD ao oferecer personalização, feedback imediato e suporte à organização dos estudos, mas também revela limitações importantes, como imprecisões, vieses, dependência excessiva e riscos à integridade acadêmica\. Os estudos convergem ao indicar que os efeitos positivos ocorrem principalmente quando o uso dos LLMs é mediado por práticas pedagógicas estruturadas e alinhadas a diretrizes institucionais\. Conclui\-se que os LLMs apresentam potencial significativo para qualificar a EaD no ensino superior, desde que integrados a modelos pedagógicos éticos e estruturados, com políticas institucionais claras e estratégias de inclusão digital\. Palavras\-chave: Ética\. Inteligência artificial\. Educação a Distância\. Processo de aprendizagem\.

## [MONTE CARLO TREE SEARCH: A REVIEW OF DRAWBACKS, ADVANTAGES AND LIMITATIONS IN COMPLEX MULTIPLAYER GAMES](../publications/46c85e28b8834732e4b1.md)

João Luis Almeida Santos; Andrei Camilotto; Djonatan Bonelli; Eduardo Fiorentin; Felipe Grando

O MCTS ganhou destaque após sucessos em Go, Xadrez e Shogi, mas a maioria dos estudos concentra\-se em jogos de dois jogadores com informação perfeita\. Este artigo analisa o MCTS em jogos digitais e de tabuleiro multijogador, frequentemente caracterizados por informação imperfeita\. Com base em 18 artigos selecionados entre 22 recuperados nas bases IEEE Xplore, HAL Science Ouverte e Google Scholar \(2013–2025\), o estudo identifica três limitações estruturais recorrentes: platôs computacionais, pontos cegos no raciocínio tático e trade\-offs na modelagem de oponentes\. Além disso, mostra que a informação imperfeita e as restrições de tempo real intensificam essas limitações\. O artigo também reúne estratégias de mitigação, como ajuste via NTBEA, playouts baseados em conhecimento especializado e Information Set MCTS, além de apontar cinco lacunas de pesquisa em ambientes pouco explorados, incluindo jogos digitais em tempo real, jogos de cartas cooperativos e jogos de tabuleiro modernos\.

## [Designing dynamic pricing for bike\-sharing systems via differentiable agent\-based simulation](../publications/46ed74d95b841c370ffc.md)

Tatsuya Mitomi; Fumiyasu Makinoshima; Fumiya Makihara; Eigo Segawa

Abstract Bike\-sharing systems are emerging in various cities as new eco\-friendly transportation systems\. In these systems, spatiotemporally varying user trip demand leads to imbalances in inventory at bicycle stations, resulting in additional relocation costs\. Therefore, user trip demand must be managed through optimal dynamic pricing for these systems\. However, optimal pricing design is challenging because these systems involve users with diverse backgrounds and probabilistic choices\. To address this problem, we develop a differentiable agent\-based simulation to rapidly design dynamic pricing in bike\-sharing systems\. We first validate our approach through experiments involving 25 bicycle stations and five time slots, yielding 100 parameters\. In this small\-scale synthetic scenario, our approach achieves a 73–78% reduction in loss and more than a 100\-fold reduction in the number of simulation runs required for convergence compared to differential evolution and finite\-difference\-based gradient descent\. We further validate our approach on a synthetic scenario involving 289 bicycle stations, resulting in 1,156 parameters\. While we do not compare against conventional methods due to computational limitations, we observe that the number of simulation runs required by our approach does not increase with the number of optimized parameters\. To illustrate the applicability of our method to real\-world trip demand, we conduct simulation experiments using NYC Citi Bike data, where user behavior is specified heuristically\. The results show that, in simulation, the estimated dynamic pricing can induce balanced inventories without any manual relocation\. Additionally, we observe that the cost of discounts required to induce inventory balance can be reduced by choosing appropriate initial pricing parameters, even though this cost is not included in the optimization objective\.

## [The role and mechanism of endothelial cell\-specific molecule\-1 in respiratory diseases](../publications/46f2c6b0e9db6f68357e.md)

Ling Huang; Xiaofei Liu; Qianbiao Rao; Yingchun Zou; Yiqiong Wen; Talhah Arif; 郑园园; Shibo Sun

Endothelial cell\-specific molecule\-1 \(ESM1\) is a soluble dermatan sulfate proteoglycan and is mainly expressed in pulmonary endothelial cells\. It is reported that ESM1 plays an important role in promoting cell proliferation, such as metabolic reprogramming, and inhibiting autophagy\. In addition, ESM1 exerts a dual regulatory effect on inflammation\. However, the mechanism of the dual regulatory effect of ESM1 on inflammation remains unclear\. Moreover, evidence suggests that ESM1 is involved in multiple signaling pathways, such as the EGFR/ESM1, EGFR/HER3\-Akt/ANGPT2, HGF/c\-MET, VEGF\-A/ESM1, mTOR, and ZEB1/PI3K/AKT pathways\. Increasing studies suggested that ESM1 is involved in various respiratory diseases, such as lung cancer, obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome \(OSAHS\), pulmonary arterial hypertension \(PAH\), and acute lung injury \(ALI\)/acute respiratory distress syndrome \(ARDS\)\. In lung cancer, ESM1 promotes cancer cell proliferation through the EGFR, NF\-κB, and HGF/c\-MET signaling pathways\. In OSAHS, ESM1 enhances inflammatory factor secretion and monocyte\-endothelial cell adhesion through the HIF\-1α/VEGF signaling pathway\. In PAH, ESM1 may promote vascular remodeling and inflammation via a positive feedback loop with TNF\-α\. Conversely, in ALI/ARDS, ESM1 may inhibit leukocyte recruitment to reduce inflammation\. However, the specific roles and mechanisms of ESM1 in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\), asthma, and pneumonia need to be further explored\. Accordingly, ESM1 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for various respiratory diseases\.

## [Addressing symbolic obstacles in undergraduate calculus through artificial intelligence scaffolding](../publications/46f3bf387c47fc296fab.md)

Isbadar Nursit; Toto Nusantara; Erry Hidayanto

Symbolic obstacles in calculus prevent students from moving away from intuition and towards formal thinking, but are rarely studied in the context of artificial intelligence \(AI\) interaction logs\. We investigated symbolic obstacles and AI\-supported representational transitions among 12 Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students in a non\-intrusive intrinsic case study\. Semi\-structured interviews, eight classroom observations, diagnostic tests, academic artifacts, and AI logs were analyzed through inductive\-deductive thematic analysis, based on Tall’s Three Worlds of Mathematics\. Four obstacles are highlighted: graph\-to\-symbol translation, integral and sigma notation, limit notation, and symbolic algebraic manipulation\. Participant\-level comparisons showed 27\.4%–53\.8% fewer coded symbolic errors in post\-activity assessments than at baseline\. AI scaffolding through dynamic visualization, adaptive feedback, step\-by\-step guidance, and solution validation was associated with representational cycling, metacognitive reflection, reported self\-efficacy gains, and lower mathematics anxiety\. The study integrates AI\-log evidence with the Three Worlds framework to explain how scaffolding can support students in addressing symbolic obstacles\.

## [Developing an Industry\-Based DevOps Learning Framework Through Microservices, CI/CD, and AI\-Driven Bus Scheduling Optimization for Vocational Education](../publications/4702cb5708745d11f63f.md)

Roni Andarsyah; Cahyo Prianto; Dodi Permadi

The digital transformation within the public transportation industry demands information systems that are responsive, modular, and capable of supporting data\-driven decision\-making\. This research integrates two previously independent strategic approaches: \(1\) a DevOps architecture utilizing a CI/CD Pipeline based on Microservices, enhanced with API Logging and centralized monitoring to support the ticketing Dashboard system for bus operators, and \(2\) a hybrid optimization approach combining Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithms \(GA\) to optimize airport bus scheduling\. Beyond these technical contributions, this research develops an Industry\-Based DevOps Learning Framework, a training\-oriented framework that can be adapted for vocational education and industry\-based learning in DevOps and data\-driven optimization\. The implementation of CI/CD and Microservices enables rapid, scalable, and zero\-downtime deployment, while centralized monitoring using Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana \(ELK\) Stack and Prometheus–Grafana improves Observability and early anomaly detection\. On the operational side, a LightGBM model is employed to predict the probability of passenger occupancy \(load factor ≥ 70%\), and these predictions are used as a fitness function within the GA to generate optimal schedules\. Experimental results show significant improvements: total estimated passengers increased from 478 to 841, and the average load factor improved from 82% to 87%\. Furthermore, the proposed integrated system was validated as a project\-based training platform through a pilot training involving 22 vocational students, who acquired hands\-on competencies in Microservices development, CI/CD Pipeline, and intelligent optimization within a real\-world transportation context, showing statistically significant improvement across all six competency domains \(Wilcoxon signed\-rank test, p 0\.001\) with large effect sizes \(r = 0\.78\-0\.94\)\. The integration of these two approaches results in a reliable, adaptive ticketing and scheduling system capable of supporting real\-time operational decision\-making for bus companies\.

## [Role of the digital specialist community public health nurse: reimagining community nursing in the AI\-enabled public health landscape](../publications/470aea129ac08ca71ee2.md)

Michelle Lorraine Vizard

Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are redefining how people access and navigate community healthcare\. Concurrently, community nursing services are facing a sustained workforce decline\. While digital nurse leadership has matured in many acute organisations, community nurses are increasingly expected to deliver technology\-enabled care without equivalent leadership structures, support or career pathways\. In this article, the author details a proposal for a digital specialist community public health nurse \(digital SCPHN\) role framework\. The author describes the digital SCPHN as first and foremost a clinician, with digital capability as an essential enhancement rather than a replacement of core nursing objectives\. Positioned as a digital translator and champion within community teams, the digital SCPHN helps people to navigate complex digital healthcare systems while supporting their colleagues through technology\-enabled care prioritisation, secure safeguarding communication and community risk insight\. The author also outlines six actionable recommendations for front\-line nurses, team leads and system commissioners to strengthen community nursing impact, improve digital literacy and ensure equitable, person\-centred care in digitally enabled neighbourhood healthcare systems\.

## [Reshaping Industry 5\.0 manufacturing processes](../publications/470fd8f6f0d25a96207b.md)



Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting\-edge research and case studies\. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context\. Findings Greater real\-time control, efficient interaction between humans and robots and increased sustainability are among attainable outcomes when manufacturers combine machine learning with cyber\-physical systems\. To increase the likelihood of achieving such results in an Industry 5\.0 environment, firms must also address various challenges relating to issues that include data reliability, algorithmic bias, workforce skills, network complexity, system verification and cybersecurity\. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy\-to\-digest format\.

## [Multiscale vascular responses to passive heat stress: from endothelial injury to adaptive remodeling](../publications/471da03d7ae50b2f6084.md)

Linke Zhong; Xue Xia; Jirui Wen; Yimin Li; Tang Feng; Jiang Wu

The escalating occurrence of extreme high temperature weather exposes individuals to passive heat stress more frequently, resulting in strain on the vascular system\. One example of this strain is the doubling of cardiac output during heat stress, achieved through an increase in heart rate and the redirection of blood flow from non\-cutaneous tissues\. These combined stressors can present substantial risks, potentially leading to syncope and cardiovascular collapse\. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the principal cardiovascular responses to passive heat stress, with a specific focus on the cellular and molecular reactions of blood vessels to passive heat stress, to facilitate the formulation of treatment guidelines and preventive measures to mitigate risks associated with the escalating occurrence of severe heat events\. Furthermore, in addition to its function as an environmental stressor, mild passive heat stress is also acknowledged as a therapeutic intervention for enhancing or ameliorating deteriorations in vascular wellbeing\. Consequently, passive heat stress assumes dual roles with potential benefits and drawbacks in relation to vascular health, necessitating further investigation to comprehensively grasp the ramifications of heat intensity on vascular reactions and ascertain the most effective strategy for managing heat stress in susceptible populations\. Importantly, the vascular consequences of passive heat stress are highly dependent on the intensity, duration, and frequency of heat exposure, with moderate thermal stimulation promoting adaptive vascular remodeling whereas excessive heat exposure may lead to endothelial injury, circulatory dysfunction, and multiple\-organ damage\. A better understanding of these context\-dependent vascular responses may facilitate the development of evidence\-based thermal interventions and improve prevention strategies for heat\-related cardiovascular complications, particularly in vulnerable populations such as older adults and individuals with cardiometabolic diseases\.

## [GIYOHVANDLIK VOSITALARINING NOQONUNIY MUOMALASIGA QARSHI KURASHISHNING XALQARO\-HUQUQIY MEXANIZMLARI SHAKLLANISHI VA RIVOJLANISH BOSQICHLARI](../publications/4728c57a3acd70e9c508.md)

МУСАЕВ Джамалиддин Камалович

This article examines the historical and legal evolution of international legal regulation and international cooperation of States in combating the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs\. It analyses the principal stages of development from the International Opium Convention to the contemporary universal treaty\-based system established within the framework of the United Nations\. Particular attention is paid to the significance of the 1961 Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, the 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances, and the 1988 United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances in the formation and development of international legal cooperation\. The article also explores the transformation of cooperation between States from treaty\-based and control\-oriented mechanisms to institutional, criminal\-law and operational forms of cooperation\. Special consideration is given to contemporary challenges arising from the digitalisation of drug trafficking, including the use of Darknet platforms, crypto\-assets, electronic evidence and artificial intelligence\. The study substantiates the need to develop a comprehensive model of international legal cooperation that integrates treaty\-based, institutional, law\-enforcement, digital and preventive mechanisms\.

## [The role of AI robotics and marketing execution capabilities in B2B value realization and accumulation under technological uncertainty](../publications/473ed40510d91876bd4f.md)

Rafique Ahmed Khuhro; Dapeng Liang; Rohail Ashraf; Muhammad Asif Khan

Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence \(AI\) robotics capability is associated with customer value realization \(CVR\) and brand value \(BV\) in business\-to\-business \(B2B\) markets, and whether marketing execution capability \(MEC\) explains these relationships under technological uncertainty\. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the resource\-based view and resource orchestration perspectives, this study uses unbalanced panel data from 234 Chinese B2B firms \(2011–2022\)\. AI\-enabled robotics capability is measured using patent portfolio data, whereas MEC is constructed as a multidimensional index using principal component analysis\. A moderated mediation model was tested using fixed\-effects regression with cluster\-robust standard errors\. Findings AI robotics capability \(AI\-RC\) does not exhibit an automatic direct association with CVR and BV; rather, its value potential is realized when firms can effectively execute, coordinate and deliver AI\-enabled offerings through MEC, supporting it as a transformational mechanism\. However, technological uncertainty weakens the positive association between AI\-RC and MEC\. This dual\-value framework demonstrates that the value potential of AI\-robotics capability is conditional on the strength of MEC and the level of technological uncertainty\. Practical implications For managers, AI robotics should be viewed not merely as operational tools but also as strategic resources that require strong MEC to convert technical knowledge into CVR and BV through consistent articulation, coordination and delivery\. Originality/value This study contributes to the B2B marketing scholarship by \(1\) introducing a dual\-value framework that integrates customer\-side \(customer value realization\) and firm\-side \(brand value\) outcomes; \(2\) positioning MEC as an execution\-oriented marketing capability and arguing that the relationship between technological and marketing capabilities is task\-contingent rather than uniformly complementary; and \(3\) demonstrating technological uncertainty as a boundary condition\.

## [Curvature\-driven passive mixing in three\-dimensional conical helix micromixers](../publications/4750b1bf7e26dcb5f1be.md)

İsmail Bütün; Tunahan Parlayıcı; Süleyman Çelik; Erchan Aptoula; Ali Koşar

Passive microfluidic mixing is fundamentally constrained by the dominance of laminar flow, a limitation commonly addressed using embedded obstacles or surface modifications, often at the cost of increased fabrication complexity and hydraulic resistance\. Here, we introduce a conical helix micromixer \(CHM\) that combines circular and helical microchannel topologies into a monolithic geometry capable of passively generating progressively intensified Dean vortices through continuously varying curvature\. This curvature\-driven mechanism induces strong transverse transport and achieves a mixing index \(MI\) &gt; 95% in the first turn of the CHM across varying flow rates \(1–2500 µL min −1 \) without requiring any internal roughness structures or external energy inputs, as validated by field\-based mixing simulations\. A central methodological contribution is a reduced\-order planar representation of the full three\-dimensional \(3D\) CHM geometry for flow\-field analysis and optimization\. Direct geometrical validation against the original 3D conical\-helix centreline demonstrated projection\-induced deviations below 2% across all investigated configurations, with most cases remaining below 1%, confirming that the planar representation preserves the dominant geometric characteristics of the true 3D flow path with negligible loss of fidelity\. This reduced\-order strategy lowered computational costs by approximately an order of magnitude, while preserving a strong correlation with full 3D field\-based calculations across the investigated ranges of Reynolds numbers\. Geometric and flow parameters were systematically explored using a Taguchi framework, while gradient\-boosted machine\-learning models were employed as mechanistic analytical tools to quantify parameter sensitivity\. Both analyses consistently identified the inlet curvature radius as the dominant design variable governing Dean vortex onset and mixing\-length compression, with tighter curvature significantly accelerating the development of transverse mixing\. The results prove that controlled curvature modulation alone can function as an efficient passive mixing engine, providing a compact, fabrication\-ready platform for microreactor synthesis, point\-of\-care diagnostics, and scalable lab\-on\-a\-chip applications\.

## [Application of Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture](../publications/47679785e9c909d61f8e.md)

Shailendra Bhalawe; Rishikesh Thakur; Ajay Singh Lodhi; Atul Shrivastav; Surendra Rai

Abstract: Climate change, population growth, and increasing pressure on natural resources pose major challenges to global agricultural production\. Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has emerged as a promising technology for addressing these challenges through precision farming, machine learning, robotic automation, and data\-driven decision\-making\. This study examines the applications of AI in crop management, real\-time monitoring, yield prediction, resource optimization, and sustainable agricultural production\. The integration of AI with advanced genetic technologies can improve productivity, resource\-use efficiency, and climate resilience\. However, challenges related to technology, infrastructure, farmer awareness, data availability, affordability, and regulatory frameworks limit its widespread adoption\. The study highlights the need for supportive policies, capacity building, digital infrastructure, and collaboration among farmers, researchers, industries, and policymakers\.
