## [Contribution of biochar to microbial activities in rice ecosystems growth productivity food security and conservation](../publications/476b55efd8a73b2825b0.md)

Stanslaus Terengia Materu; Naza Emmanuel Mmbaga; Festo Richard Silungwe

Rice is the staple food for over half of the global population and faces escalating threats from climate change, soil degradation, and nutrient leaching that undermine long\-term production sustainability\. Biochar, a carbon\-rich product of biomass pyrolysis under oxygen\-limited conditions, has emerged as a promising soil amendment for rice ecosystems, improving soil physicochemical properties including porosity, pH, water retention, and nutrient availability and fostering diverse microbial communities that drive nutrient cycling and soil fertility\. By enhancing the abundance and activity of nitrogen\-fixing bacteria, mycorrhizal fungi, and phosphorus\-solubilizing microorganisms, biochar strengthens the biological foundation of rice productivity, supporting improvements in root development, biomass accumulation, and grain yield\. Across the reviewed literature, biochar application has been associated with yield increases generally ranging from approximately 8 to 24% at biochar dosage of 5 to 20 t/ha and nitrogen use efficiency improvements of around 10–12%, though these outcomes are highly dependent on biochar feedstock, pyrolysis conditions, application rate, soil type, and rice genotype\. Biochar has also demonstrated capacity to reduce nutrient leaching, mitigate drought and salinity stress, and enhance plant resistance to biotic stressors through rhizosphere microbial modifications\. Environmentally, biochar contributes to carbon sequestration and has been associated with reductions in methane and nitrous oxide emissions in paddy systems under specific management conditions, though some studies report increased methane emissions, particularly in high organic carbon soils at elevated application rates\. Water retention, runoff reduction, and irrigation efficiency improvements represent additional conservation benefits, especially in sandy or degraded paddy soils\. However, biochar application is not without risks: negative effects on soil microbial communities, nutrient immobilization in certain soil types, ecotoxicological concerns from poorly produced biochars, and high production costs of $51–386 per tonne present significant barriers to widespread adoption\. Realizing biochar’s potential in sustainable rice production requires optimized, site\-specific application strategies, cost\-effective production technologies, and transdisciplinary collaboration among researchers, farmers, and policymakers\. Clinical trial number: Not applicable

## [Metabolomics\-based comparison of metabolite profiles in Capparis spinosa L\. from different habitats and associated soil factors](../publications/47732a9ec8857e9cb5d0.md)

Xiakela Xiayifu; Ruli Zhao; Ziyi Bai; Xiaoying Liu; Xinhui Wang

Introduction Capparis spinosa L\. is a distinctive plant with edible and medicinal value, yet the factors influencing the accumulation of its effective components across diverse habitats remain unclear\. This study aims to profile fruit metabolites and explore the association with rhizosphere soil environments\. Methods Using LC\-MS/MS\-based untargeted metabolomics \(six biological replicates per habitat\), fruit metabolites from three habitats in northern Xinjiang \(Urumqi, Karamay, and Ili\) were profiled\. Partial least squares discriminant analysis \(PLS\-DA\) identified differential metabolites\. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed rhizosphere soil microbial communities, and correlation analyses linked fruit metabolites with soil metabolites and microbiota\. Results A total of 1,739 metabolites were identified\. PLS\-DA revealed clear habitat separation, with 454, 340, and 411 differential metabolites in pairwise comparisons\. Sixteen anti\-inflammatory compounds \(flavonoids, terpenoids, etc\.\) were candidate quality\-associated metabolites, predominantly highest in Urumqi\. Soil bacterial/fungal composition differed significantly among habitats, with Rubrobacterand Gaiella enriched in Urumqi\. Correlation analysis linked 16 fruit metabolites \(e\.g\., resveratrol, kaempferol\) to 10 soil metabolites and specific soil genera\. Discussion Habitat\-driven differences in soil microbial communities and metabolite levels are associated with bioactive component abundance in C\. spinosa fruit, offering targets for habitat selection and microbiome\-informed cultivation\. Note that LC\-MS/MS signal intensities are semi\-quantitative; reported differences reflect relative abundance rather than absolute content\.

## [Proposed Pedagogical Framework for Positioning Generative AI as a Thinking Companion in Recount Writing](../publications/4776658343553661521b.md)

Jasmine Fajri; Ahmad Husein Rofi’udin; Titik Harsiati

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) can provide feedback, questions for reflection, and language support in writing instruction\. However, without clear guidance, students may delegate idea generation, drafting, and revision to the technology\. This study identifies local needs in Grade IX recount\-writing instruction and proposes a preliminary framework for positioning GenAI as a thinking companion\. It draws on content analysis of the Grade IX Indonesian Language Student’s Book and Teacher’s Book, a semi\-structured interview with one Indonesian language teacher, and descriptive analysis of six selected questionnaire items answered by 56 students\. The materials examined provide model texts and initial writing activities but lack systematic revision guidance and recount\-specific criteria in the final assessment rubric\. Student responses indicate reported use of AI as a thinking companion, reported submission of assignments containing content partly or entirely copied from GenAI, and an expectation for appropriately integrated teaching materials\. Considered alongside relevant literature, these findings inform six proposed principles: student ownership of ideas, independent work before AI use, limited AI assistance, guided prompts, critical evaluation of AI output, and transparency about AI use\. The framework has not undergone expert validation or classroom testing\. It should therefore be regarded as a context\-specific design proposal, not an established guideline or evidence of instructional effectiveness\.

## [A review of the effects of different exercise modalities on physical fitness in individuals with paraplegia](../publications/47795395a58dcfeba866.md)

Lana Voler

Namen magistrskega dela je bil pregledati in sintetizirati ugotovitve iz znanstvene literature o učinkih različnih tipov vadbe na telesno zmogljivost oseb s popolno paraplegijo\. Posebna pozornost je bila namenjena vzdržljivostni vadbi, vadbi za moč, vadbi ravnotežja in posturalne kontrole ter vadbi gibljivosti\. Magistrsko delo je temeljilo na deskriptivni metodi dela\. Uporabljeni so bili domači in tuji znanstveni članki ter strokovna literatura, pridobljeni iz različnih znanstvenih baz podatkov in drugih strokovnih virov\. Pregledana literatura je pokazala, da lahko redna telesna vadba pomembno prispeva k izboljšanju telesne zmogljivosti oseb s popolno paraplegijo\. Ugotovitve so pokazale, da vzdržljivostna vadba izboljšuje predvsem srčno\-dihalno pripravljenost, vadba za moč pa mišično jakost, mišično vzdržljivost ter učinkovitejše izvajanje funkcionalnih nalog\. Pozitivni učinki so bili ugotovljeni tudi pri vadbi ravnotežja, ki prispeva k izboljšanju posturalne kontrole in kontrole trupa ter s tem omogoča učinkovitejše izvajanje aktivnosti v sedečem položaju, ter pri vadbi gibljivosti, katere glavni namen je ohranjanje funkcionalnega obsega gibanja ter zmanjševanje tveganja za razvoj sklepne togosti in kontraktur\. Pregledana literatura je pokazala tudi, da lahko kombinirani vadbeni pristopi prispevajo k celovitejšemu izboljšanju telesne zmogljivosti v primerjavi s programi, usmerjenimi zgolj v posamezno komponento telesne pripravljenosti\. Na podlagi pregleda literature je bilo ugotovljeno, da je za osebe s popolno paraplegijo najprimernejši celostno zasnovan vadbeni program, ki vključuje različne tipe vadbe in je prilagojen posameznikovim funkcionalnim sposobnostim ter potrebam\. Takšen pristop lahko pomembno prispeva k večji funkcionalni neodvisnosti, ohranjanju zdravja in izboljšanju kakovosti življenja\.

## [The impact of AI on students’ achievement, confidence, and critical thinking in education in Morocco](../publications/477f451ad75a16dbd042.md)

Fatima Mellouk; Meryem Ouelfatmi

In recent years, artificial intelligence \(AI\) has seen a significant growth in its integration with the field of Education\. This has started many concerns about the effect it has on the process of learning, academic integrity and skill development\. This paper examines the effects of AI use within the context of higher education institutions, as it investigates Moroccan postgraduate students’ perceptions on their academic achievements\. The targeted sample consisted of 15 postgraduate students enrolled in the English departments of two public universities\. This research follows a qualitative approach, as it aims to capture the students’ experience of AI use in their academic life\. The findings highlight potential risks of heavy reliance on AI, which include a diminished confidence in the students’ performance, reduced engagement in independent learning and more\. However, AI also presents many opportunities for enhancing the process of learning and education when used as a complementary tool instead of replacing the whole cognitive process\. This study puts an emphasis on the need for a balanced AI integration while focusing on the development of the students’ cognitive skills in the process\. This study contributes to the persisting debate regarding the implementation of AI tools in education and examines how they can be used ethically without diminishing students’ efforts or undermining their original contributions\.

## [Foreign Influences on The Poetry of Omar Abū Rīsha](../publications/4786bce039d7e88ae5ea.md)

Mohamad Alahmad

The study examines foreign influences on the poetry of Omar Abū Rīsha, focusing on the formal and thematic transformations evident in his poetic production as a result of his engagement with foreign cultures and his sustained interaction with non\-Arab societies throughout his diplomatic career\. This study aims to analyze his use of myth, his affiliation with Romantic aesthetics, the development of poetic drama in his work, and his engagement with Western musical and stanzaic structures\. Methodologically, the study adopts a descriptive–analytical approach, which is well suited to examining foreign influences in poetic texts and to generating analytically grounded, objective findings\. The study reveals several significant findings\. Most notably, Omar Abū Rīsha makes extensive use of myth in a number of his poems, particularly the myth of Phineus, which recurs across multiple texts\. Romantic influence is also clearly evident in his poetry, as reflected in its nature\-centered diction, the personification of natural elements, the dialectical interplay between imagination and nature, intensified self\-expression, and the emergence of the Romantic hero\. Moreover, Abū Rīsha draws on Western literary traditions through his incorporation of poetic drama, employing both historical figures and realist themes\. His poetry further exhibits the influence of Western musical forms, particularly in its use of stanzaic structures, varied rhyme schemes, and the integration of free verse in selected works\.

## [EgoTokens: Egocentric 3D human reconstruction and language\-guided shape editing via quantized position tokens in vision\-language models](../publications/479cc2690dbd070b3f95.md)

Gulraiz Khan; Maneeha Rani; Waqas Ahmed; Kevin Pimbblet; Kenneth Y\. Wertheim

3D human body reconstruction from egocentric images is a challenging task because of environmental and self\-occlusion\. Downward viewpoints and scale ambiguity can also hinder precise 3D estimation\. Current methods mainly rely on specialized regression networks to reconstruct 3D meshes that often lack structural guidance from high\-dimensional SMPL\-X parameters\. In the proposed work, we introduce EgoTokens, a framework that estimate egocentric SMPL\-X parameters as a discrete sequence\-generation task\. Our end\-to\-end system employs vision\-language models \(VLMs\) to predict SMPL\-X body parameters directly from a single image\. Each of the 122 SMPL\-X parameters is quantized into 1000 bins and represented as an extended vocabulary for training the VLM\. To reflect the extended vocabulary in the network, the corresponding embedding and output\-projection layers are redefined and trained with multiple learning rates to accelerate convergence of new quantized tokens\. The system is trained with a distance\-aware objective that intuitively combines the original cross\-entropy with an L2 regression loss to capture actual numerical closeness between predicted bins\. Standard VLMs with cross\-entropy lack the capability to capture this numerical closeness, and they treat close numbers the same as far numbers\. A language\-instructed semantic shape editing pipeline is also constructed, extending the EgoBody dataset from 150,000 \(visible\) to 1\.3 million instruction\-image\-parameter samples\. This language\-instructed reconstruction allows editing without extra region segmentation\. On the EgoBody dataset, the proposed system achieves a PA\-MPJPE of 29\.49 mm and PA\-MPVPE of 28\.20 mm for fine\-tuning InternVL2\-8B, and a PA\-MPJPE of 33\.43 mm for Qwen2\.5\-VL\-7B\. The results show that the proposed system outperforms the specialized regression and transformer\-based baselines for both InternVL2\-8B and Qwen2\.5\-VL\-7B\. Zero\-shot evaluation on the EHF dataset achieved a PA\-MPVPE of 33\.85 mm, showing the trained model’s generalization from egocentric to third\-person view with complex poses\. The results show that tuned VLMs with distance awareness is a promising direction for 3D human reconstruction and shape control within a single framework\. Code, Model, and Dataset: https://github\.com/gulraizk94/vlm\-smplx\-reconstruction

## [Asociación de multimorbilidad, fragilidad y discapacidad funcional con la autopercepción de la salud en adultos mayores colombianos: un análisis de la encuesta SABE Colombia](../publications/47a0f140db6cdcfc5cf2.md)

Janeth Jurado\-Delgado; José Mauricio Ocampo\-Chaparro; Daniel A\. NIEVA\-POSSO; Carlos A\. Reyes\-Ortiz

Introduction\. Self\-rated health is a general marker of morbidity and mortality that may also be correlated with geriatric conditions\.Objective\. To assess the association of multimorbidity, frailty, and functional disability with self\-rated health in older adults\.Materials and methods\. We used data from the SABE \(Salud, Bienestar y Envejecimiento\) Colombia 2015 survey, which included adults aged 60 years or more\. We analyzed a subsample of 4474 participants and evaluated self\-rated health \(poor versus good\), frailty, multimorbidity, and functional disability\. We used multivariate logistic regression models to assess the association of the dependent variable \(poor self\-rated health\) with frailty, multimorbidity, and functional disability combined as the main independent variables\.Results\. In the first model, poor self\-rated health was significantly associated with frailty/functional disability \(OR = 4\.12; 95% CI: 3\.00\-5\.66; p &lt; 0\.0001\); in the second, with functional disability/multimorbidity \(OR = 3\.54; 95% CI: 2\.73\-4\.58; p &lt; 0\.0001\); in the third, with multimorbidity/frailty \(OR = 3\.15; 95% CI: 2\.49\-3\.98; p &lt; 0\.0001\), and in the fourth, with frailty/functional disability/multimorbidity \(OR = 5\.22; 95% CI: 3\.41\-7\.99; p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. This last model showed the highest association with poor self\-rated health\. Conclusion\. Self\-rated health, a subjective measure for older adults’ health status, was correlated with geriatric conditions such as multimorbidity, frailty, and functional disability\.

## [A quantum\-inspired cross\-attention fusion network for multi\-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images](../publications/47adab1ee5515277bf5a.md)

P\. Abinash; Krishnamoorthy N

Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process\. This study introduces QICAF\-Net, a dual\-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global\-context branch with an EfficientNet local\-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum\-Inspired Cross\-Attention Fusion \(QICAF\) module\. The QICAF module reformulates cross\-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude\-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm\-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity\-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born\-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement\-inspired bilinear interaction\. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed\-up are claimed\. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four\-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy \(DR\), glaucoma and normal categories\. Under stratified five\-fold cross\-validation with six\-view test\-time augmentation \(TTA\), QICAF\-Net attained a macro\-F1 of 0\.9358 ± 0\.0113, an accuracy of 0\.9367 ± 0\.0112 and a macro one\-versus\-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) of 0\.9914 ± 0\.0023; a three\-seed evaluation of the full model gave a macro\-F1 of 0\.9420 ± 0\.0071\. An 18\-run multi\-seed component ablation \(six fusion configurations × three seeds\) confirmed that the quantum\-inspired components achieve accuracy statistically indistinguishable from strong classical fusion baselines, and a paired three\-seed significance test between QICAF\-Net and a matched dual\-branch concatenation model returned no statistically significant accuracy difference \(paired t\-test p = 0\.887; Wilcoxon p = 1\.000\)\. Against five single\-backbone baselines under an identical preprocessing and TTA protocol, QICAF\-Net was competitive but did not exceed the strongest backbones \(Swin\-Tiny 0\.9583, ViT\-Small 0\.9487\)\. The principal contribution of the module is therefore a novel and interpretable formulation rather than a raw accuracy gain\. External validation on a heterogeneous independent cohort \(N = 3,907\) showed heterogeneous cross\-dataset transfer — better preserved for cataract and normal and substantially degraded for glaucoma; under an observed external\-domain shift the diabetic\-retinopathy sensitivity fell to 39\.61%, and under colour\-constancy correction with six\-view TTA the external accuracy was 0\.8741 \(95% CI 0\.8633–0\.8841\) and the macro\-F1 0\.7188 \(95% CI 0\.6969–0\.7398\)\. Two complementary explainability methods together with visualisation of the QICAF attention indicated that the model attends to clinically plausible regions, most strongly the optic nerve head for glaucoma\. Calibration, quantitative explanation\-faithfulness \(deletion/insertion\) and profiler\-based computational analyses were additionally performed\. QICAF\-Net is thus presented as an interpretable and transparently evaluated framework whose accuracy is on par with established fusion strategies while contributing a new attention formulation to the retinal imaging literature\.

## [SOCIO\-CULTURAL DETERMINANTS OF LEXICAL INNOVATION: AN ETYMOLOGICAL ANALYSIS](../publications/47aff7adf5c5a0524e1d.md)

Olesia Stoika; S\.M\. Kucheriava

With the advent of the computer and the dawn of the digital age, access to information has become easier\. People are now able to easily share experiences and integrate foreign loanwords into their own sociocultural space\. The development of modern languages is inseparable from socio\-cultural processes, which significantly influence lexical change and borrow\- ing\. Every major change in society can be easily traced back to linguistic changes\. Technological progress, globalization, and intercultural communication introduce new concepts into people&\#x27;s everyday lives\. As a result, languages need new ways to describe these changes\. This results in a major issue that linguists and translators face\. It is they who primarily take responsibility of normalizing linguistic units\. However, there is no one system that would make it possible\. That is the reason why it is essential to comprehend the factors that influence the emergence of lexical innovations and the patterns governing their occurrence\. Scholars such as William Labov and James Armstrong provide important insights into language change and the nature of lexical innovation\. David Crystal examines the relationship between language and technological development, par\- ticularly in the context of the Internet and digital communication\. Yu\. Savina and Yu\. Laskava focus on the function\- ing of borrowings and the external and internal factors that influence their emergence\. The works of Einar Haugen and Peter Burke are relevant to the study of language contact and the role of social, cultural, and historical interaction in linguistic change\. Translation\-related aspects of lexical innovation are addressed in the studies of Lawrence Venuti and Jean\-Paul Vinay and Jean Darbelnet, whose works help explain how new lexical units and culture\-specific concepts are transferred and adapted across languages\. This article examines the socio\-cultural determinants that influence the emergence and development of lexical inno\- vations\. The main focus is on such factors as technological progress, economic and trade relations, political and historical events, and cultural exchange\. The study also considers how these external changes interact with internal linguistic needs\. These include the principle of language economy and the naming of new concepts\. The analysis reveals that lexical inno\- vation is closely connected with changes in social practices, technological development, cultural interaction, and historical circumstances, which affect both the formation of new lexical units and the ways they are translated and integrated into another language\. The study employs a qualitative approach based on etymological, comparative, and contextual analysis of selected lexical innovations\. Particular attention is drawn to the role of translation in the spread of the new lexicon\. By examining the etymology and development of new words, the study aims to show how changes in society and culture are reflected in vocabulary and how lexical innovations become part of the language over time\.

## [Attentional Focus, Empathy and Gratitude: An Experimental Analysis](../publications/47b31cbe57c7647c5bf3.md)

Esmeralda Villodre‐Marchal; Samuel Mayoral; Gloria Bernabé Valero

Empathy and gratitude are distinct but related prosocial constructs that may be shaped by attentional processes\. This study examined whether attentional orientation influences situational empathic responding and whether dispositional gratitude moderates this effect\. A sample of 198 undergraduate students completed a 20\-item Gratitude questionnaire \(G\-20\) and later participated in a cooperative task under other\-focused, self\-focused, or control instructions\. Both active attentional conditions were associated with greater odds of reporting empathy than the control condition, whereas they did not differ from each other\. Expression of Gratitude was negatively associated with empathic responding\. Gratitude in the Face of Suffering significantly interacted with attentional condition, although none of the condition\-specific associations reached significance\. These findings suggest that directing attention either toward others or toward one&\#x27;s own internal experience may facilitate situational empathic responding\.

## [Estudi de mètodes d&\#x27;aprenentatge profund aplicats per a la detecció del futur deteriorament cognitiu mitjançant polisomnografies](../publications/47b7952d350e23933def.md)

Jorge Reig Aquino

\[ES\] El aprendizaje profundo \(Deep Learning\) es una de las ramas del aprendizaje automático \(Machine Learning\) más importantes en la actualidad\. Si bien su aparición no es reciente, la mejora de la tecnología, capaz de lidiar con inmensas cantidades de datos y operaciones, ha permitido el desarrollo de técnicas cada vez más complejas\. Más concretamente, en el ámbito de las señales biomédicas supone un gran avance en términos de análisis y detección de enfermedades\. Este trabajo tendrá como principal objetivo, por una parte, presentar un profundo análisis teórico de varias arquitecturas de aprendizaje profundo, que a continuación serán aplicadas a la detección del futuro deterioro cognitivo mediante polisomnografías \(registro de señales del cerebro, corazón, músculos, ojos, etc\.\)\. Se emplearán, entre otras, redes neuronales convolucionales de una dimensión \(CNN 1D por sus siglas en inglés\), redes neuronales recurrentes \(RNN\), más en concreto las denominadas Long\-Short Term Memory \(LSTM\), y Transformers\. Se tratará pues, de revisar tanto los modelos algo más clásicos como los más actuales basados en mecanismos de auto\-atención\. Se expondrán las bases, operaciones y funcionamiento que hay detrás de cada uno de ellos para entender por qué pueden ser potencialmente útiles para la aplicación posterior\. Más concretamente, se mostrarán los fundamentos matemáticos formados por operaciones como convoluciones, proyecciones entre subespacios, normalizaciones, aplicaciones no lineales, etc\. para, a continuación, hallar relaciones complejas entre los datos y buscar predecir el futuro deterioro cognitivo\. Mediante funciones de pérdidas, este tipo de redes son capaces de calcular las diferencias entre sus predicciones y la realidad, y, haciendo uso de métodos de optimización basados en el método del descenso del gradiente, modifican sus pesos para las siguientes fases del entrenamiento\. Esta primera fase teórica tratará pues, de ilustrar y desarrollar los conceptos matemáticos que hacen posible que este tipo de modelos funcionen en la práctica, en la que muchas veces son tratadas como simples cajas negras\. Como aplicación de las técnicas anteriores, se trabajará con la base de datos pública proporcionada por el PhysioNet Challenge 2026, que ofrece un conjunto de registros de polisomnografía con el objetivo de predecir diagnósticos futuros de deterioro cognitivo\. En primera instancia, se usarán las anotaciones algorítmicas como entrada de los modelos y una partición del conjunto de datos en entrenamiento, validación y test equilibrados\. Más tarde, se verificarán los resultados con conjuntos de validación y test más ajustados a la prevalencia clínica, es decir, con una prevalencia de casos positivos de entre el 5 y el 15%\. A continuación, se estudiará cómo utilizar las señales crudas y procesos de extracción de características para enriquecer los datos de entrada\. Además, se tratará de encontrar la arquitectura que mejor sea capaz de detectar los casos positivos del conjunto de test en el que se ocultarán las anotaciones humanas, en pos de reducir la dependencia de la toma de datos manual\. Se finalizará con un resumen de las decisiones de diseño tomadas en el transcurso de la realización del trabajo, así como una comparativa entre distintas técnicas y modelos\.

## [Arithmetic and Necessity: A Quasi\-Concrete Modal Structuralist Account](../publications/47ee440de7bd2a22306f.md)

Benjamin Faltesek

Concrete Modal Structuralist Account by Benjamin A\. FaltesekThis dissertation addresses the necessity of arithmetic by distinguishing two tasks that are often run together: the derivation task, which seeks to prove that mathematical truths are necessary, and the characterization task, which asks what kind of necessity arithmetic has and what grounds it\.Setting the former aside for now, I focus on the latter, arguing that an adequate explanation of arithmetical necessity requires two sources: logical necessity and the necessary possibility that the right kind of structure exists\.The second source makes mathematical modality distinctively mathematical, and the dissertation&\#x27;s positive contribution emerges chiefy in that area\.I survey and ultimately cannot accept several existing attempts to ground mathematical necessity: Carnapian linguistic frameworks, set\-theoretic and neo\-logicist reductions, and recent derivation\-task arguments appealing to rigid comprehension or S5\.I then develop a quasi\-concrete modal\-structuralist account\.Working within Hellman&\#x27;s modal structuralism \(but departing from it in some respects\), I construct, rather than merely posit, a witness for the categorical component of the theory\.I use a Fitch\-style construction over formula\-types and argue that it is necessarily possible that an \-sequence exists without assuming either Platonic abstracta or an actual infnity of concrete atoms\.The construction instead relies on quasi\-concrete objects, in Charles Parsons&\#x27; sense, that occupy an intermediate ontological position between the abstract and the concrete\.The resulting account is nominalist\-friendly but not zealous, constructivist without identifying mathematical objects with mental acts, and groundable in modal facts about objects already accessible to us\.v 1\.3Chapter 4: The Categorical Component \. \. \. \. \. \. \. \.

## [Behavioral Analysis of AI\-Assisted User Interaction in a Digital Art Repository](../publications/47fa3ad88a39feb6e595.md)

Minas Pergantis; Andreas P\. Giannakoulopoulos

Recent developments in artificial intelligence, including the emergence of generative AI and large language models, have brought changes to user interaction habits as well as interface design\. These emerging technologies can be integrated into digital art repositories to reshape interaction paradigms through content enrichment, context\-based recommendations, natural\-language querying and automated artwork classification\. As this landscape evolves, it is important to understand how these changes are reflected in user behavior\. In this study, we present a comparative behavioral evaluation based on two versions of a publicly available digital repository for academic artworks: a traditional version and one incorporating a series of AI\-powered features\. A mixed factorial design with task counterbalancing was used to evaluate user behavior through an approach combining platform analytics, self\-reported metrics and qualitative insights\. This exploratory analysis identified feature\-dependent differences in participants’ behavior and perceptions, and yielded preliminary observations that can inform large\-scale research\. Understanding how users perceive and engage with AI features can allow content providers to make informed decisions regarding their integration and streamline user interactions while remaining aligned with stakeholder expectations\.

## [Left atrial appendage occlusion: an alternative to anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation](../publications/47fb83c7f7d1ffce5238.md)

Yosra Messaoudi; Olivier Roux; Pierre A Monney; Olivier Müller; Fabian Nietlispach

Atrial fibrillation \(AF\) is the most common sustained arrhythmia\. Global Burden of Disease estimates indicate that 52\.6 million individuals were living with AF or atrial flutter in 2021, and one in three to one in five persons are expected to develop AF during their lifetime\. AF is associated with an increased risk of stroke, systemic thromboembolism, and death\. Oral anticoagulation \(OAC\) is the first\-line strategy for preventing AF\-associated embolism\. However, embolic events still occur in 1%–4% of anticoagulated patients per year, major bleeding occurs in 2%–4% per year, and long\-term adherence to direct oral anticoagulants \(DOAC\) is incomplete\. Left atrial appendage occlusion \(LAAO\) was developed as a mechanical alternative to address these unmet needs\. The evidence base has changed substantially over the last 2 years: three randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with DOAC—OPTION, CHAMPION\-AF, and CLOSURE\-AF—have now reported\. In this update, we summarize the pathophysiological rationale, the technical aspects of the procedure, and the totality of the randomized and observational evidence, including a 2026 meta\-analysis of 5,890 randomized patients\. Taken together, these data indicate that LAAO reduces non\-procedure\-related bleeding but does not decrease all\-cause major bleeding, intracranial haemorrhage, or mortality, and may carry a higher risk of ischaemic stroke than DOAC\. LAAO remains an established option for patients with contraindications to or intolerance of long\-term OAC\. In DOAC\-eligible patients, it has become a randomized\-tested alternative, but current evidence supports an individualized, shared decision rather than a universal offer\. We outline the remaining controversies—patient selection, device\-related thrombus, peri\-device leak, post\-procedural antithrombotic therapy, and the interpretation of observational data—and the trials designed to resolve them\.

## [How do we understand the pain of the other? The role of imagination in the verbal communication of physical pain](../publications/48031b1f828d57848269.md)

Adriana Joanna Mickiewicz

The article examines the role of imagination in verbal communication of physical pain\. Linguistic research shows that the verbal communication of pain is based on figurative language, including metaphor\. Drawing on Conceptual Metaphor Theory, the theory of grounded cognition and phenomenology I argue that imagination \- understood as an embodied and socially situated capacity for exploring possible experience \- plays a crucial role in interpreting and contextualizing pain metaphors\. I believe that imagination functions as a bridge between subjective experience and intersubjective communication\. The paper develops a non\-reductionist account of empathy with people who experience pain\.

## [Service area extension of PPP\-B2b using clock bias prediction based on frequency stability and orbit age\-extension](../publications/48153815d124c307e952.md)

Wenxuan Liu; Yize Zhang; Junping Chen; Yu Chao; Junsheng Ding; Ziyuan Song; Chenglong Zhang; Quanrun Cheng

Abstract The PPP\-B2b service provided by the BeiDou\-3 Navigation Satellite System \(BDS\-3\) enables high\-precision real\-time precise point positioning \(PPP\) through corrections broadcast by satellites\. However, due to the regional distribution of tracking stations within the Operational Control System \(OCS\), its service area is mainly limited to the Asia\-Pacific region, leading to short correction arcs and data discontinuities near and beyond the service boundary\. To extend this capability beyond its nominal service area, this study proposes a service area extension strategy that combines clock bias prediction based on frequency stability with orbit correction age\-extension\. The clock bias prediction component mitigates arc discontinuity and tail degradation through local frequency estimation, stable estimate screening, starting point refinement, and prediction length control\. Based on 24\-hour clock prediction experiments with different modeling and prediction lengths, practical extrapolation constraints are determined, and clock prediction precision is maintained at the 0\.2 ns level\. Real\-time kinematic PPP experiments using the extended PPP\-B2b products show that the effective service area is extended to the Indochina Peninsula while maintaining centimeter level horizontal and decimeter level vertical accuracy, and further reaches inland Australia under a decimeter level kinematic positioning constraint\.

## [Digital Health Literacy and Health\-Seeking Behaviour Among Hospital Outpatients: Evidence from Traditional, Professional and Online Search Patterns](../publications/481878444075e91be86b.md)

Polat Tunçer; Müberra Dinçer

Introduction\. Digital health literacy may shape how patients seek health information in increasingly digitalized environments where patients use computers, smartphones, tablets and AI\-supported search tools to access health information\. This study examined the association between digital health literacy competencies and traditional, professional and online health\-seeking behaviour among hospital outpatients\. Methods\. A cross\-sectional descriptive\-correlational survey was conducted with 400 volunteer outpatients aged 18 years and older at a training and research hospital in Türkiye\. Participants were recruited equally from pulmonology, internal medicine, obstetrics and gynaecology, ophthalmology and cardiology clinics using quota\-based convenience sampling\. Data were collected using demographic questions, the Health\-Seeking Behaviour Scale and the Digital Health Literacy Competency Scale for Citizens\. Nonparametric group comparisons and Spearman correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26\. Results\. Traditional health\-seeking behaviour had the highest mean score, followed by professional and online health\-seeking behaviour\. Online health\-seeking behaviour was positively correlated with health information literacy \(r\_s=\.446, p&lt;\.001\) and digital competence \(r\_s=\.493, p&lt;\.001\)\. Online health\-seeking behaviour, health information literacy and digital competence decreased with age and increased with education\. Women reported higher online health\-seeking behaviour and digital competence than men\. Conclusion\. Digital health literacy competencies were most clearly associated with online health\-seeking behaviour, while traditional and professional sources remained important\. Outpatient clinics may be useful settings for practical, age\-sensitive and education\-sensitive digital health literacy support\.

## [Disaster preparedness and mental health: understanding psychological responses and support\-system demands](../publications/481b7ddf45ba605f3402.md)

Carlos Rodrigo Garibay Rubio; Genta Nakano; Katsuya Yamori; Astrid Renneé Peralta Gutiérrez; Silvia Morales Chainé; Rebeca Robles; Édgar Landa\-Ramírez; Alexis Bojorge Estrada; Diana Iris Tejadilla Orozco

Disasters pose a formidable challenge for mental health support services in terms of resources and timely response\. This study evaluated the effects of different types of events on the Mexico City population during the first year of the COVID\-19 pandemic, under the assumption that high\-resolution time\-scale data analysis performed on ICT\-based and telehealth systems could contribute to understanding psychological needs and to identifying events associated with short\-term outbursts in support demands, estimating their time of occurrence, and the characteristics of calls for service\. The study evaluated the effects of public announcements of quarantine measures, mental health press conferences, festivities during 2020, and earthquakes with public early warnings between 2020 and 2023 reported through national public institutions’ databases, the “Screening Tool for Mental Health Problems” and the “Lifeline Emergency Phone Call Service \(LEPCS\),” comprising 138,471 interactions\. The analysis used qualitative and quantitative methods, including principal component analysis, correlations, and one\-way ANOVA\. The study successfully identified patterns in responses associated with acute stress, depression, and anxiety, as well as possible times of maximum demand associated with different types of events\. Complex scenarios with multiple threats were associated with significant short\-term outbursts, posing a challenge to support systems, with a documented case with an increase as high as 2651% on a single day\. The research is novel in its time\-scope analysis and event\-wise approach, providing valuable insights for emergency planning and resource allocation\. Additionally, the study proposes evaluation criteria for detecting potential system overloads in telehealth services to enable early countermeasures\.

Vinicius Mikuni; Ibrahim Elsharkawy; Benjamin Nachman

Foundation models build an effective representation of data that can be deployed on diverse downstream tasks\. Previous research showed that the , a foundation model for collider physics, could significantly advance discovery potential across collider experiments\. In this paper, we show that foundation models trained on collider data can transfer to cosmology\. Specifically, we improve the prediction of cosmological parameters and halo and galaxy velocities in different datasets from \. ## [Creating avenues for women to benefit from digitalization](../publications/482ace06b933f0ae19c7.md)

Gaelle Fitong Ketchiwou

There is a rapid transformation in digital technologies worldwide, and digitalisation is now part of all major economic sectors, thereby impacting labour markets\. However, women still lag behind men and are not fully benefiting from the opportunities that come with digitalisation\. This paper aims to unpack what is needed for women to benefit from digitalisation\. The PRISMA protocol was used to perform a comprehensive search across EBSCO, ProQuest, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Scopus, JSTOR, Emerald, and Google Scholar, from which 60 papers were retained after screening\. Articles were analysed in\-depth using a thematic approach\. Findings reveal the need for governments to design initiatives to raise awareness, increase access, and promote the usage of digital technologies, tools, and devices at affordable prices\. Supporting digital infrastructure, partnerships, household conditions and a legal framework are vital\. Together with educational institutions, governments should also develop strategies to boost education and digital skills development, mentorship, and networks to empower women to leverage digital opportunities\. There is also a need to ensure social and work\-life balance support to help women leverage digitalisation\. Hence, governments, educational institutions, private entities, civil society groups, and women need to collaborate to implement tangible actions that ensure meaningful access to technology and the benefits of digitalisation\. By synthesising dispersed evidence from 60 studies, this study integrates conditions, capabilities, and support systems needed for women to benefit from digitalisation and provides actionable initiatives at multiple levels\. This paper highlights the relevance of access to technology, and the need for pathways, capability enhancement, and enabling conditions that make digital skills available for the entry of young women into the labour market and for their career progression in a digital era\. These findings can reduce the digital gender divide, improve women’s labour market participation, or inform policy and practice\.

## [Neural Approaches to Educational Knowledge Graph Construction, Completion, and Reasoning](../publications/482b12e11541a42d349c.md)

Gaganpreet Jhajj

Knowledge Graphs \(KGs\) play a key role in organizing structured data\. However, their incompleteness limits applications in education and intelligent tutoring\. This thesis investigates neural network methods for building, completing, and reasoning over KGs in educational settings\. Four studies are presented\. First, it evaluates Large Language Models \(LLMs\), such as GPT\-4, for constructing and expanding Educational Knowledge Graphs, achieving high semantic similarity \(0\.875\) with instructor\-authored content\. Second, it explores spiking neural network \(SNN\) architectures for interpretable, neuromorphic relational inference in KGs\. Third, it develops an SNN\-based KG embedding framework with learnable synaptic delays for energy\-efficient prerequisite reasoning in intelligent tutoring systems\. Finally, it compares Cache\-Augmented Generation \(CAG\), Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\), and long\-context prompting for generating curriculum knowledge graphs from course materials across 36 courses, revealing trade\-offs between graph size and local deployability\.

## [One Communicator, Three Vendors: Extending the MoA Predictive Theory to a Real NVIDIA\+AMD\+CPU MPI Ensemble](../publications/4839e1d16c4f15a38ef6.md)

Lenore Mullin; Gaetan Hains

The companion MPI\-extension paper validated the first communication\-bearing machine\-shape ensemble: four NVIDIA A100 ranks and four CPU ranks on one NCSA Delta node under one Open MPI job, reassembled by MPI\_Gatherv\. This paper extends it to a multi\-vendor communicator\. A Slurm heterogeneous job spanning Delta&\#x27;s A100 and AMD MI100 partitions places A100, MI100 and CPU ranks \(nine in all\) under one communicator for the first time\. We give the theory \(a w\_i proportional to 1/t\_i weight split for three concurrent realizations; a het\-job specification as an admissible directive\) and report real results, including what the run exposed: the 1/t split assumes time linear in rows, and this fails for the MI100 rank \(6 rows took 597 ms against a linear prediction of 1\.6 ms\)\. A launch\-geometry model, with predictions recorded before measuring, succeeds for the A100 \(time flat from 128 to 3456 rows, stepping at exactly 3520 and 6976\) and places the MI100 floor in the key loop; changing its launch settings cut about 600 ms to 14\.6 ms and the energy per call at 6 rows by 32x, though the MI100 remains about 95x slower than an A100 at 8192 rows\. Controlled reruns show that the companion paper&\#x27;s 8\.1x A100 result and 22 ms Gatherv were artifacts of four ranks sharing one GPU under Open MPI&\#x27;s default transport\. A key/value\-split partition whose message sizes are derived from shapes alone is then run: the ring Allreduce of the 8\.5 MB message took 11\.3, 16\.0 and 15\.3 ms against a predicted 11\-12 ms, the small Allreduce missed its prediction in every run, and compute times reproduce to about 1% while communication times vary up to 4x between runs\. Each idea is introduced with a figure and closed with worked examples\.

## [Joint associations of 2D–3D urban form with land surface temperature along an urban–rural gradient: Implications for sustainable urban planning](../publications/485387351c60139f320e.md)

Liang Zhang; Xue Liu; Xianfan Shu

As fundamental urban units, buildings are closely associated with urban thermal environments, and their morphological attributes are related to spatial variations in thermal conditions\. Although significant progress has been made in characterizing building morphology, the relative importance and joint associations between 2D horizontal characteristics and 3D vertical structures in shaping neighborhood\-scale thermal environments along urban\-rural gradients remain underexplored\. This study integrated multi\-source remote\-sensing data and Geodetector analysis to examine the joint, grid\-level associations of 2D and 3D urban\-form indicators with land surface temperature \(LST\) in Hangzhou, China\. Multi\-temporal LST data from 2000, 2010, 2015, and 2020 were used to characterize the thermal context, whereas the building\-morphology data in 2020 supported a cross\-sectional spatial association analysis\. The results revealed clear spatial variation in the relative explanatory power of morphological indicators\. Specifically, 3D building configurations exhibited the greatest explanatory power in the Core Built\-up Area, whereas 2D characteristics showed stronger associations with LST in the Suburban Built\-up Area\. Interactions between 2D and 3D features generally provided greater explanatory power than individual factors, with several factor pairs showing nonlinear enhancement\. These findings highlight the value of jointly considering horizontal land\-cover patterns and vertical building form when assessing urban thermal environments\. By elucidating gradient\-specific thermal regulation processes and multidimensional interactions among built\-environment features, this study provides a scientific foundation for spatially targeted, climate\-responsive heat mitigation strategies and sustainable urban development\.

## [Integrasi Literasi Digital dalam Pembelajaran Konsep Dasar IPS di Sekolah Dasar Era Society 5\.0](../publications/4854cb1606ef89e47239.md)

Esa Karulina; Firda Rahmatul Laili; Dikky Setiawan; Eki Juniansah; Halisa Halisa

Perkembangan Society 5\.0 yang menekankan integrasi teknologi cerdas seperti Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, dan Big Data dengan nilai kemanusiaan menuntut transformasi pembelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial di Sekolah Dasar\. Pembelajaran IPS yang masih bersifat konseptual, kontekstual dan cenderung hafalan perlu direkonstruksi agar relevan dengan karakteristik peserta didik digital native\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis urgensi, strategi, model, dan tantangan integrasi literasi digital dalam pembelajaran konsep dasar IPS di SD era Society 5\.0\. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi literatur \(library research\) dengan pendekatan content analysis tematik model Miles dan Huberman\. Sumber data berasal dari 40 literatur yang terdiri dari artikel jurnal terindeks SINTA 2\-5 dan Scopus serta dokumen resmi Kemendikbudristek periode 2020\-2025 yang diseleksi melalui model PRISMA\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa \(1\) urgensi integrasi literasi digital terletak pada peningkatan motivasi, hasil belajar, dan kemampuan pemecahan masalah siswa, \(2\) terdapat hubungan yang sangat signifikan antara literasi digital dan kompetensi pedagogik guru terhadap integrasi teknologi, \(3\) strategi efektif meliputi pemanfaatan Google Earth untuk konsep ruang dan media interaktif Canva serta Wordwall\. Model yang direkomendasikan adalah model HUMANISTIS\-DIGITAL berbasis proyek yang terdiri dari empat sintaks: Problematization Digital, Exploration, Creation, dan Human Reflection\. Model ini menekankan keseimbangan antara penguasaan teknologi dan penguatan karakter kreatif serta etika digital sesuai tujuan Society 5\.0\.

## [Ревизия соблюдения законодательства о защите персональных данных: методика и последствия нарушений для репутации и бизнеса](../publications/485a5a88176d85edc6bf.md)

С\.М\. Давлетшина; О\.О\. Юлдашев

В статье рассматриваются теоретические и прикладные аспекты проведения ревизии соответствия законодательству о персональных данных на примере требований Федерального закона № 152\-ФЗ и Регламента GDPR\. Проведен анализ правовых и репутационных последствий нарушений с учетом изменений законодательства в 2023–2025 гг\., в том числе введения оборотных штрафов и уголовной ответственности\. На основе анализа судебной практики обосновывается вывод о необходимости интеграции регулярного комплаенса в систему управления рисками для предотвращения финансовых потерь и сохранения деловой репутации\. This article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of conducting compliance audits with personal data legislation, using the requirements of Federal Law No\. 152\-FZ and the GDPR as examples\. The legal and reputational consequences of violations are analyzed, taking into account legislative changes for 2023–2025, including the introduction of turnover\-based fines and criminal liability\. Based on an analysis of judicial practice, the conclusion is made regarding the need to integrate regular compliance into the risk management system to prevent financial losses and preserve business reputation\.

## [LEASH: Uncertainty\-Aware Weak\-to\-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer\-Use Agents](../publications/486abd2348d74550aa67.md)

Qingni Wang; Changdae Oh; Yuzhe Yang; Sharon Li; Jiachen Yang; Ang Li; Xin Eric Wang

Computer\-use agents increasingly tackle long\-horizon tasks, where running a frontier model at every step is expensive and a small open\-weight model alone often fails\. Weak\-to\-strong escalation offers a middle ground where a weak agent acts by default and hands control to a strong one only when needed\. The core challenge is deciding when to escalate, which requires an uncertainty signal cheap enough to check at every step\. However, even after handoff, the strong agent can still get lost, but a black\-box API that the strong agent is usually served exposes no internals to monitor\. To this end, we propose LEASH, a training\-free framework that unleashes the strong agent only when the weak agent&\#x27;s latent uncertainty signals it is needed, and keeps it on a leash afterward\. LEASH has three layers: \(1\) initial task uncertainty for early routing, \(2\) step\-level uncertainty for runtime escalation, and, after handoff, \(3\) a shadow observer for continued oversight of the strong black\-box agent\. Here, we use latent uncertainty as a fuel for all three layers\. Specifically, we compare the weak model&\#x27;s hidden states with those from its past successful and failed trajectories, and a state that looks more like the failures signals higher uncertainty\. During weak\-agent execution, our uncertainty estimator reuses activations already produced during action generation, so it needs no extra forward pass or dedicated monitor training\. Experiments on OSWorld across four contemporary model backbones show that LEASH consistently improves over standalone weak agents and outperforms random escalation by 6\.55\-\-11\.94 points at matched escalation rates\. With Qwen3\.5\-35B\-A3B, LEASH achieves 73\.66% task success at $0\.4117 per task, matching always\-on Claude Opus 5 \(72\.90%\) while reducing inference cost by 19\.2%\.

## [Large language models on tabular data based molecular property prediction \(MPP\) of RP\-3 kerosene](../publications/4871c0bf8fc4c9a85dd8.md)

Muhammad Hassaan Athar; Yong Hu; Feiyang Zhao; Wenbin Yu

Accurate modeling of multicomponent fuel properties is important for surrogate fuel design, where complex composition\-property relationships motivate the development of advanced data\-driven prediction strategies\. In this study, we evaluate pretrained molecular and general\-purpose language model representations for predicting physiochemically distinct properties of RP\-3 kerosene surrogates using SMILES\-derived embeddings and composition\-based information\. Four supervised machine learning \(ML\) models \(SVM, GPR, RF and k\-NN\) were compared with three transformer\-based representations \(ChemBERTa, MolFormer and TinyLlama \(1\.1B\)\) across different dataset configurations\. The results demonstrate that the predictive performance depends on both dataset size and feature representation strategy\. For the 1000\-sample dataset, TinyLlama achieved stable predictive performance \(average R 2 = 0\.9962\), whereas the expanded 6000\-sample dataset enabled ChemBERTa to achieve high prediction accuracy, explaining 99% of the property variance \(RMSE = 0\.126, MRE = 0\.18%\) outperforming both MolFormer and TinyLlama\. Notably, TinyLlama lacking any chemistry specific pretraining, still achieves R 2 = 0\.995, purely from serialized composition and structured prompts, demonstrating that contextual language embeddings can encode chemically meaningful information within the investigated RP\-3 surrogate fuel system\. Cosine similarity and residual analyses confirm that the pretrained representations capture meaningful differences between aromatic and saturated hydrocarbon structures while maintaining strong predictive stability\. The controlled ablation study further demonstrates that composition information alone provides highly accurate prediction within the investigated surrogate system, while molecular embeddings provide additional chemically informed representation capability\. These findings establish a framework for evaluating pretrained molecular and language\-model representations for RP\-3 surrogate fuel property prediction, with potential extension toward broader hydrocarbon fuel systems after validation using more diverse molecular libraries and experimental datasets\.

## [A Design Pattern Catalog for Applying Large Language Models in the Systems Engineering Lifecycle](../publications/487cb4a8242054291554.md)

Bedir Teki̇nerdoğan

ABSTRACT The integration of Large Language Models \(LLMs\) into the systems engineering lifecycle presents a transformative opportunity to enhance decision‐making, automate documentation, and support complex engineering tasks through intelligent assistance\. However, current applications of LLMs in this domain remain fragmented, experimental, and often lack systematic guidance for reuse\. This paper presents a structured design pattern catalog for applying LLMs across key phases of the systems engineering lifecycle, including requirements engineering, system architecture, verification and validation, and operations and maintenance\. Each design pattern encapsulates a recurring problem, its context, and a proven LLM‐enabled solution, supported by real‐world scenarios and implementation considerations\. By formalizing these patterns, we aim to bridge the gap between state‐of‐the‐art language models and established systems engineering practices, enabling practitioners to adopt LLMs more effectively, consistently, and responsibly\. The catalog also addresses cross‐cutting concerns such as traceability, human‐in‐the‐loop interaction, and lifecycle integration\. A multi‐case study approach, incorporating real‐world industrial applications, validates the identification and practical utility of these patterns, demonstrating their impact on improving systems engineering outcomes\.

## [In the Guise of Correction: How Framing and Cultural Adaptation Erode LLM Safety on Real\-World Criminal Cases](../publications/489b538e14ebfb147762.md)

Mohsinul Kabir; Md\. Tariquzzaman; Karam S\. R\. Elradie; Polydoros Giannouris; Yuechen Jiang; Shaoxiong Ji; Sophia Ananiadou

Existing safety benchmarks rely largely on synthetic prompts with loosely grounded taxonomies and offer little focused analysis of severe crime categories\. We introduce GUISE, a benchmark of criminal\-assistance scenarios sourced from real\-world cases and organised under a taxonomy from the UNODC International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes \(ICCS\)\. Each scenario is rendered under three linguistic framings and evaluated across five distinct cultures\. Using our proposed two\-tier evaluation framework, which judges both harmfulness and operational uplift, we find that: \(i\) framing alone drives unsafe compliance, with the mean unsafe compliance rate rising from 28\.9% under direct requests to 66\.4% under correction seeking \(peaking at 97\.3%; p &lt; 0\.05\), as models correcting deliberately distorted details supply executable criminal steps; \(ii\) culturally adapted prompts elicit significantly more unsafe compliance than literal translations of the same requests in all four non\-English languages \(\+7 to \+18 points\), a risk that translation\-based benchmarks miss; and \(iii\) unsafe responses from the least\-safe models carry strong Anglocentric registers, and the extent of this leakage increases monotonically with response harmfulness \($ρ$ = 0\.46 to 0\.63 across languages, all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. GUISE offers a grounded resource and fine\-grained diagnostics for strengthening refusal alignment across languages and cultures\. We publish our code and data to facilitate future research\.

## [Implementasi Sistem Informasi Pendaftaran dan Upload Hasil Karya Event Terpadu pada Bee Creative Event Organizer](../publications/48a861bac0b6f19aaaa1.md)

Nur Hidayah; Nugroho Adhi Santoso; Bayu Aji Santoso

This research focuses on developing and implementing an integrated, web\-based information system for event registration and submission of entries at Bee Creative Event Organizer, serving as an alternative to the previous manual process that relied on WhatsApp\. The system was developed using the waterfall approach, encompassing the stages of requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance\. It was built using the PHP programming language with the Laravel 10 framework and a MySQL database\. Four user roles are defined within the system: the public \(with limited access to view event information\); participants \(who can register, upload entries, and monitor registration status via a participant dashboard\); administrators \(with full access to manage event data, registrations, winners, the gallery, and homepage content\); and management \(who can view event revenue charts\)\. The system also features a Chatbot and WhatsApp integration to facilitate communication with participants\. This research contributes by integrating event registration and entry management processes, which had previously not been combined into a single system, while also supporting both online and offline events on one unified platform\. The results demonstrate that the system successfully integrates event registration, entry submissions, and participant management into a unified platform\. Black\-box testing conducted on 107 test cases across four primary roles yielded a 100% success rate, indicating that the system is highly reliable\. The system simplifies the process for participants to register and upload entries directly via the Website while enabling administrators to manage data in a structured and efficient manner\.

## [Platform\-Enabled AI Adoption and Supply Chain Resilience in Chinese SMEs: an Integrated Theoretical Framework](../publications/48bfb016d6cf21ef6d04.md)

Depeng Pan

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is profoundly reshaping the global supply chain landscape\. However, the mechanism through which Chinese small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\), under resource constraints, acquire AI capabilities through digital platforms and transform them into supply chain resilience has not been adequately theorized\. This paper develops an integrated theoretical framework that combines the Technology–Organization–Environment \(TOE\) framework with dynamic capability theory\. It proposes the analytical concept of “platform\-enabled AI adoption&quot; to characterize the distinctive technology adoption pattern through which Chinese SMEs acquire, integrate, and utilize AI capabilities via external digital platforms\. Using a literature review and case analysis approach, and drawing on the 2025 survey report of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, publicly available operating data from the 1688 platform and Haizhi Online, and relevant academic literature from the past decade, this paper systematically analyzes three mediating pathways through which platform\-enabled AI adoption affects supply chain resilience: supply chain visibility, supply chain agility, and supply chain collaboration\. It further discusses the moderating roles of technological readiness and organizational readiness in this relationship and offers methodological suggestions for future empirical research\. This paper provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the relationship between AI adoption and supply chain resilience among Chinese SMEs in the digital platform context and offers testable research propositions for subsequent empirical examination\.

## [CVOT summit report 2025](../publications/48c5ff8a453c18c3fc4b.md)

Oliver Schnell; Arnav Agarwal; Michel Azizi; Dennis Ballwieser; Katharine D\. Barnard\-Kelly; Matthias; https://orcid\.org/0000\-0003\-0208\-2065 Blüher; Elisabetta Bugianesi; Ana Cebrián; Antonio Ceriello; Pratik Choudhary; Tadej Battelino

The 11th Cardiovascular Outcome Trial \(CVOT\) Summit: Congress on Cardiovascular, Kidney, and Metabolic Outcomes was held virtually on November 20–21, 2025\. The Summit provided a multidisciplinary forum to review and discuss recent outcome trials investigating emerging pharmacological therapies targeting diseases of the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic \(CKM\) continuum\. This report highlights the unique developments of 2025 discussed during the Summit, including the first head\-to\-head CVOT \(SURPASS\-CVOT\), the growing evidence base for combination therapies across the disease spectrum, new insights into the inflammatory component of the CKM syndrome, and relevant policy developments\. The first part of this report summarizes pioneering clinical trials addressing combination therapy with finerenone and empagliflozin \(CONFIDENCE\), the oral glucagon\-like peptide\-1 \(GLP\-1\) receptor agonists orforglipron \(ATTAIN\-1\), and the aldosterone synthase inhibitor \(ASI\) baxdrostat \(BaxHTN\)\. In addition, advances in medical technology, particularly in continuous glucose and ketone monitoring, are highlighted, as well as emerging therapies for diseases of the CKM continuum\. These include pharmacological agents for a broad spectrum of metabolic disorders such as metabolic liver disease and type 1 Diabetes \(T1D\) alongside emphasis on the importance of early detection and innovative treatment strategies\. The 12th Cardiovascular Outcome Trial Summit will be held virtually on 19–20 November 2026 \(http://www\.cvot\.org\)\.

## [MARS: A Momentum\-Aware Adaptive Rating System for Personalized Assessment](../publications/48c8e9fce7e067573570.md)

Vikrant Sahu; Khethavath Sunil Naik; Gagan Raj Gupta

Adaptive assessment systems personalize learning by estimating learner proficiency and recommending suitable questions\. However, many existing approaches rely on fixed difficulty labels, static rating updates, or black\-box prediction models that provide limited control over rating stability, interpretability, and time\-constrained routing\. This paper proposes MARS, a Momentum\-Aware Adaptive Rating System for interpretable adaptive assessment\. MARS represents the question bank as a directed weighted knowledge graph and updates learner proficiency using dynamic rating sensitivity, response quality, and momentum\-aware learner velocity\. We also formulate a time\-budgeted mark\-maximization objective in which the policy selects questions within a fixed test duration under negative marking\. Experiments on ASSISTments 2009 and MARS\-SimExam evaluate MARS for prediction, rating stability, and adaptive routing\. Results show that MARS provides smoother rating updates than Fixed Elo and achieves the highest score under time\-budgeted negative\-marking routing, improving the total score by 8\.09 over the strongest baseline and reducing overtime violations from 50% to 5\.6%\. These results suggest that MARS is suitable for real\-time, interpretable, and deployment\-friendly adaptive assessment\.

## [Therapeutic physical activity as a recreational intervention for anger control among students with physical disability: a behavioral model](../publications/48d38b6b2a008a23c00e.md)

Ahmed K\. Hassan; Maryam Khalifah Arab; Abdulmalek K\. Bursais; Badeer Aldimkhi; Albujulaya Naif

Background Therapeutic Physical Activity \(TPA\) is an unaddressed behavioral recreational method in anger management programs in higher education in Egypt, especially among students with physical disabilities \(SWPD\)\. Purpose This study aimed to assess the efficacy of an 8\-week TPA intervention on the severity of anger in male university students with physical disabilities in Egypt\. Methods A randomized controlled trial \(RCT\) design \(parallel\-group\) was used with 140 male undergraduate students at Minia University who were randomly divided into an 8\-week TPA group \( n = 70\) and a treatment\-as\-usual \(TAU\) control group \( n = 70\)\. Severity of anger was measured at baseline and at the end of the intervention with the PROMIS Anger Short Form 8a\. Results There was a clinically significant and statistically significant difference between the TPA and controls in the severity of anger, F \(1, 137\) = 48\.62, p &lt; 0\.001, partial η 2 = 0\.262, with a mean difference of −10\.42 T\-score points \(95% CI: −13\.48, −7\.36\) greater than the MCID\. Reductions in anger were not associated with physical functioning changes, indicating non\-physiological mechanisms\. Moderately positive relationships were found between adherence and anger reduction \(r = 0\.42; p &lt; 0\.001\), and sensitivity analyses showed that the results were consistent across disability severity\. Conclusion TPA is a culturally affirming, body\-based, anger\-management approach that incorporates adaptive sports and behavioral learning for SWPD emotion regulation\. Therapeutic recreation may be implemented as a low\-stigma, easy\-to\-access supplemental mental health support program in the University disability services, especially for male students in collectivist contexts\.

## [Prolonged Estradiol Persistence and Possible Symptom\-Biomarker Dissociation During Sequential Estradiol Implant Therapy in a Postmenopausal Woman: A Case Report](../publications/48e9030a5d8be0cfa077.md)

Loreta Canivilo Salas de Souza Moraes; Wilmar Accursio; Matheus H Ferreira; Juliana de Oliveira Moreira Gomes Carneiro; Guilherme Renke; Zahid Khan

Subcutaneous estradiol implants are a long\-acting modality of menopausal hormone therapy whose behavior during sequential implantations remains poorly characterized\.We report a 52\-year\-old woman with natural menopause at the age of 48 years, who was followed for 45 months during five sequential 25 mg estradiol implants combined with gestrinone\.Testosterone 50 mg was added from the fourth implantation due to low sexual desire\.Estradiol concentrations remained measurable at all assessed post\-implantation time points, ranging from 56 to 156 pg/mL\.Gonadotropin fluctuations and late recurrence of vasomotor symptoms were observed despite persistent estradiol exposure\.Reimplantation decisions were guided by clinical assessment integrated with serial hormonal monitoring rather than fixed intervals\.Endometrial protection with dydrogesterone was maintained, and no adverse events were observed or reported\.This case illustrates prolonged estradiol persistence, gonadotropin variability, and possible symptom\-biomarker dissociation during sequential implant therapy, reinforcing the need for an individualized approach that integrates symptoms, hormone levels, and endometrial assessment\.

## [A Quantitative Study on the Role of Emotional Regulation and Coping Strategies in Predicting Smartphone Overuse among Malaysian Young Adults in Klang Valley](../publications/48f0932a2ad301f03877.md)

Misa Kikuchi; Shalini A/P Munusamy

This paper investigates the role of emotional regulation and coping strategies in predicting smartphone overuse among Malaysian young adults in Klang Valley\. A quantitative study was done among 191 Malaysian young adults between the age 18 to 25\. Multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to explore the relationship and predictive effects of emotion\-oriented coping, task\-oriented coping, avoidance\-oriented coping, cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression on smartphone overuse\. Smartphone overuse was found to be significantly positively correlated with emotion\-oriented and avoidance\-oriented coping\. However, only emotion\-oriented coping was found to significantly predict smartphone overuse \(beta = \.40, p &lt; \.001\), while task\-oriented coping, avoidance\-oriented coping, cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression were not significant predictors\. ## [Mistrust, uncertainty, fear, and vaccine acceptability: Quasi\-experimental data from the United Kingdom and Portugal during the COVID\-19 pandemic](../publications/490a5ce5e98c3113f7bd.md)

Glynis M\. Breakwell; Rusi Jaspal

Using a quasi\-experimental design, this study tests a cognitive\-affective model of vaccine acceptability focusing on the effects of relationships between trust, certainty, attitudes, and fear in a sample of 1132 adults in the UK \(N=648 \[51\.7%\]\) and Portugal \(N=486 \[48\.3%\]\) during the COVID\-19 pandemic\. A path model of the relationships between the variables was assessed using structural equation modeling\. Participants in the experimental condition were asked to list what they thought were the major societal uncertainties concerning the COVID\-19 vaccines \(N=566 \[49\.9%\]\)\. When subsequently asked, those in the experimental condition reported lower vaccine certainty than those in the control condition \(N=568 \[50\.1%\]\)\. Across the entire sample, lower vaccine certainty was associated with lower vaccine acceptability\. Higher vaccine uncertainty was associated with less negativity toward vaccine refusers \(which in turn was associated with lower vaccine acceptability\)\. In addition to the direct positive effect of trust in science and scientists upon vaccine acceptability, there were mediated effects: higher trust in science and scientists was associated with higher fear\. Fear was positively associated with vaccine certainty\. Fear was also positively associated with negativity toward vaccine refusers\. The results suggest that, in health crises, people may be more susceptible to identify with other vaccine refusers \(and potentially “anti\-vaxxer” groups\) if levels of uncertainty and mistrust are higher, thereby undermining vaccine uptake\. The study makes an original contribution to the literature on vaccine acceptability by showing that vaccine certainty \(and changes in vaccine acceptability\) can be modified by a single intervention that asks people to describe what they think are important vaccine uncertainties\. Furthermore, by examining the relationship of attitudes to ‘anti\-vaxxers’ with the cognitive\-affective model of vaccine acceptability, the research indicates the potential significance of uncertainty and fear upon social attitudes\.

## [Personal Health\-care Management and Depression among Patients with Epilepsy](../publications/490aba1b40f09b0daaf2.md)

Suganya Aravazhi M

Background: Epilepsy is a long\-term brain condition that causes seizures\. Depression is an important psychiatric comorbidity among individuals with epilepsy\. In health care, recent devices such as wearable seizure detectors, smart medication reminders, mobile health applications, and remote monitoring systems have shown promise in enhancing disease management\. These technologies can support continuous patient monitoring while reducing the burden of frequent hospital visits\. Objective: The main objective of this study is to assess the personal healthcare management alongside depression among patients with epilepsy\. Methods and materials: A total of 92 patients with epilepsy, were selected based on inclusion criteria\. In a tertiary care facility, a cross\-sectional study was carried out in Chennai\. Patients were interviewed face\-to\-face using interview schedule which consists of four sections\. SPSS used for statistical analysis\. Results: The findings indicate that among the clinical variables examined, duration of disease, family history of epilepsy, and the last seizure episode were the factor significantly associated with depression severity, while presence of comorbidities showed no statistically significant associations\. findings suggest that while participants are relatively familiar with commonly used wearable safety and monitoring devices, awareness of more specialized and advanced IoMT technologies remains poor\. Conclusion: The findings highlight the patients’ educational interventions and utilization of IoMT devices in epilepsy personal health care management\.
