## [Estamos realmente conectados? Proposta de modelo de avaliação do relacionamento com clientes do e\-commerce](../publications/491a9026fe1207694c7a.md)

Yuri de Souza Odaguiri Enes; Gisela Demo

A transição do comércio tradicional para o ambiente virtual transformou o comportamento dos consumidores e o posicionamento das organizações, tornando o marketing de relacionamento essencial na retenção de clientes\. Nesse contexto, o objetivo deste estudo foi avaliar os aspectos essenciais para a construção e manutenção de um relacionamento com uma marca de comércio eletrônico, sob a perspectiva dos consumidores brasileiros\. Desse modo, adaptou\-se um instrumento seminal validado no Reino Unido ao contexto nacional por meio de tradução, análise de juízes, análise semântica e pré\-teste\. A partir deste instrumento, realizou\-se uma survey com 416 participantes, utilizando Análise Fatorial Exploratória, Análise Fatorial Confirmatória e Modelagem por Equações Estruturais\. Foram obtidas evidências de validade exploratória e confirmatória, de confiabilidade e de conteúdo da escala denominada Escala de Relacionamento com Clientes do E\-commerce\. A escala final estrutura\-se em três fatores: Experiência com o site, Relacionamento com a marca e Experiência de compra\. Este estudo amplia a compreensão do relacionamento entre clientes e marcas digitais ao identificar os principais elementos necessários ao desenvolvimento e à manutenção de relações sólidas no ambiente de comércio eletrônico, por meio da adaptação de um instrumento científico à realidade brasileira\. Foram identificadas as principais características do relacionamento de clientes com empresas de comércio eletrônico, permitindo processos de decisão e o desenvolvimento de estratégias de marketing baseadas no comportamento do consumidor\. Ainda, a literatura avançou com a produção de um instrumento operacionalmente válido e confiável para a avaliação de relacionamentos no comércio eletrônico a partir da perspectiva dos clientes brasileiros\.

## [How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning](../publications/491ed3362a0ed30c7a17.md)

Ashray Saxena; Sharad Shrivastava

Isogai&\#x27;s case A, a pitch\-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number\. We map this boundary, and the family obtained by moving the elastic axis, with coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian\-process surrogate of the damping coefficient trained by batch active learning, and split conformal prediction on independent random simulations, which turns the surrogate into stability calls with a distribution\-free error rate\. Three failure modes of time\-domain damping labels that leave no trace in the residuals are documented, and the half\-degree mean incidence left by the common one\-degree start is shown to raise the flutter speed at the dip by 2\.8%, more than any numerical setting\. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 64 of 65 independent runs correctly, and calibrated calls are wrong in at most 1\.6% of cases\. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs show that the fold exists only for elastic axes more than about 0\.4 chord ahead of the leading edge; it closes between 0\.39 and 0\.33 chord ahead, on two meshes\. Chordwise energy budgets, closed against the solver loads and the growth rate within a few per cent, explain the boundary\. The lower branch is crossed through the reduced frequency at unchanged shock phase\. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge, and moving the elastic axis aft brings the pivot of the flutter mode towards the section, so that the damping of the supersonic surface falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes\.

## [Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding](../publications/4928ea16c1c29f399d0e.md)

Jinho Choi; Hyesu Lim; Jaegul Choo; Steffen Schneider

Sparse autoencoders \(SAEs\) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms\. However, the learned dictionaries can vary across training runs, limiting the reliability and reproducibility of SAE\-based analyses\. We propose Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning \(ConSDL\), which replaces the standard linear encoder with per\-sample sparse coding\. This is motivated by our synthetic analysis showing that coefficients from a single linear encoder pass are suboptimal compared with those obtained by per\-sample optimization, suggesting that sparse coding is a reliable mechanism for dictionary learning\. Across 16 synthetic settings, ConSDL achieves near\-perfect dictionary and coefficient recovery\. These gains translate to state\-of\-the\-art cross\-seed consistency across four vision and language settings, where ConSDL improves dictionary and coefficient consistency by 17\.6% and 35\.9%, respectively, over the average of six SAE baselines\.

## [Detecting Trade\-Based Money Laundering in the Documents Themselves: A Cross\-Validation Graph with Closed\-Loop Self\-Iteration](../publications/4939ba8386fb8fd7957a.md)

Shijie Qu

Trade\-based money laundering \(TBML\) hides in the documents of trade rather than in the payments that settle it\. Conventional transaction\-monitoring systems examine amounts, frequencies, and velocities, and are therefore blind to the documentary substance of a shipment; machine\-learning systems trained on transaction\-level features inherit the same blindness; and static models of either kind decay as laundering typologies migrate across goods, corridors, and forgery techniques\. This paper describes a detection system, disclosed in U\.S\. Provisional Patent Application No\. 64/170,275, that is organised around the documents themselves\. Heterogeneous trade documents — commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, packing lists, letters of credit, and associated payment records — are parsed into canonical shipment assertions that retain provenance metadata, and entity mentions across documents are resolved to canonical identities, with alias collisions preserved as signals rather than merged away\. The resolved material is assembled into a heterogeneous entity–document–shipment graph whose edges are of two kinds: documentary edges recording what each document declares, and consistency edges — computationally verifiable assertions linking attributes across documents that purport to describe the same shipment — each carrying a consistency score\. From this graph the system computes features that encode known TBML typologies at the documentary level: unit\-price deviation against benchmark price distributions indexed by HS code, trade corridor, and time window; cross\-document quantity and value reconciliation; circular\-trading cycles; phantom\-shipment document asymmetries; and shipment\-structuring patterns\. A calibrated scoring model emits per\-shipment and per\-entity risk scores with machine\-readable documentary reason codes, exposed through a real\-time scoring API designed for pre\-settlement interception\. Investigation outcomes — suspicious activity report filings, confirmed typologies, and analyst labels — close the loop: confirmed activity reweights the suspicious\-entity subgraph and re\-runs community detection, labelled cases retrain the model, an active\-learning strategy allocates analyst review by uncertainty over graph neighbourhoods, and per\-corridor stationarity testing of benchmark price distributions detects typology drift and triggers benchmark re\-estimation, targeted labelling, and model refresh — all without manual feature re\-engineering\. A further embodiment extends the graph across the full lifecycle of direct\-to\-consumer cross\-border e\-commerce\. The paper reports no evaluation and no measurements; numerical values cited are the design targets and structural parameters stated in the disclosure\.

## [From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self\-Improving Agents](../publications/493b9a5b0d22f24f2795.md)

Yewei Zhao; Derong Xu; Wei Chen; Yin Xu; Peilun Zhou; Xiaohan Wang; Guojun Yin; Wei Lin; Mingjun Xiao

Large language model \(LLM\) agents tackle complex tasks through reasoning and interaction with external environments\. Agent skills provide persistent, transferable capabilities that guide task planning, inform contextual decisions, support tool use, and enable executable procedures\. Yet existing skill\-evolution methods largely organize knowledge around skill artifacts, overlooking the functional heterogeneity within individual skills and its implications for knowledge maintenance and use\. Inspired by cognitive science, we propose Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution \(CDSE\), which evolves a unified skill through four functionally distinct yet coordinated components: Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script\. CDSE extracts evidence\-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories, consolidates them by functional role, and applies component\-specific updates and validation with cross\-component coordination and adaptive invocation\. An analysis of 500 top\-ranked skill packages shows that 96\.8% contain knowledge spanning at least two functional roles\. Across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, CDSE achieves the highest scores in all 36 settings, improving over the Base agent by 7\.6 percentage points and the strongest competing method in each setting by 2\.6 points on average\. Ablation studies further support the importance of functional differentiation and adaptive invocation\.

## [The Impact of Social Media on the Realization of the Right to a Fair Trial in the Republic of Kosovo](../publications/493cc2eb05460d290397.md)

Valeri Qatani

Background: Social media may create conditions that influence public perceptions and potentially exert pressure on judicial actors\. Using statistics obtained directly from citizens of the Republic of Kosovo, this paper examines how social media has influenced the realization of judicial impartiality\. However, this paper particularly emphasises the negative role of social media in the realization of judicial impartiality\. Another challenge is that public opinion is shaped by how information is distributed through social media and how convictions are formed in society\. The impact of social media is inevitable, as we are witnessing enough cases in practice; the prejudices transmitted on social media are reaching their peak and are being perceived by society\. Method: This study employed a quantitative survey\-based research design complemented by an analysis of selected judicial cases\. The study collected empirical data through a structured questionnaire administered to 492 respondents in the Republic of Kosovo\. The questionnaire included five\-point Likert scale items designed to test three research hypotheses concerning public opinion formation, the presumption of innocence, and perceived pressure on judicial actors\. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and interpreted alongside selected high\-profile criminal cases and the applicable legal framework\. Results and Conclusions: The results indicate that social media influences public opinion about judicial processes in the Republic of Kosovo, clearly shaping how the public perceives them\. Furthermore, exposing judicial cases on social media jeopardises the presumption of innocence, as public information and commentary can create bias before the judicial process concludes\. At the same time, social media can compromise judicial impartiality through public pressure and the influence of social perceptions on judicial decision\-making\.

## [Visualizing, modeling and forecasting age distribution of fertility](../publications/493eb23c4f3af41c0305.md)

Han Lin Shang; Yang Yang

The study of fertility differences has often focused on average fertility levels, such as age\-specific fertility rates, while neglecting the age distribution of fertility\. We introduce three novel summary statistics to analyze fertility distributions: we identify the modal age of women for each year; we use Wasserstein distance to find the medoid density; and we apply Taylor’s power law to assess regional heterogeneity in the age distribution of fertility\. Then, we present two methods for modeling and forecasting state\-wise fertility gaps\. A compositional data analytic framework, particularly a centered log\-ratio transformation, is employed to generate out\-of\-sample density forecasts\. The cumulative distribution function supports visualization and comparison of fertility densities\. Applied to Australian birth counts from 1975 to 2024, our results show a decline in births along with continued postponement of childbearing, with Victoria projected to experience greater delays than New South Wales and Queensland\.

## [Prospective evaluation of combination oral S\-1 and intravenous cisplatin in cancer patients with severe hepatic dysfunction – a feasibility, safety, and pharmacokinetic study](../publications/4940c135a700ab115c61.md)

Yong Xiang Gwee; Andrea Li Ann Wong; Boon Cher Goh; Ross Andrew Soo; Wei Peng Yong; David S\.P\. Tan; Cheng Ean Chee; Siew Eng Lim; Yvonne Ang; Yiqing Huang; Wan Qin Chong; Joline Lim; Gloria Hui Jia Chan; Natalie Y\.L\. Ngoi; Samuel G\.W\. Ow; Rachel Wong; Kenneth W\.X\. Sooi; Joan R\.E\. Choo; Soo Chin Lee

Introduction Patients with advanced solid tumors and severe hepatic dysfunction have limited systemic therapy options due to impaired drug metabolism and increased toxicity risks\. This population is often excluded from clinical trials, leaving a critical treatment gap\. This study evaluates the feasibility, safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of S\-1, an oral prodrug of 5\-fluorouracil \(5\-FU\), plus cisplatin in these patients\. Methods Between September 2016 and November 2023, 61 patients were enrolled into four cohorts based on hepatic function per NCI\-ODWG criteria: normal \(Cohort 1\), mild \(Cohort 2\), moderate \(Cohort 3\), and severe dysfunction \(Cohort 4\)\. Primary endpoints were safety and 5\-fluorouracil pharmacokinetics; secondary endpoints included objective response rate \(ORR\) and 3\-month clinical benefit rate \(3M\-CBR\)\. Results On Cycle 1 day 15, patients with severe hepatic dysfunction \(Cohort 4\) had lower 5\-FU C max and longer T max than those with normal hepatic function \(Cohort 1\) \(p&lt;0\.05\), though 5\-FU AUC remained comparable across cohorts\. Safety in Cohort 4 were similar to those in Cohorts 1–3\. No grade 5 treatment\-related adverse events occurred\. In Cohort 4, 22\.2% achieved a partial response, 40\.7% derived clinical benefit, and 22\.2% maintained progression\-free survival ≥6 months, providing preliminary evidence of clinical activity in this population\. Conclusion Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction had similar 5\-FU AUC and toxicities to those with less severe hepatic dysfunction, and preliminary evidence of clinical activity was observed with cisplatin \+ S\-1\. These findings provide prospective preliminary evidence that this combination may be feasible in selected patients with severe hepatic dysfunction, a population frequently excluded from clinical trials\. Larger studies are needed to further define its safety, pharmacokinetics, and clinical activity in this population\. \(Clinical Trial Registration: NCT03519074\. Retrospectively registered 08 May 2018\)\.

## [Cancer nanomedicine and RNA/Lipid nanoparticle platforms in oncology: developmental evolution, translational barriers, and precision\-therapy opportunities](../publications/4953315e390d7fcb0145.md)

Bhasker Sambar; Anil Kumar Dudam

Nanomedicine has become an important translational platform in oncology by enabling altered pharmacokinetics, controlled exposure, reduced systemic toxicity, intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, and improved handling of complex therapeutic payloads\. Early cancer nanomedicines, including pegylated liposomal cytotoxics and albumin\-bound drug products, demonstrated that nanoscale formulation design could improve the clinical utility of established anticancer agents\. More recently, lipid nanoparticles, RNA therapeutics, individualized neoantigen vaccines, gene\-regulatory approaches, and immune\-modulating delivery systems have expanded the role of nanoparticles from passive drug carriers to programmable oncology platforms\. This narrative review examines the developmental evolution of cancer\-focused pharmaceutical nanoparticles, with emphasis on liposomes, lipid nanoparticles \(LNPs\), albumin\-bound systems, polymeric particles, polymeric micelles, nanocrystals, nanoemulsions, solid lipid nanoparticles, inorganic particles, extracellular vesicles, and hybrid delivery technologies\. Each platform class is treated systematically, covering representative approved products, formulation characteristics, route of administration, clinical evidence, and the specific development risks that limit it\. There view connects platform design with oncology\-specific barriers, including tumor heterogeneity, variable enhanced permeability and retention \(EPR\) effects, dense extracellular matrix, abnormal tumor vasculature, mononuclear phagocyte clearance, protein\-corona formation, endosomal escape, immune activation, and the difficulty of translating animal tumor models into clinical benefit\. These barriers are organized as a sequential delivery cascade, and the behavior of each platform class is compared step by step rather than described as a set of universal phenomena\. Nanoparticle candidates that accumulated well in preclinical tumors but failed in clinical trials are examined alongside approved products, because the contrast between the two is where most of the transferable lessons sit\. A product\-development perspective is used to discuss critical quality attributes \(CQAs\), manufacturing scalability, potency testing, sterility strategy, stability, release methods, regulatory expectations, commercial feasibility, and clinical differentiation\. A development\-to\-translation framework is proposed for comparing cancer nanomedicine platforms across formulation maturity, analytical maturity, manufacturing maturity, biological rationale, clinical evidence, regulatory readiness, and commercial feasibility; regulatory and commercial maturity are scored separately, the criteria behind each level are defined explicitly, and the resulting rankings are presented as a heuristic aid to discussion rather than a validated quantitative metric\. Future progress in oncology nanomedicine will depend not only on novel materials or targeting claims, but also on disciplined product design, biologically meaningful potency assays, scalable manufacturing, patient\-selection strategies, and clear integration with precision oncology\.

## [Adaptive multi\-parameter fusion for sports outcome prediction: a context\-aware intelligent platform](../publications/4957e6fcda1889140781.md)

Yanxiao Zhang; 尤双从

Abstract Sports outcome prediction is crucial for performance assessment and strategic decision\-making\. Traditional models \(Elo\-based, regression\-based\) rely on limited historical data and fail to capture dynamic interactions between players, teams, and contexts\. We introduce an adaptive multi\-parameter fusion \(AMPF\) framework using hierarchical attention\-based neural networks to integrate team ratings, performance trends, and contextual factors\. Unlike fixed\-weight models, AMPF employs learnable attention mechanisms for adaptive, context\-specific feature weighting\. Implemented in PyTorch, AMPF is validated on FiveThirtyEight datasets covering 45,000\+ football matches \(2010–2024\) and 20,000\+ basketball games \(2012–2024\)\. AMPF achieves statistically significant improvements over all baselines: 1\.6–2\.2% higher accuracy and 3\.8–5\.6% lower Brier scores compared to deep MLPs, with larger gains \(4\.7–4\.8% accuracy, 10\.9–11\.8% Brier reduction\) over classical Elo ratings\. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of contextual embeddings and adaptive fusion\. We deploy a platform providing real\-time predictions, interpretability visualizations, and provenance tracking, bridging traditional rating systems and modern deep learning for sports analytics\.

## [Clinical outcome and implant accuracy in cervical fractures stabilization using 3D\-printed patient\-specific drill guides for placement of bicortical screws in 16 dogs](../publications/49644b70662afd840941.md)

Alba Manzanedo‐Delgado; Bill Oxley; Sébastien Behr

Objective To describe the clinical outcome of dogs with cervical fractures undergoing spinal stabilization surgery using 3D\-printed patient\-specific drill guides, and to evaluate the accuracy of pedicle screw placement with this technique\. Study design Retrospective descriptive study\. Animals or sample population Sixteen dogs\. Methods Medical records were searched between August 2015 and January 2025 for dogs with traumatic spinal fracture via CT scan causing signs of cervical myelopathy that underwent spinal stabilization surgery using 3D\-printed patient\-specific drill guides followed by a postoperative CT scan\. Neurological status was graded retrospectively with the Modified Frankel Score \(MFS\) on presentation, preoperatory on the day of the surgery, postoperatively on the first day after surgery, at hospital discharge and at the follow\-up examination performed 4–6 weeks after surgery, when available\. A telephone questionnaire was obtained for the long\-term outcome\. Results Sixteen dogs met the inclusion criteria \(3/16 grade 2 MFS, 5/16 grade 3 MFS, 7/16 grade 4 MFS and 1/16 grade 5 MFS\)\. Two dogs showed mild minor transient intraoperative complications\. Optimal pedicle screw placement was achieved in 85/90 \(94\.4%\) of screws\. Twenty\-four hours after surgery, the neurological grade remained unchanged in 10/16 dogs, improved in 5/16, and transiently deteriorated in 1/16 dog, which recovered by discharge\. Postoperative complications occurred in 10/16 dogs and resolved with medical management in 9/10 cases\. Short term follow\-up revealed a static stable \(6/14\) or improved \(8/14\) neurological grade since discharge\. Among the 12 dogs with owner\-reported long\-term follow\-up, all were reported by their owners to be ambulatory and to have improved neurologically\. Long\-term quality\-of\-life \(5 = excellent; 1 = poor\) was scored by the owners 5/5 in 11/12 \(91\.7%\) dogs and 4/5 in 1/12 \(8\.3%\) dogs\. Conclusion Dogs in this study overall had an improved neurological status and favorable long\-term outcomes when follow\-up information was available\. However, postoperative adverse events, including complications, should be considered when interpreting overall clinical outcome\.

## [DIGITAL TWIN AS AN INTEGRATED DECISION\-SUPPORT PLATFORM FOR SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT: A CONCEPTUAL AND IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORK FOR TASHKENT](../publications/497881f60b18e37581a1.md)

S\. Salimov; J\.Sh\. Inoyatxodjayev

Rapid urban growth increases the interdependence of transport, land use, utility infrastructure, environmental conditions, public services, and emergency\-management systems\. In Tashkent, these domains are increasingly supported by digital technologies, yet the fragmentation of data and sector\-specific information systems limits the ability of public authorities to evaluate the combined consequences of urban\-development decisions\. This paper develops an integrated conceptual and implementation framework for a cityscale Digital Twin designed to support sustainable urban development and data\-driven governance in Tashkent\. The study applies systems analysis, functional modelling, comparative analysis, and scenario\-based assessment to connect urban challenges with data acquisition, integration, simulation, decision support, and measurable outcomes\. The proposed framework consists of five interconnected layers: a spatial and physical model, dynamic urban data, data integration and governance, analytics and simulation, and decision\-support services\. These layers operate within a continuous decision cycle in which information from the physical city updates the Digital Twin, alternative scenarios are simulated, management decisions are implemented, and the resulting urban changes generate new data\. Priority applications include transport management, utility infrastructure, environmental monitoring, development control, and emergency management\. A four\-stage implementation roadmap is proposed for Tashkent, supported by governance, cybersecurity, open architecture, lifecycle financing, and outcome\-based performance indicators\. The framework shifts the role of the Digital Twin from urban visualization toward an operational mechanism for testing the consequences of decisions before physical implementation\.

## [AVALIAÇÃO DA RELAÇÃO ENTRE O CRONOTIPO E FALSAS MEMÓRIAS EM ESTUDANTES DA UFFS \- REALEZA](../publications/497d27ba5990f09696a8.md)

Luiza do Nascimento; Maria Elisa de Oliveira Lima; YAMIN PEQUINI; Bianca Cestaroli; Felipe Beijamini

A memória de reconhecimento facial apresenta relevância em diferentes contextos, especialmente no âmbito jurídico, devido à suscetibilidade da memória à formação de falsas lembranças\. Nesse sentido, o cronotipo, associado às diferenças individuais nos ritmos circadianos, pode influenciar o desempenho cognitivo conforme o período do dia\. Este estudo objetiva avaliar o efeito do cronotipo na formação de falsas memórias de faces, distinguindo\-o dos efeitos da pressão de sono, e comparar o desempenho de indivíduos matutinos e vespertinos em tarefas realizadas pela manhã e à tarde\. Trata\-se de um estudo experimental, com delineamento intra\-sujeitos e medidas repetidas\. Foram analisadas respostas de acertos, alarmes falsos e rejeições incorretas, além de características do sono dos sete dias anteriores e níveis de sonolência subjetiva\. Dos 129 indivíduos inicialmente recrutados, 58 atenderam aos critérios de elegibilidade e foram convidados para a etapa experimental\. Até o momento, dois participantes realizaram os testes, impossibilitando análises estatísticas\. Resultados preliminares indicam associação entre cronotipo e qualidade do sono, com indivíduos matutinos apresentando melhor qualidade do sono em comparação aos vespertinos e intermediários\. A continuidade da coleta permitirá avaliar a relação entre cronotipo, sono, período do dia e reconhecimento facial\.

## [Query\-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion](../publications/499b3d64fd876b55c3ac.md)

Shiyuan Zhang; Xuheng Li; Qiwei Di; Quanquan Gu

Masked diffusion models \(MDMs\) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output\. Anari et al\. \(2026\) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token\-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token\. We propose the Single\-Increment Rejection Sampler \(SIRS\), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query\. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al\. \(2026\)\. Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao\-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping\. We show that the KL\-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model&\#x27;s training error\. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within\-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range\.

## [HTN\-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi\-Agent Orchestration](../publications/499eab8a0d860a4ac5ad.md)

Yanchen Deng; Jianguo Huang; Yao Long Teng; Yixuan Li; Handuo Zhang; Ning Wang; Liangcai Su; Xinyu Wang; Bo An

Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning\. Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins\. Therefore, we introduce HTN\-Orchestrate, a two\-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network \(HTN\)\. The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask\. Results propagate upward under \\textbf\{AND\} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task\. On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN\-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89\.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73\.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2\.45 and 4\.69 percentage points, respectively\.

## [Exploring early perceptual processing of faces displaying Down syndrome features from a masked priming paradigm](../publications/49a3fa1eabc9135b232e.md)

Nazaret Hernández\-Espeso; Carmen Moret‐Tatay; Loreto Bustos\-Hernando; Roberta Diamanti

Background Understanding how facial characteristics associated with intellectual disability are processed during early stages of perception may provide new insights into disability\-related social cognition\. Masked priming paradigms offer a useful approach for examining how contextual information influences face recognition before conscious deliberation\. Methods Digitally generated facial stimuli displaying Down syndrome characteristics were developed from standardized facial photographs and validated by 66 experts and 136 participants from the general population\. The validated stimuli were subsequently used in a masked priming face recognition task completed by 22 psychology students, in which reaction times \(RTs\) and recognition accuracy were recorded across three priming conditions\. Results Priming condition significantly influenced reaction times, with faster responses observed in the identity condition, in which prime and target shared both identity and facial phenotype, than under feature\-based or different priming conditions\. Facial phenotype alone did not significantly affect reaction times or recognition accuracy\. However, recognition accuracy varied according to the interaction between priming condition, facial phenotype, and stimulus type, indicating that behavioural performance depended on the experimental context rather than on facial phenotype alone\. Conclusion This exploratory study provides preliminary evidence that the recognition of faces displaying Down syndrome characteristics involves early perceptual processes\. The findings contribute to the emerging field of disability\-related social cognition and support the use of experimental cognitive paradigms to better understand disability perception\.

Kehua Liao; Xiaojuan Wei; Yan Chen; Dongyun Meng; Shaozhou Mo; Zeyong Sun; Fengyang Song; Lu Lu; Wentan Huang

Objective To examine whether pretreatment nocturnal sleep duration and Clinical Activity Score \(CAS\) are associated with thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine \(¹³¹I\) therapy in Graves’ disease \(GD\) with concomitant thyroid\-associated ophthalmopathy \(TAO\)\. The primary endpoint was thyroid functional remission, not ocular cure\. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 153 patients at a single center \(53 in remission; 100 not in remission\), followed for at least 12 months after ¹³¹I therapy\. Sleep duration and CAS were pretreatment baseline measures; 20 patients received prednisone before ¹³¹I therapy \(discontinued ≥ 3 days prior\) and 133 received none; no thyroid\-directed or immunosuppressive treatment was given during follow\-up\. Remission was coded using the response categories of the 2021 Chinese Society of Nuclear Medicine ¹³¹I treatment guideline \(euthyroidism or hypothyroidism vs\. partial or ineffective response\)\. Missing continuous values were multiply imputed \(20 chains\)\. Analyses included false discovery rate \(FDR\)–controlled univariate screening, cross\-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\) selection, post\-selection logistic regression, Firth sensitivity analysis, interaction tests, and mutually adjusted restricted cubic splines \(RCS\)\. Results No patient sleeping less than 6h achieved remission \[0/31; 95% confidence interval \(CI\) 0%–9\.2%\]\. After FDR adjustment, GD duration, TAO duration, sleep duration, and CAS remained associated with remission\. LASSO \(one\-standard\-error rule, C = 0\.142\) retained GD duration, sleep duration, and CAS\. In the post\-selection model, the odds ratio \(OR\) per month of GD duration was 0\.991 \(95% CI 0\.979–1\.003; P = 0\.152\); per additional sleep hour, 6\.13 \(95% CI 3\.16–11\.91; P &lt; 0\.001; Firth OR 5\.64, 95% CI 2\.99–10\.63\); and per CAS point, 0\.64 \(95% CI 0\.48–0\.86; P = 0\.003\)\. The CAS × sleep interaction was not significant \(Wald P = 0\.096; likelihood\-ratio P = 0\.086\)\. Mutually adjusted RCS supported non\-linearity for CAS \( P &lt; 0\.001\) but not for sleep \( P = 0\.585\)\. Conclusions Longer pretreatment nocturnal sleep and lower CAS were associated with thyroid functional remission after ¹³¹I therapy in this single\-center cohort, with consistent directions across sensitivity models\. These retrospective, post\-selection associations require prospective validation; the absence of remission below 6h and the fitted threshold effects are exploratory post hoc observations, not validated thresholds\.

## [Transferable conditional brain charts link cortico\-subcortical structure to Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease progression](../publications/49b1894ff7fdd24e9899.md)

Nitin Sharma; Sicheng Dai; Francesco A\. Mallus; Atharva Kand; Marc Lemnitzer; Minh\-Hieu Nguyen; Mebin Muhammed Hamzakoya Sulaikha; Jijia Xing; Mariam Zabihi; Gülce Lale; Gokul Perumbayil Vijayakrishnan; Elias Schreiner; Madhumitha Sivakumar Punitha; Paul Buttkus; Çağatay Yıldız; Poornima Kumar; Thomas Grote; Esten Leonardsen; Francesco Sammarco; Vinod Kumar Jangir; Sarah Sobotta; Barbora Rehák Bučková; Augustijn A\. A\. de Boer; Konstantinos Tsilimparis; Christian Gaser; Charlotte Fraza; Saige Rutherford; Seyed Mostafa Kia; Andre F\. Marquand; Yanwu Yang; Richard Dinga; Thomas Wolfers

Normative models chart how brain measures vary across the lifespan, expressing each individual as a deviation from a healthy reference\. However, most regional models of cortical thickness disregard dependencies between cortical and subcortical anatomy, and transferring them to a new site typically requires retraining or a recalibration of location and scale alone\. We condition lifespan norms of cortical thickness on subcortical volume, such that each deviation indicates whether an individual&\#x27;s cortex lies within the healthy range given their subcortical anatomy, and make them transferable\. In 21,351 healthy individuals from 216 sites, conditioning on ten subcortical structures improved out\-of\-sample prediction on average, most for the amygdala and hippocampus\. Refitting only the intercepts of all four distributional parameters on about 20 healthy individuals, as implemented in our open\-source package NormGAMLSS, calibrated most of six unseen sites without retraining, for base and conditional models\. In the Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, global deviation and structural dissociation \(the reduction in mean absolute deviation under conditioning\) predicted conversion to mild cognitive impairment and dementia beyond the Clinical Dementia Rating and dissociation added beyond global deviation for dementia, even at similar clinically recorded impairment\. Conditional norms thus provide relevant, individual\-level information\.

## [Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM\-Based Text Scoring](../publications/49b945de78a96b9d55b9.md)

Wonjeong Jo; Gyuwan Kim; Ming Shan Hee

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used in computational social science to assign scalar scores to social and psychological constructs\. However, studies use different rating scales, and whether their scores remain comparable across scale designs is understudied\. To address this gap, we define and systematically investigate scale sensitivity, the variation in LLM\-generated scores caused by rating scale design\. We distinguish numerical sensitivity, changes in normalized scores, from semantic sensitivity, changes in score interpretation\. To assess both, our experimental design crosses 2 formats \(continuous vs\. ordinal\), 4 ranges \(3, 5, 11, and 21 points\), and 2 signs \(signed vs\. unsigned\) across 3 tasks \(political leaning, sentiment, and toxicity\), 2 prompting strategies \(zero\-shot and rubric\-based\), and 5 LLMs\. We find that changing one design element shifts normalized scores by about 0\.10 on average and changes the category of roughly 20% of texts\. Sensitivity is greatest for toxicity, the only unipolar construct examined\. Also, rubric\-based prompting does not reduce sensitivity compared with zero\-shot prompting\. We provide practical guidance for designing more reliable LLM\-based text scoring and highlight the need for robustness checks across alternative scales\.

## [Anytime Contracts for AI Services](../publications/49c0ebb7abfaa8ab1a9e.md)

Boris Velasevic; Eden Saig; Eric Mazumdar

AI services are prone to moral hazard, as model providers can silently route requests to cheaper, lower\-quality models, and the inherent stochasticity of model outputs makes this degradation hard to detect\. Contract theory addresses moral hazard by designing payment rules that reward high\-quality outputs and prevent strategic overcharging\. However, existing frameworks assume interactions of fixed duration, whereas AI services are typically consumed through subscriptions and pay\-as\-you\-go APIs that users can terminate at any time based on observed performance\. We show that this flexibility can break standard contracts, opening them up to abuse by either the providers or users\. To address this, we extend contract theory to account for unknown exit rules\. We formalize the problem as a Principal\-Agent game, and show that budget\-optimal contracts in this setting are proportional to anytime\-valid hypothesis tests based on likelihood\-ratio e\-values\. We give an efficient algorithm for computing anytime contracts and show how betting e\-processes can be used to approximate them when the models are unknown\. Finally, we evaluate our findings on synthetic data and data from deployed LLMs\.

## [Uncertainty\-aware AI\-enabled framework for predicting hydrogen dispersion in confined spaces to enhance operator situational awareness](../publications/49c67f1f4766f425b0d3.md)

Niclas Flehmig; Mary Ann Lundteigen; Shen Yin

We present a two\-stage AI\-enabled framework for enhancing operator situational awareness during compressed hydrogen bunkering in maritime confined spaces\. In the event of a leak, the framework first estimates the unknown leakage rate from early sensor readings and then forecasts how the hydrogen cloud will disperse over the next time steps, providing operators with a predicted concentration map together with confidence bounds\. The framework is based on two independent AI models building one AI system\. The AI system is designed as a decision\-support tool\. It augments sensor readings, and thus enhances operator situational awareness and supports decision\-making\. This enables preventive safety barriers to be deployed before hazardous concentrations are reached, while an independent emergency shutdown system remains the ultimate safety layer\. The system design incorporates safeguards to ensure the AI system operates within its competence envelope\. Trained and tested on an open dataset of confined\-space hydrogen releases, the framework achieves a mean absolute error of $0\.052$\~g/s in leakage\-rate estimation and $\\approx0\.018$ in hydrogen\-concentration prediction, approaching the sensor precision bound of $\\pm0\.01$\. The hydrogen\-concentration prediction provides well\-calibrated uncertainty estimates that allow operators to judge the reliability of each forecast\. These results suggest that the framework may provide early information about hazardous concentration build\-up, potentially supporting preventive actions by operators\.

联 周; Xianya Deng; Yunfei Lu

With the continuous deepening of educational reform, cultivating core competencies has become the fundamental goal of primary and secondary education\. Structuring knowledge offers a new perspective and pathway for mathematics teaching oriented toward these core competencies\. Based on the requirements for developing core competencies, this paper systematically elaborates on the main characteristics and core functions of “mathematics teaching based on structured knowledge,” drawing from key viewpoints on “knowledge structuring” and “mathematics pedagogy”\. ## [From salinity, alkalinity, and sodicity to vegetation recovery: a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping of plant responses and restoration strategies](../publications/49f42581bda45303f05f.md)

Xiaofeng Chen; Qian Hong; Wenjie Zhang; Yanbing Wang; Chao Liu; Xin Liu

Introduction Saline, alkaline, and sodic soils constrain plant establishment, but research on vegetation restoration is spread across plant physiology, soil reclamation, and restoration ecology\. Methods We searched Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, obtaining 554 English\-language articles and reviews published through 2025, and used bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping to examine research patterns and thematic development\. Publication, country, and text analyses used all 554 records; keyword networks, thematic trends, and cited\-reference analyses used 386 Web of Science records\. Results Of the 554 publications, 343 \(61\.9%\) appeared in 2019–2025, with 102 in 2025\. China, the United States, Australia, India, and Spain contributed the most publications\. The keyword network comprised 120 terms and 951 edges\. Greedy modularity analysis identified four communities \(Q = 0\.279\), covering vegetation restoration, plant salt\-stress responses, soil reclamation, and soil–nutrient–microbial associations\. Annual output \(Pearson r = 0\.984\) and country rankings \(Spearman ρ = 0\.917\) were highly consistent across databases\. Discussion Drawing on these bibliometric results and representative studies, we propose an establishment\-bottleneck perspective that considers transitions between germination, seedling survival, root development, and persistent vegetation cover, together with potential feedbacks between these processes and soil conditions\. The accompanying conceptual Diagnose–Match–Sequence–Monitor–Adapt framework and reporting checklist connect stress diagnosis, intervention sequencing, and joint plant–soil monitoring to inform field research on plant establishment and sustained vegetation restoration\.

## [ScopeNovo: a De Novo Peptide Sequencing Method Using Spectrum\-Spectrum Similarity to Refine the Prediction Accuracy](../publications/49f58fff82f16ca9dbfb.md)

Zhi Song; Zejian Ding; Lusheng Wang

MOTIVATION: De novo peptide sequencing from tandem mass spectra is essential for characterizing unknown proteins, identifying novel post\-translational modifications, and analyzing samples without reference databases\. While recent deep learning models have improved the predicted peptide accuracy, they typically select the predicted peptide sequence based solely on sequence\-level decoding scores\. Very often, high scores are assigned to peptides without the direct support from the observed mass spectrum\. RESULTS: We present ScopeNovo, a de novo peptide sequencing method that improves predicted peptide accuracy by using spectrum\-spectrum similarity between the input spectrum and the &quot;representative&quot; spectrum corresponding to the predicted peptide sequence\. ScopeNovo generates multiple candidate peptides using an existing peptide de novo sequencing learning model and reranks candidates based on spectrum\-spectrum similarity\. To test our method, we use π\-PrimeNovo as the base learning model\. Experimental results on the standard nine\-species benchmark datasets V1 and V2 show that ScopeNovo can substantially improve the prediction accuracy\. We designed two settings, where Setting 1 is for well\-annotated species, and Setting 2 is for species that are not well annotated\. For Setting 1, ScopeNovo improves the average peptide accuracies of π\-PrimeNovo over the nine species by 6\.1% and 4\.0% on V1 and V2, respectively\. For Setting 2, ScopeNovo can still improve the peptide accuracy of π\-PrimeNovo over the nine species by 3\.4% and 1\.9% on the V1 and V2 benchmark datasets, respectively\. Compared to the best known method, RankNovo, the peptide accuracies over the nine species on V1 and V2 of our method for Setting 1 are 0\.711 and 0\.737, where the peptide accuracies for RankNovo are 0\.687 and 0\.682\. Even for Setting 2, the peptide accuracies of our method are comparable to those of RankNovo\. AVAILABILITY: ScopeNovo is implemented in Python under an MIT license\. The source code is freely available at https://github\.com/SoSongzhi/ScopeNovo\.git\. The test data are available at https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.23181841\. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online\.

## [MODERN TECHNOLOGIES IN TEACHING PSYCHOLOGY](../publications/49f83038789180ecde42.md)

Khalimova Naima Vakhidovna; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre

The rapid development of digital technologies is reshaping the aims, methods, and learning environments of psychology education\. Contemporary psychology teaching increasingly combines established pedagogical principles with learning management systems, multimedia resources, simulations, collaborative platforms, learning analytics, and carefully governed applications of artificial intelligence\. This article examines how modern technologies can support the teaching of psychology in higher education while preserving the discipline’s emphasis on evidence, ethical reflection, human interaction, and critical interpretation\. The study uses a structured narrative review and conceptual analysis of research on educational technology, multimedia learning, self\-regulated learning, online and blended education, simulation, and artificial intelligence in education\. The literature is organized around five instructional functions: representation of psychological concepts, active and collaborative learning, experiential practice, feedback and assessment, and personalization\. The analysis suggests that technology is most educationally valuable when it is aligned with explicit learning outcomes and integrated into a coherent instructional design rather than introduced as an end in itself\. Digital case studies, interactive experiments, structured discussion, reflective e\-portfolios, and low\-stakes formative assessment can make abstract concepts more observable and help students connect theory with practical situations\. At the same time, digital delivery creates risks related to superficial engagement, unequal access, privacy, algorithmic bias, overreliance on automated feedback, and the inappropriate simulation of clinical or sensitive situations\. The article proposes a technology\-enhanced framework for psychology teaching based on pedagogical alignment, active participation, ethical safeguards, accessibility, and continuous evaluation\. It concludes that modern technologies should augment—not replace—professional teaching, interpersonal dialogue, and methodologically sound psychological inquiry\.

## [Del residuo agroindustrial al biochar diseñado: composición, estructura molecular y aplicaciones de alto valor agregado](../publications/49fb9a5b432d2d7978e2.md)

Farid Chejne; Valentina Sierra\-Jiménez; Robert Macias; Javier Ordoñez; Juan C\. Maya; Carlos A\. Gómez

En este artículo se examina cómo la composición de la biomasa agroindustrial y las condiciones de pirólisis determinan la estructura molecular y el desempeño funcional del biochar desde una perspectiva de ingeniería de materiales\. En el contexto colombiano y latinoamericano, la valorización descentralizada de residuos agrícolas y forestales \(cascarilla de arroz, bagazo de caña, podas urbanas, residuos de palma y pulpa de café\) representa una vía estratégica para la transición energética y la economía circular, en línea con los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y el enfoque One Health\. Se describen los procesos termoquímicos \(torrefacción, pirólisis lenta y rápida y gasificación\) y las rutas biológicas complementarias y se analizan los mecanismos que rigen la formación del biochar: despolimerización, fragmentación, condensación aromática y desarrollo de defectos estructurales\. A partir de estos fundamentos, se construye una matriz que vincula las principales aplicaciones del biochar —secuestro de carbono, mejoramiento de suelos, catálisis heterogénea, adsorción de contaminantes y almacenamiento electroquímico de energía— con las características estructurales y las condiciones de síntesis que las favorecen\. Se concluye que el biochar debe entenderse como un material diseñado, y no como un subproducto indiferenciado de la pirólisis, y se propone la ingeniería de biochar como marco para orientar su desarrollo hacia aplicaciones de alto valor agregado\.

## [Machine Learning\-Driven Optimization of Multiphase Chemical Processes for Energy\-Efficient and Sustainable Manufacturing](../publications/4a00bbfd490c0a138a02.md)

Mustafa Soniwala; Taha Mandviwala

There are many industrial chemical manufacturing processes that involve multi\-phase chemistry, such as gas–liquid, liquid–liquid, gas–solid, solid–liquid and three\-phase systems, and these are among the most energy\-intensive and complex unit processes to optimise, due to the complex, nonlinear and often unmeasurable interfacial phenomena\. The hydrodynamic, thermal and mass transfer coupling involved in these systems are difficult to model with traditional first\-principles or empirical optimization approaches and make it challenging to progress towards industrially relevant scales and energy efficient, sustainable manufacturing targets\. This narrative review aims to collect and condense the surge of literature on the application of machine learning \(ML\) algorithms for optimizing multiphase chemical processes, which spans from classic statistical process control \(SPC\) to advanced data\-driven, hybrid and physics\-informed learning algorithms\. We study the use of supervised learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, Bayesian optimization and evolutionary algorithms in important multiphase unit operations for surrogate modelling, soft sensing, real\-time control and multi\-objective optimization\. The literature reviewed indicates that the combined results of the different strategies with ML can produce energy efficiency gains ranging from 8% \- 28%, improvements in yield and product quality and predictive accuracy can be identified, and computational costs can be reduced when compared to other conventional approaches such as computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\) and first\-principles \(FP\)\. The challenges highlighted include issues such as limited data, interpretability of models, scalability, and real\-time deployment\. The future scope for this research is physics\-informed and hybrid models, digital twins, transfer and federated learning, and benchmarking\.

## [Pathogen\-mediated selection and phylogeny shape MHC architecture in 33 bat genomes](../publications/4a11eb2a5aba0f4d7f1d.md)

Luke W\. Silver; Dominik W\. Melville; Andrea L\. Schraven; Magdalena Meyer; Bismark A\. Opoku; Katherine Belov; Simone Sommer; Carolyn J\. Hogg

Background Adaptive immunity is an ancestral hallmark of jawed vertebrates, yet its genomic organisation is far from static—continually reconfigured through extensive gene family duplication and evolutionary turnover\. The major histocompatibility complex \(MHC\) plays a central role in presenting antigens derived from intra\- and extracellular pathogens, eliciting pathogen\-specific immune responses\. Its polymorphic nature makes the MHC particularly difficult to study with genomic architecture deciphered only in a handful of species\. Methods We manually annotated 2,095 MHC\-I, \-II and flanking genes across 33 high quality bat genomes, covering all 21 Chiropteran families, mapping the pan\-bat genomic organisation of the MHC for the first time\. Results Selection and phylogenetic conservatism drive the organization of class I and II loci, while copy number variation appears largely independent of host, ecological, or environmental factors\. However, we observe suggestive trends indicating that roosting behaviour, body size, and geographic distribution may predict copy number variation at certain loci\. Moreover, core gut bacterial similarity increased with structural similarity in class II loci, suggesting that bacterial communities may exert selective pressures that shapes the class II repertoires\. In contrast, neither viral diversity nor similarity – estimated from a public virus database – appeared to influence class I organisation\. Ancestral reconstructions indicate that similarities were present in the ancestor of both Yinpterochiroptera and Yangochiroptera species, and family\-level differences emerged later, particularly in speciose families such as Rhinolophidae, Hipposideridae and Vespertilionidae \. Conclusion Overall, the genomic organization of the complete MHC region provides insight into how bat ecology may have shaped its evolution\.

## [Unbounded number line estimation as a mechanism linking spatial skills and mathematical performance in adults](../publications/4a26e8768757f79dcb01.md)

Felix Ayesu; Darcy Hallett; Nicole Eddy

Spatial skills are robustly associated with mathematical performance, yet the cognitive mechanisms underlying this relationship in adults remain poorly understood\. The present research examined whether unbounded number line estimation mediates the association between spatial skills and mathematical performance in adults\. Ninety \(90\) undergraduate students completed measures of spatial visualization, mental rotation, algebra, fractions, arithmetic, and unbounded number line estimation\. Results indicated that spatial skills significantly predicted mathematical performance and that unbounded number line estimation indirectly mediated this relationship across all three mathematical domains\. These findings extend spatial representation theory to adulthood, suggesting that stronger spatial skills may support the construction of more precise internal representations of numerical magnitude, which in turn facilitate mathematical proficiency\.

## [DOES TECHNOLOGY AFFECT ADOLESCENT MENTAL HEALTH DIFFERENTLY? A COMPARATIVE STUDY](../publications/4a307b02abf403e794b9.md)



The rapid proliferation of information and communication technology has fundamentally transformed adolescent life, raising concerns about its impact on mental health\.However, it remains unclear whether mental health outcomes related to technology usage differ across demographic groups\.The present study aimed to compare the mental health status of adolescents with respect to technology usage based on gender, locality, and educational board\.A quantitative descriptive survey research design was adopted\.The sample consisted of 400 adolescent students selected through stratified convenience sampling from schools in Lucknow city\.The Mental Health Battery developed by Singh and Sen Gupta and a self\-constructed Technology Usage Scale were used as data collection tools\.Independent samples t\-test and Cohen&\#x27;s d were employed for data analysis after conducting assumption checks including the Shapiro\-Wilk test for normality and the Brown\-Forsythe test for homogeneity of variance\.The findings revealed no significant differences in mental health scores between boys and girls, rural and urban students, or U\.P\. Board and CBSE students\.The study concludes that adolescent mental health status with respect to technology usage does not differ significantly by gender, locality, or educational board\.These findings imply that interventions to promote healthy technology use may be applied uniformly across these demographic groups\.However, caution is warranted due to violations of normality and homogeneity of variance in some comparisons\.

## [CGDT\-CESN: Correlation\-Guided and Dynamics\-Trained Clustered Echo State Network for Multivariate Time\-Series Prediction](../publications/4a3a095f47ba288f1fb8.md)

Hariharan Srinivasan; Masoom Bhargava; Sayan Gupta

Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable\-specific dynamics and cross\-variable interactions\. In this work, a Correlation\-Guided and Dynamics\-Trained Clustered Echo State Network \(CGDT\-CESN\) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series\. An innovative reservoir design is proposed in which inter\-cluster connections are enabled by empirically observed correlations among variables, providing a data\-driven coupling mechanism\. Apart from conventional readout training, inter\-cluster connection weights informed by correlations are trained, which in turn allows the reservoir to capture time\-varying cross\-variable dependencies without sacrificing computational efficiency and further improves forecasting accuracy\. The prediction performance of CGDT\-CESN is found to be superior to that of the conventional ESN when evaluated on two fundamentally different datasets: Twitter information cascade evolution and solar wind forecasting\. Also, the improvement in performance is preserved across multiple prediction horizons, even when presented with a low volume of data\. By unifying cluster\-specific specialization with learned inter\-variable coupling, CGDT\-CESN offers a principled, data\-driven route to multivariate time series prediction\.

## [Popularity Regression\-Based Latent Space Model for Large\-Scale Sparse Network Analysis](../publications/4a468b2bb7e2a69b0c48.md)

Zhan Gao; Danyang Huang; Rui Pan; Hansheng Wang

Degree heterogeneity is one of the most important properties of network data\. It is widely observed that degree heterogeneity is often related to the nodal features\. In this study, we investigate the estimation and statistical inference for a popularity regression\-based latent space model with nodal features\. Given the complex dependence structure induced by the latent space model, we aim to derive analytically tractable objective functions that effectively account for this structure for sparse networks\. Specifically, we propose a total of four estimators\. The first two estimators are developed by utilizing only the first\-order structure of the network \(e\.g\., the nodal degree\), while the last two estimators are developed by leveraging the higher\-order network structures \(i\.e\., reciprocity and transitivity\)\. Rigorous asymptotic theory is established based on various non\-standard U\-statistics\. We find that different estimators might have different convergence rates\. The extension to higher\-order moments\-based estimators is also discussed\. Extensive numerical experiments and a real data analysis of link prediction for an author citation network are conducted for illustration purposes\.

## [Wildlife management in the United States – thoughts on evolving to better address species overabundance and disease transmission](../publications/4a49440cd2d019404e69.md)

Kurt C\. VerCauteren

Abstract Wildlife managers across the United States face growing challenges associated with locally overabundant native species, invasive species, and increasing disease risks at wildlife–livestock–human interfaces\. Drawing from field experience and emerging research, this opinion piece examines pressing issues for the profession: locally overabundant populations of white‑tailed deer and feral swine, and the diseases linked to these species\. Traditional reliance on recreational hunting is often insufficient to meet population‑reduction goals for deer, particularly in suburban landscapes where hunting access and hunter participation limit effectiveness\. Integrated strategies—including professional sharpshooting, private‐land access programs, venison donation programs, and exploration of regulated commercial harvest—may provide additional tools for agencies striving to reduce ecological impacts while enhancing societal benefits\. For invasive feral swine, recreational hunting can exacerbate their spread, necessitating science‑based suppression led by trained professionals using targeted, highly effective removal methods\. Disease concerns further highlight the need for interdisciplinary, One Health–oriented approaches to prevent and manage infections shared among wildlife, livestock, and humans\. By embracing evolving technologies, strengthening human‑dimensions capacity, and engaging the public as partners, wildlife professionals can better address the multifaceted challenges of overabundance and disease in a changing management landscape\.
