## [CodaRAG: Connecting the Dots with Associativity Inspired by Complementary Learning](../publications/4a6d8fe78600cec294e3.md)

Cheng\-Yen Li; Xuanjun Chen; Claire Lin; Wei\-Yu Chen; Wenhua Nie; Hung\-Yi Lee; Jyh\-Shing Roger Jang

Large Language Models \(LLMs\) struggle with knowledge\-intensive tasks due to hallucinations and fragmented reasoning over dispersed information\. While Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) grounds generation in external sources, existing methods often treat evidence as isolated units, failing to reconstruct the logical chains that connect these dots\. Inspired by Complementary Learning Systems \(CLS\), we propose CodaRAG, a framework that evolves retrieval from passive lookup into active associative discovery\. CodaRAG operates via a three\-stage pipeline: \(1\) Knowledge Consolidation to unify fragmented extractions into a stable memory substrate; \(2\) Associative Navigation to traverse the graph via multi\-dimensional pathways, including semantic, contextual, and functional dimensions, explicitly recovering dispersed evidence chains; and \(3\) Interference Elimination to prune hyper\-associative noise, ensuring a coherent, high\-precision reasoning context\. On GraphRAG\-Bench, CodaRAG achieves absolute gains of 7–10% in retrieval recall and 3–11% in generation accuracy\. These results demonstrate CodaRAG&\#x27;s superior ability to systematically robustify associative evidence retrieval for factual, reasoning, and creative tasks\.

## [Machine learning\-based thorium normalization in airborne gamma\-ray spectrometry for enhanced critical mineral exploration](../publications/4a6f16d19c9ed69b2c32.md)

Jessica Derkacz Weihermann; Yaoguo Li; Mengli Zhang

Airborne gamma\-ray spectrometry \(AGRS\), also known as radiometric surveying, is one of the most cost\-effective large\-scale methods for geological mapping, critical mineral exploration, and radiometric anomaly detection through the measurement of potassium \(K\), uranium \(eU\), and thorium \(eTh\) in rocks and weathered materials\. However, the identification of radioelement anomalies is often affected by factors such as soil moisture variability, precipitation, and radiation attenuation\. While primary single channel maps \(K, eU, and eTh\) reflect bedrock composition, secondary maps derived through mathematical operations among channels can highlight geochemical processes and modify radiometric contrast\. Thorium is an important radioactive element in AGRS due to its relative geochemical stability and its relevance to critical mineral and nuclear energy\-related systems and has therefore been widely used to normalize potassium and uranium variations\. This study proposes a target\-informed, machine\-learning\-based methodology for normalizing thorium concentrations using a Random Forest regression model to derive a model\-estimated thorium reference response\. The resulting reference response is then used to calculate relative normalized deviations and enhance thorium radiometric contrast in airborne gamma\-ray spectrometry data\. In this study, thorium is treated as a relatively stable reference component, and thorium\-derived feature transformations, including squared thorium values and radiometric ratios \(eTh 2 /eU and eTh/\(eU \+ eTh\)\), are deliberately combined as part of a target\-informed nonlinear normalization procedure\. The squared thorium term emphasizes elevated thorium responses, whereas the ratio\-based variables represent complementary relationships between thorium and uranium\. The model was trained and evaluated using high\-resolution AGRS data, and the resulting normalized products were analyzed in a Geographic Information System \(GIS\) to assess their geological relevance\. The resulting model\-estimated thorium reference surface response was used to derive normalized thorium values, modifying the spatial contrast of the original eTh response and highlighting spatially coherent thorium variations\. Results indicate that the proposed feature transformations provide complementary radiometric information that may support geological interpretation and the identification of areas potentially associated with thorium enrichment and REE\-bearing materials, demonstrating the potential of machine learning as an exploratory tool for radiometric data analysis and geological exploration\.

## [Multi\-height spectropolarimetric signatures of magnetoacoustic waves in solar plage](../publications/4a7595fcf3c33de248d6.md)

Taylor Sitterson; M\. M\. S\. Marcos Santos; Joshua Bentley; Tom Schad; Momchil Molnar; Bart De Pontieu; Juan Martínez‐Sykora; A\. G\. M\. Pietrow

We analyze high\-cadence spectropolarimetric observations of solar plage obtained with the Visible Spectro\-Polarimeter on the Daniel K\. Inouye Solar Telescope \(DKIST\) to investigate low\-chromospheric waves sampled by the Na I D 1 5896 Å and Ca II 8542 Å lines\. Observations were taken at an oblique viewing angle, providing sensitivity to transverse motions\. Magnetic oscillations within plage elements exhibit significant line\-of\-sight \(LOS\) Root\-mean\-square amplitudes of δ B L O S ≈ 9 G on average in the Na I D 1 line, whereas the corresponding Ca II oscillations are only marginally above the noise level\. Adaptive profile tracking provided line\-core intensities and Doppler velocities, the weak\-field approximation provided LOS magnetic fields, and non\-LTE inversions provided mass densities and formation heights\. Cross\-spectral analysis shows velocity–intensity phase distributions coupled at − 90 ° , consistent with compressive oscillations\. The velocity phases in Na I–Ca II indicate upward propagation and the phase speeds are predominantly sub\-Alfvénic, consistent with slow magnetoacoustic waves\. Although the slit geometry prevents a definitive identification of the tube\-eigenmode, the differing magnetic phase relationships suggest a height\-dependent sausage\-like behavior in the coupling between the magnetic and compressive perturbations\. Additionally, our inferred wave fluxes are insufficient to heat active region plage\.

## [Cost\-effectiveness of remote monitoring of dental patients: tariff formation and cost analysis based on real\-world data of a healthcare organization\.](../publications/4a7bba3cdfeab758658b.md)

Чернявская Татьяна Константиновна; Konstantin Eduardovich Sobolev; М\. А\. Амхадова; Z\. V\. Bazhanova

Relevance\. The development of telemedicine and artificial intelligence has driven the wide adoption of remote monitoring of dental patients, whose clinical and organizational effectiveness has been demonstrated\. However, the economic justification of such technologies and approaches to tariff setting for the remote\-monitoring service remain undeveloped, which hinders their inclusion in healthcare financing\. Objective: to develop a method for calculating the cost \(tariff\) of the remote\-monitoring service for dental patients and to assess the cost\-effectiveness of the technology using real\-world data of a healthcare organization\. Material and methods\. The study comprised a prospective clinical\-organizational part and an economic evaluation\. Clinical and organizational effects of remote monitoring were obtained in a prospective single\-center non\-randomized controlled study \(528 patients enrolled; 516 analyzed: 262 remote monitoring, 254 conventional follow\-up\)\. Real\-world unit costs were derived from the 2025 service registry of the dental department of MONIKI \(13,200 services totalling RUB3,532,311\)\. The tariff was calculated using the normative method of direct and indirect cost calculation\. Cost\-effectiveness was assessed by a cost\-offset analysis with calculation of the net economic result, benefit–cost ratio, break\-even point, and budget impact; robustness was tested in a base\-case \(conservative\) scenario and a full\-visit\-cost scenario\. Results\. The estimated cost of remote monitoring was RUB333\.12 per patient per month \(labour 49\.6%, indirect costs 49\.0%, equipment depreciation 1\.4%\)\. With a mean postoperative follow\-up of 45 days \(≈1\.5 months\), the cost of remote support per patient was about RUB500 per episode\. A reduction of 4\.4 in\-person visits per patient generated savings of RUB1,091 \(conservative, perconsultation cost\) to RUB7,115 \(full\-visit cost\) per patient\. The net economic result ranged from \+RUB591 \(base\-case conservative scenario\) to \+RUB6,615 \(upper bound\) per patient per episode, with a benefit–cost ratio from 1:2\.2 to 1:14\.2\. The technology remained cost\-saving as long as the cost of one in\-person visit exceeded RUB114\. Conclusion\. Remote monitoring of dental patients is a cost\-saving technology with a robustly positive economic result that persists in the conservative scenario\. The developed tariff\-calculation method provides a basis for including the remote\-monitoring service in the financing of specialized dental care\.

## [ANALISIS DAN VISUALISASI POLA PARAMETER CUACA HARIAN DAN BULANAN JAKARTA TIMUR DENGAN K\-MEANS CLUSTERING](../publications/4a83e0ee2f00927a27c9.md)

Lola; Aji Nurrohman; Sigit Wibisono; Rachmat Setiabudi; Atang Supen

Weather observation data produced by the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency \(BMKG\) has multivariate characteristics, so it requires an analysis method that is able to identify patterns based on similarities in data characteristics\. This research aims to analyze and visualize daily and monthly weather parameter patterns in the East Jakarta area using the K\-Means Clustering algorithm\. The dataset used is daily observation data from the Halim Perdanakusuma Meteorological Station for the period January–December 2025, totaling 365 observations with six meteorological parameters, namely TN, TX, TAVG, RH\_AVG, RR, and FF\_AVG\. The research stages include merging data, handling missing values ​​using median imputation, data normalization using StandardScaler, data exploration, determining the optimal number of clusters using the Elbow Method and Silhouette Score, followed by the clustering process using K\-Means\. The evaluation results show that there are three optimal clusters \(K=3\), which represent variations in the daily weather characteristics of East Jakarta\. The clustering results identified different characteristics, namely Cluster 0 \(Hot Dry Weather\), Cluster 1 \(Cool Cloudy Weather\), and Cluster 2 \(Heavy Rainy Weather\)\. Visualization in the form of correlation heatmaps, time series graphs, scatter plots, box plots and bar charts provide informative representations of weather parameter distribution patterns, making it easier to interpret analysis results\. This research proves that K\-Means Clustering is used as an effective exploratory method for identifying weather parameter patterns and visualization of meteorological analysis\.

## [REGULATORY CHALLENGES AND VALIDATION PROTOCOLS FOR CHIP\-BASED ORGAN MIMICRY](../publications/4a8f77c2c94f675bcc9e.md)

Pradip Karale; Sakshi Ithaped; Seema Gosavi; Nitin Sutar; Amit Narang; Agasti Ware; Nilesh B Chaudhari; Anjali Gavit; Raosaheb S\. Shendge

The function of tissues and perhaps organs could be replicated utilize organ\-on\-a\-chip technology\. Clone organs, create functional organ\-like components on a fluidic chip platform, and replicate the microbiome of humans\. By getting rid of significant differences between cell cultures and common animal These bioengineered models have advanced toxicity testing &amp; customized medicine\. Organ chip technology may rebuild the human microbiota, recreate the physiology of tissues and organelles, and produce functional organs on multiple levels of chip substrates\. The regulatory acceptance of OoC systems becomes even more important as they find applications into preclinical and clinical research spheres\. Though dispersed, worldwide regulatory systems make standardisation and certification rather difficult\. Along with the global regulatory landscape for OoC platforms, the legislative framework for OoC technologies in important countries namely the United States, the European Union, Japan, China, and developing nations is exhaustively examined in this review stressing the status, verification problems, and future orientations\. The lack of uniformity, unclear classification, and reproducibility concerns create significant obstacles to regulatory approval\. Forward\-thinking initiatives like “Innovative Science and Technology Approaches for New Drugs” \(ISTAND\) Pilot project, which encourages the creation of pharmaceutical research contrivance have been started by the US Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\)\.

## [BETWEEN TECHNICAL RATIONALITY AND RELATIONAL LABOR: A TECHNOFEMINIST ANALYSIS OF PRESERVICE PRESCHOOL TEACHERS&\#x27; AI PERCEPTIONS AND METAPHORS](../publications/4a9bb686af496f6ce805.md)

Gülçin Bilgener

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) threatens to undermine teaching by simplifying practices into a rationalized process and potentially causing deskilling\. This study investigated preservice preschool teachers’ professional perspectives and metaphorical conceptualization of AI within a technofeminist framework\. The study focused on the inherent tension between the relational nature of early childhood education and the technical rationality of AI\. A convergent parallel mixed\-methods design was employed with 150 preservice preschool teachers at a Turkish state university\. Data were collected utilizing a 15\-item AI perception scale, a metaphor form, and three open\-ended questions probing the uses of AI, collaboration with AI systems, and broader anxieties\. Findings indicated that despite preservice teachers holding a high awareness of the instructional advantages of AI, their moral reservations persisted independently of pedagogical assessments and showed no correlation with frequency of application\. Qualitatively, preservice teachers framed AI through theory\-driven themes such as “the God trick” and “deskilling”\. Female participants&\#x27; exclusive articulation of the “domestication” theme illustrated a strategy where women tailor technology to their pedagogical goals through relational metaphors such as “mother” and “confidant\.” The study demonstrated that AI is not a neutral tool in education but is actively shaped by societal gender structures, necessitating a politically informed approach to teacher education\.

## [International Trade Outlook for Latin America and the Caribbean, 2026: the importance of modern services exports and how to promote them\. Executive summary](../publications/4aa0c9797809f873a2c8.md)



This edition of International Trade Outlook for Latin America and the Caribbean includes an analysis of the profound reconfiguration of global trade, driven by economic security, resilience and sustainability concerns\. Against this backdrop of uncertainty and geopolitical and geoeconomic tensions, growth in trade has nevertheless remained robust in 2026, led by the Asian economies\. Likewise, Latin America and the Caribbean’s goods and services exports and imports rose sharply in the first half of 2026 and are expected to maintain that trajectory in the second half\. This report also outlines a strategy to boost the region’s modern services sector, based on three pillars: promotion of exports of these services, attraction of foreign direct investment and development of human talent\.

## [GJA1 dysfunction suppresses Wnt/c\-MYC signaling and promotes inflammatory imbalance and MMP3\-associated ECM remodeling in fibroblasts and mesenchymal stromal cells from patients with ODDD](../publications/4aa53e932d4f6f8f6eee.md)

Siyuan Tao; Binshan Zhao; Xinyu Wang; Xiaofang Shen; Xiuli Zhao

Oculodentodigital dysplasia \(ODDD\) is caused by variants in GJA1 , but its downstream molecular network remains unclear\. This study found that GJA1 defects lead to comprehensive suppression of Wnt/β\-catenin signaling and the co\-activator c\-MYC in patients’ skin fibroblasts and mesenchymal stem cells \(MSCs\)\. This change induces a dual pathological process: On the one hand, the loss of Wnt lifts the transcriptional repression of MMP3 , leading to abnormally high secretion of matrix metalloproteinases; on the other hand, the absence of c\-MYC results in a specific inflammatory bias in NF\-κB activation \(a surge in IL\-6 , while CXCL8 \( IL\-8 \)are paradoxically and significantly reduced\), accompanied by impaired cell migration, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation\. To validate the causal relationship, we demonstrated through genetic intervention that knocking down GJA1 in normal cells replicates the patient phenotype, while overexpressing wild\-type GJA1 completely reverses the aforementioned abnormalities\. Pharmacological intervention further revealed the hierarchical relationships within the pathway: the Wnt activator \(CHIR99021\) targets a core upstream hub, correcting CXCL8 abnormalities, inhibiting MMP3 , and promoting osteogenesis by restoring c\-MYC ; in contrast, simply blocking IL\-6 \(IL6i\) acts only on downstream effects; although it can downregulate the interferon response, it fails to restore c\-MYC and thus cannot rescue CXCL8 or effectively inhibit MMP3 ; the combination of the two produces the optimal combined effect\. Collectively, we define a novel pathogenic framework linking GJA1 dysfunction to Wnt/c\-MYC suppression\-driven inflammatory bias and ECM degradation, identifying Wnt activation as a potential therapeutic avenue requiring further validation\.

## [Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD](../publications/4aa764172cf6e19454fb.md)

Yibo Zhou; Yirong Xiang

Relational out\-of\-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly\. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image\. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics\. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption\. This makes image\-only, text\-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples\. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision\-language scores\. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image\-caption matching from directional role\-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features\. In a shortcut\-contaminated COCO outlier\-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near\-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0\.882 to 0\.927\. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling\. The official implementation is available online\.

## [From Farm Records to a Digital Control Tower: Integrating Production, Harvest, Finance, Markets, and Traceability for Independent Oil Palm Smallholders — A Review](../publications/4aa7ee091a52dde73c18.md)

Loso Judijanto

Independent oil palm smallholders operate simultaneously as growers, employers, input purchasers, harvest managers, logistics coordinators, sellers, and increasingly as actors responsible for demonstrating legal and sustainability compliance\. Yet these functions are often managed through fragmented records, informal communication, delayed information, and disconnected transactions\. This qualitative literature review examines how an integrated digital farm\-management architecture could transform those fragmented activities into a coherent management\-control system\. Recent literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 was purposively reviewed across oil palm agronomy, farm management information systems, digital agriculture, precision technologies, agricultural marketing, certification, and supply\-chain traceability\. The thematic synthesis identifies seven interconnected domains: farm visibility and management control; harvest integrity and fresh\-fruit\-bunch quality; agronomic and input management; financial visibility; buyer and transaction management; legality and traceability; and digital adoption conditions\. The review argues that the main opportunity is not simply to digitize farm records, but to establish a closed\-loop system connecting measurement, verification, diagnosis, decision, action, transaction, reconciliation, and organizational learning\. A conceptual Digital Smallholder Oil Palm Control Tower is consequently proposed to connect field\-level data with managerial dashboards, farm\-to\-mill transactions, financial reconciliation, sustainability evidence, and decision support\. The framework suggests that farmer\-centred, mobile\-first, interoperable, and progressively implemented systems may strengthen productivity, profitability, bargaining capacity, traceability, and resilience while limiting digital complexity and exclusion

## [QLOBALLAŞMA DÖVRÜNDƏ İMMUNİTETİN ANADANGƏLMƏ SƏHVLƏRİ: ELMI KONSEPSIYALARIN İNKİŞAFI VƏ KLİNİK ƏHƏMİYYƏTİ](../publications/4aab7ec4211bbdca9813.md)

G\.M Nasrullayeva

Qloballaşma, miqrasiya, urbanizasiya və ətraf mühitdə baş verən dəyişikliklər insan sağlamlığına, xüsusilə immun sisteminin funksional vəziyyətinə əhəmiyyətli təsir göstərir\. Bu amillərin təsiri nəticəsində anadangəlmə immun çatışmazlıqları haqqında elmi təsəvvürlər əhəmiyyətli dərəcədə dəyişmiş və hazırda bu xəstəliklər daha geniş anlayış olan immunitetin anadangəlmə səhvləri \(Inborn Errors of Immunity – IEI\) termini ilə ifadə olunur\. Əvvəllər nadir və çox zaman gec diaqnostika olunan xəstəliklər kimi qiymətləndirilən bu patologiyalar hazırda qlobal səhiyyənin mühüm problemlərindən biri hesab edilir\. Molekulyar\-genetik texnologiyaların sürətli inkişafı immunitetin anadangəlmə səhvlərinin erkən və dəqiq diaqnostikasına imkan yaratmışdır\. Beynəlxalq əməkdaşlığın genişlənməsi, qlobal xəstə registrlərinin yaradılması və klinik protokolların standartlaşdırılması bütün dünyada bu xəstəliklərin aşkar edilmə səviyyəsinin yüksəlməsinə şərait yaratmışdır\. Eyni zamanda, ətraf mühit amillərinin mikrobiota və mikrobiomun tərkib və funksiyasına təsiri immun sisteminin fəaliyyətinin formalaşmasında mühüm rol oynayır\. TREC/KREC analizlərindən istifadə etməklə neonatal skrininq bir sıra ölkələrdə ağır immun çatışmazlığı formalarının, xüsusilə ağır kombinə olunmuş immun çatışmazlığının \(SCID\) erkən aşkarlanması məqsədilə getdikcə daha geniş tətbiq olunur və standart diaqnostik yanaşmaya çevrilməkdədir\. İmmunitetin anadangəlmə səhvləri konsepsiyasının formalaşması immun pozğunluqlarına yanaşmada yeni paradiqmanı əks etdirir\. Bu konsepsiyaya əsasən, immun sisteminin xəstəlikləri sadəcə ayrı\-ayrı immun hüceyrələrinin və ya molekullarının funksional pozğunluğu kimi deyil, genetik və ətraf mühit amilləri ilə qarşılıqlı əlaqədə olan mürəkkəb və dinamik proseslər kimi qiymətləndirilir\. Müasir yanaşmada immun sistemi yalnız hüceyrə və molekulların məcmusu deyil, genetik xüsusiyyətlər və ətraf mühit amilləri ilə qarşılıqlı əlaqədə fəaliyyət göstərən inteqrasiya olunmuş bioloji ekosistem kimi nəzərdən keçirilir\.

## [Lightweight Transformer\-based Ai Model for Multilingual and Code\-mixed Sentiment Analysis](../publications/4aacf9f07120000f1d4d.md)

vijay kumar

Social media users increasingly communicate across language boundaries, often combining two or more languages within the same sentence and frequently writing Indian languages in Roman script\. This creates a difficult setting for sentiment analysis because conventional monolingual models must cope with spelling variation, transliteration, informal vocabulary, emojis, abbreviations, language switching, and context\-dependent sentiment\. Large multilingual Transformer models have improved contextual understanding, but their computational cost can make deployment difficult on resource\-constrained systems\. This thesis proposes a lightweight Transformer\-based framework for multilingual and code\-mixed sentiment analysis\. The framework uses a multilingual teacher model, language\-aware normalization, and knowledge distillation to transfer contextual knowledge into a smaller student model\. The study focuses primarily on Hindi\-English \(Hinglish\) and Spanish\-English \(Spanglish\) social\-media text, using the SemEval\-2020 Task 9 SentiMix corpora as a reproducible benchmark\. The proposed framework is evaluated against classical machine\-learning, recurrent neural\-network, and full\-size Transformer baselines\. Evaluation is designed to consider not only accuracy and macro/weighted F1, but also inference latency, parameter count, memory consumption, robustness to noisy and code\-mixed text, and the consistency of predictions across language pairs\. An explainability component is also included so that important tokens contributing to a prediction can be inspected\. The central research question is whether a substantially smaller Transformer can retain useful multilingual sentiment knowledge while reducing computational requirements\. The thesis therefore treats sentiment analysis as both a language\-understanding problem and an engineering deployment problem\. The resulting framework is intended for applications such as social\-media monitoring, customer\-feedback analysis, multilingual communication systems, and other AI systems where language diversity and limited computing resources must be considered together\. Keywords: Transformer, multilingual NLP, code\-mixed text, sentiment analysis, knowledge distillation, Hinglish, Spanglish, lightweight AI, explainable AI, social media\.

## [AI for Grading from the Teaching Perspective \(with an EssayGrader Case Comparison\)](../publications/4ab072147534c4c325d3.md)

Ian J\. Shepherd

AI has taken the academic world by storm, dramatically affecting written assignments and student performance evaluations\. This paper examines the use of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) from the teaching perspective, with emphasis on daily grading workflows\. We analyze benefits such as fair and consistent application of rubrics, the ability to incorporate articles and course materials as inputs to grading, and the delivery of individualized, extensive feedback\. We compare these capabilities against a representative product—EssayGrader—situate our claims within current scholarship on Automated Essay Scoring \(AES\) and Large Language Models \(LLMs\) as graders, and provide policy guidance\.

## [Instrument\-Agnostic Machine Learning Framework for Accurate Prediction of Functional Groups from Tandem Mass Spectrometry](../publications/4ab1a16ccf8194a4ef2f.md)

Connor H\. Beveridge; Prageeth R\. Wijewardhane; Matthew Muhoberac; Nicolás M\. Morato; Andreas Kaerner; Li‐Kang Zhang; Douglas D\. Richardson; Ayanna Shoulds; Jeffrey R\. Gilbert; Christopher J\. Welch; Shane E\. Tichy; Gaurav Chopra

Abstract Structural elucidation of unknown compounds using tandem mass spectrometry \(MS/MS\) is an ongoing challenge\. Expert chemists will often use common product ion peaks and neutral losses or peak matching software to predict structural aspects from MS/MS spectra, a process which is time consuming and limited by the molecular entries in the database\. We introduce an instrument\-agnostic machine learning \(ML\) framework that predicts functional groups directly from MS/MS spectra, eliminating the need for conventional database searches\. The ML models are trained on data from different sources, the MassBank of North America \(MONA\), a public database, and a custom MS/MS database acquired using a single high throughput desorption electrospray ionization \(DESI\) MS/MS platform to showcase transferability of model predictions independent of instrument acquisition\. Additionally, a novel spectral representation is developed for ML use by standardizing the spectra to the precursor ion m/z\. We utilized molecular metrics, specifically, average molecular F1 score of 87% \(MONA\) and 76% \(DESI\) and average molecular accuracy of 94% \(MONA\) and 87% \(DESI\), indicating similar model performance when trained on different databases to validate the ML framework\. To further illustrate the robustness and transferability of our ML framework, models trained on DESI\-generated data successfully predicted functional groups, using spectral data generated from a blind test set of molecules using two different company laboratories using distinct mass spectrometry instruments \(Orbitrap and TOF\) operated in positive\-ion mode electrospray ionization\. We believe that such an approach, where models trained on data from one instrument can reliably make accurate predictions on spectra acquired using different instruments in a database\-free manner, will significantly expand the practical applications of ML to mass spectrometry\.

## [Automated detection of inflammation in foot thermographic images of patients with diabetes acquired in an uncontrolled clinical environment](../publications/4abfa8a80613a5414213.md)

Riki Wartakusumah; Hiroshi Noguchi; Saldy Yusuf; Kanae Mukai; Mayumi Okuwa; Makoto Oe

AIMS: Quantitative methods for detecting diabetic foot inflammation remain limited, though localized skin\-temperature elevation is a promising early indicator\. Because background variability can hinder AI\-based foot identification, we evaluated AI\-driven thermal imaging for diabetic foot inflammation under uncontrolled clinical backgrounds and assessed whether curtain\-based background control and grayscale conversion improved detection\. METHODS: Cross\-sectional study design was conducted in Makassar, Indonesia, 100 plantar thermal images from 50 diabetic patients were acquired with and without a curtain, preprocessed \(sensitivity, 1\.5; emissivity, 0\.98\), and converted to grayscale\. Expert\-identified inflammatory hotspots were annotated and used to train a YOLO11n model with 5\-fold cross\-validation, evaluated using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, ROC\-AUC, IoU, and case\-error analysis\. RESULTS: With a curtain, color\-map images achieved sensitivity of 0\.773, versus 0\.455 without one\. Grayscale images performed consistently across conditions, with best results in the mixed dataset \(accuracy, 0\.980; precision, 0\.976; sensitivity, 0\.932; specificity, 0\.994; AUC 0\.966 vs\. 0\.886 for color\-map\)\. Correctly detected cases showed IoU &gt; 0\.9\. Low thermal contrast and small region of interest were the most frequent failure categories\. CONCLUSIONS: AI\-driven thermal imaging detects diabetic foot inflammation under uncontrolled conditions\. A curtain improved color\-map detection, but grayscale imaging provided robust, curtain\-independent performance, supporting its use for clinical screening\.

## [Tax Knowledge, Tax Literacy, Learning Motivation, and Students’ Tax Understanding](../publications/4ac51da59dd815444326.md)

Anastasya Nastiti; Umarudin Kurniawan; Indriyani; Eksa Ridwansyah

This study examines how tax knowledge, tax literacy, and learning motivation relate to tax understanding among tax accounting students at Politeknik Negeri Lampung\. Primary data from 122 students in the 2022 and 2023 cohorts, selected through purposive sampling, were collected using a 16\-item Likert\-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression\. Tax knowledge \(β = 0\.408, p &lt; 0\.001\) and learning motivation \(β = 0\.268, p = 0\.001\) were positively and significantly associated with tax understanding, whereas tax literacy had a positive but nonsignificant coefficient \(β = 0\.166, p = 0\.061\)\. Jointly, the three variables were significant and explained 44\.1% of the variation in tax understanding\. Tax understanding is associated mainly with conceptual knowledge and sustained motivation to learn, while tax literacy acts as a supporting capability\. The findings direct study programs to prioritize conceptual reinforcement and learning motivation and to embed literacy activities in case\-based application\. The purposive sample comes from one study program and all variables were measured with short self\-report scales in a cross\-sectional questionnaire, so the results indicate associations and cannot be generalized to all students\.

## [Integrating domain knowledge and user requirements in kitchen layout optimization](../publications/4ac8df1bbaab37e0d6b5.md)

Zoltán Nádudvari; Natabara Máté Gyöngyössy; János Botzheim

Abstract Layout design data sources exhibit a fundamental asymmetry: the challenge lies in processing structured, high\-quality domain knowledge alongside task\-specific natural language user requirements\. To address this, we propose a hybrid evaluation framework for evolutionary algorithms \(EAs\) that quantifies constraint violations as virtual displacement costs\. The framework is evaluated in the present study on four kitchen\-layout optimization scenarios with task\-specific user requirements and component sets\. By integrating hard\-coded domain rules with a fuzzy\-logic\-driven Abstract Syntax Tree \(AST\), the system enables a flexible yet explainable scoring mechanism\. This approach allows for a granular penalty system for individuals, while also guiding local search heuristics through component\-level diagnostic logging\. The implementation of the AST results in a marginal reduction in convergence cost while reducing the relative dispersion of the algorithms\. Within this kitchen\-layout benchmark, the evolutionary algorithms achieved lower execution times and aggregate penalty scores than the selected LLM chat applications\. The three non\-expert human\-generated layouts were included only as an exploratory reference because of the small and demographically homogeneous participant sample\.

## [Inclusion or exclusion? Arab teacher leaders’ experiences of faith visibility and cultural recognition in Western schools](../publications/4ad3945a2ed553d245d6.md)

Norma Ghamrawi; Norma Ghamrawi; Tarek Shal; Najah A\. R\. Ghamrawi; Najah A\. R\. Ghamrawi

Inclusion is widely promoted in Western education, yet how it is lived by minoritised professionals in everyday school life remains underexamined\. This interpretive qualitative study investigates how Arab teacher leaders in Western schools experience and interpret inclusion in routine professional interactions, especially where faith visibility and gendered courtesy norms become salient, and how they respond when such moments generate tension or disagreement\. Semi\-structured interviews were conducted with 12 teacher leaders working across Western countries\. Data were analysed using NVivo, and findings indicate that inclusion is often experienced as conditional, enacted through boundary tests around greetings, touch, warmth, and sociability, and stabilised through sensemaking that can amplify incidents into reputational judgements\. Participants also described intersectional scrutiny and credibility penalties that shape whose explanations count, constraining informal authority and teacher leadership legitimacy\. The study extends inclusion and teacher leadership scholarship by theorising inclusion as a struggle over recognition and interpretive authority and by identifying everyday mechanisms through which legitimacy is granted or withdrawn in practice\.

Sara Zenoni; Alessandra Amato

## [The riverine legacy of reservoirs](../publications/4add652632a797e77d1e.md)

Leandro Esteban Miranda

Reservoirs exposed to similar environmental drivers frequently exhibit markedly different ecological responses\. Existing reservoir concepts describe many aspects of impounded rivers, but none directly explains why environmental drivers produce contrasting ecological responses among reservoirs\. I propose riverine legacy , defined as the enduring ecological characteristics that reservoirs inherit from the rivers they impound\. Riverine legacy arises because impoundment transforms river systems without completely erasing their spatial, environmental, ecological, and trophic organization\. Riverine legacy consists of five interconnected dimensions through which inherited characteristics interact with contemporary environmental drivers to generate ecological responses at population, community, and ecosystem levels\. I provide three examples to illustrate how riverine legacy may explain contrasting responses to biological invasions, longitudinal variation in community organization, and differences in ecological transformation among impounded rivers\. The concept yields six testable predictions concerning ecological organization, ecosystem responsiveness, fisheries, recovery trajectories, and conservation opportunities across reservoir networks\. Riverine legacy is not proposed as a metric but as a concept that generates testable hypotheses about how inherited riverine characteristics influence contemporary ecological responses\. Recognizing that reservoirs retain enduring ecological characteristics inherited from their riverine origins provides a foundation for improving ecological interpretation, conservation planning, monitoring, management, and restoration across impounded river systems\.

## [Electrochemical strategies for peptide synthesis, deprotection and scalable reactor technologies](../publications/4af5e069fb320f97b5b7.md)

Pradip Mali; I\. Sreedhar

Peptides have high target specificity, favourable safety profiles, and increasing applications in oncology, metabolic disorders, infectious diseases, and precision medicine, making them one of the fastest\-growing classes of therapeutic molecules\. Traditional peptide synthesis involves more hazardous solvents and stoichiometric quantities of coupling reagents, which lead to high process mass intensity and environmental impact\. In electrochemical synthesis, electrons are traceless redox reagents that allow for the controlled activation and transformation of peptide substrates under mild conditions\. Advances in electrochemical peptide bond formation, electrochemical deprotection methods, and new technologies of electrochemical reactors for peptide synthesis are critically discussed\. The focus is on phosphine\-mediated anodic peptide coupling, iodide\-mediated amide formation, residue\-selective electrochemical modifications and redox\-triggered deprotection methods\. Advances in flow electrochemistry, scalable reactor designs and sustainable peptide production methods are thoroughly discussed\. The effect of electrochemical parameters such as the electrode materials, current density, solvent systems, electrolytes, reaction time, and reactor design on reaction efficiency and selectivity is critically evaluated\. However, there are still some issues that need to be addressed, such as the scope of the substrates, the lack of understanding of the mechanisms, fouling of the electrodes, scalability and the absence of a standardized method of reporting\. Opportunities for the future include the combination of electro­chemistry and continuous\-flow processing, sustainable solvent systems, automated synthesis platforms, and machine learning\-assisted process optimization\. Electrochemical approaches provide valuable potential for development of greener, more efficient and potentially scalable technology for next\-generation pharmaceutical manufacturing of peptides\.

## [GraphACM: Graph\-based Action Consistency Measurement for Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents](../publications/4b093e19bf49838c2b57.md)

Yaxin Ma; Wenbo Zhang; Satya Krishna Pothapragada; Alina Zare

Behavioral consistency across repeated executions provides an informative signal for assessing the reliability of large language model \(LLM\) agents\. However, existing approaches typically summarize consistency with a single task\-level score, without identifying where behavioral differences occur or whether actions are compared under equivalent decision contexts\. We propose a graph\-based framework for fine\-grained behavioral consistency measurement and uncertainty quantification\. Given multiple rollouts of the same task, we merge equivalent states into a directed, action\-labeled graph, enabling action comparisons at shared decision states\. We introduce node\-level and global measures of action consistency, using the global consistency score as a proxy for uncertainty to predict task success or failure\. Experiments across three LLMs on ALFWorld, AppWorld, and WebShop demonstrate that our measure is positively associated with task success and achieves an average AUROC of 0\.811 for task\-success prediction, outperforming the strongest behavioral\-consistency baseline \(0\.729\) and verbalized confidence \(0\.769\)\. These results highlight the effectiveness of state\-conditioned behavioral consistency and pinpoint where agent actions agree\.

## [KONSEP DAN PRINSIP MANAJEMEN MUTU DALAM PENINGKATAN KUALITAS PROGRAM KESEHATAN: A LITERATURE REVIEW](../publications/4b0aaabfdf08d0623a0b.md)

Alya Masthura Safwan; Irwan Saputra

Manajemen mutu dalam bidang kesehatan tidak lagi cukup dipahami sebagai upaya memastikan pelayanan sesuai standar\. Mutu menjadi bagian dari cara organisasi merencanakan, menjalankan, mengevaluasi, dan memperbaiki program secara berkelanjutan\. Literature review ini bertujuan menganalisis konsep dan prinsip manajemen mutu serta keterkaitannya dengan peningkatan kualitas program kesehatan berdasarkan 20 artikel yang diterbitkan pada tahun 2026\. Artikel yang ditelaah meliputi penelitian kuantitatif dan kualitatif, studi implementasi, studi kasus organisasi, systematic review, scoping review, umbrella review, artikel konseptual, dan editorial ilmiah\. Hasil sintesis menunjukkan bahwa manajemen mutu dibangun oleh delapan prinsip utama, yaitu fokus pada pengguna layanan, kepemimpinan, keterlibatan tenaga kesehatan, pendekatan sistem dan proses, standardisasi, pengambilan keputusan berbasis data, keselamatan, dan perbaikan berkelanjutan\. Berbagai pendekatan seperti Plan\-Do\-Study\-Act, Lean Six Sigma, quality improvement collaboratives, akreditasi, High Reliability Organization, systems leadership, dan improvement science memperlihatkan cara berbeda untuk mencapai tujuan yang sama, yaitu membangun organisasi kesehatan yang mampu belajar, beradaptasi, dan mempertahankan hasil perbaikan\. Dengan demikian, manajemen mutu perlu ditempatkan sebagai bagian dari keseluruhan siklus pengelolaan program kesehatan, bukan sebagai kegiatan penilaian yang berhenti setelah target atau standar tertentu tercapai\.

## [Current perspectives on smart grid cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection](../publications/4b124f71953de5848064.md)

Nilesh Jain

The increasing convergence of renewable energy sources, information and communication technology, Internet of Things devices, smart meters, and phasor measurement units has enhanced the efficiency, reliability, and real\-time operation of Smart Grids\. However, this interconnected cyber\-physical infrastructure has also increased cybersecurity vulnerabilities and attack surfaces\. This paper reviews AI/ML\-based security approaches for Smart Grid cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection, focusing on major threats such as False Data Injection Attacks, Denial\-of\-Service attacks, Man\-in\-the\-Middle attacks, spoofing, malware, and malicious command injection\. The study examines existing protection mechanisms, including authentication and access control, intrusion detection, attack mitigation, secure communication, data protection, and privacy preservation\. The study further discusses cyber\-physical system protection, resilience, incident response, continuous monitoring, network segmentation, and AI/ML\-based security approaches\. A review of recent research highlights advances in anomaly detection, trust management, multilayer security, and intelligent threat detection\. However, challenges remain in scalability, real\-time processing, interoperability, adaptive defense, limited datasets, and real\-world validation\. The findings emphasize the need for integrated, intelligent, scalable, and adaptive cybersecurity approaches to strengthen Smart Grid resilience, reliability, availability, and operational continuity\.

## [Thalidomide dose selection for prevention of camrelizumab\-induced reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation: a multicenter, randomized phase II trial](../publications/4b170a15cb9ae1eb7861.md)

Xiao Fu; Shuning Xu; Peng Cheng; Haitao Lan; Yina Wang; Dong Zhao; Mingyue Liu; Shouguo Li; Weidong Liu; Guiping Yu; Xiaowei Wei; Feilong Sun; Yu Yao; Ying Liu

Background Reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation \(RCCEP\) is a characteristic cutaneous adverse event associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors\. This study compared two prophylactic thalidomide doses to identify the more promising dose for further evaluation\. Methods In this multicenter, randomized clinical trial, patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma or non\-small cell lung cancer \(NSCLC\) were randomly assigned to receive thalidomide 50 mg/day \(Group A\) or 100 mg/day \(Group B\) during first\-line treatment with camrelizumab plus standard chemotherapy\. The primary endpoint was overall RCCEP incidence; secondary endpoints included grade ≥3 RCCEP, median time to RCCEP onset, week 6 and week 9 RCCEP incidence, and safety\. Results A total of 72 patients were randomized\. RCCEP occurred in 12 of 36 patients \(33\.3%\) in Group A and 9 of 36 patients \(25\.0%\) in Group B\. RCCEP incidence at week 6 was 13\.9% in Group A and 19\.4% in Group B, and by week 9 was 25\.0% and 19\.4%, respectively\. No grade ≥3 RCCEP occurred; all first RCCEP events were grade 1, with 1 grade 2 event reported in Group A\. Among patients who developed RCCEP, median onset time was 1\.49 and 1\.31 months, respectively\. Thalidomide\-related adverse events occurred in 22\.2% and 41\.7% of patients, and grade 3 or higher thalidomide\-related adverse events occurred in 8\.3% and 22\.2%, respectively\. Serious adverse events occurred in 11\.1% and 13\.9% of patients, respectively\. Conclusion Thalidomide 100 mg/day met the prespecified incidence\-based dose\-selection criterion compared with 50 mg/day but was associated with a higher incidence of grade 3 or higher toxicity\. Further controlled evaluation is warranted\. Clinical trial registration https://clinicaltrials\.gov/study/NCT06231680 , identifier NCT06231680\.

## [Comparative outcomes of primary closure, rhomboid flap reconstruction, and open excision for pilonidal sinus disease: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/4b18f9add4d83c0b3009.md)

Abdullah  AA\. Abdullah; Mohamed  TM\. Sayed

Background Pilonidal sinus disease \(PSD\) is a common surgical condition with multiple operative options, each associated with different recurrence and recovery profiles\. ObjectiveTo compare postoperative outcomes and recurrence rates among primary closure, rhomboid flap reconstruction, and open excision for PSD\. MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 300 patients with primary or recurrent PSD treated with primary closure \(n = 100\), rhomboid flap reconstruction \(n = 100\), or open excision \(n = 100\)\.Demographic characteristics, operative variables, postoperative pain, length of hospital stay, wound healing time, return to work, postoperative complications, and recurrence were analyzed\.Continuous variables were compared using the Kruskal\-Wallis test, while categorical variables were analyzed using the χ 2 test or Fisher exact test\.Risk ratios \(RRs\) and risk differences with 95% CIs were calculated for comparative outcomes, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with recurrence\. ResultsBaseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable across treatment groups\.Operative time and early postoperative pain did not differ significantly according to disease status within each surgical technique\.Open excision was associated with a significantly lower overall recurrence risk than primary closure \(RR, 0\.29; 95% CI, 0\.11\-0\.77\),including among patients with primary disease\.Rhomboid flap reconstruction demonstrated the shortest healing time \(approximately 30 d\), followed by primary closure \(approximately 36 d\), whereas open excision required substantially longer healing \(&gt;75 d\)and delayed return to work\.Postoperative complication rates were similar among techniques\.Higher body mass index and positive family history were associated with increased recurrence\.Conclusions Surgical technique was a major determinant of recurrence and recovery outcomes in PSD\.Open excision achieved the lowest recurrence risk but required prolonged healing and delayed return to work\.Rhomboid flap reconstruction provided faster recovery without a significant recurrence advantage over primary closure\.These findings support individualized surgical decision\-making based on recurrence risk, recovery expectations, and patient\-related factors\.

## [Script Reform, Human Capital and Social Change: Evidence From Uzbekistan&\#x27;s Latin Alphabet Transition](../publications/4b1caf1aadc7c0b84031.md)

Angelina Nazarova

ABSTRACT Script reforms are common nation‐building tools, yet rigorous evidence on their effects is scarce\. This paper examines Uzbekistan&\#x27;s transition from Cyrillic to Latin script, mandated in 1993 and implemented in schools from 1996\. I study heterogeneous effects across initial conditions using a difference‐in‐differences design that exploits variation in exposure across birth cohorts and pre‐reform district characteristics\. The reform had no significant average effect on literacy, but it generated substantial heterogeneity: districts with lower baseline literacy gained 0\.09 standard deviations per standard deviation of the baseline literacy gap, whereas districts with more Russian speakers experienced relative losses of about 0\.05 standard deviations\. These patterns reveal the redistributive politics of nation‐building\. The reform also reshaped labour markets: Latin‐exposed cohorts moved away from state employment and, less sharply, from entrepreneurship\. The same cohorts became more likely to express intolerance towards speakers of other languages, an effect specific to the linguistic margin\. The findings suggest that script reforms do not deliver aggregate literacy improvements but have significant distributional consequences and may heighten ethnolinguistic divisions\.

## [Circadian rhythm dysregulation and ferroptosis in hypertension: mechanisms and therapeutic implications](../publications/4b2b3d04eb6bee3cb779.md)

Hui Zeng; Jiawen Lin; Jun Chen

Hypertension exhibits a pronounced circadian rhythm; however, the mechanisms by which circadian disruption translates temporal imbalance into sustained vascular and renal injury remain unclear\. Increasing evidence suggests that circadian misalignment may promote endothelial dysfunction, vascular remodeling, and renal injury through ferroptosis driven by oxidative stress dysregulation, thereby increasing the risk of hypertension\. Based on current evidence, this review proposes that circadian disruption induces a temporal mismatch between oxidative stress generation and antioxidant defense, thereby lowering the threshold for ferroptosis in cardiovascular and renal tissues\. This process may amplify hemodynamic stress, impair endothelial integrity, and disturb renal sodium handling, ultimately contributing to the development and progression of hypertension\. Although direct causal evidence remains limited, this review integrates circadian biology with ferroptosis and provides a mechanistic link between time\-dependent physiological regulation and structural organ damage, highlighting a potentially promising strategy for future hypertension intervention\.

## [Testing the dimensionality of public attitudes toward artificial intelligence](../publications/4b3812aee2300f408201.md)

James Everett Katz

Public opinion about artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly measured and invoked in debates about AI governance, yet heterogeneous survey items are often interpreted as indicators of one underlying attitude\. Using a weighted survey of registered voters in the U\.S\. state of Pennsylvania \( N = 929\), this article tests whether four AI attitude and policy items form a coherent dimension and examines the correlates of a nervous\-to\-excited affect item\. A principal\-component analysis of polychoric correlations in the complete\-case subset \( N = 460\) does not support a strong unidimensional scale\. A companion sensitivity analysis of the three non\-employment items on the larger available sample reproduces the same two\-component pattern, so the negative scaling finding is not an artifact of the employment\-contingent job item\. A weak first component links excitement, lower job concern, and opposition to regulation, but reliability is low \(ordinal alpha = 0\.45; KMO = 0\.48\)\. An item asking whether the U\.S\. federal government is equipped to regulate AI loads separately and aligns more closely with evaluations of the named institution than with AI affect\. Weighted regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity\-robust standard errors, corroborated by multiple imputation with 20 datasets, shows that AI excitement is associated most strongly with personal AI use, followed by prospective economic optimism, age, and education\. This ordering holds in both the listwise and multiply imputed specifications\. The findings are bounded to this survey module, but they show why AI affect, behavioral exposure, policy preference, and institution\-specific governance judgments should not be combined into an accidental scale without first establishing that they measure a common construct\.

## [FedPoP: federated learning meets proof of participation](../publications/4b3aed10e4d305a6c941.md)

Devriş İşler; Elina van Kempen; Seoyeon Hwang; Nikolaos Laoutaris B

Federated learning \(FL\) offers privacy preserving, distributed machine learning, allowing clients to contribute to a global model without revealing their local data\. As models increasingly serve as monetizable digital assets, the ability to prove participation in their training becomes essential for establishing ownership\. In this paper, we address this emerging need by introducing FedPoP , a novel FL framework that allows non\-linkable proof of participation while preserving client anonymity and privacy without requiring either extensive computations or a public ledger\. FedPoP is designed to seamlessly integrate with existing secure aggregation protocols to ensure compatibility with real\-world FL deployments\. We provide a proof of concept implementation and an empirical evaluation under realistic client dropouts\. In our prototype, FedPoP adds lightweight proof\-generation and verification overhead on top of securely aggregated FL and enables a client to prove participation to a service provider in 0\.0612 s\. These results indicate FedPoP is practical for real\-world deployments that require auditable participation without sacrificing privacy\.

中文简介 \(Abstract in Chinese\) 《升维》第一卷《碳硅:螺旋升维》是一部在人工智能狂飙与社会危机交织的风暴眼时期写就的理论与工程宣言。全书以微分几何、非平衡态热力学、控制论与物理第一性原理为骨架,尝试为人类文明在“自杀式刹车”与“毁灭性狂飙”这两条绝路之外,劈开“碳硅共生与双螺旋升维”的第三条生路。 全书核心理论与学术贡献涵盖四大维度: 破除“软件唯心主义”,重构 AI 第一性物理底座:深刻诊治自回归大模型\(LLM\)因“物理感官缺失公理”导致的大模型自噬综合征\(MAD\)、相空间方差塌缩与高维“空心橙子皮”测度零陷阱;率先提出硅基物理断奶路径,将李代数 $\\mathfrak\{se\}\(3\)$、诺特定理与哈密顿能量守恒硬化为网络先验约束,消除死锁与虚假发散,构建基于李雅普诺夫第二方法与 CLF\-CBF 对偶二次规划\(QP\)的安全控制屏障。 击碎“无用阶级论”,重塑人本尊严与新劳动价值论:彻底粉碎“数据主义”与投降主义神话,将劳动重新公理化定义为“高维连续具身负熵发生过程”。确立“控制指挥权不可让渡公理”,倡导“以人为本的外骨骼具身共生”路线,确保人类对核心意图的掌控与物理级熔断权。 首创“双轨制”立体架构:兼具面向公众与政策制定者的宏大“文明叙事轨”,以及完全符合国际顶级学术规范的“硬核科学轨附录”\(严密展开公理、定理与李雅普诺夫势盆证明\)。 碳硅共生实体的“活体创作自证”:本书由人类作者牢牢掌控一阶因果航向,结合前沿人工智能大模型展开高维求证与跨学科协同推导,以成书实践本身完成了后大模型\(Post\-LLM\)时代知识生产范式跃迁的活体自证。 \(注:本书完整 503 页专著正文目前处于受保护禁运期 Embargoed Access,待正式纸质专著出版发行后自动开放。本记录用于确立该理论体系的国际学术优先权与永久数字对象标识符 DOI。\) Abstract in English Ascending Dimensions \(Vol\. I\): Carbon\-Silicon Double\-Helix Co\-Evolution is a foundational theoretical and engineering treatise addressing the systemic crisis of unconstrained artificial intelligence\. Rooted in differential geometry, non\-equilibrium thermodynamics, modern control theory, and first\-principles physics, this work charts a third civilizational path beyond reactionary stagnation and destructive accelerationism: the co\-evolutionary double helix of carbon\-based and silicon\-based intelligences\.
