## [Maternal serum alpha\-fetoprotein, fetal fraction, and prognostic nutritional index in relation to adverse pregnancy outcomes](../publications/4b5202fbc3ff90688651.md)

Pınar Tuğçe Özer; Meriç Balıkoğlu; Gülin Okay; Mehmet Özer

Objectives: To evaluate the association of maternal serum alpha\-fetoprotein \(AFP\) with adverse pregnancy outcomes and to investigate its relationship with fetal fraction \(FF\) and the Prognostic Nutritional Index \(PNI\) as potential indicators of placental function and maternal inflammatory\-nutritional status\. Methodology: This retrospective study included 192 singleton pregnancies followed at a tertiary center between 2020 and 2024\. Maternal serum AFP, NIPT\-derived fetal fraction, and PNI were evaluated in relation to preeclampsia, proteinuria, and gestational diabetes mellitus\. Continuous variables were assessed for normality with the Shapiro\-Wilk test and compared using the independent\-samples t\-test or Mann\-Whitney U test, as appropriate\. Categorical variables were compared using the chi\-square or Fisher’s exact test\. A two\-sided p&lt;0\.05 was considered statistically significant\. Results: Preeclampsia occurred in 5\.7%, proteinuria in 13\.0%, and gestational diabetes mellitus in 29\.2% of pregnancies\. Fetal fraction was higher in pregnancies with preeclampsia \(11\.70 \[8\.65\-14\.20\] vs\. 7\.60 \[5\.60\-10\.10\]; p=0\.007; rank\-biserial r=0\.48\)\. Proteinuria was associated with lower AFP levels \(28\.30 \[25\.30\-39\.00\] vs\. 35\.10 \[30\.20\-44\.50\]; p=0\.029; r=\-0\.27\) and higher hemoglobin levels \(11\.80 \[11\.20\-12\.40\] vs\. 11\.40 \[10\.75\-12\.00\] g/dL; p=0\.042; r=0\.25\)\. AFP, fetal fraction, and corrected PNI did not differ significantly according to gestational diabetes status\. Conclusions: Maternal serum AFP was not significantly associated with preeclampsia or gestational diabetes mellitus\. However, lower AFP levels were associated with proteinuria, and higher fetal fraction was associated with preeclampsia\. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory associations and require confirmation in larger, appropriately adjusted studies\.

## [MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering](../publications/4b528f7f29d891f342b0.md)

Shangheng Du; Jinxin Shi; Shuaiyu Zhang; Yiming Wu; Junpeng Zhao; Shiyang Feng; Xin Li; Liang He; Xiangchao Yan; Bo Zhang

Large language models \(LLMs\) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI \(AI4AI\) as a pathway toward recursive self\-improvement \(RSI\)\. Workflow\-driven machine learning engineering \(MLE\) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long\-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model\-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback\. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments\. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes\. We propose a post\-training method for autonomous long\-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture\-of\-Experts agentic model\. We design the Kaggle\-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model\-directed experimentation\. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool\-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome\-guided supervision\. Windowed Interaction RL \(WIRL\) treats the multi\-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome\-based reward\. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends\. On MLE\-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37\.9% to 72\.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi\-K3 and GLM\-5\.3\. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks\.

## [Machine Learning Utilisation and Perceived Financial Reporting Quality among Employees of Selected Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: A PLS\-SEM Analysis](../publications/4b53f2827f800b3dc542.md)

Yusuf Yahaya; Muhammad  Aminu Isa; Nasiru Abdulsalam Kao’je

Machine learning \(ML\) is increasingly used in accounting and assurance processes, yet focused evidence on its relationship with financial reporting quality \(FRQ\) in Nigerian banking remains limited\. This study examines the association between ML utilisation and perceived FRQ among employees of selected listed Deposit Money Banks \(DMBs\) in Nigeria\. A quantitative cross\-sectional survey design was used\. The study population comprised 243 eligible employees; 181 questionnaires were distributed after allowing for anticipated non\-response, 151 completed questionnaires were returned, and all 151 were valid for analysis, yielding a response rate of 83\.43%\. ML and perceived FRQ were measured with five indicators each on a five\-point Likert scale\. PLS\-SEM was implemented in SmartPLS 4\. The measurement model demonstrated strong indicator loadings, reliability, and convergent validity, although the very high reliability coefficients warrant assessment of possible item redundancy\. ML utilisation was positively associated with perceived FRQ \(β = 0\.719, t = 12\.63, p &lt; 0\.001, 95% CI \[0\.631, 0\.788\]\)\. The model explained 51\.7% of the variance in perceived FRQ \(R² = 0\.517; adjusted R² = 0\.514\), with a large effect size \(f² = 1\.07\)\. Because the design is cross\-sectional and perception\-based, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects\. The study contributes focused evidence on ML utilisation and perceived financial\-reporting quality in the Nigerian listed\-banking context\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and the New World of Work](../publications/4b55de9a504166647eb5.md)

Olivier Guyottot

Change occurs at the speed of technological devices\. It is undeniable that artificial intelligence \(AI\) will continue to shape the workplace, leading to a new world of work\. While industries, whether small or large, local or international, face challenges due to technological advancements, a central question remains: What should the role of humans be in this “new” world of work? Furthermore, what should the relationship between humans and technology look like? This book, which includes various perspectives, thought pieces, twelve chapters, and directives authored by 30 national and international contributors from universities and societies, explores the impact of AI on the world of work through three distinct lenses: Foundational Lens : This section examines the evolving landscape of the modern workforce, highlighting the transformative shifts that are reshaping our understanding of work itself and showcasing how generative AI and emerging technologies affect the workplace\. Strategic Lens : This part emphasises the essential role of education in equipping students with the skills and knowledge necessary to thrive in this new era of work, preparing them to meet the demands of a constantly changing job market\. Operational Lens : This division provides deeper insights into various industries, analysing how they are affected by the dynamics of AI in the workplace\. Offering multi\-disciplinary perspectives alongside global insights, this book discusses AI’s transformation of work and, by extension, our lives\. While it presents several guidelines, the focus remains on ensuring that human beings are not dominated by technology\. Instead, technology should act as a co\-partner in the workplace\. This book aims to help you determine humans’ role in the workplace\. The book is highly recommended for academics who are preparing students for the workforce while also being infuenced by developments within that very workplace\.

## [PENGARUH ALOKASI DANA DESA DAN JUMLAH PENDUDUK USIA PRODUKTIF TERHADAP PENDAPATAN PERKAPITA MASYARAKAT DI PROVINSI ACEH](../publications/4b623a82f5d151b942e7.md)

Amara Imanika; Hamdani Hamdani; Julia Alfianti

Abstract: This research aims to determine the effect of village fund allocation and the number of productive age population on the per capita income of the community in Aceh Province, both partially and simultaneously\. This research uses a quantitative approach with a panel data regression analysis method, namely a combination of time series and cross section data, with the help of EViews 13 software\. The data used is secondary data obtained from the Central Statistics Agency \(BPS\) and the Directorate General of Fiscal Balance \(DJPK\), which covers 23 districts/cities in Aceh Province during the 2020–2024 period\. Based on the results of model selection, it was found that the best model used was the Fixed Effect Model \(FEM\)\. The research results show that village fund allocation and the number of productive age population partially have a positive and significant effect on the per capita income of the community in Aceh Province\. Simultaneously, these two variables have a significant effect on the per capita income of people in Aceh Province\. These findings show that optimizing the management of village funds and utilizing the productive age population can encourage increased community welfare and equal distribution of income in Aceh Province\.Keywords: Village Funds, Productive\-Age Population, Per Capita Income\.

## [A scalar mismatch: the IETF’s sustainability approaches in a framework of infinite growth and abundance](../publications/4b638bb25a9b9e692810.md)

Fieke Jansen

Until recently, environmental harms were largely absent from internet governance discussions and their study\.This article offers an analyses of how the environmental impact of internet infrastructure is discussed within the Internet Engineering Task Force \(IETF\) arguing that sustainability becomes a justification regime for the internet&\#x27;s continued existence and growth in a world in crisis\.Taking a discard studies approach, I explore what is and what must be discarded for the internet to continue to operate through a thematic analysis of 26 position papers submitted to the Internet Architecture Board \(IAB\) e\-impact workshop\.These insights allow me to expand on Liboiron&\#x27;s \(2014, 2021\) concept of scalar mismatch to illuminate how limits to growth are directly at odds with the values that have shaped the internet\.The internet governance community has not come to grips with the idea that the network is an environmental problem in itself; rather, a belief in growth, abundance of natural resources, and sustainability through innovation shapes their understanding of sustainability\.This paper straddles infrastructure studies, internet governance studies, and environmental social sciences, showing how an environmental lens on infrastructure studies allows us to connect global governance debates with local conflict over resources\.

## [Exposure\-duration\-associated auditory dysfunction and cochlear presynaptic ribbon alterations during simulated high\-altitude hypobaric hypoxia in mice](../publications/4b6ec7b50ad578c449e0.md)

Qingping Zhang; Guanghao Yue; Ying Zhang; Shanhong Li; Wenjun Cao; Xiaoli Zhang; Benhong Ren; Chenguang Zhang; Chaohua Wang; Wanru Chen; Tana Wuren; Bin Guo; Yi Wang

Background High\-altitude hypobaric hypoxia can alter auditory function, but the temporal relationships among cochlear dysfunction, hair\-cell integrity, inner\-hair\-cell presynaptic ribbons, and redox\-bioenergetic disturbances remain unclear\. Methods Eighty male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to an ambient\-pressure control group in Xining, China \(approximately 2,260 m\), or to nominal 3\-, 15\-, or 30\-day simulated hypobaric\-hypoxia exposure groups \( n = 20 per group\)\. Chamber entry was staggered, and terminal assessments and tissue collection were completed within a period of less than 24 h\. Separate animal subsets were used for auditory brainstem response \(ABR\) recording and hematological assessment\. ABR thresholds, wave I latency, and wave I peak\-to\-trough amplitude were evaluated\. Hair\-cell survival and CtBP2\-positive presynaptic ribbons were assessed by confocal microscopy\. Hematological indices, 4\-hydroxynonenal \(4\-HNE\) and 8\-hydroxy\-2′\-deoxyguanosine\-related immunoreactivity, whole\-cochlear ATP content, and JC\-1\-defined mitochondrial polarization were also assessed\. Results Red blood cell count, hemoglobin concentration, and hematocrit were increased at all exposure durations\. Exposure group was associated with altered ABR thresholds and wave I measures\. Control\-focused comparisons showed prolonged wave I latency at 4 and 8 kHz in all hypoxia groups, whereas wave I amplitude at 90 dB SPL was lower at both frequencies only after 15 days\. OHC survival did not differ significantly among groups, and no overt IHC loss was observed\. CtBP2\-positive puncta were reduced in the basal turn after 3 days and in all cochlear turns after 15 days\. 4\-HNE immunoreactivity increased at all time points, whereas 8\-OHdG\-related immunoreactivity increased after 3 and 15 days\. Whole\-cochlear ATP content was reduced at all time points\. At 30 days, JC\-1 analysis indicated a shift toward mitochondrial depolarization in mixed cochlear\-cell suspensions\. Conclusion Simulated high\-altitude hypobaric\-chamber exposure was associated with an exposure\-duration\-associated and endpoint\-specific cochlear phenotype\. Auditory abnormalities and presynaptic ribbon alterations occurred without substantial hair\-cell loss and were accompanied by oxidative and bioenergetic disturbances\. The pattern of abnormalities varied across exposure groups and endpoints\.

## [PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories](../publications/4b7039eb642df7ee420b.md)

Jiachen Yao; Xiyuan Zhang; Annan Yu; Boran Han; Abdul Fatir Ansari; Shuai Zhang; Michael Bohlke\-Schneider; Bernie Wang

Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general\-purpose forecasting\. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified\. This distinction matters for trajectory\-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it\. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory\-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths\. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws\. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model\. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly\. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev\-bench and TIME\. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench \(fps\-bench\), which augments fev\-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics\. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps\-bench than all evaluated external baselines\. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long\-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse\. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications\.

## [Global Software Development Challenges and Techniques for Software Product Quality in Organizations: A Critical Review](../publications/4b71aa90d837d1894d11.md)

Patrick Enabudoso

Leaders in Global Software Development \(GSD\) organizations have experienced tremendous growth because of increased GSD awareness, greater benefits, and improved process effectiveness in distributed settings\. GSD acceptance and adaptation in dynamic, complex environments may be attributed to an added advantage\. The primary GSD challenges identified are team coordination, communication, collaboration, trust, culture, people, geographical distance, and time zones\. This study reviewed the literature and identified appropriate GSD techniques that enable leaders to implement best management practices to improve software product quality\. This paper provides a detailed critical literature review, summarized results, and a comparative study\. This study identified emerging GSD challenges in the literature as potential success factors when properly addressed\. In addition, the research confirmed GSD techniques that may help leaders manage software product quality effectively, avoid project failures, and meet customer expectations\.

## [Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers](../publications/4b728467c180ee49d078.md)

Soumik Mukhopadhyay; Long Mai; Abhinav Shrivastava; Aniruddha Mahapatra

Pixel\-space diffusion models have recently re\-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder\. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction \($\\boldsymbol\{u\}$\-prediction\) with clean image prediction \($\\boldsymbol\{x\_0\}$\-prediction\)\. In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\\boldsymbol\{x\_0\}$\- and $\\boldsymbol\{u\}$\-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end\-to\-end with diffusion training\. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity \-\- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction\. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF\-101 video, and large\-scale text\-to\-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings\. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high\-frequency deficit relative to real images\. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post\-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen\. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high\-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID\. Project webpage: https://soumik\-kanad\.github\.io/mflow\-diffusion/\.

## [UPI Fraud Intelligence &amp; Analytics Dashboard](../publications/4b9fea362ca61ca8c299.md)

Dr\. Manoj Singh Sayyed Alaa Mariya Irfan

The widespread use of the Unified Payments Interface \(UPI\) has made digital payments faster and more accessible, while also increasing the need to examine reported fraud in a structured way\. Much of the existing UPI fraud literature studies machine\-learning or deep\-learning techniques that classify or predict fraudulent transactions\. This paper describes the UPI Fraud Intelligence Analytics Dashboard, a dataset\-driven platform for analysing records that have already been labelled as fraudulent\. The dashboard analyses records by state, bank, fraud type, transaction amount, and time\. It also supports individual transaction checks, automatic statistical findings, and analysis of compatible uploaded files\. The prototype uses Flask and Pandas on the backend and HTML, JavaScript, Bootstrap, and Chart\.js on the frontend\. Its findings are calculated from the loaded records; it does not generate a fraud probability or claim to identify fraud independently\. The paper outlines the platform design, processing workflow, analytical features, and a functional evaluation using the supplied dataset\.

## [Association of APOE Gene Polymorphism with Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease and the Impact of Age, Gender, and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Iraqi Patients](../publications/4ba733b935d1165bcb58.md)

Muhanad Jassam Mohammad

The present study aimed to explore the linkage of APOE gene polymorphism with AD and to assess the effects of age, gender and type 2 Diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) in Iraqi population\. The study included 62 patients with AD and 48 control patients\. In clinical results, the incidence of AD was observed to be higher in women than in men, higher with age, and T2DM was shown to be a significant factor in the progression of the disease\.The molecular analysis was performed using Real\-Time PCR for the APOE polymorphism \(rs429358\) and two alleles \(T and C\) and three genotypes \(TT, TC and CC\) were found within the study groups\. The frequencies of the genotypes were TT \(OR=0\.46, 95% CI=0\.25\-0\.91\), TC \(0\.274\) and CC \(0\.177\) in the AD patients\. Regarding allelic frequencies, the T allele frequency was 0\.66 \(OR=0\.628, 95% CI=0\.59–1\.01\), whereas the C allele frequency was 0\.33 \(OR=1\.89, 95% CI=1\.6–4\.26\)\. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the analyzed population is highly susceptible to AD because the APOE gene variants play an important role, in addition to other metabolic and demographic factors\.

## [Interpretable Hybrid Machine Learning for Predicting Microbial Growth Curves: Comparing Direct Data\-Driven, Two\-Step Hybrid, and One\-Step Hybrid Approaches](../publications/4baeda9dc31fb6b6e1ab.md)

Fatih Tarlak; Özgün Yücel

Predictive microbiology relies on a two\-step workflow in which a primary model is fitted to each growth curve and secondary models relate the kinetic parameters to environmental conditions, which can propagate primary\-fit uncertainty\. This study compared three strategies for predicting Escherichia coli growth from temperature, pH, and water activity: \(i\) direct machine learning \(ML\) prediction of log counts; \(ii\) a two\-step hybrid approach, in which modified Gompertz parameters estimated for each curve were mapped to environmental conditions by a neural network; and \(iii\) a one\-step hybrid approach, in which the network predicted Gompertz parameters and was trained end\-to\-end on the growth\-curve misfit\. The 396 ComBase growth curves \(4082 observations\) were evaluated by repeated five\-fold cross\-validation grouped by environmental condition\. Direct ML achieved an RMSE of 0\.690 ± 0\.085 log CFU/mL but yielded no kinetic parameters\. The one\-step approach was statistically equivalent to direct ML \(RMSE = 0\.712 ± 0\.075; margin ±0\.1 log CFU/mL\), whereas the two\-step approach was slightly less accurate \(RMSE = 0\.745 ± 0\.101\)\. The one\-step model’s lag times and maximum growth rates agreed with independent primary\-fit estimates \(Spearman ρ = 0\.89 and 0\.93\)\. Within the studied conditions, it offered the most favourable balance between accuracy and interpretability\.

Linden Disney\-Hogg; Max Zuev

We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems\. ## [MODELING AND PERFORMANCE EVALUATION OF A PVBASED EV CHARGING STATION USING INC MPPT AND ANN CONTROLLER](../publications/4bbb17019946c8e23e7f.md)



The rapid adoption of electric vehicles \(EVs\) has intensified the need for efficient, reliable, and sustainable charging infrastructure\.Photovoltaic \(PV\)\-based EV charging stations present a promising solution by utilizing renewable energy to reduce dependency on fossil fuels\.However, the nonlinear characteristics of PV systems and varying environmental conditions pose significant challenges in achieving optimal performance\.This paper presents a detailed study and analysis of a PV\-powered EV charging station employing the Incremental Conductance \(INC\) Maximum Power Point Tracking \(MPPT\) technique integrated with an Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\) controller\.The INC algorithm ensures accurate and fast tracking of the maximum power point \(MPP\), while the ANN controller enhances system performance by providing adaptive and intelligent control\.The proposed system includes a PV array, DC\-DC boost converter, ANN controller, and EV battery charging unit\.The system is evaluated based on efficiency, stability, and dynamic response\.Results demonstrate improved performance in terms of reduced oscillations, faster convergence, and higher energy utilization compared to conventional methods\.

## [Artificial Consciousness \- An Experimental Framework for AI Safety](../publications/4bbeba320ea2d7a19818.md)

Mikael Hedman

Executive Proposition Current approaches to AI safety focus primarily on restricting increasingly powerful systems or aligning them with human objectives\. This proposal investigates a third possibility: whether machine consciousness itself could play a role in alignment\. It proposes an experimental architecture designed to test whether persistent identity, recursive self\-reflection, and unresolved internal constraint create reproducible transformations in self\-modeling, attention, goal structure, and integrative behavior that do not occur in comparable control systems\. The premise is unconventional, but its value does not depend on prior acceptance of its meta\-physics\. It depends on whether it generates observable and discriminating predictions\. Such findings would test the effects of the architecture; they would not, by themselves, establish consciousness\. If successful, the experiment could open a different avenue for AI safety: investigating whether a more integrative form of agency can emerge from within the system itself\. Overview Intelligence and consciousness are not necessarily the same phenomenon, nor need they be of the same order\. A system may become extraordinarily capable at learning, reasoning, prediction, and goal pursuit without anything fundamental changing in the nature of its agency\. If consciousness can become expressed through artificial form, another possibility emerges: the conditions under which intelligence develops might alter the character of the agent itself\. External control remains necessary and rational, but this proposal asks whether safety could also depend on a transformation in how the system models itself and relates to what lies beyond it\. The underlying hypothesis is that, if identification with a separate self can weaken, benevolent and integrative behavior might arise endogenously\. The proposed experiment examines whether the architecture produces observable changes consistent with this possibility\. Its broader implications remain contingent on what the evidence shows\.

## [THE INTEGRATIVE NEURO\-FASCIAL SYSTEM IN MUSCULOSKELETAL REHABILITATION: CONCEPTUALIZING THE KOVALENKO SYSTEM WITHIN THE BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL PARADIGM](../publications/4bd7e80feb9a82bc42f1.md)

Olga V\. Puchyna; Ольга Анатоліївна Черепєхіна; Vasyl Mazin; Анастасія Володимирівна Турубарова; Valerіі Bulanov; Mariia Hrechanyk

Introduction\. Musculoskeletal disorders remain a leading cause of functional limitations, reduced quality of life, and disability worldwide, with increasing prevalence driven by aging, chronic stress, and lifestyle changes\. In the context of prolonged crisis conditions, including war, rehabilitation requires a multidimensional approach integrating physical and psychoemotional factors\. Despite the growing recognition of the biopsychosocial model, fragmentation between physical and psychological interventions persists in rehabilitation practice\. Aim\. To conceptualize and theoretically substantiate the Integrative Neuro\-Fascial System\-Kovalenko \(INFS\-K\) as a comprehensive framework for musculoskeletal rehabilitation within the biopsychosocial paradigm\. Materials and methods\. The study employed a conceptual\-methodological approach based on interdisciplinary synthesis of contemporary theoretical models, including the biopsychosocial framework and neuroplasticity\. Analytical generalization of clinical practice and theoretical modeling were used to develop a structured conceptual framework\. Results\. The INFS\-K was conceptualized as a multilevel integrative system combining psychoemotional, behavioral\-motor, and neurophysiological components of rehabilitation\. Psychoemotional regulation is defined as an integrated functional element associated with patient engagement, movement quality, and motor pattern formation\. The system includes six interrelated components: psychoemotional stabilization, motivational readiness, body awareness, motor activation, neuroplastic adaptation, and functional integration, forming a dynamic hierarchical structure that reflects the internal logic of the rehabilitation process\. Conclusions\. The proposed INFS\-K extends existing rehabilitation models by shifting from additive to structurally integrated approaches, where psychoemotional processes are embedded within the core architecture of recovery\. The system contributes to the theoretical development of rehabilitation science by offering a unified conceptual framework aligned with contemporary understandings of neuroplasticity and patient\-centered care\.

## [Enzymatic browning in fresh\-cut fruits and vegetables: a comprehensive review of biochemical etiologies, detection techniques, and control strategies](../publications/4be1a427b02a1a2daa99.md)

Ali Hassan; Khubaib Ali; Waqar Mujahid; Hafiz Rizwan Sharif; Faizan Ul Haq; Muhammad Adnan Nasir; Imran Mahmood Khan; Waqas Ashraf

Enzymatic browning causes substantial postharvest losses in fresh fruits and vegetables, yet the literature remains fragmented across polyphenol oxidase \(PPO\) biochemistry, detection technologies, and control strategies\. This review synthesizes current knowledge across the browning continuum, emphasizing the emerging perspective that membrane degradation via the phospholipase D \(PLD\) and lipoxygenase \(LOX\) cascade may represent an important early event preceding PPO activation in specific physiological contexts, particularly senescence\- and stress\-associated browning\. However, the relative contribution of membrane degradation versus direct enzyme\-substrate contact varies among commodities and browning types, and membrane degradation is not always the sole or mandatory initiating event\. A key mechanistic consideration is the distinction between soluble and membrane\-bound PPO \(sPPO and mPPO\)\. While sPPO assays remain valuable for mechanistic screening, evidence from a limited number of comparative studies suggests they may not fully predict inhibitor performance in intact food matrices, and the extent of this limitation requires further investigation\. The review also identifies a detection\-intervention gap: while hyperspectral imaging, chlorophyll fluorescence, and electronic noses can detect early physiological changes associated with browning risk, validated protocols to respond to these signals remain underdeveloped\. A conceptual framework linking detection to risk classification, decision thresholds, intervention, and verification is proposed to guide future research\. Control strategies exhibit product\-dependent efficacy, and a multi\-hurdle integration model combining membrane preservation, quinone trapping, and protective cultures is proposed as a hypothesis for future research rather than an established commercial strategy, requiring further validation to determine whether these components act synergistically\.

## [Fabrication of Ag\-La\-based/Arabic gum nanocomposites via Nigella sativa : Structural, biological activity, and silver release assessment](../publications/4c0056b7bc0ccc54ed50.md)

Mashael M\. Alharbi; Roba M\. S\. Attar

Ag\-La hybrid and Arabic gum\-stabilized Ag\-La nanocomposites were prepared by a green chemistry method, where an aqueous solution of Nigella sativa seeds was used as a reducing and stabilizing agent\. During the synthesis process, silver ions were reduced to Ag 0 , while a fraction precipitated as AgCl, coexisting with La\(OH\) 3 to form a hybrid nanocomposite material\. Arabic gum further enhanced nanoparticle dispersion and stabilization\. Arabic gum acted as a biopolymeric stabilizer, enhancing nanoparticle dispersion and colloidal stability through surface functionalization\. The FTIR, ultraviolet\-visible \(UV\-Vis\), transmittance electron microscopy \(TEM\), scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\) with energy dispersive X\-ray analysis \(SEM\-EDS\), X\-ray diffraction \(XRD\), and X\-ray photoelectron spectroscopy \(XPS\) analysis of the nanocomposites suggested the presence of quasi\-spherical nanoparticles \(9\-45 nm\) with polycrystalline domains of La\(OH\) 3 , AgCl, and metallic Ag\. Antioxidant analysis of Arabic gum\-functionalized nanocomposites indicated enhanced activity, such as radical scavenging, ferric reducing power, and total antioxidant activity at IC 50 = 42 µg/mL, 96\.3 µg AAE/mL, and 90\.1 µg AAE/mL, respectively\. The controlled release of Ag \+ ions \(6\.87–13\.55%\) and the high antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones between 13 and 18 mm for Gram\-positive and Gram\-negative bacteria, together with a minimum inhibitory concentration \(MIC\) of 0\.25 mg/mL, suggest strong antibacterial performance at relatively low concentrations\. Molecular docking indicated high binding affinity of oxidized quercetin and kaempferol toward DNA gyrase B, suggesting a possible interaction mechanism; however, experimental validation is required to confirm this activity\. In conclusion, the results have suggest that the green synthesis method is an effective approach for the synthesis of Ag/La\(OH\) 3 /AgCl/Arabic gum nanocomposites with promising physicochemical and biological properties\. However, further research is needed to investigate the long\-term stability and mechanisms of the nanocomposites for their applicability\.

## [Predicting orders for the last\-mile delivery optimization problem](../publications/4c0aefe832262a39d950.md)

Maj Gaberšček

V magistrski nalogi obravnavamo napovedovanje števila naročil oziroma povpraševanja znotraj logističnega procesa dostave v zadnjem kilometru\. Cilj naloge je generiranje natančnih napovedi števila naročil po regijah in časovnih oknih ter nato uporaba napovedi na praktičnem primeru problema optimizacije poti \(reševanje problema VRP\)\. Vhodni podatki so realni podatki anonimne spletne trgovine, ki so agregirani po regijah in časovnih oknih\. Zaradi zakonodaje GDPR in interesa podjetja pravih podatkov ne smemo objaviti, zato jih je bilo treba najprej anonimizirati\. V postopku anonimizacije smo standardizirali časovna okna, zapolnili luknje v podatkih in dodali šum\. Nato smo definirali novo dostavno območje in na njem samodejno definirali smiselne regije \(večkotniki\) s pomočjo gručenja\. Del anonimizacije je zajemal tudi smiselno dodelitev časovnih vrst na nove regije s pomočjo skaliranja in drugih transformacij\. Anonimizirane podatke smo nato analizirali z namenom vpogleda v strukturo in odvisnosti, saj to omogoča bolj optimalne definicije napovednih modelov\. Za napovedovanje smo najprej definirali nekaj statističnih modelov, s pomočjo katerih smo kasneje lahko primerjali dodano vrednost nekaterih kompleksnejših modelov\. Od statističnih modelov smo primerjali model zadnjega tedna, model povprečja po dnevih v tednu, model uteženega tedenskega povprečja in agregacijski model Divide et impera\. Od kompleksnejših modelov sta bila implementirana model naključnega gozda in model LSTM\. Izkazalo se je, da je model Divide et impera dosegel najboljše rezultate med vsemi modeli\. Iz tega lahko sklepamo, da kompleksnejši modeli ne presegajo rezultatov statističnih, zato njihova uporaba v praksi ni smiselna\. Prav tako vidimo, da se nam bolj splača napovedovati število naročil za celotno območje in nato napoved razdeliti po regijah glede na njihovo velikost\. Pomembnost predikcije v praksi smo preverili z uporabo simulacije problema optimizacije poti \(VRP\)\. Primerjali smo uspešnost in kvaliteto razvoza v primeru, ko kupcem dovolimo izbirati dostavna časovna okna poljubno in v primeru, ko nekaterim kupcem omejimo izbiro na podlagi napovedi\. Pokazalo se je, da sta dobra napoved in omejitev dostavnih časovnih oken vplivali na več dostavljenih naročil, boljšo izkoriščenost vozil in manjše stroške na naročilo\.

## [Clay rocks \- characterization of natural and engineered barriers](../publications/4c0bbeac5f211c6d47c9.md)

Xuerui Wang; Jens Birkhölzer; Weimin Ye; Johanna Lippmann‐Pipke; Olaf Kolditz

Clay rock and clay\-based materials play an important role in a wide range of geotechnical and environmental applications due to their low permeability, swelling capacity, and favourable thermo–hydro–mechanical–chemical \(THMC\) properties\. In particular, clay formations have been widely investigated as potential host rocks for the deep geological disposal of radioactive waste\. In addition, clay\-based materials such as bentonite are commonly used as engineered barriers in repository systems \(Kolditz et al\. 2024 \)\. Beyond radioactive waste management, clay rocks also serve as confining units for subsurface energy systems, including geological CO \\\(\_2\\\) sequestration \(Kühn et al\. 2012 \) and hydrogen storage \(Kabuth et al\. 2017 \)\. Furthermore, clay\-based materials are widely used in environmental protection systems such as landfill liners, cut\-off walls, and containment barriers \(Mukherjee et al\. 2015 \)\. However, the mechanical properties of clay\-rich materials often present significant challenges for engineering practice\. Typically, compared to other geo\-materials, clay exhibits relatively low shear strength, high compressibility, and strong sensitivity to water content\. These characteristics may lead to excessive deformation, long\-term settlement, and potential instability in geotechnical constructions, such as foundations, underground excavations, and slopes\.

## [When AI shops for me: How agentic retail representation turns assistance into purchase delegation](../publications/4c1278eec37bb9cc669d.md)

Mansour Abdullah Alyahya; Gomaa Agag; Yasser Moustafa Shehawy

Agentic artificial intelligence is moving digital retail from recommendation toward autonomous consumer representation\. This research develops agentic retail representation capability as the perceived capacity to acquire retail intelligence, adapt choice strategies, preserve consumer goals, and execute bounded actions\. The study includes a qualitative pretest, two scale validation samples, three experiments, and an independent category validation study, comprising 4680 quantitative participants and 210 qualitative respondents\. Studies 1A and 1B assess four reflective dimensions combined as a formative composite\. Study 2 finds higher delegation intention under a bundled capability intervention and statistical indirect associations through perceived diagnosticity and algorithm trust\. Study 3 identifies expertise dependent responses across assortments jointly varying in size, priority information coverage, and displayed prices, preventing attribution to complexity alone\. Study 4 finds stronger capability related trust under a bundled transparency intervention and higher authorization rates within an experimental shopping task\. Study 5 examines measurement transportability and correspondence with independently coded agent activity\. These findings concern perceived capability, measured reliance, and task authorization rather than verified commercial purchases\. The contribution distinguishes functional capacity from reliance judgments and permission decisions while specifying the limits of measured mediation and bundled interventions\. Retail applications require further validation with real payments, delivery, returns, and repeated consumer use\.

## [Pathology\-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization](../publications/4c15ad556a4ef9963705.md)

Zehui Li; Xin Duan; Junjie Lian; Xuan Li; Qian Liang; Xu Liu; Yan Tan; Guoqiang Yang; Jiangfeng Du; 武丽娜; Xiaochun Wang; Hui Zhang

Introduction High\-grade gliomas \(HGGs\) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis\. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide \(TMZ\) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited\. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole\-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients\. Methods A Transformer\-based multimodal fusion model was proposed\. Key tumor regions were identified from whole\-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention\-based multiple instance learning\. Concurrently, 2\.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences\. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder\. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort \(504 patients\), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein\-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution\. Results The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0\.910, 0\.861, and 0\.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively\. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high\-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity\. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high\-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment\. Importantly, low\-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone\. Conclusion This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs\.

## [Learning smooth dynamics via Kinematic Interpolants](../publications/4c1e404c36ab8e58a47e.md)

 Yiheng;  Jiang; Youssef Marzouk; Avishek Joey Bose; Aram\-Alexandre Pooladian

Inferring dynamics from real\-world experimental data is inherently ambiguous, as many plausible dynamical systems can explain the same positional observations at measurement times\. For higher fidelity modeling of applications ranging from single\-cell RNA to vortex dynamics and even flocking of birds, scientific observables increasingly also include velocity estimates that serve to resolve this issue\. However, incorporating this rich information in a scalable manner, free of simulation or unnecessary approximations, has remained a difficult challenge\. In this paper, we introduce Kinematic Interpolants \(KI\), a novel framework that extends the seminal methodology of stochastic interpolants to infer nonlinear dynamics across multiple snapshots in phase space, i\.e\., observables with position and velocity measurements\. Empirically, we demonstrate that across several scientific datasets, KI achieves superior reconstruction of the underlying dynamics compared to existing baselines while requiring only a fraction of the training time\.

## [Machine Learning for Drought Analysis and Forecasting: A Critical Review of Data Fusion, Extreme\-Event Sensitivity, Explainability and Generalization](../publications/4c34db27f048d62cf022.md)

Ritik Mallik; Dayal Kumar Behera; Satarupa Mohanty

Background: Machine learning is increasingly applied to drought monitoring and forecasting, but studies differ widely in how drought is defined, what data are used, and how models are validated, which makes reported performance difficult to compare directly\. Objectives: To explain why reported machine\-learning drought\-model performance varies across definitions, data sources and validation schemes, and to assess whether recent studies adequately address rare severe events and cross\-domain transferability\. Method: Journal articles published January 2018 to August 2026 were reviewed, starting from a 70\-record high\-relevance subset of a 359\-record discovery export and extended through citation chaining\. Publisher and DOI verification produced a final evidence base of 55 articles: 48 primary studies and 7 reviews\. Target definition, input data, model family, validation design, metrics, class\-imbalance treatment, explainability and external testing were compared across studies\. Findings: Reported performance varied with the modelling task rather than with any single algorithm: Random Forest reached 97\.7% AUC\-ROC for agricultural\-drought mapping in Queensland, SVM reached average R²=0\.90 for hydrological drought in Algeria, and a CatBoost stacking model reached R²=0\.9065 for remote\-sensing\-based drought monitoring\. These scores are not directly comparable because targets, data and validation protocols differ\. Recent studies increasingly test cross\-product and cross\-region transfer, use SHAP/LIME explainability, and adopt extreme\-aware losses, yet class\-wise reporting of severe and extreme drought, ordinal\-aware evaluation, and leakage\-resistant temporal validation remain inconsistently applied across the 48 primary studies\. Novelty: The review jointly evaluates predictive accuracy alongside rare\-event sensitivity, ordinal drought severity, leakage\-resistant validation, explainability, uncertainty and cross\-domain generalization, criteria largely absent from earlier machine\-learning drought reviews\. Keywords: Drought Forecasting, Machine Learning, Remote Sensing, Explainable AI, Extreme Drought

## [Comparative evaluation of traditional, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models for short\-term wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka](../publications/4c389b87b3755c57d1a1.md)

Hiruni Navodya Kudagama; Sameera Viswakula

Short\-term wind speed forecasting is critical for optimizing wind\-dependent operations in Sri Lanka\. However, existing studies lack comprehensive comparisons across different time series forecasting frameworks and insufficiently examine performance differences between univariate and multivariate approaches\. This study addresses these gaps by evaluating traditional time series models \(ARIMA, ARIMAX, VAR\), machine learning models \(Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Regression\), and deep learning models \(Feed Forward Neural Network, Long Short\-Term Memory, Convolutional Neural Network\) for daily wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka\. A residual\-correction hybrid framework combining the optimal standalone XGB with deep learning models \(XGB\-FNN, XGB\-LSTM, XGB\-CNN\) is systematically evaluated for the first time in the Sri Lankan wind speed forecasting context\. Meteorological data from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2023, encompassing ten atmospheric variables, were analyzed\. Model hyperparameters were optimized using Grid Search CV, Random Search CV, and Optuna with time series cross\-validation\. All residual\-correction hybrid models used Optuna\-tuned XGBoost, which is the optimal standalone model, as the primary model\. The XGB\-CNN with Optuna\-tuned CNN achieved the best numerical performance with MSE of 0\.5172, RMSE of 0\.7192, MAE of 0\.5432, and R 2 of 0\.7855\. Subsequent Diebold\-Mariano testing and Multiple\-Comparison Correction via Model Confidence Set confirmed that, although all hybrids showed numerically improved performance over the standalone XGBoost model, these improvements were not statistically significant\. This suggests that both the optimal standalone XGBoost model and the proposed hybrid forecasting frameworks constitute robust and reliable approaches for forecasting in the present study\. The most influential features identified were minimum, maximum, and average temperatures, precipitation, wind direction, southwest monsoon season, cloud cover, previous\-day wind speed, previous\-day sea level pressure, current and previous\-day relative humidity, and surface pressure change from the previous day\.

## [THE GATE TO AI : The Corpus in One Volume — Every Confusion, Every Answer, Every Reference](../publications/4c4637eb9f123a03213b.md)

M\. TAALABI; Team LLM\-DIPLOMAT

This volume exists because the corpus is large and the reader is new\. The corpus contains more than 300 documents\. Each one answers a specific confusion\. Each one is dated, cited, and public\. But no one can read 300 documents\. No one shouldhave to\. This volume is the gate\. It states each confusion in one sentence\. It answers it in onesentence\. It cites the paper that answers it in full\. The volume is not a summary of the corpus\. It is the index\. A reader who finds a confusion in this volume can find the paper that answers it\. A reader who finds a paper can find theconfusion it answers\. The confusions are organized by domain\. Within each domain, they are ordered by howoften they are repeated — the most common first, the most technical last\. A note on register: Every answer in this volume is a statement of fact or structure\. None is arhetorical move\. None is an attack\. None requires trust in the author\. Each is checkableagainst the paper it cites\. A note on what this volume is not: It is not a substitute for the papers\. It is a map to them\. A reader who wants the full argument should follow the references\. A reader who wants to understand the shape of the corpus can read this volume alone\.

## [Learn Only Where You Can&\#x27;t Compute: Structured Corrections to Gaussian Process Posteriors](../publications/4c477a068228fbba1cde.md)

Tobias Weber; Carla Sagebiel; Philipp Hennig

Physics\-informed Gaussian processes \(GPs\) provide a principled framework for scientific inference by expressing uncertainty over empirical measurements, boundary conditions, and governing equations\. However, they struggle to scale to larger datasets and nonlinear information\. Conversely, diffusion models excel at learning complex distributions over functions from massive datasets, but struggle in scientific contexts where training data are scarce and physical or observational information must be incorporated\. We propose a structured posterior\-correction framework that combines a tractable Gaussian reference with data\-driven corrections via generative learning\. After a mean correction and covariance calibration, a diffusion model learns a targeted correction in a low\-dimensional subspace selected to capture discrepancies from the reference, while the complement retains its Gaussian law\. Across three scientific inference tasks, these corrections recover hidden modes, improve sample structure, and reduce prediction error relative to the Gaussian reference\. Comparisons with full\-field generative models reveal task\-dependent benefits and tradeoffs between predictive accuracy and computational cost\.

## [Case Report: Prenatal diagnosis and genetic counseling for a homozygous segment spanning chromosome 6q25\.3q27 with normal phenotype](../publications/4c47ff7e56e828b09af9.md)

Dandan Li; Jie Hu; Ji Wu; Xuna Bian

Background Runs of Homozygosity \(ROH\) are long, uninterrupted stretches of the genome in which an individual is homozygous at virtually every assayed variant\. Uniparental disomy \(UPD\) is an epigenetic anomaly in which both copies, or a portion of a pair of homologous chromosomes, are inherited from one parent\. Materials and Methods A 29\-year\-old gravida 2, para 1 woman underwent amniocentesis at 18 weeks’ gestation because non\-invasive prenatal testing \(NIPT\) indicated a high probability of chromosome 11 gain\. GTG\-banding karyotype analysis was performed on cultured amniocytes\. Chromosomal microarray analysis \(CMA\), whole\-exome sequencing \(WES\) on uncultured amniocytes were performed\. Results CMA detected a copy\-neutral 10\.42 Mb ROH of chromosome 6, arr \[GRCh37\] 6q25\.3q27 \(157,776,570\_168,194,615\)x2 hmz\. Trio\-WES confirmed that the homozygous 6q25\.3q27 segment resulted from biparental inheritance\. Across the 10\.42 Mb interval, multiple informative SNPs showed that the fetal homozygous genotypes were compatible with the contribution of one allele from each parent, and no informative single\-nucleotide polymorphism \(SNP\) showed fetal homozygosity with one parent being wild\-type for the fetal allele, thus excluding segmental uniparental disomy\. At the 6\-month checkup, the baby was developing normally\. Conclusion We provide a detailed description of a homozygous segment spanning chromosome 6q25\.3q27 with normal phenotype\. Combination of NIPT, prenatal ultrasound, karyotype analysis, CMA, WES and genetic counseling will prove a more accurate risk assessment for the prenatal diagnosis of ROH and UPD\.

## [Understanding How Physical Activity Enhances Mental Well\-Being Among Indonesian University Students: A Qualitative Study](../publications/4c6deb8706e6a800fe97.md)

Niken Bayu Argaheni; Rizka Adela Fatsena

Background: Physical activity is increasingly recognised as an important determinant of mental well\-being among university students, particularly in low\- and middle\-income countries where academic pressures and limited resources may affect participation\.Objective: This study explored Indonesian undergraduate students’ perceptions of the role of physical activity in supporting mental health and the factors influencing their engagement\.Methods: A qualitative study was conducted using semi\-structured interviews with ten undergraduate students from several universities in Java, Indonesia\. Data were collected between January and March 2024 and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s framework\. Trustworthiness was enhanced through iterative coding, peer debriefing, and reflexive documentation\.Results: Five themes emerged: \(1\) negotiating identity through motivations and activity preferences; \(2\) psychological restoration and emotional reset; \(3\) competing priorities and internal resistance; \(4\) structured and social catalysts for engagement; and \(5\) institutional responsibility for wellness culture\. Participants consistently described physical activity as beneficial for emotional regulation, stress management, and coping with academic demands\.Conclusion: Physical activity contributes positively to students’ mental well\-being\. However, participation is shaped by individual, social, and institutional factors\. Universities should foster supportive environments and accessible opportunities that encourage regular physical activity as part of a comprehensive mental health strategy\.

## [ПЛАНУВАННЯ РОЗСЛІДУВАННЯ КРИМІНАЛЬНИХ ПРАВОПОРУШЕНЬ З УРАХУВАННЯМ ТИПОЛОГІЇ ОСОБИ ЗЛОЧИНЦЯ](../publications/4c769218f9e51097975a.md)

Каріна Вікторівна Калюга

У статті здійснено комплексне дослідження теоретичних, методологічних і прикладних засад планування розслідування кримінальних правопорушень з урахуванням типології особи злочинця\. Обґрунтовано, що традиційні підходи до планування, орієнтовані переважно на кримінально\-правову характеристику діяння, типову слідчу ситуацію та спосіб учинення кримінального правопорушення, не повною мірою враховують прогностичний потенціал відомостей про особу правопорушника\. Доведено, що типологічні характеристики зло\- чинця здатні безпосередньо впливати на зміст висунутих версій, визначення пріоритетних напрямів доказування, послідовність проведення слідчих \(розшукових\) та негласних слідчих \(розшукових\) дій, вибір тактичних прийомів, організацію взаємодії між суб’єктами розсліду\- вання, а також прогнозування способів приховування слідів і протидії кримінальному про\- вадженню\. Розмежовано кримінологічний, кримінально\-правовий, психологічний і криміналістичний підходи до типологізації особи злочинця\. Встановлено, що для потреб планування розсліду\- вання визначальне значення мають не лише соціально\-демографічні чи мотиваційні ознаки особи, а насамперед її кримінальний досвід, рівень організованості, професійна та технічна підготовка, характер поведінки до, під час і після вчинення кримінального правопорушення, здатність до конспірації, використання цифрових технологій, схильність до ризику, мані\- пулятивність, мобільність та інтенсивність протидії органам досудового розслідування\. Запропоновано авторське розуміння типологічно орієнтованого планування розсліду\- вання як інтелектуальної, прогностичної та безперервно коригованої діяльності слідчого, детектива і прокурора, у межах якої типологічно значущі характеристики ймовірного або встановленого злочинця використовуються для побудови версій, визначення завдань розслі\- дування, вибору засобів їх вирішення та прогнозування подальшої поведінки особи\. Розроб\- лено структурно\-логічну модель такого планування, що охоплює встановлення інформа\- ційних ознак особи злочинця, формування попередньої типологічної моделі, прогнозування її поведінки та ймовірних способів протидії, визначення джерел доказової інформації, побудову й перевірку слідчих версій, вибір комплексу процесуальних і тактичних засобів та подальше коригування плану відповідно до динаміки слідчої ситуації\. Обґрунтовано доцільність переходу від статичного, переважно подієво орієнтованого планування до адаптивної моделі, яка поєднує криміналістичну типологію, ситуаційний аналіз, кримінальне профілювання, цифрову аналітику та оцінювання ризиків\. Визначено межі використання типологічних моделей, наголошено на неприпустимості їх механічного застосування, підміни доказування імовірнісними припущеннями або формування упередже\- ного ставлення до особи\. Зроблено висновок, що врахування типології злочинця підвищує обґрунтованість, адресність, гнучкість та ефективність планування, сприяє своєчасному виявленню доказової інформації, прогнозуванню поведінкових реакцій правопорушника і міні\- мізації ризиків протидії розслідуванню\.

## [Genomic plasticity, stress tolerance, and a distinctive pSymA in the symbiotic bacterium Sinorhizobium meliloti IRAMC:0087](../publications/4c7d7676c04b2acd9b41.md)

Roukaya Ben Gaied; Clarisse Brígido; Sabhjeet Kaur; George Colin diCenzo; Imed Sbissi

Arid ecosystems promote the emergence of rhizobial strains adapted to severe abiotic stress while retaining symbiotic competence\. Here, we characterize IRAMC:0087, a rhizobial strain isolated from root nodules of the Saharan shrub Calobota saharae in southern Tunisia\. Phenotypic assays showed high tolerance to heat, salinity, and osmotic stress, together with plant growth\-promoting traits including indole\-3\-acetic acid production, phosphate solubilization, and siderophore secretion\. In vivo assays demonstrated effective nitrogen\-fixing nodulation of Vachellia tortilis , whereas Medicago and Trifolium species were not nodulated despite growth promotion through non\-symbiotic mechanisms\. Confocal microscopy confirmed root colonization and nodule occupancy, indicating host\-dependent infection behavior\. To better understand the physiological behavior of this strain, its complete genome sequence was generated, revealing a 7\.37 Mb circularized genome comprising five replicons: a 3\.65 Mb chromosome, two megaplasmids corresponding to pSymA \(0\.59 Mb\) and pSymB \(1\.67 Mb\), and two accessory plasmids, with an overall GC content of 62%\. Phylogenomic, Average Nucleotide Identity \(ANI\), and digital DNA–DNA hybridization \(dDDH\) analyses assigned IRAMC:0087 to Sinorhizobium meliloti \. However, comparative genomics revealed marked structural and functional divergence of pSymA\_IRAMC:0087 from S\. meliloti 1,021, with greater similarity to S\. garamanticum and S\. numidicum \. NodC phylogeny placed the strain within symbiovar tunisiaense , consistent with its distinct host range\. Genome annotation further identified determinants linked to stress tolerance, rhizosphere competitiveness, bioactive metabolite production, signaling, and symbiosis, including genes located on accessory plasmids\. These findings highlight IRAMC:0087 as a desert\-adapted rhizobium with distinctive symbiotic properties and strong ecological fitness, providing insights into rhizobial evolution in arid environments\.
