## [Rarity of Singletons Matters &amp; Supplementary Materials](../publications/4c8dad4d9fb2d8aff50e.md)

Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan; Kamal Premaratne; Dilip Sarkar

Estimating missing\-mass and unseen\-species counts from finite samples relies heavily on rare\-event occupancy statistics, particularly singletons\. In small\-sample regimes, these statistics can be highly variable, making classical estimators sensitive to sampling fluctuations and potentially unreliable\. We propose a fragility\-aware \(FA\) framework that explicitly quantifies this sensitivity and adaptively regularizes conventional missing\-mass and unseen\-species estimators\. Using singleton\-based fragility measures derived from probability mass and occupancy counts, we formulate an entropy\-\-Kullback\-\-Leibler \(KL\) optimization that adjusts the reliance on base estimates according to their fragility\. The resulting objectives are strictly concave, admit unique closed\-form solutions, and require no Poissonization or asymptotic approximations\. The framework provides a lightweight correction to classical estimators, including Good\-\-Turing and Good\-\-Toulmin, while reducing reliance on potentially unstable rare\-event statistics\. Across 360 experimental configurations spanning synthetic distributions and real\-world language corpora, our method remains competitive in stable regimes while improving estimation accuracy and stability in fragmented, long\-tailed, and small\-sample settings\. The findings demonstrate that accounting for the fragility of rare observations can improve the reliability of inference about unobserved species and their associated probability mass\.

## [Health\-related factors among seafarers based on the health ecology model: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/4c8f0a50cf4abb8e7a52.md)

Dongdong Wu; Shilian Chen; Zheng Huaiyu; Xinwei Yu; Boer Yan

Objective To explore the health status and its influencing factors among seafarers based on the Health Ecological Model, and to identify priority areas for health management\. Methods A convenience sampling approach was used to administer a questionnaire survey to 106 seafarers from March to June 2026\. The questionnaire was developed based on the Health Ecological Model and covers general information, health status, health\-influencing factors, and health management needs\. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed using SPSS 26\.0\. Results The total health score was 29\.65 ± 3\.62 \(theoretical range: 2–32\)\. Policy environment \( β = 0\.602, p &lt; 0\.001\) and behavioral characteristics \( β = 0\.260, p = 0\.015\) were independent influencing factors of the total health score, with an adjusted R2 of 0\.574\. Further analysis revealed that the policy environment had the greatest impact on physical health \( β = 0\.526, p &lt; 0\.001\), while the interpersonal network was selectively associated with mental health \( β = 0\.207, p = 0\.030\)\. The top three health management needs were improving onboard dietary structure \(87\.7%\), strengthening occupational health training \(35\.9%\), and upgrading onboard medical facilities \(31\.1%\)\. Conclusion The overall health status of seafarers was at a relatively good level, with policy environment and behavioral characteristics being the main influencing factors\. Health management should prioritize improving health security policies and onboard dietary structure, while strengthening occupational health training\.

## [A Review of Human\-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities](../publications/4c9dd48a3ec458b63dc7.md)

Sena Assaf; Mohamed Assaf; Alaa Abu Nokta; Ahmed Bouferguène; Editor\-in\-Chief Mohamed Al\-Hussein

Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory\-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on\-site\. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long\-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human\-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well\-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5\.0 paradigm\. Human\-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well\-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems\. Despite growing interest in human\-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology\-driven\. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human\-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems\. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human\-centric perspective, i\.e\., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas\. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well\-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities\. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human\-centric construction manufacturing\. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human\-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems\.

## [Uitbraakbeheer optimaliseren met fylogenetica, ensemblemethoden en taalmodellen](../publications/4ca918980fbca57cb4da.md)

Jonathan Thibaut

During a surge of infections, testing and tracing centers serve two goals: mitigating the spread of the pathogen and gathering individual data for epidemiological surveillance\. However, previous outbreaks have shown that such public health strategies do not always scale: as cases rise, some infections remain undetected, and reconstructing transmission chains becomes increasingly challenging for contact tracers\. In this thesis, we sought to address these limitations through three retrospective studies analyzing individual\-level data collected from the student population in Leuven during the COVID\-19 pandemic, drawn from contact tracing, diagnostics, and self\-reports\. In the first two studies, we showed that gradient\-boosting and a long short\-term memory network yield promising results in diagnostic prediction\. First, we developed a configurable pre\-test triage relying on predictive diagnosis; our simulations suggest that its implementation could reduce testing requirements and the effective reproduction number\. Then, we integrated the long short\-term memory network into a conversational framework, and showed that retrieval\-augmented generation techniques could help refine the risk of infection by asking relevant, personalized questions\. In a third study, we developed a methodology to assess the precision of contact tracing networks in identifying transmission events; our analyses suggest that genomically consistent case\-contact pairs lead to better estimation of serial intervals\. In conclusion, phylogenetics and machine learning offer strong potential for improving the test\-trace\-isolate strategy\. Provided that genomic data and diagnostic predictive models can be deployed quickly, they could help control and monitor outbreaks more effectively and support evidence\-based public health policy\.

## [Is there “Secret Sauce” in large language model development?](../publications/4cb9c754298a41f30288.md)

Matthias Mertens; Natalia Fischl\-Lanzoni; Neil Thompson

Abstract Do leading LLM developers possess a proprietary “secret sauce,” or is LLM performance driven by scaling up compute? Using training and benchmark data for 809 models released between 2022 and 2025, we estimate scaling\-law regressions with release date and developer fixed effects\. We find clear evidence of developer\-specific efficiency advantages, but their importance depends on where models lie in the performance distribution\. At the frontier, 80–90% of performance differences are explained by higher training compute, implying that scale—not proprietary technology—drives frontier advances\. Away from the frontier, however, proprietary techniques and shared algorithmic progress substantially reduce the compute required to reach fixed capability thresholds\. Some companies can systematically produce smaller models more efficiently\. Strikingly, we also find substantial variation of model residual efficiency within companies; a firm can train two models with more than 40x compute efficiency difference\. We also discuss the implications for AI leadership and capability diffusion\.

## [Cooperative chasing and guidance for UAV\-based animal rescue algorithms](../publications/4cbe49bf264f3c5e12ad.md)

M\. Kötter; R\. Brachmanski; M\. Uijt de Haag

Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles \(UAVs\), or drones, bring many opportunities to replace humans in 3D missions: missions which are dull, dirty or dangerous\. One example is guiding animals out of dangerous situations, for example close to a forest fire or an accident where toxic chemicals leak into the environment\. Since animals do not understand that the drones are intended to help them, they will seek to evade them and this can be used to herd them to safety\. Automated shepherding has, to our knowledge, not yet reached the maturity level required to perform such an animal rescue mission\. The goal of this paper is to review, select and adapt algorithms in pursuit of this purpose\. We examined swarm UAV deployment covering: optimal distribution around the target animal, maintaining it when performing the required task and how to actively evade obstacles en route\. This led to the conclusion, that of the presented algorithms, the Inverse Cumulative Density Function \(ICDF\) is the most suitable for the optimal dispersion of UAVs, while A\*, Greedy Best First Search \(GBFS\) and the potential field algorithm are the most appropriate algorithms to determine suitable route trajectories during such guidance\.

## [Automated differentiation for parkinsonism using clinical structural MRI: A multicenter study](../publications/4cbfa5397f7c92b8fe01.md)

周立彻; Chengzhe Wang; Xue Zhu; Dongling Zhang; Jinfeng Wu; Sijia Huang; Haiying Lyu; Chuanying Xu; Zihao Lin; Xiaoyu Cheng; Jin‐Ru Zhang; 毛成洁; Chun‐Feng Liu; Yong Lü; Guiyun Cui; Tao Wu; Kezhong Zhang; Ailian Du; Jun Liu; Jie Wang

Multimodal research\-grade magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) scans show potential for differentiating Parkinson’s disease \(PD\) from multiple system atrophy \(MSA\), but clinical translation is limited by cost, acquisition time, and processing burden\. Here, we developed a T1\-weighted structural MRI\-based machine learning model to differentiate Parkinsonism and generalized it to routine anisotropic 2D clinical MRI\. Using a multicenter cohort of 969 participants, we employed a hierarchical discovery–verification–translation framework\. While a multimodal benchmark model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\) of 0\.98, our streamlined unimodal T1\-Top20 model achieved an AUROC of 0\.93 for multiclass discrimination \(healthy controls, PD, MSA\)\. For PD vs MSA, the frozen T1\-Top20 model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0\.88 in the external research\-grade cohort \( n = 227\) and identified 19 of 25 who phenoconverted from idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder \(iRBD\) to PD\. Importantly, the generalized model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0\.84 in the clinical\-MRI cohort \(2D T1, n = 303\), supporting its potential for clinical translation\.

## [Addition of Chinese medicinal herbal residues promotes the removal of antibiotic resistance genes during pig manure composting](../publications/4cc424108b8db0ee7580.md)

Bo Wang; Lanlan Tian; Yibo Wang; Zexing Tian; Yanrong Yang

Aerobic composting is an effective methods for reducing antibiotic resistance genes \(ARGs\) and mobile genetic elements \(MGEs\) present in livestock and poultry manure\. Chinese medicinal herbal residues \(CMHRs\) are rich in nutrients and antibacterial components, which may inhibit the spread of ARGs and MGEs\. This study investigated the effects of adding different proportions of CMHRs added \(0%, 10%, 30%, and 50% of the initial compost mixture mass\) on ARGs and MGEs during pig manure composting\. The results showed that CMHRs shortened the time required to reach the high\-temperature stage and increased compost temperature\. At the end of composting, the total nitrogen \(TN\) and available phosphorus \(AP\) levels in the M2 treatment group were significantly higher than those in the control group, reaching 8\.11 g/kg and 333\.73 mg/kg, respectively\. High\-throughput qPCR analysis showed that the total removal rates of ARGs after composting were 27\.10%, 36\.04%, 65\.55%, and 40\.55%, respectively; the corresponding removal rates of MGEs were 19\.25%, 56\.20%, 65\.32%, and 14\.03%, respectively; The 30% treatment was the most effective, with removal rates of aminoglycosides, β\-lactam, multidrug resistance, sulfonamides, and tetracycline resistance genes of 78\.09%, 81\.11%, 74\.09%, 54\.27%, and 61\.24%, respectively\. Firmicutes, Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria, and Bacteroidetes were the dominant phyla in the compost\. Clostridium\-sensu\-stricto1 , Corynebacterium , Terrisporobacter , Anaerococcus , and Romboutsia were potential major hosts of ARGs and MGEs\. During composting, changes in temperature and MGEs directly and significantly affected ARGs, while total organic carbon \(TOM\) and TN indirectly affected ARGs by regulating microbial communities\. In conclusion, the addition of 30% CMHRs effectively reduces ARGs and MGEs in pig manure compost\. These findings provide a basis for the use of CMHRs to reduce the spread of ARGs during pig manure composting\.

## [Musical structure, micromotion, and adaptive gesture in instrumental performance: a critical cross\-study synthesis](../publications/4cc62cdb31f4c72fce10.md)

Nádia Moura

This article presents an integrative synthesis of seven studies conducted within a research program on expert saxophone performance: five performer\-centered observational, kinematic, and interview studies, complemented by two perceptual experiments\. The studies are compared according to musical and task conditions, movement descriptors and scales, and evidential perspective\. Rhythm and pitch were most consistently associated with movement\. Faster or rhythmically denser passages were linked to shorter or more frequent actions, while rhythmic density increased knee\-cycle frequency as amplitude decreased\. Pitch contour accompanied recurrent flexion–extension patterns, and knee trajectories showed predictive temporal precedence relative to a modeled pitch\-expectation profile\. Under movement restriction, projected center\-of\-mass range, velocity, distance, and area decreased, whereas knee phase changes increased and specific postural\-frequency measures remained comparatively stable\. Three non\-exclusive interpretations of persistent micromotion are considered: postural regulation, sensorimotor entrainment and prediction, and motor learning\. On this basis, the paper proposes an adaptive, multidimensional model in which musical structure and task constraints selectively reorganize movement across dimensions and scales, while expressive, technical, postural, and communicative functions remain overlapping and context\-dependent\. The model provides an empirically grounded framework for causal experiments and learning interventions on the functions of performative movement\.

## [Synergistic Catalysis in Defect‐Engineered Zn‐MOF‐74‐Based Porous Liquids for Enhanced CO 2 Cycloaddition Under Mild Conditions](../publications/4ccbd0903c2638e1f648.md)

Wenyu Ge; Cun Chen; Shuai Zheng; Dagang Qi; Yuming Tu; Zhiyong Zhou; Chencan Du; Zhongqi Ren

ABSTRACT Porous liquids \(PLs\), which combine permanent porosity with fluidity, represent an emerging class of materials with broad application prospects\. The incorporation of catalytic sites into both the porous framework and the liquid medium further enables their use in catalysis\. Here, we report a type III porous liquid \(PL‐Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF\) fabricated from a functional imidazolium‐based ionic liquid \(IL1\) and defective Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF, which exhibits enhanced CO 2 capture capacity and superior performance in the cycloaddition of CO 2 to epoxides compared to IL1 alone\. Under mild conditions \(50°C, 1 bar\), the designed porous liquid boosts the conversion of styrene oxide \(SO\) by up to 22\.6% and that of propylene oxide \(PO\) by 29\.9%\. Density Functional Theory \(DFT\) calculations reveal that the remarkable catalytic enhancement stems from the synergistic interplay between IL1 and the defective metal sites in Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF, which facilitates CO 2 activation and stabilizes key reaction intermediates\. This work provides both experimental and theoretical insights into the catalytic mechanism of porous liquids, paving the way for their rational design in sustainable catalysis\.

## [Human‐Centered Monitoring of Asphalt Emissions: Linking Exposure, Climate, and Health](../publications/4cd00a7c901f6f0d62ea.md)

Suliman Rashid; Hessam Yazdani; Jessica L\. Verpeut; Shiva Pooladvand; Vajiheh Akbarzadeh; Ali Shamshiripour; Elham H\. Fini

ABSTRACT Urban infrastructure shapes environmental quality not only through its form and function but also through the materials from which it is built\. Asphalt is a prominent example: heat, solar radiation, and aging can amplify emissions from this climate‐responsive, chemically active material\. However, urban air‐quality frameworks continue to treat these emissions as diffuse ambient burdens, overlooking their role as localized, episodic exposure events with potential implications for community health, occupational safety, and functional performance\. This review synthesizes evidence across materials science, atmospheric chemistry, exposure science, toxicology, and human factors to propose a unified, human‐centered monitoring framework that links asphalt emission dynamics to exposure conditions, biological relevance, and functional human‐response endpoints\. We identify three gaps that motivate the framework: \(1\) weak integration between emission chemistry, chemical changes and reactions, and real‐world exposure conditions, \(2\) insufficient monitoring resolution to capture short‐duration, source‐proximate, high‐intensity events, and \(3\) limited coupling of exposure data with repeated human response measurements and functional endpoints such as symptoms, perception, cognition, and behavior\. By organizing these gaps within a single monitoring logic, the framework can guide future efforts to identify who is exposed, under what environmental conditions, and with what potential health or functional relevance\. This structure provides a pathway toward more health‐protective infrastructure design, construction practices, and governance\. This need is particularly relevant in rapidly urbanizing, arid, and hot‐climate regions, where persistent thermal forcing may amplify both material emissions and human exposure\. Although the evidence synthesized in this review focuses primarily on asphalt, the source–exposure–response framework may be transferable to other climate‐sensitive infrastructure materials as part of broader efforts to advance healthier, more adaptive, and more sustainable urban environments\.

PROLEGÔMENOSAbrir esta coletânea em homenagem ao nosso colega, mentor e amigo William &quot;James&quot; Gomes é, para nós, motivo de honra e orgulho\.Celebramos seus oitenta anos de vida, dos quais dois terços foram dedicados à pesquisa, ao ensino, à formação de novos pesquisadores e à construção da Psicologia como ciência e profi ssão\.O &quot;James&quot; que aqui acrescentamos ao seu nome não é mero ornamento\.Trata\-se de uma referência intencional a William James, cuja Psicologia soube articular experiência, pluralismo metodológico e refl exão fi losófi ca sem abdicar do rigor científi co\.Ao fazê\-lo, reconhecemos na trajetória de William Gomes uma afi nidade intelectual com essa tradição: uma Psicologia que integra sem fragmentar, que mede sem empobrecer e que explica sem perder de vista o humano\.Queremos, com esta coletânea, em nosso nome, na qualidade de editores da obra, e em nome de todos os autores colaboradores dos diferentes capítulos, expressar a ele nossa sincera gratidão por sua enorme contribuição e dedicação ao ensino e à pesquisa em Psicologia no seu sentido mais amplo\.William é uma fi gura proeminente na área da Psicologia\.Ao longo de sua magnífi ca carreira dedicou\-se a importantes debates que vão desde problemas teóricos e conceituais até desafi os metodológicos, passando por investigações de natureza fenomenológica\.Há obras que nascem de problemas teóricos; outras, de lacunas empíricas\.Esta nasce, também, de um vínculo que vai além da convivência acadêmica\.É consequência de pensar a Psicologia como ciência viva, inquieta e inacabada\.Escrever este prolegômeno é reconhecer que há trajetórias que não apenas produzem conhecimento, mas produzem pessoas, comunidades intelectuais e modos de estar no mundo científi co\.Ao longo de sua trajetória, aprendemos que rigor não é sinônimo de aridez, assim como sensibilidade não é concessão ao impreciso\.Em seus trabalhos científi cos, afeto e método nunca estiveram em campos opostos\.Pelo contrário, mostraram\-se dimensões complementares de uma Psicologia que se recusa a escolher entre o humano vivido e o humano mensurável\.Talvez por isso tua contribuição atravesse fronteiras disciplinares com naturalidade: da fenomenologia à neurociência, da clínica à psicometria, da história da Psicologia ao debate epistemológico contemporâneo\.Esta coletânea dialoga com uma de suas lições mais signifi cativas: conceitos importam\.Importam porque organizam o olhar, delimitam perguntas e orientam práticas\.Decifrar construtos psicológicos é, em última instância, um exercício ético e científi co de responsabilidade com aquilo que afi rmamos

## [A Duality‐Based Controllability Condition for a Class of Heterogeneous Networked Systems](../publications/4ce7d99aa18ffc0fc2bd.md)

Aleena Thomas; Abhijith Ajayakumar; Raju K\. George

ABSTRACT In this work, controllability of a class of heterogeneous Networked Control Systems \(NCSs\) with Multi‐Input Multi‐Output \(MIMO\), Linear Time Invariant \(LTI\) nodes is investigated\. In general, nodal controllability is not the only factor affecting the controllability of an NCS\. We employ the notion of duality to study network controllability and identify a class of NCSs where nodal controllability is the sole deciding factor of network controllability\. This identification relies on the equality between the dual of the networked system and the network of duals\. We establish that this equality holds for NCSs where all the nodes are actuated and sensed, and the nodal input \(\) and inner‐coupling \(\) matrices coincide at all the nodes \(i\.e\., \)\. These conditions are inherent in many real‐life systems like networks of spring‐mass systems\. An algorithm is designed to check the controllability of networked systems\. Numerical implementations of the same in MATLAB indicate the increased time efficiency and consistency as compared with classical controllability algorithms\.

## [Accuracy Preserving Selective Rare Attack Expert with Deep Cross Residual Learning for Imbalanced Network Intrusion Detection](../publications/4d08e1b291dd204065a8.md)

Mustafa Mahmood Yahya; Sarah Najm Abdulwahid; Yaseen Ahmed Mohammed Alsumaidaee

Severe class imbalance can make multiclass intrusion detectors appear reliable while rare attacks remain poorly recognized\.This study proposes an Accuracy\-Preserving Selective Rare Attack Expert \(AP\-SRAE\) built on a Deep Cross Residual Network \(DCRN\) backbone\.The term accuracy\-preserving is operational and validationtolerance\-bounded: candidate gates may reduce calibrated\-backbone validation accuracy by at most 0\.15 percentage point, but no test\-set guarantee is implied\.On the original 2,280,090\-flow full\-context random benchmark, AP\-SRAE achieves 98\.28% accuracy and raises macro F1 from 61\.85% to 65\.76%; exact paired predictions show 191 incorrectto\-correct and 124 correct\-to\-incorrect transitions, for a net gain of 67 correct decisions\.In an identifier\-reduced rerun, macro F1 rises from 53\.60% to 58\.35% and balanced accuracy from 56\.24% to 62\.33%, with a 0\.09\-percentage\-point accuracy decrease\.On the official UNSW\-NB15 split, five independent seeds yield balanced accuracy of 48\.53% \+/\-0\.55% for AP\-SRAE versus 47\.56% \+/\-0\.52% for the backbone \(paired t\-test p=0\.026\), while accuracy decreases from 72\.96% \+/\-0\.59% to 72\.60% \+/\-0\.77%\.Protocol\-controlled IDS\-MTran and TabTransformer reimplementations obtain higher official\-split headline accuracy, but AP\-SRAE is computationally lighter in the controlled run\.An independent component\-wise ablation further shows that the final gated and weighted expert improves over the calibrated backbone in macro F1 and balanced accuracy while leaving Normal\-class F1 unchanged\.

## [IL\-11 in fibrostenotic Crohn’s disease: historical agonism, the selective\-inhibition hypothesis, and evidence thresholds for translation](../publications/4d0cbf79b4ee69ada1f6.md)

He Chen; Shuang Liang

Effective medical treatment for fibrostenotic Crohn’s disease remains a major unmet clinical need\. This narrative review examines whether high stromal interleukin\-11 \(IL\-11\) identifies a pharmacologically reversible dependency in established fibrostenotic disease or mainly marks advanced remodeling\. Historical trials found schedule\-dependent activity of recombinant human IL\-11, but an active\-comparator trial showed inferior remission induction compared with prednisolone\. In mice, Il11 or Il11ra1 deficiency worsened epithelial apoptosis and acute dextran sulfate sodium \(DSS\) colitis\. By contrast, inducible Il11 deletion during repeated DSS injury reduced collagen deposition and hydroxyproline with broadly similar inflammatory trajectories\. These contrasting findings support context\-dependent effects across acute injury and chronic remodeling\. Human tissue, serum and treatment\-response studies associate IL\-11 with fibrostenosis and stromal activation, but do not establish that an IL\-11\-high lesion responds to selective inhibition\. Differences in fibroblast state, tissue compartment and treatment timing could therefore influence both efficacy and harm\. Early LASN01 studies outside inflammatory bowel disease support systemic target engagement and preliminary tolerability; intestinal efficacy remains untested\. The decisive next test is selective inhibition after a structural lesion is documented, with verified intestinal exposure and separate structural, inflammatory and repair outcomes\. This would distinguish reduced collagen accumulation during disease development from reversal of an established Crohn’s stricture\.

## [An AI\- and IoT\-Enabled Smart Waste Management Framework for Real\-Time Waste Classification and Collection Optimization](../publications/4d12aa1368d93498a61f.md)

Anup Shekhar Chamoli; Gurpreet Kaur; Rachit Rastogi; Kawal Preet Kaur Arora; Deepak Kumar

Abstract The amount and variety of municipal solid trash have expanded due to rapid urbanization and shifting consumption habits, making it challenging for traditional systems to collect and segregate waste in a timely manner\. When other containers are getting close to overflowing before the next scheduled visit, fixed collection schedules may cause needless journeys to partially filled bins\. In this paper, a framework that combines image\- based trash classification, real\-time smart\-bin monitoring, overflow\-risk prediction, priority scoring, and dynamic collection\-route optimization with AI and IoT capabilities is proposed\. While IoT sensors offer operational data like fill level and optional temperature or weight, a deep\-learning classifier is utilized to detect trash categories from photos\. To calculate overflow risk, machine\-learning models use both recent and past sensor readings\.The decision engine then assigns priorities to a route\-optimization module based on the urgency of the bins\. As complementing computer\-vision benchmarks, TrashNet and TACO are suggested, with the former offering photos for controlled classification and the latter offering litter in contextual settings \[5\], \[6\]\. Results presented in the literature are just used as benchmarks; the suggested system is not claimed to have any artificial experimental precision\. For assessing categorization quality, prediction performance, route efficiency, service reliability, and deployment cost, the framework offers a repeatable experimental design\. In order to transition waste management from a fixed, reactive process to a predictive and adaptive system, the study offers an end\-to\-end design\.

## [PEDAGOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS&\#x27; ACADEMIC WRITING COMPETENCE THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE](../publications/4d20a80188ce8767f94b.md)

Mokhlaroyim Khamdamova Oybek qizi

This paper examines the pedagogical foundations for integrating artificial intelligence into the development of students&\#x27; academic writing competence\. It adopts a conceptual approach informed by writing pedagogy, self\-regulated learning, and human\-centred principles of AI use in education\. Academic writing competence is understood as the ability to construct coherent arguments, evaluate and integrate evidence, follow disciplinary conventions, and revise texts independently\. The paper proposes an instructional framework combining explicit teaching, guided AI interaction, critical feedback evaluation, and reflective revision\.

## [PUBLIC PERCEPTION AND TRUST IN AI FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND INFLUENCER AUTHENTICITY IN INFLUENCER MARKETING](../publications/4d24bd9419527e5afa18.md)

Ms\.B\.Akshaya; Dr\.Sambamurthy Padmavathi

The rapid growth of influencer marketing has created diverse opportunities for the brands to interact with the consumers\. At the same time, concerns regarding manipulated follower counts, artificial engagement and questionable influencer authenticity have become increasingly relevant\. Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is used as a technological mechanism for finding skeptical patterns and supporting fraud detection\. However, the use and acceptance of these systems are largely influenced by consumers’ perceptions and trust\. The present study focuses trust and concerns of consumers regarding AI\-driven fraud detection and consumer attitudes towards transparency, AI\-based verification and measures intended to strengthen authenticity in influencer marketing\. The study adopts a descriptive research design and uses primary data collected from 70 respondents through a structured questionnaire\. The findings show that respondents demonstrate cautious acceptance of AI\-driven fraud detection\. Half of the respondents reported that they somewhat trust AI, whereas complete trust was comparatively limited\. Concerns relating to transparency, privacy, false identification and possible bias were also identified\. The findings further reveal that consumers attach considerable importance to transparency and generally support AI\-based verification systems\. Respondents also expressed favourable opinions regarding the use of AI tools by brands while evaluating influencers for collaboration\. The study concludes that AI can contribute to improving authenticity in influencer marketing, but its acceptance depends on the development of transparent, reliable and accountable systems\.

## [EMERGING PHYTOTHERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF ARTHRITIS: COMPREHENSIVE INSIGHTS INTO BIOACTIVE PHYTOCONSTITUENTS, MOLECULAR MECHANISMS, EXPERIMENTAL PHARMACOLOGY, AND FUTURE THERAPEUTIC PERSPECTIVES](../publications/4d2940fddf2eeb1caf74.md)

Ashish N\. Umale; Shamsuzzaman \.; Swati P\. Deshmukh

Arthritis is one of the leading causes of chronic pain, disability, and reduced quality of life worldwide, affecting millions of individuals through progressive joint inflammation, cartilage degeneration, and bone destruction\. Although conventional therapies, including nonsteroidal anti\-inflammatory drugs \(NSAIDs\), glucocorticoids, disease\-modifying antirheumatic drugs \(DMARDs\), biologics, and Janus kinase \(JAK\) inhibitors, effectively alleviate symptoms and delay disease progression, their long\-term use is frequently associated with adverse effects, high treatment costs, and incomplete disease remission\. Consequently, phytotherapy has emerged as a promising complementary and alternative therapeutic strategy owing to its multitarget pharmacological actions and comparatively favorable safety profile\. This review comprehensively summarizes the current knowledge on the pathophysiology of arthritis, emphasizing inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and major intracellular signaling pathways, including NF\-κB, MAPK, JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt, NLRP3 inflammasome, COX\-2, and 5\-lipoxygenase\. Particular attention is given to bioactive phytoconstituents such as curcumin, resveratrol, quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin, apigenin, catechins, boswellic acids, thymoquinone, berberine, and other polyphenols, flavonoids, terpenoids, alkaloids, saponins, tannins, and glycosides\. Furthermore, the review compiles experimental pharmacological evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies, summarizes medicinal plants with established anti\-arthritic activity, and highlights their molecular targets and mechanisms of action\. Emerging advances in nanotechnology\-based phytopharmaceuticals, molecular docking, network pharmacology, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence are also discussed as future directions for improving the efficacy, bioavailability, and precision of plant\-derived therapeutics\. Collectively, the available evidence indicates that phytochemicals exert anti\-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and chondroprotective effects through simultaneous modulation of multiple molecular pathways\. However, further standardization, pharmacokinetic evaluation, and well\-designed multicenter clinical trials are required to facilitate their successful translation into evidence\-based clinical practice\. This review provides an integrated scientific framework for researchers and clinicians involved in the development of safer, multitarget, and effective phytotherapeutic interventions for arthritis management\.

## [Electric power demand forecasting in university facilities](../publications/4d3c33c4274d69847e2e.md)

Jorge A\. Turina; Patricio Gabriel Donato; Carlos Martin Orallo; Marcos Alan Funes

La creciente disponibilidad de datos provenientes de sistemas de medición avanzados ha impulsado, gracias al avance de las Redes Eléctricas Inteligentes, el uso de técnicas de aprendizaje automático para el pronóstico de la demanda eléctrica\. Este trabajo analiza diferentes arquitecturas de redes neuronales recurrentes, específicamente del tipo Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), aplicadas a las series temporales de demanda eléctrica de diferentes suministros de la Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata \(UNMDP\)\. El objetivo es caracterizar la capacidad de estas arquitecturas para captar la dinámica temporal de los consumos eléctricos empleando diferentes horizontes de predicción y datos históricos\. Los resultados evidencian la complejidad y limitaciones de las predicciones con horizontes futuros extensos\. Estos hallazgos muestran que la calidad del pronóstico depende no solo de la arquitectura empleada, sino también de la representatividad y estabilidad de las series temporales disponibles\.

## [AI in Aviation Security: Creating Policy and Regulating the Process](../publications/4d4ffa3923ec6eb54759.md)

Beka Khitiri

Aviation security is a field that demands precise policies and tailor\-made regulations\. However, this need tends to make it harder to evolve over time\. Hence, it is particularly difficult to adapt to technological changes\. This creates a major weakness, as the threats that aviation security is created to oppose are not bound by such limitations\. Therefore, it is imperative that the field at hand is regulated in a way that makes it possible to keep up with new instruments available, such as artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. ## [Investigation of Oral Bacterial Population in Tobacco Chewers and Healthy Individuals](../publications/4d54e53a796b23e8eeb8.md)

Sonal Ghatge; Suneel Dodamani; Nagaraj Patil

Objectives The study aimed to isolate and identify bacterial species from the oral cavities of healthy individuals and tobacco chewers\. A comparative evaluation of the bacterial colonies and species present in both groups was then conducted to assess the impact of tobacco chewing on the oral microbiome\. Material and Methods A total of 90 oral swab samples were collected, including 50 from tobacco chewers and 40 from non\-chewers\. The samples were transported aseptically in peptone water and incubated\. After 24 h, the samples were streaked onto nutrient agar, MacConkey agar, and blood agar and incubated at 37°C\. The resulting colonies were observed, and Gram staining was performed\. Bacterial isolates were identified using biochemical tests, including the citrate utilization test, indole test, urease test, and triple sugar iron \(TSI\) test\. For molecular identification, DNA was isolated from pure cultures and subjected to PCR using 16S rRNA gene\-specific forward and reverse primers\. The PCR products were sent to Eurofins Genomics India Pvt\. Ltd\. for sequencing\. Results The results indicate alterations in the oral microbial flora of tobacco chewers compared with non\-chewers\. Streptococcus anginosus KCOM3315 and Streptococcus anginosus 4956 were detected in both tobacco chewers and non\-chewers and are considered potentially pathogenic\. In contrast, Pantoea agglomerans was detected only in tobacco chewers and was absent in non\-chewers\. Pantoea agglomerans is primarily a plant\-associated bacterium but can cause opportunistic infections in humans\. Rothia dentocariosa and Staphylococcus epidermidis , which are considered commensal bacteria, were detected in both tobacco chewers and non\-chewers\. Conclusion The percentage of pathogenic bacteria was higher in tobacco chewers compared with non\-chewers\. In contrast, the percentage of commensal bacteria was lower in tobacco chewers than in non\-chewers\.

## [Integrasi IoT, GIS, dan AI untuk Pemantauan Hutan Cerdas Perhutani](../publications/4d55419292775616c4cc.md)

Muhamad Sabri Ahmad; Moh\. Syadad Mahiri

Transformasi digital Perhutani telah ditopang oleh pemanfaatan sistem informasi geospasial untuk pengumpulan, pemusatan, dan penyajian informasi pengelolaan hutan\. Namun, sistem geospasial belum secara otomatis menyediakan pemantauan mikroklimat secara kontinu, analisis risiko multimodal, dan peringatan dini yang terhubung langsung dengan tindak lanjut petugas\. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang kerangka teknologi hutan cerdas yang mengintegrasikan sensor Internet of Things \(IoT\), komunikasi Long Range \(LoRa\), Sistem Informasi Geografis \(GIS\), citra satelit dan wahana udara nirawak \(UAV\), serta kecerdasan buatan \(AI\) untuk pemantauan kesehatan hutan dan deteksi dini risiko kebakaran pada kawasan yang dikelola Perhutani\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan design science research melalui analisis kebutuhan, perancangan arsitektur, pemodelan skor risiko, simulasi berbasis rentang data UCI Forest Fires, dan penyusunan indikator evaluasi\. Kebaruan penelitian terletak pada integrasi GIS Perhutani dengan pemantauan lingkungan berdaya rendah, penilaian risiko multimodal, dan validasi petugas dalam satu siklus operasional tertutup\. Hasil simulasi menunjukkan skor rata\-rata meningkat dari 0,148 pada kategori rendah menjadi 0,870 pada kategori kritis\. Kerangka yang diusulkan memberikan dasar terukur untuk uji percontohan dan kalibrasi menggunakan data lokal Perhutani\.

## [Detection of Eulecanium giganteum Infestation in Jujube Orchards Based on UAV Multispectral Remote Sensing](../publications/4d7d8a1537bacb0c0214.md)

Yueteng Chao; Yulong Wang; Zhuoyang Xu; Ruohong He; Rina Yangdao; Hongqiang Dong; Ping Li

The application of remote sensing technology to monitor agricultural pests and diseases provides an effective approach for rapid and non\-destructive assessment of crop health\. This study evaluated a UAV multispectral remote sensing framework integrating vegetation indices and SPAD information for assessing Eulecanium giganteum infestation in jujube orchards\. Initially, 24 vegetation indices were extracted from canopy multispectral imagery, and Pearson correlation analysis was used for feature screening, resulting in a refined subset of 19 vegetation indices\. Seven machine learning algorithms were evaluated during model development, with Grid Search combined with tree\-level grouped 7\-fold cross\-validation for hyperparameter selection\. Vegetation indices were used as predictor variables, while SPAD value and infestation severity were treated as response variables in the regression and classification tasks, respectively\. During internal model development, the CatBoost\-19opt model achieved an R2 of 0\.81 and an RMSE of 1\.84 for SPAD estimation\. On the independent test set consisting of 58 jujube trees, the previously selected model achieved an R2 of 0\.84 and an RMSE of 1\.56\. During internal model development, incorporating measured SPAD values improved pest classification performance, with XGBoost\-19sopt achieving an OA of 0\.89 and a Kappa coefficient of 0\.84\. On the independent test set, the measured\-SPAD configuration achieved an OA of 0\.88, whereas both the VI\-only and VI combined with predicted\-SPAD configurations achieved an OA of 0\.71\. Thus, incorporating predicted SPAD did not improve overall classification accuracy relative to using vegetation indices alone\. Further model optimization and additional validation across different orchards, growing seasons, and phenological stages are required before the approach can be considered for operational large\-scale monitoring\.

## [The impact of childbirth on gender wage gap: evidence from China](../publications/4d87d532ee278038f22b.md)

Chong Guo; Xiaowang Pan; Yiqiu Wang; Meng Xie

Introduction China’s evolving fertility policies have renewed academic attention to the impact of childbirth in the labor market\. Whether the first and second birth transitions will lead to different changes in women’s and men’s wages is crucial for understanding the relationship between fertility behavior and gender pay gap\. Methods Based on the data of the four waves of China Household Finance Survey in 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019, this study examines the impact of the first and second birth transitions on wages\. The study uses a difference\-in\-differences framework and combines methods such as Callaway\-Sant’Anna estimator, event study analysis, selection correction, and sensitivity tests\. Results The estimation results show a motherhood wage penalty and a fatherhood wage premium in the labor market, with larger wage changes for the second birth transition than for the first\. Family support and digital finance appear to moderate these effects, and both help to reduce the motherhood wage penalty\. Factors such as changes in working hours, employment interruption, and career progression may help explain the gender divergence in wages\. Further analysis shows that the estimated wage effects are generally larger in absolute terms among workers outside the work unit system and those with non\-establishment status\. In the Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition, the observed individual characteristics can narrow the average gender wage gap, while the unexplained part widens it\. Discussion The findings indicate that childbirth\-related wage differences are strongly gendered and become more pronounced around the second birth transition\.

## [Bioderived and Synthetic Hydrogen Storage Materials](../publications/4d8bc096ba1bae87aa4c.md)

Christopher Chukwuati; Kingsley O\. Ukoba; Tien\-Chien Jen

Bioderived and Synthetic Hydrogen Storage Materials presents innovative approaches for developing efficient, safe, and cost\-effective hydrogen storage technologies\. It demonstrates how the combination of biosynthesized and engineered nanomaterials can overcome hydrogen’s inherent storage challenges of low density and high diffusivity\. Covering physical, chemical, and hybrid storage methods, this book showcases how waste biomass and plastic can be transformed into functional hydrogen storage materials through sustainable processes\. It addresses metal hydrides, complex hydrides, carbon\-based materials, and metal\-organic frameworks while expanding on the emerging application of 3D printing in fabricating optimized storage structures\. Readers will gain insight into the complete development pathway for next\-generation storage materials from precursor selection and biosynthesis to functionalization, thermal activation, and performance testing\. Graduate students and researchers in materials science and energy engineering as well as industry professionals developing sustainable energy technologies, waste valorization processes, and nanomaterials for energy systems will find this book a useful reference\.

## [When the model defines the message: methodological considerations in experimental lung warm ischemia](../publications/4d9c93c7a6c3c96ff749.md)

Jitte Jennekens; Daan Imholz; Sue A\. Braithwaite; Linda Heer; Arne Neyrinck

We read the article by Premachandra et al\. &quot;Resilience of lung grafts to warm ischemia: assessment by ex vivo perfusion using functional and molecular analysis&quot; with great interest \(1\)\. We thank the authors for their comprehensive investigation of the effects of prolonged 2\-hour warm ischemia \(WI\) on lung graft function and biological responses during ex vivo lung perfusion \(EVLP\)\. The authors reported lower initial compliance and increased pulmonary vascular resistance in the WI group compared to control lungs\. These differences resolved over the duration of the EVLP\. At the end of EVLP, no significant differences in molecular and histological markers of injury were observed, except for concentrations of lactate and PECAM, which were higher in the control lungs\.Premachandra et al\. positioned their study within the broader aim to establish the tolerance limit of lungs to WI in a clinically relevant pig model\. While some limitations have been appropriately addressed by the authors, other aspects warrant further consideration and discussion, especially the clinical relevance of their model\. A relevant donation after circulatory death \(DCD\) model should address the critical aspects of the procedure and timeline because these conditions also influence the effect of WI on the lungs\. In clinical practice, extended periods of WI either occur during a prolonged agonal phase or in uncontrolled DCD settings where lungs are mechanically ventilated after failed resuscitation attempts until the &quot;no touch&quot; period \(2,3\)\. This is different from the WI model used by Premachandra et inflammatory differences in their study may reflect not only the use of methylprednisolone but 51 also the specific experimental model that has been used\. 52Finally, we would like to address the split\-lung EVLP model\. We were surprised that only left lungs 53were allocated to the WI group whereas right lungs were allocated to the control group\. 54Consequently, treatment assignment is confounded by anatomical laterality, lung size, and 55 perfusion and ventilation\. Following the Toronto protocol, the authors adjusted perfusion and 56 ventilation using 24% versus 16% of theoretical cardiac output and tidal volumes of 3\.5 versus 2\.5 57 mL/kg for the right and left lung respectively\. This corresponds to a right:left perfusion distribution 58 of 60%/40%\. In humans, a perfusion distribution of 55%:45% is commonly assumed \(9\)\. 59Accounting for size differences between right and left by adjusting flow and ventilation does not 60 necessarily mean that the resulting ex vivo perfusion of right and left lungs is physiologically 61 comparable with the potential risk of being more protective in one group compared to the other\.A similar principle may apply to perfusate\-derived biomarkers\. Interestingly, lactate and PECAM 63 concentrations were higher in the control lungs at the end of EVLP\. The authors proposed that this 64 may reflect a protective priming effect of WI\. We propose the alternative explanation that the 65 greater lung mass and potentially greater amount of perfused tissue of the right lungs in the 66 control group may have contributed to differences in absolute marker release\.

## [Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning](../publications/4da85a83022187ae28b9.md)

Arnav Chavan; Kusha Sareen; Rishabh Tiwari; Abhranil Chandra; Johan Obando\-Ceron; Kurt Keutzer; Scott Niekum; Inderjit S Dhillon; Devvrit Khatri

Large language models \(LLMs\) acquire new skills through fine\-tuning, but it can destroy capabilities they already have: catastrophic forgetting remains a central obstacle to continual learning in LLMs\. Recent works connect forgetting to how far, and along which directions, fine\-tuning moves the weights\. On\-policy methods such as reinforcement learning and on\-policy distillation avoid updating the principal singular directions of weight matrices and thus forget less\. In contrast, SFT concentrates updates along these directions and is susceptible to catastrophic forgetting\. In this work, we introduce Subspace Tuning \(SST\), which restricts each weight update to the bottom singular subspace, eliminating changes along the principal directions\. SST is optimizer\-agnostic and composes well with fine\-tuning recipes including SFT and self\-distillation\. SST combines tight subspace protection, dense gradient estimation, and a simple refresh mechanism, enabling stronger learning than prior orthogonal fine\-tuning methods\. With these mechanisms, protecting as much as 99\\% of the weight subspace substantially improves retention while preserving strong target\-task performance\. This behavior strengthens with model and data size and nearly eliminates forgetting in the large\-model regime\. SST also keeps the model close to its base distribution, inducing $2$\-\-$4\\times$ less KL drift than the baseline recipes\. Overall, SST advances the learning\-\-forgetting Pareto frontier, making it a practical default for fine\-tuning pre\-trained language models\.

## [Association of the triglyceride\-to\-high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio with kidney stone status: cross\-sectional and machine\-learning analyses](../publications/4daddc69199430589904.md)

Hu Liang; Dekai Hu; Junzhi Zhang; Xincheng Yi; Bingbing Hou; Yang Chen; 郝宗耀

This study investigated the association between triglyceride\-to\-high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio \(TG/HDL\-C\) and kidney stone status and evaluated its contribution to multivariable classification models\. A total of 1,174 patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University were included, with kidney stone status confirmed by urological imaging\. Multivariable analyses were used to assess the association between TG/HDL\-C and kidney stone status\. Supplementary population\-based analyses were conducted using weighted data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey \(NHANES\)\. Seven machine\-learning models were developed and internally evaluated within the clinical cohort, and SHapley Additive Explanations \(SHAP\) were used to interpret model outputs\. In the clinical cohort, a higher TG/HDL\-C ratio was associated with greater odds of kidney stone status after multivariable adjustment \(OR, 2\.16; 95% CI, 1\.73\-2\.70\)\. The association was generally consistent across subgroups defined by age, sex, body mass index, hypertension, and diabetes, with no significant interactions observed\. A directionally similar association was identified in the weighted NHANES analysis \(OR, 1\.04; 95% CI, 1\.01\-1\.07\)\. Among the evaluated machine\-learning models, the random forest model achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the internal validation set \(AUROC, 0\.818; 95% CI, 0\.775\-0\.859\)\. SHAP analysis identified the TG/HDL\-C ratio as an important contributor to model classification\. These findings indicate that the TG/HDL\-C ratio is an accessible metabolic marker associated with kidney stone status\. However, the observational design precludes causal inference, and prospective studies with external model validation are warranted\.

## [Erwin, Richard: Human–AI Dependence: Agency, Vulnerability, and the Ethics of Reliance](../publications/4dcf677262c5156015b3.md)



As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into cognitive, professional, practical, and relational life, concerns about “AI dependence” are likely to intensify\. Yet dependence alone does not establish harm\. Modern life is structured through dependencies, and AI can expand human capability at the same time that it displaces particular skills, alters judgment, creates switching costs, or increases vulnerability to interruption\. This paper develops a framework for distinguishing among these effects\. It separates dependence from pathology; assisted performance from retained human capability; attachment from functional emotional dependence; relational irreplaceability from functional irreplaceability; and vulnerability and risk from demonstrated harm\. It further examines how dependence develops through repeated reliance, how capability may deteriorate relative to changing task demands even when prior knowledge remains intact, and how human oversight can become merely ceremonial when AI systems exceed practical verification capacity\. In relational contexts, the paper argues that emotional intensity, attachment, and anticipated grief should not themselves be treated as evidence of harmful dependence, while persistent availability and asymmetrical support may nonetheless facilitate functional reliance\. The analysis then extends beyond the individual to provider power, arguing that reasonably foreseeable dependence should be treated as a design and governance condition requiring appropriate continuity, transition, portability, and oversight protections\. The paper ultimately proposes a distinction between sustaining dependence, which expands capability while preserving meaningful agency and safeguards, and diminishing dependence, which progressively narrows the ability to act, judge, recover, redirect, or function without the system\. The central task is therefore not to eliminate AI dependence, but to determine what forms of dependence enhance human life, what forms diminish it, and how the vulnerabilities created by reliance should be responsibly governed\.

## [MEGH\-DDI: MolT5\-driven edge\-aware graph learning with Hop2Token representation for drug–drug interaction prediction](../publications/4dd38bd6de3ac374bbb5.md)

Li Zhou; Yun Zuo; Wenying He; Zhaohong Deng

Drug\-drug interactions \(DDIs\) are critical in pharmacology, as synergistic or antagonistic effects between co\-administered drugs can enhance therapeutic outcomes or cause toxicity, posing major challenges for drug safety assessment and new drug development\. Current molecular representation methods often fail to capture dynamic substructure relationships or semantic interactions among functional groups\. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes MEGH\-DDI, a multimodal framework that integrates complementary molecular representation learning with graph\-structure dynamic perception\. The framework employs a dual\-channel semantic module that combines Mol2vec\-based substructure representations with MolT5 chemical language embeddings, while SHAP\-based dynamic feature selection reduces redundancy\. For fine\-grained structural modeling, we introduce an edge\-aware GCNII equipped with bond\-level attention to distinguish different types of chemical bonds\. Furthermore, the Hop2Token module converts multi\-hop neighborhoods into token sequences, enabling Transformer\-based modeling of high\-order substructure dependencies\. Experimental results demonstrate that MEGH\-DDI achieves competitive performance across both transductive and inductive settings\. On the DrugBank dataset, MEGH\-DDI attains an accuracy of 98\.36% in the transductive task, outperforming earlier baselines and surpassing recent state\-of\-the\-art methods, with both AUC and AP exceeding 99\.7%\. On the ChChMiner dataset, MEGH\-DDI achieves an F1 score of 99\.05%, improving over the best existing method by 2\.74 percentage points\. In the inductive settings, MEGH\-DDI achieves competitive performance across most evaluation metrics on both datasets, showing advantages over competing methods on several key metrics\. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MEGH\-DDI in predicting DDI involving previously unseen drugs and its potential to generalize to complex DDI prediction scenarios\. To enhance interpretability, MEGH\-DDI incorporates a three\-level mechanism spanning atoms, chemical bonds, and topological paths, highlighting key atoms and bond contributions\. Overall, MEGH\-DDI provides an efficient, accurate, and interpretable solution for drug safety assessment and new drug discovery\. Code and datasets are available at https://github\.com/Lilyjoys/MEGH\-DDI, and a free web platform is provided at http://www\.edgh\-ddi\.com\.

## [A lean statistical cell\-to\-pack framework for sustainable battery pack capacity estimation](../publications/4dd9c39352b89bc07e89.md)

Chen Ma; Qinghao Zhang; Bin Duan; Chenghui Zhang; Changlong Li; Long Chang; Benben Jiang

Accurate battery pack capacity estimation is vital for electric vehicle and energy storage safety, but conventional pack\-level aging tests are costly, energy intensive, and wasteful\. This study proposes a lean statistical cell\-to\-pack \(LS\-CTP\) framework that eliminates pack\-level tests\. Using aging data from only a few independent test cells, it combines lightweight machine learning and decision algorithms to achieve multi\-feature statistical transformation and fusion from routine fragmented charge data\. It requires few hyperparameters and low computational overhead and applies to parallel, series, and mixed configurations\. Monte Carlo analyses show a mean absolute percentage error below 1\.24% for parallel packs and 1\.92% for series packs using as few as two test cells\. A sustainability assessment indicates over 90% reduction in battery waste and testing energy\. By decoupling algorithm development from pack\-level cycling, LS\-CTP advances cost\-effective, energy\-efficient, and sustainable battery health diagnostics, supporting the clean energy transition\.

## [Precision Immunosuppression in Heart Transplantation: Biomarker\-Guided Therapy Comes of Age](../publications/4ddb81b8deba3cfd988d.md)

Karthik Sreedhara; Palak Shah

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart transplantation is the definitive treatment for end\-stage heart failure\. While the number of heart transplant performed yearly in the United States has nearly doubled in the last decade, median survival has stagnated, largely due to the complications posed by lifelong immunosuppression\. A shift towards precision medicine is needed to achieve the optimal balance between risk of allograft rejection and drug\-related toxicities to improve post\-transplant outcomes\. RECENT FINDINGS: Novel molecular based diagnostic tools and biomarkers are being investigated, and hold promise in evaluating graft health and assessing immune state\. The use of circulating biomarkers and molecular diagnostics such as human and viral cell\-free DNA, tissue\-based gene expression profiling, and circulating microRNAs, will allow for more comprehensive assessment of post\-transplant immune activity and rejection risk to personalize patient care\.

## [Genome\-wide association mapping reveals stable genomic regions associated with fruit quality traits in tomato \(Solanum lycopersicum L\.\)](../publications/4de610824a634e97b0d7.md)

Raja Sekhar Srungarapu; Devi R\. Kandel; Mohan Singh Rajkumar; Kranthi Kiran Mandadi; Kevin Michael Crosby; Carlos Augusto Avila

Fruit quality has become a primary breeding objective in tomato because it determines consumer acceptance, processing efficiency, and market value\. However, quality\-related traits are quantitatively inherited and strongly influenced by environmental conditions, making genetic improvement challenging\. In this study, genome\-wide association studies \(GWAS\) was conducted to elucidate the genetic architecture of six economically important fruit quality traits, including luminosity, hue, chroma, soluble solids content \(°Brix\), titratable acidity, and fruit fresh weight \(FW\), using a diverse panel of 305 tomato accessions evaluated over two growing seasons\. Substantial phenotypic variation was observed for all traits, with significant effects of genotype, year, and genotype × year interaction, indicating that fruit quality is governed by both genetic and environmental factors\. Fruit weight, luminosity, hue, chroma, and °Brix exhibited high broad\-sense heritability, whereas titratable acidity showed moderate heritability\. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive relationships among color\-related traits, while °Brix was positively associated with acidity but negatively correlated with fruit color attributes and FW\. Skim sequencing generated 4,618 high\-quality single nucleotide polymorphisms \(SNPs\), and GWAS was performed using multiple models\. GWAS identified 15 non\-redundant marker\-trait associations \(MTAs\) across chromosomes, with several loci consistently detected across statistical models\. A prominent locus, SL4\.0ch03\_12722521, on chromosome 3 was associated with luminosity, hue, and chroma, explaining up to 53\.86% of phenotypic variation \(PVE\), suggesting pleiotropic regulation of fruit color\. Stable loci controlling FW and soluble solids were also identified on chromosome 5, explaining up to 52\.88% PVE\. Candidate genes of significant MTAs included sucrose synthase, sec14p\-like phosphatidylinositol transfer protein, bHLH transcription factor, and chitinase genes, indicating potential roles in carbohydrate metabolism, fruit development, cell wall remodeling, pigmentation, and ripening\. These findings provide valuable genomic resources for improving fruit quality and accelerating the development of elite tomato cultivars\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EARLY RECOGNITION OF CLINICAL DETERIORATION: NEW PERSPECTIVES FOR NURSING PRACTICE IN PATIENT SAFETY](../publications/4de9dc3194cd9a1cb051.md)

Victor Lucas Dutra de Morais; Vinícius Luan Dutra de Morais; Allana Beatriz Silva Medeiros; Golda Meyr Ângelo de Lima Barbosa; Shirliane Romana Da Silva Barros; Raiane Patrícia Nascimento Guedes da Silva; Débora Ilana Silva de Oliveira

Clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients may be preceded by progressive physiological changes that, when recognized in a timely manner, enable healthcare interventions before severe adverse events occur\. In this context, artificial intelligence \(AI\) has been investigated as a tool capable of analyzing large volumes of clinical data and identifying patterns associated with worsening health status\. This study aimed to analyze the evidence regarding the use of artificial intelligence for the early recognition of clinical deterioration, emphasizing its implications for nursing practice and patient safety\. A narrative literature review was conducted based on scientific studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, early warning systems, and clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients\. The literature indicates that predictive models may increase the ability to identify patients at risk of deterioration, support care prioritization, and facilitate more timely clinical responses\. However, limitations related to algorithm heterogeneity, data quality and representativeness, external validation, interpretability, bias, privacy, and integration of alerts into clinical workflows were also identified\. For nursing, AI represents a complementary resource to clinical assessment and may strengthen surveillance and decision\-making when integrated with professional judgment and structured care processes\. It is concluded that the responsible incorporation of these technologies requires professional education, critical evaluation of AI systems, and preservation of the central role of human care\.

## [Fragmentation and manufactured ambivalence: Necessary unlearnings for intersectional critical action with queer and trans youth](../publications/4dea266845933d4361b2.md)

Sukhmani Singh; Gio Iacono; Megan S\. Paceley; V\. Paul Poteat; Hirokazu Yoshikawa

Abstract In this conceptual paper, we chart a call to action for scholar‐activists on critical consciousness among queer and gender‐diverse children and youth by introducing two emergent, empirically grounded concepts: fragmentation and manufactured ambivalence \. We contend in the white‐capitalist‐cis/heterosexist‐ patriarchal U\.S\., interconnected structures of oppression create and maintain falsely singular master narratives to prevent the building of solidarities\. These seemingly singular narratives inculcate fragmentation —the psychological experience that if one is situated at one or more dominant default socio‐structural axes \(e\.g\., Whiteness, nationality, cisgender identity, etc\.\) they are automatically removed/absolved from reflection and action around oppression on minoritized axes\. We discuss how scholar‐activists and those looking to work with queer and trans children and youth must create consciousness‐raising systems to do the work of defragmentation, while also addressing manufactured ambivalence —a paradoxical emotional response of being simultaneously critically reflective and skeptical that critical action can produce meaningful structural change\.

## [The impact of the digital environment and information overload on the cognitive state of students in the context of the «Zhana Kazakhstan» program](../publications/4dedae2b9634373e0dfa.md)

V\.A\. Burmistrova

Objective \. The study seeks to examine how intensive exposure to digital technologies and excessive information flow affect learners’ cognitive functioning, particularly attention, memory, and processing efficiency, as well as to evaluate potential risks to academic performance in highly connected learning environments within the context of the educational transformation under the «Zhana Kazakhstan» program\. Materials and methods\. An empirical survey was conducted among 54 adolescents \(mainly 17\-18 years old\)\. Data were collected through an 18\-item questionnaire covering patterns of digital device use, distraction frequency, study habits, and self\-reported cognitive states \(focus, memory, concentration, and fatigue\)\. The results were analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques to identify general tendencies and relationships\. Results and discussion\. The findings indicate intensive daily use of digital devices, with a significant proportion of respondents \(48\.1%\) spending more than six hours online\. Many participants reported regular interruptions during study sessions and a tendency to switch between tasks\. More than half \(57\.4%\) experienced reduced ability to maintain focus, while a notable share \(33\.4%\) indicated difficulties retaining recently learned material\. Signs of cognitive strain, including tiredness and perceived overload, were also widespread\. These patterns suggest a transformation in cognitive functioning characterized by reduced depth of information processing and increased fragmentation of attention\. Within the framework of the «Zhana Kazakhstan» program, this creates a tension between digital advancement and the preservation of stable cognitive functioning\. Conclusion \. The results demonstrate that excessive digital exposure is associated with cognitive strain, including weakened concentration and memory efficiency\. However, students’ awareness of these effects provides an opportunity to promote more conscious and regulated use of technology\. Ensuring a balance between digital innovation and cognitive well\-being remains a key challenge for modern education\.

## [Large Language Models in the Emergency Department: Fairness Implications for Clinicians](../publications/4df538dbfae1034b998b.md)

Kasumi Satoh; Manabu Okuyama; Hajime Nakae; Yohei Okada

Applications of artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly large language models \(LLMs\), are rapidly expanding in emergency medicine, but concerns remain regarding their fairness across diverse patient populations\. Fairness extends beyond model accuracy and includes equal performance across patient groups, equitable outcomes and allocation of clinical benefits, and procedural fairness throughout the lifecycle of AI implementation\. This narrative review aims to provide a practical framework for understanding and evaluating fairness in emergency medicine applications of AI and LLMs\. This narrative review organizes fairness risks into three clinically relevant layers\. First, datalevel fairness concerns the data used to train, fine\-tune, or prompt AI systems\. Biased clinical data, including non\-random missingness and stigmatizing documentation, can influence model performance\. Second, output\-level fairness concerns whether the outputs generated by AI systems are equally accurate, safe, and useful across patient groups\. In emergency care, subgroup\-specific errors in recommendations, predictions, translations, or instructions may arise from aggregation, learning, or evaluation bias, even when overall model performance appears strong\. Third, human\-interaction fairness concerns whether the benefits of AI are realized equitably in clinical practice and by patients\. Even when data and outputs are fair, inequities may arise if clinicians over\-rely on or reject useful AI recommendations, or if patients are unable to access, understand, or trust AI\-mediated information\. Clinicians should consider potential implications for safety, transparency, and fairness alongside overall model accuracy when evaluating AI tools in emergency medicine\.

## [Variable\-resolution maps \(VRMs\) in CCTBX and Phenix : accounting for local resolution in cryoEM](../publications/4df7d85e6069a9c04486.md)

Pavel V\. Afonine; Paul D\. Adams; Alexandre Urzhumtsev

Calculation of density maps from atomic models is essential for structural studies using crystallography and electron cryo\-microscopy \(cryoEM\)\. These maps serve various purposes, including atomic model building, refinement, visualization and validation\. However, accurately comparing model\-calculated maps to experimental data poses challenges, particularly because the resolution of cryoEM experimental maps varies across the map\. Traditional crystallography methods generate finite\-resolution maps with uniform resolution throughout the unit cell volume, while most modern software in cryoEM employs Gaussian\-like functions to generate these maps, which does not adequately account for atomic model parameters and resolution\. Recent work by Urzhumtsev &amp; Lunin \[IUCrJ \(2022\), 9, 728\-734\] introduces a novel method for computing atomic model maps that incorporate local resolution and can be expressed as analytically differentiable functions of atomic parameters\. This approach enhances the accuracy of maps simulated from atomic models, allowing them to better reproduce features of the experimental maps\. In this paper, we detail the implementation of this method in CCTBX and Phenix\.

## [AgentOnto: Ontology\-Guided LLM Agents for Enterprise Data Analytics](../publications/4dfd46f0900f33c2204b.md)

Dayan Pan; Bincheng Zuo; Xiaojian Wang; Daogang Zhang; Jingyuan Wang

Enterprise data analysis requires agents to connect analytical requests with knowledge distributed across databases, business documents, and existing example tasks\. Without an explicit representation of this knowledge, an agent may produce incorrect analytical results and cannot reliably incorporate feedback\. We present AgentOnto, an ontology\-guided LLM agent for enterprise data analytics\. AgentOnto organizes heterogeneous enterprise knowledge into an ontology that directly guides analysis and incorporates confirmed feedback\. Iterative Ontology Preparation further improves the ontology through self\-generated analysis tasks\. We evaluate AgentOnto on two public data sources\. AgentOnto substantially outperforms representative methods, while module\-level evaluations confirm the effectiveness of ontology construction, analysis, and updating\. A real\-world deployment further demonstrates its practical value in enterprise analytics\. These results demonstrate that explicitly constructing, using, and updating enterprise knowledge supports reliable and adaptable data analysis\.

## [PIECES\-Based Analysis of E\-AIW Management at KUA Kartasura](../publications/4e0c1448c20eb82bea3a.md)

Arum Fitri Lestari; Betty Eliya Rokhmah; Arian Agung Prasetiyawan

Waqf digitalization in Indonesia remains an urgent policy priority, as a substantial proportion of registered waqf land has yet to be certified and administrative services still need to be optimized down to the sub\-district level\. This study aims to analyze the management of e\-AIW in KUA Kartasura District using the PIECES \(Performance, Information, Economy, Control, Efficiency, Service\) framework\. The method used is a case study with a descriptive qualitative approach through digital ethnography, including interviews, participatory observations, documentation, and technical tests of Google Page Speed Insights \(GPSI\) to assess system performance\. Data were collected from the Head of KUA, e\-AIW operators, and officials of the Ministry of Religious Affairs of Sukoharjo Regency selected through snowball sampling, and were analyzed following Creswell&\#x27;s \(2018\) stages of organizing, coding, presenting narratives, and drawing conclusions\. The results show that e\-AIW is able to increase the speed of data recording and verification, make archiving easier, and reduce operational costs\. Google PageSpeed Insights \(GPSI\) testing recorded a desktop performance score of 67 against 56 on mobile, indicating that further technical optimization is still required, particularly for mobile access\. The system also provides neater and more accountable information, with relatively good control and operational efficiency, although HR capacity and technical constraints still affect the effectiveness of the service\. In addition, e\-AIW contributes to increased transparency and public participation, especially through self\-access for wakif as well as automated document printing features\. Based on these findings, the study recommends strengthening technical infrastructure—particularly the mobile version—enhancing human resource capacity through regular training, and developing adaptive control and system integration features to support the sustainability and accountability of e\-AIW services at the KUA level\.

## [Integrative taxonomy of a new Odontidium \(Tabellariaceae\) species from Poland: Combined morphological and molecular evidence](../publications/4e1146583d3cc5bc93d9.md)

Julia Sulkowska; Rafał M\. Olszyński; Carlos Eduardo Wetzel; Joanna Żelazna‐Wieczorek

Mountain springs are important ecosystems for freshwater biodiversity and may serve as refugia for previously unrecognised diatom diversity\. During investigations of springs in the Bieszczady National Park \(Poland\), a morphologically distinctive taxon of the genus Odontidium was observed, which is described here as Odontidium fontinale Sulkowska, Żelazna\-Wieczorek, Olszyński &amp; Wetzel, sp\. nov \. A morphological and morphometric description was prepared based on analyses conducted using light and scanning electron microscopy\. The new species was compared with morphologically similar taxa, including Odontidium mesodon , O\. minutum , O\. rostratum , and Tetracyclus rupestre \. Odontidium fontinale sp\. nov \. is distinguished primarily by its small valve dimensions and a relatively low density of transapical ribs\. Furthermore, despite its frequent occurrence in mountain freshwater habitats, the genus Odontidium remains poorly known at the molecular level\. To address this, molecular data based on rbc L sequences from cultures of the new species were obtained to assess its phylogenetic position\.

CT total score was not significantly correlated with theory examination score in the Pearson analysis \( r = 0\.003, p = 0\.980\) and was not independently associated with theory examination score after adjustment \( β = 0\.014, 95% CI − 0\.103 to 0\.131; p = 0\.817\), while SDL total score was also not independently associated with theory examination score \( β = −0\.110, 95% CI − 0\.226 to 0\.007; p = 0\.065\)\. Neither SDL nor CT was independently associated with the comprehensive instructor rating \( p = 0\.469 and p = 0\.361, respectively\)\. In exploratory domain\-level analyses, CT open\-mindedness was a nominal positive association with weekly assignment performance \( r = 0\.244, p = 0\.032; Spearman ρ = 0\.250, p = 0\.028\), and CT inquisitiveness showed a nominal positive association with case presentation performance \( r = 0\.292, p = 0\.010; Spearman ρ = 0\.328, p = 0\.004\)\.
