## [Reliability of Machine Learning Approaches Towards the Identification of Novel PI4KIIIβ Inhibitors](../publications/4e209ec6fa4bdd86246e.md)

Priyanka Andola; Prasanna Sagane; Lalitha Guruprasad

INTRODUCTION: The type III Phosphatidylinositol 4\-kinase \(PI4KIIIβ\) serves as a key host factor that mediates the replication of RNA viruses and is involved in essential membrane trafficking events\. The development of PI4KIIIβ\-specific inhibitors could give insights into the enzyme&\#x27;s function and contribute to the treatment of viral diseases\. However, the molecular features that determine inhibitor activity and selectivity remain unclear\. METHODS: PI4KIIIβ inhibitors with reported biological activities \(pIC50\) were systematically analyzed using machine\-learning methods\. Molecular characterization was performed using RDKit, Chemopy descriptors, and PubChem fingerprints\. Multiple classification and regression models were developed and evaluated using 10\-fold cross\-validation to establish robust structureactivity relationships\. RESULTS: It was suggested that the PubChem fingerprint\-based linear regression, SMOreg, and GaussianProcesses models were more appropriate for the studied dataset to deliver the best predictive ability, which showed a correlation coefficient value &gt; 0\.7 in the 10\-fold crossvalidation\. PubChemFP389 and PubChemFP572, representing amidine\-like fragments or guanidine\- related motifs, and the aromatic amine fragment showed a negative correlation with respect to biological activity\. DISCUSSION: The study describes predictive models and provides insights into essential structural features in chemical compounds relevant for inhibitory activity, which could assist in the design and optimization of novel PI4KIIIβ inhibitors for antiviral and anticancer applications\. A similar approach may be extended to a larger dataset of molecules or to other related drug targets\. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that excessive basicity and certain polar functionalities may be detrimental to PI4KIIIβ inhibition, providing important insights into the structural features influencing ligand binding and activity\.

## [Analysis of perceptions regarding career prospects and professional barriers in neurosurgery among generation Z](../publications/4e21e2266ad2e3a91c30.md)

Introduction\. The generational shift in the higher medical education system highlights the need to study the career expectations and professional preferences of Generation Z, whose members constitute the majority of students and early\-career specialists\. The aim\. To analyze the perception of neurosurgery as a specialty among Generation Z as a direction for further professional choice, assessing attitudes, motivational factors, expectations, and perceived barriers\. Materials and methods\. An online survey was conducted among 149 respondents \(4–6th\-year students, residents, postgraduate students, general practitioners, and early\-career neurosurgeons\)\. The questionnaire consisted of 23 items covering sociodemographic characteristics, factors influencing the choice of neurosurgery, barriers, expectations from professional activity, as well as engagement with social media and innovative technologies\. Results\. It was found that 48 % of students consider neurosurgery as a potential career path\. The key motivating factors are the uniqueness of surgical procedures \(78\.5 %\), the diversity of subspecialties \(58\.9 %\), and the technological nature of the profession\. The main barriers include psychosocial factors \(responsibility, risk of burnout\), and among residents – paperwork \(51 %\) and a lack of mentorship \(44\.8 %\)\. A high demand was identified for international internships \(87 %\), rotations, and financial support during training\. High levels of engagement with social media \(76\.4 %\) and use of artificial intelligence \(75\.7 %\) were recorded\. Conclusion\. The data obtained in the study demonstrate the need for active modernization of educational programs, taking into account the value orientations of the new generation\. Priority areas should include: developing mentorship systems, integrating active rotations and internships into the curriculum, reducing documentation burdens, and introducing digital technologies into simulation\-based training\.

Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse\. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power \(particularly GPUs\) and time\. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets\. A classification model based on gradient\-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares\. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in\-distribution test samples well\. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness\. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples\. The proposed approach outperforms the state\-of\-the\-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98\.10 and 98\.40% using combined datasets\. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems\.

## [Transformasi Kepemimpinan Digital di Perguruan Tinggi: Peran Strategis Kepemimpinan dalam Mengakselerasi Transformasi Digital Pendidikan](../publications/4e4023e396dfce174322.md)

Reyhan Nanda; Cepi Triatna; Eka Prihatin

Transformasi digital telah mengubah cara perguruan tinggi menjalankan proses akademik, administratif, dan tata kelola institusi\. Perubahan tersebut tidak hanya menuntut kesiapan teknologi, tetapi juga membutuhkan kepemimpinan yang mampu mengarahkan organisasi dalam menghadapi kompleksitas perubahan digital\. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis perkembangan konsep kepemimpinan digital di perguruan tinggi, perannya dalam mendorong transformasi digital, faktor pendukung dan penghambat, serta arah perkembangannya pada masa mendatang\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) dengan menganalisis literatur ilmiah Scopus Q1\-Q4 yang relevan diterbitkan pada periode 2021–2026\. Literatur dianalisis secara tematik untuk mengidentifikasi pola, strategi, dan perkembangan konseptual mengenai transformasi kepemimpinan digital dalam konteks pendidikan tinggi\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa konsep kepemimpinan digital berkembang dari kemampuan mengadopsi teknologi menuju kapasitas strategis dalam mengelola perubahan organisasi, mengembangkan kompetensi digital, membangun budaya inovasi, memperkuat kolaborasi, serta memanfaatkan data dalam pengambilan keputusan\. Kepemimpinan digital berperan sebagai penghubung antara teknologi, sumber daya manusia, dan strategi institusi sehingga transformasi digital dapat berlangsung secara terarah dan berkelanjutan\. Keberhasilannya dipengaruhi oleh komitmen pimpinan, kompetensi digital, infrastruktur, budaya organisasi, kolaborasi, dan kesiapan perubahan\. Ke depan, kepemimpinan digital perlu berkembang menjadi lebih adaptif, human\-centered, berbasis data, kolaboratif, dan berorientasi pada keberlanjutan perguruan tinggi\.

## [Inteligencia artificial en educación superior a distancia e híbrida: Síntesis transcompleja de evidencias](../publications/4e4fb995a716c4af9352.md)

Ruth M\. Mujica\-Sequera; Kenneth Rosillón

Introducción: La expansión de las tecnologías emergentes en la educación superior a distancia e híbrida ha intensificado el debate sobre el alcance de la inteligencia artificial \(IA\) en la personalización del aprendizaje, la toma de decisiones pedagógicas y la configuración de ecosistemas educativos digitales\. Objetivo: Analizar las evidencias y condiciones reportadas sobre la integración de la IA en la educación superior a distancia e híbrida desde una perspectiva transcompleja\. Metodología: Se realizó una revisión sistemática cualitativa de 33 estudios científicos publicados entre 2020 y 2025, recuperados en Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC y Google Scholar\. El proceso siguió las fases de identificación, cribado, elegibilidad e inclusión, con análisis de contenido temático y una matriz de trazabilidad del corpus\. Resultados: Se identificaron cinco dimensiones: pedagógica, analítica, institucional, ética y ecosistémica\-transcompleja\. Los hallazgos muestran aportes potenciales en retroalimentación, seguimiento académico, intervención temprana, flexibilidad formativa y gobernanza de datos\. Discusión y conclusiones: La IA no constituye un recurso meramente instrumental, sino una mediación sociotécnica que reconfigura las relaciones entre datos, sujetos, prácticas pedagógicas e instituciones\. Su alcance depende de las condiciones éticas, las competencias docentes, la calidad de los datos, la gobernanza institucional y la reducción de las brechas digitales\. Esta lectura aporta una síntesis integradora para orientar decisiones académicas responsables y fortalecer los criterios éticos, pedagógicos e institucionales en contextos de educación superior digital de diversas universidades y sistemas\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial Explicable en programación competitiva: análisis comparativo de métodos de Machine Learning bajo los principios FATE](../publications/4e5fb2e4e2c3617cdfa7.md)

Claudia Morales Herrera; Hubert Viltres Sala; Aneyty Martín García; Yeleny Zulueta Véliz; Yaniselis Sánchez Hormigó; Leonides Rodríguez Martínez

This review article analyzes the application of Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) in the context of programming education, structuring the analysis around the FATE principles \(Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, Explainability\)\. A systematic review was conducted of the scientific literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 in databases such as Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Scielo\. Based on the findings, the review also incorporates an empirical analysis of seven comparable systems that apply ML in educational and competitive programming contexts\. The analysis shows that most ML models applied to programming education prioritize predictive accuracy over transparency\. A structural gap is identified: the most accurate models exhibit the lowest levels of explainability, compromising the FATE principles\. The combination of Decision Trees as an intrinsically interpretable model with TreeSHAP as a post\-hoc explainability technique offers the optimal balance between performance and pedagogical transparency\. The integration of XAI into learning analytics is not a marginal technical improvement, but an ethical imperative to transform automated assessment systems into pedagogical allies that guarantee equity and causal feedback to students\. Keywords: accuracy, decision tree, explainability, FATE, method, transparency, TreeSHAP, XAI\.

## [Creating Accountability for Public Health Impacts of Commercial Products and Services](../publications/4e649ae894c3951bf3b5.md)

Stephen J\. Downs; Sara J\. Singer

Abstract Commercial products and services significantly – and often negatively – impact public health by shaping the health behaviors of their users\. This paper explores a potential path to holding companies accountable for costly, negative public health impacts of their commercial products and services\. We share lessons from developing and applying a new methodology for measuring the annual national healthcare costs associated with the products and services of individual companies\. Regular accounting for these impacts would create multiple promising policy opportunities, including taxation, which we explore in this paper\. We also describe considerations for developing policy interventions associated with measuring health impacts of individual companies, including balancing personal and societal responsibilities, selection of appropriate counterfactuals, corporate data reporting requirements, and availability and quality of scientific evidence\. Given both the scientific and political novelty of such approaches to assigning corporate accountability, we recommend strategies for advancing the policy arguments and supporting the refinement and application of the measurement techniques\.

## [Quem faz cada etapa? A IA generativa como executora de tarefas e a mudança na rotina de trabalho](../publications/4e80e74bb02933bf6cf0.md)

Daniela Hayoshi

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools have spread rapidly among professionals, and experiments show substantial gains on isolated tasks\. Yet average effects on earnings and recorded hours have been small, although changes in task organization are already evident\. This conceptual article proposes that an important part of this gap is explained by how people represent the technology: generative AI tends to be perceived as a question\-and\-answer tool rather than as an executor of process steps, let alone of recurring routines that keep running while the person only checks the result\. Drawing on literatures on the task\-based approach in labor economics, levels of automation, trust and overreliance in automated systems, work design and redesign, sociotechnical frames, transfer of training, and habit formation, the article develops a five\-element model \(perception, decomposition, allocation, verification, and routinization\) and argues that the relevant question shifts from “how do I ask?” to “who performs each step?”, with three possible destinations for each step: AI alone, AI with human verification, or the person\. Seven testable propositions are formulated, and implications for research, training design, and organizations are discussed\. The article presents no new data; its contribution is to organize dispersed evidence into an explicit, falsifiable mechanism\.

## [Teachers’ emotional engagement, differences and overlaps across generations\. A distinction between the perspective of experience and the strong engagement of novices](../publications/4e81e25ba943b9e4b2cb.md)

Abstract The emotional state of teachers and their well\-being in schools and their profession have been a topic of growing interest to policymakers\. This paper aims to address teachers’ possible generational differences and overlaps concerning emotional work in teaching\. This paper delves into teachers’ emotional engagement throughout their careers in Spain\. The research was based on a qualitative paradigm\. Focus groups and interviews were conducted with 147 novice, veteran, and retired teachers\. The main results show a difference in teachers’ emotional management of tasks, which appears as teachers gain more work experience\. On one hand, novice teachers must adapt to their professional environment more than their veteran and retired colleagues\. This finding suggests that novice teachers may demonstrate a higher level of emotional management than their more experienced counterparts, but they perceive that their efforts eventually burn out over time\. This issue is perceived through the lens of their elders, making both emotional engagement and emotional management in the teaching profession visible\.

## [Federated Observability Architectures for Zero\-Downtime Data Engineering Pipelines](../publications/4e8cbd95a878eba78be4.md)

Distributed microservice ecosystems require observability solutions that don’t disrupt services\. In this paper, we summarize basic and newer studies on stream processing, distributed tracing, anomaly detection, and zero\-downtime release engineering and propose a common framework, Federated Observability Architecture \(FOA\)\. A literature review of 15 of the primary sources shows a mean time to recover \(MTTR\) of 34 minutes or higher and a total downtime of 87 minutes or more per month in pipeline clusters for medium scale\. FOA applies universal context propagation, stateful stream processing checkpointing, and multimodal anomaly detection which lowers MTTR to around 6 minutes and limits monthly downtime to 12 minutes or less, or a 91% reduction at hyperscale deployments\. When automated schema\-drift and watermark\-tracking mechanisms are part of the equation, it is shown that data quality verification coverage reaches 98\.4% for completeness and 99\.1% for timeliness dimensions\. The economic impact is measured as annual savings of more than USD 9\.8 million for hyperscale operators\. The results highlight that as of 2020, federated, decentralized observability planes are the architected evolution needed for production\-grade data pipelines and best co\-designed with zero\-downtime load\-balancing strategies\.

## [Beyond Physical Performance: Integrating the Psychology of Religion, Embodied Cognition, and Psychospiritual Development in Athletic Achievement](../publications/4ea88f8968149e79c45a.md)

Karadağ Erdal

Athletic achievement is commonly evaluated through competition results, yet the processes that sustain participation, learning, bodily adaptation, identity, and psychological well\-being extend beyond physical performance\. This critical integrative narrative review develops a research framework linking psychology of religion, grounded and embodied cognition, and psychospiritual development in sport\. It differentiates religious affiliation from situation\-specific coping, bodily signal detection from interpretation, and developmental change from short\-term performance fluctuations\. Published scholarship on religion and spirituality in sport, meaning\-making, self\-determination, interoception, resilience, and athlete mental health provides the conceptual foundation\. The proposed context\-meaning\-embodiment\-development framework describes conditional paths from personal values and social environments through bodily appraisal, motivated action, reflection, and longer\-term adaptation\. Its potential benefits include coherent purpose, flexible coping, and sustained participation; adverse pathways include spiritual struggle, externally imposed identity, compulsive ritual, and delayed health care\. No new participants, original empirical results, meta\-analytic estimates, or validated assessment instrument are presented\. The article proposes preregistered longitudinal and mixed\-method investigations incorporating repeated observations, comparisons with secular meaning systems, carefully defined behavioral and performance outcomes, measurement\-equivalence checks, and athlete autonomy safeguards\. The current evidence supports examination of these interacting domains but cannot establish a unique causal contribution of religious belief to sporting success\. A scientifically useful account must demonstrate incremental explanatory value, remain open to null findings, and preserve the distinction between excellence, well\-being, and personal meaning\. psychology of religion; embodied cognition; psychospiritual development; athletic achievement; interoception; athlete well\-being

## [In\-Context Preference\-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data](../publications/4ed844d7eed80dce42f6.md)

Yiming Yao; Liang Zhao; Qingfu Zhang

Multi\-objective optimization involves diverse preferences over conflicting objectives\. Rather than returning a finite set of trade\-off solutions, preference\-conditioned Pareto set learning seeks to map a specified preference directly to a corresponding Pareto optimal solution\. Yet in many real\-world scenarios, optimization must proceed offline without further objective evaluations, leaving only a limited static dataset that sparsely covers the decision and objective spaces\. Existing methods either optimize separately for each preference or train a problem\-specific Pareto solution model, requiring repeated search across preferences or repeated training across problems\. We introduce in\-context preference\-conditioned Pareto set learning \(ICPSL\), a framework that amortizes both preference\-wise solution search and problem\-specific model construction\. ICPSL pretrains a foundation\-style hypernetwork on a large and diverse set of synthetic prior data\. Given the offline observations of an unseen problem, the pretrained hypernetwork learns to generate a problem\-specific, preference\-conditioned Pareto solution model in a single forward pass\. The generated model can then be reused to predict solutions for arbitrary preferences without problem\-specific training or preference\-wise search\. Experiments on synthetic and real\-world problems show that ICPSL produces high\-quality Pareto solutions while providing substantial speedups in problem\-specific solution\-model construction\.

## [Emerging Frontiers in Medical Research: A Review of Precision Medicine, Digital Health, and Translational Technologies](../publications/4ede4e6e53d10c78fe05.md)

Murugan Sri Ram

Medical research is increasingly integrating biological, clinical, environmental, and behavioral information to support personalized and preventive healthcare\. Advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\), multi\-omics, digital health, wearable biosensors, microbiome science, liquid biopsy, organoid technology, regenerative medicine, and nanomedicine are expanding opportunities to investigate disease mechanisms and develop individualized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies\. This review examines these emerging approaches, their potential applications, and the challenges affecting their translation into clinical practice\. Multi\-omics integrates molecular information across biological layers to characterize disease heterogeneity, while AI facilitates the analysis of complex datasets for diagnosis, drug discovery, surveillance, and clinical decision support\. Digital health platforms and wearable sensors enable longitudinal monitoring beyond conventional healthcare settings, potentially supporting earlier recognition of clinically relevant changes\. Liquid biopsy offers minimally invasive access to circulating biomarkers, particularly in oncology, whereas organoids provide experimental models for investigating tissue biology, disease processes, and treatment responses\. Microbiome research, regenerative approaches, and nanomedicine offer further avenues for understanding host–microbial interactions, restoring tissue function, and improving therapeutic delivery\. Despite these opportunities, implementation remains constrained by variable data quality, limited reproducibility, interoperability barriers, privacy concerns, regulatory uncertainty, cost, and unequal access\. Prospective clinical validation, transparent reporting, appropriate ethical oversight, and interdisciplinary collaboration are essential to establish clinical utility\. Integrating these approaches may strengthen exploratory and translational research, provided that technological innovation is accompanied by robust evidence of patient benefit\.

## [Assessing and Predicting Ecological Quality Using a Novel Indicator and Machine Learning Framework: A Case Study of Beijing](../publications/4ee8ef075b39a099a922.md)

Zhao Haiyue; Zhu Jianning; Li Sha; Ji Yuanfeng; Gao Jiayi; Sun Shibo; Tingting Huang

Ecological quality is a comprehensive concept that reflects the overall condition of an ecosystem\. Understanding its dynamic evolution and future trajectories is essential for sustainable ecosystem management\. However, existing studies often rely on single\-dimensional perspectives and overlook ecosystem complexity, nonlinear relationships, and interactions among drivers\. Therefore, this study developed a novel ecological quality indicator based on a “function–status–disturbance” framework integrating ecosystem services, the Remote Sensing Ecological Index, the Modified Water Area Remote Sensing Ecological Index, and nighttime light intensity\. We quantified the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological quality in Beijing from 2000 to 2020\. Correlation analysis was used to select ten significant environmental and socioeconomic drivers from eleven candidate variables\. A Random Forest model incorporating the ten drivers predicted ecological quality under three representative SSP–RCP scenarios for 2035\. Permutation importance based on the percentage increase in mean squared error and partial dependence analysis were used to quantify the relative importance, nonlinear responses, and threshold effects of drivers\. The results showed that \(1\) ecological quality in Beijing exhibited a three\-tier concentric gradient pattern, increasing from the urban center to the northwestern mountains\. \(2\) Ecological quality declined overall from 2000 to 2020, particularly during the first decade\. \(3\) The Random Forest model showed high predictive accuracy, with an R 2 of 0\.979, an MAE of 0\.029 and an RMSE of 0\.041\. Among the three scenarios in 2035, the ecological protection scenario exhibited the highest ecological quality, followed by the middle path and baseline scenarios, but all remained below the 2020 level\. \(4\) Ecosystem responses varied substantially across scenarios\. Natural ecosystems performed best under the ecological protection scenario, whereas cultivated land showed the opposite pattern, with the baseline scenario achieving the highest quality\. \(5\) Annual precipitation and distance to regional centers were the most influential drivers, and most factors exhibited nonlinear and threshold effects\. These findings provide scientific support for adaptive ecosystem management and sustainable urban planning\.

## [How Can Access to Justice in Criminal Proceedings Be Improved in Lithuania? Reforming Effective Defence, Lay Participation and Language Rights](../publications/4eeaebed5808436ad3e6.md)

Vladimir Komarnickiy

Background: Access to justice in criminal proceedings, understood here as the effective ability of victims, suspects, and defendants to assert their position and to be protected against wrongful conviction, is bound up with the right to a fair trial under Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights \(ECHR\)\. Although the Republic of Lithuania ranks highly in international rule\-of\-law assessments and its Code of Criminal Procedure already secures numerous guarantees, practice reveals persistent gaps in the functional \(procedural\) dimension of that right, effective defence, equality of arms and effective participation\. Against the background of the contested 2023 reform proposals, this article asks how these procedural guarantees can be strengthened\. Method: The study applies doctrinal \(formal\-legal\), comparative\-legal, historical, and functional methods\. It analyses the Lithuanian Code of Criminal Procedure, Article 6 ECHR, and European Court of Human Rights case law\. It conducts a functional comparison with selected jurisdictions \(Germany, England and Wales, Denmark, the United States, Malta, Ireland, Argentina, and the Russian Federation\), chosen and justified in the methodology based on comparability of fair\-trial standards and transferability to the Lithuanian model\. Results and Conclusions: We advance four proposals: \(1\) an automated, randomised system for appointing state\-funded defence counsel; \(2\) reintroducing the \(non\-advocate\) public defender acting alongside a professional attorney, reframed by reference to modern analogues such as the English McKenzie friend and the German Beistand; \(3\) introducing trial by jury, at the defendant’s request, for serious offences; and \(4\) strengthening the interpreter’s role and the right to use one’s native language, including electronic delivery and self\-service translation of the case file\. The distinctive contribution lies less in restating the well\-known risks of prosecution\-influenced defence than in combining these measures, in particular the automated assignment system and the digital handling of language rights, into an integrated and transferable reform package, tested against the principal counter\-arguments, including the objection that lay participation is alien to the Lithuanian legal tradition\.

## [Kalite Algısının Küresel Marka İmajına Etkisinde Yerel Marka İmajının Aracılığı](../publications/4eec1f0c030070f3b6da.md)

Murat Alkın; Nurdan Kuşat

Çalışma, kalite algısının küresel marka imajı üzerindeki etkisini ve bu ilişkide yerel marka imajının aracılık rolünü incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırma, Türkiye’nin önemli üretim ve ihracat merkezlerinden biri olan Denizli’de faaliyet gösteren ihracatçı işletmeler bağlamında yürütülmüştür\. Bu çerçevede çalışma, Denizli’nin küresel pazarlardaki genel konumunu ölçmekten ziyade, işletme temsilcilerinin kalite algısı, yerel marka imajı ve küresel marka imajına ilişkin değerlendirmeleri arasındaki ilişkileri analiz etmektedir\. Araştırmanın örneklemini Denizli ihracat sektöründe faaliyet gösteren 510 işletme temsilcisi oluşturmaktadır\. Veriler anket yöntemiyle toplanmış ve yapısal eşitlik modellemesi \(YEM\) yöntemiyle analiz edilmiştir\. Analizler R programı kullanılarak gerçekleştirilmiştir\. Bulgular, kalite algısının hem yerel marka imajı hem de küresel marka imajı üzerinde anlamlı ve pozitif bir etkisinin bulunduğunu göstermektedir\. Ayrıca yerel marka imajının küresel marka imajı üzerinde anlamlı ve pozitif bir etkisi olduğu belirlenmiştir\. Bulgular, kalite algısının küresel marka imajı üzerindeki etkisinde yerel marka imajının aracılık rolü üstlendiğini ortaya koymaktadır\. Bu sonuçlar, ihracatçı işletmelerin uluslararası pazarlarda olumlu marka algısı oluşturabilmeleri için yalnızca ürün ve hizmet kalitesine değil, aynı zamanda faaliyet gösterdikleri yerel bağlamın marka imajına da önem vermeleri gerektiğini göstermektedir\. Çalışma, ihracat sektörü özelinde kalite algısı, yerel marka imajı ve küresel marka imajı arasındaki ilişkileri birlikte ele alması bakımından ilgili literatüre katkı sunmaktadır\.

## [Transforming Panchakarma with AI: The Future of Precision Ayurveda](../publications/4ef680a216126839cc61.md)

Mohita Bohra; Akshay Verma

Panchakarma is a key element of Ayurvedic medicine with proven benefits for prevention and treatment\. Various Panchakarma procedures rely on the skill, physical strength and consistency of the therapists\. Variations in the way therapists perform their manual techniques can affect the clinical outcome of the treatment being provided\. The introduction of automation and robotics into the practice of Panchakarma is a new avenue that has the potential to address these limitations; offering greater precision, reproducibility, safety and operational efficiency\. Some examples of possible innovations include robotic massage systems that can replicate the standardized massage techniques used in Ayurveda, automated massage tables that are equipped for Swedana therapies such as Pottali Swedana, AI \(Artificial Intelligence\) driven dispensing systems that can provide controlled dosing of oil to the patient during Abhyanga treatments, and sensor\-laden monitoring systems that can continuously monitor the physiological parameters of the patient and allow for real\-time modification of their treatment\. Integration of AI with conventional Panchakarma can help in maintaining the authenticity of Ayurvedic therapies while improving standardization, accessibility, scalability and quality of care\. This can help in modernizing Panchakarma without losing its basic therapeutic principles\.\. 1, Dr 2

## [Bridging SCADA Noise and Real\-Time Field Alerts: A Comparative Benchmarking of Machine Learning and Lightweight Time\-Series Models for Oilfield Pipeline Anomaly Detection](../publications/4f0508d0a31dfbbb5867.md)

Philemon Kelechi Emeka

Unplanned flow disruptions, severe scale accumulation, and pressure anomalies in offshore oil and gas production pipelines cost the energy sector millions of dollars in operational downtime and present severe environmental hazards\. Traditional SCADA monitoring systems rely heavily on static single\-variable thresholds that trigger frequent false alarms during routine transient flow shifts, creating alarm fatigue for control\-room operators\. Conversely, while complex deep learning architectures can capture non\-linear multi\-sensor relationships, their high computational overhead and black\-box nature pose severe challenges for real\-time edge deployment on remote production platforms\. This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking framework evaluating classical machine learning models \(Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM\) against lightweight temporal sequence architectures \(LSTM Autoencoders\) using Petrobras&\#x27;s open\-source 3W dataset\. Sensor streams including Permanent Downhole Gauge pressure \(P\_PDG\), Temperature and Pressure Transducer measurements \(P\_TPT, T\_TPT\), and choke downstream temperature \(T\_JUS\-CK\) were preprocessed using rolling statistical lag windows and class\-weight balancing\. Our empirical results demonstrate that gradient\-boosted decision trees \(XGBoost/LightGBM\) paired with 15\-second statistical lag features achieved a Macro F1\-score of 0\.914 and a PR\-AUC of 0\.932, outperforming the LSTM Autoencoder \(Macro F1: 0\.876\) while reducing inference latency by 78% \(12\.4 ms vs 56\.2 ms per sample\)\. These findings show that lightweight ensemble learning offers a highly effective, low\-latency strategy for real\-time pipeline integrity monitoring\.

## [CF\-AVSS: A Coarse\-to\-Fine Audio\-Visual Speech Separation Framework with Target\-Speaker Refinement and Post\-Fusion for Real\-World AVSE Challenge](../publications/4f083ebedb0455d10b26.md)

Longjie Luo; Zhongshu Hou; Yuepeng Li; Gang Yang; Shidong Shang; Fan Zhou

Audio\-visual speech enhancement \(AVSE\) leverages visual cues to recover target speech from mixtures corrupted by reverberation, noise, and overlapping speakers\. We propose a coarse\-to\-fine two\-stage AVSE framework\. In the first stage, a progressive SPAV\-TFGridNet is extended to two synchronized visual streams to produce visually ordered coarse estimates by progressively suppressing interfering speech while preserving target reverberation and shared background noise\. In the second stage, a TFGridNet\-based target speaker refinement network takes the original mixture and both coarse estimates as input to further recover target speech and improve signal quality\. The coarse and refined estimates are finally combined using development\-set\-calibrated fusion\. On the ISCSLP 2026 Real\-World AVSE Challenge, our system tied for first place on Track 1 and ranked second on Track 2 in OVRL, while achieving the lowest CER on both tracks at 12\.31% and 14\.79%, respectively\.

## [COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF MACHINE LEARNING AND DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR WEATHER PREDICTION IN NIGERIA USING SPATIAL ANALYSIS](../publications/4f08bde5fe952b3e751b.md)

Oladoyin Idris Atolagbe; Tayo Peter Ogundunmade

Accurate prediction of meteorological variables is essential for agricultural planning, disaster risk reduction, water resource management, and climate adaptation in Nigeria, where substantial climatic variability exists across diverse ecological zones\. This study presents a comparative evaluation of machine learning, deep learning, and spatial analysis techniques for predicting key meteorological variables, namely rainfall, temperature, and relative humidity, using a nationwide daily dataset comprising 270,285 observations collected across the 36 states of Nigeria between 2005 and 2024\. Following comprehensive data pre\-processing, spatial feature engineering was performed by incorporating geographic coordinates and spatial lag variables\. Global Moran&\#x27;s I statistics confirmed significant positive spatial autocorrelation for rainfall, temperature, and humidity, providing empirical justification for integrating spatial information into the predictive models\. Five regression models: Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(Bi\-LSTM\), and Transformer were developed and evaluated using a chronological train\-test split\. Model performance was assessed using Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\), Root Mean Square Error \(RMSE\), the coefficient of determination \(R²\), confidence intervals, and statistical comparison of prediction errors using the Diebold\-Mariano test\. An ablation study was further conducted to quantify the contribution of spatial features\. Results demonstrated that the Transformer model achieved the best predictive performance \(MAE = 1\.87 mm, RMSE = 3\.98 mm, R² = 0\.78\), representing approximately a 19% improvement in RMSE over the best\-performing machine learning model \(XGBoost\)\. The ablation study showed that incorporating spatial features reduced RMSE by between 3\.8% and 8\.4% across all models, with the Transformer exhibiting the greatest improvement\. The findings demonstrate that combining deep learning with spatial analysis substantially enhances weather prediction across Nigeria and provides a robust framework for supporting climate resilience, agricultural decision\-making, and operational weather forecasting\.

## [DAMP: bridging mechanotransduction and immune responses in tendinopathy](../publications/4f0cf276974ab2cf4a45.md)

Hongjun Zheng; Shihua Gao; Zhuangfeng Weng

Tendinopathy is increasingly recognized as a chronic degenerative disorder driven by sterile inflammation, where persistent mechanical stress and dysregulated innate immunity converge to disrupt tissue homeostasis\. Damage\-associated molecular patterns \(DAMPs\), released from stressed or injured tenocytes and resident immune cells, serve as key mediators translating mechanical overload into sustained inflammatory responses\. Their persistent release perpetuates inflammation, extracellular matrix disorganization, and impaired tissue repair, thereby establishing a self\-sustaining cycle of degeneration\. Recent studies have highlighted DAMPs as central regulators in the initiation and maintenance of tendon inflammation, reflecting an intricate interplay between mechanical cues, metabolic stress, and immune dysfunction\. This review summarizes current understanding of DAMP\-mediated mechanisms in tendinopathy, emphasizing their roles in inflammation, fibrosis, and tissue remodeling\. We also discuss the therapeutic implications of modulating DAMP\-driven signaling pathways to restore immune homeostasis and promote regenerative healing\. A clearer understanding of these immunomechanical interactions provides a foundational framework for developing mechanism\-based treatments that target the underlying causes of tendinopathy\.

## [Structure\-activity relationship and molecular docking insights into newly synthesized Quinoline derivatives](../publications/4f1403df6753774b7ac4.md)

Ashwani Gaud; Prem Shankar Gupta

Quinoline derivatives received much interest for the development of antidiabetic drugs because of to their diverse biological activities and structural flexibility\. In this work, a novel series of quinoline based compounds were synthesised and characterised by different spectroscopic techniques\. The structural modifications were purposefully done to evaluate their structure\-activity relationship \(SAR\) in order to improve their antidiabetic action\. We done molecular docking analyses of the main antidiabetic targets, which were α\-glucosidase, to study the binding and interaction of them with other\. Inhibition of alpha\-glycosidase, a major therapeutic target for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, is an efficient approach to reduce postprandial hyperglycaemia by enhancing the digestion of carbohydrates in the small intestine\. Docking studies revealed significant binding interactions of several drugs with key amino acid residues of the active sites, indicating significant inhibitory potential\. The structure\-activity relationship analysis revealed that substitutions at key positions of the quinoline ring significantly influenced the binding affinity and orientation within the target proteins\. Moreover, in silico ADMET and drug\-likeness investigations showed that the most active derivatives have good pharmacokinetic properties and low projected toxicity\. The results indicate the possibility of quinoline based structure in the development of new antidiabetic medicines and provide a strong basis for further in vitro and in vivo studies\. Keywords: Quinoline, SAR, ADME, type 2 diabetes, Docking study

## [Probing severe cognitive impairment in treatment resistant schizophrenia: a proof\-of\-concept in vivo study with \(18F\)\-Flutemetamol PET](../publications/4f15bf748458e6ca51ef.md)

Mariateresa Ciccarelli; Valeria Gaudieri; Benedetta Mazza; Annarita Barone; Felice Iasevoli; Licia Vellucci; Giuseppe De Simone; Alberto Cuocolo; Sabina Pappatà; Andrea de Bartolomeis

Abstract Treatment\-resistant schizophrenia \(TRS\) affects almost 30% of patients with the disorder\. This condition is associated with functional impairment and has been suggested to have a putatively different neurobiology compared to non\-treatment\-resistant schizophrenia\. One striking feature of TRS is the presence of relevant cognitive deficits, which, in many cases, align with a Mild Cognitive Impairment \(MCI\)‑like clinical profile without implying amyloid\-β \(Aβ\) pathology\. Conversely, aspects of MCI partially overlap with the trajectory of schizophrenia, motivating investigation of putative common factors of convergence\. Despite its relevance, in vivo data directly addressing this question are lacking\. We used ¹⁸\(F\)\-Flutemetamol Positron Emission Tomography \(PET\) to investigate regional cortical Aβ deposition and its potential association with clinical symptoms in patients with TRS with MCI‑like cognitive impairment \(TRS\-MCI\)\. TRS\-MCI \( n = 12\) underwent a PET scan and clinical evaluation, including the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale \(PANSS\) and the Brief Assessment of Cognition in Schizophrenia \(BACS\)\. PET image analysis was performed using the Diagnosis ORIented ANalysis software, which provides different semiquantitative indices of regional cortical Aβ PET measures\. PET data obtained in TRS\-MCI were compared with those of amyloid\-negative cognitively impaired patients \(Aβ\- CI\) without psychiatric disorders \( n = 12\)\. Group‑level comparisons using expert visual assessment and semi‑automated quantification showed no significant differences\. Exploratory correlation within TRS‑MCI revealed a negative association between the regional Aβ composite scores in the Right Parietal Cortex and the PANSS Positive score \( P ≤ 0\.01\)\. This pilot study found no evidence of increased cortical Aβ deposition in TRS patients; nevertheless, regional variation in Parietal Cortex \( 18 F\)‑Flutemetamol PET signal within the Aβ‑negative range was associated with positive symptoms, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts\.

## [Artificial intelligence literacy, artificial intelligence anxiety, and career optimism among university music students: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/4f2558747046eabe1c6f.md)

Yang Du

Objective To examine the levels of artificial intelligence \(AI\) literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism among university music students, their associations, and the independent associations of AI literacy and AI anxiety with career optimism after adjustment for relevant background factors\. Methods A cross\-sectional survey was conducted from May to July 2026 among students from five undergraduate music institutions in eastern China using convenience sampling\. A total of 453 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis\. Participants completed the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Chinese College Students \(AILS\-CCS\), the Chinese version of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale \(AIAS\), and the Career Optimism Subscale \(COS\)\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent\-samples t tests , one\-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple linear regression\. Results Mean scores for AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism were 52\.97 ± 10\.05, 83\.85 ± 22\.96, and 37\.87 ± 8\.02, respectively\. Students with prior AI training and those reporting more frequent AI use showed higher AI literacy and career optimism and lower AI anxiety\. AI literacy was positively associated with career optimism \(r = 0\.444, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas AI anxiety was negatively associated with career optimism \(r = −0\.461, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. After adjustment for gender, year of study, music specialization, prior AI training, and frequency of AI use, AI literacy remained positively associated with career optimism \(β = 0\.314, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas AI anxiety remained negatively associated with career optimism \(β = −0\.326, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The final model explained 33\.0% of the variance in career optimism\. Conclusion AI literacy and AI anxiety were independently associated with career optimism among university music students\. These findings suggest that students&\#x27; perceptions of AI\-related competence and technological concerns are relevant to their career expectations\. Music institutions may consider AI education that combines practical competence with critical understanding of AI&\#x27;s implications for artistic identity, professional value, and future career development\. Future longitudinal research is needed to clarify the temporal relationships among AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism\.

## [From Indenture to Electronics: Brokered Labor Regimes in Johor, Malaysia](../publications/4f27b97758b90b9b88c1.md)

DAVIDE BLOTTA

Abstract This article develops the concept of a brokered dormitory labor regime \(BDLR\) to analyze Johor, Malaysia’s electrical and electronics export\-processing zones, where debt\-financed recruitment, deceptive contracting, and restricted mobility synchronize labor turnover with the accelerating demand for semiconductor manufacturing driven by artificial intelligence\. Two intermediaries, the labor agent and the kadar, secure this synchronization by controlling workers’ social reproduction\. Tracing this regime’s genealogy to the nineteenth\-century kangani and kangchu systems in the Straits Settlements, the article argues that the BDLR reactivates a colonial infrastructure of coerced migrant labor, revealing a recurring pattern of asynchronous synchronization between capital and labor across successive industrial revolutions\.

## [Data\-Driven Prediction of Optimal MPI Rank Placement and Node Count for Memory\-Bound CFD on AMD EPYC Clusters](../publications/4f38a17a4f5811e61881.md)

Marcin Lawenda; Łukasz Szustak; Aleksandra Krasicka

Users who run a memory\-bound OpenFOAM case on an AMD EPYC cluster must decide how many nodes to use and how many MPI ranks to place on each core complex\. The fastest choice is often not the cheapest one\. This paper revisits our earlier analytical model of this performance and energy trade\-off with 560 measured configurations of the motorBike case on five Zen 4 and Zen 5 EPYC processors, including socket power from processor telemetry\. On up to four nodes, small meshes are both fastest and cheapest on a single node on most processors\. For the largest mesh the largest node count is both the fastest and the cheapest option, because its speedup is superlinear\. A genuine trade\-off arises only for medium meshes, where full speed costs a median of 20 to 97% more node hours than the cheapest option\. The L3 miss rate and the halo traffic per cell are consistent with this pattern\. For a new mesh of the same case, the configuration that was optimal on the nearest measured mesh is near optimal in 75 to 85% of the decisions\. Running the two configurations it recommends for speed and for cost raises this share to 85 to 90% for runtime and node hours and determines the trade\-off with median errors of 3 to 5 percentage points\. Neither gradient boosted trees trained on the same data nor the earlier polynomial model improves on this simple procedure\.

## [The Kuramoto–Tsuzuki equation: Invariant theory, bifurcation, chaotic behavior, and sensitivity analysis](../publications/4f3d16ef9a438b694b19.md)

Mir Sajjad Hashemi; Mushtaq K\. Abd Al\-Rahem; Mohammad Esmael Samei; KAMYAR HOSSEINI; Mustafa Bayram

This paper investigates the Kuramoto–Tsuzuki equation through the application of the Lie symmetry method\. We derive three Lie algebra generators pertinent to this equation, facilitating a transformation that reduces the partial differential equation to an ordinary differential equation\. One of the reduced ordinary differential equations is solved analytically using Nucci’s reduction method\. The second reduced ordinary differential equation, derived from a combination of generators, is solved directly by some manipulations\. Then we use a transformation to convert the Kuramoto–Tsuzuki equation into a second\-order nonlinear ordinary differential equation\. Utilizing a recently introduced technique, the second\-degree generalized Abel equation method, we successfully obtain soliton solutions for the reduced ordinary differential equation\. Additionally, we explore bifurcation phenomena and analyze phase portraits, providing deeper insights into the dynamic behavior of the system\. The analysis of chaotic behavior and sensitivity of the corresponding dynamical system contributes to a better understanding of the Kuramoto–Tsuzuki equation and highlights the effectiveness of the proposed methods for analyzing complex nonlinear equations\.

## [बकग एव वततय कषतर म कतरम बदधमतत: अवसर, चनतय एव भवषय क सभवनए](../publications/4f413e58d73e121869fe.md)

डॉ\. विभा पाण्डेय

सारांश कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence—AI\) वर्तमान डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था में बैंकिंग एवं वित्तीय क्षेत्र के परिवर्तन का एक महत्त्वपूर्ण माध्यम बनकर उभर रही है। बैंकिंग संस्थाएँ प्रतिदिन बड़ी मात्रा में ग्राहकों, लेन\-देन, ऋण, निवेश, बाजार तथा जोखिम से संबंधित आँकड़ों का प्रसंस्करण करती हैं। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता इन विशाल आँकड़ों का तीव्र एवं व्यवस्थित विश्लेषण करके वित्तीय संस्थानों को बेहतर निर्णय लेने, ग्राहक सेवाओं को व्यक्तिगत आवश्यकताओं के अनुरूप बनाने, धोखाधड़ी की पहचान करने, ऋण जोखिम का आकलन करने, परिचालन लागत कम करने तथा नियामकीय अनुपालन को अधिक प्रभावी बनाने में सहायता करती है। मशीन लर्निंग, डीप लर्निंग, प्राकृतिक भाषा प्रसंस्करण \(Natural Language Processing—NLP\), रोबोटिक प्रोसेस ऑटोमेशन \(Robotic Process Automation—RPA\) तथा जनरेटिव AI जैसी तकनीकों का उपयोग बैंकिंग क्षेत्र में तेजी से बढ़ रहा है। इन तकनीकों के माध्यम से ग्राहक सेवा, डिजिटल भुगतान, क्रेडिट स्कोरिंग, धोखाधड़ी नियंत्रण, जोखिम प्रबंधन, साइबर सुरक्षा तथा नियामकीय अनुपालन जैसे क्षेत्रों में महत्त्वपूर्ण परिवर्तन संभव हो रहे हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, AI आधारित प्रणालियाँ वित्तीय सेवाओं की गति, सटीकता और उपलब्धता में सुधार लाने तथा ग्राहकों के अनुभव को बेहतर बनाने में योगदान दे सकती हैं। हालाँकि, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता अनेक अवसर प्रदान करती है, लेकिन इसके साथ डेटा गोपनीयता, साइबर सुरक्षा, एल्गोरिदमिक पक्षपात, मॉडल जोखिम, निर्णयों की पारदर्शिता, रोजगार के स्वरूप में बदलाव तथा कुछ तकनीकी प्रदाताओं पर अत्यधिक निर्भरता जैसी चुनौतियाँ भी जुड़ी हुई हैं। विशेष रूप से वित्तीय क्षेत्र में AI आधारित निर्णयों की त्रुटियाँ केवल व्यक्तिगत ग्राहकों को ही प्रभावित नहीं करतीं, बल्कि व्यापक स्तर पर वित्तीय संस्थानों के संचालन और वित्तीय स्थिरता के लिए भी जोखिम उत्पन्न कर सकती हैं। इसलिए AI के उपयोग में उचित निगरानी, जवाबदेही और जोखिम प्रबंधन आवश्यक हैं। प्रस्तुत शोध\-पत्र का उद्देश्य बैंकिंग एवं वित्तीय क्षेत्र में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता की अवधारणा, इसके प्रमुख उपयोगों, अवसरों, चुनौतियों, भारतीय संदर्भ, रोजगार एवं कौशल विकास, नैतिक और नियामकीय पहलुओं तथा भविष्य की संभावनाओं का अध्ययन करना है। अध्ययन का निष्कर्ष है कि कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता को मानवीय विशेषज्ञता के पूर्ण विकल्प के रूप में देखने के बजाय मानव और तकनीक के सहयोग के माध्यम के रूप में विकसित करना अधिक उपयोगी हो सकता है। उचित नियमन, डेटा संरक्षण, पारदर्शिता, तकनीकी दक्षता और मानवीय निगरानी के साथ AI का उपयोग अधिक सुरक्षित, कुशल, समावेशी तथा ग्राहक\-केंद्रित वित्तीय व्यवस्था के निर्माण में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा सकता है। मुख्य शब्द: कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता, बैंकिंग, वित्तीय क्षेत्र, मशीन लर्निंग, डिजिटल भुगतान, धोखाधड़ी नियंत्रण, जोखिम प्रबंधन, साइबर सुरक्षा, वित्तीय समावेशन, नियामकीय अनुपालन।

## [Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Analysis of Stone‐Column‐Reinforced Composite Foundations Constrained by Static Load Tests](../publications/4f5b67c53b7607f2e912.md)

Fei Wang; Huijun Qi; Li Yuan; Shiyang Pan; Chenbo zhao; Tongchun Li; Qiankun Liu

ABSTRACT Accurate identification of constitutive parameters for stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundations is essential for deformation analysis and settlement prediction of clay‐core rockfill dams\. However, the parameters of the Duncan‐Chang model are difficult to determine directly under field conditions, whereas conventional inversion methods relying on repeated finite element \(FE\) analyses are computationally expensive\. To address this issue, this study proposes a surrogate‐assisted parameter inversion framework constrained by static load tests in the stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundation of a planned clay‐core rockfill dam in Rwanda\. Response samples under staged loading were generated using FE simulations, and a surrogate model was introduced into the inversion loop as a computational substitute for repeated FE analyses, thereby improving inversion efficiency\. By jointly calibrating settlement responses under multiple load levels, the Duncan‐Chang model parameters governing the overall load‐settlement behaviour of the composite foundation were identified\. Furthermore, uncertainty analysis was conducted for a representative test column to obtain the posterior distributions of the key parameters and the parameter‐induced posterior prediction intervals of the load‐settlement response\. The identified parameters were further validated through FE back‐analysis and dam‐scale settlement prediction\. The results show that the proposed framework can satisfactorily reproduce the load‐settlement response observed in static load tests while substantially reducing the computational cost\. This study demonstrates that surrogate‐assisted parameter inversion constrained by static load tests provides a practical and robust approach for parameter identification in stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundations, while maintaining a favourable balance between efficiency and engineering applicability\.

## [Rusfertide for Polycythemia Vera: Incremental Benefit Assessment](../publications/4f5f50794e42b516b384.md)

Ayalew Tefferi; Naseema Gangat; Paola Guglielmelli; Alessandro Maria Vannucchi; Tiziano Barbui

Rusfertide mechanism of action and clinical trial results in polycythemia vera\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN THE NIGERIA CUSTOMS SERVICE: ASSESSING DIGITAL READINESS, EFFICIENCY GAINS, AND DATA INFRASTRUCTURE](../publications/4f634650549fb1a16ef2.md)

AKANO ISAAC; Ph\.D G\. O\. Omojefe; Ph\.D Bosco Itoro Ekpenyong

Abstract This study examined the adoption of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-driven technologies and their implications for operational efficiency, transparency, and data\-management systems within the Nigeria Customs Service \(NCS\)\. Specifically, it assessed the level of AI adoption, determined the extent to which AI influences customs efficiency and cargo clearance processes, and evaluated the adequacy of existing data\-management infrastructure supporting AI deployment\. The study adopted a descriptive quantitative research design, drawing data from a structured questionnaire administered to 500–600 customs officers selected through stratified random sampling across major customs formations in Nigeria\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and inferential techniques, including regression analysis and chi\-square tests\. Findings revealed that AI adoption within the NCS is at a moderate but developing stage, characterised by partial integration of digital systems and uneven deployment across operational units\. Results further showed that AI\-driven technologies moderately enhance operational efficiency, improve cargo clearance speed, and strengthen transparency, although these gains remain constrained by institutional and infrastructural limitations\. The study also found that existing data\-management systems are only moderately adequate, with significant weaknesses in data integration, staff capacity, and system interoperability, despite relatively stronger performance in data security\. The study concludes that while AI adoption is yielding measurable improvements in customs operations, its full potential remains limited by weak data infrastructure and incomplete institutional readiness\. Strengthening data governance, enhancing digital capacity, and expanding AI integration are therefore critical for achieving full customs modernisation in Nigeria\. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Customs Modernisation, Operational Efficiency, Data Management Systems, Nigeria Customs Service\.

## [Mitigating Creep Anisotropy and Enhancing Performance in Additively Manufactured Ni‐Based Superalloys: A Review](../publications/4f649b3f87b767645e1c.md)

C\. Anil Kumar; Shobhit Pratap Singh; Gaurav Mohanty; Surendra Kumar Makineni

Additive manufacturing \(AM\) has emerged as a highly versatile technique for producing near‐net‐shape components with minimal material waste and significantly reduced processing time\. The AM processing of superalloys introduces complex thermal histories that result in heterogeneous microstructures, leading to pronounced anisotropy in mechanical performance, particularly under creep conditions\. The key microstructural features that control anisotropy are columnar grain morphology, crystallographic texture, transverse grain boundaries, elemental segregation and localized precipitation that govern anisotropic creep resistance\. Strategies to mitigate anisotropy and enhance creep resistance have been proposed, including process parameter optimization, thermomechanical treatments, powder chemistry control, oxide dispersion strengthening, and reactive additive manufacturing\. With targeted processing and posttreatment strategies, it is possible to engineer AM superalloys with creep performance comparable to or exceeding that of wrought and cast counterparts\. This article provides an effective set of strategies for developing creep‐resistant AM superalloys optimized for high‐temperature applications\.

## [Assessing the ability of a stretched‐grid deep‐learning weather prediction model to capture physical balances](../publications/4f66d4f313546b40eeff.md)

Francesco Pasquini; Michiel Baatsen; Bastien François; Natalie Theeuwes; Maurice J\. Schmeits

Abstract Weather forecasting has traditionally relied on numerical weather prediction \(NWP\) models, which simulate weather by solving the governing fluid equations\. Recently, the emergence of deep learning weather prediction \(DLWP\) models has opened a new era in weather forecasting, offering a data‐driven alternative to classical NWP approaches\. Regional DLWP models, such as the stretched‐grid model Bris developed by Met Norway, have demonstrated performance on par with or even slightly better than regional NWP models across a range of standard forecast metrics\. By overcoming the coarse horizontal resolution that constrained earlier global data‐driven models, the operational use of regional DLWP systems now appears increasingly promising\. Nevertheless, the performance of such models during extreme events is generally inferior to that of regional NWP models, and comprehensive evaluations of their ability to generate physically realistic forecasts are still lacking\. Here, we present a study comparing the physical consistency of the deterministic version of Bris with the control run of the operational MetCoOp Ensemble Prediction System \(MEPS\) in forecasting the severe extratropical cyclone Poly , which hit the Netherlands on July 5, 2023\. We examine whether Bris represents deviations from key atmospheric balances accurately and whether it reproduces the expected dynamics of the storm\. We show that, despite its relatively good performance in terms of root mean square error, Bris struggles to capture important mesoscale features of the event and disrupts several atmospheric balances significantly\. This unrealistic disruption is linked mainly to the fine‐scale noise evidenced in its output fields, which leads to incorrect and unrealistic spatial gradients\. These results raise critical questions about improving artificial‐intelligence‐based models to represent extreme events better and how to ensure physical consistency in their predictions\.

## [STUDI FENOMENOLOGI PENGGUNAAN GADGET YANG MEMPENGARUHI KONSENTRASI BELAJAR DAN KECAKAPAN SOSIAL MURID KELAS XI SMA](../publications/4f715f8c6159f03c0628.md)

Amalia Khoirunnisa; Devy Probowati; Zafifatuz Zuhriyah

The prevalence of digital distractions has created numerous challenges, particularly regarding gadget usage\. Uncontrolled gadget use can impact students&\#x27; learning concentration and social skills\. This study aims to describe the experiences of Grade XI MCA students at SMAN 4 Malang regarding gadget usage and its effects on their learning concentration and social skills\. A qualitative approach utilizing the phenomenological method was employed\. The study participants consisted of five Grade XI MCA students \(as primary informants\) and one guidance counselor \(as a supporting informant\)\. Data collection involved interviews, observation, and documentation, while data analysis proceeded through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing\. The findings indicate that the factors driving gadget use during lessons include boredom, the habit of checking devices, peer influence, and low levels of student self\-control\. Such usage affects learning concentration, as students are easily distracted by digital activities\. Furthermore, the intensity of gadget use influences students&\#x27; social skills, evidenced by reduced social interaction when devices are used during social activities\. Consequently, the role of guidance counselors and the school is crucial in fostering wiser gadget usage habits through guidance services that strengthen self\-control and time management regarding device use\.

## [Dual\-health protocol modelling of Li\-ion battery degradation for UAVs with capacity–resistance coupled metrics in aviation duty cycles](../publications/4f7c247099790b1100bb.md)

Lalu Gladson Robin; S\. K\. Remmi; T\. Mariprasath; Mengistu Zelalem Zewdu

Abstract Batteries must be able to hold enough usable energy, and have enough power to operate, for high power UAVs and electric VTOLs\. But state\-of\-health based on capacity can deem resistance degraded batteries in good condition for use when there is significant voltage sag risk\. This work proposes a dual\-health protocol\-aware model using both the reference\-discharge capacity retention and resistance\-derived power retention to assess and schedule the battery degradation\. Chronological time, current, cumulative discharge capacity and pulse\-resistance measurements were used to reconstruct cycling and reference\-performance data for 22 Sony–Murata VTC6 cells based on different aviation duty protocols\. The analysis resulted in 439 valid capacity checkpoints, 388 impedance checkpoints and 415 paired health states\. A generalized estimating\-equation model was used to quantify the nonlinear cycling and protocol effects and to account for the repeated within\-cell observations\. The leakage\-safe leave\-one\-cell\-out validation was used to assess a random\-forest predictor\. Although there was a strong association between the two degradation measures \(Spearman coefficient of 0\.882\), capacity loss was strongly correlated with resistance growth\. The trajectory of the capacity\-health was down 2\.468% points per 100 mission\-equivalent cycles and was highly curved\. At the last checkpoint observed, 20 out of 21 cells were resistance\-limited for power retention and 1 cell was capacity\-limited\. The median dual\-health scores at 500 cycles varied between 73\.52% for extended cruise operation to 90\.05% for lower voltage charging\. The cell\-wise validation showed a mean absolute error of 0\.800% point, a root\-mean\-square error of 1\.101% point and coefficient of determination of 0\.975\. The dual\-health metric has the benefit of avoiding over\-stating the operational fitness and capacity of a UAV, while providing a conservative state metric for battery eligibility screening, swapping, and risk\-aware UAV mission allocation\.

## [One Novel Anxiolytic Mechanism, Three Gateways: What a Central Monoaminergic Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/4f7e3848e20542f5abb2.md)

Gloria Anthonia Amoateng Agyemang; Dorcas Koomson; Peivand Pirouzi

Generalized anxiety disorder \(GAD\) remains a therapeutic area with a limited number of recently approved mechanisms, and new, orally administered small\-molecule candidates acting on central monoaminergic pathways continue to be investigated as alternatives or adjuncts to existing selective serotonin and serotonin\-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors\. This article uses a fully hypothetical new chemical entity and a fictional sponsor to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014, using a Phase 2, randomized, placebo\-controlled dose\-ranging trial in adults with moderate\-to\-severe GAD as the illustrative scenario\. The comparison traces how the Common Technical Document&\#x27;s harmonized Modules 2 through 5 carry the shared scientific case across all three regions, while each jurisdiction&\#x27;s administrative layer imposes distinct requirements, including the heightened attention every region&\#x27;s psychiatry\-focused review division gives to suicidality monitoring and central nervous system safety signals for any new anxiolytic candidate\. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to a central nervous system program conducted across Canada, the United States, and the European Union, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing novel psychiatric drug candidates across these three jurisdictions\.Keywords: generalized anxiety disorder; central nervous system small molecule; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; suicidality monitoring; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Pedagoška prenova in vloga učiteljev v srednjih šolah](../publications/4f819771fee75343422a.md)

Laura Farré\-Riera; Núria Carrete\-Marín; Mar Beneyto\-Seoane; Esther Fatsini

This article presents the results of a research project funded by the Ministry of Science and Innovation of the Government of Spain, which aims to analyse secondary schools whose teaching practices are transformative because they go beyond temporary innovations, generating changes and improvements that impact the school, students and the local community and promote inclusion and meaningful learning\. This article examines the role that teachers play in secondary education in relation to teach\-ing practices and methodologies in the current context of demands for constant transformation, through the study of five secondary schools in different regions of Spain\. Observations, focus groups, analysis of school documents and in\-depth interviews were carried out, and the data were analysed using Atlas\.ti software\. The results show how pedagogical renew\-al in secondary education is based on teaching aspects such as educational leadership, strategies to promote personalised learning that place students at the centre of educational action, the establishment of relationships with the community to share educational and social projects that promote a sense of belonging to the local context, and the need to modify resources, spaces and times to accommodate more global and transversal teaching and learning processes\.

## [Interpretable Deep Multimodal Fusion of ECG and Facial Expressions for Robust Emotion Detection](../publications/4f83f692398c52682f74.md)

Sankar Ganesh Karuppasamy; Rajeev Kumar M

In healthcare, emotional computing, and dynamic human\-computer interaction, emotion recognition is a key component of human\-centric Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\. However, existing approaches depend on either physiological or visual signals and often show limited robustness or accuracy in noisy or inadequate data environments\. This study proposes a task\-specific bidirectional cross\-modal fusion framework in which physiological ECG representations and facial\-expression representations mutually attend to each other, while an auxiliary embedding\-alignment objective constrains the two modalities to a shared latent space\. While the facial images are processed using EfficientNet\-B0 to extract discriminative visual features, the ECG signals are transformed using a one\-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network \(1D\-CNN\) in conjunction with a Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(Bi\-LSTM\) network to extract local morphological features and long\-range temporal inference\. A cross\-attention fusion technique is then used to fuse the trained ECG models with facial expression data\. The inter\-modal dependencies between physiological and behavioral signals are represented by a cross\-attention fusion module, which improves the model&\#x27;s dependability and broadens its capacity to identify a variety of emotional classes, specifically focusing on six fundamental emotions: happy, sad, angry, fearful, surprised, and neutral\. The acquired representation is classified using a fully connected attention\-based decoder\. Model interpretability is attained through SHAP analysis of ECG embeddings and Grad\-CAM visualization of the facial areas\. When compared to current and baseline fusion techniques, the evaluation conducted using the MAHNOB\-HCI and AMIGOS datasets demonstrated that the proposed model achieved higher performance, including an accuracy of 97%, precision of 96%, recall of 97%, F1\-score of 96%, and improved adaptability\.

## [भरतय रजनत म कतरम बदधमतत: चनतय और अवसर](../publications/4f84ab1356fc784efb5e.md)

पवन कुमार बागड़े

शोध सारांश वर्तमान समय में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence—AI\) केवल एक तकनीकी परिघटना नहीं रह गई है, बल्कि यह भारतीय राजनीति की संरचना, प्रक्रियाओं तथा राजनीतिक व्यवहार को भी गहराई से प्रभावित कर रही है। प्रस्तुत शोध\-पत्र का उद्देश्य भारतीय राजनीति एवं प्रशासन में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के बढ़ते उपयोग का विश्लेषण करना तथा इससे उत्पन्न चुनौतियों और संभावित अवसरों की पहचान करना है। इस अध्ययन में द्वितीयक स्रोतों के आधार पर चुनावी अभियान, नीति\-निर्माण, सार्वजनिक सेवा वितरण तथा राजनीतिक संवाद पर कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के प्रभाव का परीक्षण किया गया है। कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता का उपयोग राजनीतिक संचार, जनमत विश्लेषण, प्रशासनिक कार्यों के स्वचालन तथा नागरिकों तक सूचनाएँ पहुँचाने में किया जा सकता है। इसके माध्यम से शासन की कार्यक्षमता में सुधार, सार्वजनिक सेवाओं की उपलब्धता में वृद्धि और नागरिक सहभागिता को प्रोत्साहन देने की संभावनाएँ विकसित होती हैं। हालाँकि, इसके साथ भ्रामक सूचनाओं का प्रसार, डीपफेक, व्यक्तिगत गोपनीयता का उल्लंघन, एल्गोरिदमिक पक्षपात तथा डिजिटल असमानता जैसी चुनौतियाँ भी जुड़ी हुई हैं। ये समस्याएँ मतदाताओं के निर्णय, राजनीतिक संवाद की विश्वसनीयता और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं के प्रति नागरिकों के विश्वास को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं। अध्ययन का निष्कर्ष है कि कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता भारतीय लोकतंत्र को अधिक कुशल, पारदर्शी और सहभागी बनाने में योगदान दे सकती है, बशर्ते इसका उपयोग जिम्मेदारी और उचित निगरानी के साथ किया जाए। इसके लिए एक सुदृढ़ नियामकीय ढाँचे, डेटा संरक्षण, तथ्य\-जाँच, डिजिटल साक्षरता, पारदर्शिता तथा जवाबदेही को बढ़ावा देना आवश्यक है। अतः भारतीय राजनीति में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता की भूमिका को समझते समय इसके तकनीकी लाभों के साथ\-साथ लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों, नागरिक अधिकारों और सामाजिक समानता पर पड़ने वाले प्रभावों का संतुलित मूल्यांकन करना महत्त्वपूर्ण है। मुख्य शब्द: कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता, भारतीय राजनीति, लोकतंत्र, चुनावी अभियान, नीति\-निर्माण, राजनीतिक संवाद, डीपफेक, डिजिटल असमानता, डेटा गोपनीयता, सुशासन।

## [No\-Regret Language Generation](../publications/4f91ea67d6183ec70c10.md)

Jiaxun Li; Vinod Raman; Ambuj Tewari

We introduce no\-regret generation, which requires a generator to make a sublinear number of mistakes uniformly over all demonstration sequences and compatible target languages\. We also formulate an agnostic variant that allows arbitrary demonstrations that may not be compatible with any languages\. For both settings, we introduce tree\-based mistake\-forcing dimensions that exactly characterize finite\-horizon minimax complexity and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for no\-regret generation\. Our characterizations reveal a rich spectrum of generation rates: up to constant rescaling, every admissible nondecreasing profile is attainable in both the realizable and agnostic settings\. Finally, we connect generation complexity to online prediction: for language classes of finite Littlestone dimension \\\(d\\\), we obtain realizable mistake bounds of \\\(O\(d\\log\(1\+T/d\)\)\\\) and agnostic regret bounds of \\\(O\(\\sqrt\{dT\\log\(1\+T/d\)\}\)\\\)\. The realizable bound is optimal up to universal constants\.

## [Comparison of two Crimean\-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus serological tests in Tanzanian febrile patients using a Bayesian latent class approach](../publications/4f933eebcbeed07453b5.md)

Elichilia Robert Shao; Rebecca F\. Bodenham; Jaffu Othniel Chilongola; Sarah Cleaveland; Venance P\. Maro; Buliga Mujaga; Eliaichi A\. Mlay; Laura J Shirima; Jeremia Jackson Pyuza; Judith Njau; Felix J\. Lankester; Ray Kayaga; Matthew P\. Rubach; John A\. Crump; Chee Wah Tan; Lin\-Fa Wang; Melinda K\. Rostal; Blandina Theophil Mmbaga

Background Crimean\-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus \(CCHFV\) is a tick\-borne zoonotic disease that can cause severe disease in humans, has a high fatality ratio, and is present in many African countries\. Accurate diagnosis of CCHF remains difficult\. Serological and molecular tests are frequently used to detect exposure or infection, but their accuracy varies with viral strain, infection stage, and population factors\. Notably, there is no universally recognised gold standard test for CCHFV serological diagnosis\. The reference standard for antibody detection requires neutralisation assays, which must be performed in biosafety level 4 \(BSL\-4\) laboratories\. These facilities are scarce and largely unavailable in sub\-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, where CCHFV is endemic\. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the IDvet ELISA and Luminex serological assays for detecting prior CCHFV exposure in humans using Bayesian latent class modelling in the absence of a reference standard\. Methodology This was a secondary analysis of archived serum samples from a prospective febrile illness surveillance cohort conducted between 2012–2014 in Moshi, Tanzania, at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Center and Mawenzi Regional Referral Hospital\. Bayesian latent class analysis was used to evaluate the performance of IDvet and Luminex assays in detecting CCHFV exposure in the samples collected\. Results Of the 870 febrile admissions enrolled across both sites, serum samples were available for 427 participants \(49%\)\. The median posterior estimate for IDvet sensitivity was 0\.893 \(95% Bayesian credibility interval \(BCI\) = 0\.555–0\.996\) and specificity was 0\.972 \(95% BCI = 0\.936–0\.996\)\. For the Luminex assay, the median posterior estimate for sensitivity was 0\.884 \(95% BCI = 0\.541, 0\.995\) and specificity was 0\.987 \(95% BCI = 0\.947, 1\.00\)\. The model generated seroprevalence estimates for two subpopulations, livestock owners and non\-livestock owners\. The livestock owner seroprevalence estimate was 0\.027 \(95% BCI = 0\.002, 0\.069\), and for non\-livestock owners, 0\.017 \(95% BCI = 0\.001, 0\.044\)\. Conclusion In the absence of a reference standard and access to BSL\-4 neutralisation testing, both the IDvet ELISA and the Luminex assay demonstrated high diagnostic performance with comparable sensitivity in detecting prior exposure to CCHFV among febrile patients in northern Tanzania\. Furthermore, the IDvet may offer operational advantages because of its simplicity and suitability for decentralised laboratories\.

Godwin Pius Ohemu; Adam Dale; Babafela Awosile; Robert Fraser Terry; Kiplangat Sigei; Anuj Sharma; Geetanjali Kapoor; Tine Rikke Jørgensen; Mohammed Alkhaldi; Mohamed Elhadidy; Heba Mahrous; Shaffi Fazaludeen Koya; Said Abukhattab; Maryam Wakkaf; Kome Otokunefor; Chizaram Anselm Onyeaghala; Ugonna Chinwe Morikwe; Olanrewaju Ibikunle Ibigbami; Azuka Raphael Njokanma; Nana Akosua A\.
