## [Deep Learning\-driven ECG Signal Interpretation for Predictive Cardiac Health Monitoring in Personalized Medical Care Systems](../publications/4fb6fcd2b23097c7cbfa.md)

Mahmood Hameed Majeed; Mohammed H\. Dosh; Safa L\. Kailan; Ali HamzahNajim; Maizatul Alice Meor Said

Cardiovascular diseases \(CVDs\) remain a major global health burden, making accurate ECG\-based classification important for automated cardiac assessment\.Existing ECG interpretation methods often employ computationally complex hybrid or Transformer\-based architectures and provide limited cross\-dataset evaluation\.To address these limitations, this study proposes a TCN\-MLP framework that uses a Temporal Convolutional Network \(TCN\) with causal dilated convolutions and residual connections to extract temporal ECG representations, followed by a Multi\-Layer Perceptron \(MLP\) for CVD classification\.Age, gender, and their missingness indicators are incorporated as demographic metadata to examine their contribution to classification\.The framework was evaluated on PTB\-XL, MIT\-BIH, and PhysioNet/CinC 2021 using a patient\-independent 70% training, 10% validation, and 20% testing protocol, with additional five\-fold cross\-validation\.The proposed framework achieved 98\.7% accuracy, 98\.5% precision, and 98\.7% AUC\-ROC, outperforming the evaluated baseline models\.The results demonstrate effective demographic\-assisted ECG classification and cross\-dataset evaluation under retrospective patient\-independent testing\.

## [‘Some of it&\#x27;s fucked, some of it&\#x27;s useful’: Young men&\#x27;s experiences navigating masculinity content on TikTok](../publications/4fb9bc97622c526c5e75.md)

Krista Fisher; Lauren Powell; Emily C\. Lewis; Jasleen Chhabra; Vivian Gerrand; Zac E\. Seidler

Masculinity content on TikTok is rapidly reshaping young men&\#x27;s identities, health and relationships, yet how young men perceive and navigate this content remains poorly understood\. This qualitative study explored the perspectives of 142 young men aged 16–25 \(Mage = 18\.85, SD = 2\.64\) from Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States\. Thematic analysis of open\-text responses generated two themes: A Blueprint for Masculine Self\-Development, capturing young men&\#x27;s simultaneous aspiration toward, and critique of, masculinity self\-improvement narratives; and Navigating Manosphere Ideologies, reflecting how young men engage with, interrogate or reject masculinist ideologies embedded within mainstream content\. Findings reveal a dynamic process of critical appraisal, weighing perceived benefits against ideological harm\. This carries significant implications for health promotion and digital policy: Evidence\-informed approaches are needed that leverage young men&\#x27;s desire for self\-improvement, address unmet psychosocial needs, encourage accountability and embed digital literacy and ideological safeguarding into digital places of meaning\.

## [From environmental exposure to disease burden: Institutional capacity, structural vulnerability, and global malaria inequality, 2000–2023](../publications/4fc75336dc303a726f17.md)

ZAWADI ALLY NKULIKWA; Godfrey William

Malaria burden varies markedly between countries with similar environmental conditions\. We examined national associations between malaria incidence, institutional capacity, economic development, structural vulnerability and selected environmental indicators during 2000–2023\. An ecological panel comprised 4,382 complete country\-years across 186 countries\. Year\-fixed\-effects models related log\(incidence \+ 1\) to standardised predictors, with country\-clustered uncertainty\. Vulnerability was positively associated with incidence \(β = 0\.931, p = \.007\), whereas GDP per capita was inversely associated \(β = −2\.014, p &lt; \.001\)\. Institutional capacity and the selected environmental indicators were not statistically significant after adjustment\. With country\-and\-year fixed effects, vulnerability attenuated to β = 0\.406 \(p = \.232\), while GDP remained inversely associated\. Excluding the malaria\-related ND\-GAIN indicator retained the positive year\-effects association; excluding the whole health sector and changing sector coverage affected the findings\. GDP showed a relatively consistent association; vulnerability depended on specification and composite construction\. National aggregation, incomplete source provenance and potential confounding limit interpretation\. These ecological associations do not establish causal pathways\. Subnational environmental, intervention and health\-system data are needed to investigate the proposed mechanisms\.

## [Morphometric typology of Ming Chinese export and domestic porcelain bowls in trade and production contexts](../publications/4fe6054497a3e48456f3.md)

Shengying Feng; Wenkang Huang; Miao Zhao; Yingying Wang; Jinghui Ao; Gangwei Cai; Wenwen Shi

Abstract Chinese export porcelain bowls are heritage materials associated with Ming maritime trade, yet their morphology remains insufficiently quantified\. This study develops a morphometric typological framework to characterize concentration, size variation, and atypical forms, comparing 37 export references with 25 domestic comparators\. Profile extraction, typological coding, AutoCAD scaling, and Rhinoceros\-assisted measurement were applied to 62 bowls\. Round feet and curved bodies comprised 88\.7% \(55/62\) and 69\.4% \(43/62\), while everted and open rims together comprised 66\.1% \(41/62\)\. Rim diameter ranged from 7\.6 to 41\.2 cm, including 20 miniature, 36 regular\-sized, and 6 large bowls\. Among 60 specimens retained for angular analysis, HFJA was concentrated \(mean 59\.0°, median 58\.0°, SD 8\.3°\), whereas LFJA was dispersed \(mean/median 47\.0°, SD 10\.2°\)\. Export specimens showed broader size, rim\-type, and angular variation within a shared morphological framework\. The workflow provides reproducible evidence while treating production, trade, consumption, and function as contextual associations rather than causal mechanisms\.

## [A VGG16\-Based CRAFT Network for Vertical Container Number Detection](../publications/4fe6642259d0d7265c15.md)

Pima Hani Safitri; Alqis Rausanfita; Fidi Wincoko Putro

Container identification is critical in logistics and port management, where container numbers must be detected accurately for tracking and operational efficiency\. In practice, container numbers may appear in vertical orientations, which challenges conventional optical character recognition \(OCR\) systems\. This study proposes a vertical container\-number detection approach based on Character Region Awareness for Text Detection \(CRAFT\) with a VGG16 backbone\. The method focuses on character\-level localization using annotated container\-number datasets, including images captured in a harbor environment in Surabaya, Indonesia\. The CRAFT\-based model localizes individual characters under varying orientations, enabling more reliable detection of vertically arranged container numbers\. Experimental results show that the method achieved a maximum Intersection over Union \(IoU\) of 0\.944 and an average IoU of 0\.389 across the evaluated test images over 10 reported iterations\. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach for vertical container\-number detection in real\-world port environments and its applicability to automated container\-management systems\.

## [Solutions to LLM \+ Robotic Oncology Trial Problems](../publications/4ff549d6d9a3da37eb44.md)

Kevin Kawchak

Solving new large language model \(LLM\) and robotic based oncology clinical trial industry problems requires proper publication of protocols, standards, legislation, and funding applications prior to deployment\. This paper provides solution sets derived from prior author works for upcoming Physical SI \(super intelligence\) oncology trials\. The publications referenced here require whole implementation, as capabilities differ between state\-of\-the\-art AI models and robots per problem type\. Many AI manufacturers’ models have been tested between 2024\-2025 in order to discover novel and useful clinical trial applications\. These developments include the creation of a patient matching machine learning pipeline, the combination of generated clinical trial meta\-analyses to provide new AI insights for indications and cancer drugs, emerging clinical trial simulations, and accelerating the speed and quality of the academic paper creation process\. Ultimately, 2026 multi\-prompt processes have been optimized to single master prompt systems featured in new trial protocols, drug applications, and funding requests \- which feature autonomous AI sub\-prompt generation and execution, professional machine readable diagrams, and iterations of full academic paper source code files using a repository\-based LLM\. Resulting single master prompt\-based publications contained high contextual awareness, with a limited number of author corrections required for diagram positioning and paper formatting\. Two comprehensive LLM and oncology clinical trial literature reviews conducted in 2025 and 2026 yielded a limited number applications, delayed implementations of new AI models \- prompting the oncology trial solutions\.

## [Dijital Aktivizm Kampanyalarının İletişim Faaliyetleri ve Paydaş Kurumlara Stratejik Etkileri](../publications/4ff622a75fec589f657f.md)

Ayla Topuz Savaş; Emine ŞARDAĞI; Orkun ŞEN

Dijital aktivizm kampanyalarının sayısı artmaktadır ancak kampanyaların iletişim faaliyetlerinin nasıl düzenlenmesi gerektiği önemli bir sorundur\. Paydaş kurumların bu işbirliğinden stratejik olarak nasıl etkilenecekleri de hem kampanyanın başarısı hem de kurumlar açısından son derece önemlidir\. Çalışmanın temel amacı dijital aktivizm kampanyalarının iletişim boyutuyla, kampanya paydaşı kurumların da stratejik yönetim boyutuyla değerlendirilmesidir\. Bu amaç doğrultusunda nitel araştırma yöntemi ve olasılıklı olmayan örneklem türlerinden olan amaçlı örneklem kullanılmıştır\. Dijital aktivizm üzerinde çalışan akademisyenlerle Kafessiz Türkiye Kampanyası aktivizm faaliyetleri üzerine derinlikli görüşmeler yapılmıştır\. Elde edilen veriler Maxqda Analytical programı ile analiz edilmiştir\. Araştırmada kampanyanın iletişim boyutu, güçlü ve güçlendirilmesi gereken yönler, fırsatlar ve tehditler, dijital içeriklerin taşıması gereken özellikler, kampanyaya dahil olan kurumların stratejik yönetim ve rekabetçi politikalarına sağlayacağı yararlar değerlendirilmiştir\. Bulgular göstermektedir ki; kampanyanın farkındalığı arttırılmalı, etkileşimli içerikler üretmelidir\. Paydaş kurumların stratejik olarak başarısı için kampanyaya desteklerini iletişim faaliyetlerinin bir parçası haline getirmelerinin gerekliliği de bir başka bulgudur\. Sonuç olarak dijital aktivizm kampanyalarının iletişim ve etkileşim boyutunun geliştirilmesinin kampanyanın etkisini arttıracağı ve paydaş kurumların etkili bir stratejik yönetim perspektifiyle kampanyaya destek olmalarının da hem kampanyaya hem de paydaş kuruma olumlu etkiler yaratabileceği öngörülmektedir\. Literatürde bir kampanya özelinde iletişim faaliyetleri ve stratejik yönetim kapsamında alan uzmanı akademisyenlerin birlikte değerlendiren ve öneriler sunan bir çalışmaya rastlanmamıştır\. Bu bağlamda elde edilecek bulgular, dijital aktivizm literatüründeki önemli bir boşluğu dolduracaktır\. Gelecekte hedef kitle ve kampanya düzenleyicileriyle çalışmalar yapılabilir\.

Vladislav Yu\. Buslaev; Vladimir Gennadyevich Druzhinin; Andrey V\. Shabaldin

In this review data about contribution of lung microbiome in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease development are systematized\. For systematic review systems like PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Google Scholar, e\-library were used for search of scientific articles\. As result 35 publications were included in review\. Information was given about dominative taxa of respiratory microbiota, involved in disease development and also about possible mechanisms providing this linkage\. It was shown that the basis of this phenomena is linked with dysbacteriosis which expressed in microbial diversity decrease and also in enhancement of recent taxa size\. ## [Mapping generative AI in higher education teaching and learning: a scoping review](../publications/5016edba492ae6ad83b4.md)

Michael Pin\-Chuan Lin; Daniel Chang; Philip H\. Winne; Gervase Michael Bowen; Jeeho Ryoo

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) has rapidly entered higher education, but empirical research on its roles in teaching and learning remains fragmented across instructional activities, outcomes, assessment approaches, and stakeholder perspectives\. This scoping review followed PRISMA\-ScR guidelines to map 394 empirical studies of GenAI use in higher education published from November 2022 through December 2025\. The review examined how GenAI tools were integrated into authentic teaching and learning activities, what outcomes or skills were targeted, how studies assessed those outcomes, and how students and instructors perceived GenAI use\. Across the reviewed studies, GenAI was most often used to support existing academic tasks, especially feedback, tutoring, and writing\. The most frequently targeted outcomes included engagement, usability and acceptance, critical thinking, disciplinary knowledge, academic performance, writing quality, and AI literacy\. Self\-regulated learning, ethics, creativity, feedback quality, and equity received less attention\. Assessment practices relied mainly on surveys, tests or rubrics, artifact analysis, and interviews, suggesting that much of the evidence base is shaped by short\-term and readily implemented methods\. Student and instructor perceptions were predominantly mixed, reflecting perceived benefits alongside concerns about pedagogy, integrity, workload, and governance\. The review highlights the need for stronger alignment between learning constructs and assessment methods, more process\-sensitive evidence, clearer reporting of governance practices, and greater attention to equity in GenAI\-supported higher education\. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi\.org/10\.1186/s41239\-026\-00630\-9\.

## [Robot\-assisted training for post\-stroke lower\-limb dysfunction: an umbrella review](../publications/503ed30df58a9c1c36cd.md)

Lei Wang; Can Wang; Qian Cao; Keping Yin; Lingnan Ding; Ailian Chen

Objective This study aimed to reappraise published systematic reviews and meta\-analyses on robot\-assisted training for lower\-limb motor dysfunction after stroke and evaluate their methodological quality, reporting completeness, and certainty of evidence\. Methods Seven databases were searched, including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science, from inception to January 15, 2026\. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta\-analyses that were based on randomized controlled trials\. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal\. The methodological quality of the included reviews was assessed using A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews \(AMSTAR\) 2, and the reporting of this umbrella review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews \(PRIOR\) guideline\. The reporting completeness of the included systematic reviews and meta\-analyses was evaluated using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA\) 2020 checklist\. The certainty of evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation \(GRADE\) framework\. Results Nineteen reviews were included, comprising eight Chinese and 11 English publications\. Primary\-study overlap across reviews was moderate \(CCA = 7\.44%\)\. According to AMSTAR 2, three reviews were rated as high quality, six as moderate quality, six as low quality, and four as critically low quality\. PRISMA completeness scores ranged from 14\.5 to 23\.5 out of a maximum possible score of 27\. Among the 70 extracted outcomes, none was rated as high\-certainty evidence, 20 were of moderate certainty, 32 were of low certainty, and 18 were of very low certainty\. Overall, robot\-assisted training showed potential benefits for balance and lower\-extremity motor function, whereas evidence for walking\-related outcomes remained less consistent\. Conclusion Evidence was most consistent for balance and lower\-extremity motor impairment, whereas findings for walking independence, endurance, functional mobility, and gait speed were less consistent and generally supported by low\-to\-moderate certainty evidence\. More rigorously designed primary trials and better\-conducted systematic reviews are needed\. Systematic review registration The review protocol was registered under Prospero, https://www\.crd\.york\.ac\.uk/PROSPERO/home \(Registration No: CRD420261419692\)\.

## [STCP\-Net: A few\-shot learning approach based on spectral\-temporal convolution and an improved prototypical network for ECG classification](../publications/50454a052016dfdc52b6.md)

Jia Li; Dainan Gan; Xiaolin Zhan; Wei Yao; Bin Zou; Bin Zhang; Dong Li; Dan Li; Lin Li

To address the heavy reliance of deep learning models on manually labeled data in ECG classification, we need to tackle two major limitations\. First, sample sizes are often limited in clinical settings, making data annotation costly and impractical\. Second, existing few\-shot learning methods still fall short in two key areas: 1\) Existing strategies pay insufficient attention to rare arrhythmia types\. This makes it difficult to effectively identify rare clinical cases\. 2\) Single feature representation fails to fully integrate the global frequency, local time\-frequency, and semantic information of ECG signals\. This results in incomplete feature representation\. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel few\-shot learning method for ECG classification\. In terms of feature extraction, a spectral\-temporal convolution feature extractor is designed to precisely focus on the key information of ECG by efficiently integrating the global frequency, local time\-frequency features and semantic information of the signal\. Furthermore, with regard to classification, an improved prototypical network based on cross\-class bias diminishing is developed to enhance the recognition performance for rare arrhythmia type samples\. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves significant classification performance across multiple public datasets, especially on Chapman, it attains an average accuracy exceeding 90% in the 2\-way 1\-shot and 2\-way 5\-shot tasks\.

## [A Conversational AI Framework for Teacher Training](../publications/504a0fff32b7b873e8ea.md)

Sergio Miranda; Antonio Calvani

This paper introduces ETQ\-AI \(Effective Teaching Questionnaire—Artificial Intelligence\), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection\. Building on Evidence\-Informed Education \(EIE\) principles, the system integrates a 50\-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini\-driven Explainable AI \(XAI\) feedback layer\. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta\-analytic evidence \(e\.g\., Hattie’s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory\) or argue personal objections\. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark \(N=64 items\) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators \(70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders\) recruited at an EIE conference\. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations \(97%\), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction \(Mean = 4\.1/5 vs\. 3\.8/5\)\. Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity\. While the findings validate the technical proof\-of\-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ\-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice\.

## [Mechanistic insights into the synergistic interactions between macrolides and beta\-lactams in bacterial infections](../publications/505d240b119a81cbc130.md)

Qiaochun Lu; Xubo Qian; Yandie Li; Yao Liu; Zijin Chen; Le He; Yilin Yu; Zhigang Jin; Yuting Shi

β\-Lactams and macrolides are two cornerstone classes of antimicrobials in clinical practice\. Traditionally, this combination was considered potentially antagonistic\. However, accumulating evidence from basic and clinical research has begun to challenge this view and indicates that the two classes may exert complementary and synergistic effects in specific clinical contexts\. This review first describes the mechanisms of action and resistance of both antibiotic classes, and then presents clinical evidence supporting the use of combination therapy\. The greatest clinical benefit of combination therapy is observed in adults with severe community\-acquired pneumonia \(CAP\)\. By contrast, results from non\-severe CAP or pediatric populations have been inconsistent\. We then systematically review potential synergistic mechanisms, including complementary antibacterial targets, macrolide penetration facilitated by β\-lactam\-induced cell\-wall injury, suppression of bacterial repair and stress responses, biofilm disruption, immunomodulation, and quorum\-sensing interference\. We also classify the strength of evidence for each proposed mechanism\. Finally, we compare the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic \(PK/PD\) profiles of azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin and assess their potential impact on combination efficacy\. We also discuss safety concerns, including adverse effects, drug interactions, and selection for resistance, along with strategies to address these issues\. It should be emphasized that most mechanistic evidence derives from in vitro or animal studies, and only a minority comes from clinical research\. The combination should be used with strict attention to indications, and its benefits should not be extrapolated indiscriminately to other conditions\. We conclude that β\-lactam–macrolide combination therapy demonstrates promising synergy in severe CAP and other specific infections\. The multi\-level mechanistic framework lends biological plausibility to the observed synergy, but biological synergy does not guarantee clinical benefit in all patients\. Only when used in the right patients, at the right time, and with the right drug combination can this therapeutic strategy produce clinical benefit\.

## [ІНФОРМАЦІЙНО\-КОМУНІКАЦІЙНІ ТЕХНОЛОГІЇ ЯК СКЛАДНИК ЦИФРОВОЇ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ ПРАВООХОРОННИХ ОРГАНІВ УКРАЇНИ](../publications/50601dffedb4c2f8f456.md)

У статті досліджено роль інформаційно\-комунікаційних технологій у цифровій трансформації правоохоронних органів України\. ## [Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution\-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries](../publications/5068b4f54f93b0e5ec6d.md)

Anna Mazhar; Seiji Maekawa; Nikita Bhutani

Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e\.g\., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution\. When several candidates could satisfy the same need, execution may be required to identify the relevant one\. Investigating candidates in a shared trajectory can leave alternatives unexplored or allow failed attempts to influence subsequent reasoning\. To address this, we present BRIA \(BRanch\-Inspect\-Adopt\), a simple yet effective agent that temporarily isolates candidate investigations in separate branches\. Each branch retrieves and executes tools to investigate its candidate; a task agent inspects the resulting execution evidence and adopts only useful results into its continuing trajectory\. BRIA retrieves additional tools as new capability needs arise during task execution\. We evaluate BRIA on PlanBench\-XL and MCP\-Atlas using a shared pool of 1897 tools, three language models, and static and adaptive retrieval baselines\. Across all settings, BRIA matches or exceeds the strongest retrieval baseline\. On MCP\-Atlas, it achieves an average claim score of 89\.77, compared with 75\.40 for MCP\-Zero, a gain of 14\.37 percentage points\. BRIA also lies on the Pareto frontier for task performance and input\-token cost\.

## [Spektral analiz görsellerinde ölçekleme etkisi: Derin öğrenmede gizli bir parametre](../publications/50780995f3455fdaadd7.md)

Onur Demirci; Seral Özşen

Derin öğrenme günümüzde birçok alanda kullanılmakta ve gelecek için önemli bir vizyon oluşturmaktadır\. Bundan kaynaklı olarak modelin güvenilir ve yüksek doğrulukta sınıflama yapabilmesi oldukça önemlidir\. Yapılan çalışmalar, model ve analiz yöntemlerinin parametrelerine odaklanmıştır\. Fakat spektral analiz ile elde edilen verilerde skala aralığı da modelin performansında önemli bir etkiye sahiptir\. Çalışmamızda MAEEG ve LSEEG veri setinde dinamik ve sabit skala yöntemi kullanılarak görsel veriler oluşturulmuştur\. MAEEG veri setinde analizler özne\-bağımlı, LSEEG veri setinde ise özne\-bağımsız gerçekleştirilmiştir\. Dinamik skala yönteminde MAEEG ve LSEEG veri setlerinde sırasıyla %70,35 ve %59,61 sınıflama doğruluğu elde edilmiştir\. Aynı veri setlerinde önerilen sabit skala yöntemi kullanıldığında sırasıyla doğruluk %87,31 ve %89,41 oranına çıkmıştır\. Bu durum skalanın da derin öğrenme modelleri için oldukça önemli bir parametre olduğunu göstermektedir\. Kısa Zamanlı Fourier Analizi için skala belirleme yöntemi önerilmiştir\.

## [Managerial Innovation as a Lever for Digital Transformation Success: Toward an Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework](../publications/508359ce213360f59a8a.md)

Mohamed Amine LOUKILI; Abbas MOKHTARI

The accelerating pace of digital transformation has fundamentally restructured competitive landscapes across industries, compelling organizations to reconsider not only their technological investments but, more critically, their managerial architectures and innovation capacities\. While extant scholarship has extensively examined the technological dimensions of digital transformation, comparatively limited attention has been devoted to managerial innovation as a primary enabling condition for sustained digital transformation success\. This article addresses that gap by developing a theoretically grounded, integrative conceptual framework—the Integrated Organizational Value Creation Framework \(IOVCF\)—that articulates the causal pathways through which managerial innovation drives digital transformation and ultimately generates organizational value\. Anchored in four complementary theoretical perspectives—Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Resource\-Based View \(RBV\), Organizational Change Theory, and Socio\-Technical Systems Theory—the framework models a cascading logic: managerial innovation cultivates organizational capabilities \(agility, learning, adaptability, and collaborative intelligence\), which in turn facilitate digital transformation success \(technology adoption, process digitalization, data integration, and digital innovation\), culminating in multi\-dimensional organizational value creation \(operational performance, resilience, stakeholder satisfaction, and sustainable competitive advantage\)\. Twelve formal research propositions are derived and theoretically justified\. Managerial implications emphasize that digital transformation leaders must invest in organizational redesign, agile management practices, digital culture formation, knowledge management systems, employee empowerment, and collaborative ecosystems alongside—and often prior to—technology deployment\. A rich agenda for future empirical research is outlined, encompassing cross\-national validation, SME contexts, AI\-enabled transformation, and sustainability\-oriented digital strategies\.

## [Pengaruh Motivasi dan Lingkungan Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan UMKM di Konveksi Alive Sportwear, Sumedang](../publications/509853b7841694b59712.md)

Nadya Syahla; Arlinda Syakila Ananda; Thia Nurafifah Ramadani; Erna Herlinawati; Gurawan Dayona Ismail

Employee performance is key to MSME sustainability, affecting target achievement, work quality, and customer satisfaction\. Garment production requires accuracy, coordination, comfort, and consistency\. Alive Sportwear Garment in Sumedang, a growing MSME, faces challenges in optimizing motivation and the work environment\. This study analyzes work motivation and the work environment on employee performance, partially and simultaneously\. A quantitative approach was employed, involving 30 employees selected through saturated sampling\. Data were collected through questionnaires, observation, and documentation, then analyzed using multiple linear regression, t\-test, F\-test, and coefficient of determination\. The results show that motivation has a positive but insignificant effect on performance, with a coefficient of 0\.048 and significance of 0\.856, while the work environment has a positive and significant effect, with a coefficient of 0\.328 and significance of 0\.034\. Simultaneously, variables significantly affect performance, with F\-value 6\.971, significance 0\.004, and R² 34\.1%\. The work environment should be prioritized to improve performance\.

## [UTILIZAÇÃO CONTEMPORÂNEA DAS RADIOGRAFIAS PANORÂMICAS E DAS TOMOGRAFIAS LINEAR, COMPUTADORIZADA E DE FEIXE CÔNICO NA ODONTOLOGIA: INDICAÇÕES, APLICAÇÕES E PERSPECTIVAS DIGITAIS](../publications/5099c90c088764f9edf4.md)

Rogério Hernandes

A evolução dos métodos de diagnóstico por imagem modificou profundamente a prática odontológica, especialmente nas áreas de Implantodontia, Cirurgia e Traumatologia Buco\-Maxilo\-Facial, Ortodontia, Endodontia e Radiologia Odontológica\. A radiografia panorâmica permanece como importante método de avaliação inicial devido à sua ampla cobertura anatômica, facilidade de execução e capacidade de fornecer uma visão geral do complexo maxilomandibular\. Paralelamente, técnicas tomográficas evoluíram da tomografia linear para a tomografia computadorizada médica e, posteriormente, para a tomografia computadorizada de feixe cônico \(TCFC\), possibilitando avaliação tridimensional das estruturas maxilofaciais\. O presente artigo apresenta uma revisão narrativa sobre a utilização contemporânea desses métodos, abordando suas características, indicações, vantagens, limitações e aplicações clínicas\. São discutidos particularmente os princípios de justificação e otimização da exposição à radiação, a seleção do campo de aquisição, a resolução espacial e a integração da TCFC aos fluxos digitais de planejamento implantodôntico\. Destaca\-se ainda sua aplicação no planejamento de implantes convencionais, curtos, inclinados, zigomáticos e pterigoídeos, bem como na cirurgia guiada, cirurgia navegada e integração de arquivos DICOM e STL\. Conclui\-se que os métodos radiográficos e tomográficos não devem ser considerados tecnologias concorrentes, mas ferramentas complementares cuja indicação deve estar fundamentada na questão clínica a ser respondida\.

## [Structural Evolution of the Python Dependency Network: Evidence from a Decade of Ecosystem Growth](../publications/50a5f1603573c60de2d2.md)

Juan Ignacio Catania; Mateo Guerrero Schmidt; Sofia Gutierrez; Martina Rosario Pérez; Carlos Sarraute

Presentamos un análisis longitudinal de la red de dependencias del ecosistema de librerías de Python, evidenciando transformaciones estructurales sistemáticas a lo largo de casi una década\. Los ecosistemas de paquetes de software pueden modelarse como redes complejas cuya topología refleja prácticas de desarrollo y tendencias tecnológicas\. Para caracterizar su evolución, construimos grafos dirigidos de dependencias correspondientes a dos cortes temporales \(2016 y 2025\) y calculamos métricas estructurales, medidas de centralidad y organización comunitaria\. Los resultados muestran una expansión masiva del ecosistema acompañada por cambios topológicos significativos\. El número de paquetes crece más de un orden de magnitud, mientras que el número de dependencias aumenta aún más rápidamente, lo que indica un proceso de densificación\. Asimismo, observamos un incremento del grado promedio, una disminución de la modularidad y una reconfiguración de los nodos centrales\. Mientras que en etapas tempranas predominaban librerías asociadas al desarrollo web y la compatibilidad, en el período más reciente emergen como hubs estructurales paquetes vinculados a ciencia de datos, computación científica y testing automatizado\. Estos hallazgos sugieren que el ecosistema Python evoluciona hacia una arquitectura más interconectada y que su crecimiento sigue patrones consistentes con leyes conocidas de redes complejas, tales como la densificación y la reorganización de hubs\. En términos más generales, el estudio aporta evidencia empírica sobre la evolución estructural de ecosistemas tecnológicos a gran escala y destaca el valor de los enfoques de ciencia de redes para su análisis\.

## [Forgotten lobotomies in Rome: new evidence of psychosurgery in postwar Italy](../publications/50a9e948c3ff340f5e56.md)

Elisabetta Sirgiovanni; Livia Castelli

The history of psychosurgery, perhaps the most controversial venture in clinical neuroscience&\#x27;s past, has long been written without Rome\. While leucotomies and lobotomies performed have been documented in northern and southern Italian centres, the Italian capital \- despite being the birthplace of electroconvulsive therapy \(ECT\) and home to two major state psychiatric institutions \- has remained largely absent from historical accounts\. Drawing on previously unexamined archival materials from Italy and the United States, and despite substantial gaps in the surviving documentation\-including the inaccessibility of all but one patient record\-, this study reconstructs psychosurgical activity in Rome between 1949 and the early 1950s, identifying interventions performed both at the University Neuropsychiatric Clinic and at the Santa Maria della Pietà Asylum\. The Roman experience reveals an ambivalent attitude toward psychosurgery\. Although new surgical modifications were proposed locally, growing scientific and ethical concerns soon emerged, leading, at least in one of the two institutions, if not both, to the eventual abandonment of the initiative\. By restoring Rome to the history of psychosurgery, this study challenges established narratives of postwar Italian clinical neuroscience and highlights the early emergence of doubts surrounding lobotomy\.

## [Exploring Empowerment Challenges Facing SMMEs in the Nelson Mandela Bay Automotive Industry](../publications/50b4e618b59795780b21.md)

Luthando Rafani; Siyabonga Sirayi; Ayanda Pamella Deliwe

Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises \(SMMEs\) play a critical role in South Africa&\#x27;s automotive industry by promoting economic growth, supplier development, and employment creation\. However, persistent empowerment challenges continue to constrain their participation in automotive value chains and limit their contribution to youth skills development and workforce development pathways\. This study aimed to explore the empowerment challenges facing SMMEs within the Nelson Mandela Bay automotive industry and to examine how these challenges influence opportunities for youth skills formation and sustainable workforce development\. A qualitative case study design was adopted, employing purposive and snowball sampling to recruit 15 participants comprising SMME owners, Sector Development representatives, and Automotive Industry Development Centre \(AIDC\) officials\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews and analysed using six\-phase thematic analysis\. The findings identified six interrelated themes that constrain SMME empowerment: access and resources, skills and training, communication and information, policy and leadership, infrastructure and operations, and motivation and organisational culture\. Collectively, these barriers restrict SMMEs&\#x27; competitiveness, reduce their ability to participate in supplier development initiatives, and weaken their capacity to provide workplace learning opportunities, apprenticeships, and technical skills development for young people entering the automotive industry\. The study concludes that strengthening institutional support, improving communication between stakeholders, expanding access to finance and infrastructure, and aligning empowerment initiatives with industry needs are essential to enhancing SMME sustainability and supporting inclusive workforce development\. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on SMME empowerment by demonstrating the close relationship between enterprise development, youth employability, and regional workforce development within South Africa&\#x27;s automotive industry\.

## [Human\-in\-the\-Loop Enterprise AI Architecture](../publications/50b755f539712b93f9a7.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

Human\-in\-the\-Loop \(HITL\) architecture is a foundational control pattern for enterprise Artificial Intelligence where AI systems assist with analysis, recommendations, content generation, or task execution while designated people retain authority at critical decision points\. As Generative AI and Agentic AI become more autonomous, enterprises require a systematic architecture for determining when human review is mandatory, how work is routed, what evidence reviewers receive, how approvals are recorded, and how overrides and escalations are governed\. This paper proposes a Human\-in\-the\-Loop Enterprise AI Architecture integrating AI models, RAG, enterprise data, policy engines, workflow orchestration, identity, approval services, audit trails, security, Responsible AI, and operational monitoring\. It defines risk\-based review patterns, confidence thresholds, exception routing, separation of duties, and measurable governance controls\. The architecture enables organizations to balance automation and human judgment while improving safety, accountability, explainability, compliance, and enterprise trust\.

## [Behavioral and Obstetrical Factors Associated with Self\-Reported Cervical Cancer\-Related Symptoms Among Women of Childbearing Age in Medan City, Indonesia](../publications/50cb84bcfcfb13577592.md)

Fatwa Imelda; Lawra Lofty Maharaja; Reni Asmara Ariga

Background: Cervical cancer remains the second most common malignancy among women in Indonesia, driven by late\-stage clinical diagnoses\. This cross\-sectional correlational study investigated the relationship between behavioral\-obstetrical risk profiles and the early manifestation of self\-perceived cervical cancer symptoms among women in vulnerable reproductive groups at the primary care level\.Aims: This study aimed to analyze the association between behavioral\-obstetrical risk profiles and self\-reported cervical cancer symptoms among women of childbearing age \(15–49 years\) at the primary healthcare level\.Methods: A consecutive sample of 108 women of childbearing age completed an anonymous, self\-administered questionnaire assessing behavioral–obstetrical risk factors and a 10\-item cervical cancer symptom checklist at UPTD Puskesmas PB Selayang II, Medan, Indonesia\.Results: Self\-reported symptoms were identified in 59\.3% of respondents, predominantly systemic fatigue \(50\.0%\), lower back pain \(37\.96%\), and pelvic pain \(25\.93%\), while late\-stage signs were completely absent\.Conclusion: These results demonstrate a significant cross\-sectional association between specific behavioral\-obstetrical profiles and self\-reported cervical cancer\-related symptoms among women accessing primary care\. Because symptoms were self\-reported and unconfirmed by clinical or cytological diagnostic tests, universal screening remains essential to distinguish subjective reproductive complaints from actual cervical pathology\.

## [FedHEAL\-IoMT: A Federated Hierarchical Evidential Adaptive Learning Framework for Zero\-day DDoS Detection in Internet of Medical Things Networks](../publications/50cc22f18d4be8a65a7b.md)

Tejinder Sharma; Bharti Sharma

Distributed denial\-of\-service \(DDoS\) traffic dominates the attack taxonomy of current Internet of Medical Things \(IoMT\) testbeds, and federated learning \(FL\) has become the accepted way of training detectors without moving patient\-adjacent traffic off hospital premises\.Existing federated IoMT detectors nevertheless combine conventional averaging with an off\-the\-shelf classifier and report results on independent and identically distributed partitions, so their published accuracy reveals little about the conditions a deployed hospital federation meets: attack variants absent from the training distribution, gradual drift in traffic composition, compromised gateways that poison the aggregate, and devices too constrained to host the full model\.This paper presents FedHEAL\-IoMT, a three\-tier framework treating those conditions as one coupled problem\.An evidential head emits Dirichlet concentration parameters whose total uncertainty acts as an open\-set alarm and, through an exponentially weighted shift statistic, as a label\-free drift trigger; a trust\-weighted rule gates outlying updates by geometric\-median deviation, evaluated inside a two\-server secure\-computation protocol that reveals no individual update, distance or trust score, before a differentially private secure sum; and a normalized\-cost rule places the split\-learning cut layer per device class\.Validation spans CICIoMT2024, WUSTL\-EHMS\-2020, ECU\-IoHT and CICIoT2023\.On CICIoMT2024 FedHEAL\-IoMT attains 99\.41% accuracy under homogeneous partitions against 99\.35% for the strongest baseline, a difference of 0\.06 points lying inside the seed spread, while raising macro\-F1 by 4\.57 points at Dirichlet α = 0\.1, open\-set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve by 4\.31 points over the strongest zero\-day baseline, and accuracy under 30% non\-adaptive malicious gateways by 5\.34 points over the strongest robust comparator, FedMADE, and 8\.01 over Krum, at 71\.9% lower peak resident memory measured on the Raspberry Pi 4B gateway platform\.Code, configurations, seeds and per\-seed results are released publicly\.

## [Analysis of ChatGPT Usage Intensity Patterns on Student Creativity and Productivity Using a Data Analytics and SEM\-PLS Approach](../publications/50cd1dc6fef4cb08e4a4.md)

Sri Muliani Nurrohmah; Setiawan Assegaff; Sharipuddin Sharipuddin; Effiyaldi Effiyaldi; Gunardi Gunardi

The development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), particularly ChatGPT, has provided significant support for students in carrying out academic activities\. This study aims to examine the effects of Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, Subjective Norm, Task Relevance, Content, Accuracy, Format, and Timeliness on the Intensity of ChatGPT Usage, as well as the effects of ChatGPT Usage Intensity on Student Creativity and Student Productivity\. This study employed a quantitative approach by distributing an online questionnaire to active students at Universitas Dinamika Bangsa, Universitas Islam Negeri Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin Jambi, and Universitas Jambi\. Data were analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares \(SEM\-PLS\) method with the assistance of SmartPLS software\. The results indicate that all eleven proposed hypotheses were supported\. The eight exogenous variables have a positive and significant effect on the Intensity of ChatGPT Usage, while the Intensity of ChatGPT Usage has a positive and significant effect on both Student Creativity and Student Productivity\. Furthermore, Student Creativity also has a positive and significant effect on Student Productivity\.

## [Understanding stroke and spasticity: patient and caregiver experiences and quality\-of\-life impact](../publications/50d2eefee0c7e920ec31.md)

Monica Verduzco‐Gutierrez; Émilie Pain; Jonathan R\. Bouchard; Amandeep Mann

Introduction Poststroke spasticity \(PSS\) is a common sensorimotor disorder following a stroke, presenting in up to 38% of patients 1 year after first stroke\. Owing to its heterogeneous and progressive presentation, PSS represents a significant challenge both in its effect on patients and in its clinical management\. The objective of this US real\-world survey was to assess the impact of self\-reported PSS symptoms, gathering patient and caregiver perspectives on awareness of PSS and its treatments, the extent of shared decision\-making, and the quality of life \(QoL\) impact of PSS\. Methods This study was a noninterventional, cross\-sectional, web\-based survey of patients \(or their caregivers\) within 1 year of stroke resulting in hemiparesis\. Participant demographics and survey responses were summarized using descriptive analyses\. Subgroup analyses were performed between patients and caregivers and by sex, age group, and type of last stroke\. A short version of the Stroke\-Specific QoL \(SS\-QoL\) scale was used to assess patient QoL\. Results The study included 221 patients and 62 caregivers answering on behalf of patients\. Almost all patients \(98%\) experienced PSS symptoms after their most recent stroke, with 59% experiencing ≥3 symptoms\. Approximately half \(56%\) of patients who reported PSS symptoms were aware of drug treatments; of these, most \(95%\) had received ≥1 drug treatment\. Among treated patients, 68% had been involved in the initial drug selection\. Over half of patients reported difficulties carrying out daily activities, but caregivers were more likely to report difficulty showering or bathing unassisted \(84%\) compared with the patient group \(58%\); fatigue was reported by most patients \(84%\)\. The overall median \(IQR\) SS\-QoL score was 2\.5 \(2\.0–2\.9\) and was higher in the patient group \(2\.5; 2\.1–2\.9\) than the caregiver\-reported group \(2\.1; 1\.8–2\.8\)\. Our real\-world survey findings demonstrate a considerable impact of PSS on patient QoL, largely driven by fatigue and limitations in daily activities\. Furthermore, subgroup analysis revealed significant differences between patient and caregiver perceptions of PSS symptoms and their impact\. Discussion This study highlights the need for increased awareness of PSS among healthcare providers, patients, and caregivers to promote timely diagnosis and improve management with targeted, multidisciplinary interventions that enhance patient outcomes and support caregivers\.

## [Multidrug\-resistant monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34 strain producing blaNDM\-5 carbapenemase isolated from a patient with rectal cancer in Hainan, China: comprehensive whole genome dissection of antibiotic resistance and virulence determinants](../publications/50d7d019af37a4893f07.md)

Shan Zhong; Lei Xing; Licheng Wang; Chongzhen Wang; Xiaoying Fu; Lixia Xu; Yuanli Li; Huaxiong Zhu; Lvfen He; Xiong Zhu; Huan Li

Background Here, we report the identification and comprehensive whole\-genome characterization of a New Delhi metallo\-β\-lactamase 5 \( bla NDM\-5 \)\-producing multidrug\-resistant \(MDR\) monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium ST34 strain SYA001 from an immunocompromised rectal cancer patient\. Monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium \( Salmonella enterica subsp\. enterica serovar 1,4,\[5\],12:i:\-\) is one of the leading causative agents of foodborne gastroenteritis and hospitalization worldwide, and the rapid emergence and spread of carbapenem\-resistant strains have severely compromised clinical treatment and posed a major threat to public health\. Methods In this study, a series of standardized phenotypic assays were performed to characterize the microbiological, biochemical, and antimicrobial resistance profiles of strain SYA001\. Matrix\-assisted laser desorption/ionization time\-of\-flight mass spectrometry \(MALDI\-TOF MS\), biochemical identification, and slide agglutination serotyping were used for species and serotype confirmation\. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the VITEK 2 compact system, and six types of carbapenemases were screened via a colloidal gold immunochromatographic assay\. Whole\-genome sequencing \(WGS\) was performed on the DNBSEQ\-T7 platform, and a comprehensive bioinformatics pipeline was applied to dissect the genomic structure, phylogenetic characteristics, antibiotic resistance determinants, plasmid profiles, prophage regions, Salmonella pathogenicity islands \(SPIs\), and protein\-protein interaction \(PPI\) network of the strain\. Results Our results confirmed that SYA001 is a serovar 1,4,\[5\],12:i:\- monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium belonging to the globally epidemic ST34 clone\. The strain exhibited an MDR phenotype, with resistance to 7 classes of antibiotics including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides, and was only susceptible to aztreonam, amikacin, tigecycline, and colistin\. Genomic analysis identified the core carbapenem resistance gene bla NDM\-5 , along with multiple coexisting resistance genes including bla OXA\-10 , qnrS 1, tet \(A\), sul 2, and sul 3 and so on\. Four plasmid replicons \(IncHI2, IncHI2A, IncQ1, p0111\), 15 prophage regions, and a complete set of virulence\-related SPIs \(SPI\-1 to SPI\-5,SPI\-9, SPI\-13, SPI\-14\) were detected\. PPI network analysis revealed AcrA as the core hub of the efflux\-mediated resistance regulatory network\. Conclusion This study provides genomic insights into bla NDM\-5 \-producing MDR monophasic Salmonella\. Typhimurium from an immunocompromised rectal cancer patient, supplements clinical surveillance data of carbapenem\-resistant Salmonella in Hainan\.

## [KONSULTASI KEAGAMAAN DI ERA AI: PERBANDINGAN RESPONS CHATGPT DAN GEMINI TERHADAP KASUS\-KASUS MODERASI BERAGAMA](../publications/50e0009e46b27bb65eea.md)

Nazwa Niswatusshofiyah; Raudlatul Intan Nurul Balqies; Iksan Kamil Sahri; Muhammad Bachrul Ulum

The shift of religious consultation from traditional authorities toward artificial intelligence \(AI\) chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini raises new challenges for Islamic Religious Education, particularly regarding the accuracy, consistency, and level of moderation in the responses generated\. This study aims to compare the capabilities of ChatGPT and Gemini in providing religious consultation based on four religious moderation indicators established by the Ministry of Religious Affairs, namely tolerance, national commitment, anti violence, and acceptance of local traditions, as well as to examine the sensitivity of responses to framing and their consistency across repeated prompts\. The study employs the Comparative AI Religious Consultation Audit \(CARCA\) method with a mixed\-method approach combining quantitative content analysis and qualitative comparative analysis\. The results show a mean score of 92\.07 for ChatGPT and 90\.90 for Gemini, with high and relatively comparable performance on the three normative\-social criteria, but markedly lower performance on religious accuracy \(around 71% for both models\)\. ChatGPT outperformed Gemini in context sensitivity, while provocative framing produced opposite effects across models, raising ChatGPT&\#x27;s score slightly while lowering Gemini&\#x27;s score\. The study concludes that both AI models are able to translate some principles of religious moderation into moderate practical advice, but cannot yet be fully relied upon as a source of religious authority, given their weaknesses in accuracy and religious textual grounding\. These findings underscore the importance of positioning AI as a companion to, rather than a replacement for, traditional religious authority\.

## [CA\-VSN: A Context\-aware Variable Selection Network with Context\-guided Cross\-attention for Personalized Recommendation](../publications/50ecfe6b65e0df9a3c97.md)

Bhumika Pahwa; Indu Kashyap; Rachna Behl

Providing personalized recommendations, depends on two complementary sources of information, one is user&\#x27;s past interactions and the second is the context in which a new decision is made\.In practice, however, combining these two sources is not straightforward\.Many existing methods either treat contextual variables too uniformly which introduces context noise\.The context noise weakens personalization as user history is utilized without adequately accounting for the current context at hand\.To address this problem, this paper proposes CA\-VSN, a Context\-Aware Variable Selection Network for highly personalized recommendation\.The model first uses a Variable Selection Network to assign instance\-specific importance weights to contextual variables and build a refined context representation\.It then applies a Context\-Gated Cross\-Attention mechanism, where the refined context vector is used to retrieve the most relevant signals from the user&\#x27;s historical interactions\.A gating function further controls how strongly historical information should influence the prediction under the current context\.CA\-VSN is evaluated on ITM\-Rec and MovieLens\-100K for both rating prediction and Top\-K recommendation\.CA\-VSN remains competitive in both score prediction and ranking with Recall@20 = 0\.831 and NDCG@20 = 0\.460 on ITM\-Rec and Recall@20 = 0\.705 and NDCG@20 = 0\.383 on MovieLens\-100K\.Additional ablation and sensitivity analyses confirm the importance of the proposed components and the robustness of the model design\.Beyond predictive performance, CA\-VSN provides inspectable feature selection and history attention signals whose behavioural relevance is supported by perturbation, stability, and counterfactual analyses\.Refining context before modelling history offers an effective approach to personalized recommendation\.

## [Efeitos do monitoramento durante a aquisição do responder sobre a manutenção do seguimento de regras](../publications/50ee99cf3d87d95a7939.md)

Letícia Fernanda da Silva; Maíra Costa Gonçalves; Mariéle Diniz Cortez

This study evaluated the effect of monitoring during the acquisition of responding on the maintenance of discrepant rule\-following\. Twenty college students, divided into two conditions, were exposed to a computerized matching\-to\-sample task\. In Phase 1 \(Acquisition of Responding\), participants were exposed to conditions in which the rule was corresponding to the contingencies in the presence \(Condition I\) or absence \(Condition II\) of the experimenter\. Phase 2 assessed, for all participants, the maintenance of rule\-following in blocks that were either corresponding or discrepant to the contingencies\. Five participants from Condition I and six participants from Condition II maintained rule\-following in the discrepant blocks\. No statistically significant difference was found in the number of correct responses in the discrepant blocks between the two conditions\. The presence of the experimenter during the acquisition phase of responding appeared to have little influence on the maintenance of following discrepant rules\.

## [Caring cannot be prompted: An Autoethnography of Becoming a Nurse Educator in an AI\-Enabled ODeL Environment](../publications/51070e257046451b500e.md)

Regine Karla Bagalanon

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) integration into nursing education presents challenges to preserving the human values that define the profession\. While AI offers opportunities to enhance teaching and learning, it raises questions about authentic learning, educator identity, and the place of human caring in technology\-mediated environments\. Guided by Watson&\#x27;s Theory of Human Caring, this analytic autoethnography examined the evolving identity of a nurse educator across intersecting roles as a registered nurse, Open and Distance e\-Learning \(ODeL\) learner, and educator during the emergence of generative AI \(GenAI\)\. Personal experiences across these roles traced how the understanding of caring evolved—from recognizing vulnerability in clinical practice to intentionally designing learning experiences that cultivate reflection, educator presence, and authentic engagement in an AI\-enabled classroom\. The findings demonstrated that AI did not diminish caring; rather, it clarified the distinctly human dimensions of teaching that technology cannot reproduce, including ethical judgment, compassion, meaningful relationships, and reflective practice\. These experiences further demonstrated that caring could be intentionally expressed through instructional design, authentic assessment, timely feedback, and sustained educator presence, even within ODeL environments\. The study argues that the future of nursing education is not defined by the adoption of AI itself but by the capacity of educators to preserve and cultivate human caring while thoughtfully integrating technological innovation\. Ultimately, while AI may enhance learning, caring remains the moral foundation of nursing education because it cannot be automated, replicated, or prompted\.

## [Interpolation of unitaries with time\-dependent Hamiltonians via Deep Learning](../publications/510831b42e8eec1d4231.md)

Antonio Guerra; Daniel Uzcátegui Contreras; A\. Delgado; Esteban S\. Gómez

Abstract Quantum systems governed by time\-dependent Hamiltonians pose significant challenges for the accurate computation of unitary time\-evolution operators, which are essential for predicting quantum state dynamics\. In this work, we introduce a physics\-informed deep learning approach based on Physics\-Informed Neural Networks to estimate these operators over the full time domain\. By incorporating physical constraints such as unitarity and leveraging the second\-order Magnus expansion or Trotterization on the evolution operator, the proposed framework enables the estimation of unitary matrices at different time intervals\. The model is trained using simulated unitary operators and evaluated on quantum systems ranging from 2 to 6 qubits, governed by a fully non\-zero Pauli Hamiltonian\. For larger many\-body systems, specifically those with 7 and 8 qubits, the same methodology is employed to reconstruct an effective time\-dependent Hamiltonian, restricted to nearest\-neighbor Ising and XYZ Heisenberg models, from which the corresponding time\-evolution operator is computed over the entire temporal domain\. Across all system sizes, the framework achieves high gate fidelities using a limited number of unitary samples, with a statistical analysis over independent Hamiltonian realizations confirming mean fidelities close to 0\.99 and low variability\. Furthermore, once trained, the model interpolates the evolution operator with inference times substantially lower than those of a numerical interpolation baseline, indicating a potential reduction in measurement and data acquisition costs\. These results highlight the effectiveness of the approach for data\-driven simulation and identification of quantum dynamical systems, with direct relevance to quantum computing and quantum simulation applications\.

## [Auditoría tributaria digital del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas mediante el Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos en el Perú: revisión sistemática y propuesta preliminar de indicadores de riesgo](../publications/510b9de48e2d70b10184.md)

Jenny Estéfani Mejía Estela; Jorge Alejandro Tejada Carrera

La digitalización de la administración tributaria peruana ha trasladado una parte creciente del control del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas hacia registros electrónicos y cruces automatizados\. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia científica, normativa e institucional sobre auditoría tributaria digital, facturación electrónica y crédito fiscal, y derivar una propuesta preliminar de indicadores de priorización aplicables al Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos\. Se desarrolló una revisión sistemática documental guiada por PRISMA 2020, con publicaciones de 2015 a 2026, en español e inglés y con acceso a texto completo\. El flujo reportado identificó 74 registros; 29 fueron retirados antes de la evaluación a texto completo, 45 textos fueron evaluados y 22 documentos integraron la síntesis principal\. La evidencia muestra que la información electrónica mejora la trazabilidad, los cruces declarativos y la selección de casos, pero no acredita por sí misma la realidad económica de las operaciones\. A partir de la síntesis se organizaron 15 señales en cinco dimensiones: riesgo formal, declarativo, analítico\-conductual, sustantivo y de comportamiento posterior\. La propuesta utiliza ponderación equiprobable entre dimensiones y se presenta expresamente como herramienta heurística de priorización, no como índice validado ni como criterio legal de determinación tributaria\. Se concluye que la auditoría digital del crédito fiscal requiere integrar validaciones automáticas, analítica de riesgos y verificación documental y económica\.

## [The LLM\-Attacker: A Unified Red\-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems](../publications/51116e9fd0c8d8c7311d.md)

Georgios Politis; Evangelos Pappas

Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server\. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages\. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures\. We present LLM\-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation\. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring\. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass\. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested\. In a controlled GPT\-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94\.20% to 97\.38% and exact\-document recovery from 13\.71% to 37\.77%\. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two\-percentage\-point threshold fixed before testing\. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access\. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code\. The framework reports implementation checks separately from measured attack effectiveness\. Each privacy claim should state the attacker, dataset and scoring rule, report its controls and identify untested attacks\.

## [Machine learning\-based analysis of heat and mass transfer in casson hybrid nanofluid flow over a variable porous riga plate](../publications/511ee7b38e626c94495c.md)

Shajar Abbas; Syeda Farzeen Fatima Gilani; Imran Siddique; Rashid Jan; Mohammad Farooq Hakimi; Aiedh Mrisi Alharthi; Mamurakhon Toshpulatova; Ibrahim Mahariq

This study uses an artificial neural network \(ANN\) architecture in combination with the Levenberg\-Marquardt backpropagation \(LMBP\) method to investigate the impact of heat radiation on the hybrid nanofluid flow through a variable porous medium beneath a stretchy Riga plate\. The purpose of this work is driven by the increasing demand for accurately modeling complex nonlinear thermal systems involving electromagnetic control, porous media, and nanofluids, which are not sufficiently covered in the existing literature\. Single\-walled carbon nanotubes \(SWCNTs\) and multiwalled carbon nanotubes \(MWCNTs\) are suspended in propylene glycol, which is regarded as the base fluid\. The Riga plate is a plate composed of alternating electrodes as well as permanent magnets to form electromagnetic forces, which act significantly on the flow and the heat transfer properties\. The governing nonlinear partial differential equations \(PDEs\) are transformed into ordinary differential equations \(ODEs\) via similarity transformations in order to provide datasets for ANN training\. The finite difference technique \(FDM\) is then used to numerically solve these ODEs\. Then the successive over relaxation method, executed through custom MATLAB code, is used to obtain the solutions of these equations\. The novelty of the work is in the integrated evaluation of hybrid nanofluid flow over a Riga plate in a variable permeable media with radiative heat transfer, as well as the use of an ANN\-LMBP predictive model, which is trained on high\-fidelity numerical data\. The numerical data show that the thermal radiation increases the temperature distribution by about 21% in the case of SWCNT\-based nanofluid and 18% in the case of MWCNT\-based nanofluid\. The porosity parameter decreases the velocity of fluid by approximately 12%, whereas the modified Hartmann number increases the fluid velocity by 15–17%\. Additionally, SWCNTs exhibit 8–10% higher thermal conductivity compared to MWCNTs\. The ANN\-LMBP model demonstrates excellent predictive performance with a coefficient of determination R 2 &gt; 0\.998 and a mean squared error on the order of 10 −4 \. These results confirm that the proposed ANN\-based framework is a fast, accurate, and computationally efficient tool for modeling nonlinear thermal fluid systems, with significant applications in thermal management, cooling technologies, energy systems, and industrial fluid flow processes\. Clinical trial number not applicable\.

## [Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young\-like single\-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells](../publications/513f8de11542a973e698.md)

Yoseph W\. Dance; Alice Amitrano; Nicolas C\. Macaluso; Chanhong Min; Ladaisha T\. Thompson; Annaka M\. Saffron; Zhuoxu Ge; Ian Michael Smith; Charles Ezenwanne; Nicholas Milcik; Abigail Fennell; Kendall A\. Pyndell; Crystal Szczesny; Jacqueline Langdon; Jeanine A\. Ursitti; Christopher W\. Ward; Kimberly M\. Stroka; Jeremy D Walston; Sean X\. Sun; Κωνσταντίνος Κωνσταντόπουλος; Jude M\. Phillip

Aging is a complex biological process often characterized by increased vulnerability to disease, infection, and death\. This increased vulnerability is mechanistically linked to a progressive and functional decline of the immune system\. In humans, aged T cells lose their ability to effectively surveil complex microenvironments, thereby decreasing their capacity to clear infections, eradicate diseases, and maintain physiological homeostasis\. However, specific mechanisms by which aged T cells lose this capacity to surveil remain unclear\. Here, we profile three core characteristics of T cell surveillance at single\-cell resolution, specifically migration, deformability, and sensing\. While aged human T cells retain their capacity to migrate ex vivo, they exhibit impaired cellular deformability and deficiencies in sensing local biological signals\. To modulate this surveillance defect, we perform mechanical reprogramming using elevated fluid viscosity\. Results indicate that acute priming of aged T cells with elevated fluid viscosity recovers a transient young\-like surveillance phenotype, particularly within CD4\+ memory T cell populations\. This recovered young\-like phenotype is mechanistically linked to elevated SDF\-1α receptor expression together with increased membrane tension, cortical F\-actin, and Arp3 expression\. Altogether, these findings identify a key source of surveillance defects among aged T cells and offer an effective mechano\-inducible strategy for modulating single\-cell behaviors\. Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function\. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells\. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity\. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4\+ T cells\.

## [Improving Laboratory Test Turnaround Time Through Collaboration Between Secretary Nurses, Laboratory Specialists, and Medical Records Professionals](../publications/51410b8292b28f534dea.md)



Background: Laboratory test turnaround time \(TAT\) is a critical quality indicator in healthcare It has a direct impact on patient safety, emergency department productivity, clinical decision\-making, and general healthcare quality\.Delays in laboratory testing often arise from communication failures, incomplete documentation, inefficient specimen management, and fragmented interdisciplinary collaboration\.Objective: This review explores how structured collaboration among secretary nurses, laboratory specialists, and medical records professionals can significantly improve laboratory turnaround time while enhancing patient safety and workflow efficiency\.Methods: A narrative review of current healthcare quality improvement literature was conducted\.Evidence regarding laboratory workflow optimization, health information management, interdisciplinary teamwork, electronic medical records \(EMRs\), and laboratory information systems \(LIS\) was synthesized to identify collaborative strategies that reduce delays throughout the laboratory testing cycle\.Results: Successful collaboration improves every phase of laboratory testing, including order entry, specimen collection, transportation, analysis, result reporting, and documentation\.Digital integration, standardized communication, and clearly defined professional responsibilities significantly reduce turnaround time and decrease laboratory errors\.Conclusion: Improving laboratory performance can be achieved through the establishment of cooperative multidisciplinary workflows backed by electronic information systems, increasing patient satisfaction, and promoting healthcare quality\.
