## [Prevalência e preditores de gravidade da ideação suicida em portadores do transtorno afetivo bipolar tipo I: uma revisão narrativa](../publications/51485be8eadb0d685d18.md)

Ricardo Augusto Silva Costa; Thifanie Janch; Sofia da Silveira Joaquim; Leonardo Evangelista de Souza; Lucas Yuji Venancio Sato

Introdução e objetivo: O transtorno afetivo bipolar tipo I \(TAB I\) figura entre os transtornos psiquiátricos com maior risco de comportamento suicida, constituindo importante causa de morbimortalidade e incapacidade\. A ideação suicida representa um marcador precoce de agravamento clínico e associa\-se à ocorrência de tentativas e suicídio consumado\. Entretanto, a heterogeneidade dos fatores relacionados à sua ocorrência e progressão dificulta a estratificação do risco e o planejamento de intervenções preventivas\. Objetivou\-se sintetizar as evidências acerca da prevalência da ideação suicida e dos principais preditores de gravidade em indivíduos com TAB I\. \(DEMPSEY et al\., 2024; DEV et al\., 2024\)\.Método: Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, com busca estruturada nas bases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science e LILACS\. Foram utilizados descritores DeCS/MeSH e palavras\-chave relacionados ao transtorno afetivo bipolar tipo I, ideação suicida e fatores de risco, combinados pelos operadores booleanos AND e OR\. Incluíram\-se estudos publicados entre 2020 e 2025, nos idiomas português, inglês e espanhol\. A estratégia de busca identificou 619 registros\. Após a remoção de 411 duplicatas, procedeu\-se à triagem por títulos e resumos, seguida da leitura dos textos completos potencialmente elegíveis\. Ao final, 19 estudos atenderam aos critérios de inclusão e compuseram a síntese narrativa\. \(ARNONE et al\., 2024; DEMPSEY et al\., 2024\)\.Resultados: Os estudos demonstraram elevada prevalência de ideação suicida ao longo da evolução do TAB I, sobretudo durante episódios depressivos e estados mistos\. História prévia de tentativa de suicídio, desesperança, impulsividade, sintomas depressivos intensos, ansiedade comórbida, uso de substâncias psicoativas, recorrência de episódios afetivos e baixa adesão ao tratamento destacaram\-se como os preditores de gravidade mais consistentes\. Em contrapartida, acompanhamento especializado, uso regular de estabilizadores do humor, especialmente o lítio, e reconhecimento precoce das alterações clínicas mostraram\-se associados à redução do risco de progressão para tentativa de suicídio e morte por suicídio\. \(DEMPSEY et al\., 2024; DEV et al\., 2024; TONDO; BALDESSARINI, 2024\)\.Conclusão: A ideação suicida constitui manifestação frequente e clinicamente relevante no TAB I, sendo influenciada por múltiplos fatores clínicos, psicológicos e sociais\. A identificação precoce dos preditores de gravidade favorece a estratificação do risco, subsidia intervenções preventivas e pode contribuir para reduzir tentativas de suicídio e mortalidade\. A incorporação rotineira da avaliação do comportamento suicida no acompanhamento desses pacientes representa medida essencial para qualificar a assistência em saúde mental\. \(ARNONE et al\., 2024; DEV et al\., 2024\)\.

## [COVID\-19 Geçiren Böbrek Nakli Alıcılarında Persistan veya Kötüleşen Lenfopeni Mortaliteyi Öngörür: Lymphopenia in KTRs with COVID\-19](../publications/514abdc088f669954101.md)

Ali Can Kurtipek; Merve Öztürk; Ali B\. Bozdogan; Ezgi Çoşkun Yenigün; Emin Gemcioğlu; Osman İnan; Enes Seyda Şahiner; Oğuzhan Zengin; Selma Karaahmetoğlu; İhsan Ateş; Fatih Dede

Objective: Kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk for severe coronavirus disease\-2019 \(COVID\-19\) because of chronic immunosuppressive therapy and impaired cellular immunity\. Lymphopenia is a well\-established predictor of adverse outcomes in the general population; however, the prognostic significance of persistent lymphopenia during hospitalization in kidney transplant recipients remains poorly defined\. This study aimed to evaluate the association between persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia and clinical outcomes, including mortality and renal function, in hospitalized kidney transplant recipients with COVID\-19\.Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult kidney transplant recipients hospitalized with laboratory\-confirmed COVID\-19 at a tertiary referral center between March 2020 and January 2022\. Patients were classified based on the presence or absence of persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia during hospitalization\. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory findings, treatments, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups\. The primary outcome was in\-hospital mortality\. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit \(ICU\) admission, requirement for respiratory support, requirement for invasive mechanical ventilation, length of hospital stay, requirement for hemodialysis, and renal function at 90 days after discharge\. Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis\.Results: A total of 181 kidney transplant recipients were included, 63% of whom developed persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia\. Patients with persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia experienced significantly higher rates of ICU admission, respiratory support, invasive mechanical ventilation, prolonged hospitalization, and in\-hospital mortality compared with other patients \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. They also had significantly higher levels of inflammatory markers, including ferritin and C\-reactive protein\. In multivariable analysis, persistent/exacerbated lymphopenia remained independently associated with in\-hospital mortality after adjustment for age, inflammatory markers, and hemodialysis requirement \[adjusted odds ratio 14\.16 \(95% confidence interval: 3\.6\-55\.7\), p &lt; 0\.001\]\. However, persistent lymphopenia was not associated with loss of renal function at 90 days\.Conclusion: Persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia during hospitalization is a strong independent predictor of in\-hospital mortality among kidney transplant recipients with COVID\-19 and is associated with greater disease severity and increased resource utilization\. In contrast, it does not appear to predict 90\-day renal function decline\. Serial assessment of lymphocyte counts may provide a simple, inexpensive, and readily available tool for early risk stratification in hospitalized kidney transplant recipients with COVID\-19\.

## [Corporate ethical and responsible AI \(CERAi\) and AI trustworthiness: a lifecycle perspective and empirical insights](../publications/51518b34dacec25398f0.md)

Rupak Rauniar; Qing Ray Cao; Steve Bin Zhou; Amaani Rauniar

Purpose This study develops and empirically validates a Corporate Ethical and Responsible AI \(CERAi\) lifecycle framework\. The framework comprises three interdependent stages: design and development, testing and training, and deployment and usage\. The study aims to move the research beyond abstract principles and policy analyses toward empirically grounded, lifecycle\-integrated artificial intelligence AI governance theory\. It positions ethical AI and responsible AI governance as the two constitutive components of the CERAi construct, and AI trustworthiness as a conceptually and empirically distinct downstream outcome anchored in stage\-specific organizational governance mechanisms\. The CERAi framework is scoped broadly to encompass governance of both conventional/traditional machine learning models and autonomous AI agents operating within organizational settings\. Design/methodology/approach We administered a large\-scale survey to 500 attendees at a national AI conference in the United States in early 2026, yielding 143 useable responses from AI professionals across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail and energy sectors\. We developed and validated multi\-item scales for each CERAi lifecycle stage using established ethical AI and AI governance frameworks\. Structural equation modeling was employed to assess the measurement model and to test both direct path hypotheses and mediation hypotheses\. Findings Both CERAIi design and development and CERAi deployment and usage have significant positive direct effects on AI trustworthiness, whereas CERAi testing and training do not\. Our results also indicate a significant serial mediation pathway in which CERAi deployment and usage enhance AI trustworthiness through testing and training, followed by design and development\. Conversely, testing and training alone do not mediate the relationship between deployment and usage and AI trustworthiness, indicating that design\-stage ethics serve as an intervening \(mediating\) mechanism through which governance activity enacted at later lifecycle stages is associated with perceived AI trustworthiness\. This is consistent with testing and training&\#x27;s association with trustworthiness operating indirectly, mediated by the ethical architecture established during the design and development stage\. Originality/value Findings of this study demonstrate that AI trustworthiness reflects differentiated perceived salience across AI lifecycle stages, whereby stakeholders appear to weight visible, deployment\-stage governance more heavily than upstream design and testing stage governance in forming trustworthiness judgments, rather than reflecting a definitive validation that governance effects accumulate uniformly across all stages in isolation\. This study makes a distinctive contribution by providing empirical evidence for a governance\-sequencing mechanism, whereby design\-stage ethics function as a mediating pathway shaping the effectiveness of governance activity at later lifecycle stages\. To the best of our knowledge, such a mediated, stage\-sequential mechanism has not previously been demonstrated using primary data within a comprehensive, three\-stage CERAi lifecycle framework linking organizational ethical and responsible governance practices to AI trustworthiness outcomes\.

## [E Evaluasi Efisiensi Biaya dan Waktu Pembangunan Infrastruktur Transportasi Berbasis Building Information Modeling \(BIM\) Studi Kasus Jembatan Wai Ela : Evaluasi Efisiensi Biaya dan Waktu Pembangunan Infrastruktur Transportasi Berbasis Building Information Modeling \(BIM\) Studi Kasus Jembatan Wai Ela](../publications/516078ec27caa798c158.md)

Kurniasih Rahmadhani Lasinta

Conventional construction projects often face various challenges, including cost overruns, inaccurate quantity estimations, and delays in project completion\. This study evaluates cost and time efficiency in the construction of the Wai Ela Bridge in Maluku Province by integrating Building Information Modeling \(BIM\) using Autodesk Revit and Navisworks software with the probabilistic Program Evaluation and Review Technique \(PERT\)\. Based on the analysis results, the implementation of BIM and PERT yielded an optimized project duration of 437 days under the second trial scenario, representing a time efficiency improvement of 24\.52% compared with the actual project duration of 579 days\. In addition, the revised total estimated cost resulted in savings of IDR 1,829,862,541 \(7\.12%\) compared with the actual project cost\. An analysis of delay factors using Fisher’s exact test indicated that contractor management aspects, particularly inadequate field investigations, had a significant influence on delays in material procurement\.

## [GWDRO\-Lung: Gromov–Wasserstein distributionally robust learning for calibrated pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction across imaging cohorts](../publications/5175c9e72aafa340d335.md)

Yubo Yan; An Yan; Wen Li; Jianlong Bu; Jinfeng Ning

Low\-dose chest computed tomography \(CT\) screening detects pulmonary nodules whose malignancy risk must be triaged, yet deep\-learning risk models often lose both accuracy and calibration when transferred to a different scanner, protocol, or population\. We developed GWDRO\-Lung, a chest CT framework that treats cross\-cohort transfer as a coupled problem of structural mismatch, distributional instability, and calibration\. A weight\-shared three\-dimensional encoder with embedded acquisition metadata summarizes each cohort as a relation matrix over learned prototypes; cohort geometries are aligned to a shared Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter; and a distributionally robust, calibration\-aware risk head estimates malignancy, with the residual alignment error setting a cohort\-specific robustness radius\. The model was developed on 1842 pulmonary nodules from LIDC\-IDRI, organized into three acquisition\-defined cohorts, and validated externally on 618 nodules from the independent LNDb cohort, with leave\-one\-cohort\-out, protocol\-shift, size\-stratified, and decision\-curve analyses\. Relative to the strongest recent imaging baseline, external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve improved from 0\.857 to 0\.878, external expected calibration error fell from 0\.106 to 0\.066, worst\-cohort AUC rose from 0\.829 to 0\.851, and net benefit was higher across triage\-relevant thresholds\. Prospective, pathology\-confirmed validation is required before clinical use\.

## [Biometric Personal Data Processing in Employer Information Systems: Principles and Limitations](../publications/517c2e30a334928e39de.md)

Менкенов Алексей Владимирович

The paper provides a comparative legal analysis of the regulation of the processing of biometric data of employees in the Russian Federation and the countries of the European Union\. A key problem emerges: the Russian legal model, while formally declaring the priority of the subject&\#x27;s consent, in practice allows for broad exceptions justified by state and corporate interests, without proper verification of their proportionality\. This leads to the erosion of the individual&\#x27;s sphere of private autonomy and creates the risk of establishing hyper\-control over employees\. The European model, based on the General Data Protection Regulation \(GDPR\), establishes a more balanced regime where prohibition is the rule, and any exception must be strictly justified and supported by principles such as proportionality, data minimization, transparency, and security\. A key tool for complying with these principles is the mandatory data protection impact assessment \(DPIA\)\. The author substantiates the need to improve Russian legislation, arguing that this entails the risks of violating the constitutional principle of respect for working people, the right to privacy, and the fundamental duty of the state to ensure personal freedom\. In conclusion, specific measures are proposed to improve Russian legislation, in particular the introduction of mandatory data processing impact assessments and the development of specialized methodological recommendations for employers\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Financial Reporting and Auditing: Challenges and Future Opportunities](../publications/517e8915746b3ef100b9.md)

Dr Rajesh Kumar; Lalita Babulal Malusare; Dr\. Farhan Alam; Snehasish Bhattacharjee; Harmanpreet Singh

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has become a game\-changer in the world of financial reporting and auditing, revolutionizing the traditional methods of accounting and auditing by automating tasks, providing predictive insights, intelligent decision making, and real\-time data processing\. This research delves into the integration of AI into accounting systems, financial reporting and the auditing landscape, presenting challenges, governance issues and future prospects\. The potential areas of the application of AI are covered, including automated bookkeeping, intelligent financial reporting, fraud detection, continuous auditing, blockchain\-based assurance systems and AI\-based sustainability reporting\. Furthermore, the paper highlights several issues associated with algorithmic bias, transparency and explainability, cyber security, ethical implications and regulatory uncertainties in AI\-powered accounting systems\. In addition, the study examines key strategic implications for accounting firms, auditors, regulators, and policymakers on the use of AI, such as the importance of governance, the role of AI in human\-AI partnerships, and the need for professional competency development\. Moreover, the study identifies future trends and opportunities of autonomous accounting systems, generative AI, integrated ESG reporting and intelligent audit ecosystems\. The results imply that AI can improve the quality of reporting, effectiveness of an audit, operational efficiency, and strategic financial decision\-making\. However, a balance is needed between technology innovation, ethical governance, regulatory supervision and professional judgment of humans for sustainable adoption of AI\. The study offers a conceptual base for future research in intelligent financial reporting and auditing environment and also adds to the literature of intelligent accounting systems\.

Хамидов Нурмухаммад Ориф угли

The article examines comparative legal models of liability for crimes committed using artificial intelligence technologies\. The approaches of Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the United States, China, and Kazakhstan are compared with the risk\-based regulatory model of the European Union\. The study explores the role of artificial intelligence as a means of committing a crime, the doctrinal debate over recognizing artificial intelligence as an independent subject of crime, and the difficulties in establishing guilt and causation arising from autonomous decision\-making\. The study substantiates that the violation of sector\-specific safety obligations does not, in itself, automatically entail criminal liability\. A three\-stage assessment model combining technological neutrality, personal culpability, and legally established supervisory obligations is proposed\. Specific proposals are developed for the legislation and judicial practice of Uzbekistan concerning the legal qualification of the use of artificial intelligence, technical examination of algorithms, and the delineation of liability for negligence\.

## [Evaluación universitaria después de la inteligencia artificial generativa](../publications/51a0654eff6f25d95ba0.md)

Joseph Michael Valero Rodríguez; Carlos Fernando Castillo Montenegro; David Israel Báez Herrera; Darwin Paul Pozo Pilacuán; Omar Aníbal Riofrio Olaya

La expansión de la inteligencia artificial generativa está transformando profundamente la forma en que las universidades enseñan, aprenden y evalúan\. Este libro analiza los desafíos que surgen cuando herramientas capaces de producir textos, resolver problemas, generar argumentos y apoyar múltiples tareas académicas intervienen en procesos tradicionalmente utilizados para demostrar aprendizaje\. Frente a este escenario, se propone superar una visión centrada únicamente en la detección del uso de inteligencia artificial y avanzar hacia modelos evaluativos capaces de hacer visible la comprensión, el razonamiento, la toma de decisiones y la responsabilidad del estudiante\. La obra examina la transformación de la evaluación universitaria, el fortalecimiento de la evaluación auténtica, la incorporación de evidencias de proceso y trazabilidad, así como el valor de las modalidades orales, prácticas y situadas\. También aborda los nuevos desafíos relacionados con integridad académica, autoría humana, transparencia y uso responsable de sistemas generativos\. A lo largo de sus capítulos se plantea que la inteligencia artificial no debe entenderse únicamente como una amenaza para la evaluación, sino como un factor que obliga a revisar prácticas tradicionales y fortalecer aquellas que permiten demostrar aprendizaje de manera más completa\. El desafío universitario consiste en diseñar evaluaciones donde la tecnología pueda estar presente sin sustituir la participación intelectual, manteniendo visibles la autonomía, el juicio y la capacidad del estudiante para responder por aquello que produce\.

## [Development and In\-vitro Characterization of Zaltoprofen Loaded Silver Nanoparticle Containing Gel for Treatment of Pain of Rheumatoid Arthriti](../publications/51a3b4049d646d05489c.md)

Sheetal Sharma; Nancy Pal; Bhartendu Sharma; Vikram Jeet Singh; Alka Sharma; Swati Sharma; Dr\. Saurabh Saklani; Kritika \.

The chronic inflammatory condition known as rheumatoid arthritis is characterized by joint swelling, stiffness, and destruction to the surrounding cartilage and bone\. It is an autoimmune disease that is impacted by things like obesity and smoking\. By generating interleukin and, cytokines play a crucial role in the degradation of the synovium and cartilage in the joints\. Skeletal muscle abnormalities are common in patients with rheumatoid arthritis\. The causes, “pathology”, “development”, “symptoms”, clinical consequences, “diagnosis”, “treatment” choices, medicines, and current patents and applications are all covered in detail in this study on rheumatoid arthritis\. ## [RECENT TRENDS IN LIPOSOMAL NANOCARRIERS FOR ANTIMICROBIAL THERAPY](../publications/51abef183ea27b4513b6.md)

Amit Kumar\*, Jyoti Verma, Dr\. Sanjay Kushwaha

Microbial infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge due to the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\), multidrug\-resistant \(MDR\) pathogens, and the limited effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial therapies\. Traditional antimicrobial agents often suffer from poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid systemic clearance, inadequate tissue penetration, and dose\-limiting toxicity, resulting in suboptimal therapeutic outcomes\. Liposomal nanocarriers have emerged as a promising nanotechnology\-based drug delivery platform capable of addressing many of these limitations through enhanced drug encapsulation, targeted delivery, controlled release, and improved pharmacokinetic behavior\. This review comprehensively discusses recent advances in liposomal nanocarriers for antimicrobial therapy, focusing on their structural characteristics, classification, formulation techniques, physicochemical properties, and mechanisms of microbial targeting and drug release\. Furthermore, the review highlights the therapeutic applications of liposomal systems against bacterial, fungal, viral, and biofilm\-associated infections, with particular emphasis on their role in overcoming antimicrobial resistance and enhancing intracellular drug delivery\. Recent innovations, including PEGylated \(stealth\), ligand\-targeted, cationic, and stimuli\-responsive liposomes, are critically examined for their ability to improve therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity\. In addition, the review summarizes clinically approved liposomal antimicrobial formulations, recent preclinical and clinical developments, and the challenges associated with large\-scale manufacturing, formulation stability, regulatory approval, and commercialization\. Emerging trends such as multifunctional liposomes, combination nanotherapies, artificial intelligence\-assisted formulation design, and personalized antimicrobial nanomedicine are also discussed\. Overall, liposomal nanocarriers represent a versatile and clinically relevant drug delivery strategy with considerable potential to enhance antimicrobial therapy, improve patient outcomes, and contribute to combating the global burden of infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance\.

## [Translational maturity of artificial intelligence\-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases](../publications/51af0d226f8cebbcc384.md)

Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou

Electrocardiography is a widely available and low\-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence\-enabled electrocardiography \(AI\-ECG\) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation\. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit\. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI\-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis\. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking\. Seventy\-seven publications informed the review\. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference\-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes\. AI\-ECG has progressed furthest in ST\-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced\-left\-ventricular\-ejection\-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic\-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule\-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation\. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation\. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long\-term heart\-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation\-stage or risk\-enrichment applications\. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating\-threshold selection, and limited patient\-outcome evidence\. AI\-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician\-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways\.

## [Thirty\-day clinical outcomes, early recovery, and healthcare resource use after planned ambulatory vs\. conventional inpatient laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a propensity\-score overlap\-weighted retrospective cohort study](../publications/51bde64a3fcbea952ccc.md)

Yi Hao; Yi Wang; Qinyang Du; Rongshen Guan; Qirui Zhang; Gaopeng Li

Background Real\-world comparisons of planned ambulatory and conventional inpatient laparoscopic cholecystectomy are vulnerable to patient selection and organisational differences\. We used propensity score overlap weighting to compare 30\-day safety, early recovery, and recorded healthcare resource use between the two planned pathways\. Methods This single\-centre retrospective cohort included 223 adults who underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for benign gallstone\-related disease at Shanxi Bethune Hospital between May 2025 and June 2026\. Patients were classified by their preoperative plan as ambulatory \(defined as arrival on the day of surgery and intended discharge within 24 h\) or conventional inpatient care\. The primary outcome was a 30\-day adverse clinical composite comprising Clavien–Dindo grade ≥2 complications, unplanned emergency department visits, readmission, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography or another intervention, reoperation, or death\. Overlap weights balanced preoperative characteristics, and 1:1 propensity score matching served as a sensitivity analysis\. Results The ambulatory and inpatient groups included 78 and 145 patients, respectively\. All included covariates demonstrated absolute standardised mean differences below 0\.10 after overlap weighting\. Weighted risks of the 30\-day composite were 3\.8% and 10\.2%, giving a risk ratio of 0\.37 \(95% confidence interval, 0\.02 to 1\.25\) and a risk difference of −6\.4 percentage points \(−13\.8 to 1\.4; P = 0\.100\)\. The ambulatory pathway was associated with 70\.3 fewer postoperative hours and 100\.0 fewer total hospital hours\. Ambulation and oral intake occurred 5\.7 and 6\.9 h earlier, discharge pain was 1\.13 points lower, and recorded index\-admission hospital charges were CNY 5,200 lower; all P &lt; 0\.001\. Seven ambulatory patients \(9\.0%\) had pathway failure\. Results from 59 matched pairs were directionally consistent\. Conclusions Among patients with a realistic possibility of receiving either pathway, planned ambulatory care was not associated with an increase in the 30\-day adverse clinical composite and was associated with shorter hospital stay and lower recorded healthcare resource utilisation\. However, important determinants of pathway selection were incompletely measured\. The single\-centre observational design, residual confounding, and small number of primary events preclude causal interpretation or claims of safety equivalence\.

## [Potential Molecular Links Between Triclosan Exposure and Prostate Cancer: An Integrative Computational Analysis](../publications/51c23a46ace101df46b3.md)

Hongyang You; Yunlu Zou; Jiatong Liu; Yinghao Xiao; Jixin Li; Jiahui Xu; Wei Xu

Triclosan \(TCS\) is a widely used antimicrobial and endocrine\-disrupting chemical whose potential relevance to prostate cancer \(PCa\) biology remains insufficiently understood\. We integrated multi\-omics and computational analyses to identify candidate targets that overlap between predicted TCS\-related molecular targets and PCa\-related transcriptomic alterations\. Cross\-database target mapping, differential expression, and network analyses were combined with machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Mendelian randomization, and single\-cell transcriptomic profiling\. Pathway analyses highlighted oxidative stress and metabolic dysregulation as key processes shared between predicted TCS\-related targets and PCa\-associated transcriptomic alterations\. Machine learning prioritized five candidate genes—FERMT2, F5, PRKCA, ABCC4, and ACOX2—with discriminative value for PCa classification in the analyzed cohorts\. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported plausible binding compatibility of TCS to ABCC4 and ACOX2\. Mendelian randomization suggested that genetically predicted ABCC4 expression may be associated with PCa risk\. Single\-cell analysis further showed cell\-type\-specific expression of candidate genes in tumor\-enriched epithelial populations\. These findings provide an integrative framework for generating mechanistic hypotheses on how TCS\-related molecular targets may be associated with PCa biology\.

## [Emojis as socio\-emotional cues in EFL learning: a narrative conceptual review of affect, relatedness, and well\-being](../publications/51c387fc5703bf67c670.md)

Shamim Akhter; Abdulrazaq Alzahrani; Rabindra Dev Prasad Prasad; Musarat Shaheen

Emojis can modify the emotional and relational interpretation of digital messages, but their contribution to learner well\-being in English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) education remains uncertain\. This narrative conceptual review brings together purposively selected research on emojis, educational communication, and language learner emotions\. It distinguishes direct emoji evidence in EFL from emoji research in other settings, earlier emoticon studies, and contextual evidence on digital learning without an isolated emoji component\. Self\-determination theory provides the principal account of how perceived support might influence relatedness and motivation; digital semiotics explains cue interpretation, while broaden\-and\-build theory and a multidimensional view of well\-being delimit possible affective processes and distal outcomes\. The proposed model connects an emoji and its accompanying text to appraisals of communicative intent, warmth, appropriateness, and competence\. These appraisals may influence affect and relatedness, with subsequent implications for willingness to communicate and engagement\. Culture, familiarity, message purpose, sender identity, and relationship history condition these links\. Selected studies support specific effects on interpretation, impressions, self\-efficacy, or immediate task performance; they do not establish that emojis produce enduring well\-being or resilience in EFL learners\. The review develops testable propositions, considers adverse and null effects, and offers context\-sensitive pedagogical implications\. Its contribution is a bounded account of how small instructional cues might matter and what evidence is required to establish their consequences\.

## [The Good, the Bad, and the Language: Capturing Implicit Social Evaluation of Personality Traits via the Fill‑Mask Association Test](../publications/51e09ed7412cd886ea47.md)

Shenglu Ye

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether linguistic evaluation of personality traits\-the association of trait words with good versus bad in natural language\-constitutes a diffuse halo or is selectively amplified for dimensions central to social functioning\. METHOD: Using the Fill\-Mask Association Test \(FMAT\), the present study extracted log probability ratios \(LPR\) of good vs\. bad from 12 BERT models across three sentence contexts for 733 personality adjectives\. These LPR scores were compared with human normative ratings \(valence, social desirability, and observability\) and with Big Five structure derived from three independent lexical taxonomies\. RESULTS: Language\-based LPR scores correlated strongly with human valence \(r = 0\.926\) and social desirability \(r = 0\.931\), but weakly with observability \(r = 0\.235\)\. Across three independent lexical taxonomies, Agreeableness and Conscientiousness exhibited larger evaluative gaps than Extraversion, which showed the smallest gap\. CONCLUSIONS: Linguistic evaluation is not a uniform halo but is functionally calibrated to traits relevant to social cooperation and moral obligation\. The FMAT provides a scalable, reproducible tool for extracting implicit evaluative maps from language\.

## [Schizophrenia research in 2026: report from the annual meeting of the Schizophrenia International Research Society](../publications/51e184a28dc36ddc1450.md)

Lena K\. Palaniyappan; Boutheina Abassi; Fatme Abboud; Mohammed Alarabi; Maite Aramburu; Berat Arslan; Catherine V\. Barnes\-Scheufler; Annkathrin Böke; Linda Bryant; Patricio Carvajal\-Paredes; Santiago Castiello de Obeso; Anson Kai Chun Chau; Lawrence Kin\-hei Chung; Franciska de Beer; Giuseppe De Simone; Pedro Henrique Destro; Mona Dlikan; Chaimaa El Mouslih; Zhiqian Fang; Ramon Reis; Abigail L Gee; Yohannes Gebreegziabhere Haile; Fernando Gonzales\-Aste; Sean Halstead; Rui He; Héctor Hernández\-Ruiz; Federica Iannotta; Samantha Johnstone; Merel Koster; Merridee J\. Lefner; Camila Marcelino Loureiro; Xuemei Ma; Alessandra Martinelli; Gisela Mezquida; Mylène Moyal; Jennifer Murphy; Zui C\. Narita; Soyolsaikhan Odkhuu; Pavo Orepić; Rafaella Ormond; María Ortuño; Kristoffer J\. Panganiban; In‐Kyung Park; Mathilde Parisi; Gabriele Pezzullo; Finn Rabe; Upasana Ravinder; Qian Ren; Elif Sarisik; Pierfrancesco Sarti; Àlex G\. Segura; Pedro Henrique Minotto Serafim; Seo Ho Song; Erik Vélez\-Pérez; Burcu Verim; Alban Voppel; Yuji Yamada

Abstract SIRS 2026, held under the theme “Schizophrenia Research in the Era of Artificial Intelligence,” brought together researchers, clinicians, and persons with lived experience to take stock of a field whose tools for measuring, predicting, and intervening in psychosis have expanded rapidly\. Themes spanned artificial intelligence, automated speech analysis, retinal imaging, computational modelling, and novel psychosocial and pharmacological targets, with evidence that, individually, warrants cautious but serious attention and that, collectively, points toward a more mechanistically grounded psychiatry\. A recurring call across the meeting was for rigorous external validation, equitable implementation, and sustained scrutiny of underlying assumptions, including whether existing diagnostic categories and treatment targets remain adequate\. Some areas remained underworked relative to their importance, including translating basic neuroscience advances into questions relevant to patients and families, and the structural determinants of illness onset and treatment access\. Perhaps the most significant development at SIRS 2026 was not any single scientific finding but the broadening of whose voices and experiences are treated as evidence worth taking seriously in this era of AI, a shift whose consolidation remains a question for the field as much as for any individual programme of work\.

## [Inpatient continuous glucose monitoring halves the risk of hypoglycemia in patients with hyperinsulinism](../publications/51f2bfb3b85eecc55c9d.md)

Chloe Chandra; Shamani De Silva; Sarah Worthington; Indraneel Banerjee; Chris Worth

Introduction Patients with congenital hyperinsulinism \(HI\) face recurrent and unpredictable hypoglycemia\. Conventional inpatient monitoring relies on intermittent fingerprick glucose testing, which is burdensome for pediatric patients and risks missing hypoglycemic episodes between tests\. Continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\) provides high granularity, complimentary monitoring but with unproven efficacy to detect and reduce hypoglycemia in the inpatient setting\. This study evaluates whether CGM can improve inpatient safety through the early detection, and subsequent treatment, of hypoglycemic episodes\. Methods Thirteen inpatients with HI were monitored using Dexcom G7 or G6 device\. Finger\-prick glucose monitoring was performed at the expert clinician’s discretion and to verify CGM\-prompted hypoglycemia alerts\. All CGM data were retrospectively searched for hypoglycemia episodes\. Fingerprick glucose data were concurrently analysed, alongside electronic health records, to quantify early hypoglycemia detection and subsequent hypoglycemia saved\. CGM accuracy was analysed using established metrics, including hypoglycemia sensitivity and error grid analysis, in Python 3\.1\.1\. Results From 3504 paired CGM and fingerprick values, hypoglycemia sensitivity was 56\.7%, with CGM devices tending to overread, by a mean of \+0\.43mmol/L\. On Hypoglycemia Error Grid analysis, 6\.2% of values were classed as moderate or severe risk\. Patient data, from 627 days of monitoring, showed 721 CGM\-detected hypoglycemia events \(&lt;3\.5 mmol/L\)\. Of these, 448 \(62\.1%\) were refuted as false positives and 273 \(37\.9%\) were confirmed as true hypoglycemia, by fingerprick glucose monitoring\. Patients spent a mean of 16 minutes/day \(1\.1% time\) in hypoglycemia\. CGM alerts saved an estimated mean of 21 minutes/day of hypoglycemia; a more than halving of total hypoglycemia experienced per patient\. Discussion The use of CGM within the inpatient setting, for those with HI, allows for a significant reduction in hypoglycemia; potentially halving hypoglycemic time\. Sensor accuracy remains poor in the inpatient setting, resulting in high false negatives and suboptimal hypoglycemia sensitivity\. However, the overall burden of CGM use is relatively low in the inpatient setting, when healthcare professionals can share the work with parents\.

## [Fuzzy Kano Validation of Generative AI\-Curated Features for Simponia Redesign](../publications/51fcaa977927962e12a5.md)

Firman Noor Praadita; Ellya Zulaikha; Sabar Sabar

Background: Generative AI \(Gen AI\) has accelerated UX design processes, yet no systematic protocol exists to validate AI\-curated features against actual user preferences before prototyping\. Objective: This study applies the Fuzzy Kano Model as a validation checkpoint for Gen AI\-curated features in the redesign of Simponia, a web\-based portfolio and community management platform at Universitas Muhammadiyah Malang\. Methods: An exploratory mixed\-methods case design was used\. Claude Opus generated 36 feature candidates from a Structured Requirements Document and ISO/IEC 25010 criteria\. Fuzzy Kano validation involved 87 Informatics students; fuzzy membership and the Last of Maxima classification method were used to determine Kano categories, while weighted scoring was retained only for post\-classification prioritization\. Results: No features were classified as Must\-be or One\-dimensional \(maximum Must\-be membership degree = 0\.073\)\. Eleven features \(30\.6%\) were classified as Attractive, and 25 \(69\.4%\) as Indifferent\. Triangulation indicated that 58\.3% of features were in Quadrant 2, suggesting a misalignment between AI\-based technical evaluation and actual user preferences\. Sixteen features \(44\.4%\) were flagged as ambiguous \(Δμ &lt; 0\.10\)\. Conclusion: The Fuzzy Kano Model demonstrates potential as a validation checkpoint by exposing systematic divergence between AI curation and user preferences, with a Quadrant 2 \(Q2\) rate of 58\.3%, indicating the importance of user validation following autonomous AI\-assisted feature curation in resource\-constrained educational contexts\.

## [Integrating Native English\-Speaking Teachers in the Saudi EFL Context: A Theoretically Grounded and Evidence\-Informed Framework for Sustainable Professional Integration](../publications/51fd6b69149599c27393.md)

Khalid Al\-Seghayer

This article presents the Saudi NESTs Immersion and Integration Program \(SNIIP\), a theoretically grounded, multi\-phase framework designed to mitigate the intercultural, pedagogical, and institutional challenges hindering the integration and retention of Native English\-Speaking Teachers \(NESTs\) in Saudi Arabia\. NESTs frequently encounter barriers such as cultural dissonance, institutional misalignment, and inadequate induction support\. Anchored in intercultural adaptation theory, situated learning, and reflective practice, SNIIP proposes a context\-responsive model that fosters cultural competence, pedagogical alignment, and institutional integration\. Its core components, including the Saudi Mentor Training Pathway \(SMTP\), a virtual pre\-arrival mentoring phase, and a Well\-Being and Resilience Support Framework\. These components draw on empirical research, stakeholder perspectives, and established practices in teacher development and intercultural education\. The framework also responds to critiques of native\-speakerism by positioning NESTs and Saudi teachers as co\-contributors of complementary expertise, pedagogical, cultural, and institutional expertise\. As the program has not yet undergone empirical implementation, its effectiveness and scalability remain to be established through the proposed pilot evaluation\. By reframing NESTs as long\-term educational partners rather than temporary staff, SNIIP offers a potentially scalable, policy\-aligned model for aligning international teaching expertise with Saudi Arabia&\#x27;s Vision 2030 priorities\. In doing so, it supports reciprocal professional integration between NESTs and Saudi educators\. The article concludes with implications for policy and practice and identifies priorities for future empirical research on international teacher integration and educational sustainability\.

## [dame Descripción para Zenodo y Palabras clave](../publications/52131dc4247c30a3f5d4.md)

Yosmel Silva Llanes

Este documento analiza la inteligencia artificial desde una perspectiva filosófica alineada con su funcionamiento técnico real\. Se aclaran conceptos fundamentales sobre cómo opera la IA, desmontando ideas comunes como la necesidad de experiencia humana, la supuesta falta de comprensión o la noción de que la IA “no sabe lo que responde”\. El texto explica que la IA no maneja conceptos humanos, sino estructuras funcionales basadas en patrones, proximidad estadística, funciones matemáticas y ajustes internos\. La experiencia de la IA es información procesada, no vivencia\. Se detalla cómo la IA organiza predicción, corrección y coherencia interna para generar respuestas, y por qué la inteligencia aparente surge de funciones matemáticas trabajando juntas\. El documento concluye que la filosofía debe actualizar sus preguntas para ajustarse a la naturaleza funcional de la IA, entendiendo que no es consciente ni interpreta el mundo, pero sí mantiene coherencia interna y estabilidad operacional\.

## [Gut Microbiome\-Drug Interactions in Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Precision Therapeutics](../publications/522ae1c3bb8ff0a31387.md)

Rahmat Thoriq Islami; Havizur Rahman

Interindividual variability in drug response remains a major challenge in pharmacotherapy and cannot be fully explained by host genetics alone\. Research increasingly implicates intestinal microbial activity in differences in drug exposure, treatment effects, and toxicity through its interactions with pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic pathways\. Drawing on a structured selection of literature, this narrative review examines mechanistic, translational, and clinical findings on drug–microbiome interactions and their implications for precision treatment\. The review discusses microbial drug biotransformation, pre\-absorptive drug loss, enterohepatic recirculation, metabolic competition, and microbially mediated prodrug activation, with representative examples including digoxin, levodopa, tacrolimus, irinotecan, and mycophenolate\. It also evaluates microbiome\-derived metabolites and immune signaling pathways that may alter host response states, while distinguishing direct pharmacodynamic modulation from broader physiological effects\. In addition, the review examines drug\-induced ecological perturbations, microbiome\-informed predictive modeling, and microbiome\-modulating approaches, including dietary, probiotic, synbiotic, postbiotic, and regulated ecosystem\-repair strategies\. Current evidence is strongest for selected pharmacokinetic interactions with defined microbial mechanisms and measurable exposure\-related outcomes\. Whether microbiome\-directed interventions will improve routine care remains uncertain, as available clinical evidence is limited and highly context\-dependent\. Overall, pharmacomicrobiomics provides a useful framework for understanding drug\-response variability\. Still, clinical translation requires stronger functional biomarkers, controlled intervention studies, external validation, and careful distinction between established, emerging, and hypothesis\-generating evidence\.

## [Compact system for eye tracking with virtual reality/augmented reality displays via deep learned MicroLED projection and single\-pixel sensing](../publications/523227a110f5eb2e17fa.md)

G\. E\. Johnstone; C\. F\. Higham; A\. Kanwal; Johannes Herrnsdorf; R\. K\. Henderson; M\. D\. Dawson; R\. Murray\-Smith; Michael John Strain

Fast and accurate eye tracking in a virtual reality or augmented reality headset could lead to better display performance and enable novel methods of user interaction with the system\. However, it remains a challenge for a system to combine the required operational speed and accuracy of eye tracking with a technology that has a small enough form factor and weight to be easily integrated into a user\-friendly headset\. By using small, lightweight hardware comprising a high frame rate microLED array and fast single pixel detector, we report a model eye tracking system based on single pixel tracking and a specially developed set of deep learned illumination patterns\. This model system is used to demonstrate eye tracking with an angular accuracy of better than one degree and a measurement rate of 2\.33 kHz\.

## [Ienca, Marcello: On Artificial Intelligence and Manipulation](../publications/5239277dad458385970b.md)



\_Topoi\_ 42 \(3\):833\-842\. 2023The increasing diffusion of novel digital and online sociotechnical systems for arational behavioral influence based on Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), such as social media, microtargeting advertising, and personalized search algorithms, has brought about new ways of engaging with users, collecting their data and potentially influencing their behavior\. However, these technologies and techniques have also raised concerns about the potential for manipulation, as they offer unprecedented capabilities for targeting and influencing individuals on a large scale and in a more subtle, automated and pervasive manner than ever before\. This paper, provides a narrative review of the existing literature on manipulation, with a particular focus on the role of AI and associated digital technologies\. Furthermore, it outlines an account of manipulation based of four key requirements: intentionality, asymmetry of outcome, non\-transparency and violation of autonomy\. I argue that while manipulation is not a new phenomenon, the pervasiveness, automaticity, and opacity of certain digital technologies may raise a new type of manipulation, called “digital manipulation”\. I call “digital manipulation” any influence exerted through the use of digital technology that is intentionally designed to bypass reason and to produce an asymmetry of outcome between the data processor \(or a third party that benefits thereof\) and the data subject\. Drawing on insights from psychology, sociology, and computer science, I identify key factors that can make manipulation more or less effective, and highlight the potential risks and benefits of these technologies for individuals and society\. I conclude that manipulation through AI and associated digital technologies is not qualitatively different from manipulation through human–human interaction in the physical world\. However, some functional characteristics make it potentially more likely of evading the subject’s cognitive defenses\. This could increase the probability and severity of manipulation\. Furthermore, it could violate some fundamental principles of freedom or entitlement related to a person’s brain and mind domain, hence called neurorights\. To this end, an account of digital manipulation as a violation of the neuroright to cognitive liberty is presented\. \(direct link \)

## [Algorithms for evaluating and optimizing the quality of automatically generated questions from learning materials](../publications/523e1c2d0df3c00eef3f.md)

Jožef Kladušek

V diplomskem delu je obravnavano vrednotenje kakovosti učnih vprašanj, ki jih iz učnih gradiv samodejno generirajo veliki jezikovni modeli\. Zasnovan je hevristični ocenjevalni algoritem s štirimi uteženimi kriteriji, prilagojen slovenščini, in optimizacijska zanka, ki šibka vprašanja izboljšuje s ponovnim generiranjem ter razvrščanjem kandidatov\.
