Pokazano je, da oba strojna ocenjevalca zgrešita večino vsebinsko slabih vprašanj, zato je predlagana večstopenjska arhitektura vrednotenja\.

## [A One Health scoping review of genomic and machine learning approaches for predicting antimicrobial resistance in low\- and middle\-income countries](../publications/52474907ef8329d62cbc.md)

Zuhura Idd Kimera; Majigo Mtebe; Upendo Ozeniel Kibwana; Salim S\. Masoud; Doreen Kamori; Erasto Vitus Mbugi; Mecky Isaac Matee

Antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) is a major global health threat, disproportionately affecting low\- and middle\-income countries \(LMICs\), where limited laboratory infrastructure constrains phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing\. Whole\-genome sequencing \(WGS\)\-enabled machine learning \(ML\) and artificial intelligence \(AI\) offer rapid approaches for AMR prediction, but their applicability across heterogeneous populations and One Health reservoirs remains uncertain\. To map genomic ML/AI approaches for bacterial AMR prediction, focusing on genomic features, model architectures, validation, performance, and LMIC and One Health applicability\. A scoping review of 27 studies published between 2020 and 2026 was conducted, including 22 with LMIC\-relevant datasets\. Evidence was narratively synthesized according to genomic features, modelling strategies, validation approaches, geographic coverage, and ecological context\. Studies were categorized using predefined LMIC relevance and One Health criteria\. Most studies used WGS\-derived features, particularly k\-mers and resistance\-gene profiles\. Tree\-based ensembles and regularized regression models predominated, while neural networks were less frequently applied but generally reported high performance\. Reported performance ranged from 78%–98% \(accuracy or AUC; not directly comparable\)\. External validation using independent LMIC\-derived or cross\-regional datasets was reported in approximately 30% of studies, whereas cross\-country LMIC validation was limited\. Six of 22 LMIC\-relevant studies \(27\.3%\) incorporated multi\-reservoir One Health datasets\. Performance varied with dataset composition, genomic feature representation, and model architecture\. Explainable AI remained limited\. Genomic ML/AI shows strong potential for AMR prediction but remains constrained by limited LMIC representation, external validation, and One Health integration\. Expanding geographically diverse WGS datasets, strengthening independent cross\-context and cross\-country validation, harmonizing evaluation frameworks, and integrating explainable AI are priorities for equitable LMIC deployment\.

## [Quadratic Morphing Morlet Transform and Multi\-Scale Frequency\-Attentive Temporal Network for sEMG Gesture Recognition](../publications/5254e18fc4f46a57329d.md)

Hazret Tekin

Accurate recognition of surface electromyography \(sEMG\) signals is essential for intuitive human–machine interaction and myoelectric prosthetic control\. However, the inherently transient, nonstationary, and low\-amplitude nature of sEMG signals limits the effectiveness of conventional time–frequency representations and deep learning models, which often struggle to capture short\-duration neuromuscular events and the multi\-scale spectral–temporal characteristics of muscle activity\. To address these challenges, this study introduces the quadratic morphing morlet \(QMM\) wavelet, a newly formulated and fully admissible wavelet designed to enhance transient resolution and spectral selectivity\. Building upon this improved representation, a hybrid deep\-learning architecture, the multi\-scale frequency\-attentive temporal network \(MFATNet\), is proposed as a novel hybrid deep learning architecture\. MFATNet integrates tri\-branch multi\-scale spectral encoding, frequency\-wise attention, and dilated temporal modeling to jointly capture spectral diversity, frequency adaptivity, and gesture dynamics within a unified framework\. The proposed QMM–MFATNet pipeline is evaluated on the 52\-class hand\-gesture corpus of the NinaPro DB1 dataset, comprising sEMG recordings from 27 subjects, wherein QMM\-based continuous wavelet transform \(CWT\) representations are used to generate high\-resolution scalograms for subsequent model training\. Experimental results indicate that QMM provides sharper and more discriminative scalograms than classical Morlet, Gaussian, and Mexican Hat wavelets\. Additionally, MFATNet outperforms standard CNN, ResNet, and MobileNet models, achieving the highest accuracy \(93\.13%\) and F1\-score \(93\.15%\)\. Comparisons of different wavelet types further demonstrate the superiority of QMM, which yields a mean accuracy of 0\.9313 ± 0\.0194, surpassing all traditional kernels\.

## [Hydroxy\-α\-Sanshool and Capsaicin as Salt Taste Enhancers: Molecular Mechanisms of TRPV1/ENaC Activation and PKCα Signaling](../publications/525a9979f4e02ca9fa53.md)

Xingyu Wang; Yang Wang; Lei Zhao; Zhen Qin; Kui Zhong; Haiyan Gao

Abstract Excessive salt intake has emerged as a significant public health concern\. Early\-phase research suggests that pungent substances have the potential to reduce salt consumption, although the precise mechanism remains incompletely elucidated\. This study systematically investigated the molecular basis of saltiness enhancement by má là compounds—hydroxy\-α\-sanshool \(3 μmol/L\) and capsaicin \(1 μmol/L\)\. We employed calcium imaging to monitor ionic flux in murine bud cells, Western blot and qPCR to quantify protein and gene expression in HEK293T cell models, and integrated molecular docking with dynamics simulations to characterize receptor\-ligand interactions\. Our findings demonstrate that both compounds significantly potentiated Ca²⁺ influx through TRPV1 and SCNN1A channels\. Notably, the hydroxy\-α\-sanshool/capsaicin combination reverses the suppressive effect of capsaicin alone on SCNN1A expression and coordinately upregulates TRPV1 and SCNN1A expression, accompanied by enhanced PKCα phosphorylation\. Structural simulations reveal that hydroxy\-α\-sanshool stabilizes TRPV1 conformational states that facilitate capsaicin binding\. Collectively, these results establish a mechanistic foundation for má là–mediated saltiness enhancement and support their potential application in taste modulation strategies\.

## [Treatment and tracking algorithm for iron deficiency anaemia among children and adolescents— a policy informed evidence— based framework for India](../publications/5261e5564ded73704b54.md)

Priyanka Gupta Bansal; Ketaki Chandiok; Dheeraj Shah; Jagdish Chandra; Bharati Kulkarni; Kapil Yadav; Krishnapilla Madhavan Nair; Reema Mukherjee

Background and objectives The Anaemia Mukt Bharat \(AMB\) programme advocates for ‘test, treat and track’ strategy\. However, limited coverage, poor adherence, workforce shortages and inconsistent follow up, affect implementation\. Recent programme monitoring data indicate suboptimal coverage of biweekly iron and folic acid \(IFA\) supplementation among children aged 6–59 mo, underscoring the need for a standardised, treatment and tracking algorithm\. This exercise aimed to develop evidence\-based treatment and tracking algorithms for iron deficiency anaemia in children and adolescents \(6 mo\-18 y\) to support clinical decision\-making, improve adherence and follow up, and strengthen the AMB programme implementation\. Methods National/International guidelines and consensus statements were reviewed\. Methodological quality was appraised using AGREE II tool\. Systematic literature searches were conducted to address specific questions related to diagnostic thresholds for serum ferritin and C\-reactive protein \(CRP\); iron supplementation dosage and frequency; and dosing strategies\. Findings were consolidated to develop anaemia management algorithms, refined through expert consultation\. Results Two algorithms one each for \( i \) mild, and \( ii \) moderate—to severe—anaemia were developed\. The algorithms included treatment initiation, follow up, response assessment, and guidance to subsequent steps\. Measurement of haemoglobin is suggested as the first line test for identification of anaemia, and serum ferritin and CRP for non\-responders\. Interpretation and conclusions The proposed algorithms provide an evidence—based operational approach to strengthen anaemia management and follow up within AMB programme settings to improve continuity of care and reduce variability in practice\. These algorithms need field validation in different settings\.

## [Calcaneal tuberosity avulsion fracture fixation: a technical note and results on cases of patients](../publications/5269a0afe27af3f0a443.md)

Pengkun Yu; Fei Zhao; Qiang Xu; Yu Wu; Min Gong

Objective Calcaneal tuberosity avulsion fractures are more common in elderly osteoporotic populations\. According to the Beavis classification, they are divided into 3 types\. Types I and III have small bone fragments that are difficult to fix with screws, and traditional open surgery has a high rate of skin necrosis and poor wound healing\. This article proposes a modified Bunnell suture combined with calcaneal tunnel fixation technique that can flexibly switch between minimally invasive and open approaches, and explores its short\-term clinical efficacy\. Methods From January 2024 to February 2026, 2 patients with calcaneal tuberosity avulsion fractures were enrolled\. One patient with Beavis type II \+ I underwent open surgery, and one patient with Beavis type II underwent a minimally invasive procedure\. Postoperatively, the Burwell\-Charnley criteria were used to assess the quality of fracture reduction\. At 6 months postoperatively, the AOFAS ankle\-hindfoot scale was used, and the maximum plantarflexion angle and dorsiflexion angle of the ankle joint were recorded\. Follow\-up recorded incision, fracture healing, and complications, with an average follow\-up of 1 year\. Results Both patients achieved anatomical reduction postoperatively, and all achieved bony union at 3 months postoperatively without loss of reduction\. At 6 months postoperatively, the AOFAS scores were 83 and 96, respectively, and both the maximum plantarflexion and dorsiflexion angles were both within the normal range\. Only the patient who underwent open surgery and had diabetes and obesity experienced delayed wound healing, which healed after regular dressing changes for 1 month\. The minimally invasive case did not develop complications related to soft tissue, sural nerve, or Achilles tendon\. Conclusion The modified Bunnell suture combined with calcaneal tunnel fixation technique may help balance rigid fixation and soft tissue protection\. The minimally invasive approach appears to lower the risk of incision\-related complications in the present series\. This technique may offer a flexible alternative for selected cases of Beavis calcaneal tuberosity avulsion fractures, especially suitable for minimally invasive fixation of types I and III fractures, and may also act as an auxiliary fixation method for type II fractures\. However, the sample size of this study is small, and long\-term efficacy still needs to be verified by large\-sample controlled studies\.

## [Analysis of China&\#x27;s new materials industry landscape and corporate strategic planning](../publications/526b3a8010bef2b0458d.md)

Jiusheng Wu

The new materials industry is a strategic pillar industry underpinning China&\#x27;s pursuit of technological self\-reliance and self\-strengthening\. It plays a vital role in the development of advanced manufacturing, the achievement of the &quot;dual carbon&quot; goals, and the security of industrial and supply chains\. The deep integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) with materials Research and Development \(R&amp;D\) is continuously reshaping the innovation and production models of the industry\. Existing literature has extensively examined new materials technologies and AI\-driven innovation, but relatively little research has systematically analyzed the competitive landscape of the industry from the perspective of industrial economics\. Clarifying the characteristics of industry competition can provide practical insights for domestic industrial policymaking and overseas industrial deployment under the framework of the Belt and Road Initiative\. Using Porter&\#x27;s Five Forces model as the analytical framework, this study examines the competitive characteristics of China&\#x27;s new materials industry by drawing on publicly available industry reports, existing literature, and online interviews with industry practitioners, given the constraints on obtaining first\-hand corporate research samples\. The findings indicate that the industry as a whole has high entry barriers, while supplier bargaining power varies significantly across different segments\. Buyers and substitutes exert moderate competitive pressure, and the intensity of intra\-industry competition differs substantially between low\-end and high\-end segments\. Based on these findings, corresponding industrial policy recommendations are proposed, followed by a discussion of the limitations of this study and directions for future research\.

## [Barriers inhibiting the availability and accessibility of digital reading in higher education](../publications/527065aa8ed71cf31e87.md)

Anna Rich Abad; Jamie Wood

This article investigates the barriers to digital reading at university level from two perspectives: first, how the \(un\)availability of digital texts affects students’ reading practices negatively, and second, how accessibility poses a significant challenge to engagement in digital reading for academic purposes\. It derives from a broader research project that focused on student and staff engagement with digital reading\. Data was gathered from students and staff from a wide range of disciplines, although respondents were predominantly from the Humanities, subjects which traditionally have a heavy focus on reading\. The research underlines the factors that prevent equitable engagement in digital reading and highlights misalignment between student, staff and institutional practices, identifying issues such as digital poverty, inequitable access to technology and deficiencies in technical skills\. It also reveals issues associated with lack of support and guidance, as well as limitations in pedagogies for teaching digital reading\. Importantly, it exposes physical barriers, mental health problems, learning difficulties, and digital distraction as key challenges limiting the engagement of some learners with digital texts\. The article closes by proposing a systemic reflection on existing digital reading practices and pedagogies, calling for further investigation into how the availability of digital texts can be improved and how practices of digital reading can be made more accessible for students\. Although the initial research focused on the Humanities, these findings have wide\-ranging implications for all disciplines and for all students, especially those who face pre\-existing barriers to accessible and inclusive reading, whether due to health issues, learning difficulties or socio\-economic factors\.

## [The Influence of Digital Promotion and Information Overload on Gen Z&\#x27;s Consumptive Behavior Mediated by Sharia Financial Management \(A Study of Shopee Users\)](../publications/527623a22386ee1a7dd0.md)

Gustina Angreani; Anzu Elvia Zahara; Beid Fitrianova Andriani

This study aims to analyze the influence of digital promotion and information overload on the consumptive behavior of Generation Z Shopee users, mediated by Sharia\-compliant financial management\. A quantitative approach utilizing Partial Least Squares\-Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) was employed\. The results indicate that information overload and digital promotion have a positive and significant effect on consumptive behavior\. Conversely, neither information overload nor digital promotion significantly affects Sharia\-compliant financial management, nor does Sharia\-compliant financial management significantly influence consumptive behavior\. Mediation analysis reveals that Sharia\-compliant financial management does not mediate the impact of information overload or digital promotion on consumptive behavior\. These findings suggest that the consumptive behavior of Generation Z Shopee users is driven more directly by informational stimuli and digital promotions than through the mechanism of Sharia\-compliant financial management\.

## [ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ КАК ФАКТОР ПОВЫШЕНИЯ КОНКУРЕНТОСПОСОБНОСТИ ЭКОНОМИКИ](../publications/527a70f05efe272e8952.md)

Артикова Шохида Ильясовна

В статье исследуется искусственный интеллект как ключевой фактор повышения конкурентоспособности национальной экономики в условиях ускоряющейся цифровой трансформации\. Обосновывается, что внедрение технологий искусственного интеллекта способствует росту производительности труда, снижению трансакционных и операционных издержек, оптимизации бизнес\-процессов, а также формированию и распространению инновационных бизнес\-моделей\. Особое внимание уделяется анализу воздействия искусственного интеллекта на развитие промышленного сектора, финансовой системы и государственного управления, где интеллектуальные технологии обеспечивают повышение эффективности процессов принятия решений, а также прозрачности и качества институционального регулирования\. Рассматривается международный опыт стран\-лидеров цифровой трансформации, а также особенности формирования национальной стратегии внедрения искусственного интеллекта в Республике Узбекистан в контексте реализации Стратегии «Узбекистан – 2030»\. Выделяются ключевые направления государственной политики, включающие развитие цифровой инфраструктуры, стимулирование инновационной активности, поддержку стартап\-экосистемы и подготовку высококвалифицированных кадров\. В работе предложена концептуальная модель влияния искусственного интеллекта на конкурентоспособность экономики, отражающая взаимосвязь технологических, экономических и институциональных факторов\. Отмечаются потенциальные риски цифровой трансформации, включая усиление цифрового неравенства, структурные изменения на рынке труда и необходимость совершенствования нормативно\-правового регулирования\. Сделан вывод о стратегической значимости искусственного интеллекта как одного из ключевых драйверов устойчивого экономического роста и повышения глобальной конкурентоспособности национальной экономики\.

## [A Weighted Hybrid Scoring Framework for Static Detection of Hash\-novel Polymorphic Worm Variants](../publications/527c6e248fd866b2b580.md)

Sulieman Mohamed Ali Sulieman; Yahia A\. Fadlalla

Polymorphic malware continuously changes its binary representation while preserving malicious functionality, reducing the effectiveness of signature\-based detection against previously unseen variants\.This paper proposes a Weighted Hybrid Scoring Framework \(WHSF\) for static detection of hash\-novel polymorphic worm variants\.WHSF integrates four complementary modalities: exact cryptographic matching \(M1\), CTPH\-based fuzzy similarity hashing \(M2\), Random Forest structural analysis of PE features \(M3\), and CNN\-LSTM semantic analysis of API\-call sequences \(M4\)\.A Normalized Dynamic Redistribution mechanism reallocates weights among available modalities, preventing inactive or unavailable evidence from imposing a fixed scoring ceiling\.The framework was evaluated on 11,146 samples comprising 5,268 polymorphic malware variants and 5,878 benign executables\.WHSF achieved a 99\.98% detection rate with a 0\.00% false\-positive rate, demonstrating that complementary static modalities with adaptive score fusion can effectively detect hash\-novel polymorphic malware\.

## [Perbandingan Metode Mean Shift Clustering Dan Density Peaks Clustering Dalam Pengelompokan Provinsi Berdasarkan Indikator Kesehatan Lingkungan Di Indonesia](../publications/5282591ae10ea64b6b45.md)

Alvira Napu; Fahrezal Zubedi; La Ode Nashar

Kesehatan lingkungan merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam meningkatkan kualitas hidup masyarakat\. Namun, capaian indikator kesehatan lingkungan masih menunjukkan perbedaan antarprovinsi di Indonesia sehingga diperlukan analisis pengelompokan untuk mengidentiikasi provinsi yang memiliki karakteristik serupa\. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kinerja metode Mean Shift Clustering dan Density Peaks Clustering \(DPC\) dalam mengelompokkan provinsi berdasarkan indikator kesehatan lingkungan di Indonesia\. Data yang digunakan merupakan data sekunder Profil Kesehatan Indonesia Tahun 2024 yang mencakup 38 provinsi dengan sembilan indikator kesehatan lingkungan\. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan bahasa pemrograman Python\. Penentuan parameter bandwidth pada Mean Shift Clustering menggunakan pendekatan quantile, sedangkan parameter cut‑off distance pada DPC menggunakan pendekatan persentil\. Kinerja kedua metode dievaluasi menggunakan Silhouette Coeficient \(SC\) dan Davies‑Bouldin Index \(DBI\)\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Mean Shift Clustering menghasilkan dua klaster, sedangkan DPC menghasilkan dua klaster utama dan satu klaster outlier yang merepresentasikan provinsi dengan karakteristik berbeda dari klaster lainnya\. DPC memperoleh nilai SC sebesar 0,7257 dan DBI sebesar 0,3342, sedangkan Mean Shift Clustering memperoleh nilai SC sebesar 0,7010 dan DBI sebesar 0,4440\. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa DPC menghasilkan struktur klaster yang lebih kompak dan memiliki pemisahan antarklaster yang lebih baik, sehingga lebih sesuai digunakan untuk pengelompokan provinsi berdasarkan indikator kesehatan lingkungan di Indonesia\.

## [Predicting the Water Retention Behavior of Biochar\-Amended Soils: A Comparative Study of Six Machine Learning Approaches](../publications/528d2829064666020832.md)

Kewen Huang; Junming Lin; Haijian Liu; Letian Wang; Zixuan Zheng; Qiang Hu; Fangyuan Zhou; Yang Lu; Ping Li; 登飞 张

The soil\-water retention curve \(SWRC\) is a key indicator characterizing soil water retention capacity\. Biochar incorporation can affect the SWRC by altering soil pore structure and physicochemical properties\. The SWRC of biochar\-amended soils is influenced by both soil\- and biochar\-related factors\. To address the time\-consuming and labor\-intensive nature of conventional SWRC measurement methods, this study employed six machine learning models, Decision Tree \(DT\), Random Forest \(RF\), Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), Categorical Gradient Boosting \(CatBoost\), Light Gradient Boosting \(LightGBM\), and Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\), to predict the SWRC of biochar\-amended soils based on a constructed dataset\. Feature importance analysis and partial dependence analysis were also conducted to identify key variables and reveal their influence patterns\. The results indicated that gradient boosting tree models, XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM, achieved the highest accuracy, with R2 = 0\.85–0\.89 on the inner\-test set and R2 = 0\.61–0\.64 on the held\-out source, demonstrating their advantage in modeling complex nonlinear relationships\. Suction was the variable most strongly associated with volumetric water content, while soil particle\-size distribution and particle packing density also played important roles\. Among biochar\-related parameters, ash content showed higher importance than carbon content and pH\. The model\-derived response of volumetric water content to ash content was non\-uniform: limited at low levels, increasing after reaching a certain range, and stabilizing at high levels\. In contrast, carbon content and pH had relatively weak marginal effects\. A staged hyperparameter optimization strategy combining random search and Bayesian optimization was then applied to optimize the XGBoost model, yielding accuracy comparable to grid search while substantially reducing the training time\. Based on the optimized XGBoost model, a prediction platform for the SWRC of biochar\-amended soils was developed, enabling volumetric water content prediction, SWRC generation, and van Genuchten \(VG\) model fitting\. This study provides a data\-driven approach and a prototype tool for rapid, preliminary SWRC estimation for biochar\-amended soils, thereby facilitating the application of biochar in engineering practice\.

## [A Narrative Analysis of the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Designing Smart Tooles for Identifying and Growing Farm Animals](../publications/52ab7508bfbf55f8b4a6.md)

Sebghatullah Subat; Salahuddin Hidayat

The increasing world population and demand for animal products have increased the need to improve farm management\. Artificial intelligence, as a new technology, plays an important role in data analysis and production optimization\. In this study, applications of artificial intelligence in the design and development of tools for identification, monitoring, nutrition, health, and welfare of farm animals was conducted, and challenges and opportunities were analyzed\. This research was conducted as a narrative review and was based on the collection, analysis, and classification of relevant research findings from scientific and international sources published between 2015 and 2024\. In this process, 55 articles were initially collected, and after applying screening steps, 20 articles related to the topic were selected and analyzed qualitatively\. The findings indicate that AI has significantly contributed to accurate animal identification, movement tracking, monitoring of growth and feeding patterns, early disease detection, and assessment of animal welfare and stress\. Despite these advancements, challenges such as inadequate digital infrastructure, a shortage of skilled personnel, and financial constraints—particularly in developing countries like Afghanistan—hinder the full\-scale adoption of these technologies\. Accordingly, the study recommends enhancing specialized training, strengthening information technology infrastructure, and implementing supportive policies to facilitate the localization and sustainable development of AI technologies\. Such efforts would not only improve livestock production and welfare but also enhance the sector’s contribution to economic growth and food security\. This review can serve as a valuable resource for researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders in the livestock industry seeking to optimize the use of AI in animal farming\.

## [In Silico Identification of Putative Fruit Crop\-Derived Antibacterial Peptides Against Aeromonas hydrophila](../publications/52b72a46fb53c51fb758.md)

SUBRAMANIAN MANONMANI; Subramanian Manivannan; Gunasekaran Indian; Murugan Paruthi Ellampirai; Sravya Keerthana Taneti

Aquaculture is a fish\-producing subsector of agriculture that has a significant role in India’s economy and livelihood\. The major threat to fish production is the outbreak of bacterial infections that creates severe losses every year\. Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic invader of human and aquatic animals, ubiquitously present in the aquatic environment\. Antibiotics are the common control measure, but their indiscriminate use has resulted in the development of resistance by the pathogen\. As an alternative to antibiotics, Antimicrobial Peptides \(AMPs\) are used nowadays to tackle antimicrobial resistance\. This study aims to identify the putative plant\-derived antibacterial peptides as a valid drug candidate against multidrug\-resistant bacteria, A\. hydrophila, using bioinformatic approaches\. Out of 10953 AMP sequences retrieved from Mendeley covering different fruit crops, 764 and 326 sequences were detected with antimicrobial and antibacterial activity, respectively\. They were shortlisted to 11 antibacterial peptides \(ABPs\) based on non\-toxic, non\-allergenic, non\-hemolytic and bioactive stable proteins\. The protein\-peptide interaction study revealed that all ABPs have positive binding affinity towards the virulent factors of Aeromonas\. Hence, the predicted ABPs derived from fruit crops have the bactericidal effect and further wet\-lab experiments are required to verify the findings\.

## [Peak\-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference](../publications/52ba7222e5026403fb92.md)

Ivan Fomin; Ivan Koryabkin; Boris Sheludko

Real\-time inference on small devices needs low activation memory without extra latency, which makes operator order the most valuable memory lever: it is free in time\. We show that the usual way of deploying a better order, handing it back to the compiler and regenerating code, is unreliable\. In PyTorch Inductor the regenerated program misses its predicted peak in 22 of 54 CPU configurations\. It is worse than the stock program in 9 of them and in 19 of 50 on a GPU, and on the GPU it also changes numerical results\. We instead profile the generated program, model its memory exactly from its own statements and their read/write effects, and permute those statements\. We prove that this realizes the modeled peak whenever allocation does not depend on history\. It does so to the byte, with bitwise\-identical results, in all our CPU runs\. On the GPU we characterize why the caching allocator breaks the condition\. To know when to stop, we give forward and reverse &quot;trap&quot; lower bounds, each computable with $O\(n^2\)$ minimum cuts\. They certify the found order optimal for 94% of held\-out wrapper graphs and all 16 microcontroller\-class models we study, in under a second\. So most inference graphs are already scheduled optimally\. Branching networks are the exception, where reordering is free and pays, e\.g\. 10\.0% on DeepLabV3\. In compiled training we save up to 7\.6%\. Beyond the certified optimum we study selective recomputation with per\-operator caps\. It is strongly NP\-hard for every fixed cap even at treewidth two, encodes knapsack exactly on series\-parallel graphs, and is solvable exactly on bounded treewidth\. It is useless on public tiny models whose peak is a single layer, but on architectures that hold a cheap value for a late reuse it pays: on the public ReDimNet speaker networks, whose order is already optimal, it lowers the peak by 5\.2\-6\.1% at under 0\.4% extra MACs, with bitwise\-identical outputs\.

## [ПРЕЕМПЦІЯ БЕЗ АВТОРИТЕТУ У КОНТЕКСТІ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ АВТОРИТЕТНИХ ВІДНОСИН В ЕПОХУ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ](../publications/52be45ef4c5bb494dc43.md)

ОЛЕКСАНДР РИБАК

У статті розглянуто питання про те, чи придатне класичне поняття авторитету для опису відносин між людиною та системами штучного інтелекту, які дедалі частіше посідають позиції, що раніше належали людям та інституціям\. Актуальність теми зумовлена тим, що алгоритмічні системи фактично витісняють власне міркування адресата, залишаючись формально лише рекомендаційними, а для України ця обставина набуває додаткової ваги через швидку цифровізацію державних сервісів в умовах війни, коли довіра до інституцій є обмеженим ресурсом\. Метою дослідження є з’ясування того, чи придатна преемптивна модель авторитету для опису відносин між суб’єктом і алгоритмічною системою, та які умови легітимації з цього випливають\. Методологічною основою є концептуальний аналіз, раціональна реконструкція преемптивної тези, компаративне зіставлення епістемічної та політичної ліній осмислення проблеми і нормативний аналіз умов легітимності\. Показано, що преемптивна модель розпадається на дві частини різної міцності\. Її нормативне ядро тримається на агентності носія авторитету, тоді як феноменологічний опис заміщення підстав від агентності не залежить\. На цій підставі запропоновано розрізнення авторитету в нормативному сенсі та преемптивної позиції у фактичному сенсі, а стан, за якого система штучного інтелекту посідає другу, не маючи властивостей, потрібних для першої, названо преемпцією без авторитету\. Обґрунтовано, що саме ця асиметрія лежить в основі ерозії епістемічної агентності і що вона виражена нерівномірно в різних режимах алгоритмічної регуляції\. Доведено, що умовою легітимації таких відносин є збереження ревізованості довіри, яка на рівні інституцій набуває форми публічності підстав\. Зроблено висновок, що ерозію довіри до інституцій доцільно описувати не як просту втрату авторитету, а як перехід до преемптивної позиції, за якого зовнішня форма підпорядкування зберігається, а нормативне підґрунтя зникає\. Запропоноване розрізнення авторитету та преемптивної позиції потребує подальшого уточнення, передусім щодо того, чи є воно градуальним, чи бінарним, бо в реальних інституційних практиках трапляються проміжні випадки, які ми тут залишили поза увагою\. Перспективним видається застосування цього розрізнення до окремих сфер, де преемпція виражена найсильніше, зокрема до автоматизованих адміністративних процедур та до медичної діагностики, оскільки саме там ціна помилкового приписування авторитету є найвищою\.

## [Global analysis reveals persistent land\-cover thresholds for river water quality across climates and decades](../publications/52d8018ba9e49d1ddb79.md)

Diogo Costa; Helen Margaret Baulch; Helen Jarvie; Jian Liu; Merrin L\. Macrae

Abstract Agricultural and urban land uses are widely recognized as major drivers of global surface water quality\. However, it remains unclear whether the magnitude of the impacts scales universally and consistently across contrasting climatic and geographical settings based on the intensity of land\-use change\. Here we analyse more than 19 million river water quality observations from 117 countries over 28 years, linking $$\\sim$$ 101,000 monitoring stations to upstream basin land cover derived from ESA CCI\. Cropland and urban areas reveal the strongest global positive correlations with nutrient and sediment concentrations, while forested landscapes are consistently associated with lower pollutant levels\. A dose\-response analysis \(term borrowed from toxicology\) based on 1\.7 million basin–year records shows that land\-cover impacts on water quality are not merely categorical but scale progressively across the full gradient of land\-cover intensity\. Nutrient concentrations increase by up to 10\-fold for nitrate and 5\.7\-fold for total nitrogen with expanding agricultural and urban land use, whereas forest cover is associated with reductions of up to 12\-fold in both nitrogen and phosphorus\. Importantly, these relationships are strongly non\-linear: the conversion of the first 20–40% of a basin to cropland drives disproportionately large increases in nutrient loads, revealing critical and actionable land\-use thresholds for watershed management\.

## [A Web\-Based Multi\-Modal AI Framework for Intelligent Content Moderation with Constructive Feedback](../publications/52dcbcfd7c27d9ded971.md)

Naveen Palanichamy; Marwah Zaid Mohammed Al\-Helali; Su\-Cheng Haw; Subhashini Gopal

Traditional content moderation systems primarily rely on punitive measures that focus on removing offending or inappropriate content without offering users any form of educational feedback or guidance\. This lack of constructive interaction often leads to a poor user experience, leaving users frustrated and uninformed regarding the reasons behind content removal\. Moreover, such a system fails to encourage long\-term positive behavioural changes within online communities, as users do not gain insights on how to improve their conduct\. This paper proposes a new constructive Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) intervention system that integrates a number of AI models in order to conceptualize content moderation as a limiting process rather than an educational process\. The framework suggested in the paper combines HuggingFace&\#x27;s BERT\-based toxicity analysis, SightEngine&\#x27;s image processing, and Google&\#x27;s Gemini large language model to provide end\-to\-end content moderation with construction of feedback\. Based on comprehensive testing through user interaction analysis and comparative analysis, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of educational intervention in content moderation\. The study advances the field by developing a novel approach to content moderation that puts user education and community development first while upholding safety regulations\.

## [¿Soledad masculina e insurrección femenina? juventud urbana, relacionamiento y guiones de género en la era del consumo cultural digital por redes sociales](../publications/52e9507e91dd798508e0.md)

Natalia Carolina Ramírez Bosiga

Esta investigación explora los estudios de género en relacion con el desarrollo de relaciones interpersonales tomando el caso de seis jóvenes colombianos e implementando el concepto de guiones de género para designar la información generizada presente en los contenidos de consumo cultural en las redes sociales\. Mediante un análisis de producciones audiovisuales y artículos noticiosos este trabajo de grado se propone hacer una lectura sobre la variedad de factores que intervienen en la construcción las esferas de relacionamiento relatando a través de testimonios que atraviesan por las condicones materiales para desembocar cómo las instituciones para la socialización han forjado una serie de expectativas y definiciones sobre las maneras correctas o incorrectas de encarnar el género o relaciónarse con las contrapartes generizadas\. A su vez, propone el internet \(o la web 2\.0\) como una nueva institucion de socializacion secundaria que ha influenciado a las juventudes con acceso temprano a esta herramienta\. Finalmente, realiza cuestionamientos sobre hacia dónde va este consumo cultural en un panorama donde la inteligenica artificial y los algoritmos de redes sociales tienen un sesgo de género cada vez más marcado\.

## [Political Narratives in the 2024 Moldovan Presidential Election: Stance, Amplification, and Influence](../publications/52ea84c46eb6de561273.md)

Andrea Piras; Osman Rahmoun; Elena Zheleva

Social media platforms play a central role in shaping political discourse during elections, particularly in geopolitically contested regions\. We study how political narratives emerged, aligned, and propagated during the 2024 Moldovan presidential election by analyzing publicly available posts collected from X, Facebook, and Reddit between August and October 2024\. Combining multilingual stance detection, coordination analysis, and causal inference, we examine both descriptive and causal mechanisms underlying online political discourse\. First, we apply large language models to classify stance toward European integration, Russia, and the two main presidential candidates, revealing clear cross\-platform and cross\-linguistic differences in how political positions are expressed\. Second, we construct retweet\-based and semantic alignment networks on X to identify amplification and aligned framing of dominating narratives\. Finally, we use a proximal causal inference framework to estimate peer influence effects in stance formation\. Our results indicate consistently positive and statistically significant average treatment effects across major stance categories\. These findings provide evidence that amplification and peer exposure contribute to the reinforcement of political narratives online\. This work offers the first analysis of social media discourse surrounding the 2024 Moldovan presidential election and demonstrates the value of integrating language\-based annotation, network analysis, and causal inference for studying political influence in multilingual and geopolitically sensitive contexts\.

## [State\-level pathogen prevalence is associated with fewer interracial marriages and more racially restrictive dating preferences](../publications/52ebb29288525d77fc5a.md)

Jason Freeman; Kodai Kusano; Joanna Rene Schug

Abstract The behavioral immune system framework has linked higher levels of environmental pathogens with increased racial prejudice and xenophobia, suggesting that avoidance of racial outgroups may be an evolved strategy to avoid infection by pathogens and parasites\. Although previous research has found a correlation between pathogen prevalence and racial bias on both regional and individual levels, few studies have examined whether this pattern predicts real\-world outcomes\. This paper presents two studies linking ecological pathogen prevalence to US state\-level variation in interracial marriage \(Study 1\) and stated racial preferences on an online dating site \(Study 2\)\. States with higher pathogen levels tended to have lower\-than\-expected rates of interracial marriage, and online daters from these states were more likely to indicate more restrictive racial preferences\. These results provide support for the pathogen prevalence hypothesis of prejudice and out\-group bias by linking environmental pathogen levels to race\-based preferences in marriage and dating\.

## [Resilient Ageing: A Concept Analysis Using the Walker and Avant Method](../publications/52ef8079284a577cea85.md)

Muhammad Arif

Populations are ageing rapidly, and older people encounter accumulating adversity, including illness, bereavement and functional decline\. Resilient ageing is increasingly proposed as a dynamic alternative to static models of healthy or successful ageing, but it is used inconsistently across disciplines and overlaps with related concepts, which limits its usefulness for nursing practice and research\. This concept analysis aimed to refine the concept of resilient ageing, distinguish it from other ageing concepts and provide a definition that can guide research, practice and evaluation\. The method of Walker and Avant was followed\. Literature published between 2014 and 2024 was retrieved from PubMed, Google Scholar and CINAHL, together with dictionary definitions of ageing and resilience, and model, borderline and contrary cases were constructed to illustrate the concept\. Three defining attributes were identified: adaptive capacity, sense of purpose and self\-efficacy\. Antecedents were adversity, positive attitude and protective factors such as proactive coping and accumulated life experience, while consequences were improved mental health and better quality of life\. Resilient ageing was distinguished from healthy, successful, active and positive ageing by its dependence on adversity, and it was found to be attainable by older people living with illness or disability\. It is defined as a dynamic process through which an older person, facing adversity, draws on adaptive capacity, purpose and self\-efficacy to maintain or regain function and wellbeing\. Resilient ageing can be strengthened over time, which makes it a modifiable target for nursing rather than a fixed personal characteristic\. The analysis provides a basis for developing and validating measures, testing nursing interventions and building middle\-range theory, ideally guided by a nursing framework such as the Roy Adaptation Model\.

## [IO\-BASED WATER QUALITY MEASUREMENT SYSTEM](../publications/52f718701b6f13c70e2d.md)

Rizky Ichwanto; Adi Winarno

This study develops an Internet of Things \(IoT\)\-based water quality monitoring system for household use\. The system integrates pH, total dissolved solids \(TDS\), and temperature sensors with an ESP32 microcontroller\. Measurement data are displayed on a 4×20 LCD and transmitted to the Blynk platform for real\-time monitoring\. The system was tested for 60 days in a residential environment using random sampling\. Results showed water temperatures of 24\.7–31\.3°C, TDS levels of 180–610 ppm, and pH values of 6\.6–8\.7\. The system identifies elevated TDS levels above 300 ppm and provides filter replacement alerts\. Following filter replacement, TDS levels returned to the normal range\. These findings demonstrate the system&\#x27;s potential to support continuous household water quality monitoring and filter maintenance\.

## [Dynamic surface chemistry of MXenes: Toward adaptive interfaces](../publications/52fabf680b0309e9709b.md)

Melena Kai Busse; Michael Naguib

MXenes are a class of two\-dimensional materials whose tunable surface chemistry renders them promising for a wide range of applications, including catalysis and energy storage\. Their surface chemistry is initially established during synthesis from their parent MAX phases through selective etching and serves as a key tunable parameter that governs MXenes’ functional properties and behavior\. However, MXene surfaces are not static\. Beyond synthesis, their surface terminations can be deliberately engineered, and, importantly, continue to evolve dynamically under chemical, electrochemical, and thermal operating conditions\. Such transformations include termination removal, substitution, reconstruction, and protonation\. Consequently, MXenes’ performance is governed by the in operando evolution of surface chemistry, rather than solely by the initial terminations introduced during synthesis or post\-synthesis modifications\. Embracing this dynamic paradigm reframes MXene surface chemistry from a synthetic descriptor to a design variable, opening opportunities to engineer reaction pathways, stabilize transient active states, and couple structure with function in real time\. By conceptualizing MXene surfaces as dynamic interfaces, this article highlights how surface chemistry transforms under working conditions and how this evolution can be rationally harnessed to optimize performance in various applications, including catalysis and energy storage\. MXene surface chemistry evolves from synthesis and post\-synthesis processing to in operando conditions, where interactions with the working environment can further transform surface terminations andactive sites\. Understanding and controlling this dynamic surface evolution provides a pathway to tailor MXene propertiesand optimize performance in applications such as catalysis and energy storage\.

## [Straňák, Pavel: What Artificial Intelligence May Be Missing—And Why It Is Unlikely to Attain It Under Current Paradigms](../publications/5305c8f774805383dab9.md)



\_Philosophies\_ 11 \(1\):20\. 2026Contemporary artificial intelligence \(AI\) achieves remarkable results in data processing, text generation, and the simulation of human cognition\. However, it appears to lack key characteristics typically associated with living systems—consciousness, autonomous motivation, and genuine understanding of the world\. This article critically examines the possible ontological divide between simulated intelligence and lived experience, using the metaphor of the motorcycle and the horse to illustrate how technological progress may obscure deeper principles of life and mind\. Drawing on philosophical concepts such as abduction, tacit knowledge, phenomenal consciousness, and autopoiesis, the paper argues that current approaches to developing Artificial General Intelligence \(AGI\) may overlook organizational principles whose role in biological systems remains only partially understood\. Methodologically, it employs a comparative ontological analysis grounded in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, systems theory, and theoretical biology, supported by contemporary literature on consciousness and biological autonomy\. The article calls for a new paradigm that integrates these perspectives—one that asks not only “how to build smarter machines,” but also “what intelligence, life, and consciousness may fundamentally be,” acknowledging that their relation to computability remains an open question\. \(direct link \)

## [Multi\-SFT: Permissively\-Licensed Multilingual Instruction\-Following](../publications/530d1c711e30b7da1ef2.md)

Daniela Baiamonte; Kamyar Zeinalipour; Elena Fano; Stefano Simonazzi; Andrea Zugarini

Supervised fine\-tuning datasets remain overwhelmingly English\-centric and commercially restricted, as their content is frequently generated by proprietary models whose terms of service forbid training competing systems\. We introduce Multi\-SFT, a commercially permissive collection of 502,818 instruction\-response pairs across five European languages, built via translation and regeneration pipelines for tasks where translation is insufficient\. Human evaluation yields inter\-annotator agreement of at least 0\.87 across all datasets and languages\. ## [Stories of loneliness: trauma, resilience and belonging among older LGBTQ\+ adults](../publications/530f33cbba1f73ef7e70.md)

Samara Suarez Hernandez

This thesis explores the lived experiences of loneliness among older—50 years\-old and above—LGBTQ\+ adults through a qualitative approach\. While loneliness is widely recognised as a significant public health concern, existing research has largely relied on quantitative measures that risk reducing complex, subjective experiences to simplified metrics\. This study seeks to move beyond such reductionism by centring the narratives and meanings attributed to loneliness by individuals themselves\. Semi\-structured interviews were conducted with 10 individuals\. Participants were recruited via social media, UK charities, snowballing, community venues and newsletter advertisement\. A narrative thematic analysis was carried out\. The findings portray participants’ experiences of loneliness as embedded within narratives of trauma, resilience, and belonging\. Participants described performing façades to navigate heteronormative social environments, often concealing aspects of their identities to ensure safety and social acceptance\. These performative acts were linked to experiences of social disconnection, invisibility, and internalised stigma\. Systemic oppression, including heteronormativity and the enduring impacts of historical discrimination as well as individual and community resilience, emerged as central to understanding loneliness in this population\. Through stories of queer loss and love, and an absence of choice, findings highlight the lasting effects of the HIV/AIDS crisis, social exclusion, and fractured community ties\. Importantly, loneliness was not experienced as a static or singular condition but as a dynamic and relational phenomenon shaped by broader socio\-cultural contexts\. The search for belonging emerged as a key process, with participants forming connections in the absence of role models\. This thesis argues for a reconceptualisation of loneliness that moves beyond binary distinctions and instead recognises its fluid, intersectional, and socially situated nature\. By adopting a queer feminist lens and integrating socio\-ecological perspectives, the research contributes to a more nuanced understanding of loneliness and calls for more inclusive, context\-sensitive approaches in both research and policy\.

## [Longitudinal metal mixture interactions and dyslipidemia in a prospective nested case control study](../publications/5322c71383a2b3be8984.md)

Dyslipidemia affects over 40% of adults aged 50 years or older and contributes substantially to cardiovascular mortality, yet prospective evidence on metal mixtures, nonlinear dose–response relationships, and metal–metal interactions in community\-dwelling older adults remains limited\. In this prospective nested case–control study \(2019–2023\) within the Yinchuan Community\-Dwelling Elderly Cohort, 436 incident dyslipidemia cases and 872 age\-, sex\-, and BMI\-matched controls were included, and 13 urinary metals were quantified by microwave\-assisted acid digestion followed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry \(ICP\-MS\), expressed as µg/g creatinine\. Single\-metal logistic models showed positive dose–response trends for copper and cadmium \(P for trend &lt; 0\.05\), elevated risks for molybdenum \(OR = 1\.44\) and arsenic \(OR = 1\.43\) in the third quartile, and a protective association for zinc in the second quartile \(OR = 0\.68\)\. Machine learning prioritized zinc, copper, cobalt, strontium, and vanadium, and SHAP revealed nonlinear patterns, including J\-shaped associations for copper and vanadium and a biphasic pattern for cobalt\. Weighted quantile sum regression indicated that low\-concentration metal mixtures were associated with increased dyslipidemia risk, and Bayesian kernel machine regression suggested potential Cu–Sr and V–Zn interactions, which generalized additive interaction models supported on an exploratory basis; these models also suggested that exercise attenuated zinc\-associated risk, whereas smoking and alcohol amplified copper and zinc toxicity and meat\-based diets exacerbated strontium and cobalt risks\. Collectively, metal exposures, individually and as mixtures, are associated with dyslipidemia risk in older adults through nonlinear and interactive mechanisms, supporting their potential relevance to precision public health\.

Open\-air farming systems represent critical landscapes for integrated wildlife monitoring, enhancing biosecurity and reducing the risk of pathogen transmission at the wildlife\-livestock interface\. This study aims to conduct comparative monitoring of the biodiversity and detectability of wild species using methods based on morphological identification and environmental DNA \(eDNA\) sampling\. This study provides preliminary insights into the most suitable non\-invasive approaches for assessing wildlife populations in livestock\-dominated landscapes, within an integrated wildlife monitoring framework\.

## [Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time\-Series Reasoning](../publications/532c8217d59f1f9644ba.md)

Hedi Zisling; Liran Nochumsohn; Ilan Naiman; Mihir Parmar; Omri Azencot

Time Series Language Models \(TSLMs\) enable language\-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time\-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks\. We instead introduce complementary representations as a design principle for time\-series reasoning\. Our model combines two visual views: line plots preserve absolute measurements and the observed coordinate frame, while normalized delay embeddings factor out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure\. Dedicated visual encoders integrate both views into a shared language model through visual tokens and multi\-level feature fusion\. Evaluation\-time interventions verify that the two views exhibit distinct invariance profiles, while single\-view ablations show that their combination is particularly beneficial beyond basic perception, with the large gains in prediction and reasoning\. Built on Qwen3\-VL\-8B, our dual\-view model improves overall TSRBench accuracy from 44\.5% with line plots alone to 53\.2%, substantially exceeding the strongest evaluated dedicated TSLM baseline at 36\.7%\. It further achieves 89\.9% accuracy on TSExam and 86\.8% numerical accuracy on multivariate ChatTS alignment\. Together, these results demonstrate that complementary representations provide an effective design principle for general\-purpose TSLMs, enabling models to exploit temporal structure without sacrificing access to the original measurement frame\.

ABSTRACT Aerosol jet printing is a compelling technology for electronics fabrication on non‐planar surfaces, but practical implementation on complex geometries typically requires sophisticated multi‐axis motion planning and hardware capabilities\. Here, a modular angled printhead extension that redirects the nozzle orientation is developed, enabling a simple motion system to support tilted, vertical, and confined surfaces with limited tooling expense and kinematic complexity\. To evaluate this printhead concept and its coupling with ink materials, seven substrate–printhead configurations are characterized for a conductive nanoparticle ink and a dielectric polymer formulation\. Controlled experiments reveal distinct physical regimes for the two inks, with the colloidal ink and polymer resin driven primarily by aerosol‐phase and liquid‐phase phenomena, respectively\. This is quantitatively supported by feature importance analysis of random forest models, showcasing a generalizable framework to analyze complex process science experiments\. Finally, the practical utility of this modular printhead design is highlighted with two demonstrations: nonplanar interconnects spanning horizontal and vertical surfaces, and patterning on the interior surface of a cylinder\. ## [PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITY IN UKRAINE&\#x27;S MINISTRY OF JUSTICE: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL](../publications/534fd15942e485eb28b0.md)

Roman Roman

Public institutions frequently state that managers and public servants bear personal responsibility, yet such clauses often fail to show how responsibility should be attributed in multistage, collegial, and digitally mediated decision\-making\. The aim of this article is to develop a conceptual model of personal responsibility for managers and public servants within the system of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine and to identify the legal, organisational, human\-resource, and digital conditions required for its implementation\. The study draws on the Constitution of Ukraine, legislation on civil service, administrative procedure, access to public information, personal data protection, public electronic registers, electronic identification, and performance evaluation, together with scholarship on public accountability, digital government, and algorithmic accountability\. The methods include system design, functional modelling, doctrinal legal analysis, risk analysis, and scenario testing\. The proposed model is structured as a closed six\-link cycle consisting of mandate, decision preparation and adoption, protected digital trace, multi\-criteria assessment, proportionate consequence, and organisational learning\. Its normative core is the principle of symmetry between lawful authority, available resources and information, controllable risk, and the scope of personal responsibility\. For collegial and technology\-mediated decisions, the model introduces distributed role attribution while preserving the identifiable contribution of each participant\. Practical instruments include a process responsibility passport, a material\-decision record, version and approval logs, recorded professional dissent, quality indicators, graduated responses, and mandatory after\-action review\. Scenario testing demonstrates the model&\#x27;s applicability to drafting normative acts, adopting individual administrative acts, enforcement proceedings, and algorithm\-supported decisions\. The article argues that digital records should be minimally sufficient, tamperevident, role\-accessible, and retention\-limited, while transparency must remain compatible with personal data protection and procedural confidentiality\. The novelty of the study lies in integrating legal individualisation, managerial accountability, and digital traceability into a single learning\-oriented cycle designed to strengthen responsibility without creating a blame culture and to support consistent institutional improvement over time\.

## [Molecular Landscapes of Tumor Dormancy in Gynecologic Malignancies: From Survival Mechanisms to Precision Interception](../publications/536215db6244787f20d3.md)

Shih\-Hsuan Cheng; Ren‐Wang Peng; Changcheng Wu; Chi‐Wen Luo; Emmanuel Naveen Raj; Zhi‐Hong Wen; Tzu‐Hung Hsiao; Weilin Liu

Late recurrence in gynecologic malignancies is associated with tumor dormancy and persistent minimal residual disease \(MRD\)\. Although current treatments reduce proliferating tumor burden, residual cells may survive therapy and drive delayed relapse\. This Review examines dormancy in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers using entry, maintenance, and awakening as an organizing framework rather than a universally demonstrated sequence\. Direct evidence is concentrated in ovarian cancer, whereas evidence in endometrial and cervical cancers remains predominantly indirect\. We delineate candidate biological dependencies\-including redox control, lipid peroxidation buffering, mitochondrial plasticity, adaptive stress\-response programs, epigenetic and post\-transcriptional plasticity, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling\-rather than established vulnerabilities\. On this basis, we evaluate two biologically distinct investigational concepts: suppression of reactivation\-associated signals to prolong clinical latency, and state modulation followed by biomarker\-defined treatment, discussed within established disease\-specific care pathways\. Finally, we propose a translational framework combining longitudinal liquid biopsy with spatial and single\-cell profiling for MRD monitoring, biological stratification, and future probabilistic inference of residual\-cell states\. Together, these concepts support a shift from reactive relapse treatment toward evidence\- and risk\-constrained recurrence\-interception research and provide a framework for validating residual\-state biomarkers and therapeutic dependencies in gynecologic malignancies\.

Andreas Ehstand

POLMANITAI presents a bilingual conceptual atlas for artificial intelligence, politics, democracy, public administration and governance\. ## [Rank Measures of Fine\-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline](../publications/53733557ddcdfe404bf2.md)

Muhammad Usman Altaf

Studies of what fine\-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $ΔW$ by its rank\. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine\-tunes without alignment content\. Measures that count directions put our fine\-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below\. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail\. The pattern holds for thirteen released pairs up to 8B parameters, and it is not a mark of alignment: with training held fixed, instruction data does not stand out from Wikipedia or code, DPO gives the same update whether its preference labels are real or half swapped at random \(one model, modest preference strength\), and scrambled text gives the most concentrated update of all\. Applied to a recent claim that post\-training is superficial because the effective rank of the weights barely changes, the baselines show that a random update of the same size leaves that rank almost unchanged while wrecking the model, and that an edit built on the effective rank of the update has no measurable effect in our tests\. Rank measures of weight updates need a noise baseline, and claims about alignment need a control without alignment content\.

Sameer Jain

IoT technologies have the potential to provide real\-time visibility of labour, materials, and plant and machinery on construction and infrastructure projects, but the knowledge gained from practical experience is rarely turned into reusable decision\-making knowledge\. Most existing studies offer only descriptive observations or technical pilot projects and rarely convert survey findings into clear, rule\-based models that can support asset management decisions\. In this study, knowledge is drawn from a survey of practitioners and a fuzzy expert\-system model is developed which links the perceived benefits of IoT for labour, materials, and plant and machinery to the perceived project performance\. The questionnaire was completed by 75 construction professionals \(96% of them working in India\) and included eleven five\-point Likert items, which were analysed using the relative importance index, Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha, exploratory factor analysis, non\-parametric tests, and clustering\. A Wang–Mendel Mamdani rule base and a Takagi–Sugeno–Kang model were trained and compared with linear regression, random forest, and a mean\-only baseline using leave\-one\-out cross\-validation\. Perceived benefits were high \(mean 3\.96 of 5; relative importance index 0\.79\), and 97\.3% of respondents would recommend IoT\-based solutions\. Materials management \(mean 4\.19\) and plant and machinery management \(mean 4\.17\) ranked highest, whereas labour productivity ranked lowest \(mean 3\.57\)\. Three factors explained 63\.1% of variance, and internal consistency across all items was high \(alpha = 0\.89\)\. Plant and machinery benefits were the dominant predictor of perceived project performance \(standardised beta = 0\.56, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Cross\-validated mean absolute error was 0\.49 for regression, 0\.53 for the Takagi–Sugeno–Kang model, 0\.59 for the Mamdani model, and 0\.64 for the baseline, although differences between models were not statistically significant\. The fuzzy approach yielded 15 interpretable, data\-derived rules\. Practitioners are strongly positive about IoT\-enabled asset management, with plant and machinery the most credible entry point\. ## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DERMATOLOGICAL IMAGE CLASSIFICATION: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY, SKIN TONE DISPARITIES, AND CLINICAL GOVERNANCE](../publications/53c1cc896e286d16a5d6.md)

Background: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly used to classify skin lesions from dermoscopic and clinical images, yet high performance in curated datasets may not translate into safe or equitable clinical use\. Objective: This structured narrative review evaluates diagnostic accuracy, skin\-tone\-related performance disparities, dataset representation, and governance requirements for AI\-based skin\-lesion classification\. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was used as the primary database, supplemented by PubMed Central, Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, journal websites, and reference\-list screening\. English\-language, peer\-reviewed literature published mainly between 2021 and 2026 was synthesised thematically across diagnostic performance, external validity, skin\-tone representation, clinical implementation, and governance\. Results: Meta\-analytic evidence indicates high sensitivity for AI\-based skin\-lesion classification, including pooled sensitivity of 0\.91 and an HSROC\-AUC of 0\.88, but lower specificity and substantial heterogeneity limit direct clinical translation\. Performance declined in darker skin\-tone groups in several external evaluations; in selected models, sensitivity fell between Fitzpatrick types I–II and V–VI\. Limited reporting of skin tone, reliance on internally tested or curated datasets, and sparse prospective evidence further constrain generalisability\. Conclusion: AI should be implemented as clinician\-supervised decision support rather than as an autonomous diagnostic system\. Equitable deployment requires representative datasets, external and subgroup\-stratified validation, transparent reporting, defined clinical accountability, regulatory oversight, and continuous post\-deployment monitoring\.

## [Host determinants of immune\-related adverse events during immune checkpoint inhibition](../publications/53c20c7433fdc4c86e5e.md)

Akram Alwithenani

Immune checkpoint inhibitors \(ICIs\) have transformed the treatment of many cancers, but immune\-related adverse events \(irAEs\) have become their principal limitation\. This review argues that irAEs are not a random hazard of checkpoint blockade but a largely host\-determined outcome layered on a drug\-set baseline\. The regimen fixes how much toxicity risk exists and, through the checkpoint it blocks, which organs are most likely affected\. Within that envelope, host determinants decide which patient crosses the threshold of tolerance, and where\. We synthesise the evidence for four classes of host determinant: germline genetic variation, including the IL7 locus and organ\-directing human leucocyte antigen \(HLA\) alleles; the baseline immune landscape; the gut microbiome and metabolic state; and clinical characteristics led by pre\-existing autoimmune disease\. We draw two distinctions the literature often blurs\. First, susceptibility should be read in two stages: determinants measurable before the first dose, which can triage patients, and on\-treatment changes, which can only signal an event already emerging\. Second, organ\-specific toxicity is neither drug\- nor host\-intrinsic but the product of their intersection, with HLA restriction and shared tumour\-tissue antigens offering the clearest mechanistic account of why a particular organ is struck\. One theme runs throughout: many host features that raise irAE risk also predict a better antitumour response, so host stratification is a matter of optimising a benefit\-to\-toxicity balance rather than screening susceptible patients out\. Multi\-omics and systems immunology are assembling the measurements needed to act on this biology, but no host\-based pre\-treatment predictor is yet validated for clinical use\. Realising one would shift checkpoint immunotherapy from the reactive management of toxicity toward its anticipation\.

## [Boundary\-aware Mixture\-of\-Experts with Calibrated Bayesian Uncertainty for Skin Cancer Detection and Multi\-class Classification](../publications/53d00a82d58740f9eb79.md)

Preeti Kathuria; Deepa Nehra

Dermoscopic analysis is held back by three coupled problems: detection and classification are trained separately, one monolithic backbone must serve lesions whose evidence ranges from keratin micro\-texture to longrange pigment topology, and its confidence is too poorly calibrated to drive a referral\.BMoE\-Net is a single network that localises a lesion, dispatches it to morphology\-specialised experts and returns a calibrated posterior with a referral flag\.Its novelty is the routing signal: prior vision mixtures\-of\-experts gate on the same appearance features their experts consume, which is close to circular, whereas BMoE\-Net computes a Contour Fingerprint Descriptor from the predicted lesion boundary and conditions expert selection on geometry\.It is shown information\-theoretically that this cannot increase the conditional entropy of the optimal routing variable, and the effect is isolated against permuted, randomised and dimension\-matched control gates: routing entropy falls from 1\.061 to 0\.694 nats, with interpretable unsupervised expert specialisations that no control reproduces\.Under lesion\-disjoint partitions BMoE\-Net reaches balanced accuracies of 89\.6%, 86\.9% and 85\.4% on HAM10000, ISIC 2019 and BCN20000 with macro\-AUCs of 0\.979, 0\.973 and 0\.966, beating fifteen baselines under paired DeLong testing with Holm\-Bonferroni correction \(adjusted p &lt; 0\.001\), and attains an AUROC of 0\.969 on ISIC 2024 SLICE\-3D under a patient\-level split\.Expected calibration error on HAM10000 is 0\.034 without rescaling, and at matched metadata availability boundary routing narrows the AUC gap between Fitzpatrick I\-II and V\-VI skin by 7\.2 points\.Code, splits, seeds, evaluation scripts and raw predictions are at https://github\.com/prtkathuria89\-png/BMOE\-NET\.

## [Serum and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers for risk stratification of hospitalized neonates and young infants with suspected serious bacterial infections: a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study](../publications/53d120fde7cfe4035358.md)

Chaymae El Abbass; Luis Alberto Benegas; Andrea Alemany; Cristina Garcia\-Mauriño; Ilham Elouardighi; Imane Zizi; Najat Amalik; Lamya El Laziji; Sobha El Ftouh; Rachid Babi; Khalid Bounagua; Nouhayla Bouali; Sara A Ajanovic; Sara Arias; Dan Ouchi; Fio Vialard; David Torres\-Fernández; Pere Millat\-Martínez; Diana Barrios; Rosauro Varo; Kevin C\. Kain; Ruth Aguilar; Carlota Dobaño; Gemma Moncunill; Houssain Tligui; Bàrbara Baró; Quique Bassat; Amina Barkat

Background Improved risk stratification strategies for neonates and young infants are urgently needed to reduce the substantial mortality burden associated with infectious diseases, particularly in low\- and middle\-income settings\. Evidence supporting the use of host\-response biomarkers to predict disease severity in this population remains limited\. Methods We conducted a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study at a National Reference Neonatology Centre in Morocco and evaluated the prognostic performance of host\-response biomarkers measured in serum and cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) to predict in\-hospital mortality among hospitalized sick neonates and young infants \(&lt;2 months\)\. Twenty\-one biomarkers of immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and neuronal injury were measured using Luminex and compared head\-to\-head\. Results Among 179 participants with available serum and/or CSF samples included in this analysis, 9% died during hospitalization \(11/136 in the serum sample set, and 12/148 in the CSF sample set\)\. In serum, lower concentrations of TRAIL and higher concentrations of Angpt\-2, IL\-8, and uPAR, were associated with in\-hospital death, with TRAIL showing the strongest prognostic performance \(AUROC 0\.86; 95% CI 0\.78\-0\.93\)\. In CSF, PCT was the strongest predictor of severe progression for in\-hospital death \(AUROC 0\.87; 95% CI 0\.80\-0\.95\), whereas higher levels of IL\-6, IL\-12p70, TNFR1, TREM\-1, Angpt\-1, NGAL, and NSE were associated with higher odds of probable or laboratory\-confirmed meningitis\. Discussion Serum levels of TRAIL showed an exploratory association with disease severity in hospitalized neonates and young infants with suspected serious bacterial infections\. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings using multiple biological matrices, characterize kinetics, and determine whether these markers may have clinical utility for risk stratification in this vulnerable population\.

## [Contextualizing CNN attribution maps using predefined image\-derived descriptors in medicinal plant seed classification](../publications/53d5c57a746e747a831e.md)

Su\-Min Chin; Yea‐Jin Park; Dae\-Hyun Jung

Deep learning classifiers can achieve high predictive performance in medicinal plant seed image classification, but prediction accuracy alone does not clarify which visual properties are linked to model responses\. Here, we analyzed RGB images from five medicinal plant seed classes by comparing convolutional neural network \(CNN\) attribution maps with predefined image\-derived descriptor maps within the seed foreground\. ResNet50, EfficientNet\-B0, and ConvNeXt\-Small showed high classification performance under controlled imaging and preprocessing conditions\. However, species\-associated differences could not be disentangled from unrecorded acquisition\-session effects\. In ConvNeXt\-Small, zero baseline absolute Integrated Gradients \(IG\) showed the largest associations with LAB L, Brightness, and fast Fourier transform \(FFT\) low pass, which formed a highly redundant intensity and lightness related cluster\. Removing the explicit input baseline magnitude term reduced these associations by 46\.3% to 49\.2%, and additional baseline, signed IG, and Grad\-CAM analyses showed variation in descriptor associations across attribution representations\. Descriptor summary feature classification further showed that foreground level descriptor statistics contained class discriminative visual information under the controlled imaging conditions\. These results support the use of predefined descriptors for contextualizing attribution patterns within image derived visual contexts, with interpretation focused on method dependent spatial associations\.

## [Sparse Federated Echo State Networks for Time\-Series Classification via Smooth\-L1 Regularization](../publications/53da2d7e5f454fd16757.md)

Gengcheng Lyu; Manuel Röder; Frank\-Michael Schleif

Echo State Networks \(ESNs\), as lightweight implementations of reservoir computing, provide efficient solutions for temporal data processing in resource\-constrained environments\. While standard ESNs offer computational efficiency, their dense readout layers inflate the stored model and the per\-sample inference cost\. This paper introduces a Smooth\-L1 regularized ESN \(SL1ESN\) that promotes sparsity in the readout layer while preserving differentiability for gradient\-based optimization\. The method employs a twice\-differentiable Smooth\-L1 approximation compatible with Newton&\#x27;s method, which we exploit both for centralized training and for a second\-order \(Newton\-step\) federated aggregation scheme\. Under a single fixed shrinkage threshold shared by every dataset and both settings, experiments on seven time\-series classification benchmarks show that SL1ESN learns readouts that are $77$\-\-$95\\%$ sparse in the centralized setting and $75$\-\-$95\\%$ sparse in the federated one, while staying within $0\.7$ accuracy points of the strongest dense baseline on five of the seven benchmarks in the centralized setting and within $1\.6$ points on the same five in the federated one, and the second\-order federated update converges in only a few rounds\. The resulting sparsity compresses the stored model, the per\-sample inference cost, and the server\-to\-client broadcast by a comparable factor\. These results demonstrate the practical value of sparse readouts for edge computing and IoT deployments\.

## [THE PEDAGOGICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF ORGANIZING INTERACTIVE LESSONS BASED ON DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES](../publications/53ea8e6214ae6f47bade.md)

 Mo&\#x27;ydinova Mohlarbegim Abdullajon qizi; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre

This article investigates the pedagogical significance of digitally supported interactive lessons and proposes a research\-informed approach to their planning and evaluation\. Rather than equating interactivity with screen use or frequent clicking, it conceptualizes interactive teaching as purposeful engagement in questioning, explanation, problem solving, collaboration, feedback, and reflection\. The analysis integrates constructive alignment, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework, the ICAP model of cognitive engagement, formative assessment principles, and inclusive learning design\. A six\-stage instructional cycle is proposed: activation, inquiry, collaborative construction, application, formative feedback, and reflection\. An illustrative 60\-minute teacher\-education lesson shows how digital tools can support the stages while retaining essential face\-to\-face dialogue\. A comparative matrix identifies relationships among instructional technologies, student actions, and assessment evidence\. The discussion addresses learner agency, cognitive overload, digital inequality, accessibility, data protection, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence\. The contribution is conceptual and methodological; it offers operational criteria for lesson quality and directions for future classroom evaluation, but it does not claim experimentally verified improvements\. The central conclusion is that digital interactivity has pedagogical value only when it produces observable, cognitively meaningful learner activity\.
