## [The application of neural net orks in the operation of engineering structures](../publications/53f4d14dd4dabba270a1.md)

I\. V\. Chaplin; Ya\. V\. Tonkushin; Бахтин Сергей Анатольевич; Сергей Иванович Герасимов; S\. V\. Efimov

The article discusses current developments in the use of artificial neural networks \(ANN – Artificial Neural Network\) and machine vision technologies in the operation of engineering structures, with an emphasis on the identification of defects in the examination of bridge structures\. Scientific research is aimed at finding the most appropriate methodology to simplify and improve the quality of the survey process, as well as the architecture of the neural network\. The analysis of domestic and foreign studies devoted to the automatic detection of defects in building structures using convolutional neural networks \(CNN – Convolutional Neural Network\), YOLO \(You Only Look Once\) algorithms, AutoML \(Automated Machine Learning\) methods and software and hardware complexes based on unmanned aerial vehicles\. The advantages and disadvantages of existing solutions related to the dependence of recognition quality on the size of the training sample, shooting conditions, the difficulty of locating low\-contrast defects and the need for additional involvement in the process of engineering interpretation of the results are considered\. The existing approaches to defect identification have been systematized, and the positive and negative elements of tools in machine vision systems have been identified for their prospective consideration when creating a module for bridge inspection\. The conclusion is made about the prospects of introducing neural network technologies into the practice of surveying engineering structures, provided that specialized training samples are formed and the accuracy of the models is independently verified\. The availability of a powerful neural network tool for examining bridge structures, trained by engineers on specific examples of the bridge sphere, will simplify the survey and increase the number of structures evaluated per unit of time by one team\. In conclusion, a multi\-stage approach is proposed for further research, including the recognition of structural elements, the detection and classification of defects, as well as subsequent engineering verification of the results\.

## [Managing an FDA BLA Lifecycle from Complete Response Letter to Indication Narrowing: An Allogeneic Cell Therapy Case Study in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/53fe39288f626786328f.md)

Yash Manish Shah; Peivand Pirouzi

When a marketing application&\#x27;s proposed indication is narrowed partway through review to align more closely with a trial&\#x27;s actual primary endpoint, the change is rarely cosmetic: it typically reflects a sponsor&\#x27;s recognition that the evidentiary case for the originally proposed, broader claim was weaker than the case for a more specific one the trial was actually designed and powered to support\. This article traces the complete regulatory lifecycle of an allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\), from its initial pharmacodynamic rationale through a Complete Response Letter, an adverse advisory committee vote, and a subsequent amendment narrowing the proposed indication from cardiomyopathy to upper\-limb function, as a case study in how indication scope and evidentiary strength are inseparable regulatory variables\. The article develops the mechanism, the evidence base, and the regulatory timeline in full, proposes a real\-world evidence strategy designed around the lessons of this lifecycle, and closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals managing indication strategy for mutation\-agnostic cell and gene therapies\.Keywords: allogeneic cell therapy; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; indication narrowing; Complete Response Letter; Biologics License Application; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [A Copula\-Based Joint Model for Speed and Accuracy](../publications/53ffd34ec5a6bf61e34f.md)

Sunbeom Kwon; Susu Zhang

This study proposes a copula\-based model that relaxes the multivariate normality assumption among latent traits in the joint modeling of multimodal data, such as item response and response times\. In the structural model, the joint distribution of latent traits is defined via a copula with tail dependence\. An expectation\-maximization algorithm with stochastic approximation is implemented for parameter estimation\. A simulation study evaluates the proposed method&\#x27;s accuracy in ability estimation under various conditions, comparing it to traditional approaches\. By better capturing the dependence structure between latent ability and speed, the proposed method outperforms the traditional approach with multivariate normality assumption\. Applied to a variety of empirical datasets, the proposed method&\#x27;s flexibility and the improvement in model fit are illustrated\. The copula\-based latent variable modeling can be generalized to broader applications in psychological testing involving multivariate latent traits\.

## [Geospatial assessment of natural hazard risks in coastal Bangladesh with a focus on communities outside embankments in Barguna](../publications/540a216df9f2a4d68ae5.md)

Md\. Najmul Kabir; Sabina Islam; Md\. Bahuddin Sikder; Shah Md Shahnewaz Sayem; Emon Barua; Md\. Mominul Islam

Bangladesh is highly disaster\-prone, with coastal areas exposed to sea\-level rise, cyclones, storm surges, flooding, and salinity intrusion, particularly in communities outside embankments\. This study developed a Coastal Vulnerability Index \(CVI\) for outside\-embankment areas of Barguna Sadar Upazila by integrating natural hazard intensity, physical\-geological conditions, and socio\-economic vulnerability\. The Natural Hazard Vulnerability Index \(NVI\), derived from cyclone wind, storm surge, flood depth, salinity, and rainfall using Log\-Pearson Type III distributions, increased from 0\.35 at the 2\-year return period to 0\.75 at 100 years\. Physical and geological vulnerability \(PVI = 0\.51\) reflected low elevation \(mean = 1\.09 m\), gentle slope \(0\.25°\), dynamic geomorphology, shoreline change \(− 4\.8 to \+ 18 m yr⁻¹\), and relative sea\-level rise \(\+ 15\.08 mm yr⁻¹\)\. Socio\-economic vulnerability was comparatively low \(SEVI = 0\.43\), with lower social \(0\.31\) and economic \(0\.32\) vulnerability but higher housing and infrastructure vulnerability \(HVI = 0\.65\)\. The mean CVI was 0\.47, with 3\.63%, 28\.88%, 49\.22%, 15\.81%, and 2\.47% of the study area classified as very low, low, moderate, high, and very high vulnerability, respectively\. NVI and PVI strongly influenced the spatial pattern of the CVI, while comparatively lower SEVI reflected greater household coping capacity, although housing and infrastructure remained important constraints\. The return\-period\-based CVI framework provides a practical approach for assessing directly exposed outside\-embankment communities and supporting location\-specific coastal adaptation planning\.

## [CT\-based multimodal radiogenomic model integrating tumor and perirenal fat features for prognosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma](../publications/540fc4b4e5892b9273fa.md)

Yi\-Fan Zhang; Yun\-Hua Ji; Didi Wen; Chen Liu; Pei\-Wen Shi; Hao\-Zhong Hou; Peng\-He Quan; Xiaozheng Fan; Bo Yang; Zhen Yao; Jia\-Min Guo; Xian\-Ming Lu; Xiaojian Yang; Minwen Zheng; Long\-Long Zhang

Clear cell renal cell carcinoma \(ccRCC\), the most common renal cell carcinoma subtype \(60%\-85%\), remains challenging due to suboptimal TNM\-based risk stratification and limited precision in adjuvant targeted therapy \(5\.4%\-10\.5% survival benefit with overtreatment risk\)\. Perirenal fat, linked to ccRCC prognosis via volume and density, is underexplored in integration with radiogenomics \(tumor molecular features\) for comprehensive prognosis\. Retrospective analysis included a training cohort \(Xijing Hospital, n = 226\) and testing cohort \(TCIA/TCGA, n = 134\) of resectable ccRCC patients with preoperative contrast\-enhanced CT and exome sequencing data\. CT\-based tumor/perirenal fat radiomic features were extracted via 3D Slicer/PyRadiomics, with scores built using LASSO and stepwise Cox regression\. Genetic scores derived from 639 cancer\-related genes \(top 20 mutated genes\) and clinical scores \(e\.g\., TNM stage\) were constructed via Cox regression\. A multimodal nomogram integrating these scores was validated using C\-index, time\-dependent AUC, and SHAP analysis\. The nomogram outperformed unimodal scores, with C\-indices of 0\.856 \(training\) and 0\.859 \(testing\)\. Time\-dependent AUCs for 1\-5\-year PFS were consistently higher\. SHAP identified tumor/perirenal fat scores, TP53 mutation, and grade G4 as key contributors\.Multiple machine learning algorithms were used to predict four genes with prognostic value, and their correlations in multimodal data were analyzed\. Subgroup analyses confirmed robust risk stratification\. Patients with targeted therapy risk difference rate ≥ 47% had longer PFS with therapy \(HR = 0\.545, p = 0\.038\), while those with &lt; 10% fared better without therapy \(HR = 2\.051, p = 0\.035\), with similar trends in high\-risk subgroups\. Targeted therapy\-related analyses are exploratory and require prospective validation\. This CT\-based multimodal nomogram integrates radiomic, genomic, and clinical data to characterize ccRCC across scales, providing auxiliary reference for screening patients who may gain potential survival benefit from adjuvant targeted therapy, reducing overtreatment/undertreatment\.

## [Reimagining Media Studies Education in Pakistan through Artificial Intelligence: Curriculum Integration, Competencies, and Challenges](../publications/5411980174a606b7cbde.md)

Syed Waqar Ul Hasan; Muhammad Aftab Madni; Taha Shabbir

This paper studies how artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping media studies education in Pakistan\. It uses primary policy data from the Higher Education Commission \(HEC\), mainly the 2025 revised curriculum for Media and Communication Studies and the national decision to make AI a compulsory course, together with recent international research\. The paper shows that AI has moved from the edges of the media curriculum to its centre\. In the new HEC scheme, a three\-credit course called “AI &amp; Data Analytics in Media” is mandatory for every undergraduate student, a Data Journalism course sits in the core, and a full specialization in Data and Computational Journalism is offered as an option\. Drawing on competency frameworks from UNESCO and leading scholars, the paper sets out the knowledge, skills, and values that media graduates now need: understanding AI, using AI tools responsibly, reading data and algorithms, judging AI outputs, and keeping ethics and human judgement central\. The paper then explains the real problems that stand in the way, including weak infrastructure and the digital divide, limited teacher training, academic integrity worries, weak support for Urdu and regional languages, and the difficulty of enforcing bans\. It closes with practical steps for universities, teachers, and policymakers\. The main argument is simple: Pakistan has taken an important first step on paper, but turning policy into real classroom learning will decide whether the reform succeeds\.

## [A systematic and critical review of artificial intelligence applications for enhancing well stimulation operations and sustainable reservoir management](../publications/54331575f1c8d5966124.md)

Ali Naderi Hamlabadi; Mohammadreza Akbari; Mobina Pazoki; Yasin Khalili

Well stimulation remains essential for improving reservoir productivity, but conventional workflows are constrained by geological heterogeneity, limited data, and dependence on empirical correlations\. This systematic and comparative review examines artificial\-intelligence applications in hydraulic fracturing, acidizing, sand control, and ultrasonic stimulation, focusing on 2020–2025 while selectively considering earlier foundational studies\. The quantitative synthesis of 23 key application studies identified 11 studies on acidizing and acid fracturing \(47\.8%\), 8 on hydraulic fracturing \(34\.8%\), 3 on sand control \(13\.0%\), and 1 on ultrasonic stimulation \(4\.3%\)\. Neural\-network architectures were reported in 16 studies \(69\.6%\), while tree\-based learners or ensembles appeared in 13 studies \(56\.5%\); these categories overlap because several studies compared multiple algorithms\. Among studies reporting numerical performance, R2 values for acidizing\-related regression tasks ranged from 0\.82 to 0\.96, while reported classification accuracies for selected acidizing and sand\-control applications ranged from 87\.5% to above 90%\. These values were not statistically pooled because the studies used different prediction targets, data scales, validation procedures, and performance definitions\. Tree\-based ensembles and neural networks currently dominate fracture\-design and acidizing applications, whereas reinforcement learning, hybrid optimization, and physics\-informed approaches remain less frequently investigated\. Field\-scale and cross\-field validation are limited, particularly for sand control and ultrasonic stimulation, for which the available evidence is predominantly laboratory\- or simulation\-based\. The principal barriers to operational deployment are proprietary and small datasets, inconsistent validation, limited interpretability, and uncertain model transferability\. Future research should prioritize benchmark datasets, standardized reporting, external field validation, explainable and physics\-constrained models, and carefully evaluated closed\-loop stimulation systems\. ## [Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation](../publications/5433c32c60cc59e56996.md)

Feiyang Chen; Runze Ma; Zichen Wang; Jiong Lou; Zihan Wang; Shuangjia Zheng; Jie Li

A language model can generate several solutions to the same problem, some leading to correct answers and others to incorrect ones\. Many post\-training methods turn these trajectories into learning signals using supervision from reference answers, verifiable feedback, or external teachers\. Without such supervision, learning from the model&\#x27;s own generations becomes less straightforward, as their correctness cannot be reliably assessed\. An incorrect solution may nevertheless contain useful intermediate reasoning, so its value as supervision need not be determined solely by its final answer\. Can a model improve by learning from its unverified peer solutions without first determining which are correct? We propose Shared Residual Distillation \(SRD\), an on\-policy self\-distillation method that learns from the model&\#x27;s own unverified peer trajectories\. SRD compares how peers change the prediction distribution relative to a control, retaining adjustments that agree in direction and are conservative in magnitude\. This yields supervision without treating any complete solution as correct, and the trained model requires no peers at inference time\. Starting from the corresponding base models, SRD raises mean AIME24\-\-26 avg@12 from 11\.02 to 16\.20 on Qwen3\-1\.7B, from 19\.07 to 45\.46 on Qwen3\-4B, and from 21\.39 to 54\.44 on Qwen3\-8B\. Controlled ablations support the value of the shared\-residual construction, and we observe no degradation relative to the base models on two general\-capability benchmarks\.

## [The artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT and its impact on the development of the integrated writing skill in students at the International Learning&\#x27; Institute](../publications/544772600ddcd990dced.md)

Paul Sebastián Montenegro Rosero; Elena Valeria Flores Borja

The present research analyzed the impact of the pedagogical use of ChatGPT on the development of English written production in students at the International Learning Institute, located in the city of Tulcán, Ecuador\. The study arose from the difficulties identified in grammatical precision, spelling, syntactic organization, coherence, cohesion, and lexical variety of the texts produced by the students\. The study was conducted with the entire population, consisting of 45 students aged between 14 and 22 years, with English proficiency levels ranging from A1 to B2\. The research was developed using a quantitative approach, with a descriptive scope and a single\-group exploratory design with a pretest and posttest\. A questionnaire and a written production evaluation rubric were used for data collection\. During the intervention, ChatGPT was used as a complementary tool to provide immediate feedback, identify grammatical and spelling errors, suggest improvements in textual structure, and promote vocabulary expansion\. The results obtained through the diagnostic survey evidenced difficulties in sentence structuring, the use of varied vocabulary, punctuation, and grammatical accuracy, as well as differences in the frequency with which students used ChatGPT to support their writing\. It is concluded that the planned, ethical, and supervised integration of ChatGPT can constitute a complementary strategy to strengthen English written production, if its application is accompanied by teacher guidance and the student&\#x27;s critical participation\.

## [Engineered live biotherapeutic products: design decisions, failure modes, and clinical translation](../publications/5455219eb880898b5b8f.md)

Sijia Shen; Junsheng Zhao; Hainv Gao

Engineered live biotherapeutic products \(LBPs\) are viable microorganisms deliberately modified to perform a therapeutic function in a patient\. Recombinant therapeutic strains are considered separately from conventional probiotics, donor\-derived microbiota products, vaccines, living diagnostics, environmental systems, and systemically administered oncolytic bacteria\. Selected oncology platforms share engineering constraints with LBPs, although their classification as LBPs depends on the specific therapy\. The target product profile sets the niche, route, and exposure requirements against which chassis, genetic control, and payload release are assessed\. Fitness costs, genetic stability, basal leakage, and clearance constrain circuit complexity\. Formulation and manufacturing must preserve viability and mechanism\-linked potency, with process control and independent containment layers evaluated quantitatively during development\. Human studies of engineered metabolic strains support feasibility, short\-term tolerability, clearance, and pharmacodynamic activity, although broad or durable clinical benefit has not yet been shown\. Microbiota products approved by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\) provide regulatory precedents for live microbial medicines, with approval specific to each unengineered product\. Clinical trials require separate assessment of target engagement and patient benefit\.

## [HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision\-Language Models](../publications/545ff655a5256be4a495.md)

Oscar Kemme; Janek Haberer; Ali Hojjat; Olaf Landsiedel

LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data\-center GPUs to resource\-constrained edge devices\. Their fixed\-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model\-size targets\. We introduce HydraLLM, an elastic MQA\-based architecture\. Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed\-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set\. We introduce a static\-to\-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre\-trained model checkpoint, includes importance\-driven weight reordering and stochastic subnetwork training with knowledge distillation\. We extend this principle to multimodal inference through an elastic projection module whose output width follows the active text width\. HydraLLM covers a wider range of active parameter configurations than FFN\-only elastic architectures\. With 75% of heads active, HydraLLM achieves 2\.2 percentage points higher TriviaQA accuracy than a state\-of\-the\-art nested baseline configuration which has 17\.25% more parameters\. With 50% of heads active, our multimodal model achieves a CLIPScore comparable to that of the 7$\\times$ larger Gemma 3 4B model\. With only 25% of heads active, HydraLLM increases token\-generation throughput by 75\.3% over the full\-width configuration\.

## [Emerging Trends in Management and Organization: Strategic Adaptation in Volatile Global Markets](../publications/546385104754179e0360.md)



In the contemporary business environment, organisations are faced with a complex set of challenges, including geopolitical tensions, increasing sustainability regulations, rapid digital transformation, and the integration of artificial intelligence into various aspects of professional activities\. In such circumstances, the degree of competitive advantage is less dependent on fixed plans and more dependent on the capacity to adapt\. This edited volume brings together seven conceptual chapters that examine strategic adaptation across three levels of analysis\. The initial section of the text concerns itself with the subject of digital transformation in the context of uncertainty\. The text revisits universalist, contingency and structuralist perspectives, discussing how digital strategy helps international firms detect, respond to and recover from geopolitical risk\. It also analyses artificial intelligence as an organisational actor that reshapes power, authority and responsibility\. The second part of the study examines legitimacy and sustainability in global markets\. It asks when ESG functions as a source of competitive advantage or merely as a market entry requirement\. It also explores how women\-focused diversity policies can decouple into pinkwashing\. The third part of the text focuses on human\-based capabilities, establishing a link between organisational emotional memory and the concepts of learning and sustainability\. The text also explains how social intelligence can become a strategic advantage through the medium of intrapreneurship\. The chapters draw on institutional theory, the resource\-based view and dynamic capabilities to argue that adaptation is not a reactive adjustment, but rather a strategic capability built through structures, people and legitimacy\. The book offers integrative frameworks for researchers, graduate students and managers seeking to understand management and organisation under uncertainty\.

## [Serum Interleukin\-1β and High\-Sensitivity C\-Reactive Protein Across Schizas Morphological Grades in Degenerative Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: An Exploratory Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/5479a85825e124ff66fc.md)

Arazy Gifta Prima; Rendra Leonas; Theodorus

Background: In degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis \(LSS\), symptom severity often bears little relation to the narrowing seen on imaging, and inflammation may contribute\. Objective: To determine whether the Schizas grade of the dural sac is associated with serum interleukin\-1β \(IL\-1β\) and high\-sensitivity C\-reactive protein \(hs\-CRP\) after confounder control\. Methods: Thirty non\-obese patients with LSS \(body mass index \[BMI\] &lt;30 kg/m²\) at Dr\. Mohammad Hoesin General Hospital, Palembang, were studied after a verified 7\-day anti\-inflammatory washout\. Two blinded radiologists graded axial T2\-weighted magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\): Grade A, n = 10; B, n = 11; C/D, n = 9 \(κ = 0\.84\)\. Morning IL\-1β and hs\-CRP were compared with Kruskal–Wallis tests and bootstrapped regression\. Results: BMI \(p = 0\.312\) and sex \(p = 0\.927\) were similar across grades, but age and symptom duration rose with grade \(both p &lt; 0\.001\)\. IL\-1β medians climbed from 5\.60 \[4\.90–6\.40\] pg/mL in Grade A to 8\.45 \[7\.20–9\.50\] pg/mL in Grade B and 11\.20 \[9\.10–13\.80\] pg/mL in Grade C/D \(p &lt; 0\.001\); hs\-CRP medians were 2\.15 \[1\.80–2\.60\], 3\.40 \[2\.90–4\.10\] and 4\.90 \[3\.80–6\.20\] mg/L \(p = 0\.003\)\. With age and BMI in the model, grade remained associated with IL\-1β \(B = 2\.05, β = 0\.46, p = 0\.012, R² = 0\.41\) and hs\-CRP \(B = 1\.12, β = 0\.49, p = 0\.009, R² = 0\.44\); no variance inflation factor reached 2\.5\. Conclusion: Greater dural sac compression went with higher serum IL\-1β and hs\-CRP, independent of age and BMI\. Larger longitudinal cohorts are needed before these markers are used alongside MRI\.

## [Balancing Short‐Term Genetic Gain and Long‐Term Diversity: Haplotype‐Based Breeding Strategies for Yield Improvement in Chickpea](../publications/547dc457b97d41801538.md)

Kotte Bhargava; Rutwik Barmukh; Will Shaffer; Oluwaseun Akinlade; Ajaya Karkee; Michael K\. Udvardi; Lee Thomas Hickey; Rajeev Kumar Varshney

ABSTRACT Chickpea \( Cicer arietinum L\.\) is one of the most important grain legumes and provides a major source of protein, vitamins and minerals worldwide\. Despite decades of traditional breeding delivering significant genetic gains in disease resistance and adaptation, seed yield improvement has advanced only incrementally, constrained by the highly polygenic nature of the trait, pronounced genotype‐by‐environment interactions and insufficient utilisation of existing genetic diversity\. This review elucidates the genetic architecture of seed yield in chickpea by integrating comprehensive QTL/association mapping across diverse populations and environments\. Haplotype‐based breeding emerges as a promising strategy, leveraging linkage disequilibrium \(LD\) defined blocks to capture multiallelic QTL variation and beneficial alleles associated with target traits of interest\. Crucially, layering multitrait information onto these haploblocks enables breeders to classify traits according to their concurrent effects on yield across the target environment, prioritising those that are yield‐enhancing and avoiding those that are yield‐reducing\. We outline the operational framework: haplotype genomic selection using local genomic estimated breeding values \(local GEBVs\) to prioritise chromosome segments over whole‐genome truncation selection; and artificial intelligence \(AI\)–driven parent selection to identify complementary parental combinations from diverse populations to make progress towards an ‘ultimate genotype’ that will stack superior haplotypes for targeted traits\. By integrating multitrait correlations, haplotype‐resolved QTL maps and computational optimisation, this strategy targets potential yield ideotypes while preserving adaptive diversity and minimising linkage drag, promising to break the current yield plateau and accelerate genetic gain in seed yield beyond the historical rate of up to 0\.6% per year\. The framework provides a blueprint for haplotype‐based breeding approaches across crops confronting polygenic yield barriers under climate‐constrained production\.

## [Airflow\-enabled swallowing rehabilitation after tracheostomy in acquired neurological disease: mechanisms, current evidence, and a stage\-based clinical pathway](../publications/5489283f79ad526021e2.md)

Jiayi Xia; Song Pei; Hongwei Qin; Yao Lu; Song Zhou; 白玉龙

Tracheostomy is common after severe stroke and other acquired neurological diseases, yet the route from airway stabilization to safe oral feeding and decannulation is often fragmented\. Dysphagia in this setting cannot be attributed to the tracheostomy tube alone: neurological injury, prolonged intubation, deconditioning, impaired alertness, and laryngeal injury interact with upper\-airway bypass\. Nevertheless, loss of expiratory airflow through the larynx and reduction of subglottic pressure may weaken sensory input, respiratory\-swallow coordination, cough effectiveness, and secretion clearance\. This Mini Review examines airflow\-restoration strategies as a way to reconnect this aerodigestive sensorimotor loop\. Cuff deflation, tube occlusion, one\-way speaking valves, above\-cuff airflow, and pulsed subglottic air or oxygen share a physiological aim but differ in airway requirements, dose control, and safety\. Small mechanistic studies and recent clinical trials suggest improvements in penetration\-aspiration, residue, spontaneous swallowing, and secretion management; however, the evidence remains heterogeneous, and oxygen has not been separated from the mechanical effects of flow and pressure\. We therefore propose that airflow should be used as phenotype\-guided sensory priming immediately before or during task\-specific feeding, rather than treated as an isolated device intervention\. A stage\-based pathway links instrumental assessment, airflow restoration, functional eating practice, and decannulation readiness\. Future trials should report gas composition, flow, pressure, pulse timing, humidity, cuff condition, and concurrent feeding tasks, and should prioritize oral intake, pneumonia, and decannulation alongside physiological outcomes\.

## [Vehicle Detection from Overhead Satellite Images in Saudi Arabia with YOLOv12](../publications/5491ed1a4138a8b0b7a2.md)

Muhamad Syukron; Radical Rakhman Wahid

One of the primary challenges in urban areas of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is managing traffic flow and implementing effective urban planning strategies in densely populated cities\. Utilizing satellite imagery for vehicle counting presents an effective solution to enhance urban planning and economic monitoring\. Based on a review of the literature, the lack of vehicle counting datasets using satellite imagery is a significant gap\. To address this, we introduce the Saudi Vehicles Dataset, which comprises 410 images, each 500x500 pixels, with 5,609 manually annotated vehicles\. To ensure the dataset&\#x27;s quality and generalization, we benchmark it against two other satellite datasets: Car Synthetic and COWC\. Benchmarking was performed using the latest version of the YOLO object detection algorithm, YOLOv12\. The results indicate that our dataset yields comparable performance metrics to the other datasets\. Specifically, when YOLOv12 was trained on the Saudi Vehicles Dataset, it achieved the high scores for mAP50, recall, precision, and F1\-score, with values of 0\.977, 0\.939, 0\.945, and 0\.942, respectively\. While the best performance was observed on the synthetic dataset, achieving a perfect precision score of 1, the Saudi Vehicles Dataset showed superior performance in terms of recall, precision, and F1\-score\. The dataset is publicly available for use and can be accessed via this link: https://github\.com/Syukrondzeko/saudi\-vehicle\-dataset

## [Interleukin pathway genotype and the grandiosity dimension of psychosis: a machine learning gene set analysis with unsupervised anomaly detection controls](../publications/549f14852685a73cf082.md)

Maksymilian Aleksander Brzezicki; Przemyslaw Temistokles Zakowicz; Paweł Kapelski; Monika Wiłkość\-Dębczyńska; Aleksandra Rajewska‐Rager; Maria Skibińska

Immune involvement in psychosis is well supported, although most of the evidence comes from studies of negative and deficit symptoms\. Grandiosity, in comparison, has received little attention\. It is, however, the one symptom for which the two main accounts of inflammation in psychosis, activation and reward blunting, make opposite predictions\. We tested these predictions in 489 patients with schizophrenia from the Poznań cohort, genotyped for 26 functional variants in eight interleukin\-pathway genes and rated with the Operational Criteria Checklist \(OPCRIT\)\. Grandiosity was scored from the two OPCRIT items for inflated self\-esteem and grandiose delusions\. The panel was first tested as a whole, and each gene was then analyzed as a set with the sequence kernel association test \(SKAT\), with false\-discovery\-rate control and selection\-adjusted permutation\. For any gene that passed, we localized the signal within it and estimated the effect with Firth penalized logistic regression\. Its stability was examined by held\-out splits, jackknife, fragility analysis, comparison with five other symptom dimensions, and anomaly detection\. The panel as a whole did not predict grandiosity \(out\-of\-fold Spearman rho = 0\.041, permutation p = 0\.159\)\. One gene, IL10, showed an association \(SKAT p = 0\.0028, q = 0\.023; selection\-adjusted p = 0\.025\), which was confined to the −819/−592 promoter locus\. Carriers of two copies had a Firth odds ratio of 5\.28 \(95% CI 2\.37 to 12\.48, p = 4\.5 × 10 \-5 \), consistent with a recessive effect, and 65% of the 26 carriers had grandiosity, against 24% of non\-carriers\. The effect was specific to grandiosity \(standardized beta 0\.19, p = 2 × 10 \-5 \) and moderately reproducible across split halves \(r = 0\.36; mania control r = 0\.03\)\. It did not depend on sex, age, or age at onset, and it was unchanged under alternative SKAT kernels, under panel principal components, and after adjustment for neuroleptic response\. Two\-copy carriage did not differ between the 466 cases and 482 controls\. We propose a recessive IL10 −819/−592 effect specific to grandiosity as a hypothesis for independent replication\.

## [VR\-FOCUS: evaluating eye tracking during a virtual reality N\-back task as a marker of cognitive load in chronic pain](../publications/549f5fd8aa134f923955.md)

Jordan Tsigarides; Jennifer O\. Bowler; Jack Dainty; Anthony J\. Bagnall; Alex J\. MacGregor

Immersive virtual reality \(VR\) is a promising medium for adaptive pain therapeutics, but objective markers of cognitive load suitable for real\-time adaptation remain insufficiently characterised in chronic pain\. This study evaluated whether eye tracking embedded within a consumer\-available VR system provides signatures of cognitive load during a VR N\-back task\. A total of 84 participants \(42 healthy controls, 42 chronic musculoskeletal pain\) completed five levels \(Baseline to 4\-Back\) while ocular responses were recorded\. Performance declined and subjective workload increased with task level, confirming successful manipulation of cognitive demand, although performance plateaued beyond 3\-Back\. In mixed\-effects models, larger pupil diameter and higher blink rate were associated with task level and workload, without group differences\. Logistic regression using summary features discriminated 1\-Back from 4\-Back at near\-chance levels \(0\.51–0\.60\)\. Time\-series classifiers exploiting temporal structure performed substantially better in healthy controls \(0\.74–0\.88\) but were attenuated in chronic pain \(0\.58–0\.65\)\. Age alone did not appear to explain this difference, although a contribution cannot be excluded\. These findings support the feasibility of VR\-embedded eye tracking for cognitive load estimation in healthy adults, but performance in chronic pain is currently insufficient for reliable individual\-level inference; closed\-loop application in this population will require participant\-calibrated models and prospective validation\.

## [Based Optimization Models for High\-Performance Computing and Intelligent Network Architectures: Graph Theory Models for Complex Network Analysis and Intelligent System Design](../publications/54a8f277a043ccfde407.md)



High\-performance computing \(HPC\) systems and large\-scale intelligent network architectures increasingly depend on graph\-theoretic models to optimize interconnect topology, minimize communication latency, balance computational load, and enable scalable data routing across thousands to millions of nodes\.As exascale computing systems and hyperscale data center networks continue to grow in size and heterogeneity, traditional ad hoc network design approaches are proving inadequate for managing the combinatorial complexity of topology selection, graph partitioning, and routing optimization\.This paper reviews graph theory\-based optimization models applied to HPC interconnect design and intelligent network architectures, examining topological structures including fattree, dragonfly, torus, and hypercube networks through the lens of graph diameter, bisection bandwidth, and spectral properties\.The study further examines graph partitioning algorithms for parallel workload distribution, spectral clustering and community detection methods for network analysis, and the emerging integration of graph neural networks \(GNNs\) into intelligent network design and traffic prediction\.A comparative methodology is described using graph\-theoretic metrics, including algebraic connectivity, average path length, and bisection width, alongside partitioning quality metrics such as edge\-cut ratio and load imbalance, evaluated across benchmark topologies and real\-world data center network case studies including Google&\#x27;s Jupiter fabric and modern dragonfly\-based supercomputer interconnects\.Reported findings indicate that dragonfly and related lowdiameter topologies achieve substantially improved bisection bandwidth and reduced hop count relative to traditional torus networks at comparable cost, while multilevel graph partitioning algorithms such as METIS remain the dominant practical solution for large\-scale workload distribution despite known limitations in preserving global structural properties\.The paper concludes by identifying key challenges in scaling graphtheoretic optimization to exascale system sizes, the integration of machine learning with classical graph algorithms, and open problems in dynamic, traffic\-adaptive network reconfiguration\.

## [An Integrated Human\-in\-the\-Loop Patent Search Workflow: An Exploratory Case Study Combining Keyword, Similarity, Semantic, and Citation\-Based Retrieval](../publications/54a9f091496fc38f66e3.md)

Federico Rotini; Francesco Saverio Frillici; Lorenzo Fiorineschi

Patent retrieval is important for innovation management, R&amp;D planning, and intellectual property strategy, yet conventional searches are hindered by terminology variability, synonymy, broad patent scopes, and classification limitations\. This study presents an integrated, iterative workflow combining keyword\-based retrieval, semantic analysis, document\-similarity searches, citation\-based refinement, and consensus\-based manual relevance assessment\. The workflow is illustrated through a single exploratory case starting from the same reference patent used by Moeller and Moehrle\. After correction of duplicate entries, the final dataset contains 49 distinct patent identifiers: 19 were assigned to the high\-relevance category, 20 to the related category, and 10 to the peripheral\-relevance category\. Six of the ten documents listed in the reference study were also retrieved; this 60% document\-level overlap is descriptive and must not be interpreted as recall because the published list is not an exhaustive ground truth\. The case illustrates how complementary retrieval channels, set intersections, iterative seed updating, and human decisions can be organized in a transparent workflow\. It does not demonstrate superiority, general effectiveness, or equivalence between non\-domain experts and expert searchers\.

## [Climate\-Related Challenges, Risk, Environmental Health Promotion: An Interdisciplinary Approach](../publications/54b68045638fd8e0613a.md)

Márcia Cristina Braga Nunes Varricchio; Sandra Ávila Gaspar; Marcelo Vacite; Armando Isaac Nigri; Marcos Tadeu Varricchio; Nelson Brêtas de Noronha Gomes; P\. S\. T\. Brioso; Ricardo Machado Kuster; Celso Luiz Salgueiro Lage; Simone da Silva; Alexandre dos Santos Pyrrho

Climate change has intensified the frequency, severity, and geographic reach of extreme weather events, posing growing risks to human and environmental health worldwide\. This study is a descriptive\-analytical systematic literature review \(PRISMA\), combined with a case study of an interdisciplinary research group, examining scientific production and official data on global climate\-related disasters from 2004 to 2024, with emphasis on historical trends and geographic distribution\. Data were drawn from specialized databases and international organizations, including Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, IPCC, EM\-DAT, NOAA, NASA, WMO, and UNDRR\. Results show a marked acceleration of climate disasters in the last two decades: between 2004 and 2024, 7\.348 events were recorded, causing approximately 1\.23 million deaths, affecting 4\.2 billion people, and generating an estimated US$2\.97 trillion in economic losses, representing substantial increases relative to the 1980\-1999 period\. The most affected regions include the Americas, Europe, and other areas exposed to hurricanes, flooding, drought, and wildfires, with disproportionate impacts on developing countries and socially vulnerable populations\. The findings reinforce the unequivocal scientific recognition of anthropogenic influence on extreme events and underscore the urgency of mitigation, adaptation, and climate justice measures\. The study also highlights the interdisciplinary and intersectoral contribution of ethnobotany, traditional knowledge, bioethics, and environmental health promotion in addressing these challenges, in line with the One Health approach, promoted to “movement people” whose collectives \(cultures and traditions\) were under social vulnerability as social subjects and work was performed at local level\. It is concluded that the current decade is critical for shaping the planetary climate trajectory, requiring integrated, culturally sensitive, and interdisciplinary strategies to reduce human suffering and promote the well\-being of both: people and ecosystems\.

## [THE INTEGRATION OF DIGITAL PEDAGOGY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN HIGHER EDUCATION: STRATEGIES, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE OUTLOOK](../publications/54be9e2b512305364efc.md)

Duysenbayeva Malika

This scientific thesis examines the transformative impact of digital pedagogy and artificial intelligence \(AI\) integration within modern higher education systems\. As educational paradigms shift from traditional instructor\-centric models toward personalized, technology\-enhanced learning environments, understanding the pedagogical, methodological, and psychological implications becomes critical\. The study evaluates adaptive learning platforms, digital assessment tools, and AI\-driven instructional scaffolding across diverse academic contexts\. Employing a mixed\-methods approach comprising empirical classroom surveys, literature synthesis, and qualitative faculty interviews, the research highlights key drivers of student engagement, academic performance retention, and critical thinking development\. The findings demonstrate a 28% increase in conceptual retention when digital interactive tools are combined with active learning frameworks\. However, significant challenges persist, including digital inequality, algorithmic bias, and the potential degradation of human\-to\-human pedagogical rapport\. The paper concludes with actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional policymakers, and educators aiming to establish an ethically sound, technologically robust educational ecosystem\.

## [A machine learning\-optimized bivalent aptasensor based on exonuclease Ⅰ amplification for trace okadaic acid detection](../publications/54c7bfa801e811785bc8.md)

Xinxin Yan; Jing Wang; Tengxin Yuan; 罗亚蒙; Wenyuan Fang; Xiaofan Wang; Yachen Wang; Junhuan Wang; Shaojie Wu; Weixia Wang; Fuhou Li; Qiang Huang; Jinri Chen

Consumption of okadaic acid \(OA\)\-contaminated seafood endangers human health, highlighting the need for sensitive quantitative detection\. Herein, a convenient and highly sensitive bivalent aptasensor was developed for fluorescence detection of OA in aquatic products\. The aptasensor was constructed using a bivalent aptamer \(B\-Apt\) as the recognition element, DNA\-silver nanoclusters \(cDNA‑B‑Apt‑cDNA‑AgNCs\) as the fluorescent probe, and Exonuclease Ⅰ \(Exo Ⅰ\)\-assisted target recycling for signal amplification\. To improve accuracy and reduce matrix interference, a machine learning \(ML\) approach was integrated for fluorescence spectral analysis\. Principal component analysis \(PCA\) was applied for dimensionality reduction, followed by linear regression for concentration prediction, and the K\-nearest neighbors \(KNN\) algorithm for classification\. Under optimal conditions, the aptasensor achieved a limit of detection of 16\.18 pM and a linear range of 500 pM\-150 nM, with high specificity against other marine toxins and superior sensitivity over previously reported methods\. Spike recovery tests in seafood samples \(clam, prawn, squid, kelp, yellow catfish\) yielded recoveries of 93\.09–106\.59 % and relative standard deviations below 9\.06 %\. The PCA\-based model demonstrated excellent concentration prediction performance \(R 2 = 0\.9906\), and the KNN model achieved 100% classification accuracy for OA at different concentrations\. ## [The Effects of Oral Contraceptive Use on Objective and Subjective Episodic Memory](../publications/54c9e92ad6c007d4c924.md)

Adelaide Jensen

Introduced more than 60 years ago, oral contraceptives \(OC\) are one of the most common forms of contraceptives used by reproductive\-aged women today\. Despite their widespread use, very little is known about the ways in which the hormones contained in OCs \(i\.e\., synthetic versions of estradiol and progesterone\) affect cognition, with much of the literature having been criticized for its predominance of cross\-sectional designs, inconsistent consideration of OC\-related factors \(e\.g\., pill formulation, reproductive history/previous hormonal contraceptive use, group heterogeneity, etc\.\), and variable characterization and measurement of cognitive domains\. Some studies have suggested that OC use may slightly enhance verbal episodic memory \(i\.e\., our long\-term, explicit recollection of personal events\), although findings are mixed\. It also remains unclear whether OC use alters subjective perceptions of one’s memory\. Across three studies, this dissertation addresses the extent to which OC use might influence objective and subjective memory\. I begin by describing the development and validation of the neuropsychological methods used in the second half of this thesis\. Next, I cross\-sectionally examine differences in subjective and objective memory between OC users and non\-users\. Finally, this thesis culminates with a quasi\-experimental, repeated\-measures investigation of objective and subjective memory changes in newly initiated OC users\. We first tested the reliability of the Multifactorial Memory Questionnaire \(MMQ\)—a widely\-used measure of subjective memory—for use with healthy young adults\. Confirmatory factor analysis \(CFA\) with age invariance testing conducted with n = 408 young and n = 327 older adults suggested that although the MMQ is more reliable in older adults, it is also adequate for use in younger populations\. Next, we piloted the remotely\-administered, web\-based implementation of a well\-established episodic memory battery in n = 50 young adults and checked the feasibility of two parallel battery versions for repeated online testing\. Additionally, using \(young female participant only\) data from a previous study employing a similar web\-based battery, CFA was used to verify relationships between individual memory tasks in the battery and replicate its factor structure\. The final study employed the measures verified above to systematically investigate the role of OC use in objective and subjective memory while addressing common methodological limitations in the literature\. Cross\-sectional analyses revealed slightly higher objective memory and memory satisfaction among OC users \(n = 60\) compared to non\-users \(n = 75\); these results were also dependent on parallel task version and participants’ first language\. Repeated measures analyses assessing group\-by\-time interactions, however, indicated no significant changes in objective or subjective memory in newly initiated OC users \(n = 37\) following three months/cycles of use, compared to long\-time OC users \(n = 43\) and non\-users \(n = 45\)\. Findings from the present dissertation shed light on the existing mixed evidence on the involvement of OCs in cognitive functioning and suggest that influences on memory may emerge following more prolonged exposure to OC hormones\. Notably, this thesis also provides preliminary support for a possible role of contraceptives in subjective memory, particularly satisfaction with everyday memory functioning\. Potential implications of our findings for the growing field of contraceptives and cognition research, including methodological considerations, underlying mechanisms of OC influences on cognition, and future research directions are discussed\.

## [Projected climate extremes and health burden in Kenya to 2050: a scenario\-based analysis under SSP245 and SSP585 pathways](../publications/54cc258f7d7f627a999c.md)

Josphat Martin Muchangi; Lolem Lokolile Bosco; Moses Lengewa; Sarah Jebet Kosgei; Samuel  Kamau Kang’ethe; Nashon Kaloki Ng’elu; Festus Kipkorir

Background Rising global temperatures and precipitation variability are intensifying extreme weather events and threatening human health worldwide\. In Kenya, climate change is projected to significantly alter the distribution and severity of climate\-sensitive diseases, particularly affecting vulnerable populations\. This study projects climate extremes and associated health impacts in Kenya through 2050 under two emission scenarios: SSP245 \(moderate mitigation\) and SSP585 \(high emissions\)\. Methods The analysis employs a scenario\-based approach using IPCC AR6\-aligned climate projections \(baseline 1995–2014; projections 2030–2050\)\. Key climate indices include precipitation extremes \(R20mm, RX5day, SDII, PRCPTOT\) and temperature indicators \(mean temperature, Excess Heat Factor\)\. Climate projections are integrated with population exposure patterns and climate\-sensitive health outcome literature to assess future health risks across Kenya’s diverse regions\. Findings Both precipitation and temperature extremes are projected to intensify nationwide, with substantially greater impacts under SSP585\. Increased rainfall intensity and flooding might amplify water\-borne disease outbreaks and disrupt health services, particularly in western and coastal regions\. Rising temperatures and increased heatwave frequency could escalate heat\-related illnesses and non\-communicable diseases, while expanding the geographic range of vector\-borne diseases \(malaria, dengue\)\. Demographic growth and urbanization, especially in informal settlements, might substantially increase population exposure to these climate\-health risks\. Conclusion Kenya faces escalating climate\-health threats, with severity contingent on global emission trajectories\. Urgent, sustained climate mitigation and adaptation are essential to minimize future health burdens\. The study recommends prioritizing climate\-resilient health system strengthening, establishing integrated early warning systems, and implementing cross\-sectoral adaptation strategies to protect vulnerable populations and enhance national climate\-health preparedness\.

## [A parametric Morison\-inspired model for wave\-induced torque fluctuations on a vertical axis tidal turbine](../publications/54d831a8a16fd506780f.md)

Yanis Saouli; Benoît Gaurier; Grégory Germain; G\. Maurice

This paper investigates the effect of surface waves on the hydrodynamic torque fluctuations of vertical axis tidal turbines\. Wave\-induced orbital velocities and accelerations are shown to generate periodic variations of the incoming flow, leading to significant unsteady torque loads\. A reduced\-order torque model inspired by Morison\-type formulations is here developed to study wave\-induced effects on vertical axis tidal turbines\. The model is derived and expressed in terms of the instantaneous wave\-modified tip\-speed ratio and decomposes the torque response into three main parameters: a mean shift term, a linear sensitivity coefficient linking torque fluctuations to tip\-speed ratio variations and an inertial coefficient proportional to the orbital acceleration\. Phase\-averaged analysis reveals the relative importance of velocity\-driven and acceleration\-driven mechanisms and the wave\-induced torque variability is interpreted as a structured perturbation of the stationary performance curve\. The results obtained under irregular waves demonstrate that the proposed Morison\-type model is able to reproduce the wave\-induced contribution to torque fluctuations with a limited number of parameters identified in monochromatic waves\. The use of conservative coefficients derived from monochromatic wave tests appears as a promising strategy to bound torque fluctuations under a given sea state\. Such an approach would provide a compact and operational modelling framework, positioned between purely linear spectral transfer\-function methods and computationally intensive fully unsteady numerical models\. This model offers practical perspectives for structural load assessment, performance optimisation and the development of control strategies for VATT operating in wave\-exposed sites\.

## [Prenatal Diagnosis of Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformation With 3D / 4D STIC Fetal Echocardiography](../publications/54f85f80bed192cece8a.md)

Amit Kumar Pandey; Balu Vaidyanathan

Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation \(PAVM\) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly characterized by direct communication between the pulmonary artery and vein, resulting in a right\-to\-left shunt\. Prenatal diagnosis remains uncommon\. We report a fetal PAVM diagnosed at 21 weeks&\#x27; gestation on fetal echocardiography\. Color Doppler with graphic flow imaging demonstrated turbulent swirling flow within the right pulmonary vein, while spectral Doppler showed an arterialized pulmonary venous waveform\. High\-definition color Doppler and 3D/4D spatiotemporal image correlation \(STIC\) rendering confirmed a fistulous communication between the right pulmonary artery and vein\. Prenatal recognition of PAVM is essential for serial surveillance, parental counseling, multidisciplinary perinatal planning, and early neonatal intervention\.

## [The dual structure of ‘total pain’: multidimensionality and holism in the foundational concept of palliative care](../publications/54fc64af4f017b12e566.md)

David Fajardo\-Chica

The concept of ‘total pain’, introduced by Cicely Saunders, is often treated as a historical milestone of the hospice movement rather than as a live theoretical resource\. I argue instead that it is a concept with a definite architecture that remains operative as an implicit theory of suffering in contemporary palliative care\. This architecture takes the form of two theses: an etiological thesis of multidimensionality, on which suffering arises from impairments across multiple dimensions of the person \(physical, psychological, social, spiritual, among others\), and an experiential thesis of holism, on which suffering is lived as affecting the person as a whole rather than a sum of discrete problems\. I show that this dual structure is legible across the WHO definition of palliative care, the field’s consensus definition, its validated measurement instruments, and the Lancet Commission’s concept of serious health\-related suffering\. Each thesis plays a distinct role: multidimensionality supports a multidisciplinary approach to suffering, while holism supports respect for patient autonomy by giving due weight to the patient’s perspective\. I then ask whether two alternative conceptions—the objective, flourishing\-based view and the thin phenomenological view—could perform the same work, and argue that the former secures clinical tractability at the cost of autonomy, while the latter centers the patient’s experience without securing its link to symptoms\. Finally, I address the objection that the dual structure cannot explain how distributed impairments become a unified experience, drawing on recent models in the philosophy of mind to show that it can\. ‘Total pain’, then, is a conceptual compromise enabling care that is at once clinically effective and ethically person\-centered\.

## [AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine\-Tuning](../publications/5505059fa929550d134f.md)

Bingxiang He; Pengqi Sun; Shihao Peng; Shaoxuan Li; Huiyu Xiao; Hongjian Shi; Zixuan Fu; Ziqing Qiao; Yuxin Zuo; Cheng Qian; Xinqiang Yu; Jiayi Li; Xiusi Chen; Yizhen Song; Xiangyang Wang; Iofai Lei; Yudong Wang; Ning Ding; Zhiyuan Liu; Xiaozhi Wang; Chaojun Xiao

Language model agents increasingly automate post\-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine\-tuning and spend most effort revising training data\. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data\. We design a data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires\. We first run this loop with a single agent, and it reaches only one action, adjusting category proportions, while its context fills with execution output and is discarded mid\-search\. We therefore introduce \\textbf\{AutoSFT\}, a multi\-agent system where a meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls a synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison\. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by $\+6\.5$, and synthesis adds $\+3\.4$ IFEval and $\+2\.9$ IFBench\. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds $\+3\.7$ MBPP\+ over a single agent that does not improve\. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each component&\#x27;s effect is individually attributable\. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on a stronger single action\.

## [Zero\-Shot Extraction of Structured Clinical Data from Free\-Text CT Reports Using Foundational Large Language Models](../publications/5506454fd7fd71f6f274.md)

Introduction\. Large language models \(LLMs\) are being explored for multiple applications in medical research, including medical text classification\. Authors of the study evaluated the performance of three off\-the\-shelf LLMs in classifying unstructured free\-text CT pulmonary angiography reports for pulmonary embolism \(PE\)\-related diagnostic labels\.Methods\. Authors assessed human\-labeled CT reports using three LLMs \(ChatGPT\-4o, Llama 3\.3 70B, and Llama 3\.1 8B\) with zero\-shot simple and chain\-of\-thought \(CoT\) prompts\. Classification tasks included acute PE \(N = 1,025\) and, among reports with PE \(n = 660\), bilateral PE and large PE\.Results\. LLMs demonstrated high classification performance for acute PE and bilateral PE but lower performance for large PE\. With simple prompts, the highest F1 scores were 97\.0% for acute PE \(Llama 3\.1 8B; sensitivity, 95\.6%; specificity, 97\.3%\), 92\.9% for bilateral PE \(ChatGPT\-4o; sensitivity, 98\.0%; specificity, 88\.6%\), and 72\.8% for large PE \(ChatGPT\-4o; sensitivity, 82\.9%; specificity, 82\.2%\)\. CoT prompting did not meaningfully improve acute PE classification but provided slight improvements in subclassification performance for bilateral and large PE\.Conclusions\. Off\-the\-shelf LLMs can classify free\-text CT reports using simple prompt engineering and may facilitate automated data extraction for medical research following appropriate evaluation of classification performance\.

## [Beyond Emotional Self\-Regulation: Affective Maturity in Light of Magda Arnold’s Work](../publications/5506b8b703e543360302.md)

Pilar Aviñó de Pablo; Juan Pablo Rojas\-Saffie; Nicolás García\-Matte

In recent decades, emotional self\-regulation \(ESR\) has emerged as a significant interdisciplinary field of research in psychology, affective neuroscience, and philosophy\. However, its link with affective maturity \(AM\) remains unexplored, even though they share an important underlying question: how to control our emotions rather than be controlled by them? Although AM lacks a scientific definition, it is employed in clinical, religious, and character\-formation contexts and is particularly pertinent in marriage annulment causes\. Drawing on Magda Arnold’s personality theory as a starting point, this paper proposes a framework for integrating ESR and AM coherently from an interdisciplinary perspective\. In particular, it delves into the anthropological foundations that can support such integration, as outlined in Arnold’s pioneering work\. By doing so, this theoretical review aims to minimise overlaps and ambiguities between the concepts, thus enabling the future development of criteria applicable to the assessment and treatment of clinical cases\.

## [Angiography\-derived fractional flow and clinical outcomes in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis](../publications/55092aea5f5254dcbd07.md)

Wanning Zheng; Rong Zou; Ming Wang; Jiahao Tang; Ruilin Chen; Chaobo Zheng; Jie Gong; Yuhai Gao; Ning Wang; Yuning Lu; Jiong Wu; Jens Fiehler; Adnan Hussain Siddiqui; Jianping Xiang; Shu Wan

Background To explore the association between fractional flow \(FF\) and clinical outcomes in patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis \(ICAS\), and to evaluate its potential role in patient stratification\. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included symptomatic ICAS patients hospitalized between March 2019 and May 2024\. FF values were derived from digital subtraction angiography using an angiography\-based computational method\. Patients were stratified according to a pre\-specified FF threshold of 0\.76 and treatment modality \(interventional vs\. conservative\)\. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale \(mRS\) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale \(NIHSS\) at discharge and 12 months\. Results Among patients with FF ≤ 0\.76, no worsening in mRS between discharge and 12 months was observed in 96\.3% of the interventional group and 78\.6% of the conservative group \( p = 0\.017\)\. In a post hoc analysis, improvement of at least one mRS point occurred in 46\.3 and 17\.9%, respectively; however, discharge mRS scores differed between groups, and the difference in improvement was not statistically significant when the analysis was restricted to patients with discharge mRS ≥ 1\. No significant differences in mRS or NIHSS improvement were observed between treatment strategies in patients with FF &gt; 0\.76 \( p &gt; 0\.05\)\. In contrast, stratification based on degree of stenosis \(DS% ≥ 70%\) did not differentiate clinical outcomes between treatment groups\. These findings suggest that FF\-based stratification may be associated with differences in functional outcomes across treatment strategies\. Conclusion FF may provide additional information for risk stratification in symptomatic ICAS patients and may help identify clinically relevant subgroups for further evaluation\. However, these findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies\.

## [Model\-based identification of medication\-associated fall\-risk signals using EMG time\-series analysis: an exploratory mechanistic approach in polypharmacy](../publications/5509a8ab6214d7462f17.md)

정우진; 신민주; Jiyeon Jeon; Soyoung Lee; Youngjin Moon; Jung\-woo Chae; Hwi\-yeol Yun

Falls are the leading cause of functional decline in older adults\. Existing fall\-risk assessments often overlook the contribution of medications, and emerging sensor\-based methods predict who is likely to fall but rarely explain why\. We present a model\-based approach for identifying medication\-related fall\-risk signals using high\-frequency time\-series electromyography \(EMG\)\. Fifteen young and 15 older adults performed perturbation\-based balance tasks, and nonlinear mixed\-effects modelling with bootstrap\-assisted covariate selection linked the EMG responses of seven lower\-limb and trunk muscles to common medication classes\. The simulation\-derived co\-contraction index \(CCI\) served as the outcome, compared against a benchmark derived from Falk et al\. Through stepwise covariate modelling followed by bootstrap\-based confirmation, two drug classes were retained as robust covariates: anticoagulants, associated with a higher co\-contraction index, and statins, associated with a lower co\-contraction index\. In model\-based simulations, anticoagulant exposure corresponded to significantly elevated odds of exceeding the CCI benchmark, whereas statins did not increase the simulated odds despite their consistent covariate signal\. This exploratory, signal\-generating framework foregrounds the identification of medication\-associated neuromuscular changes from EMG and may provide a mechanistic context that complements conventional epidemiology\. A companion web application illustrates this approach as a supplementary tool to support medication reviews during fall\-risk evaluations\.

## [Spatiotemporal Machine Learning for Smart Cities: A Comprehensive Review of Models and Applications](../publications/5509f92b4682c627cdd7.md)

Didar Yedilkhan; Gulden Ormanova; Zhibek N\. Sarsenova; Altynbek Yermekov; Batyrzhan Akhmetzhanov; Sabina Saleshova; Beibut Amirgaliyev

The rapid growth of sensor networks, satellite platforms, Internet\-of\-Things \(IoT\) devices, and urban monitoring systems has produced vast volumes of spatiotemporal data\. Modeling such data is central to applications ranging from air\-quality forecasting and climate monitoring to traffic prediction and urban planning, yet it poses challenges, including high dimensionality, spatial autocorrelation, and complex temporal dependencies that classical statistical models struggle to capture jointly\. This review provides a comprehensive survey of spatiotemporal machine learning \(STML\), synthesizing the literature published between 2020 and 2025\. We present a taxonomy of STML methods spanning traditional machine learning, recurrent neural networks \(LSTM and GRU\), convolutional architectures \(3D CNN and ConvLSTM\), graph neural networks, transformer\-based models, and hybrid or ensemble designs\. We organize representative studies by application domain, climate and environmental monitoring, transportation and traffic forecasting, and urban planning within smart cities, and provide a comparative analysis of models, datasets, evaluation metrics, and open\-source tools\. Finally, we identify emerging research trends and open challenges, including real\-time processing, interpretability and explainability, scalability and edge deployment, multimodal fusion, federated learning for privacy, self\-supervised learning, and ethical concerns such as fairness\. The review is intended to serve as a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing STML systems\.

## [Personalized stress detection from wearable physiological signals via Digital Twin\-inspired subject embeddings and recurrent neural networks](../publications/550b165014b244b288f4.md)

Hadeel Fahad Alharbi

Introduction The rising prevalence of psychological stress and its associated adverse health effects have created an urgent need for reliable and automated detection methods that move beyond traditional self\-report tools\. While wearable sensing systems offer a promising avenue for continuous monitoring, current systems often fail to account for individual physiological variability in stress responses\. This leads to suboptimal performance when applied across diverse populations\. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel framework aimed at personalized stress detection in wearable sensing systems\. Methods We introduce a DT\-GRU framework centered on a trainable subject\-embedding module that captures each individual’s unique physiological traits, thereby forming a latent Digital Twin \(DT\)\. This personalized embedding is integrated with Gated Recurrent Unit \(GRU\) features in the model&\#x27;s inference pathway, enabling the framework to utilize both temporal dynamics and subject identity for improved detection\. The DT\-GRU framework was rigorously evaluated on the WESAD dataset, incorporating various validation techniques, including subject\-independent train\-test splits and Leave\-One\-Subject\-Out \(LOSO\) cross\-validation\. Results The results from the evaluation demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy and generalizability\. The integration of the personalized subject\-embedding was shown to enhance the model’s performance across the diverse population represented in the dataset\. Discussion These findings highlight the potential of the DT\-GRU approach for deployment in real\-world stress monitoring applications\. By effectively accounting for individual physiological variability, the framework provides a more reliable and personalized method for automated stress detection, paving the way for more effective and scalable mental health monitoring solutions\.

## [The Seasons of a Career in Physical Chemistry: Himansu S\. Biswal](../publications/5511b1efdd3f9ab32628.md)

Himansu S\. Biswal; Gemma C\. Solomon; Joan‐Emma Shea; Gregory D\. Scholes

Recommendations &quot;The Seasons of a Career in Physical Chemistry&quot; is an interview series published across ACS Physical Chemistry Au, The Journal of Physical Chemistry A/B/C, and The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters\.The series celebrates the people behind physical chemistry, giving researchers at all career stages the opportunity to tell their own stories: how they came to be where they are today, the joys and challenges they have encountered along the way, and what they imagine as they look to the future\.Whether reflecting on a lifetime of work or navigating the uncertainties of an earlier career stage, each interviewee offers a window into research environments and trajectories as varied as the science itself, with the hope of providing inspiration for the broader physical chemistry community\.

## [The Scaleup Costs, Size, and Statistics Challenge to Democratic Deliberation on Health Policy](../publications/551bf28a963e216d6614.md)

Nir Eyal

Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini\-publics\. These forums&\#x27; participants are selected randomly from the general public \(sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors\)\. After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations\. According to supporters, a deliberative democratic process that holds such forums and translates their recommendations to policy legitimizes resulting policy\. That&\#x27;s thanks to this process&\#x27;s tendencies to strengthen democratic consent, to uncover which policy option is objectively best, to align policy with lay normative outlooks, and to educate the public\. I argue that one tri\-partite feature of nearly all instances of democratic deliberation on regional, national, and global health policy under current best practice, which I call the &quot;Scaleup costs, Size, and Statistics&quot; \(&quot;3S&quot;\) challenge, largely blocks these alleged welcome tendencies\. In particular, barring radical changes, true democratic deliberation is expensive to scale, keeping feasible mini\-publics small and irregular\. That makes concluding from mini\-public recommendations about the population&\#x27;s hypothetical consent, values, and will statistically unreliable\. It also caps low mini\-publics&\#x27; contribution to public education\. In these ways and in others, the long list of alleged welcome tendencies of proper democratic deliberation on health policy, and the related contribution to political legitimacy, is largely a fiction\. Public deliberation does have modest true merit, for example, providing relevant qualitative input about the lay public&\#x27;s occasional factual insights and many endemic errors; and making the public feel &quot;listened to,&quot; whether or not it is\. But those merits are modest, contingent, and most accentuated under different institutions than envisaged in deliberative democratic literature\. Certainly there is room for democratic deliberation, potentially of new breeds, but only as part of the mosaic of health policy design, alongside familiar methods like general elections, public surveys, representative government, and expert decisionmaking\. The main question is which method to use when\.

## [MIRAGE: manipulation\-immune RAG with adaptive guard against textual evidence attacks](../publications/551f5f4bb85f515d48bb.md)

Qiao Yuan; Feiyang Li; Yi Jiang; Yanming Mu; Hongwei Zhou; Yuling Liu; Yuchen Zhang

Abstract Retrieval\-augmented generation \(RAG\) substantially improves large language models \(LLMs\) on knowledge\-intensive tasks by incorporating external knowledge, yet open knowledge sources introduce prominent security risks\. The SafeRAG benchmark identifies four novel textual evidence manipulation attacks, namely silver noise, inter\-context conflict, soft advertisement, and White Denial\-of\-Service \(White DoS\), which bypass conventional defense components and threaten both the security and availability of RAG systems\. Existing single\-stage defenses fail to capture the implicit malicious characteristics of these attacks, while multi\-stage frameworks are limited by fixed parameters, weak conflict resolution, and insufficient detection of implicit toxicity and availability threats\. To address these limitations, we propose MIRAGE, a two\-stage adaptive defense framework combining retrieval\-side purification and generation\-side resolution\. The first stage applies attack\-characteristic\-aware dynamic K\-means clustering and dynamic ROUGE\-L threshold filtering to eliminate malicious documents\. The second stage employs attack\-adaptive knowledge integration rules alongside an enhanced self\-evaluation mechanism that jointly verifies factual accuracy, implicit toxicity, and availability\. Under the static, non\-adaptive attack setting defined by SafeRAG, experiments on DeepSeek\-v3\.2 show that MIRAGE achieves average improvements of 20\.9% in Attack Failure Rate \(AFR\), 11\.5% in Retrieval Accuracy \(RA\), and 14\.1% in F1\(avg\) over baselines across all four attack scenarios, providing effective technical support for the stable deployment of RAG systems in complex adversarial environments\.

## [Legal Responsibility for Copyright Infringements of Works Produced Through Artificial Intelligence Based on Law Number 28 of 2014 Concerning Copyright](../publications/5521e84e669ff0c3ad37.md)

Zahwa Ayni Sabilah; Nuraini Fitri Ramadhani

The development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has transformed the process of creating works, including works that may fall within the scope of copyright protection in the fields of science, art, and literature\. The use of AI raises legal concerns when AI\-generated works resemble works owned by other parties or incorporate protected materials without authorization\. This issue has become increasingly complex because Law Number 28 of 2014 on Copyright does not specifically establish a legal framework for liability arising from copyright infringement through the use of AI\. This study aims to examine copyright protection for works generated through AI and analyze the construction of legal liability when the use of AI results in infringement of the exclusive rights of copyright holders\. This study employs a normative juridical method using statutory, conceptual, and case approaches\. Legal materials are analyzed qualitatively to examine the relationship between the exclusive rights of copyright holders, the use of AI technology, forms of infringement, and the liability of the parties involved\. The findings indicate that copyright protection remains oriented toward protecting the moral and economic rights of copyright holders, even when the creation process involves AI technology\. When infringement occurs, legal liability cannot be determined solely on the basis of AI involvement but must consider the form of contribution, degree of control, knowledge, fault, and economic benefit obtained by each party\. AI users may bear legal liability when they know to use or commercially exploit outputs that infringe copyright, while the liability of AI developers or platform providers should be determined based on their degree of involvement and applicable legal obligations\. The novelty of this study lies in developing a differentiated framework of liability for AI users, developers, and platform providers in copyright infringement, thus ensuring that copyright protection can remain effective while accommodating technological development\.

## [Uso pedagógico de la inteligencia artificial generativa y desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes universitarios](../publications/5522fdf9b06f1d2193ae.md)

Juan Carlos Arturo González Castro

La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior plantea nuevas oportunidades y desafíos para el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes universitarios\. El objetivo de esta investigación fue analizar la relación entre el uso pedagógico de estas tecnologías y el fortalecimiento de habilidades cognitivas vinculadas con el análisis, la argumentación, la reflexión y la autonomía intelectual\. Se desarrolló una revisión sistematizada de la literatura científica, con enfoque cualitativo y alcance descriptivo\-analítico, siguiendo las orientaciones de PRISMA 2020\. La síntesis temática de las investigaciones examinadas permitió identificar cuatro dimensiones fundamentales: desarrollo de habilidades cognitivas, mediación pedagógica, dependencia tecnológica y autorregulación del aprendizaje\. Los hallazgos sugieren que la inteligencia artificial generativa puede favorecer el pensamiento crítico cuando se utiliza para contrastar información, evaluar argumentos y construir conocimientos propios\. Sin embargo, su uso pasivo puede incrementar la dependencia tecnológica y reducir el esfuerzo cognitivo\. Se concluye que su potencial educativo depende de una integración pedagógica intencional que preserve el protagonismo intelectual del estudiante y promueva aprendizajes reflexivos, autónomos y responsables en contextos universitarios contemporáneos\.
