## [More Than Memes: Recognition, Justification, and the Work of Understanding](../publications/552b925e30f332d575e1.md)

Joanne Irving\-Walton; Helen Tidy; Giulia Bini; Maria \(Masha\) Wald; Marina Gazzini; Stefano Bertacchi

This short paper emerged from a multidisciplinary collaboration investigating the use of memes in higher education across Biology, Education, Forensic Science, Mathematics, Medieval History, and Russian Studies\. As colleagues compared examples from different disciplines, it became clear that the most interesting questions were not about memes themselves\. Instead, the project highlighted a broader issue concerning how learners encounter meaning through digital artefacts and how moments of recognition relate to deeper disciplinary understanding\. What began as a study of memes ultimately led to a wider exploration of interpretation, justification, and the work of understanding in digitally mediated learning environments\. This short paper explores how digital artefacts \- including memes, diagrams, AI\-generated summaries, visual explanations, and discussion formats \- shape interpretation within higher education\. It argues that such artefacts often make ideas recognisable before they are fully justifiable within disciplinary frameworks\. Students may identify patterns, coherence, or intended meaning before they are able to explain, critique, or defend those interpretations through disciplinary reasoning\. This distinction has become increasingly significant in the context of generative AI, where fluency and coherence can easily be mistaken for understanding\. Drawing on examples from practice and insights from edusemiotics, digital pedagogy, and disciplinary learning, the discussion reframes digital artefacts not as simple engagement tools but as sites of interpretive and intellectual work\. The paper concludes with practical reflective questions and open\-access resources designed to support colleagues in working more intentionally with digital artefacts in their own teaching\.

## [HAPACT: A Benchmark For Human\-Centric Physical Impact Localization in Movies](../publications/5549053d2b7046086951.md)

Youngrae Kim; Yejin Jang; Eunho Kim; Youjin Sung; Kun\-Woo Song; Sangpil Kim; Sang Ho Yoon

Physical reasoning about humans in videos has largely focused on everyday interactions, where contact, pressure, pose, and motion support embodied perception and contact\-aware applications\. Still, short and forceful properties like impact events remain relatively underexplored, despite their relevance to broader understanding of how abrupt physical events affect the human body\. To fill this gap, we introduce human\-centric impact localization, a new task that localizes target physical impacts temporally within a video and spatially on the human body\. We further present HAPACT, a HumAn\-centric imPACT dataset and benchmark built from movie clips, containing over 2\.8K video\-query pairs with more than 20K fine\-grained human\-annotated frames\. We built HAPACT around viewer\-grounded annotation, text\-conditioned localization, and supervision at frame\-level temporal and SMPL\-X\-based spatial granularity\. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our benchmark, we conduct extensive evaluations of existing methods, employing video moment retrieval models for temporal localization and human\-scene contact models for spatial localization\. For the spatial task, we propose a text\-conditioned baseline by reformulating localization as query\-guided body\-region selection\. Benchmark results show that physical impact localization remains challenging for existing methods, motivating HAPACT as a dedicated benchmark to support physical impact reasoning in videos\.

## [Co\-developing Georgia’s National Digital Health Strategy through a multistakeholder convergence workshop: An implementation case study from the WHO European Region](../publications/556673281ba33d6ffea3.md)

Nato Gzirishili; Mehar Grover; Resham Sethi; Mariam Beridze; Tomáš Roubal; Lela Sulaberidze; Karapet Davtyan; Silviu Domente; Karthik Adapa

National digital health strategies \(DHS\) are widely recognized as essential for advancing universal health coverage\. However, published evidence on operational, multi\-stakeholder approaches to co\-development\-particularly beyond the Asian and African settings where convergence methodology has previously been applied\-remains limited\. This study details the application of a convergence\-based methodology to validate and refine the draft National DHS of Georgia, an upper\-middle\-income country, aligning it with European Union frameworks\. An implementation case study was conducted in Georgia from June to September 2025\. Central to this was the Multistakeholder Convergence Workshop, adapted from the Asian Development Bank Digital Health Convergence Meeting Toolkit and a four\-phase blueprint methodology\. Forty\-seven participants from diverse sectors \(public, private, academia, and development partners\) collaborated in five thematic working groups\. They reviewed the draft DHS, generating recommendations that were synthesized against the seven WHO\-ITU eHealth strategy building blocks using hybrid deductive\-inductive thematic analysis by two independent coders with third\-party arbitration\. The revised strategy comprises six strategic goals and 38 priority activities\. Key technical recommendations included adopting a federated data governance model, utilizing the existing national identification number instead of a separate Health ID, and establishing a national Health Information Exchange\. The strategy endorses FHIR for data exchange, LOINC for laboratory data, and the WHO\-FIC \(including ICD\-11\) complemented by SNOMED CT\. Governance recommendations emphasized enacting a stand\-alone Digital Health Act, forming a dedicated Digital Health Unit within the MoIDPLHSA, integrating digital health into professional education, and extending the strategy horizon to 2030 with a mid\-2026 review checkpoint\. Structured convergence methodologies, initially developed for Asian settings, can be effectively adapted for upper\-middle\-income WHO European Region countries pursuing European Health Data Space alignment\. This approach produced technically specific outputs, reinforced national ownership, and supported Georgia&\#x27;s transition toward implementation, offering a highly transferable framework for similar contexts\.

## [Trigeminal ganglion neurons lack detectable GLP\-1 receptor expression: a cross\-species single\-cell transcriptomic study](../publications/55700c2e073fdbdf90cd.md)

Lanfranco Pellesi; Lars Edvinsson

Background: Glucagon\-like peptide\-1 receptor agonists \(GLP\-1 RAs\) are accumulating signals of potential benefit in headache disorders, but the cellular locus of any anti\-cephalalgic action is unknown\. A direct effect on the trigeminovascular system would require GLP1R to be expressed by cells of the trigeminal ganglion \(TG\), and we therefore investigated whether GLP1R is expressed by TG neurons or non\-neuronal cells\. Methods: We reanalysed public single\-cell/single\-nucleus transcriptomic data from mouse and human TG, quantifying GLP1R detection per cell type with exact binomial 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\)\. GLP1R and the second incretin receptor GIPR were benchmarked against validated G protein\-coupled receptor \(GPCR\) drug targets and nociceptor markers, and GLP1R detection was verified in pancreatic islets, where it is expressed\. Results: GLP1R was detected in 0\.09% of mouse and 0\.05% of human trigeminal neurons, whereas validated GPCR drug targets were robustly detected in the same cells\. GLP1R was undetected in the peptidergic subtype and ≤0\.17% across the other mouse neuronal subtypes, was at the limit of detection in human neurons, and was at or below the limit of detection in all human non\-neuronal compartments, while GPCRs and compartment markers labelled their expected populations\. The same pipeline detected GLP1R in pancreatic beta cells, confirming assay sensitivity\. Conclusions: Across both mouse and human TG, GLP1R transcripts were not detectably expressed by neurons or non\-neuronal cells\. The anti\-headache signals of GLP\-1 RAs are therefore unlikely to be initiated by GLP1R within TG cell bodies and more plausibly reflect extraganglionic mechanisms\.

## [A Cryptographic Abstraction Layer for Integrating NIST Lightweight Cryptography into TLS 1\.3](../publications/5573f22ae2e9c1dc911e.md)

HUSSEIN Ali Al\-shmailawi; Emad H\. Al\-Hemiary; Axel Sikora

In the Industrial Internet of Things \(IIoT\) domain, security solutions must remain energy\-efficient and reliable under strict latency and real\-time requirements, especially for resource\-constrained devices\.Lightweight Cryptography \(LWC\) has emerged as a feasible solution to these challenges, offering new cryptographic algorithms developed for IIoT environments\.The practical integration of LWC into standardized security protocols remains largely unexplored\.In this work, we propose a new Transport Layer Security \(TLS\) cipher\-suites integration that incorporates lightweight cryptographic algorithms, recommended by National Institute of Standards and Technology \(NIST\), through a Cryptographic Abstraction Layer \(CAL\)\.Measurements on IIoT devices show that the abstraction comes at modest effort: the dispatch cost of CAL peaks at 13\.73% for the smallest records and falls to between zero and 9\.52% once payloads pass 128 bytes, with most suites under 4%\.In return, the layer separates TLS record processing from the cryptographic implementation, conceals cipher internals from the layers above, provides runtime cipher agility, and a fixed memory footprint across the registered suites\.The layer drives different ciphers spanning block, sponge, duplex, and stream constructions through one calling convention, confirming that no single internal structure is assumed\.

## [Density Functional Theory and Data\-Driven Insights into Hydrogen Incorporation and Transport in Ternary ABO3 Perovskites](../publications/557c9d14162201598749.md)

Zhen Wei Jiang; Christopher Wolverton

Abstract Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors\. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties\. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations and machine learning \(ML\) screening\. We performed DFT simulations for a diverse range of perovskites featuring a variety of A\-site cations \(Ca, Sr, Ba\) and B\-site cations \(Co, Fe, Mn, Ce, Ti, Zr\) across various phases \(cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and hexagonal\)\. By computing all data at the same theoretical level, we establish a consistent framework to compare how crystal phase, lattice\-site chemistry, and host electronic structure govern hydrogen incorporation and diffusion\. Therefore, we identify hexagonal SrMnO3, cubic SrFeO3, and hexagonal BaFeO3 as particularly promising candidates, combining favorable hydrogenation thermodynamics \(ΔG &lt; 1 eV\) with low rotation and hopping barriers \(&lt;0\.2 eV\), while orthorhombic phases, although thermodynamically preferred, suffer from proton trapping, highlighting the importance of phase engineering toward cubic/hexagonal frameworks\. Ab initio molecular dynamics further support this phase\-dependent kinetic picture by showing relatively facile H diffusion in cubic SrFeO3 but much slower proton motion in orthorhombic BaCeO3 under the same conditions\. By incorporating spatial and electronic descriptors with the DFT data into our ML models, we further develop a mechanistically motivated ML model based on structural and electronic descriptors to screen hydrogenation thermodynamics across 111 ternary ABO3 compositions\. This model led to the identification of two additional promising candidates, hexagonal BaPdO3 and cubic BaSnO3, which were subsequently validated by DFT calculations\. These findings provide a foundation for the rational design of ABO3 perovskites and demonstrate the potential of ML\-driven frameworks with chemical insights to accelerate materials discovery in energetic and catalytic applications\.

## [DOSE DO EXERCÍCIO RESISTIDO E FUNÇÃO FÍSICA EM IDOSOS COM SARCOPENIA: MAPA ESTRUTURADO DAS EVIDÊNCIAS E METANÁLISE EXPLORATÓRIA](../publications/557cb88a7ff504f1dc75.md)

Lídia Acyole de Souza

A dose do exercício resistido mais provável de melhorar a função física em idosos com sarcopenia permanece incerta, especialmente quando frequência, intensidade, progressão e cointervenções são consideradas separadamente\. Este estudo teve como objetivo mapear as evidências disponíveis sobre a prescrição do exercício resistido e a função física na sarcopenia e realizar uma síntese quantitativa exploratória quando as definições de desfecho e os dados eram suficientemente compatíveis\. Foi elaborado um mapa estruturado das evidências com base nos princípios PRISMA 2020 e PRISMA\-S\. Foram combinadas buscas públicas em PubMed/Europe PMC, CENTRAL, PROSPERO e PEDro, além de rastreamento de citações, realizadas em 28 de setembro de 2026\. Estratégias foram preparadas para Embase, Scopus, Web of Science e SPORTDiscus, mas não foi possível executar buscas autenticadas nem obter exportações completas dessas bases nesta etapa\. Foram priorizados ensaios randomizados com adultos de 60 anos ou mais e sarcopenia definida por EWGSOP, EWGSOP2, AWGS ou critério equivalente\. O risco de viés foi avaliado provisoriamente com RoB 2 e a certeza foi julgada operacionalmente com GRADE\. O mapa identificou 22 registros de estudos primários candidatos e 16 revisões ou protocolos\. Dois ensaios forneceram dados compatíveis de velocidade da marcha: 73 participantes foram randomizados e 68 contribuíram para os cálculos de efeito\. A estimativa exploratória de efeitos aleatórios favoreceu o exercício resistido \(diferença média, 0,196 m/s; intervalo de confiança de 95%, 0,126–0,266; I²=0%\)\. Os protocolos efetivos foram progressivos, supervisionados ou monitorados e, em geral, realizados duas a três vezes por semana durante 8–16 semanas, com esforço moderado a moderadamente alto\. A certeza foi muito baixa em razão da pequena base de evidências, perdas de seguimento, indireção diagnóstica e de intervenção e combinação de diferentes estimandos\. Conclui\-se que o exercício resistido é um componente plausível da reabilitação funcional, mas as evidências não estabelecem uma curva causal de dose–resposta nem demonstram que três sessões semanais sejam superiores a duas\. O manuscrito deve ser interpretado como mapa exploratório das evidências, e não como revisão sistemática definitiva e plenamente atualizada\.

## [Synthesis and biochemical evaluation of covalent caspase\-1 inhibitors based on the 3\-benzamidobenzoic acid derivative](../publications/559390853824ba234653.md)

Martina Artnak

Nevrodegenerativne bolezni, kot sta Alzheimerjeva in Parkinsonova bolezen, predstavljajo vse večji zdravstveni in družbeni izziv starajoče se populacije\. Patologija njihovega nastanka in napredovanja je kompleksna ter še vedno ni popolnoma pojasnjena, pri čemer se vse večjo vlogo pripisuje nevrovnetju\. Pri tem imajo osrednjo vlogo mikroglija, astrociti in multiproteinski kompleksi, imenovani inflamasomi\. Med njimi je najbolj raziskan inflamasom NLRP3, ki po aktivaciji sproži nastanek aktivne kaspaze\-1\. Kaspaza\-1 cepi provnetna citokina pro\-interlevkin\-1β in pro\-interlevkin\-18 v njuni aktivni obliki ter prek cepitve gasdermina D sproža piroptozo\. Zaradi pomembne vloge pri številnih boleznih predstavlja kaspaza\-1 obetavno terapevtsko tarčo za razvoj zdravilnih učinkovin\. Na podlagi strukture zaviralca kaspaze\-1 CZL80 smo v okviru magistrske naloge načrtovali in sintetizirali serijo derivatov 3\-benzamidobenzojske kisline z različnimi elektrofilnimi bojnimi glavami ter bioizosternimi zamenjavami karboksilata\. Ker se karboksilat spojine CZL80 umešča v žep S1 aktivnega mesta kaspaze\-1, hkrati pa spojina ne tvori kovalentne vezi s katalitičnim ostankom Cys285, smo proučevali vpliv modifikacij tega strukturnega elementa na zaviralno aktivnost ter možnost razvoja kovalentnih zaviralcev\. Pripravili smo spojine s karbamoil fluoridnimi, vinilsulfonamidnimi, akrilamidnimi in nitrilnimi bojnimi glavami ter več analogov za preučevanje vpliva položaja substitucije na zaviralno aktivnost\. Z in silico modeliranjem derivatov v kompleksu s kaspazo\-1 smo proučili predvidene načine vezave v aktivnem mestu kaspaze\-1 ter ocenili vpliv strukturnih sprememb na vezavno pozo in interakcije z aktivnim mestom\. Spojinam smo nato z in vitro biokemijskim testiranjem na rekombinantni človeški kaspazi\-1 ob uporabi fluorogenega substrata Ac\-YVAD\-AMC določili zaviralno aktivnost\. Rezultati so pokazali, da je zaviralna aktivnost močno odvisna od vrste in položaja elektrofilne bojne glave\. Najmočneje so kaspazo\-1 zavirali vinilsulfonamida 22 in 29 ter karbamoil fluorid 28\. Dobljeni rezultati potrjujejo, da predstavljajo derivati 3\-benzamidobenzojske kisline obetavno izhodišče za nadaljnji razvoj novih kovalentnih zaviralcev kaspaze\-1\.

## [Developmental changes in activity\-dependent plasticity of maturation\-related neuronal phenotypes](../publications/559c7084bcea3ff6036d.md)

Katsunori Kobayashi; Hiroki Imbe

Immaturity of neurons in the adult hippocampal dentate gyrus \(DG\) has been implicated in the pathophysiology of neuropsychiatric disorders\. Pseudo\-immaturity of DG neurons can be induced by neuronal hyperexcitation in adulthood\. This “dematuration,” a reversal of maturation, could lead to aberrant neuronal maturation, if activated during development\. However, it has not been directly tested whether dematuration can be induced in developing neurons\. In the present study, we examined the effect of electroconvulsive treatment \(ECT\) on DG neurons of mice at several different developmental stages\. Electrophysiological recordings were made using hippocampal slices\. We analyzed frequency facilitation, a form of short\-term synaptic plasticity, at the DG output mossy fiber synapses as an index of functional maturity of DG neurons\. ECT had no significant effects on mossy fiber synaptic transmission at early postnatal ages, but it significantly reduced frequency facilitation at the postnatal age of ≥4 weeks, suggesting the induction of dematuration\. Neuronal maturation marker analysis confirmed this result\. The development of responsiveness to ECT was accompanied by maturation of N\-methyl\-D\-aspartate receptor functions at the excitatory synaptic input onto DG neurons\. Our results demonstrate that neuronal dematuration by ECT becomes inducible in postnatal 4 weeks in the DG of mice\. Neuronal hyperexcitation such as seizures or alterations in N\-methyl\-D\-aspartate receptor signaling around this developmental stage might affect proper maturation of DG neurons, thereby possibly increasing a risk of neuropsychiatric disorders\.

## [Mapping Road Safety Inequity in India Using Artificial Intelligence Where Fatalities Cluster, Where AI Road\-Safety Technology Is Deployed, and What Should Be Prioritised](../publications/55a803143d99a7c981ad.md)

Samarth Mathur

India records more road deaths than any other country in the world, with 172,890 in 2023, but the public data behind that number is rarely studied to ask whether the danger is spread evenly and whether new artificial\-intelligence road\-safety technology is reaching the worst impacted areas\. This paper uses official Ministry of Road Transport and Highways \(MoRTH\) figures for the country, for every state and union territory, and for fifty cities, together with a list of few of India’s AI road\-safety deployments, to map where road deaths cluster and to compare that with where the technology has already been installed\. Then, it builds a simple, literature\-based model of how many lives the proven tools could theoretically save\. The work is quantitative, with fifteen figures and six tables\. The main results are as follows\. The absolute and per\-person data are almost unrelated, with a correlation of only 0\.28, so Uttar Pradesh has the most deaths but only an average rate per person, while Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, and Telangana have the highest rates per person\. AI systems have mostly been implemented in states that already had strong administration rather than to the worst impacted ones, which matches the World Bank’s split between high\-capacity and low\-capacity states\. A preventable\-fraction model estimates that AI\-suited vehicle and enforcement measures could prevent roughly 26,000 deaths a year at moderate coverage, in a range of 11,900 to 49,500, with automated speed enforcement the largest single measure at 17,600\. Even the high estimate is below the national target of halving deaths by 2030, so road engineering and emergency care must take over the burden of covering the rest\. Most of the preventable deaths fall in the worst impacted states that currently have no major deployment, which shows the real cost of the deployment gap\.

## [Optimizing Agentic Artificial Intelligence to Improve Business Process Automation Efficiency through Modern Digital Technology](../publications/55b18e300dd6edda9af6.md)

Stephen Gregorius Kurnia; Darmin Darmin

In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation \(BPA\) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision\-making tasks\. Agentic Artificial Intelligence \(Agentic AI\), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi\-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations\. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems\. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation\. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule\-based automation by enabling adaptive problem\-solving, real\-time context awareness, and cross\-system collaboration\. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions\. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment\. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes\. Because this is a literature\-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains\.

## [Global governance, regulations, and policy responses to environmental antimicrobial resistance](../publications/55b46691c2e4d85565de.md)

Nilufar Yoqubova; Закирова Рухсона Юнусовна; Fazliddin Jalilov; Shokhid Gulyamov; Avez Tuymuradovich Sharipov; Sylvester Chibueze Izah

Antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) has become a critical global threat, often described as a “silent pandemic\.” Although the broad application of antibiotics across various sectors has yielded significant benefits, inadequate regulation has led to inappropriate antimicrobial use, reducing treatment effectiveness\. Thus, the development of resistance genes has accelerated, leading to rising global mortality\. The rapid spread of these genes through soil, water, and air highlights the environment’s role as a critical reservoir and transmission pathway\. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the environmental dimensions of AMR alongside the associated governance, regulatory, and policy challenges through a One Health perspective\. Literature was drawn from recent peer\-reviewed studies and key international reports to evaluate global governance structures, including the WHO Global Action Plan, National Action Plans \(NAPs\), and the One Health approach\. Major policy gaps include weak enforcement of environmental regulations and insufficient integration of the environmental sector into One Health initiatives\. Furthermore, regulatory oversight is limited by a lack of specific antibiotic discharge standards and inadequate monitoring of pharmaceutical effluents and agricultural runoff\. The review also examines the potential of digital technologies and artificial intelligence to enhance AMR surveillance and early detection\. Eventually, stronger global governance, enforceable environmental standards, improved intersectoral coordination, and the integration of environmental indicators into NAPs and Sustainable Development Goals are essential to mitigate AMR and maintain intergenerational equity\. By aligning policy frameworks with scientific evidence and technological innovations, more resilient systems can be established to protect global health\.

## [Renewable Energy Roadmap for Hospitals: ML\-Enabled Forecasting and Sizing of a Hybrid PV–Wind System in Türkiye](../publications/55b7f3d433b4a9aa6846.md)

Mehmet Daş; Gül Nihal Güğül; Erhan Arslan

Energy use for heating, cooling, and lighting in buildings continues to increase, driving fossil fuel consumption and carbon emissions\. Hospitals face especially high demand\. This study designs and evaluates a hospital\-scale hybrid renewable system \(solar PV plus wind\) for Diyarbakır, Türkiye, and develops real data\-driven performance models to reduce energy consumption\. Pace regression, incorporating weather and building characteristics, is used to predict PV and wind generation\. Three months of data \(Aug–Oct 2022\)—average temperature 26 °C, peak solar irradiance 1012 W/m², average wind speed 1\.18 m/s—and total electricity use of 2895 MWh were analyzed\. Models were validated using RMSE and MAPE\. Results show strong fit \(PV: R² = 0\.9262, RMSE = 0\.037; wind: R² = 0\.986, RMSE = 0\.021\)\. Estimated errors were 14% for solar and 11% for wind\. Scenario analysis indicates the hybrid system could supply approximately 7\.14% of the hospital’s annual demand via PV and 0\.02% via wind\. Even in modest\-wind regimes, machine\-learning\-guided design enhances forecasting and sizing, providing a practical roadmap for public buildings in diverse climates to optimize renewables, reduce grid dependence, and lower emissions while maintaining service reliability\.

## [Physically‐Modified Fluorinated Graphene/Polyether Ether Ketone Composites Exhibiting Low Dielectric Constant and Low Dielectric Loss](../publications/55c2a6b51ed1835cb6b1.md)

景芳达; Zhang Yang; Zhaosong Sun; Na Ma; Dongyan Liu; Guoxin Sui

ABSTRACT With the explosive growth of cutting‐edge technologies such as artificial intelligence and autonomous driving, the demand for high‐performance dielectric materials in the integrated circuit industry is experiencing a sharp increase\. Polyether ether ketone \(PEEK\), with its intrinsically low dielectric constant, has great potential for applications\. However, simple and efficient strategies to obtain low‐dielectric PEEK with excellent thermal stability and mechanical properties remain largely unexplored\. In this work, a physically modified fluorinated graphene \(Si‐FG\) was first prepared through ultrasonic stripping and sol–gel method\. Subsequently, it was uniformly blended with PEEK to fabricate Si‐FG/PEEK composites\. Morphological and chemical composition characterizations confirmed the successful synthesis of Si‐FG\. Benefiting from the excellent properties and good dispersion of Si‐FG, the Si‐FG/PEEK composites exhibited a low dielectric constant of 2\.78 and a low dielectric loss of 0\.0016 at 1 MHz\. Moreover, the composites exhibited enhanced thermal stability and mechanical properties, with a thermal decomposition temperature exceeding 560°C, a glass transition temperature above 151°C, a tensile strength of 105\.37 MPa, and a storage modulus of 3502 MPa\. This study provides a novel strategy for the application of PEEK‐based dielectric materials in integrated circuits\.

## [Analysis of the effects of different protease types on volatile compounds and oxidative properties of blackthroat seaperch \( Doederleinia berycoides \) liver oil](../publications/55c3d58081d77b86d585.md)

Jixiang Zhang; Feifan Wu; Chenyang Zhao; Xiaoguo Ying; Shanggui Deng; Wenxuan Chen; Алессандра Гуиди; MA Lukai

Abstract This study evaluated the effects of different proteases on the extraction, flavor profile, and oxidative stability of blackthroat seaperch \(Doederleinia berycoides\) liver oil obtained by aqueous enzymatic extraction\. Trypsin\-assisted extraction yielded oil with the greatest oxidative stability\. Combined analysis by gas chromatography\-ion mobility spectrometry and gas chromatography\-mass spectrometry identified aldehydes as the characteristic volatile compounds in the liver oil\. The relative odor activity value analysis identified \(E\)\-2\-nonenal, furaneol, benzeneacetaldehyde and 4\-\(2,6,6\-trimethyl\-1\-cyclohexen\-1\-yl\)\-3\-buten\-2\-one as the key volatile compounds\. Differences in oxidative stability and thermal behavior were observed among the extraction methods, with the antioxidant capacity of blackthroat seaperch liver oil following the order of pepsin \(PS\) &gt; alkaline protease &gt; trypsin \(TS\) &gt; neutral protease extraction methods\. Differential scanning calorimetry analysis revealed that PS melting and cooling profiles enhanced flavor release and persistence, while TS and PS exhibited ω\-3 fatty acid pyrolysis\. These findings demonstrate the importance of enzyme selection for liver oil flavor and stability and support the valorization of blackthroat seaperch by\-products\.

## [The Impact of Digitalized Internal Control Construction on Audit Effectiveness in Small and Medium\-Sized Enterprises](../publications/55c6b620a2d95245aa43.md)

Jiulong Xie; Zihao Liu; Xiaojun Ke

In the era of the digital economy, the digital transformation of small and medium‑sized enterprises \(SMEs\) is accelerating\. The digital reconstruction of the internal control system has become a core lever for improving governance efficiency, while also profoundly changing the operational logic and performance of audit work\. This paper aims to systematically sort out domestic and international scholarly outcomes concerning digitalized internal control and audit effectiveness, clarify core conceptual connotations, theoretical foundations, influencing mechanisms, situational heterogeneity and measurement approaches, identify research gaps targeting SMEs, and propose targeted future research directions for SME digital governance and audit practice\. This paper systematically reviews domestic and international research findings related to digitalized internal control construction and audit effectiveness, and conducts a literature review from four dimensions: conceptual connotation, influence mechanism, situational characteristics, and measurement methods\. The study finds that digitalized internal control affects audit efficiency and audit quality mainly through three paths: process automation, real‑time data processing, and intelligent risk management\. Due to resource constraints and governance structure characteristics, SMEs face unique dilemmas in digitalized internal control construction and audit adaptation\. Existing research still has deficiencies in causal identification, boundary conditions, and SME‑specific studies\. Future research can further focus on the heterogeneous characteristics of SMEs, deepen the micro‑mechanism of how digitalized internal control affects audit effectiveness, and expand research on the co‑evolution of audit digital transformation and internal control construction\.

## [THE INFLUENCE OF SELENIUM ON OSTEOGENESIS: MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES](../publications/55dcb8a43400353df770.md)

P\. Ye\. Kovalchuk; S\. V\. Tulyulyuk

Objective: to investigate the effect of selenium deficiency on physiological and reparative osteogenesis\. To determine the features of reparative osteogenesis in experimental animals with metadiaphyseal defects of the femur under conditions of selenium deficiency\. Material and methods: the study was conducted on 63 randomly selected white male rats of three months of age\. The features of reparative osteogenesis were studied on a single type of traumatic injury model constructed in the proximal metadiaphysis of the femur regardless of the experimental conditions, which represented a perforated defect in the frontal region\. Results: the presented data indicate the negative impact of selenium deficiency on reparative and physiological osteogenesis, which is manifested by the inhibition of these processes and is accompanied by disorders of the formation of bone regenerator, deterioration of the structural and functional state of bone tissue, the development of degenerative\-necrotic changes in bone tissue and epiphyseal cartilage\.

## [Public relations AI practices: Neoliberalism, field theory, and professional dispositions within an AI\-mediated habitus](../publications/55f55dbd752996ca5cd1.md)

Kyle Harris

Public relations practitioners increasingly turn to artificial intelligence \(AI\) bots and agentic systems to enhance decision\-making, build campaigns, and support stakeholder research\. The growth in AI use, however, reflects pressures of neoliberalism influencing everyday practice\. Neoliberalism is an ideology that embodies market ideals and a sense of technological inevitability\. Within neoliberalism, practitioners may believe they are exercising a degree of autonomy in decision\-making, while actually navigating a field pre\-structured by market logic and efficiency goals\. This article leans on primary theorists Foucault and Bourdieu to explore these AI practices\. Interviews with practitioners \( N = 22 \) indicated that neoliberal patterns actively circulate within practitioner AI deployments\. They are made apparent in narratives around AI as compulsory to remain competitive, as a mode of self\-optimization, and as an efficiency and productivity multiplier\. Yet findings revealed the importance of field dispositions \(e\.g\., professional judgment, context, responsibility\) within practitioners’ neoliberal habitus\. These dispositions reflect the need for a unified approach — fusing human oversight, responsible risk management, and formalized governance — that may bolster professional work\. This article concludes that, amid the absence of regulatory frameworks, field dispositions serve an important, even necessary, role for public relations AI implementation\.

## [Development of the AdventureWalk mobile application](../publications/560029bafe54095df357.md)

Maksim Loknar

Diplomsko delo opisuje razvoj mobilne aplikacije AdventureWalk, ki spodbuja gibanje z igrifikacijo hoje\. Aplikacija, izdelana v ogrodju Flutter z zaledjem Supabase, dinamično generira neigralne like in naloge z odprtimi jezikovnimi modeli prek storitve OpenRouter\. Osrednja tema aplikacije je generirana vsebina, vezana na resnično kulturno dediščino: podatki iz štirih javnih slovenskih registrov so bili obogateni s koordinatami, naloge pa se gradijo na geografsko najbližjih enotah in uporabniku ponudijo povezavo do vira\. Delovanje aplikacije je bilo preverjeno z enotnimi testi in uporabniškim testiranjem s tremi uporabniki, ki so potrdili uporabnost rešitve\.

## [Two decades of conservation agriculture enhances soil structure, carbon sequestration, and water retention in Mediterranean soils](../publications/5601a32cd3d5d111f5fb.md)

Jennifer Alvarez\-Sagrero; Asmeret Asefaw Berhe; Stephany S\. Chacon; Jeffrey P\. Mitchell; Teamrat A\. Ghezzehei

Abstract\. Conservation agriculture offers a pathway for enhancing soil health with climate co\-benefits in Mediterranean agricultural systems\. This study examined long\-term impacts of combining no\-till management with cover cropping over 20 years in California&\#x27;s Central Valley, providing rare insights into soil system equilibrium under sustained conservation management\. We assessed soil physical, chemical, and structural properties comparing reduced tillage with cover crops \(CTCC\) to standard tillage without cover crops \(STNC\), employing density fractionation and spectroscopic analysis to understand carbon protection mechanisms\. After two decades, conservation agriculture achieved dynamic equilibrium characterized by fundamental shifts in carbon stabilization pathways\. Water\-stable aggregate analysis revealed the most pronounced management effects, with CTCC exhibiting 136% greater stability than STNC, indicating substantial improvements in soil structural integrity\. These structural enhancements corresponded with a reorganization of carbon protection mechanisms: CTCC disproportionately enriched the occluded light fraction \(44\.1% vs\. 35\.4% of total recovered carbon in STNC\), demonstrating that physical protection within aggregates becomes a dominant carbon stabilization pathway under long\-term conservation management\. Mineral\-associated organic carbon saturation analysis revealed that both management systems remained well below theoretical maximum capacity \(11\.5% vs\. 7\.4% saturation for CTCC and STNC, respectively\), indicating substantial remaining potential for carbon sequestration even after reaching equilibrium\. Physical property improvements under CTCC included 15% lower bulk density and 13% greater water retention at field capacity, though benefits were concentrated in the surface horizon\. Our findings demonstrate that two decades of conservation agriculture fundamentally transforms soil functioning through aggregate\-mediated physical protection, while creating substantial improvements in soil structural integrity and water retention capacity\. This mechanism shift represents a new soil system equilibrium that maintains enhanced functionality and continued carbon sequestration potential in Mediterranean agricultural systems\.

## [From Counterfeit Detection to Supply Chain Resilience: How Converged Digital Trust Technologies Secure Third\-Party Logistics Supply Chains](../publications/5608c16a66003a133bd2.md)

Sheng Yuanwei; Suhaiza Hanim Mohamad Zailani; Al Nasrie Weli

Counterfeit goods create economic, security, and sustainability risks for supply chains, yet blockchain, radio\-frequency identification \(RFID\), and artificial intelligence \(AI\) have mostly been studied as separate technologies\. This study conceptualises their joint adoption as Logistics Anti\-Counterfeiting Digital Technology \(LACD\) adoption, a converged capability combining identification, traceability, and analytical detection\. Drawing on Rational Choice Theory and Deterrence Theory within a perspective informed by the Technology\-Organisation\-Environment framework, it examines the antecedents and outcomes of LACD adoption and the moderating role of government regulation\. Survey data from 232 medium and large third\-party logistics \(3PL\) firms in China were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling\. Perceived benefit, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty were positively associated with LACD adoption, whereas perceived complexity and cost were negatively associated with it; sanction celerity was not significantly associated with adoption\. LACD adoption was positively associated with logistics security effectiveness and supply chain resilience\. Government regulation strengthened the effects of perceived benefit, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty and weakened the negative effect of perceived cost, but did not moderate the effects of perceived complexity or sanction celerity\. The study also proposes, as an untested proposition, that LACD may provide traceability infrastructure for circular supply chain practices\.

## [Nashville in the Charts: Tracing Country Music’s Mainstream Expansion, 1990–2024](../publications/560d0954588bcb55e800.md)

Tim Rakowitz

Abstract This paper investigates the growing presence of country music on the Billboard Charts between 1990 and 2024, examining the factors behind the genre’s mainstream crossover and commercial rise\. Drawing on a mixed\-methods approach, the study combines analysis of Billboard Year\-End charts, Chartmetric data, and song credits\. It defines ‘country crossover’ songs as tracks appearing on both the Billboard Year\-End Charts and the Hot Country Songs charts within the same year\. The dataset is examined through the frequency and roles of artists, songwriters, producers, and labels, with particular attention to collaboration trends, gender, audience demographics, and chart performance\. Key developments include the 1990s country\-pop surge, the ‘bro\-country’ wave of the 2010s, and the recent chart dominance of Morgan Wallen, Zach Bryan, and Luke Combs\. The findings highlight the musical, structural, and cultural factors shaping country music’s mainstream evolution\.

## [50 years of estimating exposures for different jobs: the past, present and future of developing and using job exposure matrices \(JEM\)](../publications/560fdc1a6a72a7ad2148.md)

Marc Fadel; Karina Undem; Marcel Goldberg; Annette Leclerc; Bradley Evanoff; Alexis Descatha

OBJECTIVES: Obtaining valid estimates of occupational exposures is an important objective of epidemiological studies involving the work exposome\. Job\-exposure matrices \(JEM\) Job\-exposure matrices \(JEM\) link coded job titles to estimates of workplace exposures\. This paper reviews their development over the past 50 years and provides practical guidance on their construction, selection, and use\. METHODS: We synthesized published literature and examples of existing JEM in a narrative overview of their historical development, construction, validation, and application\. We organized practical considerations for developing and selecting JEM around exposure metrics, occupational classifications, temporal and geographical coverage, and validity\. RESULTS: JEM frameworks include exposure components and metrics; timing or location; whether exposures are based on direct measurements, expert opinion, or both; differentiation of qualitative, semi\-quantitative, and quantitative matrices; type of job classification used; incorporation of sex and other variables; and validity testing\. Investigators seeking to use a JEM must assess several important features: existing JEM and their availability, compatibility of job coding systems \(or existence of a correspondence table\), relevant components and exposure metrics, and JEM limitations\. CONCLUSIONS: Awareness of the strengths and limitations of JEM is important for their effective use\. To date, JEM have been mostly used in large general population studies though future applications in research, exposome evaluation and for other public health and policy issues are likely\.

## [Taiwan and Ukraine: reassessing the analogy through realist and constructivist lenses](../publications/5619f708193d6d2b8286.md)

Shuangling Wu

Since the 2022 Russia–Ukraine war, scholars and political commentators have drawn parallels between Ukraine and Taiwan\. Yet no comparable conflict has occurred in the Taiwan Strait\. This article applies a realist lens of power transition and a constructivist lens of legitimacy and identity to reassess the analogy\. It asks why Russia has used force against Ukraine while the PRC has not, and whether the conditions that shaped Ukraine’s wartime experience could be reproduced in the Taiwan case\. Examining these questions through domestic political contexts, the strategic calculus underlying U\.S\.\-led external involvement, and the role of national identity, this article argues that the Ukraine–Taiwan analogy is fundamentally flawed\.

## [Robust Client Behavior Tracking for Malicious Detection in Secure\-Aggregated Federated Learning](../publications/56219267df77849b5353.md)

Ungutur Vishnu Priya; A\. Ramaswami Reddy; M\. Anupama

Federated learning \(FL\) is a successful distributed machine learning paradigm, where diverse clients are able to collaboratively train a global model without releasing their raw data, thereby preserving the data privacy\. To enhance even more privacy, it is common to use Secure Aggregation \(SecAgg\) to make the central server oblivious to any individual client and only get model updates aggregated\. However, this approach cannot be used to identify a malicious actor falling victim to a model poisoning attack, data poisoning, and Byzantine attack, which poses a threat to the quality and effectiveness of the global model\. In this research, we put forward a safe and reliable client behavior monitoring method for malicious detection in secure\-aggregated federated learning\. It does so by measuring the client&\#x27;s actions in an indirect way \(consistency of contribution over time, stability of the updates, reliability of the training, convergence trends, reputation scores based on trust\), and ensuring that the secure aggregation protocols are not broken\. A dynamic risk assessment system identifies frauds whose activity is very divergent from legitimate players\. Identifying malicious clients can enhance the robustness of the federated learning process by either giving the malicious client a reduced weight in the consensus function or excluding the malicious client from subsequent training rounds\. Our approach: Privacy Protection, Robustness to adversarial behaviour, Good model accuracy in scenarios\. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can successfully detect malicious clients, better handle the poisoning attacks than the conventional secure aggregation approach without behavioral monitoring, consider the convergence stability and higher classification accuracy\. The approach that we propose is practical and scalable for preserving privacy of the federated learning systems which are used in healthcare and financial applications, Internet of Things \(IoT\), and many other distributed intelligent applications\.

## [AI\-supported first consultation preparation in oncology: a real\-world clinical usability study](../publications/562a9a312843b745b0ce.md)

Josephine van Koevorden; Rachael Mertooetomo; David Neal; Bilge Çelik; Veerle Struben; Nanne Aben; Niels van den Hork; Vincent van der Noort; Marene Kroon; Luc H\. E\. Karssemakers; Ludi Smeele; Michel W\. Wouters; Richard J\. Dirven

Abstract Large Language Models \(LLMs\) may support clinicians by facilitating information management, but their usability in real\-world oncology practice remains understudied\. This study evaluated the workflow performance of Artificial Intelligence\-based First Consultation Preparation \(AI\-FCP\), generating structured summaries from unstructured clinical documentation, co\-created with end users\. In a prospective single‑group pre‑post design, nine clinicians completed a person\-level baseline, followed by 33 consultations with AI\-FCP\. Case numbers varied by clinic scheduling and enrollment timing, potentially introducing survivorship bias\. Usability was evaluated using validated questionnaires and study\-specific instruments\. Post AI\-FCP, overall perceived workload \(NASA\-TLX\) was 28\.9% lower than baseline \(Hodges\-Lehmann estimate difference −12\.3; 95% CI –21\.7 to –3\.3\), with self\-reported average time savings of 3\.26 min \(SD = 2\.65\) per case\. Preparation succeeded in 84\.9% of consultations; 63\.6% of summaries were complete\. These exploratory findings suggest clinicians perceived lower workload and reported improved workflow efficiency with AI\-FCP\. Further research is needed to determine generalizability\.

## [De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain\-as\-prompt deep learning framework](../publications/5636fe9ca1d9f2ec9211.md)

Fan Zhang; Xuchang Yu; Yuzhu Wu; Lei Li

Antimicrobial lipopeptides \(AMLPs\) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N\-terminal fatty acid modification\. Here we develop a deep learning\-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain\-as\-prompt mechanism with domain\-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid\-induced bioactivity\. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP\-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N\-terminal fatty acid chains \(C6–C18\) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences\. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate \( ≥ 0\.3\) and common fatty acid tails \(C12 and C16\) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences\. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities \(a positive rate of 95\.7%\)\. The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad\-spectrum activities against typical Gram\-positive, Gram\-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models\. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning\-enabled high\-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics\. Authors present their chain\-as\-prompt deep learning framework, which identifies antimicrobial lipopeptides that show efficacy against drug\-resistant bacterial pathogens in laboratory and animal model\.

## [The Influence of Training Programs on Work Motivation of Indonesian National Police Officers: An Empirical Study at the South Tangerang Police Resort](../publications/564b4a1943384e64f61a.md)

Paringsih; Pusporini Palupi Jamaludin

Work motivation is a critical factor influencing the performance and professionalism of Indonesian National Police \(POLRI\) officers in carrying out their public service duties\. Within police organizations, training programs represent a key instrument for human resource development that not only aims to improve technical competence but also influences the psychological conditions of officers in performing their responsibilities\. This study aims to analyze the influence of training programs on the work motivation of POLRI officers at the South Tangerang Police Resort\. The research employed a quantitative approach using a survey research design\. The population consisted of all POLRI officers with the rank of Bintara serving in five police sectors within the South Tangerang Police jurisdiction, totaling 338 personnel\. The research sample consisted of 136 respondents selected using proportional random sampling\. Data were collected through structured questionnaires using a Likert scale and analyzed using simple linear regression analysis\. The findings indicate that training programs have a significant influence on the work motivation of police officers\. These results suggest that well\-structured and relevant training programs can contribute to strengthening officers&\#x27; professional readiness and encouraging stronger work motivation in performing policing duties and providing services to the community\.

## [Prevalence and Factors Associated With Adverse Birth Outcomes in Bangladesh: Evidence From the 2022 Demographic and Health Survey](../publications/564d4e774563c13f9f08.md)

Nowshin Tabassum Shohana; Afsana Mimi; Ansuwa Karmokar

ABSTRACT Background Adverse birth outcomes \(ABOs\) are a prevalent health issue that includes a number of unfavourable health consequences for both the mother and the newborn\. Conditions such as still birth, low birth weight, preterm birth, and macrosomia are linked to a range of both immediate and long‐term complications\. Therefore, this study aimed to estimate the prevalence and identify the determinants of ABOs in Bangladesh\. Methods This study used data from the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey \(BDHS\), a nationally representative cross‐sectional survey\. A total of 3322 cases of birth outcomes were included in the study\. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed to summarise the explanatory variables and evaluate their associations with adverse birth outcomes\. To identify the factors associated with adverse birth outcomes, a survey‐weighted multivariable logistic regression model was applied\. Results The prevalence of adverse birth outcomes was 30\.9% \(95% CI: 29\.3–32\.5\)\. Among these adverse outcomes, low birth weight contributed the largest share of 13\.8% \(95% CI: 12\.6%–15%\), followed by preterm birth which was 12\.9% \(95% CI: 11\.8%–14\.0%\)\. Western region \(aOR: 0\.773, 95% CI: 0\.633–0\.943\), teenage mothers \(aOR: 1\.287, 95% CI: 0\.987–1\.679\), mother&\#x27;s higher education level \(aOR: 0\.575, 95%CI:0\.351–0\.943\), multiple birth \(aOR: 2\.398, 95% CI: 1\.213–4\.744\), unwanted pregnancy \(aOR: 1\.603, 95% CI: 1\.287–1\.997\), place of birth at home \(aOR: 2\.633, 95% CI: 2\.016–3\.439\) and intimate partner violence \(aOR: 1\.442, 95% CI: 1\.129–1\.843\) were significant determinants of ABOs\. Conclusions This study found that factors such as region, mother&\#x27;s education, multiple births, pregnancy intention and intimate partner violence are associated with ABOs in Bangladesh\. It highlights the need to reduce regional disparities by implementing region‐specific interventions, special precautions to reduce teenage pregnancies, ensuring higher education for mothers, care for multiple pregnancies, support women with unplanned pregnancies, and prevent intimate partner violence to reduce ABOs\.

## [Perception and Creativity Symbiosis:The Evolution of Architectural Representation from Hand\-Drawing to VR](../publications/56544197ee10777b4f3b.md)

Luís Moreira Pinto; Joana Nascimento

This study investigates the evolution of perception in architectural drawing, tracing the shift from hand\-drawn sketches to computer\-assisted techniques and immersive virtual reality\. Through a comprehensive theoretical review and comparative analysis, it explores how these tools reshape spatial representation and enhance creative expression, with a particular focus on the pedagogical implications for drawing instruction in universities\. The research explores the evolution of our understanding of perceptual processes over time, focusing on descriptive geometry&\#x27;s role in conceptualizing and communicating complex spatial forms\. Findings point to a balanced synergy, advocating a hybrid approach that integrates the intuitive creativity of hand\-drawn sketches with the technical precision of digital tools\. Informed by classroom experiences, this proposed methodology empowers architectural students to navigate technological advancements while preserving the cognitive engagement and artistic intuition essential to drawing\. The study contributes significantly to spatial design knowledge, providing actionable insights for architects, educators, and researchers on nurturing creativity through integrated representational practices that bridge historical techniques with contemporary technologies in the teaching/learning environment

## [DIGITAL LOBBYING MODEL OF THE DIASPORA IN THE ERA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: SOCIAL MEDIA, NARRATIVE DIPLOMACY AND TRANSNATIONAL POLITICAL COMMUNICATION](../publications/56596a22d423143010e5.md)

Kamandari A\.

The article examines digital diaspora lobbying as an organizational and communicative process linking collective interests with their presentation to decision\-making institutions\. It aims to clarify the functional relationship between representation, social media, narrative diplomacy and artificial intelligence, and to propose a conceptual model of the main stages of this process\. The study is based on an analytical review of selected scientific literature, conceptual comparison and functional modeling\. Five foundations of diaspora representation are identified: defining the represented community, agreeing on common interests, granting representative authority, ensuring internal participation and maintaining accountability\. The model includes six stages: defining the mandate, specifying the problem and evidence base, preparing the narrative and institutional proposal, public communication, engagement with decision\-making institutions, and evaluation of results\. Artificial intelligence supports data classification, source search, multilingual drafting and document comparison, while collective decision\-making and public responsibility remain with the organization\. Results are assessed through communicative visibility, trust and institutional response\. The proposed framework links these levels to specific stages and traceable outputs and requires further empirical verification\.

## [Neuromyths about motor development and coordination among Hungarian teachers: prevalence and associations with completion of motor therapy training](../publications/565c64838220bc46f7e3.md)

Katalin Kälbli; Julianna Víg; Mónika Kaj; Bence Kas; Tamás Berki; László Tóth; Tamás Csányi

Neuromyths—misconceptions arising from the misinterpretation or oversimplification of neuroscientific findings—are common among educators and may influence educational practice\. However, neuromyths about motor development and coordination remain relatively underexplored\. This study examined the prevalence of movement\-related neuromyths among Hungarian in\-service teachers, with particular emphasis on whether endorsement differed according to completion of motor therapy training, and explored additional factors associated with incorrect responses\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 734 Hungarian in\-service teachers, including 206 who had completed motor therapy training\. Participants completed the 44\-item Hungarian Neuroliteracy Questionnaire, of which 13 items addressed motor development and coordination\. Descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney U tests, and ordinal logistic regression were used for analysis\. The prevalence of incorrect responses across the 13 statements ranged from 7\.6% to 95\.8%, indicating that misconceptions about motor development and coordination were common\. Teachers who had completed motor therapy training showed a higher mean incorrect response rate than those who had not \(77\.9% vs\. 71\.2%\) and a lower rate of uncertainty \(“I don&\#x27;t know”: 3\.6% vs\. 10\.3%\)\. Completion of motor therapy training was independently associated with higher odds of belonging to a higher incorrect\-response category \(OR=1\.672, 95% CI \[1\.177, 2\.374\], p = 0\.004\)\. More frequent use of pedagogical journals and textbooks was also associated with higher incorrect response rates, whereas more frequent use of neuropedagogical methods in professional practice and English\-language peer\-reviewed journals was associated with lower incorrect response rates\. These findings indicate that neuromyths related to motor development and coordination are highly prevalent among Hungarian in\-service teachers and that completion of motor therapy training is associated with greater, rather than lower endorsement of such misconceptions\. Strengthening evidence\-informed professional development and neuroscience literacy, as well as improving access to high\-quality scientific literature, may help teachers critically evaluate neuroscience\-related claims and support more evidence\-informed educational practice\.

## [Tubal Reconstruction After Previous Tubal Sterilization](../publications/5662a95613fb8299fe24.md)

Karolina Kolosovaitė; Diana Bužinskienė

Background\. Tubal reconstruction after previous tubal sterilization remains an important fertility\-restoring procedure for women wishing to conceive naturally\. In Lithuania, voluntary tubal sterilization for contraceptive purposes is not legally permitted, whereas in countries such as the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, and most Western European states, voluntary tubal sterilization is legally accessible and widely practiced\. Purpose\. To review, based on recent scientific literature, the possibilities of tubal reconstruction after prior sterilization by evaluating the clinical outcomes of reanastomosis, comparing them with assisted reproductive technologies, and discussing relevant surgical techniques, selection criteria, and technological innovations\. Materials and methods\. A descriptive literature review was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar databases with the following keywords and combinations: “tubal reanastomosis”, “In vitro fertilization and tubal ligation”, “robotic surgery”, “barbed sutures”, and “tubal sterilization complications”\. 23 sources published between 2015–2025 were included in the analysis\. Results\. Tubal reanastomosis was found to be an effective fertility restoration method in carefully selected patients, especially women younger than 35–37 years with ≥4–6 cm of remaining tubal length\. Reported pregnancy rates reach 42–69%, with most conceptions occurring within 6–12 months postoperatively\. In younger patients, clinical pregnancy rates of 60–75% and live\-birth rates of 50–55% are commonly achieved\. Reanastomosis is more cost\-effective for younger women planning more than one pregnancy; however, the risk of ectopic pregnancy and postoperative adhesions remains elevated\. Assisted reproduction is generally more effective for women over 40 years of age\. Conclusions\. Tubal reanastomosis is an effective but selection\-dependent fertility restoration method that remains an important alternative to assisted reproductive technologies\.

## [Integrated architectures for IFC interoperability and legacy BIM migration with a deterministic IFC2X3 data\-quality pilot](../publications/5667d2864c8456d87d9d.md)

Ratan Lal; Mariam Sharif; Muhammad Tariq Bashir; Mohammad Khishe; Alemineh Sorsa; Md\. Munir Hayet Khan; Ahmad Zaland

Interoperability remains a persistent limitation in Building Information Modelling \(BIM\) because Industry Foundation Classes \(IFC\) exchanges can preserve file syntax while losing or misrepresenting geometry, properties, quantities, and relationships\. This study makes an architectural contribution by defining two proposed systems: the Globe\-IFC framework for core\-schema and regional rule governance, and the Legacy\-IFC Bridge for traceable migration of legacy information into IFC\. Evidence combines a structured 95\-study review, a cross\-industry comparison, a deterministic data\-quality pilot, and a de\-identified practitioner survey \(n = 26\)\. The pilot evaluated 300 seeded elements from three professional IFC2X3 steel models\. Class\-matched LoadBearing properties were present in 255/300 elements, positive Length properties in 200/300, recognized material grades in 210/300, and identifiers and relationship participation in 300/300\. The structural\-class check served as the sampling eligibility filter and was therefore satisfied by all 300 sampled elements by design\. Two investigators independently annotated every sampled element and the retained manual dataset is the reconciled consensus baseline, which the automated implementation matched exactly\. The manual–automated agreement is interpreted only as implementation consistency rather than validation of the proposed AI components\. For C1280, no positive Length was returned through the R5 extraction pathway, but inspection of six sampled elements confirmed dimensional Span properties in Pset\_BeamCommon and Pset\_MemberCommon\. Therefore, the 0/100 R5 result reflects how dimensions were represented and extracted rather than absence of dimensional information from the model\. Survey respondents primarily used IFC for coordination \(12/26\), rated legacy integration highly \(mean 4\.31/5\), and rated automated error\-resolution tools highly \(mean 4\.46/5\)\. The findings support the relevance of the proposed integrated IFC\-interoperability workflow for infrastructural development and building design, while showing that AI regulatory updating, machine\-learning validation, and blockchain provenance remain future components requiring separate empirical evaluation\.

## [Isavuconazole: Real\-World Data and Clinical Considerations for Pediatric Patients](../publications/5669eaec8cb1a120d76e.md)

Lorenzo Chiusaroli; Danila Seidel; Daniel Ebrahimi‐Fakhari; Luise Martin; Karoline Ehlert; Andreas H\. Groll; Ζωή Δωροθέα Πανά

Isavuconazole \(ISAV\) is a broad\-spectrum triazole antifungal approved for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis and has recently received approval for use in children ≥1 year of age\. Pediatric approval was based on limited registration data, underscoring the importance of real\-world evidence to better define efficacy and safety in children and adolescents\. In this manuscript, we reviewed pediatric registration trials and real\-world studies evaluating ISAV, with a focus on treatment and prophylaxis indications, pharmacokinetics, and safety\. The literature review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases to identify relevant real\-world and clinical studies published between January 1, 2005, and October 31, 2025\. Studies reporting ISAV use in patients &lt;18 years of age, including registration trials, observational cohorts, case series, and pharmacokinetic\-pharmacodynamic studies, were included\. Twenty\-six real\-world publications and two clinical registration trials met inclusion criteria\. Among the real\-world publications, ISAV was used for treatment in 23 studies and for prophylaxis in 5 studies, while 17 studies evaluated drug exposure or pharmacokinetics \(several studies involved more than one mode of administration\)\. Most patients had underlying hematologic or oncologic conditions\. Across heterogeneous study populations and outcome definitions, complete or partial response was reported descriptively in approximately 72% of evaluable patients treated for invasive fungal disease, with breakthrough fungal infections reported in approximately 10% of patients receiving prophylaxis\. Adverse events were generally mild and predominantly consisted of reversible hepatic laboratory abnormalities; serious drug\-related toxicity, including one reported case of acute liver failure, was rare\. Pharmacokinetic data demonstrated predictable exposure and achievement of target plasma concentrations in the majority of patients\. Taken together, current evidence, although limited and derived largely from retrospective and salvage\-treatment cohorts, suggests promising clinical activity and generally favorable tolerability of ISAV for invasive mold infections in pediatric populations\. Real\-world data support its use as a therapeutic option in selected patients, while underscoring the need for prospective studies to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and assess long\-term safety\.

## [An AI Algorithm for Strategic Financial Decisions of Firms in Risky Imperfect Markets](../publications/5674e67a181c1d18823b.md)

T\. V\. S\. Ramamohan Rao

Both the investors and the firms in imperfect markets experience information asymmetry\. As a result, they find obtaining full information before making any decisions to be more expensive relative to expected gains\. In general, individuals provide finances based on the market price of the common stock, dividend payments, and the ease with which they can liquidate common stock\. However, such decisions cannot be explained by a market like mechanism\. Similarly, there is no satisfactory behavioral basis to rationalize the choices of the firms and the investors\. It is possible to develop AI algorithms since a large amount of data is available on the actual decisions made\. The present study postulates a behavioral basis for the observed decisions\. In particular, it will be postulated that the financial manager wishes to generate adequate finances to support the capital decisions of the production manager\. Similarly, the production manager will consider it necessary to invest in capital stock to avoid losing market share to rival firms\. Intuitively, faced with the valuation of many objectives the financial manager attempts to pursue the numerically best objective and utilize the most productive strategy until they find some superior choice\. Empirically it was found that in industries like motor vehicles the demand in the long run would be basically for replacement\. Financial managers tend to concentrate on the short run objectives\. On the other hand, electrical and chemical products do not experience shortage of demand even in the long run\. They focus attention on long run objectives\. The proposed algorithm accounts for such differences\. It was noted that there is a recurrent change in the objectives and strategies of firms\. The numerical magnitudes may themselves be inadequate to describe the behavior\. Far more detailed data on the relative valuation of objectives and patterns of change over time would be necessary to develop satisfactory predictive algorithms\.

## [TURQUALITY\-SUPPORTED COMPANIES IN THE PLASTICS\-RELATED SECTOR: A CONTENT ANALYSIS OF SUSTAINABILITY AND DIGITALIZATION VISIBILITY IN CORPORATE REPORTS](../publications/567b670b6a7a8d34dc60.md)

Taner AKÇACI; Merve Tatar; Yasin Bayar

In this study, it was aimed to examine the transformation awareness and sustainability visibility of Turquality\-supported plastics companies in Türkiye\. In the study, the most up\-to\-date sustainability reports of six Turquality\-supported plastics companies were evaluated with content analysis using qualitative research methods\. In the analysis, the prominent words in the report were determined by word frequency and word cloud analysis\. As a result of the analysis, it was determined that environmental sustainability received the highest emphasis among the reports, followed by social and economic dimensions\. Furthermore, digitalization\-themed words have also been found to have relatively limited visibility\. Looking at the company\-level results, it can be said that Brisa and Teklas are the companies with the highest corporate visibility, standing out in the overall sustainability outlook and digital transformation indicators, respectively\. The findings provide strategic insights for policymakers and firms, emphasizing the necessity of strengthening digital transformation capacity alongside environmental initiatives to fully realize Turquality’s strategic objectives\. This study is one of the first to analyze the intersection of Turquality support and twin transformation in the plastics industry, and is thought to provide empirical insights into how national brand programs promote sustainability\-oriented digital competitiveness\.

## [Short\-term outcomes of a novel anti\-reflux biologic flap technique versus double flap technique after laparoscopic proximal gastrectomy: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/5686728f186e1bee23a0.md)

Lindi Cai; Guanglin Qiu; Pengwei Zhao; Gan Li; Junxiang Zhang; Enmeng Li; Yongtai Ma; Yanjun Sun; Mengke Zhu; Xinhua Liao; Xiangming Che; Xuqi Li; Lin Fan

BACKGROUND: The prevalence of proximal gastric cancer continues to rise\. Proximal gastrectomy is effective in preserving a favorable postoperative nutritional status, but mitigating postoperative reflux esophagitis poses a formidable challenge\. METHOD: We developed a novel anti\-reflux procedure for laparoscopic proximal gastrectomy \(LPG\) using a biologic patch to construct a mechanical anti\-reflux barrier, termed the biologic flap technique \(BFT\)\. In this retrospective cohort study, patients who underwent LPG at our center between January 2020 and June 2024 were reviewed\. Among them, 25 received BFT reconstruction and 54 underwent double flap technique \(DFT\) reconstruction\. Short\-term outcomes of the patients were compared to evaluate the clinical application value of BFT\. RESULTS: Tumors were more frequently located at the esophagogastric junction and were larger in the LPG\-BFT group than in the LPG\-DFT group \(60\.0% vs\. 27\.8%, P = 0\.006; median size 2\.5 cm vs\. 1\.5 cm, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The median operation and anastomosis times were significantly shorter with LPG\-BFT \(170 min vs\. 235 min and 28\.0 min vs\. 62\.5 min, respectively; both P &lt; 0\.001\)\. No statistically significant differences were observed in the rates of early and late postoperative complications between the groups, although anastomotic stenosis was less frequent in LPG\-BFT \(4\.0% vs\. 9\.3%, P = 0\.716\)\. Multivariate analysis identified tumor location at the esophagogastric junction and the use of LPG\-DFT as independent predictors of longer operation time\. Los Angeles grade B or higher reflux esophagitis was observed in 8\.7% of LPG\-BFT patients and 7\.5% of LPG\-DFT patients \(P = 1\.000\)\. CONCLUSION: BFT following LPG is a safe and feasible procedure that can reduce operation time and may provide an alternative for anti\-reflux reconstruction when DFT is technically challenging\. Favorable short\-term clinical outcomes support further evaluation of BFT as an alternative reconstruction technique\.

## [Network analysis and machine learning approach identifies HSP90\-associated synthetic lethal targets and drug responses in breast cancer](../publications/5689c47b54e01cb9f621.md)

Aftab Alam; Mohd Faizan Siddiqui; Suresh Kumar Kali; Lena Labania; Samir Attoub; Aydah M\. Al\-Awadhi; Maria J\. Fernández\-Cabezudo; Basel K\. al\-Ramadi

Heat shock protein 90 \(HSP90\) is an ATP\-dependent molecular chaperone that stabilizes numerous oncogenic proteins involved in proliferation, survival, DNA repair, and therapeutic resistance\. Despite its central role in breast cancer \(BRCA\), monotherapy targeting HSP90 has shown limited clinical success, highlighting the need to identify therapeutically actionable HSP90\-associated vulnerabilities\. Here, we integrated transcriptomic, network, pharmacogenomic, single\-cell, and CRISPR dependency datasets\. The major HSP90 isoforms, HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 , were significantly overexpressed in BRCA and independently associated with poor survival\. Immune and single\-cell analyses linked high HSP90 expression to an immune\-cold tumor microenvironment and tumor cell programs related to proliferation, DNA damage response, invasion, and metastasis\. Network analysis identified synthetic lethal/viable \(SL/SV\) interactions involving key regulators, including PAK1, MAP2K1, MAPK3, NFKB1, TNF, CALN1, and HACD3 , highlighting interconnected therapeutic vulnerabilities\. Pharmacogenomic integration with GDSC and six machine\-learning algorithms identified 26 candidate compounds predicted to be effective across 51 breast cancer cell lines\. CRISPR dependency analyses demonstrated negative gene effect scores for HSP90 and several SL partners, supporting their essential roles in tumor cell viability\. These findings establish HSP90 as a central regulatory hub and provide a rationale for mechanism\-based combination therapies and computational prioritization of precision oncology targets for experimental validation\.

## [Amino Derived Drug Precursors for Drug Developments Using Biocatalyst](../publications/56a4d4bcc345f7b6b8af.md)

Rajesh Ram; Laxmi Yadav; Mamta Verma

Amino acid\-derived drug precursors are essential intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis because they provide structurally diverse and stereochemically defined building blocks for the development of modern therapeutics\. Biocatalysis has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional chemical synthesis by enabling highly selective and environmentally friendly transformations\. This review evaluates the role of biocatalysts in the synthesis of amino acidderived drug precursors and highlights recent advances, pharmaceutical applications, industrial translation, emerging technologies, and future perspectives\. A narrative review was conducted by critically analyzing recent literature on amino acid\-derived drug precursors, enzyme classes, biocatalytic strategies, pharmaceutical applications, industrial process development, and emerging technologies\. Relevant studies were synthesized to provide a comprehensive overview of current progress and future opportunities\. Biocatalysts, including transaminases, dehydrogenases, imine reductases, hydrolases, cytochrome P450 enzymes, and multienzyme cascade systems, enable efficient synthesis of optically pure pharmaceutical intermediates with excellent chemo\-, regio\-, and stereoselectivity\. Advances in protein engineering, artificial intelligence, synthetic biology, and metabolic engineering have further enhanced enzyme performance, process scalability, and industrial applicability while supporting sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing\. Biocatalysis has become a cornerstone technology for producing amino acid\-derived drug precursors by integrating catalytic precision with green manufacturing principles\. Continued innovation in enzyme engineering and computational technologies is expected to accelerate the development of efficient, scalable, and sustainable pharmaceutical production platforms\.

## [ON ART, CULTURES, AND REEXISTENCE: VIEWS ON THE MOVIMENTO NEGRO EDUCADOR \(MNE\) IN CONTEMPORARY TIMES](../publications/56a65cb20ba57fce9a5d.md)
