## [Piezoelectric and Dielectric Enhancement in Orientation‐Engineered Freestanding Epitaxial Ba\(Ti,Sn\)O 3 Membranes](../publications/56a97d8a0b6cadcd0a39.md)

Pranab Kumar Roy; Soumen Pradhan; Harsh Nitinkumar Joshi; K\. Gurukrishna; Fabian Hartmann; Sven Höfling; Ashish Garg; Shikhar Misra

ABSTRACT Heterogeneous integration of freestanding single‐crystalline ferroelectric membranes offers a promising route to leverage their dielectric, piezoelectric, and nonlinear optical behavior in adaptive electronics\. Crystallographic orientation engineering in these membranes further enables tuning of strain states, domain characteristics, and resulting functional properties\. While orientation‐engineered Pb‐based piezoelectric membranes have been demonstrated, similar studies on Pb‐free systems remain limited\. Here, single‐crystalline BaTi 0\.97 Sn 0\.03 O 3 \(BST\) membranes along three different crystallographic orientations are fabricated via an epitaxial layer lift‐off process on Indium Tin oxide \(ITO\)‐coated glass substrates to investigate the anisotropic dielectric, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties\. Relaxation of substrate‐induced compressive strain promotes enhanced in‐plane and out‐of‐plane domain nucleation, yielding superior piezoelectric and dielectric responses across all orientations\. An enhanced piezoelectric response in all BST membranes \(61–113 pm/V\) is observed\. Dielectric analysis further reveals a significant enhancement in permittivity for all the freestanding membranes compared to their clamped counterparts, at frequencies above ∼10 5 Hz \(∼150 at 5 MHz\), indicating faster polarization relaxation dynamics\. Overall, this study demonstrates the influence of crystallographic orientation on domain evolution in freestanding membranes and paves the way for their integration into next‐generation high‐frequency dielectric and microelectromechanical devices\.

## [Talabaning axborot xavfsizligi kompetensiyasi pedagogik tushuncha sifatida: mohiyati, tarkibi va sun’iy intellekt sharoitidagi o‘ziga xosligi](../publications/56ac9d8e8ecaef23b769.md)

Шахзод Маманазар угли Мустафоев

This article provides a theoretical analysis of students’ information security competence as a pedagogical concept\. It examines its essence, structural components, and the pedagogical factors influencing its development\. Particular attention is paid to the protection of personal data, the assessment of information reliability, the identification of cyber threats, compliance with digital ethics standards, and the development of a critical approach to content generated by artificial intelligence in the context of the widespread integration of artificial intelligence tools into the educational process\. ## [Interface Rectification via Roll‐to‐Roll Dual‐Confinement Nanocoatings for High‐Temperature Polymer Capacitors](../publications/56acffa7a70c0866e363.md)

Ning Guo; Marina Dabaghian; Jierui Zhou; Josh N\. Bodin; Chong Xiang; Fei Wang; Antigoni C\. Konstantinou; Dingxin Wei; Yifei Wang; Chao Jun Wu; R\. Casalini; Bryan D\. Huey; Priya D\. Vashishta; Luyi Sun; Yang Cao

Polymer film capacitors are indispensable for energy storage and power conversion, yet their energy density and efficiency deteriorate rapidly at elevated temperatures\. At temperatures relevant to wide\-bandgap semiconductor electronics \(&gt;150°C\), heat\-resistant polymer films must be heavily derated to avoid premature aging due to intensive hot\-carrier injection\. Inspired by multilayered barrier structures in nature, we developed a scalable roll\-to\-roll self\-assembled organic\-inorganic nanolaminate coating that significantly enhances the high\-temperature dielectric performance of polymer films\. The nanolaminate architecture introduces dual confinement mechanisms: nanoconfinement of the polymer binder suppresses chain motion and enhances thermal stability, while anisotropic carrier relaxation within two\-dimensional nanoclay nanosheets impedes through\-plane hot\-carrier transport\. Together, these effects synergistically establish an interface\-rectification mechanism that promotes in\-plane energy dissipation and suppresses carrier injection at electrode\-polymer interfaces\. At 150°C, the coating significantly reduces the pre\-breakdown conduction current of polyetherimide \(PEI\), increases the breakdown strength from 450 to 501 MV/m, and improves the discharged energy density at 95% efficiency by 105%\. Furthermore, roll\-to\-roll\-coated PEI capacitors exhibit a 45\-fold lifetime enhancement at 150°C and 180 MV/m\-a design field previously sustained only by BOPP below 60°C\. This work provides a scalable and technology\-ready strategy for high\-temperature, high\-density polymer capacitive energy storage\.

## [Recent advances in dentistry](../publications/56baa9c27c2803eb5e2c.md)

Kumar Tathagat Singh; Ahemer Arif Shaikh; Sumit Bhatt; Venkatesh Kulkarni; Vivek Chaudhary

Dentistry has entered a transformative era, driven by rapid technological innovation, interdisciplinary research, and a growing emphasis on patient\-centered care\. The past decade has witnessed remarkable progress across diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive domains, reshaping both clinical practice and academic inquiry\. This book, Recent Advances in Dentistry, seeks to capture these developments in a structured and comprehensive manner, offering readers a panoramic view of the evolving landscape of dental science\. The chapters assembled herein highlight the convergence of digital technologies, biomaterials, nanoscience, and regenerative medicine with traditional dental practice\. From the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into diagnostic workflows, to the revolution brought by CAD/CAM systems and 3D printing, dentistry is increasingly defined by precision, personalization, and efficiency\. Advances in smart biomaterials and nanotechnology promise enhanced durability and biocompatibility, while innovations in orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and caries management continue to refine patient outcomes across age groups\. Equally compelling are the strides made in endodontics and periodontology, where regenerative approaches and novel instrumentation are expanding therapeutic possibilities\. The domain of implantology and esthetic dentistry has been reshaped by digital planning, guided surgery, and minimally invasive techniques, ensuring both functional and aesthetic excellence\. Emerging modalities such as laser therapy, photobiomodulation, robotics, and augmented reality further underscore the dynamic future of dental practice\.

## [Young Learners&\#x27; Motivation for AI ‐Supported Extracurricular French Vocabulary Learning: A Q Methodological Study](../publications/56bf83d593ddb2942d04.md)

Xun Lu; Nanlan Pei

ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly reshaping extracurricular language learning, yet little is known about how young learners construct motivation when using AI to learn less commonly taught foreign languages\. This study investigates primary school students&\#x27; motivational typologies and the factors related to these configurations in AI‐supported extracurricular French vocabulary learning\. Twenty learners completed a Q sorting task based on 34 motivational statements, and eight participants were subsequently selected for semi‐structured interviews\. Q factor analysis identified four motivational typologies: socially supported learners, future‐oriented learners, enjoyment‐driven learners and mastery‐oriented learners\. Thematic analysis further revealed four cross‐cutting factors related to these motivational configurations: human support, AI‐supported autonomy, interactive enjoyment and competence feedback\. The findings show that the motivational value of AI is not uniform but depends on how young learners connect technological affordances with interpersonal relationships, personal agency, enjoyment, future goals and perceived progress\. By integrating Q methodology with Self‐Determination Theory, this study advances a configurational understanding of young learners&\#x27; motivation and shows that the same AI‐supported learning opportunities can acquire different motivational meanings depending on learners&\#x27; social and psychological configurations\.

## [Cryogenic distortion compensation in guided ultrasonic waves using a Physics\-Informed Generative Adversarial Network](../publications/56cb1e6f5e0e629327a8.md)

Shuozhi Wang; Jinyu Wang; Changxian Zheng; Tao Liu; Wenfeng Zhang; Jianqiang Li; Yishou Wang

Reusable launch vehicles undergo severe thermal cycling, and cryogenic storage conditions introduce strong, nonlinear distortions in guided ultrasonic wave signals used for structural health monitoring\. These temperature\-induced effects obscure damage sensitive features and limit the robustness of both conventional compensation techniques and purely data driven learning models\. This paper proposes a physics informed machine learning framework, termed the Guided Wave Physics\-Informed Generative Adversarial Network, to compensate cryogenic guided ultrasonic wave distortions in a physically consistent manner\. The artificial intelligence component is realized through generative adversarial learning and is applied to cryogenic guided\-wave temperature compensation The model adopts a residual generative formulation in the Hilbert\-envelope domain and integrates adversarial sequence learning with wave\-physics priors through curvature based regularization and peak morphology constraints\. These physics\-informed components explicitly suppress nonphysical temporal artifacts and preserve the modal structure of guided\-wave responses, enabling stable compensation across varying cryogenic conditions\. Experiments conducted on an aluminum alloy plate under liquid\-nitrogen cooling–heating cycles demonstrate that GW\-PIGAN achieves high\-fidelity reconstruction while maintaining consistent performance across varying reference temperatures\. Compared with purely data\-driven baselines, the proposed physics\-informed formulation exhibits improved stability, physical plausibility, and generalization under extreme thermal conditions\. By embedding guided\-wave physics into generative learning, the proposed framework provides a practical and interpretable physics\-informed machine learning approach for cryogenic structural health monitoring\. It also establishes a methodological basis for future monitoring applications in reusable aerospace structures under extreme cryogenic conditions\.

## [Why do copper mining projects not fulfil their value proposition? Insights into deviations and causes in the 2015–2022 global portfolio](../publications/56cf793537da7b7f8c05.md)

Luis Lagos; Emilio Castillo; Nadia Mery; José Charango Munizaga\-Rosas; Felipe Sánchez

Abstract The copper industry, driven by the energy transition, is projected to grow significantly in the upcoming decades\. This growth requires both the expansion of existing operations and the development of new mining projects\. However, new initiatives face a series of challenges during implementation and are often commissioned with significant budget overruns and delays, resulting in substantial economic impacts for all parties involved\. This research assesses the fulfilment of the value proposition of greenfield copper mining projects in terms of investment amount, production start date, and scope, for a global portfolio of 80 projects developed between 2015 and 2022\. The study combines two complementary approaches: descriptive analysis to identify general trends, and the K\-means clustering algorithm to explore non\-evident patterns\. On average, the projects in the analysed portfolio experienced a 21\.1% cost overrun and a 3\.3\-year delay, both measured against pre\-feasibility estimates, with significant variations within the sample associated with factors such as location, scope adjustments, and ownership changes\. The clustering analysis identifies three project archetypes with distinct deviation profiles, indicating that deviations arise through more than one pathway\. Recurrent drivers of value proposition failure include unresolved community conflicts, environmental permitting challenges, inadequate supporting infrastructure, cost inflation, and financing\-related disruptions\. As these are embedded in both project\-level decisions and broader governance environments, we recommend a multi\-scalar approach, combining strengthened pre\-investment processes incorporating technical, financial, and socio\-political risk management, with robust institutional frameworks for predictable permitting, investment in enabling infrastructure, and adaptable strategies for efficient and mutually beneficial evaluation and approval processes\.

## [Halogen Engineered Chiral Amplification in Chiral Hybrid 2D Perovskites for Self‐Powered Circularly Polarized Light Detection](../publications/56d1479c99fa3c0d01bf.md)

Jie Wu; Dacheng Zhou; Pei Wang; Jiandong Yao; Xiyong Chen; Bingsuo Zou; Jia Sun; Xianli Li; Ruosheng Zeng

ABSTRACT Chiral hybrid perovskites hold great promise for optoelectronic and spintronic applications due to their superior optoelectronic properties\. However, the development of self‐powered circularly polarized light \(CPL\) detectors is often hindered by weak chiroptical anisotropy and inefficient zero‐bias operation\. Herein, we report the synthesis of chiral \( R/S ‐3BrMBA\) 2 PbBr x I 4‐x \(0 ≤ x ≤ 4\) hybrid perovskites, demonstrating that halogen engineering is an effective strategy for chiral amplification\. Through this approach, the g CD value is enhanced by more than 5‐fold, attributed to intensified octahedral distortion and the concomitant modulation of spin–orbit coupling\. Remarkably, we achieved a Zeeman splitting of 0\.663 meV, a 2\.4‐fold increase over the pristine sample, which represents the highest value reported to date for chiral 2D perovskites\. Furthermore, the \(R‐3BrMBA\) 2 PbBr 2 I 2 device exhibits an open‐circuit voltage exceeding 5 V, breaking the traditional bandgap limit while enabling self‐powered operation with a g Iph of 0\.24\. This work confirms halogen engineering as a robust strategy for chirality amplification, paving the way for advanced self‐driven chiral photodetectors\.

## [Joint molecular optimization for efficient virtual screening via machine learning](../publications/56e463d8ddc367863dea.md)

Naman Jain

Joint molecular optimization serves as the central focus of this research, which explores the synergistic integration of machine learning \(ML\) and virtual screening \(VS\) for drug discovery\. This study addresses these limitations by integrating molecular docking and ML to predict and balance multiple molecular properties concurrently\. Traditional VS methods often fall short by primarily targeting single molecular properties, such as binding affinity, overlooking the necessity of simultaneously optimizing multiple crucial parameters like ADMET \(Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity\) profiles\. Key objectives include developing and evaluating multi\-objective optimization strategies and employing ML models \(e\.g\., logistic regression, SVM, neural networks\) to enhance predictive accuracy and computational efficiency\. This research balances efficacy and safety metrics to refine VS and demonstrates the effect of combining these strategies on benchmark data\. This work contributes a controlled, reproducible framework and an explicitly defined multi\-objective prioritization procedure intended to support more efficient and transparent virtual screening, offering valuable insights for researchers in drug discovery, computational chemistry, and ML\. Claims of reduced clinical attrition or improved clinical success would require prospective experimental validation and lie beyond the scope of this computational study\.

## [A marine\-derived sesterterpenoid inhibits migration and invasion of triple\-negative breast cancer cells by suppressing the FAK signaling pathway](../publications/56e89b44ea62e2410fb7.md)

Haiyan Wen; Feifei Zeng; Yu Lan; Yuping Yin; Yuxiang Huang; Yutong Hu; Jiaheng Yin; Juanjuan Li; Siqi Zhou; Kui Hong

Background The high incidence of distant metastasis in triple\-negative breast cancer \(TNBC\) remains the principal driver of disease\-related mortality, highlighting an urgent clinical need for novel therapeutics to restrict tumor progression and dissemination\. Methods We investigated the anti\-tumor potential and underlying molecular mechanisms of MHO7 \(6\-epi\-ophiobolin G\), a structurally unique sesterterpenoid derived from a marine fungus, using MDA\-MB\-231 cells in vitro and a subcutaneous xenograft model in vivo \. Transcriptomic profiling and biochemical analyses were performed to elucidate the underlying signaling alterations\. Results Both in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that MHO7 profoundly curtails MDA\-MB\-231 cell migration and invasion, strengthens adherens junctions, and exhibits robust primary tumor growth inhibition without inducing overt systemic toxicity in preclinical mouse models\. Mechanistically, transcriptomic profiling coupled with biochemical analyses revealed that MHO7 exerts inhibitory effects on cell migration and invasion primarily by attenuating the Focal Adhesion Kinase \(FAK\) signaling pathway\. Specifically, MHO7 treatment remarkably suppressed the autophosphorylation of FAK \(Y397\) and the subsequent recruitment of p\-Src \(Y419\)\. This pathway suppression consequently altered cytoskeletal architecture, attenuated the downstream PI3K/AKT signaling cascade, and curtailed tumor angiogenesis\. Furthermore, we identified a dual inhibitory mechanism wherein MHO7 successfully dismantled the oncogenic crosstalk between FAK and the canonical Wnt/β\-catenin pathway by significantly downregulating nuclear β\-catenin accumulation\. Conclusion MHO7 exerts tumor\-suppressive and anti\-migratory effects in TNBC primarily by attenuating FAK signaling and its downstream pathways, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for highly aggressive TNBC\.

## [Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving](../publications/56f987d7731752c3a722.md)

Yihan Xu; Jia\-Chen Gu; Junyi Zhang; Di Wu; Haikang Deng; Po\-Nien Kung; Kai\-Wei Chang; Amit Sahai; Wei Wang; Nanyun Peng

Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine\-checkable proofs from established mathematical results\. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi\-hop dependencies among declarations\. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems\. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph\-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib&\#x27;s forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi\-hop dependency chains\. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph\-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query\. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3\.7% of extra groups\. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end\-to\-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback\. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at \{8, 16, 32\} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy\-cost efficiency\. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure\-aware search for proof discovery\.

## [Seeing the hidden reservoir: Earth observation and geoinformatics for assessing sand dam impacts in dryland rivers](../publications/56fbfc9e2dc873f3a073.md)

Andreas Braun; Anna Müller; Nimrod Kibet; Volker Hochschild; Martin Sudmanns

Sand dams are small water\-harvesting structures that store water within the sandy matrix of ephemeral riverbeds\. They are widely promoted as nature\-based solutions for water security and climate adaptation in drylands\. Nonetheless, it remains difficult to systematically assess their environmental and socio\-ecological impacts for multiple reasons\. This review synthesizes Earth observation and geoinformatics research on sand dams and evaluates how reliably their impacts can be detected from spatial data\. A structured literature search and citation tracking identified 11 relevant studies published between 2008 and 2026\. Evidence on impacts is dominated by vegetation effects: six studies assess vegetation responses, five report localized greening, higher vegetation vitality, or greater drought resilience, while one finds no average greening\. Direct hydrological evidence is less prominent: gravimetric and radar\-based approaches could not fully resolve local storage effects, and long\-term regional responses remain inconclusive\. Geomorphological evidence is limited to one study, while thermal approaches remain largely exploratory\. Across these studies, differences in spatial scale, control\-site selection, dam maturity, and temporal design constrain comparability and attribution\. We develop a methodological taxonomy and propose future research based on time series, Before\-After\-Control\-Impact designs, climatic controls, in\-situ validation, multi\-sensor integration, automated inventories, and data fusion supported by artificial intelligence\.

## [Assessing Urban Heat Island Dynamics in Hot\-Arid Climates: Impacts of Building Materials, Morphology, and Urban Expansion](../publications/57021641d7a840544321.md)

Abdollah Mobaraki; Mojdeh Nikoofam; Mohammad Bagher Ahmadi; Behnam Mobaraki

Urban Heat Island \(UHI\) formation is influenced by urban morphology, land use, vegetation cover, transportation, and construction materials\. This study investigates the principal factors contributing to UHI formation in Shiraz, Iran, through a qualitative comparative assessment of five central districts, selected because they represent contrasting urban conditions within the same climatic context\. The findings indicate that dense development, limited vegetation, extensive impervious surfaces, transportation\-related heat emissions, and low\-reflectivity façade and pavement materials are closely associated with accumulation of UHI\. Accordingly, vegetation enhancement, sustainable transportation, cool roofs, and high\-albedo materials were identified as relevant mitigation measures\. Among these measures, improving construction materials was further assessed experimentally using polypropylene fiber\-reinforced cementitious composites\. Thermal transmittance and flexural\-strength tests indicated stable thermal behavior and enhanced mechanical performance, with optimum results obtained at nano\-clay contents of 3\.0–4\.5%\. Although the experimental assessment does not directly quantify UHI reduction, it demonstrates the potential of sustainable cementitious materials to improve construction material performance and reduce cooling demand\. The findings support the combined application of planning measures and experimentally assessed material solutions in hot semi\-arid cities\.

## [Para além da psicopatologia: o papel da organicidade nos comportamentos suicidários inaugurais no idoso](../publications/57061487fba0c1a26dc6.md)

Rita Isabel Martins Ortiga; Catarina Eusébio; Elisa Catarina Fernandes Lopes; Luís Fonseca

Suicidal risk increases with age, characterized by more lethal methods and less prior communication of intent\. Although psychopathology is a well\-established classic risk factor, many older adults make first\-ever suicide attempts without any psychiatric history, challenging traditional screening models\. Through a review and two clinical cases, we explore the role of organic factors in inaugural suicidal behaviors in older adults\. Clinical information was obtained through interviews and review of hospital records, with informed consent for publication\. A woman and a man, aged 73 and 77 respectively, both without previous psychiatric follow\-up, self\-inflicted severe penetrating abdominal trauma\. The first showed hypochondriacal concern with chronic constipation that had worsened and become refractory to treatment, amplified by a family history of gastrointestinal cancer\. Sleep deprivation in the preceding days likely facilitated the transition from somatic rumination to an impulsive act\. The second developed a similar preoccupation with constipation that began after hospitalization for decompensated cardiorespiratory disease, suggesting delirium as a precipitating factor\. Constipation is an independent predictor of suicidal behaviors, mediated by the gut–brain axis: the intestinal microbiome influences serotonin synthesis, systemic inflammation, and the psychological distress associated with persistent physical discomfort\. Additionally, sleep deprivation and delirium increase impulsivity by impairing inhibitory control and judgment mediated by the prefrontal cortex\. Thus, a multidimensional assessment of suicidal risk in older adults is essential, integrating physical and mental health, with particular attention to early detection of confusional states and management of distressing somatic symptoms\.

## [A technical review of dynamic brain functional imaging combined with EEG spectral parameters in the screening of early\-stage brain injury](../publications/570b68f62e16e261175c.md)

Hongmei Ruan; Liqing Liao; Yuan Zhang; Zicai Liu; WU Qiang

Background Early\-stage brain injury encompasses subtypes such as mild traumatic brain injury \(mTBI\), silent stroke and subclinical brain injury\. It is characterised by negative imaging findings, subtle symptoms and a high risk of long\-term neurological deficits, presenting a key challenge in the early screening and prevention of neurological diseases\. Traditional imaging techniques, such as structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\) and Computed Tomography \(CT\), can only identify organic morphological lesions\. Their detection rate for early micro\-injuries at the level of neuronal electrophysiology and brain network function is extremely low\. Consequently, these techniques struggle to meet the clinical needs for early screening, assessment, and intervention\. Methods Electroencephalography \(EEG\) spectral changes \(including conventional spectral slowing and 1/f aperiodic abnormalities\) and large\-scale dynamic neural network disruption across the entire brain are core pathological features of early brain functional damage; they may serve as indirect correlates of microscopic pathological changes such as an imbalance in neuronal excitation\-inhibition and abnormalities in the efficiency of brain information transmission\. Based on this, this paper proposes a Dynamic\-Spectral Coupling \(DSC\) framework, which proposes spectral abnormalities as a potential upstream mechanism associated with network reorganisation\. Within this framework, this narrative review summarizes dynamic functional magnetic resonance imaging \(dynamic fMRI\), EEG spectral analysis and multimodal fusion technologies, with a particular focus on elucidating the coupling mechanisms between EEG periodic and 1/f aperiodic spectral parameters and dynamic brain network indicators\. Results The review outlines the screening value and application advantages of multimodal fusion technologies in mTBI, occult cerebrovascular injury and subclinical brain injury\. Furthermore, the paper summarises the current limitations of these technologies in terms of clinical translation, methodology and database development\. Conclusions Taking into account the clinical needs of neurorehabilitation, it proposes future development directions, including the development of lightweight devices, AI\-assisted diagnosis, the establishment of standardised analytical systems and the translation of precision rehabilitation\. The aim is to provide technical guidance and theoretical support for screening, risk stratification and rehabilitation planning in early\-stage brain injury, while acknowledging that clinical utility remains to be established\.

## [Factors influencing surgical residual deviation and their impact on higher\-order aberrations after SMILE surgery](../publications/5714430d23de6e1a1faa.md)

Xujie Deng; Rong Huang; Fangfang Lu; Shigang Xia; Jia Zhang; Jing Lu; Yu Wang; Jiahuan Yi; Xinxin Song; Lijing Deng; Qiguo Xiao; Zhi Wang

PURPOSE: To investigate the factors influencing the surgical residual deviation after Small Incision Lenticule Extraction \(SMILE\) and its impact on postoperative higher\-order aberrations \(HOAs\)\. METHODS: This retrospective study included 77 patients \(146 eyes\) who underwent SMILE surgery at our Eye and Vision Center from February 2021 to June 2022\. Surgical data collected included uncorrected distance visual acuity \(UDVA\), refraction, spherical equivalent \(SE\), corneal curvature, central corneal thickness \(CCT\), axial length \(AL\), intraoperative actual refractive correction, posterior corneal surface height \(PME\), total corneal HOAs, spherical aberration \(SA\), coma aberration \(CA\), and trefoil aberration\. Changes in central corneal thickness were observed preoperatively and at 1 and 3 months postoperatively\. The actual lenticular thickness removed during surgery was compared with the predicted lenticular thickness, and statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26\.0\. RESULTS: The average deviation of CCT at 1 month postoperative was \- 7\.11±9\.933 µm, and at 3 months postoperative was \- 13\.37±9\.665 µm\. The difference between actual and predicted lenticular thickness showed statistical significance \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. At 1 month and 3 months postoperative, the ratio of eyes with negative deviation to positive deviation was 113:33 and 137:9, respectively\. Statistically significant differences were observed in preoperative CCT, with the negative deviation group positively correlating with preoperative refraction, SE, intraoperative actual refractive correction, curvature, CCT, and PME \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. Conversely, the positive deviation group showed a negative correlation with preoperative curvature, CCT, and PME \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. At 1 month and 3 months postoperative, HOAs, SA, CA, and trefoil aberration increased compared to preoperative values, with UDVA, SE, HOAs, SA, and CA showing statistically significant differences \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. In the negative deviation group at 1 month postoperative, deviation values positively correlated with SE \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. In the negative deviation group at 3 months postoperative, deviation values were positively correlated with HOAs, SA, and CA \(P&lt;0\.05\)\. No significant correlation was found between deviation values and UDVA, SE, HOAs, SA, CA, or trefoil aberration in the positive deviation group at both 1 and 3 months postoperative\. CONCLUSION: There is a difference between the actual lenticular thickness removed during SMILE and the predicted lenticular thickness\. Central corneal thickness gradually increases over time postoperatively\. The cutting deviation after SMILE is correlated with preoperative refraction, curvature, and PME, and has a certain impact on postoperative HOAs\.

## [Mechanism\-specific acute silent ischaemic lesions and ischaemic periprocedural stroke after PTAS for severe symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis](../publications/5717304b6c3615e6ac1c.md)

Mu Yuan Li; Zhengyu Wang; Xiaoxin He; Xuebing Feng; Peng Gao; Liqun Jiao

Background Preprocedural acute silent ischaemic lesions \(ASILs\) may reflect distinct ischaemic mechanisms in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis\. We examined whether mechanism\-specific ASIL phenotypes were associated with ischaemic periprocedural stroke after percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting \(PTAS\)\.Methods This secondary mechanistic analysis included 1427 patients undergoing PTAS\. Candidate lesions in 185 examinations were re\-adjudicated against the index\-event or baseline MRI\. Final phenotypes were no definite ASIL, other definite ASIL patterns and isolated perforator\-pattern definite ASIL\. Firth\-penalised logistic regression adjusted for prespecified covariates\. Supportive analyses compared definite ASILs with and without a perforator component and used a global 2 df penalised likelihood\-ratio test of the three\-level phenotype for ischaemic periprocedural stroke; sensitivity analysis excluded non\-retained examinations\.Results Re\-adjudication retained 138/185 examinations as definite ASILs; 47/185 were not retained\. Final groups were no definite ASIL \(n=1289\), other definite ASIL patterns \(n=117\) and isolated perforator\-pattern definite ASIL \(n=21\), with ischaemic periprocedural stroke in 26 \(2\.0%\), 6 \(5\.1%\) and 6 \(28\.6%\), respectively\. Compared with no definite ASIL, isolated perforator\-pattern definite ASIL was associated with ischaemic periprocedural stroke \(adjusted OR, 16\.52; 95% CI 5\.03 to 48\.51; p&lt;0\.001\), whereas the association for other definite ASIL patterns did not reach statistical significance \(adjusted OR, 2\.58; 95% CI 0\.97 to 6\.01; p=0\.058\)\. ASILs with a perforator component had higher odds than those without one \(adjusted OR, 6\.20; 1\.66 to 22\.89; p=0\.008\); the global test was significant \(χ²=19\.34; df=2; p&lt;0\.001\)\. After excluding the 47 non\-retained examinations, isolated perforator\-pattern definite ASIL remained associated with ischaemic periprocedural stroke versus no definite ASIL \(adjusted OR, 15\.64; 4\.75 to 46\.05; p&lt;0\.001\)\.Conclusion Isolated perforator\-pattern definite ASIL was associated with ischaemic periprocedural stroke after PTAS; external validation is required\.

## [Designing a Learning Matrix for Business Education within a Human–AI Learning Community: A Pedagogical Design Study](../publications/572593f9fd826fdec8d9.md)

Di Fan; Qianqian Chen

This study examines the redesign and implementation of a Management Accounting Practice course at a Chinese university during the autumn 2025 semester\. Adopting a pedagogical design\-study approach, the study draws on learner\-context evidence, prior teaching records and reflection, professional digital demands, course\-design documents, task and assessment materials, and selected student work\. Three design problems were identified: insufficient integration of disciplinary content with digital and intelligent resources; fragmented teaching implementation that limited coherent progression from understanding to analytical application and integrative practice; and an assessment approach that did not adequately capture staged skill development and broader professional growth\. In response, a learning matrix was developed around three progressive stages—exploratory understanding, analytical application and integrative practice—and three recurring dimensions of disciplinary knowledge, digital and analytical skills, and professional judgement and decision\-making\. The matrix was enacted through foundation knowledge practice, project and case learning, integrative practice, differentiated support, and stage\-specific use of digital and intelligent tools\. Implementation records and an AI\-Supported Cost–Volume–Profit \(CVP\) Decision Lab illustrate how disciplinary reasoning, digital tool use, verification and managerial judgement were connected in practice\. The study contributes a problem\-to\-design framework for integrating digital and intelligent technologies into applied business education while retaining accountable human judgement\.

## [School Librarians as Academic Migrants: Information Poverty and Digital Resilience in Cross\-Cultural Information](../publications/572daca1626c5e68b20b.md)

Nancy Everhart

This study explores school librarians as academic migrants who must adapt to unfamiliar cultural and technological environments\. Drawing on an autoethnographic study conducted during a six\-month Fulbright appointment in China, 2,181 information\-seeking incidents are analyzed through Chatman&\#x27;s Theory of Information Poverty\. Findings reveal how information barriers were addressed through mobile technologies, risk\-taking, and adaptive information practices\. Interpreted through a school librarianship lens, the results demonstrate that digital resilience and intercultural competence are critical professional capacities for school librarians working in international schools, global partnerships, study\-abroad programs, and culturally diverse educational communities\.

## [The dynamics of knowledge transfer and retention in entrepreneurial education: a conceptual exploration of enabling technologies](../publications/573de7d8843611a1d9cd.md)

Lucia Pizzichini; Massimo Pescarollo; Paola Pisano; Miroslav Svítek

Purpose This conceptual paper aims to examine Entrepreneurial Education \(EE\) in Higher Education Institutions \(HEIs\) through a Knowledge Management \(KM\) lens\. It explains how enabling technology affordances, when aligned with the characteristics of entrepreneurial knowledge, shape Knowledge Transfer \(KT\) and Knowledge Retention \(KR\) under conditions of cognitive bias\. It clarifies how KM processes support durable entrepreneurial capability development\. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a theory\-driven conceptual methodology\. Drawing on KM process theory and conceptual theory\-building guidance, the paper develops a mechanism\-based framework through six stages: problematisation, theoretical anchoring, construct selection, mechanism mapping, model integration and proposition development\. The framework positions KT and KR as the analytical core, enabling technologies as differentiated KM affordances, and cognitive bias as an embedded condition that can distort knowledge interpretation, transfer, retention and reuse\. Findings The framework proposes that enabling technologies can strengthen KT and KR when their affordances align with the knowledge’s tacitness, codifiability and contextual dependence, and are supported by interaction, reflection, curation and governance routines\. Immersive/simulation, AI/analytics and collaborative/process technologies support KT/KR mechanisms\. Cognitive bias can weaken or distort knowledge transfer, retention and reuse, whereas bias\-aware routines and cohort\-to\-cohort feedback can improve knowledge fidelity, programme memory and entrepreneurial capability development\. Originality/value The paper advances a KM\-centred reframing of EE by positioning KT and KR as the focal mechanisms linking enabling technologies to durable entrepreneurial capability development\. It differentiates technologies by their KM affordances and integrates cognitive bias, boundary conditions and programme\-level feedback within a single conceptual architecture, offering testable propositions and design principles for technology\-enabled EE\.

## [Al\-Mīzān Conceptual Framework for Ecological Mitigation](../publications/57417a9cb5039313319a.md)

Abdul Zaenuri; Rismawati Rismawati; Abdul Mufid; Muhammad Syaiful; Wilhanul Haq

The hydrometeorological crisis in Indonesia, marked by the catastrophic flash floods and landslides that struck Sumatra and Aceh in late 2025, has been demonstrated to originate primarily from large\-scale deforestation and upstream land\-use conversion rather than from extreme rainfall anomalies alone\. Although disaster mitigation studies in Southeast Asia have advanced substantially in their technical, infrastructural, and institutional dimensions, the spiritual and religious values that motivate community behavior toward ecosystems remain largely overlooked\. Likewise, existing studies on Islamic ecotheology have yet to be operationalized into a systematic disaster mitigation framework\. This study aims to identify and synthesize the hermeneutical clusters derived from the Qur’an that constitute the al\-mīzān conceptual framework, examine their conceptual relevance to the causal roots of the 2025 Sumatra–Aceh disaster, and formulate their operational implications for strengthening value\-based disaster mitigation\. The study employs a qualitative approach using thematic Qur’anic exegesis \(tafsīr mawḍū‘ī\) as its primary methodological framework, complemented by an extensive literature review and empirical\-contextual analysis, integrated through three mutually reinforcing analytical layers: hermeneutical\-exegetical, comparative\-academic, and empirical\-contextual\. Collectively, they constitute a coherent normative system operating across four analytical dimensions: theological\-cosmological, etiological\-diagnostic, structural\-normative, and responsive\-preventive\. This framework exhibits a clear normative\-conceptual resonance with the empirical realities of the 2025 Sumatra–Aceh disaster, functioning as an ethical lens through which the structural drivers of the disaster can be critically diagnosed and evaluated, including widespread deforestation, failures in environmental governance, and the inequitable distribution of disaster risks\. The study concludes that the al\-mīzān conceptual framework provides a relevant normative\-theological instrument for addressing the underlying crisis of values that drives ecological degradation\. Its principal academic contribution lies in bridging the discourse between Islamic ecotheology and disaster mitigation studies, developing a methodological model that integrates thematic Qur’anic exegesis with empirical disaster data, and offering practical relevance for the formulation of value\-based disaster mitigation policies in disaster\-prone Muslim communities\.

## [Immunomodulation and biofilm disruption of piezoelectric materials in bone infection](../publications/574bd81e15286f066d72.md)

Zhen Wang; Kai Zheng; Yunfeng Tang; Zhen Zhang; Zhou Zhong; Dong Wang; Zijian Chen; Ye Wang; Zan Chen; Pengrui Feng; Wenjie Huang; Mengkun Liu; Yun Hao; Feng Yu; Guanglin Wang; Min Yi; Xiangtian Deng

Bone infection remains a persistent clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, antibiotic resistance, and impaired bone regeneration\. This manuscript focuses on the application of piezoelectric biomaterials in the treatment of bone infection and systematically elucidates their ability to convert in vivo mechanical stimulation into localized electrical signals and, in catalytically active systems, promote reactive oxygen species generation, thereby enabling efficient bacterial eradication and biofilm disruption\. We further synthesize recent evidence showing that piezoelectric stimulation can modulate the infection\-associated immune microenvironment and support osteogenesis and angiogenesis\. Rather than considering antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and regenerative effects as parallel functions, we integrate them into a stage\-adaptive therapeutic framework in which early biofilm disruption, bacterial eradication, and antimicrobial immune activation are followed by oxidative\-stress control, inflammation resolution, pro\-reparative immune remodeling, angiogenesis, and osteogenesis\. This pathophysiology\-oriented perspective highlights the potential of piezoelectric materials to coordinate the sequential therapeutic requirements of infected bone repair\. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives regarding material design optimization, mechanistic understanding, and clinical translation are discussed\.

## [A reliability\-oriented multimodal ensemble framework for fake news detection in armed conflict crisis situations](../publications/574dedb8359471d3b24a.md)

Farah Mohammad; Saad A\. Al\-Ahmadi; Fahman Saeed; Nazar Hussain

Social media platforms where people can post fake news threaten public trust, social stability, and the informed nature of people’s choices because of the rapid growth of fake news\. Multimedia content is widely accessible today and has added to the complication of misinformation through the use of multimedia \(including images, audio, video\) in combination with textual information, which often contain emotional language to create narratives that deceive consumers of information\. There has been much research over the last few years that has explored ways to detect fake news on multiple platforms, and while this research has resulted in the development of many multimodal fake news detection systems, the majority of these current methods rely on single\-classifier architectures and fairly simple fusion strategies that do not provide much in terms of robustness, generalization, or reliability in terms of detection under noisy and ambiguous conditions\. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel multimodal fake news detection framework that incorporates both textual and visual representation learning based on transformer models, affective feature modeling, and a stacked ensemble decision\-fusion approach\. The textual representation learning module in the proposed framework makes use of the XLM\-R model, whereas the visual representation learning module uses the ViT\-B/16 model\. Finally, the affective modeling module utilizes pretrained sentiment and emotion models for capturing and distinguishing the affective signals\. The predictions made by the multimodal representations are combined through the meta\-classifier to generate the final classification result\. In this regard, the proposed architecture enables robust cross\-modal reasoning and probabilistic calibration\. In what follows, we discuss the empirical results of extensive experiments conducted using four large\-scale benchmark datasets \(Fakeddit, Ukraine\-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval\), which show that the proposed multimodal detection architecture always outperforms the state\-of\-the\-art multimodal detection approaches proposed recently\. The proposed framework performs competitively on four benchmark datasets and achieves the accuracy of 94\.66%, 98\.23%, 98\.12%, and 97\.98% on Fakeddit, Ukraine\-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval, respectively\. Evaluations and ablation studies confirm the efficacy of the proposed multimodal ensemble approach under the given experimental settings\.

## [Artificial Intelligence, Synchrotron Imaging, and the Virtual Unwrapping of the Herculaneum Papyri](../publications/5780451fb5469741fc65.md)

Zen Revista

In the autumn of 79 CE, the eruption of Mount Vesuvius destroyed the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum and, in doing so, produced one of the most paradoxical archives in the history of the written word\. The pyroclastic flows that swept through Herculaneum carbonized the papyrus scrolls of a wealthy seaside villa, transforming an elegant private library into several hundred brittle lumps of charcoal\. That carbonization, ordinarily an agent of total destruction, turned out to be the very condition of the texts’ survival: hermetically sealed within their own combustion products and buried beneath approximately twenty meters of volcanic material, the rolls escaped the humidity, insects, mold, and human neglect that erased nearly every other large library of classical antiquity \[9, 17\]\. The result is the only large\-scale library to have survived from the Greco\-Roman world, containing hundreds of Greek and Latin scrolls, many of which preserve otherwise unknown philosophical treatises, including forty\-four works attributed to the Epicurean philosopher and poet Philodemus of Gadara \[17, 26\]\. For almost two and a half centuries, however, survival and readability remained fundamentally opposed\. The physical opening of a carbonized scroll, whether through mechanical devices, chemical softeners, or painstaking manual intervention, exposed its text at an irreversible cost, damaging or destroying the very object under investigation \[26\]\. The problem was compounded by the chemistry of the writing itself: the ink used in the Herculaneum scrolls is essentially carbon\-based and has a composition and density remarkably similar to those of the carbonized papyrus substrate\. Consequently, even when a scroll could be imaged externally, its writing remained radiographically invisible \[10, 11\]\. Reading a closed Herculaneum scroll therefore required overcoming a double impossibility: examining a fragile object without physically opening it and distinguishing black ink from a blackened substrate\. The past decade has progressively dismantled both barriers\. Between 2015 and 2026, a succession of breakthroughs, including X\-ray phase\-contrast tomography \[10\], the complete virtual unwrapping of a carbonized scroll \[16\], machine\-learning techniques for detecting carbon ink in computed tomography scans \[11\], and the open, prize\-based Vesuvius Challenge \[13\], transformed what had appeared to be an enduring impasse into a scalable research program\. Its most recent and dramatic milestone, announced on June 25, 2026, was the complete virtual unwrapping and reading of PHerc\. 1667, the first Herculaneum papyrus to be digitally unrolled and read from beginning to end without any physical opening \[1, 25\]\. In the same announcement, the project reported that more than seventy columns of text had been read from PHerc\. 172, a scroll whose title, Philodemus, On Vices, Book 1, had been recovered a year earlier, marking the first time the title of an unopened Herculaneum scroll had been read \[20, 24\]\. A companion video by Brazilian science communicator Izabela Anholett, published on YouTube Shorts on October 16, 2026, brought this story to a broad Portuguese\-speaking audience\. Its thumbnail is reproduced in Figure 1, and the video is cited throughout this study as an example of public science communication \[2\]\.

## [Mapping Research Approaches in Islamic Religious Education in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review](../publications/578197437489ac5c5626.md)

Muhammad Raihan As Syauqi; Arvial Ilham Fahrul Syah; Tedi Priatna; Bayu Bambang Nurfauji

This article aims to map research approaches in Islamic Religious Education studies in the era of generative artificial intelligence\. This study used a literature\-based scoping review method presented through descriptive\-narrative synthesis\. The literature was drawn from Indonesian scholarly publications published between 2021 and 2025 and selected based on inclusion and exclusion criteria related to Islamic Religious Education, research methodology, digital education, artificial intelligence, and generative artificial intelligence\. The review process focused on identifying research approaches, dominant themes, data sources, analytical techniques, and research gaps\. The findings show that Islamic Religious Education research has developed through qualitative field research, quantitative research, library research, research and development, systematic literature review, bibliometric analysis, and scoping review\. The findings also indicate that most studies still discuss AI as a learning and assessment tool, while studies on Generative AI in relation to research methodology, religious source validity, academic integrity, and ethical knowledge production remain limited\. Therefore, future Islamic Religious Education research should integrate methodological accuracy, pedagogical relevance, source validity, academic integrity, and ethical responsibility in responding to generative artificial intelligence\.

## [Integrating artificial intelligence and data science in environmental geotechnics: a review](../publications/57a12fcf5e1bf0e2be9e.md)

Anubhav Kumar; Abdel‐Mohsen O\. Mohamed; Evan K\. Paleologos; Brendan C\. O’Kelly; Amin Soltani; Moza Tahnoon Al Nahyan; Yanjie Song; Xiaohui Chen; Loc Nguyen; Theo S\. Sarris; Slobodan B\. Mickovski; Malaya Chetia; Devendra Narain Singh

Environmental geotechnics plays a critical role in the development of sustainable and resilient infrastructure systems, while addressing global challenges, such as climate change and resource depletion\. This review paper explores the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and data science \(DS\) within environmental geotechnics, and their potential to advance the field while supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\)\. By leveraging diverse data sources, including sensors, satellites, laboratory testing and case\-history projects, AI\-driven and data\-centric approaches can support evidence\-based decision making for the design, construction and maintenance of climate\-resilient infrastructure\. The integration of AI and DS enables engineers to efficiently interpret complex datasets, anticipate risks, optimise resource use and respond proactively to evolving ground conditions throughout infrastructure lifecycles\. These capabilities contribute to enhanced risk mitigation, environmental protection and sustainable infrastructure development\. The synergy between AI–DS and environmental geotechnics directly supports key SDGs, including clean water \(SDG 6\), industry, innovation and infrastructure \(SDG 9\), sustainable cities and communities \(SDG 11\) and climate action \(SDG 13\), thereby fostering more sustainable and adaptive approaches to infrastructure and environmental management\.

## [Three Essays on Information Disclosure and Risk Exposure in Alternative Investments](../publications/57a6a33dca99461eb15d.md)

Jue Wang

Information disclosure and risk exposure are central to decision\-making and risk management in financial markets\. Disclosures from alternative investment firms shape the information available to regulators and investors, influencing oversight and capital allocation, while firms’ risk exposure reflects their engagement in financial and social activities\. Hedge funds and Peer\-to\-Peer \(P2P\) marketplace platforms are key components of the alternative investment industry serving institutional and retail investors\. Hedge funds, as major institutional arbitrageurs that reduce market mispricing, managed $4\.3 trillion in assets in the first quarter of 2024\. P2P lending platforms both substitute for and complement traditional financial intermediaries and contribute to financial inclusion\. This dissertation examines how regulatory and voluntary disclosures, as well as exposure to public sentiment, affect risk and performance in alternative investments\. The first chapter, coauthored with William Goetzmann and Bing Liang, studies the 2011 Dodd\-Frank reform and hedge fund transparency\. New Form ADV disclosures improve the prediction of adverse operational events\. Using machine learning, we construct a unidimensional operational risk score from regulatory filings that predicts liquidation, leverage, performance, and fund flows\. Investor sensitivity to operational risk rises after the reform, indicating greater use of disclosed information\. Mandatory disclosure outperforms voluntary vendor data in identifying operational risk and has meaningful economic effects\. The second chapter, coauthored with Bing Liang, investigates whether hedge funds capitalize on fluctuations in ESG sentiment\. Using a global dataset of public ESG perceptions, we construct composite and pillar\-level sentiment indices\. Hedge funds actively time ESG sentiment, generating higher alpha and reducing downside risk\. Timing ability varies across strategies and aligns with sectoral and geographic exposures, indicating that funds incorporate values\-based sentiment into return generation and risk management\. The third chapter, coauthored with Wenyao Hu, examines loan listing practices in the P2P marketplace\. We find that Prosper disproportionately lists higher\-fee loans at the beginning of release periods to maximize revenue\. This strategy raises ethical concerns and highlights the need for greater transparency and regulatory oversight to ensure fair treatment of borrowers\.

## [Robust Navigation Corridor Extraction from Water Segmentation for Inland Autonomous Surface Vehicles](../publications/57ac3dfcd39362da7a9b.md)

Bareq W\. Fathi; Ahmed N\. Rasheed

Vision\-based perception is essential for autonomous surface vehicles operating in inland rivers, canals, and semi\-structured waterways\.This study presents an open\-loop, navigation\-oriented evaluation framework that transforms water\-segmentation masks into left and right boundaries, a centerline, corridor width, and exploratory plausibility and robustness indices\.All experiments were conducted on the same low\-resolution USVInland split of 293 training, 52 validation, and 173 test images at 640 × 320 resolution, using identical preprocessing, mask cleaning, corridor extraction, and per\-image evaluation procedures\.The evaluation includes a seed\-based heuristic, U\-Net, the proposed Edge U\-Net, and protocol\-controlled independent reproductions of two recent models, Fuse\-ResNet and ASSA\-ResNet\.Edge U\-Net achieved the strongest clean performance in the controlled comparison, with an IoU of 0\.964 \(95% CI: 0\.960\-0\.968\),a Boundary\-F1 score of 0\.685, and an average symmetric surface distance of 4\.18 pixels\.Paired image\-level analysis further showed that similar pixel\-overlap scores can coexist with meaningful differences in boundary displacement, centerline error, corridor\-width error, and failure behavior\.Weight\-sensitivity and failuretrigger analyses were therefore used to complement conventional segmentation metrics\.The proposed NCCS and Navigation Robustness Score are treated as heuristic descriptive indices rather than calibrated safety measures\.Overall, the framework provides a reproducible bridge between water segmentation and corridor\-oriented geometric evaluation, while not establishing obstacle\-aware or closed\-loop navigation safety\.

## [Pharmacist resource use across the United States: implications for teaching and practice](../publications/57b23e076165957ae0d1.md)

Rachel Whitney; Hilary Jasmin; Christopher Giuliano; Audrey Kostrzewa; Melissa Hunter; Christopher Wisniewski; Emily F\. Gorman

Objective: To analyze practicing pharmacists&\#x27; use of drug information \(DI\) resources in the United States\. Methods: An electronic survey was distributed to practicing US pharmacists through professional organization email lists and social media\. The survey questionnaire asked respondents which subscription\-based DI resources are provided through their employer, whether they personally pay for additional resources, how often they use subscription\-based resources, and other related questions\. Results: The survey received 430 responses, 387 of which were able to be fully analyzed\. The resources that respondents most frequently had access to through their employer were UpToDate \(77\.0%\), Lexicomp \(74\.9%\), and Micromedex \(62\.3%\)\. Many respondents \(40\.8%\) paid for subscriptions with personal funds, and 28\.9% reported never experiencing access issues due to payment barriers\. Respondents in community settings were more likely to have paid for resources with personal funds \(57\.1%, p&lt;0\.05\) and have less access to resources \(51\.4%, p&lt;0\.05\)\. In the open\-text responses, the most desired resources were point\-of\-care tools \(UpToDate\) and DI databases \(Lexicomp\)\. Conclusions: US pharmacists experience a varied level of access to DI resources through their employer\. Pharmacy educators should focus their instruction on resources that are the most accessible to practicing pharmacists\. Many, especially community pharmacists, pay out of pocket for desired resources, presenting an opportunity to advocate for increased resources\.

## [India and Latin America and the Caribbean: emerging partners in a shifting global economy](../publications/57b8c6f82171dcb680d6.md)



This document presents the proceedings of the international seminar entitled “India–Latin America and the Caribbean: emerging partners in a shifting global economy”, convened by the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean \(ECLAC\)\. The seminar examined the growing economic links between India and the region and their significance amid changes in trade, investment, production and technology\. The discussions highlighted the considerable scope for expanding and diversifying economic relations between the two partners, while also identifying persistent constraints related to market knowledge, connectivity, institutional presence and limited productive linkages\. The contributions in this volume seek to provide policymakers, business leaders and other stakeholders with analytical inputs to better understand these opportunities and constraints, identify areas of mutual interest and advance trade diversification, investment, productive and technological linkages, and institutional engagement between India and Latin America and the Caribbean\.

## [GOLD: Geometric Optimized Latent Diffusion for Structure\-Aware RNA Inverse Folding](../publications/57b934711d712b1d0df6.md)

Qi Si; Xuyang Liu; Penglei Wang; Shuo Su; Limei Han; Mengzhu Li; Xin Guo; Yuan Qi; Yuan Cheng

Designing RNA sequences that fold into specific 3D structures is a fundamental challenge in therapeutics\. Current RNA inverse folding methods typically condition on 3D backbone coordinates but the generation is limited to 1D discrete sequences\. This ignores the continuous side\-chain orientations, which are essential for overall structural stability\. To address this issue, we explicitly introduce side\-chain geometry into the RNA generative process\. Unlike co\-design frameworks that diffuse across separate raw spaces, we propose Geometric Optimized Latent Diffusion \(\\textbf\{GOLD\}\), which project sequence and structure into a unified latent manifold\. GOLD employs a novel GeoVAE to elegantly integrate discrete RNA sequences with continuous side\-chain angles\. By mapping these modalities into a single, smooth latent manifold, GOLD naturally facilitates a synergistic co\-diffusion process\. To enhance structural validity, we further introduce a training\-free, gradient\-guided sampling mechanism\. By decoding the generated sequence probabilities and side\-chain geometries into structures during the sampling process, we compute analytical gradients from physical constraints\. This dynamic feedback actively guides the generated sequence to a physically stable state\. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of GOLD, achieving state\-of\-the\-art performance across sequence recovery, secondary structure validity, and 3D foldability metrics\. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github\.com/darkflash03/GOLD\.

## [From Prohibition to Supervision: Licensed Betting in Uzbekistan and the Control of Payment Flows, Financial Crime and Consumer Harm](../publications/57bacae4c28eea719e68.md)

Sardor Khushvaktov

In July 2026 Uzbekistan issued its first licences for online bookmaking, under a framework adopted in 2024\. This article argues that the reform is better understood as a shift from prohibition to supervision than as the legalisation of a new activity, because betting demand, and the payment channels serving it, existed throughout the period of prohibition\. Using doctrinal legal analysis, comparative regulatory analysis and a structured review of 30 documentary sources, including Uzbek legislation, Central Bank of Uzbekistan materials, regulatory reports from Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, the United Kingdom and Australia, and recent public\-health and household\-finance research, the article examines what licensing changes for anti\-money laundering \(AML\), fraud prevention and consumer protection, and what it leaves unresolved\. It finds that Uzbekistan&\#x27;s centralised register of bets and players gives the state an unusually strong technical basis for supervision, but that its effectiveness will depend on controls not yet clearly required: alignment between account holder and payment instrument, closed\-loop payments, a monitoring role for banks, attention to credit\-funded gambling, binding affordability limits and market\-wide self\-exclusion\. The article proposes that the reform be evaluated against three outcomes: a shrinking illegal market, more transparent financial flows, and contained consumer and social harm\. It also recommends that baseline data be collected now, before those outcomes can no longer be measured against a starting point\.

## [Integrating machine learning and statistical techniques to evaluate postural stability during hypoxia](../publications/57bcf93bbcca35afa957.md)

Yasaman Baradaran; Abishek Shrestha; Jonathan French; Maryam Ghahramani

This study investigates the effects of hypoxic altitude on postural stability using statistical analysis and feature\-selection\-based machine learning\. Thirty\-one healthy participants were exposed to four simulated altitudes \(sea level, 3,000 m, 4,000 m, and 5,000 m\) in a randomized, blinded protocol within a normobaric chamber, with arterial oxygen saturation \( SpO 2 \) confirming hypoxic exposure\. Participants completed eight standing conditions designed to manipulate visual, vestibular, and somatosensory inputs\. For each condition, 15 postural sway measures were extracted from center of pressure signals\. Statistical analysis indicates that hypoxia\-induced changes in postural stability are multidimensional and are most detectable under conditions that increase sensory integration demands, particularly foam based and tandem stance tasks\. Moderate hypoxia increased sway variability and disrupted automatic postural control, whereas more severe hypoxia under complex task conditions elicited a constrained motor strategy\. In the machine learning approach, four tree\-based ensemble classifiers, including Extra Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, and XGBoost, were employed for altitude classification using the selected postural sway features\. A feature\-selection framework using Extra Trees feature importance and participant\-grouped nested cross\-validation was implemented\. The optimized Extra Trees classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 70% using 27 selected features\. The selected features highlighted the contribution of specific sway characteristics that were not fully captured by conventional univariate metrics\. These findings show that moderate hypoxia, in sensory challenging environments, induces detectable multidimensional postural instability before the onset of conventionally recognized symptoms\. Our results highlight the importance of task selection and multivariate analysis for detecting subtle impairments\. These findings have potential applications in aerospace environments\.

## [Digital Transformation for Accounting Students in Facing the Development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in the World of Accounting](../publications/57cdb3378a62df2adc71.md)

Syarifah Aini

The development of digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) technology has brought significant changes in the world of accounting, especially in the process of recording transactions, preparing financial statements, digital audits, and fraud detection\. This research aims to analyze digital transformation for accounting students in facing the development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in the world of accounting\. The research method used is Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) with a thematic synthesis approach to scientific articles obtained from Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate, and Scopus for the 2024–2026 period\. Of the 80 articles found, 15 articles that met the inclusion criteria were obtained and analyzed further\. The results of the study show that digital transformation has a major impact on the accounting profession with the increasing use of accounting software, cloud computing, blockchain, and AI in business processes\. Accounting students are required not only to understand accounting theory, but also to have digital competencies such as mastery of accounting information systems, data analysis, and the use of AI\-based technology\. Factors that affect students&\#x27; readiness to face AI include digital literacy, educational curriculum, technology access, and adaptability\. In addition to presenting challenges in the form of increasing job competition and the need for technology skills, AI also opens up new opportunities in the accounting profession such as digital auditors, financial data analysts, and information systems consultants\. Therefore, universities need to update the curriculum to be more relevant to technological developments and industrial needs in the digital era\.

## [QD\-Rec: Open\-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality\-Diversity](../publications/57d39c7620614617e7bd.md)

Takashi Ishida; Taro Makino; Issa Sugiura

Open\-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self\-improving agents\. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision\-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not\. In high\-stakes decisions, e\.g\., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well\-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list\. We formalize open\-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high\-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural\-language reason why the item fits the needs of a decision maker\. We propose QD\-Rec, a quality\-\-diversity method that selects items with a contextual bandit and generates hypotheses with a foundation model from earlier ones kept in an archive as stepping stones\. A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor\. Across M&amp;A, customer targeting, and paper and book recommendation, QD\-Rec gives the highest mean quality and builds the largest archive in most settings\.

## [AgriSense: IoT\-Driven Precision Agriculture for National Food Sustainability and Development](../publications/57d85a346fa156c5a6a2.md)

Innocent Uzougbo Onwuegbuzie

Precision agriculture integrates digital technologies to improve agricultural resource management, productivity, and sustainability, while the Internet of Things \(IoT\) enables real\-time monitoring of soil and environmental conditions through connected sensors\. In Nigeria, inefficient water and fertilizer use, declining soil health, climate variability, and limited access to timely agricultural information constrain sustainable food production\. This study presents AgriSense, an IoT\-driven precision agriculture platform designed to support data\-informed farm management under Nigerian agricultural conditions\. The study adopts a mixed\-method research framework incorporating descriptive, experimental, and analytical approaches, with proposed data sources including IoT sensor measurements, farmer surveys and interviews, field observations, and relevant weather information\. The AgriSense platform integrates soil\-moisture, nitrogen\-phosphorus\-potassium \(N\-P\-K\), soil\-pH, temperature, and humidity monitoring with farm and field management, sensor\-status tracking, automated alerts, agronomic recommendations, and reporting functions\. The demonstrated interface represents agricultural fields and crops across Asaba Demonstration Farm, Jos Highland Farm, and Sokoto Smart Farm\. Its threshold\-based alerts identify conditions associated with low soil moisture, low nitrogen, acidic soil, high temperature, and sensor connectivity faults, linking selected conditions to recommended management actions\. The available demonstration establishes the platform’s integrated monitoring and decision\-support functionality\. However, because the interface identifies its environment as a live simulation, the displayed information does not independently establish improvements in crop yield, input\-use efficiency, soil health, or farmer income\. The study provides a technological foundation for subsequent field validation of IoT\-enabled precision agriculture and its potential contribution to sustainable food security in Nigeria\.

## [Trim the Wait, Open the Gait : Better ED Rate](../publications/57e1489ceaba89d5830b.md)

Manish Gaur; Suvasish Chakraverty; Avik Sharma

Objectives: Emergency Department \(ED\) length of stay \(LOS; EDLOS\) is a widely accepted indicator of healthcare quality, patient flow, and operational efficiency\. Prolonged EDLOS contributes to overcrowding, treatment delays, increased morbidity and mortality, and reduced patient satisfaction\. Continuous monitoring of EDLOS is therefore essential for quality improvement in emergency care\. Material and Methods: A retrospective quality\-improvement study was conducted in the ED of a tertiary care multispecialty hospital\. Data from August–September 2024 were analyzed as the pre\-intervention phase \( n =3,678\), while August–September 2025 represented the post\-intervention phase \( n =3,710\)\. Eligible patients included all ED attendees with a length of stay greater than 30 minutes\. Interventions implemented following the initial review included expansion of bed capacity, increased physician staffing, introduction of ED coordinators, and focused monitoring of diagnostic and consultation turnaround times\. Average EDLOS and compliance with institutional benchmarks were compared between the pre\-intervention and post\-intervention periods\. Results: A total of 7,388 ED encounters were included in the study\. Average EDLOS decreased from 3\.05 and 2\.42 hours during August and September 2024 to 1\.08 and 1\.25 hours during August and September 2025, respectively\. Mean EDLOS improved from 2\.74 hours during the pre\-intervention phase to 1\.17 hours post\-intervention, representing a reduction of 57\.3%\. Compliance with the institutional benchmark of EDLOS less than four hours improved from 78% during the pre\-intervention period to 93% following the implementation of operational interventions\. Conclusion: Targeted operational interventions significantly improved ED efficiency and reduced EDLOS\. Expansion of capacity, improved staffing, multidisciplinary coordination, and continuous performance monitoring contributed to sustained improvements in patient flow and service delivery\.
