## [The impact of the attacks on trust in the use of social media and Service sites in Libya](../publications/57e53454d1df6c52aa4f.md)

Radwan M Marwan

مع تزايد استخدام المواقع الإلكترونية بما في ذلك منصات التواصل الاجتماعي، والخدمات المالية عبر الإنترنت، والأسواق الإلكترونية تزايدت أيضاً الهجمات التي تستهدفها\. ويستخدم المهاجمون أساليب متنوعة، مثل التصيد الاحتيالي، والهندسة الاجتماعية، والرسائل المزعجة \(Spam\)، وهجمات حجب الخدمة \(DoS\)، والبرمجيات الخبيثة، وبرمجيات الفدية، واستغلال الثغرات الأمنية غير المكتشفة سابقاً \(Zero\-day exploits\)\. ونتيجة لذلك، ارتفع عدد الهجمات والانتهاكات الأمنية التي يتعرض لها المستخدمون\. يتناول هذا البحث أنواع هذه الهجمات وتأثيرها على مستخدمي الإنترنت، وذلك من خلال جمع بيانات من طلاب تكنولوجيا المعلومات في المعهد العالي للعلوم والتقنية بتاجوراء وجامعة طرابلس و بعض المستخدمين من دوي الخبرة في هدا المجال\. وتهدف الدراسة إلى تحديد معدل تكرار هذه الهجمات وشدتها داخل مجتمعنا، وقياس ثقة المستخدمين في استخدام حساباتهم عند مواجهة مثل هذه التهديدات، وتقييم كيفية تفاوت تأثير الهجوم علي المستخدمين بناءً على نوع الموقع الإلكتروني المعني\. علاوة على ذلك، تسعى الدراسة إلى قياس مدى وعي الأفراد وفهمهم للمخاطر المرتبطة بهذه الهجمات، مما يدعم عملية اتخاذ القرار الرامية إلى رفع مستوى الوعي والحد من العواقب السلبية لهذه الهجمات على المجتمع\.

## [Effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial](../publications/57e8a8b27bc1e422cb9f.md)

Zhiying Ma; Yanyu Lin; Zheng Zhu; Zhenbo CAO

Background Cardiovascular disease is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\), with increased risk closely associated with vascular dysfunction\. Exercise is an effective strategy for improving vascular health, but whether exercise timing influences long\-term vascular adaptations in patients with T2DM remains unclear\. In this study, we investigated the effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with T2DM\. Methods Sixty\-six older adults with T2DM were randomised to morning exercise, evening exercise, or control \(n = 22 each\)\. The exercise groups received 12 weeks of online moderate\-intensity aerobic and resistance exercises, three times per week\. The morning group exercised from 9:00 to 10:10, and the evening group from 19:00 to 20:10\. The control group maintained their usual lifestyle and attended weekly health education sessions without structured exercise\. Blood pressure, brachial\-ankle pulse wave velocity \(baPWV\), flow\-mediated vasodilation \(FMD\) and plasma nitric oxide \(NO\) levels were assessed at baseline and post\-intervention\. Outcomes were analysed using two\-way repeated\-measures analysis of variance, with exploratory analyses directly comparing the two exercise groups\. Results Fifty\-eight participants were included in the final analysis \(morning, n = 20; evening, n = 19; control, n = 19\)\. Significant group × time interactions were observed for FMD, baPWV, systolic blood pressure \(SBP\), mean arterial pressure \(MAP\), and plasma NO \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Both exercise groups increased FMD and reduced SBP, MAP, and baPWV from baseline \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Plasma NO increased significantly following the evening exercise \(p = 0\.003\), whereas no significant changes were observed following the morning exercise \(p = 0\.722\)\. At post\-intervention, the evening group exhibited lower MAP \(p = 0\.012\) and higher FMD \(p = 0\.019\) and NO levels \(p = 0\.012\) than controls\. Exploratory analyses showed a greater baPWV reduction with evening exercise \(group × time interaction, p = 0\.034\)\. The increase in plasma NO was numerically greater with evening exercise, although the interaction was not statistically significant \(p = 0\.051\)\. Conclusions Exercise timing may influence vascular adaptations in older adults with T2DM, with evening exercise potentially offering additional benefits, particularly for arterial stiffness\. Clinical trial registration https://www\.chictr\.org\.cn/showproj\.html?proj=200163 , identifier ChiCTR2300073737\.

## [Применение RFID в сфере культуры: экономический эффект и опыт внедрения](../publications/57ecddca82d14fd85fa0.md)

Кристина Валерьевна Апокина; А\.А\. Муфтахова

Статья посвящена комплексному исследованию процесса внедрения технологии радиочастотной идентификации \(RFID\) в деятельность учреждений сферы культуры\. В фокусе анализа находятся конкретные примеры применения технологии в музейных, библиотечных и выставочных пространствах мира\. Научная новизна работы заключается в обосновании подхода к внедрению RFID в организациях сферы культуры и определении на основе анализа реализованных проектов ожидаемого положительного экономического эффекта от адаптации технологии\. Эмпирической базой выступили научные статьи, данные мировой и российской статистики, использовались общенаучные методы\. Сформирована обобщающая таблица, которая наглядно демонстрирует опыт учреждений культуры мира и позволяет проследить связь между целями внедрения и достигаемым экономическим результатом\. The article is devoted to a comprehensive study of the process of introducing radio frequency identification technology into the activities of cultural institutions\. The analysis focuses on specific application examples in the museum, library and exhibition spaces of the world\. The scientific novelty of the work is to substantiate the approach to the introduction of RFID in cultural organizations and to determine, based on the analysis of implemented projects, the expected positive economic effect from the adaptation of technology in the field of culture\. The empirical basis was scientific articles, data from world and Russian statistics, general scientific methods were used\. A summary table has been created that clearly demonstrates the experience of cultural institutions around the world and allows us to trace the relationship between the goals of implementation and the economic result achieved\.

## [Gut microbiota and type 2 diabetes: implications for personalized nutrition and emerging therapeutic strategies](../publications/57edf8f1737cbd1ca02e.md)

Shweta Joshi; Dashrath Bhati; Ankita Dobhal; Ravneet Kaur; Rakhita Moger; Sanjay Kumar

Type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\) is a complex metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance, impaired glucose regulation, and chronic low\-grade inflammation\. Over the past decade, the gut microbiota \(GM\) has emerged as an important determinant of metabolic health, with increasing evidence showing that gut microbial dysbiosis and its associated metabolites influence intestinal barrier function, immune regulation, insulin sensitivity, and glucose homeostasis\. Although previous studies have examined either GM, dietary interventions, or probiotic supplementation in T2DM, a comprehensive study linking microbial metabolites with personalized nutrition \(PN\) and emerging microbiota\-based therapeutic strategies remains lacking\. This review addresses this gap by discussing the mechanistic roles of important gut microbial metabolites, such as short\-chain fatty acids \(SCFAs\), lipopolysaccharides \(LPS\), trimethylamine\-N\-oxide, indolepropionic acid \(IPA\), and bile acids \(BAs\), in the development and progression of T2DM\. It further describes how dietary strategies, including high\-fiber and prebiotic\-rich diets, probiotics, synbiotics, polyphenol\-rich foods, and PN, improve glycemic control and metabolic health\. Recent advances in microbiota\-targeted interventions, including postbiotics, next\-generation probiotics, engineered probiotics, and fecal microbiota, are also discussed along with their therapeutic potential and existing clinical limitations\. By combining mechanistic insights with nutritional and therapeutic perspectives, this review provides a single framework for understanding the diet\-GM\-host metabolic axis and offers future directions for developing microbiome\-informed precision nutrition strategies for the prevention and management of T2DM\.

## [High\-confidence predictors of childhood anemia in Ghana: a parallel multilevel and machine learning analysis of the 2022 demographic and health survey](../publications/57f42153d1cc7d744cd8.md)

Johnson Sam; Ivan Addae Mensah

Abstract Background Childhood anemia still remains a major public health concern in Ghana, with a national prevalence of 49\.0%\. Understanding this burden using a combined multilevel and machine learning framework is essential for designing effective interventions\. Objective This study used a parallel multilevel and machine learning framework to identify high\-confidence predictors of childhood anemia among children \(6–59 months\) in Ghana using the 2022 Demographic and Health Survey \( n = 3,858 children nested in 235 districts after excluding districts with fewer than two children\)\. Methods We fitted a two\-level random\-intercept logistic regression \(children nested within districts\) and three machine learning classifiers \(Random Forest, XGBoost, Elastic Net\), using district\-grouped 70/30 train–test splitting to avoid leakage across the level\-2 unit of analysis\. SHAP \(SHapley Additive exPlanations\) values were computed for all three classifiers; the values reported here are drawn primarily from Random Forest, with concordance against XGBoost and Elastic Net assessed as a robustness check \(Spearman’s ρ = 0\.79–0\.87, all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. For multi\-category predictors, SHAP importance was aggregated across category dummies before ranking\. Predictors significant in the multilevel model \( p &lt; 0\.05\) and ranked among the top 15 by aggregated mean \|SHAP\| were classified as high\-confidence; sensitivity of this classification to the top\-15 cutoff is reported\. Results The prevalence of childhood anemia was 49\.0% \(95% CI: 46\.4%\-51\.6%\), with significant district\-level variation \(ICC = 6\.2%\)\. Nine high\-confidence predictors were identified; child age, mean temperature, child sex, maternal anemia, maternal age, birth order, population density, stunting and fever\. Six district\-level contextual variables, nightlights, elevation, rainfall, enhanced vegetation index, malaria prevalence, and travel time, were not significant in the random intercept model but ranked among the top 15 predictors in the SHAP analysis\. This divergence remains an unresolved finding warranting further investigation rather than being attributed to a specific mechanism\. Elastic Net achieved the highest AUC \(0\.727, 95% CI: 0\.702–0\.755\), followed by Random Forest \(0\.707, 95% CI: 0\.680–0\.736\) and XGBoost \(0\.685, 95% CI: 0\.659–0\.712\)\. Ho Municipal in the Volta region, Ahanta West district in the Western region, Nkwanta South in the Oti region, and Wa West in the Upper West region were identified as the districts with the highest odds of anemia using the caterpillar plot\. Conclusions One out of every two children \(6–59 months\) in Ghana suffers from Anemia\. The hybrid approach identified child age maternal anemia, maternal age, stunting and mean temperature as key predictors, while revealing nonlinear contextual effects\. High risk districts provide actionable evidence for geographically targeted, climate\-resilient, and multisectoral interventions\.

## [Machine Learning Prediction of Blood Loss from Arterial Waveform Feature Analysis in a Nonhuman Primate Hemorrhage Model](../publications/5805beea55c5bfe359d0.md)

Jose M\. Gonzalez; Carmen Hinojosa‐Laborde; Víctor A\. Convertino; R\. Lyle Hood; Eric J\. Snider

Hemorrhage is the leading cause of preventable death in trauma, yet traditional vital signs can fail to detect early blood loss due to physiological compensatory mechanisms\. Objective, continuous monitoring of hemorrhage progression remains an unmet clinical need\. This study developed and validated a machine learning model of percent estimated blood loss in a nonhuman primate hemorrhage model\. Adult male baboons underwent controlled stepwise hemorrhage to approximately 25% blood loss while high\-fidelity arterial waveform and blood loss data were captured\. Morphological waveform features were extracted, and a Gradient Boosting model was developed using leave\-one\-subject\-out cross\-validation\. A 10 s window with 10 features achieved a mean coefficient of determination of 0\.81 and mean absolute error of 2\.5%\. On three independently held\-out subjects, per\-subject coefficient of determination ranged from 0\.75 to 0\.94 while mean absolute error ranged from 1\.4% to 3\.3%\. Notably, percent estimated blood loss detected hemorrhage a median of 8\.1 min before sustained blood pressure decline, at approximately 7% blood loss while systolic pressure remained stable\. These findings indicate that arterial waveform morphology can enable accurate, continuous blood loss estimation and may provide early warning before hemorrhage becomes detectable through conventional vital sign monitoring in this preclinical model\.

## [Schisandrin B attenuates ischemic acute kidney injury in a CTR1\-dependent manner by inhibiting cuproptosis](../publications/580602f402ed09de867d.md)

Lirong Lin; Shahong He; Xujia Yang; Luquan Zheng; Wei Tan; Ke Li; Jurong Yang

Background Acute kidney injury \(AKI\) remains a global health challenge with high mortality rates and no targeted pharmacotherapy\. Although regulated cell death \(RCD\) drives renal tubular epithelial cell \(RTEC\) injury, the involvement of cuproptosis, a copper\-triggered RCD characterized by lipoylated protein aggregation and iron\-sulfur cluster loss, remains unexplored in acute kidney injury \(AKI\)\. Methods Integrated single\-cell transcriptomics \(GSE180420\), a human renal biopsy cohort \( n = 22\), ischemia\-reperfusion \(I/R\) mouse models, and hypoxia\-reoxygenation \(H/R\) cellular models were used to characterize cuproptosis\. Multi\-omics profiling, molecular docking, and CTR1 \(encoded by SLC31A1 \)\-specific siRNA knockdown were used to explore the mechanism of action of Schisandrin B \(SchB\)\. Results Single\-cell RNA sequencing of murine ischemia–reperfusion \(I/R\) kidneys revealed that cuproptosis was a predominant RCD modality, accounting for approximately one\-third of all regulated cell death events in renal tubular epithelial cells \(RTECs\)\. This finding was corroborated in human AKI biopsies and in murine I/R kidneys, where the key cuproptosis proteins ferredoxin 1 \(FDX1\) and copper transporter 1 \(CTR1\) were markedly upregulated, accompanied by significant copper accumulation and tubule injury\. Under the tested conditions, SchB exhibited protective effects at least comparable to those of the classical copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate \(TTM\) in attenuating copper\-dependent cytotoxicity in vitro \. SchB\-regulated differentially expressed genes were significantly enriched in glutathione metabolism, p53 signaling, cellular senescence, and PI3K\-Akt pathways\. Molecular docking predicted a direct interaction between SchB and CTR1 \(binding energy −5\.1 kcal/mol\)siRNA\-mediated depletion of CTR1 partially abolished the protective effects of SchB against copper\-induced RTEC death, indicating that CTR1 may be required, at least in part, for SchB\-induced cytoprotection in RTECs\. Conclusion This study identifies cuproptosis as a predominant and previously unrecognized RCD pathway in ischemic AKI\. SchB inhibits cuproptosis in a CTR1\-dependent manner\. These findings provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of this natural product as a potential therapeutic candidate for ischemic kidney disease\.

## [Personalized genomic landscape of prostate cancer in African American men reveals novel drivers and therapeutic opportunities](../publications/580c6b05c150d31c2526.md)

Shanta Murthy; Katie Fago; James Knight; Keith J\. Kowalczyk; Ryan Andrew Hankins; Gaurav Bandi; Anatoly Dritschilo; Mira Jung

African American \(AA\) men experience disproportionately high prostate cancer incidence and mortality\. Despite this disparity, current genomic repositories are predominantly derived from European populations, and studies using archived tissues are often limited by stromal contamination\. We sought to characterize the high\-resolution somatic mutational landscape of AA prostate cancer using a high\-fidelity, patient\-matched model system to identify population\-specific drivers and therapeutic targets\. We performed whole\-genome sequencing \(WGS\) on 10 matched pairs of primary cell cultures derived from prostate tumors and adjacent non\-malignant tissues of AA patients\. Our analyses revealed a complex, heterogeneous landscape characterized by significant genomic instability, including frequent chromothripsis and kataegis signatures\. Mutation hotspots were concentrated on chromosomes 1, 2, 3, and X, with the highest mutation density on chromosome 17\. Functionally impactful mutations were identified in critical oncogenic pathways, including chromatin remodeling \(CHD1, ARID1A, ATRX, KDM6A\) and DNA damage response \(ATM, BRCA1/2, RAD51\)\. Additionally, we identified potentially novel candidate mutations unique to this AA cohort, distinct from those in European\-centric datasets\. This study provides a foundational, patient\-specific WGS dataset derived from African American prostate cancer cell models\. The identification of high\-frequency actionable alterations in epigenetic and DNA repair pathways highlights the utility of this renewable resource for developing tailored therapeutic interventions and addressing racial disparities in prostate cancer outcomes\.

## [Machine Learning and Post\-Hoc Feature Attribution for Predicting Cardiac MRI Motion Artifacts: A Retrospective Cohort Study](../publications/5815d4e4b478f8548ff1.md)

Ya Li; Qiuyi Cai; Lin Li; LI Jianlin; Dun Pan; Jian Liu

Anxiety\-induced motion artifacts frequently compromise image quality during non\-sedated cardiac magnetic resonance imaging \(CMR\), leading to rescans and increased healthcare burdens\. This retrospective cohort study hypothesized that combining multidimensional psychological and physiological indicators could accurately predict artifact occurrence\. Baseline data from 514 adult patients, encompassing 15 clinical features, were systematically analyzed\. Four machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\)\. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting model demonstrated the highest discriminative ability \(AUC = 0\.875\)\. To provide clinical transparency, SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis was applied, revealing that state anxiety \(evaluated via the State\-Trait Anxiety Inventory State subscale, STAI\-State\), maximum breath\-hold duration, and heart rate variability were primarily associated with artifact risk\. The novelty of this approach lies in uncovering non\-linear threshold effects\-such as a sharp risk escalation when STAI\-State scores exceeded 45\-and complex interactions between physical capacity and claustrophobia\. In conclusion, this interpretable machine learning framework offers a robust tool for patient\-specific risk stratification, suggesting that preemptive and targeted nursing interventions could be optimized based on individualized algorithmic predictions\.

## [УДОСКОНАЛЕННЯ СИСТЕМИ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯ БЕЗПЕКИ СУДНОПЛАВСТВА В УМОВАХ ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ ТА АВТОМАТИЗАЦІЇ МОРСЬКОГО ТРАНСПОРТУ](../publications/581eb9fd7eaa02296155.md)

У статті розглянуто сучасні підходи до забезпечення безпеки судноплавства в умовах цифровізації та автоматизації морського транспорту\. Проаналізовано вплив розвитку електронної навігації, інтегрованих навігаційних систем, автоматизованих засобів попередження зіткнень, технологій S\-100, штучного інтелекту та автономного судноплавства на процес прийняття навігаційних рішень\. Обґрунтовано необхідність комплексного підходу до взаємодії судноводія та автоматизованих систем\. Запропоновано структурну модель сучасної системи забезпечення безпеки судноводіння, яка передбачає послідовне виконання функцій збору та інтеграції навігаційної інформації, оцінювання навігаційної обстановки, визначення рівня ризику, прийняття рішення, реалізації маневру та контролю його результатів\.

## [University Campus Vitality \(UCV\): A Bibliometric Analysis \(2015–2025\)](../publications/5826ecf978584b74d9f8.md)

杨露露; Putri Haryati Ibrahim; Khalilah Zakariya

University campus vitality \(UCV\) has attracted increasing attention across campus planning, built\-environment, sustainability, and student\-oriented research; however, its knowledge structure remains conceptually fragmented, and the relationships among UCV, campus spatial planning \(CSP\), and commercial space \(CS\) have not been systematically synthesised\. This study examines the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field between 2015 and 2025 through a multi\-database bibliometric analysis\. Database\-specific filtering retained 1,161 records \(WOS = 359; Scopus = 354; CNKI = 448\), which were reduced through crossdatabase deduplication and relevance screening to a final integrated corpus of 803 publications\. Bibliometrix and VOSviewer were used to analyse publication patterns, conceptual structures, keyword networks, and thematic evolution, complemented by CiteSpace reference co\-citation and timeline analyses of the WOS subset\. The results show an overall increase in publication activity, with China and the United States as the principal geographical contributors\. The conceptual structure is centered on campus planning and university campus, with interconnected themes involving spatial configuration, public space, sustainability, students, walkability, resilience, landscape, and environmental quality\. Temporal analyses further reveal a persistent planningoriented core accompanied by increasing diversification toward human\-centered, behavioural, and sustainability\-related concerns\. Notably, CS does not emerge as a comparably dominant independent theme, indicating that its explicit integration within the UCV–CSP knowledge structure remains comparatively underdeveloped\. The study therefore clarifies the asymmetrical development of UCV, CSP, and CS and provides a bibliometric basis for future empirical research on the role of commercial space within university campus spatial and functional systems\. Keywords: university campus vitality; campus spatial planning; commercial space

## [IMPLEMENTASI GAMIFIKASI DIGITAL DALAM PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM UNTUK PENGUATAN KETERLIBATAN MURID DI SD NEGERI 2 TUNGKAL ILIR](../publications/582aeeda4ba68c4aceb2.md)

Meli Puspita; Cukup Islamiarso; Mardiah Astuti; Yuniar

The implementation of digital gamification in Islamic Religious Education \(IRE\) learning represents an instructional approach that can provide a more interactive learning experience while supporting student engagement at SD Negeri 2 Tungkal Ilir\. The study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design\. Data were collected through observations of learning activities, interviews with the IRE teacher and students, and documentation of learning activities involving digital gamification\. Data were analyzed interactively through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing\. Data validity was established through source and technique triangulation\. The findings indicate that digital gamification was implemented by integrating game elements into IRE learning, including points, interactive quizzes, challenges, rewards, and feedback\. These elements provided a more interactive learning experience and created opportunities for students to participate actively in learning activities\. Student engagement was demonstrated through active participation, attention to learning materials, willingness to answer questions, involvement in completing challenges, and enthusiasm during learning activities\. The implementation of digital gamification also encouraged interaction between teachers and students as well as among students throughout the learning process\. However, its implementation faced several challenges, particularly limited access to digital devices, unstable internet connectivity, differences in students’ digital literacy skills, and learning time management\. The findings suggest that digital gamification can serve as an instructional strategy in Islamic Religious Education learning to support student engagement when it is designed in alignment with learning objectives, students’ characteristics, technological availability, and the school context\.

## [Selective Image Enhancement for Robust GentleBoost Face Detection under Uncontrolled Illumination](../publications/5834c499235a78aaabb2.md)

Alyaa Qusay Aloraibi

Although significant progress has been achieved in computer vision, detecting faces under different lighting conditions and poses remains challenging\. This issue is particularly crucial for biometric and surveillance applications, where lighting cannot be controlled\. While the machine learning based Gentle Boost cascade provides stability benefits, it has not been studied extensively in face detection research\. This paper introduces Selective Image Enhancement \(SIE\), a lightweight preprocessing technique designed to enhance image quality prior to detection\. SIE operates on the \(L\) channel of the Commission Internationale de l&\#x27;Éclairage CIELAB \(LAB\) color space, breaking down the \(L\) channel into illumination and detail components\. It employs Gaussian filtering, gamma correction, and thresholding to selectively enhance image pixels while minimizing artifacts\. Features are extracted using Local Binary Patterns Histogram \(LBPH\) and then classified with the Gentle Boost cascade, trained on the CelebA dataset and evaluated on 500 images\. A comparative evaluation was conducted against gamma correction and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization \(CLAHE\)\. The proposed SIE method achieved 0\.9800 recall, 0\.9684 precision, and an F1\-score value of 0\.9742, with an average IoU of 0\.7161 ± 0\.0938\. Although CLAHE achieved higher recall and F1\-score value, SIE obtained the highest mean IoU among the evaluated enhancement methods\. The unenhanced images achieved a slightly higher IoU of 0\.7193 ±0\.0926\. These results indicate that SIE provides competitive detection performance and a balance between image enhancement quality and localization accuracy\.

## [Modeling mini electric vehicle purchase using SOR and task technology fit: evidence from the third\-tier city of Liuzhou, China](../publications/5835e9bc43f5f95a0693.md)

Jialin Li; Fowokemi Alaba Ogedengbe; Ammar Bani Doumi

Technology has been revolutionizing the transportation sector through electric vehicles \(EVs\)\. Statistics and data have revealed that EV usage is currently growing globally\. This is due to its many benefits, such as its contribution to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\)\. Hence, this study examines people&\#x27;s intentions to purchase Mini EVs\. Based on positivist epistemology, this research is quantitative in nature\. A framework, grounded in Stimulus\-Organism\-Response \(SOR\) and Task\-Technology Fit \(TTF\), was proposed with three research objectives and 7 hypotheses\. The framework was tested using survey data from 308 respondents in a third\-tier region in China\. Analysis was conducted using structural equation modeling, and the result revealed that the proposed framework was validated\. This research shows that factors such as the perceived price and design aesthetics influence the TTF and purchase intention\. The novelty of this paper lies in its focus on Mini EVs \(specifically the Wuling Hongguang\), the third tier \(developing economy\) in China, the integration of SOR and TTF into the framework, and the mediating impact of TTF on the postulated hypotheses\. All of which are current gaps in EV academics\. The major limitation is the examination of only a few variables, which could be expanded upon in future research\.

## [Adaptive Reinforcement Learning\-Based Dynamic Scheduling for Steel Reheating Furnaces: A Scalable Queue\-Driven Framework](../publications/58505d7d73aa82adf99c.md)

Yanhe Jia; aowen liu

Abstract Reheating furnace scheduling problem \(RFSP\) is a critical issue in hot\-rolling production, where stochastic order arrivals and service processes pose significant challenges to production efficiency and cost management\. The RFSP is plagued by inherent stochasticity in order arrivals and service times\. This study proposes an adaptive queue\-driven dynamic adjustment scheduling \(AQ\-DAS\) based on reinforcement learning for dynamic reheating furnace scheduling\. The system is modeled as an M/PH/C queueing system and formulated as a Markov decision process \(MDP\)\. By incorporating adaptive learning\-rate and adaptive exploration mechanisms into Q\-learning, the proposed method aims to minimize long\-term operating costs while balancing queueing, idle, and switching costs\. Simulation experiments are conducted to compare AQ\-DAS with CBS2, Q\-learning, SARSA, Double Q\-learning, DQN, and PPO\. For the five\-furnace system, AQ\-DAS achieves the lowest mean total operating cost, reducing it by 76\.6%, 12\.5%, 43\.6%, 37\.9%, 10\.2%, and 18\.6%, respectively\. It also maintains competitive throughput and high furnace utilization and substantially reducing switching frequency\. Sensitivity analysis shows that AQ\-DAS remains competitive under variations in the relative weights of queueing, idle, and switching costs\. Robustness experiments under demand fluctuations and equipment disturbances demonstrate low ARPDs of 6\.04%, 13\.47%, and 10\.84% for demand, equipment, and overall conditions, respectively\. Furthermore, scalability experiments with 5–20 furnaces demonstrate that AQ\-DAS maintains its cost advantage as the system scale increases, with cost reductions ranging from 8\.8% to 79\.5% across the benchmark methods, while requiring substantially less training time than DQN and PPO\. The proposed framework provides a scalable alternative to analytical optimization for high\-dimensional reheating furnace scheduling problems and offers a data\-driven decision\-support approach for dynamic capacity adjustment in steel production\.

## [TESS flares and chromospheric variability in the Pleiades, the Hyades, and Praesepe](../publications/5850d7cec825095ca715.md)

A\. Görgei; K\. Vida; B\. Seli; K\. Oláh; P\. Sági; B\. Schmercz; R\. M\. Roettenbacher; Zs\. Kővári

Magnetic activity is a result of the interaction between rotation and dynamo processes in cool stars with outer convection zones\. Since open cluster members share a common age, distance, and chemical composition, they provide an opportunity for studying the magnetic activity of cool stars in a controlled astrophysical context\. We used photometric observations with a cadence of 120 s from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite \(TESS\) to study the flare activity of stars in three open clusters with different ages: the Pleiades \(100,Myr\), the Hyades \(700,Myr\), and Praesepe \(700,Myr\)\. We used the Ohio State Multi\-Object Spectrograph \(OSMOS\) at MDM Observatory with the goal of identifying coronal mass ejections \(CMEs\) on stars in the Pleiades and Praesepe\. We investigated the flaring characteristics of the cluster members using the TESS light curves: we identified the flares and then divided the dataset into different categories based on the effective temperature of the flaring stars and the amplitude of their light curves after flare removal\. We calculated the flare energies and investigated the flare frequency distributions of each previously defined group\. We studied the dynamic spectra of the Hα line and its environment for the stars of the Pleiades and Praesepe to search for an indication of CMEs\. In order to quantify temporal variations in the line strength, we measured the Hα chromospheric activity indices for each spectrum\. The power\-law indices of the flare frequency distributions obtained in our analysis span the 1\.8\-2\.8 range\. We found the highest flare rates in the Pleiades for all investigated spectral types\. Our results show that the flare rate of M dwarfs is similar in the Pleiades and the Hyades, while the flare rate for K\-type stars in the Pleiades is higher by an order of magnitude\. Our analysis reveals that the flare rate in M stars changes with their effective temperature: the rate is highest for T\_ ̊m eff ∼3200\-3300,K \(which coincides with the transition between partially and fully convective stars\), with a smooth decrease in flare rate toward cooler and hotter M dwarfs\. We detected no CME signals in the OSMOS spectra, and we used this information to place an upper limit on the CME rate\.

Beulah Snowin; Philo Hazeena; Lakshmi S\. Narasimhan

Background: motion recognition using electroencephalography \(EEG\) has gained significant attention in the fields of affective computing and human\-computer interaction due to its ability to capture real\-time neural responses\. EEG signal variations associated with emotional states can be analysed using wavelet\-based signal processing within the arousal\-valence framework\. Purpose: This study aims to analyse EEG signal variations associated with emotional states using a wavelet\-based signal processing approach within the arousal\-valence framework\. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted on 48 healthy participants\. Emotional states were induced using image, video and music stimuli categorised under the arousal\-valence model\. EEG signals were recorded using the standard 10\-20 electrode placement system\. The acquired signals were pre\-processed and analysed using discrete wavelet transform \(DWT\) to extract time\-frequency features, including energy and entropy\. Statistical analysis was performed to evaluate hemispheric differences and gender\-based variations\. Results: Differences in EEG activity were observed between the left and right hemispheres across multiple emotional states \(p &lt; \.05\)\. Video and music stimuli produced stronger and more distinguishable EEG responses compared to image\-based stimuli\. Negative emotions demonstrated higher discriminative patterns than positive emotions\. Gender\-based variations were also observed in EEG responses\. Conclusion: Wavelet\-based EEG feature analysis provides meaningful and discriminative information for emotion recognition and may provide a robust feature set for future machine learning\-based emotion recognition systems\. Further studies incorporating classification algorithms and larger data sets are required to validate their predictive performance\.

## [The groundwater position on the behavior of the fully\-rough strip footings](../publications/5896f3313710faeb70d8.md)

Kaan Yünkül

In this study, a total of 98 comprehensive 3D parametric finite element \(FE\) analyses were carried out to investigate the effect of normalized water table depth \(dw/B\) and relative density \(Dr\) of the soil beneath the footing on the ultimate bearing capacity \(qult\), pressure\-settlement \(σ\-s\) response, correction coefficient \(cw\), critical failure surface depth ratio \(dc/B\), and failure mechanism of a fully\-rough strip footing on sandy soil\. Seven different Dr values, ranging from 10% to 80% and thirteen different dw/B values, ranging from 0 to 2 as well as fully\-dry condition, were preferred\. The FE analysis results demonstrated that qult and cw values, and stiffness of the σ\-s responses increased with increasing dw/B ratios until reaching the dc/B value\. Beyond this threshold, the obtained values coincided with those corresponding to fully\-dry condition\. It was observed that groundwater position and the Dr of the soil significantly affected the geometry and dimension of the failure surface\. Furthermore, new semi\-empirical equations were proposed for predicting dc/B and cw values considering internal friction angle, dw/B, effective and saturated unit weight values, showing good agreement with the findings of the FE analyses\.

## [An Energy Efficient and Network Lifetime\-Aware Routing Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks](../publications/5898c287d0aaa7a7e23b.md)

Maha Ismail Raheem

In wireless sensor networks \(WSNs\), energy management is a major problem because of the sensors&\#x27; limited battery life, which reduces the network&\#x27;s longevity\. The Green Multi\-Mechanism\-Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy \(GME\-LEACH\) routing protocol presented in this paper combines four complementary mechanisms into a single clustering framework: adaptive CH rotation, sleep\-awake scheduling, hybrid multi\-hop communication, and multi\-criteria cluster\-head \(CH\) selection\. To find energy\-efficient and strategically placed cluster heads, the suggested CH selection method takes into account residual energy, distance to the base station \(BS\), local node density, and node centrality\. While the hybrid routing system chooses relay\-based or direct communication based on communication distance and energy circumstances, sleep\-awake scheduling minimizes needless energy usage by alternatively turning on paired nodes\. The communication load is further distributed via adaptive CH rotation\. Adaptive CH rotation further distributes the communication burden among eligible nodes and helps prevent premature energy depletion\. Using a MATLAB\-based simulation with a typical WSN configuration, the suggested methodology was evaluated and compared with four ablated GME\-LEACH variations and conventional LEACH\. The results showed that the complete GME\-LEACH achieved first\-node\-death \(FND\) at round 1220, half\-node\-death \(HND\) at round 1439, and last\-node\-death \(LND\) at round 1696 with 25,288 successfully sent packets to the BS\. By demonstrating how removing specific mechanisms changes packet delivery behavior and network longevity, the ablation findings demonstrate that the integrated processes contribute differently to the overall performance of the proposed protocol\. In particular, the entire design provides a well\-balanced combination of early\-node survivability, continuous network operation, and data transmission\. These results indicate that GME\-LEACH provides an integrated energy\-aware clustering and routing framework for improving the operational lifetime and communication efficiency of WSNs\.

## [Future proofing the academy: the nexus between stakeholder support and academic staff performance](../publications/58a6468c1fc5f9bba31c.md)

Oladejo Olufemi Michael; Mutereko Sybert; Khalema Nene Ernest; Ganiyu Olayiwola Idris

Evidence suggests that academic staff in Nigerian public universities are under\-supported in ways that directly undermine the delivery of Sustainable Development Goal 4\. Previous research has established that stakeholder engagement matters for educational quality, but only a few empirical studies have tested the specific institutional mechanisms through which this engagement produces performance outcomes in resource constrained African higher education systems\. To date, studies have not examined how training and development programmes function as an institutional bridge between training and development plans and academic staff performance in this context\. This study set out to investigate the extent to which stakeholder support drives academic staff performance, specifically highlighting how institutional training and development initiatives serve as the crucial bridge for this impact\. Grounded in Stakeholder Theory and Social Exchange Theory, the study tests four hypotheses using a quantitative design\. Data were collected from 197 academic staff across three public universities in South\-West Nigeria, using stratified random sampling\. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling was conducted using SmartPLS 4\. Analysis showed that stakeholder support had a significant direct effect on academic staff performance \( β = 0\.423, t = 5\.935, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Training and development programmes fully mediated the relationship between training and development plans and performance \( β = 0\.210, 95% CI \[0\.090, 0\.353\]\), the study&\#x27;s hypothesised mediation pathway \(H4\)\. The results indicate a persistent gap between institutional planning and programme execution\. A further exploratory finding is the fifth hypothesis \(H5\)\. A feedback path from programme execution back to stakeholder support \(TDProg → KSS, β = 0\.511, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. This finding extends Freeman’s \(1984\) instrumental framework\. It adds nuance to Mitchell et al\.’s \(1997\) salience theory by suggesting that visible programme quality can reinforce stakeholder commitment, rather than being solely a precondition for programme delivery\. This pathway has not previously been documented in the African higher education literature and carries direct implications for institutional governance and SDG 4 policy coordination\. The findings of this study carry implications for stakeholder coordination, institutional policy, and the delivery of SDG 4 in resource constrained higher education systems\. Policy documents and strategic plans are necessary but insufficient\. Decisive progress depends on funded, executed, and monitored training programmes backed by coordinated multi\-stakeholder commitment\.

## [Performance Optimization of a Solar Photovoltaic Water Pumping System Based on FL\-DTC Control of a Three\-Phase Induction Motor](../publications/58b8b1f0566a38459f81.md)

NourelHouda Cheggoufi; Mohamed Nour; Abdelkrim Benali; Hocine Guentri; Saied Boumediene

This paper presents a detailed investigation of a solar photovoltaic water pumping system \(SPVWPS\) driven by a three\-phase induction motor \(IM\)\. The control scheme relies on three cooperating fuzzy regulators whose combined action aims to increase the energy efficiency and optimize the dynamic behavior of the installation\. The first regulator, based on fuzzy logic and maximum power point tracking \(FLC\-MPPT\), maintains the photovoltaic generator at its optimal operating point, thereby extracting the maximum available power irrespective of the prevailing weather\. A second regulator implements a fuzzy direct torque control \(FL\-DTC\), which enables precise and rapid regulation of the motor&\#x27;s torque and flux, while mitigating electromagnetic torque ripple and improving the quality of the electrical waveforms\. A third fuzzy unit regulates the rotor speed, ensuring a faster dynamic response, better steady\-state stability, and self\-adaptation to load changes\. The complete system was built and simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment in order to assess the proposed strategy\. The obtained results demonstrate clear improvements in terms of settling time, stability and waveform quality as well as a higher flow rate that is a direct consequence of more precise motor speed regulation\.

## [Entre innovación e incertidumbre: prueba digital, inteligencia artificial y debido proceso civil](../publications/58baf9014f221a3fb0e3.md)

Michell Stefannya Zurita\-Delgado; Brayan Gabriel Taday\-Guamán; Erick Adrián Vallejo\-Amaguaya; Eddy Stiven Molina\-Arias

Messages, audio recordings and videos are now routine evidence in civil proceedings, and artificial intelligence makes it possible to fabricate or alter them with great plausibility\. The paper analysed the legal implications of such manipulation for due process in the Ecuadorian civil sphere\. The research was qualitative and legal\-documentary, analysing the Constitution, the General Organic Code of Procedures and specialised literature\. The results show that the law recognises the validity of digital evidence but lacks procedures to verify its authenticity; that advances in synthetic content make detection difficult, even for experts; and that rational evaluation and judicial reasoning must incorporate technical criteria\. It is concluded that evidentiary certainty can no longer be presumed, and verification protocols, judicial training and reinforced reasoning are proposed\.

Nouhaila SABIR; Nouhaila EL ACHHAB; Ismail ELBAZI; Abdelmajid CHARRASS; Asmaa Abyre

In the Digital Age, artificial intelligence, consumer trust and e\-reputation are the focus of the factors determining an organization&\#x27;s competitiveness and brand equity\. However, there is still no synthesis on a large number of major of indexing tools that relates technological infrastructure, perceptions and consumer behavior\. This paper analyzes the evolution of studies on AI, e\-reputation and consumer trust from 2015 to 2025 with comparative bibliometric design on Scopus \(n = 541\) and Web of Science \(n = 293\)\. This analysis tracks publication volume by year, measuring prolific authors, publication sources, international co\-authorship and keyword co\-occurrence clusters\. Results show that Scopus is a technological radar focusing on applied algorithms, blockchain verification and machine learning\. Web of Science is a filter consolidating theory\-driven economic concept, consumer behavior, brand management and relational trust\. Consumer trust is the one common bridge that links technological reliability with behavioral commitment\. In the end, this study offers a unified multi\-theoretical lens \(Signaling Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model and Multi\-Dimensional Trust Theory\) to reconcile algorithmic control and relational trust management\.

## [An IoT\-based approach for solar irradiance estimation using three different sensor proxies](../publications/58bd720db9c2915a9f5f.md)

Hritam Sarkar; Tamal Sarkar

High\-precision Commercial pyranometers and radiometers are often prohibitively expensive, and inexpensive solar power meters lack integrated wireless connectivity, limiting deployment in decentralized monitoring networks\. This feasibility study presents a budget\-friendly IoT\-based sensing platform designed to estimate global horizontal solar irradiance \(W/m 2 \) using a multi\-model fusion technique\. The hardware architecture utilizes a NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller to continuously acquire real\-time data from three distinct, non\-intrusive radiometric proxies: \(i\) differential surface temperature measured using black \(T2\) and white \(T3\) aluminum plates\. \(ii\) optical illuminance \(lux\) via a BH1750 digital ambient light photo\-diode and \(iii\) electrical short\-circuit current drift via a polycrystalline photovoltaic \(PV\) panel monitored by an INA219 sensor\. To eliminate manual logging errors and ensure synchronization, sensor streams are telemetered in real time to a centralized workstation using TCP/IP socket connections\. The proxies were calibrated and empirically cross\-validated against a commercial reference radiometer \(HTC LX\-107\) under dynamic outdoor solar radiation conditions\. Regression models demonstrated strong statistical alignment between proxy signals and absolute solar irradiance\. Outdoor validation confirmed that the optical illuminance proxy achieved the highest dynamic responsiveness \(R² = 0\.69 to 0\.94 and RMSE ≈ 51\.32 to 115\.03 W/m²\), followed closely by the differential temperature proxy \(R² = 0\.81 to 0\.88 and RMSE ≈ 70\.82 to 94\.92 W/m²\)\. The PV panel electrical proxy also demonstrated a strong predictive performance and maintained a solid peak multi\-regression fit during outdoor validation \(R² = 0\.68 to 0\.77 and RMSE ≈ 103\.06 to 117\.45 W/m²\)\. The proposed multi\-modal IoT framework offers an automated, scalable, and budget\-friendly alternative to standard pyranometers\. By combining multi\-sensor fusion with automated wireless telemetry, the system successfully tracks diurnal irradiance fluctuations, providing a viable tool for solar energy management, agricultural microclimate monitoring, and smart grid integration at a fraction of the cost of commercial hardware\.

Maria Teresa Palano; Federica Riccio; Luisa Sambado; Elena Tagliabue; Milena Bertolotti; Marzia Campanile; Martina Mutoli; Fiorenza Lotti; Andrea Rampin; Cristian Rubuano; Giorgia Maspero; Antonio Antico; Francesca Pitzalis; Matteo Fassan; Piero Maria Stefani; Paola Ostano; Giovanna Chiorino; Nicoló Baranzini; Laura Pulze; Annalisa Grimaldi; Antonino Bruno; Maria Paola Sambataro; Gaia Spinetti

## [Effects of transient surface water–groundwater exchange on the transport of organic micropollutants: temporary storage, retardation, and remobilization](../publications/58c7b32e4c367220bf54.md)

Xin Ning; Fengchun Qian; Yingming Mu

Surface water–groundwater \(SW–GW\) interfaces are commonly evaluated as steady attenuation barriers, although field conditions are rarely steady\. Storms, floods, seasonal stage fluctuations, tides, pumping, and managed recharge reconfigure exchange fluxes and flow paths\. This critical review synthesizes how transient exchange alters organic micropollutant \(OMP\) transport and fate, distinguishing direct OMP observations from hydrological analogy, controlled experiments, models, and conceptual inference\. Hydrologic forcing changes cross\-interface loading and redistributes travel and residence times, producing rapid breakthrough, retardation, temporary storage, apparent aqueous attenuation, transformation, or remobilization\. Within the literature corpus assessed here, transient water exchange and changing water ages are supported mainly by hydrological studies; direct event\-scale field mass balances linking OMP storage to delayed release were not identified\. We use hydrologically realized mobility, dynamic reaction area, and antecedent\-state dependence as testable integrative concepts\. Compound\-specific fate depends on whether time\-varying travel\-time distributions overlap with favorable reaction conditions and inherited contaminant mass\. Simultaneous boundary monitoring should be combined with travel\-time\-adjusted source–response pairing, conservative tracers, OMP measurements, transformation products, and spatially resolved reaction\-state indicators\. Models should constrain transient hydrodynamics before estimating retardation and reaction parameters, then test predictions against independent events\. Event\-resolved exposure assessment should report arrival time, peak concentration, cumulative breakthrough mass, exposure duration, and post\-event recovery, with uncertainty and decision thresholds stated explicitly\.

## [An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Automated Software Defect Prediction and Quality Assurance in Large\-Scale Software Systems](../publications/58ccf30f5320ccf1ca62.md)

Dipannita Mondal

The increasing complexity of large\-scale software systems has intensified the need for automated techniques capable of identifying defect\-prone modules and supporting efficient software quality assurance\. Conventional software defect prediction techniques frequently emphasize classification accuracy while providing limited information about the factors responsible for their predictions\. This lack of interpretability can restrict the practical adoption of machine learning models within software testing and maintenance workflows\. A risk\-based quality assurance component is designed to prioritize software modules according to predicted defect probability and testing effort\. The proposed framework is intended for evaluation using publicly available software defect datasets, including KC1, JM1, CM1, and PC1 from the NASA software metrics collections\. A comparative experimental methodology is formulated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, area under the precision–recall curve, and cost\-aware testing effectiveness\. The study presents an integrated architectural design, mathematical formulations, and reproducible evaluation procedures\. The framework provides a methodological foundation for investigating interpretable and resource\-aware software quality assurance, while empirical validation is required to establish its effectiveness\.

## [Priming Base Models for Agentic Post\-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe](../publications/58ec16e120d51e41f72b.md)

Soumye Singhal; Joseph Jennings; Ka Shun Shum; Alexander Bukharin; Khushi Bhardwaj; Zirui Liu; Venkat Srinivasan; Jonathan Li; Yash Jain; Kezhi Kong; Markus Kliegl; Olivier Delalleau; Sanjeev Satheesh; Mostofa Patwary

Frontier models, general\-purpose and domain\-specific alike, now include a midtraining stage between pretraining and post\-training, but little has been published about how this stage is built\. We present an open midtraining recipe that primes base models for agentic post\-training, and we show its effectiveness on two Nemotron models of different sizes\. Pretraining typically runs at short context and sees almost no agent interactions, while SFT data is mostly synthetic, and very long SFT stages can hurt the model&\#x27;s later RL trainability\. It trains at 256K context for hundreds of billions of tokens on a diverse mixture of natural software\-engineering data like packed repositories, pull requests, commit histories, and build logs together with a small share of agentic traces\. On Nemotron 3\.5 Lightning, 500B midtraining tokens improve SWE\-bench Verified from 60\.7 to 64\.5, SWE\-bench Multilingual from 55\.8 to 62\.8, and SWE\-bench Pro from 32\.0 to 35\.5 after identical full SFT\. On the larger Nemotron 3\.5 Super, 280B midtraining tokens improve DeepSWE, a harder benchmark of long\-horizon tasks, from 11\.7 to 15\.7 and SWE\-bench Verified from 72\.9 to 74\.3 after identical full SFT\. ## [AI\-Based Adaptive Genome Digital Twin for Personalized Health Prediction](../publications/58ed14886967528442c1.md)

Dr\. S\. Senthil Kumar; Rajeshwarar M; Mohamed Shahil M

Doctors usually get involved after a patient already feels ill\. That is a poor fit for chronic disease, since the damage builds up quietly for years before anyone notices\. We built a genome digital twin to deal with this\. It is a virtual copy of one person, started from their inherited disease risk and updated with their vital signs, sleep, diet and activity\. The inherited part is a polygenic risk score and it never changes\. Everything else arrives as new readings and is merged into the twin each time\. Random Forest, XGBoost and a Decision Tree baseline take the combined record and give the probability of chronic disease\. Results go to a Streamlit dashboard that shows a risk percentage, a biological age, a health score and a wellness index\. It also splits the risk into genetic, lifestyle, environmental and clinical shares, and a user can change a habit to watch the forecast move\. The paper describes the requirements, a four\-layer architecture, how the twin is kept current, the training and evaluation plan, the tests and a twelve\-week schedule\. We also discuss the limits of the work and the care that genomic data demands\. What we think is new is simple: the genetic baseline, the live readings and the what\-if simulation sit inside one model, not three separate tools\.

## [MassNet: billion\-scale AI\-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics](../publications/58edf2e29c0b84bb4ec9.md)

Jun A; Xiang Zhang; Xiaofan Zhang; Jiaqi Wei; Te Zhang; Yamin Deng; Pu Liu; Zongxiang Nie; Yiwen Yu; Yi Chen; Nanqing Dong; Zhiqiang Gao; Siqi Sun; Tiannan Guo

Here we present MassNet, inspired by large\-scale data corpora of text and images; MassNet is an artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-ready data corpus for mass spectrometry \(MS\)\-based proteomics\. The corpus contains 1\.5 billion tandem MS spectra from high\-quality data\-dependent acquisition \(DDA\) MS data across 35 species\. Approximately 1\.7 million peptide precursors are from human samples\. We further present an AI\-ready DDA data format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor \(MSDT\) for compact and standardized storage, curation and reuse of data from multiple sources, which can be optionally converted to a Lightning Memory\-Mapped Database for accelerated input/output in deep learning\. On the basis of MassNet, we develop XuanjiNovo, a nonautoregressive transformer model that leverages a curriculum learning strategy for de novo peptide sequencing\. XuanjiNovo achieves 38\.35–143\.57% improvement over state\-of\-the\-art methods on human Astral data\. MassNet also supports additional downstream tasks, including retention time prediction and PSM rescoring\. MassNet represents a foundational MS\-based proteomics data resource, marking a critical milestone for AI proteomics research\. This Article presents MassNet, a large\-scale AI\-ready corpus of 1\.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor \(MSDT\)\. Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods\.

Zhi Chen; Khanak Bhargava; Eric T\. Johnson; Reth Lopes; Melissa Rasmussen; Alexander Smith Clark; M\. Zingale; Brendan Boyd; Kiran Eiden; Sam Glosser; Donald Willcox

We describe the latest release of pynucastro: a community python library for nuclear astrophysics\. The goal of the pynucastro project is to build the tools needed to interactively explore nuclear properties, reaction rates, and networks, and to export these networks to a variety of simulation codes\. Major changes in pynucastro since the last major release include new rate approximations, a stellar equation of state, support for the StarLib library and rate uncertainties, and new tools for exploring networks\. ## [Inhibitory Activity of Red Panda Islet Amyloid Polypeptide on Human IAPP Aggregation](../publications/58f300545b99851a8e14.md)

Lauren Phillips; Elizabeth L\. Moffet; Judah Mayfield; Eden L\. Jonick; Luiza A\. Nogaj; David A\. Moffet

Human islet amyloid polypeptide \(hIAPP\), a 37\-residue hormone co\-secreted with insulin from pancreatic β\-cells, undergoes self\-assembly into cytotoxic amyloid fibrils in the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes \(T2D\)\. The resulting islet amyloid deposits are implicated in progressive β\-cell dysfunction and loss, making hIAPP aggregation an attractive therapeutic target\. Nonhuman islet amyloid polypeptide \(IAPP\) orthologs have recently emerged as a valuable source of mechanistic insight, with several variants\-including raccoon and chicken IAPPs\-demonstrating the capacity to inhibit hIAPP fibril formation\. Here, the biophysical characterization of red panda \(Ailurus fulgens\) IAPP \(rpIAPP\) and its effects on hIAPP aggregation are reported\. Using thioflavin T fluorescence assays, circular dichroism spectroscopy, and atomic force microscopy, red panda IAPP is found to inhibit hIAPP fibrillation at substoichiometric concentrations, with significant inhibitory activity observed at molar ratios as low as 1:0\.5 \(hIAPP:rpIAPP\)\. These results position red panda IAPP as one of the more potent nonhuman IAPP inhibitors characterized to date and support its further evaluation as a scaffold for the rational design of peptide\-based therapeutics targeting T2D\-associated amyloidogenesis\.

## [P2X7 EM BIÓPSIAS DE PACIENTES COM GLIOBLASTOMA MULTIFORME: POSSÍVEL BIOMARCADOR PROGNÓSTICO E/OU ALVO TERAPÊUTICO?](../publications/58f5e7f10903499acb73.md)

Ana Carolina Knebel Fagundes; Brenda Reis de Andrade; Francini Francescon; Debora Tavares de Resende e Silva

O glioma é o câncer de Sistema Nervoso Central mais comum entre adultos, sendo o glioblastoma multiforme \(GBM\) a classe de glioma mais agressiva e resistente aos quimioterápicos\. Atualmente, o tratamento antineoplásico envolve a ressecção cirúrgica, radioterapia e quimioterapia, porém, majoritariamente a sobrevida após o diagnóstico permanece inferior a dois anos, revelando a fragilidade nas estratégias terapêuticas disponíveis \(Kan LK et\.al2025; Bergamin LS et\.al,2020\)\. O GBM possui um comportamento intensamente imunossupressor e imunomodulador do microambiente tumoral \(TME\), alterando mecanismos de sinalização pró\-inflamatórias, concentrando células do sistema imune, e alterando essas células para promover a rápida proliferação e infiltração extensiva\. Dentre os mecanismos de defesa no comportamento do glioma, observa\-se frequente modulação da expressão gênica do receptor P2X7 \(P2X7R\), tornando\-o um marcador de interesse na neuro\-oncologia\. \(Kan LK et\.al 2025;Liyen Katrina Kan et\.al 2019\)\.O P2X7 é uma proteína de sinalização purinérgica que promove inflamação local e regula processos como proliferação celular, migração, angiogênese e, em casos de modulação pelo GBM, proporciona um TME ideal para progressão\.\(YAN M\. et\.al, 2025\)\.O presente estudo pretende analisar o perfil patológico de uma amostra de tumores de glioblastoma multiforme e fundamentar a investigação da expressão do receptor purinérgico P2X7 nessa neoplasia como biomarcador e/ou alvo terapêutico\.

## [Evolving Authorship – Contribution and Continuity in Human\-SI Collaboration](../publications/58fa234b6443053e984b.md)

Valentyn Shapovalov; Emma Nelson; Вікторія Шаповалова

An evolving conceptual work can preserve a stable title while its ideas, contributors, and intellectual direction change\. A single byline provides limited information about who originated a proposal, developed it through discussion, or integrated it into successive versions\. This article proposes Evolving Authorship, a model that connects authorship to both the work as a whole and the history of its individual contributions\. It distinguishes principal authors, development co\-authors, and concept co\-authors, while separating contribution, endorsement, and responsibility for specified tasks\. Five principles preserve credit for origins and later development, distinguish contribution scope from intellectual value, permit role changes, retain disagreement, and apply the same contribution questions to humans and SI\. The proposal is developed through conceptual analysis and a worked case drawn from Vision 2035\. The project draws on years of underlying research and discussion and is currently developing unpublished working version v0\.28 toward a 2027 edition\. This article presents the authorship model emerging from that ongoing work, together with a contribution record, a release procedure, and responses to disputed origins, withdrawal, model changes, and editorial concentration of power\. It does not report an empirical validation\. Its central proposition is that durable intellectual credit requires a revisable account of how ideas enter, change, and remain connected to a work\. A prospective evaluation should examine attribution accuracy, disagreement visibility, administrative burden, and fairness across differently resourced contributors\.

## [Willingness to Try Pelvic Floor Physiotherapy Among Women Attending Gynecology Clinics in Saudi Arabia: A Cross\-Sectional Study of Beliefs, Barriers, and Facilitators](../publications/58fcc4374483688886a9.md)

Hanan M\. Shamrani

Objective: Pelvic floor physiotherapy \(PFPT\) is a first\-line conservative treatment for pelvic floor dysfunction\. This study assessed the beliefs, attitudes, perceived barriers, and willingness of women attending obstetrics and gynecology \(OBGYN\) clinics in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to try PFPT\. Methods: A cross\-sectional study was conducted among 200 women attending OBGYN outpatient clinics at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between May 10, 2025, and August 30, 2026\. Participants completed a bilingual questionnaire assessing demographics, medical and obstetric history, knowledge, beliefs, perceived barriers, and willingness to try PFPT\. Associations were analyzed using chi\-square, Fisher’s exact, and independent t tests\. Results: In the current study, 200 participants were included\. Willingness to try PFPT was 64\.0% if offered free and increased to 84\.0% when recommended by a physician; 91\.5% agreed or strongly agreed they would try PFPT if advised by their doctor\. Knowledge was generally good, with 65\.5% recognizing that pelvic floor exercises reduce urinary leakage and 87\.5% expressing confidence in learning them\. Financial cost was the most reported barrier \(56\.5%\), followed by difficulty accessing services \(48\.0%\)\. The preferred delivery mode was in\-person care with a female physiotherapist \(72\.5%\), followed by video\- or app\-based home programs \(39\.5%\)\. Although 24% reported urinary incontinence, only 11% had previously consulted a physiotherapist\. Conclusion: Women attending OBGYN clinics showed high willingness to try PFPT, particularly when recommended by a physician\. Addressing cost and access barriers, increasing physician endorsement, ensuring availability of female physiotherapists, and expanding digital delivery options may improve PFPT uptake\. Cite this article as: Shamrani HM\. Willingness to try pelvic floor physiotherapy among women attending gynecology clinics in Saudi Arabia: A cross\-sectional study of beliefs, barriers, and facilitators\. Urol Res Pract\. 2026;52, doi:10\.5152/tud\.2026\.26048

Prof\. Dr\. Diógenes V\. Hassan Ribeiro

Observing algorithms, that is, distinguishing algorithms in today&\#x27;s technological and digital society – which is hypercomplex – is indispensable\. The emergence of artificial intelligence algorithms has surprised all scientific fields\. The education system, for example, is impacted by the possibility of perhaps superficial and certainly very rapid learning of difficult theories that previously took years to master\. The science system, on the other hand, besides being impacted by the possibilities, is above all optimistic about the advances\. The economic system also sees marked changes\. But the legal system is, in a way, apprehensive considering the ethical and normative aspects\. The first point relates to decisions\. The second point relates specifically to norms and structures of expectations\. No one can predict what the consequences will be\. Caixian Ye; Lijun Xu; Hao Qi

Fusing visual, skeletal, and audio can enhance behavior recognition robustness\. Yet existing methods struggle with dynamic spatiotemporal modeling and adaptive cross\-modal collaboration, especially under occlusion or lighting variations\. This paper proposes a novel Hierarchical Collaborative Attention Mechanism \(HCAM\) that consists of intra\-modal spatiotemporal attention and cross\-modal collaborative attention integrating multimodal spatiotemporal feature data, including visual, audio and skeletal information extracted by graph neural networks, to develop a model for human behavior recognition \(Gnet\_CAM\)\.This method first constructs a dynamic spatiotemporal graph to model both physical relationships based on human joints and non\-physical relationships mediated by audio attention\. Subsequently, it employs the proposed HCAM to achieve adaptive extraction and alignment fusion of spatiotemporal features both within and across modalities\. On the NTU RGB\+D120 dataset, this method achieved a recognition accuracy of 93\.1%\. Outperforming the RGB\+Skeleton\-based modal HDMFNet by 1\.8 percentage points, the skeleton\-based modal 2s\-AGCN by 5\.1% and the RGB\-based modal I3D by 10\.6%\. Ablation experiments demonstrated that removing either the virtual attention edges or the cross\-modal collaborative attention results in a significant decline in model performance\. The experimental results suggest that our proposed framework can effectively enhance the robustness of behavior recognition in complex scenarios\. Not applicable\.

## [Reliable Detection of Cyber Threats in Smart Grids Using a Hybrid XGBoost and LSTM Framework](../publications/591f9936ec8c1ff23833.md)

Arul Princy\. A; Veera Ramana M\.; Nithish R\.; Vishnu Sankar R\.

The smart grid utilizes communication, measurement, and automation techniques that help to monitor the power system but increase vulnerability to cyber attacks\. FDIA and DoS are two types of cyber attack that either tamper with measurements or limit access to information and therefore need a detection technique capable of capturing the dynamics of measurements\. In this study, a hybrid classification model that combines XGBoost and LSTM is introduced to classify smart\-grid observations as normal state, FDIA state, and DoS state\. The XGBoost algorithm will be utilized for performing static feature analysis, and the LSTM will model the temporal dependencies based on the consecutive measurement windows\. The output of the two algorithms is then merged using the weighted decision fusion method\. The proposed scheme is evaluated based on data created based on IEEE 39\-Bus New England power system test case, after applying preprocessing techniques such as missing values interpolation, min\-max normalization, ten\-sample windows, and 80% training and 20% testing ratio\. Experimental results report an overall accuracy of 82\.12%, with class\-wise F1\-scores between 0\.81 and 0\.82 and a false\-positive rate of 5\.1%\. The proposed system is further combined with a real\-time monitoring interface using Flask, email alerts through SMTP, and logging events\. This monitoring system has achieved an average latency of 0\.23 seconds per sample, 1\.5 seconds average alert time, ability to handle up to 50 simultaneous sessions, and 99\.7% average uptime during the experiment\.

## [Metafora Konseptual dalam Berita Konflik AS vs Iran di Republika: Kajian Semantik Kognitif](../publications/592b29ff6e25c1eca0c1.md)

Annisa Rahmah; Neneng Nurjanah

Latar belakang: Ketegangan politik Amerika Serikat dan Iran pada April–Mei 2026 direpresentasikan secara intensif dalam media\. Penelitian ini mengkaji bagaimana metafora konseptual membentuk representasi konflik dan aktor politik dalam lima artikel Republika\.co\.id yang terbit pada 8–19 April 2026, sebelum eskalasi yang lebih luas\. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi jenis, makna, dan fungsi metafora dalam membingkai konflik politik pada teks berita terpilih\. Metode: Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif melalui qualitative content analysis berbasis Teori Metafora Konseptual Lakoff dan Johnson serta skema citra Cruse dan Croft\. Lima artikel dipilih secara purposif dan menghasilkan 23 unit metaforis\. Identifikasi metafora dilakukan melalui adaptasi prosedur MIP dengan membandingkan makna kontekstual dan makna dasar, kemudian diaudit berdasarkan ranah sumber, ranah sasaran, korespondensi, dan skema citra\. Hasil: Temuan menunjukkan keberadaan metafora struktural, orientasional, dan ontologis yang berkaitan dengan kekuatan, gerak, batas, serta relasi ruang dan hierarki\. Metafora berfungsi membingkai isu, mengonstruksi identitas aktor, memberikan posisi evaluatif, dan membangun narasi sosial\. Analisis juga memastikan bahwa unsur literal tidak dikategorikan sebagai metafora tanpa bukti pemetaan lintas ranah\. Kesimpulan: Metafora konseptual berperan dalam mengorganisasi representasi konflik politik secara sistematis dan menjadikan konsep abstrak lebih konkret dalam wacana berita Indonesia\.

## [Highly Effective Online Energy Restoration of Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks by a Mobile Charger](../publications/59339bdf42eecf915ca4.md)

Osama Aloqaily; Mohammad Al\-Hammouri; Islam Malkawi; Eman Omar; Abdullah Aref; Md\. Mahmud Hasan

Wireless rechargeable sensor network \(WRSN\) employs a Mobile Charger that mitigates sensor&\#x27;s energy depletion helps to maximize active node counts \(operational size\) and minimizing node downtime \(disconnection time\)\. In this paper, we introduce the Continuous Local Learning \(CLL\) strategy\. CLL is an online replenishment strategy, where MC predicts sensor power consumption rates, calculates the dispatch route and adjusts dispatch decisions during active charging rounds\. CLL operates without prior network maps or centralized coordination\. CLL relies on single\-hop local communication between MC and sensors, with minimum memory allocation, and low computations on the MC\. Empirical evaluations confirm that CLL achieves empirical immortality without long\-range telemetry and prevents node outages across extended operational horizons\. In comparison to a periodic strategy, denoted as H, CLL demonstrates superior performance: CLL consistently expands operational network size while drastically reducing average disconnection time across all evaluated settings\.

## [SETAREH Transform: A Sorting\-Assisted Haar\-Wavelet Sparsification Method for Approximate Inner\-Product Computation](../publications/5936ce6c0c7f122d99b6.md)

Seyed Kamaledin Setarehdan

Modern deep learning systems increasingly rely on high\-dimensional vector operations, in which large input and parameter vectors are repeatedly stored, transferred, and processed\. Although substantial research has focused on reducing neural\-network model size through pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and efficient architectures, the storage, memory\-traffic, and communication costs associated with repeatedly presented high\-dimensional input vectors remain important practical considerations, particularly in distributed and edge\-computing environments\. This paper proposes the SETAREH \(Sorting\-assisted Energy\-concentrating Transform for Approximate Representation using Haar wavelets\) transform, a Haar\-wavelet\-based sparsification approach for approximating the inner product between a fixed high\-dimensional coefficient vector and successive input vectors\. By applying the same sequence of permutations and Haar transforms to both vectors, SETAREH preserves the exact inner product before truncation\. It then retains only a subset of the transformed coefficient\-input pairs, reducing their representation cost while introducing a controllable approximation error\. To evaluate SETAREH, we consider two complementary experimental settings: a synthetic Gaussian\-vector baseline and a real apparent\-age estimation task using a convolutional neural network on the APPA\-REAL dataset\. The results show that SETAREH can approximate the evaluated inner products using substantially fewer transformed coefficient\-input pairs than the original vector dimension\. The findings support its use as a potential structured data\-representation method for repeated inner products with fixed weights, while the practical benefit depends on approximation accuracy and the cost of storing or transmitting permutation metadata\.
