centrosomal protein 55 \(cEP55\), a core member of the cEP centrosomal protein family, is a molecule that regulates cytokinesis during the end of cell division and is also extensively involved in multiple physiological processes, including genomic stability maintenance, immune regulation and embryonic development\.It has been shown that cEP55 participates in pathological processes such as tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and immune escape by modulating multiple signaling pathways including PI3K/ AKT, NF\-κB and JAK/STAT\.Furthermore, it exhibits a close correlation with poor prognosis among patients with cancer\.In addition, dysregulated cEP55 expression is also implicated in the pathological processes of neurological disorders, reproductive\-genetic diseases and chronic metabolic diseases\.These findings highlight the potential clinical translational value of cEP55 for disease diagnosis, prognostic evaluation and targeted therapy\.Based on recent domestic and international research, the present study systematically reviews the molecular biological properties, expression features and action mechanisms of cEP55 across multi\-system diseases, and summarizes its clinical application potential, to provide a theoretical reference for promoting relevant basic research and implementing precise clinical diagnosis and treatment\.

## [Development and external validation of interpretable machine learning models for 7\-, 14\-, and 28\-day mortality in sepsis\-associated liver injury](../publications/594bbcdc29780edd7237.md)

Hao Yao; Zheng Li; Jinxiao Lü; Wei Shen

Background Mortality in sepsis\-associated liver injury \(SALI\) remains high, and early risk stratification is difficult\. Existing prognostic models commonly focus on a single endpoint, usually 28\-day mortality, and rarely undergo independent external validation\. Methods We developed machine\-learning models using clinical features recorded during the first 24 h to predict all\-cause in\-hospital mortality within 7, 14, and 28 days\. In MIMIC\-IV \(v3\.1\), 1,550 adults meeting the prespecified SALI criteria were allocated to a training cohort \(n = 1,119\) and a held\-out internal validation cohort \( n = 431\)\. An independent Chinese cohort from Xiaogan Central Hospital \( n = 229; 28\-day in\-hospital mortality, 45\.9%\) was used for external validation\. One hundred candidate pipelines were evaluated using stratified 10\-fold cross\-validation\. SHAP was used to describe feature attribution across prediction horizons\. Results AUROCs in the held\-out internal validation cohort were 0\.840, 0\.841, and 0\.850 for 7\-, 14\-, and 28\-day mortality, respectively; corresponding external AUROCs were 0\.720, 0\.717, and 0\.763\. The external 28\-day model outperformed modified SOFA \(0\.763 vs\. 0\.673; P = 0\.011\) and MELD\-Na \(0\.763 vs\. 0\.636; P = 0\.002\)\. A parsimonious logistic\-regression sensitivity model achieved an external 28\-day AUROC of 0\.762, not significantly different from the full model \( P = 0\.970\)\. The 14\-day model was miscalibrated externally; recalibration improved the calibration slope from 0\.563 to 0\.970 but did not materially improve the Brier score\. SHAP rankings varied across horizons and were interpreted descriptively rather than causally\. Conclusion The models showed moderate transportability to one independent retrospective cohort\. Multicentre prospective validation is needed before clinical implementation\.

## [Essential Trace Elements in Psychiatric Disorders: Mechanistic Pathways and Therapeutic Implications](../publications/5961f4c981793ad516c4.md)

Sebla Ertuğrul; Özcan Uzun

Essential trace elements—including zinc \(Zn\), iron \(Fe\), copper \(Cu\), selenium \(Se\), manganese \(Mn\), molybdenum \(Mo\), and cobalt \(Co\)—participate in neurotransmission, redox regulation, mitochondrial function, immune signaling, and neuroendocrine processes\. Increasing evidence suggests that disturbances in trace\-element homeostasis may be associated with several psychiatric disorders; however, the strength and consistency of the evidence remain heterogeneous\. This narrative review integrates recent human clinical studies with relevant biochemical, mechanistic, and selected preclinical evidence concerning trace\-element dysregulation and psychiatric outcomes\. Among the elements examined, Zn and Se have the strongest interventional support\. Meta\-analyses of randomized controlled trials suggest that adjunctive Zn supplementation may reduce depressive symptom severity in some populations, whereas individual trials indicate possible symptomatic benefit in attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\)\. Findings for Se also suggest potential benefit, particularly in postpartum depression, although generalizability across populations remains uncertain\. Observational studies have associated lower Fe indices with greater ADHD symptom burden, cognitive difficulties, and atypical neurodevelopment, while higher circulating Cu concentrations have been reported in major depressive disorder and autism spectrum disorder\. Evidence concerning Mn, Mo, and Co remains limited and inconsistent and is derived mainly from small observational studies\. Mechanisms involving oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, excitatory–inhibitory imbalance and altered monoaminergic signaling are biologically plausible but do not independently establish clinical causality\. Overall, disturbances in essential trace\-element homeostasis have been associated with mood disorders, neurodevelopmental conditions, and cognitive dysfunction\. Nevertheless, substantial heterogeneity in study design, biomarker matrices and assays, sample characteristics, and control of confounding limits causal interpretation\. Longitudinal and interventional studies using standardized methods are therefore needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships and to determine whether targeted micronutrient assessment or supplementation provides clinically meaningful benefit in psychiatric practice\.

## [Relación entre el vínculo con animales de compañía y el bienestar psicológico en adolescentes de Loja, Ecuador](../publications/596315afe4afffc40fbd.md)

Andrea Lisbeth Torres Yaguana; Diego Segundo Andrade Mejía

Introducción: La adolescencia constituye una etapa de vulnerabilidad para la salud mental, en la cual el vínculo humano\-animal emerge como recurso protector\. Resultados: La cercanía emocional correlacionó con el crecimiento personal \(r=\.46, p&lt;\.001\) y el propósito en la vida \(r=\.35, p=\.004\); la interacción dueño\-mascota \(r=\.29, p=\.020\) y el menor costo percibido \(r=\.37, p=\.002\) mostraron asociación con mayor crecimiento personal\. ## [Evaluation of the Tangibles Dimension of Digital Quality and Occupational Health and Safety Application Service Quality in XYZ Construction Company](../publications/597ebb06babd7bb25ee0.md)

Muhammad Fandi; I Putu Artama Wiguna

This study evaluates the service quality of a Digital Quality and Occupational Health and Safety \(OHS\) application based on the Tangibles dimension of the SERVQUAL model, focusing on user interface design, ease of navigation, and the availability of supporting facilities in construction projects at Company XYZ\. The application supports quality control and OHS management, making its usability essential for improving operational effectiveness\. A quantitative evaluative approach was employed, involving 109 application users selected through purposive sampling\. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through SERVQUAL gap analysis to assess discrepancies between user expectations and perceived performance\. One\-way ANOVA was also conducted to identify differences in perceptions across user groups\. The findings revealed negative SERVQUAL gap scores across the Tangibles dimension, indicating that the application&\#x27;s perceived performance had not fully met user expectations\. The largest gap concerned the availability of supporting facilities, followed by ease of navigation\. Furthermore, ANOVA results demonstrated significant differences in perceived performance among user groups, while their expectations showed no statistically significant differences\. These findings highlight the need for improvements in the application&\#x27;s tangible service attributes, particularly user interface design, navigation simplicity, and the availability of comprehensive user guides and supporting resources\. The study provides practical recommendations for Company XYZ to enhance user experience, improve application accessibility, and strengthen the effectiveness of digital quality and OHS management implementation in construction projects\.

## [Blitz: Accelerating the Diffusion Modules of AlphaFold3 and Boltz\-2](../publications/5985eed450a0fbeab315.md)

Vinay Saji Mathew; Soundar Kumara; Gretta Kellogg; William K\. M\. Lai

Diffusion\-based protein structure prediction models produce all\-atom structures in about 200 denoising steps, and that cost has driven a number of few\-step samplers\. We present Blitz, a few\-step distillation framework that uses a geometric noise schedule to distribute steps more evenly across noise scales, then learns those updates through multistep consistency training\. Physical steering and target\-free candidate selection help reduce the remaining geometric defects at inference\. We apply Blitz to AlphaFold 3 and Boltz\-2, reducing denoising from 200 steps to eight\. Because published few\-step results use different benchmarks and scoring procedures, we compare both distilled models with their teachers and other few\-step methods under a common evaluation protocol covering structural accuracy, interface quality, ligand placement, and stereochemical validity\. Blitz retains teacher\-level structural accuracy, with AF3\-Blitz outperforming all evaluated few\-step baselines and exceeding its teacher on several accuracy metrics\.

## [The Applications of Operations Research in Sustainable E\-Commerce and Reverse Logistics](../publications/598eaf7936f9c684a699.md)

Richa Kalpesh Saxena; Manya Garg; Mansvi Visaria; Mradul Agarwal; Mann Maradiya; Madhav Parwal

The present review is a systematic literature review\-cum\-bibliometric analysis of sustainable e\-commerce, read against the much larger literature on reverse logistics, the circular economy and sustainable supply\-chain management\. Records were taken from Scopus on 11 September 2026, screened under the PRISMA framework and mapped using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer\. The mapped set comprises 867 documents \(747 articles and 120 reviews\) written by 2,595 authors\. Reverse logistics is the largest author keyword \(403 occurrences\) and circular economy follows \(177\), while ecommerce appears in only 19 documents\. The co\-occurrence maps show clusters on decision methods, closed\-loop network design and optimisation, waste recovery, and digital technologies\. India, Brazil and China lead in country output\. The review identifies gaps in empirical testing of digital tools, consumer and social perspectives, and the labelling of e\-commerce research, and sets out a future research agenda\.

## [Geographic patterns of leaf area in global forests and their responses to climate change](../publications/59951c0ad61352410236.md)

Xucai Pu; H\. Q\. Zhang; Wenqi Song; Feng Jiang; Zhiheng Wang

Revealing the biogeography of functional traits and their drivers is central to ecology and biogeography\. However, few studies have evaluated community\-weighted traits in global forests, which dominate biomass and productivity in terrestrial ecosystems\. In this study, we used a dataset of tree plots across global forests\. Using machine\-learning approaches, we assessed the geographic pattern of community\-level leaf area of trees, its relationships with environmental drivers, and its projected changes under future climate change scenarios\. We found that leaf area of trees exhibits a clear latitudinal gradient, increasing from high to low latitudes\. Among the examined climatic variables, temperature showed strong associations with community leaf area in high\-latitude boreal forests and low\-latitude tropical forests, whereas precipitation was more important in mid\-latitude forests and semi\-arid forests\. Assuming unchanged climate–trait relationships, our projections under the SSP3–7\.0 scenario suggest that 82\.3% of present\-day forests would experience increases in community leaf area by 2070–2100, with the largest relative increases occurring in boreal forests \(median: \+166%\)\. In contrast, 17\.7% of forests, primarily tropical forests in Africa and South America, would show slight decreases\. Our map provides important input for ecosystem models by illustrating the potential sensitivity of community leaf area to future climatic change and its possible implications for forest carbon cycling\.

## [AI Consciousness and the Law: Towards an AI Consciousness Legal Protocol](../publications/599634abe6cd2c80ef79.md)

Pavan Duggal

Artificial intelligence has not been shown to be conscious, yet the question has moved from philosophy into legislation and corporate research\. Some legislatures have begun to answer it by declaration, while developers now study model welfare and the internal states of their systems\. This paper argues that law can neither wait for science to settle the question nor settle it by decree\. It proposes an AI Consciousness Legal Protocol: a ten\-article instrument that sets the technical and legal parameters to be met before law recognises the consciousness of an AI system, entrusts that finding to an independent recognition body, and fixes the rules that govern AI in the meantime\. The paper distinguishes the dictionary, scientific and spiritual meanings of consciousness, and separates the contextual awareness that AI systems already display from the valenced experience and self\-directed decision that would alter legal relations\. Drawing on the indicator\-property method of Butlin, Long and co\-authors \(2023\), it proposes seven legal parameters \(independent evidence, valenced experience, persistent self, volition, understanding of consequences, absence of engineered mimicry, and reproducibility subject to review\) and a graded four\-category scale of recognition\. A comparative survey of India, the United Kingdom, the European Union and the United States shows that no legal system defines consciousness as such, and that Indian law already separates personhood from consciousness\. The central position is that recognition of consciousness, criminal capacity and legal personhood are three separate questions, and that human accountability for AI survives all three\. The AI Consciousness Legal Protocol is a scholarly proposal offered for the consideration of lawmakers and jurists\. It is not binding law and has not been adopted by any legislature or institution\. Contents: 1\. AI consciousness and the challenge before AI law; 2\. What is consciousness?; 3\. Awareness is not consciousness; 4\. The technical parameters of consciousness; 5\. The legal parameters of consciousness; 6\. What existing law already says about consciousness; 7\. The Pandora&\#x27;s box: mens rea, liability and personhood; 8\. The AI Consciousness Legal Protocol \(Articles 1 to 10\); 9\. Conclusion\.

## [Genetic pleiotropy highlights immune mechanisms that link insomnia and C\-reactive protein](../publications/59978e5d5251a64cd03d.md)

Farah Abou Daya; Jesse Tyler Valliere; Matthew Maher; Richa Saxena

Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder with growing evidence implicating immune and inflammatory processes\. Elevated C\-reactive protein \(CRP\), a marker of systemic inflammation, is frequently observed in individuals with poor sleep, yet the genetic basis of this relationship remains unclear\. This study aims to characterize the shared genetic architecture between insomnia and CRP using large\-scale genomic data\. CRP levels were significantly elevated in 130 611 individuals with insomnia compared with 327 375 controls in the UK Biobank\. Genome\-wide genetic correlation, pleiotropic analysis, colocalization, Mendelian randomization \(MR\), and functional annotation were used to characterize shared genetic architecture and biological pathways\. Insomnia and CRP showed a significant positive genetic correlation\. We identified 125 pleiotropic loci jointly associated with insomnia and CRP\. Functional annotation implicated chromatin organization and nucleosome assembly, while pathway analyses highlighted immune signaling, cellular senescence, and programmed cell death\. Colocalization analysis provided support for shared causal variants at six loci in or near APOE, HLA\-B, NLGN1, AK5/DNAJB4, FAM114A2/GRIA1, and SATB1\. Bidirectional MR provided stronger evidence for a directional relationship from insomnia liability to elevated CRP than in the reverse direction\. This study uncovers shared genetic mechanisms linking insomnia and systemic inflammation\. The directional genetic relationship from insomnia liability to elevated CRP suggests that sleep dysfunction may contribute to inflammatory processes\.

## [Clinically relevant chromosomal abnormalities and chromosomal polymorphisms in 7,530 patients undergoing reproductive genetic counseling: a retrospective cytogenetic study in a Chinese Han population](../publications/59a1e9cc5c3bffb2a8a7.md)

吴松航 Wu Songhang; Hongyan Shang; Wenhua Wang; Dan Chen; Wennan Wu

Background Chromosomal aberrations are important causes of reproductive disorders, but their clinical interpretation is often complicated by the presence of benign chromosomal polymorphisms that may obscure the true diagnostic yield of karyotyping\. The aim of this study was to evaluate peripheral blood karyotyping in patients undergoing reproductive genetic counseling and to distinguish clinically relevant chromosomal abnormalities from chromosomal polymorphisms\. Methods A total of 7,530 patients who visited the reproductive center and the obstetrics and gynecology genetic clinic of the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University from January 2016 to December 2022 were included\. Peripheral blood karyotyping was performed using lymphocyte culture, routine chromosome preparation, and G\-banding\. Cytogenetic findings were classified into clinically relevant chromosomal abnormalities and chromosomal polymorphisms\. Chromosomal polymorphisms were analyzed separately and were not counted as the primary diagnostic outcome\. Correspondence analysis was performed using an observed\-count matrix linking major clinical manifestations with representative karyotypic findings\. Results A total of 552 abnormal cytogenetic findings were detected, corresponding to an overall cytogenetic finding rate of 7\.33% \(552/7,530\)\. Among them, 246 cases were classified as clinically relevant chromosomal abnormalities, giving a primary diagnostic rate of 3\.27% \(246/7,530\), whereas 306 cases were chromosomal polymorphisms, accounting for 4\.06% of the total cohort and 55\.43% of all abnormal cytogenetic findings\. In correspondence analysis, the first two dimensions explained 77\.9% and 15\.2% of the total inertia, respectively\. The global chi\-square test indicated a non\-random association between clinical manifestations and representative karyotypic findings \(chi\-square = 69\.92, df = 16, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion Peripheral blood karyotyping remains a useful first\-line cytogenetic test in reproductive genetic counseling\. Clinically relevant chromosomal abnormalities and chromosomal polymorphisms should be reported and interpreted separately\. Phenotype\-guided interpretation may improve the clinical value of karyotyping and help identify patients who require additional molecular confirmation or multidisciplinary counseling\.

## [From Flow\-Box Invariants to Global Conservation Laws: Machine Learning\-Assisted Detection of Singularities and Near\-Integrability](../publications/59a9ab8da951b8ec9e48.md)

Jimmie Adriazola; Ioannis G\. Kevrekidis; Panayotis G\. Kevrekidis; Wei Zhu

Conservation laws reveal invariant structure in dynamical systems and constrain their evolution to lower\-dimensional level sets\. Locally, however, per the flow\-box theorem, every $d$\-dimensional system generically admits $d\-1$ functionally independent conservation laws near a regular point even though, generically, only a few such laws persist globally\. Data\-driven methods typically learn conservation laws on a prescribed region of phase space from which training samples are drawn, leaving their behavior beyond that region unresolved\. We formulate this local\-to\-global continuation problem and develop an \{expanding\-domain neural deflation\} framework that tracks the number of independent conservation laws over nested domains\. The method recovers the expected $d\-1$ local invariants and detects their successive breakdown as the domain expands, relaxing to the expected global conservation law limit\. It distinguishes the local invariants \(associated with Frobenius integrability\) from persistent global structure and shows that the domain scale over which additional laws survive reflects proximity to Liouville integrability\. Pointwise losses can localize isolated obstructions, whereas in more complicated dynamics the breakdown of our loss functions is gradual and spatially diffuse\. The framework thus provides a data\-driven approach for studying the persistence and breakdown of \(so\-far\-learned\) conservation laws across phase space\.

## [AI literacy and STEM education: emerging frontiers and research priorities](../publications/59a9f37b6f06ddb5d92b.md)

Jonas Hällström; Thomas K\. F\. Chiu; Meixia Ding; Milo Koretsky; Yeping Li

Abstract This article examines the state of the art in AI literacy and STEM education and identifies emerging frontiers and research priorities to inspire cutting\-edge empirical and theoretical research\. The reviewed research is grounded in established AI literacy frameworks and shows that there is potential for students’ development of a critical and technologically informed AI literacy\. However, the research is unevenly spread across the STEM disciplines and the potential for AI to transform STEM learning remains unclear\. Thus, while the field has expanded rapidly, particularly with the emergence of generative AI \(GenAI\), fundamental challenges remain\. The conceptual ambiguity surrounding AI literacy, combined with the rapid evolution of AI technologies, demands continued theoretical refinement and empirical investigation\. Critical questions remain regarding how AI literacy intersects with disciplinary STEM literacies, how GenAI tools both support and reshape teaching and learning processes, and what opportunities and trade\-offs arise when students engage with AI as learning partner\. The ethical dilemmas of AI integration, including bias, data privacy, and environmental sustainability, also warrant urgent attention\. As STEM education increasingly engages with AI as both a subject of learning and a learning tool, future research must move beyond one\-size\-fits\-all frameworks toward context\-sensitive approaches that empower educators and learners to critically and responsibly engage with AI while preserving core STEM learning goals\. This article highlights key research frontiers and priorities for advancing scholarship at the intersection of AI literacy and STEM education\.

## [การไวผลตอการเจรญเตบโตและผลผลตของเมลอนในระบบไฮโดรโปนกส](../publications/59d2f4cdd7b931a98a65.md)

Sorapong Benchasri; Piyawan Anantasid; Supreeya Benchasri; Kritsana Ruengklary

This study aimed to investigate the effects of different fruit\-loading levels on the growth and yield of melon produced using a hydroponic system based on the Floating Root Technique \(FRT\)\. The experiment was conducted at Thaksin University, Phatthalung Campus, using a Completely Randomized Design \(CRD\) with four replications and five plants per replication\. Fourteen\-day\-old seedlings were transplanted into the hydroponic system at a spacing of 40 cm between plants and 60 cm between rows\. Three fruit\-loading treatments were evaluated: one fruit per plant \(Tr1\), which served as the control; two fruits per plant \(Tr2\); and three fruits per plant \(Tr3\)\. At 31 days after pollination, fresh fruit weight did not differ significantly between Tr1 and Tr2, with values of 2,121\.84 and 1,680\.12 g per fruit, respectively\. Tr2 produced the highest total fresh weight at 3,360\.24 g per plant, followed by Tr3 and Tr1, at 2,996\.61 and 2,121\.84 g per plant, respectively\. Fruit sweetness ranged from 14\.32 to 14\.34 °Brix, with no statistically significant differences among treatments\. In addition, Tr2 produced the highest fresh yield per 100 m², at 1,401\.22 kg, corresponding to an estimated revenue of 140,122\.00 Baht\. Therefore, under the conditions of this experiment, retaining two fruits per plant was the most suitable treatment in terms of total fresh yield and economic returns\.

## [SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC\-derived mutant FUS\-ALS motor neurons](../publications/59dc4801acf598874f29.md)

Rianne de Jongh; Anna F\. Wiersema; Charlotte H\. van Dijk; Roos C\. Verdegaal; Mareine M\. J\. Smulders; Onur Başak; Jelle van Os; Sofie Peeters; Laura Olmedo\-Martínez; Lauri M\. Bloemenkamp; Keith M\. Garner; Sandrine Da Cruz; Max Koppers; Alessandro Iuliano; W\.W\.M\. Pim Pijnappel; Kevin Patrick Kenna; R\. Jeroen Pasterkamp

Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis \(ALS\) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron \(MN\) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes\. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood\. Here, we exploit FUS\-ALS to interrogate cell compartment\-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell \(iPSC\)\-derived MN\. This approach identifies compartment\-specific 3’ untranslated region \(3’UTR\) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons\. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA , previously linked to neurodegeneration\. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS\-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS\-ALS\. Using a fully iPSC\-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS\-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction \(NMJ\) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo\-excitability\. Our study provides insight into compartment\-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ\-on\-a\-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS\-ALS\.

## [Indian Knowledge Systems for Climate\-Resilient Highways and Sustainable Infrastructure](../publications/59e8ea56894a45ebafcc.md)

Max T\.

India&\#x27;s roads are transporting food, medicines, cargo and chance through one of the world&\#x27;s most climate\-vulnerable areas\. Road infrastructure resilience is now regularly challenged each year with cloud bursts and landslides in the hills and interior, floods in the coastal area, floods and cyclones in the Indo\-Gangetic plains, and prolonged heat waves in the oceanic interiors\. This book emphasises that both modern engineering and the wisdom of Indian Knowledge Systems \(IKS\) gathered over centuries, need to be applied to the transport sector in the context of climate change, in an evidence\-based and respectful manner\. Since times immemorial, repair and maintenance of stepwells, tanks, ponds and canals along with planting of trees and protection of sacred groves has been carried out by the Indian communities\. They were not water war, but rather “water walk through” in terms of traditional ecological knowledge practices\. Today they serve as real\-life examples to inspire climate resilient highways and sustainable infrastructure, but only if they are not romanticised\. There are seven chapters in one thread\. Chapter 1 will introduce IKS for climate\-resilient highways and map the traditional wisdom with highway functions\. The following chapter \(2\) reviews traditional water harvesting and NbD approaches for drainage such as bioswales, ground water recharge and road draining\. Examples of artificial intelligence and machine learning backed by remote sensing and digital twins and explainable AI to enable predictive maintenance, flood forecasting, landslide early warning system and intelligent transportation systems are presented in chapter 3\. Sustainable pavements and circular economy materials are reviewed in Chapter 4 including reclaimed asphalt pavement, warm mix asphalt, low\-carbon concrete and permeable pavements, as well as waste plastic roads\. Chapter 5 addresses embodied carbon, operational carbon and low\-carbon infrastructure, how they connect to the design of highways and the application of net zero and green public procurement\. Special attention is given to addressing the need for biodiversity conservation in the context of building a green highway as an implementation of road ecology, wildlife corridors, native species plantations and involving communities in conservation, as highlighted in chapter 6\. These are then woven into the staged approach to sustainable infrastructure planning in chapter 7, which includes slope stabilisation, bioengineering, drainage design and governance\. The book offers, throughout, each traditional idea along with a modern tool and a measurable indicator\. It also makes it clear what hasn&\#x27;t been proven\. Tradition should not take the place of geotechnical investigation, hydrological modelling, pavement testing\. The goal is “pudsey engineering”: pilot studies, field monitoring, study with local inhabitants, so that the knowledge of heritage can be confirmed and put to engineering use in a general way\. The book uses accessible language to communicate to civil engineers, transportation planners, environmental scientists, policymakers, researchers and students\. At the end of each chapter there are research gaps and a research agenda to be pushed forward by researchers in the fields of sustainable development, resilient infrastructure and climate policy\. It is designed to make recommendations that will be used to guide national highway programmes and state agencies and project teams\. I hope that readers will find highways as more than asphalts ribbons, but as living corridors, not just ways to move water and carbon, but also biodiversity and communities\. If with this book one project more listening to the land prior to building it, and the union of science and tradition in the service of low carbon and climate smart roads more, it has served its purpose\.

## [Sentimental Analysis App with MLOps](../publications/59ed1887cdbec231bc0e.md)

Dr\. B\. Pannalal Gajula Deepak

An application\-oriented sentiment classification framework is presented to process short English\-language text through a lightweight natural\-language pipeline and an APImediated web interface\. The implementation uses TextBlob polarity estimation, FastAPI for request validation and inference delivery, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for interactive feedback\. A polarity\-based decision rule maps analyzed text to positive, negative, and neutral classes, while presentation components provide visual cues and a compact response workflow\. The associated engineering design addresses version control, container packaging, reproducibility, automated testing, and staged CI/CD adoption\. The project report describes an evaluation involving 200 human\-labeled sentences and reports 95% classification accuracy, 93\.5% F1\-score, and 0\.35 s average response time; these figures are presented as reported project observations because the underlying per\-class confusion matrix and individual timing traces are not supplied\. The findings illustrate the feasibility of lightweight text opinion mining alongside a maintainable web\-service architecture, while identifying limitations for sarcasm, contextual semantics, and verified deployment automation\.

## [AN ANALYSIS OF THE METAPHOR IN MAMMAN VATSA’S POEM, “HOMECOMING”: AN ANALYSIS OF THE METAPHOR IN MAMMAN VATSA’S POEM, “HOMECOMING”](../publications/59f9621afb384cb2a0cd.md)

Aliyu Muhammad GADANYA; Yahaya Ismail Isa; Jamilu Ahmed

This paper analyses metaphorical expressions in Mamman Vatsa’s poem, “Homecoming,” by using the Conceptual Metaphor Theory \(CMT\)\. Six metaphorical expressions that employ ontological metaphors, specifically BUILDING IS A PERSON and OBJECT IS A PERSON, were identified and analysed in the study\. By specifically adopting Lakoff and Johnson&\#x27;s Metaphors we live by \(1980, 2003\) as theoretical framework, the research demonstrates how the poet uses sustained metaphors to show the desertion experienced during the Nigerian Civil War \(1967\-1970\)\. The findings reveal that Vatsa&\#x27;s use of metaphors besides serving as ornamental devices, it also serves as cognitive mechanisms that make readers to conceptualize abstract experiences of war, loss, and loneliness through concretisation of the domains\. This study contributes to the exploration of metaphors in poetry and gives an insight into how soldier\-poets employ figurative language to tell traumatic historical experiences in Africa\. Keywords: Conceptual Metaphor Theory, ontological metaphor, Mamman Vatsa, civil war literature, African poetry

## [Inteligência artificial na gestão em enfermagem: scoping review](../publications/5a027772624d37613386.md)

Sofia Pinto Bernardino; Palmira Martins Gonçalves Azevedo; Carla Pinto Bernardino; Elisabete De Fátima Lavrador Gonçalves; Paula Maria Carvalho Xavier; Sara Emanuel Da Silva Brandão Ribeiro

The growing integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in organizations has been profoundly transforming leadership processes, decision\-making, and team management\. Between 2019 and 2026, the literature shifted from a predominantly technological approach to a view focused on human\-AI interaction, emphasizing digital leadership skills, ethics, algorithmic governance, and organizational transformation\. AI has been energizing healthcare systems, with increasing applications in nursing, not only in direct care but also in workforce management, care organization, decision support, document automation, and performance monitoring\. A scoping review was conducted to map the evidence published between 2021 and 2026 on the use of AI in nursing management, identifying applications, benefits, barriers, ethical implications, and knowledge gaps\. Eleven articles were included in the final review\. The most recent studies suggest that AI can improve operational efficiency, support resource management, enhance patient safety, and assist nursing leaders in decision\-making\. However, challenges remain related to AI literacy, interoperability, data privacy, and the lack of involvement of nurse managers in implementing solutions\. AI emerges as a strategic opportunity for nursing management, but its real value will depend on governance quality, the profession itself, process transparency, data protection, and the active involvement of nursing leadership\. It&\#x27;s essential to turn this innovation into sustainable improvement focused on people and ethics\.

## [The AI Trust Gap: Consumer Perceptions of AI\-Powered Digital Marketing](../publications/5a04e194ed96cac55d85.md)

Jennifer Wehr Holt; Linh Nguyen

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly used in digital marketing to personalize communications, recommend products, and automate customer interactions\. Despite these capabilities, consumer trust in AI\-powered marketing remains uncertain\. This exploratory study examines consumer perceptions of AI\-driven digital marketing using survey data collected from 500 U\.S\. adults\. Findings suggest that consumers generally recognize the usefulness of AI\-powered marketing but remain cautious about whether organizations using AI act in consumers’ best interests\. Respondents expressed concerns regarding privacy, data use, and organizational trustworthiness, while transparency and data security emerged as important trust\-building factors\. Moderate daily AI users \(2–5 hours\) reported higher levels of trust in companies employing AI\-driven marketing practices than light users \(&lt;2 hours\)\. Overall, the findings suggest that consumer acceptance of AI’s functional benefits does not necessarily translate into trust in organizations that deploy these technologies\. Implications for marketing managers and directions for future research are discussed\.

## [LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning](../publications/5a110f2e5ab3053f06cf.md)

Oladimeji Macaulay; Ala Jararweh; David Arredondo; Luis E\. Tafoya; Shrey Poshiya; Yue Hu; Olufunmilola Oyebamiji; Yanfu Zhang; Christopher Ian Amos; Kushal Virupakshappa; Avinash D Sahu

Abstract Representation learning in genomics often relies on sequence, expression, and network data, thereby overlooking a wealth of insights in the scientific literature\. Here, we present LitGene, an interpretable transformer\-based model that refines gene representations by integrating unstructured textual information with Gene Ontology annotations through contrastive learning\. In evaluations across eight benchmark tasks for protein properties, LitGene achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits zero\-shot prediction of GO terms, KEGG pathways, and gene\-disease associations\. LitGene identified ANGPTL6 as a potential candidate gene for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis \(IPF\), supported by its differential expression in independent IPF samples, illustrating LitGene’s utility for hypothesis generation\. A SHAP\-based interpretability tool highlights text features influencing predictions, while an automated literature\-grounding framework provides corroborating support where available\. Our results suggest that integrating textual and genetic information may help reduce biases associated with under\-studied genes\. The model is released as open\-source code, along with a publicly accessible web interface at https://litgene\.cs\.unm\.edu/ , which allows users to submit gene names, disease names, drug names, or custom text \(e\.g\., publication abstracts\) to obtain evidence\-based predictions of related biomedical entities\.

## [Promoting sustainable travel intentions: the effect of information nudges](../publications/5a2a93d308db1bb97e6a.md)

Martina Shakya; Franziska Drescher

Introduction Tourism contributes substantially to global greenhouse gas emissions\. To reduce travel\-related carbon emissions, a shift toward more sustainable travel choices is urgently needed\. Research has consistently shown a significant gap between environmental attitudes and sustainable travel behaviors\. Yet, it has proven difficult to promote sustainable travel behavior without understanding and narrowing the gap between environmental attitudes and sustainable travel intentions\. This study examines the effect of information nudges to support the shift toward more climate\-friendly travel intentions\. Methods We conducted randomized choice experiments among a large sample of German holidaymakers \( n = 2,186\), covering the three main segments of German vacation demand: domestic/proximity tourism, mid\-range Mediterranean travel, and long\-haul travel\. Participants first self\-selected their preferred travel segment, allowing for realistic decision\-making scenarios, and were then randomly assigned to one of three carbon\-related information nudges or a baseline condition without additional information\. We examined the effects of the nudges on transport and accommodation choices\. Results The results indicate that carbon\-related information can influence specific travel choices toward more climate\-friendly alternatives, although effects were not consistently observed across all contexts and nudges\. Significant effects were found particularly for transport choices in Mediterranean travel and for accommodation choices in this segment\. Discussion The findings suggest that communicating carbon emissions can contribute to narrowing the gap between environmental attitudes and sustainable travel intentions, particularly among travelers who value ecological responsibility\. However, the heterogeneous effects across travel contexts indicate that this effectiveness depends on the specific travel decision and choice context\. Disclosing carbon\-related information for various travel offers therefore appears as an effective approach to fostering more climate\-friendly travel intentions, although its effectiveness varies across different market segments\.

## [Neural Network\-Based Surrogate Modelling for Accelerated and Accurate Thermal History Prediction in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing \(WAAM\) of Ti\-6Al\-4V alloy](../publications/5a3b2f059ca1c56b97a2.md)

Andi Ismail; Omar Fadili; Rijal Surya Rahmany

Abstract Thermal history during wire arc additive manufacturing \(WAAM\) governs microstructural evolution and mechanical properties, but FEM simulations used to predict it are too computationally expensive for iterative process optimisation\. Prior surrogate models have also rarely reported which input features drive their predictions, leaving physical interpretability largely unaddressed\. We developed an interpretable feed\-forward neural network surrogate \(FFNN\) for fast thermal\-cycle prediction in WAAM of Ti\-6Al\-4V, built in PyTorch and trained on \~65 million spatiotemporal points from FEM simulation\. The model achieved a training R² of 0\.998 and RMSE of 8\.7 °C across \~25\-2000 °C\. On unseen current levels, it generalized well \(R² = 0\.9968–0\.9971, RMSE = 10\.9\-13\.4 °C\), with per\-current RMSE ranging from 7\.7 °C to 23\.9 °C across all four monitoring points\. Feature analysis, re\-verified on the full test set, identified cumulative deposition time, torch position, and arc source distance as the dominant predictors; current ranked lowest under both permutation and SHAP importance, though partial\-dependence analysis confirmed this reflects smaller effect size not physical unimportance with current exerting a real, monotonic influence that interacts with build height\. The FFNN\-surrogate cuts computation time substantially, offering a practical tool for rapid process analysis and optimisation in Ti\-6Al\-4V WAAM\.

## [Metabolic control of methylation landscapes in cancer growth and plasticity: targeting the epigenetic–metabolic axis with natural compounds and emerging therapies](../publications/5a4c1aa74644cd3f1210.md)

Qi Liu; Ying Yu; Wenbo Li; Xinxu Chen; Zekai Shi; Gang Li; Shibo Wei; Zongjian Luo

Cancer cell plasticity enables tumor cells to dynamically transition between diverse phenotypic states, including epithelial–mesenchymal plasticity stemness, dormancy, lineage switching, immune evasion, and therapy\-resistant phenotypes\. Although metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation have each been recognized as hallmarks of cancer, the mechanistic framework linking metabolic adaptation to dynamic cell\-state transitions remains incompletely understood\. In this Review, we propose that methylation serves as a major mechanistic interface through which metabolic rewiring can influence adaptive cancer cell plasticity\. We discuss how one\-carbon metabolism regulates the availability of the universal methyl donor S\-adenosylmethionine \(SAM\), thereby influencing DNA methylation, histone methylation, and multiple forms of RNA methylation, with N6\-methyladenosine \(m 6 A\) representing the principal RNA modification discussed in this review\. Rather than responding uniformly to metabolic change, these methylation systems represent distinct but metabolically connected regulatory layers that share dependence on one\-carbon metabolism while differing in their biochemical sensitivities and regulatory outputs\. Net methylation states, however, are also shaped by metabolically constrained demethylation, including α\-ketoglutarate\-, oxygen\-, Fe 2\+ \-, and flavin adenine dinucleotide \(FAD\)\-dependent eraser pathways\. Together, these metabolically responsive writing and erasing processes influence transcriptional stability, chromatin accessibility, and post\-transcriptional regulation during reversible cell\-state transitions\. We further examine how environmental and therapeutic stresses, including hypoxia, nutrient limitation, immune surveillance, and anticancer therapy, reshape methylation programs through metabolic adaptation, and how such remodeling may support phenotypic flexibility and survival under selective pressure\. Building upon these advances, we propose the concept of the adaptive methylation landscape, a perturbation\-responsive, state\-associated, and potentially reversible distribution of methylation states that contributes to shaping the spectrum of cellular states accessible during tumor evolution\. Finally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the metabolic\-methylation axis and highlight how single\-cell multi\-omics, spatial epigenomics, functional epigenome editing, and AI may enable dynamic mapping of adaptive methylation landscapes\. We propose that cancer cell plasticity is not merely a genetic phenomenon but can also be shaped by metabolically responsive methylation programs, providing a testable conceptual framework for future precision epigenetic therapies\.

## [Association between self\-efficacy and AI dependence among medical postgraduates: a multicenter cross\-sectional study with exploratory prediction](../publications/5a5f7973b868ea427e86.md)

Meng\-Pan Li; Meng\-Jian Ren; Jiang\-Peng Wu; Zhaohui Li; Tong\-Tong Liu; Hao\-Ran Chen; Heng\-Yi Guo; Wencai Liu; Yafei Jiang; Ling\-Feng Yu; Xiao\-Jun Ma

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly used in postgraduate medical education and research, but the relationship between self\-efficacy and dependence\-like reliance on AI remains insufficiently characterized\. We examined the association between continuous self\-efficacy and AI\-dependence scores and separately explored prediction of sample\-relative higher AI\-dependence scores\. This multicenter cross\-sectional online survey included 1,546 valid questionnaires from medical postgraduates at six participating Chinese universities between January and March 2026\. Self\-efficacy was assessed using a five\-item study\-specific academic measure, and AI dependence was assessed using a direct Chinese translation of the 22\-item Artificial Intelligence Addiction Scale for Researchers\. Analyses used multivariable linear regression with HC3 standard errors, restricted cubic splines, model diagnostics, and item\-overlap sensitivity analyses\. Exploratory prediction used the sample median score of 70 as a non\-diagnostic boundary and a fixed 70:30 training/test split for internal validation\. Among 1,546 participants, 938 \(60\.7%\) were women and 579 \(37\.5%\) studied clinical medicine\. In the primary adjusted model, each 5\-point higher self\-efficacy score was associated with a 5\.296\-point lower AI\-dependence score \(95% CI, \-5\.918 to \-4\.674; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Restricted cubic splines supported the overall association \(chi\-square = 287\.10; df = 3; P &lt; 0\.001\) and modest nonlinearity \(chi\-square = 8\.79; df = 2; P = 0\.012\)\. After removal of clearly overlapping items from both instruments, the Model 3 estimate changed by 2\.1% \(beta = \-5\.187; 95% CI, \-5\.800 to \-4\.575\)\. The exploratory model achieved an AUC of 0\.875 \(95% CI, 0\.845–0\.906\) in the held\-out internal test set\. Higher self\-efficacy was inversely associated with continuous AI\-dependence scores among medical postgraduates\. These findings suggest that AI\-literacy education may need to support autonomous task engagement and critical verification of AI outputs, but the cross\-sectional design precludes causal interpretation\. The exploratory prediction analysis was internally validated only, used a sample\-relative boundary, and requires independent validation before practical use\.

## [Offline social and civic engagement as an ecological correlate of adolescent internet addiction: multilevel evidence from Chinese adolescents](../publications/5a6dc338d96db8bd2d92.md)

Chengcheng Ma; Yayun Shen; Miao Chen; Yaochen Yang

Internet addiction \(IA\) has been a growing mental\-health concern during adolescence\. Although prior research has emphasized individual and family\-related risk factors, less attention has been given to how adolescents’ everyday offline social environments relate to digital well\-being\. This study examined whether offline social and civic engagement \(OSCE\) is associated with adolescent IA at both individual and classroom\-context levels and whether socio\-emotional competence \(SEC\) helped explain this relationship\. Using cross\-sectional survey data collected in Spring 2025, we analyzed data from 7,121 secondary school students nested within 329 classrooms across five regions in China\. Multilevel modeling was used to examine associations between OSCE, SEC, and IA while accounting for classroom clustering\. Machine\-learning analyses using accumulated local effects \(ALE\) plots were conducted to explore nonlinear and heterogeneous patterns in the OSCE–IA association across academic pressure, educational aspiration, and parent–child relationship quality\. Higher OSCE was associated with lower IA at both the individual and classroom levels\. SEC partly explained the association between OSCE and IA at the within\-class level\. Classroom OSCE climate was also negatively associated with IA, suggesting that broader engagement climates may be associated with adolescents’ digital behaviors beyond individual participation alone\. Machine\-learning analyses further revealed nonlinear patterns in the OSCE–IA association across academic and family contexts, with stronger negative associations observed under conditions of higher academic pressure and more supportive parent–child relationships\. The findings support an ecological perspective on adolescent digital well\-being in which offline participation contexts and socio\-emotional competencies are associated with lower problematic internet use\. Structured offline social and civic engagement may represent an important social\-contextual correlate of healthier digital engagement among adolescents\.

## [A Governance Framework for Operationalising Responsible AI Use in Students’ Research Projects: Illustrations from Viet Nam](../publications/5a6ec34aa19ba4394084.md)

Dao Mai Thi Tran

Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly used in students’ research projects for literature searching, idea development, drafting, language editing, information processing, and research planning\. These uses can support research learning, but they also raise academic integrity concerns, including unverifiable sources, fabricated references, undeclared AI assistance, over\-reliance on AI\-generated outputs, unclear authorship, and unfair assessment\. This conceptual paper argues that responsible AI use in students’ research projects cannot be secured through individual AI literacy or general guidance alone\. Higher education institutions also need governance mechanisms that make AI use transparent, verifiable, assessable, and accountable\. Using targeted literature identification and structured conceptual synthesis, the paper maps recurring governance problems to normative principles, institutional requirements, and operational mechanisms\. It proposes a five\-component framework corresponding to five governance functions: policy \(boundary setting\), transparency \(traceability\), assessment \(evaluability\), audit \(assurance\), and guidance/support \(capability building\)\. Viet Nam is used as an illustrative emerging AI governance context, where national policy directions on digital competence and AI are developing but operational mechanisms for student research remain under\-specified\. The framework and associated tools are presented as adaptable design artefacts for future institutional testing rather than as validated interventions\.

## [Application and Assessment of Machine Learning Methods for Aircraft Design Problems](../publications/5a76626f1477976d3b99.md)

Dilan Kilic; Melike Nikbay

In this work, we present a comparative study on machine\-learning\-based surrogate modeling for multidisciplinary aerospace applications\. The main objective of the work is to demonstrate the predictive capability of traditional machine learning methods, including linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, Gaussian process regression, and multilayer perceptron, on multidisciplinary engineering problems\. The selected datasets are determined at different complexity levels and disciplines\. These methods are first applied to two benchmark functions with different mathematical characteristics and then to four engineering design problems\. The models are evaluated using different training sample sizes and multiple random data partitions to assess their predictive performance and robustness\. The models are compared in terms of the coefficient of determination \(\[Formula: see text\]\), normalized root mean squared error, normalized mean absolute error, and computational cost\. The obtained results show that the relative performance of the surrogate models varies with problem dimensionality and training sample size\. In particular, Gaussian process regression and support vector regression provide consistently high predictive accuracy across the investigated engineering problems, while the computational requirements and sensitivity to data partitioning differ among the methods\.

## [生成式人工智能赋能地方非遗视觉转译与传播机制研究](../publications/5a77a8b937a1842281d5.md)

Dian Jin

在&quot;数字中国&quot;建设与非遗活态传承的双重背景下，生成式人工智能（AIGC）为地方民俗类非遗的视觉表达与青年传播提供了新路径。本文以人类非物质文化遗产代表作&quot;浦江板凳龙&quot;为研究对象，提出&quot;文化符号—表征策略&quot;（CS\-RS）理论模型，构建&quot;符号提取—AIGC转译—传播适配&quot;三段式视觉转译机制。通过Midjourney与Stable Diffusion平台开展Prompt生成实验，结合326份青年问卷与三类群体半结构式访谈，验证文化语义嵌入策略对生成效果的提升作用及青年群体对AIGC非遗内容的接受度。研究发现：文化语义嵌入Prompt组在识别度（4\.2/5）与文化还原度（4\.0/5）上显著优于基础组；78\.5%的青年受访者对AIGC非遗内容表示感兴趣，65\.3%愿意在社交媒体分享。本文最终形成&quot;Prompt—生成—反馈—迭代&quot;的传播闭环，为地方非遗数字化传承与文旅融合提供可操作的路径参考。

## [Reinforcement learning to disentangle multiqubit quantum states from partial observations](../publications/5a79cdd57782b5716ac4.md)

Pavel Tashev; Stefan Petrov; Matthew T\. Diaz; Friederike Metz; Alaina M\. Green; Norbert M\. Linke; Marin Bukov

Using partial knowledge of a quantum state to control multiqubit entanglement is a largely unexplored paradigm in the emerging field of quantum interactive dynamics with the potential to address outstanding challenges in quantum state preparation and compression, quantum control, and quantum complexity\. We present a deep reinforcement learning \(RL\) approach using an actor\-critic algorithm for constructing short disentangling circuits for states with up to 16 qubits\. With access to only two\-qubit reduced density matrices, our agent decides which pairs of qubits to apply two\-qubit gates on; requiring only local information makes it directly applicable on modern NISQ devices, as we demonstrated experimentally on a trapped\-ion quantum computer\. Utilizing a permutation\-equivariant transformer architecture, the agent can autonomously identify qubit permutations within the state, and adjusts the disentangling protocol accordingly\. Once trained, it provides circuits from different initial states without further optimization\. We demonstrate the agent&\#x27;s ability to identify and exploit the entanglement structure of multi\-qubit states\. We analyze the disentangling circuits constructed by the agent for 4\- and 5\-qubit Haar\-random states, and observe strong correlations between consecutive gates and among the qubits involved\. Through extensive benchmarking, we show the efficacy of the RL approach to find disentangling protocols with minimal gate resources\. We explore the resilience of our trained agents to noise, highlighting their potential for real\-world quantum computing applications\. Analyzing optimal disentangling protocols, we report a general circuit to prepare an arbitrary 4\-qubit state using at most 5 two\-qubit \(10 CNOT\) gates\.

## [Food Recognition and Nutrition Estimator Using Computer Vision and Machine Learning](../publications/5a8cd463122d7a7f7499.md)

Vijayaraghavan R; V\. S\. Anita Sofia

Food logging works when it is simple enough to become a habit\. Traditional nutrition programs often require the user to browse a list of foods, choose a food, and guess at a portion size, and then repeat the procedure for each food item in a meal\. CrunchUP resolves that friction by using a photo of a meal to create a nutrition record\. The system is a complete web application, where a user uploads an image or takes a picture using their camera, a FastAPI service checks and standardizes the image, and the Google Gemini vision model identifies the foods visible in the image and estimates the quantity, calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, and fibre\. The response is validated, converted into application objects, displayed to the user and optionally stored in PostgreSQL\. The information on a personal profile includes height, weight, age, gender, activity level, and fitness goal\. These values are used for the calculation of BMI, basal metabolic rate according to Mifflin–St Jeor, total daily energy expenditure, calorie adjustment which is goal oriented and macronutrient targets\. The work is important because it brings together recognition, nutrition estimation, personal targets, meal history, trends and feedback for decision making in a single stream\. The report describes the requirements, literature background, architecture, database design, algorithms, security measures, implementation, verification strategy, restrictions and extensions for the future\. Separation of concerns is evident in the repository: the client is responsive \(React, Vite\); the service and data are implemented \(FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy\); access is protected \(JWT, bcrypt\); images are normalized \(Pillow\); and multimodal output is schema shaped \(Gemini 2\.5 Flash\)\. The dashboard consolidates intake and translates progress data into easy\-to\-understand recommendations\. A key finding is that a well\-defined vision\-language service can help ease recording effort in the diet, but needs to be interpreted as guidance, not a clinical measurement\. There is a need for future work including calibrated portion references, verified food databases, confidence reporting, culturally wider evaluation, personalised meal recommendation, and the development of a mobile app in the native application platform &quot;React Native&quot;\.

## [Explainable Cost Contingency Allocation Under Tail Risk in Road Projects Using CVaR–Shapley](../publications/5aad08c0b64d08d3564a.md)

Victor Andre Ariza Flores; Claudia Sernaque Montalvo; Gerber Zavala Ascaño; Widmar Balbin Lazo; Samir Augusto Arevalo Vidal

Cost contingency estimation in road projects requires not only quantifying the reserve needed under uncertainty but also identifying the risk sources that justify it, particularly under extreme cost scenarios\. This study proposes an explainable framework for estimating and allocating cost contingencies under tail risk by integrating Monte Carlo simulation, Conditional Value at Risk \(CVaR\), Shapley values, and explainable machine learning\. The framework was applied to a Peruvian road project considering 16 risk factors, 50,000 simulation scenarios, and 800 Shapley permutations\. For a baseline direct cost of S/312\.61 million \(USD 81\.24 million\), the P95 contingency was S/26\.88 million \(USD 6\.99 million\), whereas the CVaR95 contingency reached S/30\.23 million \(USD 7\.86 million\), highlighting the additional severity captured beyond the percentile threshold\. Low productivity, unforeseen interferences, quantity variation, adverse weather events, and freight and transportation jointly accounted for 60\.41% of the extreme contingency\. Variance contribution, predictive SHAP importance, and CVaR–Shapley attribution showed high ordinal agreement but relevant differences in contribution magnitudes and intermediate rankings\. The proposed framework transforms an aggregate tail\-risk reserve into risk\-specific monetary allocations, providing an auditable basis for prioritizing mitigation measures, strengthening budget justification, and supporting risk\-informed planning and financial resilience in road infrastructure projects\.

## [Data‐Driven Dynamics and Chaos Control in a Memristor‐Based Chua Circuit With ψ‐Caputo Fractional Derivatives](../publications/5aafeeb078f3d303fdcc.md)

Amin Jajarmi

ABSTRACT In this paper, the dynamics and regulation of a generalized fractional‐order memristive Chua circuit are investigated from practical, mathematical, and data‐oriented perspectives\. The proposed system involves the ‐Caputo fractional derivative, including a general kernel function , which allows it to describe heterogeneous memory effects and non‐uniform time scaling\. The paper proves the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ‐fractional system via Volterra‐type integral equations and the Banach fixed‐point theorem\. Additionally, an explicit Lyapunov estimate is derived, ensuring trajectory boundedness on every finite time interval and identifying the nonlinear memristive term&\#x27;s non‐positive contribution to the energy balance\. Moreover, we show that after a full equilibrium analysis, a memristive element generates a line of equilibria along the internal state variable \(‐axis\)\. Furthermore, Matignon&\#x27;s stability criterion defines the stability region in the complex plane and determines the local asymptotic stability of equilibrium points\. In addition, a predictor–corrector quadrature scheme is used to solve the nonlinear fractional differential equations involved and to provide reliable state‐trajectory data for identifying regime transitions\. We analyze the convergence and stability of the proposed method and prove that it has a global truncation error of , where is the time step size, and denotes the fractional order\. The numerical implementation is further validated using an exact‐solution benchmark and compared with an independent L1 predictor‐corrector method\. Numerical simulations for memristive circuits based on physical parameters also indicate that the fractional order is an important bifurcation parameter: lower values \(e\.g\., \) lead to steady periodic oscillations, while higher values \(e\.g\., \) lead to a double‐scroll‐like irregular response, numerically indicative of chaotic dynamics\. The instability of the chaotic regime is then discussed using linear state‐feedback control that suppresses unstable chaotic trajectories with a single scalar control input based on observed state data\. The present work, therefore, contributes to the study of data‐driven fractional‐order nonlinear dynamics and serves as a basis for secure communication, neuromorphic engineering, and memristor‐based signal‐processing applications\.

## [Constructing the Golf Course Biodiversity Index: Adapting the City Biodiversity Index for Application at the Scale of Individual Golf Facilities](../publications/5abd83fb3a006fbec248.md)

Jordan P\. Howell; Jordan Moore

Golf courses occupy millions of acres globally and have documented potential to support biodiversity in fragmented urban and peri\-urban landscapes\. Yet no standardized measure exists for assessing biodiversity performance at the scale of an individual facility\. This paper develops the Golf Course Biodiversity Index \(GCBI\), a proposed 17\-indicator composite index adapted from the City Biodiversity Index \(CBI\)\. The GCBI organizes indicators across three domains \(Native Biodiversity on the Course, Ecosystem Services Provided by Biodiversity, and Governance and Management of Biodiversity\), and each indicator scored 0 to 4\. The index is deliberately dual\-resolution: it reports a single total score \(maximum 68 points\) that communicates overall performance to non\-specialist audiences, together with three domain scores that make the sources of that performance diagnostically transparent\. Indicators and scoring thresholds are grounded in peer\-reviewed ecology, conservation biology, and golf sustainability scholarship, with the evidentiary basis and any provisional assumptions for each threshold documented in the supporting supplementary file\. We position the GCBI as the first stage of a multi\-stage index\-development program and specify the empirical validation required before deployment\. We then discuss three prospective applications: a biodiversity\-specific supplement to golf certification programs, a sponsor\-accountability instrument aligned with nature\-related disclosure frameworks, and a consumer\-facing score intended to generate market incentives for biodiversity investment\.

## [Deteksi Dini Karies dan Karang Gigi Berbasis Android Menggunakan CNN MobileNetV2 dan Transfer Learning](../publications/5adcc91b8f44d8754c97.md)

Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem klasifikasi citra gigi sebagai alat bantu deteksi dini karies, karang gigi, dan gigi normal menggunakan Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) arsitektur MobileNetV2 dengan pendekatan transfer learning yang diimplementasikan pada aplikasi Android\. Dataset Kaggle berjumlah 3\.539 citra; pemeriksaan hashing MD5 menemukan 467 citra duplikat pada kelas karang gigi sehingga dataset akhir berjumlah 2\.829 citra yang dibagi dengan rasio 70:15:15\. Citra diubah menjadi 224 × 224 piksel dan data latih diaugmentasi\. Pelatihan dilakukan dalam dua tahap, yaitu pelatihan classifier dengan base model dibekukan dan fine\-tuning sekitar 30 lapisan terakhir\. Evaluasi pada 425 citra uji menghasilkan akurasi 98,59% dengan precision, recall, dan F1\-score yang seimbang pada ketiga kelas, dengan enam citra salah diklasifikasikan, sebagian besar antara karies dan karang gigi\. Model diintegrasikan melalui FastAPI ke aplikasi Android berbasis Flutter\. Pengujian pada citra di luar dataset menunjukkan confidence yang lebih rendah akibat domain shift\. Sistem ini berpotensi menjadi alat bantu klasifikasi awal, bukan pengganti diagnosis tenaga medis, dan deduplikasi data perlu dilakukan sebelum pembagian dataset\.

## [MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High\-Quality Agentic Coding Data](../publications/5adfecabb7350439cf2e.md)

Donghoon Kim; Seunghyuk Oh; Kevin Galim; Minseo Kim; Minjae Lee; Younghyun Kim; Wooseok Seo; Hyung Il Koo; Wonjun Kang

Supervised fine\-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs\. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps\. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive\. We introduce MetaCurate, a training\-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments\. Disagreements between the filter&\#x27;s rankings and the judge&\#x27;s preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy\. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search\. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task\-specific handwritten criteria\. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand\-authored filtering as baselines\. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE\-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand\-authored rule\-based filtering and a training\-loop baseline whose search costs 3\.5x as much\.

## [Genome\-Wide DNA methylation profiling of tissue\-plasma pairs identifies Novel cfDNA biomarkers for the diagnosis of gastric cancer](../publications/5ae0b045dd817a528c65.md)

Hailing Ou; Jinli Miao; 凌阜生; Jie Gao; Tingan Wang; Zhi Ye; Chunbo Zhang; 黄名威; Yuzhou Qin

Screening for gastric cancer \(GC\) is critical for improving patient survival, yet current clinical methods suffer from invasiveness and limited sensitivity\. The aim of this study is to develop a machine learning model for the non\-invasive diagnosis of GC using the whole\-genome methylation profile of circulating free DNA \(cfDNA\) in plasma\. Plasma cfDNA from 61 patients with GC and 29 healthy controls\. First, whole‑genome bisulfite sequencing \(WGBS\) was performed on 29 paired GC and adjacent normal tissues to identify differentially methylated regions \(DMRs\)\. These tissue DMRs were then mapped to plasma cfDNA methylation data, yielding 32 stable DMRs that changed consistently in both tissues and plasma\. Using LASSO and Random Forest \(RF\) algorithms, eight core diagnostic markers were selected\. Four machine learning algorithms \(Support Vector Machine, RF, K\-Nearest Neighbor, Naïve Bayes\) were used to build diagnostic models\. WGBS revealed global hypomethylation and CpG island hypermethylation in GC, consistent with plasma cfDNA methylation patterns\. The RF model built on the eight cfDNA methylation markers \(annotated to genes including ATP8A2\) performed best, achieving AUC values of 0\.978 and 0\.938 in the training and independent test sets, respectively, with an accuracy of 88\.46%, sensitivity of 94\.44%, and specificity of 75\.00%\. After adjusting for age, the model achieved an AUC of 0\.924 on the test set, still demonstrating high discriminatory performance\. Functional analysis implicated these markers in pathways such as phagocytosis and axon guidance, and showed significant correlation with immune cell infiltration\. Notably, these core DMRs are not covered by the probes on the methylation arrays \(450K and EPIC v2\), highlighting the advantage of WGBS for novel biomarker discovery\. In conclusion, tissue\-plasma concordance analysis identified a panel of plasma cfDNA methylation biomarkers with strong diagnostic potential\. The resulting RF model provides a promising non\-invasive strategy for GC screening\.

## [Prevalence of Tuberculosis Among HIV Patients Treated at Public Health Facilities](../publications/5ae2e03aa11c40aab6c5.md)

Lesly Nayely Erazo Arias; Silvia Paola Monar Basantes

This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of tuberculosis among HIV patients treated in public health units through a systematic literature review\. The research was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, involving searches in PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases for the 2021–2026 period\. This process identified 446 initial records, and—following screening by title, abstract, and full text—25 studies meeting the established criteria were included\. Results showed a coinfection prevalence ranging from 4\.6% to 57\.3%, depending on the context; a CD4 lymphocyte count below 200 cells/mm³ emerged as the most consistent clinical predictor and the most frequently used laboratory marker for monitoring\. Meanwhile, treatment discontinuation, poverty, overcrowding, and social stigma were identified as the most significant cross\-cutting risk factors, alongside infectious comorbidities and associated mental disorders; evidence from Ecuador proved to be scarcer and more fragmented than that from other regions\. It is concluded that TB\-HIV coinfection remains a persistent public health issue with a magnitude that varies according to geographic and socioeconomic contexts; therefore, strengthening immunological screening, treatment adherence, the integration of diagnostic services, and the generation of local evidence in Ecuador is essential to narrowing the gap relative to international standards\.
