## [Comparative Analysis of Time Series Forecasting Models for Stock Price Prediction: ARIMA, LSTM, and Prophet](../publications/5b03288bc0e4a3d4afb9.md)

Muhammad Syahid Pebriadi; Tino Kemal Fattah; Putriana Salman; Rizky Amelia

Stock price forecasting with a uniform approach is a challenging process due to nonlinearity, regime changes, and seasonality\. The following paper would like to address the practical problem of selecting an appropriate model through comparing three widely used models such as ARIMA, LSTM, and Prophet based on how they are applied to different attributes of data and forecast\-related tasks\. The structured direct comparison will be our proposal, as to be able to identify the strengths and shortcomings in abiding by each model\. Each of the model is methodologically trained and tested on the same data stock price series and parameterized by the time of standard errors: MAE, MSE, RMSE and MAPE\. Experimental design is founded on the canonical setups and reasonable hyperparameters to an algorithm and the results are measured based on the hold\-out samples, which have volatile intervals\. The results show that under the conditions of intricate dynamics and large volatility, LSTM delivers the greatest general results with MAE = 277\.50, MSE = 165,244\.61, RMSE = 406\.50 and MAPE = 3\.09%\. ARIMA performs well on stable, approximately linear and stationary segments but struggles with nonlinearity and long\-term dependencies\. Prophet is effective when strong seasonal patterns are present and is robust to missing values and outliers\. We conclude that ARIMA suits stable series, LSTM is preferable for complex and rapidly changing markets, and Prophet is advantageous under pronounced seasonality\. These findings offer practical guidance for model selection aligned with data properties and forecasting goals\.

## [Mapping Projectome Heterogeneity of Subiculum Neuron Cell Types](../publications/5b10aae6d9b3d93e9847.md)

Ann W\. Saustad; Michael S\. Bienkowski

The subiculum \(SUB\) is the main output structure of the hippocampus, influencing diverse behaviors through its widespread cortical and subcortical connections\. Our previous work creating the mouse Hippocampus Gene Expression Atlas \(HGEA\) identified four genetically distinct cellular layers across five columnar domains in the SUB, with gene expression boundaries corresponding to distinct connectivity patterns and brain\-wide networks involved in spatial navigation, social behavior, and neuroendocrine regulation\. Using the Digital Brain Mouse Projectome Atlas \(MPA\) tool, we conducted &\#x27;virtual tract\-tracing&\#x27; to assess whether connectivity patterns of single\-neuron 3D reconstructions aligned with HGEA\-defined SUB cell types\. We classified 689 SUB projection neurons into 12 HGEA cell\-type groups based on their laminar and columnar distributions, whose spatial organization recapitulated HGEA\-defined 3D boundaries\. Using this population sample, we performed a SUB cell\-type census, characterized neuronal heterogeneity and projection prevalence, identified common and rare connectivity motifs and axonal collateralization patterns, and defined distinct projection themes for each SUB cell type\. Together, this analysis integrates single\-neuron and population\-level data to advance understanding of SUB cell type organization and its contributions to brain\-wide networks regulating diverse behaviors\.

## [Mapping the Evolution of Crisis Management in Tourism: A Bibliometric Analysis of Scopus\-Indexed Literature Using RStudio](../publications/5b1670edc10e5695c83f.md)

Ram Kumar Puri; Manoj Subedi

Crisis and disaster events, from terrorism and natural hazards to the COVID\-19 pandemic, have become a defining concern of tourism research over the past two decades\. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the crisis\-management\-and\-tourism literature indexed in Scopus, using a bibliometrix/R science\-mapping workflow together with document\-level evidence reconstructed from the underlying export\. The corpus comprises 1,931 documents \(1982\-2026, plus one 2027 in\-press record\) drawn from 705 sources, involving 4,261 authors, and averaging 31\.45 citations per document\. Annual output grew from isolated contributions before the mid\-1990s to a pronounced post\-2020 surge; a logistic life\-cycle model places the field’s inflection points at approximately 2023 and its asymptotic ceiling near 1,950 documents under current publication dynamics\. Tourism Management, Current Issues in Tourism and Annals of Tourism Research anchor the source landscape, while Ritchie, Pennington\-Gray, Hall and Prideaux lead individual productivity; authorship follows Lotka’s inverse\-square distribution closely\. Keyword co\-occurrence and thematic\-mapping procedures \(Louvain clustering on merged author and index keywords\) identify five thematic clusters \- crisis, crisis management, tourism, tourism management, and sustainability \- with crisis communication, resilience, and destination recovery among the most active post\-2020 topics\. International collaboration remains moderate \(26\.8% of documents\), concentrated among China, the United States, Australia, Spain and the United Kingdom\. The absence of cited\-reference data in the export precludes co\-citation and bibliographic\-coupling analysis; this limitation is documented transparently rather than substituted with invented data\. The study offers a reproducible, methodologically explicit map of the field’s evolution and identifies gaps around long\-term recovery trajectories, non\-Western destinations, and cross\-crisis comparative theory\.

## [Genomic dissection of divergent selection reveals a roadmap for reciprocal improvement of Chinese and American soybean](../publications/5b170d80d3af8f8fe07b.md)

Chengzhi Jiao; Delin Li; Hao Zhang; Zhongren Zhang; Xueqing Wang; Yan Long; Tianqing Zheng; Chaosen Zhao; Hongmei Qiu; Guangnan Xing; Guoyu Hu; Like Liu; Qiang Wang; Wen Huang; Xing Wang; Yumin Wang; Long Miao; Yanfei Li; Xin Jing; Xiaojian Fang; Yu Tian; Yinghui Li; Xiaobo Wang; Lijuan Qiu

Soybean \(Glycine max \[L\.\] Merr\.\) was domesticated in China over five millennia ago; yet, its global expansion has resulted in two distinct, independently evolved breeding pools in China and the Americas\. While regional breeding has optimized specific traits, a comprehensive roadmap for the reciprocal exchange of these &quot;breeding\-specific&quot; beneficial alleles is lacking\. Here, we performed a large\-scale genomic dissection of 2,377 soybean accessions, integrating 8\.4 million high\-quality SNPs with multi\-environment phenotyping across 11 locations\. Through genome\-wide association studies \(GWAS\), we identified 261 significant loci \(223 novel\) governing six key agronomic traits, revealing that Chinese and American germplasms have accumulated distinct sets of beneficial alleles of seed size/protein in China and oil/yield in the Americas\. To harness this untapped potential, we developed the Soybean Targeted Improvement Navigation System \(STINS\), a framework integrating population genomics, GWAS, and genomic selection \(GS\)\. We demonstrate the potential of targeted beneficial allele introgression between populations via gene modification for rapid trait improvement\. Proof\-of\-concept functional evaluation through CRISPR/Cas9\-mediated knockout of GmST05 in an American cultivar and overexpression of a resistant GmSNAP18 haplotype in a Chinese cultivar provided experimental support for STINS\-predicted targets for protein content and SCN resistance improvement\. Our study provides a navigable genomic resource for &quot;knowledge\-driven design breeding&quot;, offering a blueprint for the global exchange of elite alleles to ensure future food security\.

## [Effect of manual vancomycin loading on the bending strength and flexural modulus of bone cement](../publications/5b1b2717dd990e2d08e5.md)

Danica Popovska; Nikola Avramov; Ivan Boev; Vilijam Velkovski; Milena Bogojevska Doksevska; Teodora Todorova

Objectives: Manual addition of antibiotics when prefabricated antibiotic\-loaded bone cement is not available is possible but should be performed with caution due to the effects of the antibiotic on the mechanical properties of polymethyl methacrylate \(PMMA\)\. This study investigates differences in bending strength and modulus and morphology of bone cement resulting from two variations in manual vancomycin loading\. Methods: Three groups of bone cement – control without antibiotic, group with coarsely mixed 1 g vancomycin, and group with finely mixed 1 g vancomycin/40 g bone cement were tested for bending strength and bending modulus according to ISO5833:2002\. The broken surfaces of the tested samples were analyzed using scanning electron microscopy\. Results: Both methods of manual vancomycin loading caused a significant decrease in bending strength but not in bending modulus\. The bending strength of the group with finely mixed vancomycin was significantly above the ISO5833:2002 threshold of 50 MPa\. The bending strength of the group with coarsely mixed vancomycin did not differ significantly from the minimum set by the standard, with 4 of 9 specimens failing to meet the minimum requirement per ISO standards\. The bending modulus exceeded 1800 MPa, with no significant differences among groups\. The addition of vancomycin increased microporosity and the incidence of microcracks in the cement samples\. Conclusion: Manual loading of finely mixed vancomycin causes an acceptable decrease in the tested mechanical properties of bone cement and can be considered for use in arthroplasty procedures\. Additional testing of compressive strength and fatigue could provide a sufficient mechanical profile of these formulations and a better understanding of whether manually loaded properties of PMMA with vancomycin are mechanically safe for implant fixation\.

## [Differentiable Optics with dLux II: Optical Design Maximising Fisher Information](../publications/5b1fe210dbc3d7b155d9.md)

Louis C\. Desdoigts; Benjamin J\. S\. Pope; Michael Gully\-Santiago; Peter Tuthill

The design of astronomical hardware operating at the diffraction limit requires optimisation of physical optical simulations of the instrument with respect to desired figures of merit, such as photometric or astrometric precision\. System design entails many parameters some of which may entangle the fidelity of science observables with strongly nonlinear dependencies upon instrument properties\. Here we present a differentiable optical simulation framework dLux, a software library designed to construct optical models that are integrated with automatic differentiation\. This approach enables the direct evaluation of gradients and higher\-order derivatives through the forward model, facilitating statistically principled design and optimisation of instrument configurations\. The methodology leverages numerically stable second\- and higher\-order derivatives to directly compute Fisher information and covariance forecasts, enabling efficient Bayesian experimental design targeted toward optimising abstracted figures of merit, such as the precision of parameters recovered through complex sets of operations\. The method is validated against analytical results and applied to optimise the astrometric precision achievable with a parametrised telescope model and a diffractive pupil design relevant to exoplanet detection missions\. To support reproducibility and facilitate methodological extension, we provide example implementations via open\-source code on the Github sharing platform\.

## [Phytometabolites and Targeted Cancer Nanotherapy: Formulation, Therapeutic Applications and Future Aspects](../publications/5b267c195ba234a73821.md)

Meenakshi Chaurasia; Naveen Jain; Hriddhi  Chakraborty; Supriti Das; Deepshikha  Dey; Sonal Sharma

Cancer remains a major global health challenge, with therapeutic failure frequently associated with tumor heterogeneity, drug resistance, systemic toxicity, poor bioavailability, and inadequate drug accumulation at tumor sites\. Phytometabolites, including polyphenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, lignans, stilbenes, and other bioactive plant\-derived compounds, have emerged as promising candidates for cancer prevention and therapy because of their diverse molecular activities against multiple hallmarks of cancer\. However, their clinical translation is often restricted by poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, rapid metabolism, limited absorption, short systemic circulation, and nonspecific tissue distribution\. Targeted nanotherapy offers an advanced strategy to overcome these limitations by improving the physicochemical properties, pharmacokinetic behavior, tumor accumulation, and therapeutic efficacy of phytometabolites\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in the formulation and targeted delivery of phytometabolite\-based nanotherapeutics for cancer management\. Different nanocarrier platforms, including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid\-based nanoparticles, liposomes, nanostructured lipid carriers, solid lipid nanoparticles, phytosomes, nanoemulsions, dendrimers, metallic nanoparticles, and stimuli\-responsive systems, are discussed with emphasis on formulation approaches, physicochemical characterization, drug loading, controlled release, stability, and scalability\. Particular attention is given to active and passive tumor\-targeting strategies involving receptors, antibodies, peptides, ligands, and tumor\-responsive stimuli to enhance selective delivery and minimize off\-target toxicity\. The therapeutic potential of phytometabolite nanocarriers is further examined across major cancer types, with emphasis on mechanisms involving apoptosis, oxidative stress modulation, cell\-cycle regulation, angiogenesis inhibition, metastasis suppression, autophagy, inflammation, and multidrug\-resistance pathways\. The review also highlights current challenges related to formulation reproducibility, nanotoxicity, pharmacokinetics, tumor heterogeneity, manufacturing, regulatory requirements, and clinical translation\. Finally, emerging approaches integrating precision nanomedicine, biomarker\-guided targeting, multifunctional nanoplatforms, combination therapy, and artificial intelligence\-assisted formulation design are discussed as future directions for developing clinically translatable phytometabolite\-based targeted cancer nanotherapies\.

## [AI\-Driven Barriers to Ethical Consumption: A Cross\-National Framework and Research Agenda](../publications/5b440cdefc89e53ad890.md)

Saleh Md Arman; Ruchi Gupta; Cecilia Mark‐Herbert

Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates ethical purchasing decisions, but its effects vary across developed and emerging markets\. This study defines AI induced ethical choice friction as the process through which adaptive algorithmic intermediaries reduce consumers’ capacity to act on ethical intentions\. A systematic review of 57 articles published between 2020 and 2025, informed by interviews with 11 participants, identifies institutional, marketplace, technological, and psychological barrier layers\. Extending the S\-O\-R framework, the study theorizes how regulatory maturity and platform trust condition these barriers across markets\. Six propositions guide future research and inform AI developers, multinational retailers, and regulators\.

## [DMG: Dual\-Stream multiple instance learning network for hunting vulnerable smart contracts via adaptive granularity fusion](../publications/5b4b7d04f7c0754c2e0f.md)

Na Wang; Kun Zhang; Moroti Sonde; Victor S\. Sheng

Abstract With the increasing complexity of smart contracts and the increasing number of vulnerabilities in real\-world scenarios, ensuring smart contract security has become a critical challenge\. Despite various detection methods being proposed, existing approaches primarily trained on synthetic \(toy\) contracts with oversimplified semantics exhibit limited generalization to deployment environments\. Furthermore, their reliance on predefined patterns or single\-perspective representations with fixed granularity, such as token sequences or control\-flow graphs, limits their ability to capture the hierarchical structures and cross\-functional dependencies of complex contracts\. To this end, we propose a novel Dual\-stream Multi\-instance and Granularity Fusion Network \(DMG\)\. It is designed to capture the structural complexity of real\-world contracts while maintaining effectiveness in simpler contracts, thereby ensuring both adaptability and practical relevance\. Specifically, DMG learns representations at both the block\-level and the function\-level from bytecode with relatively structured dispatch organization\. Then, it uses Bi\-LSTM and a Multi\-Head Attention mechanism to model block\-level sequential dependencies and capture coarse\-grained contextual relationships\. Finally, it introduces a granularity\-aware fusion mechanism to adaptively integrate both views, releasing the assumption of fixed granularity and enabling the model to learn the most informative representation under weak supervision\. By integrating hierarchical granularity modeling with instance\-level learning, DMG shifts from fixed to adaptive granularity, enabling structured and semantically aligned vulnerability analysis\. Extensive experiments on toy and real\-world datasets demonstrate strong performance, and compared with state\-of\-the\-art methods, DMG delivers a balanced solution that bridges the gap between experimental settings and real\-world applicability\.

## [From Bureaucracy to Human\-Centred Design: Reading Indonesia’s Digital Public Service Reform through Design Thinking](../publications/5b5e352a6a1d0788a0a7.md)

Adi Satrio Nugroho

Digital transformation in public services asks governments to do more than adopt new technology as it asks them to reform public services around what citizens actually need and experience\. Indonesia’s M\-Paspor is one such attempt\. The app\-based passport application service was developed to address the limitations of conventional passport services\. This paper analyses the creation of the service through the lens of design thinking \(DT\) combined with the Business Model Canvas \(BMC\), concentrating on three BMC elements: customer segments, value proposition, and channels\. DT is used to understand users’ needs and problems, and how those needs were translated into possible solutions\. Collaboratively, BMC is used to map who is served, what value is created, and how that value is delivered through service channels\. The appraisal indicates that M\-Paspor represents a shift from a service organised around physical attendance to one that is more flexible, better integrated, and oriented towards its users, even though some stages still require face\-to\-face contact\. The analysis also shows that digital service innovation is determined less by technology and significantly more by the fit between user needs, service value, and the channels through which value is delivered\. This paper indicates that the approach may be arguably transferable to other public\-sector cases, particularly services that struggle with access, queues, lengthy administration, and a high volume of public interaction, and it offers a framework for analysing user\-driven service transformation more systematically\.Keywords: business model canvas; m\-paspor, design thinking, digital transformation, public services, human\-centred design

## [Managing quality\-oriented big data: a conceptual architecture for acquisition, fusion, and analytics in data\-driven organizations](../publications/5b694365258eb96add97.md)

Shahlokhon Gafurova; Shuxrat Rahmatov; Umida Zakhidova; Dilnoza Rakhimova; Gulshan Kabilova

Data\-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast\-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes\. The transition toward data\-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4\.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens\. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under\-theorized\. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality\-oriented big data as a first\-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi\-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics\. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed\. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected\. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality\-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research\. The architecture offers a data\-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data\-driven organizational quality ultimately depends\.

## [Silahlı İnsansız Deniz Araçlarının Uluslararası Hukuktaki Statüsü ve Otonom Kullanımın Doğurduğu Sorunlar](../publications/5b7338d0ae4bfca3548b.md)

Hamza Çorum

Silahlı insansız deniz araçlarının uluslararası hukukta hangi statüye tabi olduğu meselesi, denizde kuvvet kullanımı ve kolluk yetkilerinin icrası bakımından belirleyici niteliktedir\. Bu çalışma, savaş gemisi statüsü için aranan koşulların insansız sistemler bakımından ne ölçüde karşılanabilir olduğunu incelemekte; karşılanmaması hâlinde ise bu araçların hangi hukuki rejime tabi olabileceğini değerlendirmektedir\. İnceleme, deniz hukuku ve silahlı çatışmalar hukuku ilkeleri ışığında yürütülmüş; özellikle ayırt etme ve orantılılık ilkeleri bağlamında otonomi ve yapay zekâ kullanımının doğurduğu sorunlar ele alınmıştır\. Çalışmada, yapay zekâ modellerinin doğasında bulunan algoritmik ön yargının sistematik ihlallere yol açabilecek nitelikte olduğu ve bu durumun sorumluluk rejimini belirsizleştirdiği ileri sürülmektedir\. Sonuç olarak, insan komutasının ve denetiminin arttığı ölçüde silahlı insansız deniz araçlarının uluslararası hukuk ilkeleriyle daha uyumlu hâle geldiği; seyrüsefer haklarından savaşan \(taraf\) haklarına uzanan bir eksen üzerinde artan insan kontrolü ile doğru orantılı olarak daha geniş haklara konu olabileceği iddia edilmektedir\.

## [Rethinking the Lecturer in the Digital Age: A Critical Conceptual Analysis of Role Transformation in Higher Education](../publications/5b7437dee5f2b34c5a56.md)

Elizabeth Karoya; Patrick Bwowe

Purpose: This paper critically examines how digital transformation is reshaping the lecturer’s professional role in universities\. Rather than simply describing technology adoption, it asks how digital transformation reshapes academic identity, pedagogical agency, and institutional power, and argues that role transformation is contested and non\-linear rather than a smooth technological progression\. Design/Methodology/Approach: The paper employs a critical conceptual analysis methodology\. Literature was identified through targeted searches of major education\-technology and higher\-education journals, prioritising studies published since 2012 that directly addressed lecturer roles, digital pedagogy, or academic identity, and was synthesised thematically around three theoretical traditions: Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\), Engeström’s Activity Theory, and Selwyn’s critical technology studies\. These traditions are combined to construct an original analytical framework for understanding lecturer role transformation\. Findings: The analysis reveals three core tensions structuring the transformation of lecturer roles: \(i\) the tension between pedagogical agency and institutional control embedded in digital platforms; \(ii\) the tension between professional identity stability and the demand for perpetual digital re\-skilling; and \(iii\) the tension between the rhetoric of student‑centred learning and the managerial logics that increasingly govern digital higher education\. The paper argues that these tensions are systemic rather than incidental, and that dominant theoretical models, particularly TPACK, under\-theorise the structural and political dimensions of role transformation\. Practical Implications: The findings call for a reorientation of institutional digital transformation strategies away from technocentric implementation toward critically informed professional development models that recognise the structural conditions shaping lecturer agency\. Originality/Value: The paper’s main contribution is the Critical Ecological Framework of Lecturer Role Transformation \(CEFLRT\), which integrates structural, agentic, and identity dimensions that existing models treat separately\. It repositions the lecturer not as a passive recipient of technological change but as a reflexive professional navigating contested institutional terrain\.

## [Contrast media extravasation following CT angiography in a patient with lower\-extremity atherosclerotic occlusive disease: a case report](../publications/5b79109ed72753ef54c8.md)

CongBing Yan; Ting Zhang; Qin Xu; Shiyuan Bi

Contrast media extravasation \(CME\) is a recognized complication of intravenous iodinated contrast administration during computed tomography \(CT\) examinations, with a reported incidence rate ranging between 0\.1% and 1\.2%\. Although most extravasation injuries are mild and self\-limiting, a small proportion of them progress to skin blistering, tissue necrosis, or compartment syndrome\. Blister formation, in particular, is an uncommon manifestation observed predominantly in moderate\-to\-severe extravasation\. Herein, we report a case of iobitridol extravasation that occurred during lower\-extremity CT angiography in a 68\-year\-old female patient with lower\-extremity atherosclerotic occlusive disease\. Approximately 5 h after the procedure, multiple fluid\-filled skin blisters developed at the forearm injection site\. A combined external regimen\-topical Hirudoid \(mucopolysaccharide polysulfate\) cream, intermittent ice compresses, and Jinhuang San \(Golden Yellow Powder\) mixed with green\-tea water as a wet poultice was applied immediately\. The blisters were absorbed by the following day without skin breakdown, and complete resolution was achieved within 48 h\. To our knowledge, this is the first report describing this specific three\-component topical combination for iobitridol extravasation presenting with blistering\. This case highlights the importance of early recognition and structured topical management of CME and suggests—at the hypothesis\-generating level—that integrating a traditional Chinese medicine external therapy with conventional topical agents may be a useful option for such injuries\. Prospective, controlled studies are required to confirm these observations\.

## [Contextual Acceptance of Artificial Intelligence in Commercial Policy\-Making: An Integrated Model of Acceptance, Resistance, and Institutional Factors](../publications/5b89dd0e2aa8061ff06a.md)

Hamidreza Goldouz; Ezatollah Abbasian; Nastaran Hajiheydari

This study examines how senior decision\-makers in Iranian commercial policy institutions evaluate and respond to artificial intelligence \(AI\), with particular attention to the interplay of adoption, resistance, and institutional considerations\. It develops the notion of contextual acceptance to describe the importance of whether AI\-supported decisions can be justified to relevant stakeholders\. An exploratory sequential mixed\-methods design was used\. The qualitative phase involved 18 semi\-structured interviews with experts in commercial policy, information technology, and academia\. The authors report thematic saturation after the fourteenth interview and four additional interviews to consolidate the themes\. In the quantitative phase, a 27\-item five\-point Likert questionnaire was completed by 248 senior managers and specialists selected through stratified random sampling\. The reported analysis used partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) in SmartPLS 4\. The qualitative analysis identified digital leadership, perceived usefulness, institutional trust, algorithmic opacity, organizational resistance, and perceived risk\. In the structural model, digital leadership \(β = 0\.36, t = 6\.3\), perceived usefulness \(β = 0\.34, t = 5\.9\), and institutional trust \(β = 0\.28, t = 4\.7\) were positively associated with attitudes toward AI\. Algorithmic opacity \(β = −0\.22, t = 3\.8\) and organizational resistance \(β = −0\.19, t = 3\.4\) were negatively associated with attitudes\. The reported R² values were 0\.64 for attitude and 0\.69 for behavioral intention, with an overall GOF value of 0\.61\. All nine hypotheses were reported as supported, although the indirect\-effect coefficient and test statistic for mediation were not provided\. The findings are consistent with a context\-sensitive account of AI acceptance in which perceived institutional accountability and the defensibility of algorithm\-supported decisions complement assessments of technical usefulness\. Potential implications include clearer accountability arrangements, explainable AI systems, and digital leadership development; causal and policy\-effectiveness claims require further study\.

## [Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke](../publications/5b9035457f4ba8bb3f5f.md)

Xiaoyan Hao; Juan Wang; Jing Wang; Yujiao Hu; Fengjuan Wang; Xinran Liu; Congxia Bai

Background Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage \(ICH\) and acute ischemic stroke \(IS\) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment\. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory\-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS\. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the clinical and laboratory data of 12,213 hospitalized stroke patients \(including 3,251 with ICH and 8,962 with IS\) and 2,893 hypertensive controls at Xijing Hospital between 2013 and 2023\. A temporal validation cohort comprising 153 ICH and 342 IS patients admitted from January to December 2024 was also established\. To address class imbalance, BorderlineSMOTE\-2 \(BS2\) was applied\. Candidate variables were screened using three feature selection strategies, including RFECV\-ADA, Lasso, and Boruta\. Six supervised machine learning models were trained using ten\-fold cross\-validation\. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy\. Feature importance was interpreted using SHAP analysis\. Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses were performed as exploratory complementary analyses\. Results Ten routine laboratory parameters were retained for model construction: white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, uric acid, total protein, potassium, sodium, chloride, fibrinogen degradation product, and D\-Dimer\. In the test cohort, the final model \(BS2\_LightGBM\_V10\) achieved AUCs of 0\.926 for discriminating ICH from IS, 0\.979 for discriminating ICH from controls, and 0\.923 for discriminating IS from controls\. For the three\-class classification task \(ICH, IS, and controls\), the overall accuracy reached 79\.07%\. SHAP analysis indicated that neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, D\-Dimer, and total protein were the most influential predictors\. Mendelian randomization analysis suggested that uric acid had a potential causal association with the risk of ICH \(OR = 1\.309\), whereas uric acid \(OR = 1\.0008\), cystatin C \(OR = 1\.0011\), and potassium \(OR = 1\.0040\) had potential causal associations with the risk of IS\. Colocalization analysis identified 18 genes linked to uric acid in the context of ICH\. Conclusion A diagnostic model based on ten routine laboratory indicators accurately differentiated ICH from IS\. Uric acid may also play a causal role in the pathogenesis of both disorders\.

## [Modelling, Estimation and Control for an Up\-flow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket Reactor Treating Blackwater Towards Resource Recovery](../publications/5b9a3dcc22c17f84e150.md)

Antonio Felype Maciel; Otacílio B\.L\. Neto; Michela Mulas; Hamse Kjerstadius

This work investigates the model calibration, state estimation, and control of an Up\-flow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket \(UASB\) reactor for the task of increasing its biogas production while complying with effluent quality requirements\. We consider a dynamic model based on the Anaerobic Digestion Model No\. 1 \(ADM1\), calibrated using experimental data from a blackwater treatment plant located in Helsingborg, Sweden\. Using this model, we design a control solution composed of an operating point optimiser, defining the setpoints that achieve maximum biogas production, and a feedback controller, that tracks these setpoints while rejecting disturbances\. For the feedback controller, we consider two alternative approaches: a multiloop Proportional\-Integral\-Derivate \(PID\) controller and an output\-feedback Model Predictive Controller \(MPC\)\. The control solution is showcased on simulated experiments of operating the UASB reactor under different influent disturbance scenarios and compared with the nominal open\-loop operation\. Our results show that the controlled system is able to increase biogas production, while also improving effluent quality\. Both control approaches have similar setpoint tracking performances, with the MPC being more economical and robust to influent disturbances\.

## [Utilising wild genetic diversity for climate\-resilient moth bean \(Vigna aconitifolia \(Jacq\.\) Maréchal\) improvement through introgression breeding: A review](../publications/5b9a773b93aa3f27fcc4.md)

S S Kaviya; S\. Saravanan; S\. Juliet Hepziba; J Sheela; A\. Kavitha Pushpam

Moth bean \(Vigna aconitifolia \(Jacq\.\) Maréchal\) is an underutilised, climate\-resilient grain legume well adapted to the arid and semi\-arid regions of the Indian subcontinent\. Despite its exceptional tolerance to drought and heat, its genetic improvement has been constrained by a narrow\-cultivated gene pool, limited genomic resources and the underutilisation of wild relatives\. As climate change increases the occurrence of abiotic and biotic stresses, broadening the genetic base of moth beans has become essential for developing resilient and high\-yielding cultivars\. This review critically examines the potential of introgression breeding as a strategic approach for incorporating beneficial alleles from wild Vigna species, including Vigna trilobata \(L\.\) Verdc\., Vigna stipulacea \(Lam\.\) Kuntze, Vigna indica T\.M\.Dixit, K\.V\.Bhat and S\.R\.Yadav and Vigna aridicola N\.Tomooka &amp; Maxted\. Previous reviews have primarily emphasised the nutritional value, genetic diversity and general breeding potential of moth bean, with limited focus on systematic wild relative utilisation and introgression pathways\. In contrast, this review integrates wild gene\-pool classification, donor\-trait relationships, reproductive barriers, linkage drag, pre\-breeding strategies and genomics\-assisted approaches within a unified breeding framework\. It further evaluates the application of marker\-assisted backcrossing, advanced backcross quantitative trait loci analysis \(QTL\), comparative genomics, genomic selection and emerging molecular tools for efficient trait introgression\. The synthesis indicates that combining systematic donor characterisation with reproductive barrier management, precision introgression and validated genomic tools can accelerate the deployment of adaptive alleles from wild relatives\. Future breeding efforts should prioritise multi\-environment validation, high\-throughput phenotyping, cost\-effective genotyping and targeted utilisation of wild germplasm to broaden the genetic base and develop climate\-resilient moth bean cultivars\.

## [Neurobehavioral assessments and biomarkers in school children who are highly exposed to air pollution](../publications/5b9dd6f32c49c85f3af5.md)

Stephanie M\. Holm; Nina Holland; John Randolph Balmes; Tim R\. Tyner; Weihong Guo; Anabelle Garza; Debra Manzo Garcia; Briseida Vasquez\-Vasquez; Sierra Loomis; Elizabeth M\. Noth

Background Children are uniquely vulnerable to ambient air pollution\. Yet, data remain limited relating standardized academic metrics with neurobehavioral outcomes measured by more in\-depth testing, and how neurobehavioral outcomes are associated with non\-criteria pollutants—such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons \(PAHs\) and elemental carbon \(EC\)\. Methods Utilizing data from the Children’s Health and Air Pollution Study \(CHAPS\) in Fresno, California, we evaluated neurobehavioral outcomes in a cohort of highly exposed children \( n = 193, ages 7–18\)\. Prenatal and year of life one exposures to PM 2\.5 , PM 10 , O 3 , NO 2 , NO x , PAH 456 and elemental carbon \(EC\) were estimated daily\. Outcome measures included the NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery, the Child Behavior Checklist \(CBCL\), standardized test scores, and serum brain\-derived neurotrophic factor \(BDNF\) and urinary 8\-hydroxy\-2\-deoxyguanosine \(8\-OHdG\) biomarkers\. Correlations between the various outcomes were assessed, and linear and distributed lag models \(DLM\) associated outcomes with pollutant exposures\. Results Third\-grade test scores demonstrated robust correlations with the NIH Toolbox total and crystallized cognition composites \( r \~ 0\.55–0\.60\) and moderate correlation with BDNF \( r = 0\.35\)\. Linear models revealed that first\-trimester exposure to traffic\-related air pollutants was associated with elevated aggressive and rule\-breaking behavior\. First\-year of life exposure across all pollutants was associated with depressed BDNF levels with a susceptibility window around 5 to 6 months of life\. Conclusion Early\-life exposure to ambient air pollution is associated with persistent differences in neurocognitive and behavioral outcomes measured into adolescence\. The strong concordance between school\-administered standardized test scores and resource\-intensive neurobehavioral tools indicates that academic datasets might provide proxy endpoints for assessing environmental neurotoxicity\.

## [Polling Without People: Can Silicon Samples of CASM\-Inspired LLM Personae Mimic Human Respondents in Pre\-Election Polling?](../publications/5ba538438256b912bf0e.md)

Danielius Jonaitis; Brendan Corcoran; BINAM POUDYAL; Alexandra Roskam; Ava Ali; Shriya Agrawal; Raymond M Duch; Roberto Cerina

We introduce a framework for simulating pre\-election survey responses with large language model \(LLM\) synthetic personae\.Drawing on the Cognitive Aspects of Survey Methodology \(CASM\) literature, our approach combines synthetic biographies, salient\-event memories and conditional news exposure with a staged cognitive process for answering turnout and candidate\-choice questions\.We apply the framework to a single weekly wave for the 2026 US House elections and produce national and district estimates using multilevel regression and post\-stratification\.Relative to a demographicsonly synthetic personae baseline, CASM\-inspired enrichment shifts estimates towards Democrats, consistent with the direction suggested by contemporary polling\.However, the estimated Democratic margin is 18\.7 percentage points, compared with 8\.7 points in the polling average\.Personae randomly assigned to news\-based judgement construction produce a larger Democratic margin than retrievers, who are not exposed to news, although uncertainty is substantial\.These comparisons show that our enrichment strategy changes synthetic responses in the correct direction, but do not isolate the effects of all components or establish predictive accuracy conclusively\.The framework offers a structured approach to studying synthetic survey responses whilst highlighting persistent challenges of leftward bias, uncertainty calibration and benchmarking novel methodologies during an election campaign\.

## [Immunohistochemical analysis of substance P from cerebral ganglion of S\. maculata and B\. bengalensis](../publications/5ba593c99b85def6b3ab.md)

Saniya Sunil Tendulkar; Nitin Anandrao Kamble

Abstract Background In agriculture, various chemicals and fertilizers are used to enhance the plant growth; however, their excessive use can cause environmental pollution and adversely affect both invertebrates and vertebrates\. The present study was undertaken to investigate the effect of the phytoregulators Chlormequat chloride \(CCC\) and Paclobutrazol \(PBZ\) on Substance P immunoreactivity in the neuronal cells of the cerebral ganglion of Semperula maculata and Bellamya bengalensis after 96 hours of exposure\. Substance P immunoreactivity was quantified as the percentage area of immunostaining to assess neurochemical alterations induced by these phytoregulators\. Results Substance P immunoreactivity increased significantly in both gastropod species following exposure to CCC and PBZ compared with the control group\. Among the two phytoregulators, PBZ induced a greater increase in Substance P immunoreactivity than CCC\. In Semperula maculata , immunoreactivity increased by 14\.35% following CCC exposure and by 16\.77% following PBZ exposure\. Similarly, in Bellamya bengalensis , immunoreactivity increased by 10\.71% and 12\.31% after CCC and PBZ exposure, respectively\. Conclusion Comparative analysis showed that the relative increase in Substance P immunoreactivity was greater in Semperula maculata , whereas Bellamya bengalensis exhibited higher overall Substance P immunoreactivity under all experimental conditions\. These findings indicate that CCC and PBZ induce significant neurochemical alterations in gastropods, suggesting their potential neurotoxic effects on non\-target invertebrates\. The study emphasizes the need to monitor the environmental impact of these phytoregulators in both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems\.

Logan Kugler

Frontier labs say their AI models now help build their own successors\.

## [From Memory Hits to Answerable Evidence: Query\-Conditioned Memory Compilation for Long\-Term Agent Memory](../publications/5bab2204295f590c2415.md)

Shangze Li; Yanyu Yao; Derong Xu; Zhi Zheng; Tong Xu

Long\-term agent memory requires recovering answer\-relevant evidence dispersed across turns and sessions\. Existing systems increasingly use structured memories and adaptive retrieval, yet often pass retrieved or expanded units directly to the reader, coupling memory addressing with evidence presentation and leaving the final context redundant or incomplete\. To address this gap, we propose MemCompile, a query\-conditioned evidence compilation framework for long\-term conversational memory\. Given a query, the Address Plane locates relevant support through compact source\-linked descriptors and capacity\-aware Cells, while a normalization boundary resolves heterogeneous retrieval hits to stable SourcePacket identities\. Its Evidence Plane then allocates a bounded evidence budget across complementary packets, admits limited additional support, and renders the retained claims associated with each selected packet into an answer\-ready context\. MemCompile achieves 80\.52% Judge Accuracy on LoCoMo and extends the empirical quality\-cost Pareto frontier to a higher\-quality regime\. Its strong performance on LongMemEval\-S further suggests that the benefits of query\-conditioned compilation generalize across long\-term conversational\-memory benchmarks\.

## [Assessment of heavy metal content in rivers and sediments: exploring relationships with land use and soil characteristics](../publications/5bacdf50ce99d55d938f.md)

Guillermo Calvo\-Brenes; Noemi Quirós\-Bustos

Heavy metal\(s\) \(HM, HMs\) are essential to biological and environmental processes, but excessive concentration threaten ecosystems and human health\. This study assessed HM concentrations in river water and sediments, examining their relationships with land use and soil characteristics\. A total of 26 sampling points were selected across Costa Rica, primarily based on land use: Arenal, Caño Negro, Tempisque, Pital, Toro, Tigre, Rincón, Sierpe, Torres, Poás, Segundo, Pacuare, Penshurt, and Birrís\. The sampling period extended from September 2017 to July 2020\. Most sampling sites showed detectable HM levels, with arsenic, nickel, and mercury sometimes exceeding thresholds for probable toxicity, most metals in sediments fell within an “undefined toxicity” range, though cadmium levels were notably high\. Predictive models in sediments were more accurate: lead \(70%\), chromium \(73%\), arsenic \(71%\), and nickel \(74%\)\. The main predictors are: Urban land use \(89%\) for Lead; industrial activity \(41\.5%\) and bare soil \(17\.7%\) for Chromium; Cane \(52%\), Coffee \(14%\) and Cassava \(13%\) for Arsenic; and Bare Soil \(78%\) for Nickel\. Models showed variable and complex patterns, but bivariate correlations were strong \(80%, 90%, and 95%\)\. Effective management strategies and continuous monitoring are critical to reducing contamination risks and protecting river ecosystems and water quality\.

## [Between overlap and encroachment: power transition without confrontation and China–Russia structured rivalry in Central Asia](../publications/5bba13074b4e5dc3d494.md)

I\.Kh\. Supyaldiyarov; Saule Aliyeva; Galina Kakenova; Ибрагимова Гульнара Ералиевна; Диляра Супыалдиярова

Central Asia has become a region in which the relative position of China and Russia is shifting in China’s favour, yet this shift has not produced open rivalry\. Power Transition Theory would expect a narrowing gap between a rising and an incumbent power to generate friction; the “New Great Game” literature anticipates intensified competition; and the accommodation literature explains the absence of rivalry through Russia’s adaptation and China’s restraint\. This article asks whether, and how, that accommodation has survived the intensification of asymmetry after Russia’s full\-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022\. Drawing on Relational Power Analysis, it argues that the transition in Central Asia is sectoral rather than systemic: China’s gains are concentrated in connectivity, trade, finance and institution\-building, while Russia retains central positions in regime security, labour migration and parts of the energy\-transit network\. Open confrontation is suppressed by three conditions – Russia’s growing reversed dependency on China, China’s calibrated restraint in regime security, and the hedging strategies of Central Asian states, which disperse the transition across issue areas and extract benefits from both powers\. The resulting pattern is conceptualised as structured rivalry: incompatible long\-term positional interests pursued through low\-visibility mechanisms rather than overt contestation\. The argument is assessed through a structured, focused comparison of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan \(2022–2026\), which systematically weighs it against power\-transition, alignment and accommodation explanations\. The findings refine the accommodation thesis, specify the scope conditions under which regional power transitions remain peaceful, and show how the agency of smaller states shapes the pace and form of great\-power adjustment\.

## [Precision Psychopharmacology in Schizophrenia: Integrating Neurotransmitter Signatures and Sympathetic Nervous System Biomarkers for Personalized Treatment](../publications/5bc0e55972fa54b6bdbe.md)



Schizophrenia is a heterogeneous syndrome and nearly one third of patients gain no benefit from dopamine antagonist therapy\.This systematic review interrogates whether neurotransmitter signatures and sympathetic nervous system biomarkers can stratify treatment responsivity and thereby guide precision psychopharmacology\.Five studies were synthesized after a structured screening cascade reported through a PRISMA workflow\.Dopaminergic and glutamatergic indices showed divergent associations with antipsychotic outcome and elevated anterior cingulate glutamate distinguished nonresponders with an area under the curve of 0\.59\.Resting vagal tone was markedly attenuated in schizophrenia with a pooled Hedges g of \-0\.98 for high frequency heart rate variability\.Inflammatory and epigenetic markers including interleukin 6 and methylation panels reached discriminative accuracy up to 0\.92\.The convergent evidence supports a neuroimmunoautonomic framework in which glutamatergic refractoriness autonomic hypotonia and cytokine dysregulation jointly sculpt treatment resistance\.Multimodal biomarker integration appears indispensable because no solitary index attains clinical separability\.

## [Intelligent Threat Detection Using Explainable AI and Autonomous Incident Response in Cloud Enterprise Security Systems](../publications/5bc855892b3b2ead38db.md)

Vijay Singh Rathore

Cloud enterprise security systems face increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, including credential compromise, lateral movement, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, and previously unknown attack patterns\. Traditional security mechanisms often depend on predefined rules and signature\-based detection, which may struggle to identify evolving threats across distributed cloud infrastructures\. This study proposes an integrated framework combining artificial intelligence \(AI\), explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\), and autonomous incident response to strengthen cloud enterprise security\. The framework employs machine learning and behavioral analytics to identify suspicious activities across network traffic, identity events, application logs, and cloud audit records\. Explainability techniques provide interpretable justifications for threat classifications, enabling security analysts to understand the factors contributing to alerts and evaluate their operational significance\. An autonomous response component uses predefined policies and risk\-based decision mechanisms to initiate proportionate containment actions, including session revocation, temporary access restriction, and isolation of affected resources where supported\. The research adopts a design\-oriented methodology involving data preparation, model development, explainability assessment, controlled incident simulation, and performance evaluation\. Detection effectiveness is assessed using precision, recall, F1\-score, and false\-positive rates, while response performance is evaluated through detection latency, containment time, and response accuracy\. Human oversight is incorporated for high\-impact or uncertain decisions\. The proposed framework aims to improve threat visibility, operational efficiency, and response consistency while preserving accountability\. Its expected contribution is a transparent and adaptable security architecture for enterprise cloud environments\.

## [Digitally Enhanced Fitspiration Content on Social Media](../publications/5bca095aeca0d1db948a.md)

Isa Vos; Thomas N\. Friemel

Fitspiration content on social media refers to a combination of fitness and inspiration and seems to promote a healthy lifestyle\. However, some of this content may have negative implications, as the representation of super\-fit and attractive individuals may contribute to promoting unrealistic body ideals and behaviours\. It can be assumed that this negative relation has amplified due to the use of digital modification of visual content\. To inform future research and health interventions, this scoping review summarises existing research across different scientific disciplines to identify key variables and findings regarding digitally enhanced Fitspiration content\. Dimensions, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English articles published between 2015 and 2025 that focused on Fitspiration, digital enhancements and social media\. Through systematic screening and assessment, 26 articles presenting original empirical data were identified and analysed in detail\. The results show that empirical research applied both qualitative and quantitative methods and focused on Instagram, women and young adults as main demographics\. The findings suggest that men and women were aware of the prevalence of digital enhancements\. Negative effects were found for increased appearance\-based comparisons and internalisation\. Although some individuals used strategies to reduce potential negative effects, interventions could further empower social media users\.

## [A Hybrid Handcrafted\-Transformer Framework for Multiclass AMD Classification with Efficient Downstream Recalibration](../publications/5bd33d1870ea6f8a821a.md)

Leonardo Petra Refialy; Sri Hartati; Sigit Priyanta; S Supanji

This study proposes a hybrid handcrafted\-transformer framework for three\-class age\-related macular degeneration classification from color fundus photographs\.The model combines 32 macula\-centered color and texture descriptors with frozen ViT\-B/16 embeddings, followed by principal component analysis and RBF\-kernel support vector classification\.Evaluation used 594 unique duplicate\-controlled images from four repositories with five\-seed nested cross\-validation and leave\-one\-dataset\-out testing\.The framework achieved 93\.27% ± 0\.43% accuracy, 91\.67% ± 0\.54% macro\-F1, and 91\.23% ± 0\.54% balanced accuracy, improving the handcrafted baseline by 4\.51, 4\.97, and 4\.99 percentage points, respectively, based on the underlying unrounded five\-seed means\.Leave\-one\-dataset\-out performance decreased to 81\.38% ± 0\.49% accuracy and 80\.59% ± 0\.53% macro\-F1, indicating a meaningful crossrepository generalization gap\.Full ViT fine\-tuning remained predictively stronger \(94\.71% ± 0\.73% accuracy; 93\.45% ± 0\.83% macro\-F1\)\.In the synchronized computational benchmark, Hybrid cold\-start construction required 55\.01 s per fold\-seed versus 446\.70 s for full fine\-tuning; after a one\-time 53\.53\-s feature cache, downstream Hybrid recalibration required only 0\.52 s with a 0\.763\-MiB per\-run model bundle in the matched computational benchmark\.These results support a compact performance\-efficiency trade\-off for repeated downstream recalibration using reusable frozen representations\.

## [Scalable Patterning of Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Logic Gates and Neuromorphic Computing](../publications/5bd3d427f3830a60c1aa.md)

Yifan Xie; Junyang Deng; Chengqi Wei; Jiahao Zhao; Liuyuan Lan; Yazhuo Kuang; Miao Cheng; Changrui Liu; Yue Tian; Hanlin Wang; Wan Yue; Jian Liu; Zhenjie Ni; Zhongrui Wang; Mengmeng Li

ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors \(OECTs\) are promising building blocks for bioelectronics owing to their efficient ion–electron coupling, soft‐material compatibility and high transconductance\. However, their large off‐state currents and poor scalability have so far limited high‐density integration and circuit‐level functionality\. Here we introduce a patterning strategy suitable for solution‑processable organic semiconductors, enabling high‑fidelity OECT arrays with suppressed leakage and off‑state currents, on/off ratios up to 10 7 , and good device‑to‑device uniformity\. Leveraging these patterned OECTs, we demonstrate the integration of logic circuits, including complementary inverters as well as NAND and NOR gates, exhibiting high voltage gain \(up to 203 V/V\), large noise margins \(92\.17%\) and stable operation at low supply voltages\. Benefiting from the patterning approach and the AlO x ‐induced suppression of off‐state current, the static power consumption of the inverter is reduced by approximately 90%\. Beyond digital logic, we further show that these devices emulate key synaptic functions such as short‐term plasticity and enable reservoir computing tasks, defining a manufacturable platform for integrated bioelectronic circuitry and neuromorphic architectures\. This patterning strategy therefore provides a general route toward high‐density biointerfaces and next‐generation brain–computer interfaces\.

## [Electron Transfer in Solids and Activation of Molecules](../publications/5bd3d72b6df4fcc2ee12.md)

Bing‐Liang Leng; Xiaojun Lu; Lu Li; Tian‐Nan Ye; Xin‐Hao Li; Jie‐Sheng Chen

Comprehensive Summary Electron transfer \(ET\) plays a fundamental role in heterogeneous catalysis, critically influencing the activation and transformation of molecules\. At metal‐support interfaces, spontaneous charge redistribution modulates the electronic structures of both the metal and support, thereby promoting mass transfer, enhancing intrinsic reaction kinetics, and enabling synergistic catalytic behavior\. In well‐designed photo‐driven systems, the directed migration of photogenerated carriers promotes the cleavage of highly inert bonds under mild conditions\. In intermetallic compounds, internal electron transfer driven by electronegativity differences can generate well‐defined active sites that enhance both catalytic activity and selectivity\. In this review, we introduce the mechanisms and effects of electron transfer across three catalytic systems: metal‐support interfaces, photo‐driven catalysis, and intermetallic compounds\. We further propose that achieving precise atomic‐level control over these electron‐transfer pathways, along with elucidating the influence of intrinsic electron properties such as spin and orbital configuration, are crucial for developing next‐generation high‐performance catalysts\. ## [Who reviews the reviews? When AI encounters academic aesthetics](../publications/5bd898a2cef206a92d6d.md)

Chen Qu

This paper focuses on the challenges in digital\-era peer review\. It explains why an overreliance on Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in peer review can pose problems beyond legal or ethical compliance\. ## [Artificial Intelligence in Gastrointestinal Precision Medicine: A Critical Appraisal Through the Lens of Inflammatory Bowel Disease](../publications/5be3b5091bf7294674af.md)

Abdulrahman G\. Alharbi; Abdulrahman A\. Aljabri

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) now supports many facets of gastrointestinal and hepatic care, from lesion recognition during endoscopy to the interpretation of large molecular datasets\. This review first outlines AI&\#x27;s broader role across gastroenterology and hepatology, and then uses inflammatory bowel disease \(IBD\) as a case study for AI\-assisted multiomics integration\. The review applies a consistent evidentiary framework that distinguishes exploratory, retrospective, and prospective study designs\. Retrospective genomic and image\-based studies report promising discriminative performance for risk classification and lesion detection, but this evidence remains largely exploratory or retrospective, whereas prospective randomized evidence is currently strongest for AI\-assisted endoscopic polyp detection\. Reviewing the biochemistry linking genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics to host\-microbiota interactions clarifies where this supporting evidence is strong and where it is weak, and highlights the standardization, validation, and translational barriers that continue to separate model performance from routine clinical use\.

## [Encapsulation\-integrated microneedle platforms for alopecia treatment: a review of controlled drug delivery, immunomodulation, and hair follicle regeneration](../publications/5beb0645cc9b42e2ae3b.md)

Kerlin E\. Balza Boniche; Maria José Rey\-Sanchez; Andres F\. Roca\-Arroyo; Jhonatan A\. Gutierrez\-Rivera; Diego Balda; Logan D\. Morton; David A\. Castilla‐Casadiego

Alopecia is a multifactorial disorder characterized by progressive hair loss, follicular dysfunction, and, in some cases, immune\-mediated damage, significantly affecting patient quality of life\. Although conventional therapies such as topical minoxidil, corticosteroids, and oral immunomodulators remain widely used, their clinical efficacy is often limited by poor skin penetration, short therapeutic duration, systemic adverse effects, and the need for frequent administration\. In recent years, microneedle\-based platforms have emerged as promising minimally invasive systems capable of enhancing transdermal delivery directly to the follicular microenvironment\. This review explores the emerging design space of microneedle platforms integrated with advanced encapsulation strategies for alopecia treatment, with particular emphasis on their roles in immunomodulation and tissue regeneration\. By examining the interplay between material composition, carrier architecture, and release behavior, we discuss how these systems improve localized delivery while enabling sustained and controlled therapeutic exposure within the hair follicle niche\. Recent advances in nanoparticles, nanoliposomes, porous materials, and microsphere\-integrated microneedles, as well as light\-guiding systems, have expanded the capabilities of conventional polymeric microneedles beyond passive drug delivery\. These platforms enhance drug stability, regulate release kinetics, improve follicular targeting, and actively modulate key biological processes associated with alopecia pathogenesis and regeneration\. Reported therapeutic effects include suppression of inflammatory signaling pathways, regulation of immune\-cell infiltration, stimulation of angiogenesis, reduction of oxidative stress, activation of follicular stem\-cell populations, and promotion of the telogen\-to\-anagen transition\. Collectively, these advances position encapsulation\-integrated microneedle systems as a promising class of next\-generation therapeutic platforms capable of combining localized delivery with biological microenvironment modulation\. Finally, this review discusses current translational challenges, including manufacturing scalability, formulation stability, long\-term safety, and disease\-specific platform design, while highlighting future opportunities for personalized and regenerative alopecia therapies\.

## [Noise and Drift Models for Protonic ECRAM and Their Impact on Analog In‐Memory Computing](../publications/5bee8d28fcab82d6f7c6.md)

Xin Su; H\. M\. Liu; Qing Cao; Ning Li

ABSTRACT Analog in‐memory computing \(AIMC\) with nonvolatile memories \(NVMs\) offers a promising route toward energy‐efficient deep learning\. However, because AIMC relies on analog device states, understanding device‐level nonidealities, particularly noise and drift, is essential for assessing achievable computing performance\. Among NVM candidates, the electrochemical random‐access memory \(ECRAM\) is attractive for AIMC owing to its symmetric switching, large number of accessible conductance states, low energy consumption, and small cycle‐to‐cycle variability\. However, the physical origins of ECRAM read noise and conductance drift remain insufficiently understood\. Here, we systematically investigate noise and drift in ECRAM devices, identify their dominant mechanisms, and develop physics‐based statistical models\. Based on measured device characteristics, we construct compact device models for hardware‐aware simulations to evaluate ECRAM performance in AIMC\. We show that the low noise of ECRAM enables high inference accuracy even in the low‐conductance regime with a small memory window\. This feature offers a path toward improved energy efficiency and reduced leakage currents without sacrificing computational fidelity in high‐performance AIMC applications\.

## [Vierhout, Luuk: Hunting down Consciousness: A Radical New Approach](../publications/5bf6aea6b7914bbb8ecd.md)



This manifesto proposes a radical dissolution of Chalmers’ &quot;Hard Problem of Consciousness&quot; through a combined epistemological and evolutionary shift\. It establishes Darwin&\#x27;s mechanism of variation and selection not merely as an evolutionary engine for species, but as the primary, fundamental form of intelligence itself\. Rather than treating intelligence as an internal property or brain state, it reframes it as a dynamic, relational coordination operating across the boundary between organism and environment\. Spanning cellular phototaxis, LLMs, and human cognition, this broad Darwinian process shows that subject and object are merely stabilized outputs of a continuous trial and error process\. Epistemologically, we are not detached observers of a fixed reality, but active, adaptive &quot;scanners&quot; updating weights within survival limits\. Consciousness emerges when this primary Darwinian loop folds back on itself across time, forcing the organism to collapse a vast, distributed biological storm of data into an immediate, highly compressed, qualitative first\-person readout out of structural necessity\.

## [Industrial\-Scale Production of Low\-Cement Pressed Wall Materials from Shell Limestone Sawing Waste: Binder Efficiency, Contact Zone Evidence, and Techno\-Economic Performance](../publications/5bf7c5f28eba67403410.md)

Yeldar BUKAYEV; Emilio J\. Mascort‐Albea

Shell limestone sawing generates large quantities of porous carbonate waste that is difficult to reuse because of its high water demand and variable fine\-particle content\. This study evaluates an industrial\-scale route for converting this waste into low\-cement, vibration\-compacted pressed wall materials at LLP “Firma Fial” in the Mangystau Region of Kazakhstan\. The work combines industrial process documentation, compressive strength testing, binder intensity calculations, XRD phase identification, contact zone microhardness measurements, SEM observations, and a material cost comparison\. Waste was crushed to below 5 mm without removing fines, moisture was checked before batching, and the mixtures were vibration\-filled for 15–30 s at a compaction factor of approximately 2, followed by immediate demolding\. Cement contents of 50, 75, and 110 kg/m3 produced 28\-day strengths of 3\.43, 4\.90, and 7\.36 MPa, respectively\. The corresponding binder intensity was 14\.6–15\.3 kg m−3 MPa−1\. XRD identified calcite as the dominant phase with minor dolomite and magnesite, while SEM and microhardness observations confirmed a distinct cement\-paste/carbonate\-aggregate interfacial region\. The comparison with higher\-strength reference concretes is interpreted cautiously because the strength ranges and compaction concepts differ\. At 2023 prices, material cost decreased from KZT 24,785 \(USD 54\.32\) to KZT 9982 \(USD 21\.87\) per m3\. The results demonstrate industrial feasibility while identifying mixture reproducibility, interfacial characterization, and full life\-cycle assessment as priorities for further work\.

## [Automated ultrasound computed tomography for breast mass screening: A multicenter study](../publications/5bffd39bda24e577db4a.md)

Gaoxiang Xie; 燕乐 武; Liping Wang; Hongmei Zheng; Ming Yuchi; Mingyue Ding; Xinhong Wu; Xingrui Li; X W Cui; Wu Qiu

Background The low sensitivity of mammography creates a critical screening gap for women with dense breasts in Asia, for whom conventional two\-dimensional ultrasonography is often used\. However, this method is hampered by significant operator dependence and poor reproducibility\. This study aimed to develop an automated breast mass screening tool using artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-aided ultrasound computed tomography \(USCT\)\. Methods This retrospective multicenter study analyzed data from July 2022 to March 2024 of 514 patients divided into a development set \(n = 222\) and two independent external test sets \(n = 218; n = 74\)\. Reference standards were established based on clinical ultrasound reports\. A multiple instance learning \(MIL\) model for binary mass screening classification was developed and evaluated via cross\-validation and on external test sets using area under the curve \(AUROC\), with sensitivity and specificity indicated as Youden&\#x27;s index\. Results A total of 506 women \(mean age ± standard deviation, 45 ± 12 years\) contributing 941 breasts were evaluated\. In internal cross\-validation, the model for breast\-level classification achieved a mean AUROC of 0\.94 ± 0\.02\. This performance generalized well to the independent external test set \(216 women; 419 breasts\), where the model attained an AUROC of 0\.91 \(95% confidence interval \[CI\], 0\.89–0\.94\) with a sensitivity of 81% \(251 of 308 breasts\) and specificity of 89% \(99 of 111 breasts\) in breast mass screening\. This generalizability was further confirmed on a second external test set \(73 women; 102 breasts\), where the model achieved an AUROC of 0\.87 \(95% CI, 0\.80–0\.93\) with a sensitivity of 82% \(53 of 65 breasts\) and specificity of 84% \(31 of 37 breasts\)\. Conclusion An AI\-aided USCT model was developed that can serve as an operator\-independent solution for large\-scale breast mass screening in women with dense breasts\.

## [BiotaPredictor: A machine learning framework for predicting drug depletion by the human gut microbiota](../publications/5c022d7ca95598e6bff3.md)

Benyamin Naranjani; Laura E\. McCoubrey; Anders Borde; Gustaf Hulthe; Mats Josefson; Susanna Abrahmsén‐Alami; Bertil Abrahamsson; Abdul W\. Basit

The gut microbiota can profoundly influence the performance of oral medicines by metabolizing or bioaccumulating drugs, thereby reducing systemic exposure and contributing to variable patient responses\. Despite growing recognition of these interactions, microbiota\-driven drug depletion remains insufficiently addressed during early development\. Here, we present BiotaPredictor, a freely accessible web\-based machine learning platform that predicts the likelihood of drug depletion by human intestinal microbiota from molecular structure\. We compiled two curated datasets containing microbial depletion outcomes: \(i\) a consistently annotated AstraZeneca dataset \(158 compounds\) and \(ii\) an expanded integrated dataset incorporating published evidence \(522 compounds\)\. Multiple molecular descriptors\-including physicochemical properties, 3D conformational features, and fingerprint\-based encodings\-were evaluated across a suite of classification algorithms\. A logistic regression model trained on the AstraZeneca dataset using physicochemical parameters achieved the highest performance, correctly classifying all compounds in an external validation study \(3 depleted, 9 stable\)\. BiotaPredictor enables early triage of compounds susceptible to microbiota\-mediated loss and can inform lead optimization, formulation strategy, and pharmacokinetic prediction\. Integrating microbiota liability assessment into development pipelines will contribute to safer, more efficacious drug products and support precision delivery of orally administered therapeutics\.

## [Sleep EEG oscillations and synaptic plasticity in memory consolidation across NREM and REM sleep](../publications/5c1d5eb067befe659926.md)

Yuxuan Chen; Meimei Zhao; Xue Cao; Gao Zhou; Yu Zhang

Based on a synthesis of recent advances, this review elucidates the distinct yet synergistic roles of non\-rapid eye movement \(NREM\) and rapid eye movement \(REM\) sleep in memory consolidation\. During NREM sleep, cortical slow oscillations \(SOs\) establish a temporal framework by alternating between UP and DOWN states, facilitating cross\-regional communication\. SOs phase\-couple with thalamic spindles to coordinate hippocampal sharp\-wave ripples \(SWRs\), thereby driving the reactivation and transfer of labile hippocampal memories to neocortical networks for long\-term storage\. Concurrent synaptic homeostasis optimises network efficiency through global downscaling while selectively strengthening memory\-relevant connections\. In REM sleep, theta oscillations synchronise limbic\-prefrontal\-hippocampal circuits, and ponto\-geniculo\-occipital \(PGO\) waves further integrate emotional and procedural memories\. The cholinergically dominant, monoamine\-depleted neurochemical milieu of REM sleep promotes dendritic spine remodelling and sparse neuronal reactivation, enabling affective decoupling and synaptic refinement\. Despite progress, key challenges remain in understanding cross\-frequency oscillatory coupling among slow oscillations, spindles, ripples and REM\-specific rhythms, glial contributions and clinical translation\. Future integration of high\-density electrophysiology with computational approaches may yield mechanistic models and clinically relevant biomarkers for sleep\-based cognitive monitoring and intervention\.

## [The Effectiveness of Social Media Influencers in Driving Beauty Product Purchase Decisions through Content Quality](../publications/5c230d88915919c0d4cf.md)

Isalman

The increasing adoption of social media influencers in digital marketing strategies underpins this research, particularly in triggering purchase decisions for Glad2Glow beauty products\. This research tests the argument that an influencer&\#x27;s effectiveness depends not only on their popularity but also on the quality of the content they present\. The purpose of this study is to analyze the influence of social media influencers on content quality and purchase decisions and to confirm the role of content quality as a mediating variable\. A quantitative approach was applied in this study by collecting data from 168 female consumers who use Glad2Glow products\. The analysis was conducted using structural equation modeling to test the relationship between variables\. The research findings show that the presence of social media influencers can significantly increase content quality but does not have a significant direct influence on purchase decisions\. Furthermore, content quality was found to have a significant positive effect on purchase decisions and was proven to strongly mediate the intervening relationship\. Practically, this study emphasizes that corporations must ensure that the content produced by influencers is relevant, authentic, and persuasive, rather than simply relying on the credibility of the figure\.

## [One\-Handed and Two\-Handed Backhand and Tennis Elbow Prevalence in Adult Tennis Players](../publications/5c39df0e4df8075dd6e3.md)

Ahmad Ramdoni Chusnanto

Tennis elbow, or lateral epicondylalgia, is a common musculoskeletal condition among tennis players; however, the association between backhand technique and symptom prevalence remains uncertain\. This study examined whether one\-handed \(1HB\) and two\-handed \(2HB\) backhand techniques were associated with clinically assessed tennis elbow in adult tennis players\. A cross\-sectional study included 48 participants: 23 1HB players and 25 2HB players\. Demographic characteristics, weekly training volume, and years of tennis participation were recorded\. The primary outcome, defined as dominant\-arm elbow pain \(DEP\), required the presence of lateral elbow pain, tenderness over the lateral epicondyle, and pain reproduced by resisted wrist extension or resisted middle\-finger extension\. Between\-group comparisons were performed using independent\-samples t tests, chi\-square tests, and Mann–Whitney U tests, as appropriate\. The mean age was 41\.8 ± 17\.0 years, and 72\.9% of participants were male\. The 1HB group was older than the 2HB group \(49\.9 ± 17\.2 vs\. 34\.3 ± 13\.0 years, p &lt; 0\.001\) and consisted exclusively of male participants \(100% vs\. 48\.0%, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The median weekly training volume was 6 hours in both groups \(p = 0\.757\)\. The prevalence of DEP was 47\.8% among 1HB players and 52\.0% among 2HB players \(χ² = 0\.08, p = 0\.777\)\. No statistically significant association between backhand technique and DEP was identified in this sample\. However, the analysis was unadjusted, and the substantial imbalance in age and sex between groups precluded interpretation of the findings as evidence of an independent association between backhand technique and tennis elbow\. The results also did not establish equivalence between the two techniques\. Larger prospective studies with adjustment for demographic and training\-related confounders and standardized clinical assessments are needed before backhand technique can be used to inform injury\-prevention recommendations\.

## [Enhancing library book recommendations using clustering and association rule mining](../publications/5c5b0f099ee38f9b48e6.md)

Komgrit Rumdon; Siriwan Kajornkasirat; Nathaphon Boonnam

Introduction\. This study investigates library user clusters to improve book recommendations\. The study examined the distribution of borrowed book categories and evaluated clustering performance using precision, recall, F\-measure, and hit rate\.
