The study results indicate patterns of interest and knowledge connections derived from borrowing behaviour, which can be used to improve library services and serve as a model for data\-driven library management\.

## [Visual Representation Quality Matters More Than Multimodal Enhancement in Indonesian Word\-level Lipreading](../publications/5c6319efed1248bb73c4.md)

Hanif Al Fatta; Yoga Pristyanto; Jeki Kuswanto; Rifda Faticha Alfa Aziza; Alfian Ramadhan

Visual speech recognition \(VSR\) for low\-resource languages remains challenging, particularly for Indonesian lipreading\.This study investigates whether adding architectural components or audio information can substantially improve word\-level recognition on the IDLRW \(Indonesian Lipreading Word\) dataset \(48,083 clips, 100 classes\)\.Using a controlled pipeline and the same test set \(n = 4,893\), we compare visual\-only and multimodal configurations using Top\-1 word accuracy rate \(WAR\)\.A convolutional encoder outperforms the initially considered Vision Transformer at this data scale\.The largest improvement comes from better visual\-temporal representation: domain\-specific pretraining adds 3\.0 percentage points, while replacing the temporal encoder with a Conformer using corrected relative positional encoding adds a further 4\.8 percentage points\.Audio\-logit distillation alone provides no measurable benefit, whereas representation\-level audio knowledge improves performance through cross\-modal memory\.A homophone analysis indicates a practical visual ceiling of 72\-73%, compared with 93\.29% for audio\.The best model achieves 61\.97% WAR, while a four\-model ensemble achieves 63\.72%, exceeding the published baseline of 60\.51%\.These results suggest that visual information, rather than model capacity, remains the main limitation\.

## [Efimov, Albert: A MACRO\-SHIFTED FUTURE: PREFERRED OR ACCIDENTALLY POSSIBLE IN THE CONTEXT OF ADVANCES IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY](../publications/5c6aa8025779fc28e350.md)



In Наука и феномен человека в эпоху цивилизационного Макросдвига\. Moscow: pp\. 748\. 2023This article is devoted to the topical aspects of the transformation of society, science, and man in the context of E\. László’s work «Macroshift»\. The author offers his own attempt to consider the attributes of macroshift and then use these attributes to operationalize further analysis, highlighting three essential elements: the world has come to a situation of technological indistinguishability between the natural and the artificial, to machines that know everything about humans\. Antiquity aspired to beauty and saw beauty in realistic art, but technology made indistinguishability possible, bringing the risks of deepfakes and post\-truth\. Following J\. Bernal’s logic, the author distinguishes between different types of the future, comparing them with the Kantian triad of ethical questions: \(1\) What can we know? \(2\) What should we do? \(3\) What can I hope for? Under these conditions, the fact that technology has become a real tool of geopolitics is no longer just a matter for discussion, but a subject of deep philosophical consideration\. AI is becoming not only an opportunity, but also a threat, on a scale that has never been seen before in our civilizational history\. Therefore, the former, linear development of science gives way to nonlinearity\. Society in the macroshift will be radically transformed, and the author identifies five main transformations of the current macroshift\. The post\-nonclassical approach in the analysis of scenarios for modeling the future, both accidentally possible and preferred, is becoming the most important tool of futurology and prognostics\. The author describes the future around five social trends that will determine the economy and society of the coming decades\. In addition, opportunities for the future development of science are proposed, subject to significant penetration of AI technologies\. These technologies will have a fundamental impact on all aspects of our society, economy, and human existence\.

## [Raman Spectroscopy Coupled With Chemometrics and Machine Learning for Exploratory Property Prediction in Polypropylene Carbon Nanotube Nanocomposites](../publications/5c6f233e1af4afcfd094.md)

Maziyar Sabet

ABSTRACT Raman spectroscopy was coupled with chemometrics and machine learning to explore associations between spectral descriptors and functional properties of polypropylene/carbon nanotube \(PP/CNT\) nanocomposites containing 0–5 wt% CNT\. The dataset comprised 105 spatial spectra nested within 21 independently compounded batch specimens across seven compositions, with each specimen‐specific property response assigned to its five corresponding Raman spectra\. Spectra underwent artifact filtering, asymmetric least‐squares baseline correction, vector normalization, and Savitzky–Golay smoothing\. Principal component analysis \(PCA\) was used for spectral exploration, while partial least squares \(PLS\), random forest \(RF\), and XGBoost were evaluated for property prediction\. Under specimen‐grouped validation, XGBoost achieved R 2 /RMSE values of 0\.96/0\.29 for electrical conductivity, 0\.94/0\.10 for storage modulus, and 0\.97/0\.91 for EMI shielding effectiveness\. Under leave‐one‐composition‐out \(LOCO\) validation, the corresponding values were 0\.81/0\.52, 0\.85/0\.15, and 0\.88/1\.42, respectively\. The results support exploratory within‐series property prediction and show the expected loss of accuracy when transferring to an unseen CNT loading\. SHAP analysis was used for model‐specific interpretation rather than causal inference\.

## [From Pre\-Geometric Informational Renewal to Localized Awareness: A Thermodynamic and Boundary\-Driven Model of Consciousness](../publications/5c717dda106f224c2cf1.md)

William R\. Williamson III

Traditional physicalism struggles to resolve the hard problem of consciousness, while standard General Relativity treats spacetime as a static, fundamental geometric background\. Building upon pre\-geometric informational renewal dynamics and tension\-field symmetry breaking, we propose that spacetime and local physical boundaries share a unified cosmic origin\. We hypothesize that consciousness is not a secondary emergent epiphenomenon, but the thermodynamic and informational consequence of universal background energy being trapped, compressed, and forced into recursive feedback loops by localized physical boundaries\. Furthermore, we outline quantifiable metrics—including boundary capacitance, recursive feedback density, and metabolic energy dissipation—to bridge subjective awareness with empirical testing\.

## [A cross\-domain review of artificial intelligence techniques for iot security, computer networks, image processing and smart agriculture in connected environments](../publications/5c7697bdae9fa2e50711.md)

Bashir Olaniyi Sadiq; Mohammed Dahiru Buhari; IBRAHIM ADABARA; Enerst Edozie; Asaba Shabiluh

The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data\-driven solutions across connected systems\. However, these domains face persistent challenges such as heterogeneous datasets, limited labeled data, real\-time processing constraints, privacy concerns, model interpretability, and poor generalization across environments\. This review examines the application of major Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) techniques for solving classification, prediction, optimization, anomaly detection, routing, image analysis, and decision\-support problems\. The empirical patterns across the literature are summarized cautiously across studies\. General lessons that emerged across the reviewed domains were also presented\. Overall, the review provides researchers with a concise foundation for understanding current AI methods, their practical limitations, and future research directions in the aspect of connected environments\. This article has tried to clarify various aspects and overall issues related to the use of AI techniques in computer networks, image processing and computer vision, smart agriculture and related intelligent systems\. The authors believe that this is a comprehensive and integrated survey of these AI techniques in a number of application domains, with an emphasis on their practical suitability, their current empirical limitations, and future research directions\. Thus, the article is informative to researchers in the field and may be a guide to future research on the development of robust, interpretable, scalable, and context\-aware AI\-based connected systems\.

## [ResQAI – Intelligent Emergency Resource Allocation and Crisis Response Using Artificial Intelligence](../publications/5c7a28b26c5bde8af860.md)

Aswath\.T Dr\. B\. Meena Preethi

During an emergency, getting the right help at the right time is very important\. However, many existing emergencyreporting methods mainly depend on manual communication, which can cause delays in identifying the type and severity of an emergency and assigning suitable resources\. This paper presents ResQAI, an intelligent emergency response application designed to improve the process of reporting, analyzing, and responding to emergency situations\.ResQAI uses artificial intelligence to identify the emergency category from the user&\#x27;s description and predict its severity\. Based on the emergency type, severity, location, and availability of resources, the system helps assign suitable resources and volunteers\. The application also uses GPS to capture the emergency location and Firebase Cloud Messaging \(FCM\) to send notifications to the concerned users and organizations\. A voice\-based reporting option allows users to describe an emergency using speech, which is converted into text before submitting the report\. To support situations where internet connectivity is unavailable, ResQAI stores emergency requests locally using SQLite and synchronizes them with the server when connectivity is restored\. The proposed approach combines artificial intelligence, location services, mobile technology, and offline synchronization in a single emergency response platform\. The system is intended to reduce manual effort, improve response coordination, and provide a more organized approach to emergency resource allocation\.

## [Next\-Gen Fitness: AI\-Based Diet Plans and Real\-Time Exercise Monitoring with Gradient Boosting, GMM and MediaPipe](../publications/5c93043994c52d569e38.md)

K\. Revathi; Kavitha I\.; Vanathi B\.; SanjaiKumar K\.

Global shifts toward sedentary habits and refined dietary choices are magnifying public\-health pressures from obesity, metabolic dysregulation, and cardiovascular disease, positioning targeted, personalized fitness coaching tools at the forefront of preventive\-care strategy\. By embedding tailored nutritional and physical\-activity plans into daily life, these tools reinforce adherence, enhance intrinsic motivation, and catalyze sustained wellness achievements—each moderated by real\-time analytics, feedback loops, and progressive adaptation to evolving behavior and physiology\. Their leading benefits include prolonged engagement, diminished risk of relapse, and deep integration of healthful routines, culminating in lowered lifetime healthcare costs and improved individual life satisfaction\. Current machine\-learning approaches deliver commendable dietary and activity personalization yet often fragment the upstream clustering, forward\-looking forecasting, and downstream monitoring into separate silos\. This manuscript proposes a comprehensive intelligent coaching architecture that combines probabilistic Gaussian Mixture Models to cluster users by real\-time activity and baseline health profile, fulfills dietary and regimen prescription by context\-sensitive Extreme Gradient Boosted Trees, and pairs MediaPipe biosignal capture for on the\-spot performance diagnosis and postural adjustment\. User\-background information—age, weight, and unique preferences—pours into the platform and sparks tailored exercise plans that refresh automatically via the linked mobile app, ensuring routines stay fresh and relevant\. Progress is recorded continuously, and instant feedback is given to maintain safety during workouts\. When tested against varied datasets, the system delivers strong results: Gaussian Mixture Model clustering reaches 92% in segmenting users, XGBoost\-based recommendations report 95% precision, 93% recall, and 94% F1\-score for personalizing plans, and posture tracking powered by MediaPipe achieves 96% accuracy with minimal latency\. Collectively, the metrics confirm the platform’s effectiveness in fostering sustained and meaningful wellness engagement\.

## [Hydraulic, Economic, and Environmental Assessment of Throughput\-Increase Strategies in Intermittently Pumped Water Treatment Systems](../publications/5c995672e4105d9a40a0.md)

Diego Gouveia Marques; Haroon R\. Mian; Thais Ayres Rebello; Kasun Hewage; Rehan Sadiq; Valquíria Campos

Abstract In regions facing water scarcity, optimising existing treatment infrastructure is increasingly important\. In the São Paulo Metropolitan Region, low per capita water availability and declining reservoir levels have increased reliance on the São Lourenço water treatment system\. The system, however, operates below full capacity because pumps are shut down on peak\-tariff hours to cut electricity costs\. This study proposes an integrated hydraulic, economic, and environmental framework combining mass balance, tariff\-based operational expenditures \(OPEX\) savings, Net Present Value \(NPV\) analysis, and comparative Life Cycle Assessment to support decisions on increasing treatment throughput\. Economic and environmental dimensions explored sensitivity in discount rate, capital expenditure \(CAPEX\), pump degradation, coagulant dose, construction allocation and parameters, complemented by Monte Carlo simulation of tariff variation\. Two scenarios were compared: operating existing pumps on\-peak, and constructing an additional raw\-water reservoir to avoid on\-peak pumping one business day per week\. Both achieved similar maximum treatment throughput \(&lt; 1\.7% difference\)\. Under the modelled assumptions, scenarios showed no material differences in environmental performance \(&lt; 1\.7% difference\), as pipeline construction dominated construction\-phase impacts \(91–96%\), and intake specific energy consumption remained nearly constant \(1\.3126–1\.3185 kWh/m³\)\. Economic assessment indicated negative net NPV under base CAPEX and 8% discount rate \(− R$34\.29 to − R$11\.93 million\); CAPEX, pump degradation, and tariff escalation emerged as the main variables capable of shifting viability, restricted to the three\-pump on\-peak configuration\. Among the explored scenarios, the pumping\-based strategy proved more attractive than storage expansion in most configurations\. The framework offers a transferable approach for evaluating storage\- and pumping\-based strategies trade\-offs\.

## [Italian Society of Obesity XII National Congress](../publications/5c9a805d1dbdb43e31c2.md)

2026; :O1

Introduction: Excess White Adipose Tissue \(WAT\) deposition in obesity is characterized by low\-grade chronic inflammation; as such, WAT is one of the organs mostly affected by senescence, a cellular process characterized by cell\-cycle arrest and metabolic alterations\.Although cell senescence \(CS\) is a physiological processes, chronic or excessive CS is harmful for organisms and is a key driver of aging\.Senescent cells remain viable and release inflammatory cytokines which spread systemic tissue damage, thus contributing to the multi\-organ dysfunction of obesity, of which cardiovascular disease is the most common\.Reducing CS could therefore represent a valuable therapeutic tool toward obesity\-associated diseases\.We have previously shown that essential amino acids \(EAAs\), by increasing mitochondrial biogenesis \(MB\), have a positive outcome on obesity and diabetes, counteract doxorubicininduced cardiotoxicity, and also extend lifespan in mice 345 \.Here, we investigated whether the anti\-obesity and cardioprotective effects of EAAs are associated with reduced CS\.Methods: C57BL/6N mice were fed with chow \(CD\), a high\-fat diet \(HFD\-60% fat\), or a HFD in which the protein content was substituted with a mixture of EAAs \(HFD\-EAA\) for 10 weeks; afterwards, markers of CS and MB were analysed in epididymal WAT \(eWAT\)\.Furthermore, doxorubicin\-treated HL\-1 cardiomyocytes were used as in an in vitro model of cardiotoxicity\-induced senescence\.Results: After 10 weeks, body weight \(BW\) and glucose intolerance of HFD\-fed animals increased \(\+ 35% and \+ 56% vs CD, respectively\); however, HFD\-EAA diet prevented the increase in BW and improved glucose homeostasis of HFD\-fed mice \(\-25%, \-22% vs HFD\)\.This was associated with an increase in the expression of CS markers and β\-gal staining in eWAT of HFD mice, which were both blunted by HFD\-EAA diet\.Furthermore, in vitro supplementation of an EAA mixture with an equivalent formulation of HFD\-EAA diet also increased MB and oxygen consumption and normalized the doxorubicin\-induced increase in CS markers and β\-gal staining in HL\-1\.Conclusion: Our data suggest that EAAs mitigate CS in obesity and cardiotoxicity\.This nutritional strategy may therefore represent a promising approach for combating CS and improving outcomes in obesity and age\-related diseases\.

## [Kunstig intelligens i regnskap og revisjon: Hvilken kompetanse blir viktig for nyutdannede?](../publications/5ca8ab86eda735514b46.md)

Ellen M\. Kulset; Kjell Magne Baksaas; Tonny Stenheim

Denne artikkelen undersøker hvilken kompetanse nyutdannede innen regnskap og revisjon trenger i et arbeidsliv preget av kunstig intelligens \(KI\), automatisering og dataanalyse, og hvilke implikasjoner dette har for masterutdanningen i regnskap og revisjon \(MRR\)\. Studien bygger på en kunnskapsoppsummering av internasjonal forskningslitteratur om endrede arbeidsoppgaver, kompetansebehov og utdanningsmessige konsekvenser for tidlige karriereløp i regnskaps\- og revisjonsprofesjonen\. Gjennomgangen viser at KI ikke gjør tradisjonell regnskaps\- og revisjonskompetanse mindre relevant\. Tvert imot synes grunnleggende fagforståelse, profesjonelt skjønn og kritisk vurderingsevne å bli viktigere når rutinepregede oppgaver automatiseres eller støttes av digitale verktøy\. Samtidig må fagkompetansen suppleres med fagspesifikk digital kompetanse, teknologiforståelse og evne til å kommunisere og samhandle om analyser, risikoer og vurderinger\. Artikkelen argumenterer for at MRR\-utdanningen bør videreutvikles gjennom integrering av KI, dataanalyse og autentiske læringsformer i eksisterende regnskaps\- og revisjonsemner, heller enn ved å erstatte kjernefag eller prioritere opplæring i enkeltverktøy\. English abstract Artificial Intelligence in Accounting and Auditing: Consequences for Recent Graduates&\#x27; Entry into the Workforce – What Knowledge and Skills Will Be Important in the Future? This article examines the competencies that accounting and auditing graduates need in a labour market shaped by artificial intelligence \(AI\), automation and data analytics, and discusses the implications for Norwegian master’s programmes in accounting and auditing \(MRR\)\. The study is based on a scoping review of international research on changing entry\-level tasks, competence requirements and educational responses in the accounting and auditing profession\. The review indicates that AI does not make traditional accounting and auditing knowledge less relevant\. Rather, foundational disciplinary knowledge, professional judgement and critical evaluation skills appear to become more important as routine tasks are automated or supported by digital tools\. At the same time, this knowledge must be complemented by domain\-specific digital competence, technological understanding, and the ability to communicate and collaborate on analyses, risks and professional assessments\. The article argues that MRR programmes should be developed by integrating AI, data analytics and authentic learning activities into existing accounting and auditing courses, rather than by replacing core disciplinary content or focusing narrowly on training in specific tools\.

## [Clone\-Node Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Behavioral Analysis and Machine Learning](../publications/5cb7e041a5029e4d32a2.md)

Swetha Pandithahalli Mahadevaswamy; B T Prasanna

Wireless Sensor Networks \(WSNs\) remain vulnerable to clone\-node attacks, in which malicious replicas use the identity or credentials of legitimate sensor nodes\. This study presents an intelligent learning\-based approach for clone\-node detection using behavioral characteristics related to communication, topology, traffic, distance, and energy consumption\. Since the WSN\-DS dataset does not contain a native clone\-node class, a controlled synthetic clone\-node scenario was developed from legitimate sensor observations by preserving node identities while introducing behavioral changes associated with replication\. A group\-aware evaluation strategy was used to evaluate Logistic Regression, Random Forest, 1D\-CNN, and a correlation\-enhanced DCNN under the same experimental conditions\. The results showed different detection characteristics among the evaluated models\. Random Forest achieved the strongest overall classification performance, while Logistic Regression also provided strong discrimination with a low false\-positive rate\. The deep\-learning models achieved high clone\-detection recall, with the correlation\-enhanced DCNN reaching 99\.46% recall\. These results demonstrate that different learning approaches provide different advantages for clone\-node detection and highlight the importance of considering accuracy, detection sensitivity, and false\-positive behavior together\. The findings provide a useful basis for developing more reliable and adaptive intelligent clone\-node detection methods for resource\-constrained WSN environments\.

## [A Case Study of Business–Engineering Integrated Dual Carbon Postgraduate Training at Chongqing Technology and Business University](../publications/5cb9ef668a4b5a7a38c1.md)

yongli chen; Keyu Chen; Yixuan Zhou

To achieve China’s “dual carbon” goals, interdisciplinary talent is urgently needed\. Taking Chongqing Technology and Business University as a case, this paper examines a “business–engineering integration” model for dual\-carbon postgraduate training\. Launched in 2024, the program offers carbon economy, carbon finance, carbon management, carbon technology, and digital intelligence directions\. It builds a “policy–technology–market” curriculum with compulsory, elective, and practical modules, supported by interdisciplinary mentors, industry mentors, and joint training bases\. The paper also reviews relevant literature and proposes recommendations on differentiated positioning, double\-qualified faculty teams, and industry\-education integration to improve local university talent training and regional service capacity\.

## [Diabetic Ketoacidosis as the Presenting Feature of Type 3C Diabetes: A Case Report of Missed Chronic Calcific Pancreatitis](../publications/5cba999c09519b3481ae.md)

Ronak Prakashkumar Shah; Mittal Sindhav; Parth Rohitkumar Shah

Type 3C Diabetes Mellitus \(T3cDM\), also termed pancreatogenic or pancreatic diabetes, arises from exocrine pancreatic disease, yet remains widely underdiagnosed and misclassified as Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus \(T2DM\)\. This misclassification carries significant therapeutic consequences, as standard oral hypoglycaemic regimens used in T2DM are often inappropriate or contraindicated in the setting of pancreatic exocrine failure\. We report a 38\-year\-old male driver with a five\-year history of diabetes mellitus managed on tablet metformin 500 mg and glimepiride 1 mg twice daily, who presented with epigastric pain, low\-grade fever, and incidental post\-varicella cutaneous lesions\. Investigations revealed metabolic acidosis with an elevated anion gap consistent with mild Diabetic Ketoacidosis \(DKA\), hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, and a markedly elevated C\-Reactive Protein \(CRP &gt;300 mg/L\)\. Retrospective analysis confirmed that this patient had been inappropriately treated with oral hypoglycaemic agents contraindicated in pancreatogenic diabetes\. In\-hospital management included intravenous fluid resuscitation, broad\-spectrum antibiotics, continuous actrapid insulin infusion, and subsequent initiation of basal insulin glargine once the metabolic acidosis resolved\. The case highlights prolonged misclassification of T3cDM as T2DM, atypical DKA presentation, and the diagnostic limitation of normalto\-low pancreatic enzymes\.

## [ChatGPT, integridad académica y plagio: percepciones de estudiantes universitarios de educación](../publications/5cc830f421ad468a8a69.md)

Lili Gualasca Camones Pariamachi; Jéssica Paola Palacios Garay; Pablo Celestino Olivares Rodríguez; Alan Rodrigo Olivares Vásquez

El uso de ChatGPT en la educación superior plantea desafíos para distinguir entre el apoyo tecnológico y la sustitución del trabajo intelectual\. Este estudio analizó las perspectivas de los estudiantes sobre su uso y sus implicaciones para la integridad académica, con énfasis en las prácticas asociadas al plagio durante 2025\. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa basada en la fenomenología hermenéutica, en la que participaron nueve estudiantes de los programas de educación inicial, primaria y secundaria de la Escuela de Educación Superior Pedagógica de Loreto\. Los testimonios obtenidos mediante entrevistas se analizaron inductivamente a través de la transcripción, la lectura, la codificación y la interpretación de unidades de significado, con el apoyo de ATLAS\.ti\. La integridad académica emergió como un eje transversal que articuló la responsabilidad, la verificación, la transparencia, la equidad, la mediación docente y el apoyo a la escritura\. Los participantes valoraron la organización textual y el ahorro de tiempo, pero también reconocieron prácticas de copia y ocultamiento del uso de la inteligencia artificial\. Algunos consideraron que modificar palabras permitía evitar el plagio, lo que evidenció tensiones entre la honestidad declarada y la comprensión de la autoría\. Los hallazgos sugieren la necesidad de fortalecer conjuntamente la alfabetización digital y la formación en integridad académica mediante la orientación docente y el establecimiento de criterios institucionales que promuevan la verificación de la información, el reconocimiento de las fuentes y la transparencia en el uso de herramientas de asistencia tecnológica\.

## [Tariffs, FDI, and tourism drive transport CO2 emissions: evidence from SCO countries](../publications/5cca4fbdbfd357ed4f18.md)

Muhammad Imran; Hui Zhang; Na Wei; Abad Alzuman; Qian Liu; Gulnara Mamirkulova; Xuebing Zhang; Siyuan Du

Abstract The Shanghai Cooperation Organization \(SCO\) includes fast emerging member states with their trade, investment and industrial policies affecting trans boundary ecosystem\. The study examines how tariff laws, tourism, direct foreign investment, industrialization, and inflation affect CO 2 emissions in the transport sector in the SCO members from 1994 to 2024\. The study is the first inclusive analytical research of tariff regimes on transport CO 2 emissions in SCO countries using principal component analysis, dynamic panel autoregressive distributed lag\-error correction mechanism and kernel regularized least squares models as one unified analytical model\. There is a relationship between FDI, ITA, TRM, TRA, and CO 2 emissions that are in equilibrium in the long term, and that CO 2 emissions are highly persistent\. Despite the fact that it decreases over time, FDI reduces the CO 2 emissions; however, industrialization is the most prevalent source of CO 2 emission\. The causative effects of ITA on CO 2 emissions are more pronounced in the medium\- and long\-run, though the short\-term effects depend on the individual policies\. TRA affects tourism in China positively whilst negatively affecting tourism in India and Pakistan; however, the opposite is true of TRM\. The study also enhances to the trade\-environment theory by showing that the tariff mechanisms toil through assorted channels and so contest the assumption of a uniform impact of the tariffs\. Instead of limiting the flow of investments in the SCO countries, policymakers should offer special relief on tariffs and focus on FDI as the way to facilitate transfer of clean technology\.

## [Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV\-uninfected adults: a study from China](../publications/5ccb8eccfb86866db767.md)

Jinfeng Su; Kai Gao; Shasha Han; Xuewen Tang; Xue Guo; Hui Liang; Xiaoqin Liu; Xu Xiaoteng; Jun Yan; Ye Qiu; Ye Yao; Dingyan Yan; Baiqing Zhao; Kexing Zhou; Chenlu Xu; Xiaohua Qi; Yehong Wu; Jianhua Yu

Objective To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine \(IIV3\) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China\. Methods This single\-center, open\-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three\-arm clinical study\. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV \(Group 1\) and 236 age\- and sex\-comparable HIV\-uninfected adults \(Group 2\)\. Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 \(0\.5 mL\) on Day 0\. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition \(HI\) antibody testing against A\(H1N1\), A\(H3N2\), and B/Victoria strains\. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer \(GMT\), and geometric mean increase \(GMI\)\. Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events \(AEs\) and serious adverse events \(SAEs\) during 6 months of follow\-up\. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza\-like illness \(ILI\), without assessment of vaccine efficacy\. Results A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2\. At 28 days post\-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A\(H1N1\) \(91\.00% vs\. 86\.69%, P &gt; 0\.05\), but significantly lower for A\(H3N2\) \(49\.50% vs\. 89\.52%\) and B/Victoria \(40\.00% vs\. 64\.52%\) \(both P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A\(H1N1\), A\(H3N2\), and B/Victoria \(94\.00% vs\. 97\.98%, 63\.50% vs\. 97\.18%, and 40\.50% vs\. 68\.55%, respectively\)\. Post\-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. GMI was higher for A\(H1N1\) but lower for A\(H3N2\) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine\-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A\(H3N2\)\. IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated\. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine\-related SAEs were reported\. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza\-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza\. Conclusion Adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains\. A\(H1N1\) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A\(H3N2\) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV\-uninfected adults\. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine\-induced immune responses for several strain\-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A\(H3N2\)\. IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV\. Clinical trial registration https://www\.chictr\.org\.cn/showprojEN\.html?proj=255613 , identifier ChiCTR2500112191\.

## [Interdependent urban economies: a network analysis of socio\-economic relationships between street vendors and formal businesses in Ratnapura, Sri Lanka](../publications/5cda948f30e1c4b6f5da.md)

Oshini Kularathne; Lakshika Meetiyagoda; Kokila Sooriyagoda; Nimesh Akalanka

Introduction The struggle between street vendors and authorities over access to public spaces in urban areas has drawn the attention of scholars for a long time\. In the case study of Ratnapura in Sri Lanka, we aim to make visible the social network infrastructure of street vendors with a focus on two major objectives: \(1\) Exploration of the nature of the relationship between street vendors and formal urban space, and \(2\) Evaluation of the importance of street vendors for the functions of formal urban spaces\. Methods The primary data collection methods were systematic observations and semi\-structured interviews with 30 participants selected through snowball sampling\. The collected data were used to develop activity maps by adapting Håkansson’s Economic Network Model \(ENM\) and Social Network Analysis \(SNA\)\. Results The results revealed four types of relationships among the street vendors and formal shop owners—direct, indirect, uni\-directional, and bi\-directional—based on the three dimensions of actor bonds, activity links, and resource ties\. The findings further demonstrate that street vendors interact directly with a wide range of actors and serve as bridges or intermediaries within the urban economic network\. Moreover, the results indicate that street vendors do not merely survive in public spaces; they also generate indirect benefits, provide essential services, and support the functioning of other actors within the formal urban system\. Discussion These findings contribute novel insights to social network analysis research by demonstrating the patterns of socio\-economic relationships between street vendors and formal urban actors\. Moreover, this research encourages urban planners and policymakers to recognize the contribution of street vendors to urban economic development\.

## [Physics\-Constrained Transfer Learning Uncovers Mineralogical Controls on Shale Caprock Integrity During CO2 Storage](../publications/5ce86c28c831759d13de.md)

Xiaolong Peng; Chen Zhuoheng; Fanhua Zeng; Wanju Yuan; Hyojong Lee; Chunqing Jiang

Quantifying caprock integrity for CO2 storage is often constrained by the limited availability of well\-preserved caprock samples for geomechanical testing and a limited understanding of the localized CO2\-induced mineralogical alterations\. To address this challenge, this study develops a physics\-constrained transfer learning framework to predict static Poisson’s ratio and fracture pressure directly from shale mineralogy\. A fully connected neural network was pre\-trained using a large synthetic siliceous shale dataset generated with a coherent potential approximation model and subsequently fine\-tuned with limited experimental measurements\. The optimized model achieved strong predictive performance \(MAE = 0\.016, RMSE = 0\.024, MAPE = 6\.223%\) on the small experimental dateset\. Application to Clearwater siliceous shale caprocks in Alberta, Canada, indicates limited matrix\-scale mechanical degradation after 84 days of exposure to CO2\-saturated brine, with predicted fracture pressure reductions below \~ 3%\. The proposed framework provides a scalable and non\-destructive approach for early\-stage caprock screening and may be transferable to other subsurface storage systems, including H2 and geothermal applications\.

## [Developmental and Regulatory Framework of Shoot Branching in Plants](../publications/5cf2eb70f981b5d39eb7.md)

Linan Yue; Shuo Liu; Song Yu

How do plants build a branch? Shoot branching is a fundamental determinant of plant architecture and is best understood as a dynamic developmental program governed by the coordinated action of multiple regulatory processes rather than by isolated pathways\. Branch formation proceeds through a series of coordinated developmental transitions, from axillary meristem initiation and bud establishment to dormancy, activation, and sustained branch outgrowth, driven by interactions among phytohormones, transcription factors, environmental cues, and cellular processes\. Here, we propose a developmental framework that integrates these successive stages and synthesize recent advances from both herbaceous and woody plants to illustrate how hormonal, transcriptional, and environmental signals coordinate branch development\. We further highlight that these regulatory networks ultimately converge on fundamental cellular processes—including cell cycle progression, vascular differentiation, cell wall remodeling, and mechanical regulation—to execute branch formation\. Finally, we discuss the evolutionary diversification of branching mechanisms and emerging technologies, including single\-cell and spatial omics, comparative genomics, and artificial intelligence, that are advancing our understanding of shoot branching and accelerating the molecular design of plant architecture\. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding how plants build branches and offers new perspectives for future research and crop improvement\.

## [Campus public opinion monitoring method based on Bi\-LSTM and attention mechanism](../publications/5d02fe270641f5ef4433.md)

Muyun Hai; Xiaofei Mo

With the widespread use of social media on campus, online public opinion has become a major factor affecting the stability of universities\. Traditional public opinion monitoring methods mainly rely on keyword filtering and statistical models\. These methods fail to capture the contextual semantic features of text and lack the ability to predict the dynamic evolution of sudden opinion events\. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a campus online public opinion monitoring model that combines Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory and Attention Mechanism\. The Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory learns the temporal features of text in both directions, enhancing its ability to represent contextual information\. The Attention Mechanism dynamically focuses on key opinion\-related words, improving the efficiency of extracting critical information\. Experimental results show that the model achieved an F1 score of 0\.81 and a recall of 0\.72 on the THUCNews dataset, slightly lower than BERT’s 0\.73\. On the Twitter dataset, the recall was 0\.75\. In sentiment analysis, the model achieved a strength score of 0\.82 on 10,000 data points, 0\.07 higher than the second\-best model\. In terms of text analysis efficiency, the proposed model achieves 78\.35% on the THUCNews dataset and 82\.47% on the Twitter dataset, both higher than the three comparative models\. These results demonstrate that the proposed model has high accuracy and applicability in sentiment classification of campus public opinion\. It provides a new approach for public opinion monitoring on campus and supports its development toward efficient systems\.

## [Leveraging Zakat as a Multilayered Interest\-Free Financing Framework for Entrepreneurial Empowerment](../publications/5d07852c471221474f54.md)

Rashed Jahangır

Zakat, a core pillar of Islam, is a religious duty requiring the redistribution of wealth to eight eligible categories \(asnaf\) specified in the Qur&\#x27;an\. Beyond its redistributive role, Zakat has significant potential to alleviate poverty and promote broader socioeconomic empowerment when managed effectively\. This study introduces the Jellyfish Zakat Model, a layered, interest\-free fund system that combines structured fund pooling with Islamic social finance to direct Zakat toward immediate relief and sustainable nano\-entrepreneurship\. The model operates through cyclic, layered fund pools that transfer Zakat from local \(micro\) to national \(macro\) levels in a “jellyfish\-like&quot; pattern\. Each layer allocates a large share to urgent aid for disadvantaged groups and a smaller share to fund nano\-businesses for vulnerable individuals, helping them achieve self\-sufficiency\. This approach aligns with Shariah objectives of wealth sharing and social justice, fostering financial inclusion and sustainable development\. Methodologically, the paper uses conceptual models and an illustrative distribution analysis based on secondary macroeconomic data from Bangladesh\. Results reveal that, with full collection, the framework could support around 3\.54 million nano\-enterprises annually and deliver direct aid to about 53 million households\. Even with a conservative 20% collection rate, over 700,000 nano\-enterprises could benefit\. The study also explores conditions needed for success, including regulatory reform, Islamic financial literacy, and multi\-layered governance\. It discusses policy implications for Islamic finance, highlighting that a well\-structured, multi\-tier Zakat system could transform obligatory charity into a powerful tool for socioeconomic growth among vulnerable populations\.

## [Urine sediment classification using deep learning models](../publications/5d07a8df8c76b1c9871e.md)

Lara Musuruana; Mauro Pacchiotti

El análisis de sedimentos urinarios es una práctica fundamental en el diagnóstico clínico de patologías renales y urológicas\. Sin embargo, su ejecución manual es dependiente del operador, consume tiempo y está sujeta a variabilidad subjetiva, mientras que los sistemas automatizados comerciales suelen resultar costosos para laboratorios de mediana escala\. En este contexto, este trabajo aborda la aplicación de técnicas de aprendizaje profundo para la identificación y clasificación automática de partículas en imágenes microscópicas de sedimento urinario\. Bajo una adaptación de la metodología CRISP\-DM, se integran diversos conjuntos de datos multiclase mediante un proceso de estandarización de formatos compatibles con arquitecturas de detección de objetos como YOLO \(You Only Look Once\)\. El tratamiento de los datos prioriza la integridad de las muestras originales, evitando técnicas que pudieran alterar la distribución natural de las clases\. El desbalance de clases se aborda mediante la configuración de las funciones de pérdida y las estrategias de aumento de datos aplicadas durante el entrenamiento\. La evaluación del desempeño se realiza utilizando métricas como F1\-Score, Sensibilidad y matrices de confusión, permitiendo un análisis detallado del comportamiento del modelo en distintas clases\. Los resultados obtenidos evidencian un desempeño satisfactorio, lo que sugiere que el uso de modelos preentrenados junto con estrategias de ajuste fino constituye un enfoque prometedor para la automatización del análisis de sedimentos urinarios en contextos clínicos\.

## [Design Innovation and Collaborative Supply Chain Management in the Development of Animation Derivatives](../publications/5d0dc553ceed4ac0fd19.md)

Zheng Sun

The rapid development of animation\-related derivative products is undergoing a transition from full\-process production in traditional factories to modularized division of tasks and supply chain collaboration\. In 2025, the market size of derivative products tied to the animation industry reached RMB 652\.1 billion, while the total retail value of collectible toys stood at RMB 67\.69 billion, with new categories such as rotocast plush toys and AI\-powered toys showing notable and sustained growth\. However, beneath this rapid industry growth, the dual challenges of design homogenization on the creative side and lagging supply chain responsiveness on the manufacturing side have severely constrained both product quality and development efficiency\. Drawing on comprehensive industry survey data, this paper systematically analyzes the manifestations and root causes of insufficient design innovation and supply chain collaboration failures in the development of animation derivatives\. Countermeasures are proposed from four dimensions: deep intellectual property\-based transformation, design process reengineering, industrial cluster collaboration, and flexible manufacturing adoption of advanced technologies\. The study suggests that modular decomposition of components and specialized division of tasks provide an effective pathway to enhancing overall product quality\. Furthermore, the quantitative management of supply chain collaboration plays a significant role in shortening delivery lead times and improving overall operational efficiency within the creative manufacturing sector, ultimately fostering sustainable market competitiveness\.

## [Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi\-level Process Rewards](../publications/5d177c7f9c6ce54e699d.md)

Ruida Wang; Gerald Friedland; Tong Zhang; Chris Kong

Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models \(LLMs\) to tackle complex software engineering \(SWE\) and general terminal\-usage problems is a pressing challenge\. Current state\-of\-the\-art LLMs often go through large\-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning \(RL\)\. However, they mostly rely on high\-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low\-level toolcall and mid\-level workflow\-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective\. To overcome this limitation, we propose \*\*Lean4AgenticRL\*\*, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi\-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open\-ended agentic RL\. \*\*Lean4AgenticRL\*\* first builds a \*problem\-specific workflow\* system that balances the agent&\#x27;s own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification\. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi\-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system\. It provides multi\-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow\-stage\-normalized GRPO algorithm\. Using \*\*Lean4AgenticRL\*\*, we train \*\*LAR\-9B/27B\*\*, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability\. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size\. \*\*LAR\-27B\*\* achieves \*\*77\.3%\*\* on TerminalBench\-2\.1\. On average, our models outperform the base model by \*\*9\.89%\*\* and surpass the second\-best model of comparable size we know by \*\*5\.07%\*\*\. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open\-ended agentic RL\.

## [Reduced belief updating impairs adaptive step initiation in older adults](../publications/5d1cf3e96605ba124f28.md)

Alan Bince Jacob; Sonja A\. Kotz; Ryszard Auksztulewicz; Markus Köpcke; Kenneth Meijer; Tjeerd W\. Boonstra

Abstract Ageing is associated with declines in mobility and balance that threaten independence and increase fall risk\. These changes are multifactorial, resulting from interactions among peripheral, multisensory, and central nervous system processes\. Among these factors, altered cognitive control plays an important role in contributing to postural instability and gait impairments\. Here, we examined whether shifts in cognitive control strategy underlie impaired gait initiation in older adults by modelling how individuals update beliefs about upcoming actions\. Older and younger adults performed a choice\-stepping go/no\-go task in which step likelihood was manipulated across trials\. We measured anticipatory postural adjustments \(APAs\), the preparatory weight shifts preceding stepping and modelled age\-related differences in APA onset using a hierarchical Bayesian framework\. Older adults initiated slower APAs, particularly after repeated go trials\. Computational modelling revealed reduced learning rates and heightened sensitivity to uncertainty in older adults, identifying altered belief updating as a cognitive mechanism shaping age\-related changes in adaptive stepping\.

## [ABNAT: Attention\-Based Noise\-Aware Training for Robust Transformers on Analog Compute\-in\-Memory Systems](../publications/5d1dfcdced269208056d.md)

Wenshuai Yao; Wenyong Zhou; Hanyong Shao; Zhiyuan Ning; Yizhe Chen; Yuannuo Feng; Kechao Tang; Ru Huang

Transformer\-based models have become the backbone of a wide range of tasks, but their intensive computation and data movement incur substantial energy overhead\. Analog compute\-in\-memory \(CIM\) offers an energy\-efficient alternative, yet its inherent hardware non\-idealities perturb stored weights and can significantly degrade model performance\. Although existing noise\-aware training \(NAT\) methods improve robustness by injecting noise during training, they largely overlook the critical role of attention mechanisms in Transformer inference\.To bridge this gap, we analyze how CIM\-induced noise reshapes attention in Transformers and identify two key observations: \(1\) the divergence between clean and noisy attention maps increases substantially in deeper layers, and \(2\) conventional NAT can remain overconfident even when its attention routes deviate markedly from the clean reference\. Motivated by these findings, we propose ABNAT, an attention\-based noise\-aware training framework that teaches the noisy student to preserve the clean teacher&\#x27;s headwise attention routes rather than merely reproduce answers, without hardware changes or inference overhead; selective variants further reduce training cost\.Extensive experiments across vision, language, and multimodal Transformers show that ABNAT consistently improves robustness over corresponding NAT baselines, improving noise\-degraded accuracy by up to 11\.28% and reducing attention deviation by up to 85\.77%\.

## [Alternative Monitoring Approach for IPTV](../publications/5d229f00dbfb3302ba07.md)

Angel Ignatov; Hristo Toshkov Hristov; Jan Látal; Ivan Ivanov; Simeon Kondov

IPTV emerged in the late 1990s as a solution for delivering Video on Demand \(VoD\) and live television over managed networks\. Its widespread adoption accelerated after the expansion of broadband internet and the introduction of web technologies such as HTML5 and adaptive streaming protocols \(MPEG\-DASH and HLS\), which enabled television content to be streamed directly through web browsers\. Across Europe, major operators and platforms including Vivacom and A1 in Bulgaria, Zattoo, Molotov TV, Cosmote TV, and Waipu\.tv have successfully adopted browser\-based and OTT television services\. The proposed solution is designed to collect IPTV viewership data while supporting remote device management\. Its architecture includes a Chromium\-based browser controlled through Selenium Wire, enabling the monitoring of network traffic and playback events\. Additional components include a user management interface for collecting demographic information, utility tools for software deployment, inventory tracking and log processing, a secure data transmission module, and VPN\-based remote administration\. The study highlights a key challenge in IPTV audience measurement: The widespread use of end\-to\-end encryption, which limits traditional monitoring methods\. Existing approaches typically rely either on cooperation with IPTV providers to access proprietary data or on computer\-vision techniques that identify channels after the content has been decoded\. Both approaches involve considerable technical, legal, and financial challenges\. The proposed solution addresses these limitations by operating as a native IPTV client on standard consumer hardware\. This enables the independent collection of multimedia metadata and playback information without bypassing the existing security mechanisms, thereby providing a provider\-independent approach that can be evaluated for scalability in future work\.

## [Global burden, trends, and projections of five major upper gastrointestinal diseases, 1990–2046: an analysis of GBD 2021](../publications/5d270342ac9c1fbef948.md)

Xiru Liang; Yutong Cheng; Yutong Cheng; Qiuai Shu; Ziwei Wang; Haitao Shi; Ning Xie; Yan Cheng; Yan Cheng

Background Upper gastrointestinal \(GI\) diseases, including gastroesophageal reflux disease \(GERD\), peptic ulcer disease \(PUD\), gastritis and duodenitis \(GD\), stomach cancer, and esophageal cancer, pose significant global health and economic challenges\. This study analyzes their trends, regional disparities, risk factors, and future projections from 1990 to 2046\. Methods Using the 2021 Global Burden of Disease database, we analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability\-adjusted life years \(DALYs\) across 204 countries, 21 regions, and five Socio\-demographic Index \(SDI\) levels\. Temporal trends were assessed with estimated annual percentage change and joinpoint regression\. Decomposition analysis evaluated the contributions of population growth, aging, and epidemiological changes to changes in absolute disease burden\. Risk\-attributable fractions identified socioeconomic and behavioral factors, and Bayesian models projected future burdens\. Results From 1990 to 2021, global burdens of PUD, GD, stomach cancer, and esophageal cancer decreased, while GERD increased, particularly in middle SDI regions\. Regional and sex disparities persisted, with higher burdens in lower SDI areas\. Aging drove absolute disease burden in high\-middle SDI regions, while population growth dominated in lower SDI regions\. Smoking and alcohol significantly contributed to upper GI cancers\. Projections suggest continued GERD increases and a modest PUD rebound, especially in aging and resource\-limited populations\. Conclusion Evolving upper GI disease patterns highlight persistent health inequities\. Targeted public health interventions are essential to mitigate future burdens and promote equitable digestive health outcomes globally\.

## [Customer complaint analytics in digital financial services: temporal prediction of untimely responses and capacity\-aware prioritization](../publications/5d56dd42f8da5ad73cf3.md)

Jinho Cha; Lam Trong Vu; Thanh\-Tung Nguyen; Long K\. Pham

Abstract Digital financial service providers often receive more customer complaints than can be examined through intensive review and individualized handling\. Prior research has examined technology adoption, service quality, satisfaction, trust, loyalty, and artificial intelligence in finance, but less is known about how complaint records can support transparent prioritization when review capacity is limited\. This study develops a customer complaint analytics framework for capacity\-constrained digital financial services using public Consumer Financial Protection Bureau records\. Because realized churn, customer lifetime value, intervention histories, and treatment effects are unavailable, the empirical target is not customer defection or a proxy constructed from complaint text\. Instead, the study predicts an independently observed post\-intake service process outcome: whether the company subsequently provides an untimely response\. The final analytical sample contains 266,337 complaints received between January 2024 and April 2026\. Model development is restricted to 2024–2025 through three blocked temporal validation folds, while January–April 2026 is reserved as an untouched final holdout\. Structured attributes, sparse lexical features, and fixed dense semantic embeddings are compared under the same temporal design, with mean development average precision \(AP\) used for model selection\. The selected term frequency–inverse document frequency \(TF–IDF\) logistic model achieves a final holdout area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(ROC AUC\) of 0\.7653 and AP of 0\.04985\. Within the highest ranked 10% of complaints, precision is 4\.83% against a holdout prevalence of 1\.24%, corresponding to a lift of 3\.89 and capture of 38\.94% of all untimely responses\. The study therefore shows that intake time complaint information contains predictive signal available at intake for identifying complaints that later receive untimely company responses and can support capacity\-aware early review\. These results should not be interpreted as evidence of customer churn, retention effects, consumer harm, or causal service recovery benefit\.

## [Reflections on Sociotechnical Change: New Directions for and Continuities in Research on New Technology, Work, and Employment](../publications/5d5b1e62a03ef36b7a65.md)

Debra Howcroft; Miguel Martínez Lucio; Phil Taylor

ABSTRACT This reflective article identifies three interconnected themes for advancing scholarship on new technology, work and employment\. First, it calls for stronger theorisation of technology and deeper engagement with the political economy of Big Tech and AI\. Attending to the material and political dimensions of technological systems is vital for challenging dominant narratives that present technologically driven change as inevitable\. Second, the article argues for widening the empirical scope of research beyond the “new, new technologies,” while overlooking less visible sectors and the differing experiences of adopters and non‐adopters within the same industries\. Broadening the empirical field and methodological repertoire would illuminate the uneven and variegated nature of digitalisation\. Third, the article emphasises the importance of historical contextualisation\. Situating contemporary developments within longer trajectories of workplace transformation is essential for understanding ongoing challenges and informing research on work futures\.

## [INNOVATIVE DIRECTIONS IN SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING IN TOURISM: EVIDENCE, ATTRIBUTION, AND STRATEGIC ADOPTION](../publications/5d68a40c580b2ffc7df1.md)

Zilola Kasimova

This article critically evaluates eight emerging directions in social media marketing for tourism and examines whether their growing practical adoption is supported by peer\-reviewed empirical evidence\. Particular attention is paid to the attribution gap between platform\-level exposure and engagement metrics and subsequent tourism outcomes, including destination consideration, bookings, tourist expenditure, and post\-visit advocacy\. The study employs a structured literature review and conceptual analysis\. Peer\-reviewed research in tourism and hospitality, including recent systematic reviews, constitutes the primary evidence base\. Official statistics, platform\-reported data, and industry statistics are used exclusively to provide contextual information and are assessed according to the transparency of their sources\. Assessments of adoption levels and evidence strength are explicitly analytical judgments rather than quantitatively measured scores\. The reviewed evidence suggests a persistent imbalance between the adoption of marketing innovations and the demonstrated effects on tourism outcomes\. User\-generated content and electronic word of mouth have the strongest support for their underlying mechanisms among the eight directions examined, whereas influencer marketing, short\-form video, social search, generative artificial intelligence, and other rapidly adopted practices are supported by varying levels of empirical evidence\. The principal structural challenge concerns attribution: social media platforms effectively measure exposure and engagement, while economically meaningful tourism outcomes often occur at later stages, outside the platform environment, and without reliable data links to the initial exposure\. The article approaches marketing innovation as an empirical proposition requiring evaluation rather than merely as an emerging trend to be adopted\. It develops an evidence\-graded assessment of eight innovative directions, proposes a three\-tier strategic adoption framework—adopt now, pilot with measurement, and watch—and identifies a practical visitor\-side measurement approach designed to help reduce the attribution gap between social media activities and tourism outcomes\.

## [Rapid bursts and long\-term stasis: phylogeny, evolutionary dynamics, and expression of B3 transcription factors in Arabidopsis, Cannabis, and Humulus](../publications/5d6d9410157b47b89930.md)

Matteo Toscani; Ainhoa Riera\-Begue; Nina Trubanová; Susanne Schilling; Rainer Melzer

The B3 superfamily is one of the largest plant transcription factor gene families, yet its evolutionary dynamics in dioecious species like Cannabis sativa remain largely unexplored\. Here, we present a comprehensive phylogenetic, molecular evolution, and transcriptomic analysis of B3 domain\-containing genes in Arabidopsis thaliana , C\. sativa , and Humulus lupulus \. Using a gene mining pipeline, we identified 110, 101, and 88 B3 genes across the five established subfamilies \( ARF , ABI3 , HSI , RAV , and REM\), respectively\. We identified two distinct evolutionary trajectories with the B3 superfamily\. On the one hand the REM subfamily was by far the largest and characterized by massive lineage\-specific tandem duplications subjected to relaxed selective constraint, suggesting distinct or partially redundant roles in reproductive development\. On the other hand, specific non\-tandem clades remained highly conserved under strong purifying selection\. Detailed analysis of the candidate sex\-determination gene CsREM16 showed low dN/dS ratios, clear one\-to\-one orthology across studied species, and unique persistent sex\-biased expression across all six analyzed developmental stages in C\. sativa \. Comparative analysis of its ortholog HlREM16 confirmed a conserved female\-biased expression in H\. lupulus \. Together, these results demonstrate a dual\-mode evolutionary dynamic in the B3 superfamily and particularly in the REM genes and establish CsREM16 as a strong candidate for sex determination in C\. sativa , with a potentially conserved role in H\. lupulus \.

## [Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring](../publications/5d759b7bac2a92b68248.md)

Felix Conrad Oettl; Bálint Zsidai; James A\. Pruneski; Jacob F\. Oeding; Umile Giuseppe Longo; Michael Tobias Hirschmann; Du Hyun Ro; Kristian Samuelsson

Musculoskeletal care is being reshaped by population aging, multimorbidity, frailty, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, polypharmacy and increasing vulnerability to postoperative loss of independence\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has entered orthopaedic research, but its clinical translation remains constrained\. Many models address isolated diagnostic, imaging or short\-term prediction tasks rather than the longitudinal care trajectories that determine outcomes in older musculoskeletal patients\. The central limitation is therefore not simply whether older adults are represented in datasets, but whether AI systems are valid across the continuum of geriatric orthopaedic care\. This review argues for a transition from task\-specific orthopaedic AI toward continuum\-of\-care AI for the aging musculoskeletal patient\. Upstream, radiomics, longitudinal osteoarthritis phenotyping, opportunistic computed tomography \(CT\)\-based skeletal assessment and AI\-augmented dual\-energy X\-ray absorptiometry \(DXA\) modelling may improve prediction of disease progression, fracture risk, treatment failure and surgical timing\. At the point of intervention, AI\-assisted arthroplasty planning may help move total knee arthroplasty from generic alignment targets toward phenotype\-specific reconstruction strategies that account for constitutional alignment, bone morphology, ligament envelope, neuromuscular control, frailty and functional reserve\. Perioperatively, automated frailty and sarcopenia phenotyping, wearable gait analysis and multimodal temporal models integrating imaging, electronic health records, laboratory data, medications, patient\-reported outcomes and wearable signals may support dynamic risk prediction\. After discharge, continuous monitoring of mobility, sleep, pain trajectories, wound\-related symptoms and rehabilitation adherence may help close the high\-risk surveillance gap during the 90\-day postoperative episode\. However, clinical adoption requires more than high discrimination\. Explainable AI should be understood as one component of a broader trust framework that also includes calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision\-curve analysis, external and prospective validation, workflow integration, post\-deployment monitoring and accountability\. The future of orthopaedic AI is not simply better diagnosis or more precise surgery, but longitudinal, multimodal support across the full care continuum: predicting progression, selecting treatment, personalizing surgery, optimizing perioperative care, monitoring recovery and preserving mobility and independence\. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV\.

## [Exploring long noncoding RNAs as a molecular connection between immune response and autism spectrum disorder](../publications/5d7656395144457ce923.md)

Anaya Roschyk; Daniel B\. Campbell

Autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\) is a neurodevelopmental condition increasingly linked to immune dysregulation, with long noncoding RNAs \(lncRNAs\) emerging as potential regulators of both neural and immune processes\. This study commenced by analyzing ten unique lncRNAs and integrated ASD whole\-blood datasets using the online platform GTex to identify expression of lncRNAs in various tissues\. Moreover, the platform Network Analyst was utilized to assess differentially expressed lncRNAs and associated transcriptomic networks\. A total of 93 upregulated and 51 downregulated lncRNAs were identified in people with ASD with tissue specific enrichment observed for MSNP1AS and LNC01238 in immune related systems\. The transcription factor CEBPA was shown to interact with the upregulated lncRNA MALAT1 , which influenced immune cell differentiation, inflammation and cytokine signaling\. Intriguingly CEBPA simultaneously interacted with downregulated lnc RNA MIR22HG\. Comparatively, downregulated lncRNAs were associated with the transcription factors TEAD2, CEBPA, CTCF, E2F4, TFAP2C, HIF1A, ETS1, HNF4A, SNAPC4, STAT1, STAT2, TEAD2, FOXC1, BRCA1, AR, E2F4, EOMES, SPI1, DACH1, E2F1, TP63, HMAP1, KLF9, HDGF, and MAZ\. Overall, the findings support a role for lncRNAs in ASD pathophysiology and immune dysregulation, pointing to their potential as biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for future research\.

## [Engaging Patient Communities in Intracranial Neuroscience Research](../publications/5d818afd12fb881f7ea7.md)

Ashley E\. Walton; Erika Versalovic; Amanda R\. Merner; Gabriel Lázaro‐Muñoz; Alan Bush; Robert Mark Richardson

Patients who participate in intracranial neuroscience research make invaluable contributions to our understanding of the brain, accelerating the development of neurotechnological interventions\. Engagement of patients as part of this research presents unique challenges, where study goals can be distant from immediate clinical applications and require specialized domain knowledge\. Yet methods for meaningfully integrating patient communities as part of these research efforts are essential, as intracranial neuroscience guides the application of artificial intelligence \(AI\) for understanding and enhancing human cognition\. In order to identify what patients consider meaningful research engagement we interviewed individuals who participated in a study during their Deep Brain Stimulation \(DBS\) surgery and attended a group event where they interacted with our research team\. Analysis of semi\-structured interviews identified four main themes: interest in science and the future of clinical care, contributing to science to improve lives, connecting with others, and accessibility considerations\. Based on these insights, we propose strategies for transformational participation of patient communities in intracranial neuroscience research with respect to engagement objectives, communication and scope\. This approach offers a foundation for sustaining relationships between scientists and communities rooted in trust and transparency, to ensure that impacts of AI\-driven neurotechnology on human health and cognition are aligned with patient needs as well as desired public values\.

## [Smart Portable Sensor System for Microplastic Detection in Water](../publications/5d8a45238ace35ced7f6.md)

Bavatharani K\.; Janani S\.; Leena Sri S\.; Preethi Monika K\.

Microplastic contamination is existing as one of the major environmental issues, which needs to be addressed in an efficient manner using economical detection methods\. Existing microplastics detection methods use spectroscopic and microscopic approaches to provide accurate results but these methods rely on expensive equipment and sample preparation processes\. In the proposed system, LED is used, while the photodiode measures the change in the intensity of transmitted light with the LM358 being the operational amplifier used for signal conditioning\. The Arduino Uno serves as the microcontroller, which takes the data input and classifies the level of contamination based on a threshold level\. The contamination level is indicated by using an OLED interface and indicator LEDs is used to enable instant interpretation for the users\. Experiments carried out using water with various levels of contamination showed reliable sensor operation with quick response time and accurate classification of the contamination level\.

## [Undergraduate Nursing Students’ Experiences and Perceptions of Virtual Reality\-based Clinical Skills Training in Saudi Arabia: A Qualitative Study](../publications/5d8a9ea07cea2f5f6cbe.md)

Amal A Alfouzan; Ahmed S\. Alsadoun; Fahad Alharbi; Albaraa N Aloudah; Yazan A Alghamdi; Yahia Aldhamri

Introduction: Virtual Reality \(VR\) is increasingly used in nursing education to support clinical skills through immersive and interactive learning\. Although evidence of its educational benefits is growing, qualitative research exploring nursing students’ experiences of VR\-based learning in Saudi Arabia remains limited\. Aim: To explore nursing students’ experiences and perceptions of VR\-based clinical skills training at King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia\. Materials and Methods: A qualitative study was conducted with 11 undergraduate nursing students who had participated in VR\-based clinical skills training at King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia\. Participants were recruited based on predefined eligibility criteria\. Data were collected through individual semistructured interviews via Zoom and analysed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis\. Results: Four main themes were identified: VR as an immersive and engaging learning environment; building confidence and clinical readiness; comparing VR with traditional clinical skills training; and challenges and future directions for VR\-based nursing education\. Participants reported that VR increased engagement, improved their understanding of clinical procedures, and strengthened confidence, clinical judgement, and readiness for practice\. They valued repeated practice in a safe environment but emphasised that VR could not reproduce the relational and emotional dimensions of real patient care\. Participants therefore preferred a blended approach combining VR with traditional clinical training\. Reported challenges included initial unfamiliarity with the technology, occasional temporary dizziness, and the limited range of clinical scenarios available\. Conclusion: Nursing students perceived VR\-based clinical skills training as a valuable educational approach that supported learning, confidence, and clinical preparedness\. VR may be most beneficial when used as a complementary tool alongside traditional simulation and clinical education rather than as a replacement for direct clinical experience\.

## [Пружина цифровой эволюции\. Эссе, часть 2 / The Spring of Digital Evolution\. Essay, part 2 / Die Feder der digitalen Evolution\. Essay, Teil 2](../publications/5d8bbbee24f279a53daf.md)

Khomenko Serhii

English\. An essay by Serhii Khomenko \(www\.homensai\.com\), part 2 of 2 of &quot;The Spring of Digital Evolution&quot;\. Twelve short chapters, each on one page with a diagram, about the human being who has found himself inside the process of digital evolution: the opportunity of self\-realization with AI, the price of saving on models, the &quot;needle&quot; of cloud computing and the problem of time perception, the digital Wild West and the expansion of the state, the shadow computing universe, the digital sect, the range between zero and infinity, AI as a person&\#x27;s helper and as a concentrated beam of energy\. The text is the author&\#x27;s own reflection; he does not present it as established truth but as a vector toward understanding the current situation\. The Russian original \(revision 2\) is the authoritative text; the English and German translations were made from it and have not been proofread by a native speaker\. Part 1 of the essay: https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.23426352\. Русский\.
