## [Neurophysiological Effects of Pranayama on Brain\-Wave Modulation: An EEG\-Based Analytical Study of Alpha, Beta, Theta, and Delta Activity](../publications/5d9db7afb667ef556554.md)



Background: Pranayama is usually defined as slow nasal breathing and involves the control of the breathing rate, route, and timing, accompanied by a high degree of concentration\.It is still not clear how this type of breathing exercise influences the autonomic system and respiration\-coupled neural activity, and little research has been done to measure the effects of pranayama on the four major brain wave frequencies \-alpha, beta, theta, and delta \-in a controlled setting\.The objective of this work is to provide the basis of an analytic framework based on electroencephalography \(EEG\) to assess the short\-term effects of Nadi Shodhana pranayama in a highly regulated experiment as compared to quiet seated rest\.The example synthetic demonstration data used in this work included a sample of 60 healthy adults who participated in one of the two conditions of either 20 minutes of pranayama or seated rest\.Baseline \(T0\) and resting, eyes\-closed EEG were collected post\-condition \(T1\) and post a 10\-minute recovery period \(T2\)\.Change in relative spectral power for the 4 frequency bands \(delta, theta, alpha, beta\) was computed\.A 2 \(condition\) by 3 \(time\) mixed analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) was performed, and each of the group, time, and group\-by\-time effects were analyzed\.The primary analysis was augmented with effect sizes, Holm\-adjusted contrasts, correlations, and multiple regression\.Findings: A significant interaction effect for group and time was found for alpha power, F\(1\.48, 85\.56\) = 7\.13, p = 0\.004, partial η² = 0\.110\.In the pranayama group, alpha power increased \(adjusted mean: 2\.48\) compared to the control group \(adjusted mean: 0\.37\) with an approximate 95% confidence interval of 0\.64 to 1\.74 for Hedges g = 1\.19\.A clear interaction was found for beta power, while effects for delta and theta were much smaller and interpreted based on p\-values and intervals\.The pranayama condition resulted in more favorable outcomes for breathing rate, heartIn this synthetic analytical demonstration, it was found that pranayama brought about a considerable increase in alpha power and brought about a reduction of beta power when compared to quiet rest\.The differences seen in theta and delta of the groups were small and of no statistical significance\.The framework shows how upcoming preregistered studies can capture the integration of EEG quality control, repeated\-measures modelling, effect\-size estimation and open data practices\.

## [Empowering Omani EFL Learners through AI\-Based Vocabulary Instruction: Reimagining Next Generation](../publications/5da57e25e9a0cfa37662.md)

Ameena M\. Ali; Afrah Al Busaidi

This study emphasizes the role of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in aiding Omani students in the General Foundation Program to learn English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\)\. Despite the growing use of AI tools like ChatGPT, Google Translate, and Grammarly, there is limited research in Oman on learners&\#x27; attitudes and the implications of AI for vocabulary instruction\. A mixed\-methods research design was used, and the sample comprised 151 respondents studying in the Sultanate of Oman\. SPSS version 29 was used to analyze the quantitative data\. The qualitative data revealed that EFL Omani students relied heavily on ChatGPT \(49\.7%\) as the most widely used AI tool, followed by Google Translate \(21\.2%\), Gemini AI \(17\.9%\), Grammarly \(6\.6%\)\. In addition, the trust in AI \(frequency: 60\), followed by cross\-checking the meaning with other reliable resources \(frequency: 67\), learner autonomy \(frequency: 67\), and academic honesty \(frequency: 64\), but learning grammar, enhancing writing and reading skills had the lowest frequency\. The quantitative data indicate an overall mean score of 3\.67, suggesting a high frequency of AI tool use for vocabulary learning\. The lowest mean score, 3\.45, corresponds to the students&\#x27; trust in the new vocabulary suggested by AI tools\. In contrast, the effectiveness of AI tools received the highest mean score of 3\.92\. Additionally, it was found that AI tools, learners&\#x27; attitudes and challenges, learning strategies, digital literacy, and how factors such as gender and academic level affect AI\-assisted vocabulary learning in EFL Omani students were examined for vocabulary acquisition\.

## [DeLTA 3\.0: A modern segmentation and tracking tool for microscopy images](../publications/5db9fe2bf37686f94dca.md)

Virgile Andreani; Jean‐Baptiste Lugagne; Owen M\. O’Connor; Mary J\. Dunlop

Time\-lapse microscopy is a popular approach for quantifying single\-cell dynamics\.Analyzing image sequences requires two steps: segmentation \(locating the cells\) and tracking \(following them\)\.DeLTA \(Deep Learning for Time\-lapse Analysis\) is a Python package that performs segmentation and tracking\.Initially developed to handle images of bacteria growing within the &quot;mother machine,&quot; \(Wang et al\., 2010\) a popular microfluidic device for single\-cell analysis that constrains cells to grow in one dimension \(Lugagne et al\., 2020\), it was later extended to handle cells growing in 2D \(O&\#x27;Connor et al\., 2022\)\.After three years of experience and feedback, we are releasing version 3\.0 \-a major overhaul to achieve four objectives: enhance usability for scientists, improve modularity and adaptability for developers, integrate features like growth rate computation and lineage manipulation, and adopt modern open\-source development practices\.

## [Shifting cognitive structures in human\-AI collaborative learning design](../publications/5dc5edf70fc6bca50a52.md)

Yanyi Wu

This study examines collaborative learning design with a generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) co\-pilot among in\-service university English teachers in China\. In a between\-subjects experiment \( N = 60\), epistemic network analysis \(ENA\) was used to model the situated discourse structures of team dialogues, complemented by thematic analysis of interviews\. AI\-supported teams achieved higher overall scores on a rubric covering constructive alignment, Universal Design for Learning principles, and other aspects of learning design\. ENA identified task\-specific differences in collaborative discourse, with AI\-supported teams displaying a more interconnected and learner\-centered network\. Participants described the AI as a pedagogical conscience and an intellectual sparring partner whose prompts kept professional judgment visible during the design process\. The findings suggest that, in complex professional tasks, GenAI may support reflection and pedagogical reasoning alongside design work\.

## [AI\-Enabled Telerehabilitation for Chronic Nonspecific Neck Pain: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial](../publications/5dcca1648fa63f2eb9ef.md)

Yiwei Zhao; Yanbin Zhang; Ye Lin; D Liu; Jiamin Zheng; Siyi Cai

Background: Exercise therapy is effective in managing chronic nonspecific neck pain \(CNP\)\. Nevertheless, the high burden of CNP continues to place pressure on existing rehabilitation services, especially in remote or resource\-constrained settings where continuous and standardized physical therapy may be difficult to access\. By combining home\-based exercise with remote supervision and movement feedback, AI\-enabled telerehabilitation may broaden access to rehabilitation and support the continued management of CNP\. Objective: This study examined whether an AI\-enabled telerehabilitation program was noninferior to standard outpatient rehabilitation for improving neck\-related disability in individuals with CNP and compared the effects of the 2 interventions on pain, health\-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion\. Methods: This multicenter, prospective, parallel\-group randomized noninferiority trial was conducted at Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Beijing Jishuitan Hospital\. Patients with CNP of at least 3 months&\#x27; duration were randomized 1:1 to a telerehabilitation group \(TG\) or outpatient rehabilitation group \(OG\) using concealed, web\-based, variable blocks stratified by center and baseline Neck Disability Index \(NDI\) severity\. Both groups completed identical 24\-week strengthening and stretching programs \(3 sessions per wk; ≈30 min per session\) and were assessed at weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, and 24\. TG trained at home using sensor\-based movement recognition and threshold rules; OG received face\-to\-face outpatient rehabilitation\. Week\-24 NDI was the primary outcome; Numeric Pain Rating Scale \(NPRS\), EQ\-5D, and cervical range of motion were secondary\. Noninferiority required the upper 95% CI bound of the TG\-OG NDI difference to be &lt;10 percentage points \(5/50\)\. Analyses were intention\-to\-treat; assessors and statisticians were blinded\. Results: =\.15\) at week 24\. At week 24, the upper 95% CI bound was below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 10 percentage points on the 0 to 100 NDI scale, equivalent to 5 points on the original 0 to 50 scale, demonstrating noninferiority of TG\. Both groups showed clinically meaningful reductions in NDI, with comparable improvements in NPRS, EQ\-5D, and cervical range of motion\. No intervention\-related harms occurred\. Conclusions: Over 24 weeks, AI\-enabled telerehabilitation was noninferior to exercise\-matched outpatient rehabilitation for neck\-related disability, with broadly comparable improvements in pain, health\-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion\. AI\-enabled telerehabilitation may be a practical alternative for patients with CNP who are unable to attend outpatient rehabilitation\.

## [Physicians’ perceptions, reported experience, and perceived structural barriers to shared decision\-making in South Korea: a multispecialty survey](../publications/5dd4338c32566d8e3122.md)

Sang\-Ho Yoo; Min Ji Kim

Introduction Shared decision\-making \(SDM\) is a health communication practice that supports patient participation and aligns care with patients’ values\. Routine implementation depends on clinicians’ familiarity and communication practices as well as consultation time, workflow, organizational support, and financing\. In this study, we examined physicians’ perceptions of patient and professional roles, reported familiarity and experience with SDM, associated physician and practice characteristics, and perceived priorities for wider implementation in South Korea\. Methods We conducted a nationally distributed, non\-probability, volunteer, web\-based cross\-sectional survey from April 3 to August 31, 2025\. This pragmatic design was used because no comprehensive sampling frame was available and the study sought professionally and geographically diverse responses\. Eligible participants self\-reported a Korean medical license and at least 1 year of clinical experience\. Recruitment used academic societies, professional associations, web postings, email distributions, and professional networks\. Analyses included descriptive statistics, paired t\-tests, chi\-square tests, and modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation\. Results Of 709 screening entries, 542 complete, eligible, non\-duplicate questionnaires were analyzed\. Respondents rated both physicians’ views \(mean 4\.68, SD 0\.57\) and patients’ views \(mean 4\.64, SD 0\.59\) highly in their own decision\-making; physicians’ explanations received the highest rating among the predefined factors \(mean 4\.71, SD 0\.60\)\. Self\-ratings of patient\-centered communication and decision\-making practices exceeded ratings of physicians in general \(mean differences 0\.22–0\.27; all p &lt; 0\.001\), but effect sizes were small \(Cohen’s d = 0\.25–0\.29\)\. Overall, 366 \(67\.5%\) respondents reported having heard of SDM, 270 \(49\.8%\) reported experience with SDM, and 211 \(38\.9%\) rated their understanding as high or very high\. Reported SDM term awareness was associated with self\-reported experience \(adjusted prevalence ratio 2\.32, 95% CI 1\.74–3\.08; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Among 200 respondents who rated implementation as neutral or less feasible, 157 \(78\.5%\) prioritized environmental factors\. Discussion Support for patient participation coexisted with substantial professional input, while reported familiarity and experience with SDM were not universal\. Among respondents uncertain about implementation, structural conditions were the dominant perceived priority\. Because volunteer sampling, self\-report, and the cross\-sectional design limit generalizability and causal inference, the policy implications are hypothesis\-generating and require evaluation using representative, validated, observational, and longitudinal approaches\.

## [Epilepsy: Current Insights into Etiology, Pathophysiology, Classification, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Advances](../publications/5ddec1830c833f16fd63.md)

Amim Aktar; Arijit Chaudhuri

Epilepsy is the commonest neurological disorder where the normal excitability of the neurons is altered, resulting in unpredictable and recurrent seizures\. It occurs in all continents and is a medical and social issue, as about 50 million people have it\. Stigma, misinformation, and access to care continue to be barriers to patients’ health\. Despite over 20 antiepileptic drugs, 30\-40% of patients are drug\-resistant, and many patients who are taking antiepileptic drugs have side effects that affect their mood, quality of life, and cognitive functioning\. In this paper, we briefly summarize the current understanding of the biology, diagnosis, and therapeutic advances in epilepsy\. It includes the history of the disease, how we have come to understand the properties of neuronal excitability and network synchronization, and how changes to genetic, structural, viral, and neurodegenerative processes contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease\. The epidemiological information highlights inequalities between high\-income and low\-income countries and suggests there are inequalities in treatment\. New research in pharmacology, neuroimaging, and surgical techniques has failed to provide a solution to the issue of medication resistance, and innovation is needed\. Future directions include identifying predictors of seizure control that affect quality of life; establishing a new strategy based on artificial intelligence and network pharmacology for individualized seizure prediction and optimizing therapeutic interventions; and investigating the potential for neuroprotective and disease\-modifying therapy based on epileptogenesis itself as the therapeutic target\. The overall results underscore the need for early diagnosis and tailored therapeutic approaches to provide effective and compassionate treatments\. Treatment of epilepsy is more than managing symptoms; using patient\-centered care and the progress of science, it can be more than managing symptoms and towards claiming autonomy, dignity, and hope\.

## [IoT Applications in Fire Safety Management: Bibliometric Study on Resilience and Emergency Response](../publications/5de21301417f8ec6c5b2.md)

Nur &\#x27;Amirah Mhd Nor; Nor Rima Muhamad Ariff; Ahmad Amru Mohamad Zaid; Rabeah Md Zin

In the past few years, the Internet of Things \(IoT\) has been used more often in fire safety\. Simple devices like smoke sensors, alarms, and connected networks are now able to detect signs of fire earlier and send alerts faster\. These systems are not perfect, but they do make it easier to react before a small incident becomes serious\. This paper reviews how research in this area has developed\. The study looked at three main databases—Scopus, Web of Science \(WoS\), and IEEE Xplore\. At first, the searches gave thousands of results, most of which were not directly related to fire safety\. After the keywords were refined, the numbers went down to 84 in Scopus, 44 in WoS, and 52 in IEEE Xplore\. These papers formed the main dataset\. From the analysis, several points stand out\. First, more studies are being published every year, showing a growing interest in this field\. Second, much of the work is about smart detection, real\-time monitoring, and automatic response systems\. A smaller but important group of studies also looks at how IoT can support firefighters, improve awareness during emergencies, and help with planning resources\. Overall, the findings show that IoT has clear benefits but also leaves questions\. Some systems are not widely tested in real\-life situations, and problems like cost, security, and reliability remain\. This review helps outline what has been done so far, where the gaps are, and what directions future research might take to make IoT more useful in fire safety\.

## [PanRes: A database of latent and acquired antimicrobial resistance allowing 3D\-based protein homology search](../publications/5de216cc6fecb64b402b.md)

Martina Vojtková; Martynas Baltušis; Hannah\-Marie Martiny; Amulya Baral; Nikiforos Pyrounakis; Attila Beleon; Rebecca Freitag; Anna Pico\-Tomàs; Rolf Sommer Kaas; Thomas N Petersen; Patrick Munk

MOTIVATION: Antimicrobial resistance databases are central to genomic surveillance, but resistance determinants remain distributed across resources with different scopes, structures, and annotations\. RESULTS: We developed PanRes, a curated resistance database of 11 717 genes integrating acquired and latent determinants of antibiotic, biocide, and metal resistance within a unified ontology\. We predicted representative protein structures and clustered them by structural similarity, grouping proteins into 505 high\-confidence structurally conserved clusters coherent despite sequence divergence\. Their structure\-guided alignments were used to build Hidden Markov Models \(HMMs\) for remote homology search\. In seven wastewater metagenomes from five European cities, PanRes 3D\-based HMMs expanded detection beyond what was possible with BLAST, with 35\.3% of retained hits identified only by the HMMs and generally showing greater divergence from known proteins\. For beta\-lactamases, several proteins retained beta\-lactamase\-like folds and catalytic geometry despite weak sequence similarity\. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: PanRes is available through an interactive web platform \(https://panres\.rambio\.dk/\), a structure\-informed resource for exploring the whole resistome\. The database, HMM profiles, and ontology are available at Zenodo \(10\.5281/zenodo\.22876216\)\. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online\.

## [Behind the Façade: Genderwashing in Indian HEIs](../publications/5de405b92b0d986db70b.md)

Bidisha Banerji; Smitha Girija; Neetika Batra; Gautam Agrawal

ABSTRACT This study investigates genderwashing practices in Indian higher education institutions \(HEIs\) as an organisational phenomenon\. It draws on Joan Acker&\#x27;s framework of gendered organisations to examine the manifestations of genderwashing through five processes: the division of labour, cultural symbols, interactions, individual identities and organisational logic\. Semi‐structured interviews with 26 senior academic administrators across non‐STEM fields in HEIs reveal how symbolic compliance with gender policies coexists with hidden biases in work allocation, cultural norms and leadership progression\. The findings demonstrate how symbolic gender compliance sustains male‐dominated management structures while fulfilling external regulatory demands for gender equity\. These results affect HEIs’ contribution to meeting Sustainable Development Goals targets related to gender equality and decent work\. Instead of framing structural barriers as ‘individual choices’, the authors recommend that HEIs invest in processes and structures that make them gender‐inclusive, such as affordable childcare and flexible working arrangements, which impact career progression\. Gendered actions and attitudes embedded in the structures and minds of stakeholders involved in higher education need re‐examination and subsequent action\.

## [Social Support and Psychological Resilience: Understanding Their Role in Reducing Psychological Distress](../publications/5df95119d44a88cd2ce2.md)

Ahmad Mujtaba; Muhammad Usman; Muhammad Hasnain

Early adulthood and university life expose students to significant psychosocial stressors\. This study investigated the protective roles of perceived social support and psychological resilience against psychological distress among Pakistani university students, while evaluating gender differences across these variables\. Utilizing a cross\-sectional correlational research design, data were collected from 200 university students \(50% men, 50% women; age range: 18–30 years\) selected via purposive sampling\. Data collection utilized the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support \(MSPSS\), the Brief Resilience Scale \(BRS\), and the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale \(K10\), all of which demonstrated exceptional internal consistency in the sample\. Pearson correlation analysis indicated that perceived social support and psychological resilience were significantly negatively associated with psychological distress\. Linear regression models revealed that social support and psychological resilience significantly negatively predicted psychological distress\. Furthermore, independent samples t\-tests demonstrated significant gender differences: male students reported higher perceived social support and resilience, whereas female students experienced significantly higher psychological distress\. These findings highlight the critical need for higher education institutions in Pakistan to implement targeted resilience\-building programs, gender\-sensitive support structures, and accessible campus counseling services to mitigate student distress\.

## [Cerebrospinal Fluid: From the Sacred River of the Brain to an Emerging Reservoir of Neural Stem and Progenitor Cells](../publications/5dfeafec3ac559044dac.md)

Jingzhong Ding; 许春茹; Thomas Boland; Yuanyuan Zhang

For centuries, cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) was regarded primarily as a protective and nutritive fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord\. Advances in developmental neuroscience, stem cell biology, and regenerative medicine have transformed this traditional view by demonstrating that CSF functions as a dynamic biological microenvironment enriched with growth factors, extracellular vesicles, cytokines, metabolites, and regenerative cellular populations\. Emerging evidence suggests that CSF serves both as a critical signaling niche for neural stem cells and as a source of heterogeneous stem\-like and progenitor cell populations that may contribute to central nervous system \(CNS\) development, homeostasis, and repair\. Unlike established stem\-cell sources such as bone marrow, umbilical cord blood, or adipose tissue, the identity, origin, and functional significance of CSF\-derived regenerative cells remain incompletely understood\. Recent studies implicate multiple cellular sources, including the choroid plexus, ventricular\-subventricular zone, ependymal\-associated progenitors, and other periventricular stem\-cell niches\. Furthermore, growing recognition of the roles of the choroid plexus\-CSF axis, glymphatic transport system, and age\-associated changes in CSF composition has expanded our understanding of how the CSF microenvironment regulates neurogenesis and neurological health\. This review summarizes current knowledge of CSF\-derived stem/progenitor cells, including their putative origins, biological properties, mechanisms of action, and potential applications in disease modeling, biomarker discovery, and regenerative medicine\. We further highlight emerging engineering approaches, including choroid plexus organoids, biomaterial\-based niche engineering, microphysiological systems, neural organoids, three\-dimensional bioprinting, single\-cell multi\-omics, and artificial intelligence\-driven analyses that may accelerate progress in the field\. Finally, we discuss current challenges involving cellular identity, standardization, scalability, and clinical translation, as well as future opportunities for leveraging CSF\-derived cellular and molecular components in precision neurology and next\-generation regenerative therapies\.

## [A Finite‐Time Criterion for Non‐Stabilizability of Discrete‐Time Switched Linear Autonomous Systems](../publications/5e00d90ff4720d8baab3.md)

Xuehui Li; H Z Chen

ABSTRACT Existing methods based on state space covering often fail to determine the non‐stabilizability of discrete‐time switched linear autonomous systems within a finite number of steps\. To address this limitation, this article proposes a novel approach that establishes a finite upper bound for the verification time of stabilizability\. First, we rigorously define the convergence exponent for switched linear systems and establish its correspondence between the original system and a scaled‐down system\. Second, we derive the relationship between the contraction regions induced by any switching path in both the original and the scaled‐down systems\. This leads to an estimate of a lower bound on the maximum path length for a global norm‐contracting path set in the original system\. By integrating this bound with the derived properties of the convergence exponent, we develop a verifiable criterion for determining the stabilizability of the original system\. Furthermore, to facilitate the analysis of the scaled‐down system, we propose an efficient method to verify the stabilizability of systems with minimal non‐contraction regions\. Finally, two numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach\.

## [The illusion of outsourcing learning: A learner\-centered perspective on AI in education](../publications/5e04622e2619f6a4a395.md)

Markus H\. Hefter

Generative artificial intelligence \(genAI\) is rapidly transforming education, but not the cognitive mechanisms through which humans learn\. However, genAI’s effects on learning are often discussed in terms of technological capabilities rather than the cognitive processes through which learning occurs\. In this paper, I build on learner\-centered accounts for evaluating genAI in education\. Through an educational psychology and cognitive science lens, I argue that technologies can influence learning only insofar as they support or interfere with learners’ active cognitive processing\. This perspective is particularly important because genAI can increasingly perform cognitive operations on learners’ behalf, such as generating explanations, organizing information, and solving problems\. Such capabilities may indeed increase efficiency, but they may also deprive learners of cognitive activities essential for learning\. Therefore, the key question for genAI in education is not whether genAI improves learning, but whether the cognitive operations delegated to genAI are operations that learners need to perform themselves for the intended learning to occur\. The same genAI function may therefore support learning under one learning objective and undermine it under another\. Thus, performing better with genAI support should not be mistaken for learning that remains once the support is removed\. Moreover, explicit learning objectives do not capture all cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, social, or developmental opportunities afforded by an activity\. Educational psychology is uniquely positioned to determine which cognitive operations learners need to perform themselves and which may be delegated to genAI\. It can also help identify what may be lost when such operations are outsourced\.

## [Emergency Department Operational Measures Associated with EMS Redirection Activation and Duration](../publications/5e0e50c5ce8fc99a3018.md)

Barry J\. Hahn; Anna Van Tuyl; Josh Greenstein; Kurien Mathews; Arsalan Shawl; Paul Barbara; Amin Mohamadi

Introduction: Emergency medical services \(EMS\) redirection is used to manage emergency department \(ED\) strain, but whether it reflects operational conditions is unclear\. We compared associations of prespecified ED operational measures, including visit volume, patient flow times, admissions, boarding, and left\-early measures, with redirection activation and total daily redirection minutes\. Methods: We performed a retrospective study at a single urban tertiary care center over 392 consecutive days from April 7, 2021 through May 3, 2022\. Redirection temporarily routed ambulances away from the study hospital and was activated centrally by EMS\. New York City’s 9\-1\-1 system included about 500 ambulance units and over 60 hospitals\. The primary outcome was activation, defined as any redirection during a calendar day\. The secondary outcome was total redirection minutes among days with redirection\. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated activation, and negative binomial regression evaluated duration\. Results: Redirection occurred on 250 of 392 days \(63\.8%\)\. Median daily duration was 47 minutes \(interquartile range 23\-78\)\. Higher ED visit volume was associated with activation \(odds ratio \[OR\] 1\.14 per 10 patients; 95% CI, 1\.02\-1\.27\)\. Longer door\-to\-room time was associated with activation \(OR 1\.42 per 5 min; 95% CI, 1\.04\-1\.92\) and duration \(incidence rate ratio 1\.022 per min; 95% CI, 1\.002\-1\.042\)\. Boarding time and admission count were not associated with either outcome\. Conclusion: Emergency department visit volume was associated with activation but not duration, while door\-to\-room time was associated with both\. Evaluating redirection as a single outcome may obscure differences between activation and cumulative duration\.

## [&quot;Digital Transformation in English Language Teaching: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Future of Humanities&quot;](../publications/5e13a07a93cb72220e8d.md)

Ameen Jbarah

Pushed by the Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), the rapped digital transformation has significantly affected English language teaching by loading a pressure on teaching methods manipulating the role of both, teacher and student\. The present paper investigates the role of AI driven language application and platforms, digital classrooms, and personalized learning systems in changing learning approaches and the future of education\. By reviewing recent researches, this paper emphasizes the opportunities and challenges offered by digital transformation in language teaching\. Discussing basic issues like ethical consideration, teacher preparing, and equitable access\. The final results indicate that the adopting of AI through a human\-centered approach, can improve learner autonomy, culture awareness, and essential digital literacy, using this transformation a means to amuse innovation in language teaching\. Keywords: English Language Teaching \(ELT\), Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Pedagogical Innovation,Humanities Education, Technology Integration

## [Quality of recovery \(QoR\-15\) after patient\-controlled sedation during venous port implantation: A prespecified substudy of the PACSPI\-2 randomised clinical trial](../publications/5e40232af5b23337f4d6.md)

Stefanie Seifert; Andreas Nilsson; Josip Ažman; Olle Eriksson; Michelle S\. Chew; Fredrik Hammarskjöld; Knut Taxbro

BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation is generally considered uncomplicated; however, patient\-reported recovery outcomes in patients with cancer remain poorly characterized\. The impact of patient\-controlled sedation \(PCS\) on postoperative recovery has not been established\. OBJECTIVE: To assess early postoperative recovery using the Quality of Recovery\-15 \(QoR\-15\) questionnaire in a prespecified substudy of the PACSPI\-2 randomised clinical trial and to compare recovery between patients receiving local anaesthesia alone and those receiving local anaesthesia combined with patient\-controlled sedation\. DESIGN AND SETTING: Prespecified substudy of a randomised, open\-label clinical trial conducted at two Swedish anaesthesia departments\. PATIENTS: Three hundred thirty\-four adult patients with cancer\. INTERVENTIONS: Local anaesthesia \(LA\) alone or LA combined with propofol\-alfentanil PCS during SVP implantation\. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome was difference of postoperative total QoR\-15 scores between groups\. The primary endpoint of the parent PACSPI\-2 trial was maximal intraprocedural pain\. RESULTS: There was no overall difference in total postoperative QoR\-15 scores between the treatment groups \(P = 0\.61\)\. Total QoR\-15 scores changed significantly over time \(P &lt; 0\.001\) in both groups\. By postoperative day 1 \(POD 1\), mean QoR\-15 scores had increased from baseline in both groups \(mean difference 2\.9 and 3\.1, respectively; P = 0\.02 for both\), although these changes were below the published minimal clinically important difference \(MCID\) of 6\. Before discharge, the LA \+ PCS group showed its largest within\-group improvement in QoR\-15 \(mean difference 5\.6, P &lt; 0\.001\), primarily driven by the &quot;Emotional state&quot; and &quot;Psychological support&quot; dimensions, however no significant between group differences were observed\. Median pain scores on POD 1 were 3 \(IQR 2\-5\) in both groups, with NRS ≥ 4 reported by 49% in the LA and 48% in the LA \+ PCS group\. CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation was generally good and did not differ between the LA and LA \+ PCS group\. A transient within\-group improvement in emotional and psychological recovery domains was observed before discharge in the LA \+ PCS group\. Pain on POD 1 remained common in both groups\. These findings were based on secondary analyses and should therefore be considered exploratory\. TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Union Clinical Trials Registry: EudraCT: 2021\-003821\-31, ClinicalTrials\.gov: NCT05688384\.

## [The Relatıonshıp Between Leader–Member Exchange and Organızatıonal Cıtızenshıp Behavıors Among Nurses](../publications/5e471b0958ae2a4ffbe5.md)

Kübra Özkara; Yılda Arzu Aba

Introduction: Nurses’ organizational citizenship behaviors \(OCB\) are critical to the effectiveness of healthcare services and the quality\-of\-care delivery\. The quality of leader–member exchange \(LMX\) established between nurses and their managers plays a decisive role in fostering these voluntary and discretionary behaviors\. This study aimed to examine the relationship between leader–member exchange and organizational citizenship behaviors among nurses\. Methods: This cross\-sectional study included 322 nurses\. Data were collected using professional characteristics, Leader–Member Exchange, and Organizational Citizenship Behavior scales\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Shapiro–Wilk, independent t\-test or Mann–Whitney U test, and linear mixed\-effects models\. Statistical significance was set at p &lt; 0\.05\. Results: The mean total score of the Leader–Member Exchange Scale indicated a moderate level of LMX \(3\.74 ± 1\.00\), whereas the mean total score of the Organizational Citizenship Behavior Scale reflected a high level of OCB \(4\.45 ± 0\.62\)\. Multiple regression analyses showed that the contribution dimension significantly and positively predicted altruism \(β = 0\.347, p &lt; 0\.001\), conscientiousness \(β = 0\.283, p &lt; 0\.001\), sportsmanship \(β = 0\.215, p = 0\.008\), and civic virtue \(β = 0\.318, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Affect and loyalty positively predicted altruism, whereas professional respect negatively predicted altruism; none of the LMX subdimensions significantly predicted courtesy\. Conclusions: Contribution\-based dimension of leader–member exchange plays a key role in enhancing organizational citizenship behaviors among nurses\. Strengthening leadership practices that promote mutual trust, responsibility, and contribution may increase nurses’ voluntary organizational behaviors, thereby supporting care quality and organizational effectiveness\.

## [An Empirical Study on the Impact of Moral Interventions on Addictive Behavior and Psychological States in Mobile Applications](../publications/5e499bd0ac4c5c16605b.md)

Jiuyuan Zhu; Yixin Yu; Yao Chen; Xuesong Li

INTRODUCTION: With the widespread use of intelligent mobile devices, addictive design in mobile applications has increasingly influenced users&\#x27; behavioral patterns and psychological well\-being\.OBJECTIVES: This study examines the effects of addictive interface design and the feasibility of ethical intervention through a three\-stage conceptual pathway of “addictive mechanisms–moral intervention–user response\.”METHODS: A five\-day controlled experiment with 72 participants compared a standard interface containing addictive mechanisms with an otherwise equivalent interface incorporating duration reminders, excessive\-reading prompts, and exit guidance\. Behavioral logs, GAD\-7 and short\-form SAS scores, a post\-experiment acceptance questionnaire, and semi\-structured interviews with three domain experts were used for triangulation\.RESULTS: After Holm–Bonferroni correction, the intervention group showed significantly shorter usage duration, lower scrolling frequency, and lower anxiety and dependency scores than the control group; the corresponding effects were moderate to large\. The intervention received a mean acceptance rating of 4\.2 out of 5\.CONCLUSION: Mild, non\-coercive interventions can reduce immersive use while preserving user acceptance, providing empirical and practical guidance for ethically responsible mobile interface design\.

## [Developing a Comprehensive Public Health Nursing Practice Model for Promoting Social Inclusion Among Populations Experiencing Social Exclusion: A Qualitative Study](../publications/5e553dfd5db0ef0b815e.md)

Atsushi Matsunaga; Megumu Iwamoto; Chikage Tsuzuki; Michiyo Hirano; Taichi Sakai; Kaori Takeda; Atsuko Taguchi; Yoko Sumikawa Tsuno; Soichiro Mochizuki; Ryoko Kawasaki; Ruriko Yamashita; Noriko Shiraiwa; Kazuko Saeki; Kiyomi Asahara; Masae Ueno; Emiko Kishi; Junko Omori

AIMS: To develop a comprehensive practice model delineating public health nursing practices that promote social inclusion and illustrate their outcomes in Japan\. DESIGN: Qualitative descriptive research design\. METHODS: Semi\-structured interviews were conducted with 12 public health nurses from municipalities, ordinance\-designated cities, and prefectures in Japan\. Transcripts were analysed using the framework method structured by a logic model and secondary inductive analysis, deriving the model\. RESULTS: Public health nurses recognized community friction and isolation as signs of social exclusion and intervened by establishing trust with individuals and families facing social exclusion, improving their daily lives, and empowering them\. They also developed support networks and empowered community residents\. Although some practices yielded positive outcomes, others required reassessment and adaptation\. This iterative process advanced a more inclusive social system\. All practices were consistently grounded in five core values and implemented using eight basic skills\. CONCLUSION: We develop a model empirically demonstrating the logical pathways through which public health nursing promotes social inclusion\. The model provides a framework that flexibly addresses diverse and emerging forms of social exclusion\. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Public health nurses should recognize that routine practices are key to facilitating social inclusion\. The model can serve as a communication tool to explain these practices to non\-professional staff, fostering organizational environments that support inclusive public health nursing practices\. IMPACT: This study addresses the lack of an explicit framework for operationalizing social inclusion in community settings\. The findings reveal an empirical pathway connecting individual/family support to system\-level change\. The model supports public health nurses&\#x27; competency development and assists in creating environments that enable proactive, inclusive public health nursing practices\. REPORTING METHOD: The study was reported following the COREQ checklist\. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting\.

## [Personalized Pricing as a Form of Price Discrimination Based on Behavior in E\-Commerce from the Perspective of Business Competition Law](../publications/5e6c45d006cfdf855222.md)

Ham Young

This chapter examines personalized pricing in e\-commerce as a form of behavioral price discrimination and evaluates its implications for Indonesia’s business competition law\. It argues that algorithm\-driven personalized pricing, enabled by big data and consumer profiling, aligns with first\-degree price discrimination and may create risks of behavioral exploitation that challenge the fairness principles as stipulated in Law Number 5 of 1999\. Despite its economic justification as an efficient strategy, the practice potentially violates the prohibition against unjustified discriminatory pricing when consumers in similar circumstances receive different prices without objective grounds\. Using a doctrinal legal method through statutory and conceptual analysis, the chapter is aimed to assess to what extent personalized pricing fits within existing legal norms and underscores the need for clearer regulatory guidance to address discriminatory algorithmic pricing in e\-commerce\.

## [Entrepreneurial intention, legal and institutional context, and corporate governance: Evidence from university students](../publications/5e6e6fc6eaad5df2430f.md)

Le Thi Hai Ha; Mai Quynh Phuong; Dang Thi Bac; Pham Vu Ha Thanh; Do Thi Ngoc Lan; Vu Hong Phong

This study considers the broader institutional and legal framework that promotes responsible entrepreneurship while examining how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control \(PBC\) affect entrepreneurial intention among economics and business students in Hanoi, Vietnam\. It expands upon the theory of planned behavior \(TPB\) \(Ajzen, 1991\)\. The study used a quantitative technique using survey data from university students\. The proposed correlations were examined using reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and multiple linear regression\. The findings indicate that entrepreneurial ambition is positively impacted by all three antecedents, with PBC being the most important predictor\. In line with the TPB \(Ajzen, 1991\) and other entrepreneurship studies \(Liñán &amp; Chen, 2009\), the results highlight the need for integrating entrepreneurial skills with enabling legal and governance frameworks\. The study adds to the body of knowledge on entrepreneurship and corporate governance\. It also offers useful implications for academic institutions and policymakers looking to improve entrepreneurship education, legal awareness, and responsible entrepreneurial behavior\.

## [Depressão e síndrome demencial no idoso: diagnóstico diferencial e manejo clínico](../publications/5e807280e1ecc21aaab9.md)

Eberson da Silva Rodrigues do Nascimento; Victoria Fernandes de Oliveira; Maria Eloisa Gomes Ferreira; Márcio José de Carvalho Lima; Iza Pereira Bezerra; Marcello Yuri Pinheiro Pacheco; Cristóvão Otero de Aguiar Araújo Filho; Júlia Borges Batbero

A depressão e as síndromes demenciais constituem causas relevantes de comprometimento cognitivo e funcional na população idosa, com apresentações frequentemente sobrepostas\. Objetivou\-se discutir os principais elementos do diagnóstico diferencial e sistematizar condutas de avaliação e manejo clínico diante de sintomas depressivos e declínio cognitivo no envelhecimento\. Realizou\-se revisão narrativa com busca bibliográfica dirigida de publicações científicas, consensos e diretrizes clínicas, privilegiando evidências publicadas entre 2018 e 2026 e incluindo estudos anteriores de referência\. A síntese foi organizada em eixos relacionados à apresentação clínica, entrevista com informante, avaliação cognitiva e funcional, exclusão de condições potencialmente modificáveis, tratamentos e seguimento\. Os achados indicam que queixas cognitivas marcantes, lentificação e alteração atencional podem ocorrer na depressão, mas a ausência de melhora cognitiva após remissão do humor, a perda progressiva de autonomia e o comprometimento de múltiplos domínios aumentam a suspeita de doença neurocognitiva\. Delirium, efeitos de medicamentos, déficits sensoriais e doenças clínicas devem integrar a avaliação inicial\. O tratamento exige abordagem individualizada, com intervenções psicossociais, psicoterapia e farmacoterapia da depressão quando indicadas, além de medidas específicas para demência e apoio aos cuidadores\. Em pessoas com demência, metanálises não demonstraram benefícios consistentes dos antidepressivos sobre sintomas depressivos, reforçando a prioridade das intervenções não farmacológicas nos quadros leves a moderados e a necessidade de avaliação individualizada da relação benefício\-risco\. Conclui\-se que o diagnóstico diferencial é longitudinal e depende da integração entre história temporal, cognição, funcionalidade e resposta terapêutica, evitando tanto a atribuição indevida de todo déficit à depressão quanto o diagnóstico prematuro de demência\.

## [Difficulty aware temporal transformer optimized by multi objective particle swarm optimization for sports score trend forecasting](../publications/5e830d46c10693e2fdf4.md)

Xunlong Ji

Historical score trend forecasting is important for sports analytics, but existing methods often treat schedule\-related variables as ordinary features and lack explicit modeling of match difficulty\. To address this issue, this paper proposes a difficulty\-aware temporal forecasting framework, termed DAT\-IPSO, for historical score trend prediction and schedule\-difficulty attribution\. A composite schedule\-difficulty coefficient is constructed from opponent strength, home–away difficulty, schedule density, rest pressure, and recent\-form difficulty\. This coefficient is incorporated into a temporal Transformer through difficulty embedding and normalized difficulty\-guided self\-attention to condition temporal dependency modeling on varying schedule contexts\. Meanwhile, an improved particle swarm optimization strategy with scalarized multi\-criteria validation fitness is introduced to jointly configure model hyperparameters, difficulty\-factor weights, and loss\-function weights\. Experimental results show that DAT\-IPSO outperforms representative statistical, machine\-learning, recurrent neural\-network, and standard Transformer baselines in prediction accuracy and trend consistency\. Difficulty\-weight stability, factor\-removal sensitivity, and test\-wide attention analysis indicate that opponent strength, schedule density, and rest pressure provide relatively strong predictive contributions to the forecasting model\. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves score trend forecasting while providing model\-level schedule\-difficulty attribution without implying causal effects\.

## [HYBRID PHOTONIC COMPUTING FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE From Nanophotonics Physics to System Level Integration](../publications/5e86543b7d7cf28cccb0.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

This monograph presents a realistic engineering framework for hybrid photonic computing in artificial intelligence, addressing the critical bottlenecks of Von Neumann architecture, power consumption, and memory bandwidth\. Unlike optimistic claims of million\-fold improvements, this work establishes that realistic energy efficiency gains range from 5x to 10x after accounting for signal converters, lasers, and cooling overhead\. The core innovation lies in intelligent task partitioning: photonics handles massive linear operations like matrix multiplication with 200x latency improvement, while electronics manages non\-linear activation functions and precise control\. The framework introduces Phase Change Materials for non\-volatile photonic memory, achieving zero static power consumption and breaking the memory bottleneck\. Novel photonics\-aware training algorithms, including noise injection and modified straight\-through estimators, enable neural networks to tolerate hardware imperfections\. The Thermally\-Aware Realistic Photonic Efficiency Index provides holistic evaluation by explicitly accounting for cooling overhead\. Commercial viability analysis demonstrates break\-even within 12\-18 months in data centers through energy savings\. This work bridges nanophotonics physics with system\-level integration, offering a physics\-aware roadmap from 2025 to 2035 for heterogeneous computing where electrons and photons collaborate optimally\.

## [OLIY TA&\#x27;LIMDA ONLAYN ADAPTIV TA&\#x27;LIM TIZIMLARINI JORIY ETISHNING PEDAGOGIK SHART\-SHAROITLARI VA BOSQICHLARI](../publications/5e88391379e80d23fe11.md)

## [Strategi Kampanye Militer Terpadu: Analisis SWOT Terhadap Peran Komando Operasi TNI di Papua](../publications/5e89d67ef7357233332f.md)

Ilham Panji Akbar; Agus Winarna; Ruslan Arief

Tesis ini menganalisis secara mendalam peran strategis Komando Operasi Tentara Nasional Indonesia \(Koops TNI\) Papua dalam melaksanakan konsep operasi terpadu guna mendukung tugas pokok TNI di wilayah perbatasan darat Papua\-PNG\. Pendekatan penelitian yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus tunggal terjalin\. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam dengan 11 informan kunci lintas sektor \(operasi, intelijen, logistik, Pemda, dan tokoh adat\), observasi lapangan di Jayawijaya dan Nduga, serta studi dokumentasi kebijakan nasional\. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Koops TNI Papua, khususnya melalui sub\-komando terpadu Koops Habema, telah menggeser paradigma operasi dari militeristik murni menuju integrasi fungsi pertahanan darat dan Pembinaan Teritorial yang humanis berbasis smart power\. Analisis SWOT kuantitatif menghasilkan skor IFAS sebesar 2,984 dan EFAS sebesar 2,629, menempatkan organisasi di Kuadran I \(Agresif\) pada koordinat \(\+1,330; \+1,039\)\. Hal ini merekomendasikan implementasi Strategi Strengths\-Opportunities \(SO\) secara ofensif\. Hambatan operasional utama yang diidentifikasi meliputi kendala medan geografis ekstrem, fenomena blank spot komunikasi, keterbatasan armada transportasi helikopter, serta ancaman taktik gerilya asimetris KKB/OPM\. Strategi optimalisasi dirumuskan melalui penguasaan informasi udara berbasis drone surveillance, pembentukan pusat koordinasi terpadu TNI\-Polri\-Pemda secara real\-time, serta akselerasi pembangunan jalan inspeksi perbatasan terintegrasi pemberdayaan ekonomi masyarakat lokal adat Papua

## [The Integration of Orff Teaching Method and Intelligent Software](../publications/5e9537e3bb97febfaccc.md)

Han Wei

With the development of information technology, music education is facing profound changes\. Orff teaching method, which emphasizes perceptual experience and emotional participation, has received increasing attention for music education in Chinese colleges and universities\. At the same time, the emergence of intelligent educational software provides more personalized and interactive support for teaching\. This study explores the influence of Orff teaching method combined with intelligent education software on students&\#x27; sense of happiness and self\-worth\. Through questionnaires and classroom observation, this study analyzes the trend of students&\#x27; psychological changes in the integrated teaching environment\. The results show that this integration model helps to enhance students&\#x27; positive emotional experiences and self\-worth\. This study enriches the application of Orff teaching method in the modern educational environment and provides new ideas for the reform of music teaching in colleges and universities\.

## [Levenberg–marquardt based ANN solution for MHD nanofluid flow and heat transportation over a thin needle with thermophoresis effects](../publications/5e95b90f8603134fb428.md)

Haider Ali; Aaqib Majeed; Taoufik S\. Saidani; Parvez Ali

Artificial neural network \(ANN\) techniques have emerged as powerful data\-driven tools for their effectiveness in analysis, modeling, and simulation\. These supervised learning approaches are designed to reduce the error between predicted and observed data, providing accurate approximations of complex physical systems\. To improve training performance, the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm \(LMA\) is widely adopted due to its fast convergence and suitability for nonlinear problems\. The objective of this study is to develop an ANN\-based computational framework using the LMA to accurately predict the flow and heat transfer characteristics of an MHD nanofluid over a thin needle based on Buongiorno’s model\. The novelty of the present work lies in applying an ANN\-based predictive framework to the Buongiorno nanofluid model over a moving thin needle, which has received limited attention in the existing literature\. The impacts of transverse magnetic field, Brownian motion, and thermophoresis are contained in the mathematical model\. The governing equations for fluid flow are converted to ordinary differential equations \(ODEs\) and numerically solved\. The results are also predicted by using Artificial Neural Networks \(ANNs\) techniques\. The effect of physical parameters like magnetic parameter \( $$M$$ \), Prandtl number \( $$\\Pr $$ \), thermophoresis parameter \( $$\{Nt\}$$ \), Brownian motion parameter \( $$\{Nb\}$$ \), and Schmidt number \( $$\{Sc\}$$ \) on velocity, temperature and concentration profiles are explored\. The outcomes indicate that the velocity of the fluid decreases with the upsurge of the magnetic parameter while the temperature increases\. Higher values of $$\\Pr $$ and $$\{Sc\}$$ reduce the temperature and concentration profiles, correspondingly\. The Brownian motion parameter boosts the temperature but lowers the concentration, while the thermophoresis parameter rises both temperature and concentration\. It is also observed that the magnetic field increases the skin friction coefficient but decreases the heat and mass transfer rates\. The ANN results are very close to the numerical results, showing that ANN is an accurate and reliable method for predicting complex nanofluid flow problems\.

## [THE EFFECTIVENESS OF USING ELECTRONIC RESOURCES AND MULTIMEDIA TOOLS IN HIGHER EDUCATION](../publications/5e95f40168ae297afc6e.md)

 Mo&\#x27;ydinova Mohlarbegim Abdullajon qizi; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre

This conceptual article examines the conditions under which electronic educational resources and multimedia tools can support meaningful learning in higher education\. Building on research in multimedia learning, constructive alignment, digital pedagogy, self\-regulated learning, and inclusive course design, the study compares the pedagogical functions of digital textbooks, academic databases, audiovisual materials, virtual laboratories, learning management systems, online assessments, and collaborative platforms\. A critical narrative synthesis is used to distinguish the accessibility of a resource from evidence of its educational effectiveness\. The principal contribution is a practical alignment framework linking learning outcomes, resource selection, active student tasks, assessment evidence, and subsequent instructional adjustment\. An illustrative university learning sequence demonstrates the application of this framework\. The analysis suggests that digital materials are most educationally valuable when they minimize unnecessary cognitive load, make thinking visible, provide actionable feedback, and remain accessible to students with different circumstances and abilities\. The article also examines unequal access, platform dependence, privacy, unreliable content, and uncritical uses of generative artificial intelligence\. No original student experiment is reported; the proposed framework should therefore be treated as a research\-informed design proposition rather than an empirically validated intervention\.

## [Recent Development of Machine Learning Strategies for Restaurant Review Sentiment Classification: Challenges, Applications, and Opportunities](../publications/5ead5f599aaf649fd580.md)

Keshav Prakash; Ram kumar Sahu ; Arjun Rajput

Online restaurant reviews have grown in number significantly providing an excellent source of customer reviews for analyzing quality of the food, services offered, ambiance of the place, pricing policy and other aspects of customers&\#x27; dining experience\. Hence, restaurant review sentiment classification is a good way to classify customer opinions into positive, negative and neutral sentiments automatically\. This review paper gives a comprehensive overview of sentiment analysis techniques used for sentiment classification of restaurant customers&\#x27; reviews\. It gives an insight into the history of development of these algorithms from the feature engineering era to modern ML\-based approaches\. It explores different types of sentiment analysis techniques, features of restaurant reviews, application areas and challenges of using these algorithms\. Comparative analysis of existing research papers on this topic helps to understand their advantages, weaknesses and further perspectives\. Thus, it can be seen that while traditional methods of sentiment classification are rather computationally effective, their contextual understanding is quite low in contrast to transformer\- and language models\-based techniques\.

## [Enhancing Vocational Milling Machine Learning through PowerPoint Hyperlink\-Based Interactive Media](../publications/5ecb4efc5ea391019edf.md)

Ilham Bayu Haliludin; Marsono Marsono; Yayi Febdia Pradani; Yuli Panca Asmara

The advancement of educational technology has led to the development of innovative learning media to improve student engagement and learning outcomes\. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of PowerPoint Hyperlink\-based interactive learning media for milling machine material\. The research employed the Research and Development \(R&amp;D\) method using the 4D model, consisting of the Define, Design, and Develop stages\. The research subjects were 20 tenth\-grade students of the Machining Engineering Department at SMK Muhammadiyah 1 Kepanjen\. The research instruments included expert validation sheets, questionnaires, pretest\-posttest assessments, and documentation\. Data were analyzed descriptively, while the effectiveness of the learning media was evaluated using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test and N\-gain analysis\. The results indicated that the learning media achieved a feasibility score of 87\.2%, categorized as highly feasible, based on expert evaluations\. The Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test revealed a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores \(p = 0\.000 &lt; 0\.05\)\. Furthermore, the N\-gain score of 0\.48 was classified as moderate, indicating that the learning media effectively improved students&\#x27; learning outcomes\. Therefore, the PowerPoint Hyperlink\-based interactive learning media is feasible and effective as an alternative learning resource for milling machine instruction in vocational high schools\.

## [Desain UI/UX Game\-Based APP Edukasi Pengenalan Bahasa Daerah Batak Toba Dengan Metode Design Thinking](../publications/5ece2bf885611ec3c55f.md)

Angela Fadilla S; Randi Rian Putra; Heni Wulandari

The Batak Toba regional language in North Sumatra is currently classified as Level 6b \(Threatened\) on the Expanded Graded Intergenerational Disruption Scale \(EGIDS\)\. Conventional learning media have failed to engage the digital native generation\. This study aims to design an interactive, user\-centered User Interface \(UI\) and User Experience \(UX\) for a mobile game\-based educational application focused on basic vocabulary \(greetings, numbers, colors, and common objects\)\. The design process systematically follows the five stages of the Design Thinking methodology: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test\. The research scope is limited to high\-fidelity visual prototype development using Figma\. An empirical evaluation was conducted with 20 student respondents from Universitas Pembangunan Panca Budi Medan using structured task scenarios\. Usability was measured quantitatively using the standard 10\-item System Usability Scale \(SUS\) questionnaire\. The calculation yielded a global average SUS score of 78\.5\. This scientifically proves that the prototype design exceeds the standard acceptable threshold of 68 and achieves a &\#x27;Good&\#x27; rating\. Consequently, the proposed UI/UX design is validated as effective and ready for the software engineering phase as a preventive effort against digital language extinction\.

## [Beyond Beauty: Microalgae and Cyanobacteria as Next\-Generation Platforms for Functional Dermocosmetics, Cutaneous Delivery, and Skin Health](../publications/5ed2de5701b2dadcd6f3.md)

Clément Daviaud; Herminia Domı́nguez; Luana Granja Fernández; M\. Lourdes Mourelle; Kévin Baranger; Nicolas Bridiau; Laurent Picot

Microalgae and cyanobacteria are valuable sources of bioactive ingredients and innovative biological systems for skin applications\. Their metabolites include exopolysaccharides \(EPS\), mycosporine\-like amino acids \(MAAs\), carotenoids, phycobiliproteins, peptides and lipopeptides, polyunsaturated lipids, chlorophyll derivatives, and distinctive secondary metabolites such as scytonemin\. Cyanobacteria additionally provide defined molecular candidates, including sacran, C\-phycocyanin, MAAs, scytonemin\-related compounds, and specialized peptide scaffolds\. These compounds may support hydration and barrier function, photoprotection, control of oxidative stress and inflammation, pigmentation, antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, extracellular\-matrix preservation, and wound repair\. This review examines major bioactive families, their sources and mechanisms, with particular emphasis on the strength of evidence supporting skin applications\. Recent developments from 2024 to 2026 are highlighted, including microalgal extracellular vesicles \(nanoalgosomes\), photoactivated antimicrobial systems, photosynthetic hydrogels and microneedle patches, green extraction and biorefinery strategies, reconstructed human skin and skin\-on\-chip models, and artificial\-intelligence\-assisted formulation\. Most reported effects remain supported mainly by biochemical, cellular, or preclinical evidence, whereas human validation is still limited\. Translation will, therefore, depend on rigorous chemical standardization, effective cutaneous delivery, demonstrated stability and safety, scalable manufacturing, and validation in human\-relevant models\. Microalgae and cyanobacteria thus extend beyond conventional natural extracts toward next\-generation dermocosmetic and cutaneous\-delivery platforms\.

## [The บทบาทของ ICT ในการกำหนดทศทางการแขงขนเชงกลยทธของมหาวทยาลยเอกชน](../publications/5ed5db6f8e362e0e1ae8.md)

Supon Phrommaphan; Amnart Vangjeen; Boonsiri Masan; Pongsuwat Sermsirikarnjana

The objectives of this research are as follows: \(1\)\. To study the strategic potential in the application of Information and Communication Technology \(ICT\) in private universities\. The study categorizes this potential into four key dimensions: 1\)\. Information Technology strategy, 2\)\. Capability in the use of information technology, 3\)\. Effectiveness of information products, and 4\)\. The utilization of outcomes derived from information and communication technology to support the achievement of organizational goals; and \(2\) To compare the levels of ICT utilization strategies adopted by individual private universities in their strategic management practices\. The research findings reveal that, overall, the strategic potential in the use of Information and Communication Technology among private universities is at a high level\. The dimension with the highest mean score is information technology strategy, followed by capability in the use of Information Technology and the Effectiveness of information products\. The utilization of ICT outcomes to achieve organizational goals records the lowest mean score; however, it remains at a high level as well\. Furthermore, the results indicate that there are statistically significant differences in the strategic potential of ICT utilization among private universities at the 0\.05 level of significance \(F\-Test = 7\.223, P\-Value &lt; 0\.01\)\. These findings underscore that, in shaping strategic competitive directions, private universities must place greater emphasis on enhancing the effective and tangible utilization of ICT outcomes in order to strengthen sustainable competitive advantage amid technological change in the digital era\.

## [ЗМІНА РОЛІ ВИКЛАДАЧА АНГЛІЙСЬКОЇ МОВИ В ДОБУ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ](../publications/5ed6177e4a425c8028fb.md)

А\.Є\. Александрова; Анна Віджаївна Благорозумна; В\.М\. Намазова

У статті розглянуто трансформацію професійної ролі викладача англійської мови в умовах активного впро\- вадження штучного інтелекту та генеративних технологій у мовну освіту\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена тим, що сучасні ШІ\-системи дедалі частіше виконують функції, які традиційно належали до професійної діяль\- ності викладача: генерують навчальні матеріали, надають автоматизований зворотний зв’язок, виявляють мовні помилки, адаптують завдання до рівня здобувачів освіти та підтримують письмову й усну практику\. Метою статті є визначення основних напрямів зміни ролі викладача англійської мови в добу штучного інтелекту\. Дослідження ґрунтується на критико\-аналітичному огляді сучасних англомовних наукових праць, присвячених використанню ШІ в мовній освіті, автоматизованому зворотному зв’язку та цифровій компетентності викладачів\. Для конкрети\- зації теоретичних положень також проаналізовано аргументативні есе студентів немовних спеціальностей з ура\- хуванням їхніх мовних, структурних і стилістичних особливостей\. Установлено, що впровадження ШІ не зменшує значення викладача, а спричиняє перерозподіл його професійних функцій\. Автоматизовані інструменти можуть ефективно виконувати окремі рутинні завдання та виявляти типові мовні помилки, однак оцінювання логіки, аргу\- ментації, індивідуального стилю й відповідності тексту реальному рівню мовної підготовки потребує професійного педагогічного аналізу\. Обґрунтовано, що сучасний викладач поступово переходить від ролі основного джерела знань до ролі дизайнера навчального середовища, фасилітатора, наставника з відповідального використання ШІ, модератора академічної доброчесності та провідника критичного мислення\. Зроблено висновок, що ефективність ШІ в мовній освіті залежить передусім від педагогічно обґрунтованої інтеграції технологій та професійної компе\- тентності викладача\.

## [Accelerometry\-based comparison of functional outcomes across total and partial knee and hip arthroplasty](../publications/5ed8705c36f18fe81fc6.md)

Sevasti Panagiota Glynou; Omar Musbahi; Sara Sousi; Justin Peter Cobb

Aims: To evaluate objectively measured physical activity after hip and knee arthroplasty using accelerometry, by comparing bone\-preserving procedures with total athorpalsties rthorpalsties and benchmarking both against non\-arthritic controls\. Methods: This observational study was conducted within the UK Biobank\. Adults aged 40 to 69 years with total knee arthroplasty \(TKA\), unicompartmental knee arthroplasty \(UKA\), total hip arthroplasty \(THA\), or hip resurfacing \(HR\) were identified through linked hospital records and completed seven\-day wrist\-worn accelerometry \(Axivity AX3\)\. Outcomes included adjusted daily step count \(primary\), peak cadence, moderate\-to\-vigorous physical activity \(MVPA\), and Euclidean Norm Minus One \(ENMO\)\. Surgical groups were propensity score\-matched to non\-arthritic controls on demographics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities\. Direct comparisons between procedure types were examined using both propensity\-matched analyses and complementary multivariable regression, and adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates\. Subgroup analyses considered &lt; 12 months and ≥12 months post\-surgery\. Results: A total of 2,283 participants were included \(TKA = 860, UKA = 162, THA = 1,168, HR = 93\)\. Compared with matched controls, TKA and THA patients showed persistently lower activity, while UKA and HR achieved levels similar to controls\. In the knee cohort, UKA patients walked significantly more steps/day than TKA \(9,150 vs 7,920; \+ 15\.5%, p &lt; 0\.001\) with higher cadence\. In the hip cohort, HR patients outperformed THA \(10,122 vs 9,139 steps/day; \+ 10\.6%, p = 0\.032\) and demonstrated higher peak cadence, and HR remained comparable to controls\. All groups fell within the &\#x27;somewhat active&\#x27; to &\#x27;active&\#x27; step\-count range \(7,500 to 12,499 steps/day\)\. Conclusion: UKA and HR are associated with higher postoperative activity compared with total arthroplasty \(TKA, THA\)\. Accelerometry provides an objective, scalable assessment of functional recovery, highlighting procedure\-specific differences that should be considered alongside implant longevity when selecting surgical options\.

## [Self\-Calibrated Subspace Robust PCA for Parameter\-Free Removal of Mixed Noise and Line Stripes in Hyperspectral Images](../publications/5ed920766a38e8b4fd04.md)

Wenzhe Wang

Hyperspectral images \(HSIs\) are often corrupted by Gaussian noise, impulses and stripes whose intensities vary across bands\. The representative coefficient correlated total variation \(RCCTV\) model restores HSIs efficiently, but it lacks Gaussian and stripe terms, and its noise\-aware extensions require the noise level and a stripe budget to be specified in advance\. This article proposes a self\-calibrated RCCTV \(SC\-RCCTV\) model, in which the noise parameters are estimated adaptively during the iterations\. A band\-wise dense term and line\-constant column and row stripe terms are introduced into RCCTV\. The noise level of each band is initialized by a stripe\-invariant median absolute deviation estimator and refined online from the residual, which turns the separation of sparse and dense noise into a band\-adaptive Huber loss, and the stripe thresholds follow from a significance test whose false\-alarm rate can be predicted analytically\. No parameter is tuned for a specific image, and every subproblem of the alternating direction method of multipliers \(ADMM\) solver is solved in closed form\. Under line stripes, SC\-RCCTV outperforms the parameter\-free FastHyMix by 8\.17 dB on native\-size cubes, and, without any noise information, it exceeds S3TTV, which is given the true noise parameters, by 1\.52 dB while running more than 1,900 times faster\. On average, it stays within 0\.01 dB of the same model given the true noise levels, and its online calibration improves on a two\-stage estimate\-then\-denoise scheme\. Experiments on real Indian Pines and Urban data further delineate its scope for stripes that do not span entire lines\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and Ecological Integration Drive Weed Control 4\.0 for Sustainable Medicinal Crop Production](../publications/5ede1e4cb54fb31ce0ec.md)

Yuan Liu; Dan Gao; Chongning Lv; Yifei Pei; Tielin Wang; Yan Zhang; Chengcai Zhang; Yiheng Wang; Yuan Cui; Binbin Yan; Chuanzhi Kang; Lanping Guo

Abstract Weed infestation is a persistent constraint on the cultivation of medicinal and aromatic crops, reducing yield, quality consistency, raw\-material safety, and production standardization\. Although herbicide\-based weed management has improved labor efficiency, increasing concerns over pesticide residues, herbicide resistance, crop selectivity, and ecological impacts limit its suitability for high\-quality herbal medicine production\. This review synthesizes the evolution of weed control in medicinal crop systems from manual and mechanical practices to chemical control, integrated weed management, and emerging intelligent–ecological strategies\. We propose the concept of Weed Control 4\.0 as a crop\-specific framework that combines artificial intelligence, intelligent machinery, bioherbicides, and ecological regulation\. The review summarizes how microbial and plant\-derived bioherbicides suppress weeds through growth inhibition, allelopathic interference, pathogen\-mediated damage, and disruption of weed physiological metabolism\. It further discusses how machine vision, sensor fusion, robotic platforms, precision spraying, and data\-driven decision support can enable real\-time weed identification and site\-specific intervention\. Ecological approaches, including crop rotation, intercropping, mulching, cover crops, allelopathic crops, beneficial insects, and soil microbial manipulation, are evaluated for their potential to suppress weed communities while maintaining soil health and agroecosystem stability\. Finally, we identify key challenges for implementation, including medicinal crop\-specific weed databases, biosafety and efficacy evaluation of bioherbicides, integration of field machinery with agronomic practices, and residue\-safe regulatory standards\. Weed Control 4\.0 offers a pathway toward sustainable, precise, and residue\-safe weed management for the standardized production of high\-quality herbal medicines\.

## [Anomalies in neural network field theory](../publications/5f084080192143cc53d7.md)

Christian Ferko; Samuel Frank; James Halverson; Vishnu Jejjala

A bstract Neural network field theory \(NN\-FT\) formulates field theory in terms of a network architecture and a density on its parameters\. We derive Schwinger–Dyson equations and Ward identities in NN\-FT and utilize them to study anomalies\. The equations depend on a conserved parameter space current that characterizes symmetries and how they break\. It is relevant even in non\-local NN\-FTs, but can recover local currents in the case of a local Lagrangian by an appropriate fiber\-wise average\. In machine learning, this formalism is applied to feedforward networks and the attention mechanism\. In physics, we use this machinery to study U\(1\) symmetry for a complex scalar, the scale anomaly in 4 d massless ϕ 4 theory, the Weyl anomaly for the bosonic string \(including a new computation of the critical dimension\), and examples involving discrete topological data, such as winding numbers and T\-duality\. Since the results are obtained in network parameter space rather than the standard field space, they represent a new way to understand symmetries in quantum field theories\.

Objective This study examined the effects of news content on fear of COVID\-19 by examining perceived social distance and audience\-protagonist similarity\. Method Participants \( N = 78\) read a fictitious news story about a COVID\-19 patient \(similar/dissimilar protagonist\) and then rated social distance regarding this protagonist and their fear of COVID\-19\. Results The results showed that participants exposed to a similar protagonist reported significantly lower perceived social distance, and that social distance was moderately negatively correlated with fear of COVID\-19\. Social distance mediated the association between audience\-protagonist similarity and fear of COVID\-19\. Conclusion These findings provide insights into how exposure to health\-related news content can impact fear of disease\.
