Marisa Wong; Gregory Sean Stapleton; Julio Dicent Taillepierre; Katharine M\. Benedict

Introduction Turtles with shell length &lt;4 inches \(“small turtles”\) are prohibited for sale as pets in the United States because of their potential to expose people, particularly children, to Salmonella \. In previous multistate turtle\-associated salmonellosis outbreaks, people of Hispanic or Latino ethnicity have been disproportionately affected\. This study aimed to describe the demographic characteristics of United States adults who own small turtles and to document the purchase locations of these small turtles\. Methods We analyzed data from a nationally representative survey of Hispanic United States adults and a nationally representative survey of all United States adults\. Both surveys included similar questions about small turtle ownership and purchase locations\. We compared frequencies of responses from these two surveys using weighted cross\-tabulations\. Results Twenty percent \(95% CI: 16\.1–24\.1%\) of Hispanic or Latino people reported ever owning small turtles, compared with 14% \(95% CI: 12\.8–14\.9%\) of respondents of all other racial and ethnic groups in the United States\. Sixty four percent \(95% CI: 54\.3–74\.4%\) of Hispanic respondents reported purchasing their small turtles from pet stores\. Conclusion A greater percentage of Hispanic or Latino adults have ever owned small turtles compared to other United States adults, which may contribute to the overrepresentation of Hispanic and Latino people in turtle\-associated outbreaks\. Additional research could help elucidate factors contributing to higher turtle ownership among Hispanic and Latino people and how knowledge, attitudes, and practices of small turtle owners affects salmonellosis risk\. Such information could aid in focusing public health prevention efforts on populations who are more likely to ownreported higher weighted prevalence of owning small turtles\. Such information could aid in focusing public health prevention efforts on populations who reported higher weighted prevalence of owning small turtles\.

## [A Structure‐Guided Multistrategy Design Enhances Thermostability of an α‐L‐Rhamnosidase for Efficient Biotransformation](../publications/5f2fc7bee543f8011015.md)

Yilin Kang; Bin Wei; Yaru Zhao; Shuyi Yao; Hao Liang

α‐L‐Rhamnosidase is a key biocatalyst for natural product biotransformation, but its poor thermostability limits industrial applications\. To address this challenge, this study developed a structure‐guided multiplatform rational design strategy and applied it to a Bifidobacterium α‐L‐rhamnosidase \(BcRha\), identifying T384P as a key thermostable mutant\. T384P exhibited a half‐life of 353\.3 min at 60 °C \(3\.3‐fold that of the wild type, WT\) and 81\.8 min at 65 °C \(4\.4‐fold\), together with a 4\.3 °C increase in melting temperature\. Mechanistic analyses indicated that T384P enhanced thermostability by strengthening long‐range dynamic coupling, establishing a multipoint polar locking network, and reducing global conformational fluctuations\. Notably, combination mutants failed to exhibit synergistic enhancement, possibly due to coupling interference between distinct dynamic modules\. Under high substrate loading \(30 g/L rutin\), T384P achieved an 18\.8% higher isoquercitrin yield than WT at 60 °C and retained substantial activity at 65 °C, approximately twice that of WT\. This study provides an efficient rational design strategy for improving α‐L‐rhamnosidase thermostability, reveals a possible mechanistic basis for nonadditive mutation effects, and offers a promising biocatalyst for high‐temperature flavonoid biotransformation\.

## [AI Based Cyber Threat Detection and Intelligent Security Assistant](../publications/5f479e533a1486f56bf6.md)

Aishwarya, Chandrika, Lovely Devi, Priya

Cybersecurity is becoming more Challenging due to the wider use of the internet, IoT devices, mobile applications cloud computing and interconnected computer networks has increased the complexity and high frequency of cybersecurity threats\. Common attacks such as malware, phishing, Denial\-of\-Service \(DoS\), brute\-force attacks, port scanning, botnets and unauthorized access are becoming harder to detect using traditional security methods that mainly depend on fixed rules and known attack signatures\. To address these challenges, this research proposes an AI \-based Cyber Threat Detection and Intelligent System for analysing cybersecurity activities\. The Proposed system uses machine learning techniques to examine security related data and identify whether the observed activity is normal or potentially harmful\. Along with thread detection, the system also considers unusual pattern so that activities which do not clearly match known attack categories can be identified for future analysis After identifying the threat, the system generates an alert and suggests suitable security measures so that the user can understand the problem and respond accordingly\. The performance of the detection models can be measured using accuracy, recall, precision, F1\-score and confusion matrix\. By combining threat detection, anomaly identification, threat classification and risk assessment, the approach provides a single framework for analysing suspicious activities\. It can also reduce the need for continuous manual analysis and provide users with useful information about potential security issues\. The system can help users understand suspicious activities at an early stage and get a clearer idea about the detected security issue\. It provides information about the type of threat and suitable security measures based on generated alerts\. In future, this approach can be improved for real\-time monitoring and handling of new types of cyber threats\.

## [Capsule endoscopy: Emerging technologies and future clinical applications](../publications/5f58aa100f12b767643b.md)

Clelia Marmo; Maria Elena Riccioni

Capsule endoscopy has evolved from a diagnostic tool for small bowel evaluation into a complex platform with expanding diagnostic and prognostic potential\.This mini review aims to summarize recent advances in capsule endoscopy and explore potential clinical applications and future directions of this technology\.The introduction of pan\-enteric capsule endoscopy has enabled comprehensive evaluation of the entire gastrointestinal tract in a single, minimally invasive examination, supporting treat\-to\-target approaches and improving disease phenotyping in inflammatory bowel disease\.Artificial intelligence \(AI\) represents one of the most important recent developments in capsule endoscopy\.Deep learning algorithms have demonstrated high accuracy in lesion detection while reducing reading times\.More recently, AI has been applied to automated inflammatory activity scoring, bowel cleansing assessment, and computer\-assisted reporting, facilitating standardized interpretation and improving report quality\.Magnetically controlled capsule endoscopy has further expanded the role of capsule technology by enabling active navigation within the upper gastrointestinal tract\.Recent innovations include detachable\-string systems for esophageal examination, remote 5Gassisted capsule navigation, and integration with AI\-assisted image analysis, opening new perspectives for noninvasive evaluation from mouth to anus\.Experimental robotic capsule prototypes have explored the feasibility of interventional functions, including tissue sampling and targeted drug delivery\.These technologies remain at the preclinical stage, and their potential clinical applicability requires further investigation\.

## [Dose\-dependent cardiac autonomic dysregulation under classroom crowding: heart rate variability analysis and machine learning classification](../publications/5f5b2361598436ad1b58.md)

Mohamed Naeem

Abstract Classroom overcrowding affects hundreds of millions of students globally, yet its physiological impact on cardiac autonomic function remains uncharacterized\. This controlled within\-subjects experiment enrolled 30 healthy university students who attended standardized 30\-min lectures under three calibrated density conditions: low \(30 students/150 m 2 \), medium \(60/150 m 2 \), and high \(100/150 m 2 \), with all environmental parameters held constant\. Twenty\-five heart rate variability \(HRV\) parameters spanning time\-domain, frequency\-domain, and nonlinear domains were extracted from continuous electrocardiogram \(ECG\) recordings\. Subjective workload was assessed via the NASA Task Load Index \(NASA\-TLX\), and RoBoSS\-SVM \(a Support Vector Machine using the Robust, Bounded, Sparse, and Smooth loss function\) with Recursive Feature Elimination \(RFE\) classified density conditions from HRV features\. Repeated\-measures ANOVA revealed significant density effects on all 25 HRV parameters \(all p &lt; 0\.001\), with 64% demonstrating exceptionally large effect sizes \( η 2 p ≥ 0\.50\)\. Parasympathetic markers showed the largest responses: pNN50 declined 52% \( η 2 p = 0\.702\), HF power declined 51% \( η 2 p = 0\.654\), and RMSSD declined 32% \( η 2 p = 0\.420\) from low to high density—while sympathetically influenced indices showed substantially smaller effects, confirming parasympathetic withdrawal as the predominant autonomic mechanism\. These suppression magnitudes approach levels associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes\. NASA\-TLX scores increased 74% across conditions \( p &lt; 0\.001\) and correlated with HRV vagal indices \( r = −0\.69 to −0\.76\), providing corroborating, though not definitive, evidence that crowding engages both subjective and autonomic stress pathways \(see Discussion for caveats regarding this association\)\. Temporal analysis confirmed progressive autonomic suppression without habituation across 10\-min windows\. RoBoSS\-SVM achieved 92\.2% accuracy for three\-class discrimination and 97\.2% accuracy \(AUC = 0\.993\) for binary classification, with parasympathetic time\-domain features comprising 64% of the optimal feature set\. Classroom spatial density produces dose\-dependent, mechanism\-specific cardiac autonomic dysregulation dominated by vagal withdrawal—consistent with polyvagal theory’s prediction for social\-environmental stressors\. The excellent classification performance supports feasibility of real\-time wearable monitoring for evidence\-based classroom capacity management\.

## [Severe capillary leak syndrome caused by postnatal cytomegalovirus infection in a very preterm infant: a case report](../publications/5f5d0eeacf8485e5f505.md)

Junchen Fang; Xin Chen; Tingting Li; Liyuan Cao; Li Ma

Postnatal cytomegalovirus \(pCMV\) infection in very preterm infants may lead to severe adverse outcomes; however, capillary leak syndrome as a complication of CMV infection has rarely been reported in this population\. This article reports a case of severe capillary leak syndrome \(CLS\) in a very preterm infant following postnatal CMV infection\. Despite conventional treatments, including antiviral therapy, fluid management, and cardiopulmonary support, the infant&\#x27;s condition progressively worsened, with signs of progressive fluid overload and acute kidney injury \(AKI\)\. Following the initiation of continuous renal replacement therapy \(CRRT\), the infant&\#x27;s clinical status improved, leading to eventual cure and discharge\. This case highlights severe CLS can be a major manifestation of pCMV infection in very preterm infants\. In addition to traditional therapy, CRRT can serve as an effective treatment option\.

## [Electron‐Deficient Destabilization Coupled With Mg‐philic Catalysis: A Dual‐Modulation Strategy for Low‐Temperature Dehydrogenation of Mg\(BH 4 \) 2](../publications/5f6b2beab7bae1449c46.md)

Chaojie Liu; Ziyang Li; Yongyang Zhu; Xiaoye Zhou; Zhongliang Ma; Yachun Lei; Mingrui Wan; Xinyan Zhang; Shun Wang

ABSTRACT Mg\(BH 4 \) 2 stands out as a promising high‐capacity hydrogen storage material, yet its application is hindered by sluggish dehydrogenation kinetics and high operation temperatures\. To break the bottleneck, we propose a novel coupling strategy of electron‐deficient destabilization and Mg‐philic catalysis\. Specifically, an electron‐deficient boron‐doped graphene host is fabricated to induce charge redistribution and structural destabilization of Mg\(BH 4 \) 2 and thereby weaken B─H bonds\. Meanwhile, Nb‐based catalysts with moderate Mg affinity are incorporated to drive the full dehydrogenation of Mg\(BH 4 \) 2 , during which multifunctional Nb‐based active sites are in situ evolved that facilitate B─H bond cleavage, hydrogen diffusion and Mg nucleation\. Benefiting from such coupling effect, the optimized nanocomposite features record‑low temperatures for two‐step dehydrogenation from Mg\(BH 4 \) 2 via MgH 2 to Mg, initiating at 50°C and peaking at 81/144°C, with substantially reduced dehydrogenation activation energy of 38\.74/58\.86 kJ mol −1 \. Moreover, the stable Nb‐based Mg‐philic sites enable the durable catalysis for the reversible conversion of MgH 2 /Mg and suppress the accumulation of MgB 12 H 12 intermediate byproducts, enhancing the cyclic stability\. This work offers instructive insights into the performance modulation of Mg\(BH 4 \) 2 and other complex metal hydrides for advanced hydrogen storage\.

## [An Adaptive Explainable AI Framework for Reliable Decision\-making in Real\-world Environments](../publications/5f7d8bf76bb224ffdf91.md)

Gajanan Ankatwar

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) systems increasingly support decisions in environments where data distributions, operational conditions, user needs, and risk levels change over time\. Models that perform well during development may become unreliable after deployment because of data drift, concept drift, sensor degradation, population changes, or unexpected interactions\. At the same time, predictive performance alone is insufficient for high\-impact decisions: users need explanations that are understandable, relevant to the decision context, and accompanied by appropriate uncertainty information\. This paper proposes an Adaptive Explainable AI \(A\-XAI\) framework intended to integrate reliability monitoring, explanation generation, uncertainty estimation, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation within a unified lifecycle\. The framework contains nine conceptual components: contextual data acquisition; data\-quality, privacy, and drift assessment; prediction with uncertainty estimation; context\-sensitive explanation generation; decision support and human oversight; risk\-aware reliability gating; feedback and audit logging; controlled adaptation; and post\-adaptation revalidation with version control\. A formal decision policy is presented to connect predictive confidence, drift evidence, explanation quality, and consequence severity to actions such as automated recommendation, human review, abstention, or retraining\. The paper also proposes an evaluation protocol spanning predictive performance, calibration, robustness, explanation fidelity and stability, fairness, latency, and operational outcomes\. As a conceptual contribution, the framework is not presented as experimentally validated; its effectiveness must be tested in domain\-specific studies using real deployment data and preregistered evaluation criteria\. The proposed design offers a structured basis for developing AI systems that remain interpretable and risk\-aware as real\-world conditions evolve\.

## [Machine learning modeling and interpretation of saline soil thermal conductivity](../publications/5f7fcaa8707b2eae3001.md)

Mahdi Abbasi

Soil thermal conductivity is a key parameter in geothermal design, buried infrastructure, frozen\-ground engineering, agricultural heat\-transfer assessment, and subsurface energy systems\. This study developed an interpretable multi\-model machine\-learning framework for predicting soil thermal conductivity from 903 literature\-derived observations and 15 predictors describing temperature, texture, bulk density, volumetric water content, salt concentration, salt molar mass, and ionic identity\. Eleven regression algorithms were optimized by five\-fold cross\-validation within a common 90% development subset and compared on an untouched 10% random hold\-out\. Extra Trees yielded the lowest observed random\-holdout error \(R² = 0\.9816, RMSE = 0\.0625 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, MAE = 0\.0446 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, AARE = 3\.93%, and A20 = 98\.90%\), with CatBoost and XGBoost providing similarly high point performance\. Because the database was assembled from 20 independent literature sources, source\-aware validation was added\. Pooled leave\-one\-study\-out prediction decreased to R² = 0\.2367 and RMSE = 0\.3983 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹\. A stricter retrospective external source validation was then performed by withholding all 100 observations from the two 2024 sources before any refitting or tuning and developing Extra Trees only on the remaining 803 observations from 18 earlier sources\. The resulting external\-source performance was R² = −3\.3720, RMSE = 0\.5855 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, MAE = 0\.5438 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, AARE = 51\.14%, and A20 = 12\.00%, demonstrating substantial between\-study domain shift\. Feature ablation showed that a physical\-only Extra Trees model achieved test R² = 0\.9551; adding salt concentration increased R² to 0\.9679, adding salt molar mass increased it to 0\.9813, and the full chemistry representation reached R² = 0\.9816\. The results therefore support high\-accuracy interpolation within represented experimental domains but do not support universal transfer to unseen studies\. Source\-specific or local validation is required before engineering deployment\.

## [Effect of discharge planning rooted in the integrated Care for Older People Concept on the maintenance of intrinsic capacity in older adults](../publications/5f82b9140459fcc43722.md)

Danni Zheng; Ren Xu; Shuhong Cai; Danfeng Pang; Xuemin Zhang; Yunxuan Zhu; 赵敏

Objective To assess how integrated care for older people \(ICOPE\)\-based discharge planning \(DP\) affects older patients’ intrinsic capacity \(IC\)\. Methods Between December 2023 and June 2024, 112 geriatric inpatients were randomly assigned to control \(routine care\) or Experimental \(routine care \+ ICOPE discharge services\) groups\. Intrinsic capacity domains were evaluated using the Short Physical Performance Battery, Saint Louis University Mental Status, Geriatric Depression Scale\-Short Form and Mini Nutritional Assessment\-Short Form tools and self\-report at discharge and 3 months post\-discharge\. Analysis of covariance and binary logistic regression were used, with baseline scores, living status and gender as covariates\. The primary analysis was supplemented by a sensitivity analysis using continuous domain scores as separate outcomes to verify the robustness of the composite score findings\. Results 108 patients completed follow\-up\. Intrinsic capacity decline was lower in the experimental group \(1\.2 ± 0\.2\) than in the control group \(3\.1 ± 0\.3; mean difference: –1\.9, 95% CI: −2\.5 to −1\.3, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Motor, cognitive, psychological and nutritional domains improved more in the Experimental group \(all p &lt; 0\.001\); sensory function showed no difference \( p = 0\.267\)\. Conclusion The ICOPE\-based DP approach slows IC decline and enhances multiple functional domains, offering a valuable reference for transitional care for older adults\.

## [Association mapping and molecular marker development for cassava brown streak disease resistance](../publications/5f8a53cac06874191f56.md)

Camilo E\. Sánchez‐Sarria; Samar Sheat; Stephan Winter; Edward Kanju; Xiaofei Zhang; Nelsón Morante; Carmen A\. Bolaños; Luz A\. Gómez\-Martínez; Adriana Bohórquez\-Chaux; Edda Mushi; Emmanuel Justine Mrema; Kasele Salum; Ting Yang; Tong Wei; Jonathan Newby; Winnie Gimode

Introduction Cassava brown streak disease \(CBSD\) – caused by Cassava brown streak virus \(CBSV\) and Ugandan cassava brown streak virus \(UCBSV\) – severely threatens cassava production and food security in sub\-Saharan Africa\. Breeding for resistance is the most sustainable control strategy, but it requires reliable resistance sources and a clear understanding of the underlying genetic mechanisms\. Methods In this study, we utilized resistance introduced from Latin American cassava germplasm and mapped the genetic basis of CBSD resistance relevant to African environments\. Whole\-genome sequencing \(WGS\) was applied to a segregating population consisting of 426 F1 progeny derived from crosses with CBSD\-resistant lines and genome\-wide association studies \(GWAS\) conducted to dissect the genetic basis of resistance\. Results and discussion A major QTL on chromosome 11 was consistently and significantly associated with CBSD resistance across multiple GWAS models tested and marker types \(SNPs and indels\), explaining up to 34\.89% of the phenotypic variation\. Three Kompetitive Allele Specific PCR \(KASP\) markers were developed and validated from the associated SNPs\. All three markers successfully differentiated between known resistant and susceptible parental lines and the mapping population, and one remained significantly associated with resistance in a broader validation population\. Interestingly, the same resistance region was previously reported in genetic mapping of East African germplasm, highlighting the central role of this locus across diverse genetic backgrounds\. Developing these markers targeting the major chromosome 11 QTL provides a practical molecular tool to accelerate marker\-assisted selection and facilitate the development of resistant cassava varieties, ultimately enhancing food security and supporting farmer livelihoods in regions affected by CBSD in Africa\.

## [Building Students’ Self\-Efficacy Through Cross\-Age Mentorship Focused on Stem Growth Mindset: A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Study](../publications/5fb1310dc481098ae923.md)

Heidi J Reid

The purpose of this phenomenological study was to understand the self\-efficacious experiences through a cross\-age mentorship program between sixth\-grade and Kindergarten students for parents at Seven Maples Elementary School in the Southeastern United States\. The theory guiding this study is Albert Bandura’s self\-efficacy theory, which describes how building confidence influences a person’s self\-efficacy\. This study employed a hermeneutic phenomenological methodology and gathered data through interviews, physical artifacts, and focus groups with parents whose students participated in the Kindergarten Buddy Program, a cross\-age mentor program between sixth\-grade and kindergarten students\. The interviews, physical artifacts, and focus group responses were recorded and transcribed for data analysis following van Manen’s design, in which transcripts were coded and compiled into themes by identifying recurring patterns within code clusters\. Four central themes emerged across the three forms of data analysis: confidence, relationships, leadership, and ownership\. The findings of this study emphasized that providing students with opportunities to build cross\-age mentor relationships helped them develop stronger self\-efficacy by strengthening confidence and a growth mindset, and by fostering a sense of connection and belonging\. Parents saw their children carry this higher self\-efficacy confidence from the academic setting within the school community out into their daily lives\.

## [From local markets to global economies: business approaches to economic development](../publications/5fb29b144ddc4841855d.md)

Pradeep Kumar

This research paper examines how businesses expand from domestic markets into global economies and how internationalisation contributes to both corporate growth and regional economic development\. Through a comparative analysis of Walmart, Tata Motors, and Volkswagen, the study explores how firms transform local market knowledge into international business strategy and how cultural intelligence, consumer understanding, and adaptive business models influence global performance\. The paper addresses a key issue in international business and development studies: why some companies succeed internationally while others struggle despite strong operational capabilities and established domestic market positions\. Particular attention is given to the relationship among international trade, foreign direct investment, and sustainable competitive advantage within rapidly changing global markets\.The research adopts a qualitative comparative case study methodology grounded in international business and development economics\. Drawing on the Ownership–Location–Internalisation \(OLI\) paradigm, cultural dimensions theory, and competitive advantage frameworks, the study analyses secondary data from academic literature, corporate reports, policy publications, and industry sources\. Each case illustrates a different dimension of global expansion and developmental impact\. Walmart’s experience in Germany demonstrates the risks of excessive standardisation and the failure of imposing a domestic retail model on culturally distinct markets without adequate localisation\. The Tata Nano project highlights both the opportunities and limitations of grassroots innovation designed for underserved populations, revealing that affordability alone cannot guarantee commercial success without aspirational consumer value\. Volkswagen’s development reflects the transition from strong national branding and engineering leadership to growing pressure from technological disruption and emerging\-market competition\.The findings indicate that operational efficiency and scale alone do not ensure successful internationalisation\. Sustainable global competitiveness depends on cultural adaptation, institutional responsiveness, strategic flexibility, and innovation\-driven business models aligned with local consumer realities\. The study contributes to international business and development literature by linking globalisation strategies with socio\-economic and cultural dynamics through evidence\-based comparative analysis\. Using Economic Development, Trade, Business Strategy, Sustainable Growth, Evidence, and Emerging Markets as analytical anchors, the paper provides practical insights for managers, policymakers, and development practitioners seeking resilient and adaptive strategies for international growth\.

## [An ensemble of regional CMIP3/CMIP5 wind wave scenarios for the North Sea and the Baltic Sea: a revisit](../publications/5fb3e373cdeef170aeda.md)

Nikolaus Groll; Iris Grabemann

Abstract\. Storms and associated marine hazards pose a environmental risks, particularly under long\-term changes driven by anthropogenic climate change\. This study assesses the potential impacts of future climate change on annual median and extreme wave conditions in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea using a ensemble of up to 14 and 8 regional projections, respectively\. The ensemble includes simulations based on IPCC CMIP3 and CMIP5 scenarios, incorporating a range of global and regional climate models, initial conditions, and emission scenarios to reflect diverse sources of uncertainty\. High\- and low\-emission sub\-ensembles were used to evaluate the influence of emission scenarios on projected wave climate changes towards the end of the 21st century\. Despite variations in magnitude and spatial patterns across the ensemble, some robust spatial and temporal trends emerge\. A meridional gradient of changes is simulated in the North Sea\. Significant wave heights decrease along the western margins and increase in the east\. These changes are more pronounced under high\-emission scenarios, with median values decreasing by up to 5 % in the west and annual maxima increasing by over 5 % in the east\. Time series analysis confirms these trends at selected locations, although there is still considerable internal variability among ensemble members\. In the Baltic Sea, both median and extreme wave heights are simulated to increase by more than 5 % in some areas\. Although the response to emission scenarios is less distinct than in the North Sea, high\-emission scenarios still yield more pronounced increases\. Temporal analysis reveals that simulated changes become statistically significant by mid\-century in central areas and later in western regions\. The results indicate a robust increase in wave height in the eastern North Sea and many regions of the Baltic Sea, as well as a consistent decrease in the western North Sea, particularly under high\-emission scenarios\. However, these trends are superimposed on substantial temporal and internal variability, highlighting the importance of using ensemble\-based assessments to evaluate future marine climate conditions\.

## [The role of cuproptosis in periodontitis: Current advances and future perspectives](../publications/5fb5283555ae3a259e85.md)

Qiqi Shi; Xu Qin; Chenxi Jiang; Guangxun Zhu

Periodontitis is a prevalent chronic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive destruction of the periodontal supporting tissues\. Copper homeostasis maintains intracellular copper balance through sophisticated regulatory networks, and its dysregulation may promote cuproptosis, a form of regulated cell death driven by excessive intracellular copper accumulation\. Emerging evidence indicates that cuproptosis contributes to periodontitis by impairing macrophage mitophagy, blocking autophagic flux, and modulating immune responses\. In addition, cuproptosis\-related genes \(CRGs\) regulate immune cell infiltration and inflammatory mediator production, and their expression levels are closely associated with periodontal pathogens\. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying copper homeostasis and cuproptosis and discusses their roles in the pathogenesis and progression of periodontitis, highlighting potential therapeutic targets and future research directions\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and China’s Cross\-Border E\-Commerce Development: Threshold Effects and Transmission Mechanisms](../publications/5fc18ed05ae1f96ab248.md)

Meina Zhao; Lu Zhou

The integration of artificial intelligence and search technology is transforming traditional online shopping models, particularly cross\-border e\-commerce \(CBEC\), which involves complex customer multi\-attribute decision\-making with numerous considerations\. This study systematically examines the influence of artificial intelligence on the high\-quality advancement of CBEC and its underlying mechanisms using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces covering the period 2013–2023\. The study found a significant positive correlation between artificial intelligence and cross\-border e\-commerce\. This conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness tests \(including removing the interference of pandemic\-related data, substituting core explanatory variables, substituting the dependent variable, and lagging explanatory variables by one period\)\. Mechanism analysis indicates that the positive impact of AI on the high\-quality development of cross\-border e\-commerce is realized through improvements in logistics capabilities and the unlocking of consumer potential, with mediation effects accounting for 40\.27% and 17\.02%, respectively\. Threshold model results show that the positive impact of AI on the high\-quality development of cross\-border e\-commerce exhibits a single threshold effect based on the level of human capital; once human capital exceeds the threshold value, the coefficient further increases\. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that AI has the most significant empowering effect on the development of cross\-border e\-commerce in the eastern regions; however, its impact on the central and western regions is relatively minor\. It is worth noting that AI exerts its empowering effect more effectively in regions with high e\-commerce procurement activity, whereas the relationship is not significant in regions with low activity\.

## [Integrated Modeling, Simulation, and Experimental Optimization of Vibratory Coffee Sorting Performance Using Response Surface Methodology](../publications/5fc8d94b887c1eb12fb8.md)

Engelbert Harsandi Erik Suryadarma; Chandra Dewi Kurnianingtyas; Rosalia Kartika Dewi

This study presents an integrated theoretical, simulation, and experimental approach to optimize the performance of a vibratory coffee sorting machine using Response Surface Methodology \(RSM\)\. A physics\-based model of granular flow and segregation was developed to quantify the influence of inclination angle \(α\) and vibration frequency \(f\), and numerical simulations using MATLAB and DEM confirmed nonlinear interactions between both parameters, predicting optimal performance at α = 28\.5° and f = 47\.5 Hz with a throughput of 3541\.3 g/min and sorting accuracy of 98\.14%\. Empirical validation through a Central Composite Design \(CCD\) demonstrated significant effects of α and f on system responses \(p &lt; 0\.001\) and produced highly accurate regression models \(R² = 98\.32% for throughput and R² = 92\.52% for accuracy\)\. Multi\-response desirability optimization yielded an empirical optimum at α = 29\.8° and f = 50 Hz, achieving a throughput of 3667\.44 g/min and an accuracy of 98\.32%, closely aligning with simulation predictions\. The results confirm the robustness of the integrated modeling framework, highlight the inherent trade\-off between throughput and segregation efficiency, and provide a practical guideline for improving productivity and quality in vibratory coffee sorting operations\.

## [Generative AI adoption and innovative behavior among Gen Z students: a deep\-learning based dual\-stage PLS\-SEM\-ANN analysis](../publications/5fd6a11c3a322b31c69f.md)

Jiale Zhang; Jiale Zhang; Farzana Quoquab; Zihan Xu; Jiaqi Zhang; Jiaqi Zhang; Jihad Mohammad; Botao Yan

This study explores the impact of generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) adoption on the innovative behavior of Generation Z students in higher education\. Anchored in the UTAUT and Social Cognitive Theory, a conceptual model was developed to examine the determinants of GAI adoption and its subsequent effect on students’ innovative behavior\. Data were gathered through an online survey in China, yielding 291 valid responses, and analyzed using PLS\-SEM and Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\) approaches\. The PLS\-SEM results affirmed that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions positively influence GAI adoption, with actual GAI use significantly enhancing students’ innovative behavior\. Furthermore, knowledge sharing and creative self\-efficacy were identified as positive drivers of innovative behavior, mediating the relationship between GAI use and innovative behavior, thus enriching the understanding of these mediators in educational settings\. Complementing these findings, the ANN analysis underscored the pivotal role of creative self\-efficacy in fostering innovation\. This study advances the burgeoning literature on GAI in education by highlighting its capacity to cultivate innovative behavior among students and offering actionable insights for its effective integration into learning environments\.

## [FORENSIC TRACES IN GAN\-GENERATED FACE IMAGES: FORMATION MECHANISMS, EVOLUTION, AND FORENSIC INTERPRETATION](../publications/5fd9b3bc7442610e6c9b.md)

Yi Wang

Generative adversarial networks \(GANs\) can synthesize highly realistic fictional faces, creating new challenges for digital image authentication and source attribution\. Forensic examination requires more than a binary real\-or\-fake decision: relevant traces should be reproducible, mechanistically interpretable, and evaluated under clearly defined conditions\. This structured narrative review updates the literature through October 2026 and groups forensic traces in GAN\-generated face images into three mechanism\-based categories: differences between physical camera imaging and neural synthesis pipelines; traces introduced by generator architecture; and anomalies in physiological, geometric, and physical consistency\. The review focuses on color and noise statistics, texture, upsampling and spatial\-frequency structure, generator fingerprints, StyleGAN\-specific artifacts, and ocular geometry, with particular attention to whether these traces persist as generator architectures evolve\. Evidence shows that StyleGAN&\#x27;s blob\-like and progressive\-growing\-related phase artifacts were specifically addressed in StyleGAN2, while texture sticking was substantially reduced by the alias\-free design of StyleGAN3\. High\-frequency spectral\-falloff discrepancies can also disappear after changes to the upsampling architecture and therefore are not intrinsic properties of CNN\-based generators\. Frequency\-domain, autocorrelation, and ocular geometric differences continue to be reported in newer models, but their expression depends on the generator, training data, image quality, and post\-processing history\. The forensic significance of these findings is discussed in terms of trace persistence, alternative explanations, processing history, and independent corroboration\. No single anomaly should be used in isolation to support a conclusion of AI generation or a specific source\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Related Sentiments and Perceptions on Federated Social Networks: A Computational Text Analysis](../publications/5fde3558a5e80ef53fe6.md)

Sadettin Demirel

This study aims to examine public perceptions of artificial intelligence \(AI\) on federated social networks, specifically Bluesky and Mastodon\. While existing research focuses on centralized platforms, a significant gap exists regarding AI perception within decentralized networks\. This study addresses this gap through computational analysis of AI related posts in Bluesky and Mastodon\. A text\-as\-data approach was employed to analyze 61,285 posts collected from Bluesky and Mastodon between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2025\. The methodology integrated topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and text analysis to identify prevalent themes, sentiment polarity, and discussion patterns within AI\-related discourse\. Findings demonstrate predominantly positive sentiment towards AI across both platforms, with trust, anticipation, and joy as primary emotional responses, accompanied by underlying fear and anxiety\. Platform\-specific variations emerged: Mastodon discourse centers on creativity, digital art, and societal\-ethical implications including regulation, bias, and disinformation concerns\. Conversely, Bluesky posts emphasize economic and geopolitical dimensions, featuring startups, funding, stock markets, and international policy\. The analysis reveals significant fragmentation in public AI perception, characterized by discourse division into distinct economic and ethical spheres across platforms\. While this fragmentation accommodates diverse social group perspectives, it presents challenges for establishing comprehensive societal consensus on AI governance\. The analytical framework provides insights for understanding decentralized social network dynamics and implications for policy makers examining AI perception in federated digital environments\.

## [РОЛЬ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЕКТА В НЕОТЛОЖНОЙ КАРДИОЛОГИИ](../publications/5febc4dcf59e5ffec39f.md)

Ашурова Махфуза Уктамовна

Актуальность: Кардиологические заболевания остаются одной из ведущих причин смертности во всем мире\. В условиях неотложной помощи быстрая и точная диагностика критически важна для спасения жизни пациентов и улучшения клинических исходов\. Искусственный интеллект, с его способностью анализировать огромные объемы данных и выявлять скрытые закономерности, предлагает уникальные возможности для повышения качества медицинской помощи в кардиологии\.

## [Evaluating Large Language Models’ Responses to Common Queries on Retinal Surgery: Readability and Accuracy Analysis](../publications/5feecf9dea6a64e0d1f9.md)

Erkan Duman; Aydın Maçin; Ayşe Ergin

BACKGROUND/AIMS: Large language models \(LLMs\) such as ChatGPT\-4o mini, ChatGPT\-4o, Gemini 1\.5 Pro and Microsoft Copilot play an important role in improving health literacy and supporting patient decision making\.This study aims to evaluate the clinical appropriateness and readability of responses provided by these LLMs to frequently asked questions about retinal detachment \(RD\), epiretinal membrane \(ERM\), and macular hole \(MH\)\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This comparative cross\-sectional study did not involve human participants\.A total of 121 questions related to RD, ERM and MH were compiled\.These questions were presented to LLM interfaces and were categorised into different themes\.Inter\-rater agreement between two retinal specialists who scored the responses based on their clinical expertise was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient \(ICC\)\.In addition, the readability of the responses was analysed using five readability indices\. RESULTS:Response appropriateness rates were similar for ChatGPT\-4o mini \(100%\), ChatGPT\-4o \(99\.2%\) and Gemini 1\.5 Pro \(99\.2%\), while Microsoft Copilot \(90\.9%\) showed comparatively lower performance\.A high level of inter\-rater agreement was observed among clinicians\.Regarding readability, ChatGPT\-4o performed best, whereas ChatGPT\-4o mini performed worst\.Gemini 1\.5 Pro and Microsoft Copilot were intermediate between these two models\.The excellent inter\-rater agreement \(ICC: 0\.891\-0\.938\)further supports the reliability of the expert evaluation process\.CONCLUSION: Our study showed that the evaluated LLMs provided largely appropriate and comprehensive answers to questions related to vitreoretinal surgery\.ChatGPT\-4o showed the highest performance in both appropriateness and readability, while ChatGPT\-4o mini, despite its high appropriateness, had the lowest readability score\.

## [Measuring Youth Mental Health Vulnerability Across Communities: Development and Validation of ThriveAtlas](../publications/5ff1f0b52a91e61ca28c.md)

Christina A\. Mehranbod; Domonique M Reed; Emily Yetton; Aaron Dibner\-Dunlap; Tomas Engelthaler; Peter Smittenaar; Hannah Kemp; Sema K\. Sgaier; Adele Wang

CONTEXT: Youth mental health is shaped by interacting individual, relational, and structural factors that vary across communities, yet few tools integrate these drivers into youth\-specific, geographically granular measures for decision\-making\. OBJECTIVE: This study describes the development and preliminary validation of ThriveAtlas, a geographically granular index designed to identify factors that prevent youth from thriving\. DESIGN: ThriveAtlas was developed through a multistep process including a targeted literature review; selection and construction of indicators from public and proprietary data sources; aggregation into thematic domains and a composite index; and preliminary validation using county\-level mental health outcomes\. SETTING: County\-level analysis using school\-based survey data from California \(California Healthy Kids Survey, 2021\-2023\)\. PARTICIPANTS: Ninth\-grade students across 53 California counties\. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: County\-level principal components derived from 5 self\-reported mental health indicators; prioritization overlap with the Social Vulnerability Index \(Jaccard statistic\); and univariate explanatory power \(R2\) of ThriveAtlas domains versus Social Vulnerability Index \(SVI\) domains\. RESULTS: The review identified key gaps in existing tools: youth\-focused indices often emphasize general well\-being rather than mental health, while structurally focused indices lack youth specificity or substate granularity\. ThriveAtlas revealed geographic variability in vulnerability, including regional clusters and isolated high\-risk counties\. Validation analyses showed expected patterns in California, where higher vulnerability aligned with greater distress and lower well\-being\. ThriveAtlas and SVI were correlated \(Spearman ρ = 0\.66\) across California counties; however, ThriveAtlas themes better explained county\-level mental health outcomes than SVI domains \(R2 = 0\.41 vs\. 0\.27\), and the 2 tools agreed on only one\-third of high\-priority counties \(Jaccard = 0\.33\)\. CONCLUSION: ThriveAtlas addresses a critical measurement gap by providing a youth\-centered, multidimensional, and geographically granular index of vulnerability\. Early validation supports its utility as a decision\-relevant signal to identify communities with elevated youth mental health challenges and inform targeted intervention strategies\.

## [Contribution of artificial intelligence research to the development of inclusive applications for people with disabilities: A scoping review \(2015–2025\)](../publications/5ff397bb1086a10ff761.md)

Soutongnoma Safiata Kaboré; Azadeh Bayani; Leandre Parfait Epoh Ewane; Davllyn Santos Oliveira dos Anjos; Jean Noel Nikiéma; Muriel Mac\-Seing

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is rapidly transforming healthcare\. Yet people with disabilities \(PWD\), representing 16% of the global population, remain disproportionately excluded from these advances\. This exclusion is driven by algorithmic bias, non\-representative datasets, and limited involvement of PWD in the design, development, and evaluation of AI applications\. This scoping review examines the extent to which AI research in health contributes to the development of inclusive technologies for PWD, focusing on equity considerations\. It identifies current trends, methodological gaps, and opportunities for socially responsive innovation\. We conducted a systematic search across MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL for the 2015\-2025 period, following Arksey and O&\#x27;Malley&\#x27;s five\-stage scoping review methodology and the PRISMA\-ScR guidelines\. Data were extracted and synthesized thematically using the Population\-Concept\-Context approach\. Of 4,233 references retrieved, 93 studies were included\. Most studies originated from high\-income countries, particularly in North America \(45\.2%\) and Europe \(26\.9%\)\. AI applications addressed motor, sensory, cognitive, communication\-related, and psychosocial disabilities, with emphasis on prediction/diagnosis, assistive technologies, and personalized care\. While about 60% of studies referenced equity, only 12 \(12\.9%\) implemented concrete measures \(e\.g\., adapting tools for vulnerable groups or ensuring sample diversity\), and only six \(6\.5%\) actively involved PWD through co\-design or user validation\. AI holds significant potential to enhance autonomy, access, and quality of life for PWD\. Realizing this promise will require moving beyond technical optimization to embrace inclusive design, participatory methods, and equity\-driven frameworks aligned with responsible AI development and use\.

## [From pragmatic inference to grammatical structure: A critical review of grammaticalization at the grammar–pragmatics interface in English](../publications/5fffe49f27c3dc8aece0.md)

Azhar Wazir Thealib Al\-Mayali

The relation between pragmatic meaning and grammatical structure has been a major topic of research in linguistics, especially in the study of language change and grammaticalization\. This paper traces the development of contextual meanings and discourse\-based inferences into conventional grammatical structures in English\. In this paper, we study the mechanisms of structural constraints on pragmatic interpretation in the functional, cognitive and generative approaches, such as the semantic\-pragmatic abstraction, subjectification, frequency\-driven change, and syntactic reanalysis\. The review critically assesses previous historical studies and discusses three major areas of English grammatical development: the development of modal auxiliaries, the grammaticalization of connectives and subordinating structures, and the transition from flexible word order patterns to the more fixed Subject–verb–object \(SVO\) order of modern English\. The analysis shows that grammatical change cannot be explained in terms of one theoretical perspective but it is the result of the interaction of communicative practices, of cognitive processes and of structural reorganization\. The review also identifies current gaps in the literature, in particular the divide between corpus\-based historical studies and theoretical treatments of syntactic change, and the neglect of contemporary digital discourse and sociolinguistic variation\. The paper shows an integrated view of how contextual meanings become grammatical patterns in English\. Grammar and pragmatics are seen as steps in the paper, connected by the ongoing process of language change\.

## [Beyond the Answer: Student\-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation](../publications/6007296cb5a2b6d7bd82.md)

Shaoang Li; Yanhang Shi; Yufei Li; Mingfu Liang; Frank Shyu; Sandeep Pandey; Luke Simon; Xi Liu; Jian Li

A reasoning trace can accompany a correct answer without providing effective supervision for a particular student\. We study how to construct traces that improve learning beyond answer\-only supervision by considering both their intermediate content and their accessibility to the target learner\. We introduce ReDiST, a student\-conditioned trace\-construction and distillation framework for evidence\-rich reasoning\. Starting from the student&\#x27;s own attempts, ReDiST revises answer\-correct drafts against the supplied evidence and repairs unsuccessful drafts with additional guidance from the verified answer\. A frozen student\-matched reader screens and ranks original and edited candidates using answer recovery and verified\-answer probability, given the question, evidence, and candidate trace\. We distill the selected targets while balancing trace and final\-answer supervision with an auxiliary answer loss\. Construction and selection occur offline, and inference uses only the distilled student\. Experiments on question\-answering benchmarks show that ReDiST can improve both source\-task and cross\-benchmark performance over answer\-only, original\-trace, and the evaluated trace\-selection and rewriting baselines\. Across supervision recipes, performance rankings can differ between source and transfer benchmarks, highlighting the importance of evaluating trace teaching utility across distributions\.

## [Bimetallic Coinage Metal Complexes of Tetradentate ortho ‐Ter‐arylene Ligands](../publications/600b12f726a27160ed4b.md)

Darius Allen Shariaty; Thabassum A\. Nattikallungal; Yi\-Jyun Lien; Peter I\. Djurovich; Stephen E\. Bradforth; Mark E\. Thompson

ABSTRACT We report a series of photoluminescent bimetallic Cu\(I\), Ag\(I\), and Au\(I\) complexes supported by tetradentate donor‐acceptor ligands containing two monoanionic amide donors \(D\) and two aza‐arene acceptors \(A\)\. The metal complexes of the ligand containing carbazolide and pyridyl ligating groups possess high photoluminescence quantum yields \(up to 65% in solution\) and emission properties consistent with thermally‐activated delayed fluorescence \(TADF\)\. Bimetallic Cu\(I\) complexes of similar ligands containing benzannulated donor \(benzo\[a\]carbazolide\) or acceptor \(isoquinoline\) moieties demonstrate that absorption/emission properties are tunable by modification of D/A groups\. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction of the bimetallic complexes reveals metal–metal distances shorter than the sum of their van der Waals radii, suggesting metallophilic interactions between the d 10 metal centers\. Ultrafast excited‐state kinetic analysis reveals nearly equal exergonic intersystem crossing rates between Cu\(I\) and Au\(I\) complexes, contrary to what is expected from each metal&\#x27;s spin–orbit coupling contributions\. These findings are corroborated with theoretical modeling, which suggests that the optical transitions of these bimetallic complexes are characterized as metal–ligand‐to‐ligand charge transfer \(MLLCT\) states\.

## [Afetler Türkiye’nin Uluslararası Ticareti Üzerinde Etkili Olmuş Mudur? 2015Ç1\-2025Ç2 Dönemi için Ampirik İnceleme](../publications/6022b78aa3c2a15db71b.md)

Hakkı Özbaş

Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de 2015Ç1\-2025Ç2 döneminde yaşanan büyük ölçekli afetlerin, özellikle COVID\-19 pandemisi ile 6 Şubat 2023 Kahramanmaraş depremlerinin uluslararası ticaret üzerindeki etkilerini incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırmada Türkiye’nin çeyrek dönemlik ithalat ve ihracat verileri kullanılmış, afetlerin dış ticaret üzerindeki etkileri yapısal kırılma analizleri aracılığıyla test edilmiştir\. Bu kapsamda öncelikle Perron \(1989\) ve Lee\-Strazicich \(2003\) yapısal kırılmalı birim kök testleri, ardından Bai\-Perron \(2003\) çoklu yapısal kırılma testi uygulanmıştır\. Elde edilen bulgular, COVID\-19 pandemisinin dış ticaret üzerinde belirgin etkiler yarattığını göstermektedir\. İhracat ve ithalat serilerinde 2020 yılının ikinci çeyreğinde anlamlı yapısal kırılmalar tespit edilmiştir\. Bu durum, pandeminin ticaret hacmini kısa vadede olumsuz etkilediğini, sonraki dönemlerde ise belirgin bir toparlanma yaşandığını ortaya koymaktadır\. Bai\-Perron \(2003\) test sonuçları, ihracatta biri 2020 yılının ikinci çeyreğinde olmak üzere iki dönemde, ithalatta ise yine biri 2020 yılının ikinci çeyreğinde olmak üzere dört dönemde rejim değişikliği meydana geldiğini ve 2020Ç2’nin her iki seri için ortak kırılma dönemi olduğunu göstermiştir\. Buna karşılık, 6 Şubat 2023 depremleri sonrasında ithalat ve ihracat serilerinde anlamlı bir yapısal kırılma tespit edilmemiştir\. Sonuçlar, pandeminin dış ticaret üzerinde daha belirgin etkiler yarattığını, deprem etkisinin ise toplam dış ticaret verilerinde daha sınırlı göründüğünü ortaya koymaktadır\.Çalışmada öncelikle Perron \(1989\) ve Lee\-Strazicich \(2003\) birim kök testleri, ardından Bai\-Perron \(1998\) çoklu yapısal kırılma testi uygulanmıştır\. Elde edilen bulgular, COVID\-19 pandemisinin dış ticaret üzerinde belirgin etkiler yarattığını göstermektedir\. İhracat ve ithalat serisinde 2020 yılının ikinci çeyreğinde anlamlı yapısal kırılmalar tespit edilmiştir\. Bu durum, pandeminin ticaret hacmini kısa vadede olumsuz etkilediğini, ancak sonraki dönemlerde hızlı bir toparlanma yaşandığını ortaya koymaktadır\.Bai\-Perron \(1998\) test sonuçları, ihracatta birisi 2020 yılının ikinci çeyreği olmak üzere 2 dönemde; ithalatta ise birisi 2020Q yılının ikinci çeyreği olmak üzere 4 dönemde rejim değişikliğinin meydana geldiğini göstermiştir\. Buna karşın 6 Şubat 2023 depremleri sonrasında ithalat ve ihracat serilerinde anlamlı bir yapısal kırılma tespit edilmemiştir\. Sonuç olarak, Türkiye örneğinde pandeminin dış ticaret üzerinde rejim değişiklikleri yarattığı, buna karşın depremlerin kısa vadede sınırlı etkiler oluşturduğu görülmüştür\.

## [Predicting Customer Frustration Before Formal Complaint: A Deep Learning Approach for Proactive Customer Service](../publications/6022c887beb2f78cc4c2.md)

Jasmine Kaushal

This study explores the application of machine\-learning and deep\-learning techniques to customer sentiment analysis as a potential foundation for proactive customer service\. Using the Twitter US Airline Sentiment dataset, the study compares Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), Bidirectional LSTM \(BiLSTM\), and Gated Recurrent Unit \(GRU\) models for classifying customer messages as positive, neutral, or negative\. The research examines model performance using classification metrics and discusses the challenges associated with interpreting customer sentiment, including sarcasm, contextual ambiguity, and limitations in individual\-message analysis\. The study also explores the potential role of automated sentiment analysis in proactive customer\-service systems and identifies sequential customer\-interaction data as an important direction for future research into early complaint prediction\.

## [Artificiell intelligens i redovisningsprocesser: En kvalitativ studie av implementering och dess påverkan på anställda](../publications/60239ad8fe1eadfbb40d.md)

Pontus Persson; Linus Svensk

Denna studie undersöker hur artificiell intelligens \(AI\) implementeras i redovisningsprocessen och hur implementeringen påverkar anställdas arbete och arbetsroller\. Bakgrunden är den snabba teknologiska utvecklingen där AI i allt större utsträckning används för att automatisera arbetsuppgifter, förbättra datakvalitet och stödja analys och beslutsfattande\. Trots den ökade användningen finns begränsad kunskap om hur implementeringen sker i praktiken och hur den upplevs av de anställda\. Studien genomfördes med en kvalitativ metod baserad på semistrukturerade intervjuer med personer verksamma inom redovisning och HR\. Materialet analyserades genom tematisk analys\. Resultaten visar att AI främst implementeras stegvis genom automatisering av repetitiva och regelbaserade arbetsuppgifter, ofta integrerat i befintliga system\. Implementeringen drivs huvudsakligen av behovet av effektivisering och varierar mellan olika organisationer\. Studien visar även att AI förändrar arbetsinnehållet genom att minska manuella arbetsuppgifter och skapa större fokus på analys, rådgivning och andra värdeskapande aktiviteter\. Samtidigt ökar kraven på teknisk förståelse och kritisk granskning\. Resultaten visar även att AI medför både möjligheter och utmaningar, men att mänsklig kompetens, erfarenhet och omdöme fortsatt är avgörande inom redovisningsarbetet\.

## [Friction properties of boundary film formed by polymer additives in wide\-area contacts with nanoscale gap](../publications/602f93004e6c88872d77.md)

Wataru Yagi; Toshiyuki Tsuchiya; Naoki Yamashita; Tomoko Hirayama

Polymer additives, originally used as viscosity index improvers, have attracted increasing attention as friction\-reducing lubricant additives because of their ability to adsorb onto surfaces through polar groups\. Although adsorbed polymer films are known to play an important role in friction under boundary lubrication conditions, how their interfacial properties change during sliding and how these changes affect tribological behavior remain unclear\. To elucidate the relationship between the interfacial behavior of polymer additives and friction characteristics, we investigated changes in the coefficient of friction and oil film thickness using lubricating oils containing polymethyl methacrylate \(PMA\)\. A custom\-built friction tester capable of applying unidirectional sliding over a contact area of approximately 1 mm 2 was used to evaluate PMA additives with different numbers of polar groups and molecular weights, with a base oil and an olefin copolymer \(OCP\) used for comparison\. The base oil and OCP\-containing oil exhibited a nearly constant dynamic coefficient of friction, whereas all PMA\-containing oils exhibited lower friction accompanied by stick\-slip behavior at low shear velocities\. No clear difference in the coefficient of friction was observed between PMA additives with different numbers of polar groups\. However, the oil film thickness of the PMA additive with fewer polar groups decreased with increasing load\. Although the coefficient of friction was nearly the same for high\- and low\-molecular\-weight PMAs, the oil film thickness of the high\-molecular\-weight PMA decreased after friction compared with that before friction\. These results suggest that the number of polar groups affects the stiffness of the adsorbed polymer film in the load direction, whereas molecular weight affects the oil film thickness\. For high\-molecular\-weight PMA, shear\-induced desorption or rearrangement of a weakly formed topmost layer may reduce the thickness of the remaining strongly adsorbed film\. These findings clarify the relationship between the interfacial behavior of polymer additives and friction characteristics and provide insights into the design of polymer additives for friction reduction\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Use in Honours Research: Implications for Supervision Relationships, Knowledge Development, and Research Quality](../publications/603d7f4a64d6649bf3b0.md)

Sympathy Luyanda Mncube

The increasing use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools in higher education has reshaped how students engage with academic research, particularly at Honours level, where students transition from structured undergraduate learning to independent postgraduate research\. Guided by Self‑Regulated Learning \(SRL\) theory, this study examines how reliance on AI by Honours research students influences the supervisor\-supervisee relationship, the quality of research produced, and the extent of knowledge gained through the research process\. SRL theory emphasises learners’ ability to plan, monitor, and reflect on their own learning, which is central to successful postgraduate research development\. This study adopts a conceptual and literature‑based review methodology, drawing on peer‑reviewed studies on AI use in higher education, literature on postgraduate supervision, and academic integrity and research skills development frameworks, with specific attention to Honours‑level contexts\. The documents were analysed using thematic content analysis, focusing on self‑regulatory behaviours, supervisory interaction, research skill development, and learning depth\. The findings suggest that limited and transparent use of AI can support honours students by reducing surface‑level cognitive load and assisting with language clarity\. However, excessive reliance on AI may undermine key self‑regulation processes, weaken critical thinking, and reduce meaningful engagement with supervisors\. Supervisors may struggle to accurately assess students’ understanding, potentially straining trust and feedback processes\. The review further indicates that over‑reliance on AI risks producing research that is technically adequate but conceptually shallow, with reduced long‑term knowledge acquisition\. The study concludes that clear supervision practices and explicit guidance on responsible AI use are necessary to ensure that AI supports, rather than replaces, the self‑regulated learning essential for high‑quality Honours‑level research\.

## [Conformal Policy Selection: When to Deploy AI Decisions for Targeted Intervention](../publications/60421548b7644a5fe734.md)

Junyu Cao; Ruijiang Gao; Maytal Saar\-Tsechansky; Mingzhang Yin

Artificial\-intelligence \(AI\) policies are increasingly used to make consequential decisions in medicine, finance, education, and public services, yet deploying them responsibly requires knowing not only whether a policy helps on average, but for whom\. Existing tools for off\-policy evaluation and safe policy learning provide population\-level guarantees, but some individuals may experience adverse treatment effects\. We recast targeted deployment as a multiple\-testing problem: for each candidate unit, test whether the outcome under the AI policy would exceed a user\-specified threshold, and control the false discovery rate \(FDR\) among the selected set\. Our method, Conformal Policy Selection, combines weighted conformal $p$\-values that account for the distributional shift from behavior to target policy with a two\-step selection\-and\-pruning procedure\. We prove finite\-sample FDR control and establish a doubly robust asymptotic guarantee, where FDR remains controlled if either the outcome model or the propensity model is correctly specified\. Synthetic experiments verify these guarantees across four misspecification regimes, and a semi\-synthetic study built on real electronic\-health\-record covariates illustrates how the same FDR control can act as a deployment safety gate, bounding the harmful treatments that a globally trained policy would otherwise administer to a high\-risk subpopulation where it misgeneralizes\. The framework offers a principled method for safe AI deployment in high\-stakes applications\.

## [Macrophage lipid metabolism and inflammasome activation in rheumatoid arthritis: emerging mechanisms and therapeutic implications](../publications/605085cbf3b6cfc8cd6a.md)

Hua Hao; Zhao Hongyu; Ping Dong; Xuanting Fan; Jun Liu; Hao Wu; Lifen Jia; Chen Li; Limei Ao; Qiumei Dong

Rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and bone erosion\. Within the multicellular RA synovial network, macrophages act as important inflammatory effectors and metabolic sensors whose functional states are shaped by lipid metabolic reprogramming\. In RA synovium, impaired cholesterol efflux and altered fatty acid flux remodel membrane lipid composition and lipid\-raft\-dependent Toll\-like receptor \(TLR\)–NF\-κB signaling, thereby enhancing the expression of NOD\-like receptor family pyrin domain\-containing 3 \(NLRP3\) and pro\-interleukin\-1β \(pro\-IL\-1β\)\. Cholesterol overload or crystallization, saturated fatty acid\-induced lipotoxicity, mitochondrial and lysosomal injury, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, ionic imbalance, and lipid peroxidation generate activation\-associated signals that lower the threshold for NLRP3 inflammasome activation\. Mechanistic studies, largely outside RA, suggest that fatty acid synthase \(FASN\)\-dependent production of palmitate\-derived acyl donors may support ZDHHC\-mediated NLRP3 palmitoylation, subcellular trafficking, NEK7 interaction, ASC recruitment, and inflammasome assembly\. Liver X receptor \(LXR\) and peroxisome proliferator\-activated receptor \(PPAR\) function as complementary lipid\-sensing regulators: LXR mainly controls cholesterol efflux and membrane signaling, whereas PPARs coordinate fatty acid handling, mitochondrial adaptation, efferocytosis, and resolution\-associated programs\. Activation of the NLRP3–caspase\-1 axis promotes IL\-1β and IL\-18 maturation and gasdermin D\-mediated pyroptosis, amplifying macrophage–fibroblast\-like synoviocyte crosstalk, immune\-cell recruitment, osteoclastogenesis, and structural joint damage\. Because direct validation of the complete FASN–palmitoylation–NLRP3 sequence in RA synovial macrophages remains limited, this axis is presented as a testable RA\-relevant mechanistic framework rather than an established RA\-specific pathway while highlighting potential targets for macrophage\-directed immunometabolic intervention\.

## [Complex\-valued orthogonal unitary superposition encoding\-based multi\-qubit system for quantum image transmission](../publications/605457acb935f40bbf8d.md)

Udara Thilini Darshika Jayasinghe Mudalige; Thanuj Fernando; Anil Fernando

Reliable high\-fidelity image transmission over noisy quantum channels remains a significant challenge, especially under bandwidth constraints, where the use of quantum error correction is often impractical due to its high computational and implementation complexity\. Existing encoding schemes, such as Hadamard\-based encoding, often exhibit limited noise resilience and low information capacity, reducing their effectiveness for compressed image transmission in high\-noise environments\. To address these issues, we propose a multi\-qubit quantum image transmission framework employing complex\-valued orthogonal unitary superposition \(COUS\) encoding based on the established phase–Hadamard–phase \(SHS\) unitary transformation, enabling joint amplitude and phase representation for improved robust ness against noise\. Input images are first compressed using JPEG or HEIF and channel\-encoded using polar codes before being mapped into multi\-qubit COUS states for transmission\. At the receiver, quantum states are sequentially COUS decoded, channel decoded, and source decoded to reconstruct the images\. The system is evaluated through simulations under noisy quantum channel conditions\. System performance is analyzed using peak signal\-to\-noise ratio \(PSNR\), structural similarity index mea sure \(SSIM\), and universal quality index \(UQI\)\. Simulation re sults demonstrate that COUS encoding consistently outperforms Hadamard\-based encoding, achieving up to 4 dB channel SNR gain even with a single\-qubit configuration, while higher\-qubit configurations further enhance robustness and image quality\. These results highlight COUS as a scalable, low\-complexity, and noise\-resilient approach for high\-fidelity quantum image transmission\.

## [Temperature dependence and consistency of dark current measurement methods for infrared focal plane arrays](../publications/6057632b5f3d9c022094.md)

Rongjie Feng; Jiaping Long; Xinjie Li; Yongyong Cao; Zilong Zeng; Zhenyi Deng; Zixin Liang; Yu Liu; Bo Li; Sanjie Liu

Dark current is a critical parameter for infrared focal plane detectors, while practical measurement methods may exhibit temperature\-dependent discrepancies\. This study systematically evaluates the consistency between the blind cold shield \(BCS\) and theoretical coefficient \(TC\) methods using paired measurements of 24 mid\-wave infrared detector chips at 120 K and 150 K, with 140 K measurements included as an intermediate experimental condition for descriptive analysis\. Relative deviation and Bland–Altman analyses were employed to quantify inter\-method consistency\. At 120 K, 70\.8% of chips showed TC dark\-current values more than 20% below the BCS baseline, compared with 29\.2% at 150 K\. The mean absolute relative deviation decreased from 74\.9% to 42\.1%, while the geometric mean TC/BCS ratio increased from approximately 0\.40–0\.92\. Bland–Altman analysis showed persistent absolute chip\-to\-chip variability, while the geometric mean TC/BCS ratio moved closer to unity at 150 K\. These results indicate improved relative BCS–TC consistency over 120 K–150 K while emphasizing that the applicable measurement range is detector and configuration dependent\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE GOVERNANCE READINESS AND RESPONSIBLE ADOPTION AMONG HEALTH ADMINISTRATION AND HEALTH INFORMATION PROFESSIONALS: A MULTICENTER CROSS\-SECTIONAL STUDY](../publications/6058e4d315326c7239c1.md)

Fawaz Mofareh N Gohal, Abdullah Ai thamari, Riyadh\.T\. AlRabeeah and Moudhi Hashim Alabdulrahman

Health systems are adopting artificial intelligence \(AI\) faster than many organizations are developing the policies, workforce capability, data controls, and monitoring processes needed to govern it safely\. Health administration and health information professionals are central to procurement, data stewardship, workflow design, quality oversight, and implementation, yet their readiness for responsible AI adoption remains underexamined\. To propose and test an analysis framework for assessing AI governance readiness and responsible adoption among health administration and health information/informatics professionals across multiple Saudi healthcare organizations\. A multicenter cross\-sectional survey design was specified for six coded healthcare institutions across three Saudi regions\. The proposed 31\-item instrument covers governance readiness, data and technical readiness, workforce AI capability, responsible AI climate, perceived value, and responsible adoption\. Because field data have not yet been collected, a synthetic dataset of 432 complete records was generated solely to test scoring, reliability, tables, figures, and regression procedures\. Analyses included frequencies, means with 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\), Cronbach alpha, group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and multivariable linear regression with center fixed effects and HC3 robust standard errors\. In the sample, 241 \(55\.8%\) records represented health administration professionals and 191 \(44\.2%\) represented health information/informatics professionals\. Proposed high governance readiness was observed in 119 \(27\.5%\) records\. Mean scores ranged from 2\.97 \(SD 0\.75\) for governance readiness to 3\.45 \(SD 0\.80\) for perceived value; Cronbach alpha ranged from 0\.80 to 0\.85\. Health information/informatics records had higher workforce capability \(3\.46 vs 3\.20; p=0\.001\), responsible adoption \(3\.45 vs 3\.28; p=0\.031\), and overall readiness \(3\.18 vs 3\.07; p=0\.037\)\. In the adjusted model, responsible AI climate \(B=0\.204 per SD, p&lt;0\.001\), workforce capability \(B=0\.167, p&lt;0\.001\), perceived value \(B=0\.159, p&lt;0\.001\), governance readiness \(B=0\.133, p=0\.001\), data and technical readiness \(B=0\.079, p=0\.020\), and prior AI use \(B=0\.159, p=0\.019\) were positively associated with responsible adoption\. Adjusted R2 was 0\.425\. The prototype demonstrates a coherent way to measure and analyze AI governance readiness in the healthcare administrative and information workforce\. The simulated pattern suggests a potentially important gap between perceived AI value and operational governance capacity, but no prevalence or association should be interpreted as an empirical finding\. Real\-world content validation, pilot testing, ethics approval, and multicenter data collection are required before scientific submission\.

## [Evaluation of Demographic, Clinical, and Radiologic Characteristics of Patients with Wernicke&\#x27;s Encephalopathy: A Retrospective Study](../publications/605eb074d8f61d44426a.md)

Sarra Elhamida Lazrak; Furkan Sarıdaş; Gizem Güllü; Rıfat Özpar; Emel Oğuz Akarsu; Yasemin Dinç; Ahmet Bilgehan Şahin; Murat Şen; Rümeysa Ayşe Güllülü; Aylin Bican Demir; Sevda Erer

Wernicke&\#x27;s encephalopathy \(WE\) is an acute neurologic condition caused by thiamine \(vitamin B1\) deficiency that can lead to permanent neurologic damage if not diagnosed and treated early\. In this retrospective study, the demographic, clinical, etiologic, and radiologic characteristics and functional outcomes of 26 patients aged over 18 years who were diagnosed as having WE and whose diagnoses were supported through magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) findings at our center between January 2000 and September 2025 were examined\. The mean age of the patients was 48\.35 years, and the majority were female\. The most common clinical findings were altered mental status, ataxia, and oculomotor disorders\. Etiologically, the most frequent causes were systemic conditions such as chronic alcoholism, cancer, dialysis, and total parenteral nutrition, followed by malabsorption, malnutrition, persistent vomiting, and bariatric surgery\. Imaging findings showed medial thalamus involvement as the most prominent feature, and hyperintensity was frequently observed in T2/FLAIR sequences\. Patients followed for at least 1 month had an average follow\-up period of 14\.1 months, and functional status was assessed using the modified Rankin Scale, with an average score of 0\.9 ± 1\.29\. In contrast, diffusion\-weighted imaging \(DWI\) positivity was significantly higher, particularly in cases associated with cancer, dialysis, and total parenteral nutrition \(p=0\.016\)\. WE is a condition that can arise from various etiologies, requiring careful clinical and radiologic evaluation\. Early diagnosis and thiamine treatment are critically important in preventing neurologic sequelae, especially in high\-risk patient groups\.

## [Inclusive Culture in Higher Education: University Teacher and Student Perceptions](../publications/605f510a15b3b9fcb26a.md)

Beatriz Duda\-Macera; María de los Ángeles Sánchez Trujillo

The objective of this study was to analyse the inclusive culture in the Faculty of Engineering of a private university in Lima\. The research focused on teaching staff and student perceptions regarding the value of student diversity and the barriers that hinder academic performance\. The approach was qualitative with a phenomenological design and included a sample of 10 university teachers and six students\. The instruments used were a semi\-structured interview guide for university teachers and a focus group guide for students\. The data analysis procedure was conducted using ATLAS\.ti \(version 23\)\. The results demonstrate a gap between the valuation of diversity and inclusive practice, whereby Universal Design for Learning \(UDL\) is not incorporated into session planning\. Likewise, a lack of learning supports is recognised as a result of institutional deficiencies\.

## [Recreation providers&\#x27; and end\-users&\#x27; twofold experiences: perception and knowledge about recreation programs in the Ba\-Phalaborwa Local Municipality, South Africa](../publications/606f96fa9a9062abd0bf.md)

T\. B\. Ngobeni; Makhaya Johannes Malema

Introduction The current study sought to provide insights from two stakeholder groups: recreation service providers and youth with disabilities\. People with disabilities continue to face various challenges related to their involvement in recreational programs, particularly in rural areas\. Recreational service providers appear to offer programs that can accommodate all individuals; however, the reality is different\. This study explored the recreational program experiences of youth with disabilities and recreation program service providers&\#x27; perceived knowledge\. Methods This study used a qualitative interpretive research approach with an exploratory design\. Participants included local recreation service providers and youth with disabilities in Ba\-Phalaborwa, Limpopo Province\. Data analysis followed the social model framework and was conducted inductively\. Data were collected through semi\-structured, open\-ended interviews\. The study followed ethical standards and adhered to research governance principles and guidelines\. Findings/Results The findings provide significant insights from two different perspectives\. Recreation service providers report having a unique understanding of how recreational programs should be implemented for people with disabilities\. Their understanding demonstrates the inclusive practices and steps required for inclusivity\. On the other hand, youth with disabilities reported their experiences, highlighting the lack of consultations during activity planning\. Their experiences reflect a lack of consideration within their communities and limited access to basic facilities that would enable barrier\-free recreational programs\. Discussion The implications of the present study involve various stakeholders, including local municipalities as a primary liaison for joint efforts, so they can meaningfully influence the livelihoods of people with disabilities and their recreational participation\. In conclusion, meaningful participation in recreation requires collaboration between recreation service providers and community members, particularly people with disabilities\.

## [Exploring GenAI Chatbot Use for L2 Learning: A Mixed\-Methods Study of Foundation\-Year Students in Oman](../publications/607595e278a1cbd3b899.md)

Moosa Ahmed Ali Sulaiman; Mohamed Abdelmageed; Nagwa Mohammed Khallaf

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) chatbots have increasingly become part of many university students&\#x27; English as a second language \(L2\) learning\. However, little is known about how students in general foundation programmes use them during the move from Arabic\-medium schooling to English\-medium higher education\. This sequential explanatory mixed\-methods study examined GenAI chatbot use among foundation\-year students at a private university in Oman\. A questionnaire \(N = 262\) covered usage patterns, perceived usefulness for L2 skills, AI output verification practices, challenges and support needs, and was followed by two focus groups \(n = 15\)\. Results showed that ChatGPT was the dominant tool \(91\.2%\) that students accessed mainly by smartphone \(80\.5%\)\.
