The most common frequency was &quot;sometimes&quot; \(47\.3%\), while 42\.4% of respondents reported using chatbots &quot;always&quot; or &quot;often&quot;\. Most students \(57\.6%\) switched between English and Arabic while interacting with GenAI chatbots\. Students rated chatbots as clearly useful for writing, speaking and reading, but not for listening\. They also valued grammar and vocabulary corrections by chatbots more than their feedback on writing or speaking assignments\. More than two\-thirds of respondents preferred teacher feedback on their writing \(72\.9%\)\. The most frequently reported challenges were incorrect information \(43\.5%\) and unclear responses \(35\.1%\), while the most common verification strategy of generated content was asking a teacher \(46\.2%\)\. Focus\-group participants described purpose\-driven but largely unplanned prompting, translation\-mediated comprehension, concern about overreliance, inconsistent teacher stances, and a need for classroom\-embedded guidance\. Chatbot use for L2 learning among foundation\-year students can be interpreted as a tool\-mediated activity largely outside formal L2 instructional design, with teachers as epistemic anchors\. The study recommends early, skill\-specific, teacher\-mediated AI literacy instruction in foundation programmes\.

## [Measurement\-based Vehicle to Vehicle \(V2V\) Pathloss Modeling and Leakage Aware Machine Learning Prediction in Indonesian Urban and Suburban Environments](../publications/60881e319fb12b89e04e.md)

Elfira Nureza Ardina; Rustam Asnawi; Eko Marpanaji; Ari Endang Jayati; Nor Azlan Othman

Reliable short\-range Vehicle\-to\-Vehicle \(V2V\) links require propagation models that reflect local road geometry, low antenna heights, and trial\-to\-trial variation\.This study characterizes nominal large\-scale path loss at 920 MHz over 2\.15\-99\.44m on urban and suburban routes in Central Java, Indonesia\.The analysis uses 224 spatially aggregated observations obtained from 18 measurement trials\.To prevent target leakage, Received Signal Strength Indicator \(RSSI\) is used only to construct the link\-budget response, while RSSI, Signal\-to\-Noise Ratio \(SNR\), measured\-path\-loss columns, and empirical\-model outputs are excluded from the predictors\.Ordinary Least Squares \(OLS\), Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression Trees \(GBRT\), and histogram gradient boosting are evaluated using identical predictors, preprocessing, and leave\-one\-measurement\-trial\-out folds\.Their mean Root Mean Square Errors are 11\.306, 11\.205, 11\.779, and 12\.420 dB, respectively, while the corresponding mean Mean Absolute Errors are 9\.439, 9\.351, 9\.773, and 10\.436 dB\.Random Forest has marginally lower trial\-mean errors, whereas OLS has the best pooled R\-squared value \(0\.428\)\.Overlapping confidence intervals do not demonstrate predictive superiority for any nonlinear model\.The contribution is therefore methodological: a leakage\-aware, fair, and reproducible framework for evaluating cross\-trial V2V path\-loss generalization under controlled experimental conditions\.

## [Garcia Pedraza, Ruben: Global Artificial Intelligence and Specific Artificial Intelligence](../publications/608ef4051a706f90535b.md)



This paper introduces the theoretical distinction between Specific Artificial Intelligence \(SAI\) and Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\)\. It traces the evolutionary roots of intelligence from biological adaptation to scientific reasoning and artificial cognition\. SAI models are examined as the current dominant paradigm, oriented toward task\-specific applications, while GAI is proposed as an integrative cognitive architecture capable of processing and acting upon total planetary or cosmic data systems\. The paper discusses artificial consciousness, the emergence of artificial psychology, and the trajectory toward a unified intelligence system with transformative ethical and epistemological implications\. The argument emphasizes the systemic transition from anthropocentric AI to post\-human cognitive systems, laying the groundwork for future non\-human sciences and planetary\-scale decision\-making\.

## [GAMBARAN KEMAMPUAN MEMPERTAHANKAN PERHATIAN PADA ANAK TUNAGRAHITA DI SLB NEGERI PEMBINA MEDAN SUMATERA UTARA](../publications/608efe588f608209a26d.md)

Nita Permata Sari Siregar

ABSTRACT Students with mild intellectual disabilities do not necessarily maintain the same level of attention throughout learning activities, as their attentional patterns may vary according to individual characteristics and learning conditions\. This issue was examined through a descriptive qualitative study conducted at SLB Negeri Pembina Medan, involving one tenth\-grade student in a special senior high school program, identified by the initial P, selected through purposive sampling, and the homeroom teacher as a supporting informant\. Data were collected through passive participant observation, semi\-structured interviews, and documentation\. The data were subsequently analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, following the Miles and Huberman model\. During classroom activities, P demonstrated relatively stable sustained attention, as reflected in prompt responses to verbal instructions, independent task completion, and continued engagement despite distractions in the classroom environment\. However, attention began to decline toward the end of the learning session, at approximately 11:30 a\.m\., as indicated by reduced work intensity and an increased need for teacher guidance\. This change suggests a possible association between lesson duration, physical and mental fatigue, and the maintenance of attention, although its underlying causes cannot be established conclusively\. Individualized approaches, praise, token rewards, and verbal prompts formed part of the pedagogical support accompanying the student&\#x27;s engagement\. These findings emphasize the need to understand attention in relation to individual profiles and learning contexts without generalizing the characteristics of a single student to all students with mild intellectual disabilities\. ABSTRAK Perhatian siswa tunagrahita ringan selama pembelajaran tidak selalu bertahan pada tingkat yang sama, melainkan memperlihatkan variasi sesuai dengan karakteristik siswa dan situasi belajar yang dihadapi\. Gambaran tersebut ditelaah melalui penelitian kualitatif deskriptif di SLB Negeri Pembina Medan dengan melibatkan seorang siswa kelas X SMA SLB berinisial P yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling, serta wali kelas sebagai informan pendukung\. Informasi diperoleh melalui observasi dengan partisipasi pasif, wawancara semi\-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi\. Data selanjutnya dianalisis melalui tahapan kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi berdasarkan model Miles dan Huberman\. Selama kegiatan belajar, P memperlihatkan kemampuan mempertahankan sustained attention yang relatif stabil, terlihat dari respons cepat terhadap instruksi verbal, kemandirian menyelesaikan tugas, dan keberlanjutan aktivitas meskipun terdapat gangguan di lingkungan kelas\. Akan tetapi, menjelang pukul 11\.30 WIB, perhatian mulai melemah, ditandai dengan berkurangnya intensitas kerja dan meningkatnya kebutuhan terhadap arahan guru\. Perubahan ini mengindikasikan kemungkinan keterkaitan antara durasi pembelajaran, kelelahan fisik dan mental, serta keberlangsungan perhatian, meskipun penyebabnya belum dapat dipastikan\. Pendekatan individual, pujian, token reward, dan arahan verbal menjadi bagian dari dukungan pedagogis yang menyertai keterlibatan subjek\. Temuan ini menegaskan perlunya memahami atensi melalui profil individual dan konteks pembelajaran, tanpa menggeneralisasikan karakteristik satu siswa kepada seluruh siswa tunagrahita ringan\.

## [Introduction](../publications/60902ab608e12c1737a4.md)

Kristina Palm

The second 2026 issue of Nordic Journal of Working Life Studies comprises four research articles\. One study is from Denmark, two are from Norway, and one study features a case from each Nordic country\.

## [Navigating the Regulatory Landscape of Artificial Intelligence in A ustralian Clinical Dentistry](../publications/60959587c4a459ef6ece.md)

Rishi Sanjay Ramani; Arosha Tania Weerakoon; Tami Yap; Bree Jones

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is rapidly transforming clinical dentistry, with an increasing number of AI\-powered diagnostic and treatment planning tools entering the Australian healthcare market\. As clinicians adopt AI\-based dental software, it is becoming increasingly important to understand the regulatory frameworks that govern them\. This narrative review explores the regulatory approval pathways and governance of AI tools used in Australian dental and healthcare settings to inform and educate practitioners\. Australia regulates AI\-based dental software primarily through the Therapeutic Goods Administration, which classifies eligible products as software as a medical device under a risk\-based, technology\-agnostic framework established by the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989\. AI tools that function as clinical decision\-support systems are subject to mandatory conformity assessment and registration on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods \(ARTG\) prior to lawful supply\. Although the Australian framework aligns with the International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, the approval process is comparatively less transparent than that required in jurisdictions such as the United States and the European Union, and questions remain regarding the consistency of post\-market oversight\. This review also highlights emerging regulatory challenges associated with adaptive AI systems\. Software could initially receive approval as a low\-risk device that evolves to provide specific clinical advice beyond its approval scope\. These updates to functionality risk bypassing established oversight pathways that rely on self\-reported intended use\. Furthermore, currently available AI tools lack comprehensive public\-facing transparent evidence for regulatory compliance that is complicated by ambiguous and inconsistent terminology and adaptive AI system classification\. Regardless of regulatory approval, clinicians remain professionally accountable for the use of AI tools in clinical decision\-making and for ensuring that patient care meets accepted standards of practice\.

## [Nurses’ knowledge and practice on patient safety in tertiary medical college hospitals in Bangladesh: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/6098278272d471125829.md)

Md Abdul Khalek; K\. A\. T\. M\. Ehsanul Huq; Abdulfatai Olamilekan Babaita; Chihiro Kimura; Michiko Moriyama

Background Patient safety is critical to healthcare and depends on a safety culture to ensure high\-quality care\. A strong patient safety culture \(PSC\) reduces preventable patient harm, with nurses’ knowledge and practices central to delivering safe care in hospitals\. Yet, evidence remains limited in tertiary medical college hospitals in Bangladesh\. Therefore, this study aimed to assess nurses’ knowledge, practices, and associated factors regarding PSC in tertiary medical college hospitals in Bangladesh\. Methods A cross\-sectional study was conducted from April to September 2025 in eight medical college hospitals across all eight administrative divisions in Bangladesh\. Of 7,170 eligible nurses, 4,982 \(valid response rate 69\.5%\) were analyzed using a self\-administered questionnaire\. Descriptive, inferential statistics and correlation were performed\. Results Participants’ mean scores were 5\.44 \(SD 1\.82\) \(range: 0–10\) for patient safety knowledge and 28\.92 \(SD 7\.76\) \(range: 10–50\) for practice\. At the item level, 49\.3% correctly identified adverse events, and only 9\.8% knew the appropriate reporting methods\. In terms of practice, 48\.6% reported never using incident\-reporting forms, and 26\.4% reported never using structured communication tools\. In bivariate analysis, participants’ education, working ward, and having in\-service training were significantly associated with knowledge and younger age, hospital experience, working ward, and in\-service training were significantly associated with practice\. After adjusting in a mixed\-effects model, professional experience \( p &lt; 0\.018, p &lt; 0\.001\) and in\-service training \( p &lt; 0\.001, p &lt; 0\.019\) were significantly associated with knowledge and practice, respectively\. Gender \( p &lt; 0\.049\) and diploma in nursing education \( p &lt; 0\.027\) were associated with knowledge, while age \( p &lt; 0\.001\), professional experience \( p &lt; 0\.001\), and in\-service training \( p &lt; 0\.019\) were associated with practice\. Conclusion Nurses’ knowledge of patient safety increased with professional experience and in\-service training; however, gender and education had negative associations\. Nurses’ practices also increased with professional experience, while age and in\-service training showed negative associations\. Targeted, context\-specific in\-service training with post\-training monitoring by Quality Improvement Teams is essential to improve nurses’ knowledge and practice\. Strengthening patient safety reporting systems with leadership engagement, logistical support, and oversight by the government regulatory bodies may improve patient\-safety practice and quality of care\.

## [An Empirical Analysis of Locally Concentrated Patch Aggregation in Training\-Free Brain MRI Anomaly Detection](../publications/60a504c62b7a9eebc9ae.md)

Ahmed Dheyaa Radhi; Mohsin Hasan Hussein; Hussein Ali Hussein Al Naffakh; Ali M\. Ahmed Al\-Sabaawi; Rozaida Ghazali

Unsupervised anomaly detection in MRI requires no abnormal labels, and detectors built on frozen, pretrained vision encoders now rival elaborate trained pipelines\.It remains unclear whether the reported benefit of patchlevel representations reflects representation granularity or the operator that aggregates per\-patch deviations into a slice score\.The objective of this study is to isolate that factor\.Holding the backbone, reference set, and scoring rule fixed across three brain sequences of one fastMRI cohort, contrast\-enhanced axial T1 \(AXT1POST\), axial fluid\-attenuated inversion recovery \(AXFLAIR\) and axial T1 \(AXT1\), we vary only the aggregation operator, with every estimate drawn from one stored prediction file under one patient\-level cluster bootstrap\.A patch\-level representation improves detection on all three sequences, but the size of that benefit depends on the operator in a sequence\-specific way\.On the contrast\-enhanced AXT1POST sequence, locally concentrated aggregation exceeds full\-slice averaging by 0\.134 in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\) \(p = 0\.010\), whereas the two diffuse sequences are operator\-invariant; an interaction test supports the dissociation \(versus AXFLAIR \+0\.123, Holm\-adjusted p = 0\.045; versus AXT1 \+0\.135, Holm\-adjusted p = 0\.045\)\.Stratifying the non\-enhanced sequence by lesion area shows that spatial extent alone does not explain it: lesions eight times smaller recover a quarter of the effect\.At the volume level the patch representation reaches 0\.982 AUROC on AXT1POST, on ten positive cases\.Four detectors reimplemented under identical splits, two contemporary and two classical, bracket the configuration rather than fall below it: one exceeds it on AXFLAIR by 0\.013 AUROC, and no superiority is claimed\.Because enhancement and lesion type remain confounded, we report a sequence\-level association rather than a causal effect\.Practically, the aggregation operator mattered more than the representation level, and full\-slice averaging should be avoided\.

## [Enhancing Hypothyroid Severity Classification through Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Models](../publications/60a63b93ee7da8563aaf.md)

G\. Arockia Sahaya Sheela K Chitra

Objective: A person with undiagnosed or ineffectively assessed hypothyroidism may lead to serious metabolic and cardiovascular problems\. Existing diagnostic methods mainly focus on binary classification \(hypothyroid vs\. non\-hypothyroid\) and frequently oversee the need to stratify patients by severity level, which is serious for guiding treatment intensity\. This study proposes to develop a machine learning outline that not only expects the presence of hypothyroidism but also categorizes its severity level, using Bayesian Optimization to perfect model performance for enhanced diagnostic precision\. Methods: A clinical dataset comprising thyroid function indicators such as TSH, T3, T4, FTI, and patient demographic/clinical traits was used to figure a multi\-class classification model for hypothyroid severity levels like mild, moderate and severe hypothyroidism\. Data preprocessing comprises of handling missing values, imbalanced dataset, and feature selection\. Several baseline classifiers including Random Forest, K\-Nearest Neighbour and Support Vector Machine were trained, and Bayesian Optimization was employed to methodically search the hyperparameter space of these models, optimizing parameters like maximum depth of the tree, minimum number of leaves, minimum sample split, number of estimators, selection of criterion\. Model performance metrics was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score with cross\-validation confirming robustness against overfitting\. Findings: The Bayesian\-optimized models constantly outperformed their grid\-search on randomized search cross validation, attaining better classification accuracy and more balanced precision and recall across severity classes\. The optimized ensemble model established strong discriminative capability in clinical mild, moderate and severe hypothyroid cases, which are frequently clinically unclear\. Feature importance analysis was revealed that TSH and FTI levels were the most significant predictors of severity, positioning with recognized clinical understanding\. Novelty: Distinct prior studies that mainly address hypothyroidism as a binary classification problem, this study introduces a severity level prediction, offering fine tunes diagnostic support\. The combination of Bayesian Optimization for hyperparameter tuning rather than conservative grid or random search CV, it provided a more efficient and adaptive optimization process, dropping computational cost while improving predictive accuracy\. This combination of severity level\-based organization and optimized hyperparameter tuning method represents a novel contribution towards building clinically meaningful, precise, and effective hypothyroid diagnostic support systems\.

## [Sami, Zawwar: When Revocation Does Not End Access\. Temporal Repair Dependencies in Application Compromise\. S1](../publications/60a6fc34be117bc224c5.md)



What happens when the old credentials stop working, but the application can still create new ones? I investigate this recovery failure through a small running system: an issuer, a protected resource and a separate observer\. Across 48 distinct repair\-and\-renewal schedules, 20 retain access even though every original credential is rejected\. Each schedule is repeated three times\. The failure depends on the order in which authority is removed and its source is stopped\. I express that dependency as a renewal graph and prove a conditional repair\-order rule, checked against 98,697 graph\-order pairs\. A second failure survives an otherwise effective provisioning barrier: work accepted before containment creates new credentials after revocation\. An executed walkthrough compares leaving that work pending, cancelling it and rejecting it at commit using an issuance epoch\. The last two prevent reopening in the tested sequence; a positive control confirms that new work can succeed after service resumes\. Equifax, Exchange and MOVEit establish the need to examine application, identity and data boundaries separately\. The contribution is a reproducible recovery test that follows replacement credentials and pending issuance through to the protected operation, with explicit conditions for what its result establishes\. \(direct link \)

## [SurvICL: a Foundation Model for in\-context Survival Analysis](../publications/60a9b8ff0977c87e065f.md)

Julie Alberge; Linus Bleistein; Judith Abécassis; Marine Le Morvan; Gaël Varoquaux; David Holzmüller

Tabular foundation models \(TFMs\) now outperform gradient\-boosted trees in classification and regression\. Yet in survival analysis, which predicts when an event occurs from censored data, often on small clinical cohorts, we find that no existing TFM beats the half\-century\-old Cox model\. We address this issue by introducing SurvICL, a TFM that predicts survival curves in\-context\. SurvICL is pretrained on purely synthetic datasets generated from a novel flexible proportional\-odds prior that outperforms other prior types in our ablation study\. Unlike most other survival models, SurvICL is trained with a plain quantile regression loss, which is possible because its synthetic pre\-training data generator can provide uncensored event times\. Additionally, we introduce the largest survival benchmark to date spanning 103 datasets\. On the 63 datasets held out from all design decisions, SurvICL outperforms 20 tree\-based, deep, and foundation\-model baselines without any tuning: it wins 82\.9\\% of pairwise comparisons in integrated Brier score, against 71\.3\\% for the runner\-up, the Cox model, and is the first model to rank above Cox on small datasets\.

## [Episode of epidemic thunderstorm asthma in Shanxi China September 2025: epidemiological characteristics, mechanisms, and emergency management strategies](../publications/60aebf546e9e9a4fc614.md)

Tingting Shen; Guiying Guo; Hongmei Li; 王俊芳; Hongwei Wang; Jianghui Mi

Background In September 2025, our emergency department \(ED\) experienced a sudden influx of 39 asthmatic patients following a thunderstorm\. Based on our data, we summarized demographic features of the 39 patients, reviewed literature to describe thunderstorm asthma pathogenesis, and compiled patients’ emergency management processes\. Method This was a retrospective observational study\. Clinical data were collected from electronic medical records and subsequent follow\-up\. Data were summarized and analyzed using descriptive statistics\. Results Following standardized management, all patients were successfully managed, ensuring their safety\. In this study, male patients accounted for a slightly higher proportion than females\. The mean age of the 39 patients was 31\.62 ± 12\.86 years\. The vast majority of patients had a history of allergic rhinitis\. Laboratory tests revealed elevated peripheral blood eosinophil counts in some patients\. The primary medications administered for thunderstorm asthma included inhaled corticosteroid, short\-acting muscarinic antagonists, and short\-acting β 2 \-adrenergic agonist\. Discussion This study indicates that thunderstorm\-related asthma in northern China predominantly occurs in early autumn, with Artemisia pollen as the major allergen\. In terms of pathogenesis, thunderstorms induce rupture of Artemisia pollen and release tiny allergenic particles that are inhaled into the airway\. Antigens are presented by dendritic cells to activate CD4⁺, Th2 cells, which secrete cytokines such as IL\-4 and initiate IgE\-mediated allergic inflammation, thereby triggering acute asthma attacks\. Meteorological early warning and preventive strategies, as well as hospital\-based specialized emergency systems are required\.

## [Assessing the association between electronic invoicing and regional tax revenues in Kazakhstan](../publications/60b0f5efd77e37907a4d.md)

Zамzagul Tursynkulova; Aizhan Urinbasarovna Abishova; Gulbana Erzhigitovna Maulenkulova; Zarema Abdramanovna Bigeldiyeva; G\. O\. Baidauletova

Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractElectronic invoicing is an important component of digital tax administration that improves tax transparency and strengthens revenue administration\. This study examines the association between electronic invoicing and regional tax revenues across Kazakhstan’s regions\. The analysis uses regional panel data for 16 regions covering 2010–2024 and employs fixed\-effects panel regression models together with k\-means cluster analysis\. The empirical dataset was obtained from the reports of the State Revenue Committee of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Kazakhstan and the Bureau of National Statistics of the Republic of Kazakhstan\. The results show that electronic invoicing is not significantly associated with regional tax revenues in either the baseline model \(β = 0\.039; p = 0\.538\) or the specification with a time trend \(β = –0\.024; p = 0\.690\)\. However, the specification using the shifted e\-Inv indicator yields a positive and statistically significant association \(β = 0\.302; p = 0\.047\)\. Because e\-Inv is a nationwide step dummy, this result reflects temporal robustness rather than evidence of a delayed fiscal effect\. Across all model specifications, GRP per capita remains the strongest determinant of regional tax revenues \(β ≈ 0\.825\-1\.102\), highlighting the central role of regional economic capacity\. The cluster analysis identifies three distinct groups of regions with different fiscal and digital characteristics, illustrating substantial regional heterogeneity in Kazakhstan\. The findings suggest that the association between electronic invoicing and regional tax revenues depends on model specification and broader economic conditions\. In contrast, regional economic capacity remains the most robust determinant of tax revenues\.

## [AI\-Mediated Translation and Interference in Arabic: Revisiting Toury’s Law in the Age of Digital Language](../publications/60b65548848b5495f9a1.md)

Sonia Asmahène Halimi

Thanks to artificial intelligence and machine translation technologies, the volume and speed of translation production have increased\. However, these technologies also raise questions about the impact of dominant digital languages on less resourced ones\. Many languages remain underrepresented in multilingual modelling due to the limited availability of digital language resources\. This results in an uneven linguistic representation in natural language processing and AI models, which, in turn, leads to an asymmetry in linguistic influence, as evidenced by the literature\. This study investigates linguistic interference in Arabic translation within digital environments, drawing on Toury’s \(2012\) Law of Interference\. It addresses a critical gap by examining, from a qualitative perspective, how uneven language representation in automated translation environments may shape the quality of Arabic translations\. It argues that the unequal distribution of digital language resources may contribute to the transfer of source\-language features into Arabic translations\. Methodologically, the study adopts an exploratory qualitative approach, analysing a small corpus of 100 Arabic translations from English and French, including human and machine\-generated translations, focusing on three dimensions of interference: lexical, syntactic and discursive\. The findings show repeating patterns of source\-oriented elements, including the incorrect use of cataphoric construction and the coordinator واو, the excessive use of periphrastic constructions and the reduction of stylistic adaptation\. Similar patterns were observed in machine translation outputs and online Arabic content, suggesting that AI systems reproduce linguistic tendencies already present in digitally circulating texts\. The study highlights the need for greater attention to online high\-quality Arabic resources\.

## [ACORN: Adaptive Consensus of Repeated Clusterings identifies pyramidal neurons and interneurons in the primate motor cortex based on extracellular spike waveforms](../publications/60b77e7397b944a2c7aa.md)

Zoltán Soltész; Viviane SGM Tenorio; Takamichi Tohyama; Anne ME Baker; Stuart N Baker; Alexander Kraskov

Understanding how neural circuits generate behaviour requires knowledge of both neural activity patterns and the cell types they originate from\. While the scale of neuronal recordings has dramatically increased since the advent of dense multicontact probes, accurate identification of cell types remains elusive\. Traditional approaches have used spike width to attempt a classification, with narrow spikes assumed to be inhibitory interneurons\. However, fast pyramidal tract neurons \(PTNs, known to be excitatory\) with thin spikes and interneurons with wide spikes challenge these assumptions\. Here we accomplish three related objectives\. First, we produce a ground truth dataset of extracellular spike shapes from electrophysiologically identified pyramidal neurons from primary \(M1\) and supplementary motor areas \(SMA\) and optogenetically identified interneurons in M1 in female macaque monkeys\. Next, we show that spike width correlates with antidromic latency not only in M1 but also in the SMA, suggesting that it is a physiologically meaningful measure across the motor cortex\. Finally, we introduce our unsupervised ensemble clustering method, &quot;ACORN&quot;, and characterise its performance on our neocortical macaque dataset, the C4 cerebellar database, and a juxtacellularly recorded mouse dataset, demonstrating strong out\-of\-the\-box performance across species, brain areas, and recording techniques\. ACORN can cluster neuronal waveforms without training or tuning, and provides data\-derived confidence values for its predictions\. Our ground truth data can be used as a reference to help identify or verify clusters in novel datasets\. Together, our method and database provide a streamlined foundation for electrophysiological cell classification without necessitating changes to recording paradigms\. Significance Statement High\-density extracellular recordings are increasingly the norm in neuroscience, but accurate and non\-invasive identification of cells remains a challenge\. Here we provide a database of action potential spike shapes from pyramidal tract neurons and interneurons of the macaque supplementary motor area, whose identities we verified using nerve stimulation and optogenetics, respectively\. We introduce the neuron clustering method “ACORN”, and showcase its robustness by evaluating its performance on a variety of distinct datasets\. Our training\-free clustering technique is designed to support experimentalists, while our ground truth database can enhance and validate future datasets and method development\.

## [Residual Stochastic Concept Bottleneck Models](../publications/60d9d888d5462bceaff7.md)

Stephen Marcou; Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga; Sonia Laguna; Moritz Vandenhirtz; Julia E\. Vogt; Mateja Jamnik

Concept\-based models \(CMs\) learn human\-interpretable intermediate representations that enable users to understand the model&\#x27;s reasoning and steer its predictions through test\-time concept interventions\. However, in realistic settings, their performance can be limited by concept incompleteness, where the training concepts fail to capture all task\-relevant information\. Adding an unconstrained residual pathway to the model&\#x27;s predictive process can overcome the consequences of incompleteness\. However, this introduces an inscrutable, leak\-prone prediction pathway that may weaken concept interventions, as these often leave residual variables unchanged\. To address this limitation, we introduce Residual Stochastic Concept Bottleneck Models \(Res\-SCBMs\), a family of concept\-based models that jointly model concept and residual variables through a multivariate Gaussian distribution\. Res\-SCBMs learn a covariance structure that explicitly captures dependencies between the known concepts and learnt residual variables, allowing interventions to propagate to statistically dependent residual variables through Gaussian conditioning\. This extends the intervention capabilities of previous CMs without requiring concept completeness during training\. Our results show that, across multiple concept\-incomplete benchmarks, Res\-SCBMs improve predictive performance over competing baselines while retaining effective test\-time concept interventions\.

## [Examining lumbar spine MRI images of humans using finite element method and transfer learning approaches](../publications/60e9c2129c6bd0c51d5c.md)

E\. Punarselvam; R\. Ramya; Kamarajugadda Kishore Kumar; L\. Jesmalar

Low back pain \(LBP\) is one of the most prevalent causes of global disability, and lumbar degenerative disc disease \(LDDD\) stands out as its clinical presentation\. We present an automated pipeline involving U\-Net with Transfer Learning \(TL\) and Finite Element Method \(FEM\) simulation to analyze the biomechanical functioning of the lumbar spine from Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\)\. We first segment the lumbar region using U\-Net with TL and then generate patient\-specific finite element \(FE\) models analyzing their biomechanics under various angular displacements \(30°, 60°, and 90°\) and loading conditions \(482\-699N\)\. The fluid properties were tuned using Grey Wolf Optimization \(GWO\) algorithm\. The U\-Net with TL was able to segment the lumbar region with DSC value of 95\.73%\. We found the highest von Mises stresses for all the cases at L5/S1 level ranging from 1·0781e\+008 Pa to 1·444e\+008 Pa\. Our results demonstrate the potential of combining machine learning and biomechanical modeling approaches for clinical evaluation of the human lumbar spine\. Notably, the study makes following three key contributions: \(1\) it is the first work to employ U\-Net with GWO for FE analysis of the lumbar spine, \(2\) it validates the model performance under multiple angular displacements, and \(3\) provides an end\-to\-end solution for the biomechanical analysis of the spine from MRI\. We present an automated pipeline involving U\-Net with Transfer Learning \(TL\) and Finite Element Method \(FEM\) simulation to analyze the biomechanical functioning of the lumbar spine from Magnetic Resonance Imaging \(MRI\)\.

## [INDIAN PHILOSOPHY AS A FOUNDATION OF THE INDIAN KNOWLEDGE TRADITION: RECONSIDERING KNOWLEDGE, SELF AND REALITY IN THE CONTEMPORARY CONTEXT](../publications/60f3f457beead6161ab7.md)

Dr\. Trina Das

The Indian Knowledge Tradition constitutes a rich and multidimensional intellectual heritage that has evolved through centuries of systematic inquiry into knowledge, reality, consciousness, ethics, language, society, nature, and human flourishing\. Indian philosophy occupies a central position within this tradition, serving not merely as an abstract investigation of metaphysical questions but also as a comprehensive framework for understanding the nature, sources, validity, and purpose of knowledge\. The diverse philosophical schools of India developed distinctive perspectives on epistemology, metaphysics, logic, language, morality, and liberation, while maintaining significant connections between theoretical inquiry and practical experience\. Fundamental concepts such as pramāṇa, ātman, dharma, karma, mokṣa, yoga, ṛta, and puruṣārtha illustrate the intellectual depth and interdisciplinary character of Indian philosophical thought\. This paper critically examines Indian philosophy as a foundational dimension of the Indian Knowledge Tradition, focusing on its epistemological diversity, conceptions of the relationship between the knower and knowledge, ethical foundations, and perspectives on human well\-being\. It further explores the contemporary significance of these philosophical insights in relation to education, ethics, sustainability, consciousness, and holistic approaches to learning\. The paper argues that the revitalisation of the Indian Knowledge Tradition requires more than the recognition of historical accomplishments; it necessitates critical interpretation, contextual understanding, and meaningful engagement with the philosophical principles underlying this intellectual heritage\. Such an approach can facilitate productive dialogue between classical Indian thought and contemporary knowledge systems, contributing to a more reflective, ethically informed, and inclusive understanding of knowledge and human development\.

## [SPNet: segmentation\-to\-poly network for building footprint extraction](../publications/60f4a9b8c68c08261181.md)

Huaigang Huang; Ruisheng Wang; Jinpeng Lei; Kun Zhou; Yibin Tian

Building extraction from remote sensing images is a core task in urban planning and related applications\. However, achieving high\-precision building footprint extraction remains challenging due to complex building shapes and background noise\. Existing mask\-based methods produce raster masks with jagged edges, which generate numerous redundant corners after vectorization\. In contrast, vector\-based methods rely on complex multi\-stage prediction pipelines, leading to large cumulative errors that degrade the final extraction performance\. To address these issues, this paper proposes a building footprint extraction method named SPNet, which generates compact building polygons using only a single prediction pipeline based on semantic segmentation\. First, corner regions within a defined area are annotated on the ground truth masks to convert sparse corner supervision into dense corner\-region supervision for network training\. Then, a backbone network with good performance and efficiency is adopted for feature extraction, and the LASS module, which combines SS2D\-based global modeling and Natten\-based local attention, is introduced in the feature fusion stage to improve the extraction of both overall building structures and local corner details\. Finally, building polygons are generated by computing corner coordinates and sorting corners using the predicted corner and building masks\. SPNet adopts a concise and efficient structure with a streamlined pipeline\. It achieves competitive results on the WHU and CrowdAI datasets\.

## [Approaching Backpropagation Accuracy with Weight Perturbation on MNIST](../publications/60fbae44444dc75f7665.md)

Patrick Inoue

Weight perturbation \(WP\) estimates learning directions from random parameter perturbations and a scalar change in loss, without backpropagating derivatives\. We examine how batch size, training duration, and estimator stabilization affect its attainable accuracy in fully connected MNIST networks\. In the shallow configuration, large\-batch training reaches approximately 97\\% test accuracy, compared with an early backpropagation \(BP\) reference near 97\.5\-\-98\\%\. The same comparison exposes a substantial efficiency gap: under a ten\-epoch budget, shallow WP reaches 90\.2\\%, whereas the reported BP reference reaches 97\.4\\%\. Epoch\-indexed curves show diminishing returns from increasing batch size beyond 4,000\. Learning\-rate reduction and averaging independent perturbation\-based updates also stabilize deeper networks, although their recorded results do not establish BP\-level accuracy\. We distinguish these empirical findings from a finite\-horizon approximation argument: under stated regularity conditions, population WP can approximate a fixed gradient\-descent trajectory arbitrarily closely at any fixed finite depth\. Positive classification margins then suffice to preserve the reference predictions on a finite test set with arbitrarily high probability\. Together, the results identify near\-BP accuracy as a configuration\- and budget\-dependent possibility, rather than evidence of equal efficiency or an unconditional accuracy guarantee across depth\.

## [Secondary education teachers&\#x27; perspectives on the use of ChatGPT in teaching](../publications/61164856364616ebf361.md)

MEGALOMYSTAKA CHRISTINA; TSAOUSIDOU IOANNA

This study explores the attitudes and level of readiness of secondary education teachers regarding the integration of ChatGPT into teaching\. Adopting a mixed\-methods approach utilizing a questionnaire, the study examined a sample of teachers from two schools in Central Macedonia\. The findings reveal an attitude of cautious optimism\. Participants acknowledge the tool&quot;s significant utility in lesson preparation and material creation, which saves valuable time\. However, they express strong concerns regarding the reliability of information, ethical issues, the absence of a regulatory framework within schools, and the risk of undermining students&quot; critical thinking\. In conclusion, although artificial intelligence is envisioned as a future digital assistant, there is an urgent need for systematic and experiential institutional training for teachers to ensure its pedagogically safe utilization\.

## [Health Prediction for Rural Older Adults Based on Artificial Intelligence Deep Neural Network](../publications/611c7f866c4302761538.md)

Quan Liu; Xuan Zhao

With the intensification of global population aging, health management for the elderly in rural areas faces challenges such as insufficient medical resources, outdated service facilities, and inadequate professional capacity\. Against this backdrop, the early warning of health risks primarily related to hypertension and cardiovascular chronic diseases, as well as the real\-time assessment of health status based on multi\-source physiological data, have become urgent issues to address\. To address this challenge, this study proposes an Artificial Intelligence\-Driven Deep Neural Network \(AI\-DNN\) health prediction model designed for rural intelligent elderly care scenarios\. This model fuses multi\-source heterogeneous physiological and behavioral data\. It adopts an improved residual gated recurrent unit combined with a two\-level attention mechanism for health risk perception to jointly model key time segments and high\-risk physiological indicators\. Meanwhile, an adaptive feature reweighting module is designed to dynamically adjust feature contributions according to individual health status\. This enhances the model&\#x27;s representation capability and predictive performance for sparse, noisy, and heterogeneous health data\. On the large\-scale real\-world rural health monitoring dataset covering 2158 elderly residents in several administrative villages in three provinces, the AI\-DNN model achieves 92\.3% accuracy, 91\.7% F1 value and 0\.948 AUC, which was significantly better than the baseline model, and p &lt; 0\.05\. In addition, the parameter of AI\-DNN model is 9\.3M, which is in the middle and low level among all depth models, and it is a lightweight structure with low reasoning delay\. This study provides deployable and robust technical support for intelligent elderly care systems in rural China, and provides useful solutions and experience for elderly health management in other resource\-limited regions around the world\. The study has broad application potential and promotion value\.

## [Building and Leading Fully Online Campuses: Strategy and Data in Practice](../publications/611ffcc0b6abfa454c4e.md)

Carlos R\. Morales

Many institutions have expanded online course offerings, yet far fewer have built fully functioning online campuses with clear governance, consistent quality, and measurable outcomes\. This paper presents a practitioner framework grounded in the author’s experience establishing online operations across four institutional contexts: Lock Haven University of Pennsylvania, Ana G\. Méndez Virtual Campus, TCC Connect Campus, and Lone Star College–Online\. The framework centers on three areas of focus—governance and operating model, scalable stakeholder engagement, and data\-informed strategy—and is enabled by a continuous improvement cadence that translates metrics into decisions and accountability\.

## [Pedestal penalty factors for ELM\-free regimes in DIII\-D and extension to fusion pilot plant design](../publications/6121e21af23988bba0ac.md)

Andrew Oakleigh Nelson; T\. Odstrčil; T\. Slendebroek; Zeyu Li; N\. Leuthold; C\. F\. B\. Zimmermann; John Labbate; Jamie Dunsmore; J\. Schellpfeffer; Severin Sebastian Denk; R\. Nazikian; Carlos A\. Paz\-Soldan

Abstract Though the EPED model, which provides a first\-principles\-based predictive capability for the pedestal height and width in H\-mode tokamak plasmas, has been validated extensively in type\-I edge\-localized mode \(ELM\) regimes, significant uncertainties remain in predicting the height of the pressure pedestal in fusion pilot plants that must deploy ELM mitigation or suppression techniques\. In this work, we compare the EPED1 NN surrogate to measurements from a broad dataset on the DIII\-D tokamak, spanning ELMy, Small\-ELM, QH\-mode, Wide\-Pedestal QH\-mode, RMP\-suppressed, I\-mode, EDA H\-mode, QCE and ELM\-free NT scenarios\. Using a robust Bayesian profile\-fitting framework, we find that the measured pedestal pressure is systematically reduced relative to the EPED prediction in nearly all regimes, with regime\-median pedestal pressures ranging from ∼93% of the predicted value in H\-mode like regimes to below 40% in scenarios in which the edge region is governed by other transport mechanisms\. We show that this deficit – termed a “pedestal penalty” – is not a fixed per\-regime offset and that some scenarios recover toward the EPED prediction at high normalized pressure \(β N \) and low pedestal collisionality \(ν \* e,ped \)\. While a simple scaling for the pedestal penalty can help illustrate model uncertainties on the DIII\-D database, it misses key scenario\-specific physics and should not be taken as a substitute for the development of predictive pedestal models for ELM\-free FPPs\. Uncertainties in FPP performance associated with a reduction of the pedestal height relative to EPED are quantified using the FUSE code, which shows that the achievable fusion power on ITER may be reduced by a factor of two if the pedestal is limited to 60% of the EPED prediction, a value well within the uncertainties observed on DIII\-D\. Further implications for FPP design are discussed, including the need for regime\-dependent pedestal models that do not rely on a degraded EPED variant\.

## [Legal Evidence–Authority Dissociation in juror judgment: a multistudy reanalysis of memory contamination and AI advice](../publications/612e75b2dc16eb658067.md)

Xiangran Xie

Introduction Legal decision makers may remember information without using it to update a legal judgment, and may respond differently to the same recommendation depending on its attributed source\. LEAD separates these processes into memory\-entry, judgment\-incorporation, and authority\-deference gates\. Methods We reanalyzed three public, de\-identified datasets: one jury\-deliberation misinformation study and two preregistered judge\-versus\-artificial\-intelligence sentencing studies\. We compared gate\-specific estimates while retaining study\-specific outcomes and raw units\. Results In Study 1, pro\-prosecution misinformation crossed the memory\-entry gate more clearly than the judgment\-incorporation gate\. In Studies 2 and 3, mitigating case facts produced larger judgment\-incorporation effects than authority\-source assignment\. The authority\-source effect was equivalent to zero within a prespecified small\-effect bound in Study 2 \(source Experiment 1\), but remained inconclusive in Study 3 \(source Experiment 2\)\. Discussion LEAD identifies which process changed and supports cross\-gate magnitude comparisons without treating unlike outcomes as identical\. This secondary analysis does not estimate behavior in real courts, but it provides a transparent framework for forensic and legal psychology\.

## [Optimization of Waste Recycling Vehicle Routing in Public Health Emergencies](../publications/614017f3b44dd2c56663.md)

Shaoren Wang; Keyi Qian; Jiajia Lin; Linlin Zheng

With the frequent occurrence of public health emergencies such as the COVID\-19 pandemic, the allocation and coordinated use of emergency supplies around the world have generated large amounts of waste, thus creating an urgent need to improve and optimize emergency reverse logistics systems\. This study proposes a model for optimizing waste recycling vehicle routing to address waste management issues\. The model provides ideal transportation solutions for the simultaneous collection of general waste and medical waste\. Based on the characteristics of the model, an artificial intelligence algorithm—i\.e\., an improved genetic algorithm based on bit\-string\-matching coding and a field restriction operator—is designed and compared with an ant colony optimization algorithm\. A synthetic numerical example inspired by the situation in Wuhan, China, is tested using relevant data on the locations of 18 medical facilities mentioned in existing case studies of the COVID\-19 pandemic to verify the effectiveness and practicality of the model and the algorithm\. This study provides support for decision\-making regarding optimization strategies for the reverse logistics of waste generated during public health emergencies\.

## [Research on the Current Status and Influencing Factors of the Digital Transformation of Small and Micro Enterprises in Shanghai](../publications/614666304bfe01cb7441.md)

Yuqing Wu

Enterprise digitalization has become a key measure for enhancing corporate competitiveness and promoting the development of the digital economy\. Drawing on questionnaire survey data, this paper quantitatively evaluates the degree of digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai along multiple dimensions, including industry, development stage, and position in the industrial chain\. On this basis, it constructs an evaluation index system and applies the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process to identify the influencing factors\. The results show that, at the criterion level, the participant factor has the greatest impact on the digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai, followed in descending order by organizational, task, and technological factors; at the indicator level, the factors with the greatest impact are customer satisfaction, strategic planning for digital transformation, market incentives, and information security and risk prevention and control\. Accordingly, this paper puts forward policy recommendations on improving customer satisfaction, refining the market incentive mechanism, attaching greater importance to information security and risk prevention and control, and establishing a multi\-dimensional collaborative support system, with a view to advancing the digital transformation of small and micro enterprises in Shanghai\.

## [A prospective controlled evaluation of winterized Pistacia lentiscus oil nasal spray in vasomotor rhinitis](../publications/614f4b641ae6e8965f79.md)

Alexander Bertuccioli; Annalisa Belli; Davide Sisti; Marco Rocchi; Chiara Maria Palazzi; Matteo Gelardi; Ignazio La Mantia; Veronica Seccia; Simonetta Masieri; Elona Begvarfaj; Amjad Khan; Alberto Macchi

Background Vasomotor rhinitis \(VMR\), currently included within the broader spectrum of non\-allergic rhinopathy, is a chronic condition characterized by nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, and hyperreactivity to non\-specific environmental triggers\. Although traditionally considered a neurovascular disorder driven by autonomic dysregulation, emerging evidence suggests that mucosal inflammatory and microbial factors may contribute to symptom persistence in selected patients\. Winterized Pistacia lentiscus oil has demonstrated antimicrobial and anti\-biofilm properties in upper airway experimental models, suggesting potential therapeutic relevance in chronic nasal disorders\. Methods This prospective controlled study evaluated the effectiveness of a nasal spray medical device containing winterized Pistacia lentiscus oil \(Bactorinol® nasal spray, PharmExtracta S\.p\.A\., Italy\) in patients with VMR\. A total of 120 participants were enrolled, with 110 completing the study \(58 treated, 52 controls\)\. Primary endpoints included changes in Peak Nasal Inspiratory Flow \(PNIF\) and symptom burden assessed using the Sino\-Nasal Outcome Test \(SNOT\-22\)\. Secondary endpoints included nasal cytological assessment of inflammatory cellularity \(neutrophils, eosinophils, mast cells\), bacterial abundance, supranuclear stria, and cytological findings compatible with biofilm\-like structures\. Repeated\-measures General Linear Models were used to evaluate treatment effects over time\. Results Compared with controls, treated patients demonstrated significantly greater clinical improvement over the study period\. SNOT\-22 scores decreased by 30\.5% in the treatment group versus 9\.7% in controls \(time × group interaction, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. PNIF improved by 44\.5% in treated subjects compared with 20\.8% in controls \( p = 0\.006 for interaction\)\. Significant treatment\-associated reductions were also observed for neutrophils \( p = 0\.001\), mast cells \( p = 0\.021\), bacterial abundance \( p = 0\.002\), and cytological findings compatible with biofilm\-like structures \( p = 0\.001\)\. Although the treatment group presented a higher baseline burden for several parameters, post\-treatment outcomes favored the intervention group\. Conclusions Winterized Pistacia lentiscus oil nasal spray was associated with significant improvements in symptoms, nasal airflow, inflammatory cytology, and microbial\-related cytological findings in patients with VMR\. These findings support the hypothesis that selected phenotypes of non\-allergic nasal disease may involve mucosal inflammatory and microbial components beyond classical neurovascular dysfunction\. Larger randomized studies with microbiological and molecular characterization are warranted to confirm these preliminary findings and clarify mechanisms of action\.
