## [ЦИФРОВИЙ ГУМАНІЗМ У КОНТЕКСТІ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ СУЧАСНОЇ ГУМАНІСТИЧНОЇ ДУМКИ: СУТНІСТЬ, ЦІННОСТІ ТА НОВА СУБ’ЄКТНІСТЬ ЛЮДИНИ](../publications/61645ea7c1ed9c11688c.md)

IRINA KOLOMOETS

У статті досліджено філософську сутність цифрового гуманізму як сучасного напряму гуманістичної думки, сформованого під впливом цифрової трансформації суспільства та стрімкого розвитку штучного інтелекту\. Цифровий гуманізм доцільно розглядати як соціальний феномен, який має забезпечити ціннісну орієнтацію розвитку штучного інтелекту та сформувати умови для коеволюції людини й технологій без втрати людської суб’єктності\. Саме це визначає актуальність дослідження та його зв’язок із сучасними науковими завданнями філософської антропології, соціальної філософії, етики технологій, філософії науки і техніки\. Метою статті є концептуалізація цифрового гуманізму як нової філософської парадигми коеволюції людини та штучного інтелекту, визначення її антропологічних, аксіологічних, етичних і соціальних засад та обґрунтування принципів людиноцентричного розвитку інтелектуальних технологій\. Результати досліджень Систематизовано теоретико\-методологічні засади цифрового гуманізму крізь призму взаємодії людини, цифрових технологій, штучного інтелекту та суспільства\. Розкрито філософську сутність цифрового гуманізму, визначено його ключові принципи та ціннісні орієнтири, з’ясовано його місце в сучасній системі гуманітарного, соціального та філософського знання\. Розробдено синергетичну модель цифрового гуманізму як коеволюційної взаємодії людини та штучного інтелекту, спрямованої на формування людиноцентричного, етично відповідального та гуманістично орієнтованого цифрового суспільства\. Встановлено, що ключовою характеристикою нової парадигми є коеволюція людини та ШІ\. Вона передбачає взаємну трансформацію: людина набуває нових цифрових і когнітивних компетентностей, а штучний інтелект розвивається відповідно до суспільних потреб, етичних принципів, правових норм і гуманістичних цінностей\. Трансформація сучасної гуманістичної думки відбувається у напрямі осмислення коеволюції людини і штучного інтелекту як нового етапу розвитку людиноцентричного суспільства\. Цифровий гуманізм розглядає ШІ не як заміну людині, а як технологічного партнера, взаємодія з яким має ґрунтуватися на людській гідності, свободі, відповідальності, довірі та етичних принципах\. Перспективи подальших досліджень полягають у поглибленні теоретико\-методологічних засад цифрового гуманізму; розробленні індикаторів оцінювання рівня людиноцентричності систем штучного інтелекту; розробленні моделей етичного та відповідального ШІ; вивченні феномену когнітивної симбіозності людини та ШІ; визначенні практичних механізмів упровадження принципів цифрового гуманізму в державне управління, освіту, соціальний захист, економіку та процеси повоєнного відновлення України\.

## [Integrating color classification and circularity metrics in wool fabric recycling](../publications/61664348849cad9baee7.md)

Rocco Furferi

This work proposes a methodological framework for circularity\-aware color classification in textile recycling\. The approach combines machine vision data, spectral reflectance information, and process\-related data within a unified architecture\. The main aim is the definition of a circular color sorting index able to link classification outcomes to manufacturing feasibility and environmental impact, particularly in terms of avoided post classification operations\. Unlike traditional performance metrics, the defined index incorporates classification confidence, chromatic proximity, environmental coefficients, and material reuse potential into a single indicator\. The proposed framework is validated on a dataset of recycled wool fabrics representative of typical industrial conditions for companies working with such fabrics\. Despite the experimental results are intended as a proof of concept, this work shows that models optimized for circularity\-aware scoring can achieve substantially improved environmental performance at batch level, even when raw classification accuracy improvements are moderate\.

## [THE INDIVIDUAL, SOCIETY, AND THE STATE IN AN INFORMATION SOCIETY](../publications/61671be45801f6583a9b.md)

Abdullayeva Maryambibi Djumaniyazovna

This article analyzes the transformation of social relations among the individual, society, and the state, as well as emerging social paradigms, within the context of the formation of an information society\. It highlights how the development of digital technologies, artificial intelligence, big data, e\-government, digital education, and social networks is deeply permeating almost every aspect of human life\. While the information society creates new opportunities for individuals regarding learning, communication, creativity, and social engagement, it also gives rise to challenges such as information security issues, digital inequality, personal data protection, information manipulation, and digital dependency\. The study examines the individual&\#x27;s new status within the information environment, changes in the communicative structure of society, and the digital transformation of public administration as interconnected processes\. It also highlights the impact of digital transformation on human interests, social justice, and state\-society relations\. The article substantiates digital literacy, information culture, openness, responsibility, and the safeguarding of human rights as crucial factors for the sustainable development of the information society\.

## [Circular economy for packaging waste: Bridging technological, behavioral, and policy gaps](../publications/616ceaf89ca1c6384580.md)

Mehmet Melikoğlu

This paper provides a comprehensive review of the circular economy for packaging waste, focusing on recent literature from 2020 to 2025\. A systematic methodology was employed to analyze advancements in mechanical and chemical recycling, socio\-economic drivers, and life cycle assessments \(LCA\)\. Key findings highlight the transformative role of artificial intelligence and sensor\-based technologies, which now achieve sorting accuracies frequently around 90–95% for various polymers, with high\-purity material recovery reaching above 98%\. In the realm of chemical recycling, novel catalytic processes are shown to convert non\-recyclable fractions into high\-value outputs, such as syngas with hydrogen content surpassing 70% and upcycled composites with tensile strength improvements exceeding 50%\. Concurrently, behavioral research reveals that consumer engagement is highly sensitive to policy design; specifically, deposit\-refund systems elicit a willingness to pay two to three times higher than traditional fee\-based models\. Environmental assessments via LCA and material flow analysis demonstrate that while mechanical recycling typically offers the lowest global warming potential, potentially reducing greenhouse gas emissions around 350 kg CO 2 \-eq per tonne of waste, chemical pathways offer superior resource conservation in specific scenarios\. The review identifies critical research gaps, including the need for real\-time integrated waste management systems and a global, harmonized framework for impact assessment\. By bridging these technological and behavioral pillars, future research can accelerate the transition toward a resilient circular economy where packaging is treated as a high\-value resource\.

## [Role of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Information, Social Media, and Information Management in Disaster Response: A Case Study of the 2026 Nepal Flood Tragedy](../publications/617d737a2d9fe3b7b66d.md)

Sunil Kumar; Riju Kumari; Swinki Behl

The 2026 Nepal floods are a good example to illustrate the importance of integrating and processing digital information during humanitarian crises\. In this study, we will analyze and assess the roles of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), digital information, social media and information management during the same 2026 floods, and suggest improvements to the disaster management process\. A variety of governmental and nongovernmental materials, peer reviewed journal articles and 300 records of synthetic data were used for this study\. Reliability, correlation, multiple regression and one way analysis of variance \(ANOVA\) were performed\. All constructs had acceptable level of inter\-relations \(alpha = \.783 to \.855\)\. During this study, it was found that the use of Artificial Intelligence \(2026 Nepal floods case = 46\.6%\), digital information \(51\.3%\) and social media \(43\.7%\) improved disaster management process\. Of the three variables, information management showed the highest impact \(28\.7%\)\. Satellite images, drones and digital mapping integrated with humanitarian information became essential to respond to humanitarian crises in Nepal\. Misinformation and fragmented nature of digital information across various platforms challenged responders in Nepal\. The use of Artificial Intelligence during the 2026 floods was also essential\. We recommend the use of integrated digital systems \(six level framework\) during humanitarian crises\. KEYWORDS Artificial intelligence; disaster response; Nepal floods; digital information; social media; information management; crisis informatics

## [CULTIVATING ENGINEERING LITERACY THROUGH A FIVE\-STAGE UP\-IDEA PEDAGOGICAL FRAMEWORK: EVIDENCE FROM A DIGITAL CIRCUIT COURSE REFORM](../publications/618767d52eb279c4626d.md)

Xin Zhang; Xiaoliang Ji; YanXia Xue; Junhua Yang; JingJing Zhou; Li Jiang

Engineering literacy cultivation in foundational engineering courses remains a persistent challenge in higher education\. Traditional approaches often emphasize analytical proficiency over design competence and component knowledge over systems thinking\. This study presents a pedagogical reform aimed at fostering engineering literacy through a five\-stage Up\-IDEA framework in a Digital Circuit and Logic Design course\. The reform was implemented over three years with more than 2,000 students across 13 majors at Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications\. The framework comprises five interdependent stages: Up \(pre\-class design submission\), Inquiry \(problem\-driven classroom engagement\), Design \(software\-based hardware design using Verilog HDL\), Engineering \(case\-based practical application with engineering ethics integration\), and Assess \(multi\-dimensional reflective evaluation\)\. A quasi\-experimental design was employed, triangulating learning platform analytics, questionnaire surveys, and institutional assessment data\. Implementation yielded measurable improvements across three dimensions\. Student engagement significantly increased, with class attendance reaching 98% and homework completion reaching 100%\. Over 80% of students independently resolved more than 70% of pre\-class learning problems, indicating enhanced autonomous learning capacity\. Engineering practice outcomes showed 342 students receiving national or provincial awards in electronic design and FPGA competitions over three years\. Comparative analysis with pre\-reform cohorts indicated improvements in both student participation and design performance\. The Up\-IDEA framework provides a structured approach to integrating engineering literacy cultivation into foundational engineering courses\. The closed\-loop pedagogical cycle — connecting pre\-class preparation, inquiry\-based instruction, design\-oriented learning, practical application, and reflective evaluation — offers a transferable model for comparable engineering education contexts\.

## [Ideal Convergence of Regular Uncertainty Distributions in $L^p$\-Distance](../publications/618ed557a1a0b4e3905b.md)

Ömer Kı̇şı̇; Mehmet Gürdal

Let $1\\leq p&lt;\\infty$\. On the class of regular uncertainty distributions with $p$\-integrable inverse distributions, we consider the $L^p$\-distance between the inverse distributions\. Using the standard quantile representation, we identify the completion of this metric space with the closed cone of almost\-everywhere equivalence classes of nondecreasing functions in $L^p\(0,1\)$ and characterize its relatively compact subsets by uniform $p$\-integrability\. For an admissible ideal $I$ on $N$, the Cauchy criterion for complete metric spaces gives the equivalence of ideal convergence and the ideal Cauchy condition in the completed space\. The classical additive\-property criterion also applies: ideal convergence is realized along a subsequence indexed by some $M \\in\\mathcal F\(I\)$ for every sequence if and only if $I$ has the additive property\. Under uniform $p$\-integrability, convergence in $d\_p$ is equivalent to pointwise ideal convergence of the associated distribution functions at every continuity point\. An endpoint\-concentration example shows that pointwise distributional convergence alone does not imply convergence in $d\_p$\. Finally, expected values satisfy a sharp Lipschitz estimate, and $d\_2$ reduces to the Euclidean distance between the location and scale parameters of normal uncertainty distributions\.

## [INCLUA\-LA: PROTÓTIPO CONCEITUAL DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL E LEARNING ANALYTICS PARA O ACOMPANHAMENTO INCLUSIVO DE UNIVERSITÁRIOS COM TDAH](../publications/6196fa9d7ad48907cd50.md)

Joselene Granja Costa Castro Lima; Simone Romano

Este artigo apresenta o INCLUA\-LA, uma representação prototípica de um Modelo Conceitual Integrado destinado ao acompanhamento educacional inclusivo de trajetórias universitárias, com atenção a possíveis necessidades de apoio observadas entre estudantes com TDAH\. O objetivo é demonstrar como princípios de Inteligência Artificial e Learning Analytics podem ser traduzidos em uma arquitetura de acompanhamento que preserve interpretação contextual, participação humana, proteção de dados e apoio à autorregulação acadêmica\. O estudo adota abordagem qualitativa, natureza aplicada e caráter teórico\-conceitual, derivando de pesquisa bibliográfica e documental\. O protótipo foi elaborado no Figma após a consolidação do modelo conceitual, sem uso de dados acadêmicos reais, testes com usuários ou finalidade diagnóstica\. A representação organiza registros, indicadores longitudinais, sinalizações educacionais, interpretação contextual, apoio personalizado, acompanhamento, revisão e governança\. A análise do protótipo indica que a principal contribuição do protótipo está na separação entre análise e decisão: mudanças observadas podem gerar atenção e diálogo, mas não classificações clínicas nem intervenções automáticas\. Conclui\-se que o INCLUA\-LA constitui uma representação conceitual visual destinada a orientar futuras implementações, cuja validação empírica, usabilidade e eficácia ainda precisam ser investigadas\.

## [EEG\-biometric authentication system using multi\-paradigm neurophysiological measurements and artificial intelligence](../publications/61a4c45192f3bbc40cdb.md)

Chetan Rakshe; P Sriram Kumar; Christy Bobby Thomas; Mohanavelu Kalathe; Vanteemar Sathyanarayana Sreeraj; Ganesan Venkatasubramanian; John Thomas; Yuvaraj Rajamanickam; Deepesh Kumar; Jac Fredo Agastinose Ronickom

Electroencephalography \(EEG\) provides a promising physiological modality for biometric authentication due to its inherent neural uniqueness and resistance to spoofing attacks\. However, reliable EEG\-based authentication remains challenging because brain signals are highly non\-stationary and vary across cognitive states\. To address this limitation, this study proposes a multi\-paradigm neurophysiological measurement protocol designed to capture stable subject\-specific EEG signatures across diverse brain conditions\. EEG signals were recorded from participants during six complementary paradigms, including eyes\-open and eyes\-closed resting states, left and right\-hand motor tasks, working\-memory encoding, steady\-state visual evoked potentials \(SSVEP\), and steady\-state auditory evoked potentials \(SSAEP\)\. The recorded signals were preprocessed and segmented into 2\-s epochs with 50% overlap\. We extracted 28 quantitative descriptors per channel from time, frequency, time\-frequency, and nonlinear domains\. These descriptors were used to evaluate several decision models, including Mahalanobis distance\-based template matching, logistic regression \(LR\), support vector machine, random forest, and a one\-dimensional convolutional neural network\. The performance of the proposed measurement system was analyzed under both single\-paradigm and multi\-paradigm configurations using cross\-session validation\. Experimental results show that the multi\-paradigm measurement protocol reduces the equal error rate \(EER\) by 2% compared with single\-paradigm systems\. The LR decision model achieved the best performance with an EER of 1\.6% \(95% confidence interval: 1\.48−1\.73\), with false rejection rates of 2\.06% and 9\.01% at false acceptance rates of 1% and 0\.1%, respectively\. Feature analysis indicated that Hjorth mobility and Mel\-frequency cepstral coefficients derived from fronto\-central cortical channels provide the most reliable neural identity descriptors\. These results demonstrate that multi\-paradigm EEG acquisition improves the stability of neural measurements across cognitive states and enables reliable biometric authentication in dynamic conditions\.

## [Antioxidant, Anti\-Inflammatory And Neuroprotective Properties Of Bruguiera Sexangula \(Lour\) Poir And Avicennia Officinalis L\. Blume](../publications/61a55ce698984d9906d2.md)



Neurodegenerative diseases have become the greatest challenge in the modern world due to the increase in life expectancy and the lack of effective treatments\.In this context, bioactive compounds like phenols and flavonoids can play a major role due to their pharmacological potential\.The current study investigated the preliminary phytochemical screening, antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities of Bruguiera sexangula \(BSL\) and Avicennia officinalis leaves \(AOL\) methanolic extracts\.DPPH and ABTS scavenging assays were employed to determine the antioxidant activity, and the egg albumin denaturation assay to assess the anti\-inflammatory property\.Further neuroprotective efficiency was evaluated on H2O2\-exposed SH\-SY5Y cells\.The phytochemical screening revealed the presence of different bioactive compounds in both the extracts\.However, BSL extract exhibited comparatively higher antioxidant and anti\-inflammatory activities than AOL due to its higher phenol and flavonoid content\.The pretreatment of BSL and AOL significantly mitigated H2O2\-induced oxidative damage in SH\-SY5Y cells by improving the cell viability and reducing the ROS generation\.This study highlights the promising antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory and neuroprotective role of BSL and AOL\.However, further detailed in vitro investigations are needed to validate their mechanism of action\.

## [Motor action observation evaluation questionnaire: development and initial validity evidence for the scores in people with and without chronic low back pain](../publications/61af55c002b8e2b260c0.md)

Roy La Touche; Prado Silván‐Ferrero; Encarnación Nouvilas\-Pallejà; Alba Paris‐Alemany; Alfonso J\. López\-Rivero; Miguel Ángel Sorrel

Introduction Chronic low back pain \(CLBP\) is highly prevalent and associated with functional limitations\. Although action observation is increasingly used as a cognitive–motor rehabilitation strategy, no brief instrument exists to assess how individuals appraise and understand movements during observation\. Methods The Questionnaire for the Assessment of Motor Action Observation \(CENOAM\) was developed using a sequential mixed\-methods design\. Phase 1 involved item generation based on literature review and qualitative analysis, followed by expert content validation using Aiken’s V \. Phase 2 consisted of a cross\-sectional study including 280 participants \(140 with CLBP and 140 asymptomatic\)\. Dimensionality and psychometric properties of the CENOAM scores were examined using exploratory factor analysis, complementary dimensionality methods, internal consistency \( α , ω \), floor and ceiling effects, concurrent associations, and known\-groups comparisons, following COSMIN recommendations\. Results The final seven\-item instrument showed a parsimonious two\-dimensional structure, comprising Familiarity and Competence–Demand, supported by converging evidence across multiple methods\. Internal consistency was high for both total and subscale scores, and no floor or ceiling effects were observed\. CENOAM scores were positively associated with motor imagery ability, physical activity, and pain self\-efficacy, and negatively associated with fear of movement\. Participants with CLBP showed significantly lower scores than asymptomatic individuals across all dimensions, with large effect sizes\. Conclusion The CENOAM provides a brief and interpretable measure of movement appraisal during action observation\. Its scores show initial evidence of validity and may support the individualization of action\-observation–based rehabilitation in musculoskeletal conditions\.

## [Nested Self\-Similarity as a Created Icon of Perichoresis: Toward an Analogical Structural Isomorphism of the Vestigium Trinitatis in Physical and Mystical Systems](../publications/61c5db18c94d6600179f.md)

Fr Joseph Gee

AbstractClassical dogmatic theology asserts that the created order bears the footprint \(vestigium Trinitatis\) of its Triune Creator \(ex parte creaturae\)\. However, modern dialogues between theology and science often rely on vague, poetic metaphors or superficial triadic associations\. This paper demonstrates a precise analogical structural isomorphism between the Trinitarian dogma of perichoresis—the mutual indwelling and &quot;distinction without separation&quot; of the Three Divine Persons—and the mathematical\-physical phenomenon of nested self\-similarity\. By framing nested self\-similarity as a created icon of divine indwelling, this paper establishes a unified structural grammar linking macro\-cosmic astrophysics \(solar system formation via disks inside disks and exponential distance spacing\), acoustic wave mechanics \(fundamental pitch and integer harmonics\), recursive fractal topology \(V to 0, A to infty\), Thomistic hylomorphism \(Summa Theologiae I, q\. 76\), the interconnection of virtues \(connexio virtutum, ST I\-II, qq\. 65–66\), and Carmelite interior topography \(Nada\-Todo, Stanza 5 of the Spiritual Canticle, and the &quot;deep caverns&quot; of St\. John of the Cross\)\. Preserved by the Analogia Entis and the doctrine of Divine Simplicity \(ST I, qq\. 3 &amp; 13\), this framework offers a rigorous, orthodox, and integrated Christian cosmology\. AI / ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY DECLARATIONIn accordance with emerging academic transparency standards and ecclesiastical guidelines for published scholarship, the author discloses the use of generative artificial intelligence \(LLM\) tools during the preparation of this working paper\. AI technology was utilized strictly in an assistive capacity for structural drafting, cross\-referencing of canonical texts, comparative stylistic refinement, and formatting optimization\. All theological synthesis, canonical interpretations, doctrinal evaluations, and final text selections remain entirely the original work and responsibility of the author\.

## [Bridging the Gap Between Practice and Science: Reflections on the Journey Towards Becoming a Scholar\-Practitioner](../publications/61c99085d8193663aafa.md)

Willem Jan H Roestenburg

The scholar\-practitioner paradigm has become increasingly important in social work as the profession continues to strengthen its commitment to evidence\-based practice \(EBP\) and accountability\. This article reflects on the role of the social work practitioner as both a consumer and producer of knowledge, emphasizing the importance of practice\-based research in narrowing the gap between theory and practice\. Drawing on the author’s three decades of experience as a social work educator, doctoral program coordinator, and mentor to undergraduate and postgraduate students, the article reflects on how practitioners transition toward becoming scholar\-practitioners\. Four developmental phases are proposed: \(1\) the beginning phase, in which practitioners learn to connect theory and practice; \(2\) the discovery phase, characterized by the use of theory and evidence to guide practice decisions; \(3\) the scholar realization phase, where practitioners begin generating and analyzing practice\-based evidence; and \(4\) the practicing scholar phase, in which findings are disseminated through presentations, publications, and broader scholarly engagement\. The article highlights common barriers to practitioner\-led research, including time constraints, organizational limitations, insufficient research training, and uncertainty regarding the implementation of EBP\. It further identifies key characteristics of successful scholar\-practitioners, including methodological competence, data literacy, technological adaptability, writing proficiency, and engagement in mentorship relationships\. The article concludes that strengthening the scholar\-practitioner identity is essential for advancing social work knowledge, improving practice outcomes, and enhancing professional accountability\. Recommendations are offered to promote practitioner\-scholarship through supportive training environments, mentorship opportunities, and dedicated publication platforms that encourage the dissemination of practice\-generated evidence\.

## [Targeting the Mind to Heal the Body: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis of Psychotherapists&\#x27; Work With Medically Unexplained Symptoms](../publications/61ca2625106d2519a569.md)

Lesley A\. Kalish; Maria Luca; Chris A Roe

ABSTRACT Background Medically unexplained symptoms \(MUS\) can present complex challenges in psychotherapeutic practice, occupying an ambiguous space at the intersection of physical suffering and psychological distress\. While MUS are predominantly managed within medical settings, there remains limited qualitative research exploring how psychotherapists understand and work with this client group\. This study contributes to an emerging understanding of MUS as relational and embodied phenomena within psychotherapeutic practice\. Aim The study aimed to explore psychotherapists&\#x27; lived experiences of working with patients presenting with MUS\. Method A qualitative design was used, involving semi‐structured interviews with 14 psychotherapists\. Data were analysed using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis \(IPA\)\. Findings The analysis generated themes relating to embodiment, mind–body integration, developmental adversity, trauma, and the centrality of the therapeutic relationship\. Participants conceptualised MUS as meaningful bodily expressions shaped by relational, emotional and developmental contexts, rather than as symptoms reducible to either psychological or physiological processes alone\. Practitioners frequently linked MUS to trauma, encompassing both acute adverse events and more subtle, cumulative experiences such as emotional invalidation and childhood neglect\. Participants described a form of clinical knowing that developed over time, grounded less in specific techniques and more in an embodied, relational stance\. This stance was characterised by emotional attunement, warmth and a fundamental belief in the reality of the client&\#x27;s pain\. Conclusion and Implications The findings suggest that psychotherapy may provide a valuable context for working with MUS and chronic pain, particularly when clients experience safety, validation and relational depth\. The therapeutic alliance emerged as central to both engagement and perceived therapeutic change, highlighting the potential importance of relational and trauma‐informed approaches when working therapeutically with this population\.

## [Deep Learning\-Based Japanese Speech Recognition for Robust Organizational Knowledge Capture](../publications/61f9786617129988cc0f.md)

Zhiyuan Li

Online Japanese teaching and organizational knowledge management depend on reliable Japanese automatic speech recognition, while existing conformer models perform poorly amid regional dialects, complex phonetics, and background noise\. This paper proposes an improved conformer connectionist temporal classification framework with multi\-scale acoustic feature enhancement, dialect adaptation layers, bidirectional acoustic\-language model fusion, and multi\-task training\. Tests on 800 hours of standard, mixed\-dialect, and noisy speech data and three months of real\-scene deployment show the model improves dialect recognition accuracy by nearly 15% and reduces word error rate by 12% under heavy noise, with only 5 milliseconds longer inference latency than the baseline\. Separate module tests show each design strengthens noise resistance, dialect adaptability, and long\-sentence modeling\. The framework balances accuracy and efficiency, supporting real\-time oral teaching feedback and structured extraction of implicit enterprise knowledge from voice recordings\.

## [Neighborhood built environment and fracture risk among older adults: comparing high versus low clusters](../publications/6204f381f1fd4473f427.md)

Qiaohui Zhou; Riken Homma

Osteoporotic fracture is a leading cause of disability and a major contributor to medical care costs worldwide\. Given that over half of fractures occur outdoors, understanding the relationship between the outdoor environment and fracture risk is essential\. However, few studies have investigated the relationships between built environment and fractures\. No study has explored how built environment attributes relate to fractures across different geographical areas\. In this study, utilizing a five\-year period of fracture data and fine\-grained residential point data, we employed ordinal scan statistics to identify high and low fracture clusters among Japanese older adults\. We then applied a zero\-inflated ordered logit \(ZIOL\) model within each cluster to examine the associations between built environment attributes and fracture occurrence as well as fracture frequency\. As a result, we identified one high and one low fracture clusters\. In the low cluster areas, no significant associations were found between built environment attributes and fracture occurrence as well as fracture frequency\. In contrast, in the high cluster areas, four individual built environment attributes—population density, intersection density, accessibility of bus services, and mix of function—showed statistically significant negative associations with fracture occurrence in their respective models\. Notably, population density was particularly significant\. This research provides valuable insights for developing preventions aimed at promoting active and independent aging by targeting specific neighborhood characteristics\.

## [Intellectual Property in Digital Age](../publications/620883788cc865d36b73.md)

Jayashree Raman

The rapid growth of digital technology has transformed the way ideas, information, and creative works are created, shared, and accessed\. Intellectual Property \(IP\) plays a crucial role in protecting the rights of creators, authors, artists, inventors, and businesses in the digital world\. However, the internet has also increased challenges such as online piracy, copyright infringement, plagiarism, and the unauthorised use of digital content\. Social media platforms, artificial intelligence, and digital marketplaces have further complicated the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights\. This article explores the importance of intellectual property in the digital age and examines the legal challenges associated with protecting original creations online\. It also highlights the role of intellectual property laws in encouraging innovation, creativity, and technological development\. Understanding these rights is essential to maintaining a balance between protecting creators and ensuring public access to knowledge\. Ultimately, effective legal frameworks and responsible digital practices are necessary to safeguard intellectual property in an increasingly interconnected world\.

## [Capacité organisationnelle en intelligence artificielle et qualité de la prise de décision managériale : le rôle médiateur de la prise de décision fondée sur les données](../publications/6214f448d61d0033c18f.md)

Nada RHERIB; Mohamed Charif El HARRANE; Fadoua Anairi; CHENNAOUI Abdelhak; Salaheddine BELFDAIL; Ouissam EL ALAOUI

Chaque fois que l’intelligence artificielle \(IA\) est introduite dans une entreprise, on se demande comment ses capacités peuvent réellement rendre les décisions plus bonnes\. Notre étude cherche à comprendre l’impact de la capacité organisationnelle en IA sur la qualité des décisions managériales, en considérant la prise de décision fondée sur les données \(Data\-Driven Decision\-Making – DDDM\) comme un facteur intermédiaire\. Nous avons utilisé une approche quantitative et envoyé un questionnaire à des cadres, managers, responsables fonctionnels et dirigeants d’entreprises marocaines\. Sur les 274 questionnaires reçus, 171 données valides ont été prises en compte\. Les résultats ont été traités avec SPSS, en vérifiant la fiabilité, en réalisant des analyses factorielles, de corrélation et de régression\. Pour tester l’effet médiateur, nous avons employé la macro PROCESS, modèle 4, avec 5 000 réplications bootstrap\. Les chiffres montrent que la capacité organisationnelle en IA touche positivement la prise de décision fondée sur les données et la qualité des décisions\. De même, la DDDM est liée positivement à la qualité des décisions managériales\. L’analyse de médiation indique un impact indirect positif et significatif de la capacité en IA sur la qualité décisionnelle via la DDDM \(B = 0,3247 ; IC bootstrap à 95 % \[0,2166 ; 0,4498\]\)\. L’effet direct reste significatif \(B = 0,2423 ; p = 0,0034\)\. Ainsi, nos résultats montrent une médiation partielle\. En bref, les avantages de l’IA en matière de décision ne dépendent pas seulement des outils technologiques, mais aussi de la façon dont les organisations utilisent réellement les données dans leurs processus décisionnels\.

## [Country Roads, Take Me to the Polls: Does Youth Voter Turnout Vary Between Urban and Rural Settings?](../publications/621d0db6ec57ab62aaa5.md)

Brent Jamsa

This thesis investigates whether or not urban\-dwelling youth voters in Western democracies possess a universal voter turnout advantage compared to their non\-urban peers\. Utilizing the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems \(CSES\) integrated module dataset that consists of historical election study data from over 230 electoral studies that took place across about 59 jurisdictions between 1996 and 2021, the study employs country and year fixed\-effect logistic regression models with interaction terms to test this relationship\. The results reveal that there is no evidence of a universal voter turnout advantage for urban youth voters\. Rather, it appears that any turnout advantage along the urban/rural divide found in a given country is a result of country\-specific contextual factors\. These findings also suggest that traditional micro\-level factors, such as education, remain the dominant drivers of voter participation across all age cohorts\. Consequently, the thesis concludes by stating that any electoral reforms or get\-out\-the\-vote initiatives must focus on these country\-specific contexts, rather than simply relying on urban density and resources to foster youth electoral participation\.

## [integrating single\-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility profiling to decipher the molecular landscape of Hepatocellular carcinoma](../publications/622f0dc72602d7e8599e.md)

Kaile Pan; Lijian Chen; Yitao Zheng

BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\) is a prevalent and lethal liver malignancy, characterized by high recurrence rates and limited therapeutic options\. Current diagnostic and treatment strategies are hindered by drug resistance and a lack of effective biomarkers for early detection\. METHODS: This study aims to elucidate the role of lactylation and fibroblast cells within the tumor microenvironment \(TME\) of HCC, focusing on their potential as therapeutic targets\. Utilizing a comprehensive multi\-omics approach, we integrated single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\) and single\-cell ATAC sequencing \(scATAC\-seq\) data from public databases \(GEO, TCGA\) to explore transcriptional and epigenetic landscapes at single\-cell resolution\. RESULTS: Our analysis identified fibroblast cells as key players with high lactylation\-related pathway activity, and CREB1 as a central transcription factor regulating lactylation\-associated genes in these cells\. The CREB1 regulatory network was associated with specific immune cell infiltration patterns, drug sensitivity profiles, and enrichment in critical signaling pathways such as Chemokine, TNF, NF\-κB, and EMT\. These findings underscore the pivotal role of lactylation\-driven epigenetic regulation in fibroblasts, influencing the HCC immune microenvironment and disease progression\.

## [THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL\-METHODOLOGICAL COMPETENCE OF PROSPECTIVE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ADA](../publications/623367885015561b232d.md)

Jo&\#x27;rayevna Qarshiyeva Sharifa

The digital transformation of higher education necessitates the reconsideration of approaches to preparing prospective English language teachers\. In this context, the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and adaptive learning technologies represents a promising direction for developing professional\-methodological competence, enabling future educators to design learner\-centred instruction, differentiate educational content, analyse learning progress, and select appropriate pedagogical strategies\. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of competence development through the integration of AI\-supported tools and adaptive learning environments\. It synthesises competence\-based, learner\-centred, constructivist, and technology\-enhanced learning approaches to establish a conceptual framework for teacher preparation\. The proposed framework comprises five interrelated components: motivational and value\-based, cognitive, technological, operational\-methodological, and reflective\-evaluative\. Particular attention is given to the relationship between AI literacy, pedagogical decision\-making, adaptive instructional design, and professional reflection\. A phased methodological model is proposed, encompassing diagnostic assessment, personalised learning, AI\-supported methodological practice, teaching simulation, and reflective evaluation\. The article also addresses ethical considerations, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, academic integrity, and the importance of maintaining teacher autonomy\. The findings provide a theoretical basis for designing university\-level teacher education programmes that respond to the demands of digital transformation\.

## [From Moralizing to Textual Mechanization: The Trajectory of Efferent Reduction and Aesthetic Erosion in Teaching Folkloric Texts](../publications/62407b813a2f3401c1f8.md)

Syamsul Maarif; Zulfa Fahmy; Citra Rizky Lestari

This study investigates how 48 folktales from the official textbooks of Indonesian subjects at the elementary through high school levels are presented, as well as the reductions that occur as a result of pedagogical processes\. Focusing on text reduction and its evaluation, the main objective of this study is to test the application of Bloom’s cognition taxonomy and pedagogical reduction through the framework of transactional reading theory\. Research data were collected by documenting folktale texts from official textbooks and processed using Pedagogical Critical Discourse Analysis\. The findings of this study indicate a shift toward reduction\. From moralizing at the elementary school level, continuing to structural mechanization at the junior high school level, and leading to pragmatic functionalism at the high school level\. All three consistently destroy aesthetic experiences and perpetuate efferent attitudes in reading folktale\. This study argues that learning a folktale using an efferent approach is not the most appropriate\. Folktale should be taught aesthetically, rather than efferently\. This aesthetic treatment will perpetuate the folktale as indigenous knowledge\.

## [Driving forces of contemporary wildfire severity in the American Southwest: a remote sensing and machine learning case study in Arizona, USA](../publications/6245b7a902e68839ff98.md)

Helen Mills Poulos; Sarah Hardy; Jenna Lynne Otaola; Andrew  Marder Barton

As climate change continues to intensify atmospheric moisture demand across the American Southwest, predicting where wildfires cause severe vegetation mortality remains a major challenge\. New thermal and optical harmonized satellite products provide emerging opportunities for evaluating how pre\-fire vegetation moisture and water stress influence fire severity compared to other variables\. We modeled continuous Relativized differenced Normalized Burn Ratio \(RdNBR\) for 45 wildfires that burned in the 2019 and 2020 fire seasons using random forest to compare Harmonized Landsat–Sentinel\-2 vegetation indices, ECOSTRESS \(ECOsystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station\) evapotranspiration and evaporative\-stress metrics, Daymet pre\-fire weather variables, LANDFIRE fuels attributes, and topographic predictors across five cumulative pre\-ignition windows from 1 week to 3 months before ignition\. Despite exceptional drought and anomalous fire\-weather conditions, low\-severity fire was common over the study period\. Integrated models outperformed individual product\-family models, indicating that fire severity was best explained by combined antecedent weather, terrain, fuels, vegetation type, and vegetation\-moisture predictors\. Temperature, elevation, solar radiation, vapor pressure, and HLS Normalized Difference Moisture Index \(NDMI\) were among the most consistent predictors\. NDMI was the most consistent HLS plant\-moisture metric, but vegetation moisture alone did not explain fire severity\. Canopy cover was also important in woodlands and forests\. Models using data from shorter pre\-ignition windows outperformed longer pre\-fire window models\. They varied in performance among vegetation types, with the strongest vegetation\-specific performance in forests and woodlands\. These findings show that emerging high\-resolution satellite products can help characterize pre\-fire vegetation conditions and improve fire\-risk assessments, especially when integrated with short\-term antecedent weather, landscape moisture, and terrain data\.

## [A lightweight knowledge distillation framework for few shot unsupervised industrial surface anomaly detection and localization](../publications/62528b97ec84e6314569.md)

Xian Gao

Abstract Industrial surface anomaly detection under data\-scarce, unsupervised conditions requires models that are both label\-efficient and computationally lightweight\. This paper presents LKDF\-AD, a knowledge\-distillation framework combining a frozen pretrained teacher with a compact student network \(385,168 parameters\), trained using only k = 1–10 normal reference images per category, without any labeled anomalies\. Evaluated across 15 MVTec AD categories and five shot counts, the framework achieves 77\.88–86\.19% image\-level and 90\.59–94\.87% pixel\-level AUROC, and generalizes to the independent BTAD benchmark \(73\.6–90\.99% image\-level AUROC\), with a larger BTAD pixel\-AUROC/PRO gap flagged as an open question\. Measured end\-to\-end \(teacher plus student together, as deployed\), the framework uses 1\.93× fewer parameters \(11\.56 M vs\. 22\.35 M\) and achieves 1\.57× lower inference latency \(4\.436 ms vs\. 6\.954 ms\) than a full\-size STFPM\-style baseline trained under an identical protocol\. Under category\-level paired testing \(using 15 independent category means, the statistically appropriate unit given repeated measurements across shot counts\), neither the image\-level nor the pixel\-level advantage over STFPM reaches statistical significance \(two\-sided p = 0\.7197 and p = 0\.188, respectively\)\. Consequently, the framework’s established advantage over STFPM is its directly measured computational efficiency \(1\.93× fewer end\-to\-end parameters, 1\.57× lower end\-to\-end latency\), rather than accuracy\. In contrast, against the RegAD\-inspired baseline, both accuracy advantages remain highly significant under the same corrected test \(two\-sided p = 0\.00201 for image\-level and p = 0\.00153 for pixel\-level\)\. A random, completely untrained student achieves only near\-chance performance \(52\.7% image\-level, 46\.6% pixel\-level AUROC\), confirming that the observed localization signal reflects genuine distillation rather than an architectural artifact\. A dedicated investigation of the framework’s weakest category \(screw, near\-chance performance\) tested a rotation\-sensitivity hypothesis directly across the full test set; the result was a significant correlation in the direction opposite to that hypothesized, and we report the mechanism as unresolved rather than settled\. These results position the framework as a genuinely lightweight, empirically characterized — rather than definitively superior — approach to few\-shot unsupervised industrial anomaly detection\.

## [CALM\-MER: Calibrated Alignment and Latent Modality\-conflict Modelling for Multimodal Emotion Recognition with a Released Audio\-visual Congruence Benchmark](../publications/62535fe4e1be01876a84.md)

Mamta Goyal; Vivek Srivastava

Audio\-visual emotion recognition systems are increasingly deployed in affective\-computing and clinicalcommunication settings, yet their reliability collapses precisely when the face and the voice disagree, and that failure is rarely quantified against an independent ground truth\.Existing conflict\-aware fusion methods estimate disagreement from their own unimodal probes, which is circular, and report point estimates without calibration, statistical testing or a reproducible artefact\.This paper introduces CALM\-MER, a three\-stage framework that self\-supervisedly aligns frozen contrastive predictive coding speech tokens and ConvNeXt\-V2 facial tokens through an InfoNCE objective, estimates modality conflict with a dual\-source prior fusing probe disagreement with a newly collected human\-rated audio\-visual congruence signal, and routes fusion through a Beta\-distributed uncertainty gate calibrated by temperature scaling\.It releases IEMOCAP\-AVCongruence, an independent congaruence annotation over 5,531 utterances rated by three annotators at an average\-measures ICC\(2,k\) = 0\.75\.Under one immutable evaluation script and five seeds it attains 80\.9% weighted and 81\.4% unweighted accuracy on six\-class IEMOCAP and 67\.2% macro\-F1 on six\-label CMU\-MOSEI, at an expected calibration error of 0\.029 and a Brier score of 0\.071, exceeding eight external audiovisual\-only baselines \-a naive\-concatenation reference, three systems reimplemented from their published descriptions and four adapted to this protocol \-together with an internal fixed\-gate ablation of CALM\-MER, giving nine comparators evaluated under one identical protocol and one scoring script\.Under McNemar&\#x27;s exact test with Holm\-Bonferroni correction over the nine comparators, seven of the eight external baseline comparisons reach a corrected p &lt; 0\.01 and the comparison with the strongest baseline, SADGR\-AV, reaches a corrected p &lt; 0\.05; the internal fixed\-gate ablation also reaches a corrected p &lt; 0\.01\.Conflict supervision is out\-of\-fold and speakerindependent, one mandatory inference configuration never reads a human rating, and the full artefact is released at https://github\.com/mamtagp/Calmmer\_code\.

## [Multifocal Glioblastoma Managed With Primary Temozolomide as a Strategy to Delay Radiation Therapy: Clinical and Radiological Outcomes](../publications/625fb6283a4fbd9f39c1.md)

Chun Khai Loh; Helen Wheeler; Adrian Lee; Matthew Wong; Malmaruha Arasaratnam; Nicola Cove; Marina Kastelan; Michael Back

AIM: To evaluate the clinical and radiological outcomes of upfront temozolomide \(TMZ\) monotherapy in deferring radiotherapy for multifocal glioblastoma \(GBM\)\. METHODS: We analysed 18 consecutive adult patients with newly diagnosed, multifocal GBM treated with upfront TMZ monotherapy between 2016 and 2024\. The primary endpoint was a 6\-month progression\-free survival \(PFS\)\. Secondary endpoints were overall survival \(OS\) and radiological tumor response\. RESULTS: The median age of the cohort was 69 years\. The median follow\-up was 12 months\. Thirteen \(72\.2%\) patients had O⁶\-methylguanine\-DNA methyltransferase \(MGMT\)\-methylated tumors\. Bi\-hemispheric disease was present in 16 patients \(88\.9%\) at baseline\. Patients received a median of six TMZ cycles\. Disease relapse occurred in 94\.4% \(n = 17\) of cases, with 47\.0% of failures involving distant sites\. The 6\-month PFS was 61% \(95% CI: 42\.3%\-88\.3%\), and the median OS was 12\.2 months \(95% CI: 11\.2\-31\.1\)\. MGMT\-methylated tumors demonstrated a significant volumetric reduction at 3 months compared to unmethylated cases \(median \-34\.2% vs\. \+114\.0%; p = 0\.007\)\. Survival outcomes trended in favour of the methylated cohort \(6\-month PFS 69\.2% vs\. 40\.0%; median OS 12\.3 vs\. 11\.2 months\), though these associations did not reach statistical significance \(p = 0\.480\)\. CONCLUSION: This study provides valuable insights into the use of primary TMZ as an exploratory strategy for short\-term modulation in highly selected patients with extensive multifocal GBM\. Whilst this approach facilitates a strategic delay in large\-volume radiation, the high relapse rate underscores that upfront TMZ serves as a temporary window for deferring neurotoxicity rather than achieving durable disease control\.

## [Bridging design disciplines: a literature review of biologically\-inspired design, human\-centered design, and human\-robot interaction](../publications/62600847c323afffeb9d.md)

Daniel Whitman; Deeksha Seth

Abstract As robotic technologies become more integrated into society, there is a growing demand for systems that are not only technically robust, but also socially accepted, safe, and designed for long\-term use\. Biologically\-Inspired Design \(BID\), Human\-Centered Design \(HCD\), and Human\-Robot Interaction \(HRI\) each offer valuable theories, methodologies, and tools to support the design and evaluation of such systems\. Despite their complementary goals, these fields have largely developed in isolation\. The lack of integration across BID, HCD, and HRI presents significant barriers for researchers and designers seeking to create biologically\-informed, human\-centered robots that facilitate meaningful interactions\. In this work, an integrative literature review was conducted to examine the fields of BID, HCD, and HRI\. An analytic categorization approach was used to categorize 63 papers into one or more of the three fields: 20 in BID, 27 in HCD, and 21 in HRI, with some papers categorized into multiple categories\. Within each field, an inductive, interpretive coding and thematic analysis were used to identify key terminology, tools, methods, and conceptual frameworks, helping establish a shared vocabulary and summarize the state of the art\. This was followed by a synthesis of limitations and field\-specific gaps\. Cross\-field analysis revealed only four papers demonstrating overlap within the reviewed corpus: three showing implicit connections between HCD and HRI, and one showing implicit overlap between BID and HRI with indirect ties to HCD\. This review lays the groundwork for more integrated design research by identifying opportunities for collaboration across BID, HCD, and HRI, highlighting the potential for more biologically\-informed, user\-centered, and socially responsive robotic systems\.

## [Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug\-and\-Play Networks](../publications/6266bc887d7953a2e384.md)

Danilo Saccani; Leonardo Massai; Giancarlo Ferrari\-Trecate

We address the problem of improving the performance of pre\-stabilized networked systems subject to plug\-and\-play \(PnP\) operations, namely additions or removals of subsystems\. While distributed baseline controllers can preserve stability after a PnP transition, augmenting them with expressive neural policies can invalidate the formal stability guarantees\. To overcome this issue, we build on recently proposed Performance Boosting controllers based on the Internal Model Control \(IMC\) principle, which reduce closed\-loop stability to a finite $\\ell\_2$\-gain requirement on an auxiliary operator\. In the distributed setting, this operator is formed by interconnecting local neural operators that exchange information only between neighboring subsystems\. We then derive free parametrizations of this interconnection, namely explicit maps from unconstrained trainable variables to interconnected neural operators satisfying a prescribed network gain bound for every parameter value\. The obtained distributed neural controller can therefore be trained by unconstrained gradient\-based optimization without stability constraints or projection steps, while retaining the prescribed gain bound at every training iterate\. We develop two complementary parametrizations\. A neighbor\-based compositional parametrization uses local coupling bounds, so that after a PnP event only subsystems whose bounds change need to update their gain parameters\. A network\-norm parametrization instead uses a bound on the overall coupling matrix and can reduce conservatism, at the price of requiring network\-wide information\. A PnP DC\-microgrid case study shows that the proposed neural layer improves voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed\-loop stability\.

## [Promises and Problems of Paediatric Digital Radiography in Nigeria: A Commentary](../publications/62874df2880e0e0181fd.md)

Flavious Bobuin Nkubli

Abstract Background: Advances in paediatric digital radiography promise improved image quality and enhanced patient radiation protection\. However, clinical challenges including overexposures, underexposures, and suboptimal image quality persist despite the availability of proven technical interventions\. Consequently, a critical gap remains in translating these safety standards into routine clinical practice within developing healthcare systems\. Objective: To explore the dual realities of promises and operational challenges in paediatric digital radiography within the Nigerian context, and to articulate the imperative for adopting implementation research frameworks\. Methods and Materials: A comprehensive review of current literature, quality improvement guidelines, and diagnostic reference paradigms was synthesized alongside anecdotal clinical evidence from the Nigerian radiographic setting to identify systemic execution bottlenecks\. Results: While efficacious interventions and safety guidelines exist internationally to ensure paediatric radiation protection, contemporary evidence in Nigeria reveals a rising burden of unintentional radiation exposure and &quot;dose creep\.&quot; Implementation research offers the necessary methodologies to design, test, and sustain context\-specific implementation strategies, directly bridging the gap between established radiation protocols and real\-world clinical compliance\. Conclusion: Promising paediatric radiation protection interventions fail to deliver intended outcomes in Nigeria due to contextual implementation barriers\. Embracing implementation research is imperative to design practical strategies that safeguard vulnerable paediatric populations\. Keywords: paediatric radiography; digital radiography; implementation research; radiation protection; dose creep\.

## [Evaluating cytokine\-based therapeutics in human 3D in vitro immune\-containing assembloids](../publications/628bce005f6cc4c89748.md)

Nina Maenhoudt; Mechthild Lütge; Melanie Obenloch; Aljona Caironi; Maria Kiratzis; Pol Jean\-Mairet; SAMUELE GRAZIANO; Philipp Fröbel; Tamara Hüsser; Emilio Yángüez; Maria Antsiferova; Adrian M\. Filip; Christian Müller; Stéphane Leclair; Stephan Gasser; Pablo Umaña; Sara Colombetti; Floriana Cremasco; Samuele Calabrό

Introduction Cancer immunotherapies require accurate preclinical models that recapitulate the complex cellular interactions within the human tumor microenvironment\. While patient\-derived organoids have emerged as powerful tools for cancer research, standard cultures lack the stromal and immune compartments necessary to evaluate immunotherapeutic mechanisms\. This limitation hampers the development of next\-generation targeted cytokine therapies\. Methods We applied a 3D immune\-containing colorectal cancer assembloid platform integrating patient\-derived organoids, cancer\-associated fibroblasts and allogeneic peripheral blood mononuclear cells within a collagen matrix\. We characterized cellular responses to interferon\-gamma \(IFNg\) and engineered IFNg receptor agonists targeted to fibroblast activation protein \(FAP\) through single\-cell transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, cytokine profiling, and functional T\-cell migration assays\. Results The assembloid model successfully recapitulated key features of IFNg signaling, including tissue growth suppression, enhanced chemokine secretion \(CXCL10\), and CD8 \+ T\-cell recruitment\. Single\-cell transcriptomics revealed that fibroblasts were the most responsive cell population, undergoing a phenotypic transition from myofibroblasts toward antigen\-presenting CAFs \(apCAFs\), characterized by robust upregulation of MHC class II genes\. FAP\-targeted IFNg molecules exhibited attenuated activity compared to recombinant IFNg, successfully avoiding upregulation of the severe immunosuppressive checkpoint molecule PD\-L1\. Discussion This 3D assembloid model provides a physiologically relevant platform for dissecting complex tumor\-immune interactions and optimizing targeted immunotherapies\. This approach enables the study of epithelial\-stromal\-immune crosstalk in cancer and offers a robust preclinical framework for screening and mechanistically validating next\-generation targeted cytokine therapies\.

## [School\-Based Executive Function Guideline \(SB\-EFG\): A Practice Guideline for Executive Function Assessment and Intervention in School\-Based Practice](../publications/62950fcc56ca393eb417.md)

Ida Koraitem; Amanda Sarafian; Lenin C\. Grajo

Executive functioning \(EF\) is comprised of various cognitive skills, such as working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility, which monitor and guide goal\-directed behavior and set a foundation on which healthy development may occur\. Although the impact of EF skills on school participation has increasingly been recognized over the years, there are limited occupational therapy models that help occupational therapists integrate EF intervention into school\-based practice\. Children with limitations in EF have unique needs and challenges that impact school participation; therefore, it is imperative that occupational therapists address EF in school\-based practice\. This author\- developed practice guideline discusses essential elements of assessment and intervention that school\-based occupational therapists should consider when working with students with EF limitations\. The essential elements are displayed as a conceptual model that provides a comprehensive understanding of how to use and apply evidence\-based EF strategies to enhance student school performance\. The goal of this model is to also guide school\-based therapists on how to widen their practice lens and develop clinical capacity to address EF skills that will, in turn, enhance student school participation\.

## [Optimal approximation of smooth functions by ReLU neural networks](../publications/62960d665b8fab936bd8.md)

Thomas Nagler

We study uniform approximation of the Hölder ball $\\mathcal H\_1^s\(\[0,1\]^D\)$ by fully connected ReLU networks\. Except in the one\-dimensional Lipschitz case, existing constructions remain separated from the information\-theoretic efficiency limit\. This article closes the gap for every $s&gt;0$ and $D\\ge1$: networks with width $O\(N\)$, depth $O\(L\)$, and parameter magnitude $O\(1\)$ attain uniform approximation error of order $\(N^2L^2\\log N\)^\{\-s/D\}$\. No relation between width and depth is required\. The construction uses new encoding and decoding mechanisms that exploit higher\-order finite\-difference bounds for local Taylor coefficients of the target function\. As a statistical consequence, empirical risk minimizers over the corresponding clipped network classes attain the minimax regression rate $n^\{\-2s/\(2s\+D\)\}$ without additional logarithmic factors\. The paper also gives a detailed exposition of the key approximation techniques, covering both established and new mechanisms\.

## [Expert intuition vs\. Algorithmic clustering: Mapping radiological subtypes in pulmonary sarcoidosis](../publications/62a50975eaba042d87a9.md)

Justyna M\. Sobczak; Adam Jerzy Białas; Joanna Miłkowska\-Dymanowska; Łukasz Gwadera; Patryk Sobczak; Katarzyna Torbiarczyk; Piotr Łacwik; Wojciech Jerzy Piotrowski

BACKGROUND: Pulmonary sarcoidosis is a heterogeneous granulomatous disease with a broad spectrum of clinical and radiological manifestations\. While the traditional Scadding classification based on chest radiography remains a cornerstone of disease staging, it provides limited information regarding parenchymal involvement and poorly correlates with functional impairment\. High\-resolution computed tomography \(HRCT\) offers superior sensitivity in detecting subtle and early interstitial changes, yet standardized HRCT\-based classification systems for sarcoidosis remain underdeveloped\. AIM: This study aimed to propose and validate a novel HRCT\-based classification of pulmonary sarcoidosis grounded in expert consensus, to assess its relationship with clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and quality of life, and to compare it with data\-driven radiological groupings obtained through cluster analysis\. METHODS: The study population included patients with confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis managed at a tertiary referral center, either as inpatients or outpatients\. HRCT scans were evaluated using a modified version of the previously published questionnaire, capturing 22 radiological features per lung lobe\. Based on characteristic imaging patterns, four expert\-defined subtypes were proposed: \(1\) Lymphonodal, \(2\) Disseminated\-Nodular, \(3\) Central, and \(4\) Fibrotic\. Symptom burden was assessed using the Fatigue Assessment Scale \(FAS\) and the Sarcoidosis Health Questionnaire \(SHQ\)\. Spirometric and gas transfer parameters \(FEV1, FVC, TL,CO\) were recorded\. Statistical analyses included ANOVA, Spearman&\#x27;s correlation, and hierarchical clustering \(Ward&\#x27;s method with Euclidean distances\), with Cohen&\#x27;s kappa used to evaluate concordance between classification systems\. RESULTS: Four distinct HRCT subtypes were identified through expert assessment, each reflecting varying degrees and distributions of parenchymal involvement\. These subtypes differed significantly in clinical and functional presentation\. The fibrotic subtype demonstrated the most severe functional impairment, with the highest prevalence of abnormal spirometry and diffusion deficits\. In contrast, the lymphonodal subtype exhibited preserved lung function and minimal symptomatology\. The Van den Heuvel radiological severity score showed strong correlation with radiological subtype and was significantly associated with FEV1, FVC, TL,CO, and SHQ scores\. Unsupervised cluster analysis independently identified four data\-driven radiological groups that partially overlapped with expert\-defined subtypes, particularly in nodular and central patterns\. However, the fibrotic subtype showed less distinct clustering, underscoring its radiological complexity\. The agreement between expert\-defined and cluster\-derived classifications was limited \(κ = 0\.271\), suggesting that the two approaches capture complementary but distinct dimensions of disease morphology\. CONCLUSIONS: HRCT\-based radiological subtypes of pulmonary sarcoidosis reflect clinically meaningful differences in symptom burden, ventilatory function, and radiological severity\. While expert\-driven and data\-driven classifications show limited concordance, both provide valuable insights into disease heterogeneity\. Radiological phenotyping using HRCT may serve as a practical adjunct to traditional staging systems, offering improved risk stratification and guiding personalized treatment decisions\. Further prospective validation is needed to determine its utility in routine clinical practice and to explore its integration with emerging clinical and molecular phenotyping strategies\.

## [Case Report: Beyond the initial diagnosis: a case of Wilson&\#x27;s disease presenting as acute decompensated cirrhosis](../publications/62b30ab12d7f92d6e33b.md)

Aun Ali Bangash; Muhammad Ali Bangash; Chloe Cheree Harris; Veronica L O&\#x27;Brien; Learsi De Hoyos; Jose Campo Maldonado

Wilson disease is a rare inherited disorder of copper metabolism that can cause progressive hepatic injury, cirrhosis, and, in severe cases, acute liver failure\. Its variable presentation can overlap with more common causes of liver disease and delay recognition\. We present a 28\-year\-old patient with one week of worsening jaundice, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, and marked hyperbilirubinemia\. Given a history of heavy alcohol use and a Maddrey Discriminant Function score of 73, severe alcohol\-associated hepatitis was initially suspected\. However, several months of reported alcohol abstinence, a strong maternal family history of early\-onset cirrhosis, imaging evidence of established portal hypertension, and the severity of hepatic dysfunction prompted broader evaluation\. Testing demonstrated low ceruloplasmin and elevated 24\-h urinary copper, while autoimmune and viral testing was unrevealing\. The overall clinical evaluation favored Wilson disease\. During the hospitalization, suspected hepatorenal syndrome was managed with albumin, midodrine, and octreotide; portal\-hypertensive ascites required paracentesis; and trientine plus zinc were prescribed as disease\-specific therapy while transplant evaluation was pursued\. Renal function improved, but severe liver disease persisted, and the patient was transferred to a transplant center for further evaluation\. Long\-term follow\-up after transfer was unavailable\. This case highlights the need to maintain a broad differential diagnosis in young adults with acute decompensation of chronic liver disease and to distinguish clinical diagnostic confidence from the degree of objective Wilson disease confirmation achieved during the index hospitalization\.

## [Vibration amplification mechanism and theoretical mitigation strategy for feedwater flow meter brackets in nuclear power plants](../publications/62b3537c6cdbf6993d25.md)

Shiliang Jiang; Bo Gu; Shuai Wang; Bo Zhao; Yaofei Li

Excessive low\-frequency vibration can impair the reliability of safety\-class instruments in nuclear power plants\. This study investigates vibration amplification in a feedwater flow meter bracket mounted on a steel grating platform in Unit 4\. Field tests showed that the 10–50 Hz band contributed more than 56\.1% of the mean\-square acceleration at the transmitter and valve\-group panels\. An equivalent cantilever\-beam model and a single\-degree\-of\-freedom isolation model guided the retrofit\. The design combined local reinforcement, a 250 mm reduction in effective cantilever length, and BE\-40 rubber vibration isolators\. Finite element response trends, laboratory tests, and field measurements all showed lower dynamic responses after the retrofit\. The overall vibration acceleration level at the transmitter decreased by 18\.4–26\.4 dB over 10 Hz\-8 kHz and met the applicable NB/T 25,081–2018 criterion\. These results provide a practicable design route for mitigating vibration in lightweight instrument brackets mounted on flexible support platforms\.
