## [Postpandemic Social Contact Patterns: A Cross\-Sectional Survey in Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam](../publications/62c47e688133ca12eb2e.md)

June Young Chun; Yunseop Shin; Yongdai Kim; Shinya Tsuzuki

INTRODUCTION: Social contact patterns are one of the key determinants of infectious disease transmission, but post\-coronavirus disease 2019 \(COVID\-19\)\-pandemic evidence from East and Southeast Asia remains limited\. We examined age\-specific contact patterns in Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam and assessed whether contact frequencies had returned to prepandemic levels\. METHODS: We conducted online, single\-day contact surveys in 2025 using quota sampling by age and sex\. Participants reported contacts on the preceding day, defined as physical contact or direct conversations of at least three sentences held within 2 m\. Age\-specific contact matrices were constructed for weekdays and weekends and combined using a 5:2 weighting\. Factors associated with daily contact counts were examined using negative binomial regression\. RESULTS: The analysis used data from 10,279 individuals: 8,080 in Japan, 1,102 in South Korea, 589 in Thailand, and 508 in Vietnam\. Mean daily contact counts were 8\.1, 6\.2, 6\.4, and 8\.8, respectively; medians were 4, 4, 4, and 6, respectively\. All four countries showed age\-assortative mixing, although assortativity was less pronounced in Thailand and Vietnam\. In Japan and South Korea, younger age and larger household size were associated with more contacts, whereas greater mask\-wearing tendency was associated with more contacts in Japan and fewer contacts in South Korea\. Compared with available historical estimates, contact frequencies in Japan and South Korea remained below prepandemic levels\. Sparse baseline data and methodological differences precluded firm conclusions being made for Thailand and Vietnam\. CONCLUSIONS: Contact frequencies in Japan and South Korea remained below prepandemic levels in 2025, suggesting persistent postpandemic changes in mixing behavior\. Evidence for comparable changes in Thailand and Vietnam was inconclusive\. Future surveys should collect setting\-specific information, in addition to contact frequency and age, to clarify how changes in work, education, and household interaction shape postpandemic social mixing patterns\.

## [INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL EN LA PRÁCTICA DOCENTE: PERCEPCIONES Y USOS PEDAGÓGICOS EN LA NIVELACIÓN DE LA UNIVERSIDAD NACIONAL DE CHIMBORAZO](../publications/62c69daf27f5e87eb478.md)

Alexander Larrea; Santiago Baldeon; Melanny Guevara; Samantha Ruiz; María Heras

El Acelerado avance de la inteligencia artificial \(IA\) en el ámbito académico de tercer nivel impone desafíos y oportunidades para la gestión académica y el diseño pedagógico de los docentes y estudiantes\. La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo general caracterizar las percepciones, los usos pedagógicos y la eficiencia percibida de la IA en los docentes que imparten los cursos de nivelación de la Universidad Nacional de Chimborazo \(UNACH\)\. Se empleó un enfoque cuantitativo con un diseño no experimental, orientado en el método empírico analítico, aplicando un cuestionario estructurado en 3 bloques\. Bloque I: Datos demográficos y perfil profesional; Bloque II: Percepciones y actitudes ético \- pedagógicas; Bloque III: Usos pedagógicos y eficiencia didáctica\. Los reactivos del cuestionario fueron estrictamente evaluados por profesionales en las áreas de: Innovación Educativa, Metodología de la Investigación Científica, y Tecnologías de la Información y Comunicación, para así, aplicarlo a la totalidad de los docentes del área N=94\. Los resultados evidencian una alta percepción de utilidad pedagógica tanto en la dimensión de creación de recursos didácticos \(lecturas, resúmenes, casos de estudio, cuestionarios, etc\.\) 47, %, y la planificación de clases o guías didácticas 40,4%\. Además, Un hallazgo determinante radica en la Asunción de un rol docente guiado por la revisión crítica de los contenidos generados por la IA, garantizando la supervisión pedagógica y descartando que la herramienta vulnere la objetividad educativa \(86,96%\)\. Se concluye que existe una adopción ética y proactiva de la inteligencia artificial por iniciativa autónoma del profesorado, la cual requiere ser respaldada por políticas institucionales de capacitación continua y modelos de alfabetización digital en la educación superior\.

## [Revisiting Identification Thresholds of Specific Learning Disorders \( SLD \) in Gifted Children \( GC \)\. A Comparison of Three Groups: Twice‐Exceptional \( TE \) Children, GC Without SLD and Non‐ GC With SLD](../publications/62c748b295602376b34a.md)

Laurent Lesecq; Laurent Querné; Julie Gornes; Laura Buffo; Louise Corbel; Loïse Perrais; Maëlys Kartner; A\.G\. Le Moing; Béatrice Bourdin; Patrick C\. Berquin

This study investigates assessment of Specific Learning Disorders \(SLD\) in Twice\-Exceptional \(TE\) children, gifted children \(GC\) who also present SLD, in oral and written language domains\. Applying the standard threshold for identification \(&lt; 7th percentile\) to GC often results in the assessment and identification of SLD in the TE population, thereby limiting access to appropriate support\. The objective was to determine which language tests effectively identify SLD in TE children and establish optimal threshold values\. The prospective study included 301 children 7\-16 years, divided into three groups: GC without SLD \(n = 71\), TE children \(n = 114\), and non\-gifted children with SLD \(n = 116\)\. Language test performances were compared across groups, and Classification and Regression Tree \(CART\) analyses were employed to optimize test sensitivity and specificity in the TE group\. TE children performed better than the SLD group but worse than GC without disorders\. At standard thresholds, text reading and spelling tests showed the highest sensitivity, which significantly improved when CART\-derived decision thresholds \(62nd and 38th percentiles\) were applied, while maintaining satisfactory specificity\. Results indicate that standard thresholds lead to under\-identification of SLD in GC, and that adjusted thresholds enhance identification accuracy\. These findings should generalize to similarly complex languages, such as English\.

## [Multi\-feature Response Attention Network for kidney stone detection and measurement of stone size in ultrasound images](../publications/62da119bc12384700aab.md)

Vijaya Padmanabha; Mohamed Sirajudeen Yoosuf; Anand Mahendran; Joseph Mani; Anisha Prima Rodrigues; Gururaj Bijur; Hothefa Shaker Jassim

Kidney stones are hard deposits formed in the urinary tract due to excess waste and low fluid intake, causing severe abdominal pain\. Ultrasound\-based kidney stone detection involves identifying and locating stones in the kidneys using high\-frequency sound waves to visualize renal structures\. Measuring stone size is crucial for early treatment and preventing infection\. However, detection is challenging because ultrasound images suffer from noise, lower contrast, and variable quality\. To overcome these limitations, the Multi\-feature Response Attention Network \(MFRANet\) is proposed to detect kidney stones\. Initially, the input image is allowed for image denoising and edge preservation using Windowed Variation Kernel Wiener Filter \(WV\-KWF\)\. Further, the kidney region is segmented by the Fuzzy Clustering algorithm with Variable Multi\-pixel Fitting spatial information \(FCM\-VMF\)\. Moreover, descriptor computation is processed by rotated Binary Robust Independent Elementary Feature \(rBRIEF\) with Discrete Cosine Transform \(DCT\)\. Afterwards, the kidney stone is detected using MFRANet, wherein MFRANet is designed by combining Multi\-feature Multi\-Attention Network \(MFMANet\), along with Group Response Attention Network \(GRA\-Net\)\. Next, the detected stone is segmented using Optimized DA\-TransUNet \(O\-DAT\), and lastly, the kidney stone size is measured\. Performance of the proposed MFRANet is assessed with Accuracy, F1\-score, Precision, and True Positive Rate \(TPR\) which achieved superior values of 96\.64%, 96\.65%, 97\.44%, 95\.88% Response Attention Network, Multi\-feature Multi\-Attention Network, Optimized DA\-TransUNet\.

## [CHATGPT КАО ДИГИТАЛНИ САПУТНИК У УЧЕЊУ НЕМАЧКОГ ЈЕЗИКА: АУТОЕТНОГРАФСКА СТУДИЈА СЛУЧАЈА](../publications/62eea2cc69cdecf90d11.md)

Татјана Грујић

Овај рад истражује потенцијале и ограничења употребе ChatGPT\-а као допун ског дигиталног алата у самосталном учењу немачког језика на почетном нивоу \(А1\.1\)\. Ис траживање је засновано на аутоетнографској студији случаја, у којој ауторка истовремено делује у улози ученика – корисника уџбеника Schritte international Neu A1\.1 и ChatGPT\-а – и у улози истраживача који систематски анализира писане интеракције настале током процеса учења\. Прикупљени транскрипти обрађени су квалитативном садржинском анализом, уз фокус на лингвистичку тачност одговора, њихову примереност нивоу А1, дидактичку вредност, као и потенцијалне ризике које модел може представљати за апсо лутне почетнике\. Резултати показују да ChatGPT може бити користан у областима које се ослањају на јасна и структурирана правила, као што су основна граматика, почетни вокабулар и моделовање писане продукције\. Алат пружа јасна објашњења, контекстуали зоване примере и једноставне дијалоге који могу подржати развој комуникативне компе тенције\. Ипак, анализом је утврђено да се јављају значајне недоследности у превођењу на српски језик, стварању неправилних или хибридних лексичких јединица и задацима који подразумевају логичко повезивање информација, што представља ризик за почетнике који немају довољно језичког предзнања да уоче грешке\. Закључак истраживања указује на то да ChatGPT не може да функционише као поуздан језички модел у процесу учења страног језика на најнижим нивоима, али може имати значајну улогу као допунски алат у контексту индивидуализованог и аутономног учења\. његова употреба захтева критичко преиспитивање генерисаних садржаја и, по могућству, педагошко усмеравање како би се оптимално искористиле предности модела, а истовремено избегле потенцијалне заблуде у учењу\.

## [Machine Unlearning: Techniques, Challenges, Evaluation, Applications, and Future Directions](../publications/62f8eedc9db01678c004.md)

Akshat Kumawat; Balraj; Vishal Shrivastava; Akhil Pandey

Abstract—The widespread deployment of deep neural networks and foundation models has introduced acute legal, operational, and ethical challenges regarding data privacy and algorithmic accountability\. Regulatory mandates, notably the European Union General Data Protection Regulation \(GDPR Article 17 &quot;Right to be Forgotten&quot;\) and the California Consumer Privacy Act \(CCPA\), legally obligate data controllers to purge personal records upon individual request\. However, physical data deletion from storage disks fails to sanitize trained models: gradient optimization permanently embeds training data signatures into overparameterized weights\. While complete model retraining from scratch on retained data provides exact statistical revocation, its prohibitive computational, financial, and environmental costs render it intractable for modern architectures and streaming deletion requests\. To overcome this bottleneck, Machine Unlearning has emerged as a fundamental discipline in trustworthy artificial intelligence, aiming to excise the influence of designated training subsets without compromising general model utility on retained data\. This paper presents an academically rigorous, comprehensive survey of machine unlearning\. We mathematically formalize the unlearning problem under Empirical Risk Minimization \(ERM\), classify paradigms into exact, approximate, and certified regimes, and establish an exhaustive taxonomy spanning data\-partitioning \(SISA\), gradient inversion, influence functions, knowledge distillation, parameter\-saliency pruning, certified differential perturbations, federated unlearning, and autoregressive Large Language Models \(LLMs\)\. We examine multi\-dimensional evaluation suites—including membership inference attacks \(MIA\), loss distribution divergence, and relearning susceptibility protocols—while systematically contrasting unlearning with differential privacy and model editing\. Finally, we analyze critical vulnerabilities and outline thirteen structured future research directions for verifiable unlearning systems\.

## [Age\-related differences in the mental health burden among Ukrainians during war and forced migration](../publications/631daabb00fdd8436f8b.md)

Larysa Spitsyna

Introduction Our study focuses on the effects of the stressors of modern conditions of martial law and forced displacement on the state and mental health of Ukrainians adult\. The aim of our study is to analyze the state of mental health and wellbeing of Ukrainians during war and forced migration compared, namely to determine the level of the most common mental health problems \- depression, anxiety and post\-traumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\), as well as resources for overcoming the consequences of stressful influences\. Method We developed a conceptual model of the components of mental health and wellbeing, which became the basis for the development of an online questionnaire on the LimeSurvey platform, with using the PTSD Checklist for DSM\-5 \(PCL\-5\), the Life Events Checklist for DSM\-5 \(LEC\-5\), the Refugee Post\-Migration Stress Scale \(RPMS\), the Brief Symptom Inventory Derogatis \(BSI\-18\), block of open\-ended socio\-demographic issues, and SPSS Statistics 21\.0\. Results The sample comprised 306 Ukrainian participants\. Participants were grouped by age: under 26 years and 26 years or older; and place of residence: 1\) “lives in another country;” 2\) “lives in Ukraine, moved;” 3\) “lives in Ukraine, did not move\.” Differences in symptom scores were observed between subgroups, with the smallest subgroup interpreted cautiously\. Among Ukrainian people affected by armed conflicts and migrants, the most common mental disorders \(CMDs\), such as depression, anxiety disorders and post\-traumatic stress disorder, constitute a significant proportion of serious illnesses worldwide\. The results obtained in our study confirm this trend also among Ukrainians, who are currently experiencing all the difficulties of wartime\. Discussion The findings provide a descriptive comparison of psychological symptoms and perceived coping resources across different age and residential groups of Ukrainians adult in the condition of war\. Resource\-oriented to mental health assessment and intervention for war\-affected populations is important, contributing to understanding adaptive functioning in the context of protracted armed conflict and may nevertheless inform future research and support planning for war\-affected populations\.

## [Knowledge Structure and Evolution of Industrial Heritage Digitalization: A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis Using CiteSpace and AI\-Assisted Methods](../publications/631fc66a00cbc10d7a6b.md)

Feng Wang; Haoyu Yang; Yuting Yin; Zilin Zhou

Industrial heritage digitalization increasingly connects documentation, conservation, adaptive reuse, regeneration, and heritage management, yet its interdisciplinary terminology complicates systematic characterization of the field\. This study examines the knowledge structure and evolution of industrial heritage digitalization by applying CiteSpace\-based and artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted bibliometric analyses to the same literature samples\. A total of 431 publications from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure \(CNKI; n = 260\) and Web of Science Core Collection \(WoSCC; n = 171\) were analyzed separately\. The two approaches examined corresponding dimensions of keyword prominence and relationships, thematic structure, and temporal evolution, with their outputs compared in terms of substantive correspondence rather than numerical equivalence\. The findings indicate that industrial heritage digitalization has expanded from documentation and geometric representation toward the wider use of digital information in conservation, adaptive reuse, regeneration, and management\. The two approaches showed broad correspondence in keyword prominence, major network nodes, major thematic domains, and overall temporal evolution, whereas specific network relationships, thematic organization, and temporal signals were only partially consistent\. Such correspondence indicates convergence across analytical procedures rather than validation against an external ground truth\. Differences between the two representations were associated with terminology processing, network construction, clustering, and temporal indicators rather than semantic processing alone\. Overall, the findings indicate increasing integration of digital information across heritage functions and spatial scales and emphasize the importance of information continuity across conservation and adaptive\-reuse processes\. Methodologically, researcher\-supervised large language model \(LLM\)\-assisted semantic processing can complement established science\-mapping approaches when combined with transparent and reproducible analytical procedures\.

## [Beyond Mean Absolute Error: Ancestry\-Stratified Calibration and Explainability for Warfarin Dosing Models](../publications/632a58ca416c3eee080e.md)

Hassan Barmandah; Omar A\. Bawazir; Siraj Aldeen Marghalani; Muath Shaat; Abdullah Alkattan; Mariam M\. AlEissa

Background: Warfarin’s narrow therapeutic index requires precise dose individualization, yet published machine\-learning studies report accuracy that is inversely correlated with evaluation rigor: the field’s best\-reported mean absolute error \(MAE\) comes from an unreliably small test set\. Methods: We present a reproducible, nine\-phase ML pipeline on the public International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium \(IWPC\) dataset \(n=6037 and n=1780\) with fixed patient\-level splits, strict leakage controls, and a nested clinical/genetic ablation across nine architectures\. Results: AutoGluon with combined features achieves MAE =8\.55 mg/week, R2=0\.475, PW20 \(percentage of predictions within 20% of the true dose\) =0\.466 on the larger cohort \(MAE =7\.96, R2=0\.480, PW20 =0\.497 on the smaller\), exceeding prior rigorous benchmarks\. A leave\-one\-ancestry\-group\-out evaluation, cross\-checked across two model families, reproduces only part of an earlier analysis’s known error concentration in Black/African\-American patients: the Black label shows no penalty under either model, while Han Chinese and Caucasian show model\-dependent penalties\. A deep ensemble is badly miscalibrated \(24\.9%/21\.6% coverage of a nominal 90% interval\), while MAPIE \(Model Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator\) conformal prediction on the same model achieves near\-nominal coverage \(89\.8%/93\.3%\); per\-ancestry coverage shows every Black/African\-American label under\-covered, a fairness gap the aggregate number hides\. On IWPC\-1780, SHAP \(SHapley Additive exPlanations\) attributes 64% of feature importance to genetics, confirming VKORC1 as the strongest predictor\. Conclusions: To our knowledge, no previously published pipeline evaluated on the IWPC dataset jointly reports accuracy, ancestry\-stratified fairness, calibration, and explainability on the same fixed splits\.

## [Insomnia and medication overuse headache: neurobiological links, reciprocal interactions, and integrated therapeutic strategies](../publications/632b383d2864317b8982.md)

Ervin Michelstaedter Cotrik; Abouch Valenty Krymchantowski; Carla Jevoux; Isabela Caldas Ferreira; Leila Monteiro Auler; Maria Carolina Ferreira Fontoura Sousa; Ana Paula Marcussi

Medication overuse headache \(MOH\) and insomnia are not merely coincidental companions: each measurably worsens the severity and treatment response of the other\. Whether this association reflects a genuine reciprocal influence, a shared constitutional vulnerability, or some combination of both carries direct practical consequences for clinical decision\-making\. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from Mendelian randomization genetics, polysomnographic cohort studies, pharmacological withdrawal trials, and mechanistic neurobiology, based on a search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar through 20 June 2026\. Genetic analyses are compatible with a directional association between insomnia liability and migraine risk, although causation is not established and the instruments capture migraine broadly rather than the MOH phenotype, a limitation that applies to all causal inferences in this review\. In the other direction, opioids, barbiturates, and triptans each disrupt sleep architecture through mechanisms specific to their molecular targets, and questionnaire\-based withdrawal studies consistently report parallel improvements in sleep quality and headache frequency\. Three neurobiological substrates appear centrally involved: orexinergic dysregulation, melatonin suppression, and glial neuroinflammation\. Together, they may sustain a self\-reinforcing cycle that neither detoxification alone nor sleep treatment alone can fully dismantle\. The COMISA phenotype \(comorbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea\) and concurrent psychiatric illness compound treatment resistance and raise relapse rates at one year\. Objective polysomnographic evidence that sleep architecture actually recovers after drug withdrawal is absent from the literature — a gap that limits the mechanistic conclusions that can be drawn\. The available evidence is consistent with the hypothesis that concurrent medication withdrawal, CBT\-I, preventive pharmacotherapy — including anti\-CGRP monoclonal antibodies — and CPAP where indicated may yield better outcomes than sequential management, but this hypothesis has not been tested in a randomized controlled trial\. Designing that trial is the most pressing research need in this field\.

## [Exploring Graduate Students’ Perspectives of Clinical Supervision in Speech\-Language Pathology: A Qualitative Study of Facilitators and Barriers](../publications/6348caf66277500cb92f.md)

Andrew J Clare; Joyce Maring

This qualitative study explored second\-year graduate students’ perceptions of clinical supervision practices in Speech\-Language Pathology \(SLP\), focusing on how specific aspects of the supervisory approach were experienced by students as either barriers or facilitators to their learning during clinical practicum experiences\. Twenty graduate students from a single SLP program, each with experience in at least seven clinical practica, participated in semi\-structured interviews\. An inductive thematic analysis approach was used to examine the patterns in the students’ experiences\. Two mirrored sets of themes emerged, reflecting the dual importance of relational and pedagogical aspects of supervision\. Facilitators included supportive relationships and effective instructional scaffolding, whereas barriers involved strained interpersonal dynamics and instructional shortcomings\. Participant responses highlighted varied preferences and revealed the importance of adaptive, individualized supervision strategies\. The findings underscore the need for supervision practices that are both pedagogically sound and relationally responsive\. These insights contribute to the emerging evidence base for effective SLP supervision and offer practical implications for supervisor training and clinical education program development\.

## [The Influence of the Role of Peer Presence on Game‐Based Chemistry Learning: Evidence From EEG](../publications/6353db313bba2c09e1e3.md)

Qian Huangfu; Yujia Guo; Tingting Deng; 黃志方

ABSTRACT Background Game‐based learning \(GBL\) has become an important way to innovate chemistry teaching\. However, it is still unclear how different peer roles in GBL shape learners&\#x27; learning outcomes and cognitive processes\. Objectives The study examined how different peer roles \(individual vs\. collaborators vs\. competitors\) influence learners&\#x27; outcomes in game‐based chemistry learning\. It also examined differences in theta and alpha power across these conditions\. Methods The study employed a between‐subjects design with 69 ninth‐grade students from a secondary school in China who had not yet learned the target chemical concepts\. Students were randomly assigned to individual, collaborative or competitive learning\. Outcome measurement included immediate and delayed testing, motivation, cognitive load, interest and electroencephalography \(EEG\)‐based alpha and theta power\. Results and Conclusions Both the collaborative and competitive conditions showed higher learning performance and interest than the individual condition\. The collaborative condition also showed higher motivation than both the competitive and individual conditions and higher cognitive load than the individual condition\. EEG analyses showed that the collaborative condition elicited higher theta and alpha power than the individual condition across both phases, although differences from the competitive condition were not consistently significant\. These patterns may reflect greater demands on cognitive control and selective processing during collaborative learning\. Implications The findings highlight the value of collaborative peer roles in game‐based chemistry learning\. Teachers may consider incorporating structured collaborative activities to promote students&\#x27; engagement and cognitive involvement\. The findings also suggest that different peer roles may serve distinct motivational functions, which may inform the design of GBL activities\.

## [The Use of Artificial Intelligence to Reduce Teacher Workload: Opportunities and Limitations](../publications/6363eb2e6025c39093bb.md)

Karina Tairova

This conceptual note examines the use of artificial intelligence as a tool for reducing teacher workload\. It focuses on the difference between task automation and actual workload reduction, emphasizing the need to consider the complete teacher workflow, including checking, correction, adaptation, formatting, and source verification\. The paper argues that AI tools should be evaluated not only by generation speed, but by whether they reduce the total amount of teacher effort required to produce a reliable and usable educational result\.

## [Semana internacional relatoría científica opción de grado – diplomado internacional en dirección estratégica e innovación organizacional 2026](../publications/636b794e1ea039b573d6.md)

## [PFOCUS study protocol: a prospective case–control study investigating genetic, haemodynamic, and platelet function in migraine with aura with or without patent foramen ovale](../publications/636ce0d3a478e9ee8a75.md)

Matteo Paolucci; Giacomo Urbinati; Ludovica Migliaccio; Alice Marucci; Valentina Favoni; Davide Mascarella; Flavia Palombo; Valério Carelli; Mario Sebastiani; Silvia Stagni; Rita Mancini; Sabina Cevoli; Andrea Zini

Background Migraine with aura \(MA\) is associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke, particularly in young individuals without conventional vascular risk factors\. A growing body of evidence indicates a strong association between MA and patent foramen ovale \(PFO\), the prevalence of which is up to three times higher in patients with MA than in the general population\. The mechanisms underlying this association remain incompletely understood and are likely to extend beyond paradoxical embolism\. Methods and design PFOCUS is a prospective, monocentric, observational case–control study designed to investigate the genetic, neurosonological, and hematological determinants linking MA and PFO\. Specifically, the study evaluates whether genetic variants, particularly within the Notch signaling pathway, contribute to the coexistence of PFO and MA, and whether these patients display distinct cerebrovascular and prothrombotic profiles\. As exploratory aims, the study will assess whether aura phenotypes and the distribution of MRI lesions are associated with different haemodynamic and prothrombotic profiles, potentially identifying clinically relevant subgroups within MA\. A total of 240 patients with MA will be enrolled and classified as right\-to\-left shunt \(RLS\)\-positive or RLS\-negative on the basis of contrast\-enhanced transcranial Doppler \(TCD\), used as a surrogate marker of PFO\. Participants will undergo comprehensive phenotyping including genetic testing by whole\-exome sequencing, neurosonological assessment of right\-to\-left shunt, cerebral microemboli detection, dynamic cerebral autoregulation and cerebral vasomotor reactivity \(VMR\), and platelet function testing\. The primary endpoint is the difference in the frequency of NOTCH3 gene variants between groups\. Secondary endpoints include associations with other panel genes, correlation with shunt size, and differences in haemodynamic and platelet function parameters\. ClinicalTrials\.gov : NCT07349004\. Discussion PFOCUS aims to identify a biologically distinct phenotype of MA associated with PFO, potentially driven by genetic predisposition and vascular dysfunction\. Its findings may inform stroke risk stratification and open new avenues for personalized preventive strategies in patients with MA\. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials\.gov , identifier NCT07349004 \( https://clinicaltrials\.gov/study/NCT07349004 \)\.

## [Does climate adaptation policy deliver a health dividend? Exposure, modeled health burden, and defensive capacity in China&\#x27;s climate\-adaptive city pilots](../publications/636e72091c94e3721f12.md)

Cun Wang; Hantao Gong

Climate policy is widely expected to yield a health dividend: cleaner air can improve health without a simultaneous expansion of defensive capacity\. We distinguish exposure reduction from defensive adaptation in China&\#x27;s 2017 climate\-adaptive city pilot, using a 2011–2022 panel of 264 cities, including 21 treated units\. A difference\-in\-differences design examines fine particulate matter \(PM2\.5\) exposure, while the Global Exposure Mortality Model translates exposure into modeled pollution\-related health burden\. Physicians, hospital beds, and employee\-insurance enrolment measure selected defensive inputs\. The pilot is associated with a 3\.87 μg/m 3 lower PM2\.5 \(95% confidence interval −6\.49 to −1\.25; wild\-bootstrap P = 0\.0067\)\. The estimate remains negative after pollution\-convergence adjustments but is smaller and imprecise in the matched sample\. The central accounting model implies an approximately 8\.10% lower burden \(conditional 95% confidence interval −11\.32 to −4\.76%\), not an observed mortality reduction\. Average capacity estimates are imprecise and cannot establish the absence of defensive adaptation\. A physician\-based coupling calibration admits positive and negative contributions and cannot bound the total defensive response\. Among nine pre\-policy capacity interactions, telecommunications intensity is positively associated with bed expansion \(\+4\.40 per 10,000 residents; pointwise 95% confidence interval 2\.47–6\.32; adjusted P = 0\.021\), although pre\-trend concerns limit causal interpretation\. Other interactions remain uncertain\. The main estimate is close to an illustrative detection threshold, warranting caution with non\-significant findings\. The results support an exposure\-related health co\-benefit under explicit accounting assumptions\. Assessment incentives, coordination, and financing are possible explanations for uneven responses, but their roles are not identified by these estimates\.

## [REIMAGINING MARKETING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CASE STUDIES AND MANAGERIAL INSIGHTS](../publications/636f3750bf9b6d3fd774.md)

Shruti Shukla; Gurudutta Japee

This document explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in marketing, emphasizing its widespread adoption across businesses of all sizes and the complexities involved in its implementation, such as data privacy concerns and algorithmic bias\. The research methodology involves a detailed analysis of real\-world case studies from diverse industries, examining how organizations utilize AI\-powered tools like machine learning and predictive analytics to enhance customer engagement and optimize marketing strategies\. The conclusion highlights AI&\#x27;s potential to create personalized experiences and automate processes, while also stressing the importance of addressing ethical challenges and maintaining consumer trust\. It calls for the development of strategies that effectively leverage AI capabilities while prioritizing ethical considerations, and suggests future research directions focused on the long\-term impacts of AI on customer loyalty and best practices for integrating AI technologies into existing marketing frameworks\.

## [Combined effects of video self\-modeling and preferred music on motor skill acquisition and psychological engagement in adolescent shot\-put learning](../publications/637ae38e4096f85b4def.md)

Manar Boujabli; Nidhal Jebabli; Safaa Mostafa Ali Elkholi; Marouen Souaifi; Hamdi Chtourou; Wissem Dhahbi

This exploratory cluster\-randomized pilot study investigated the individual and combined effects of Video Self\-Modeling \(VSM\) and preferred music during warm\-up on physical, technical, and psychological performance following a nine\-week shot\-put learning program in secondary school students\. Eighty students, nested within four intact classes, were allocated to four conditions at the class level \(one class per condition\): neutral self\-talk with no music \(control\), VSM only, preferred music only \(PM\), and combined VSM plus preferred music \(CVSMPM\)\. Shot\-put distance, technical execution, rating of perceived exertion, feeling scale, and situational motivation \(SIMS\) were assessed\. Physical performance improved significantly in all groups\. Because randomization occurred at the class level with a single class per condition, intervention and class\-level effects cannot be statistically separated; results are reported as descriptive contrasts\. Descriptive contrast analysis showed medium\-to\-large effect\-size differences favoring the combined intervention over control on physical and technical performance at formative \(0\.79 &lt; d &lt; 1\.50\) and summative assessments \(0\.62 &lt; d &lt; 1\.32\)\. Feeling\-scale scores increased with large\-to\-very\-large effects in CVSMPM and PM \(1\.34 &lt; d &lt; 2\.02\), and situational motivation improved with medium\-to\-large effects in CVSMPM \(0\.87 &lt; d &lt; 1\.69\) and PM \(0\.79 &lt; d &lt; 1\.21\)\. CVSMPM showed the most consistent pattern of medium\-to\-large effect\-size differences in motor skill acquisition, technical proficiency, and psychological engagement relative to the other conditions\. Given the cluster design and exploratory analyses, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis\-generating\.

## [Perceived Readiness for Artificial Intelligence Enabled Auditing in Power Equipment Procurement at Guangxi Electric Power Vocational and Technical College](../publications/63855da50e76f08e954a.md)

Yan Chen; Pattama Yimsakul

The research objectives were 1\) to explore stakeholders’ perceptions of the key enabling conditions associated with the applicability of AI\-enabled auditing in power equipment procurement, and 2\) to explore experts’ perspectives on the applicability and expected governance contributions of AI\-enabled auditing in power equipment procurement\. The sample consisted of 255 respondents involved in equipment procurement, auditing, management, and utilization at Guangxi Electric Power Vocational and Technical College and three experts who participated in the focus group discussion\. The instruments used were a structured questionnaire and a semi\-structured focus group discussion guide\. The quantitative data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, and standard deviation, and the qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis\. The findings revealed that 1\) stakeholders perceived the five key enabling conditions at an overall high level \(M = 3\.70, S\.D\. = 0\.77\); Data Quality received the highest evaluation, while Auditor Competency received the lowest evaluation and was at a moderate level, indicating a particular need for AI\-related professional development, and 2\) the experts perceived AI\-enabled auditing as applicable to transaction analysis, supplier evaluation, document review, risk identification, compliance monitoring, audit\-efficiency improvement, education cost control, and asset\-lifecycle management, provided that implementation is gradual, supported by reliable data and infrastructure, and subject to professional oversight and institutional governance\.

## [The hidden costs of technological change: investigating pathways through which highly automatable jobs undermine workers’ health in Germany](../publications/638693f161cd424fea0f.md)

Mariia Vasiakina; Christian Dudel

The ongoing economic transformation driven by automation has significant social implications, particularly for the health and well\-being of workers who face the risk of job displacement and the pressure to acquire new skills and qualifications\. However, the specific pathways through which exposure to automation risk affects health outcomes remain poorly understood, and the relative contribution of each potential mechanism is still unclear\. In this study, we examine the nature of the relationship between high workplace exposure to automation risk and a range of subjective health outcomes – including self\-reported health, anxiety, and both physical and mental component summary scores from the SF\-12 Health Survey – among workers in Germany\. Using data from the German Socio\-Economic Panel \(SOEP\) linked with administrative records from the Occupational Panel for Germany \(2014–2022\), we apply the Karlson\-Holm\-Breen \(KHB\) mediation analysis method to assess whether broader indicators of economic uncertainty, alongside automation\-specific factors, mediate the relationship between high automation risk and workers’ health\. Our results indicate that the negative impact of high automation risk on health in Germany primarily operates through indirect pathways \(related to mediators\) for both genders, with the exception of physical health among male workers, where a direct negative effect is also evident\. Economic concerns – particularly job insecurity and worries about one’s future financial situation – emerge as more significant mediators than automation\-specific factors\. Overall, our findings suggest that the mechanisms linking high automation risk to health are gender\- and context\-sensitive, and are shaped by broader economic conditions and workplace environments\.
