## [Measuring fraud potential in the context of crop insurance: honesty among smallholder coffee farmers in Latin America](../publications/639fc297b3b563025396.md)

Hannah Miller; Oliver Mußhoff; Daniel Hermann

Purpose Honesty plays an important role in insurance fraud as a potential result of moral hazard\. Knowing the honesty of policyholders can give insights into the risk of fraudulent behavior and costs of an insurance product\. The purpose of this study is to measure honesty in a context inspired by an agricultural crop insurance case\. Design/methodology/approach We conduct a lab\-in\-the\-field experiment among coffee farmers in Colombia and Peru to elicit farmers&\#x27; honesty\. The experiment is a contextualized version of the die\-roll task, in which numbers on the die are replaced by pictures of coffee trees\. Findings On average, 3\.8% of the participants lie in the experiment\. Lying \(reporting a higher payoff\) is not frequent for pictures with high\-yielding coffee trees, although these are associated with the lowest payoff\. Potential reasons for the heterogeneity of honesty levels are the contextualization of the experiment, gender and culture\. Research limitations/implications Our contextualized experiment is a step towards increased external validity of honesty research\. Future research can build on our approach by designing the experiment even closer to an insurance situation or another real\-world economic context\. Social implications Effective insurance solutions are crucial for farmers to manage the multitude of risks they face\. Estimating honesty in a contextualized insurance setting can help insurance companies and policy makers to design better and more effective insurance solutions for farmers\. Originality/value To the best of our knowledge, our study is the first using a contextualized honesty task to measure potential dishonesty in a context inspired by an agricultural crop insurance case\.

## [Implementation of Digital Marketing and Web Analytics Solutions in a Small Enterprise: A Case Study](../publications/63a9c7371db42040d410.md)

Tjaša Morandel Kangler

Digitalni marketing in spletna analitika predstavljata pomemben del sodobnega poslovanja, vendar njuna učinkovita uporaba za mala podjetja zaradi omejenih kadrovskih, časovnih in finančnih virov predstavlja poseben izziv\. V magistrskem delu je obravnavano uvajanje rešitev digitalnega marketinga in spletne analitike na primeru malega podjetja\. Analiza je zajela spletno mesto in spletno trgovino podjetja, prisotnost na družbenih omrežjih, spletno oglaševanje ter uporabo spletne analitike\. Rezultati kažejo, da ima podjetje vzpostavljene pomembne digitalne kanale ter dobro organsko in lokalno spletno prisotnost, vendar posamezne aktivnosti niso celovito povezane in sistematično spremljane\. Obstoječa ureditev spletne analitike zato ne omogoča celovitega spremljanja uporabniške poti od prvega stika z digitalnim kanalom do povpraševanja, neposrednega kontakta oziroma spletnega nakupa\. Na podlagi ugotovitev so bile opredeljene rešitve za izboljšanje spletnih okolij, optimizacijo za spletne iskalnike, spletno oglaševanje, družbena omrežja in druge digitalne aktivnosti ter za nadaljnji razvoj spletne analitike\. Raziskava kaže, da je za malo podjetje pomembnejše od uvajanja številnih novih digitalnih kanalov njihovo načrtno povezovanje, prilagajanje značilnostim podjetja in njegovim kupcem ter sistematično spremljanje rezultatov\.

## [Language management in the age of LLMs: AI tools in proofreading as emerging norm authorities?](../publications/63adc849688f34f77f15.md)

Vít Dovalil; Adriana Hanulíková

Who decides what counts as “correct” or standard language today? Correcting language has always been an act of authority\. This authority seems now to be quietly shifting toward large language models \(LLMs\), because they are routinely consulted for proofreading in educational, academic, and professional contexts, valued for the apparent ease with which they produce standardized, well\-formed texts\. However, which linguistic norm these models draw on when “correcting” language remains underexplored\. This is a critical issue, because less linguistically informed users are more likely to accept AI\-generated corrections uncritically\. In this paper, we examine such corrections and argue that treating LLMs as de facto norm authorities with regard to standard language is premature\. We first rethink standard language as a sociolinguistic concept that is negotiated among linguists, norm authorities, model speakers/writers, and codifiers \(authors of dictionaries, grammars etc\.\) rather than a fixed property of a language\. We then illustrate LLMs&\#x27; performance in proofreading empirically, by submitting a German text containing 13 targeted morphosyntactic phenomena for grammar correction to six LLMs \(eight model configurations\) at three time points\. Expectedly, results show variability both between and within models over time, as well as some consistency and several discrepancies with codification and model texts\. LLMs, we conclude, may be reasonably reliable for some morphosyntactic variables, and they could be treated as an autonomous norm authority if they can be shown to draw transparently on knowledge codified by reliable sources\.

## [A Three\-Layer Formative Feedback Framework for Kit\-Build Concept Mapping: Feasibility Evidence from Three Classroom Trials](../publications/63ae1226fe3e9a72bd0a.md)

Putra Prima Arhandi; Banni Satria Andoko; Nurmaya; Aryo Pinandito; Tsukasa Hirashima

Kit\-Build Concept Mapping \(KBCM\) supports formative assessment by externalizing learning goals as a teacher reference map and diagnosing proposition\-level gaps through automated comparison\. However, typical KBCM use provides mainly verification feedback \(what is missing/incorrect\) and offers limited support for how students should act to close those gaps\. Leveraging KBCM’s diagnostic outputs as an enabling infrastructure, this study proposes and implements a three\-layer formative feedback framework that operationalizes structured gap\-closing actions: \(Layer 1\) Evidence Access links each frequently missing proposition to specific source\-text evidence; \(Layer 2\) Comprehension Verification prompts learners to articulate the reasoning behind the proposition through guided questioning; and \(Layer 3\) Integration Practice requires coordinated application of multiple propositions in authentic problem\-solving tasks\. We report three classroom trials with undergraduate informatics students \(N = 11, N = 10, N = 10\)\. Across all trials, large overall learning gains were observed from post\-reading \(T1\) to post\-intervention \(T3\) \(Wilcoxon r =\.895,\.878,\.889; all $$p &lt;0\.05$$ \)\. The magnitude of additional improvement beyond KBCM diagnostics differed by content complexity\. These findings suggest that KBCM\-based diagnosis can be systematically transformed into progressive, pedagogically grounded feedback that supports students’ gap\-closing actions in classroom practice\.

## [Leadership Communication in the Implementation of Technology\-Based Learning in Rural Junior High Schools](../publications/63b386b5e1990ce64ae2.md)

Muhamad Khadafi Firman; Nur Kholisoh; Afdal Makkuraga Putra

Background: Digital transformation in education requires school leaders to coordinate technology, human resources, and communication effectively, particularly in rural schools where infrastructure, digital literacy, and access to technological resources remain limited\. In such settings, leadership communication is important for reducing resistance to technological change, strengthening teachers’ readiness, and facilitating the effective integration of technology into teaching and learning\. However, the communicative mechanisms used by school principals to manage intergenerational differences, infrastructure constraints, and regulatory challenges in resource\-limited rural schools remain insufficiently explored\. Aims: This study aims to analyse how a principal&\#x27;s leadership communication is constructed and implemented to transform conventional instructional practices towards technology adoption amidst rural facility constraints\. Specifically, it examines leadership communication strategies in aligning intergenerational teacher potential, managing infrastructure limitations, and navigating regional regulatory tensions\. Study Design: A qualitative approach with a descriptive\-analytical case study design was employed\. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted at Negeri 7 Krui Junior High School, Pesisir Barat Regency, Lampung, Indonesia, from February to March 2026\. Methodology: Data were collected through in\-depth interviews, direct observations, and documentation\. The data were analysed using the Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña interactive model\. Results: The findings reveal that the school principal implemented transformational and servant leadership communication strategies based on three primary pillars: \(1\) sensemaking to dismantle myths surrounding technological complexity and reduce technophobia; \(2\) intergenerational peer coaching that paired junior and senior teachers; and \(3\) institutionalised periodic sharing sessions to facilitate continuous knowledge exchange\. At the managerial level, the principal established a centralised multimedia scheduling system to address limited electrical capacity and damaged laboratory facilities\. The findings indicate that successful instructional technology integration depends not only on hardware availability but also on the mobilisation of relational and social capital to reduce diffusion uncertainty and challenge deficit narratives surrounding rural education\. Conclusion: Adaptive, humanistic, and contextual leadership communication is a determining factor in establishing a competitive and socially equitable digital learning ecosystem in rural educational institutions\.

## [Untrained CNN and coefficient\-space regularization for joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography](../publications/63b6c83f487193b95e85.md)

Alfio Bozi; Anwesa Dey; Souvik Roy

The joint reconstruction of the initial pressure and spatially varying sound speed in photoacoustic tomography from boundary measurements is considered\. A regularized data\-driven framework is proposed in which the unknown fields are represented in finite\-dimensional wavelet spaces and fixed nonlinear features generated by an untrained convolutional neural network \(CNN\) are used to reconstruct the initial\-pressure coefficients through Tikhonov\-regularized least squares\. A learned coefficient\-space prior is subsequently used to infer the squared sound\-speed coefficients\. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction on held\-out data and strong generalization to previously unseen phantom geometries\. The frozen reconstruction map also remains stable under measurement noise not represented during training, with only minor changes in reconstruction accuracy for noise levels up to $10\\%$\. In comparison with the supervised trained\-CNN approach considered in this work, the untrained representation yields substantially smaller reconstruction errors while requiring approximately one\-sixth of the computational time\. These results demonstrate that fixed random convolutional features combined with regularized coefficient\-space learning provide an efficient and robust approach to joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography\.

## [A Lightweight Traffic Sign Recognition Network for Autonomous Driving: Integrating Dual\-Branch Attention and Weather\-Robust Augmentation](../publications/63ba85bc2226dbc54544.md)

Ting Wang; Zhihao Weng

Traffic sign recognition is a key perception task in autonomous driving and advanced driver\-assistance systems, where accuracy and real\-time performance directly affect road safety\. In real\-world scenes, fog, rain, and low illumination reduce image contrast and introduce noise, degrading deep models, while in\-vehicle platforms impose strict limits on model size and computation\. We propose CAMSNet, a lightweight traffic sign recognition network\. Its architecture uses a lightweight residual backbone based on depthwise separable convolutions and a Dual\-branch Attention Calibration Module \(DACM\), whose parallel channel\- and position\-attention branches model channel dependencies and spatial location\. Their weights are fused elementwise and applied through residual reweighting to enhance sign features adaptively\. During training, a weather\-robust augmentation strategy based on atmospheric scattering randomly adds synthetic fog, Gaussian noise, and brightness changes\. This augmentation is applied only to training data, leaving inference as a lightweight, one\-way network\. On the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark \(GTSRB\), CAMSNet achieves 98\.19% top\-1 accuracy with 0\.458 million parameters and 35\.88 million multiply\-accumulate operations \(MACs\), exceeding ResNet\-18, which has about 24 times as many parameters, and MobileNetV2, which has about five times as many\. CAMSNet with weather augmentation \(CAMSNet\+W\) reaches 98\.50% accuracy and 96\.34% under severe synthetic fog\. This is 36\.98 percentage points above ResNet\-18 and 36\.12 points above CAMSNet without weather augmentation\. CAMSNet\+W also shows the smallest accuracy drops under severe noise and low brightness\. Ablation and controlled comparisons indicate that attention improves robustness under degraded conditions while maintaining similar clean\-domain accuracy\. DACM is competitive with ECA and CBAM and offers a useful balance between parameter count and robustness\. In this single run, weather augmentation improved robustness without an observed loss in clean\-test accuracy\. Robustness conclusions are based on synthetic corruptions; generalization to real adverse\-weather scenes remains to be established\.

## [Metaverse in education: combining theory and expert knowledge to inform adoption](../publications/63bfe599b847a8dffc0f.md)

Umar Bashir Mir; Vipulesh Shardeo; Bishal Dey Sarkar; Hana Trollman; Sandeep Jagtap

Purpose This study aims to examine the factors influencing metaverse adoption in education, addressing a context that remains underexplored and contested\. It aims to identify and structure the key determinants shaping stakeholder adoption decisions while highlighting the metaverse’s implications for knowledge management through immersive and experiential learning\. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a multimethod design combining the task\-technology fit model and the extended resource\-based view\. Expert insights were analysed using fuzzy ordinal priority approach \(F\-OPA\) to prioritise factors, modified Total Interpretive Structural Modeling \(m\-TISM\) to examine interrelationships and develop a hierarchical framework and MICMAC analysis to classify factors by driving power and dependence value\. Findings Fourteen factors influencing metaverse adoption were identified and grouped into four categories: infrastructure, pedagogy, accessibility and socioeconomic conditions\. The findings show that adoption depends on both enabling capabilities and contextual constraints\. The metaverse can enhance knowledge creation, sharing and application through immersive learning, but adoption is limited by infrastructure readiness, equitable access and socioeconomic disparities\. Originality/value This study offers novel empirical evidence on metaverse adoption in education by integrating task\-technology fit with the extended resource\-based view and applying a combined F\-OPA, m\-TISM and MICMAC approach to generate prioritised and interpretive insights\.

## [Feature analysis for malware detection](../publications/63c2677ade428a0567cd.md)

Αγγελική Μποϊλέ

Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία σχετίζεται με την ανάλυση χαρακτηριστικών για αναγνώριση κακόβουλου λογισμικού χρησιμοποιώντας μεθόδους μηχανικής μάθησης\. Στόχος είναι να αξιολογηθεί ένα νέο σετ δεδομένων, να γίνει σύγκριση της απόδοσης ανάμεσα στους διαφορετικούς τύπους αρχείων που περιλαμβάνει, καθώς επίσης και να ελεγχθεί κατά πόσο τα νέα χαρακτηριστικά που περιέχει το συγκεκριμένο dataset μπορούν να ανιχνεύσουν το κακόβουλο λογισμικό\. Αρχικά πραγματοποιήθηκε διαχωρισμός των δεδομένων σε υποσύνολα για να γίνει γρηγορότερα η εκπαίδευση\. Στη συνέχεια έγινε η μετατροπή τους σε διανυσματική μορφή και επιλέχθηκαν τυχαία δείγματα ώστε να ξεκινήσει η εκπαίδευση με τεχνικές μηχανικής μάθησης\. Ο αλγόριθμος που χρησιμοποιήθηκε ήταν ο Random Forest, ο οποίος γενικά παρουσιάζει υψηλά αποτελέσματα όσον αφορά την αναγνώριση malware\. Κατά τη διάρκεια των πειραμάτων, δόθηκε σημασία στην απόδοση και τον χρόνο εκπαίδευσης όλων τωνχαρακτηριστικών και ιδιαίτερα στα νέα χαρακτηριστικά που έχουν προστεθεί στην τελευταία έκδοση του dataset\. Οι μετρικές που αναλύθηκαν ήταν, μεταξύ άλλων, η απόδοση \(accuracy\), το recall, το F1\-score και το ROC AUC και πράγματι παρατηρήθηκε ότι τα νέα χαρακτηριστικά αποδίδουν καλύτερα και μπορούν να αναγνωρίσουν το κακόβουλο λογισμικό\.

## [Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One\-Sided Feedback](../publications/63c6a6711d32bf925ce2.md)

Kaixuan Ji; Zixiang Chen; Wenting Zhao; Cheng Qian; Heng Wang; Weizhi Zhang; Jielin Qiu; Liangwei Yang; Quanquan Gu; Silvio Savarese; Shelby Heinecke; Huan Wang

Long\-term memory enables language\-model agents to personalize future interactions, but a finite memory bank cannot preserve every extracted fact\. Existing memory gating policies are typically shared across users and therefore fail to account for user\-specific patterns of future reuse\. In this paper, we study memory gating at the fact level\. We first propose a retrieval\-based labeling strategy that labels each fact by whether it is later retrieved and incorporated into responses\. We then formulate online memory gating as contextual apple tasting with delayed one\-sided feedback, and propose Warm\-Start UCB, which combines offline learning from existing data with online adaptation to the current user\. Our theoretical analysis establishes a high\-probability regret upper bound of $\\tilde\{O\}\(Tε\\wedge d\\sqrt\{T\}\)$ when the delay window is at most $O\(\\sqrt\{T\}\)$, where $T$ is the total number of rounds, $ε$ is the initialization error, $d$ is the dimension of the feature map, and $\\tilde\{O\}\(\\cdot\)$ hides constant and poly\-logarithmic factors\. The results of our experiment demonstrate that our method outperforms all baselines under different memory budgets and history lengths, establishing it as a promising personalized memory gating policy\.

## [Mass as topological charge: an axiomatic framework for the equivalence principle and topological phase transitions in spiral spacetime](../publications/63c9200174dde5441797.md)

liwei ji

This paper establishes an axiomatic differential\-geometric framework for spiral spacetime\. Static mass is defined as a conserved flux charge of spacetime singularities\. Under explicitly stated divergence\-free conditions, its invariance under divergence\-preserving diffeomorphisms yields a conservation\-law interpretation of mass conservation with geometric\-flux structure\. Within this framework, gravitational and inertial mass are represented as two response projections of the same topological charge\. The equivalence principle is not derived from the axioms; rather, the framework provides a common mathematical carrier for it and yields a falsifiable corollary: gravitational and inertial mass must modulate synchronously and in equal proportion under external driving\. Parametric\-resonance\-driven topological phase transitions are investigated using Floquet stability theory\. Under testable phenomenological hypotheses H1–H3, two quantitative residual\-mass predictions are presented, with residual mass fractions ranging from 2\.58 % to 3\.93 % \. A four\-level rescaling\-gain principle is formulated as an efficiency optimization constrained by global conservation laws\. The mass\-energy balance requires an open\-system flux\-exchange channel, stated explicitly as an open validity postulate\. Five falsifiable experimental predictions are provided for future verification\.

## [Reference Points and Affordability Perceptions of Hybrid Maize Seed in Uganda: Evidence on Endowment and Expectations](../publications/63d25f08865cc3d06448.md)

Astrid Mastenbroek; Robert A\. Sparrow; Geoffrey Otim; Christine Kawuma

ABSTRACT Despite demonstrated yield advantages, adoption of hybrid maize seed in Sub‐Saharan Africa remains low, raising questions about smallholders&\#x27; perceptions of value and affordability\. We examine whether farmers value hybrid maize seed differently depending on whether they already possess it or form expectations about likely prices or ownership, and how this affects willingness to pay \(WTP\) for a 1‐kg pack of seed in Uganda\. We elicit WTP and willingness to accept \(WTA\) using Becker‐DeGroot‐Marschak auctions and measure ownership expectations with a multiple price list\. The experiment tests three mechanisms: an endowment effect, by comparing WTP and WTA; price expectations, by randomly varying price probabilities; and ownership expectations, by varying the probability of keeping the seed for free\. We find a strong endowment effect: farmers require substantially more money to give up seed they already possess than they are willing to pay to acquire the same seed, with WTA exceeding WTP by about 60%\. The average WTP of UGX 4605 is well below the market price of UGX 8500\. Loss aversion is associated with lower WTP and higher WTA, but these effects are small, imprecise, and do not explain the valuation gap\. We do not find evidence that price expectations or ownership expectations generate economically meaningful reference points\. Overall, our results indicate that current possession of seed is a more salient benchmark for valuation than forward‐looking expectations\. These findings suggest that scaling strategies establishing early ownership, such as trial packs or plant‐now/pay‐after‐harvest schemes, may be more effective than attempts to shift price expectations alone\.

## [Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell\-cycle progression by microRNA\-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification](../publications/63d45822a587459e0d6e.md)

Arpan Das; Yuheng C\. Fu; Haimin Li; Megan A\. Wong; Annalina Che; Anumeha Singh; Jimin Han; Glen A\. Bjerke; Dongmei Wang; Rui Yi

Abstract The microRNA\-200 family \(miR\-200s\) is known for inhibiting epithelial\-to\-mesenchymal transition and cell\-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear\. Here we show that miR\-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle \(HF\), where sebaceous gland \(SG\) and HF stem cells are specified\. Ectopic miR\-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis\. Genome\-wide identification of miR\-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell\-cycle regulators\. Single\-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR\-200 induction\. Genome\-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty\-acid metabolic program required for SG specification\. Together, these findings show that miR\-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development\.

## [Remote Activation of Wnt Signaling and Cell Proliferation by E‐Cadherin Magnetomechanical Stimulation](../publications/63d855ca2f912eecde85.md)

Christian Castro\-Hinojosa; Pablo Martínez‐Vicente; Lucia G Recaredo; Susel Del Sol‐Fernández; Pilar Gomollón\-Zueco; Yilian Fernández‐Afonso; Raluca M\. Fratila; María Moros

ABSTRACT The ability to remotely and precisely manipulate intracellular signaling pathways is crucial for fundamental research and therapeutics\. The Wnt/β‐catenin cascade regulates cell proliferation, differentiation, and tissue regeneration, but current pharmacological activation methods lack spatiotemporal control and induce off‐target effects\. Here, we introduce a pioneering magnetogenetic toolkit to modulate the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway through magnetomechanical stimulation of E‐cadherin, a key cell adhesion molecule intimately linked to β‐catenin dynamics\. Magnetic nanoparticles functionalized with the extracellular domain of E‐cadherin \(MNPs@E/EC15\) selectively bind cellular E‐cadherins\. Applying a low‐intensity, low‐gradient magnetic field via a custom stimulator generates localized mechanical forces that trigger E‐cadherin mechanotransduction\. This stimulation induces β‐catenin membrane release, nuclear translocation, and Wnt target gene activation, confirmed by transcriptomic profiling and a luciferase reporter assay\. These molecular changes translate into enhanced cell proliferation and accelerated gap closure\. This work establishes an innovative, non‐invasive tool for probing E‐cadherin mechanobiology and remotely modulating Wnt/β‐catenin signaling\. Unlike other mechanotransduction tools, this approach enables simultaneous, high‐spatiotemporal modulation of multiple cells using low‐intensity magnetic fields adaptable for in vivo designs\. Our findings open promising avenues for studying mechanotransduction and developing targeted regenerative therapies based on mechanical stimulation\.

## [Algoritma Fiqh dan Limitasi Otoritas Keagamaan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis Penetrasi Kecerdasan Buatan dalam Penalaran Hukum Islam dan Fatwa Digital](../publications/63d926f70574d1240698.md)

Nasrul Faiz; Achmad Faqihuddin

Penetrasi kecerdasan buatan \(Artificial Intelligence\) ke dalam ranah hukum Islam telah memicu pergeseran cara umat Muslim mengakses fatwa, namun sekaligus menimbulkan krisis otoritas keagamaan akibat keterbatasan algoritma dalam memahami kompleksitas ushul Fiqh\. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan karakteristik pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan dalam penalaran hukum Islam, mengidentifikasi limitasi epistemologis algoritma Fiqh \(sistem komputasi cerdas yang mereplikasi pola penalaran hukum Islam\), serta merumuskan batas otoritas antara mesin dan ulama\. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review berbasis pedoman PRISMA 2020 pada database Scopus \(2021–2026\) melalui kueri Boolean bertahap dengan kriteria inklusi studi primer yang mengkaji AI dalam Fiqh, fatwa, peradilan agama, dan kepatuhan syariah\. Dari 506 artikel awal \(0 duplikasi\), dilakukan penyaringan ketat dan mengeluarkan 463 artikel hingga menghasilkan 43 studi primer yang dianalisis secara kuantitatif deskriptif dan tematik kualitatif\. Hasil penelitian mengelompokkan literatur ke dalam lima tema: penalaran hukum dan otoritas fatwa \(23,26%\); peradilan agama dan penyelesaian sengketa \(9,30%\); kepatuhan keuangan syariah dan robo\-advisors \(25,58%\); etika Maqasid al\-Shariah \(27,91%\); serta transformasi digital tafsir dan hadis \(13,95%\)\. Sintesis bukti empiris menunjukkan bahwa pemrosesan bahasa alami dan pembelajaran mendalam mempercepat pencarian dalil serta layanan peradilan namun rentan terhadap halusinasi dalil dan bias data, sedangkan secara normatif\-konseptual ushul Fiqh mesin tidak memiliki kapasitas mukallaf, ketakwaan, dan sanad keilmuan\. Disimpulkan bahwa kecerdasan buatan hanya sah diposisikan sebagai instrumen pendukung keputusan \(wasilah\) di bawah pengawasan ulama manusia\.

## [Implementing AI and Virtual Reality in Elite Sports Psychology](../publications/63d9749668c6eac115da.md)

Jian Cao; Weimin Shen

In team sports, psychological regulation is crucial, yet traditional methods lack personalization, rely on subjective assessments, and offer low realism\. This study examined the integration of computer\-assisted technologies into psychological training\. A six\-month trial involved 90 professional football, basketball, and ice hockey players, randomly assigned to an experimental group or control group\. Data on physiology, psychology, performance, and team communication were analyzed using t\-tests\. Per the results, the experimental group showed 21\.3% lower anxiety, 25\.4% higher cohesion, 21\.2% faster decision response, 14\.3% higher clutch success, 38\.7% better communication efficiency; clutch error rate was also reduced from 27% to 11%\. However, \~15% experienced virtual reality discomfort, and artificial intelligence overreliance reduced tactical creativity by 19%\. Computer\-assisted technologies enhance psychological resilience and team performance\. Balancing data\-driven precision with human\-centered coaching is vital\. Future work should optimize training models and establish data ethics\.

## [Transição Amazônia\-Cerrado: impactos na cobertura da terra na bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires](../publications/63e735c4030a85d41c2e.md)

Layse Gomes Furtado; Aline Maria Meiguins de Lima

Situada em uma região de grande biodiversidade, a bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires vem sofrendo sucessivas e intensas mudanças no uso e cobertura da terra, trazendo impactos ambientais provocadas pelas atividades econômicas da região\. Ressaltando a necessidade do monitoramento dessas transformações, esta pesquisa objetivou analisar as transformações no uso e cobertura da terra na bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires nos últimos 36 anos\. Utilizando a plataforma do MapBiomas para extração e interpretação das classes de uso e cobertura da terra entre os anos de 1986 a 2022, e por meio da quantificação das áreas das classes e cruzamento dos mapas foi possível descrever as mudanças e apontar as principais conversões de área ocorridas durante o período\. Os resultados salientaram o crescimento das classes de cultivo de soja \(3\.459,52%\) e pastagem \(189,79%\) em detrimento da redução das áreas naturais de floreta \(\-34,54%\) e formação natural não florestal \(\-47,48%\)\. Essa perda vegetal se intensifica mais ao sul da bacia, onde há maior alteração na cobertura da terra, e aos poucos se propaga no sentido norte, onde é encontrada a maior extensão de área destinada ao cultivo da soja, pastagem e mineração, diferentemente do que se encontra no extremo norte da bacia, grande presença de floresta, que se explica por existirem muitas áreas de proteção nas adjacências\. Além do crescente desenvolvimento agropecuário, a presença de grandes empreendimentos hidrelétricos ao longo do rio Teles Pires provocou alagamento no entorno, resultando em um ganho de área de \(44,82%\) na classe de corpo d’água\.

## [Career Development and Job Selection Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making Model](../publications/63e9aa1b733c5959ab93.md)

R\. Chandrasekar; M Ramachandran; Arunambigai Ramesh

Career Making decisions is a difficult process that entails weighing several variables to determine which suitable job path\. The Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution \(Fuzzy TOPSIS\) is used in this study to assess and rank career alternatives based on key job attributes\. The research focuses on four primary evaluation parameters: employment prospects, job stability, job adaptability, and job advantages and perks\. Research Significance: This study provides a structured and data\-driven approach to career selection, enabling individuals and policymakers to make well\-informed decisions by prioritizing job attributes based on their importance\. The Fuzzy TOPSIS methodology helps in handling uncertainty and subjectivity in career evaluations, offering a reliable decision\-making model\. Methodology: The Fuzzy TOPSIS method is used to evaluate and prioritize various career alternatives\. The process involves normalizing decision matrices, determining fuzzy weights, calculating ideal solutions, both positive and negative, and calculating closeness coefficients to rank career choices\. Alternative Career Options: The study evaluates different career paths based on the following parameters: Career opportunities \(growth potential and advancement prospects\), Job security \(stability and long\-term sustainability\), Job flexibility \(work\-life balance and adaptability\), Job benefits and perks \(compensation, incentives, and additional benefits\) Results: The analysis ranks career options based on their alignment with the ideal job conditions\. The findings suggest that job security and career opportunities are the most influential factors, while job benefits and perks have relatively lower weight\. The results provide valuable insights for career planning by highlighting the most favorable career paths based on individual preferences and priorities\.

## [Multimodal Experiential Meaning in Ninth\-Grade Digital Procedure Infographics: A Systemic Functional Linguistic Analysis](../publications/63ead179c7f914349d53.md)

Lina Ekawati; Dwi Santoso; Surono Surono

While digital compositions are increasingly prominent in language education, the unresolved problem remains of how student\-created digital infographics coordinate language, image, and layout to represent procedural experience\. To address this gap, this qualitative case study investigates the multimodal realization of experiential meaning in digital procedure infographics created by ninth\-grade students in a private junior high school within a Central Kalimantan palm oil plantation, Indonesia\. Analyzing ten purposive student infographics using Systemic Functional Linguistics \(SFL\) Transitivity and Visual Grammar, data were triangulated with semi\-structured interviews and observations\. Findings reveal that verbally, instructional steps are heavily dominated by Material Processes \(90%–95%\), transitioning to Relational Processes at closures to signal product readiness\. Visually, students localized the genre by integrating Dayak cultural motifs to assert local identity\. Intermodally, a critical &quot;Static Paradox&quot; \(intermodal mismatch\) occurs when dynamic verbal commands are paired with conceptually frozen static images lacking action vectors, a challenge further constrained by unstable plantation Wi\-Fi\. This study contributes directly to English language teaching by demonstrating how socio\-technical and cultural factors shape students’ multimodal representations\. To guide layout, text\-image alignment, and culturally situated designs, educators should implement an Integrated Multimodal Cohesion Rubric for assessment and introduce Structural Macro\-Layout Blueprints during the design process\.

## [Bridging model attention to physical insights in structure\-property dynamics](../publications/63f5be09f971ec376e0d.md)

Duc\-Anh Dao; Minh\-Quyet Ha; Tien\-Sinh Vu; Dinh\-Cong Vuong; Keisuke Ishizuka; Yoshifumi Oshima; Masato Suzuki; Tomohiko Nagao; Naoya Amino; Hieu‐Chi Dam

Time\-resolved experiments increasingly capture structural evolution together with measured physical responses, creating new opportunities to interrogate spatiotemporal structure–property dynamics\. Although deep learning models, including attention\-based transformers, can predict such responses directly from image sequences by modeling complex correlations, predictive accuracy alone does not provide physical understanding\. Attention mechanisms identify statistically influential regions within evolving images, yet these signals do not explicitly reveal the structural organization governing system response\. A framework is therefore established in which attention–derived emphasis guides physics\-informed structural analysis, treating attention not as explanation but as a constraint for domain\-grounded transformation that exposes the dominant mode of structural organization associated with measured properties\. Applied to gold\-nanocontact deformation \(atomic scale\) and wet rubber–surface contact \(macroscale\), the framework recovers, in each system, the structural organization associated with the measured response\. By translating attention–derived emphasis into physical descriptors, this work establishes a pathway from predictive modeling to physical interpretation of hidden structure–property relationships\.

## [A Unified Microscopic Picture of Cation and Anion Migration in MAPbI3](../publications/63fe2b497a7374253c92.md)

Viren Tyagi; Geert Brocks; Shuxia Tao

Abstract Passivating defects and restricting defect mobilities in halide perovskites to increase device lifetimes has become a main field of research\. Modeling structure and mobility of point defects is an essential contribution to this endeavor\. We employ molecular dynamics, based on neural network potentials trained on density functional theory data, to model ion migration in MAPbI3 triggered by I and MA vacancies or interstitials\. Most of these species diffuse rapidly at room temperature, with migration barriers between 0\.15 and 0\.20 eV\. MA interstitials are highly mobile despite their molecular nature, because of a collective reorientation of neighboring MA ions\. No evidence of MA vacancy migration is obtained\. While the diffusion of I\-related defects appreciably depends on their charge state, the diffusion of MA defects does not\. These results revise the conventional picture of ion transport in hybrid perovskites and highlight the role of collective molecular motion in enabling fast ionic migration\.

## [Designing a Predictive Expense Tracking Mobile Application: A Comparison of Random Forest, Linear Regression, and Prophet\-Based Models](../publications/63ff39aa2f38e1662a65.md)

Li Zhe Poh; Li Wei Tai; Md Ismail Hossen

In today’s fast\-paced world, people engage in various forms of daily consumption, yet many lack the habit of tracking their expenses due to low financial awareness\. Without proper expense recording and budgeting, individuals often struggle to understand their consumption habits and are at a disadvantage when it comes to financial planning, especially during emergencies\. To address these issues, this project proposes the development of a user\-friendly expense tracking mobile application designed to help adults build healthy financial habits and utilize predictive algorithms to forecast future expenses\. The application enables users to record daily transactions, analyse their spending patterns, plan budgets, and receive personalized saving recommendations\. An experiment was conducted to compare four forecasting models: Random Forest, Linear Regression, Facebook Prophet, and Neural Prophet\. The models were evaluated using the same synthetically generated transaction dataset, which yielded a limited number of monthly observations for testing\. Random Forest showed the most stable overall performance under this experimental setting and was selected as the forecasting model for the prototype, though these results should be interpreted with caution given the small evaluation sample\.

## [Joint Psychometric Validation of the Shame and Release Scale \(SRS\) and the Fundamental Peace Scale \(FP20\) in Indian Organisational Contexts: A Pre\-Registered Validation Protocol](../publications/64015150ccfe2bcf1eb2.md)

Luis Miguel Gallardo

Background The Shame and Release Scale \(SRS\) and the Fundamental Peace Scale \(FP20\) address a critical measurement gap in South Asian organisational contexts: the absence of validated instruments that simultaneously assess shame burden and fundamental wellbeing\. The SRS is a 40\-item instrument measuring shame load across five subscales \(Inner Verdict, Others&\#x27; Eyes, Exposure at Work, Inherited Shame, Shame Loop\) and release capacity \(Release subscale\), conceptualizing shame and release as opposite poles of a single psychological continuum\. The FP20 is a 20\-item instrument measuring fundamental peace as an integrative positive state distinct from the absence of distress, grounded in the Yoga Vasishtha Hypnotherapy \(YVH\) Model\. Both instruments are designed for oral administration in low\-literacy populations and are being validated within the World Happiness Foundation&\#x27;s Shameless Institutions programme in India, which provides ecological validity through programme data waves as validation samples\. Methods This protocol employs a longitudinal multi\-wave cohort design embedded in the WHF Shameless Institutions programme\. The validation sample comprises 400 participants at baseline, 350 at mid\-point, and 300 at endpoint, stratified across three occupational levels: artisan communities, field staff, and head office personnel\. Both instruments undergo expert review for content validity \(Content Validity Index ≥ 0\.78\), cognitive interviews \(15–20 per occupational group\), pilot exploratory factor analysis \(n=150\), confirmatory factor analysis \(n=400\), and validity testing against established measures\. Convergent validity is assessed using the External and Internal Shame Scale \(EISS\), which has demonstrated validity across multiple countries \[1\], the Transgression\-Related Interpersonal Motivations Inventory \(TRIM\-18\), and the Self\-Compassion Scale Short Form \(SCS\-SF\)\. Discriminant validity testing examines the distinctness of SRS and FP20 constructs\. Measurement invariance is tested across occupational levels and gender\. The oral administration protocol accommodates low\-literacy artisan participants through picture\-based answer cards and research partner\-assisted completion\. Expected Results We predict strong convergent validity: SRS Shame Load subscales will correlate positively with the validated EISS measure of external and internal shame \[1\] and TRIM\-18 revenge/avoidance dimensions, and negatively with SCS\-SF and FP20; SRS Release will correlate positively with SCS\-SF and FP20, and negatively with EISS\. Discriminant validity testing will demonstrate that SRS and FP20 measure distinct but related constructs \(HTMT &lt; 0\.85\)\. Confirmatory factor analysis will support a six\-factor structure for SRS \(five shame load factors plus release\) and a four\-factor structure for FP20, with fit indices meeting recommended thresholds \(CFI ≥ 0\.95, RMSEA ≤ 0\.06, SRMR ≤ 0\.08\)\. Measurement invariance will be established across occupational levels and gender\. Longitudinal analysis will reveal significant reductions in shame load and increases in fundamental peace from baseline to endpoint\. Discussion Successful validation of the SRS and FP20 will provide the first psychometrically robust instruments for simultaneously measuring shame burden and fundamental wellbeing in South Asian organisational contexts\. This joint validation contributes to cross\-cultural psychometrics by developing culturally adapted instruments for shame measurement in collectivistic cultures, where shame is more prominent and associated with subordinance\-related experiences \[2\]\. The validated instruments will enable wellbeing measurement in South Asian organisational contexts where shame is a principal factor regulating social behavior \[2\], supporting evidence\-based programme evaluation in the WHF Shameless Institutions initiative and similar interventions\. The oral administration protocol extends measurement accessibility to low\-literacy populations, addressing a critical gap in inclusive psychometric practice\. Conclusion This pre\-registered protocol establishes a rigorous validation pathway for the SRS and FP20 in Indian populations, providing validated tools for measuring shame and fundamental peace in South Asian organisational and development contexts where such instruments have been absent\.

## [Biotecnología en comunidades indígenas: oportunidades, desafíos éticos y sostenibilidad](../publications/64023ab0769d122127ba.md)

Israel Osuna\-Flores; Arturo Rafael Armenta\-López; Xavier Eduardo Verdugo\-Contreras; Estela Sañudo\-Ayala; Mario Guadalupe López Ayala

Biotechnology is considered a pillar of current scientific and technological development, and its implementation in indigenous communities poses ethical, social, and environmental challenges that require critical and contextualized analysis\. This article aims to analyze the relationship between biotechnology and indigenous peoples, with emphasis on Latin America and Mexico, through a qualitative methodology based on a documentary review supported by critical\-interpretive analysis of the scientific literature published between 2015 and 2026, aside from a few exceptions involving foundational works\. It examines specific applications such as the conservation of native species, ecosystem restoration, sustainable agriculture, and genomics applied to health and territory\. It also presents cases from indigenous communities, such as the Tzeltal and Tzotzil peoples in Chiapas and the Nahua peoples in Puebla, as well as experiences in Latin America \(the Ecuadorian Amazon and Chimborazo\), which reveal both potential benefits and existing tensions\. Among the challenges identified are biopiracy, violations of free, prior, and informed consent, asymmetries in benefit\-sharing mechanisms, and the persistence of colonial approaches in scientific research\. The article incorporates new governance frameworks such as the Cali Fund for Digital Sequence Information \(COP16\) and the C\.A\.R\.E\. Principles of Indigenous Data Sovereignty\. It concludes that biotechnology can effectively contribute to sustainable development when it is based on the principles of justice, effective community participation, and respect for cultural autonomy, and that co\-design approaches integrating scientific and traditional knowledge are required\.

## [АДМІНІСТРАТИВНО\-ПРАВОВЕ РЕГУЛЮВАННЯ ВПРОВАДЖЕННЯ ТА ВИКОРИСТАННЯ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ ПУБЛІЧНОЮ АДМІНІСТРАЦІЄЮ В УМОВАХ ДІЇ СПЕЦІАЛЬНИХ ПРАВОВИХ РЕЖИМІВ: ДОСВІД ІЗРАЇЛЮ ТА УКРАЇНИ](../publications/64115e0afb732a96315d.md)

Павло Іванович Крайній

У статті досліджується актуальний стан правового регулювання впровадження та використання технологій штучного інтелекту \(далі – ШІ\) Ізраїлем та Україною\. Проаналізовано тенденції використання різних інструментів ШІ, які здійснюються публічною адміністрацією обидвох держав в умовах дії спеціальних правових режимів\. Наголошено, що ізраїльський та український досвід впровадження згадуваних технологій залежить від рівня адміністративно\-правового регулювання відносин внутрішнього та зовнішнього адміністрування\. Ізраїль кілька років поспіль виступає одним зі світових лідерів розробки, тестування, впровадження та використання технологій ШІ у різних сферах суспільного життя\. Це зумовлюється рівнем розвитку відповідних технологій, активністю приватного сектору, який у взаємодії з державою поширює свої напрацювання на сферу публічного врядування та публічного адміністрування\. Перебуваючи понад кілька десятків років в умовах дії спеціального правового режиму \(state of emergency\), ізраїльське суспільство та держава продемонстрували високий рівень розвитку технологій, впровадження стартапів у сфері, яка пов’язана зі ШІ\. Незважаючи на постійну критику, яка лунає від урядів європейських держав, країн Близького Сходу, ізраїльська держава вибрала модель адміністративно\-правового регулювання, основою якої виступає людиноцентризм\. Затверджена політика у сфері ШІ «Відповідальні інновації» \(«Responsible Innovation» AI policy\) встановлює рекомендації в частині розробки й використання ШІ, якими визначаються принципи, сектори економіки та супутні ризики щодо впровадження згадуваних інструментів\. Обрання такого підходу відрізняється від моделей, які реалізуються державами\-членами Європейського Союзу \(далі – ЄС\), проте є схожими за своїм змістом до вибраної Сполученими Штатами Америки \(далі – США\) моделі впровадження ШІ\. Встановлено, що синергія між приватними компаніями, стартапами та державою, яка полягає у спільному тестуванні відповідних рішень з використання ШІ, виявленні потенційних викликів та проблем, позитивно вплине на відповідний горизонт планування для створення локального нормативного регулювання за відповідними напрямами\. Український досвід щодо адміністративно\-правового регулювання впровадження та використання ШІ подібний до ізраїльського у тому сенсі, що перші кроки на шляху до розроблення відповідних цифрових платформ здійснювались під час триваючої російсько\-української війни\. Поряд з цим іще одним важливим фактором, який вплинув на формування технологічного та адміністративно\-правового складників у цій сфері, було створення Міністерства цифрової трансформації, яким впроваджено велику кількість важливих інструментів, які нині є невід’ємною складовою частиною діяльності публічної адміністрації, здійснення публічного врядування\. Створення та підтримка діяльності Єдиного порталу державних послуг «Дія» дозволили запровадити Дія\.AI – перший у світі національний ШІ\-асистент у сфері державних послуг \[1\]\. Вплив законодавства ЄС, прийнятих актів щодо регулювання використання ШІ зумовив обрання українською державою bottom\-up підходу, який передбачає поступове впровадження ШІ\-інструментів у два етапи\. Перший стосується підготовки на рівні приватного сектору, заслуховування його пропозицій та бачення\. Другий – прийняття спеціального закону про ШІ за аналогом Акта про ШІ \(далі – EU AI Act\)\. Водночас вдосконалення української моделі впровадження та адміністративно\-правового регулювання ШІ у діяльність публічної адміністрації може посилюватись із активним залученням приватних осіб, компаній\-розробників інструментів та органів публічної влади\. Створення належних адміністративно\-правових механізмів налагодження такої взаємодії у вигляді публічно\-приватного партнерства може позитивно сприяти триваючому технологічному домінуванню України серед держав, які спроможні впроваджувати ШІ\. Використання ізраїльського досвіду в частині оголошення конкурсів спільно між міністерствами та окремими розробниками ШІ щодо істотного покриття витрат на впровадження таких ШІ\-інструментів може позитивно вплинути на виконання поставленої нашою державою мети – входження до першої трійки держав\-лідерів за рівнем впровадження ШІ у державному секторі\. Крім цього, активне залучення приватного сектору вимагатиме адміністративно\-правового регулювання в частині співробітництва, навчання публічних службовців, обговорення необхідних вдосконалень\. Ізра\- їльський досвід у цьому аспекті демонструє гнучкість та дозволяє швидко вирішувати такі завдання\. Авторська позиція, що викладена у висновках, сформульована виходячи із тези, що спеціальні пра\- вові режими, впливаючи на зміни окремих інститутів та галузей права, зокрема й адміністративного, незважаючи на введення обмежень щодо реалізації конституційних прав і свобод людини, виступають каталізаторами вдосконалення публічного врядування та публічного адміністрування\. ШІ\-інструменти пришвидшуватимуть цей процес\. ## [A wearable ultrasonic system monitoring skeletal muscle activities](../publications/6412e273e07d6c7588b4.md)

Shuo Wang

The skeletal\-muscular system plays a vital role in human physiology, facilitating movement and locomotion essential for interaction with the environment\. Ultrasound can be a proper way to help monitor the status of skeletal\-muscular system\. Compared to traditional bulky and complicated ultrasound monitoring system, wearable ultrasound sensor with customized control and signal reception circuit with tailored algorithm is capable of implementing the same monitoring function easily and quickly\. For the development of ultrasound sensor, a completely rigid ultrasound sensor is not suitable for use during wearing\. Flexible ultrasound sensors usually involve complex manufacturing processes and require tedious steps to achieve the desired performance\. Moreover, they are typically unfavorable for wearing due to the non\-breathable substrates and materials used\. Additionally, for B\-mode flexible sensor arrays, deformation compensation is also an urgent issue that needs to be addressed\. For the control and signal reception circuit, typical commercial devices are quite bulky or complicated\. Some proposed hardware usually lacks customization and scalability in frequency, number of channels, or algorithm logic for specific applications\. For the algorithm, algorithms are developed according to different monitoring objectives\. In the field of gesture classification using ultrasound signals, few studies focus on recognizing specific gestures based on a single transducer unit\. In existing research, the proposed machine learning methods are often complicated, with limited recognition accuracy\. Furthermore, the possibility of deploying the algorithms on edge devices is not considered, which limits their scope of application\. Therefore, in this study, we propose to develop a fabric\-based wearable ultrasound sensor with customized circuit and algorithms to monitor skeletal\-muscular status\. We investigate to develop ultrasound sensors with good performance on space cotton substrates using a minimalist manufacturing process \(mainly based on hot pressing\), which can fully leverage the advantages of fabric in terms of comfort and wearability\. And we explore the possibility of using strain sensors with deep learning method for shape calibration for B\-mode sensor array in the future with an error less than 2\.5 mm\. Then, a customized hardware for ultrasound signal control and reception has been developed based on Zynq, which can help customize the control logic, the excitation frequencies and deploy or accelerate algorithms because of the ARM and FPGA cores\. The design demonstrates the potential for further multi\-channel expansion in the future\. Finally, experiments have been carried out for monitoring extensor digitorum \(ED\) muscle&\#x27;s morphology changes with angles and strength variations\. The results show a strong positive correlation between the thickness change of the ED muscle and the applied force under different angles\. On the other hand, a lightweight framework for gestures classification based on the proposed system with a single transduce has been proposed, which combines virtual channels, multi\-scale, and transformer modules to achieve an average accuracy rate of over 98\.5%\. The distilled model can achieve over 95% accuracy while significantly reducing parameters and computational complexity, which can help with the future deployment of the model onto the proposed hardware\.

## [THE USE OF MODERN TECHNOLOGIES \(TRACKING DEVICES, SOFTWARE, AND APPLICATIONS\) IN YOUTH SPORTS TRAINING: A FIELD STUDY OF CHABAB AIN FAKROUN’S U19 TEAM](../publications/6414a375f662c8ba0e17.md)

Idris Zouaghi

This study aimed to identify the current state of the use of modern technologies in sports training for youth categories, particularly tracking devices \(GPS\), software, and digital applications, and to examine their effect on developing the physical performance of U19 players\. This study is particularly important given the rapid changes taking place in modern sports training, where technology has become a key tool for regulating training loads and monitoring athletes’ physiological condition\. The research problem concerned the extent to which coaches use tracking devices, software, and applications when training youth categories, and the effect of these technologies on the development of selected components of physical fitness\. The study adopted a descriptive\-analytical approach suited to the subject\. The sample consisted of 16 U19 players from Chabab Ain Fakroun, in addition to 4 coaches\. Data\-collection tools included questionnaires for players and coaches, interviews, and physical tests to assess speed and speed endurance\. The results showed that the level of use of modern technologies in training the U19 team at Chabab Ain Fakroun was moderate, with a usage rate of 62\.5%\. The results also revealed statistically significant differences in the speed and speed\-endurance tests between the pre\-test and post\-test in favour of the post\-test\. The calculated t\-values were 3\.42 for speed and 4\.18 for speed endurance at a significance level of 0\.01\. A significant positive correlation was also found between the use of tracking devices and improvements in physical fitness \(r = 0\.68\)\. The study concluded that modern technologies contribute effectively to improving young players’ physical performance and recommended wider adoption of these technologies and training coaches in their use\.

## [Tests of exchangeability for high\-dimensional data](../publications/64210e2262fd05f52026.md)

Rauf Ahmad

Abstract Exchangeability is an important data structure and, if appropriately discovered, may help in discernible dimension reduction\. This aspect carries special significance for high\-dimensional data\. For certain data sets, such as when same units are repeatedly observed, not only across all time points, but further under all experimental conditions, exchangeability is strongly expected, and a test to determine its presence is desired\. For example, the same patients might be observed across several time points, under both drug and placebo\. In another setting, expressions from normal and tumor cells from the same individuals may be evaluated\. The notion of exchangeability in such cases implies that the distinction of different conditions is of no significance, or that the sub\-vectors under different conditions are exchangeable\. The aim of this article is to present tests for multivariate exchangeability when the distributions may not necessarily be normal and the dimensions of the vectors, even of sub\-vectors, may exceed the sample size\. The test statistics are composed of consistent and computationally highly efficient estimators, and their properties are studied under a few mild assumptions\. Extension to two\-layer pattern of exchangeability, i\.e\., when the sub\-vectors are further partitioned into sub\-sub\-vectors, based on an additional variable, is also considered\. Simulation results are used to show the accuracy of the proposed tests\. Applications on real data examples are demonstrated\.

## [Evo\-B&amp;B: Behavior\-Aware LLM\-Guided Joint Evolution of Branching and Node Selection Policies for MILP](../publications/6421707296580b636fb9.md)

Jiayu Chen; Chentong Chen; Yuhan Liu; Ye Fan; Jianyong Sun; Jialong Shi

In branch\-and\-bound for Mixed\-Integer Linear Programming \(MILP\), branching and node selection are two critical and tightly coupled decisions, yet most existing learning\-based approaches focus on optimizing them separately\. We propose Evo\-B&amp;B, an LLM\-guided evolutionary framework that jointly evolves executable branching and node selection policies using end\-to\-end SCIP solving feedback\. To improve search efficiency and reduce redundant evaluations of behaviorally similar policies, Evo\-B&amp;B introduces a behavior\-aware multi\-island evolutionary mechanism\. It measures policy similarity from branching and node\-selection behaviors on a fixed set of B&amp;B decision states and uses this similarity to preserve population diversity\. We evaluate Evo\-B&amp;B on four standard MILP benchmarks across multiple instance scales\. Experimental results show that Evo\-B&amp;B achieves competitive solving performance and generalizes well to larger\-scale instances, while ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of joint evolution and behavior\-aware diversity management\.

## [Comparative Analysis of Asterix Ads\-B Cat 021 Edition 0\.23 And Edition 2\.1 Data On Thales Ax680 Equipment At Perum Lppnpi Airnav Denpasar Branch](../publications/6425c13687454b5c246a.md)

Yani Yudha Wirawan; Natasya Sandra Prastiwi; Nur Hazwani Dzulkefly

Automatic Dependent Surveillance\-Broadcast \(ADS\-B\) transmits aircraft target data to the ATC System using the ASTERIX \(All Purpose Structured Eurocontrol Surveillance Information Exchange\) Category 021 format\. At Perum LPPNPI AirNav Denpasar Branch, the Thales AX680 ADS\-B was upgraded from ASTERIX edition 0\.23 to edition 2\.1; within less than a year, aircraft targets intermittently disappeared and reappeared on the ATC System display, and the configuration was reverted to edition 0\.23\. This descriptive case study examines the problem by comparing the Cat 021 data items of both editions, using target recordings from the Tools Recorder and WireShark, Hexadecimal\-Binary\-Decimal conversion, and the Eurocontrol Cat 021 specification \(Part 12\)\. Edition 2\.1 contains 23 data items compared with 15 in edition 0\.23, including items that carry ADS\-B version and quality information defined for DO\-260B/ED\-102A avionics\. The most plausible explanation is that targets from aircraft with older DO\-260/ED\-102 avionics, which cannot supply these parameters, were handled inconsistently by the ATC System under edition 2\.1; reverting to edition 0\.23 restored stable target detection\. The study highlights the importance of understanding surveillance data formats and fleet avionics readiness before migrating to a newer data standard, and of a staged migration with documented acceptance criteria\.

## [Consequences of tilt of the magnetic field in magnetically enhanced capacitively coupled plasma reactors](../publications/6427403b19ba73171ce9.md)

Mark J\. Kushner

Abstract Magnetically enhanced reactive ion etching \(MERIE\) reactors are capacitively coupled plasmas \(CCPs\) used in microelectronic fabrication with a static magnetic field that is typically parallel to the wafer\. The purpose of the magnetic field is to increase plasma density and ion fluxes, while affording some control to the ion energy and angular distribution \(IEAD\) incident onto the wafer\. The uniformity of the plasma produced reactive fluxes onto the wafer are sensitive to the orientation of the magnetic field with respect to the wafer\. For example, fluxes are sensitive to the tilt of the magnetic field with respect to the surface of the wafer, as opposed to being strictly parallel to the wafer\. There is some likelihood that this angle may change from before to after preventative maintenance of a commercial MERIE reactor\. In this paper, we discuss results from a computational investigation of the consequences of tilt in the magnetic field in MERIE reactors on the uniformity of ion fluxes and IEADs delivered to the wafer\. This investigation was performed for CCPs sustained in Ar and Ar/Cl2 mixtures at tens of mTorr pressure with magnetic fields up to 150 G\. We found that tilt of the magnetic field of as small as 1 o produces significant side\-to\-side non\-uniformity in ion fluxes delivered across a 20 cm wafer\. There is less sensitivity of the IEAD to the tilt angle\. The dynamics of electric field reversals, which are common in MERIE reactors, are sensitive to the tilt angle, with the electric field reversals traversing diago\-nally across the reactor as the tilt angle increases\. The role of digital twins in insuring consistent performance of plasma reactors is discussed\.

## [Mapping the evolution of China\-affiliated piano education research \(1975–2025\): a bibliometric review](../publications/642bdbc3a16a7fa9bf53.md)

Mengyang Zhao; Zihang Zeng; Yiing Siing Wong; Kenny Cheah Soon Lee; Wen Fen Beh

This study conducted a bibliometric review of English\-language China\-affiliated piano education research between 1975 and 2025\. Using bibliometric methods and visualisation tools, a total of 523 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection were analysed\. The study examined publication trends, citation patterns, collaboration networks, and the thematic structure of the field\. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analysis, while VOSviewer was used to visualise keyword co\-occurrence and collaboration patterns\. Publication activity was uneven for several decades and increased markedly after the mid\-2010s\. Citation analysis identified highly visible publications across piano pedagogy, music learning, educational psychology, and adjacent areas; citation counts were treated as indicators of visibility rather than research quality or theoretical maturity\. Keyword analysis indicated a pedagogical core connected with learner\-centred topics, including motivation, self\-efficacy, self\-regulated learning, creativity, and technology\-enhanced learning\. The collaboration maps showed small, weakly connected groups, although the bibliometric evidence does not by itself establish the theoretical maturity of the field\. Because the search used the address field, the dataset represents internationally indexed publications involving China\-affiliated authors rather than all research conducted in China\. The study therefore provides a bounded overview of the field and identifies priorities for broader database coverage, transparent keyword reporting, stronger collaboration, and empirical investigation of psychological and technological themes\.

## [Confucian Political Virtues in the Age of Technology](../publications/642ca559f43603f030e8.md)

Wenqi Ouyang; Minghui Xiong

This paper explores the potential of a Confucian framework to address the crisis of political virtue in the technological age\. It argues that under conditions of highly institutionalized and technologically mediated governance, the central normative problems no longer concern individual character alone, but also involve collective agents, the allocation of responsibility, and the procedural conditions of public participation\. The paper combines philosophical analysis of classical Confucian political virtue with critical engagement in contemporary debates on these challenges\. At the theoretical level, it develops a critical reconstruction of Confucian political virtues centred on ren \(benevolence\) and li \(propriety\)\. More specifically, the paper argues that li plays a pivotal mediating role in this reconstruction: while ren provides the value\-orientation of public concern, li translates this concern into role\-based responsibilities, public procedures, and adjustable institutional processes\. At the practical level, it examines two cases of Chinese digital governance—Hangzhou’s City Brain traffic system and Xiong’an New Area’s integrated governance evaluation framework—as sites for applying an operational checklist to assess how these reconstructed virtues can be institutionalized\. The paper argues that technology does not necessarily erode political virtue, but reshapes the conditions under which virtue is practised\. The co\-development of ren and li offers a non\-Western normative approach to reconnecting public concern with procedural legitimacy in technological governance\. Methodologically, it proposes an operational checklist for diagnosing and strengthening digital li across governance domains\.

## [Proximity as a factor of space cluster formation in a European peripheral economy: evidence from the Greek Space 4\.0 ecosystem](../publications/642d341666e60187b684.md)

Hrysi Stathaki; Pantoleon Skayannis; Yeoryios A\. Stamboulis; Apostolos Vetsikas

Introduction Space 4\.0 has transformed predominantly state\-led space activity into heterogeneous ecosystems requiring coordination across organizational and institutional boundaries\. Although proximity research explains knowledge exchange and collaboration, its governance role in emerging space ecosystems remains insufficiently specified\. This study examines how proximity shapes partner selection, collaboration design, and uncertainty management in the Greek Space 4\.0 ecosystem\. Methods This qualitative case\-study draws on 22 semi\-structured interviews with representatives of si\-Cluster firms and research organizations\. Theory\-informed thematic analysis combined deductive coding around five proximity dimensions with inductive pattern identification and constant comparison\. The analysis progressed from individual dimensions to recurring configurations, interaction mechanisms, functional effects, and the proximity profile\. Results Collaboration depended less on co\-location, cluster membership, or national affiliation than on context\-specific proximity configurations\. Cognitive and organizational proximity jointly shaped knowledge integration and project execution, while social and institutional proximity influenced expectations under uncertainty\. Misalignment generated coordination difficulties and constrained collaborative viability\. Geographical proximity played a conditional role and was partly offset by non\-spatial alignment, digital interaction, and temporary co\-presence\. The relative significance of proximity dimensions varied across project stages\. These findings informed the proximity profile, a qualitative framework for identifying relational complementarities, vulnerabilities, and alignment requirements in partnership design\. Discussion The findings position proximity as a dynamic governance mechanism whose effects arise from interactions among multiple dimensions\. Collaborative viability depends on evolving patterns of relational alignment rather than isolated dimensions or geographical concentration\. Instead of proposing an additional proximity dimension, the study advances a configurational interpretation of how established dimensions interact under particular contextual conditions\. The proximity profile translates this logic into a context\-sensitive basis for partnership assessment, while multi\-level governance depends on relational compatibility across EU/ESA, national, ecosystem, and project levels\.

## [The Affective Economy of Cringe: Salt Bae and the Politics of Online Celebrity](../publications/64386a06f864dab3f608.md)

Deniz Gürgen Atalay; Nilay Ulusoy

This article examines the affective economy of cringe as a constitutive mechanism within the visibility regimes of contemporary social media celebrity, focusing on the digital persona of Nusret Gökçe, globally known as “Salt Bae\.” Drawing on Sara Ahmed’s conceptualization of affective economies, Erving Goffman’s dramaturgical account of self\-presentation, and Alice Marwick’s framework of micro\-celebrity, the study explores how Gökçe’s hyper\-performative gestures and aesthetic excess generate tensions around authenticity, legitimacy, and public recognition\. Employing a qualitative, theory\-driven content analysis, the article investigates two widely circulated YouTube Shorts: one documenting Gökçe’s symbolic intrusion into the ritual space of the 2022 FIFA World Cup celebrations, and another centered on audience critique of luxury consumption through a popular restaurant review\. Across both cases, the analysis suggests that the disjunction between Gökçe’s intended authority and the audience’s ridicule becomes a key driver of circulation within platform\-based visibility economies\. Tracing Gökçe’s shift from viral charisma to a “cringe icon,” the study argues that contemporary celebrity can be sustained not only through admiration but also through ambivalent forms of engagement rooted in vicarious embarrassment, mockery, and moralized critique\. Ultimately, cringe emerges as a revealing affective mechanism through which digital publics negotiate cultural legitimacy, while simultaneously contributing to the persistence—and precarity—of online fame under platform capitalism\.

## [A dual layer explainable artificial intelligence approach for prediction and action in telecom customer churn analytics](../publications/643c4dc9824311fc304b.md)

Snehlata Barde; Sneha Soni; Dinesh Swami; Kaustubh Sutar

Churn is a critical problem in the telecommunications industry with high requirements on the accuracy of the machine learning models used to address this issue\. In this paper, we propose a framework that incorporates machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\) to solve the problem of customer churn in the telecommunications industry\. Using the Telco Customer Churn dataset, we present an XGBoost model that has been optimized to achieve high accuracy in predicting the churn of customers in the telecommunications industry\. Furthermore, SHAP and LIME are utilized to provide explanations for the model’s predicted outcomes for individual customers\. The level of agreement between these two explanation methods is calculated using Spearman’s correlation coefficient and the Jaccard index\. Based on the explanations provided by the XAI methods, the Strategic Actionability Score \(SAS\) is calculated to determine the business value of the model’s predictions\. The results of this framework illustrate the potential of using XAI methods in the telecommunications industry to provide explanations for the predictions of machine learning models and to translate these explanations into actionable business insights\. In addition, the proposed explainable AI\-based churn prediction framework supports sustainable customer relationship management, efficient resource utilization, and long\-term operational sustainability in the telecommunications industry by enabling telecom providers to optimize retention strategies and reduce unnecessary operational expenditure\. Using this framework, telecommunications companies can develop responsible and transparent strategies to retain their customers\.

## [From Assistance to Dependence: Investigating the Effects of Generative AI on Student Learning, Retention, and Study Effort](../publications/6444f30bd3f7017f21aa.md)

Najeeb Parkar

Purpose: Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\), including tools such as ChatGPT, is increasingly used by university students for explanations, summaries, problem\-solving, feedback, and academic support\. This paper examines whether such assistance supports learning or may encourage dependence that affects long\-term retention and independent thinking\. Methods: The study uses secondary research and a descriptive synthesis of published experimental studies, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta\-analyses\. No primary data were collected and no new statistical meta\-analysis was conducted\. Results: The reviewed studies generally report positive effects on academic performance and engagement\. Reported effect sizes include approximately g = 0\.712 across 69 experimental studies, Hedges’ g = 0\.577 across 37 studies, and an effect size of approximately 0\.804 across 57 studies\. However, one randomized controlled study reported 45\-day retention of 57\.5% for a ChatGPT\-assisted group compared with 68\.5% for a traditional\-learning group\. Conclusion: GenAI can be a useful learning assistant when students actively use it for explanation, feedback, comparison, and clarification\. However, completing tasks efficiently should not be treated as proof of deep or lasting learning\. Students should retain opportunities for independent recall, reasoning, analysis, and problem\-solving\.

## [UCEC: A Knowledge Graph\-Assisted Machine Learning for Molecular\-Mechanism\-Interpretable Natural Product\-Disease Association Prioritization](../publications/6447935e506de3d20fd2.md)

Wenyu Lu; Yihui Cai; Xiaoqian Peng; Shulan Mei; Xunkai Yin; Zhe Zheng; Zhenzhen Zhu; Songyun Xu; Hanyuan Zhang; Yue Wang; Weijiang Lin; Xia Zhang; Lihong Hu; Jian Liu

Abstract Natural products \(NPs\) have been considered a critical source of therapeutic drugs, but prioritizing NP\-disease associations remain challenging because supporting evidence is distributed across multiple ingredients, targets, protein interactions, and pathways\. Herein, we propose a knowledge graph\-assisted machine learning model: Uncertainty\-Calibrated Evidence\-Chains \(UCEC\) for prioritizing NP\-disease associations\. UCEC separates predicted association strength from the evidence\-conditioned stability of local mechanistic support\. On a proxy benchmark designed to recover graph\-supported indirect associations, evidence\-chain integration increased Hits@50 from 0\.392 to 0\.509, with 68\.8% of NPs indicating improved per\-NP AUPRC\. Source\-separated validation using HERB 2\.0 clinical trial records further supported candidate prioritization\. Thus, UCEC provides a reliability\-aware approach for prioritizing graph\-supported NP\-disease candidates and generating traceable mechanistic hypotheses for subsequent validation\.

## [Puerta Politécnica al Cosmos: understanding programme implementation in an itinerant science popularisation initiative in peri\-urban Mexico](../publications/6452071e8247e9a3a4e7.md)

Ma\. Luisa Montes Rojas; F\. Caballero‐Briones; David Alonso Leija Román

Although itinerant science popularisation initiatives extend opportunities for public engagement beyond established science communication infrastructure, limited empirical evidence exists on how programme implementation is shaped under peri\-urban conditions\. This Practice Insight examines Puerta Politécnica al Cosmos, an itinerant astronomy programme in north\-eastern Mexico, as an instrumental case for identifying recurring implementation conditions from which analytically transferable implementation insights were derived\. We employed a convergent mixed\-methods design integrating visitor surveys \(N = 404\), collaborator surveys \(N = 30\) and semi\-structured student interviews \(N = 40\) through analytical triangulation\. We identified four interdependent implementation conditions demonstrating how educational experiences, organisational coordination, participant engagement and territorial context interacted throughout programme delivery\. These conditions revealed implementation trade\-offs associated with accessibility, logistics, visitor management and technical infrastructure\. The study demonstrates how analytical triangulation can generate implementation knowledge that provides the basis for analytically transferable implementation insights to inform the planning, adaptation, delivery and evaluation of itinerant science popularisation initiatives in peri\-urban and other territorially underserved communities\.
