## [Comparative evaluation of plaque removal efficacy of manual and electric interdental brushes around orthodontic brackets: A randomized clinical study](../publications/646f33d13acf7df452b8.md)

Prachi Agarwal; Vijay Agarwal; Hari Narayan Choudhary; Pallavi Goswami; Bhavya Gupta; Kanika Agarwal

Introduction: Fixed orthodontic appliances increase plaque accumulation owing to the presence of brackets and arch wires, making oral hygiene maintenance difficult and increasing the risk of gingivitis and enamel demineralization\. Adjunctive interdental cleaning tools, including interdental brushes \(IDBs\), are recommended\.Aim and Objectives: To compare the plaque removal efficacy of manual and electric interdental brushes around orthodontic brackets\.Materials and Methods: A randomized crossover controlled trial was conducted on 60 patients \(aged 12–35 years\) undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment\. Participants were allocated into two groups \(n = 30 each\): Group I used a manual IDB \(Stim IDB\) and Group II \(U Brush\) used an electric IDB\. Dental plaque was disclosed and scored across eight classified buccal tooth surface zones per tooth at two time intervals \(T1 and T2, four weeks apart\), using a binary plaque index\. The Mann–Whitney U test and Wilcoxon signed\-rank test were applied for intergroup and intragroup comparisons, respectively \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\.Results: The two IDBs showed statistically significant plaque reduction at T1 and T2 levels \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. However, the electric IDB showed a significantly higher degree of plaque reduction in all surface regions compared to the manual IDB\. The mean plaque reduction around brackets was twice that of the manual IDB \(0\.708 ± 0\.045 vs 0\.353 ± 0\.128\)\.Conclusion: It can be concluded that manual as well as electric interdental brushes both have the capacity to decrease the plaque deposits around the orthodontic brackets\. Electric IDB proved to be much better in plaque removal especially in the area around the brackets\.

## [A Classroom Intervention Study to Assess the Potential of a 360\-Degree Virtual Reality Learning Environment to Enhance Conceptual Understanding and Engagement in Physics](../publications/64764f672738d34291d7.md)

Eliane Merki; Andreas Lichtenberger; Volker Eisenlauer; A\. Vaterlaus; Sarah Isabelle Hofer

Abstract The use of individual student laptops and tablets in K\-12 classrooms enables large\-scale implementation of innovative learning technologies\. Theories of multimedia and immersive learning suggest that immersive features can influence cognitive and affective learning processes\. Therefore, 360\-degree virtual reality learning environments \(VRLEs\) represent a promising area for further investigation\. This study compares an interactive desktop\-based low\-immersive 360\-degree VRLE with a traditional paper\-and\-pencil approach to investigate effects on students’ conceptual understanding of Galilean transformations of uniform motion in position\-time graphs and on student engagement\. Both conditions worked with multiple representations within a Predict\-Observe\-Explain framework to support active learning\. A total of 313 students \(176 female, 137 male\) from the advanced track of upper secondary school participated in the pre\-post classroom study\. Conceptual understanding was assessed using the Inventory for Galilean Transformation of Uniform Motion in Position\-Time Graphs\. Students in both conditions improved their understanding, but no significant difference between conditions was observed\. However, students using the VRLE reported a stronger inclination to perform well\. These findings suggest that 360\-degree VRLEs may support certain aspects of self\-reported student engagement related to effort, but further research is needed to better understand how learning outcomes can be improved\.

## [Genetic Liability to Psychiatric Disorder and Risk of Musculoskeletal Diseases: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Study](../publications/647ae233bd72c01606c5.md)

Xiaohai Luo; Ning Wu; 王兆福; Jingzu Ma; Xiaoyu Zhang

Background: Psychiatric disorders, particularly major depressive disorder \(MDD\), are increasingly recognized as systemic diseasesthat may predispose individualsto a range of physical comorbidities\. Epidemiological studies have reported associations between depression and musculoskeletal diseases; however, causal inferences remain limited due to confounding factors and reverse causation\. This study aims to investigate the bidirectional causal relationships between common psychiatric disorders and musculoskeletal outcomes using a Mendelian randomization \(MR\) framework\. Methods: A bidirectional two\-sample MR analysis was conducted using summary statistics from a large\-scale genome\-wide association study \(GWAS\) in European ancestry populations\. Genetic instruments for seven psychiatric disorders were obtained from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, while musculoskeletal outcomes were sourced from the IEU Open GWAS and UK Biobank\. Causal effects were primarily estimated using an inverse variance weighted model, with sensitivity analyses conducted using the weighted median \(WM\) and MR\-Egger methods\. Established diagnostic methods were employed to assess horizontal pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and robustness, and false discovery rate \(FDR\) corrections were applied to account for multiple testing\. Results: The genetic liability to MDD showed the most consistent evidence of association with osteoarthritis \(OA\) and osteomyelitis \(OM\)\. The association with OA appeared to be the most stable overall, while the findings regarding OM should be interpreted more cautiously due to the relatively limited number of available instrumental variables\. Nominal associations were also observed for fracture and osteoporosis \(OP\) in relation to MDD, as well as between autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\) and fracture risk and between anorexia nervosa \(AN\) and fracture risk; however, these findings were either modest in magnitude or did not remain significant after multiple\-testing correction, and thusshould be considered exploratory results\. There was no strong evidence supporting a reverse causal effect of musculoskeletal diseases on psychiatric disorders\. Conclusions: This MR study suggests that genetic liability to MDD may be associated with susceptibility to specific musculoskeletal diseases, particularly OA, and more cautiously, OM\. These findings should be interpreted with caution, especially for associations based on limited instrumental support or modest effect sizes, and require replication in different populations\.

## [Increasing domain asymptotics for covariate\-based nonparametric Bayesian intensity estimation with Gaussian and Besov–Laplace priors](../publications/648c1c46c5925c1ff53b.md)

Patric Dolmeta; Matteo Giordano

We study the problem of estimating the intensity function of a covariate\-driven point process based on observations of the points and covariates over a large window\. We consider the nonparametric Bayesian approach, and show that a wide class of Gaussian priors, combined with flexible link functions, achieves minimax\-optimal posterior contraction rates in the increasing domain asymptotics and under the assumption that the covariates be ergodic\. We also employ Besov\-Laplace priors, which are popular in imaging and inverse problems due to their edge\-preserving and sparsity\-promoting properties\. We prove that these yield optimal estimation of spatially inhomogeneous intensities belonging to Besov spaces with low integrability index\. These results are based on a general concentration theorem that extends recent findings from the literature\. To corroborate the theory, we provide extensive numerical simulations, implementing the considered procedures via suitable posterior sampling schemes\. Further, we present two real data analyses motivated by applications in forestry and the environmental sciences\.

## [Mechanization pathways in cotton cultivation: adoption, barriers, and productivity implications in India](../publications/648c91fe16d54dcd5345.md)

Arjun Chouriya; Peeyush Soni; Pradeep Kumar; Naseeb Singh; Harsh Nagar

This study addresses the critical role of cotton as a leading cash crop in India, focusing on how mechanization influences productivity and farm profitability amid global competition with major producers like China and the USA\. Mechanization practices were evaluated across key stages of cotton cultivation—field preparation, sowing, spraying, weeding, and harvesting—through a comprehensive review of the available literature\. The analysis quantified machinery adoption, identified operational gaps, and assessed impacts on cost and labor efficiency\. Findings show progressive but uneven mechanization, with advanced use in field preparation and spraying, while sowing and harvesting remain largely dependent on manual labor\. Barriers include limited access to suitable machinery, high costs, and insufficient farmer awareness\. Where implemented, mechanization improved operational efficiency, reduced production costs, and increased yields and profits\. Expanding mechanization offers significant potential to strengthen India’s cotton sector, increasing productivity and global competitiveness\. Addressing current gaps through technology promotion, tailored machinery, and support initiatives can enhance cotton farming practices and farmer incomes\.

## [The hive mind is a single reinforcement learning agent](../publications/64903879ac56969de9d6.md)

Karthik Soma; Yann Bouteiller; Heiko Hamann; Giovanni Beltrame

Abstract Decision\-making is an essential attribute of any intelligent agent or group\. Natural systems are known to converge to effective strategies through at least two distinct mechanisms: collective decision\-making via imitation of others, and trial\-and\-error by a single agent\. This paper establishes an equivalence between these two paradigms\. We show that the emergent distributed cognition \(sometimes referred to as the hive mind \) arising from individuals following simple, local imitation\-based rules is that of a single online reinforcement learning \(RL\) agent aggregating action\-value samples from many parallel instances of a multi\-armed bandit\. More specifically, we show that, in the blindly imitative weighted voter model of honey bees’ waggle dance, the update rule through which this macro\-agent learns is an RL algorithm that we coin Maynard\-Cross Learning \. Our analysis implies that a group of individuals following simple imitative strategies can be equivalent to a more complex learning entity, substantiating the idea that group\-level intelligence may explain how seemingly irrational individual behaviors are selected in nature\. Beyond biology, the framework offers new tools for analyzing economic and social systems where individuals imitate successful strategies, effectively participating in a collective learning process\. Our findings may further inform the design of scalable RL\-inspired collective systems in artificial domains\.

## [Tracking recent extremes and interannual variability of global fire emissions using a near\-real\-time extension to the Global Fire Emissions Database](../publications/64983556aab58610cda6.md)

Yang Chen; Guido R\. van der Werf; M\. Mu; Dave van Wees; Joanne V\. Hall; Louis Giglio; Roland Vernooij; Douglas C\. Morton; Li Xu; Tianjia Liu; Rebecca C\. Scholten; Shane Coffield; Melanie B\. Follette‐Cook; Lesley E\. Ott; James T\. Randerson

Abstract\. The Global Fire Emissions Database \(GFED\) is widely used to quantify spatiotemporal variability and long\-term trends in burned area and fire emissions, supporting assessments of fire impacts on ecosystems and atmospheric composition\. GFED has historically relied on observations from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer \(MODIS\), but orbital drift and planned sensor decommissioning pose challenges for maintaining record continuity and near\-real\-time \(NRT\) monitoring\. Here we present the GFED5 near\-real\-time extension \(GFED5NRT\), a global fire emissions dataset that enables daily NRT analyses using active fire observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite \(VIIRS\)\. GFED5NRT uses biome\- and region\-specific lookup tables of effective fire area and fuel consumption, derived from VIIRS observations and standard GFED5 datasets, to estimate burned area and emissions from VIIRS active fire counts in a manner consistent with the GFED5 time series\. Comparisons with GFED5 and independent datasets show strong agreement in spatial patterns, seasonal cycles, and interannual variability of fire activity\. GFED5NRT captures recent major fire extremes and provides daily global NRT estimates of burned area and emissions for multiple trace gases and aerosols\. Together, GFED5 and GFED5NRT provides a coherent framework for long\-term analyses and NRT monitoring of evolving fire regimes in a changing climate\. The GFED5NRT dataset is publicly available at https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.18702700 \(Chen et al\., 2026\)\.

## [Neurologist\-focused workflows for immune effector cell\-associated neurotoxicity syndrome in CAR T\-cell therapy and CD3\-engaging bispecific antibodies](../publications/6498c8b319626c7616c4.md)

Walid Alesefir; Mariam Hejazi; Basil Alashger; Abdulrahman Abodahab; Menna Abdelrazek; Karma Abouelnaga; Sara Koudeimati; Abdullah Alshibani; Lara Aljohani

Objective To synthesize current evidence into a neurologist\-focused workflow for early recognition, bedside monitoring, diagnostic triage, mitigation, and therapy\-specific surveillance of immune effector cell\-associated neurotoxicity syndrome \(ICANS\)\. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar were searched in English from inception through 25 March 2026\. Of 201 records, 18 duplicates were removed, 183 were screened, 157 full texts were assessed, and 26 studies were included in a narrative synthesis\. The selection process was reported using applicable PRISMA 2020 elements and the narrative presentation was evaluated using SANRA\. Results Evidence supports early neurologic co\-management in selected high\-risk patients, serial language\- and attention\-sensitive bedside assessment, and clinically triggered rather than routine electroencephalography\. Pilot neurocognitive data suggest that subtle decline may precede deterioration on the Immune Effector Cell\-Associated Encephalopathy \(ICE\) score\. Bispecific\-antibody programs generally show lower neurotoxicity burdens than many CAR T\-cell platforms but create repeated risk windows around step\-up dosing and outpatient transition\. Delayed B\-cell maturation antigen \(BCMA\)\-associated movement and neurocognitive syndromes remain an important safety signal, although therapeutic evidence is largely observational or case based\. Conclusion The evidence supports documenting a baseline neurologic phenotype, performing serial bedside monitoring, deploying electroencephalography and neuroimaging when results may change management, and maintaining product\-specific vigilance for delayed syndromes\. Tiered pathways are needed for community and resource\-limited settings\.

## [Love as a foundation for global citizenship in human\-centred AI\-driven higher education institutions – a theoretical exploration](../publications/649968a6ce1525066461.md)

Claude‐Hélène Mayer

Purpose This article aims at exploring global citizenship in the context of higher education institutions \(HEIs\) which are increasingly affected by artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-driven interactions\. By using AI in a human\-centred way, educators can expand ways to create global citizenship, offer personalised and empathetic learning while transcending conventional boundaries of education\. AI technologies, including natural language processing, machine translation and adaptive learning systems, enable learners to engage with diverse linguistic and cultural materials in increasingly meaningful ways\. These tools facilitate immersive language learning, simulate intercultural interactions and provide real\-time feedback connected to individual needs in contemporary HEIs\. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a theoretical/conceptual approach\. Findings While human\-centred AI\-driven HEIs are gaining importance, the need to create awareness of character strengths and human\-centred new learning environments increases as well\. In this article, it is argued that pedagogical love, as a character strength, becomes more important in contemporary HEIs than ever before\. By integrating AI thoughtfully and ethically into curricula, educators and institutions can contribute to the education of empathetic, multilingual global citizens\. Research limitations/implications This research is limited to a qualitative theoretical and conceptual study and may build the base for future empirical studies\. Practical implications Love, as a character strength, might support mental health, well\-being and human interconnectedness\. Originality/value This approach can strengthen the role of HEIs in creating a more peaceful, integrated world\.

## [Multi\-Objective Dhole Optimization for Saturation\-Aware Autonomous Underwater Forensic Search and Evidence Recovery Missions](../publications/649f559d49d8cda1ae69.md)

Marimuthu Sree Rajeswari; Praveena Narayanan; Aravind Balakrishnan; Manikandan Rajagopal; Manivasagam Shankar; Nandhini Mahadevan

Background: Underwater forensic investigations frequently involve searching, locating, and recovering submerged human remains and associated forensic evidence under challenging environmental conditions\. Efficient coordination of multiple unmanned underwater vehicles \(UUVs\) can support forensic investigators by reducing search time, improving spatial coverage, and limiting unnecessary energy consumption during underwater recovery operations\. This study proposes a Multi\-Objective Dhole Optimization Algorithm \(MO\-DOA\) for discrete saturation\-aware allocation\. Methods: The method maps each candidate to a continuous latent score matrix, decodes it to UUV\-to\-region assignments, repairs assignment and saturation violations, and uses Pareto dominance with a diversity\-preserving external archive to select leaders for the Dhole Optimization Algorithm search, encircling, and attack phases\. Results: Evaluation uses an 800 m × 500 m maritime benchmark with eight UUVs, four clustered target regions, and three inaccessible reef zones\. In the supplied 20\-run results package, MO\-DOA attained HV = 0\.921, IGD = 0\.048, mission effectiveness = 93\.8, energy/travel cost = 142\.6, threat exposure = 0\.220, saturation deviation = 0\.50, and runtime = 10\.7 s, outperforming CEA, Improved WOA, MDO, IMMP\-GWO, and IPSO\-VP on the reported criteria\. Convergence curves show earlier improvement and sustained Pareto\-front quality\. Conclusion: The findings support MO\-DOA as a compact Pareto\-based allocation framework, subject to final verification of the supplied run\-level statistics\.

## [Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation](../publications/64a21fe9ddc3fd89fb29.md)

Shuo Han; Ziqing Hu

Reinforcement learning has become a widely used approach to post\-training large language models\. In a typical implementation, learning is off\-policy: The policy generating the responses differs from the policy being trained because of training\-inference mismatch or policy staleness in asynchronous training\. This discrepancy is commonly addressed by importance sampling, whose ratio is usually regularized in practice through truncation, masking, or clipping\. Under regularized importance sampling, the importance\-weighted policy gradient is no longer invariant to constant shifts in the reward\. This invariance is recovered by using the covariance between the reward and the importance\-weighted score as the estimand, which coincides with the policy gradient when the ratio is not regularized\. This note develops this covariance perspective for both sequence\-level and token\-level importance sampling\. The covariance perspective reveals the roles of the group\-mean baseline and score centering in policy gradient estimation\. Both perform centering in covariance estimation, but they differ in the mean being subtracted: The group\-mean baseline uses a sample mean, whereas score centering uses a population mean\. The two lead to distinct unbiased covariance estimators with different variances\. Whether both forms of centering should be used simultaneously depends on whether importance sampling is applied at the sequence level or at the token level\. With sequence\-level importance sampling, score centering adds no benefit once the group\-mean baseline is used; with token\-level importance sampling, using the group\-mean baseline without score centering generally introduces bias when the importance ratio is regularized\.

## [Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles](../publications/64ae2f4658d68b646a49.md)

Sophia Ohnemus; Albert Dasí; Ahmed Ramadan; Joachim Greiner; Eike M\. Wülfers; Matthew R\. Stoyek; Linda Tillert; Johannes Vierock; Thomas Alexander Quinn; Peter Karl Kohl; Patrick M\. Boyle; Viviane Timmermann; Franziska Schneider‐Warme

Abstract Cardiac re‐entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death\. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti‐arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light‐gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated\. Previous studies assessed either cation \(e\.g\. ChR2\) or anion \(e\.g\. GtACR1\) non‐selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes\. Recently identified light‐gated K \+ channels \(e\.g\. WiChR\) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored\. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR\. Single‐cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca 2\+ \(by 42\.6% and 52\.6%, respectively\), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes \(by 4\.0%\), suggesting lower pro‐arrhythmogenic risk\. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na \+ \(by 15\.1% vs \. 0\.1% and 3\.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1\), consistent with the residual Na \+ permeability of currently available K \+ ‐conducting channelrhodopsins\. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re‐entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm 2 \. Complementary tissue‐scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na \+ channel inactivation \(ChR2 and partly GtACR1\), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities \(large‐conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR\)\. Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms\. image Translational perspective Re‐entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death\. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter‐defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury\. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high‐voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light‐gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells\. Determining which light‐gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation\. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts\. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non‐selective cation‐ and anion‐conducting channels terminate re‐entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca 2\+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro‐arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety\. K \+ ‐conducting channels largely avoid this pro‐arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na \+ accumulation attributable to residual Na \+ permeability\. Together, these trade‐offs define clear clinical implications: K \+ ‐conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K \+ selectivity and red‐shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood‐perfused myocardium become available\. Key points We use computational simulations to compare cation non‐selective \(ChR2\), anion non‐selective \(GtACR1\) and K \+ ‐selective \(WiChR\) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re‐entrant arrhythmia\. Single‐cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca 2\+ , which is minimized when using WiChR\. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation\. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re‐entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities\. Tissue‐scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na \+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins \(ChR2, GtACR1\), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large‐conductance channels \(GtACR1, WiChR\), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel&\#x27;s reversal potential at high light levels\.

## [IN THE VIEWS OF THE JADIDS, THE ROLE OF LABOR IN HUMAN LIFE AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOCIETY](../publications/64b78cf45801bfbfe180.md)

Muxtarov Utkirbek Mutalibjonovich

This scientific article highlights the role of labor in human life and societal development in the views of the Jadids\. It analyzes the views of Jadid enlighteners on hard work, learning, mastering a profession, honesty, and moral perfection\. It is also revealed that in the works of Jadid representatives such as Mahmudkhodja Behbudi, Abdulla Avloni, and Abdurauf Fitrat, labor is interpreted as an important factor that spiritually elevates a person and develops their abilities and capabilities\.

## [Academic buoyancy and engagement in EFL learning: a latent growth curve modeling analysis of their dynamic relationship](../publications/64bfa914ef2b12f9bfae.md)

Tengyao Zhang

Grounded in the conservation of resources theory, this 16\-week longitudinal study tracked the developmental trajectories of academic buoyancy and learning engagement among college\-level English\-as\-a\-foreign\-language \(EFL\) learners in China via repeated questionnaire administrations\. Employing latent growth curve modeling \(LGCM\), this research analyzed changes in both constructs and explored developmental associations between academic buoyancy—a core personal learning resource—and engagement over time\. Key findings include: \(1\) Both academic buoyancy and learning engagement exhibited overall upward trends across the semester, with substantial individual variability observed in initial states and growth rates; \(2\) Higher latent intercept of academic buoyancy correlated with greater subsequent growth in this construct, whereas the initial state of learning engagement showed no significant association with its own developmental trajectory; \(3\) The latent intercept of academic buoyancy was positively associated with both the intercept and growth rate of learning engagement, while growth in academic buoyancy aligned with parallel growth in engagement\. This study illuminates the dynamic, malleable nature of academic buoyancy and learning engagement in EFL contexts and illustrates the value of LGCM for examining developmental patterns in second language acquisition research\.

## [Strip flatness prediction in cold rolling: a review of models, challenges, and emerging directions](../publications/64cd530396da9ef2eac0.md)

Giorgio Previati; Federico Maria Ballo

Abstract Cold rolling is one of the most widely applied metal\-forming processes, where strip flatness is a critical quality requirement affecting downstream manufacturability, dimensional accuracy and product performance\. Flatness defects arise from non\-uniform longitudinal stresses generated through tightly coupled interactions between roll bite mechanics, roll stack deformation, friction and lubrication, material behaviour and post\-bite buckling\. Although numerous modelling strategies exist, the literature remains fragmented across analytical, numerical, hybrid and data driven approaches, making it difficult to identify the most appropriate tools for prediction and control\. This review provides a unified framework for strip flatness prediction in cold rolling, presenting a structured taxonomy of modelling approaches and evaluating their assumptions, predictive capability, computational cost and industrial applicability\. Analytical and semi\-analytical models are compared with numerical techniques and hybrid coupled formulations\. Key transversal components, including constitutive laws, friction and lubrication models and buckling formulations, are examined with respect to their influence on widthwise stress distributions and the formation of flatness defects\. Recent developments in physics\-based, data driven and hybrid modelling, including digital twins and reduced\-order models, are discussed with emphasis on their potential to meet the real\-time requirements of advanced flatness\-control systems\. Major research gaps are identified in mixed\-lubrication modelling, advanced constitutive descriptions, transient buckling prediction, standardised validation benchmarks and hybrid physics–data driven modelling to support digital twin deployment\. By synthesising current knowledge and highlighting emerging research directions, this review provides guidance for selecting and developing strip modelling strategies capable of supporting high precision crown and flatness control in modern, data\-enriched rolling mills\.

## [A machine learning assisted net zero maturity model for MSMEs in Eastern Uttar Pradesh India](../publications/64d261fada34142358ef.md)

Gaurav Upadhyay; Cherian Samuel; Dilawar Ahmad Bhat; Nitesh Thakur

Global warming and climate change have emerged as the predominant issues of this decade\. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises \(MSMEs\) substantially contribute to global Greenhouse Gas \(GHG\) emissions\. However, there are limited strategies specifically designed for MSMEs, especially in the Indian context\. To formulate customized strategies or action plans for MSMEs, assessing their preparedness for Net Zero practices are essential\. A maturity assessment model has been proposed to assess the organizational readiness of Indian MSMEs for the Net Zero transition\. The model comprises four parameters: awareness and engagement; knowledge and capabilities; planning and strategy; and physical actions\. Based on these parameters, data is collected from various MSMEs and experts through surveys and interviews\. Data analysis \(DA\) techniques and supervised Machine Learning \(ML\) classification algorithms have been used to categorize MSMEs into four maturity levels\. Following the implementation of the model to a varied cohort of MSMEs operating in various domains in India, the findings indicate that 26% of the MSMEs were at an insufficient maturity level, 49% were at a primary maturity level, 17% were at an evolving maturity level, and only 8% were operating at a consolidated maturity level\. Results show that 75% of MSMEs operate at the earliest two maturity levels\. The proposed maturity model can help MSMEs identify gaps in their organizational readiness and prioritize actions supporting the Net Zero transition\. Existing studies have primarily focused on individual sustainability dimensions, whereas the proposed framework provides a comprehensive Net Zero maturity assessment for Indian MSMEs\.

## [OpenTyreF1: A Data\-Driven Mobile Platform for Formula 1 Telemetry Analysis, Tyre\-Degradation Modelling and Counterfactual Race\-Strategy Simulation](../publications/64d38d48571e6a0f64f7.md)

Atharva Joshi; Prachi Jain; Ankit Sawalakhe; Araju Yelekar; Devshree Khodke; Kripa Patil

Formula 1 publishes one of the richest open telemetry streams in professional sport, yet most public tools built on it are descriptive: they show what happened and stop there\. This paper presents OpenTyreF1, a full\-stack system that turns that data into decision support on a mobile phone\. The system integrates three public sources \(Jolpica\-F1/Ergast, OpenF1 and FastF1\) into one normalised 15\-table relational corpus of 237,308 records covering 492 races from 2002 to 2026\. On top of this corpusit builds a shared clean\-lap filter, a gradient\-boosted \(XGBoost\) lap\-time model, a counterfactual stint\-strategy simulator, a 1,500\-run Monte Carlo outcome estimator, seven pit\-wall decision modules and a grounded question\-answering assistant, all served by a FastAPI backend to an Expo/React Native app\. Evaluated on 12 completely unseen races, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0\.893 s, RMSE of 1\.205 s and R 2 of 0\.978, beating the strongest naive baseline by 0\.270 s\. An ablation shows that predicting a lap’s offset from its race median, rather than the absolute lap time, cuts error four\-fold, a far larger effect than adding features\. The results show that, for motorsport data of this size, careful lap admission, target design and leakage\-free evaluation matter more than the choice of learner\.

## [Limited sex‐specific structural alterations across common epilepsies: A worldwide ENIGMA study](../publications/64e6cad3cc5bf96525a9.md)

Huantao Wen; Bin Wan; Taha Gholipour; Ke Xie; Judy Chen; Bianca Serio; Meike D\. Hettwer; Marina K\. M\. Alvim; Donatello Arienzo; Rafael Batista João; Tobias Bauer; Andrea Bernasconi; Neda Bernasconi; Paolo Bonanni; Maria Eugenia Caligiuri; Fernando Cendes; Raphaël Christin; Luis Concha; Arielle Dascal; Edward Davoodi Boyd; Orrin Devinsky; Niels K\. Focke; Francesco Fortunato; Marian Galovic; Antonio Gambardella; Renzo Guerrini; Sean N\. Hatton; Mirana Iliza; Sara K\. Inati; Victoria Lyn Ives\-Deliperi; Robert‐Paul Juster; Jonathan K\. Kleen; Mohamad Zakaria Koubeissi; Angelo Labate; Sara Larivière; Meng Law; Matteo Lenge; Stefano Meletti; Patrick B\. Moloney; Marlo Naish; Alexander Ngo; Terence John O&\#x27;Brien; Raluca Pana; Sofia Maria Panzeri; Heath Pardoe; Erik Hans Ulrich Rauf; Antonella Riva; Raúl Rodríguez‐Cruces; Jessica Royer; Theodor Rüber; Ella Sahlas; Lucas Scárdua‐Silva; K Schubert; Leigh N\. Sepeta; Mariasavina Severino; Benjamin Sinclair; Hamid Soltanian\-zadeh A; Travis R\. Stoub; Pasquale Striano; Sophia I\. Thomopoulos; Nina V\. Valientes; Anna Elisabetta Vaudano; Lucy E\. Vivash; Clarissa Lin Yasuda; Paul M\. Thompson; Sanjay M\. Sisodiya; Carrie R\. McDonald; Boris C\. Bernhardt; Sofie Louise Valk

Abstract Objective Epilepsy is characterized by widespread cortical and subcortical structural alterations beyond the epileptic zone\. Importantly, the clinical manifestation of epilepsy, including seizure types, psychiatric comorbidities, and treatment responses, has been shown to differ between sexes\. However, sex differences in structural alterations in epilepsy are seldomly reported in neuroimaging studies, partly due to limited sample sizes and single‐center designs\. We therefore tested whether epilepsy‐related structural alterations differ between males and females, and whether the associations between structural measures and clinical characteristics vary by sex\. Methods We analyzed clinician‐assigned biological sex differences in common epilepsies and their related clinical variables using structural neuroimaging biomarkers in an international multicenter cohort of 1253 epilepsy patients and 1077 healthy controls\. We studied cortical thickness and subcortical volume in temporal lobe epilepsy \(TLE\) and genetic generalized epilepsy \(GGE\)\. Results Both male and female patients with TLE showed widespread cortical and subcortical alterations in sex‐stratified analyses, whereas GGE showed more extensive alterations in female patients and only subtle alterations in male patients\. However, no significant sex‐by‐diagnosis interactions were identified in either the TLE \( t = −2\.153 to 1\.705, all p FDR &gt;\.05\) or GGE \( t = −1\.797 to 2\.774, all p FDR &gt;\.05\) cohort\. Likewise, no significant interactions were found between sex and age at onset \( t TLE = −1\.835 to 1\.092, t GGE = −2\.394 to 1\.392, all p FDR &gt;\.05\) or disease duration \( t TLE = −2\.643 to 2\.048, t GGE = −1\.234 to 2\.017, all p FDR &gt;\.05\) in either patient group\. Significance Overall, although sex differences in behavioral and clinical outcomes of epilepsy have been consistently reported in previous studies, our results indicate that sex‐related clinical differences in epilepsy are not strongly captured by macroscale structural magnetic resonance imaging measures, and may instead arise from hormonal, neurochemical, or functional–network mechanisms\.

## [Оптимизација питања за квизове уз помоћ вештачке интелигенције](../publications/64f2df0abe2ef571fe9a.md)

Milos Josipovic

This paper presents a web application for creating and taking quizzes that integrates artificial intelligence into the educational process\. Particular emphasis is placed on the automatic generation of quiz questions using AI, significantly accelerating and simplifying the quiz preparation process\. In addition, several AI\-powered functionalities have been implemented with the aim of enhancing the teaching and learning experience, improving educational outcomes, and increasing the efficiency of both teachers and students\.

## [Gender\-based variations in learning styles: a study of higher education students](../publications/650a5fa825bf6e5072a0.md)

Muhammad Abo ul Hassan Rashid; Rashida Qureshi

Learning style research increasingly examines whether gender shapes how students engage with instruction, yet findings across disciplines and cultural contexts remain inconsistent, and most studies rely on small, single\-institution samples\. This study examined gender\-based differences in learning style preferences among a large, multi\-institutional sample of higher education students in Pakistan\. Learning style preferences were assessed using the Grasha–Riechmann Student Learning Style Scales \(GRSLSS\), which measure six dimensions: Independent, Avoidant, Collaborative, Dependent, Competitive, and Participant\. Gender differences were tested using independent\-samples t\-tests, with Cohen&\#x27;s d used to estimate effect sizes and Pearson correlations used to examine relationships among subscales\. Male students scored significantly higher than female students on four of six subscales — Avoidant, Dependent, Competitive, and Participant \(all p &lt; \.05\) — while Independent and Collaborative styles showed no significant gender difference\. However, all effect sizes were negligible to small \(d = 0\.05–0\.11\), indicating limited practical significance despite statistical significance driven by the large sample\. Independent, Competitive, and Participant styles were moderately\-to\-strongly intercorrelated \(r = \.51–\.60\), suggesting a shared underlying orientation toward active, engaged learning\. Gender accounts for only a small proportion of variance in learning style preferences among this population, with substantial overlap between male and female students\. Rather than tailoring instruction to gender, higher education institutions should adopt flexible, learner\-centered pedagogical approaches that accommodate individual variation\. Limitations related to subscale reliability and the cross\-sectional design are discussed, along with directions for future instrument validation and longitudinal research\.

## [3D\-Based building damage assessment and visualization for sustainable maintenance planning: A case study of the Universitas Muhammadiyah Sukabumi rectorate building](../publications/650e7f682b3790b0d6f6.md)

Nia Kartika; Pratikso; Henny Pratiwi Adi

Background: Effective building maintenance requires systematic damage assessment and integrated condition information to support informed decisions and sustainable infrastructure management\. However, conventional inspection reports often lack spatial visualization, limiting the identification and management of damaged building components\. Aims: This study aims to assess building damage and develop a three\-dimensional \(3D\) visualization model integrating damage characteristics, severity classifications, repair recommendations, and cost estimates to support sustainable maintenance planning\. Method: A descriptive case study was conducted at the Universitas Muhammadiyah Sukabumi Rectorate Building through regulatory reviews, technical documentation, field inspections, damage severity analysis, and 3D modeling using Autodesk Revit 2025\. Results: The assessment identified 108 damage instances involving architectural components, comprising 77 minor, 19 moderate, and 12 severe cases\. The overall building damage level was 11\.01%, indicating minor damage\. The developed 3D model linked damaged components with spatial locations, damage dimensions, severity levels, repair recommendations, and cost estimates\. The total estimated repair cost reached IDR 149,175,912\. Conclusion: Integrating damage assessment with 3D visualization facilitates structured damage documentation, component identification, and maintenance prioritization, providing a practical foundation for more systematic and potentially resource\-efficient building maintenance planning\.

## [Aerobic anoxygenic phototrophs are widespread and active members of Greenland Ice Sheet microbiomes](../publications/6521f457bc23c7163f95.md)

Christoph Keuschnig; Helen K\. Feord; Emily L\. M\. Broadwell; Athanasios Zervas; Martyn Tranter; Alexandre Magno Anesio; Liane G\. Benning

The Greenland Ice Sheet \(GrIS\) hosts diverse microbial communities where glacier ice algae, snow algae, and cyanobacteria act as key primary producers across bare ice, snow, and cryoconite habitats, yet the ecological roles of associated heterotrophic prokaryotes remain poorly understood\. Aerobic anoxygenic phototrophs \(AAPs\), known to couple light harvesting to heterotrophy and enter trophic relationships with algae in marine systems, suggesting they may represent an important but underexplored functional group in supraglacial ecosystems\. Using genome\-resolved analyses of supraglacial metagenomes and metatranscriptomes from Greenland, we recovered nine AAP metagenome\-assembled genomes \(MAGs\) \(4% of the 229 recovered MAGs\) consistently enriched in bare ice and cryoconite communities, but nearly absent in snow\. A meta\-analysis of 2 451 public metagenomes supported this cryospheric habitat association\. AAP\_MAGs were disproportionally enriched in thiosulfate oxidation and bicarbonate\-dependent carbon assimilation pathways relative to other MAGs\. Iron and CO oxidation pathways were broadly distributed across the GrIS microbiome, including in AAPs, together suggesting adaptation strategies in supraglacial ecosystems\. Genomic evidence for algal coupling via sulfoquinovose degradation was limited\. Overall, we document that AAPs are active and widespread in weathering crust habitats, highlighting their potential contributions to biogeochemical cycling in supraglacial ecosystems\.

## [Long\-term sport participation is associated with a selective auditory\-musical performance profile](../publications/6523d2cda99960cdd174.md)

Bartłomiej Jacek Swebodziński; Kuba Korta; Jacek Łantowski

Long\-term sport participation has been associated with selective differences in temporal and perceptual\-cognitive processing, but it remains unclear whether such differences extend to auditory\-musical perception\. We examined overall and component\-level performance on the Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia \(MBEA\) in 83 participants: 31 sport\-trained participants and 52 psychology\-student controls\. Between\-group differences were tested using ordinary least\-squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors, adjusting for age and years of formal musical education; Holm correction was applied across the six MBEA subtests\. Sport\-trained participants obtained higher Total MBEA scores than controls \( B = 15\.34, p = 0\.002\)\. At the component level, they scored higher on the a priori temporal outcomes Rhythm \( B = 2\.87, Holm\-adjusted p = 0\.030\) and Meter \( B = 3\.72, Holm\-adjusted p = 0\.012\)\. An exploratory difference was also observed for Memory \( B = 4\.20, Holm\-adjusted p = 0\.002\), whereas Contour did not remain significant after correction and no significant differences were found for Scale or Interval \. Supplementary d ′ models and their leave\-one\-out sensitivity analyses converged on the same pattern for Rhythm , Meter , and Memory \. Within the sport\-trained group, years of sport participation were not positively associated with Total MBEA performance after adjustment for age \( B = −0\.78, p = 0\.108\)\. These findings suggest that long\-term sport participation is associated with a selective rather than generalized profile of auditory\-musical differences, with the clearest group differences in temporal processing and an exploratory difference in recognition memory\. The cross\-sectional design does not permit causal attribution to sport training, and the observed profile may reflect training\-related adaptations, pre\-existing individual differences, or both\.

## [The False Affordability Economy: How Instalment Credit Changes Consumer Decision\-Making in America](../publications/652ad83693204a4ff180.md)

Damian Aadi Jones

American consumer behavior is shaped by many different aspects\. Some such aspects include modern installment credit and machine learning algorithms\. The “False Affordability Economy” framework helps explain how online and digital payment methods can manipulate buyers, changing their perception of financial health\. By conducting a systematic literature review and a case study, this re\-search looks at how transparency in algorithms and data privacy can affect trust across the general population\. The findings suggest that secretive processes are often a friction point among the people, impacting long\-term trust, consumer sta\-bility and repayment consistency negatively\. An initiative of stricter oversight and improved standards of design and algorithmic transparency would help in the bat\-tle against mass debt cycles\. Such work would also help in bridging the gap be\-tween innovation and the preservation of one’s financial health\.

## [Why we should move beyond treating the Impostor Phenomenon as categorical construct and instead adopt the continuous approach](../publications/652d2c3f5e503a1f2a7c.md)

Kay Brauer

The Impostor Phenomenon \(IP\) is a psychological trait that receives increasing interest across study disciplines\. Although the IP is conceptualized as an individual difference variable that describes expressions on a continuum from low to high expressions, some studies still treat the IP as categorical\. One consequence of this approach is that prevalence rates are estimated based on arbitrary and unvalidated cutoffs\. I discuss the theoretical and methodological flaws of this approach, which are also evident when considering findings from three recent meta\-analyses of the IP\. Further, I suggest adopting the continuous approach to the IP and illustrate, based on data from 137 samples \( N = 22,552\), that aims such as testing differences between populations \(i\.e\., students and employees\) and whether the IP increased over time can be well addressed using distributional parameters\. I discuss implications of this approach for the field\.

## [LocalIntent: Outcome\-Specific Structured Generation for Backend\-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs](../publications/65362d7d6729ca797bef.md)

Tianyang Liu; Jiayue Wang; Zhanhao Cheng; Changyang Wang; Shaoshu Zhu; Zhenghao Wu; Hadi Tabatabaee Malazi

Locally deployed large language models \(LLMs\) can reduce reliance on remote cloud services for natural language smart building automation, but backend\-facing processing requires correct outcome selection, alignment with local capabilities, and valid structured outputs\. We investigate whether a complete outcome\-specific prompting design improves compact\-model outputs beyond generic route\-then\-generate prompting\. The proposed LocalIntent approach routes requests to ordinary or persistent\-rule branches: the former produces commands, clarifications, or rejections, while the latter generates trigger\-action rules, followed by deterministic validation\. We evaluate four locally executed Gemma and Qwen models spanning 2B\-9B parameters on 101 non\-persistent and 54 persistent\-rule records, comparing Monolithic prompting, generic two\-stage prompting, LocalIntent, and validation\-guided repair\. Across the evaluated datasets, LocalIntent achieves higher intent understanding, device identification, and action/parameter correctness than generic two\-stage prompting, while clarification/mode correctness remains model\-dependent\. The largest gains occur for rules, where LocalIntent improves intent understanding from 26\.4% to 80\.6%, device identification from 59\.3% to 84\.7%, rule\-mode correctness from 49\.1% to 98\.6%, and action/parameter correctness from 5\.6% to 44\.9%\. For non\-persistent requests, pooled gains are smaller: intent understanding increases from 39\.6% to 53\.2%, and action/parameter correctness from 30\.7% to 42\.8%\.

## [Core–Shell Molecularly Imprinted Polymer@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 for Low‐Cost and Selective Electrochemical Sensing of Paraquat](../publications/6537dba75b1154240d96.md)

M\. Ashraful Kader; Gang Li; Yang Liu

The widespread use of the water‐soluble paraquat \(PQ\) herbicide has found to be linked with numerous toxic outcomes to humans as well as aquatic animals, while the on‐site and rapid measurement is still challenging due to unsuitability and lack of selectivity of the existing techniques\. This study presents a selective, sensitive, and low‐cost electrochemical sensor for detecting residual PQ in water by combining a core–shell molecularly imprinted polymer \(MIP\)@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 material with a portable screen‐printed carbon electrode \(SPCE\)\. Adsorptive stripping voltammetry \(AdSV\) was employed to determine PQ using the proposed MIP@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 /SPCE, exhibiting high analytical performance with a sensitivity of 7\.27 µA/µM, a two‐segment linear range of 0\.25–20 and 20–50 µM, and a detection limit of 0\.043 µM\. In addition, excellent selectivity towards PQ was achieved, even in the presence of a 20‐fold excess of interfering substances commonly found in various water matrices\. Recoveries of 89\.72%–113\.46% were obtained at the MIP@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 /SPCE for the determination of PQ in tap water, river water, and seawater samples, and the results were validated using high‐performance liquid chromatography, demonstrating its strong potential for practical applications in aquatic analysis\.

## [AI\-guided extraction of plant\-derived bioactives for edible packaging films](../publications/654a2376e65f7297bfac.md)

Yogesh Kumar Awasthi; Renu Sharma; Mehak Katyal; Anupam Singha Roy; Kumud Kant Awasthi; Mahipal Singh Sankhla; Garima Awasthi; Alak Kumar Singh; Stavros\-Richard G\. Christopoulos; Theodoros H\. Varzakas

The increasing concern for plastic pollution and the rising demand for sustainable food packaging, have accelerated research on edible packaging films fortified with bioactive compounds from plants\. Phytochemicals such as flavonoids, terpenoids and polyphenols confer antioxidant, antimicrobial and functional properties to improve food safety, maintain quality and extend shelf\-life\. However, conventional extraction methods such as Soxhlet, maceration and solvent extraction have disadvantages of high solvent and energy consumption, low selectivity and extraction efficiency and thermal degradation of bioactives\. Furthermore, the nonlinear relationships among the extraction variables are complex and limit the performance of conventional statistical optimization methods\. This review critically examines the integration of conventional statistical optimization tools, especially response surface methodology \(RSM\) and design of experiments \(DoE\), with machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) strategies for advanced green extraction processes such as microwave\-assisted, ultrasound\-assisted, enzyme\-assisted, supercritical fluid, pulsed electric field, and pressurized liquid extraction\. RSM/DoE helps in systematic experimental design and optimization of processes, whereas ML methods, including Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\), Support Vector Regression \(SVR\), Random Forest \(RF\), and Adaptive Neuro\-Fuzzy Inference System \(ANFIS\), enable data\-assisted prediction of nonlinear relationships\. DL architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\), autoencoders \(AE\), transformers, and Physics\-Informed Neural Networks \(PINNs\), support complex and high\-dimensional datasets when sufficient training data are available; However, their significance in edible packaging research, where datasets are relatively small and heterogeneous, must be addressed in terms of model complexity, overfitting and validation robustness\. It further evaluates AI\-guided incorporation of plant bioactives into edible packaging through optimized encapsulation, prediction of mechanical and barrier properties, controlled release behavior, safety assessment, and sustainability evaluation\. AI\-assisted and hybrid models have demonstrated, in various reported studies, enhanced predictive accuracy and optimization efficacy compared with conventional response surface methodology in terms of extraction yield, solvent use, energy demand and experimental trials\. However, the limitations of standardised datasets, computational complexity, regulatory issues and lack of large\-scale validation restrict the applications in industry\. The reviewed literature still provides limited evidence directly linking mechanical, barrier and release properties, as well as safety outcomes such as migration, to ML\-based modeling and optimization\. Formulation\-specific experimental validation is therefore still required\. Future advances in explainable AI frameworks, harmonized databases, industrial\-scale studies and multidisciplinary collaboration will be crucial for the commercialization of intelligent and sustainable edible packaging systems\. Further scale\-up studies are needed before these approaches can be considered viable for industrial application\. Their translation will depend on process reproducibility, regulatory acceptance, sufficiently large and representative datasets, appropriate computational resources, formulation\-specific testing, mechanism\-informed modeling and uncertainty quantification\. Any proposed formulation will also require independent experimental validation, together with food\-safety and shelf\-life studies, before it can be accepted for food\-contact applications\.

## [Interaction of sex and insulin resistance with cognitive impairment in community\-dwelling middle\-aged and older adults](../publications/654f48625e47a129544a.md)

Jung Sook Kim; Byung Chul Chun; Joong\-Yeon Lim

Introduction Cognitive impairment is a major global health challenge\. However, whether sex and age interactively varies the association between insulin resistance and cognitive impairment remains unclear\. This cross\-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association between insulin resistance and cognitive impairment and identify sex\- and age\-specific interactions in community\-dwelling adults\. Methods The study involved 3,898 participants \(aged 54–86 years\) from the Ansan\-Ansung cohort of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study \(2017–2018\)\. Insulin resistance was assessed via Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance \(HOMA\-IR\), with participants dichotomized by the median \(1\.97\)\. Cognitive impairment was defined as a score of ≤23 on the Korean Mini\-Mental State Examination score\. Multivariable logistic regression was applied to examine the interaction and stratified effects of sex and age \(≥65 vs\. &lt;65 years\) on the insulin resistance–cognitive impairment association\. Results Among 3,898 participants \(mean age 66\.6 years; 55\.5% women\), 635 \(16\.3%\) had cognitive impairment\. A significant interaction was observed between sex and HOMA\-IR \( p = 0\.04\), whereas the interaction for age was not significant \( p = 0\.17\)\. In stratified analyses, higher HOMA\-IR was significantly associated with cognitive impairment exclusively in women aged ≥65 years \(OR 1\.37; 95% CI 1\.02–1\.84; p = 0\.04\)\. Conclusion Higher insulin resistance is a significant modifiable factor for cognitive impairment, specifically in women aged ≥65 years\. These exploratory findings suggest potential sex\-related differences in the metabolic\-cognitive association, underscoring the importance of sex\-specific metabolic management starting from midlife to help preserve cognitive health in later life\.

## [Surgeon\-Derived Design Insights Regarding Real\-Time Artificial Intelligence Decision Support for Endoscopic Cancer Surgery](../publications/6553b91beb40304f82d4.md)

Cathleen A\. McCarrick; Samo Erzen; Antonello Forgione; Jacques Marescaux; Ronan A\. Cahill

IntroductionReal\-time artificial intelligence \(AI\) decision\-support systems are increasingly proposed for use in endoscopic and minimally invasive surgery although how best to present such information intraoperatively is unclear\. This study explored surgeon perspectives regarding the user\-interface, interpretation and workflow integration of a prototype AI system \(CLASSICA\-OR\) for real\-time endoscopic cancer characterization during surgery\.MethodsSurgeons specialising in minimally invasive gastrointestinal surgery were asked for their first impressions in their evaluation of the CLASSICA\-OR system within a high\-fidelity surgical simulation environment\. For this, participants viewed prerecorded colonoscopic imagery of significant rectal neoplasia while the AI analysis was applied in real\-time to the video\. Commentary and responses to semi\-structured interview were recorded audiovisually for transcription and analysis using qualitative thematic analysis supported by NVivo \(Lumivero\)\.ResultsEighteen surgeons participated, generating rich qualitative data\. Four major themes emerged: \(1\) AI was viewed as a valuable but evolving decision\-support tool; \(2\) institutional culture, governance and commercial realities were recognised as important determinants of adoption; \(3\) real\-time perfusion\-based lesion characterisation \(foundational to CLASSICA\-OR\) was considered promising but with specific challenges; and \(4\) clarity, usability, transparency and workflow compatibility are surgeon priorities in decision\-support displays\. Participants emphasised minimised cognitive load, preserved surgeon autonomy, clear communication of uncertainty and seamless workflow integration\. Preferences differed between simplified binary outputs and more detailed numerical displays supporting the need for adaptable interfaces\.ConclusionsSurgeons perceive real\-time intraoperative AI decision support as promising but requiring thoughtful user\-centred design\. They articulate practical development and implementation insights for intraoperative AI systems\.

## [Evidence for Reduced Somatic T‐Cell Receptor Sequence Diversity Profiles Among Midwestern Amish in an Aging Cohort Study](../publications/6553eb8dc7f639c2b94d.md)

Lauren A\. Cruz; Shiying Liu; Kristy L\. S\. Miskimen; Jessica N\. Cooke Bailey; Tyler G\. Kinzy; Yeunjoo E\. Song; Reneé A\. Laux; Penelope L\. Miron; Paula K\. Ogrocki; Alan J\. Lerner; Audrey Lynn; Sarada L\. Fuzzell; Sherri D\. Hochstetler; Ioanna Konidari; Jacob L\. McCauley; William K\. Scott; Margaret Ann Pericak‐Vance; Jonathan L\. Haines; Dana C\. Crawford

BACKGROUND: The causes of late onset Alzheimer disease \(LOAD\) are not known but several recent lines of evidence implicate the adaptive immune system\. OBJECTIVE: To characterize the adaptive immune system among Midwestern Amish participating in longitudinal studies of aging\. METHODS: We immunosequenced the T\-cell receptor \(TCR\) beta chain from genomic DNA of 72 participants, including those with clinically diagnosed LOAD \(n = 6\), mild cognitive impairment \(MCI; n = 16\), cognitive impairment but not AD \(n = 3\), and 35 cognitively unaffected\. For a subset of participants, LOAD pathogenesis plasma biomarkers were available\. RESULTS: TCR sequence diversity measured as Simpson&\#x27;s clonality was lower among LOAD\+MCI compared with non\-LOAD, but these differences were not independent of age\. Relatively few clonotypes \(exact nucleotide sequences\) were shared across participants; of those few shared include the Epstein Barr virus associated clonotype\. HLA\-A\*03:01 and several HLA\-DRB1 alleles were under\-represented among LOAD\+MCI participants compared with cognitively unaffected participants, but these associations were no longer significant in adjusted analyses\. Among LOAD\+MCI participants, increased p\-tau181 was nominally associated with decreased TCR sequence diversity, and the nominal association was independent of age; however, this association did not remain statistically significant after strict correction for multiple testing and the limited sample size precluded formal tests of heterogeneity\. RESULTS: In this limited Midwestern Amish sample, the preliminary TCR diversity trends are consistent with the involvement of the adaptive immune system in LOAD\.

## [IMPACT OF PSYCHIATRIC MEDICINE, PHARMACOTHERAPY, AND DRUG METABOLISM ON DEPRESSION AND EMOTIONAL REGULATION IN ADOLESCENTS](../publications/656e7a42ecaead07e0f5.md)

Vishal Dogra; Archana Mishra

Background: Adolescence is this kind of dynamic neurodevelopmental phase, where neural circuits in charge of emotion control, reward processing, executive regulation, stress responsivity and social cognition start maturing a lot\. During this time, depression often shows up together with emotional dysregulation, sleep problems , harder thinking, and reduced psychosocial functioning\. This review sort of brings together psychological, neurobiological, psychiatric, pharmacological and pharmaco\-metabolic lenses, to look at how adolescent depression links to emotional regulation, and there’s a special focus on antidepressant pharmacotherapy plus cytochrome P450 mediated drug metabolism\. Method: This kind of qualitative narrative review goes through current literature that talks about adolescent depression and emotional regulation, neurodevelopment and the prefrontal limbic circuitry, reward processing and also hypothalamic\-pituitary\-adrenal\-axis activity\. It also touches inflammation, neuroplasticity, sleep, and then moves into antidepressant pharmacotherapy, including pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics , and pharmacogenetics\. There is, in a way, special attention on CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 , since they’re already known to be tied in with the metabolism of several antidepressants\. Adolescent depression seems to come about from a messy set of interactions between developmental, psychological, environmental, and biological processes, not like one lone neurochemical glitch\. Result &amp; Conclusion: Emotional regulation might be a key clinical phenotype, sort of linking altered affective processing, with the later depressive symptoms too\. At the same time, antidepressant exposure isn’t consistent across individuals, and variation in CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 genetics could help explain differences in pharmacokinetics, and tolerability\. But, the developmental stage, co\-prescribed drugs, how well someone sticks to the regimen, the disease characteristics and the surrounding environment, all steer the treatment response\. So, integrating emotional regulation and neurobiology with pharmacokinetics and pharmacogenetics might end up giving this more complete framework for figuring out why people respond differently\. Still, the evidence in pediatrics is kind of less developed compared with adults, and genotype shouldn’t be read as a self\-standing cause of antidepressant efficacy\.

## [Application of LLM combined with knowledge base in improving C\-TIRADS grading of thyroid nodules](../publications/6579cdc48f2cae313e27.md)

Qian Qu; Hanwen Bi; Xiaofei Yu; Rui Zhou; Zhen Liu; Tengteng Hao

Objective This study used the unified text\-based grading results of senior sonographers as the primary reference \(this text benchmark is not pathological diagnostic gold standard\) to evaluate the concordance of text\-derived C\-TIRADS grades assigned by six large language models \(LLMs\), with and without FastGPT Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) knowledge base assistance\. Our primary endpoint was the concordance between grading and physician consensus—a measure fundamentally distinct from pathological diagnostic accuracy\. Only a small subgroup with pathological confirmation was used for a supplementary exploratory analysis of the correlation between model risk stratification and pathological benign or malignant findings\. Methods Six LLMs were configured using the C\-TIRADS criteria\. A FastGPT knowledge base was built from 11,489 thyroid ultrasound records collected at Yantai Yuhuangding Hospital between 2022 and 2023\. Cases were assigned to manual, LLM, and knowledge\-base\-augmented LLM groups\. C\-TIRADS grading concordance with expert ultrasound consensus, and grading speed were assessed\. A subgroup of 62 pathologically confirmed nodules was used for supplementary exploratory analysis\. AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and Mantel\-Haenszel linear trend χ2 were computed to examine the alignment of model C\-TIRADS risk tiers with pathological benign and malignant findings\. Results Among the standalone LLMs, DeepSeek\-V3 achieved the highest numerical grading concordance \(81\.14%\)\. Following the integration of the RAG knowledge base, overall grading consistency improved significantly \( P &lt; 0\.001\), with Doubao\-pro\-128k demonstrating the highest overall concordance at 89\.04%\. Concordance increased significantly for C\-TIRADS Categories 1 and 3 \( P = 0\.027 and P &lt; 0\.001, respectively\), increased numerically for Category 2 \( P = 0\.596\), and decreased numerically for borderline Category 4A \( P = 0\.106\)\. The average concordance across all categories rose significantly from 70\.39% to 79\.75% \( P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The knowledge\-augmented Doubao\-pro\-128k model exhibited excellent inter\-rater agreement \( linear\-weighted Kappa&gt;0\.8, Bonferroni\-corrected P&lt;0\.006 \)\. The average single\-case grading duration of all 12 AI risk tiering pipelines \(6 LLMs with/without knowledge base\) was 1\.30 s, which was 15 times faster than manual grading \(19\.25 s\)\. Stratified trend and ROC analyses were performed on 62 thyroid nodules with pathological outcomes\. Within this small\-sample exploratory pathological subgroup, the Doubao\-pro\-128k integrated with knowledge base established a significantly ascending malignant risk gradient, achieving an AUC of 0\.783 \(95% CI : 0\.635, 0\.932\) for distinguishing benign from malignant lesions\. In comparison, knowledge\-enhanced Doubao\-pro\-128k exhibited a trend toward better matching trend with pathological malignancy distribution and numerically the highest positive Youden index of 0\.277 \(95% CI : 0\.071, 0\.482\)\. Conclusion Doubao\-pro\-128k integrated with knowledge base accelerated text grading and improved overall sonographer concordance; category\-specific concordance increased significantly for C\-TIRADS 1 and 3, increased numerically for Category 2, and declined numerically without statistical significance for borderline C\-TIRADS 4A, indicating that these ambiguous nodules require further optimization\. Exploratory pathological analysis revealed variable model\-pathology alignment at the C\-TIRADS ≥ 4A cutoff: DeepSeek\-V3 integrated with knowledge base produced a negative Youden index, while Doubao\-pro\-128k integrated with knowledge base showed a tentative trend toward better reflected pathological malignancy gradients\.

## [A machine learning\-based platform for predicting the potential energy of small molecules](../publications/657ea44090eef9f43445.md)

Alexandra Farcaș; Paul Pernes; Aurel Baloi; Bogdan Belean

Accurate estimation of molecular potential energy after energy minimization is vital for the rational design of targeted therapeutics\. In this study, we present a machine learning platform that leverages sophisticated neural network architectures to predict the potential energy of small molecules\. Accurate prediction of molecular potential energy can facilitate the computational characterization of drug\- and gene\-delivery\-related molecules and support molecular modeling workflows\. Our methodology involves designing and evaluating deep learning models, including convolutional neural network–bidirectional long short\-term memory architectures, with and without multihead attention mechanisms\. These models are trained on a comprehensive dataset comprising small molecules structures\. By utilizing atom\-wise sequential representations that preserve key geometric and chemical information, our approach effectively estimates potential energies and surpasses traditional descriptor\-based machine learning methods\. The integration of attention mechanisms enhances model generalization by capturing complex structural relationships, thereby streamlining virtual screening processes\. Comparative analyses against existing benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of sequence\-based neural networks in molecular energy prediction, paving the way for more efficient drug discovery and polymer informatics\. This platform offers a robust, computationally efficient tool for virtual screening and energy estimation of candidate molecules, supporting the advancement of targeted therapeutics through rapid molecule prioritization based on predicted potential energies\.

## [Glycemic control and COVID\-19 outcomes across the continuum of glucose regulation: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/65a6a889c80dd1082ce1.md)

Armand Mbanya; Serena Leung; Alan Bienvenida; Elizabeth Leslie; Sangmin Ryan Shin; Kate E\. Koplan; Felipe Lobelo

Introduction Coronavirus disease 2019 \(COVID\-19\) has disproportionately affected individuals with underlying metabolic dysfunction\. This study investigates the association between varying levels of pre\-infection glycemic control and COVID\-19\-related health outcomes\. Methods A retrospective chart review was conducted on Kaiser Permanente Georgia patients with confirmed COVID\-19\. Participants \(N = 2071\) were categorized into five groups based on their HbA1c levels: patients without diabetes, those with prediabetes, and those with diabetes with varying degrees of glycemic control\. We adjusted for demographics, social determinants of health, comorbidities, medications, and lifestyle factors\. Results Among 2071 patients, 986 \(47\.6%\) were without diabetes, 658 \(31\.8%\) had prediabetes, 183 \(8\.8%\) had diabetes with HbA1c&lt;7%, 162 \(7\.8%\) had diabetes with HbA1c ≥ 7% ≤ 9% and 82 \(4%\) had diabetes with HbA1c&gt;9%\. Patients with HbA1c&gt;9% had the highest proportion hospitalized \(38\.3%, p&lt;0\.001\), and admitted to ICU \(14\.8%, p&lt;0\.001\)\. In multivariable logistic regression models, prediabetes and insulin use were associated with greater odds of hospitalization; odds ratio 1\.43 \[95% CI 1\.09\-1\.87\] and 3\.02 \[95% CI 1\.95\-4\.68\], respectively\. Conclusions There is a gradient of increasing COVID\-19 severity with worsening glycemic control\. The study shows the importance of recognizing prediabetes as a significant risk factor for severe COVID\-19, comparable to poorly controlled diabetes\.

## [Elizabeth Anscombe’s Challenge: An Adequate Philosophy of Psychology](../publications/65a8fd7c41c04e1f5384.md)

Georgina Raventos

This paper revisits Elizabeth Anscombe’s call for an ‘adequate philosophy of psychology’ through the lens of contemporary psychology education\. It argues that current curricula tend to institutionalize a predominantly causal\-explanatory model of mind, in which the conceptual resources required to understand intentional action remain underdeveloped\. Drawing on an illustrative analysis of selected European psychology programmes, the paper identifies a structural imbalance between empirical training and conceptual reflection\. From an Anscombean perspective, this imbalance risks obscuring the distinction between causes and reasons, which is central to understanding human action\. While contemporary psychology does engage with concepts such as intention and motivation, these often remain theoretically underexamined within a naturalistic framework\. The paper concludes by proposing a cooperative model in which philosophical analysis and empirical research are integrated, thereby enriching both disciplines and contributing to a more adequate account of human agency\.

## [DaiSy: A Library for Scalable Data Series Similarity Search](../publications/65bd0ea356e9fc189d91.md)

Francesca Del Gaudio; Manos Chatzakis; Gayathiri Ravendirane; Botao Peng; Themis Palpanas

Exact similarity search over large collections of data series is a fundamental operation in modern applications, yet existing solutions are often fragmented, specialized, or tailored to specific execution environments\. In this paper, we present DaiSy, a unified library for exact data series similarity search that integrates multiple state\-ofthe\- art \(iSAX\-based\) algorithms within a single, coherent framework\. DaiSy is the first library to support exact similarity search across diverse execution environments, including implementations for disk\-based, in\-memory, GPU\-accelerated, and distributed scalable similarity search\. Although designed for data series, DaiSy is also directly applicable to exact similarity search over vector data, enabling its use in a broader range of applications\. The library supports interfaces in both C\+\+ and Python, enabling users to easily integrate its functionality into a variety of tasks\. DaiSy is open\-sourced and available at: https://github\.com/MChatzakis/DaiSy\.

## [HPV\-Associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Arab Populations: Histological Heterogeneity, Regional Evidence, and the Syrian Knowledge Gap](../publications/65c930b6ccbf29b1ae57.md)

Mohamad Omar Belali \*; Mohammad Walid Alhaj Ali

Human papillomavirus \(HPV\)\-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma \(OPSCC\) is biologically and clinically distinct from HPV\-independent disease\. Classically, HPV\-associated OPSCC is nonkeratinizing in morphology, less desmoplastic in stroma, and more lymphoid\-rich in background; however, it is increasingly recognized as histologically heterogeneous\. Keratinizing, maturing, basaloid, papillary, lymphoepithelial, glandular, and other components can be encountered in an HPV\-associated tumor, and recent evidence suggests that such micromorphological diversity may be prognostically significant after HPV association has been demonstrated through established assays\. In contrast, research from Arab populations has focused largely on HPV prevalence, p16 expression, genotype, and clinical outcome rather than on detailed histology or tumor organization\. This critical review synthesizes evidence from Arab countries \(focused on Syria\) into the contemporary international literature and suggests a regional framework for understanding HPV\-associated OPSCC pathology\. Studies from Jordan, Lebanon, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates have demonstrated HPV\-related or p16\-positive OPSCC, with widely varying estimates due to differing anatomical selection and testing strategies\. Syrian studies identify high\-risk HPV in head\-and\-neck squamous carcinomas but have not yet estimated the HPV\-attributable fraction or histology of anatomically verified Syrian OPSCC\. We speculate that future regional research should shift from dichotomous HPV categorization to quantitative characterization of squamous maturation, tumor architecture, stromal response, tumor\-associated lymphocytes, front of invasion morphology, and spatial tumor heterogeneity\. Digital pathology and interpretable artificial intelligence offer exciting opportunities to engage with these questions\. A principal unresolved regional question is the extent and biological significance of HPV involvement in oropharyngeal SCCs, while an important research challenge is to understand how HPV\-associated carcinogenesis is expressed through regional variations in tissue architecture\.

## [الوقف الاسلامي وتطوره من النصوص التأسيسية الى النماذج التطبيقية في الذكاء الاصطناعي \(صدر الاسلام انموذجا \)](../publications/65cb86b1c74a072cdd22.md)
