## [Comprehension under threat: outgroup threat predicts perceived accent strength, ease of comprehension, and speaker evaluations](../publications/65d9f5da150779268547.md)

Priscilla Lok‐chee Shum; Chi‐Shing Tse; Stephen C\. Wright

Nonnative speakers, influenced by their first language, often produce accented speech that systematically deviates from that of native speakers\. Nonnative\-accented speech is often judged more harshly than native\-accented speech, in part due to increased comprehension difficulty\. However, non\-linguistic factors like social attitudes can bias perceptions of nonnative accent strength and comprehensibility, which in turn impacts social evaluations of speakers\. Grounded in Intergroup Threat Theory, this study examines the relationship between perceived outgroup threat, speech perception, and speaker evaluations within the Hong Kong context\. Specifically, in a sample of native Cantonese\-speaking Hong Kong undergraduates \( N = 691\), we investigate how perceived threat from Mainland Chinese people influence perceived nonnative accent strength, comprehensibility, and subsequently, social evaluations of native Putonghua speakers, Cantonese\-accented Putonghua speakers, native Cantonese speakers, and Putonghua\-accented Cantonese speakers\. Speakers were rated in terms of competence and warmth, perceived nonnative accent strength, and comprehensibility\. Mediation analyses tested the mechanisms through which threat influences speaker evaluation\. Perceived outgroup threat was associated with lower competence ratings for Putonghua\-accented Cantonese speakers\. Threat selectively biased speech perception for Putonghua\-accented Cantonese speakers, predicting stronger perceived nonnative accent strength and lower comprehensibility, which mediated the relationship between outgroup threat and speaker evaluations\. Robustness checks testing the effects of outgroup threat separately by datasets and accent levels indicated perceived comprehensibility played a more consistent and pivotal role than accent strength in this model\. Results suggest listeners engage in social creativity strategies to yield positive ingroup distinctiveness, utilizing linguistic differentiation as a strategic mechanism to penalize speakers from threatening outgroups\.

## [Psychophysiological and physiological characteristics of individuals with different response profiles to hyperventilation stress](../publications/65db0cb0abd7815b4e12.md)

Roman A\. Zorin; М\. М\. Лапкин; В\. А\. Жаднов; Anastasia D\. Filina

Hyperventilation refleсts the functioning of adaptive mechanisms during intense physical exertion, as well as under the influence of various stressful factors on the body and also is associated with disorders of central regulation of respiration\. Artificial hyperventilation \(hyperventilation test\) makes it possible to identify individual features of the central and peripheral adaptive mechanisms of the human body and identify their most significant markers\. Research methodology: The study was conducted on 63 practically healthy subjects aged \(31 ± 2\.48\) years; 31 of them were men and 32 were women\. The study assessed a complex of psychophysiological \(level of aggression, personal and situational anxiety, level of pretensions\) and physiological \(endogeunous evoked potentials, heart rate variability, CO2 and O2 content in exhaled air\) indicators in a state of relative physiological rest and hyperventilation test conditions\. The data obtained has been processed using multidimensional statistics, including cluster, correlation, and logit regression analysis\. The results of the research: In general, healthy individuals who differ in the types of reactions to hyperventilation have a certain pattern of psychophysiological characteristics and their interrelationships\. During a standardized hyperventilation load, it is possible to distinguish a group with moderate dynamics of indicators and a “highly reactive” group\. The group with moderate level of CO2 change is characterized by high psychomotor reaction speed, higher activation of associative areas of the brain during preparation for activity and lower activation of sympathetic autonomic regulation\. In this subgroup we describe weaker coupling between physiological mechanisms\. Highly reactive group exhibits opposite characteristics\. Physiological characteristics of contingent negative variation potential and heart rate variability are included in a logistic regression model to classify groups with different CO2 dynamics during hyperventilation test\. Conclusions: Groups of apparently healthy individuals with different types of response to hyperventilation load exhibit a specific profile of psychophysiological interrelationships, which reflects the features of the systemic organization of functions\.

## [Evaluation of a novel body temperature sensor \(CORE\) in dogs under general anesthesia following premedication with dexmedetomidine or acepromazine: A pilot study](../publications/65e3ed3a9598e6b37b28.md)

Chloe R\. Dupleix; Jacob P\. Rastas; Qianqian Zhao; Robert Young; Rebecca A\. Johnson

Core body temperature monitoring in anesthetized dogs is a vital part of physiological evaluation\. Depending on the procedure and patient positioning, consistent core temperature measurements can be difficult to obtain\. The objective of this study was to evaluate the reliability and clinical validity of a wireless, non\-invasive, superficial heat flux\-based thermometric device \(CORE, greenTEG AG, Rümlang, Switzerland\)\. Three healthy beagle dogs were premedicated with either dexmedetomidine or acepromazine prior to induction with intravenous propofol and isoflurane maintenance\. They were monitored every five minutes with pulse oximetry, non\-invasive blood pressure, electrocardiography, and capnometry\. Rectal thermometry and temperatures from the CORE sensor placed on clipped and unclipped skin over the jugular veins were measured every three minutes for up to 120 minutes following induction\. Based on the correlation coefficient for repeated measures \(rrm\) and the Shrout\-Fleiss intraclass correlation coefficient \(ICC\), in dogs administered acepromazine, there was good, statistically significant correlation and reliability between rectal and clipped CORE temperatures \(rrm = 0\.81, P &lt; 0\.0001; ICC = 0\.78\) and rectal and unclipped CORE temperatures \(rrm = 0\.79, P &lt; 0\.0001; ICC = 0\.85\)\. In dogs administered dexmedetomidine, although values were correlated \(rrm = 0\.30, P &lt; 0\.0001\), there was poor reliability \(ICC = 0\.28\) between rectal and clipped CORE temperatures which improved if dogs were unclipped \(rrm = 0\.48, P &lt; 0\.0001; ICC = 0\.88\)\. Clinically acceptable Bland\-Altman agreements were found between rectal and unclipped CORE methods\. These preliminary results suggest that the CORE sensor may provide an alternative method for assessing core body temperatures in unclipped, anesthetized dogs\.

## [Beta\-blockers after acute coronary syndrome: insights across the ejection fraction spectrum](../publications/65ef55fdbc6d8d0d7323.md)

Eirinaios Tsiartas; Sokratis Oikonomou; Aristea Iordanidou; Athanasios Samaras; Αndreas S\. Papazoglou; Dimitrios V\. Moysidis; Vassilios Pericles Vassilikos; Antonios Ziakas; Periklis A\. Davlouros; Konstantinos P Tsioufis; Dimitrios N\. Tziakas; Ιoannis Zarifis; George A\. Giannakoulas

Abstract Aims To evaluate the association between beta\-blocker \(BB\) prescription and long\-term all\-cause mortality after acute coronary syndrome \(ACS\), and to assess whether this varies across the left ventricular ejection fraction \(LVEF\) spectrum\. Methods We analysed ACS patients from the retrospective multicentre CardioMining study \(NCT05176769\)\. The primary analysis used inverse probability of treatment weighting \(IPTW\) and restricted mean survival time \(RMST\) derived from weighted Kaplan\-Meier curves\. RMST and survival differences were estimated at 1 and 5 years\. A landmark analysis evaluated survival between years 1 and 5 among first\-year survivors\. Results Among 6,049 ACS patients \(age 66\.8±13\.2 years; 74\.9% male\), 5,107 \(84\.4%\) were discharged on BBs\. During a median 4\.6\-year follow\-up, 1,912 deaths \(31\.6%\) occurred\. Overall, the 1\-year RMST difference associated with BBs was 6\.3 days \(95%CI 0\.0 to 13\.2\), which attenuated further by 5 years \(11\.3 days, 95%CI \-30\.7 to 63\.9\)\. The largest 1\-year RMST difference was observed among patients with LVEF≤40% \(18\.8 days, 95%CI 1\.1 to 37\.4\), whereas associations were smaller and non\-significant among patients with LVEF 41\-49% and LVEF≥50%\. At 5 years, confidence intervals crossed the null across all LVEF categories\. Continuous LVEF analyses suggested greater short\-term benefit at lower values, with progressive attenuation across the LVEF spectrum\. Among 1\-year survivors, no significant RMST differences were observed between years 1 and 5\. Conclusion Discharge BB prescription was not associated with a clear long\-term survival advantage after ACS in this large real\-world cohort\. Apparent associations were strongest at lower LVEF values and attenuated during longer follow\-up\.

## [Estimation of rubber yield on Hainan Island, China using multi\-source data during 2021\-2025](../publications/65f3b20838479feb932b.md)

Ruofan Jing; 廖静娟; Li Zhang; 尧德明; X\. Liu

Rubber is both a strategic material and an essential industrial raw commodity, making accurate yield estimation critically important\. Current remote sensing\-based physical models require enhancement to converting potential yield into actual yield using limited field samples, while improving parameter applicability and estimation accuracy\. Integrating DEM, Sentinel\-2 imagery, and meteorological data, this study develops a multi\-stage framework that couple the CASA model, SOLARFLUX, a conversion module, and a parameter calibration scheme\. Calibrated and validated with field\-measured data, the model enables high\-resolution dynamic monitoring of dry rubber yield across Hainan Island\. Validation demonstrates strong model performance \(R2 &gt; 0\.95\), with relative error \(RE\) reduced from 21\.99 % to 16\.62 % after refinement\. The model substantially outperforms machine learning approaches\. Results reveal a year\-on\-year decline in total rubber yield from 2021 to 2023, followed by a marked rebound during the 2023\-2024\. The proposed framework offers a robust and practical solution for data‑scarce regions, and its products provide valuable support for the sustainable development and ecological monitoring of Hainan’s rubber industry\.

## [A natural hedging framework for longevity risk with graphical risk assessment](../publications/660c256af44149a2bc2c.md)

Lydia J\. Gabric; Kenneth Q\. Zhou

Abstract Natural hedging allows life insurers to manage longevity risk internally by offsetting the opposite exposures of life insurance and annuity liabilities\. Although many studies have proposed natural hedging strategies under different settings, calibration methods, and mortality models, a unified framework for constructing and evaluating such hedges remains undeveloped\. While graphical risk assessment has been explored for index\-based longevity hedges, no comparable metric exists for natural hedging\. This paper proposes a structured natural hedging framework paired with a graphical risk metric for hedge evaluation\. The framework integrates valuation, calibration, and evaluation, while the graphical metric provides intuitive insights into residual dependencies and hedge performance\. Applied to multiple hedging scenarios, the proposed methods demonstrate flexibility, interpretability, and practical value for longevity risk management\.

## [Klasifikasi Arah Tren Harga Bitcoin Menggunakan Metode Ensemble Learning Random Forest](../publications/661700f3bd6307047193.md)

Fadhlan Subhan Fadilah; Indra Yustiana; Nugraha

Bitcoin&\#x27;s extreme price volatility poses significant challenges for investors and traders in making informed investment decisions\. Conventional technical analysis approaches are often subjective and unable to capture complex market dynamics accurately\. This study aims to develop a Bitcoin price trend direction classification system as a more objective technical analysis tool using the Random Forest ensemble learning method\. Historical Bitcoin price data from January 2017 to March 2026 with an H1 \(1\-hour\) timeframe was obtained from MetaTrader 5 and Binance\. Raw price data \(Open, High, Low, Close, Volume\) were processed through preprocessing stages and converted into 106 technical indicator features grouped into nine categories, including Trend Indicators, Momentum Oscillators, Volatility Features, and Rolling Statistics\. The Random Forest Classifier model was built and optimized through hyperparameter tuning with time\-series cross\-validation, then evaluated using standard classification metrics as well as trading metrics under scenarios employing a trailing stop mechanism\. The results show that the model achieved an accuracy of 58\.65%, precision of 41\.38%, recall of 99\.50%, and F1\-score of 0\.5856\. Although the low AUC\-ROC value \(0\.5106\) indicates the model can hardly distinguish between the two classes individually, the backtest generated significant trading performance with a net profit of 8,491 USD from an initial capital of 10,000 USD, a win rate of 45\.08%, and a profit factor of 1\.30\. Feature importance analysis identified RSI\_14\_std\_168 \(3\.77%\), SMA\_200 \(3\.03%\), and ATR\_pct\_14\_mean\_168 \(2\.92%\) as the three most influential technical indicators\. This study concludes that although standard classification accuracy is limited, the Random Forest model combined with probability threshold optimization and risk management strategies can serve as a beneficial technical analysis tool\. The system has been implemented as an interactive web dashboard providing real\-time prediction features\.

## [Development of a video game in MonoGame framework](../publications/662401d681d0c4fcbe38.md)

Nejc Černelč

Razvoj računalniških iger danes ni več zgolj tehnični postopek, temveč predstavlja preplet ustvarjalnega izraza, pripovedovanja in načrtovanja uporabniške izkušnje\. Hiter napredek na področju tehnologije je omogočil boljši dostop tudi širši populaciji, tako posameznikom kot manjšim razvojnih ekipam\. Cilj diplomske naloge je prikazati celovit proces izdelave računalniške igre, od začetne ideje do končnega izdelka\. V ta namen se osredotočamo na izdelavo platformske igre, razvite z uporabo ogrodja MonoGame\. Izbira MonoGame temelji na njegovi večplatformski podpori in nizkonivojski naravi, ki omogoča boljši vpogled v osnovne koncepte razvoja iger\. Ti so posebej uporabni za študente in začetnike na področju razvoja iger, saj olajšajo razumevanje delovanja igralnega pogona ter omogočajo nadaljnjo prilagoditev glede na specifične potrebe in optimizacije\. Razvoj same igre temelji na preverjenih dobrih praksah, ki izhajajo iz delovanja uspešnih igralnih sistemov in pogonov\.

## [Agroecologia e animais: reflexões sobre invisibilidade e relações interespecíficas nos sistemas alimentares](../publications/6633392dcbecf177b4c9.md)

Juliana Vieira Paz; Anna Cristina Souza; Beatriz S\. Souza; Paulo Eduardo Moruzzi Marques; Carolina Refinetti Schiesari

Agroecological transition is necessary in the face of socio\-environmental crises associated with agrifood chains\. However, non\-human animals are frequently excluded from discussions, even though they are part of most agricultural systems\. When included, the motivations are centered on anthropocentric interests, keeping them invisible\. This marginalization reproduces the concept of animal welfare and the interspecific relationships developed from the industrial logic, preventing a full rupture with this model of exploitation\. This Agroecological Note argues that discussions on agroecology must urgently include non\-human animals in a meaningful way, effectively breaking with the industrial, anthropocentric, and exploitative model and logic that have been perpetuated in animal husbandry, even where agroecology has been the guiding principle\.

## [Association of the COX\-2 rs689466 genetic variant with aspirin resistance in patients with Ischemic heart disease](../publications/663b49af7e2789971a58.md)

Mehak Batool; Nazish Saqlain; Asif Haleem Khan; Sidra Rasool

Objectives: To determine the prevalence of laboratory\-defined aspirin resistant cases and to find the association of COX\-2 rs689466 polymorphism with aspirin resistance \(AR\) in Pakistani ischemic heart disease \(IHD\) patients\. Methodology: This cross\-sectional analytical study was carried out at UHS and PGMI, Lahore from February 2025 to January 2026, involving 120 adult IHD patients who had been on aspirin therapy for the last 07\-days\. Laboratory\-defined AR was determined using Light transmission Aggregometry, where resistance was defined by aggregation criteria with agonists like Arachidonic acid \(≥ 20%\), ADP \(≥ 70%\), and Collagen \(≥ 70%\)\. Genotyping for the COX\-2 rs689466 polymorphism was performed using the phenol chloroform method for extraction of DNA, followed by a Polymerase Chain Reaction \(PCR\) based protocol\. Data was analyzed using SPSS version\-24\. Results: The laboratory defined aspirin resistance was observed in 70\(58\.3%\) patients\. Genotype analysis for COX\-2 rs689466 showed the T/T genotype was the most common in the case group \(73%\), followed by T/C \(23%\), and the rare C/C genotype \(4%\)\. No significant association was found between the COX\-2 rs689466 polymorphism and aspirin resistance under any genetic model \(codominant, dominant, recessive, over\-dominant, or log\-additive\)\. For instance, the codominant model for the T/C genotype yielded an odds ratio \(OR\) of 1\.16 \(95% CI: 0\.47–2\.86, p = 0\.69\) compared to T/T\. Conclusion: Despite a high incidence of laboratory\-defined aspirin resistance among this cohort, the COX\-2 rs689466 polymorphism was not significantly associated with Aspirin resistance\. These findings predict its multifactorial nature and suggest the need for individualized antiplatelet therapy\.

## [Autism as Developmental Constraint Reconfiguration](../publications/663b5784c4d9ae20f067.md)

Ari Ariel Marom

Autism is conventionally framed as a neurodevelopmental spectrum defined by differences in social communication, restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour, and atypical sensory processing\. While this clinical description is indispensable, it does not by itself specify the systems\-level architecture that makes such a phenotype possible\. This monograph formalizes autism within Informational Nosology as a developmental regime of constraint reconfiguration rather than as a late degenerative collapse or a paroxysmal failure\. The core claim is that early neurodevelopment in autism is characterized by an atypical setting of precision weighting and sensory\-boundary control\. Instead of progressive uncoupling \(as in Alzheimer’s\), subcortical gain failure \(as in Parkinson’s\), or conduction\-noise accumulation \(as in multiple sclerosis\), the autistic regime is organized around an early, stable, and often highly ordered reallocation of informational constraint: locally elevated precision, altered sensory gating, and a distinctive trade\-off between environmental volatility and internal model stability\. Hypersensitivities, insistence on sameness, and atypical social attunement are read as consequences of this architecture, not as primary social deficits detached from sensory\-computational organization\. The account is explicitly non\-eliminative\. It does not displace genetic, synaptic, or circuit\-level findings; it relocates them within a common dynamical language already used across the Nosology corpus — energetic headroom, noise, threshold stability, and the maintenance of operational constraint\. Autism is thereby placed as a developmental portal rather than a broken version of typical development: a different early solution to the problem of remaining coherent under sensory and social load\. The monograph specifies demarcation criteria from schizophrenia, trauma\-related lock\-in, and the gradual neurodegenerative portals, and it states the empirical signatures that would support or weaken the proposed architecture\. Autism is formalized as developmental constraint reconfiguration, not as degeneration, psychosis, or simple social deficit\. Core mechanism: atypical early precision weighting and sensory\-boundary control, producing a stable alternative architecture rather than progressive collapse\. Phenotype reinterpreted: hypersensitivities, sameness, and social\-attunement differences follow from informational organization, not from a primary absence of social motivation alone\. Strict demarcation from schizophrenia, PTSD\-related lock\-in, and the gradual portals \(AD, PD, MS\)\. Non\-displacement stance: genetics, synapses and circuits remain intact; the contribution is a systems\-level architecture within one formal Nosology language\. Keywords: autism; neurodevelopment; precision weighting; sensory gating; constraint reconfiguration; informational nosology; predictive processing; developmental phenotype; systems neuroscience

## [Performance of four large language model chatbots in responding to patient\-facing questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a cross\-sectional paired evaluation](../publications/6642758622bbe1f80a64.md)

Ting Mao; Feifei Bian; Wei Liu; Xianglong Zhou; Guoqin Zhang

Background Large language model \(LLM\) chatbots are increasingly used by the public to obtain health information, but the safety and quality of their responses to questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures \(OVCFs\) remain unclear\. Objective To compare the safety and patient\-facing response quality of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots when responding to standardized questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures\. Methods In this cross\-sectional paired evaluation, 36 standardized OVCF\-related patient\-facing questions were submitted to each of four publicly accessible LLM chatbot interfaces—ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao—in an initial response\-generation round on June 20, 2026, from Jiangsu, China\. Queries were conducted in English in independent single\-turn sessions under matched conditions, yielding 144 responses for the primary between\-chatbot analysis\. A second independent generation round using the same 36 questions and matched query procedures was conducted 7 days later \(June 27, 2026\), yielding an additional 144 responses for within\-model stability analysis\. The questions covered symptoms and warning signs, diagnosis and imaging, conservative management, medication safety, rehabilitation, vertebral augmentation, fracture prevention, and special clinical scenarios\. Five clinical raters, blinded to chatbot identity and generation round, independently evaluated safety, factual accuracy, empathic communication, treatment\-related information quality using DISCERN, patient\-information quality using EQIP, transparency using the JAMA benchmark criteria, and overall quality using the Global Quality Score\. Readability was assessed automatically using six established indices\. Between\-chatbot comparisons and test–retest stability analyses used paired methods appropriate for the outcome type\. Results Inter\-rater agreement was high, with a Fleiss’ kappa of 0\.818 for safety and ICC\(2,1\) values of 0\.816 for accuracy, 0\.820 for empathy, 0\.820 for DISCERN, 0\.820 for EQIP, 0\.821 for JAMA, and 0\.818 for GQS\. Potentially unsafe responses were identified for every chatbot: 3 of 36 ChatGPT responses \(8\.3%\), 5 of 36 DeepSeek responses \(13\.9%\), 6 of 36 Gemini responses \(16\.7%\), and 7 of 36 Doubao responses \(19\.4%\)\. The overall paired difference in safety was not statistically significant \(Cochran&\#x27;s Q = 3\.621, df = 3, P = 0\.305\)\. Factual accuracy differed significantly but only modestly among chatbots \( P = 0\.009; Kendall&\#x27;s W = 0\.108\)\. Empathy showed substantially greater variation \( P &lt; 0\.001; W = 0\.817\), with higher scores for ChatGPT and Gemini than for DeepSeek and Doubao\. DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark, and GQS scores also differed significantly among chatbots \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Doubao produced responses with the greatest estimated textual complexity\. Across the two generation rounds, safety agreement ranged from 88\.9% to 97\.2% \(Gwet&\#x27;s AC1, 0\.838–0\.966\), and median ICC\(2,1\) values across the 12 non\-safety outcomes ranged from 0\.781 to 0\.904\. Conclusions In this time\-stamped, single\-location, two\-round evaluation, all four chatbot interfaces produced some responses classified as potentially unsafe despite generally high clinician\-rated factual accuracy\. Differences were greater in empathy, information quality, transparency, overall quality, and readability than in factual accuracy\. The observed within\-model stability was generally good but did not eliminate variability across generations\. These findings are specific to the evaluated access location, language, single\-turn conditions, and generation dates and should not be assumed to represent stable performance across settings or future model updates\. LLM\-generated OVCF information should not be used as a standalone patient education resource; any potential use should involve clinician oversight, safety safeguards, and further validation\.

## [Anabolic steroid use increases intervertebral disc height and reduces vertebral subchondral bone volume in the lumbar spine in male mice](../publications/664678c454a4e9461c99.md)

Jeffrey L\. Hutchinson; Ermina Hadzic; Oke Shelby; Diana I Quinonez; Emily Lara White; Joy Feng; Andrew Leung; Frank Beier; Matthew William Grol; Cheryle A\. Séguin

Abstract Anabolic steroids are increasingly explored for the management of musculoskeletal disease\. Physiological testosterone levels support joint health, and supraphysiological levels of testosterone are linked to increased intervertebral disc \(IVD\) height and reports of vertebral endplate hyperconcavity\. The ability of high\-dose testosterone to modulate joint repair or degeneration remains speculative\. The goal of this study was to determine if supraphysiological doses of testosterone promote IVD repair or alter the progression of age\-associated IVD degeneration or knee osteoarthritis \(OA\) in the mouse\. To assess injury repair, a percutaneous caudal IVD puncture was implemented at Co7/Co8 in 16\.5\-month\-old male CD\-1 mice \(N=8/group\)\. The lumbar spines of these mice were uninjured to assess age\-related IVD degeneration\. Mice were treated weekly with 15 mg/kg of testosterone enanthate for 6 weeks to emulate anabolic steroid use\. Changes to IVDs and vertebral bones were assessed using microCT and histopathology, and the severity of knee OA was assessed by histopathology\. In the caudal spine, loss of disc height induced by IVD puncture was partially rescued by testosterone with histological features associated with repair\. In the lumbar spine, testosterone induced subchondral bone loss within the vertebral bodies, increased disc height, and promoted endplate hyperconcavity\. Knee histopathology revealed severe OA by 18 months of age, irrespective of treatment\. These findings highlight context\-dependent effects of testosterone at doses modelling anabolic steroid use\. Testosterone rescued disc height loss following IVD injury in the tail but did not improve age\-associated IVD degeneration or knee OA\. In the lumbar spine, testosterone induced vertebral subchondral bone loss, and increased disc height associated with endplate hyperconcavity resembling radiographic changes described as codfish vertebrae associated with osteoporosis and prolonged steroid therapy\. Taken together, these findings suggest that both the IVD and vertebral bone respond to supraphysiological testosterone, with important differences in injury and age\-associated degeneration\.

## [A Phenomenological Study: Life During the Pandemic as an Adolescent in Hidalgo County, Texas, and Life Today](../publications/6646fcbc3546a6182637.md)

Melissa Guevara\-Pérez

The COVID\-19 pandemic disrupted the lives of adolescents during a critical part of social, emotional, and identity development\. Although previous research has noted the immediate effects of the pandemic on adolescents, limited research has examined the long\-term impact on individuals who experienced the pandemic during adolescence and are now transitioning into adulthood\. The purpose of this qualitative phenomenological study was to explore the lived experiences of Hispanic young adults who experienced the COVID\-19 pandemic as adolescents and to understand how those experiences influenced their social and personal development as they transitioned into adulthood\. Participants included 10 Hispanic young adults who resided in Hidalgo County, Texas during the onset of the pandemic\. Data were collected through semi\-structured virtual interviews and analyzed using interpretive phenomenological analysis\. Five overarching themes emerged from the data: Disruption of Adolescent Development, Emotional Distress and Uncertainty, Lasting Changes in Social Development, Identity Development, and Personal Growth and Adaptation\. The findings suggest that participants experienced lasting developmental effects that extended beyond the immediate public health crisis while also demonstrating resilience and personal growth\. The study contributes to the understanding of the long\-term developmental impact of the pandemic among Hispanic young adults and provides implications for developmental psychology, psychological practice, education, and future research involving adolescents affected by large\-scale disruptions\.

## [Control of Chain Transfer by Tailored Metal–Phenyl π ‐Interactions in Bis\(Imino\)Pyridyl Cobalt‐Catalyzed Ethylene Polymerization](../publications/6647a1f8d0aa99d8bc06.md)

Heng Gao; Heng Gao; Chong Wang; Xieyi Xiao; Chunyu Feng; Handou Zheng; Aoxiang Liu; Haiyang Gao; Haiyang Gao

ABSTRACT In bis\(imino\)pyridyl iron/cobalt‐catalyzed ethylene polymerization, broad and bimodal molecular weight distributions of polyethylenes \(PEs\) are often produced because of two different chain transfer pathways\. In this paper, a combined theoretical and experimental study demonstrates how weak attractive metal–phenyl π ‐interactions can favor β ‐H transfer to ethylene over chain transfer to Al to achieve a unimodal distribution\. A series of bis\(imino\)pyridyl cobalt complexes with a substituted 8‐\( p ‐R‐phenyl\)naphthylamine \(R = OMe, Me, CF 3 \) were designed and synthesized for ethylene polymerization\. The intramolecular Co–phenyl π ‐interactions between the capping aryl groups and the cobalt metal are clearly identified in “half‐sandwich” bis\(imino\)pyridyl cobalt complexes\. Ethylene polymerization results show that bis\(imino\)pyridyl cobalt catalyst with an electron‐donating methoxy group can produce low‐molecular‐weight polyethylene with a unimodal distribution\. This control of β ‐H transfer to ethylene monomer is promoted by weak Co–phenyl interactions, operative only for the case of sufficiently electron‐rich aryls \(R = OMe\) and low temperatures \(−10°C–30°C\)\.

## [Influence of Direct Saponification Conditions on Sterol Yield and Composition of the Unsaponifiable Fraction of the Microalga Isochrysis galbana and the Seaweed Ascophyllum nodosum](../publications/66504a663460b0256186.md)

Mina Zareie; Suzanne M\. Budge

ABSTRACT Saponification is a key step for recovering the unsaponifiable fraction \(USF\) of lipids, which contains bioactive sterols, tocopherols, and carotenoids\. This study optimized direct saponification conditions \(50–300 g L −1 KOH; 60°C–100°C\) to recover sterol‐rich USFs from the microalga Isochrysis galbana and the brown seaweed Ascophyllum nodosum , and compared this one‐step approach with conventional lipid extraction followed by saponification\. Changes in carotenoid profile and in vitro antioxidant activity were secondary outcomes\. Sterols and carotenoids were characterized by GC–MS and LC–MS/MS, respectively, and antioxidant capacity by 2,2‐diphenyl‐1‐picrylhydrazyl \(DPPH\) and 2,2′‐azino‐bis \(3‐ethylbenzothiazoline‐6‐sulfonic acid\) \(ABTS\) assays\. Direct saponification gave a USF profile broadly comparable to the two‐step method\. In I\. galbana , brassicasterol was the dominant sterol \(up to 3 mg g −1 dry weight, DW\), whereas fucosterol was dominant in A\. nodosum \(up to 1\.7 mg g −1 DW\)\. Measured sterol content increased with KOH concentration up to 200 g L −1 but declined at higher alkalinity or elevated temperatures, indicating a trade‐off between hydrolysis and degradation\. Under hot alkaline conditions, intact fucoxanthin was not detected in the USFs, while β‐carotene and putative oxygenated \(hydroxy−/keto‐\) carotenoids became more prominent among the detected species, indicating pigment transformation\. The USFs exhibited measurable antioxidant activity, particularly in the ABTS assay \(IC 50 0\.13 and 0\.36 mg mL −1 for A\. nodosum and I\. galbana , respectively\); these activities likely co‐varied with sterol and carotenoid contents, reflecting overall fraction composition rather than a single dominant contributor\. Overall, ≈200 g L −1 KOH at 80°C–100°C produced the highest sterol yields while transforming thermolabile carotenoids\.

## [La resiliencia y autoeficacia como predictores de calidad de vida del profesorado](../publications/66526f458ca0b5f28842.md)

Jacob Fernández González; Sergio Guadalupe Torres Flores; José Alfredo Fernández\-González

El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar cómo la resiliencia académica y la autoeficacia laboral actúan como predictores de la calidad de vida en docentes de educación básica, y su comparación por sexo\. A partir de una muestra de 400 docentes de secundaria, se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, correlacional y transversal con enfoque diferencial\. Los resultados revelan que tanto la autoeficacia como la resiliencia influyen significativamente en la percepción del bienestar laboral, con variaciones relevantes en el profesorado, donde se identificaron desafíos emocionales vinculados a la sobrecarga de responsabilidades y a la limitada valoración institucional, contrastados con percepciones de mayor estabilidad emocional en otros sectores del magisterio\. El estudio visibiliza la necesidad de incorporar la perspectiva de género en el análisis del bienestar docente y sugiere rutas institucionales de intervención para fortalecer el equilibrio psicosocial y profesional\.

## [Facial Expression Recognition using Label\-and Scale\-Distribution\-aware Loss\-assisted Cross Vision Transformer](../publications/66538b8cf5e7dfd584fc.md)

Bharathi Manchenahalli Gopalakrishna Rao; Divya Savithramma Ramakrishna Reddy

In recent years, Facial Expression Recognition \(FER\) has gained attention as a crucial area of computer vision\. However, FER methods depend on single\-source facial data that often experience reduced accuracy and instability because of challenges such as facial occlusion and variations in illumination\. Moreover, existing FER approaches fail to understand the salient facial regions, resulting in poor interpretability and performance\. Hence, this research proposes the Label\- and Scale\- Distribution\-aware Loss\-assisted Cross Vision Transformer \(LSDL\-CrossViT\) to solve the issues in FER\. The proposed model captures the global facial structure and local expression\-specific cues through cross\-attention\-based feature learning\. By incorporating the attention mechanism through discriminative loss design, the pipeline improves class separability and reduces classification errors across multiple facial expression categories\. This research considers three benchmarks such as RAF\-DB, AffectNet\-8, and CK\+, to estimate the complete performance of the proposed approach\. The experimental results illustrate that the proposed LSDL\-CrossViT gains a balanced accuracy of 93\.18%, 71\.84%, and 99\.01% on the RAF\-DB, AffectNet\-8, and CK\+ datasets, respectively, as compared to the reproduced Distract your Attention Network \(DAN\) and Self Learning Weight Network related to Label Distribution Training \(SLW\-LDT\) models\.

## [Differences in spatial imagery from the dual perspectives of residents and tourists: A case study of Shiwei village](../publications/667d2308d5c33103379d.md)

Yuhui Xu; Chang an; Batu nacun; Jiaming Wu; Lu Han; Kachalov Ilia

Spatial imagery \(SI\) refers to people’s experiential understanding of the surrounding environment\. Residents’ and tourists’ spatial imagery \(SI\) of rural tourism destinations can provide important references for the coordinated development and spatial optimization of destinations\. This study has constructed a theoretical framework of “SI elements\-SI structure\-SI pattern”, and employed a mixed approach including interviews, cognitive map \(CM\), spatial interpolation methods, and GIS spatial analysis to reveal the differences in SI between residents and tourists in Shiwei village\. The results show that: \(1\) In terms of SI elements, residents primarily organize SI through region and path elements, emphasizing spatial continuity, familiarity, and daily practicality; whereas tourists mainly rely on landmark elements to perceive SI, focusing on symbolic uniqueness tourism and functionality\. \(2\) In terms of SI structure, residents frequently employ high\-level sequential CM, whereas tourists primarily utilize low\-level monolithic CM\. \(3\) In terms of SI pattern, the image hotspots of residents exhibit an elliptical clustering pattern with a “dense in the north, sparse in the south” spatial distribution; whereas the image hotspots of tourists are distributed in multiple clusters concentrated in three main areas, forming an overall arc\-shaped distribution pattern\. This research provides empirically grounded insights for the development and spatial planning of rural tourism destinations and represents a methodologically rigorous attempt to analyze village SI using a mixed qualitative and quantitative approach at a micro\-scale\.

## [Beyond Error Correction: ChatGPT as Formative Feedback for Arabic Writing](../publications/66815d057bf7c969a1c2.md)

Abdul Hafidz bin Zaid; Muassomah Muassomah; Moh\. Ismail; Alif Cahya Setiyadi; Agus Yasin

The increasing adoption of large language models \(LLMs\) is transforming language education; however, evidence regarding their pedagogical value for Arabic writing remains limited\. This study investigates the educational potential of ChatGPT as an AI\-assisted formative feedback tool for Arabic academic writing in a pesantren\-based university in Indonesia\. To achieve this, employing a qualitative descriptive design, the study integrates Error Analysis with the Student Feedback Literacy framework to examine students’ writing errors and evaluate the educational quality of AI\-generated feedback\. A corpus of 30 Arabic writing texts produced by 30 first\-year students enrolled in an intensive Arabic matriculation program was analyzed\. ChatGPT \(GPT\-4, May 2024 version\) generated corrective feedback using a standardized prompt, and two Arabic linguistics experts evaluated the linguistic accuracy and pedagogical usefulness of each response\. The findings identified 132 errors comprising 39\.4% lexical, 32\.6% syntactic, and 28\.0% morphological errors\. Notably, ChatGPT produced fully acceptable feedback for 50\.76% of the errors, demonstrating its capacity in lexical and syntactic correction\. However, its performance was less consistent in addressing morphologically complex and context\-dependent constructions\. Overall, the findings indicate that ChatGPT supports learners’ ability to recognize and revise writing errors, although it still requires teacher validation\. Consequently, this study contributes valuable insights into AI\-assisted language education through meaningful engagement with formative feedback in Arabic writing\.

## [REGULATING DEEPFAKES IN NIGERIA: ASSESSING THE ADEQUACY OF THE EXISTING CYBERCRIME FRAMEWORK](../publications/668fa449c642468e7099.md)

Ridwan Kolapo; Sarah Ousmane Yaye; Samirah Usman; Sanusi Wakilat Olanrewaju; Babagoni Muhammad; Abdul\-Shakur Sambo

Generative artificial intelligence now enables the cheap fabrication of audio, images and videos of real people\. Nigeria has been the scene of a range of such abuse, from a cloned\-voice clip preceding the 2023 elections to deepfakes of the President and of Peter Obi from 2024 to 2026\. This article examines the adequacy of Nigeria’s cybercrime law to regulate deepfakes, based on four stages of their life: acquisition, synthesis, dissemination and consequence and four criteria of evaluation: rule clarity, institutional responsibility, enforceability and remedy\. Using a qualitative doctrinal method, the Cybercrimes \(Prohibition, Prevention, etc\.\) Act 2015 \(as amended in 2024\), the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the Evidence Act 2011 \(as amended 2023\) and constitutional privacy are evaluated for application to deepfakes\. The cybercrime law covers fraud, impersonation and child sexual abuse imagery deepfakes, and \(arguably\) sexual deepfakes, but offers no definition of synthetic media, no offence of non\-consensual synthesis \(or of possession/distribution of synthetic media\), no takedown duty for deepfakes, and no rules or capacity for authenticating electronic evidence\. Statutory reform is recommended, focused narrowly on the regulation of deepfakes, including through labeling duties, victim\-focused remedies, forensic capacity\-building and harmony with national\-level AI governance\.

## [PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION MECHANISMS FOR ENSURING HIGHER EDUCATION QUALITY: RESULTS OF APPLICATION AND PROSPECTS FOR DEVELOPMENT](../publications/66b33080dc2a8a5c3247.md)

Д\. К\. Шутов

The article examines the mechanisms of public administration for ensuring the quality of higher education in Ukraine through the prism of the classifications established in the scholarly discourse, as well as through the practices of their functioning and their actual impact on the international competitiveness of domestic higher education institutions\. The methodological basis of the research combines the analysis of regulatory and legal acts, programme documents of the international and national levels, statistical data of the National Agency for Higher Education Quality Assurance, and a comparative analysis of the dynamics of the positioning of Ukrainian universities in the leading international rankings during 2022–2026\. A contradiction has been identified between the architectonics of building the higher education quality assurance system and the comparatively low positioning of Ukrainian universities in international rankings \(Quacquarelli Symonds World University Rankings; Times Higher Education World University Rankings; Academic Ranking of World Universities, ShanghaiRanking\)\. In particular, it has been established that the number of Ukrainian universities represented in the QS World University Rankings decreased from 11 in 2023 to 4 in 2026, while the highest position of domestic institutions in the Times Higher Education ranking has consistently remained within the 801–1000 group despite the quantitative growth of their representation\. The exhaustion of the potential of the traditional regulatory\-legal, organisational\- administrative and economic mechanisms of public administration in the higher education sphere has been substantiated, along with the need to search for new mechanisms of public administration for ensuring quality\. The article also offers proposals on the necessity of applying innovative mechanisms for ensuring the quality of higher education, namely those grounded in the toolkit of artificial intelligence, big data analytics, and robotic process automation, the practical significance of which is confirmed by international experience and the analytical priorities of the national quality assurance system\.

## [Loss‐Engineered Terahertz Pixelated Metasensors for Enhanced Molecular Vibrational Fingerprint Sensing](../publications/66b57a39671f0d9499b0.md)

Chenglin Yang; Yuqing Cui; Donghai Han; Yushan Hou; Zhonglei Shen; Andreas Tittl; Liuyang Zhang; Ruqiang Yan; Xuefeng Chen

Molecular vibrational fingerprints in the terahertz \(THz\) regime offer unique opportunities for label\-free chemical and biological sensing\. Metasensors can amplify these vibrational signals through local near\-field enhancement\. However, current THz molecular fingerprint metasensors lack a systematic design and optimization methodology, which severely limits their potential\. Here, we unveil the crucial role of resonant loss rate in THz molecular fingerprint sensing and present a loss\-engineering methodology for optimized molecular vibrational sensing\. Based on the proposed methodology, we experimentally demonstrate a 12\.6\-fold enhancement of the molecular fingerprint signal with three\-dimensionally printed pixelated metasensors\. Furthermore, the pixelated metasensors support vibrational strong\-coupling, providing a unified platform for enhanced molecular sensing and strong light\-matter interaction\. Overall, the proposed metasensor could bridge THz molecular vibrational fingerprint sensing to end\-use applications in label\-free chemical and biomedical detection\.

## [Modeling of titanium blast\-finished surface roughness for dental implants using strictly grouped validation and SHAP\-explainable machine learning](../publications/66b585aca7db3242a762.md)

Junjiang Hao; Yibo Liu; Qiqi Liu; Yuan Sui; Hanqi Su; Yucheng Su

Predictable control of implant surface roughness is important because a consistent micrometre\-scale topography may provide reproducible conditions for early osteoblast attachment and subsequent osseointegration\. To address the low efficiency of traditional trial\-and\-error optimization and its limited ability to characterize the nonlinear relationship between sandblasting parameters and surface roughness \(Ra\) in pure titanium substrates for oral implants, this study developed a machine learning\-based predictive model\. Grit size \(60–100 mesh\), Pressure \(0\.2–0\.4 MPa\), Distance \(50–100 mm\), and Time \(15–60 s\) were selected as input variables\. A total of 180 datasets were obtained by combining orthogonal experiments with random experiments\. Ten machine learning algorithms, including ensemble learning, nonlinear, and linear models, were compared\. To avoid the apparent data leakage caused by random splitting of repeated measurements, Leave\-One\-Group\-Out Cross\-Validation \(LOGO\-CV\) was used to evaluate the model’s predictive performance and stability onunseen process combinations\. The results showed that, within the investigated parameter range, the Ra values of the titanium surfaces ranged from 1\.083 to 2\.494 μm\. This range lies between the approximate dimensions of osteoblast cell bodies and their filopodial extensions and may provide local anchorage sites for filopodia, thereby facilitating early mechanical interlocking at the bone–implant interface\. Comparative analysis showed that the support vector regression \(SVR\) model achieved the best predictive performance\. After Bayesian optimization, the optimized SVR model achieved an R² of 0\.7538 and an RMSE of 0\.1480 μm\. Analysis of variance and SHAP\-based interpretability analysis confirmed that grit size and blasting pressure had significant effects on Ra \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. The relative importance of the parameters was ranked as follows: grit size &gt; blasting pressure &gt; blasting time &gt; blasting distance\. Within the tested parameter range, the proposed model may facilitate sandblasting\-parameter screening and improve the consistency of implant surface preparation, thereby providing process\-level support for the reproducible production of surface conditions relevant to early osseointegration and implant stability and establishing a basis for subsequent biological validation and clinical translation\.

## [Consumer perceptions of marketing mix in supermarkets: a cross\-cultural analysis of Croatia and Tanzania](../publications/66be0f97b393637209fa.md)

Marko Šoštar; Robert Suphian; Gabrijela Garic; Josip Knežević

The primary objective of this study was to examine whether significant differences exist in the perception of supermarket marketing mix elements between consumers in Croatia and Tanzania\. The analysis focused on five key dimensions \(product, price, distribution, promotion, and personnel\) with the aim of identifying the factors contributing to consumer satisfaction or dissatisfaction within distinct market contexts\. The research employed a quantitative methodology, gathering data from 991 respondents \(400 from Croatia and 591 from Tanzania\) through a structured survey based on a five\-point Likert scale\. The findings revealed statistically significant differences across all five marketing mix dimensions\. Tanzanian respondents consistently expressed more favorable perceptions, particularly in relation to promotional activities and personnel interactions\. Exploratory factor analysis suggested three broader dimensions, whereas confirmatory factor analysis provided stronger support for the theoretically specified five\-factor structure\. Multi\-group CFA further supported metric and scalar measurement invariance across the Croatian and Tanzanian samples\. The findings highlight the importance of adapting retail marketing strategies, particularly communication, service delivery, and promotional activities, to the specific characteristics of different national market contexts\.

## [Two‐Step Grafted AlN /Silicone Composites Thermal Interface Materials With Balanced Thermal Conductivity and Electrical Insulation for Thermal Management](../publications/66c361cb41657bc32902.md)

Lin Wang; Ji‐Yong Zou; Qiu Zeng; Li Zhang; Hao Zhang; Shengyong You

ABSTRACT In this study, tris\(2‐methoxyethoxy\)vinylsilane was grafted onto aluminum nitride \(AlN\) fillers to improve interfacial compatibility with silicone oil and reduce interfacial thermal resistance\. A two‐step covalent bonding strategy, combining surface grafting with subsequent curing, was developed to fabricate AlN‐Vi/silicone composites with high thermal conductivity and excellent electrical insulation\. XPS, FTIR, and SEM confirmed successful grafting and uniform filler dispersion\. The optimized composite \(G‐240\) achieved a thermal conductivity of 2\.723 W m −1 K −1 at 240 wt% loading, approximately 6\.8 times that of neat silicone, with volume resistivity exceeding 1\.0 × 10 14 Ω cm and dielectric breakdown strength of 15\.33 kV mm −1 , significantly outperforming the unmodified composite\. Accelerated aging tests further demonstrated that the grafted silane layer may suppress AlN hydrolysis and preserve thermal performance\. This work offers a simple and effective route for high‐performance silicone composite thermal interface materials in electronic packaging and 5G applications\.

## [When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross\-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models](../publications/66c629f63639d75534cf.md)

Wei Cai; Jian Zhao; Yuchen Yuan; Xuelong Li

Multimodal large language models \(MLLMs\) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly\. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent\-level risk, where cross\-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path\-level optimization alone cannot correct\. We propose SAFE\-PRO, which uses a Risk\-Conditioned Uncertainty \(RCU\) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross\-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety\-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over\-refusal\. We also build SSUI\-Dialog, a multimodal multi\-turn dataset with dual\-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe\-completion risk under RCU\. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE\-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over\-refusal, and surpasses GPT\-4o and Claude\-3\.5\-Sonnet in average single\-turn safety\.

## [Level of Utilization of Video\-Based Lessons in Chemistry during Modular Distance Learning \(MDL\) In Selected Public High Schools of Lapu\-Lapu City](../publications/66c70b9128ec7307f289.md)

Reynaldo Abella Magallanes

Video\-based lessons have emerged as vital instructional support during Modular Distance Learning \(MDL\), yet teachers’ experiences in developing and delivering such materials for Chemistry instruction remain insufficiently explored\. Employing a descriptive–correlational research design, this study involved thirty \(30\) Chemistry teachers from Mactan National High School and Babag National High School selected through total enumeration\. Data were gathered using a structured survey questionnaire covering demographic profile and level of utilization of vide\-based lessons in Chemistry across Preparation and Development, Implementation and Instructional Delivery, Alignment with Chemistry Learning Competencies, and Monitoring and Assessment of Learning\. Mean, frequency, percentage, Spearman rho, and Rank\-Biserial Correlation were used for statistical analysis\. Findings revealed that respondents were predominantly young, female, and with graduate units; most had fewer than six years of service and attended a limited number of trainings\. Teachers assessed their overall experiences as Very Good, with Monitoring and Assessment of Learning rated highest and Implementation and Instructional Delivery lowest\. Correlational analysis showed no significant relationship between profile variables age, sex, educational attainment, teaching experience, and trainings attended and level of utilization of video\-based lessons\. Results suggest that Chemistry teachers are capable of using video\-based lessons regardless of personal or professional background\. Recommendations include utilization of video\-based lesson exemplar in Chemistry\.

## [Graph Dirichlet Energy for Fitting\-Free Bivariate Causal Inference](../publications/66c8e2f18a1031ff0ffc.md)

Povilas Daniušis

We propose the Graph Dirichlet Energy Causal Inference \(GDECI\) criterion for distinguishing cause from effect in bivariate settings\. For a candidate direction $X\\to Y$, we construct a kernel similarity graph from $X$ and treat $Y$ as a graph signal\. The score is the Dirichlet energy of this signal, induced by the unnormalized graph Laplacian\. The reverse score swaps the variables, and the lower\-energy direction is inferred as causal\. The method requires neither regression fitting nor independence testing\. After the empirical probability integral transform, its decisions are invariant under strictly monotone transformations of either variable, and the graph operations reduce to convolutions, allowing exact evaluation in $O\(n\\log n\)$ time and $O\(n\)$ memory\. At the population level, GDECI compares degree\-weighted Bayes squared prediction errors plus a non\-negative smoothness term of the regression function\. As the bandwidth tends to zero, the weights become uniform and the smoothness term vanishes, reducing the criterion to a RECI\-type comparison of expected conditional variances in copula space\. Empirically, we compare GDECI with QCCD, GRCI, CAM, IGCI \(two variants\), RESIT, LOCI, QPE\-k, and RECI \(two variants\), in accuracy on 1899 cause\-\-effect pairs and in inference speed\. GDECI ranked fifth of eleven methods in macro\-averaged accuracy on 12 synthetic suites \($0\.776$\)\. On the real\-world Tuebingen pairs, it ranked third in unweighted accuracy \($0\.684$\) and fifth in weighted accuracy \($0\.678$\)\. It was also the fastest of the compared methods up to $n\\approx10^\{4\}$\. The accompanying code repository: https://github\.com/povidanius/gdeci\.

## [Type I Error in Single\-Case Experimental Designs](../publications/66cd564ffa303780dba2.md)

Katie Wolfe; John M\. Ferron

Abstract Type I errors, or false positives, occur when a researcher erroneously concludes that the independent variable caused a change in the dependent variable\. Type I errors can result in resources being misused in both research and practice\. Although Type I errors are most often associated with group design paradigms, researchers using single\-case experimental designs are also susceptible to making Type I errors\. In this article, we describe the research on Type I errors in single\-case experimental designs across analytic methods, including visual analysis, machine learning, effect estimation, and randomization approaches\. We also suggest ways that each analytic method can be used to mitigate Type I errors and highlight aspects of Type I error in single\-case experimental designs that are understudied and in need of additional research\.
