## [Trgovina z ljudmi na Karibih: Kritična analiza regionalnih odzivov in prevencijskih strategij](../publications/66d285b5b5b544756a6f.md)

Kaja Urbančič

Migration in the Caribbean region is not a new phenomenon, as these island nations and their economies were built around the movement of people between islands and mutual collaboration\. The rise of human trafficking in this part of the world is a direct result of push and pull factors unique to the region&\#x27;s economic, political, geographical, social and cultural spheres\. It takes the form predominantly of sex work, forced labour, domestic servitude and child exploitation, making women and children the most vulnerable demographic groups\. The Caribbean trafficking route is used because of its many facilitating factors, such as the islands&\#x27; lax border security, lack of resources, insufficient prioritisation and local culture facilitating the demand for sexual services and child exploitation\. Countries’ reliance on overlapping industries, the inability of individuals to obtain work in their country of origin, and political instability in some island states act as drivers of intra\-regional migration within the Caribbean region, facilitating domestic trafficking\. Ever since the U\.S\. Office to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons started including Caribbean nations in its annual Trafficking in Persons reports, the region has seen an influx of international attention pertaining to this type of criminal activity, although the results of the inclusion of Caribbean nations in these reports have been mixed\. This work analyses a selection of literary sources, with an emphasis on post\-COVID literature, to present an up\-to\-date overview of human trafficking in the Caribbean region, nations&\#x27; responses and their prevention strategies\. It provides a series of contextualised challenges nations face in their anti\-trafficking efforts, including vague terminology, extended court proceedings and severe administrative backlogs, and finds it imperative that governments promptly address the issues of underreporting, lack of monitoring and fear of retribution\. Political incentive is a catalyst for improving legislation and eradicating social inequalities but seems to marginalise human trafficking, so more is needed in the fields of data collection and victim care to adequately assess its current scope\. This work provides a basis for improving regional responses, relevant prevention strategies and revised legislation\. However, it also recognises that an updated, standardised, internationally recognised definition of human trafficking is the first step towards improving the multifaceted process required to successfully combat human trafficking\.

## [Hubungan Dukungan Sosial terhadap Kelelahan Kerja pada Barista di Banjarmasin](../publications/66d62620b57169e8560a.md)

Wandira; Dyta Setiawati Hariyono; Gladis Corinna Marsha

Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui hubungan antara dukungan sosial dan kelelahan pada barista di Banjarmasin\. Barista menghadapi tuntutan kerja tinggi, seperti jam kerja panjang hingga 13 jam per hari dan shift malam, yang berpotensi menimbulkan kelelahan fisik maupun mental\. Penelitian kuantitatif korelasional ini melibatkan 85 barista di Banjarmasin yang dipilih melalui teknik convenience sampling\. Dukungan sosial diukur menggunakan skala aspek Sarafino \(Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha = 0,754\), sedangkan kelelahan diukur dengan Fatigue Assessment Scale \(Cronbach&\#x27;s Alpha = 0,829\)\. Hasil uji Pearson Correlation menunjukkan hubungan negatif yang signifikan antara dukungan sosial dan kelelahan \(r = \-0,33; p &lt; 0,01\)\. Artinya, semakin tinggi dukungan sosial yang diterima barista, semakin rendah kelelahan yang dialaminya\. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya penciptaan budaya kerja suportif di lingkungan kafe melalui peningkatan apresiasi, interaksi positif, dan dukungan informasional kepada barista sebagai upaya menekan kelelahan kerja\.

## [Equivalence testing and run\-count design for stochastic machine\-learning experiments](../publications/66d668088eea6318f084.md)

Dmytro Knopov; Nadiya Shvai

Claims that two training methods perform equally well often rest on a non\-significant difference between two or three runs per method\. We develop a protocol, with its power theory, for certifying practical equivalence in per\-run metrics such as the AUROC \(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve\)\. It rests on a two\-level \(seed x item\) variance model separating between\-run dispersion from item\-level noise\. Equivalence within a pre\-specified margin is tested by two one\-sided tests \(TOST\), equivalently by a confidence interval inside the margin; a two\-level bootstrap covers composite statistics\. A closed\-form formula converts a margin and a target power into runs per method; its shifted\-t refinement is calibrated against the realised two\-level process\. Simulations on a 270\-cell grid and under non\-Gaussian seed laws confirm the formula within its design\-relevant range, from five runs per method\. For four published runs of a joint energy\-based model, the failure to certify equivalence was largely decided by design: with the variance calibrated to those runs, two per method certify with probability near three per cent, whereas certifying 0\.01 AUROC at 80 per cent power needs twelve even under exact equality\. A second case study on a thousand\-seed CIFAR\-10 zoo and the MultiBERTs checks the formula against real seed laws \(within 0\.05 in that range\) and resolves comparisons that two or three runs leave undecided\. In a two\-stage design \(pilot, then formula\), our experiments suggest that an upper confidence bound on the pilot variance substantially reduces the undersizing seen with its point estimate\.

## [A language portrait study of the language awareness of speech therapy and audiology professionals in South Africa](../publications/66e543f173afd1235294.md)

Susan Coetzee‐Van Rooy; Verbra Frances Pfeiffer

For this study, Pfeiffer collected 20 language portraits from multilingual participants who are speech therapy or speech audiology professionals in South Africa with the portrait\-corpus instrument\. Within the Dynamic Model of Multilingualism \(DMM\), it is argued that the communicative needs of people drive the development of their multilingual system\. Speech therapists and audiologists in South Africa engage in complex multilingual professional communication, and they receive linguistic training\. The aim of the study is to evaluate the usefulness of the portrait\-corpus instrument to garner information about the meta\- and crosslinguistic awareness of multilingual participants\. Evidence from using the portrait\-corpus instrument indicates that for the participants in this study \(language professionals\), references to metalinguistic awareness are not prominent, and references to crosslinguistic awareness are very prominent, similar to other studies with multilingual students\. Within the context of this small sample of multilingual clinicians, the cautious conclusion is that the written portrait narratives elicited few explicit metalinguistic reflections, suggesting that the portrait\-corpus approach might not be the most effective instrument for investigating metalinguistic awareness\.

## [On the tracks of Pulvis Puteolana: provenance and selection of Roman hydraulic materials](../publications/66e60b71b5ada34c2cd3.md)

Martina Mercurio; Giovanna Montesano; Piergiulio Cappelletti; Paola Petrosino; Sossio Fabio Graziano; Assunta Campanile; Barbara Liguori; Concetta Rispoli

Abstract Phlegraean pozzolana played an important role in the production of Roman hydraulic mortars, capable of enhancing mechanical strength even in contact with water\. For this reason, this geomaterial was widely exported along the Mediterranean coasts \(ROMACONS Project\)\. Nowadays, the term pozzolana is strictly referred as the unconsolidated facies of the Neapolitan Yellow Tuff \(NYT; ca\. 15 ka\), while the term pozzolan suits any fine\-grained, mainly glassy volcanic ash as well as commercial products exhibiting pozzolanic activity\. This study characterizes pozzolana stricto sensu and two incoherent deposits belonging to post\-NYT eruption collected from quarries from Phlegraean Fields area, historically used by the Romans and compares them with pozzolanic aggregates found in hydraulic mortars from both Campanian and extra\-regional archaeological sites\. A multi\-analytical approach was employed to obtain detailed minero\-petrographic and chemical information with Polarized Optical Microscopy \(POM\), X\-Ray Powder Diffraction \(XRPD\), X\-Ray Fluorescence \(XRF\), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy\-Dispersive X\-Ray Spectroscopy \(FESEM\-EDS\)\. In addition, technological and physical properties were assessed through pozzolanic activity test and laser particle size analyses\. Experimental data showed that post\-NYT pyroclastic deposits also exhibit pozzolanic activity and can develop hydraulic properties\. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that both NYT and selected post\-NYT deposits were recognized empirically by Romans as suitable raw materials for hydraulic mortars preparation for both local and distal constructions\. The Fratini test is therefore used here as a modern assessment of pozzolanic reactivity, while provenance and selection hypotheses are primarily based on the combined petrographic, mineralogical and geochemical evidence\. In fact, the compositional match between pozzolana samples analyses and literature glass data from Roman mortars, in relation to the compositional fields of known Phlegraean Fields eruptions, suggests that post\-NYT deposits were also employed as pulvis puteolana \. This research establishes a first reference database to further the knowledge of ancient Roman construction technology\.

## [Repeated pressure build\-up tests to characterise mining\-induced permeability changes around in\-seam gas drainage boreholes](../publications/66ec8415d72f09ed3b4e.md)

Kamal Omarov; Xin Zhang; Europe Paudyal; Yu Jing; Guangyao Si

Mining\-induced permeability enhancement around in\-seam boreholes offers a critical opportunity to improve gas drainage efficiency in low\-permeability coal seams, yet its quantitative characterisation under longwall top coal caving \(LTCC\) remains largely unexplored\. This study presents a unique field\-validated, quantitative characterisation of this permeability evolution in an active LTCC setting, through a programme of sixteen repeat pressure build\-up tests conducted in a thick lignite deposit\. Eight tests with sufficient pressure recovery were interpreted using Horner analysis and log\-log pressure\-derivative diagnostics\. The initial coal seam permeability confirms dual\-porosity behaviour characteristic of natural coal\. As the longwall face advanced, systematic contraction of the wellbore storage regime provided progressive evidence of permeability enhancement, increasing by approximately one order of magnitude at intermediate face distances and reaching two orders of magnitude as the face approached the borehole\. Independent boundary inversion corroborated this trend, yielding enhancements approaching 200\-fold at close face proximity\. Late\-time diagnostics revealed an evolving drainage geometry, transitioning from a channelled no\-flow boundary configuration to a fully enclosed rectangular drainage domain as the expanding drainage radius intercepted additional boundaries\. These findings demonstrate that LTCC\-induced stress redistribution can dramatically and progressively enhance coal seam permeability, with direct implications for optimising borehole placement and drainage scheduling in gassy LTCC panels\.

## [Building Business Resilience of Food MSMEs in Tourism Destinations: The Roles of Adaptive Marketing Capability, Supply Chain Resilience, and Digital Transformation Amid Climate and Tourism Disruptions](../publications/66ee14975aea5986bb54.md)

Siwi Manganti; Bayu Wardhana

Food micro, small, and medium enterprises \(SMEs\) in Bali&\#x27;s tourism destinations face dual pressures stemming from climate disruption and tourism visit volatility\. Both forces simultaneously threaten the operational continuity and business resilience of small\-scale food businesses that are heavily dependent on the stability of the tourism ecosystem\. This study empirically examines the roles of adaptive marketing capabilities \(AMC\), supply chain resilience \(SCR\), and digital transformation capability \(DTC\) in building the business resilience \(BR\) of food SMEs, as well as the moderating effect of climate and tourism disruption \(CTD\) on the SCR–BR relationship\.A quantitative approach with a cross\-sectional survey design was employed, collecting data from 220 food SME owners and managers across Badung Regency, Denpasar City, and Gianyar Regency, Bali\. The structured questionnaire instrument used a 5\-point Likert scale covering 26 indicators across five latent constructs\. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) via SmartPLS 4\.0 software, with a 5,000\-sample bootstrapping procedure applied for significance testing\. All seven hypotheses were supported with statistically significant results\. AMC positively and significantly influenced SCR \(β=0\.449; t=7\.242; p&lt;0\.001\) and directly influenced BR \(β=0\.162; t=2\.077; p&lt;0\.05\)\. SCR positively influenced DTC \(β=0\.528; t=9\.103; p&lt;0\.001\) and directly influenced BR \(β=0\.249; t=3\.320; p&lt;0\.01\)\. DTC positively influenced BR \(β=0\.311; t=4\.380; p&lt;0\.001\)\. The sequential mediation AMC→SCR→DTC→BR was confirmed as significant with an indirect effect of β=0\.074 \(BC\-CI 95% \[0\.032, 0\.127\]\)\. CTD was found to strengthen the effect of SCR on BR \(β=0\.143; t=2\.103; p&lt;0\.05\)\. The model collectively explained 46\.7% of the variance in business resilience \(R²=0\.467\), with positive Q² values confirming adequate predictive relevance\. Adaptive marketing capabilities, supply chain resilience, and digital transformation capability constitute three mutually reinforcing strategic pillars for building business resilience among food SMEs in tourism destinations\. The identified sequential mediation mechanism confirms that investment in market adaptive ability progressively translates into supply chain robustness and ultimately catalyzes digital transformation as the foundation of long\-term business resilience\. As climate and tourism disruption intensifies, enhancing supply chain resilience becomes increasingly critical and of high strategic value\. This study contributes theoretically to the dynamic capabilities framework and SME resilience literature, while offering practical recommendations for business practitioners and policymakers in Bali&\#x27;s tourism sector\.

## [Self\-reported memory strategy use following acquired brain injury](../publications/66f09d3ce1f20e5b4a48.md)

Edo Grevers; Nikita L\. Frankenmolen; Michelle G\. Jansen; Joukje M\. Oosterman; Roy P\. C\. Kessels; Dirk Bertens

INTRODUCTION: Neuropsychological rehabilitation following acquired brain injury \(ABI\) often involves interventions teaching individuals with ABI strategies to compensate for memory impairment\. However, little is known about spontaneous memory strategy use \(i\.e\. without treatment\) and its determinants\. The primary aim was to compare spontaneous memory strategy use in daily life and during a memory task between participants with ABI and cognitively unimpaired controls\. Other aims were to investigate the relationships between strategy use, demographic and clinical characteristics, and memory performance\. METHODS: Sixty adults \(aged 27\-71\) with ABI \(≥3 months post\-injury\) were included at the start of their rehabilitation program\. The control group consisted of 187 cognitively unimpaired volunteers \(aged 18\-79\)\. Spontaneous memory strategy use in daily life was measured using the strategy scale of the Metamemory in Adulthood Questionnaire \(MIA\)\. Memory complaints were assessed with the Everyday Memory Questionnaire\-Revised \(EMQ\-R\) and memory performance with the subtest Verbal Paired Associates of the Wechsler Memory Scale\-Fourth Edition \(WMS\-IV VPA\)\. Additionally, memory strategy use during the VPA was assessed\. RESULTS: = \.367\)\. Within both groups, more memory complaints and female sex were related to using more strategies in daily life\. Task\-related strategies were unrelated to memory performance in the ABI group but positively related in controls\. CONCLUSIONS: ABI participants report using fewer memory strategies in daily life than controls, despite performing worse on a memory task and experiencing more memory complaints\. Since efficiently employed compensation strategies are the most effective way to compensate for memory impairment, our results emphasize the importance of training memory strategies after ABI and provide valuable insights for creating individual treatment plans\.

## [Multistage CBAM\-enhanced deep learning for three\-class classification of radiographically derived bone mass status labels on knee radiographs](../publications/66f946d943e706fbaf8e.md)

Songjia Li; Jing Lv; Tao Fang

Objective To develop and validate a deep learning model incorporating multistage convolutional block attention modules \(CBAMs\) for classifying the radiographically derived bone\-mass labels \(normal bone mass, osteopenia, and osteoporosis\) of a public knee radiograph dataset, and to investigate the potential of knee radiography for opportunistic screening of abnormal bone mass\. Methods This study used the publicly available Multi\-Class Knee Osteoporosis x\-Ray Dataset, which was released on Kaggle and compiled from multiple publicly accessible knee radiograph sources\. The class labels \(normal bone mass, osteopenia, and osteoporosis\) were assigned by the dataset provider on the basis of radiographic features and were not verified against dual\-energy x\-ray absorptiometry \(DXA\) T\-scores; the model therefore classifies the dataset&\#x27;s radiographic labels rather than DXA\-defined bone mass status\. After assessing image integrity, label consistency, and data usability, a total of 1,947 knee radiographs were included, comprising 780 images labeled as normal bone mass, 374 as osteopenia, and 793 as osteoporosis\. The dataset was stratified into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 70:20:10\. All images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels and normalized using the ImageNet mean and standard deviation\. A multi\-stage convolutional block attention module \(CBAM\)\-enhanced classification model was developed based on a VGG19\-style convolutional neural network and compared with the ResNet50, EfficientNet\-B0, DenseNet121, and VGG19 baseline models, as well as several attention\-based ablation models\. Model performance was evaluated using overall accuracy, class\-wise precision, recall, and F1\-score, together with confusion matrices and one\-vs\.\-rest receiver operating characteristic curves\. Gradient\-weighted class activation mapping \(Grad\-CAM\) was further used to visualize and assess the image regions contributing to model predictions\. Results On the independent test set, the multistage CBAM model achieved the highest overall accuracy of 90\.77% \(177/195\), outperforming VGG19, ResNet50, EfficientNet\-B0, DenseNet121, and a reproduced model from the literature\. The area under the ROC curve \(AUC\) was 0\.982 for normal bone mass, 0\.991 for osteopenia, and 0\.981 for osteoporosis\. The confusion matrix showed 68/78, 34/38, and 75/79 correctly classified images in the three categories, respectively, with most errors occurring between adjacent bone\-mass states\. Ablation experiments showed that multistage CBAM outperformed attention\-free VGG19, SE\-VGG19, ECA\-VGG19, and stacked CBAM\. Grad\-CAM highlighted primarily the distal femur, proximal tibia, and periarticular osseous structures\. All results were obtained from a single stratified split and a single random seed \(42\); because of limited computational resources, repeated runs over multiple seeds and k\-fold cross\-validation could not be performed\. Conclusion The multistage CBAM\-enhanced model effectively distinguished the radiographically derived bone\-mass labels \(normal bone mass, osteopenia, and osteoporosis\) of this public knee radiograph dataset\. Because the labels were not verified against DXA, the model should be regarded as a classifier of the dataset&\#x27;s radiographic labels rather than of DXA\-defined bone mass status\. It may serve as an adjunctive tool for opportunistic screening of abnormal bone mass and provide imaging\-based prompts for subsequent DXA assessment and fracture\-risk evaluation, subject to further validation against DXA\-derived ground truth, de\-duplication and patient\-level partitioning, and external data\.

## [Peran Media Sosial Dalam Mendorong Semangat Bela Negara di Kalangan Generasi Muda](../publications/66faf3631226dd1ea689.md)

Amelia Putri; Oktaviyani; Sesilia Teme

Sangat penting untuk menanamkan kesadaran bela negara kepada semua warga negara, terutama generasi milenial karena mereka adalah penerus dan pewaris kelangsungan kehidupan berbangsa dan bernegara\. Ini akan membantu mempertahankan negara dari ancaman dari dalam dan luar, baik militer maupun non militer\. Pendidikan sangat penting dalam bela negara karena membantu generasi muda memahami sejarah, prinsip, dan komitmen untuk melindungi kedaulatan negara\. Melalui pendidikan, siswa dapat memahami pentingnya mempertahankan persatuan dan kesatuan bangsa dan menjadi pelaku pembangunan yang bermanfaat bagi masyarakat dan negara\. Penelitian yang akan digunakan pada makalah ini adalah penelitian yuridis normatif yang bersifat perspektif dengan pendekatan melalui ideologi, undang\-undang, dan fenomena\. Tujuan dari pembuatan makalah ini, yaitu mengetahui sejauh mana pendidikan formal di Indonesia memberikan kontribusi dalam membentuk kesadaran bela negara di kalangan generasi muda, menyelidiki faktor\-faktor yang mempengaruhi pemahaman dan kesadaran bela negara, menganalisis implementasi kurikulum pendidikan nasional, memberikan rekomendasi untuk peningkatan sistem pendidikan\. Manfaat dari Penulis ini Menjaga integritas bangsa Indonesia dalam konteks transformasi digital merupakan sebuah tantangan yang perlu di hadapi\.

## [Анализа утицаја пожара на депонијама на животну средину](../publications/66fc0955b4408760f5bc.md)

Александра Стевановски

The thesis addresses the problem of landfill fires, which represent a significant risk to the environment and human health\. The paper analyzes the causes and mechanisms of landfill fire occurrence, as well as their negative impacts on air, soil, and water\. Special attention is given to modern methods of prevention and management of such fires\. The research includes an overview of innovative technologies for early detection and monitoring, such as temperature and landfill gas monitoring systems, thermal cameras, drones, and digital early warning systems\. The application of these technologies enables timely detection of potential fires and reduces their consequences\. The importance of this research lies in improving landfill management systems and reducing the risk of fire occurrence\.

## [Full\-Curve Five\-Parameter Extraction of a Commercial Photovoltaic Module Using the Single\-Diode Model at Standard Test Conditions](../publications/66fee4805b54599db8a8.md)

Erdem Cüce

Extracting the parameters of photovoltaic \(PV\) modules accurately from the experimental current\-voltage \(I\-V\) curves is important for operating simulation, assessment of energy yield and degradation diagnostics\. This study applies a transparent full\-curve parameter\-extraction method for the single\-diode model \(SDM\) of a commercial crystalline\-silicon PV module under standard test conditions \(STC\)\. The unknown parameters are the light\-generated current Iph, diode reverse saturation current I0, series resistance Rs, shunt resistance Rsh, and modified diode ideality factor a\. Unlike methods based only on short\-circuit, open\-circuit, and maximum\-power points, the adopted procedure minimises the residuals of the implicit SDM equation over 100 measured voltage\-current pairs from short circuit to open circuit\. The extracted model reproduces the measured I\-V and P\-V characteristics with very high accuracy, with a maximum\-power error of only 0\.009% and an R2 value of 0\.99999996\. These results demonstrate the high numerical accuracy of the full\-curve fitting procedure without relying on module\-specific voltage, current, or power values\. The results obtained confirm that it is possible to obtain full\-curve residual fit capable of describing the experimental I\-V and P\-V characteristics with a very high precision\. Simultaneously, the article highlights the importance of understanding the remarkable numerical consistency of the parameter identifiability and measurement resolution concerning cases when the experimental curve is either rounded or approximates the ideal one before reaching the knee point\.

## [Solving multipole challenges in the GW100 benchmark enables precise low\-scaling GW calculations](../publications/670ffad377d13afc0e05.md)

Mia Schambeck; Dorothea Golze; Jan Wilhelm

The GW approximation is a widely used method for computing electron addition and removal energies of molecules and solids\.The computational effort of conventional GW algorithms increases as O\(N 4 \) with the system size N, hindering the application of GW to large and complex systems\.Low\-scaling GW algorithms are currently very actively developed\.Benchmark studies at the single\-shot G 0 W 0 level indicate excellent numerical precision for frontier quasiparticle energies, with mean absolute deviations &lt;10 meV between low\-scaling and standard implementations for the widely used GW100 test set\.A notable challenge for low\-scaling GW algorithms remains in achieving high precision for five molecules within the GW100 test set, namely O 3 , BeO, MgO, BN, and CuCN, for which the deviations are in the range of several hundred meV at the G 0 W 0 level\.This is because of a spurious transfer of spectral weight from the quasiparticle to the satellite spectrum in G 0 W 0 calculations, resulting in multipole features in the self\-energy and spectral function, which low\-scaling algorithms fail to describe\.We show in this paper that including eigenvalue self\-consistency in the Green&\#x27;s function \(evGW 0 \) achieves a proper separation between satellite and quasiparticle peak, leading to a single solution of the quasiparticle equation with spectral weight close to one\.evGW 0 quasiparticles energies from low\-scaling GW closely align with reference calculations; the mean absolute error is only 12 meV for the five molecules\.We thus demonstrate that low\-scaling GW with self\-consistency in G is well suited for computing frontier quasiparticle energies\.

Aelion Kannon
