## [A new image similarity metric for a perceptual and transparent geometric and chromatic assessment](../publications/6726937edd084a627e00.md)

Antonio Di Marino; Vincenzo Bevilacqua; Emanuel Di Nardo; Angelo Ciaramella; Ivanoe De Falco; Giovanna Sannino

Full\-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks\. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements\. We propose EDOKS \(Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity\), a white\-box full\-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel\-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space\. Evaluated on the Berkeley\-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN\-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low\-level full\-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters\. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel\-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance\-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score\.

## [CO 2 Capture in MOFs: Connecting Experiments, Multiscale Simulations, and Data‐Driven Approaches](../publications/672e98610e5baaf2fda8.md)

Prakash Govindaraj; Mullapudi V\. Jyothirmai; Kathirvel Venugopal; Anand Rajkamal; Hern Kim

ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks \(MOFs\) have emerged as promising porous materials for CO 2 capture due to their tunable pore structures and chemically versatile adsorption sites\. However, achieving efficient capture at low CO 2 concentrations while balancing adsorption strength, regeneration, and structural stability remains challenging\. Existing reviews often treat experimental and computational investigations separately, limiting the development of unified design principles\. This review integrates experimental insights with multiscale computational approaches, including density functional theory \(DFT\), grand canonical Monte Carlo, molecular dynamics, and computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\)\. DFT calculations provide molecular‐level understanding of adsorption behavior, highlighting the role of electronic structure at open metal sites and functionalized pores\. Classical simulations predict adsorption capacity, selectivity, and diffusion, while CFD extends these insights to macroscopic transport and process‐level performance, enabling direct comparison with experiments\. In addition, emerging data‐driven approaches are discussed to uncover structure–property relationships and accelerate performance prediction across large materials spaces\. The integration of these methods establishes a closed‐loop framework linking theory, simulation, and experiment, guiding the rational design of efficient and stable porous materials for practical CO 2 capture applications\.

## [Carbon accounting method for industrial sectors at prefectural level: the case of Shanxi Province](../publications/672eb42c2d97a0abda25.md)

Zongyu Li; Guitian Huang

Abstract Accurately quantifying carbon dioxide \(CO₂\) generation from industrial sectors at the prefectural level is both critically important and highly amenable to methodological improvement\. This study develops a systematic, machine learning–enhanced framework for precise sectoral CO₂ generation estimation and robust imputation of missing data\. Utilizing this framework, an extensive carbon accounting analysis is performed for Shanxi Province, a major energy production hub in China, encompassing 30 industrial sectors across its 11 prefectural regions during the years 2007 to 2022\. Furthermore, the resulting dataset is used to characterize the spatial distribution and sectoral heterogeneity of industrial CO₂ generation\. This study advances the existing literature along four dimensions: \(i\) it achieves carbon accounting at a significantly finer spatial and sectoral resolution; \(ii\) it introduces a more sophisticated, algorithm\-driven accounting framework grounded in state\-of\-the\-art machine learning techniques; \(iii\) it incorporates a broader spectrum of energy types and explicitly accounts for sector\-specific variations in carbon emission factors across energy sources; and \(iv\) it implements a rigorous reclassification of industrial sectors alongside nuanced, deflation\-adjusted treatments of monetary indicators to ensure temporal consistency and comparability of industrial carbon dioxide generation estimates over time\.

## [Artificial Intelligence And The Future Of Geography](../publications/67314a9001ccd5949a8a.md)

Geeta; Suresh Awase

ABSTRACT Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly transforming the nature, methods, and applications of geographical research\. The integration of AI with Geographic Information Systems \(GIS\), Remote Sensing, Global Positioning Systems \(GPS\), and geospatial big data has created new opportunities for analyzing complex spatial and temporal processes\. This study examines the evolving relationship between Artificial Intelligence and Geography, with particular emphasis on its applications, transformative potential, limitations, and future possibilities\. The study adopts a descriptive, analytical, and exploratory approach based primarily on secondary data obtained from research articles, academic publications, institutional reports, and relevant scholarly literature\. It examines the application of AI across major geographical domains, including Physical Geography, Human Geography, Urban Geography, and Economic Geography\. The findings indicate that AI enhances geographical research through automated spatial analysis, image classification, predictive modelling, environmental monitoring, disaster prediction, urban planning, and data\-driven decision\-making\. However, challenges related to data quality, algorithmic bias, transparency, privacy, technological dependence, and unequal access to digital infrastructure remain significant\. The study argues that AI should not be viewed as a replacement for geographical expertise but as a complementary technological capability\. The future of Geography is therefore likely to be shaped by human–AI collaboration, integrating computational intelligence with geographical reasoning, field knowledge, contextual understanding, and ethical judgement to address emerging spatial and environmental challenges

## [Response\-function\-conditioned inverse design enables disorder as a design dimension in porous materials](../publications/6731ed0e7e16a6da7d1e.md)

Wei Zhao; Ran Chen; Jiaxiu Zhang; Liangliang Nan; Song Wang; Honghua Chen; Hanyang Yu; Songcan Chen; Mingqiang Wei

Disordered porous materials offer broad mechanical\-response spaces, but their non\-periodic three\-dimensional architectures make inverse design ill\-posed: structurally distinct configurations can produce similar stress\-strain curves, while scalar descriptors such as porosity cannot resolve the underlying topology\. Here, we introduce a response\-function\-conditioned inverse design framework that learns directly from XCT\-derived closed\-cell aluminium\-foam architectures and targets complete nonlinear stress\-strain responses rather than individual properties\. A point\-cloud encoder and forward surrogate establish the structure\-response relation, while conditional generation and gradient\-based refinement search the learned structural space for manufacturable candidates\. Trained on 844 XCT\-derived subvolumes spanning porosities of 0\.4034–0\.8935, the forward model achieves a pointwise R² of 0\.9918 and a median curve\-level NRMSE of 3\.015% on a parent\-specimen\-separated test set\. For targets admitting multiple accepted solutions, inverse\-designed candidates retain a median response NRMSE of 0\.0358 while exhibiting a median pairwise structural distance of 0\.2328, demonstrating non\-trivial one\-to\-many design\. Finite\-element analyses and compression tests on additively manufactured architectures across three aluminium\-alloy systems further confirm physical realizability\. These results establish full\-response conditioning as a practical route for designing real disordered porous materials beyond predefined unit cells\.

## [Forest green\-up in the Pearl River Basin: trends, driving factors, and relationships with net primary productivity](../publications/6734b3661c68d66e7c9d.md)

Shijie Yang; Zhaoju Zheng; Xueming Zhao; Zhipeng Zhang; Xiaohui Cui; Yuan Zeng

The spring green\-up date \(GUD\), a critical indicator of ecosystem response to climate change, profoundly influences terrestrial productivity\. However, the complex drivers of GUD remain elusive, while the contentious relationship between GUD and net primary productivity \(NPP\) challenges the universal validity of the hypothesis that earlier green\-up enhances productivity\. Using MODIS NDVI data \(2000\-2020\), we quantified forest GUD dynamics in the Pearl River Basin and combined random forest, SHAP, and structural equation modelling to identify drivers and assess GUD\-NPP relationships\. GUD was advanced by approximately 5 days, with 81\.8% of forestland pixels advancing and 18\.2% delaying\. Only 5\.39% of advances showed significant trends, whereas 30\.45% of delays were concentrated near croplands and developed areas\. The random forest model explained 58\.2% of GUD variation\. Elevation, precipitation, and soil potassium and phosphorus were dominant; elevation\-induced thermal gradients outweighed ambient temperature effects, with elevations above 1,200 m exhibiting markedly delayed GUD\. Spatially, GUD had a positive correlation with NPP, indicating that later GUD was associated with higher forest NPP, possibly because of early\-spring cold snaps and frost\. Temporally, areas with stronger GUD delays tended to show greater NPP increases\. This study identified key controls on subtropical forest phenology and revealed a GUD\-NPP trade\-off\.

## [Accounting for Fiscal Governance in Risale\-i Felekiyye](../publications/6734e2ccb78d68c46e44.md)

Batuhan Güvemli; Muhsin Aslan; Özgür Muhittin Esen

This research revisits Risale\-i Felekiyye – Kitab\-us Siyakat by applying a comparative analysis of seven sector\-specific accounting forms preserved in Chapter 8: stables, construction, rice cultivation, granaries, mint operations, sheep herding and treasury\. Rather than considering this document a comprehensive archive of Ilkhanid administrative practice, this study treats it as an instructional and practical work providing examples of accounting forms\. Using a standard analytical procedure, it explores who bears responsibility, what resource flow or transformation is recorded, how the accounting record is validated or reconciled, and what kind of accountability results from this\. This comparative analysis has demonstrated that Risale\-i Felekiyye did not require identical formats for the records of all state functions\. Different record formats depended on the physical properties of the resource, the nature of administrative relations, and the point where responsibility became reviewable\. Thus, the record format distinguished animal custody, project inputs, process losses, in\-kind distribution, metal conversion into money, changes in the flock size, and treasury transactions\. The article therefore interprets Risale\-i Felekiyye as evidence of sectoral accountability in fiscal governance\. Some records display paired presentations, residual balances and reconciliation, but they do not establish a unified modern double\-entry system\.

## [KLASIFIKASI TINGKAT PERCERAIAN BERDASARKAN FAKTOR PENYEBAB MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA K\-NEAREST NEIGHBOR \(KNN\)](../publications/67386cd08f7ca4a02495.md)

Agrinda Aulia Lubis; Harmayani

Divorce is a social phenomenon whose rate continues to rise in various regions of Indonesia and has become a shared concern for both the government and society, since it may give rise to social, psychological, and economic consequences for the individuals and families involved\. Divorce is generally caused by several interrelated factors, namely economic problems, continuous domestic disputes, infidelity, and domestic violence \(KDRT\)\. This study aims to apply the K\-Nearest Neighbor \(KNN\) algorithm to classify the level of divorce \(Low, Medium, and High\) based on these four causal factors\. The data used are secondary data obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics \(BPS\) covering ten provinces on Sumatra Island for the 2023\-2025 period\. Prior to classification, the data were normalized using the Min\-Max Normalization method so that every attribute shared a comparable value range\. The dataset was divided into 20 training data \(2023\-2024\) and 10 testing data \(2025\), with the value of K determined using the formula K = √n, resulting in K = 5\. The classification process was carried out by calculating the Euclidean Distance between the testing data and the entire training data, then determining the predicted class through majority voting among the five nearest neighbors\. The classification model was implemented in a web\-based application built with PHP and MySQL that supports dataset import, data normalization, KNN computation, and classification result display\. The test results on the ten testing data for 2025 show that the system achieved an overall accuracy of 70%, with the best performance obtained for the Low class \(recall of 100%\), while the Medium and High classes still experienced misclassification due to the limited amount of training data in those classes\. These results indicate that the KNN algorithm is capable of recognizing divorce patterns based on their causal factors and can be used as a decision\-support tool related to the analysis of divorce rates on Sumatra Island\.

## [Tech Mining with LLMs: Unveiling Trends from Corporate Websites](../publications/67414aa29b953b402959.md)

Xavier Martínez\-Barbero; Ana Pastor\-Merino; Josep Domènech

Abstract Technology mining enables the systematic extraction and analysis of trends regarding scientific and technological developments from diverse Science, Technology, and Innovation \(ST&amp;I\) data sources\. Traditionally, indicators such as patents, surveys, and R&amp;D statistics have been widely used to monitor technological change and innovation\. This study proposes a novel methodology leveraging semantic analysis of corporate website content using large language models \(LLMs\) to facilitate real\-time monitoring of technological developments\. Specifically, we focus on Spanish manufacturing firms that have adopted artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. A pipeline was developed to automatically extract and classify bigrams and unigrams from corporate websites into technological and non\-technological terms, enabling a temporal analysis of technologies for the years 2023 and 2025\. The results indicate an increase in AI\-related mentions, as well as notable patterns of co\-occurrence with Internet of Things \(IoT\) and Industry 4\.0 technologies\. Our study demonstrates the utility of the combination of corporate websites and LLMs as scalable, dynamic, and cost\-effective sources for technology mining, contributing methodologically through advanced text analytics and empirically by providing granular, web\-derived insights into technological dynamics within the manufacturing sector\.

## [Neuroimmune–oligovascular signaling shapes oligodendrocyte precursor cell fate and repair after ischemic stroke](../publications/674cb3a28a156e465b1c.md)

Bin Li; Ruixi Ming; Zijun Wu; Shifeng Pan

BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes neuronal and oligodendroglial injury, axonal and myelin damage, and neurovascular unit dysfunction\. Oligodendrocyte precursor cells \(OPCs\) are lifelong progenitors that generate oligodendrocytes while receiving and transmitting signals within neural, immune, and vascular microenvironments\. This review examines how neuroimmune\-oligovascular communication and intracellular signaling shape OPC survival, recruitment, state transitions, differentiation, and remyelination after ischemic stroke\. MAIN BODY: We first define OPC lineage identity, functional heterogeneity, and signaling interfaces with neurons, microglia/macrophages, astrocytes, endothelial cells, and pericytes\. We then examine how excitotoxic, metabolic, redox, inflammatory, vascular, extracellular\-matrix, and regulated cell\-death signals converge on OPCs across lesion compartments and disease phases\. Severe core ischemia depletes the progenitor pool, whereas partially perfused peri\-infarct tissue permits reactive proliferation and migration\. During the subacute phase, intercellular signals within the post\-ischemic niche influence whether recruited OPCs adopt inflammatory, angiogenic, differentiation\-competent, or arrested states\. Long\-term repair ultimately depends on lineage completion and stable myelin formation rather than OPC accumulation alone\. The strongest causal evidence supports signaling from the surrounding niche as a regulator of OPC differentiation and demonstrates that OPC\-derived myelin repair contributes to neuronal preservation and functional recovery\. By contrast, evidence that endogenous OPCs themselves substantially regulate post\-stroke inflammation, angiogenesis, blood\-brain barrier integrity, or synaptic reconstruction remains less complete and often derives from culture, conditioned\-medium, pharmacological, or transplantation paradigms\. Therapeutic strategies are therefore organized according to the signaling and lineage bottleneck they target, including acute OPC preservation, niche remodeling, lineage completion, oligovascular reconstruction, and cell\-based interventions\. CONCLUSIONS: OPC fate after ischemic stroke is determined by the interaction of cell\-intrinsic signaling competence with temporally and spatially changing neuroimmune\-oligovascular cues\. Translation will require lineage\-resolved causal studies, human spatial and longitudinal validation, signaling\-linked target\-engagement measures, and treatment strategies matched to lesion phase, compartment, and repair bottleneck\. A cell\-communication framework may therefore provide a more mechanistically testable basis for OPC\-centered white\-matter repair after stroke\.

## [Macrophage lipophagy in atherosclerosis: from molecular mechanisms to traditional Chinese medicine interventions](../publications/674d14a7f4af2536e455.md)

Ying Hu; Shuo Yuan; 陈兴娟; Wen Yu; Fang Liu; Xuewei Dong; Mengxuan Cui; Na Zhao; Hua Dong

Macrophage lipophagy, the selective autophagic degradation of intracellular lipid droplets, plays a central role in maintaining lipid homeostasis and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for atherosclerosis \(AS\)\. This review systematically synthesizes the classification, molecular mechanisms, and key signaling networks of macrophage lipophagy\. Moreover, recent evidence on the anti\-AS effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine \(TCM\) mediated by the regulation of macrophage lipophagy has also been summarized and evaluated, including active metabolites, medicinal plants, herbal formulas and commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations\. Despite robust preclinical evidence, challenges remain\. Significant efforts are still required to facilitate clinical translation and offer novel comprehensive strategies for the prevention and management of AS\.

## [Problem management plus with emotional processing module for refugee youth in the Netherlands: pilot trial of feasibility, acceptability and safety](../publications/67516d44b39800ec3cfa.md)

Cansu Alözkan; Pim J\. Cuijpers; Ellenor Mittendorfer‐Rutz; Aemal Akhtar; Richard Allan Bryant; Katie S Dawson; Michael Matewos Abraham; Jolnar Makhous; Zainab Safar; Sonya Vasylieva; Ilse L\. Verhagen; Marit Sijbrandij

Background Refugee youth are at elevated risk for post\-traumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\) and other mental health disorders, yet systemic and cultural barriers limit access to care\. Scalable, transdiagnostic interventions such as Problem Management Plus \(PM\+\) are promising, but their impact on trauma symptoms is modest\. Incorporating brief trauma\-focused components may enhance effectiveness\. Aims To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of PM\+ with an emotional processing module \(PM\+EP\) for refugee youth aged 16–25 years in the Netherlands\. Method Refugee youth with elevated psychological distress \(K10 &gt; 15\) and impaired functioning \(World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2\.0 \(WHODAS 2\.0\) &gt; 16\) were randomised into PM\+EP, PM\+ with supportive counselling \(PM\+SC\), or care as usual \(CAU\)\. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via recruitment, adherence, fidelity and qualitative interviews\. Psychological distress, PTSD symptoms, functioning and self\-identified problems were measured at baseline, post\-intervention and follow\-up\. Registered in Overview of Medical Research in the Netherlands \(OMON; Trial ID: NL\-OMON56254\)\. Results Fifty\-two participants were randomised \(PM\+EP: n = 17; PM\+SC: n = 19; CAU: n = 16\)\. Attendance and fidelity were high, and PM\+ interventions were rated as acceptable and culturally appropriate\. No significant between\-group differences were observed in the primary analyses\. Exploratory analyses suggested greater short\-term symptom reduction for probable depression in PM\+EP versus CAU \( b = –0\.79, s\.e\. = 0\.38, p = 0\.04\)\. Effect size estimates ranged from small to large across outcomes \(Hedges’ g = –0\.98 to 0\.19\)\. Conclusions PM\+ is feasible, acceptable and safe for refugee youth aged 16 years and older\. The potential added value of the EP module remains unclear and warrants further investigation\. Trial Registration Number The trial was registered in the Dutch clinical trial registration: Overview of Medical Research in the Netherlands \(OMON\) \(Trial ID: NL\-OMON56254; https://onderzoekmetmensen\.nl/en/trial/56254 \)\.

## [Mind the gaps\! exploring the relationship between hierarchy and creative cognitive climate](../publications/67623520b3b26350e744.md)

Scott G\. Isaksen; Eric Arne Lofquist; Soli Pupal

The role of hierarchy in organizations is under attack, particularly from those focused on organizational creativity and the digital transformation \(DT\)\. The call for flatter structures, reduced bureaucracy and network organizations, with the appropriate dispersion of authority, responsibility and power to achieve high levels of employee engagement, is the current rage\. However, according to Elliot Jaques \(1990\), hierarchy itself is not to blame for our problems\. He argued that we need an improved understanding of both hierarchy and human nature\. The aim of hierarchy should be the improved deployment of human talent and energy\. Despite attempts to reduce hierarchy in modern organizations, formal and informal hierarchies persist, in fact, even thrive in today’s DT environment\. We investigated the relationship between creative cognitive climate at three levels of hierarchy: leaders, managers and staff\. Exploring creative cognitive climate allowed for examining a deeper level of diversity\. Using an assessment of these style differences across multiple industries and organizations, we found distinct gaps in collective style preferences across the three levels of stratification\. Those at higher levels tended to prefer more novelty and less detailed structure and concern for authority\. Those as lower levels tended to prefer novelty that fits the system and more structure and access to authority in dealing with their tasks\. Based on these gaps, we identified four general and interrelated implications for improving communication, coordination, and collaboration across and within levels of various kinds of hierarchy\.

## [Learning Disaster Journalism in a Media Anthropology Classroom](../publications/67680cc67dbb0fdd1deb.md)

Lia Lola V\. Kotnik; Karmen Medica

Disaster journalism has not been institutionally or curricularly established within Slovenian higher education\. This article examines how disaster journalism can be taught in a media anthropology classroom through a case study of an experimental pedagogical intervention carried out in 2024–2025 in a master’s\-level Media Anthropology course at a Slovenian public university\. Implemented in a non\-journalism communication and media programme, the intervention introduced disaster journalism as a temporary analytical framework through two seminar\-based assignments: the reading of peer\-reviewed scholarship and qualitative case studies of media coverage of floods, bushfires, technological disasters, war, pandemic, and school shootings\. The article is based on a qualitative interpretive synthesis of student seminar papers, class presentations, and reflective discussions rather than on a formal assessment of learning outcomes\. The findings show that students engaged scholarly literature mainly through preferential readings, while the greatest conceptual challenges emerged in relation to Bourdieu’s journalistic field theory and the translation of disaster journalism terminology into Slovenian\. In their empirical analyses, however, students applied the framework more critically and identified recurring patterns such as humanitarian normalisation, routinisation of crisis coverage, politicisation, and ethical tensions in victim representation\. The article argues that disaster journalism can serve as a productive interdisciplinary framework for developing media literacy, ethical sensitivity, structural reflexivity, and critical engagement among students who are not journalism trainees\. Overall, the intervention suggests that experimental pedagogy may provide a viable pathway for institutionalising disaster journalism in academic environments where it currently lacks curricular status\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA EDUCAÇÃO SUPERIOR: IMPACTOS NAS METODOLOGIAS DE ENSINO E NA FORMAÇÃO CONTINUADA DE DOCENTES](../publications/67724971fe0cd48815df.md)

Sandra Regina Vieira; Alexandra Hubner da Silva; Adriana Alves Lima Magri; Andrea Gomes Nunes Caetano; Daiana Longo Modolon

O estudo analisou os impactos da IA nas metodologias de ensino e na formação continuada de docentes da educação superior, considerando as transformações provocadas pela incorporação de ferramentas inteligentes às práticas pedagógicas\. A pesquisa foi orientada pela seguinte questão: de que maneira a utilização da IA na educação superior impactou as metodologias de ensino e as demandas de formação continuada dos docentes? O objetivo geral consistiu em analisar esses impactos no contexto universitário\. Especificamente, buscou\-se identificar as principais mudanças nas práticas e metodologias de ensino decorrentes da utilização da IA e analisar as competências e necessidades formativas dos docentes diante de sua integração às práticas pedagógicas\. Metodologicamente, o estudo caracterizou\-se como uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa, fundamentada em Santana e Narciso \(2025\)\. Foram selecionadas produções científicas recentes e pertinentes ao tema, submetidas à leitura analítica e comparativa\. Os resultados evidenciaram mudanças relacionadas à personalização da aprendizagem, à avaliação, ao acompanhamento do desempenho, à produção de conteúdos e à mediação pedagógica\. Também se constatou que a integração responsável da IA exigiu competências digitais, pedagógicas, analíticas e éticas, ultrapassando o domínio operacional das ferramentas\. Concluiu\-se que a incorporação da IA apresentou potencial para qualificar o ensino superior, desde que permanecesse vinculada à intencionalidade pedagógica, à mediação docente e a processos permanentes de formação continuada\.

## [Developing smart learning environments in general education schools: A conceptual framework for digital transformation](../publications/67752147a11ba0766e25.md)

Đinh Thị Hải

Digital transformation has created new opportunities for improving teaching, learning, and educational management through the development of smart learning environments\. However, the effective integration of digital technologies into general education requires a comprehensive approach that connects technological infrastructure, pedagogical innovation, data driven management, and institutional capacity\. This study aims to examine the theoretical foundations of smart learning environments and propose a conceptual framework for their development in general education schools\. Using a qualitative research approach based on literature review and conceptual analysis, the study synthesizes international perspectives on smart education, digital transformation, and technology enhanced learning\. The findings identify five interconnected components of smart learning environments: digital infrastructure and learning resources, smart pedagogical practices, learner centered support, educational data and assessment, and institutional governance and teacher capacity\. Based on these components, an integrated conceptual framework is proposed to guide the development and implementation of smart learning environments in primary and secondary education\. The study further discusses implementation strategies, institutional requirements, and implications for Vietnamese general education schools\. The proposed framework provides a theoretical foundation for aligning digital transformation initiatives with educational objectives, emphasizing that technological innovation should support meaningful learning experiences, educational equity, and sustainable school development\.

## [“Morphological, Functional, and Molecular Progression of Blood\-Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Alzheimer’s Disease”](../publications/677df15281ede3f79a5a.md)

Karen León‐Arcia; Humberto Martínez\-Orozco; M\. Crespo; Sofía Y\. Díaz\-Cintra; Luis Oskar Soto\-Rojas

Blood\-brain barrier \(BBB\) dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an early pathological event in sporadic Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\), which represents over 95% of cases\. Vascular risk factors and cerebral insulin resistance are considered potential contributors to its initiation\. This review synthesizes evidence available through March 2026 on the temporal progression of morphological, functional, and molecular BBB alterations in AD patients and experimental models\. This review emphasizes the proposed role of BBB disruption in perpetuating neurodegeneration through feedback loops involving pericyte damage, hypoxia, perivascular inflammation, and dysregulation of amyloid\-β transport systems\. By integrating data from neuroimaging, fluid biomarkers, and post\-mortem studies, available evidence suggests that BBB alterations can be detected from preclinical stages, most consistently in the hippocampus, and may exhibit sex\-specific differences\. The review compares findings from familial transgenic models with the more limited characterization available in sporadic AD models \(notably the intracerebroventricular streptozotocin model\), and highlights key knowledge gaps regarding temporal dynamics\. This synthesis supports further exploration of strategies to preserve BBB integrity\. An integrated vascular approach may usefully complement current amyloid\- and tau\-centered therapies, particularly in sporadic AD\.

## [Dietary frequency, body satisfaction, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among offspring of healthcare workers in China](../publications/67872e8eaee4738f49df.md)

Tingke Xu; Rongxiu Ding; Chao Lin; Qiuhua Zhang; Pan Ding

Background Dietary behaviors may be associated with body image and emotional health in young people, but evidence integrating these outcomes in Chinese populations remains limited\. This study examined associations of dietary frequency with body satisfaction, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms\. Methods This cross\-sectional study included 584 offspring of healthcare workers aged 10–24 years in Zhejiang, China\. A 10\-item food\-frequency questionnaire generated a frequency\-based score reflecting more frequent consumption of meat, fish, vegetables, fruit, eggs, soy products, and dairy products and less frequent consumption of pickled, sugary, and fried foods\. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were used to assess associations and dose–response patterns\. Counterfactual mediation analysis estimated indirect associations through body satisfaction\. Results The proportions screening positive for anxiety and depressive symptoms were 23\.1 and 33\.6%, respectively\. In fully adjusted models, higher dietary frequency scores were associated with higher odds of body satisfaction \(OR = 1\.21, 95% CI: 1\.02–1\.44\) and lower odds of anxiety \(OR = 0\.65, 95% CI: 0\.52–0\.79\) and depressive symptoms \(OR = 0\.84, 95% CI: 0\.70–0\.99\)\. Restricted cubic spline analyses indicated approximately linear associations, with no evidence of nonlinearity\. For each 1\-SD increase in the dietary frequency score, indirect associations through higher body satisfaction were observed for anxiety \(OR = 0\.97, 95% CI: 0\.93–0\.99; 6\.8%\) and depressive symptoms \(OR = 0\.96, 95% CI: 0\.92–0\.99; 17\.3%\)\. Conclusion Higher dietary frequency scores were associated with greater body satisfaction and lower odds of anxiety and depressive symptoms among healthcare workers’ offspring\. These findings cannot be generalized to other young people in China\.

## [Machine learning\-based detection and area quantification of mechanical and corrosion damage in femoral stem tapers](../publications/67a50ba851ed858beb27.md)

Lochan Upadhayay; Amit Kumar Bandyopadhyay

Corrosion and mechanical damage at modular femoral taper junctions remain important degradation mechanisms in total hip arthroplasty\. Yet, their assessment commonly relies on ordinal visual scoring methods that reduce spatially heterogeneous damage to a single severity grade\. Here, we present a SegFormer\-based semantic segmentation framework for pixel\-level identification and quantitative assessment of tribocorrosion damage on Ti6Al4V tapered shafts following controlled hip simulator testing\. We manually annotated a dataset of 576 high\-resolution scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\) images into background, corrosion, and mechanical damage classes, using representative SEM and energy\-dispersive X\-ray spectroscopy analyses and literature for damage feature identification\. The model was trained using a hybrid weighted cross\-entropy and Dice loss, and a structured three\-stage hyperparameter optimization strategy\. Five independently seeded models were subsequently combined for ensemble inference to improve full\-field damage quantification and assess seed\-dependent prediction variability\. On the independent test set, the final model achieved IoU values of 0\.678 for corrosion and 0\.496 for mechanical damage, with an overall pixel accuracy of 0\.947\. As a proof\-of\-concept application, the developed framework was applied to two representative taper cases, consisting of Ti6Al4V shafts coupled with either Ti6Al4V or CoCrMo femoral heads, to demonstrate full\-field damage quantification\. Ensemble analysis showed that the representative Ti6Al4V/CoCrMo case exhibited a greater corrosion area and more spatially concentrated corrosion than the Ti6Al4V/Ti6Al4V case\. Region\-size analysis further revealed that larger localized regions contributed substantially to the total corrosion area, including a single 0\.50 to 1\.00 mm 2 region accounting for approximately 23\.6% of the corrosion area in the Ti6Al4V/CoCrMo case\. Once trained, the framework enables rapid full\-surface damage prediction and quantitative analysis, substantially reducing the manual effort required for large SEM datasets\. Overall, the framework provides spatially resolved quantification of damage extent, distribution, and region size beyond conventional ordinal scoring\.

## [Novel assay for accelerated anaerobic phenotypic susceptibility testing for Clostridioides difficile](../publications/67ac43dd47ba341d6f7c.md)

Meriem Boukili; Omar Zmerli; Sara Bellali; Saidi Daoud; Rita Abou Abdallah; Florence Fenollar; Jacques  Yaacoub Bou Khalil

Introduction Clostridioides difficile infection \(CDI\) remains one of the leading healthcare\-associated infections\. CDI management is increasingly complicated due to rising antimicrobial resistance, variability in treatment response, and the lack of standardized antimicrobial susceptibility testing \(AST\) in routine practice\. The current reference method, agar dilution, is laborious and time\-consuming, leaving therapy largely empirical\. Methods We present the development and proof\-of\-concept for a novel accelerated AST assay for C\. difficile using tabletop scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\)\. Following confirmation of C\. difficile growth in liquid medium, a broth microdilution\-based AST protocol was established and evaluated using SEM imaging at early time points\. Susceptibility to fidaxomicin and vancomycin was assessed for eight isolates with different toxigenic profiles\. Results Analysis of SEM images enabled the detection and quantification of antibiotic effects, including bacterial growth inhibition, reduced bacterial viability, and pronounced morphological alteration as early as three hours following exposure\. This facilitated the determination of SEM\-based minimum inhibitory concentration \(SEM\-MIC\) ranges, which concorded with MICs determined using standard agar dilution\. Conclusion The SEM\-AST assay achieved a substantial reduction in turnaround time from 48 hours to approximately 7 hours, without compromising accuracy\. These results demonstrate that combining optimized culture conditions with SEM imaging at early time points allows for rapid and reliable MIC estimation, establishing the first SEM\-based AST approach for strict anaerobes and providing promising potential for future CDI diagnostics\.

## [Optimization of Bandpass Filters for Modern Communication Systems: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm\-Machine Learning Framework with Fractal Defected Ground Structures](../publications/67ad2fc878553003d205.md)

Ashikur Mollik, Md Nadim Hosain, Md Imran Hossain

Bandpass filters set the achievable selectivity and the noise floor of practically every radio front end, yet the design cycle for millimetre\-wave and multi\-band devices is still dominated by repeated full\-wave simulation\. This paper reports a synthesis and optimization framework that couples a genetic algorithm to a convolutional surrogate model, and applies it to three realizations: a 28 GHz substrate\-integrated waveguide filter for 5G base stations, a 2\.4 GHz miniaturized microstrip filter for battery\-powered IoT nodes, and a Ka\-band cavity filter for satellite payloads\. The surrogate is trained on 5000 previously simulated geometries spanning 1\-100 GHz and screens an entire candidate population in under one hour, roughly twelve times faster than direct electromagnetic evaluation; only the top decile is passed to full\-wave verification, and the surrogate is retrained on the augmented archive at every cycle\. Convergence is reached in five cycles instead of fifteen, which cuts wall\-clock optimization time from 72 h to 12 h and lowers the average passband insertion loss of the converged population from 2\.1 dB to 1\.8 dB\. A dual\-band variant built on Hilbert\-curve defected ground structures occupies 15 mm × 10 mm, about 70 % smaller than comparable published designs, and suppresses the third harmonic at 4\.8 GHz by 12 dB relative to hairpin and interdigital references\. Measured insertion loss for the 28 GHz prototype is 2\.1 dB against 1\.8 dB simulated, a 0\.3 dB gap consistent with the surface roughness of the fabricated copper\. The obstacles that remain are the cost of low\-loss laminate in volume IoT production and the scarcity of training data above 100 GHz, both of which limit how far the method extends towards terahertz designs\.

## [IMPROVING METHODS FOR OPTIMIZING THE HYDRAULIC REGIMES OF URBAN WATER DISTRIBUTION NETWORKS BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MATHEMATICAL MODELING](../publications/67adf76dc45eb9f6fd32.md)

SHERZOD AKROM UGLI KHUDAYNAZAROV

This article reviews scientific approaches to mathematical modeling and artificial intelligence\-based optimization of hydraulic regimes in urban water distribution networks\. It considers uneven pressure distribution, hydraulic losses, water leakage, and energy consumption\. Traditional hydraulic models, evolutionary optimization, machine learning, and digital twins are compared\. The review proposes a conceptual hybrid framework combining physics\-based simulation, sensor data, demand forecasting, and multi\-objective optimization\. The framework is presented as a research direction rather than an experimentally validated solution

## [Beyond seizures: the hidden burden of developmental epileptic encephalopathies](../publications/67af70cf08a72463c133.md)

Giovanni Battista Dell’Isola; Michele Sorrentino; Sara Massara; Gianluca Dini; Vincenzo Salpietro; Pietro Ferrara; Pasquale STRIANO; Federico Vigevano; Alberto Verrotti

Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies \(DEEs\) are a group of severe childhood\-onset disorders characterized by drug\-resistant epilepsy and a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental, behavioral, psychiatric, and systemic manifestations\. Although seizure control has traditionally been the primary therapeutic goal, growing evidence indicates that non\-seizure manifestations often represent the main determinants of long\-term disability, quality of life, and caregiver burden\. This review highlights the hidden burden of DEEs by focusing on three paradigmatic syndromes: Lennox–Gastaut syndrome \(LGS\), Dravet syndrome \(DS\), and tuberous sclerosis complex \(TSC\)\. DS and LGS represent prototypical DEEs, whereas TSC is a multisystem genetic disorder that is frequently, although not invariably, associated with early\-onset drug\-resistant epilepsy and DEE\-like neurodevelopmental trajectories\. Across these conditions, the severity and progression of clinical manifestations are influenced by complex interactions between genetic, structural, developmental, and epileptic mechanisms, supporting the concept that epilepsy and associated manifestations represent interconnected features of a broader neurodevelopmental disorder\. The review also emphasizes the substantial psychosocial, physical, and economic burden experienced by families and caregivers, which often exceeds the impact of seizures alone\. Current management strategies should therefore extend beyond seizure reduction and adopt a multidisciplinary, life\-course approach integrating early genetic diagnosis, syndrome\-specific surveillance, developmental interventions, rehabilitation, behavioral support, and coordinated multidisciplinary care\. Future research should prioritize disease\-modifying therapies and personalized strategies aimed at addressing both epileptic and non\-epileptic manifestations, ultimately improving functional outcomes and quality of life for individuals with DEEs and their families\.

## [Monolithic fabrication of 1S1R cross\-point device using single GexTe1\-x material by controlling composition between memory and threshold switching](../publications/67b45b088b503a0df3a2.md)

Young\-Min Kim; Sangheon Park; 이지혜; Sangyeop Kim; Siwon Park; Jong‐Souk Yeo

Abstract Three\-dimensional \(3D\) integrated one\-selector one\-resistor \(1S1R\) cross\-point arrays are emerging as a leading next\-generation memory technology\. Achieving both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching within a single material system offers tremendous potential for simplifying fabrication\. This study demonstrates that the memory and threshold switching behavior of germanium\-telluride \(Ge x Te 1\-x \) devices can be precisely tuned by controlling their atomic ratio\. In the Te\-deficient Ge x Te 1\-x system, the device exhibits nonvolatile memory switching with fast operating speed\. Conversely, the Te\-rich system functions as an excellent bidirectional selector for high\-density memory applications, exhibiting high selectivity \(&gt; 10 4 \) and a short delay time \(&lt; 55 ns\)\. Material analyses using X\-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy reveal that these distinct electrical behaviors are driven by composition\-dependent changes in the atomic structure\. Furthermore, the fully integrated 1S1R stack demonstrates robust SET/RESET switching characteristics, maintaining a stable memory window of 0\.2 V and an on/off current ratio exceeding two orders of magnitude \(\~ 1\.12 × 10 2 \)\. Notably, this integrated configuration provides superior operational reliability and enhanced endurance \(\~ 8 × 10 6 cycles\) compared to standalone phase\-change memory devices\. By elucidating these underlying mechanisms, this work reduces the fabrication complexity of stackable devices and opens up wide\-ranging applications for unified memory and selector systems\.

## [The Reflection Penalty: when managers accept leadership coaching from a human but not an AI agent](../publications/67c0111e14a3572ed133.md)

Tessa Forshaw; Jacob Hale; Mari Longmire

Leadership coaching develops managers but is expensive and difficult to scale\. AI may be able to help scale access, but “answering machine” like AI coaching agents invite cognitive offloading and weaken learning\. We instantiated a human coaching protocol, supported across prior cycles, as a text\-based AI coach built to prompt reflective questioning\. In the fourth cycle of a design\-based research program at a global consulting firm, eight managers received the same protocol from a human coach and the AI coach, applied each session in an observed onboarding activity, and reflected on both in interviews\. All eight welcomed the probing questions and preferred the human coach\. Notably, they resisted the same protocol of questioning from the AI coach and wanted answers from it instead\. This study’s theoretical contribution is the Reflection Penalty, the cost an AI coach pays for asking a user to do the reflective work that makes human coaching effective\. Its practical contribution is a jobs\-to\-be\-done map for AI coaching, assembled from proposals participants raised on their own\. It divides coaching into distinct jobs and assigns each to the human or the AI best suited to it\. Both contributions are offered to those designing AI tools that aim to support reflection

## [Integrated machine learning, pharmacophore screening, and structure\-based computational approaches for the identification of novel JAK3 inhibitors](../publications/67c58773f820cb59542e.md)

Muhammad Yasir; Jinyoung Park; Eun‐Taek Han; Won Sun Park; Jin\-Hee Han; Jongseon Choe; Wanjoo Chun

AIM: Janus kinase 3 \(JAK3\) is a key therapeutic target in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases\. This study aimed to identify novel JAK3 inhibitors using an integrated machine learning and structure\-based computational approach\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Random Forest Regression model was developed from 4,336 JAK3 inhibitors using molecular descriptors and Morgan fingerprints, then applied to screen 4\.6 million Enamine library compounds\. Top hits underwent pharmacophore screening, molecular docking, triplicate molecular dynamics simulations, and MM\-PBSA binding free energy calculations\. RESULTS: estimation\. Docking analysis further prioritized the lead compounds, and MD simulation triplicates confirmed stable binding of prioritized compounds within the JAK3 active site, with persistent interactions involving hinge residues Glu903 and Leu905, and charge residues Cys909, Arg911, and Arg953\. Lead compounds \(Z2953646389, Z2235801948, and Z56791230\) were stabilized by Coulombic and van der Waals interactions, exhibiting more favorable MM\-PBSA ΔG values than the reference inhibitor ritlecitinib\. CONCLUSION: Integrating machine learning with structure\-based computational approaches provides an efficient strategy for JAK3 inhibitor discovery\. The identified leads show strong predicted potency and favorable binding profiles, warranting further experimental validation\.

## [Longitudinal peripheral DNA methylation remodeling following ketamine\-assisted psychotherapy in major depressive disorder](../publications/67ca6e5ff8725f2f7afe.md)

Arghavan Nepton; Sonya C\. Faber; Zachary A\. Kaminsky; Mario Nucci; Hesam Farahani; Monnica T\. Williams; Sergio Pérez Rosal

Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects, but the molecular processes associated with their persistence remain poorly defined in humans\. We examined longitudinal DNA methylation changes in 10 adults with major depressive disorder undergoing ketamine\-assisted psychotherapy using two pre\-treatment assessments \(T1, T2\) and one post\-treatment assessment \(T3\)\. Participants received three sessions of intranasal racemic ketamine within a structured psychotherapy protocol\. Buccal DNA methylation was measured using the Illumina MethylationEPIC v2\.0 BeadChip\. Depressive symptoms improved markedly following treatment, with mean Beck Depression Inventory–II scores declining from the severe to the mild range \(p &lt; \.001\)\. Of 802,595 CpG loci evaluated, 20,770 met the nominal T3\-versus\-T2 screening criterion\. Sequential filtering for methylation\-change magnitude and movement relative to pre\-treatment fluctuation identified 962 retained CpG loci, including 517 retained gene\-annotated loci\. A supplementary linear mixed\-effects analysis modeled repeated measurements within participants across the 603 preselected gene\-annotated magnitude\-filtered loci; because these loci were selected using the same contrast and cohort, this analysis was not treated as independent confirmation\. Exploratory enrichment analysis of this 603\-locus set identified NOTCH1\-related Reactome terms driven by NOTCH1, DLL1, and ADAM17\. Within the retained signature, multiple core and adjacent Notch\-related components formed a coherent signaling module spanning ligand, receptor processing, transcriptional regulation, and pathway cross\-talk\. These findings identify a structured peripheral methylation signature associated with ketamine\-assisted psychotherapy\. They do not establish brain\-specific pathway activation or causality, but provide a longitudinal basis for investigating regulatory adaptations accompanying clinical improvement\.

## [الحوكمة المهنية للممارسات الإدارية: اختبار الاستحقاق التنظيمي المهني المتناسب مع المخاطر](../publications/67cc6dff69cd7ed48e19.md)

Mohammad Saad Abuhaimed

الهدف: تطوير اختبار معياري مفاهيمي يحدد متى تبرر الممارسات الإدارية ذات الأثر العام تدخلًا مهنيًا ملزمًا، وأين يقع التنظيم، وما الأداة الأقل تقييدًا القادرة على خفض الضرر، مع فحص قابلية التنظيم للمراجعة والتخفيف عبر التحول السعودي في تنظيم الاستشارات الإدارية للأفراد\.‏المنهجية: اعتمدت الدراسة تركيبًا مفاهيميًا وتحليلًا وثائقيًا موجهًا للأدبيات والنماذج المهنية والوثائق التنظيمية\.‏ ورُمزت المواد وفق الضرر وإسناده، وفشل التحقق أو المساءلة وصعوبة التراجع، والبدائل، والمنافسة، والشرعية، وسلطة الإلزام، ومحل التنظيم\.‏ واستُخدمت حالات قصدية متفاوتة النضج لاختبار الحدود والتفسيرات المنافسة، دون ادعاء مراجعة منهجية أو أثر سببي\.‏النتائج: أسفرت الدراسة عن اختبار الاستحقاق التنظيمي المهني \(PRJT\) المكوّن من ست بوابات: خمس موضوعية تفحص مبرر التدخل، هي تعريف الممارسة؛ والضرر القابل للإسناد؛ وفشل التحقق أو المساءلة وصعوبة التراجع؛ وقصور البدائل الأخف؛ وصافي المنفعة والمنافسة؛ تليها سادسة تفحص القابلية المؤسسية والمراجعة والانقضاء\.‏ ويُطرح سؤال محل التنظيم عند كل بوابة لا مرة واحدة في نهايتها\.‏ وتبين الحالة السعودية أن نقل الاختصاص خفف آلية الإصدار مع استمرار الاعتراف بالممارسة، ولم يظهر التدرج المهني في مسار الإصدار المعاين\.‏ وتدعم النتيجة حوكمة موزعة، مع بقاء المرجعية الجامعة خيارًا مشروطًا بثبوت وظائف غير مؤداة وضرر متبقٍ\.‏الأصالة/ الإضافة: تعيد الدراسة بناء وحدة القرار حول ممارسة محددة وخطر قابل للإسناد، وتستخدم بوابات غير تعويضية، وتفصل محل التنظيم عن شدة الأداة، وتدمج المراجعة والانقضاء في مبرر استمرار القيد\.‏ وبذلك يمنع الاختبارُ القفزة من أهمية الإدارة إلى ترخيص الأشخاص، وقد ينتهي بعدم التدخل أو بتنظيم المنشأة أو العقد أو القرار، أو بمرجعية جامعة إذا ثبتت ضرورتها ومنفعتها الصافية\.

## [Late enhancement and washout maps for distinguishing tumor progression from radiation necrosis in malignant brain tumors: an exploratory study](../publications/67d0030dfd90845ba773.md)

Eya Khadhraoui; Leon Schmidt; Stefan Klebingat; I Erol Sandalcioglu; Roland Schwab; Philipp Arndt; Daniel Behme; Klaus\-Peter Stein; Sebastian Johannes Müller

BACKGROUND: Distinguishing between tumor progression and radiation necrosis during brain tumor follow\-up is challenging\. Advanced MR imaging techniques, such as perfusion, diffusion\-weighted imaging \(DWI\), and spectroscopy, can help differentiate between these conditions\. In our clinic, we established a novel technique, the rapid washout and late\-enhancement map\. This study investigated the value of this map in distinguishing true progression from radiation necrosis\. METHODS: Patients with a histologically confirmed initial diagnosis of glioblastoma, high\-grade astrocytoma, primary central nervous system lymphoma, or brain metastasis who were undergoing radiochemotherapy and participated in our MRI protocol, including MR perfusion and rapid washout imaging, between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, were included in the study\. We volumetrically measured late enhancement and washout in brain tumors at all follow\-up examinations and analyzed the resulting volumes\. Additionally, we evaluated diffusion\-weighted imaging and MR perfusion images\. RESULTS: A total of 33 patients \(25 with glioblastoma, two with astrocytoma grade 4, two with astrocytoma grade 3, one with CNS lymphoma, and three with brain metastasis\) were included\. Diagnostic confirmation was obtained by histopathological assessment in 20 patients, MRI follow\-up in 13 patients, with additional fluorodeoxyglucose\-positron emission tomography in two\. Among these patients, 23 were diagnosed with tumor recurrence, four with mixed pathology comprising &quot;radiation necrosis with scattered active tumor cells&quot;, and six with radiation necrosis\. The mean washout ratio \(± standard deviation\) was 31 ± 18 % for progressive disease, 35 ± 20 % for mixed pathology, and 10 ± 7 % for radiation necrosis, respectively\. CONCLUSIONS: The washout ratio can enhance the differentiation between recurrent tumor growth and radiation necrosis during post\-treatment monitoring of malignant brain tumors\. As MR perfusion can yield inconclusive results in this setting, the proposed method offers complementary information that supports initial diagnostic decision making\. Diagnostic discrimination may be strengthened by combining the relative cerebral blood volume with washout ratio analysis, rather than relying on a single imaging marker\.

## [Co\-GRFuzz: Shared\-Corpus Cooperative Fuzzing for Python Libraries](../publications/67d2ca3effd03c91138c.md)

Anh Le Minh Viet; Hiệu Nguyễn Huy; Thang Hoang Nam; Hai Anh Tran; Truong Tran Xuan

Parallel fuzzing can exchange successful inputs, but the behavior of different Python mutation strategies under a shared corpus is not well characterized\. We evaluate four Pythonfuzz\-anchored two\-worker configurations\-PP, PD, PO, and PG\-on five Python libraries and compare them with isolated single\-process references under one common sys\.settrace\-based line\-transition coverage representation\. The observed outcomes are target\-dependent and do not favor GRPO as a cooperative partner\. On python\-dateutil, PD and PO each reach a global union of 3407 edges, whereas PG reaches 2913 despite similar local coverage of the learning\-guided worker\. On cryptography, PD and PO reach a 47\-edge union while PG shows no union gain\. A provenance\-enabled PG run records 106 global\-first discoveries whose direct parent was produced by the peer worker, documenting within\-run seed reuse without establishing a causal benefit of sharing\. Each configuration is represented by one six\-hour campaign; the reported values are therefore individual campaign observations rather than statistical comparisons\. Two previously undocumented exceptions are also reported as qualitative bug\-finding evidence\.

## [Unintended Environmental Consequences of Government Subsidies: Evidence from Chinese Industrial Firms](../publications/67faab104a481c12b553.md)

Bing Xiang; Xu Cheng; Xiaoyun Shang; Lili Guo

Government subsidies can alleviate firms’ financing constraints and facilitate production expansion, but they may also increase pollution emissions\. Their environmental consequences depend on the relative effects of production expansion and improvements in environmental efficiency\. By matching data from the China Environmental Statistics Database and the China Industrial Enterprise Database, this study examines the relationship between government subsidies and firm\-level pollution emissions using firm fixed effects and multidimensional interacted fixed effects\. The results reveal a significant positive association between government subsidies and firms’ chemical oxygen demand \(COD\) emissions\. This finding remains robust to alternative pollution measures, entropy balancing, double machine learning, and instrumental variable estimation\. An examination of firms’ responses shows that government subsidies are associated with higher industrial output, greater resource consumption, and increased wastewater discharge\. At the same time, subsidies are associated with lower industrial water use and wastewater discharge per unit of output, as well as higher COD removal rates, suggesting that production expansion and improvements in environmental efficiency may occur simultaneously\. Further analysis reveals a significant convex nonlinear relationship between government subsidies and pollution emissions\. Firms’ information technology infrastructure weakens the positive relationship, whereas a larger existing capital stock strengthens it\. These findings suggest that improvements in resource\-use efficiency and pollution abatement may be insufficient to offset the additional emissions associated with production expansion\. They highlight a potential trade\-off between promoting firm production and controlling pollution through fiscal support, providing firm\-level evidence to inform assessments of the environmental consequences of general government subsidies and the design of subsidy policies\.

## [Exploring Potential Psychological, Behavioral, and Physiological Predictors of Human Flourishing in Division 1 Athletes: Toward a More Comprehensive Mental Health Screening](../publications/680733885976c98ebe24.md)

Derek Aaron Wheeler

The National Collegiate Athletic Association \(NCAA\) has created numerous task forces and guidelines to address the rise in mental health challenges faced by student\-athletes\. However, these efforts have largely focused on identifying psychopathology rather than promoting flourishing\. The purpose of this study was to examine the predictive utility of self\-report and objective measures of human flourishing among NCAA Division I student\-athletes at initial screening \(i\.e\., preparticipation exam\)\. This retrospective, cross\-sectional, correlational study analyzed archival data from 92 student\-athletes from 13 different sports\. Measures included the Secure Flourishing Index \(SFI\), Patient Health Questionnaire\-9 \(PHQ\-9\), Athlete Sleep Behavior Questionnaire \(ASBQ\), and Power Points, an objective measure of Heart coherence\. Simple linear regression showed that Power Points significantly predicted SFI scores, explaining 4\.8% of the variance \(R² = \.048, p = \.037\)\. Multiple linear regression examined PHQ\-9, ASBQ, Power Points, sport type, and gender as predictors of SFI scores\. The model was significant and explained 29\.4% of the variance \(R² = \.294, p &lt; \.001\)\. Depression was the only significant individual predictor \(B = −\.124, p &lt; \.001\)\. The implications for these results are 1\) objective measures should continue to be researched for their predictive utility of human flourishing at initial screening and 2\) all universities should at a minimum use the PHQ\-9 to assess depression\. Finally, this study suggests using the SFI and an objective physiological marker as an adjunct to the initial health screening may provide a more comprehensive, data\-driven, strength\-based screening model that could potentially enhance early identification and intervention among elite student\-athletes\.

## [The Intersection of AI and Emotional Intelligence in Leadership: Augmenting Human\-Centered Decision\-Making](../publications/6810bffe35242d37949c.md)

Sathishkumar Ramamurthy Samireddyar

Emotional intelligence \(EI\) the capacity to perceive, understand, regulate, and leverage emotion has long been recognized as a defining trait of effective leadership\. That recognition now faces a new test: artificial intelligence is becoming embedded in the modern workplace, and with it comes a real opportunity to augment, rather than replace, the emotionally intelligent leader\. This paper looks at where AI and emotional intelligence meet in leadership practice\. Affective computing, sentiment analysis, and conversational agents are increasingly able to help leaders read team climate, tailor communication, and make decisions that are both empathetic and data informed\. I trace the specific mechanisms through which AI can sharpen self\-awareness, empathy, and relationship management, while weighing the real benefits stronger engagement, more inclusive decisions against genuine risks: surveillance, bias, and the slow erosion of authentic human connection\. Drawing on illustrative use cases and a look at adoption patterns across industries, I argue that AI delivers the most value to leaders not as a replacement for judgment, but as an emotional mirror and decision aid one that strengthens human judgment while keeping accountability, ethics, and genuine empathy firmly in human hands\.

## [Traditional Chinese medicine\-related interventions and the cGAS–STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action](../publications/68240ec8aa8515f2d51c.md)

Cunlong Zhang; Qin Li

Research on traditional Chinese medicine \(TCM\)\-related interventions has shifted from overall phenotypic effects to defined neuroimmune targets\. The cyclic GMP\-AMP synthase\-stimulator of interferon genes \(cGAS\-STING\) axis connects cytosolic DNA sensing with host defense and sterile inflammatory injury, but the functional direction of this pathway changes with disease context\. This review organizes preclinical findings by pathological setting and site of action\. It examines herbal formulas and natural compounds, followed by acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and related delivery systems\. Several sterile injury models associate benefit with reduced pathway\-related inflammation\. Acute sleep deprivation provides an example of protection accompanying restored STING signaling\. Early herpes simplex virus infection follows a different pattern: restoration of suppressed antiviral signaling improves host defense\. In acute postoperative pain and cancer\-induced bone pain models, increased STING\-IFN\-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture\-induced analgesia\. Some interventions reduce mitochondrial DNA stimulation\. Others act on cGAS or STING, with separate studies targeting STING trafficking\. Downstream inflammatory and cell\-death responses form the final level\. Mechanistic attribution is strongest when genetic or pharmacological perturbation links pathway change to functional outcome; direct binding has been demonstrated for a small group of compounds\. These findings support a context\-sensitive framework for interpreting modulation direction that requires validation within individual disease models\. Clinical translation will depend on reproducible formulation composition, effective brain exposure, and safety\.

## [BOSHLANG&\#x27;ICH SINF O&\#x27;QUVCHILARIDA IJROCHILIK KO&\#x27;NIKMALARINI SHAKLLANTIRISH METODIKASINI TAKOMILLASHTIRISH: PEDAGOGIK YONDASHUV](../publications/682863ac9ca5fb2109e2.md)

## [Selection of Outcomes and Measurement Methods in Clinical Trials for Digital Therapeutics: Qualitative Analysis](../publications/6838dca1eb7ebc90dcc7.md)

Johannes Mahlmann; Anne Mainz; Vera Weirauch; Achim Mortsiefer; Sven Meister

Background: In recent years, the availability of digital therapeutic apps in medicine, digital therapeutics \(DTx\), has significantly increased\. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of DTx, an increasing number of scientific studies have been conducted in this field\. Several authors have pointed out that a standardized approach to DTx evaluation is relevant to improving the comparability of apps in the future\. Currently, it is unclear how study authors proceed when selecting outcomes and measurement methods \(O&amp;M\) for DTx studies\. Objective: The primary aim of this study was to investigate how study authors currently select O&amp;M in DTx studies, specifically for applications delivered in the form of apps\. The secondary objectives were to collect suggestions for improving the comparability of DTx apps and studies in the future and to examine whether core outcome sets \(COS\) could represent a possible solution for enhancing comparability\. Methods: This study was based on 19 semistructured interviews\. All interview partners had prior experience in planning and conducting DTx studies\. The interviews were conducted between August 2024 and November 2024\. Subsequently, qualitative data analysis was performed according to Kuckartz and Rädiker using a deductive\-inductive research approach\. Results: The results of this study showed that the methodological approach for selecting O&amp;M in DTx studies was primarily based on research, as well as on personal prior experience and individual ideas\. Interview participants indicated that when selecting O&amp;M, they particularly focused on aspects such as scientific quality criteria or practical implementation and feasibility\. A suggestion for achieving better comparability of DTx studies in the future was to use standardized O&amp;M per therapeutic indication area\. Almost all interviewees considered COS to be a suitable approach for improving the comparability of DTx and associated studies\. However, we also identified critical perspectives that questioned their application\. Conclusions: Across professional groups, both commonalities and differences were observed in methodological approaches as well as in the selection of O&amp;M in DTx studies\. To improve the comparability of DTx interventions and trials, several approaches have been developed, for example, through the use of guidance frameworks, artificial intelligence programs, or the establishment of COS\. However, further research is warranted to advance this field\.

## [Nature\-based mindfulness program for parents and caregivers: a mixed\-methods study](../publications/68526db06e6c29015c68.md)

Zoe Jiwen Zhang; Herman Hay Ming Lo; Wai Fong Lok; Qi\-Rong Chen

Introduction There is a growing interest in incorporating nature into mindfulness\-based programs\. This study is unique as it targets parents and family caregivers experiencing caregiving stress\. Methods A mixed\-methods study was conducted to evaluate the outcome of a nature\-based mindfulness intervention program\. A comprehensive outcome measures targeting benefits of parents and caregivers, including mental health symptoms, wellbeing, physical distress, family functioning, and family conflicts, were assessed over time\. The role of nature in overall outcome was investigated through the participants&\#x27; perceived connectedness to nature and time spent in nature\. The program consists of four sessions, totaling 8 h of contact time, held at a retreat center and social care units\. A total of 95 participants were recruited, including 40 caregivers of older adults and 55 parents under stress\. The study employed a time series design, with assessments conducted 1 month before the program, pre\-program, post\-program, and at a 3\-month follow\-up\. Results For caregivers, significant improvements were observed in multiple outcome measures, including anxiety, stress, physical distress, daily functioning, and wellbeing, following the program\. Further improvement in connectedness with nature was noted between the pre\-test and the 3\-month follow\-up, with depression and family functioning approaching significance\. For parents under stress, significant improvements were found only in wellbeing after the program\. However, additional improvements in anxiety, stress, physical distress, and family conflicts \(psychological aggression, corporal punishment, and physical maltreatment\) were observed during the follow\-up period, with depression and daily functioning approaching significance\. Hierarchical regression analysis indicated that connectedness to nature significantly associated with the program&\#x27;s effect on depression\. Qualitative analysis revealed that participants benefited from attention restoration, increased awareness, and insights gained from nature and mindfulness practices\. Discussion Due to the limitations of the study, including the lack of control group and the use of self\-reported measures, future study should verify the benefits of nature\-based mindfulness programs particularly on the effects on parents and caregivers under stress and at risk of mental health conditions\.

## [Quantum eddy current wall thickness tomography using nitrogen\-vacancy vector magnetometry for onshore crude oil pipeline integrity assessment](../publications/685271b523669ffbd4de.md)

Kuan Fu; Rui Li; Pengchao Chen; Xiaoben Liu; Lili Zuo

As core infrastructure for global energy distribution, onshore long\-distance crude oil pipelines face multiple challenges, including wax deposition, structural stress concentration, and H 2 S release\. Traditional non\-destructive testing \(NDT\) techniques, such as eddy current testing and magnetic flux leakage \(MFL\), suffer from limitations including low spatial resolution, limited penetration depth, and directional blind spots, making high\-resolution and omnidirectional defect identification difficult\. Diamond nitrogen\-vacancy \(NV\) centers have shown strong potential for high\-precision vector magnetic sensing\. However, their application in pipeline inspection remains limited by insufficient environmental adaptability, the lack of quantitative wall\-thickness inversion models, and difficulties in large\-scale sensor array integration\. To address these issues, this study develops a hybrid framework combining NV vector magnetometry with quantum eddy\-current tomography\. Directional dependence is substantially reduced through a three\-phase orthogonal excitation field, as verified by controlled comparisons with single\-phase and dual\-phase excitation, while deterministically laser\-written NV centers integrated with metal lenses enable sensor array implementation\. A machine\-learning\-assisted tomographic reconstruction algorithm is further proposed to convert discrete magnetic measurements into continuous wall\-thickness images\. The results show a detection accuracy of 61\.0% for a controlled 1 μm nominal wall\-thickness perturbation and a coherence time of 70\.5 μs under 25 nT noise\. In the matched field evaluation, the proposed system achieved an overall detection rate of 93\.5%, compared with 65\.6% for MFL under the tested conditions, while ultrasonic calibration indicated close agreement between reconstructed and reference thicknesses\. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of NV\-based quantitative pipeline inspection under the evaluated conditions\.

## [Beyond sum scores: a network analysis of dark triad traits and nonsuicidal self\-injury in emerging adults](../publications/685387b4205987bc37f4.md)

Weiman Yan; Siqi Ma; Tenglong Wang; Yajun Tian; Yulin Xu; Kewei Sun; Chaoqun Wang; Qingjun Guo

Background Previous studies have investigated the relationships between dark triad traits and nonsuicidal self\-injury \(NSSI\) based on sum scores of corresponding scales\. However, this practice has hampered the fine\-grained understanding of how specific dark triad traits relate to NSSI at the item level\. This network analysis study aimed to examine these relationships in a joint framework and identify potential intervention targets\. Methods Dark triad traits and NSSI were measured using the Dirty Dozen \(DD\) and the behavior subscale of the Adolescent Nonsuicidal Self\-Injury Assessment Questionnaire \(ANSAQ\) among 1,950 emerging adults\. A regularized partial correlation network was constructed, and expected influence and bridge expected influence were calculated for each node\. Results In addition to connections within each community, several cross\-community edges were observed\. The strongest direct edge between the Dark Triad Traits and NSSI was found between N4 “I tend to expect special favors from others” \(narcissism\) and B1 “Intentionally pinching myself” \(NSSI\), but this edge was small in magnitude\. P1 “I tend to lack remorse” \(psychopathy\) and N1 “I tend to want others to admire me” \(narcissism\) had the highest expected influence values, whereas P4 “I tend to be cynical” \(psychopathy\) and P1 “I tend to lack remorse” \(psychopathy\) had the highest bridge expected influence values\. Conclusion These findings suggest that the item\-level connections between dark triad traits and NSSI are generally weak, with the most prominent associations occurring within the Dark Triad Traits dimensions themselves\. P1 and N1 appear to occupy central positions in the Dark Triad Traits network, while P4 and P1 mainly serve as bridges among the three dark traits traits rather than as direct links to NSSI\. The direct association between narcissistic entitlement and intentional pinching may warrant further investigation, but its clinical significance remains unclear\. Future research should examine whether these specific personality characteristics and self\-injury behaviors can inform targeted prevention or intervention efforts among emerging adults with dark triad traits\.

## [QoS\-Aware Secure Federated Intelligence for Biomedical Electronics and Medical Informatics in Wireless Health Monitoring Networks](../publications/68555a2c8322f23371b5.md)

Anandalakshmi Thevampalayam Kaliappan; P\. Senthilkumar; Tamilselvi K; Ravi A T; S\. P\. Santhoshkumar; V\. Asha

Wireless Health Monitoring Networks \(WHMNs\) that utilize Biomedical Electronics \(BMEs\) are rapidly changing how medical information is gathered and used in contemporary Medical Informatics through providing ongoing, real\-time, and remote assessment and monitoring of essential physiological parameters; including electrocardiogram \(ECG\), body temperature, blood oxygen saturation, and heart rate\. A number of constraints can limit the practical implementation of WHMNs including: stringent Quality of Service \(QoS\) requirements; limited energy availability; network scalability limitations; and significant risks associated with the transfer of sensitive medical information via open wireless networks\. While conventional centralized routing and learning based approaches provide the ability to route packets and learn network behavior they require high levels of communication, make the network vulnerable to cyber threats, and do little to protect the privacy of patients&\#x27; data\. This paper describes a QoS aware secure federated intelligence framework designed specifically for BME driven WHMNs\. The proposed framework will include: \(1\) Decentralized Federated Learning to enable distributed intelligence among edge nodes; \(2\) Trust based QoS Aware Routing to enable reliable and energy efficient communication throughout the network; and \(3\) a Lightweight Blockchain\-Assisted Mechanism to provide authentication, integrity, and tamper resistance to the network\. In contrast to traditional federated learning where edge node models are aggregated into a central server model for processing, the proposed framework enables edge nodes to train their own local models on their own data and to share only encrypted model updates rather than raw biomedical data; thereby reducing communication costs and increasing patient data privacy protection\. Simulation results show that the proposed framework outperform other state of the art WHMN protocols in terms of Packet Delivery Ratio \(PDR\); End\-To\-End Delay \(E2ED\); Residual Energy per Node \(REPN\); and Overall Network Lifetime \(ONL\)\. Additionally, the security analysis provided in this paper demonstrates the proposed framework&\#x27;s robustness against Insider Attacks, Data Manipulation Attacks, and Unauthorized Access Attacks\. These findings indicate the strong feasibility of the proposed framework for next generation Intelligent Healthcare and Medical Informatics Applications\.
