Roger Burrows; Alison Wallace; David Beer; Alexandra Ciocănel; James Cussens

This piece replies to some fine scholarship from the five commentators who have taken up the pen in response to our focus article\. We take up four themes running through the commentaries: the novelty of the imagined future, the politics of prediction, the social life of the score and the presence of hope, and we add an eighth vignette\. We hope our reply does them justice and invites others to join the conversation\.

## [XCAT\-UIR: explainable cross\-attention guided ConvNeXt\-transformer framework for underwater image restoration systems](../publications/685d1620560a0ea0d18e.md)

T Veeramakali; Md Shohel Sayeed; Sumendra Yogarayan

Underwater images play a significant role in ocean exploration, but they frequently suffer from major loss of image quality due to light absorption and scattering in underwater conditions\. However, underwater image restoration remains a challenging issue because of various distortions\. The primary cause of information degradation includes wavelength\-dependent color attenuation, light scattering effects, and blurring of objects\. Currently, deep learning methods are widely utilized for image enhancement, leveraging the concept that hidden features can be learned to improve the image quality\. Nevertheless, the black\-box nature of deep learning methods limits the understanding of how the model produces its restoration outputs\. This study presents an Explainable Cross\-Attention Guided ConvNeXt\-Transformer for Underwater Image Restoration \(XCAT\-UIR\) model\. The major objective of the proposed XCAT\-UIR approach is to increase the visibility, correct color distortions, preserve fine details, and improve the overall quality of degraded underwater images\. The proposed approach initially performs preprocessing to improve image quality for further analysis\. Subsequently, ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer techniques are employed to extract local texture and global contextual information from the preprocessed images to enhance the feature understanding\. The integration of convolution\-based and transformer\-based feature extraction networks improves the representation capability of the restoration model\. Besides, the Cross\-Attention Fusion model is used to integrate local features from ConvNeXt and global features from Swin Transformer to generate discriminative fused feature representations\. Furthermore, Residual Reconstruction Blocks reconstruct the enhanced underwater image from the fused features while preserving important details and reducing information loss\. Lastly, Grad\-CAM and cross\-attention maps are used to enhance visual evidence for restoration\-relevant areas and local\-global feature interactions\. To ensure the improved performance of the proposed model, a widespread experimental analysis is performed using a benchmark dataset\. An extensive comparison study emphasized that the proposed model has gained significant performance over recent methods in terms of different measures, indicating its superiority in underwater image restoration\.

## [RECREG: Recovery\-based Shielding for Regular Safety Properties in Reinforcement Learning](../publications/686c10519593cca6bb14.md)

Alexander W\. Goodall; Francesco Belardinelli

In many real\-world scenarios we need to consider formal requirements, such as safety and constraint compliance, to deploy Reinforcement Learning \(RL\) agents\. In this paper we introduce RecReg, a safe RL framework capable of enforcing non\-Markovian regular safety properties via recovery\-based shielding\. RecReg is a unified approach that supports different levels of a priori knowledge and safety guarantees\. The paper primarily focuses on building the theoretical foundations for RecReg in the tabular setting, providing rigorous safety and convergence guarantees that are not present in related work\. We provide an extensive set of empirical results using the MASA\-Safe\-RL library, and we outline an extension of RecReg to deep RL domains using SOTA model\-based RL\. Our empirical results demonstrate that RecReg achieves efficient learning and matches the theory in this paper\.

## [Extent of Coverage and Prominence of Science and Technology News in Select Nigerian Newspapers \(2014\-2024\)](../publications/687234a89003b73957ae.md)

Olugbenga Olanrewaju Akanmu; Benjamin Olumuyiwa Popoola

This study evaluated the extent of coverage and the level of prominence given to Sci &amp; Tech stories by two leading Nigerian national dailies, The Punch and The Guardian, from June 2014 to May 2024\. The paper specifically attempted to assess the extent of coverage given to science and technology stories by Nigerian newspapers; and examine the level of prominence of science and technology stories by Nigerian newspapers\. Premised on the Agenda\-Setting Theory, the study adopted a quantitative content analysis research design\. From a population of 5,280 newspaper editions, a sample size of 696 editions was selected using the systematic sampling technique, yielding 584 relevant Sci &amp; Tech stories\. Findings revealed a steady volume of coverage, with The Punch contributing 51\.9% and The Guardian 48\.1%\. In addition, the paper found that coverage suffered from significantly low editorial prominence, as 87\.0% of the stories were relegated to the inside pages, with a mere 8\.7% appearing on the front page\. The study concluded that while Nigerian newspapers maintain a consistent baseline volume of science and technology reporting, their structural relegation to less prominent pages signals to the public that they are secondary to political and economic news\. The paper recommended that editorial boards should elevate significant scientific breakthroughs to front pages to enhance citizen participation in technological development\.

## [Greening Islamic Education: A Conceptual Framework for Integrating Ecotheology into Organizational Dynamics](../publications/68a37c0986715708ef09.md)

Trian Hermawan; Samsul Hadi; Subandi Subandi; Asma’ Adniyyah Binti Che Ismail

This study develops an ecotheology\-based transformation framework explaining how Islamic educational institutions translate ecological values into sustainable organizational systems\. Environmental challenges require these institutions to move beyond fragmented programs toward systemic organizational transformation\. Although Islamic ecotheology provides strong foundations for ecological responsibility, limited research explains how religious values operate as mechanisms for sustainability transformation\. A Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) following PRISMA 2020 examined literature on Islamic education, sustainability, ecotheology, and organizational transformation\. Thematic synthesis examined 32 studies to identify transformation mechanisms, enabling factors, and barriers\. The findings show that Islamic ecotheology serves as a foundational value that shapes ecological identity and institutional commitment\. Prophetic\-transformational leadership translates these values into strategic action and collective commitment\. Organizational structures, governance systems, and sustainability policies institutionalize ecological values in practices\. Sustainability\-oriented organizational culture strengthens ecological responsibility and continuity\. Participation and collective learning reinforce sustainability initiatives through distributed responsibility\. However, limited resources, fragmented governance, and insufficient institutional capacity constrain ecological transformation\. The findings imply that transformation requires alignment among values, leadership, governance, culture, and participation rather than isolated programs\. Theoretical implications include integrating religious value systems into sustainability transformation theory\. Practical implications include embedding ecotheological principles in strategic planning, leadership development, governance, organizational culture, and practices\.

## [Deep learning–accelerated contrast\-enhanced 3D MRI for acute optic neuritis: faster acquisition and improved lesion conspicuity](../publications/68e0d8b4bc9dcc4b8565.md)

Ying Liu; Weiyin Vivian Liu; Zhi Wen; Min Lu; Changsheng Liu; Liang Li; Ting Chen; Renjie Yang; Yunfei Zha

Objective To compare a deep learning\-accelerated contrast\-enhanced 3D T1\-weighted sequence \(T1\-CUBE\-DLS\) with standard parallel imaging\-accelerated T1\-CUBE for detecting acute optic neuritis \(ON\)\. Methods This prospective study enrolled 59 patients with suspected acute ON \(38 females; mean age 41\.2 ± 12\.8 years\)\. All underwent contrast\-enhanced whole\-brain 3\.0 T MRI including both T1\-CUBE\-DLS and standard T1\-CUBE sequences\. Two blinded neuroradiologists independently scored motion artifacts, subjective noise, and optic nerve clarity\. Consensus readings recorded enhancement laterality, involved segments, and visual conspicuity\. Enhancement length was measured per optic nerve, with inter\-observer reliability assessed via intraclass correlation coefficient \(ICC\) and Bland–Altman analysis\. Clinical diagnosis by a senior neuro\-ophthalmologist served as the reference standard\. Results Acute ON was confirmed in 43 of 59 patients \(72\.9%\)\. T1\-CUBE\-DLS reduced acquisition time by 36\.2%\. Subjective noise was equivalent between sequences \( p &gt; 0\.05\), but T1\-CUBE\-DLS showed significantly fewer motion artifacts and superior optic nerve clarity \(both p &lt; 0\.05\)\. No significant difference was detected in diagnostic performance between the two sequences: sensitivity \(88\.4% vs\. 86\.0%\), specificity \(93\.8% vs\. 93\.8%\), and accuracy \(89\.8% vs\. 88\.1%; all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. T1\-CUBE\-DLS demonstrated stronger visual conspicuity \( p = 0\.011\) and slightly longer measured enhancement length \(mean difference, 0\.836 mm; p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. ICC for length measurement was 0\.91 for T1\-CUBE\-DLS vs\. 0\.83 for standard T1\-CUBE, with narrower 95% limits of agreement \(−1\.37 to 1\.51 mm vs\. − 3\.1 to 2\.4 mm\)\. Conclusion T1\-CUBE\-DLS reduces acquisition time by 36\.2%, with no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy detected, while improving enhancement conspicuity and measurement reproducibility, supporting its potential as a practical and efficient alternative for ON evaluation\.

## [Aspen Bark\-Based Phytocomplexes: Applications in Health Nutrition](../publications/68ea5a5834ae9c4ffcbc.md)



This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the development, technological optimization, and standardization of innovative dietary supplements derived from aspen bark \(Populus tremula\) extract\.The study substantiates the critical relevance of utilizing this botanical resource as a potent source of bioactive phenolic glycosides\-specifically salicinalongside flavonoids and polyphenolic compounds, which are essential for the prevention and adjunctive therapy of diverse metabolic disorders\.Integral to the research are the detailed quality control methodologies and the empirical results of chemical profiling conducted via High\-Performance Liquid Chromatography \(HPLC\), ensuring precise identification of active markers\.The work meticulously delineates the multi\-stage technological manufacturing schemes and proprietary formulations for two distinct delivery systems: &\#x27;Ekorsol \+&\#x27; granules and the high\-potency &\#x27;Ekorsol \-Forte \+&\#x27; capsules\.By establishing rigorous standardized organoleptic and physicochemical parameters\-ranging from moisture content and disintegration rates to quantified thresholds for salicin and flavonoids\-the research confirms the products&\#x27; full compliance with contemporary safety and efficacy mandates\.Ultimately, these phytocomplexes represent a scalable advancement in pharmaceutical technology, offering standardized therapeutic solutions within the global health nutrition and nutraceutical segments for metabolic health management\.

## [Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance‐guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single‐center retrospective study](../publications/68f51cf3faa589ea206a.md)

Lelio Guida; Emma Losito; Sébastian Rodrigo; Catherine Chiron; Ludovic Fillon; Marie Bourgeois; Anna Kamińska; Johan Pallud; Nicole Chémaly; Volodia Dangouloff‐Ross; Stephane Aunvin; Blandine Dozières‐Puyravel; Rima Nabbout; Olivier David A; Nathalie Boddaert; Thomas Blauwblomme

OBJECTIVE: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance\-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy \(MRgLITT\) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone \(IOZ\)\. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single\-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy\. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography \(EEG\) and magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography \(FDG\-PET\) and stereo\-EEG \(SEEG\) were performed in negative\-MRI cases\. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording\. Postablation contrast\-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi\-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection \(MELD\) MRI analysis, FDG\-PET voxel\-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available\. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes \(International League Against Epilepsy classification\)\. RESULTS: Eight children \(median age = 10\.4 years, range = 2\.3\-17\) were included, with a median postoperative follow\-up of 38 months\. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation\. Among the six MRI\-negative patients, FDG\-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster \(range 1\-3\), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases\. Overall, four negative\-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection\. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed\. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons\. A greater proportion of FDG\-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes \(p = \.012\)\. SIGNIFICANCE: MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach\. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation\.

## [Digital Twin\-Based Modeling and Optimization of Continuous Biomanufacturing Processes: A Data\-Driven Simulation Study](../publications/68f9e175254919a6983f.md)

ijbes

Continuous biomanufacturing, particularly perfusion\-based monoclonal\-antibody production, offers highproductivity and consistent quality but requires faster, more reliable monitoring and control thanconventional fed\-batch operation\. This paper reviews digital\-twin\-based optimisation of continuousbiomanufacturing and presents an illustrative, reproducible simulation informed by publicly availablebioprocess datasets\. A three\-tier digital\-model, digital\-shadow, and digital\-twin architecture is examinedalongside mechanistic, data\-driven, and hybrid modelling paradigms\. The simulation demonstrates modelpredictive control of glucose set\-point tracking in a perfusion bioreactor\. Across the reviewed studies andillustrative results, hybrid mechanistic\-machine\-learning twins provide stronger predictive performancethan purely mechanistic or data\-driven alternatives, while digital\-twin\-based control reduces glucosedeviation relative to conventional control and open\-loop feeding\. Key barriers include fragmenteddatasets, model validation, regulatory acceptance, cybersecurity, and cross\-scale transferability\. The studytherefore recommends open, standardised bioprocess datasets and rigorous deployment validation tosupport reproducible, industrially credible digital\-twin research\.

## [DEVELOPMENT OF A WAREHOUSE ACCOUNTING SYSTEM IN WHOLESALE TRADE ENTERPRISES BASED ON THE TOE METHODOLOGY](../publications/68ff227a05dcdf1ca824.md)

Наталія Бабурнич

The purpose is to establish the theoretical foundation for organising accounting in trade enterprises with consideration of the TOE model, to substantiate the accounting and economic functions of inventories, and to determine the methodological principles for implementing a warehouse accounting system under conditions of digital transformation\. Methodology\. The study is grounded in systemic and process\-oriented approaches, combining theoretical generalisations of scientific principles with a practical analysis of warehouse operations in retail enterprises\. The systems approach was applied to conceptualise warehouse management as an integrated, multifunctional system, while the process approach enabled the interdependence of its elements to be described within the framework of management accounting\. General methods of analysis and synthesis were employed to generalise scientific principles regarding the role of inventory in business operations\. The theoretical foundation of the study is the TOE model, which explains the implementation of innovative warehouse accounting systems through technological, organisational, and environmental contexts, including an assessment of the impact of digital technologies such as automation, robotisation, cloud solutions, and artificial intelligence\. Results\. The study found that warehouse management in wholesale enterprises plays a strategic role by forming the basis for competitive advantages and economic stability\. The use of the TOE model enabled the systematic identification of factors influencing the implementation of innovative solutions in warehouse management and their adaptation to the needs of trading enterprises\. The technological context encompasses process automation, the use of cloud platforms, robotic systems, blockchain solutions, and artificial intelligence\. The organisational context is determined by staff readiness, management support, and the structural characteristics of the enterprise\. The external environment includes competitive pressure, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations\. The modernisation of warehouse accounting helps to optimise business processes in several dimensions: time, physical volumes, information, and storage conditions\. Practical implications\. The proposed approach can be applied by retail enterprises to optimise warehouse processes, reduce the risk of asset loss, and improve the accuracy of accounting data\. Its practical significance lies in utilising the TOE model to introduce innovative accounting technologies, thereby enhancing the competitiveness and resilience of enterprises in times of crisis\. Value / originality\. The originality of this study lies in the combination of an accounting and economic analysis of inventories with a process\-based approach to warehouse operations and the application of the TOE model in explaining the digital transformation of accounting\. This provides a comprehensive understanding of the role of warehouse management as a strategic tool for the development of retail enterprises, integrating economic, organisational, and technological aspects\.

## [An Artificial Intelligence Framework to Predict Box Office Performance Through Multimodal Analysis of Movie Trailers and Online Audience Responses](../publications/6915a246f05aaf4123d5.md)

Jing Wang

In the film industry, box office predictions are crucial for making investment decisions, marketing plans, and distribution choices\. Current prediction approaches mainly use movie metadata or single\-modal information, ignoring trailer video content and audience responses, resulting in low prediction accuracy and robustness\. The proposed framework is novel in that it uses a Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\)–Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(BiLSTM\)–Attention \(CNN–BiLSTM–Attention\) regression and Artificial Rabbits Optimization \(ARO\)\-based feature selection to integrate trailer visual features, trailer audio features, movie metadata, and audience responses into a single multimodal architecture\. The proposed framework used the Movies YouTube Trailers &amp; Sentiment dataset, which was preprocessed using mean value imputation, followed by Min–Max normalization and one\-hot encoding\. Vision Transformer \(ViT\) was used to extract visual characteristics from the trailer, and Mel\-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients \(MFCC\), chroma, spectral centroid, zero\-crossing rate, and Root Mean Square \(RMS\) energy were used to extract audio features\. Audience response features were derived from sentiment scores, favorability, and vote counts\. Visual, audio, metadata, and audience response features were fused into a unified multimodal representation\. In order to forecast box office revenue, ARO chose the CNN–BiLSTM–Attention network&\#x27;s most informative feature subset\. Mean Absolute Error \(MAE\) of 0\.0246, Mean Squared Error \(MSE\) of 0\.0009, Root Mean Squared Error \(RMSE\) of 0\.0304, Mean Absolute Percentage Error \(MAPE\) of 0\.0586, and Coefficient of Determination \(R 2 \) of 0\.9549 were all attained by the suggested model\. The results showed that the proposed model improved prediction accuracy and provided an effective decisionsupport tool for movie producers and distributors\.

## [Fake News Detection Using AI](../publications/69188eb89a34d438cae2.md)

Jananai A; Nivetha D; Prabhavathi U; Sumathi S\.

The rapid circulation of news through websites and social\-media platforms makes it difficult for readers to distinguish trustworthy reporting from fabricated or misleading content\. This paper presents an AI\-based fake news detection system that applies Natural Language Processing \(NLP\) and machine learning to classify textual news content into predefined categories such as fake and real\. The workflow includes data preparation, text cleaning, feature extraction using Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\), model training, prediction, and presentation of the result through an application interface\. Logistic Regression is considered as the baseline classifier because it is efficient for sparse text features and provides a practical reference for text\-classification tasks\. The proposed system is intended to support early screening of suspicious news, not to replace source verification or professional fact\-checking\. The paper describes the design, implementation workflow, evaluation metrics, risks, and future improvements\. Since verified experimental logs and final test measurements were not supplied for this manuscript, numerical performance is not fabricated; the results section specifies the measurements that the team should insert after running the final model\. The work provides a structured, reproducible approach for building and evaluating a news\-text classification application\.

## [Transitional Nursing Care for Oesophageal Cancer Patients: A Scoping Review](../publications/69272aa13293f4ada9c8.md)

Yeonju Kim; Boseul Cho; Kenrick Cato; Mona Choi

AIMS: To understand the extent and characteristics of transitional nursing care for patients with oesophageal cancer across treatment modalities, examine patient experiences and the role of nurses, and identify research gaps\. DESIGN: A scoping review\. METHODS: The scoping review followed the framework of Arksey and O&\#x27;Malley and the JBI methodology\. DATA SOURCES \(INCLUDE SEARCH DATES\): PubMed, CINAHL, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched on 11 June 2025 for relevant articles with no date restrictions\. RESULTS: This scoping review included 33 studies \(26 quantitative, 7 qualitative\) conducted primarily in Asia \(n = 25, 75\.8%\)\. Evidence predominantly reflected postoperative care involving multicomponent and nutrition\-focused interventions, whereas evidence for nonsurgical treatments and social support interventions remained limited\. Qualitative evidence revealed patients&\#x27; need for multidimensional support across individual, relational, and system levels\. Nurses&\#x27; primary roles included guidance and counselling, whereas evaluation and feedback roles were least reported\. Evidence gaps existed in care coordination, particularly for hospital\-to\-community transitions, with most studies extending only to outpatient follow\-up rather than home and community settings\. CONCLUSION: Patients with oesophageal cancer require multifaceted, continuous transitional nursing care across the care continuum, yet current interventions inadequately address relational, social, and system\-level needs\. Evidence gaps exist between patients&\#x27; experienced needs and available interventions, particularly in hospital\-to\-community care coordination and nonsurgical treatment pathways\. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Clinical nurses should assess the social support systems of patients with oesophageal cancer and their ability to utilize community resources during discharge education\. Nursing management should incorporate evaluation and feedback as a core responsibility in transitional care and formalize communication between hospital and community services\. Future studies are recommended to target nonsurgical populations and to address unmet coordination needs\. REPORTING METHOD: PRISMA\-ScR\. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution\. TRIAL AND PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework \(http://doi\.org/10\.17605/OSF\.IO/86BGR\)\. IMPACT: Identifies key gaps in transitional nursing care for oesophageal cancer patients across care settings and treatment modalities\. Informs the design of more comprehensive, patient\-centered transitional care approaches\. Supports improvements in hospital\-to\-community care continuity and coordination\. Guides future research and policy initiatives to better address complex patient needs\.

## [ANSIEDADE NA PESSOA IDOSA: MEDOS, FUNCIONALIDADE E INTERVENÇÕES DE CUIDADO](../publications/692e7fae6007f9c9b692.md)

Ana Beatriz de Magalhaes Pavan; Amanda Bruna de Lima Aquino; Ana Freitas Goulart Terra; Elenize de Oliveira Silva Neves; Lívia Ximenes Rocha; Marielle Cury Costa Siqueira; Pablo José de Paula Cardoso; Joao Vitor M\. Lamim; Joao Victor Reder Souza; Lucas Ximenes Rocha; Marcos Henrique Dias Fonseca; Fábio Luiz Fully Teixeira

RESUMO: A ansiedade na pessoa idosa constitui uma importante questão de saúde mental, especialmente diante do acelerado processo de envelhecimento populacional\.Trata\-se de um fenômeno multifatorial, relacionado a aspectos biológicos, psicológicos e sociais, que pode repercutir sobre a funcionalidade, autonomia, participação social e qualidade de vida\.Este estudo teve como objetivo reunir e discutir evidências sobre a ansiedade na pessoa idosa, considerando fatores associados, sua relação com a funcionalidade e as possibilidades de cuidado\.Este estudo é uma revisão de literatura, de precoce, bem como de novas pesquisas sobre estratégias de cuidado em diferentes contextos\.

## [Mangrove litter mixing alters elemental composition more frequently than mass loss, with species\-specific patterns across nitrogen\-enrichment plots](../publications/69466f5a23f5e7f54d10.md)

Zhouxiang Zheng; Qijuan Cao; Yuxi Chen; Mingxuan Zheng; 刘志彦 LIU Zhiyan; Yisheng Peng

Introduction Mangrove litter decomposition contributes to coastal carbon and nutrient cycling, yet changes in litter mass may not fully reflect changes in elemental composition\. This study investigated litter decomposition and C: N stoichiometry in relation to species identity, nitrogen enrichment, and litter mixing in a subtropical mangrove wetland\. Methods Two field experiments were conducted on Hailing Island, southern China\. A previously reported nitrogen\-enrichment experiment included an untreated control and three nitrogen\-input levels \(22\.85, 114\.24, and 228\.48 g N m \-2 yr \-1 \)\. As each treatment was represented by a single plot, the results were examined descriptively\. A separate litter\-mixing experiment examined three mangrove species \( Sonneratia apetala , Kandelia obovata , and Avicennia marina \) and their two\- and three\-species mixtures\. Litter mass remaining, total organic carbon \(TOC\), total nitrogen \(TN\), total phosphorus \(TP\), and C:N ratios were measured during decomposition\. Results S\. apetala and A\. marina decomposed faster than K\. obovata , with differences corresponding to their initial litter chemistry\. Mass loss varied among nitrogen\-enrichment plots without a consistent response to increasing nitrogen input\. Compared with the control, mean aboveground\-litter TP was 14\.02% higher and N was 11\.53% lower in the high\-nitrogen plot\. In the litter\-mixing experiment, significant deviations from weighted single\-species expectations occurred in only 20% of mass\-remaining comparisons, compared with 65%, 70%, and 55% for TOC, TN, and TP, respectively\. Most elemental deviations occurred during the early and intermediate stages of decomposition\. The three\-species mixture did not consistently show greater mass loss than the two\-species mixtures\. Discussion Litter mixing produced more frequent changes in elemental composition than in mass remaining, with responses varying among species combinations\. These findings suggest that litter mass loss alone may not adequately reflect changes in nutrient composition during mangrove litter decomposition\. The nitrogen\-enrichment results also showed variation in litter stoichiometry, although these observations require confirmation through replicated field experiments\.

## [A class of unrooted phylogenetic networks inspired by the properties of rooted tree\-child networks](../publications/695412c21448479b3502.md)

Leo J\. J\. van Iersel; Mark Jones; Simone Linz; Norbert Zeh

A directed phylogenetic network is tree\-child if every non\-leaf vertex has a child that is not a reticulation\. As a class of directed phylogenetic networks, tree\-child networks are very useful from a computational perspective\. For example, several computationally difficult problems in phylogenetics become tractable when restricted to tree\-child networks\. At the same time, the class itself is rich enough to contain quite complex networks\. Furthermore, checking whether a directed network is tree\-child can be done in polynomial time\. In this paper, we seek a class of undirected phylogenetic networks that is rich and computationally useful in a similar way to the class tree\-child directed networks\. A natural class to consider for this role is the class of tree\-child\-orientable networks which contains all those undirected phylogenetic networks whose edges can be oriented to create a tree\-child network\. However, we show here that recognizing such networks is NP\-hard, even for binary networks, and as such this class is inappropriate for this role\. Towards finding a class of undirected networks that fills a similar role to directed tree\-child networks, we propose new classes called $q$\-cuttable networks, for any integer $q\\geq 1$\. We show that these classes have many of the desirable properties, similar to tree\-child networks in the rooted case, including being recognizable in polynomial time, for all $q\\geq 1$\. Towards showing the computational usefulness of the class, we show that the NP\-hard problem Tree Containment is polynomial\-time solvable when restricted to $q$\-cuttable networks with $q\\geq 3$\.

## [Psychometric validation of the Chinese Physical Effort Scale and profiles of physical\-effort approach and avoidance among Chinese university students](../publications/69638c184d591ff5d73a.md)

Yijun Liu; Qiang Zhou

Objective Individual differences in tendencies to approach or avoid physical effort may be relevant to exercise\-related psychological and behavioral characteristics\. This study examined the psychometric properties of the Chinese Physical Effort Scale \(PES\) and investigated individual differences in physical\-effort approach and avoidance tendencies and their associations with exercise\-related psychological and behavioral variables among Chinese university students\. Methods Participants were 1,273 students from six universities across eastern, central, and western China\. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, reliability and validity analyses, and multigroup confirmatory factor analysis were used to evaluate the factor structure, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance of the Chinese PES\. Latent profile analysis identified configurations of physical effort approach and avoidance, and BCH analyses compared profiles on emotion regulation, exercise motivation, and physical activity\. Results Factor analyses supported a two\-factor structure comprising physical effort approach and avoidance\. The scale showed high internal consistency and test–retest reliability, with evidence supporting convergent and discriminant validity and metric and scalar invariance across gender and academic year\. Three profiles were identified: Balanced \(59\.07%\), Avoidance\-Oriented \(14\.93%\), and Approach\-Oriented \(26\.00%\)\. The Approach\-Oriented profile showed higher cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, external regulation, introjected regulation, and autonomous regulation, and lower amotivation\. It also showed higher total physical activity than the other profiles and higher weekly exercise frequency than the Balanced profile\. Conclusion The Chinese PES showed psychometric support among Chinese university students\. Distinct configurations of physical effort approach and avoidance were associated with emotion regulation, exercise motivation, and physical activity\.

## [Financial literacy in digital and AI\-supported educational contexts](../publications/696d136e04f3e1d8edf6.md)

Drnovšek, Nika, vzgoja in izobraževanje; Stanislav Avsec; Francka Lovšin Kozina

In an era of expanding digital finance, fintech innovation and AI\-supported decision\-making, financial literacy has become a critical educational priority for informed, inclusive and responsible participation in contemporary financial systems\. This study examines financial literacy in digital and AI\-supported educational contexts through bibliometric mapping and a PRISMA\-based systematic review\. A bibliometric analysis of 3,105 Web of Science and Scopus records identified the broader conceptual structure of the field, followed by thematic synthesis of 29 studies with educational relevance\. Methodological quality was assessed using design\-specific JBI Critical Appraisal Tools\. The findings show that financial literacy and financial inclusion form the main conceptual hubs, while fintech and digital finance act as bridging themes\. AIrelated research is visible, but is mainly linked to prediction, decision\-making, fintech adoption and digital services rather than direct pedagogy\. The review further shows that digital tools are used across diverse educational and assessment contexts, with the more consistent evidence emphasizing structured instructional design and pedagogical integration rather than technology exposure alone\. AI\-related evidence remains limited and is predominantly analytical, diagnostic, advisory or supportive rather than directly pedagogical\. The main research gap lies in the limited empirical evidence on pedagogically grounded AI\-supported approaches to financial literacy education\. Overall, the study provides an integrated framework for identifying conceptual structures, emerging digital and AI\-supported trends, and critical pedagogical gaps relevant to evidence\-informed and inclusive financial literacy education\.

The use of ChatGPT among university students is growing rapidly, yet empirical evidence on its effect on cognitive learning outcomes in courses that demand higher\-order thinking, such as Research Methodology, remains limited in Islamic higher education\. This study aimed to determine the effect of ChatGPT use on the cognitive learning outcomes of Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) students at Institut Agama Islam Hamzanwadi Pancor in the Research Methodology course\. A quantitative approach with an ex post facto design was used\. The population was 487 students in the sixth and eighth semesters; the sample of 83 students was determined using the Slovin formula and proportionate stratified random sampling\. ChatGPT use was measured with a four\-point Likert questionnaire \(20 valid items\), while cognitive learning outcomes were taken from final course grades through documentation\. Data were analyzed with simple linear regression in SPSS after the normality, linearity, and heteroscedasticity assumptions were met\. The results show a regression equation of Y = 64\.465 \+ 0\.278X, with a t value of 17\.778 \(greater than the t table value of 1\.990; Sig\. 0\.000\) and an R² of 0\.796\. ChatGPT use therefore had a positive and significant effect on cognitive learning outcomes, accounting for 79\.6% of their variance\. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the ex post facto design, the narrow range of grades, and the measurement of usage intensity rather than usage quality\.

## [Dynamic mechanical cues in 2D and 3D matrix mechanobiology: from static to time\-resolved bioengineered platforms](../publications/697d120b23f4bbcf4fd9.md)

Crescenzo Frascogna; Valeria Panzetta; Maurizio Ventre

The extracellular matrix \(ECM\) is a dynamic regulator of cell behaviour, continuously changing its biophysical state, including mechanical properties, architecture and ligand presentation, during development, homeostasis, repair and disease\. However, conventional in vitro models stimulate cells through static and simplified signals, limiting investigation of how cells decode the temporal features of their surroundings\. This work examines dynamic two\-dimensional \(2D\) and three\-dimensional \(3D\) bioengineered platforms designed to reproduce time\-changing biophysical signals and their mechanobiological consequences\. In dynamic 2D interfaces, tuneable stiffness, cyclic deformation, fluid flow and shear stress, reversible ligand presentation, and switchable topographies or curvature enable controlled delivery of mechanical, biochemical and architectural cues\. These systems show that cellular responses, including adhesion organization, cytoskeletal remodelling, cell polarity, nuclear morphology, chromatin organization and mechanoresponsive signalling, depend not only on cue magnitude, but also on rate, frequency, duration, waveform, persistence and mechanical history\. We also discuss how dimensionality reshapes the interpretation of dynamic cues\. In 3D matrices, cells experience confinement, multidirectional force transmission, matrix degradability, pore architecture and cell\-mediated remodelling, making mechanotransduction fundamentally more complex than in planar cultures\. Organ\-on\-chip devices, bioprinted matrices and responsive hydrogels integrate ECM\-like architectures with perfusion, mechanical actuators and functional readouts, enabling tissue remodelling to be reconstructed as a controllable experimental variable\. Overall, dynamic matrix mechanobiology shifts the focus from fixed material properties to the temporal logic of cell–ECM interactions\. More predictive in vitro models will require not simply increasingly complex matrices, but platforms that combine physiological dynamics with sufficient experimental control to identify mechanobiological mechanisms\.

## [Revisiting brain asymmetry in schizophrenia: insights from machine learning subtypes from 1,761 patients](../publications/697d2dde84128a3e75a9.md)

金璐; Zhaoyun Liu; Xiao Chang; Xinjia Lin; Zhenyu Huang; Hongxing Hu; Ruixue Yang; Jie Zhang; Hao Hu; Qian Guo; Yingying Tang; Tianhong Zhang; Jijun Wang; Huan Huang; Jingyu Zhou; Long‐Biao Cui; 伊琦忠; Cheng Luo; Dezhong Yao; Jianfeng Feng; Yuchao Jiang

Brain asymmetry serves as a measure of typical neurodevelopment, and its disruption is implicated in the etiological framework of schizophrenia \(SZ\)\. While previous studies have reported significant alterations in brain structural asymmetry in SZ patients, their interpretations are often limited by relatively small sample sizes, varying approaches to process MRI data, and inconsistent findings\. This study aims to identify robust brain asymmetry alterations in SZ using large\-scale neuroimaging data, and to investigate how these alterations vary across neuroanatomical subtypes\. We analyzed T1\-weighted magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) data from 1,761 individuals with SZ and 1,513 healthy controls \(HC\), primarily of East Asian ancestry\. Regional asymmetry in cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volume was quantified using a standardized pipeline\. We examined case\-control differences in regional asymmetry and further compared two neuroanatomical subtypes previously derived using a machine learning algorithm \(i\.e\., Subtype and Stage Inference\)\. Compared with HC, SZ patients displayed significantly reduced leftward asymmetry in the rostral middle frontal gyrus, reduced rightward asymmetry in the medial orbitofrontal cortex, and enhanced rightward asymmetry in the amygdala \( p &lt; 0\.001, Bonferroni\-corrected\)\. Comparison with prior Western cohort findings over 5,000 SZ individuals revealed only moderate similarity in cortical surface area asymmetry \( r = 0\.36, p = 0\.02\), with no significant correlations for cortical thickness or subcortical volume\. Subtype differences emerged in temporal and parietal lobes, precentral gyrus, and caudate \( p &lt; 0\.05, Bonferroni\-corrected\)\. Furthermore, asymmetry in anterior cingulate volume correlated differently with negative symptoms across subtypes \(permutation test, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. This study confirms that while case\-control asymmetry effect sizes are small, they are statistically significant in certain regions when SZ is stratified into neuroanatomical subtypes\. These findings extend the long\-standing hypothesis of abnormal cerebral asymmetry in SZ, and underscore the influence of subtype and ancestry on observed asymmetry alterations\.

## [The reliability of clinical judgments in dermatology: a descriptive review on their role as a reference standard for technological diagnostic research](../publications/69817a4702f76bde7d2d.md)

Nelly Mwageni; Robin van Wijk; Anne Schoenmarkers; John Elisante Masenga; Christa Kasang; Liesbeth F\. Mieras; Stephen Eliatosha Mshana

The expansion of dermatological mobile health \(mHealth\) and teledermatology has generated numerous diagnostic support tools, typically validated against traditional face\-to\-face assessments\. Histopathological confirmation through skin biopsy is invasive, resource\-intensive and, in many African settings, not readily available as a dermatological research reference standard\. Yet, the reliability of clinical diagnoses used as such standards remains uncertain\. The study objective was to assess the consistency \(inter\-rater reliability\) of face\-to\-face clinical judgments among multiple dermatologists evaluating the same patient group\. For this descriptive literature review, a comprehensive search of seven databases and information platforms was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses \(PRISMA\) reporting guideline\. In total, 1,700 studies were found after deduplication and screened using pre\-set criteria\. Eighteen studies were included: three compared clinical diagnoses directly and 15 assessed the reliability of dermatological scoring systems for disease severity and activity\. All studies involved two or more dermatologists assessing the same patients\. Reported agreement among raters ranged from 0\.15 to 0\.98 for studies evaluating clinical diagnosis and from 0\.07 to 0\.95 for studies assessing disease severity or activity scores, demonstrating wide variability in inter\-rater reliability\. In conclusion, clinical diagnosis alone, especially if made by one or a limited number of dermatologists, may not provide a sufficiently reliable reference standard for validating teledermatology, dermatological mHealth applications, or artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools\. Strengthening evidence on the reliability of diagnostic reference standards is essential for evaluating emerging digital health innovations, particularly in regions with limited access to dermatologists and histopathology services\. Future studies, with similarly experienced dermatological assessors, should have larger sample sizes, assess diagnostic agreement rather than disease severity outcomes, combine inter\- and intra\-rater assessments, and include diverse geographic contexts such as Africa, Asia and Latin America\. The potential influence of assessors&\#x27; levels of experience on agreement should also be explored\. A final recommendation is to come to a consensus about skin color classification\.

## [Healthcare That Learns](../publications/69834982ae2cbd260e4f.md)

Dong‐Gil Ko; Umberto Tachinardi; Brett M\. Kissela M\. D

Healthcare has more evidence, data, and artificial intelligence \(AI\) than ever\. A risk model can flag a patient, a dashboard can reveal a gap, and a guideline can recommend the next step\. But if no one owns the response, if the workflow cannot support action, or if the patient’s reality is not part of the loop, better information does not become better care\. Healthcare That Learns: Value\-Based Care and the AI\-Enabled Learning Health System argues that the central challenge is not discovery, technology, or payment reform\. It is conversion: turning practice into data, data into knowledge, knowledge into standards, standards into routines, and routines back into better practice\. Written for health system executives, clinical leaders, informaticians, quality and safety professionals, policymakers, clinicians, and trainees, this book offers a practical operating model for the AI\-enabled learning health system\. It shows how value\-based care, AI, informatics, operations, governance, equity, implementation, and workforce readiness must work together to close the know–do gap and make better care routine\. Through real\-world cases and a clear learning architecture, the book explains why AI creates value only when connected to trustworthy data, legitimate standards, owned workflows, response capacity, monitoring, and patient partnership\. It also shows how organizations can reduce avoidable variation, govern AI responsibly, design for bioequity, and measure return on learning rather than isolated project gains\. At a moment when health systems are investing heavily in digital transformation while struggling to improve outcomes at sustainable cost, Healthcare That Learns offers a road map for organizations that must learn continuously, act responsibly, and improve care that matters\.

## [THE ROLE OF CUSTOMER SATISFACTION IN MEDIATING THE INFLUENCE OF USER\-GENERATED CONTENT \(UGC\) AND SERVICE QUALITY ON ELECTRONIC WORD\-OF\-MOUTH \(E\-WOM\)](../publications/6986416c030f9061943d.md)

Gede Bagus Nando Khrisnayana Dwi Susila; I Gst\. Ngurah Jaya Agung Widagda K; Putu Saroyini Piartini; Komang Agus Satria Pramudana

Developments in tourism and digital technology have transformed consumer behavior regarding information seeking, accommodation selection, and experience sharing via digital platforms\. Consequently, User\-Generated Content \(UGC\), Service Quality, Customer Satisfaction, and Electronic Word of Mouth \(e\-WOM\) have become critical aspects of the hospitality industry\. Pecatu Guest House has experienced a decline in occupancy rates despite the overall increase in tourist visits to Bali\. Furthermore, customer reviews on digital platforms reveal mixed assessments regarding service quality and the guest experience\. This study aims to analyze the influence of UGC and Service Quality on e\-WOM, with Customer Satisfaction serving as a mediating variable at Pecatu Guest House\. A quantitative approach utilizing a survey method was employed\. The study population consisted of 4,598 customers who stayed at Pecatu Guest House between 2022 and 2024\. The sample was selected using probability sampling—specifically, simple random sampling\. Based on 33 indicators and a ratio of six respondents per indicator, a total of 198 respondents were obtained\. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling\-Partial Least Squares \(SEM\-PLS\)\. The results indicate that UGC has a positive and significant effect on both e\-WOM and Customer Satisfaction\. Service Quality also exerts a positive and significant influence on e\-WOM and Customer Satisfaction\. Additionally, Customer Satisfaction has a positive and significant impact on e\-WOM\. Furthermore, Customer Satisfaction was found to mediate the effects of both UGC and Service Quality on e\-WOM, demonstrating a complementary partial mediation relationship\. The findings suggest that enhancing the quality of user\-generated information and service quality can strengthen customer satisfaction and foster positive e\-WOM\. This study offers implications for Pecatu Guest House, highlighting the need to ensure alignment between digital information and actual service, improve the customer experience, and encourage customers to share positive experiences\.

## [A general recipe for data\-adaptive anytime\-valid envelopes for iterative algorithms](../publications/69a34994ca638736d2a8.md)

Soham Bonnerjee; Aaditya Ramdas

Most convergence guarantees for iterative stochastic algorithms are stated at a fixed iteration count and do not justify stopping at a data\-dependent time\. Recent work has constructed anytime\-valid envelopes that do, but deterministic envelopes are typically too conservative for practical stopping, and existing data\-adaptive ones are derived case\-by\-case, each coupling a specific algorithm to a specific noise model and boundary construction\. This paper provides a general recipe for constructing such anytime\-valid data\-adaptive boundaries for a large class of iterative algorithms\. Performance measures of many of these algorithms satisfy a one\-step recursion that reduces the entire error analysis to a single general requirement: time\-uniform concentration for predictably weighted sums of noise\. We formalize this through a strongly adapted sub\-$ψ$ condition, and derive off\-the\-shelf boundary constructions via continuous and discrete mixtures, stitching, and product betting martingales\. We show how these boundaries can be directly coupled with a separate algorithmic analysis that derives the one\-step recursion to provide a class of readymade anytime\-valid envelopes across diverse settings including stochastic gradient descent \(SGD\), temporal difference learning, and Bures\-Wasserstein SGD\. In particular, for SGD, our framework either recovers or significantly sharpens every existing envelope we are aware of\. Our constructions come with explicit implementation details and are substantiated by numerical experiments\.

## [Stacking Ensemble Learning for Copper Grade Prediction at the Sungun Porphyry Copper Deposit: Statistical Performance Versus Geological Coherence](../publications/69a37cb3a3cee403d450.md)

Constanza Núñez; Nadia Mery; Mohammad Maleki

Mineral resource estimation has traditionally relied on geostatistical techniques such as Ordinary Kriging \(OK\), which explicitly account for spatial continuity but may introduce smoothing effects and require extensive manual parameterization\. In parallel, Machine Learning \(ML\) methods have emerged as flexible alternatives capable of modeling complex nonlinear relationships; however, their ability to generate geologically reliable block models remains insufficiently evaluated\. This study assesses stacking ensemble learning for copper grade prediction at the Sungun porphyry deposit \(Iran\), comparing its performance against individual ML models, including Artificial Neural Networks \(ANNs\), Random Forest \(RF\), and Support Vector Regression \(SVR\), as well as domain\-constrained and global unconstrained OK\. Two ML scenarios were evaluated, using spatial coordinates either alone or in combination with mineralogical domains\. Model performance was assessed using random and spatially buffered cross\-validation together with spatial and geological validation criteria\. Under random cross\-validation, RF and Stacking 1 \(ANN–RF–SVR\) achieved the highest statistical performance among the ML models; however, all ML approaches showed substantial performance deterioration under spatially buffered cross\-validation, indicating that the stronger performance observed under random cross\-validation was strongly influenced by spatial autocorrelation\. The incorporation of mineralogical domains had a limited and model\-dependent effect under random cross\-validation, but improved the spatially buffered cross\-validation R2 values of all ML models, although these remained negative, while also enhancing geological compartmentalization and boundary preservation\. Stacking 2 \(ANN–SVR\) produced the most geologically coherent ensemble model, although it overestimated tonnage relative to the domain\-constrained OK benchmark\. Overall, within the evaluated framework, the results indicate that predictive accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating ML\-based grade\-prediction models and that spatial and geological validation criteria provide essential complementary information for assessing the reliability of the resulting block models\.

## [Assessing Cognitive Workload using Electroencephalogram \(EEG\) in Technology\-Mediated Work Environments](../publications/69b49ff2d154b735be02.md)

Saman Jamshid Nezhad Zahabi

Human–machine interaction has expanded rapidly with the growing integration of automation, robotics, and intelligent systems into industrial and training environments\. Emerging technologies such as Augmented Reality \(AR\) and Virtual Reality \(VR\) are designed to enhance these interactions by providing immersive training, real\-time task guidance, and enriched visual feedback\. While these technologies have the potential to improve efficiency, safety, and learning outcomes, they also impose additional cognitive demands on operators who must process complex visual and spatial information while maintaining attention and situational awareness\. In complex collaborative and immersive work environments, operators are often required to interact simultaneously with humans, machines, and digital interfaces\. As human information\-processing capacity is inherently limited, assessing cognitive workload is critical for understanding how operators respond to technology\-mediated systems and for designing systems that better align with human capabilities and limitations\. This research examines changes in operators&\#x27; cognitive workload within three rapidly evolving technology\-mediated environments: VR\-based training, triadic human–robot\-human collaboration, and AR\-assisted teleoperation\. Rather than relying solely on subjective self\-reports, this research employs neurophysiological measures, specifically electroencephalography \(EEG\), to assess workload during task performance\. To examine cognitive workload across these technology\-mediated environments, three separate studies were conducted\. Study 1 investigated cognitive workload among novice forklift drivers in a VR\-based training environment\. In a within\-subject experiment involving 20 novice drivers, workload variations were analyzed across different task difficulty levels and repeated training sessions\. Results indicated that both subjective assessments \(NASA\-TLX\) and objective measures \(EEG\) effectively distinguished workload across varying levels of task difficulty\. However, an additional training session did not substantially reduce the workload experienced by novice operators\. Study 2 evaluated cognitive workload during triadic human\-robot collaboration involving a teleoperator and an onsite worker performing a collaborative assembly task with and without robotic assistance\. Thirty\-two participants were recruited and assigned to either teleoperator or onsite roles\. We also evaluated whether manipulating the task demands of onsite participants indirectly affected teleoperator workload\. Findings demonstrated that EEG effectively detected workload differences across collaboration conditions and showed that robotic assistance reduced cognitive workload\. However, no evidence of workload transfer from the onsite participant to the teleoperator was observed when the onsite task demands were manipulated\. Study 3 assessed the effects of AR\-based visual augmentation and material visibility on teleoperator workload\. We developed an AR interface that overlays the real\-time posture and position of the onsite participant onto the teleoperator&\#x27;s view\. In a within\-subject study involving 17 participants, workload was evaluated using NASA\-TLX, EEG, and eye tracking measures under AR guidance and traditional multi\-camera conditions, as well as under varying levels of material occlusion\. Results showed that AR guidance reduced workload, while Occlusion level influenced EEG patterns and gaze behavior, suggesting adaptive visual information\-processing strategies under limited visibility conditions\. Overall, these studies demonstrate the value of multimodal approaches for assessing cognitive workload in technology\-mediated environments\. In particular, the findings highlight the sensitivity of EEG in capturing subtle variations in operator workload, with different EEG measures responding to changes in task demands and system design across VR training, human–robot collaboration, and AR\-assisted teleoperation\. While increased task difficulty consistently elevated workload, supportive technologies such as robotic assistance and AR guidance effectively reduced cognitive demands\. These findings underscore the importance of integrating cognitive factors into the design of technology\-driven systems to enhance human–machine interaction, improve operator performance, and support safer and more effective work environments\.

## [Acquired Palmoplantar Keratoderma as a Rare Adverse Drug Reaction to Losartan: A Case Report](../publications/69b6ae39e9d123301f2e.md)

Rahul Garg; Sawan Malhan

Palmoplantar keratoderma \(PPK\) is a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by excessive epidermal thickening of the palms and Insert “and soles, and” may rarely arise as an adverse drug reaction\. Drug\-induced PPK has been most frequently linked to targeted kinase inhibitors; its association with angiotensin receptor blockers \(ARBs\) remains exceedingly rare and underrecognized\. We report a 34\-year\-old woman with hypertension who developed progressive diffuse hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles approximately 2 months after initiation of losartan 50 mg once daily, with lesions present for approximately 2 months at the time of presentation\. Hereditary, infectious, metabolic, and malignant etiologies were systematically excluded\. Skin biopsy was declined by the patient’s family\. Following discontinuation of losartan, appreciable clinical improvement was observed at 4 weeks, substantial improvement at 8 weeks, and complete resolution of palmoplantar hyperkeratosis at 12 weeks\. Causality assessment using the Naranjo scale and World Health Organization–Uppsala Monitoring Centre \(WHO\-UMC\) criteria supported a probable causal relationship\. This is the second published case of losartan\-induced PPK in the English literature and corroborates the probable role of angiotensin II type 1 \(AT1\) receptor blockade in acquired PPK\. Clinicians prescribing ARBs should be aware of this rare but recognizable cutaneous complication\.

## [A Lightweight Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Parameterized Human Behavior Classification](../publications/69b8d1ab8e130b2db273.md)

Jyoti Gupta; Brijesh Kumar \-; Ashish Pandey

Human\-behavior modeling is commonly approached through video, sensor, handwriting, or textual signals, yet many practical settings require a lightweight model that can operate on structured behavioral responses\. This study develops a hybrid supervised\-learning framework that combines logistic regression with transparent rule\-based decision logic for binary classification of parameterized behavioral\-response patterns\. The experimental dataset described in the source study contains 500 questionnaire\-derived instances represented by ten behavioral attributes, including responsibility, gratitude, patience and listening, positive attitude, respectfulness, confidence, humility, kindness and compassion, honesty, and justice and integrity\. A stratified 90:10 train\-test protocol was used, supplemented by five\-fold cross\-validation\. The source confusion matrix for the 50\-instance hold\-out set contains 24 true negatives, 24 true positives, one false positive, and one false negative, corresponding to 96% hold\-out accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, and specificity\. Five\-fold cross\-validation is reported at 97\.00 ± 0\.63%, while ROC\-AUC is reported as 0\.985\. The proposed approach is computationally simple and interpretable, but its outputs must be treated as probabilistic decision\-support signals rather than deterministic judgments about individuals\. The study therefore emphasizes human oversight, privacy safeguards, external validation, and bias auditing before any real\-world deployment\.

## [A Comparative Review and Benchmarking Evaluation of Step Detection Methods for Longitudinal Gait Assessment](../publications/69bd3bcf6bad3c10a5e9.md)

Alejandro Ena; José Javier Serrano Olmedo; Claudia Mazzà; Shibeshih Mitiku Belachew; Óscar Reyes

Gait analysis based on inertial measurement units \(IMUs\) enables scalable longitudinal gait assessment, with step detection as a foundational component\. However, an understanding of available step detection methods and their comparative performance across sensor placements, clinical populations, and real\-world environments remains limited\. This paper addresses this gap through a twofold contribution\. First, a structured taxonomic review organises the landscape into six families—rule\-based heuristics, phase portrait, template matching, time–frequency analysis, adaptive oscillators, and machine learning—characterising the trade\-offs of each in terms of noise robustness, generalisability, and computational efficiency\. Second, nine algorithms drawn from five of these families, all but phase portrait, are benchmarked across three large datasets encompassing healthy adults and people with mobility\-impairing conditions such as Parkinson’s disease and multiple sclerosis, at multiple sensor placements under both controlled laboratory and free\-living conditions\. Accuracy depended on sensor placement, gait pathology and recording environment: step detection proved reliable in structured laboratory settings across most sensor locations and clinical cohorts, whereas unsupervised free\-living monitoring produced a substantial degradation for most algorithms\. Over all conditions, the three evaluated time–frequency methods obtained the best average ranks for detection accuracy, step\-duration error and cadence error\.

## [Chatbot as a Feedback Partner: An Applied Linguistics Study on AI\-Mediated Corrective Feedback in Enhancing EFL Learners&\#x27; Writing Accuracy and Revision Behavior](../publications/69c07e621bdae78e808e.md)

Muh Zaky Rahmat Dany\.S

This study investigates the role of AI chatbot\-generated corrective feedback in enhancing the writing accuracy and revision behavior of EFL undergraduate learners\. Employing a descriptive qualitative design grounded in Applied Linguistics, the research involved undergraduate students who exhibited persistent grammatical errors, limited revision strategies, and infrequent access to individualized writing feedback\. Data were gathered through multiple drafts of argumentative paragraphs, chatbot\-generated feedback logs, and semi\-structured interviews conducted across several feedback\-revision cycles\. The findings indicate substantial improvement across four indicators: grammatical accuracy, depth of revision, error noticing, and learner autonomy in the editing process\. Learners progressively shifted from surface\-level corrections, such as spelling and punctuation, toward meaning\-level revisions involving clause structure, cohesion, and argument development\. The chatbot&\#x27;s explicit, metalinguistic feedback encouraged learners to notice recurring error patterns and apply self\-correction in subsequent drafts\. Learners&\#x27; dependence on external correction gradually decreased as their confidence in self\-editing increased\. These findings support corrective feedback theory, the noticing hypothesis, and computer\-mediated writing feedback frameworks, which emphasize that written accuracy develops through repeated, learner\-engaged feedback cycles\. This study contributes a new perspective by positioning the AI chatbot not as an automatic error\-correction tool, but as an interactive feedback partner that scaffolds learners&\#x27; revision competence\. Chatbot\-mediated feedback can therefore serve as a practical alternative for sustained writing improvement in contexts where individualized teacher feedback is limited\.

## [A Novel Red\-Eared Slider Optimisation Algorithm Based on A Two\-Stage Basking–Foraging Strategy](../publications/69cd74354e9de708640c.md)

H\. Hammod Helal Al\-Badrei; N\. Ali Majeed Alhammadi; A\. Rajab Kadhim; Z\. Ali Abdulabbas

Purpose: This study aims to develop a novel nature\-inspired metaheuristic optimisation algorithm based on the semi\-aquatic behaviour of the red\-eared slider \(Trachemys scripta elegans\)\. Design/Methodology/Approach: An experimental research design was adopted\. The proposed algorithm models two behavioural stages of the red\-eared slider: “foraging in water” as an exploration mechanism and “sunbathing on a platform” as an exploitation mechanism\. The agent population adaptively switches between these two behavioural states\. RESO is evaluated using 23 single\-objective benchmark functions with different dimensions and compared with Particle Swarm Optimisation \(PSO\) and Genetic Algorithm \(GA\)\. Performance was analysed descriptively through convergence\-curve comparison in terms of solution quality, convergence speed, and robustness against local optima\. Research Limitation: The evaluation is limited to 23 standard single\-objective benchmark functions and is based on convergence curves without inferential statistical testing; further validation with statistical tests and on real\-world optimisation problems is required\. Findings: The experimental results indicate that RESO achieves faster convergence and better final solutions than PSO and GA on many benchmark functions, with competitive results on most others\. The combination of adaptive switching and spatial memory also supports effective exploration of the search space and reduces the tendency to become trapped in local optima\. Practical Implication: The proposed framework provides a basis for applying the algorithm to engineering, industrial, planning, control, and path optimisation problems\. Social Implication: The development of effective optimisation techniques may indirectly support more efficient computational solutions for complex practical problems\. Originality/Value: The study introduces a two\-stage optimisation framework inspired by the behavioural cycle of the red\-eared slider and integrates adaptive behavioural switching with a spatial memory of promising platforms, offering a behaviour\-driven way to balance exploration and exploitation in metaheuristic search\.

## [PENINGKATAN KESADARAN PELAJAR TERHADAP PENGGUNAAN SMARTPHONE, MEDIA SOSIAL, DAN KEAMANAN DIGITAL](../publications/69ce9fb765532115ea29.md)

Bintang Fajar Ruslita Putra; Rahma Nadila; Delfi Apriansyah; Amal Fathullah Al Arsy; Muhammad Irwansyah

Perkembangan teknologi digital menjadikan smartphone dan media sosial sebagai bagian penting dalam kehidupan pelajar, tetapi penggunaannya juga menghadirkan berbagai risiko, seperti pelanggaran privasi, cyberbullying, phishing, penyebaran informasi yang tidak benar, dan penggunaan secara berlebihan\. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkuat kesadaran pelajar mengenai penggunaan smartphone dan media sosial secara aman, sehat, etis, dan bertanggung jawab\. Kegiatan dilaksanakan kepada 175 pelajar kelas XII, terdiri atas 120 pelajar SMA Negeri 1 Aek Kuasan dan 55 pelajar SMK YASPENDA Pulau Rakyat\. Metode yang digunakan adalah pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif melalui penyampaian materi secara langsung menggunakan presentasi, interaksi dan pertanyaan sederhana, observasi respons peserta, dokumentasi, serta evaluasi internal\. Materi meliputi manfaat smartphone dan media sosial, ancaman digital, perlindungan data pribadi, cyberbullying, phishing, penipuan daring, verifikasi informasi, etika bermedia sosial, privasi, jejak digital, dan penggunaan smartphone secara bijak\. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pelajar mengikuti kegiatan dengan antusias, aktif merespons materi dan pertanyaan, serta menunjukkan pemahaman berdasarkan pengamatan selama kegiatan\. Namun, karena tidak dilakukan pre\-test dan post\-test, perubahan tingkat kesadaran digital belum dapat diukur secara statistik\. Kegiatan ini menunjukkan pentingnya edukasi digital yang dilakukan secara berkelanjutan di lingkungan sekolah\.

## [Stuart, Michael T\.: Towards a dual process epistemology of imagination](../publications/69d6f288ca527ed24f8f.md)



\_Synthese\_ \(2\):1\-22\. 2019Sometimes we learn through the use of imagination\. The epistemology of imagination asks how this is possible\. One barrier to progress on this question has been a lack of agreement on how to characterize imagination; for example, is imagination a mental state, ability, character trait, or cognitive process? This paper argues that we should characterize imagination as a cognitive ability, exercises of which are cognitive processes\. Following dual process theories of cognition developed in cognitive science, the set of imaginative processes is then divided into two kinds: one that is unconscious, uncontrolled, and effortless, and another that is conscious, controlled, and effortful\. This paper outlines the different epistemological strengths and weaknesses of the two kinds of imaginative process, and argues that a dual process model of imagination helpfully resolves or clarifies issues in the epistemology of imagination and the closely related epistemology of thought experiments\. \(direct link \)

## [GENOTOXIC IMPURITIES IN PHARMACEUTICALS: ADVANCES IN RISK ASSESSMENT, ANALYTICAL STRATEGIES, REGULATORY PERSPECTIVES, AND CONTROL APPROACHES](../publications/69d8b786671db8aca968.md)

N\. Hari Priya1, V\. Vatsnavika1, T\. Himaja1, M\. Hemanth Kumar1, B\. Harihanth Desay1, P\. Srinivasa Babu2, A\. Bhavani Sailu1\*

Genotoxic impurities \(GTIs\) are trace\-level contaminants capable of damaging DNA and increasing the potential for mutation and carcinogenesis\. They may arise from starting materials, reagents, catalysts, intermediates, by\-products, degradation pathways, manufacturing operations, or packaging interactions\. Their control is therefore a critical component of pharmaceutical quality assurance\. This review summarizes the major sources and classes of GTIs, mechanisms of DNA damage, toxicological risk\-assessment approaches, regulatory expectations, in silico prediction, analytical strategies, method validation, genotoxicity testing, and practical control measures\. Particular attention is given to ICH M7\(R2\), the Threshold of Toxicological Concern \(TTC\), Acceptable Intake \(AI\), \(Q\)SAR, read\-across and weight\-of\-evidence approaches\. Modern analytical platforms such as LC\-MS/MS, GC\-MS/MS, high\-resolution mass spectrometry, ICP\-MS and ICP\-OES provide sensitive detection, while optimized sample preparation and analytical quality by design improve method performance\. Quality by Design \(QbD\), Process Analytical Technology \(PAT\), impurity purge studies, green chemistry and continuous manufacturing support prevention rather than relying only on end\-product testing\. Nitrosamines, including drug substance\-related nitrosamines, remain an important area because of their very low acceptable exposure levels and their occurrence through synthesis, degradation and storage\. Emerging approaches involving artificial intelligence, digital laboratories, chemometrics, metabolomics, portable devices and real\-time release testing are expected to strengthen lifecycle impurity control\.

## [Context\- and Cell\-Dependent Roles of S1PR1 in Atherosclerosis: Therapeutic Implications of Selective S1PR1 Modulation](../publications/69dafa24972fc0bf1de1.md)

Thang H\. Nguyen; Shih\-Chang Hsu; Ching\-Lu Chen; Cuong Duong; Thang Vu; Soan Hoang; Quyet Nguyen; An Thi Thu Bui; Cong Nguyen; Binh Tran

Abstract Sphingosine 1\-phosphate receptor 1 \(S1PR1\) regulates vascular homeostasis and immune function, but its role in atherosclerosis has remained controversial because activating the same receptor produces divergent effects across cell types\. This review synthesizes evidence on S1PR1 signaling in endothelial cells, macrophages, and vascular smooth muscle cells, and proposes a context\-dependent framework, shaped by cell type, ligand presentation, and inflammatory environment, to reconcile these conflicting findings\. In endothelial cells, S1PR1 preserves barrier integrity and limits leukocyte recruitment when activated by ApoM\-bound HDL\-S1P\. In macrophages, it promotes anti\-inflammatory polarization, cholesterol efflux, and efferocytosis via PI3K/Akt and LXR signaling\. In vascular smooth muscle cells, by contrast, injury\-induced S1PR1 drives proliferation and neointimal hyperplasia through IL\-6/STAT3 signaling\. This framework also explains the variable efficacy of S1PR1\-targeting drugs, favoring selective, non\-degrading agonists over functional antagonists, though murine\-to\-human differences in circulating S1P biology remain a key translational barrier\. Future therapeutic strategies should prioritize cell\-selective delivery, biased or non\-degrading agonists, restoration of ApoM\-mediated signaling, and biomarker\-guided patient selection to maximize vascular protection while avoiding adverse remodeling\.

## [Serum Metabolic Differences Across Glucose Metabolic States Using Untargeted UPLC\-HRMS Metabolomics](../publications/69edd7d08749838c100e.md)

Zhulidezi Bahati; Runze Zou; Zhongda Zeng; Wei Duan

Abstract Insulin resistance \(IR\) and impaired glucose regulation \(IGR\) involve metabolic disturbances beyond changes in blood glucose\. This cross\-sectional study applied untargeted UPLC\-HRMS metabolomics to serum from 109 participants across normal glucose tolerance \(NGT\), IR, IGR, and type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\)\. An integrated analysis of 457 putatively annotated metabolites combined multivariate statistics, clustering, and machine learning to characterize differences among glycometabolic groups and assess the discriminatory information\. Pairwise comparisons respectively identified 60, 42, and 59 differential metabolites for NGT vs IR, IR vs IGR, and IGR vs T2DM, including five shared across all comparisons\. LASSO and random forest evaluated fixed differential\-metabolite panels through stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation repeated ten times and 1,000 label permutations\. The corresponding pooled AUC ranges were 0\.918–0\.923, 0\.995–0\.996, and 0\.828–0\.950\. Because panel selection preceded cross\-validation, these estimates describe within\-cohort discrimination rather than generalizable predictive performance\. Pathway analysis of the union of differential metabolites indicated nominal enrichment of lysine degradation and nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism\. Shared metabolites also showed associations with clinical measures of glucose homeostasis and insulin response\. These findings characterize distinct yet partly shared metabolic features across glycometabolic states and provide candidates for targeted confirmation and independent longitudinal validation\.
