## [Implementing Cloud Computing Accounting Software in the CCMAS Business Education Undergraduates Programme for Employability Skills Development in Rivers State Universities](../publications/69f90350491b1024b92a.md)

Ruth Chioma Ejekwu; Philip Festus Ukata

This study evaluated the implementation of cloud computing accounting software in the Core Curriculum and Minimum Academic Standards \(CCMAS\) Business Education undergraduate programme for employability skills development in Rivers State\-owned universities\. A descriptive survey research design was adopted, focusing on three cloud accounting software applications: Xero, Zoho Books, and Sage\. The population comprised 127 Accounting Business Education undergraduates from Rivers State University \(RSU\) and Ignatius Ajuru University of Education \(IAUE\), with 113 valid questionnaires retrieved and used for analysis\. Data were collected using a structured and validated questionnaire Implementing Cloud Accounting Software for Employability Skills Development Questionnaire \(ICASESDQ\), which had a Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient of 0\.82\. Descriptive statistics \(mean and standard deviation\) were used to answer the research questions and measure the spread in respondents’ opinions, while an independent\-samples t\-test was employed to test three null hypotheses at a 0\.05 level of significance\. The findings revealed that the extent of implementing Xero, Zoho Books, and Sage accounting software leading to the development of automated bank statement reconciliation, electronic bookkeeping management, and electronic payroll employability skills was very low in both universities\. The results of the t\-tests showed no significant differences between RSU and IAUE students regarding implementing the three accounting software applications\. The study concluded that cloud accounting software in the Business Education curriculum has not been adequately implemented for employability skills development\. It was recommended that Rivers State\-owned universities should provide structured practical training for undergraduate students using Xero to develop automated bank statement reconciliation skills\. This includes hands\-on exercises in inputting transactions, matching entries, and generating reconciliation reports to ensure students gain workplace\-ready competence\.

## [Compressive strength and gel formation of enhanced geopolymer with addition of nanomaterials – a review](../publications/6a0b3c47433766ee88e2.md)

Shadman Rahman Sabab; U\. Johnson Alengaram; Chiu Chuen Onn; Saznizam Sazmee Sinoh

Nanomaterial reinforcement has emerged as a pivotal strategy to overcome the mechanical and durability limitations of traditional geopolymer binders\. This review systematically evaluates the integration of zero\- to one\-dimensional nanomaterials, like graphene oxide, carbon nanotubes, and nano silica, etc\., into geopolymer matrices synthesized from diverse industrial precursors such as fly ash, slag, and red mud\. The fundamental mechanisms of reinforcement, specifically nucleation, matrix densification, and micro\-crack bridging, are analyzed to illustrate the transition from brittle to ductile behavior\. Beyond mechanical enhancement, the critical roles of dispersion techniques, particle size, and optimal dosages in mitigating workability trade\-offs and agglomeration are examined\. This work delineates the relationship between microstructural evolution and crack\-arrest mechanisms through a systematic evaluation of SEM, XRD, and Nanoindentation results reported in recent literature\. Furthermore, the review explores innovative processing trends, such as the synergy between nano\-additives and rapid microwave curing, which significantly reduces energy consumption compared to conventional thermal methods\. Finally, industrial scaling challenges, cost\-effectiveness, and the environmental life\-cycle of nano\-engineered composites are addressed\. By identifying critical research gaps in multi\-nanomaterial synergy and standardized durability testing, this paper provides a strategic roadmap for the development of high\-performance, resilient, and sustainable geopolymer infrastructure\.

## [Policymakers&\#x27; Presentation Strategy and Message Framing: Effects on Trust and Compliance in Public Crises](../publications/6a11339a55f4f379cd05.md)

Min Kim; Taewon Suh

ABSTRACT During public crises, strategic communication plays a pivotal role in shaping public compliance by influencing how information is framed and presented\. This study investigates how policymakers&\#x27; communication strategies, specifically positive versus negative presentation approaches, affect public compliance during a public crisis\. Drawing on collected panel data, this study conducted sentiment analysis of governors&\#x27; press releases and linked these to behavioural indicators of compliance in a PLS‐SEM\. The results identify approval‐based institutional trust as a mediating mechanism connecting communication tone to vaccination uptake\. Useful information flow by vaccine information‐seeking intensity and positive presentation tone had limited direct associations with uptake but were positively associated with the institutional trust proxy\. Negative presentation tone was also positively associated with institutional trust and uptake\. Because transparency was not directly measured, these findings concern message valence and do not establish that transparent disclosure produced the observed relationships\. Overall, the findings suggest that trust‐mediated communication, regardless of valence, can optimise compliance while maintaining institutional credibility, offering evidence‐based insights for effective crisis governance\.

## [Development and cost\-utility analysis of a predictive model to reduce central venous catheterization in patients with shock: study design and analysis plan, amendment 1 \(Alberta 2012 to 2021, external validation in MIMIC\-IV\)](../publications/6a15e9b72fe86095d80a.md)

Jasper C Ho; Nasim Zamir; Elizabeth Munroe; Tiago V Pereira; Federico Angriman; Naheed Jivraj; Akash Goel; Nick Bosch; H\. Tom Stelfox; Hannah Wunsch; Bijan Teja

This version adds the external validation in MIMIC\-IV version 3\.1: the performance of the equations deposited in the previous version, saved with their checksums before any model was fitted to MIMIC\-IV outcomes, then the recalibrated equations\. This version adds the development results, deposited before the external validation is run \(Section VII of the plan\): the availability table and the frozen list of candidate predictors \(made before any outcome was derived\), the development equations of every model with their bootstrap settings and optimism\-corrected performance, the final model and its points score, and the temporal validation within Alberta\. The equations in this version are the ones applied, unchanged, in MIMIC\-IV\. This amends the analysis plan registered on the Open Science Framework on June 23, 2025 \(https://doi\.org/10\.17605/OSF\.IO/G93JA\)\. The attached version of October 17, 2026 lists the changes and the reasons for them in its Section XII\. In summary: Data\. The model is developed in Alberta ICU data from July 2012 to December 2021: the eCritical Alberta extract of the registered plan \(2012 to 2018, 31 ICUs\) and a later extract of the same clinical information system \(2019 to 2021\)\. It is validated externally in MIMIC\-IV version 3\.1 \(Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, 2008 to 2022\)\. A 2012 to 2025 data cut considered in an unregistered revision \(October 1, 2026\) is not used\. Validation\. Instead of a random split, development with bootstrap internal validation in the Alberta patients; the fixed equations are deposited \(as a new version of this record\) and then validated once in MIMIC\-IV, the primary result; recalibration if needed; a temporal validation within Alberta \(2012 to 2018 to 2019 to 2021\)\. Time of prediction and population\. Every eligibility criterion is assessed 3 h after vasopressor initiation \(t3\): an infusion running at t3; no central venous catheter at vasopressor start; no ECLS; no comfort or medical\-care goals\-of\-care designation in effect; dose not already above 0\.3 mcg/kg/min; one stay per patient\. Outcome\. Acceptable peripheral delivery = maximum norepinephrine\-equivalent dose \(sustained 30 minutes\) of 0\.3 mcg/kg/min or less from t3 to 72 h; the registered outcome \(which also required 72 h or less of cumulative vasopressor infusion\) is analysed and reported beside it\. Predictors and missing data\. Predictor sets A \(dose trajectory in the first 3 h\), a middle set, B and C; availability rules fixed before the outcome is derived; complete\-case analysis with a multiple\-imputation sensitivity analysis\. Respiratory rate, pulse oximetry and serum bicarbonate are not used \(not recorded in the extracts\); invasive and non\-invasive ventilation are separate candidates\. Modelling\. Lasso logistic regression with the one\-standard\-error rule and an unpenalized refit; an unpenalized logistic comparator; one flexible lasso comparator instead of the three machine\-learning models; a numerical rule for the final model; minimum sample sizes by Riley et al\.; AUROC from continuous probabilities, calibration, net benefit\. Simulation\. Model\-informed conversion to a central catheter at 3 h when the predicted probability of an event is at or above the risk threshold \(0\.25, 0\.5 and 0\.75; the registered wording was reversed\), simulated in the base case and the highly resourced vascular access scenario of the decision model, each with and without a delay between the decision to convert and catheter placement, and compared with its three strategies, with a two\-way threshold analysis of the sensitivity and specificity a model would need\. Work done before this amendment: models using the dose trajectory only were fitted in the 2012 to 2018 extract in 2025 with a split\-sample design \(results seen; superseded\); descriptive checks were run in the 2012 to 2025 data cut, which is not used\. For this study nothing has been done in the 2019 to 2021 extract or in MIMIC\-IV; aggregate descriptions of both Alberta extracts made for other studies \(inventories, file coverage, record counts\) were seen, with no outcome of this study\. Ethics: University of Calgary Conjoint Health Research Ethics Board, REB19\-0959 \(Alberta extracts\); MIMIC\-IV under the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement\.

## [Write right\! Writing in Swedish syllabi and National Tests from primary to upper secondary education](../publications/6a1f589063bd62b186f4.md)

Sara Silverdal; Erika Sturk

Abstract This article examines the underlying beliefs about writing and learning to write as reflected in the curricula of the Swedish as L1 and L2 subjects in Swedish compulsory and upper secondary school\. It also analyses the National Tests in Swedish at all levels and compares them with the findings from the curriculum analysis and discusses the alignment\. Drawing on Ivanič&\#x27;s Discourses of Writing and Learning to Write , the study shows that when the Swedish syllabi are compared with the National Tests, writing appears in a narrower form in the tests, reflecting only a few discourses and showing a progression mainly toward genre‐based writing\. ## [Association of the metabolic signature of sleep patterns with breast cancer risk: a prospective cohort study](../publications/6a3270a7a98ef8ffa36c.md)

QiMei Yang; Fang Ai; Yalan Zhao; Zihan Wang; Zhaohong Bi; Rui Ma; Dabao Xu

Background Existing evidence regarding the association between sleep patterns and breast cancer development remains inconsistent\. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between sleep patterns and breast cancer risk while examining the potential mediating effects of sleep score\-related metabolic signatures\. Methods A total of 220,089 participants from the UK Biobank study were analyzed\. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the relationships among the sleep score \(based on 5 sleep factors\), genetic risk \(based on 22 variants\), metabolic signature \(derived from 251 metabolites\), and breast cancer incidence, adjusting for age, BMI, sociodemographic, and lifestyle factors\. Mediation analysis was used to test whether the metabolic signature mediated the association between the sleep score and breast cancer risk\. Results A total of 8459 incident breast cancer cases \(3\.84% of the cohort\) were identified during a median follow\-up of 11\.6 years\. Compared with individuals with a sleep score of 5 points, those with a score of 0–1 points had a significantly greater risk of developing breast cancer \(HR = 1\.30, 95% CI = 1\.11–1\.52\)\. The sleep\-related metabolic signature was also associated with elevated breast cancer risk \(HR = 1\.62, 95% CI = 1\.32–1\.99\)\. Mediation analysis revealed that the metabolic signature accounted for 13\.5% of the observed association between the sleep score and the incidence of breast cancer\. Conclusion Maintaining healthy sleep patterns may lower the risk of breast cancer irrespective of genetic predispositions\. The metabolic signature partially mediated the association between the sleep score and breast cancer development\.

## [Development and Preliminary Evaluation of an Ethnoscience Project\-Based Learning Module on Virgin Coconut Oil Production and Creative Thinking](../publications/6a33e09aaa11c6b4af25.md)

lalu Syukran Muhsin; Karnan Karnan

Locally grounded science projects may support creative thinking by connecting scientific inquiry with familiar cultural practices\. This study developed a module integrating ethnoscience and project\-based learning through virgin coconut oil production and examined preliminary changes in Grade VII students’ creative thinking\. Development followed the Four\-D model, with three experts reviewing the instructional materials and assessment\. Feasibility was examined through teacher and student responses and lesson observations\. A nonequivalent pretest–posttest comparison involved an experimental class \(n = 32\) and a control class \(n = 30\) at SMPN 1 Pujut, Central Lombok, Indonesia, over three meetings\. Product\-review scores ranged from 68% to 77%, teacher response scores from 74% to 84%, and student response scores from 68% to 77%; observed implementation increased from 80\.0% to 87\.5%\. Mean creative\-thinking scores increased from 63 to 85 in the experimental class and from 62 to 70 in the control class\. Reported overall normalized gains were 0\.61 \(moderate\) and 0\.21 \(low\), respectively\. The findings suggest the module’s potential to support creative thinking\. However, these outcomes remain descriptive because individual\-level scores and dispersion estimates were unavailable; stronger conclusions require auditable individual\-level data and baseline\-adjusted analyses\.

## [Association between the triacylglycerol–glucose index, TyG\-BMI and hypertension in children and adolescents: a cross\-sectional study with machine\-learning\-based risk stratification](../publications/6a462ae996e167313a6c.md)

Jialiang Zhu; Chen Zhang; Jialin Sun; Huiyu Du; Wenxin Zhao; Gang Tian; Jingge Zhao; Dandan Tian; Mengwei Wang; Zhanfeng Liu; Min Liu; Yibin Hao

Background Hypertension in children and adolescents is closely linked to obesity and metabolic disturbance\. The triacylglycerol–glucose \(TyG\) index and TyG\-BMI are surrogate markers of insulin resistance, but their associations with pediatric hypertension remain incompletely characterized\. Methods This cross\-sectional study included 25,886 children and adolescents aged 7–17 years from 18 prefecture\-level cities in Henan Province, China\. The TyG index was calculated as ln\[triglycerides \(mg/dL\) × fasting plasma glucose \(mg/dL\)/2\] and TyG\-BMI as TyG × BMI\. Hypertension was defined as a blood pressure at or above the 95th percentile for age, sex and height \(mean of the last two of three measurements\)\. Logistic regression \(Models I–IV\) estimated odds ratios \(ORs\) per 1 SD and across quartiles, with non\-linearity and effect modification assessed on both scales\. Eleven machine\-learning models were developed on a stratified 70:30 split, with imputation and feature selection performed strictly within the training set and discrimination \(area under the receiver\-operating characteristic curve, AUC\) evaluated in the held\-out validation set\. Results Among 25,886 participants, 1,798 \(6\.95%\) had hypertension\. Median TyG was 8\.05 \(IQR 7\.77–8\.35\) and median TyG\-BMI 154 \(IQR 133–180\)\. Each 1\-SD increment in TyG was associated with hypertension in all models \(Model IV 1\.306 \(95% CI 1\.145–1\.489\)\), and the association was graded across quartiles; TyG\-BMI showed stronger associations \(Model IV 2\.109 \(95% CI 1\.985–2\.241\)\)\. No multiplicative product term was significant after correction, whereas on the additive scale all six relative excess risk estimates were positive with confidence intervals excluding zero\. In the held\-out validation set, discrimination was moderate \(best AUC 0\.7544, 95% CI 0\.7302–0\.7777, for TyG and 0\.7534, 0\.7298–0\.7759, for TyG\-BMI\), and adding either index to the same baseline model already containing BMI increased discrimination only marginally \(about 0\.003 in AUC\)\. Conclusions Higher TyG and TyG\-BMI were associated with hypertension in Chinese children and adolescents, more strongly for TyG\-BMI\. No multiplicative interaction survived correction, but all additive\-scale estimates were positive, so effect modification cannot be excluded\. Machine\-learning models built from routinely available variables showed only moderate discrimination and remain hypothesis\-generating tools for risk stratification rather than validated prediction models\. Longitudinal studies are needed to assess causality\.

## [Mapping smart technologies in sustainable tourism: Knowledge structure, research fronts, and future research directions](../publications/6a4970ec2af032cbf7d0.md)

Nguyen Tuong Lai; Cao Thi Sen

This study maps the development, knowledge structure, research fronts, and emerging directions of research on smart technologies in sustainable tourism\. Bibliographic data were retrieved from Scopus on August 31, 2026\. The initial search identified 645 documents, of which 220 articles and reviews were retained after applying subject\-area, document\-type, language, and relevance criteria\. The study combines performance analysis with science mapping techniques, including reference co\-citation analysis, keyword co\-occurrence analysis, and document\-level bibliographic coupling, using VOSviewer\. The results show that research at the intersection of smart technologies and sustainable tourism has expanded rapidly, particularly since 2024\. The intellectual structure of the field is primarily rooted in smart tourism, smart destinations, Big Data, technology acceptance, and sustainability\-oriented applications of digital technologies\. Keyword co\-occurrence analysis identifies five major thematic clusters: technology\-enabled sustainable tourism and digital transformation; data\-driven tourism management and destination development; smart tourism, machine learning, and sustainability analytics; artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence for sustainable destination management; and digital innovation in smart ecotourism experiences\. Bibliographic coupling further reveals seven contemporary research fronts: digital platforms and sustainable consumption, artificial intelligence\-enabled governance, smart destinations, generative artificial intelligence, data\-driven planning and mobility, Big Data analytics, and smart\-green integration\. Overall, the findings indicate a transition from technology\-centred research towards a broader perspective that emphasises governance capacity, sustainability outcomes, stakeholder coordination, and technological trade\-offs\. The study contributes to the literature by integrating fragmented technological and sustainability\-oriented research streams and identifying future directions concerning artificial intelligence governance, smart\-green integration, destination resilience, responsible tourist behaviour, and evidence\-based destination management\.

## [Institutional readiness for generative artificial intelligence is linked to resource constraints and governance capability in Ghanaian higher education](../publications/6a5b4462f6a71e33ec17.md)

Anthony Aapia Korku Dzidzornu; Xukan Xu

Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) is diffusing across higher education, yet institutional governance struggles to adapt in resource\-constrained settings\. Existing research emphasizes adoption and acceptance, with less attention to how infrastructure and governance shape institutional readiness\. This study investigates GenAI governance in Ghanaian higher education\. A sequential multi\-method design combined the Decision\-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory \(DEMATEL\) and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. DEMATEL drew on a 12\-member expert panel to diagnose perceived influence among institutional factors, while PLS\-SEM independently evaluated a literature\-derived model using 792 student and faculty responses\. Resource Sensitivity \(RS\) emerged as the strongest net\-source factor in the expert\-perceived influence structure \(D−R = \+3\.685\)\. In the PLS\-SEM model, RS was negatively associated with Institutional Readiness \(IR\) \(β = −0\.295\), whereas Technological Governance Architecture \(TGA\) was positively associated with IR \(β = 0\.454\); the model explained 48\.4% of IR variance \(R 2 = 0\.484\)\. The RS → TGA → IR indirect association was significant \(β = −0\.061\), consistent with complementary partial mediation\. AI Literacy \(AIL\) showed no significant direct association with adoption\-related risk, conceptualized as the Adoption–Risk Paradox \(ARP\), but showed a significant indirect association through Perceived Usefulness \(PU\)\. Policy Uncertainty \(PUC\) was positively associated with ARP, whereas TGA was negatively associated with it\. The findings support a Hard–Soft Governance Gap in which infrastructural constraints and governance capability constitute distinct but interconnected conditions of readiness\. Strengthening responsible GenAI integration requires coordinated attention to infrastructure, governance, policy clarity, and responsible\-use practices\.

## [УДОСКОНАЛЕННЯ ІНФОРМАЦІЙНОГО СЕРВІСУ ЦИФРОВИХ БІБЛІОТЕК У КОНТЕКСТІ ЗБЕРЕЖЕННЯ ТА ПОПУЛЯРИЗАЦІЇ КУЛЬТУРНОЇ СПАДЩИНИ](../publications/6a693814d46ea1eb7ee5.md)

Orest Khamula; Sana Strelbycka

Розглянуто вдосконалення інформаційного сервісу цифрових бібліотек як складової збереження, дослідження та популяризації документальної культурної спадщини\. Метою є розроблення концептуальної моделі сервісу, що поєднує інтелектуальний пошук, керовану персоналізацію та контекстне представлення оцифрованих видань, рукописів і архівних документів\. Застосовано системний аналіз, порівняння нормативних підходів до метаданих та концептуальне моделювання\. Запропоновано шестикомпонентну архітектуру з наскрізними вимогами щодо походження об’єкта, атрибуції, правового статусу та зв’язків між колекціями\. Сформовано набір показників для оцінювання релевантності, повноти опису, доступності, прозорості й результативності культурно\-історичного пошуку\. Показано доцільність застосування моделі у бібліотеках, музеях та архівах за умови забезпечення фахової перевірки метаданих і належних процедур цифрового збереження\. Робота має теоретико\-методичний характер; наведені пропозиції потребують подальшої емпіричної апробації\.

## [Patient transfer adaptation through a crisis: The dynamics of a Hospitals Network during the COVID\-19 pandemic](../publications/6a7877b6d19ba5e1731e.md)

Tomás Cicchini; Micaela Gonzalez Dardik; Ariel Salgado; Silvia Kochen; Lisandro Otero; Mariano Goldman; Leonardo Boechi; Inés Caridi

La pandemia de COVID\-19 puso en crisis a los sistemas de salud en todo el mundo\. Muchas infraestructuras sanitarias preexistentes tuvieron que adaptarse a condiciones nuevas y que además, cambiarían continuamente\. Un sistema informático construido al inicio de la pandemia para recolectar, organizar y visualizar información sobre el uso y la disponibilidad de camas en la red hospitalaria ayudó a la Red Sudeste \(que involucra 14 hospitales del sudeste de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, Argentina\) en la gestión de la crisis \(Instituto de Cálculo, 2020; Yacobitti et al\., 2021\)\. Además, el sistema permitió almacenar información sobre los traslados de pacientes que ocurrieron dentro de la Red\. Los traslados representan uno de los rastros digitales posibles para entender cómo se interrelacionaron los hospitales de la red\. Este trabajo estudia la dinámica del funcionamiento de la red a través de los traslados a lo largo de cuatro etapas diferenciadas de la pandemia\.

## [A review of machine learning and the internet of things for remote patient monitoring covering advances challenges and opportunities](../publications/6a7becb3313d91b76cd5.md)

Sumitra Singar; Raghuveer Singh Dhaka; Manmohan Sharma

As Machine Learning \(ML\) and the Internet of Things \(IoT\) have matured, their convergence has placed Remote Patient Monitoring \(RPM\) at the centre of personalized, cost\-effective care\. The present work reviews progress in ML and IoT based RPM, covering how ML is applied within RPM, the principal ML models employed, the IoT infrastructures that underpin it, the use of RPM across different patient populations, the challenges that arise, and the directions the field may take\. After a PRISMA\-guided screening of work indexed in Springer, IEEE, MDPI, ACM, and Elsevier, 101 peer\-reviewed studies published from 2020 onward were retained for a qualitative \(narrative\) synthesis structured around five research questions\. The review is narrative in form yet is carried out under a structured and transparent protocol\. Within the studies examined, RPM was reported to enable real\-time monitoring, cut the number of in\-person hospital visits, and reduce the cost of patient\-centred care, while IoT\- and ML\-based designs that built in privacy\-preserving techniques strengthened data security; across these studies, deep learning and hybrid ML models often reported higher predictive accuracy than conventional approaches, though typically on particular datasets and at greater computational cost\. Across the ten systems compared here, the eight that reported a single determinate figure gave accuracies with a median of 94\.5% \(range 92% to 98%\) and latencies with a median of 265 ms \(range 120 ms to 350 ms\), and not one of them was evaluated at a site other than the one where it was developed, so these numbers describe individual study conditions rather than performance at population level\. Among the obstacles that surface repeatedly are patient adherence, interoperability, scalability, and the protection of data\. On balance, the body of evidence gathered here suggests that RPM built on ML and IoT can make monitoring safer, more flexible, and more anticipatory; reaching that level across whole populations, however, will call for sturdier systems, broader patient participation, and thorough clinical validation\.

## [A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft](../publications/6a8938cea88ed625e4d9.md)

Maxence Faldor; Satinder Singh; Roberta Raileanu

We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon\. Each agent controlled a player via an open\-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in\-game chat and shared memory\. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic\. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves\. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene\. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way\. To our knowledge, this is the first end\-to\-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre\-scouted seeds or other game\-specific tools written by humans\. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day\. Complex real\-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long\-horizon coding and multi\-agent coordination\. We describe the setup, how the run unfolded, the team&\#x27;s strategies \(dividing the work, sharing what they learned, recovering each other&\#x27;s items\), and the limits of the result\.

## [Multi\-omics perspectives on mitochondrial vulnerability in the aging liver: biological modules and translational implications](../publications/6a9d095be5f989bafad8.md)

Hanxi Chen; Weiwei Lu; Kainan Wang; Rui Fang; Sunjae Lee; Shi Chen; Zhengtao Liu

Chronological age alone is an incomplete proxy for the biological heterogeneity of the aging liver\. Mitochondrial vulnerability may provide a mechanistic link between biological aging and the loss of hepatic resilience under metabolic, toxic, and ischemic stress\. Accumulating multi\-omics evidence suggests that hepatic aging is best understood as a set of coordinated pathway\-level disturbances rather than through isolated biomarkers\. Transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic studies converge on five interrelated biological modules: lipid stress, diminished oxidative reserve, proteostatic strain, inflammatory sensitization, and reduced recovery capacity\. These modules are interconnected through impaired mitochondrial metabolic flexibility, redox buffering, organelle crosstalk, and quality\-control mechanisms\. Age\-associated changes may remain partly compensated at baseline but become more apparent during metabolic overload, ischemia–reperfusion injury, cold preservation, or ex vivo machine perfusion\. Building on cross\-species evidence, this Review organizes current findings into a modular framework and examines how mitochondrial vulnerability may connect physiological liver aging with metabolic and ischemic stress\. Transplantation and machine perfusion are discussed as stress\-exposed settings for evaluating candidate tissue\- and fluid\-based readouts\. Although most omics\-derived signals remain insufficiently validated for clinical decision\-making, a mitochondrial\-centered interpretation may help prioritize biologically coherent mechanisms and improve the translational study of aging\-related liver vulnerability\.

## [ОТ ОФИЦИАЛЬНОГО ОПУБЛИКОВАНИЯ К ЭФФЕКТИВНОМУ ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЮ: ЭВОЛЮЦИЯ ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫХ МЕХАНИЗМОВ ОБЕСПЕЧЕНИЯ РАСПРОСТРАНЕНИЯ И ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЯ ПРАВОВОЙ ИНФОРМАЦИИ](../publications/6aaa25b39a3a05f18b9d.md)

Содиков Акмал Шавкат угли; Youwei Yan

This article analyzes mechanisms for disseminating legal information and ensuring its effective use, as well as the evolution of key procedures in this field\. The advanced practices of European Union countries and New Zealand are examined, with particular attention to mechanisms for disseminating normative legal acts from a doctrinal perspective\. The article also identifies stages of institutional development in the dissemination of legal information\. Scientifically grounded proposals and recommendations are developed to improve existing mechanisms\. The study also addresses effective ways to ensure that legal information is delivered rapidly, reliably, and conveniently in the digital environment, with particular emphasis on accessibility, openness, and public use\.

## [INDUSTRIAL MACHINE FAILURE PATTERN ANALYSIS FOR AUTOMATED DEFECT DIAGNOSIS IN ADVANCED MANUFACTURING SYSTEMS](../publications/6aade61455b37b4a6a60.md)

Umme Habiba Aesha; Reyan Hridoy Bhuiyan; Sumaya Mahajabin Khan; Yeasir Arafat Ayan

This study investigates the application of exploratory data analysis as a tool to facilitate automated defect diagnosis and reliability engineering of advanced industrial automation systems\. The research is based on a quantitative exploratory design with the help of the Predictive Maintenance Dataset with Irregularities to explore the machine operating conditions and failure patterns\. The focus of the analysis is on the distribution of machine failures, variations in operating parameters, and relationships between the operating parameters of the machines\. These results show that the dataset is dominated by normal operating conditions, and the failure events make up a relatively small fraction of the dataset\. The most common fault categories are heat dissipation failure and overstrain failure\. It is discovered through comparative analysis of the operating conditions that various types of failure have different characteristics in operation, specifically in terms of torque, rotational speed, tool wear, temperature, etc\. The air temperature and process temperature are highly positively correlated, and the rotational speed and torque are highly negatively correlated\. Failure status is correlated with air temperature and torque, with weak to moderate positive correlations, which could be used as diagnostic criteria\. Air temperature and torque are correlated with failure status with weak to moderate positive correlation, indicating that they could be used as diagnostic variables\. The results suggest the importance of exploratory analysis to detect patterns of operation and factors that repeat as failure in an industrial setting\. The study is an important contribution to reliability engineering by providing evidence\-based information that could help maintenance personnel in detecting problems early and making informed decisions, as well as help design future automated defect diagnosis frameworks\.

## [AI and Journalism: Exploring Ethics, Transparency and Self\-Regulation among Pakistani TV Journalists](../publications/6ab0684755e45920b93f.md)

Adiba Akhtar; Naeem Ullah Tariq; Aqeel Ahmed; Nur Nadia Abd Mubin

Aim of the Study: Newsrooms are increasingly integrating artificial intelligence \(AI\) for their news operations in the evolving journalistic landscape\. The journalists have started realizing AI as a collaborative assistant that can facilitate them in effective execution of their professional tasks\. Despite various prospects, adoption of AI may pose several challenges for the journalism professionals including that of ethical implications, transparency and self\-regulation to ensure objectivity\. Methodology: Guided by the social responsibility theory, this research has analyzed integration of AI into newsroom operations with its implications for media ethics\. This qualitative study involved in\-depth interviews of 13 journalists, dealing with the news operations at various levels in Pakistani TV News Organizations \(Urdu/English Channels\)\. While reaching the data saturation, the documented responses were thematically analyzed\. Findings: The findings of the research reveal that Pakistani TV journalists face ethical challenges related to information bias, public opinion influence, human judgement, professional autonomy, and lack of appropriate legal and global regulatory framework in the age of AI\. Conclusion: The study concludes that the journalists are aware of the challenges posed by AI technologies with the consideration for their cautious execution\.

## [Advances in Sport Physiology, Nutrition, and Metabolism](../publications/6ac221c7aeb48fb0563c.md)



This Reprint brings together seven original research articles and one review presenting current developments in sport physiology, training adaptation, nutrition, and applied sport science\. The contributions address two principal research areas—the first concerns acute physiological responses to exercise and conditioning stimuli, including optimizing isometric conditioning protocols and the immediate mechanical responses of muscle and tendon tissues to maximal aerobic effort; the second focuses on longer\-term training interventions and their physiological and performance\-related effects across athletic and clinical populations, including integrated training, plyometric training, and low\-volume resistance exercise\. Complementary contributions examine sport\-specific nutritional strategies for breath\-hold divers and methods for assessing lower\-limb asymmetry in youth football players\. Collectively, the articles highlight the multifactorial nature of human performance and adaptation to exercise and demonstrate the importance of integrating physiology, nutrition, biomechanics, and performance analysis\. This Reprint provides relevant insights for researchers, practitioners, coaches, and students working in sport and exercise science\.

## [Inhibitors of PIM‐1 Signaling Pathways as Anticancer Agents: Pharmacological and Structural Viewpoints](../publications/6ae3f06fb69b70cfe919.md)

Banty Kumar; Ankur Vaidya; Shweta Jain; Sanjeev Kumar Sahu; Preeti Patel; Vivek Asati

Pim\-1, a carcinogenic threonine and serine kinase, inhibits apoptosis and advances the cell cycle\. It is overexpressed in several human cancers\. The proviral integration site of Moloney murine leukemia virus 1 is Pim\-1\. Previous studies have shown that the Pim\-1 30\-UTR regulates the stability of Pim\-1 mRNA\. Threonine and serine are identified as the proto\-oncogene Pim\-1 kinase\. Pim\-1 mediates numerous biological processes, including apoptosis, cell division, proliferation, and cancer\. Pim\-1\-mediated anticancer activity has been reported in several analogs of thiazole/bis\-thiazole, tetrazine, thiophenes, quinoline, pyrazolopyrimidine, 3\-cyanopyridine, thiazolidine\-2,4\-dione, thieno\[2,3\-b\]pyridine, triazolo\[4,3\-b\]pyridazine, pyrazolo\[1,5\-a\]pyrimidines, and pyrazolo\[3,4\-b\]pyridine derivatives\. Additionally, flavonoids and amino alcohol compounds that constitute Pim\-1\-mediated cancer therapy have also been identified thus far\. Many compounds with Pim\-1\-mediated cytotoxicity have been discovered up to this point, and scientists are currently concentrating on bringing novel compounds with anticancer potential to the market\.

## [From Avocado Seed Waste to Green Synthesis Laser\-Induced Graphene: A Rapid, Direct, Low Cost and Flame\-Retardant\-Free Route](../publications/6af15bc5b81cbf222540.md)

Byron Tipán; Gema González; Carlos Reinoso; Fernando Pantoja\-Suárez

Laser\-induced graphene \(LIG\) offers a rapid and versatile route for converting carbon\-rich precursors into conductive graphitic materials\. However, the direct conversion of lignocellulosic biomass remains challenging because of its heterogeneous composition and thermal degradation behavior\. In this work, Fuerte avocado seed \( Persea americana Mill\.\) waste was investigated as a lignocellulosic precursor for the direct synthesis of LIG using CO₂ laser irradiation without flame retardants or chemical pretreatment\. The influence of laser power, scanning speed, number of irradiation passes, inter\-irradiation time, processing atmosphere, irradiation area, and precursor particle size was systematically evaluated\. Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X\-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that the structural and chemical characteristics of the resulting carbon material strongly depend on the applied processing conditions\. Larger irradiation areas and the T\-80 precursor fraction produced lower defect densities, while an argon atmosphere reduced the I D /I G ratio compared with processing in air\. Based on the combined evaluation of defect density and structural integrity, LIG was subsequently produced using the T\-80 precursor fraction, a single irradiation pass, 8\.8 W laser power, 50 mm s⁻¹ scanning speed, and an irradiation area of 56\.4 mm²\. The resulting material exhibited a porous morphology, an I D /I G ratio of 0\.16 ± 0\.07, an I 2D /I G ratio of 0\.48 ± 0\.07, and a sheet resistance of 25\.31 ± 2\.44 Ω sq⁻¹\. These results demonstrate the feasibility of directly converting avocado seed waste into conductive graphitic structures and provide a processing framework for the flame\-retardant\-free conversion of lignocellulosic biomass into LIG\.

## [Impurity\-Tolerance Design and Strengthening–Toughening Strategies in Recycled Aluminium Alloys](../publications/6af6e58eb0a2819e9d5a.md)

Dongxu Yang; Huafeng Wei; 李浩哲 Li Haozhe; 张洪武; Zengwu Yue; Xingshuo Liu

Recycled aluminium moves from downcycling towards the automotive sheet, structural castings and high\-performance extrusions\. The central constraint on closed\-loop recycling is no longer the mere presence of impurities\. It is the multiscale microstructure that those impurities generate during solidification, heat treatment and deformation, and how that microstructure participates in load bearing and damage\. Iron is the most representative cumulative impurity because its equilibrium solubility in solid aluminium is low and its removal by conventional refining is difficult and costly\. At a given Fe content, variations in Si, Mn, Cu and Cr, cooling rate and downstream processing can produce plate\-like β\-Al\-Fe\-Si, Chinese\-script α\-Al\(Fe,Mn\)Si, Al6\(Fe,Mn\), Al13Fe4 and Al7Cu2Fe intermetallics with distinct size distributions, shape anisotropy, three\-dimensional connectivity, phase fractions and interface states\. Consequently, Fe content has no alloy\-independent monotonic relationship with strength, ductility or damage tolerance\. This review follows a composition\-phase selection\-three\-dimensional microstructure\-mechanical response evidence chain to examine Fe\-rich intermetallic formation and evolution, strengthening\-damage competition, alloying and solidification control, thermomechanical processing, solid\-state recycling and coupled Fe\-Si\-Cu\-Mn\-Zn effects\. The available evidence supports defining impurity tolerance as a microstructural acceptance window tied to the alloy system, processing route and target property, rather than as a fixed compositional ceiling\. Its assessment must at least account for the hazardous upper tail of particle\-size distribution, morphology, three\-dimensional connectivity, phase fraction, matrix strength and interface integrity\. CALPHAD, in situ synchrotron methods, three\-dimensional X\-ray computed tomography and machine learning are shifting recycled\-alloy design from grade\-based impurity limits towards composition\-process feasibility domains matched to scrap distributions\. Comparable three\-dimensional descriptors, quantitative matrix\-particle\-damage maps and robust design methods for variable feedstocks are now required to complete this transition\.

## [Evaluation of UAV Flight Planning Strategies on the Accuracy of Glacier Mapping in Rugged Antarctic Terrains: A Case Study of Horseshoe Island](../publications/6b191f49d98d491a3fb4.md)

Mahmut Oğuz Selbesoğlu; Mustafa Fahri Karabulut; Esra Günaydın; Oleg Vassilev; Tolga Bakırman; Burak Akpınar; Özgün Oktar; Burcu Özsoy

Changes in the Earth’s radiation balance have increased global average temperatures, accelerating glacier melt in Antarctica\. Monitoring this process has become of great importance for future modeling studies\. Therefore, obtaining accurate, reliable, and most importantly rapid, logistically feasible, and cost\-effective measurements of glacier melt is critically important for regions with harsh conditions such as Antarctica\. The Ground Sampling Distance \(GSD\) and positional accuracy of photogrammetric products generated by unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\) photogrammetry are critical to accurately assessing snow and glacier dynamics\. In this context, the study presents accuracy assessments and planning recommendations for various flight plan scenarios in a rugged area with slopes up to 40% and partial snow and glacial cover\. The study was conducted on a test site on Horseshoe Island, and the UAV flight missions were performed under two operational modes: \(i\) terrain\-follow and \(ii\) fixed\-height\. The flight missions were real\-time kinematic \(RTK\)\-supported; however, ground control points \(GCPs\) were also placed and measured prior to the flights\. The images were evaluated to assess the positional accuracy achieved through RTK\-supported processing and GCP\-based georectification, with each flight mode analyzed separately\. Fixed\-height flight planning resulted in lower spatial accuracy than terrain\-follow mode, indicating that maintaining a constant flight height over irregular topography reduces spatial resolution due to variable image scales\. It was also observed that it performs better in terms of key points per image and bundle block adjustment \(BBA\)\-Average reprojection error in terrain\-follow scenarios\. In terms of 3D positional accuracy, using a limited number of GCPs resulted in root mean square error \(RMSE\) values of approximately 1–2 cm in the horizontal and 2–3 cm in the vertical components; however, the RTK\-supported flights exhibited higher errors in the Z component, with values of 12\.18 cm for the fixed\-height and 6\.85 cm for the terrain\-follow flights\.

## [Security and Privacy for Connected Systems: A Layered Review of Cryptography, Intrusion Detection and Privacy\-Preserving Learning in IoT, Cloud and Mobile Networks](../publications/6b1f1ec6ff343b7c73d7.md)

Maharajpet Sheela; Kennedy R; Karthi Rajan M

Connected systems now carry medical readings, financial records and personal data across sensors, mobile networks and cloud servers\. Each layer of such a system faces different threats\. Small IoT devices cannot run heavy encryption, ad hoc networks change their topology all the time, cloud stores hold large volumes of data from many users, and users themselves are targeted by phishing and privacy attacks\. Defences are usually designed and evaluated one layer at a time, which makes it hard to see how cryptography, intrusion detection and privacy\-preserving learning fit together\. This chapter reviews security and privacy mechanisms across four layers: devices and communication links, networks, cloud data stores, and users and applications\. It covers lightweight, elliptic curve and quantum\-safe cryptography, authentication and blockchain\-based trust for constrained devices, security\-aware resource management in 5G and 6G networks, moving target defence, learning\-based intrusion detection, optimized cloud encryption, phishing detection and privacy protection in federated learning and the metaverse\. The review finds that cryptographic designs for constrained devices trade key size and latency against strength, that ensemble and deep learning detectors report very high accuracy on benchmark traffic, and that metaheuristic optimization is increasingly used to tune encryption and detection parameters\. Few studies, however, evaluate several layers together or test detectors on attacks that were absent from training\. Future work should combine defences across layers, measure their overhead on real devices and evaluate them against new attack types\.

## [International Multi\-Centre Validation of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Precise Discrimination between Normal and Abnormal Retinal Development](../publications/6b29332afc46ddc66391.md)

Zhanhan Tu; Nikhil Reddy; Helen J\. Kuht; Ha\-Jun Yoon; Gail D\. E\. Maconachie; Ravi Purohit; Prateek Pani; Line Kessel; Jinu Han; Jing Jin; Shui\-Hua Wang; Karthik Bharadwaj; Viral Sheth; Michael Hisaund; Rebecca J\. McLean; George Garratt; Chetan Kantibhai Patel; Kanmin Xue; Callum Hunt; Zisen Zhou; Ian De Silva; Seema Teli; Sonal Shah; Vanessa Rodwell; Aarti Patel; Irene Gottlob; Yu\-Dong Zhang; Zedong Zheng; Girish Varma; Mervyn G\. Thomas

Arrested retinal development can cause childhood visual impairment, but grading optical coherence tomography scans is difficult to standardise across devices and centres\. We developed and evaluated an unsupervised domain adaptation model to classify normal and abnormal retinal development across different OCT systems\. This retrospective multicentre study used OCT scans from five centres in four countries and the UK Biobank\. Data covered four OCT devices, including table mounted and handheld systems\. A ResNet50 based Domain Adversarial Neural Network was trained using labelled images from a source device and unlabelled images from a target device\. We evaluated six source to target pairings and compared model performance with seven clinician graders\. A separate Heidelberg Spectralis dataset was reserved for external evaluation\. Across validation sets, accuracy ranged from 87\.75% to 96\.06%, sensitivity from 88\.68% to 98\.38%, and specificity from 78\.00% to 98\.02%\. The best performing model, adapted from TM OCT1 to HH OCT1, achieved 96\.06% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0\.994, with a 95% confidence interval from 0\.981 to 0\.999\. Several models also maintained discrimination on the unseen Heidelberg device\. Unsupervised domain adaptation enabled OCT classification across devices without labelled target device data\. The approach may support more consistent assessment of retinal development and large scale analysis of existing imaging datasets\.

## [Flash RNN\-T: Memory\-Efficient Joint Network and Transducer Loss Computation](../publications/6b2dc3dc1d7cdf2aed3c.md)

Mahmoud Ashraf

The recurrent neural network transducer \(RNN\-T\) remains a practical choice for streaming speech recognition, but training requires large intermediate tensors\. We present Flash RNN\-T, a joint and loss implementation combining specialized kernels with optional tiled recomputation over the full alignment space and vocabulary\. Tiled and untiled Flash form the entire measured throughput\-memory frontier on medium and long workloads\. On H100, untiled Flash achieves 24\-39% higher throughput with 26\-56% less memory than the fastest baseline on these workloads wherever it fits\. Tiling reduces memory further through recomputation\. On medium, tiled Flash uses ninefold less memory than that baseline at 16% lower throughput when both use one backward call per batch\. On long, it fits where all tested alternatives with that backward schedule run out of memory with 80 GB\. These comparisons use each implementation&\#x27;s lowest\-memory configuration reaching at least 95% of its peak throughput\.

## [OS\-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer\-Using Agents](../publications/6b2ef016d9deb2f7af9a.md)

Bowen Yang; Kaiming Jin; Zichen Ding; Zhenyu Wu; Zehao Li; Zhoumianze Liu; Kanzhi Cheng; Fangzhi Xu; Yanan Sun; Qiushi Sun; Yu Qiao

Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic\. Agents must understand user\-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state\. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt\-level tool composition\. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high\-quality hybrid data\. We present OS\-Helix, an end\-to\-end trained multimodal computer\-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space\. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application\-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment\-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality\. We cold\-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments\. For RL, we propose Step\-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous\-action optimization\. On OSWorld\-Verified, OS\-Helix\-27B and OS\-Helix\-35B\-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35\.0% and 33\.7% over their matched Qwen3\.5 hybrid baselines, while OS\-Helix\-27B\-RL further improves by 42\.9% to reach 66\.44% success\. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross\-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena\. Our project homepage is at https://os\-copilot\.github\.io/OS\-Helix/\.

## [Statistical Foundations and Machine Learning Perspectives in Quantitative Finance](../publications/6b2fffa5408d3e95a1ac.md)

Maeenuddin; Safwan Mohd Nor; M\. Ishaq Bhatti

Although advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) have transformed financial risk assessment, many early\-warning frameworks for systematic risk still rely on isolated macro\-financial indicators with limited integration of established statistical models\. This study bridges that gap by incorporating classical quantitative financial methodologies such as the Capital Asset Pricing Model \(CAPM\), Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity \(GARCH\) models, and Monte Carlo simulations within a modern data\-driven analytical framework\. Integrating these statistical methodologies into an early\-warning system should improve its ability to detect both micro\-level asset price dynamics and macro\-level contagion trends, especially in emerging economies\. This paper demonstrates how traditional models can complement AI\- and ML\-based predictive systems, enhancing the interpretability and robustness of early\-warning mechanisms in finance\. We apply these models to three notable stocks listed on Bursa Malaysia\. Our analysis of market behaviour encompasses various theoretical dimensions, utilising daily data over a 10\-year period from 2015 to 2024, resulting in 2,451 observations\. CAPM evaluates systematic risk and anticipated returns via beta coefficients, GARCH models time\-varying volatility and clustering phenomena, whilst Monte Carlo simulations generate probabilistic price paths under stochastic processes\. The consolidated findings reveal varied risk\-return characteristics among the equities, providing essential insights into volatility persistence, scenario\-based forecasting, and portfolio optimisation\. The analysis captures both micro\-level asset dynamics and macro\-level contagion effects\. The results reveal distinct patterns in volatility persistence, systematic risk, and probabilistic return distributions\. This paper demonstrates the empirical significance of each model and emphasises their theoretical foundations in contemporary finance literature\. The results possess practical significance for investors, policymakers, and educators seeking to improve risk modelling, capital allocation, and financial decision\-making in emerging economies\.

## [The Role of Pharmacists and Nurses in Enhancing Safety During Ultrasound\-Guided Vascular Access](../publications/6b314206be942d5f96c3.md)

Mohammed Hassan Asiri; Waleed Ahmed Asiri; Abdulaziz Ahmed Asiri; Zyad Saad Al Twaim; Shahad Almutairi; Amjad Alotaibi; Bader Yahya Ali Alshahrani

Ultrasound\-guided vascular access \(UGVA\) has become the preferred technique for peripheral and central venous catheter insertion due to its superior success rates and lower complication rates compared with landmark\-guided techniques\. While physicians and sonographers are primarily responsible for ultrasound\-guided catheter placement, pharmacists and nurses play indispensable roles in ensuring patient safety before, during, and after the procedure\. Nurses contribute through patient assessment, preparation, aseptic technique, monitoring, and catheter maintenance, whereas pharmacists optimize medication therapy, evaluate anticoagulation status, recommend appropriate vascular access devices, prevent medication\-related complications, and participate in infection prevention initiatives\. Interprofessional collaboration among pharmacists, nurses, physicians, and ultrasound professionals significantly reduces catheter\-related bloodstream infections \(CRBSIs\), thrombosis, bleeding complications, and medication errors\. This paper reviews the multidisciplinary contributions of pharmacists and nurses in enhancing safety during ultrasound\-guided vascular access and highlights evidence\-based strategies for improving clinical outcomes\.

## [ФІЛОСОФІЯ І БЕЗПЕКА: ТЕОРЕТИЧНІ ЗАСАДИ ДОСЛІДЖЕННЯ КОГНІТИВНИХ ЗАГРОЗ](../publications/6b3a93911c721a803391.md)

МІКАЕЛЬ САЛІХ

Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням ролі когнітивного виміру безпеки в умовах цифровізації суспільства, розвитку ШІ та трансформації сучасного інформаційно\-комунікаційного середовища\. Зростання масштабів когнітивних впливів актуалізує необхідність філософського осмислення механізмів формування знання, суспільної довіри, колективної ідентичності та моделей інтерпретації реальності\. Метою статті є обґрунтування теоретичних засад дослідження когнітивних загроз крізь призму філософського аналізу безпеки, процесів пізнання та механізмів когнітивного впливу\. У дослідженні використано методи теоретичного аналізу, систематизації, узагальнення, порівняння наукових підходів і структурно\-логічного моделювання\. У результаті дослідження обґрунтовано доцільність розгляду когнітивних загроз як самостійного різновиду сучасних безпекових загроз, спрямованих на трансформацію механізмів формування знання, суспільної довіри, історичної пам&\#x27;яті та колективної ідентичності\. Встановлено, що методологічною основою їх дослідження є комплексне використання епістемологічних, герменевтичних і соціально\-конструктивістських підходів, які дозволяють пояснити механізми формування когнітивних впливів у цифровому середовищі\. Доведено, що інформаційні, комунікативні та дискурсивні механізми впливу реалізуються через фреймування, наративне конструювання, алгоритмічну персоналізацію контенту та використання філософських ідеологем для легітимації політичних рішень і формування суспільних моделей сприйняття реальності\. Визначено, що сучасні цифрові платформи, генеративний ШІ і технології deepfake істотно посилюють масштаб, швидкість та ефективність когнітивних впливів\. Запропоновано концептуальний підхід до забезпечення когнітивної безпеки як міждисциплінарного напряму, що інтегрує філософський, соціально\-комунікаційний, психологічний, технологічний і безпековий підходи\. Практична цінність дослідження полягає у можливості використання отриманих результатів для вдосконалення концептуальних підходів до оцінювання когнітивних загроз, розвитку когнітивної стійкості суспільства та формування державної політики у сфері когнітивної безпеки\. Перспективи подальших досліджень пов&\#x27;язані з розробленням методик оцінювання когнітивної стійкості та аналізом трансформації когнітивних впливів в умовах розвитку генеративного ШІ\.

## [Passive Electromagnetic Compatibility Enhancement in Autonomous Vehicles via Conformal Meta\-Surfaces](../publications/6b46a61d49d907278e5e.md)

Emre K\. Yılmaz; Elif Z\. Demir; Caner M\. Kaya

This study presents the design, fabrication, and characterization of a flexible meta\-absorber for suppressing electromagnetic interference in automotive radar systems operating at 77 GHz\. The proposed structure, consisting of a patterned copper layer on a PDMS substrate, achieves over 92% absorption at 77\.2 GHz with a bandwidth of 2\.8% and maintains efficiency above 90% under bending radii down to 2 cm\. Experimental validation demonstrates a 12 dB enhancement in signal\-to\-noise ratio and 38% reduction in false alarm rate during field tests\. The absorber exhibits excellent thermal and humidity stability, offering a practical, low\-cost solution for improving radar immunity in complex driving environments\.

## [Research on Anti\-Money Laundering Regulatory Issues and Risk Prevention and Control in Insurance Intermediary Channels](../publications/6b4e25b101f5d801268c.md)

Ya An

As the insurance industry evolves, intermediaries serve as a bridge between insurance companies and their clients\. However, the complexity of transaction workflows and the diversity of fund flow mechanisms give rise to potential money laundering risks and challenges for effective regulation\. This study identifies key anti\-money laundering \(AML\) risk points within the core business processes of insurance intermediaries\. It finds that regulatory challenges, specifically unclear and fragmented accountability alongside disjointed information systems, undermine core risk control measures\. Consequently, the study proposes a series of targeted recommendations: establishing an integrated transaction monitoring system, leveraging fintech tools to strengthen internal compliance frameworks, and building a risk\-based AML system tailored to the specific characteristics of insurance intermediary channels\.

## [Synergistic Phase Transition and Defect Engineering Enables High‐Sensitivity Optical Thermometry in Ferroelectric Oxides](../publications/6b65de85e5c7b9e6f07f.md)

Jie Yang; Tao Zhou; Yuyan Deng; Xiahong Lin; Haiqin Sun; Pei Lin Han; Fuchi Liu; Qiwei Zhang

ABSTRACT High‐sensitivity optical thermometry based on non‐thermally coupled levels \(NTCLs\) is vital for advanced remote sensing\. However, achieving robust anti‐thermal luminescent quenching remains a significant challenge by relying solely on negative thermal expansion effect or defect engineering designs, owing to material scarcity and limited carrier compensation\. For this, we propose a novel synergistic strategy that integrates ferroelectric phase transitions with defect engineering in NaNbO 3 :Nd 3\+ /Yb 3\+ \. This approach leverages oxygen vacancies for carrier storage and release, combined with polymorphic phase transitions to modulate local crystal‐field symmetry, effectively offsetting non‐radiative energy relaxation\. Consequently, our results demonstrate a 654‐fold luminescent enhancement at 673 K\. This dramatic enhancement significantly enhances the fluorescence intensity ratio of Nd 3\+ ions \(498 nm/683 nm\), yielding a high relative sensitivity of 4\.3% K −1 and absolute sensitivity of 9\.38 K −1 \. These results not only offer a novel strategy for designing thermally enhanced upconversion luminescent materials, but also reveal the significant potential of ferroelectric oxides as promising candidates for high‐temperature optical thermometry\.

## [Una estrategia de descomposición de alta precisión para problemas con restricciones a gran escala](../publications/6b83c1422939aaaa3c86.md)

Fabiola Paz; Guillermo Leguizamon; Efrén Mezura‐Montes

Decomposition strategies, such as cooperative coevolutionary \(CC\) algorithms, have proven effective in solving various large\-scale constrained optimization problems\. This approach decomposes a largescale constrained problem into simpler, smaller\-scale subproblems without significantly affecting the performance of the optimization algorithm\. The effectiveness of the approach depends greatly on the quality of this decomposition\. An effective decomposition takes into account the interactions between the variables\. However, recent strategies such as RDG and ERDG identify only additive interactions in the problem decomposition\. As a result, these strategies tend to work well only for problems with this property\. Nevertheless, in real\-world problems, other types of separability besides additive separability may arise\. This paper proposes a new decomposition strategy called Constrained Dual Differential Grouping \(CDDG\)\. The novelty of CDDG is that it can be used for both additive and multiplicative separable functions, which greatly increases the range of CC\. To validate the effectiveness of CDDG, experiments and comparisons with state\-of\-the\-art methods are conducted\. The results demonstrate that CDDG can better adapt to the specific characteristics of each benchmark test problem\.

## [FutureLift: Lifting Trajectory Proposals into Bidirectional Future Graphs for Motion Forecasting](../publications/6b84474a1164dfe64903.md)

Daniel Grimm; J\. Marius Zöllner

Accurate motion prediction is critical for safe autonomous driving, yet even strong forecasters leave residual errors in their multimodal proposals\. Existing refiners compress complete proposals or update their segments sequentially, preventing the full proposed future from serving as explicit relational context for correction\. We introduce FutureLift, a backbone\-agnostic refiner that represents each multimodal proposal as a heterogeneous future graph, with spatially grounded temporal nodes connected to agent histories, map elements, alternative modes, and, for joint prediction, other agents future trajectories\. Bidirectional temporal edges allow later evidence to revise earlier segments in a single pass, and the updated nodes predict residual coordinate and confidence corrections\. Requiring only proposals, scores, and scene context, FutureLift provides a common refinement interface for structurally different forecasting backbones\. On Argoverse2 and the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, it consistently improves frozen proposals and outperforms native and specialized refiners across marginal and joint forecasting\. On the WOMD motion\-prediction leaderboard, FutureLift ranks first in minADE \(0\.5049m\) and minFDE \(0\.9942m\) among the compared standard\-input methods, without LiDAR or ensembling, while achieving a competitive 0\.4874 Soft mAP\.

## [Gut\-liver axis in liver pre\-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities](../publications/6b85a24131857e8229bd.md)

Leyi Zhao; Qiutong Lin; Danyuan Zhang; Yani Liu; Mingtong Zong; Lingze Xi; Feiyu Xie; Shuyi Song; Peng Xue; Shijie Zhu; Xuelei Chu

The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis\. The formation of pre\-metastatic niches \(PMNs\) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive “soil” for disseminated tumor cells\. However, how the gut\-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood\. In this review, we delineate the six hallmark features of PMN assembly, with an emphasis on the complex crosstalk among gut microbiota, their bioactive metabolites, and resident liver cells—including hepatocytes and hepatic immune populations\. Notably, these elements engage in a dynamic, reciprocally regulated network characterized by bidirectional feedback loops, rather than a linear signaling cascade\. We further survey the emerging landscape of diagnostic biomarkers, including exosomal microRNAs and neutrophil extracellular traps, alongside microbiota\-targeted therapeutic interventions\. This framework provides testable hypotheses for early interception of liver metastasis and highlights precision medicine opportunities targeting the gut\-liver\-immune axis\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Media Organizations: Emerging Practices, Opportunities and Implications for Social and Cultural Development](../publications/6b94b1d91e7b1d466c84.md)

Shikeb Majeed

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is becoming an increasingly visible part of the modern media environment\. Its role is no longer limited to automated or computational journalism; it is now being explored across several stages of media production, including content writing, editing, transcription, translation, fact\-checking, audience analysis, recommendation, and personalization\. As generative AI and large language models have developed, academic interest in their use within journalism and media organizations has also increased considerably\. Recent studies and reviews show that research in this area has expanded from early discussions of automated journalism to broader questions concerning how AI is changing newsroom practices and professional work\. This review examines existing research on AI adoption in media organizations, focusing particularly on changes in newsroom practices, organizational processes, journalistic roles, editorial decision\-making, and the social and cultural dimensions of AI use\. The paper brings together earlier research on automated and algorithmic journalism with more recent literature on generative AI, journalist–AI collaboration, newsroom implementation, ethical concerns, and organizational barriers\. The literature suggests that AI can help media organizations handle repetitive and data\-intensive tasks more efficiently, allowing journalists to devote greater attention to activities that require interpretation and editorial judgement\. However, the growing use of AI also raises important concerns about human oversight, algorithmic transparency, accountability, professional autonomy, and the quality and context of media content\. Particular attention is given to India and other countries of the Global South, where the adoption of AI takes place within different economic, organizational, linguistic, and cultural settings\. Research from these contexts indicates that AI adoption is developing, but its implementation is not always uniform\. Limited resources, inadequate training, organizational preparedness, and the absence of clear ethical guidelines can influence how effectively media organizations integrate AI into their professional practices\. Overall, the review suggests that AI adoption in media should not be understood simply as a technological shift aimed at improving speed and efficiency\. It is also influencing the nature of journalistic work, editorial responsibility, and the relationship between media organizations and the communities they serve\. Therefore, understanding AI adoption requires attention not only to its operational benefits but also to its implications for the social and cultural responsibilities of media\.

## [Resolving the Data Dilemma in Catalyst Design: A Generative\-Enhanced Manifold\-Preserving Machine Learning Method for CO2\-to\-Aromatics](../publications/6b95e28be7cf39b9a40d.md)

Zhao Wang; Jingsong Guan; Minmin Zhou; Jun Hu; Qiwen Guo; M Wang; Qingchun Yang

Abstract Direct CO2 hydrogenation to aromatics \(CTA\) offers a sustainable alternative to petroleum\-based aromatic production, yet its catalyst design is severely hindered by data scarcity, feature heterogeneity, and conflicting multiobjective requirements\. Therefore, this study proposes a generative enhancement and manifold preservation\-driven interpretable machine learning \(GEMP\-ML\) framework\. It integrates heuristic hybrid encoding, hierarchical missing value management, generative data augmentation, and active\-learning\-based sample screening to construct an information\-enriched catalyst training set\. To enable semantically faithful numerical representation of high\-cardinality categorical features, a best\-first sampling strategy is designed to identify the optimal hybrid encoding scheme from 89 candidate combinations specifically for these categorical variables\. Combined with hierarchical semantic missing\-value management and high\-fidelity imputation algorithms, the data integrity of the CTA dataset is restored while preserving the semantic integrity of categorical features\. GMM\-based generative augmentation combined with diversity\-aware active learning improved the utilization of synthetic data, and the CatBoost surrogate model achieved an average test set R2 of 0\.973 across the three targets\. Complementary interpretability analysis further identifies key descriptors governing catalyst performance, guiding the Pareto optimization of catalyst formulations and operating parameters\. The recommended Zn–Al/HZSM\-5 catalyst is predicted to achieve approximately 36\.5% CO2 conversion, 78\.6% C5\+ selectivity, and 0\.35% CO selectivity\. The model is further validated against two independent experimental datasets covering 100 h time\-on\-stream, with prediction errors of &lt;8%, supporting its ability to reproduce the observed performance trends under the evaluated conditions\. This generalizable framework provides a systematic, data\-driven paradigm for accelerating the design of high\-performance catalysts in data\-sparse catalytic systems\.

## [Automatic Data Dependence Analysis by Deductive Verification](../publications/6b9f5835609645b3ea7d.md)

Asmae Heydari Tabar; Richard Bubel; Reiner Hähnle

Abstract Parallelization of programs is of essence in the high\-performance computing \(HPC\) area\. But parallelization is only correct if certain data dependences can be reliably excluded, for example, read\-after\-write dependences, where a read access occurs as the subsequent access on a data element after a write access\. Data dependence analyses should not merely be correct, but as precise as possible, so as not to miss any opportunity for parallelization\. Various dynamic and static analyses were proposed in the HPC community, but, until recently, none based on program logic and deductive verification, even though the latter approach has important advantages, including soundness, precision, and modularity\. Previously a proof\-of\-concept was given that fully automatic dependence analysis based on deductive verification is possible, but it suffered from limitations that rendered it impractical: the restriction to one\-dimensional arrays and flat loops and, importantly, it does not differentiate between inter\- and intra\-iteration data dependences, which often results in a loss of precision\. In this paper we lift all three limitations and show that a deductive approach is a competitive alternative to the kinds of dependence analyses used hitherto in HPC\. Our axiomatization in a deduction system constitutes the first formalization of the semantics of inter\-iteration dependence\.

## [ЛІНГВОСТИЛІСТИЧНІ ОСОБЛИВОСТІ АНГЛОМОВНОГО МАРКЕТИНГОВОГО ДИСКУРСУ В УМОВАХ ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ](../publications/6ba3a98ae59222fde2a7.md)

Khrystyna Dzyubynska; Н\.П\. Ваврін

У статті розглянуто лінгвостилістичні особливості англомовного маркетингового дискурсу та мовні засоби реалі\- зації комунікативного впливу в цифровому середовищі\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена динамічним розвитком цифрової маркетингової комунікації, у межах якої мовна організація тексту безпосередньо пов’язана з характером взаємодії бренду та цільової аудиторії\. Теоретичну основу дослідження становлять наукові праці, присвячені семан\- тичним, синтаксичним, лексико\-семантичним і комунікативно\-прагматичним характеристикам англомовного реклам\- ного та маркетингового дискурсу\. У процесі аналізу увагу зосереджено на функціонуванні лексичних, синтаксичних і стилістичних засобів, їх взаємодії та залежності від характеристик цільової аудиторії\. Лексичний рівень представ\- лено оцінною, емоційно забарвленою та експресивною лексикою, яка виконує номінативну, оцінну, емоційну та спо\- нукальну функції\. Синтаксична організація маркетингових повідомлень характеризується використанням коротких конструкцій, імперативів, повторів, паралелізмів і риторичних запитань\. Стилістичну виразність формують метафора, порівняння, персоніфікація, гіпербола та гра слів\. Окрему увагу приділено персоналізації мовлення, яка скорочує комунікативну дистанцію між брендом і споживачем\. На матеріалі англомовних цифрових маркетингових текстів про\- стежено лексичні опозиції «реальне – штучне», «автентичність – технологічність», «професійні можливості – ско\- рочення зайнятості», що відображають актуальні зміни у сфері цифрового маркетингу\. Розглянуто функціонування професійної термінології, пов’язаної зі штучним інтелектом, автоматизацією, цифровим маркетингом та організацією праці\. Окремо окреслено значення перекладу й локалізації маркетингових текстів з урахуванням їхньої комунікатив\- ної спрямованості, мультимодальної структури та національно\-культурної специфіки\.

## [Confidence Based Sequential Drift Detection Under Resource Constraints](../publications/6ba9c4dfd89a1e2fd58d.md)

Palak Thakur

Concept Drift Detectors are the methods that are used to identify the patterns and behaviors of data that changes over time\. These methods are tested separately on different datasets, which makes it difficult to compare which detector is suitable for particular situation\. This paper presents the comparison of seven concept\-drift detectors: ADWIN, DDM, EDDM, KSWIN, Page\-Hinkley, Naive\-T and a new lightweight detector called SeqConf\. These seven detectors were tested on 120 simulated data streams\. This experiment used two basic problems, three types of drift and twenty different random seeds for each case\. Here we already know the drift points, the performance of each detector could be measured accurately\. All detector used the same fixed online classifier, so that their detection performance, false alarms and computational requirements could be compared under the same conditions\. SeqConf combines confidence\-based monitoring, it does not require labels after deployment and uses constant memory\. It uses persistence rule to reduce false alarms caused by single unusual samples\. The results from 840 detector run shows that it has lowest memory usage and second lowest false alarm rate with 0\.30 false alarms per 9000 samples on stationary data\. Its detection rate is lowest among the seven detectors, at 12\.5%\. This experiment also showed that confidence\-based detectors such as KSWIN, Page\-Hinkley and SeqConf had difficulty detecting a gradual drift in the SEA dataset\. EEDM, KSWIN and the Naïve\-T baseline, produced alarms very frequently\. The paper provides the complete experimental results and figures so that experiments can be repeated and verified\.

## [Beyond the Dominant Label: Recovering Coexisting Lesion Evidence with Multiple Instance Learning](../publications/6bb3340637359e64604c.md)

Lubin Gan; Jing Zhang; Xinming Zhang; Chengpeng Xu; Siying Wu; Xiaoyan Sun

Whole\-slide images may contain coexisting lesions, yet weak supervision typically provides only the most severe diagnosis\. We formulate this setting as dominant\-label multiple instance learning, where the observed label is the maximum\-severity element of a latent lesion set\. Standard multiclass MIL treats it as a complete one\-hot description and therefore suppresses lower\-severity evidence whenever it co\-occurs with a dominant lesion\. We propose DomSet\-MIL, a label\-aware framework that aligns the annotation mechanism across bag and instance levels\. Dominant\-Label Censored Likelihood models the reported diagnosis without declaring unreported lesions absent\. Severity\-Ordered Residual Routing assigns patch evidence from high to low severity and preserves residual support for secondary findings, while top\-$q$ pooling links local routing scores to bag prediction\. Experiments across natural and controlled settings show that DomSet\-MIL achieves state\-of\-the\-art performance in dominant\-label prediction while more effectively recovering latent coexisting\-lesion evidence\. These findings demonstrate that modeling the dominant\-label mechanism can improve diagnostic prediction without sacrificing clinically meaningful secondary findings\.

Carlos Salomón; Andrew Lai; Dominic Guanzon; Katherin Scholz‐Romero; Nihar Godbole; Carlos Palma; Sophia Apostolidou; Aleksandra Gentry‐Maharaj; Gregory Edward Rice; Usha Menon
