## [Psikolojik sağlamlık ve ilişkili faktörler: Çocukluk dönemi olumsuz yaşantıları, duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti ve yalnızlık](../publications/6bb79262045d46a1352c.md)

İrem Tanrıvermiş; Ayşe Kübra Özcan; Huri Gül Bayram Gülaçtı

Psikolojik sağlamlık, bireyin olumsuz durumlarla baş edebilmesini destekleyen bir mekanizmadır\. Bireyin psikolojik sağlığını korumadaki etkin rolü düşünüldüğünde, psikolojik sağlamlıkla ilişkili bireysel ve çevresel risk faktörleri belirlenmiş olsa da beliren yetişkinlik dönemindeki bireylerde bu faktörlerin bütüncül biçimde araştırılmasına ihtiyaç duyulmaktadır\. Bu araştırmada çocukluk dönemi olumsuz yaşantıları, duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti ve yalnızlığın psikolojik sağlamlıkla ilişkisinin kesitsel desenle incelenmesi amaçlanmıştır\. Çalışmaya 18\-29 yaş aralığında 468 kişi katılmıştır ve Connor\-Davidson Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği Kısa Formu, Çocukluk Çağı Olumsuz Yaşantılar Ölçeği, Duyusal İşlemleme Hassasiyeti Ölçeği ve UCLA Yalnızlık Ölçeği uygulanmıştır\. Korelasyon analizleri sonucunda psikolojik sağlamlık ile duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti \(r = \-\.255, p &lt; \.001\), çocukluk dönemi olumsuz yaşantıları \(r = \-\.117, p = \.011\) ve yalnızlık \(r = \-\.324, p &lt; \.001\) arasında negatif yönlü bir ilişki bulunmuştur\. Hiyerarşik regresyon analizine göre, birinci basamakta sosyo\-ekonomik düzey, eğitim düzeyi ve cinsiyet istatistiksel olarak kontrol edildikten sonra ikinci basamakta duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti \(β = \-\.109, p = \.023, part² = \.009, 5% GA \[\-\.153, \-\.011 \]\) ve yalnızlık \(β = \-\.300, p &lt; \.001, part² = \.074, 95% GA \[\-\.056, \-\.030\]\) psikolojik sağlamlık düzeyini negatif olarak yordamıştır\. Bu doğrultuda duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti ve yalnızlık arttıkça psikolojik sağlamlık düzeyleri azalmaktadır\. Ayrıca, beklenenin aksine, çocukluk dönemi olumsuz yaşantıları psikolojik sağlamlığı anlamlı bir biçimde yordamamıştır\. Duyusal işlemleme hassasiyeti ve yalnızlığın psikolojik sağlamlık için risk faktörü olabileceği düşünülmektedir\. Dolayısıyla, risk altındaki gruplar için müdahale programlarının tasarlanmasında öneme sahip olabilecek bu çalışma, kuramsal tartışmaların geliştirilmesine katkı sağlayabilir\.

## [Scholarly publishing literacy and perceptions of predatory publishing among educational partners at a chiropractic college: a case report](../publications/6bc975ff009207b9cee7.md)

Jennifer R\. Smith; Edward W\. Murphy; Stacie A\. Salsbury

Background: Chiropractors must find, appraise, and apply high quality, peer\-reviewed information sources to make evidence\-based clinical practice decisions\. This case report describes perceptions of scholarly publishing practices, with a focus on predatory and deceptive publishing, among chiropractic educational partners at one chiropractic college\. Case Presentation: An anonymous, online, cross\-sectional survey was administered to a convenience sample of 2,476 faculty, staff, and students\. The 35\-item questionnaire elicited publishing experience, critical appraisal skills, knowledge of scholarly and predatory publishing, and perceptions of chiropractic journals and information resources\. Respondents \(n=204, 111 students, 36 faculty, 16 administrators, and 41 staff\) provided usable survey responses, though skipped items were common\. Twenty\-six percent had published one or more peer\-reviewed publications\. Most self\-rated themselves as novice or intermediate in their ability to perform literature searches \(87%\) or critically appraise research articles \(82%\)\. Forty\-six percent to 69% had not read or were unsure of the quality of scientific evidence for 11 chiropractic\-related journals\. Fifty\-seven percent were unsure or unfamiliar with predatory journals and 51% lacked confidence in recognizing these journals\. Predatory practices identified included insufficient or fast peer review, editorial board and impact factor issues, publication fees, plagiarized articles, and unsolicited request for paper submissions\. Sixty\-one percent requested training or resources on identifying quality academic journals for publication or research\. Conclusion: Chiropractic educational partners were unfamiliar with most chiropractic journals and had little familiarity with predatory publishing\. Targeted training on identifying quality academic publications, conducting literature reviews and critically appraising research articles is recommended\.

## [First record of Yellow\-throated Sparrow, Gymnoris xanthocollis \(Burton, 1838\) \(Aves, Passeriformes, Passeridae\) in Bangladesh](../publications/6bcc103a4216db493198.md)

Ahsan Uddin Chowdhury; Raihan Bablu; Jahir Mahmud Sohag; Nahidul Hasan

We provide a new distributional record of the Yellow\-throated Sparrow, Gymnoris xanthocollis \(Burton, 1838\), from south\-eastern Bangladesh based on photographs\. This is the eastern most record of this species and a new country record\. We identified G\. xanthocollis based on morphological characteristics, which include fine bills, indistinct eyebrows, grey\-brown body colouration with a chestnut shoulder patch, a yellow throat spot, and one distinct, white wing bar\. Our new record suggests that continuous monitoring is necessary to better understand species diversity and geographical distribution of the avian fauna in this densely populated tropical region\.

## [Information Estimation with Discrete Diffusion](../publications/6bd1b7bf675268081789.md)

Alberto Foresti; Giulio Franzese; Pietro Michiardi

Information\-theoretic measures, such as Mutual Information \(MI\), play a crucial role in understanding non\-linear relationships between random variables and are widely used across scientific disciplines\. Yet, their use on real\-world discrete data remains challenging\. Existing methods typically rely on embedding discrete data into a continuous space and apply neural estimators originally designed for continuous distributions\. This process requires careful engineering for both the embedding model and estimator architecture, but suffers from issues related to high data dimensionality\. In this work, we introduce InfoSEDD, a discrete diffusion\-based approach that bridges information\-theoretic estimation and generative modeling such that they can be used to compute Kullback\-Leibler divergences\. Backed by Continuous Time Markov Chains theory principles, the design of InfoSEDD is lightweight and scalable and allows seamless integration with pretrained models\. We showcase the versatility of our approach through applications on motif discovery in genetic promoter data, semantic\-aware model selection in text summarization, and entropy estimation in Ising models\. Finally, we construct consistency tests on real\-world textual and genomics data\. Our experiments demonstrate that InfoSEDD outperforms alternatives that rely on the &quot;embedding trick&quot;\. Our results position InfoSEDD as a robust and scalable tool for information\-theoretic analysis of discrete data\.

## [Yandangshan Dendrobium officinale flower flavonoids alleviate dextran sulfate sodium \(DSS\)\-induced colitis in association with local intestinal ecological remodeling](../publications/6bd3a9b8fd6efc8bb23d.md)

Xiang\-Dong Wang; Yujiao Zhang; Jiahao Pan; Rong Huang; Jinou Lin; Xiaodan Zhang; Bolu Sun; Xiaojie Zheng

Abstract Objectives Ulcerative colitis arises from epithelial barrier disruption, gut microbial dysbiosis, and aberrant mucosal immune activation\. Given that many food\-derived flavonoids achieve limited systemic exposure after oral administration, how local intestinal activity translates into host tissue protection remains a central question\. Resolving this process is challenging because microbial communities, metabolite outputs, and mucosal responses operate across distinct biological levels and often yield disconnected evidence\. Materials and Methods : Here, we studied chemically consistent Dendrobium officinale flower flavonoids \(DOFF\), validated across six independent batches by liquid chromatography\-mass spectrometry \(LC\-MS\), and integrated absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion \(ADME\) prediction, conventional and antibiotic\-perturbed dextran sulfate sodium \(DSS\) colitis models, 16S rRNA sequencing, targeted short\-chain fatty acid quantification, untargeted fecal metabolomics, host\-response network analysis, single\-cell virtual knockout, and whole\-slide artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted spatial pathology\. Results DOFF reduced dextran sulfate sodium\-induced disease activity and colonic injury, restored ZO\-1\- and Occludin\-associated barrier integrity, reconfigured gut microbial structure and fecal metabolic profiles, and suppressed TLR4/MYD88/NF\-κB signaling; computational integration and single\-cell virtual knockout further prioritized FFAR2/HCAR2, TLR4/RELA, and EGFR/LGR5 as candidate host targets associated with metabolite sensing, inflammatory regulation, and epithelial repair, respectively, while DOFF retained partial tissue protection after broad\-spectrum antibiotic perturbation, accompanied by limited shifts in residual microbiota and AI\-predicted spatial pathology features\. Conclusions These findings support a local ecology\-first working model in which DOFF\-associated microbiota\-metabolite remodeling coincides with epithelial barrier restoration and mucosal inflammatory suppression without necessarily requiring high systemic exposure or action through a single host target, although direct causal roles for the microbiota, key metabolites, and host receptors require further validation\.

## [Add\-on sirolimus in refractory iMCD\-TAFRO: a TAFRO\-enriched 8\-patient case series with paired single\-cell profiling](../publications/6bd9033f737bd1ea2e7e.md)

Remi Sumiyoshi; Tomohiro Koga; Toru Michitsuji; Masataka Umeda; Ayuko Takatani; Yoshito Nishimura; David C\. Fajgenbaum; Frits van Rhee; Atsushi Kawakami

Introduction Anti–IL\-6 therapy with tocilizumab \(TCZ\) is ineffective in a proportion of patients with idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease \(iMCD\), particularly the TAFRO subtype, and rescue options remain limited\. Evidence for mTOR inhibition comes mainly from cohorts in which iMCD\-TAFRO was underrepresented\. Methods Eight Japanese patients with refractory iMCD \(iMCD\-TAFRO, n=6; iMCD\-NOS, n=1\) or TAFRO syndrome without iMCD \(n=1\) received add\-on sirolimus \(1–2 mg/day\)\. Five had active refractory iMCD\-TAFRO at initiation and formed the efficacy set; Case 5 \(sirolimus for glucocorticoid sparing\), Case 1 \(iMCD\-NOS\) and Case 3 \(TAFRO syndrome without iMCD\) are reported descriptively\. Response was defined as improvement in at least one refractory feature \(CRP &lt;0\.3 mg/dL, platelets &gt;15×10 4 /µL, improvement of anasarca, or a ≥50% rise in eGFR\) at 3 and 12 months\. Results In the efficacy set, 4/5 responded at 3 months \(80%; 95% CI 28–99\) and 3/4 evaluable at 12 months \(75%; 95% CI 19–99\); a prespecified TAFRO\-phenotype analysis \(n=6, including Case 3\) gave 5/6 \(83%; 95% CI 36–100\) and 4/5 evaluable \(80%; 95% CI 28–99\)\. Under a prespecified stringent definition additionally requiring CRP normalization and no escalation of concomitant immunosuppression, proportions fell to 3/5 \(60%\) and 2/4 evaluable \(50%\), each reclassification resting on a single criterion\. All six responders eventually discontinued sirolimus without relapse during available follow\-up\. Glucocorticoids were withdrawn in all four responders receiving prednisolone, TCZ intervals were extended to ≥5 weeks in three patients, and both patients with dialysis\-dependent active disease stopped hemodialysis\. Exploratory paired single\-cell RNA sequencing in one TAFRO\-phenotype patient showed reductions in inflammatory monocytes and B cells with lower cytotoxic and proliferative programs\. Discussion Given the very small sample, wide confidence intervals and the sensitivity of the estimates to the response definition, add\-on sirolimus should be regarded as a hypothesis\-generating adjunctive rescue option on top of standard treatment, not a substitute, in refractory iMCD\-TAFRO\.

## [Fabrication and Characterization of CL‐20@Sodium Alginate Core‐Shell Composites With Enhanced Safety](../publications/6bde0a6d54dcf668f945.md)

陈子键; Jing Wei Hou; Bindong Li

ABSTRACT To address the high mechanical sensitivity limitation of CL‐20, a core–shell‐structured CL‐20@sodium alginate composite was fabricated using a facile solution dispersion and filtration method\. Comprehensive characterization confirmed that sodium alginate was successfully coated onto the surface of ε ‐CL‐20 crystals through hydrogen‐bonding interactions without altering the crystal structure of CL‐20\. Thermal analysis revealed that the sodium alginate coating modulates the decomposition behavior, resulting in a more gradual energy release process\. Impact sensitivity testing demonstrated that the limiting impact energy significantly increased from 2\.0 J for pristine CL‐20 to 22\.5 J for the composite, corresponding to an 11‐fold reduction in impact sensitivity\. This study demonstrates that low‐cost sodium alginate serves as an effective desensitizing shell material, offering a promising strategy for developing high‐energy insensitive energetic composites with enhanced safety characteristics\.

## [A Hybrid Deep\-Learning and Impedance\-Based Scheme for Fault Classification and Location in Transmission Lines: A Physics\-Validated, Leakage\-Free Evaluation](../publications/6bdf530708ceb12d75ab.md)

Abdulla Habbib; Omar Ibrahim; Mohammed Majeed

Deep\-learning fault classifiers and locators for transmission lines are often evaluated on unvalidated simulations, with possible data leakage and without comparison against the impedance\-based methods used in practice\. This study builds an exact time\-domain simulator of a 400 kV, 200 km two\-source line, whose fault currents agree with symmetrical\-component calculations within 2%, and generates 22,600 independent scenarios covering ten fault types, fault resistance, location, inception angle, loading and source strength\. Single\-ended 25 ms windows sampled at 4 kHz were used to train one\-dimensional convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\), which were compared with feature\-based classifiers and with the reactance and Takagi locators\. The CNN classified faults with 99\.91% accuracy in 0\.4 ms per window, but feature\-based classifiers were equally accurate, and all learned classifiers failed for fault resistances beyond the training range until that range was included in training, which in turn increased false alarms under strong noise\. CNN regression located faults with a mean absolute error of 5\.81 km, better than other learned models but far worse than the Takagi method on the third post\-fault cycle\. A hybrid scheme, in which the CNN supplies the fault type and the Takagi method the distance, reduced the error to 1\.40 km, located 93\.8% of faults within 2% of the line length, and remained accurate for weak sources, noise and high fault resistance\. Deep learning is thus best used for fast classification, and physics\-based methods for precise location\.

## [Nootropic Potential and Amnesia Reversal Efficacy of Methanolic Leaf Extract of Lantana camara L\. in Swiss Albino Mice: A MultiParadigm Behavioural Study](../publications/6be0cc7fd7875bed3339.md)



Background: Memory loss and cognitive impairment are common features of neurodegenerative conditions and age\-related brain changes\.Medicinal plants rich in bioactive phytochemicals denote a promising path for the discovery of natural cognitive enhancers\.Lantana camara L\. is a extensively distributed shrub with documented antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, yet its direct nootropic effects remain insufficiently characterized\.Objective: This study aimed to assess the nootropic and memory\-enhancing potential of methanolic extract of Lantana camara \(MELC\) in both normal mice and a Diazepam\-induced amnesic mouse model, alongside its phytochemical characterization and antioxidant profiling\.Methods: Standard qualitative phytochemical tests, OECD 423\-based acute oral toxicity evaluation, and DPPH free radical scavenging assay were carried out\.Cognitive performance was assessed using four validated behavioral models: Elevated Plus Maze \(EPM\), Object Recognition Test \(ORT\), Hebb\-Williams Maze \(HWM\), and Active Avoidance Paradigm \(AAP\)\.MELC was administered orally at 200 and 400 mg/kg\.Piracetam \(200 mg/kg, i\.p\.\) was used as the standard nootropic drug, and diazepam \(1 mg/kg, i\.p\.\) was used to induce experimental amnesia\.All data were analyzed statistically using one\-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett&\#x27;s post\-hoc test\.Results: Phytochemical screening detected the presence of flavonoids, tannins, saponins, steroids, and triterpenoids\.No mortality or adverse effects were observed at doses up to 2000 mg/kg\.MELC demonstrated potent concentration\-dependent DPPH radical scavenging activity with an IC50 value of 15\.82 µg/mL\.In normal mice, oral administration of MELC significantly improved cognitive parameters, including reduced transfer latency in EPM, enhanced novel object discrimination in ORT, decreased total run count in HWM, and improved avoidance responses in AAP\.In the diazepam\-induced amnesic model, MELC markedly reversed the memory deficits across all behavioral paradigms\.The 400 mg/kg dose consistently produced the most pronounced cognitive enhancement, with efficacy comparable to piracetam\.Conclusion: MELC demonstrates significant nootropic and antioxidant activities in preclinical models\.The cognitive enhancement observed is likely attributable to the rich phytochemical composition, particularly flavonoids and saponins\.These results support the potential of L\. camara as a natural therapeutic agent in managing memory impairment and cognitive disorders\.Further investigations to identify active constituents and clarify molecular mechanisms are warranted\.This is the first study to demonstrate the nootropic potential of Lantana camara methanolic leaf extract across four complementary behavioural paradigms, underscoring its translational relevance as a candidate cognitive\-enhancing agent\.

## [Mobile phone forensics and criminal justice in India: evidentiary reliability, institutional readiness, and reform under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023](../publications/6be7f152ff99677dab5c.md)

Ayush Mudgal; Gururaj Devarhubli

Mobile phone evidence is now routine in Indian criminal trials\. This study asks whether the admissibility regime of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 \(BSA\) and its supporting forensic institutions can secure the reliability of that evidence\. Through doctrinal analysis of the BSA, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, case law and official reports, it compares India with Canada, Australia, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the European Union on five dimensions\. Section 63 of the BSA retains and strengthens the former Section 65B certificate, adding a prescribed form, an expert’s signature and a hash value\. Yet a “reliability gap” persists: the certificate attests only the device’s regular operation and the record’s integrity, not attribution, forensic interpretation or acquisition practice\. Official data show substantial laboratory vacancies, a cyber\-forensic backlog and uneven, voluntary accreditation, whereas comparable systems rely on accreditation, regulators and extraction safeguards, not presumptions\. The study concludes that reliability requires regulating the forensic process between seizure and production: a statutory chain\-of\-custody duty with hashing at extraction, a certificate disclosing method and accreditation status, defence access to the forensic image, and safeguards for device examination\. A statutory presumption of integrity should await those reforms\.

## [Bridging Compressed Communication and Local Steps via Spectral Method in Federated Learning](../publications/6beb77962b0e7600ae8b.md)

Dmitriy Bystrov; George Chirkov; Daniil Medyakov; Dmitry Bylinkin; Aleksandr Beznosikov

Federated Learning \(FL\) enables collaborative training of complex models across large\-scale networks of edge devices while keeping data localized\. However, data heterogeneity and high communication overhead remain fundamental bottlenecks\. Recently, the spectral optimizer Muon has demonstrated remarkable advantages over Adam\-like methods in centralized training\. While recent efforts have attempted to transition Muon to FL, naive integrations into traditional architectures fail short\. Crucially, existing approaches do not support the the communication compression and local steps \-\-\- the two foundational techniques of efficient FL\. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel spectral FL method that utilizes both local updates and compression\. We establish rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, notably eliminating the restrictive bounded heterogeneity condition\. Empirical evaluation on standard image classification benchmarks validates the efficiency and robustness of our approach\.

## [Specimen\-based records of the rarely collected weevil Cyamobolus sturmii Boheman, 1837 \(Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Molytinae\) from the Yaeyama Islands, southwestern Japan, with the first record from Iriomote Island and notes on adult microhabitat](../publications/6beca69a569ea5745bcb.md)

Kyôgo Hosaka; Nakatada Wachi; Kosei Hirai; Shû Arai; Hiroaki Kojima

We report recent specimen\-based records of the rarely collected weevil Cyamobolus sturmii Boheman, 1837 from Ishigaki Island, together with the first record from Iriomote Island, in the Yaeyama Islands, southwestern Japan\. Adults were found during the daytime inside presumed emergence holes in dead wood of Diospyros maritima Blume on Ishigaki Island, providing new information on adult microhabitat\. These records update the known distribution of C\. sturmii in Japan and illustrate the value of documenting specimen\-based occurrence data for species poorly represented in public biodiversity databases\.

## [Designing intergroup interaction in social virtual reality: avatar identity\-cue visibility and environmental plausibility](../publications/6befa1a39da3382a428b.md)

Timor Schwartz Miler; Nili Steinfeld

Social Virtual Reality \(SVR\) enables designers to configure the conditions under which users meet and interact\. This qualitative study examines two design dimensions in intergroup encounters: the visibility of identity cues in avatars, which governs which social group categories are immediately available to participants, and the plausibility of the environment, which governs which everyday interactional scripts are available for acting on them\. 166 Israeli participants from the Haredi and Ethiopian Israeli minorities, and the Jewish non\-Haredi majority population, took part in structured encounters across three theoretically selected designed configurations: a plausible environment with avatars displaying visible identity cues, the same environment with identity\-neutral avatars, and a less plausible environment with visible identity cues\. Session recordings, observational notes, open\-ended questionnaires and semi\-structured interviews were analyzed through inductive thematic analysis and compared across configurations descriptively\. Where identity cues were visible, participants referred more often to appearance and group affiliation, formed group\-based connections, and adapted their communication to others’ perceived backgrounds\. Where avatars were identity\-neutral, recognition was available through names, accents and interactional style\. The less plausible environment was associated with more extended and exploratory dialogue, the plausible setting with rapid, task\-focused agreement\. Proximity\-based affiliation, humor, embodied communication and interpersonal familiarization appeared across all configurations\. Technological proficiency, unevenly distributed along the same social lines the encounter was meant to bridge, was translated into initiative and leadership, somewhat eroding the equal status condition intergroup contact emphasizes\. The study positions SVR as a designed social environment and draws design implications for intergroup encounters\.

## [Altered prefrontal suppression of striatal activity during intrusive images in obsessive‐compulsive disorder](../publications/6c049837ca2d2272f32b.md)

Anaïs Vandevelde; Sonia Dollfus; Pierre Gagnepain

BACKGROUND: Current models of obsessive\-compulsive disorder \(OCD\) emphasize dysfunction in frontostriatal circuits that support flexible behavioral control, leading to impulsive and compulsive actions\. However, how these disruptions contribute to obsessions and intrusive thoughts remains poorly understood\. Clarifying these mechanisms is essential for understanding cognitive control deficits in OCD\. METHOD: We examined intrusive memories elicited by emotional and neutral scenes in individuals with OCD \(N = 24\) and healthy controls \(N = 21\)\. Participants learned scene\-cue associations and were later instructed to suppress memory retrieval when presented with reminder cues\. Functional magnetic resonance imaging \(fMRI\) measured neural activity during suppression\. Generalization of findings with alternative materials was assessed in larger samples of healthy controls \(N = 73\) and individuals with post\-traumatic stress disorder \(PTSD; N = 55\)\. RESULTS: fMRI analyses showed preserved activity in frontoparietal, basal ganglia, and limbic regions in individuals with OCD, even during emotional intrusion suppression\. However, unlike healthy controls, individuals with OCD failed to suppress striatal activity during intrusive memory, regardless of emotional content\. Connectivity analyses indicated that this hyperactivity reflected reduced top\-down inhibitory control, a disruption associated with greater obsessive symptom severity\. Test of generalizability confirmed the role of frontostriatal downregulation in controlling intrusive thoughts and showed that this alteration was specific to OCD\. CONCLUSIONS: These findings emphasize the central role of frontostriatal circuits in regulating intrusive thinking\. Obsessions in OCD may result from disrupted inhibitory mechanisms that normally restrict access to striatal\-dependent information, contributing to persistent intrusive thoughts\.

## [Mathematical Modeling of Student Enrollment Trends in Higher Education in Nepal](../publications/6c0f0bf6f1becb444dae.md)

Prem Kumar Nayak; Suresh Kumar Sahani

Rapid enrollment growth in Nepal’s higher education sector has outpaced the expansion of institutional capacity, faculty strength, and public investment\. This study analyzed historical enrollment trends and compared mathematical models to generate projections for sectoral planning\. Secondary data from the University Grants Commission Nepal, the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, and the Central Bureau of Statistics covered the academic years 2016/17–2025/26\. Linear regression, exponential growth, and logistic \(Verhulst\) growth models were fitted using least\-squares estimation and evaluated using the coefficient of determination \(R²\)\. Enrollment increased from approximately 371,000 to 749,392 students, corresponding to a compound annual growth rate of approximately 8\.1%\. All three models closely fitted the historical observations, with R² values of 0\.987, 0\.984, and 0\.987 for the linear, exponential, and logistic models, respectively\. The logistic model incorporated finite enrollment capacity, estimating a long\-run carrying capacity of approximately 1\.57 million students\. Under current conditions, it projected approximately 912,000 students by 2030, compared with 888,000 under the linear model and more than one million under the exponential model\. Structural analysis identified an increase in management education’s enrollment share from 39% in 2015 to 47\.1% in 2025 and a gender parity index of 1\.3 in 2023/24\. Community and private campuses enrolled 62% of students but were not required to report full\-time faculty data, constraining assessment of staffing capacity\. The findings indicate continued enrollment growth alongside capacity and reporting challenges\. The study provides a quantitative basis for capacity\-sensitive planning and emphasizes proportionate investment in faculty recruitment, infrastructure, and quality assurance to support sustainable expansion\.

## [Job satisfaction, psychological well\-being, and movement facilitation self\-efficacy among primary school classroom teachers](../publications/6c1268b8aa0d06b3b5e7.md)

Arzu Pekğöz Çeviker; Mahmut Karakaya; Fatma Özoğlu; Yener Aksoy; Varol Tutal; Gamze Dağdeviren; Hüseyin Şimşek; Jindong Chang; Zhuoling Lei; Quanrui Tang

Introduction This study examined the direct and indirect relationships among primary school classroom teachers’ job satisfaction, psychological well\-being, and movement facilitation self\-efficacy in physical education and games lessons using structural equation modeling \(SEM\)\. Method A quantitative, cross\-sectional correlational design was employed\. Data were collected from 320 classroom teachers working in Ankara, Türkiye\. The Minnesota Job Satisfaction Scale, the short form of the Psychological Well\-Being Scale, and the Teacher Self\-Efficacy Scale for Providing Physical Activity in the Classroom were administered\. The measurement model was validated through confirmatory factor analysis, and convergent and discriminant validity were established\. The structural model was tested using maximum likelihood estimation, and mediation was examined via 5,000 bootstrap resamples\. Results Results indicated that job satisfaction was strongly and positively associated with psychological well\-being \( β = 0\.64, p &lt; 0\.001\), and psychological well\-being was significantly and positively associated with movement facilitation self\-efficacy \( β = 0\.39, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Job satisfaction was also significantly and positively associated with movement facilitation self\-efficacy \( β = 0\.27, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Bootstrap analysis revealed a significant indirect association through psychological well\-being \( β \_indirect = 0\.25, 95% CI \[0\.17, 0\.34\]\)\. The model accounted for 39% of the variance in movement facilitation self\-efficacy\. Conclusion Findings suggest that teachers’ job satisfaction and psychological resources are important correlates of movement facilitation self\-efficacy\. By situating self\-efficacy within the specific context of physical activity promotion, this study integrates occupational well\-being theory with school\-based physical activity research and highlights implications for teacher support policies and instructional capacity development\.

## [INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT DESIGN IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: FRAMING THE NEED, SHAPING THE USE](../publications/6c14c706eb39b0940fc7.md)

Maria Poli; Fotini Maniou; Ioanna Maniou; Maria Manola

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly embedded in physical products, from domestic appliances and vehicles to medical devices and wearables, yet the success of such products depends less on algorithmic performance than on whether people understand, trust and meaningfully integrate them into everyday life\. This paper examines the contribution of industrial product design to the current need for, and use of, AI\. Through a conceptual and integrative narrative review of literature in design research, human–computer interaction \(HCI\), computational design and AI ethics, it develops an analytical framework of five contributions: \(1\) framing human needs so that AI addresses problems worth solving; \(2\) making AI capabilities legible through form, interaction and feedback; \(3\) calibrating trust and control; \(4\) embedding AI in sustainable and ethical product lifecycles; and \(5\) integrating AI as a tool within the design process itself\. The analysis indicates that industrial design acts as a mediating layer between technological capability and human practice, and that its contribution lies as much in deciding where AI should not be used as in enabling it\. The paper closes with implications for practice, education and policy, and five propositions for empirical testing\.

## [“ChatGPT Says You’re Wrong\!” How Generative AI Exposes the Fragility of Explanation\-Centered Pedagogy](../publications/6c1f957930ad9b1d8706.md)

Jon Billsberry; Albert Munoz; Véronique Ambrosini

In this essay, we examine a growing tension in management education revealed when students use generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT to question and challenge their educators\. We argue that these encounters expose a contest over educational authority\. Management education has long relied on explanation\-centered pedagogy, allowing authority to rest on theoretical articulation rather than on the demonstrable development of students’ judgment and capability to act\. Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) destabilizes this arrangement by making fluent explanation ubiquitous, inexpensive, and readily contestable\. Our provocation is that business schools have misdiagnosed this as primarily a technological problem when it more fundamentally reveals the fragility of explanation\-based authority\. We contribute by explaining how explanation became a scalable and defensible proxy for forms of managerial capability that are difficult to observe and assess, and why generative AI now devalues that currency\. We call for authority to be rebuilt around capability\-oriented education organized at the program level, with theory repositioned as a resource for interpreting, guiding, challenging, and evaluating action\. This requires coordinated work by educators, program leaders, deans, and university administrators to make students’ developing capabilities visible, cumulative, and assessable\.

## [Impact of supportive virtual characters on presence and pain perception](../publications/6c3157950c76e781f6ca.md)

Isabel Neumann; Paul Pauli; Ivo Käthner

Introduction The benefit of social virtual characters is of particular interest in the context of digital health interventions\. The present study aimed to gain a deeper understanding of the social influence of virtual characters in the context of social pain modulation\. To this end, we investigated how virtual characters varying in perceived agency and perceived empathy impact the social influence on users in the context of social pain modulation\. Methods In this mixed design study, healthy participants \( N = 98\) were immersed in a virtual laboratory and underwent three within conditions\. In two of these conditions, a virtual character supported the participants verbally immediately before heat pain stimulation\. In one of these support conditions, the virtual character was presented as empathic, in another as unempathetic\. The third within condition served as control condition\. In this condition, no virtual human was present, and no social support was provided\. The perceived agency of the virtual characters served as between\-subjects factor\. Participants in the avatar group were led to believe that another participant controlled the virtual characters\. Participants in the agent group were told that they interacted with a computer\. However, in both conditions, virtual characters were computer\-controlled\. Pain ratings, presence ratings, and psychophysiological measurements were recorded\. Results Participants reported a higher feeling of presence and social presence in conditions with virtual characters compared to the control condition\. The avatar group showed higher skin conductance levels than the agent group\. Virtual verbal support did not affect pain responses\. Conclusion The current study contributes to insights into the use of virtual characters in the context of social pain modulation\. However, future research is needed to unravel the direct effects of virtual social support on pain perception\.

## [Environmental indicator changes associated with solar photovoltaic plants: A data\-driven multi\-regional assessment](../publications/6c3950463e1a22241b01.md)

Jia Zhang; Yadong Ge; Zaixin Li; Zhenchao Li; Yibo Wang; Junyu Tao; Beibei Yan; Guanyi Chen

With the rapid expansion of photovoltaic \(PV\) construction, the potential environmental impact of PV power plants has become a crucial consideration for large scale development\. This study develops a machine learning\-based model, termed the PV Environmental Indicators Forecasting \(EIF\) model, to predict the changes in typical environmental indicators caused by PV plants\. Using one\-year environmental monitoring data from four representative PV plants across major climate zones and application scenarios in China, the model enables prediction of six atmospheric and soil environmental indicators for shaded and non\-shaded areas of PV plants, including Atmospheric Temperature \(AT\), Atmospheric Humidity \(AH\), Deep Soil Temperature \(DST\), Shallow Soil Temperature \(SST\), Deep Soil Moisture Content \(DSMC\), and Shallow Soil Moisture Content \(SSMC\)\. Among the tested algorithms, the random forest model achieves the best predictive performance\. Under the selected hyperparameters, the PV EIF model yields high accuracy for the six environmental indicators in the internal test dataset, with an average R 2 of 0\.99 and RMSE of 0\.93\. External validation using field data from two additional PV plants in Hami and Wujiaqu further support the model’s predictive capability under comparable climatic and fixed\-layout PV conditions, with average R 2 values of 0\.90 and 0\.95, respectively\. This study provides an effective framework for forecasting PV\-induced changes in typical environmental indicators\. The proposed approach is particularly applicable to fixed\-layout, ground\-mounted PV systems under climatic and deployment conditions similar to those represented in the monitored datasets, and it can support environmental assessment and ecological design during PV planning\.

## [Students&\#x27; Perceptions of Online Lectures in Mechanical Engineering Vocational Education](../publications/6c4aee01eff730acf36c.md)

Wahyu Efendi Manullang; Ikhsanudin Ikhsanudin; Hamid Abdillah

Online lectures have remained relevant beyond the emergency conditions of the COVID\-19 pandemic; however, their effectiveness depends on students&\#x27; access to technology, opportunities for interaction, comprehension of learning materials, and learning motivation\. This phenomenological study explored students&\#x27; perceptions of online lectures in the Mechanical Engineering Vocational Education Study Program at Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa University, focusing on adaptation to online learning, social interaction, comprehension of instructional materials, and learning motivation\. The study involved 15 students who were purposively selected based on their previous experience with online lectures\. Data were collected through semistructured interviews, observations, and document analysis and were analyzed through data reduction, data display, conclusion drawing and verification, and the identification and organization of phenomenological meaning units\. The findings revealed that students appreciated the flexibility of online lectures in terms of time and location, accessibility, and convenience when attending in\-person classes was difficult\. Google Meet, Zoom, Google Classroom, and WhatsApp were the most frequently reported platforms used for online learning\. However, students generally experienced greater difficulty understanding instructional materials because of limited opportunities for direct clarification and peer interaction\. Unstable internet connections, inadequate technological devices, unfavorable learning environments, and reduced social interaction negatively affected students&\#x27; concentration and learning motivation\. Online interactions were perceived as more structured but less personally engaging than face\-to\-face interactions\. Furthermore, practice\-oriented courses presented particular challenges when hands\-on training was replaced by theoretical instruction\. These findings suggested that effective online learning in mechanical engineering vocational education required reliable technological infrastructure, interactive instructional strategies, accessible learning materials, lecturers&\#x27; digital competencies, and sustained academic and social support\.

## [Sources of Cryptocurrency Return Predictability: Econometric and Machine Learning Evidence Across Market States](../publications/6c51cbd02d2929e42561.md)

Jie Xu

This study examines whether nonlinear machine\-learning methods improve cross\-sectional cryptocurrency return prediction beyond parsimonious linear benchmarks\. Using a dynamic point\-in\-time cryptocurrency universe, we construct weekly characteristics capturing size, past returns, liquidity, risk, and return distributions and compare OLS, Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost, a neural network, and forecast combinations under strictly out\-of\-sample evaluation\. Cryptocurrency returns remain difficult to predict in levels, and greater model complexity does not generate monotonic forecasting gains\. Random Forest delivers the strongest rank prediction, while predictive importance is concentrated in risk, return\-distribution, and past\-return characteristics\. Importantly, the relative forecast\-loss performance of nonlinear models improves as the probability of a high\-volatility market state increases, although this improvement does not translate into comparably stronger cross\-sectional rankings\. Forecast\-sorted portfolio returns are also statistically imprecise\. Overall, the evidence indicates that cryptocurrency return predictability is characterized by a concentrated but time\-varying information structure, for which model flexibility has conditional rather than universal value\.

## [Rectal colonization with multidrug\-resistant organisms in adult acute leukemia patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a retrospective, longitudinal, single\-center study](../publications/6c55baf46b6a0d453774.md)

Edoardo Tamellini; Chiara Bonetto; Annarita Mazzariol; Fulvia Mazzaferri; Erica Diani; Francesca Tolio; Sara Pagnin; Alessandra Vatteroni; Angela Crema; Alberto Schena; Cristina Tecchio

Introduction Rectal colonization with multidrug\-resistant organisms \(MDROs\) represents a frequent issue in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation \(allo\-HSCT\) for acute leukemia\. However, the prognostic significance of MDRO\-colonization in these patients remains debated\. Methods This retrospective, longitudinal, single\-center study included 100 patients with acute myeloid or lymphoblastic leukemia treated at Verona University Hospital from diagnosis to allo\-HSCT\. MDRO\-colonization was monitored by rectal swab at admission and weekly during hospitalization\. Colonized patients underwent targeted antibiotic therapy when clinically required\. Aim of the study To assess epidemiology, timing, and impact of rectal MDRO\-colonization on infection occurrence, infection\-related mortality \(IRM\) within day \+100, overall survival \(OS\), and transplant\-related mortality \(TRM\)\. Results Rectal colonization with 44 MDRO strains was detected in 35 \(35%\) patients undergoing allo\-HSCT, either at hospital admission \(45\.7%\) or during hospitalization \(54\.3%\)\. Enterobacterales accounted for 72\.7% of MDROs, with 68\.5% of colonizing strains being detected during previous hospital stays for induction or consolidation therapies\. MDRO\-related bloodstream infections \(BSI\) occurred in 9 \(9%\) patients, 7 \(77\.8%\) of whom being rectal carriers\. IRM within day \+100 was null\. OS was significantly lower in MDRO\-carriers as compared to non\-carriers only at univariate analysis\. TRM did not differ significantly between the two groups in both univariate and multivariate analyses\. Conclusion Despite the limitations of a single\-center retrospective study, our data show that careful monitoring of rectal colonization and prompt use of targeted antibiotics may temper the negative impact of MDRO\-related infections in adult acute leukemia patients undergoing allo\-HSCT, even in the setting of a higher rate of BSIs\.

## [Mindful Mind: Understanding Internal Dialogue, Managing Emotions, and Finding Calm Through Communication with the Self](../publications/6c5fc78a8b364d929b5b.md)

Rahma Yurliani; Rahmi Putri Rangkuti; Indri Kemala Nasution; Eka Ervika

This study examines how internal dialogue functions as intrapersonal communication, how mindful awareness supports emotional regulation, and how deliberate self\-communication can contribute to psychological calm\. A non\-empirical conceptual design was employed by synthesizing theoretical propositions and empirical findings concerning self\-talk, inner speech, mindfulness, self\-compassion, cognitive reframing, emotion regulation, and breathing\-based calming practices\. The analysis organized these materials into functional relationships linking internal interpretation, emotional activation, regulatory awareness, and self\-directed action\. The findings indicate that internal dialogue can operate through supportive or critical modes, while cognitive distortions such as all\-or\-nothing thinking, catastrophizing, and mind reading can intensify emotional difficulty\. Mindful self\-communication supports regulation through emotional labeling, psychological distancing, balanced reframing, and the Pause–Reflect–Choose sequence\. Self\-compassion and reality\-based affirmations further strengthen constructive self\-relating, while breathing practices support physiological calming\. These elements were integrated into the Mindful Mind framework consisting of Notice, Name, Pause, and Reframe, supported by daily intention setting, mindful breathing, non\-judgmental review, and journaling\. The study contributes an integrated communication\-based model for reflective learning, emotional literacy, and everyday self\-regulation while recognizing that severe psychological distress requires appropriate professional support\. The framework positions calm not as the absence of difficult emotion, but as regulated engagement through aware, constructive, and deliberate self\-response\.

## [Review of Enshittification: Why Everything Suddenly Got Worse and What to Do About It, by Cory Doctorow](../publications/6c70c4e047c86af01ec3.md)

## [Institutional Transformation Of Islamic Higher Education Institutions Based On Autonomy, Governance, Data, And Islamic Values](../publications/6c766d28a831890ea6e4.md)

Nur Muhabibudin

Institutional transformation in Islamic higher education cannot be understood merely as organizational restructuring or compliance with governance documentation\. It also concerns how institutions exercise authority, lead change, manage information, make decisions, and connect Islamic values with institutional practices\. This study aims to analyze the mechanisms linking institutional autonomy, leadership, governance, data utilization, deliberation and quality assurance in the institutional transformation of STAI Sangatta Kutai Timur\. The study employs a qualitative approach with a case study design\. Data sources include institutional leaders, departments and study programs, the Quality Assurance Unit, the governing foundation, observations of institutional activities, and documents such as the Statutes, organizational and working procedures, institutional development plans, strategic plans, operational plans, internal quality assurance documents, standard operating procedures, the official website, and the academic information system\. The analysis focuses on five themes: autonomy, leadership, governance as practice, data\-driven decision\-making, and the integration of Islamic values\. The available findings indicate that authority at STAI Sangatta is distributed hierarchically among the foundation, institutional leadership, departments, study programs, and supporting units; leadership operates through cross\-unit coordination; governance is supported by institutional documents, quality systems, and information systems; and decision\-making combines information, analysis, coordination, and deliberation\. The conceptual contribution of the study is directed toward an institutional transformation model that positions data as an empirical basis, deliberation as a mechanism for collective consideration, and Islamic values as an ethical orientation\. The model extends the understanding of Islamic education management from the integration of structures and functions toward an explanation of decision\-making mechanisms that connect autonomy, governance, data, participation, and values\.

## [AIoT quality, supply chain intelligence, and sustainable competitive advantage: A study of Taiwan’s semiconductor industry](../publications/6c8a08ac134908638cfe.md)

Jung‐Yu Lai; Yu\-Rou Cheng; Cian\-Cih Huang

Driven by the demands of 5 G and high\-performance computing, Taiwan’s semiconductor industry is increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence of Things \(AIoT\) to sustain its cluster\-based competitive advantage\. While research has highlighted the potential benefits of AI, IoT, and big data analytics in supply chain management, the mechanism by which AIoT quality links to sustainable competitive advantage \(SCA\) through supply chain processes remains underexplored\. This study investigates how AIoT quality influences supply chain intelligence \(SCI\), supply chain quality management practices, and supply chain management performance, thereby driving sustainable competitive advantage\. Empirical data were collected through a questionnaire survey of firms in Taiwan’s semiconductor industry and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The results reveal that AIoT quality significantly enhances supply chain intelligence, which serves as a pivotal mediating mechanism that strengthens quality management practices and operational performance, ultimately fostering sustainable competitive advantage\. These findings demonstrate that the value of AIoT extends beyond technology adoption and depends on the quality of AIoT\-enabled information and systems and their ability to support supply chain intelligence and management capabilities, thereby advancing the understanding of how AIoT contributes to sustainable competitive advantage\. Practically, the findings provide guidance for semiconductor firms to improve AIoT quality and intelligence capabilities to strengthen supply chain coordination and long\-term competitiveness\.

## [Intelligent Academic Software: Transforming Higher Education through AI\-Driven Learning Ecosystems](../publications/6c8b697bfcea839eb69c.md)

Sandeep Hanumant Bhokare; Siddhant kumar Vasantrao Wadmare

The digital transformation of higher education has accelerated with the integration of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) technologies into academic software systems\. Intelligent Academic Software \(IAS\) represents a paradigm shift from static learning management systems toward dynamic, data\-driven learning ecosystems capable of personalization, predictive analytics, automated assessment, and institutional decision support\. This study proposes a comprehensive AI\-driven learning ecosystem model integrating adaptive learning engines, intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics modules, and administrative automation frameworks\. A multi\-institutional dataset comprising 1,200 student records was analyzed using supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to evaluate performance prediction, engagement analytics, and risk detection accuracy\. Experimental results demonstrate improved academic performance forecasting \(92% accuracy\), enhanced learner engagement, and optimized resource allocation\. The study contributes to AI\-enabled higher education transformation by presenting a scalable intelligent software architecture aligned with ethical AI governance and institutional digital strategies\.

## [Fine‐Grained Hybrid Attention‐Aware Deep Learning Framework for Automated Multi‐Layer Cyberattack Detection in IoT‐Cloud Environments](../publications/6c8b95fbd41cb2270481.md)

B\.M\. Sangeetha; N\. Suguna; S\. M\. Uma

ABSTRACT The integration of Internet of Things \(IoT\) with cloud platforms has generated an extremely decentralized, data‐driven network that is transforming industries\. At the same time, the integration poses intricate cybersecurity challenges because of scalability requirements, device heterogeneity, and an evolving threat environment\. Conventional security metrics are inadequate in some circumstances, creating a necessity for adaptive, intelligent, and proactive defense modules\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) offers beneficial capabilities for intrusion detection, predictive threat modeling, anomaly detection, and malware analysis\. Moreover, deep learning \(DL\) models have proved exceptional effectiveness in automatically learning intricate patterns from larger‐scale network traffic information, allowing precise identification of advanced cyberattacks in IoT‐cloud systems\. Therefore, this manuscript presents a Fine‐Grained Hybrid Attention‐Aware Deep Learning Framework for Multi‐Layer Cyberattack Detection \(FGHADL‐MLCD\)\. The major intention of the proposed model is to enhance the reliability and intelligence of cyberattack detection in large‐scale IoT‐cloud infrastructures\. The FGHADL‐MLCD approach operates through a sequence of stages, including preprocessing, attribute selection, cyberattack classification, and model optimization\. Initially, the collected network traffic data from TON‐IoT and Edge‐IIoT datasets undergo preprocessing operations such as data cleaning, label encoding, feature scaling, and dataset splitting to ensure consistency of input data\. Following that, an effective attribute selection mechanism is introduced using the Boruta feature selection technique, which identifies the most relevant network traffic features\. For multi‐layer cyberattack detection and classification, the proposed model employs a bidirectional temporal convolutional network integrated with an attention mechanism\. Furthermore, the training process of the deep learning model is optimized using the Adam optimizer\. To assess the model&\#x27;s effectiveness, extensive experiments are conducted using the benchmark IoT cybersecurity datasets\. The experimental results indicate that the proposed technique achieves improved cyberattack detection performance compared to recent models\. Thus, the proposed model delivers a reliable solution for securing IoT‐cloud infrastructures against diverse and evolving cyber threats\.

## [Explainable ArcFace\-Based Deep Metric Learning for Multimodal Biometric Recognition and Authentication Systems](../publications/6c983e59c1e3ccdb3b66.md)

Ram Mohan Babu Srividya; Arthanari Latha

Background: Biometric recognition offers a reliable solution for recognizing individuals based on unique physiological traits such as fingerprints and iris patterns\. Fingerprint\-based systems are widely employed because of their simplicity and distinct ridge structures, but they are generally affected by partial, worn, and noisy captures\. Iris recognition provides higher accuracy and stability because iris patterns remain largely unchanged over an individual’s lifetime\. This study presents the Fingerprint\-Iris Feature Fusion with Deep Metric Learning \(FIF\-DML\) approach for multimodal biometric recognition and authentication\. Methods: The proposed model learns features using two parallel EfficientNet\-B0 networks that independently extract deep representations from fingerprint and iris inputs\. These extracted features are then fused at the feature level to form a unified representation\. In addition, ArcFace\-based metric learning maps the fused features into a compact embedding space, enhancing inter\-class separability and intra\-class compactness\. In the identification stage, a query fingerprint\-iris pair is converted into a 128\-dimensional embedding and matched with gallery embeddings using cosine similarity to predict the identity\. Finally, Grad\-CAM visualizes the regions that most influence the model’s final decision\. Results: We conduct extensive experimental analysis of the proposed FIF\-DML model on the Multimodal Iris Fingerprint Biometric dataset, achieving 97\.33% precision and demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods\. Conclusion: The results confirm that the proposed FIF\-DML model provides a reliable and effective solution for secure biometric authentication\.
