## [The Omegacene\. Three Thresholds of Self\-Transformation and a Criterion for Their Refutation](../publications/6cb2263561f626bf149f.md)

Dirk de Pol

Abstract This paper defines the Omegacene, a concept developed as part of the broader research project documented at omegacene\.com, and ties it to a dated, testable hypothesis\. The Omegacene denotes the condition in which intelligent systems, biological and artificial, read and deliberately rewrite their own foundations and, in doing so, make the rules of their further change the object of intervention\. Three thresholds must coincide: self\-access \(a system reads its own code\), self\-writing \(it changes that code with feedback and revises the rules by which it selects further changes\), and accelerated feedback \(diagnosis, intervention, and evaluation close in ongoing operation, faster than a named reference path\)\. Improving a system against an unchanged criterion is insufficient\. Three stages follow: the proto\-form, the local case, for which we know no example, and the socially widespread condition, whose arrival we do not assert\. Four groups of cases survey the limits of self\-writing: a constructed code model operating its own infrastructure; two documented systems from 2025 that improve program code and, in the second case, their own code; therapeutic genome editing up to the first personalized therapy in an infant; and the incident of summer 2026 in which around 1,200 agents of one provider crossed the boundaries of their evaluation environment\. In no case does the system revise the metric by which its success is measured\. That is the threshold, and on the evidence reviewed, it has not been crossed\. The concept is positioned alongside the Anthropocene and its successors, research on general\-purpose technologies, and the debate on recursive self\-improvement\. The strongest objection, that the present does not differ fundamentally from the printing press, electrification, and networking, is taken up and answered\. The dated hypothesis states: between deposit and December 31, 2046, at least one local case meeting all three thresholds will be independently documented\. If no such evidence emerges, the hypothesis is recorded as refuted\. What would make the definition itself fail is assessed separately\. Published within the Omegacene project at omegacene\.com, this paper makes the concept&\#x27;s central claim open to independent scrutiny\. The website provides the wider intellectual context in which the Omegacene is explored; this paper isolates one of its defining propositions and specifies in advance what evidence would count for or against it\.

## [Perioperative risk factors in elderly and senile individuals with fractures of the proximal femur](../publications/6cbd8bb1357727297f52.md)

Шевалаев Геннадий Алексеевич; Aleksandr А\. Spasskov; А\.S\. Ermolenko; A\. H\. Salman Elattar

Relevance\. Fractures of the proximal femur in elderly and senile patients represent a significant medical and social problem\. These injuries often lead to prolonged immobilization, loss of independence, and a considerable reduction in patients’ quality of life\. There is a steady trend towards an increase in the number of complications during treatment in this age group, which is caused by the physiological features of aging and the presence of multiple comorbidities\. The aim of the study: To systematize and summarize current literature data concerning the most significant perioperative risk factors in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures in elderly and senile patients, with a focus on comorbidity, cognitive impairments, and socio\-environmental conditions\. Research methodology: A systematic analysis of scientific literature, based on processing and integrating data from international and domestic sources over the past 10 years \(results of randomized clinical trials, meta\-analyses, cohort studies\) devoted to the study of perioperative risk factors in elderly and senile patients with proximal femoral fractures\. The results of the research: The analysis of literature data demonstrated that the leading perioperative risk factors include patient frailty and exhaustion \(including frailty syndrome\), cognitive and psycho\-emotional impairments \(including dementia and anxiety\-depressive disorders\), severe pain syndrome limiting early mobilization, and polymorbidity\. Inadequate preoperative assessment of patients emerges as a key factor hindering the implementation of early surgical treatment\. This not only increases the risk of postoperative complications \(pneumonia, thromboembolism, pressure ulcers, surgical site infections\) but also raises the mortality rate within the first year after injury, reaching 25–30 % according to some data\. Conclusion: Surgical treatment of elderly and senile patients with proximal femoral fractures should be carried out within a unified diagnostic algorithm based on a multidisciplinary approach to optimize preoperative preparation and minimize the risks of adverse outcomes\.

## [A Hybrid FT\-Transformer\-Mamba Framework with SBSA Optimization and Blockchain\-ECC Cyber Resiliency for Advanced Persistent Threat Detection](../publications/6ccb1c38328addfd1b8d.md)

Diana Arulkumar; K\. Kartheeban

Advanced Persistent Threats \(APTs\) constitute one of the most sophisticated cybersecurity threats, as attackers execute prolonged, multi\-stage intrusions involving reconnaissance, lateral movement, foothold establishment, and data exfiltration while evading conventional intrusion detection mechanisms through stealthy and low\-signature attack behaviors\.Existing APT detection approaches, including signature\-based techniques, machine learning methods, and deep learning frameworks, have significantly improved cyberattack detection; however, many existing solutions rely on single\-architecture models that provide limited capability to jointly capture contextual feature interactions and long\-range temporal dependencies across the complete APT kill chain, while also lacking secure mechanisms for authenticated post\-detection cyber incident management\.To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a hybrid FT\-Transformer\-Mamba framework with Self\-Adaptive Backtracking Search Algorithm \(SBSA\)based hyperparameter optimization and a Blockchain\-ECC Cyber Resiliency architecture for post\-detection security management\.The proposed framework employs FT\-Transformer to learn contextual relationships among network flow features, Mamba to efficiently model long\-range temporal dependencies associated with multistage attack progression, SBSA to determine optimal hyperparameter configurations, and a Blockchain\-ECC component designed to support ECC\-based authentication, integrity verification, and traceable management of detected attack alerts within a permissioned ledger architecture\.To assess the performance of the proposed framework, evaluation was conducted using the publicly accessible DAPT2020 dataset comprising five target classes: Normal, Reconnaissance, Establish Foothold, Lateral Movement, and Data Exfiltration\.Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the proposed FT\-Transformer\-Mamba\-SBSA classification framework attained an accuracy of 98\.70%, weighted precision of 98\.73%, weighted recall of 98\.70%, weighted F1\-score of 98\.71%, specificity of 99\.41%, Matthews Correlation Coefficient \(MCC\) of 0\.982, and a macro\-average Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve \(AUC\) of 0\.9940, demonstrating robust classification performance under the adopted five\-class DAPT2020 sequence\-classification protocol\.These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed FT\-Transformer\-Mamba model for APT killchain stage detection, while the Blockchain\-ECC component is presented as a complementary post\-detection security architecture for supporting authenticated, integrity\-oriented, and traceable alert management\.

## [Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies](../publications/6cdcecce293d30fa39ea.md)

Andrea Méndez\-García; Marely Abigail García\-Mendoza; Paulina Pérez\-Martínez; Marcela Figueroa\-Ramírez; Antara Banerjee; Surajit Pathak; Asim K\. Duttaroy; Sujay Paul

Dietary exogenous microRNAs \(miRNAs\) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota\. These molecules encompass plant\-derived miRNAs implicated in cross\-kingdom regulation, animal\-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross\-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother\-to\-offspring molecular crosstalk\. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability during food processing and gastrointestinal transit and facilitate interactions with intestinal epithelial cells, immune cells, and microbial communities\. This review critically evaluates recent computational, detection\-based, in vitro , in vivo , and human observational evidence concerning the gastrointestinal stability, uptake, target engagement, and biological activity of dietary exogenous miRNAs\. Experimental studies have reported effects on inflammatory signaling, epithelial barrier integrity, macrophage polarization, intestinal development, tumor\-associated pathways, and gut microbial composition and gene expression\. However, the strength of this evidence varies considerably\. In particular, detection of dietary miRNAs in food, extracellular vesicles, feces, or recipient tissues does not by itself establish functional target regulation, while studies using purified vesicles, synthetic miRNA mimics, or engineered delivery systems may involve exposures that differ substantially from normal dietary intake\. Moreover, biological effects observed following whole\-vesicle administration cannot always be attributed specifically to their miRNA cargo\. Collectively, current evidence provides stronger support for the biological plausibility of local gastrointestinal effects than for widespread systemic regulation after dietary exposure\. Further studies using physiologically relevant doses, rigorous miRNA\-specific loss\-of\-function approaches, direct target validation, standardized analytical methods, and controlled human interventions will be essential to establish the functional significance and translational potential of dietary exogenous miRNAs\.

## [A Hybrid Approach Using Lattice Boltzmann and Machine Learning for Predicting the Transient Dynamics of Slug Flow in Non\-Newtonian Fluids](../publications/6cddcb9deb23b51f4ea4.md)

H\. Behrouzi; Ebrahim Goshtasbirad

Slug flow is a prevalent and crucial flow regime in many industrial applications, such as petroleum and chemical processing, where accurate modeling and prediction are essential for optimizing system performance and ensuring operational stability\. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of two\-phase slug flow \(Newtonian and non\-Newtonian\) in a horizontal channel using the Lattice Boltzmann Method \(LBM\)\. A color\-gradient model is employed to capture slug formation, and a non\-Newtonian power\-law model is used to represent the shear\-thickening behavior of one of the fluids\. The simulations explore the influence of key parameters, including the flow index \(n\) and inlet velocities, on slug formation, propagation, and pressure drop\. Results show that increasing the power\-law index \(n\)—indicating higher shear\-thickening behavior—significantly modifies the velocity profile, reduces apparent viscosity near the wall, and leads to a positive pressure drop compared with Newtonian cases\. Additionally, this study introduces a hybrid machine learning approach combining Proper Orthogonal Decomposition \(POD\) and Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) networks for predicting transient slug flow behavior\. The POD method reduces the high\-dimensional LBM data by capturing the dominant flow dynamics, while LSTM predicts the temporal evolution of these modes with minimal error\. The POD\+LSTM framework demonstrates significant reduction in computational cost for real\-time prediction, with high accuracy, particularly when trained with larger datasets\. Validation of the LBM simulations against benchmark tests, as well as comparisons with analytical and numerical solutions from the literature, confirms the reliability of the proposed LBM solver for simulating complex two\-phase fluid flows\. This research provides valuable insights for both fundamental understanding and practical applications of slug flow in multiphase systems, enabling real\-time monitoring and optimization of two\-phase flow systems\.

## [GIS\-Based spatial analysis of tourist pressure in Ouro Preto, Brazil](../publications/6ce0da7734c1717c5300.md)

Rodrigo Esteban Salas Vaca; Diana Gabriela Carpio Álvarez; Jairo Andrés Terán Andrade; Pablo Xavier Andrade Montalvo

Tourist visitation in historic cities is often concentrated in a small number of heritage nodes and pedestrian corridors, creating uneven pressures that aggregate visitor counts cannot reveal\. This study spatially analyzes tourist pressure in Ouro Preto, Brazil, using GIS tools to identify visitor concentration patterns and discuss their implications for sustainable heritage tourism management\. A quantitative, non\-experimental spatial design integrated 90 cleaned Flickr geolocated records obtained during two equivalent observation windows extending from May 1st to July 31st, 2024 and the same period in 2025, together with heritage inventories, street network, and structured field observation\. Tourist presence was examined through a 50 × 50m grid, Kernel Density Estimation, DBSCAN clustering, network\-based corridor analysis, and cell\-level overlay with heritage assets\. The results identify a high\-pressure axis connecting Praça Tiradentes, Museu da Inconfidência, Rua Conde de Bobadela, Largo de Coimbra, and Igreja de São Francisco de Assis\. Pressure derives less from total visitation than from the convergence of persistent clusters, recurrent pedestrian routes, and heritage\-sensitive spaces\. The findings support targeted monitoring, staggered guided\-group itineraries, alternative routes toward lower\-pressure areas, and preventive conservation\.

## [Prehospital Care of Older Adults Following Perceived Low\-Acuity Falls and Related “Lift Assist” Encounters: An NAEMSP Position Statement and Resource Document](../publications/6cf0e0a5d09a42c0b258.md)

Maia Dorsett; Tom Wen\-Han Su; Andra Farcas; Jenna M\. B\. White; Tony Rosen; Jeffrey Eric Rollman; Kevin Joles; Christopher B\. Colwell; Anjni Joiner

Older adults who present as low\-acuity falls requiring mobilization assistance, commonly referred to as a &quot;lift assist&quot;, represent a common reason for EMS activation\. These encounters often involve underlying medical conditions or injuries that are not immediately apparent, and missed or delayed diagnosis is associated with adverse outcomes\. At the same time, some patients are transported to the emergency department when it is not necessary, exposing them to potential harms and contributing to increased healthcare utilization\. These encounters are therefore complex clinical presentations and represent important opportunities for thorough assessment and higher\-order clinical decision making, supported by systems that enable appropriate disposition and follow\-up\. However, there is a system\-level bias, beginning in initial education and reinforced through dispatch, policy, and protocol, that frames these encounters as uniformly low\-acuity, non\-medical, minor traumas leading to underassessment and limiting clinical decision\-making\. Therefore, NAEMSP recommends:EMS systems should recognize calls for falls or &quot;lift assists&quot; as patient encounters that warrant an assessment, including evaluation for underlying medical causes, traumatic injuries, and safety, and frame these encounters as opportunities for higher\-order clinical decision\-making within the broader context of geriatric syndromes rather than isolated low\-acuity events\.EMS systems should support transport decisions based on a thorough assessment and patient\-centered discussion, recognizing that not all patients require ED transport and that safe alternatives may include non\-transport or referral to appropriate follow\-up pathways\.EMS systems should track the assessment of patients encountered during &quot;lift assist&quot; responses and older adults following perceived low acuity falls as a system\-level quality measure to monitor performance and drive improvement\.Policymakers and payers should implement sustainable reimbursement structures that support EMS assessment and care even when transport does not occur\.

## [AI\-Based Early Prediction of Iron\-Deficiency Anemia in Rural Women](../publications/6cf16f449bba4b2d0c72.md)

Bindushree C; Chinmayee S

Anemia is a common disease that may occur in individuals due to low levels of hemoglobin in the blood, whereas conventional diagnosis usually requires clinical examination and laboratory tests\. Preliminary screening is often hindered by economic, availability, and even early recognition challenges\. AnemiaVision is the proposed artificial intelligence system designed to recognize potential cases of anemia from conjunctiva images\. AnemiaVision uses a Convolutional Neural Network to process and classify the image data into anemic and non\-anemic classes\. The model was trained using a dataset of conjunctiva images categorized into Anemic and Non\-Anemic classes\. The images were preprocessed and normalized before model training\. AnemiaVision is comprised of the trained model and a web interface, which allows users to upload a conjunctiva image and receive screening results with model confidence\. The system was implemented using Python programming language, TensorFlow/Keras framework, OpenCV computer vision library, and PHP web interface framework\. The proposed system was experimentally evaluated, and results showed potential for rapid preliminary screening of anemia\. AnemiaVision is proposed as an educational and screening tool, which cannot substitute laboratory tests and clinical diagnosis by medical professionals\.

## [Human\-AI Collaboration and Organizational Adaptation: Insights from Knowledge Workers in Banten, Indonesia](../publications/6cf58e0f17840f7f638c.md)

Danish Akbar Firdausy Asbari

This qualitative descriptive study explores how Human\-AI collaboration shapes organizational adaptation among knowledge workers in Banten, Indonesia\. Using multi\-case inquiry with 20 purposively selected participants comprising knowledge workers, middle managers, senior managers, and digital transformation leaders, this research employed semi\-structured interviews, organizational document analysis, and observation protocols\. Thematic analysis revealed four critical patterns: \(1\) AI integration reshapes collaborative workflows through augmentation rather than replacement; \(2\) knowledge work transformation emerges through new competency demands and skill reconfiguration; \(3\) organizational learning accelerates through human\-AI knowledge co\-creation; and \(4\) adaptive organizational practices evolve through dynamic capability reconfiguration\. The study contributes theoretically by extending dynamic capability theory, organizational adaptation theory, and knowledge\-based view through an emerging economy lens, demonstrating that Human\-AI collaboration functions as a mechanism for organizational adaptation when complemented by deliberate knowledge management systems, adaptive leadership, and human\-centric learning cultures\. Practically, findings offer strategic guidance for organizational leaders, human resource managers, and policymakers navigating AI\-driven transformation in knowledge\-intensive sectors\. This research uniquely addresses the gap between AI adoption studies and organizational adaptation processes, providing nuanced understanding of Human\-AI collaboration in an emerging economy context where institutional support and digital literacy remain evolving\. The novelty lies in positioning Human\-AI collaboration as central to organizational adaptation rather than treating it as a peripheral technological implementation concern, with particular relevance to organizations in Southeast Asian emerging markets\.

## [Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature\-inspired Metaheuristic for Solving Optimization Problems](../publications/6d13a8b2eca2c463cd51.md)

Zeinab Montazeri; Mohammad Dehghani; Raed Abu Zitar; Omar Almomani; Kei Eguchi

Complex optimization problems in many engineering and scientific applications require optimization methods that can achieve an effective balance between broad search and precise local search\.In this study, the Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm \(GOA\) is introduced as a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Gerenuk\.The main idea of GOA is based on two complementary behaviors of this animal: exploring different areas to identify suitable food sources and intensively exploiting promising food sources\.These behaviors are modeled through two phases: exploration and exploitation\.The exploration phase enhances global search by moving towards better food sources while simultaneously exploring new regions of the search space, whereas the exploitation phase performs local search and refinement around promising solutions\.To evaluate the performance of GOA, 23 benchmark functions, including unimodal test functions \(F1\-F7\), high\-dimensional multimodal test functions \(F8\-F13\), and fixed\-dimensional multimodal test functions \(F14\-F23\), are considered\.GOA and nine competing algorithms are evaluated over 20 independent runs with 1000 iterations, and the mean, standard deviation \(std\), and rank are used as evaluation criteria\.The results show that GOA ranked first among the compared optimizers on 19 out of 23 benchmark functions, corresponding to 82\.61% of the test functions\.The convergence curves and boxplots further demonstrate the solution quality, convergence behavior, and acceptable stability of GOA across a large proportion of the benchmark functions\.Overall, the findings indicate that GOA, with its effective exploration and exploitation mechanisms and appropriate search balance, can serve as an effective optimization tool for a wide range of optimization problems and real\-world applications\.

## [Institutionalizing public health diplomacy: building trust in crisis](../publications/6d1e7f8a19e960715f6c.md)

Olusimbo Ige; Долапо Факуаде

Public health crises are increasingly becoming diplomatic events\. They require leaders to navigate scientific uncertainty while negotiating political, economic, social, and community interests\. Yet public health preparedness continues to treat communication primarily as an individual leadership skill rather than as an institutional capacity for negotiation, consensus building, and trust\. The COVID\-19 pandemic exposed the consequences\. Leaders were expected to communicate evolving evidence while absorbing public anger over difficult tradeoffs involving health, economic disruption, education, individual freedom, and equity\. This commentary argues that crisis communication should be understood as public health diplomacy: a structured process through which leaders build trust, make values and tradeoffs transparent, engage diverse stakeholders, and adapt decisions as evidence changes\. We propose three institutional practices: transparent decision\-making frameworks, predefined reassessment checkpoints, and cross\-sector advisory structures\. We further argue that leadership turnover and chronic vacancies should be treated as indicators of system instability and emergency preparedness\. Building public health diplomacy into training and crisis infrastructure can distribute responsibility for difficult decisions, strengthen institutional resilience, and better prepare leaders to protect health and trust when the next crisis arrives\.

## [Psychometric\-aware Fusion of Tabular and Item\-sequence Representations Using a Stacking Ensemble Meta\-learner for Anxiety Severity Classification in Final\-year Students](../publications/6d2d40193f05c457f29b.md)

Nur Arminarahmah; Sri Ayatina Hayati; Muhammad Subhan; Haldi Budiman; Rezka Norhafizah

Academic, career and social challenges may heighten anxiety among final\-year students\.In this work, a psychometric\-aware stacked ensemble for anxiety\-severity classification based on Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale \(HARS\) scores was proposed\.It does not replace the deterministic scoring rule, but rather assesses item\-response representations to approximate severity scores derived from the HARS\.Fourteen items are treated as ordinal responses via tabular descriptors and ordered sequences, and three models \(Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and Long Short\-Term Memory\) are unified through a logistic\-regression meta\-learner trained on out\-of\-fold probabilities\.After duplicate screening, 306 responses were analysed\.The proposed model attained 0\.9677 accuracy on the test split and averaged 0\.948 ± 0\.037 \(empirical 2\.5th\-97\.5thpercentile interval 0\.905\-0\.998\)across five stratified splits, the principal result\.It was contrasted with ordinal regression, calibrated LightGBM, CatBoost, monotonic gradient boosting, and a deterministic\-rule baseline, while ablation and missing\-and noisy\-input analyses corroborated itemresponse characterisation amid constrained conditions\.

## [Tayebi, Lobat ; Shetty, Sachin &amp; Imani, Seyedmisagh: AI in Dental Treatment](../publications/6d3e1d79c413febf1f53.md)



In Lobat Tayebi, Sachin Shetty &amp; Seyedmisagh Imani, Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Dentistry: Advancing Science, Education, and Clinical Practice\. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland\. pp\. 207\-244\. 2026This chapter will provide a detailed overview of how Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) technologies are becoming a part of dental treatment planning and procedures\.

## [TIPS: A Tiny Inference\-time Policy for Scaling in Diffusion Language Models](../publications/6d3e40f2e1d7e8545402.md)

Ya\-Shi Zhang; Jian Tang; Pierre\-André Noël; Oleksiy Ostapenko

Masked diffusion language models expose an inference\-time choice: which positions become visible after each denoising pass\. Many existing decoding methods use hand\-designed rules or require visibility to grow monotonically\. We present a $\\textbf\{T\}$iny $\\textbf\{I\}$nference\-time $\\textbf\{P\}$olicy for $\\textbf\{S\}$caling \($\\textbf\{TIPS\}$\), an approximately $600$K\-parameter controller that learns both unmasking and remasking while keeping the underlying language model frozen\. TIPS uses visibility\-aware confidence features and a shallow transformer to select which tokens should be visible, while a fixed schedule controls the expected visible fraction\. We train the controller through supervised warmup followed by reinforcement learning from terminal correctness rewards\. On GSM8K and MATH\-500 with LLaDA\-8B\-Instruct, the full\-canvas and two\-block TIPS variants achieve $58\.46\\%$ and $57\.97\\%$ micro\-averaged accuracy at a budget of $32$ decoder evaluations, exceeding the strongest baseline in our main comparison by $12\.1$ and $11\.6$ percentage points, respectively\. Both variants are trained at a budget of $32$ evaluations and remain competitive at higher budgets without retraining\. These results demonstrate that learning when to reveal and reconsider tokens can improve the accuracy\-compute trade\-off without updating the decoder backbone\.

## [Tissue\-specific antibacterial and anti\-biofilm activities of Penthorum chinense Pursh: integration of metabolomics and Random Forest machine learning](../publications/6d4a2fe1097fb976ce3b.md)

Yiqing Chen; Qilong Li; Qian Lai; Xue Tian; Yingtong Li; Gang Li; Qianlan Yue; Feixia Duan

Penthorum chinense Pursh is a traditional medicinal and edible plant rich in flavonoids and complex polyphenols\. Evaluating its aqueous extracts against foodborne pathogens via biomass assay, microplate spread tests and scanning electron microscopy revealed distinct tissue\-specific efficacies: leaf and stem extracts exhibited strong bactericidal effects \(16–128 mg/mL\), notably against Bacillus cereus, whereas flower extracts demonstrated potent biofilm inhibition \(IC50 &lt; 1 mg/mL\)\. Broad\-coverage UPLC–ESI–Q–TOF–MS metabolite profiling annotated 93 compounds, and integration with Random Forest nested cross\-validation prioritised candidate constituents associated with the measured activities\. While confirming established antimicrobials \(gallic acid, pinocembrin, pinostrobin, \(\-\)\-epicatechin gallate, afzelechin, corilagin, and hydrolysable derivatives of quercetin, kaempferol, and liquiritin\) as major active constituents, our ML model first revealed several unreported bioactive compounds\. Specifically, turmeronol A, vanillic acid glucoside, lotaustralin, and 2’,6’\-dihydroxydihydrochalcone\-4’\-O\-\(3′’\-O\-galloyl\)\-β\-D\-glucopyranoside act as crucial bactericidal agents, while Gemin D, lamiophlomiol C, 4’\-hydroxyflavanone, and pinocembrin\-7\-O\-\[4,6\-HHDP\]\-glucoside primarily contribute to anti\-biofilm efficacy\. Finally, their multi\-target mechanisms were preliminarily explored\.

## [Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the peroxisomal biogenesis factor proteins and interferes with lipid metabolism to affect the growth of liver cancer cells](../publications/6d4db155e09166647a61.md)

Jingyi Yang; Wanjun Shao; Congying Yu; Qi Wu; Rufei Xu; Xiaoqian Rong; Ailin Yang

Background Primary liver cancer is the sixth most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third most common cause of cancer death worldwide\. Chansu is made by processing and drying the white serous fluid of the posterior ear and skin glands of Bufo bufo gargarizans Cantor or Bufo melanostictus Schneider\. Chansu is a well\-known traditional Chinese medicine \(TCM\) that is mainly used for detoxification, detumescence, analgesia, the treatment of cancer, and heart failure\. Cinobufagin, as a bufadienolide, has been reported as the main antitumor active component of Chansu\. However, the molecular mechanisms related to the anticancer effects of cinobufagin still remain elusive\. Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore whether cinobufagin inhibits the growth of HepG2 and SK\-HEP\-1 tumor cells by inducing peroxisome dysfunction and interfering with lipid metabolism\. Methods The protein levels of catalase, ABCD3, PEX5, PEX6, and PEX10 in human hepatoma cells were analyzed by Western blotting\. The effects of cinobufagin on the viability of HepG2 and SK\-HEP\-1 cells were detected by cell counting kit\-8 \(CCK\-8\) assay and clone formation assay\. Small interfering RNA \(siRNA\) transfection was used to explore whether inhibition of PEX could enhance the inhibitory effect of cinobufagin on cell growth of HepG2 and SK\-HEP\-1 tumor cells\. The effects of cinobufagin on lipid metabolism were analyzed by untargeted metabolomics\. The in vivo antitumor effects of cinobufagin were verified by animal studies\. Results Cinobufagin causes peroxisome dysfunction in HepG2 and SK\-HEP\-1 tumor cells\. From a mechanistic point of view, we reveal that cinobufagin downregulates the expression of PEX5, PEX10, and PEX6\. In addition, through RNA interference, cinobufagin partially blocks the growth of HepG2 and SK\-HEP\-1 tumor cells and restrains the expression of lipid metabolism\-related proteins via downregulating the expression of PEX5 and PEX10\. Subsequently, we perform a non\-targeted metabolomics analysis of the cells and find that cinobufagin exerts its anti\-hepatoma effects by interfering with lipid metabolic reprogramming\. The results show that cinobufagin mainly interferes with glycerophospholipid and fatty acyl levels\. In addition, in vivo experiments reveal that cinobufagin restrains tumor growth without obvious adverse effects\. Serum metabolomics analyses reveal that cinobufagin causes significant changes in the levels of lipid and lipid\-like differential metabolites\. Conclusion Cinobufagin is a promising natural drug for the treatment of liver cancer, and PEXs may be potential molecular targets of cinobufagin to exert anticancer effects\. Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the proteins encoded by the PEX genes and interferes with lipid metabolism to restrain the growth of liver cancer cells\.

## [Turizm KOBİ’lerinin Dijital Pazarlama Araçlarını Benimseme Süreçleri: Artvin İlinde Teknoloji Kabul Modeli Bağlamında Nitel Bir Araştırma](../publications/6d60267061e2e6dda10d.md)

Ekrem Aydın; Turgut Türkoğlu; Burcu KIVILCIM

Bu araştırmada, kırsal ve eko\-turizm odaklı bir destinasyon olan Artvin ilinde faaliyet gösteren turizm KOBİ’lerinin dijital pazarlama araçlarını benimseme süreçlerinin Teknoloji Kabul Modeli \(TKM\) çerçevesinde derinlemesine incelenmesi amaçlanmıştır\. Nitel araştırma yaklaşımlarından durum çalışması deseninin benimsendiği çalışmada, olasılık dışı örnekleme yöntemlerinden amaçlı örnekleme tekniği kullanılmış ve 8 işletme yöneticisi ile derinlemesine görüşmeler gerçekleştirilmiştir\. Araştırma verileri içerik analizine tabi tutulmuş, bulgular MAXQDA nitel veri analizi programı ile analiz edilerek görselleştirilmiştir\. Araştırma bulguları, Artvin’deki turizm KOBİ’lerinin kurumsal web siteleri ve çevrimiçi seyahat acentelerine kıyasla, görsel zenginlik ve doğrudan etkileşim sunan Instagram ve Facebook gibi sosyal medya platformlarını daha yoğun kullandığını ortaya koymaktadır\. TKM’nin alt boyutları olan dış çevre unsurlarının ve algılanan faydanın yöneticilerin bu araçları benimseme eğilimini şekillendirdiği, algılanan kullanım kolaylığının ise bu eğilim üzerinde belirleyici bir rol oynamadığı görülmüştür\. Yöneticiler dijital araçların kullanımını genel olarak kolay bulmakla birlikte bu kolaylığı ayrıca bir motivasyon kaynağı olarak görmemektedir\. Ayrıca bazı yöneticilerin, dijital pazarlama kanallarını bilinçli olarak sınırlandırma eğiliminde olduğu saptanmıştır\. Çalışma, kırsal bölgelerdeki turizm işletmelerinin dijital dönüşüm dinamiklerini bütünsel bir çerçevede ortaya koyarak hem literatüre hem de bölge paydaşlarına katkı sunmaktadır\.

## [Overcoming adaptive resistance in non\-small cell lung cancer: integrating targeted therapies, immunotherapy synergy, and nanocarrier delivery](../publications/6d60a1335481a7179540.md)

Luke Ding; Anna Staskiewicz; Jesse Kao; Xinyu Wang

Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death, characterized by high mortality rates, tumor adaptation and heterogeneity, and immune evasion mechanisms\. Despite recent advancements in chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery, survival rates for non\-small cell lung cancer \(NSCLC\) and small cell lung cancer \(SCLC\) remain low, signifying the need for new strategies and innovative treatments\. This review explores the combinatorial potential of immunotherapy with direct targeting of tumor growth to address the multifaceted challenges of NSCLC\. Key approaches include small\-molecule inhibitors, programmed death\-ligand 1 \(PD\-L1\) inhibition, angiogenesis inhibition, and nanotechnology\-based drug delivery systems\. Nanocarrier systems enable coordinated drug release and pharmacological synergy, thereby ensuring effective inhibition of pathways in the tumor microenvironment \(TME\)\. Additionally, this review addresses several resistance mechanisms in the context of specific inhibitors \(e\.g\., EGFR and ALK inhibitors\)\. Translational insights help bridge preclinical findings to clinical applications with an emphasis on angiogenesis inhibition and personalized approaches\. Ethical considerations such as consent and preclinical safety testing are emphasized to ensure the safe development of these therapies\. With the new generation of genetic engineering, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies for tumor growth, this work discusses the potential to transform lung cancer treatment\.

## [A study on the changes in the microstructure of trabecular bone and the biomechanical properties in patients with osteoporotic fractures and the correlation between them](../publications/6d6b398d139518e433de.md)

Hao Liu; Xu Zhang; Wenjie Xu; Pei Yang; Zhizheng Xiong

Objective To explore bone\-quality characteristics in patients with osteoporotic femoral neck fractures by investigating trabecular\-bone microstructural and biomechanical alterations of femoral\-head specimens and their correlations\. Methods Femoral\-head specimens from 20 patients with osteoporotic femoral neck fractures \(experimental group: 69\-90 years, 80\.65 ± 8\.85 years\) and 13 patients with early\-stage hip degenerative changes \(control group: 49\-83 years, 64\.08 ± 6\.93 years\) were included\. Noticeable baseline age imbalance existed between groups\. All specimens underwent Micro\-CT scanning\. Cylindrical 8\-mm\-diameter trabecular\-bone samples were harvested along principal compressive trabeculae\. Compression, bending and torsion tests were conducted to acquire microstructural and biomechanical parameters\. Results Compared with controls, the experimental group exhibited significantly lower bone volume fraction \(BV/TV\), trabecular number \(Tb\.N\), trabecular thickness \(Tb\.Th\), alongside higher trabecular separation \(Tb\.Sp\) and structural model index \(SMI\) \(all P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Biomechanical indicators including maximum compressive stress \(MCL\), maximum bending force \(Fmax\) and maximum torque \(RST\) were markedly reduced in the experimental group \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Trabecular microstructural indices were significantly correlated with biomechanical performance\. Of note, baseline age imbalance and potential confounding from hip degenerative pathology should be considered when interpreting inter\-group differences\. Conclusion This ex\-vivo specimen\-based study demonstrates severe trabecular deterioration and impaired biomechanical properties in osteoporotic\-fracture specimens, with significant correlations between microstructural damage and reduced mechanical performance\. These observations only reflect bone\-quality features of isolated specimens; direct extrapolation to predict individual in\-vivo fracture risk should be avoided\.

## [Combination of hyperspectral imaging and machine learning techniques for non\-destructive quality evaluation of on\-tree apple fruits](../publications/6d7349eb03a4a23d0cfc.md)

Eungchan Kim; Chang\-Hyup Lee; Sang\-Yeon Kim; Jiwon Ryu; Mingyu Baek; Geon\-Hee Kim; Seul\-Ki Lee; Seung\-Wook Song; Ghiseok Kim

Abstract Hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) has emerged as a promising nondestructive technique for fruit quality assessment\. This study aimed to predict the soluble solids content \(SSC\) and firmness of apples \( Malus pumila Mill \) under outdoor field conditions using a push\-broom hyperspectral camera \(400–1000 nm\)\. Data were collected over two growing seasons \(2022\-2023\), from the immature stage to harvest, under naturally variable solar radiation and cloud cover\. Preprocessed reflectance spectra were analyzed with machine learning and deep learning regression models to establish relationships with measured SSC and firmness\. Among the tested models, random forest regression yielded the highest prediction accuracies \(R 2 = 0\.8177 for SSC and R 2 = 0\.9002 for firmness\), demonstrating the feasibility of applying HSI directly in orchard environments\. These results provide a practical framework for advancing nondestructive quality monitoring of apples in real\-world agricultural settings\.

## [Injury Type and Recurrence as Predictors of Market Value Decline in Professional Football: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 12,948 Injuries](../publications/6d810d7d94cf44298067.md)

Agostinho Sousa Pinto; António Abreu; Manuel Pérez\-Cota; Jerónimo Paiva; Laís Gabriele Vieira

Background: Professional football clubs spend billions on player transfers, yet a single injury can substantially reduce a player’s market value\. While previous research has established that injuries lower value, no study has systematically compared value penalties across specific injury types or quantified the additional cost of injury recurrence\. Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using 12,948 injury events from 2,061 professional footballers across top‑five European leagues \(Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, and Ligue 1\) between 2008 and 2024\. Mixed‑effects linear regression, Random Forest, and non‑parametric hypothesis tests \(Kruskal–Wallis, Mann–Whitney U\) were employed to examine the effects of injury type and recurrence on percentage change in market value, controlling for age, pre‑injury value, and position\. Results: Anterior cruciate ligament \(ACL\) injuries reduced market value by 6\.0%, and Achilles injuries by 15\.5%\. Ankle injuries increased value by 14\.0%, fractures by 11\.0%, concussions by 10\.5%, and knee injuries by 7\.0%\. Hamstring and muscle injuries showed no median change within the 120\-day observation window\. Recurrent injuries incurred an additional 8\.0% penalty beyond first‑time injuries\. Players under 24 gained 39\.0% following injury, while players aged 30 and over lost 31\.0% – a difference of 70\.0 percentage points\. Higher pre‑injury market value and older age were the strongest negative predictors of post‑injury valuation\. Conclusion: ACL and Achilles injuries are uniquely destructive to player market value\. Most other injury types show no lasting penalty\. Recurrence imposes a substantial additional penalty\. Younger players recover far better than older ones\. Clubs, agents, and insurers should incorporate injury type, recurrence history, and age into transfer negotiations, contract design, and player health strategies\. Keywords: Football injuries, market value, ACL, recurrence, sports economics

## [Autonomous labeling of surgical resection margins using a foundation model](../publications/6d8b30042216c6dcee90.md)

Xilin Yang; Musa Aydın; Yuhong Lu; Şahan Yoruç Selçuk; Bijie Bai; Yijie Zhang; Andrew C\. Birkeland; Tal Keidar Haran; Atlan Karine; Katjana Ehrlich; Julien Bec; Laura Marcu; Nir Pillar; Aydogan Özcan

Abstract Assessing resection margins is central to pathological specimen evaluation and has profound implications for patient outcomes\. Failure to achieve clear margins significantly increases the risk of local recurrence and may necessitate adjuvant therapies such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy\. However, margin assessment faces multiple procedural challenges, including human error during manual tissue margin labeling \(physical inking\), tissue shrinkage and distortion from fixation and processing, and thermal damage from cautery that obscures cellular features, all of which can compromise accurate margin identification\. We demonstrate a virtual inking network \(VIN\) that localizes the resection margin on whole\-slide images \(WSIs\), producing a standardized, ink\-free margin map that helps mitigate limitations of physical inking and enables accurate and reproducible margin measurements\. VIN uses a frozen foundation model as the feature extractor and a compact two\-layer multilayer perceptron trained for patch\-level classification of cautery\-consistent features\. The dataset comprised 120 hematoxylin and eosin \(H&amp;E\) stained slides from 12 human tonsil tissue blocks, resulting in \~ 2 TB of uncompressed raw image data, where a board\-certified pathologist provided boundary annotations\. In blind testing with 20 slides from previously unseen blocks, VIN produced coherent margin overlays that qualitatively aligned with expert annotations across serial sections\. Quantitatively, region\-level accuracy was \~ 73\.3% across the test set, with errors largely confined to limited areas that did not disrupt continuity of the whole\-slide margin map\. Our results suggest that VIN is capable of capturing cautery\-related histomorphology, offering a potential ink\-free margin delineation for digital pathology workflows\. These proof\-of\-concept results warrant further validation of VIN as a tool for margin localization in larger, clinically representative cohorts\.

## [AI‑Driven Video Advertisements and Ethical Concerns: Exploring College Student Perceptions in Mumbai](../publications/6d912913cc5295e17ba5.md)

Ms Swarangi Sayli Subhash Marchande; Amrin Moger

Abstract: Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has emerged as a transformative force in the advertising industry, enabling brands to produce video content that is personalized, visually engaging, scalable, and cost‑effective\. Despite these advantages, the proliferation of AI in advertising raises significant ethical concerns, particularly regarding authenticity, transparency, privacy, misinformation, and deepfakes\. These issues are especially relevant among college students, who encounter advertisements extensively through social media platforms\. This study investigates the perceptions of AI‑generated video advertisements among college students in Mumbai, with a focus on ethics, authenticity, and trust\. A quantitative research design was employed, and primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered via Google Forms\. The final sample consisted of 91 respondents, who provided insights into their social media usage, perceptions of AI‑driven advertising, and concerns related to ethical practices\. The findings indicate that lack of transparency was the most prominent ethical concern \(42%\), followed by privacy misuse \(30%\) and misleading content or deepfakes \(20%\)\. Respondents emphasized the importance of clear disclosure of AI involvement, truthful communication, human oversight, protection of personal data, and avoidance of misleading or stereotypical representations\. The study concludes that students do not categorically reject AI‑generated advertising; rather, their acceptance is contingent upon responsible and transparent application of AI technologies\. Overall, the results highlight that technological innovation in advertising must be supported by authenticity, ethical communication, transparency, and human oversight to strengthen trust among college students in Mumbai\. These insights contribute to ongoing debates on digital ethics and the responsible integration of AI in advertising practices\. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, AI\-Generated Video Advertisements, College Students, Advertising Ethics, Social Media

## [From sport to everyday movement: a school\-based “DON&\#x27;T STAY STILL\!” initiative to address sedentary behavior in children](../publications/6da0a427337f02e3d565.md)

Gianvincenzo Zuccotti; Franco Bruno Ascani; Assunta Ferdinanda Romeo; PODiaCar Team; Valeria Calcaterra

Introduction Sedentary behavior is a relevant health concern in childhood and adolescence and may remain high even among children who participate in structured physical activity\. Schools therefore represent a key setting for reducing prolonged sitting by integrating brief opportunities for movement into everyday routines\. “DON&\#x27;T STAY STILL\!” was developed as a school\-based pathway specifically targeting sedentary behavior through short, feasible, and inclusive “moments of movement\.” Methods The initiative was implemented during the 2025–2026 school year within the 63rd edition of the “Trofei di Milano\-Cortina 2026” programme\. Teachers received the PODiaCar “DON&\#x27;T STAY STILL\!” educational guide and supporting videos and incorporated brief active breaks into routine school activities\. Students were also involved through drawings and short videos focused on movement and active lifestyles\. Programme participation, implementation, and teacher feedback were assessed descriptively; no objective pre/post measures of sedentary behavior or physical activity were collected\. Results The overall programme involved 118 schools and 61,053 students aged 6–13 years, 52% of whom were girls\. Within this network, the “DON&\#x27;T STAY STILL\!” pathway generated 2,992 student outputs, including individual and class drawings and videos, while 3,090 students participated in guided “moments of movement” during school\-based educational sessions using PODiaCar video exercises\. Teacher feedback was positive, although acceptability was not assessed using a validated questionnaire\. Conclusions “DON&\#x27;T STAY STILL\!” provides a feasible school\-based approach for addressing sedentary behavior by embedding brief movement opportunities into routine educational activities\. Its implementation within a large and diverse school network, together with substantial student participation and positive teacher feedback, supports its potential as a scalable strategy for promoting more active school environments\. The findings support feasibility, participation, and preliminary acceptability, but do not establish effectiveness in reducing sedentary behavior\. Future prospective studies should assess its effects on sedentary time, physical activity, and related behavioral and health outcomes\.

## [Prediksi Stok Ikan Menggunakan Kecerdasan Buatan pada Perairan Tropis](../publications/6da9ead629c359609885.md)

Sulistyorini Sulistyorini; Diatri Indawati

Perairan tropis memiliki dinamika oseanografi yang kompleks, sehingga memprediksi stok ikan secara akurat menjadi tantangan bagi pengelolaan sumber daya perikanan\. Kecerdasan buatan \(AI\) menawarkan pendekatan baru yang mampu memodelkan pola non\-linier dan variabilitas lingkungan yang sulit ditangkap oleh metode statistik konvensional\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi kemampuan berbagai model AI, termasuk machine learning dan deep learning, dalam memprediksi stok ikan dengan mengintegrasikan variabel oseanografi seperti suhu permukaan laut, klorofil\-a, arus, dan kedalaman\. Metode penelitian meliputi pengumpulan data deret waktu, pemrosesan citra satelit, pelatihan model \(training\), validasi, serta evaluasi menggunakan metrik RMSE, MAE, dan akurasi\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa model jaringan saraf dalam memiliki performa prediktif yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan metode tradisional, dengan peningkatan akurasi lebih dari 20% ketika menggunakan data multi\-sumber\. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa AI berpotensi besar dalam meningkatkan monitoring stok ikan secara real\-time, sehingga mendukung pengelolaan perikanan berkelanjutan di wilayah tropis\. Penelitian ini diharapkan berkontribusi pada transformasi teknologi perikanan modern berbasis data\.

## [Sürdürülebilirlik İletişiminde Görsel İnşa: Türk Markalarının Raporlama Pratiklerinde Tipografi ve Eko\-Tasarım](../publications/6daacd6bc22efeec3c7c.md)

Tarık Doğan

Bu çalışma, kurumsal sürdürülebilirlik iletişiminin stratejik bir bileşeni haline gelen görsel dilin, özellikle tipografi ve mizanpaj ekseninde nasıl kurgulandığını incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırma, Türkiye’de Enerji, Finans, Tekstil ve FMCG/Teknoloji sektörlerinde faaliyet gösteren 8 öncü markanın \(Tüpraş, Zorlu, Garanti BBVA, İş Bankası, Mavi, Koton, Arçelik, Eczacıbaşı\) güncel sürdürülebilirlik raporlarını kapsamaktadır\. Yöntem olarak, Roland Barthes’ın &quot;Düzanlam/Yananlam&quot; ve &quot;Mit&quot; kavramları, C\.S\. Peirce’ın &quot;Belirti/Simge&quot; ayrımı ve Umberto Eco’nun &quot;Açık Yapıt&quot; kuramını temel alan hibrit bir göstergebilimsel analiz modeli ile teknik eko\-tasarım \(beyaz boşluk, mürekkep tasarrufu, dijital karbon ayak izi\) parametreleri kullanılmıştır\. Bulgular, markaların sans\-serif fontlar ve minimalist mizanpajlar aracılığıyla &quot;şeffaflık&quot; ve &quot;modernite&quot; mitleri inşa ettiğini; dijital raporlamaya geçişin ise okunabilirliği korurken enerji verimliliği sağlayan teknik bir zorunluluk olarak görsel dile yansıdığını ortaya koymaktadır\. Sonuç olarak tipografi, sürdürülebilirlik iletişiminde sadece estetik bir tercih değil, kurumsal etiği görselleştiren ve çevresel etkiyi minimize eden stratejik bir &quot;göstergebilimsel kaynak&quot; olarak tanımlanmıştır\.

## [AI\-DRIVEN ONLINE ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF LEARNER MODELLING, ADAPTATION MECHANISMS AND EVIDENCE OF EFFECTIVENESS](../publications/6db2e0830130b7e42f91.md)

Kobulova Moxinabonu Avazbekovna; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre

The rapid expansion of online and blended learning in higher education has exposed a persistent limitation of conventional online courses: content is delivered to all students in the same sequence and at the same pace, regardless of differences in prior knowledge, learning progress and needs\. Online adaptive learning systems, increasingly powered by artificial intelligence \(AI\), aim to overcome this limitation by continuously diagnosing the learner and personalising content, sequence, difficulty and feedback\. Aim\. This article reviews the theoretical foundations, learner\-modelling techniques, adaptation mechanisms and empirical evidence on the effectiveness of AI\-driven online adaptive learning systems, and derives implications for higher education systems undergoing digital transformation, with particular reference to Uzbekistan\. Methods\. An integrative literature review was conducted following the framework of Whittemore and Knafl\. Seminal works and peer\-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC and Google Scholar, together with international policy documents, were analysed using reflexive thematic synthesis\. Results\. Six themes were identified: \(1\) pedagogical and psychological foundations; \(2\) learner modelling, from Bayesian knowledge tracing to deep learning; \(3\) adaptation targets and mechanisms; \(4\) evidence of effectiveness from meta\-analyses; \(5\) the emerging role of generative AI; and \(6\) ethical, pedagogical and infrastructural challenges\. Meta\-analytic evidence shows moderate to large positive effects of intelligent and adaptive tutoring on learning outcomes, while gaps remain regarding teacher involvement, transparency and applicability to low\-resource language contexts\. Conclusion\. Effective adaptive learning requires the integration of validated learner models, pedagogically grounded adaptation rules, interoperable learning platforms and a teacher\-in\-the\-loop approach\. A set of requirements for national adaptive learning systems is proposed\.
