## [Green Accounting Practices and ESG Performance: Assessing their Impact on Corporate Financial Performance in Bangladesh](../publications/6de51296180564ef61f4.md)

Kazi FarhanaYeasmin; Piklu Sarker; Habibur Rahaman; Mohammad Khairul Islam Juman

This study explores how environmental, social, and governance\-oriented accounting practices are associated with ESG disclosure quality and corporate financial performance in listed companies in Bangladesh\. The research considers Environmental Accounting Practices \(EAP\), Social Accounting Practices \(SAP\), and Governance Accounting Practices \(GAP\) as explanatory constructs, while ESG Disclosure Quality \(EDQ\) is examined as a potential mechanism linking these practices with Corporate Financial Performance \(CFP\)\. The study is grounded in Stakeholder Theory and Legitimacy Theory and adopts a quantitative, cross\-sectional research design\. Primary data were obtained from 300 respondents representing listed companies through a structured questionnaire based on a five\-point Likert scale\. Data analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS and SmartPLS 4\.0, with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) applied to evaluate the measurement and structural models\. The results indicate that EAP, SAP, and GAP are significantly and positively associated with EDQ\. EDQ also demonstrates a significant positive relationship with CFP\. In addition, EAP and GAP show significant direct relationships with CFP, whereas the direct relationship between SAP and CFP is statistically insignificant\. The mediation results indicate that EDQ significantly transmits the effects of all three accounting\-practice dimensions to CFP\. The structural model accounts for 36\.1% of the variance in EDQ and 38\.2% in CFP\. Overall, nine of the ten proposed hypotheses receive empirical support\.

## [Cognitive impairment profiles in patients with cerebrovascular diseases: a latent profile analysis](../publications/6def1cb4b63095f47c21.md)

Yao Yin; Hui Ma; Rong Zou; Chaofeng Fan; Wei Zhu; Jun Zheng

Background Cognitive impairment is an increasingly recognized condition predominantly attributable to cerebrovascular diseases \(CVDs\)\. It substantially diminishes patients’ quality of life and imposes considerable burdens on caregivers and healthcare systems\. However, how cognitive impairment manifest across multiple functional domains in individuals with CVDs remains poorly understood, often resulting in generalized care plans that fail to meet patients’ specific rehabilitation needs\. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of cognitive impairment and their associated factors in patients with CVDs using latent profile analysis \(LPA\)\. Methods This cross\-sectional study was conducted using convenience sampling in a tertiary hospital in southwestern China from November 2023 to September 2025\. LPA was employed to identify distinct cognitive impairment profiles among patients with CVDs\. Multinomial logistic regression was subsequently performed to examine factors associated with profile categories\. Results The final three\-profile model classified 474 participants into three groups: a mild impairment group \(82\.5%\), a moderate impairment group \(11\.4%\), and a severe impairment group \(6\.1%\)\. The three profiles reflected increasing severity of cognitive impairment among patients with CVDs\. Compared with the mild impairment group, higher NIHSS scores \(OR = 1\.222, 95 %CI = 1\.126–1\.326, p &lt; 0\.001\) were associated with higher odds of membership in the moderate impairment profile\. Male gender and lower NIHSS scores were associated with lower odds of membership in the severe impairment profile \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Conclusion In this predominantly hemorrhagic and neurosurgical cohort, the retained three\-profile model represented different levels of MMSE\-based global cognitive severity among patients with CVDs\. NIHSS score and gender showed exploratory associations with profile membership\. The applicability of these findings to broader CVD populations requires further validation\.

## [ANN\-Based sensitivity analysis for the prediction of energy consumption and head rice yield in a pneumatic paddy dryer](../publications/6e0a5ecbfd4ac6484545.md)

Aphisik Pakdeekaew; Manop Yamfang; Manaporn Guptasa; Tawarat Treeamnuk; Krawee Treeamnuk

In this study, the performance of a pneumatic paddy dryer was investigated through a sensitivity analysis with an artificial neural network, in order to identify the relative importance of the process variables affecting the energy consumption and head rice yield \(HRY\)\. Experiments were conducted using Thai Jasmine 105 paddy rice, which was dried from 24% to 14% wet basis at drying air temperatures of 60°C, 80°C, and 100°C\. Increasing the drying air temperature increased the drying rate from 0\.46 to 1\.11 kgwater/h\. Drying at 60°C resulted in the lowest specific energy consumption \(SEC\) of 3\.17 MJ/kgwater and the highest HRY \(51\.91%\), but approximately 6 h was needed to reach the target moisture content for a batch of 20 kg\. Higher drying temperatures substantially shortened the drying time but increased the SEC and reduced the HRY to 39\.01–41\.15%, suggesting a trade\-off between drying rate, energy use, and milling quality\. The model accurately predicted the moisture content, electrical energy consumption, and HRY, with coefficients of determination \(R²\) ≥ 0\.997 for both the training and testing datasets\. Through a sensitivity analysis, the paddy grain temperature \(Tpaddy\) was identified as the most informative predictor, accounting for approximately 38% of the total relative importance, followed by drying time \(32%\) and drying air temperature \(21%\)\. These findings indicate that Tpaddy provides valuable information on the transient thermal state of the grain, and can serve as a key process variable for forecasting drying behavior\. Rather than representing a standalone commercial drying solution, the framework presented here provides a basis for developing multi\-stage drying strategies in which rapid pneumatic pre\-drying can be followed by tempering or drying at lower temperatures to strike a balance between drying efficiency and HRY\.

## [6G Evolution Towards Connected Intelligent Machines](../publications/6e120dbb690c8f6cc6fe.md)

Dejan Vukobratović

The evolution towards 6G raises a fundamental question: will future mobile networks connect machines more efficiently, or will they become an integral part of intelligent systems? This overview paper explores this question through the concept of task\-oriented communications, which shifts the focus from faithfully transmitting data towards delivering the information needed to accomplish a task\. We illustrate these ideas through two connected\-robotics scenarios investigated in our research: semantic communication of 3D point clouds for industrial object recognition, and edge\-based robotic localisation and mapping supported by 5G/6G connectivity\. These examples highlight how communication, computation and sensing can be designed together to support potentially the fundamental role of 6G technology, that is to connect intelligent machines\.

## [IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF PSCRB TRAINING TO ENHANCE SEAFARERS’ SAFETY KNOWLEDGE AND EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS](../publications/6e24641294d5dcf961ac.md)

Natriya Faisal Rachman; Fika Devi Anggraini; Muhammad Zainul Arifin; ⁠Femmy Asdiana; Jaka Septian Kustanto; Wahyuni Oktavia

This community\-service study evaluated the implementation of Proficiency in Survival Craft and Rescue Boats \(PSCRB\) training to examine changes in participants’ safety knowledge and emergency preparedness within the STCW framework\. The evaluation focused on knowledge of safety procedures, emergency readiness, and survival capability at sea\. A mixed\-methods descriptive evaluation was complemented by pre\- and post\-training assessment of 25 participants\. Evidence was drawn from training observations, activity records, participant reflections, and competency scores\. The program combined classroom explanation with demonstrations, hands\-on simulations, interactive discussion, survival craft and rescue\-boat operations, abandon\-ship exercises, and emergency\-response practice\. Descriptively, the mean score rose from 56\.4 before training to 80\.2 afterward, an increase of 23\.8 points \(about 42\.2%\)\. Every participant improved, and the lowest post\-test score was 75\. The pattern indicates that practice\-centered instruction, simulation, and participant interaction supported better understanding, engagement, preparedness, emergency coordination, and safety awareness\. These findings support continued practice\-oriented PSCRB training to develop capable maritime personnel and reinforce compliance with safety requirements in rescue operations\.

## [Liquid Crystal as Solid Electrolytes: Selected Developments and Perspectives](../publications/6e2691b0fc018090f67e.md)

Manasa Chandramouli; Vrushabendra Basavanna; Srikantamurthy Ningaiah

The liquid crystalline state arises from orientation\-dependent, non\-covalent interactions among molecules in condensed phases, producing materials that combine structural order with molecular mobility\. Because this ordered arrangement depends on a delicate balance of intermolecular forces, liquid crystals \(LCs\) are highly responsive to external stimuli, making them attractive for sensing and electrochemical applications\. This review critically examines recent advances in liquid crystal\-based solid electrolytes, with emphasis on materials design strategies, ionic transport mechanisms, and electrochemical performance\. The discussion is organized into key thematic sections covering \(i\) fundamental intermolecular interactions governing liquid crystalline behavior, \(ii\) classes of ionic liquid\-crystalline systems, including zwitterionic and mesoionic mesogens, and \(iii\) liquid crystalline materials composed of organic cations paired with organic or inorganic anions interacting through electrostatic and other non\-covalent forces\. Representative studies from recent literature are analyzed to highlight structure–property relationships and performance trends in solid\-state devices such as lithium batteries, fuel cells, and dye\-sensitized solar cells\. By integrating material design principles with functional performance analysis, this review provides a focused perspective on the potential and limitations of liquid crystalline solid electrolytes for next\-generation all\-solid\-state technologies\.

## [Generalization Guarantees of Randomized Block Coordinate Descent for Nonconvex Learning](../publications/6e2ea2760a231411ac53.md)

Ruixi Hu; Liang Wu

Randomized block coordinate descent \(RBCD\) is a popular optimization algorithm for many large\-scale machine learning problems\. The existing theoretical analysis of RBCD mainly focuses on its convergence behavior from an optimization perspective, while its generalization behavior remains less understood for nonconvex problems\. In this paper, we establish high\-probability generalization guarantees for RBCD with nonconvex objectives\. In the general nonconvex setting, we derive bounds on the gradients of both empirical and population risks, requiring only standard smoothness assumptions\. With polynomially decaying step sizes, we tune the iteration number to balance optimization and generalization, thereby quantifying how early stopping leads to the optimal convergence rate for the population gradients\. In the gradient\-dominated setting, we provide bounds in terms of functional suboptimality, which nearly match the optimistic rates in convex and low\-noise settings\. Finally, we develop dimension\-independent bounds for loss functions of a specific structure, making the generalization guarantees applicable to high\-dimensional problems\.

## [ANALISIS KOMPARATIF MODEL PENGEMBANGAN KURIKULUM DAN RELEVANSINYA DALAM PENDIDIKAN MODERN ABAD KE\-21](../publications/6e3401f8a5703868bfdb.md)

Nafaisal Ulumi; Ifa Zumrotin; Ali Ahmad Yenuri; Muhammad Arif Syihabuddin

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis secara komparatif berbagai model pengembangan kurikulum serta mengkaji relevansinya terhadap kebutuhan pendidikan modern abad ke\-21\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis penelitian kepustakaan \(library research\) yang bersifat deskriptif\-analitis\. Data diperoleh dari berbagai buku, artikel jurnal, dan publikasi ilmiah yang relevan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik analisis isi melalui proses identifikasi, seleksi, kategorisasi, perbandingan, interpretasi, dan sintesis\. Kajian ini membahas delapan model pengembangan kurikulum, yaitu The Administrative Model, The Grass Roots Model, The Demonstration Model, Beauchamp’s System Model, Taba’s Inverted Model, Roger’s Interpersonal Relation Model, The Systematic Action Research Model, dan Emerging Technical Model\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa setiap model memiliki karakteristik, keunggulan, keterbatasan, dan relevansi yang berbeda\. Tidak terdapat satu model yang secara mutlak paling sesuai untuk seluruh konteks pendidikan abad ke\-21\. Pendidikan modern membutuhkan kurikulum yang fleksibel, kontekstual, humanis, inovatif, reflektif, dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi\. Oleh karena itu, pengembangan kurikulum lebih relevan dilakukan melalui pendekatan integratif yang memadukan standardisasi, fleksibilitas, partisipasi guru, pendekatan humanistik, evaluasi berkelanjutan, inovasi, serta pemanfaatan teknologi\. Pendekatan tersebut diharapkan mampu menghasilkan kurikulum yang lebih adaptif terhadap perubahan dan kebutuhan kompetensi peserta didik pada abad ke\-21\.

## [Heterophily Limits Spatial Graph Encoding for PM2\.5 Forecasting in IoT Smart Cities](../publications/6e3528c74d804d826aca.md)

Abdessamad Badouch; Kaoutar Belhoucine

Graph neural networks are widely assumed to improve air\-quality forecasting as the spatial heterogeneity of Internet of Things monitoring networks grows\.We test this on a reproducible four\-network benchmark under identical preprocessing, comparing a temporal\-only Transformer against three graph architectures, and we introduce a spatial heterophily index computable in advance\.Across the three networks on which all architectures were evaluated, no graph model delivers a practically meaningful accuracy gain, and comparison against a margin fixed before analysis places them at parity or worse throughout; on the fourth, the fixed\-adjacency model again degrades at every station\.The failure is architecture\-specific: only the fixed\-adjacency model collapses in the heterophilous networks, a collapse neither the Spatio\-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network \(STGCN\) nor Graph WaveNet reproduces\.The problem lies in aggregation over a predetermined neighbourhood rather than in spatial encoding itself\.The index ranks networks by the severity of that degradation but identifies no threshold below which aggregation becomes beneficial: a timestamped prediction to that effect was refuted\.We present it as a preliminary diagnostic indicator for the architectures tested\.

## [Support and fracture: understanding sociotechnical imaginaries in Chinese grassroots’ AI governance frames](../publications/6e3cc405570db3742630.md)

Shuo Wang

This study examines how Chinese grassroots publics construct and contest sociotechnical imaginaries \(SIs\) of AI governance\. Drawing on six online focus groups with 30 non\-expert participants, we integrate SIs with Technological Frame to explore three dimensions of AI imaginaries: social representations, governance mechanisms, and future trajectories\. Findings reveal a marked divergence between instrumentalist and humanistic imaginaries, generating competing narratives at the intersection of technological development and governance\. However, these imaginaries are constrained by structural power asymmetries that limit grassroots publics’ capacities to envision future technological directions\. This constraint gives rise to SIs fracture, a loss of imaginative agency where idealized futures feel inaccessible\. As a result, individuals retreat from governance discourse, perceiving AI development as a vehicle for disempowering control\. This study thus highlights how structural power asymmetries undermine public imaginaries and pose critical risks to inclusive technological futures\.

## [Adaptive Leader Development by Black Women Students in Medical School](../publications/6e492cec47bc68c693a8.md)

Mark Anthony Torrez; Darren E\. Pierre; Antonio Durán; Sydney Torres; Ashley F\. Curtis

Black women continue to be underrepresented in leadership theory, including within scholarship on leadership in higher education\. What does exist typically centers on undergraduate student leaders, overlooking the realities that Black women students in graduate/professional programs face\. In response, this project placed critical perspectives on leadership theory in conversation with the testimonies of eight Black women medical students to understand how they define, manage, and perform their leadership identities\. Findings revealed how these participants viewed environmental threats that framed their leader development, how they managed identity perceptions through their performance, and how they committed to continual learning regarding their leadership\. Informed by their perspectives, we offer implications for practice, research, and leadership theory\.

## [BEYOND STATISTICAL INFERENCE: A CAUSAL AND TOPOLOGICAL ARCHITECTURE FOR VERIFIABLE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY](../publications/6e581b817cb3e03da50e.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Causal and Topological AI Architecture transcends statistical AI limitations by establishing a deterministic framework for verifiable scientific discovery\. Current models fail to guarantee mathematical rigor and physical conservation\. This architecture integrates three pillars: Causal Neural Ordinary Differential Equations constrained by Directed Acyclic Graphs for physical dynamics; Topological Information Geometry, mapping proofs to Riemannian manifolds to drastically reduce logical discontinuities; and Causal Zero\-Knowledge Machine Learning, using zk\-SNARKs to cryptographically verify conclusions without exposing data\. To support these tasks, the framework introduces the Neuro\-Photonic Silicon Architecture, employing memristive arrays and non\-equilibrium thermodynamics for unprecedented energy efficiency\. Performance is quantified via the El\-Rakhawi Causal Fidelity Metric, ensuring strict alignment with physical axioms, and the Neuro\-Photonic Efficiency Metric\. This unified paradigm provides a rigorous foundation for Artificial General Intelligence, ensuring machine\-generated scientific discoveries are logically sound, physically consistent, and mathematically verifiable\.

## [GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E\-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search](../publications/6e5df9627edd0c51d315.md)

Hyunseo Kim; Suil Choe; Sukkyoung So; Daeyeon Yi

Optimizing product listings for generative search requires language agents not only to rewrite effectively but also to continually self\-improve by retaining successful strategies across diverse categories\. However, existing approaches often treat structured listings as free\-form text, leaving effective strategies implicit in prompts, search trajectories, or rewritten outputs rather than accumulating them as a reusable agentic memory\. To address this limitation, we introduce GLOBE, an agentic framework that drives continual self\-improvement by storing optimization knowledge in an evolving handbook of explicit, field\-scoped behaviors\. In each episode, an Editor applies relevant behaviors and receives rank\-based feedback, which a Reflector converts into behavior updates\. Crucially for dependable execution in real\-world settings, a Moderator removes redundant proposals, a Curator commits accepted changes, and consistently harmful behaviors are deactivated\. This cycle transforms episodic feedback into a persistent, field\-scoped optimization memory\. Experiments show that structured behaviors outperform monolithic prompt optimization, while feedback\-driven evolution and moderation further improve effectiveness and reduce downside risk\. The learned behaviors also remain effective on unseen product categories, suggesting that agentic memory evolution supports interpretable and transferable product optimization\.

## [Toponimi Jalan Berunsur Sayur\-Mayur di Kawasan Pondok Cabe Ilir, Kecamatan Pamulang: Kajian Antropolinguistik](../publications/6e674bedd346d8f0d18d.md)

Dhini Akhiriani; Siti Nurhasanah

Penelitian ini mengkaji toponimi nama jalan berunsur sayur\-mayur di kawasan Pondok Cabe Ilir, Kecamatan Pamulang, Kota Tangerang Selatan dengan menggunakan pendekatan Antropolinguistik\. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh keunikan sistem penamaan jalan yang secara konsisten menggunakan nama\-nama sayuran, seperti Jalan Bayam, Jalan Kubis, Jalan Selada, dan Jalan Kentang\. Penelitian bertujuan mendokumentasikan nama\-nama jalan tersebut, mendeskripsikan latar belakang penamaannya, serta mengungkap fungsi sosial dan makna budaya yang terkandung di dalamnya\. Penelitian menggunakan metode deskriptif kualitatif dengan teknik pengumpulan data berupa observasi, wawancara mendalam, dokumentasi, dan studi pustaka\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penamaan jalan berunsur sayur\-mayur di Pondok Cabe Ilir bukan merupakan penamaan yang bersifat arbitrer, melainkan hasil kebijakan administratif Pemerintah Kabupaten Tangerang sebelum terbentuknya Kota Tangerang Selatan\. Sistem penamaan berbasis tema ini bertujuan memudahkan identifikasi dan pemetaan wilayah serta memperkuat identitas lokal masyarakat\. Kajian ini menunjukkan bahwa nama jalan tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai penanda geografis, tetapi juga merepresentasikan memori kolektif dan identitas budaya suatu komunitas\.

## [Designing for Imperfect Prompts: A Simulation\-Based Evaluation of an LLM\-Based Enterprise Data Assistant Using Knowledge Graphs](../publications/6e67b2d4c40500891ad4.md)

Niklas Wagner; Alexander Mädche

Enterprise data assistants using large language models \(LLMs\) promise democratized data access in organizations\. Yet in our real\-world deployment within the CFO unit&\#x27;s data lake at an industry partner, we observed that business users frequently pose imperfect prompts that include domain\-specific vocabulary and lack schema references or structural information\. This Design Science Research study examines automatic resolution using a semantic mediation layer\. We design and evaluate two design variants: schema\-based mediation via semantic similarity, and knowledge graph\-based mediation leveraging an automatically constructed knowledge graph from the data lake\. Our simulation\-based evaluation using real\-world data, supported by LLM\-as\-a\-Judge assessments and human validation, shows that knowledge graph\-based mediation outperforms the schema\-based approach in Precision, Recall, F1, and preserving user intent\. We propose a design principle for knowledge graph\-based mediation, demonstrating that structured knowledge representation bridges user intent and database structure and guides the design of enterprise data assistants across skill levels\.

## [Frozen vision transformers can be reused via cross\-scale feature fusion](../publications/6e6858bb58157beaf9b4.md)

Lei Qin; Liang Kou

Abstract As Vision Transformer \(ViT\) models continue to scale, the training and fine\-tuning costs for achieving advanced performance have surged, forcing us to rethink the sustainability of relying solely on model scaling\. In this work, we explore a more cost\-effective alternative\. By effectively exploiting the complementary potential of existing frozen models, we avoid the expense of training large models from scratch\. Based on this idea, we propose the Dual\-ViT Fusion Transformer \(DVFT\)\. This framework explicitly aligns and fuses heterogeneous features from different frozen backbones, thereby addressing the limited representational scope and insufficient cross\-scale semantic coverage of a single frozen model\. Such limitations are difficult to mitigate within existing parameter\-efficient fine\-tuning frameworks, which are primarily designed for single\-model settings\. Specifically, DVFT introduces two complementary guidance paradigms\. The first is Intrinsic Anchor\-based calibration, which uses the frozen models’ own global semantic representations as alignment references to establish cross\-model semantic consistency\. The second is Extrinsic Query\-based guidance, which employs learnable queries as an information bottleneck to progressively extract and integrate complementary discriminative features across models, enabling flexible feature interaction\. Experimental results show that our method approaches the performance of expensively trained models with very few training epochs\. These findings indicate that DVFT provides a scalable and low\-cost pathway for efficiently reusing existing frozen models to achieve high\-performance visual recognition\.

## [Encoder Selection and Segmentation Quality in U\-Net\-based Retinal Vessel Analysis](../publications/6e695c4f092582178634.md)

Jegan Sivaraman; Arjun Paramarthalingam; Arulnancy Thirunavukkarasu; Regan Rajendran

Retinal vessel segmentation through automation is a very significant area in retinal image processing, which can help in diagnosing many different ocular and systemic diseases\. In this research study, a comparative study of the encoder\-based U\-Net models is presented for retinal vessel segmentation\. Five different models including ResNet18\+U\-Net, ResNet34\+U\-Net, Traditional U\-Net, VGG16\+U\-Net, and VGG19\+U\-Net have been developed and trained on the retinal images belonging to the DRIVE and CHASE\_DB1 databases\. The proposed methodology involves image pre\-processing, image normalization, image augmentation, feature extraction from image using the encoder architecture, and U\-Net decoding with the skip connection for pixel\-wise segmentation of retinal vessels\. Among all models evaluated in this paper, the VGG19\+U\-Net model gives the highest value of Jaccard score of 81\.83%, F1 score of 89\.53%, Precision of 89\.47%, Accuracy of 98\.41%, and Specificity of 99\.13%, whereas the highest Sensitivity score of 90\.32% is achieved by the VGG16\+U\-Net model\.

## [Precision Plant Breeding: Integrating Genome Editing with Artificial Intelligence\- A Review](../publications/6e699263bdc71b37809b.md)

B L Santhosh; Nakka Amulya; Madhuri Singh; C\. Varshitha; Biju Sidharthan; Vijay Kumar; Prabha Banjarey; Udit Prakash

Precision plant breeding seeks to link biological target discovery with the development and evaluation of useful alleles in crop improvement\. Genome\-editing platforms, including CRISPR–Cas nucleases, base editors, prime editors, multiplex editing and cis\-regulatory editing, enable targeted genomic alterations; however, their successful use depends on appropriate target choice, editing performance and phenotypic validation\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) offers complementary approaches for integrating pangenomic, multi\-omics, phenotypic and environmental data to prioritise genes and regulatory sequences, predict guide\-RNA activity and off\-target effects, and support selection across genetic backgrounds and environments\. This review examines the potential of combining these methods within a design–build–test–learn framework that connects edit design with molecular verification, high\-throughput phenotyping, genomic prediction and conventional breeding operations\. Examples discussed include susceptibility\-gene and promoter editing for disease resistance, regulatory interventions associated with stress responses, nutritional modification and the emerging application of AI\-designed nucleases in rice\. Although these advances demonstrate technical feasibility, widespread implementation remains constrained by plant\-specific data scarcity, differences among genotypes and environments, transformation and regeneration bottlenecks, complex trait architecture, unintended editing outcomes and regulatory diversity\. The review emphasises prospective model validation, causal interpretation, pangenome\-aware design, rigorous molecular characterisation and replicated field evaluation\. It concludes that AI\-guided genome editing can support crop improvement when used alongside quantitative genetics, breeder\-defined objectives and responsible governance, rather than as a substitute for empirical breeding evidence\.

## [Exigência de impugnação específica e tutela da liberdade: a súmula 182 do STJ entre a dialeticidade recursal, o dever de fundamentação e o apoio tecnológico à admissibilidade](../publications/6e6a77bb214470742b21.md)

Alexandre Moura Lima Neto

O artigo examina a aplicação da Súmula 182 do Superior Tribunal de Justiça \(STJ\) aos recursos que discutem a liberdade do acusado\. O enunciado exige que o agravante impugne especificamente os fundamentos da decisão agravada, exigência hoje prevista nos arts\. 932, III, e 1\.021, § 1º, do Código de Processo Civil \(CPC\)\. Investiga\-se se essa regra pode encerrar o exame de questões ligadas à liberdade sem ofender o dever de fundamentação e o direito a uma resposta constitucionalmente adequada, sobretudo quando a análise de admissibilidade passa a contar com apoio de inteligência artificial \(IA\)\. A hipótese é que o problema não reside na dialeticidade recursal, mas na leitura que converte o não conhecimento em ponto final da jurisdição criminal\. A pesquisa é qualitativa e de matriz hermenêutica\. Combina análise normativa, exame documental da íntegra dos Embargos de Divergência em Agravo em Recurso Especial \(EAREsp\) n\. 746\.775/PR e dos precedentes que originaram a súmula, e comparação funcional com o direito português, em especial com o convite ao aperfeiçoamento das conclusões previsto no art\. 417\.º, n\.º 3, do Código de Processo Penal português\. Os resultados indicam que os precedentes de origem censuravam a mera repetição de razões e que a exigência de impugnar todos os fundamentos surgiu depois, em caso cível, apoiada em razões de política judiciária\. Nos recursos de liberdade, a inadmissão por deficiência de impugnação somente se sustenta quando acompanhada de verificação expressa e fundamentada de ilegalidade flagrante, realizada por julgador humano\. Propõem\-se quatro critérios para essa verificação\.

## [Asari, Minato: From Concealment to Communication: Integrating Camouflage into Animal Signaling Research](../publications/6e6f41e98cab81f8f4a8.md)



\_Philosophy of Science\_:1\-20\. forthcomingCamouflage is a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature, yet most researchers in animal communication have overlooked it because it does not typically qualify as a signal\. I argue against this prevailing view and show that at least one type of camouflage, masquerade, can be regarded as a signal\. I then introduce two notions—information\-transmitting signals and information\-masking signals—and characterize them in such a way that typical signals fall into the former category and camouflage into the latter, drawing on an information\-theoretic approach to animal signaling\. Lastly, I compare information\-masking signals with misinformation and deception\. \(direct link \)

## [Information adequacy and household transition to low\-carbon energy solutions: a qualitative case study from Uganda](../publications/6e70416f746379b35d87.md)

Florence Nakajubi; Joseph Mpeera Ntayi; Hassan Bashir; Livingstone Senyonga; Muyiwa  Samuel Adaramola; Ronnette Atukunda

Introduction Household dependence on traditional biomass remains high in Uganda despite growing policy efforts to promote cleaner household energy alternatives\. This study examines how information adequacy shapes household transitions to low\-carbon energy solutions in Uganda\. Methods A qualitative case\-study design was adopted, involving semi\-structured interviews with 20 participants comprising 15 household heads and 5 policymakers\. Data were analysed using the Gioia methodology\. Results The analysis generated seven first\-order concepts, organised into two second\-order themes, information quantity and information quality, and one aggregate dimension of information adequacy\. Three first\-order concepts captured information quantity, while four captured information quality\. Information quantity broadened households’ awareness and practical knowledge of low\-carbon energy alternatives by providing sufficient information on available technologies, costs, suppliers and use\. Information quality enhanced households’ ability to evaluate these alternatives when information was clear, credible, accessible and contextually relevant, particularly when communicated through local language, practical demonstrations, visual materials and relatable peer experiences\. Discussion The findings further show that information quantity primarily supports the knowledge stage of Diffusion of Innovations theory, whereas information quality strengthens the persuasion stage by enabling households to assess the relevance and feasibility of alternative energy technologies\. The study concludes that household energy\-transition interventions should move beyond increasing information exposure to providing sufficient, understandable and locally relevant information alongside broader measures addressing economic, technological and infrastructural constraints\.

## [GLOBALIZATION, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LEGAL ENGLISH: TRANSFORMING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION IN LAW ENFORCEMENT](../publications/6e87e6e4deb13accc8a6.md)

Лариса Володимирівна Дудікова; Марина Костюк; Viktoriia Mikaielian

The article examines changes in professional English\-language communication in law enforcement under the influence of globalization and the growing use of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. Particular attention is given to Legal English as a means of international cooperation, professional information processing and interaction in intercultural settings\. The study argues that contemporary language training for law enforcement professionals should move beyond the acquisition of specialized terminology and develop the ability to understand legal concepts in context, adapt communication to different audiences, and use digital tools critically and responsibly\. Drawing on a narrative literature review and conceptual analysis of research in legal linguistics, intercultural police communication, AI\-assisted language learning and large language models in legal contexts, the article identifies an emerging gap between these research areas and proposes their integration into a four\-component framework of professional communicative competence\. The framework comprises linguistic, professional\-legal, intercultural and digital/AI competences\. The article also outlines practical applications for Legal English teaching, including AI\-assisted translation review and scenario\-based police communication\. Particular attention is given to accuracy, confidentiality, source verification and the limits of automated systems\. The proposed framework can support the design of more realistic, human\-centred and professionally relevant language training for future law enforcement professionals\.

## [Real\-time exploration of the billion\-scale human repertoire for precursor frequency analysis and rational antibody design](../publications/6e9000db53c095d4b3ec.md)

Tom U\. Schlegel; Jannis von Blanckenburg de Riz; Jakob R\. Riccabona; Franz Dietzmeyer; Julia Koehler Leman; Jens Meiler; Clara T\. Schoeder; Torben Schiffner

The success of germline\-targeting vaccines and rational antibody design depends on quantifying the population\-level frequencies of specific antibody features, such as CDR lengths, sequence motifs, germline usage or preferred chain pairings, across the natural human repertoire\. The maturation of high\-throughput sequencing has generated large database repertoires containing billions of sequences, allowing researchers to assess naïve B\-cell precursor frequencies and evaluate biologically plausible chain combinations\. However, leveraging this scale of data remains a significant bottleneck, as current databases trap scientists between computationally demanding bulk downloads, restrictive, single\-purpose web interfaces or outdated datasets\. To address this gap, we introduce ABHunter, an automatically updated, open\-access framework designed to explore and filter the healthy\-human subset of the Observed Antibody Space \(OAS\) database, which currently stands at \~1\.86\-billion\-sequence as of January 2026\. Accessible via any web browser, the platform executes searches with median times ranging from 3\.7 seconds for simple gene usage profiles to 20\.8 seconds for complex paratope motifs, with full sequence retrieval completed in 118 seconds for 1 million hits\. The interface allows users to quantify antibody feature frequencies to assess the natural abundance of targeted B\-cells across various isotypes \(e\.g\., utilizing IgM for precursor B\-cell analysis\), as well as map native repertoire contexts to scaffold isolated features\. Additionally, it predicts biologically plausible inter\-chain pairings for therapeutic design by using a statistical co\-occurrence model that extrapolates pairing probabilities from the limited natively paired subset comprising 0\.03% of the data across six donors\. Furthermore, every search generates a comprehensive statistical landscape, detailing underlying complementarity\-determining regions length distributions, amino acid compositions, and gene coupling patterns\. For custom analysis and integration into bioinformatic pipelines, the optimized data structure reduces the storage footprint to 106 GB, allowing the entire tool to run locally on a standard laptop\. ABHunter eliminates the compromise between accessibility and flexibility, transforming large\-scale sequencing data into a universally accessible resource for next\-generation therapeutic discovery\. The platform is freely available at abhunter\.org \.

## [FOODTECH INNOVATIONS AND ESG IN THE TRANSFORMATION OF TRADITIONAL WINEMAKING INTO SMART WINE TOURISM DESTINATIONS](../publications/6e9a700b1d2bff9e4992.md)

Олена Олегівна Ахмедова; Anna Chernykhivska

The paper examines the roles of FoodTech innovation and ESG in transforming contemporary wine tourism systems from traditional winemaking models to smart, sustainable destinations\. Particular attention is given to the interaction between technological modernisation in viticulture and winemaking, sustainability\-oriented management practices and the creation of competitive wine tourism experiences\. The study examines how precision viticulture, digital terroir management, traceability platforms, artificial intelligence, craft winemaking innovations and indigenous grape varieties contribute to the development of modern wine tourism ecosystems\. The research substantiates that FoodTech extends beyond technological improvements in wine production and functions as an integrated mechanism that connects vineyard management, wine quality, destination branding, visitor engagement, and sustainability objectives\. Special emphasis is placed on the role of terroir\-based differentiation, alternative vinification methods and the growing importance of craft wineries in strengthening the authenticity and attractiveness of wine\-producing territories\. The study employs a comparative analytical approach and a KPI framework comprising five dimensions\. The comparative assessment covers France, Italy, Portugal, Spain and Ukraine\. The article proposes an integrated analytical framework for evaluating FoodTech\-driven transformation in wine tourism\. It confirms that the long\-term competitiveness of wine\-producing territories increasingly depends on the ability to combine technological innovation, sustainability principles, local identity and visitor\-centred value creation\.

## [Digital self\-management for chronic disease care: a mini review of service integration, equity, and public health implementation priorities](../publications/6e9b6d7ec0827b54751e.md)

Feng Wang; Hongyang Qiao; Yuqin Wu; Xiaoming He; Lan Ying

Digital self\-management is increasingly used to support people with chronic non\-communicable diseases between visits, but its public health value depends on integration into routine care\. This SANRA\-informed critical narrative mini review synthesized 28 sources identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, backward citation tracking and targeted supplementary searches\. It examines digital self\-management as service redesign across three delivery models: patient centered digital support, remote patient monitoring, and integrated primary care or community coordination\. It also analyzes three implementation tensions: empowerment versus digital exclusion, data visibility versus clinical accountability, and engagement versus uncertain long term outcomes and workload\. Evidence suggests benefits for engagement, behavioral support and selected intermediate indicators, but these benefits remain uneven\. Public health implementation should therefore prioritize accountable workflows, interoperable procurement, equity oriented support, safe use of large language model based agents, and evaluation of outcomes, safety, equity, cost and workforce burden\. Digital self\-management should be judged by whether it supports routine, inclusive and sustainable chronic disease care\.

## [Controlled Evidence Mapping of Digitally Enabled Climate\-Smart Tourism: From Fragmented Applications to Integrated Destination Climate Intelligence](../publications/6ea42d553e11fed581e3.md)

Eren Gönül

This study maps the knowledge structure of AI\-enabled climate\-smart tourism and examines how artificial intelligence, digital twins, the Internet of Things, remote sensing, predictive analytics, and climate services support adaptation, mitigation, and destination resilience\. A systematic evidence\-mapping design was combined with controlled bibliometric science mapping\. Following PRISMA 2020 and SPAR\-4\-SLR, 77 records were screened, yielding 50 eligible publications available through June 2026\. Analyses included concept co\-occurrence, temporal overlay, technology–function cross\-tabulation, climate\-relevance coding, and evidence\-maturity assessment\. Publication activity increased after 2023, with planning and governance dominating the literature\. Only 11 studies explicitly addressed climate risk, adaptation, weather, or resilience, while outcome\-level evaluation remained limited\. The findings reveal a sensing\-to\-action gap, as observation, prediction, simulation, implementation, and learning are rarely integrated\. The study conceptualizes AI\-enabled climate\-smart tourism as an outcome\-oriented destination capability and proposes a six\-stage climate\-intelligence cycle connecting sensing, integration, prediction, simulation, decision\-making, adaptation, and learning\.

## [From data to knowledge: how DPP startups span boundaries across stakeholder divides](../publications/6eccb0870fc84d64d7cd.md)

Serdar Temiz; Ayse Ege Palaz; Anders Brantnell

Purpose Digital Product Passports \(DPPs\) aim to increase product transparency and enable circular economy practices\. However, transforming DPP data into actionable knowledge across diverse stakeholder groups remains a key challenge\. This study aims to investigate how startups span syntactic and semantic knowledge boundaries to make DPPs understandable, drawing on knowledge management theory to examine the communicative mechanisms through which product data is translated into shared knowledge across organizational boundaries\. Design/methodology/approach Using Carlile’s \(2004\) boundary\-spanning theory alongside constructs from absorptive capacity, knowledge integration and knowledge governance, this qualitative study analyzes digital materials from 12 European startups and interviews with 10 industry practitioners\. The analysis identifies strategies used to communicate DPP systems across different media and stakeholder contexts\. Findings Extending sequential accounts of knowledge boundary management, startups deploy syntactic and semantic strategies simultaneously through a bundled boundary\-spanning approach\. Syntactic strategies include standardized terminology, visual schemas and role definitions, while semantic strategies encompass narrative framing, technical metaphors, contextual use cases and ESG\-aligned messaging\. These bundles vary systematically across communication channels, stakeholder types and stages of DPP adoption, with web pages prioritizing semantic appeals and whitepapers emphasizing syntactic formalization\. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to early\-stage ventures, publicly available materials and EU\-based contexts\. Further research could explore stakeholder reception, cross\-cultural comparisons and pragmatic boundary dynamics involving interest\-based negotiations\. Practical implications Startups can benefit from intentionally designed communication frameworks that bundle structural clarity with interpretive scaffolding when engaging stakeholders in emerging regulatory contexts\. Policymakers should consider providing communication support tools alongside technical requirements\. Social implications Effective communication of DPPs supports transparency, regulatory compliance and wider public understanding of sustainable product systems\. Originality/value This study offers three contributions to boundary\-spanning scholarship: first, by demonstrating that syntactic and semantic strategies are bundled rather than sequenced in pre\-regulatory contexts; second, by introducing the concept of startups as “trust translators” who convert cryptographic guarantees into accessible narratives; and third, by revealing a temporal dimension to boundary\-spanning in anticipatory regulatory environments where both technical infrastructure and interpretive frameworks must be constructed simultaneously\.

## [Pediatrik Dentofasiyal Sağlık Danışmanlığında Yapay Zekâ Tabanlı Bir Dijital Danışmanın Güvenilirliği: ediatrik Dentofasiyal Sağlıkta Yapay Zekâ Tabanlı Danışmanlık](../publications/6ed0346be4f065aee080.md)

Ceren Yapar Gümüş; Süleyman Kutalmış Büyük; Hale Akdemir

Objective: To evaluate the reliability and quality of Grok artificial intelligence’s \(AI\) responses to commonly asked questions about pediatric dentofacial health\.Methods: Four queries related to detrimental oral habits were submitted to Grok AI in separate sessions\. The generated responses were independently evaluated by orthodontists, pediatricians, and parents without a medical or dental background\. Reliability was assessed using the eight\-item modified DISCERN instrument, and overall information quality was evaluated using the Global Quality Scale \(GQS\)\. Group comparisons were performed using the Kruskal\-Wallis test, and correlations among scores were analyzed using Spearman’s rank correlation\.Results: Across evaluator groups, mean modified DISCERN scores ranged from 23\.85 to 27\.66, and mean GQS scores ranged from 3\.61 to 4\.12, corresponding, overall, to moderate\-to\-good reliability and quality\. No statistically significant differences were observed among orthodontists, pediatricians, and parents for any query\. Correlation analyses showed significant positive associations among several modified DISCERN and GQS parameters, particularly across different queries within the same evaluator groups\. These findings suggested consistent scoring patterns, especially among parents and pediatricians\.Conclusion: Grok AI provided moderately reliable and generally useful responses regarding pediatric dentofacial health\. However, its responses should be considered as supportive educational information rather than a substitute for a professional pediatric or orthodontic assessment\. Further validation using larger question sets, multiple AI models, and more diverse evaluator groups is needed\.

## [Predicting pathogen\-positive blood culture episodes at two hours using electronic health record data](../publications/6eec0f116eb6b4086260.md)

Radu C\. Grovu; Hala Soomro; Nathan Gelinas; Michael Rossi; Sean F\. Monaghan

Most blood cultures obtained early in hospitalization do not yield a pathogen\. We evaluated prediction 2 h after the first blood\-culture record using MIMIC\-IV\. Adults with an initial routine culture record within 24 h of hospital presentation were eligible if alive and still receiving care at prediction\. The cohort included 145,914 encounters, 99\.3% eventually admitted, and 6,404 pathogen\-positive episodes \(4\.39%\)\. Comparisons at 2, 4 and 6 h supported the earliest tested prediction time because later gains were small and uncertain\. The primary XGBoost model was evaluated in 11,523 test encounters; 242 episodes were positive \(2\.10%\)\. AUROC was 0\.819 \(95% CI 0\.792–0\.844\), average precision 0\.124 \(0\.096–0\.167\), and Brier score 0\.0201\. The top 5% of predicted risk contained 81 positives among 577 encounters, giving 14\.0% positivity and 6\.68\-fold enrichment\. Laboratory values, particularly lymphocyte percentage, contributed most to prediction\. Secondary analyses assessed the added value of previous culture results\. Mean predicted risk was 3\.78%, compared with 2\.10% observed\. This 2\-h model was able to concentrate pathogen\-positive episodes in higher\-risk groups, but calibration and transportability require further validation before clinical use\.

## [Sigmoid Volvulus Causing Prolonged Complete Mechanical Intestinal Obstruction Without Bowel Ischemia in a Geriatric Patient: A Case Report](../publications/6ef505638bcfa4ee172c.md)

Felicia Evelyne Soesilo; Yunita Yunita; Ajie Teguh Saputra; Daniel Ardian Soeselo

Introduction: Sigmoid volvulus is a major cause of large bowel obstruction in older adults and can progress to bowel ischemia, necrosis, and perforation\. Although prolonged complete obstruction raises concern for bowel compromise, symptom duration alone does not necessarily indicate bowel nonviability\. This case highlights the importance of intraoperative assessment of bowel viability in determining surgical management\. Case: A 76\-year\-old male with chronic constipation and recently reduced mobility presented with progressive abdominal distension, abdominal pain, and complete absence of defecation and flatus for one week\. He had no fever, nausea, or vomiting\. Laboratory investigations showed hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and impaired renal function\. Contrast\-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated marked bowel dilatation, a redundant sigmoid colon, and twisting consistent with complete mechanical obstruction due to sigmoid volvulus\. After fluid resuscitation, electrolyte correction, and gastrointestinal decompression, exploratory laparotomy was performed\. A 360° rectosigmoid volvulus was identified without ischemia or perforation\. Detorsion and manual decompression were followed by three\-point sigmoidopexy\. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 5\. Discussion: This case is clinically significant because it demonstrates preserved bowel viability despite prolonged complete obstruction\. Intraoperative assessment, rather than symptom duration alone, guided surgical management and allowed a non\-resectional approach\. Conclusion: Prolonged complete mechanical intestinal obstruction due to sigmoid volvulus may occur without bowel necrosis\. Timely stabilization, diagnosis, surgical exploration, and assessment of bowel viability are essential for individualized management\.

## [Investigating Oral Performance Anxiety Among Iraqi First\-Year EFL University Students: Levels, Types, and Contributing Factors](../publications/6f12546bf6eeaf5adc01.md)

Hussien Jawad Abdulridha

Speaking is often the most anxiety\-inducing language skill for EFL learners, and first\-year university students face particular pressure as they transition to more demanding, evaluative oral tasks; however, this challenge remains underexamined among Iraqi university EFL learners specifically\. The present study examined the level, dominant type, and causes of oral performance anxiety among first\-year Iraqi EFL learners\. One hundred\-fifty undergraduate EFL learners from Iraq participated, selected via purposive sampling based on intermediate English proficiency \(ages 20–25\)\. The Causes of Speaking Anxiety Questionnaire \(CSAI\) and the Foreign Language Classroom Anxiety Scale \(FLCAS\) were used, and data were analyzed using SPSS\. Results showed that speaking anxiety was a major problem for the learners in this sample: 90\.6% exhibited high levels of anxiety, with mean scores of 3\.64 for cognitive anxiety, 3\.40 for somatic anxiety, and 3\.40 for behavioral anxiety\. Cognitive anxiety was the most prevalent type\. Fear of receiving a low grade from teachers was the leading cause \(M = 3\.99\), endorsed by 116 of 150 participants \(77\.3%\)\. These findings suggest that speaking anxiety is not a uniform trait among students, and that instructors should adopt supportive feedback, low\-stakes speaking practice, gradual increases in task difficulty, and dedicated preparation time when designing oral activities\.

## [Simulasi Pengambilan Keputusan Berbasis Data dalam Manajemen Pendidikan Islam: Penerapan Metode Simple Additive Weighting dan Analisis Sensitivitas Monte Carlo pada Penetapan Program Prioritas Madrasah](../publications/6f15e3e26a2459c7cb5c.md)

Husnia Ulfa; Waridatul Husna; Ahmad Hilfan Thobiby; Siti Masrohatin

Pengambilan keputusan di madrasah masih banyak bertumpu pada intuisi dan pengalaman pimpinan, padahal sistem informasi manajemen pendidikan telah menyediakan data yang melimpah\. Artikel ini bertujuan merancang dan mendemonstrasikan simulasi pengambilan keputusan berbasis data untuk penetapan program prioritas madrasah\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kajian pustaka terhadap 16 artikel jurnal terbitan 2022–2026 yang dipadukan dengan simulasi kuantitatif\. Simulasi menerapkan metode Simple Additive Weighting \(SAW\) pada empat alternatif program dan lima kriteria, kemudian diuji dengan analisis skenario dan analisis sensitivitas Monte Carlo sebanyak 10\.000 iterasi\. Hasil simulasi menunjukkan bahwa program pelatihan literasi data guru memperoleh skor tertinggi \(V = 0,860\) dan tetap menempati peringkat pertama pada seluruh iterasi, sedangkan urutan peringkat kedua dan ketiga sensitif terhadap perubahan bobot kriteria\. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa simulasi tidak hanya menghasilkan rekomendasi, tetapi juga memetakan tingkat keyakinan atas rekomendasi tersebut sehingga musyawarah pimpinan dapat difokuskan pada alternatif yang benar\-benar bersaing\. Artikel ini merekomendasikan integrasi model simulasi sederhana ke dalam siklus perencanaan madrasah, disertai penguatan literasi data dan prinsip etika Islami seperti amanah dan syura\.

## [Reasoning with Negations: The Australian Plan, Negation\-as\-Failure, and Card Selection Tasks](../publications/6f1f65f6288b31f75a43.md)

Francesco Berto; Greg Restall

Abstract Two kinds of formal semantics for negation can help us understand puzzles in the psychology of reasoning: the Australian Plan semantics , which generalises the account of negation found in frame semantics for intuitionistic logic, relevant and substructural logics; and negation\-as\-failure , found in logic programming and default logic\. We provide a framework where the two kinds of negation coexist, mapping them to the celebrated distinction between System 1 and System 2 thinking\. We use the framework to target the phenomenon of Matching Bias : specifically, to explain why reasoners fare differently in card selection tasks, depending on whether the target property is phrased positively or negatively\.
