## [Multidimensional analysis of social discourse on Twitter \(X\) around Venezuelan migration in Colombia](../publications/6f2987d3f6ea8ef04cb0.md)

Joseph Martínez; Melissa Miller\-Felton; José J\. Padilla; Erika F\. Frydenlund; Katherine Palacio

Colombia has become the principal host of Venezuelan migrants in Latin America, prompting a complex mix of solidarity, anxiety, and discrimination\. This study offers a multidimensional analysis of Twitter \(now X\) discourse on Venezuelan migration in Colombia between 2014 and 2022, using natural language processing, geolocation inference, sentiment analysis, and manual annotation of derogatory terms\. Drawing from 7\.4 million posts, we examine how online discourse evolves across time, space, and language\. While negative sentiment is pronounced in original tweets during periods of political and social unrest, our findings highlight that users tend to amplify neutral and positive messages\-over 67% of retweets fall into these categories\-suggesting an informal counterbalance to polarized discourse\. Additionally, the analysis of the derogatory terms veneco and veneca reveals significant gendered patterns: the feminine form veneca appears more frequently in negative contexts, pointing to the gendered dimensions of xenophobic language\. These results underscore the dual function of social media as a site of both stigmatization and resistance, offering insights into the emotional and cultural dimensions of migration discourse in Colombia&\#x27;s digital public sphere\.

## [Microbiome\-driven precision psychiatry: integrating multi\-omics, artificial intelligence, and personalized interventions along the gut\-brain axis](../publications/6f350ae50c2e059b6721.md)

Yi Zhang; Changyong Pei; Daohua Zhang; Jun Liu

Introduction This scoping review maps evidence for microbiome\-driven precision psychiatry in depression and anxiety\. Methods Following JBI guidance and PRISMA\-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and PubMed Central from inception to July 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and backward citation searching\. Human primary studies were screened and charted; findings were synthesized narratively\. Results Of 58 identified records, 49 remained after deduplication, 35 full texts were assessed, and 28 studies were included\. The evidence was predominantly observational\. Taxonomic findings varied across populations, while studies of microbial functions, metabolites, multi\-omics signatures, and treatment response suggested potential for biological stratification\. Microbiome\-targeted interventions and artificial intelligence models remain exploratory\. Discussion Microbiome\-derived biomarkers and predictive models require standardized methods, independent validation, and prospective evidence of clinical utility before routine psychiatric use\.

## [Interpretable surrogate modeling for load\-aware thermal risk assessment of bolted switchgear busbar joints using electro\-thermal simulation](../publications/6f4504ca3d03459b975d.md)

Kuineng Chen; Huan Liu; Fenglu Li

Thermal\-risk assessment of bolted busbar joints is complicated by the coupled effects of electrical loading, contact condition, and heat dissipation\. This study develops an interpretable forward\-surrogate framework based on three\-dimensional electro\-thermal finite\-element simulation\. Physics enters through finite\-element generation of the training data, physically defined input variables, and post hoc consistency checks, rather than through constraints embedded in the learning algorithm\. Five prescribed inputs were considered: load current, contact resistance, effective contact ratio, ambient temperature, and convective heat\-transfer coefficient\. The effective\-contact heating power was checked against P ≈ I 2 R c , with a maximum relative deviation of 0\.173% across 400 simulated cases; 382 cases were retained within the intended applicability domain\. Four candidate models were compared using 5 × 10 repeated cross\-validation\. The XGBoost regressor achieved R 2 = 0\.990 ± 0\.005 , R M S E = 1\.877 ± 0\.542 , and M A E = 1\.042 ± 0\.198 K , with performance comparable to random forest\. For four\-class simulation\-oriented thermal\-risk classification, XGBoost achieved an accuracy of 0\.938 ± 0\.026 and a macro F1\-score of 0\.941 ± 0\.033 \. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis identified load current and prescribed contact resistance as the dominant contributors, while convection, ambient temperature, and effective contact ratio produced smaller, condition\-dependent effects\. The lower global importance of effective contact ratio reflects the area\-averaged temperature\-rise target and does not imply that current constriction is physically unimportant\. Across three threshold schemes, all out\-of\-fold errors were between adjacent classes\. The framework is geometry\-specific and has not been experimentally validated\. It predicts internal effective\-contact temperature rise; relating this quantity to infrared surface measurements requires further validation\.

## [F2D\-RetinaNet: a feature\-to\-decision dual\-path network with fractional operators for retinal disease detection and grading](../publications/6f525abf26880ea563e5.md)

Mukesh Delu; Priyanka Harjule; Rajesh Kumar; Kushal Gajjar; Pilani Nkomozepi

Visible pathological abnormalities and vascular integrity help diagnose retinal diseases\. This paper introduces a unified feature\-to\-decision framework that first extracts vasculature and enhances lesions\. First, this study proposes the fractional anisotropic diffusion–based hybrid enhancement \(FADHE\) method that selectively amplifies lesion contrast and vessel visibility in the green channel using long\-memory fractional diffusion dynamics\. Second, this study introduces a fractional Hessian\-based attention U\-Net \(FHAU\-Net\), a multi\-scale vessel segmentation model that leverages fractional Hessian responses across eight fractional orders and attention\-guided skip connections to capture fine vessel structures\. Finally, this work designs a dual\-branch disease grading model, F2D\-RetinaNet, which jointly processes the enhanced image and vessel map to learn lesion\-related and vascular feature representations for the recognition and grading of retinal diseases\. The FHAU\-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0\.8987, a sensitivity of 0\.9084, an accuracy of 0\.9804, and a specificity of 0\.9876 across the unified test set, which contains variations in resolution, acquisition site, camera type, and imaging conditions\. The F2D\-RetinaNet is evaluated for Diabetic retinopathy \(DR\) detection, DR grading, and multiclass retinal disease classification tasks\. Extensive testing and comparisons to the baseline procedures support the reliability of the proposed methodology on the datasets evaluated here\.

## [Digital Transformation and Sustainable Performance: A Moderated Mediation Model of Knowledge Sharing Culture, Big Data Analytics, and Environmental Dynamism](../publications/6f59295c2b2eb7069d78.md)

Hanlin Sun; Yongyuan Ma; Ye Wang

ABSTRACT This study investigates the integrative relationships among knowledge sharing culture \(KSC\), big data analytics capability \(BDAC\), digital orientation \(DO\), digital innovation capability \(DIC\), and sustainability performance \(SP\), while examining the mediating role of DIC and the moderating influence of environmental dynamism \(ED\)\. A quantitative cross‐sectional survey methodology was employed, collecting data from 323 managers and senior executives across manufacturing and service sector organizations, with data analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics through descriptive statistics, reliability assessment, correlation analysis, hierarchical regression, and bootstrapping‐based mediation and moderation procedures\. The findings confirm that KSC, BDAC, and DO each exert significant positive direct effects on SP, while DIC successfully mediates all three antecedent relationships with SP, and ED positively moderates the DIC–SP relationship, amplifying innovation‐driven sustainability gains under conditions of heightened external volatility\. This study makes original theoretical contributions by integrating multiple theoretical perspectives within a comprehensive sustainability‐oriented digital capability framework, establishing DIC as a critical mediating bridge and ED as a significant boundary condition, offering practical guidance for leaders seeking to leverage digital capabilities, knowledge culture, and analytics to achieve stronger, more durable SP\.

## [Nearly Tight Spectral Sparsification of Directed Hypergraphs by a Simple Iterative Sampling Algorithm](../publications/6f5f23560f459269925f.md)

Kazusato Oko; Shinsaku Sakaue; Shin‐ichi Tanigawa

Spectral hypergraph sparsification, an attempt to extend well\-known spectral graph sparsification to hypergraphs, has been extensively studied over the past few years\. For undirected hypergraphs, Kapralov, Krauthgamer, Tardos, and Yoshida \(2022\) have proved an $$\\varepsilon $$ \-spectral sparsifier of the optimal $$O^\*\(n\)$$ size, where n is the number of vertices and $$O^\*$$ suppresses the $$\\varepsilon ^\{\-1\}$$ and $$\\log n$$ factors\. For directed hypergraphs, however, the optimal sparsifier size has not been known\. Our main contribution is the first algorithm that constructs an $$O^\*\(n^2\)$$ \-size $$\\varepsilon $$ \-spectral sparsifier for a weighted directed hypergraph\. Our result is optimal up to the $$\\varepsilon ^\{\-1\}$$ and $$\\log n$$ factors since there is a lower bound of $$\\Omega \(n^2\)$$ even for directed graphs\. We also show the first non\-trivial lower bound of $$\\Omega \(n^2/\\varepsilon \)$$ for general directed hypergraphs\. The basic idea of our algorithm is borrowed from the spanner\-based sparsification for ordinary graphs by Koutis and Xu \[30\]\. Their iterative sampling approach is indeed useful for designing sparsification algorithms in various circumstances\. To demonstrate this, we also present a similar iterative sampling algorithm for undirected hypergraphs that attains one of the best size bounds, enjoys parallel implementation, and can be transformed to be fault\-tolerant\.

## [How do multidimensional land use conflicts shape rural multifunctionality? An empirical study of the Yangtze River Delta from a conflict–coordination perspective](../publications/6f64ed39dc717797c2da.md)

Chen Xing Li; Weifeng Qiao; Juan Tang; Meng Yu; Yan Wu; Binpin Gao

In the context of urban–rural integration, how multidimensional land use conflict \(LUC\) differentially shapes rural multifunctionality is a key question for sustainable rural development\. Existing studies, however, have largely treated the two independently, with limited systematic analysis\. This study extends the conflict–coordination perspective from explaining land\-use transition itself to analyzing its effects on rural multifunctionality\. It combines planning\-oriented and machine\-learning suitability assessments to construct an integrated analytical framework linking the pattern, mismatch, and competition dimensions of LUC with rural multifunctionality\. Drawing on multi\-source data for 2000, 2010, and 2020 in the Yangtze River Delta \(YRD\), we use 3\-km rural grid cells as evaluation units and apply generalized additive models and piecewise regression, XGBoost–SHAP, and the geographical pattern causality \(GPC\) model through a progressive sequence of association identification, impact analysis, and causal inference\. The results show that, under the conflict–coordination perspective, the effects of LUC on rural multifunctionality exhibit differentiation, nonlinearity, and bidirectional feedback\. During the study period, rural multifunctionality continued to improve, with non\-agricultural economic function growing fastest, while composite LUC rose at an accelerating rate\. Composite LUC was positively associated with the rural multifunctionality index \(RMI\) in all three study years, but the association weakened beyond the thresholds\. Analysis of changes over 2000–2020, however, showed that intensifying LUC generally coincided with declining rural multifunctionality\. Multidimensional LUC produced differentiated nonlinear effects through spatial form, factor allocation, and functional composition\. The relative importance of LUC increased\. In 2020, spatial pattern conflict showed inverted\-U effects on agricultural production and ecological functions\. Suitability mismatch conflict showed L\-shaped decreasing effects on RMI, agricultural production function, and ecological function, but was associated with stronger non\-agricultural economic function\. Use\-competition conflict had generally positive effects on RMI and agricultural production function, showed an inverted\-U effect on living function, and constrained non\-agricultural economic function in areas where use\-competition conflict was high\. These effects were moderated by natural and locational conditions and varied markedly across space\. GPC tests revealed bidirectional feedback between composite LUC and RMI, with the LUC\-to\-RMI direction dominant\. The negative causal strength of composite LUC on RMI declined slightly before rising again\. Agricultural and non\-agricultural economic activities played a greater role in shaping LUC pressure, whereas living and ecological functions more often reflected the consequences of land allocation\. Non\-agricultural expansion intensified LUC, with gains in living function coexisting with agricultural and ecological losses\. Negative effects on agricultural production function operated mainly through spatial pattern conflict and suitability mismatch conflict, while all three LUC dimensions exerted negative causal effects on ecological function in each study year\. These findings reveal the coexistence of alignment and dislocation between land allocation and functional demands, providing an analytical perspective for understanding the relationship between land use and rural development in regions where rapid urbanization intersects with rural transformation\.

## [What Factors Influence University Students’ Well\-Being and Satisfaction When Engaging in Gig or Platform\-Based Work?](../publications/6f6920262b3dc63ea88e.md)

Tiankai Wu

Despite rapid gig economy growth among university students, research on their well\-being is limited\. Using the JD\-R model, this study examines how job demands \(insecurity, income instability\) and resources \(social support\) affect subjective well\-being and job satisfaction in Chinese student gig workers, with work stress and engagement as mediators, and academic stress and algorithmic transparency as moderators\. A cross\-sectional survey of 155 Chinese student gig workers was analysed via SPSS and PROCESS\. Results show insecurity negatively predicts well\-being, income instability reduces satisfaction, and social support has the strongest positive effects\. Work stress fully mediates the insecurity–well\-being link, while engagement partially mediates social support effects\. No moderation effects were found\. Findings extend the JD\-R model to this under\-studied population, reveal distinct psychological pathways, and offer practical implications for platforms, universities, and policymakers\. Limitations and future directions are discussed\.

## [PERKEMBANGAN AKUNTANSI DI ERA INDUSTRI 4\.0 : TANTANGAN DAN PELUANG UNTUK PROFESI AKUNTANSI](../publications/6f6c45ebb88afce7efab.md)

Anggi Arista

The industrial revolution has evolved from Industry 1\.0 through Industry 2\.0 and 3\.0, and has now reached the midpoint of the fourth revolution—the Industry 4\.0 era\. This era is characterized by automation, the integration of cyber\-physical systems, big data, artificial intelligence \(AI\), the Internet of Things \(IoT\), and cloud computing\. The adoption of these technologies is transforming business procedures and models across various sectors\. As a vital aspect of the business world, accounting is inevitably affected by these changes; indeed, many accounting functions have been enhanced by the advent of these modern technologies\. This study aims to examine the impact of Industry 4\.0 technological advancements on accounting practices, as well as the roles, challenges, and opportunities facing the accounting profession in this digital era\. It employs a literature review approach to analyze data sourced from materials such as books, scholarly journals, and other relevant documents, without involving fieldwork\. A descriptive\-qualitative approach is used to explain the concepts, theories, and expert perspectives related to the research topic\. The findings indicate that technological advancements in the Industry 4\.0 era have brought about fundamental changes in accounting practices and the profession\. The utilization of digital technologies—such as automation, artificial intelligence, big data, and cloud\-based information systems—has improved the efficiency and accuracy of accounting processes\. However, this shift also presents challenges for the profession, including the need for information technology proficiency, the requirement to enhance human resource competencies, and risks associated with data security and professional ethics\.

## [Phenanthrene\-based Pyrazoline Derivatives as Emerging Anticancer Agents: Synthetic Strategy, Molecular Targets, Structure Activity relationships and in\-silico Approaches](../publications/6f708125de2e5ef80d5f.md)



Cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide and continues to pose a major challenge to healthcare systems despite significant advances in diagnosis and treatment\.Conventional chemotherapy is frequently associated with poor selectivity, systemic toxicity, multidrug resistance and disease recurrence, highlighting the need for safer and more effective targeted anticancer agents\.Hybrid molecules containing multiple pharmacologically active scaffolds have emerged as a promising strategy for overcoming these limitations\.Among these, phenanthrene, pyrazoline, carboxamide and phenolic pharmacophores have attracted considerable attention because of their diverse biological activities and their ability to interact with multiple molecular targets involved in tumor initiation and progression\.Phenanthrene derivatives exhibit strong DNAbinding properties and interfere with cell proliferation, whereas pyrazoline derivatives possess remarkable antiproliferative, antiangiogenic and pro\-apoptotic activities\.Carboxamide moieties enhance receptor binding through hydrogen\-bonding interactions and contribute to improved pharmacokinetic properties, while phenolic substituents provide antioxidant activity and regulate intracellular signaling pathways associated with oxidative stress and apoptosis\.This review summarizes recent developments in phenanthrene\-based pyrazoline carboxamide derivatives as potential anticancer agents\.Particular emphasis is placed on synthetic strategies, structure\-activity relationships\(SAR\), molecular mechanisms and important therapeutic targets including Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor \(EGFR\), Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptor\-2 \(VEGFR\-2\), Carbonic Anhydrase IX/XII \(CA IX/XII\), Topoisomerase II, BRAF kinase, Aurora kinases, Cyclin\-Dependent Kinase\-2 \(CDK2\) and tubulin\.The role of molecular docking, virtual screening, drug\-likeness evaluation and ADME/ADMET prediction in lead optimization is also discussed\.Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for developing multifunctional phenanthrene\-pyrazoline hybrids are highlighted\.The integration of experimental medicinal chemistry with computational drug discovery is expected to accelerate the development of novel targeted anticancer therapeutics\.

## [Waste Bin Design Matters: Evidence From a Controlled Experiment With a Waste Separation Task](../publications/6f7a7a85eb718546a3f3.md)

Anna Högberg; Camilla Grane; Patrik Sörqvist

Waste separation prevents material contamination, which is key to sustainable recycling\. Evidence suggests that waste bin design can influence the way people separate waste when recycling\. However, this evidence comes from field studies with relatively low internal validity\. We report results from a controlled experiment \(N = 100\) using a novel waste sorting task to isolate the effect of bin design on recycling behavior\. We focused on whether participants accurately placed refundable bottles/cans in special waste bins \(called &quot;deposit collection tubes&quot;\)\. Results showed that a blue/experimental deposit collection tube improved sorting of refundable bottles/cans compared to a gray/conventional version\. This effect was quite large \(odds ratio = 2\.25\), remained consistent after statistical control of individual differences \(e\.g\., recycling norms, habits\), and was explained by the blue tube&\#x27;s superior noticeability\. These results show that waste bin design really matters to recycling behavior and that an appropriate design can guide people to a desirable outcome\. Design and policy implications are discussed\.

## [Enhanced Access Control Management System in an Edge Computing Environment Using Bimodal Biometrics Technique](../publications/6f85afe92067f7f22c74.md)

Paul Ohia; Friday Eleonu Onuodu; Ugochi A\. Okengwu

This study presents an enhanced access control management system for edge computing environments using bimodal biometrics, contextual risk analysis, and Chinese Wall policy enforcement\. The work addresses a limitation in context\-only access control frameworks, namely their inability to confirm that the person requesting access is the genuine enrolled user\. To close this identity\-verification gap, the proposed system integrates face recognition, fingerprint recognition, and contextual decision support into a unified edge\-aware authentication workflow\. The implementation was developed in Python using Flask, with MySQL for transactional data storage and IPFS for content\-addressed storage of biometric\-related artifacts\. A hybrid dataset strategy was adopted\. Public datasets such as VGGFace2 and SOCOFing supported preliminary experimentation, while locally captured biometric samples were emphasized for operational training and evaluation in order to reduce domain mismatch\. A one\-dimensional convolutional neural network was used for contextual access analysis, while transfer\-learning\-based convolutional neural networks were used for face and fingerprint recognition\. The datasets were split into 70% training and 30% testing\. Experimental results showed strong performance for the biometric and contextual modules\. The face model achieved about 0\.96 accuracy, the fingerprint model achieved about 93\.36% classification accuracy with 95\.83% precision, recall, and F1\-score for the enrolled\-user fingerprint class, and the contextual Conv1D model achieved 84\.08% test accuracy\. System\-level testing further showed that integrating biometric evidence with contextual intelligence and policy enforcement improved access\-decision reliability over the earlier context\-only model\. The study concludes that combining bimodal biometrics with edge\-based contextual reasoning can provide stronger identity assurance, better real\-time responsiveness, and more dependable access control for distributed computing environments\.

## [A Critique of the Argument View:](../publications/6f87e3a495df4ef94bbe.md)

Roberto Schmitz Nitsche; Tiegüe Vieira Rodrigues

The Argument View posits that thought experiments are merely arguments in disguise, deriving their epistemic power from logical inference\. This paper challenges this view, arguing that it rests on a fundamental category error by mischaracterizing the cognitive activity of thought experimentation\. We demonstrate that the process of running a thought experiment is phenomenologically and structurally distinct from executing an inference\. Specifically, it fails to satisfy the necessary taking condition – where a thinker must take their premises to support their conclusion – a core feature of genuine, person\-level reasoning\. This critique is shown to be decisive against the strong Execution Thesis\. We then extend our analysis to the weaker Reconstructibility Thesis, arguing that it severs the link between a subject and their justification and makes a fatal concession about the indispensable epistemic role of the narrative itself\. We conclude that the Argument View is an untenable model because it conflates the imaginative process of discovery with its potential post\-hoc logical validation\.

## [Right access, right patient, right time: Individualized planning](../publications/6f94174135b8db68b4de.md)

Muhammad Nauman Hashmi

Vascular access is the lifeline for patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis, yet selection, creation, and maintenance remain challenging\. Arteriovenous fistulas provide superior long\-term patency, lower infection risk, and better dialysis efficiency but require suitable vessels and maturation time\. Arteriovenous grafts offer faster usability in patients with inadequate veins but have higher rates of infection and intervention\. Central venous catheters provide immediate access but are associated with the highest morbidity and mortality\. Vascular access failure is driven primarily by neointimal hyperplasia, thrombosis, abnormal vascular remodeling, and, occasionally, distal ischemia\. Optimal outcomes require individualized, patient\-centered strategies that integrate patient characteristics, vessel anatomy, and timing\. A structured framework aligning “right patient, right access, and right time” can minimize complications, reduce reliance on temporary catheters, and improve dialysis efficacy and patient quality of life\.

## [Noise\-Robust Forced Alignment for Spontaneous Speech](../publications/6faa40e2a8964fa990aa.md)

Laurin Wagner; Mario Zusag

We show that forced aligners degrade on spontaneous, noisy real\-world speech, and that fillers, laughter, and disfluencies corrupt word boundaries, impacting many downstream applications\. We revisit the classical GMM\-HMM aligner with upsampled WavLM features instead of MFCCs, explicit phone units for fillers and non\-lexical vocal events trained on verbatim\-annotated spontaneous speech, and a discriminative projection fitted on clean and noise\-corrupted feature pairs to improve robustness\. The pipeline is self\-bootstrapped from 149h of curated audio without manual or external boundary targets\. On conversational \(Buckeye\) and disfluent \(FluencyBank\) speech it reaches word\-boundary MAEs of 20\.6 and 76\.9ms, 19% and 17% lower than the strongest of ten baselines\. Catastrophic misalignments \(&gt;200ms\) are 2\.7 times rarer than Montreal Forced Aligners \(MFA\) best model even after widening MFA&\#x27;s search beam, which we show removes a large pruning artifact from its conversational error; event units halve the error next to laughter, while being meaningfully more robust than existing aligners\.

## [Research on the Teaching Mechanism of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Promoting Young Children&\#x27;s Imitative Poetry Composition](../publications/6fb2da5b3a9c97026425.md)

Tingting Wang

In this work we examine pedagogical role and underlying mechanisms of generative AI in helping young children with imitative poetry composition because it is complex task that can be difficult for students in classroom\. Also I analyze how AI intervention affects language expression and classroom interaction, and creative performance in classroom and it is worth noting that these are important factors for the study\. I use a quasi\-experimental design with mixed methods\. Through the use of the Imitative Poetry Ability Scale assessment, classroom observations, analysis of student works, and interviews, combined with independent samples t\-tests and thematic coding, the following findings were obtained that generative AI can improve language completeness in children&\#x27;s imitative poetry, and the imagery creativity and classroom engagement are also enhanced\. AI generated images and interactive feedback can stimulate imaginative expressions\. It is worth noting that they also help support collaborative multimodal learning\.

## [Examining Emotion Regulation and the Link Between Childhood Adversity and Secondary Trauma in First Responders](../publications/6fcc1389e2423fa618f3.md)

Maci Lenora Harmon

First responders are routinely exposed to traumatic events in the course of their professional duties, placing them at increased risk for secondary traumatic stress \(STS\)\. However, psychological responses to occupational trauma exposure vary considerably across individuals\. Developmental research suggests that adverse childhood experiences \(ACEs\) may contribute to long\-term alterations in emotional functioning and stress responsivity, potentially increasing vulnerability to later trauma\-related symptoms\. Emotion regulation \(ER\) has been identified as a transdiagnostic process associated with trauma\-related stress\. Furthermore, ER may function as a pathway linking early adversity to occupational stress outcomes\. The purpose of this quantitative, cross\-sectional correlational mediation study was to examine the relationship between ACEs and STS among first responders, and to determine whether ER mediates this relationship\. Participants included active, or recently active, first responders in the state of Georgia\. Participants completed an anonymous online survey consisting of the Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire \(ACE\-Q\), the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale\-Short Form \(DERS\-SF\), and the Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale \(STSS\-17\)\. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlations and mediation analysis\. Results indicated significant positive relationships among ACEs, difficulties in ER, and STS\. Mediation analysis further demonstrated a significant indirect effect of ACEs on STS through difficulties in ER\. When ER difficulties were included in the model, the direct effect of ACEs was no longer statistically significant, consistent with a mediating relationship\. These findings highlight ER as an important mechanism in the relationship between childhood adversity and STS\. Furthermore, these findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the developmental and regulatory factors associated with vulnerability to STS within trauma\-exposed professions\.

## [Linguistic complexity and writing proficiency in assessing L2 Spanish writing](../publications/6fcc9cb8603d7a344b66.md)

Peiyu Yang; Wenqian Huang; Guangyuan Yao

Abstract Although linguistic complexity is widely used to assess second language \(L2\) writing proficiency, the linguistic correlates of L2 Spanish writing proficiency remain relatively underexplored\. This study addresses this gap by examining how selected lexical, syntactic, and morphological complexity indices predict L2 Spanish learners’ standardized proficiency scores\. We analyzed a corpus of 3,034 essays from L2 Spanish learners, utilizing their standardized placement test scores as a continuous measure of proficiency\. A multiple linear regression model identified a concise set of complexity indices that effectively predicted proficiency scores, explaining a significant portion of the variance \( R 2 = \.557\)\. Results reveal a clear proficiency\-based linguistic profile: advanced writing was significantly predicted by greater phrasal complexity, sustained clausal subordination, and higher lexical sophistication\. In contrast, beginners’ writing was characterized by simpler syntactic strategies\. These findings provide a robust, empirically derived profile of L2 Spanish writing development, offering valuable implications for pedagogical instruction, assessment rubrics, and automated evaluation tools\.

## [Physics\-informed hybrid machine learning for predicting effects of metal oxide nano additives on performance and emissions of biodiesel\-fueled engines](../publications/6fd2f955da769728318a.md)

Chenxu Duan; Ya Wang; Luwen Wang; Huiyi Cui; Shiqiang Luo

Accurate prediction of the performance and emission characteristics of nanoparticle\-enhanced biodiesel\-fueled compression ignition engines is essential for efficient engine optimization, cleaner combustion, and reducing experimental costs and time\. This study integrates combustion physics with stacked ensemble learning to develop a physics\-informed Bayesian\-optimized hybrid \(PIBoH\) framework to simultaneously predict brake thermal efficiency \(BTE\), brake\-specific fuel consumption \(BSFC\), hydrocarbon \(HC\), carbon monoxide \(CO\), and nitrogen oxide \(NO x \) emissions\. A comprehensive experimental database was compiled from published studies covering diverse biodiesel feedstocks, metal oxide nanoparticles, and engine operating conditions\. To embed domain knowledge into the learning process, conventional categorical descriptors were replaced with physically meaningful fuel\-property variables, a quantitative additive overall effectiveness index, and seven physics\-informed engineered features\. Bayesian optimization was employed to fine\-tune hyperparameters of the PIBoH framework\. The designed framework predicted 298 datasets with average absolute relative deviations of 4\.48%, 3\.44%, 5\.42%, 6\.63%, and 5\.30% for BTE, BSFC, HC, CO, and NO x , respectively, corresponding to coefficients of determination of 0\.9543, 0\.9808, 0\.9924, 0\.9934, and 0\.9901\. Applicability\-domain analysis further demonstrated reliable prediction stability across the investigated operating conditions\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis identified fuel density and engine load as the dominant variables governing both engine performance and pollutant formation\.

## [Digital Resilience](../publications/6fd9f22e27a77547c3b7.md)

Heejung Ryoh

The COVID\-19 pandemic served as a brutal stress test for museum resilience\. While many institutions relied on a &\#x27;substitutive model&\#x27; of mere digital replacement, the National Museum of Korea \(NMK\) achieved anomalous growth through a strategic pivot\. This study employs an explanatory single\-case study design to investigate the mechanisms behind this success\. Applying pattern matching logic, the research validates the efficacy of a &\#x27;Transformative Model&\#x27; grounded in Cultural Democracy\. Findings reveal that the NMK&\#x27;s integration of AI\-driven personalization, immersive Extended Reality \(XR\) experiences, and radical inclusivity reconfigured the visitor relationship from passive consumption to active co\-creation\. Crucially, empirical data confirms a positive correlation where high\-level digital engagement functioned as a catalytic gateway that drove, rather than cannibalized, physical attendance\. This case illustrates how sustainable resilience can be achieved when technology is strategically deployed to democratize heritage access and empower the visitor as an active participant\.

## [Coronary plaque characteristics of acute myocardial infarction patients with and without previous ischemic stroke](../publications/6fdb3039a098bbf03e39.md)

Qiuping Wang; Fuhong Dong; Chao Fang; Sining Hu; Haibo Jia; Weili Pan; Lulu Li; Jianjun Wu; Luping He; YiNi Wang; Tao Chen; Huai Yu; Jiannan Dai; Bo Yu

Background Acute myocardial infarction \(AMI\) occurring after ischemic cerebral stroke leads to substantially worse short\- and long\-term outcomes, as indicated by emerging evidence\. Few studies explore possible plaque features\. Methods From September 2019 to December 2021, 1050 AMI patients were enrolled\. The individuals were divided into two groups based on whether they had suffered an ischemic stroke before percutaneous coronary intervention \(PCI\)\. Patients from both groups underwent 1:1 propensity score matching \(PSM\) with a caliper width of 0\.02\. Ultimately, the final study cohort comprised 386 patients\. Results Regarding culprit lesions, patients in the stroke group exhibited a greater prevalence of thin\-cap fibroatheromas \(TCFA, 70\.0% vs\. 55\.4%, p = 0\.003\), macrophage accumulation \(52\.3% vs\. 39\.4%, p = 0\.011\), a longer lipid core length \(15\.3 ± 7\.4 mm vs\. 13\.5 ± 6\.4 mm, p = 0\.013\), and a higher lipid index \(3,465\.0 ± 2,135\.8 vs\. 2,946\.4 ± 1,784\.4, p = 0\.011\), compared to non\-stroke patients\. Concerning non\-culprit plaques, prior stroke was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of TCFA \(OR 2\.08, 95% CI 1\.15–3\.74, p = 0\.014\)\. The clinical follow\-up results revealed a significantly higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in the stroke group \(8\.9% vs\. 4\.2%, p = 0\.009, HR 2\.61, 95% CI 1\.28–5\.34\), along with a greater frequency of recurrent stroke \(4\.2% vs\. 1\.6%, p = 0\.019, HR 3\.78, 95% CI 1\.23–9\.30\) and a higher cardiac mortality rate \(5\.8% vs\. 1\.6%, p = 0\.011, HR 3\.55, 95% CI 1\.33–9\.47\) than the non\-stroke group\. Conclusion In stroke patients, coronary multivessel disease is common and characterized by high\-risk plaque features and increased cardiovascular event susceptibility, with prior ischemic stroke being associated with a higher prevalence of these OCT\-defined high\-risk features\.

## [Chemogenetic inhibition of the ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex disrupts novelty\-guided updating of spatial memories and alters hippocampal engram reactivation](../publications/6fdd97a907159f234b5b.md)

K I Kim; Dawnbe Yu; William F Wade; Rowan Zdziarski\-West; Z\. Ahmad; Mikayla Cutler; Grace Romanelli; Adam Daki; Stephanie L\. Grella

Abstract Rationale Adaptive behavior requires revising memories when outcomes deviate from expectations\. The orbitofrontal cortex \(OFC\) is implicated in representing outcome expectancies, but its role in memory\-updating, beyond value\-based learning, remains unclear\. Objectives We tested whether the ventrolateral OFC \(VLO\) contributes to hippocampal\-dependent memory\-updating in the Objects in Updated Locations \(OUL\) task, where novelty\-driven exploration provides a behavioral readout consistent with successful updating of spatial information Methods Using inhibitory DREADDs, in male and female \(Swiss Webster and C57BL/6\) mice, we suppressed VLO activity during the Updating session, when new object\-location information was introduced\. Results Control mice preferentially explored the updated object\-location configuration during Updating and discriminated between updated and novel object\-location configurations at Test, whereas VLO\-inhibited mice did not\. VLO inhibition when no updating demand was present did not alter exploration of novel object\-location configurations or memory for the original spatial configuration at Test\. Conclusions These results indicate that VLO activity is selectively required when novelty must be interpreted relative to prior experience, implicating this region in evaluating change rather than detecting it\. To assess hippocampal ensemble dynamics, we tagged neuronal ensembles, in the dorsal dentate gyrus \(dDG\) recruited during Updating, followed by quantification of overlap between Updating\-tagged cells and ensembles reactivated at Test\. We found that VLO inhibition reduced reactivation of Updating\-tagged dDG ensembles, paralleling the behavioral impairments observed in the OUL task\. These findings support a role for the VLO in hippocampal\-dependent memory\-updating and extend OFC models beyond reward contexts to include predictive updating of spatial memory representations\. Significance Statement Using a spatial paradigm that distinguishes detection of changed information from incorporation of that information into an updated hippocampal representation, we found that ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex \(VLO\) activity is required for memory\-updating when new information is present\. We found behavioral deficits accompanied by impairments in hippocampal ensemble representations, indicating VLO activity is necessary for memory\-updating at the hippocampal engram level\. Through this mechanism, the OFC supports the flexible updating of expected outcomes when environmental conditions shift, allowing for the re\-evaluation of previously learned associations\. These findings extend models of orbitofrontal cortex function beyond reward\-guided behavior and identify a cortical contribution to predictive spatial memory processes\. Disruption of this computation may contribute to the cognitive rigidity observed in neuropsychiatric disorders\.

## [Sustainable Competitive Intelligence for Institutional Resilience: Crisis Response and Sustainable Development in Private Universities](../publications/6fe2ede893495734d24c.md)

Yutong Yang; Pengfei Chen; Kexiu Fang

Purpose: This study examines how private universities convert environmental intelligence into institutional sustainable development \(ISD\), testing whether organizational resilience mediates the relationship between crisis response and ISD\. Drawing on competitive intelligence and complemented by dynamic capabilities theory, it treats crisis response and resilience as the utilization and feedback stages of an institution\-level intelligence capability that supports a sustainable competitive position\. Methodology/approach: Guided by a competitive\-intelligence and dynamic\-capabilities framework, a cross\-sectional survey was administered to faculty members and administrators of private universities in Yunnan, China, yielding 742 valid responses\. Constructs were validated through confirmatory factor analysis; the mediation model was tested with hierarchical regression and bias\-corrected bootstrapping \(5,000 resamples\), controlling for gender, age, and leadership level\. Originality/Relevance: The study reframes crisis response and organizational resilience as components of an institution\-level competitive\-intelligence capability, which is the utilization and feedback stages of the intelligence cycle that underpins a university&\#x27;s sustainable competitive advantage, and provides rare evidence from resource\-constrained, non\-elite private higher education\. Key findings: Crisis response positively predicted organizational resilience \(β = \.33\) and ISD \(total effect β = \.49\), and resilience positively predicted ISD \(β = \.32\)\. Resilience partially mediated the crisis response–ISD relationship \(indirect effect = \.11; 95% CI \[\.076, \.136\]\), accounting for roughly 22% of the total effect\. All four hypotheses were supported\. Theoretical/methodological contributions: This study extends dynamic capabilities theory to the institutional level in higher education and links it to the competitive\-intelligence literature, positioning crisis response and resilience as the utilization and feedback stages of an institutional intelligence system\. Methodologically, it empirically establishes resilience as the mechanism linking crisis response to sustainability and validates a multidimensional instrument for reuse\.

## [Use of artificial intelligence in health education: A bibliometric analysis \(2018–2025\)](../publications/6fe77c000e52d4d7bfc8.md)

Gamze AĞARTIOĞLU KUNDAKÇI; İbrahim Halil Özdemır; Fırat Sarsar

Objective: This study aimed to provide an overview of the current state and emerging directions of artificial intelligence research in health education \(focusing on patient and public health education rather than professional medical training\) through a bibliometric analysis\. Methods: Publications indexed in the Web of Science database between 2018 and 2025 that focused on artificial intelligence in health education \(encompassing patient education, public health and community health communication\) were analysed\. 577 articles meeting the inclusion criteria were examined using Biblioshiny and Python to assess annual publication trends, citation patterns, influential journals and authors, collaboration networks, co\-citation structures and thematic evolution\. Findings were synthesised using descriptive statistics and visual mapping\. Results: The findings show a marked increase in artificial intelligence research in health education, particularly after 2023\. The literature increasingly concentrates on patient education–related themes, including health literacy, readability, accuracy and the use of conversational agents\. Research output and citation impact are dominated by a few countries, notably the USA and China, and are concentrated within a small group of core journals and collaborative networks\. Thematic analyses reveal a transition from technology\-oriented foundations towards patient\- and clinic\- applications\. Conclusion: Artificial intelligence research in health education now plays a strategic role beyond technical discussions, focusing on patient education and patient–provider health communication\. This study maps research trends and highlights areas for future work, especially on the quality, clarity and reliability of artificial intelligence–supported patient information\.

## [LLM\-Driven Query Planning for Intelligent Access to Structured and Semi\-Structured Data](../publications/6fe91c8bde72473f5c71.md)

Mykola Khoroshevskyi

This paper addresses intelligent access to structured and semi\-structured data using large language models \(LLMs\)\. We develop an approach to LLM\-driven query planning in which a user’s information need is handled as a sequence of interdependent operations: query analysis, grounding in data sources and the schema, plan construction, execution, validation of intermediate results, and, when needed, replanning\. The study draws on a comparative analysis of the open benchmarks BIRD, Spider 2\.0, and HybridQA and of representative published approaches, from Text\-to\-SQL pipelines such as DIN\-SQL and CHASE\-SQL to hybrid methods such as BlendSQL and Weaver\. The proposed architecture separates planning from execution and allows SQL operations to be combined with semantic processing by an LLM\. We formalize the plan as a directed acyclic graph of typed SQL, semantic, and lookup operations with validation predicates, define the conditions for partial replanning, and illustrate the procedure with a worked example\. Our analysis of existing experimental results indicates that decomposing complex queries, combining heterogeneous sources, and monitoring intermediate state are each associated with higher accuracy or lower cost in multi\-step data access tasks\. The evidence supports assigning the LLM the role of a control component that coordinates the sequence of actions, although the proposed architecture still needs to be evaluated quantitatively under uniform experimental conditions\. To that end, we propose an evaluation protocol with baselines, ablation variants, and falsifiable predictions\.

## [Design and Construction of Web\-Based and Mobile Cattle Feed Management System and Cattle Health Monitoring System Using the Prototyping Method](../publications/700ce052f540f54d842a.md)

Hernawati Susanti Samosir; Cynthia Deborah Nababan; Bella Wahmilyana Asril; Tantri Harianti Silaen; Oktavia Letisya Simatupang; Keren Simanjuntak; Christian Jhon Pranata Panjaitan; Hasan Sinaga; Nita Herlinda Kurnyawati Simangunsong; Sahat Pandapotan Nainggolan

Livestock management operations are often inefficient and error\-prone because agricultural institutions frequently rely on manual recording of cattle feed and health data\. This study aims to develop an integrated web and mobile information system for cattle feed management and health monitoring, implemented for the Herbal and Horticultural Science and Technology Park \(TSTH2\), Pollung, Humbang Hasundutan Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia\. The system was designed using a prototyping methodology through three iterative cycles, each involving stakeholder communication, rapid planning, design, modeling, prototype construction, and user evaluation\. The resulting system includes 68 functional components: 24 for feed management and 44 for health monitoring\. The web platform was implemented using React\.js for the front end, with Express\.js serving as the back end for the feed management subsystem and Django REST Framework for the health monitoring subsystem\. In contrast, Flutter was used for the mobile platform of both subsystems\. Functional testing used black\-box testing with a 100% success rate on both devices, and user acceptance testing had a satisfaction score of 76\.96% \(good/acceptable\)\. To improve the system&\#x27;s intelligence, future research should add flexible scheduling algorithms and AI\-based decision support\. ## [The Role of Smart Systems on Reducing the Recovery Time Objective “RTO” for Security Service Continuity in Airports: A Case Study of Dubai International Airport](../publications/700de4ba94bfe9b011c6.md)

Ahmed Mohamed Saleh Ahmed; Ibrahim Mohamed Alsaa&\#x27;dy Elshreei

Research Summary This research examines the role of smart systems in enhancing the continuity of security services and managing crises and operational disruptions in smart airports, with particular emphasis on their impact on reducing the Recovery Time Objective “RTO”\. The research is grounded in the premise that the integration of smart systems extends beyond improving routine operational efficiency to becoming a critical enabler of dynamic security resilience during crisis situations\. Using a descriptive\-analytical approach, the study combines theoretical frameworks related to risk management and business continuity with an applied case study of Dubai International Airport as a high\-density smart airport model\. The findings demonstrate that the “security – operational” integration of automated screening systems, biometric identification technologies, self\-service platforms, and command\-and\-control centers significantly contributes to reducing response time and RTO while maintaining decision accuracy and the continuity of critical security functions\. The study concludes that smart systems represent a strategic pathway for strengthening security resilience in airports, supporting sovereignty requirements, crisis management capabilities, and the sustainability of security operations in highly sensitive environments\.

## [Compound heterozygous RHCE null genotype underlying D−− phenotype in a Chinese pregnant woman: molecular characterization and sequential transfusion strategy](../publications/701a26e4aa28e5ed85ea.md)

Wenjing Zhou; Li An; Lei Li; Haiyan Wan; Wangnan Sun; Qi He; Na Zhao; Mo Wang; 浑守永

The D−− phenotype is an extremely rare Rh blood group variant with absence of C, c, E, and e antigens but preserved D expression, predisposing to anti\-Rh17 alloimmunization and hemolytic disease of fetus and newborn \(HDFN\)\. We report a 25\-year\-old Chinese woman \(gravida 3, para 1\) with D\+C−c−E−e− phenotype and a history of severe neonatal jaundice and fetal demise\. In her current pregnancy, admitted at 25 \+5 weeks for elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity\. PacBio sequencing \(proband and her parents\) and Oxford Nanopore whole\-genome sequencing \(ONT WGS; proband\) were performed\. PacBio sequencing preliminarily identified a compound heterozygous state at the RHCE locus involving two distinct RHCE \-null haplotypes, a paternal complex structural variant and a maternal RHCE\*02N\.03 null allele with seven mutations\. Subsequent ONT WGS resolved a novel paternal chimeric RHD–TMEM50A–RHCE rearrangement arising from dual recombination events\. Serological and family evidence suggest that the maternal RHCE\*02N\.03 allele with c\.486 \+ 1G&gt;A results in a C−e− null phenotype in the compound heterozygous state\. Four serial intrauterine transfusions used allogeneic D−− donor blood or maternal autologous washed irradiated packed red blood cells\. All transfusions were well tolerated, with delivery at 37 weeks by cesarean section and favorable neonatal outcomes\. This case demonstrates a sequential transfusion strategy for D−− pregnancies—prioritizing allogeneic D−− blood from rare donor networks when available, with maternal autologous blood as a safe alternative—and, through complementary PacBio and ONT WGS, adds evidence that complex RHD\-RHCE inversion\-recombination events may represent recurret mechanisms in the Chinese population while refining RHCE\*02N\.03 annotation from C− to C−e−\.

## [Domain\-specific language alignment of multimodal embeddings towards explainable predictions](../publications/70203e6efefb093a8ec9.md)

Gabrielė Tijūnaitytė; Thijs L\. van der Plas; Mohamed\-Bachir Belaid; Rob Knapen; Maciej J\. Soja; Ioannis N\. Athanasiadis

Multimodal data are commonly fused into latent representations that improve downstream task performance but are not interpretable, limiting their application in domains that require explainable model decisions\. Vision\-language alignment has made image embeddings interpretable through language, but requires vast image\-caption training data\. However, captioned data are typically not available for multimodal embeddings, as relevant features cannot directly be observed and annotated from embeddings alone\. Here, we propose a framework to language\-align any embedding space that can be linked to interpretable auxiliary data\. Captioning functions convert auxiliary data into partial captions; a soft contrastive loss weights pairs by the similarity of their properties that each caption describes; and a rank\-based concept retrieval task evaluates alignment against the auxiliary data rather than the captions\. We apply this framework to multimodal Earth embeddings to facilitate explainable predictions for two species distribution modelling tasks: S2BMS and SatBird\. AlphaEarth embeddings beat previous state\-of\-the\-art models on 6/7 metrics, while our framework language\-aligns domain\-specific concepts of the embedding space, outperforming previous Earth observation vision\-language models on average concept retrieval for both datasets\. Finally, aligned concepts recover species\-habitat associations \($ρ$=0\.44\) and relate habitat descriptions to species predictions, showing that abstract embeddings can be interrogated in the language of domain experts\.

## [Au, André: Das ungeteilte Feld: Wie Quantenphysik, Kognitionswissenschaft und Mystik im Unus Mundus konvergieren](../publications/70246065632165741f4a.md)



Diese interdisziplinäre philosophische Abhandlung untersucht die Möglichkeit, dass Bewusstsein, Materie und Information keine voneinander getrennten Grundgegebenheiten darstellen, sondern unterschiedliche Erscheinungsweisen einer tieferen, ungeteilten Wirklichkeit\. Ausgangspunkte sind das harte Problem des Bewusstseins und die Krise der Raumzeit als fundamentale Kategorie\. Erkenntnisse aus Quantenphysik, Kosmologie und Kognitionswissenschaft werden mit philosophischen und mystischen Traditionen in Beziehung gesetzt – nicht als naturwissenschaftlicher Beweis spiritueller Lehren, sondern als Einladung, die Grenzen eines rein mechanistisch\-materialistischen Weltbildes zu überprüfen\. Wahrnehmung erscheint dabei als evolutionär geformtes Interface: nicht als unmittelbare Abbildung der Wirklichkeit, sondern als biologisch nützliches Modell, dessen Gegenstände symbolischen Charakter besitzen\. Zugleich wird gefragt, ob künstliche Intelligenz und die technologische Entwicklung als Fortsetzung einer umfassenderen kosmischen Evolution verstanden werden können\. Der Begriff des Unus Mundus dient als verbindendes Denkbild für eine Wirklichkeit, in der die Trennung zwischen Beobachter und Beobachtetem, Geist und Materie sowie Individuum und Welt nicht ursprünglich, sondern abgeleitet ist\. Das Werk versteht sich als philosophischer Essay und als Anregung zu eigener Prüfung, nicht als abgeschlossene Theorie\. Eine englische Übersetzung ist unter dem Titel The Undivided Field: How Quantum Physics, Cognitive Science, and Mysticism Converge in the Unus Mundus verfügbar\.

## [Automation of Food and Beverage Processes using Integrated Software Solutions](../publications/7050f459b8b16c43f7d0.md)

K\. Dzhangaziev

The rapid digital transformation of the hospitality industry has increased the importance of software\-based automation in food and beverage \(F&amp;B\) operations\. Restaurants, cafés, catering companies, hotels, and other food\-service businesses increasingly rely on integrated digital systems to manage ordering, inventory, kitchen operations, procurement, workforce scheduling, customer relationships, payments, and managerial analytics\. This study examines the role of software solutions in automating F&amp;B processes and evaluates their potential contribution to operational efficiency, cost control, service quality, and data\-driven decision\-making\. The research applies a qualitative analytical approach based on a structured review and synthesis of contemporary studies concerning restaurant technologies, self\-service systems, artificial intelligence, digital inventory management, demand forecasting, and service automation\. The analysis identifies five major areas of F&amp;B automation: order and payment management, kitchen operations, inventory and procurement, workforce management, and business intelligence\. The findings indicate that the greatest value is generated when individual digital applications are integrated into a unified information environment in which operational data are automatically exchanged between point\-of\-sale systems, kitchen displays, inventory modules, customer interfaces, and analytical platforms\. At the same time, technological fragmentation, implementation costs, employee resistance, cybersecurity concerns, data quality, and dependence on reliable digital infrastructure remain significant barriers\. The study proposes an integrated model of F&amp;B process automation and argues that software automation should be considered not simply as a mechanism for replacing manual tasks but as an organizational capability supporting scalability, operational transparency, resource optimization, and improved customer experience\.

## [Python&\#x27;s Indispensability in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: A Review](../publications/705d1c0348024d5c8e58.md)

 Toyosi Mercy Fatoba

This review paper explores the vital role played by the programming language Python in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Machine Learning \(ML\)\. It will discuss the origin of AI and ML, the first programming language used for it, and its bottlenecks will be made known\. There will also be an exposition on the emergence of Python, its elements, and the comparison between Python and LISP\. The adoption and integration of Python into AI and ML will be considered, and the advanced components of Python and their uses in AI and ML will also be discussed\. The trajectory of AI and ML with Python and the game\-changing benefits of using Python in AI and ML will be assessed\. Suggestions will be given on what should be improved in Python to improve AI and ML\.

## [A Stability\-aware Computational Intelligence Framework for Risk\-guided Corrective Decision Support in Execution\-stage Routing Systems](../publications/70692d55a4530f5331aa.md)

Ayub Prasetyo; Sarifuddin Madenda; Ernastuti; Murni

Route disruptions require corrective decisions that respect what has already been served\.This study develops a stability\-aware framework that locks the executed route prefix and re\-sequences only the remaining suffix, combining quantile travel\-time risk, an adaptive metaheuristic search, and a route\-stability term with an admissible unchanged\-route option\.Sixty\-three daily instances were split into calibration and held\-out subsets, the latter used only for evaluation\.Daily\-instance statistical analysis confirmed significant differences among the compared methods\.The proposed method significantly reduced lateness relative to no re\-planning while accepting higher lateness than free and risk\-guided re\-sequencing in exchange for greater route stability and fewer route changes\.An adapted external adaptive\-large\-neighborhood\-search comparator achieved lower lateness but with more than twice as many moved stops and lower route stability, and higher computational cost\.A complementary fuzzy decision\-activation gate, calibrated only on the calibration subset, retained most of the always\-SA lateness\-reduction benefit as a post\-review robustness check\.

## [Media Affordances as Dialogue Rules: A Corpus\-Driven Analysis of Ethos\-Centered Argumentation in TV Debates and Social Media](../publications/706b72c287af31e951b7.md)

Ewelina Gajewska

Abstract This article investigates how the structural affordances of communication media alter the interactional pragmatics of political argumentation\. Through a diachronic, mixed\-methods analysis of the 2016 and 2024 U\.S\. presidential campaigns, we compare synchronous broadcast television debates with asynchronous social media \(Twitter/X\) discourse\. Combining manual annotation of argumentative moves with automated sentiment and incivility scoring, we demonstrate that platform architectures rewrite the rules of political argumentation\. In TV debates, institutional constraints incentivize self\-referential supports of ethos \(face enhancing acts\) and pragmatic mitigation of uncivil language\. Conversely, Twitter’s algorithmic affordances like quote\-tweeting incentivize aggressive attacks on opponents’ ethos \(face threatening acts\) and digital impoliteness\. Furthermore, we observe a difference in how speakers build ethotic arguments: TV demands contrastive ethos positioning, whereas social media primarily facilitates lay testimony\. Ultimately, this study provides evidence that media affordances are associated not only with differences in rhetorical style but also with variation in the interactional objectives manifested in political discourse\.

## [Public technical disclosure of AI implementation in finance: Python\-framed evidence from 253 NYSE\-listed financial companies](../publications/706f5e03eff296a1d838.md)

Veliota Drakopoulou

Abstract Artificial intelligence \(AI\) claims in public markets increasingly raise disclosure, comparability, and investor\-protection questions, yet evidence on how listed financial firms publicly describe implementation remains fragmented and difficult to compare\. This study examines public technical disclosure rather than internal adoption by constructing a screened, exchange\-bounded corpus for 253 NYSE\-listed financial companies\. The source intake contained 554 rows; six exact repeated rows were removed before screening, leaving 548 screened rows\. The 505\-sentence extended analysis corpus combines a 253\-sentence firm\-anchor layer with a 252\-sentence direct\-verification layer; the remaining issuer is retained in the direct\-verification audit as a closed unit with no strict direct match\. Firms are coded into three disclosure states: explicit Python, indirect AI, and none, and the corpus is used to map subsector profiles, channel location, and the rarity of quantified public outcome claims through an outcome claims index \(OCI\)\. The results show that 34 firms \(13\.4%\) are classified as Explicit Python, 216 \(85\.4%\) as Indirect AI, and 3 \(1\.2%\) as None\. Explicit Python naming is uneven across subsectors and is concentrated mainly in employment materials and technical documentation rather than in filings or investor\-facing channels\. The public technical surface is therefore real but thin: firms more often signal implementation orientation than disclose a detailed tool stack\. Quantified public outcome claims are rarer still, with five OCI\-positive firms and five OCI\-positive sentences \(1\.98% of firms\)\. These findings indicate that public financial\-sector communication is much stronger on AI\-related implementation signals than on measurable outcomes\. The paper offers a reproducible disclosure map for a bounded listed firm population and a framework for distinguishing general AI language, implementation\-specific technical naming, and quantified public claims in regulated capital market settings\.

## [Generative AI and Literary Ambiguity: A Prompt\-Based Study of Henry James’s The Turn of the Screw](../publications/7078523a077c1b801146.md)

Meena A\. Mosa; Ghada Kamil Mustafa; \. Ali Adel Hashem

This exploratory paper investigates the influence of prompt framing on AI\-generated analyses of literary ambiguity in Henry James’s The Turn of the Screw\. It examines nine responses across three chosen episodes and under the conditions of open\-ended, supernatural, and psychological/narratological prompts\. The study is guided by Wolfgang Iser’s reader\-response theory to contemplate textual accuracy, competing interpretations, uncertainty and explanation versus evidence\. These responses generally adjust to the perspective requested but once in a while mistakenly credit a fundamental statement in a final scene\. The case study demonstrates the interpretive advantage of generative AI as well as its need for textual verification, whilst acknowledging its limited data set

## [Enhancing Liver Cirrhosis Diagnosis Using Machine Learning With Explainable AI and Cross\-Validated Hyperparameter Tuning Techniques](../publications/708522523945cd842b7a.md)

Dhande Sujal Prashant, Prof\. P B Chandane,  Dr\. H\. B\. Jadhav

Cirrhosis is a form of Chronic Liver Disease \(CLD\) resulting from sustained liver damage from several causes, including viral infection, autoimmune disorders, cholestatic and metabolic disease Non\-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease \(NAFLD\) or heavy alcohol use\. Testing for the presence of Liver Cirrhosis \(LC\) is one of the most critical diagnostics and prognostic assessments for patients\. Detecting liver illness in its early stages is challenging as initial symptoms are often mild and difficult to diagnose\. Cirrhosis may not present symptoms until an advanced stage, posing a challenge for identification and diagnosis\. The lack of explanations for a complex model’s decision\-making process creates clinician distrust by concealing the reasoning behind its choices\. This research sought to design and assess a novel and non\-invasive proposed model by utilizing the XGBoost classifier with Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) for diagnosing liver cirrhosis\. In this work XAI framework enhances transparency in complex models, offering valuable insights into decision\-making, thereby guiding treatment strategies, and improving cirrhosis diagnosis\. The experimental results have shown superiority for the proposed method compared with various machine learning models\. The proposed method has achieved significantly 91\.19% using XGBoost for cirrhosis dataset with K\-fold validation\(K=10\) approach\.

## [HEALTHCARE AI](../publications/70898e85a02638cfcc6d.md)

Tanuja Sakhare

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly being explored in healthcare to support access to information, patient engagement, administrativeefficiency, and selected clinical workflows\. This paper proposes a Healthcare AI framework that organizes healthcare\-related requests andprovides structured, understandable information through a digital interface\. The framework combines a user interface, request classification,retrieval from approved healthcare information sources, privacy and safety checks, and a response\-generation layer\. It can support generalhealth education, service navigation, and appointment\-related guidance where authorized services are available\.
