## [When civic duty feels personal: psychological ownership as a pathway to prosocial behavior](../publications/708cf781fd2dc0c5d44b.md)

Rini Rahmawati; Asrid Juniar; Meiske Claudia; Muhamad Rusmin Nuryadin; Megi Nediawan; Liko Noor Rafianto Rahadhian; Muhammad Rayyan Adhiyani; Vina Tampi

Tax compliance is increasingly understood as a form of prosocial behavior shaped by internal moral orientations and individuals’ psychological attachment to public institutions rather than solely by external enforcement mechanisms\. This study examines how civic moral obligation influences prosocial behavior through psychological ownership while considering the moderating role of institutional trust\. A quantitative survey design was employed, and data were collected from 180 individual taxpayers in Tapin Regency, South Kalimantan, Indonesia\. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The results indicate that civic moral obligation positively affects both psychological ownership and prosocial behavior, suggesting that individuals who internalize tax compliance as a moral responsibility are more likely to develop a sense of ownership toward public institutions and engage in prosocial behavior\. Psychological ownership also significantly enhances prosocial behavior and partially mediates the relationship between civic moral obligation and prosocial behavior, highlighting its role as an important mechanism through which moral values are translated into action\. Furthermore, institutional trust strengthens the positive relationship between psychological ownership and prosocial behavior, indicating that higher levels of trust amplify the behavioral consequences of psychological attachment to public institutions\. These findings emphasize the importance of integrating moral, psychological, and institutional factors in promoting sustainable voluntary tax compliance\.

## [Enhancing Student Learning in Online STEM Labs Through Live Support: The Lab Assist Project](../publications/7099c65a5b50a1144218.md)

Dhouha Kbaier Ben Ismail; Annemarie Kane; Karen Kear

Remote access to laboratory equipment enables distance\-learning STEM students to engage with authentic experimental activities, but some students experience barriers when using remote laboratories\. This paper reports an exploratory mixed\-methods study undertaken within the two\-year Lab\-Assist Project, which examined students’ and tutors’ perceptions of real\-time or near\-real\-time support in remote STEM laboratory activities\. Data were collected through stakeholder consultations with 13 Module Chairs, surveys of 41 students and 8 tutors, and a pilot of live\-supported sessions involving two of the participating tutors within The Open University’s OpenSTEM Labs in the UK\. Quantitative responses were analysed descriptively and qualitative responses thematically\. Findings indicate that students valued timely and tailored support, particularly when experiencing difficulties with equipment, experimental procedures, or uncertainty about their performance\. Tutor feedback highlighted challenges associated with fragmented information, preparation, and interpreting experimental tasks, providing a basis for considering the potential role of timely support in managing extraneous cognitive load\. However, the study did not directly measure cognitive load or learning outcomes, and low pilot attendance and small voluntary survey samples limit the strength and generalisability of the evidence\. Participants also expressed mixed views on automated support, suggesting that AI\-based assistance may be appropriate for routine queries but should complement rather than replace human support\. The study contributes design\-oriented insights for developing responsive, accessible, and inclusive support models for remote STEM laboratories\.

## [New requirements for medical device safety monitoring: key challenges for healthcare organizations\.](../publications/709c3724237df88a654c.md)

D\. V\. Piven; Igor V\. Ivanov; E\. A\. Trofimova

Relevance\. Medical device safety monitoring is one of the consistently and strictly controlled mandatory requirements imposed on healthcare organizations\. Objective: to analyze the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring and the new Procedure for reporting adverse events in the field of medical device circulation with a view to identifying the new tasks now facing healthcare organizations\. Results\. It is noted that the new orders of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation have significantly clarified and detailed the requirements for information, the collection, processing, and recording of which are carried out during medical device safety monitoring\. This includes, inter alia, data transmitted by software employing artificial intelligence technologies that constitutes a medical device; information on adverse events in the field of medical device circulation in other states; and information contained in an adverse event report\. Attention is drawn to the increased significance of the Classification of adverse events related to the circulation of medical devices\. Conclusion\. Healthcare organizations should pay special attention to the fact that the identification of adverse events in the field of medical device circulation must now be carried out in strict accordance with the Classification of adverse events approved by Order No\. 4513 of the Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare \(Roszdravnadzor\) dated May 20, 2021\. In accordance with the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring, each healthcare organization is required to appoint an official responsible for organizing the work of collecting information in order to ensure the safe use of medical devices and to establish the procedure for this work\.

## [Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction\-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents](../publications/709f1a306ed58e4d6a63.md)

BHVSP Subrahmanyam; Neeraj Choudhary

LLM\-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence\. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence\. We study per\-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full\-memory behavior\. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural\-language decisions, and exact sufficient\-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost\-ordered group\-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records\. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost\-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum\-cost sufficient set in 100\.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30\.00 to 11\.13 \(62\.9%\), and achieves 87\.8% active\-memory savings\. Across four 12B\-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10\.28 versus 16\.00 model queries and 50\.6% versus 43\.1% minimum\-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion\. Both methods preserve full\-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface\. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior\. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment\-ready memory compression\.

## [The Impact of Game Design and Monetisation Strategies on Player Engagement in Online Games](../publications/70a34a7efc9c3afa64ee.md)

Venkateswararao Podile; K Mahalakshmi; Guduri Nagaveni

Free\-to\-play titles cost nothing to install, so whatever a developer earns arrives after the download, and only if players stay long enough for some of them to start paying\. The present study asks two linked questions\. How strongly are game design and monetisation strategies related to how engaged players say they are, and do those relationships look different for experienced and inexperienced players? A structured questionnaire was completed online by 240 adult gamers\. Three five\-item Likert scales captured engagement, game design and monetisation, and all three proved reliable \(Cronbach&\#x27;s alpha 0\.866 to 0\.878\)\. The hypotheses were tested with multiple linear regression, chi\-square tests and one\-way ANOVA\. Game design was the stronger of the two predictors of engagement \(β = 0\.48, p &lt; 0\.001\), although monetisation also contributed \(β = 0\.26, p &lt; 0\.001\), and the two together explained just over a third of the spread in engagement scores \(R² = 0\.363\)\. More experienced respondents reported greater engagement \(F = 6\.40, p &lt; 0\.001\) and were likelier to have bought something inside a game \(χ² = 12\.54, p = 0\.006\)\. Experience, on the other hand, left both relationships unchanged in strength\. The results point to the quality of play, and not pressure to purchase, as the surer route to engagement, and suggest that monetisation helps only when players regard it as fair\.

## [Functional versus mechanical alignment in robot\-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a prospective randomized single\-center trial](../publications/70a99b779a35b0ff48df.md)

Georgii Alexandrovich Airapetov; А\. П\. Призов; Armen A\. Daniliyants; Расул Николаевич Алиев; Abdoulaye A\. Akhmat; Varvara Iatsukova

Background\. Despite substantial advances in total knee arthroplasty \(TKA\), a considerable proportion of patients remain dissatisfied with surgical outcomes\. One possible explanation is the discrepancy between restored joint biomechanics and the patient’s native anatomy\. Functional alignment has recently emerged as a promising personalized alignment strategy facilitated by robotic\-assisted technologies\. The aim of the study\. To compare the early clinical, functional, and radiographic outcomes of robotic\-assisted total knee arthroplasty performed using functional alignment versus mechanical alignment\. Methods\. A prospective randomized single\-center study was conducted including 103 patients with Kellgren–Lawrence grade III–IV knee osteoarthritis\. Patients were allocated to robotic\-assisted functional alignment \(n=52\) or robotic\-assisted mechanical alignment \(n=51\)\. All procedures were performed using the CORI Surgical System and Anthem Total Knee System\. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee Society Score \(KSS\), Forgotten Joint Score\-12 \(FJS\-12\), and Visual Analogue Scale \(VAS\)\. Soft\-tissue release requirements and radiographic parameters including HKA, LDFA, and MPTA were also evaluated\. Results\. At 3 months postoperatively, the functional alignment group demonstrated significantly higher KSS Knee, KSS Function, and FJS\-12 scores, as well as lower VAS pain scores compared with the mechanical alignment group \(p0\.05\)\. Functional alignment was associated with a reduced need for additional soft\-tissue releases and a lower mean number of released structures per knee\. Both groups demonstrated excellent accuracy of surgical plan execution with comparable deviations from planned alignment parameters\. By 12 months, clinical outcomes became comparable between groups\. Discussion\. The findings suggest that functional alignment may facilitate faster early recovery by preserving native soft\-tissue balance and constitutional anatomy\. However, the magnitude of intergroup differences decreased over time, indicating convergence of outcomes during later stages of recovery\. Conclusion\. Robotic\-assisted functional alignment is a safe and reproducible TKA strategy associated with improved early functional outcomes and reduced soft\-tissue release requirements compared with mechanical alignment\. Further multicenter studies with longer follow\-up are required to determine its long\-term advantages\.

## [A Causal\-Comparative Study of Self\-Efficacy in Certificate and Degree Programs at the Community College Level Upon Graduation](../publications/70cac8c8903864e5d8fe.md)

Stephen Wakefield Phelps

This quantitative causal\-comparative study investigated whether student\-perceived occupational self\-efficacy differs between graduates of community college certificate programs and those completing Associate of Applied Science \(AAS\) degrees\. The research also addresses a gap in the literature regarding how award type influences occupational self\-efficacy among students in automotive, diesel, manufacturing, and welding programs\. The study employed a causal\-comparative research design, examining the relationship between the categorical independent variable of award type \(certificate or AAS degree\) and the quantitative dependent variable of occupational self\-efficacy\. Participants \(N=209\) were students in their graduating term from community colleges in a Northwestern state who were completing one of the target programs\. Data was collected using the Occupational Self\-Efficacy Scale \(OSES\)\. Descriptive statistics summarize demographic and study variables, including means, standard deviations, frequencies, and percentages\. A two\-way ANOVA tested for statistically significant differences and found no significant interaction or main effects between the award types or the disciplines on occupational self\-efficacy\. The findings of this study expand the literature on occupational self\-efficacy at the community college level with technical graduates and offer insights that can support program development and leadership decision\-making\. This research serves as a foundation for future studies exploring the nuances of student self\-efficacy post\-graduation\. Future research should assess data through longitudinal study methodology and incorporate a mixed\-method approach among a different population compared with a different instrument\.

## [Effect of Low\-Impact Aerobic Exercise on Blood Pressure Among Older Hypertensive Adults](../publications/70d3e472852525701f03.md)

Eka Febby Andrea; Widiharti Widiharti; Diah Fauzia Zuhroh; Ervi Suminar

Introduction: Hypertension is known as a silent killer because it is often a cause of sudden death\. Furthermore, many people today consume unhealthy, high\-fat foods while lacking exercise\. This accumulation of food leads to high cholesterol, which can trigger hypertension\. To prevent and treat hypertension, exercise can be done by increasing physical activity and low\-impact aerobic exercise to see if low\-impact aerobic exercise has an effect on lowering blood pressure\. Methods: This study uses a pre\-experimental design research design\. This type of research is quantitative research\. Using a one group pretest posttest approach\. The researcher measured the respondents&\#x27; blood pressure using a digital blood pressure monitor before and after low\-impact aerobic exercise\. The researcher recorded the results on an observation sheet\. The respondents then performed low\-impact aerobic exercise for 20 minutes\. Low\-impact aerobic exercise was performed three times a week for two weeks\. Results: The results of the Paired Sample T\-Test obtained a p\-value of 0\.000 &lt;α \(0\.05\), indicating that systolic blood pressure decreased by 6\.27 mmHg with a std\. Deviation of 10,074, while diastolic blood pressure decreased by 8\.8 mmHg with a std\. Deviation of 6,997\. Conclusions: There is an effect of low\-impact aerobic exercise on reducing blood pressure in hypertension sufferers at the Sukomulyo Gresik Health Center\. It is necessary to hold low\-impact aerobic exercise for hypertension sufferers in the Prolanis activities which are routinely carried out every week at the Sukomulyo Gresik Health Center\.

## [Microglial dynamics associate with the spatial pattern of tau deposition in early Alzheimer’s disease](../publications/70d843c0681aafbacb4e.md)

Marco Öchsner; Matthias Brendel; Nicolai Franzmeier; Lena Trappmann; Mirlind Zaganjori; Ersin Ersoezlue; Carolin Kurz; Jan Haeckert; Julia Utecht; Philine Marie Schirge; Boris Papazov; Oliver Pogarell; Daniel Janowitz; Katharina Büerger; Michael Ewers; Carla Palleis; Endy Weidinger; Gloria Biechele; Sebastian Schuster; Anika Finze; Florian Eckenweber; Rainer Rupprecht; Axel Rominger; Oliver Goldhardt; Timo Grimmer; Daniel Keeser; Sophia Stoecklein; Olaf Dietrich; Peter Bartenstein; Johannes Levin; Günter Höglinger; Robert Perneczky; Boris‐Stephan Rauchmann

BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation is implicated in Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) pathogenesis, yet how changes in TSPO PET signal are associated with tau deposition, and how brain network architecture shapes this relationship remain poorly understood\. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multimodal neuroimaging study in 56 participants: 35 amyloid\-positive individuals across the AD spectrum \(ADS\) and 21 amyloid\-negative healthy controls \(HC\)\. Amyloid status was classified primarily by CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 and, when eligible CSF was unavailable, by baseline amyloid PET\. Participants underwent TSPO PET using \[18 F\]GE\-180 and resting\-state fMRI at baseline\. A longitudinal subgroup additionally underwent follow\-up tau PET using \[18 F\]PI\-2620 \(n = 24\) and repeat TSPO PET \(n = 18\) approximately 18 months later\. RESULTS: Baseline TSPO did not differ significantly between groups\. Baseline TSPO was associated with regional tau in both groups; the reciprocal association between tau and TSPO change was numerically weaker in AD, but this group difference was not statistically significant\. Connectivity to baseline\-TSPO epicenters was associated with higher tau in both groups, whereas connectivity to TSPO\-change epicenters was associated with lower tau in AD but not controls \(group\-by\-connectivity interaction p &lt; 0\.001, participant\-level slope difference p = 0\.012\), a dissociation replicated in independent participants\. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that connectivity to established versus emerging TSPO epicenters carries distinct spatial information about tau in the AD spectrum, a pattern shaped by functional brain connectivity and absent in healthy controls\. \(ClinicalTrials\.gov: NCT06224920\)\.

## [Overdimension Vehicle Violation Detection and Monitoring System with Multi\-camera Sensors Using Deep Learning](../publications/70da2483f5f5c1aa83eb.md)

Arief Rianto Kurniawan; Diah Puspito Wulandari; Rudzidatul Akmam Dziyauddin; Javier Janeti Suprantiyo; Eko Mulyanto Yuniarno

Overdimension vehicles, defined as vehicles exceeding legally permitted dimensional limits, remain a challenge in traffic enforcement due to limited automated monitoring\.This study proposes an edge\-based multi\-camera system integrating YOLOv8n\-seg, DeepSORT, and SIFT\-based cross\-camera association\.The selected model achieved an mIoU of 0\.66, a Dice coefficient of 0\.75, and 14\.87 FPS\.On 800 held\-out cross\-camera pairs, SIFT achieved 0\.863 accuracy and a 0\.856 F1\-score, compared with 0\.861 accuracy and a 0\.869 F1\-score for a recent ReIDbased baseline\.In 57 labeled trajectories, overdimension classification achieved 91\.23% accuracy and a 73\.68%F1score\.Ablation on 35 vehicles increased coverage from 94\.29%/88\.57%for the single cameras to 100% and consolidated 64 local trajectories into 35 unique records\.For seven physically measured overdimension vehicles, height estimation achieved an MAE of 0\.061 m, RMSE of 0\.071 m, and MAPE of 2\.46%\.A web\-based platform supports monitoring and violation management\.

## [Makna dan Implementasi Kurikulum Merdeka Belajar Serta Relevansinya Bagi Perkembangan Siswa di Sekolah Dasar](../publications/70da7f2447bbe4ce32b1.md)

Yanri Sarlince Tahun; Maria Indriani Sesfao; Welmince Tefa

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendalami makna serta implementasi dari perubahan kurikulum merdeka belajar serta relevansinya dengan dengan perkembangan siswa khusunya di Sekolah Dasar di dasarkan atas telaah kritis dalam tinjauan pedagogis\. Kurikulum Merdeka belajar merupakan sebuah gagasan yang di implementasikan dalam sebuah kebijakan yang di keluarkan oleh pemerintah dengan memberikan kebebasan kepada para guru dan siswa dalam menentukan sistem pembelajaran dengan tujuan Mengembangkan Sumber Daya Manusia \(SDM\) yang unggul melalui pendidikan yang menyenangkan bagi siswa dan guru dengan mengedepankan pada aspek pengembangan karakter yang sesuai dengan nilai\-nilai Budaya Bangsa Indonesia\. Latar belakang dari studi ini adalah menganalisis makna dan implementasi tentang kurikulum merdeka belajar serta relevansinya dengan perkembangan siswa di Sekolah Dasar\. Metode Penelitian yang di gunakan adalah studi pustaka dengan tahapan 1\) memilih sumber materi dari jurnal; 2\)menelusuri rujukan pustaka; 3\) membaca rujukan pustaka; 4\)menuliskan catatan\-catatan; dan 5\) menyajikan hasil kajian jurnal\. Berdasarkan kajian jurnal maka dapat disimpulkan bahwa perubahan kurikulum merdeka di latar belakangi oleh rendahnya tingkat kompetensi siswa, kesenjangan dalam kualitas pembelajaran dan Perkembangan dunia pendidikan yang semakin pesat khususnya di bidang tekhnologi yang mengharuskan siwa beradaptasi dengan cepat, dan kurikulum merdeka hadir sebagai solusi untuk meningkatkan pembelajaran, sesuai dengan makna dari kurikulum merdeka yaitu merdeka berpikir, merdeka berinovasi, belajar mandiri dan merdeka untuk kebahagiaan dan dalam implementasinya kurikulum ini sangat relevan dengan perkembangan siswa saat ini\.

## [Egypt&\#x27;s Comprehensive Development Vision — Part III: A Strategic Framework for National Transformation, Institutional Development, Human Capital, and Technological Innovation](../publications/70dc18d69d255febcb6c.md)

Detective ElShazly; Ahmed Saher

Abstract and Research Description This research is the third installment of Egypt’s Comprehensive Development Vision, a broader initiative exploring strategic approaches to Egypt’s long\-term development and national transformation\. The study presents a comprehensive conceptual framework for developing state institutions, strengthening strategic planning, improving public administration, advancing education and human capital, promoting technological innovation and artificial intelligence, and enhancing accountability and institutional effectiveness\. It explores the metaphor of the state as a living organism, examining the interconnected roles of national leadership, citizens, intelligence and strategic analysis, defense institutions, legislative bodies, public oversight, and essential infrastructure\. The research also proposes approaches to urban and regional development, the modernization of Egyptian cities and villages, the development of religious and educational institutions, the intellectual advancement of society, the growth of domestic technology and digital platforms, and the sustainable use of national resources, including the Nile River and its islands\. In addition to presenting strategic proposals, the study explores practical implementation mechanisms, institutional coordination, performance measurement, innovation initiatives, and long\-term planning\. Its objective is to develop an integrated vision that connects human development, institutional reform, scientific progress, technological capability, economic advancement, cultural identity, and national sustainability\. This document is published in both English and Arabic\. The complete English version appears first, followed by the complete original Arabic version, making the research accessible to international readers as well as Arabic\-speaking audiences\. This work forms part of an ongoing conceptual research series dedicated to exploring ideas and proposals for Egypt’s future development\. The proposals are intended to encourage strategic thinking, constructive discussion, and the development of practical solutions suited to Egypt’s national priorities and circumstances\.

## [Reciprocal modulation between beef protein and wine phenolics during in vitro co\-digestion: a proposed ternary complex\-mediated mechanism modulated by cooking technique](../publications/70e029571dad76f4c2cd.md)

Ziruo Sun; Shaoyun Xing; Wei Tang; Taihong Liu; Kaiyue Liu; Du Chao; Shuyang Sun; Wenguang Jiang

Background Beef and red wine form a classic dietary combination, yet how their components reciprocally influence each other during digestion remains unclear\. Methods This study co\-digested steamed, boiled and grilled beef with red wine using the INFOGEST 2\.0 in vitro digestion model, combined with molecular docking, to investigate bidirectional modulation between beef proteins and wine phenolics\. Results Wine co\-digestion suppressed gastric carbonyl formation by 21\.5%−30\.8% and preserved free sulfhydryl groups by 27\.7%−50\.5% across cooking methods\. Two\-way analysis of variance indicated significant cooking × wine interactions for protein oxidation and amino acid release\. The largest improvement occurred in grilled beef, whose gastric digestibility and intestinal amino acid content increased by 20\.9% and 67\.2%, respectively\. Docking simulations predicted that selected phenolics bound to myosin heavy chain and pepsin through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, supporting a proposed phenolics\-pepsin\-myosin ternary complex that may strengthen enzyme\-substrate association\. Reciprocally, the beef matrix enhanced ABTS antioxidant activity by 24\.9% \(gastric\) and 125\.3% \(intestinal\) relative to wine alone, and was associated with selective phenolic regulation: gastric gallic acid increased by up to 135\.7%, whereas intestinal epicatechin and resveratrol rose up to 3\.5\- and 11\.6\-fold, respectively\. Conclusion These findings support the proposed ternary complex as a plausible molecular hub governing protein–phenolic reciprocity, providing a proposed mechanistic basis for optimizing cooking methods and meat–wine pairing strategies in mixed meals\.

## [Age\-Reversal](../publications/70e4fa66eec1cc1ef8da.md)

William Faloon

This perspective discusses emerging regenerative interventions that target biological aging\. Over recent decades, scientific advances have expanded understanding of aging as a potentially modifiable biological process\. Technologies under investigation include partial cellular reprogramming, senescent cell clearance, artificial\-intelligence\-driven drug discovery, organ regeneration, and modulation of epigenetic aging clocks\. Preclinical studies indicate that aged cells may regain more youthful functional characteristics under specific experimental conditions\. For example, inhibition of interleukin\-11 signaling initiated in late life extended median lifespan by approximately 20–25% in mice and partial reprogramming has improved tissue function and survival in aged mouse model\. Developments in DNA\-methylation\-based biomarkers now permit estimation of biological age, allowing more efficient assessment of candidate interventions\. All reprogramming data to date are preclinical, and human senolytic and IL\-11 data are early\-phase\. Although many findings remain experimental or early translational, they represent a convergence of approaches that may influence future biomedical research\. This paper summarizes selected topics related to biological age modulation and highlights ongoing areas of investigation\.

## [Cross\-lingual phoneme\-aware audio synthesis framework for low\-resource Yoruba word generation](../publications/70ef726d28f71a5af811.md)

Julius Olaniyan; Deborah Olaniyan; Ibidun Christiana Obagbuwa

The scarcity of annotated data and unique linguistic challenges have made low\-resource African languages largely bypassed in the development of high\-fidelity TTS systems\. This paper presents a novel cross\-lingual, phoneme\-aware audio synthesis framework for the Yorùbá language, a tonal and morphologically rich West African language with limited computational resources\. Our approach leverages a transfer learning paradigm where an English\-trained FastSpeech 2 model is adapted using a custom Yorùbá phoneme\-to\-tone transcription pipeline, combined with tonal embeddings and speaker conditioning\. A high\-quality but limited dataset consisting of 6 h of annotated Yorùbá speech from 12 native speakers was used to fine\-tune the system\. Extensive evaluations, including mel cepstral distortion, tone classification accuracy, and Mean Opinion Score \(MOS\) native speaker evaluations demonstrate that the system can synthesize intelligible and tonally accurate Yorùbá speech despite limited data\. Attention\-based alignment visualizations and SHAP interpretability analyses also confirm that the model captures the phoneme\-tone dependencies which are critical for the language intelligibility\. This work makes an important contribution to the field of low\-resource speech synthesis, with wide implications for linguistic preservation, accessibility, and inclusive AI for underrepresented languages\.

## [Current applications of artificial intelligence for advancing agriculture, sustainability and climate mitigation](../publications/70f3cee95c9a3b1af879.md)

Mostafa Farajpour

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping agriculture by enabling data\-driven decision\-making across crop production systems and supporting the transition toward more sustainable, resilient, and climate\-smart farming\. This review critically synthesizes advances in AI applications spanning precision irrigation, nutrient and soil management, yield prediction, pest and disease monitoring, computer vision, autonomous agricultural robotics, and large language model \(LLM\)\-based decision support systems\. Beyond summarizing technological developments, the review evaluates their practical deployment, emphasizing that successful agricultural AI depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on model generalizability, explainability, economic feasibility, interoperability, and integration with existing agronomic knowledge\. Emerging technologies including Vision Transformers, foundation models, Digital Twins, multimodal AI, Retrieval\-Augmented Generation, and federated and continual learning—are discussed as important directions for overcoming limitations related to data scarcity, environmental variability, and scalable field implementation\. The review highlights that responsible AI adoption requires transparent governance frameworks addressing data ownership, privacy, algorithmic fairness, cybersecurity, and equitable access, particularly for smallholder farming systems\. Although numerous AI models report outstanding performance, widespread agricultural adoption remains constrained by cross\-region validation, fragmented datasets, infrastructure requirements, and insufficient real\-world deployment\. Future progress will depend on multidisciplinary collaboration integrating advances in artificial intelligence, sensing technologies, robotics, crop science, and agricultural engineering to develop robust, trustworthy, and farmer\-centered decision\-support systems\. By critically evaluating technological innovations and implementation challenges, this review provides a framework for understanding the current state of AI in agriculture while identifying research priorities that will shape the next generation of sustainable and climate\-resilient agricultural systems\.

## [Recent advances in electrospun hydrogen\-rich polymeric nanofiber composites for space radiation shielding](../publications/70f611c7745a621a2fec.md)

Alka; Siddhi Srivastava; Priyanka Prajapati; Archana Bharti Sonkar

As human space exploration extends beyond Low Earth Orbit toward sustained lunar and future Mars missions, lightweight and multifunctional radiation\-shielding materials are increasingly required to mitigate the complex Galactic Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Event \(SPE\) environment\. Hydrogen\-rich polymers offer advantages over conventional high\-Z metallic shields because of their low density and reduced production of high\-energy secondary radiation\. This review critically evaluates recent advances \(2020–2026\) in electrospun hydrogen\-rich polymeric nanofiber composites for space radiation shielding, with emphasis on the relationships among polymer chemistry, nanofiber architecture, functional fillers, and shielding performance\. Particular attention is given to polyethylene\-based systems, boron\-containing fillers, hierarchical architectures, and the influence of processing and interfacial characteristics on radiation attenuation and multifunctional performance\. Radiation\-transport modelling, including Monte Carlo approaches, together with molecular\-scale and computational materials\-design strategies, is examined as a route toward predictive optimization; however, limitations associated with heterogeneous datasets, model validation, and the lack of standardized mission\-relevant testing remain significant barriers\. The review further identifies critical challenges in electrospinning scalability, environmental durability, long\-duration radiation exposure, and translation from laboratory testing to aerospace implementation\. Overall, the available evidence indicates that shielding performance cannot be attributed to nanofiber morphology alone and must instead be evaluated through the combined effects of hydrogen content, areal density, architecture, filler distribution, and radiation type\. Future progress will require quantitatively validated structure\-property\-performance relationships, standardized testing protocols, scalable manufacturing, and integrated experimental\-computational approaches to enable reliable qualification of lightweight shielding systems for long\-duration space missions\.

## [RELAÇÃO ENTRE USO DE CANNABIS E ALTERAÇÕES CENTRAIS E ENDÓCRINAS: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA DE LITERATURA](../publications/70f61be891c3ea35e179.md)

Jordana Barbosa Guimarães Carvalho; Giulia Vicente Carneiro da Paixão; Sophia Artiaga Gomes; Andressa Adorno e Albuquerque; João Eduardo Gervásio Pereira; Ana Clara Ferreira Segato; Yasmim Vicente da Paixão; Isabella Vicente da Paixão; Luiza Stábile de Oliveira; Ronair Rosa Dias Filho; Jaidan Rezende Dos Santos Lopes; Ana Julia Mota Clemente; João Cássio Rebouças Saldanha Filho; JOÃO PEDRO DE GODOY PITALUGA; Paola Ochoa Michelon

Os compostos da Cannabis atuam através de receptores endógenos, CB1 e CB2, que estão distribuídos pelo corpo\. O CB1 está localizado principalmente no cérebro e tem um efeito inibitório sobre neurotransmissores como GABA e glutamato, mas seu principal efeito é a liberação da dopamina, gerando uma sensação de recompensa\. O CB2, por outro lado, está principalmente em órgãos periféricos com função imunológica\. O estresse pode interferir na saúde mental, afetando a cognição, aprendizagem, causando transtornos de ansiedade, obesidade e depressão\. Além disso, o estresse pode afetar a qualidade de vida, aumentando o absenteísmo no trabalho e impactando negativamente a produtividade econômica\. O estudo foi realizado como uma revisão narrativa da literatura, pesquisadas de agosto de 2022 a janeiro de 2023 com as seguintes palavras\-chave em inglês: Cannabis sp, THC, CBD, neuroendocrin pathways, stresse\. A busca resultou em 34 artigos, dos quais 6 foram selecionados, devido á maior relação com os objetivos do estudo\. Diante disso, há uma necessidade de desenvolver pesquisas para a compreensão dos mecanismos neuroendócrinos que possam esclarecer o caminho para novas abordagens terapêuticas no manejo do estresse e de condições relacionadas\.

## [أثر استخدام الحاسوب في التحصيل الدراسي لدى طلبة قسم الحاسوب بجامعة بنغازي دراسة ميدانية على عينة قوامها \(300\) طالب وطالبة](../publications/70f6473c7e957495cd19.md)

سعاد خليفه علي اغليلب

هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى الكشف عن أثر استخدام الحاسوب في التحصيل الدراسي لدى طلبة قسم الحاسوب بجامعة بنغازي، وذلك من خلال دراسة ميدانية على عينة عشوائية طبقية قوامها \(300\) طالب وطالبة، موزعين بالتساوي بين الذكور والإناث، وعلى أربعة مستويات دراسية\. واستخدمت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي \(المسحي\)، واعتمدت على استبانة إلكترونية مكونة من \(25\) فقرة موزعة على ثلاثة محاور: درجة استخدام الحاسوب، والتحصيل الدراسي، والمعوقات\. وقد أظهرت النتائج وجود علاقة ارتباطية موجبة متوسطة ذات دلالة إحصائية بين استخدام الحاسوب والتحصيل الدراسي \(r = 0\.47, p &lt; 0\.01\)، ووجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في التحصيل الدراسي تُعزى إلى المستوى الدراسي لصالح طلبة السنوات النهائية \(F = 5\.32, p &lt; 0\.01\)، في حين لم تظهر النتائج فروقاً ذات دلالة إحصائية تُعزى إلى متغير الجنس \(t = 1\.42, p = 0\.158\)\. كما كشفت الدراسة عن وجود معوقات مرتفعة تحدّ من الاستفادة المثلى من الحاسوب، أبرزها ضعف الإنترنت \(متوسط 4\.35 من 5\) وقلة الأجهزة في المختبرات \(متوسط 4\.12 من 5\)، وبلغ المتوسط العام للمعوقات \(3\.97 من 5\)، مما يشير إلى مستوى مرتفع من المعوقات\. وقد قدمت الدراسة مجموعة من التوصيات والمقترحات العملية\.

## [Artificial intelligence maturity in buyer–seller exchange](../publications/70fc4ea6d32b042d7ea8.md)

Molly R\. Burchett; Karen E\. Flaherty; Douglas E\. Hughes; Avinash Malshe; Ryan R\. Mullins

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is rapidly reshaping business\-to\-business \(B2B\) buying and selling, yet research has largely examined AI as a unilateral process enabler\. While this perspective has generated important insights regarding AI adoption and performance, it overlooks a fundamental characteristic of B2B selling: exchange outcomes depend on the compatibility of buyer–seller decision processes at the exchange interface\. To address this gap, the authors advance the concept of AI exchange maturity \(i\.e\. extent to which decision authority within buyer–seller exchange is delegated to AI systems\) and theorize its organizational antecedents\. Building on this construct, the authors develop a bilateral theory of buyer–seller AI exchange in which value co\-creation depends on the configuration of AI exchange maturity across exchange partners\. The framework identifies four configurations \(buyer AI\-maturity advantage, seller AI\-maturity advantage, agentic\-AI maturity alignment, and pre\-AI maturity alignment\) and theorizes how each configuration shapes value co\-creation through information\-processing fit and buyer–seller trust\. The authors further identify strategies for selling organizations to manage each configuration to enhance value co\-creation\. In doing so, the framework shifts the theoretical focus from whether individual firms adopt AI to the distribution of decision authority between humans and AI systems across exchange partners\.

## [Problemáticas actuales: un abordaje desde las neurociencias](../publications/710fc17d7bb6fdc96f76.md)

Catalina Quintero López; Víctor Daniel Gil Vera; Yenis Patricia Espinosa Espinosa; Jordan Amalin; Sara Ortiz Saldarriaga; Antonio Olivera\-La Rosa; Estefanny Acevedo Correa; Nathaly Vanegas Samper; Valentina Loaiza Valencia; Yenni Rivera Montoya; Sergio Gómez Saldarriaga; Paula Muñoz Marín; Omar Amador Sánchez; Luis Jorquera\-Zapata; Miguel Ángel Albor Licona; Juan Diego Betancur Arias; César Andrés Carmona\-Cardona; Camila Montoya\-Osorio; Dubis Marcela Rincón\-Barreto

La compilación Problemáticas actuales: un abordaje desde las neurociencias tiene como propósito presentar resultados de investigaciones cuyo objetivo estuvo relacionado con el papel que tienen las neurociencias en la comprensión y resolución de algunas problemáticas modernas, como, por ejemplo, el comportamiento suicida, la agresión, la violencia, el estrés postraumático y el conflicto armado\.Así mismo, se presentan avances y desafíos relacionados con la urgente necesidad de realizar precisiones conceptuales y metodológicas, que favorezcan el desarrollo de los diferentes campos de acción y también, que propendan por el uso cuidadoso del prefijo “neuro”, superando la superficialidad que se contrapone al rigor epistemológico y metodológico que implica su uso\.Esta obra es ideal para estudiantes, profesionales y personas interesadas en temas relacionados con los procesos de evaluación neuropsicológica, la neurociencia cognitiva y la salud mental\.

## [The impact of microbiota and interferons on the regulation of dendritic cells across age](../publications/7110487e7776adf98723.md)

Ramin Shakiba

Conventional dendritic cells \(cDC\) are key immune sentinels, orchestrating context specificimmune responses\. They exist as type 1 and type 2 cDC \(cDC1, cDC2\) with specialized roles in immunity\. Previous work in our lab identified differences in the capacity to support Th17 and Treg polarization between splenic cDC2 from neonatal and adult mice, which correlated with shifts in cytokine signaling across age\. However, it is unclear when cDC2 function transitions from a neonatal to an adult phenotype and how this process is regulated\. During the period spanning from birth to weaning the organism establishes life\-long immune homeostasis\. The transition to solid foods is accompanied by an exponential increase in intestinal microbial diversity\. Commensal derived signals also reach the spleen where they induce interferon \(IFN\) signaling, which promotes cDC function\. As we found functional differences of cDC2 in early life to disappear around weaning, we hypothesised that changes in microbial colonization at this age mediate this transition\. Longitudinal single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\) confirmed an enrichment of IFN stimulated genes \(ISG\) in cDC2 around weaning and quantitative real\-time PCR \(qRT\-PCR\) identified a corresponding increase of splenic IFNg expression with age\. However, functional analyses of cDC2 from germ\-free \(GF\) mice or mice with a DC\-specific loss of STAT1 \(CD11cCreStat1flox\) which mediates intracellular signaling downstream of IFN receptors found that neither IFN signaling nor microbial colonization are responsible for changes in support of Th17 polarization by cDC2 across age\. cDC1 are potent activators of CD8\+ T cells\. As with cDC2, longitudinal scRNA\-seq of splenic cDC1 revealed decreased ISG in 1\-week\-old mice, compared to mice at weaning age or older\. While microbial colonization did not appear to regulate cDC1 function, cDC\-specific loss of STAT1 \(Clec9aCreStat1flox\), but not type I IFN receptor, lead to reduced production of IL\-12p40 and CXCL9, which are cytokines driving CD8\+ T cell responses\. Concurrently, Clec9acreStat1flox mice exhibited a specific reduction of CD49dhi CD8\+ T cells with high cytotoxic capacity, which phenotypically resemble effector memory T cells\. scRNA\-seq revealed a loss of CXCL9\-expressing cDC1 with an activated phenotype in Clec9acreStat1flox mice compared to littermate controls\. In contrast, CCR7\+ cDC1 arising from homeostatic maturation were unaffected\. Cell\-cell interaction analysis confirmed impaired interaction between CXCL9 producing cDC1 and cytotoxic T cells via the CXCL9/CXCR3 axis\. Taken together our data indicate an increase of splenic IFNg signaling around weaning that induces a distinct activation state of cDC1 which drives the homeostasis of cytotoxic CD8\+ T cells\.

## [Predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two\-year\-old infants in Northern Uganda](../publications/7111a9fec06e22c04575.md)

David Mukunya; Grace Ndeezi; Gertrude Namazzi; Thorkild Tylleskär; Brendah Nambozo; Milton Wamboko Musaba; Beatrice Mpora Odongkara; Vincentina Achora; Justin Bruno Tongun; Josephine Tumuhamye; Agnes Kasede Napyo; Vicent Ssentumbwe; Victoria Nankabirwa; James Kashugyera Tumwine

BACKGROUND: Data on neurodevelopmental disabilities in sub\-Saharan Africa are scarce\. Identifying children at the highest risk of neurodevelopmental delay could enable health workers to target these groups more effectively, improve resource allocation and programmatic focus\. OBJECTIVE: To develop and assess a model for predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two\-year\-old infants in Northern Uganda using easily obtainable predictors\. METHODS: We studied children born to women enrolled in a cluster randomized controlled trial \(January 2018\-March 2019\) evaluating the effect of peer counseling on health facility births\. At the trial&\#x27;s final visit \(day 50\), 1,804 children were enrolled\. In November 2020, we followed up 1,421 children \(78\.8%\) and assessed their neurodevelopment at 2 years using the Malawi Developmental Assessment Tool\. We used least absolute shrinkage and selection operator penalized regression with 10\-fold cross\-validation to select the best subset of predictors and assessed model performance using the area under the curve \(AUC\)\. RESULTS: Of the 1,421 children, 70 \(4\.9%; 95% CI: 3\.6\-6\.7%\) had neurodevelopmental delays\. Of the 19 candidate predictors, six were retained in the final model \(lambda = 0\.0076\): moderate wasting, prolonged neonatal hospitalization \(up to 28 days\), maternal education, place of birth, preterm birth, and absence of skin\-to\-skin contact at birth\. The model showed strong discriminative power \(AUC 0\.75\) and reasonable calibration \(calibration slope 1\.37; calibration belt 0\.536\-0\.727\)\. CONCLUSION: We developed a promising tool for identifying infants at increased risk of neurodevelopmental delay in low\-resource settings, which could help prioritize children for follow\-up and specialized interventions\.

## [Peripheral and cerebrospinal fluid inflammatory markers in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis an exploratory cross\-sectional association study](../publications/711264dce4f95c37c3cf.md)

Agnieszka Wełnicka; Karolina Łuczkowska; Przemysław Nowacki; Edyta Paczkowska; Agnieszka Meller; Karolina Machowska\-Sempruch; Bogusław Machaliński; Monika Gołąb\-Janowska

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis \(ALS\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with an ambiguous etiology, whose onset may be linked to innate immune system activation outside the central nervous system \(CNS\)\. We investigated the association between peripheral blood and CNS inflammatory parameters in 45 sporadic ALS patients compared to 30 controls, analyzing peripheral blood tests \(C\-reactive protein \[CRP\], blood count, fibrinogen\) and cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) immunological measures \(Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha \[TNF\-α\], TNF receptor type 1 \[TNFR\-1\], CRP\) alongside clinical characteristics\. Results revealed significantly higher concentrations of TNFR\-1 in the CSF of ALS patients compared to the control group \(1,029\.5 ± 176\.0 vs\. 846\.1 ± 167\.5 pg/ml; p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. This difference remained significant in multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age and sex \(OR 1\.82 per 100 pg/ml increment, 95% CI 1\.26\-2\.63; p = 0\.0015\)\. In an exploratory ROC analysis, CSF TNFR\-1 discriminated patients from controls with an AUC of 0\.78 \(95% CI 0\.67\-0\.88\)\. TNFR\-1 correlated with age \(R = 0\.32, p = 0\.038\), associations with disease severity and a lower concentration in bulbar\-onset disease were exploratory and not robustly significant\. Plasma and CSF CRP concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, but strongly correlated with each other in both ALS \(R = 0\.83\) and control \(R = 0\.82\) cohorts, indicating a disease\-non\-specific relationship\. CSF TNFR\-1 is independently associated with sporadic ALS and warrants further investigation as a candidate disease\-associated inflammatory biomarker\. Given the limitations, our findings do not prove diagnostic accuracy or causality\. Longitudinal studies with disease controls and blood\-CSF barrier integrity measures are needed\.

## [Onyeukaziri, Justin Nnaemeka: Artificial Intelligence and Suppositum: A Critique of the Critique of the Notion of Selfhood](../publications/711279e3464974bf9aa9.md)



\_Scientia et Fides\_ 13 \(1\):57\-74\. 2025The objective of this paper is to posit a critique of the contemporary critique of the notion of selfhood in the philosophy of mind and cognitive neuroscience\. The research in artificial intelligence \(AI\) as the science of intelligence per se and/or of cognition, in general, has been considered and employed as a formidable theoretical tool in sustaining philosophical arguments for the denial of the existence of the Self or selfhood in the human person\. It has revitalized the philosophical problematics of the existence or otherwise, of consciousness, intelligence, and autonomy not only in biological systems but also in non\-biological systems and the deepening of the body\-soul and/or brain\-mind problem in the philosophy of mind\. This paper will give an exposition of the critique of selfhood in the human person, especially as expounded by Daniel Dennett\. It will also posit a counter\-critique of the critique of selfhood based on John Eccles’s dualistic\-interactionalist philosophy of neuroscience and Karol Wojtyła’s philosophical anthropology based on the notion of suppositum\. Hence, it shall defend the philosophical anthropology of the human person as a metaphysical suppositum possessing ontological subjectivity\. \(direct link \)

## [Raman\-Grounded Deep Learning for Calcium Carbonate Polymorph Sensing during Microfluidic Biomineralization](../publications/711291213454e8a45b30.md)

Brooke E\. Filanoski; David Erickson

Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation \(MICP\) in microfluidic systems produces spatially and temporally heterogeneous precipitates whose polymorph composition governs material outcomes but is difficult to monitor non\-destructively in situ\. We present a Raman\-grounded deep learning framework that decouples spectroscopic labeling from optical inference: each Raman spectrum is matched to an individually segmented crystal instance, and a five\-channel EfficientNet\-B0 classifier trained on these per\-instance labels assigns polymorph identity to the remaining crystals from brightfield and polarized light alone\. Trained on 550 Raman\-labeled instances and applied across 5123 segmented crystals spanning five experimental datasets, the framework achieved 97\.3% test accuracy across three polymorph classes\-calcite, early\-stage vaterite, and late\-stage vaterite\-at individual\-crystal resolution\. Late\-stage vaterite emerged as a third optically distinct class, identified from 48 h imaging and confirmed by Raman to retain vaterite phase identity despite its altered optical signature\. The framework resolved systematic effects of solution composition, bacterial density, pH, and time on polymorph composition and captured the dissolution of vaterite toward a calcite\-dominated state within a single device\. Operating at individual\-crystal resolution across heterogeneous crystal populations without requiring droplet confinement, the approach provides a practical route to non\-destructive polymorph monitoring in MICP and living building materials applications\.

## [Stacking‐Tuned Phonon Renormalization and Effective Heat Transport in Moiré Semiconductor Superlattices](../publications/711fd957cb9cc83bc035.md)

Choudhury Abinash Bhuyan; Antonio Cobarrubia; Shrawan Roy; Arik Rafiquddin Ahmed; Nicholas Schottle; Ryan Palmares; Jaedan Ford; Vincent Juliano; Nate Webb; Carlos M\. Torres; Steve Smith; Santosh KC; Mansour Mortazavi; Sanjay Kumar Behura

ABSTRACT Optically driven moiré semiconductor bilayers involve coupled phonon anharmonicity, interlayer interactions, and local heat dissipation, but experimental benchmarks across supported homo‐ and heterobilayers remain limited\. Here, we combine temperature‐dependent Raman spectroscopy, excitation‐power‐dependent Raman thermometry, and photoluminescence to study twisted MoS 2 /MoS 2 , WS 2 /WS 2 , and MoS 2 /WS 2 bilayers\. From 90 to 300 K, both homobilayers show conventional softening of Raman‐active phonons with negative effective anharmonic coefficients\. In contrast, the WS 2 ‐derived out‐of‐plane A ‐mode in the MoS 2 /WS 2 heterobilayer hardens with increasing temperature, exhibiting a positive linear temperature coefficient of \+0\.00700 ± 0\.00029 cm − 1 K − 1 and a positive effective Balkanski coefficient of \+1\.28 ± 0\.19 cm − 1 , while other modes remain softening‐dominant\. Photoluminescence reveals an interlayer excitonic channel only in the heterobilayer, indicating an interface‐specific phonon renormalization pathway beyond equilibrium anharmonic decay\. Using two excitation objectives with distinct laser‐heating radii, the supported Raman thermometry resolves mode‐dependent effective thermal‐transport parameters and reduces covariance in extracting in‐plane heat‐transport and heat‐sinking coefficients\. We further develop a physics‐guided monolayer‐to‐stacked neural‐network framework to reconstruct Raman spectra across temperature and power conditions and identify optimal optothermal regimes\. These results establish heterointerface‐controlled phonon renormalization as a key factor in phonon dynamics controlling heat dissipation and provide a scalable platform for thermal design in moiré quantum devices\.

## [Exploring Playful Language Learning in Higher Education Through a Virtual Reality Game](../publications/712b55eb635c38e3236a.md)

Riikka Ilona Partanen; Riitta\-Liisa Valijärvi; Pia Rajaniemi; Heidi Grönstrand; Miika Puljujärvi

This study investigates playful language learning in an immersive Virtual Reality \(VR\) environment\. The authors designed a VR language game for adult learners of Finnish in higher education in Sweden and Finland, aiming to support foreign\-language speaking skills\. Survey data were collected from 36 participants, who reported their learning experiences, emotional responses, and perceptions of VR as a language\-learning tool\. Drawing on Nicola Whitton’s theory of playful learning, the findings show that positive emotions, such as excitement, curiosity, and enjoyment, were more common than negative reactions, suggesting that the VR environment functioned effectively as a “magic circle” for experimenting with oral skills without real\-world consequences\. Negative emotions were mainly associated with perceptions that the game was too repetitive, too complex, or lacked sufficient action\. For many participants, the testing session was a transformative experience that increased their confidence and openness to using playful learning environments for language learning\.

## [The Role of Graded Motor Imagery in Managing Shoulder Dysfunction Post\-Mastectomy: Evidence from a Randomized Controlled Study](../publications/712ef85a58c4a0be5ad5.md)



Introduction: Functional limitation of upper body is widely recognized as a common postoperative consequence of surgical treatment for breast cancer\.Following surgery, nearly 67% of patients have upper limb/ shoulder dysfunction, such as numbness, painful sensations, weakening of the muscles, and limited motion range \[1\]\.Objective: This study aimed to investigate whether graded motor imagery affected shoulder dysfunction following a mastectomy\.Subjects and methods: Fifty\-four patients, aged between 35 to 55, experiencing shoulder dysfunction following mastectomy, were split into two equivalent groups using a random selection process\.Group \(A\): 27 patients underwent graded motor imagery \(GMI\) in addition to a conventional physiotherapy program, two sessions weekly for 6 weeks\.Group \(B\): 27 patients underwent conventional physiotherapy program, two sessions weekly for 6 weeks\.Conventional physiotherapy program included capsular stretching and active assisted ROM exercises, including codman/ pendular exercises involving forwardbackward movement, side\-to\-side movement, and circular movements, as well as wall climbing \(finger ladder\), shoulder wheel, and wand exercises\.Measures of shoulder pain, disability, range of motion, and muscular strength were taken both before and following the intervention\.Results: The findings indicated that graded motor imagery had a favorable impact on shoulder dysfunction\.Individuals showed decreased levels of shoulder pain and achieved greater mobility in the joint\.Furthermore, increases in muscle strength were observed \(p &gt; 0\.05\)\.Conclusion: Graded motor imagery was with significant improvements in shoulder pain, range of motion, and muscle strength, indicating its therapeutic value in shoulder rehabilitation\.

## [High Performance Thin Layer Chromatography \(HPTLC\) Analysis of Anti\-hypertensive Combination Therapy in Pharmaceutical Dosage form](../publications/7130b86b4f8af80805af.md)

Yesha M\. Patel; Dhara Patel; Grishma Patel; Maitri Patel; Dhvani Joshi; Dhyey Shah; Shaili Patel; Prasanna Kumar Pradhan; Komal Rahevar; Dhananjay B Meshram

A simple, selective, rapid and sensitive high performance thin\-layer chromatography \(HPTLC\)\-densitometric method was developed and validated for the simultaneous determination of Amlodipine besylate, Telmisartan and Indapamide in bulk and pharmaceutical dosage form\. Chromatographic separation achieved on precoated silica gel 60 F 254 plates using chloroform: toluene: ethyl acetate: methanol: TEA\(4:3:1\.5:1\.5:0\.1, v/v\) as the mobile phase with densitometric detection at 240 nm\. The analytes showed satisfactory separation with Rf values of 0\.21± 0\.0004, 0\.53 ±0\.002 and 0\.64 ± 0\.003 for AMLO, TELMI and INDA, respectively\. The method exhibited excellent linearity over the ranges of 250\-1250 ng/band for AMLO, 2000\-10000 ng/band for TELMI and 125\-625 ng/band for INDA\. Accuracy studies demonstrated recoveries within 98\-102 %, while precision studies showed %RSD values below 2 %\. The method remained robust following deliberate variation in mobile phase composition, migration distance and chamber saturation time\. Application of the method to the pharmaceutical formulation demonstrated assay values within the acceptable range, with no interference from excipients\. Compared with convention HPLC methods, the proposed HPTLC procedure offers rapid analysis, lower solvent consumption, operational simplicity and cost effectiveness making it suitable for routine quality control of AMLO, TELMI and INDA in pharmaceutical formulations\.

## [One\-step purification of ethylene by porous coordination polymers: from impurity\-specific design logic to quantitative structure–property relationships](../publications/7138038ecdafd8c0784c.md)

Yi Ding; Hujun Zhang; Lin Yin; Tingting Liu; Jie Tang; Jingui Duan

The purification of ethylene \(C 2 H 4 \) constitutes a foundational yet energetically demanding operation in the petrochemical industry, where conventional separation technologies remain intrinsically energy\-intensive\. In recent years, adsorptive separation employing porous coordination polymers \(PCPs\) has emerged as a promising and sustainable alternative or transitional strategy\. This review consolidates recent advances in the one\-step purification of C 2 H 4 from multi\-component C2 light hydrocarbon and carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) mixtures, delineated through four overarching design principles: \(i\) pore geometry and size engineering for molecular sieving and kinetic control; \(ii\) pore chemistry and functional\-site engineering for thermodynamic selectivity toward impurities; \(iii\) pore electrostatic potential engineering for the differential recognition of impurities over C 2 H 4 ; and \(iv\) dynamic structural effects in flexible PCPs enabling adaptive separation\. Going beyond a qualitative inventory of materials, we further translate these design principles into a set of quantitative mechanistic descriptors—including the pore\-to\-kinetic\-diameter ratio \(λ\), the electrostatic potential extremum \(ΔESP\), the isosteric heat difference \(Δ Q st \), the diffusion barrier difference \(Δ E a \), and the gate\-opening pressure ratio \(Π\)—and examine how they correlate with selectivity, capacity, and regenerability\. On this basis, the review examines the process\-level challenges that must be surmounted for industrial deployment and outlines prospective research directions spanning materials chemistry, process engineering, and machine learning, thereby offering mechanistic and design insights for the next generation of PCPs\.

## [Diagnostic accuracy of a modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system: a retrospective study](../publications/713ae77cde21cc49241d.md)

Yan Ren; Can Cui; Zhijing Zhang; Wei Liao; Chen Zhang; Yue Cheng; Wen Shen

OBJECTIVE: To develop a modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O\-RADS MRI system\. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A\. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort\. The diagnostic performance of the two scoring models was assessed by estimating the area under the curve \(AUC\), net reclassification improvement \(NRI\), and integrated discrimination improvement \(IDI\)\. In addition, 352 adnexal lesions from cohorts B and C were included to further evaluate the diagnostic ability of the modified scoring system\. RESULTS: In cohort A, the papillary projections exhibiting the sea anemone sign were highly indicative of borderline lesions \(p = 0\.001\)\. Diffusion restriction in solid components significantly distinguished benign from malignant masses \(p = 0\.001\)\. The apparent diffusion coefficient \(ADC\) value of cystic components yielded a cutoff of 1\.74 \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The DeLong test revealed no statistically significant difference in AUCs between the two systems in cohort A \(p &gt; 0\.05\)\. The NRI and IDI for the modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system were \-4\.13% and \-0\.04, respectively \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. In cohorts B and C, the AUCs were 0\.933 and 0\.910\. CONCLUSION: The diagnostic efficacy of the modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system was comparable to that of the standard O\-RADS MRI risk stratification system, facilitating the distinction between benign and malignant adnexal neoplasms\. KEY POINTS: Question How can a modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system be developed, and can this scoring system accurately classify adnexal masses? Findings The modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI system demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance and reliable risk stratification of adnexal masses by evaluating key imaging features\. Critical relevance statement The modified non\-contrast O\-RADS MRI scoring system contributes to the risk stratification of adnexal masses, particularly for patients who cannot undergo contrast agent administration\. This system provides a reliable tool to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes\.

## [A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels](../publications/7150390415b05c5e56b9.md)

Zhongtian Sun; Fan Mo; Prayag Tiwari; Kelin Xia

How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry\. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations\. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic\. On a fixed CIFAR\-10/ResNet\-18 training probe, equally sized clean\-label and corrupted\-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted\-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50\. The contrast survives uniform\-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7\-11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint\. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR\-10/ResNet\-18, whereas CIFAR\-100/ResNet\-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions\. In a separate noise\-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in\-sample R2 than raw persistence \(0\.936 versus 0\.908\)\. These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low\. Comparing persistence under scale controls with label\-fitting measurements offers a way to study how representations respond to label corruption beyond what training accuracy reveals\.

## [AI SMART AGRO SYSTEM: A WEB\-BASED AI\-ASSISTED DECISION SUPPORT PLATFORM FOR FARMERS](../publications/71674eea0c7efecb612b.md)



Farmers often have to decide on disease control, crop selection, soil management and irrigation without timely expert advice, which leads to yield loss and wastage of water and fertiliser\.This paper presents AI Smart Agro System, a web\-based decision\-support platform that brings five services into one dashboard: leaf disease detection from an uploaded photograph, crop recommendation, soil health analysis, irrigation advisory and weather\-based farming advice\.The system is built with PHP, MySQL and JavaScript, while disease detection and crop recommendation are handled by an external Python Flask AI service that is called through a secured REST API\.Soil, irrigation and weather advice are generated by transparent rule\-based logic using soil pH, N\-P\-K values, soil moisture, rainfall, temperature and humidity\.Every result is stored in the user&\#x27;s history, and notifications and an administrator panel support monitoring\.The prototype is designed to return the disease name, confidence, treatment and prevention tips for an uploaded leaf image, to recommend the three most suitable crops, and to give clear advice for soil and water management\.Quantitative evaluation of the AI models is left for future work\.

## [ScoutRoute: Efficient Mixture\-of\-Experts Routing Using Internal Language Model Signals](../publications/71897691b5d8fde6a98e.md)

Rajdeep Pandhare; Delzaan Bharucha

Efficient expert routing is a fundamental challenge in Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) systems, particularly for heterogeneous collections of independently trained Large Language Mod els \(LLMs\)\. Existing routing approaches typically rely on jointly trained gating networks, prompt\-based predictors, or computationally expensive multi\-model inference, limiting their flexibility and efficiency\. This paper presents ScoutRoute, a lightweight post\-hoc routing framework that predicts expert competence using internal language model signals extracted from a single forward pass through an inexpensive scout model\. Hidden\-state representations are used to estimate cross\-model competence through lightweight logistic probes, while logit\-derived confidence measures are incorporated within a domain\-aware routing strategy for efficient expert selec tion without modifying the underlying language models\. ScoutRoute isevaluatedon fiveopen\-weightlanguagemodels across fourbenchmark datasets covering mathematical reasoning, code generation, commonsense reasoning, and multidis ciplinary knowledge\. Experimental results show that ScoutRoute consistently outperforms individual routing signals while requiring only a single scout\-model inference\. The proposed competence probes also achieve superior calibration compared with conventional confidence measures, demonstrating that internal language model representations provide transferable information for accurate and efficient expert routing across heterogeneous language models

## [اتجاهات الجمهور العراقي نحو توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في إنتاج الأخبار التلفزيونية وعلاقتها بالمصداقية المدركة](../publications/718ce7459834beaf1570.md)

م\.م\. احمد ناظم فارس الرميض

هدفت الدراسة إلى الكشف عن اتجاهات الجمهور العراقي نحو توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في إنتاج الأخبار التلفزيونية، وقياس مستوى المصداقية المدركة لهذه الأخبار، فضلاً عن تحديد مستوى المعرفة بالتطبيقات الذكية ومتطلبات الشفافية والإشراف البشري والمخاوف المرتبطة بها\. وانطلقت الدراسة من تساؤل رئيس مفاده: ما اتجاهات الجمهور العراقي نحو توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في إنتاج الأخبار التلفزيونية، وما علاقتها بالمصداقية المدركة لديه؟ واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج المسحي، مستخدمة الاستبانة أداةً لجمع البيانات، وطُبقت على عينة غير احتمالية متاحة قوامها \(100\) مبحوث من الجمهور العراقي المتابع للأخبار التلفزيونية\. وأظهرت النتائج وجود اتجاه إيجابي نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي بمتوسط بلغ \(3\.66\)، ومستوى مرتفع نسبياً من المصداقية المدركة بمتوسط \(3\.45\)، فيما سجل محور الشفافية والإشراف البشري أعلى متوسط بلغ \(4\.14\)، وبلغ متوسط المخاوف المهنية والأخلاقية \(3\.99\)\. كما كشفت النتائج عن علاقة موجبة دالة إحصائياً بين الاتجاه نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي والمصداقية المدركة، وعلاقة موجبة بين معرفة الجمهور بهذه التقنيات واتجاهه نحو استخدامها\. وخلصت الدراسة إلى أن تقبل الجمهور للذكاء الاصطناعي يمثل قبولاً مشروطاً بالشفافية والمراجعة البشرية واستمرار المسؤولية التحريرية للمؤسسة الإعلامية\.

## [RiskPercept\-X: Explainable Transaction\-level Prediction of Investor\-perceived Risk on E\-investment Platforms](../publications/7191dcd09cccfc5e8119.md)

Shubhi Saxena; Garima Bhardwaj; Loveleen Gupta

Retail investing has gone mobile, yet almost everything known about perceived risk in it comes from crosssectional questionnaires analysed with structural equation models\.Such designs count associations in one cross\-section rather than predicting an unseen case, ignore the risk statements accumulating in public platform reviews, and use taxonomies blind to the frictions of digital brokerage\.RiskPercept\-X removes all three by making the platform event the unit of analysis: a risk\-adaptive encoder and taxonomy\-prior gate turn an event into a seven\-dimensional risk profile, learned per\-dimension prototypes align review text, sentiment benchmarks and survey records without cross\-source pairing, an ordinal cumulative\-link head treats long\-tailed intensity as a graded response, and a recency\-weighted escalation operator turns a history into a churn early warning\.On a temporally held\-out split it attains 89\.0% accuracy and 86\.8% macro\-averaged F1 \(macro\-F1\) on risk dimensions, 0\.841 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) on investor outcomes with an increment of 0\.033 from transferred signal, and 92\.3% accuracy on the Financial PhraseBank, where the comparison is with published reference values; against the strongest baseline reimplemented under an identical protocol it improves by 1\.9 macro\-F1 points on D1 and by 2\.9 on D2\.A leakagecontrolled replication confining every unsupervised and calibration stage to pre\-cut\-off data reproduces the ordering at 85\.9% macro\-F1 and 0\.834 AUC\.Three platform\-native dimensions absent from classical instruments carry 34\.0% of risk\-bearing reviews, supply the two highest\-ranked outcome drivers and together hold 0\.338 of the attribution mass, and escalation scores are associated with subsequent disengagement up to six weeks ahead\.Code and result files are released publicly\.

## [AI\-Assisted Early Detection of Breast Cancer Using Histopathological Image Analysis](../publications/7196c86418e0646ec086.md)

R\. Gurumoorthy; H\. Rajyashree; R\. Muthu Pandeeswari; G\. Nirrmal; A\. Aravindrajan; Sri Ram; Kannan Pattabiraman

Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers among women worldwide with more than 2\.3 million new breast cancer cases diagnosed each year \[1\], where early detection has a significantly positive effect on patient survival rates\. Examination of histopathological features remains the gold standard \[2\] in the diagnosis of breast cancer, however, clinical histopathological assessment is labor\-intensive, time consuming and can potentially have inter\-observer variability in the determination of the final clinical diagnosis\. The current paper presents an AI\-assisted deep learning framework for automatic breast cancer detection using histopathological images\. Multiple transfer learning models, including VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, and EfficientNetB5, were evaluated\. The proposed framework incorporates data augmentation, mixed precision training, and Binary Focal Loss to improve performance and computational efficiency\. Experimental results on a dataset of over 14,000 histopathological images demonstrate that DenseNet121 achieves the best performance, with a test accuracy of 81%, sensitivity of 80\.8%, specificity of 76\.7%, and ROC\-AUC of 0\.87\. VGG16 also shows stable performance, while ResNet50 suffers from low specificity due to over classification of malignant classes\. EfficientNet models exhibit poor generalization and strong class bias\. The result highlights the importance of evaluating multiple performance metrics beyond accuracy in medical image classification\. The proposed frameworks can assist pathologists by improving diagnostic consistency and reducing workload, making it a practical tool for clinical applications\.

## [Cyber Law in India: Emerging Issues and Challenges](../publications/71a21d5801941c6ff1f8.md)

IFFAT ZEHRA

This paper explores Indian cyber law&\#x27;s development since the passage of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and its current strains, arguing that lack of law is the prime hurdle\. India has a new criminal law, a complete set of intermediary regulations, a data protection act, and a rising number of relevant constitutional verdicts\. The prime problem is the amount and coherence of what&\#x27;s been built: too much relies on delegated legislation, there are few safeguards in cases that the State itself acts, and enforcement trails far behind the amount of online harm\. Cybercrime and electronic evidence, intermediary liability and online speech, data protection, artificial intelligence and synthetic media, and surveillance and shutdowns are the five areas of stress analyzed in this paper that concludes with recommendations\. As of October 2026, developments are reported\.
