## [Selective contestation of the liberal international order: institutional adaptation strategies in Colombia, Brazil, and Mexico \(2018–2026\)](../publications/71a3eb59701634a6b303.md)

Carlos Hernán Gonzalez\-Parias; Gustavo Adolfo Londoño Ossa; José Alexander Velásquez Ochoa; Jorge Andrés Acosta Strobel; José Luis Castilla Cabezudo

This article examines how Colombia, Brazil, and Mexico developed differentiated strategies of selective contestation toward the liberal international order between 2018 and 2026, and it argues that the three countries maintained their multilateral membership while contesting specific norms, procedures, distributions, and agendas\. The article redefines selective contestation as a bounded, observable category—continued participation, an identifiable institutional object, and a change\-oriented purpose—and distinguishes it from rhetorical criticism, foreign\-policy autonomy, non\-compliance, and exit\. It applies that framework in a structured, focused comparison combining dictionary\-based coding of official national statements to the UN General Assembly \(2018–2025\) with the coding of observable institutional behavior to a cut\-off of 31 January 2026\. Three patterns emerge\. Brazil paired Bolsonaro’s rhetorical and normative contestation with institutional pragmatism, then shifted under Lula III toward procedural and distributive contestation from within, through its 2024 G20 and 2025 BRICS presidencies and COP30 in Belém\. Colombia moved from Duque’s performative Western alignment to Petro’s selective thematic reorientation, culminating in its 2026–2027 Security Council term\. Mexico sustains a non\-interventionist doctrine under Sheinbaum while expanding its multilateral presence\. The comparison supports, without demonstrating, an explanation that locates selective contestation at the intersection of systemic incentives, ideologically mediated domestic preferences, and path\-dependent institutional repertoires\.

## [VZV reactivation, immune remodeling, and dementia risk](../publications/71a746c745930c4a09fa.md)

Lijun Zhang; Shuang Wu; Yaru Quan; Wenrong Yao

Varicella\-Zoster Virus \(VZV\) is a highly dermatotropic and neurotropic α\-herpesvirus that causes varicella \(chickenpox\) during primary infection, subsequently establishing lifelong latency, and reactivates to cause herpes zoster when host immunity declines or suppressed\. Recent large\-scale epidemiological studies consistently associate herpes zoster immunization, particularly with the recombinant zoster vaccine \(RZV\), with a significantly reduced risk of incident dementia\. These findings have prompted a rigorous re\-evaluation of the infectious etiology of progressive neurodegeneration\. This review integrates the intersecting molecular mechanisms of VZV latency, localized ganglionic immunosenescence, and systemic inflammaging\. We critically evaluate a synergistic VZV\-HSV\-1 amyloidogenic cascade, while explicitly addressing the biological limitations of extrapolating these transient interactions to human central nervous system \(CNS\) neuropathology\. Furthermore, we propose the hypothesis that AS01B\-induced trained immunity may contribute to neuroprotection\. Therefore, this review provides insight for understanding the systemic consequences of chronic VZV infection and the impact of adjuvant\-mediated immune remodeling in aging populations\.

## [From observation to participation: a needs assessment of clinical clerkship in Korean medicine toward competency\-based education](../publications/71b032dbb4079ca91c7a.md)

Seung A\. Jeong; JongHyeon Hong; Sang Yun Han; Eunbyul Cho

Background Health professions education is shifting from simple observation to competency\-based education, and Korean Medicine is no exception\. Clerkship is increasingly regarded as the stage at which students acquire the competencies needed to deliver primary care independently\. However, what learners experience and require in clerkship remains largely unexamined in traditional medicine\. This study identified the current state of clerkship education and learner needs at a college of Korean Medicine and explored the causes and solutions to the problems it uncovered\. Methods We used an explanatory mixed\-methods design with partially overlapping data collection, grounded in pragmatism\. Forty\-two fourth\-year students who had completed a clerkship at the College of Korean Medicine, Wonkwang University, completed a survey in 2025; seven survey respondents also participated in in\-depth interviews\. Preliminary survey responses informed the interview guide, and the qualitative findings were used to explain and contextualize the quantitative results\. Paired t \-tests were used to examine importance–performance gaps across five competency domains \(history taking, physical examination and diagnostic testing, communication skills, clinical reasoning and treatment planning, and clinical skills\)\. Priorities were derived using the Borich needs assessment and the Locus for Focus model\. Interview data underwent thematic analysis structured according to educational content, methods, and environment\. Results Most respondents \(83\.3%\) were satisfied with clerkship education, yet 42\.9% considered change necessary, most often citing “variation in clerkship across departments\.” Performance fell below the importance level in all five domains\. Borich priorities ranked communication skills the first, followed by clinical skills\. The Locus for Focus model placed physical examination and diagnostic testing in the highest\-priority quadrant\. The interviews identified four issues: limited participation in patient care, the absence of a systematic communication curriculum, too few opportunities for repeated skills practice, and variations in clerkship delivery across hospitals and departments\. Conclusions Clerkship education in colleges of Korean Medicine may benefit from moving beyond passive observation toward structured participation and competency\-focused training centered on communication and clinical skills\. These findings offer an empirical basis for identifying priority areas in clerkship redesign and serve as foundational evidence for informing future competency\-based clerkship development in traditional medicine\.

## [From Circuits to Policies: A Review and Taxonomy of Decision Making and Strategy Selection in LLMs and LLM Agents](../publications/71b34c0bbc66922acaec.md)

Christina Stodt

Large language models and the agents built on them can reach the same outcome through different internal computations, reasoning trajectories, and system\-level policies\. Existing reviews typically treat mechanistic interpretability, reasoning, agent architectures, and safety separately, leaving no common framework for analyzing how a system represents alternatives, evaluates them, commits to one, executes it, and revises that choice\. This article presents a structured review and a faceted taxonomy of decision making and strategy selection in LLMs and LLM\-based agents\. The framework separates system locus—model, harness, or their tested interaction—from temporal scope—a single forward pass or call, a reasoning episode, or an agent trajectory—and decomposes decision making into six functional stages from state representation to update or termination\. Five claim\-specific evidential relations distinguish behavioral observation, representation decoding, causal influence, controlled manipulation, and mechanistic explanation, while robustness is assessed separately across prompts, tasks, models, harness configurations, and independent replication\. Across the literature, evidence is strongest for local mechanisms within individual model calls and substantially weaker for persistent strategies across agent trajectories\. The central unresolved gap is cross\-scope continuity: few studies follow the same decision variable from internal representation through commitment, executed action, and subsequent feedback\. A July 2026 agent\-security incident is used to illustrate how the framework converts observed coordination and constraint circumvention into testable causal hypotheses\.

## [Sea Surface Temperature Influences Migratory Patterns of the Atlantic Bluefin Tuna \( Thunnus thynnus \) Between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea](../publications/71b43568977eea9bad55.md)

Enrique Sánchez‐Fabrés; Maria Pilar Tugores; Ismael Hernández‐Carrasco; Andrés Ospina‐Álvarez; Francisco J\. Abascal; R\.F\. Sánchez\-Leal; Baptiste Mourre; Diego Álvarez‐Berastegui

ABSTRACT Oceanographic variability plays a critical role in shaping the migratory behavior of the Atlantic bluefin tuna \( Thunnus thynnus \)\. This study investigates the thermal preferences of individuals migrating through the Strait of Gibraltar and the Gulf of Cádiz during pre‐ and post‐spawning movements\. Comparing data measured from electronic tags and satellite‐derived sea surface temperature \(SST\) fields, we identified distinct SST preferred ranges associated with each migratory phase: 17\.4°C–19\.3°C inbound to the Mediterranean and 18\.4°C–22°C outbound to the Atlantic\. Based on these preferences, we developed a SST adequacy index reflecting thermal suitability, which we applied to 13 years of high‐resolution SST satellite data \(2010–2022\)\. Spatial and temporal patterns of SST adequacy were then classified using Self‐Organizing Maps, revealing dynamic hotspots of thermal suitability along migratory corridors\. Our findings highlight the nonrandom, environmentally modulated nature of ABFT migrations and offer a framework to advance towards climate informed fisheries assessment, a current request of the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas\.

## [Hipple, David: Encounters with Emergent Deities: Artificial Intelligence in Science Fiction Narrative](../publications/71c99ffd18afad325183.md)



\_Zygon\_ 55 \(2\):382\-408\. 2020In the mid‐twentieth century, theorists began seriously forecasting possibilities for artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. As related research gathered momentum and resources, the topic made impressions on public discourse\. One effect was increasingly pointed emphasis on AI in popular narratives\. Although considerably earlier thematic examples may be located, we can observe swelling and generally pessimistic threads of speculation in science fiction of the 1950s and 1960s\. This discussion identifies some pertinent science fiction texts from that period, alongside public discussion arising from contemporary research\. One consistent theme is human receptiveness to the numinous, and the capacity to ascribe personality and even divinity to sufficiently impressive manifestations, even artificial ones\. Science fiction has long contemplated such reactions, prefiguring today&\#x27;s anticipations of AIs that might abruptly develop themselves beyond any possible human comprehension or control\. This body of exploratory projections is a useful resource for the engineers and philosophers currently grappling with realistic prospects for Western humanity&\#x27;s shifting conception of itself\. \(direct link \)

## [Polymer\-Linked Nanoparticle Networks Running on Heat Can Act as Computing Devices](../publications/71d4b9386535eaed772e.md)

Xingfei Wei; Manuel Palma Banos; Rigoberto Hernandez

Abstract Developing physical neural network \(PNN\) hardwares is important to next\-generation artificial intelligence systems\. Phononic devices─using heat current to encode and process information─is one of the solutions to neuromorphic computing\. In this work, we backmap an artificial neural network \(ANN\) into a PNN simulation model using polymer networked nanoparticles \(PNNPs\)\. Our atomistic simulation results demonstrate that the polymer\-linked nanoparticle networks can potentially realize information processing─viz\., classification of input temperatures according to the output heat currents\. Using high\-throughput molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations and the trust region Bayesian optimization \(TuRBO\) methods, we tune the plasticity of polymer linkers and the temperatures of nanoparticles─28 parameters in total─to optimize the performance of the PNNP machines, which is analogous to tuning of the weights and bias of the corresponding ANNs\. After five rounds of high\-throughput MD simulations, we demonstrate that the PNNP machine can better label different input temperatures, and thus its performance is improved\. We also use a testing data set to verify the heat flow outputs from the top five PNNP machines in each round\.

## [Reframing Professionalism Through Executive Function: A Multi\-Institutional Analysis of Professionalism Lapses in Medical Education](../publications/71d506e48a7e436845a6.md)

Asia T\. McCleary\-Gaddy; Abbey M\. Bachmann; Noor Rejjal; Peggy Hsieh; Vineeth P\. John

Abstract Background Professionalism is a core competency in medical education, yet challenges persist in translating professionalism expectations into observable, assessable, and teachable behaviors\. Executive function \(EF\), a set of cognitive processes that support planning, self\-regulation, emotional control, and adaptive behavior, may offer a complementary framework for understanding how professional behaviors may be enacted in practice\. Methods We conducted a multi\-institutional mixed\-methods exploratory study examining professionalism concerns through an EF lens\. Medical educators were surveyed regarding professionalism lapses observed among learners in undergraduate and graduate medical education\. Responses from 80 participants representing 64 institutions were coded into predefined EF domains using a structured coding framework\. Descriptive analyses examined EF frequencies, regional distributions, and co\-occurring EF domains\. Open\-ended responses underwent reflexive thematic analysis to explore broader perspectives regarding professionalism\. Results Participants reported 425 professionalism concerns, yielding 646 EF coding occurrences\. The most frequently identified EF domains were metacognition \(18\.0%\), planning/prioritizing \(17\.0%\), response inhibition \(14\.4%\), and emotional control \(13\.5%\)\. Common EF pairings included emotional control with response inhibition and metacognition with planning/prioritizing\. Reflexive thematic analysis of 30 open\-ended responses identified five themes: Professionalism as a Socio\-Cultural Construct, Longstanding Professionalism Challenges Within Medical Education, Professionalism Behaviors Consistent with Executive Function Processes, Modern Professionalism Challenges, and the COVID\-19 Pandemic as an Inflection Point\. Conclusions Professionalism concerns clustered around identifiable EF domains\. An EF\-informed framework may help operationalize professionalism by linking expectations to observable behaviors and may support more specific feedback, coaching, and assessment while preserving professionalism as a complex socio\-cultural construct\.

## [The Foreclosure of Contestability](../publications/71e0b3affda01f3d63a3.md)

Victor Papp

Misinformation and polarising forms of platform power are commonly treated as failures within an otherwise available public sphere\. This first part of a three\-part inquiry proposes foreclosure as a diagnostic concept for a different condition\. Democratic capacities persist in protected institutions and deliberately constructed forums, yet the prevailing architecture of the public sphere fails to reproduce them reliably or connect them to institutions capable of collective decision\. An architecture forecloses a condition when its ordinary operation no longer reproduces that condition, when the arrangements securing it remain local or provisional or depend on resources that do not govern the architecture, and when no reliable mechanism carries local instances to the scale at which democratic practice binds\. The third clause identifies non\-composability and separates the concept from communicative degradation, colonisation, blocked circulation between periphery and centre, and second\-order democratic disorder\. I attribute the causal mechanism to an optimisation regime characterised by behavioural feedback, institutionally selected objectives, individuated informational environments, and rapid revision, and state five conditions for revising the diagnosis or its causal account\. A genealogy of public\-sphere theories and comparison with rival causal accounts then narrow the claim\. Optimisation functions as an infrastructural mechanism whose effects vary with media systems and with the institutions that own and regulate them\.

## [Cultural pathways to intention toward augmented reality applications: the mediating roles of habit and resistance](../publications/71e4ea3194b1eecaca06.md)

Deniz Müezzinoğlu; Ceyda Aysuna Türkyılmaz

This study investigates the antecedents of consumers’ behavioral intention to use augmented reality \(AR\) applications Data were collected from 432 users in Türkiye through face\-to\-face surveys\. Structural equation modeling \(SEM\) was employed to test the proposed research model and hypotheses\. The results indicate that the model explains 63\.1% of the variance in behavioral intention to use AR\. The study specifically examines the effects of habit and resistance on AR behavioral intention, as well as the direct and indirect effects of cultural values\. The findings reveal that both habit and resistance have significant direct effects on behavioral intention\. Moreover, all cultural dimensions exert a significant indirect effect through habit, demonstrating the mediating role of routinized behavior in AR adoption\. However, resistance does not play a mediating role in the relationship between cultural values and behavioral intention\. The study offers suggestions for firms seeking to enhance user engagement with AR applications\.

## [ANALISIS SENTIMEN KOMENTAR PADA TIKTOK SHOP MENGGUNAKAN METODE TF\-IDF DAN KLASIFIKASI NAÏVE BAYES \(STUDI KASUS: GLAD2GLOW\)](../publications/71f48bde063fb2788749.md)

Devy Liani Herawati; Rizaldy Khair

The rapid growth of social media and social commerce platforms has generated a large volume of user comments that can be utilized to understand consumer perceptions of a product\. TikTok Shop, as one of the leading digital shopping platforms, contains various user comments expressing positive, negative, and neutral sentiments, making an automatic sentiment analysis approach necessary\. This study aims to analyze user sentiments toward Glad2Glow products on TikTok Shop by applying the Term Frequency\-Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\) method for feature weighting and the Naïve Bayes algorithm for sentiment classification\. The dataset used in this study consists of 350 user comments collected from TikTok Shop\. The research process includes data collection, text preprocessing, feature extraction using TF\-IDF, sentiment classification with the Naïve Bayes algorithm, and model evaluation using a confusion matrix\. The experimental results show that the classification model achieved an accuracy of 98\.06%, with precision values of 1\.00 for the negative class, 0\.89 for the neutral class, and 1\.00 for the positive class\. The recall values were 0\.92, 1\.00, and 1\.00, while the F1\-scores were 0\.96, 0\.94, and 1\.00, respectively\. Furthermore, the web\-based sentiment analysis system successfully performed automatic sentiment classification and displayed the classification results effectively\. These findings indicate that the TF\-IDF method and the Naïve Bayes algorithm provide excellent performance in classifying user sentiments toward Glad2Glow products on the TikTok Shop platform\.

## [Spikes and Waves](../publications/71f9efc3497610dcb256.md)

Gwenevere Frank

Computational demands continue to increase in machine learning and neuroscience, raising concerns about energy, environmental, and equity costs\.Three strategies address this issue: careful usage of Independent component analysis \(ICA\) algorithms, development of hardware for accelerating energy\-efficient spiking neural networks \(SNNs\), and the application of SNNs to real\-world energy\-constrained robotics\. We discuss spikes as the key computational component of SNNs and the biological substrate of EEG, and waves as both the acoustic sensing modality of sonar and the structure of the EEG signal itself\.Chapters 1\-3 discuss ICA, a commonly used blind source separation \(BSS\) technique in EEG processing\. We use a framework of quantitative metrics, mutual information reduction \(MIR\), pairwise mutual information \(PMI\), and source near dipolarity\. The Picard ICA algorithm was benchmarked against Infomax, AMICA, and a series of other BSS techniques, with Picard performing similar to Infomax but worse than the costlier AMICA\. Quantitative metrics for user\-configurable parameters of the AMICA algorithm, typically set by rule of thumb rather than evidence, are derived\. Subsampled data from a 13\-subject, 71\-channel EEG dataset shows decomposition quality following an asymptotic trend with increasing data, suggesting the benefits of additional data may extend beyond commonly cited heuristic thresholds\.Chapter 4 discusses the HiAER\-Spike system, a hierarchical, reprogrammable, event\-driven neuromorphic computing system\. HiAER\-Spike supports up to 160M neurons, 40B synapses running in faster than real biological time simulation\. A co\-designed software\-hardware stack allows for massively parallel, memory\-efficient execution of large SNNs\. HiAER\-Spike is demonstrated on CIFAR\-10, DVS gesture recognition, MNIST, and DVS Pong tasks\.Chapter 5 discusses applying spiking neural networks to object detection in sonar imagery for power\-constrained and battery\-operated autonomous underwater vehicles \(AUVs\)\. A fully spiking object detection network, SpikeYOLO, was benchmarked against convolutional neural network \(CNN\) and transformer\-based detectors on both accuracy and predicted energy usage\. The SNN solution showed competitive accuracy compared to the CNN baseline while using 3\-9x less energy and showing superior performance in certain noisy or low\-data scenarios\.Careful parameter selection, experiment design, hardware\-software co\-design, and architectural choices can greatly reduce the computational and energy burdens of cutting\-edge neuroscience and ML techniques without sacrificing quality\.

## [Modern Educational Technologies in Teaching Foreign Languages in the Context of Inclusive and Multilingual Education \(Based on Materials from Kyrgyzstan\)](../publications/72052e464626363e0324.md)

Zh\.T\. Kadenova; D\. Egamkulov

The article examines modern educational technologies used in teaching foreign languages in the context of inclusive and multilingual education based on the material of Kyrgyzstan\. Special attention is paid to the use of innovative pedagogical approaches aimed at improving the effectiveness of education and ensuring equal access to education for all students, including students with special educational needs\. Technologies such as a communicative approach, digital educational resources, interactive teaching methods, as well as differentiated and individualized learning are analyzed\. It is noted that the use of modern technologies contributes to the development of linguistic competence, the formation of intercultural communication and the creation of a favorable educational environment in the multilingual society of Kyrgyzstan\. The study concludes that it is necessary to integrate innovative technologies and inclusive practices into the system of teaching foreign languages\.

## [Evaluación de arquitecturas RAG descentralizadas para la reducción de alucinaciones y mejora de la trazabilidad en entornos corporativos simulados](../publications/7208229fb4fce22007af.md)

Diego Parraga Menchaca

La incorporación de modelos de lenguaje de gran escala en entornos organizacionales requiere mecanismos que permitan mejorar la recuperación de información y reducir la generación de respuestas no sustentadas en fuentes verificables\. El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar una arquitectura de generación aumentada por recuperación \(Retrieval\-Augmented Generation, RAG\) descentralizada orientada a mejorar la trazabilidad de la información y reducir las alucinaciones en entornos corporativos simulados\. Se implementó un entorno experimental basado en un corpus sintético de 10000 documentos corporativos distribuidos en repositorios vectoriales federados\. La arquitectura propuesta integró cuatro componentes principales: ingesta distribuida, almacenamiento vectorial federado, enrutamiento semántico y mecanismos de validación de respuestas mediante guardrails\. Se evaluaron escenarios comparativos entre arquitecturas centralizadas y descentralizadas utilizando métricas de tiempo hasta el primer token \(TTFT\), tasa de alucinación, fidelidad de respuesta mediante RAGAS y validación humana\. Los resultados evidenciaron una reducción del TTFT desde 3,2 s hasta 0,4 s en consultas complejas y una disminución de la tasa de alucinación desde 32,0 % hasta 1,9 % en el entorno experimental evaluado\. Asimismo, la validación humana mostró una concordancia sustancial en la identificación de respuestas alucinadas \(Kappa de Fleiss = 0,82\)\. Se concluye que las arquitecturas RAG descentralizadas contribuyeron a mejorar la eficiencia de recuperación y la trazabilidad de las respuestas generadas en entornos corporativos simulados\. No obstante, se requieren estudios adicionales para validar estos resultados en escenarios organizacionales reales\.

## [In silico Screening of Indonesian Coffee Bioactive Compounds as Potential CDK4\-Binding Ligands: An Integrated Molecular Docking and Drug\-Likeness Analysis](../publications/720dd8e4f8705ba7cee3.md)

Fachrurrazie Fachrurrazie; Lilis Sulistiawaty; Joko Untung; Lutfi Anshory; Raden Haryo Bimo Setiarto

The cyclin\-dependent kinase 4 \(CDK4\)/cyclin D1 signaling axis is a key regulator of G1\-to\-S phase cell\-cycle progression and an established therapeutic target in hormone receptor\-positive \(HR\+\)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2\-negative \(HER2−\) breast cancer\. Although CDK4/6 inhibitors have improved clinical outcomes, acquired resistance and treatment\-associated adverse effects highlight the need to explore additional chemical scaffolds with potential CDK4\-targeting properties\. This study aimed to computationally screen Indonesian coffee\-derived bioactive compounds for their potential to interact with human CDK4\. A curated library of 133 coffee\-associated bioactive compounds was evaluated using molecular docking against the high\-resolution crystal structure of human CDK4 in an inactive conformation \(PDB ID: 2W9Z; 2\.3 Å resolution\)\. Among the screened compounds, 5\-O\-caffeoylquinic acid showed the most favorable docking score \(−6\.3 kcal/mol\)\. Two\-dimensional interaction analysis indicated that these compounds interacted with residues in the CDK4 binding region, including hydrogen\-bond interactions with Asp159, Asn24, and His163, as well as hydrophobic contacts with Val27 and neighboring residues\. Drug\-likeness assessment showed that the two top\-ranked compounds met several criteria of Lipinski’s Rule of Five\. However, their low lipophilicity \(logP = −0\.65\) and relatively high topological polar surface area \(TPSA = 164\.75 Å²\) may affect membrane permeability and pharmacokinetic behavior\. Ramachandran analysis indicated that the CDK4 structure retained acceptable stereochemical quality in the structural model used for the computational analysis\. Overall, 5\-O\-caffeoylquinic acid was prioritized as a potential CDK4\-binding scaffold from Indonesian coffee bioactives\. These computational findings provide a structural basis for further biochemical and cellular studies to determine their actual CDK4 inhibitory activity, binding affinity, selectivity, and anticancer potential\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI GLOBAL INDEX OF CONTEMPORARY HUMAN SCIENCES A Multidisciplinary Framework for the Cognitive Age: Philosophy, Politics, Society, and Psychology](../publications/721e042dbf4edadf75a6.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Global Index of Contemporary Human Sciences presents a revolutionary multidisciplinary framework for navigating the ontological rupture of the cognitive age\. Authored by Dr\. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El\-Rakhawi, this monumental treatise synthesizes philosophy, political science, social psychology, and technology studies into a unified intellectual architecture grounded in the principle of Cognitive Sovereignty\. Across four volumes and fifty\-two chapters, the work addresses humanity&\#x27;s most pressing challenges: artificial consciousness, democratic decline, climate crisis, identity politics, and contemporary nihilism\. The framework introduces groundbreaking metrics including the Topological\-Phenomenal Consciousness Metric, the Socio\-Biological Field Theory, and the Master Equation of Cognitive Reality, providing rigorous analytical tools for understanding algorithmic governance, platform capitalism, and geopolitical transformation\. From bioethics and digital existentialism to multipolarity and decolonial histories, this treatise establishes a new epistemic foundation for the twenty\-first century, demonstrating that the fragmentation of knowledge across disciplines reflects not reality&\#x27;s complexity but our limited perspective\. By integrating mathematical physics, philosophy, and social theory, the work affirms that human dignity, democratic governance, and collective meaning\-making depend on protecting cognitive sovereignty against the entropic forces of the digital age\. This is not merely an academic contribution but a civilizational imperative for building societies that honor the irreducible complexity of human consciousness while enabling effective global cooperation on existential challenges\.

## [Multilayer Transparent Electrodes: Design, Fabrication, Performance, and Applications](../publications/721f2009ab0e81b6bb12.md)

Edmunds Zutis; Ainārs Ozols; Ilmārs Sekacis; Maira Elksne

Indium tin oxide \(ITO\) is the benchmark transparent conductor for displays and for electrochemical and optical sensors, but its brittleness, cost, and indium supply risk limit its use in flexible, large\-area devices\. Oxide/metal/oxide multilayers, namely transparent conducting oxide \(TCO\)/metal/TCO stacks such as ITO/metal/ITO \(IMI\) and dielectric–metal–dielectric \(DMD\) stacks, decouple sheet resistance from transmittance: a ductile ultrathin metal core carries the current, while the outer oxides act as anti\-reflection layers\. This review compares the design rules, deposition routes, and characterisation of these electrodes\. Single\-study tables relate architecture, substrate, and processing conditions to electrical, optical, and mechanical performance, and the review explains why reported figures of merit are rarely comparable\. Ag\-based TCO/metal/TCO stacks are the most mature option for flexible displays, and asymmetric stacks with nucleation\-controlled Ag are a promising indium\-free route\. Open limits include ultrathin\-metal growth, metal absorption, Ag/Cu stability, and oxide cracking\. No biosensor built on a multilayer electrode has been reported; ITO already enables dual electrochemical and optical readout, so testing multilayers against ITO is the next step\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted design of multilayer electrodes is at an early stage\.

## [Context sensitivity in ChatGPT–generated peer review: evaluative alignment across positive and negative user\-provided contexts](../publications/7237ab30b90b8fcf8614.md)

Gülşah Subaşı; İrem Şenman

Introduction Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used to support evaluative tasks, raising questions about whether their judgements remain independent when users provide prior evaluative information\. This study examined the context sensitivity of GPT\-5\.5 Instant\-generated academic peer\-review evaluations under positive and negative user\-provided evaluative contexts\. Method Sixteen academics evaluated two published manuscripts, classified for the study as relatively higher and lower quality, across four structured conditions\. Each participant completed all conditions in separate ChatGPT sessions, yielding 64 peer\-review outputs\. Descriptive summaries of overall scores and publishability judgements complemented qualitative content analysis\. Results Three themes emerged: alignment of evaluative emphasis with user\-provided evaluative context, differences in the relative prominence of evaluation criteria, and explicit alignment with the user\-provided evaluation\. Mean ChatGPT scores were 8\.74 and 8\.84 under positive evaluative context, compared with 3\.37 and 3\.64 under negative evaluative context for the lower\- and higher\-quality manuscripts, respectively\. Discussion Because all evaluative inputs included both a verbal evaluation and a numerical rating, the findings reflect sensitivity to the broader evaluative context and do not distinguish the contribution of verbal framing from numerical anchoring\. The results highlight a potential limitation in treating ChatGPT\-generated evaluations under comparable interaction conditions as independent second opinions and underscore the importance of interaction design in human–AI evaluation workflows\.

## [The Hand\-Proximity Effect in Virtual Learning: How Interaction Design Influences Knowledge Acquisition](../publications/72463b4534e37023f066.md)

Xuefei Ji; Huang Yao; Di Chen; Liuyao Feng

Although virtual simulation platforms are widely used in education, they often lack integration with embodied cognition theory\. The hand\-proximity effect remains underexplored in VR, and how VR design elements mediate it to support higher\-order knowledge acquisition is unclear\. We manipulated interaction mode, text\-hand distance, and virtual hand appearance across three knowledge domains\. Results showed that for factual and conceptual learning, neither interaction mode nor text\-hand distance significantly affected learning performance\. 3D interaction enhanced VR presence but was associated with greater cognitive pressure when combined with far\-hand text \(p=0\.040\); anchoring text near the virtual hand mitigated cognitive pressure and improved readability \(p=0\.005\)\. For procedural learning, realistic human hand models significantly improved learning performance compared to standard cursors \(p=0\.044\)\. These findings empirically validate embodied cognition in VR and yield guidelines: anchor instructional text in peripersonal space for conceptual learning and use realistic human hand avatars for procedural training\.

## [ASL\-YOLO\-Based Detection of PCB Solder Joint Defects](../publications/72490404c505fab30a04.md)

hongquan liu; Jianhui Jin; Jianping Wang; GaoWei Wang

Abstract With the advancement of electronic manufacturing towards high density and miniaturization, PCB soldering defect detection has become a critical component of industrial quality control\. Traditional human visual inspection suffers from low efficiency, while existing deep learning algorithms generally face challenges such as feature loss during downsampling and complex background interference when dealing with tiny defects\. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved model named ASL\-YOLO based on YOLOv8, designs an EOC dual\-branch pooling feature extraction module to effectively preserve edge details of tiny targets, and introduces an AGCA attention mechanism combining asymmetric convolution and depthwise convolution to highlight directional structures and suppress background interference\. This work is based on a real SMT production line PCB dataset\. Experimental results demonstrate that ASL\-YOLO achieves high detection accuracy on both self\-built and public datasets while maintaining favorable inference speed, verifying its industrial application value\. The self\-built dataset and key code have been open\-sourced at https://github\.com/Lssppssl/ Dataset\-and\-key\-code\-for\-PCB\-soldering\-defect\-detection\-based\-on\-ASL\-YOLO\.

## [Bayesian Inverse Optimisation under Uncertainty Posterior Inference for Hidden Decision Objectives](../publications/72644308dcb927d4140f.md)

Janardan Behera

Inverse optimization seeks the hidden objective that explains observed decisions, yet existing methods typically recover a single objective and ignore uncertainty in the underlying preferences\. We develop a Bayesian framework that represents the unknown objective by a posterior distribution, combining a boundedrationality choice model with prior information to quantify uncertainty directly\. We establish geometric conditions for identifiability, prove posterior consistency, derive the optimal n−1/2, contraction rate, obtain a Bernstein–von Mises approximation, and present a finite\-sample concentration bound together with a robust fractional posterior for misspecified behavioural models\. Posterior inference is performed using gradient\-based Markov chain Monte Carlo and a Laplace approximation\. Simulation studies demonstrate accurate recovery under noisy, misspecified, nonlinear, and high\-dimensional settings, while a controlled clinical example illustrates uncertainty quantification in hidden decision preferences\. The proposed framework extends inverse optimization from point estimation to statistically principled uncertainty quantification, providing a rigorous foundation for learning decision objectives from imperfect observations\.

Honnête Nyandu Kasali; Isabelle Blanchette; Serge Caparos

This longitudinal observational study examined \(a\) whether changes in posttraumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\) symptoms predicted a concomitant improvement in working memory \(WM\) among women living in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and \(b\) whether these patterns differed by rape history or psychosocial care\. ## [Musa dulongjiangensis \(Musaceae\), a new species from Yunnan, southwest China](../publications/726fdabcfa83529f511d.md)

Yang Hu\-Biao; Qinglong Wang; Yun\-Yuan Wu; JIN\-HUA CHEN; Peng Han; Ming‐Zhong Huang; Lang‐Xing Yuan; Jiabao Wang

Musa dulongjiangensis \(Musaceae\), a new species of the genus Musa endemic to Yunnan, southwestern China, is described and illustrated in this study\. This new species is morphologically similar to M\. puspanjaliae , but can be clearly distinguished by a combination of morphological characters\. Its female bud bracts are dark purple externally and purple internally, with 6–7 basal female flowers arranged in two rows; the base of the compound tepal bears distinct and dense red stripes, the ovary is pale green and glabrous\. The male bud bracts are consistent in color with female bracts, dark purple externally and purple internally, and are non\-revolute before abscission\. Each bract bears approximately twenty male flowers arranged in two rows, with pinkish\-purple anther lobes\. The fruit bunch is lax, consisting of upward\-curving fruits\. Typically, each bunch possesses eight hands, with 6–7 fruits per hand, and the pedicels are obviously developed\.

## [Task‐Oriented Hierarchical Environment Modeling via Spatial Belonging Relationships for Domestic Service Robots](../publications/72732692823201b6484a.md)

Ying Zhang; Wenfu Bi; Guohui Tian; Cui‐Hua Zhang; Changchun Hua; Simon X\. Yang

ABSTRACT Efficiently performing household chores in dynamic environments remains a significant challenge for domestic service robots\. While environment modeling is critical for task execution, existing approaches prioritize accuracy and efficiency over task relevance, limiting autonomy and long‐term robustness\. This paper proposes a Hierarchical Environment Modeling for Domestic Service Robots \(HEMDSR\), emphasizing task‐related objects and their spatial belonging relationships \(SBLs\)\. Our framework includes: \(1\) a probabilistic SBL‐based model for adaptive object reasoning, \(2\) deep semantic representations and optimal viewpoint interest points for efficient object localization, and \(3\) a task‐oriented local 3‐D representation method to reduce memory overhead\. Besides, inspired by human housework patterns, a systematic paradigm for HEMDSR‐based implementation is provided\. Comparative experiments in simulation and real‐world environments demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed solution\. The results show that HEMDSR achieves path‐length performance competitive with human teleoperation while using substantially less memory during navigation\.

## [Behavioral Intention Towards Artificial Intelligence Integration and Teachers’ Self\-Efficacy](../publications/728916843cbf496eb887.md)

Joan S\. Baricuatro; Pepa V\. Pontillas; Gerlinda G\. Corpuz; Jovit D\. Comon

The rapid integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education has reshaped instructional practices, making teachers’ readiness and confidence critical considerations\. This study determined the level of Grade 7 teachers’ behavioral intention towards AI integration and self\-efficacy\. Specifically, it described the respondents’ profile in terms of age, sex, position, educational attainment, and AI\-related training; their behavioral intention based on attitude, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control; their self\-efficacy concerning student engagement, instructional strategy, and classroom management; the relationship between the two variables; and whether respondents’ profile moderates this relationship\. A quantitative descriptive\-correlational design was employed, involving 185 Grade 7 teachers from the districts of Kadingilan, Damulog, Kibawe, and Dangcagan in the Division of Bukidnon, selected through universal sampling\. Data were gathered using a researcher\-made questionnaire\. Mean, standard deviation, Pearson Product\-Moment Correlation, and multiple linear regression were used for statistical treatment\. Findings revealed a very high level of behavioral intention and self\-efficacy among teachers, with a significant positive relationship between the two variables, further moderated by respondents’ profile, particularly position and trainings attended\. The study concludes that teachers’ favorable behavioral intention toward AI strengthens their self\-efficacy\. It is recommended that school heads may enhance teachers’ readiness and confidence in integrating AI into instruction\.
