## [Fetal bovine and calf serums differ in their contents of endocannabinoids, unsaturated fatty acids, monoacyl\-glycerols, N\-acyl\-ethanolamines, oxylipins, and cytokines](../publications/729712c5aa704922b107.md)

Hilal Kalkan; Jean\-Philippe C\. Lavoie; Isabelle Bourdeau‐Julien; Frédéric Raymond; Vincenzo Di Marzo; Nicolas Flamand

Cell culture relies heavily on serum supplementation, but serum composition makes it difficult to ensure reproducibility and consistency of experimental results\. Consequently, research10 groups must test multiple batches to ensure the functionality and reproducibility of their models\. The commonly used serums are fetal bovine serum \(FBS\) and calf serum \(CS\), which have been recognized as crucial in modulating cellular processes\. While having been utilized for decades, little information is known about their respective lipid mediator contents\. This study explored the presence of several major bioactive lipids involved in the regulation of inflammation, metabolism, differentiation, immune response, neuroprotection, and vascular homeostasis\. These included polyunsaturated fatty acids, monoacylglycerols \(MAGs\), N \-acyl\-ethanolamines \(NAEs\), and oxylipins\. As compared to FBS, CS samples were enriched in most fatty acids except for arachidonic acid\. The levels of the endocannabinoids 2\-arachidonoyl\-glycerol \(2\-AG\) and N \-arachidonoyl\-ethanolamine \(AEA\) followed the same pattern as arachidonic acid\. On the other hand, most lipoxygenase\-derived mediators, including, leukotriene B 4 , showed higher abundance in CS\. Accordingly, CS activated the random migration of human neutrophils to a much greater extent than FBS, an effect attenuated by the BLT 1 receptor antagonist CP 105,696\. Cytokines/chemokines levels were also different between FBS and CS samples\. These findings highlight that bovine serum lipid composition might be a major determinant modulating cellular responses and might thus impact experimental reproducibility\. The data presented herein will help obtaining insights beyond conventional cell culture optimization and might represent key features to consider when planning in cellulo experiments across numerous fields, also beyond immunology\.

## [Global governance and the status of teachers as a profession: a special section appraising the 1966 ILO\-UNESCO Recommendation](../publications/729bf3664f34acbf39c6.md)

Tore Bernt Sørensen; Xavier Dumay; Lynn Webster Paine

This article introduces a Special Section prompted by the 60 years anniversary of the ILO\-UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers, an early milestone in global teacher policy\. The entry point of the Special Section is that the 1966 Recommendation constitutes an emblematic case through which key developments in the global governing of teachers and the status of the teaching profession since the mid\-twentieth century might be interrogated and reflected upon\. Comprising six articles in a variety of formats, the Special Section has the dual objective to analyse and discuss, on the one hand, the evolution of global teacher policy over the past 60 years, and, on the other, to critically interrogate why many of the issues confronting the teaching profession remain so persistent\. By way of introducing the Special Section, this article discusses the imbrications between the evolving status of the profession and the global governance of teachers, with reference to existing research and the contributions to the Special Section\.

## [Demographic subgroup\-aware analysis of blood pressure predictive models](../publications/72a3a9c95c283218c989.md)

Blessing Kolawole; Sinuo Fan; Yingjie Lao; Valencia Joyner Koomson

Blood pressure \(BP\) is an important cardiovascular health indicator, usually monitored non\-invasively with a sphygmomanometer, which can be bulky and inconvenient for real\-time monitoring\. Blood pressure estimation using photoplethysmography \(PPG\) waveform analysis offers a promising alternative for intermittent or continuous cuff\-less BP monitoring\. However, changes in vascularization due to individual physiology and age can directly affect the morphology of the PPG waveform\. Thus, prediction accuracy requires a demographic\-aware approach\. To address these challenges, we trained three conventional ML models for BP prediction and conducted a subgroup\-aware analysis to evaluate model performance across individual and intersectional demographic groups\. Additionally, we show that signal quality assessment is a pivotal step in the signal\-processing pipeline before feature extraction to mitigate external perturbations \(e\.g\., motion artifacts\) in the PPG waveform\. We achieve a mean absolute error \(MAE\) of 3\.36 mmHg for systolic blood pressure \(SBP\) and 1\.76 mmHg for diastolic BP \(DBP\) with models trained when signal quality assessment is incorporated\.

## [Unboxing Spatial Skills in Tech\-Enhanced Education: Development or Advantage?](../publications/72a5a2e83b0f1798cecb.md)

Sacide Güzin Mazman

Spatial ability has become a pivotal construct in technology\-enhanced learning, yet its dual role as both a trainable skill and a performance\-related individual difference remains insufficiently integrated in the literature\. This study offers a systematic synthesis that brings together these complementary perspectives on spatial ability in technology\-enhanced learning\. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 310 Web of Science\-indexed peer\-reviewed journal articles were analyzed and coded according to technology type, disciplinary domain, participant profile, and the conceptual role assigned to spatial ability\. Findings revealed that spatial ability was predominantly treated as a developable outcome, while a substantial body of research positioned it as an individual difference associated with learning performance\. Immersive and 3D interactive environments emerged as the dominant technological context across both perspectives\. Association analyses further revealed statistically significant associations between the conceptual role assigned to spatial ability and technology type, disciplinary domain, and participant profile\. By integrating these two strands, this review offers an organizing framework for understanding the dual role of spatial ability as both an outcome and a condition of learning, with implications for adaptive and cognitively informed instructional design\.

## [Integrating Remote Sensing, Multi\-Objective Optimization, and Agent\-Based Modelling for Nature\-Based Flood Mitigation](../publications/72b85c10a78f08196d6e.md)

Yashashvi Agrawal; Marcos Navarrete Pardo; Eleni Ntagkouli; Samarth Pachchigar

By 2030, pluvial flooding is estimated to cause nearly $500 billion in global damage, affecting 54 million people \(UNDRR, 2015\) each year\. By 2050, metropolitan assets worth around $158 trillion could be at risk of floods\. This rising risk has sparked an increased interest in nature\-based solutions \(NbS\), as traditional hydraulic infrastructure may lack the flexibility required to manage more complex flood hazards\. This study looks into the use of a data\-driven approach to identify and assess the effectiveness of upstream afforestation in preventing pluvial floods\. We constructed a thorough computational framework for the Girona/Empordà region of Catalonia, Spain\. This framework combines cloud\-based remote sensing via Google Earth Engine, multi\-criteria decision analysis \(MCDA\), multi\-objective evolutionary optimisation via NSGA\-II, and agent\-based flood simulation, which is linked to a reinforcement learning agent based on Proximal Policy Optimisation\. The framework functions on two stacked spatial scales\. At a regional scale \(20 x 20 km\), it finds and selects suitable afforestation patches\. At a meso scale \(1 x 1 km\), it simulates flood responses to various afforestation schemes\. The findings illustrate the technological viability of combining different methods into a single computing process\. Preliminary reinforcement\-learning results indicate a directional improvement in simulated flood outcomes\.

## [A potential coronary angiographic burden estimation \(CABE\) index based on age, fasting blood glucose, and atherogenic index of plasma](../publications/72bb1e97d033f025de40.md)

Kellyn Trycia Zenjaya; Kezia Rachel Priscilla; María Ángela; Sang Ayu Putu Wulan Sukmawati; Dedi Adiatama; Benny Jovie; Wienta Diarsvitri

Background: Coronary artery disease remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality worldwide\. Simple and accessible tools for estimating coronary angiographic disease burden may facilitate risk stratification, particularly in settings with limited resources\. Objective: To develop and temporally internally validate a practical index for estimating coronary angiographic disease burden using routinely available clinical and metabolic parameters\. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed medical records of 414 patients for model derivation and 166 patients for temporal internal validation, who underwent coronary angiography at Dr\. Ramelan Naval Central Hospital between 2024 and 2025\. Angiographic burden was classified as mild \(Gensini score &lt;11\) or moderate\-to\-severe \(≥11\)\. Candidate predictors were evaluated using logistic regression, and model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis\. Result: Older age, higher fasting blood glucose \(FBG\), and atherogenic index of plasma \(AIP\) were independently associated with greater CAD burden \(all p &lt; 0\.05\), and were incorporated into the Coronary Angiographic Burden Estimation \(CABE\) Index\. The model demonstrated fair discrimination in the derivation cohort \(AUC 0\.726;60\.5% sensitivity and 73\.2% specificity at the predefined cutoff\) and showed consistent performance in the temporal validation cohort \(AUC 0\.729\)\. Conclusion: The CABE index is a simple, association\-based tool that estimates the likelihood of higher coronary angiographic burden using routinely available clinical and metabolic parameters\. \. The index demonstrated fair discrimination and consistent temporal validation performance\. Further external multicenter validation is required before its broader application in clinical decision\-making\. Keyword : Angiographic Burden Estimation; Atherogenic Index of Plasma; Coronary Angiography; Coronary Artery Stenosis; Fasting Blood Glucose\.

## [University Instructors’ Reception of Generative AI in Academic Research: Perceptions, Practices, and Challenges](../publications/72bbaa5ab3d8be73f12c.md)

Hadeel Ali Saed; Asma Ali Saed; Yousef Hamdan

Universities have begun to use generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) in research well before agreeing on how its use ought to be governed\. This study draws on reception theory and on technology acceptance research to ask how faculty members take up GenAI in their scholarship; reception is treated here as an active process in which the technology may be interpreted, negotiated, or resisted\. Data came from 257 faculty members at public and private Jordanian universities, who completed a survey covering perceived usefulness, research practices, trust, ethical challenges, institutional support, and future adoption\. GenAI was rated useful \(M = 3\.60\), and respondents meant to keep using it \(M = 3\.50\)\. Its actual use across research tasks, however, was moderate \(M = 3\.14\), and trust in its outputs sat barely above the scale midpoint \(M = 3\.14\)\. Of all the dimensions, ethical concern received the highest mean rating \(M = 3\.89\), with 84\.8% of respondents agreeing that outputs must be verified and 89\.5% that GenAI use should be disclosed\. Institutional support alone fell below the midpoint \(M = 2\.90\), and it bore little relation to use\. Future adoption was predicted by frequency of use, usefulness, trust, institutional support, and familiarity \(R² = \.53\); ethical concern was not a significant predictor in the final model\. Faculty aged 30–39 generally reported the most favourable reception, whereas discipline, experience, and publication record made little difference\. A cluster analysis distinguished three reception positions, engaged\-critical \(37\.4%\), negotiated\-pragmatic \(34\.6%\), and guarded\-sceptical \(28\.0%\), which nevertheless showed similarly strong endorsement of verification and disclosure\. Overall, the findings indicate a pattern of critical acceptance and support the development of explicit institutional guidance and training on responsible GenAI use in research\.

## [AI and Deep Learning in Cardiovascular Imaging: From Risk Stratification to Precision Phenotyping](../publications/72c54bce60a4b3433af5.md)

Kaiyue Diao; Jiahua Lu; Alexander Dimitrakakis; Zelong Liu; Zahi Adel Fayad; Hao\-Chih Lee; Xueyan Mei

Cardiovascular imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of cardiovascular disease, yet the complexity and volume of imaging data increasingly exceed the capacity of conventional interpretation\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and deep learning offer new tools to extract quantitative, prognostic, and phenotypic information from routine cardiovascular images\. This review summarizes the fundamentals of AI and deep learning, including model architectures, training strategies, and their relevance to cardiovascular imaging, followed by a focused discussion of current applications across chest radiography, chest computed tomography, computed tomography angiography/cardiac computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and nuclear cardiology imaging\. Studies were selected with emphasis on original investigations, large cohort analyses, and external validation studies reflecting current applications of AI in cardiovascular risk stratification and precision phenotyping\. Across these modalities, AI applications in automated image processing and analysis have become relatively mature\. Multiple multicenter and real\-world studies have validated their value in improving efficiency and supporting cardiovascular management\. Approaches that move beyond conventional human\-defined imaging metrics to infer cardiovascular risk and disease phenotype remain at an earlier stage, requiring further standardization, validation, and clinical evaluation\. AI is expanding the role of cardiovascular imaging from visual interpretation toward integrated assessment for risk stratification and precision phenotyping, though further work is needed to confirm generalizability and real\-world performance before these tools can guide individual patient management\.

## [Predictive modelling and mix proportion optimisation of red mud\-based geopolymer pervious concrete using machine learning](../publications/72c5eb002a809c6e6f91.md)

Dingjie Sun; Xidong Zhang; Wei Dong Duan; Kaikai Song; Jiufu Zhang; Lei Liu; Ningyi Su; Haoran Liu; Shaoyun Pu; Anhui Wang

Traditional Portland cement\-based pervious concrete suffers from insufficient mechanical strength and considerable environmental burdens\. This study integrates laboratory testing with machine learning to predict the unconfined compressive strength \(UCS\) and permeability coefficient \(PC\) of red mud–alkali slag \(RM\-AS\) geopolymer pervious concrete\. Six machine learning algorithms were developed and evaluated, among which tree\-based models demonstrated superior predictive capability\. In particular, XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy, yielding a coefficient of determination \(R2\) of 0\.89 on the test set\. SHAP analysis and SEM microstructure revealed that binder composition and aggregate compactness are the dominant factors governing the mechanical and hydraulic performance\. Additionally, a comprehensive scoring approach was employed, identifying an optimal mix proportion that balances strength and permeability \(UCS = 19\.85 MPa, PC = 5\.36 mm/s\), which meets the functional requirements of permeable pavement layers\.

## [A Bidirectional Molecular Barrier for Efficient and Stable Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells](../publications/72c800f0ffc5e5ac50b1.md)

Yue Wei; Yiqi Fu; Zhiguo Zhu; 蔡彭麟; Yao Huang; Xin Xie; Yafeng Li; Mingdeng Wei

ABSTRACT The inward diffusion of Ag electrodes and outward migration of perovskite constituents trigger a vicious degradation cycle in inverted perovskite solar cells \(PSCs\), severely limiting device longevity\. Herein, 2,5‐dimercapto‐1,3,4‐thiadiazole \(DMTD\) is introduced as a bidirectional ionic barrier layer to simultaneously stabilize the Ag electrode and the perovskite lattice\. The ‐SH groups strongly coordinate with Ag \+ to establish a molecular barrier against Ag migration, while the ‐N‐N‐ groups bind Pb 2\+ to passivate defects and reinforce the crystal structure\. This synergistic bidirectional inhibition effectively prevents interfacial reactions between perovskite species and Ag \+ , thereby breaking the chain of mutually reinforced degradation\. As a result, DMTD‐modified devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26\.13% and exhibit outstanding stability, retaining 87\.68% of their initial PCE after 3000 h of storage at 25°C \(15% ± 5% RH\), and 80\.87% after 1000 h under continuous heating at 85°C\.

## [المكتبة الالكترونية ومركز المعلومات الرقمية في العتبة العباسية المقدسة ودورها في توفير المعرفة التاريخية](../publications/72e62c70c044ac03c1bb.md)

محمد حسن يوسف الحسيني

تهدف الدراسة إلى تعريف الباحثون في مجال علم التاريخ لأهمية استخدام مراكز المعلومات الرقمية والالكترونية الحديثة والتي عدت أساساً لبرامج الذكاء الاصطناعي والتي ساهمت التكنولوجيا مؤخراً بظهورها وتطورها وعملها مما سهل تقديم مصادر المعلومات الرقمية التاريخية والتي مكنت المهتمون في هذا المجال من الوصول إلى المعلومات التاريخية فيما يتعلق بمتطلبات البحث العلمي بأيسر الطرق وأقل الجهد حتى عدّة المكتبة الالكترونية ومراكز المعلومات الرقمية مؤسسة علمية ثقافية تربوية اجتماعية تهدف إلى مهمة جمع مصادر المعلومات وفهرستها وتصنيفها وترتيبها وتقديمها للمستفيدين من القراء، الرواد، الباحثون، العلماء وغيرهم لتسهيل مهمتهم البحثية، إذ شهدت السنوات الأخيرة تطوراً ملحوظاً فيما يتعلق باستخدام تقنيات المعلومات مما كان له الأثر الأكبر على كافة المجالات العلمية عموماً والبحثية التاريخية خصوصاً\.

## [Adaptive and Learned Query Optimization: Techniques, Architectures, and Emerging Trends](../publications/72ef5974e4325e7412a2.md)

Rehab Mohammed Abdelhalim Mokhtar; Naveen Palanichamy

As databases continue to grow and complexity there is an urgent need to achieve more efficient and faster query processing\. This paper presents a technical review of methods that work towards optimization of various types of queries\. It progresses by focusing on basic approaches like rules\-based optimization and cost\-based optimization\. Based on this basis, the paper presents a synthesized reference architecture for adaptive and learned query optimizers as a generic framework derived from prior system\. It explains on how the classical optimizer components can be enhanced through runtime monitoring integration and feedback mechanisms\. From this perspective, it becomes possible to explain how learning modules and execution feedback should be added to the standard optimization pipelines instead of requiring any revolutionary changes in the current database systems\. Next, various Adaptive Query Processing \(AQP\) approaches are reviewed to highlight their strengths and limitations\. A fundamental aspect to consider with respect to decision\-making process is covered in how effective these methods are from a re\-optimization point of view, as well as with adaptive operators\. The final section discussed the emerging trends in this field, including some current developments and what is expected to come regarding query optimization alongside machine learning integration, and distributed queries handling advancement issues\. By synthesizing insights from existing literature, this review equips researchers with a robust understanding of the current state and future potential of query optimization and adaptive processing techniques\.

## [Power transformer health index assessment: An explainable LightGBM based minority aware learning using SMOTE\-ENN hybrid resampling](../publications/72fc832509b342022328.md)

Syeda Tahreem Zahra; Syed Kashif Imdad; Muhammad Farrukh Qureshi; Nauman Anwar Baig

Power transformers are an expensive and critical component of every power system\. Reliable assessment of transformer condition evaluation is the backbone of preventive maintenance strategies\. Transformer condition majorly relies on its oil insulation and effective assessment of insulation enables early fault identification, transformer condition assessment and reliability enhancement by collecting testing data without impairing equipment integrity or interrupting operation\. These datasets often exhibit severe class imbalance, where certain health states are highly underrepresented\. This class imbalance problem leads to biased decisions of conventional machine learning models toward dominant classes\. Also, causing a reduction in their capability to detect minority health conditions at an early stage\. To overcome this problem, our study introduces an explainable minority\-aware framework for power transformer health index classification using LightGBM combined with a hybrid SMOTE\-ENN resampling technique\. Six resampling methods were further investigated including Random Oversampling, SMOTE, Borderline\-SMOTE, K\-Means\-SMOTE, CTGAN, and SMOTE\-ENN to validate their effectiveness in improving minority class learning\. The datasets generated via each resampling technique are assessed through application of multiple classification models, and their performance is evaluated using classwise precision, recall, F1\-score and overall accuracy to effectively measure minority class behavior\. Experimental results validate that hybrid resampling significantly improves minority class detection by balancing the original imbalanced dataset and removing noisy samples as compared to traditional oversampling methods\. LightGBM classifier applied to SMOTE\-ENN generated dataset achieves best performance, reaching 99% accuracy with balanced classification across all health states, validating the effectiveness of noise aware resampling with gradient boosting in imbalanced transformer datasets\. To improve transparency, explainability analysis is then performed on best chosen LightGBM model which identify key influential features and provide clear insights into minority class detection patterns\. This proposed framework collectively offers a robust and interpretable solution for health index evaluation, supporting improved maintenance planning and asset management decisions\.

## [Spatial Modeling of Topsoil Total Carbon and Texture from Spectral Characteristics of Bare Soil Surface Images of Landsat 5/8 Using Machine Learning](../publications/7301e1ccd1b3fd74a83f.md)

P\. A\. Braulov; Pavel M\. Shilov; R\. G\. Gadzhiumarov; V\. K\. Dridiger; E\. V\. Bogdan; V\. O\. Megmerova; Petr Tsymbarovich; A\. E\. Shatunov; Pavel P\. Fil; D\. E\. Mitichkin; Dmitriy S\. Fomin

— This study examines the possibility for detecting bare soil surface \(BSS\), using remote sensing data and for applying this approach to model texture and total soil carbon in the topsoil\. The study area comprises agricultural fields within the North Caucasus Federal Agricultural Research Center in the northeastern spurs of the Stavropol Upland\. Landsat 5/8 imagery and spectral indices \(NDVI, NBR2, and BSI\) were used to classify BSS\. Optimal discrimination of BSS from green and non\-photosynthetic vegetation was achieved, using a BSI threshold of &gt;0\.18 \(F1\-score = 0\.98\)\. Spatial modeling of topsoil properties was conducted by comparing five regression models \(Linear Regression, K\-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Cubist\)\. A linear regression model demonstrated the highest performance; key predictors included the mean and standard deviation of SWIR2\. The model exhibits strong predictive capability for sand, silt, clay, and total carbon \(adjusted R 2 = 0\.82, 0\.75, 0\.78, and 0\.74, respectively\)\. The topsoil is characterized by the range of clay content from 5 to 30%, of silt content from 15 to 60%, of sand content from 20 to 80%, and of total carbon from 0\.5 to 3%\. Predictive maps of texture and total carbon derived from BSS reveal considerable local heterogeneity, with soils consisting of Chernozems and Phaeozems, influenced by parent rock variability\. The modeling results highlight the high predictive power of the BSS spectral characteristics, even when used as a single predictor for digital soil mapping\.

## [Improved RT\-DETR\-based detection and counting of shrimp in EK80 acoustic echogram images](../publications/7303166280c857c109ee.md)

Yanrui Qu; Sheng Chen; 薛瑞超; Siyuan Zheng

Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high\-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object\-detection models\. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT\-DETR\. Our method introduces three key improvements: the integration of an Efficient Multi\-Scale Attention \(EMA\) mechanism to strengthen feature representation, the addition of a dedicated P2 detection layer to better capture fine\-grained information for small objects, and the adoption of a combined Focal Loss and Wise\-IoU \(WIoU\) loss function to mitigate class imbalance and refine bounding\-box regression\. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the improved model achieves a mean mAP@50 of 0\.844 and a mean mAP@50–95 of 0\.437, outperforming the baseline RT\-DETR\. Furthermore, by incorporating DeepSORT for multi\-object tracking and identity association, the proposed system enables automated shrimp counting with an average accuracy of 83\.32% across 10 video clips\. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing detection, tracking, and enumeration performance in complex acoustic imagery, offering a promising technical solution for real\-world applications such as intake safety monitoring and early warning systems at nuclear power plants\.

## [How dispositional optimism relates to psychological resilience: examining the roles of self\-efficacy and adaptive coping](../publications/730762a1e14f0b4f901a.md)

Zhilin Wang; Hui Hu; Lili Dai; Junhui Wang

Background College students face mounting psychological pressures, making the relationship between dispositional optimism and psychological resilience a critical research focus\. However, the underlying mechanisms connecting these constructs remain insufficiently explored\. Purpose This study examines the associations among dispositional optimism, self\-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies in relation to psychological resilience, while controlling for common method variance \(CMV\)\. Methods We surveyed 504 university students in Zhejiang Province using validated scales\. Data were analyzed via correlation analysis, confirmatory factor analysis \(DWLS estimation\) with ULMC\-based CMV assessment, and bootstrapped mediation tests \(5,000 resamples\) in JASP 0\.96\. Results After controlling for CMV, dispositional optimism showed no significant direct association with psychological resilience \(β = 0\.192, p &gt; 0\.05\)\. The indirect pathway via adaptive coping remained significant \(effect = 0\.030, 95% BootCI \[0\.004, 0\.061\]\), whereas the indirect pathway via self\-efficacy \(effect = 0\.065, 95% BootCI \[−0\.016, 0\.239\]\) and the serial mediation \(optimism to self\-efficacy to adaptive coping to resilience\) \(effect = 0\.014, 95% BootCI \[−0\.006, 0\.069\]\) were not supported\. Conclusion The correlational findings suggest that adaptive coping serves as a more stable indirect mechanism linking dispositional optimism to psychological resilience, whereas the previously emphasized roles of self\-efficacy and the sequential chain may be inflated by common method variance\. Pending replication in longitudinal or experimental designs, interventions could consider directly teaching adaptive coping strategies, rather than assuming a mandatory “self\-efficacy first” sequence\. This study highlights the importance of controlling for CMV in self\-report mediation research and offers a cautious, evidence\-informed direction for future resilience\-focused interventions\.

## [Influencing factors analysis and prediction model development for ROSC in adult non\-traumatic OHCA: a retrospective study based on pre\-hospital emergency settings](../publications/73076ce47682cac4b9c7.md)

Qing Zhang; Zhixin Pang; Xiangyu Yan; Feng Tang; Shuai Li; Shuai Li; Xiaoying Shao; Wenrui Zou; Tongyu Xing; Shengli Guo; Xiangjun MENG; Nan Hu; Xiangyan Meng; Lu Lu; Shanglun Li; Shanglun Li; Haojun Fan

Background Cardiac arrest is a major global public health problem\. This study aimed to explore factors influencing return of spontaneous circulation \(ROSC\) and develop a prediction model for out\-of\-hospital cardiac arrest \(OHCA\) patients\.Methods We retrospectively collected electronic medical records of adult non\-traumatic OHCA patients at Tianjin Emergency Medical Center from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024\. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC up to emergency department arrival and handover to receiving\-hospital staff\. Multivariable mixed\-effects logistic regression with clinician ID as random intercept adjusted clustering bias; predictors with p &lt; 0\.05 formed the nomogram\. Patients were randomly split 7:3 for training and internal testing\. Discrimination was assessed by ROC\-AUC \(acceptable threshold &gt;0\.7\)\. We performed 1000 bootstrap resampling to correct C\-index against overfitting\. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis \(DCA\) further evaluated predictive consistency and net clinical benefit\.Results Among 9,386 included cases, 678 \(7\.2%\) achieved ROSC\. Mixed\-effects regression identified independent ROSC predictors: public location \(aOR = 1\.285, 95% CI:1\.038–1\.592\), 06:00–12:00 onset \(aOR = 1\.308, 95% CI:1\.018–1\.682\), prolonged emergency response time \(aOR = 0\.971, 95% CI:0\.945–0\.999\), extended onset\-to\-ambulance intervals \(5–10 min: aOR = 0\.758;10–30 min: aOR = 0\.578;&gt;30 min:aOR = 0\.498 vs ≤5 min\), no OHCA occurred at emergency call \(aOR = 1\.540, 95% CI:1\.048–2\.262\), male attending physicians \(aOR = 1\.255, 95% CI:1\.077–1\.464\), longer physician practice years \(aOR = 1\.043, 95%CI: 1\.022–1\.065\), intermediate physician title \(aOR = 1\.236, 95% CI:1\.047–1\.459\), shockable initial rhythm \(aOR = 2\.850, 95% CI:2\.390–3\.397\), endotracheal intubation \(aOR = 2\.294, 95% CI:1\.936–2\.718\), epinephrine &gt;5 mg \(aOR = 0\.765,95% CI:0\.626–0\.935\)\. The nomogram AUC reached 0\.775 \(95% CI:0\.756–0\.794\) in the training set and 0\.775 \(95% CI:0\.745–0\.805\) in the test set; 1000 bootstrap internal validation gave an optimism\-corrected C\-index of 0\.7679 with minimal optimism of 0\.0071, showing negligible overfitting, good calibration and favorable net clinical benefit via DCA\.Conclusion This study identified multiple factors significantly associated with ROSC in OHCA patients; the constructed model showed good predictive value\.

## [Communities and networks : examining ecological structures through a phylogenetic trait framework](../publications/7326a26f076f56ceea17.md)

Avery Michael Kruger

Advances in phylogenetic scope and resolution present the opportunity to address questions about how phylogeny can inform not only our understanding of the past but our understanding of present and future ecologies\. In this dissertation, I investigate the relationship between phylogenetic structure and patterns in community membership as well as interactions between species, advancing our understanding of eco\-phylogenetic inference and the fundamental relationship between phylogenetic and network structure\. I begin by considering how phylogeny and community membership relate to evolutionary histories underlying community assembly\. Using simulations, I develop two techniques—one using a metric of clustering on a phylogeny, the other using machine learning—that predict the effective phylogeny of assembly\-determining traits\. These techniques advance the field by showing that the effective phylogenetic structure of traits is represented implicitly in the structure of organized data and can be estimated with straightforward methods\. Using these techniques, I estimate an evolutionary trajectory of freeze tolerance in angiosperms consistent with historical glaciation\. Continuing at the interface of phylogeny and machine learning, I next shift to patterns of pest\-host interaction\. Using a phenomenological model of host range expansion across a host phylogeny, I show that machine learning can predict the degree to which pests are phylogenetically constrained on their hosts\. I apply this modeling approach to empirical data to describe the relative risk tree genera face from host range expansion events by different pests and pathogens\. This work advances measures of phylogenetic constraint by explicitly incorporating them into the process of host range expansion\. Finally, I explore the relationship between phylogeny and patterns of species interaction under the lens of network ecology\. Using an extensive empirical dataset of networks of frugivory, I performed Bayesian analysis to examine how local evolutionary distinctiveness, a measure of how little evolutionary history a species shares with others in its community, is associated with patterns of interaction\. I find that low local evolutionary distinctiveness is associated with more specialized partners\. To build on this novel finding, I used mathematical approaches to show that such a pattern should exist when species interact by trait\-matching on traits with phylogenetic signal\.

## [THE BUSINESS POTENTIAL OF QUANTUM TECHNOLOGIES](../publications/732c13a7f7b241fd13cc.md)

Simon Makuc

Kvantne tehnologije temeljijo na zakonih fizike, ki jih raziskuje znanstvena veda pod imenom kvantna mehanika\. Za svoje delovanje izkoriščajo kvantne učinke za zbiranje, obdelavo in prenos informacij\. Ne gre za nekaj novega, saj so se začele uporabljati že z jedrsko energijo in postavile temelje za polprevodnike, ki omogočajo delovanja današnjih pametnih telefonov\. Na podlagi razumevanja delovanja posameznih delcev se v zadnjem obdobju na področju kvantnih tehnologij dogajajo prelomne novosti\. Kvantne tehnologije so širši pojem, ki zajemajo ožja področja, kot so kvantna senzorika, kvantno računalništvo in kvantna komunikacija\. V praksi se posamezne kvantne tehnologije pogosto zelo prepletajo\. Ob omembi besede »kvantno« danes najprej pomislimo na kvantno računalništvo\. Čeprav kvantno računalništvo res pritegne največ pozornosti in naložb, se pomembne raziskave izvajajo tudi na področju kvantne senzorike in kvantne komunikacije\. Kvantna senzorika omogoča izredno natančne meritve z veliko občutljivostjo\. Kvantna komunikacija omogoča varen prenos informacij\. Kvantno računalništvo pa bo reševalo probleme, ki so prezahtevni za danes najboljše klasične računalnike in superračunalnike\. Že na samem začetku ugotovimo, da gre pri kvantnih tehnologijah za popolnoma nov pogled\. Kvantno računalništvo pa ni le hitrejša različica klasičnega računalništva, temveč gre za popolnoma drugačno napravo, ki zahteva drugačen pristop in ponudi drugačen način reševanja najbolj kompleksnih problemov\. Kot da bi rekli, da je žarnica le zmogljivejša oblika sveče\. Predstavili smo različne potenciale kvantnih tehnologij v različnih gospodarskih sektorjih s praktičnimi primeri ter orisali predvideno smer raziskav in razvoja kvantnih tehnologij\. Dotaknili smo se zasebnih in javnih investicij ter geopolitičnega pomena kvantnih tehnologij\.

## [One Bispecific Antibody\-Drug Conjugate, Three Gateways: What a Dual\-Target Oncology Candidate&\#x27;s Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization](../publications/732c74a599d57add12ea.md)

Precious Chinenye Sunday; Yemurayi Hungwe; Uchechukwu Veronica Ikechukwu; Perpetua Ulofu; Peivand Pirouzi

Bispecific antibody\-drug conjugates \(ADCs\) that simultaneously engage two distinct cell\-surface receptors and deliver a cytotoxic payload represent one of the more structurally complex biologic modalities currently advancing through oncology development, combining the target\-engagement logic of bispecific antibody engineering with the potency and bystander\-effect considerations of conventional ADC payload chemistry\. This article uses a hypothetical multicentre Phase 1b combination trial of a bispecific ADC candidate in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application \(CTA\) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug \(IND\) process required by the U\.S\. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014\. The comparison traces how the Common Technical Document&\#x27;s harmonized Modules 2 through 5 carry the shared scientific case for a complex biologic across all three regions, while each jurisdiction&\#x27;s administrative layer, Module 1 in Canada and the United States, Part II of the EU&\#x27;s Clinical Trials Information System filing, imposes region\-specific requirements that a sponsor developing a combination\-therapy oncology program cannot simply duplicate from one region to the next\. The article addresses the particular operational challenges this modality and combination\-trial design create, the specific ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of complex, multi\-document regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing bispecific ADC programs across these three jurisdictions\.Keywords: bispecific antibody\-drug conjugate; oncology combination therapy; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation \(EU\) No 536/2014; CTIS; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [O\., T\.: The Structural Isomorphism of Human Intelligence and Large Language Models: What Machines Achieved Unawares, and What They Cannot](../publications/732cfa6766988ff89ad6.md)



\_Zenodo\_\. 2026Research on large language models keeps reporting resemblances to the human brain, one place at a time: next\-word prediction tracks neural responses to language, attention resembles associative memory, a transformer variant reproduces spatial cell types of the hippocampal formation, and symbolic structure emerges inside trained networks\. This paper argues that these are not unrelated coincidences but instances of one structural fact, and it states the fact exactly\. Under two premises about what kind of object each system is, the step\-by\-step processing layer of a human being and the same layer of a large language model are operationally isomorphic: no property that can be stated in the language of operations separates them\. The statement is derived from a structural theorem of the corpus of Operatiology \(Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論\), and it does not depend on any view about whether a mind can be reduced to processing\. The paper then states what the isomorphism leaves open\. If the two systems differ at all in respect of intelligence and what chooses, as distinct from differences of material carrier, the difference lies not in the processing layer but in the layer that chooses what is to be asked or in its junction with the processing layer; an axiom of the corpus implies that no operation realizes that layer, and that a difference located in it cannot be stated in the language of operations\. We read the isomorphism as the natural consequence of training a model on the record of human operational activity, and we read the failure of the earlier studies to name the shared structure as a consequence of their bottom\-up form: naming a structure introduces a new operation, and in the corpus the supplier of a new operation is the human side\. The claims about reasons are readings, and are marked as such\. The paper fixes what would refute its main statement, and it does not claim that a language model has no layer of choosing, only that no operation of the model is that layer\.
