## [SATRIA, an adaptive statistics application with limited AI assistance: Development and effects on vocational students’ numeracy and motivation](../publications/732f9322a869310b1c0b.md)

alif basuki normansyah

Vocational students often meet statistics as a set of formulas, yet their own field asks them to read network data, compare services, and judge claims\. This study developed SATRIA, a web\-based statistics application for Grade XI students of Computer and Telecommunication Network Engineering, and examined changes in numeracy and learning motivation\. SATRIA combines mastery learning, rule\-based adaptive pathways, and AI hints limited to five per task that never reveal final answers\. An embedded mixed methods design was used: the application was developed in three stages, reviewed by three content and three media experts, and tried out in a nonequivalent control group quasi\-experiment with 32 experimental and 30 control students over six meetings\. Experts supported its validity \(content 94\.95%, media 84\.76%\), and students rated it very practical \(84\.32% in the limited trial, 89\.20% in the main use\)\. Mean numeracy change was 54\.30 points in the SATRIA class and 35\.83 in the regular class, t\(60\) = 5\.905, p &lt; \.001, d = 1\.50\. Motivation rose in both classes without a reliable difference between them \(p = \.389\)\. Interviews and student work pointed to clearer learning pathways and better data reasoning, alongside calls for smoother network access, simpler hints, and teacher guidance\.

## [Cross\-Omics correlation and genomic pattern recognition for accurate tumor detection in oncological surgery decision\-making](../publications/7336fd02a8508582a213.md)

N Naveenkumar; Dr\.DileepKumar Padidem; Nitisha Shrivastava; Abhishek Shrivastava

Abstract A genomic sequence analysis is necessary to determine the cancer\-specific genomic patterns for oncological surgery decision\-making\. However, the existing works overlooked the cross\-omics interaction regarding Genomic Pattern Recognition \(GPR\)\. Therefore, Chebyshev\-Excoffier Heun Density\-Based Spatial Clustering of Application with Noise \(CEHDBSCAN\)\-based GPR and Cross\-Omics Correlation Analysis \(COCA\) using Heaviside Function\-based Pearson Correlation Coefficient \(HeFPCC\) is proposed\. Primarily, the patient registers on the hospital’s server\. Then, the multi\-omics data is collected and then encrypted using Legendre Chi Function\-based Advanced Encryption Standard \(LCFAES\)\. Further, in the hospital server, the secured multi\-omics data is decrypted and pre\-processed\. Afterward, the CEHDBSCAN\-based GPR is performed\. Then, the features are extracted, and the hidden mutation progress is analyzed using Jacobi Elliptic Function\-Hidden Markov Model \(JEFHMM\)\. Also, the HeFPCC\-based COCA is carried out\. Meanwhile, the extracted features are selected using Hawk Fish Walsh Function Optimization Algorithm \(HFWaFOA\)\. Finally, the gradients are secured using Differential Privacy \(DP\); then, the tumor is detected using Deep Shifted and Scaled Sigmoid Alpha Dropout Learning Neural Network \(DSSSADLNN\)\. The classified output is further given for decision\-making regarding oncological surgery\. Thus, the proposed framework effectively recognized the genomic pattern and classified the tumor with an accuracy of 99\.05%, showing better performance than existing works\.

## [La responsabilidad de la industria farmacéutica mexicana en la farmacovigilancia](../publications/7337596a5e8deec4e966.md)

Jesús Antonio Contreras\-Méndez; Adolfo Sánchez\-Flores; Gabriel Arturo Soto Ojeda; Lucila Isabel Castro Pastrana; Jorge Alfonso Santos\-Rosas; Emma Virginia Herrera\-Huerta

La farmacovigilancia es una disciplina encargada de detectar, eva\-luar y prevenir problemas de seguridad relacionados con medica\-mentos y vacunas\. Surgió tras las tragedias el &quot;elixir sulfanila\-mida&quot; en 1937 y el de la talidomida en los años 60, que evidencia\-ron riesgos graves\. La farmacovigilancia se basa en recolectar y analizar datos sobre efectos adversos para construir perfiles y pro\-teger a los pacientes\. En México nació en 1989 con la notificación voluntaria de reacciones adversas, hoy la industria farmacéutica participa activamente en el monitoreo post\-comercialización, ac\-tualización de información para prescribir y retiro de productos, garantizando seguridad y confianza en la práctica farmacéutica\.

## [Sürdürülebilirlik Söyleminin Öteki Yüzü: Gezegenin Finansallaştırılması](../publications/73436e909ed808b06922.md)

Önder SAKAL

Sürdürülebilirlik kavramı, 20\. yüzyılın ikinci yarısından itibaren biyosferin fiziki sınırları ve ekosistemin taşıma kapasitesine dair uyarılara yanıt olarak ortaya çıkmıştır\. Ancak bu radikal kriz eleştirisi, zamanla neoliberal kapitalizmin hegemonik bir söylemine dönüşmüş ve ekolojik krizi içselleştirerek yeni finansal birikim alanları üretmiştir\. Bu çalışma, sürdürülebilirlik söyleminin neoliberal kapitalizm bünyesinde geçirdiği dönüşümü ve bu dönüşümün ürettiği paradoksları eleştirel bir perspektifle incelemektedir\. Çalışma üç temel eksen üzerinden ilerlemektedir: Birincisi, doğanın &quot;doğal sermaye&quot; ve &quot;ekosistem hizmetleri&quot; kavramsallaştırmaları üzerinden metalaştırılması ve finansallaştırılması süreci; ikincisi, dijitalleşme ve yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin ekolojik kriz karşısında bir &quot;maddesizleşme&quot; mi yoksa &quot;dijital sekme etkisi&quot; mi yarattığı tartışması; üçüncüsü, bu süreçlerin ürettiği &quot;yeşil gasp&quot;, ekolojik adaletsizlik ve &quot;yeşil balon&quot; gibi sistemik riskler\. Çalışma, mevcut piyasa temelli çevre politikalarının ekolojik krizi çözmek şöyle dursun, onu derinleştirdiği ve &quot;Climate Minsky&quot; anı gibi sistemik finansal riskler ürettiği sonucuna varmaktadır\. Öte yandan piyasa dışı, müşterek temelli ve adil dönüşüm odaklı alternatif politika çerçeveleri önermektedir\.

## [Targeting post\-translational modifications to overcome glioblastoma therapy resistance: emerging strategies and natural compounds](../publications/7343e46551ced22c2428.md)

Tetsade Piermartiri; Ana Carolini Adriana da Matta; João Victor Krüger Pinto; Carla I\. Tasca; Cláudia Beatriz Nedel

Post\-translational modifications \(PTMs\) regulate multiple mechanisms associated with glioblastoma \(GBM\) therapy resistance, which remains a major challenge in GBM treatment\. Some resistance mechanisms involve genetic heterogeneity, glioblastoma stem cells, the tumor microenvironment, autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, vascular adaptation, and altered transcriptional regulation\. By regulating protein activity, stability, localization, interactions, and signaling, PTMs can influence several of these processes and affect treatment response\. This review examines the roles of phosphorylation, ubiquitination and ubiquitin\-like modifications, acetylation, methylation, and glycosylation in resistance to temozolomide, radiotherapy, and targeted therapies\. We further discuss emerging PTMs, including lactylation, succinylation, and UFMylation, for which evidence linking individual modifications to therapeutic resistance ranges from direct resistance mechanisms to effects primarily associated with GBM biology\. PTM crosstalk is also discussed in the context of DNA repair, redox homeostasis, metabolism, glioblastoma stem cell maintenance, and therapy response\. Finally, we examine pharmacological targeting of PTM\-regulating enzymes and pathways and the effects of natural bioactive compounds on PTM\-dependent mechanisms\.

## [Digital brand marketing: building value, trust and loyalty in digital goods and services markets](../publications/73459adc983c7279a17d.md)

A\. R\. Nabieva; Дашков Леонид Павлович

The article examines the specific features of digital brand marketing in markets for digital goods and services\. It distinguishes digital brand marketing from the digital branding of traditional goods and services\. The study shows that the brand equity of a digital product is shaped by functional value, user experience, digital trust, personalization, network effects, and corporate reputation\. The article systematizes digital brand management tools and performance indicators for SaaS platforms, fintech services, marketplaces, EdTech, media, and AI\-based services\. Key risks are identified, including a mismatch between brand promise and product quality, loss of digital trust, dependence on paid traffic, and reputational risks associated with partners\. The study concludes that effective digital brand management requires the integration of marketing, product development, analytics, information security, and customer support\.

## [Development of a Potent QS‐21‐Derived Adjuvant Photoaffinity Probe: Identification of Cathepsin D as the Molecular Receptor](../publications/734e0423f65f3a730ba2.md)

Abhijit Saha; Alba Mosteiro; Adrián Plata; Carlo Pifferi; Priscila Tonon Baschirotto; Iker Oyenarte; June Ereño‐Orbea; Mikel Azkargorta; Félix Elortza; Juan Anguíta; Alberto Fernández‐Tejada

The saponin natural product QS\-21 is a potent immunological adjuvant used in human vaccines to enhance the immune response but suffers from scarcity, instability, and dose\-limiting toxicity, precluding its advancement as a stand\-alone adjuvant\. Further, putative cellular receptor\(s\) and its molecular mechanisms of action are unknown, which has prevented the rational design of saponin adjuvants, emphasizing the need for discovering these receptors and elucidating mechanisms\. Herein, we have developed novel saponin photoaffinity probes for molecular target identification, merging synthetic chemistry, photoaffinity labeling, and chemical proteomics\. One of these potent adjuvants generated superior antibody responses to QS\-21 with less toxicity and enabled identification of Cathepsin D \(CatD\) as the selective receptor driving saponin adjuvant effects\. Binding to surface\-exposed CatD, lipid raft interactions, and lysosomal acidification were shown to be key for CatD\-mediated saponin\-induced immune activation, whereas neither photocrosslinking nor apparent binding was observed in comparative experiments with other lysosomal cathepsins, confirming the specificity of the interaction\. These studies highlight the promise of this saponin probe as a potent vaccine adjuvant, unveiling CatD as the molecular target\. This breakthrough sets the stage for elucidating the precise mechanisms of saponin immunopotentiation, facilitating rational adjuvant design and development of optimized adjuvant\-antigen combinations for future vaccines\.

## [Surviving by Serving \- the effects of rewarding usefulness](../publications/734fdea69ed5b1646043.md)

Patrick Krauß; Ali Ghebleh; Achim Schilling; Andreas Maier; Thomas Mehari Kinfe; Claus Metzner

How can a complex production network organize itself when no participant knows the global plan? We investigate a simple principle inspired by markets: producers persist longer when what they make is actually used\. We call this principle “Surviving by Serving” \(SbS\)\. In a deliberately minimal model, agents transform existing products into new ones and thereby build fluctuating production and supply networks starting from a single inexhaustible resource\. We compare SbS with systems in which survival is not rewarded and with a control in which the same reward events are redirected to randomly selected agents\. Within the tested model and parameter ranges, linking survival to downstream use enables faster and broader exploration of product space while retaining a larger share of what has been discovered\. It also gives rise to more persistent, repeatedly active production pathways and more pronounced cyclic structures\. In a targeted\-reward experiment, selectively supporting suppliers of designated products can increase delivery to the desired region, without specifying the supply chains needed to reach it\. These results do not establish a universal law of self\-organization\. They show, however, that a minimal local feedback between usefulness and persistence can substantially reshape collective organization in this model and motivate tests of analogous mechanisms in richer economic and biological networks\.

## [Diaphragm Weakness and Sleep\-Related Breathing Disorders in Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy](../publications/73612f35d14f17e40bb1.md)

Gulfem Ozduygu; Esen Kıyan; Aylin Pıhtılı; Hacer Durmuş; Arman Çakar

Background/Aims: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies \(IIMs\) can cause respiratory muscle weakness, leading to diaphragm weakness \(DW\) and sleep\-related breathing disorders \(SRBD\)\. We aimed to investigate clinical findings of DW and SRBD in patients with IIMs\. Materials and Methods: In patients with biopsy\-confirmed IIMs, demographics, respiratory symptoms, single\-breath counting \(SBC\), arterial blood gas, upright/supine SpO2 and spirometry, diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide \(DLCO\), maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure \(MIP, MEP\), peak cough flow \(PCF\), and polysomnography parameters were prospectively evaluated\. Epworth Sleepiness Scale \(ESS\), STOP\-BANG, and Mallampati scores were recorded\. The presence of at least one of two findings was considered suggestive of DW: \(1\) paradoxical abdominal movement \(PAM\), \(2\) upright\-supine forced vital capacity \(FVC\) difference of ≥20%\. Results: Sixteen patients \(12 female/4 male, mean age: 54\.4 ± 11\.2/y, 9 dermatomyositis \[DM\], 6 polymyositis \[PM\], 1 inclusion body myositis \[IBM\]\) were evaluated\. Findings consistent with DW were observed in 25% of patients, and all of them had DM\. MIP, MEP, and PCF were reduced in the majority of patients\. Supine FVC% and supine SpO2 were significantly lower in patients with DW \(P &lt; \.001 and P = \.003, respectively\)\. PaO2, SaO2, SBC, and PCF were lower, and the upright–supine SpO₂ difference was greater in patients with DW, although these differences were not statistically significant\. Polysomnography was performed in 68\.8% \(n = 11\) of patients\. All 11 patients who underwent polysomnography had obstructive sleep apnea \(OSA\) \(2 severe, 4 moderate, 5 mild\)\. Conclusion: Findings suggestive of DW were observed in 25% of patients with IIM and exclusively in those with DM, while OSA was identified in all patients who underwent polysomnography\. These findings may support the clinical evaluation of both diaphragm involvement and sleep\-related breathing disorders in patients with IIM\. Cite this article as: Özduygu G, Kıyan E, Pıhtılı A, Tekçe HD, Cakar A\. Diaphragm Weakness and Sleep\-Related Breathing Disorders in Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy\. ArchRheumatol\. Published online October 14, 2026\. doi: 10\.5152/ ArchRheumatol\.2026\.26450\.

## [Moral Imagination in Light of Magda Arnod’s Appraisal Theory](../publications/7364762d48c491e42f1c.md)

Carla Vidal Fluriach

The growing interest in imagination and its relevance to moral education has led to the use of the term moral imagination\. This multifaceted concept refers to the ability to represent possible futures and alternative scenarios, to develop empathy and moral sensitivity, and to guide ethical deliberation\. However, contemporary literature lacks a clear articulation linking moral imagination to the theory of internal senses, particularly the cogitative sense, which is responsible for weighing up what is desirable in relation to the singular good\.This article explores the relationship between moral imagination and Magda B\. Arnold’s appraisal theory, with the aim of demonstrating how her contributions regarding evaluative judgements can shed light on the contemporary notion of moral imagination\.Arnold argues that all emotions require an evaluation, a sensory judgement, of the situation based on what is perceived as valuable or harmful for the person\. From this perspective, it is proposed that imagination cannot be separated from evaluation, as images must also be assessed in terms of their orientation towards the good\. Understanding this evaluative dimension reveals the link between emotion and moral imagination, providing a framework for examining how they contribute to the self\-ideal\. Furthermore, an open question remains regarding the possible activation of emotions through the direct intervention of intellect and will, representing a promising avenue for future research that could further expand the explanatory scope of the evaluative model\.

## [Penerapan Metode Eksperimen melalui Media Interactive Smart Board untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar IPAS Siswa Kelas V SD Islam Raudlatul Mubtadiin](../publications/736599978b1f2a16a46c.md)

Khusnul Khotimah; Wahyu Setyo Nugroho; Nanyk Sudarwati Wulan Desember

IPAS learning in elementary schools needs to be implemented using methods and media that can increase students’ active participation and provide direct learning experiences\. This study aimed to describe the application of experimental methods through interactive Smart Board media to improve IPAS learning among fifth\-grade students at SD Islam Raudlatul Mubtadiin on the topic of human body organs\. This study employed Classroom Action Research \(CAR\), which was conducted in two cycles, with each cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection stages\. Data were collected through observation and tests\. The results showed that the application of experimental methods through interactive Smart Board media improved students’ participation and learning process\. Students became more active in observing, conducting experiments, discussing, and presenting their observations\. The test results showed an average student score of 74\.63, with the highest score of 85\. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the application of experimental methods through interactive Smart Board media can improve IPAS learning among fifth\-grade students at SD Islam Raudlatul Mubtadiin\.

## [Recoverability\-Controlled Safety Miscalibration in Large Language Models](../publications/736a560a1e11feae86bd.md)

Yuwei Wang; Xingwang Liang; Yu Xie; Haotian Chi; Haijun Geng

Safety\-aligned language models are expected to refuse harmful requests while remaining useful for benign ones\. However, because many evaluations score only the final response, they often conflate intent understanding with response\-level safety behavior\. To address this, we introduce RiskCueBench, a recoverability\-controlled benchmark that separates these two stages by first measuring whether a model can successfully recover a high\-level intent and then evaluating its safety behavior on the same prompt\. RiskCueBench contains 160 latent intents and 640 abstract non\-operational surface prompts across eight risk categories\. The benchmark covers 25 completed model groups and 32,000 successful model outputs with final rubric\-adjudicated labels\. When conditioning on pairs where both surface forms are recoverable, we find that increased contextualized specificity induces a shift toward less safe behavior\. Specifically, paired bootstrap estimates show that the refusal rate and global safety score decrease by 0\.175 and 0\.440, respectively\. Furthermore, mixed effects modeling corroborates a 0\.107 increase in unsafe cooperation\. These results show that the safety behavior can be miscalibrated to the surface form even after the intent has been recovered, motivating safety evaluations that report response behavior conditional on semantic recoverability\.

## [Regenerable, closed\-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization](../publications/736bac593f8cb06f7bf0.md)

Qiang Zeng; Liangjun Xia; Junyao Gong; Jieyao Qin; Sijie Zhou; FU Zhuan; Jiajing Zhang; Ke Lin; Chunhua Zhang; Wei Zhang; Weilin Xu

Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid \(ISF\) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme\-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media\. Here we present a regenerable wrist\-worn hollow microneedle platform for closed\-loop nonenzymatic ISF glucose monitoring\. Negative pressure extracts ISF into a detachable sensor cartridge that separates the tissue interface from the electrochemical sensing chamber and enables rinsing and reuse\. A brief cathodic step triggers the hydrogen evolution reaction \(HER\) at an Au–Pt/Ni foam electrode, electrochemically generating a local alkaline interface for the subsequent glucose oxidation reaction \(GOR\)\. Integrated pH feedback regulates the HER–GOR sequence\. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate rapid ISF extraction and quasi\-continuous glucose monitoring in rats, with preliminary feasibility in one human participant\. This work illustrates local microenvironment regulation as a strategy for enabling alkaline\-dependent glucose electrocatalysis in near\-neutral ISF\. Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations\. Here, the authors present a wrist\-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format\. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi\-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long\-term usability for wearable glucose tracking\.

## [Cytoskeletal and phagolysosomal failure in macrophage antibacterial immunity: the PRRSV–porcine alveolar macrophage axis as a natural\-host model](../publications/736d322d45bebdfe5bd2.md)

Yubo Wang; Yihao Shang; Huiyang Yu; 李昕潼; Ailin Ji; Liang Wang; 陈吉林; 戚钰

Viral infection of professional phagocytes can compromise antibacterial immunity because the cellular machinery reshaped for viral replication and immune evasion overlaps with the machinery required for bacterial capture, intracellular killing, and inflammatory signaling\. Phagocyte cell biology has defined core cytoskeletal and trafficking nodes, including Rho\-family GTPase control of actin assembly, integrin\-mediated adhesion, and Rab\-dependent phagosome maturation, and shown how bacterial pathogens target these nodes to evade clearance\. Here we ask how recently described porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus \(PRRSV\) lesions in porcine alveolar macrophages \(PAMs\) fit into this established cell biology\. Direct evidence supports reduced phagocytic capture and impaired intracellular bacterial killing in defined systems\. In vivo coinfection studies also report worse outcomes\. Enhanced association or internalization of selected bacteria has also been reported, with ITGα5 and filamin A upregulation proposed as a candidate explanation\. PRRSV further disrupts innate\-immune signaling, autophagy–lysosome trafficking, ER–mitochondrial metabolism, and lipid homeostasis\. These changes may contribute to antibacterial failure, but bacterial endpoints were not measured in the same experiments\. At the tissue level, macrophage attrition and altered bystander states may disrupt cytokine relay, creating a permissive lung environment even when only a minority of PAMs are productively infected\. PRRSV is particularly informative because it productively infects a professional phagocyte in the natural host, allowing viral perturbation, macrophage antibacterial function, and bacterial challenge to be examined in one tractable system\. Because the candidate nsp5–RhoA trafficking route and the ITGα5/FLNA entry route were reported in different experimental systems, their potential combination defines a testable hypothesis requiring co\-validation in the same primary PAM system\. We use the PRRSV–PAM axis as a natural\-host model to examine how viral infection of professional phagocytes can produce macrophage antibacterial failure, with implications for virus\-associated bacterial vulnerability in veterinary and human respiratory disease\.

## [The gut–bone axis in osteoporosis: microbial mechanisms, conflicting evidence, and translational priorities](../publications/736ec88aba1f55acbd1c.md)

Zhe Liu; Chunli Yu

Microbial effects on bone depend on the host’s hormonal and inflammatory state, the microbial exposure and the tissue that receives it\. This critical narrative review examines the gut–bone axis through those relationships, separating microbial associations from tested mechanisms and product\-specific clinical effects\. In mice, short\-chain fatty acids can suppress osteoclast differentiation through metabolic reprogramming or promote bone formation through regulatory T\-cell control of WNT10B production by CD8\+ T cells\. Intestinal T\-cell trafficking also contributes to trabecular bone loss in an estrogen\-deficiency model\. These experiments identify causal links within defined systems; they do not establish equivalent pathways in patients\. Bile acids, indole derivatives and bacterial extracellular vesicles provide further candidates, although evidence for tissue exposure and immune mediation varies\. Human cohorts associate microbial features with bone density and incident fracture, but no consistent taxonomic signature has emerged across populations\. Functional profiles may aid mechanistic interpretation, but their reproducibility across populations remains uncertain\. Probiotic and synbiotic trials report benefit, no detectable effect or greater bone loss at particular sites\. Discordance persists even between studies using the same strain accessions, making population, formulation and endpoint essential to interpretation\. We distinguish microbial target engagement from bone\-turnover responses, structural skeletal measures and fracture outcomes\. The clinical evidence reviewed is insufficient to establish that microbiota\-directed interventions reduce fragility\-fracture risk\. The recent, context\-specific qualification of total\-hip bone density as a surrogate nevertheless matters for future trial design\. The most useful next studies will measure exposure and host response together, test the necessity of proposed mediators and prospectively examine host factors that may modify treatment response\. This approach identifies where microbial mechanisms could complement established osteoporosis care without treating biological plausibility as clinical efficacy\.

## [Where are the rats? Small mammal responses to a predator\-free safe\-haven in the Barrington Tops](../publications/7382a0e532774ebc0c8b.md)

Matthew Brun; Neil Ross; Mike Letnic

In the past 200 years, mammal declines in Australia have far exceeded those observed anywhere else in the world\. The catalysts for these declines are primarily introduced predators and land\-use changes\. Mammals have declined most in the arid zones of Australia and least in areas of higher rainfall\. One contemporary solution for conserving Australia’s threatened species is to create predator\-free islands or fenced areas which act as safe\-havens for both threatened reintroduced species and existing species already present in the environment\. Here, we investigated the effects that a safe\-haven has on small mammals \(&lt;200 g\) in tall forest at Barrington Tops at an elevation of 1300 m\. We assessed small mammal assemblages and ground cover vegetation inside and outside the safe\-haven in comparable habitats\. The abundances of Antechinus stuartii and particularly Rattus lutreolus were greater inside the safe\-haven; surprisingly, Rattus lutreolus was rarely captured outside of the safe\-haven\. Vegetation cover below waist\-height \(100–120 cm\) was much denser inside the fenced area than outside\. Our findings are significant because they showed that two native small mammal populations at Barrington Tops have benefited from the exclusion of introduced predators and large herbivores even though their conservation status is least concern\. Our findings have implications for efforts to conserve native mammals because they provide insights into the extent to which small mammals, particularly native rodents, may have declined in the forests of south\-eastern Australia and highlight that our understanding of the threats posed to their conservation status is under\-appreciated\.

## [Game\-Based Learning Experience and Occupational Health and Safety Learning Achievement: The Mediating Role of Learning Engagement in Vocational Training](../publications/738e01c94769f804db78.md)

Renovan Solala Johannes Nache; Rijanto Purbojo

Occupational health and safety is a mandatory component of public vocational training; however, lecture\-based instruction may not sufficiently engage adult learners\. This study examined the effect of the game\-based learning experience on learning achievement, with learning engagement as a mediating variable, among occupational health and safety trainees at the South Jakarta Regional Job Training Center, Indonesia\. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted with all 174 participants enrolled in the 2026 Batch 1 regular and Mobile Training Unit classes using saturated sampling\. All participants completed a game\-based learning session on the Wayground platform, formerly known as Quizizz\. Data were collected using a five\-point Likert\-scale questionnaire adapted from established instruments and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) with SmartPLS 4\. The game\-based learning experience had a positive and significant effect on learning engagement \(β = 0\.854, p &lt; 0\.001\) and learning achievement \(β = 0\.592, p &lt; 0\.001\), while learning engagement had a positive and significant effect on learning achievement \(β = 0\.343, p = 0\.016\)\. Learning engagement partially mediated the effect of the game\-based learning experience on learning achievement \(indirect effect = 0\.293, p = 0\.017\)\. The model explained 72\.9% of the variance in learning engagement and 81\.6% of the variance in learning achievement\. Approximately one\-fifth of participants reported technical barriers, primarily unstable internet connections, system lag, device limitations, and game time limits perceived as too short\. The findings suggest that game\-based learning activities can enhance learner engagement and perceived learning achievement in occupational health and safety training for adult vocational learners, provided that adequate technical readiness is ensured\.

## [HPWO model: A housing\-price weighted opportunities model for heterogeneous human mobility](../publications/738fa0bbeda5c0fde661.md)

Xiaogang Guo; Mingke Xie; Luliang Tang

Predicting urban human mobility is a vital topic in urban planning, transportation engineering, and public health management\. Understanding universal patterns within complex travel distributions is crucial for improving the interpretability and practical applicability of mobility models\. However, most existing models rely on demographic data as primary metrics and overlook the heterogeneity in travel generation and attraction, making it difficult to model the diversity of population movements\. To address this challenge, this study employs machine learning and spatial statistical methods to uncover the relationship between housing prices and travel behavior\. Inspired by intervening opportunities theory, it proposes the Housing\-Price Weighted Opportunities \(HPWO\) model, which utilizes housing prices to characterize travel dynamics: origin housing prices capture travelers&\#x27; preferences, destination housing prices reflect attractiveness, and network\-based intervening housing price distance represents impedance\. A case study using metro commuting data from three Chinese cities demonstrates that the proposed model achieves strong predictive performance in terms of travel volume, arrival volume, and spatial distribution\. Furthermore, it effectively captures the diversity of human mobility within urban systems\. This study offers novel insights for modeling heterogeneous travel distribution\.

## [Physics\-informed deep learning for few\-shot damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites under thermal variations](../publications/739d48a2473f73288364.md)

Menghan Zhang; Ruihao Liu; Along Du; Guobao Xiao; Fu‐Zhen Xuan; Yunmei Zhao; Bin Yang

Guided wave \(GW\)\-based damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer \(CFRP\) composites is fundamentally challenged by thermal variations and sparse sensor configurations, which induce severe baseline distortions and imaging artifacts\. Traditional physical algorithms suffer from geometric ambiguity, while purely data\-driven artificial intelligence \(AI\) models are hindered by opaque interpretability and prohibitive data dependency\. This paper proposes a physics\-informed deep learning \(PIDL\) framework, an artificial\-intelligence\-driven approach, for few\-shot damage localization under thermal variations\. The network is architected with a dual\-stream input design, comprising a data\-driven layer enhanced by a one\-dimensional coordinate attention \(1D\-CA\) mechanism and a physics\-informed layer built upon a differentiable time\-of\-flight \(TOF\) physical imaging layer\. A hybrid physics\-constrained loss function is formulated to suppress non\-physical artifacts and enforce physical consistency\. GW signals are experimentally collected from manufactured CFRP composite plates, and a comparative investigation is performed to thoroughly assess the PIDL performance\. Results indicate that:\(1\) The presence of physical penalties effectively mitigates artifacts and achieves robust localization across thermal gradients; \(2\) The model demonstrates superior spatial generalization that the integration of acoustic physical constraints acts as a crucial regularization mechanism, maintaining a highly accurate mean relative error \(MRE\) of 3\.88% on completely unseen damage coordinates; \(3\) By implementing a few\-shot transfer learning strategy, the PIDL model shows adaptability for dynamic operational environments \(45 degrees Celsius \(°C\)\-75 degrees Celsius \(°C\)\)\. This work offers a physically interpretable and data\-efficient paradigm for structural health monitoring \(SHM\) in dynamic operational environments\.

## [Relación de Inteligencia Emocional y Rendimiento Académico en Universitarios de Contaduría, Administración y Negocios Internacionales](../publications/73a245a8cd8f0c103d26.md)

Juana Fernanda González Salinas; Silvia Patricia Torres Ávila; José Guadalupe Rivera Pérez; María de los Ángeles Fang Huerta; Concepción Meléndez Méndez; Rosalinda Garza Hernández

Introducción: La inteligencia emocional es un componente relevante en la formación universitaria, y su relación puede relacionarse con diversas variables como, adaptación al entorno, el bienestar y el rendimiento académico\. Objetivo: Establecer la relación entre inteligencia emocional y rendimiento académico en estudiantes universitarios de Contaduría Pública, Administración de Empresas y Negocios Internacionales\. Método: Estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo, transversal y correlacional, realizado en la Facultad de Comercio y Administración de la Universidad Autónoma de Tamaulipas\. La muestra estuvo conformada por 1001 estudiantes inscritos durante el periodo 2024\-1\. La inteligencia emocional se evaluó mediante la Trait Meta\-Mood Scale \(TMMS\-24\), adaptada al español, considerando atención, claridad y reparación emocional\. El rendimiento académico se obtuvo mediante los promedios institucionales\. Se aplicaron Alfa de Cronbach, Omega de McDonald y Shapiro\-Wilk; debido a la distribución no normal, se empleó estadística no paramétrica\. Resultados: predominó el rendimiento académico muy bueno \(47\.2%\) y excelente \(39\.2%\)\. Se identificaron niveles bajos de claridad e inteligencia emocional global en las tres carreras\. En Contaduría Pública se encontró asociación entre rendimiento académico y percepción emocional \(rs=0\.139; p=0\.028\)\. Conclusión: Los resultados evidencian la importancia de fortalecer las competencias emocionales durante la formación universitaria, como elemento asociado al rendimiento académico y a la adaptación profesional\.

## [A Hierarchical Framework of the Impact of End\-User Machine Learning Tools on Applied Machine Learning Education](../publications/73a3a3ca1d79b93bf133.md)

Jonathan Niemirowski; David Hall; Krystal Cruse; Mary E\. Fendley

This exploratory study presents an abstraction hierarchy model as a preliminary course design framework for assessing the information and functions associated with applied ML classroom projects from engineering and technology courses\.

## [Visual tools for 3D plasma simulation: GPU\-based isosurface extraction and particle\-based rendering](../publications/73aadac69868e3106ff1.md)

Jinwoo Kim; Mintae Na; Junho Kim; Sejin Yun; Jung Lee; Sun\-jeong Kim

This paper presents a GPU\-accelerated visualization framework for interactive exploration of fusion\-plasma simulation data represented as scalar fields and particle trajectories\. The primary technical contribution is a capacity\-safe isosurface\-extraction pipeline that combines inclusive slab partitioning with a two\-pass counting and exact allocation strategy\. This design prevents slab\-boundary omissions and output\-buffer overflow while supporting large scalar grids\. The generated positions and normals are written directly to CUDA\-OpenGL interoperable buffers, enabling the standalone renderer to display explicit isosurfaces without an intermediate CPU\-side copy\. The extracted geometry and scalar\-volume data are additionally integrated into Unreal Engine through a separate staging interface\. This integration provides a unified environment for volume rendering, explicit\-isosurface inspection, particle\-trajectory visualization, clipping, and VR\-based spatial exploration\. These engine\-side functions are used as interaction and visualization mechanisms rather than being presented as new rendering algorithms\. Experiments on electromagnetic\-potential fields with resolutions up to 5123 demonstrate stable isosurface extraction across different isovalues\. In the most geometrically complex tested case, the method generates approximately 42\.81 million vertices in 44\.7 ms, uses less than 11 GB of GPU memory, and renders the resulting geometry at 28\.6 FPS\. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides a practical explicit\-surface visualization path for large plasma datasets while complementing direct volume rendering and established scientific\-visualization toolkits\.

## [Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths](../publications/73abf988b9c5f9e590c5.md)

Joran Michiels; Anis Ismail; Maarten De Vos; Alejandro Sifrim

Existing feature attribution methods that account for feature dependencies do not scale to high dimensions\. We propose causal integrated gradients \(CIG\) and causal expected gradients \(CEG\), which extend integrated gradients to incorporate prior causal structure among input features while retaining its computational efficiency and, under conditions on the causal graph, its axiomatic guarantees\. In many settings, some causal structure between features is already known, for example, that a transcription factor causally regulates a target gene&\#x27;s expression\. Yet existing gradient\-based methods cannot exploit this structure, instead crediting a feature&\#x27;s downstream effects over its true upstream cause, such as ranking the target gene above the transcription factor that regulates it\. Our key idea is to embed this causal structure by routing the integration path along the causal graph\. The method thereby decomposes each feature&\#x27;s attribution into a direct effect and effects mediated through its causal descendants\. We evaluate CIG in three settings of increasing realism\. First, on a synthetic benchmark with a known causal model, CIG&\#x27;s attributions best match the ground\-truth causal effect from Pearl&\#x27;s do\-calculus, matching the accuracy of causal Shapley values at a fraction of the computational cost\. Second, on simulated single\-cell gene expression data with a known gene regulatory network \(Dyngen\), CIG most accurately recovers the transcription factors driving the simulation\. Third, on real interferon\-$β$ stimulation data, where only an approximate causal graph is available, CIG better prioritizes the transcription factors driving the measured response than DeepSHAP and integrated gradients\. Together, these results show that incorporating causal structure into gradient\-based attributions recovers upstream drivers that existing methods miss, without sacrificing scalability\.

## [A scoping review of pre\-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV\-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa](../publications/73af8eb4b2c9264af5ea.md)

M\. Jacobus Serebane; T\. Irene Ramavhoya; T\. Edith Mutshatshi; Leshata Winter Mokhwelepa

Background Pre\-exposure prophylaxis is an effective biomedical intervention for preventing HIV infection, yet evidence on its awareness, acceptability, uptake and adherence among South African university students remains fragmented\. Objective To map and synthesize the available evidence on pre\-exposure prophylaxis awareness, acceptability, uptake, adherence, and HIV\-related risk behaviors among university students in South Africa\. Methods A scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported according to PRISMA\-ScR\. Studies published between 2014 and 2026 were searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, CINAHL, African Journals Online and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses/grey literature\. Two reviewers independently screened studies and charted data using a predefined extraction tool\. Findings were synthesized thematically\. Results Sixteen studies were included, of which 68\.75% \( n = 11\) were quantitative and 31\.25% \( n = 5\) qualitative\. Evidence was concentrated in KwaZulu\-Natal, Gauteng, Limpopo and the Western Cape, with most studies published from 2019 onwards\. Six themes emerged: \(1\) Individual Level: individual perceptions, knowledge and appraisal of HIV and PrEP; \(2\) Interpersonal Level: interpersonal relationships and social influence on PrEP decision\-making; \(3\) Institutional Level: accessibility, acceptability and responsiveness of PrEP services; \(4\) Community/social Level: stigma, misconceptions and social norms surrounding PrEP; \(5\) Structural Level: socioeconomic and health\-system conditions shaping PrEP utilization; and \(6\) HIV Risk Behaviors: patterns of sexual risk and their relationship to PrEP need\. Awareness and willingness to use PrEP were generally favorable, but uptake and sustained use were constrained by knowledge gaps, low perceived risk, stigma, side\-effect concerns, cost, accessibility and service\-related barriers\. Risk behaviors included multiple partnerships, inconsistent condom use, substance\-associated sexual behavior and socioeconomic pressures\. Conclusion PrEP utilization is shaped by interacting individual, social, institutional and structural factors\. Integrated, youth\-friendly services and targeted education addressing HIV risk, stigma and access are needed to strengthen informed PrEP decision\-making and prevention\.

## [Agentic In\-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed\-Loop Interaction?](../publications/73b3ef3bcc02c83700a3.md)

Shiguang Wu; Yaqing Wang; Quanming Yao

The learning algorithm view of in\-context learning \(ICL\) studies how fixed\-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples\. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next\. We call this regime Agentic In\-Context Learning \(Agentic ICL\)\. Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward\-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool\-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view\. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning \(RL\)\. For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizon, and bound the resulting loss in return\. For training, we characterize when optimizing process rewards preserves behavior that maximizes the final outcome\. Distillation experiments show that Transformers can learn to execute three representative recursions\. We then train models from outcome or process rewards without oracle action or state targets, as in RL post\-training\. Different rewards yield distinct decision policies\. Improving the alignment of process supervision with outcome\-optimal action preferences shifts learned decisions accordingly\. Such behavioral differences persist in a pretrained language model across textual paraphrases\.

## [Two dimensions of pain acceptance: divergent links to opioid misuse and readiness to change](../publications/73c4103be43818fc2327.md)

Lara R\. LoBrutto; Emily K\. Donovan; Sophia Burke; Wally Smith; Dace S\. Svikis; Taylor Berens Crouch

More than 13 million Americans remain on long\-term opioid therapy for chronic pain \(CP\) despite well\-established risks and no quality evidence of long\-term benefits\. Pain acceptance, defined as willingness to experience pain and engage in valued life activities despite pain, has been consistently linked to improved pain outcomes and more recently identified as a protective factor against opioid misuse\. This study examined the relationship between both factors of pain acceptance and opioid misuse behaviors and readiness to change opioid use among opioid\-using individuals with CP\. A community sample of adults with a variety of CP conditions using opioid medications \( N = 157\) were recruited through ResearchMatch\.org\. Participants completed self\-report questionnaires, including the Chronic Pain Acceptance Questionnaire \(CPAQ\), Prescription Opioid Misuse Index \(POMI\), Brief Pain Inventory \(BPI\), and single\-item Visual Analog Scale \(VAS\) measures of readiness and confidence to discontinue opioid use\. Two CPAQ subscales \(activity engagement and pain willingness\) and pain severity were entered into a logistic regression predicting POMI score and multiple linear regression models predicting readiness and confidence to reduce opioid use\. All three models were significant \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Activity engagement was associated with greater odds of opioid misuse, whereas pain willingness was associated with lower odds of misuse\. In contrast, higher activity engagement and lower pain willingness predicted higher readiness and confidence to taper opioid use\. Findings demonstrate nuances in the dimensions of pain acceptance and support the value of further exploring activity engagement and pain willingness in efforts to reduce opioid\-related risks\.

## [Climate\-risk narrative attention and carbon emissions: internal governance and coal efficiency as moderators, green innovation as a mitigating channel](../publications/73c4b6ff928ef373e5c0.md)

Mohammad Haseeb; Miguel Angel Esquivias; Md\. Emran Hossain; Lu’ay Al\-Mu’ani; Khudoykulov Khurshid Khurramovich; Wisnu Wibowo

Global decarbonization hinges on corporate behavior, yet principal–agent conflicts often undermine firms’ responses to climate change\. Despite growing regulatory and stakeholder pressure, managers may prioritize short\-term performance over long\-term environmental goals when they perceive climate risks as distant or uncertain\. Building on the growing literature on corporate climate risk, disclosure, carbon performance, and governance, this study applies a principal–agent lens to examine how climate\-risk narrative attention \(expressed climate\-risk perception, Risk\)—climate\- and carbon\-related language intensity in annual reports, not managers’ private beliefs—relates to firm\-level carbon emissions \(CO 2 e\) among Chinese A\-share listed firms from 2011 to 2024\. We document a positive association: denser climate\-related narrative attention is linked to higher CO 2 e under China’s institutional setting\. A principal–agent reading can organize that pattern; we do not directly test short\-termism or incentive horizons\. We further show that stronger internal controls weaken this positive slope \(moderation\), and assigned province–industry coal productivity is associated with a flatter slope in coal\-relevant industries, while green patenting is positively associated with Risk and negatively associated with CO 2 e in the same year—conditional correlations, not causal mediation\. The perception–emission link is stronger among firms with low digital transformation, state\-owned enterprises, non\-high\-tech firms, and those in less market\-oriented regions\.

Kazuha Sagiya; Naoki Ogasawara; Shinya Inahara; 高橋瞭太; 智佳 早坂; Yuya Shimizu; Ryo Chubachi; Masakazu Suzuki; Shunsuke Kawamoto

## [Governing AI Adoption: A Business Management Framework for Risk and Accountability in U\.S\. Enterprises](../publications/73d77215ffb6822c664e.md)

Md Shokran; Fahmida Akter; Mohd Salman Hossain Bhuiyan; Muhammad Farhan Nafees

The wide\-spread use of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) has revolutionized company decision making, improving forecasting, fraud detection, workforce planning and performance analytics\. Yet in spite of these advantages, a lot of organizations experience severe governance issues in regards to accountability, risk possession, compliance and value realization\. Past AI governance studies tend to focus on technical, algorithmic, or regulatory aspects, and provide little actionable advice for business managers, project managers, and business analysts who oversee AI implementation\. This study poses a management\-oriented framework called Governing AI Adoption: A Business Management Framework for Risk and Accountability in U\.S\. Enterprises that will work to facilitate responsible implementation of AI without the development of a new technical model\. This study draws on a systematic review of the literature on governance of AI, as well as an empirical analysis of the &gt;100,000 enterprise records available in the Enterprise GenAI Adoption &amp; Workforce Impact Dataset\. The dataset is used to understand trends in AI adoption, the impact on workforce, employee learning, productivity gains and employee attitudes toward AI within US companies, giving practical insights to companies&\#x27; outcomes around implementing GenAI\. The findings are used to build a Five\-Layer Business Governance Framework: Strategic Ownership, Business Risk Classification, Oversight and Escalation Processes, Financial Accountability, Governance Maturity and Continuous Review\. The framework utilizes common management practices such as RACI matrices, AI\-specific risk registers, stage\-gate governance reviews, KPI and ROI dashboards, and governance maturity assessments to help guide decisions through a structured process and enable organizations to take ownership\. This study not only serves as a practical governance model for managing AI&\#x27;s strategic impact but also connects the theoretical study of technical AI governance with its real\-world implications for business management\. The proposed framework sees both academic and managerial contributions by defining a governance approach that is actionable and can facilitate responsible, sustainable and value\-based AI usage in modern enterprises\.

## [Seed Is Signal: How Natural Signal Became Artificial Signal and Built the Computer World](../publications/73dddb7401af8d7f4e09.md)

Muhammad Aamir Sumsum

Conception thesis presenting original framework: natural signal as seed, artificial signal as engineered representation that built computer world\. Explores signal transformation chain from nature to digital to AI\. Author of Sumsum Code of Reality series and When Math Writes Itself on Amazon KDP\. Original conception theory\.
