## [Evaluating Machine Learning Affinity Prediction Methods on Novel Lead Optimization Data: A 15‐PGDH Case Study](../publications/73e3073912893a71f0ea.md)

Alexander Rich; Leela S\. Dodda; Daniel J\. Price

Recent machine learning \(ML\) methods for protein–ligand affinity prediction, such as Boltz‐2 and AEV‐PLIG, have been reported to approach free energy perturbation \(FEP\) accuracy on well‐known benchmarks\. Even short of that accuracy, ML‐based potency models that fall between FEP and common docking scoring functions in accuracy and speed offer clear potential value\. Here, we report a case study using recently disclosed data from four related ligand series targeting 15‐hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase \(15‐PGDH\)\. We evaluate each ML method&\#x27;s predictive accuracy with a focus on when it could be used to influence synthetic priorities\. AEV‐PLIG performed poorly across most series, and adding literature 15‐PGDH inhibitors to its training did not improve performance\. Boltz‐2 performed well on series most similar to published inhibitors in its training, achieving accurate cofolding \(median ligand RMSD ≤0\.81 Å\) and rank order\. However, for a series exploring a new region of the binding pocket, Boltz‐2 sometimes generated less accurate poses and predicted all ligands in the series to be less potent than a published exemplar, despite experimental potency gains of up to 500x\. These results highlight both the promise in well‐characterized chemical space and limitations in the novel regions where computational guidance is most needed\.

## [Machine learning reduces questionnaire items while maintaining reliability and validity](../publications/73e449e274b3a218d346.md)

Xuanfeng Li; Yuejing Zhai; Yiping Li; Chitin Hon

Traditional long questionnaires often suffer from respondent fatigue, leading to decreased completion rates and compromised data quality\. This study introduces a novel algorithmic item\-reduction methodology, named NNAQ, designed to streamline high\-dimensional survey instruments while strictly preserving both downstream classification capabilities and psychometric construct validity\. Operating as a structured case study, the proposed multi\-tiered framework strategically orchestrates linear filters, non\-linear tree\-embedded layers, and information\-theoretic criteria\. This hybrid architecture allows different mathematical paradigms to cross\-validate and error\-correct each other, successfully overcoming the limitations of traditional single\-stage dimension reduction methods\. This study evaluated the framework empirically using an expanded field dataset collected from 1,022 citizens\. The experimental results demonstrate that the original 96\-item questionnaire can be reduced to a parsimonious 34\-item instrument, representing a 64\.58% reduction in questionnaire length\. Downstream evaluation via machine learning classifiers indicates that the predictive accuracy loss is kept under 5 percent, while comprehensive confirmatory factor analysis confirms that the shortened scale yields superior parsimonious fit indices and stable internal reliability\. Furthermore, rigorous bootstrapping resampling and benchmarking experiments against alternative reduction methods validate the exceptional structural stability and empirical superiority of our pipeline\. Overall, this research provides a robust, data\-efficient, and scalability\-tested framework for human\-centered digital assessment, effectively mitigating respondent fatigue while securing high\-fidelity data quality\.

## [Positive error\-handling in TGfU\-based basketball instruction: effects on tactical decision\-making and the role of perceived classroom psychological safety](../publications/73ef5d12f0716765b0d5.md)

Shen Fan

Background Basketball learning involves rapid decisions and visible mistakes that may carry interpersonal risk\. This study examined whether positive error\-handling within Teaching Games for Understanding \(TGfU\) improved tactical decision\-making and whether improvements were associated with changes in perceived classroom psychological safety\. Methods Sixty students \(30 male and 30 female\) were individually randomized within gender strata before formation of two instructional classes, with one class per condition \( n = 30 each\)\. The same teacher delivered TGfU with positive error\-handling \(PEH\) or neutral error\-handling \(NEH\) over eight weeks\. Tactical decision\-making was assessed through standardized 3\-on\-3 games at pretest \(T0\), posttest \(T1\), and three\-week retention \(T2\); psychological safety was assessed at T0 and T1\. Passing, dribbling/driving, and shooting decisions were coded using the focused BALPAI rubric\. Results Exploratory student\-level analyses showed a condition × time interaction for decision\-making, F \(1\.583, 91\.821\) = 9\.89, p &lt; 0\.001, ηp 2 = 0\.146\. PEH increased from M = 1\.951 \(SD = 0\.202\) at T0 to 2\.304 \(0\.258\) at T1 and 2\.295 \(0\.279\) at T2; NEH increased from 1\.902 \(0\.179\) to 2\.114 \(0\.251\) and 2\.087 \(0\.291\)\. Psychological safety also showed a condition × time interaction, F \(1, 58\) = 11\.07, p = 0\.002, ηp 2 = 0\.160\. PEH increased by 0\.462 points, whereas the NEH increase of 0\.129 points was not statistically significant\. An exploratory within\-subject mediation analysis in PEH yielded a model\-implied indirect effect of ab = 0\.160, 95% bootstrap CI \[0\.100, 0\.221\]\. Conclusion The PEH class showed larger observed gains within the common TGfU curriculum, and increases in psychological safety covaried with decision\-making improvements\. These concurrent changes suggest a possible explanatory role for psychological safety but do not establish temporal or causal mediation\. With one instructional class per condition, classroom\-specific influences could not be separated from the condition effect, and inferential statistics were not adjusted for within\-class dependence\. Future studies should include multiple classes per condition, account for within\-class dependence, and assess psychological safety before subsequent decision\-making outcomes to examine the proposed explanatory process\.

## [KI\-kompasset: Et strategisk verktøy for å navigere KI\-implementering](../publications/73fd0d62f6460a0145a2.md)

Joel Wenæs Berge; Dan\-Richard Knudsen

Når KI bygges inn i beslutningssystemer kan det forsterke gode valg, men også skalere konsekvensene av dårlige\. Organisasjoner behandler ofte KI\-implementering som et teknisk problem, men det er i stor grad et strategisk spørsmål om verdiforslag og ansvarsfordeling\. Hvilke mål skal KI optimaliseres mot, og hvilke beslutninger bør vi ikke delegere bort? I denne artikkelen presenteres KI\-kompasset, et verktøy som definerer fire idealtypiske roller for KI i ulike beslutningsprosesser\. Ledere må først diagnostisere beslutningstypen, deretter velge KI\-rolle\. Kompasset hjelper ledere med diagnose slik at KI\-satsninger underbygger i stedet for undergraver organisasjonens egen strategi og dens kunders opplevde verdiforslag\. ENGLISH ABSTRACT The AI ​​Compass: A Strategic Tool for Navigating AI Implementation Integrated into decision systems, AI can amplify both good and bad decision\-making\. Organizations often treat AI implementation as a technical issue, yet it is largely a strategic question of value proposition and accountability\. Which goals should AI optimize, and which decisions should not be delegated? We present the AI Compass, which defines four ideal\-typical roles for AI in decision processes\. Managers must first diagnose the decision type, then choose AI&\#x27;s role\. The compass supports this diagnosis so that AI initiatives reinforce rather than undermine the organization&\#x27;s strategy and its customers&\#x27; perceived value proposition\.

## [The Modern Face of Depression: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/740230adbe38c655cbc3.md)

Nidhi Sharma

Depression is one of most widespread disabling and one of most important global mental health problems among the main causes of disability, affecting more than 332 million people worldwide\. The incidence has dramatically increased, especially among youths, who showed a clinically elevated symptom range, and who were in their environment stressed by the COVID\-19 pandemic and consequently were around 25\.2% more depressed\. Depression is not just related to mental health, but also cardiovascular disease, immunological deficit and suicide – finally the biggest killer of the young adult population \(15\-29 years\)\. In addition to the depression and apathy symptoms, numerous individuals with depression or apathy will have more irritability, numbness, brain fog, notification fatigue, and sleep difficulties due to tech\-neglect, just to name a few\. Mechanistically, it&\#x27;s now understood that depression involves dysfunction in multiple systems such as neuroinflammation \(elevated blood markers of inflammation like C\-reactive protein \[CRP\], interleukin \[IL\] 6, and tumor necrosis factor \[TNF\] α\), dysfunction of the HPA\-axis, dysfunction of the fronto\-limbic circuit, and a disrupted circadian rhythm\. Therefore, the informal workers face a more high risk of depression symptoms, 27% more likely than the formal workers in LMICs\. With available effective treatments ranging from pharmaceutical, from psychosocial to neuromodulatory, over 75% of people who are affected in low to middle income countries do not receive treatment partly due to any combination of stigma, and lack of resources\. Innovation in recent approaches, such as digital biomarkers, app\-based cognitive behavioral therapy \(CBT\), ketamine\-esketamine, closedloop neurostimulation, and others is making it apparent once again that novel methods for directly intervening with precision are being born\. This paper draws together the latest global statistics, common symptom domains, possible origins, and emerging interventions for digital\-age depression, aiming to promote a multidisciplinary approach that integrates psychology, behavioural factors, digital and biological treatments to combat the emerging and escalating worldwide burden of digital\-age depression\.

## [FUTURE OF LEGAL TECH](../publications/741f23fe3fb0c53b8c61.md)

Priyanka Kiran Khawale

A fresh headline after every few months declares that artificial intelligence is about to replace lawyers but the story especially in India isn&\#x27;t of replacement but adaptability\. In India, where the courts are infamous for their overburdened pending cases, judges outnumbered and resistance to change, the statutory notification of Digital Personal Data Protection Rules is quietly forcing the legal industry to modernize faster with help of technology\. Legal Tech is the combination of technology with legal services from digitally signing contracts to formulating systems that streamline trials\. Driven by advancement of technology and generative AI, the shift in client&\#x27;s expectations and a surge to access justice is the unfolding reality in which the future of legal tech is no longer a far\-sighted vision but a step closer to massive technological evolution\.

## [Metal Mutfak Eşyaları İmalatı Sektöründe Yapay Zekâ Hazırlığı, Güvenilir Yapay Zekâ ve Algılanan İşletme Verimliliği: Mühendis Deneyimlerine Dayalı Nitel Bir Araştırma](../publications/741f6e7ba500072f44ec.md)

Alaeddin Koska

Bu araştırma, metal mutfak eşyaları imalatında çalışan mühendislerin yapay zekâ kullanım deneyimlerini yapay zekâ hazırlığı ve güvenilir yapay zekâ bağlamında incelemekte; işletme verimliliğine ilişkin algılanan katkılara odaklanmaktadır\. Veriler, 30 mühendisin eşzamansız olarak yanıtladığı yarı yapılandırılmış yazılı açık uçlu form aracılığıyla toplanmış ve nitel içerik analiziyle desteklenen tematik analizle çözümlenmiştir\. Bulgular, genel amaçlı/üretken yapay zekânın raporlama, metin düzenleme ve özetlemede; süreç odaklı uygulamaların ise üretim planlama, kalite, bakım, enerji, stok ve tasarımda deneyim ya da beklenti düzeyinde yer aldığını göstermektedir\. Katılımcılar zaman tasarrufu, karar desteği, kalite, hata/fire, koordinasyon ve müşteri memnuniyetiyle ilişkili katkılar bildirmiştir\. Bu değerlendirmeler doğrulanmış performans sonuçları değil, öz bildirime dayalı algılanan etkilerdir\. Veri güvenliği, hatalı çıktı, altyapı, maliyet, uzman personel eksikliği ve direnç öne çıkan engellerdir\. Katılımcı anlatıları, algılanan verimlilik katkısını örgütsel hazırlık, veri kalitesi, güvenilir kullanım ve insan denetimiyle ilişkilendirmektedir\. Metal mutfak eşyaları imalatında faaliyet gösteren işletmeler için yapay zekâ hazırlığının değerlendirilmesi ve sınırlı kapsamlı uygulamaların güvenli, insan denetimli pilotlarla sınanması önerilmektedir\.

## [Implementasi Undang\-Undang di Masa Konstitusi Hukum dalam Menghadapi Tantangan dan Peluang di Indonesia](../publications/741fbec148b59bba7bd7.md)

Muhammad Iqbal Arinanda

In the context of a rule of law, laws act as the main instrument for achieving justice, order and social welfare\. This research aims to analyze the effectiveness of implementing laws in Indonesia, identify the obstacles faced, as well as opportunities that can be exploited within the legal constitutional framework\. Using normative and empirical approaches, this research evaluates various aspects, including coordination between state institutions, regulatory quality, and public participation in the legislative process\. The research results show that, despite serious efforts in drafting and implementing laws, challenges such as legal inconsistencies, corruption, and lack of effective law enforcement remain major obstacles\. However, the digital era and bureaucratic reform provide great opportunities to improve the legislative system and legal implementation through increasing transparency, accountability and community involvement\. In conclusion, to optimize the role of laws within the legal constitutional framework, continuous reform is needed that involves various stakeholders in order to face challenges and utilize existing opportunities effectively\.

## [AI can persuade people to take political actions](../publications/7423ac69acac912e0972.md)

Kobi Hackenburg; Luke Hewitt; Catharina Wagner; Christopher Summerfield; Ben M Tappin

There is substantial concern about the ability of advanced AI to influence people&\#x27;s behavior\. A rapidly growing body of research has found that AI can produce large persuasive effects on people&\#x27;s attitudes, but whether AI can persuade people to take consequential real\-world actions has remained unclear\. In two large preregistered experiments \(\[Formula: see text\] responses from 14,779 people\), we used conversational AI models to persuade participants on a range of attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including signing real petitions and donating money to charity\. We found sizable AI persuasion effects on these behavioral outcomes \(e\.g\. \[Formula: see text\]19\.7 percentage points on petition signing\)\. However, we observed no evidence of a correlation between AI persuasion effects on attitudes and effects on behavior\. Moreover, we replicated prior findings that information provision drove effects on attitudes, but found no such evidence for our behavioral outcomes\. In a test of eight behavioral persuasion strategies, the strategy focused on information provision produced the smallest behavioral effect, though differences among the eight were small\. Taken together, these results suggest that previous findings relying on attitudinal outcomes may generalize poorly to behavior, and therefore risk substantially mischaracterizing the real\-world behavioral impact of AI persuasion\.

## [Administrative Law Innovation And Discretionary Protocols During Public Health Crises](../publications/742b7c11878b65834144.md)

Atthayya Tabittha Bilbiina; Sri Suhartati Pasaribu; Tri Paskah Nainggolan; Yohana Christine Napitupulu; Dinaya Aulya Salsa; Vironika Anivyya Syavitri

General Background National emergencies require rapid governmental intervention to ensure population protection and stability\. Specific Background During the recent multidimensional crisis, state apparatus utilized the freies ermessen concept to overcome legislative voids\. Knowledge Gap Current academic discourse primarily examines institutional powers, yet rarely evaluates the juridical transformation of internal directives into societal mandates\. Aims This study examines the structural trajectory of national governance and analyzes the specific implementation of executive mandates during emergency periods\. Results Utilizing normative legal literature analysis, findings reveal that officials extensively employed executive authority to formulate pseudo\-legislation, primarily through Circular Letters\. However, the untethered execution of these beleidsregel instruments generated uncertainty, regulatory overlapping, and potential financial accountability impunity\. Novelty This investigation specifically addresses the juridical shift wherein strictly internal guidelines were improperly utilized as instruments of societal constraint during emergency governance\. Implications Strengthening integrated oversight mechanisms alongside the stringent application of Good Corporate Governance principles remains paramount to preventing unconstitutional governance\. Highlights State officials utilized freies ermessen to bypass legislative voids rapidly\. Internal directives were improperly transformed into pseudo\-legislation regulating broad behaviors\. Untethered executive authority threatens constitutional certainty and creates financial accountability risks\. Keywords State Administration; Freies Ermessen; Pseudo Legislation; Good Corporate Governance; Emergency Management

## [A predefined sulphur\-handling transcriptional programme is associated with colorectal cancer molecular subtypes](../publications/742c2af0e3abb2928718.md)

Shaheryar Shafi; Arslan Hamid; Jiao Yang; Xiaoxia Cheng; Minxuan Sun

Background Colorectal cancer \(CRC\) exhibits substantial metabolic and transcriptomic heterogeneity, but the relationship between sulphur\-handling transcriptional programmes and consensus molecular subtypes \(CMS\) remains incompletely resolved\. Methods We analysed a predefined 14\-gene sulphur\-handling panel across The Cancer Genome Atlas colon and rectal adenocarcinoma cohorts \(TCGA\-COAD/READ\) and six independent HG\-U133 validation cohorts \( n = 1,337 tumours\)\. Analytical workflows integrated differential expression comparing tumours with adjacent\-normal mucosa, CMS association modelling, random\-effects meta\-analysis, adjustment for three orthogonal tumour\-purity estimators \(ESTIMATE, consensus purity estimates, and ABSOLUTE\), reference\-based single\-cell deconvolution with independent cross\-atlas verification, and direction\-aware therapeutic triage\. Results Colorectal tumours demonstrated branch\-specific transcriptional alterations, marked by coordinated downregulation of sulphur oxidation and clearance genes \( SQOR , ETHE1 , TST \) and of the cysteine\-catabolism genes CDO1 and CTH , and selective upregulation of SLC7A11 and AHCY , whereas CBS was not significantly altered\. The composite programme score differed across CMS subtypes and was consistently lower in mesenchymal CMS4 tumours than in non\-CMS4 tumours across all discovery and validation series\. This association remained statistically detectable after adjustment for three global tumour\-purity metrics\. The programme score showed no statistically detectable independent association with overall, recurrence\-free, or disease\-free survival\. Single\-cell deconvolution supported expression across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments\. Direction\-aware therapeutic triage prioritised SLC7A11/xCT inhibition as an exploratory candidate for preclinical testing\. Conclusion Sulphur\-handling transcriptional architecture is reproducibly linked to CRC molecular taxonomy and is not fully explained by measured tumour purity variation, providing a computational framework for future functional and compartment\-resolved investigation of sulphur metabolism in stratified CRC populations\.

## [Digital Transformation and Employee Engagement in Healthcare Organizations: The Role of Digital Capability and Innovation](../publications/7436edb03ade25ac2faa.md)

Mst Shahinur Begum; Md Saiful Islam Bhuiyan; Tamanna Akter; Sayema Afroz Eva; Rajib Kumar Malakar

Purpose: Healthcare organizations are undergoing sustained digital transformation, yet the workforce\-level mechanisms through which this transformation translates into employee engagement remain theoretically underdeveloped\. This paper develops a conceptual framework explaining how digital transformation shapes employee engagement among healthcare professionals through the dual pathways of perceived digital capability and innovative work behavior\. Design/methodology/approach: This is a conceptual paper\. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, the Job Demands\-Resources \(JD\-R\) model, and the componential theory of organizational innovation, the paper synthesizes literature on digital transformation, employee engagement, and innovative work behavior in healthcare settings to propose an integrated model and a set of formal, testable propositions\. The paper is positioned as a companion piece to a related framework addressing workplace stress, psychological safety, and well\-being in the same healthcare workforce population, together constituting a cohort\-based conceptual research pair\. Findings: The proposed framework positions perceived digital capability as a job resource that both directly predicts engagement and indirectly predicts it through innovative work behavior, with organizational innovation climate moderating the strength of this relationship\. Technostress is identified as a countervailing job demand that can attenuate the otherwise positive digital capability\-engagement relationship, reconciling mixed findings in the empirical digital\-health literature\. Research limitations/implications: As a conceptual contribution, the framework and its propositions have not been empirically tested; the paper proposes a survey\-based validation agenda using the same healthcare professional cohort addressed in the companion well\-being paper\. Practical implications: The framework offers healthcare managers a diagnostic basis for sequencing digital transformation initiatives with workforce capability\-building and innovation\-climate investment, rather than treating technology rollout and engagement outcomes as independent\. Originality/value: The paper contributes a dual\-pathway, moderated\-mediation framework specific to the healthcare context, integrating digital capability and innovation climate as joint explanatory mechanisms linking digital transformation to engagement, an integration not yet made explicit in the existing healthcare management literature\.

## [Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi\-condition comparative study](../publications/7439549816ae6250fd8d.md)

Kübra Aykaç; Osman Çubuk; Osman Oguz Demir; Young June Choe; Soichiro Kawata; Kamila Maria Ludwikowska; Mike Yat Wah Kwan; Malik Aydin; Yasemin Özsürekçi

BACKGROUND: Evaluating how appropriate current large language models \(LLMs\) respond to common pediatric infectious disease \(PID\) questions is important for understanding their potential role in education and clinical support\. Therefore, we evaluated and compared the clinical quality of answers produced by different LLMs when given professionally written, clinician\-style case descriptions, using a purpose\-built multi\-domain evaluation tool\. METHODS: Three different LLMs, including DeepSeek\-V3\.2\-Exp, ChatGPT\-5, and Gemini 2\.5 Flash, were investigated using 12 relevant PID scenarios\. Each scenario included five open\-ended questions: etiology, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment options, and complications\. Two PID specialists independently reviewed all responses using a Likert scoring tool\. RESULTS: All three models received high overall scores\. ChatGPT\-5 achieved perfect domain scores \(10\.0\), whereas DeepSeek\-V3\.2\-Exp showed similarly strong results, with only minor reductions in diagnostics \(9\.83\) and treatment \(9\.92\)\. Gemini 2\.5 Flash demonstrated higher variability, particularly in treatment \(8\.83\) and diagnostics \(9\.75\), while matching the other models in clinical findings and complications \(10\.0\) and scoring 9\.83 in etiology\. However, there were no statistically significant differences across models in domain\-level comparisons \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. In addition, model\-level analyses similarly demonstrated high accuracy \(6\.0; 5\.98; 5\.85\), completeness \(3\.0; 2\.97; 2\.87\), and safety \(1\.0; 1\.0; 0\.97\) for ChatGPT\-5, DeepSeek\-V3\.2\-Exp, and Gemini 2\.5 Flash, respectively \(accuracy: p = 0\.074; completeness: p = 0\.066; safety: p = 0\.14\)\. CONCLUSION: Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert\-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early\-stage clinical reasoning\. However, their optimal use remains within clinician\-supervised workflows, where AI\-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment\. IMPACT: Current large language models \(LLMs\) show consistently high\-quality performance across pediatric infectious disease scenarios, with no significant differences between models\. Our study adds a structured, multi\-domain comparison using clinician\-style cases and expert evaluation, providing detailed insights into accuracy, completeness, and safety\. The findings support the use of LLMs in medical education and early clinical reasoning, while highlighting their role as clinician\-supervised tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment\. The results demonstrate the reliability of LLMs in organizing clinical information and identifying key diagnostic and management elements in standardized scenarios\.

## [To Vernaculate A Verb for the Living Self and the One Body of Humanity](../publications/743b83c3ef6e8a28b5e6.md)

Nasser Hajjaj; Nasser Hajjaj

This article argues that English needs, and now has, a verb for an act it previously had no word for: the affirmation by a person or people of its own living self, beginning with its language\. The form &quot;vernaculate&quot; is attested in late nineteenth\-century American English only in a thin sense \(to call something by its popular name; to use vernacular language\)\. Vernacularism \(Arabic al\-Maḥallaniyyah, المحلانية\) gives the verb a new theoretical sense: self\-affirmation, starting from language understood as the human operating system \(ManOS\), and resistance to hegemony and symbolic violence\. The article distinguishes vernaculation from decolonization, vernacularization and localization; relates it to Bourdieu&\#x27;s notion of symbolic violence and to the protection of human thought in the age of artificial intelligence; and develops the image of humanity as a single body in which no member is shamed by another, drawing on Islamic, Christian and Persian sources while noting the hierarchical misuse of the same image\. It names the internal danger of closure and calls on the scholars of every language to find a native term for the concept, as Arabic has done with maḥlana / maḥlanah \(محلن / محلنة\), rather than borrowing the English word\. This record documents the use of the English verb &quot;vernaculate&quot; in the sense defined by the author within the paradigm of Vernacularism \(المحلانية\)\.

## [The Use of Artificial Intelligence for Managing Emerging Risks in Green Finance: A Literature Review on Financial Institutions](../publications/7444a38c59128b52ce4f.md)

Claresta Gabriel Pasaribu; Franciskus Antonius Alijoyo

This study aims to analyze the role of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in managing emerging risks within the green finance sector through a systematic literature review approach\. The growing importance of green finance in supporting sustainable development has been accompanied by the emergence of new and complex risks, including greenwashing, regulatory uncertainty, renewable energy project volatility, and reputational risk faced by financial institutions\. These risks are often difficult to predict and manage using traditional risk management frameworks due to their dynamic nature and limited historical data\. To address this issue, this study adopts the PRISMA 2020 framework, complemented by the SPAR\-4\-SLR and TCCM models, to systematically review and synthesize recent academic literature published between 2020 and 2025\. The findings indicate that AI plays a significant role in enhancing the effectiveness of risk management in green finance by enabling large\-scale data analysis, identifying complex and non\-linear risk patterns, and improving the accuracy and timeliness of risk prediction\. AI applications, such as machine learning and predictive analytics, are particularly effective in detecting greenwashing practices, supporting regulatory compliance, and strengthening sustainable investment decision\-making\. However, the implementation of AI in managing emerging risks in green finance still faces several challenges\. Key obstacles include limited data availability and quality, potential algorithmic bias, and the absence of clear regulatory frameworks governing the use of AI in sustainable finance\. Despite these challenges, the study concludes that AI represents a strategic and promising solution for strengthening sustainable risk governance\. This research contributes to the existing literature by providing a comprehensive overview of current trends, challenges, and opportunities related to AI\-driven risk management in green finance, particularly in the context of developing economies\.

## [Análise de conceitos Lean Office em uma empresa de projetos de Engenharia em Sergipe](../publications/74508a67e5ae2b338926.md)

Luana de Jesus Souza; Victor Mateus Santos de Oliveira; Débora de Gois Santos

A busca por eficiência e competitividade em ambientes administrativos, onde o fluxo de valor é imaterial, impulsionou a adaptação dos princípios da Produção Enxuta para o conceito de Lean Office\. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar a manifestação das práticas enxutas em uma empresa de projetos de engenharia localizada em Aracaju\-SE, buscando identificar perdas e propor melhorias para a otimização de processos\. A pesquisa foi conduzida mediante uma abordagem exploratória\-descritiva, iniciando\-se com uma análise bibliométrica para embasar a fundamentação teórica, seguida de um estudo de caso qualitativo, com coleta de dados por dois procedimentos complementares: análise documental e observação direta participante, com a categorização dos achados baseada nas sete perdas adaptadas para escritórios\. Os resultados evidenciaram um cenário híbrido: a coexistência de boas práticas, como a centralização da comunicação em sistemas integrados e o uso de gestão visual, que mitigaram perdas por transporte e processamento excessivo; em contrapartida, foram diagnosticadas ineficiências persistentes, especificamente a superprodução de informações, materializadas como excessos de e\-mails e a espera por dados externos\. Conclui\-se que, embora a empresa adote soluções pontuais eficazes, a implementação sistêmica do Mapeamento do Fluxo de Valor \(MFV\) é necessária para transitar de um fluxo empurrado para um fluxo puxado, garantindo maior eficiência operacional\.

## [Associations Between Daily EMA of Emotional Exhaustion and Monthly Burnout Symptoms During Work Reintegration: Longitudinal Multilevel Study](../publications/745fe490a1be2f66bd69.md)

Lea Berkemeier; Wim Kamphuis; Hilbrand K\. E\. Oldenhuis; Rudolf M\. Verdaasdonk; Julia E\.W\.C\. van Gemert‐Pijnen

Abstract Background Burnout is increasingly conceptualized as comprising both stable, slowly changing features and more dynamic, fluctuating features, with emotional exhaustion widely regarded as one of burnout’s core components\. Traditionally, burnout has been assessed using retrospective self\-report questionnaires, such as the Burnout Assessment Tool \(BAT\), administered at sporadic intervals\. In contrast, ecological momentary assessment \(EMA\) enables high\-frequency assessment of daily experiences while reducing recall bias\. However, it is not well understood how EMA\-based measures fluctuate and develop longitudinally within individuals or how they relate to retrospective burnout measures\. Objective This paper examined the relationship between 30\-day aggregates of daily EMA\-assessed emotional exhaustion, specifically the within\-person mean level and variability \(SD\), and monthly burnout symptoms measured with the BAT\. Methods Eighteen participants undergoing work reintegration after stress\- or burnout\-related sick leave completed daily EMAs of emotional exhaustion \(N=3157\) and monthly BAT questionnaires over 6 months \(N=94\)\. For each monthly BAT assessment, EMA data from the preceding 30 days were aggregated into within\-person mean and SD values\. Linear mixed\-effects models with random intercepts and time effects were fitted separately for each BAT subscale\. Additionally, intraclass correlation coefficients \(ICCs\) were calculated to quantify the proportion of variance attributable to between\-person differences\. Results ICCs indicated that a large proportion of variance in the BAT subscales was attributable to between\-person differences, whereas daily EMA emotional exhaustion showed relatively greater within\-person variability\. Significant time\-related changes were observed for the BAT subscales of Cognitive Impairment, Mental Distance, and Emotional Impairment\. Within\-person increases in the EMA mean of emotional exhaustion were significantly associated with higher scores on BAT Exhaustion \( β =0\.073; P =\.001\) and BAT Cognitive Impairment \( β =0\.041; P =\.04\)\. EMA\-based variability \(SD\) and between\-person mean levels were not significantly associated with any BAT subscale\. Conditional R 2 values were high \(0\.667\-0\.777\), whereas marginal R 2 values were modest \(0\.056\-0\.121\)\. Consistent with the ICC findings, these results suggest that most explained variance in BAT scores reflects between\-person differences and time\-related changes, with EMA\-derived predictors accounting for only a limited additional proportion of explained variance\. Conclusions EMA\-based aggregates showed partial correspondence with monthly burnout scores\. Within\-person increases in mean daily emotional exhaustion were associated with higher subsequent scores on the BAT Exhaustion and Cognitive Impairment subscales, but EMA\-based variability was not associated with any BAT subscale\. Together with the ICC results, these findings suggest that EMA\-based aggregates of emotional exhaustion can reflect short\-term fluctuations and longer\-term changes in symptom severity of exhaustion and cognitive impairment\. Retrospective questionnaires remain useful for global symptom assessment or diagnoses at specific time points but appear less well suited for tracking within\-person changes and supporting personalization\. These results highlight the importance of aligning the choice of assessment with temporal and clinical goals\.

## [Artificial Intelligence and Financial Tail Risks](../publications/746598c338a41f4ebc96.md)

Javier Ojea\-Ferreiro; A\. Ugolini; Juan C\. Reboredo

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has a double\-edged relationship with financial stability: it may improve efficiency and risk management, while also creating new vulnerabilities and amplification channels\. This paper studies whether market\-perceived exposure to AI is reflected in the tails of financial\-sector returns, and whether this relationship depends on macroeconomic conditions\. We develop a framework that decomposes financial\-sector tail outcomes across contemporaneous AI and macroeconomic scenarios, and identifies whether the AI\-related episodes are primarily associated with extreme gains or losses\. Using daily equity returns for financial sectors in Canada, the United States, Europe, the United Kingdom, and China, we document substantial heterogeneity\. Financial\-sector\-specific scenarios dominate tail outcomes across markets, while the contribution of AI\-related scenarios to return asymmetry differs substantially across countries\. AI\-sector scenarios contribute to downside asymmetry in Europe, China, and especially the United Kingdom, but make only a limited contribution in Canada and have the smallest tail weights in the United States\. China is the only market exhibiting positive average skewness, driven by the financial and systemic scenarios rather than by AI\-related outcomes\. Overall, AI\-related market movements are neither uniformly stabilizing nor destabilizing; their financial\-stability interpretation depends on the market considered and on whether AI\-sector tail events occur in isolation or jointly with broader macroeconomic movements\.

## [Task\-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits](../publications/7466a626537fe0a82e35.md)

Felix Frohnert; Adrián Pérez\-Salinas; Sebastian Lange; Marcus Schwaebisch; Evert van Nieuwenburg; Vedran Dunjko

Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task\-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood\. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task\-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed\. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit&\#x27;s hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample\-dependent information\. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding\. We examine this connection in a classification task inspired by synthetic aperture radar, where acquisition geometry determines a query for classifying unfocused spectral patches before image formation\. Across small\-scale spectral and radar\-like tasks, aligned queries improve learning from limited data over parameter\-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries\. These results provide a route from known spectral task structure to the design and validation of inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits\.

## [Human\-in\-the\-loop large language model framework for identification of cutaneous immune\-related adverse events](../publications/74718a8cf183b7d8b361.md)

Charles Lu; Olivia Burke; Debby Cheng; Adam Kashlan; Caitlyn Duffy; Zeyun Lu; Lirit Fuksman; Jin Ning Tian; Andrew Sedlack; Priya Katyal; Eudora Lee; Ralina Karagenova; Chuck Lin; Kun‐Hsing Yu; Nicole LeBoeuf; Alexander Gusev; Yevgeniy R\. Semenov

This study evaluated a retrieval\-augmented, multi\-agent large language model \(LLM\)–driven, human\-in\-the\-loop framework for detecting cutaneous immune\-related adverse events \(cirAEs\) from clinical notes\. Compared with the unassisted manual\-review group, the LLM\-assisted group demonstrated higher accuracy \(F1 = 0\.88 vs 0\.77\) and inter\-rater agreement measured by Cohen’s κ \( κ = 0\.82 vs 0\.50\), and reported an approximately one\-third shorter average review time\. ## [Pulneo: Prototipo móvil gamificado con detección acústica de ac\-tividad respiratoria para fisioterapia domiciliaria](../publications/7475e69a47db8db61fdb.md)

María Gabriela Viñansaca Cabrera; David Fernando Valladarez Muñoz

La fisioterapia respiratoria domiciliaria requiere repetición y retroalimentación, pero muchas sesiones se realizan sin supervisión directa\. Este artículo presenta Pulneo, un prototipo móvil gamificado que detecta localmente la actividad respiratoria mediante señales acústicas y la traduce en biorretroalimentación visual durante ejercicios guiados\. El modelo se entrenó con 69 634 ventanas balanceadas: 34 817 de actividad respiratoria de 1061 sujetos sanos de Coswara y 34 817 negativas de 5 608 archivos de UrbanSound8K, con una partición 70/15/15 por grupos, sin solapamiento de sujetos ni de archivos\. En 10 347 ventanas de prueba, el modelo TensorFlow Lite INT8 alcanzó 97,64 % de accuracy, 98,09 % de precisión, 97,18 % de recall, F1 de 97,63 % y ROC\-AUC de 99,65 %\. La cuantización redujo el modelo de 88 488 a 31 600 bytes \(64,29 %\) y mantuvo 99,55 % de concordancia con TFLite FP32\. La aplicación interpreta la salida como P\(respiración\) y aplica un umbral calibrado en validación \(P ≥ 0,29\)\. Pulneo no distingue inspiración de exhalación ni ha sido validado clínicamente; los resultados respaldan su funcionamiento técnico, no su eficacia terapéutica\. Un autor fisioterapeuta con maestría en terapia respiratoria realizó una revisión conceptual interna para delimitar el uso previsto, la interpretación de la biorretroalimentación y los requisitos de seguridad para futuras evaluaciones\.

## [EVALUATION OF ANTIANXIETY ACTIVITY OF DELONIX REGIA LEAVES EXTRACT ON SWISS ALBINO MICE](../publications/747ee0d7b4fe4dbbbaa8.md)



Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent psychiatric illnesses worldwide and continue to pose a significant public health challenge\.The present study investigated the anxiolytic potential of the ethanolic leaf extract of Delonix regia using validated experimental models in Swiss albino mice\.The extract was prepared by the maceration method and subjected to preliminary phytochemical analysis, which revealed the presence of flavonoids, alkaloids, tannins, glycosides, and phenolic compounds\.Its antioxidant activity was evaluated in vitro using the 2,2\-diphenyl\-1\-picrylhydrazyl \(DPPH\) free radical scavenging assay\.The anxiolytic effect was assessed in vivo using the Elevated Plus Maze \(EPM\) and Actophotometer tests following oral administration of the extract at doses of 200 and 400 mg/kg\.Diazepam \(1 mg/kg\) was employed as the standard reference drug\.The ethanolic extract exhibited a dose\-dependent anxiolytic response, with the 400 mg/kg dose producing greater behavioural improvement than the 200 mg/kg dose\.Although its efficacy was lower than that of diazepam, the extract significantly improved anxiety\-related behavioural parameters compared with the control group\.In addition, the extract demonstrated appreciable antioxidant activity in the DPPH assay, suggesting that its anxiolytic effect may be associated, at least in part, with its antioxidant properties\.The observed pharmacological activity is likely attributable to the synergistic action of the bioactive phytoconstituents identified during preliminary screening\.Overall, the findings provide scientific evidence supporting the traditional use of Delonix regia as a medicinal plant for the management of anxiety\.The study highlights the potential of the ethanolic leaf extract as a promising natural source of anxiolytic compounds with a favorable safety profile

## [ПРОГНОЗУВАННЯ ЗАЛИШКОВОГО РЕСУРСУ ПІДШИПНИКОВИХ ВУЗЛІВ МОБІЛЬНИХ МАШИН НА ОСНОВІ ВИЯВЛЕННЯ ПОЧАТКУ ДЕГРАДАЦІЇ ТА ПРОТОКОЛУ ОЦІНЮВАННЯ](../publications/7484655dc608980184b0.md)

Oleksandr Matviienko; Віктор Аулін; Andrii Hrynkiv

The paper addresses the problem of building the prognostic loop of an intelligent maintenance system for bearing units of mobile machinery using run\-to\-failure test data\. Unlike diagnostic benchmarks with artificially seeded faults, run\-to\-failure trajectories expose the entire life of a unit, from run\-in to natural failure\. They therefore allow the validation of prognostic rather than purely classification methods\. Four components of the methodology are proposed and experimentally verified on twelve natural degradation trajectories of the public IMS bearing dataset: four complete failure trajectories and eight censored ones\. The first component of the methodology is an integral technical condition index \(health index\)\. It is constructed as the first principal component of fifteen snapshot features normalized to the baseline period of each trajectory\. The trendability of the index is higher for failed bearings than for censored ones \(0\.654 versus 0\.493, Mann–Whitney p = 0\.055\)\. However, it is not a universal indicator, because both false trends of healthy units \(up to 0\.737\) and a failure without any trend \(0\.296\) are documented\. For this reason the index serves as an input to onset detectors rather than as a stand\-alone decision criterion\. The second component is a quorum ensemble of three heterogeneous degradation onset detectors: a robust MAD threshold, an EWMA control chart and an isolation forest\. Each of them is confirmed by five consecutive snapshots against the self\-healing effect\. The ensemble detects the onset in three of four trajectories with lead times of 72–623 hours\. This is sufficient to schedule the replacement outside the seasonal peak period and, in the best case, to order spare parts without urgent logistics\. The k\-out\-of\-N quorum rule turns detector disagreement on non\-monotonic trajectories into an adjustable trade\-off between early warning and false alarms\. The third component is a defect\-type identification rule based on matched scoring of the harmonic comb of bearing characteristic frequencies in the envelope spectrum\. It yields three correct diagnoses out of four versus one out of four for the dominant\-peak rule\. Moreover, the diagnosis becomes readable almost simultaneously with the detected onset\. The fourth component is an honest object\-level evaluation protocol for remaining useful life regression \(leave\-one\-bearing\-out\)\. Its comparison with the common random snapshot split quantifies the data leakage caused by temporal autocorrelation of a trajectory as a 2\.5\-fold understatement of the prediction error \(RMSE 21\.5 versus 53\.8 hours\)\. The same object\-level requirement is also formulated for the calibration of conformal prediction intervals\. A principal limitation of single\-channel vibration monitoring is documented separately, namely a failure with no vibration manifestation in the available channel\. It is translated into architectural requirements of channel and modality redundancy\. The results extend the model selection methodology and the integrated diagnostic pipeline proposed in the authors&\#x27; previous works with a prognostic loop of condition\-based maintenance\.

## [QANDLI DIABETGA CHALINGAN SHAXSLARGA PSIXOLOGIK XIZMAT KO‘RSATISH MEXANIZMLARINI TAKOMILLASHTIRISHNING ILMIY\-NAZARIY VA AMALIY ASOSLARI](../publications/748b3fc6bc072478673e.md)

This article examines the scientific, theoretical, methodological, and organizational foundations for improving psychological support mechanisms for people living with diabetes mellitus\. Drawing on scientific literature, it systematizes factors influencing emotional well\-being, diabetes\-specific distress, treatment motivation, cognitive appraisal of Ta’limda istiqbolli izlanishlar \- xalqaro ilmiy\-metodik jurnal № 9/2026 ISSN: 3060\-527X illness, and social adaptation\. A comparative analysis is conducted using data from the International Diabetes Federation, the American Diabetes Association&\#x27;s 2026 Standards of Care, studies on diabetes distress, and the relevant legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan\. Based on the theoretical synthesis, a five\-stage integrative psychological support model is proposed, incorporating psychological screening, assessment of individual needs, psychological interventions, social collaboration, and dynamic monitoring\.
