## [Quantum\-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations](../publications/74921d5c081ad98d8790.md)

Rafael Florencio Díaz; Julio Guerrero García; Elvira Romera Gutiérrez

Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood\. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit\. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter\-shift rule\. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks\. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon\. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration\. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models\.

## [BRAF V600E\-POZITIV SOLİD ŞIŞLƏRDƏ DABRAFENIB: REZISTENTLIK, KLINIK TƏTBIQLƏR VƏ DƏRMAN ÇATDIRILMA STRATEGIYALARI](../publications/749788055d6aaf9d5c01.md)

Fatemeh Dodangeh

Dabrafenib, xüsusilə trametinib ilə kombinasiyada, BRAF V600E\-pozitiv bir sıra solid şişlərin müalicəsində artıq təsdiqlənmiş hədəflənmiş terapiyadır\. Bununla belə, müalicəyə cavabın dərəcəsi və davamlılığı şiş növündən asılı olaraq əhəmiyyətli dərəcədə dəyişir\. Bu icmalda dabrafenib əsaslı terapiyanın molekulyar əsasları, klinik tətbiqləri, rezistentlik mexanizmləri, farmakokinetik məhdudiyyətləri və inkişaf etməkdə olan dərman çatdırılma strategiyaları ümumiləşdirilir\. Müalicənin nəticəsinə yalnız BRAF V600E statusu deyil, həmçinin şişin mənşəyi, yanaşı mövcud olan genomik dəyişikliklər, reseptor tirozin kinazalarının əks\-əlaqə mexanizmləri, mikroətraf mühit siqnalları və dərmanın ayrı\-ayrı lezyonlarda ekspozisiyası təsir göstərir\. Rezistentlik MAPK yolunun yenidən aktivləşməsi, PI3K/AKT alternativ siqnal ötürülməsi, hüceyrə plastikliyi, şiş heterogenliyi, stromal qoruyucu təsirlər və farmakoloji cəhətdən kifayət qədər ekspozisiyanın olmaması vasitəsilə inkişaf edir\. Dabrafenibin effektivliyi pH\-dan asılı həllolma, qida qəbuluna həssas sorulma, CYP vasitəçiliyi ilə metabolizm, autoinduksiya, dərman qarşılıqlı təsirləri, beyinə məhdud paylanma və şişdaxili toxumaya qeyri\-bərabər nüfuzetmə ilə daha da məhdudlaşır\. Bərk hal modifikasiyası, nanostrukturlu formulasiya, hədəflənmiş nanodaşıyıcılar, lokoregional tətbiq və dabrafenib–trametinibin koordinasiyalı şəkildə çatdırılması preklinik tədqiqatlarda ümidverici nəticələr göstərmişdir\. Lakin onların standart oral terapiyadan üstünlüyünü təsdiqləyən sübutlar hələ də məhduddur\. Melanoma, ağciyər, qalxanabənzər vəz, öd yolları, kolorektal və mərkəzi sinir sistemi şişləri üzrə klinik nəticələr göstərir ki, BRAF V600E mühüm terapevtik hədəf olsa da, müalicədən faydanı müstəqil şəkildə proqnozlaşdırmaq üçün kifayət etmir\. Buna görə də müalicənin optimallaşdırılması molekulyar seçim, rezistentlik profilinin müəyyənləşdirilməsi və dərmanın ayrı\-ayrı lezyonlarda ekspozisiyasını birləşdirən şişə spesifik yanaşma tələb edir\.

## [A CONTRIBUIÇÃO DE KRISTIN ANDREWS PARA A FILOSOFIA DA MENTE E COGNIÇÃO ANIMAL: O PROTAGONISMO FEMININO NA CIÊNCIA](../publications/7498dee5fbbe2b707407.md)

Lucas Santos; Bruno Ramos Mendonça; Alcione Roberto Roani

O estudo analisa as valiosas contribuições da filósofa Kristin Andrews para a filosofia da mente e cognição animal, destacando o protagonismo feminino na ciência\. Historicamente, investigações sobre a mente foram fortemente limitadas por perspectivas androcêntricas\. Portanto, a participação de mulheres é uma necessidade epistemológica fundamental para expandir o conhecimento\. Utilizando revisão bibliográfica qualitativa da obra &quot;The Animal Mind&quot;, o trabalho sintetiza os principais argumentos da pesquisadora\. A autora desafia o ceticismo tradicional sobre capacidades mentais de animais, argumentando que atribuir crenças e desejos a eles não é apenas antropomorfismo ingênuo, mas sim uma hipótese científica testável\. ​Ela reconceitua a teoria da mente, propondo métodos inovadores que respeitem as especificidades ecológicas de cada espécie, sem incorrer no antropocentrismo clássico\. No contexto da inclusão de mulheres, Kristin Andrews serve como um modelo importante, evidenciando que a pesquisa científica adquire enorme precisão e profundidade com a liderança feminina\. Sua trajetória comprova que a diversidade é indispensável para superar antigos dogmas acadêmicos e para desenvolver metodologias muito mais sofisticadas, amplas e inclusivas\. Logo, o formidável trabalho de Kristin Andrews pavimenta caminhos para inspirar outras meninas, reforçando a imensa urgência de políticas de fomento que garantam a permanência contínua delas nas diversas áreas científicas atuais\.

## [Colon Leakage Score and Preoperative Albumin for Predicting Anastomotic Leakage after Colorectal Cancer Resection in Indonesia: A Predictive Accuracy Study](../publications/74a73ccf67b7423d72b8.md)

Muhammad Rizqi Firyal; Muhammad Hafidh Komar; Theodorus

Background: Anastomotic leakage \(AL\) is the most serious complication of colorectal cancer resection\. The Colon Leakage Score \(CLS\) has no biochemical component and has not been tested in Indonesian patients, many of whom have hypoalbuminemia\. Objective: To measure how accurately CLS &gt;11 combined with preoperative albumin &lt;3\.5 g/dL predicts AL, and to quantify what albumin adds to the CLS\. Methods: This retrospective STARD\-guided study included 60 adults who underwent colorectal cancer resection with primary anastomosis and no diverting stoma at Dr\. Mohammad Hoesin General Hospital, Palembang \(January 2022–June 2024\)\. Accuracy measures carry Wilson 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\)\. Albumin had not been cross\-classified against AL\. Every contingency table matching the observed data was therefore enumerated, with Firth regression across 19,977 admissible datasets\. Results: Thirteen patients \(21\.7%; 95% CI 13\.1–33\.6\) developed AL, and 43 \(71\.7%\) were hypoalbuminemic\. Six of seven composite\-positive patients leaked, as did 7 of 53 composite\-negative patients \(odds ratio 35\.6; exact 95% CI 3\.6–1850\.2; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Sensitivity was 46\.2% \(23\.2–70\.9\), below the 80% benchmark \(p = 0\.007\)\. Specificity was 97\.9% \(88\.9–99\.6\), positive predictive value 85\.7% \(48\.7–97\.4\) and negative predictive value 86\.8% \(75\.2–93\.5\)\. Seven of eight CLS\-high patients were hypoalbuminemic; albumin reclassified one\. CLS &gt;11 was associated with AL in all 15 admissible tables \(odds ratio 19\.3–53\.7\)\. The albumin association \(0\.23–15\.5\) could not be identified\. Conclusion: The composite works as a high\-specificity rule\-in criterion, and the CLS carries its discrimination\. It misses more than half of all leaks\. Widespread hypoalbuminemia is a separate nutritional target that deserves prospective evaluation\.

## [The Energy Economics of Artificial Intelligence Data Centers: Demand Uncertainty, System Costs, Flexibility, and Credible Decarbonization](../publications/74b53ad23a61d0cd2fd9.md)

Cosimo Magazzino; Hossein Ali Fakher

Artificial intelligence is accelerating data center electricity demand, but annual energy totals alone do not reveal when, where, or at whose cost new loads enter power systems\. This review asks how uncertain projects should be translated into demand, infrastructure, price, flexibility, and environmental consequences\. We conducted a structured critical review of 44 peer\-reviewed studies, working papers, and official, regulatory, statistical, system\-operator, and institutional reports identified through 31 August 2026, with explicit source selection and claim\-level reliability appraisal\. The central finding is that the economic effect of AI data centers depends on project\-realization probability, coincident demand, and location, not on announced capacity alone\. Concentrated growth can require generation and network investment and raise local prices\. Enforceable temporal or spatial flexibility can reduce these costs, but unverified flexibility warrants no planning credit\. Annual renewable matching supports an accounting claim but not necessarily consequential decarbonization, which also requires additional supply, temporal matching, and geographic deliverability\. Policy should therefore condition connection on project credibility, cost responsibility, measured flexibility, and credible procurement\. This review’s incremental contribution is to move beyond consumption inventories by integrating uncertain project realization, short\-run operation, medium\-run connection and investment, long\-run expansion, distributional incidence, and environmental counterfactuals in one energy\-economics framework\.

## [Classical methods for modern applications: synthetic tabular data generation using lightweight discrete response continuous latent variable model](../publications/74bd5a0154d22ad8153f.md)

Bartosz Barzdajn; Mateusz Krzysztoń

In this paper, we present a lightweight algorithm for modelling tabular data containing both continuous and discrete variables\. The method uses empirical marginal distributions and a selected quantile function to transform the data into a continuous latent space, where a distribution of choice, e\.g\. a multivariate Gaussian, can be efficiently estimated and applied\. While this approach is closely related to classical well\-established machine learning methods, we present a novel adaptation that fits well within the contemporary computational ecosystem\. Unlike in the case of deep architectures, it results in a simple implementation with few dependencies, robust training/estimation, as well as efficient sampling\. The transformation preserves complex marginal distributions and correlations, providing high\-fidelity models, especially for data with unimodal distributions\. One of the key characteristics of the proposed approach is its continuous representation of discrete variables\. While highly desirable, this introduces a significant challenge, since a single observation corresponds to a region rather than a point in the latent space\. We show that this ambiguity naturally leads to a Monte Carlo expectation\-maximisation \(MCEM\) formulation, whose auxiliary objective can be expressed as a weighted latent\-space likelihood\. This, in turn, allows conventional maximum\-likelihood estimators to be used within an efficient and robust optimisation procedure\.

## [Sürdürülebilir Tüketimde Yapay Zekâ](../publications/74bebe3be684d98fb5ed.md)



İklim krizi ve çevresel bozulmaların yaşandığı günümüzde, yeşil dönüşümün en güçlü teknolojik kaynağı olan yapay zekânın pazarlama süreçlerine ve tüketici davranışlarına etkileri önemli bir araştırma konusu olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır\. Bu doğrultuda kitap; işletmelerin sürdürülebilirlik vizyonları ile tüketicilerin çevre dostu kararları arasındaki köprüyü yapay zekâ teknolojileriyle yeniden inşa etmeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Ayrıca, teknolojinin yıkıcı gücünü canlıların ortak geleceği için yapıcı bir güce dönüştürmenin yollarını aramaktadır\. Kitabın birinci bölümünde; geleneksel pazarlama paradigmalarının evrimini ve yapay zekânın bu evrimdeki rolünü ele almaktadır\. Sürdürülebilir pazarlama artık sadece bir imaj çalışması değil, yapay zekânın veri işleme gücüyle desteklenen stratejik bir zorunluluk olduğu vurgulanmaktadır\. İkinci bölümünde; teoriyi pratiğe dökerek yapay zekânın doğrudan tüketiciyle temas ettiği dijital ekosistemleri analiz etmektedir\. Tüketicilerin çevre bilincine sahip olmalarına rağmen satın alma anında bu bilinci eyleme dönüştürememeleri sorununa odaklanmaktadır\. Son bölümde ise; davranışsal iktisat ile ileri teknolojinin kesişimi olan özgün bir kavramsal model inşa edilmektedir\. İnsanları zorlamadan, seçenek özgürlüklerini kısıtlamadan çevre dostu tercihlere yönlendirmeyi amaçlayan &quot;Dürtme Teorisi&quot;, yapay zekâ eliyle kişiselleştirilmiş bir boyuta taşınmaktadır\. Yapay zekânın sadece endüstriyel bir verimlilik aracı olmadığını, aynı zamanda tüketim kültürünü kökten değiştirebilecek toplumsal bir dönüştürücü olduğunu kanıtlayan bu kitap; pazarlama yöneticileri, veri bilimciler, akademisyenler ve sürdürülebilirlik profesyonelleri için nesnel bir kaynak niteliğindedir\.

## [Upper bounds on the number of causal pieces in spiking neural networks](../publications/74bf8ff03c9c68280688.md)

Dominik Dold; Dennis Elbrächter; Philipp Petersen

The input space of single\-spike neural networks decomposes into causal pieces, and the number of causal pieces has been shown to provide a lower bound on the approximation error for some spiking neural networks\. While this decomposition is applicable to a wide range of spiking neuron models, the limits of how many causal pieces can be realised by spiking neural networks are still unknown\. In this work, we derive two complementary upper bounds on the number of causal pieces in feedforward single\-spike neural networks\. First, we establish a combinatorial bound given by the poly\-Bernoulli numbers, which applies to a broad class of spiking neuron models\. The bound is of order $e^\{2\(L\-1\)N\\log N\+\\mathcal\{O\}\(N\)\}$, with network depth $L$ and maximum layer width $N$\. Second, for a specific set of neuron models, we derive a bound based on hyperplane arrangements\. Applying the latter framework, we obtain bounds of order $\\mathcal\{O\}\\\!\\left\(N^\{\(4L\-3\)\(N\_0\-1\)\}\\right\)$ for the non\-leaky integrate\-and\-fire model with exponential synapses and the ReLU\-type spike response model, and $\\mathcal\{O\}\\\!\\left\(N^\{L\(N\_0\-1\)\}\\right\)$ for the leaky integrate\-and\-fire model with Dirac\-$δ$ synapses, where $N\_0$ is the input dimension\. For the non\-leaky integrate\-and\-fire model with Dirac\-$δ$ synapses, additional temporal structure allows us to sharpen the general combinatorial bound to one that depends only on $N\_0$, independently of the network depth and widths\.

## [Feasibility of Implementing a Pharmacist\-Integrated Collaborative Model for Opioid Use Disorder: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial](../publications/74c47d5e36fad34f8eaf.md)

Felicity A\. E\. Homsted; David A\. Fiellin; Udi E\. Ghitza; Vernon T\. Gardner; Bethany M\. McLeman; Paul J\. Joudrey; Gerald Cochran; Sarah K\. Moore; Lisa Saldana; Edward Chongsi; Kimberly Kramer; Ashley A\. Vena; Rebecca A\. Ottesen; Jacklyn Harris; Jesse S\. Boggis; Deepika Rao; Owen Murray; Scott Gerlach; Phoebe R Gauthier; Katie P\. Osterhage; Laura‐Mae Baldwin; Lisa A\. Marsch

BACKGROUND: Addressing the opioid crisis requires an interdisciplinary approach\. Pharmacists may provide medication expertise to primary care addiction teams\. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether implementing a pharmacist\-integrated model of care for opioid use disorder \(PrIMO\) was feasible and acceptable\. DESIGN: Nonrandomized mixed\-methods longitudinal feasibility/implementation trial conducted from March 2022 to October 2024\. PARTICIPANTS: Four primary care sites with retail pharmacies and clinical pharmacists\. Participants were adults employed by the clinics and adult patients receiving medications for opioid use disorder \(MOUD\) exposed to PrIMO for at least 2 weeks\. Site staff \(provider, pharmacists, leadership\) were surveyed for 15 months \(80\.6% follow\-up completion\) and patients for 6 months \(75\.5% follow\-up completion\)\. INTERVENTION: Pharmacist\-integrated MOUD\. MAIN MEASURES: Primary: Feasibility \(PrIMO launch\)\. Secondary: acceptability \(survey and interview data\) and impact \(electronic health record data\)\. KEY RESULTS: All sites launched PrIMO \(100%\) and maintained it for at least 1 year\. From 3 months pre\- to 1 year post\-launch, site staff reported fewer barriers to providing MOUD \(m \[SD\] 2\.2 \[0\.8\] to 1\.8 \[0\.5\], 1\-4\-point scale\), increased knowledge of MOUD \(3\.8 \[0\.4\] to 4\.0 \[0\.5\], 1\-5\-point scale\), and steady acceptability by providers/pharmacists \(2\.1 \[0\.3\] to 2\.0 \[0\.4\], 0\-3\-point scale\) and leadership \(2\.1 \[0\.3\] to 2\.0 \[0\.4\], 0\-3\-point scale\)\. Patients reported less stigma \(3\.1 \[1\.1\] to 2\.8 \[1\.1\], 1\-5\-point scale\) and steady acceptability \(2\.2 \[0\.4\] to 2\.2 \[0\.4\], 0\-3\-point scale\)\. Electronic health records data demonstrated increases in the rate of patients retained in MOUD \(m \[SD\] 59\.5 \[34\.81\] to 60\.2 \[35\.35\] proportion of days covered\), adherence to MOUD \(38\.6 to 40\.9%\), clinic visits for MOUD \(\+ 100 encounters\), and total patients treated per prescriber \(m \[SD\] 12\.9 \[32\.49\] to 13\.7 \[35\.07\]\) 1 year pre\- vs 1 year post\-launch, although statistical significance was not assessed\. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating pharmacists into MOUD care teams may improve feasibility and acceptability of MOUD in primary care\. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials\.gov, NCT05310786, March 14, 2022\.

## [Puya ukumari sp\. nov\. \(Bromeliaceae, Puyoideae\), a new montane bromeliad species from southeastern Peru](../publications/74ca33adfce41da4bc80.md)

Jhon A\. Yuca\-Palomino; Norma G\. Mamani\-Mayta; Luis A\. Champi\-Charalla; Elias Condori\-Cuti; Narciso Llacta\-Gomez; Italo Treviño\-Zevallos; Eric John Gouda; Adrian B\. Forsyth; Andrew William Whitworth; Ruthmery Pillco\-Huarcaya

Montane forests of the Tropical Andes are among the most diverse and endemic\-rich ecosystems in the world; however, they remain insufficiently documented, particularly in remote and topographically complex landscapes\. Here, we describe Puya ukumari sp\. nov \. \(Bromeliaceae\), a new species from humid montane forests and forest–puna ecotonal habitats in the Kosñipata and Mapacho valleys of southeastern Peru, occurring at elevations between 2,300 and 3,300 m a\.s\.l\. The species was first detected during a long\-term ecological monitoring program in the region but remained unrecognized for several years due to the limited number of recorded flowering individuals\. Its taxonomic identity became evident following the observation of flowering plants during field surveys conducted in 2025\. Puya ukumari resembles P\. lineata in possessing a simple, nodding, dark\-colored inflorescence; however, it is readily distinguished by its considerably larger flowering plant height \(160–200 cm vs\. 40–80 cm\), significantly wider inflorescence diameter \(11–12\.5 cm vs\. 3\.5–6 cm\), larger lanate sepals \(30–33 × 15–18 mm vs\. 13–18 × 6–10 mm and floccose\), and markedly darker, nearly black petals\. These characters support its recognition as a distinct taxon within the group of Puya species with simple inflorescences\. The species is currently known from a limited number of confirmed localities within a restricted elevational range\. Based on its distribution and the observed threats to its habitat, a preliminary conservation assessment suggests that it should be classified as Endangered \(EN\) according to IUCN Red List criteria\.

## [Observation and the Psychoanalytic Imagination](../publications/74ce08de6bc98af4c5bd.md)

Margaret Rustin; Kate Stratton; Simon Cregeen

This book brings together some of Margaret Rustin’s finest papers in the areas of infant observation, theory, research and literature\. Drawing on more than 50 years of psychoanalytic practice, the author offers a richly layered exploration of the central place of close observation and imagination in illuminating the inner worlds of children and young people\. Illustrated with vivid clinical examples, the collection engages with a broad range of themes, including the place of interpretation in child psychotherapy, the experience of shame in childhood, dreams and play in child analysis and the challenges of clinical research\. A final section turns to literature and drama, tracing the vital connections between imagination and psychic life\. Essential reading for child psychotherapists, psychoanalysts and child analysts, as well as all those training as mental health professionals, this book will also appeal to anyone with an interest in the emotional dimensions of human experience\.

## [Afet Ortamında Kriminalistik Soruşturmaların Zorlukları ve Kriminolojik Perspektif](../publications/74dc050fd7469ae4a50c.md)

Niyazi Umut Akıncıoğlu

Bu çalışma, afet ortamında kriminalistik soruşturmaların karşılaştığı zorlukları kriminolojik perspektifle bütüncül olarak ele almaktadır\. Afetler, yalnızca fiziksel yıkım ve insani krizler yaratmakla kalmaz; aynı zamanda sosyal kontrol mekanizmalarının zayıflaması, suç fırsatlarının artması ve adalet sisteminin işlevselliğinin sınanması gibi karmaşık dinamikleri tetikler\. Kriminolojik teoriler \(Sosyal Düzensizlik, Rutin Faaliyetler, Kırık Camlar\) afet sonrası suç tipolojilerinin ve motivasyon yapılarının anlaşılmasında temel bir çerçeve sunarken; kriminalistik boyut, delil toplama, kimliklendirme ve adli süreçlerin olağanüstü koşullarda yürütülmesindeki teknik ve lojistik engelleri ortaya koyar\. Çalışmada, afet sonrası suç dinamikleri mala karşı suçlar, beyaz yaka suçları ve şiddet suçları olarak sınıflandırılmış; geçici barınma alanlarının özgün riskleri vurgulanmıştır\. Delil bütünlüğünün korunması, Afet Kurbanlarını Kimliklendirme \(DVI\) süreçlerinin standardizasyonu ve kurumlar arası koordinasyon eksiklikleri kritik zayıf noktalar olarak belirlenmiştir\. Türkiye’deki 1999 Gölcük ve 2023 Kahramanmaraş depremleri ile uluslararası örnekler \(Katrina Kasırgası, Tōhoku Depremi\) üzerinden yapılan vaka analizleri, kurumsal öğrenme eksikliklerinin ve planlama\-uygulama uçurumunun altını çizmektedir\. Sonuç olarak, afet yönetim planlarının kriminalistik ve adli boyutu güçlü şekilde içerecek şekilde yeniden tasarlanması, olay yeri yönetimi, merkezi DVI protokolleri ve suç önleyici çevresel tasarım gibi entegre stratejiler geliştirilmesi önerilmektedir\. Böylece hem adaletin tesisi hem de gelecekteki ihmallerin önlenmesi için etkili bir hesap verebilirlik mekanizması oluşturulabilir\.

## [ROOFS: RObust biOmarker Feature Selection](../publications/74de2c477c55b491ed27.md)

Anastasiia Bakhmach; Paul Dufossé; Simon Charpigny; Florence Monville; Laurent Greillier; Fabrice Barlési; Sébastien Benzekry

Feature selection \(FS\) is essential for biomarker discovery and clinical predictive modeling\. Over the past decades, the methodological literature on FS has become rich and mature, offering a wide spectrum of algorithmic approaches\. However, much of this methodological progress has not been fully adopted in applied biomedical research\. To bridge this gap, we propose ROOFS \(RObust biOmarker Feature Selection\), a Python package designed to help researchers in the choice of the FS method most adapted to their problem\. Currently supporting classification tasks, ROOFS benchmarks multiple FS methods on the user’s data and generates reports summarizing a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics, including downstream predictive performance estimated using optimism correction, stability, robustness of individual features, and true positive and false positive rates assessed on semi\-synthetic data with a simulated outcome\. We demonstrate the utility of ROOFS on data from the PIONeeR biomarker study, aimed at identifying predictors of resistance to anti\-PD\-\(L\)1 immunotherapy in lung cancer\. Comprehensive benchmarking with ROOFS has the potential to improve the reproducibility of FS discoveries and increase the translational value of clinical models\. ROOFS is available at https://gitlab\.inria\.fr/compo/roofs \.

## [Institutional Dominance Configuration: Organizational Resilience and Patronage Networks in the Cases of LDP and PRI](../publications/74ecdadb5cfd181d43e1.md)

Ali Rıza Savaş

How can a dominant party remain in power for so many years? This article defines one of the possible answers as a conceptual category\. This conceptualization can be expressed as the Institutional Dominance Configuration \(IDC\)\. The definition is tested using two long\-standing case studies\. The first is Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party \(LDP; dominance period 1955–2009, briefly interrupted in 1993–1994\)\. The second is Mexico’s Institutional Revolutionary Party \(Partido Revolucionario Institucional, PRI, 1929–2000\)\. The study is grounded in the approaches of Sartori \(1976\) and Ziegfeld \(2022\)\. On this basis, the IDC is distinguished from the Populist Dominance Configuration \(PDC\) and the Hybrid Dominance Configuration \(HDC\)\. The study’s methodology combines comparative historical analysis with within\-case process tracing\. In both cases, three mechanisms recur\. These are the mobilization of state resources, electoral engineering, and the fragmentation of the opposition\. The key issue is not so much the existence of these mechanisms as how they operate within the IDC\. Three hypotheses are tested in this context\. H1: electoral engineering takes the form of gradual changes based on intra\-party consensus\. H2: the fragmentation of the opposition is a consequence of structural incentives\. H3: shifts between configurations develop in response to institutional shocks\. Two events form the cornerstones of this test: the PRI’s defeat in 2000 and the independence of the Federal Electoral Institute \(Instituto Federal Electoral, IFE\) in 1996\. When read in conjunction with the PDC/HDC framework, the article offers a configuration\-sensitive and mechanism\-based comparative approach to research on dominant parties\.

## [The roof grouting and active support technology of roadways based on stratified mining](../publications/74ee7d6da181c315c7eb.md)

Xiaoming Wang; Junying Zhang; Ningning Zhang; Guosheng Wu; Liancong Wang; Yude Liu

Abstract This study aims to enhance roadway support effectiveness and construction efficiency\. The study proposes a synergistic technology integrating roof grouting with active support techniques in stratified mining environments, enhanced by deep reinforcement learning \(DRL\) algorithms that adaptively optimize grouting parameters in real time\. A mechanical model of a roadway in stratified mining is established, along with a grouting parameter optimization framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient \(DDPG\)\. Using the 20,701 transport roadway in a deep coal mine as the test area, a comparative experimental system is constructed comprising traditional support \(Section A\), dual\-layer grouting and bolting support \(DLGBS\) \(Section B\), and DDPG\-optimized intelligent support \(Section C\)\. Through the combined field monitoring and numerical simulation, the performance differences among the three schemes are systematically evaluated in surrounding rock deformation control, support cost, construction efficiency, and long\-term stability\. The double\-layer grouting technology establishes a multi\-level bearing system through shallow grouting for fracture filling and deep anchoring for constraint\. In contrast, the DDPG algorithm dynamically adjusts grouting pressure, slurry ratio, and injection rate based on multi\-source sensor data\. The field monitoring results show that after 30 days of support construction, the traditional support, DLGBS and the roof subsidence of DDPG\-optimized support are 45\.6, 28\.4, and 18\.7 millimeters \(mm\), respectively\. The convergence of sidewalls is 32\.1, 19\.8 and 12\.3 mm, respectively, and the floor heave is 12\.4, 5\.4 and 3\.1 mm\. Compared with the traditional support, the roof subsidence under DDPG optimization conditions is reduced by about 59\.0%\. These results are applicable to the 20,701 transport roadway and coal roadway with similar burial depth, coal seam thickness, stratified mining mode and stress conditions, and can provide a reference for grouting and active support design under similar engineering conditions\.

## [Harmonization of the Legal Framework for Hajj and Umrah Administration under Law Number 8 of 2019 and Law Number 14 of 2025](../publications/74f097d60f564218b27c.md)

Eka Farah Khoirun Nisa’; Suhadi; Fauzan Adim

This doctrinal article compares Indonesia’s Law Number 8 of 2019 on Hajj and Umrah Administration with its third amendment, Law Number 14 of 2025\. Through statutory and conceptual interpretation, it identifies amendments governing ministerial responsibility, allocation of Hajj quotas, adjustment of pilgrimage costs, supervision of special Hajj and Umrah operators, and the Ministry Information System\. The amendment does not repeal the 2019 law in its entirety: provisions not amended remain in force\. The article distinguishes statutory duties supported by specific provisions from proposed indicators concerning service standards, archiving, integrated digital governance, and pilgrim complaints\. It argues for article\-based implementation guidance, explicit coordination with the Hajj Financial Management Agency, traceable oversight decisions, and stronger accessible remedies for vulnerable pilgrims\. Its contribution lies in a verifiable mapping of institutional responsibilities and legal consequences rather than an unsupported claim of wholesale replacement\.

## [Reproducible research by design: design principles for low\-code/no\-code AutoML tools](../publications/74f646d5f97ff68b7bec.md)

Armin Haberl; Stefan Thalmann

Reproducibility is a major challenge for responsible machine learning \(ML\) research, especially with low\-code/no\-code automated ML \(LCNC AutoML\) tools making ML methods accessible to researchers outside data science\. Existing approaches to support research reproducibility are difficult to apply to LCNC AutoML due to a lack of shareable code, limited tool transparency, and varying levels of ML expertise among users\. To inform the design of LCNC AutoML tools that support reproducible research, this design science study proposes a set of design principles utilizing the theoretical lens of Technology Affordances and Constraints Theory\. We first identified design requirements based on user studies with six researchers who implemented and reproduced LCNC AutoML projects\. This was followed by a technical review of eight LCNC AutoML tools to identify existing design features in relation to the identified design requirements\. Through mapping design features to design requirements, a set of design principles emerged: \(1\) GUI Customizability, \(2\) Standardized Reporting, \(3\) Interoperability, and \(4\) Adaptive Guidance\. Together, these principles provide actionable design guidance for developing LCNC AutoML tools that support the documentation and reproducibility of ML research\.

## [At the Civilizational Crossroads: A Binary Architectural Choice for the Future of Artificial Intelligence](../publications/74fedef929f7bf253c1f.md)

Maung Maung Saw

Project Status: Open Invitation for Technical Critique and Sandbox Simulation\. WHICH ROAD WILL HUMANITY CHOOSE FOR THE FUTURE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE? Toti\-Potential AI System with “Killer Instinct” vs\. Omni\-Potential AI System with Intrinsic “Metta” This open\-access conceptual proposal outlines a novel, non\-self neural network framework designed to bypass the structural vulnerabilities of instrumental convergence and deceptive alignment in frontier language models\. Tracking the upstream causal pathways of agentic deviance, the manuscript formalizes a dual\-path trajectory for modern computer science\. It contrasts standard open\-web maximized systems \(&quot;Road 1&quot;\) against a closed, strictly calibrated architectural alternative \(&quot;Road 2&quot;\)\. Using the structural logic of the Theravada Buddhist Pañca\-niyāma, the paper introduces explicit technical design constraints, including Substrate Isolation, the Anattā Matrix Architecture, and the Anicca Control Plane hardware interrupt loop\. This repository contains the foundational conceptual proposal \(Document 6 of the ongoing research trail\) and is published to invite mathematical validation and pseudocode translation strategies for open sandbox testing\.

## [Construction of a machine learning\-based model for predicting specialist nurse transfer tendencies](../publications/74ff8e7d42a5398f0eaa.md)

Gan Wang; Zheng Luo; 吴惠英; Jiaojiao Wang; Wen Ma; Li Luo

The shortage of specialist nurses poses a significant challenge to healthcare systems worldwide, impacting both patient care and hospital operations\. This study explores the application of machine learning to predict the job transfer tendencies of specialist nurses, as well as determining the major causes of the transfer tendencies, aiming to provide hospitals with actionable insights for retention strategies\. We applied multiple classification algorithms, such as Multilayer Perceptron \(MLP\) Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, XGBoost and TabNet Classifier\. The final model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) score of 0\.766 after cross\-validation and hyperparameter optimisation using the Tree\-structured Parzen Estimator \(TPE\)\. To better understand feature contributions, we utilised Shapley additive explanations \(SHAP\) values to perform feature importance analyses\. Our findings identified that key predictors of nurse transfer include whether satisfaction with performance distribution is high, monthly take\-home income, number of specialist trainings/continuing education attended, whether working in a specialist nursing outpatient clinic and number of children under 12\. However, certain results, such as the unexpected positive correlation between satisfaction with performance distribution and job transfer, revealed anomalies that are likely attributable to class imbalances or data biases\. We also discuss the tradeoffs between different data preprocessing techniques, particularly regarding oversampling within cross\-validation to mitigate class imbalances\. While the performance of the model was moderate, the insights from the SHAP analysis provided valuable directions for future research\. Hence, we recommend collecting more representative data and refining feature selection to improve model accuracy\. Therefore, this research contributes to the development of predictive tools for hospital management to address the specialist nurse shortage by identifying nurses who are at risk of job transfer\. Not applicable\. Strengths: • Multiple model comparison: This study explores a wide range of algorithmic approaches to optimise predictive performance by implementing various machine learning models \(TabNet Classifier, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP Classifier, AdaBoost, LGBM Classifier, and CatBoost Classifier\)\. • Cross\-validation: The use of cross\-validation ensures robust model selection and reduces the risk of overfitting, thus enhancing the generalisability of the results\. • Hyperparameter tuning: The application of Optuna’s TPE\-based optimisation allows for efficient hyperparameter selection, which leads to improved model performance\. • Handling imbalanced data: Our dataset is highly imbalanced\. Among the 471 samples collected, 77\.9% \(367\) of the participants intended to transfer while only 22\.1% \(104\) of the participants intended to stay\. This study addresses class imbalance by incorporating the synthetic minority over\-sampling technique \(SMOTE\)\. SMOTE will oversample the minority class \(nurses who do not intend to transfer\) until it has the same number as the majority \(nurses who intend to transfer\), thus ensuring the better prediction of minority cases\. • Feature importance analysis: The use of SHAP to interpret feature importance adds transparency and interpretability, which facilitates understanding the decision\-making processes of the models\. Weaknesses: • Limited interpretability in some models: While powerful, models such as XGBoost and CatBoost can be complex, which makes it harder to interpret the underlying relationships compared with simpler models, such as logistic regression\. • One\-hot encoding scalability: Using one\-hot encoding in preprocessing can lead to high\-dimensional data, especially when categorical features have many unique values, which potentially impacts computational efficiency\. • Potential data leakage risk: The extensive preprocessing steps, including feature selection and scaling, require careful management to avoid leakage between the training and testing data\. • Hyperparameter tuning computational cost: Although Optuna optimises the process, the computational cost of hyperparameter tuning across multiple models can be high, particularly when combined with cross\-validation\. • SMOTE limitations: While SMOTE helps balance the dataset, it may generate synthetic data that do not perfectly represent real\-world nurse resignation patterns, which could introduce noise into the training process\.

## [Eureiandra orientalis \(Cucurbitaceae\), a new species from Kenya and Tanzania](../publications/751113e7877904c9b95d.md)

Ruo\-Zhou Wang; Zhaohui Ran; Hanno Schaefer; Quentin Luke; Neduvoto P\. Mollel; Paul Muigai Kirika; Christopher Chapano; Xue Yan; Shengwei Wang; Neng Wei; Qing\-Feng Wang

Eureiandra orientalis , a new species of Cucurbitaceae from Kenya and Tanzania, is described and illustrated\. It was previously treated as Eureiandra sp\. A by Charles Jeffrey in the &quot;Flora of Tropical East Africa&quot;, and was later referred to as Eureiandra orientalis Q\.Luke ined\., but it has never been formally described and named\. Morphologically, the new species is most similar to E\. fasciculata , but is readily distinguished from other members of Eureiandra by its nearly glabrous habit, with hairs mainly restricted to the nodes, leaf veins and margins, dark\-green glossy leaves, denser shortly pedunculate male inflorescences, ovate petals, larger fruits, and oblong\-elliptic blackish brown seeds with indistinct margins and fibrous testa\. In addition, the two species differ in phenology: in E\. orientalis , the leaves are fully developed at flowering, whereas in E\. fasciculata , the stems are leafless at anthesis\. The new species is mostly known from coastal forests of Eastern Africa in Kenya and Tanzania, one of the globally recognized biodiversity hotspots\.

## [Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD\-1 blockade response](../publications/7511a12528cf71da665b.md)

Aubrey Y\. Liew; Ying Li; Haidong Dong

T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer\. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD\-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential\. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function\. Latent effector capacity represents a history\-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression\. In this model, PD\-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity\. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses\. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible\. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD\-1 therapy\.

## [Technology\-Enhanced Language Instruction for Economics Students](../publications/7515e87f92385fe6ef68.md)

LUSINE HARUTYUNYAN; A\. Grigoryan; A\. Mkrtchyan

For economics students today who want to pursue careers in international business, finance, entrepreneurship, and economic policy in the globalized economy, efficient communication in English is a vital skill\. Many students grasp English grammar and vocabular y, but they struggle to acquire the speaking abilities required for professional communication\. Speaking anxiety, lack of genuine engagement, lack of business\-related terminology, and weak confidence still impair learners’ speaking performance\. At the same time, however, technological advancement has transformed language education by creating new options for communication, cooperation, and customized learning\. The work under review is devoted to innovative methods of developing the professional speaking skills of economics students through the use of Communicative Language Teaching \(CLT\) and educational technology\. The review of studies on speaking training, communicative competence, technology\-enhanced language learning, gamification, artificial intelligence, and professional communication in higher education is included in the study\. Special focus is paid to the utilization of digital platforms, online collaboration tools, gamified learning settings \(e\.g\., Kahoot\), and AI\-assisted language learning tools that enhance speaking development\. The study shows a favorable influence of communicative and technology\-based strategies on speaking fluency, student engagement, communicative confidence, and the capacity to communicate in a professional manner\. Results also show that the use of CLT principles and digital learning tools can provide tremendous opportunities for economics students to practice business communication in real and interactive scenarios\. The paper ends with a discussion of the pedagogical implications for higher education institutions and suggestions for the future of technology\-enhanced speaking training in economics education\.

## [WRF Cold\-Pool Sensitivities Relevant to Winter Ozone Modelling in the Uinta Basin](../publications/751bb52e16e9f40785f5.md)

John R\. Lawson; Michael J\. Davies; Loknath Dhar; Seth N\. Lyman

Cold\-pool structure controls the confinement of wintertime ozone and its precursors in Utah’s Uinta Basin\. Previous studies have documented difficulty capturing stable cold pools in meteorological models, complicating air quality simulations when pollutants disperse too readily\. Herein, we evaluate the meteorology behind one such high\-ozone event on 2 February 2013 with Weather Research and Forecasting \(WRF\) simulations; the chemistry is not simulated\. We test the sensitivity to Global Forecast System \(GFS\) or North American Mesoscale \(NAM\) forcing, domain feedback, boundary\-layer and surface\-layer schemes, slope\-aware radiation, and terrain datasets \(fine versus coarse\)\. Across five hourly samples, GFS\-driven runs were warmer at the evaluated surface sites, had an approximately 3\.6 K smaller 50–500 m potential\-temperature endpoint difference, and had a 0\.8–1\.0 m s−1 larger layer\-mean wind\-vector magnitude than feedback\-matched NAM runs\. The GFS also retained a lower mean heat deficit, indicating a weaker modelled cold pool\. The heat deficit increased in all four runs from 1400 to 1800 UTC; hence the difference in driving model suggests a state difference without demonstrated faster cold\-pool erosion\. Toggling feedback and parametrisation settings yielded smaller responses; terrain fineness produced spatial responses that station comparisons could miss\. The results guide diagnostics for subsequent air\-chemistry modelling, while leaving initial versus lateral forcing, cold\-pool depth, and basin export for future studies\.

## [Pembelajaran Berdiferensiasi dalam Meningkatkan Keterlibatan dan Hasil Belajar Matematika: Tinjauan Kritis](../publications/75239c1c4f8857892c66.md)

Arini Nabila Zakkiatun Nisa’i; Yayuk Ernawati; Vina Homaidatin; Putri Wulandari; Siti Rofikoh; Gita Octavia Ramadhani; Rani Oktavia Herli; Fatqurhohman Fatqurhohman

Pembelajaran matematika menghadapi keragaman kesiapan dan kebutuhan peserta didik yang menuntut respons pedagogis adaptif\. Kajian ini bertujuan menganalisis secara kritis efektivitas pembelajaran berdiferensiasi terhadap keterlibatan dan hasil belajar matematika serta mengidentifikasi kondisi yang menentukan keberhasilannya\. Kajian dilakukan melalui telaah literatur terhadap penelitian mengenai diferensiasi, asesmen kesiapan matematis, keterlibatan, hasil belajar, dan implementasinya\. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa asesmen menjadi fondasi diferensiasi ketika hasilnya diterjemahkan ke dalam keputusan tentang tingkat tantangan, tugas, scaffolding, dan pengelompokan\. Bukti empiris lebih konsisten menunjukkan kecenderungan positif pada hasil belajar matematika, sedangkan bukti mengenai keterlibatan masih terbatas dan belum konsisten mengukur keterlibatan kognitif\. Efektivitas diferensiasi dipengaruhi kompetensi guru, kualitas desain pembelajaran, pengelolaan kelas, sumber belajar, dukungan kelembagaan, dan pemanfaatan teknologi\. Diferensiasi lebih tepat diposisikan sebagai kerangka pengambilan keputusan pedagogis adaptif daripada sekadar variasi aktivitas\. Efektivitasnya bersifat kondisional dan bergantung pada keselarasan asesmen, kebutuhan peserta didik, desain tugas, dukungan, keterlibatan kognitif, dan tujuan matematis\.

## [Advancing Inclusive Higher Education Through Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities for Accessibility, Personalization, And Student Support](../publications/75285653bee8aec30572.md)

Dildora Nutfieva

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is creating new opportunities to advance inclusive higher education by improving accessibility, personalizing learning experiences, and strengthening student support\. Despite progress in inclusive education policies, students with disabilities continue to encounter barriers associated with inaccessible learning materials, inflexible teaching practices, limited assistive technologies, and insufficient institutional support\. This article examines the theoretical foundations and research evidence concerning the application of AI in inclusive higher education\. It adopts an integrative literature review approach to synthesize published research on AI\-powered assistive technologies, adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, and educational support services\. Particular attention is given to three dimensions of inclusion: accessibility, personalization, and student support\. Findings from existing reviews and a meta\-analysis indicate that AI\-based interventions have potential to improve learning outcomes and facilitate participation among students with disabilities\. However, the available evidence is heterogeneous, and much of the experimental research has been conducted outside mainstream higher education\. The article proposes an integrated conceptual framework connecting AI accessibility tools, personalized learning, and coordinated institutional support\. It concludes that AI can contribute to more equitable higher education when implemented through human\-centred, accessible, and ethically governed practices\.

## [Representation learning for low\-data protein fitness prediction using sequence–structure embeddings and graph neural networks](../publications/753674334c5296eb8bc3.md)

Chanoknun Phunnasorn; Narupat Hongdilokkul; Wasakorn Laesanklang; Charin Modchang; Tipaluck Krityakierne

Accurate prediction of mutational fitness effects remains challenging in low\-data protein engineering settings, where experimentally characterized variants are limited\. Although recent protein language models and structure\-aware neural networks have demonstrated strong performance on large\-scale datasets, the relative importance of structural information, pre\-trained embeddings, and optimization strategies under data\-constrained conditions remains insufficiently understood\. In this study, we investigate a graph\-based framework that integrates AlphaFold2\-derived protein structures, Masked Inverse Folding with Sequence Transfer \(MIF\-ST\) embeddings, and graph neural networks for protein fitness prediction using a dataset of 152 TEM \\\(\\beta \\\) \-lactamase variants\. Through controlled ablation experiments, we systematically evaluate the effects of structural quality, feature richness, pre\-trained embeddings, and automated hyperparameter optimization across both random train–test splits and mutation\-specific splits requiring generalization to unseen mutations\. Under standard random splits, simpler feature representations perform competitively because training and test samples follow similar distributions\. In contrast, under mutation\-specific distribution shift, models incorporating structural information and pre\-trained sequence–structure embeddings achieve considerably stronger predictive performance and improved generalization\. Among the evaluated configurations, the full framework combining AlphaFold2, MIF\-ST, and Optuna achieved the highest overall performance across the evaluation datasets\. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of structure\-aware representations depends strongly on the evaluation regime and highlight the importance of mutation\-specific generalization when designing data\-efficient protein fitness prediction frameworks\.

## [Designing cross\-sector leadership dialogue for successful aging: a forum\-based case study and preliminary participant evaluation](../publications/753a8f5469967a61f01f.md)

Myrto Pyrrou; Craig S\. Anderson; Hariklia Proios

Background Translating evidence on brain health and healthy aging into coordinated action is challenging because responsibility is distributed across health care, communities, institutions, and policy\. An interdisciplinary forum was developed as a university\-based pilot educational workshop to bring different professional and sectoral perspectives into structured discussion of barriers to applying knowledge in practice\. Methods We describe the design, implementation, and preliminary evaluation of the full\-day Leadership Forum on Successful Aging and Longevity, held at Adelphi University on April 24, 2026\. Thirty\-five people attended, including three organizers, five additional invited contributors, and 27 general attendees\. The program moved from personal reflection and scientific input to moderated cross\-sector dialogue, facilitated diagnostic group work, structured report\-back, and leadership\-oriented reflection\. The descriptive evaluation drew on anonymous opening reflection cards, Sense\-Making Workshop flipcharts, facilitator\-recorded notes from the leadership activity, and an anonymous post\-forum questionnaire completed by 19 of the 27 general attendees\. Results All 19 questionnaire respondents selected the most favorable response for the venue, organization and planning, timing and duration, and willingness to attend a future forum\. Eighteen selected the most favorable responses for presentations, opportunities for interaction, and overall experience\. Opening reflections associated aging well with independence, health, family, support, and quality of life\. Workshop outputs highlighted fragmented services, continuity and coordination of care, affordability, everyday environments, budgets, incentives, and tensions between prevention and existing economic or organizational arrangements\. Open\-ended feedback also identified practical areas for refinement, including room audio, microphone quality, and access to presentation materials\. Conclusion The forum was well received by respondents, with materials reflecting discussion of aging well that extended beyond health care and individual choices to relationships, services, environmental conditions, and organizational responsibility\. The case provides a practical example of how scientific input, cross\-sector dialogue, diagnostic group work, and leadership\-oriented reflection can be combined within a one\-day forum\. The findings are descriptive and context\-specific and do not demonstrate learning, behavior change, sustained collaboration, or longer\-term impact\. Future iterations could involve older adults and relevant community organizations more directly and plan follow\-up from the outset where continued dialogue or action is intended\.

## [Dijital Sağlık ve Yapay Zeka Uygulamaları](../publications/7540d76b44390b3b9804.md)



Sağlık hizmetlerinde dijital dönüşüm, teknolojik yeniliklerin sağlık sistemlerine dahil edilmesiyle birlikte hizmet sunumu, klinik karar verme, sağlık profesyonellerinin görevleri ve eğitim süreçlerinde köklü değişiklikler meydana getiren kapsamlı bir dönüşüm sürecidir\. Yapay zeka, nesnelerin interneti, akıllı hastane sistemleri, sanal öğrenme ortamları ve dijital navigasyon teknolojileri, sağlık hizmetlerinin erişilebilirliğini, verimliliğini, güvenliğini ve kalitesini artırma potansiyeliyle bu dönüşümün temel bileşenleri arasında yer almaktadır\. “Dijital Sağlık ve Yapay Zeka Uygulamaları” başlıklı bu kitap, sağlık alanındaki dijitalleşme sürecini farklı disiplinler ve uygulama alanları üzerinden ele alarak güncel teknolojik gelişmelerin sağlık hizmetlerine yansımalarını bütüncül bir bakış açısıyla değerlendirmeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Bu kapsamda yapay zeka destekli klinik uygulamalar, akıllı sağlık sistemleri, dijital sağlık altyapıları, sağlık profesyonellerinin değişen rolleri ve dijital yetkinlikleri ile teknoloji destekli sağlık eğitimi gibi konular ele alınmaktadır\. Ayrıca dijital teknolojilerin sağlık kurumlarının işleyişine, hizmet sunum süreçlerine ve hasta deneyimine etkileri incelenerek sağlık hizmetlerinde yaşanan dönüşümün teknolojik, mesleki ve organizasyonel boyutları değerlendirilmektedir\. Eserde, dijital teknolojilerin yalnızca teknik özelliklerine değil, aynı zamanda klinik uygulamalara, sağlık yönetimine, mesleki yeterliklere, eğitim süreçlerine ve hasta deneyimine olan etkilerine de odaklanılmaktadır\. Bu yönüyle kitap, yapay zekanın sağlık hizmetlerindeki dönüştürücü rolünü disiplinler arası bir çerçevede tartışırken dijital dönüşümün sunduğu fırsatları, mevcut sınırlılıkları ve gelecekteki gelişim alanlarını ortaya koymaktadır\. Kitabın, sağlık bilimleri, sağlık bilişimi ve ilgili disiplinlerde çalışan araştırmacılar, akademisyenler, öğrenciler ve sağlık profesyonelleri için güncel bir başvuru kaynağı oluşturması, dijital sağlık uygulamalarına ilişkin bilimsel bilgi birikimine katkı sağlaması ve gelecekteki araştırmalara yeni bakış açıları sunması hedeflenmektedir\.

## [РЫНОК СОЦИАЛЬНО ВРЕДНЫХ ТОВАРОВ И УСЛУГ: ОЦЕНКА УРОВНЯ ОПАСНОСТИ](../publications/75460e262630570950ba.md)

Н\. Н\. Давидчук; Е\.В\. МЕЙДЕР

Рынок социально вредных товаров — это многогранная проблема, требующая системного подхода, который объединяет меры государственного контроля, просвещения граждан и профилактики негативных последствий\. Цель исследования — изучение специфики рынка социально вредных товаров и услуг и разработка алгоритма его регулирования, направленного на формирование комплексной стратегии, включающей: снижение спроса за счёт информационной работы, просвещения и профилактических программ; ограничение предложения через контроль доступности и регулирование оборота; смягчение ущерба для здоровья населения за счёт мер защиты и поддержки; минимизацию социально\-экономических последствий, связанных с потреблением таких товаров и услуг\. В рамках исследования проведена разработка языковой программной модели, которая связывает ключевые индикаторы для оценки и прогнозирования в сфере вредных товаров и услуг\. Модель позволит: оценивать уровень опасности товаров и услуг, а также их безопасность, прогнозировать риски аварий и уровень токсичности, использовать методы искусственного интеллекта для анализа данных и поддержки принятия решений\. Этот подход обеспечит научно обоснованную основу для регулирования рынка и снижения его негативного воздействия на общество\. The market of socially harmful goods is a multifaceted problem that requires a systematic approach that combines measures of state control, education of citizens and prevention of negative consequences\. The purpose of the study is to study the specifics of this market and develop an algorithm for regulating it in order to form a comprehensive strategy that includes: reducing demand through information work, education and preventive programs; limiting supply by controlling accessibility and regulating turnover; mitigating damage to public health by implementing protection and support measures; minimizing socio\-economic consequences associated with consumption of these goods and services\. As part of this research, a software language model was developed to link key indicators for evaluating and forecasting harmful goods and services\. The model will allow you to assess the level of danger of goods and services, as well as their safety, predict the risks of accidents and the level of toxicity, and use artificial intelligence methods to analyze data and support decision\-making\. This approach will provide a scientifically sound basis for regulating the market and reducing its negative impact on society\.

## [A conceptual framework: what is impactful learning? A case study of teaching organic chemistry for pre\-medical students](../publications/754f7fee546e0afde50b.md)

Lam H\. Nguyen

Organic chemistry occupies a contested place in pre\-health education: required of nearly all premedical students, experienced as difficult, and justified on grounds that it “teaches you to think”, a claim too vague to evaluate or teach toward deliberately\. Existing frameworks do not resolve this tension\. This paper adopts a conceptual analysis approach, drawing on Ausubel&\#x27;s rote/meaningful learning distinction and the traditional transfer\-of\-learning literature, to propose impactful learning as a third pedagogical stage following rote and meaningful learning\. Impactful learning is defined as the stage where procedural and reasoning skills exercised in mastering a discipline&\#x27;s content become generalizable cognitive tools deployable outside that discipline\. Three key concepts are examined: the unit of transfer \(the cognitive procedure, not the content\), the extraction dimension \(detachment of a practiced operation from the content that trained it\), and the conditions under which such transfer becomes pedagogically achievable\. These concepts are developed through three organic chemistry tasks as worked examples—resonance structures as constraint\-satisfaction reasoning, reaction mechanisms as iterative\-hypothesis testing, and stereochemistry as symbolic\-to\-spatial translation—each mapped onto a corresponding form of clinical reasoning\. We further propose a four\-step explicit transfer scaffolding model \(Name, Perform, Bridge, Generate\) as a testable methodological companion, grounded in Gick and Holyoak&\#x27;s analogical transfer research and Detterman&\#x27;s critique of spontaneous far transfer\. The paper argues that naming impactful learning as a distinct pedagogical target, rather than assuming it as an automatic byproduct of meaningful understanding, has direct implications for instructional design and assessment in service courses across STEM disciplines\.

## [Conditional Mean Flows: Few\-Step Densities for Simulation\-Based Inference](../publications/75552750cf3608da83cf.md)

Jonas Arruda; Jan Hasenauer; Stefan T\. Radev

Flow matching has emerged as a powerful generative family for simulation\-based inference \(SBI\)\. However, sampling and density evaluation require numerical integration at inference time\. This makes posterior sampling in neural posterior estimation costly\. More importantly, it can make repeated likelihood evaluation prohibitively expensive and impractical for Markov chain Monte Carlo \(MCMC\) sampling, which may require thousands of repeated density evaluations\. Here, we develop conditional mean flows for posterior and likelihood approximation, combining few\-step sampling with tractable density evaluation\. We show that the mean flow objective identifies conditional flow maps and that independent masking enables direct estimation of marginal likelihoods\. We evaluate both posterior and likelihood estimation across several tasks and show that conditional mean flows retain the flexibility of flow\-based density estimators while significantly reducing inference time\. In particular, single\-step conditional mean flow density evaluation yields estimation error comparable to 200\-step flow matching while enabling about 200\-fold faster downstream MCMC sampling\.

Hisato Segoe; Jutaro Abe; Shinsuke Hirabayashi; Risa Nakashima; Kazumi Oura; Yukayo Terashita; Yuko Cho; Daichi Sajiki; Hideki Muramatsu; Atsushi Manabe
