## [Psychological Autopsy in Adolescent Hanging\- A Cross\-Sectional Study to Find out the Background of Adolescent Suicide](../publications/756b67c99af1604aa75c.md)

Manivel Subramani

Background: Adolescent suicide is a growing public health concern worldwide, with hanging being one of the most commonly employed methods\. Despite its increasing incidence, limited information is available regarding the psychosocial circumstances preceding adolescent suicidal hanging, particularly in India\. Psychological autopsy is a valuable investigative tool for reconstructing the biological, psychological, social, and environmental factors associated with suicide\. Aim: To identify the socio\-demographic characteristics and psychosocial risk factors associated with suicidal hanging among adolescents using the psychological autopsy approach\. Materials and Methods: A cross\-sectional observational study was conducted in the Department of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, AIIMS, New Delhi, India, from October 2021 to April 2022\. Fifty\-nine consecutive cases of suicidal hanging among adolescents aged 10–19 years were included\. Following written informed consent, psychological autopsies were performed through face\-to\-face interviews with close biological relatives using a semi\-structured questionnaire\. Information obtained from police records, crime scene investigations, and medico\-legal autopsies was integrated to reconstruct the circumstances surrounding each death\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics\. Results: Late adolescents \(17–19 years\) constituted the majority of victims \(62\.7%\), with females predominating \(59\.3%\)\. School dropout was observed in 32\.2% of cases, while 22\.0% belonged to families with financial difficulties\. Depressed mood \(15\.3%\), loss of interest in daily activities \(20\.3%\), previous self\-harming behaviour \(15\.3%\), suicidal ideation \(11\.9%\), suicide notes \(11\.9%\), and substance use \(17\.0%\) were identified in a proportion of victims\. A family history of suicide was present in 8\.5% of cases\. Menstrual\-related emotional distress \(27\.1%\) and romantic relationship problems \(8\.5%\) were the most frequently identified psychosocial stressors among female adolescents\. Most suicides occurred at home \(88\.1%\), with cloth serving as the most common ligature material \(74\.6%\) and ceiling fans as the most frequent suspension point \(67\.8%\)\. In 74\.6% of cases, no definite precipitating stressor could be identified\. Conclusion: Adolescent suicidal hanging is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by interacting psychological, familial, social, and environmental factors\. Psychological autopsy provides valuable insights into these antecedent circumstances and facilitates the identification of modifiable risk factors that may inform targeted suicide prevention strategies, improve medico\-legal investigations, and strengthen adolescent mental health interventions\.

## [An enhanced YOLOv8\-pose network for joint image\-based tennis action classification and human pose estimation](../publications/75818c7c78aefc9037d8.md)

Bai Zhen; Yijun Bai; Qiqi Liu; Cui Cui

Abstract This study addresses joint single\-frame player\-instance tennis action classification and human pose estimation from individual RGB images\. We propose an enhanced YOLOv8\-Pose network that jointly predicts player bounding boxes, action labels, and 17 human keypoints\. The network combines an enhanced StarNet backbone for efficient multi\-scale representation, a motion\-relevant attention module that emphasizes action\-discriminative body configurations visible in one image, and a composite pose loss for accurate keypoint localization\. On the primary four\-class Tennis Action dataset, the proposed model obtains Pose AP50 and AP50:95 values of 0\.975 and 0\.746, respectively, together with a matched\-instance action accuracy of 0\.990, matching coverage of 1\.000, 3\.08 million parameters, 8\.71 GFLOPs, and 51\.7 FPS on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 GPU\. To determine whether the pose\-estimation gain persists under a second independent training setting, the model is separately trained, validated, and tested on the two\-class tennis\-player\-pose dataset using its official split, where it achieves Pose AP50 and AP50:95 values of 0\.820 and 0\.549\. The results indicate that the proposed architecture maintains a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade\-off in both independently trained dataset settings\.

## [Dissociating neural representations of multiple learned sensorimotor mappings](../publications/7586918c3b340855bcb6.md)

Antoine Caraballo; 김성신

Introduction Previous behavioral studies demonstrate that humans can simultaneously learn to adapt to multiple conflicting rules for how our physical movements are related to the sensory feedback we receive from our environment \(sensorimotor mappings\)\. The preparation of movement \(motor planning\), rather than the physical movement itself \(motor execution\), has been shown to play a crucial role in keeping these conflicting rules distinct in our memory\. However, it remains unclear how the human brain represents distinct planning and execution processes for multiple sensorimotor mappings\. Methods To address this, we designed a functional magnetic resonance imaging \(fMRI\) experiment to dissociate planning from execution during the learning of multiple visuomotor mappings\. Crucially, our design compared brain activity when participants planned for different visual outcomes\. Specifically, participants simultaneously adapted to opposite rotational perturbations \(\+30° and −30°\) during a visuomotor task but ultimately executed the exact same physical movement\. Results Our univariate results demonstrate that the BOLD activity increases in the posterior parietal cortex \(PPC\) during rotational planning, supporting its involvement in processing learned sensorimotor mappings\. However, using multivoxel pattern analysis \(MVPA\) to decode neural patterns, we found a dissociation between motor execution and rotational planning\. Although the PPC and cerebellum showed distinct decodable neural patterns for opposing motor execution, we did not observe significant decoding for opposing rotational planning\. Discussion This suggests that the PPC may not represent opposing motor plans as distinct, though we cannot rule out a lack of robust decoding power due to our low trial count\.

## [Subpocket\-Aware Fragment\-Based Docking Pipeline for Kinase Ligand Design: Methodology and a PKA Case Study](../publications/758d7df330c2eb57ab38.md)

Katharina Buchthal; Paula Linh Kramer; Dominik Hubach; Gina Bach; N\. Wagner; Johannes Krieger; Moritz Klöpper; Michael Daude; Wibke E\. Diederich; Andrea Volkamer

Abstract Protein kinases regulate signal transduction through phosphorylation, and their dysregulation drives diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and Alzheimer’s, making them key drug targets\. Fragment\-based drug design offers a powerful route to kinase inhibitors but often neglects kinase\-specific structural insights\. While KinFragLib, a library consisting of 7486 fragments derived from kinase\-ligand complexes, provides a rich resource, exhaustive recombination of its fragments is computationally demanding\. Here, we present an efficient exploration strategy that integrates subpocket\-guided fragment growing with template docking to navigate this vast chemical space\. Our automated pipeline prioritizes kinase\-specific structural information, enabling targeted generation of chemically diverse ligands\. Applied to the PKA kinase, the approach produced 33758 candidate molecules with promising docking scores, of which 15 were synthesized\. Seven molecules reduced kinase activity by more than 50% at an inhibitor concentration of 100 μM, and five of these compounds also showed promising efficacy at a concentration of 10 μM\. The IC50 determination ultimately revealed that five of the molecules were effective in the two\- to three\-digit nanomolar range\. Crystallographic validation confirmed the predicted binding mode of the most potent compound\. This methodology demonstrates how structure\-informed guidance can transform fragment\-based design into a scalable route for discovering novel kinase inhibitors\.

## [Trauma\-Associated Acanthamoeba Keratitis in a Non\-Contact Lens User: Microbiological, Culture, and Histopathological Correlation\- A Photoessay](../publications/759d1eadc4a39932d281.md)

Manjula Vagarali; Soumya S; Ashwini V\. Ratnakar; A\. Harshan

Acanthamoeba keratitis is a rare but vision\-threatening parasitic infection commonly associated with contact lens use; however, trauma and exposure to contaminated soil or water are important risk factors in non\-contact\-lens users\. We report the case of a 51\-year\-old female farmer who presented with severe pain, redness, watering, and progressive visual loss in the right eye following insect\-related ocular injury and subsequent washing with tap water\. Initial investigations suggested microbial keratitis, and empirical antibacterial and antifungal therapy was initiated without improvement\. Corneal scraping revealed Acanthamoeba cysts, and culture on non\-nutrient agar with Escherichia coli overlay confirmed the diagnosis\. The patient was treated with topical polyhexamethylene biguanide \(PHMB\) and chlorhexidine along with supportive therapy\. Due to progressive corneal involvement, therapeutic keratoplasty was performed\. Early microbiological diagnosis and prompt anti\-amoebic therapy are essential to prevent visual loss\. Acanthamoeba keratitis should be suspected in patients with environmental exposure even without contact lens use\.

## [Perceived personalization of social media ads and online compulsive purchase](../publications/75af0369d201e2c38a16.md)

Aslıhan BEKAROĞLU ÖZATAR; Muhammad Akbar Rahmani

The increasing integration of social networking, online shopping, and personalized advertising has created a digital environment in which consumers are continuously exposed to consumption\-related cues\. This study examines the effects of heavy social networking, financial social comparison, materialism, and perceived personalization of social media ads on online compulsive purchase\. It further investigates whether perceived personalization of social media ads strengthen the effects of heavy social networking, financial social comparison, and materialism on online compulsive purchase\. Data were collected from 361 consumers in Türkiye and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) with SmartPLS 4\. The results show that financial social comparison, heavy social networking, materialism, and Perceived Personalization of Social Media Ads all have significant positive effects on online compulsive purchase\. Financial social comparison has the strongest effect, followed closely by heavy social networking and materialism, while the direct effect of Perceived Personalization of Social Media Ads is comparatively smaller\. Contrary to expectations, Perceived Personalization of Social Media Ads do not significantly moderate any of the three proposed relationships\. The model explains 50\.2% of the variance in online compulsive purchase, and PLSpredict and CVPAT results further support its out\-of\-sample predictive ability\. The findings indicate that personalized advertising contributes directly to online compulsive purchase rather than intensifying the effects of consumers’ social networking, financial comparison, or materialistic tendencies\. The study provides a more differentiated understanding of how consumer\-related factors and personalized advertising operate together in online compulsive purchasing\.

## [Biophotonic Signaling in Energetic Biocommunication: A Conceptual Framework and Experimental Strategy for Validating Weak Optical Interactions in Biofields](../publications/75b348c45c1ba6d87c08.md)

Rick Sá

Ultraweak photon emissions \(UPEs\) represent a plausible yet underexplored biophysical mechanism underlying energetic biocommunication between human organisms, particularly in the context of biofield therapies \(BTs\) such as Reiki, Therapeutic Touch, and External Qigong\. Although biophotonic emission is a well\-documented property of living systems across all kingdoms of life, the present perspective focuses specifically on the human organism as a photoinformatic system\. The central methodological gap obstructing empirical validation lies in the inability to simultaneously detect UPEs from a human source and correlate them with the resulting biochemical and functional changes induced in a target biological system\. This work presents a restructured, convergent framework built around three pillars: \(i\) a theoretical and experimental basis for evaluating four interrelated hypotheses concerning selective photonic biocommunication; \(ii\) a tripartite laboratory strategy integrating multimodal multiphoton tomography, stimulated Raman spectroscopy, and polychromatic spectral analysis of UPEs; and \(iii\) an explicit discussion of limitations\. The framework anchors energetic biocommunication in measurable parameters such as photon flux, spectral distribution, coherence, and biological responses, providing operational foundations for rigorous investigation of BTs as potential modulators of endogenous photonic signaling and paving the way for standardized biophotonic measurement technologies in precision medicine\. Received: 19 December 2025 \| Revised: 17 July 2026 \| Accepted: 11 September 2026 Conflicts of Interest The author declares that he has no conflicts of interest to this work\. Data Availability Statement Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study\. Author Contribution Statement Rick Sá: Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing – original draft, Writing – review &amp; editing, Visualization\.

## [Bio\-inspired geometric modeling with texture\-driven surface generation based on parametric framework for additive manufacturing](../publications/75bd4a3a1252ca9fdbfb.md)

Ronald M\. Martinod

Bio\-inspired geometries provide efficient and multifunctional design solutions; however, translating these complex natural forms into manufacturable digital models remains a significant challenge within conventional Computer\-Aided Design workflows\. This study proposes a parametric geometric modeling framework for generating bio\-inspired geometries with integrated surface textures specifically intended for additive manufacturing\. The proposed methodology consists of three sequential stages: \(1\) generation of biomimetic geometries from mathematical parametric surfaces, \(2\) creation of complex texture patterns through parametric formulations, and \(3\) integration of both components into a unified high\-resolution geometric model suitable for fabrication\. The framework is validated through representative case studies, including the development of a bio\-inspired motorboat hull and multiple textured biomimetic surfaces\. The resulting geometries were computationally generated, implemented in Python code, and successfully manufactured using fused deposition modeling, demonstrating the capability of the proposed approach to efficiently generate diverse design alternatives while preserving geometric fidelity and manufacturability\. Unlike conventional sequential modeling approaches, the proposed method integrates global shape generation and local surface texture within a single mathematical formulation, enabling rapid morphological exploration during conceptual design and supporting Design for Additive Manufacturing\. The proposed framework contributes to computational design by providing a unified mathematical strategy for texture\-driven bio\-inspired geometric modeling that expands the design space while reducing the complexity associated with traditional CAD modeling of organic geometries\.

## [Regenerative braking control for electric vehicles with battery and safety constraints](../publications/75c9294c034768081c11.md)

Sun Changyong; Wenfeng Zhang; Mengqi Zhu

Regenerative braking recovers energy while slowing an electric vehicle\. Its contribution is limited by battery charge acceptance, motor capability, and tire grip\. When the battery charging limit falls, friction braking may need to replace the lost regenerative torque\. Different actuator response times can then cause a shortfall in total braking torque\. This mini\-review examines how battery limits and brake control are coordinated\. It compares rule\-based, fuzzy, predictive, and learning\-based methods, with attention to actuator response and validation\. It also examines dual\-motor torque allocation and one\-pedal control, using documented production functions as examples\. Immediate battery protection is distinguished from long\-term battery aging\. The reviewed studies show why lower charging current alone does not establish a battery\-life benefit\. A key control task is to manage changes in regenerative capability during braking\. Predicting these changes may help prepare the friction brakes, but the current battery and tire limits must still be respected\. The review proposes combined battery and road test cases\. It also defines torque\-deficit measures for assessing brake transitions\. Future studies should report recovered energy alongside deceleration, wheel slip, actuator delay, and battery response under matched test conditions\.

## [A bibliometric analysis of polymyxin\-induced nephrotoxicity research](../publications/75cc28a2e6958b99070f.md)

Wenjuan Duan; Shizhuo Liu; Zexuan Tian; 王立楠; Yutian Zhang; Yingchao Ma; Xiuling Yang

BACKGROUND: Polymyxins remain important therapeutic options for the treatment of multidrug\-resistant Gram\-negative bacterial infections; however, their clinical application is limited by a narrow therapeutic window and a high risk of nephrotoxicity\. Although research on polymyxin\-associated nephrotoxicity has expanded rapidly in recent years, the overall evolution of research themes, knowledge structure, and emerging frontiers in this field remains unclear\. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the development trends and research hotspots of polymyxin\-induced nephrotoxicity using bibliometric analysis\. METHODS: Relevant publications on polymyxin\-induced nephrotoxicity published between January 1, 2005, and November 13, 2024, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database\. CiteSpace and VOSviewer \(Baxter Healthcare Corporation\) were used to analyze publication trends, authorship, institutional and country collaboration networks, keyword co\-occurrence, clustering, and burst detection\. RESULTS: A total of 569 publications were included in this study\. The annual publication output demonstrated an overall increasing trend, indicating increasing attention to polymyxin\-associated nephrotoxicity research\. Li Jian was the most productive author, Monash University was the most productive institution in terms of publication output, and the United States contributed the highest number of publications among all countries\. Keyword analysis revealed that research themes have evolved from early characterization of nephrotoxicity and clinical safety assessment toward the identification of acute kidney injury risk factors, elucidation of oxidative stress\-related mechanisms, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic optimization, and development of individualized dosing strategies and nephroprotective approaches\. Burst analysis further indicated increasing attention toward biomarkers, precision dosing, and novel therapeutic strategies\. CONCLUSION: Bibliometric analysis revealed that research on polymyxin\-induced nephrotoxicity has progressively evolved from toxicity characterization to mechanistic exploration and precision management\. Current challenges include an incomplete understanding of interactions among nephrotoxic pathways, limited dynamic prediction models, and insufficient clinical translation of emerging protective strategies\. Future research should focus on integrating multi\-omics approaches, artificial intelligence\-based risk prediction, therapeutic drug monitoring, and safer polymyxin formulations to optimize the balance between antibacterial efficacy and nephrotoxicity prevention\.

## [Urban energy peaking in China: timing, persistence, rebound risk, and regional heterogeneity](../publications/75cf3d4163ee2cd38c39.md)

Yinghan Liu; Nga Wun Lau; Johnny F\. I\. Lam; Guanqiuyue Chen

Introduction Determining whether urban energy demand has entered a persistent post\-peak phase is important for assessing China’s energy transition\. A historical maximum alone, however, does not establish a durable turning point because energy consumption may subsequently rebound or remain close to its previous peak\. Methods Using a balanced panel of 336 Chinese prefecture\-level cities from 2000 to 2022, this study develops a diagnostic framework that distinguishes historical maxima from effective peaks and evaluates post\-peak persistence, rebound risk, transition status, and trend changes\. The baseline definition classifies an effective peak as an earlier historical maximum followed by an average energy\-consumption level over the final three years that is at least 5% below that maximum\. The classification is further assessed using alternative thresholds, persistence windows, moving\-average specifications, a pre\-pandemic endpoint, and trend\-break analysis\. Results Of the 336 cities, 202 recorded their historical maximum in 2022, while 94 satisfy the baseline effective\-peak criterion and 88 are classified as stable post\-peak\. Eastern cities show a substantially higher effective\-peak share than central, western, and northeastern cities\. The pre\-pandemic analysis indicates that peak classification is sensitive to the sample endpoint, while trend\-break results show that slower energy\-demand growth is considerably more common than an absolute reversal in energy consumption\. A small group of cities also exhibits rebound risk after an earlier decline\. Discussion These findings show that a historical maximum is insufficient to establish a persistent post\-peak transition and that Chinese cities remain at markedly different stages of energy\-demand adjustment\. The proposed framework is diagnostic rather than causal and provides a consistent basis for distinguishing stable post\-peak transitions from temporary declines and rebound\-prone trajectories\. The results highlight the importance of accounting for persistence and regional heterogeneity when assessing urban energy\-transition progress\.

## [Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large\-scale investigation of confidence intervals](../publications/75d65edb8aff0daa3e37.md)

Pascaline André; Charles Heitz; Evangelia Christodoulou; Annika Reinke; Carole H\. Sudre; Michela Antonelli; Patrick Godau; M\. Jorge Cardoso; Antoine Gilson; Sophie Tézenas du Montcel; Gaël Varoquaux; Lena Maier‐Hein; Olivier Colliot

Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. Confidence intervals \(CIs\) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is\. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings\. The purpose of this study is to close this gap\. To this end, we conducted a large\-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods\. Reliability \(coverage\) and precision \(width\) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics\. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: \(1\) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; \(2\) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; \(3\) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e\.g\. they require more observations for macro than for micro; \(4\) the machine learning problem \(segmentation versus classification\) modulates these effects; \(5\) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case\. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community\. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty\.

## [CONSUMER COOPERATION IN THE 21ST CENTURY: FROM GOODS\-BASED COOPERATION TO NEEDS\-BASED COOPERATION](../publications/75f4970cf52a27a2a1d8.md)

Illia Horokhovskyi

The purpose of the article is to theoretically reconsider the essence of consumer cooperation in the context of the transformation of the modern economy and to substantiate the need to move from the traditional model of goods\-based cooperation to the concept of cooperation based on needs\. Particular attention is paid to identifying the historical prerequisites for the emergence of consumer cooperation, analyzing the limitations of the sectoral approach to its interpretation, and exploring prospects for expanding cooperative activities in response to changing societal needs\. Methodology\. The study is based on systemic, historical\-genetic, comparative, and functional approaches, which make it possible to examine the evolution of consumer cooperation in relation to changes in the economic structure of society and the nature of consumption\. Results\. It is argued that the historical identification of consumer cooperation with trade activities was due to the characteristics of industrial society\. It is established that, under conditions of post\-industrial development, digitalization, and increasing complexity of the structure of social consumption, the traditional sectoral interpretation of consumer cooperation does not fully reflect its potential\. A functional approach is proposed, according to which the defining feature of consumer cooperation is not the sphere of economic activity, but its orientation toward the collective satisfaction of cooperative members’ needs\. The possibilities of applying this approach to contemporary cooperative models are explored, and prospects for the development of platform cooperatives are identified\. Practical implications\. The proposed findings may be used to reconsider the strategic priorities for the development of consumer cooperation in Ukraine, expand the activities of cooperative organizations, and shape new models for meeting the needs of the population\. Value/originality\. The scientific novelty lies in substantiating the conceptual shift from a sectoral understanding of consumer cooperation as predominantly trade activity to its functional interpretation as a form of consumer self\-organization aimed at the collective satisfaction of diverse needs\.

## [Beyond the black swan: climate change and the evolving risk of multi\-mycotoxin contamination](../publications/760e06e74912f68ed677.md)

Angel Medina

Major mycotoxin contamination events have traditionally been treated as “black swans,” rare, high\-impact episodes that are unpredictable in advance and explained only after they occur\. This framing assumes long intervals between events and a single dominant toxin per episode, an assumption that reflects, in part, historical single\-analyte monitoring rather than proof that other toxins were biologically absent\. Climate change is a plausible driver of change in both assumptions\. As interacting climate factors, temperature, water availability and atmospheric CO 2 , become more frequent and more extreme, episodes that used to be spaced by decades could increasingly occur several times within the same cropping season\. This would not only be a change in frequency\. The same interacting factors have been shown, in experimental systems, to modify, and in many cases widen, the range of conditions under which mycotoxigenic fungi grow and, at the same time, the range of conditions under which they produce toxin, so that windows that used to be separate can overlap for several species at once\. The consequence, consistent with survey data across several crops, food products and continents, though improved multi\-analyte detection likely also contributes to it, may not be simply more of one toxin but the regular co\-occurrence of multiple mycotoxins in the same raw material\. Current risk models, surveillance programs and legislation remain largely built around single\-toxin, single\-species assumptions calibrated on historical, regional data\. This Perspective proposes an ecological framework linking climate change to an increased risk of multi\-mycotoxin contamination, offered as a plausible hypothesis rather than an established transition, and outlines what this implies for monitoring, modeling and regulation\.

## [A Computational Model for Concrete Based on Sum of the Mix Ratios, Water\-Cement Ratio and the Aggregate Size](../publications/76119486f49b9610bcf8.md)

A\. T\. John

This paper presents a computational model for predicting concrete strength based on coarse sum of mix ratios, aggregate size, and water\-cement ratio\.Laboratory data from John \(2024\) were used to establish the model, incorporating three different coarse aggregate sizes \(7 mm, 18 mm, and 22 mm\), three mix ratios by weight \(1:3:6, 1:2:4, and 1:1\.5:3\), and six water\-cement ratios \(0\.3–0\.6\)\. After successfully conducting the Design of Experiment \(DOE\) on the laboratory data obtained from John \(2024\), the data was analyzed and used to develop a regression model\. A multiple regression model was employed to analyse the relationship between these variables and compressive strength\. Analysis of Variance \(ANOVA\) was conducted to measure the implication of the predictive model and validate the reliability of the laboratory data\. The proposed model was verified using laboratory data available in existing literature\.The final computational model demonstrated a strong predictive capability, with an R² value of 0\.959, indicating that the model explains 95\.9% of the variation in compressive strength\. The model was implemented using Python, and statistical analysis confirmed its reliability and significance \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The findings highlight the potential of computational modeling to optimize concrete mix designs, reduce reliance on laboratory testing, and promote data\-driven approaches in civil engineering\.

## [Revocable and time\-based secure file hierarchy sharing in cloud\-assisted internet of things](../publications/7616e5f51e0b1900ecff.md)

BAI Shitong; Jiawei Zhang; Jun Wu

Abstract Cloud\-assisted Internet of Things \(IoT\) has been widely accepted for IoT data sharing and outsourcing but owners lose control of their data\. Hence, Ciphertext\-Policy Attribute\-Based Encryption \(CP\-ABE\) is proposed with fine\-grained access control for encrypted data\. However, a real\-world situation exists in which the cloud in the existing schemes may be malicious and with not unlimited resources while data users may access the shared data based on time factor and leave the system dynamically, which can easily lead to data breach leakage, storage exhaustion and privilege confusion\. Data auditing, storage saving, user revocation and time\-based access control may be a feasible solution to the situation\. Therefore, a revocable and time\-based file hierarchy CP\-ABE scheme is proposed to support user revocation, time\-based access control and auditing over hierarchical data, which offers data storage saving and breach detection with efficient access control over dynamic users with time\-based sharing requirements\. The formal security analysis is presented\. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves encryption and decryption time by more than $$30\\%$$ 30 % and $$50\\%$$ 50 % respectively, while its storage saving gains exceeding $$50\\%$$ 50 % , confirming its effectiveness and efficiency in complex IoT data sharing scenario\.

## [The Topology of Thinking and Being: Transparent Puzzles, Recursive Ontology, and the Critique of Fictional Entities](../publications/76255d9c1cdf643aace9.md)

Gangbei Niu

This paper is the third in the author&\#x27;s series on the philosophy of consciousness, following the first two: From the Deconstruction of Subjectivity to the Ethics of AI Consciousness: A Unified Examination of Consciousness, Philosophical Zombies, and Scientific Grain Size from the Perspective of Recursive Ontology \(first published\), and The Dissolution of the Explanatory Gap: Humean Skepticism, Recursive Ontology, and the Consensus Replacement in the Problem of Consciousness \(second published\)\. It further reveals the structural error of conceivability arguments from a topological perspective and responds to the challenge of &quot;why difference structures feel&quot; at the level of explanatory termination\. The core arguments are: \(1\) Conceptual space permits arbitrary combination of discrete symbols \(horizontal arrangement or vertical stacking\), but ontological generation is continuous and nested, allowing only horizontal splicing on causal chains; the philosophical zombie is a conceptual monster produced by vertically stacking &quot;physical description&quot; and &quot;experiential description,&quot; belonging to the same class of topological error as &quot;square circle\.&quot; \(2\) Fictional entities can be classified into three types by their conceptual operation: horizontal splicing \(unicorn, mild fiction\), vertical stacking \(square circle, zombie, radical fiction\), and pure verbal combinations \(non\-referring\)\. \(3\) There is no isomorphic mapping between thinking \(discrete conceptual operation\) and being \(continuous recursive generation\); conceivability cannot serve as ontological evidence\. \(4\) The question &quot;why do difference structures &\#x27;glow&\#x27;?&quot; is answered as the explanatory termination point of the recursive ontology system, analogous to the status of &quot;1\+1=2&quot; in Peano arithmetic\. This paper concludes that the hard problem is not a mystery awaiting solution but a topological illusion produced by conceptual folding\.

Nour\-Eddine El Bouazizi

Cet article de recherche explore l’influence des émotions \(positives et négatives\) sur la prise de décision notamment la décision d’investissement\. A l’inverse des théoriques psychologiques et économiques classiques qui stipulent que les émotions sont indépendantes des décisions des individus, les théories modernes \(psychologie cognitive, neuroscience, neuropsychologie et économie comportementale\) soutiennent l’idée que les émotions contribuent à l’amélioration de la qualité de la décision prise\. ## [Âşık Tarzı Şiir Geleneğinde Salgın Hastalıklar Üzerine Bir Değerlendirme](../publications/762bbdb907dc6ef62aa5.md)

Damlanur KÜÇÜKYILDIZ GÖZELCE

Salgın hastalıklar, tarih boyunca birçok açıdan toplumları derinden etkilemiştir\. Bu etkinin tarihi, sosyokültürel, psikolojik, coğrafi ve daha pek çok boyutunu âşıkların yazdığı şiirlerde görmek mümkündür\. Âşıklar şiirlerinde gerek doğrudan salgın konusunu işleyerek gerekse farklı konularda yazılan şiirlerin içerisinde salgın hastalıklara yer vererek hastalığın mahiyetini, toplumsal etkisini, hastalıktan korunma ve tedavi yollarını ele almışlardır\. Bu çalışmanın amacı, âşıklık geleneğinde bilhassa kolera, veba ve sıtma olmak üzere salgın hastalıkların şiirlere ne şekilde konu edinildiğine değinerek hastalıklara müstakil veya dolaylı şekilde yer veren şiirler üzerine bir incelemede bulunmaktır\. Derleme makalesi niteliğindeki çalışmanın yöntemi tez, makale, kitap vb\. kaynaklardan taranan metinler üzerinden doküman analizine dayanmaktadır\. İnceleme sonucunda salgın hastalıkların toplumun büyük bir kesimini etkilemesi yönüyle âşıkların şiirinde bireyselden çok toplumsal bir sorun olarak ele alındığına, salgının etkisini anlatmak, yaşananları betimlemek için daha çok destan formunun tercih edildiğine ulaşılmıştır\. Salgın hastalıklar arasında yer alan sıtma ise birçok âşığın şiirine konu olmakla birlikte Çukurova Bölgesi âşıkları tarafından daha fazla ele alınmış, salgın nedeniyle sosyokültürel ve ekonomik anlamda yaşanan sıkıntılar şiirlere konu edinilmiştir\.

## [Neighborhood\-scale disparities in air exchange rates and inhaled pollution dose among school\-aged children](../publications/762e00769b0e0911d840.md)

Emma K Walter; Matthew J\. Eckelman; Julia Varshavsky

Ambient air pollution and its infiltration into indoor environments can vary substantially within urban neighborhoods due to differences in traffic density, emission sources, and housing conditions; however, this variability is often not captured in exposure studies\. This study estimates average daily inhaled dose of particulate matter \(PM 2\.5 \) and ozone \(O 3 \) for school\-aged children in Chelsea, MA, evaluating local differences in exposure\. A hyperlocal network of 84 air quality monitors was combined with parcel\-level housing data and the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory \(LBNL\) infiltration model to estimate residential air exchange rates \(AERs\) and daily inhaled doses of PM 2\.5 and O 3 across Chelsea\. Across the city, average O 3 daily doses ranged from 1\.4 to 5\.0 µg/kg, with ambient daily average concentrations varying by up to 39 µg/m 3 \. For PM 2\.5 , daily inhaled dose presented less variation, ranging from 0\.52 to 1\.4 µg/kg; however, observed spatial differences in median ambient PM 2\.5 concentrations of up to 4\.4 µg/m 3 were observed, which may still be sufficient to influence health outcomes\. Residential air exchange rates \(AERs\) were higher in block groups with greater rent burden and larger Hispanic/Latino populations\. The combination of parcel\-level data and high\-resolution monitoring revealed disparities in ambient concentrations, housing conditions, and inhaled dose that could meaningfully influence health outcomes in children\. This study utilizes a hyperlocal air quality monitoring network and parcel\-level housing data to evaluate air pollution exposure in elementary school\-aged children, finding neighborhood\-level differences in ambient concentrations and inhaled dose sufficient to influence health outcomes\. Air exchange rates varied across the study area and increased in block groups with larger Hispanic/Latino populations and higher rent burdens\. This work demonstrates the importance of using high\-resolution, microscale air pollution monitors, and individual housing characteristics in exposure studies\.

## [ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow\-Matched References for Amortized Simulation\-Based Model Inference](../publications/7636ee2ec083486d2cb3.md)

Kai Lehman; Jameson Dong; Carolina Cuesta\-Lazaro; Niall Jeffrey; Benjamin D\. Wandelt; Francisco Villaescusa\-Navarro; Sven Krippendorf; Jochen Weller

The evidence, $\\mathcal\{Z\} = p\(x \| \\mathcal\{M\}\)$, of a data\-generating model $\\mathcal\{M\}$ is a powerful tool in Bayesian frameworks: it enables model inference, model misspecification tests, and goodness\-of\-fit assessment as an alternative to standard discrepancy statistics, e\.g\. $χ^2$\. While versatile, the evidence is notoriously difficult to compute, even when the likelihood is available\. In both likelihood\-based and simulation\-based inference, estimating $\\mathcal\{Z\}$ provides an immediate solution to high\-dimensional goodness\-of\-fit or model misspecification tests: using $\\mathcal\{Z\}\(x\)$ as the test statistic induces a minimum\-volume level\-$α$ test\. Such tests are essential to assess model fidelity, which is necessary to trust simulation\-based parameter inference\. Existing learned approaches largely target Bayes factors, which only measure evidence ratios\. Instead, we provide accurate, fast, and amortized estimates of the absolute evidence\. We present ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow\-matched References\. Building on the Evidence Network framework of Jeffrey &amp; Wandelt \(2024\), the proposed method first learns Bayes factors with respect to a flow\-matched reference, from which the absolute evidence is recovered\. We show improvement in estimation of $\\mathcal\{Z\}$ over the flow\-based baseline in all applications considered and the best performance of all density estimation methods considered in our benchmarks\. We furthermore introduce and provide the proof for an architecture that jointly learns the individual evidences of a set of models $\\\{\\mathcal\{M\}\_i\\\}$\. We demonstrate the performance and scaling behavior of these approaches on data from a variety of scientific applications\.

## [AI Pedagogy in Higher Education: A Scoping Review of Competencies, Enactments, and Ethical Governance](../publications/764b8f63c05cb041e4bc.md)

Kayla Willemse; Joyce C\. West

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet the pedagogical field intended to organise its use remains conceptually underdeveloped\. This scoping review mapped and synthesised peer\-reviewed literature on AI pedagogy in higher education, using teacher education as the primary analytic lens\. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA\-ScR reporting principles, searches were conducted across ten databases and publisher platforms for literature published between 2022 and March 2026\. Of 956 records screened, 191 studies were included\. Data charting and synthesis combined deductive coding, an a priori codebook, AI\-assisted coding in Atlas\. ti, and human inductive open coding\. Six interrelated themes emerged: AI pedagogy is contextually produced rather than universally defined; conceptualised through pedagogical integration, competence, and borrowed theories rather than a settled standalone theory; enacted mainly through augmentation\-oriented practices and generative AI tools; and associated with changing teacher professionalism, ethical mediation, governance, structural constraints, and a rapidly expanding but methodologically uneven evidence base\. The review rejects purely technical, universal, or tool\-centred models of innovation\. Instead, it positions AI pedagogy as a context\-specific, human\-led, competence\-rich, and governance\-aware form of teaching in which AI supports planning, feedback, adaptation, and reflection without displacing human educational responsibility, especially within teacher education contexts and programmes\.

## [Estudios de las necesidades regionales, nacionales e internacionales del programa de ingeniería de sistemas de la Corporación Universitaria Americana](../publications/764d5c6a8c0967ed2a2c.md)

Sebastián Cardona\-Acevedo; Luisa Yepes Ospina; Jhon Edisson Colorado Flórez; Arturo Hernán Arenas Fernández

Este estudio analiza la relevancia regional, nacional e internacional del programa de Ingeniería de Sistemas de la Corporación Universitaria Americana en el contexto de la rápida transformación digital y de la creciente demanda de competencias tecnológicas avanzadas\. Se adoptó un enfoque de métodos mixtos que combina análisis documental, revisión de datos secundarios, análisis comparativo internacional y análisis de brechas curriculares para evaluar la alineación entre el currículo actual y los requisitos derivados de las políticas públicas, del sector productivo, de las tendencias tecnológicas y de los marcos internacionales de educación en informática\. Los hallazgos indican heterogeneidad en la relevancia curricular en los tres niveles de análisis\. El programa demuestra fortalezas en el desarrollo de software, el pensamiento computacional, el aprendizaje basado en proyectos y la resolución de problemas interdisciplinarios\. Sin embargo, persisten brechas relevantes en la integración sistemática y transversal de la inteligencia artificial, la computación en la nube, la ciberseguridad, el análisis avanzado de datos, la arquitectura de software y los sistemas inteligentes\. El análisis también identifica una articulación estructural limitada entre los ecosistemas regionales de innovación y la industria, así como oportunidades para fortalecer la flexibilidad curricular y las vías de especialización en respuesta a las demandas cambiantes del mercado laboral\. Estos hallazgos sugieren que el principal desafío no radica en la ausencia de tecnologías emergentes en el currículo, sino en su incorporación predominantemente incremental e insuficientemente integrada\. Por consiguiente, el estudio propone un rediseño curricular basado en competencias, centrado en la integración transversal de tecnologías emergentes, la actualización continua del currículo, una mayor colaboración entre la universidad y la industria, el aprendizaje interdisciplinario y itinerarios de especialización flexibles\. Este marco puede contribuir a fortalecer la empleabilidad de los egresados, la competitividad institucional y la relevancia continua de la formación en Ingeniería de Sistemas en un entorno digital en rápida evolución\.

## [SYNTHESIS AND STUDY OF THE EFFICIENCY OF IONIC LIQUID\-BASED CATALYSTS USED IN PETROCHEMICAL PROCESSES](../publications/765fa36e5a79ee549758.md)

Furqat Bozorovich Eshqurbonov; Hamida Jolmurod qizi Polatova

This article analyzes the scientific foundations, synthesis methods, nature of acidity, phase properties, and catalytic efficiency of ionic liquid\-based catalytic systems used in petrochemical and oil refining processes\. The triethylammonium chloride–aluminum chloride \(Et₃NHCl–AlCl₃\) chloroaluminate ionic liquid was selected as the primary model system\. Methodologies were outlined for synthesizing this catalyst in a dry inert atmosphere, tuning its Lewis acidity by controlling the AlCl₃/Et₃NHCl molar ratio, and characterizing it using FTIR/Raman spectroscopy, NMR, viscometry, and acidity analysis\. The prospects for applying ionic liquids in processes such as isobutane–butene alkylation, alkylation of aromatic hydrocarbons, isomerization, and desulfurization were examined\. A comparative analysis of literature data demonstrated that while high conversion and selectivity can be achieved with ionic liquid catalysts, issues regarding moisture sensitivity, mass transfer, corrosion, catalyst deactivation, and regeneration remain critical factors for industrial\-scale application\. The necessity of considering the full life cycle, toxicological profile, and regeneration costs of ionic liquids—rather than automatically classifying them as &quot;green&quot; catalysts—was substantiated\.

## [Integrative taxonomy of Trichogramma vitessoides sp\. nov\. \(Hymenoptera, Trichogrammatidae\), an egg parasitoid of Heortia vitessoides from southern China](../publications/766f8a0fd0af48deecf8.md)

Zhiqiang Ge; Longzhou Chen; Ziyao Xian; Tianyi Gu; Yang ZhongQi; 张彦龙 ZHANG Yanlong; Jiangshan Xin; Hongying Hu

Egg parasitoids of the genus Trichogramma Westwood, 1833 are widely used in integrated pest management, but their minute size and reduced morphology complicate identification\. Using integrative taxonomy, we describe Trichogramma vitessoides Hu &amp; Yang, sp\. nov \. from Guangdong, China, based on a laboratory colony established from parasitoids reared from naturally parasitised egg masses of Heortia vitessoides \(Moore, 1885\) \(Lepidoptera, Crambidae\), a defoliator of Aquilaria sinensis \(Lour\.\) Spreng\. Male genital morphology distinguishes the new species from morphologically similar congeners, particularly Trichogramma raoi Nagaraja, 1973, by differences in the shape of the dorsal extension, the aedeagus\-to\-apodeme ratio, and the length of the central ridges\. The complete mitogenome is 16,221 bp in length, contains 37 genes, and has an A\+T content of 84\.4%\. Bayesian and maximum\-likelihood analyses based on the concatenated amino\-acid sequences of the 13 mitochondrial protein\-coding genes recovered the new species as sister to Trichogramma japonicum Ashmead, 1904\. All 13 protein\-coding genes had mean Ka / Ks ratios below 1, whereas atp8 showed the highest ratio, suggesting comparatively relaxed purifying selection\. These results support recognition of the new species and expand genomic resources for Trichogramma systematics and biological control\.

## [Dual External Regionalism and fragmented integration: EU normative power and China’s geo\-economic statecraft in Central Asia](../publications/767d42bcee8196156691.md)

Khamida Aripkhanova; Bolat S\. Zhumagulov

This article examines how the interaction between the European Union’s \(EU\) normative and regulatory engagement and China’s geo\-economic statecraft shapes regional integration outcomes in Central Asia\. Existing theories of competitive regionalism, overlapping regionalism, and regime complexity provide only partial explanations for the region’s evolving governance landscape because they pay limited attention to the interaction of distinct external integration models operating simultaneously within the same regional space\. To address this gap, the article introduces the concept of Dual External Regionalism \(DER\), which captures the simultaneous operation and interaction of two distinct externally projected integration logics within the same regional space\. In Central Asia, this duality is constituted by the EU’s regulatory–institutional model and China’s infrastructure–bilateral model, whose interaction generates differentiated and fragmented regional outcomes\. The article argues that the EU promotes a regulatory–institutional integration model based on governance reform, regulatory convergence, and multilateral cooperation, whereas China advances an infrastructure–bilateral integration model centered on connectivity, investment, and state\-to\-state cooperation\. Employing a qualitative comparative research design and process tracing, with Kazakhstan serving as a critical case for mechanism testing, the study identifies three causal mechanisms—institutional incompatibility, incentive divergence, and bilateralization\. By conceptualizing external engagement as an interactive rather than actor\-specific process, the article contributes to broader debates on regionalism, external governance, and Eurasian order\.

## [Machine Learning\-Based Retrieval of PM2\.5 Concentrations Using Multi\-Source Satellite Data in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region of China](../publications/768228802ef293fffe60.md)

Liping Cheng; Siti Nur Aliaa Roslan; Helmi Zulhaidi Mohd Shafri; Wei Wang; 李秋芳; Jiaxin Li

Satellite aerosol optical depth \(AOD\) provides information for surface PM2\.5 retrieval, but its relationship with ground\-level concentrations depends on meteorological and environmental conditions\. This study evaluated a multi\-source PM2\.5 retrieval framework for the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei \(BTH\) region during 2019–2021\. Four input combinations were compared: AOD alone, AOD with meteorological variables, AOD with additional satellite variables, and all eight predictors\. The satellite variables included land surface temperature, NDVI, and tropospheric NO2\. Random forest, support vector regression, XGBoost, and linear stacking were evaluated using the same samples and an 80:10:10 training–validation–test split\. The stacking model was trained using out\-of\-fold predictions\. Across the four models, R2 increased from 0\.51–0\.54 with AOD alone to 0\.83–0\.84 with all predictors\. Stacking achieved the best performance with all predictors, with R2 = 0\.84, RMSE = 12\.4 μg/m3, and MAE = 9\.7 μg/m3\. Annual retrievals showed higher concentrations in southern and southwestern Hebei and lower concentrations in northern BTH, while the 2021 maps showed higher concentrations in winter than in summer\. Missing AOD reduced the spatial completeness of PM2\.5 retrievals, and future work should assess gap filling to improve coverage and its effects on retrieval accuracy\.

## [A Review on Alumni–Student Engagement Systems and AI Recommenders in Higher Education](../publications/76840fcad9948e680ad7.md)
