## [DINÂMICA TEMPORAL DA RESPIRAÇÃO DO SOLO EM VARIEDADES DE Pinus caribaea](../publications/768c3ff4b787b4cccb8e.md)

Wanderson Benerval de Lucena; Maria Elisa Vicentini; Daniel Carlos Machado; Deysiele Oliveira Alves; Polyana Pereira; Kalil Nunes Candido

Este estudo analisou a variabilidade de curto prazo na emissão de CO2 e no influxo de O2 em Oxisol \(Haplic Acrustox\) sob duas variedades de Pinus caribaea \(Pinus caribaea var\. hondurensis \- PCH e Pinus caribaea var\. caribaea \- PCC\), localizado em Selvíria, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brasil\. Foram realizadas medidas repetidas ao longo do tempo, acompanhando a emissão de CO2 do solo \(FCO2\), o influxo de oxigênio \(iO2\), a temperatura do solo \(ST\) e a umidade do solo \(SM\), usando o sistema EGM\-5\. As coletas ocorreram em 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 e 20 de julho de 2022, numeradas de 1 a 6, indicando os dias de respiração do solo\. Os resultados indicaram que a emissão média de CO2 não apresentou diferenças significativas entre as variedades, embora tenha havido variação ao longo do tempo, com maior FCO2 na PCH no primeiro dia\. O influxo de O2 foi significativamente maior na área de PCC, que também apresentou valores superiores em quatro dos seis dias de medição\. A umidade do solo foi consistentemente maior na PCC, com média de 2,7% \(vol/vol\), enquanto a temperatura do solo foi significativamente mais alta na PCH, atingindo 30,5 ºC \(p &lt; 0,05\), em comparação a 29,5 ºC na PCC\. Conclui\-se que, embora as variedades de Pinus não afetem a emissão média de CO2, elas modulam de forma distinta os padrões temporais de emissão e influxo de O2, sugerindo que a escolha da variedade pode influenciar os processos microbianos e a dinâmica gasosa no solo a curto prazo\.

## [THE PHYSICO\-MATHEMATICAL INTELLIGENCE OF ENERGY FROM WIND EQUATIONS TO LEGAL FRAMEWORKS A Unified Theory of Wind Energy Physics, Mathematical Optimization, Artificial Intelligence, and Energy Law](../publications/7691b5a743cc543b9fda.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The Physico\-Mathematical Intelligence of Energy: From Wind Equations to Legal Frameworks by Dr\. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El\-Rakhawi \(DOI: 10\.5281/zenodo\.23459497\) establishes Physico\-Mathematical Energy Intelligence as a groundbreaking academic field integrating wind physics, mathematical optimization, artificial intelligence, and energy law\. The framework unfolds through four pillars: \(1\) Physical and Mathematical Foundations, exploring Navier\-Stokes equations, logarithmic wind profiles, Betz limit \(59\.3%\), Weibull distributions, and Blade Element Momentum theory; \(2\) AI and Optimization, featuring wake modeling via Jensen model, MILP/GA/PSO algorithms for wind farm layout optimization, LSTM networks for RUL prediction, and MPC for hybrid energy storage dispatch; \(3\) Engineering Applications, covering fluid\-structure interaction with Euler\-Bernoulli beam theory, smart blades with piezoelectric actuators, LVRT grid compliance, Morison equation for offshore hydrodynamics, and floating wind platforms; \(4\) Legal Frameworks, addressing EIA permitting, Feed\-in Tariffs, Contracts for Difference, PPAs with Force Majeure clauses, decommissioning bonds, Paris Agreement Article 6 carbon markets, WTO TRIMS challenges to local content requirements, and UNCLOS Article 56 for offshore wind in EEZs\. Novel concepts include physics\-informed neural networks for wind prediction, digital twins for virtual turbines, and intelligent wind energy civilization\. Applications span 15MW\+ offshore turbines, predictive maintenance reducing OPEX by 30%, and grid integration enabling 50%\+ renewable penetration\. Key equations: AEP optimization J = \(AEP·Re \- CAPEX \- OPEX\)/LCOE, wake deficit vi/v0 = 1 \- Σ\(1\-√\(1\-CT\)\)\(r0/\(r0\+k·dij\)\)², reliability Weibull f\(t\) = \(β/η\)\(t/η\)^\(β\-1\)e^\-\(t/η\)^β, Morison force F = ∫\(ρCM·πD²/4·u̇ \+ ½ρCDD\|u\|u\)dz\. This foundational treatise provides both rigorous scholarship and practical guidance for realizing intelligent wind energy systems\. Protected under international copyright with multiple citation formats \(APA, Chicago, MLA, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver\)\.

## [Edible films and coatings for sustainable food packaging: a critical review of materials, functional performance, sustainability, and industrial translation](../publications/76940966893960f104b6.md)

Abhivyakti Mishra; Manshuk Iskapalli; Divya Rai; Sapnita Shinde; Prasanna Prakash Bhalerao

Edible films and coatings \(EFCs\) are promising alternatives to conventional petrochemical food packaging due to their biodegradability and potential to extend food shelf life \(SL\)\. However, successful commercialization requires balancing mechanical strength, barrier performance, food safety, sensory acceptability, cost, and environmental sustainability\. This comparative literature review analyzes polysaccharide, protein, lipid, composite, and multilayer EFCs, emphasizing structure–property–performance relationships, formulation strategies, processing technologies, and multifunctional additives\. This study was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and ScienceDirect, covering representative publications between 2021 and June 2026\. The review examines fabrication methods; active and IP; nano\-enhanced edible films; encapsulation and controlled\-release systems; and the influence of formulation, plasticizer content, relative humidity \(RH\), temperature, film thickness, and food matrix composition on performance\. It also compares laboratory\-scale findings with practical food applications and distinguishes edible, bio\-based, biodegradable, compostable, and sustainable packaging within an LCA framework\. Furthermore, migration, toxicological, and allergenicity concerns, regulatory requirements, and commercial manufacturing challenges are critically discussed\. The review concludes that composite and multilayer EFCs offer superior multifunctional performance, but their industrial success depends on optimized formulations, standardized characterization, regulatory compliance, economic feasibility, and comprehensive life\-cycle assessment\.

## [The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret](../publications/76a06115c723459c4614.md)

Mohammad Pedramfar; Siamak Ravanbakhsh

Many modern learning systems are used not to select a single best action, but to sample diverse high\-quality outputs\. Examples include entropy\-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward\-guided generative modeling\. Motivated by these settings, we study tilted sampling: an online learning problem in which the goal is to sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward function\. We define sampling regret as the temperature\-normalized cumulative KL divergence between the learner&\#x27;s distribution and the Gibbs target, corresponding to the suboptimality gap in entropy\-regularized reward maximization\. Our framework generalizes recent sampling\-based and KL\-regularized formulations in bandits and reinforcement learning\. Our main contribution is a general regret framework that captures the different uncertainty structure of tilted sampling and classical regret minimization\. While standard regret scales as $\\widetilde\{O\}\(\\sqrt\{T\}\)$ due to first\-order uncertainty, sampling regret is governed by squared confidence widths, yielding logarithmic\-in\-$T$ regret in standard settings at fixed temperature\. We develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling \(UCS and TS$^2$\) and provide unified regret decompositions that explain and extend recent logarithmic guarantees, including the first Bayesian sampling\-regret decomposition based on new bounds for posterior\-random Gibbs distributions\. Our results show that learning to sample from a soft\-optimal distribution is statistically distinct from learning to identify a hard optimum\.

## [MEDICAL AND BIOLOGICAL PHYSICS AS A FUNDAMENTAL NATURAL DISCIPLINE: MODERN CHALLENGES AND INNOVATIONS IN PRE\-PROFESSIONAL AND PROFESSIONAL MEDICAL EDUCATION](../publications/76b0e05c755fe19b0502.md)

Alexander V\. Chalyi; Olena Chaika; Dmytro Lukomsky; E\. G\. Zaitseva; Наталія Леонідівна Гриценко

Aim\. To analyze the impact of physical and technical discoveries on the development of instrumental and new, high\-tech methods in medicine\. To investigate modern educational processes in institutions of pre\-professional and professional medical education and to substantiate the effectiveness of using electronic laboratory online practical training in medical and biological physics for students of Ukrainian\-language and English\-language forms of education in the conditions of modern challenges\. Materials and methods\. The materials of the research included legislative documents and resolutions regulating educational processes at the pre\-professional and professional levels\. The research methods included the bibliosemantic method, system analysis, comparison, generalization, and statistical hypothesis testing to analyze the efficiency of electronic laboratory online practical training in medical and biological physics in online learning\.Results\. In order to provide high\-quality training for future doctors at the stage of professional education, an electronic laboratory online workshop in medical and biological physics was developed with an orientation towards the practical use of modern digital medical devices and applications\. Statistical hypothesis testing proved the efficiency of the electronic laboratory online workshop in medical and biological physics compared with offline study\. Conclusions\. An electronic laboratory online workshop in medical and biological physics for students of Ukrainian\-language and English\-language forms of education is an innovative and relevant adaptive environment that meets the modern challenges of the time and has significant methodological value for professional education\.

## [Kecerdasan Buatan Agentik dalam Onkologi: Dari Tumor Board Virtual Menuju Pengobatan Kanker yang Dipersonalisasi](../publications/76b743b5d7d9359cdd91.md)

Tono Haryanto Gunawan; Vera Amelia Salsabila

Kecerdasan buatan agentik \(agentic AI\) telah muncul sebagai paradigma transformatif dalam onkologi, menawarkan kemampuan untuk mengintegrasikan dan menafsirkan data multimodal dalam skala yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya\. Penelitian ini mengkaji evolusi AI dalam onkologi dari alat pendukung keputusan sederhana menuju sistem multi\-agen yang mampu bertindak sebagai kolaborator intelektual dalam perawatan kanker\. Melalui tinjauan sistematis terhadap perkembangan terkini di ASCO Breakthrough 2026 dan berbagai inisiatif global, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi empat arsitektur utama agen AI dalam onkologi: \(1\) sistem virtual tumor board yang mengintegrasikan data radiologi, patologi, dan genomik untuk memberikan rekomendasi pengobatan yang dipersonalisasi; \(2\) kerangka kerja penemuan biomarker berbasis agen yang mampu secara otonom menghasilkan dan memvalidasi hipotesis biologis; \(3\) platform pendukung keputusan genomik yang menghubungkan data molekuler dengan hasil klinis; dan \(4\) ekosistem multi\-agen berbasis percakapan yang mengintegrasikan data klinis, genomik, dan determinan sosial kesehatan\. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa sistem multi\-agen dapat menyederhanakan proses tumor board dengan mengorganisasi informasi klinis yang kompleks, membebaskan dokter untuk berfokus pada diskusi dan pengambilan keputusan\. Implementasi klinis memerlukan arsitektur sistem yang hati\-hati, tata kelola yang kuat, dan validasi prospektif untuk memastikan keamanan dan keandalan\. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa kecerdasan buatan agentik menjanjikan pengobatan kanker yang lebih personal, efisien, dan adil, tetapi memerlukan pendekatan yang terintegrasi dan kolaboratif untuk mewujudkan potensi penuhnya\.

## [Exploration of AI\-Empowered Talent Cultivation Pathways for Emerging Engineering Education in Integrated Circuits](../publications/76dba9d40aa733c90d61.md)

Binrui Xu; Jingyan Wu; Min Liu; Jincan Zhang; Yuxiang Li; Bo Liu

Amid the profound convergence of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and integrated circuits \(IC\), traditional talent development models remain shackled by entrenched disciplinary silos, constrained practical training, and institutional decoupling between academia and industry\. Grounded in the strategic paradigm of Emerging Engineering Education, this study transcends conventional tool\-oriented perspectives by elevating AI to a transformative meta\-capability that reshapes the entire educational ecosystem, thereby systematically exploring innovative pathways for AI\-empowered IC talent cultivation\. In response to evolving industrial imperatives for a conical interdisciplinary knowledge architecture and holistic systems engineering thinking, this research formulates a tripartite cultivation objective integrating knowledge, capability, and literacy alongside four overarching guiding principles\. Anchored in this top\-level blueprint, a comprehensive four\-dimensional implementation framework is architected across curricular, pedagogical, faculty, and institutional dimensions\. Specifically, this framework reconstructs a three\-tiered progressive modular curriculum matrix spanning foundational, core, and frontier levels while forging a smart pedagogical paradigm that unifies personalized instruction, high\-immersion virtual practice, and intelligent evaluation\. Concurrently, it builds an interdisciplinary dual\-qualified faculty force through synergistic external recruitment and internal training, and fosters a deeply collaborative industry\-education community of shared future leveraging an intelligent crowdsourcing R&amp;D platform and joint laboratories, ultimately delivering a systematic and actionable roadmap to overcome the critical talent bottleneck in the semiconductor sector\.

## [Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models](../publications/76dc2cada66843382844.md)

Minhua Lin; Zijun Wang; Zewen Liu; Zhaotian Weng; Bing He; Zhan Shi; Benoit Dumoulin; Xiang Zhang; Suhang Wang; Hanqing Lu

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language\-model \(LM\) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self\-improvement\. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges\. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning \(RL\) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model\-training run\. Even at ten GPU\-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU\-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate\. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts\. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals\. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model \(RWM\), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL\. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current\-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context\. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real\-execution evaluations on held\-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3\.8\-27B to outperform GPT\-6\-sol, even when GPT\-6\-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data\-generation cost\. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training\.

## [CerviDBF\-Net: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Features for Accurate Cervical Cancer Diagnosis](../publications/76e2e4ef959aee327377.md)

Sathupati Lydia; Nagadasari Merrin Prasanna

Cervical cancer screening increasingly relies on automated image analysis to support colposcopic assessment and improve the consistency of clinical decision\-making\. This study proposes CerviDBF\-Net, a novel deep learning framework for automated cervix\-type classification from colposcopic images\. The proposed architecture combines DenseNet121 for spatial feature extraction, a brain\-inspired Liquid Neural Network \(LNN\) for contextual and temporal feature modelling, and a fully connected Softmax layer for final classification\. To improve image quality and feature representation, the preprocessing pipeline incorporates bicubic interpolation, Bi\-Histogram Equalization with Plateau Limit \(BHEPL\) for contrast enhancement, Kapur entropy\-based thresholding, and the Roberts Cross operator for edge detection\. The framework is evaluated on the Intel &amp; MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset, which contains three cervix types \(Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3\) defined by the location and visibility of the transformation zone\. CerviDBF\-Net achieves an accuracy of 98\.92%, sensitivity of 99\.13%, specificity of 98\.38%, precision of 98\.69%, and an F1\-score of 98\.27%, demonstrating strong classification performance compared with the evaluated existing models\. The proposed approach provides an automated baseline tool for cervix\-type classification that may support triage in colposcopy\-assisted screening by helping clinicians assess whether adequate visualization of the squamocolumnar junction has been achieved\.

## [Circular economy strategies for lithium\-ion battery recycling from electric vehicles: Pathways toward achieving SDG 12\.5](../publications/76e6f5004b2fd36e4f68.md)

T\. Brindha; B\. Vasanthan; A\. Ravanan; V\.; P\. Selvakumar; A\. Lakshmi Priya

Lithium\-ion batteries \(LIBs\) are increasingly becoming a vital part of electric vehicles \(EVs\) and are now in widespread use across the globe, which has led to the need for sustainable end\-of\-life battery management\. EVs help to lower tailpipe emissions but the lifecycle of the battery must be handled responsibly from its production to use, reuse, and recycling to be environmentally sustainable\. The increase in the number of spent LIBs creates environmental problems arising from the production of hazardous waste, but also a potential for recovering metals \(e\.g\. Li, Co, Ni, Mn\) which enables a more efficient utilization of resources and less reliance on primary metal production\. In this context, strategies of circular economy can be very important to reach the Sustainable Development Goal \(SDG\) 12\.5 goal of reducing waste, the recovery of materials, reusing materials and managing them responsibly\. This review endeavors to analyze the current status of EV LIBs recycling technologies by combining LCA, end of life \(EoL\) battery management, pretreatment technologies and advanced technologies, such as pyrometallurgical, hydrometallurgical and direct recycling systems\. The review also examines second\-life applications of retired EV batteries for stationary energy storage and highlights the emerging trend of the use of artificial intelligence and data\-driven methods in battery state of health estimation, second\-life suitability assessment, battery recycling pathway selection and process optimization\. A comparative evaluation of the available recycling technologies is presented considering aspects of resource recovery efficiency, environmental impact, technological maturity and industrial scale\. Finally, the review identifies the key technological, economic and policy challenges currently hindering the scale\-up and adoption of circular battery management systems, and outlines future research directions to address these challenges and enhance the contribution of lithium\-ion battery recycling to the SDG 12\.5 and to building a sustainable circular economy\.

## [Enteropathy in inborn and acquired errors of immunity: histological patterns and clinical correlates](../publications/76f9873346fe75f9b44f.md)

Meera Thangarajah; Samar Ojaimi; Alisa Kane; Sanjay Swaminathan; Ming Wei Lin; Alberto Pinzón‐Charry; Tiarni Templeton; Peter B\. McNaughton; Thanh\-Thao Adriana Le; Constance Helen Katelaris; Julian J\. Bosco; Lucinda J\. Berglund

Introduction Enteropathy is a significant and under\-recognised complication of inborn errors of immunity \(IEI\), frequently misclassified as inflammatory bowel disease \(IBD\) or coeliac disease due to overlapping and non\-specific histopathological findings\. Diagnostic criteria remain poorly defined, contributing to substantial diagnostic delay and associated morbidity\. Methods We conducted a structured literature review and established the AT\-SEA \(Adult Tertiary Severe Enteropathy Audit\) working group, a collaborative network of Australian clinical immunologists operating under the Clinical Immunogenomics Research Consortium Australasia \(CIRCA\), to characterise the clinicopathological features of IEI\-associated enteropathy across a multicentre cohort\. Results Twenty\-eight patients were identified\. Moderate or severe disease was present in 89%, with malabsorption in 71% and protein\-losing enteropathy in 43%\. Across 48 biopsy reports, the most frequent histopathological patterns were coeliac\-like changes \(including villous atrophy, increased intraepithelial lymphocytes and crypt hyperplasia\), IBD\-like changes, reduced or absent plasma cells, graft versus host disease \(GVHD\)\-like changes or increased apoptotic bodies and intraepithelial neutrophilia\. Seventy\-seven percent of patients demonstrated two or more concurrent patterns\. Increasing histological complexity correlated significantly with clinician\-assessed disease severity \(Kruskal\-Wallis p=0\.042\)\. Discussion IEI\-associated enteropathy is characterised by overlapping and evolving histopathological patterns rather than discrete subtypes\. The co\-occurrence of multiple patterns should prompt consideration of an underlying IEI\.

## [AI data licensing deals, July 2023 to October 2026: a public dataset and what it shows](../publications/7703271fb96369dbeae3.md)

Yuma Heymans

Licences of content to developers of artificial intelligence \(AI\) are negotiated privately and recorded in no registry; what is known comes from announcements, securities filings and press reports\. This paper describes an open dataset that compiles those disclosures, with a source link, date and verbatim quote for every row, and reports what it shows\. The version analysed here \(reviewed 17 October 2026\) holds 111 records dated 11 July 2023 to 15 October 2026\. It names 24 licensees; OpenAI appears in 29 records, Meta in 14 and Google in 12\. News publishers are the licensor in 52 records \(46\.8%\) and music companies in 18\. The use licensed shifted: 66\.7% of 2024 records include training, against 36\.1% in 2025 and 44\.7% in 2026 to date, while licences to show content in AI answers became the most common news arrangement\. Disclosure of money is sparse and skewed\. Nineteen records \(17\.1%\) carry a dollar figure, but only 11 of the 89 records that describe a specific licence do, and 7 of those 11 rest on press reports citing unnamed people\. No music licence in the table has a stated amount\. A contract term is stated in 7 records\. We describe the fields, collection and dating rules, versioning and verification, and the disclosure and survivorship biases that limit inference\. The dataset is released under CC BY 4\.0, with a snapshot on Zenodo\. Keywords: AI training data; content licensing; data licensing; generative AI; disclosure bias; news publishers; music licensing; open dataset Use of AI: this paper was prepared with generative AI tools, which compiled and analysed the open datasets and drafted the text\. The author takes responsibility for its content\. Competing interests: the author is CEO of AIData\.Broker, which acts for companies that license their data to AI developers and publishes the open datasets the paper draws on\. Also at aidata\.broker/research/paper\-deals\.

## [Automatic Termination Strategy of Inelastic Neutron\-scattering Measurement Using Bayesian Optimization for Bin\-width Selection](../publications/770b6fff47fbf5824062.md)

Kensuke Muto; Hirotaka Sakamoto; Kenji Nagata; T\. Arima; Masato Okada

Currently, an excessive amount of event data is being obtained in four\-dimensional inelastic neutron\-scattering experiments\. A method for automatic bin\-width optimization of multidimensional histograms has been developed and recently validated on real inelastic neutron\-scattering data\. However, measuring beyond the equipment resolution leads to inefficient use of valuable beam time\. To improve experimental efficiency, an automatic termination strategy is essential\. We propose a Bayesian\-optimization\-based method to compute a stopping criterion that can support online decisions on whether to continue or terminate an experiment\. In the proposed method, the bin\-width optimization is performed using Bayesian optimization to efficiently compute the optimal bin widths\. The experiment is terminated when the optimal bin widths become smaller than the target resolutions\. In numerical experiments using real inelastic neutron\-scattering data, the optimal bin widths decrease as the number of events increases\. Even the optimal bin widths for data downsampled to 1/5 are comparable with the resolutions limited by the sample size, choppers, and so on\. This implies excessive measurement of the inelastic neutron experiments for the moment\. Moreover, we found that Bayesian optimization can reduce the search cost to approximately 10% of an exhaustive search in our numerical experiments\.

## [Real\-Time Streaming Analytics for Predictive Fault Diagnosis in Cyber\-Physical Energy Infrastructures](../publications/772295e86c03ca4c724a.md)

Ishrat Zahan Mukti; Ebadur Rahman Khan

Cyber\-Physical Energy Infrastructures \(CPEIs\) are becoming more complex and networked, and therefore there is an increased risk of failures occurring, especially the unexpected ones, thus predictive fault diagnosis becomes imperative to assure reliability and continuity of operations\. Conventional methods of diagnosis are based on batch analysis and off\-line\-work and are exceedingly inadequate to deliver speedily and rapidly accessible understanding to make appropriate real\-time decision\-making in transient energy arrangements\. The study offers a real\-time streaming analytics solution that allows the early identification and forecast of faults in CPEIs that involve real\-time processing of data streams received by various sources of heterogeneous data, including phasor measurement units \(PMUs\), smart meters, and SCADAs\. It is a framework that incorporates edge computing, distributed stream processing \(Apache Kafka and Apache Flink\), light machine learning \(Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) networks and Random Forest classifiers\)\. Edge preprocessing of real\-time data is done on edge, and predictive models are updated on the fly to enable low latency anomaly detection and fault classification\. It was verified through a simulated 33\-bus IEEE test network with injected faults achieving sub\-second fault prediction accuracy of up to 96\.4 percent\. The system is also scalable and fault tolerant when data loads and edge deployment scenarios change\. Such findings reveal that the given architecture would work effectively and is scalable to the predictive fault diagnosis of CPEIs, contributing to the resilience of the grid and allowing proactive maintenance approaches in intelligent energy management systems\.

## [Technology\-driven sustainability: the impact of digitalization on ESG ratings of large companies](../publications/7722affc37de56c6eaf9.md)

Melinda Timea Fülöp; Constantin Aurelian Ionescu

This study investigates the relationship between digitalization and ESG performance in DAX 40 companies by combining correlation analysis with regression models that include firm\-level controls\. While bivariate correlations indicate a positive association between digitalization and the environmental and social components of ESG, these effects dissipate once market capitalization and other firm characteristics are accounted for\. This discrepancy suggests that the initial correlations reflect structural firm attributes rather than an independent influence of digital transformation\. Regression results show that firm size remains the strongest predictor of ESG performance, whereas digitalization exhibits limited explanatory power when considered in a multivariate context\. Furthermore, the magnitude of the estimated effects is economically modest, indicating that digitalization contributes only marginally to substantive sustainability improvements\. These findings imply that digital tools alone do not drive higher ESG outcomes; instead, they function as complementary enablers embedded within broader resource, governance, and regulatory conditions\. The study contributes to the literature by clarifying the boundary conditions under which digitalization affects ESG performance and by highlighting the need for stronger theoretical and empirical differentiation between statistical associations and economically meaningful effects\. First published online 14 October 2026

## [Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution](../publications/77377719896a941ad70d.md)

Ancheng Peng; Shihan Guan; Laurent Albera; Régine Le Bouquin Jeannès; Huazhong Shu; Michael S\. Engel; André Nel; Bó Wáng; Corentin Jouault; Frédéric Legendre

Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large\-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods\. We introduce HAIKA \(Hierarchical Attention\-based Interpretable K\-dimensional Autoencoder\), a self\-supervised residual channel\-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations\. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding\. When applied to Hymenoptera \(i\.e\., ants, bees, and wasps\), the HAIKA\-derived continuous characters improved morphology\-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation\. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality\. HAIKA provides a scalable, image\-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets\.

## [Case Report: Four\-year durable remission, cerebral oligoprogression, and femoral head necrosis following severe recurrent immune checkpoint inhibitor\-related pneumonitis in a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma](../publications/773973b7338532bbf149.md)

Yanjun Xue; Aizhen Xu; Xin Tong; 尹辛大; Lei Wei

Severe immune checkpoint inhibitor\-related pneumonitis \(CIP\) typically leads to the permanent discontinuation of immunotherapy; however, its long\-term oncological outcomes and late drug toxicity remain poorly defined\. This report describes a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma who, following recurrent grade 3 CIP, achieved durable systemic remission for more than 4 years and displayed a distinctive pattern of cerebral oligoprogression\. A 66\-year\-old male patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma achieved a partial response \(PR\) after four cycles of sintilimab combined with chemotherapy\. Three weeks after the last dose, he developed grade 3 CIP complicated by acute pulmonary embolism\. Recurrence occurred twice because of overly rapid corticosteroid tapering and was ultimately controlled through an ultralow tapering regimen \(50 mg/day prednisone initially, reduced by 5 mg per week\) combined with pirfenidone for antifibrotic therapy\. Following the resolution of CIP, no further systemic antitumor therapy was administered\. During 48 months of follow\-up, the patient maintained complete remission \(CR\) of extracranial metastases; the sole site of progression was a solitary cerebellar lesion, which exhibited three episodes of oligoprogression, each of which was successfully managed with either radiotherapy or bevacizumab\-based therapy\. At 34 months after the onset of CIP, the patient developed bilateral osteonecrosis of the femoral head \(ONFH\), with right\-sided slight collapse \(ARCO stage III\) and left\-sided stage I\. This case suggests a potential synergistic toxic mechanism between cumulative corticosteroid exposure \(approximately 7,300 mg prednisone equivalents\) and VEGF inhibition\-mediated microvascular injury\. This case also suggests that ultralow corticosteroid tapering combined with antifibrotic therapy can effectively manage refractory CIP; the dissociation between durable peripheral immunological memory and isolated central nervous system \(CNS\) progression supports the hypothesis of CNS immune privilege\. Finally, clinicians must remain vigilant about long\-term musculoskeletal toxicity in long\-term survivors of ICI therapy\.

## [Function\-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate with bladder neck and 12 o&\#x27;clock urethral mucosal preservation for large\-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia: a single\-center retrospective case series](../publications/775103d218870b91764e.md)

Wenshuai Yan; Jie Jia; 彦名 霍; Jixue Gao; Feng Wang; 宋红雄

Background Large\-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia \(BPH\) poses a significant surgical challenge, as conventional transurethral resection yields suboptimal tissue removal efficiency and high rates of ejaculatory dysfunction\. While endoscopic enucleation techniques \(e\.g\., HoLEP and PKEP\) offer improved efficacy, the systematic preservation of functional anatomical structures — particularly the bladder neck and anterior urethral mucosa — remains inadequately addressed in current practice\. Objective To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and functional outcomes of function\-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate \(FP\-PKEP\) — a modified technique incorporating systematic preservation of the bladder neck circular fibers and the 12 o&\#x27;clock urethral mucosal strip — in patients with large\-volume BPH\. Methods This single\-center, retrospective case series included 52 consecutive patients with large\-volume BPH \(prostate volume &gt;80 mL, International Prostate Symptom Score \[IPSS\] &gt; 20, maximum urinary flow rate \[Qmax\] &lt; 10 mL/s\) who underwent FP\-PKEP between January 2025 and December 2025\. The primary outcome was the change in IPSS at 3 months postoperatively; secondary outcomes included Qmax, post\-void residual urine volume \(PVR\), quality of life \(QoL\) score, perioperative safety parameters, and functional preservation outcomes \(urinary continence and ejaculatory function at 6 months\)\. Results All 52 patients \(mean age 67\.8 ± 7\.2 years; mean prostate volume 93\.7 ± 15\.2 mL\) successfully underwent FP\-PKEP without conversion\. Mean operative time was 72\.5 ± 15\.8 min; postoperative hemoglobin decrease was 9\.8 ± 4\.2 g/L; catheterization duration was 2\.8 ± 0\.9 days; and hospital stay was 4\.2 ± 1\.3 days\. At 3 months, IPSS decreased from 26\.1 ± 3\.0 to 6\.8 ± 2\.6 \( P &lt; 0\.001\), and Qmax increased from 7\.2 ± 1\.6 to 21\.2 ± 4\.5 mL/s \( P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Transient stress urinary incontinence occurred in 4 patients \(7\.7%\), all requiring no more than one pad per day and resolving within 1 month without surgical intervention\. Among the 16 patients who were sexually active before surgery, antegrade ejaculation was preserved in 14 \(87\.5%\) and suspected retrograde ejaculation was recorded in 2 \(12\.5%\)\. No clinically apparent cases of permanent urinary incontinence, bladder neck contracture, or urethral stricture were observed during the 6\-month follow\-up\. Conclusions In this uncontrolled case series, FP\-PKEP showed a favorable safety profile and achieved significant relief of bladder outlet obstruction, with promising early urinary continence and ejaculatory outcomes\. The systematic preservation of the bladder neck and 12 o&\#x27;clock urethral mucosa warrants further evaluation in prospective randomized controlled trials, as these preliminary findings are exploratory and hypothesis\-generating\.

## [Evaluating ChatGPT for Dam Behavior Prediction, Interpretation, and Safety Assessment: An Experimental Study](../publications/7754281a37cd50b312ad.md)

Fernando Salazar; Aryan Baibordy; José Manuel González; J\. Mata

Structural dam safety control is fundamentally based on visual inspections and on the analysis of monitoring data and their comparison with the expected behavior for a given load combination, which in turn is calculated with a predictive model\. In recent decades, the development of machine learning algorithms has led engineers and researchers worldwide to explore their capabilities for predicting dam behavior and supporting safety assessment\. Regardless of the model used, a prediction is generally obtained together with an expected model error, which is compared with the observed value in order to support decision\-making\. This process, however, requires the intervention of experts in dam engineering, and particularly in the prior behavior of the structure under analysis\. In recent years, the emergence of generative artificial intelligence models has opened up considerable opportunities to improve processes in various fields, including civil engineering\. The reported capabilities of these models make them well suited to some tasks in the field of dam safety, particularly for developing predictive models and interpreting their results\. In this work, we tested ChatGPT to assess its potential in these tasks, using the data from the ICOLD 2022 Benchmark Workshop, in which 18 teams provided their best predictions of the behavior of an arch dam\. ChatGPT was provided with the same problem description and monitoring data available to the participants and was asked, through brief and neutral prompts, to propose a modeling strategy, generate predictions for six response variables for short\- and long\-term periods, create the corresponding source code, and interpret the results from a dam safety perspective\. The complete procedure was performed twice using the same information and prompts\. The results show considerable potential for increasing productivity in building and applying machine learning models, with predictive accuracy comparable to that obtained by the Benchmark participants\. ChatGPT achieved a lower mean absolute error than the participants’ average in 10 \(first run\) and 12 \(second run\) of the 12 variable–period combinations, and outperformed the best participant in one case\. However, the interpretation of the results was considerably weaker, with important aspects being only partially addressed or overlooked\. These findings highlight the potential of ChatGPT to assist in the development of data\-based predictive models, but also reveal its limitations in terms of the domain\-specific knowledge required to draw conclusions on dam safety\.

## [Web Interactive Content Filtering Model Integrating Prompt Classifier and Intent Understanding](../publications/77582e1740197e2cddcc.md)

Yanghao Li; Shisong Wu; Pengfei Zhang; Shengyao Zhuang; Lulu Chen

To accurately identify and intercept harmful content generated in user interactions on Web platforms such as social media and online forums, this study proposes a Web interactive content filtering model that integrates Prompt classifiers and intent understanding\. The model adopts a hierarchical review architecture with dual\-module collaboration\. The front\-end deploys a Prompt classifier based on Deep Contrastive Learning \(DCL\), and uses the attention mechanism and deep convolutional network to perform rapid semantic analysis and preliminary screening of real\-time comments and conversations\. The back\-end introduces an intent understanding module based on search\-enhanced generation and Large Language Models \(LLMs\) to conduct in\-depth contextual analysis of preliminary screening warning content to distinguish malicious attacks from legitimate sensitive topic discussions\. Experiments showed that the system performed well on a test set containing 52,397 Chinese Web interactive texts\. The Prompt classifier module achieved a precision of 95\.2% and a recall of 96\.5%\. After collaborative calibration with the intent understanding module, the false alarm rate of the system was significantly reduced to 4\.4%, while the recall rate remained at 96\.1%\. From the results, this study provides a content security solution for Web interactive scenarios that combines high accuracy, strong semantic understanding capabilities, and real\-time response performance\. It can effectively purify the cyberspace environment while ensuring freedom of interaction, with important practical application value\.

## [Exploring foot pressure patterns for skiing experience classification in a simulator\-based environment](../publications/7759f117e21f72d25c29.md)

Shigeharu Ono; Ryosuke Atsumi; Hideaki Kanai; Hideki Koike

Abstract This study investigated whether deep learning can distinguish groups of ski experience based on plantar\-pressure distributions measured during simulator\-based training and whether classifier outputs change during repeated training\. Weight\-shift images from 27 participants were classified into beginner, novice, and intermediate groups, operationally defined by self\-reported skiing exposure, using a YOLO11\-based image classifier\. Participant\-wise generalization was explored using leave\-one\-participant\-out \(LOPO\) cross\-validation, with performance summarized at the participant and session levels\. The classifier showed moderate discrimination between the beginner and novice groups but limited generalization to the intermediate group\. Session\-level classification achieved an accuracy of 0\.667, macro\-F1 of 0\.489, and balanced accuracy of 0\.524\. Longitudinal changes in classifier outputs were subsequently examined in six beginner participants using fixed participant\-dependent models trained only on baseline data\. Mixed\-effects analyses provided tentative evidence of nonlinear changes in classifier outputs across repeated training sessions, although the results were sensitive to model specification, and substantial inter\-individual variability was observed\. Qualitative Eigen\-CAM visualization and biomechanical analyses further indicated that the classifier responded to distributed plantar\-pressure characteristics\. These findings support the feasibility of using plantar\-pressure patterns to characterize skiing\-experience groups and to track longitudinal changes in simulator\-derived pressure patterns, while highlighting the need for larger sample sizes and independently validated skiing\-skill criteria before such models can be used for objective proficiency assessment\.

## [C\. elegans GPCR kinase GRK\-1 maintains behavioral persistence in a dynamic thermal environment](../publications/775a1ac2d9118ab4ad5c.md)

Tzu‐Ting Huang; Shunji Nakano; Maria Lukova; Hironori J\. Matsuyama; Leona C\. Cesar; Yuki Tsukada; Ikue Mori

How do animals maintain behavioral states as sensory inputs vary with movement and location? Here, we uncover a neuronal mechanism that allows the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans to move isothermally on a temperature gradient for several minutes at temperatures associated with its food experience\. We find that prolonged isothermal tracking along the preferred temperature requires GRK\-1, the C\. elegans homolog of human GPCR kinase GRK5\. Loss of grk\-1 reduces isothermal tracking durations, and these defects can be rescued by simultaneous grk\-1 expression in RIM and AVA interneurons\. Furthermore, silencing RIM and AVA restores the short isothermal tracking defects in the absence of grk\-1, while leaving wild\-type isothermal tracking unchanged\. These data suggest that wild\-type RIM and AVA are in a suppressed neuronal state during isothermal tracking\. Also, imposing a normally suppressed neuronal state in RIM and AVA during isothermal tracking can functionally compensate for the loss of grk\-1\. Together, our findings reveal a previously unknown molecule\-to\-circuit function of GRK\-1/GRK5 in RIM and AVA interneurons that maintains a minute\-scale behavioral state on a temperature gradient\.

## [Can machine learning be used to quantify blood loss based on hemodynamic data? Experimental study of controlled hemorrhagic shock in anesthetized piglets](../publications/775c4643021fa24ec89c.md)

Dino Tikvesa; Maxime Carriere; Fabien Coisy; Laura Grau‐Mercier; Céline Occelli; Thomas Sanchez; Florian Ajavon; Thibaut Markarian; Xavier Bobbia

Background Hemorrhagic compensatory physiological mechanisms may initially lead to an underestimation of the severity of a hemorrhage, for which quantification of blood lost volume is difficult\. The objective of our study was to assess the suitability of machine learning \(ML\) to quantify blood depletion from critical care settings routinely available clinical and ultrasound data during the management of a hemorrhagic patient in a model of controlled hemorrhagic shock in anesthetized piglets\. Methods We used data from anesthetized and ventilated piglets that underwent blood spoliation at 2 mL kg −1 min −1 until a mean arterial pressure \(MAP\) of 40 mmHg was achieved\. The data recorded consisted of the hemodynamic and echocardiographic parameters routinely measured during the care of critically ill patients\. We used these data to develop six machine learning models for blood loss quantification\. Judgment criteria were the coefficient of determination R 2 , root mean squared error \(RMSE\) and mean absolute error \(MAE\), reported in mL between real depletion and that assessed by the ML models\. Results A total of 84 piglets were included\. For assessing blood depletion, R 2 was 0\.62 ± 0\.08, 0\.61 ± 0\.10, 0\.60 ± 0\.10, 0\.60 ± 0\.08, 0\.58 ± 0\.11, 0\.57 ± 0\.13, and 0\.54 ± 0\.10 for Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, Multicorrelation Models, Random Forest, K\-Nearest Neighbors, Ensemble, and Multilayer Perceptron, respectively\. The best\-performing model \(SVM\) achieved an RMSE of 240 ± 27 mL and MAE of 186 ± 17 mL\. Area under curve for detecting abundant blood loss \(&gt; 500 mL, equivalent to 15 mL kg −1 \) ranged from 0\.856 to 0\.895 across all classification models\. Conclusion In this model of controlled hemorrhagic shock in piglets, ML seems to offer promising accuracy to quantify blood depletion using hemodynamic and echographic measures\.

## [Integrating machine learning and sustainability indices for biomass energy forecasting in Türkiye: a data‐driven framework for agricultural, hydrological, and environmental policy design](../publications/775d5df3d64d3bfae4a1.md)

Betül Göncü; Gencay Sarıışık

Abstract Biomass energy is increasingly recognized as a strategic component of sustainable energy transitions and global efforts toward the Sustainable Development Goals \(SDG‐7 and SDG‐13\) and long‐term net‐zero emission targets\. However, most national‐scale forecasting studies prioritize predictive accuracy while treating sustainability indicators as secondary inputs\. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated and explainable machine learning \(ML\) framework that combines biomass energy forecasting with sustainability assessment\. The empirical analysis focuses on Türkiye during 2016–2024 using an annualized dataset derived from 108 monthly observations, including biomass energy capacity, agricultural productivity, water and waste‐to‐energy efficiency, greenhouse gas emissions, and macroeconomic indicators\. Gradient boosting \(GB\), XGBoost, and CatBoost models were implemented to capture nonlinear interactions among energy, environmental, and agricultural variables that are difficult to represent using conventional statistical approaches\. Model performance was evaluated using multi‐metric diagnostics and rolling time‐series validation\. The GB model demonstrated robust out‐of‐sample performance with a rolling RMSE below 2 MW and consistently outperformed a naive trend benchmark\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) identified agricultural productivity and water and waste‐to‐energy efficiency as the dominant structural predictors, jointly accounting for more than 80% of total explanatory importance\. Building on these explainability results, a novel Biomass Sustainability Index \(BSI\) was developed using empirically derived SHAP weights rather than subjective weighting schemes\. The BSI exhibited a strong positive association with biomass energy capacity \( r = 0\.87, R 2 = 0\.81\), while lagged analyses indicated that favorable sustainability conditions systematically precede capacity expansion\. Uncertainty‐aware forecasting based on quantile GB generated probabilistic prediction intervals and future scenarios for 2025–2035\. Results suggest continued biomass growth, with projected capacities ranging from approximately 1\.8 GW under conservative assumptions to 2\.14 GW under optimistic conditions\. The proposed ML–BSI framework provides a transparent, interpretable, and transferable tool for sustainability‐oriented biomass energy planning by integrating prediction, explainability, and sustainability diagnostics within a unified analytical framework\.

## [From Copilots to Coworkers: How Autonomous AI Agents Reshape Organizational Roles and Decision Authority: A Structured Integrative Review and Research Agenda](../publications/7761aad6f0d573241e05.md)

Miguel Rozalez

Autonomous artificial intelligence agents extend generative AI from producing content on demand to pursuing goals through planning, memory, tool use, environmental feedback, and iterative action\. This shift matters organizationally because agency is no longer confined to recommendation: systems can increasingly initiate and coordinate consequential work\. This article integrates research on AI\-enabled work, algorithmic management, organizational design, human–AI collaboration, automation, and responsible AI to explain the transition from copilots to digital coworkers\. The review distinguishes five configurations—tool, copilot, teammate, delegate, and coworker—and argues that the central organizational variable is not technical capability alone but the allocation of decision authority\. We synthesize evidence showing that AI assistance can improve speed and quality in bounded tasks, often benefiting less experienced workers, while also producing uneven performance at the frontier of model capability\. Extending this evidence to agentic systems, we develop an authority allocation matrix based on task risk, reversibility, verifiability, and auditability\. We identify three mechanisms through which agents reshape organizations: role reconfiguration, authority redistribution, and coordination redesign\. Benefits arise when agents compress search and execution costs, diffuse expertise, and enable new forms of modular organizing\. Risks arise when action outpaces verification, responsibility becomes diffused, tacit knowledge erodes, or agents acquire excessive access to organizational resources\. We propose a layered governance architecture combining explicit mandates, least\-privilege access, execution limits, provenance, continuous monitoring, and human escalation rights\. The article concludes with propositions and a research agenda for studying agentic organizing through field experiments, longitudinal process research, digital trace analysis, and comparative institutional designs\.

## [Backward Compatibility in Zero\-Bit Neural Audio Watermarking](../publications/776f2c8995c6cfbb3cc4.md)

Admir Krnić; Kosta Pavlović; Petar Nedić; Željko Bolević; Slavko Kovačević; Igor Djurović

Neural watermarking systems are typically trained as tightly coupled embedder\-detector pairs and implicitly assume static deployment\. In real\-world deployments, embedders and detectors are frequently updated and selectively decoupled for security and versioning purposes, which can break detection in previously embedded content and, more critically, increase false\-positive rates on embedders that a given detector is intentionally not intended to recognize\. In this paper the concept of backward compatibility in zero\-bit audio watermarking is formalized\. A training framework is proposed that pairs a new detector with a sequence of frozen legacy embedders \(its legacy chain\), using a performance\-weighted sampling strategy so that the detector retains accuracy across all earlier versions\. This coupling, while necessary for backward compatibility, is shown to induce an embedder\-collapse effect that catastrophically degrades the true negative rate \(TNR\) against out\-of\-chain embedders\. To counteract this, a Angular Diversity Loss \(ADL\) is introduced that explicitly forces each new embedder to occupy a distinct region of the output space\. The combined approach restores near\-perfect TNR with no measurable cost to detection accuracy or perceptual audio quality\.

## [AI and Machine Learning: Concepts, Models and Real\-World Applications](../publications/777129037c71dfa7484c.md)

Goldi Soni; Dr\. Kranti Kumar Dewangan; Omprakash Dewangan

AI and Machine Learning: Concepts, Models and Real\-World Applications provides a structured introduction to the fundamental concepts, models, techniques, and practical applications of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Machine Learning \(ML\)\. The book covers AI foundations, machine learning fundamentals, data collection and preprocessing, feature engineering, supervised and unsupervised learning, regression, classification, decision trees, ensemble models, artificial neural networks, and deep learning\. It also explores natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, validation, explainable AI, ethical considerations, and responsible AI practices\. The book discusses real\-world applications across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, retail, transportation, and technology\. It also addresses practical challenges involving data quality, computational resources, model performance, privacy, security, and regulatory compliance\. This book is intended for students, researchers, educators, and professionals seeking to understand AI and machine learning concepts, models, workflows, and real\-world implementations\. Publisher: Geh Press Edition: 2026 ISBN: 978\-81\-68406\-60\-5

## [Interfaces and Modules: A Scalable Representation for Weight\-Space Learning across Architectures](../publications/777da270ae0e595687a3.md)

Michał Kozyra; Michael Bronstein

Weight\-space learning across architectures requires representations that respect parameter symmetries and scale to large networks\. Existing equivariant tensor encoders require architecture\-specific symmetry specifications, while neuron graphs make global attention costly\. We introduce a typed graph organized around shared coordinate\-permutation actions\. Its nodes, called interfaces, represent coordinate spaces whose bound tensor axes must be permuted jointly; operation occurrences, called modules, form typed hyperedges\. A compiler derives this graph from supported PyTorch models, with exact recovery of the permutation factors defined by its constraints\. The Universal Weight Encoder \(UWE\) combines local equivariant updates to parameter features with global attention over invariant interface summaries\. The small number of interfaces makes global attention practical, and a single encoder processes different supported architectures\. UWE is competitive with architecture\-specific state\-of\-the\-art methods on established benchmarks\. On a new zoo of 1,200 transformers spanning 100 architectures, it outperforms the evaluated baselines at ranking networks within unseen architectures, including architectures larger than those used for training, while using substantially less memory\.

## [Association of the red cell distribution width/albumin ratio with 6\-month readmission risk in heart failure patients](../publications/7784afe5a4ff3de94237.md)

Hanyu Wang; Lihua Yang; Zhengye Liu; Yitian Wang; Xing Lv; Ruina Ma; Min Li

Background Readmission due to heart failure \(HF\) remains a major clinical and economic challenge\. The red cell distribution width\-to\-albumin ratio \(RAR\) has been proposed as a novel biomarker reflecting chronic inflammation, nutritional status, and multi\-organ involvement in cardiovascular diseases\. However, the association between RAR and readmission risk, particularly in Asian populations with HF, remains unclear\. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between RAR levels and the 6\-month readmission risk among Chinese patients with heart failure\. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the Zigong Heart Failure Database, which included 2008 patients hospitalized for HF between December 2016 and June 2019\. After excluding patients with missing RDW, albumin, or readmission data, 1854 patients were included in the final analytical cohort\. Based on RAR values, patients were divided into four quartiles\. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between RAR and 6\-month readmission risk, adjusting for demographics, clinical parameters, comorbidities, and medications\. Subgroup analyses were performed to examine the consistency of associations across different patient characteristics\. Results The overall 6\-month readmission rate was 38\.5% \(714/1854\)\. Patients in higher RAR quartiles had a significantly greater risk of readmission than those in lower quartiles \( P = 0\.0025\)\. In unadjusted analyses, each unit increase in RAR was associated with a 57% higher risk of 6\-month readmission \(HR 1\.57, 95% CI: 1\.27–1\.93, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. This association remained significant after adjusting for confounding variables \(HR 1\.52, 95% CI: 1\.21–1\.92, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. After full adjustment, patients in the highest quartile \(Q4\) had a 39% higher risk of readmission compared with those in the lowest quartile \(Q1\) \(HR 1\.39, 95% CI: 1\.10–1\.76, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across sex, age, BMI, NYHA classification, and medication use, with no significant interactions observed\. Conclusion Elevated RAR was independently associated with an increased 6\-month readmission risk among Chinese patients with HF\. As a simple and cost\-effective biomarker, RAR may enhance risk stratification and inform clinical decision\-making in HF management, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare burden\.

## [Prediction of Ischemic Heart Disease with A Hybrid Algorithm of Support Vector Machine \(SVM\) and Xgboost Using Data from Yazd Health Study \(YaHS\)](../publications/77899fe7dccfe7fc91bd.md)

Azam Barzegari; Mahyar Abdulmaleki; Masoud Mirzaei

Introduction: Ischemic heart disease represents one of the most prevalent conditions characterized by elevated mortality rates\. The aim of this research was to provide an efficient instrument for the early diagnosis of ischemic heart disease and to assist clinical decision\-making processes through the application of hybrid artificial intelligence algorithms\. Methods: The data used in this study were from Yazd Health Study \(YaHS\) enrollment phase dataset, comprising 9969 participants and 30 selective features from a total of 300, collected between 2014 to 2015\. Data were analyzed using SVM and XGBoost machine learning algorithms using Python version 3\.11\.8\. Results: Combining the strengths of SVM and XGBoost models through a Voting Classifier approach enhanced both the accuracy and efficiency of the heart disease prediction model\. When evaluating the predictive performance for heart disease, the Voting Classifier model achieved in accuracy rate of 90%\. Conclusion: These findings suggest that implementing machine learning techniques and hybrid algorithms for early diagnosis and prediction could facilitate earlier intervention in CHD, ultimately helping to lower mortality rates\.

## [Data\-driven insight into CO2 electroreduction: Ensemble machine learning for CO Faraday efficiency prediction in single\-atom catalysts](../publications/779405e8b75806013e35.md)

Dhanveer  Singh Rawat; Amit Pratap Singh; Arjun Singh Rawat

This study presents an ensemble machine\-learning \(ML\) framework to predict the Faraday efficiency of CO formation \(FE CO \) for electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction \(CO 2 RR\) on single\-atom catalysts \(SACs\)\. A literature\-derived dataset of 795 experimental entries from 42 primary studies was compiled, representing 24 carrier classes, 12 dopant atoms, and H\-cell, flow\-cell, and membrane\-electrode\-assembly \(MEA\) configurations\. Eighteen regressors from nine algorithm families were systematically evaluated\. A stacking ensemble combining gradient boosting decision tree, random forest, extremely randomized trees, support vector regression, k \-nearest\-neighbor regression, and CatBoost base learners with a kernel\-based meta\-regressor achieved the highest record\-level performance, with a test R 2 of 0\.9106 and an RMSE of 8\.41 percentage points\. Repeated five\-fold cross\-validation confirmed robust within\-domain performance across random partitions \(mean R 2 = 0\.882 ± 0\.006 \)\. Permutation importance, SHAP, partial\-dependence analysis, and descriptor ablation identified dopant atom, applied potential, catalyst identity, and carrier as the dominant model\-associated descriptors\. Screening recovered established associations with Ni\-based SACs, with graphene showing the highest mean model\-predicted FE CO among the represented carrier classes\. A discrete metal\-potential response surface identified a Ni\-associated region with a mean predicted FE CO of approximately 85% near \-0\.77 V versus RHE and a maximum of approximately 99% near \-0\.97 V\. More stringent catalyst\-, publication\-, and Ni\-restricted grouped validation showed weaker transfer to unseen systems\. Thus, record\-level performance primarily reflects interpolation within the represented experimental domain, while screening identifies experimentally grounded, dataset\-conditioned trends for further validation\.

## [Geochronology and geochemistry of granitic dikes in the Xiaogushan gold deposit NE China and implications for gold mineralization](../publications/779e06deac5350745b30.md)

Wenzhao Fu; Yu Yang; Lei Zhu; Zhigang Yin; Lianfeng Gao; Zhenguo Zhang; Chao Liu

The Xiaogushan cryptoexplosive breccia\-type gold deposit is located within the eastern Hebei\-western Liaoning gold belt along the northern margin of the North China Craton\. The mining area contains multiple episodes of subvolcanic dikes, among which the granite porphyry and granitic aplite dikes show close temporal and spatial relationship with gold mineralization\. To constrain their emplacement age, petrogenesis, tectonic setting, and metallogenic significance, integrated zircon U\-Pb\-Hf isotopic and whole‑rock geochemical analyses were carried out on these dikes\. Zircon U\-Pb dating yields emplacement ages of 163\.9 ± 2\.0 Ma for the granite porphyry and 162\.2 ± 4\.9 Ma for the granitic aplite, indicating Late Jurassic magmatism in the region\. The rocks are enriched in SiO2, K2O, and LILEs, depleted in HFSEs, and classified as strongly peraluminous, high‑K calc‑alkaline S‑type granites\. The primary magma, derived from Paleoproterozoic lower crust \(εHf\(t\) = \-17\.7 to \-13\.5; TDM2 = 2\.29 to 2\.07 Ga\), and the geochemical variations are consistent with fractional crystallization of K‑feldspar and plagioclase\. Regional tectonic evidence indicates that these dikes were emplaced in a continental collisional setting related to the closure of the Mongol‑Okhotsk Ocean\. This collision caused crustal thickening, deformation, and subsequent extension, which promoted mineralization\. These dikes characterized by high oxygen fugacity, alkali enrichment, and moderate evolution, may facilitate metal transport and remobilize pre‑existing mineralization via associated hydrothermal systems\. Their clustered occurrence thus serves as a potential indicator for deep‑seated hydrothermal activity and gold mineralization, reflecting the intense Mesozoic tectono\-magmatic\-metallogenic event in the northern North China Craton\.

## [Primary damage and mechanical degradation of WTaCrV refractory high\-entropy alloy: Effects of solid\-solution and chemical ordering](../publications/77a8b6b83774af0e05e9.md)

Yihan Wu; 余鹏飞; Yaohong Suo; Lei Zhang

As advanced nuclear reactors demand novel irradiation\-tolerant materials, this study investigates the radiation damage and mechanical degradation of the promising WTaCrV refractory high\-entropy alloy \(RHEA\)\. To isolate complex nanoscale chemical effects, we propose an atomistic modeling strategy comparing Average\-Atom \(AA\), random solid\-solution \(RSS\), and local chemical order \(LCO\) configurations using newly developed interatomic potentials\. Collision cascades simulations reveal that the number of Frenkel pairs follow N RSS &gt; N LCO &gt; N AA at the same radiation dose\. While the RSS effect accelerates defect generation due to rugged energy landscapes, LCO enhances lattice cohesion to mitigate radiation damage\. Despite more primary defects in the RSS and LCO configurations compared with the AA configurations, the RSS and LCO effects can suppress radiation\-induced mechanical degradation\. Irradiation severely degrade the homogenized AA model but exert a limited impact on the strength and flow stress of the RSS and LCO models\. This exceptional resistance is driven by inherent lattice distortion resulting from interactions among different alloy elements, which outweighs point defect induced lattice disruptions\. Moreover, the complex interactions between deformation twins and point defects cause confined plastic flow, elevating flow stress in the RSS and LCO models\. The findings provide atomistic guidance for performance assessment of next\-generation structural materials for extreme nuclear environments\.

## [QUALITY AND STANDARDS IN CUSTOM FURNITURE PRODUCTION: A PRACTICAL SMALL\-SCALE PRODUCTION APPROACH](../publications/77b5a4be52ee46f2736e.md)

Vitalii Zalitok

Purpose\. The purpose of this study is to develop a practical quality management framework for custom furniture production that enables small\-scale manufacturers to ensure product quality while maintaining the flexibility required for highly customized, low\-volume production\. Methodology\. The research is based on an analytical review of recent developments in wood defect detection, Total Quality Management \(TQM\), Lean methodologies and intelligent manufacturing systems\. Approaches such as Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-based inspection, Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making \(MCDM\) methods and sustainability\-driven design were adapted to small\-scale conditions, resulting in a hybrid quality management model that integrates simplified Lean Six Sigma tools, defect detection technologies and process optimization strategies\. Results\. Consistent quality in custom furniture production depends primarily on structured process control, effective knowledge transfer and flexible production planning rather than on extensive automation; small manufacturers can achieve high product quality with a limited number of appropriate digital technologies alongside continuous process improvement\. Practical implications\. The framework offers a scalable solution for small and medium\-sized custom furniture enterprises, improving process consistency, reducing defects and aligning quality assurance with customer\-specific requirements without compromising operational flexibility\. Value/originality\. Unlike quality systems developed for mass manufacturing, the model combines Lean Six Sigma principles, modern defect detection technologies and process optimization techniques in a framework adapted to artisanal and highly customized production, bridging the gap between industrial quality standards and small\-scale furniture production\.

## [Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Recommender System Based on Collaborative, Evolutionary, and Content\-Based Techniques](../publications/77b9bfeb0e92e5b69257.md)

José Luis Junior Gutiérrez Agüero; Christian Daniel von Lucken Martínez

Los sistemas de recomendación \(SR\) son herramientas computacionales que predicen qué ítems serán de interés para un usuario, y se encuentran presentes en múltiples lugares a lo largo de nuestra vida digital\. Uno de los principales desafíos que enfrentan los SR es el problema del inicio frío, que surge cuando la falta de historial de interacciones impide generar recomendaciones confiables para nuevos usuarios o ítems\. El presente trabajo presenta el diseño, implementación y evaluación de una extensión del algoritmo HP\-MOEA \(Hybrid Probabilistic Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm\), aplicado al dominio de los sistemas de recomendación\. El algoritmo original combina filtrado colaborativo basado en usuarios con algoritmos evolutivos multiobjetivo para mitigar este problema\. La extensión propuesta incorpora un componente basado en contenido que pondera la función objetivo de novedad mediante perfiles de afinidad temática entre usuarios e ítems\. Los resultados experimentales utilizando el dataset MovieLens ml\-100k muestran que el algoritmo modificado mantiene un rendimiento competitivo en métricas de convergencia como la distancia generacional \(GD\) y su versión inversa \(IGD\), al tiempo que logra una mejora del 3\.4 % en hipervolumen respecto al algoritmo original, estadísticamente significativa y consistente en todos los tamaños de población evaluados, reflejando una frontera de Pareto más amplia y soluciones mejor distribuidas\. La propuesta demuestra que la integración de información de contenido en la función de novedad mejora la diversidad de soluciones sin sacrificar convergencia, ofreciendo un aporte concreto en el tratamiento del problema del inicio frío\.

## [The Role of Immunohistochemical Markers in the Differential Diagnosis of Lichen Simplex Chronicus](../publications/77bb2946f470d5d96069.md)

A\. S\. Sidikov; G\.B\. Pyagay; Адхамжон Пакирдинов; Ashurov Dilshod Davlatovich

BACKGROUND: Lichen simplex chronicus \(Vidal&\#x27;s lichen\) is one of the most common chronic pruritic dermatoses, characterized by a persistent itch–scratch cycle and the development of marked lichenification\. Despite its high prevalence, the immunopathogenic mechanisms underlying the disease remain incompletely understood, and the immunohistochemical criteria for its differential diagnosis from atopic dermatitis and psoriasis require further clarification\.AIM: To investigate the immunohistochemical expression patterns of cellular markers in patients with lichen simplex chronicus and to determine their diagnostic significance in comparison with atopic dermatitis and psoriasis\.METHODS: An immunohistochemical analysis was performed on skin biopsy specimens obtained from 60 patients with lichen simplex chronicus, 30 patients with atopic dermatitis, 30 patients with stable plaque psoriasis, and 10 samples of normal skin from healthy controls\. The expression of CD4, CD8, CD1a, CD68, CD207 \(Langerin\), and S100 was evaluated in both the epidermis and dermis, followed by comparative statistical analysis\.RESULTS: Patients with lichen simplex chronicus demonstrated pronounced dermal infiltration by CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ lymphocytes, indicating chronic T\-cell–mediated inflammation\. CD1a expression confirmed the activation of epidermal Langerhans cells, whereas strong CD68 expression suggested a substantial role of macrophages in sustaining chronic inflammation and tissue remodeling\. Statistically significant differences in the expression of CD4, CD8, CD1a, and CD207 among the study groups confirmed their diagnostic value\. The limited expression of S100 indicated the absence of significant structural alterations of nerve fibers and supported the predominantly functional nature of chronic pruritus\.CONCLUSION: Lichen simplex chronicus is characterized by chronic T\-cell– and macrophage\-mediated inflammation accompanied by activation of Langerhans cells and dermal dendritic cells, in the absence of significant structural damage to nerve fibers\. These immunohistochemical findings improve the accuracy of the differential diagnosis of lichen simplex chronicus from atopic dermatitis and psoriasis and provide further insight into the immunopathogenesis of this dermatosis\.

## [The association between short\-term nitrogen dioxide \(NO2\) exposure and ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attacks \(TIA\): a national study in Israel](../publications/77d0b4f4fe8314ecc531.md)

Placidus S\. Fernando; Helena Krasnov; Itai Kloog; Mike Z\. He; Gal Ifergane; Inbar Zucker; Victor Novack; Carmit Libruder; Maayan Yitshak‐Sade

Air pollution is an environmental risk factor for stroke, but most studies have focused on fine particulate matter \(PM 2\.5 \), and fewer have investigated the independent association with exposure to nitrogen dioxide \(NO 2 \)\. We conducted a nationwide case\-crossover study including all ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack \(TIA\) reported in the Israeli National Stroke Registry from 2014 to 2018\. We obtained daily NO 2 levels from high\-resolution geospatial models and linked them to residential addresses\. We used distributed lag nonlinear models to assess the cumulative association of NO 2 exposure over 0–5 lag days, adjusting for PM 2\.5 and temperature\. We further evaluated the modification of the associations by age, sex, urbanicity, and comorbidities \(ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and diabetes\)\. We included 85,162 cases, about 54% were males, and the mean age was 71\.8\. Cumulative NO 2 exposure was associated with increased odds of ischemic stroke or TIA \(odds ratio – OR and 95% confidence interval − 1\.057 \[1\.034–1\.081\]\), with the strongest effects 3–5 days before the event\. The associations were more pronounced in urban areas \(1\.064 \[1\.032;1\.097\]\) compared to suburban areas \(1\.045 \[1\.012;1\.080\]\)\. Although the overall association was similar across ages and sexes, the lag\-specific associations on lag days 3–5 were more pronounced in younger adults and women\. Short\-term exposure to NO 2 is associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke and TIA, with differential associations across urbanicity, sex, and age groups\. These results underscore the urgent need for public health initiatives to reduce NO 2 emissions\.
