## [Управление человеческими ресурсами с помощью технологий искусственного интеллекта](../publications/77e7332f4db1e9abc837.md)

Юлия Валентиновна Никиточкина

В связи с растущим интересом к технологиям, используемых в сфере искусственного интеллекта, особое значение приобретает практическая тема — примеры успешных решений на основе технологий искусственного интеллекта в сфере управления персоналом\. Цель данной статьи — определить возможность применения совокупности технологий искусственного интеллекта на предприятии с учетом особенностей управления человеческими ресурсами\. Исследование является поисковым и направлено на изучение практики применения платформ на базе искусственного интеллекта в сфере управления человеческим ресурсами\. На основании сравнительного анализа публикаций из источников и авторской методики \(группы системообразующих характеристик коллектива и их объединение в модель управления человеческими ресурсами\) в работе выявлены недостающие компоненты из совокупности системообразующих характеристик, имеющихся в платформах для целей управления человеческими ресурсами, которые помогут эффективнее использовать технологии искусственного интеллекта для обеспечения долгосрочного развития и конкурентных преимуществ предприятий\. В результате исследования определено, что существует ряд платформ на базе искусственного интеллекта для разных сфер УЧР, но большинство из них работают как автономные модули и не интегрированы в централизованные системы управления персоналом, и большинство платформ неприменимы в России\. Вместе с тем выявлено, что в рассматриваемых платформах наиболее часто встречающимися характеристиками, включенными в аналитику соответствия персонала или кандидата, являются такие характеристики как: квалификация и компетенции\. Реже — культура, внутрикорпоративная кооперация и конкуренция\. Абсолютно отсутствует анализ соответствия по характеристике координация\. Для экономии времени и ресурсов предприятия, автор статьи предлагает объединение обработки всех системообразующих характеристик одновременно в одно целое с помощью технологий искусственного интеллекта\. Результаты данного исследования позволят руководителям проводить эффективную кадровую политику с учетом особенностей управления человеческим ресурсами\. Due to the growing interest in AI technologies, practical examples of successful AI\-based solutions in HR management are gaining particular importance\. The purpose of this article is to determine the feasibility of applying a combination of AI technologies at an enterprise, considering the specifics of human resource management\. This is an exploratory study aimed at examining the practical application of AI\-based platforms in HR management\. Based on a comparative analysis of published sources and the author&\#x27;s methodology \(groups of systemically important team characteristics and their integration into an HR management model\), the paper identifies missing components from the set of systemically important characteristics available in HR management platforms\. These components will help more effectively utilize AI technologies to ensure long\-term development and competitive advantage for enterprises\. The study revealed that several AI\-based platforms exist for various HR areas, but most operate as stand\-alone modules and are not integrated into centralized HR management systems\. Most platforms are not applicable in Russia\. However, it was found that in the platforms under consideration, the most common characteristics included in personnel or candidate match analysis are qualifications and competencies\. Less commonly, culture, internal cooperation, and competition are considered\. Match analysis for the characteristic of coordination is completely absent\. To save time and resources, the author of the article proposes combining the processing of all system\-forming characteristics into a single solution using AI technologies\. The results of this study will enable managers to implement effective HR policies considering the specifics of human resources management\.

## [Elastic–Plastic Modeling and Experimental Characterization of Granular Jamming Actuators](../publications/77e73ae13a7016f77b76.md)

Saheli Patel; Prashant K\. Purohit; Jordan R\. Raney

Granular jamming enables soft actuators to transition rapidly between compliant and rigid states, yet the disordered microstructure of jammed particles has long precluded rapid predictive modeling\. Here, we develop and validate a pressure‐dependent moment–curvature constitutive framework based on elastic‐perfectly‐plastic mechanics, describing the evolution of internal stress distributions during loading and unloading for granular jammed beams spanning vacuum pressures from 0 to 101 kPa and a broad geometric design space\. The model is validated against three‐point bending experiments, which are used to identify the effective granular modulus and yield stress \. Across the loading branch, the framework shows strong agreement over the tested design space, with deviations remaining within about 10% NRMSE\. It also captures the transition from a membrane‐dominated response in the unjammed state to a granular core‐dominated response in the jammed state, together with the onset of plasticity, residual deformation, and hysteresis\. Experiments further show an order‐of‐magnitude increase in force response upon jamming, while a systematic parametric study identifies beam diameter as a dominant design parameter affecting peak force and energy dissipation\. The resulting framework provides a predictive reduced‐order design tool linking material and geometric choices to the mechanical response of tunable‐stiffness structures\.

## [Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data](../publications/77ea37dbb224bac26d59.md)

Liu Yang; 吴钦木 Wu Qinmu; Jiaheng Li; Qingxuan Guan; Qilong Zhao; Boxue Xu; Ting Yang; Lingfeng Yang; Tao Zhou

With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI\-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years\. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources\. As a privacy\-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data\. Nevertheless, federated learning still faces several critical challenges in practical applications, including heterogeneous data distributions and model bias caused by non\-independent and identically distributed \(Non\-IID\) data\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic weighted learning method based on federated contrastive learning\. Different from approaches that focus solely on local representation optimization or employ fixed aggregation weights, the proposed framework couples supervised contrastive local training with loss\-feedback\-based multi\-factor client weighting, thereby jointly controlling local representation drift and server\-side model aggregation\. Specifically, contrastive learning is integrated into the federated learning framework by jointly leveraging local and global model representations for supervised contrastive optimization\. This strategy effectively mitigates the distribution discrepancy among different clients and gradually aligns local models with the global model as communication rounds progress\. Furthermore, during global aggregation, a loss\-feedback rule is introduced to accept the candidate global model parameters and aggregation weights only when the candidate loss\-feedback value decreases\. In addition, a multi\-factor weighted aggregation mechanism is introduced to comprehensively evaluate client contributions based on multiple factors, thereby assigning larger aggregation weights to local models that are more beneficial to global model optimization\. Experiments were conducted on an osteoporosis knee X\-ray dataset and a COVID–Pneumonia–Normal chest X\-ray dataset under IID and different Non\-IID settings\. Under severe Non\-IID conditions, the proposed method achieved accuracies of 92\.12% and 96\.27%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) values of 98\.31% and 97\.68%, and F1 scores of 90\.92% and 93\.22% on the two datasets, respectively\. Comparisons with representative federated learning methods and the static\-weighting ablation setting demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive classification performance and stable training behavior under heterogeneous client distributions\.

## [A call for minimum standards in methodological reporting for studies using animal\-borne accelerometers](../publications/77f24b11b6a183f84248.md)

Dáire Carroll; Jessica Harvey‐Carroll; José Luís Crespo\-Picazo; Daniel García‐Párraga; David March

Animal\-borne tri\-axial accelerometers are increasingly used to investigate animal behaviour and energetics\. Critical methodological details, such as device placement and dynamic range, are frequently underreported\. This lack of reporting hampers study replicability and interpretation of results\. It also complicates comparisons between studies\. In addition, as device placement and attachment method can impact animal welfare and survival, transparent reporting should be considered vital for ethical publication\. In this comment, we highlight these issues through a review of methodological reporting in studies involving attaching accelerometers to sea turtles\. To address these challenges, we propose a framework for minimum standardised reporting that outlines key metadata which researchers should include when publishing studies utilizing animal\-borne accelerometers\. We also recommend thorough testing of devices and attachment methods prior to their use in the field\. Adoption of this framework will enhance transparency, reproducibility, and comparability across studies, while promoting best practices in animal welfare\. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi\.org/10\.1186/s40317\-026\-00506\-9\.

## [Generative AI in Higher Education: Adoption, Risks, and Opportunities in the Nordic Region](../publications/77f7e61ab280b5912ebb.md)

Jerónimo Paiva

This study investigates how students and academic staff in Nordic higher education engage with generative artificial intelligence\. It asks what drives students to continue using these tools after initial adoption, and how academic staff perceive the opportunities and risks they bring\. The study is grounded in the Technology Continuance Theory, which holds that continued use is shaped by perceived usefulness, satisfaction, and confirmation, with trust and perceived security added as contextual factors relevant to the Nordic setting\.The research was conducted across five Nordic countries: Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland\. A mixed\-methods sequential design was used\. The quantitative phase involved an online questionnaire administered to higher education students across the region, analysed using Generalized Structured Component Analysis to test the hypothesised relationships between the constructs\. The qualitative phase involved semi\-structured interviews with professors, analysed thematically to capture the perspectives of academic staff on the use of generative AI in teaching and learning, with particular attention to linguistic representation and institutional practice\. The two phases were integrated to provide a fuller picture of adoption than either method could offer alone\.

## [Citation accuracy, citation noise, and citation bias: a foundation of citation analysis](../publications/780bb9a0306ab6100c41.md)

Lutz Bornmann; Christian Leibel

Abstract Citation analysis is widely used in research evaluation to assess the impact of scientific papers\. These analyses rest on the assumption that citation decisions by authors are accurate, representing the flow of knowledge from cited to citing papers\. However, in practice, researchers often cite for reasons that are not related to the fact that there has been \(intellectual\) input from previous papers\. Citations made for rhetorical reasons or without reading the cited work compromise the value of citations as instrument for research evaluation\. Past research on threats to the accuracy of citations has mainly focused on citation bias as the primary concern\. In this paper, we argue that citation noise—the undesirable variance in citation decisions—represents an equally critical but underexplored challenge in citation analysis\. We define and differentiate two types of citation noise: citation level noise and citation pattern noise\. Each type of noise is described in terms of how it arises and the specific ways it can undermine the validity of citation\-based research assessments\. By conceptually differing citation noise from citation accuracy and citation bias, we propose a framework for the foundation of citation analysis\. We discuss strategies and interventions to minimize citation noise, aiming to improve the reliability and validity of citation analysis in research evaluation\. We recommend that the current professional reform movement in research evaluation such as the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment \(CoARA\) pick up these strategies and interventions as an additional building block for careful, responsible use of bibliometric indicators in research evaluation\.

## [Theorising Prompt Humanities: Human–AI Interpretation and Postcolonial Knowledge in Amitav Ghosh&\#x27;s The Calcutta Chromosome](../publications/7815cced55bf3e7fc0ca.md)

Ramyabrata Chakraborty

Generative artificial intelligence has made prompting a prominent mode of interaction between users and large language models, but prompting is not exhausted by its technical role in eliciting model outputs\. This article proposes Prompt Humanities as an interdisciplinary interpretive framework for examining prompts as rhetorical, hermeneutic, and culturally situated acts\. Drawing on philosophical hermeneutics, reader\-response criticism, speech\-act theory, poststructuralism, Digital Humanities, and postcolonial studies, the framework asks how prompt\-mediated interaction reframes questions of interpretation, authorship, dialogue, and knowledge production\. The framework is developed through a qualitative close reading of Amitav Ghosh&\#x27;s The Calcutta Chromosome\. Rather than claiming that Ghosh predicted contemporary generative AI, the article treats the novel retrospectively as a literary site in which recursive questioning, fragmented archives, distributed forms of knowledge, and computer\-mediated inquiry can be compared with prompt\-mediated interpretation\. The analysis focuses on Murugan&\#x27;s revisionary hypotheses, Mangala&\#x27;s counter\-scientific network, Antar&\#x27;s interactions with the digital system Ava, and the novel&\#x27;s persistent resistance to epistemological closure\. The article argues that Prompt Humanities can complement existing Digital Humanities and postcolonial approaches by making the prompt itself an object of literary and cultural analysis\. Its contribution is therefore not the claim that prompting has been absent from humanities scholarship, but the development of a specific integrative vocabulary for analysing how questions, responses, archives, and interpretive agents are organised in human–AI and literary contexts\. The framework is presented as provisional and transferable, requiring further testing across texts, languages, genres, and forms of human–AI interaction\.

## [The Role of Non\-Coding RNAs in Chemoresistance to Cancer Therapies](../publications/78170ceae4b7084ff73b.md)

Ismail Ibrahim Al\-Janabi

Chemoresistance remains one of the greatest challenges in modern oncology and is responsible for most cancer\-related deaths\. Growing evidence has identified non\-coding RNAs \(ncRNAs\) as key regulators of resistance to anticancer therapy\. These molecules influence a wide range of classical resistance mechanisms, including drug efflux, apoptosis evasion, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, enhanced DNA repair, altered drug metabolism, and autophagy\. The growing understanding of ncRNA biology has created new opportunities for clinical translation\. Non\-coding RNAs show considerable promise as predictive biomarkers of treatment response and as therapeutic targets, several of which have already entered early\-phase clinical evaluation\. Nevertheless, significant challenges remain, including efficient and selective delivery, off\-target effects, tumor heterogeneity, and redundancy in ncRNA regulatory networks\.

## [Decoding Cell–Cell Interactions in Neurovascular Unit Co\-Cultures Through Molecular Vibrational Spectroscopy and Biology](../publications/781bae429857d6874a56.md)

Aleksandra Pragnąca; Agata Borkowska; Anna Antolak; Monika Leśniak; Karolina Augustyniak; Iga Czechowska; Kamilla Małek; Robert Zdanowski

The blood–brain barrier \(BBB\) is a coordinated multicellular interface in which intercellular communication shapes responses to injury and metabolic stress\. However, the contributions of individual cell types to collective stress adaptation remain poorly understood\. Here, we examined molecular and metabolic responses of 2D neurovascular unit \(NVU\) co\-culture models comprising endothelial cells, astrocytes, and pericytes exposed to hypoxia or sublethal HgCl2 toxicity\. An integrated platform combining gene and protein expression profiling, label\-free vibrational spectroscopic imaging, and machine\-learning\-based analysis was used to assess stress\-induced changes in cell\-cycle regulation and metabolism across mono\- and co\-culture configurations\. Hypoxia broadly suppressed G1/S and G2/M regulators, inducing cell\-cycle arrest with limited cell death, consistent with an adaptive response\. HgCl2 caused heterogeneous, model\-dependent changes in viability and proliferative capacity\. Spectroscopic phenotyping revealed that the triple co\-culture exhibited spectral features resembling those of pericyte monocultures, although the contributions of cell–cell interactions and differences in culture conditions could not be distinguished\. Fluorescence imaging further revealed mitochondria\-associated signals at cell–cell contact sites, suggesting a possible association of mitochondrial material with regions of close cellular interaction\. The presence of pericytes was associated with a more stress\-resistant cellular phenotype in the investigated co\-culture configurations\. The developed spectroscopic–molecular platform provides a label\-free framework for characterizing cellular communication and stress responses in multicellular NVU co\-culture models\.

## [Inter\-system reliability of markerless motion capture in older hip and knee patients during walking](../publications/78351c75b0d65645e4a7.md)

Leonhard Stein; Lukas Gschoßmann; Mareike Barthel; Sebastian Dendorfer

This study evaluated the inter\-system reliability of multi\-camera markerless motion capture \(MMC\) during walking in older adults with hip or knee pathology and compared inter\-system disagreement with a healthy control group\. Forty\-one participants were included: 15 hip patients, 13 knee patients, and 13 healthy controls\. All participants performed walking trials recorded simultaneously by two temporally aligned MMC systems\. Inter\-system consistency was assessed using waveform\-based comparison of joint angle trajectories across the gait cycle and discrete range of motion parameters\. Waveform disagreement was quantified using one\-dimensional statistical parametric mapping and root\-mean\-square error, while discrete outcomes were evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficient \(ICC\), standard error of measurement \(SEM\), minimal detectable change at the 95% confidence level, and Bland–Altman metrics\. Group differences in subject\-level inter\-system disagreement metrics were tested using linear models\. ICC\-based inter\-system reliability was predominantly high, with 18 of 36 parameters classified as excellent, 10 good, 6 moderate, and 2 poor\. SEM values were below 2 ∘ for most parameters\. The least robust results were consistently observed for trunk flexion and selected transverse\-plane variables\. Exploratory group comparisons did not reveal a consistent directional pattern of increased disagreement in the pathological groups, and clinically plausible group differences were similarly reflected by both systems\. However, the modest group sizes limit the ability to exclude smaller pathology\-related effects on measurement consistency\. These findings indicate small within\-platform inter\-system disagreement in most lower\-limb outcomes for gait analysis in older adults with hip or knee pathology\. Trunk and some transverse\-plane outputs should be interpreted with greater caution\.

## [Multiyear Pattern Discovery and Policy Implications of Transit Bus Involved Fatal Crashes](../publications/783d517446427c2c52d1.md)

Tausif Islam Chowdhury; Sharif Ahmed Rafat; Subasish Das

Abstract Fatal transit bus crashes remain a significant safety concern in urban transportation systems, with buses operating in complex, high\-risk environments where interactions with pedestrians, cyclists, and other vehicles are frequent\. This study seeks to identify the key factors contributing to these fatal incidents using Cluster Correspondence Analysis \(CCA\), applied to data from the Fatality Analysis Reporting System \(FARS\)\. By analyzing crash patterns over multiple years, the study uncovered distinct crash characteristics related to intersection\-related conflicts, high\-speed roadways, non\-motorist involvement, and inadequate traffic control\. The findings highlighted the crucial role of roadway design, including the presence of unprotected medians and the lack of traffic control devices, in increasing crash severity\. In response to these patterns, the study proposes a series of policy recommendations aimed at improving road infrastructure, enhancing traffic management systems, and promoting safer driving behaviors\. These policy measures are designed to reduce the risk of fatal crashes involving transit buses and to ensure safer streets for all road users\. The insights provided in this study offered a comprehensive foundation for future transit safety strategies and policy development\.

## [Representative Social Choice: From Learning Theory to AI Alignment](../publications/7845a863ffba442d4a13.md)

Tianyi Qiu

Social choice theory is the study of preference aggregation across a population, used both in mechanism design for human agents and in the democratic alignment of language models\. In this study, we propose the representative social choice framework for the modeling of democratic representation in collective decisions, where the number of issues and individuals are too large for mechanisms to consider all preferences directly\. These scenarios are widespread in real\-world decision\-making processes, such as jury trials, legislation, corporate governance, and, more recently, language model alignment\. In representative social choice, the population is represented by a finite sample of individual\-issue pairs based on which social choice decisions are made\. We show that many of the deepest questions in representative social choice can be formulated as statistical learning problems, and prove the generalization properties of social choice mechanisms using the theory of machine learning\. We further formulate axioms for representative social choice, and prove Arrow\-like impossibility theorems with new combinatorial tools of analysis\. Our framework introduces the representative approach to social choice, opening up research directions at the intersection of social choice, learning theory, and AI alignment\.

## [النقد الأدبي الحديث بين عبقرية الناقد البشرية والذكاء الاصطناعي: تحديات وآفاق](../publications/784dae75eb2345b09fb2.md)

كرار جواد كاظم المفرجي; حمد زكي رمضان الزبيدي

للنقد الأدبي عوالم شاسعة شغلتها العقول البشرية منذ نشأة الأدب، وحملت على عاتقها ميكانيزمات وعلائق تتجاوز أرضيتها الابستمولوجية والانطباعية، حتى بلغت أوجها في العصور المتقدِّمة، بيد أنَّ للعصر الرقمي رأي آخر في محاولة المقاربة من العقلية النقدية للجنس البشري بعدما شهد تقافزاً في المسارات البحثية وأثار جدلاً واسعاً في تفكيك وتحليل النص الشعري، فقد اعتمدت برامج الذكاء الاصطناعي مثل: \(Chat GPT\) و \(Deepseek\) على تحليل النصوص بشكل بيانات متجزِّئة ومنحها القدرة على تفكيك النصوص بشكل تفصيلي تبعاً للظواهر النقدية الأساس، وهذا ما يكشفه البحث في تباين التحليل النقدي بين العقلية البشرية وتحليل الذكاء الاصطناعي\.

## [Familiar Style and Calibrated Correction in Repeated AI Use\. A framework for style recognition discrimination and substantive correction](../publications/785a6c77271e49574c02.md)

Luiza Scurtu

Repeated users of an artificial\-intelligence agent may learn both its competence and how it sounds\. This paper proposes that acquired style congruence can change acceptance independently of evidential quality, while any benefit to error management may arise through more than one route\. Learned style–correctness contingencies can guide classification; reduced processing demands may also free attention for substantive checking when style itself is non\-diagnostic\. The framework distinguishes recognition, response criterion, classification sensitivity, competence learning, defect identification, successful correction, and final accuracy\. Five competing mechanisms are specified: familiarity halo, anomaly vigilance, diagnostic cue learning, competence learning, and processing\-efficiency learning\. Building on appropriate\-reliance research, calibration symmetry is treated as a requirement for identification and measurement: both familiar\-looking wrong answers and unfamiliar\-looking correct answers must be examined\. It does not imply equal frequency, cost, or normative importance\. The contribution is a bounded synthesis for acquired, source\-specific style, not a new general principle of reliance or a demonstrated familiarity effect\. Study 1 crosses acquired style congruence with correctness while preserving randomized assignment and measuring inferred source or version change\. Study 2 varies cue diagnosticity and distinguishes classification through style from identifying and repairing substantive defects\. Outcome feedback, trial\-level learning, delayed unaided performance, and transfer are specified separately from assisted performance\. Conversational affirmation and linguistic accommodation are adjacent pathways, not evidence of acquired\-style effects\. Governance implications remain provisional pending direct evidence\.

## [Sustainable Development and Sustainable Agriculture Principles Approach for the Future of Agriculture: The Case of Erzurum and Türkiye](../publications/785eb7e8e2a922bfae78.md)

Çağlar Kıvanç Kaymaz; Cabir ZEREN

This study employs Multi\-Criteria Decision\-Making \(MCDM\) to evaluate sustainable agriculture priorities in Türkiye and Erzurum, addressing climate change and resource scarcity\. Using a two\-stage expert consultation process—comprising a 5\-expert Nominal Group Technique \(NGT\) panel to establish criteria and a 16\-expert panel \(encompassing Geography and Agricultural Sciences specialists with 5 to 25\+ years of experience\) using the Best\-Worst Method \(BWM\)—a hierarchical framework of three main dimensions and 16 sub\-criteria was evaluated; the core panel participated across both national and regional evaluations while expanded experts assessed localized priorities\. Results indicate that Soil Management is the primary environmental priority for both regions\. Socially, Education emerged as the most critical factor\. Economic priorities diverged, with Agricultural Inputs leading across Türkiye, while Product Selection and Productivity proved paramount for Erzurum\. These findings underscore the necessity of aligning sustainable agricultural policies with regional dynamics rather than adopting a one\-size\-fits\-all approach\. By identifying localized weighting for sustainability criteria, this research provides a strategic framework for decision\-makers to optimize agricultural management systems and enhance regional resilience\.

## [Prediksi Kurs Rupiah terhadap Dolar dan Yuan Menggunakan LSTM\-PSO dan XGBoost](../publications/78697617d354ad8b00ba.md)

Oktaria Indi Cahyani; Joan Angelina Widians; Fahrul Agus

The Indonesian rupiah exchange rate is a key determinant of Indonesia&\#x27;s economic conditions and is vulnerable to global geopolitical dynamics, yet geopolitical risk is still rarely incorporated explicitly into exchange rate forecasting models\. This study compares the accuracy of XGBoost and Long Short\-Term Memory optimized with Particle Swarm Optimization \(LSTM\-PSO\) in forecasting IDR/USD and IDR/CNY, using the Geopolitical Risk Daily \(GPRD\) index as an external predictor\. The dataset comprises daily IDR/USD, IDR/CNY, and GPRD observations from February 2022 to February 2026\. The workflow includes data collection, cleaning, and integration, feature engineering, normalization, chronological data splitting, and model evaluation using RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R²\. Under the tested scenario, LSTM\-PSO yielded lower errors than XGBoost for both currency pairs, with a MAPE below 1% and an R² above 0\.89, whereas XGBoost produced a negative R²\. These findings indicate the potential of LSTM\-PSO as an exchange rate forecasting model that incorporates geopolitical risk information, and may serve as a consideration for banks, investors, and international businesses in monitoring exchange rate movements\.

## [Adaptive lightweight intrusion detection system for internet of things and internet of medical things security](../publications/7869b090baa4d1cf43d1.md)

M\. S\. Padmini; V\. Amruth; A\.S\. Sindhu; M\. Asha Rani; V\. K\. Annapurna; C S Asha

Abstract The rapid development of Internet of Things \(IoT\) and Internet of Medical Things \(IoMT\) environments has increased the risks of cybersecurity, especially from DDoS, DoS, and other complex cyberattacks\. Extensive research has been carried out on existing Machine Learning \(ML\) and Deep Learning \(DL\) based Intrusion Detection Systems \(IDS\); however, they still face several challenges such as class imbalance, high computational complexity, and poor generalization over heterogeneous datasets\. This research addresses the gaps by proposing an Adaptive Weighted Feature\-Optimized Lightweight Intrusion Detection System \(AWFOL\-IDS\)\. The main goal is to design a scalable and efficient IDS that accurately detects attacks in both IoT and IoMT environments\. AWFOL\-IDS integrates Adaptive Weighted Information\-Entropy Feature Selection \(AWIE\-FS\) with a Weighted Adaptive Random Forest with Feature\-Integrated Optimization \(WARF\-FIO\) classifier with imbalance\-aware sampling and weighted decision mechanisms\. Experimental evaluation on CICIoT2023 and CICIoMT2024 datasets shows strong performance with 0\.9989, 0\.9968, and 0\.9939 accuracy for 2\-class, 8\-class, and 34\-class tasks and 0\.9998, 0\.9992, and 0\.9856 accuracy for 2\-class, 6\-class, and 19\-class tasks, respectively\. Also, evaluation was conducted using 5\-fold cross\-validation, where findings showed better performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F\-score\. In conclusion, AWFOL\-IDS is a lightweight and efficient solution for real\-world intrusion detection in IoT and IoMT environments\.

## [Botune: an AI\-supported scaffolding system for children’s drawing\-based narrative expression in nature learning](../publications/787698cc98adc6f2b150.md)

Yi Li; 陈忆帆; 季书战; Yao Hu; Yuyan Ma

Nature exploration fosters children’s cognitive development and environmental awareness; however, kindergarten curricula are often constrained by limited resources and repetitive interaction, leaving children’s observations only weakly integrated into structured understanding and expression\. We present Botune, an AI\-supported creative\-expression tool for kindergarten planting activities that integrates plant observation, drawing, spoken narration, and animation\-based sharing\. We conducted an exploratory, fixed\-order within\-participant study in kindergarten planting classes with 27 children and three educators; 24 complete cases were analysed after excluding data from three children who did not complete the drawing task\. The traditional activity preceded the Botune\-supported activity by seven days\. The proportion of activity time spent observing and teacher\-rated involvement scores during sharing were higher in the later session\. The later narrations contained significantly more actions and character interactions; character counts were descriptively higher but did not remain statistically significant after Holm correction, and state\- or emotion\-related expressions did not differ significantly\. These semantic counts index narrative elaboration rather than overall narrative quality or general narrative ability\. These differences cannot be attributed to Botune alone\. Scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding were not directly assessed by these measures\. The study offers exploratory observations and design considerations for AI\-supported narrative expression in kindergarten nature learning\.

## [Effectiveness of Mobile Health \(mHealth\) Applications in Chronic Disease Management: Implications for Medical\-Surgical Nursing Practice](../publications/78770d444d20eeb0f3a9.md)



Chronic diseases, including diabetes mellitus, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\), chronic kidney disease, and cancer, account for the majority of global morbidity and mortality\.The increasing prevalence of these conditions has placed substantial pressure on healthcare systems, emphasizing the need for innovative approaches that support long\-term disease management\.Mobile health \(mHealth\), a component of digital health that utilizes smartphones, wearable devices, mobile applications, and wireless technologies, has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance patient engagement, medication adherence, self\-management, and remote monitoring\.Recent evidence indicates that mHealth interventions improve clinical outcomes by facilitating continuous communication between patients and healthcare providers, promoting lifestyle modification, and enabling early identification of disease\-related complications\.For medical\-surgical nurses, mHealth applications provide opportunities to deliver patient\-centered care beyond hospital settings, strengthen health education, and improve continuity of care\.Despite these advantages, challenges such as digital literacy, privacy concerns, interoperability, long\-term user engagement, and equitable access remain barriers to widespread implementation\.This review examines the effectiveness of mHealth applications in chronic disease management, highlights current evidence, discusses implications for medical\-surgical nursing practice, and outlines future directions for integrating digital health technologies into evidence\-based nursing care\.Current reviews suggest that digital health interventions improve self\-management, communication with healthcare providers, and quality of life, although sustaining long\-term engagement remains a key challenge\.\.\.\.\.

## [Isolated TERT promoter mutation may define a high\-risk prognostic subgroup in papillary thyroid carcinoma: an exploratory, hypothesis\-generating analysis of TCGA and GSE33630 datasets](../publications/78887d20b675435a1f86.md)

Bing Guan; Rong Zhou; Sijia Zhang; Yawen Chen; Lulu Li; Ping He

Background The prognostic value of combined BRAF V600E and TERT promoter \(TERTp\) mutations in papillary thyroid carcinoma \(PTC\) has been established in surgical cohorts\. However, the independent impact of TERTp mutation in the absence of BRAF mutation remains underexplored, particularly within publicly available genomic datasets\. Methods We analyzed 49 PTC patients with available BRAF and TERTp mutation data from The Cancer Genome Atlas \(TCGA\) Thyroid Carcinoma \(THCA\) cohort\. Patients were stratified into four subgroups: BRAF−/TERTp−, BRAF\+/TERTp−, BRAF−/TERTp\+, and BRAF\+/TERTp\+\. Progression\-free interval \(PFI\) was compared using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression\. Additionally, differential gene expression analysis was performed using GSE33630 \(n = 42 PTC samples\) to explore transcriptomic correlates of BRAF mutation\. Results Overall log\-rank analysis revealed significant PFI differences across the four subgroups \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The BRAF−/TERTp\+ group demonstrated the worst prognosis, with 3 of 5 patients experiencing disease progression \(median PFI = 5\.7 months\), compared with no events in the BRAF−/TERTp− group\. Univariable Cox regression identified BRAF−/TERTp\+ as the strongest adverse predictor \(HR = 9\.57, 95% CI: 2\.02–45\.25, p = 0\.004\), which remained significant after adjustment for age \(HR = 8\.38, 95% CI: 1\.67–42\.19, p = 0\.010\)\. In GSE33630, 42 differentially expressed genes \(DEGs; FDR &lt; 0\.05\) were identified between BRAF\-mutant and wild\-type PTC, including downregulation of PCDH20, HES1, and TLR2, and upregulation of DAPK2\. Conclusions This hypothesis\-generating, exploratory analysis suggests that isolated TERTp mutation may represent an underrecognized high\-risk PTC subgroup\. The wide confidence intervals reflect the small sample size and limited event counts inherent to this dataset\. These preliminary findings warrant validation in larger prospective cohorts with comprehensive molecular annotation\.

## [Divergent Failure Modes of Two Intrusion Detection Benchmarks Under A Common Audit](../publications/78891880af0c55daaf33.md)

Arya K S; Selvavinayaki

Two public corpora carry much of the empirical load in machine learning research on intrusion detection for wireless sensor networks and for industrial internet of things deployments\. Accuracy on both is routinely reported near the ceiling\. We audit both with one procedure, holding features, models, metrics and seeds fixed, and they fail in different ways\. On Edge\-IIoTset the binary task is settled before any model is fitted\. Four string valued fields record how the capture was serialised rather than how the traffic behaved, because the absent value was written as one token on benign rows and a different token on attack rows, and a depth one decision stump on any of them reaches 1\.0000 where the majority baseline is 0\.8417\. All seven learners in the bank reach that ceiling\. Removing the four fields separates them again\. On WSN\-DS the same audit returns almost nothing, and that is the second result\. Discarding 8,873 duplicate records moves the bank average equal error rate by 0\.0000, and a node disjoint split that shares no sensor with training moves it by 0\.0005, against a spread of 0\.0158 across the models themselves\. A third check finds what neither corpus level audit does\. With one attack family withheld from training, detection of the withheld behaviour runs from 0\.007 to 0\.886\. These checks are cheap, and which of them bites is not predictable in advance\.

## [Development and Comparative Analysis of AI\-Based Classification Models for Mitigating Email\-Related Cyber Risks](../publications/788d8ffe0a5591cbfca8.md)

Mehmet Tepeli

Corporate email systems are a fundamental component of businesses&\#x27; communication and business processes, but they also bring significant cybersecurity risks such as spam and phishing attacks\. Especially as digitalization increases, the accurate and rapid detection of email\-based threats faced by businesses has become a critical requirement\. This research presents a comparative performance analysis of machine learning and transformer\-based deep learning models for the automatic classification of spam, normal, and phishing messages\. A large\-scale, three\-class dataset consisting of 479,466 English email records was used in the study\. Traditional machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines \(SVM\-LinearSVC\), Logistic Regression \(LR\), Naive Bayes \(NB\), and Decision Tree \(DT\) models, as well as transformer\-based BERT, RoBERTa, and ELECTRA models, were evaluated\. The performance of the models was analyzed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-Score, ROC\-AUC, and confusion matrix metrics\. In addition, statistical comparisons, phishing\-specific security errors, cost\-sensitive scenarios, and computational efficiency were evaluated to provide a more comprehensive assessment of model performance\. Transformer\-based models generally achieved stronger overall and class\-specific classification performance, while conventional machine learning models offered substantially lower computational requirements\. BERT achieved the highest overall performance, with 98\.84% accuracy and a Macro F1\-Score of 0\.9827, while RoBERTa produced statistically comparable results\. Security\-oriented and computational analyses further showed that the model with the highest aggregate performance was not necessarily optimal for all deployment scenarios, highlighting the importance of considering misclassification consequences, computational requirements, email traffic volume, and available infrastructure in model selection\. It is considered that the research contributes to the literature on email security and AI\-based cyber risk management through models developed using a large\-scale, three\-class dataset, diverse AI architectures, and security\-oriented evaluation criteria\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Capability and Corporate Green Innovation: The Role of Knowledge Fusion and Technology Cooperation](../publications/7895f4a739700e1792c4.md)

Ruiyi Cao; Minggao Xue

This paper examines the relationship between firms’ artificial intelligence \(AI\) capability and corporate green innovation and the potential channels underlying this relationship\. Using a firm\-year panel of Chinese A\-share firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen main boards from 2002 to 2024, we find that stronger AI capability is positively associated with green innovation output, citation\-based green innovation impact, and green technological knowledge breadth\. Further mechanism analyses provide evidence consistent with knowledge fusion and formal technology cooperation as two potential channels\. Specifically, stronger AI capability predicts greater technological overlap between firms’ AI and green patent portfolios and broader formal green technology cooperation in the subsequent year, including inter\-firm cooperation and industry–university–research collaboration\. Overall, the findings suggest that AI capability may help shape the knowledge generation and collaborative development processes of green innovation, potentially contributing to greater green innovation output, impact, and knowledge breadth\.

## [A Language\-Informed Loss for Visual Generation](../publications/789f91317fdf31c290b0.md)

Suchir Agarwal; Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran; Ziyu Chen; Kyle Sargent; Juan Carlos Niebles; Li Fei\-Fei; Jiajun Wu

End\-to\-end visual generation with pixel\-space loss has recently achieved competitive performance without the need for learned image tokenizers\. In this work, we study whether language\-informed supervision can provide a richer training signal than pixel loss for visual generation\. We introduce LILIE \(pronounced &quot;lily&quot;\), a Language\-Informed and Lossless Image Encoder\. LILIE is an invertible image transform trained such that a vision\-language model can recover captions from noised features\. The encoder uses a normalizing flow transformer trained jointly with a vision\-language model via next token prediction\. We then use the encoder to extract a simple language\-informed loss for text\-to\-image generation\. We train JiT models with LILIE loss, reducing gFD by 14 points \(66\.84 $\\to$ 53\.01\) against a pixel\-only baseline on the GPIC dataset\. Our code, encoders, and generative models are available at https://suchiragarwal\.com/lilie\.

## [Marine Pharmacognosy: A Revised Review on Bioactive Compounds from Marine Natural Sources](../publications/78b2263a77bb9e220a89.md)



Marine pharmacognosy is the study of bioactive chemical constituents obtained from marine organisms and their application in drug discovery, pharmaceutical development, nutraceutical research, and biotechnology\.The marine environment contains exceptionally diverse ecological niches, including coral reefs, intertidal zones, deep\-sea sediments, hydrothermal vents, mangroves, and microbial symbioses\.Organisms living in these competitive and physically demanding habitats produce secondary metabolites with unusual scaffolds, halogenation patterns, stereochemistry, and mechanisms of action\.This revised review summarizes the historical development, major marine sources, chemical classes, clinically important drugs, pharmacological activities, extraction and isolation techniques, biotechnological advances, limitations, and future prospects of marine pharmacognosy\.A narrative review method was adopted using standard review\-writing principles and transparent literature selection\.The evidence indicates that marine\-derived or marine\-inspired compounds have contributed to anticancer, analgesic, antiviral, antimicrobial, anti\-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective drug leads\.Successful examples such as cytarabine, ziconotide, trabectedin, eribulin, and marine\-toxin\-based antibody\-drug conjugates demonstrate the translational value of marine natural products\.However, ecological sustainability, low natural abundance, structural complexity, dereplication, scalable production, toxicity, and regulatory barriers remain major challenges\.Emerging strategies including genome mining, metagenomics, metabolomics, synthetic biology, aquaculture, microbial fermentation, green extraction, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence can improve the discovery and development pipeline\.Marine pharmacognosy therefore represents a scientifically significant and clinically promising field for future therapeutics, provided that exploration is coupled with ethical access, biodiversity conservation, and reproducible pharmaceutical evaluation\.
