## [Unlocking the “black box” of food prediction models: Applications and perspectives of explainable artificial intelligence in agri\-food chemical analysis and quality control](../publications/78d836af92b98ff30539.md)

Wenting LI; Junwei Guo; Hexin Chen; Ran Wan; Meijuan Fan; Yali Liu; Song Yang; Cong Wang; Fuwei Xie; Cong Nie; Zhao Le; Hongbo Wang

With the deep integration of global agri\-food supply chains, artificial intelligence and machine learning have been widely applied in fields such as food traceability, adulteration detection, and quality grading\. However, high\-precision models like CNN and XGBoost are often considered “black boxes” due to opaque decision\-making, undermining their credibility and robustness\. Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) offers a pathway to model transparency\. This paper systematically reviews XAI progress in food chemistry over 2021–2026, covering inherently interpretable models and post\-hoc methods \(e\.g\., SHAP, LIME, Grad\-CAM\)\. Focusing on three major scenarios—geographical traceability and adulteration detection, flavor chemistry and sensory evaluation, food safety risk assessment—it analyzes XAI applications in quantifying feature contributions, identifying key spectral bands, and identifying candidate biomarkers for subsequent targeted validation\. Application paradigms for different data types \(spectra, images, chemical composition, sensor data\) are summarized\. In view of the challenges in current research, such as methodological biases under high\-dimensional collinearity and the lack of an integration mechanism between interpretation results and prior chemical knowledge, this paper proposes key directions for future breakthroughs, with the expectation of promoting food science research toward a more intelligent, transparent and trustworthy new paradigm\.

## [Can Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) Design Better Antibodies? Advances and Future Prospects](../publications/78f5243b9bf66875e080.md)

Bhavani Puvvala, Sanjeev Kumar, Anisetty Shilpa Sree, Balivada Deepika, Kautuk Kumar Sardar

Anthelmintic resistance is a considered to be pose threat to cattle health and profitability of livestock\. This review mainly focuses on the important factors that speed up the development of resistance to anthelmintics by cattle, of which three most common gastrointestinal nematodes are Ostertagia ostertagi, Cooperia species, and Haemonchus placei\. The biological and physiologicalmechanisms that are reason for these parasites to withstand exposure mainly involves: mutations at target site \(such as β\-tubulin gene alterations\), P\-glycoprotein efflux pumps upregulations, and enhancement of drug metabolismvia detoxifying enzymes\. These adaptations mainly help in development of resistance to three important primary anthelmintic classes like benzimidazoles, macrocyclic lactones, and nicotinic agonists\. Additionally, some farm management practices which includes prophylactic deworming of entire herd, underdosing of drugs, improper route of drug application, and the elimination of refugiaseverely exacerbate selective pressure\. Failing to control the development of resistance results in severe subclinical production loses, increased mortality rates, and economic losses\. To enhance the future livestock sustainability, a transition toward Integrated Parasite Management \(IPM\) is very important\. This approach mainly focuses on Targeted Selective Treatment \(TST\), monitoring of the faecal sample by via Faecal Egg Count Reduction Tests \(FECRT\), rotational grazing, and combination therapies to conserve drug efficacy\.

## [Whole\-Body Dexterity](../publications/78fb5b16c8f519639561.md)

Conor Mc Gartoll; An Dang; Pranay Thangeda; Arjun Gupta; Carolina Higuera; Nima Fazeli; Mustafa Mukadam; Manikantan Nambi

Current humanoid dexterous manipulation remains largely confined to end\-effectors and simple grasps, falling short of humans&\#x27; ability to engage the entire body by bracing and sliding bulky objects against the arms and torso\. We introduce Whole\-Body Dexterity \(WBD\), a general framework that uses the robot&\#x27;s body and appendages as contact surfaces to grasp and manipulate objects\. Our sim\-to\-real pipeline first generates a dataset of feasible whole\-body grasps, then trains reinforcement\-learning experts on a general any\-to\-any repositioning objective by sampling initial and goal grasps from the dataset, and distills these experts into a single policy that uses proprioception and object geometry\. We show that the distilled policy transfers zero\-shot to a real Unitree G1, where it repositions a basketball and a cardboard box to regions around the torso and completes a long\-horizon task that stows a box under one arm, carries it from a shelf to a table, and places it\. The controller operates interactively, steered by coarse motion references from a human teleoperator\. Across real\-world whole\-body manipulation tasks, the distilled controller completes 90% of trials, compared with 18% for direct retargeting and 4% for a generalist whole\-body controller\.

## [Klasifikasi Kelayakan UMR 98 Kota di Indonesia Berdasarkan Harga Pangan Pokok Menggunakan K\-Nearest Neighbor](../publications/790127dc890d2a4a6532.md)

Eliza Tata Amalia; Farid Akbar Siregar

Upah Minimum Regional \(UMR\) merupakan instrumen kebijakan pengupahan yang idealnya mencerminkan kemampuan daya beli pekerja terhadap kebutuhan pangan pokok, namun disparitas harga pangan antarwilayah di Indonesia menyebabkan nominal UMR yang sama dapat memiliki tingkat kelayakan yang berbeda\. Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun model klasifikasi untuk menilai tingkat kelayakan UMR pada 98 kota di Indonesia berdasarkan harga tujuh komoditas pangan pokok \(beras, minyak goreng, telur, daging ayam, gula pasir, cabai, dan UMR\) menggunakan algoritma K\-Nearest Neighbor \(KNN\)\. Data dikumpulkan dari Pusat Informasi Harga Pangan Strategis \(PIHPS\) Nasional/Badan Pangan Nasional, Badan Pusat Statistik, dan Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan Republik Indonesia periode 2025\-2026, kemudian diproses melalui tahapan Knowledge Discovery in Database meliputi seleksi, pembersihan, transformasi Min\-Max Normalization, penerapan algoritma KNN, dan evaluasi menggunakan Confusion Matrix dengan pembagian data latih dan data uji sebesar 80:20\. Pengujian terhadap beberapa nilai K menunjukkan bahwa K=3 memberikan kinerja terbaik dengan akurasi 80,00%, presisi 100,00%, recall 42,86%, dan F1\-Score 60,00%\. Nilai presisi sempurna mengindikasikan model tidak pernah salah mengklasifikasikan kota berkategori Tidak Layak sebagai Layak, sementara nilai recall yang relatif rendah disebabkan oleh ketidakseimbangan kelas pada data latih yang didominasi kategori Tidak Layak\. Model klasifikasi ini diimplementasikan dalam aplikasi berbasis Python Tkinter yang dapat digunakan sebagai alat bantu evaluasi kelayakan UMR oleh pemangku kebijakan daerah\.

## [Remotely profiling the tropospheric absolute humidity using a single ground\-based GNSS meteorological station based on an artificial neural network](../publications/790bfeedcd7d62fa5cd2.md)

周守东; Wang Degao; Zheng Qingqing; Jiang Peng

Near\-real\-time profiling of the vertical distribution of tropospheric water vapor is important for a wide range of weather monitoring and forecasting applications\. In this study, a GNSS\-based Profiling Tropospheric Humidity Network \(GPTHNet\) was developed to retrieve tropospheric absolute humidity using observations from a single ground\-based GNSS meteorological station\. The input variables of GPTHNet include observation time, precipitable water vapor \(PWV\), ground\-level meteorological parameters from the GNSS meteorological station, and the nearest radiosonde humidity profile prior to the observation epoch\. Historical radiosonde observations are used to provide initialization information for GPTHNet\. The training data for the artificial neural network \(ANN\) models were mainly obtained from the Atmospheric Radiation Measurement \(ARM\) User Facility and covered the period from 2002 to 2011\. Absolute humidity was estimated at 40 height levels ranging from 250 m to 10,000 m, with a vertical interval of 250 m, using two ANN profiling models\. The performance of the two ANN profiling systems was evaluated by comparing their predictions with independent humidity profiles obtained from radiosondes and Raman lidar\. The ANN\_Init generally outperformed the ANN\_NoInit, particularly in the middle and upper troposphere, where the relative error of the ANN\_Init was noticeably smaller than that of the ANN\_NoInit\. For the independent GNSS–radiosonde\-combined validation, the RMSE of the ANN\_Init reached a maximum of 1\.90 g/m 3 at 500 m and decreased to below 0\.1 g/m 3 at the highest levels; against the Raman lidar observations, the relative RMSE increased from about 12% at the lowest level to about 75% at the upper levels during the monsoon season\. The results indicate that the accuracy of the ANN profiling algorithm is comparable to that of tomographic techniques\.

## [SMART SURGICAL SCHEDULING: AN AI\-ENABLED FRAMEWORK FOR OPERATING ROOM EFFICIENCY AND QUALITY OF CARE](../publications/7919f71e27e9de84cbd5.md)

Mohammed Mudassir; Bater Ibrahim khan; Mudassir Uddin Ahmed; Mohammed Mushtaq

The scheduling of surgical procedures is a vital and intricate aspect of hospital operations, significantly impacting patient outcomes, financial success, and clinician welfare\.Traditional manual scheduling techniques are inadequate for managing the dynamic and unpredictable characteristics of the operating room \(OR\) environment, resulting in staff fatigue, increased overtime expenses, and a decline in care quality\.This study presents a comprehensive artificial intelligence \(AI\) framework that utilises predictive analytics, multi\-objective optimisation, and natural language processing to create dynamic, efficient, and equitable surgical schedules\.The technology utilises a continuous feedback loop, assimilating historical and real\-time data to optimise operational efficiency while considering human aspects\.Conceptual analysis indicates Smart Surgical Scheduling: An AI\-Enabled Framework for Operating Room Efficiency and Quality of Care https://iaeme\.com/Home/journal/IJCET

## [Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations](../publications/791ac8a28012eb6c2a91.md)

Anchal Saxena; P\. Daniel Meerburg; Guochao Sun; Tzu‐Ching Chang; Lluís Mas\-Ribas

Abstract Reconstructing the initial conditions of the Universe from late\-time tracers would unlock cosmological information buried by non\-linear structure formation and astrophysics\. We reconstruct the initial density field corresponding to z = 300, with its linear amplitude extrapolated to z = 0, from simulated 21\-cm and CO\(1–0\) line\-intensity maps at z = 8 generated with the semi\-numerical code, LIMFAST\. Using a three\-dimensional U\-Net, we reconstruct the initial conditions and evaluate their impact on cosmological parameter constraints\. The two tracers probe complementary environments: 21\-cm emission traces neutral, low\-density regions of the intergalactic medium, while CO traces overdense, star\-forming regions\. We additionally train and evaluate the reconstruction on maps incorporating SKA1\-Low– and COMAP\-ERA–like instrumental response and thermal noise\. In the noiseless case, combining both tracers delivers the most accurate reconstruction across ionisation states, with the cross\-correlation coefficient between the reconstructed and true initial density fields, \|C\(k\)\| ≳ 0\.90 for k ≲ 0\.75 Mpc−1\. With observational effects, small\-scale information is degraded, but the joint reconstruction retains substantial large\-scale coherence, with \|C\(k\)\| ≳ 0\.70 for k ≲ 0\.3 Mpc−1\. To quantify the cosmological information gain, we perform simulation\-based inference using power\-spectrum summaries pre\- and post\-reconstruction\. Across an ensemble of realisations, reconstruction yields the largest improvements for σ8 and ns, with a median aggregate marginal compression of 1\.17 bits in the noiseless case, corresponding to a 56% reduction in the factorised product of prior\-normalised 68% marginal widths\. With observational effects, the corresponding median compression is 1\.29 bits\. These results demonstrate that joint 21\-cm–CO reconstruction can recover cosmological information beyond that captured by the pre\-reconstruction summaries\.

## [Serviceability\-oriented multimodal data integration for prescriptive road\-tunnel maintenance digital twins](../publications/792cc7406fb0757506f0.md)

Mengqi Huang; Mohammad Matin Rouhani; Zhihang Li; Huamei Zhu; Qianbing Zhang

Road tunnels are indispensable components of transport networks, providing critical connections while operating continuously under demanding environmental, geological, and hydrogeological conditions\. Their large dimensions, confined geometry, and uninterrupted operation make comprehensive inspection challenging\. Full\-face inspection technologies such as light detection and ranging \(LiDAR\) can rapidly capture high\-resolution surface data; however, the resulting digital models are often descriptive rather than explanatory or instructive\. This limitation is critical because seemingly minor defects may indicate latent deterioration and, if untreated, can lead to severe safety and operational consequences\. With advances in artificial intelligence, particularly large language models \(LLMs\) and robotic inspection platforms, tunnel inspection is expected to move beyond defect detection towards knowledge\-driven diagnosis and decision support\. This paper presents a serviceability\-oriented Prescriptive Twin framework for road\-tunnel maintenance, that is, a digital twin that represents asset conditions and recommends maintenance actions from inspection evidence and codified engineering knowledge\. The framework connects inspection data, prescriptive knowledge, decision\-making, and verification through a Web Ontology Language \(OWL 2\) domain ontology populated by a schema\-guided LLM pipeline\. The ontology integrates tunnel maintenance standards, road asset data requirements, and an extended Construction Operations Building Information Exchange \(COBie\) schema, while the pipeline converts narrative standards into expert\-validated seven\-level Failure Mode and Effects Analysis \(FMEA\) chains\. A multimodal layer maps red–green–blue \(RGB\), RGBD \(RGB with depth\), thermal, and ground\-penetrating radar \(GPR\) outputs to causal\-chain entry points, such as level 4 indicators and level 5 causes\. The framework specifies an identity\-resolution rule that binds observations from different modalities, and from successive inspection cycles, to a persistent defect instance, and a governance layer that binds every decision threshold to a dated clause of a specific standard edition, so that a prescription can be reconstructed against the edition under which it was issued\. Chain traversal maps onto the inspection report and an inter\-cycle change report\. Demonstrated on two defects in an operating road tunnel, the framework generates traceable prescriptions and shows how multimodal evidence improves intervention accuracy: at the worked example, thermal and GPR evidence escalated the intervention tier and expanded the repair scope by a factor of 3\.2 relative to RGB\-only inspection, delivering an industry\-deployable pathway for standards\-compliant maintenance decision support\.

## [Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI\-enabled phenotyping](../publications/7939c9a5f6e959b01fbf.md)

M\. Fares; N\. Al Kai; F\. Zahran; J\. Khalil; D\. Brunato; M\. C\. Allé; L\. J\. Boulos

Abstract Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes\. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises\. Using a multimodal, AI\-enabled approach combining clinical assessments, narrative coding, and large\-scale linguistic and emotional profiling of life stories, we show that mental health burden does not scale linearly with acute war or displacement\. Despite higher cumulative exposure, war\-time groups did not exhibit higher PTSD or depression than pre\-war participants, and resilience was lowest among non\-displaced individuals\. In contrast, narrative organization showed non\-linear reconfiguration: displacement was associated with enhanced temporal structuring but reduced global causal coherence, whereas acute war exposure without displacement amplified autobiographical reasoning and explicit self\-change\. AI\-based analyses further revealed emotional blunting rather than emotional overload, alongside increased linguistic complexity decoupled from symptom severity\. By enabling scalable analysis of life narratives, this approach isolates acute vs chronic effects and reveals sub\-clinical adaptations not captured by symptom measures alone, that can inform healthcare and policy in conflict\-affected regions\.

## [Trust Rhythm in Human and AI Collaboration for Digital Marketing in Nonprofit and Service Organizations](../publications/79413c3ce0e146e740f7.md)

Alina Anatolyevna Demydova

This paper builds a conceptual model that explains how artificial intelligence changes the temporal structure of trust in a brand and defines the threshold beyond which automation erodes trust instead of supporting it\. The study applies framework synthesis to peer\-reviewed literature published from 2018 onward, supplemented by four earlier works whose definitions and instruments later studies reuse\. Antecedents of trust are coded into four operational domains, namely transparency, authenticity, timeliness and human accountability, and converted into six propositions with explicit falsification conditions\. A simulation on synthetic parameters tests the internal consistency of the model\. Trust under machine mediation depends on three parameters of communication rhythm: frequency, amplitude and predictability\. Artificial intelligence raises frequency and predictability because it removes the dependence of regular communication on staff availability\. It lowers amplitude because content produced in volume without organizational substance carries no verifiable information\. The simulated trust index reaches an interior maximum, after which further automation pushes it below its unautomated level\. Disclosure of machine use is not the decisive variable\. The decisive variable is whether the audience can read human authorship behind the message\. The paper contributes a matrix for allocating marketing tasks between people and machines, indicators for monitoring communication rhythm, and a disclosure rule that reports the configuration of human control rather than the bare fact of technology use\. The model is theoretical, its evidence base is concentrated in commercial settings, and the nonprofit case is therefore a boundary condition awaiting longitudinal and experimental testing\.

## [Revisiting Inherited Metabolic Diseases \( IMDs \) Through the Lens of Selective Autophagy](../publications/795013aec578cb0d4403.md)

Marianna Maddaluno; Laura Cinque; Viviana Cetrangolo; Chiara De Leonibus

Selective autophagy is increasingly recognized as a fundamental quality\-control mechanism that complements bulk autophagy by enabling the targeted degradation of specific intracellular cargos, including mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum \(ER\), lipid droplets, glycogen, peroxisomes, ferritin, ribosomes, and protein aggregates\. Cargo selectivity is mediated by selective autophagy receptors \(SARs\), which link damaged or superfluous substrates to the autophagic machinery through LC3/GABARAP interactions, thereby coordinating cargo sequestration\. Recent studies have revealed substantial mechanistic differences between bulk and selective autophagy, highlighting the specialized signaling pathways, receptor networks, and transcriptional programs that regulate selective cargo clearance\. Dysregulation of these pathways has emerged as a key contributor to the pathogenesis of inherited metabolic diseases \(IMDs\), a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by defective metabolism and multisystem involvement\. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying major forms of selective autophagy, including mitophagy, pexophagy, glycophagy, lipophagy, ER\-phagy, and ferritinophagy\. It also discusses their relevance across IMD classes, such as mitochondrial disorders, lysosomal storage disorders, and peroxisomal diseases, among many others\. Furthermore, selective autophagy is highlighted as a potential therapeutic target, with modulation of autophagy receptors and signaling pathways offering promising strategies to restore cellular homeostasis and improve disease manifestations in IMDs\.

## [Integrated multi\-omics reveals plasma biomarkers of fatigue in HIV immunological non\-responders](../publications/795d7342ed22ce89030d.md)

Baixue Li; Xi Chen; Jibin Liu; Li Wen; Zhengnan Shen; Hang Zhou; Peijie Wu; Quansheng Feng

Objective To characterize the metabolic and inflammatory signatures distinguishing fatigued from non\-fatigued HIV immunological non\-responders \(INRs\) and to explore candidate biomarkers and potential mechanistic pathways underlying HIV\-associated fatigue\. Methods We performed untargeted metabolomics and cytokinomics on plasma obtained from 18 fatigued and 17 non\-fatigued HIV\-INRs\. Mechanistic insights were explored via Protein\-Protein Interaction \(PPI\) networks and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes \(KEGG\) enrichment analyses\. Results Compared to non\-fatigued controls, the fatigued cohort showed significant up\-regulation of 4\-ketopimelic acid, cholesterol, and 1\-hexadecyl\-sn\-glycero\-3\-phosphocholine, with concurrent down\-regulation of DL\-arginine and D\-pipecolic acid \(P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Immunologically, the fatigued group displayed elevated macrophage migration inhibitory factor \(MIF\) but reduced interferon\-induced protein 10 \(IP\-10/CXCL10\) and interleukin\-18 \(IL\-18\) levels \(P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Functional enrichment analysis suggested the involvement of necroptosis, lipid metabolism, and atherosclerosis signaling pathways\. Conclusion Fatigue in HIV\-INRs receiving long\-term antiretroviral therapy was associated with distinct lipidomic and cytokinomic alterations\. These results underscore the potential roles of dysregulated fatty acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and chronic low\-grade inflammation in the pathophysiology of fatigue\. Cholesterol and IL\-18 emerged as candidate biomarkers associated with HIV\-associated fatigue; however, their combined discriminatory performance was not statistically validated in this exploratory study and requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts\.

## [กรอบเขมทศการศกษาไทยสอนาคต: ความกาวหนาในวชาชพคร](../publications/7960b2ffdab60baa407e.md)

Panus Junsrithong; Anothai Teeratee; Pratakorn Kulsrithanaphat

This article aims to analyze the directions of educational development and professional advancement in the teaching profession by linking the concepts of Education 2030 and Education 2040 with the development of learner competencies, curriculum quality, and teacher professional development, based on a synthesis of relevant documents and the author’s perspectives\. Future education faces significant challenges arising from technological, economic, and social transformations, necessitating a shift in educational systems from traditional academic knowledge transmission toward the development of competencies and learner attributes aligned with the demands of the future world\. This approach emphasizes the cultivation of knowledge, skills, competencies, and values essential for enhancing learners’ quality of life\. However, limitations remain in practical implementation\. Consequently, emerging approaches increasingly highlight the pivotal role of teachers and instructional systems\. Learners must be developed as well\-rounded individuals equipped with essential competencies such as critical thinking, creativity, communication, and collaboration\. Learning in both real and virtual environments must be meaningfully integrated and balanced\. Curricula should therefore be designed to encompass self\-development, readiness for lifelong learning, and practical competencies\. Such developments directly influence teacher growth, which constitutes a crucial factor affecting student achievement\. Teachers are thus required to possess competencies in instructional management, technology integration, research, and innovation, as well as a deep understanding of individual learners\. Professional development for teachers should emphasize competency\-based career pathways, innovation creation, and collaborative learning to foster lifelong learning at their full potential\. Enhancing professional advancement in the teaching profession requires the establishment of competency\-based career progression systems that systematically link performance outcomes, student learning achievements, and educational innovation with transparent and sustainable evaluation and professional ranking systems\. Furthermore, promoting Professional Learning Communities \(PLCs\) is essential to enable teachers to engage in collaborative learning, knowledge exchange, and continuous self\-improvement, ultimately leading to career stability and advancement alongside the overall enhancement of educational quality\.

## [Non\-asymptotic oracle inequalities for the Lasso in high\-dimensional mixture of experts](../publications/796288c3a746d242606d.md)

TrungTin Nguyen; Hien D\. Nguyen; Faïcel Chamroukhi; Geoffrey John McLachlan

Abstract We study Lasso estimation for high\-dimensional softmax\-gated Gaussian mixture\-of\-experts \(SGMoE\) regression models, where the predictor dimension P may exceed the sample size N \. Under bounded parameters, we establish a non\-asymptotic Kullback–Leibler \(KL\) oracle inequality with an explicit sufficient regularization level and explicit dependence on N , P , response dimension Q , number of experts K , and boundedness constants\. We derive sparse well\-specified and approximation\-space rates, showing how deterministic SGMoE approximation error transfers into statistical KL\-risk bounds\. The theory extends to random covariates and, under misspecification, controls the best Gaussian SGMoE approximation in the candidate class\. Reproducible experiments validate KL decay and density recovery, compare Lasso with SCAD when $$P&gt;N$$ P &gt; N , evaluate model\-selection criteria, handle multivariate covariance structures, and assess high\-dimensional biological benchmarks relevant to heterogeneous genotype–phenotype mapping, omics\-to\-trait prediction, and AI\-enabled virtual\-cell modelling in systems biology\.

## [Promoting learners’ right to human dignity: perspectives of school management teams in two South African primary schools in the Ehlanzeni District](../publications/796e6e18eced56afa72c.md)

Ngwenya Lihle Tracia; Makhasane Sekitla Daniel; Mulaudzi Lebohang Victoria

Introduction Human dignity is a foundational constitutional value in South Africa and a core principle underpinning learners’ rights in education\. Despite constitutional and legislative protections, learners’ dignity continues to be undermined in schools through bullying, humiliation, discrimination, and punitive disciplinary practices\. This study explored how School Management Teams \(SMTs\) understand and promote learners’ right to human dignity in two South African primary schools\. Methods Guided by Human Rights Theory \(HRT\), the study adopted an interpretive qualitative case study design\. Data were generated through semi\-structured interviews and document analysis in two public primary schools in the Ehlanzeni District, Mpumalanga Province\. Eight SMT members, comprising principals, deputy heads, and departmental heads, were purposively selected\. The data were analysed thematically, including cross\-case attention to convergence and differences between the two schools\. Results The findings show that SMTs understood learners’ dignity in relation to respect, fairness, inclusion, and recognition of learners’ inherent worth\. Across both schools, dignity was promoted through awareness initiatives, ethical leadership, policy implementation, supportive discipline, anti\-bullying measures, and stakeholder collaboration\. Cross\-case analysis showed differences in emphasis: School 1 participants more often used explicit rights and anti\-bullying language, whereas School 2 participants more often foregrounded belonging, shared values, relational modelling, and home–school continuity\. These efforts were constrained by inconsistent educator practices, limited resources, weak parental involvement, cultural and linguistic differences, learner behavioural challenges, and broader community influences\. Discussion The study positions SMTs as institutional duty\-bearers who translate constitutional commitments to dignity into everyday school practice\. It contributes to scholarship on school leadership and human rights education by showing that dignity is not only a legal principle but also a leadership, governance, curricular, and relational practice\. The study recommends sustained human\-rights and dignity education for learners and staff, dignity\-focused staff development, clearer anti\-bullying mechanisms, restorative disciplinary procedures, and stronger home–school collaboration\.

## [ToPA: Block\-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine\-Tuning](../publications/7997af8a8701f52fdd29.md)

Sicong Li; Qianqian Xu; Zhiyong Yang; Zitai Wang; Longtao Huang; Xiaochun Cao; Qingming Huang

Parameter\-Efficient Fine\-Tuning \(PEFT\) has emerged as a prevalent strategy for adapting large pre\-trained models\. Among PEFT techniques, reparameterization\-based methods, particularly those that employ low\-rank or sparsity structures, have attracted significant attention\. However, these approaches often underperform full fine\-tuning\. Specifically, low\-rank methods constrain the update rank, which is misaligned with the inherently high\-rank nature of full fine\-tuning\. In contrast, sparsity\-based techniques limit the flexibility of the parameter space and compromise connectivity across weights\. To overcome these limitations, we explore the use of Toeplitz matrices, whose entries are constant along each diagonal, therefore providing a compact parameterization without imposing explicit rank or sparsity constraints\. A straightforward approach is to update weights via a product of Toeplitz matrices\. However, similar to RNNs, long multiplicative chains often lead to gradient instability\. To address this issue, we propose \\textbf\{ToPA\}, a more refined version of this idea that replaces standard Toeplitz matrices with block\-wise Toeplitz, greatly increasing each factor&\#x27;s capacity and shortening the chain, thereby stabilizing training and improving expressiveness\. We theoretically show that products of block\-wise Toeplitz matrices can approximate arbitrary matrices under shorter chain length, justifying the structural design of ToPA\. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ToPA offers greater expressivity than existing low\-rank and sparse parameterizations\. Empirical evaluations across 21 NLP and CV datasets, spanning 5 model architectures, consistently validate the effectiveness of ToPA\.

## [Tendências científicas e complicações associadas ao uso de esteróides anabolizantes: análise bibliométrica e temática da literatura indexada na PubMed entre 2015 a 2025](../publications/799b5a19e23275dda987.md)

Gabrieli Facina Rodrigues Costa; Maria Clara Sastre Lunhani; Nawan Sevidani Maluf Duarte; Tayná Kailaine Guterres; Gabriel de Moraes Borges

Os esteroides anabolizantes androgênicos \(EAA\) são compostos sintéticos derivados da testosterona, utilizados na prática clínica para condições específicas, mas que também são empregados de forma não terapêutica, com objetivos estéticos e de melhorar o desempenho físico\. A utilização indiscriminada dos EAA está relacionada a alterações em diferentes sistemas do organismo, incluindo complicações cardiovasculares, endócrinas, hepáticas, renais, neurológicas, psiquiátricas e dermatológicas\. Essas complicações podem ocorrer conforme a dose utilizada, o tempo de exposição, a combinação entre substâncias e as características individuais dos usuários\. Diante do crescimento do uso dessas substâncias e do aumento das pesquisas sobre seus efeitos, torna\-se importante compreender como a produção científica sobre o tema tem evoluído\. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar as tendências científicas e as complicações associadas ao uso de EAA por meio de uma análise bibliométrica e temática da literatura indexada na PubMed entre 2015 a 2025\. Buscou\-se identificar a evolução das publicações, os principais temas abordados, os padrões da produção científica e as complicações relacionadas ao uso dessas substâncias que apresentam maior destaque na literatura atual\.

## [Cross\-Domain Behavioural Mapping for IoT Attack Detection in Educational Networks Using CICIoT\-2023 Dataset](../publications/79aef14cfcd4ff5c2661.md)

P Basil Raja; L Arockiam; A Aloysius

Objectives: The study develops a cross\-domain behavioural intrusion\-detection framework for transferring attack knowledge from CICIoT\-2023 to a derived educational IoT representation\. Method: The proposed Cross\-Domain Behavioural Mapping Intrusion Detection System \(CDBM\-IDS\) integrates an Educational IoT Digital Twin Layer \(E\-DTL\), Behaviour Spectrum Encoder \(BSE\), Hierarchical Deviance Encoder \(HDE\), Tri\-Context Fusion \(TCF\), and Sector\-Transfer Consistency Loss \(STC\-Loss\)\. EduTwin is generated from CICIoT\-2023 through educational device\-role mapping, interaction modelling, and sector\-oriented behavioural transformation\. Findings: Under the controlled EduTwin evaluation protocol, CDBM\-IDS achieves 98\.72% accuracy, 98\.64% precision, 98\.51% recall, 98\.57% F1\-score, and 99\.21% AUC\-ROC\. Ablation analysis confirms measurable contributions from BSE, HDE, TCF, and STC\-Loss\. Novelty: The framework introduces educational role abstraction, frequency\-domain behavioural encoding, hierarchical deviation modelling, geometric context fusion, and consistency\-driven sector mapping\. Keywords: IoT security, educational network, intrusion detection, cross\-domain learning, behaviour modelling

## [A Descriptive Needs Analysis of Poetry\-Writing Teaching Materials for Grade X Vocational High School Students](../publications/79b53334ecd996ce82ab.md)

Fadia Nafa Yastia; Kastam Syamsi

Poetry writing is an important component of Indonesian language learning because it enables students to express ideas, experiences, emotions, imagination, and creativity through written language\. However, poetry\-writing instruction requires appropriate instructional support, particularly to help students generate ideas, select diction, organize poems, and apply figurative language\. This study aimed to analyze the needs for poetry\-writing teaching materials for Grade X vocational high school students\. A descriptive needs analysis examined four aspects: lesson planning, lesson implementation, students’ learning difficulties, and teachers’ efforts and expectations\. Data were collected using a questionnaire administered to Indonesian language teachers at the participating schools, and the responses were analyzed descriptively using percentages for each aspect\. The results showed that teachers required instructional support across all four aspects, with the strongest needs related to students’ learning difficulties and teachers’ efforts and expectations\. The findings indicate that prospective materials should provide structured guidance throughout the poetry\-writing process, including poetry examples, contextual stimuli, guided exercises, diction and figurative\-language activities, varied learning activities, and opportunities for revision and reflection\. These findings provide an empirical basis for developing poetry\-writing teaching materials that correspond to the instructional needs of Grade X vocational high school students\.

## [Infection\-related research in Parkinson’s disease: an exploratory trends analysis](../publications/79b73280477211ed20bf.md)

Xiang Li\-Qin; Yan\-Jun Chen; Sheng\-Qiang Zhou; Fang Liu

Background Infection and Parkinson&\#x27;s disease \(PD\) appear to interact through complex mechanisms\. Infection may promote the occurrence and progression of pathological processes related to PD, while PD and its associated dysfunctions may increase the risk of infection\. This study depicts the evolution, thematic structure, and emerging directions of infection\-related research in PD\. Methods Publications related to infection and PD from 1999 to June 30, 2026 were retrieved from the WoSCC and Scopus databases\. R software packages bibliometrix, CiteSpace, and VOSviewer were used for data analysis\. Results The number of published studies on PD and infection showed a gradual upward trend and increased significantly after 2020\. The United States published the largest number of documents \( n = 509\) and received the most citations \( n = 33,628\); China and the UK published 218 and 164 papers, respectively\. The University of Florida is the most productive institution \( n = 23\)\. Dr\. Rajesh Pahwa and Dr\. Michael S\. Okun are among the most productive authors \( n = 12\)\. Parkinsonism &amp; Related Disorders \( n = 59\) and Movement Disorders \( n = 46\) are the most active journals in this field\. The keyword analysis identified five main themes: infection exposure and clinical outcomes; infection\-induced neuroinflammation; shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration; virus\-related neurological manifestations and PD; and gut microbiota–gut–brain interactions involved in PD pathogenesis and treatment response\. Conclusion The research on infection and PD has developed rapidly, especially since the COVID\-19 epidemic\. This field is going beyond epidemiological association to explore how infection can trigger PD through neuroinflammation, α\-synuclein \(α\-syn\) pathology, the gut brain axis, and other factors\. Infection management in patients with PD has also become an important clinical concern\. This study reviews the development of this field, defines the emerging direction, and provides a reference for future mechanism research and clinical practice\.

## [Quantifying behavioral contributions to diabetes risk using an explainable multiclass machine learning framework with BRFSS 2024](../publications/79d8aaf70e5e76ca07ba.md)

Sumit Barua; Sohaib Jabran; Charles Rodgers; Alvis C\. M\. Fong

Abstract This study developed an explainable multiclass framework to evaluate discrimination among non\-diabetes, prediabetes, and diabetes using 2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data \( $$n=453\{,\}241$$ \)\. A dual\-feature\-set design compared behavioral/health\-status predictors alone with an expanded set including demographic and anthropometric variables across four classifiers\. Logistic Regression Model\-2 showed the strongest class\-balanced performance \(macro\-F1 = 0\.426; balanced accuracy = 0\.512\), while Decision Tree Model\-2 achieved the highest prediabetes recall \(0\.338\)\. XGBoost Model\-2 achieved the highest weighted F1\-score \(0\.775\) and macro ROC–AUC \(0\.765\), and showed better probability calibration than Logistic Regression, but failed to identify prediabetes in the held\-out test set\. SHAP analysis of XGBoost Model\-2 showed that demographic predictors accounted for 45\.21% of total diabetes\-class mean absolute attribution, behavioral/health\-status predictors for 42\.71%, and anthropometric predictors for 12\.08%\. Exploratory geographic SHAP aggregation showed variation in model\-attributed signals, but these patterns should not be interpreted as population\-level prevalence, comparative risk, or causal geographic effects\. Overall, the findings show that behavioral/health\-status information remained a substantial component of diabetes\-class model attribution after demographic and anthropometric predictors were included, while also highlighting the importance of class\-balanced and class\-specific evaluation in multiclass diabetes prediction\.

## [Multimodal imaging and clinical evolution of an optic nerve head granuloma with prominent overlying vessels in ocular sarcoidosis: a case report and literature review](../publications/79e720cc383e7907178e.md)

Jiahao Xiong; Jiyue Tan; Jun Xiao

Background Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disorder of unclear etiology, histopathologically characterized by noncaseating granulomas\. Ocular involvement is among the most common extrapulmonary manifestations, whereas optic nerve involvement occurs in fewer than 5% of cases\. Direct granulomatous infiltration of the optic nerve represents the rarest form of optic nerve involvement\. We report a rare case of a sarcoidosis\-associated optic nerve head granuloma with prominent overlying vessels and describe its multimodal imaging features, clinical course, and treatment response, with a review of the clinical spectrum of sarcoid optic nerve head granulomas reported in the English\-language literature\. Case presentation A 31\-year\-old woman presented with floaters in the left eye\. Best\-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes\. Fundus examination of the left eye revealed a white elevated optic nerve head lesion with fine tortuous surface vessels, accompanied by vitreous inflammatory haze, retinal periphlebitis, and candle\-wax drippings\. Fundus fluorescein angiography demonstrated early filling of lesion\-associated vessels with marked late leakage, and optical coherence tomography angiography detected abnormal flow signals corresponding to the lesion\. Additionally, chest computed tomography revealed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and transbronchial lung biopsy demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and no definite necrosis\. The overall findings supported the diagnosis of sarcoidosis\. The lesion initially progressed after the patient declined corticosteroid therapy, but gradually regressed following systemic corticosteroid treatment, with parallel disappearance of the lesion\-associated abnormal flow signals\. At the final follow\-up, the lesion had completely regressed, leaving only a thin gliotic membrane, while visual acuity remained 20/20 throughout the entire follow\-up\. Conclusion Although rare, sarcoid optic nerve head granuloma is a highly suggestive ocular manifestation that may be the presenting sign of systemic sarcoidosis and can mimic infectious or neoplastic optic disc mass lesions\. Multimodal imaging is valuable for early recognition, assessment of treatment response, and longitudinal monitoring\. Once the diagnosis is established, corticosteroid\-based systemic therapy may be considered\. In this case, systemic corticosteroid therapy was associated with anatomic regression of the optic nerve head granuloma, while visual acuity remained stable throughout follow\-up\.

## [A questionnaire\-based model to prioritize additional support during HIV testing encounters among men who have sex with men: temporal and geographic external validation](../publications/79eef73419988bb44b75.md)

Jian Zhao; Yazhou Yang; Ping Zhu; Shilin Zheng; Xiaowei Xu; Xiaoyi zhou

Background HIV sentinel surveillance collects behavioral and service\-use information from men who have sex with men \(MSM\), but these data are mainly used for routine reporting\. We assessed whether pre\-test questionnaire data could help prioritize testing encounters for optional additional support\. Methods We conducted a retrospective prediction modeling study using de\-identified MSM surveillance records\. Data from Nantong collected in 2020–2023 were used for model development, and records from 2024–2025 were used for temporal validation\. Surveillance records from an external city in Shandong Province were used for geographic external validation\. The final model was a calibrated stacked ensemble combining penalized logistic regression, random forest, and HistGradientBoosting\. We evaluated the complete modeling and calibration workflow using nested cross\-fitting\. Model selection, calibration, and threshold selection used development data only\. Results The development cohort included 1,585 encounters and 73 confirmed HIV\-positive events\. Temporal validation included 803 encounters and 29 confirmed HIV\-positive events, while geographic external validation included 1,622 encounters and 52 confirmed HIV\-positive events\. AUROC values were 0\.963 \(95% CI 0\.930–0\.990\) and 0\.974 \(95% CI 0\.955–0\.989\) in temporal and geographic validation, respectively\. The corresponding AUPRC values were 0\.696 \(95% CI 0\.536–0\.880\) and 0\.746 \(95% CI 0\.652–0\.842\)\. At the locked threshold, sensitivity was 75\.9 and 86\.5%\. Selecting the highest\-scoring 10% of encounters captured 86\.2 and 88\.5% of confirmed events\. Calibration slopes were 1\.530 and 1\.414, respectively\. The model overestimated overall risk in geographic validation\. Conclusion Pre\-test questionnaire data supported the ranking of HIV testing encounters in both temporal and geographic validation\. The model may help services plan optional counseling, prevention assessment, peer support, or follow\-up when service capacity is limited\. The scores should not be treated as exact individual probabilities\. They should not be used for HIV diagnosis or to restrict access to testing or other standard services\. Prospective evaluation and monitoring are needed before routine use\.

## [Secure reversible data hiding system in encrypted images for improving payload using efficient parametric binary tree labeling](../publications/79f11e52887c44b1f78e.md)

Cheng\-Ta Huang; Wai\-Long Cheang; Hao\-Yu Weng; Wei\-Jen Wang; Chi\-Yao Weng

Recently, an encoding technique called Parametric Binary Tree Labeling \(PBTL\) has attracted attention in the field of Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images \(RDHEI\)\. We observe that the classification strategies for non\-embeddable pixels within existing PBTL based methods remain sub optimal, leaving room for further improvement\. In order to mitigate these constraints, we develop a novel approach: Improved Efficient Parametric Binary Tree Labeling \(IEPBTL\)\. The proposed IEPBTL scheme distinguishes pixels into four independent classes: embeddable pixels, self\-recording pixels 1 and self\-recording pixels 2, and non\-embeddable pixels\. Compared with existing methods, IEPBTL significantly reduces the proportion of non\-embeddable pixels, thereby enhancing the overall embedding capacity\. The findings demonstrate that this refinement effectively curtails the volume of auxiliary data across most benchmarks, which directly contributes to a significant boost in the net payload rate\. Furthermore, most existing PBTL based RDHEI schemes adopt a global embedding strategy\. Such approaches often overlook the non\-uniform distribution of prediction errors in local image regions, thereby failing to fully exploit the available embedding capacity\. We overcome the drawbacks of global processing by introducing a preprocessing method that utilizes independent block\-based partitioning\. For each block, we compute the optimal parameters prior to the data embedding phase\. Extensive experimental evaluations confirm that the proposed approach effectively maximizes the embedding capacity while maintaining superior visual quality and reversibility\. An enhanced maximum embedding capacity is achieved by the introduced method, providing a significant gain over existing schemes when evaluated against standard test images\.

## [Artificial Intelligence‐Assisted Ultrasound for Sarcopenia Assessment: A Scoping Review](../publications/79f2137e153bb7a5ded9.md)

Weikang Jiang; Jianguo Sheng; Wanqiong Zhou; Yan Zhang; Ying Wang; Jing Wang; Wei Luan

ABSTRACT Background Muscle ultrasound offers a portable, non‐invasive, and cost‐effective option for sarcopenia assessment, but operator dependency limits its standardization\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) may help automate and improve ultrasound‐based muscle evaluation\. This scoping review aims to map the current landscape of AI‐assisted ultrasound for sarcopenia assessment, including research trends, methods, clinical uses and performance, and to suggest future work\. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the PRISMA‐ScR checklist, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ProQuest, CNKI, WanFang Data, Yiigle, VIP, and Sinomed up to July 25, 2026\. Two researchers independently selected studies and extracted data\. Results Thirty studies were included\. This field is developing rapidly, with 76\.7% of studies published in the last 3 years, primarily from Spain and China\. Model development and validation studies \(43\.3%\) were most common\. U‐Net and its variants were the predominant AI architectures, mainly for image segmentation\. B‐mode ultrasound with high‐frequency linear probes was frequently used\. The rectus femoris was the most assessed muscle for sarcopenia \(73\.3%\)\. AI‐integrated models for sarcopenia diagnosis achieved AUCs of 0\.640–0\.950\. Reported Dice coefficients for muscle segmentation ranged from 0\.73 to 0\.99\. In‐house datasets were used in 66\.7% of the studies, and global classification labels were the most frequent annotation strategy \(46\.7%\)\. Conclusions AI‐assisted ultrasound shows potential for objective and scalable sarcopenia assessment but remains early‐stage\. Operator dependency in image acquisition has not been fully resolved\. Further investigation should determine the added value of integrating multimodal imaging, combining diverse AI techniques, and evaluating multiple muscle groups\. Future efforts should deepen image‐processing strategies to extract clinically relevant features and facilitate standardized, scalable implementation in clinical practice\.

## [Untersuchungen zum Potenzial einer Trapezprofil‐CLT‐Verbunddecke](../publications/79f7b64b9c2ea57761a1.md)

Johannes Weber; Markus Kuhnhenne

Abstrakt Die zunehmende Bedeutung ressourcenschonender Bauweisen erfordert die Entwicklung leistungsfähiger Hybridtragwerke, welche z\. B\. die werkstoffspezifischen Vorteile von Holz und Stahl gezielt miteinander kombinieren\. In diesem Beitrag wird eine neuartige Stahltrapezprofil‐CLT‐Verbunddecke \(SCLT‐Decke\) vorgestellt, bei der eine Brettsperrholzplatte \(CLT\) mit einem kaltgeformten Stahltrapezprofil verbunden wird\. Während die CLT‐Platte die Druckkräfte aufnimmt, dient das Stahlprofil als Zuggurt und ermöglicht eine effiziente Ausnutzung beider Werkstoffe bei gleichzeitig reduziertem Holzbedarf\. Zur Entwicklung des Deckensystems wurden unterschiedliche Profilgeometrien und Konstruktionsdetails untersucht\. Die Kraftübertragung zwischen Stahl und Holz erfolgt über eine geklebte Verbundfuge\. Zur Validierung des Tragverhaltens wurden 6‐Punkt‐Biegeversuche sowie dynamische Untersuchungen zur Bestimmung der Eigenfrequenz durchgeführt\. Die Ergebnisse belegen eine hohe Verbundwirkung der geklebten Verbindung und bestätigen die hohe mechanische Beanspruchbarkeit des Systems hinsichtlich Tragfähigkeit und Gebrauchstauglichkeit\. Die vorgestellte SCLT‐Decke stellt damit in Kombination mit einer Abhanglösung ein vielversprechendes Deckensystem mit hohem Potenzial für diverse Anwendungsbereiche dar\.

## [Baseline Self\-Ratings and Functional Self\-Assessments Among Predominantly Female Participants in a 21\-Day Digital Corrective Exercise Programme: A Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/79fd2c686d8f2ac52c05.md)

Ana\-Marija Jagodić Rukavina; Luka Pongračić

Background: Brief digital exercise programmes are easy to access, yet relatively little is known about the people who enrol in them or the baseline assessments used to guide programme content\. This study described the lifestyle profile, self\-ratings, and functional self\-assessments of participants entering the PBS\+ “21\-Day Challenge”\. Methods: Baseline data were analysed for 2,442 self\-selected adults \(97\.7% women; mean age 50\.75 years\)\. The online assessment included seven ratings of present state \(NOW\) and personally attainable desired state \(POT\), together with six self\-administered functional tasks\. Missing values were not imputed\. Functional results are reported as both total\-sample and valid\-case percentages\. Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank Tests were used to describe paired NOW and POT responses, but the main emphasis was placed on the size of the descriptive POT–NOW gaps across domains\. Results: Nearly two thirds of participants reported low\-intensity physical activity, and 41\.2% spent at least six hours a day using a computer\. NOW ratings were the lowest for abdomen and stability \(M = 3\.08\) and posture and spine \(M = 3\.60\)\. The largest mean gaps were observed for abdomen and stability \(3\.15 points\), breathing \(2\.77\), and posture and spine \(2\.70\)\. As expected from the wording of the question, POT ratings were higher than NOW ratings for almost all participants\. Among valid functional responses, difficulties were common in deep abdominal activation, foot and ankle mobility, and the breathing task used in the programme\. Conclusion: At programme entry, participants reported the greatest room for improvement in abdominal stability, breathing, and posture\. Functional self\-assessments also indicated common difficulties in abdominal activation and foot and ankle mobility, together with mixed performance in the breathing task\. Because the measures were self\-reported and developed for this programme, the findings describe this cohort rather than clinical impairment or programme effectiveness\. Keywords: Digital exercise, functional self\-assessment, middle\-aged women, sedentary behaviour, trunk stability

## [EXPRESS: Valuation Bottlenecks: Why Isn’t a Better Business Enough for a Higher Market Capitalization?](../publications/7a02d824d2fb8081d655.md)

Shumpei Iwao; Vatsal Mitesh Tailor; Qi Wu

Firms often improve operations, disclosure, governance, or financing capacity without an immediate and proportional market\-capitalization response\. Could a single unresolved concern limit the market&\#x27;s response to improvements elsewhere in the firm? Classical multifactor and machine\-learning models ask which risks or characteristics explain or predict returns\. We ask whether the relatively weakest among several coexisting firm conditions receives disproportionate valuation weight\. We model equity value as the lower envelope of lens\-specific valuations\. A hard minimum makes one lens locally binding; a soft minimum assigns continuous, state\-dependent weights\. We use exploratory factor analysis on 268 accounting characteristics to construct five firm\-state lenses, with membership and weights determined by the loading structure rather than by an economic taxonomy, and rank each lens within industry, size, and quarter peers\. We document a weakest lens effect : beyond the additive effects of all five lens ranks, a firm&\#x27;s weakest lens carries an incremental association with next\-quarter returns, and it survives saturated joint rank\-quintile controls\. Gating the test at the bottom decile and then the bottom quintile of the peer distribution, the association is concentrated among firms whose weakest lens is weak against peers and not merely lowest within the firm\. In baseline soft\-min specifications, it fades steadily as the gate is widened\. We then investigate whether analyst attention may help explain this pattern\. We use large language models on 1\.7 million earnings\-call questions and find that, in baseline specifications, the weakest lens attracts a larger share of questions, especially when it is also weak among peers; this cross\-sectional alignment is consistent with an attention channel as one possible explanation for the observed return pattern\. The framework offers managers seeking to maximize market capitalization a new perspective on prioritizing scarce managerial attention\.

## [Interpretable Dynamic Graph Learning via Dual‐Granularity Large Language Model Alignment](../publications/7a034c6ddc553d1d59a6.md)

Yingjie Xie; Wenjun Wang; Tianpeng Li; Xiaoming Li; Lin Yuanbo Wu

ABSTRACT Dynamic graph‐level embedding aims to learn whole‐graph representations from temporal snapshots\. Existing methods predominantly follow a single‐vector paradigm that encodes each snapshot as a continuous latent vector, suffering from two key limitations: \(1\) Stage–Snapshot Entanglement, where within‐stage fluctuations and cross‐stage transitions are conflated without explicit granularity distinction; and \(2\) Implicit Structural Semantics, where meaningful structural properties remain buried in latent coordinates and are never exposed as interpretable, language‐compatible units\. To address these issues, we propose DyGLLM, an LLM‐compatible framework that constructs and aligns dual‐granularity structural representations for dynamic graph understanding\. Specifically, DyGLLM maps temporally coherent evolution regimes into selective structural tokens , providing explicit stage‐level anchors in the LLM token space\. It further constructs graph fingerprints to verbalize each snapshot&\#x27;s prototype deviation, temporal variation and topological profile into language‐readable structural descriptions\. A hybrid structure QA alignment mechanism with LoRA fine‐tuning is then introduced to align structural tokens and graph fingerprints with the LLM&\#x27;s representation space, enabling the model to interpret and reason over explicit structural contexts\. Extensive experiments on five dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate that DyGLLM achieves consistently competitive performance across graph similarity ranking, temporal anomaly detection and change point detection, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dual‐granularity structural representation\.

## [From landscapes to lesions: Pathology&\#x27;s role in wildlife mortality investigations and conservation health](../publications/7a19716d9b766871e2e4.md)

Nicole M\. Nemeth

Abstract To effectively recognize and manage wildlife mortality events, we need to understand who, what, why and how – who are the individual animals and species involved; what are the surrounding circumstances in time and space in which they are found; what are the causes and contributors to illness, injury and/or death; why is this happening in this time and place? And ultimately, how should we best surveil, mitigate and/or manage the event \(and perceived risks of similar future or related events\) based on potential population health threats\. Wildlife pathologists play a central role in this process, particularly in elucidating causes and contributors to mortality, a function that is increasingly critical to recognize as wildlife populations confront mounting and multifactorial challenges\.

## [Advancing waste\-derived feedstocks valorization and cleaner coal utilization: A critical review of co\-gasification synergistic mechanisms, process optimization, multiscale modeling, and prospects](../publications/7a1b88892ef3c1aa7fd5.md)

Shuyuan Zhang; Yunan Chen; 吴根记

Coal and waste\-derived feedstocks co\-gasification is a promising strategy for waste valorization and cleaner coal utilization by integrating the high energy density and process stability of coal with the high volatile content, reactivity, and inherent mineral catalytic components of waste\-derived feedstocks\. This review critically summarizes recent progress in coal and waste\-derived feedstocks co\-gasification, focusing on feedstock complementarity, synergistic mechanisms, key operating parameters, alkali and alkaline earth metals \(AAEM\) behavior, reactor type, and multiscale modeling approaches\. The analysis shows that co\-gasification performance is not a simple linear combination of individual feedstocks\. Both synergistic and inhibitory effects have been reported, indicating that synergy is a conditional phenomenon governed by feedstock composition, AAEM availability, K–Si–Al interactions, Ca competitive reactions, temperature, gasifying agent, blending ratio, and reactor type\. In particular, total AAEM content alone is insufficient to predict gasification behavior\. The speciation, mobility, and accessibility of K, Na, and Ca, as well as their interactions with Si and Al, determine whether AAEM promote char gasification or become deactivated through stable silicate and aluminosilicate formation\. Therefore, K/Si, K/Al, and Ca/\(Si \+ Al\) ratios can serve as useful indicators for interpreting the transition from catalytic promotion to mineral\-induced inhibition, but they should not be regarded as universal thresholds\. This review also discusses the applicability of thermodynamic, kinetic, machine learning, and numerical simulation to different research objectives\. Future research should emphasize standardized and dynamic synergy evaluation, controlled validation of mineral threshold hypotheses, direct characterization of AAEM migration and deactivation, mechanism\-informed catalyst/additive design, and integrated mechanism–model–system frameworks to support scale\-up and industrial application\.

## [User Experience in Board Games: An Agentive Semiotic Evaluation in Higher Education Settings](../publications/7a1fa52ae3d27275a93e.md)

Paola Andrea Castillo Beltrán; David Sebastián Baldeón Padilla; Jimmy Gilberto Dávila Vélez; Adrián Patricio Beltrán Montalvo

Play has emerged as a valuable pedagogical strategy in higher education, offering experiential and situated learning opportunities that integrate knowledge, skills, and attitudes\. Within this context, analog board games are gaining renewed attention as tools that foster strategic thinking, collaboration, and emotional engagement\. This study explores educational board games not merely as content carriers, but as intentionally designed artifacts that shape meaningful learning experiences\. The research examines two Colombian games with distinct design paradigms: Guanga: Textiles Andinos \(cultural\-symbolic\) and Construyendo la Autopista \(technical\-procedural\)\. Adopting a mixed\-methods approach, the study combines designer interviews, artifact analysis, and gameplay observation with biometric data \(facial expression analysis, eye tracking, and GSR\) and standardized questionnaires \(MEEGA\+\)\. The originality of this research lies in the application of agentive semiotics to board game analysis, a perspective rarely explored in Game\-Based Learning\. Instead of viewing players as passive decoders of signs, this framework analyzes how design decisions create conditions for agency, action, and sense\-making\. Findings reveal that while Guanga fosters a reflective agency characterized by creative tension and symbolic exploration, Autopista promotes a procedural agency defined by stability and operational execution\. This study contributes to game design research by proposing an experience\-centered methodology to evaluate how players activate and transform intended meanings through embodied interaction\.

## [The insufficiency of statistical analysis as security proof in image encryption: A comparative analysis with the IND\-CPA security model](../publications/7a1fd8931394ef9ddd8f.md)

Cemile İnce

The majority of studies in the field of image encryption attempt to prove the security of proposed encryption methods through statistical tests such as entropy, NPCR \(Number of Pixels Change Rate\), UACI \(Unified Average Changing Intensity\), correlation coefficient, and histogram analysis\. In this study, it is experimentally demonstrated that these statistical tests alone are insufficient to prove cryptographic security\. For this purpose, a logistic map\-based XOR encryption algorithm is implemented in two different configurations: System\-A \(deterministic, without IND\-CPA security\) and System\-B \(using a random initialization vector, designed to satisfy the structural precondition for IND\-CPA security\)\. Experiments conducted on five standard test images \(baboon, pepper, plane, splash, ship\) from the USC SIPI dataset reveal that both systems pass statistical tests with nearly identical values\. However, IND\-CPA security game analysis, evaluated over 1000 trials using three independent discrimination strategies \(pixel\-based L2 distance, structural similarity \(SSIM\), and a machine learning\-based discriminator\), proves that System\-A can be completely broken by a chosen\-plaintext attack \(adversary advantage = 1\.000\), while System\-B consistently yields low adversary advantage \(ranging from 0\.004 to 0\.076 across test images and discriminators\), statistically indistinguishable from random guessing and consistent with the operational conditions of IND\-CPA security\. The results clearly demonstrate that while statistical analyses are useful for evaluating the visual quality of encryption, cryptographic security can only be established through cryptanalysis methods\.

## [Higher Clostridia Expression Is Associated with Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitor Treatment in People Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus](../publications/7a2ba7e09c7adf5ff585.md)

Sebastian Tenorio Romero; E\. Sobczak; Jordan Drotsky; Emily Huang; Emily Wiebe

Human immunodeficiency virus \(HIV\) causes gut dysbiosis, exacerbating chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction\. Antiretroviral therapies \(ART\) reduce viral replication and slow disease progression, yet conventional antiretroviral drug classes can contribute to further dysregulation of the gut microbiota through polymerase– or protease–inhibition\. Integrase strand transfer inhibitors \(INSTIs\), a novel ART class, target HIV integrase, preventing viral DNA integration, potentially reducing side effects associated with other ART classes\. We analyzed a dataset by Taylor et al\. \(2020\) \(accession: PRJEB38909\) of 16S rRNA sequences from 488 fecal samples of people living with HIV \(PLWH\), to investigate the impact of INSTI on gut microbiome diversity and composition\. We observed significant differences in beta diversity associated with both HIV status and INSTI treatment, but no differences in alpha diversity\. Five core microbiome genera and three indicator species were identified in INSTI\+ individuals, both notably enriched in the Clostridia class\. Differential abundance analysis revealed specific genera within the Clostridia class significantly upregulated in INSTI\+ individuals\. Functional pathway analysis indicated downregulation of microbial pathways related to methanogenesis and archaeal lipid biosynthesis\. Machine learning models, k\-nearest neighbors and random forest moderately predicted INSTI status based on microbiome composition and host metadata, with the random forest demonstrating superior predictive performance\. Our findings highlight INSTIs&\#x27; nuanced effects on gut microbiome composition and functionality, suggesting potential clinical implications for alleviating HIV\-associated gut dysbiosis\. Given the complexity and combinatorial nature of ART regimens, further analysis should examine how INSTIs interact with specific ART drug classes to influence microbiome dynamics\.

## [Federated and Privacy\-Preserving Machine Learning: Methods and Trade\-offs](../publications/7a35e015d55c0489dee0.md)

Saritha E

Federated learning trains a shared model across many decentralized clients while keeping raw data on the device, which addresses data silos and tightening privacy regulation such as GDPR and HIPAA\. This paper reviews the methods and the practical trade\-offs of federated and privacy\-preserving machine learning\. The discussion begins with the FedAvg protocol and the distinction between cross\-device settings, with millions of intermittent participants, and cross\-silo settings, with a small set of reliable institutions\. Statistical heterogeneity, where client data is non\-IID, slows convergence and biases the global model; proximal correction in FedProx and control variates in SCAFFOLD reduce this client drift\. Because the uplink is often the bottleneck, the survey covers gradient compression, quantization, and sparsification that cut communication cost by an order of magnitude\. Sharing model updates is not by itself private: membership inference and gradient leakage attacks can recover sensitive information, so the paper examines differential privacy, secure aggregation, and homomorphic encryption as defenses, together with the accuracy cost each one carries\. Personalization methods that adapt the global model to local distributions are summarized, followed by applications in healthcare, mobile keyboards, and finance\. Illustrative experiments on a non\-IID benchmark show SCAFFOLD reaching a target accuracy in fewer rounds than FedAvg, and a differential\-privacy sweep quantifies the privacy\-utility curve\. The results are illustrative and do not describe a deployed production system\.

## [Influence of behavioral phenotype on the response of the rat body to cold stress in control and after hypoxic preconditioning](../publications/7a394ea341f6690190ee.md)

Арокина Надежда Константиновна; A\. V\. Belyakov; Dmitry G\. Semenov

Studying the cold resistance of homoiothermic organisms is important for identifying general physiological mechanisms, as well as for assessing individual phenotypic variations\. The aim of the work was to study the effect of the behavioral traits of Wistar rats, pre\-evaluated in Barnes maze task, on cardiorespiratory functions disorder during cooling\. Тhe behavioral testing reveals exploratory activity and working memory\. Two different psychotypes have been identified, one with increased impulsivity during learning \(No\.1 – “proactive”\) and the other with poor exploratory activity and reduced cognitive flexibility during retraining \(No\.2 – “reactive”\)\. Some rats of both psychotypes were subjected to a moderate hypobaric hypoxia \(three daily exposures at 360 mmHg, each lasting 2 hours\), the others served as a control\. On the fourth day after last behavioral trial, all rats were urethane anesthetized and cooled in water bath \(9\-10 °C\) until respiration stopped\. Frequency of breathing, heart rate and body temperature were recorded\. It was revealed that rats of psychotype No\.2 showed greater cold resistance and greater sensitivity to neuroprotective hypoxic preconditioning than psychotype No\.1\. Our results could be valuable not only for fundamental psychophysiology, but also for medicine dealing with dip cooling situations\.

## [La Escuela Frente al Cambio: Tecnología, Valores y Ciudadanía](../publications/7a3bbfc5f34327160a94.md)

Linda de las Mercedes Amancha Chiluisa; Rina Katherine Sánchez\-Reinoso; Ana del Rocío Martínez Yacelga; Liliana del Rocío Mena Hernández; Mayra Cristina Mena Mena; Veronica Lissette Mantilla Pazmiño

La transformación de la escuela contemporánea exige comprender los cambios sociales, tecnológicos, culturales y democráticos que están redefiniendo las formas de enseñar, aprender y convivir\. Este libro analiza ese proceso desde una perspectiva integradora, articulando la evolución de la institución escolar, la incorporación de tecnologías digitales e inteligencia artificial, la formación ética y socioemocional, la ciudadanía crítica y los desafíos asociados con la construcción de una educación pertinente para el futuro\. A lo largo de la obra se sostiene que la innovación educativa no depende únicamente de la incorporación de herramientas tecnológicas, sino de su integración pedagógica, ética e inclusiva, acompañada por docentes capaces de orientar el aprendizaje, comunidades corresponsables y estudiantes con pensamiento crítico, autonomía y compromiso social\. Desde esta perspectiva, se propone una visión de escuela humana, tecnológica y democrática, capaz de responder al cambio sin perder su función esencial de formar personas, fortalecer vínculos y contribuir a sociedades más justas, participativas y conscientes\.

## [NRF2: sensing stress, shaping immunity \- keeping inflammation quiet and antigens out of sight](../publications/7a433345033fa736f32b.md)

Yvonne Benatzy; Bernhard Brüne

The Cap ‘n’ Collar basic leucine zipper transcription factor NRF2 has been linked to inflammation almost since its identification as the master regulator of oxidative stress responses\. Early studies demonstrated systemic inflammation and dysregulated immune responses following NRF2 loss\. Initially, NRF2 was thought to regulate pro\-inflammatory genes primarily through its antioxidant function, by binding to antioxidant response elements\. However, studies by Kobayashi et al\. revealed that, in LPS\-treated murine macrophages, NRF2 binds to a non\-ARE sequence near the Il6 and Il1b genes, where it regulates RNA polymerase II recruitment and represses pro\-inflammatory gene transcription\. More recent findings have further expanded the role of NRF2 in regulating immune and inflammatory responses by demonstrating that NRF2 suppresses transcription of the MHC class II transactivator \( CIITA \), a master regulator of major histocompatibility complex class II expression and antigen presentation\. This article provides an overview of the historical evidence linking NRF2 to inflammatory conditions and discusses the emerging role of NRF2 in the transcriptional control of pro\-inflammatory cytokines and CIITA \. The molecular mechanisms through which NRF2 regulates Il6 , Il1b , and CIITA remain incompletely understood and may involve yet\-unidentified transcriptional co\-regulators, which will be explored in this review\.

## [Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo\-EM Inverse Problems](../publications/7a4cc0fcff7919dc0b30.md)

Nithin Chalapathi; Theo Sternlieb; Ethan Han; Sonya M\. Hanson; Pilar Cossio; Aditi S\. Krishnapriyan; Ritwik Gupta

Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three\-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy \(cryo\-EM\) is a powerful tool\. Cryo\-EM produces noisy two\-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded\. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction\. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems\. Since biologically meaningful differences may be spatially localized, we study self\-distillation with complementary global and masked patch objectives\. Because experimental dataset discrimination can reflect acquisition\-specific cues, we develop controlled synthetic and experimental evaluations and find that structural discrimination benefits from dense spatial features\. We introduce the EMber family of vision transformers, pre\-trained on &gt;50 million experimental particle images from 214 EMPIAR datasets together with simulated projections from 268,000 molecular assemblies\. EMber improves upon existing methods at conformational and compositional discrimination by 14\.85 and 14\.26 percentage points, estimates conformational populations to within 1\.59pp error with a linear probe, and produces particle assignments yielding reference\-quality reconstructions in fewer epochs\. We demonstrate how to learn representations that capture biological information for use across multiple cryo\-EM inverse problems\.

## [Artificial intelligence\-based prediction of postoperative voiding dysfunction following midurethral sling](../publications/7a4e726ce43182f5c838.md)

Melody Chang; Leila Magistrado; Bilal Kaaki

Purpose of review Midurethral sling \(MUS\) surgery is the standard procedure for stress urinary incontinence, offering favorable long\-term outcomes\. Despite its success, postoperative voiding dysfunction – manifesting as urinary retention, elevated post\-void residuals \(PVRs\), slow or weak stream, hesitancy, or the need for prolonged catheterization – remains a clinically significant complication that is difficult to predict using traditional risk stratification\. Conventional methods, including history, physical examination, PVR measurement, and selective urodynamics, provide limited individualized predictive power and fail to integrate the complex interplay of patient, anatomical, and surgical factors\. Recent findings Artificial intelligence and machine learning offer a promising approach to addressing this gap by analyzing multidimensional datasets to forecast individualized risk and guide perioperative management\. While artificial intelligence applications in pelvic floor surgery have demonstrated utility in predicting general surgical outcomes, validated models specifically targeting post\-MUS voiding dysfunction are lacking\. Development of such predictive tools will require high\-quality multicenter datasets, careful algorithm selection, and validation\. Summary Integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice has the potential to enhance preoperative counseling, support shared decision\-making, optimize surgical planning, and ultimately improve patient outcomes\. This perspective highlights the unmet need for predictive modeling of voiding dysfunction after MUS, outlines the promise of artificial intelligence, and emphasizes the importance of responsible implementation\.

While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood\. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation\. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling \(MKM\)\. The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate \(EC\), propylene carbonate \(PC\), dimethyl carbonate \(DMC\), and acetonitrile \(AN\) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI\. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride \(\) and fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates\. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species\. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth\.

Introduction: Posttraumatic stress and posttraumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\) are highly prevalent among Servicemembers and veterans\.
