However, a series of recent studies examined the efficacy of a service dog training program \(SDTP\) which demonstrated improvements in symptoms\. Methods: A privatized archival dataset of redacted transcripts was used\. The interviews were collected during a broader mixed methods study and maintained for a phenomenological, thematic analysis\. There were 119 transcripts from 84 of the original 117 participants who engaged in a SDTP between 2019\-2022\. After screening, 112 transcripts from 81 participants were included in this analysis\. Microsoft Excel and a closed artificial intelligence tool were used during the final thematic analysis\. Results: Participants were mostly white, male, Servicemembers or veterans between the ages of 18 and 65 years with symptoms or a diagnosis of PTSD\. ## [The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain\-of\-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls](../publications/7a893d000e51008c91e9.md)

Lucas Resck; Jingyi Sun; Qianli Wang; Isabelle Augenstein; Anna Korhonen

Chain\-of\-Thought \(CoT\) faithfulness matters for monitoring, explaining and safely deploying large language models, yet it has been studied mostly in English\. Languages differ in level, the amount of text available to learn from, so models know less in lower\-resource languages, which may change how much they rely on their reasoning\. To our knowledge, we are the first to relate CoT faithfulness to both resource level and task type \(knowledge\- or reasoning\-intensive\)\. On parallel multiple\-choice questions from Multilingual Massive Multitask Language Understanding \(MMMLU\) in eight languages, faithfulness rises as resource level falls on knowledge\-intensive tasks but not on reasoning\-intensive ones, a gap that points the same way across four models and several faithfulness measures\. We propose, and find support for, the Reliance Hypothesis: models rely more on their reasoning when they cannot recall the answer, as in lower\-resource languages on knowledge\-intensive tasks\. Model confidence partly explains the effect of resource level, but not the knowledge\-reasoning gap\. Languages in which models are less confident rely more on reasoning, yet less confident answers within a language do not, a Simpson&\#x27;s paradox\. In lower\-resource languages, models rely on their reasoning for more answers, not more strongly for each\. CoT monitoring may therefore be most informative in lower\-resource languages, where it is least often validated\.

## [Cloud Governance and Vendor Risk Management: A Case Study of Sri Lanka&\#x27;s NMRA Data Loss](../publications/7a93b3c67d09015314ad.md)

Sahan Samarathunga; Anjula Handapangoda; Shehan Suraweera; Theekshani Hettiarachci; K\. M\. Piyumal

Digital transformation improves operational efficiencies but poses several risks related to data sovereignty, vendor risk management \(VRM\), and information technology \(IT\) governance\. The research paper focuses on the data loss case at the National Medicines Regulatory Authority \(NMRA\) in Sri Lanka\. In this incident about two terabytes of pharmaceutical data became lost\. The data included proprietary information and manufacturing approval of drugs obtained from the e\-NMRA system in the Lanka Government Cloud\. This evaluation of the technical problem is carried out against various Governance, Risk, and Compliance \(GRC\) models, including ISO/IEC 27001 and COBIT 2019\. The analysis is also based on Heeks&\#x27; design\-reality gap \(DRG\) model, which allows us to establish the nature of deficiencies in sharing of responsibilities and disaster recovery plans within an institution\. All these mentioned GRC models offer manay solutions to address governance problems and security risks\. But, those GRC models operate assuming that organizations possess certain levels of institutional maturity and technical expertise\. Unfortunately, this assumption does not always hold true\. As a result, an empirical analysis of this case proves that there are serious problems with the management of data within government organizations in emerging digital economies\. Therefore, this paper suggests creating a new framework: Sovereign Cloud Governance and Vendor Risk Management Model more suited for countries in this stage\.

## [URL tabanlı zararlı web sitesi tespiti: Derin öğrenme ve makine öğrenimi yöntemleriyle bir yaklaşım](../publications/7a960e0e90977a5e4cfa.md)

Halil Kaya; Ali Çalhan; Murtaza Ci̇ci̇oğlu

Siber tehditler, artan çeşitlilik ve karmaşıklıkla kullanıcıları hedef alarak maddi ve manevi kayıplara yol açmaktadır\. Bu tehditlerin başında gelen zararlı bağlantılar \(URL \- Uniform Resource Loader\), kullanıcıların kişisel ve finansal bilgilerini ele geçirmeye yönelik en yaygın güvenlik ihlallerinden biridir\. Literatürde zararlı URL tespitinde genellikle web sitesi içerikleri, yönlendirmeler, görseller, meta veriler ve site trafiği gibi ek veri kaynakları kullanılırken, bu çalışmada URL&\#x27;nin yapısal özniteliklerine dayalı bir yöntem benimsenmiştir\. Yapay Sinir Ağları \(ANN\), Evrişimsel Sinir Ağları \(CNN\), Uzun Kısa Vadeli Bellek \(LSTM\), Kapılı Tekrarlayan Birim \(GRU\), CatBoost, XGBoost ve Destek Vektör Makineleri \(SVM\) modelleriyle karşılaştırmalı bir analiz yapılmıştır\. Çalışmanın önemli katkılarından biri, yalnızca URL analiziyle %98,88 doğruluk, %98,55 F2 skoru ve %98,21 AUC değeri elde edilmesidir; en iyi performansı CatBoost modeli göstermiştir\. Ayrıca alan adı yaşı özniteliğinin etkisi incelenmiş; bu öznitelik dahil edildiğinde doğruluk önemli ölçüde artarken \(%98,88\), çıkarıldığında belirgin bir düşüş gözlenmiştir \(%93,38\)\. Bu sonuç, alan adı yaşının önemli bir öznitelik olduğunu göstermekte ancak yeni oluşturulan alan adlarının yanlışlıkla zararlı olarak sınıflandırılması riskini de doğurmaktadır\. Sonuç olarak çalışma, yalnızca URL yapısal öznitelikleriyle yüksek doğruluk sağlayarak literatüre katkı sunmakta ve alan adı yaşının model performansı üzerindeki etkisini açıkça ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Makine öğrenmesi destekli ergiyik biriktirme modelleme eklemeli imalat ile üretilen PA6 kompozit parçaların mekanik ve mikroyapısal özelliklerinin incelenmesi](../publications/7aa7b08b31696420cbe7.md)

Ahmet Sefil; Koray Özsoy; Bekir Aksoy

Çalışmada karbon fiber takviyeli PA6 kompozit filament kullanılarak Ergiyik Biriktirme Modelleme \(EBM\) eklemeli imalat yöntemiyle üretilen numunelerin mekanik ve mikroyapısal özellikleri deneysel ve makine öğrenmesi destekli yaklaşımlar ile incelenmiştir\. Baskı hızı, doluluk oranı ve nozul sıcaklığı parametrelerinin etkilerini belirlemek amacıyla Taguchi L9 deney tasarımı uygulanmıştır\. ASTM standartlarına uygun olarak üretilen çekme ve eğme numunelerinin bir kısmına cam geçiş sıcaklığının üzerinde 120 °C’de 4 saat tavlama işlemi uygulanmış ve numuneler fırın içinde yavaş soğutulmuştur\. Mekanik test sonuçları, tavlama işleminin hem çekme hem de eğilme mukavemeti ile elastisite modülünü belirgin şekilde artırdığını göstermiştir\. Mikroyapı analizleri, tavlama sonrası katmanlar arası bağlanmanın iyileştiğini, mikro\-boşluk yoğunluğunun azaldığını ve daha kompakt bir matris yapısının oluştuğunu ortaya koymuştur\. ANOVA sonuçlarına göre, çekme ve eğilme dayanımı üzerinde en baskın parametrenin doluluk oranı olduğu belirlenmiştir\. Deneysel veriler kullanılarak oluşturulan veri seti üzerinde Destek Vektör Regresyonu, Aşırı Gradyan Güçlendirme, Karar Ağacı, Rastgele Orman ve Torbalama makine öğrenme algoritmaları ile mekanik dayanımlar tahmin edilmiş; özellikle Rastgele Orman modelin yüksek tahmin doğruluğu sağladığı görülmüştür\. Elde edilen bulgular, EBM yöntemi kullanılarak üretilen numunelerde kullanılan PA6 kompozitlerde uygun proses parametreleri ve tavlama işlemi kombinasyonunun mekanik performansı önemli ölçüde iyileştirdiğini ve makine öğrenmesi yöntemlerinin bu tür kompozitlerin performans öngörüsünde etkin bir araç olduğunu ortaya koymuştur\.

## [The memory that walks out the door: Generative AI and the knowledge depletion spiral in permacrisis](../publications/7ac229c91a8d753776b5.md)

Geshwaree Huzooree

Permacrisis leaves no interval to rebuild what each crisis removes\. Experienced people leave, and the judgment that crisis response depends upon goes with them, faster than handover and succession planning can replace it\. This knowledge depletion spiral compounds when the next crisis arrives before those losses are restored\. The institutional memory model interrupts it at three points, early spiral detection, crisis\-speed knowledge capture, and memory reintegration\. Generative AI makes each component feasible at the speed permacrisis demands, under consent and data\-handling commitments\. Run as a loop, the components let each crisis add to institutional memory rather than deplete it\. Boundary conditions identify where the model applies most directly and when leaders should adapt or defer it\. Cautionary notes address the mistakes that recur in implementation\.

## [Development of a Deep Learning Based Mathematics Module for Statistics Learning to Enhance Conceptual Understanding and Support SDG 4: Quality Education for Grade 10 Students](../publications/7aec6cf4beb3e83a3ca4.md)

E D R Fajri; Jasrial; Fetri Yeni J; Mutiara Felicita Amsal; Rayendra Rayendra

Improving students’ conceptual understanding of mathematics remains a challenge in Indonesian secondary education, particularly in statistics\. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a printed mathematics module that applies Indonesia’s pedagogical Deep Learning approach—mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning—to statistics for Grade 10 students\. The study used Research and Development with the Four\-D model: Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate\. The module was reviewed by material, media, and language experts and then tried out with six students and implemented with one mathematics teacher and 30 Grade 10 students at SMAN 2 Koto Baru\. Data were collected using validation and practicality questionnaires, observations, interviews, and pretest–posttest tests\. Expert assessment used a five\-point scale and produced mean scores of 4\.50 for content, 4\.60 for media, and 4\.25 for language, all categorized as very valid\. Teacher and student practicality means were 4\.76 and 4\.71, respectively, both categorized as very practical\. The mean pretest and posttest scores were 56\.40 and 82\.75, producing an N\-Gain of 0\.61 \(moderate\)\. The module therefore demonstrated high content and media validity, high practicality, and moderate learning improvement\. Its contribution lies in embedding the three Deep Learning principles across explanation, contextual activities, reflection, practice, and assessment\.

## [Diseño y validación preliminar de un chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias estudiantiles en la facultad de ciencias económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal, 2025](../publications/7aefa06bfd579a9dea28.md)

Raquel Leonor Atoche Wong; Jenny Ruiz\-Salazar; Cinthya Virginia Soto Hidalgo

El estudio tuvo como objetivo diseñar y validar preliminarmente un Chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para apoyar la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias de los estudiantes de la Facultad de Ciencias Económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal durante 2025\. La investigación se desarrolló desde un enfoque cualitativo, con alcance exploratorio y propositivo, mediante la metodología de investigación\-acción participativa\. La información se recopiló a través de un grupo focal con estudiantes, una entrevista semiestructurada al personal administrativo, observación de procesos, revisión documental, elaboración del mapa de experiencia del usuario y análisis FODA institucional\. Asimismo, se diseñó un prototipo funcional y se realizó una validación preliminar con usuarios\. Los resultados evidenciaron demoras en la atención de solicitudes, fragmentación de los canales de comunicación, limitada trazabilidad de los trámites, información institucional poco estandarizada y sobrecarga del personal administrativo\. El mapa de experiencia permitió identificar como momentos críticos la búsqueda de información, el inicio de los trámites, la espera de respuestas y el seguimiento de las solicitudes\. A partir de estos hallazgos, se estructuró un Chatbot con módulos destinados a consultas académicas, trámites administrativos, incidencias relacionadas con los sistemas institucionales y consulta del estado de los procedimientos\. La validación preliminar mostró una percepción favorable respecto de su utilidad, claridad y facilidad de navegación\. Se concluye que el Chatbot constituye una alternativa tecnológica viable para fortalecer la orientación estudiantil y contribuir a la digitalización de los servicios universitarios, siempre que su implementación incluya actualización permanente de contenidos, capacitación de los usuarios, integración con los procesos institucionales y mecanismos de seguimiento\.

## [Motivated Reasoning, Social Networking, and Perceived Alikeness of Political Issues](../publications/7af431e229f480806900.md)

Stephen Bok; James Shum; Maria Lee

Social media \(SM\) has become a major source of political information in the digital age\. Campaigns simplify political issues into short terms for public communication \(e\.g\., radical terrorism and violent extremism\)\. Differentiation is crucial to generating perceived value that motivates behavior\. However, the influx of negative political news over time has generated cynicism and partisanship\. Based on the motivated reasoning theory \(MRT\), citizens interpret information through a preconceived filter in the decision\-making process\. This lens translates into a belief that policy terms are approximately the same even though there are meaningful nuanced differences \(e\.g\., addressing income inequality and increasing the minimum wage\)\. Moderated mediation analysis evinced social networking interest \(SNI\) related to greater perceived alikeness \(PA\) of issues\. SNI related to greater rigidity \(mediator\)\. Rigidity related to greater PA of issues\. Intellect moderated the relationship between SNI and rigidity\. High SNI and high intellect dampened rigidity and thereby PA of issues\. Political marketing implications discuss how to appeal to voters that view issues similarly\.

## [La Brújula Humana Forjando un Futuro sin Desigualdad a Través del Conocimiento Inclusivo y la Colaboración Ética](../publications/7af8af56374288427acd.md)

Yosmel Silva Llanes

Este documento analiza cómo la humanidad puede avanzar hacia un futuro con menor desigualdad mediante una visión ética del conocimiento, la colaboración y el uso responsable de tecnologías emergentes como la Inteligencia Artificial\. Se explora el dinamismo del conocimiento humano, la importancia de la apertura intelectual, el valor de la diversidad en la inteligencia colectiva y el potencial latente de cada individuo\. También se examina cómo la división social destruye conocimiento y oportunidades, y se plantea la necesidad de una IA centrada en el bienestar humano\. El texto propone una “brújula humana” basada en inclusión, justicia y cooperación como guía para construir un futuro equitativo\.

## [Innovation Systems and Nano‐Macromolecular Translation: Market Structures, Behavioral Gaps, and Regional Asymmetries](../publications/7b0448698c2184048d95.md)

Mayank Punetha; Jainish Bhagat; Ankit Shah

ABSTRACT The commercialization of nanotechnology‐enabled macromolecular materials remains uneven despite strong scientific progress\. This study reconceptualizes commercialization as a system‐mediated stage of translation and comparatively analyzes the United States, the European Union, and India\. Using a systems‐oriented mixed‐methods design, the research integrates cross‐regional market‐structure data, firm‐level commercialization architectures, institutional configurations, and behavioral survey evidence\. Results reveal pronounced asymmetries in product scale, certification intensity, ecosystem dependence, and revenue logic, despite broadly comparable scientific capabilities\. Commercial activity converges toward structurally simpler morphologies, primarily nanoparticles and nanocomposites, and is dominated by business‐to‐business models, reflecting scale‐up and validation constraints\. Behavioral analysis identifies persistent awareness–confidence and confidence‐commitment gaps that limit consumer‐driven demand\. The findings demonstrate that commercialization outcomes are shaped less by intrinsic material performance and more by institutional alignment, validation infrastructure, and ecosystem maturity, positioning nanotechnology commercialization as a system‐conditioned process embedded within innovation architectures\.

## [A multimetric clustering approach for unbiased categorization of computer science journals: the framework proposed](../publications/7b07af587029adac89cd.md)

Abdul Hameed; Muhammad Omar; Rahat Hussain Bokhari; Han Woo Park

Purpose The rank of a journal is usually quantified by a single metric like Impact Factor \(IF\), CiteScore or SCImago Journal Rank \(SJR\)\. To avoid bias due to the use of a single metric, a multimetric\-based data\-centric unsupervised machine learning framework is proposed for journal categorization\. Design/methodology/approach This study integrates six bibliometric indicators as features to map the latent structure of journal impact\. The proposed framework incorporates two state\-of\-the\-art dimensionality reduction algorithms \(PCA and t\-SNE\), which also contribute to feature engineering\. Using PCA, the correlated metrics are transformed into reduced dimensions \(2D/3D\) that serve as input for k\-means clustering\. The optimal clusters \(k = 4\), aligned with IF, Scopus and SJR quartiles, are validated through internal and external evaluation measures\. Findings Multimetric\-based clustering of 4,146 computer science \(CS\) journals is compared with established single\-metric approaches \(SJR, IF and Scopus quartiles\) and with HJRS&\#x27;s proprietary multimetric approach, adopted in Pakistan\. The average metric\-based results provide interpretable outcomes against SJR, IF and Scopus quartiles \(single\-metric\) as well as HJRS \(multi\-metric\)\. The proposed journal categorization method is fully automated and offers improved classification of journals compared to well\-known traditional metrics\. Originality/value The contribution of this study is evident in the proposed framework for categorizing journals using multiple metrics\. The novelty of our work lies in the integration and domain\-specific adaptation of unsupervised machine learning to categorize CS journals\. ## [Digital application literacy as a mediator of GAI\-TPACK among non\-STEM teachers after year\-long professional development](../publications/7b0a62f7e6e268c09c3c.md)

Yi Min Dai; Zixin Ye; Marie Du; Xuesong Zhai

Generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) can produce and revise instructional content through probabilistic, conversational interaction, creating demands that extend beyond routine use of digital tools\. This study examined how digital technology knowledge and skills \(DL\-S\) and digital application literacy \(DL\-A\) relate to GAI\-integrated technological pedagogical content knowledge \(GAI\-TPACK\) among 224 Chinese primary and secondary teachers in general\-subject settings\. Participants completed a year\-long professional development program and a post\-intervention survey\. Structural equation modeling showed positive paths from DL\-S to DL\-A \(β = 0\.300\) and GAI\-TPACK \(β = 0\.317\), and from DL\-A to GAI\-TPACK \(β = 0\.453\)\. The indirect effect of DL\-S through DL\-A was 0\.137 \(95% bootstrap CI \[0\.069, 0\.219\]\), consistent with partial mediation\. The larger point estimate for DL\-A was not tested directly against the DL\-S coefficient and is therefore interpreted descriptively\. These findings position DL\-A as a plausible practice\-oriented mechanism linking foundational digital capability with subject\-specific GAI integration\. Because competence was self\-reported at one post\-intervention time point, the model does not establish causal development\. The study offers a bounded operational account of GAI\-TPACK for non\-STEM professional development and identifies priorities for multi\-wave and performance\-based research\.

## [Sep\-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning](../publications/7b14c2d9539beac17804.md)

Yinlong Xu; Jianfeng Huang; Zhengdong Zhou; Mingjie Lin; Fuyu Lv; Dan Ou; Hongxia Xu; Jian Wu

Large Language Models \(LLMs\) have demonstrated remarkable success in complex reasoning through explicit Chain\-of\-Thought \(CoT\), but the associated computational overhead and token verbosity remain significant barriers to efficiency\. While implicit reasoning in continuous latent spaces offers a promising alternative, existing methods like Coconut and CODI often rely on fixed\-length latent sequences and suffer from representational collapse\. In this paper, we propose Sep\-Latent, an adaptive implicit reasoning framework that utilizes separator tokens as structural semantic anchors\. By introducing an Attention\-Decay mechanism, we force the model to aggregate and compress reasoning logic into these anchors during training\. We then align explicit and implicit pathways through multi\-level distillation across all layers to ensure logical consistency\. Crucially, Sep\-Latent enables dynamic reasoning depth by adaptively terminating the latent thinking phase based on query complexity\. Experimental results on the GSM8k\-Aug benchmark show that Sep\-Latent achieves an accuracy of 56\.8\\% with an average of only 5\.4 tokens, significantly outperforming prior fixed\-length implicit models in efficiency while narrowing the performance gap with explicit CoT\. Further analysis via PCA and symbolic variant testing confirms that our method ensures semantic grounding and exhibits superior robustness to perturbations\.

## [Constructing the algorithmic gaze: viewer positioning in AI\-generated cinematic images](../publications/7b15a9962ad316685cc9.md)

Seda Aktaş

This study examines how cinematic gaze is reconstructed within generative artificial intelligence systems\. It argues that AI\-supported image generation processes do not merely produce visual content, but also establish algorithmic regimes of spectatorship that organize the viewer’s position within the scene\. To investigate this process, the same cinematic scene was regenerated through differently structured prompts using Midjourney V6, Leonardo AI, and Stable Diffusion based systems\. The research combines a practice\-based approach with comparative visual analysis\. The generated images were analysed through three main categories: viewer\-addressing gaze, viewer\-aligned gaze, and external observer positioning\. Particular attention was given to facial orientation, gaze direction, camera alignment, and spectator positioning\. The findings demonstrate that generative AI systems tend to privilege frontal, highly readable, and viewer centred compositions\. The study also reveals that different platforms respond to identical prompts through distinct visual organizations, suggesting that image generation is shaped not only by user input but also by model\-specific aesthetic tendencies and learned visual biases\. In several cases, the systems maintained dominant visual patterns even when prompts explicitly attempted to redirect spectator positioning, indicating forms of prompt resistance and algorithmic preference\. The article argues that AI generated imagery should be understood not simply as aesthetic output, but as a post\-cinematic visual regime that reorganizes perception, spectatorship, and visual orientation through algorithmic processes\. By bringing together film theory, digital visual culture, and generative AI studies, the study aims to establish a theoretical bridge between cinematic gaze and algorithmic visuality\.\.

## [Mapping Digital Transformation, Innovation and Sustainability in European Union Countries](../publications/7b2904416a8547d19e42.md)

Dilek VEYSİKARANİ

Digital transformation, innovation and sustainability are important factors for the competitiveness and long\-term development performance of a country\. This study aims to compare the digital transformation, innovation and sustainability performance of the European Union countries and to reveal their similarities and differences\. The Knowledge, Technology and Future Readiness dimensions of the IMD World Digital Competitiveness Index were used to represent digital transformation\. For innovation, the Global Innovation Index was used and for sustainability, respectively, the SDG Index, Spillover indicator and Environmental Performance Index\. The first analysis was made by the Multidimensional Scaling method and the structure obtained was tested for accuracy by the hierarchical clustering and the K\-Means analysis\. The findings reveal that the European Union countries are divided into three clusters for digital transformation, innovation and sustainability\. The analysis results show a strong relationship between digital competitiveness and innovation performance while sustainability indicators show more limited differences between countries\. It was also found that Northern and Western European countries have a similar and high performance in terms of digital transformation and innovation, and Eastern and Southern European countries have a relatively low performance\.

## [Beyond the Species Boundary: The Judicial Evolution, Adversarial Arguments and State of the Art of Non\-Human Personhood](../publications/7b4f12efb856a76cf55a.md)

Fernando José Sadio\-Ramos

The traditional divide separating Homo sapiens from other animal species has historically relied on a Cartesian and Roman Law dualism that classifies non\-human animals as property \(&quot;things&quot;\)\. This essay analyzes the paradigm shift from viewing animals as objects to recognizing them as subjects of rights and non\-human persons\. Grounded in the ethical frameworks of sentience and the &quot;subject\-of\-a\-life&quot; concept, this work evaluates the historical impact of the Great Ape Project \(GAP\) and the civil law transition from property status to sentient beings\. Expanding upon these foundations, this study incorporates strategic litigation efforts, such as the habeas corpus petitions led for chimpanzees and elephants, alongside contrasting case studies like the top\-down judicial recognition of the orangutan Sandra in Argentina and the bottom\-up empirical communication demonstrated by the gorilla Koko\. The debate encompasses robust opposition arguments centered on the lack of reciprocal legal duties, contrasted with progressive jurisprudential views advocating for dynamic legal personhood\.

## [Implications and Inferences: On the Organised Irresponsibility of Generative Artificial Intelligence](../publications/7b59faa7306b88128afb.md)

Jack Stilgoe

We are told we are living in the “Age of AI\.” As social scientists, we are often expected to explore and explain the implications of this new technology\. In this article, based on a pair of recent lectures, I argue that, rather than focussing on what the technology implies, we should instead study what it infers\. We need to take our sociological tools upstream, to understand how generative AI technologies are being constituted\. Those of us working with terms such as “responsible AI” and “responsible innovation” should first consider how irresponsibility is organised as part of the emerging politics of AI\.

## [RoleQ: Role\-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary](../publications/7b5a6b979b0f2bcc2883.md)

Johannes Knittel; Alec Helbling; Hanspeter Pfister

Weight quantization below four bits shrinks memory and bandwidth at a perplexity that looks acceptable, but often at the cost of factual knowledge and task accuracy\. Ternary weights have mostly been obtained by training from scratch or long fine\-tuning\. We introduce RoleQ, a quantization framework that places scales by the functional roles of Transformer units rather than by the layout of the weight matrix, as conventional formats do\. Vectors that read from the residual stream take one scale per output unit; those that write to it, one per input unit\. The rule is structural, needs no search, calibration or stored state, and holds on integer and ternary grids\. In a rotated basis it matches a per\-layer axis search at half the solver work, and at ternary it cuts perplexity by up to half against layout\-based placement in two families at every size from 0\.6B to 14B, where per\-row scales leave MMLU at chance\. Our lightweight post\-training pipeline converts an existing checkpoint to 1\.59 bits per weight in a few GPU\-hours, a fraction of the cost of learned ternarization, and leads every post\-training ternary method at matched or lower memory\-resident bits on perplexity, zero\-shot accuracy and MMLU, most widely on knowledge\. A sparse second ternary plane placed by a per\-unit Fisher saliency keeps the matmul multiplication\-free and recovers what ternary loses first: at 8B, a fraction of a bit returns about half the MMLU that conversion costs, well ahead of random or Hessian\-based placement at equal bits\.

## [Improving talent management practices in the organization by the tool of competency\-based HR functions](../publications/7b5d13b8d74d85a8c2b5.md)

Purvi Avantilal Chavla; Priti Nigam

Purpose Organizations invest in competency frameworks and talent programmes, yet the two are mostly run and studied apart\. This paper closes that gap\. It tests a single model showing how competency\-based HR functions \(recruitment, training and development, performance appraisal, career development and succession planning\) work together to turn employee competencies into lasting talent\. Design/methodology/approach Primary data were collected from 546 employees across four manufacturing industries in Gujarat, India: Agro and Food Processing, Oil and Gas, Pharmaceuticals and Biotechnology and Chemical and Petrochemical\. Responses were recorded on a five\-point Likert scale\. PLS\-SEM was used to test the measurement and structural models, while Importance\-Performance Map Analysis \(IPMA\) showed where action matters most\. Findings Competencies and competency\-based applications significantly shaped Competency\-Based HR Functions \(ß = 0\.432, R2 = 0\.542\), which in turn significantly predicted Talent Development \(ß = 0\.641, R2 = 0\.411\)\. The message is clear: competency\-based HR delivers results when its functions work as one connected system, not as isolated routines\. IPMA placed competency\-based HR functions high on both importance and performance, while talent retention stood out as the clearest gap\. Practical implications Manufacturing firms should use competency information across the employee lifecycle, build career paths around competencies and strengthen retention through open, participative competency assessment\. Originality/value Grounded in the resource\-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, the study repositions competency management as a capability\-building engine rather than a personnel routine\. It offers rare empirical evidence from emerging\-economy manufacturing, giving HR scholars, managers and policymakers a tested route from competencies to talent\.

## [Partial\-Revelation Panel Forecasting: Predictive Information Gain, Allocation, and Coarsening\-Consistent Operators](../publications/7b6575b537ab2103d95c.md)

Bin Wen; Dai\-Qiao Zhang; Tien\-Ping Tan

We study partial\-revelation panel forecasting: given $k$ of $n$ annotator votes on the previous dialogue turn, predict the full count distribution of the next turn&\#x27;s panel\. This cross\-turn predictive information differs from same\-item annotation value\. Under any nested revelation mechanism, the population decrement satisfies $V\(k\)\-V\(k\+1\)=I\(Y;R\_\{k\+1\}\\mid X\_k\)$; a fitted model also contributes adjacent excess\-risk differences\. Coarsened\-completely\-at\-random \(CCAR\) masking supplies the exchangeable random\-rater interpretation used in our operators\. We define coarsening\-consistent panel operators with a closed\-form Dirichlet\-multinomial realization, learned completion, and rater\-count transfer\. Against per\-level lookup, cold\-start count negative log\-likelihood differences are \-0\.422/\-0\.166/\-0\.014 nats on IEMOCAP/M3ED/EmoWOZ\. A held\-out rater experiment measures same\-item value: first and second additional votes reduce NLL by 0\.583/0\.221, 0\.578/0\.184, and 0\.180/0\.069 nats, respectively\. Cross\-turn and same\-item gains are not interchangeable, and CCAR masks are controlled interventions rather than observed arrival processes\. Consistency is auditable but does not guarantee predictive improvement; per\-level marginalization can outperform a shared table\. Target\-free allocation beats uniform only where row\-level signal is predictable: at budget one it recovers 83\-\-93% of retrospective feature class headroom on IEMOCAP/M3ED but does not improve EmoWOZ\. Gains are modest and corpus\-dependent, with several small or null partial\-revelation differences\. Code and aggregate result artifacts accompany the preprint\.

## [Automated Data Preprocessing Using Parameterized SWRL Inference within a Local RAG Pipeline](../publications/7b689698ee0327ba0260.md)

Maria de los Ángeles Contreras Trujillo; Mayerli Rosario Quintuña Ramón; Claudia Tamara Serpa Flores; Marcia Patricia Ullauri Carrasco; Marcos Orellana

This work formalizes expert knowledge in data preprocessing through the Web Ontology Language \(OWL\) and parameterized Semantic Web Rule Language \(SWRL\) rules, integrated with a Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) pipeline for natural\-language queries\. An OWL ontology comprising 47 classes, 42 individuals, and 19 SWRL rules was designed in Protégé and validated on the Netflix Movies and TV Shows dataset \(8,807 records, 12 columns\)\. A Python\-implemented inference engine, which parses the SWRL rule structure from the RDF/XML serialization and evaluates antecedents through deterministic conditionals without invoking a native OWL DL reasoner, generated 15 preprocessing\-technique recommendations across 9 analyzable columns; the remaining 3 columns \(show\_id, title, description\) were excluded as identifiers and free\-text fields, respectively, for which tabular preprocessing is not applicable\. The system guides data scientists in selecting preprocessing techniques based on each column&\#x27;s statistical profile, reducing reliance on manual configuration\. The novelty lies in parameterizing SWRL rules using dynamically computed statistical metrics and multilingual semantic retrieval, within a fully local RAG pipeline that supports traceability and privacy\.

## [Experimental protocols used in tactile perception of materials: a mini review](../publications/7b6933bd411403ffefa3.md)

Simran A\. Sutavane; Subhash H\. Risbud

Tactile perception plays a central role in how humans evaluate and interact with materials, influencing perceived roughness, softness, friction, warmth, wetness, comfort, quality, and usability\. In recent years, experimental studies on tactile perception have expanded across diverse material systems, including textiles, synthetic fibers, plastics, wood, building materials, soft rubbers, textured surfaces, and haptic overlays\. However, the experimental protocols used across these studies remain highly varied\. This mini\-review examines recent experimental approaches adopted in tactile perception studies of materials, with emphasis on work published within approximately the last 5 years\. We identified common methodological strategies, including psychophysical rating scales, forced\-choice and pairwise\-comparison tasks, tactile\-only and visual–tactile testing, active\-touch standardization, instrumented material characterization, and multisensory or haptic\-interface protocols\. By comparing these approaches, the review highlights how differences in material selection, sensory access, exploratory movement, subjective rating methods, and physical characterization influence the interpretation of tactile perception data\. We also discuss key research gaps, including the need for standardized reporting, cross\-material benchmark datasets, diverse participant populations, improved control of touch behavior, and stronger links between tactile perception experiments and material\-design guidelines\.

## [Managing a Disputed Statistical Analysis Plan in an FDA Biologics License Application: An Allogeneic Cell Therapy Case Study in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/7b6b0a7c683c661d47e7.md)

Kaushik Barad; Peivand Pirouzi

Allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) illustrates a regulatory lesson that extends well beyond this single product category: in a disease area without a validated pharmacodynamic biomarker, the integrity of the prespecified statistical analysis plan can determine a regulatory outcome as decisively as the underlying biology does\. This article examines a representative case in which a sponsor&\#x27;s Biologics License Application for a mutation\-agnostic cell therapy, built on an immunomodulatory and antifibrotic mechanism rather than dystrophin restoration, produced materially different effect estimates depending on which statistical analysis plan was applied to the same pivotal trial data, prompting a Complete Response Letter and a subsequent advisory committee vote against approval\. The article develops the regulatory and statistical lessons this case offers, situates them against the field&\#x27;s existing mutation\-specific accelerated\-approval precedent, and proposes a real\-world evidence framework built specifically to prevent the analysis\-plan dispute from recurring post\-approval\. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals managing evidentiary strategy for mutation\-agnostic cell and gene therapies in rare pediatric disease\.Keywords: allogeneic cell therapy; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; statistical analysis plan; Biologics License Application; real\-world evidence; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Scale formation mechanism and green strategies for its prevention and control](../publications/7b6b8c645b7e3cd33ee8.md)

Ifeanyi F\. Udorji; Anthony Ikechukwu Obike; Jude Chibuzo Igwe; James Onyedikachi Nwagba; Chiemeziem Adanma Obike; Ahamefula A\. Ahuchaogu; Moses Macaulay

Scale formation is a common operational problem in aqueous, industrial and oilfield systems where dissolved mineral ions exceed their solubility limits and precipitate as solid deposits\. This manuscript reviews the mechanisms of scale formation, the factors influencing deposition, the major types of scale, and the approaches used for scale prevention, inhibition and removal\. Scale development generally occurs through supersaturation, nucleation, crystal growth, surface deposition and ageing\. Its formation is influenced by water hardness, temperature, pressure, pH, ionic strength, CO₂ partial pressure, fluid velocity and surface roughness\. The manuscript discusses several scale types, including calcium oxalate, calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, calcium sulfite, calcium phosphate, calcium aconitate, calcium citrate, silicate scale and sugar\-charcoal deposits\. These deposits may reduce heat\-transfer efficiency, restrict fluid movement, increase energy consumption, damage equipment and contribute to operational downtime\. Prevention and inhibition strategies include chemical inhibitors, mechanical techniques, operational adjustments and green inhibitors derived from natural or biodegradable sources\. Conventional inhibitors remain useful; however, environmental concerns have encouraged interest in plant extracts, natural polymers and other eco\-friendly alternatives\. The review also notes that green inhibitors may present practical challenges, including removal from systems after application\. Overall, the manuscript emphasises the need to connect scale\-formation mechanisms with safer and more effective inhibition strategies\.

## [The Optimal Ranking Tradeoffs Between Two Ranking Scores in Two\-Class Classification](../publications/7b75668a71a10cdf0aa4.md)

Sébastien Piérard; Adrien Deliège; Marc Van Droogenbroeck

The accuracy, true negative rate \(negative class recall\), true positive rate \(positive class recall\), negative predictive value \(negative class precision\), positive predictive value \(positive class precision\), class\-specific intersections over unions, class\-specific F\-scores, Cohen&\#x27;s kappa, and balanced accuracy are scores that one intuitively wants to maximize when developing machine learning methods\. However, they lead to different rankings of such methods\. So, how can we establish a ranking that is an optimal tradeoff between any pair of these scores? It turns out that all these scores are special cases of ranking scores: a continuum of scores parameterized by the relative importance values assigned to the true negative, false positive, false negative, and true positive outcomes\. Since all these scores are known to induce meaningful rankings, we seek the optimal tradeoffs among them\. We consider the tradeoff between two scores to be optimal when it minimizes the Fréchet variance regarding the Kendall distance \(also known as the bubble\-sort distance\) between rankings\. For any given set of classifiers to rank, the optimal tradeoff lies at the center of the shortest \(geodesic\) path on the manifold of all rankings induced by the ranking scores\. However, in the parameter space of the ranking scores, it is rarely achieved by averaging the importance values corresponding to the initial scores\. In this paper, we present an exact analytical solution for determining a ranking score that is an optimal tradeoff for any given pair of initial scores, in the common case where the class priors are the same for all compared performances\. We also experimentally investigate what happens when performance follows some distributions with fixed priors\.

## [Comparative study of thermoelectricity in cotton fabrics coated by immersion with Pyrograf® III carbon nanofibers\-based inks](../publications/7b78c4f871c290e1d9ef.md)

Antonio J\. Paleo; Jose Abreu; Beate Krause; Sergio González\-Casal; Louis Thomas; Maria F\. Cerqueira; Enrique Muñoz; Petra Pötschke

Herein, the thermoelectric \(TE\) properties of cotton woven fabrics \(CWFs\) modified by dip coating in aqueous inks made from two Pyrograf® III carbon nanofibers \(CNFs\), PR 24 LHT XT and PR 25 PS XT, are compared\. Transmission Electron Microscopy \(TEM\) and Raman spectroscopy analyses of CNFs reveal similar morphologies and structures, although PR 24 LHT XT have smaller diameters and higher grade of crystallinity than PR 25 PS XT\. Despite these differences, CWFs made from inks with them are quite similar in terms of their electrical conductivity \( σ \), Seebeck coefficient \( S \), and thermal conductivity \( k \)\. Although, overall, textiles produced using PR 24 are slightly superior to those obtained using the PR 25 PS XT CNFs, achieving σ of ∼35 S m −1 and negative Seebeck coefficients around −6 μVK −1 \. These values correspond to a Power Factor \(PF\) of ∼1 × 10 −3 μW mK \-1 , and a figure of merit \(zT\) of ∼6 × 10 −6 at 30 °C\. Notably, between 30 °C and 100 °C, the S of the conductive textiles \(CTs\) is slightly higher, in absolute terms, than that of the corresponding CNFs\. In addition, in this same temperature range, the CTs exhibit negative temperature coefficient \(NTC\) behavior, which according to the 3D variable range hopping \(VRH\) model, can be interpreted as resulting from the thermal activation of charge carriers capable of crossing several potential wells, and a simultaneous increase in their S \. All of these results are discussed in order to clarify the role played by these two types of Pyrograf® III CNFs on the TE properties of their conductive textiles\.

## [Real Time Release Testing \(RTRT\) In Pharmaceutical Industry: Analytical Technologies, Regulatory Landscapes and Future Perspective](../publications/7b81ef87b8dfc985781c.md)

Narendra Laxmi; Dhara Patel; Patel Grishma; Meshram Dhananjay

Real\-Time Release Testing \(RTRT\) is an advanced pharmaceutical quality\-assurance approach that enables product quality to be evaluated using real\-time process data, in\-process measurements, and validated analytical technologies\. Unlike conventional end\-product testing, RTRT focuses on building quality into the manufacturing process through continuous monitoring and control\. The integration of Process Analytical Technology \(PAT\), Quality by Design \(QbD\), multivariate data analysis, automation, and advanced analytical techniques facilitates improved understanding and control of critical material attributes and critical process parameters\. This review discusses the principles, implementation strategies, pharmaceutical applications, advantages, challenges, and regulatory aspects of RTRT\. The major benefits include reduced testing time, faster batch disposition, improved process understanding, reduced product waste, enhanced manufacturing efficiency, and consistent product quality\. However, implementation can be challenging due to high initial investment, instrument calibration and validation requirements, data integrity and cyber security concerns, skilled workforce requirements, regulatory expectations, and integration with legacy manufacturing systems\. Regulatory frameworks from organizations such as the US Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\), European Medicines Agency \(EMA\), and International Council for Harmonisation \(ICH\) provide a scientific and risk\-based foundation for implementing RTRT\. Future developments involving Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Machine Learning \(ML\), Digital Twins, Internet of Things \(IoT\), Big Data Analytics, and Industry 4\.0 are expected to further enhance real\-time quality monitoring and predictive manufacturing\. RTRT therefore offers significant potential to modernize pharmaceutical manufacturing by enabling efficient, science\-based, and continuous assurance of product quality\.

## [Sistem Pakar Deteksi Dini Risiko Putus Sekolah pada Siswa SMK Menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor](../publications/7b8d3e727506eea69588.md)

Amanda Meisyah Putri; Irvan

Putus sekolah pada jenjang Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan \(SMK\) merupakan persoalan pendidikan multidimensional yang dipengaruhi oleh faktor akademik, ekonomi, dan sosial secara bersamaan, sementara identifikasi risiko yang masih dilakukan secara manual oleh guru Bimbingan dan Konseling \(BK\) cenderung subjektif dan sulit dilakukan secara menyeluruh karena keterbatasan jumlah guru BK dibandingkan jumlah siswa yang harus dipantau\. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan membangun sistem pakar berbasis web untuk mendeteksi dini risiko putus sekolah pada siswa SMK Muhammadiyah 9 Medan menggunakan metode Certainty Factor \(CF\), yang mengakomodasi ketidakpastian pengetahuan pakar melalui nilai Measure of Belief \(MB\) dan Measure of Disbelief \(MD\)\. Basis pengetahuan sistem disusun melalui wawancara dan validasi bersama guru BK sehingga diperoleh dua belas gejala risiko beserta nilai CF pakar, yang kemudian diproses menggunakan mekanisme inferensi forward chaining dan rumus CF Combine untuk menghasilkan tingkat keyakinan akhir terhadap tiga kategori risiko, yaitu rendah, sedang, dan tinggi\. Sistem bernama SIPRIS \(Sistem Informasi Prediksi Risiko Siswa\) ini dikembangkan menggunakan PHP, basis data MySQL, dan antarmuka berbasis Bootstrap 5\. Pengujian black\-box terhadap enam modul utama menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan, sedangkan validasi manual pada tiga data uji siswa menunjukkan kesesuaian penuh antara hasil sistem dan perhitungan pakar \(Risiko Tinggi 85%, Risiko Sedang 65%, Risiko Rendah 35%\)\. Pengujian confusion matrix pada 158 data siswa menghasilkan akurasi 100%, meskipun data uji masih didominasi kategori risiko rendah sehingga evaluasi pada kategori sedang dan tinggi masih terbatas dan perlu diperluas pada penelitian lanjutan\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar berbasis Certainty Factor dapat membantu pihak sekolah melakukan identifikasi dini risiko putus sekolah secara lebih sistematis, objektif, dan terukur\.

## [Cellular origins and evolutionary dynamics of plasma cfDNA in solid tumors: integrating germline, tumor\-derived, and hematopoietic variation for MRD and treatment guidance](../publications/7b9b12daff79ae381c56.md)

Quanneng Zhao; Chunlei Wu; Xiao Huang; Miyuan Yang; Bing Zhang

Plasma cell\-free DNA \(cfDNA\) is a heterogeneous and rapidly changing biological pool derived from malignant cells, normal tissues, and hematopoietic cells\. The abundance and molecular composition of circulating tumor DNA \(ctDNA\) are determined not only by tumor burden but also by tissue architecture, vascular access, cell\-death programs, chromatin organization, nuclease processing, systemic clearance, treatment exposure, and clonal evolution\. These biological determinants shape the mutation, methylation, fragmentation, nucleosomal, and temporal features exploited by contemporary liquid\-biopsy assays\. Accurate clinical interpretation therefore requires both sensitive detection and reliable source attribution, particularly the distinction of tumor\-derived variants from constitutional germline alterations and clonal hematopoiesis\. In this review, we integrate the biological origins and processing of plasma cfDNA with analytical strategies for low\-tumor\-fraction detection and critically evaluate the evidence supporting postoperative molecular residual disease \(MRD\), recurrence surveillance, treatment\-response assessment, resistance monitoring, and ctDNA\-guided therapy across solid tumors\. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing prognostic validity, treatment\-predictive value, and demonstrated clinical utility\. Current evidence is strongest in colorectal cancer and, more recently, ctDNA\-selected urothelial cancer, whereas routine ctDNA\-directed intervention in resected non\-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer remains insufficiently validated\. By linking cfDNA biology to an explicit hierarchy of clinical evidence, this review defines both the established applications and the major limitations that must be addressed before broader implementation of ctDNA\-guided precision oncology\.

## [Predicting Wetland Nitrogen Levels Through Microbial Signatures: A Taxonomy\-Based Approach Validated by Machine Learning](../publications/7ba69b959b083064af3c.md)

Nadia Arjomandi; Yasmin Faghir; Ingrid Wang; Michelle Benitez\-Muller; Ava Tiefenbach

Wetland ecosystems harbour diverse microbial communities that play a key role in regulating biogeochemical cycles, yet their potential to predict abiotic soil conditions remains underexplored\. This study investigates whether microbial community composition can be used to infer environmental conditions, focusing on five abiotic factors: pH, calcium, total carbon, respiration, and total nitrogen\. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data processed in QIIME2, total nitrogen emerged as the only abiotic factor significantly associated with microbial alpha and beta diversity\. Low\-nitrogen wetlands exhibited greater microbial richness and evenness, while high\-nitrogen soils were dominated by fewer, specialized taxa\. Core microbiome and indicator species analyses identified eight indicator species that were uniquely linked to either high\- or low\-nitrogen conditions, reflecting distinct microbial signatures tied to nitrogen availability\. These indicator species were used to train a Random Forest model that classified nitrogen levels with high levels of accuracy\. Overall, microbial signatures proved to be reliable bioindicators of nitrogen conditions, and this machine learning\-driven, taxonomy\-based framework offers practical applications in ecological monitoring, precision agriculture, and sustainable land management\.

## [Bridging herb and needle: shared hepatoprotective mechanisms of saikosaponins and acupuncture and the rationale for combined therapy](../publications/7badfafa14d1e4da0c2c.md)

Yu Xu; Lujun Tang; Min Lai; Yanmei Yang; Lu Zhang; Xiaoting Tian

Liver disease remains a major global health burden, and treatments that directly reverse established fibrosis remain limited and indication\-specific\. Radix Bupleuri was selected for this review because it is widely used in traditional East Asian liver\-directed formulas and because its principal triterpenoid constituents, saikosaponins, have a substantial but predominantly preclinical hepatology literature\. This review critically synthesizes saikosaponin evidence across chemical, immune\-mediated, alcohol\-related, cholestatic, fibrotic, and metabolic injury, emphasizing congener\-specific actions, experimental\-model limitations, poor bioavailability, dose\-dependent hepatotoxicity, and potential cytochrome\-mediated interactions\. We separately appraise manual acupuncture, electroacupuncture, moxibustion, and acupoint catgut embedding\. Human evidence is strongest for metabolic liver disease and is concentrated in electroacupuncture and embedding studies; evidence for fibrosis and cirrhosis is weaker, while most mechanistic data derive from electroacupuncture or moxibustion in rodents\. The two evidence streams show partial functional overlap in fibrogenic cell state and matrix turnover, redox control, innate\-inflammatory signaling, and metabolic\-autophagic regulation\. This overlap is asymmetric: vagus\-dependent hepatic Nrf2 activation is supported for electroacupuncture, whereas direct evidence for canonical hepatic Nrf2 activation by saikosaponins remains limited\. Gut microbiota, bile\-acid metabolism, intestinal\-barrier integrity, and gut\-brain signaling form an additional systems\-level interface, but their causal role in a combined intervention is untested\. No direct co\-administration study was identified\. The proposed combination should therefore be treated as a falsifiable research hypothesis, not as demonstrated synergy or an established therapy\.

## [Digital Transformation of Nigerian Construction Industry Through BIM, AI, Digital Twins, IoT and Data Analytics](../publications/7bb0a822f2d257cfcf6d.md)

This study assessed the digital transformation of construction processes with a view to developing an integrated framework for enhancing project performance in Abia State, Nigeria\. The study was motivated by persistent time and cost overruns, poor quality, and fragmented paper\-based processes in Nigeria’s SME\-dominated construction industry, coupled with acute last\-mile logistics challenges in Umuahia and Aba due to poor road networks and informal material delivery systems\. Despite global advancement in Construction 4\.0 driven by Building Information Modelling \(BIM\), Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Digital Twins, Internet of Things \(IoT\) and Data Analytics, existing studies in Nigeria are fragmented, focusing mainly on BIM in Lagos/Abuja without integrating the five technologies, without linking to last\-mile logistics, and without a mediated\-moderated framework for South\-East Nigeria\.

## [Formulation of Co\-crystals of Lopinavir using Co\-former to Enhance Solubility and Bioavailability](../publications/7bb5b3eca2a9599c9ffa.md)

Rahul Kumar Soni; Mohan Lal Kori

The poor aqueous solubility and limited oral bioavailability of many antiviral drugs, particularly lopinavir, present major challenges to effective oral drug delivery\. Lopinavir exhibits low solubility, poor intestinal permeability, and variable absorption, resulting in reduced therapeutic efficacy\. The present study aimed to develop and evaluate pharmaceutical cocrystals of lopinavir using pharmaceutically acceptable coformers to enhance its physicochemical and biopharmaceutical properties without altering its pharmacological activity\. Cocrystals were prepared using crystal engineering techniques, including solvent evaporation, slurry conversion, and solvent\-assisted grinding\. The prepared formulations were characterized by Fourier\-transform infrared spectroscopy \(FTIR\), differential scanning calorimetry \(DSC\), powder X\-ray diffraction \(PXRD\) and scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\), to confirm cocrystal formation and investigate structural modifications\. Solubility, dissolution, and stability studies were conducted to compare the optimized cocrystals with pure lopinavir\. The results demonstrated a marked improvement in aqueous solubility and dissolution rate, attributed to the formation of a modified crystal lattice and intermolecular hydrogen\-bonding interactions between lopinavir and the selected coformer\. The optimized cocrystals also exhibited satisfactory physicochemical stability while maintaining the therapeutic integrity of the drug\. These findings suggest that pharmaceutical cocrystal engineering is a promising, scalable, and regulatory\-acceptable approach for enhancing the oral bioavailability and therapeutic performance of poorly soluble antiviral drugs such as lopinavir\. Improved dissolution characteristics may contribute to reduced dose variability, enhanced patient compliance, and better clinical outcomes\. Keywords: Pharmaceutical cocrystals; Antiviral drugs; Solubility enhancement; Bioavailability; Coformers; Dissolution rate; Drug delivery; Crystal lattice modification

## [Effectiveness of Hidden\-State Probes for Localizing Reasoning Failures](../publications/7bb6b35ae839d421e6c2.md)

Shubham Subhnil; Yannis Belkhiter; Erik Miehling; Adam Dahlgren Lindström; Elizabeth M\. Daly

Verifying the final answer of a long reasoning trace may show that the trace is wrong but it does not distinguish three cases\. The problem may lie beyond the model&\#x27;s capability, another attempt would succeed, or one step in an otherwise recoverable trace made the trace fail\. Standard hidden\-state probes are trained on final\-answer correctness, a label that conflates these cases\. Monte Carlo rollouts distinguish the cases and locate the failing step at additional inference cost\. We test the hidden states of 4B and 8B reasoning models for the failure type and the failing step and compare each probe with the strongest baseline that uses no hidden states\. On incorrect 8B traces, the confidence probe, a calibrated correctness probe at a midpoint cutoff, misses 81% of cases in which a single step makes the trace unrecoverable and 47% of cases in which another attempt would succeed\. A probe with a different training design over the same states reverses the ordering of these two kinds of failure, so either ordering can be read from those states\. At both scales, no single tested probe locates the failing step more accurately than a rule based only on trace length, and at 4B a probe trained to predict that step fails to outperform this rule in any of 10 runs on identical traces\. The confidence probe therefore indicates that an answer is wrong, but its failure\-type ordering depends on its training design\.

## [Effectiveness of Medical French training in developing communicative competence among health professional students in Ghana](../publications/7bb715f593e9171aec00.md)

Fiawomorm Kofi Fiagbe; Jonas Kwabla Fiadzawoo; Edmond Maliyele Daberou; Dorcas Pearl Slippe; Ernest Nyamekye

This study examined the integration of Medical French into the training of health professionals in Ghana in response to the growing need for effective cross\-border healthcare communication within the multilingual ECOWAS region\. Despite the increasing relevance of French proficiency for healthcare delivery, professional mobility, and communication with Francophone patients, limited empirical research has assessed the effectiveness of Medical French instruction in Anglophone health professional education\. Guided by Stufflebeam&\#x27;s CIPP \(Context, Input, Process, Product\) evaluation model, the study adopted a quantitative descriptive design involving 176 students from the Schools of Pharmacy, Nursing, Midwifery, and Allied Sciences in a public university in Ghana\. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire based on the CIPP framework and analyzed using descriptive statistics\. Findings showed strong recognition of the relevance of Medical French for communication with Francophone patients, healthcare practice in border communities, regional collaboration, and international employment opportunities\. However, respondents perceived institutional support and instructional resources as inadequate, limiting practical immersion and authentic communicative experiences\. Although teaching strategies were considered moderately effective, students reported relatively low confidence in their communicative competence in clinical situations\. The study recommends curriculum reforms emphasizing experiential learning, clinical immersion, and cross\-border partnerships to strengthen communicative competence and enhance healthcare delivery within the ECOWAS sub\-region\.

## [From Inflammation to Resolution: Therapeutic Insights into Chronic Disease Management](../publications/7bbd43a0878833318c59.md)

Anastasia Vladimirovna Poznyak; Nikita A\. Mitkin; Daria Dmitryevna Borodko; Alexander Nikolaevich Orekhov

Inflammation is a fundamental biological process implicated in various physiological and neurological disorders, including cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes, and neurodegenerative conditions\. Chronic inflammation is linked to significant health challenges and mortality worldwide, emphasizing the importance of understanding its mechanisms and resolution\. This review elucidates inflammatory processes as essential components of the immune response, highlighting pharmacological interventions for promoting timely inflammation resolution\. We explore the dual phases of inflammation—acute and chronic—detailing the complex cellular interactions and signaling pathways that govern the inflammatory response to pathogens and tissue injury\. In particular, we emphasize specialized pro\-resolving mediators \(SPMs\), such as lipoxins and resolvins, which play crucial roles in transitioning inflammation from a detrimental to a healing state\. Additionally, we discuss innovative therapeutic approaches, including tissue engineering, cellular therapies, and the utilization of SPMs, aimed at enhancing inflammation resolution\. The roles of gaseous mediators and peptide/protein mediators in modulating inflammation are also examined\. Through this comprehensive analysis, we advocate for the development of pro\-resolving treatments to improve outcomes for patients with chronic inflammatory disorders\. By understanding the intricate dynamics of inflammation and its resolution, new avenues for targeted therapy emerge, offering promise for mitigating the impacts of chronic inflammatory diseases and enhancing patient quality of life\.

## [Variational quantum principal component analysis for Hilbert space Gaussian process regression](../publications/7bc02101915b21383a75.md)

Kerem Bükrü; Ralf Sturm; Tjark Siefkes

Abstract Gaussian processes are widely used probabilistic models for regression and classification tasks\. Their flexibility and ability to quantify uncertainties make them well\-suited for many applications\. However, their applicability to large datasets is limited by the cubic computational time complexity\. While reduced\-rank methods such as Hilbert space approximations reduce this complexity, scaling to very large datasets remains challenging\. Quantum algorithms are promising candidates to further accelerate such computations\. Quantum principal component analysis has previously been applied to Hilbert space Gaussian process regression to address this scaling limitation\. However, its applicability is limited by the requirement for fault\-tolerant quantum hardware\. In this work, we present a hybrid quantum\-classical model for reduced\-rank Gaussian process regression, where we apply a quantum principal component analysis algorithm based on parameterized quantum circuits to Hilbert space Gaussian process regression\. In noiseless simulations on a one\-dimensional test function, the resulting model reaches a regression accuracy comparable to that of the exact Gaussian process and the classical Hilbert space Gaussian process\. The framework uses shallow parameterized circuits and does not require fault\-tolerant quantum hardware, which makes it a candidate for noisy intermediate\-scale quantum devices\.

## [Caracterización de plataformas de Inteligencia Artificial para la transformación digital de la gestión educativa](../publications/7bc32c726a1c803b2437.md)

Milton Labanda\-Jaramillo; Maria de los Angeles Coloma Andrade; Henry Paul Saraguro Calle

El crecimiento imparable de la Inteligencia Artificial \(IA\) está modificando los paradigmas de gestión educativa\. Esta investigación consiste en saber qué herramientas y plataformas de IA facilitan el proceso de transformación digital de la gestión educativa en las instituciones académicas y cuál es su impacto en la mejora de la eficiencia administrativa y de los procedimientos pedagógicos\. Se ha utilizado como metodología una revisión sistemática de literatura \(SLR\) siguiendo las guías del modelo PRISMA, partiendo de una población inicial de 103 estudios empíricos y reportes técnicos, los cuales finalmente han dado lugar a la inclusión y análisis de 53 publicaciones en el periodo 2020 \- 2025, indexadas en bases de datos como Scopus, Web of Science o ScienceDirect\. Los resultados muestran que existe una categorización de herramientas en seis categorías funcionales y que la automatización de tareas administrativas permite ahorrar hasta un 44% del tiempo dedicado a la planificación y gestión; así como mejorar el aprendizaje efectivo con sistemas de aprendizaje personalizado para generar mejores resultados académicos en hasta un 30%\. La principal conclusión es que la implementación de la IA requiere de una gobernanza ética que aborde las brechas de responsabilidad, o sesgo algorítmico y privacidad de los datos, integrando la perspectiva sistémica \(macro\), organizacional \(meso\) y operativa \(micro\) del sistema educativo\.

## [Understanding and Mitigating Interlayer Thermal Crosstalk in 3D Vertical Phase‐Change Memory](../publications/7bd5b747582552fa8407.md)

Hanyuan Zhang; Xusheng Pan; Mengxi Cui; Qiang He; Qirui Zhang; Gao Jian\-feng; Xiangshui Miao

ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional vertical phase‐change memory \(3D vertical PCM\) provides a device‐level route toward vertically integrated phase‐change storage, yet vertical stacking converts cell‐level thermal confinement into a stack‐level reliability constraint\. Here, interlayer thermal crosstalk is investigated in a dual‐layer Hf‐doped Ge─Sb─Te 3D vertical PCM device by constructing an operation‐ and state‐dependent disturbance matrix\. The monitoring cell is initialized in either the crystalline low‐resistance state or the amorphous high‐resistance state, while READ‐, SET‐, and RESET‐level pulse trains are applied to the adjacent programming cell\. READ and SET produce limited disturbance, whereas RESET dominates interlayer thermal perturbation\. The amorphous high‐resistance state exhibits the highest susceptibility, showing a pronounced resistance decrease under adjacent RESET excitation\. Qualitative electrothermal simulations attribute this selectivity to localized RESET heating and transient vertical heat spreading across stacked layers\. Paired‐pulse programming temporally redistributes the RESET thermal budget by decoupling rapid selected‐layer heating from delayed interlayer heat spreading\. This strategy preserves the thermal response required for selected‐cell programming while suppressing heat transfer to the monitoring layer\. Electrical measurements confirm that paired‐pulse programming improves post‐disturbance resistance retention from &lt;40% to &gt;85%, demonstrating thermal‐budget engineering as an effective strategy for enhancing the reliability of vertically integrated 3D vertical PCM devices\.

## [Research and Practice on Intelligent Management and Control of the Urban Drainage System in Pinggu District, Beijing Based on SWMM](../publications/7bd81e1eb96464bb5002.md)

This study presents a comprehensive research initiative focused on the intelligent management and control of urban drainage systems, specifically applied to Pinggu District in Beijing\. Utilizing the Storm Water Management Model \(SWMM\), the research integrates extensive literature reviews, comparative case studies of water utility management in major global cities, and rigorous on\-site field investigations\. A critical component of this work involves the construction and calibration of a high\-resolution SWMM stormwater model for the target drainage network\. To address common challenges such as missing data in legacy pipe networks and complex parameter calibration, a systematic section\-by\-section verification and zone\-by\-zone calibration methodology was implemented\. This approach significantly stabilized the model&\#x27;s operational environment, yielding simulation results that closely align with real\-world hydrological conditions\. Furthermore, the research incorporates insights from urban lake management, analyzing eutrophication treatment through a holistic source control, process interception, and end\-of\-pipe treatment framework, exemplified by a representative urban lake in Shenzhen\. By bridging theoretical hydrological modeling with practical engineering applications, this study enhances the understanding of water body dynamics under rapid urbanization pressures\. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of calibrated SWMM applications in optimizing urban drainage infrastructure\. Ultimately, this paper details the methodological framework, simulation outcomes, and practical implications of the intelligent drainage management system, while proposing strategic directions for future research in smart water infrastructure and sustainable urban water environment engineering\.

## [The PENIMA project : artificial intelligence decision‐support tool for penile lesions – protocol paper and invitation to participate](../publications/7bef20dda68952926646.md)

J\. Mølsted; Anne Birgitte Als; Jørgen Bjerggaard Jensen; Mikael Aagaard; Lisa Anni Larsen Lethan; Sinja Kristiansen; Christian Arvei Moen; Axel Gerdtsson; Line Kibsgaard; Christina Gade Jespersen; Frederikke Eichner Soerensen; Ann‐Kathrine Rossau; Jens Kramer Rangen; Jakob Kristian Jakobsen

Objectives To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence \(AI\)‐driven decision‐support development – and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project\. Patients and Methods Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments\. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations\. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected\. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow‐up and histopathology when available\. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool \(CVAT\) environment\. Supervised machine‐learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient‐level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics\. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1‐10‐72‐150‐22\. Results As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included\. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants\. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification\. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma \(84\.6%, 95% confidence interval 75\.0–91\.0%\)\. Conclusion The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real‐world penile lesion presentations\. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image‐based clinical decision‐support tools\.
