## [A Dual\-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention Among Executives of Traditional\-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation](../publications/7c0399b11d829fc0f19f.md)

Weixiang Gan

\*\*A Dual\-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention among Executives of Traditional\-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation\*\* \*\*Weixiang Gan\*\* Post Doctorate Researcher, Lincoln University College, 47301 Petaling Jaya, Malaysia \*\*Qiaoran Liu\*\* Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau of Yindu District, Anyang City 455000, China \*\*Mengfei Xiao\*\* Post Doctorate Researcher, Lincoln University College, 47301 Petaling Jaya, Malaysia \*\*Jialin Liu\*\* School of Management and Marketing, Faculty of Business and Law, Taylor’s University, No\. 1, Jalan Taylor’s, 47500 Subang Jaya, Malaysia \*\*Tara Ahmed Mohammed\*\* SEGi University, Kota Damansara, Petaling Jaya 47810, Malaysia \*\*Abstract:\*\* Whether a small or medium\-sized firm in a traditional industry takes up artificial intelligence is usually settled by the chairman or the general manager alone, without an information\-systems de\-partment to consult\. Existing adoption research draws its evidence mainly from firms that have already completed basic informatisation, so how external conditions reach the executive remains unclear\. This study surveyed 526 SME executives in four traditional industries across four Chinese regions and esti\-mated a structural equation model linking technology\-side and environment\-side conditions, perceived value, perceived implementation risk and adoption intention, with digital foundation as a boundary con\-dition\. External conditions split into two mediating pathways, the two channels of the model\. Performance expectancy and competitive pressure raise perceived value, while effort expectancy and perceived insti\-tutional support leave it unchanged and instead lower perceived implementation risk\. Competitive pres\-sure carries opposite signs across the two pathways and its total effect on adoption intention is indistin\-guishable from zero, as is that of institutional support\. Digital foundation weakens the suppression that perceived risk exerts on intention, the slope falling from −0\.284 to −0\.125, although the two product terms add only 0\.007 to the explained variance in intention\. Peer demonstration and subsidies do not move these firms, and the estimates locate the reason in a risk they cannot absorb rather than in any shortfall of perceived value; building the data and systems base before the application layer fits the way these firms decide\. The design is cross\-sectional, so the estimates are associational and the ordering among the con\-structs rests on theory rather than on temporal precedence\. \*\*Keywords:\*\* Artificial Intelligence Adoption, SME Executives, Perceived Value, Perceived Implementa\-tion Risk, Digital Foundation, Upper Echelons Perspective, Structural Equation Modelling \*\*Citation:\*\* Gan, W\., Liu, Q\., Xiao, M\., Liu, J\., &amp; Mohammed, T\. A\. \(2026\)\. A Dual\-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention among Executives of Traditional\-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation\. \_Business and Management Perspectives\_, \_01\_\(04\), 1–28\. https://doi\.org/10\.67728/bmp\.2026\.016

## [Partner and Partnership in Society: Basic Elements and Structural Functional Models](../publications/7c0622317f40ef1f9b23.md)

Rosita Zvirgzdiņa; Jānis Vanags; Iveta Liniņa; Velga Vēvere

The relevance of the study is related to the importance of partnerships in meeting needs and their role in ensuring socio\-economic, political, and security stability\. In modern conditions, the level of partnership formation in several socially significant areas is still insufficient to effectively respond to growing global risks and threats\. The quality of partnerships is of fundamental importance in ensuring the competitiveness, security, and sustainability of individuals and social systems\. The study aims to theoretically analyze the content of the concepts “partner” and “partnership”, identifying their most important elements and explaining their importance in the formation and functioning of partnerships in conditions of changing threats and opportunities\. The tasks of the study are: 1\. to analyze the interpretations of the concepts “partner” and “partnership” in the scientific literature, identifying their structural and functional features; 2\. to study and systematize the structural\-functional models of partnership at various levels of society \(individual, organization, institution, society\); 3\. evaluate the practical aspects of the formation and functioning of partnerships, identifying the main challenges, risks and development opportunities\.

## [Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Autoencoders and Smite techniques based in Deep Neural Network \(DNN\)](../publications/7c0f8490e4023d4b7eff.md)

Jitendra Dudi; Irfan Khan

The digital payment platforms have enhanced the ease of conducting financial transactions, but they have also led to a rise in fraudulent activities\. The difficulty of detecting credit card fraud is exacerbated by the very skewed nature of the data – with a far greater number of legitimate transactions than fraudulent ones\. This imbalance makes it harder to use traditional classification methods and necessitates the use of specialized techniques for identification of frauds with confidence\. In this research, an end\-to\-end fraud detection system is explored, which considers several machine learning and deep learning solutions to detect suspicious transactions\. Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost and LightGBM are the machine learning models considered, and 1D Convolutional Neural Network, Long Short\-Term Memory network and Feed Forward Neural Network are the deep learning models explored\. The proposed framework uses the data preprocessing techniques, such as feature normalization and class balancing using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique \(SMOTE\) to enhance the recognition of the minority class\. Furthermore, a hybrid approach called SentraFraud is presented that integrates isolation forest anomaly detection and LightGBM classification for improved fraud prediction\. The developed system is made available as a web application using Flask and users can now analyze transaction details as well as receive real time fraud predictions\. This suggested framework is designed to support an efficient, scalable and intelligent model to detect fraudulent payment activities by combining anomaly detection and advanced payment activity prediction models\.

## [Investigating the Impact of AI\-Facilitated Socratic Dialogue on Critical Thinking Skills](../publications/7c1244031ff1c7f9400c.md)

Siti Sarah Abdur Rani; Sumia Salim Al Hadrami

This mixed\-method study aims to explore the impact of having Socratic dialogue with artificial intelligence \(AI\) on students&\#x27; critical thinking skills’ performance\. The data were gathered from 35 foundation\-level students\. The study utilised a Watson Glaser critical thinking pre\-test and post\-test to measure their critical thinking abilities and a questionnaire to gather their perception of AI usage\. During the intervention, students were engaged in structured AI\-facilitated Socratic questioning sessions weekly\. Data were analysed using paired\-sample t\-tests and linear regression, while survey responses were examined for thematic trends\. Even though the data collected shows that students have a positive perception of using AI, there is no statistically significant difference between the pre\- and post\-tests \(p &gt; \.05\)\. The finding shows that students’ critical thinking performance did not improve throughout the study\. Furthermore, the results for the linear regression \(R² = 0\.038, p &gt; \.05\) show that there is very little correlation between students’ perception and their critical thinking performance\. The study reveals the gap between students’ positive perception of using AI and their critical thinking skill development\.

## [Cognitive Engagement, Learning Strategies, Adjustment to College and Academic Motivation: A Structural Equation Model on Academic Success Among College Students](../publications/7c13dbb3be9a64240d96.md)

Jason D\. Dacutin; Eugenio S\. Guhao

This study examined the relationships among cognitive engagement, learning strategies, adjustment to college, academic motivation, and academic success to determine the best\-fit structural equation model among Bachelor of Elementary Education students in Region XIII \(Caraga\), Philippines\. Anchored in Self\-Regulated Learning Theory and Academic Adjustment Theory, the study employed a quantitative, non\-experimental descriptive\-correlational design involving 470 second\-, third\-, and fourth\-year students from three state universities, selected through proportional stratified random sampling\. Data were collected using five adapted, validated, and reliability\-tested questionnaires and analyzed through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and structural equation modeling\. Results revealed very high levels of cognitive engagement \(M = 4\.27\), learning strategies \(M = 4\.32\), college adjustment \(M = 4\.34\), academic motivation \(M = 4\.32\), and academic success \(M = 4\.31\)\. All four predictors demonstrated significant positive correlations with academic success, with academic motivation exhibiting the strongest relationship \(r = \.519\)\. The final structural model demonstrated excellent fit \(CMIN/DF = \.845, CFI = 1\.000, RMSEA = \.000\) and explained 32\.5% of the variance in academic success\. Academic motivation \(β = \.270, p = \.020\) and learning strategies \(β = \.262, p = \.017\) emerged as significant direct predictors, whereas college adjustment and cognitive engagement showed nonsignificant direct effects\. The findings emphasize the importance of strengthening academic motivation and effective learning strategies through learner\-centered instruction and institutional support programs\. The study supports Sustainable Development Goal 4 \(Quality Education\) by providing evidence to inform educational practices and student success initiatives\. Its sustainability contribution lies in supporting evidence\-based academic planning, student retention, and continuous improvement in higher education\.

## [Neutrophil dysregulation in sepsis\-induced acute lung injury: mechanistic framework and therapeutic targeting by natural products](../publications/7c1c7710babaacc14e14.md)

Huilin Luo; Jinyuan Lin; Honglei Shen; Dongqin Huang; Maoyao Ling; Liu Ye

Sepsis\-induced acute lung injury \(SALI\) is an important complication of sepsis associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective targeted therapies remain limited\. Neutrophils are central effectors of innate immunity and play indispensable roles in early antimicrobial defense\. However, during sepsis, persistent inflammatory stimulation drives neutrophil dysregulation, leading to excessive pulmonary infiltration, aberrant activation, delayed apoptosis, neutrophil extracellular trap \(NET\) formation, and immune imbalance, all of which contribute to alveolar\-capillary barrier disruption and lung injury progression\. Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophil heterogeneity in SALI is shaped by multiple molecular regulators rather than by maturation status alone\. Trafficking receptors, activation\-associated markers, disease\-associated transcriptional states, and intercellular signaling pathways—including CXCR4, CXCR2, CD11b, CD16, CD177, Fth1, Prok2, CD64/CD271, PD\-L1, and Notch1\-related signaling—collectively regulate neutrophil trafficking, activation, effector responses, and crosstalk with endothelial and immune cells\. In this review, we summarize the molecular determinants underlying neutrophil functional heterogeneity and discuss the dual role of neutrophils in host defense and tissue injury in SALI\. We also highlight the major mechanisms of neutrophil\-mediated lung damage and summarize emerging evidence that natural products can alleviate SALI by modulating neutrophil recruitment, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and NET formation\. Targeting neutrophil dysregulation represents a potential therapeutic approach that requires further mechanistic and clinical validation\.

## [Pooja Ramesh Singh V\. Jammu and Kashmir bank Ltd\. &amp; Another](../publications/7c1e1793b1c45e1e99f6.md)

Hiba Hayat

The case of Pooja Ramesh Singh v\. J&amp;K Bank Ltd\. represents a significant ruling concerning legal technology in India\. The Supreme Court has introduced a policy of zero tolerance towards hallucinated precedents and has stated that any such orders are entirely void, thus protecting the integrity of the judicial record\. Since artificial intelligence tools are becoming increasingly common in legal procedures, this judgment makes sure that technology stays a secondary aid to human judgment and therefore upholds the fundamental principles of natural justice, legal accuracy, and judicial accountability\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial y Emprendimiento: Oportunidades, Barreras y Modelos de Adopción en el Contexto Empresarial Ecuatoriano](../publications/7c2046ef2062f62cc878.md)

Franklin David Espinoza Sanaguano; Josselyn Patricia Ordoñez Morocho; Charles Fabián Barreno Flores; Christopher Cruz

La disponibilidad de herramientas de inteligencia artificial \(IA\) contrasta con las dificultades de las empresas de menor tamaño para integrarlas en sus operaciones\. En Ecuador, este problema se agrava por la dispersión de la evidencia y la confusión entre digitalización, expectativas y adopción efectiva\. El objetivo fue analizar las oportunidades y barreras documentadas para el emprendimiento ecuatoriano y examinar el alcance de TAM, UTAUT y la teoría de difusión de innovaciones como marcos interpretativos\. Se desarrolló una revisión narrativa con actualización documental al 5 de octubre de 2026\. Se evaluaron 33 registros preseleccionados y se integraron 30 fuentes, con una matriz de extracción que distinguió población, tecnología, indicador, hallazgo y limitación\. Los estudios ecuatorianos describieron diferencias de uso por función empresarial y restricciones relacionadas con competencias, datos y recursos\. El GEM 2025 registró que el 47,6 % de los emprendedores tempranos usaba o preveía usar IA; este indicador combinado no midió exclusivamente adopción efectiva\. Las aplicaciones documentadas se concentraron en contenidos, atención al cliente y apoyo administrativo, mientras que la analítica predictiva exigió mayores condiciones de implementación\. Los modelos aportaron categorías complementarias, aunque no se validaron empíricamente en esta revisión\. Se concluyó que la adopción requiere vincular una necesidad empresarial verificable con capacidades de uso, evaluación del desempeño y gestión de riesgos\. Se propuso una ruta de implementación gradual y una agenda de investigación que distinga intención, uso sostenido y resultados del negocio\.

## [A Theory of Personal Computing Education Rooted in Spreadsheets:The Non\-Intervening Educator and the Conditions for Human Growth](../publications/7c28e72baf871e1cc2ec.md)

Yoshihiro SATO

This paper examines the state of spreadsheet education and proposes a new educational framework\. Current spreadsheet instruction in Japan ends with explanations of functions, and learners never develop the ability to apply that knowledge independently\. This paper draws on End User Computing \(EUC\) theory, cognitive science \(working memory, schema theory, the forgetting curve\), situated learning theory, and the TPACK framework to analyze the structural causes of this problem\. The paper then proposes an educational model in which the educator’s role is to create an environment that supports autonomous growth rather than to transmit knowledge directly\. Key elements of this model include understanding what a spreadsheet is, mastering the minimum necessary elements, acquiring a six\-step operation loop, and establishing an operation philosophy\. The paper argues that genuine spreadsheet competence can only be achieved through approximately 200 hours of autonomous self\-directed practice after the initial instructional intervention\.

## [In vivo monitoring of polymorphonuclear myeloid\-derived suppressor cells in experimental rheumatoid arthritis](../publications/7c29168e4b1757a284d1.md)

Johannes Schwenck; Kerstin Fuchs; mohamed ali jarboui; Sophia Geiger; Marc Neumann; Hasan H\. Öz; Melanie Carevic; Sabrina Hoffmann; Dominik Hartl; Christoph M\. Griessinger; Irene González\-Menéndez; Leticia Quintanilla‐Martínez; Jörg C\. Henes; Gerald Reischl; Andreas Maurer; Bernd Jürgen Pichler; Manfred Kneilling

Introduction Myeloid\-derived suppressor cells \(MDSCs\) regulate immune responses, but their role in autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) remains incompletely understood\. Here, we applied non\-invasive positron emission tomography \(PET\) imaging to investigate the migration dynamics of polymorphonuclear \(PMN\)\-MDSCs in experimental RA\. Materials and methods RA was induced in female BALB/c mice via K/BxN serum\. Immune infiltrates in arthritic ankles were characterized by flow cytometry and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry \(LC–MS\)\-based proteomics\. We radiolabeled bone marrow\-derived \(BM\-PMN\-MDSCs\) and RA ankle\-derived PMN\-MDSCs \(RA\-PMN\-MDSCs\) intracellularly with \[ 64 Cu\]Cu\-PTSM or Ly6G\-specific \[ 64 Cu\]Cu\-NOTA\-1A8\. Radiolabeled PMN\-MDSCs were adoptively transferred into RA mice and tracked longitudinally by PET/MRI\. In a second cohort, \[ 64 Cu\]Cu\-NOTA\-1A8 was injected directly for in vivo imaging of Ly6G \+ myeloid cells over 48 h\. Results RA progression was associated with a marked increase in the number of CD11b \+ Ly6C med Ly6G \+ PMN\-MDSCs in arthritic ankles, whereas the number of CD11b \+ Ly6C high Ly6G − monocytic\-MDSCs remained unchanged\. PET/MRI demonstrated significantly enhanced homing of RA\-PMN\-MDSCs to inflamed ankles compared with that of BM\-PMN\-MDSCs, indicating disease\-associated functional adaptation\. Direct in vivo targeting of MDSCs with \[ 64 Cu\]Cu\-1A8 revealed strongly increased uptake in arthritic ankles at 1 h, 24 h, and 48 h p\.i\. , which was significantly reduced by Ly6G blockade, confirming tracer specificity\. Proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of extracellular matrix organization and integrin signaling pathways in RA\-PMN\-MDSCs, suggesting that a distinct inflammatory signature underlies their migratory behavior\. Conclusion PET/MRI enables non\-invasive monitoring of PMN\-MDSC migration during experimental RA and provides novel insights into the role of these cells in autoimmune inflammation, supporting the development of PMN\-MDSCs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in autoimmune diseases\.

## [Damage detection of steam turbine blades using deep neural network\-based acoustic fingerprint recognition](../publications/7c3dbbccf9cf6bb2c8b9.md)

Zhixiang Zhang; Wenyu Gao; Yizhuo Gong; Yunhao Wang; Zun Yin; Xiaomeng Li; Damao Yang; Jin Zhou; Jun Peng

This study develops an impact\-acoustic framework for classifying predefined surface\-damage states on steam\-turbine blades, identifying one of three damage regions, and estimating class\-dependent severity parameters\. Impact signals were recorded for 5 s at 22,050 Hz under controlled impact and microphone angles\. After event screening, each signal was converted into a 13\-coefficient W\-MFCC map that combines continuous\-wavelet time\-frequency localization, Mel\-scale subband mapping, and cepstral compression\. A hybrid ResNet\-50\-Transformer\-PANet\-CMTL network was designed to extract hierarchical local features, model long\-range dependencies, fuse multi\-scale information, and produce conditional multi\-task outputs\. The dataset contained 1,200 training samples and 300 validation samples covering crack, crack\-erosion, and crack\-abrasion conditions in Areas 1\-3\. On the reported validation split, W\-MFCC correctly classified 296 of 300 samples \(98\.67 %\), compared with 89\.33 % for MFCC and 87\.33 % for wavelet input, and its loss curves showed more stable convergence\. The full multi\-scale configuration also exhibited smoother training behavior than the ResNet\-50 \+ Transformer baseline\. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining W\-MFCC representation learning with multi\-scale conditional prediction for controlled turbine\-blade condition assessment\.

## [Development of a multilingual speech\-to\-text translation model to support artisans’ business communication](../publications/7c3fbb8f8bff7945a6c8.md)

O\. S\. Ojo; O\. Ajayi; O\. E\. Oyebode; O\. Oladipo

Effective communication between artisans and customers remains difficult in multilingual commercial settings in which English interacts with indigenous and contact languages such as Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin\. This study developed and evaluated a lightweight English\-to\-Yoruba and English\-to\-Nigerian Pidgin speech translation system for artisans’ everyday business communication\. The system is a five\-phase cascaded architecture comprising automatic speech recognition \(ASR\), text normalisation, an intermediate linguistic representation, language\-specific translation, and text\-to\-speech \(TTS\) synthesis\. Its hierarchical staging follows the processing principles of the Hierarchical Efficient Neural Transducer for Speech Recognition and Translation \(HENT\-SRT\), while the neural components of that design are replaced by transparent retrieval mechanisms suited to resource\-constrained devices\. A domain\-specific parallel corpus of 2,000 artisan oriented expressions per target language, built from a needs analysis with artisans in southwestern Nigeria and covering automotive repair, pricing negotiation, service delivery and customer relations, supports translation through exact bilingual lookup, with a fallback to fuzzy retrieval that combines sequence similarity and Jaccard token overlap under a confidence threshold\. The system was evaluated on 15 spoken utterances using word error rate \(WER\) for recognition and BLEU and METEOR for translation, reported at corpus and per\-utterance levels with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals\. Yoruba achieved mean BLEU and METEOR of 0\.93 and 0\.93, and Nigerian Pidgin 0\.90 and 0\.92\. Mean WER was approximately 0\.00 on the 14 scorable utterances\. Thirteen of 15 utterances \(87%\) were translated perfectly into both languages; one utterance failed completely and one failed partially in Pidgin\. Mean ASR latency was 1\.60 s, and translation accounted for less than 1% of end\-to\-end wall\-clock time\. The confidence intervals for the two languages overlapped substantially, so no reliable performance difference between them could be established at this sample size\. The findings establish the feasibility of a lightweight, transparent speech translation pipeline for in\-domain artisan communication and identify numeric expression handling, held out evaluation, and neural extension as the priorities for future work\.

## [Relationship of Information Technology System and Work Efficiency: Evidence from a Philippine Government Hospital](../publications/7c428dc9f8653ee50441.md)

G E Albaytar; M M Banado; M G F Baybayan; Jesus P\. Briones

The adoption of information technology \(IT\) is increasingly vital in improving healthcare services in government hospitals\. This study examined IT system adoption in a Philippine government hospital and its relationship to staff’s work efficiency\. Using a descriptive correlational design, data were collected from 214 plantilla and contractual employees via Google Forms and analyzed through frequency and percentage distribution, weighted mean, and Spearman’s rank\-order correlation\. Results revealed that the IT system had a moderate impact on staff performance, with usability, accessibility, and frequency of use influencing efficiency\. Staff generally agreed that the system supported daily tasks, improved workflow, and reduced backlogs, indicating its positive contribution to task completion, accuracy, and time management\. A high significant positive correlation was found between all dimensions of IT adoption and work efficiency, confirming that IT use enhances staff performance\. However, there are still challenges encountered in using IT system which can hinder optimal system utilization\. Based on the findings of the study, proposed strategies were recommended for improving IT system utilization to further enhance the overall work efficiency of hospital staff\. Theoretically, the study builds on Socio\-Technical Systems Theory by demonstrating how technology integration mitigates operational risks and strengthens institutional resilience\. Managerially, it contributes to public sector governance and risk\-informed decision\-making literature by positioning IT adoption as a strategic tool for accountability, efficiency, and sustainability in healthcare systems\. Importantly, the findings underscore the need for governance strategies that combine technological investment with workforce development to ensure reliable, resilient, and sustainable healthcare service delivery

## [Explainable Random Forest Framework for Multi\-Class Lifestyle Disease Risk Prediction Using BRFSS Data](../publications/7c44ebd48e79dc7c7048.md)

Prema P\.; Nivetha P\.; Nagasakthi N\.

With the increase in lifestyle diseases globally, there is a need for an effective machine learning approach to predict people who are at risk\. In this research, a machine learning framework for multiclass prediction of risk of lifestyle disease using the BRFSS 2024 dataset is developed\. There are six risk groups: Healthy, Diabetes Risk, Hypertension Risk, Obesity Risk, Heart Disease Risk, and Kidney Disease Risk\. Data preprocessing in the proposed framework is done by treating missing values, converting categorical variables into numeric variables, eliminating duplicate and inconsistent entries, normalizing using the Z\-score method, and correlation\-based feature selection\. Synthetic Minority Over\-sampling Technique \(SMOTE\) is implemented to solve the problem of class imbalance\. There are five classifiers tested using the 80/20 ratio for training and testing\. They include Logistic Regression, SVM, KNN, Decision Tree, and Random Forest\. The analysis reveals that the Random Forest performs well with an accuracy rate of 94\.8%, and thus, is selected as the final model for predicting the diseases\. Age, smoking, and sleep time have also been identified as important features using feature importance analysis that play an important role in predicting the risk of developing lifestyle diseases\.

## [Metaheuristic\-Based Predictive Modelling of Wind Velocity Distributions](../publications/7c4e83bbd02c0c29c974.md)

Chukwuma George Ekeoma

Accurate modeling of wind velocity distribution is essential for optimizing wind energy generation and improving resource assessments\. This study presents a predictive stochastic model utilizing the Weibull distribution, with its parameters optimized using the Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\) algorithm—a robust metaheuristic technique\. Wind speed data collected over a one\-year period in the Aba region were analyzed\. The PSO\-based estimation significantly outperformed traditional methods like Maximum Likelihood Estimation \(MLE\), yielding lower error margins and higher correlation with empirical data\. The optimized model achieved a high coefficient of determination \(R² = 0\.972\) and a reduced Root Mean Square Error \(RMSE = 0\.0087\), confirming its effectiveness\. The study demonstrates the potential of PSO\-enhanced models in supporting reliable wind energy resource evaluation and system design\.

## [RTSM: Adapting Recursive Models to Multivariate Time\-Series Classification](../publications/7c4ff05fb376256a656a.md)

Georg Tenzing; Anna Tegon; Luca Benini; Thorir Mar Ingolfsson

Accurate multivariate time\-series classification requires extracting temporal features and integrating information across a sequence\. Weight\-tied refinement offers a way to repeatedly process these features without allocating new parameters at each stage\. Applying this principle to time series requires choosing both a temporal representation and a latent\-state organization suited to classification\. We introduce the Recursive Time\-Series Model \(RTSM\), which combines a learned convolutional temporal tokenizer, single\-state weight\-tied refinement, and a pooled classification readout\. Across all 30 UEA datasets, RTSM achieves 72\.81% mean accuracy under validation\-based configuration and checkpoint selection, the highest observed mean among the 17 evaluated deep\-learning models and 1\.60 percentage points above MambaSL\. Ablations on eight datasets favor the proposed tokenizer over a simple convolutional embedding and the single\-state model over the tested two\-state variants\. The complete classifier reaches 86\.10% mean accuracy versus 84\.79% for a separately trained tokenizer\-only classifier\. These findings identify temporal encoding and state organization as key design choices for adapting recursive architectures to time series\. The resulting classifier combines competitive accuracy with a shared refinement module whose parameter count is independent of computational depth\.

## [Hepatic GHR deletion alters bile acid composition and links reduced FXR signaling to hepatic steatosis](../publications/7c559873f49386f14141.md)

Liyuan Ran; Ruolan Li; Yu Wang; Xinyu Liu; Yingjie Wu; Zichao Yu

Aims Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\) is a growing global health concern\. Growth hormone \(GH\) signaling regulates hepatic lipid metabolism, but its relationship with the bile acid–farnesoid X receptor \(FXR\) axis in MASLD remains unclear\. We investigated the effects of hepatic GH receptor \(GHR\) deletion on bile acid metabolism and hepatic steatosis and evaluated the response to pharmacological FXR activation\. Materials and methods Liver\-specific Ghr knockout \(LKO\) mice and LL controls were examined using targeted metabolomics, bile acid profiling, biochemical assays, histology, and gene and protein expression analyses\. Public human MASLD transcriptomic datasets were analyzed for GHR/IGF1–FXR expression relationships\. The effects of the FXR agonist GW4064 were evaluated in LKO mice and primary LKO hepatocytes\. Results Hepatic GHR deletion promoted steatosis, increased hepatic total and conjugated bile acids, including TαMCA, TβMCA, and TUDCA, and reduced BSEP and FXR/SHP expression\. Gallbladder total and conjugated bile acids were lower in LKO mice\. Hepatic GHR or IGF1 expression correlated positively with FXR expression in human MASLD datasets\. GW4064 ameliorated steatosis and reduced serum markers of liver injury in LKO mice and decreased lipid accumulation in primary LKO hepatocytes\. Treatment increased lipolysis\-associated gene expression without significantly changing the measured lipogenic genes or Bsep expression\. Conclusions Hepatic GHR deletion disrupts bile acid homeostasis and promotes steatosis\. GW4064 improves steatosis in this model, supporting FXR activation as a potential intervention for GHR\-deficient steatosis\. The altered bile acid pool may contribute to reduced hepatic FXR signaling\.

## [Melanin\-concentrating hormone inhibits PVN oxytocin neurons through barium\-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channels and MCH\-neuron ablation alters pup\-directed aggression](../publications/7c5651c4bdcc0ebd1a59.md)

Tingbi Xiong; Fumihito Saitow; Ayumu Inutsuka; Tatsushi Onaka; Kazuo Yamada; Chitose Orikasa

Interactions between melanin\-concentrating hormone \(MCH\) neurons and oxytocin neurons are crucial for parental care\. Whole\-cell patch\-clamp recordings demonstrated that MCH inhibits paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus \(PVN\)\-oxytocin neurons through activation of barium\-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channels, potentially G\-protein coupled inwardly rectifying potassium channels, and pup\-directed aggression was positively related to loss of MCH neurons\. Our findings offer a glimpse into the neural mechanisms underlying the evolutionary regulation of offspring caregiving and abuse in males\.

## [This Week in The Journal](../publications/7c5daf7a382e960eb2b1.md)

Paige McKeon

## [Integration of IoT And Satellite Data for Real\-Time Agricultural Crop Stress Monitoring Using Spatio\-Temporal Transformers](../publications/7c6c08b800c522a47608.md)

This research work presents an integrated framework for real\-time crop stress monitoring that combines ground\-based Internet of Things \(IoT\) sensors and multi\-temporal satellite remote sensing data\. Due to growing environmental uncertainty and limited resources, the early identification of crop stress is crucial for maximizing agricultural productivity\. The solution utilizes a Spatio\-Temporal Transformer \(ST\-Transformer\) model to integrate these heterogeneous data streams to make early crop disease and irrigation stress detection\. By integrating spatial satellite imagery with temporal IoT sequences, STT leverages attention mechanisms to offer a more holistic analysis, which translates to an impressive accuracy of 88% and a solid F1\-Score of 0\.855\. This dual capacity to concurrently handle spatial and temporal dimensions allows STT to effectively generalize across diverse crop stress categories, providing insights that are both timely and actionable

## [Ensemble\-Based Descriptor Analysis of Flexible Odorants: Conformational Landscapes of Geraniol, Nerol, and Linalool](../publications/7c81947bee590ccf4fb9.md)

Cuadrado\-Benavent Beatriz; Juan J\. Nogueira; David Ferro‐Costas

Abstract Conformational flexibility remains a central challenge in the molecular modeling of odorants because thermally accessible structures may differ from the potential\-energy minima identified in conformational searches\. Here, we combine automated conformational exploration, multistructural thermodynamics, and descriptor\-based statistical analysis to characterize the conformational ensembles of three flexible acyclic terpenic alcohols: geraniol, nerol, and linalool\. The conformational searches identify large numbers of conformers \(119, 88, and 83 for geraniol, nerol, and linalool, respectively\), but only a subset of these structures contributes substantially to the finite\-temperature equilibrium ensemble\. Across the three systems, entropy\-related contributions tend to shift the equilibrium toward more extended arrangements than those favored electronically, leading to Gibbs free\-energy minima at 310 K that can differ from the corresponding potential\-energy minima\. Descriptor–energy correlation analyses further show that, among the descriptors considered, global shape exhibits the most consistent association with thermodynamic stabilization, rather than individual local hydroxyl\-mediated contacts; decomposition of the Gibbs free energies indicates that this trend is predominantly vibrational in origin\. Principal component and clustering analyses reveal that the ensembles are better described as continuous conformational landscapes than as sharply separated structural families\. These results highlight the limitations of relying only on potential\-energy minima and support the use of ensemble\-based, descriptor\-guided molecular modeling strategies for flexible odorants and related acyclic terpenoids\.

## [Nearly Linear Private Learning of Littlestone Classes](../publications/7c83de7f5928d0adc3eb.md)

Shay Moran; Chao Yan

Differentially private learning aims to learn from data while protecting individual training examples\. For binary classification, finite Littlestone dimension characterizes approximate private PAC learnability \(Alon et al\., JACM 2022\)\. Understanding how this dimension controls private sample complexity remains a central question\. For classes of Littlestone dimension $d$, the first general upper bound was doubly exponential in $d$ \(Bun, Livni, and Moran, FOCS 2020\)\. Subsequent work improved this to $\\widetilde O\(d^6\)$ \(Ghazi et al\., STOC 2021\) and then to $\\widetilde O\(d^5\)$ \(Lyu, STOC 2026\)\. We prove a nearly linear upper bound of $O\(d\\log d\)$\. Our main algorithmic contribution is a structural exponential mechanism for data\-dependent candidate sets equipped with a rank satisfying suitable stability conditions\. For natural Littlestone classes such as subspace indicators, this rank has a simple geometric interpretation: it is the codimension\. This yields a private PAC learner for subspaces of dimension at most $d$ over any field, with tight linear dependence on $d$ and no dependence on the ambient dimension, improving the quadratic dependence of Kaplan et al\. \(STOC 2025\)\. Our second contribution is combinatorial: drawing on model\-theoretic ideas, we construct a suitable rank for general Littlestone classes and establish the counting bounds required by the mechanism\.

## [Beyond Self\-Report: A Neurocognitive Approach to UX Evaluation of Greek Municipal Websites](../publications/7c8f14ac9b6dc9af70a4.md)

Olga Tsatsani; Yannis Pollalis

Despite growing investment in e\-government infrastructure, the adoption of local municipal digital services remains limited, raising questions about how user experience \(UX\) is currently evaluated\. Traditional approaches, based on expert audits and self\-reported measures, capture primarily the conscious and observable layers of interaction, overlooking the underlying cognitive and emotional processes that shape actual user behavior\. This study introduces a multimodal, neuroscience\-informed framework for UX evaluation and presents, on a pilot basis, an exploratory application of the Neurocognitive Engagement \(NCE\) Index to three Greek municipal websites representing bad, medium, and good UX quality\. A pilot experiment \(N=10\) was conducted combining electroencephalography \(EEG\), a Post\-Session Recognition Memory Task \(PSRMT\), eye\-tracking behavioral data, and self\-reported measures\. Findings indicate that while self\-reports differentiated UX Conditions, the NCE Index revealed near\-identical engagement between medium and good UX \(5\.20 vs\. 5\.07\), despite substantial differences in audit scores\. These preliminary findings suggest that conventional UX evaluation methods may not fully capture the underlying neurocognitive processes associated with user interaction, highlighting the potential value of integrating neuroscience\-informed measures into existing UX evaluation frameworks\. The study presents exploratory results as a proof\-of\-concept for a novel methodological framework\. Future research with larger, gender\-balanced samples is needed to validate and extend these preliminary findings\. The study carries practical implications for the evidence\-based allocation of public digitalization budgets and the adoption of neurocognitive methods in applied public\-sector UX evaluation\.

## [A Theoretical Framework for Non\-Invasive Neurosurgery Utilizing Biosonic and Bioneurosonic Resonance of the Human Voice: A Technical Monograph on Biowave Mechanics](../publications/7c960eae91cee952558a.md)

Abdesselam Abouelfida

Background: Traditional neurosurgery and neuromodulation paradigms often overlook the active vibrational and mechanical parameters of the cranial environment, treating brain tissue as a passive substrate\.Methods: This paper introduces a novel biophysical paradigm, establishing that core cognitive and vocal sound units \(\\\(U\_\{s\}\\\)\) are synthesized through a dynamic, non\-linear superposition of two native internal fields: Biosonic Vibrations \(\\\(V\_\{bs\}\\\)\), representing structural mechanical, fluid, and bone\-conducted acoustic oscillations; and Bioneurosonic Vibrations \(\\\(V\_\{bns\}\\\)\), representing synchronized electrochemical neural network activity\.Results: By translating signal processing principles—historically anchored in telecommunications—into computational neuroscience, we mathematically formalize a state\-dependent phase modulation architecture\. This framework provides the quantitative baseline required to utilize focused external human vocal frequencies \(\\\(V\_\{ext\}\\\)\) via phase delay tuning \(\\\(\\Delta t\\\)\)\.Conclusion: The clinical implementation profiles demonstrate that calculated wave interference matrices can systematically yield constructive interference for localized thermal tissue ablation, or destructive interference for the complete neutralization of hyper\-synchronous neurological aberrations, such as epileptic focus discharges\.

## [Evaluation of breach and rheological parameters for self\-rescue zone \(ZAS\) definition of mining dams](../publications/7ca393e23f7496cb024e.md)

Pedro de Carvalho Thá; André Luiz Tonso Fabiani

Recent tailings dam failure in Brazil resulted in significant social, environmental and economic impact\. Following the failures, Brazilian regulation changed and demanded tailings dam breach analysis to consider Non\-Newtonian fluid behavior, where applicable\. However, in addition to rheology, other variables such as failure mode, breach hydrograph and Manning coefficient also influence tailings runout\. The objective of the present study is to evaluate the influence of rheological and breach parameters \(including failure mode\) on tailings runout and, especially, on self\-rescue zone \(ZAS\) definition\. The study evaluated tailings breach runout for four iron ore tailings dams located in Brazil\. Runout simulations considered different peak flow hydrographs for overtopping and piping, through Monte Carlo analysis\. For liquefaction a single hydrograph was considered\. Different combinations of hydrographs and rheology were evaluated, as well as Newtonian behavior \(water parameters\)\. Rheological parameters were taken specifically for one dam and from a database of 1162 vane rheometer tests in iron ore tailings and sediments for other three dams\. Manning coefficient variation was also evaluated\. Results were evaluated for four hydraulic variables along downstream path: frontal wave arrival time, time to peak, maximum wave velocity and height\. Comparison of results through Kruskall\-Walis test indicated that for most of the cases rheological parameters and Manning coefficient variation produced similar results\. Peak flow hydrographs influenced results significantly\. Self\-rescue zone downstream extent was only influenced by liquefaction failure mode\. Lateral extent of self\-rescue zone was only slightly influenced by rheology variation but was influenced by peak flow hydrographs\.

## [Genetic basis of phase amplitude coupling entrained by working memory](../publications/7cab45377036a2329368.md)

Anahita Nazari; Stefan Treue; Moein Esghaei

Abstract Working memory \(WM\) is a core determinant of cognitive functions, and its impairment is a hallmark of several psychiatric conditions\. Here, we investigated whether genetic factors contribute to WM performance\. Analyzing magnetoencephalography \(MEG\) data from the Human Connectome Project \(82 healthy adults: monozygotic \[MZ\] and dizygotic \[DZ\] twin pairs and unrelated \[UR\] pairs\) performing WM tasks, we observed that WM accuracy is markedly more similar within MZ twin pairs than in DZ or UR pairs, indicating a genetic contribution to WM performance\. To uncover a candidate neural mechanism for this genetic influence, we quantified phase\-amplitude coupling \(PAC\)—the modulation of high\-frequency amplitude by low\-frequency phase—and compared PAC patterns across individuals\. We define PAC alignment as the between\-individual similarity of PAC temporal patterns\. PAC alignment was significantly higher in MZ than in DZ or UR pairs and positively correlated with similarity in WM behavioral accuracy, linking PAC to behavior\. Together, these findings support PAC alignment as a candidate genetically influenced neural feature related to individual differences in WM\.

## [INTERPRETING RANKING MODELS: FROM FEATURE ATTRIBUTIONS TO MECHANISTIC COMPREHENSION](../publications/7cb49d98378041d064c8.md)

Tanya Chowdhury

The rapid adoption of Neural Ranking Models \(NRMs\) in Information Retrieval \(IR\) underscores the urgent need for robust interpretability methods to ensure their reliability and transparency\. Despite their widespread use, how NRMs model query\-document relevance remains poorly understood, limiting their application in high\-stakes domains\. This dissertation addresses this gap by developing generalizable, scalable, and theoretically grounded interpretability methods for ranking systems, spanning both post\-hoc feature attribution and mechanistic analysis of internal model structure\. First, we extend the Local Interpretable Model\-agnostic Explanations \(LIME\) framework to NRMs, proposing RankLIME\. This framework is able to generate local feature attributions for pointwise, pairwise, as well as listwise ranking models\. Using RankLIME, practitioners gain a scalable tool to interpret the individual contributions of features to the ranking decisions of complex neural models\. Next, recognizing the inconsistencies and contradictions in existing empirical ranking feature attribution methods, we adopt an axiomatic approach, establishing a set of fundamental principles that ranking\-based attribution methods should satisfy\. To this end, we introduce the RankSHAP framework, using the Shapley value from cooperative game theory\. RankSHAP ensures that feature attributions are generalizable, consistent, and aligned with human intuition\. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and diverse ranking models, coupled with a user study, validate the effectiveness of RankSHAP\. An axiomatic analysis further clarifies the compliance and deviations of other attribution methods relative to the proposed axioms, enhancing our understanding of their reliability\. Beyond feature attributions, this dissertation delves into the internal mechanisms of transformer\-based ranking LLMs to understand the abstract features these models internally encode to model relevance in ranking decisions\. Through a layer\-wise analysis of LLM neuron activations, we investigate whether known statistical and human\-engineered features—such as term frequency, inverse document frequency, and covered query term ratio—are embedded within network representations across different LLM configurations\. These findings provide insights into the internal workings of ranking LLMs, laying the groundwork for designing more transparent and effective ranking systems\. This dissertation further advances mechanistic interpretability by introducing a coalitional framework for studying how neurons cooperate within fine\-tuned ranking LLMs\. While prior analyses often treat neurons independently, empirical evidence suggests that task\-specific features in LoRA\-tuned models emerge through interactions among groups of neurons, particularly in mid\-layer MLP blocks\. To capture this structure, the dissertation models neurons as agents in a hedonic game, where preferences are defined by their synergistic contributions to layer\-local computations\. Using top\-responsive utilities and the PAC\-Top\-Cover algorithm, it identifies stable coalitions of neurons whose joint ablations produce non\-additive effects, and tracks how these coalitions persist, split, merge, or disappear across layers\. Applied to LLaMA, Mistral, and Pythia rerankers fine\-tuned for scalar output tasks, this framework discovers coalitions with consistently higher synergy than clustering\-based baselines\. By revealing higher\-order functional units beyond individual neurons, hedonic coalitions provide a new lens into how fine\-tuned language models encode task\-relevant features and computations\. Taken together, these contributions connect feature attribution, axiomatic analysis, probing, and coalition\-based mechanistic interpretability into a broader framework for understanding neural ranking systems\. More broadly, they point toward an emerging research agenda for the community: building a systematic science of reverse\-engineering large language models, with particular attention to the emergent features and statistical regularities encoded in their weights and internal computations, especially within MLP submodules\. Advancing this agenda will require weight\-based and mechanism\-based interpretability methods capable of recovering the latent priors, abstractions, and invariances that models internalize during training\. Such progress would not only deepen scientific understanding of how learning systems compress, organize, and represent knowledge, but also help extract actionable insights about the real\-world phenomena these models capture\. Ultimately, this dissertation contributes toward bridging interpretability and performance in neural ranking models, and toward a more principled foundation for transparent, accountable, and scientifically informative machine learning systems\.

## [Mapping of Textile Waste Management Techniques and Conversion Pathways: A Bibliometric Review](../publications/7cbbc85c3e707f0aab66.md)

Akhtarul Islam Amjad; Sameer Al‐Asheh; Nabil Abdel Jabbar

The global textile industry generates waste at multiple stages, including fiber production, fabric manufacturing, chemical processing, garment production, finishing, and post\-consumption\. This study examines approaches for effective textile waste management and maps them across stages of activity\. It includes two components: a bibliometric trend analysis and a review of developments, practices, and strategies in textile waste management and valorization\. The review identifies 2749 research articles and 988 distinct keywords, highlighting themes such as recycling, value\-added products, circular economy, and sustainability\. The study maps in\-process, after\-process, and post\-consumer waste within the supply chain or redirects it into value\-added products within a circular economy framework\. In some cases, textile waste is reused in production through reduction, reuse, and repurposing without recycling\. Recent research focuses on converting natural and synthetic textile waste such as fibers, yarns, fabrics, trims, and dyes into outputs including recycled fibers and fabrics, nonwovens, lactic acid, glucose, ethanol, biogas, char, and compost\. Mechanical recycling is gaining importance for post\-industrial waste\. When reuse or mechanical recycling is not feasible, chemical and biological treatments are applied\. Advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning support efficient sorting, waste prediction, and recycling processes\.

## [Musculoskeletal Disorders and Health‐Related Quality of Life Among Information Technology Professionals in the Post‐Pandemic Period: A Cross‐Sectional Occupational Health Study](../publications/7cbe809d23aacd508384.md)

Ramesh Chandra Patra; A\. Yashudas

ABSTRACT Background IT professionals face sustained ergonomic exposures, including prolonged sedentary behaviour, high screen time, and suboptimal workstation design, that intensified following pandemic‐driven shifts to remote and hybrid work\. These conditions predispose this occupational cohort to musculoskeletal disorders \(MSDs\) and impaired health related quality of life \(HRQoL\); however, population—specific evidence remains limited\. Objective To estimate 12‐month MSD prevalence and regional distribution among IT professionals, compare HRQoL across MSD and non‐MSD groups, and identify factors independently associated with MSDs\. Methods A purposive‐stratified cross‐sectional survey was conducted among 1568 full‐time or part‐time IT professionals \(aged 20–60 years\) recruited from corporate technology firms, software companies, BPO units, and remote working platforms across India with a response rate of 98%\. MSD prevalence and disability were assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire \(NMQ\); HRQoL was evaluated using the World Health Organisation Quality of Life \(WHOQOL‐BREF\) questionnaire\. Factors independently associated with MSD presence were identified through multivariable backward stepwise logistic regression \(Nagelkerke R 2 reported\); MSD severity—HRQoL associations were examined using linear regression\. Results The 12‐month prevalence of MSD was 71\.4%\. The neck \(59\.2%\), lower back \(53\.7%\), and shoulders \(46\.1%\) were most affected\. Multi‐regional involvement correlated with significantly greater disability \(6\.1 ± 2\.4 vs\. 4\.2 ± 1\.9; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The MSD group demonstrated markedly lower physical HRQoL \(48\.3 ± 13\.6 vs\. 71\.9 ± 12\.8; p &lt; 0\.001\), with significant differences across all WHOQOL‐BREF domains\. The strongest independent factors associated with MSDs were daily work &gt; 10 hours \(OR 2\.93, 95% CI 2\.10–4\.07\), poor ergonomic conditions \(OR = 2\.42, 95% CI 1\.99–2\.94\), and remote work modality \(OR = 1\.78, 95%CI 1\.42–2\.21; Nagelkerke R 2 = 0\.41\)\. Conclusion MSDs are highly prevalent among IT professionals and are independently associated with impaired HRQoL across all domains\. Poor ergonomic conditions, extended work hours, and remote work modality were independently associated with MSD presence and represent potentially modifiable workplace characteristics warranting further evaluation\.

## [StoBasket: Joint Upsell and Cross\-Sell Optimization for Contribution Margin](../publications/7cc0e1a1dd2116ff6ffa.md)

Xin Heng

Retail recommenders rank relevance, but retailers earn contribution margin: an upsell earns the margin difference over the item it replaces, whereas a cross\-sell earns its full margin\. We introduce joint stochastic basket editing, a formulation in which one policy selects replacement and addition offers for an existing basket, values them by expected incremental contribution margin, and couples them through displayed\-offer, accepted\-offer, and joint\-acceptance response channels\. To our knowledge, it is the first formulation in which upsell and cross\-sell responses are coupled; prior separable treatments are its zero\-coupling special case\. In real\-data\-calibrated simulations on five public basket datasets, StoBasket captures essentially all attainable offer margin: within 0\.5% in every default\-price setting and within 0\.7% when the true response lies outside its model family\. Correct economic accounting is the broadest gain: margin\-weighted popularity leaves up to 11% of attainable margin unrealized, and a published next\-basket recommender leaves 11\-52%\. Joint selection adds 10\.2% of attainable margin on Instacart, where premium tiers and add\-ons are strongly linked\. When offers pay only together, the best heuristics lose 64% while exact search stays within 0\.5%\. For a structured subclass, we characterize when staged policies fail and give an exact optimizer that solves every tested real basket in 0\.13 ms median and at most 111 ms\. Profit saturates long before prediction accuracy: a correctly structured predictor trained on 5,000 randomized sessions comes within 0\.06% of perfect prediction, while a signal\-free one loses 38%\. The same estimates yield a decision\-aware market\-basket analysis whose cost does not grow with association order\.

## [Creating a Learning Society in the Digital Era: Perspectives from Educational and Community Leaders in Banten, Indonesia](../publications/7cc1337657fbc98358c3.md)

Rudiyanto Dahlan

Background: The digital era presents unprecedented opportunities and challenges for establishing learning societies that support lifelong learning, digital literacy, and sustainable human capital development\. Educational and community leaders play pivotal roles in this transformation, yet their integrated contributions remain underexplored in emerging regional contexts\. Objective: This study aims to develop an integrated understanding of how educational and community leaders contribute to the creation of a learning society in the digital era, with specific focus on lifelong learning mechanisms, digital literacy initiatives, and human capital development pathways\. Method: A qualitative descriptive multi\-stakeholder inquiry was conducted with 28 participants including school principals, university leaders, community organization leaders, government representatives, and NGO officials from Banten Province, Indonesia\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews \(n=18\), focus group discussions \(n=3\), document analysis, and observation protocols\. Thematic analysis with source, method, and theory triangulation was employed\. Findings: Educational and community leaders jointly establish learning societies through five interconnected mechanisms: institutional learning infrastructure development, digital literacy ecosystems, collaborative knowledge\-sharing platforms, civic engagement frameworks, and capability development initiatives\. Leaders emphasized the necessity of integrating formal and informal learning, bridging digital divides, and fostering social capital through community engagement\. An Integrated Learning Society Development Framework emerged, highlighting the synergistic relationship between educational institutions, community organizations, and government agencies in facilitating sustainable human capital growth\. Novelty: This research uniquely positions learning society development as an educational\-community collaborative endeavor within the digital era context of emerging regional economies, departing from institution\-centric approaches that dominate current literature\. Implications: Findings provide strategic guidance for policymakers and institutional leaders in designing integrated learning society frameworks that harness digital technologies while maintaining social cohesion and equitable access to learning opportunities\.

## [Mapping the diverse trajectories of intrinsic capacity and their key drivers in China’s aging population](../publications/7cd8d00608d8fcef396c.md)

Ziyi Liang; Zhirou Liang; Linlin Xie; Keqing Liang; Jianxiong Hu; Sujuan Chen; Tao Liu; Jiagui Liang; Guanhao He; Fan Wu; Wenjun Ma

Background Intrinsic capacity \(IC\) is central to healthy aging\. Understanding its longitudinal change is crucial for proactive health planning\. Yet evidence on distinct IC trajectories and their determinants in China remains limited, constraining targeted interventions\. Methods We analyzed cohort data from participants aged 50 years and older in the World Health Organization’s Study on Global AGEing and Adult Health \(WHO\-SAGE\) China cohort\. A composite IC score was constructed based on the WHO framework, encompassing locomotion, cognition, psychological, sensory, and vitality domains\. We employed Latent Class Growth Analysis \(LCGA\) and Growth Mixture Modeling \(GMM\) to identify distinct IC trajectories\. Multinomial logistic regression was then used to investigate associations between these trajectories and a comprehensive set of socio\-demographic, individual health\-related, and environmental factors\. The relative importance of identified factors was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) values\. Results Four IC trajectories were identified: High and Stable IC \(HSI\), High and Slowly Declining IC \(HSDI\), Moderate and Rapidly Declining IC \(MRDI\), and Low and Rapidly Declining IC \(LRDI\)\. Older age \(OR = 5\.79, 95% CI 4\.73–7\.10\), female sex \(OR = 2\.86, 95% CI 2\.18–3\.75\), comorbidity \(OR = 8\.15, 95% CI 5\.07–13\.10\), low income \(OR = 4\.11, 95% CI 2\.82–5\.99\), low paternal education \(OR = 2\.04, 95% CI 1\.41–2\.94\), and higher physical risk scores \(OR = 1\.18, 95% CI 1\.02–1\.37\) were associated with a greater likelihood of belonging to the LRDI trajectory and were also associated with other unfavorable profiles\. Clean cooking fuel use \(OR = 0\.17, 95% CI 0\.11–0\.26\) and being married \(OR = 0\.53, 95% CI 0\.34–0\.82\) were associated with a lower likelihood of belonging to the LRDI trajectory\. SHAP identified age as the most influential contributor across all trajectories, while income, cooking fuel, ambient temperature, relative humidity, sex, education, and comorbidity also showed substantial contributions across different trajectory patterns\. Conclusion The study identified substantial heterogeneity in IC trajectories among Chinese middle\-aged and older adults\. Socio\-demographic, individual health\-related, and environmental factors were associated with distinct trajectory patterns\. Potentially modifiable contextual factors, particularly household cooking fuel and environmental conditions, may warrant greater attention in future healthy ageing strategies\.

## [Synthesis, Electrochemical Behavior, and Catalytic Activity of Cobalt Complexes of 5,15‐Diazaporphyrin and 5‐Monoazaporphyrin Derivatives Bearing Meso ‐Aryl Groups](../publications/7ce0885b060c1efa184c.md)

Momo Kaneko; Yui Wakasa; Mao Minoura; Ko Furukawa; Haruyuki Nakano; Yoshihiro Matano

ABSTRACT Cobalt \(Co\) complexes of porphyrin derivatives possess distinctive redox properties, and hence, their development has attracted significant interest across a wide range of fields\. Herein, we report the new examples of the Co complexes of 5,15‐diazaporphyrin \(DAP\) and 5‐monoazaporphyrin \(MAP\) derivatives bearing meso ‐aryl groups\. These Co complexes were prepared by metal‐templated cyclization of Co–bis\(dipyrrin\) complexes, complexation of azaporphyrin freebases with a Co salt, and meso ‐N‐functionalization of the Co complexes of DAP and MAP with diphenyliodonium hexafluorophosphate or methyl triflate\.
