## [EXPRESS: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Persistent Venous Narrowing of Downstream Parenchymal Microvessels and Pial Veins in the Male Mouse Cortex](../publications/7cf2f047f931ac3c998e.md)

Ako Miura; Hiroki Suzuki; Shuko Fujiki; Miyuki Unekawa; 裕 冨田; Iwao Kanno; Yoshikane Izawa; Jin Nakahara; Kazuto Masamoto

Chronic intermittent hypoxia \(IH\), a hallmark of sleep apnea, can lead to cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, though its precise impact on cerebral microcirculation remains unclear\. This study investigated the longitudinal effects of 2\-week chronic IH \(8% O2, 6\.5\-min cycle for 6 hours/day\) on brain microcirculation in the male mouse cortex\. We observed a significant reduction in the diameters of pial veins \(from 55 to 46 μm\) and parenchymal venules \(from 9\.9 to 8\.2 μm\) after chronic IH relative to pre\-IH conditions, while upstream arteries \(47 to 44 μm\) and arterioles \(12\.4 to 12\.0 μm\) were unaffected\. This selective reduction in downstream venule diameter led to a significant increase in arterio\-venous transit time, indicating reduced cerebral blood perfusion\. Furthermore, neurovascular coupling \(NVC\) responses showed a substantial decrease, pointing to impaired microvascular function\. Crucially, these neurovascular impairments were reversed by daily administration of an endothelin receptor antagonist during IH exposure, with the exception of pial vein constriction\. In conclusion, reduced cerebral perfusion after chronic IH is associated with persistent narrowing of parenchymal venules and pial veins\. These findings provide new insights into the cerebral microvascular complications of chronic IH and suggest the potential utility of neurovascular protective agents\.

## [A Revocable Certificateless Aggregate Signature Scheme with Efficient Invalid Signature Detection for Next Generation Vehicular Networks](../publications/7cf887f2cdc9fee030f0.md)

Anjali Bansal

Next\-Generation Vehicular Networks \(NGVNs\) rely on the continuous exchange of safety and traffic\-related information among vehicles and roadside infrastructure\. Ensuring the authenticity of these messages while maintaining low communication and computation overhead remains a critical challenge\. Although certificateless aggregate signature schemes provide an effective solution by eliminating certificate management and reducing verification costs, most existing approaches offer limited support for identifying invalid signatures within aggregated messages and handling vehicle revocation efficiently\. To address these issues, this paper presents a revocable certificateless aggregate signature \(RCAS\) scheme based on elliptic curve cryptography\. The proposed scheme avoids expensive bilinear pairing operations, making it suitable for resource\-constrained and latencysensitive vehicular environments\. An efficient invalid signature identification mechanism is incorporated to locate malicious signatures within an aggregate signature through a divide\-andconquer strategy, thereby reducing verification overhead\. In addition, a lightweight revocation framework based on a cuckoo filter is introduced to enable fast detection and exclusion of compromised vehicles\. The security of the proposed scheme is analyzed in the Random Oracle Model against both Type\-I and Type\-II adversaries\. Furthermore, performance evaluation demonstrates that the scheme achieves lower computational and communication costs while supporting efficient revocation and invalid signature detection\. These features make the proposed RCAS scheme a practical and scalable authentication solution for large\-scale next\-generation vehicular networks\.

## [Exploring the SMEFT landscape: Bayesian model selection for indirect discovery](../publications/7cfeab31220b5535dde8.md)

Luca Mantani

A bstract We develop a framework for indirect discovery in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory \(SMEFT\) based on Bayesian model selection over operator subsets\. We argue that SMEFT should be understood as a structured space of competing hypotheses rather than a single high\-dimensional model, with each operator subset corresponding to a physically distinct low\-energy realisation of new dynamics\. Bayesian inference is applied at the level of model space itself, assigning posterior probabilities to operator subsets and marginal inclusion probabilities to individual operators\. A genetic algorithm efficiently navigates the high\-dimensional discrete model space, concentrating evaluations in the high\-posterior region, while the Bayesian Information Criterion provides a tractable approximation to the Bayesian evidence\. We apply this framework to a dataset comprising electroweak precision observables from LEP and Higgs, top\-quark, and diboson measurements from LHC Run 2, at both linear and quadratic order in the Wilson coefficients, with one\-loop renormalisation group evolution systematically included\. The analysis finds no statistically significant evidence for any departure from the SM, and demonstrates that Bayesian Model Average posteriors on Wilson coefficients carry substantially improved characterisation potential compared to traditional global fits\. The operator correlation matrix encodes the relational structure of the model posterior, identifying operator pairs that co\-appear in high\-posterior models and flat directions where additional measurements would be most valuable\. The sensitivity of all results to the choice of matching scale μ 0 is assessed, and its promotion to a continuous parameter of inference is identified as a natural extension of the framework\.

## [Determinants and intensity of adoption of improved Robusta coffee in Uganda](../publications/7d10d1006c6f2ffd9a22.md)

robert sabiiti; Fredrick Bagamba; Rosemary Emegu Isoto; Fred Kwizabigira; Robert Basaza

While many tropical countries have intensified plant breeding to foster productivity and economic transformation, farmers’ technology adoption is still dismal\. Robusta coffee, Uganda’s top export crop, faces the same challenge, not yet conclusively addressed in scholarly literature\. This study examined the intensity of adoption determinants of improved Robusta coffee using five waves of the Uganda National Panel Survey data and a random\-effects Tobit model on an unbalanced pooled sample of 2037 household\-wave observations from 192 unique coffee\-growing households\. The results indicate that male\-headed households are significantly more likely to adopt\. Residing in the Western region increases the probability of adoption, whereas residence in the Eastern region reduces adoption\. Marital status was negatively associated with adoption\. An increase in wage by one unit reduces adoption by 3\.1% points, and an additional year of education reduces adoption by 0\.87% points\. Distance to the nearest murram road reduced the probability of adoption\. Gender and residence in the West were positively associated with adoption likelihood and adoption intensity\. On the other hand, residence in the East, marital status, and education negatively influenced adoption intensity\. Policies should promote labour\-saving innovations, gender inclusion, and infrastructure development\.

## [Expanding the Scope of Unit Transformation Graphs to Space and Measurement](../publications/7d11b71f3eeed8522523.md)

Joseph Antonides; Anderson Norton

Building models of students’ mathematics allows researchers to understand, appreciate, and build on students’ reasoning\. Grounded in Piagetian epistemology, unit transformation graphs provide a way to model students’ mathematics by explicating the mental actions that students use and coordinate in problem\-solving\. Prior research has focused on UTGs in numerical contexts, particularly fractions\. The purpose of this theoretical article is to expand the scope of UTGs to model students’ spatial comparison, enumeration, and measurement, by modeling students’ coordinations of numerical and spatial mental actions\. We illustrate this expansion with examples of one preservice elementary school teacher’s solutions to tasks involving 1D and 3D spatial quantities\. We conclude with implications for both theory and practice\.

## [Assessment\-guided Multi\-horizon LSTM for Dissolved Oxygen Risk Prediction in an AIoT Fish Nursery Decision Support System](../publications/7d1381234c7c2bd873cf.md)

Firda Amalia; Dewi Agushinta R\.; Sulistyo Puspitodjati; Syarifuddin Nasution

Fish nursery water\-quality management requires interpretable assessment and decision\-oriented risk information beyond sensor monitoring\.This study develops an assessment\-guided multi\-horizon dissolved oxygen \(DO\) prediction approach within a Decision\-Ready AIoT DSS\.Primary IoT data \(5,376 observations, four pond/species contexts\) were transformed using suitability, excursion, and stability features to evaluate eleven configurationsmatched LSTM/GRU pairs, two reimplemented 2024\-style baselines, and a PatchTST\-lite Transformer comparatorfor 15\-60 minute DO forecasting\.Repeated across five seeds, Raw LSTM attained the lowest RMSE \(0\.335±0\.015 mg/L\), while Full Assessment\-Guided LSTM attained the highest decision accuracy among the LSTM configurations \(0\.929±0\.010\)\.PatchTST\-lite achieved RMSE 0\.369±0\.033mg/L, recall 0\.864±0\.060,and decision accuracy 0\.926±0\.006acompetitive Transformer benchmark without universal dominance\.The proposed DSS translates assessment and forecast outputs into risk status, recommendations, and NLPbased explanations for human\-in\-the\-loop nursery management\.

## [Machine Learning Versus Traditional Statistical Models for Emergency Department Volume Forecasting](../publications/7d20c7d94cc1964f54b5.md)

Kian Huang; Enola R\. Okonkwo; Haris Choudhary; Rahul Suresh Mhaskar; Nathan Lapaix; Michael Lozano; Reginald Saint\-Hilaire

Introduction: Emergency department \(ED\) crowding harms patient care and strains hospital operations\. Forecasting daily patient arrivals can help ED medical directors, department chairs, and hospital administrators plan staffing and bed capacity in advance, rather than reacting after a surge has already occurred\. This study compared five computer\-based forecasting methods, including three machine learning models \(eXtreme gradient boosting \[XGBoost\], light gradient boosting machine \[LGBM\], and long short\-term memory \[LSTM\]\) and two traditional statistical models \(autoregressive integrated moving average \[ARIMA\] and seasonal ARIMA \[SARIMA\]\), to determine which most accurately predicts ED patient volume seven days in advance, using eight years of daily visit data from an academic freestanding ED\. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 3,202 consecutive days of daily patient volume \(March 27, 2017, to December 31, 2025\) from an academic freestanding ED with approximately 31,102 annual visits\. Each model used the preceding 365 days of data to forecast the subsequent 7 days, repeated across the study period to reflect the weekly cycle by which most EDs plan staffing\. Our primary measure of accuracy was mean absolute error \(MAE\), defined as the average number of patients per day by which a forecast missed the actual volume\. Secondary measures included root mean squared error \(RMSE\), mean absolute percentage error \(MAPE\), the coefficient of determination \(R², a score from 0 to 1 reflecting how well predictions tracked actual day\-to\-day volume\), and the percentage of forecasts accurate within 5, 10, 15, and 20 patients, thresholds selected for their relevance to staffing decisions\. The best\-performing model on initial metrics, XGBoost, served as the reference model for statistical comparison using the Diebold\-Mariano \(DM\) test, which determines whether an observed difference in accuracy between two models is statistically meaningful or attributable to chance\. Results: Among 453 rolling weekly forecast windows, SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM demonstrated the lowest absolute errors and best forecasting of patient volume, with MAE values of 9\.60 \(95% CI, 9\.29–9\.91\), 9\.61 \(95% CI, 9\.31–9\.91\), and 9\.64 \(95% CI, 9\.33–9\.94\) patients/day, respectively; these three models therefore missed the actual daily patient count by approximately 9 to 10 patients, on average\. Models ARIMA and LSTM were less accurate, with mean MAE values of 10\.54 \(95% CI, 10\.21–10\.87\) and 12\.01 \(95% CI, 11\.63–12\.39\) patients per day\. Relative to the XGBoost reference \(MAPE 13\.82%\), ARIMA \(MAPE 14\.93%\) and LSTM \(MAPE 17\.27%\) showed a marked decrease in predictive accuracy\. For operational planning, the top\-performing models \(SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM\) correctly predicted daily volume within a margin of 20 patients in 90\.3% to 90\.6% of instances, while LSTM performed less well and reached this threshold in only 83\.3% of forecasts\. Statistical testing confirmed these differences were unlikely due to chance, with XGBoost significantly outperforming ARIMA \(DM = −6\.09, P &lt; \.001\) and LSTM \(DM = −6\.96, P &lt; \.001\)\. Conclusion: Models SARIMA, XGBoost, and LGBM performed comparably well, and all three would provide reliable, operationally useful forecasts for ED staffing and resource allocation decisions\. A traditional statistical method, SARIMA, which is simpler and less resource\-intensive to implement, performed as well as the newer machine learning methods evaluated in this study\. This finding suggests that hospitals do not necessarily need to invest in more complex artificial intelligence tools to obtain accurate ED volume forecasts\.

## [Biochemical Parameters Associated With COVID\-19 Severity: A Statistical Analysis](../publications/7d2fcbf7e3ce7abbf77f.md)

Shivaswamy Umamaheshwari; Nisarga Hosaholalu Puttaraju; Mahadevaiah Neelambike Sumana; Anilkumar Kodidela; Chaithra Nagaraju

Objectives Coronavirus disease 2019 \(COVID\-19\), caused by the SARS\-CoV\-2, is a contagious infectious disease\. The aim of the present study is to identify the most effective biochemical parameters associated with COVID\-19 severity\. Early identification of these parameters is crucial for rapid risk stratification of patients and for initiating timely clinical management\. Material and Methods A total of 584 patients with COVID\-19 admitted to a tertiary care hospital in Mysuru, Karnataka, were included in the study\. The routinely measured biochemical parameters obtained after hospital admission were evaluated for their association with the study outcome\. Descriptive statistics, independent sample t \-test, Pearson’s correlation analysis, binary logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analysis were performed at a 5% level of significance using IBM SPSS Statistics version 22\. Results Demographic and clinical characteristics showed that male patients, 427 \(73%\) and older adults aged 60–80 years, 157 \(48\.5%\), constituted the largest proportion of hospitalised patients with COVID\-19\. A higher proportion of male patients was observed in both the ICU 16 \(2\.74%\) and non\-ICU 411 \(70\.38%\) groups\. Correlation analysis demonstrated mild to moderate associations among selected biochemical markers\. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, serum creatinine was the only biochemical parameter significantly associated with the study outcome \(OR = 0\.265; p = 0\.027\) and also demonstrated acceptable discriminatory performance in the ROC analysis\. Conclusion Early identification of biochemical abnormalities improves clinical prognosis by enabling timely risk stratification and appropriate therapeutic intervention\. These findings support the routine assessment of biochemical parameters as part of the initial evaluation of patients with COVID\-19\.

## [GESTÃO EMPRESARIAL, INOVAÇÃO E ESTRATÉGIA COMPETITIVA: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA E RECONFIGURAÇÃO DAS CAPACIDADES ORGANIZACIONAIS](../publications/7d3110efb14e6f153a8d.md)

Alcimar de Lima Marques Filho; Anna Cristhina Barbosa Massulo; Davi da Costa Almeida; Ernanda da Silva Moura; Marcos Galvão Marinho; Mário José da Silva; Silvya Karen de Carvalho Martins; Talyta Rocha da Silva; Valdenilson de Souza Ribeiro; Weuler Arce

A rápida disseminação da Inteligência Artificial Generativa \(IAG\) amplia possibilidades de produção e recombinação de conteúdo, apoio à inovação e suporte a atividades decisórias, mas não implica, por si só, vantagem competitiva\. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar como a IAG pode influenciar a reconfiguração das capacidades organizacionais, examinando suas implicações para a inovação e para a estratégia competitiva empresarial\. Trata\-se de um ensaio teórico\-conceitual, de natureza exploratória e descritiva, sustentado por revisão narrativa estruturada e busca dirigida de atualização bibliográfica, articulando a Resource\-Based View, a teoria das capacidades dinâmicas e estudos contemporâneos sobre transformação digital e IAG\. A síntese teórica indica que o valor estratégico potencial da IAG depende de mecanismos intermediários, entre eles integração humano–IA, aprendizagem organizacional, gestão e recombinação do conhecimento, redesenho de processos, desenvolvimento de competências e governança\. Propõe\-se um framework no qual a IAG interage com recursos humanos, tecnológicos e informacionais e pode favorecer, sob condições organizacionais específicas, a reconfiguração de capacidades, a inovação e a criação de valor\. O artigo contribui ao distinguir adoção tecnológica de apropriação estratégica e ao posicionar capacidades organizacionais como elo explicativo a ser testado entre IAG e resultados competitivos\.

## [On the possibilities and limitations of LLM\-based multi\-agent systems for multi\-criteria decision\-making in healthcare operations management](../publications/7d38ab052e444457da2e.md)

Marco Boresta; Tommaso Giovannelli; Sepehr Namirad; Giulia Riccardi

Multi\-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify\. Teams of large language model \(LLM\) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them\. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM\-generated preferences as inputs to multi\-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions\. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade\-offs from the agents&\#x27; pairwise choices between emergency department configurations\. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic&\#x27;s operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them\. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents&\#x27; implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents&\#x27; choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone\. We then formulate robust weighted\-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty\. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights\. These results indicate that LLM\-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support\.

## [Emerging Technology\-Supported Intercultural Learning for Cognitive, Attitudinal, and Behavioral Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Three\-Level Meta\-Analysis](../publications/7d4f2967eeb5de8a0b63.md)

Yuteng Wang; Junjie Gavin Wu; Danyang Zhang

Emerging technologies are increasingly used to support intercultural learning, yet evidence on the distinct effects of artificial intelligence \(AI\), augmented reality \(AR\), and virtual reality \(VR\) remains limited\. This systematic review and three\-level meta\-analysis synthesized 17 studies published from 2020 to July 2026 \(77 effect sizes\) to examine cognitive, attitudinal, and behavioral outcomes\. The overall effect was large and significant \(Hedges’ g = 0\.965, 95% CI \[0\.580, 1\.350\], p &lt; \.001\), although heterogeneity was substantial\. AI\-supported interventions also showed a significant positive pooled effect \(g = 1\.150, 95% CI \[0\.744, 1\.555\], p &lt; \.001\)\. AR showed a significantly larger estimated effect than VR \(β = −1\.481 for VR relative to AR, p = \.017\), but this difference was not robust to excluding one AR study\. Academic level \(F \(1, 75\) = 17\.27, p &lt; \.001\) and sample size \(F \(2, 74\) = 3\.873, p = \.026\) were significant moderators, with larger effects in K–12 and larger\-sample studies\. However, these exploratory comparisons involved uneven technology distributions and only two K–12 studies\. Outcome domain did not significantly moderate effects\. Sensitivity analyses supported the stability of the overall pooled effect\. The findings indicate that emerging technologies can improve intercultural learning, while better\-balanced comparative studies are needed to identify which technological approaches are most effective\.

## [RAG\-RST: Retrieved Exemplars as In\-Context Discourse Schema for RST Parsing](../publications/7d50c4bf0e4720373d04.md)

Mohammadreza Sediqin; Shlomo Engelson Argamon

In Rhetorical Structure Theory \(RST\), each edge of a discourse tree carries a nuclearity label, marking which span holds the central content, and a relation drawn from a closed inventory of functional categories\. Neither label is a surface property: the same two clauses can be Elaboration or Background depending on rhetorical intent, and the boundary between them is fixed by annotation convention rather than by lexical cues\. Predicting these labels therefore requires a formal discourse schema, and exposure to discourse\-rich pretraining text does not supply it: given only a target EDU pair, a strong LLM recovers nuclearity at 0\.794 F1 and relation at 0\.738 F1\. We propose RAG\-RST, a retrieval\-augmented framework that supplies this schema as in\-context demonstration rather than through parameter updates, raising nuclearity to 0\.846 F1 and relation to 0\.788 F1 with no training\. Two configurations are compared: a precomputed strategy that labels all EDU pairs before parsing, and a dynamic strategy that retrieves at each reduce step, so that the exemplars reaching the generator depend on the reductions the parser has already committed to\. Both outperform existing RST parsers across span, nuclearity, relation, and full tree metrics, with the dynamic variant consistently strongest\. Two properties of the retrieved schema emerge: its utility is bounded in number, saturating and then declining beyond fifty exemplars, and it depends on structural position\. Both indicate that a formal linguistic schema can be supplied to a foundation model as a demonstration rather than trained into its parameters\.

## [DEVELOPMENT OF THE “E\-XIZMAT” SOFTWARE TOOL TO IMPROVE THE EFFICIENCY OF SOCIAL SERVICES PROVIDED TO THE POPULATION](../publications/7d5cb97ad86f79959ac7.md)

Shodiyev Laziz

This scientific paper analyzes the development and implementation of the &quot;E\-Xizmat&quot; software solution designed to improve the efficiency and transparency of social public services\. Following the IMRAD structure, the study examines conventional bottlenecks in social assistance delivery, including bureaucratic latency, human bias, paper\-based workflows, and fragmented data\. The proposed system is architected upon modern microservices patterns, secure RESTful APIs, and robust data protection standards integrated with national registries\. Experimental validation demonstrates an average 75% reduction in application turnaround time, higher operational transparency, and increased citizen satisfaction\.

## [Maximizing Yield While Preserving Bioactive Volatiles in Cinnamon Essential Oil: Response Surface Optimization of Hydrodistillation and Microwave‐Assisted Extraction](../publications/7d78d5a355afd75209c2.md)

Mariana C\. Pedrosa; Joana Soares Amaral; Sandrina Alves Heleno; Manuela Pintado; Lillian Barros; Márcio Carocho

ABSTRACT Essential oils derived from plants are secondary metabolites that can act as antioxidants and antimicrobial agents\. Combined with consumer pressure for natural products, these compounds may be suitable as preservatives in food products and the extraction is essential for obtaining high‐quality oil\. For this purpose, hydrodistillation and microwave‐assisted extraction were compared and optimized to produce cinnamon \( Cinnamomum verum J\. Presl\) EO using response surface methodology\. A Box–Behnken design was applied to hydrodistillation, considering extraction time, solid‐to‐liquid ratio, particle size, and soaking time, while microwave extraction combined a fractional factorial screening with a subsequent Box–Behnken design, including solid‐to‐liquid ratio, time, and microwave power as factors, excluding soaking time\. For hydrodistillation, quadratic models for global yield and volatiles were significant, with satisfactory diagnostic statistics, and the optimal conditions \(240 min, 125 g/L, 1\.0 mm\) yielded 7\.16 mg of oil per g of sample, corresponding to a 0\.716% yield and 0\.578% of volatiles\. For microwave extraction, the model for global yield was adequate showing borderline significance but acceptable predictive metrics, and \(100 g/L, 40 min, 300 W\) yielded 18\.95 mg oil /g \(1\.895% yield\) and 1\.527% of volatiles\. Gas chromatography coupled to a mass spectrometer analysis revealed that hydrodistillation produced a more terpene‐rich oil, whereas microwave extraction yielded an essential oil strongly enriched in \(E\)‐cinnamaldehyde\.

## [The role of professional learning communities in teacher implementation of problem\-based learning in teaching senior high school mathematics](../publications/7d79112b228d079f04d8.md)

Rose Ampomah; Benjamin Adu Obeng; Francis Ohene Boateng

Problem\-Based Learning \(PBL\) is increasingly recognised as an effective approach for promoting students&\#x27; critical thinking, problem\-solving, and conceptual understanding in mathematics\. Although PBL is emphasised in the Ghanaian Senior High School mathematics curriculum, its classroom implementation remains limited, and empirical evidence on the role of Professional Learning Communities \(PLCs\) in supporting it is scarce\. This study examined the extent to which PLCs are associated with teachers&\#x27; implementation of PBL\. An explanatory sequential mixed\-methods design was adopted\. Data were collected from 86 mathematics teachers and school administrators in three public Senior High Schools using a structured questionnaire \(83 valid responses retained for quantitative analysis\), followed by semi\-structured interviews with 15 teachers\. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression, and qualitative data were analysed thematically\. Participants reported high levels of PLC participation \(M = 3\.47\) and PBL implementation \(M = 3\.48\)\. The five PLC dimensions jointly predicted PBL implementation, R² = \.424, F\(5, 77\) = 11\.345, p &lt; \.001\. Shared Mission, Vision and Values, Collective Responsibility for Student Learning, and Collective Inquiry were significant individual predictors\. Interviews indicated that PLCs were associated with collaborative lesson planning, professional dialogue, reflective practice, and teachers&\#x27; confidence in implementing PBL, while inadequate time, limited instructional resources, and insufficient institutional support constrained implementation\. Effective PLCs are associated with teachers&\#x27; greater capacity to implement PBL in Senior High School mathematics\. Strengthening PLC activities through continuous professional development, structured collaboration, and adequate resource provision is recommended to support sustained PBL implementation\.

## [Biodegradation of Trimethoprim by a Bacterial Consortium Enriched from a Sewage Treatment Plant](../publications/7d87627fa2a1d33d8918.md)

Tristan Nilsson; Bliss N\. Broussard; Darcey G\. Wayment; Himanshu S\. Raje; Ramaraj Boopathy; Achmad Syafiuddin

Antibiotic resistance is a persistent public health concern\. The excessive use of prescription antibiotics in medical and animal husbandry practices has resulted in potentially harmful levels of antibiotic residues in the environment\. Antibiotics released through excreta and industrial effluents exert selective pressure on environmental bacteria, promoting the proliferation and accumulation of antibiotic\-resistant bacteria\. Diverse microbial communities exhibiting antibiotic resistance may also serve as effective antibiotic degraders\. Sewage treatment plants are among the environments most conducive to the development of microbial communities capable of degrading antibiotics\. This study focused on Louisiana because it ranks among the five U\.S\. states with the highest antibiotic use\. Trimethoprim \(TMP\) is one of the commonly prescribed antibiotics\. The purpose of this study was to investigate the presence of TMP\-degrading microbial communities in a small community sewage treatment plant\. Sludge was collected from the anaerobic digester at the Thibodaux sewage treatment plant, and a microbial consortium was subsequently enriched\. The consortium was cultivated with TMP under various growth conditions\. TMP degradation was analyzed using high\-performance liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry\. The results showed that the consortium was capable of degrading TMP under co\-metabolic conditions, with 4\-desmethyl trimethoprim identified as a major metabolite\. The dfrA12 and dfrA5 genes, which are associated with TMP resistance, were detected in DNA isolated from the consortium\.

## [Sodium perborate tetrahydrate modulates neuroinflammation and reduces Leishmania infantum infection in astrocytes](../publications/7d96b4f9cc546e9b0b37.md)

Zeynep İşlek; Hatice İlke Özeken; Hazal Uraz; Mehmet Hikmet Üçışık; Rengin Reis; Ezgi Taşkan; Fikrettin Şahi̇n

Abstract Leishmaniasis is a neglected tropical disease caused by protozoan parasites of genus Leishmania \. Although the parasites are classically considered macrophage\-resident pathogens, accumulating evidence suggests that Leishmania can cross the blood–brain barrier and induce neurological manifestations, referred to as cerebral leishmaniasis\. Astrocytes, which are key regulators of central nervous system immune homeostasis, remain poorly characterized in the context of Leishmania infection\. In this study, we investigated neuroimmune\-based antileishmanial effects of sodium perborate tetrahydrate \(SPT\) in Leishmania infantum \-infected murine astrocytes\. SPT concentrations between 25 and 150 µM maintained astrocyte viability above 90% for 24–72 h\. Flow\-cytometric analysis demonstrated that the astrocyte infection rate, which was approximately 23% in the untreated group at 24 h, significantly decreased following SPT treatment\. At 72 h, infection rates ranged from approximately 4–7% in the SPT\-treated groups\. SPT significantly reduced intracellular oxidative stress by lowering reactive oxygen species levels to 17–29% relative fluorescence intensity compared with untreated infected cells, while simultaneously increasing intracellular glutathione levels\. Gene expression analysis demonstrated modulation of inflammatory mediators, including upregulation of IL\-12B at 100 µM and TNF\-α at 200 µM, along with downregulation of IL\-10 , indicating a shift towards a pro\-inflammatory host\-protective response\. Together, these findings provide in vitro evidence that SPT reduces L\. infantum infection and modulates redox and inflammatory responses in C8\-S astrocytes\. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the antileishmanial and immunomodulatory effects of SPT in an in vitro model of L\. infantum \-infected astrocytes\.

## [AI driven health monitoring with indoor localization using geomagnetic sensor fields and WLAN data fusion](../publications/7d9a0455d8dc6ce1b55e.md)

Pooja Narasimhan; Anuhya Arun; R\. Parvathi; V\. Pattabiraman

Indoor localization is a new technology to monitor of the health condition movements of individual patients that can be accomplished with the assistance of AI driven approach with the multimodal data fusion, i\.e\. geomagnetic sensors fields – accelerometers, gyroscopes, magnetometers and Wi\-Fi signals\. The current methods have three key limitations: \(i\) no robust cross\-modal interaction modelling, \(ii\) low sensor\-noise and environment\-variable adaptability and \(iii\) no integrated health\-conscious mobility tracking\. The concept of finding the location of a person or item in a confined space where GPS signals cannot be used is known as indoor localization\. Wi\-Fi RSSI, inertial measurement units \(IMU\) and geomagnetic sensors have become the multimodal data fusion that has demonstrated great power in enhancing localization accuracy\. This work employs two combinatorial architectures, a hierarchical clustering tree \(HCT\) fusion model model used for fine\-grained hierarchical representation and a RF dominant ensemble used for generalization under sensor noise and variability\. The hierarchical clustering tree \(HCT\) based approach proposed in this study can achieve a classification accuracy of 91\.73%, and its macro F1 score is 0\.9173 in the next\-room prediction task its mean absolute error \(MAE\) in the travel time prediction task is 2\.87 s\.

Heart rate variability \(HRV\) is widely recognized as a key mechanism that contributes to several health outcomes\. We provide a broad overview of HRV, its clinical and translational relevance, and important factors to consider when measuring HRV in research endeavors\.

## [Exploring the Impact of Self\-Efficacy on Career Future Perception](../publications/7db2e854662dd29c782d.md)

Sezin Karabulut Çakır

The primary aim of this study is to examine the effect of self\-efficacy on the perception of career future\. For this purpose, the concepts addressed in the study were examined within the framework of the relevant literature, and the extent to which these concepts are related to each other was investigated\. In line with the conducted literature review, a research model was developed based on the hypothesis that self\-efficacy may have a positive effect on the perception of career future\. To test the model, data obtained from 144 students who took the elective university course &quot;Career Planning&quot; during the 2025\-2026 fall semester at Atatürk University were analyzed using appropriate statistical methods\. University elective courses include subjects that can be taken by students from any department and chosen based on their areas of interest\. In this sense, the study was conducted on the assumption that the students who selected the Career Planning course are interested in the subject and have a high level of awareness regarding career planning\. The results show that students’ level of self\-efficacy has a positive effect on their perception of career future\.

## [Применение искусственного интеллекта в финансовом инжиниринге](../publications/7db38ceac5d5fb7ef984.md)

Cândido Coxi КОШИ КАНДИДО

В статье рассматриваются направления применения искусственного интеллекта \(ИИ\) в финансовом инжиниринге – при проектировании, оценке и хеджировании финансовых инструментов, построении портфелей и управлении рисками\. На основе обзора научной литературы и данных Банка России систематизированы основные классы задач, в которых методы машинного обучения дают преимущество перед классическими моделями, и показаны ограничения их использования\. Установлено, что в 2025 г\. ИИ на постоянной основе применяли 21 % опрошенных российских финансовых организаций, ещё 15 % тестировали пилотные проекты\. Сделан вывод о том, что ИИ не заменяет финансовую теорию, а расширяет инструментарий финансового инженера, однако требует развития систем управления модельным риском и объяснимости моделей\.

## [Intelligence artificielle et gestion des finances des organisations en Afrique subsaharienne : opportunités, risques et enjeux de gouvernance](../publications/7db652a5baf6f300aa7c.md)

MONLANDJO Eric Sedjolo Sylvanice

L&\#x27;intelligence artificielle \(IA\) occupe désormais une place centrale dans la transformation des pratiques managériales à l&\#x27;échelle mondiale\. En Afrique subsaharienne, son déploiement progressif s&\#x27;inscrit dans une dynamique plus large de transition numérique, portée par l&\#x27;entrepreneuriat technologique, la digitalisation des services financiers et la quête d&\#x27;efficience organisationnelle\. Parmi les fonctions les plus affectées, la gestion financière constitue un pilier stratégique de la gouvernance d&\#x27;entreprise et de la pérennité organisationnelle\. Dans un contexte africain structurellement marqué par la prépondérance des petites et moyennes entreprises \(PME\), la persistance d&\#x27;une économie informelle et la fragilité relative des dispositifs de contrôle interne, l&\#x27;IA se présente à la fois comme un vecteur de modernisation et une source de nouvelles vulnérabilités\. Cet article s’interroge sur la question suivante : dans quelle mesure l&\#x27;intelligence artificielle transforme\-t\-elle la gestion des finances des organisations en Afrique subsaharienne, et sous quelles conditions son adoption peut\-elle constituer un levier de performance durable et de bonne gouvernance, plutôt qu&\#x27;un facteur aggravant de fragilité organisationnelle ? Adoptant une posture épistémologique positiviste aménagée et une démarche mixte, cette recherche s&\#x27;appuie sur une enquête par questionnaire conduite auprès de 78 professionnels exerçant des fonctions financières en Afrique subsaharienne, complétée par une analyse qualitative des réponses ouvertes et une revue systématique de la littérature\. Les résultats révèlent que si la notoriété de l&\#x27;IA est largement répandue \(91 %\), son adoption opérationnelle demeure embryonnaire \(25 %\)\. Les usages observés, concentrés dans les fonctions comptables, prévisionnelles et de contrôle interne, témoignent d&\#x27;une transformation essentiellement procédurale plutôt que stratégique\. Par ailleurs, l&\#x27;absence de cadres formels de gouvernance \(80 % des organisations\) et les insuffisances de compétences \(45 %\) exposent les organisations à des risques non maîtrisés\. L&\#x27;analyse inférentielle ne révèle, dans cet échantillon, aucune association statistiquement significative entre l&\#x27;adoption et les variables organisationnelles classiques — taille, chiffre d&\#x27;affaires, expérience —, suggérant une diffusion encore opportuniste et non institutionnalisée\.

## [Real\-world evaluation of a multilingual agentic retrieval\-augmented clinical AI framework for evidence\-grounded medical decision support](../publications/7dbe688a125cfa96cb32.md)

Mohammad Mehdi Imani; Mohammad Hasannejad; Amir Hossein Imani; Mojtaba Shafiekhani

Large language models may support clinical information tasks, but hallucination, limited evidence traceability, and inconsistent workflow integration remain barriers to clinical deployment\. We evaluated Dr\.Copilot, a multilingual retrieval\-augmented clinical AI framework combining hybrid evidence retrieval, specialized tools, and model\-directed orchestration\. During a 70\-day deployment, 835 registered users generated 956 conversation threads; the analytics log contained 22,574 events and 4,226 tool\-use events\. In the original 64\-prompt expert benchmark, Dr\.Copilot and GPT\-5\.5 had comparable weighted scores \(4\.607 vs\. 4\.561; paired difference 0\.046, 95% CI \-0\.064 to 0\.140; p = 0\.103\)\. In a new independent 75\-case, fixed\-backbone external validation, Dr\.Copilot scored 4\.557 versus 4\.217 for GPT\-5\.5 \(difference 0\.340, 95% CI 0\.181 to 0\.519; p = 0\.00023\), with fewer clinically important errors \(5/75 vs\. 16/75; p = 0\.00098\)\. A 30\-case four\-arm GPT\-5\.4 ablation found the highest mean score with standard RAG \(4\.813\), while additional prespecified\-tool and model\-directed routing conditions did not yield uniform further gains\. Targeted safety, pediatric, multilingual, citation, temporal, and abstention analyses identified both strengths and important failure modes\. These findings support retrieval as the clearest incremental contributor in this evaluation, while underscoring that agentic tool orchestration requires direct validation and does not itself establish clinical benefit or patient\-safety improvement\.

## [Mental Physics\. Neurocybernetics and Psychoacoustics of the Liquid Cooling Environment in a Data Center: The Impact of mCDU Infrastructure Vibration and Noise on Cognitive Processes and Thermodynamic Isomorphism\.](../publications/7dc4c27389d698a5c256.md)

Rajmund Olszewski

Abstract\. This paper investigates the impact of the unique vibroacoustic environment in modern high\-density data centers\-shaped by high\-speed server fans and mCDU/CDU circulation pumps\-on the human nervous system and cognitive processes\. This phenomenon is analyzed at the intersection of acoustic physics and neurocybernetics\. The analysis demonstrates that overlapping frequency bands \(broadband aerodynamic noise &gt;250 Hz and structural hydraulic pulsations 50\-100 Hz\) induce effects of sensory isolation, stochastic resonance, and vibroacoustic entrainment within the cognitive apparatus\. Furthermore, the study highlights a strict isomorphism between predictive algorithms controlling mCDU circuits and the allostatic hemodynamics of the human brain\. Within the framework of Embodied Cognition theory, it is shown that long\-term engineering exposure to thermodynamic parameters, noise variance, and fluid dynamics realigns the operator&\#x27;s cognitive schema from a reactive to an anticipatory model, fostering advanced Systems Thinking\.

## [Collective action and livelihood transformation among Farmer Producer Organizations \(FPOs\) in Jharkhand: a multivariate integrated modelling framework identifying key drivers](../publications/7dc889507c980f40a165.md)

Sumit Maitra; Hari Charan Behera; Rahul Kumar; Keshav Sawarn; Rabindranath Jana; Kuntal Ghosh; Tarun Kabiraj

Farmer Producer Organizations \(FPOs\) have emerged as important institutional mechanisms for improving smallholder livelihoods in India, yet evidence on their broader socio\-economic impacts remains limited, particularly in regions such as Jharkhand\. This study examines the factors shaping farmer participation and success within FPO systems using data from 498 farmers\. The findings reveal a dominant dimension of livelihood improvement characterized by gains in living standards, nutrition, and technological adoption\. Agricultural income and institutional capacity, particularly training and exposure, are consistently associated with higher levels of success\. Distinct farmer typologies indicate that stronger institutional engagement is linked with better outcomes, even among farmers with relatively limited resources\. Overall, the results highlight that livelihood transformation within FPO systems extends beyond income growth and is closely associated with sustained capacity\-building and institutional support\. The study underscores the need for context\-specific, capacity\-oriented policy interventions to enhance the effectiveness and long\-term sustainability of FPO\-led rural development, contributing to broader efforts toward inclusive and resilient rural transformation\.

## [Oxytocin receptor signaling in the dorsal lateral septum is essential for social transmission of food preference in mice](../publications/7dc8d29ad71ca181a295.md)

Hanyu Fu; Zhiqiu Liu; Jingwei Zhou; Luyao Zhang; Cai Liu; Dewei Tang; Shuangshuang Zhang; Anan Li; Dejuan Wang

Social learning is a fundamental adaptive strategy that critically shapes decision\-making and feeding behaviors\. Through the social transmission of food preference \(STFP\), animals acquire information about food safety via social interactions, forming a food\-odor memory that overrides innate preferences and guides subsequent food preferences\. However, the neural mechanisms through which social cues durably influence feeding preferences remain unclear\. Here, we identify the lateral septum \(LS\) as a key node in STFP\. We show that LS neuronal activity increases following social learning and reliably distinguishes between socially cued and uncued foods\. Chemogenetic inhibition of the dorsal LS \(dLS\), but not the ventral LS \(vLS\), abolishes STFP\-driven food preference, revealing subregional specificity within the LS\. Furthermore, oxytocin receptor \(OXTR\) signaling within the dLS is required for STFP in mice, where it enhances neuronal excitability through PLC pathway activation\. Together, our results reveal a subregion\-specific circuit mechanism through which the dLS integrates social information with feeding motivation, and highlight oxytocinergic modulation as a key mediator of socially guided food preferences\.

## [ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio\-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves](../publications/7dc9e4c88b61010b115d.md)

Abeer Mostafa; Zahra Ahmadi

Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing\. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph\. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain\. Directly extending this operator&\#x27;s receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures\. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf\. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio\-temporal sheaf network with two key components\. First, Transitional Restriction Maps \(TRM\) decompose each node&\#x27;s restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence\. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter \(DSF\) applies a single bounded\-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio\-temporal sheaf operator\. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio\-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state\-of\-the\-art baselines\. The code is available at: https://anonymous\.4open\.science/r/ChronoSheaf\-1D7D/\.

## [Real\-world discrimination and incremental value of first\-trimester placental growth factor for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a retrospective Chinese cohort](../publications/7dca04e2a3725fd5b026.md)

Lingling Jiang; Minxia Chai; Yuan Xia

Background Placental growth factor \(PlGF\) contributes to first\-trimester screening algorithms for preeclampsia, but its prognostic performance as an isolated biomarker in routine Chinese care is uncertain\. Methods We performed a retrospective, single\-centre cohort study among pregnancy episodes recorded in a hospital PlGF workbook\. Pregnancy episodes were deduplicated, PlGF values were traced to source laboratory cells, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy \(HDP\) were ascertained using unvalidated free\-text discharge\-diagnosis keywords\. The primary operational window was 9 \+ 0 to 13 \+ 6 weeks; 11 \+ 0 to 13 \+ 6 weeks was evaluated separately\. We compared PlGF with a parsimonious maternal\-characteristics model containing age, pre\-pregnancy body mass index \(BMI\), and nulliparity\. Results From 405 source rows, 380 pregnancy episodes were resolved; 310 met the primary criteria, including 27 HDP events \(11 cases of preeclampsia and 16 of gestational hypertension\)\. PlGF alone had an area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.633 \(95% bootstrap CI 0\.523–0\.738\), and internally derived PlGF multiple of the median \(MoM\) had an AUC of 0\.636 \(0\.533–0\.740\)\. In 308 complete records, the maternal\-characteristics model had an apparent AUC of 0\.740 \(0\.635–0\.837\), while adding log10\(PlGF\) yielded an AUC of 0\.748 \(0\.638–0\.849\); paired ΔAUC was 0\.009 \(95% CI −0\.019 to 0\.037\)\. Conclusion The findings are consistent with a modest association between lower first\-trimester PlGF and subsequent HDP, but they do not support isolated clinical use or a deployable prediction model\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Eurasian Higher Education: An Empirical Study of Student Practices](../publications/7dcf47571560e6673460.md)

Shamil Sheymardanov; Muhamad Hariz Muhamad Adnan; Timur Mufazalov

Generative artificial intelligence has penetrated higher education not through official strategies but via students’ and faculty members’ personal devices, catching most universities off guard\. This article presents empirical data from a large\-scale survey conducted between March and April 2026 across six post\-Soviet countries \(Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Tajikistan\)\. The study provides a systematic cross\-national analysis of student AI use patterns in the Eurasian higher education space, complementing recent single\-country studies in the region\. The sample included 478 students\. The study measured frequency of AI use, perceived risks, compatibility with educational values, and the presence of institutional regulatory mechanisms\. The results show that 78 % of students regularly use generative AI, yet only 32 % of universities have an official policy in this area\. A deep disciplinary divide emerges: students fall into two roughly equal profiles – “pragmatic techs” \(daily users with low ethical anxiety\) and “reflective humanists” \(cautious users with a strong demand for ethical frameworks\)\. The main barrier to AI adoption is not technological infrastructure but the absence of regulatory and social technologies\. The article offers discipline\-differentiated recommendations for universities in non\-Western contexts\.

## [Boundary Detection for High\-Dimensional Point Clouds](../publications/7dd197e7477194f8fedf.md)

Abigail Hickok; Valerio Galanti; Osama Al Dalahmah; Andrew J\. Blumberg

We introduce two new methods for boundary detection in high\-dimensional point cloud data, intended to work in situations with non\-uniform density, high ambient dimension, and substantial noise\. Our first method fits a separating hyperplane on local neighborhoods after doing local dimension reduction\-\-\-this method works best when one can reliably estimate the intrinsic dimension of the data\. Our second method measures the directional uniformity of local neighborhoods, and has the best overall performance on synthetic data\. In addition to pointwise numerical boundary scores, our algorithms yield an estimated normal vector at each boundary point\. We validate our methodology on synthetic data as well as two real examples: we analyze spatial transcriptomics data, where we show that we can detect the boundary of a tumor, and we also study LLM activation geometry\.

## [Psychometric properties of the self\-reflection and insight scale \(revised\) in German\-speaking clinical psychology trainees](../publications/7dd3066acd39225f5c09.md)

Theresa Hanke; C Müller; Johanna L\. Popp; Martin Weiß; Greta Hanke; Kristin Herrmann

Introduction Self\-reflection is a core competency for clinical psychologists and mental health professionals\. Given its essential role in clinical practice and personal development, it is important to assess self\-reflective capacity reliably and efficiently\. This study aimed to translate and examine the psychometric properties of the Self\-Reflection and Insight Scale\-Revised \(SRIS\-R\) for use in German\-speaking contexts\. Methods The SRIS\-R was translated using a back\-translation procedure\. A total of 257 participants completed the questionnaires via an online survey\. Results Both the original 14\-item factor structure and revised German model solutions were tested\. Confirmatory factor analyses indicated that the original English factor structure could not be satisfactorily replicated in the German sample\. Therefore, exploratory factor analyses using polychoric correlations were conducted and suggested structural differences in the German version\. Based on these findings, a parsimonious revised 13\-item two\-factor scoring solution and a methodologically refined two\-factor model including a cross\-loading and a residual correlation were examined\. The modified 13\-item version showed improved internal consistency \(α = 0\.86 for Self\-Reflection and α = 0\.84 for Insight\)\. The parsimonious revised 13\-item scoring solution retained the conceptual distinction between Self\-Reflection and Insight while being feasible for practical questionnaire scoring\. Convergent and discriminant validity evidence supported theoretical associations of Self\-Reflection with related constructs, particularly self\-insight and reflection, whereas Insight showed negative associations with rumination and private self\-consciousness\. Additional ESEM analyses supported a two\-factor representation while indicating relevant item\-level cross\-loadings\. The 13\-item structure was subsequently tested without modification in an independent sample \( N = 161\), showing comparable model fit and high factorial similarity across samples\. Multigroup analyses further supported scalar invariance across the two samples\. Together, these findings provide cross\-sample support for the distinction between Self\-Reflection and Insight, while indicating remaining structural complexity at the item level\. Given the limited support for a general factor, interpretation of the two subscale scores rather than a total score is recommended\. Discussion However, further research is needed to replicate the revised structure in broader and more diverse German\-speaking samples\. A culturally adapted and efficient measurement, like the one presented here, is essential for fostering and assessing self\-reflective skills in clinical professionals\.

## [Temperature\-Field Reconstruction and Heat\-Source Inversion Estimation Method for High\-Voltage Switchgear Based Reduced\-Order PINN Surrogate Model](../publications/7dd720daa529eb5498b5.md)

Shengxue Tang; Xiang Zheng; Er\-Peng Wang; Songyang Han; Yize Cheng

Abstract Localized overheating induced by poor electrical contact, loosened busbar connections, and insulation degradation is a major precursor to failures in high\-voltage switchgear\. To address the difficulty in directly measuring internal heat sources, a fast three\-dimensional temperature\-field reconstruction, candidate heat\-source identification, and heat\-source power inversion method for high\-voltage switchgear is proposed based on a reduced\-order surrogate model integrating Proper Orthogonal Decomposition \(POD\) and physics\-informed neural networks \(PINNs\)\. First, a coupled three\-dimensional thermal–flow coupled computational fluid dynamics\(CFD\) model is established to generate temperature fields under different heat\-source conditions\. POD is then applied to extract the dominant thermal modes and their corresponding low\-dimensional modal coefficients from the high\-dimensional temperature fields\. A PINN\-based reduced\-order surrogate model is subsequently trained to establish the nonlinear mapping from heat\-source parameters to POD modal coefficients, while residuals of the steady\-state heat conduction equation and boundary\-condition constraints are incorporated into the loss function to enforce physical consistency and enhance prediction accuracy\. Based on external temperature measurements, an Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer \(I\-GWO\) is further adopted to identify the active fault heat source from a predefined set of candidate locations and inversely estimate its corresponding heat\-source power\. Numerical simulations and temperature\-rise experiments show that the proposed method accurately reconstructs the three\-dimensional temperature distribution and identifies local high\-temperature regions\. In the temperature\-rise experiment, the relative error of heat\-source power inversion is only 2\.27%, demonstrating that the proposed framework enables rapid and accurate temperature\-field reconstruction and heat\-source inversion\.

## [Research Trends in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and Allergic Diseases: A Bibliometric Analysis \(1994–2025\)](../publications/7de4f58b12dfaa97b75d.md)

Fatma Çiftçi; Oğuzhan Koyuncu

Aim: Attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\) and allergic diseases research has expanded rapidly, yet its global structure and hotspots remain fragmented\. This bibliometric analysis maps ADHD, allergic diseases, and asthma/atopy research to identify publication growth, influential sources, collaboration patterns, and emerging themes\.Method: A Web of Science Core Collection search was conducted on 9 January 2026\. English\-language articles and reviews published between 1994 and 2025 were included, yielding a total of 244 records\. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny was used for descriptive indicators and thematic mapping, and VOSviewer for co\-authorship, co\-citation, and keyword co\-occurrence networks\. Keywords and thematic evolution analyses were applied to detect shifts in ADHD and allergic diseases topics over time\.Results: The dataset comprised 244 publications across 168 sources and 1,306 authors \(mean 6\.32 authors/document\), with 20\.81% international co\-authorship\. Annual production increased markedly after 2015, peaking in 2021–2023\. Source analyses showed concentration in a limited set of core journals, while co\-citation patterns confirmed an interdisciplinary base spanning pediatrics, psychiatry, and allergy/immunology\. Keyword mapping highlighted persistent links between ADHD and asthma, atopic dermatitis, and allergic rhinitis, alongside emerging interest in inflammation\-related and life\-course topics\.Conclusion: ADHD–allergic diseases research is growing and increasingly interdisciplinary, with rising emphasis on mechanistic and inflammation\-oriented themes\. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal and causal designs and broaden international collaboration to strengthen clinical relevance\.

## [Use of firsekibart for acute gouty arthritis in a maintenance hemodialysis patient with multiple high\-risk comorbidities: a case report](../publications/7dea92bb0395c5698fb9.md)

Jiaqi Chen; Ruoyu Tong; Meng Shen; Weidong Zhang; 黄远航

Objective To describe the clinical course of Firsekibart treatment for acute gouty arthritis in a 51\-year\-old patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis with multiple high\-risk comorbidities, focusing on the temporal relationship among dialysis, drug administration and the timing of symptom changes\. This report adds to the limited evidence on using Firsekibart, a novel fully human monoclonal antibody targeting IL\-1β, in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis\. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the patient’s underlying diseases, acute gout manifestations, timing of Firsekibart administration relative to hemodialysis, visual analogue scale \(VAS\) pain scores, body temperature, and inflammatory markers\. The clinical course was interpreted in the context of available clinical evidence on Firsekibart, experience with other IL\-1 pathway agents in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and/or receiving dialysis, and monoclonal antibody pharmacokinetics\. Results Pain relief was documented 6–7 h after Firsekibart administration, before the first post\-dose hemodialysis session; however, tramadol and topical flurbiprofen had been administered within the preceding hour and may have contributed to the observed improvement\. No worsening or rebound of pain was observed on the day of dialysis or the following day\. No immediate hypersensitivity reaction was observed during the early post\-dose period\. Follow\-up continued through 24 June 2026 \(35 days post\-dose\), no gout flare recurred; however, biliary symptoms and a febrile episode with suspected catheter\-related bloodstream infection occurred, with uncertain relationships to Firsekibart\. Conclusion In this maintenance hemodialysis patient, gout\-related pain improved before the first post\-dose dialysis session and did not rebound after dialysis\. However, this single case, without pre\- or post\-dialysis Firsekibart concentration measurements, cannot establish causality or determine the effect of hemodialysis on drug exposure\.

## [Mapping Public Policy and Governance Research in Indonesia: A Bibliometric Analysis](../publications/7df4cd055ba538dc06de.md)

Basuki Basuki; Suswanta Suswanta

This study maps the development of public policy and governance research in Indonesia by examining publication trends, thematic patterns, research actors, and keyword relationships\. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus\-indexed publications within the defined study period\. Following a PRISMA\-based selection process, 52 documents were included in the final corpus and analyzed using VOSviewer and Microsoft Excel\. The analysis examined publication trends by year, country, author, and affiliation, as well as keyword cooccurrence and overlay patterns\. The findings show that research on public policy and governance in the selected corpus has expanded in recent years, with prominent themes including collaborative governance, public policy, regulation, environmental governance, community participation, and sustainable development\. The keyword network identifies seven thematic clusters, indicating that governance research in the corpus spans collaborative, regulatory, communitybased, regional, environmental, and institutional dimensions\. The overlay analysis further indicates changes in the prominence of research themes across publication years\. The findings provide a bibliometric map of the structure and thematic development of public policy and governance research associated with Indonesia and identify areas that may inform future research agendas

## [Genetic programming control of quasiperiodic and chaotic oscillations in a thermoacoustic system](../publications/7e00fe9421e757a61fed.md)

Bo Yin; Zhijian Yang; Yu Guan; Stéphane Redonnet; Vikrant Gupta; Larry K\.B\. Li

Self\-excited thermoacoustic oscillations remain a key obstacle to low\-emission combustion, especially in time\-aperiodic regimes where quasiperiodic and chaotic dynamics hinder conventional controller design\. We experimentally demonstrate data\-driven suppression of such aperiodic thermoacoustic oscillations in a flame\-driven Rijke tube using genetic programming \(GP\)\. In closed\-loop form, the GP\-discovered control laws are static nonlinear feedback maps that generate, in real time, actuation commands from a sensor signal\. Performance is evaluated by a cost function that penalises both the thermoacoustic amplitude \(state cost\) and the actuation effort \(input cost\), enabling efficiency comparisons\. We benchmark GP closed\-loop control \(GCC\) against GP open\-loop control and conventional open\-loop harmonic forcing\. In the quasiperiodic regime, all three strategies achieve nearly 90 percent sign 90 % $90\\,\\%$ amplitude reduction, but the closed\-loop strategy is the most efficient\. The low\-amplitude controlled state is dominated by a preferred \(high\-gain\) mode of the open\-flame describing function, and can persist even after control deactivation, indicating basin\-of\-attraction switching\. In the chaotic regime, GCC again outperforms both open\-loop strategies, achieving the largest thermoacoustic amplitude reduction with minimal actuation effort\. Synchronisation analysis reveals phase trapping, drifting and locking between pressure and heat\-release\-rate fluctuations, while the 0–1 test and complexity–entropy diagnostics reveal that the GP\-suppressed state retains measurable signatures of deterministic chaos\. Overall, this study shows that GP control can provide an efficient model\-free tool for suppressing aperiodic thermoacoustic oscillations by autonomously exploiting high\-receptivity flame pathways with state\-dependent actuation\.

## [Benzoylaconine suppresses colorectal cancer progression by modulating the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis](../publications/7e00ffd4216704a3820b.md)

李丰衣; Ke Zhang; Miao Wang; Liya Su; Ling Yang

Background Colorectal cancer \(CRC\) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management\. Owing to their multi\-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery\. Benzoylaconine \(BAC\) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti\-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined\. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets\. Methods HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems\. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound\-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry\. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein–protein interaction network\. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2\. RNA\-seq identified differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways\. Western blotting validated key protein changes\. Patient\-derived CRC organoids \(PDOs\) were established to evaluate BAC efficacy; organoid viability was assessed by CellTiter\-Glo® 2\.0 assay, and morphology by bright\-field microscopy\. Results BAC dose\- and time\-dependently inhibited CRC cell proliferation and EdU positivity, slowed wound closure, and reduced Transwell invasion, indicating impaired migration and invasion\. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that BAC induced G1/S cell cycle arrest and apoptosis\. Network pharmacology identified CDK2 and MMP2 as key targets; molecular dynamics and SPR confirmed stable binding \(KD ≈ 3\.9 and 4\.4 μM\)\. RNA\-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and tumor invasion\. Western blotting revealed that BAC dose\-dependently downregulated CDK2, CDK6, MMP2, Cyclin E1, and Cyclin D1, and upregulated p21\. BAC also inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer organoids\. Conclusion BAC induces G1/S cell cycle arrest in CRC cells, likely through modulation of the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis, thereby suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis, and may represent a promising lead for CRC therapy\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial en el desarrollo socioemocional en estudiantes con necesidades específicas de apoyo emocional: estudio de caso en Tecnópolis Guayaquil – 2025\.](../publications/7e081e6b51fa05da8fd3.md)

Oscar Rafael Guillen Valle; Vanessa Sabina Saenz Gandarillas

El presente estudio de caso cualitativo, realizado con cinco estudiantes de Tecnópolis Guayaquil con necesidades específicas de apoyo emocional, tuvo como objetivo describir e interpretar la influencia de la inteligencia artificial en su desarrollo socioemocional\. La información se recopiló mediante entrevistas semiestructuradas en profundidad y observación participante\. Como fuentes complementarias, se emplearon un diario de campo y registros anonimizados de uso de la plataforma de inteligencia artificial\. Los resultados evidenciaron una influencia ambivalente: la IA favoreció la autoconciencia y la regulación emocional, pero también se observaron riesgos de dependencia tecnológica y una menor conexión interpersonal en algunos participantes\. Se concluyó que sus beneficios dependen del acompañamiento pedagógico intencional, de políticas institucionales claras y de la formación docente\. Dado que se trató de un estudio de caso cualitativo con cinco participantes, los hallazgos se circunscriben al contexto analizado y no pretenden generalizarse a otras poblaciones\.

## [DFAS\-AML: An Integrated Conceptual Governance Framework for Ethical, Explainable, and Sovereign\-Sensitive AI in Anti\-Money Laundering Systems](../publications/7e245d94a5f3ef49e475.md)

Hasan Mohamed husain Alaali

Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in anti\-money laundering \(AML\) systems, yet improved analytical capability does not by itself ensure explainability, accountable human intervention, ethical resilience, jurisdiction\-sensitive processing, or decision traceability\. Existing research and regulatory instruments address these concerns but remain fragmented across technical, legal, organizational, and data\-governance domains\. This study adopts a normative conceptual and design\-oriented methodology\. It synthesizes peer\-reviewed research and authoritative regulatory instruments, translates identified governance problems into operational requirements, derives corresponding governance mechanisms, and evaluates the resulting architecture through conceptual coherence, functional completeness, traceability, regulatory relevance, sovereign adaptability, operational interpretability, and illustrative stress scenarios\. The analysis identifies five interdependent governance requirements: explanation governance, accountable human override, ethical resilience, sovereign calibration, and controlled decision traceability\. These requirements are integrated into the Dynamic Financial Applied Meta\-Science for Anti\-Money Laundering \(DFAS\-AML\) through five coordinated components: A\-AMLEEF, A\-AMLOCC, A\-AMLD, A\-SCEAML, and A\-AMIL\. The principal analytical finding is that effective governance of AI\-enabled AML requires governance of the complete decision lifecycle rather than the detection model alone, linking explanation adequacy, ethical and jurisdictional assessment, authorized intervention, institutional action, and tamper\-evident decision reconstruction\. DFAS\-AML provides an AML\-specific governance architecture that integrates functions otherwise addressed across separate governance domains\. It complements rather than replaces existing AML and AI\-governance instruments and does not establish empirical effectiveness\. The architecture remains conceptually evaluated and requires subsequent expert, institutional, empirical, and regulatory validation\.

## [Potencial turístico de Cumandá como territorio emergente frente a Baños de Agua Santa como destino consolidado](../publications/7e2840a15fa487bc507f.md)

Freddy Leonardo Garaicoa Fuentes; Edwin Stalin Vinueza Garcia; Dayana Yamileth López Domínguez; Jorge Alberto Meléndez Mendoza; Luis Felipe Mestanza Yanez; Danna Niyeiri Guerrero Goya

El objetivo fue analizar el potencial turístico de Cumandá y contextualizar sus condiciones de articulación territorial frente a Baños de Agua Santa\. Se realizó una revisión integrativa con síntesis cuantitativa descriptiva y análisis temático de fuentes secundarias\. El corpus incluyó 22 artículos publicados entre 2021 y 2025, un referente metodológico de 2005 y 11 documentos técnicos, normativos o institucionales, para un total de 34 referencias\. La evidencia se organizó mediante una matriz de 25 indicadores en cinco dimensiones: recursos, accesibilidad, servicios, comercialización y gobernanza\. Para Cumandá se identificaron inventarios de diferente cobertura, diez puntuaciones individuales de atractivos y cuatro rutas propuestas\. El promedio descriptivo de las diez puntuaciones fue 66,62, sin representar un índice del cantón\. Baños aportó registros administrativos de establecimientos y gestión presupuestaria, no directamente equivalentes a los de Cumandá\. Los hallazgos distinguen recursos identificados, productos formulados y operación comprobable, preservando períodos, unidades y datos faltantes\. Se concluye que Cumandá dispone de recursos naturales y culturales y antecedentes de articulación turística; su consolidación requiere conciliar inventarios, verificar servicios y evaluar el funcionamiento de las rutas, sin trasladar automáticamente el modelo de Baños\.

## [Insights from the Indonesian Family Life Survey, Fifth Wave: Job Demands\-Resources Profiles and Their Links to Mental Health](../publications/7e29210c54b2a1b7e338.md)

Fuad Hamsyah; Ramadhan Dwi Marvianto; Ridwan Saptoto

The Job Demands\-Resources \(JD\-R\) model explains how job demands and job resources shape workers&\#x27; psychological well\-being through a health impairment process and a motivational process\. JD\-R research in Indonesia has largely relied on variable\-centered approaches, which assume additive and uniform effects of demands and resources, overlooking how these factors combine differently across individuals\. This study identified latent worker profiles based on five JD\-R indicators \(wage adequacy, working hours, employment status, number of jobs, and social security\) and examined their links to depressive symptoms and life satisfaction, using data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey \(IFLS\-5\), with a final sample of 2,023 formal\-sector workers\. Latent class analysis identified three profiles: Fully Resourced \(29\.3%\), Adequate but Contract\-Vulnerable \(47\.6%\), and Under\-Resourced \(23\.1%\), consistently distinguished by job resources rather than job demands\. Membership in both the low\-resource and high\-resource profiles was significantly associated with depressive symptoms, whereas only the most fully resourced profile was associated with higher life satisfaction\. These findings indicate that job resources have a direct and differentiated effect on mental health, suggesting that labor policy should consider the configuration of job resources holistically\.

## [Quantized Mereology](../publications/7e313198cf724ce9284a.md)

Thomas Bittner

This paper investigates quantized mereology, which merges quantum information theory with classical mereology, the formal analysis of the part\-whole relationship\. It emphasizes that information about crisp mereological relations is captured by classical bits, whereas mereological vagueness involves the use of quantum bits, or qubits, to capture mereological information\. Transitioning from classical bits to qubits offers a new understanding of part\-whole relations among entities that are subject to mereological vagueness\. This paper methodically studies the quantized mereology that arises from the classical RCC5 formalism, one of the most widely studied formalisms in Qualitative Reasoning \(QR\), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence\. The argument is made that this method can be extended to quantize more sophisticated QR formalisms, mirroring how strategies are used in physics to transition from classical to quantum systems\. The study explores: \(i\) the conversion of bits to qubits while understanding that these \(qu\)bits convey mereological information; \(ii\) the representation of qubit states via set partitions, acknowledging that set theory aligns more closely with classical logic than with the complex vector spaces employed in quantum physics; \(iii\) demonstrating that classical QR formalisms can be seen as special cases within quantized formalisms; and \(iv\) showing that qubits more effectively encapsulate information about vague phenomena\.

## [The state of library publishing in the health sciences in the United States and Canada](../publications/7e3fb276200d219c3733.md)

Gina Genova

Objective: Publishing initiatives led by academic libraries have grown over the past decade\. They are often involved in the development of innovative publishing models and open initiatives, and a number of library publishers have worked in the health sciences\. This study aims to assess the current state of library publishing in the health sciences \(HS\)\. Methods: The Library Publishing Directory survey and Library Publishing Coalition&\#x27;s member directory were accessed to identify active library publishing programs in the U\.S\. and Canada\. Survey responses on disciplinary specialties and top publications were assessed, and individual publisher websites were accessed to inventory HS titles\. Journals were checked for whether they were actively publishing and indexed\. Results: One hundred eighteen survey respondents and 24 additional LPC members were assessed\. Twenty\-five percent of respondents named an HS subject as a disciplinary specialty, and 20% named an HS title as a top publication\. Two hundred seventy\-five individual HS titles from 81 different library publishers were identified\. Fifty\-three percent were journals, 39% open education resources, and 8% monographs\. Medicine was the most common field for publications\. Seventy\-three percent of journals were actively publishing\. Of those, 42% were indexed in DOAJ or a major HS database, and just over 10% appeared in PubMed or Scopus\. Conclusions: Library publishers have a track record of working with a wide variety of HS researchers\. Indexing of library\-published journals is an area for improvement\. HS librarians may be able to collaborate with their institutions&\#x27; publishing programs to further develop these services and build relationships with researchers\.
