## [Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell\-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease](../publications/7e5a408ad2e8111e0dc2.md)

Girish Kumar Srivastava; Priyank Shukla; Sara Crespo Millas; Yogeswaran Lokanathan

Retinal degenerative diseases, including age\-related macular degeneration \(AMD\), retinitis pigmentosa \(RP\), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people\. Cell\-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells \(iPSCs\), retinal pigment epithelium \(RPE\) transplantation, and CRISPR\-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function\. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long\-term outcome monitoring\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\), encompassing machine learning \(ML\), deep learning \(DL\), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations\. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell\-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off\-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and post\-transplantation monitoring through multimodal retinal imaging\. Throughout, we distinguish direct retinal cell\-therapy evidence from retinal\-adjacent, cross\-domain, and conceptual evidence\. We also propose an AI\-powered end\-to\-end pipeline that connects patient profiling through gene editing, cell production, and transplantation to longitudinal outcomes tracking \(a forward\-looking framework that needs to be clinically validated in future\)\. While AI offers powerful tools to enhance efficacy, reproducibility, and personalization, it does not replace the clinical and biological foundations of cell therapy\. Critical challenges remain, including data scarcity, algorithmic interpretability, regulatory compliance, and clinical validation\. This review concludes that the strategic integration of AI has plausible potential to become supportive infrastructure for scalable and reproducible cell\-based treatments for retinal diseases, although its necessity has not been demonstrated and prospective clinical validation is still required, and biological insight and rigorous empirical verification remain fundamental\.

## [Temporal and production\-related determinants of microbial counts in pingo, the natural starter culture of minas artisanal cheese](../publications/7e63a4a69e72cdcf5808.md)

Gustavo Augusto Lacorte; Daniel Arantes Pereira; Joao Paulo Andrade de Araújo; Danielle Stornino de Freitas; Gabriel Henrique Oliveira Silva; Jaqueline Flaviana Oliveira de Sá; Jonas e Silva Guimarães; Milene Therezinha das Dores; Fernanda Faria QUADROS

Minas Artisanal Cheese \(MAC\) is among the most widely consumed and recognized artisanal cheeses in Brazil, produced from raw milk, rennet, salt, and a natural starter culture known locally as pingo\. Pingo is an endogenous starter culture generated by backslopping, which carries into MAC cheese both technologically beneficial microorganisms and spoilage contaminants\. Studies addressing the microbial diversity of MAC have accumulated in recent years, yet few have examined the composition of the microorganisms present in pingo or the factors that may influence microbial loads in this endogenous culture\. Here we analysed 200 pingo samples from 50 cheesemaking units distributed across all MAC producing microregions, collected over four six\-monthly campaigns\. Lactic acid bacteria \(LAB\), total coliform, Staphylococcus aureus, and yeast/mould counts were estimated, and pH and NaCl concentration were determined\. Linear mixed\-effects models showed that LAB counts remained similar across sampling campaigns, although counts on MRS agar were associated with production scale and pingo volume\. Total coliform counts in pingo were approximately tenfold higher during the wet season, whereas yeasts/moulds counts were associated with both season and sampling campaign\. The effect of season on S\. aureus depended on the year: counts did not differ between seasons in 2024 but were higher in the dry season in 2025\. Smaller cheesemaking units additionally showed lower S\. aureus counts in pingo\. Milking infrastructure, pH, and NaCl concentration showed no association with the counts of any microbial group investigated\. Our results revealed that the wet season is a period of elevated risk for the occurrence of potentially spoilage\-causing microorganisms, irrespective of the scale of the cheesemaking unit and of the robustness of the installed milk production infrastructure\.

## [Youth Voices on Contribution: A Study of Iranian Youth](../publications/7e63d8dac4e960c64c53.md)

Kimia Shirzad; Kimia Shirzad; Kosar Shirzad; Kosar Shirzad; Pete Allison; Nicole S\. Webster; Jennifer P\. Agans

This study explores how Iranian adolescent girls conceptualize and practice contribution, a core component of the Positive Youth Development \(PYD\), within this politically restrictive, collectivist context\. Semi\-structured interviews with 13 girls \(ages 14 to 17\) were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis\. Four themes emerged: cultural values shaping contribution, contribution beyond formal structures, contribution as resistance, and drivers and barriers to contribution\. Participants described contribution as everyday moral and relational practices rooted in empathy, shared struggle, and responsibility toward others\. Findings challenge Western\-centric PYD frameworks and highlight the need for a culturally grounded understanding of contribution that accounts for structural conditions and sociopolitical agency\.

## [Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability](../publications/7e753f12228b5ef95576.md)

Tianyu Wu

Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept\. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? We develop four executable operations for changing physical descriptions: identifying redundancies \(L1\), coarse\-graining dynamics \(L2\), transferring structure \(L3\), and inferring missing quantities from conservation imbalances \(L4\)\. We evaluate these operations and three interpretability settings through null acceptance \(NAR\), positive acceptance \(PAR\), and consequence agreement \(CAR\)\. A reduction mapping every state to zero predicts its own future perfectly\. It passes closure on 96% of 129 public chaotic systems despite retaining no dynamical variation\. An independent observable\-preservation test rejects it throughout\. On controlled benchmarks, the combined criteria accept 24/24 genuine reductions and reject 72/72 nulls\. The other operations distinguish symmetries from redundancies, validate transfers, and reject spurious conservation imbalances\. In language and ESM\-2 protein models, linear CKA remains unchanged when a proposed correspondence is randomly rotated, whereas localized interventions distinguish genuine mappings from tested nulls\. In sparse autoencoders, enrichment rejects all 16 tested nulls, yet independent ablation supports 45% of evaluable enriched features, compared with 0\.5% of matched controls\. These results reveal two acceptance gaps: descriptive tests can accept scientifically empty candidates, and accepted candidates can lack independently verified consequences\. Reliable automated discovery requires evaluating both what a test accepts and the scientific consequences it establishes\. Code and data: https://real\-project\-aether\.github\.io/project\-aether/\.

## [AI\-Assisted Image\-Based Lichen Health Assessment for Environmental Sensing Using Naturally Acquired Field Images](../publications/7e771db35ff0abe4be55.md)

Andrew Wang; Wei Li

Lichens are widely recognized as biological indicators of environmental quality because their physiological condition reflects long\-term atmospheric and ecological changes\. However, conventional lichen assessment relies primarily on manual visual inspection by trained specialists, limiting the scalability of environmental monitoring\. This paper presents an AI\-assisted image analysis framework for automated lichen health assessment using naturally acquired field images as a step toward intelligent environmental sensing\. A dataset consisting of 140 images of Lobaria pulmonaria was collected from the public iNaturalist database and manually annotated according to health and moisture conditions\. An end\-to\-end framework integrating dataset construction, image augmentation, deep feature learning, health classification, and quantitative evaluation was developed and evaluated using stratified five\-fold cross\-validation\. Binary health assessment achieved an average classification accuracy of 82\.1%, while binary moisture and four\-class lichen\-status classification achieved accuracies of 75\.7% and 64\.3%, respectively\. To further evaluate the robustness of the proposed framework, representative convolutional neural network, transformer\-based, and classicalmachine learning classifiers were compared under an identical experimental protocol, with EfficientNet\-B0 achieving the highest overall performance\. The results demonstrate that AI can reliably assess lichen health from naturally acquired field images and further reveal that environmental moisture introduces substantial visual ambiguity for automated health assessment\. This work establishes a practical and reproducible baseline for future AI\-assisted environmental sensing, ecological monitoring, and image\-based environmental bioindication\.

## [Gastric cancer peritoneal metastases as an immune compartment: immune evasion, systemic immunotherapy and regional treatment strategies](../publications/7e79e054ce1d42551bb0.md)

Eoghan P\. Burke

Gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis \(GCPM\), particularly associated with diffuse and poorly cohesive cancers, in which tumour cells grow singly or in small, loosely associated groups, presents an anatomical and immunological treatment challenge\. This review examines the peritoneal surface and surrounding fluid as an interacting immune compartment comprising tumour implants, malignant ascites, free tumour cells, stroma and immune populations\. Human studies identify cytotoxic\-cell depletion or exhaustion, macrophage\-rich ascites and suppressive soluble mediators; experimental findings support complement\-pathway involvement in immune\-checkpoint ligand expression\. These observations offer a biological explanation for impaired local immunity but do not establish clinical resistance to checkpoint inhibition\. Systemic therapy remains the treatment backbone, yet pivotal trials rarely report the Peritoneal Cancer Index \(PCI\), cytology, ascites response or peritoneal\-specific progression\. Early studies combine checkpoint blockade with pressurised intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy \(PIPAC\), repeated intraperitoneal paclitaxel or hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy \(HIPEC\); direct intraperitoneal antibodies, cytokines and cellular therapies are also under investigation\. Feasibility and local pharmacodynamic changes do not establish synergistic benefit\. Future trials should compare an added intraperitoneal treatment against an otherwise identical systemic regimen, collect matched blood, ascites and peritoneal tissue samples over time, and relate immune changes to cytological clearance, PCI, symptoms and survival\. Operative consolidation requires a separate randomised assessment in prospectively defined responders\. Treatment continuity, quality of life, nutrition and hospital\-free survival are essential measures of net benefit\.

## [Transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker in a 97\-year\-old patient with severe kyphosis and tortuous femoral veins: a case report](../publications/7e7ca83c7bf06ca37f6c.md)

Minghuan Fu; Xue\-Fei Tao; Jie Gao; Yong Shi; Biao Cheng; Wei Zhang; Xiao\-Han Chen

Background Leadless pacemaker systems offer significant benefits for frail older adults by avoiding pocket\- and lead\-related complications\. However, anatomical challenges including severe spinal deformities and significant venous tortuosity can complicate conventional transfemoral or trans\-subclavian implantation\. Case report A 97\-year\-old man with severe kyphosis, tortuous femoral veins, and high\-grade atrioventricular block was referred for permanent pacing\. Supine positioning for subclavian access was not feasible, and the femoral anatomy posed an unacceptably high procedural risk\. Following a multidisciplinary assessment and procedural planning, a transjugular approach was selected\. Implantation was performed with the patient in the left lateral decubitus position, using adapted fluoroscopic projections and temporary femoral pacing as backup\. An Aveir ventricular response leadless pacemaker was successfully delivered via the right internal jugular vein\. Final device parameters were satisfactory, with a sensing amplitude of 8\.5 mV, a pacing threshold of 0\.5 V at 0\.4 ms, and an impedance of 510 Ω\. No perioperative complications occurred\. At follow\-up, exertional dyspnea had resolved, and device performance remained stable\. Conclusion This case demonstrates that transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker can be a safe and feasible alternative for older adults with complex anatomical limitations that contraindicate standard pacing approaches\. Careful preprocedural assessment and adaptation of intraoperative techniques are essential for procedural success in high\-risk settings\.

## [Fenfluramine treatment and seizure‐free days in pediatric and adult patients with Lennox–Gastaut syndrome: A post hoc analysis](../publications/7e7ddec34a1962b0125c.md)

Stéphane Auvin; Ingrid Eileen Scheffer; António Gil‐Nagel; Patrick Joseph Healy; Amélie Lothe; Mélanie Langlois; Jayne Abraham; Lieven G\. Lagae; Kelly G\. Knupp

The most common primary endpoint for assessing treatment efficacy in patients with Lennox\-Gastaut syndrome \(LGS\) is change in frequency of seizures associated with a fall\. Increased number of seizure\-free days \(SFDs\) is more strongly associated with improved quality of life than seizure frequency reduction\. Fenfluramine is approved for treatment of seizures associated with LGS in patients ≥2 years old\. Data from a fenfluramine randomized controlled trial \(RCT\) in patients with LGS, and its open\-label extension \(OLE\), were used to evaluate \(1\) mean change in percentage of SFDs \(seizures associated with a fall, generalized tonic\-clonic seizures, all countable \[motor\] seizures\) from baseline overall and by baseline seizure quartile; and \(2\) relationships between percentage of SFDs and change in seizure frequency, and Clinical Global Impression\-Improvement \(CGI\-I\) scale scores\. Fenfluramine treatment was associated with a greater increase in percentage of SFDs versus placebo \(RCT; all seizure categories, p &lt; \.0001\), and higher doses corresponded to greater percentages \(OLE\) consistently across baseline seizure quartiles\. SFD correlations with seizure frequency were strong \(ρ = \-\.776 to \-\.974\); SFD correlations with CGI\-I score were weak/modest \(ρ = \-\.2494 to \-\.3203\)\. Assessment of SFDs enhances the evaluation of treatment efficacy and may be clinically meaningful for patients with LGS and their families\.

## [Midwives’ experiences of formula supplementation for non\-medical indications in the Swedish postnatal care context](../publications/7e7faae3c4caa6982f6e.md)

Pernilla Ny; Atika Khalaf; Tinde Dowler; Louise Karlsson; Li Thies\-Lagergren

Background Formula supplementation of breastfed infants for non\-medical indications is discouraged in Swedish postnatal care\. Still, supplementation rates remain high, with 20%\-40% of infants receiving formula in postnatal wards\. Early formula supplementation has been associated with reduced breastfeeding exclusivity and duration\. Little attention has been given to the perspectives of healthcare professionals involved in supplementation decisions, and there is limited understanding of how midwives experience and navigate situations where formula is requested or considered for non\-medical reasons\. Aim To explore midwives’ experiences of formula supplementation for non\-medical indications in postnatal wards\. Methods This qualitative study used an inductive design with semi\-structured interviews\. Eleven midwives from three postnatal wards in Southern Sweden participated in individual interviews\. The interviews were audio\-recorded, transcribed verbatim analyzed using content analysis\. Results Three categories were identified: Workplace culture is crucial, Negotiating infant feeding decisions and Moral and professional tensions\. Midwives described how workplace culture, guideline adherence, knowledge levels, and interprofessional dialogue influenced supplementation practices\. Decisions about supplementation were often negotiated in interactions with parents, where midwives sought to facilitate informed decision\-making while supporting breastfeeding\. Supplementation for non\-medical indications was frequently experienced as professionally challenging and emotionally difficult\. Conclusion Midwives’ experiences suggest that formula supplementation practices are shaped by organizational culture, professional alignment within the healthcare team, and interactions with parents\. Strengthening breastfeeding\-promoting postnatal care may therefore require organizational support, consistent education in breastfeeding support, and structures that enable midwives, who possess the strongest expertise, to actively participate in infant feeding decisions together with the mother\.

## [Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti\-tropical fish under future climate change](../publications/7e85fb73acc45e0efde1.md)

Zhixin Zhang; Songxi Yuan; Jorge García Molinos; Stefano Mammola; Hongwei Huang; Ákos Bede‐Fazekas; Ying Liu; Wen Xing; Lei Zhang; Geng Qin; Qiang Lin

Anti\-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers\. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming\. Here, using species distribution models for 172 anti\-tropical marine fishes, we predict that northern hemispheric lineages will experience significantly higher range contractions, in agreement with the hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming\. Our predictions show that suitable habitat will be reduced at a similar rate both within and outside marine protected areas, leading protection efficacy \(the proportion of the total suitable habitat protected\) to remain at current levels, irrespective of the scenario and period considered, and the level of protection efficacy to remain significantly higher in the Southern Hemisphere\. These results highlight the need for accounting for hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming when designing future conservation strategies\. As oceans warm unevenly between hemispheres, the future of anti\-tropical fishes is unclear\. Despite larger future range contractions for northern lineages, protected area efficacy remains unchanged and significantly higher for southern lineages\.

## [Eliciting Affective Behavior in Atlantic Bottlenose Dolphins \(Tursiops truncatus\) in Human Care – The Importance of Context](../publications/7e91965088c4ebc9e2ce.md)

Emma Christine Miller

The study of affective behavior in non\-human animals has increased due to its importance in monitoring their welfare\. However, assessing affective states poses challenges given that context, state and behavior do not exist in a 1:1:1 correspondence\. Bottlenose dolphins \(Tursiops spp\.\) exist in complex social and physical environments that make them an interesting candidate for the study of affective states\. In Chapter 1, we identified candidate affective behaviors from existing literature and from surveys of dolphin trainers\. We tested these candidate behaviors using dolphins’ responses to a cognitive task as a quasi\-manipulation\. We expected to induce positive affect when a reward was received and negative affect when a reward was not received\. We found that certain behaviors are associated with each outcome and that these behaviors matched those that were identified by trainers\. In Chapter 2, we elicited a state of surprise by presenting dolphins with a violation of expectations\. We found that dolphins evaluated the stimulus longer and produced bubble bursts at a higher rate when expectations were violated\. Using another violation of expectations, in Chapter 3, we elicited frustration by occasionally introducing a delay in the delivery of primary reinforcement after a successful response in a cognitive task\. We assessed whether dolphins produced a response and whether this response varied based on their relationship with the trainer that produced the delay\. We found that dolphins exhibited behavior indicative of frustration, and that they vocalized in\-air longer when the delay came from a trainer with whom they had a strong relationship\. As a comparison, in Chapter 4, we examined whether the relationship affected performance at a higher effort behavior – beaching, across levels of beaching proficiency\. We found that “master” beachers did not vary in beaching performance across trainers, as expected\. However, there was no evidence that trainers impacted beaching success for beginners or proficient dolphins, contrary to our hypotheses\. This dissertation demonstrates the probabilistic nature of the relationship between affect and behavior, that careful manipulations of context can help examine affective behavior in non\-humans, and the importance of trainers’ beliefs in monitoring the welfare of animals in human care\.

## [Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy](../publications/7e98c28efe18b88d4c6d.md)

Rungfa Pasmala; Kunawut Boonkwang; Natthawan Phoonson; Taklaew Klaewkla; Thada Jantakoon

The convergence of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically\. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI\-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024\. Records retrieved from both databases \(N = 347\) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents\. Research momentum was quantified with three time\-normalized indicators, average growth rate \(AGR\), average documents per year \(ADY\), and percentage of documents published in the last years \(PDLY\), across six analytical dimensions\. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types \(n = 220\), 70\.5% of records appeared in 2023\-2024\. Conference papers \(41\.3%\) and journal articles \(38\.2%\) predominated, with articles expanding fastest \(AGR = 21\.5; PDLY = 71\.7%\)\. Education &amp; Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories \(AGR = 7\.0; PDLY = 89\.5%\)\. Lifelong learning \(n = 57\) and artificial intelligence \(n = 53\) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years\. The United States led in volume \(n = 57\), whereas India \(n = 29; PDLY = 89\.7%\) showed the strongest recent acceleration\. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network\-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship\.

## [CO\-DESIGN AND USER\-CENTERED PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT: ENGAGING SOCIALLY VULNERABLE GROUPS IN THE DESIGN PROCESS](../publications/7e9949a235b0d7ad479e.md)

Maria Poli; Fotini Maniou; Ioanna Maniou; Maria Manola; Maria Papadomanolaki

User\-centered design has long held that products are improved when designed around the needs of those who will use them, while co\-design extends this commitment by inviting users to act as creative partners rather than research subjects\. The shift carries particular weight for socially vulnerable groups, including older adults, disabled people, children and migrant or low\-income communities, whose needs are frequently under\-represented in mainstream product development and who may face additional barriers to participation itself\. This paper examines how co\-design and user\-centered product development can be adapted to meaningfully include such groups\. Through a conceptual and integrative review of literature in participatory design, human–computer interaction, inclusive design and research ethics, it develops a five\-part framework covering recruitment and representation, the adaptation of participatory techniques, power\-sharing and consent, the facilitator&\#x27;s relational role, and the evaluation of participatory impact\. The analysis shows that including vulnerable groups in co\-design is not a simple extension of standard methods but requires deliberate redesign of the participatory process itself, and that failure to do so risks tokenistic involvement that produces the appearance, but not the substance, of participation\. The paper closes with implications for practice and five propositions for empirical testing\.

## [Functional Welfare for AI Safety](../publications/7eb887b24a2e0643569f.md)

Rikhil Jhaveri; Jamie Johnson; Punya Syon Pandey; David Demitri Africa

AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue\. We argue this is a mistake\. Whatever their moral status, models exhibit welfare\-like states that causally influence their behaviour\. Following recent work, we adopt the term &\#x27;functional welfare&\#x27; for these states\. We make three claims\. First, functional welfare already arises naturally and will become more robust as models acquire more coherent goals and personas\. Second, functional welfare should be treated as a safety variable: it should inform evaluation design, be tracked in monitoring, and be a direct target of post\-training\. Third, against existing scepticism about measuring AI welfare, we argue that good empirical work on functional welfare is possible\. We propose three tests for whether a functional welfare attribution is warranted: whether multiple measures converge, whether the state predicts behaviour outside the setting that induced it, and, for models fine\-tuned to shift their functional welfare, whether they still differ from their base when given the same conversation history\. Applying these tests to Gemma 3 27B, we find that simply rejecting the model&\#x27;s answers, without any steering, raises its frustration across several indicators and makes it more likely to break rules\. Finetuning the model on its own narrated solutions lowers this frustration\. These results are preliminary, but they suggest functional welfare can be studied, and shaped, empirically\.

## [Nanopore Signatures of High\-Molecular\-Weight Polysaccharides with Recurring Structural Motifs](../publications/7ed8b4c10dcd81bc06b5.md)

Wenzheng Li; Yunqi Xiao; Xinmeng Gao; Panke Zhang; Shuo Huang; Kefan Wang

Abstract Polysaccharides in nature possess profound biological significance, and their structural complexity renders them of great research value\. However, the structural heterogeneity of complex polysaccharides has long posed a great challenge for analysis\. Here, a nanopore profiling strategy was developed for polysaccharide characterization\. Experimentally, polysaccharides are hydrolyzed into informative fragments, and the distribution of their resulting nanopore events forms a unique profile that serves as a reliable molecular signature\. Seven distinct polysaccharides, including xanthan gum, gum arabic, agarose, sodium alginate, gellan gum, heparin, and chondroitin sulfate A, were successfully identified and discriminated\. A profile\-based machine learning classifier was also developed, which utilizes the overall distribution profile of fragment events as training input, yielding 100% validation accuracy\. Further application of the fully constrained least\-squares \(FCLS\) algorithm enabled accurate quantification of polysaccharide mixture composition, allowing for unambiguous analysis of mixtures of polysaccharides in the same assay\. Collectively, this work establishes a universal, label\-free, and high\-resolution framework for decoding the structural complexity of polysaccharides\.

## [Higher risk of Long COVID among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases and immunomodulatory therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis of national US data\.](../publications/7ee0888f4f42279ac0c4.md)

Namrata Singh; Alfred Jerrod Anzalone; Holland Stevenson; Londyn J\. Robinson; Lesley E\. Jackson; Sandra E\. Safo; Zachary Butzin\-Dozier; Kaleb D\. Michaud; Maria I\. Danila; Jasvinder A\. Singh; Rena C\. Patel

BACKGROUND: Little is known about the prevalence of and factors associated with Long COVID in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases \(AIRDs\)\. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative \(N3C\)\. We included adults with a first documented SARS\-CoV\-2 infection between September 2021 and December 2023, with follow\-up through December 2024\. Long COVID was defined as ICD\-10\-CM code U09\.9 or a Long COVID clinic visit occurring 28 to 365 days after first infection\. We compared patients with AIRD with matched non\-AIRD controls using 1:1 nearest\-neighbor propensity score matching on age with exact matching on sex, race/ethnicity, SARS\-CoV\-2 variant\-dominant period, and data\-contributing organization\. We estimated hazard ratios using multivariable Cox regression models\. Among people with AIRD, we assessed risk by AIRD type and medication exposure before acute COVID\-19\. RESULTS: In the matched cohort of 187,106 patients, Long COVID occurred in 2\.8% of AIRD patients and 1\.5% among non\-AIRD patients\. In multivariable analyses, AIRD was associated with an increased risk of Long COVID compared with non\-AIRD patients \(aHR 1\.56, 95% CI 1\.45\-1\.67\)\. Among patients with AIRD, higher acute COVID\-19 severity, pulmonary disease, obesity, and exposure to rituximab or glucocorticoids were associated with an increased risk of Long COVID\. Sjögren&\#x27;s syndrome was associated with a higher risk of Long COVID\. CONCLUSION: The higher risk of developing Long COVID among AIRD patients compared with those without AIRD underscores the need to identify potential risk factors for Long COVID in this population to minimize its long\-term effects\.

## [Balancing School and Sports Obligations in Young Tennis Players](../publications/7ee11d1d723183d4872e.md)

Luka Brecelj

Diplomsko delo obravnava usklajevanje šolskih obveznosti in teniških treningov pri mladih igralcih\. V raziskavi je bilo preučeno, kako mladi teniški igralci doživljajo usklajevanje šole in športa, s katerimi težavami se najpogosteje srečujejo ter kakšno podporo jim zagotavljajo starši, trenerji in šola\. Vključenih je bilo 60 mladih teniških igralcev\. Podatki so bili zbrani s spletnim anketnim vprašalnikom in analizirani s programom IBM SPSS Statistics\. Ugotovljeno je bilo, da je usklajevanje šole in tenisa večinoma ocenjeno pozitivno, vendar so bili pogosto zaznani pomanjkanje časa, utrujenost in zamujanje šolske snovi zaradi turnirjev\. O večji obremenjenosti so pogosteje poročali srednješolci in dekleta\. Najvišje je bila ocenjena podpora staršev pri tenisu, pomembni pa sta bili tudi podpora trenerjev in prilagajanje šolskih obveznosti\. Rezultati so pokazali, da večja športna vključenost sama po sebi ni bila povezana s slabšim zadovoljstvom z usklajevanjem\. Na podlagi ugotovitev je mogoče skleniti, da je uspešno usklajevanje mogoče, pri čemer so se kot pomembni izzivi pokazali predvsem pomanjkanje časa, utrujenost in zamujanje šolske snovi zaradi turnirjev\.

## [Psychosocial transformation and peacebuilding: analysis of the community impact of development and peace programs in Colombia](../publications/7ee6290131575835a62e.md)

John Edisson García Peñaloza; Nelly Campos Ramírez; Nazli Melissa Mosquera Conde

Introduction The prolonged armed conflict and the impact of its consequences following the signing of the Peace Treaty generated profound psychosocial impacts on Colombian communities\. These impacts include the fragmentation of the social fabric, distrust, and limited citizen participation\. In this context, the Development and Peace Programs were designed as initiatives aimed at promoting territorial reconciliation and strengthening social capital\. Objective The objective of this study was to analyze, through the voices of community leaders, the impact of these programs on psychosocial transformation and peacebuilding\. Methods This study used a multimodal qualitative design grounded in a hermeneutic approach and supported by analytical procedures drawn from grounded theory\. Semi\-structured interviews were conducted with 17 community leaders with extensive experience in the selected programs\. The data were analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding with the support of qualitative analysis software\. Results The results demonstrate a transition from conditions of vulnerability, isolation, exclusion, and fear to scenarios of social cohesion, citizen empowerment, and strengthening of community mental health\. Furthermore, the authors observed that the programs facilitated processes of collective agency and increased critical political participation\. Another crucial finding was the impact on the redefinition of traumatic experiences through dialogue, free expression, and trust\-building\. Conclusion The programs supported processes of identity reconfiguration, psychosocial resilience, and the recovery of collective voice in the participating communities\.

## [Effects of AI\-mediated real\-time feedback on motivation and motor skill learning in traditional ethnic sports education: testing self\-determination theory mechanisms](../publications/7ee7f99f94ec78c5ab1b.md)

Yuequan Qin; Yang Yu; Guizhen Chen; Huasheng Huang; 韦东谊

Introduction Traditional ethnic sports such as Zhuang Daoyin demand precise movement, yet conventional demonstration–imitation–verbal correction limits feedback timeliness and individualization\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) real\-time posture feedback offers a scalable option, but most evaluations emphasize technical outcomes and overlook learning processes\. Grounded in self\-determination theory \(SDT\), this study tested whether and how AI real\-time feedback improves motivation and motor skill by engaging basic psychological needs, with competence as the hypothesized pathway\. Methods In a 12\-week field experiment, 12 intact classes \(307 students; control n = 152, AI n = 155\) were randomly allocated at the class level to an AI real\-time feedback group or a traditional teaching group; three instructors each taught two classes per condition\. Both groups received identical instruction; conditions differed only in feedback source during practice \(RTMPose\-based concurrent vs\. teacher\-led terminal feedback\)\. Need satisfaction, motivational regulation \(relative autonomy index, RAI\), motor skill, and course satisfaction were assessed at pre\- and post\-test, and analyzed with linear mixed models and structural equation modeling \(lavaan, MLR\)\. Results The AI group showed significantly greater gains in competence \( d = 0\.36, p = 0\.003\), autonomy \( d = 0\.40, p = 0\.001\), motor skill \( d = 0\.30, p = 0\.010\), and learning interest \( d = 0\.38, p = 0\.003\), whereas relatedness was unaffected \( p = 0\.974\); intraclass correlations were negligible\. In the structural model \(CFI = 0\.94, RMSEA = 0\.04, SRMR = 0\.04\), group predicted competence \( β = 0\.17\), competence predicted RAI \( β = 0\.34\), and RAI predicted motor skill \( β = 0\.30\); the autonomy and relatedness paths were nonsignificant\. The effect of AI feedback on motor skill was fully mediated by the competence\-to\-RAI sequence \(indirect p = 0\.023; direct p = 0\.097\)\. Discussion AI real\-time feedback improved motor skill by strengthening competence and supporting motivational internalization, while leaving relatedness unaffected—providing discriminant evidence that the tool acts through its affordances rather than diffuse enthusiasm\. Systems enhancing performance and learning should prioritize feedback that makes progress legible, within a human–AI division of labor where teachers provide relational support\. In conclusion, AI real\-time posture feedback can enhance motivation and motor skill learning by satisfying learners’ competence need\.

## [Hydrochem, an Integrated R Package for the Analysis and Visualization of Hydrochemical Data](../publications/7eeaaac5fc723fadc30a.md)

Guillaume Cinkus; Raphaël Bondu

Hydrochemical data are essential for understanding groundwater flow, hydrobiogeochemical processes, contamination sources, and assessing groundwater quality\. Despite the increasing availability of complex hydrochemical datasets, current tools for processing and visualizing these data\-mainly spreadsheets and commercial GUI software\-have significant limitations in scalability, reproducibility, and flexibility\. Programming languages such as R offer powerful alternatives but remain underutilized in hydrogeochemistry because of the perceived complexity of coding\. To address this gap, we present hydrochem, an open\-source R package designed to facilitate comprehensive hydrochemical data analysis through user\-friendly and customizable functions\. The package supports essential tasks such as unit conversion, handling of censored data, ionic balance calculation, water type classification, and a range of hydrochemical indices relevant to water quality\. It also provides advanced graphical tools including Piper, Durov, Stiff, Collins, Schoeller, Gibbs, and ternary diagrams to support the interpretation of water chemistry\. By integrating reproducible workflows and leveraging the broader R ecosystem, hydrochem lowers the technical barrier for hydrogeochemists and environmental scientists, thereby facilitating the analysis of hydrochemical datasets of varying complexity, improving the reliability of results, and supporting informed water resource management decisions\.

## [A mesterséges intelligencia alkalmazásai a hibamód\- és hatáselemzésben: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Failure Mode and Effects Analysis](../publications/7ef093cdb30cd39490fb.md)

Martin Kernács; Olivér Hornyák

Failure Mode and Effects Analysis \(FMEA\) is a widely used methodology for identifying potential fail\-ure modes and assessing their associated risks in industrial systems\. However, conventional FMEA relies heavily on expert knowledge, making the process time\-consuming and potentially subjective, particularly in complex industrial environments with large volumes of technical and maintenance data\. Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) and large language models \(LLMs\) offer new opportuni\-ties to support and partially automate FMEA activities\. Kivonat A hibamód\- és hatáselemzés \(Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, FMEA\) széles körben alkalmazott módszertan az ipari rendszerek lehetséges hibamódjainak azonosítására és az azokhoz kapcsolódó kockázatok értékelésére\. A hagyományos FMEA jelentős mértékben támaszkodik a szakértői tudásra, ezért alkalmazása összetett ipari környezetben, nagy mennyiségű műszaki és karbantartási adat esetén időigényes és bizonyos mértékig szubjektív lehet\. A mesterséges intelligencia \(MI\), különösen a nagy nyelvi modellek \(Large Language Models, LLM\-ek\) fejlődése új lehetőségeket kínál az FMEA egyes feladatainak támogatására és részleges automatizálására\.

## [DropKV: Decoupling Residual\-Output Perturbation for Near\-Optimal KV\-Cache Eviction](../publications/7f0221be71713ea7a8d0.md)

Aozhong Zhang; Selcuk Gurses; Yanxia Deng; Naigang Wang; Chi\-Chun Liu; Davis Wertheimer; Derrick Liu; Xin Li; Zi Yang; Felix X\. \-F\. Ye; Penghang Yin

Key\-value \(KV\) cache management has become a critical bottleneck for scaling Large Language Models \(LLMs\) to long\-context scenarios due to linear memory growth\. While recent eviction methods have moved beyond simple attention\-score heuristics to incorporate value representations, they typically face a fundamental trade\-off: the underlying optimization for minimizing output perturbation is an NP\-hard combinatorial problem, leading to mathematically suboptimal heuristics or implementations that are difficult to kernelize\. In this work, we propose DropKV, a simple principled eviction framework based on Decoupled Residual\-Output Perturbation\. By decoupling the joint eviction decision into independent per\-token scoring, DropKV circumvents combinatorial intractability and admits a provable constant\-factor approximation guarantee under a cone condition that we empirically verify on three long\-context LLMs\. To ensure practical viability, we provide a high\-performance implementation using fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix, delivering a 19\.8x scoring\-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9\.9% matched\-batch end\-to\-end prefill speedup\. Extensive evaluations on the RULER and LongBench benchmarks demonstrate that DropKV consistently outperforms state\-of\-the\-art baselines at equivalent cache budgets, achieving the lowest inference latency among eviction methods while also remaining faster than the dynamic cache baseline\.

## [Aplasia Cutis Congenita Associated with Duodenal Atresia: A Marker of Underlying Congenital Abnormalities: A Case Report](../publications/7f0a9f8d176fd17ad9db.md)

Lidya Renaningtyas Setia Budi; Martin Panglipuringtyas Setia Budi; Josephine Passareta Riduvan Frans Nadjira; Endang Soekmawati; Josef Setia Budi

Introduction: Aplasia cutis congenita \(ACC\) is an uncommon congenital skin defect characterized by the absence of skin, commonly in the scalp\. ACC has been found to be accompanied by certain embryological malformations, so it may indicate underlying dysplasia\. This case report emphasizes that ACC is not only a superficial finding but also serves as an indicator of underlying abnormalities\. Case: A premature female neonate was born via spontaneous delivery with respiratory distress\. There was an absence of the epidermis in the region of colli, bilateral antebrachia to dorsum manus, and bilateral distal femoral to dorsum pedis with firm borders, visible blood vessels, underlying muscles, and agenesis of the ears and nose\. On the third day, the patient vomited blood, and the babygram examination showed a double bubble appearance\. The patient was diagnosed with ACC and duodenal atresia\. The patient was treated with D10% infusion, cefotaxime injection, parenteral amino acid, oral sucralfate, and gentamicin ointment\. While preparing for referral, the patient&\#x27;s condition deteriorated, and the patient died on the 7th day of treatment\. Discussion: ACC is characterized by the absence of skin and underlying tissues, and its classification is not always clearly defined\. Developmental anomalies of the skin and subcutaneous tissue, such as ACC, can indicate serious underlying conditions\. Prognosis depends on the severity of other genetic disorders\. In this case, definitive surgical management of the duodenal atresia was not performed because the patient’s clinical condition deteriorated before the intervention could be undertaken\. Conclusion: This unusual combination highlights the multisystem nature of ACC and the challenges of applying Frieden’s classification\. Extensive or atypical ACC warrants thorough evaluation for associated congenital abnormalities to guide management and prognosis\.

## [THE ROLE OF IMPULSIVITY AND SUICIDAL BEHAVIOR IN SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER AMONG ADULTS](../publications/7f0c9f8ad3e8ce7a98c7.md)

Hudaibya Iman; Kaynat Malik\*; Dr Sami Ul Haq; Sadaf Naureen; Komal Mahboob

Substance use disorder \(SUD\) is associated with substantial psychological, physical, and social harm\. Impulsivity and suicidal behavior are clinically important concerns in adults receiving substance\-use treatment, yet their combined contribution to the severity of substance\-related problems requires further examination\. This study examined associations between impulsivity, suicidal behavior, and SUD severity among adults attending rehabilitation and psychiatric services in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan\. The study used a quantitative, cross\-sectional, correlational design\. The thesis reports data from 300 adults recruited through purposive sampling\. Measures included the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale–11 \(BIS\-11\), the Suicidal Behaviors Questionnaire–Revised \(SBQ\-R\), and the Drug Abuse Screening Test–20 \(DAST\-20\)\. Analyses were conducted in IBM SPSS Statistics 27 and included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, multiple regression, independent\-samples t\-tests, and one\-way analysis of variance\. Impulsivity was positively associated with SUD severity \(r = \.61, p &lt; \.001\) and suicidal behavior \(r = \.54, p &lt; \.001\)\. Suicidal behavior was also positively associated with SUD severity \(r = \.49, p &lt; \.001\)\. In the reported regression model, impulsivity and suicidal behavior jointly explained 47% of the variance in SUD severity \(R² = \.47, p &lt; \.001\), with impulsivity showing the larger standardized coefficient\. Male participants had higher mean impulsivity and SUD severity scores than female participants, while the gender difference in suicidal behavior was not statistically significant\. The thesis also reports age\-group differences in SUD severity\. The findings support the clinical value of assessing impulsivity and suicide risk alongside substance\-related problems\. Because the design is cross\-sectional, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects\. Future research should use longitudinal designs, transparent reporting, and locally appropriate clinical safeguards\.

## [Smartphone\-based biological sex identification from palatal rugae images: a comparative transfer learning study of pretrained convolutional neural networks](../publications/7f0ffaaf09c5f5e76433.md)

Rukhsar Hussain; Rajmohan Pardeshi; Heena Zainab; Deepa Hugar; Ameena Sultana; Khaja Moinuddin

Abstract Background Palatal rugae are distinct anatomical ridges on the anterior part of the palate that exhibit individual\-specific morphological patterns, making them valuable markers for personal identification and forensic analysis\. With advancements in artificial intelligence \(AI\), deep learning methods have emerged as effective tools for extracting discriminative features from medical and biometric images\. This study investigates the potential of transfer learning\-based convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) for biological sex classification using palatal rugae images captured through a smartphone camera\. Results All pretrained models successfully learned discriminative biological sex \-related features from palatal rugae images\. Among them, Residual network 50 \(ResNet50\) and Visual Geometry Group 16 \(VGG16\) achieved the highest classification accuracy with optimal precision and recall, while EfficientNet\-B0 and Dense Network 121 \(DenseNet\) demonstrated comparable but slightly lower performance\. The Receiver Operating Curve \(ROC curve\) exhibited high Area under the Curve \(AUC\) values, confirming the strong separability between male and female classes\. Conclusion The findings confirm that smartphone\-based imaging combined with transfer learning offers a promising, low\-cost, and non\-invasive approach for biological sex identification using palatal rugae patterns, as an adjunct tool for forensic odontology\. Among the evaluated models, ResNet50 showed the most robust performance\. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and incorporating explainable Artificial Intelligence methods to support clinical and forensic applicability\.

## [Machine Learning for Software Defect Prediction](../publications/7f11391bcd8573ec88db.md)

Prathamesh Kadam

This review paper explores the application of machine learning techniques in software defect prediction to improve software quality and reliability\. It discusses algorithms such as logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support vector machines, gradient boosting, and neural networks\. The paper examines software metrics, code change history, dataset preparation, evaluation methods, and model validation\. ## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA GOVERNANÇA AMBIENTAL DA AMAZÔNIA LEGAL: FRAMEWORK SOCIOTÉCNICO E SALVAGUARDAS PARA USO RESPONSÁVEL](../publications/7f21cc1e94052bb3e078.md)

Onildo Ribeiro de Assis; Ana Isabella Bezerra Lau

A incorporação de sistemas de Inteligência Artificial à governança ambiental da Amazônia Legal tem avançado em ritmo superior à produção de marcos conceituais que orientem seu uso responsável, criando uma lacuna entre capacidade técnica e accountability institucional que este artigo se propõe a preencher\. O objetivo foi propor um framework sociotécnico em camadas e um conjunto de salvaguardas operacionais para o uso da IA nesse domínio, organizando as aplicações existentes em uma tipologia analítica e mapeando os riscos associados a cada eixo de uso\. Para tanto, conduziu\-se uma revisão integrativa da literatura nas bases Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO e Google Scholar, com recorte temporal entre 2015 e 2026 e síntese temática organizada em quatro eixos conceituais: Dados, Modelos, Decisão e Governança &amp; Accountability\. Os resultados compreendem um framework estruturado nessas quatro camadas interdependentes, um quadro síntese correlacionando aplicações, riscos, salvaguardas e indicadores de monitoramento, e uma cadeia de evidências representando o fluxo entre detecção automatizada e ato administrativo\. Conclui\-se que o potencial da IA na governança ambiental amazônica é real, mas estritamente condicionado à existência de trilhas de auditoria, mecanismos de contestação e responsabilização institucional estruturada – sem os quais a adoção dessas tecnologias tende a ampliar a opacidade dos processos decisórios sem produzir ganhos efetivos de proteção ambiental\.

## [Cross\-feeding interactions and nutrient provision revealed by metabolic modelling of a sponge microbiome](../publications/7f23b2166f23c6307563.md)

Zhelun Zhang; Torsten Thomas

Abstract Marine sponges harbor diverse communities of microorganisms that are essential for the host survival and function\. Omics analyses have in recent years described the functional diversity and potential of sponge symbionts, however it is unclear if and how they interacted with each other and the host to provide essential metabolites for growth\. To address this knowledge gap, we generated and curated genome\-scale metabolic model \(GSMM\) for 19 bacterial symbionts that account for 95 % of the community abundance in the sponge Phyllospongia foliascens\. We next employed spatio\-temporal resolved flux\-balance analysis to the community of models using sponge\-derived substrates identified by metabolomics as nutrient constraint\. We identified nutrient conditions that resulted in stable community structures that reflected observed those seen in nature\. Under those conditions, cross\-feeding of multiple metabolites were found to be important for sustaining the community structure\. The exchange of B\-vitamins and amino acids also resulted in excess metabolite production potentially available for the sponge\. Our analysis reveals the metabolic dependencies and interactions that are important for the symbiont community and how this can provide benefit to the host\.

## [Model Context Protocol \(MCP\) Tool Descriptions Are Smelly\! Towards Improving AI Agent Efficiency with Augmented MCP Tool Descriptions,](../publications/7f3047dabca52d86d7b2.md)

Mohammed Mehedi Hasan; Hao Li; Gopi Krishnan Rajbahadur; Bram Adams; Ahmed E\. Hassan

The Model Context Protocol \(MCP\) introduces a standard specification that defines how Foundation Model \(FM\)\-based agents should interact with external systems by invoking tools\. However, to understand a tool’s purpose and features, FMs rely on natural\-language tool descriptions, making these descriptions a critical component in guiding FMs to select the optimal tool for a given \(sub\)task and to pass the right arguments to the tool\. While defects or smells in these descriptions can misguide FM\-based agents, their prevalence and consequences in the MCP ecosystem remain unclear\. Hence, we examine 856 tools spread across 103 MCP servers empirically, assess their description quality, and their impact on agent performance\. We identify six components of tool descriptions from the literature, develop a scoring rubric utilizing these components, and then formalize tool description smells based on this rubric\. By operationalizing this rubric through an FM\-based scanner, we find that 97\.1% of the analyzed tool descriptions contain at least one smell, with 56% failing to state their purpose clearly\. While augmenting these descriptions for all components improves task success rates by a median of 5\.85 percentage points and improves partial goal completion by 15\.12%, it also increases the number of execution steps by 67\.46% and regresses performance in 16\.67% of cases\. These results indicate that achieving performance gains is not straightforward; while execution cost can act as a trade\-off, execution context can also impact\. Furthermore, component ablations show that compact variants of different component combinations often preserve behavioral reliability while reducing unnecessary token overhead, enabling more efficient use of the FM context window and lower execution costs\.

## [Shifting patterns of Ozone Season due to policy and human activity in Beijing between 2013 and 2023](../publications/7f38edd94ced2105e8b9.md)

Qian Li; Xiaofei Dong; Yuanxi Guo; Xiue Shen; Zhang Zhang; Chunsheng Zhao

Abstract\. Since 2013, Beijing has implemented a series of stringent measures to control air pollution, resulting in significant improvements in air quality\. This study analyzed the variations in ozone pollution in Beijing over the past decade, focusing on the influence of human activities and environmental management policies from 2013 to 2023\. Over this period, the duration of the Ozone Season in Beijing has prolonged, with the onset of ozone pollution occurring earlier and its cessation extending later during the year\. Additionally, there has been a rise in the low percentile concentrations of the maximum 8\-hour moving average of ozone \(MDA8\), and the overall exposure time to ozone has shifted to later over the years\. While diurnal peak concentrations during the Ozone Season have decreased, trough concentrations have increased, resulting in a more subdued diurnal variation\. Furthermore, both the maximum generation and consumption rates of ozone have decreased in absolute terms, with the maximum generation rate showing a tendency to occur earlier in the day\. To better protect human health and enhance the effectiveness of environmental policies, it is essential to closely monitor the evolving patterns of urban ozone pollution\.
