## [Biogas Production From Chicken Litter: Advances, Challenges, and Perspectives of Anaerobic Digestion](../publications/7f3fb00d0062a3bc709c.md)

Caroline Zarzzeka; Jonas Goldoni; THAMIRES MARTINHO PRADOS; Giane Gonçalves Lenzi; Leda Maria Saragiotto Colpini

Anaerobic digestion stands out as a promising technology for the energy valorization of chicken litter, yielding both biogas and digestate\. This study presents a systematic bibliometric review using the Methodi Ordinatio 2\.0 methodology to identify global research trends, scientific gaps, and technological advances related to biogas production from chicken litter through anaerobic digestion\. A literature search yielded 112 articles from the Scopus database, resulting—after analysis—in a final portfolio of 101 peer\-reviewed scientific articles selected based on bibliometric criteria, including journal impact, citation count, and year of publication\. The results indicate that the main challenges associated with the anaerobic digestion of chicken litter include its high nitrogen content, low carbon\-to\-nitrogen ratio, ammonia inhibition, and the presence of recalcitrant compounds that reduce biodegradation efficiency and methane yield\. To overcome these limitations, several strategies have been proposed, including co\-digestion with carbon\-rich substrates, physical, chemical, and biological pretreatments, biochar supplementation, microaeration, high\-solids anaerobic digestion, and improved operational control\. The agricultural application of digestate contributes to nutrient recycling, improved soil fertility, and reduced dependence on synthetic fertilizers, reinforcing circular economy principles\. Therefore, the use of chicken litter for biogas production is a promising alternative, with the potential to contribute significantly to environmental sustainability, renewable energy generation and support the long\-term development of the poultry sector\.

## [Algorithmic Bias and Information Trust in Academic Library Discovery Systems: An Analytical Study of User Search Behaviour and Digital Information Literacy Using Online Primary Empirical Evidence](../publications/7f4209efee813f375687.md)

Sunil Kumar; Rajeev Manhas; Mamta Mamta; Dhiman Ruchi; Chand Chand

Background: Academic library discovery systems increasingly mediate access to scholarly information through ranking, metadata matching, filtering, database coverage, availability signals, and recommender functions\. These algorithmic arrangements can shape what users notice, cite, and trust\. Objective: This paper examines how algorithmic bias, user search behaviour, information trust, and digital information literacy intersect in academic discovery environments\. Methodology: Since no local institutional dataset was provided, the paper uses a secondary analysis of online primary empirical evidence from three verifiable sources: Project Information Literacy&\#x27;s student survey of 2,318 respondents across six U\.S\. campuses; a published Summon query/click\-log analysis based on anonymized searches by millions of users at hundreds of libraries; and an open representative German online survey on search\-engine literacy and trust involving 2,012 respondents\. Results: The data show high dependence on scholarly databases and OPACs but limited engagement with librarians\. In the Project Information Literacy survey, 84% of students used scholarly research databases and 78% used OPACs for course\-related research, while only 20% consulted librarians about assignments\. Summon logs show that users generally began with simple search, with fewer than 6% of queries using fielded search and only slightly more than 2% using advanced operators, although more than 40% used at least one filter\. Search\-engine literacy data show that 79% knew paid ads exist, but only 29\.2% knew how ads differ from organic results, and only 8\.9% knew the term SEO\. Implications: Libraries need discovery\-literacy instruction that connects searching, ranking, metadata quality, database coverage, and calibrated trust\. Keywords: algorithmic bias; academic libraries; discovery systems; information trust; search behaviour; digital information literacy; information retrieval

## [Clinical application of Xianfang Huoming decoction in hidradenitis suppurativa: a three\-case series and literature review](../publications/7f45fdf63adb030ad0e2.md)

Zixi Wang; Xuling Wu; Hongliu Zhu; Ke Liu; Yihong Gao; Yuegang Wei; Qiuxia Mao; Liyan Zhou

Hidradenitis suppurativa \(HS\) is a chronic, recurrent inflammatory follicular disease characterized by painful nodules, abscesses, and sinus tract formation that typically affects intertriginous areas, such as the axillae, inguinal regions, and gluteal region\. This condition is often persistent and is difficult to control in clinical practice\. In recent years, traditional Chinese medicine has been explored as a potential adjunct in its management\. Here, we summarize the cases of three male patients with HS treated at the Department of Dermatology, Jiangyin Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine \(2023–2024\), aged 12–29 years with disease durations of 6 months to 4 years\. The lesions were primarily located in the axillae or gluteal region and presented as recurrent papules, pustules, nodules, and painful cysts\. All cases were Hurley stage I–II and classified as heat\-toxin accumulation syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine\. All patients received individualized combination therapies incorporating Xianfang Huoming Decoction, along with topical treatments, antibiotics, and/or surgical intervention when indicated\. After 1–5 weeks of treatment, the inflammatory lesions and pain symptoms improved, with IHS4 scores decreasing by approximately 71%–81%\. Patient 1 subsequently experienced recurrence after treatment discontinuation and was lost to dermatological follow\-up\. These cases suggest that Xianfang Huoming Decoction may help reduce inflammatory activity and promote lesion resolution in HS, supporting its potential role as an adjunctive therapeutic option\.

## [Surface\-engineered biogenic TiO2 nanoparticles with tailored isoelectric point: interfacial electrical double layer interactions, solar mineralisation, and DFT\-resolved regioselectivity of azo dye degradation](../publications/7f49ff803b088e8d62b1.md)

A\. Sahraoui; M\. Hamlaoui; S\. Chikhi; H\. Boulebd; A\. Zertal; S\. Vernuccio; M\. Batool; T\. Shah

Biogenically tailored anatase TiO2 nanoparticles \(S3, 13–15 nm\) were engineered via sequential mild thermal pre\-treatment of an Eucalyptus globulus leaf extract\-derived precursor, governing crystal nucleation\-growth kinetics\. This controlled thermal pre\-treatment yielded a photocatalyst with enhanced crystallinity, suppressed aggregation, a shifted isoelectric point \(IEP = 5\.5–6\.3\), and a functionalised surface bearing residual biogenic carbonaceous species \(5\.33 wt% C\)\. The S3 catalyst matched or outperformed commercial Degussa P25 in the degradation and mineralisation of three anionic azo dyes, Methyl Orange \(MO\), Acid Orange 7 \(AO\), and Orange G \(OG\), under both UV and natural solar irradiation, demonstrating its practical photocatalytic relevance\. Dark adsorption assays \(&lt;4\.5 %\) confirmed that degradation is strictly governed by dynamic interactions within the electrical double layer \(EDL\) rather than direct hole transfer\. Photocatalytic efficiency exhibited strong pH dependence relative to the catalyst’s shifted IEP: under acidic conditions \(pH 3\), surface protonation \(Ti–OH2 \+\) compressed the EDL and drove Coulombic pre\-concentration of anionic pollutants, inducing a kinetic inversion to OG &gt; AO &gt; MO, governed by the higher structural charge of the divalent OG molecule and stabilisation of reactive hydrazone tautomers\. Conversely, alkaline regimes induced electrostatic repulsion \(Ti–O−\), shifting the degradation hierarchy to AO &gt; OG &gt; MO\. Total organic carbon \(TOC\) analysis confirmed robust mineralisation with high carbon removal efficiency across all tested conditions\. Complementary DFT calculations \(M06\-2X/6\-31\+G\(d,p\)\) revealed that electrophilic •OH attack proceeds preferentially via exergonic C–N bond addition rather than N–N cleavage, with azo\-hydrazone tautomerism serving as the key regioselectivity\-governing factor\.

## [Quantitative metabolism: data and mechanism as dual engines for a continuous, computable, and adaptive health framework](../publications/7f5354837739cc93039c.md)

Yuchen Xu; Jieli Lu; Shijia Pan; Jingsheng Lin; Yufang Bi; Guang Ning; Weiqing Wang

Abstract Metabolism is a dynamic, multiscale system, yet metabolic medicine still relies largely on static, threshold\-based measurements that poorly capture longitudinal heterogeneity and early state transitions\. We propose an operational framework for quantitative metabolism that integrates high\-resolution measurements with mechanistically constrained computational models to represent metabolic states, predict trajectories, and guide intervention\. The framework comprises four interconnected layers: multi\-omics, defining individual molecular fingerprints; physiological and behavioral dynamics, capturing time\-resolved exposures and proximal responses; phenotypic function, representing integrated organ\- and system\-level consequences; and adaptive metabolic regulation, extending toward digital twins and model\-guided interventions such as digital therapeutics \(DtX\)\. Four sequential validation stages—quantifiable representation, predictive trajectory, operable intervention, and adaptive regulation—define the evidence required to advance from measurement to closed\-loop clinical application\. By replacing threshold\-defined categories with continuous, time\-resolved state representations, quantitative metabolism provides a structured research agenda for longitudinal metabolic assessment, mechanistically interpretable prediction, and prospectively validated personalized intervention across the life course\.

## [ESL ASSESSMENT IN THE AGE OF AI: SERBIAN ESL TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES TOWARDS THE USE OF CHATGPT](../publications/7f59e26541e28fc916cc.md)

Aleksa Stošić; Marija V\. Milojković

Following the introduction of publicly accessible AI and LLMs, they have gradually started to be adopted in the ESL classroom\. Recent studies have revealed that these tools have had a wider impact on ESL assessment, allowing for enhanced accuracy, efficiency, and person alization in language evaluation\. However, how widely these technologies are understood and used by teachers is still being investigated\. This study explores how Serbian ESL teachers use and perceive ChatGPT as a tool for assessing student work\. The study employs a mixed\-methods approach, combining survey data from 53 participants with follow\-up interviews from 10 educa tors to examine their tendencies, habits, and opinions regarding ChatGPT for assessment\. Find ings revealed that grammar and vocabulary are the language skills which Serbian ESL teachers assessed most often using ChatGPT, while skills such as speaking, listening, and critical thinking were rarely assessed using AI\. Teachers also expressed moderate trust in the tool’s ability to detect grammar and syntax errors, but were concerned about its limitations\. These limitations included ChatGPT’s ability to provide accurate assessment, its tendency to give vague feedback, and its lack of contextual understanding\. While many teachers recognized its ability to save time for as sessment tasks, they also recognized their own limited experiences with AI tools and stressed the need for human oversight, formal training, and ethical safeguards\. This study indicated that even though ChatGPT does not yet have widespread use in the Serbian ESL classroom, interviewees frequently emphasized that it should be used as a supplementary tool to assist teachers, but that guidelines and professional training on its use need to be provided to the teachers before they would readily implement it in the classroom\.

## [Perspectives on Informal Learning with Digital Tools](../publications/7f5b909a256c0a77cd42.md)

Oğuz Çetin; Salih Karaca

The aim of this study is to explore pre\-service teachers’ perspectives on informal learning with digital tools, focusing on their motivational sources, challenges, acquired skills, learning strategies, and the implications of these experiences for future learning and teaching practices\. The study employed a phenomenological research design\. Data were collected from 15 pre\-service teachers through semi\-structured interviews and analyzed using content analysis\. The findings revealed that motivation for informal learning with digital tools was primarily driven by rapid access to information and the facilitation of learning\. The main challenges involved inadequate technical infrastructure, particularly internet connectivity, and limited knowledge of digital tool use\. Participants addressed these difficulties by using alternative applications and artificial intelligence tools\. Key gains included information literacy, the ability to identify accurate and reliable information, and more conscious use of technology\. Participants managed their learning processes mainly through active inquiry, information verification, and exploratory trial\-and\-error strategies\. Digital informal learning was perceived not only as a means of obtaining information but also as a strategy that facilitates learning and promotes independent learning\. Its implications for future teaching practices emphasized effective digital tool use alongside student\-centered and inquiry\-based approaches\. In informal learning environments such as science centers, participants preferred simulations, mobile devices, visual recording and data\-collection tools, artificial intelligence applications, and augmented and virtual reality technologies, particularly for their potential to concretize learning and provide direct experiences\. Overall, the findings indicate that informal learning with digital tools constitutes an important learning domain that supports information evaluation, individual learning strategies, and future teaching practices\. However, challenges related to technical infrastructure and digital competence highlight the importance of adequate access and digital literacy skills in effectively supporting these learning processes\.

## [Island invertebrate responses to single‐ and multi‐species invasive rodent eradications](../publications/7f61833515d21fd493ae.md)

Melissa Houghton; Aleks Terauds; James Charles Russell; Michael M\. Driessen; Mark I\. Stevens; Hugh Philip Possingham; Penelope P\. Pascoe; Justine D\. S\. Shaw

Abstract Globally, islands have been invaded by invasive mammals with devastating impacts on biodiversity\. In response, eradication programs have increased in number, scale, and success\. However, the conservation benefits for small and cryptic invertebrates are rarely quantified\. Monitoring invertebrate communities can provide insights into the ecosystem‐level response to eradications\. House mice \( Mus musculus \) have invaded islands globally and are a major predator of invertebrates\. Mice were declared eradicated from sub‐Antarctic Antipodes in 2018\. House mice and ship rats \( Rattus rattus \) were declared eradicated from Macquarie in 2014\. We analyzed pre‐ and post‐eradication macro‐invertebrate surveys on both islands to assess changes in invertebrate richness, diversity, and abundance\. Overall abundance and richness of invertebrates increased post‐eradication on both islands, but not diversity\. On Antipodes Island, where mice were the sole invasive mammal, abundance of invertebrate taxa preyed upon by mice increased significantly\. On Macquarie Island, except for flies, the abundance of invertebrate taxa preyed upon by mice did not increase\. The legacy impacts of invasive rabbits \( Oryctolagus cuniculus \) and ship rats persist in the island&\#x27;s ecosystem\. Rodent eradications on islands benefit invertebrate communities\. Restoration may take longer when a complex of invasive mammals has been eradicated\.

## [Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds](../publications/7f6bf0733e10c66b0863.md)

Franck B\.N\. Tonle; Alcade Segnon; Mori W\. Gouroubera; Dan Makumbi; Hugo De Groote; Saliou Niassy; Takemore Chagomoka; Henri Tonnang; Robert Zougmore

Parasitic weeds \(Striga spp\.\) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions\. We developed a spatially\-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems\. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1\.04 billion \(95% confidence interval: US$0\.94–1\.15 billion\) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses\. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas\. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high\-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas\. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data\-scarce regions\. Parasitic weeds damage maize harvests across Africa, but their economic cost has been unclear\. This study estimates about US$1 billion in annual losses, concentrated in hotspots; targeted control and spread prevention could help protect maize

## [Valorization of banana and bamboo leaf ash for sustainable binders with strength, microstructure](../publications/7f6f3e41a96e45abcf3a.md)

G\. Murali; Momo Gleh Mason; Patchamatla J\. Rama Raju; Leong Sing Wong; Marzena Kurpińska; Hakim Salem Abdelgader; V\. Ramkumar; Siva Avudaiappan

The cement sector is a major emitter of CO 2 , highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to ordinary Portland cement\. At the same time, agricultural residues such as banana biomass and bamboo leaves are largely underutilised, creating environmental burdens\. While supplementary cementitious materials \(SCM\) support low\-carbon construction, conventional sources are declining, and agro\-waste binders remain poorly understood, particularly in terms of pozzolanic activity, calcination requirements, and cementitious performance\. This study addresses these gaps by valorizing calcined banana and bamboo leaf ashes as eco\-friendly SCMs, advancing circular resource utilisation and sustainable binder development\. Ordinary Portland cement was partially substituted with banana leaf ash \(BALA\) and bamboo leaf ash \(BLA\) at replacement levels of 5, 10, 15, and 20%\. The resulting mortar mixtures were systematically evaluated for their mechanical performance and microstructural characteristics\. The results reveal that 5% BLA achieved the highest compressive strength \(63\.33 MPa at 14 days and 79\.35 MPa at 28 days\), whereas higher BLA and all BALA replacement levels reduced strength, with 20% BALA exhibiting the lowest values \(45\.40 and 61\.17 MPa\), confirming 5% BLA as the optimum sustainable cement replacement level\. This indicating 5% BLA as the optimum replacement level under the present experimental conditions when compressive strength and microstructural densification considered together\. However, 15% BLA minimized water absorption, indicating a trade\-off between mechanical strength and resistance to water ingress\. Microstructural analysis confirmed the higher pozzolanic reactivity of BLA through greater portlandite consumption, enhanced secondary C\-S\-H formation, and improved thermal stability, while BALA showed slower and weaker reactions\. Excessive replacement \(≥ 20%\) resulted in clinker dilution, increased carbonation, and reduced matrix compactness, highlighting the need for controlled ash dosage\.

## [Prenatal air pollution exposure and the risk of transient tachypnea of the newborn](../publications/7f6ff1f62a6dc6c18668.md)

Fang‐Ju Lin; Ching\-Heng Lin; Yi\-Hsuan Lin; Ming\-Chih Lin

Objective Although prenatal exposure to ambient air pollution is known to compromise neonatal health, its specific impact on transient tachypnea of the newborn \(TTN\), a prevalent cause of neonatal respiratory distress, has rarely been investigated on a population\-based scale\. This study aimed to evaluate the association between maternal exposure to certain air pollutants during pregnancy and the risk of TTN, as well as regional variations from a nationwide perspective\. Methods We conducted a nationwide, nested case\-cohort study using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database linked to the Maternal and Child Health Database \(2004–2020\)\. Newborns of primiparous mothers diagnosed with TTN \( n = 3,091\) were matched with healthy controls \( n = 12,364\) at a 1:4 ratio based on maternal age, neonatal sex, and birth date\. Individual prenatal exposure across the 40 weeks preceding birth was estimated by mapping maternal residential postal codes to the nearest of 71 active air monitoring stations\. Multiple logistic regression models were adjusted for comprehensive perinatal and clinical confounders\. Results Multivariate analysis demonstrated that elevated prenatal exposure to carbon monoxide \(CO\) was strongly associated with an increased risk of TTN \(adjusted odds ratio \[aOR\]: 1\.806, 95% CI: 1\.312–2\.487; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Significant risk elevations were also identified for nitrogen oxides \(NOx\) \(aOR: 1\.010, 95% CI: 1\.005–1\.015; p &lt; 0\.001\) and fine particulate matter \(PM 2\.5 \) \(aOR: 1\.001, 95% CI: 1\.000–1\.002; p = 0\.023\)\. Geographically stratified analysis revealed that these risks were highly pronounced in the traffic\-dominated, urban basin of northern Taiwan \(Taipei and New Taipei City\)\. Conclusion This study demonstrated that prenatal exposure to specific air pollutants, including CO, NOx, and PM 2\.5 is associated with an increased risk of TTN\. Furthermore, our regional analysis suggests that traffic\-related emissions may exert the greatest impact\.

## [Secure Enterprise Deployment of Generative AI through LLMOps Governance and Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure](../publications/7f7c08982fe148b222ed.md)

M\. Balajee Maram

The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) across enterprise environments has created new opportunities forautomation, knowledge management, intelligent decision\-making, and customer service\. However, deploying large languagemodels \(LLMs\) in enterprise settings introduces security, privacy, governance, and operational challenges associated with sensitivedata exposure, unauthorized model access, prompt injection, model supply\-chain vulnerabilities, and inconsistent regulatorycompliance\. Hybrid cloud infrastructure offers a flexible deployment architecture that combines private infrastructure withpublic cloud services, enabling organizations to balance scalability, data sovereignty, and computational efficiency\. This researchinvestigates a secure enterprise deployment framework for generative AI by integrating LLMOps governance with hybrid cloudinfrastructure\. The proposed framework incorporates model lifecycle management, identity and access controls, data protection,continuous monitoring, model evaluation, and policy\-based deployment approval\. Security mechanisms include retrieval accessrestrictions, prompt and output validation, encrypted communication, audit logging, and risk\-based model selection\. Theresearch methodology employs a controlled experimental environment to compare conventional LLM deployment practiceswith the proposed governance\-oriented architecture\. Evaluation metrics include security incident detection, unauthorized dataexposure, response quality, inference latency, compliance coverage, and operational overhead\. The study establishes a systematicfoundation for assessing how integrated LLMOps governance and hybrid cloud controls can improve enterprise AI security whilemaintaining performance, scalability, and operational reliability across diverse organizational environments\.

## [AI\-assisted Socratic Questioning for Formal Proof Competence in Plane Geometry: A Literature Review](../publications/7f930e0904625bfa6498.md)

I Putu Wisna Ariawan; ⁠I Made Candiasa; Ni Made Sri Mertasari; Dewa Gede Hendra Divayana; I Made Sugiarta

Formal proof is at the heart of university\-level plane geometry because it requires students to build deductively valid arguments based on definitions, theorems, and known results, rather than visual observation or intuition\. However, students often struggle to justify inferential steps, while generative artificial intelligence can provide fluent proofs before learners examine diagrams, check theorem conditions, or construct their own reasoning\. This conceptual article proposes a Warrant\-Seeking Socratic AI Framework for supporting formal proof learning in plane geometry\. Literature was searched in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and Google Scholar from March 15 to May 21, 2026, using terms related to formal proof, geometry, Socratic questioning, and artificial intelligence\. Of 72 records identified, 14 duplicates were removed, leaving 58 sources for screening, full\-text assessment, and narrative synthesis\. Sources were synthesized by identifying recurring pedagogical and epistemic functions related to proof construction, questioning, AI interaction, and validation\. Based on the synthesis: problem orientation, conjecture articulation, theorem\-condition analysis, inferential construction, proof validation, and metacognitive reflection, a six\-phase recursive model is proposed\. The framework positions AI as an epistemic interviewer rather than a proof generator, prompting students to distinguish visual conjectures from warranted claims, examine theorem conditions, justify inferential steps, and retain ownership of their proofs\. The synthesis distinguishes evidence directly related to geometry and mathematical proving from findings extrapolated from broader educational contexts\. The framework is therefore a theoretically grounded proposition rather than an empirically validated model, and its effectiveness remains to be established through future empirical research\.

## [Early serum n‐6 and n‐3 fatty acid profile and preschool‐age neurodevelopment](../publications/7f9ce4e89cec883c6c9f.md)

Sara Berggren; Josefine Roswall; Maria Blomqvist; Ola Andersson

OBJECTIVES: Evidence suggests that adequate supplies of omega\-6 \(n\-6\) and omega\-3 \(n\-3\) fatty acids \(FAs\) are beneficial for brain development, but serum data are scarce\. We explored correlations between early serum proportions of n\-6 and n\-3 FAs and neurodevelopment at 4 years of age\. METHODS: Serum proportions for docosahexaenoic acid \(DHA\), total n\-3 and the n\-6/n\-3 ratio were analysed from umbilical\-cord, at 4 and 12 months for 119 children born vaginally at full\-term at the Halland Hospital Halmstad, Sweden, in 2008\-2009\. Neurodevelopmental testing at 4 years of age included the complete Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence \(WPPSI\-III\) and the Ages and Stages Questionnaire \(ASQ\-3\)\. Pearson correlation analysis was conducted for WPPSI\-III and Spearman&\#x27;s rho for ASQ\-3 followed by forward\-selection regression models for significant correlations\. RESULTS: Higher proportions of DHA, n\-3 FAs and low n\-6/n\-3 ratio at birth correlated with higher gross motor scores at age 4 \(Spearman&\#x27;s rho, 0\.278, 0\.292 and \-0\.261, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Low n\-6/n\-3 ratio at 12 months correlated with higher full\-scale intelligence quotient \(IQ\) and higher verbal IQ \(\-0\.279 and \-0\.269, p &lt; 0\.05\), at age 4\. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, elevated serum n\-3 FAs and low n\-6/n\-3 ratio during the brain growth spurt show statistical correlations with higher neurodevelopmental scores with respect to motor control, verbal abilities, and overall cognition at 4 years of age, with small\-to moderate effect sizes\.

## [Generative AI in Higher Education: Global Trends, Challenges, and Policy Implications](../publications/7fb6df630d12e22cb35d.md)



Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral tool to a routine feature of student life in higher education\.This paper examines how generative AI, and ChatGPT specifically, is used across global and regional student populations, and what challenges accompany that use\.Drawing on secondary analysis of four public survey datasets, including a global sample of 23,218 students across 110 countries \(Ravšelj et al\., 2025\) and three available regional datasets from Bangladesh, Colombia, and Ecuador, the study addresses three research questions concerning prevalence and institutional readiness, task level application and regional variation, and the ethical and institutional challenges tied to AI adoption\.Results show that 71\.4% of the global sample had used ChatGPT, primarily for brainstorming, summarizing, and research assistance, though usage intensity and institutional policy awareness varied meaningfully by region\.The three regional datasets converge on a common theme even though each measure it differently: a substantial share of students report reduced verification behavior and self\-perceived overreliance on AI tools, a pattern this paper terms experienced dependency to distinguish it from the abstract ethical concern measured by the global dataset\.The paper argues that adoption, ethical concern, and experienced dependency function as related but distinct dimensions rather than opposite poles of a single spectrum, and that institutions should track them independently\.Implications for policy, faculty development, and future research are discussed\.

## [Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina \(Sicily, Italy\)](../publications/7fbaca7d699b599115ef.md)

Mauro Bonasera; Stefania Nisio; Luigi Guerriero

Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina \(Sicily, Italy\), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain\. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross\-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances\. To frame site\-effects in a seismic setting, we consult the Italian catalogue of earthquake\-induced ground failures \(CEDIT\) and the Italian catalogue of earthquake environmental effects \(EEE\), which document widespread ground cracking, settlement and liquefaction during major historical earthquakes, notably the 1908 Messina event\. Our results highlight clusters along culverted stream corridors and in zones influenced by underground legacy, supporting future scenario\-based prioritization of inspections and post\-event checks\.

## [Qiraat Dialectics in Islamic Religious Education: Tracing the History, Standardization, and Diversity of Al\-Qur&\#x27;an Readings](../publications/7fc5f1ee4c8d157a1e12.md)

Sopyan Hadi; Mukhlisin

This research aims to analyze the dialectics of qiraat in Islamic Religious Education by tracing the history of the development of qiraat, the standardization process of the Ottoman Mushaf, and the diversity of Al\-Qur&\#x27;an readings\. This research uses a literature study method with a qualitative\-descriptive approach\. Research data was obtained from the Al\-Qur&\#x27;an, hadith, ulumul Qur&\#x27;an books, books on the science of qiraat, academic books, journal articles, results of previous research, as well as official documents relating to the rasm and pentashihan mushaf\. Data analysis was carried out through the stages of collection, reduction, categorization, interpretation, comparison and synthesis of various relevant sources\. The research results show that qiraat is an important part of Al\-Qur&\#x27;an scholarship related to oral transmission, sanad, Arabic language rules, and Ottoman language\. The diversity of qiraat has been known since the time of Rasulullah SAW and has a reliable basis for narration\. Meanwhile, the standardization of the Ottoman Mushaf was carried out to maintain the unity of the community and establish a standard for the writing of the Qur&\#x27;an, not to eliminate all authentic qiraat\. The relationship between qiraat and the Ottoman Mushaf demonstrates the dialectic between the diversity of readings and the need for a unified written text\. In the context of Islamic Religious Education, the integration of qiraat knowledge can strengthen Qur&\#x27;anic literacy, foster tolerance, enhance critical thinking skills, and instill the value of moderation in responding to differences in Qur&\#x27;anic readings\. Therefore, qiraat knowledge needs to be introduced gradually and proportionally in Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) learning\.

## [Local Epochs as Optimal Stopping: Theory and Evidence in Federated Learning](../publications/7fc82b347a586421c1b4.md)

Ke Xiao; Qiyuan Wang; Christos Anagnostopoulos

How long should each client train before communicating? Federated learning usually answers with a fixed, hand\-tuned number of local epochs, yet an extra epoch helps only while the loss it removes outweighs the client drift it adds\. We cast local training as finite\-horizon optimal stopping: a client trains while the next epoch&\#x27;s expected loss reduction exceeds its priced squared drift\. We prove that this one\-stage look\-ahead threshold is optimal whenever stopping decisions are nested, derive closed forms for geometric and power\-law returns, and show that an estimated rule loses utility only through wrong\-signed decisions\. Epoch\-level evidence supports the model&\#x27;s structure \(geometric diminishing returns and additive drift\) and reveals a simple regularity: the stage of training, not the client, sets the budget\. The resulting rule, FedStop, is never more than one point below tuned FedAvg in mean accuracy\. Where its budgets vary, it raises worst\-decile accuracy by 4\-8 points over tuned FedAvg and an adaptive\-interval baseline, and every one of these gains remains significant after a Holm correction\. Against the client\-side stopping rules ALT and FLASH, it has the highest CIFAR\-10 worst decile on every seed and is level elsewhere\. It stays stable where per\-client early stopping collapses, and each stopping decision takes constant time\.

## [A INTERFACE ENTRE ENFERMAGEM ONCOLÓGICA E ENFERMAGEM FORENSE: CUIDADO, SEGURANÇA E PRÁTICA ÉTICA](../publications/7fd7c485e1cb51340685.md)

Lilian Nascimento Rosa; Marlon Felix dos Santos; Priscila Rosa Ribeiro; Rosicleide dos Anjos Costa; Michelly Esteves Silva; Edileuza Maria da Silva; Fabiana Rosa Paiva; Maria de Fátima das Dores; Thiago Moreira; Maria Eliete Silva

Introdução: A assistência prestada pela enfermagem no cenário oncológico exige elevada competência técnica e científica diante da complexidade dos tratamentos e da vulnerabilidade dos pacientes\. Simultaneamente, a ascensão da enfermagem forense destaca\-se na gestão de riscos e na garantia da segurança jurídica e assistencial\. Objetivo: Analisar a interface entre a oncologia clínica e a enfermagem forense, identificando atribuições assistenciais, avanços tecnológicos, aspectos ético\-legais e a relevância da humanização\. Metodologia: Revisão integrativa da literatura realizada nas bases BVS, SciELO, PubMed, LILACS, BDENF e CINAHL, compreendendo o período de 2010 a 2025, além de legislações do COFEN e documentos institucionais \(INCA, UICC, OMS\)\. Resultados e Discussão: A literatura demonstra que a atuação do enfermeiro expandiu\-se da assistência paliativa inicial para a navegação, gestão da segurança e aplicação de tecnologias como inteligência artificial e prontuário eletrônico\. O domínio do estadiamento TNM e do manejo de metástases orienta a sistematização do cuidado\. A enfermagem forense insere\-se na investigação de eventos adversos, auditoria rigorosa de prontuários e proteção aos direitos dos pacientes e profissionais\. Conclusão: A integração entre oncologia e enfermagem forense fortalece a assistência baseada em evidências, responde integralmente aos objetivos do estudo ao comprovar que a prática ética, documentada e humanizada reduz riscos e eleva a qualidade da linha de cuidado\.

## [Traceable Burned\-Area Evidence for Territorial Governance: Scenario\-Based multi\-pyDEMATEL and ABBI Mapping in the Vesuvian Interface](../publications/7fd95ad212c1bd106297.md)

Salvatore Polverino; Elif Gizem Yetkin; Hourakhsh Ahmad Nia

MODIS/EFFIS burned\-area archives provide reproducible information on wildfire occurrence, perimeter geometry, administrative attribution, mapped area, date fields, and land\-cover composition\. However, their translation into proportionate municipal documentation, monitoring, coordination, and territorial\-management evidence remains only partially formalized, especially in volcanic–urban interfaces where relatively compact burned\-area records may still generate non\-negligible administrative pressure\. This study develops a scenario\-based multi\-pyDEMATEL workflow for assessing Administrative Burned\-Area Burden in the Vesuvian interface, southern Italy\. Rather than modelling burn severity, hydrogeomorphic susceptibility, legal responsibility, or field\-validated damage, the analysis reframes MODIS/EFFIS records as traceable administrative evidence for multi\-criteria decision\-chain screening\. Four bounded objectives are addressed: \(i\) to construct a GIS\-ready burned\-area support for the Vesuvian interface while retaining Napoli and Campania layers as contextual references; \(ii\) to derive ten non\-hydrogeomorphic Administrative Burned\-Area descriptors describing burned\-area share, recurrence, large\-event dominance, administrative concentration, protected\-area exposure, agricultural exposure, urban/interface exposure, forest–shrubland signature, event\-duration burden, and reporting/update lag; \(iii\) to structure these descriptors through a scenario\-based multi\-pyDEMATEL ensemble comprising 121 scenario\-specific DEMATEL computations, and to audit the resulting fingerprints through PCA; and \(iv\) to translate the resulting Administrative Burned\-Area Burden Index into municipal ABBI classes suitable for QGIS visualization, documentation prioritization, and verification\-oriented monitoring\. The results indicate a marked concentration of Vesuvian burned\-area burden across a limited number of event and municipal supports, while the DEMATEL/PCA outputs help distinguish stable and divergent descriptor configurations within the administrative evidence system\. The resulting ABBI layer is therefore interpreted as a governance\-sensitive, GIS\-ready decision\-support product, not as a hazard map, burn\-severity product, legal\-liability surface, municipal\-responsibility boundary, or DEM\-derived susceptibility model\. The framework provides a reproducible audit chain for converting open burned\-area archives into cautious and interpretable territorial\-management evidence\.

## [Perceptions, experiences, and mental health outcomes of surgical posting among medical students](../publications/7ff04b668093835c34ce.md)

Qozeem Opeyemi Asafa; Esther Boluwatife Omolosho; Aishat Omowunmi Asafa; Olajide Emmanuel Babalola; Kehinde Adesola Alatishe; Adebukola Ganiyu Oyeniyi; Kehinde Awodele; Ayodeji Olaolu Oyeniran; Kabir Ademola Jimoh; Adegboyega Segun Afolabi

Objectives: Surgical rotations play a vital role in undergraduate medical training by exposing students to practical patient care and operative practice\. Although these experiences strengthen clinical competence, the demanding nature of surgical training may negatively influence students&\#x27; psychological well\-being\. This study explored the relationship between experiences during surgical posting and mental health among clinical medical students\. Material and Methods: A descriptive cross\-sectional study was conducted between April and June 2026 at UNIOSUN Teaching Hospital, Osogbo, Nigeria, among undergraduate clinical medical students in their first, second, and final years of clinical training \(400\-, 500\-, and 600\-level classes\)\. Participants were selected using a stratified random sampling technique\. A total of 216 questionnaires were distributed, of which 191 were returned, giving a response rate of 88\.4%\. After excluding 22 questionnaires because of incomplete responses, 169 questionnaires \(78\.2% of those distributed\) were included in the final analysis\. Information was obtained using a pretested, validated, self\-administered questionnaire covering the clinical learning environment, surgical exposure, workload, mental health challenges, and coping strategies\. Data were analysed with IBM SPSS Statistics version 27 using descriptive statistics and the Pearson chi\-square test\. Statistical significance was defined as p &lt; 0\.05\. Results: Most respondents viewed the teaching and learning environment positively \(75\.7%\) and reported satisfactory clinical exposure \(87\.0%\)\. Despite these favourable educational experiences, 74\.0% described their workload as high, while 73\.4% experienced substantial psychological challenges during the surgical rotation\. Good coping strategies and supportive networks were reported by 70\.4% of participants\. A significant association was observed between surgical posting experiences and mental health outcomes \(χ 2 = 69\.695, df = 1, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion: Surgical posting offered valuable opportunities for clinical learning but was accompanied by considerable psychological demands\. Strengthening mentorship, expanding student support services, and incorporating mental health promotion into surgical training programs may improve students&\#x27; well\-being while maintaining the educational quality of clinical rotations\.

## [Human–AI interaction in parotid ultrasound diagnosis: a prospective two\-phase observer\-performance study](../publications/7ffee7759349902153b1.md)

Jeonghwan Kim; Seyeon Lee; Hyewon Hwang; Soonho Ha; Yeongmin Kim; Inyong Jeong; Min\-Suk Kim; Byungjae Kang; Joon Hong Kim; Sung Jun Hong; Young Hen Lee; Yeon Soo Kim; Seung\-Kuk Baek; Sung\-Hye You; Hyojeong Kim; Hyun Soo Park; Yeojin Yoo; Thomas J\. Kwack; Soon Young Kwon; Hwamin Lee

Differentiating pleomorphic adenoma \(PA\) from Warthin’s tumor \(WT\) — the two most common benign parotid neoplasms — on ultrasound is challenging even for experienced ultrasonographers\. Most existing AI systems for parotid ultrasound have been static, retrospective, and tested without prospective reader evaluation\. We developed a confidence\-aware AI system with a radiologist\-editable interface and prospectively evaluated its impact on radiologist performance in an observer\-performance study\. We developed a confidence\-aware hybrid pipeline combining a YOLO detection model with a classification model fallback for parotid ultrasound differentiation, using an internal dataset of 949 images \(Korea University Ansan Hospital\) and an external dataset of 427 images \(Korea University Anam Hospital\)\. We exploratorily evaluated 35 detection × classification combinations to characterize model complementarity, and then prospectively validated a single pre\-specified deployment configuration \(τ = 0\.80, YOLOv12m \+ ConvNeXt\) through a two\-phase observer\-performance study with three board\-certified radiologists on 107 external cases \(321 reads total\)\. Standalone detection and classification models achieved external AUROCs of 0\.811 and 0\.919, respectively\. The confidence\-aware pipeline outperformed both standalone models in 22 of 35 combinations on external data \(highest macro\-F1 = 0\.838\) with the complementary effect most apparent when the two models performed comparably\. In the reader study, AI assistance improved pooled diagnostic accuracy from 76\.3% to 81\.6% \(generalized linear mixed model \[GLMM\] odds ratio = 1\.54, 95% CI: 1\.12–2\.13, p = 0\.008\) and inter\-reader agreement \(Fleiss’ κ increasing from 0\.475 to 0\.611\), with larger gains on more difficult cases\. Reader response was selective: readers followed correct AI predictions more often than incorrect ones \(76\.2% vs\. 51\.1%, p = 0\.008\), and per\-class sensitivity changed in opposite directions for WT \(\+ 18\.1% points\) and PA \(− 9\.3% points\), aligning with the AI’s prediction profile\. A confidence\-aware AI system with a radiologist\-editable interface improved radiologist diagnostic accuracy and inter\-reader agreement in a prospective observer\-performance study\. These findings support the system’s potential as a decision\-support tool that operates alongside the interpreting physician, and motivate further evaluation in real\-world clinical workflows\.

## [Pretransplant plasma soluble PD\-1 and recurrence after liver transplantation in ICI\-treated hepatocellular carcinoma: an exploratory biomarker study](../publications/8009aa1b81406df56a90.md)

Lizhen Zhu; Ruolin Wang; Wenzhi Shu; Yi Gao; Geng Zhang; Wenlong Zhao; Yucheng Hou; Qian Lü

Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors \(ICIs\) are increasingly used as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplantation \(LT\) for hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\), but biomarkers of posttransplant recurrence in this setting are lacking\. We evaluated the association between pretransplant plasma soluble programmed death\-1 \(sPD\-1\) and posttransplant outcomes after pretransplant ICI therapy\. Methods We enrolled 105 HCC patients undergoing LT, including 51 receiving ICIs and 54 without prior ICI exposure\. Pretransplant plasma sPD\-1 and sPD\-L1 were measured by ELISA\. The primary endpoint was 2\-year recurrence\-free survival \(RFS\)\. Associations were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression\. Results Pretransplant sPD\-1 was higher in the ICI group than in the non\-ICI group \(P &lt; 0\.0001\)\. Within the ICI\-treated cohort, patients who experienced recurrence had higher sPD\-1 than those who did not \(P = 0\.0002\), whereas sPD\-L1 did not differ\. At an internally derived exploratory cutoff of 2073 pg/mL, high sPD\-1 was associated with lower 2\-year RFS \(7\.7% vs\. 76\.3%; log\-rank P &lt; 0\.0001; HR, 4\.42; 95% CI, 1\.75–11\.17\)\. As a continuous variable, each doubling of pretransplant sPD\-1 was associated with an increased risk of recurrence in the unadjusted analysis \(HR = 1\.51, 95% CI 1\.25–1\.82; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The association remained significant after adjustment for AFP, tumor number, and maximum tumor diameter \(adjusted HR = 1\.51, 95% CI 1\.20–1\.89; P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion Elevated pretransplant sPD\-1 is independently associated with increased posttransplant recurrence risk in HCC patients receiving ICIs before LT\. This association remained after adjustment for AFP and pretransplant tumor burden, and appeared distinct from MVI status, ACR occurrence, and the timing of blood sampling\. sPD\-1 may serve as a complementary biomarker for risk stratification, but external validation is required\.

## [Being recognized as human by AI: algorithmic disrespect and the crisis of recognition in the digital age](../publications/800a9acdb4e591142351.md)

Min Tang; Jinqi Yan

Artificial intelligence increasingly does more than identify individuals; in many institutional contexts, it helps determine who is seen, trusted, and included\. This paper argues that algorithmic systems increasingly participate in practices of social recognition, and that their failures can become forms of structural disrespect when classifications acquire institutional authority and shape how persons are treated\. Drawing from Hegelian and Honnethian recognition theory, the paper introduces the concept of algorithmic disrespect, manifesting across three dimensions: embodied \(when certain bodies are excluded from visibility\), agential \(when predictive models preempt human action\), and symbolic \(when value is indexed through computational relevance\)\. These mechanisms indicate a crisis in the social grammar of recognition, where data replaces dialogue and visibility becomes a tool of both inclusion and domination\. Rather than treating algorithmic bias as a problem of fairness alone, the study reframes it as a philosophical and political issue, rooted in how AI systems mediate identity, agency, and esteem\. The paper concludes by proposing a relational ethics of recognition grounded in justification, accountability, and institutional responsiveness, shifting attention from model\-level corrections to the infrastructural conditions under which recognition is distributed\. In doing so, it repositions recognition as both a site of harm and a potential locus of democratic struggle in algorithmic society\.

## [An Intelligent SDN\-Enabled Framework for Real\-Time IPv6 IP Spoofing Detection and Prevention](../publications/801ec1c4c713e0d37f6e.md)

Navaneethan C\. Arjuman; Ahmad Fikri Sharudin; Zar Chi Hlaing; Supriyanto Praptodiyono

With the increase in the adoption of Internet Protocol version 6 \(IPv6\), the issue of Internet Protocol \(IP\) spoofing has remained a significant risk that damages the integrity of networks\. Although some countermeasures, like Secure Neighbor Discovery \(SEND\) and Router Advertisement \(RA\) Guard, are available, these solutions are complex to deploy, consume high resources, and can be bypassed by advanced attacks\. This paper provides a critical review of the available IPv6 spoofing prevention methods and proposes an enhanced multi\-layered framework that uses improved ingress and egress filtering, Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\-based anomaly detection, and Software\-Defined Networking \(SDN\) to automatically mitigate threats in real time\. The enhanced framework is precisely identifying spoofed traffic, whereas SDN dynamically applies policies in the network to isolate and block malicious sources without affecting legitimate traffic\. The framework is implemented over a Mininet and Docker\-based setup in which it is tested under controlled and real\-world traffic conditions\. It had an average precision and recall of 0\.98 with an F1\-score of 0\.97 and a prevention latency averaging less than 0\.4 seconds\. Through the centralized traffic visibility provided by SDN and the pattern recognition capabilities of Machine Learning \(ML\), the proposed framework adjusts smoothly to traffic changes and new spoofing techniques\. Its modular architecture allows it to be integrated into existing systems and deployed in a manner that does not interfere with the flow of operations\. The proposed solution is better in robustness, scalability, and adaptability than any traditional static filtering approach, and therefore it is a practical approach to enhance security in both dual\-stack and IPv6\-only network environments\. This research provides practical implications and further highlights the possibility of ML and SDN contributions in the creation of proactive IPv6 security systems

## [How gender shapes public speaking in virtual reality: a multimodal analysis](../publications/80327ec437344b2f370c.md)

Marion Ristorcelli; Rémy Casanova; Magalie Ochs

Virtual Reality \(VR\) has proven effective for public speaking training, particularly due to its ability to simulate immersive speaking environments and automatically extract behavioral cues reflecting performance\. However, limited attention has been paid to the impact of speaker gender and the gendered appearance of the virtual audience on the public speaking experience in VR\. To address this gap, we conducted an experiment with 55 participants who performed oral presentations within a VR simulation that allowed for the systematic manipulation of the virtual audience&\#x27;s gendered appearance and social attitude\. We captured a comprehensive dataset of multimodal nonverbal behavioral data, alongside subjective evaluations from both the participants and an expert using standardized and non\-standardized questionnaires\. By combining statistical analysis and machine learning approaches, our findings revealed no significant effect of speaker gender on her/his emotional experience or her/his public speaking performance\. In contrast, male and female speakers exhibited distinct nonverbal behavioral patterns, identified through both expert evaluation and automatic multimodal behavioral analysis\. Moreover, Virtual audience social attitude influenced participants&\#x27; emotional experience and self\-reported performance, whereas no significant effect of audience gendered appearance was detected\. These findings highlight the importance of considering behavioral variability when studying and assessing public speaking in VR\.

## [Orchestrating cancer stem cell plasticity: deubiquitinases as key regulators of EMT and metabolic rewiring](../publications/803867ad19eb039e530b.md)

Tao Qin; Yupeng Wang; Minhao Li; Qian Liu; Lu Yue; Shuzhen Liang; Duoping Sun

Cancer stem cells \(CSCs\) drive tumor relapse, metastasis, and multidrug resistance, primarily attributed to their profound phenotypic plasticity\. This plasticity largely depends on the dynamic interplay between the epithelial\-mesenchymal transition \(EMT\) program and metabolic reprogramming\. However, the molecular mechanisms coordinating these processes remain incompletely elucidated\. Emerging evidence suggests that deubiquitinating enzymes \(DUBs\) may participate in regulating this complex crosstalk\. This review systematically elaborates on the functional roles of DUBs in maintaining CSC characteristics within malignancies, exploring how they regulate CSC fate by modulating developmental signaling cascades \(Wnt/β\-catenin, Hedgehog \(Hh\), Notch, and TGF\-β\)\. By preventing the proteasomal degradation of key transcription factors, DUBs simultaneously drive EMT and coordinate metabolic reprogramming to meet the energetic demands of migrating CSCs\. Furthermore, we emphasize the bidirectional feedback loops between EMT\-TFs and DUBs, which cooperatively amplify stemness\. Finally, selective targeting of the DUB\-EMT\-metabolism axis may represent a potential strategy for dismantling CSC plasticity and improving responses to anticancer therapies\.

## [Potential effectiveness of war\-adapted brief prolonged exposure for PTSD prevention: preliminary study among Nova Festival survivors during ongoing conflict](../publications/803cc0c759c398a3e473.md)

Nitsa Nacasch; Hadas Afgin; Netta Shoenfeld; Ilanit Wul; Gay Meschiany; Edna B\. Foa; Raz Gross; Nadav Goldental; Gal Levi; Joseph Zohar; Mark Weiser; Hagit Cohen

Background The 7 October 2023, terrorist attack at the Nova Festival in southern Israel caused deaths, injuries, hostage\-taking and prolonged life\-threatening exposure, creating an urgent need for early interventions to reduce post\-traumatic morbidity\. Although prolonged exposure is an established post\-traumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\) treatment, its feasibility and benefit during ongoing threat remain unclear\. Aims This preliminary study evaluated a war\-adapted brief prolonged exposure protocol \(WBPE\) delivered shortly after trauma in Nova Festival survivors with acute stress disorder\. Method Forty survivors completed the WBPE and were assessed at baseline and immediately post treatment\. A subsample of 27 WBPE completers and 18 untreated wait\-list controls was reassessed after 5 months\. Outcomes were PTSD \(PDS\-5\), depression \(PHQ\-9\) and anxiety \(GAD\-7\) symptom severity\. Results WBPE was associated with significant reductions in PTSD, depression and anxiety immediately after treatment\. At 5 months, WBPE participants showed greater reductions in PTSD and depressive symptom severity and lower PTSD and depression symptom scores than controls, with large effect sizes\. Anxiety symptoms improved in both groups, consistent with possible natural recovery\. Clinically significant depressive symptoms \(48\.15 v \. 77\.78%\) and anxiety symptoms \(37\.04 v \. 72\.22%\) were less frequent in WBPE participants than controls, whereas probable PTSD rates did not differ significantly\. Substance use during the study period was associated with poorer outcomes and smaller symptom reductions\. Conclusions WBPE appears feasible and potentially beneficial under wartime conditions, with meaningful improvements in PTSD and depression despite persistent threat\. Substance use was linked to poorer recovery and should be systematically assessed in post\-trauma care\.

## [Machine Learning &amp; Artificial Intelligence in the Development of Gastro\-Retentive Drug Delivery Systems: Current Advances &amp; Future Prospectives](../publications/8043c42c69cc9ad54900.md)

Sahil Sanjay Nantekar; Madan Pomaje; Avadhut Nitin Hande; Sanika Mahesh Gangan; Ashwini Patil

The integration of machine learning \(ML\) and artificial intelligence \(AI\) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems\. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems \(GRDDS\) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows\. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time\-consuming and resource\-intensive\. AI and ML bring a data\-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters\. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods\. AI\-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior\. Moreover, AI can streamline experimental design, reduce trial\-anderror iterations, and accelerate the development timeline, thus improving formulation robustness and performance\. The convergence of AI with gastroprotective systems also promises personalized approaches that account for patient\-specific gastric motility and physiological factors, fostering tailored therapies\. Although challenges remain—such as the need for high\-quality datasets, interpretability of complex models, and integration with regulatory frameworks—the current advances provide a compelling foundation for future research\. Embracing these intelligent tools in GRDDS development is likely to expand the frontiers of oral drug delivery by enhancing design precision, improving therapeutic outcomes, and reducing developmental costs\. Continued innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to fully harness the transformative potential of AI and ML in pharmaceutics\.

## [Integrating Unplugged Coding into Experiential Learning: Its Impact on Elementary Students&\#x27; Mathematical Conceptual Understanding](../publications/804e0c114068186097fb.md)

Nurul Hasna Haifa; Hafiziani Eka Putri; Alfiana Nurussama; Teten Ginanjar Rahayu

The integration of coding into Indonesia&\#x27;s elementary curriculum is often constrained by limited technological infrastructure, while students&\#x27; understanding of number\-related concepts remains low\. This study examined the effectiveness of an experiential learning model based on unplugged coding in improving elementary students&\#x27; conceptual understanding of numbers\. Using a quantitative quasi\-experimental approach with a Nonequivalent Control Group Design, 48 third\-grade students from Purwakarta Regency \(2025/2026 academic year\) were purposively selected and divided into an experimental group \(24 students\), taught with the unplugged\-coding\-based experiential model, and a control group \(24 students\), taught using Problem\-Based Learning\. Conceptual understanding was measured through a descriptive test covering four indicators, with data analyzed via normality, homogeneity, and independent\-sample t\-tests, and N\-Gain calculations using SPSS\. Results showed a statistically significant difference between groups \(p = 0\.005\), with the experimental group scoring higher than the control group\. The N\-Gain analysis revealed an average improvement of 60\.34% \(moderately effective\) in the experimental group versus 42\.83% \(least effective\) in the control group\. These findings confirm that the unplugged\-coding\-based experiential learning model effectively enhances students&\#x27; understanding of number concepts, offering a practical, technology\-independent strategy for resource\-limited educational settings\.

## [Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration](../publications/804fd8441d4f549f381c.md)

Yingzhi He; Yunjia Jiang; Lingyao Wang; Weidong Zhu; Banglin Chen; Yuanbin Zhang

ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes\. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption\. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels\. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged \(Hbpa \+ \) and negatively charged \(HEDP 4− \) recognition sites\. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated \(ZNU‐33‐α\), intermediate \(ZNU‐33‐β\), partially dehydrated \(ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2\), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition\. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2\+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains\. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake \(9\.50 mmol/g at 2\.85 kPa and 298 K\) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons\. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites\. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents\.

## [Pedraza, R\.: Replication processes in Artificial Research by Deduction in the Global Artificial Intelligence](../publications/8059d899266e589f443f.md)



In Global Artificial Intelligence: First Prototype of Global Artificial Intelligence\. London: Ruben Garcia Pedraza\. pp\. 1\-24\. 2025This paper explores the replication processes involved in Artificial Research by Deduction within the framework of the Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\)\. Specifically, it focuses on the second stage of Artificial Research by Deduction, which follows the construction of the global matrix—a unified, standardized data architecture formed by integrating specific matrices and databases from all sciences, disciplines, and activities\. The paper adopts the second strategy of matrix construction, wherein each specific matrix is treated as a single factor supplying structured flows of information packages composed of nested sub\-factors\. Once the global matrix begins receiving data from robotic measurement systems, the flow of information packages is continuously transformed into a flow of empirical hypotheses\. These hypotheses are then subjected to rational contrastation, using statistical, probabilistic, or other logical methods\. Validated hypotheses become part of the system’s rational truth, supporting the construction of virtual models and informing descriptive research decisions grounded in moral and practical principles\. These decisions are transferred to the Decisional System, while hypotheses and models are forwarded to the Modelling System to generate predictive and evolutionary models\. The paper emphasizes the collaborative and recursive interaction among all core systems of GAI—including Artificial Research by Deduction, the Modelling System, the Decisional System, the Learning System, and the Application System—each functioning as an autonomous yet interdependent organ within a unified cognitive structure\. The result is a non\-stop, self\-sustaining process of scientific reasoning and decision\-making, effectively replicating human rationality at a planetary scale\. Ultimately, the replication processes described here pave the way toward full auto\-replication, the third and final stage of Artificial Intelligence, in which the system evolves, improves, and sustains itself independently\. \(direct link \)

## [TyG\-ABSI and TyG\-WWI as insulin\-resistance body shape markers of mortality in middle\-aged and older adults within the cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic framework](../publications/805ab964a40b603a011b.md)

Fangping Xiao; Hui Guo; Lei Wang; Yanyan Qu; Chunsun Dai

Insulin resistance, adiposity, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease are closely interconnected in middle\-aged and older adults and are central to the cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic \(CKM\) framework\. Triglyceride\-glucose \(TyG\)\-related indices combine routine lipid, glucose, and anthropometric information, but their cross\-population consistency and incremental prognostic value for mortality\-risk assessment remain uncertain\. We analyzed harmonized participant\-level data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey \(NHANES\), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing \(ELSA\), China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study \(CHARLS\), and Health and Retirement Study \(HRS\), with HRS used as a sensitivity cohort\. Eligible participants were aged ≥ 50 years, had follow\-up beyond baseline, available mortality status, and complete data for 7 TyG\-related indices\. Cohort\-specific Cox models estimated associations of standardized TyG, TyG\-body mass index, TyG\-waist circumference, TyG\-waist\-to\-height ratio, TyG\-weight\-adjusted waist index \(WWI\), TyG\-a body shape index \(ABSI\), and TyG\-body roundness index with all\-cause mortality\. Nonlinearity, proportional\-hazards assumptions, sensitivity analyses, NHANES heart disease mortality, incremental prediction, and survival machine learning with external validation were further assessed\. The primary analytic sample included 21,044 NHANES participants, 5454 ELSA participants, and 11,157 CHARLS participants, among whom 5566, 116, and 1393 deaths occurred during follow\-up, respectively\. The HRS sensitivity cohort included 4103 participants and 484 deaths\. In fully adjusted Cox models, all 7 TyG\-related indices were associated with higher all\-cause mortality in NHANES, with the strongest associations observed for TyG\-ABSI \(hazard ratio \[HR\] 1\.159, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] 1\.115\-1\.205\) and TyG\-WWI \(HR 1\.155, 95% CI 1\.113\-1\.199\)\. In CHARLS, TyG\-ABSI was positively associated with mortality \(HR 1\.088, 95% CI 1\.029\-1\.151\), whereas estimates in ELSA were imprecise\. In HRS sensitivity analyses, TyG\-WWI and TyG\-ABSI remained positively associated with mortality\. Adding TyG\-related indices to a clinical Cox prediction framework produced only minimal absolute gains in discrimination\. The final TyG\-ABSI extreme gradient boosting survival model yielded 5\-year time\-dependent area under the curves of 0\.808 in the NHANES internal test set and 0\.760 in CHARLS\. A research\-use web calculator was developed for 5\-year and 8\-year mortality\-risk estimation\. TyG\-ABSI and TyG\-WWI were the most consistent TyG\-related body shape markers of all\-cause mortality across international aging cohorts\. Although TyG\-ABSI supported externally validated survival prediction, its incremental predictive value beyond established clinical and CKM variables was limited\. These findings suggest that TyG\-related body shape indices may serve primarily as interpretable, low\-cost CKM risk markers rather than standalone prediction tools\.

## [Selective etching of 2D materials for quantum computing devices: A computational perspective](../publications/806cc20aaf60ef0c691f.md)

Md\. Aminul Islam; Safiullah Khan; Nayem Hossain; Abdullah Al Alif; Sabiha Jannat; Mst\. Fahmida Akter; Mithila Farzana; Jannatul Fardous Shorna

Achieving atomic\-level precision in the fabrication of quantum devices built from two\-dimensional \(2D\) materials requires a thorough understanding of how selective etching reshapes surface chemistry, defect populations, and electronic structure at the nanoscale\. This review consolidates recent computational advances in density functional theory, molecular dynamics, machine learning, and quantum chemical methods that model etching pathways in graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides, hexagonal boron nitride, and MXenes\. We critically assess how these simulations predict etchant–surface reactivity, defect\-driven selectivity, and post\-etch changes in band structure, spin–orbit coupling, valley polarization, and coherence lifetimes\. Key experimental validations, including graphene Josephson junctions, etched double quantum dots, and MoS₂ valley qubits, illustrate how reliably simulations can guide fabrication\. Closed\-loop machine\-learning–density\-functional\-theory frameworks and digital twin architectures are highlighted as promising routes toward automated, adaptive manufacturing of quantum\-grade 2D devices\. The review also identifies persistent gaps in multi\-scale modelling and dynamic environment simulation, and suggests directions for future research\.

## [Adaptive interaction in intelligent augmented reality: design decision considerations and framework](../publications/8073d3dbcf5fe202ad89.md)

Shokoufeh Bozorgmehrian; Joseph L\. Gabbard

Integrating Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) into Augmented Reality \(AR\) systems has evolved AR from a passive visualization tool into an intelligent medium for dynamic task execution\. For this new role, Intelligent Augmented Reality \(IAR\) systems must adapt user interfaces \(UIs\) in real\-time to users’ cognitive and physical states, task requirements, and environmental constraints, which raises foundational questions: what design decisions contribute to useful adaptive interaction? To address this question, this paper presents a systematic review of IAR systems through the lens of interaction design at the intersection of AR technologies , AI integration , and User Experience \(UX\) considerations \. After screening 798 peer\-reviewed works, 241 full\-text records were assessed for eligibility\. We reviewed 24 IAR published works based on their interaction features, including proactivity versus reactivity and communication styles and modalities, as well as their types of adaptation and control dynamics\. Analyzing these features led to the development of a taxonomy for Levels of Automation and a top\-down design framework for adaptive UIs in IAR Systems\. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of assistive interaction and semi\-autonomous IAR systems that achieve a balanced integration of adaptive assistance with prioritizing user agency while also revealing a noticeable gap in implicit understanding within current IAR implementations\.

## [THE EFFECT OF ESG DISCLOSURE, CAPITAL INTENSITY, AND SALES GROWTH ON TAX AVOIDANCE PRACTICES IN INDONESIA’S ENERGY SECTOR COMPANIES](../publications/807fa28062f87b2f6d90.md)

Intan Puspitasari; Sari Rusmita; Muhsin

This research analyzes the effect of ESG Disclosure, Capital Intensity, and Sales Growth on Tax Avoidance practices among energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange \(IDX\) for the 2023\-2025 period\. The energy sector warrants investigation due to its complex cost structures, which are highly susceptible to Tax Avoidance practices\. Utilizing a quantitative approach with purposive sampling technique, this research selected a sample of 14 companies\. Data Analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model \(REM\) on EViews\. The results reveal that ESG Disclosure, Capital Intensity, and Sales Growth each have a statistically significant negative effect on Tax Avoidance\. These findings indicate that increased sustainability reporting transparency, higher fixed asset investment, and stable sales growth in energy sector can drive companies toward greater tax compliance\. The novelty of this research lies in the implementation of the latest reporting standard, specifically the GRI Standard 2021 to measure ESG Disclosure, addresses a critical research gap in the existing literature, as previous studies primarily utilized outdated reporting standards\.

## [Generative AI summarization tools and deep reading comprehension among Chinese university students: the mediating role of elaborative processing and the moderating role of reading motivation](../publications/8092087896ec705970ee.md)

Ruyu Bai

Generative AI tools that condense texts into summaries have become a routine part of student reading routines, and educators increasingly worry that convenient summaries displace the effortful processing on which deep comprehension depends\. This study drew on cognitive offloading theory and the levels\-of\-processing framework to test a moderated mediation model in which elaborative processing statistically links generative AI summarization tool use to deep reading comprehension, and reading motivation moderates the negative association between tool use and processing\. Undergraduate students \( N = 608; 53\.6% female; mean age 19\.9 years\) from three universities in Changchun, China, completed a six\-item scale of generative AI summarization tool use, an eight\-item elaborative processing scale adapted from the deep\-processing subscale of the R\-SPQ\-2F, a seven\-item reading motivation measure adapted from the Motivation for Reading Questionnaire, and a researcher\-developed deep reading comprehension test\. Scale reliabilities were satisfactory \(Cronbach alpha = 0\.88, 0\.87, and 0\.86\)\. Tool use correlated negatively with elaborative processing \( r = −0\.41\) and comprehension \( r = −0\.24\); elaborative processing correlated positively with comprehension \( r = 0\.59\)\. PROCESS analyses \(Model 7\) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples showed that tool use negatively predicted elaborative processing \( b = −0\.310, p &lt; 0\.001\) and that this association weakened as reading motivation rose \(interaction b = 0\.433, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Elaborative processing, in turn, predicted comprehension \( b = 10\.097, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas the residual direct path of tool use did not reach significance\. The indirect effect of tool use on comprehension through elaborative processing was significant and negative at low \(−6\.142, 95% BC CI \[−7\.353, −5\.091\]\) and average \(−3\.130, \[−3\.851, −2\.497\]\) reading motivation but nonsignificant at high reading motivation \(−0\.117, \[−0\.876, 0\.629\]\); the index of moderated mediation was 4\.374 \[3\.428, 5\.402\]\. These results are consistent with an account in which elaborative processing statistically links summary reliance to lower deep reading, with reading motivation associated with a weaker negative indirect association; given the cross\-sectional design, the modeled paths represent associations rather than established causal effects\. They suggest that motivation\-oriented reading instruction should accompany, rather than follow, the integration of AI tools into academic reading\.
