## [EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post\-Training via Quality\-Diversity Search](../publications/809b50116a0a4e616690.md)

Hanane Nour Moussa; Doeun Lee; Sachin Kumar

Reinforcement learning has become a common post\-training technique to improve the accuracy of LLMs on verifiable tasks\. However, such training can narrow the set of solutions the model can produce\. Several approaches have attempted to address this behavior\-sharpening effect, but they often optimize metrics that do not reflect the diversity of correct solutions\. Ideally, we want a model that can produce multiple good solutions, not only a single reliable one\. We propose EliteReplay, a post\-training recipe that pairs GRPO with an &quot;elite&quot; archive built by quality\-diversity search\. Before training, we use the frozen base model to collect solutions that span distinct approaches; during training, GRPO is combined with a replay loss on this archive\. The result is a post\-trained model that improves accuracy while preserving more of the base model&\#x27;s solution diversity\. On multiple text\-to\-SQL tasks, EliteReplay achieves a higher pass@128 than all baselines, producing up to 77% more distinct correct strategies than the strongest baselines\. It preserves most of the base model&\#x27;s correct strategies, outperforming existing methods in strategy retention\. This diversity translates into practical benefits on ambiguous questions, where EliteReplay covers both interpretations nearly twice as often as the strongest baseline on AmbiQT\.

## [Physics informed distributionally robust learning for urban distribution network resilience under extreme events](../publications/809bc77b0ed558697b29.md)

Fan Bai; Dongbo Yang; Jing Wang; Jingwei Li; Yu Lei

Extreme events expose urban distribution networks to correlated branch outages, uncertain hazard evolution, and rapidly changing operating conditions\. Static indices and repeated Monte Carlo studies remain useful, but they either compress recovery behavior into a fixed score or impose substantial computational cost when many hazard realizations must be screened\. This study develops a physics\-informed, distributionally robust graph\-learning framework for estimating node\- and system\-level resilience from scenario\-dependent topology, measured post\-event operating states, and hazard information\. The contribution lies in the joint implementation of masked graph propagation, auxiliary electrical\-state reconstruction, Wasserstein\-robust training, and a common recovery\-prioritization interface; none of these ingredients is claimed as new in isolation\.The network encoder uses branch\-availability masks and physical edge attributes to update graph messages\. An auxiliary decoder reconstructs voltage, active and reactive injection, and branch\-flow quantities, allowing AC\-balance, voltage, and thermal residuals to regularize the latent representation\. These penalties promote physical consistency but do not constitute hard feasibility guarantees\. Distributional uncertainty is represented by a Wasserstein ball over normalized continuous operating and hazard features, while discrete topology masks remain fixed during each inner maximization\. The learned resilience score is supervised by a transparent trajectory\-based target constructed from restored service, unmet demand, time to 50% recovery, and voltage\-violation exposure\. The principal quantitative evaluation uses 20,000 operating states generated from 500 hazard scenarios on a modified IEEE 123\-bus feeder\. Across five random seeds, the full model attains an MAE of \\\(0\.031\\pm 0\.002\\\) , an RMSE of \\\(0\.042\\pm 0\.003\\\) , and an \\\(R^2\\\) of \\\(0\.935\\pm 0\.008\\\) \. Removing Wasserstein training increases RMSE to \\\(0\.058\\pm 0\.004\\\) , while removing the operator block increases it to \\\(0\.052\\pm 0\.004\\\) \. When every assessment method is coupled to the same restoration simulator, the proposed ranking signal is associated with \\\(25\.1\\%\\pm 1\.5\\%\\\) load shedding at hazard intensity \\\(\\xi =0\.8\\\) and a \\\(2\.48\\pm 0\.16\\\) h time to 50% restoration\. These recovery quantities measure the effect of assessment\-informed prioritization under fixed restoration assumptions; the learning model does not directly issue switching, dispatch, or repair actions\.

## [Tertiary lymphoid structure\-associated chemokine programs define an immune\-organized tumor microenvironment with prognostic relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma](../publications/80a07e8a4d0448f3475f.md)

Kun Chen; Yue\-Qi Wang; Meng\-Chen Guo; Xiaoyu Gu; Xue\-Mei Chen; Su\-Su Luo; Shuang Liu

BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\) exhibits marked heterogeneity in the tumor immune microenvironment, leading to variable outcomes and immunotherapy responses\.Tertiary lymphoid structures \(TLSs\) are organized immune architectures associated with anti\-tumor immunity, but their transcriptomic programs and biomarker potential remain unclear\.AIM To systematically characterize TLS\-associated chemokine programs in HCC by integrating bulk transcriptomic data, single\-cell RNA sequencing \(scRNA\-seq\), and histologically defined TLS status across multiple independent cohorts, and to evaluate their relationship with immune organization and clinical outcomes\.METHODS Transcriptomic TLS signatures were derived from histologically annotated HCC samples in the Cancer Genome Atlas\-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma \(TCGA\-LIHC\) cohort using differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses\.The 12chemokine TLS signature was further evaluated\.scRNA\-seq data from GSE149614 were analyzed to localize TLS\-associated chemokine and receptor expression across cellular compartments\.A TLS\-related prognostic model was constructed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression in the TCGA\-LIHC cohort and externally validated in the International Cancer Genome Consortium\-Liver Cancer\-RIKEN\-Japan \(ICGC\-LIRI\-JP\) cohort\.Prognostic value was assessed using survival analysis and time\-dependent C\-index analysis\.RESULTS 4 / 44 TLS\-associated chemokines were dysregulated in tumors\.CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, CCL19, CCL21, and CXCL13 were downregulated, whereas CCL8, CCL18, CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11 were upregulated\.Higher expression of CCL2, CCL5, CCL8, CCL18, CCL19, CCL21, CXCL9, and CXCL10 was associated with longer OS, and most chemokines with favorable recurrence\-free survival, progression\-free survival and disease\-specific survival\.Single\-cell analysis showed that these chemokines were mainly expressed by T cells, B cells, myeloid cells, and fibroblasts, with T cells as the dominant cell type in CXCL and CCL signaling crosstalk\.Histologically TLS\-positive tumors had better overall survival \(OS\), higher 12\-chemokine scores, lower tumor purity, greater immune infiltration, and increased checkpoint expression\.A seven\-gene model \(CCR7, ICOS, SEMA3C, VTCN1, IRF4, MS4A1, ADAM28\) identified high\-risk patients with poorer OS in TCGA\-LIHC \[hazard ratio \(HR\) = 1\.716,P = 0\.005\] and ICGC\-LIRI\-JP \(HR = 2\.12, P = 0\.035\)\.CONCLUSION TLS\-associated chemokine programs are associated with an organized immune state in HCC and provide a biologically informative framework for immune\-informed prognostic stratification\.

## [La identidad cultural de los pueblos y nacionalidades ecuatorianas frente a la inteligencia artificial y las nuevas formas de aprendizaje](../publications/80a5d772831456008061.md)

Luisana Narcisa Del Rosario Borbor; Mancilla Solís Elvira María; Muñoz Valdez Mónica Azucena; Lourdes Gioconda Bonito Lopez; Margarita del Rocío Pesantes\-Jácome

La acelerada incorporación de la inteligencia artificial \(IA\) y los entornos algorítmicos de aprendizaje en los sistemas educativos plantea tensiones epistémicas profundas respecto a la preservación y fortalecimiento de las identidades culturales comunitarias\. El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar el impacto de la inteligencia artificial y las nuevas formas de aprendizaje en la identidad cultural de los pueblos y nacionalidades del Ecuador, evaluando las dinámicas de apropiación tecnológica, preservación lingüística y soberanía epistemológica en el marco del Sistema de Educación Intercultural Bilingüe \(SEIB\)\. Se desarrolló una investigación de enfoque cuantitativo con alcance descriptivo\-explicativo y diseño cuasi\-experimental con mediciones pretest y postest en dos grupos de estudiantes de bachillerato pertenecientes a unidades educativas comunitarias interculturales bilingües\. Se aplicaron escalas validadas de reafirmación de la identidad cultural, rúbricas de competencias de alfabetización digital crítica y análisis de producciones educativas contextualizadas desarrolladas durante 12 semanas bajo un modelo de aprendizaje mediado por IA generativa adaptada con pertinencia cultural frente a entornos convencionales\. Los resultados evidenciaron mejoras estadísticamente significativas en el grupo experimental en pensamiento crítico intercultural, revitalización de saberes locales y auto reconocimiento identitario, en contraste con el grupo control que experimentó riesgo de asimilación cultural y desplazamiento lingüístico\. La IA no debe operar como un vector homogeneizador eurocéntrico, sino que requiere una reconfiguración descolonial y comunitaria que garantice la soberanía de datos y la supervivencia de las cosmovisiones originarias en la era digital\.

## [Speaking Up in Hierarchical Operating Rooms: A Qualitative Descriptive Study of Nurses&\#x27; Safety Communication With Surgeons and Anaesthetists](../publications/80a7729aad185f3df54e.md)

Yang Guo; Yaqing Quan; Manhong Zhang; Weiwei Zhang

BACKGROUND: Hierarchy can inhibit nurses from raising patient\-safety concerns in operating rooms, yet how Chinese peri\-operative nurses navigate this with surgeons versus anaesthetists remains underexplored\. AIM: To explore when and how peri\-operative nurses in Chinese operating rooms voice, withhold, or adapt patient\-safety concerns with surgeons and anaesthetists\. DESIGN: A multi\-site qualitative descriptive study using the Critical Incident Technique, supplemented by an interpretive interprofessional workshop\. METHODS: Twenty peri\-operative nurses from three tertiary hospitals in Taiyuan, China, were recruited through stratified purposive sampling\. Each completed one in\-depth interview, generating 40 critical incidents, and a subsequent workshop informed interpretation\. Template thematic analysis was conducted, using psychological safety and power distance as sensitizing concepts\. RESULTS: Three themes were developed: \(1\) nurses spoke up mainly when risk was concrete and imminent; \(2\) they used cautious linguistic and non\-verbal strategies to preserve professional relationships and face; \(3\) voice depended on prior punitive experiences, perceived openness, and task relationship\. Anaesthetist\-directed concerns were more collaborative, whereas surgeon\-directed concerns required greater deference\. CONCLUSION: Speaking up was situational, relational, and shaped by hierarchical norms and local team climate, with nurses adapting concerns to different professional audiences\. IMPACT: Nurse voice in Chinese operating rooms is target\-specific, shaped by professional jurisdiction and local team climate\. Findings support nurse managers, peri\-operative educators, and interprofessional leaders in developing psychologically safer climates, hierarchy\-sensitive communication training, and role\-specific strategies for raising concerns with surgeons and anaesthetists\. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Not applicable\.

## [Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) and Teaching Readiness of Pre\-service Teachers](../publications/80af53474be0b0d3b67f.md)

Johnny G\. Basong; Jolina M\. Boteja; Mary Rose S\. Bebillo; Jovan P\. Bermudo; Al Jouie B\. Apolinar; John Mark B\. Traña

Although Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) is widely recognized as an important component of teacher preparation, limited localized evidence explains how TPACK is associated with the teaching readiness of pre\-service teachers, particularly within Bachelor of Elementary Education programs\. This study determined the level of TPACK and teaching readiness and examined the relationship between these two constructs among 233 Bachelor of Elementary Education pre\-service teachers at Don Carlos Polytechnic College during School Year 2025–2026\. A quantitative descriptive\-correlational research design was employed, using a validated researcher\-made questionnaire to gather the data\. Weighted mean was used to determine the levels of TPACK and teaching readiness, while the Pearson Product\-Moment Correlation Coefficient was used to examine their relationship\. The findings revealed that the respondents demonstrated a high level of TPACK with an overall mean of 4\.22, with Integration of Technology in Teaching obtaining the highest mean among the TPACK dimensions\. The respondents also demonstrated a high level of teaching readiness, with an overall mean of 4\.29, with Lesson Planning and Instructional Delivery obtaining the highest mean among the identified dimensions\. Furthermore, the analysis revealed a very strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship between TPACK and teaching readiness \(r = \.820, p &lt; \.001\)\. This indicates that higher levels of TPACK were associated with higher levels of teaching readiness among the respondents\. The findings suggest that TPACK constitutes an important dimension of pre\-service teacher preparation, particularly in developing technological competence alongside pedagogical and content knowledge\. The study contributes localized evidence on the relationship between TPACK and teaching readiness and provides a basis for teacher education institutions to strengthen technology\-integrated coursework, practice\-based learning, and professional development initiatives that prepare future teachers for technology\-enriched and diverse classroom environments\.

## [Orthostatic hypotension in diabetes mellitus: From cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy to clinical management](../publications/80c8916e7a2d4f964b18.md)

Rahul Garg

Orthostatic hypotension \(OH\) is a common yet often overlooked complication of diabetes mellitus that significantly impacts patients&\#x27; quality of life and health outcomes\. This review explores the relationship between diabetes and OH, covering its prevalence, pathophysiology, clinical implications, diagnostic approach, and management strategies\. The pooled prevalence of OH across unselected diabetic populations is approximately 20–24%, notably higher than in the general population, and rises further among patients with established cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy \(CAN\) or diabetic neuropathy\. The pathophysiology is closely linked to CAN, involving impaired baroreflex sensitivity, sympathetic denervation, and endothelial dysfunction\. Poor glycemic control accelerates autonomic nerve damage and worsens OH, while hypoglycemic episodes may independently precipitate hemodynamic instability\. Clinical implications include increased fall risk, cardiovascular events, postprandial hypotension, cognitive impairment, and elevated mortality\. Supine hypertension, coexisting in up to 50% of patients with neurogenic OH, represents a critical therapeutic dilemma\. Diagnosis rests on routine lying\-and\-standing blood pressure measurement and identification of reversible contributors, with autonomic function testing and, in selected cases, plasma norepinephrine measurement or sympathetic imaging reserved for specialist evaluation to distinguish neurogenic from non\-neurogenic subtypes\. Treatment encompasses non\-pharmacological approaches and pharmacological agents, including midodrine, droxidopa, fludrocortisone, and pyridostigmine\. This review emphasizes the importance of an individualized, multifaceted approach, including optimized glycemic control, in managing OH in diabetic patients\.

## [Prevalence and factors associated with suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior among police personnel in Kerala, India: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/80e42ee91a18591f1e9a.md)

Adithya Sasi; Rashita Ravi; Jeby Jose Olickal; Kavumpurathu Raman Thankappan

Introduction Although police personnel are exposed to substantial occupational stress and Kerala has one of the highest suicide rates in India, evidence on suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior among police personnel in the state remains limited\. This study estimated the prevalence of suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior and identified their associated factors among police personnel in Kerala, India\. Methods A cross\-sectional study was conducted among 400 police personnel \(mean age 37\.94 years; 81% men\), from Civil Police Officers \(CPOs\) to Inspectors, recruited from 15 police stations in Ernakulam and Malappuram districts of Kerala using a multistage cluster sampling approach\. Data were collected using a self\-administered structured questionnaire\. Suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior during the past 12 months were assessed using the Columbia\-Suicide Severity Rating Scale \(C\-SSRS\), with the reference period adapted to the past 12 months\. Survey\-weighted generalised linear models with a Poisson distribution and log link were used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios \(aPRs\) and 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\) for factors associated with suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior\. Results The survey\-weighted prevalence of suicidal ideation was 9\.39% \( n = 36; 95% CI: 6\.18–14\.01%\), while 4\.11% \( n = 14; 95% CI: 1\.68–9\.70%\) reported suicidal behavior during the past 12 months\. Actual suicide attempts were reported by 1\.47% \( n = 6; 95% CI: 0\.66–3\.25%\)\. Among participants with suicidal ideation, 13\.56% \( n = 6\) reported active suicidal ideation with a specific plan and intent\. A higher prevalence of suicidal ideation was observed among participants aged &gt;36 years \(aPR: 2\.90; 95% CI: 1\.31–6\.38\), CPOs \(aPR: 2\.31; 95% CI: 1\.59–3\.37\), those working &gt;12 h per day \(aPR: 1\.67; 95% CI: 1\.05–2\.65\), those with a previous psychiatric illness \(aPR: 1\.67; 95% CI: 1\.19–2\.35\), and those reporting workplace violence or harassment \(aPR: 3\.16; 95% CI: 1\.11–9\.04\)\. A higher prevalence of suicidal behavior was observed among participants with &gt;15 years of service \(aPR: 13\.82; 95% CI: 5\.00–38\.19\), CPOs \(aPR: 12\.32; 95% CI: 6\.12–24\.80\), those with a previous psychiatric illness \(aPR: 5\.94; 95% CI: 2\.58–13\.66\), and those reporting workplace violence or harassment \(aPR: 13\.81; 95% CI: 2\.71–70\.34\)\. Conclusion Nearly one in ten police personnel reported suicidal ideation and approximately one in twenty\-five reported suicidal behavior during the past 12 months\. The findings highlight the need for workplace mental health strategies addressing occupational stressors and improving access to confidential mental health support among police personnel\.

## [Inteligência artificial no diagnóstico pré\-natal de cardiopatias congênitas](../publications/80f0b19c89696b394f18.md)

Hemilly Dias Figueira; Amanda da Silva Freitas; Alice Andrade Leão; Arthur Cabral Pereira Ornelas; Barbara Livia Santos de Araújo; Giovanna Paula Silva de Queiroz; Jeferson Noslen Casarin; Iracema Sousa Santos Mourão; Larissa Beatriz Silva Simielli; Cristiane Santos Silva e Silva Figueiredo

Objetivo: Analisar o potencial da inteligência artificial como ferramenta de apoio ao diagnóstico precoce de cardiopatias congênitas durante o pré\-natal\. Métodos: Revisão integrativa, qualitativa e descritiva, realizada nas bases PubMed, SciELO, LILACS e Google Acadêmico\. Utilizaram\-se os descritores “cardiopatias congênitas”, “diagnóstico precoce”, “diagnóstico pré\-natal” e “inteligência artificial”, combinados por AND e OR\. Foram identificados 214 estudos, dos quais 25 compuseram a amostra final\. Incluíram\-se artigos publicados entre 2015 e 2026, em português e inglês, sobre inteligência artificial aplicada à ultrassonografia obstétrica e ecocardiografia fetal\. Resultados: Técnicas de aprendizado de máquina e aprendizado profundo, especialmente Redes Neurais Convolucionais, apresentaram elevada capacidade para detectar alterações cardíacas fetais, aumentar a sensibilidade diagnóstica, reduzir a variabilidade interobservador e padronizar a interpretação das imagens\. Também foram observadas melhorias na qualidade das imagens e na triagem pré\-natal, sobretudo em regiões com escassez de especialistas\. Persistem limitações relacionadas à validação externa, heterogeneidade dos algoritmos e dependência da qualidade das imagens\. Considerações finais: A inteligência artificial mostra\-se promissora para fortalecer o diagnóstico pré\-natal das cardiopatias congênitas, embora sua incorporação clínica dependa de padronização metodológica e validação robusta dos algoritmos\.

## [Generative AI and Digital Inequality in South African Higher Education: Students’ Experiences of Access and Meaningful Use at a Rural University](../publications/80f9987fcb193e3e0385.md)

Julius Theledi Nkube; Khashane Malatji

This study examined the conditions that enable or constrain undergraduate students’ access to, and meaningful use of, generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) at a rural South African university\. Using an interpretivist qualitative case study design, researchers conducted semi\-structured, face\-to\-face interviews with 12 undergraduate students with prior experience using GenAI for academic purposes\. Data were analysed thematically following Braun and Clarke’s ix\-phase approach\. Four interconnected conditions shaped students’ experiences: device and connectivity reliability, the affordability of sustained data access, artificial intelligence \(AI\) literacy, and institutional infrastructure and training\. Students consistently perceived GenAI as useful, but their capacity to realise that usefulness depended on resources and competencies that were unevenly distributed\. The study uses this gap to extend TAM’s construct of perceived usefulness with a distinct construct of realised usefulness, and this study argues that generative AI introduces a literacy demand, critical evaluation of machine\-generated, plausible\-sounding but sometimes inaccurate output\. The study contributes to digital\-inequality scholarship by extending the access–skills–benefits distinction into the generative AI context and by identifying the gap between perceived and realised usefulness as a mechanism through which existing inequalities may be reproduced\. The study recommends that institutional responses combine connectivity, affordable access, structured AI literacy instruction, and explicit academic guidance, rather than treating any one of these as sufficient on its own\.

## [Impacto de la inteligencia artificial generativa en el aprendizaje de estudiantes de profesiones de la salud: revisión sistemática](../publications/80fa36a2993e4e2bea93.md)

María José Vizcaíno Villarreal; Jefferson Ivfin Narvfiez Quendi

La inteligencia artificial generativa \(IAG\) se ha incorporado con rapidez a la formación de las profesiones de la salud\. El objetivo de esta revisión sistemática fue sintetizar la evidencia empírica publicada entre 2023 y septiembre de 2026 sobre el efecto de la IAG en el aprendizaje y la evaluación de estudiantes de profesiones de la salud\. Se revisaron estudios identificados mediante PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Elsevier/ScienceDirect y búsqueda complementaria en las referencias de los artículos recuperados, junto con documentos disponibles para la revisión\. Se incluyeron 12 estudios primarios que cumplieron los criterios de elegibilidad: diez ensayos controlados aleatorizados, un estudio cuasiexperimental y un estudio transversal, realizados en estudiantes de medicina, enfermería, farmacia y odontología\. Debido a la heterogeneidad de las intervenciones y desenlaces, los resultados se integraron mediante síntesis narrativa\. Los resultados favorables fueron más frecuentes cuando la IAG se incorporó a actividades estructuradas de aprendizaje, retroalimentación, simulación o práctica\. Sin embargo, los efectos fueron menos consistentes para la retención del conocimiento y no se observaron beneficios uniformes en escenarios de razonamiento o evaluación clínica compleja\. En conjunto, la evidencia sugiere que el beneficio educativo depende de la forma en que la herramienta se integra al proceso de enseñanza y no únicamente de su disponibilidad\. Se requieren estudios multicéntricos, con muestras mayores y seguimiento prolongado, para determinar qué modalidades de integración producen beneficios sostenibles\.

## [Response surface evaluation of wheat straw\-reinforced fly ash\-GGBS geopolymer bricks for mechanical and thermal performance](../publications/80fa51de59aa963a45bb.md)

Md\. Zia Ul Haq; Sandeep Singh; Omar K\. Alghazawi; Pratikkumar S\. Shata; H\. Srikantha; Shahbaz Juneja; J\. Vanjinathan

The use of agricultural residues in alkali\-activated composites offers a practical route for waste valorisation, although its environmental benefit requires a complete system\-level assessment\. This study evaluates treated wheat straw in fly ash\-GGBS geopolymer bricks using a 27\-run Box–Behnken design\. Wheat straw content \(0\.50–2\.00%\), fibre length \(10–30 mm\), NaOH concentration \(8–12 M\), and GGBS replacement \(20–40%\) were examined against eight mechanical, physical, thermal, and ultrasonic responses\. Measured compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths ranged from 30\.2 to 43\.3 MPa, 4\.74–6\.16 MPa, and 2\.57–3\.31 MPa, respectively\. DOE1 \(1\.25% wheat straw, 20 mm fibre length, 12 M NaOH, and 40% GGBS\) produced the highest measured 28\-day compressive strength and is identified throughout as the best\-performing experimental condition\. An equal\-weight desirability analysis predicted a compromise at 1\.21% wheat straw, 18\.4 mm fibre length, 12 M NaOH, and 40% GGBS, with a composite desirability of 0\.816\. Because this predicted combination was not independently tested, it is presented as a model\-derived result within the investigated factor space\. All eight quadratic models were significant \(p &lt; 0\.001\); the thermal\-conductivity model is used as a screening model because its lack\-of\-fit was significant\. SEM, XRD, FTIR, and TGA/DTA provide qualitative, mutually consistent evidence of differences in matrix morphology, phase features, bonding environments, and mass\-loss behaviour, without constituting direct quantitative confirmation of reaction extent or interface chemistry\.

## [Experimental evidence of threshold\-driven gas breakthrough in thawing permafrost](../publications/810508f275019e60ac66.md)

Zihao Shang; Leela Radarapu; Marcelo Sánchez

Introduction Gas breakthrough is an important but poorly constrained mechanism for abrupt methane release during permafrost warming\. This study presents an experimental investigation of gas breakthrough in saturated permafrost analogue soils subjected to controlled freezing and progressive thawing\. Methods A silty sand collected from Alaska’s North Slope was tested using an integrated program comprising unfrozen water content measurements, direct tensile tests, constant\-volume gas breakthrough experiments, and stress\-controlled breakthrough tests under confining pressures representative of shallow to deep permafrost\. Results Unfrozen Water Content \(UWC\) measurements revealed a sharp, nonlinear reduction below 0 °C, with residual unfrozen water persisting at low temperatures and minor thermal hysteresis between freezing and thawing paths\. Tensile strength increased nonlinearly with decreasing temperature, transitioning from ductile behavior near −2 °C to brittle failure at lower temperatures, while tensile resistance near −1 °C was negligible\. Gas breakthrough occurred only when gas pressure exceeded thresholds governed by temperature\-dependent unfrozen water content, tensile resistance, and confinement\. Under high confinement, breakthrough pressures substantially exceeded unconfined tensile strength and occurred primarily during thawing near −1 °C\. Discussion These results demonstrate that permafrost thawing significantly increases susceptibility to gas breakthrough and provide experimental constraints for assessing methane release from degrading permafrost\.

## [As Within, So Without: Veteran Identity and Posthuman Alchemical Inquiry](../publications/81061411201a23e5be64.md)

Natalie Danielle Baker; Zeno E\. Franco

This paper reimagines veteran identity through an alchemical and posthuman lens, positioning the warrior’s return as a threshold condition, suspended between military and civilian worlds\. Founded on more than a decade of community\-based research with veteran peer mentors, we introduce generative AI as a daimonic analytic witness within a liminal epistemology, where threshold consciousness interprets threshold experience\. Our analysis reveals five archetypal dualities structuring veteran transformation: trust\-mistrust, stigma\-witness, liminality\-stuckness, power\-resistance, and disconnection\-connection, mapped onto Jung’s alchemical movements of nigredo, albedo, and rubedo\. Because the phenomena under study resist diagnostic and procedural prose, our method must risk an alternative use of scholarly language\. Here, prose is part of the inquiry\. Findings suggest that peer mentorship operates as an alchemical vessel where moral injury may become collective medicine through the Wounded Healer archetype, as veterans craft third\-path identities through symbolic bricolage\. This work challenges clinical reductionism by centering veteran voice\.

## [Digital Health Africa \(DHA 2025\) – Conference Report](../publications/8107d1b3e07e9ccb030a.md)

Tirhani Maluleke; Catriona John Waitt; Veshni Pillay\-Fuentes Lorente; Bernd Rosenkranz; Beate Kampmann; Karin Steinecke; Goonaseelan Colin Pillai

Introduction The Digital Health Africa 2025 Conference \(DHA\-2025, https://digitalhealthafrica\.org/ \) addressed the integration of digital tools within critical global health priorities, including maternal and child health \(MCH\), antimicrobial resistance artificial intelligence \(AI\), and pharmacometrics\. While the adoption of digital health shows immense potential for improving healthcare access in Africa’s resource\-limited environments, its practical application in the public sector remains sub\-optimal due to policy misalignment and inadequate systemic investments\. Digital health interventions can achieve sustained, large\-scale impact when properly supported, as demonstrated by successful platforms like MomConnect in South Africa and MomCare in Kenya\. However, successfully scaling these systems beyond initial pilots requires a robust foundation built on three pillars: technical capacity \(infrastructure\), legal legitimacy \(regulation\), and effective management \(governance\)\. Furthermore, while advanced tools like AI and pharmacometric modeling are now practical realities in healthcare in developed countries, the most significant challenge remains operationalizing and transitioning these sophisticated tools safely from the laboratory to the clinical bedside in Africa\. Conclusion Scientific advancement in digital health is insufficient on its own; the true test of innovation lies in its safe and practical integration into end\-user healthcare delivery\. To successfully scale digital health solutions in resource\-constrained settings, stakeholders must prioritize cross\-continental collaborations, invest heavily in capacity building, and secure long\-term commitments to infrastructure and policy development\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence — Integration, Segregation, Metastability, and Composite Dynamics](../publications/810ae73b73a0a7d8a7a0.md)



SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence is a Structural Neuroscience extension distinguishing measured neural coordination from native Structural Coherence and examining the information retained by aggregate descriptions of composite dynamics\. Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience\. The extension distinguishes anatomical connectivity, functional connectivity, phase synchronization, global phase order, pairwise phase locking, spectral coherence, metastability, and criticality while preserving their different physical and mathematical meanings\. It develops the constituent / composite problem through an exact three\-oscillator construction in which two states have equal present phase order but opposite instantaneous changes within one fixed dynamical system, establishing that the aggregate alone does not admit autonomous prediction across the full state space\. Published evidence concerning selective synchronization, task\-related network integration, focal seizures, signal mixing, metastability, and quasicritical dynamics supplies scoped empirical comparison cases\. The resulting framework treats neural synchrony as a family of defined physical relations while retaining Structural Coherence, sovereign distinction, and orientation as native relations requiring additional functional and relational evidence\. \(direct link \)

## [The representation of order and randomness in the auditory cortex](../publications/81142ade9fda45f636d4.md)

Sapir Bashari; Maciej M\. Jankowski; Israel Nelken

Perception fundamentally relies on the brain’s ability to extract structure from its sensory environment\. The auditory cortex possesses significant sensitivity to statistical regularities in tone sequences\. To examine this phenomenon at the single\-neuron level, we used multitone sequences and recorded responses from the auditory cortex of awake adult female Sprague Dawley rats\. Tones were presented in periodic sequences with a fixed, repeated cycle; in a fully random condition; or in an intermediate condition in which cycles were maintained, but tones were randomly permuted within each cycle \(random cycle condition\)\. Units showed a continuum of preferences between order\-preferring neurons and randomness\-preferring neurons\. Unexpectedly, we found sensitivity to the position of sounds in the cycle \(‘phase modulation’\)\. The strongest and most consistent phase modulations were in the responses to the random cycle condition\. Finally, we show how such phase sensitivity may emerge from a simple, biologically plausible computation\. Neurons in the auditory cortex exhibit a continuum of preferences from order to randomness, and show sensitivity to the position of tones in abstract repeating patterns\.

## [Carsten, Korth: Tool evolution as a prerequisite for consciousness](../publications/811bf5c6f0e3df356d5c.md)



\_Reviews in the Neurosciences\_ 36 \(6\):587\-613\. 2025Within the concept of the extended mind, the active modification of external objects, externalizations, is seen as an auxiliary means to adapt to the environment\. Toolmaking and use are advanced stages of externalizations that evolve\. All past or present tools can, theoretically, be precisely assigned a location in an evolutionary tree with predecessors and progeny\. Tools are reliably replicated, modified, and selected by their ability to facilitate human needs\. Tool evolution, therefore, fulfills Darwinian criteria where the material tool is the phenotype and the instruction to build it is the code\. The ostensive triangle consisting of a pointing individual, an observing individual, and a pointedat object or tool is the germ cell of social transmission of instructions\. Tool\-building instructions ultimately can be reduced to distinct sequences of motor acts that can be recombined and are socially transmitted\. When executed, they replicate tools for the reward of convenience or improved fitness\. Tools elicit affordances relating to their use that synchronize different individuals’ perceptions, result in psychological “understanding,” and thereby modify social networks\. Massive tool fabrication as present today in the “tool\-sphere” has, therefore, accelerated prosociality and over time led to the acquisition of an individual’s third person perspective\. The entangled biological evolution accelerated the ongoing cumulative cultural evolution by selecting traits facilitating social transmission\. In this context, tool evolution and the corresponding acquired individual instructional content is a precondition to the emergence of higher cognition and “consciousness\.” A neuroscience investigating externalizations as the starting point of this process is urgently needed\. \(direct link \)

## [Instability\-Aware Digital Twins for Robust Co\-Optimization of Operational Carbon Emissions, Thermal Comfort, and Structural Serviceability Reliability under Uncertainty in Smart Buildings](../publications/811dbdbbed22fcd1a1af.md)

Seyed Reza Samaei; Jarek Kurnitski; James Riffat

Modern smart buildings operate under continuously varying climatic, occupancy, equipment, grid\-carbon, material, degradation, and sensing conditions, making nominal optimization insufficient for reliable operational decision\-making\. This study develops and numerically evaluates an instability\-aware digital twin for robust co\-optimization of operational carbon emissions, occupied\-zone thermal discomfort, and component\-level structural serviceability reliability under uncertainty\. The framework combines a multi\-rate thermal–energy–moisture–IAQ–structural model, carbon\-aware CO₂\-based ventilation control, extended Kalman filtering, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, FORM and design\-point importance sampling, Gaussian\-process surrogate modeling, NSGA\-II, and dimensionless objective\- and decision\-instability metrics\. A controlled six\-zone benchmark represents a six\-story office building with a gross floor area of 10,200 m² over a one\-year operational horizon and a 20\-year reliability horizon\. Re\-evaluation of the nominally selected P0 policy under the full modeled uncertainty set increased carbon emissions from 42\.6 to 50\.4 kgCO₂e m⁻² year⁻¹, occupied zone\-time discomfort from 115 to 128 K h year⁻¹, and the serviceability limit\-state exceedance probability from 0\.021 to 0\.031\. The corresponding nominal\-input underestimations were 15\.5% for carbon and 32\.3% for the exceedance probability\. The selected robust policy produced 48\.8 kgCO₂e m⁻² year⁻¹, 98 K h year⁻¹, and PSLS = 0\.012, with a reliability index of 2\.257\. Relative to the uncertainty\-aware P0 evaluation, it reduced carbon by 3\.2%, discomfort by 23\.4%, PSLS by 61\.3%, and decision instability by 65\.7%\. The robust policy maintained a mean occupied zone\-time CO₂ concentration of 684 ppm, a 99th percentile of 821 ppm, and zero occupied zone\-hours above 1,000 ppm\. Within the controlled numerical benchmark, the results show that Pareto efficiency alone does not establish operational robustness and that explicit instability quantification materially changes policy selection\.

## [RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM PAKAN KUCING OTOMATIS DENGAN NOTIFIKASI TELEGRAM UNTUK MONITORING KETERSEDIAAN PAKAN](../publications/8129ad18a815352fa840.md)

Wahyuni Fegi; Rikki Vitria; Amelia Yolanda

Regular cat feeding is often hindered by the owner&\#x27;s busy schedule, especially when away from home, making it difficult to monitor food availability and risking the cat running out of food without the owner&\#x27;s knowledge\. This study aims to design an automatic cat feeding system with Telegram notifications to monitor food availability\. The system uses an Arduino Uno as the main controller, an RTC DS3231 for feeding schedule management, a servo motor to dispense the food, and an ultrasonic sensor to detect food availability\. In addition, an ESP32\-CAM is used to monitor the food condition through image processing, classifying it into three categories: sufficient, low, and empty\. The research was conducted through hardware design, software design, system integration, and testing stages\. The test results show that the system is able to dispense food according to the predetermined schedule, monitor the food condition using the ESP32\-CAM, and send food condition notifications via Telegram, allowing the owner to monitor the cat&\#x27;s food availability remotely\.

## [Assessment of utilization of ChatGPT on Medical Research Paper Writing Practices amongst University students in Lahore, Pakistan](../publications/812ebb7eedd693bf29cd.md)

Ahmed Hassan; Rabbiya Sarwar; Nida Asif; Asma Kanwal; Aneesa Mahreen; Tehreem Farooq

Background :The integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in academic applications has transformed medical research writing\. ChatGPT is an AI\-based language model that has been introduced by Open AI\. It is been commonly used for literature review, manuscript organization, and writing research papers and articles\. Objective: To assess utilization of ChatGPT on medical research writing practices among university students\. Method: An analytical cross\- sectional study conducted among university student of The University of Lahore and Rashid Latif Khan University\. The study participants were split into 3 groups on the basis of their enrolled degree programs; MBBS, BDS and Allied health sciences \(undergraduate, graduate and post\-graduate students\)\. Duration of study was from January 2025 to June 2025\. Descriptive statistics, frequencies, percentages, and cross\-tabulations were employed to summarize the demographic features\. For inferential testing, statistical tests were used to investigate the relationship between the question variable utilization of ChatGPT and Chi\-square \(?²\) tests were used to detect relationships between categorical variables\. Following an extensive study of the literature, a questionnaire was prepared\. Total of 381 students were selected according to sample size\. A sample of 381 students was selected using non probability convenience sampling technique\. A self\-constructed online validated questionnaire was used\. Results: Among 381 participants, 81\.9% of participants agreed that it improved their academic writing\. A majority of respondents \(92\.1%\) found it is easy to comprehend difficult ideas\. Furthermore, 74\.0% found that it helped them to organize their ideas while writing research papers\. In addition, 79\.0% students felt that it improved their ability to research independently\. However, 70\.9% students said inaccuracies were present in ChatGPT’s results\. 50\.1% agreed to use the text generated by ChatGPT without further validation\. Conclusion: ChatGPT enhances enrolled university students’ academic writing, manuscript structure, conceptual understanding, time management, productivity and critical thinking\. However, due to risks of inaccuracies and ethical concerns, its use must involve human oversight, verification, and adherence to academic integrity\.

## [Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI‐powered communication of scientific knowledge](../publications/81378b6a0d573d613b88.md)

Brahim Chaqour

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor\. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever\-expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data\. Beyond the bench, these tools can improve and refine manuscript architecture and streamline the flow of information by honing the articulation of simple or complex scientific ideas and sharpening the clarity and cadence of scientific information, which ultimately strengthens the writing in publications and grant proposals alike\. For researchers working across languages or at early career stages, these tools allow them to express ideas with greater clarity and fluency, ultimately ensuring that intellectual contributions are assessed on the basis of their conceptual merit and experimental validity\. However, the growing persuasiveness of AI\-generated writing raises an important concern as to whether persuasive language can create an impression of rigor that is not necessarily matched by rigorous science\. AI tools can improve the clarity and presentation of scientific writing, but they cannot establish biological relevance, experimental validation and/or the nuanced judgment required to identify confounding variables, and draw meaningful conclusions\. Similarly, an eloquently written grant proposal cannot substitute for an innovative idea, testable hypothesis, feasible experimental approach, and meaningful anticipated contribution\. It is therefore essential to view AI tools as instruments of improvement not replacement\. They can enhance clarity, efficiency, and readability but they should not replace investigators&\#x27; intellectual ownership, accountability, and critical interpretation\. Disclosure of AI use, together with continued investigators&\#x27; responsibility for originality, accuracy, citations, data integrity, and interpretation, is essential to maintain trust in scientific discoveries\. Similarly, editors, peer reviewers, authors, and funding panels bear a renewed obligation to distinguish writing quality from scientific quality and continue to evaluate approach, innovation, experimental rigor, reproducibility, investigator skills, and scientific and/or clinical significance\. Used judiciously and with discernment, AI can free researchers to invest more deeply in the irreplaceable human dimensions of scientific discovery\.

## [DeepLabV3\+\_KBSS for lightweight pavement crack segmentation and quantification in complex scenarios](../publications/8140fc4f3d1fc6d420ba.md)

Xianfeng Tan; Lan Ye; Qing Fang; Fengkuo Hu; Bing Liu; Xiaofeng Man; Lei Li

Accurate pavement crack detection and quantitative assessment are essential for road infrastructure maintenance\. However, existing segmentation methods suffer from limited robustness under complex illumination, insufficient modeling of elongated crack continuity, and a lack of automated pipelines for engineering\-grade evaluation\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeepLabV3\+\_KBSS, a lightweight crack segmentation and assessment framework\. The model integrates three complementary modules in a position\-aware cascade: a KAN Pyramid Enhancement Module for adaptive illumination normalization, a post\-ASPP BiFormer module for capturing long\-range crack dependencies via bi\-level routing attention, and a decoder\-embedded SaE module for optimizing edge\-semantic feature fusion\. Based on the segmentation results, a skeleton\-based post\-processing pipeline is established to extract geometric parameters—length, width, and area—and compute the Pavement Condition Index \(PCI\) in accordance with the JTG 5210 − 2018 standard\. Experiments are conducted on a mixed dataset comprising 4,029 images \(3,000 from the public Crack\-BPHDR dataset and 1,029 from field\-collected road scenes\), with an 8:1:1 train\-validation\-test split\. The proposed method achieves an mIoU of 82\.58%, mAP of 90\.28%, mRecall of 89\.21%, and mDice of 89\.88%, with only 3\.18 M parameters and an inference speed of 108 FPS, outperforming CNN\-based and attention\-based methods\. These results demonstrate that the proposed method provides an effective, lightweight, and deployable solution for automated pavement distress inspection and maintenance decision\-making\.

## [Beyond Tapering: Conventional, Pharmacological, and Complementary Strategies to Facilitate Long\-Term Benzodiazepine Discontinuation](../publications/814162461a28daebb3ea.md)

Jozélio Freire de Carvalho

Background: Long\-term benzodiazepine \(BZD\) use remains a major clinical challenge because discontinuation may be complicated by physical dependence, rebound symptoms, recurrence of the underlying disorder, withdrawal manifestations, and psychological reliance on medication\. Although gradual individualized reduction remains central to deprescribing, successful discontinuation may also depend on educational, behavioral, pharmacological, and complementary interventions\. Objective: To provide a clinically oriented narrative review of conventional, pharmacological, behavioral, and complementary strategies used to facilitate long\-term BZD discontinuation, with particular attention to quantitative outcomes and the distinction between dose reduction, complete discontinuation, sustained discontinuation, and withdrawal tolerability\. Methods: Human studies directly addressing BZD or related sedative\-hypnotic reduction or discontinuation were reviewed, including systematic reviews, meta\-analyses, randomized and nonrandomized trials, and observational studies\. Complementary interventions were evaluated using the same outcome\-oriented framework as conventional treatments\. Studies addressing only anxiety or insomnia without a BZD\-discontinuation context were considered indirect evidence\. Results: Structured withdrawal and brief interventions increased cessation compared with usual care, with odds ratios of 5\.96 and 4\.37, respectively\. Direct patient education resulted in 27% versus 5% discontinuation at 6 months in the EMPOWER trial\. CBT combined with supervised withdrawal produced complete discontinuation rates ranging from approximately 75% to 85% in selected trials, with benefits persisting for up to 12 months\. Pharmacological adjuncts showed heterogeneous results; pooled melatonin data did not demonstrate increased complete discontinuation\. Complementary approaches produced heterogeneous quantitative findings\. At 12 months after E2R hypnotherapy, 57\.5% had completely discontinued medication and 79\.5% had reduced or stopped it\. Adjunctive Passiflora incarnata was associated with ≥50% BZD reduction in 95\.69% versus 72\.04% of controls and complete discontinuation in 69\.89% versus 52\.69% at 3 months\. A multicomponent program incorporating balneotherapy produced 75\.3% overall reduction and 41\.4% complete discontinuation at 6 months\. Controlled acupuncture studies yielded differing results\. Conclusions: BZD deprescribing should not be represented by a single binary endpoint\. Dose reduction, complete discontinuation, sustained discontinuation, and withdrawal tolerability are clinically distinct outcomes\. The available evidence supports individualized, patient\-centered, and frequently multicomponent management, with conventional and complementary interventions evaluated according to study design and quantitative outcomes rather than treatment category alone\.

## [Stellar wind driven Alfvén wing dynamics in planetary and exoplanetary magnetospheres](../publications/814247602e64049837b6.md)

S K Gupta; Arnab Basak; Dibyendu Nandy

Magnetized obstacles embedded within a plasma flow generate magnetohydrodynamic structures known as Alfvén wings, which act as primary conduits for the transfer of momentum and energy between the body and the surrounding medium\. This study employs three\-dimensional resistive magnetohydrodynamic simulations to explore how these wings and the magnetosphere respond to diverse stellar wind conditions\. Our results, gleaned from a large number of simulations spanning a wide range of stellar wind speed and magnetic field–and planetary dipole field–show that the global magnetospheric configuration is highly sensitive to the upstream Alfvén Mach number\. We find that increasing stellar wind speed leads to a systematic closure and narrowing of Alfvén wing structures, while stronger stellar magnetic fields facilitate their opening\. Analysis of the Alfvén wing morphology demonstrates a distinct dependence of wing opening angle on stellar wind speed, with internal wing analysis showing a reduction in plasma velocity and significant magnetic\-flux accumulation\. Our results exhibit a clear interdependence between the day\-side magnetopause stand\-off distance and the night\-side magnetotail current sheet length\. We find a linear scaling between the magnetotail dynamics and upstream forcing parameters\. This study bridges the gap between solar system observations and \(exo\)planetary systems by demonstrating how Earth\-like magnetospheres might transform into wing\-dominated configurations during extreme stellar events or within the sub\-Alfvénic regimes of close\-in \(exo\)planets\. Our findings can aid the interpretation of Alfvén wing signatures in observational data and enhance our understanding of how \(exo\)planetary magnetospheres respond to dynamic stellar wind forcing\.

## [Anatomical Correlation of Stanarohita Marma: A Cadaveric and Virtual Dissection Study](../publications/8145f758a501719bf9ba.md)

Roopa Teggi; S\.Prasanna

Introduction: Stanarohita Marma is a paired vital point of the anterior chest described in Ayurveda\. Classical texts specify its position, size, structural classification, and prognosis after injury, but its anatomical correlation remains incompletely defined\. The present study was undertaken to identify the anatomical location and structural constituents corresponding to the classical description\. Methods: A descriptive observational anatomical study combined a review of classical Ayurvedic and contemporary anatomical literature, Anatomage\-based virtual dissection, and layer\-by\-layer dissection of four embalmed adult cadavers \(two male and two female\)\. The region was marked 2 Aṅgula above the Stanacūcuka \(nipple\), and structures within the Ardhāṅgula region were documented and correlated with the classical description\. Results: The marked region was located approximately 2 Aṅgula superomedial to the Stanacūcuka and corresponded broadly to the second and third intercostal spaces\. Pectoralis major was the predominant superficial structure, with pectoralis minor and intercostal muscles in deeper planes\. The internal thoracic artery and vein and anterior intercostal vessels were identified in the region\. Pleura, lung, and adjacent mediastinal structures formed deeper relations\. Discussion: The findings support a regional anatomical interpretation of Stanarohita Marma rather than a one\-to\-one correspondence with a single modern structure\. The muscular predominance is consistent with its classification as a Māṃsa Marma, while the internal thoracic vessels provide a plausible anatomical correlate of the classical Avedhya Sirā\. The observations may provide anatomical context for the described Viddha Lakṣaṇas and Kālāntara Prāṇahara prognosis, although causal clinical mechanisms cannot be established from this cadaveric study\. Keywords: Stanarohita Marma, Marma Śārīra, Cadaveric Dissection, Virtual Dissection, Thoracic Anatomy

## [Prognostic Utility and Exploratory Cut\-off Threshold of the First 24\-Hour APACHE II Score for In\-Hospital Mortality After Thoracotomy: A Single\-Center Retrospective Cohort Study](../publications/814dd77f84ab9253e7b8.md)

Awan Rochaniawan; Ahmat Umar; Erial Bahar

Background: Open thoracotomy imposes severe physiological stress, so objective early risk stratification is needed at General Intensive Care Unit \(GICU\) admission\. Objective: To evaluate how well the first 24\-hour Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II \(APACHE II\) score predicts in\-hospital mortality after thoracotomy, to set an exploratory cut\-off, and to examine differences by surgical indication and organ component\. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 33 consecutive adults admitted directly to the GICU of Dr\. Mohammad Hoesin General Hospital, Palembang, Indonesia, after open thoracotomy \(January–December 2024\)\. Analyses included Mann\-Whitney U, Spearman&\#x27;s ρ, logistic regression, and Receiver Operating Characteristic \(ROC\) analysis with Youden&\#x27;s J index\. Results: In\-hospital mortality was 27\.3% \(9/33\)\. Non\-survivors had higher median APACHE II scores than survivors \(23\.0 \[IQR: 19\.0–27\.0\] vs\. 8\.0 \[IQR: 6\.75–12\.0\]; U = 9\.5, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The score correlated with mortality \(ρ = 0\.706, p &lt; 0\.001\) and remained significant on multivariable regression \(aOR = 1\.74; 95% CI: 1\.13–2\.69; p = 0\.0127\)\. The AUC was 0\.956 \(95% CI: 0\.891–1\.000\)\. A cut\-off of ≥12\.5 gave 88\.9% sensitivity, 87\.5% specificity, 72\.7% positive predictive value, and 95\.5% negative predictive value\. Mortality was 32\.0% in malignancy and 12\.5% in non\-malignancy cases \(p = 0\.394\)\. Glasgow Coma Scale \(6\.33 vs\. 1\.83 points\), serum creatinine \(3\.44 vs\. 0\.96\), and arterial pH \(1\.89 vs\. 0\.33\) components differed between non\-survivors and survivors \(all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion: The initial 24\-hour APACHE II score is a hypothesis\-generating predictor of post\-thoracotomy mortality at a candidate threshold of ≥12\.5\.

## [The hidden burden of viral hepatitis B and C in healthcare settings: a cross\-sectional study of seroprevalence, predictors, and occult infection](../publications/815d406e4b6f5313fd9e.md)

Mikhail Kostinov; Olga Isaeva; Ivan Samolygo; Эрдес Светлана Ильинична; Marina Manina; Albina Pestova; Anton Antishin; Polina Kondrashova; Asadi Mobarhan Fedor; Alexander Novikov; Elena Tanaschuk; Tatiana Androsova; Izabella Khrapunova; Andrey Viktorovich Linok; Marina Loktionova; Naida Magomedova; Nikolay Briko; Aristitsa Mikhailovna Kostinova

Background Bloodborne viral hepatitis B and C remain critical occupational hazards for healthcare workers \(HCWs\)\. Current mandatory screening in some countries, including Russia, relies solely on hepatitis B surface antigen \(HBsAg\) detection, which may overlook occult infections\. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, predictors, and occupational risks of HBV \(including occult HBV infection\) and HCV among HCWs in multidisciplinary facilities\. Methods A cross\-sectional observational study of 1,643 HCWs and auxiliary staff was conducted\. Blood serum samples were tested for anti\-HBc, anti\-HBs, and anti\-HCV antibodies using ELISA\. Seropositive individuals underwent real\-time PCR testing to detect HBV DNA and HCV RNA\. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of seropositivity\. Results Anti\-HBc IgG was detected in 36\.6% of HCWs, demonstrating a strong age gradient \(aOR = 1\.55 per 10 years of age; p &lt; 0\.001\), rising from 12\.4% in those under 30 to 50% in those over 60\. Anti\-HBs levels ≥10 mIU/mL were observed in only 54\.8% of HCWs, dropping to 29\.7% at a stricter threshold \(&gt;100 mIU/mL\)\. High anti\-HBs titers \(100–1,000 mIU/mL\) were strongly associated with anti\-HBc positivity \(aOR = 4\.65; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Occult hepatitis B infection \(OBI\) was detected in 3\.1% \(95% CI 0\.85–7\.73%\) of tested anti\-HBc\-positive HCWs, who exhibited lower median anti\-HBs concentrations compared to PCR\-negative counterparts \(7 vs\. 165 mIU/mL; p = 0\.003\)\. HBV DNA was detected in 4 of 129 HBsAg\-negative, anti\-HBc\-positive participants \(3\.1%\), a finding consistent with possible occult HBV infection\. Notably, 75% of OBI cases were classified as low occupational risk\. Anti\-HCV prevalence was 5%, but HCV RNA was detected in only 3\.6% of seropositives \(overall prevalence 0\.18%\)\. Logistic regression for anti\-HCV showed poor predictive value \(AUC 0\.546, p = 0\.68\)\. Conclusion Despite vaccination efforts, a high rate of HBV exposure and waning seroprotection persist among HCWs\. The detection of OBI and active HCV in “low\-risk” personnel highlights the limitations of current HBsAg\-only screening\. Epidemiological surveillance should transition to active monitoring of anti\-HBc / anti\-HBs status and targeted PCR screening, alongside strict adherence to standard precautions by all staff\.

## [A Systematic Benchmark of Physics\-Informed Neural NetworkStrategies for Stiff Ion Transport in Lithium Symmetric Cells](../publications/815ea9e533061569ec89.md)

David Pankaczy; Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo

Abstract The Poisson–Nernst–Planck \(PNP\) system governs ion transport in lithium\-ion battery electrolytes and presents a canonical stiff coupled PDE challenge: extreme coefficient ratios, sharp electric double\-layer boundary layers, and nonlinear coupling between the Poisson and Nernst–Planck equations\. Physics\-informed neural networks \(PINNs\) are appealing because they require no mesh and handle forward and inverse problems in one framework, but spectral bias and multi\-task loss imbalance have limited their accuracy on stiff PNP systems\. We present the first systematic, simulation\-only benchmark of eleven PINN configurations, organised into four strategy groups \(adaptive loss weighting, spectral bias mitigation, spatio\-temporal decomposition, and physics enrichment\), on a physically parametrised one\-dimensional PNP model for a lithium symmetric cell, implemented in NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo Sym and validated against a high\-resolution finite volume method reference\. Root\-mean\-square errors span 10⁻² to 10⁻⁴: Neural Tangent Kernel \(NTK\) adaptive weighting achieves the lowest errors \(RMSE = 6\.6×10⁻⁴ for anion concentration\), while the balanced residual decay rate \(BRDR\) scheme matches NTK within 10% RMSE for concentrations while reducing wall\-clock time by 3\.2 ± 0\.4 h per run\. Loss landscape geometry corroborates the RMSE ranking\. An open\-source PhysicsNeMo Sym implementation is released for reuse in electrochemical modelling\.

## [The potential for habitat support structures to address habitat deficits in a declining marine ecosystem](../publications/8168a0605e515cf598b2.md)

Hanna Koch; William C\. Sharp; John H\. Hunt

Concurrent local and global stressors are rapidly degrading marine ecosystems\. Consequences of this degradation include widespread reductions in the availability, quality, and structural complexity of habitats\. For example, coral reef habitats across the Western Atlantic/Caribbean are flattening and becoming more structurally homogeneous as warming waters, severe bleaching events, unprecedented disease outbreaks, deteriorating water quality, and hurricanes continue to drive stony coral mass mortality\. This is problematic because the physical structure of a habitat profoundly influences its associated biodiversity and ecosystem functioning\. Structurally complex habitats support greater species richness and abundance as they have more microhabitats and ecological niches available for life history functions that support survival and reproduction\. Conversely, habitat loss and degradation can drive reductions in the abundance and diversity of organisms, which negatively impacts the health of our ecosystems, as well as the goods and services they provide\. While active restoration of species that create biogenic structure is underway, efforts may be slow to be effectively upscaled, and sources of environmental decline and mortality continue unabated\. Complementary or synergistic management interventions involving the deployment of habitat support structures designed to maximize ecological function, promote biodiversity, and instantaneously increase relief and complexity may ameliorate certain habitat deficits related to fish and invertebrate life histories\. Improving habitat availability and quality may in turn improve conditions and resources in an area, thereby strengthening ecosystem resilience and functioning\. Considering the configuration of habitat support structures to support species’ ontogenetic movements may provide further ecosystem benefits by promoting persistence across multiple life stages and therefore production\. Herein, we provide a perspective on the potential utility of such structures to mitigate habitat deficits in the Florida Keys \(U\.S\.A\), using nearshore hardbottom and offshore coral reef habitats as examples\.

## [Antidiabetic drugs and its pharmacological profile target in human for type 2 diabetes mellitus](../publications/8168c6dfa4005dc347f2.md)

David Calderón Guzmán; Norma Osnaya Brizuela; Armando Valenzuela Peraza; Hugo Juárez Olguı́n; Maribel Ortíz Herrera; Francisca Trujillo Jiménez; Daniel Santamaria del Angel; Ernestina Hernández García

With the advent of Covid\-19, it is necessary to repurpose new treatment alternatives, either in the form of an effective single dose of these antidiabetic drug agents or an efficacious combination of them for elderly population with or had suffered this condition\. Newer medication classes for diabetes have been increasing in use, and their utilization varied across provinces and how the COVID\-19 pandemic may have affected these trends\. This mini review has the objective of predicting the targets of bioactive small molecules in human using healthcare applied artificial intelligence\. These substances in the body are target specific receptors on the surface of cells, and antidiabetic drugs contains moiety´s and functional groups that may act on one or several subtypes of receptors\. The tool is a tuned algorithm, with novel data bank in web interface\. Information figures of Swiss Target Prediction \(STP\), which allow predictions on therapy combinations and probable side effects, were reordered\. The bibliographic databases were searched to identify existing cost studies, economic evaluations and models, and most of the parameters were derived from the published literatura\. Predictions are done using a ligand\-based approach, based on the similarity between a query molecule and the known ligands of a large collection of protein targets\. The result of this study highlighted crucial recommendations for the use of some of the antidiabetic agent groups in diabetic patients\. Our findings provide real world evidence supporting the potential clinical benefits of diabetes drug agents in mitigating side effects and development in patients with T2DM\.

## [Machine Learning–Assisted Fluorescent Eu@ZnMOF for the Enoxacin and Glyphosate Detection in Food by Suppressing Sensitization and Ligand–Metal Charge Transfer](../publications/816a34b36ebb226cd5c5.md)

Ze Li; Yan Man; Qingju Liu; Jilong Han; Zhikun Zhang

ABSTRACT The antibiotics and pesticides in the ecosystem environment, owing to their extensive application in veterinary medicine and insecticides, present a significant hazard to public health\. Herein, we developed a novel bimetallic metal‐organic framework \(MOF\) as a ratiometric fluorescent sensor for the simultaneous monitoring of enoxacin \(ENX\) and glyphosate \(GLY\)\. To fabricate a dual‐responsive probe, we synthesized the ZnMOF by reacting Zn 2\+ ions with the ligands \(2,2′‐bipyridine‐5,5′‐dicarboxylic acid, 8‐hydroxyquinoline, and 2‐aminoterephthalic acid\)\. Subsequently, the bimetallic Eu@ZnMOF was synthesized by loading europium \(Eu 3\+ \) ions into the ZnMOF based on the coordination with the 2,2′‐bipyridine‐5,5′‐dicarboxylic acid sites\. The Eu@ZnMOF‐based detection system exhibits a distinct green emission due to the suppression of excited‐state intramolecular proton transfer in 8‐hydroxyquinoline by Zn 2\+ ions\. In the detection system, ENX enhances the red emission of Eu@ZnMOF by sensitizing Eu 3\+ ions\. Accordingly, the ENX fluorescent sensing system was fabricated\. Moreover, ENX‐modified Eu@ZnMOF was fabricated\. Upon the addition of GLY, suppression of sensitization and ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer \(LMCT\) occurs, which quenches the red emission of Eu 3\+ and boosts the blue emission, resulting in a distinct color transition from red to blue\. The ratiometric fluorescent sensor allows detection limits of 0\.05 and 0\.10 mg/L for ENX and GLY, respectively\. Moreover, we integrated this material into a microfluidic chip\. By combining this platform with smartphone imaging and machine learning algorithms, we constructed a rapid detection protocol capable of simultaneous multi‐sample analysis\. These results demonstrate the promising application potential of Eu@ZnMOF for advanced environmental and food‐safety testing\.

## [Use of imaging technologies to support complex generic drug development](../publications/816b13b6bb69a11ffe80.md)

Priyanka Ghosh; Sam G\. Raney

Significance: Complex drug products remain costly and inaccessible to many patients\. The use of modern imaging technologies offers transformative tools to address generic drug research challenges, allowing for improved patient access to safe and effective generic medicines\. Aim: This review summarizes imaging research related to a wide range of complex drug products across five coordinated initiatives: high\-order characterization of the arrangement of matter in complex products; elucidation of the relationship between the structural features and the functional performance of these dosage forms; establishment of noninvasive approaches to characterize and compare the rate and extent of drug bioavailability from these dosage forms; development of reliable artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches to analyze imaging data; and provision of mechanistic insights to inform the construction of computational models\. Results and Conclusions: The technologies summarized in this work enabled non\-destructive structural characterization of complex drug products, establishment of structure\-performance relationships, and direct measurement of drug availability at local sites of action\. Furthermore, currently available technologies used for imaging complex drug products continue to support the establishment of scientifically rigorous, efficient bioequivalence pathways for complex generic products, reducing reliance on costly comparative clinical endpoint studies\.

## [Die Rolle des Menschen in Datenpipelines: Erkenntnisse aus vier KI\-Anwendungsfällen in KMU](../publications/816db3d79cbbad86defc.md)

Jörg Schließer; Christian Schlecht; Nadja Hemming; Anja Brückner; Amit Kirschenbaum; Philipp Hein

Zusammenfassung Die Digitalisierung kleiner und mittlerer Unternehmen wird durch die zunehmende Verfügbarkeit leistungsfähiger KI\-Anwendungen beschleunigt, wodurch neue Potenziale sowie Herausforderungen entstehen\. Ein entscheidender Faktor für die erfolgreiche Einführung von KI\-Anwendungen ist die Verfügbarkeit ausreichender Datenmengen, die oft aus einer langfristigen Datenaggregation resultieren\. Kleine und mittlere Unternehmen leiden in der Regel unter Datenmangel, wodurch ihr Bedarf an hoher Qualität steigt\. Hierbei stellt der Aufbau von Datenpipelines für sie eine Herausforderung dar\. Bislang unzureichend betrachtet wird dabei die Abhängigkeit von Mitarbeitenden als Teil der Pipeline, insbesondere wenn diese Aufgaben zur Datenerfassung in ihre Arbeitsroutine integrieren müssen\. Dieser Beitrag beleuchtet reale Szenarien in Unternehmen mit der Herausforderung, Daten angemessen zu erfassen, ohne die Entwicklungsprozesse datengetriebener nachgelagerter Aufgaben und Prozesse zu beeinträchtigen\. Daraus werden Potenziale und Risiken von Menschen als Teil von Datenpipelines sowie praxisnahe Empfehlungen zur Vermeidung von Fallstricken abgeleitet\. Dadurch können sowohl Datenqualität als auch Mitarbeitendenzufriedenheit langfristig verbessert werden\.
