## [Double Take: Using True\-False Exams to Deepen Student Learning](../publications/8185d93a8e8b9e106013.md)

Angela Collins; Eric Nelson

The Double Take True\-False Test is a proposed revitalization of a traditionally dismissed assessment format\. By embracing, rather than avoiding, intentional ambiguity, this article suggests that instructors craft deliberately provocative true\-false statements that lack definitive answers\. Students first respond individually, justifying their reasoning in writing, then reconvene in small groups to argue the opposite position\. Drawing on cooperative learning theory and two\-stage exam research, this approach develops critical thinking, perspective\-taking, and applied reasoning skills that prepare students for real\-world professional environments in which clear\-cut answers rarely exist\.

## [Label\-Efficient and Edge\-Ready Alzheimer’s Disease Staging from MRI using Knowledge Distillation and Adaptive Inference](../publications/8185e5c1c362e9352497.md)

B Sowjanya

Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, and early detection from structural MRI can slow decline through timely clinical intervention\. Deep convolutional neural networks have shown strong accuracy for AD staging, but they need large annotated datasets and high\-end GPUs, which most hospitals and research labs in developing regions do not have\. This paper proposes LRA\-Net, a Lightweight and Resource\-Adaptive deep learning framework that classifies brain MRI slices into four stages: Non\-Demented, Very Mild Demented, Mild Demented and Moderate Demented\. LRA\-Net combines depthwise separable convolutions, inverted residual blocks and a channel\-spatial attention module, and it scales its width and input resolution to match the memory and compute budget of the target device\. To counter the small and imbalanced dataset, the framework uses skull\-stripping, intensity normalization, class\-aware augmentation, transfer learning from ImageNet and a focal loss\. Experiments on the 6,400\-image Kaggle Alzheimer&\#x27;s MRI dataset show that LRA\-Net reaches 97\.8% accuracy and a 0\.97 macro F1\-score with only 1\.9 million parameters and 0\.31 GFLOPs\. It matches or exceeds heavier models such as VGG16 and ResNet50 while using over 13 times fewer parameters than ResNet50, and it runs at 18 ms per image on a CPU\. Grad\-CAM maps confirm that predictions focus on the hippocampus, ventricles and cortical regions known to atrophy in AD\. The results show that accurate AD screening is feasible on low\-cost hardware with limited data\.

## [Highly Diastereo‐ and Enantioselective Imine Reductases Engineered for γ‐Piperidinamines Bearing Contiguous Stereocenters](../publications/8188bf32f0f39720a611.md)

Min‐Min Zhao; Jia\-Neng Xu; Jinluan Chen; Zhe Dou; Yue Wang

ABSTRACT Imine reductases \(IREDs\) represent a highly promising class of biocatalysts for the asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines bearing two stereogenic centers\. Herein, we report an IRED‐catalyzed asymmetric reductive amination strategy that converts racemic ketones into γ‐piperidinamines with contiguous stereocenters and operates through a pathway consistent with a dynamic kinetic resolution‐asymmetric reductive amination \(DKR‐ARA\)\. The wild‐type Ac IRED afforded the 1‐benzyl‐ N ‐cyclopropyl‐3‐methylpiperidin‐4‐amine \( 1a \) in 60\.8% conversion, but with only 78\.5% enantiomeric excess \( ee cis \) for \(3 S ,4 R \)‐ 1a and 23\.5% ee trans for \(3 R ,4 R \)‐ 1a , giving an 84:16 diastereomeric ratio \( dr \)\. To enhance stereoselectivity, we employed a “trans‐drop, enantio‐catch” strategy to reshape the pocket architecture of Ac IRED\. The resulting variant Mut‐5 afforded 99\.9% ee cis for \(3 S ,4 R \)‐ 1a and &gt; 99:1 dr , along with a 19‐fold increase in specific activity and a 24\.7°C elevation in \. Remarkably, at a cumulative substrate loading of 700 mM \(142\.3 g·L –1 \), Mut‐5 furnished \(3 S ,4 R \) −1a with 95% conversion, a space‐time yield \(STY\) of 208\.7 g·L –1 ·d –1 \. This strategy not only provided highly efficient imine reductases but also established a robust platform for the atom‐economical synthesis of γ‐piperidinamine building blocks bearing two stereogenic centers\.

## [What counts as a skill?](../publications/81904143a2c1d7431b60.md)

Lucy Terina Sattler

Over the past decade, multiple major skills taxonomies have been developed or revamped, each presented by its developers as a ‘common language’ for skills\. Despite this shared purpose, the taxonomies differ at two levels: in what each defines a skill to be, and in which skills each contains and how they are described\. The result adds to the confusion rather than alleviating it\. This impacts young people, who are asked to name their skills to employers yet struggle to do so\. This study profiles eight major skills frameworks to identify how skill is defined within the documents, and which core skills are identified\. Document analysis of the released files and method documents for eight skill taxonomies against a template covering purpose, method, structure, coverage, and definition, combined with reflexive thematic analysis of the core skills named within the taxonomies\. The frameworks use common sources and share a dual\-layer structure separating core from technical skills; construction methods combine expert, industry, and AI/ML approaches, and method shapes the hierarchy\. At the level of the concept, the frameworks differ in whether and how each defines skill, and in where each places attributes and attitudes\. At the level of the named skills, they largely agree: the same 12 core skills recur, described in similar terms under different titles\. Skills taxonomies hold potential to improve access to, and clarity over, the labour market\. Using familiar language for skills, sharing descriptions with other taxonomies, and allowing individuals to see and choose from alternative titles could improve usability\.

## [The Construction of College Counselor Team based on Professional Competence from the Perspective of Building a Leading Country in Education: Logical Implications, Realistic Challenges and Practical Approaches](../publications/8191d89ede055d94d7a5.md)

Lingling Wang; Youmai Li

With the building China into a leading country in education shaping a new pattern of fostering moral character, the college counselor team, along with teaching, research, and management, is referred to as the &quot;fourth team&quot;\. The new strategic positioning has raised higher requirements for the construction of the college counselor team\. This article, based on the theory of competence and the strategy of building China into a leading country in education, explores from three logical perspectives \(the theoretical alignment basis, the value\-oriented goals, and the evolving trends in reality\) how professional competence can be integrated into the construction of the college counselor team\. It analyzes the current practical challenges, such as blurred identity boundaries, unbalanced ability structure, weakened professional identity, and lagging evaluation mechanisms, and proposes using the competence model as a guiding principle to establish a complete chain mechanism of &quot;selection\-training\-utilization\-assessment,&quot; empower the upgrade of competence through stratified and categorized training, build an evaluation and incentive system through collaborative and coordinated linkage, optimize the competence structure through digital means, and promote the high\-quality development of the &quot;fourth team&quot;\.

## [LLM\-based multi\-agent systems for code generation: A multi\-vocal literature review](../publications/81a0c1a2252e75efbdec.md)

Zeeshan Rasheeda; Muhammad Waseema; Kai\-Kristian Kemella; Mika Saari; Pekka Abrahamsson

Large Language Models \(LLMs\) have enabled multi\-agent systems to perform autonomous code generation for complex tasks\. Despite the recent growth in research and industrial applications in this area, there is little work on synthesizing evidence from both academic and industrial sources to capture the current state of research on LLM\-based multi\-agent systems for code generation\. To this end, we conducted a Multi\-Vocal Literature Review \(MLR\), combining insights from both academia and industry, including peer\-reviewed studies and grey literature\. The aim of this study is to systematically synthesize and analyze existing knowledge on LLM\-based multi\-agent systems for code generation\. Specifically, the review examines the motivations for their use, employed benchmarks and models, key challenges, proposed solutions, and potential directions for future research\. We selected and reviewed 114 studies, and the key findings are: \(1\) the identified reasons for adopting multi\-agent systems for code generation were classified into nine categories; \(2\) the models and evaluation benchmarks utilized across the studies were systematically analyzed to provide a structured overview of commonly adopted LLM configurations and assessment practices; \(3\) the reported challenges and corresponding solutions were synthesized into seven main categories and 26 subcategories; and \(4\) future research directions were identified and organized into six main categories and 18 subcategories\. The results of this MLR will assist researchers and practitioners in pursuing further studies and supporting the real\-world adoption of multi\-agent systems in industrial settings\.

## [Microbial cell factories for gamma\-linolenic acid biosynthesis: metabolic engineering, downstream processing, and future perspectives](../publications/81b1cc875efd3cfb2544.md)

Jie Qiao; Wei Wang; Peiyao Duan; Z ZHANG; Rongrong Yang; Haiyang Cui; Xiujuan Li

Gamma\-linolenic acid \(GLA\) is a vital anti\-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acid, yet its traditional supply from plant seeds such as evening primrose and borage is constrained by low yields and climatic instability\. Consequently, microbial cell factories present a sustainable and season\-independent alternative for scalable GLA production\. This review critically synthesizes recent biotechnological advancements in utilizing oleaginous microorganisms as production platforms\. It systematically elucidates the microbial lipid biosynthesis pathways and evaluates strategies to enhance GLA accumulation, with particular emphasis on rational metabolic engineering\. Furthermore, emerging technologies for microbial lipid production, alongside the latest progress in industrial\-scale applications, are thoroughly examined\. Finally, comprehensive insights are provided to guide the optimization of the entire value chain, ranging from upstream strain engineering to downstream processing\.

## [Hubungan Intensitas Penggunaan Smartphone Dengan Sustained Attention Pada Mahasiswa](../publications/81bb2033a5c3d472b9df.md)

Azzatul Mumtaza; Luh Putu Shanti Kusumaningsih

Penggunaan smartphone yang masif di kalangan mahasiswa kini menjadi paradoks; di satu sisi mendukung aktivitas harian, namun di sisi lain menjadi sumber distraksi digital utama\. Tingginya intensitas keterlibatan dengan smartphone tersebut memicu perpindahan perhatian yang cepat, yang pada akhirnya menurunkan sustained attention mahasiswa saat menyelesaikan tugas akademik\. Penelitian ini dilaksanakan untuk mengetahui hubungan antara intensitas penggunaan smartphone dengan sustained attention pada mahasiswa Fakultas Psikologi Universitas Islam Sultan Agung\. Subjek penelitian mencakup mahasiswa Fakultas Psikologi Universitas Islam Sultan Agung dengan jumlah sampel sebanyak 109 responden yang ditentukan melalui teknik cluster sampling\. Proses pengumpulan data meggunakan dua instrumen penelitian, yaitu Skala Intensitas Penggunaan Smartphone dan Skala Sustained Attention, yang masing\-masing memiliki koefisien reliabilitas sebesar 0,936 dan 0,780\. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan uji korelasi Spearman yang menghasilkan koefisien korelasi \(rₛ\) sebesar \-0,205 dengan nilai signifikansi 0,033 \(p &lt; 0,05\)\. Temuan tersebut mengindikasikan ada hubungan negatif yang signifikan antara intensitas penggunaan smartphone dan sustained attention pada mahasiswa Fakultas Psikologi Universitas Islam Sultan Agung\. Dengan demikian, peningkatan intensitas penggunaan smartphone cenderung diikuti oleh penurunan sustained attention, sehingga mahasiswa yang memiliki intensitas penggunaan smartphone lebih tinggi menunjukkan kemampuan mempertahankan atensi yang relatif lebih rendah\.

## [Lipid profiles and treatment response across symptom\-based subgroups in acute schizophrenia: a post\-hoc analysis of a randomized clinical trial](../publications/81bb2f990cb5a77820fc.md)

Meng Zhou; Mengxuan Qiao; Qiang Wang; Mingli Li; Hongyan Ren; Peiyan Ni; Wei Deng; Wanjun Guo; Yamin Zhang; Tao Li

Clinical heterogeneity in schizophrenia complicates treatment optimization and contributes to substantial variability in antipsychotic response\. Symptom\-based stratification may help to identify more homogeneous patient groups and improve prediction of treatment outcomes\. However, evidence from large longitudinal studies remain limited\. Metabolic abnormalities are also highly prevalent in schizophrenia and may contribute to differential treatment response across clinical subgroups\. We conducted a post hoc analysis of a multicenter randomized clinical trial including 2,990 patients with acute schizophrenia\. Symptom\-based subgroups were identified using K\-means clustering\. Baseline metabolic indices were compared across subgroups, and 6\-week treatment outcomes were evaluated using logistic regression and mixed\-effects models for longitudinal symptom trajectories\. Mediation analyses were performed to assess whether metabolic markers contributed to subgroup\-related differences in treatment response\. There are three subgroups were identified: a negative symptom\-predominant subgroup \(N, n = 1,010\), a positive symptom\-predominant subgroup with lower overall severity \(P, n = 1,226\), and a globally severe subgroup \(S, n = 754\)\. Treatment response and symptom\-improvement trajectories differed significantly across subgroups\. Baseline triglyceride and low\-density lipoprotein cholesterol \(LDL\-C\) levels were higher in Cluster N, whereas high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels were higher in Cluster S\. Mediation analyses further showed that LDL\-C significantly mediated subgroup differences in treatment response\. Overall, our study suggested that symptom\-based subgroups in acute schizophrenia showed differences in metabolic profiles and antipsychotic treatment responses\. LDL\-C may partially account for subgroup\-related variability in short\-term clinical outcomes, highlighting a potential link between metabolic status and treatment heterogeneity in schizophrenia\.

## [CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF OBSESSIVE\-COMPULSIVE DISORDER IN KARBALA](../publications/81bc00b04ee76c4f78f5.md)

Dr\. Ahmed Jaafar Mohammed Al\-Karaqully; Dr\. SHAKIR ABDULRAZZAQ AWAD ALGBURI; Dr\. Saleh Ali Abdulrasool Alrabeeah

The objectives of the study are to know the most frequently encountered symptoms of OCD in our psychiatric outpatient sample, the age of onset, time to first psychiatric consultation, and the correlation with the sociodemographic variables\. The sample consisted of 70 patients of OCD who were interviewed at Al Hussain teaching hospital was diagnosed according to the Diagnostic &amp; Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition \(DSM\-5\), and to clarify the symptoms of OCD were clarified as obsessive\-compulsive symptoms using the Yale\-Brown Checklist \(YBCL\)\. The majority of patients have both obsessions &amp; compulsions \(87\.2%\); the most common types of obsessions were religious &amp; contamination \(62\.9% and 58\.6%, respectively\), while rituals is the most common compulsion \(67\.2%\)\. Most patients presented with a young age of onset \(mean 17\.9 years; males had an earlier onset of 16\.4 years\)\. Married patients were more than single patients \(40% and 30%, respectively\)\. The mean time between the first psychiatric consultation and the initial treatment was over 5 years \(5\.4 years\)\. With minor differences, the pattern of symptoms with various contents in this sample was similar to that in other countries\.

## [Extracellular matrix remodeling and regulated cell\-death\-immune associations in adhesive capsulitis: a three\-cohort transcriptomic analysis](../publications/81c5c5da2b43bb4985b5.md)

Lin Huang; Ling Cheng; Jin He; Rui Zhang; Xia Li; Qiurong Xia

Background Adhesive capsulitis \(AC\) is a fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by painful shoulder restriction and progressive capsular fibrosis\. Whether regulated cell\-death \(RCD\) programs are consistently altered across independent transcriptomic cohorts remains uncertain\. Methods We reanalyzed three public bulk RNA\-seq cohorts\. GSE140731 was the discovery cohort \(22 AC and 26 shoulder\-instability surgical controls\), and GSE190023 and GSE238053 were independent validation cohorts\. Differential expression was estimated from filtered raw counts with PyDESeq2, with age/sex adjustment in GSE140731\. Curated pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and necroptosis gene sets; immune marker–gene scores; pathway enrichment; STRING network structure; cross\-cohort concordance; an exploratory three\-gene classifier; and qPCR validation of four selected genes in TGF\-β1\-stimulated SW982 cells were evaluated\. Results The adjusted discovery analysis identified 439 upregulated and 113 downregulated genes at FDR &lt; 0\.05\. ECM–receptor interaction was strongly positively enriched \(NES = 2\.299, q = 0\.001\), making extracellular\-matrix remodeling the clearest pathway\-level signal\. RCD findings were mixed: pyroptosis was not different \(delta = −0\.105, q = 0\.708\), ferroptosis was lower but borderline after FDR correction \(delta = −0\.426, q = 0\.056\), and necroptosis was lower \(delta = −0\.320, q = 0\.035\); the core necroptosis gene set was also negatively enriched \(NES = −1\.673, q = 0\.038\)\. Six immune marker scores were FDR\-significant in discovery, but none replicated at cohort\-wise FDR significance in the validation cohorts\. Cross\-cohort gene\-effect concordance was heterogeneous \(Spearman rho = −0\.047 for GSE190023 and 0\.383 for GSE238053\)\. The COL11A1–SPON2–PITPNC1 classifier achieved a pooled out\-of\-fold AUC of 0\.820 \(95% CI, 0\.684–0\.930\) in GSE140731; external\-cohort AUCs ranged from 0\.750 to 0\.812 with wide confidence intervals, and non\-nested feature selection precluded claims of clinical utility\. qPCR showed higher COL11A1 and SPON2 and lower PLA2G4A expression after TGF\-β1 stimulation, whereas PITPNC1 did not differ significantly, providing model\-specific support without establishing causal or clinical validity\. Conclusion Across the three cohorts, ECM remodeling was the most reproducible feature of AC, whereas RCD\- and immune\-related signals were cohort\-dependent and did not support uniform activation of pyroptosis, ferroptosis, or necroptosis\. The classifier and RCD signatures remain hypothesis\-generating\. The SW982 qPCR results provide model\-specific experimental support for selected candidates, but broader functional validation in primary AC tissues and cells is required\.

## [Early post\-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice](../publications/81c6aca16f231a820c3f.md)

Xin Yuan; Huakun Shangguan; Ying Zhang; Ruimin Chen

Objective To characterize the effects of early post\-weaning multi\-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short\-chain fatty acid \(SCFA\) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window\. Methods Female C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to probiotic \(Pro\) or control \(Con\) groups; after gavage\-related losses, final sample sizes were Pro: n = 9 and Con: n = 6\. The probiotic suspension contained Bifidobacterium longum, Lactobacillus bulgaricus, and Streptococcus thermophilus and was administered from postnatal day 21 to 27\. Fecal samples were collected during the three days preceding vaginal opening for 16S rRNA gene sequencing \(V3–V4 region, DADA2/ASV pipeline, SILVA 138\.1 database\), PICRUSt2 functional prediction, and targeted SCFA quantification\. PERMANOVA with multivariate dispersion testing was used for beta\-diversity analysis, and Benjamini\-Hochberg correction was applied for multiple comparisons\. Results A total of 2,946 ASVs were identified from 15 fecal samples\. Probiotic supplementation significantly decreased alpha diversity \(Observed species, Chao1, ACE, and Shannon; all P &lt; 0\.05\) and altered overall community structure \(PERMANOVA: Bray\-Curtis R² = 0\.193, P = 0\.013; Jaccard R² = 0\.158, P = 0\.008\), with no difference in multivariate dispersion\. No genus remained significant after FDR correction\. At a nominally significant level, Prevotellaceae UCG\-001 and an unclassified Bacteroidales genus were depleted, while Dubosiella, Parabacteroides, and an unclassified Lachnospiraceae genus were enriched\. Akkermansia showed a trend toward enrichment \(9\.39% vs\. 45\.85%; ANCOM\-BC2: log2FC = \+2\.15, P = 0\.179, FDR = 0\.395\)\. PICRUSt2 identified 63 MetaCyc pathways at nominal significance, none surviving FDR correction \(minimum FDR = 0\.106\)\. SCFA analysis revealed nominally significant reductions in caproic acid \(P = 0\.039\) and elevations in acetic acid \(P = 0\.039\), neither surviving FDR correction \(FDR = 0\.121\)\. Two correlations remained significant at the exploratory FDR &lt; 0\.1 threshold: Prevotellaceae UCG\-001–acetic acid \(rho = −0\.693\) and Akkermansia–valeric acid \(rho = −0\.670\)\. Conclusion A brief post\-weaning probiotic intervention significantly altered overall gut microbial community structure in female juvenile mice, with exploratory shifts in predicted functional capacity and a trend toward Akkermansia enrichment, without disrupting normal pubertal development\. These findings should be considered exploratory given the small sample size\.

## [Ubiquitin signaling in tumor\-associated macrophage reprogramming: mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities in cancers](../publications/81c8d1e83171ba5ae240.md)

Xudong Li; Yaomei Wang; Ruochen Xu; Ziheng Qian; Meimei Yan; Mengya Gao; Zexing Liu; Yun Zhai; Lijie Wang; Yushan Cui; Lina Liu; Yongping Song; Zhilei Bian; Linping Xu; Wei Li; 房佰俊

Tumor\-associated macrophages \(TAMs\) are key regulators of tumor progression and immune suppression within the tumor microenvironment \(TME\)\. Emerging evidence identifies ubiquitination, a dynamic post\-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, and signaling activity, as a critical determinant of TAM function\. Ubiquitin signaling orchestrates macrophage inflammatory responses, metabolic reprogramming, and tumor cell\-immune cell crosstalk through coordinated actions of ubiquitin\-activating enzymes, ubiquitin\-conjugating enzymes, ubiquitin\-protein ligases \(E3s\), and deubiquitinating enzymes \(DUBs\)\. Dysregulation of these ubiquitin networks fosters an immunosuppressive microenvironment, thereby promoting tumor growth, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance\. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the role of ubiquitination in TAM biology, focusing on key E3 ubiquitin ligases and DUBs in TAM immunity\. We further discuss emerging ubiquitin\-dependent signaling pathways that integrate metabolic and inflammatory cues within TAMs\. Finally, we highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting ubiquitination machinery to reprogram TAMs and remodel the TME\. Collectively, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding ubiquitin\-mediated regulation of TAM function and offers novel perspectives for developing ubiquitination\-based cancer immunotherapies\.

## [Seeking Attention: Economies, Modes, Ecologies](../publications/81e77260c518b136f348.md)

George Burdon; Thomas Jellis

ABSTRACT Concerns about attention in the current era call for geographic approaches that contend with attention&\#x27;s important place in socio‐spatial life\. To this end, this paper first notes that ‘economies’ have emerged as the most prevalent frame for geographic analyses of attention to date but warns that the dominance of such frameworks might close down other approaches\. Second, it argues that discourses surrounding attention are often marked by a normative and moralising understanding of what attention is\. To surmount this, it proposes appreciating attention&\#x27;s many modes, which allows us to understand new and emerging modes of attention—attention that is disordered, distributed, distracted—outside of moralising judgements that would see them as somehow deficient or inferior types of attention\. Third, it suggests conceptualising attention ‘ecologies’ to better understand attention in relational and environmental terms\. To think attention ecologically is to understand attention as a capacity that emerges in the relation between the neurobiological processes of the body and the set of multi‐scalar and intersecting social, material and technological environments in which it is situated\. The argument is therefore that attention is inseparable from the environments we inhabit and so is not a strictly human capacity\. The paper concludes with some critical reflections on the idea that we might ‘reclaim’ our attention, proposing instead a perspective that attention might be ‘re‐made’\.

## [Ingeniería de características basada en análisis exploratorio de datos para el modelado y la previsión de gastos en turismo](../publications/81ea0db74c39543dfd99.md)

Juan Ignacio Acciardi; Antonio Quintero\-Rincón

This pilot study introduces a feature engineering \(FE\) methodology based on exploratory data analysis \(EDA\) to augment and enrich an initially limited dataset\. The primary objective is to establish a systematic framework for accurately predicting tourism\-related expenditures at an operational resort in Esquel, Argentina\. Data collection practices in such tourism facilities are often suboptimal: reservations are typically recorded manually or stored in simple spreadsheets, then examined informally to identify apparent trends\. Under these conditions, EDA is a valuable tool for investigating relationships among the original variables and for constructing derived variables that more effectively capture their association with the studys target variable\. A multivariate linear regression model was specified to predict Tourist Spending\. The newly engineered predictors derived through FE informed by EDA, namely Interaction between guests and days, Spending per person, and Staydays, enabled a transparent and interpretable decomposition of the variance in the dependent variable\. Model performance, assessed using RMSE, MAE, MSE, and the F\-test, suggests that the model explains approximately 66\.6% of the variability in Tourist Spending at the resort\. These results are promising and provide further evidence of the critical role of FE and EDA in developing enterprise\-level predictive models for tourism\-related expenditures\.

## [Global epidemiology of metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease: 2026 update](../publications/81ec3e60fe96fc266e91.md)

Tie Xiao; Nicholas Chew; Giovanni Targher; Christopher D\. Byrne; Gregory YH Lip; Xiao\-Dong Zhou; Ming\-Hua Zheng

Metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatotic liver disease \(MASLD\) now affects approximately one\-third of the global adult population and is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide\.An epidemiological update is needed because recent developments have implications for clinical care and treatment of MASLD as a multisystem disease\.The epidemic of MASLD is growing\.Global Burden of Disease 2023 analyses estimate approximately 1\.3 billion prevalent cases, with projections approaching 1\.8 billion by 2050, and a disproportionate rise in metabolic dysfunction\-associated steatohepatitis \(MASH\) and advanced fibrosis\.MASLD is increasingly recognized as a systemic metabolic disorder with hepatic, cardiovascular, renal, and other extrahepatic manifestations\.Recently, the 79 th World Health Assembly adopted a resolution recognizing steatotic liver disease as a major global noncommunicable disease challenge\.Concurrently, cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic frameworks and non\-hepatology guidelines have incorporated liver fibrosis assessment into evaluations of selected highrisk populations\.Advances in non\-invasive diagnostics have expanded case\-finding, while the availability of MASH\-directed pharmacotherapies has shifted the clinical and economic rationale for earlier detection\.This narrative review synthesizes the latest epidemiological data on global and regional prevalence and incidence, comorbidities, hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes, advances in screening and prevention strategies, and future directions\.

## [Conserved but Not Continued: Decoherence, Information, and the Finality of the Conscious Subject \(Part II\)](../publications/81eed877469842fb1c31.md)

Henri Baskorvil

The first part of this study argued that a human self is best understood as an organised information pattern, that the Hard Problem of consciousness leaves the fate of subjective experience at death formally undecided, and that epistemic agnosticism is the honest response\. This second part examines that gesture in detail through quantum mechanics—unitarity, many worlds, decoherence, and quantum biology—arguing four main propositions: observer neutrality, a strict timescale constraint in neural tissue, the distinction between fine\-grained information conservation and pattern continuation \(&quot;conserved but not continued&quot;\), and the failure of quantum immortality as a survival guarantee\. Physics closes the quantum doors to survival, leaving the metaphysical question open\.

## [Central obesity and blood pressure burden among Chinese children and adolescents with normal body mass index: a repeated\-measures analysis of the China health and nutrition survey](../publications/81f0a8c0ea419ac98937.md)

Xin Zhang; Lili Chen; Jiaqi Peng; Liuhui Su; Xiaoying Cao; Fa Chen

Objective Body mass index \(BMI\) is widely used to screen for pediatric adiposity, but it cannot differentiate fat distribution and fails to identify central fat accumulation among normal\-weight youth\. We aimed to evaluate whether central obesity was independently associated with high blood pressure among Chinese children and adolescents with normal BMI\. Methods We analyzed repeated examination data from 4,841 Chinese children and adolescents aged 7–17 years \(7,192 complete\-case observations\) with normal BMI from the China Health and Nutrition Survey \(1993–2011\)\. Central obesity was defined as a waist\-to\-height ratio \(WHtR\) ≥ 0\.50\. The primary outcomes were above\-normal blood pressure and high blood pressure at survey examination, classified using age\-, sex\-, and height\-specific Chinese references\. Population\-average associations were estimated using generalized estimating equations \(GEE\) with robust standard errors\. Standardized absolute risks, robustness checks, subgroup analyses, and exploratory longitudinal analyses were also performed\. Results Central obesity was present in 4\.3% \(323/7,469\) of normal\-BMI person\-wave observations\. In fully adjusted models, central obesity was associated with significantly higher odds of above\-normal blood pressure \(OR 1\.43, 95% CI: 1\.07–1\.90; p = 0\.016\) and high blood pressure \(OR 1\.54, 95% CI: 1\.07–2\.21; p = 0\.022\)\. Standardized absolute risk differences were 5\.1 and 3\.5 percentage points, respectively\. Sensitivity and subgroup associations were generally consistent across sex, urbanicity, and survey period\. Exploratory longitudinal analyses \(lagged, transition, and trajectory models\) were directionally compatible with the primary findings but limited by sparse exposed observations\. Conclusion Among Chinese children and adolescents with normal BMI, central obesity was associated with a higher burden of blood pressure\. Waist\-based anthropometric assessment may complement BMI in identifying normal\-weight youth with an unfavorable blood pressure profile, warranting confirmation in contemporary pediatric cohorts\.

## [A review: indigenously processed dried powdered food product “Nkwakwa” and the nutrients of Strychnos madagascariensis from Bushbuckridge Local Municipality, Mpumalanga, South Africa](../publications/81fa39bffb9b4dac1df0.md)

Mnisi Philix

The Strychnos madagascariensis \(Black Monkey Orange\) is commonly found in tropical and subtropical Africa\. Black monkey orange \(BMO\) species can strive in hot and relatively dry conditions of Southern Africa\. It is one of the diverse indigenous fruit species \(IFSs\) in Bushbuckridge Local Municipality \(BLM\), Mpumalanga Province in South Africa\. The BMO fruit can be consumed fresh or processed into flour known as “Nfuma” in southern Mozambique\. The same processed product is known as “Nkwakwa” within BLM\. The current review invented the processing cycle of indigenous dried powdered food product \(“Nkwakwa”\) from the BMO’s seed coat, and evaluated its nutritional value in human diet, using the body of available literature\. Terms and keywords such as processed dried Strychnos madagascariensis, processed fruit pulp from monkey oranges, and dried monkey orange fruit processing, were used in a methodical online literature search\. The following steps outlined within indigenous processing cycle of dried powdered food product “Nkwakwa”: \(i\) Gathering the tree’s ripened BMO fruit; \(ii\) Cracking the ripened fruit’s hard woody shell; \(iii\) BMO’s fruit seed pulp is sun\-dried; \(iv\) Seed extraction from dried seed coat; \(v\) Dried seed coat/cover is crushed; \(vi\) BMO’s nutritional composition such as macronutrients \(K, Na, Mg, Ca\) required for multi\-body functions and micronutrients \(Zn, Mn, Fe, Cu\) essential in the human diet for numerous biological processes\. Evidently, BMO’s fruit and its value\-added products are nutrient dense to meet various human bodily functions\. Thus, recommended that the significant BMO species be preserved and that their value\-added products be processed and consumed\.

## [The Dynamics of the Racial Wealth Gap](../publications/81fb747406c609945392.md)

Dionissi Aliprantis; Daniel R\. Carroll; Eric R\. Young

ABSTRACT We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap \(the wealth of Black households relative to white ones\) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations\. We match the model to the cross‐sectional distributions of wealth and earnings by race\. We find that equalizing earnings is critical for permanent reductions in racial wealth inequality, and that one‐time transfers will have only transitory effects unless earnings are also equalized\. Our results are robust to the introduction of racial differences in returns to saving, which only matter after earnings inequality is reduced\.

## [DINO\-FIL: Multi\-Layer Transformer Fusion for Generative Inpainting Forgery Localization](../publications/81fc0cec2fe3710b60ac.md)

Simon Freitter; David Fischinger; Silvia Poletti; Marcel Hasenbalg; Martin Boyer

We propose DINO\-FIL, a transformer\-based framework for pixel\-level localization of generative image forgeries\. The method leverages multi\-layer representations from a pretrained DINOv3 ViT\-H\+/16 encoder combined with a lightweight fusion decoder to capture both semantic structure and fine\-grained texture inconsistencies introduced by image editing\. By aggregating intermediate transformer features across depths, the model improves sensitivity to subtle, spatially localized artifacts that are often missed by standard single\-layer approaches\. We evaluate DINO\-FIL in a cross\-dataset setting, training on B\-Free and testing on Beyond the Brush, CocoGlide, TGIF, and SAGI\-D\. The model achieves strong generalization, outperforming existing baselines on average and on four of five evaluated datasets, while maintaining a high true negative rate on pristine images\.

## [Practical Business Negotiation](../publications/8205e1d4aa8c050b8bb9.md)

William W\. Baber; C\. Y\. Chen

Known for its practical approach and real\-life examples, the third edition of Practical Business Negotiation continues to equip readers with the necessary knowledge and tools to negotiate well in business\. This latest edition comes with a refreshed set of case studies and addresses the topic of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in negotiations\. Designed to include non\-native English speakers, it employs a clear writing style and explains key terminology to enable readers to operate at an international standard\. Chapters guide readers on getting started and getting through the negotiation process with a sequence of actions, expectations when negotiating, planning tools, applicable language, interactions with different cultures, and the completion of a negotiation\. Each section of this book contains one or two key takeaways about planning, structuring, verbalizing, or understanding negotiation\. With its practical focus, this book is ideal for introductory negotiation courses or postgraduate courses where students already have an industry background\. Detailed teaching notes for the case simulations in Appendix II are available as a digital download for instructors\.

## [Fragmented control, collective risk: multi‐agent AI and the coming governance crisis](../publications/82134d4403a38d9fce24.md)

Caryn Lusinchi

Abstract Multi‐agent artificial intelligence \(MAAI\) systems are increasingly deployed across economic and digital infrastructures\. Existing regulatory frameworks, including the EU AI Act and related initiatives, largely focus on individual AI systems and are therefore poorly suited to govern risks that arise from agent interaction\. This paper argues that multi‐agent AI introduces distinct governance challenges, including emergent behavior, tacit coordination, cascading systemic risks, and difficulties in assigning accountability\. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static and component‐based analysis, are inadequate for adaptive, networked systems operating across jurisdictions\. Through a comparative review of policy developments in the European Union, United States, and Asia‐Pacific region, the paper identifies a growing governance gap, alongside early regulatory experimentation such as China&\#x27;s emerging standards for intelligent agents\. The paper concludes that effective oversight will require a shift from model‐centric regulation toward system‐level and adaptive governance frameworks capable of addressing the collective dynamics of multi‐agent AI systems\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery and Development: Current Advances and Future Perspectives](../publications/821b3790c64bde69184e.md)

Kartik Deshmukh\*, Shubham Kanawade, Sakshi Dengle, Gaytri Dalvi, Sandhya Nivdunge

Developing a new medicine takes years of research and requires many decisions along the way\. Researchers must identify a promising biological target, find or design a suitable compound, test its safety, and determine whether it benefits patients\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is beginning to support each of these steps\. Machine\-learning systems can analyse large biological and chemical datasets, while newer generative models can suggest molecules for further study\. AI can also help predict drug properties, identify possible new uses for existing medicines, and improve aspects of clinical\-trial planning\. These developments are encouraging, but they need to be viewed realistically\. A computer\-generated prediction is only a starting point: it must be tested in the laboratory and, ultimately, in people\. AI systems can also be affected by incomplete or biased data, may not work well on unfamiliar problems, and can be difficult to interpret\. This review discusses how AI is being used across drug discovery and development, what its current strengths and limitations are, and what will be needed for its responsible use\. The central message is that AI is most valuable when it works alongside experimental science and clinical expertise—not as a replacement for them\.

## [Theoretical and Methodological Foundations for Preparing Prospective Primary School Teachers to Use Generative Artificial Intelligence in Teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz Languages](../publications/821c5e8271f228f372b9.md)

A\. Iusupova; Zh\. Algozhoeva; Asylgul Sarinjievna Jumataeva

The article addresses the pressing scholarly problem of preparing prospective primary school teachers to use generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) in teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz languages within the context of the digital transformation of education and the transition of the Kyrgyz Republic to a new, modern twelve\-year model of school education\. The relevance of the study stems from the shared need to update the content of teacher education, the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies, and the increasing requirements for the digital and methodological competence of modern teachers\. The analysis of contemporary international research, regulatory documents, and national and international pedagogical experience demonstrates the need to develop a new component of prospective teachers’ professional preparation — AI\-based linguodidactic competence\. This competence is understood as an integrative ability of a teacher to use generative artificial intelligence in a pedagogically justified, ethically responsible, and safe manner when designing, organizing, and assessing the process of teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz languages in primary school\. For the first time, the article proposes an original concept for preparing prospective primary school teachers to use generative artificial intelligence in language education\. It outlines the methodological foundations, structural components, and pedagogical conditions for implementing this concept, as well as the practical possibilities of integrating advanced intelligent digital technologies into language\-teaching methodology\. The proposed author\-developed model comprises motivational and value\-oriented, cognitive, technological, methodological, communicative, and reflective\-evaluative components\. It is aimed at developing prospective teachers’ professional readiness to work in a modern digital educational environment\. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of using the proposed model to improve teacher\-education programmes at higher educational institutions in the Kyrgyz Republic, introduce new academic disciplines, develop professional development programmes for teachers, and support the practical implementation of the Concept for the Transition to a Twelve\-Year General Education System\.

## [Aligning management accounting and accounting information systems for better decisions in Malaysian SMEs](../publications/821fc29a657aadcf1b9c.md)

Faidzulaini Muhammad; Danilah Salleh; Jamaliah Abdul Majid; Lok Yee Huei; Norhaiza Khairudin; Zakiyah Sharif

Small and medium enterprises \(SMEs\) are central to the Malaysian economy, yet many continue to rely on basic accounting routines that limit the quality of managerial decisions\. Management accounting practices \(MAPs\) and accounting information systems \(AIS\) have each been studied extensively, but they are usually examined in isolation, leaving limited understanding of how the two jointly shape decision\-making in resource\-constrained firms\. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by proposing an integrated framework that links MAPs, AIS capability and the alignment between them to decision\-making effectiveness and, in turn, to the sustainable performance of Malaysian SMEs\. Drawing on contingency theory, the resource\-based view and information processing theory, the paper synthesises classic and recent literature to develop six research propositions\. The framework positions AIS capability as an enabler of contemporary MAPs, treats MAP\-AIS alignment as a distinct organisational capability, and recognises the moderating roles of perceived environmental uncertainty and owner\-manager digital and accounting competence\. The paper contributes to the management accounting and AIS literature by bridging two research streams that rarely meet in the SME context, and it offers practical guidance for owner\-managers, accounting professionals and policymakers pursuing digitalisation\. Empirical operationalisation and testing are recommended for future research\.

## [Lightweight multimodal fusion for UAV classification with explicit missing\-modality modeling](../publications/823518b1c76c3d41a69f.md)

Yibo Feng; Ning Li; Di Wu; Ximing Ma; Xiangyue Yu; Haiyang Bao

Abstract Fine\-grained unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\) type classification benefits from complementary sensors, yet real deployments face incomplete observations and heterogeneous stream reliability\. We present a missing\-aware fusion framework for RGB detections \(YOLO11\-S\), Livox Avia LiDAR, 360° LiDAR, and radar\-enhanced point clouds on MMAUD\. Confidence–density scores are masked and renormalized so fusion weight is assigned only to observed streams \(Eq\. \(2\)\); each absent stream still occupies a classifier slot via a learnable missing embedding that is not multiplied by the zero weight \(Eq\. \(1\)\), keeping absence as a trainable signal rather than a numerical zero\. On a time\-stratified split, Tiny MLP \(≈ 0\.1 M fusion parameters\) reaches 96\.12% test accuracy in a representative seed\-42 run\. Over seeds 42–46, final test accuracy is 95\.29 ± 0\.60% without training\-time modality dropout and 95\.77 ± 0\.90% with 30% training ModDrop \(mean ± sample s\.d\.\)\. Under matched 30% test missingness, accuracy remains 83\.68% \(seed 42\)\. Protocol\-aligned baselines and orthogonal ablations support the slot rule\. Fusion\-stage inference is about 2\.1 ms per sample with pre\-extracted features on an RTX 4090\. Under our fixed split and frozen features—not as a challenge\-leaderboard claim—compact missing\-aware fusion is practical for heterogeneous UAV sensing under partial sensor availability\.

## [Multi\-objective process route optimization for aero\-engine casings via graph\-guided large language models under multi\-feature interference constraints](../publications/82382a9cb1e90ebac453.md)

Yubo Wang

Abstract Aero\-engine casings contain densely distributed hole arrays, cavities, bosses, mounting flanges, and datum features whose adjacency relations couple operation sequencing with machine\-tool, fixture, and tolerance constraints\. Process\-route evaluation must account for setup\-related time consumption, propagation of dimensional\-quality risk across tolerance\-coupled features, and dispersion of machine utilization under the same feasible\-route constraints\. This paper presents GGLM\-CAPP, a graph\-guided large language model framework that evaluates and ranks feasible candidate routes generated by constraint\-propagation pruning\. A convolutional\-fully connected branch represents operation arrangement patterns within local setup windows, while a Proximity\-enhanced graph convolution branch represents multi\-hop constraint topology through gated neighborhood aggregation and Laplacian regularization\. Their outputs are fused by residual addition\. A learnable sparse mask then identifies a route\-conditioned focused subgraph\. The retained nodes, relation types, route attributes, and three engineering\-calibrated objectives are converted by deterministic structured serialization into text before tokenization and large language model reasoning\. The three objectives are fixed as setup cost, error propagation risk, and equipment load imbalance, all with lower values preferred\. Their definitions are anchored respectively to setup and changeover time, tolerance\-related dimensional\-quality measurements, and machining\-time\-based equipment utilization\. Segment\-wise prompts read different information from the same process\-knowledge\-graph schema rather than introducing objective\-specific edge types\. Case validation uses one local casing dataset and five mapped benchmark datasets\. The evaluation protocol covers objective calibration, Pareto quality, constraint satisfaction, expert agreement, statistical reliability, and computational cost under a consistent LLM inference configuration\. Cross\-dataset experiments compare GGLM\-CAPP with seven baselines using synchronized HV, IGD, and CSR evaluations, while ablation and convergence analyses examine the contributions and optimization behavior of the main components\. On the local casing dataset, GGLM\-CAPP achieves an HV of 0\.876, an IGD of 0\.112, a CSR of 0\.964, and an LLM\-QAcc of 0\.940 over five independent runs\. Physical calibration yields R^2=0\.94 for setup\-duration validation and R^2=0\.91 for utilization\-dispersion validation, confirming the traceability of the measurement\-informed objectives\.

## [Selection of suitable earthquake ground motions for the development of best performing AI model for seismic structural health monitoring of shear wall buildings](../publications/823cca63e5b2448e65d1.md)

Rohit Patel; Aloke Kumar Datta

This study highlights the importance of selecting suitable earthquake ground motions to enhance Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) models used in seismic structural health monitoring \(SSHM\) for shear wall buildings\. The primary focus is identifying and selecting ground motion records that directly optimise AI model performance\. A diverse dataset of earthquake ground motions, representing realistic seismic conditions, was compiled and applied to simulate the dynamic response of shear wall buildings with varying structural properties\. These simulations were utilised to train, validate and test AI models designed to detect, predict and assess structural damage\. Specifically, the models evaluate key structural parameters, including maximum displacement, maximum interstorey drift \(MISD\), base shear and maximum overturning moment under seismic loading\. The research evaluates specific ground motion selection criteria—such as Peak Ground Acceleration \(PGA\), Peak Ground Velocity \(PGV\), Peak Ground Displacement \(PGD\), time duration and frequency content—to ensure optimised input data\. The findings demonstrate that carefully selected ground motions significantly improve the accuracy, generalisation and robustness of AI models in identifying structural damage\. Ultimately, this work advances SSHM systems for shear wall buildings and contributes to more effective, reliable post\-earthquake damage evaluations in active seismic zones\.

## [RiboTRAP\-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans](../publications/8244d2ca93e3d0d3c00c.md)

Chung‐Chih Liu; Nicolas Seban; Supriya Srinivasan

Abstract The intestine integrates food\-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear\. Here, we generate cell type\-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells \(INT1\) and the remaining 8 pairs of intestinal cells \(INT2\-9\)\. We found that the anterior\-most INT1 cells are a translationally distinct intestinal sub\-compartment that is particularly enriched for immune\-and stress\-response genes\. Functional assays using novel INT1\-specific genes emerging from this study reveal that these specialized cells play a previously unappreciated role in pathogen avoidance and organismal survival\. A second critical function of INT1 cells is their role in sensing and responding to the contents of the gut lumen\. We show that luminal pyruvate is the key signal linking bacterial nutrients in the gut, to secretion of the gut insulin antagonist INS\-7\. These findings establish INT1 as sentinel enteroendocrine cells that integrate metabolic and immune cues to couple food status with immune and endocrine responses\. Our studies also provide a rich resource for dissecting segment\-specific intestinal biology, an overlooked and fertile area for future research\.

## [Diffusion Language Models as Open Quantum Systems](../publications/824aef41c543c7f865ad.md)

Akinori Tanaka; Yukinao Akamatsu; Takuki Tomita; Yuji Hirono

Diffusion language models generate text by reversing a classical diffusion process over token sequences\. We show that their continuous\-time forward and reverse dynamics can be embedded in the framework of open quantum systems, which describes quantum systems interacting with their environment\. This connection provides a basis for extending diffusion sampling to superpositions of sentence states and for modifying the underlying generation dynamics\. We construct a $τ$\-leaping unraveling scheme that simulates stochastic trajectories of these states while updating multiple token positions at each step\. This enables generation conditioned on superposed prompts or thoughts, which we call Superposition of Prompts \(SoP\) and Superposition of Thoughts \(SoT\)\. The same formulation yields Quantum\-Inspired Remasking \(QIR\): perturbing the masked\-diffusion dynamics produces a confidence\-based rule for revising previously generated tokens\. Experiments with pretrained diffusion language models show that superposition\-based generation can retain information from conditioning components not selected at the final measurement, while QIR improves LLM\-assessed text quality when applied at an appropriate stage of generation\.

## [Physical environmental indicators of protected area representativeness: a machine\-learning approach across 35 Japanese national parks](../publications/826b62f6c052d3544650.md)

Hajime Ise; Mahito Kamada

Evaluating the physical environmental representativeness of protected area networks requires spatially explicit indicators that are locally calibrated yet nationally comparable\. We introduce PhysRep \(Physical Representativeness score\), a continuous indicator of how closely physical environmental conditions at any location resemble those within a protected area&\#x27;s strictly protected zones\. PhysRep is derived from park\-specific XGBoost classifiers trained on climatic, topographic, geological and micro\-landform variables within an H3 hexagonal grid at approximately 0\.1 km 2 resolution, and demonstrated across all 35 Japanese national parks\. Spatially grouped nested cross\-validation guarded against inflation from spatial autocorrelation, and SHAP values identified the variables driving PhysRep at park and network scales\. All 35 park\-specific models outperformed label\-shuffled negative controls in ROC\-AUC \(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, median 0\.792 versus 0\.488; smallest margin 0\.113\), the metric used for tier assignment because it is invariant to class prevalence \(median F1: 0\.777\)\. Climatic and topographic variables dominated nationally, while geological and micro\-landform features dominated in regionally specific contexts\. Nationwide mapping revealed spatially coherent high\-representativeness areas extending beyond current park boundaries, but for most parks these occur as many small, scattered patches rather than large contiguous tracts, indicating limited environmental continuity around individual parks\. PhysRep surfaces thus make representativeness gaps and redundancies explicit at the park level\. We recommend that protected area network planning under area\-based frameworks such as 30 × 30 and Other Effective Area based Conservation Measures \(OECMs\) incorporate park\-specific similarity assessments alongside existing biological and connectivity indicators, prioritizing parks with little contiguous environmental continuity nearby and recognizing where such continuity already provides regional\-scale redundancy\. The indicator is modular and transferable, requiring only spatial boundaries and environmental rasters as inputs\.

## [Operationalizing the physiological state \(P\) in nonlinear behavioral systems: a measurement framework for state\-dependent dynamics](../publications/82772d288efb9f47a7b6.md)

Yoandra M Gomez Uncu

Behavioral outcomes may vary within the same individual even when measured environmental conditions appear comparable\. To test whether an organism’s changing physiological condition provides information about such variation, this article proposes an operational measurement framework for Physiological State \( P\)\. P is defined as a latent, multidimensional, and time\-dependent configuration generated by ongoing Physiological Organization\. Antecedent conditions \( A \) and consequence\-related conditions \( C \) remain external environmental variables, whereas behavior \( B \) is modeled as a separate downstream outcome\. Rather than uniquely determining behavior, P influences Physiological Accessibility—the state\-dependent availability of existing Adaptive Capacities for recruitment and use—and thereby constrains behavioral expression\. The construct is distinguished from emotional and cognitive constructs, subjective reports, observable behavior, stress, allostatic load, and individual physiological indicators\. Operationalizing requires prespecifying the target behavior and timescale; selecting reliable, sensitive, feasible, and nonredundant physiological indicators; aligning and preprocessing observations; deriving dynamic features; integrating those features through an identifiable latent\-state model; representing estimated uncertainty; and conducting prospective validation\. The Thirteen Physiological Systems and Seven Layers of Physiological State guide physiological coverage and interpretation but do not correspond one\-to\-one with the latent dimensions\. In a candidate nonlinear state\-space implementation, physiological observations, Y \(t\), provide evidence for estimating P \(t\), while state evolution depends on preceding P, current A , and relevant prior C \. Filtered estimates use only information available through the prediction time\. Because B remains outside the physiological observation vector and is evaluated prospectively as B \(t \+ Δ\), the framework avoids circularly defining the state by the outcome it is intended to predict\. Empirical support would require reliable, interpretable, and temporally coherent state estimates that demonstrate reproducible prospective and incremental value beyond environmental variables, prior behavior, isolated physiological indicators, established single constructs, simple physiological composites, and appropriate linear or lower\-dimensional alternatives\. Failure to obtain identifiable state estimates or incremental prospective information about B would count against the proposed operationalization\. The framework is theoretically and methodologically developmental and should not be interpreted as a validated instrument, diagnostic measure, or universal physiological score\.

## [Large language model assistance for report\-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi\-reader study](../publications/827e6f05b13b2f208bca.md)

Mengfei Wang; Yixiao Tang; Yulu Yang; Yifan Tu; Zhongzheng Cao; Runjianya Ling; Kaiyue Sun; Jian Ma; Zhicheng Zhang; Ruipeng Zhang; Xiaoer Wei; Dan Wang; Y S Li

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists&\#x27; agreement with a text\-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free\-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria\-guided prompting\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions\. In a report\-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance\. In standalone evaluation, a rule\-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria\-guided prompting\. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text\. RESULTS: Among 433 patients \(mean age, 65\.9 years ± 13\.4; 248 males\), AI assistance improved six\-class agreement with the text\-based reference standard\. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61\.75% to 83\.12% \(Qwen3\-8B\) and 87\.75% \(DeepSeek\-R1\); senior radiologists from 77\.00% to 87\.50% and 92\.25%, respectively \(all Holm\-corrected p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Patient\-level agreement increased from 41\.0% to 78\.8% \(junior\) and from 59\.8% to 87\.8% \(senior\) with DeepSeek\-R1\. Agreement increased \(quadratic\-weighted κ: 0\.231 without AI vs 0\.775 with DeepSeek\-R1\)\. In standalone evaluation, criteria\-guided prompting improved Qwen3\-8B agreement from 38\.91% to 81\.52% \(95% CI: 78\.87\-84\.06%\), remaining 5\.89 percentage points below DeepSeek\-R1 \(87\.41%; 95% CI: 85\.10\-89\.61%\)\. CONCLUSION: In this report\-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists&\#x27; agreement with the text\-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists\. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text\-based workflows\. KEY POINTS: Question Report\-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience\-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi\-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load\. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text\-based reference standard and raised inter\-reader consistency \(weighted κ 0\.231\-0\.775\), narrowing the junior\-senior gap\. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B\-model agreement \(38\.91\-81\.52%\), supporting standardized text\-based workflows without fine\-tuning\.

## [From Answer Generator to Questioning Coach: Designing AI\-Assisted Coaching for Self\-Regulated Learning in Higher Education](../publications/828b9831eef06ecbb9c5.md)

Sherif Welsen

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) can support self\-regulated learning \(SRL\), but its pedagogical value depends on whether interaction elicits learner cognition or substitutes for it\. This study examined how students’ reported use of GenAI corresponded to an intended question\-first coaching design, the perceived processes and tensions associated with SRL, and conditions relevant to potential scale\. A qualitatively driven embedded case study utilized 31 reflective portfolios as the primary dataset, complemented by 53 survey responses and 68 weekly logs from 12 maximum\-variation cases\. Abductive, reflexive thematic analysis generated five themes\. Question\-led interaction appeared most useful when it prompted problem reframing, led to a bounded evidence\-producing action, and preserved learner judgment through evaluation, modification, or rejection of AI suggestions\. Benefits were qualified by role drift, generic interaction, cognitive substitution, uneven engagement, and continued need for human support\. The findings support a distributed coaching\-system interpretation in which AI\-supported elicitation, pedagogical scaffolding, learner agency, reported AI\-role configuration, and function\-specific human support interact\. The study does not demonstrate institutional scalability; instead, it identifies scale\-relevant conditions including sustained engagement, manageable scaffolding, role boundaries, safety, learner judgment, and routes to human expertise\.

## [Rivera, Fernanda Lilibeth Ormeño &amp; Cedeño, Michelle Antonella Sánchez: Training in the Field of Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities in Health Science Education](../publications/828badd4efb4f8cee405.md)



\_EthAIca\_ 3:134\. 2024Introduction: Artificial intelligence in higher education teacher training has become an imperative that challenges teachers to update themselves to be able to use this tool to generate knowledge for their students\. Method: A systematic review was conducted in databases such as PUBMED, Cochrane Central Library, CINAHL, and SCIENCE DIRECT, using keywords like &quot;health sciences,&quot; &quot;artificial intelligence,&quot; and &quot;teaching&quot; during the period 2018\-2024, following the PRISMA checklist\. Results: Studies predominantly originated from Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the USA, especially involving nursing and medical students\. The most notable opportunities of AI include the relationship between ethics and technology, the training of academic tutors, and its contribution to professional education, clinical case management, literature searches, and student learning\. However, challenges were identified, such as uncertainty about employability, limited funding for training, and the acquisition of licenses\. Additionally, there is a need to promote responsible use of AI to avoid diminishing empathy and humanization in patient care\. Conclusion: AI is a valuable ally in health sciences education, but ethical considerations and teacher training must be taken into account for responsible use, as well as fostering critical and reflective thinking in its implementation\. \(direct link \)
