## [Assessment of climate change impacts on hydropower potential in intermittent river basins using bootstrap aggregating machine learning method](../publications/828e5feb602769d7e255.md)

Turan Alakbar; Halil İbrahim Burgan

ABSTRACT Devastating environmental effects of relying too much on fossil fuels include air pollution, acid rain and global warming\. One renewable energy source that is crucial for slowing climate change is hydropower\. However, climate change affects its potential and makes hydropower generation unpredictable\. The bootstrap aggregating machine learning approach is being used in this study to evaluate the hydropower potential in intermittent river basins\. The performance of the Bootstrap Aggregating \(BA\) model was benchmarked against Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms, demonstrating superior predictive stability with an average absolute error of 5\.46%\. A regional model was developed using future precipitation data unique to the Antalya basin \(2025–2055\) under the RCP 4\.5 intermediate emission scenario\. The findings demonstrate that the approach effectively estimated power duration curves and cease\-to\-flow points, with only minor discrepancies between the modeled and observed data\. Quantitative analysis using Area Under the Curve \(AUC\) revealed a downward shift in future energy potential, particularly impacting mid\-range generation capacities\. The influence of climate change on hydropower potential, emphasizing its role as a renewable energy source amidst growing water scarcity and energy demands\. Future research may incorporate deep learning techniques to enhance these models\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI UNIFIED THEORY OF NEURO\-JURIDICAL CONSCIOUSNESS AND COGNITIVE SOVEREIGNTY \(UTNJCS\)](../publications/829157e1ec4c67321a16.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Unified Theory of Neuro\-Juridical Consciousness and Cognitive Sovereignty \(UTNJCS\) introduces a groundbreaking, biophysically grounded framework bridging neuroscience, sociology, philosophy, and law\. It resolves the historical disconnect between subjective legal intent \(Mens Rea\) and objective neurobiology\. UTNJCS quantifies an individual&\#x27;s &quot;Cognitive Sovereignty Index&quot; \(CSI\) and models the degrading effects of &quot;External Socio\-Environmental Pressure&quot; \(S\_ext\)\. The core innovation is the El\-Rakhawi Cognitive Accountability Metric \(CAM\), a probabilistic, dimensionally consistent mathematical equation that estimates legal and moral responsibility\. Operating as a retrospective probabilistic reconstruction, CAM utilizes post\-hoc neuro\-psychological data within strict confidence intervals to evaluate decision\-making capacity, not thought content, strictly prohibiting neuro\-surveillance\. This paradigm shifts global justice from blind retribution to objective, restorative &quot;Cognitive Justice,&quot; ensuring accountability is proportional to actual biological and social capacity, while protecting human cognitive liberty\.

## [Towards a New Learning Ecology: The Mediator Role of Teachers Facing Generative AI in the University Context of Peru, Chile, and Colombia](../publications/8292f1ca8536e43e2441.md)

Óscar Rafael Boude Figueredo; Jessica Meza\-Jaque; Luis Peréz

Background The emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\) has created an ontological disruption in higher education, challenging traditional pedagogical mediation and academic production\. This study examines the transformation of the teaching role in university environments across Peru, Chile, and Colombia, addressing a knowledge gap in Latin American empirical research regarding faculty perceptions and daily practices with Large Language Models\. Methods The research employed a descriptive\-interpretative qualitative design with an open\-ended survey approach interpreted through a hermeneutic lens\. A non\-probabilistic sample of 48 undergraduate and graduate professors from 20 Higher Education Institutions in the region participated\. Data were collected through a validated 18\-item structured online questionnaire and analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis assisted by Atlas\.ti software\. Results The findings identify a transition from traditional instructional roles toward a “mediator\-curator” model, where educators act as orchestrators of human\-AI co\-intelligence\. Key applications include pedagogical re\-engineering, such as dynamic curricular design, Socratic tutoring, and the shift from product\-oriented to process\-oriented assessment\. Critical dimensions emerged regarding the need for pedagogical re\-engineering, ethical challenges in academic integrity, and the development of critical AI literacy\. National variations showed Chile focusing on pedagogical equity, Colombia on research productivity, and Peru on didactic agility\. Conclusions The integration of GenAI in the Latin American university context requires a situated pedagogical response that transcends instrumental use\. The study proposes a new learning ecology where the teacher facilitates critical interaction between students and generative systems\. This shift necessitates a reconfiguration of teaching competencies toward epistemic curation and algorithmic responsibility to ensure meaningful and ethical learning\.

## [MR Imaging and Radiomics Features for Predicting Variant Histology of Bladder Cancer: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis](../publications/829350602adeb2161a34.md)

Jessie L\. Chai; Zhou Lan; Orysya Svystun; Mohd Javed Saifullah Shaikh; Michael Daniel Weintraub; Stephanie Siegmund; Michelle S\. Hirsch; Matthew Mossanen; Atul Bhanudas Shinagare

INTRODUCTION: Compare MRI features of bladder variant histology \(VH\) and pure urothelial carcinoma \(UC\) and determine if MRI radiomics features can predict VH\. METHODS: In this retrospective study, cystectomy pathology database search yielded 37 patients with tumours with more than 50% VH and preoperative MRI&\#x27;s\. Cystectomy database search yielded 38 consecutive patients with pure UC and preoperative MRI&\#x27;s\. Three radiologists characterized MRI T2, diffusion\-weighted, apparent diffusion coefficient \(ADC\) maps and postcontrast features of bladder tumours\. Inter\-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet&\#x27;s agreement and intra\-class coefficients\. Another radiologist segmented bladder tumours and adjacent perivesical fat on T2\-weighted and ADC images using radiomics software\. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\) was used to determine radiomics features that distinguished VH from UC\. Fifty datasets were prepared using multiple imputation approach, and variables were normalized for LASSO variable selection\. RESULTS: Patients with VH \(mean age = 68, 54 \(72%\) men\) included squamous cell \(n = 17\), sarcomatoid \(n = 6\), plasmacytoid \(n = 6\), adenocarcinoma \(n = 4\) and small cell \(n = 4\) variants\. Inter\-reader agreement was similar for VH and UC \(p &gt; 0\.44\)\. All readers characterized all squamous cell carcinoma as T2 intermediate\. For two of three readers, 92%\-100% of hypoenhancing tumours were VH at pathology whereas 74%\-78% of hyperenhancing masses were UC \(p = 0\.001\)\. Combination of 11 selected radiomics features had AUC of 0\.98 for training and 0\.95 for validation data for prediction of VH\. CONCLUSION: Squamous cell carcinoma was T2 intermediate, and VH was more likely to hypoenhance compared to UC\. Our radiomic model had excellent performance for predicting VH\.

## [Dynamic pricing for improved parking space utilization: a data\-driven Bayesian optimization approach](../publications/8299768969d34cc6eae2.md)

Prakash Ranjan; Fatemeh Fakhrmoosavi; Krishna Murthy Gurumurthy; Abdelrahman Ismael; James Cook

Parking scarcity in downtown areas presents a major challenge for commuters seeking convenient spaces near their destinations\. This study proposes a dynamic pricing optimization framework for garage parking in downtown Chicago, balancing the often\-conflicting objectives of garage operators and users\. The framework formulates garage pricing as a multi\-objective optimization problem that combines normalized garage revenue and occupancy, with the weight factors calibrated through a sensitivity analysis to identify the trade\-off that maximizes occupancy gains while approximately preserving baseline garage revenue\. Using simulated POLARIS data, we applied a Bayesian optimization framework to determine the optimal garage prices for both peak and off\-peak periods, then evaluated key performance metrics, including the temporal and spatial distribution of garage fees, occupancy rates, and revenues over a 24\-hour period\. Results showed that the optimized pricing strategy substantially reduced off\-peak garage fees, improving accessibility during off\-peak periods, while peak\-period fees remained close to existing baseline levels, avoiding disadvantage to peak\-period travelers\. Peak\-hour occupancy increased from approximately 50% to over 70%, with improved overall parking space utilization and limited revenue trade\-off\. The study also highlights the influence of allocating a portion of parking spaces to other road users\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in the Assessment and Management of Spasticity: A Scoping Review](../publications/82b13827f67f2b99dbb0.md)

Ruoxi Cao; Ruojin Li; Joon Sin Ser; Yeow Leng Tan; Jing Chen

Spasticity is a prevalent and disabling consequence of upper motor neuron disorders, yet its assessment and management remains clinically challenging\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) may offer opportunities to enhance the objective assessment, prediction, and management of spasticity; however, the current evidence base has not been comprehensively characterised\. This review systematically mapped evidence on the application of AI across the continuum of spasticity care and identified key evidence gaps to inform future research\. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched for peer\-reviewed English\-language studies evaluating AI in adult spasticity\. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using NHLBI tools and PROBAST \+ AI\. This scoping review was prospectively registered with the Open Science Framework Registries\. The search yielded 1832 records, of which 21 studies were included after screening\. One additional study was identified through citation searching, bringing the total to 22 studies involving 1114 participants\. Applications spanned four clinical domains: discrimination between spastic and healthy individuals \(n = 2\), severity assessment \(n = 18\), risk prediction \(n = 1\), and treatment response prediction \(n = 1\)\. Most studies focused on post\-stroke upper limb spasticity\. Surface electromyography was the most frequently used input modality, often integrated with kinematic or kinetic sensors\. Conventional machine learning predominated, with reported accuracies of 74–96% and the Modified Ashworth Scale as the most common reference standard\. All 22 studies were at high overall risk of bias on PROBAST \+ AI, and none performed external validation, highlighting substantial methodological limitations that constrain clinical translation\.

## [Access to Justice for Deepfake Victims in Indonesia: A Normative Analysis of Privacy Rights Protection](../publications/82b2d9ff41151a0d4506.md)

Arini Salsabila; Ali Masyhar

Deepfake technology poses growing threats to privacy and personal dignity in Indonesia, particularly through the creation and dissemination of non\-consensual synthetic intimate imagery\. This study examines the extent to which Indonesia’s legal framework facilitates or constrains access to justice for victims of such practices and identifies the normative, procedural, institutional, and sociocultural barriers to effective legal protection\. Employing normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, the study analyzes primary and secondary legal materials, institutional reports, and selected comparative legal sources\. The analysis draws primarily on the Access to Justice framework, complemented by Satjipto Rahardjo’s Progressive Law theory to assess how existing legal provisions can be interpreted responsively to technological developments\. The findings indicate that Indonesian law provides partial protection through the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, the Sexual Violence Crimes Law, the Personal Data Protection Law, the Pornography Law, and the new Criminal Code\. However, these legal instruments remain fragmented and do not adequately address the specific challenges associated with the creation, identity misuse, and dissemination of synthetic intimate imagery\. In particular, gaps in legal characterization, procedural mechanisms, digital evidence management, and institutional coordination may impede victims’ access to effective remedies\. This study proposes a victim\-centred interim framework encompassing prompt content removal, privacy restoration, accessible reporting mechanisms, reliable digital evidence preservation, and enhanced institutional capacity\. These measures should be complemented by legislative reform that expressly addresses deepfake\-related harms and clarifies the responsibilities of digital platforms\. Comparative experiences from South Korea, the United Kingdom, and Australia are examined selectively to identify regulatory approaches that may be adapted to Indonesia’s legal and institutional context\. The study contributes to the development of a more coherent and responsive legal framework for protecting deepfake victims and strengthening access to justice in Indonesia\.

## [Integration of AI in Education Toward Future\-Ready Assessments](../publications/82b5008ebba301d9b9b4.md)

Einas AL Maqbali; Taef AL Riyami

This research examines the dual impact of artificial intelligence in education, in response to the rapid development of AI technologies\. The study explores how AI can enhance learning efficiency and educational outcomes while presenting challenges to academic integrity and fundamental skills development\. Employing a mixed\-methods approach, the study involved 44 EFL students in Oman and surveyed 102 students from various educational institutions\. Researchers analyzed students’ performance in both AI\-assisted and traditional writing tasks while observing behavioral patterns and attitudes toward these technologies\. Key findings revealed a 42% reduction in grammatical errors with AI assistance, yet 63% of students failed to fully follow instructions, demonstrating limited deep content understanding\. While 91% of students reported using AI tools, 60\.4% expressed the need for training in ethical usage\. The study concludes with three critical recommendations: developing clear institutional policies for AI governance, redesigning assessment methods to focus on learning processes rather than products and strengthening academic values and transparency\. These proposals align with the vision of balancing innovation with adaptation to technological change\.

## [DemoStream: Batched Task\-and\-Motion\-Plan Optimization for Automated Learning from Demonstration](../publications/82ed035a8c375ee96955.md)

Caelan Garrett; Neel Jawale; Fabio Ramos

Learning from demonstration is an effective strategy for endowing robots with manipulation capabilities but requires training on datasets comprised of massive amounts of demonstrations\. Existing demonstration collection approaches either require constant human involvement, for example, via teleoperation or are specialized for a single task\. Task and Motion Planning \(TAMP\) systems are able to autonomously solve and therefore generate demonstrations for general\-purpose tasks; however, learning from their demonstrations has proven difficult due to multi\-modality in their solutions\. In this work, we build on recent work leveraging GPU acceleration for TAMP and propose DemoStream, a TAMP system that optimizes demonstration quality in order to improve behavior cloning success rates\. First, we introduce batched TAMP sampling operations along with a new TAMP algorithm that correspondingly performs batched constraint satisfaction in order to explore many solutions in parallel\. We conduct simulation experiments ablating different action spaces, cost functions, and batch sizes to analyze the effect of these choices on downstream policy success rates\. Finally, we show that we can leverage the safety guarantees of TAMP to directly collect real\-world demonstrations at an average rate of 66 demos per hour\. See our website for policy rollout videos: demostream\.github\.io\.

## [The Impact of Generative AI on the Future of Work: Opportunities, Risks, and Human Skills](../publications/82ef3bf73c33818fcd1b.md)

Vahid Parsa

Background: Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) has expanded the range of cognitive tasks that can be assisted by software, raising questions about productivity, job displacement, and the future value of human skills\. Objective: To critically synthesize selected empirical and institutional evidence concerning productivity, occupational exposure, adoption, and skill complementarity\. Methods: This narrative review draws on a purposively selected set of peer\-reviewed studies, working papers, and institutional reports published primarily between 2023 and 2026\. It does not claim systematic coverage or PRISMA\-ScR compliance\. Findings: Controlled experiments document substantial productivity gains for some writing and programming tasks, while workplace evidence suggests heterogeneity across experience levels\. Occupational exposure estimates indicate the scope for task transformation but do not measure realized job losses\. Adoption studies show that workplace use is growing, yet aggregate outcomes remain uncertain\. Creative assistance may raise individual performance while narrowing output diversity\. Conclusions: The future of work is better understood through task reallocation, complementary skills, organizational implementation, and distributional choices than through simple predictions of mass replacement\. Further longitudinal and cross\-country research is needed\. Keywords: generative artificial intelligence; future of work; productivity; employment; occupational exposure; human skills; narrative review

## [A Review on Digital Twin with AI Based Predictive Maintenance System](../publications/82f40f1b45656915060b.md)

Nikambe S\. B; Maske V\. V; Pauskar S\. D; Kazi K\. S\.; Prof\. Patil J\. M

Predictive maintenance reduces unexpected machine failures and downtime by continuously observing equipment condition and identifying abnormal behaviour before severe failure occurs\. This review paper examines recent research on Digital Twin \(DT\), artificial intelligence \(AI\), machine learning, multi\-sensor condition monitoring, and predictive maintenance of industrial machines, with emphasis on induction motors\. Based on the reviewed literature, a low\-cost integrated architecture is proposed using temperature, vibration, current, and RPM sensing, an ESP32 controller, AI\-based fault prediction, Digital Twin updating, and IoT\-based monitoring\. Random Forest is considered as the main classification model because related literature demonstrates strong performance for motor\-fault classification\. Sample formulas for RMS vibration, mean, variance, RPM, and percentage change are presented\. The proposed workflow connects physical sensing, data processing, AI prediction, virtual representation, alert generation, and predictive\-maintenance decision support\. Illustrative graphs are included only as sample results and must be replaced by measured experimental data before final validation\.

## [Artificial intelligence and machine learning, a game changer in pharmaceutical development? – An updated perspective arising from Journees Galeniques 2024](../publications/82f6c808f448b41d2f32.md)

René Holm; Sanjay Konagurthu; Tausif Ahmed; Guillaume Louit; Brendan T\. Griffin; Sune Holm; Phatsawee Jansook; Wei Wu; Yi Lü; Christine Allen; Panagiota Angeli; Christel A\. S\. Bergström; Anette Müllertz; Daniel Reker; Ferrán Sanz; Martin Kuentz

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) are increasingly being applied across pharmaceutical development, from drug\-property prediction and safety assessment to formulation design, model\-informed development and clinical research\. This perspective synthesizes discussions from Journées Galéniques 2024 and updates them in light of scientific and regulatory developments through 2026\. ML enables prediction, pattern recognition, and data\-driven decision\-making, helping researchers identify drug targets, design new molecules, predict toxicity, and optimize drug properties\. In formulation development, ML can improve solubility prediction, excipient selection, and formulation strategy by reducing trial\-and\-error approaches\. AI\-based models and imaging technologies can also enhance understanding of drug delivery systems and improve prediction of in vivo performance\. However, much of the published literature remains retrospective and is based on small or heterogeneous datasets, with limited external, prospective or clinically relevant validation\. Recent regulatory frameworks place increasing emphasis on a clearly defined context of use, risk\-based assessment of model credibility, data governance, generalizability, human oversight and lifecycle management\. AI and ML should therefore be viewed not as replacements for pharmaceutical science, but as increasingly powerful tools that can strengthen and accelerate it\. Their broader impact will depend on high\-quality, interoperable data, rigorous validation, integration with pharmaceutical and clinical expertise, and clear evidence of meaningful clinical, manufacturing or regulatory value\.

## [Temporal Dynamics of Complement Activation and Outcome in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke](../publications/82fca6a13795fac204a8.md)

Yan Wang; Willeke F\. Westendorp; Merijn W\. Bijlsma; Michael W\.T\. Tanck; Wing Kit Man; Matthijs C\. Brouwer; Inge A\. Mulder; Jonathan M\. Coutinho; Diederik van de Beek

BACKGROUND: Immune\-mediated inflammatory responses exacerbate brain injury and affect the prognosis in acute ischemic stroke\. METHODS: We characterized longitudinal complement activation after acute ischemic stroke using serial plasma samples from 10 patients and 8 controls\. Initial markers of classical \(C1q\), lectin \(mannose\-binding lectin\), and alternative \(complement factor Bb\) pathways, as well as regulatory \(complement factor H\) and downstream markers \(C3a, C5a, and C5b\-9\) were measured by ELISA at 9 time points\. RESULTS: Patients with stroke showed broad complement activation, with increased C1q, mannose\-binding lectin, complement factor Bb, C3a, C5a, and C5b\-9, and reduced complement factor H compared with controls\. Complement components showed distinct temporal patterns during follow\-up\. Complement factor Bb levels were lower in patients with unfavorable functional outcome and in those with moderate\-to\-severe stroke\. C1q and C3a trajectories differed according to functional outcome, whereas C3a trajectories also differed according to stroke severity\. C1q trajectories differed according to age group and infarct volume\. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest dynamic, pathway\-specific complement activation after acute ischemic stroke and highlight the need for larger studies to clarify its prognostic and therapeutic relevance\.

## [CULINARY HERITAGE OF UKRAINE: POST\-WAR TRANSFORMATION AND DIGITAL APPROACHES TO PRESERVATION](../publications/83027c733a2b3e3614fd.md)

K\. Svidlo; Nataliia M\. Bogdan; Larysa V\. Obolentseva; Лідія Піддубна; Олена Каролоп

In the context of the post\-war transformation of rural areas in Ukraine, culinary tourism is considered an important tool for sustainable development and regional recovery\. The preservation and promotion of culinary heritage through tourism practices create opportunities for economic diversification, support of local communities, and strengthening of cultural identity\. The aim of the study is to analyze the processes of integrating Ukrainian culinary heritage into the tourism sector and to assess its impact on the development of rural areas under current conditions\. The methodological framework combines qualitative and quantitative approaches: semi\-structured interviews were conducted with stakeholders \(entrepreneurs, experts, and community representatives\), along with an analysis of statistical and analytical data for 2024–2025\. The results of the study show that culinary heritage is a key element of national identity, as it includes traditional recipes, cooking technologies, local ingredients, and gastronomic practices\. At the same time, its preservation is challenged by globalization, urbanization, and military conflict, which lead to the loss of cultural practices and the destruction of infrastructure\. It has been found that the effectiveness of culinary tourism development depends on the level of coordination among stakeholders and the involvement of local communities\. Insufficient public participation and fragmented policies reduce the potential of such initiatives, whereas participatory approaches enhance their effectiveness\. Culinary tourism contributes to rural development through job creation, the formation of local branding, and support for creative industries\. Digital technologies, including online archives and artificial intelligence tools, play a significant role in documenting and promoting heritage\. Culinary heritage has strong potential as a resource for the post\-war recovery of Ukraine; however, its effective use requires integrated governance, digitalization, and active community participation\.

This study aims to examine the effects of principals’ instructional leadership and AI\-assisted teacher instructional performance on students’ learning motivation in Economics subjects at senior high schools in Sub Rayon 03, Semarang Regency\. The study employed a quantitative approach with a survey method and a correlational design\. Primary data were obtained from students’ questionnaire responses\. The population comprised 184 students from four senior high schools, with a sample of 126 students determined using Slovin’s formula at a 5% margin of error\. Respondents were selected using \[insert the sampling technique used\]\. Data were collected through a closed\-ended questionnaire using a five\-point Likert scale\. Multiple linear regression analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25, with t\-tests, an F\-test, and the coefficient of determination assessed at a 5% significance level\. The results showed that principals’ instructional leadership had a positive and significant effect on students’ learning motivation \(B = 0\.622; t = 8\.358; p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas AI\-assisted teacher instructional performance had a negative and significant effect \(B = −0\.364; t = −3\.693; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. ## [Undergraduate Research for a Sustainable Future](../publications/831a1fd5a04ee5ad02f9.md)

Nancy H\. Hensel

This timely book presents undergraduate research as a powerful vehicle for engaging students in addressing the United Nations&\#x27; Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\)\. ## [A Qualitative Examination of Female Academics’ Awareness of Blockchain Technology](../publications/832b5199852fd0cb01ce.md)

Ayşen Konuşkan

This study examines female academics’ levels of awareness and perceptions of blockchain technology, as well as how they make sense of this technology within an academic context\. Adopting a qualitative phenomenological research design, semi\-structured interviews were conducted with ten female academics employed at Isparta University of Applied Sciences and Süleyman Demirel University\. The data were analyzed manually in line with the interpretative phenomenological analysis approach; meaningful statements were coded and grouped under sub\-themes and broader analytical categories\. The findings indicate that participants predominantly associate blockchain technology with security, transparency, data management, and reliable record\-keeping systems\. Although the overall level of awareness is limited, perceptions of blockchain were found to be mostly positive\. Participants considered this technology to offer significant opportunities not only for academic processes but also for areas such as education, healthcare, finance, and trade\. ## [An explainable graph transformer framework integrating structural reasoning and visual attention for interpretable nail disease diagnosis](../publications/83374e3883ab82f8f7ef.md)

R\. Bhuvanya; Sujithra Thandapani; M\. Mohamed Iqbal; S\. Adikrishanan

Abstract Automated nail\-disease classification remains a challenging task as different nail disorders present subtle and overlapping variations in color, texture and morphology\. This paper introduces GraphX, an explainable graph\-transformer framework that improves the baseline Graph Vision Transformer by incorporating image\-specific graph construction, graph\-transformer fusion, and attention guidance during training\. The Adaptive Graph Construction module constructs a sparse graph per image based on the cosine similarity of spatially and texture enriched patch representations and retains the eight most similar neighbors per patch\. The Cross\-Attention Fusion module allows reciprocal refinement between graph\-based structural embeddings and transformer\-based contextual tokens\. The Explainability\-Aware Attention module learns to match the attention distribution with continuous lesion\-prior maps generated from local intensity contrast and color deviation, providing weak spatial guidance without dermatologist\-annotated lesion mask\. In classification, GraphX achieved 94\.97% accuracy and macro\-averaged one\-vs\-rest ROC\-AUC of 0\.98, which outperformed the baseline models evaluated\. Explainability was measured with Grad\-CAM visualization, normalized attribution entropy, and deletion–insertion faithfulness testing\. The results demonstrate strong internal classification performance and provide preliminary evidence of model’s attention patterns, highlighting the potential of GraphX as a transparent framework for automated nail disease classification\.

## [Intergenerational Talent Management in Industry 4\.0: Toward Organisational Cybernetic Autopoiesis](../publications/833ab59ed176ca94bbb9.md)

Eben Haeser Swanepoel; Anna\-Marie Pelser

The advent of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, or Industry 4\.0, brings to the fore various opportunities for organisations to globalise with more efficient ways of implementing processes, from customer relations through artificial intelligence to the automation of production\. This article presents a desktop review exploring the influence of generational factors on employee talent management, aiming to develop a cybernetic theory to account for autopoiesis\. Framed through cybernetics and person–environment theory, this manuscript focuses on the tenets of systemic behavioural and communication patterns constituting generational cohorts subsumed by Generation Z, Generation X, Generation Y, and Baby Boomers, with specific reference to the global and South African context\. Leadership should potentially account for generational feedback loops that influence organisational non\-purposeful drift to sustain governance\. A heightened awareness of generational cultures influencing communication and behavioural patterns may allow leaders to better manage key personnel and potentially optimise resource pooling and feedback loops within the system to retain organisational integrity and promote organisational autopoiesis during future world of work disruptions and uncertainty\.

## [Web Traffic Time Series Forecasting Using GRU Neural Networks with Sequence\-to\-Sequence Architecture: A Case Study at a National University](../publications/833c9fb50824d110336a.md)

Enrique Gauto Sand; Alice Rambo

Este artículo presenta un caso de estudio sobre el pronóstico de series de tiempo de tráfico web para las páginas institucionales de una universidad nacional de Argentina\. La variable objetivo considerada en este estudio fue el número diario de vistas de página \(page views\), obtenido a partir de registros históricos de Google Analytics, complementada con variables derivadas de usuarios, sesiones, canales, dispositivos y procedencia geográfica\. Los datos provinieron de tres sitios web institucionales y fueron recolectados tanto mediante Universal Analytics \(UA\) como Google Analytics 4 \(GA4\), se implementaron redes neuronales recurrentes de Unidad Recurrente con Compuertas \(GRU\) con arquitectura secuencia a secuencia \(seq2seq\) codificador\-decodificador\. La metodología CRISP\-DM \(Chapman, et al\., 2000; Schröer, et al\., 2021; Shimaoka et al\., 2024\) guió el proceso completo de minería de datos, incluyendo recolección, preprocesamiento, diseño de modelos, entrenamiento y evaluación\. Se utilizó el algoritmo Hyperband para la optimización de hiperparámetros\. Los modelos fueron evaluados mediante el Error Medio Absoluto \(MAE\), la Raíz del Error Cuadrático Medio \(RMSE\) y el Error Absoluto Medio Porcentual Simétrico \(SMAPE\)\. Los resultados evidencian que, para el sitio TUM Transmedia, el mejor modelo alcanzó un MAE de aproximadamente 11 con datos de UA, superando resultados similares reportados en la literatura\. Al aplicar el modelo sobre datos de GA4, se mantuvo un MAE inferior a 30\. Para el sitio de la Editorial Universitaria, los resultados fueron menos satisfactorios, con un MAE de 71, lo que refleja la mayor complejidad de la dinámica de tráfico de ese sitio\. El trabajo demuestra la viabilidad de las redes GRU para el pronóstico de tráfico web institucional y sienta las bases para futuras investigaciones sobre analítica predictiva en la gestión de infraestructura universitaria\.

## [Spatially Programmable S‐Scheme Heterojunction Photoanodes via Aerosol‐Jet Printing for Efficient Solar Water Oxidation](../publications/835760a99b1ef794b7bd.md)

Xiaoli Ran; Feihong Ke; Wenzheng Yang; Yanlong Gong; Haitao Fu; Xizhong An; Dawei Su; Xiaohong Yang

ABSTRACT S‐scheme heterojunctions enable efficient charge separation while preserving the strong redox ability of photogenerated carriers, offering a powerful platform for advanced photoelectrochemical \(PEC\) water splitting\. However, translating such rationally designed heterostructures into scalable, high‐performance photoanodes remains a critical bottleneck for conventional fabrication methods\. Here, we develop an aerosol‐jet printing \(AJP\) approach to fabricate S‐scheme SrTiO 3 /g‐C 3 N 4 heterojunction photoanodes with well‐controlled stacking sequences\. The interfacial built‑in electric field drives recombination of SrTiO 3 photogenerated electrons with g‑C 3 N 4 holes, preserving the strongly oxidizing holes in SrTiO 3 for the oxygen evolution reaction \(OER\)\. The SrTiO 3 ‐on‐C 3 N 4 configuration delivers enhanced PEC water oxidation activity, with a photocurrent density of 2\.3 mA cm − 2 , double that of single‐component and reversed‐structure photoanodes\. It is found that this enhancement stems from stacking‐order‐dependent synergy between the heterojunction built‐in electric field and semiconductor‐electrolyte band bending\. Notably, AJP enables fabrication of large‐area, module‐sized photoanodes, demonstrating practical scalability for device manufacturing\. This work provides a controllable, scalable route for the rational design of high‐performance S‐scheme heterojunction photoelectrodes for PEC water splitting\.

## [Discrete Wavelet Transform and Multi\-scale Parallel Convolutional Network for gas recognition](../publications/8375508a57a30d38afd3.md)

Jingxiao Li; Lingwei Yu; Hai Yang; Zhe Wang

Abstract Electronic nose \(e\-nose\) systems based on metal oxide sensor arrays are widely deployed in food safety, environmental monitoring, and medical diagnosis\. However, accurate gas identification remains challenging due to two factors: \(1\) most deep learning methods insufficiently exploit the transient dynamics of sensor response signals, discarding critical time\-frequency information; \(2\) the limited receptive fields of standard convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) hinder the modelling of long\-range dependencies across sensor channels and temporal evolution\. To address these issues, we propose a Discrete Wavelet Transform and Multi\-scale Parallel Convolutional Network \(DWT\-MPCN\) that formulates gas recognition as a time\-frequency image classification problem\. Specifically, a fixed five\-level db5 discrete wavelet transform \(DWT\) module converts multi\-channel raw time\-domain signals into two\-dimensional wavelet coefficient maps without manual feature engineering, preserving both rapid transient details and slow recovery trends\. A Multi\-scale Parallel Convolution \(MPC\) module then employs parallel convolutional branches with different kernel sizes to simultaneously capture local transient features and broader contextual patterns while maintaining a lightweight architecture \(only 1\.75M parameters\)\. Finally, a convolutional Transformer encoder adaptively weights cross\-sensor and cross\-scale features to produce discriminative representations\. Evaluated on three public e\-nose datasets with distinct sensor configurations and gas types, DWT\-MPCN achieves competitive performance, including 99\.72% accuracy on the OPEN SAMPLING dataset, 99\.22% on the TWIN dataset, and 100% on the large\-scale array sensor dataset\. Component ablations, capacity\-aware comparisons, hyperparameter analyses, and wavelet\-parameter sensitivity studies validate the contribution of each component and clarify the design choices\. The proposed method provides a compact and interpretable framework for edge\-intelligent olfaction systems\.

## [Current strategies for controlling gastrointestinal nematodes of pigs in Europe](../publications/8376c58d1fe094a2dd95.md)

Luise Hohensee; Larissa Oser; Alexandra Laubschat; Josephine Schlosser\-Brandenburg; Friederike Ebner

Gastrointestinal nematodes \(GIN\) remain an often\-underestimated challenge in European pig production, affecting animal health, performance, and economic outcomes\. The predominant species, Ascaris \(A\.\) suum, Oesophagostomum \(O\.\) spp\., and Trichuris \(T\.\) suis, impair growth, feed efficiency, and carcass quality, whilst also contributing to reproductive losses and liver condemnation\. Moreover, GIN can modulate host immunity, interfere with vaccine responses, and influence coinfection outcomes, thereby compromising overall herd health\. The zoonotic potential of A\. suum and T\. suis further highlights the need for effective control strategies\. This review critically synthesises the available evidence on the occurrence, impact, and control of porcine GIN in Europe and identifies pig\-specific knowledge gaps and priorities for integrated control\. GIN occur across all European pig production systems\. However, accurate surveillance remains challenging due to methodological heterogeneity, uneven geographical coverage, and limited recent large\-scale epidemiological data\. Reported farm\-level prevalences therefore vary widely, ranging from 1 to 100% \(A\. suum\), 2\-27% \(O\. spp\.\), and 0\.3\-75% \(T\. suis\)\. Higher infection levels are generally reported in outdoor, organic, and small\-scale production systems\. Current control strategies largely depend on anthelmintics\. Reports of reduced efficacy and resistance, particularly in O\. spp\., highlight the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic\-based treatment\. Hygiene practices, housing design, flooring, bedding, pasture, and herd management can influence transmission, but their effectiveness under commercial conditions remains insufficiently evaluated\. Alternative approaches, including dietary interventions, probiotics, genetic selection, and vaccine development, may complement conventional measures, although most are not yet established for routine use\. Changes in climate, animal welfare requirements, production systems, and expectations concerning pharmaceutical use may further alter GIN exposure and control needs\. Standardised surveillance, contemporary assessments of animal health and economic consequences, field\-based intervention studies, and sustainable, integrated control programmes are therefore key priorities for European pig production\.

## [Discordant muscle\-adipose phenotypes and insulin resistance in prediabetes: sex\-specific associations and predictive utility of TyG\-WHtR combined with HDL\-C](../publications/83784272b9e334707910.md)

Zhishan Wang; Chen Lin; Yuanya Xie; Liangliang Huang; Shaojian Xiao; Huiyun Chen; Hongjie Ge; Yuxin Zhou; Jiaying Chen; Wensi Wu; Xiaoling Wang; Shujiao Chen

Objective We aimed to explore the interplay between muscle\-adipose composite phenotypes and insulin resistance \(IR\) among individuals with prediabetes\(Pre\-DM\), and to evaluate the discriminative capacity and sex\-specific variations of the triglyceride\-glucose\-waist\-to\-height ratio \(TyG\-WHtR\) when combined with high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol \(HDL\-C\)\. Methods A total of 167 subjects with Pre\-DM were enrolled and categorized into four phenotypes—high\-muscle/low\-fat, high\-muscle/high\-fat, low\-muscle/high\-fat, and low\-muscle/low\-fat—based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index and visceral fat level\. Fasting blood glucose, lipid profiles, and body composition parameters were measured, and the TyG index and its derived indices were calculated\. Hierarchical linear regression and logistic regression were used to evaluate the independent and interactive contributions of these phenotypes, lipid profiles, and TyG\-derived indices to HOMA\-IR\. Subsequently, a nomogram was constructed using binary logistic regression, and its performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\), calibration curve, decision curve analysis \(DCA\), and clinical impact curve \(CIC\)\. Results Significant intergroup differences emerged for body mass index, waist circumference, fasting insulin, HOMA\-IR, HDL\-C, and TyG\-derived indices \(all P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Spearman’s correlation analysis revealed that fasting insulin and HOMA\-IR were positively correlated with WHtR, waist circumference, BMI, body fat mass, visceral fat level, body fat percentage, and ASMI \(all P &lt; 0\.01\)\. Triglycerides showed a positive correlation with these metrics, whereas HDL\-C exhibited a negative correlation \(all P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Notably, TyG\-WHtR displayed the strongest correlation with HOMA\-IR \( P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Hierarchical regression identified HM/HF as the strongest independent predictor of HOMA\-IR, remaining significant after full adjustment \(B = 3\.264, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. The protective effect of LM/LF was attenuated to marginal significance after adjusting for blood lipids \(B=−0\.705, P = 0\.082\), suggesting that this association largely reflects low visceral fat rather than muscle mass per se\. The final model accounted for 36\.0% of the variance in HOMA\-IR\. We did not detect a statistically significant multiplicative interaction \( P =0\.089\); however, the study may be underpowered, and additive interaction was not formally assessed\. In exploratory stratified analyses, the HM/HF effect was more pronounced in men \(B = 5\.662\) and in adults aged &lt;60 years \(B = 4\.425\), whereas the protective LM/LF effect was restricted to women \(B=−0\.914\)\. In the ≥60\-year group, the sex coefficient changed from negative to positive without reaching significance, suggesting that age may modify the sex effect; formal interaction testing is needed to confirm this possibility\. Logistic regression identified TyG\-WHtR \(OR=8\.231\) and HDL\-C \(OR=0\.183\) as independent determinants of IR; the corresponding Cohen’s d values exceeded the conventional large\-effect threshold of 0\.8\. The combined nomogram achieved an AUC of 0\.815 \(95% CI 0\.748–0\.881\)\. The Hosmer\-Lemeshow test showed no evidence of departure from perfect calibration, and the calibration curve derived from 1000 bootstrap resamples closely followed the ideal diagonal line\. Decision curve analysis indicated that, across threshold probabilities of 0\.2–0\.8, the net benefit remained consistently greater than that of both the “intervene\-all” and “intervene\-none” strategies\. Conclusion In Pre\-DM, insulin resistance appears to be driven primarily by visceral adiposity rather than overall obesity\. The metabolic impact of skeletal muscle is highly dependent on the surrounding lipid milieu\. The interaction term between low muscle mass and high visceral fat was non\-significant, with no multiplicative interaction detected\. Consequently, it remained inconclusive whether their effects on IR followed an additive pattern\. Sex and age may modify the association between body composition and IR, although formal interaction testing is needed to confirm this\. The nomogram integrating TyG\-WHtR and HDL\-C demonstrated good calibration and may serve as a practical screening tool in primary care settings\. Maintaining moderate muscle mass in the context of low visceral adiposity is likely to confer greater metabolic benefit\.

## [Research on Visual Communication Design Based on Communication Theory](../publications/838ae417db287b8834d3.md)

Xuelian Lv; Ju Li

In the era of information overload and rapid digital transformation, visual communication design faces challenges in accurately and attractively transmitting information\. This study conducts a case\-driven analysis of two Information Technology \(IT\)\-integrated projects: Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes&\#x27; digital initiative \(using TikTok short videos and Unity 3D/Augmented Reality \(AR\) with &gt;1m Location\-Based Service\) and Suzhou Wenlv&\#x27;s brand modernization \(via interactive HTML5 \(H5\) and semiotics\-based symbol optimization\)\. Empirical results show that short\-video channels achieved 300% user growth with 87% longer user engagement, while AR\-based channels delivered 500% user growth with 82% longer engagement\. Meanwhile, AI\-driven visual symbol optimization improved accuracy of information memory by 63% and cross\-cultural recognition rate by 62% \(A/B test, N=200\)\. Challenges include theoretical complexity and creativity constraints\. The study offers a reusable framework for integrating communication theory with AR/dynamic media to optimize visual communication in cultural/commercial contexts\.

## [When Protection Becomes Control: Parental Fear and the Reorganization of Familial Intimacy in Hold Tight](../publications/83a3be87cd6e3704a49e.md)

C\. Wulan Ndari; Mia Fitria Agustina; Ririn Kurnia Trisnawati

This paper explores how parental anxiety shapes both behavior and perception in Hold Tight, particularly within the parent\-child relationship\. Using a psychoanalytic approach, especially Melanie Klein’s theory, combined with contemporary psychological perspectives, the analysis focuses on digital surveillance as a response to parental anxiety and the projection of fear onto the child as parental confidence declines\. The findings show that surveillance is not only used as a form of protection but also becomes a way of maintaining control, which gradually disrupts trust and relational boundaries\. At the same time, anxiety influences perception, leading to interpretive bias, projection, and projective identification, where the child is no longer seen as they are but as a reflection of parental fear\. Overall, this paper highlights that parental anxiety operates on both behavioral and psychological levels, affecting not only what parents do but also how they interpret their child, ultimately transforming care into control and creating distance within the relationship\.

## [The impact of comprehensive medical system reform on rural household economic resilience](../publications/83ad0c73f8c07e97bdb2.md)

Tianshu Zhang; Jianguo Dong

Introduction Strengthening the capacity of rural families to withstand health\-related economic shocks is critical to consolidating poverty alleviation achievements and preventing large\-scale relapse into poverty\. However, existing studies pay limited attention to the resilience\-shaping effects of the medical security system as a fundamental social policy, especially among rural households\. Methods Using data from the China Family Panel Studies \(CFPS\) from 2012 to 2022, this paper employs a single\-period difference\-in\-differences method to empirically examine the impact of comprehensive medical system reform on rural household economic resilience and its underlying mechanisms\. Results The results indicate that the reform significantly enhances rural household economic resilience, and this finding remains robust across a series of robustness checks\. Mechanism analysis suggests that the reform may enhance resilience by reducing medical burden and alleviating financial vulnerability\. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that these effects are more pronounced among high\-income families and those with higher levels of social trust\. Discussion This study expands the evaluative horizon of medical security system reforms in terms of economic outcomes and offers empirical evidence to support the deepening of medical reform and the prevention of poverty induced by illness\.

## [Dentists’ Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence in Dental Practice](../publications/83bb5e4ec6bc0829fd17.md)

Anshuman Swami; Astha Chauhan; Bhuvnesh Airen; Ranjan Mani Tripathi; Chirag Vyas; Surbhi Gendar

Background: Dentists’ readiness to use artificial intelligence \(AI\) remains an important concern in dental practice\.Aim: This study explored attitudes, perceived barriers, and willingness to use AI\.Materials and Methods: A survey of 220 dentists was analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson’s chi\-square tests\.Results: Willingness was 70\.0%, while 75\.0% reported privacy concerns and 90\.0% reported a demand for training\.Conclusion: This analysis provides a framework for studying responsible AI adoption and testing educational needs in future empirical research\.

## [Effect of Risk Management Strategies on the Mitigation of Cybersecurity Threats in Fintech Companies in Nairobi City, Kenya](../publications/83d1aced96aac9357dee.md)

Justine Odero; Samuel Osike; E Bor

Purpose: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of risk management strategies on the mitigation of cybersecurity threats in fintech companies in Nairobi City, Kenya\. Specifically, the study identified the cybersecurity threats faced by fintech companies, assessed the types and levels of risk management strategies they employ, and determined the effect of these strategies on threat mitigation\. Methodology: The study adopted a correlational research design anchored on Deterrence Theory and the Resource\-Based View\. The target population comprised 306 cybersecurity, risk, information technology and compliance professionals drawn from 98 fintech companies in Nairobi City\. A sample of 173 respondents was selected through stratified random sampling and 12 key informants were purposively selected\. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and key informant interviews, and 145 usable questionnaires were returned \(83\.8%\)\. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression, while qualitative data were analysed thematically\. Findings: Malware infections were the most prevalent threat \(M = 4\.57, SD = 0\.524\), followed by phishing \(M = 3\.46\) and Distributed Denial of Service \(DDoS\) attacks \(M = 3\.41\), although the consequences of DDoS attacks were rated as severe \(M = 3\.91\)\. Regular vulnerability assessments \(M = 3\.83\) and threat intelligence gathering \(M = 3\.79\) were the most widely implemented practices, while technical controls recorded the lowest level of implementation \(M = 3\.52\)\. Risk management practices were strongly correlated with mitigation \(r = \.705, p &lt; \.01\) and explained 49\.8% of the variance in mitigation outcomes \(R² = \.498, F = 141\.604, p &lt; \.01\), rising to 55\.6% when threat exposure was added \(R² = \.556, F = 89\.050, p &lt; \.01\)\. Improved perception of security posture \(M = 4\.04\) was rated higher than reduction of the financial impact of attacks \(M = 3\.31\), revealing a perception–protection gap\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Fintech companies should enforce multi\-factor authentication, move from annual to continuous vulnerability scanning, institute role\-based awareness training with phishing simulations, and appoint dedicated cybersecurity personnel in proportion to their risk profile\. Regulators should harmonise Kenya’s fragmented cybersecurity rules into proportionate minimum standards for all categories of fintech, mandate independent security audits for high\-volume firms, and operationalise sector\-wide threat intelligence sharing\. Theoretically, the study shows that deterrence in fintech cybersecurity works mainly through denial rather than punishment, and that resource\-based advantage lies in dynamic cybersecurity capabilities rather than in information technology budgets\.

## [Perbandingan RoBERTa dan Lexicon\-Based untuk Pseudo\-Labeling Sentimen Komentar YouTube dengan Machine Learning](../publications/83e9f494a2997594835f.md)

Valentino Juanito; Manuele Jocelyn Blasius; Hafiz Irsyad; Abdul Rahman

Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan pendekatan RoBERTa dan Lexicon\-Based dalam menghasilkan pseudo\-label sentimen komentar YouTube serta mengevaluasi kinerja algoritma machine learning dalam mengklasifikasikan label yang dihasilkan\. Data penelitian berasal dari komentar pada video “Presiden Prabowo Menjawab \(PART 2\): Efisiensi, Pertaruhan MBG &amp; Reformasi Kepolisian” dari Mata Najwa\. Setelah proses penyaringan dan preprocessing, diperoleh 2\.850 komentar yang dianalisis\. Penelitian menerapkan dua jalur preprocessing, yaitu pemrosesan minimal pada RoBERTa untuk mempertahankan konteks kalimat serta pemrosesan tambahan pada Lexicon\-Based melalui tokenisasi dan penghapusan stopword\. Label sentimen yang dihasilkan oleh kedua pendekatan digunakan untuk melatih dan mengevaluasi algoritma Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), Naïve Bayes, dan Neural Network menggunakan fitur Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency \(TF\-IDF\)\. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa pada dataset berlabel RoBERTa, Neural Network memperoleh nilai accuracy sebesar 0,7333 dan F1\-score sebesar 0,6024\. Sementara itu, pada dataset berlabel Lexicon\-Based, SVM menghasilkan accuracy sebesar 0,6439 dan F1\-score sebesar 0,6323\. Dengan demikian, Neural Network menghasilkan accuracy tertinggi pada dataset berlabel RoBERTa, sedangkan SVM menghasilkan F1\-score tertinggi pada dataset berlabel Lexicon\-Based\. Perbedaan hasil tersebut menunjukkan adanya variasi kinerja klasifikasi pada kedua skema pelabelan otomatis\. Namun, karena evaluasi didasarkan pada label hasil pseudo\-labeling, nilai metrik tersebut menggambarkan kemampuan model dalam mereplikasi label otomatis dan belum secara langsung membuktikan ketepatan klasifikasi terhadap sentimen sebenarnya\. Validasi menggunakan anotasi manusia diperlukan untuk menilai kualitas label dan memperkuat kesimpulan penelitian\.

## [Digital Islam as an Institutional Governance Lens: An Exploratory Survey of Digital Practices and Knowledge Integration in Sharia Study Programs at UIN Antasari](../publications/83ea51495367331efac6.md)

Arie Sulistyoko; Ergina Faralita

Digital transformation in Islamic higher education involves institutional arrangements as well as technological services\. This cross\-sectional, descriptive\-exploratory survey maps perceptions of digital practices, knowledge integration, and governance\-change priorities in Sharia\-related study programs at UIN Antasari\. The online questionnaire was circulated through class WhatsApp groups in each participating study program and by direct WhatsApp contact with lecturers during May 1–June 19, 2026\. Responses came from 53 participants \(43 students and 10 lecturers\) recruited through nonprobability channels; the number invited and response rate were not documented\. Descriptive statistics and thematic coding were used\. Digital\-practice items were completed by only 10 lecturers, with a composite score of 82\.8/100; knowledge integration scored 82\.9/100 \(n = 53\), and perceived need for governance transformation scored 84\.2/100 \(n = 53\)\. Five items measuring existing governance conditions had no responses in the raw export; current governance performance was therefore not assessed\. Thematic coding identified 38 substantive responses on knowledge integration \(multiple codes permitted\) and 30 substantive governance\-improvement priorities \(one dominant theme each\)\. Results inform a tentative four\-domain governance mapping, with Digital Islam employed as an interpretive ethical lens, not a measured variable\. SIGAP\-Syariah is proposed as an unvalidated self\-assessment prototype; institutional competitiveness is a prospective implication rather than an observed outcome\.

## [Preparing Teachers to Assess in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Critical Integrative Review and Framework for Assessment\-AI Knowledge](../publications/83ec510b4bc6e5011773.md)

Konstantinos Τ\. Kotsis

Artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly generative AI, changes assessment by altering the evidential relationship among student work, learning, and professional judgment\. Teachers must design tasks when students can readily obtain machine\-generated responses, interpret automated feedback and analytics whose validity is conditional, and justify consequential decisions under uncertainty\. This critical integrative review synthesizes scholarship on AI in education, assessment, teacher learning, and emerging professional\-development interventions\. It proposes Assessment\-AI Knowledge \(A\-AIK\) as an assessment\-specific configuration of professional knowledge rather than a replacement for assessment literacy, AI literacy, or technological pedagogical content knowledge\. A\-AIK comprises three interdependent capacities: design competence, which establishes conditions for eliciting meaningful evidence; interpretive competence, which calibrates the meaning, uncertainty, and evidential weight of AI\-mediated information; and justificatory competence, which supports transparent, fair, and reviewable decisions\. Disciplinary authenticity, human agency, equity, transparency and data governance, and epistemic humility operate as cross\-cutting commitments\. The reviewed literature suggests that promising interventions use scenarios, authentic assessment redesign, structured critique, peer deliberation, and iterative classroom trials\. Recurrent limitations include small samples, reliance on self\-report, short duration, and measures of confidence or acceptance rather than demonstrated assessment performance\. A four\-phase professional\-learning model—calibrate, redesign, enact, and justify, is proposed as a synthesis\-informed design hypothesis requiring empirical evaluation\. The article concludes with provisional performance indicators, institutional conditions, and a research agenda for responsible AI\-mediated assessment\.

## [The impact of generative artificial intelligence on business process design and optimization](../publications/83ef06c1b22c33f15a10.md)

Dragana Jovanović

V času, ko generativna umetna inteligenca postaja vse bolj prisotna v poslovnem okolju, se odpirajo nove možnosti za njeno uporabo pri analizi, modeliranju in optimizaciji poslovnih procesov\. Prenova procesov je pogosto časovno zahtevna in odvisna od strokovnega znanja procesnega analitika, zato se postavlja vprašanje kakovosti in praktične uporabnosti rezultatov generativnih orodij\. Magistrsko delo obravnava generativno umetno inteligenco kot podporo pri prenovi poslovnih procesov\. Predmet obravnave je proces nabave, ki poteka od prejete interne nabavne zahteve do poslanega naročila dobavitelju\. Pri procesu so bile ugotovljene pomanjkljivosti, kot so papirna dokumentacija, večkratno vnašanje podatkov, nepovezani informacijski sistemi, razpršeno potrjevanje in omejena sledljivost\. Rezultati tradicionalne prenove so bili primerjani z rezultati orodij ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot in Claude\. ChatGPT je pripravil podrobna grafična modela procesa, Claude pa bolj zgoščena in pregledna modela\. Microsoft 365 Copilot je proces predstavil samo v besedilni obliki\. Rezultati kažejo, da so vsa tri orodja prepoznala glavne težave procesa in predlagala povezovanje informacijskih sistemov, elektronsko potrjevanje, spremljanje statusa ter digitalno izmenjavo in arhiviranje dokumentacije\. Njihova uporaba je pomembno skrajšala čas priprave analiz in predlogov za prenovo\. Sklepno ugotavljamo, da lahko generativna umetna inteligenca predstavlja učinkovito podporo pri prenovi poslovnih procesov, vendar je treba rezultate preveriti z vidika poslovnih pravil, organizacijskega okolja in tehnične izvedljivosti\. Strokovnega znanja in praktičnih izkušenj procesnega analitika zato ne more v celoti nadomestiti\.

## [Rethinking AI integration in African higher education: a mixed\-methods investigation of capacity, equity, and governance across sub\-Saharan Africa](../publications/83f6c48c35c54d22a9bb.md)

J\. N\. A\. Aryee; P\. Davies; G\. A\. Torsah; M\. M\. Apaw; S\. M\. Mwando; C\. Kwisanga; C\. D\. Boateng; Eric Ouma Jobunga; D\. Mutale; Leonard  Kofitse Amekudzi

The Revolutionizing Tertiary Education for Africa&\#x27;s Thriving AI Economy and Workforce \(RetAIn\) project presents a comprehensive, multi\-method investigation into the conditions, constraints, and catalysts shaping Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) adoption across African Higher Education Institutions \(HEIs\)\. Deploying both qualitative multi\-stakeholders Focus Group Discussions \(FGDs\) from three African countries \(Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia\) and a quantitative cross\-country survey across five Sub\-Saharan African nations \(Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya, and Zambia\), this study produces a richly triangulated account of AI integration dynamics on the continent\. The FGD strand revealed a stark divergence in national AI trajectories: Rwanda operates under a strong top\-down policy vision hindered by institutional rigidity; Namibia exhibits pragmatic institutional adaptability constrained by geographic and economic smallness; and Ghana demonstrates emergent, bottom\-up innovation within a national policy vacuum\. The survey strand, drawing on 156 responses across five countries, corroborated these qualitative tensions, documenting widespread recognition of AI&\#x27;s strategic importance alongside limited structured engagement, persistent infrastructure deficits, and marked equity barriers, particularly for women, vulnerable groups, rural students, and part\-time workers\. From both methods, a unifying finding emerges: AI integration in African HEIs consistently fails when technical adoption outpaces social, pedagogical, and governance co\-evolution\. The study argues for context\-specific, socio\-technically grounded strategies that pair curriculum co\-design with robust industry partnerships, that centre equity and cultural relevance, and build governance frameworks capable of guiding, rather than chasing, technological change\.

## [Pembrolizumab\-associated primary hypothyroidism followed by central hypothyroidism: a case report](../publications/84025b55ab3f172f9045.md)

Jiawei Sun; C\. Wang; Zhanzhan Sun; Wei Li

Introduction PD\-1 inhibitors are widely used anticancer drugs and frequently trigger immune\-related adverse events, with thyroid dysfunction as the most prevalent\. Suspected isolated central hypothyroidism emerging during PD\-1 inhibitor therapy has rarely been documented\. Case presentation A 56\-year\-old man received pembrolizumab for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma\. Before treatment, he had pre\-existing Hashimoto’s thyroiditis with low TT4 and normal TSH\. He developed painless thyroiditis manifesting as transient thyrotoxicosis followed by primary hypothyroidism\. Shortly after hypothyroidism was pharmacologically controlled, TSH progressively declined to the lower limit of detection, accompanied by low TT4\. Pituitary MRI showed pituitary gland thinning without focal structural abnormalities\. Integrating the clinical course, central hypothyroidism was considered\. Given altered upper gastrointestinal anatomy after esophagectomy, split\-dose levothyroxine was administered, and the patient’s FT4 levels remained stable\. Conclusion This rare sequential evolution of thyroid dysfunction may represent an uncommon endocrine immune\-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitors\.
