## [Severity\-dependent and sex\-biased dysregulation of A\-to\-I RNA editing in COVID\-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target](../publications/840d6e0acb0f675d2440.md)

Jingyuan Wang; Zhao Ya\-di; Li\-Ping Wang; Yu\-Qing Ren; Jia\-Nuo Li; Teng Wang; Hua\-Kang Zhang; Feng Zhu; Jian‐Huan Chen; Yunyun Jin

SARS\-CoV\-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease\. Adenosine\-to\-inosine \(A\-to\-I\) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID\-19 severity and sex\-biased disease remains unclear\. We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non\-COVID controls and COVID\-19 patients spanning different disease severities\. We detected 1,466 differentially RNA\-edited sites in 514 genes linked to clinical outcomes\. Although ADAR expression increased in COVID\-19 patients overall, it was strongly reduced in ICU patients compared with non\-ICU patients, and this shift was far more prominent in males\. This severity\-associated and sex\-biased ADAR/ADARB1 downregulation coincided with decreased global RNA editing and perturbed expression of immune\-related edited transcripts\. Cathepsin S \(CTSS\) was identified as a central regulatory node: elevated A\-to\-I editing within its 3&\#x27; UTR in ICU patients stabilizes CTSS mRNA\. Without stratifying by disease severity, ADAR expression and global editing showed no significant sex differences; the large sex divergence only appeared among ICU patients\. This indicates severity\-dependent, not infection\-innate, disruption of A\-to\-I editing, disproportionately amplified in critically ill males\. CTSS 3&\#x27;UTR editing may serve as a biomarker for patient stratification, revealing a mechanistic connection between epitranscriptomic changes and male\-biased severe COVID\-19\.

## [Advancing generative AI for stakeholder empowerment in community\-based tourism: an experimental approach to inclusivity and sustainability](../publications/8410e3329a822280499b.md)

Jinsheng Jason Zhu; Aranya Siriphon

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is transforming community\-based tourism \(CBT\) by promoting inclusivity and sustainability\. This study investigates the use of Kimi\.ai, a GenAI platform developed by Moonshot AI, to simulate interactions among six key stakeholder groups: administrators, investors, entrepreneurs, local business owners, marginalized residents, and tourists\. The findings demonstrate that identity\-based chatbot interactions effectively address stakeholder\-specific needs, support cultural preservation, and encourage economic inclusivity\. Through thematic and sentiment analyses, the study shows GenAI’s potential to enhance stakeholder engagement, resource coordination, and problem\-solving within Community\-Based Tourism ecosystems\. It offers practical insights for policymakers and practitioners, highlighting GenAI’s role in advancing equitable and sustainable tourism\. Future research on emerging technologies is encouraged to further strengthen decision\-making and operational effectiveness in community\-based tourism development\.

## [The relationship between functional prognosis in patients with infection after upper limb trauma: a predictive model based on HbA1c stratification and the mediating role of delayed rehabilitation](../publications/8410e57f79b78f995b26.md)

Sheng Chen; YiFei Zhu; 田敏涛; Honglei Hu; Lu Xu; BiYun Li

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between preoperative glycated hemoglobin \(HbA1c\) and upper limb function \(Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand \[DASH\] score\) at 6 months post\-surgery in patients with fracture\-related infection \(FRI\) after upper limb trauma, and to test the mediating role of rehabilitation initiation time\. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 100 patients with FRIs after upper limb trauma surgery \(September 2020 to August 2025\)\. Demographic characteristics, fracture features, HbA1c levels, time to initiate rehabilitation, and debridement frequency of patients were collected\. With the DASH score at 6 months after surgery as the outcome variable, multiple linear regression was used to analyze the association between HbA1c and functional prognosis, and the Bootstrap method was used to test the mediating effect of rehabilitation initiation time\. RESULTS: HbA1c was significantly positively correlated with the DASH score \(β = 6\.90, 95% CI 3\.91\-9\.89, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Recovery initiation time played a partial mediating role between the HbA1c and the DASH scores, with a mediating ratio of 27% \(indirect effect 2\.04, 95% CI 0\.63\-3\.59, p = 0\.004\)\. There was no significant interaction between HbA1c and recovery initiation time or debridement frequency \(p &gt; 0\.05\)\. Thresholding effect analysis did not find a definite breakpoint \(log\-likelihood ratio test p = 0\.220\), and HbA1c was linearly related to the DASH score\. CONCLUSION: Preoperative HbA1c is independently associated with 6\-month upper limb function in patients with post\-traumatic infection, with rehabilitation initiation time playing a partial mediating role\. Clinicians should prioritize glycemic control and initiate rehabilitation as early as safely possible\.

## [Biological Significance of Peptides and Their Role in the Functioning of Tissues, Organs, and Cells: A Comprehensive Review with a Focus on Immunomodulatory Potential](../publications/84157fa4b8b74e689447.md)



Peptides are essential biologically active natural products present in a vast array of living organisms\.These molecules, isolated from animal, avian, marine, and plant tissues, possess significant nutraceutical and therapeutic value due to their broad spectrum of biological activities, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and neuroprotective effects\.This article provides an in\-depth analysis of the role of regulatory peptides in maintaining genetic homeostasis and coordinating cellular populations\.Special attention is given to tissue\-specific bioregulators and their capacity to restore functional impairments in corresponding organs\.The study emphasizes the importance of the Bursa of Fabricius as a unique source of immunomodulatory peptides in avian species and its potential implications for human medicine\.Furthermore, the mechanisms of peptide interaction with the blood\-brain barrier and their role in metabolic regulation, including anti\-diabetic and anti\-atherosclerotic activities, are discussed\.The findings underscore the potential of peptidebased drug development for chronic disease prevention and immune system correction\.

## [Spatial Statistics for Screening Molecular Structures](../publications/8419caf4347fa29a710b.md)

Pranoy Ray; Surya R\. Kalidindi

ABSTRACT The dominant paradigm in computational materials discovery relies on heavily parameterized deep architectures, including message‐passing graph and equivariant networks, that typically require large density functional theory \(DFT\)‐labeled training sets and produce nonconvex latent representations complicating inverse design, a limitation in the data‐scarce regimes common to exploratory screening\. Standard formulations also face specific difficulties with chemically disordered configurations and with distinguishing chiral geometries \(e\.g\., ‐invariant models are reflection‐blind by construction\)\. These are task‐ and formulation‐dependent tendencies, not universal deficiencies, and are reduced by pre‐training, transfer, and equivariant designs\. This review presents spatial‐statistics feature engineering as a physically rigorous, deployable complement\. Molecular structures are encoded as voxelized fields, and two‐point auto‐ and cross‐correlations are evaluated deterministically via Fast Fourier Transforms, moving spatial pattern recognition into a closed‐form, physics‐informed operation\. Principal component analysis yields low‐dimensional, convex representations supporting lean neural networks and non‐parametric surrogates, achieving sub‐2% normalized errors from as little as 0\.1% of the dataset in reported cases\. Demonstrated across periodic crystals, disordered high‐entropy alloys, and non‐periodic molecules, the framework enables Bayesian active learning and zero‐shot extrapolation on commodity hardware, which remains challenging for large‐scale architectures at equal data budgets\.

## [A hybrid predictive and uncertainty\-aware framework for renewable hydrogen system efficiency assessment and sustainable energy planning](../publications/841c1f92122c7df133fb.md)

Anjan Kumar; Anuradha Devi Tellapati; Tariq Alkhrissat; B Spoorthi; M\. G\. M\. Johar; Satish Choudhury; S\. Radhika; Gaganjot Kaur

Abstract Renewable hydrogen is emerging as a critical element in the transition toward low\-carbon and sustainable energy systems; however, accurately evaluating system efficiency remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear interactions among technical and environmental factors\. This study proposes a hybrid predictive and uncertainty\-aware framework for assessing renewable hydrogen system efficiency and supporting sustainable energy planning\. The framework integrates Elastic Net and Extra Trees regression models enhanced through meta\-heuristic optimization using Sparrow Search and Firefly algorithms to improve predictive performance\. Recursive Feature Elimination is applied to identify the most influential variables governing system behavior, while Dempster–Shafer Theory is incorporated to model uncertainty and construct a robust ensemble prediction strategy\. The proposed approach is evaluated using a dataset of 2,535 renewable hydrogen system records with spatial attributes derived from documented geographical coordinates\. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in predictive accuracy, with a 12% increase in R² and a 15% reduction in MAE compared to baseline approaches\. Sensitivity analysis indicates that photovoltaic power generation and electrolysis efficiency are the most influential factors affecting hydrogen system performance\. Beyond improved prediction accuracy, the framework provides interpretable insights that can support infrastructure development, investment planning, and energy policy design\. The proposed methodology demonstrates how hybrid predictive modeling combined with uncertainty quantification can enhance decision\-making processes in renewable hydrogen systems and contribute to more reliable low\-carbon energy transitions\.

## [Stimuli\-Responsive Hydrogel Platforms for Precision Management of Diabetic Wounds: Integrating Controlled Drug Delivery, Biomarker Sensing, and Tissue Regeneration](../publications/842a0387106b2d98a688.md)

Swati Srivastava; Zufnoon Khan; Md\. Quamuddin; Md Sarafaraz Alam; Priya Pandey; Nitin Kumar; Amit Kumar; Deepak Garg; Md Sarafaraz Alam; Shubham Sharma

Background: Diabetic wounds represent a critical global health challenge, affecting over 40 million individuals worldwide\. The complex pathophysiology\-characterized by hyperglycemia, persistent inflammation, excessive oxidative stress, recurrent bacterial infection, and impaired angiogenesis\-renders conventional wound dressings inadequate for effective management\. Objective: This review critically evaluates recent advances in stimuli\-responsive hydrogel platforms designed for precision management of diabetic wounds, with emphasis on systems integrating controlled drug delivery, realtime biomarker sensing, and tissue regeneration capabilities\. Methods: A comprehensive literature review was conducted focusing on smart hydrogel systems responsive to glucose, pH, reactive oxygen species \(ROS\), temperature, and enzymes\. Studies were categorized based on responsive mechanisms, therapeutic payloads, and preclinical efficacy outcomes\. Results: Stimuli\-responsive hydrogels demonstrate significant advantages over conventional dressings through their ability to sense microenvironmental changes and execute programmed therapeutic responses\. Glucoseresponsive systems utilizing phenylboronic acid or glucose oxidase enable self\-regulated insulin delivery\. pHresponsive platforms exploit the acidic\-to\-alkaline transition in infected wounds for targeted antimicrobial release\. ROS\-scavenging hydrogels incorporating nanozymes or antioxidant polymers restore redox balance\. Multiresponsive systems achieve synergistic therapeutic effects by integrating multiple sensing modalities\. Nanohybrid architectures\-incorporating metal nanoparticles, carbon\-based nanomaterials, and metal\-organic frameworksenhance mechanical properties and add multifunctional capabilities including real\-time wound monitoring\. Conclusion: Stimuli\-responsive hydrogel platforms represent a paradigm shift in diabetic wound management, moving from passive coverage to active, intelligent intervention\. Key challenges remain in clinical translation, including regulatory approval pathways, long\-term biosafety validation, cost\-effective manufacturing, and integration with point\-of\-care diagnostic technologies\.

## [Magnetic‐Field‐Annealing‐Induced Short‐Range Order in High‐Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response](../publications/84334a1ceae0d4d7f651.md)

Lu‐Yang Li; Zhuang Ma; Ji‐Xing Bai; Wen‐Qiang Cao; Lihong Gao; Qi Cao; Miao Jiang; Mao‐Sheng Cao

The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response\. Here, magnetic field annealing \(MFA\) is investigated in rGO\-supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0\.5, and 0\.95 T\. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0\.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses\. Reflection loss yields a minimum of \-72\.30 dB at 1\.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4\.40 GHz\. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4\.08 GHz, corresponding to 92\.7% retention of temperature\-specific maxima\. Local microscopy, field\-associated atomistic modeling, and fixed\-composition electronic\-structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co\-centered chemical correlations\. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration\.

## [Legalità algoritmica e antropocentrismo formale: la deci\-sione amministrativa automatizzata alla prova dell&\#x27;art\. 14 l\. 132/2025](../publications/84455de695ae4db9af1e.md)

Dominique Andreoli

This paper analyses Article 14 of Law No\. 132/2025 on the use of artificial intelligence in public administration, within the broader framework of algorithmic legality\. It examines the relationship between administrative automation, transparency, traceability, human oversight and responsibility, highlighting the main critical issues raised by opaque systems, automation bias, discretionary power and the effectiveness of safeguards\.

## [Disengagement and reintegration as psychosocial capacity\-building after violent extremism](../publications/8445b53add0c8c1cea22.md)

Deepti Ramaswamy

Efforts to address violent extremism increasingly acknowledge the relevance of mental health, yet psychological factors are still often treated as background vulnerabilities rather than as active processes shaping whether reintegration can be sustained over time\. This paper offers a conceptual, theory\-generating account of how therapeutic engagement supports the consolidation of disengagement and the conditions for sustainable reintegration\. All participants had already disengaged before starting therapy, so the paper is not an evaluation of a specific therapy’s effectiveness in supporting disengagement; instead, it traces the psychosocial mechanisms through which change unfolds over time\. Drawing on longitudinal narrative interviews with six individuals, the analysis traces changes in emotional regulation, identity, trust in others, and moral reasoning over time\. All six had disengaged, for a minimum of two years, from far\-right or Islamist extremist or extremist\-adjacent environments, or from the incel milieu\. They subsequently took part in trauma\-informed therapeutic work delivered individually and remotely over approximately nine to twelve months\. Participants described therapeutic engagement as supporting emotional safeness and regulation, and their accounts point to an accompanying capacity to revisit past involvement without collapse, integrate responsibility into more coherent self\-narratives, and move away from rigid, polarised ways of relating to others\. These psychosocial shifts shaped participants’ capacity to engage with everyday social, practical, and civic domains\. However, the durability of these changes depended on external conditions, such as stability, social recognition, and access to meaningful roles\. Where those conditions were absent, exclusion or precarity could undermine even real psychosocial gains\. The study reframes post\-exit reintegration as a relational and developmental process of psychosocial capacity\-building, in which therapeutic engagement is one enabling condition among others\.

## [Mapping natural sinkhole susceptibility in Italy: integrating a national inventory with machine learning](../publications/844fbdf23c56f34d47eb.md)

Livio Ruggiero; Giancarlo Ciotoli; Federico Mori; Sergio Madonna; Stefania Nisio

Natural sinkholes are a widespread geohazard in Italy, complicating landuse planning and risk reduction\. This study develops the first national\-scale susceptibility map for natural sinkholes using an updated inventory and data\-driven modelling\. Building on the ISPRA National Sinkhole Database, we assembled more than 14,000 documented features from literature, historical records, imagery and regional datasets\. Geological, geomorphological, structural, hydrogeological and geochemical factors were converted into gridded predictors and combined with the inventory through a machine\-learning regression framework estimating a continuous susceptibility score\. The calibrated model, evaluated on a held\-out 20% test subset, produces a susceptibility surface for the Italian territory\. Interpretation tools emphasize the importance of soluble rocks, fault\-controlled permeability, deep gas emissions and mineralized springs, consistent with previous studies\. High\-susceptibility zones align with major karst and evaporitic provinces, including the Friuli\-Veneto piedmont, northern Apulia, Latium travertine basins and central Sicilian evaporites, whereas western Alpine sectors and Sardinia show very low scores\. The map offers a coherent national overview of where natural sinkholes are more likely to occur and provides an operational basis for prioritizing surveys, monitoring programmes and planning measures, while the methodology can be refined to incorporate time\-dependent drivers and multi\-hazard interactions\. These advances support more resilient and sustainable territorial development\.

## [Dexterity from Supervised Play](../publications/84595fe0327358e93ff0.md)

Botao He; Yiming Dou; Yiannis Aloimonos; Jitendra Malik; Akash Sharma; Ruoshi Liu

How can robots autonomously collect the contact\-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model\. During inference, the same play policy then guides model\-predictive control \(MPC\) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model\. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed\-loop, goal\-conditioned policy through self\-play within the learned world model\. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any\-to\-any in\-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world\. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69\.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data\. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model\-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task\-specific demonstrations or sim\-to\-real transfer\.

## [A Machine Learning Model With Temporal Validation for Predicting Walking Ability in Nontraumatic Spinal Cord Injury](../publications/845a22bda3dba991e34c.md)

An\-Ni Tong; Jiekai Guo; Cai Xiaoe; Lifan Wang; Mengqi Chen; Yang Gao; Chen Shugeng; Shuai Tong; Wenting Wang

BACKGROUND: Walking ability is the priority for spinal cord injury \(SCI\) patients\. Nontraumatic SCI \(NTSCI\) is increasing with aging populations, yet its prognosis remains understudied\. Early predictionF using admission clinical indicators could facilitate decision\-making and rehabilitation planning\. OBJECTIVE: To preliminarily develop and validate a machine learning model using early admission clinical indicators for predicting post\-rehabilitation walking ability probability \(with a classification threshold of 0\.5\) in patients with NTSCI\. METHODS: This retrospective study included model development and temporal external validation\. We enrolled 148 NTSCI patients, randomly allocating them into training \(80%\) and internal test \(20%\) sets\. Four feature sets were constructed from objective clinical measures\. Nine algorithms were compared; Gradient Boosting Decision Tree \(GBDT\) was selected based on AUC, recall, and F2\-score, followed by hyperparameter tuning\. The final model was validated independently on a cohort of 37 NTSCI patients \(July 2025 to May 2026\)\. Ethical approval \(M202616\) and consent waiver obtained; retrospectively registered \(MR\-11\-26\-021748\); no patient involvement\. RESULTS: The GBDT\-based model outperformed all others\. On internal testing, it achieved an AUC of 0\.91 \(95% CI: 0\.77\-1\.00\), recall 0\.92 \(95% CI: 0\.71\-1\.00\), and accuracy 0\.90 \(95% CI: 0\.77\-1\.00\)\. Key predictors included total lower limb muscle strength, age, and others\. On temporal external validation, it showed encouraging performance with accuracy 0\.81 \(95% CI: 0\.68\-0\.92\) and recall 0\.70 \(95% CI: 0\.40\-1\.00\)\. CONCLUSION: This preliminary model may have potential for predicting walking ability in patients with NTSCI; however, these findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts before any clinical application can be considered\.

## [Machine learning for predicting clinical complete response after total neoadjuvant therapy in advanced rectal cancer](../publications/845e34907f8577902ecf.md)

Sergei Bedrikovetski; Ishraq Murshed; Tracy R\. Fitzsimmons; Michael Croft; Timothy Jay Price; Michael Penniment; S\. Selva‐Nayagam; Tarik Sammour

Abstract Background Predicting clinical complete response \(cCR\) to total neoadjuvant therapy \(TNT\) helps optimize therapeutic strategies and identify the best candidates for a watch\-and\-wait strategy\. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict cCR to TNT in a mixed curative\-intent cohort of patients with advanced rectal cancer, including selected oligometastatic cases treated with curative intent\. Methods A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database of consecutive rectal cancer patients treated with TNT with curative intent at three South Australian hospitals between 2019 and 2026 was performed \. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\) analysis was used for variable selection, and ten machine learning algorithms were employed to develop prediction models for cCR\. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver\-operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\)\. Results A total of 245 patients were identified, of whom 193 were assigned to the training set and 52 to the external validation set\. LASSO identified albumin, clinical T stage, tumour length, systemic immune\-inflammation index, extramural vascular invasion, platelet count, and body mass index as key predictors of cCR\. Among the ten models, the logistic regression model performed best in the training set, achieving an AUROC of 0\.817\. In external validation, the multilayer perceptron \(MLP\) model achieved the highest predictive performance with an AUROC of 0\.755\. Conclusion Machine learning models based on seven pretreatment variables show promise in accurately predicting cCR following TNT in patients with advanced rectal cancer\. On external validation, the MLP model demonstrated the strongest predictive performance with moderate discrimination\. However, further validation in larger, non\-metastatic/selected populations may be required before clinical implementation\.

## [Feeling or thinking? User aversion to AI customer service in online education](../publications/84628847e6f88a604063.md)

Yuan He; Lin Huang

Introduction AI customer service is increasingly integrated into online education, yet users may not always respond favorably to AI\-assisted service interactions\. Drawing on robotic role theory, this study examines how thinking and feeling AI customer service influence user aversion in online educational service encounters\. Methods Three experiments were conducted to examine the effect of AI customer service type on user aversion \(Study 1, N = 120\), the mediating role of perceived intelligence \(Study 2, N = 120\), and the moderating role of AI identity disclosure timing \(Study 3, N = 120\)\. Across the three between\-subjects experiments, thinking AI was operationalized through analytical, information\-processing, and task\-oriented communication, whereas feeling AI emphasized emotional recognition and relational support\. Results The results show that feeling AI generates greater user aversion than thinking AI\. Perceived intelligence mediated this effect, such that feeling AI is perceived as less intelligent, which in turn increases user aversion\. Further, AI identity disclosure timing moderates the indirect effect through perceived intelligence\. Early disclosure of AI identity attenuates the negative effect of feeling AI\. Discussion These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of different AI customer service types depends on the service context and highlight the importance of aligning AI communication with users’ task\-oriented service needs\.

## [Los Caminos del Futuro Tecnológico Entre el Desplazamiento Humano y la Convivencia Productiva con la Robótica y la IA](../publications/846792509560c653355d.md)

Yosmel Silva Llanes

Este documento analiza dos posibles caminos para el futuro tecnológico: uno donde las máquinas reemplazan al ser humano y generan estancamiento, y otro donde la tecnología potencia la productividad humana mediante trabajo remoto, simulación, manejo de robots y una economía abundante\. Se concluye que el futuro dependerá de las decisiones presentes y de cómo se diseñe la convivencia entre tecnología y humanidad\.

## [Stochastic Resonance and Library Space Design: Rethinking Silent Policy Through Cognitive Psychology](../publications/846838ec1dc569c4ce5e.md)

Stanislaus N\. Ezeonye; Susan Nnadozie Umeozor

This study explored the integration of cognitive psychology into library space design, specifically examining how stochastic resonance where background noise enhances cognitive performance can inform acoustic zoning policies in academic libraries\. Anchored in Ranganathan’s principles and the shifting demands of emotionally responsive users, the research critiqued the traditional silent library model\. The population included 5,201 users in Donald E\. U\. Ekong Library, University of Port Harcourt\. The sample size was determined using Kpolovie minimum sample size formula, and 400 respondents were determined and sampled using simple random sampling technique\. Using a mixed\-method approach involving surveys and interviews at the Donald E\. U\. Ekong Library, the study applied the Swedish Soundscape\-Quality Protocol to analyze user perceptions\. Findings revealed that structured background sounds, such as music and human activity, moderately increased cognitive focus, emotional engagement, and memory recall while reducing annoyance\. Thematic analysis underscored user diversity in sound preferences, challenging the uniform application of silence in libraries\. The study advocated multi\-zoned library spaces that accommodate both silence\-preferring users and stochastic resonants, thereby fostering inclusive learning environments\. Recommendations include the adoption of sound\-aware policies and architectural zoning to support cognitive diversity and enhance user experience in academic libraries\.

## [Deep Learning and Domain Expertise for Fabricating High\-Performance Biosensors](../publications/84711a8b1bc4eaff7cb2.md)

Meiling Xiao; Pengcheng Zhang; Zhijie Li; Nuo\-Qiao Lin; Xiaowo Wang; Jian\-Zhong Liu

Transcription factor\-based biosensors are essential for the scalable bioproduction of plant natural products\. However, a major bottleneck in developing high\-performance biosensors is the engineering of responsive promoters due to the vast sequence space and poorly understood sequence\-function relationships\. Here, we extend our previously published DeepSEED framework into an artificial intelligence\-driven pipeline for efficient and extensible biosensor\-responsive promoter optimization\. This strategy integrates deep learning with domain\-specific biological expertise\. By fixing core promoter elements, varying the number and position of transcription factor binding sites \(TFBSs\) to define promoter backbones, and subsequently optimizing the flanking sequences, we enable the de novo design of promoters\. We systematically apply this strategy to optimize a panel of biosensors across different transcription factors and regulatory modes, including four metabolite\-responsive biosensors and a quorum\-sensing\-based environmental sensor\. The resulting biosensors exhibit diverse dynamic behaviors with markedly improved sensitivity, expanded dynamic range, and increased maximum output\. For instance, the optimized naringenin biosensor demonstrates a 32\-fold broader dynamic range and a 27\-fold higher maximum output compared to its parent\. To illustrate its utility in metabolic engineering, we employed a DeepSEED\-designed promoter to dynamically regulate a p\-coumaric acid biosynthesis pathway, boosting production by 117\.0%\. Our work extends the previously published DeepSEED framework into a powerful pipeline for biosensor optimization and delivers a portfolio of high\-performance regulatory elements, addressing a critical need and facilitating the development of more intelligent and productive metabolic engineering systems\.

## [Cues for you: a comparative test of agenda cueing and attitudes toward algorithmic news in the US and the UK](../publications/847253fc39869dd8360c.md)

Elizabeth Stoycheff; Robert B Swetlic

Abstract Agenda cues, or news heuristics that signal issue importance, are an important determinant of the public’s issue priorities\. As these cues shift from editorial recommendations to personalized algorithms, we test the boundary conditions of the agenda cueing hypothesis\. We use a comparative online experiment to examine how two different regulatory environments in the US and the UK replicate established cueing effects and provide a formal test of their underlying causal mechanism\. Results from the US sample confirm that journalistic agenda cues are effective at cueing issue importance, but algorithmic cues are not\. Algorithmic cueing effects do not interact with respondents’ general attitudes toward AI nor their attitudes toward algorithmic news to influence their issue judgments but rather are contingent on one’s ideology and political interest\. Implications of journalistic and algorithmically derived agenda cues in different regulatory environments are discussed\.

## [Skin Longevity Medicine: A Hierarchical Framework for Personalized Skin Health and Aging Intervention](../publications/847725f265487b954ab5.md)

Liangsen Zhao; Yong Liao

The expanding framework of aging hallmarks and the emerging paradigm of precision geromedicine have created new opportunities for translating molecular geroscience into clinical skin health\.Skin longevitydefined as the sustained maintenance of tissue function, structural integrity, and biological resiliencerepresents a conceptual shift from appearance\-oriented anti\-aging toward evidence\-based, multimodal intervention\.This review examines the scientific basis of skin longevity, including the cutaneous manifestations of aging hallmarks, dermal fibroblast senescence, and extracellular matrix \(ECM\) degeneration, while identifying critical limitations in current fragmented intervention approaches\.We propose a hierarchical intervention pyramid comprising five pillars: systemic metabolic and nutritional optimization, lifestyle and psychoneurobiological regulation, epidermal barrier maintenance and local epigenetic modulation, ECM homeostasis and regenerative injectables, and energy\-based devices\.This framework emphasizes temporal sequencing, biological synergy, and individualized precision strategies rather than isolated treatment accumulation\.By integrating evidence from nutraceuticals, topical therapeutics, biostimulatory agents, and procedural interventions within a unified mechanistic hierarchy, this perspective aims to stimulate scholarly discourse and advance the development of personalized skin longevity medicine as a component of precision health\.

## [A Retrospective Benchmark of Quantitative Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction Tools](../publications/847c872f53a7960b6550.md)

Jianda Yue; Zhaoyang Tang; Xie Li; Jiawei Xu; Hua Tan; Qizhang Yang; Zhonghua Liu; Yue Wang

Antimicrobial peptides \(AMPs\) are critical candidates for addressing the global antibiotic resistance crisis\. AI\-driven quantitative models capable of directly predicting peptide antimicrobial activity, specifically minimum inhibitory concentration \(MIC\), are gaining scientific prominence by providing precise guidance for the rational design of AMPs\. To assess their real\-world, out\-of\-the\-box performance, we conducted a retrospective benchmark of 10 publicly released quantitative AMP prediction tools spanning classical machine learning and contemporary deep learning approaches\. Using an external dataset and reconstructed native datasets, we evaluated absolute MIC regression, retrospective reproducibility, directional prediction patterns, ranking capability, and virtual\-screening enrichment\. Most released tools exhibited poor absolute MIC regression and limited transferability to the external benchmark, while selected tools retained useful relative\-ranking and enrichment capabilities\. Retrospective evaluation further revealed marked differences in implementation\-level reproducibility among the released tools\. Error\-stratified analyses identified systematic associations between prediction errors and peptide residue composition, together with a general compression of the predicted activity range\. Collectively, these findings characterize the practical performance boundaries of currently accessible quantitative AMP prediction tools and support their use primarily as early\-stage screening filters rather than precise substitutes for experimental MIC measurements\.

## [Industrial Paradigm of Multidimensional Poverty in Karawang Regency \(Determinant Analysis and Policy Implementation\)](../publications/847ff85fc2c41ccd012a.md)

Tia Devianty; Pandji Santosa

Karawang Regency is known as one of the largest processing industry centers in West Java, with the sector&\#x27;s contribution of around 71 percent to GDP on a Constant Price Basis in 2024\. However, the dominance of the industrial economy has not been followed by an inclusive poverty reduction: the number of absolute poor people will increase by March 2024, the open unemployment rate remains above the West Java average, and the inequality of expenditure between the poor is widening\. Previous studies of the determinants of poverty have generally addressed economic, population, or environmental factors separately, and have rarely linked the structure of the industrial labor market to skills mismatches, gender inequality, and spatial vulnerability in a single industrial district\. This article aims to explain the paradox, identify the determinants of multidimensional poverty in Karawang, and formulate policy implications for more inclusive industrialization\. The research uses a descriptive\-analytical approach with policy case studies, sourced from secondary data from the Central Statistics Agency, Regsosek/Sepakat, and regional planning documents in the Final Report of the Karawang Regency Regional Poverty Alleviation Plan 2025\-2029\. The results of the analysis show that poverty in Karawang is formed from the interaction of economic determinants, employment, education, health, basic services, gender, population, and coastal\-rural vulnerabilities that are mutually reinforcing and cannot be overcome only through industrial growth\.

## [Multi\-objective Parametric Optimization of Chemical Mechanical Polishing for BK7 Optical Glass Using RSM\-NSWOA\-TOPSIS](../publications/848d7474cf98ae04e5be.md)

Xincheng Yin; Zikai Wang; Huijun Han; Youliang Wang; Yufei Chen; Yanjun Shen

Abstract This study investigates the effects of chemical mechanical polishing \(CMP\) process parameters on the surface quality, polishing efficiency, and material removal mechanism of BK7 optical glass\. The primary objectives are to optimize parameters to enhance polishing performance and to accurately predict surface roughness \(Ra\) and material removal rate \(MRR\)\. Preliminary single\-factor experiments were conducted to determine the appropriate parameter ranges for polishing time, polishing pad rotational speed, CeO2 concentration, and slurry pH\. Based on these ranges, a response surface methodology \(RSM\) model was established using the four process parameters as input variables\. With the objectives of minimizing Ra and maximizing MRR, multi\-objective optimization was performed using the Non\-dominated Sorting Whale Optimization Algorithm \(NSWOA\), and the optimal parameter combination was identified via the TOPSIS method\. The RSM models for Ra and MRR yielded R² values of 0\.9840 and 0\.9878, respectively, indicating good agreement with the experimental data used for model development\. The hybrid RSM\-NSWOA\-TOPSIS approach yielded the optimal parameters: polishing time of 51 min, polishing pad rotational speed of 59 r/min, CeO2 concentration of 0\.62 wt%, and slurry pH of 5\.6, with predicted values of Ra=2\.30 nm and MRR=1\.74 µm/min\. Experimental validation under these optimal conditions yielded a Ra of 2\.10 ± 0\.07 nm and an MRR of 1\.92 ± 0\.06 µm/min, with deviations between predicted and measured values within 10%\. XPS results revealed surface chemical changes during CMP, while nanoindentation measurements showed a lower mean indentation modulus after polishing and load\-dependent changes in hardness, suggesting that surface chemical interactions contributed to the mechanical removal process\. The proposed hybrid strategy RSM\-NSWOA\-TOPSIS effectively improves both polishing efficiency and surface quality for BK7 optical glass, providing guidance for balancing surface quality and material removal efficiency under the investigated conditions\.

## [A Randomized Open\-Labelled Controlled Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Jambavādi Kaṣāya in the Management of Asṛgdara with Special Reference to Menorrhagia](../publications/8493584077a858cb263d.md)

Komal R Gaikwad; Savita Patil

Background: Asṛgdara is a common gynecological disorder described in Ayurveda, characterized by excessive or prolonged menstrual bleeding and comparable to menorrhagia in contemporary medicine\. It can adversely affect women&\#x27;s physical, psychological, and social well\-being\. Ayurvedic management focuses on correcting the underlying Samprāpti through Pitta Śamana, Rakta Prasādana, Rakta Sthāpana, and Stambhana\. Jambavādi Kaṣāya, a classical formulation indicated in Raktapitta, possesses Stambhana, Rakta\-Prasādana, and Pitta\-Śamana properties and may therefore have therapeutic potential in Asṛgdara\. However, clinical evidence regarding its efficacy in Asṛgdara remains limited\. Aim: To clinically evaluate the efficacy of Jambavādi Kaṣāya in the management of Asṛgdara with special reference to menorrhagia\. Methods: A randomized, open\-label, controlled clinical study was conducted on 30 participants fulfilling the predefined diagnostic and inclusion criteria for Asṛgdara\. Participants were randomly allocated into two groups of 15 each\. Group A \(n = 15\) received Jambavādi Kaṣāya, while Group B \(n = 15\) received Pathyāmalakādi Kaṣāya\. Treatment was administered for 2 months, followed by a 1\-month follow\-up period\. The outcomes assessed included the amount and duration of menstrual bleeding, passage of clots, lower abdominal pain, bodyache, and fatigue, along with objective parameters such as the Pictorial Blood Assessment Chart \(PBAC\) score and hemoglobin level\. Appropriate parametric and non\-parametric statistical tests were used for within\-group and between\-group comparisons\. Results: Both groups demonstrated improvement in the clinical features and objective parameters of Asṛgdara following treatment\. Statistically significant improvement was observed in amount and duration of menstrual bleeding\. Hemoglobin levels, PBAC scores, menstrual bleeding characteristics, associated symptoms, and quality\-of\-life measures showed significant improvement\. No significant adverse effects were reported during the treatment and follow\-up period\. Discussion: Both Jambavādi Kaṣāya and Pathyāmalakādi Kaṣāya were associated with improvement in the clinical and objective parameters of Asṛgdara\. The observed therapeutic effects of Jambavādi Kaṣāya may be attributed to its Stambhana, Rakta\-Prasādana, Pitta\-Śamaka, and Garbhāśaya\-Saṅkocaka properties\. However, comparative efficacy should be interpreted based on the statistical significance of the between\-group differences\. Conclusion: Jambavādi Kaṣāya was associated with improvement in the clinical and objective parameters of Asṛgdara after 2 months of treatment\. Where between\-group differences were statistically non\-significant, the findings do not establish superiority of Jambavādi Kaṣāya over Pathyāmalakādi Kaṣāya\. The results suggest that Jambavādi Kaṣāya may be a useful therapeutic option in the management of Asṛgdara, subject to interpretation of the observed between\-group statistical differences\. Keywords: Asṛgdara, Menorrhagia, Jambavādi kaṣāya, Pathyāmalakādi kaṣāya

## [Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells](../publications/849cbeb8a9691332a70a.md)

Xiaotao Liu; Jiangshan Qu; Hao Tian; Zhanjun Zhu; Xin Wen Guo; Can Li

ABSTRACT Dion–Jacobson \(DJ\) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films\. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper \(RP\) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method\. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites\. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21\.1% \(19\.05% for 1 cm 2 devices\) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98\.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination \(ISOS‐L‐2 protocol\) and 98\.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%\.

## [Ultrasound cycloplasty: dynamic efficacy and long\-term safety in glaucoma patients from northwest China](../publications/84a27bcdc19aa1ae955a.md)

Ping Ge; Rui Shi; Qing\-Qing Mu; Rui\-Xue Zhang; Xiangxiang Yang; Yuan He

Purpose To comprehensively evaluate the dynamic efficacy of UCP in treating different types of glaucoma patients in Northwest China, systematically analyze treatment outcome variations across follow\-up time points, and assess long\-term safety profiles Methods In a 1\-year follow\-up study, 24 patients \(30 eyes\) with various types of glaucoma were enrolled and underwent UCP treatment \(10 sectors or 8 sectors\)\. Follow\-up visits were conducted at different postoperative time points \(1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year\)\. Follow\-up assessments consisted of IOP measurements, IOP reduction from baseline, surgical success rate, 24\-hour IOP fluctuation, pain score improvement, and complications\. Furthermore, the correlation between IOP at the final follow\-up and baseline IOP was evaluated\. Results 1\. The overall IOP in all patients significantly decreased after UCP compared to preoperative levels \( P &lt; 0\.01\)\. 2\. UCP demonstrated significant long\-term IOP\-lowering effects in patients with various types of glaucoma, with a 59\.91% reduction at 1 year postoperatively\. The efficacy was particularly notable in patients with primary angle\-closure glaucoma, achieving a surgical success rate of 96\.67% at 1 year\. 3\. Preoperative baseline IOP showed a positive correlation with IOP reduction at 1 year postoperatively \( r s = 0\.641, P &lt; 0\.01\), indicating that higher baseline IOP was associated with greater IOP reduction\. 4\. UCP significantly improved IOP fluctuation, with the mean 24\-hour IOP fluctuation decreasing from 10\.6 preoperatively to 5\.3 postoperatively \( P = 0\.001\)\. 5\. UCP exhibited acceptable safety, with significant reductions in pain scores \( P &lt; 0\.05\) and no severe complications such as hypotony or macular edema observed during follow\-up\. Conclusion 1\. In glaucoma patients in the Northwest population, UCP demonstrates significant long\-term and dynamic efficacy—the higher the baseline IOP, the more pronounced the IOP\-lowering effect, with outstanding performance in stabilizing IOP fluctuations\. 2\. UCP exhibits acceptable safety and controllable complications\. Postoperative IOP stabilizes by 3 months, allowing for gradual withdrawal of medications, making it a reliable treatment option for glaucoma\.

## [Collected: Trauma, Wonder, and the Birth of the Modern Museum Movement](../publications/84a46d3a820389819b93.md)

Cheryl Harned

This dissertation investigates the life and collecting practices of Joseph Allen Skinner \(1862–1946\), a Holyoke, Massachusetts silk manufacturer, philanthropist, and childhood survivor of the Mill River Flood disaster of 1874, and the museum he created in South Hadley, Massachusetts, which he bequeathed to Mount Holyoke College upon his death\. Drawing on material culture studies, the history of emotions, and scholarship in trauma and neuroscience, it argues that Skinner&\#x27;s lifelong collecting habits and eventual museum\-making were shaped by two intertwined emotional responses to catastrophic loss: trauma and wonder\. Chapter II, &quot;Trauma Collected,&quot; examines Skinner&\#x27;s accumulation of Mill River flood relics—illustrated newspapers, silk remnants, a six\-ton chunk of a broken dam—as material responses to disaster that persisted across seven decades\. Chapter III, &quot;Wonder Collected,&quot; traces his childhood rock collecting, fascination with optical devices, and engagement with World&\#x27;s Fair objects as expressions of wonder—trauma&\#x27;s twin—arguing that collecting wondrous objects became a primary strategy for processing loss\. Chapter IV, &quot;Birth of the Modern Museum Movement,&quot; chronicles Skinner&\#x27;s journey from nervous prostration in 1900 to his museum&\#x27;s opening in 1932, demonstrating how he rebuilt himself by rebuilding everything around him: churches, a mountain, a college, and finally a historic village assembled from the ruins of towns flooded to create the Quabbin Reservoir\. Ultimately this dissertation argues that the Joseph Allen Skinner Museum occupies a liminal space between the nineteenth\-century cabinet of curiosity and the modern professional institution, representing a moment when museums could still serve simultaneously as personal memory houses and public educational spaces, and that understanding this history enriches our broader understanding of how trauma and wonder shaped American collecting and museum\-making at the birth of the modern museum movement\.

## [FAOPs: Normal Forms and an Algebra for AI Agent Workflows](../publications/84a8597b7a07b782639d.md)

Ali Mohammadi Shanghooshabad

Organizations increasingly encode operational procedures as multi\-step agent skills, here called Agent Operating Procedures \(AOPs\), that must be traceable, auditable, reproducible, access\-controlled, and bounded in time and cost, requirements that regulated sectors make mandatory\. Yet AOPs are typically kept as coarse\-grained files, in which steps bundle actions, copied procedures drift apart, any step may reach any tool, and refactoring goes unchecked\. We present Functional Agent Operating Procedures \(FAOP\), a formal theory that brings database\-grade discipline to AI agent workflows\. FAOP recasts each workflow as a typed function over scoped state and subjects an entire library to four progressive normal forms: Decomposed \(FNF\-1\) splits a workflow into atomic steps, Typed \(FNF\-2\) makes its data flow explicit and type\-checked, Factored \(FNF\-3\) gives each shared procedure a single canonical definition so a change propagates instead of drifting, and Scoped \(FNF\-4\) confines every step to least\-privilege tool access\. Once normalized, every atomic step is a separate entity with a declared contract and can be type\-checked, scope\-confined, bounded, tested, traced, and audited on its own\. A FAOP algebra of provably sound equalities turns refactoring and parallelization into compiler rewrites; orthogonal extensions add verified termination \(\+V\), optimization \(\+O\), and time and cost bounds \(\+B\); and an architectural\-level classifier \(0\-3\) determines whether a workflow needs AI at all\. Together, these make integrity, isolation, typing, termination, cost, and optimization compile\-time concerns across the whole library, not runtime hopes\. We implement the theory in SkillBase, an AOP management system \(what PostgreSQL is to data, SkillBase is to AOPs\), together with a separate executor that enforces these guarantees at run time\. A worked financial workflow illustrates the approach end to end\.
