## [Usko särkyneissä maailmoissa : Uskonnon representaatiot viimeaikaisessa dystopiakirjallisuudessa](../publications/84b61366322ba5b1aff1.md)

Kaisa Kaukiainen

This study examines the representation of religion in recent North American dystopian literature\. It investigates how religious beliefs and practices are portrayed, what roles faith and spirituality play within dystopian narratives, how dystopian worlds shape religious expression, and how religion is mediated through the perspectives of characters\. By focusing on North American dystopian novels published over the past three decades, the study establishes a distinct framework within the broader field of research on religion and dystopian literature\. The study begins by outlining key genre theories and methodological approaches and by defining the concept of religion as it is used in the analysis\. American exceptionalism, civil religion, and the problem of theodicy provide an essential conceptual background for the discussion\. Religion is examined from two complementary perspectives\. First, the study analyses dystopian storyworlds, exploring whether and how religion is addressed, how religious elements are represented, and how they are transformed by dystopian conditions\. Religion may appear explicitly or emerge indirectly through allegorical structures\. Second, the study investigates religion as it is perceived and experienced by individual characters\. Because dystopian fiction frequently relies on personal viewpoints and first\-person narration, characters’ emotions, moral choices, and religious or spiritual attitudes become central to the representation of religion\. The analysis begins with Margaret Atwood’s MaddAddam trilogy \(2003–2013\), which provides a comprehensive depiction of dystopian religiosity\. The study then examines other works, including Octavia E\. Butler’s Parable novels, as well as popular young adult dystopias, such as Suzanne Collins’s The Hunger Games trilogy and Lois Lowry’s The Giver series, where belief systems often function at an allegorical level\. Additional novels are also considered to broaden the analytical scope\. The study demonstrates that American cultural and religious heritage forms an important background for many recent dystopian narratives, particularly given their attempts to confront evil and imagine sustainable futures\. Many of the texts analysed can be characterised as critical dystopias that combine bleak visions with elements of hope\. Resistance movements, a recurring feature of dystopian fiction, often resemble religious movements; this structural parallel shapes both world\-building and processes of meaning\-making\. A thematically related chapter also considers artificial intelligence as a contemporary phenomenon that challenges established conceptions of religion through its literary portrayal as an omniscient or quasi\-divine entity\. Across the works examined, religiosity emerges as a fluid and often ambiguous element\. Religion may occasionally appear as a dominant feature, but more frequently it remains indirect and open to interpretation\. Although many texts portray religion in indifferent or negative terms, depicting it as outdated, ineffective, or associated with authoritarianism and fanaticism, religion nevertheless permeates dystopian narratives through symbolic frameworks, imagery, and modes of thought\. The study concludes that religion in dystopian fiction frequently signifies the inadequacy of established systems in a radically altered world\. Traditional religious frameworks are often displaced by more fluid and individualised forms of belief that emphasise personal spirituality and meaning\-making\. Individual perspectives become key indicators of faith, particularly in young adult dystopias, which commonly focus on selfhood, resilience, and engagement with the inexplicable, a realm traditionally associated with religion\.

## [Effect of an Educational Intervention on Lower Limb Pain During the Hajj Mass Gathering: A Randomized Controlled Trial](../publications/84b880a1e3fd73e1ac1d.md)

Yasser Bouchouata; Latifa Tahiri; Salma Elboughabi; Safa Rakhami; Ayda Belmlih; Hajar Elgmiri; Saad Sihida; Nouhaila El\-Maimouni; Meryem Kardoudi; Moncef Ziani; Hammou Jaouad; Amina Chrif Alaoui; Mustapha Oufqir; Khadija Fajjary; Fatima Jassab; Rédouane Abouqal; Jihane Belayachi; Fatine Kronbi; Hanan Rkain; Mohammed Youbi; Samia Karkouri; Fadoua Allali

Introduction/objectives: Lower limb pain is common and disabling from age 50 onwards, yet prevention before predictable episodes of intense ambulatory load has never been tested\.We evaluated a pre\-departure therapeutic patient education program in pilgrims attending a mass gathering\.Method: A parallel\-group randomized controlled trial \(1:1\) was conducted in two Moroccan vaccination centers: 218 pilgrims aged 50\-75 years were enrolled in April 2025 and followed until late June 2025\.The intervention group received a therapeutic patient education program, comprising a one\-hour group education session plus an unsupervised home\-based adapted physical activity program and WhatsApp reminders; controls received none\.The primary outcome was lower limb pain on a visual analog scale \(0\-10\) 48 hours after the end of the peak activity period\.Analysis was by intention to treat, using linear mixed models, with blinded assessors and analyst\.Results: The primary outcome was available for 216 of 218 participants \(mean age: 62\.6 years; 147 \(67\.4%\) women\)\.At T2 \(48 hours after the end of the peak activity period\), lower limb pain was lower in the education group \(\-1\.75 points; 95% CI: \-2\.40 to \-1\.09; p&lt;0\.001\); a smaller difference was already present seven days before departure, and the difference persisted seven days after return\.The education group also had less limping \(24 \(22%\) versus 42 \(39\.3%\);p=0\.01\), less increased analgesic use \(33 \(30\.3%\) versus 48 \(44\.9%\); p=0\.027\), less foot pain \(11 \(10\.1%\) versus 24 \(22\.4%\);p=0\.01\), and better quality of life \(\+0\.059;p=0\.021\)\.Low back pain, healthcare use, and falls did not differ\.Conclusions: A pre\-departure therapeutic patient education program, evaluated as a whole, produced a statistically significant reduction in lower limb pain in adults aged 50\-75 years exposed to several days of intense walking\.The point estimate did not reach the 2\-point threshold set a priori, so a clinically important benefit can be neither confirmed nor excluded\.Predictable episodes of high ambulatory load may offer a practical window for resource\-light prevention, which requires confirmation against an active comparator\.

## [Association between uncertainty regarding malignant risk and anxiety in patients with pulmonary nodules: a serial mediation analysis of illness perception and rumination](../publications/84c0bbf493d0f12b9be5.md)

Shanshan Wu; Min Liu; Song Yi; Rui Wang; Zhiqiang Song; Feng Xie; Wei Chen; Hong Qu; 黄玉蓉

Objective This study examined the relationship between uncertainty regarding the risk of malignancy after pulmonary nodule detection and anxiety, and the serial indirect effects of illness perception and ruminative thinking\. Methods A total of 308 patients with pulmonary nodules who were admitted to our hospital between January 2023 and January 2026 were included in the study\. General information was collected, and participants were assessed using the MUIS, BBIPQ, RRS, and the Chinese version of the GAD\-7\. Correlation and serial indirect effect analyses were performed using SPSS 26\.0 and the PROCESS macro \(Model 6\)\. Bootstrap resampling with 5,000 samples was used to assess the stability of indirect effects\. Results Among the 308 patients with pulmonary nodules, the MUIS scores ranged from 24 to 86, with a mean of 56\.10 ± 12\.21\. The BIPQ scores ranged 3 to76, with a mean of 43\.26 ± 10\.67, the RRS scores ranged from 22 to 72, with a mean of 44\.66 ± 10\.60, and the GAD\-7 scores ranged from 1 to16, with a mean of 8\.84 ± 2\.62\. No significant differences in GAD\-7 scores were observed among patients with different demographic or disease characteristics \( P &gt;0\.05\)\. Pearson’s correlation analysis showed that MUIS scores were positively correlated with BIPQ, RRS and GAD\-7 scores \( r = 0\.687, 0\.577, and 0\.745, P &lt; 0\.05\)\. BIPQ score was positively correlated with RRS and GAD\-7 score \( r = 0\.577; 0\.601, P &lt; 0\.05\)\. RRS score was positively correlated with GAD\-7 score \( r = 0\.574, P &lt; 0\.05\)\. The MUIS had a significant direct effect on GAD\-7, accounting for 75\.63% of the total effect\. The indirect effect consists of three paths: ① MUIS → RRS → GAD\-7, with an indirect effect of 0\.014, accounting for 8\.75% of the total effect; ② MUIS → BIPQ → GAD\-7, with an indirect effect of 0\.016, accounting for 10\.00% of the total effect; and ③ MUIS → BIPQ → RRS → GAD\-7, with an indirect effect of 0\.009, accounting for 5\.62% of the total effect\. Conclusion After pulmonary nodule detection, uncertainty regarding the risk of malignancy is positively associated with anxiety, partly explained by the serial indirect effects of illness perception and ruminative thinking, consistent with the hypothesized model\.

## [Güncel Makro İktisat Araştırmaları](../publications/84c4f4ff133b36b78aec.md)



Küresel ekonomide derinleşen yapısal dönüşümler, makroekonomik istikrarın belirleyicilerinin ve iktisat politikalarının etkinliğinin yeniden değerlendirilmesini gerekli kılmaktadır\. Parasal ve finansal sistemlerdeki değişimler, jeopolitik belirsizlikler, dijitalleşme ve ekolojik kısıtlar, makroiktisadi analizin kapsamını genişletmektedir\. Bu kitap, söz konusu dinamikleri on bir bölümde kuramsal, ampirik ve bibliyometrik yaklaşımlarla inceleyerek çağdaş makroiktisat tartışmalarına çok boyutlu bir değerlendirme sunmaktadır\. Eserin parasal iktisat ekseninde, arz şoklarının enflasyon dinamikleri ve merkez bankalarının politika tercihleri üzerindeki yansımaları, merkez bankası bağımsızlığının enflasyonla ilişkisi ve doğal faiz oranının yapısal belirleyicileri ele alınmaktadır\. Türkiye ekonomisine ilişkin incelemeler, dolarizasyon, Kur Korumalı Mevduat ve ters para ikamesini parasal istikrar bağlamında değerlendirirken, bankacılık sektörünün kriz sonrası yeniden yapılandırılmasını finansal sağlamlık göstergeleri üzerinden tartışmaktadır\. Dijital merkez bankası paralarının parasal aktarım mekanizmasına ve finansal aracılık süreçlerine yönelik olası etkileri, para politikasının kurumsal ve teknolojik dönüşümünü tamamlayan bir inceleme alanı oluşturmaktadır\. Uluslararası makroiktisat kapsamında jeopolitik risklerin ve siyasi istikrarın döviz kuru dinamikleriyle ilişkisi, dijital dönüşüm ve büyümenin doğrudan yabancı yatırımlardaki rolü ile Türk Devletleri Teşkilatı çerçevesindeki ekonomik bütünleşme olanakları değerlendirilmektedir\. Temiz enerji–büyüme literatürünün bilimsel yapısı ve tematik yönelimleri ile ihracat çeşitliliği, beşerî sermaye ve çevresel kalite arasındaki ilişkiler ise büyümenin ekolojik sürdürülebilirliğine ilişkin tartışmaları derinleştirmektedir\. Farklı analiz düzeylerini ve yöntemsel yaklaşımları buluşturan kitap, makroekonomik sonuçların parasal, kurumsal, teknolojik ve çevresel belirleyicilerini ortak bir tartışma zemininde değerlendirmektedir\. Eser, akademisyenler, lisansüstü araştırmacılar ve politika analistleri için çağdaş makroekonomik sorunların incelenmesine ve yeni araştırma gündemlerinin geliştirilmesine katkı sunmayı amaçlamaktadır\.

## [Coaching for Wellbeing in Entrepreneurial Education](../publications/84c8cf60da8576212121.md)

Elona N\. Ndlovu\-Hlatshwayo; Patrick Ebong Ebewo; Tendai Makwara

Entrepreneurship education in emerging economies often emphasises venture creation and technical competencies, with comparatively less attention to the psychological, relational, physical, environmental, and economic conditions that may shape students&\#x27; entrepreneurial learning and well\-being\. This paper develops the Coaching for Well\-being \(C4W\) conceptual framework to integrate coaching\-informed pedagogy and student well\-being within entrepreneurship education\. The framework was developed through a conceptual synthesis of relevant literature, informed in part by findings from an earlier systematic review of entrepreneurial coaching, complementary scholarship on coaching, positive psychology, well\-being and entrepreneurship education, and the authors&\#x27; practice\-informed experience in African higher education\. C4W uses the nine dimensions of PERMA\+4, Positive Emotion, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, Accomplishment, Physical Health, Mindset, Environment, and Economic Security as its well\-being architecture, and conceptually maps these dimensions to entrepreneurship teaching and coaching\-informed activities\. These include reflection, peer coaching, goal setting, networking, business simulations, values clarification, ecosystem mapping, and financial\-resource activities\. The framework articulates the pedagogical rationale that links these activities to the PERMA\+4 dimensions and identifies the intended entrepreneurial learning outcomes\. C4W contributes a context\-sensitive framework that positions well\-being as integral to entrepreneurial learning rather than as a separate student\-support concern, with relevance to resource\-constrained higher education environments\. As a theoretically informed conceptual framework rather than an empirically validated intervention, its proposed relationships require testing and refinement across different institutional, cultural, and socioeconomic contexts\.

## [Urinary biomarkers in non\-muscle invasive bladder cancer: translating multiplex and genomic liquid biopsies into clinical practice](../publications/84caf7d5f6cb33df717f.md)

Yuanyuan Zhang; Colton Walker; Adham Bassen; Tracy Criswell; Navid Jabalameli; Michael Patrick Feloney; Liang Cheng; Anthony Atala; Soroush Rais‐Bahrami

Urinary biomarkers have long promised to reduce the cystoscopy burden in bladder cancer, but a persistent gap separates assay performance from clinical practice\. This review synthesizes the shift from protein\-based tests to multiplex, genomic, and extracellular\-vesicle liquid biopsies, including minimal residual disease detection and therapy selection, and sets out an implementation roadmap spanning pre\-analytical standardization, decision thresholds, and pragmatic trial design\.

## [Dhikr and Cognitive Neuroscience](../publications/84cdcfcc432717889dd9.md)

Wildanul Kholis Alhadi; Ikhwan Arfa&\#x27; Bimantoro; Winka Ghazi Nafi; Fariz Istiqlal Harahap; Afifah Anwari Mattali Ahmad

The increasing prevalence of anxiety and psychological distress in the post\-pandemic era has intensified interest in spiritual and religious sources of mental tranquility\. Although previous studies have discussed the psychological and spiritual benefits of dhikr, the relationship between the Qur’anic concept of tranquility and its cognitive\-neuroscientific mechanisms remains insufficiently explored through an integrated interdisciplinary framework\. This study examines the relationship between dhikr and ṭuma’nīnah in Q\.S\. Al\-Ra‘d \[13\]: 28 by integrating Qur’anic linguistic\-semantic analysis, spiritual exegesis, and cognitive neuroscience\. Using qualitative library research, the study analyzes the linguistic structure of the verse, examines interpretations of selected classical and modern mufassir, and reviews relevant findings from neuroscience and cognitive psychology\. The findings show that ṭuma’nīnah is presented as a dynamic and continuous process, linguistically reflected in the verbal structure of taṭma’innu\. Exegetically, dhikr involves not merely verbal repetition but the internalization of divine awareness within human consciousness\. From a cognitive\-neuroscientific perspective, repetitive religious and contemplative practices may support emotional regulation, reduce stress reactivity, and promote physiological relaxation\. The novelty of this study lies in proposing an integrative framework connecting the linguistic meaning of ṭuma’nīnah, Qur’anic interpretations of dhikr, and contemporary cognitive\-neuroscientific perspectives, contributing to an interdisciplinary understanding of Qur’anic spirituality in addressing contemporary psychological challenges\.

## [Machine Learning Identifies Community\-Level Factors Associated with Lung Cancer Incidence](../publications/84d02caad08f84f8031d.md)

Gianni Pucillo; Allison C\. Jue; Chandler G\. Law; Sandip Pravin Patel; Uduak Z\. George

BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer\-related death in the United States\. Individual\-level risk factors such as tobacco use are well characterized, but the community\-level environmental, social, and economic contributions to geographic variation in incidence remain incompletely understood\. METHODS: We conducted an ecological analysis of 542 Medical Service Study Areas \(MSSAs\) in California, linking age\-adjusted lung cancer incidence rates \(AAIR, 2015\-2019\) to 27 indicators of pollution, population characteristics, and adult smoking prevalence\. Machine learning and SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) distinguished high\- versus low\-incidence MSSAs; ordinary least squares \(OLS\) regression quantified covariate\-AAIR associations\. RESULTS: A Support Vector Machine \(radial basis function kernel\) trained on 15 autoencoder\-selected indicators discriminated best \(cross\-validation AUC = 0\.891\), outperforming a smoking\-only model \(AUC = 0\.685\)\. By SHAP, smoking, linguistic isolation, neighborhood SES, unemployment, and housing burden contributed most\. In OLS regression, neighborhood SES quintile \(standardized β = \-0\.57\) and Hispanic population proportion \(β = \-0\.51\) were the strongest predictors of lower AAIR; higher Black population proportion was associated with higher AAIR\. Subpopulation\-stratified models performed better for White\-specific \(AUC = 0\.926\) than Hispanic\-specific AAIR \(AUC = 0\.744\)\. CONCLUSIONS: Community\-level smoking, pollution, and population characteristics data improved the identification of regions with elevated lung cancer risk\. IMPACT: Community\-level indicators can identify areas of elevated lung cancer burden, including the many where registry rates are suppressed\. These associations are concurrent rather than etiologic, and no causal interpretation is intended\. Lower predictive performance in some subpopulations highlights data gaps that must be addressed for equitable cancer prevention\.

## [Measuring eccentric hamstring strength in senior athletes: reference values, age and sex associations, and limb asymmetry](../publications/84e02c82c4af0713a43d.md)

Lee J\. Hinkle; James D\. Mead; E\. A\. Merrill; Joshua K\. Sponbeck; Ronald L\. Hager; Aaron Wayne Johnson

Background Participation in Masters sport has increased; however, reference eccentric hamstring strength values are unavailable\. Instrumented Nordic hamstring exercise \(NHE\) testing is used in younger athletes, but reports for senior athletes are lacking\. Purpose Establish sex\-stratified reference values for senior athletes\. Secondary aims examined associations with age, sex, and inter\-limb asymmetry\. Methods This study included 203 senior athletes \(100 female\) and measured eccentric hamstring strength during testing\. Absolute peak force, relative peak force, and limb asymmetry were calculated\. Results Mean unilateral absolute peak force was 156 N in females and 242 N in males, corresponding to relative values of 2\.46 N /kg and 2\.99 N /kg, respectively\. Males demonstrated greater absolute peak force \(mean difference: 85\.6 95% CI 70\.2 to 100\.9; d = 1\.54, 95% CI 1\.22 to 1\.85\) and greater relative peak force \(mean difference: 0\.53 N /kg, 95% CI 0\.34 to 0\.73; d = 0\.76, 95% CI 0\.47 to 1\.04\)\. Increasing age was associated with lower absolute peak force \(−2\.10 N /year, 95% CI −3\.09 to −1\.11\) and lower relative peak force \(−0\.020 N /kg/year, 95% CI −0\.033 to −0\.008\)\. Mean asymmetry was 11\.6 ± 8\.8% \(75th percentile: 16\.1%\)\. Asymmetry was not significantly associated with age or sex\. Conclusions This study provides the first reference eccentric hamstring strength values for senior athletes\. Male athletes demonstrated greater absolute and relative strength than females, whereas increasing age was associated with lower strength despite high physical activity levels\. Common asymmetry thresholds may overclassify high\-functioning senior athletes as having concerning inter\-limb asymmetry, highlighting the need for population\-specific interpretation\.

## [The impact of frailty syndrome on illness acceptance and treatment adherence in older patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/84ef8f91d4278d8455ec.md)

Aleksandra Pytel; Izabella Uchmanowicz; Martyna Grech; Katarzyna Malewicz; Stanisław Karol Manulik; Robbert J\.J\. Gobbens

Abstract Rheumatoid arthritis \(RA\) in older adults frequently coexists with frailty syndrome, a condition associated with reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse outcomes\. However, limited evidence exists regarding the relationship between frailty, illness acceptance, and treatment adherence in this population\. This study evaluated associations between frailty syndrome, illness acceptance, and adherence to treatment in older adults with RA, and examined whether psychological distress statistically mediated these relationships\. In this single\-centre cross\-sectional study, 210 community\-dwelling patients with established RA aged ≥ 65 years \(mean age 71\.3 years; 53\.8% men\) were assessed using the Tilburg Frailty Indicator \(TFI; physical, psychological and social domains, with physical frailty covering mobility, balance, strength, fatigue, sensory function and weight loss\), Acceptance of Illness Scale \(AIS\), Adherence to Refills and Medications Scale \(ARMS\), GHQ\-30, and DAS28\-CRP\. Frailty \(TFI ≥ 5\) was present in 75\.2% of patients and was more frequent in women than men \(84\.5% vs\. 67\.3%; p = 0\.004\)\. Higher frailty correlated with lower illness acceptance \(ρ = \-0\.342; p &lt; 0\.001\), higher disease activity \(ρ = \+0\.304; p &lt; 0\.001\), and greater psychological distress \(ρ = \+0\.190; p = 0\.006\)\. Physical frailty showed the strongest correlation with DAS28\-CRP \(ρ = \+0\.500; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. In multivariable models, frailty \(B = \-0\.34 AIS points per TFI point; p = 0\.005\) and disease activity \(B = \-0\.29; p = 0\.025\) were independently associated with lower illness acceptance\. Non\-adherence was not correlated with frailty bivariately \(ρ = 0\.11; p = 0\.124\); after adjustment a small association of opposite sign emerged \(B = \-0\.24; p = 0\.012\), consistent with a suppression effect\. Non\-adherence was associated mainly with lower educational attainment \(B = \-2\.20 per educational level; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Psychological distress did not statistically mediate the frailty\-acceptance association\. In this cross\-sectional sample of older adults with RA, higher frailty and higher disease activity were independently associated with lower illness acceptance, and psychological distress did not account for this association\. Medication non\-adherence was associated primarily with lower educational attainment rather than with frailty\. Routine frailty assessment with the TFI, psychosocial and functional support scaled to the frailty profile, and adherence support adjusted to educational level may therefore be useful in this population\.

## [Design and development of a photochromic material based on spiropyran for Bisphenol A removal](../publications/84f037635d47431290ae.md)

Andreea Elena Maftei; Maria Ignat; Marius Dobromir; Mariana Neamțu

A photochromic material including spiropyran \(SP\) and multi\-walled carbon nanotubes \(MWCNTs\) was designed and evaluated as a catalyst for the removal of Bisphenol A \(BPA\) in aqueous solution\. All photodegradation processes followed pseudo\-first\-order kinetics, with calculated rate constants \(k\) ranging from 0\.0013 min − 1 in the absence of the catalyst to 0\.0251 min − 1 in the presence of 1\.00 g/L of the catalyst under simulated solar irradiation\. The recycling experiments showed a gradual decrease in photocatalytic performance over four consecutive reaction cycles, suggesting a slight loss of catalyst activity during repeated use\. XRD analysis showed that the overall crystalline structure of the catalyst remained essentially unchanged after four cycles compared with the fresh material\. The photochromic properties of spiropyrans make them highly efficient molecules that are capable of producing Reactive Oxygen Species \(ROS\)\. The Electron Spin Resonance \(ESR\) experiments pointed to the efficient formation of 1 O 2 by the studied catalyst in aqueous suspension\. The radical scavenging experiments indicated that both singlet oxygen \( 1 O₂\) and hydroxyl radicals \(•OH\) play an important role in the BPA degradation process\. In addition, the MCF\-7 cell viability tests showed that the aqueous samples became less cytotoxic after photocatalytic treatment\. Thus, it was demonstrated that the developed catalyst shows potential as a photocatalyst, particularly for the removal of micropollutants such as BPA from contaminated water\.

## [Mental health literacy moderates the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms among Chinese young adults: a population\-based cross\-sectional study](../publications/84f1acfcfa0f347a2686.md)

Xuhua Chen; Wenqing Rao; Duanhua Xiong; Jiawu Ji

Background Mental health literacy \(MHL\) plays an important role in the recognition, prevention, and management of mental disorders, but its current status among Chinese young adults and its potential moderating role in the association between anxiety and depression remain underexplored\. This study examined MHL among young adults in China, identified its influencing factors, and tested whether MHL moderates the relationship between anxiety and depressive symptoms\. Methods A cross\-sectional survey was conducted in Fujian Province, China, using multistage stratified cluster random sampling\. A total of 2,164 young adults aged 18–35 years were included in the analysis\. Measurement instruments comprised a study\-developed sociodemographic questionnaire, the National Mental Health Literacy Questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire\-9 \(PHQ\-9\), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale\-7 \(GAD\-7\)\. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with MHL, and Model 1 of the PROCESS macro for SPSS \(with 5,000 bootstrap resamples\) was used to test the moderating effect of MHL on the anxiety–depression association\. Results Only 22\.4% of young adults had MHL attainment\. Compared with participants without depressive or anxiety symptoms, those with such symptoms were less likely to have good MHL \(both p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were strongly comorbid and positively correlated, and MHL significantly moderated this association \(β = 2\.04, p = 0\.043\)\. At low anxiety levels, the risk of depression was lower in the good MHL group than in the poor MHL group; at high anxiety levels, however, the rate of depression was higher in the good MHL group, suggesting that individuals with good MHL may identify their psychological issues earlier, resulting in a higher detection rate of depression during screening\. Conclusion MHL among Chinese young adults remains low and is closely linked to depressive and anxiety symptoms\. For young adults with good MHL, early\-screening pathways should be established to translate symptom awareness into timely professional assessment and intervention\. For those without good MHL, public\-health efforts should focus on improving symptom recognition and correcting cognitive biases that lead to underestimation of mental health risks and delays in help\-seeking\. however, this explanation remains speculative and requires further validation through longitudinal studies\.

## [AI Tutors, Worksheets, and Task Design: Matching AI Tools to Learning Structure](../publications/8500c36447594611bbbd.md)

Brock Casselman@unlv\.edu

Artificial intelligence is increasingly used by students as a learning resource in STEM courses\. However, classroom observations and survey data suggest that unstructured AI use may correlate with reduced student achievement\. Two concerns are especially relevant: AI systems can produce incorrect responses in tasks requiring precise validation, and students may use AI in ways that reduce active engagement with course material\. This session presents two instructional approaches designed to address these limitations: structured AI\-generated worksheets and in\-chat AI tutors\. AI worksheets generate controlled sets of practice problems within instructor\-defined course constraints\. In\-chat tutors provide interactive practice through problem generation, Socratic questioning, and feedback\-driven guidance\. The usefulness of each approach depends on the structure of the learning task\. Drawing from iterative development and testing primarily in introductory chemistry, we examine four types of tasks: \(1\) conceptual and explanatory, \(2\) structured tasks with low ambiguity, \(3\) multi\-step quantitative tasks, and \(4\) highly deterministic symbolic or structural tasks\. Examples from chemical nomenclature, dimensional analysis, stoichiometry, Lewis structures, laboratory writing, and mathematical validation illustrate where different AI approaches worked reliably—and where they did not\. Participants will receive ready\-to\-use prompts for both AI worksheet systems and in\-chat tutors, along with implementation strategies and observed limitations\. The session concludes with a practical framework for selecting AI tools based on the structure of the learning task rather than disciplinary content alone\.

## [Beyond Downstream QA: Rethinking How We Evaluate Agent Memory](../publications/8516737de8bfc18fee4e.md)

Sebastian\-Antonio Toma; Jean de Kernier; Mike Ply; Oliviu Matei

Agent memory benchmarks evaluate whether an agent&\#x27;s responses reflect correct knowledge, measuring downstream question\-answering accuracy as a proxy for memory quality\. We show this evaluation paradigm is incomplete: it conflates memory correctness with retrieval and generation quality, producing both false positives where correct responses mask broken memory and false negatives where incorrect responses blame correct memory for retrieval failures\. We introduce FEB\-30, a benchmark of 30 fact\-evolution trajectories spanning 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels, constructed via paradigm inversion: documents are generated from known fact trajectories, yielding deterministic ground truth without human annotation\. Each trajectory defines how a fact should evolve across multi\-author artifacts \(documents, emails, conversations\), enabling direct inspection of the memory store after each ingestion step\. Applying FEB\-30 to a representative memory system, we demonstrate that intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation diverge by an average of 16 percentage points, with 44% of trajectories exceeding meaningful divergence thresholds\. Diagnostic decomposition reveals that the system correctly classifies memory operations \(create, update, reinforce, supersede\) only 20% of the time, a failure entirely invisible to extrinsic evaluation, and that failure modes differ systematically by category and difficulty\. We release the benchmark, document generation pipeline, and scoring framework to support reproducible evaluation of agent memory systems\.

## [CONSTRUCTING PROFESSIONAL IDENTITIES IN AI\-ENHANCED LANGUAGE CLASSROOM: A STUDY OF PAKISTANI ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS’ PERSPECTIVES AND PRACTICES](../publications/851a4c6da09afc361350.md)

Muhammad Atiq\-ur\-Rehman; Muhammad Sabboor Hussain

The main aim of the study is to investigate the construction of English Language Teachers’ \(ELTs\) professional identity in the Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) era in the Pakistani Punjab context\. The qualitative analysis is embedded in semi\-structured interviews\. Multilayered sampling techniques were used, and data were collected from ELTs working in public and private educational institutions and analyzed using the Grounded Theory Approach \(GTA\)\. Initially, purposive sampling was used to identify appropriate samples, and those samples referred additional samples until saturation was attained on the thirteenth sample\. The investigation was theoretically informed by Gee’s \(2000\) distinction between I\-identity and A\-identity\. Findings created five interrelated categories: Institutionally Framed Professionalism, Agentive Professional Self, Constrained Autonomy, Negotiation Professional Identity, and Hybrid Identity Construction\. Results highlight that examination\-driven systems, curricular mandates, and administrative checks and balances powerfully form ELTs’ identities\. They are sustained simultaneously by contemplative practice, adaptive strategies, and professional achievement\. Autonomy was developed as conditional rather than absolute, leading teachers to negotiate between organizational compliance and personal pedagogical obligation\. The study demonstrates that ELT identity in Punjab is dynamic, context\-sensitive, and permanently negotiated\. By integrating hierarchical and agentive dimensions of identity, this research contributes to a nuanced understanding of teacher professionalism within examination\- focused educational systems\.

## [LLM application in digital asset assessments: mixed methods research](../publications/852805df11b948095d63.md)

Yann Thorens; Martin Angerer; Pejman Ebrahimi; Johannes Schneider

Abstract Digital asset markets are expanding but remain difficult to evaluate, particularly for retail investors who face information overload, unstructured disclosures, and limited regulatory safeguards\. Traditional due diligence methods often fail to capture the complexity of blockchain\-based projects, exposing investors to misrepresentation and fraud\. At the same time, LLMs have shown remarkable results on analyzing large information quantities\. Thus, this paper investigates whether large language models \(LLMs\) can enhance digital asset assessments by providing inspectable, automated, and low\-cost decision support\. Using a Design Science Research methodology, we developed a framework and a prototype tool to apply LLM\-based evaluation to token\-offering whitepapers, evaluated across 1,139 generated runs covering 29 token offerings\. We compared different content processing approaches, from raw document analysis to aspect\-focused summarization, and tested prompting strategies including Zero\-Shot, Few\-Shot, and Chain\-of\-Thought reasoning\. Our findings show a nuanced pattern\. On aggregate quantitative metrics, structured summarization combined with Chain\-of\-Thought prompting achieves the lowest rating error, although differences in rank correlation between configurations are not statistically resolvable given the number of projects evaluated; aspect\-focused summarization structures criterion\-specific evidence and candidate red flags explicitly, but its rating error is higher and the interpretability of this representation was not independently evaluated\. To address the single\-model limitation, we added a lightweight multi\-model robustness check using two small open\-source models on a matched subset of cases; the results suggest that the observed optimism bias is not specific to the original closed LLM, although performance still varies across model configurations\. Overall agreement between model and expert ratings remains limited, which suggests that LLMs are better understood as decision\-support tools for screening and explanation than as substitutes for expert judgment\. The study therefore contributes a design\-oriented due diligence artifact and a dependence\-aware evaluation of how summarization and prompting choices affect calibration, output\-level inspectability, and validity boundaries in digital asset assessment\.

## [Magnetized joystick with dual\-anisotropy for high\-capacity wearable human\-machine interactions](../publications/852aa0723fb7717916e8.md)

Yuanzhe Liang; Ming Lei; Biao Qi; Yingyi Zhang; Ziyi Dai; Dan Fang; Jinbo Wu; Jianyi Luo; Bingpu Zhou

One of the urgent demands for flexible and wearable sensors is to achieve single\-channel, less\-sensor, and multi\-output for effective communications\. However, expansion of signal capacity on a single interface often requires sensor arrays, which significantly increases the complexity in electrode layout and multiple device design\. In this work, we developed a flexible magnetized joystick \(FMJ\) with structurally induced eigenfrequency anisotropy by applying laser cutting process to a raw magnetized cubic\. Using an eigenfrequency\-polarity dual\-anisotropy addressing method, we show that single FMJ can achieve four identifiable outputs based on the direction of in\-plane mechanical inputs\. According to the cantilever beam model, the eigenfrequency library can be expanded by adjusting cutting parameters, dimensions, and material properties, laying the foundation for further expanding signal capacity through the combination of multiple FMJs\. The advantages of FMJs in terms of high capacity and multi\-functionality are demonstrated through a range of human\-machine interaction \(HMI\) applications, including game control, PowerPoint slides, robot car control, and a fingertip calculator\. The increased signal requirement would not impose the complexity of electrical connection thanks to the interference\-free parallel design of the electrodes\. We expect that the development strategy will provide valuable insights for further advancement of high\-capacity wearable HMI\.

## [Probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus provides an adjuvant effect to an orally administered chitosan nanoparticle\-based Salmonella subunit vaccine in broilers against Salmonella Enteritidis infection](../publications/85311189f063a35ecccc.md)

Sara Dolatyabi; Shreeya Sharma; Comfort Olaitan Shekoni; Raksha Suresh; Sudhir Yadav; Jennifer Schrock; Ronna Wood; Gowtham Avverahalli Shivalingaiah; Alok Dhakal; Megan Tenney; Tonima Rahman; James Sanko; Ramon Zegpi Lagos; Khaled Abdelaziz; Gourapura J\. Renukaradhya

Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis \(SE\) is a prominent zoonotic pathogen that contaminates poultry meat and eggs, leading to widespread foodborne illness in humans\. Despite better biosecurity measures and available commercial vaccines, SE foodborne illness from broiler meat remains a challenge, necessitating a novel vaccination strategy\. This study investigated the adjuvant efficacy of probiotic Lactobacillus acidophilus to a mannose\-conjugated chitosan nanoparticle\-based Salmonella subunit nanovaccine encapsulated with outer membrane proteins \(OMP\) and flagella antigens \(FLA\) of SE\. Broiler chicks \( n = 17–22 birds/group across six treatment groups\) were administered the probiotic in ovo \(embryonic day 18\) and post\-hatch \(days 2, 4, and 6\), and oral vaccination was performed at days 3 and 21 and challenged with SE at day 35\. The physical nature of the nanovaccine includes zeta potential \(34\.62 ± 1\.34 mV\), particle size \(286\.5 ± 6\.87 nm\), and polydispersity index \(0\.45 ± 0\.04\), ensuring stability and suitability for mucosal delivery\. Our results demonstrated that the probiotic\-nanovaccine combination synergistically elicited specific immune responses associated with a 1\.2 log 10 reduction in cecal SE colonization at day post challenge 4 compared with a commercial live\-attenuated vaccine\. Immunological analysis revealed an elevated frequency of activated B\-cells, increased specific secretory IgA in the intestines and bile\. Cytokine profiling in the cecal tonsils showed upregulation of Th1/Th17\-associated cytokines \(IFN\-γ/IL\-17\) gene expression and transition to regulatory cytokine IL\-10, indicative of a balanced immune response\. Furthermore, 16S rRNA sequencing of cecal contents showed that the probiotic\-nanovaccine did not alter overall microbiota diversity but significantly shifted microbial community composition \( R 2 = 0\.378, p = 0\.001\)\. Probiotic\-supplemented groups were enriched with short\-chain fatty acid producing Clostridiales , including Blautia, Butyricicoccus , and Christensenellaceae R\-7 group , whereas the commercial vaccine group exhibited higher abundance of Escherichia/Shigella and reduced Lactobacillus \. These findings underscore the potent adjuvant effect of L\. acidophilus in enhancing the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an oral Salmonella nanovaccine, while favorably modulating the gut microbiome\. This integrated probiotic\-nanovaccine approach represents a promising, antibiotic\-free paradigm for mitigating salmonellosis in poultry, with implications for reducing zoonotic transmission, incidence of foodborne illness, and antimicrobial resistance\.

## [Adolescent Stress Level Classification Using Ensemble Machine Learning and LSTM Models](../publications/8533ea70d7c9c0ed7b89.md)



As stress\-related disorders grow increasingly common, we need effective therapies that can be widely utilized to detect and manage them early\.This research shows how to use machine learning \(ML\) and natural language processing \(NLP\) to find and sort people&\#x27;s stress levels\.We gathered textual data that showed emotional and mental states and used typical NLP methods to clean it up\.This included tokenization, removing stop words, and TF\-IDF vectorization\.We used many machine learning models, such as Multinomial Naive Bayes \(MNB\), k\-Nearest Neighbors \(KNN\), and Logistic Regression \(LR\), to sort the stress levels into low, medium, and high\.We also trained a Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) model to fmd patterns in the data that happen in a certain order and have certain significance\.We used accuracy, precision, recall, and F1\-score to see how well each model worked\.The results show that it is possible to use machine learning and textual signals to locate tension without having to touch the person\.This might be useful for keeping an eye on mental health in schools and in corporate wellness initiatives\.The research shows that using NLP with both shallow and deep learning models is a good way to understand how people feel\.

## [Magnetocardiographic characteristics in patients with varying severity of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome](../publications/853905fcc98402dc9e9a.md)

Liang Liu; Zhen\-Fa Zhou; Yu\-Jie Zhang; Yu\-Pu Liu; Yue\-Li Zhang; Jian Ma; Chengxing Shen

Background Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome \(OSAS\) is an established risk factor for cardiovascular disease\. Magnetocardiography \(MCG\) is an emerging non\-invasive electrophysiological technique with potential value in cardiovascular assessment; however, its utility in evaluating OSAS severity remains unclear\. This study aimed to characterize MCG features across different severities of OSAS and to evaluate their predictive performance for moderate\-to\-severe disease\. Methods This retrospective study enrolled OSAS patients between June 2023 and October 2024, all of whom underwent MCG examination\. Patients were stratified by OSAS severity, and MCG parameters were compared between the normal\-to\-mild and moderate\-to\-severe groups\. Baseline data, complete blood count, serum biochemical indicators, and MCG parameters were collected along with relevant clinical and laboratory data\. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of moderate\-to\-severe OSAS, and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curves were constructed to evaluate the predictive performance of each parameter and the combined model\. Results Group comparisons revealed significant differences in traditional OSAS severity risk factors \(sex, body mass index, etc\.\)\. Diastolic function indicators, including E/A ratio and left atrial size, also showed marked differences between groups, with the moderate\-to\-severe subgroup exhibiting larger left atria and a higher proportion of E/A ratio values below 1\. Univariate analysis identified 35 MCG parameters that differed between groups, while multivariate regression retained four independent predictors \(htrt, tmdf, RS\-didma, and qr\_rela\_dist\_neg\_mode\)\. ROC analysis indicated that T\-wave\- and QRS\-wave\-related indices had moderate predictive value; a combined model incorporating htrt, tmdf, and RS\-didma showed superior area under the curve compared to any single parameter\. Conclusion MCG parameters demonstrate distinct characteristics across OSAS severity levels and yield favorable predictive performance for moderate\-to\-severe OSAS, positioning MCG as a promising non\-invasive tool for early diagnosis\. The observed changes in diastolic function markers may suggest underlying coronary microcirculatory alterations in patients with moderate\-to\-severe OSAS\. Rigorously designed prospective studies are warranted to validate MCG as a standardized diagnostic modality for OSAS\-related coronary microcirculation disorder\.

## [Prediction of CO2 Solubility in Deep Eutectic Solvents Using Machine Learning with Compact σ\-Profile\-Derived Descriptors](../publications/85452073f57397d018a4.md)

Ying\-Jung Chen; Tzu\-Hsuan Fu; Chieh‐Ming Hsieh

Abstract Deep eutectic solvents \(DESs\) are promising for CO2 capture, yet rapid screening remains challenging because of their chemical diversity\. This study develops an interpretable machine learning framework integrating experimental conditions with compact molecular descriptors derived from COSMO solvation calculations and the resulting σ\-profiles\. A data set of 2,398 CO2 solubility measurements across 114 unique DESs was used to develop tree\-based machine learning models\. XGBoost achieved the highest testing accuracy \(R2 = 0\.990, RMSE = 0\.070, MAE = 0\.043, AARD = 10\.05%\) using only nine input features\. Benchmark comparisons showed performance comparable to or better than models using full σ\-profiles or larger feature sets\. SHAP analysis identified pressure as the dominant predictor and highlighted contributions from molecular geometry and hydrogen\-bonding\-related descriptors\. The proposed framework therefore provides an accurate, efficient, and interpretable approach for screening DESs within chemically related design spaces and supports future data\-driven solvent design\.

## [Mitochondrial metabolic remodeling and blood–brain barrier dysfunction after repetitive mild traumatic brain injury](../publications/854a17095463ae68c2d8.md)

Lingjuan Gao; Xincheng Xue; Xianhui Deng; Yu Xu; Heng Gao

Repetitive mild traumatic brain injury \(rmTBI\) may arise when concussive or subconcussive impacts recur before physiological recovery is complete\. Mitochondrial dysfunction and blood–brain barrier \(BBB\) impairment are shared features across the traumatic brain injury \(TBI\) spectrum; in rmTBI, repetition may alter their magnitude, duration, and temporal coupling\. This focused narrative review evaluates evidence that mitochondrial metabolic remodeling contributes to neurovascular\-unit dysfunction after rmTBI\. We discuss energy failure, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, succinate, fumarate, alpha\-ketoglutarate, NAD \+ depletion, and lactate as candidate links between metabolic stress and BBB injury\. Direct rmTBI evidence is prioritized, while single\-TBI studies are used as mechanistic context when rmTBI data are limited\. Available studies support a model in which recurrent metabolic stress, redox imbalance, inflammatory signaling, and impaired mitochondrial quality control converge on endothelial and multicellular neurovascular\-unit dysfunction\. Metabolism\-directed interventions are promising but require validation across rigorously defined rmTBI paradigms and clinical cohorts\.

## [La Reinvención del Aprendizaje: Claves del Conectivismo para la Educación Digital](../publications/854ca81545eb78c4aa39.md)

Miguel González Díaz

En las instituciones educativas actuales persiste una confusión conceptual\. Se asume que el manejo de dispositivos tecnológicos equivale al aprendizaje mediado por su uso\. Esta premisa alimenta un enfoque instrumental que convierte la innovación en una continuidad de prácticas educativas similares a las de la década de los noventa, pero con dispositivos digitales\. El artículo examina el conectivismo, teoría propuesta por George Siemens \(2005\) y Stephen Downes \(2019\), para extraer ideas que permitan repensar la educación digital\. Se revisaron 34 textos \(fundacionales, teóricos y debates recientes\) mediante un análisis temático abierto\. Emergieron tres claves: aprender es enlazar redes más que acumular datos; el conocimiento se vuelve provisional y obliga a actualizarse sin cesar; el docente se concibe como un tutor más que como un dueño del saber\. Estas claves desplazan la mirada de la herramienta hacia las conexiones, cuestionan la estabilidad del conocimiento y transforman la práctica docente\. También se discuten objeciones conocidas al conectivismo–¿es realmente una teoría nueva? ¿ignora las desigualdades de acceso?– y se sugieren salidas para la práctica cotidiana\. Como señala Zapata\-Ros \(2015\), el conectivismo requiere una revisión crítica de sus fundamentos para consolidarse como modelo teórico en entornos conectados\. Sin ser una fórmula definitiva, el conectivismo ofrece pistas valiosas para reinventar el aprendizaje, siempre que se aplique con precaución y sin perder de vista los contextos reales\.

## [Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures](../publications/8552abe1c7d0ab08d61d.md)

Yasin Onuralp Özkılıç; Osman Ahmed Umiye; Thamer Salman Alomayri; Fatih Yılmaz; Sadık Alper Yildizel; Ali İhsan Çeli̇k

This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder \(WGP\) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine\-learning\-based framework for mixture design optimization\. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C\. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP\-temperature space, a physics\-aware data augmentation method and a multi\-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture\-wise three\-fold cross\-validation, parity plots, Y\-randomization tests, SHAP\-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap\-based uncertainty quantification\. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA\-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room\-temperature strength, high\-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency\. Both prospective within\-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses\. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade\-off between initial strength and thermal resilience\. The results demonstrate the two\-fold role of WGP as a micro\-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures\. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML\-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP\-modified concrete for fire\-exposed or high\-temperature applications\. SEM analyses of the glass powder\-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O \(51\.49%\), Ca \(20\.78%\), and Si \(8\.17%\); FT\-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the \~ 3400 and \~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the \~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature\. TGA results indicated that room\-temperature\-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre\-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization\.

## [Mixed lignocellulosic biomass for continuous bioethanol production: logistics, process integration and biodesign](../publications/8554aa979f06584bf522.md)

Akshay Kumar; Bipasha Choudhury; Arun Goyal

The increasing demand for renewable energy and the urgent need to mitigate climate change have driven global interest in bioethanol as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels\. However, reliance on edible feedstocks such as corn, sugarcane or wheat has proven unsustainable due to food\-fuel competition\. In contrast, second\-generation bioethanol production that utilizes lignocellulosic biomass primarily depends on a single biomass, limiting the continuous production because of seasonal variability and high production costs\. Mixed lignocellulosic biomass \(MLB\) utilization has emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by integrating diverse agricultural residues, forestry waste, energy crops and industrial by\-products within biorefineries\. MLB provides supply stability, enhances enzymatic saccharification and minimizes inhibitor formation through synergistic buffering and compositional complementarity\. This review comprehensively evaluates the significance of feedstock diversity, pretreatment strategies, enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation approaches in MLB\-based bioethanol production\. It further examines process integration strategies, such as simultaneous saccharification and fermentation, consolidated bioprocessing and hybrid reactor systems for year\-round operations\. Techno\-economic assessments demonstrate that MLB reduces the production costs, while life\-cycle analyses confirm significant greenhouse gas mitigation potential\. Despite these advantages, this study describes challenges in feedstock logistics, inhibitor management, strain robustness and process stability\. Moreover, it outlines future directions that emphasize the roles of artificial intelligence and machine learning in feedstock blending, synthetic biology for robust microbial consortia and supportive policy frameworks to promote biomass aggregation\. Overall, MLB represents a scalable and sustainable pathway for continuous second\-generation bioethanol production, offering environmental, economic and technological advantages over single\-feed approaches\.

## [Reconnections: Art, Education, and Inclusive Futures](../publications/857f0d20d3f862fedb5c.md)

Adrienne Boulton

researches et enjeux en éducation artistique, our Editorial Board collaborated on a publication call to invite arts education researchers to reflect on art education&\#x27;s priorities, purposes, and possibilities for the present and the future and the response was overwhelming\.In this issue, we hear from 26 authors in 10 articles and Salon Section visual essay to examine how arts education holds a unique space to call people in to cultivate inclusive, creative, and critical spaces for dialogue, reflection, and action \(CRAE Call for Submissions: Special Issue 2025\)\.LeBlanc, Reid, Weibe, Moalem, &amp; Qian approaches this call through a profound discussion of an artists&\#x27; residency program which activated anti\-racist and anti\-oppressive modes of engagement for students and gallery attendees\.Drawing on contemporary art practices, this work explores play\-, will\-, and care\-infused practices for their potential to stimulate empathetic responses as sites for transformative learning\.Trabelsi &amp; Moldoveanu&\#x27;s work examined the arts for its potential to cultivate inclusive, creative teaching practices in the visual arts to foster the well\-being of students with special educational needs\.Drawing on educational and public programs that were developed for Place Where the Waters Crossed, a solo exhibition by Diné artist Raven Chacon, Krishnan &amp; Dumoulin\-Bush problematize the framing of reconciliation and introduce the concept of conciliation to establish a framework for the non\-colonial museum programs\.The authors contend that conciliation must become a continuous institutional practice, not a temporary project, and that meaningful collaboration is where that work begins\.Beaudry, Brehm, Hammoun, Carignan, &amp; Sénéchal found that, in a study of 80 grade 11 high school students, a slam poetry program made poetry and writing feel more accessible, engaging, and relevant, particularly for students who were less interested in school\-based cultural activities\.Through creative workshops and performance, students gained confidence, participated more actively, and developed stronger connections with their classmates, themselves, and the arts\.The findings suggest that school\-based arts programs can create meaningful opportunities for student expression and inclusion, while also underscoring the importance of supportive artists, flexible participation, and continued funding for such initiatives\.Author and featured artist Lo&\#x27;s Silk Cocoon examines the uses of silk and collaborative art\-making to recover fragmented family histories while exploring the complexities of Chinese\-Canadian identity and belonging\.Drawing on the history and symbolism of silk, Lo transforms a lost legacy of craftsmanship into a contemporary meditation on migration, cultural hybridity, memory, and the possibility of reimagining inherited narratives\.The project ultimately argues that art education can use material engagement as a powerful form of knowledge\-making, connecting personal histories to broader cultural histories while creating space for empathy and more hopeful futures\.

## [Visual effects of urban environment art design based on composite Cycle Generative Adversarial Network](../publications/858ebf811758cbf6bb92.md)

Changning Wang; Na Li; Jiyu Wang

In recent years, many regions have invested significant efforts in the in\-depth study of artistic visual effects in urban environments to enhance the aesthetic appeal of urban districts\. However, traditional visual optimization models are unable to refine image edges and textures, leading to distorted results\. To optimize the artistic effects of urban district images, this study proposes a Cycle Generative Adversarial Network that incorporates a multi\-head self\-attention mechanism to enhance design\. The network architecture is modified by adding multi\-head self\-attention modules\. Spectral normalization is also introduced to improve the optimization process of both the generator and the discriminator\. Finally, the images generated at different layers are concatenated, and the average of the extracted features is used as the output\. The study compares the proposed network with publicly available datasets and commonly used optimization networks\. The generated images achieve a pixel accuracy of 96\.8% and a classification accuracy of 97\.4%\. In validation tests with a self\-built dataset, the Peak Signal\-to\-Noise Ratio reaches 34\.2 dB, outperforming the comparison models\. In a comprehensive evaluation across various metrics, the Structural Similarity Index is 98\.23% and the Visual Semantic Similarity is 96\.78%\. These results demonstrate that the proposed model analyzes images in various artistic styles and optimizes the visual effects of urban environments\. It is beneficial for creating urban districts with distinctive artistic styles, enhancing the local cultural atmosphere, and attracting more domestic and international tourists\.

## [Ashrafian, Hutan: Artificial Intelligence and Robot Responsibilities: Innovating Beyond Rights](../publications/858f8f64467667c60dff.md)



\_Science and Engineering Ethics\_ 21 \(2\):317\-326\. 2015The enduring innovations in artificial intelligence and robotics offer the promised capacity of computer consciousness, sentience and rationality\. The development of these advanced technologies have been considered to merit rights, however these can only be ascribed in the context of commensurate responsibilities and duties\. This represents the discernable next\-step for evolution in this field\. Addressing these needs requires attention to the philosophical perspectives of moral responsibility for artificial intelligence and robotics\. A contrast to the moral status of animals may be considered\. At a practical level, the attainment of responsibilities by artificial intelligence and robots can benefit from the established responsibilities and duties of human society, as their subsistence exists within this domain\. These responsibilities can be further interpreted and crystalized through legal principles, many of which have been conserved from ancient Roman law\. The ultimate and unified goal of stipulating these responsibilities resides through the advancement of mankind and the enduring preservation of the core tenets of humanity\. \(direct link \)

## [SQL Optimization in e\-Commerce Platforms Using Large Language Models: A Multi\-Pattern Query Empirical Study](../publications/8595b2e01bd95d00badb.md)

N\. D\. Salih; Min\-Ming Lee

The rapid expansion in e\-Commerce domains has presented an unprecedented challenge to database systems that support the execution of complex analytic queries on multi\-billion transaction data stream while keeping queries’ response latency under one second\. It is commonly observed that Large Language Models \(LLMs\) are very good at processing natural language queries, rather than struggling with syntax or semantics\. This feature is instrumental to various tasks like analytics acceleration, transaction speed\-up and handling large workloads across different domains\. In this paper, a detailed examination of how LLMs can be employed as intelligent assistants for Structure Query Language \(SQL\) query optimization throughout eight different types of query patterns is performed \(with two test cases each, resulting in 16 test cases\)\. An in\-depth experimental study is carried out among three main database systems \(PostgreSQL 16, MariaDB ColumnStore, and SQLite\) with relevant real\-world e\-Commerce datasets such as Brazilian e\-Commerce Public Dataset and Synthetic e\-Commerce Relational Dataset ranging from 10 million to 1 billion records\. Our methodology of sixteen test\-cases includes temporal aggregations, multi\-dimensional grouping, ranking queries, window functions, complex joins, full\-text search, recursive queries and geospatial analysis\. Results demonstrate that implementing the LLM&\#x27;s recommended query, indexing, and schema\-level changes yielded performance improvements ranging from 43% to 94% across test cases, whereby temporal aggregations yield 89% average improvement while multi\-dimensional grouping nets 86% improvement on the whole system\.

## [Hedayet, Hridi &amp; Haseen, Fariha: Artificial Intelligence in Public Health: A Review Article](../publications/85ad11c622f67c0e9b73.md)



\_Bangladesh Journal of Bioethics\_ 15 \(2\):15\-19\. 2024Background: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, such as learning, reasoning, and problem\-solving\. AI has the potential to transform the field of public health, which is concerned with promoting and protecting the health of populations and preventing diseases\. AI can help public health organizations perform their essential functions more efficiently, effectively, and equitably; AI can transform the public health field, but it also poses some challenges and risks that must be addressed carefully and responsibly\. Objectives: This paper reviews the current and potential applications of AI in public health, discusses the opportunities and challenges of AI for public health, and provides recommendations for the ethical and responsible use of AI in public health\. Results: AI can improve the speed and accuracy of diagnosis, screening, and treatment of various diseases and support disease surveillance, outbreak response, and health systems management\. However, AI poses significant challenges and risks, such as ethical, legal, and social implications, data quality and security, algorithmic bias and fairness, and environmental impact\. Conclusion: AI has the potential to revolutionize public health, but it comes with risks that must be addressed\. Promoting digital literacy, establishing modern data governance frameworks, and investing in advanced data infrastructure and procedures are essential\. Public health organizations must also train their workforce to collaborate with AI\. By doing so, they can improve health outcomes, reduce health disparities, and advance public health science and practice\. \(direct link \)

## [Process\-informed micromechanical modelling of anisotropy and defect sensitivity in additively manufactured 316L stainless steel](../publications/85b3515c2b9d0afd4b8d.md)

Majid Kavousi; Patrick McGarry; P\.E\. McHugh; S\.B\. Leen

Laser powder bed fusion \(PBF\-LB\) of 316L stainless steel produces melt\-pool\-driven columnar grain structures that result in significant mechanical anisotropy\. This study develops a predictive, process\-informed 3D geometrically based process\-structure \(GBPS\) framework integrated with crystal plasticity finite element \(CPFE\) modelling to simulate the tensile response of AM 316L\. The framework replaces the need for experimental microstructure data with an idealised, computationally efficient 3D unit cell\. Methodological optimisations, including the use of cuboid elements and regularised grain boundaries, achieve a 10\-fold reduction in CPU time with negligible \(&lt;1%\) loss in accuracy\. The model successfully predicts the characteristic anisotropy of AM 316L, yielding ≈9% higher yield strength and ≈12% higher UTS in the transverse direction compared to the build direction\. Furthermore, a defect\-sensitivity study reveals that horizontal build orientations are significantly more susceptible to porosity\-induced strain localisation, showing a ≈15% drop in ductility at 2% porosity\. This framework provides a physically motivated yet lean tool for exploring process\-structure–property relationships in PBF\-LB alloys across varied scanning strategies\.

## [Reward Engine: Reward\-Centric Self\-Evolution for Open\-Ended Tool Agents](../publications/85b9515df6a495b75fb6.md)

Litong Feng; Ji Qi; Yiran Cheng; Shaowu Pan; Xinyu Zhang; Qijun Li

Open\-ended tool agents can complete the same objective through different tool paths, and their quality depends jointly on the interaction trace, environment state, and final artifacts, so such tasks rarely admit an executable ground\-truth reward\. The central challenge is therefore to construct a reward from existing experience that exposes the current policy&\#x27;s failures while remaining stationary during optimization\. We introduce Reward Engine, which, like a self\-motivated student, first works out what success requires and then optimizes toward it\. From the task and initial trajectories, it builds a RewardPack of testcases for required correctness and rubrics for graded quality, each executed as a check that returns a judgment with evidence\. The frozen RewardPack then guides the agent to revise and select its outputs, and can also serve as a reward for reinforcement learning\. On WorkBuddy Bench Office and Claw\-Eval, the constructed reward largely agrees with the benchmark graders, not reversing their ordering on 82\.3\\% and 80\.5\\% of candidate pairs\. Used to revise executions, it raises three\-run consistency \($\\mathrm\{Pass\}^\{3\}$\) over Baseline from 45\.0\\% to 54\.0\\% and from 78\.4\\% to 83\.7\\%\.

## [Testosterone and Functional Speed Adaptation to Combined Lower limb Neuromuscular and Motor Coordination Training in Collegiate Badminton players: A Randomized Controlled Trial](../publications/85bc4479d811ecd15177.md)

Himanshu Himanshu; Amit Saraf; PoojaAnand PoojaAnand

Background: Hormone influence the body function which causes biochemical and metabolic changes\. Physical function are to be considered as strong influencer for the endocrinal variability mainly the testosterone and cortisol\. Aim:The study was aimed to examine the impact of combined lower limb neuromuscular training and motor coordination training on the level of testosterone among the male and female collegiate badminton players\. Methods and Material \- Randomized controlled trail was performed with inclusion of Collegiate Badminton players \(1625 years\) of both genders which were recruited from the university and colleges\. Ethical consent and CTRI was done before starting the study\. Statistical analysis:The analysis was done using software SPSS 24 version 2\.0\. Pearson’s test, Independent T test were performed\. P values were taken significant &lt;0\.05\. Results:The findings were signifying an enhancement of training regime in level of testosterone in experimental group whereas control group was also detrimental enhancement but the changes were minimal and no substantial\. Similarly, Speed was demonstrating noticeable improvement in values among the participants of experimental group whereas the control group was not showing any meaningful progress\. Additionally, the progress was more noticeable among males than females\. Conclusion:The exercise programs are effective and strong stimulators for the enhancement in values of testosterone as free marker of performance\. As some sports also shows such findings and remained it as a marker of performance among the athletes\.

## [A Minimal ReLU Classifier on Non\-Linearly Separable Data: Convergence and Implicit Bias at and beyond the Edge of Stability](../publications/85c00790cab62f01ab0b.md)

Quan Nguyen; Robin Yadav; Param Mody; Mark Schmidt

Gradient descent \(GD\) with large learning rates can successfully optimize neural networks even though classical smoothness\-based learning rate conditions are violated\. Yet theory for this regime largely covers linear models or linearly separable data\. We analyze a minimal setting outside both regimes\. Specifically, a two\-neuron ReLU network trained with logistic loss on 1D non\-linearly separable data\. The objective is nonconvex and nonsmooth, and GD exhibits edge\-of\-stability \(EoS\) behavior\. We identify an active cone in parameter space that contains every perfect classifier, where the problem becomes piecewise logistic regression with a varying effective dataset\. Within this cone, we prove a finite\-time loss bound for constant learning rates and show that GD converges in direction to an explicit max\-margin vector, while the orthogonal component converges to the unique minimizer of a non\-strongly convex potential\. We further establish catapult results where exponentially small loss is reached after a single loss spike\. Furthermore, we propose an adaptive schedule that lets learning rates grow to infinity without leaving the active cone\. We prove that this schedule achieves a loss rate of $O\(1/\(T\\log\{T\}\)$, which is faster than the standard $O\(1/T\)$ rate\. Our theoretical results extend to local convergence on more general network and are validated on MNIST dataset\. Overall, we show that this setup provides a tractable neural\-network model for studying large and adaptive step sizes beyond linear predictors and separable data\.

## [Exploratory Study on the Association Between Pre\-treatment Factors and Hematological Toxicity in Colorectal Cancer Patients Receiving CapeOX \(Capecitabine Plus Oxaliplatin\) Therapy](../publications/85c0570b27f994e87d7d.md)

Makoto Kishimoto; Jin Tokunaga

Background: The capecitabine plus oxaliplatin \(CapeOX\) regimen is commonly used for adjuvant treatment and selected first\-line treatment settings in colorectal cancer\.However, hematologic toxicities, such as leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, may adversely affect treatment continuity, resulting in treatment delays, dose reductions, or treatment discontinuation\.If these toxicities could be predicted based on pre\-treatment blood test results and markers of inflammation and nutrition, it would lead to improved treatment continuity\.In this study, we explored potential associations related to hematologic toxicities that occur at the end of the first cycle of CapeOX therapy\.Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 108 patients with colorectal cancer who began CapeOX therapy between September 2020 and October 2023\.We evaluated hematologic toxicity \(Grade ≥ 1\) at the end of the first treatment cycle based on the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events \(CTCAE\) version 5\.0 and examined its association with pre\-treatment blood test results, nutritional indices \(PNIs\), and inflammatory markers \(systemic inflammation response index \(SIRI\), systemic immune\-inflammation index \(SII\), neutrophil\-to\-lymphocyte ratio \(NLR\), platelet\-to\-lymphocyte ratio \(PLR\), and lymphocyte\-to\-monocyte ratio \(LMR\)\)\.We performed multivariate logistic regression analysis on factors showing significant differences and calculated cutoff values using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis\.Results: An SII value of ≤496\.8 was identified as a significant pretreatment factor associated with the development of leukopenia\.For hemoglobin reduction, age ≥68 years, red blood cell count ≤394 × 10⁴/μL, and hemoglobin \(Hb\) ≤11\.7 g/dL were associated; for thrombocytopenia, lymphocyte count ≤12\.41 × 10²/μL and SII ≤477\.9 were significantly associated\.The identified associations may help generate hypotheses for future prospective studies of pre\-treatment risk assessment and supportive\-care strategies\.Conclusions: Evidence suggests that some of the hematologic toxicities associated with CapeOX therapy show exploratory associations with pre\-treatment blood tests and markers of inflammation and nutrition\.These exploratory associations may help inform future hypothesis\-generating research on pretreatment risk assessment and supportive\-care strategies\.

## [Perceived cross\-cultural competency and purchase intention in foreign\-influencer live streaming commerce: an extended theory of planned behavior perspective](../publications/85e7ee8892490b5ad818.md)

Qingqing Liu; Kavitha Balakrishnan; Mokhtarrudin Bin Ahmad

Foreign influencers are playing a growing role in China&\#x27;s live\-streaming commerce industry\. Yet, little is known about how consumers respond to foreign influencers’ ability to communicate and adjust across cultures\. To address this gap, the present study draws on the Theory of Planned Behavior \(TPB\) and distinguishes between two consumer perceptions: Intercultural Communication Competency \(ICC\) and Intercultural Adaptability \(ICA\)\. It examines the relationship between each perception and Purchase Intention \(PI\)\. The study also considers whether this relationship operates through three key TPB factors—Attitude \(ATT\), Subjective Norm \(SN\), and Perceived Behavioral Control \(PBC\)\. Survey data from 450 eligible consumers in Zhejiang Province, China, were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling\. ICC was positively associated with PI directly and indirectly through all three TPB constructs\. ICA had no significant direct association with PI but showed significant specific indirect associations through ATT, SN, and PBC\. ATT was the strongest indirect pathway for ICC, whereas SN was the strongest for ICA\. The findings differentiate communication\-based and adaptation\-based routes into consumer decision\-making and show how culturally relevant perceptions of foreign communicators can be incorporated as antecedents within TPB\. Because the data are cross\-sectional and were obtained from a convenience sample of topic\-interested consumers in Zhejiang Province, the findings represent conditional associations within this specific sample and should not be generalised to all Chinese consumers\.
