## [Conversion‐Controlled Poly\(Ionic Liquid\)/Aluminum Nitride Thermal Interface Materials with Internal Plasticization for Reliable Chip‐Level Thermal Management](../publications/860606f94b84c2fbf8ff.md)

Longfeng Zou; Yucheng Jiang; Taoying Rao; Siying He; Long Teng; Yilan Guo; Ping Zhu; Yimin Yao

ABSTRACT The increasing power densities of artificial intelligence and high‐performance computing \(HPC\) chips place stringent demands on thermal interface materials \(TIMs\), which are designed to combine efficient heat transport with interfacial conformability, stress relaxation, and long‐term reliability\. Conventional silicone‐based TIMs can suffer from oil bleeding, pump‐out, and insufficient adhesion during prolonged thermal exposure\. Here, a conversion‐controlled poly\(ionic liquid\)/aluminum nitride \(PIL/AlN\) thermal gel is developed by partially polymerizing the PIL matrix\. The resulting chain‐entangled PIL framework retains residual monomer and oligomer species that provide internal plasticization, promote interfacial wetting, and facilitate stress relaxation, while densely packed spherical AlN particles establish heat‐transfer pathways\. After optimization of polymerization time and filler loading, the 55 vol% AlN composite exhibits an elongation‐at‐break of 291%, adhesion strengths of 5\.4 MPa on Cu and 3\.7 MPa on Si, and a bulk thermal conductivity of 2\.0 W·m −1 ·K −1 \. Its mechanical compliance enables intimate contact with Si, yielding an interfacial thermal resistance of \(2\.93 ± 0\.96\) × 10 −6 K·m 2 ·W −1 \. T3Ster cycling and high‐temperature aging further show stable device‐level thermal responses and no detectable macroscopic defects under the tested conditions\. This conversion‐controlled strategy provides a route to silicone‐free TIMs that combine mechanical compliance, interfacial adhesion, low interfacial thermal resistance, and operational stability\.

## [Severe Bacterial Infections and Sepsis in Children and Adolescents in São Paulo, Brazil: A Population\-Based Time\-Trend Study, 2015\-2025](../publications/860bb34b072d68c1c985.md)

André Luís Bastos Lima; Juan Silva Martins; Isadora Rita Carvalho; Cauê da Silva Manara; Stella Bernachi Rodrigues; Julia Pinheiro Almeida; Marcella Magliano Marins; Paola Zelada Florence; Ana Clara Fernandes

Background: Severe bacterial infections and sepsis are leading causes of pediatric hospitalization and death worldwide, yet recent Brazilian population\-based data spanning the COVID\-19 pandemic and distinguishing severe bacterial infection broadly from strict septicemia remain scarce\.Objectives: To describe hospitalization trends, mortality, and factors associated with in\-hospital death among children and adolescents with severe bacterial infections and sepsis in São Paulo State, Brazil, from 2015 to 2025, comparing the broad cohort with a strict\-sepsis subgroup\.Methods: Population\-based, repeated cross\-sectional study in São Paulo State, Brazil, 2015\-2025, using Hospital Information System of the Brazilian Unified Health System \(Sistema de Informações Hospitalares do Sistema Único de Saúde, SIH/SUS\) records for hospital admissions of individuals aged 28 days to 19 years\.The primary exposure was age group \(infant, preschool\-age, school\-age, adolescent\); the primary outcome was in\-hospital death\.Poisson regression estimated the annual trend in the number of admissions\.Crude relative risks \(RR\) were calculated directly from contingency data; adjusted RR \(aRR\) were obtained by predictive marginal standardization from a multivariable logistic model, with modified Poisson regression \(robust variance\) as a sensitivity analysis\.Results: Among 553,218 hospitalizations \(277,644; 50\.2% male\), overall case fatality was 1\.6% \(8765 deaths\)\.Compared with infants \(case fatality 1\.8%; 3038/170,495\), adolescents had over double the risk of death \(crude RR 2\.16, 95% CI 2\.06\-2\.27\),while preschool\-age \(RR 0\.47, 95% CI 0\.44\-0\.50\)and school\-age children \(RR 0\.59, 95% CI 0\.54\-0\.63\)had lower risk\.Male sex carried modestly higher risk \(RR 1\.16, 95% CI 1\.11\-1\.21\),and comorbidity \(49,952; 9\.0% of admissions\) more than tripled risk \(RR 3\.22, 95% CI 3\.07\-3\.38\)\.The number of admissions declined over the study period \(Poisson regression trend ratio 0\.96 per year, 95% CI 0\.96\-0\.97\),with a pronounced, non\-linear drop during the pandemic and partial recovery thereafter\.The strict\-sepsis subgroup comprised 27,181 admissions \(4\.9% of the cohort\) but had a case fatality of 14\.7% \(3985 deaths\), nine times that of the broad cohort\.Conclusions: Severe bacterial infections impose a substantial, age\-concentrated hospital burden among Brazilian children, while strict sepsis, though comparatively uncommon, remains markedly lethal\.Distinguishing these entities is important for surveillance and resource planning\.

## [Korelasi Self\-Efficacy dengan Kemampuan Pemecahan Masalah Matematis Siswa SMP](../publications/860e3a296e8a7e97a6ef.md)

Maydina Novarianti; Chintia Malinie

Kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis merupakan kompetensi esensial dalam pembelajaran matematika, tetapi keberhasilannya tidak cukup dijelaskan oleh penguasaan konsep semata dan diduga berkaitan dengan faktor nonkognitif seperti self\-efficacy\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis korelasi antara self\-efficacy dengan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis siswa kelas VIII SMP Negeri 1 Muncar\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional\. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 50 siswa dari populasi 200 siswa, dipilih menggunakan purposive sampling\. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket self\-efficacy dan tes kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis berbasis tahapan Polya, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas Shapiro\-Wilk, uji linearitas, dan korelasi Pearson Product\-Moment\. Hasil analisis deskriptif menunjukkan skor self\-efficacy siswa berada pada kategori sedang \(rata\-rata 112,36; 58,00% siswa\), sedangkan rata\-rata kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis sebesar 71,84 \(rentang 45–94\)\. Data kedua variabel memenuhi asumsi normalitas dan linearitas\. Hasil korelasi Pearson menunjukkan hubungan positif dan signifikan antara self\-efficacy dengan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis \(r = 0,624; p &lt; 0,001\)\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa siswa dengan self\-efficacy yang lebih tinggi cenderung memiliki kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis yang lebih baik, tanpa dapat ditafsirkan sebagai hubungan kausal karena desain penelitian bersifat korelasional

## [From Diagnosis to Decision‐Making: AI ‐Driven Triage of Oral Mucosal Lesions Detected on Intraoral Photographs](../publications/860f4ff01444540fb4bf.md)

Julia Schwärzler; Ekaterina V\. Tolstaya; Antonín Tichý; Tami Yap; Michael John McCullough; Yoana Malenova; David Steybe; Sven Otto; Sebastian Paris; Falk Schwendicke

BACKGROUND: Managing oral mucosal lesions in general dental practice is challenging, as visually similar conditions may require very different treatments\. We developed an AI\-based triage system connecting intraoral image analysis with guideline\-based treatment recommendations, tested it externally, and compared its performance with clinicians&\#x27; recommendations\. METHODS: YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 were trained on 4079 intraoral photographs to classify 11 oral mucosal lesion types\. These were mapped into five treatment tiers defined by urgency and management aim: T1 specialist referral for malignant and high\-risk lesions, T2 interdisciplinary referral for specialist\-led non\-cancer management, T3 risk\-adapted surveillance, T4 dental treatment with reassessment, and T5 no treatment\. Model performance was compared with two general dentists and four specialists on an internal test set\. YOLOv11 was additionally tested on an external dataset\. RESULTS: YOLOv11 outperformed YOLOv8 in macro\-averaged precision, recall, and F1 score, achieving 0\.72, 0\.74, and 0\.73 respectively\. However, 25% of T1 high\-risk cases were under\-triaged\. YOLOv11 significantly outperformed all clinicians, whose F1 scores ranged from 0\.33 to 0\.69\. External performance decreased markedly \(F1 score: 0\.58\), consistent with domain shift\. CONCLUSION: Guideline\-oriented AI triage is feasible but requires multicentre training for improved generalizability, as well as safety\-focused optimization, and prospective user evaluation before clinical use\.

## [CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model\-Driven Harness](../publications/86121dde8a5ff8bcd876.md)

Dongjie Cheng; Ruifeng Yuan; Ran Wei; Ning Song; Yongqi Li; Wenjie Li

As Vision\-Language Models \(VLMs\) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show\. Video World Models \(VWMs\) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task\-relevant visual content as additional evidence\. However, existing approaches typically invoke a VWM through fixed pipelines centered on a predefined form of visual imagination, such as novel\-view synthesis\. To support flexible visual imagination for diverse reasoning tasks, we introduce CoWorld Reasoner, an agentic framework that uses a VWM as a unified visual reasoning engine\. Its Video World Model\-Driven Harness exposes multiple visual operations through tools and uses skills to guide the VLM in deciding whether to imagine, selecting an operation, constructing a generation request, and interpreting the resulting visual evidence\. We further introduce VLM\-VWM Harness Co\-Evolution, which jointly revises tools, skills, and execution code based on execution feedback while keeping both model weights fixed\. Across seven benchmarks spanning spatial intelligence, temporal and causal reasoning, and perceptual reasoning, CoWorld Reasoner outperforms direct reasoning with the same VLM\. The strongest variant improves on all seven benchmarks, including relative accuracy gains of 11\.8% on MMSI and 13\.0% on ERQA, and outperforms all five evolving baselines using the same backbone across five benchmarks\.

## [Sexual behavior dysfunction and sickness behavior as an early warning indicators of imidacloprid exposure, associated with pituitary–adrenal axis dysregulation and DNA damage in Japanese quails](../publications/86279407374adad04170.md)

Ramadan D\. El Shoukary; Doaa S\. Abd El\-Maguid; Asmaa H\. Abd El Kareem; Aymen S\. Abd El\-Maguid; Gehad Seddik; Asmaa Fahmy Khafaga; Nora Abdelbaeth

Introduction Japanese quails \( Coturnix coturnix japonica \) serve as vital models in behavioral neuroendocrinology and ecotoxicology, particularly for understanding the neuroendocrine pathways regulating avian mating strategies\. Subchronic exposure to neonicotinoid insecticides poses critical threats to avian reproduction and population dynamics\. Methods This study comprehensively evaluated the neuroendocrine, behavioral, morphometric, and genotoxic impacts of chronic oral imidacloprid \(IMI\) exposure in Japanese quail \( Coturnix coturnix japonica \) across developmental and adult stages \(weeks 7–12 of age\)\. Results Imidacloprid administration significantly delayed pubertal onset and increased body weight at sexual maturity in both sexes \( p ≤ 0\.003\)\. Morphometric analysis revealed profound somatic and gonadal hypotrophy, evidenced by persistent reductions in the brain\-somatic index \(BSI\) and gonado\-somatic index \(GSI; testicular and ovarian masses\) across development \( p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. Endocrine profiling demonstrated systemic disruption of the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal \(HPG\) axis, marked by significant suppression of circulating anterior pituitary gonadotropins \(FSH and LH\), testosterone, progesterone, and total estrogens \( p &lt; 0\.0001\), alongside biphasic 17β\-estradiol deregulation\. Behaviorally, exposed birds exhibited pronounced hypodipsia, increased stationary crouching, and progressive sickness behavior \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. In males, IMI induced severe reproductive and behavioral deficits, characterized by marked reductions in cloacal gland area \(304\.66 vs\. 332\.90 mm\), relative testis mass, and merocrine foam production \( p &lt; 0\.001\), accompanied by significant suppression of appetitive courtship displays \(chasing, waltzing, wing flapping\) and consummatory copulatory performance \(mounting, cloacal contact movements, libido scores, and copulatory efficiency\) in both rearing cages and standard testing arenas \( p &lt; 0\.05 to p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. In females, IMI significantly blunted proceptive squatting and holding\-still compliance scores during mounting encounters without altering running escape frequency, alongside severe reductions in total weekly egg production, egg weight, hen\-day egg production, and total egg mass \( p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Furthermore, the alkaline comet assay revealed marked hepatic and cerebral genomic DNA damage, with significant elevations in percentage DNA damage and tail moment \(p &lt; 0\.05 to p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion Overall, these findings demonstrate that chronic imidacloprid exposure induces multi\-level neuroendocrine disruption, systemic genotoxicity, and severe reproductive failure in avian models, highlighting significant ecotoxicological risks to non\-target avian species\.

## [Garbha Saṃskāra and Maternal Diet: A Critical Analysis of Ayurvedic Prenatal Care, Fetal Phenotype Development and Epigenetic Programming](../publications/862c86ee87e0b6946fb7.md)

Sumol Anand Pawar

Background: The prenatal period represents a critical window of developmental plasticity, where maternal nutritional, physiological, psychological, and environmental factors influence fetal phenotype and lifelong health outcomes\. The concept of Developmental Origins of Health and Disease \(DOHaD\) provides a modern scientific framework explaining how intrauterine exposures regulate developmental trajectories through epigenetic mechanisms\. Ayurveda describes a comprehensive prenatal care approach through Garbha Saṃskāra, emphasizing the role of maternal diet \(āhāra\), lifestyle \(vihāra\), mental wellbeing, and environmental influences in fetal development\. Objective: This review aims to critically analyse the relationship between Garbha Saṃskāra and contemporary concepts of fetal programming, with particular emphasis on maternal diet, fetal phenotype development, and genetic expression regulation\. Methods: A narrative integrative review was performed by analysing classical Ayurvedic references from Caraka Saṃhitā Śārīrasthāna along with contemporary scientific literature on maternal nutrition, developmental biology, DOHaD, and epigenetic mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modification, and non\-coding RNA regulation\. Results: Classical Ayurvedic descriptions identify fetal development as a multifactorial process involving maternal \(mātṛja\), paternal \(pitṛja\), nutritional \(rasaja\), adaptive \(sātmyaja\), psychological \(sattvaja\), and individual \(ātmaja\) determinants\. Modern evidence demonstrates that maternal nutritional status, particularly availability of methyl donors such as folate, vitamin B12, and choline, influences fetal growth, metabolic regulation, and gene expression through epigenetic pathways\. Maternal psychological stress also affects fetal development through neuroendocrine and molecular mechanisms\. However, direct experimental validation of Garbha Saṃskāra as an epigenetic programming intervention remains limited\. Conclusion: Garbha Saṃskāra represents a holistic prenatal framework with conceptual similarities to modern developmental science\. While its principles align with established evidence on maternal nutrition and psychosocial influences, rigorous interdisciplinary research is required to validate specific mechanisms and clinical outcomes\. Keywords: Garbha Saṃskāra, maternal diet, fetal phenotype, epigenetics, developmental origins of health and disease, prenatal programming

## [Peran Guru Al\-Islam dan Kemuhammadiyahan dalam Pembentukan Karakter Peserta Didik di SMA Muhammadiyah 01 Pekajangan](../publications/865fbfa5b74ac2de629b.md)

Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran guru AIK dalam membentuk karakter peserta didik di SMA Muhammadiyah 01 Pekajangan serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya\. Pembentukan karakter didukung oleh visi Islami sekolah, kurikulum ISMUBARIS, pembiasaan budaya 5S, dan ekstrakurikuler\. ## [The Effect of the Inquiry Learning Model on the Historical Thinking Skills of Grade XI Students at SMA Negeri 1 Pandeglang : Pengaruh Model Inqiry Learning Terhadap Kemampuan Berpikir Historis Siswa Kelas XI SMA Negeri 1 Pandeglang](../publications/866633366569f268ce30.md)

The 21st\-century educational paradigm shift demands a transition from teacher\-centered to student\-centered learning\. However, history learning at SMA Negeri 1 Pandeglang is still dominated by conventional methods that hinder the development of students&\#x27; historical thinking skills, compounded by a lack of prior evaluation regarding historical thinking indicators\. This study aims to describe the effect of implementing the inquiry learning model on the historical thinking skills of Grade XI students regarding the Proclamation of Indonesian Independence\. A quantitative method with a pre\-experimental design \(One Group Pretest\-Posttest Design\) was employed\. The sampling technique used non\-probability sampling involving 34 students from class XI\-12\. Data were collected through an essay test based on Sam Wineburg&\#x27;s indicators and analyzed using the parametric Paired Sample T\-Test\. Descriptive analysis results indicated an increase in the students&\#x27; average score from 41\.24% in the pre\-test \(very low category\) to 66\.47% in the post\-test \(moderate category\)\. Furthermore, hypothesis testing yielded a Sig\. \(2\-tailed\) value of 0\.000 \(&lt; 0\.05\) and a t\-value of 9\.911 &gt; t\-table 2\.03452, thereby rejecting H0\. In conclusion, the inquiry learning model has a positive and significant effect on improving students&\#x27; historical thinking skills comprehensively across all measured indicators\.

## [Algorithm Modelization: Transforming Optimization Algorithms into Evolvable Intelligence](../publications/86748eac21a13255a8ba.md)

Jian Yao; Zhiyao Zhang; Yichen Li; Xingyu Wu; Kay Chen Tan

Can algorithms be learned and evolved as models, rather than repeatedly redesigned as programs? We explore this question by introducing Algorithm Modelization, a new paradigm that turns iterative algorithms into trainable models\. Its central idea is to regard algorithm execution trajectories as computational experience: by learning how algorithmic states evolve over iterations, a model can internalize the knowledge embodied in existing algorithms, reproduce their computational behaviors, and further evolve beyond them through training\. As a first realization of this paradigm, we modelize iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, where preceding generations constitute the computational context for generating the next population\. We develop a dimension\-independent population\-temporal architecture to capture both population interactions and iterative dynamics, together with an imitation\-to\-surpassing learning framework that first acquires algorithmic knowledge from heterogeneous teachers and then improves the resulting optimizer directly through optimization feedback\. The modelized optimizer consequently goes beyond reproducing individual algorithms: it consolidates heterogeneous search knowledge into a single trainable model, achieves stronger optimization capability through subsequent improvement, and generalizes its acquired knowledge across problems and substantially larger unseen dimensions\. More fundamentally, Algorithm Modelization makes algorithmic capability accumulable through learning, where new algorithms and problem\-solving experience can become training resources for progressively improving the model\. Our results establish a promising path from manually designed algorithms toward general algorithm models that learn, generalize, and evolve from computational experience\.

## [Pan\-genomics in One Health: linking pathogens, hosts, and environments](../publications/8687ebb8df53ad1c9ca4.md)

Andrei Giacchetto Felice; Sandeep Tiwari; Diego Lucas Neres Rodrigues; Arun Kumar Jaiswal; Rodrigo Bentes Kato; Franciele Maboni Siqueira; Wylerson Guimarães Nogueira; Rodrigo Dias Oliveira Carvalho; Roberta Torres Chideroli; Ulisses de Pádua Pereira; Selma Soares de Oliveira; Sheila da Silva; Thais Vilela Rodrigues; Pedro Henrique Marques; Fabiana Vieira Dominici; Eduarda Sousa Guimarães; Victor Augusto Sallum Ceballos; Roberto Montes de Oca JimÃ©nez; Aristoteles Goes Neto; Mateus Matiuzzi da Costa; Flávia Figueira Aburjaile; Rommel Thiago Jucá Ramos; Vasco Azevedo; Siomar de Castro Soares

The One Health approach recognizes the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health for managing global health challenges\. The increasing incidence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and environmental degradation underscores the relevance of integrated surveillance strategies\. In this context, pan\-genomics has emerged as a valuable tool for characterizing the genetic diversity of bacterial pathogens across hosts, geographic regions, and ecological niches\. By distinguishing core from accessory genome components, pan\-genomic analyses inform vaccine target identification through reverse vaccinology; elucidate antimicrobial resistance determinants; and reveal host adaptation mechanisms\. This review examines the application of pan\-genomics within the One Health framework, focusing on bacterial pathogens of relevance to human, animal, and environmental health, including Bacillus anthracis , Mycobacterium bovis , Corynebacterium pseudotuberculosis , Mycobacterium marinum , Leptospira interrogans , Yersinia pestis , Francisella tularensis , Corynebacterium ulcerans , and Vibrio vulnificus \. For each pathogen, we discuss available genomic data, pan\-genome characteristics, and implications for surveillance, diagnostics, and intervention strategies\. Additionally, we address the role of metagenomics in environmental monitoring and the contribution of computational approaches, such as reverse vaccinology and subtractive genomics, to the development of novel therapeutic and prophylactic targets\.

Annisa Novita Putri Siregar; Hafni; Muhammad Zen

Indoor air quality is an important factor affecting human health because most daily activities are carried out in enclosed environments\. This study aims to design and implement an Internet of Things \(IoT\)\-based air purifier using ESP32, MQ\-9 and MQ\-135 gas sensors, MQTT, Node\-RED, InfluxDB, and Grafana\. The proposed system monitors indoor air quality in real time, automatically controls DC fan speed based on air quality conditions, provides local notifications through RGB LEDs and a buzzer, stores sensor data in a time\-series database, and visualizes historical data through a web\-based dashboard\. System testing was conducted using several pollutant sources, including paper combustion smoke, air freshener, and perfume under both open and enclosed conditions\. The results indicate that the system successfully detected changes in air quality, automatically adjusted fan speed, activated visual and audible indicators according to predefined thresholds, and transmitted sensor data to the monitoring dashboard in real time\. These results demonstrate that the proposed system can effectively integrate real\-time monitoring, automatic air purification, historical data storage, and user notification within a single IoT\-based platform\.

## [Optimized bilateral segmentation deep learning network for wild animal detection](../publications/8696e703696df5f9f809.md)

B\. Srikanth; Johnwesily Chappidi; Gunakala Archana; Anitha Rani Palakayala; Guggilam Venkata Vidya Lakshmi; Khasim Syed; Shaik Salma Asiya Begum

The use of Deep learning \(DL\) for recognition of wild animals has become an important development in wildlife monitoring\. The advances will include the use of multimodal data for improved accuracy and development of lightweight models for use in edge devices\. As a result, DL will help contribute to global conservation efforts as it tackles the issues\. The key novelty of the proposed framework is the integration of bilateral segmentation with DL to enhance relevant animal feature extraction while reducing the influence of complex background information\. The paper proposes the Optimized Bilateral Segmentation DL Network that uses Harris Hawks Optimization \(HHO\) to improve Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) parameters for wild animal identification\. The first step in the process was collecting datasets from various online sources\. The image quality was improved through image processing methods such as Adaptive Histogram Equalization \(AHE\) as well as median filtering\. The classifier was trained and validated using pre\-processed images\. This classifier combines the Bilateral Segmentation Deep Learning Network \(BSDLN\) with the HHO algorithm\. CNN is utilized for detection and the weight parameter is utilized by HHO\. In order to enhance model convergence also with performance, HHO dynamically adjusts the learning rate during training within the BSDLN\. This balances speed and accuracy by adapting to gradients and losses behavior\. By adaptively adjusting the learning rate, HHO and BSDLN optimize the CNN learning process and enhance convergence and classification performance\. The suggested approach is put into practice in Python, and statistical metrics are used to assess its effectiveness\. The results are compared with other approaches to verify the strategy&\#x27;s efficacy\. With just 0\.2% FPR and 0\.3% FNR, the suggested BSDLN performed the best overall, achieving 99\.4% precision, 99\.8% accuracy, 99\.6% recall, 99\.5% F1\-score, and 99\.3% specificity\. The experimental findings show that the combination of HHO and bilateral segmentation enhances the efficacy of wild animal detection, offering a strong foundation for automated wildlife monitoring\.

## [Cross\-Lexicon Emoji Sentiment Divergence for Arabic Sarcasm Detection](../publications/86b3379572f90f99c4a2.md)

Rusul Hussein Hasan; Zinah Rajab Hussein; Mustafa Hussein Zwayyer; Nafea Jameel Khalaf ALHelal; Arkan Raheem Jebur; Duaa Adnan Tawfeek; Rasha Majid Hassoon

This study aims to determine whether the divergence between context\-free and context\-sensitive emoji sentiment scores can serve as a complementary signal for sarcasm detection in Arabic\. This phenomenon has received little systematic attention so far\. To address this aim, we conducted a multi\-scale empirical investigation\. At the lexicon level, we compared 1,031 overlapping emoji from two Arabic sentiment resources: the context\-sensitive Arab\-ESL, derived from 144,196 tweets, and the context\-free CF\-Arab\-ESL, annotated by 53 native speakers across seven Arab regions\. At the corpus level, we examined the divergence pattern in a stratified random sample of 199,999 tweets drawn from the 1,414,523\-tweet TEAD collection\. At the task level, we developed a divergence\-augmented transformer architecture by concatenating eight cross\-lexicon features with the \[CLS\] representation produced by three Arabic BERT encoders: MARBERT, AraBERTv2, and CAMeLBERT\. We evaluated it on the ArSarcasMoji dataset of 24,630 samples across five random seeds\. The results indicate that only 56\.8% of overlapping emoji maintain consistent sentiment labels across the two annotation paradigms \(W = 91,029, p = 2\.44× 10\-74, Cohen&\#x27;s d = 0\.656\)\. The corpus\-level analysis confirms that context\-free scores are systematically more positive than their contextual counterparts \(d = 1\.124, p &lt; 10\-300\)\. At the classification level, the divergence\-augmented MARBERT achieves the highest mean F1\-sarcasm of 0\.5234 ± 0\.015 across five random seeds, compared with 0\.5149 ± 0\.017 for the text\-only baseline, and the augmentation produces a directionally consistent gain across all three encoders\. Ablation analysis shows that continuous divergence scores contribute most of this improvement, whereas binary irony\-risk indicators tend to introduce noise at low prevalence\. The findings establish cross\-lexicon emoji sentiment divergence as a measurable and pervasive feature of Arabic digital discourse, and indicate a modest but directionally consistent benefit when the divergence signal is supplied as a complementary feature for downstream sarcasm detection\. A controlled emoji\-aware comparison further shows that retaining emoji as input tokens allows encoders whose vocabularies cover emoji to recover the dataset construction rule almost perfectly \(F1\-sarcasm up to 0\.998\), which establishes the emoji\-token\-free protocol adopted here, in which no raw emoji tokens reach the text encoder while emoji\-derived lexicon features are retained, as the methodologically sound setting for this corpus\.

## [Intelligent account takeover detection in single sign\-on systems using behavioral and device login analytics](../publications/86bc3e070715544775bf.md)

Rinku Mohan; Farrukh Saleem; Khaled H\. Alyoubi; Aisha Y\. Alsobhi; Wafi Bedewi

With changing times and digitalization in the field of information technology, Single Sign\-On \(SSO\) mechanisms have become an important feature of identity management systems\. SSO enables users to access numerous services with one set of login credentials, but it can increase risks like account takeover \(ATO\), affecting security and privacy\. The research aims to use advanced statistical analysis and Machine Learning \(ML\) to improve authentication mechanisms and identify predictive features for risk\-based authentication\. The behavioral changes demonstrated by users after account takeover \(ATO\) incidents are also examined to design risk indicators\. To achieve these objectives, this research utilized a large dataset of 33 million login attempts from 3\.3 million users in Norway from February 2020 to February 2021\. Using machine learning models evaluated with an 80:20 train\-test validation strategy and complementary performance metrics, we observed that ASN, city, Round\-trip time \(RTT\), device type, and login success were the key features for accurately identifying attackers, achieving 93% prediction accuracy\. In addition, the login attempts were found to be maximum during typical office hours \(9 AM, 12 PM, 3 PM, and 6 PM\), where attackers may be trying to imitate themselves as normal users\. The research findings will aid in the implementation of secure, user\-friendly, and dependable authentication schemes that strengthen all aspects of digital identity management\.

## [GeoQA\-PG: a knowledge system\-guided retrieval\-augmented framework for geographical question answering in Pedogeography](../publications/86e89db0964915325f9c.md)

Shijia Ke; Yi Huang; Yehua Sheng; Ran Tao; Liu Yang; Xiangqiang Min; Jike Chen; Yufei Chen

Geographical Question Answering \(GeoQA\) is transitioning from traditional rule\-based and retrieval\-based approaches to intelligent paradigms driven by large language models\. As an important component of geographic artificial intelligence, GeoQA aims to provide reliable and interpretable geographic knowledge services\. However, existing Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) methods remain inadequate for geographic questions requiring structured knowledge and coherent logical reasoning\. To address these challenges, this study proposes GeoQA\-PG, a question answering framework for pedogeography\. Specifically, a tree\-network knowledge system is constructed by integrating a hierarchical knowledge framework with a fine\-grained knowledge graph\. Building on this knowledge system, a dual\-channel retrieval mechanism, named SoilKnowRAG, is developed\. It combines text and graph retrieval to mitigate knowledge fragmentation\. Based on GeoQA\-PG, SoilGPT is implemented and evaluated using a question answering dataset\. Experimental results demonstrate that SoilGPT significantly outperforms baseline models with comparable parameter scales on both objective and subjective tasks, while the comparative evaluation of SoilKnowRAG further confirms its effectiveness compared with other RAG methods\. Overall, GeoQA\-PG provides a transferable framework for knowledge\-driven GeoQA and advances the intelligent representation, reasoning, and services of geographic knowledge\.

## [Leadership\-Driven ESG Integration in Islamic Education: Developing a Sustainability Management Model for Islamic Secondary Schools](../publications/86f2c3b00e64ad4bc94e.md)

Kelik Wardiyono; Baidi Baidi; Heldy Ramadhan Putra; Siti Fathonah Wijayanti

This study aims to examine how Environmental, Social, and Governance \(ESG\) principles are interpreted, integrated, and managed within Islamic secondary education and to develop a Leadership\-Driven ESG Integration Management model\. This study conducted a qualitative case study at an Islamic secondary school from April to June 2026\. The study collected data through semi\-structured interviews, observations, and document analysis with relevant school stakeholders\. The data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion verification, supported by triangulation to strengthen the credibility of findings\. The results indicate that ESG integration was constructed by aligning sustainability practices with Islamic values and ecotheological principles, including Khalifah, Amanah, mas’uliyyah, and ihsan\. Leadership played a central role by combining spiritual, transformational, and instructional functions to coordinate environmental, social, and governance initiatives, such as BeRAANI, waste management programs, Ketep Pass Project\-Based Learning, community service, Adiwiyata, and quality assurance systems\. The study concludes that leadership bridges Islamic values and sustainability governance\. The proposed model contributes theoretically by extending sustainable leadership perspectives and practically by offering an applicable framework for managing sustainability in Islamic schools\. Future studies should examine its transferability through comparative and longitudinal research designs\.

## [Challenges to Enhancing the Competitive Advantage of Startups in Algeria A Quantitative Sociological Analysis](../publications/86f2f731f237b7972b11.md)

Dr\. Boufarh Monira; Dr\. Rahmani Khelifa

This study aims to shed light on the implications of enhancing the competitive advantage of Algerian startups by examining the contribution of organizational commitment to operational processes and activities, data analysis, and strategic decision\-making at various organizational levels\. In accordance with the methodological requirements of the research topic, its two variables, and the proposed hypotheses, the study adopted a descriptive approach using statistical methods\. A total of 53 questionnaires were distributed to a purposive sample of Algerian startups\. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS version 27\. The findings revealed that organizational commitment contributes to strengthening and developing the competitive advantage of startups, particularly in the areas of operational processes and activities, innovation, and the development of products and services\. ## [Determinants of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Construction Project Delivery: Evidence from Large Construction Firms in Nigeria Using the TOE Framework](../publications/86fc07185a888a2636a5.md)

Sonter John Chen; Aisha P\. Abdullahi; Isaac A\. John; Precious Aniette Umoren

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly recognized as a transformative technology for enhancing construction project delivery\. However, empirical evidence explaining the factors associated with its adoption remains limited, particularly in developing\-country construction contexts\. This study investigated the determinants of AI adoption across construction project delivery functions among large\-scale construction firms in Nigeria using the Technology–Organization–Environment \(TOE\) framework\. A quantitative survey design was adopted, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to construction professionals across 14 purposively selected large\-scale construction firms\. A total of 288 valid responses were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics and SmartPLS 4\. Descriptive statistics were employed to examine respondent characteristics, AI application areas, and construct performance, while Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\) was used to test the hypothesized relationships\. The findings indicate that AI adoption remains at a moderate stage, with implementation concentrated in design and BIM processes \(50\.7%\) and planning and project control \(38\.9%\)\. Organisational factors demonstrated the strongest statistical association with AI adoption \(β = 0\.404\), followed by technological \(β = 0\.169\) and environmental factors \(β = 0\.158\), with the TOE model explaining 30\.8% of the variance in adoption\. The relatively high organisational readiness score alongside moderate AI adoption suggests that favourable internal conditions do not necessarily translate into extensive AI implementation\. By providing TOE\-based empirical evidence from these firms in Nigeria, the findings contribute to the growing literature on construction digitalization and offer practical insights for firms seeking to accelerate AI\-enabled project delivery\.

## [Enterprise Architecture for Autonomous Enterprises](../publications/87093a58954fde38d5dc.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

Autonomous enterprises increasingly combine Artificial Intelligence, Agentic AI, automation, event\-driven platforms, digital twins, data products, and intelligent decision services to execute business processes with reduced manual intervention\. Traditional enterprise architecture methods are often insufficient when systems can plan, reason, act, learn, and coordinate dynamically across organizational boundaries\. This paper proposes an Enterprise Architecture for Autonomous Enterprises framework that aligns business capabilities, operating models, data, applications, integration, AI, security, governance, and human oversight\. The framework introduces architectural principles for bounded autonomy, policy\-driven execution, decision rights, digital workforce governance, real\-time observability, resilience, and continuous assurance\. It also defines reference layers, implementation stages, governance gates, and measurable outcomes\. The proposed approach enables organizations to scale autonomous operations while maintaining accountability, interoperability, trust, regulatory readiness, and business control\.

## [Artificial intelligence and machine learning for sustainable polymeric marine antifouling coatings: current evidence, challenges, and future perspectives](../publications/8710bce0f5db019a08ff.md)

Maha Mohammed Elsawy

Marine biofouling causes significant economic and environmental impacts by increasing drag, fuel consumption, emissions, maintenance costs, and material degradation\. Despite advances in sustainable antifouling coatings, their development still relies largely on trial\-and\-error approaches\. Recent advances in AI, ML, and materials informatics can accelerate the discovery and optimization of sustainable marine antifouling coatings by predicting performance, identifying structure–property relationships, and optimizing formulations while reducing experimental effort\. Nevertheless, the direct application of AI and ML specifically to marine antifouling coating design remains relatively limited, and much of the available evidence originates from broader materials science and coating research\. Therefore, this review critically examines the emerging application of AI and ML to sustainable polymeric marine antifouling coatings, while distinguishing between directly demonstrated antifouling applications and transferable approaches from related materials systems\. The review focuses on the application of AI for predicting fouling resistance, durability, corrosion protection, and environmental sustainability and evaluates the extent to which these approaches can be translated to marine antifouling systems\. Key challenges, including data scarcity, heterogeneous experimental datasets, lack of standardized testing protocols, limited field validation, and model interpretability, are highlighted, together with future opportunities in digital twins, explainable AI, generative AI, and autonomous materials discovery for next\-generation sustainable antifouling coatings\. By critically assessing the current evidence, methodological limitations, and research gaps, this review identifies priorities for developing reliable AI\-assisted antifouling coating design frameworks and proposes a staged pathway from standardized data generation and predictive modeling toward experimental validation, active learning, and autonomous materials discovery\. AI and machine learning approaches for sustainable marine antifouling coatings are critically reviewed\. Current evidence is distinguished between direct antifouling applications and transferable materials\-science approaches\. Key challenges include data scarcity, heterogeneous datasets, limited standardization, and field validation\. Emerging tools include explainable AI, generative AI, digital twins, and autonomous experimentation\. A staged roadmap toward predictive, validated, and sustainable antifouling coating design is proposed\.

## [Antimicrobial Resistance in Chronic Diarrhea: A Case Report of Cefazolin\-Resistant Enteric Infection](../publications/8713f54f324dbd2e1de1.md)

Gembong Satria Mahardhika; Aulia Nurul Izzati; Nimas Adiani Sekar Laranti; Fatmanur Hurulhanifa; Hanifa Nur Shabrina; Qodri Santosa

Introduction: Antimicrobial resistance is an emerging global health challenge that may lead to treatment failure and prolonged illness\. Although cefazolin resistance is relatively uncommon, it can complicate infectious disease management, including chronic diarrhea\. Case: A 7\-month\-old girl presented with fever and chronic mucoid diarrhea\. Despite treatment with multiple antibiotics, including cefazolin, metronidazole, and vancomycin, her symptoms worsened, with diarrhea increasing to seven episodes daily, accompanied by severe anemia and malnutrition\. Antibiotic susceptibility testing revealed isolated cefazolin resistance \(MIC = 64 μg/mL\)\. After susceptibility\-guided treatment with intravenous ciprofloxacin and supportive care, the patient improved significantly and was discharged after 10 days\. Discussion: This case highlights the importance of considering antimicrobial resistance in children with persistent diarrhea who fail to respond to empirical antibiotic therapy\. Cefazolin resistance likely contributed to treatment failure and clinical deterioration\. Early microbiological investigation and susceptibility\-guided therapy were essential to achieve clinical recovery and prevent further complications\. Conclusion: Clinicians should consider cefazolin\-resistant enteric infection in cases of chronic diarrhea with poor response to empirical treatment\. Prompt culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing are crucial to guide appropriate antimicrobial therapy and improve patient outcomes\.

## [Triad of national security management: Controlled artificial intelligence, neural interfaces, and directive personnel allocation](../publications/8715d791c86c344e949c.md)

D\. M\. Bortnikov; Mikhail A\. Lebedev; Дмитрий Александрович Репин

Aim\. To substantiate the content and limits of application of three heterogeneous but interrelated areas of strengthening state capacity in the sphere of national security, specifically controlled artificial intelligence, neural interfaces, and directive personnel allocation, as well as to determine the conditions for their coordinated development without artificial unification into an automated system\. Objective s\. To reveal the concept of controlled artificial intelligence as applied to public administration; to establish the legal and organizational boundaries of delegating analytical and managerial functions to algorithms; to analyze directive personnel allocation as state planning of the training and placement of competencies while preserving the contractual freedom of citizens; to assess the technological maturity of neural interfaces and to identify proven areas of their application; to determine the points of interconnection among the three areas in the tasks of big data processing, predictive modeling, anti\-terrorist prevention, and socio\-economic development\. Methods\. The study employs systemic, institutional, functional, and comparative\-legal approaches, methods of analyzing strategic and regulatory legal documents of Russia, scenario analysis, and qualitative comparison of technological maturity\. The empirical basis consists of materials from the National Anti\-Terrorism Committee and the Federal Security Service of Russia, strategic documents of the Government of Russia, scholarly publications by Russian researchers on data mining, artificial intelligence ethics, and neural interfaces, as well as OECD and UNESCO recommendations and regulatory acts of the European Union\. Results \. It is established that the elements under consideration are at different stages of institutional and technological maturity\. Controlled artificial intelligence is used in analytics, monitoring, forecasting, and the preparation of decision options, provided there is documented human control\. Directive personnel allocation has an existing legal basis in the mechanisms of targeted education, state orders, personnel forecasting, and service rotation, but requires a transition from planning professions to planning competencies and teams\. Neural interfaces have high evidentiary maturity, primarily in medicine and assistive technologies; their application in public administration appears permissible in limited tasks of digital system accessibility, training, and voluntary support for operators\. A differentiated model of state policy is proposed in which the three areas are interconnected at the level of goals and regulations rather than through the unification of data and powers on a single platform\. Conclusions\. The triad can be viewed as a concept of coordinated development of the state’s analytical, personnel, and human\-machine capacity, but not as a ready\-made unified technological framework\. The most mature areas are controlled artificial intelligence and state management of the personnel order\. Neural interfaces require special legal guarantees, ethical expertise, and phased piloting\. The condition for the effectiveness of the triad is the preservation of personal human responsibility, technological sovereignty, the contractual nature of personnel obligations, and the prohibition of covert use of neural data\.

## [An Adaptive Machine Learning Framework for Predicting and Enhancing Student Performance in STEM Education](../publications/871afe83803422ea992b.md)

B\. Fathimamary

The advent of machine learning in the educational environment opens a number of opportunities for the optimization of the teaching process and the improvement of the results of training in STEM subjects\. In this work, we propose a comprehensive application\-oriented machine learning framework to predict student academic achievement and apply personalized interventions in STEM education\. With the help of a well\-crafted dataset consisting of records of academic and behavioral performance of 2,500 undergraduate students for three consecutive academic years, we design and validate a hybrid ensemble approach which uses a combination of Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms\. The framework reaches the level of prediction accuracy of 94\.2% in detecting at\-risk students and an AUC\-ROC value of 0\.972\. Our method outperforms all individual base models\. Apart from the predictive task, our framework offers the use of an adaptive recommendation engine suggesting personalized educational resources to students\. The proposed framework operates in the form of web\-based analytics dashboard for educators\. This work highlights how machine learning approaches can be successfully utilized in educational practice, thus bridging the gap between research in education and practical applications of educational technologies\.

## [EFFICIENT DEEP LEARNING FOR CHAGAS CARDIOMYOPATHYDETECTION: DATA\-DRIVEN ECG FEATURE REDUCTION](../publications/871b3b6b0edded027d9c.md)

Ahmed Faeq Hussein; Auns Qusai Al\-Neami; Qais Ahmed Habash

Chagas cardiomyopathy, a severe complication of chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection,requires early and efficient diagnosis to improve outcomes\. While electrocardiograms \(ECGs\) areaccessible diagnostic tools, their high dimensionality limits the scalability of deep learning methods\. Thisstudy proposes an interpretable and computationally efficient deep learning pipeline combining PrincipalComponent Analysis \(PCA\) for feature reduction and a Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) forclassification of ECG signals\.Using data from the publicly available SaMi\-Trop cohort, the ECG signals were preprocessed witha Butterworth high\-pass filter to remove baseline wander, followed by PCA to reduce feature space whilepreserving critical variance\. A custom CNN was then trained on the reduced feature set to classify signalsas Chagas or non\-Chagas\.The PCA\+CNN model achieved 95\.52% sensitivity, 91\.11% specificity, 93\.31% accuracy, and anAUC of 96\.78%, outperforming the baseline CNN trained on unreduced data\. The approach reducedoverfitting, improved generalization, and accelerated convergence, demonstrating strong potential for usein real\-time and low\-resource healthcare settings\.

## [An integrated AI\-based software architecture for load forecasting, controlled anomaly detection, and predictive energy management](../publications/871cf195e79000cdca8e.md)

Karlygash Alibekkyzy; Gulnur Massabayeva; Michal Majka; Мадина Базарова; Daniyar Kaliyev; Талшын Керибаева; Saule Askerbekovna Belginova; Alina Bugubayeva

The increasing deployment of smart meters and Internet of Things technologies has created a demand for intelligent computational systems capable of jointly forecasting electricity consumption, detecting abnormal behavior, and optimizing load management\. This study proposes an integrated artificial intelligence\-based framework for automated energy metering and consumption management in smart\-grid environments\. The framework combines a Long Short\-Term Memory network for short\-term load forecasting, an autoencoder\-based model for anomaly detection, and Model Predictive Control for demand\-side optimization\. The system architecture includes data acquisition, communication, preprocessing, predictive analytics, anomaly monitoring, and decision\-support layers\. The primary empirical evaluation used 4,380 measured hourly observations \(approximately 6 months\) from a single administrative building\. A separately flagged synthetic temporal extension was retained only as an auxiliary dataset and was excluded from all primary performance metrics\. Across five independent model initializations, the final LSTM achieved a MAPE of 3\.423 ± 0\.555%, an RMSE of 0\.336 ± 0\.048 kW, and an R 2 of 0\.973 ± 0\.007 on the 633\-sequence independent measured test subset\. The synthetic extension was maintained as a separately identified auxiliary component and was excluded from all primary training, validation, and independent test metrics\. Using a validation\-selected reconstruction\-error threshold, the autoencoder detected 12 of 30 controlled anomalies in the independent test subset, yielding 100\.00% precision, 40\.00% recall, and an F1\-score of 57\.14%\. Under the same controlled protocol, One\-Class SVM achieved higher recall \(53\.33%\) and F1\-score \(69\.57%\), indicating that the autoencoder should be interpreted as an architectural component rather than as the best\-performing anomaly detector for the present dataset\. A historical proof\-of\-concept MPC simulation, retained for architectural illustration, reported a 15% reduction in simulated peak demand and a 12% reduction in estimated electricity cost; these values are not interpreted as measured outcomes from the administrative\-building experiment\. Controlled anomaly injection was used to establish reproducible validation and test labels for the anomaly\-detection component\. The results demonstrate that the joint integration of forecasting, anomaly detection, and predictive control provides a computationally coherent framework for supporting energy\-management efficiency, operational reliability, and data\-driven decision\-making in intelligent energy systems\.

## [Development and validation of the AI literacy questionnaire for health professions students using Rasch analysis](../publications/871da22e24703ed4a809.md)

Yue Li; Qin Ye; Wei Qin; Ning Liu

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is reshaping healthcare and creating new competency requirements for health professionals\. However, assessment instruments tailored to this population remain limited, and item\-level measurement evidence is scarce\. This study aimed to develop and validate an AI literacy scale \(AILS\) for health professions students using an integrated theoretical framework\. The item pool was informed by UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Students, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge model, the Kirkpatrick evaluation model, a literature review, and qualitative interviews\. Items were refined through Delphi method, content validation, and pilot testing\. Data were collected from 473 students\. The sample was divided into two subsamples for exploratory factor analysis \( n = 241\) and confirmatory factor analysis with Rasch rating scale analysis \( n = 232\)\. The final 33\-item AILS comprised four dimensions: Technical Understanding, Ethical Awareness, Practical Ability, and Social Impact\. The four\-factor solution explained 63\.676% of the total variance\. The total scale demonstrated high internal consistency \(Cronbach’s α = 0\.979\), and CFA showed acceptable model fit \(χ²/df = 2\.175, IFI = 0\.917, TLI = 0\.908, CFI = 0\.916, and RMSEA = 0\.071\)\. In the Rasch analysis, person and item reliabilities were 0\.96 and 0\.95, respectively\. The person–item map showed that the mean person measure was 1\.66 logits above the mean item difficulty of 0\.00 logits, indicating limited upper\-end targeting\. This mismatch may reflect insufficiently difficult items, sample characteristics, previous AI experience, limited curricular emphasis on advanced competencies, or a combination of these factors\. The AILS demonstrated evidence of validity and reliability for assessing AI literacy among health professions students\. The combined use of factor analysis and Rasch measurement illustrates the potential value of Rasch analysis for evaluating item functioning and person–item targeting\. The current scale appears better suited to group\-level assessment of foundational and intermediate AI literacy than to distinguishing advanced competence\. Further research should develop more challenging items and validate the AILS in independent, multicentre samples\. Application in other professional education domains would require discipline\-specific adaptation and validation\.

## [Initial Development and Content Validity of an Occupation\-Focused Assessment: Occupations in Higher Education Transitions Inventory](../publications/871e46edfdcb2d45af62.md)

Karen M\. Keptner; Rachel Rogers; Alyssa Chandler Lee; Daniel Martin

University students face occupational disruption during post\-secondary transitions, yet existing campus screening tools leave occupational challenges largely unassessed\. No comprehensive, occupation\-focused screening instrument exists for this population\. To describe the theoretical development and content validation of the Occupations in Higher Education Transitions Inventory \( OHETI \), a screening tool assessing university student adaptation across 10 domains of occupation grounded in the Theory of Occupational Adaptation \(OA\) a five\-phase iterative development process was used: \(a\) initial item generation; \(b\) preliminary expert review for face validity \( N = 3 occupational therapists with expertise in OA theory\); \(c\) tool reconceptualization based on expert feedback; \(d\) cognitive interviews with undergraduate students for face validity and comprehensibility \( N = 10\); and \(e\) formal content validation using a Content Validity Index \(CVI\) rating procedure with \( N = 6\) occupational therapy professionals with clinical and academic experience with emerging adult students\. Initial item generation yielded 68 items across seven OA constructs\. Expert feedback prompted a fundamental restructuring, producing 116 items across 10 occupations, covering aspects of relative mastery: satisfaction, effectiveness, and efficiency\. Revision based on student cognitive interviews resulted in 122 items\. Formal content validation produced I\-CVI scores ranging from 0\.667 to 1\.0, with S\-CVI scores of 0\.9516 for clarity and 0\.9435 for relevance\. Two items were removed, resulting in a final tool of 120 scorable items across 10 occupations\. The OHETI demonstrates strong content and face validity as a theoretically grounded, occupation\-focused screening tool for university students\. Online administration and individualized feedback distinguish it from existing instruments\. Psychometric validation is needed before broad implementation\.

## [Hydro Digital Twins for Coastal Governance: A Scoping Review of Objectives, Data Characteristics, and Maturity](../publications/872063bdb201a7da79f8.md)

Letizia Artioli; Giovanni Borga; Pietro Costa; Federica D’Acunto; Filippo Iodice

Coastal zones and their connected freshwater and marine systems are among the environments most acutely exposed to accelerating climate hazards\. European policy has responded by placing Digital Twin \(DT\) infrastructures at the centre of its climate adaptation and ocean governance agenda: Destination Earth for the Earth system, and the European Digital Twin of the Ocean \(EDITO\) for the marine and coastal domain\. This scoping review defines and evaluates Hydro Digital Twins \(HDTs\), encompassing Digital Twins of the Ocean \(DTOs\), coastal\-zone DTs, and freshwater\-system DTs, as instruments for coastal management, water territory governance, and climate adaptation decision support\. Conducted in accordance with PRISMA\-ScR, the review screened 231 records \(January 2020 to September 2025\) and retained 21 studies, each coded against a thirteen\-parameter framework organised on a governance axis and a data\-centric axis\. Governance objectives consistently outweigh technical motivations: risk reduction dominates \(7/21 studies, 33%\), followed by environmental monitoring \(5/21 studies, 24%\) and coastal management \(4/21 studies, 19%\)\. Remote sensing is used in 19/21 studies \(90%\) as the near\-universal data backbone; artificial intelligence, coded as an analytical method rather than a data source, appears in 10/21 studies \(48%\) and concentrates in the River/Lakes domain \(6/7 studies, 86%\), which also holds three of the four predictive outputs; citizen science data, though a stated European policy priority, appears operationally in only 2/21 studies \(10%\)\. The modal maturity category is TRL 4–5 \(6/21 studies, 29%\), only one study reaches TRL 6, and 6/21 studies \(29%\) report no formal validation\. The review clarifies the architectural distinction between HDTs and Web GIS and situates these findings within the European coastal governance agendas of Destination Earth and EDITO\. All proportions above are properties of the reviewed corpus and are not extrapolated to the HDT field as a whole\.

## [Validation of a MALDI Intact Cell Mass Spectrometry Workflow for Routine Application in Monitoring Industrial E\. coli Fermentations](../publications/872cbc3c8476bd7f47eb.md)

Cristian Zanetti; Christopher Stephan; Rudolf Bednar; Alexandra Foettinger‐Vacha; Martina Marchetti‐Deschmann

Today, matrix\-assisted laser desorption/ionization\-intact cell mass spectrometry \(MALDI\-ICMS\) is used in clinical environments for rapid pathogen identification, referred to as MALDI biotyping\. This method relies on the generation of characteristic mass spectrometric profiles of intact microorganisms\. Single\-celled organisms are often used for pharmaceutical production, while this allows for the production of complex products, close monitoring and control of these processes is essential\. In this study, we propose the use of MALDI\-ICMS as a potential at\-line approach for fast monitoring of the progress of a biotechnologically relevant fermentation process employing E\. coli as a host\. We demonstrate the reproducibility of the method, thereby indicating its potential to predict the progress of antibody fragment production in E\. coli in an industrial setting\. We evaluated various aspects of sample preparation, including the choice of matrix and solvent concentration, sample loading, and sample\-to\-matrix ratios\. Our workflow allowed monitoring of over 100 signals across a 32\-h span of E\. coli fermentation\. To control instrumental variability, we performed eight technical replicates and achieved excellent repeatability, with 9% median relative standard deviation of peak intensities\. Principal component analysis revealed strong time\-related differences of the mass spectra, allowing to differentiate the data based on fermentation phases\. Furthermore, to assess direct monitoring of product expression, we adapted acquisition parameters to enable product detection via MALDI\-ICMS\. The presented MALDI\-ICMS workflow allowed reliable monitoring of cellular changes during fermentation, thereby expanding the applications of MALDI\-ICMS to process analytical technologies \(PAT\)\.

## [Decoding Naturalistic Speech from fMRI with Temporal Modeling and Multimodal Alignment](../publications/873d343987a1f00153d1.md)

Corentin Caris; Louis Jalouzot; Nona Rajabi; Géraud Ilinca; Ahmed Hassayoune; Asilbek Muminov; Thaddée Delebarre; Clara Fonteneau; Charles Maussion; Bertrand Thirion; Alexis Thual; Antoine Collas

Reconstructing what a person perceives from their brain activity is a stringent test of whether neural recordings carry meaningful information\. Naturalistic speech offers a rich testbed for this challenge: it unfolds over multiple timescales, but fMRI&\#x27;s noisy, temporally smeared measurements make this structure hard to recover\. We introduce NOEMA, a temporal convolutional decoder that aligns windows of consecutive fMRI measurements with multimodal stimulus embeddings\. These embeddings combine complementary text, audio, and speech representations of the same stimulus segment, enabling its retrieval directly from brain activity\. On two naturalistic speech datasets, Cephalonauts One and LeBel, NOEMA retrieves the correct segment among 2,000 candidates within the top 10 for more than 42% of held\-out queries\. This substantially outperforms baseline decoders, an advantage that persists when the candidate pool is extended with thousands of distractors absent from training\. Controlled ablations establish the contributions of temporal modeling and complementary stimulus representations\.

## [Fostering belonging and engagement in inclusive chemistry classrooms: teachers’ experiences through a universal design for learning framework](../publications/874051e322f7b0a90bc7.md)

Jamil Suprihatiningrum; Fradhika Maulidina

Engagement and a sense of belonging are essential to inclusive education, particularly for students with education needs and disabilities \(SEND\) in chemistry classrooms\. This study investigates how secondary school chemistry teachers in Indonesia apply the Multiple Means of Engagement \(MME\) principle of the Universal Design for Learning \(UDL\) framework to enhance participation and inclusion for students with SEND\. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, data were gathered through in\-depth interviews with 11 experienced chemistry teachers and were analyzed thematically\. The findings reveal that teachers adopted strategies such as offering task choices, integrating culturally relevant contexts, providing affirming feedback, and encouraging self\-reflection\. These practices were perceived to strengthen students’ motivation, participation, and sense of belonging\. Nonetheless, implementation was uneven, constrained by limited conceptual understanding and institutional barriers\. The study concludes that UDL\-informed engagement strategies have the potential to foster both cognitive and affective inclusion and highlights the importance of professional development that bridges global pedagogical theory with local classroom realities\.

## [Python Using GPT\-5 and Gemini](../publications/87484ad804baed449e8f.md)

Oswald Campesato

Python Using GPT‑5 and Gemini provides a practical, up‑to‑date guide that combines solid Python programming skills with real‑world integration of today’s leading large language models \(LLMs\)\. This book teaches essential Python techniques while showing readers exactly how to connect and use GPT‑5, Google Gemini, Claude, Grok, Perplexity, and other major 2026 models in their daily work\. Readers will gain a strong foundation in Python data structures, comprehensions, generators, regular expressions, and object‑oriented programming\. This book then moves into detailed coverage of GPT‑5 \(including GPT‑5\.4 and GPT‑5\.3 Instant\), Gemini 3\.1, Claude Mythos, and Opus 4\.6, along with practical Python code samples for chatbots, tool calling, data analysis, graphics generation, and integration with PowerPoint and Excel\. Additional chapters explore LLM benchmarks, deceptive behaviors such as alignment faking and scheming, military AI applications, and comparisons between the major models, giving readers clear insight into their relative strengths and limitations\. This book is written for intermediate Python developers, data scientists, technical professionals, and anyone who wants to move beyond basic prompting and build production‑ready applications that effectively combine Python with the latest generation of LLMs\.

The main challenges were the high investment costs, shortage of skilled labor, data privacy and security, and organizational resistance to change

## [How Do Mutual Funds Respond to Salient Pollution Events?](../publications/877e841f810c6379cea5.md)

Han Zhou; Daniel Chai; H Neef; Jin Zhang

ABSTRACT We examine how salient chemical spill incidents influence mutual fund portfolio allocations\. Using a sample of 36 major chemical spills between 2000 and 2019, we find that funds located in the same designated market area as a spill increase their portfolio ESG scores in the year following the incident, primarily by divesting from low‐ESG firms\. This response is particularly pronounced for funds with a higher share of socially responsible investors and for funds located in Democratic‐leaning counties and regions with stronger pro‐environmental attitudes\. ## [Artificial Intelligence Applications in Poultry Production: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Implications for Afghanistan](../publications/8782497955d0a6721e7c.md)

Abdul Khaliq Sahes; Abdul Ghafoor Muradi; Lutfullah Zaheri; Abdul Jamil Ghanizada

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly being investigated as a tool for improving poultry production, health monitoring, environmental management, and farm automation\. This narrative review synthesizes scientific evidence on AI applications in poultry production and evaluates their potential applicability, infrastructure requirements, limitations, and future opportunities in Afghanistan\. Literature was searched using Google Scholar, Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, IranMedex, and Magiran using terms related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, poultry production, disease detection, computer vision, Internet of Things, robotics, animal welfare, and Afghanistan\. The initial search identified 66 potentially relevant records, and 30 publications were included in the narrative synthesis after screening and eligibility assessment\. Current evidence indicates that AI can support early disease and abnormal\-behavior detection, environmental monitoring, precision management of feed and production, and robotic farm operations\. However, successful implementation depends on data quality, reliable electricity and connectivity, suitable sensors and computing infrastructure, technical expertise, and economic feasibility\. Importantly, the available literature does not provide sufficient evidence to conclude that AI is already widely adopted in Afghanistan’s commercial poultry sector\. Therefore, AI adoption in Afghanistan should be approached through locally validated, gradual, and economically appropriate applications, beginning with digital record keeping, environmental sensing, computer\-vision monitoring, and decision\-support systems\. Future studies should evaluate these technologies under real Afghan poultry\-farming conditions\.

## [Performing Interpretation](../publications/8793d6382f0c3008a4ea.md)

Abimbola Alao; Erika Katjaana Sarivaara; Satu Uusiautti; Syed Fahad Javaid

This study explores how art\-based research \(ABR\) can be used to raise awareness of front temporal dementia \(FTD\) in the United Kingdom\. Although drama is often used as a tool for dissemination in health\-related research, its potential as a method of interpretation remains underdeveloped\. In this study, the art\-based method was used to create a narrative, a play called “My Name is Beatrice,” based on autoethnographic conversations and observations and desk\-based research\. First, the data from observations and conversations, together with findings from desk\-based research, were analysed using narrative analysis to develop an understanding of the essential components ethnodrama should encompass\. This analysis resulted in the creation of a play\. Second, a narrative analysis was conducted, focusing on the structure of the play\. This analysis examines the play’s construction and central findings through key dramatic elements\. In this article, ethnodrama is positioned as an analytic tool that highlights cultural silence, stigma, and misdiagnosis while offering new ways of engaging communities and professionals in dialogue about FTD\. The intersection of culture, dementia, and the arts highlighted in this study highlights the need for interdisciplinary approaches to dementia research\. Photo: John Alao

## [Digital insurance adoption and financial inclusion among urban consumers in Chennai: Mediating effects of awareness, digital literacy, and trust](../publications/879c810878bc3eef0d38.md)

Sherin Amala; Poornima A\. S\.

Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractInsurance penetration in India remains critically low \(2\.7 per cent life, 1\.0 per cent general\) despite two decades of market liberalization and substantial digital infrastructure expansion\. This study investigates how insurance awareness and digital literacy translate into digital insurance adoption among Chennai&\#x27;s urban consumers, with perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust as cognitive and relational pathways linking capability to market action\. Data were collected in August\-September 2024 from 405 purposively sampled consumers with digital device access, comprising existing insurance holders and potential first\-time buyers, using a structured questionnaire\. Chennai, a theoretically relevant research setting with mature digital infrastructure and diverse urban demographics, allows perceptual and informational barriers to be examined independently of connectivity constraints, offering transferable insights for comparable Indian urban markets\. Structural equation modeling showed excellent measurement model fit across standard indices, explaining 50\.2 per cent of adoption intention variance\. Awareness was the strongest predictor of perceived ease of use \(β = 0\.758, R2 = 57\.5 per cent\) and digital literacy of perceived usefulness \(β = 0\.752, R2 = 56\.5 per cent\)\. Both influenced adoption intention entirely through their respective mediators without significant direct effects, consistent with complete statistical mediation\. Trust added serial mediation pathways, reinforcing the role of institutional confidence in credence good markets\. Awareness campaigns and literacy programs yield negligible adoption gains unless designed to strengthen perceived platform utility and navigability\. Insurers and policymakers should prioritize interface design optimizing functional value and operational ease, with transparent claims processes converting platform confidence into durable institutional trust\.AcknowledgmentsThe authors used an AI language tool \(Claude, Anthropic\) for assistance with language editing, readability improvement, and proofreading of this manuscript\. ## [Compressing multivariate functions with tree tensor networks](../publications/87a55e29febfacef65c7.md)

Joseph Tindall; Miles Stoudenmire; Ryan Levy

Tensor networks are a compressed format for multi\-dimensional data\. One dimensional tensor networks—often referred to as tensor trains \(TT\) or matrix product states \(MPS\)—are increasingly being used as a numerical Ansatz for continuum functions by \`\`quantizing’’ the inputs into discrete binary digits\. Here we demonstrate the power of more general tree tensor networks \(TTNs\) for this purpose\. We provide direct constructions of a number of elementary functions as generic tree tensor networks and interpolative constructions for more complicated functions via a generalization of the tensor cross interpolation algorithm\. For a range of multi\-dimensional functions we show how more structured tree tensor networks offer a significantly more efficient Ansatz than the commonly used tensor train\. Finally, we demonstrate how the methods introduced in this work can be used to realize a TTN\-based solver for multi\-dimensional, non\-linear Fredholm equations\.
