BACKGROUND: Mild cognitive impairment is common among older adults and a significant risk factor for future dementia\. Cognitive stimulation activities may help promote and maintain cognitive function and delay cognitive decline\. OBJECTIVES: To compare cognitive function scores among older adults with mild cognitive impairment before intervention baseline, after a 2\-week intervention, and at 3\- and 6\-month follow\-ups\. METHODS: This quasi\-experimental study used a one\-group pretest\-posttest design with long\-term follow\-up\. The sample included 30 older adults with mild cognitive impairment from the catchment area of Phai Lom Sub\-district Health Promoting Hospital, Lap Lae District, Uttaradit Province, who met the inclusion criteria assessed by the MoCA, TGDS\-15, and ADL scales\. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the MMSE\-Thai 2002 to assess cognitive function\. The cognitive stimulation program &quot;Challenge Your Mind,&quot; developed based on the concept of Spector et al\., covered all six cognitive domains and was delivered over 2 weeks, 3 times per week, with 45\-60 minutes per session\. Data were analyzed using repeated\-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni\-corrected post hoc tests\. RESULTS: Cognitive function scores differed significantly across time points \(F=28\.64, p&lt;0\.001\)\. Mean scores rose from 16\.8±3\.4 at baseline to 21\.3±3\.8 after the 2\-week intervention and remained significantly higher than baseline at the 3\-month \(20\.7±3\.9\) and 6\-month \(19\.9±4\.1\) follow\-ups\. The program demonstrated a large effect size \(partial eta squared=0\.50\)\. CONCLUSIONS: The &quot;Tha Khwam Khit&quot; \(Challenge Your Mind\) program effectively improved and sustained cognitive function among older adults with mild cognitive impairment for up to 6 months\. It can be applied in healthcare settings and communities to prevent and delay dementia\. However, because this study used a one\-group pretest\-posttest design without a control group, along with purposive sampling and a relatively small sample size, further studies with a control group and larger sample size are warranted to confirm the effectiveness of this innovation before broader application\.

## [A Closed Form Depth\-Width Law for Neural Collapse in Deep Linear Networks](../publications/87ac70cc148c084361da.md)

Pankhil Gawade; Kirsten Fischer; Guy Wolf; Ewa Szczurek

How depth and width of neural networks shape learned representations is usually studied only after training\. We show that, in a tractable feature\-learning setting, this dependence can instead be obtained in closed form\. Using neural collapse as a probe of representation geometry, we express NC1\-\-NC3 directly in terms of the learned feature kernel, extending an identity known for NC1 to the angular part of NC2 and to NC3 under a ridge readout\. For deep linear networks with exchangeable class structure, the resulting kernel equations yield a geometric law, exact within the theory, for the layerwise evolution of within\-class variability\. At large width, the accumulated compression becomes a function of the depth\-to\-width ratio $L/N$, with its rate determined self\-consistently by the data, prior and architecture\. Numerical experiments support the derived dependence on depth, width and signal\-to\-noise ratio\. The result is a representation\-level scaling law derived from feature\-learning theory rather than fitted after training\.

## [Traumatismo Cranioencefálico: Papel da Tomografia Computadorizada no Diagnóstico e Avaliação da Gravidade](../publications/87bc1e3fa860020d04b3.md)

Marcela Lorany Facundo de Oliveira; Polyana Milani Guerra; Lucas Padovan Lira; Helen Rocha de Morais Gonçalves; Heloisa Antonelli; Dirsse Asteria Antezana Gonzales; Fabrício Augusto Pedrão de Almeida Prado; Paulo Victor Gomes Ramos; Matheus Claudino de Morais; Ana Hecktheuer Canzi; MARIA EDUARDA DOS SANTOS SOARES; Flávio Junior Silveira Ribeiro; Thiago Pessini Kempa; Ávila Beatriz Pontes Soeiro; Júlia Mendonça

Introdução: O traumatismo cranioencefálico \(TCE\) constitui importante causa de mortalidade e incapacidade, podendo provocar lesões intracranianas de diferentes magnitudes\. A avaliação inicial deve integrar exame neurológico, Escala de Coma de Glasgow e métodos de imagem\. Nesse contexto, a tomografia computadorizada \(TC\) de crânio apresenta papel central na identificação rápida de alterações potencialmente graves e na definição da conduta\. Objetivo: Analisar a importância da TC de crânio no diagnóstico do TCE e na identificação de achados associados à gravidade e ao prognóstico\. Metodologia: Foi realizada revisão narrativa nas bases PubMed, SciELO e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde \(BVS\), priorizando diretrizes da Sociedade Brasileira de Neurocirurgia, Ministério da Saúde, Brain Trauma Foundation e NICE, além de estudos relevantes sobre neuroimagem e prognóstico no TCE\. Discussão/Resultados: A TC é o principal exame de imagem na investigação inicial de pacientes com suspeita de lesão cerebral traumática clinicamente significativa, devido à rapidez e à capacidade de demonstrar hemorragias, fraturas, contusões, edema e efeito de massa\. A indicação deve considerar dados clínicos, evitando exposição desnecessária à radiação, especialmente nos casos de TCE leve\. Entre os achados relacionados à maior gravidade destacam\-se hematomas intracranianos, hemorragia subaracnoidea traumática, desvio da linha média, compressão ou ausência das cisternas basais e sinais de herniação\. Esses parâmetros auxiliam na estratificação prognóstica e na identificação de pacientes que podem necessitar de abordagem neurocirúrgica ou monitorização intensiva\. Em pacientes com TCE grave, alterações tomográficas também contribuem para decisões relacionadas ao monitoramento da pressão intracraniana\. A ressonância magnética possui utilidade complementar, sobretudo quando há necessidade de caracterizar lesões não evidenciadas adequadamente pela TC, mas não substitui o exame tomográfico como investigação inicial\. Conclusão: A TC de crânio permanece fundamental na avaliação inicial do TCE, permitindo diagnóstico rápido, identificação de lesões potencialmente ameaçadoras e melhor estratificação da gravidade\. Sua utilização deve ser orientada por critérios clínicos e protocolos validados, integrando os achados de imagem à avaliação neurológica\.

## [Case Report: Electroencephalography\-informed low\-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder](../publications/87cc5a4af40db3a15a2e.md)

Chiaki Takahashi; Takashi Asahi; 基生 神田; Yoshihiko Ohta; Isao Matsushita

Background Functional movement disorder \(FMD\) is increasingly being recognized as a condition associated with abnormal brain network connectivity; however, effective treatment strategies remain limited\. Methods We report the case of a patient with severe FMD that developed following an occupational injury and was characterized by functional tremors accompanied by migraines and prominent autonomic symptoms\. Based on electroencephalography \(EEG\) network analysis, low\-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area was administered, followed by staged rehabilitation incorporating visual feedback\. Results The combined intervention reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity\. Conclusion This case highlights the potential utility of combining EEG\-guided neuromodulation with staged rehabilitation for the treatment of FMD and supports further investigation of this approach\.

## [Responsible AI Governance as an Organisational Capability: A Theory\-Building Integrative Review for Sustainable Organisations](../publications/87ce5653bf7b9cc7dc2c.md)

Amlan Haque

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly embedded in organisational decision\-making, creating opportunities for innovation and sustainability while intensifying concerns about accountability, transparency, stakeholder responsibility and human oversight\. This structured theory\-building integrative review synthesises a purposively bounded corpus of 35 unique works on responsible AI, AI governance, responsible leadership and organisational sustainability\. Responsible AI Governance \(RAIG\) is conceptualised as a multidimensional organisational capability: the repeatable, coordinated and adaptive capacity through which responsible AI principles are translated into governance structures, decision processes, accountability arrangements, stakeholder relationships, human oversight and assurance across the AI lifecycle\. Six interdependent dimensions are specified: ethical\-strategic alignment, accountability architecture, human oversight and agency, stakeholder inclusion, transparency and assurance and lifecycle governance and adaptability\. Responsible leadership is positioned as an antecedent managerial microfoundation rather than a constitutive dimension of RAIG\. The framework separates sustainability from the content of RAIG and theorises sustainable organisational and stakeholder outcomes as consequences of effective governance\. Propositions and a staged research programme establish a foundation for construct operationalisation, cross\-context validation and subsequent nomological testing\.

## [The Impact of English Borrowings on Modern French: Lexical, Grammatical, and Stylistic Perspectives \(Based on Mass Media Materials\)](../publications/87e2c8caf700e2c73692.md)

Ilaha Ashrafova; Sadagat Rasulova; Remziyye Esgerova; Намик Аббасов; Arif Zeynalov

This study examines the integration of English borrowings into contemporary French media discourse, focusing on their lexical, grammatical, and stylistic functioning across different media platforms\. Drawing on a structured corpus of 120 media texts published between 2011 and 2025, including print newspapers, television broadcasts, digital news platforms, and social networks\. The analysis combines qualitative content analysis with quantitative frequency and grammatical assessment\. The results demonstrate that Anglicisms constitute a stable and functionally differentiated layer of modern French media language\. Fully adapted borrowings account for 37% of the corpus, partially adapted forms for 34%, and non\-adapted items for 29%, with clear variation depending on the institutional status and communicative purpose of the medium\. Grammatical integration is manifested through systematic gender assignment \(predominantly masculine\), plural formation according to French norms, and high derivational productivity, particularly in digital and youth\-oriented discourse \(e\.g\., liker, tweeter, booster\)\. Stylistically, Anglicisms serve distinct functions: terminological precision in print and television media, and identity construction, expressiveness, and irony in online platforms and social networks\. The findings indicate that English borrowings do not undermine the structural integrity of French but interact dynamically with its grammatical and stylistic systems, contributing to lexical innovation and media\-driven language change\. The study highlights the central role of media environments in regulating the degree of adaptation of borrowings and offers insights relevant to media linguistics, sociolinguistics, and the analysis of language change under conditions of globalisation\.

## [Sustainable Competitive Intelligence for Inclusive School Readiness: An Educational Intelligence Framework for Children with Disabilities](../publications/87feaad2c2ce3433c8a1.md)

Jiatong Liu; Khairul Farhah Khairuddin; Nurul Khairani Ismail

Purpose: This review explores the ways in which teachers use observations, assessments, family knowledge, and service records to interpret and form educational intelligence for making judgments and providing support to children with disabilities regarding school readiness\. Methodology/approach: Using a structured integrative design, the review synthesized 34 peer\-reviewed articles published between 2020 and 2025\. Sources were located through targeted searches and citation chaining, then checked against publisher records and DOI metadata\. Evidence was coded by readiness domain, intelligence\-cycle stage, source, decision use, organizational condition, and ethical safeguard\. Originality/Relevance: The article adapts competitive\-intelligence logic to inclusive early childhood education without treating children or schools as competitors\. Educational intelligence is framed as an ethical capacity to scan signals, triangulate evidence, interpret uncertainty, coordinate action, and learn from outcomes\. Key findings: Useful intelligence comes when one integrates the process of observing with developmentally appropriate assessment, family voice, a multidisciplinary approach and contextual information\. Data, by themselves, do not lead to better decisions\. Teacher data literacy, team structures and workflows, data records, organizational structures and supports, and mitigations against deficit labeling, surveillance, and inaccurate precision are all key factors in quality\. Theoretical/methodological contributions: The review outlines an Inclusive Educational Intelligence Cycle and six propositions relating to scanning breadth, triangulation, interpretive competence, family engagement, organisational learning and ethical governance with readiness support\. It also outlines a research agenda focused on access, inclusion and responsible decision\-making\.

## [Legitimation Strategies in Trump’s Venezuela Post\-Operation Address Through Illocutionary Speech Acts Analysis](../publications/88091c0134fb206500bb.md)

Yasir Mubarok; Sabri Koebanu

This study examines how political legitimacy is constructed through illocutionary speech acts in President Donald Trump’s address following the U\.S\. military operation against Venezuela\. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach with a single\-case study design, the study analyzes a 58\-minute\-and\-41\-second presidential address comprising 295 clauses\. The analysis integrates Searle’s \(1979\) classification of illocutionary speech acts and van Leeuwen’s \(2007\) framework of legitimation strategies\. The findings reveal that assertive speech acts dominate \(69\.8%\), followed by expressive \(14\.2%\), commissive \(12\.5%\), directive \(2\.4%\), and declarative \(1\.0%\) acts\. Assertive acts primarily construct the official narrative of the operation by presenting claims about military achievements, security threats, and operational effectiveness as factual accounts\. These utterances contribute to rationalization by portraying military intervention as necessary, successful, and strategically justified\. Authorization is established through references to presidential and institutional authority, while moral evaluation emerges through negative representations of opponents and positive portrayals of American actions\. Mythopoesis appears less prominently, mainly through warnings emphasizing the consequences of resistance\. Commissive acts further reinforce legitimacy by projecting commitments to national security and political stability\. The findings demonstrate that political legitimacy is discursively constructed through the interaction of different illocutionary functions and legitimation strategies\. This study contributes to political pragmatics by explaining how micro\-level speech acts support broader strategies of political legitimation in presidential discourse concerning military intervention\.

## [A double inertial method for non\-monotone variational inequality problem](../publications/8810d10db36df1f5191f.md)

Olayinka Martins Onifade; Austine Efut Ofem; S\. A\. Kajola; Chinedu Izuchukwu; Ojen Kumar Narain

Abstract In this paper, we propose a viscosity\-type double inertial algorithm with self\-adaptive stepsizes for solving non\-monotone variational inequality problems involving uniformly continuous operators in real Hilbert spaces\. The proposed method combines viscosity approximation and double inertial extrapolation techniques with a self\-adaptive stepsize rule that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant\. Under suitable conditions, we establish a strong convergence of the generated sequence without assuming monotonicity, Lipschitz continuity, line\-search procedures, or additional projection techniques\. The obtained results extend several existing inertial and viscosity methods to a broader class of non\-monotone and non\-Lipschitz variational inequality problems\. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm\.

## [A Case Study of Medical School Leadership Perceptions and Experiences in Implementing Academic Support Services for Students](../publications/883575fef05cdd3d4825.md)

Elda Martinez Muller

The purpose of this qualitative case study was to understand the perceptions and experiences of medical school leadership regarding the implementation of academic support services at a medical university in the Southeastern United States\. The study was guided by the central research question: How did medical school leaders perceive and experience the implementation of academic support services for students within their institutions? Servant Leadership Theory \(Greenleaf, 1970, 1977\) provided the theoretical framework, emphasizing the leader’s responsibility to serve first, prioritizing the growth, development, and well\-being of others while fostering shared decision\-making and a culture of care\. This framework offered a lens through which to examine how medical school leaders approached academic support in ways that promoted student flourishing and aligned with institutional missions\. The study employed a qualitative case study design \(Stake, 1995\)\. Participants were selected through purposeful criterion sampling, identifying medical school leaders with direct roles or experience in the development or implementation of academic support services\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews, observations, surveys, and document analysis to ensure data triangulation and strengthen the study’s credibility and trustworthiness\. Data analysis followed thematic procedures guided by Yin \(2018\), Moustakas \(1994\), and Creswell and Poth \(2024\), integrating multiple perspectives to identify patterns and insights into leadership practices and decision\-making processes\.

## [Structure based\-molecular modeling and pharmacokinetic investigation of Caesalpinia sappan L\. against obesity and hypothyroidism](../publications/8840d0b19c6d1161e0b6.md)

Pritha Raji Ayyanar; Azar Zochedh; Jyothi Kanagaraj

In the present study, an integrated in silico approach was employed to investigate phytocompounds from Caesalpinia sappan in the context of their predicted interaction with LepR\. Molecular docking was performed using a SWISS\-MODEL\-generated human LepR homology model based on the UniProt sequence \(ID: P48357\)\. Among the screened phytocompounds, lupeol exhibited the most favorable predicted docking affinity \(−9\.4 kcal/mol\) and was therefore selected for further computational characterization\. The predicted binding mode indicated predominantly hydrophobic/alkyl interactions within the putative LepR binding pocket; however, the observed interactions did not involve the ideal/key residues, and therefore the docking results were interpreted as a predicted ligand–receptor association rather than evidence of receptor modulation\. DFT\-based frontier molecular orbital analysis yielded a HOMO–LUMO energy gap of 6\.998 eV, providing information on the electronic structure and theoretical reactivity of lupeol\. SwissADME and pkCSM analyses indicated a mixed drug\-likeness and ADMET profile, including high predicted lipophilicity and poor aqueous solubility, as well as model\-dependent differences in predicted intestinal absorption\. Overall, the findings identify lupeol as a computationally prioritized phytocompound for further investigation in the context of LepR\-associated metabolic research\. Experimental binding, cellular, and in vivo studies are needed to establish the biological relevance of the predicted interaction and assess its potential pharmacological significance in obesity and hypothyroidism\.

## [Unmanned aerial vehicle time‐series phenotyping illuminates genotype‐specific responses to off‐target dicamba exposure in soybean](../publications/8844d9cfcad4e3f08584.md)

Seda Ozer; Brian W\. Diers; Dean E\. Riechers; Caio Canella Vieira; Alper Adak

Abstract Dicamba, a synthetic auxin herbicide, is widely used for postemergence weed control\. However, the high potential for volatility and spray drift raises concerns about damage to nontarget dicot crops lacking the dicamba monooxygenase transgene, which provides bioengineered resistance\. Our objective was to evaluate the practical application of unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\)‐based multispectral imaging for quantifying off‐target dicamba injury, using non‐genetically modified \(GM\) soybean \( Glycine max \(L\.\) Merr\.\) genotypes with known tolerant \(T\) and sensitive \(S\) responses to provide a reference framework\. We conducted field experiments in 2021 and 2022 using varying dicamba rates\. Temporal visual injury estimates \(0–5 scale\) were recorded approximately every 5 days for 6–8 weeks\. Significant differences were detected between T and S lines, especially with 1/500 single and weekly repeated treatments, which provided the largest separation\. To augment the precision of visual injury assessment, UAV‐based multispectral imagery from each of multiple flights was used to calculate four vegetation indices \(VIs\): green leaf index \(GLI\), normalized excess green index \(ExG2\), normalized green red difference index \(NGRDI\), and red edge normalized difference vegetation index \(RENDVI\)\. These VIs captured differences between T and S lines, indicating dicamba injury can be quantified through remote sensing across contrasting soybean genotypes\. Strong negative correlations were observed between visual injury scores and VI scores across treatments at each flight date, with overall correlations for GLI, ExG2, NGRDI, and RENDVI being −0\.43, −0\.43, −0\.44, and −0\.39 in 2021 and −0\.54, −0\.54, −0\.64, and −0\.57 in 2022\. These results support the utility of UAV‐derived VIs for detecting and quantifying off‐target herbicide injury in soybean, facilitating scientific research efforts to develop non‐GM‐tolerant genotypes\.

## [Yijing Decoction improves oocyte quality and inhibits lactate accumulation in mice with diminished ovarian reserve](../publications/884a54f85a05689760ac.md)

Jiaqi Yang; Mengyuan Chu; Han Zhang; Wenman Meng; Chi Zhang; Yunfei Han; Genping Zeng; Qianyi Zhou; Xiaoyu Zhang; Fengrong Zhang; Ying Yan

Background Diminished ovarian reserve \(DOR\) is characterized by a decline in both oocyte quantity and quality, leading to compromised fertility\. Yijing Decoction \(YJD\) has demonstrated promising therapeutic potential in DOR management\. Nevertheless, the mechanisms driving this phenomenon are still largely unclear\. This study is designed to comprehensively assess the effects of YJD on ovarian reserve function and oocyte quality in DOR mice, while investigating its potential underlying mechanisms of action\. Methods A DOR mouse model was established by administering cyclophosphamide via a single intraperitoneal injection\. The therapeutic efficacy of YJD was systematically assessed through multiple functional and histological parameters, including ovarian index, estrous cycle regularity, serum sex hormone levels \(FSH, LH, E 2 , AMH, and INH\-B\), and follicle counts, as well as the number, quality, and spindle morphology of metaphase I \(MI\) oocytes\. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, ATP levels, pyruvate uptake, and lactate production were further quantified using commercially available ATP, pyruvate, and lactate assay kits\. Additionally, immunofluorescence microscopy was employed to assess the protein expression levels of glycolysis\-related proteins, including GLUT1, GLUT4, and LDHA, as well as components of the SIRT3/HIF\-1α/PDK1 signaling axis in MI oocytes\. Results YJD treatment improved ovarian reserve function and oocyte quality in DOR mice, as evidenced by increased ovulated oocyte numbers, improved spindle integrity, and restored ATP levels\. In addition, YJD treatment was associated with reduced expression of glycolysis\-related proteins, including GLUT1, GLUT4, and LDHA, as well as decreased pyruvate uptake and lactate production in MI oocytes\. YJD treatment also partially restored the expression pattern of the SIRT3/HIF\-1α/PDK1 signaling pathway in DOR oocytes\. Conclusion YJD improves oocyte quality in DOR mice, and its protective effects may be associated with the regulation of lactate metabolism and the SIRT3/HIF\-1α/PDK1 signaling pathway\.

## [When Words Are Not Enough: Emotional Spillovers from Fed Chair Communication to Global Financial Markets](../publications/8861882cac97eef1fec2.md)

Yiru Chen; Muhammad Ali Nasir; Xingjie Wei

Given the important role of the Federal Reserve Chair, their communications may generate substantial cross\-border effects on international financial markets\. Building on this perspective, this article investigates whether emotional signals conveyed by the Fed Chair during FOMC post\-meeting press conferences generate emotional spillovers to global financial markets\. Using press conferences held between 2011 and 2025, we construct multimodal emotional indices from textual, vocal, and facial cues using machine learning techniques, and examine their high\-frequency effects on exchange rates and equity markets across six major economies\. Using local projection methods with minute\-level event windows, the results show that Fed Chair emotional signals have immediate and economically significant impacts on global financial markets\. Among different modalities, facial and textual emotions exhibit stronger and more robust effects than vocal signals\. In particular, positive emotional cues are generally associated with increases in equity ETF returns, while exchange rate responses display substantial cross\-country heterogeneity, with emerging market currencies tending to appreciate\. We also provide evidence that the effects of emotional cues are non\-additive and depend on cross\-modal interactions, with vocal signals conditioning the impact of textual and facial emotions\. Moreover, the findings show that the transmission of emotional spillovers is shaped by macro\-financial vulnerability and global risk conditions\. On the one hand, economies with higher vulnerability exhibit stronger responses to emotional shocks, indicating that macro\-financial vulnerability acts as a moderating mechanism\. However, the effects of emotional signals, especially facial and textual emotion, are amplified during periods of higher global uncertainty\. Our main findings remain robust across several robustness checks\. In particular, for vocal and facial emotions, coefficient equality is not rejected in 85\.8% and 78\.3% of the market horizon comparisons, respectively, indicating that the main findings are not systematically driven by the choice of emotion extraction algorithms\.

## [Sustainability practices and customer loyalty in the insurance industry: A PLS\-SEM\-approach](../publications/88726a227b002c0808a1.md)

Alli Noah; John Aina; Kamal Ganiyu

This study examines the relationship between sustainability practices and customer loyalty in the Nigerian insurance industry, specifically investigating how perceptions of corporate social responsibility \(CSR\), environmental sustainability practices \(ESP\), and perceived ethical behavior \(PEB\) influence customer loyalty through the mediating role of customer trust\. A quantitative cross\-sectional survey design was employed with 700 insurance customers in Nigeria who had maintained active policies for at least three years\. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling \(PLS\-SEM\) with SmartPLS 4\.0 software\. The study tested a comprehensive theoretical model integrating stakeholder theory, social exchange theory, relationship marketing theory, and signaling theory\. The results provide strong empirical support for all hypothesized relationships\. Corporate social responsibility \(β = 0\.307, p &lt; 0\.001\), environmental sustainability practices \(β = 0\.238, p &lt; 0\.001\), and perceived ethical behavior \(β = 0\.252, p &lt; 0\.001\) all showed significant positive effects on customer trust, which, in turn, exhibited a substantial positive effect on customer loyalty \(β = 0\.618, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Mediation analysis indicated that sustainability practices influence customer loyalty primarily through trust\-building mechanisms, with indirect effects ranging from 0\.147 to 0\.190 and substantially exceeding the direct effects\. The model explained 37\.5 % of the variance in customer trust and 45\.5 % of the variance in customer loyalty, indicating moderate explanatory power\. Overall, the findings provide strong empirical evidence that sustainability practices are positively associated with customer loyalty in the Nigerian insurance industry through trust\-building mechanisms\. This study extends the literature on sustainability and relationship marketing by providing evidence from the Nigerian insurance sector using a comprehensive PLS\-SEM mediation model\.

## [AI\-Assisted Lawyers’ Practice and Professional Indemnity Insurance: Between Traditional Coverage and Emerging Risks](../publications/8883740d264e8a82821c.md)

Mirjana B\. Glintić

The growing use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) by lawyers is transforming the delivery of legal services\. AI can improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enable lawyers to process large volumes of information more rapidly\. However, the integration of AI also raises significant legal and professional issues, as AI systems may generate inaccurate or fabricated information, potentially giving rise to claims of professional negligence and liability\. This paper examines whether damage arising from the use of AI falls within the scope of professional indemnity insurance, given that AI\-related risks are not yet explicitly excluded, despite the lack of information necessary for adequate risk assessment\. The author argues that coverage may depend on whether the lawyer’s conduct qualifies as a covered ‘professional service’ and whether the technology was reasonably supervised\. Consequently, insurers are likely to place greater emphasis on lawyers’ AI governance, verification procedures, data protection, and technological competence when underwriting professional liability risks, drawing on comparative legal solutions\.

## [From Chemistry 4\.0 to Chemistry 5\.0: Digital Transformation, Sustainability, and Human\-Centred Innovation](../publications/88907598b77f7198f1cc.md)

Luana Costa de Souza; Vithórya Monteiro dos Reis; Paula Cristina Santana Cardilli; Boutros Fouad Sarrouh; Renata Carolina Zanetti Lofrano

Chemistry 5\.0 connects digital chemical technologies with measurable sustainability, human\-centred design, and operational resilience\. This critical narrative review examines artificial intelligence, autonomous experimentation, digital twins, green chemistry, and circular resource use across chemical research and process engineering\. Foundational and recent literature is synthesized through four analytical domains: digital capability, environmental performance, human oversight, and resilience\. The review proposes an implementation framework that links data and models to explicit design constraints, validation, decision authority, and life\-cycle boundaries\. Two technology and implementation tables map capabilities to benefits, risks, and staged actions\. The resulting framework identifies practical indicators for yield, material intensity, safety, data quality, workforce participation, and system robustness\. These indicators require documented baselines and system boundaries; the framework itself has not yet been empirically validated\. Chemistry 5\.0 is therefore presented as a testable approach for directing digital tools toward safer and more sustainable chemical processes, with future research needed to compare measured outcomes across scales\.

## [Wind Power Scenario Generation Based on Dual‐Domain Generator and Improved Spectral Bias Generative Adversarial Network](../publications/88aab03d6ed4e470ac27.md)

Shiwei Su; Xiaowan Dou; Zhenyu Zhang; Yuzhe Su; Qingbin Hu; Jingwen Wan; Meixuan Su

Scene generation is a core technology for quantifying wind power uncertainty\. Addressing issues such as insufficient scene realism and low spectral matching accuracy in traditional generation models, this paper proposes a frequency domain generative adversarial network \(FD‐GAN\) method for wind power scene generation based on a dual‐domain generator and improved spectral deviation\. First, a frequency domain branch is added to the original time domain main branch of the GAN\. This branch performs a Fourier transform on the input signal to extract its frequency domain features\. The two branches are then fused, maintaining the existing stability while incorporating frequency domain correction capabilities\. Second, it couples adversarial learning with frequency‐domain loss by introducing a frequency‐domain alignment loss to the original WGAN‐GP objective function\. This compares spectral differences between generated and real data, dynamically focusing on error‐prone frequency bands to enhance optimization efficiency\. Experimental results demonstrate that this method provides high‐precision scenario support for quantifying wind power uncertainty, thereby providing a reliable data foundation for subsequent power system planning and dispatch decisions\. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC\.

## [Pemanfaatan Atificial Intelligence \(AI\) Secara Etis Dalam Pembelajaran Mahasiswa](../publications/88bb90368cf761bbf5af.md)

Ahmad Difa Awlia Aslim; Nurul Ayuni; Nina Agustina; Putri Dzakilla Handayani; Annisa Fitri

Artikel pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini mengkaji implementasi pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan \(Artificial Intelligence/AI\) secara etis melalui edukasi literasi digital bagi mahasiswa di Universitas Negeri Makassar\. Didorong oleh pesatnya adopsi AI generatif, mahasiswa sering kali dihadapkan pada tantangan terkait integritas akademik, privasi data, validitas informasi, serta transparansi pengungkapan\. Melalui pengembangan e\-modul &quot;Optimalisasi Penggunaan AI dalam Pembelajaran Mahasiswa&quot;, kegiatan sosialisasi interaktif, dan diskusi komparasi studi kasus, program ini dirancang untuk menumbuhkan kesadaran kritis serta integrasi teknologi yang bertanggung jawab\. Hasil pelaksanaan menunjukkan bahwa edukasi terstruktur ini berhasil meningkatkan kemampuan mahasiswa dalam membedakan pemanfaatan AI yang konstruktif sebagai mitra berpikir dengan tindakan plagiarisme atau pengumpulan tugas pasif, sekaligus memperkuat keterampilan verifikasi informasi, kesadaran keamanan data, dan etika pengungkapan akademik\. Secara keseluruhan, inisiatif ini menjembatani efisiensi teknis dan etika pedagogis sebagai model praktis untuk menjaga integritas akademik di perguruan tinggi\.

## [CAUSE AND EFFECT AS A LINGUISTIC CATEGORY: LOGICAL\-PHILOSOPHICAL, COGNITIVE AND PRAGMATIC FOUNDATIONS FOR STUDYING CAUSAL RELATIONS IN MODERN KARAKALPAK](../publications/88c39e5c35a7759f7133.md)

Abdalieva Sarbinaz Bakhtiyarovna

Causality is usually taught in Karakalpak grammar as one semantic type of the complex sentence: a clause joined to another by a conjunction such as sebebi or sonlıqtan\. That description is accurate as far as it goes, but it leaves most of the phenomenon outside the frame\. Speakers of Karakalpak express cause and effect through nouns and verbs, case endings, participles and converbs, unmarked sequences of sentences, and inferences that the reader draws without any marker at all\. This article develops the theoretical and methodological foundations needed to study that whole range\. Drawing on logical\-philosophical accounts of causation, Talmy&\#x27;s force dynamics, script and frame theory, discourse coherence research, and the functional\-semantic tradition of Russian and Turkic linguistics, it proposes a working definition of the cause\-effect relation for Karakalpak and separates causation from five neighbouring relations: temporal sequence, condition, purpose, concession and pretext\. It then sets out a two\-stage analytical model: a functional\-semantic stage that fixes the direction, level, marker, explicitness and field position of each causal unit, and a pragmatic stage that determines its domain \(content, epistemic or speech\-act\), source of subjectivity, factivity and communicative function\. Five criteria are proposed for admitting unmarked \(implicit\) examples into a corpus\. The scientific novelty of the study lies in offering the first integrated, multi\-level model of causality designed specifically for Karakalpak material\. The main conclusion is that causality in Karakalpak is best described not as a clause type but as a centre\-periphery field whose units are selected by speakers for communicative ends\.

## [Commonsense Knowledge and Its Representation in Artificial Intelligence: A Conceptual Review of Symbolic, Graph\-Based, Neural, and Neuro\-Symbolic Approaches](../publications/88c5289437a6bce76269.md)

Ndiana Okon Asuquo \(PhD Candidate\); Ubon Asuquo Obonguko

Commonsense knowledge comprises the everyday facts, expectations, causal assumptions, social conventions, Physical regularities, and practical inference patterns that people ordinarily use without explicitly stating them\. Although artificial intelligence \(AI\) has achieved substantial progress in natural\-language processing, vision, planning, decision support, and generative language, reliable commonsense remains difficult to acquire, represent, retrieve, update, and reason over\. This article presents a conceptual review of commonsense knowledge and its representation in AI, synthesizing the major representational traditions from symbolic logic, frames, scripts, and semantic networks to ontologies, knowledge graphs, probabilistic models, neural language models, and neuro\-symbolic architectures\. Particular attention is given to Cyc, ConceptNet, ATOMIC, and ATOMIC 2020 as influential resources that illustrate complementary approaches to explicit and inferential commonsense\. The review shows that commonsense is characterized by implicitness, context dependence, defeasibility, uncertainty, temporal and spatial structure, social situatedness, and cultural variation\. These characteristics make a single universal representation difficult to sustain\. The article therefore proposes a layered hybrid architecture comprising input interpretation, an explicit commonsense knowledge graph, neural retrieval, rule\-based and probabilistic reasoning, and an explanation/provenance layer\. The framework is positioned as a research design rather than an experimentally validated system\. The article also identifies knowledge acquisition, coverage, inconsistency, temporal change, cultural variation, grounding, scalability, evaluation, provenance, and hallucination control as continuing challenges\. Finally, it highlights opportunities for educational AI and context\-sensitive systems in Nigerian and African settings, where local linguistic and institutional knowledge can complement globally developed commonsense resources\. Keywords: commonsense knowledge; knowledge representation; artificial intelligence; knowledge graphs; symbolic reasoning; neural reasoning; neuro\-symbolic AI; ConceptNet; Cyc; ATOMIC\.

## [Development of a Web\-Based Management Information System for Customer Complaints and Feedback](../publications/88cbd3e71362de5d007e.md)

Yana Suryana; Verdi Yasin; Hidayatul Ichwan

Small distributors often handle customer complaints through instant messaging, where complaint information is produced but not retained\. Prior complaint\-management systems are reported after the transition, for institutional users or structured datasets, without a measured account of the process they replace\. This single\-case study at a heavy equipment spare part distributor in Central Jakarta measures that pre\-formalisation baseline and derives the system design and its evaluation indicators from it\. Observation, WhatsApp history review and interviews with five staff and eight customers were triangulated into a case register with fixed counting rules: from January to March 2026 it held 70 complaints, of which 24 \(34\.3%\) took more than three working days to resolve and 18 \(25\.7%\) had histories administrators could not retrieve\. A web\-based system was developed through Rapid Application Development and tested with eight black box scenarios derived by equivalence partitioning\. All scenarios produced the expected output, and each baseline problem has a corresponding capability at handover\. These are functional and process\-level results; no post\-implementation data were collected and security, boundary, concurrency and volume testing were outside scope, so no improvement in service quality is claimed\. The contribution is a measured baseline, a low\-cost design traceable from each baseline problem to a tested function, and indicators with baseline values for later evaluation\.

## [QUALITY OF HIGHER EDUCATION IN INDIA: CHALLENGES, OPPORTUNITIES AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES](../publications/88d80eb1c88356416863.md)

Anand Katare; Indravesh Arya; Kamlesh Yadav

Higher education plays a pivotal role in shaping a nation&\#x27;s economic growth, technological advancement, and social development\. India possesses one of the world&\#x27;s largest higher education systems, comprising over one thousand universities and thousands of colleges that collectively educate millions of students annually\. Despite significant expansion in institutional capacity and enrolment over the past two decades, maintaining quality remains a major concern\. Challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, faculty shortages, disparities in access, limited research productivity, employability gaps, insufficient industry\-academia collaboration, governance issues, and unequal digital access continue to impede the realization of globally competitive higher education\. Simultaneously, transformative initiatives including the National Education Policy \(NEP\) 2020, digital learning platforms, research funding reforms, international collaborations, multidisciplinary education, and the integration of artificial intelligence present unprecedented opportunities for systemic improvement\. This review critically examines the current status of higher education quality in India by synthesizing evidence from government reports, policy documents, and contemporary scholarly literature\. The paper discusses the multidimensional challenges affecting educational quality and evaluates emerging opportunities driven by technological innovation, quality assurance mechanisms, competency\-based curricula, and global academic partnerships\. Furthermore, it proposes strategic recommendations to strengthen governance, faculty development, research ecosystems, institutional autonomy, accreditation, digital transformation, and employability\. The study concludes that achieving sustainable excellence in higher education requires coordinated efforts among policymakers, regulatory agencies, academic institutions, industry, and society\. A learner\-centric, technology\-enabled, research\-oriented, and globally connected higher education system will be fundamental to realizing India&\#x27;s vision of becoming a global knowledge economy by 2047\.

## [Individualized sequencing of targeted immunotherapies in generalized myasthenia gravis across distinct patient profiles](../publications/88e47cfeb5c512362c9a.md)

Βασιλική Ζούβελου; Dimitra Tzavella; Eleni Strataki; Aigli G\. Vakrakou

Background Targeted immunotherapies have expanded treatment options for acetylcholine receptor antibody\-positive generalized myasthenia gravis \(gMG\), but evidence regarding their sequencing and individualized therapeutic pathways remains limited\. Methods We describe seven selected adults with AChR\-positive gMG managed through individualized targeted\-treatment pathways involving administered and, in some cases, planned sequential therapy\. Treatment selection was guided by disease severity, corticosteroid\-related risks, presence of thymoma, comorbidities, peripheral venous access and the need for rapid clinical improvement and/or sustained disease management\. Results Across the seven cases, FcRn antagonists were used for rapid symptom control, corticosteroid dose reduction and bridging therapy while the appropriate vaccinations required before planned complement inhibition or B\-cell depletion therapy were completed\. Rituximab was selected as a long\-term B\-cell\-directed immunosuppressive strategy, particularly in recent\-onset gMG\. Ravulizumab was planned as a long\-term, non\-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy in thymoma\-associated myasthenia gravis and in chronic gMG with symptoms refractory to conventional non\-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy and dependent on corticosteroids\. Conclusion These seven cases illustrate how targeted immunotherapies may be used sequentially and individualized according to their onset of action, MG subgroup, treatment goal, required vaccinations and route of administration\.

## [Unified Expression, Semantic Dimensions, and Ontological Commitment: A Recursive\-Ontological Challenge to Two\-Dimensional Semantics and the Philosophical Zombie Argument](../publications/88e9713871bfaaa8ad0a.md)

Gangbei Niu

This paper challenges the move from two\-dimensional semantic distinctions to conclusions about the metaphysical separability of consciousness\. It develops a recursive\-ontological perspective according to which cognition, supposition, linguistic expression, and theoretical assessment are events within causally continuous relations\. The central claim is not that public language can express only one meaning, nor that semantic distinctions are unreal\. Rather, distinctions between modes of semantic evaluation do not, without further argument, establish independent ontological dimensions\. A theory intended for public assessment must specify how its semantic dimensions are identified, coordinated, and applied through shared rules; it must then independently justify any transition from those rules to claims about possible worlds and phenomenal consciousness\. The paper applies this demand to zombie conceivability, first\-person authority, and the explanatory gap\. It concludes that two\-dimensional semantics may clarify modal and epistemic distinctions, but cannot by itself establish an ontological fracture between physical organization and experience\.

## [Negotiating Authorship with Generative AI in Cinema Education: Attribution and Creative Decision\-Making in Screenwriting](../publications/88f0b4b24ce81e45fb07.md)

Ufuk Kucukcan

This study examines how cinema students attribute authorship during AI\-assisted screenwriting and how those judgments relate to creative decisions\. Drawing on a fourteen\-week, design\-based course, it compares logbooks with 436 student turns across twenty generative\-AI conversations\. In four of six co\-writing cases, students selected and retained system\-originated material\. The clearest tension appeared when students claimed the idea as their own but assigned the text entirely to AI while repeatedly rejecting generated material, a response the instrument’s own categories leave ambiguous\. Read against Livingston, Gaut and Sellors, these cases show that textual generation, creative decision\-making and authorship attribution can diverge within one process\. Cinema education should ask not only who authored a text, but on what basis\.

## [Inclusive Community Engagement in Mosque Networks: Developing a Communication Model for a Multicultural Society through the FOSIL BKM Medan Case Study](../publications/89190a39488aa42635d7.md)

Muhammad Dalim; Agus Edy Rangkuti; Irwan Musriza Harahap; Suriyadi

Objective: This study analyzes communication and inclusive community engagement in FOSIL BKM Medan and develops an initial communication model for mosque networks in a multicultural society\. Theoretical framework: The study draws on participatory communication, social capital, collaborative governance, and symbolic interaction to explain relationships between dialogue, trust, collective action, and organizational meaning\. Literature review: Previous studies address religious volunteering, community empowerment, and collaboration\. The remaining question concerns how relational closeness becomes traceable decisions and coordinated action across mosque organizations while accommodating different community perspectives\. Methods: A qualitative single\-case approach uses participant observation, in\-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and organizational document analysis\. Interview excerpts from Informants support thematic interpretation\. Analysis involves data condensation, presentation, verification, and pattern matching, distinguishing reported practices from normative policy proposals\. Results: The accounts identify silaturahim as relational capital and emphasize documented follow\-up, responses to aspirations, transparent commitments, and complementary digital and direct communication\. These themes inform seven CECMN components: needs and asset mapping, structured dialogue, joint planning, collaborative implementation, network strengthening, hybrid communication, and participatory evaluation\. Four propositions connect voice with influence, trust with commitment, networks with resources, and experience with learning\. Implications: The model offers guidance for inclusive dialogue, responsibility allocation, and shared learning within Medan’s culturally plural setting\. North Sumatran relational traditions provide contextual insights without establishing interethnic or interfaith outcomes\. Implementation testing remains necessary\. Novelty: The contribution is a context\-specific integration of relational communication mechanisms and governance supports in the Community Engagement Communication Model for Mosque Network\.

## [Molecular Genetic Analysis and Prenatal Diagnosis of a Family With MECP2 Duplication Syndrome](../publications/891b7fcca8a8bd0fcbd0.md)

FengQiu Lin; DingGuo Chen; Zhenglin Lu; Yu Huang; Chun Wang; Juhua Liang; Xuejuan Nong; ZhengYi Chang; FuBo Wei; Guidan Xu

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to conduct a molecular genetic analysis and prenatal diagnosis for a family with MECP2 duplication syndrome \(MDS\), with the goal of improving diagnostic accuracy and enabling informed reproductive decisions to reduce the incidence of this condition\. METHODS: The study involved a proband \(a 15\-week\-old fetus\), his symptomatic older brother, and their parents\. Genomic DNA from chorionic villus and peripheral blood samples was analyzed using high\-throughput sequencing to detect chromosomal copy number variations \(CNVs\)\. To confirm the findings, multiplex ligation\-dependent probe amplification \(MLPA\) was specifically employed\. RESULTS: High\-throughput sequencing identified a 0\.35 Mb duplication at Xq28 in the fetus and his mother, and a 0\.4 Mb duplication in the brother\. The duplicated region contained the critical MECP2 gene\. MLPA analysis confirmed the MECP2 gene duplication in the fetus, leading to a definitive diagnosis of MDS\. The mother was identified as an asymptomatic carrier\. CONCLUSION: Both the proband and his brother were diagnosed with MDS, having inherited the duplication from their asymptomatic mother\. The combined use of high\-throughput sequencing and MLPA proved to be an effective strategy for accurate pedigree analysis and prenatal diagnosis of MDS, providing a crucial basis for genetic counseling\.

## [Enhanced detection of occult and active infections using multiplex HIV/HBV/HCV nucleic acid testing in high\-risk populations: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/891cad3f56c6e79fdda7.md)

Cong Jin; Yu Wang; Zuyang Zhang; Mingzhu Niu; Jingyi Wang; Huichao Chen; Hongxiang Yuan; Ning Liu; Enlong Yao; Man Li; Yuehui Zhang; Xia Feng; Yuhua Shi; Kai Lu

Introduction Given the shared modes of transmission, HIV, HBV, and HCV confer a high risk of co\-infection, particularly among key populations\. Currently, clinical screening for these viruses still relies predominantly on serological assays, which fail to detect a substantial proportion of infections, including occult HBV infection \(OBI, defined as HBsAg\-negative but HBV DNA\-positive\) and current HCV infection\. HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex nucleic acid testing \(NAT\) has been widely adopted in blood screening due to its superior sensitivity, specificity, and shorter window period\. However, this highly effective screening assay has not yet been translated into routine clinical screening for high\-risk populations\. Methods To evaluate its clinical performance and feasibility, we conducted a cross\-sectional study enrolling 802 people who use drugs \(PWUD\) and 400 men who have sex with men \(MSM\) in China\. All participants underwent parallel serological screening and HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT, with final infection status confirmed by supplementary testing, epidemiological history, and clinical symptoms\. Results Upfront HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT identified 12 additional OBI cases \(incremental yield 12/1,202\) that were missed by HBsAg\-only screening and HBsAg\-triggered reflex testing\. HCV RNA testing distinguished current from non\-current HCV infection, but this benefit was not specific to the multiplex strategy\. Acceptance of multiplex NAT and post\-diagnosis treatment was high among participants\. Conclusion Our findings suggest that HIV/HBV/HCV multiplex NAT could detect clinically relevant infections undetectable by serology in key populations, suggesting potential clinical benefits\. However, further prospective implementation studies and cost\-effectiveness analyses are warranted before routine integration into clinical practice\.

## [Revisiting semantic plurality I: mapping the terminology around semantic plurality in nineteenth\-century French and German scholarly works](../publications/8941c5abeebe1982fda7.md)

Nicolas Gignac

This paper examines how nineteenth\-century French and German scholars mobilised semantic plurality in thirty key texts focused on linguistic meaning\. Through historical and lexical\-semantic analyses, the study traces how scholars from these linguistic traditions contributed to the construction of a terminology \(understood as a ‘set of linguistic signs’\) that has shaped contemporary understandings of semantic plurality \(commonly referred to as polysemy since the end of the nineteenth century\)\. By combining quantitative and qualitative methods, the research identifies key terminological trends in how semantic plurality was put into text, showing that French discourse leaned towards literary and symbolic terms and expressions\. At the same time, German scholarship adopted a more holistic, meaning\-driven approach\. These findings challenge prevailing views in the history of linguistics by emphasising the multidimensional nature of semantic plurality – of which polysemy is only one facet\. The paper ultimately calls for a more nuanced, data\-driven approach to studying the development of linguistic ideas and highlights the importance of historical perspectives for enriching contemporary semantic theory\.

## [Perbandingan Word2Vec dan N\-Gram pada Klasifikasi Sentimen Gaji Guru Honorer Mengggunakan Support Vector Machine](../publications/8943ea5cc8904c274d3a.md)

Nur Kholifatun Nisais Sobaro; Moh\. Dasuki; Ari Eko Wardoyo

Komentar pengguna Instagram dapat dimanfaatkan untuk menggambarkan persepsi masyarakat terhadap berbagai isu sosial, termasuk kesejahteraan guru honorer\. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi pengaruh dua pendekatan representasi teks, yaitu Word2Vec dan N\-Gram berbasis TF\-IDF, terhadap performa klasifikasi sentimen menggunakan algoritma Support Vector Machine \(SVM\)\. Dataset komentar Instagram diproses melalui tahapan pembersihan teks dan pelabelan sentimen sebelum dilakukan penyeimbangan kelas menggunakan Synthetic Minority Over\-sampling Technique \(SMOTE\)\. Representasi teks yang diuji meliputi Word2Vec CBOW, Word2Vec Skip\-Gram, TF\-IDF Unigram, Bigram, dan Trigram\. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan Stratified 5\-Fold Cross Validation dengan kernel Linear, Polynomial, Radial Basis Function \(RBF\), dan Sigmoid\. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa TF\-IDF Unigram memberikan kinerja terbaik dengan akurasi 94,87%, sedangkan Word2Vec CBOW, TF\-IDF Bigram, Word2Vec Skip\-Gram, dan TF\-IDF Trigram masing\-masing memperoleh akurasi 87,04%, 86,35%, 85,78%, dan 77,22%\. Selain mencapai akurasi tertinggi, TF\-IDF Unigram juga menghasilkan nilai precision, recall, dan F1\-score sebesar 95%\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa representasi berbasis kata tunggal dengan pembobotan TF\-IDF lebih efektif dalam mengidentifikasi sentimen komentar Instagram dibandingkan pendekatan Word2Vec pada dataset yang digunakan\.Kata Kunci: N\-Gram ; Support Vector Machine; TF\-IDF; Word2Vec; analisis sentimen

## [Predictive Test Case Prioritization in Agile Workflows: A Machine Learning Approach with SMOTE\-ENN and PCA](../publications/894d2ba2464c692de912.md)

Sin\-Ban Ho; Kavinraj Baskaran; Junaidi Abdullah; Said Suleiman Naseer Al Harthy; Ian Chai

Test Case Prioritization \(TCP\) is an essential part of agile software development, allowing for the identification and execution of critical test cases early in the process to maximize fault detection efficiency\. Traditional TCP techniques often depend on static metrics, like code complexity and historical pass/fail rates, that do not conform with the dynamic nature of Agile workflows\. To overcome this, the proposed research presents a discriminative machine learning\-based predictive prioritization model that incorporates historical defect data, execution history, as well as requirement criticality to improve auspiciousness of TCP\. The study assesses a range of machine learning models like Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting across two datasets, namely CarFinTest and MISPriority\. Though the target variable in the MISPriority dataset was nicely structured with respect to the feature set, allowing models to reach a predictive accuracy up to 78\.63%, the CarFinTest showed a high degree of imbalance in classes along with poor class separability\. Through iterative improvements, the addition of SMOTE\-ENN to balance classes, dimensionality reduction via PCA, and feature engineering techniques all greatly increased model performance, with Random Forest and Gradient Boosting performing the best\. In addition, the proposed research presents an automatic dashboard for preprocessing dataset, training models, and prioritizing them for implementation into an Agile environment for practical usability\. Through adaptive machine learning\-based techniques, this research connects traditional and dynamic test prioritization methods, realizing a scalable and data\-oriented approach compatible with Agile processes\. Future work should focus on enhancing real\-time prioritization through incremental learning techniques and expanding dataset generalization across diverse software development projects\.

## [Economic burden of myasthenia gravis in France: A nationwide claims database study \(STAMINA\)](../publications/896088916efb2a4eff7f.md)

Gérard de Pouvourville; Pascal Laforêt; Emmanuelle Salort‐Campana; Anne Crochard; Grégory Chollet; Camille Nevoret; Stephane Bouée; Céline Tard

Myasthenia gravis \(MG\) is a chronic autoimmune disease with symptoms of muscle weakness and fatigability\. The aim of this study was to estimate MG\-related healthcare resource use \(HCRU\), associated direct costs and their determinants in France\. Data were extracted from the French national claims database \(SNDS\) for the period 1/1/2008\-31/12/2019\. Adult patients with MG were identified using an algorithm based primarily on the G70 ICD\-10 code\. The incident and prevalent MG populations were compared with matched non\-MG controls and direct costs were estimated\. An exploratory indirect cost analysis restricted to sick leave and disability was also performed and a multivariable model used to identify patients&\#x27; characteristics associated with higher direct MG costs\. In 2019, the mean annual direct cost per patient with MG was €8,506 compared with €3,670 in controls, leading to an MG\-excess cost of €4,836 per patient\. Patients with MG had significantly \(p &lt; 0\.0001\) higher HCRU than controls in all items of inpatient and outpatient care\. MG\-excess costs were high, especially in the first year after disease identification and were mainly driven by hospitalizationsfor crises and exacerbations\. They remained relatively stable thereafter\. Patients with MG were on sick leave more often and for longer periods and were 2\-3 times more likely to receive disability or living allowance than controls\. The highest costs were concentrated during the first year after MG identification due to exacerbations and crises requiring hospitalization with costly medications and procedures\. Novel innovative treatments are expected to change these main drivers of medical costs\.

## [Seasonal lags and legacy effects on vegetation cover and carbon uptake in Kuwait from 2014 to 2024: A MODIS GPP–ET–NDVI analysis](../publications/8963151d6bfa2892becb.md)

Shereen Nadoum

Abstract Remote sensing provides a consistent framework for quantifying vegetation dynamics in hyper\-arid environments where field observations are sparse\. This study integrated MODIS\-derived gross primary productivity \(GPP\), evapotranspiration \(ET\), and normalized difference vegetation index \(NDVI\) with GPM IMERG precipitation to evaluate seasonal variability, carbon–water coupling, rainfall\-response lags, and cumulative hydroclimatic controls across Kuwait during 2014–2024\. Vegetation activity peaked in spring, when mean GPP reached 2\.25 ± 0\.41 g C m⁻² d⁻¹ and NDVI 0\.26 ± 0\.05, compared with 0\.92 ± 0\.21 g C m⁻² d⁻¹ and 0\.12 ± 0\.03 in summer\. ET was strongly associated with GPP \(R² = 0\.680, p &lt; 0\.001\) and NDVI \(R² = 0\.533, p &lt; 0\.001\), whereas same\-month precipitation explained substantially less variation in GPP \(R² = 0\.189, p = 0\.003\) and NDVI \(R² = 0\.081, p = 0\.061\)\. Cross\-correlation analysis showed that both vegetation indicators responded strongly when rainfall preceded vegetation activity by one month \(GPP: r = 0\.711; NDVI: r = 0\.678; both p &lt; 0\.001\), with the NDVI response persisting longer than GPP\. At the cumulative interannual scale, ET remained significantly associated with GPP \(R² = 0\.524, p = 0\.012\) and NDVI \(R² = 0\.630, p = 0\.004\), whereas cumulative precipitation was not significant\. These findings demonstrate that vegetation dynamics in Kuwait are better characterized by ecosystem water use and antecedent rainfall than by contemporaneous or cumulative precipitation alone, highlighting the importance of rainfall timing and short\-term hydroclimatic legacy effects in hyper\-arid ecosystems\.

## [Encoding tactile stimuli for Braille recognition with organoids](../publications/89632c02af3706cbbf6a.md)

Tianyi Liu; Hemma Philamore; Benjamin Ward\-Cherrier

This study proposes a transferable encoding strategy that maps tactile sensor data to electrical stimulation patterns, enabling neural organoids to perform an open\-loop artificial tactile Braille classification task\. Human forebrain organoids cultured on a low\-density microelectrode array \(MEA\) are systematically stimulated to characterize the relationship between electrical stimulation parameters \(number of pulse, phase amplitude, phase duration, and trigger delay\) and organoid responses, measured as spike activity and spatial displacement of the center of activity\. Implemented on event\-based tactile inputs recorded from the Evetac sensor, our system achieved an average Braille letter classification accuracy of 61% with a single organoid, which increased to 83% when responses from a three\-organoid ensemble were combined\. Additionally, the multi\-organoid configuration demonstrated enhanced robustness against various types of artificially introduced noise\. This research demonstrates the potential of organoids as low\-power, adaptive bio\-hybrid computational elements and provides a foundational encoding framework for future scalable bio\-hybrid computing architectures\.

## [ЦИФРОВЕ СЕРЕДОВИЩЕ У ФОРМУВАННІ ІНШОМОВНОЇ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТІ ЗДОБУВАЧІВ ОСВІТИ](../publications/89686f8b945f3deb66c2.md)

Marina Konieva; Anastasia Vakulenko

У статті теоретично обґрунтовано та практично розроблено методичну систему використання цифрового освіт\- нього середовища для підвищення рівня іншомовної компетентності здобувачів освіти\. Сформульовано сутність цифрового освітнього середовища як динамічної екосистеми, що інтегрує п’ять ключових компонентів: інфраструк\- турно\-технологічний, контентно\-інформаційний, інструментально\-платформений, комунікативно\-інтерактивний та інтелектуально\-адаптивний\. Проаналізовано трансформацію ролі викладача у цифровому просторі з традиційного транслятора знань на фасилітатора, тьютора й ментора\. Наукова новизна одержаних результатів полягає у систематизації лінгводидактичного потенціалу сучасних цифро\- вих платформ та технологій штучного інтелекту, а також у визначенні їхньої ролі як цілісної екосистеми для розвитку мовленнєвих навичок\. Уточнено сутність освітньої автономії здобувачів в умовах цифровізації та доведено необхідність переходу від епізодичного використання застосунків до поетапної інтеграції цифрового інструментарію в освітній процес\. Особливу увагу приділено дидактичному потенціалу технологій штучного інтелекту \(генеративним мовним моделям, сервісам автоматизованого аналізу писемного мовлення та адаптивним алгоритмам інтервальних повто\- рень\)\. Доведено, що інтеграція ШІ\-інструментів забезпечує ефективну персоналізацію навчання в умовах масової освіти, безперервну комунікативну практику, мінімізацію мовного бар’єра та миттєвий зворотний зв’язок\. Обґрунтовано комплексну методичну систему, побудовану на синергії комунікативно\-когнітивного, діяльнісного та змішаного підходів\. Визначено послідовність реалізації методики через підготовчо\-орієнтувальний, процесуаль\- но\-діяльнісний і рефлексивно\-оцінювальний етапи\. Розроблено діагностичний інструментарій моніторингу результатів, який включає чотири критерії: мовно\-дискур\- сивний, комунікативно\-діяльнісний, мотиваційно\-ціннісний та автономно\-цифровий\. Представлено критеріально\-рів\- неву карту \(репродуктивний, реконструктивний, творчо\-інноваційний рівні\) та обґрунтовано доцільність формуваль\- ного оцінювання й використання цифрового портфоліо \(e\-Portfolio\) для розвитку освітньої автономії здобувачів\.

## [Ai\-Enabled Digital Twins for Proactive Fault Prediction and Self\-Healing in Distributed Cloud–Edge Systems: A Conceptual Framework](../publications/896936b9e86022f9a28d.md)

Dr\. Anil Karadwal

Distributed cloud–edge systems support modern applications by combining centralised cloud infrastructure with computing resources located near data sources\. Despite their advantages, these environments remain vulnerable to hardware faults, software failures, network disruptions, resource contention, and changing workloads\. Conventional fault\-tolerance mechanisms often respond after a failure has occurred, potentially increasing service interruption and recovery costs\. Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Digital Twin \(DT\) technology offer opportunities to anticipate system degradation, evaluate alternative responses, and support automated recovery\. This paper proposes a conceptual framework integrating digital twins, AI\-based fault prediction, adaptive resource management, and self\-healing mechanisms for distributed cloud–edge environments\. The framework comprises six components: real\-time monitoring, digital representation, predictive analytics, risk\-aware decision\-making, self\-healing execution, and continuous feedback\. It also identifies challenges relating to data quality, prediction uncertainty, model drift, computational overhead, security, and coordination across distributed nodes\. A proposed evaluation methodology outlines measurable indicators, including prediction performance, service availability, recovery time, false\-alarm rate, and resource overhead\. The paper contributes a structured design approach for future investigation of predictive and autonomous fault management\. As a conceptual study, it does not claim experimental validation or quantified performance improvements\. Its proposed framework requires implementation and empirical evaluation under representative cloud–edge workloads\.

## [The oxidative stress index predicts the likelihood of non\-communicable disease \(NCD\) onset, disease prevention strategy and potential impact on human survival](../publications/896e647e6b379fe4beb1.md)

Harold I\. Zeliger

Worldwide increases in noncommunicable diseases \(NCDs\) are a threat to the ongoing human existence\. Total oxidative stress \(OS\) is well known to be a direct cause of non\-communicative disease \(NCD\) onset\. The Oxidative Stress Index \(OSI\), obtained from a non\-invasive eight item questionnaire, has been shown to be indicative of total OS level in the human body and a predictor of the likelihood of NCD onset\. The eight OSI parameters are: age, weight, genetics, socioeconomic status, environmental pollution, pre\-existing chronic illness, numbers of medications regularly taken and chronic psychological stress\. This review paper presents the evolution of the OSI, its applications, justifications for the use of each of its eight parameters in measuring total OS and how the inter\-relationships of these parameters contribute to NCD onset\. Also discussed are the implications of ever\-increasing OS on the human existence\.

## [Blunted cerebello\-basal ganglia\-thalamic circuit connectivity in melancholic depression](../publications/896ef6fe7fefe846fb83.md)

Xiaoqin Wang; Yi Xia; Yujue Wang; Na Shen; Junling Sheng; Wubin Chen; Junchen Bao; Rui Yan; Zhijian Yao; Qing Lü

Melancholic major depressive disorder \(MDD\-M\), characterized by anhedonia, is a clinically distinct subtype with poor treatment response and impaired social function\. This study aimed to investigate abnormal patterns of inter\-regional neural communication in MDD\-M\. This study included 1541 participants who underwent resting\-state fMRI scans across three independent datasets: an exploration dataset \(n = 1175\), a validation dataset \(n = 216\), and a longitudinal clinical cohort \( n = 150\) with at least two scans per participant\. Granger causality analysis was used to evaluate directed information flow between brain regions\. In the exploration cohort, we applied directed Network\-Based Statistics to identify melancholic\-specific network features and correlate these features with clinical characteristics\. These features were then used to construct a classification model in the validation dataset\. Finally, we assessed the stability of these features in the longitudinal cohort via repeated\-measures ANOVA\. MDD\-M exhibited a hypo\-connectivity network pattern compared to the control group\. Specifically, MDD\-M reported weakened bidirectional connectivity between the thalamic ventrolateral nucleus \(ThalVL\) and the nucleus accumbens, as well as diminished causal outflow from the cerebellar vermis to both the globus pallidus and the ThalVL\. This hypo\-connectivity network pattern achieved an AUC of 0\.81 in the validation set\. Longitudinal analysis further confirmed the stability of the hypo\-connectivity pattern in MDD\-M\. We identified a connectivity pattern of diminished directed information flow within the cerebello\-basal ganglia\-thalamic circuit that may represent a potential circuit\-level feature of MDD\-M\. This stable and directional brain network feature may help identify the subtype and develop targeted treatments\.
