## [Military evolution: broadening the discussion beyond innovation and adaptation: an example based on the IDF development](../publications/897b65643dd2ee3f0f67.md)

Meir Finkel

Military force design is a dynamic process that includes complex relations among innovation, adaptation, conservatism, enlargement, and shrinkage, and other forms of change or stability arising from the ongoing interaction among the military, its environment, and, primarily, its enemies\. Changes in the development of the IDF between 1948 and 2026 are illustrated for the first time through an evolutionary phylogenetic tree and analysed using nine evolutionary theory themes, including changes in the rates of speciation and extinction over time, pre\-adaptation, over\-speciation, co\-evolution, and evolutionary/adaptive lag\. The IDF case study demonstrates how adopting evolutionary thinking could improve force\-planning processes and military organisations&\#x27; ability to adapt to changing realities when their adversaries try to enforce “selection processes,” new military “ecological niches” emerge, new technologies create new evolutionary branches, and so forth\.

## [Electrochemical Performance of Indian Loofah‐Derived Carbon in Aqueous Electrolytes for Supercapacitor Electrode](../publications/897ce1c522af6d0139bf.md)

Nityanutan Mohapatra; Kamatchi Jothiramalingam Sankaran; Swetapadma Praharaj; Dibyaranjan Rout

ABSTRACT Tailoring the electrode–electrolyte combination is an important strategy for improving the charge storage kinetics of supercapacitive devices\. Here, the effect of aqueous electrolytes \(3 m KOH, H 2 SO 4 , Na 2 SO 4 \) on the electrochemical response of Indian loofah‐derived activated carbon \(AC\) prepared via controlled carbonization and NaOH‐assisted hydrothermal activation is examined\. The electrodes exhibit high specific capacitance \(at 1 mV s −1 \) of 362\.28 F g −1 in H 2 SO 4 and 336 F g −1 in KOH, decreasing significantly to 147\.81 F g −1 in Na 2 SO 4 \. Additionally, it demonstrates an excellent capacity retention of 98% \(10 000 cycles\), a wide voltage \(≈1\.1 V\) window and delivers an energy density of 38\.08 Wh kg −1 at 549\.99 W kg −1 in 3 m KOH compared to others\. It is attributed to the ionic mobility, hydration radius, conductivity, and interactions of the electrolytic ions with surface functional groups of AC\. Besides, symmetric AC cells using a 3 m KOH aqueous solution outperform their solid‐state counterparts \(3 m KOH \+ Polyvinyl Alcohol\), delivering 215 F g −1 \(at 1 mV s −1 \) and 20\.93 Wh kg −1 \(at 500 W kg −1 \)\. These findings provide key insights into optimizing electrode‐electrolyte synergy for high‐performance energy storage systems\.

## [Modeling Hydrogen Fuel Cell of High\-Speed Passenger Ship by Using Simulink](../publications/898552f359dd9c4c6b95.md)

Japhet Augustino

The maritime industry is under increasing pressure from environmental regulations, and therefore, it is required to provide energy solutions that comply with sustainable practices immediately\. The study conducted by the researchers indicates the creation of a hydrogen fuel cell model that is designed specifically for the MATLAB Simulink high\-speed passenger vessels\. A detailed analysis sketch is laid out, which shows the design and simulation of the Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell \(PEMFC\) system, displaying the emission reduction effect of this technology\. This model is made up of extra units like a fuel cell stack, a DC/DC converter, and a flow rate regulator these give the operator the capability to change the fuel consumption and the generated power\. Several scenarios were tested in simulation and results were compared to study system efficiency and performance, where the findings mostly focused on the role of hydrogen pressures in increasing cell voltage and efficiency\. This study proves the potential of hydrogen fuel cells in sustainable maritime propulsion\. It discusses the engineering challenges that are met during the experimental deployment and test in naval conditions\.

## [Evaluating learner satisfaction and confidence in a precision agriculture MOOC: a cross\-sectional study in Palestinian higher education](../publications/898ac63bb0ebd8774bdb.md)

Walid Khalilia; Hazem Horoub; Hani Iwidat; Faiz Abdelhafid; Radoslav Židek; Ľubomí­r Belej; Zuzana Palková

Background Precision agriculture \(PA\) increasingly requires graduates who can work with sensor\-based, geospatial and data\-driven technologies, yet access to specialised training remains uneven in many under\-resourced higher\-education contexts\. Although massive open online courses \(MOOCs\) offer a potentially scalable response to this gap, empirical evaluation of precision\-agriculture MOOCs and of MOOC\-based learning in Palestinian higher education more broadly remains limited, so evidence on learners&\#x27; satisfaction and confidence in this specific educational context is needed\. Methods This study addresses that gap through a cross\-sectional, questionnaire\-based evaluation of learners participating in a precision agriculture MOOC developed within the BENEFIT Erasmus\+ project for Palestinian higher education; the design does not support causal inference\. A questionnaire administered following learners&\#x27; participation in the MOOC was completed by 62 of 69 invited learners \(response rate 89\.9%\)\. The course\-evaluation instrument comprised eight satisfaction items and nine confidence\-related items rated on a 0\-4 Likert scale; five negatively worded items were reverse\-scored for composite analyses\. We report descriptive statistics, one\-sample tests against the scale midpoint, a paired comparison of the two composites, and correlation analysis, with Spearman&\#x27;s ρ as a non\-parametric sensitivity check\. Results Learners reported positive overall satisfaction \(M = 2\.74, SD = 0\.57\) and positive overall confidence \(M = 2\.54, SD = 0\.40\), both significantly above the scale midpoint \(both p &lt; 0\.001, d &gt; 1\.2\)\. Agreement was strongest for perceived MOOC design quality \(82\.3%\), course enjoyment \(75\.8%\), confidence in mastering content \(75\.8%\), and confidence in passing an examination \(75\.8%\)\. Satisfaction and confidence were strongly and positively correlated \[ r = 0\.746, 95% CI \(0\.610, 0\.839\), p &lt; 0\.001; ρ = 0\.757\]; because both constructs were measured concurrently by self\-report within the same cross\-sectional survey, this association cannot establish the direction of the relationship or a causal link between the two constructs\. Satisfaction was significantly higher than confidence \(mean difference = 0\.20, p &lt; 0\.001, dz = 0\.53\)\. A single item\-perceived slide information density\-did not differ significantly from the neutral midpoint \( p = 0\.742\), and given this non\-significant result and a high proportion of neutral responses \(51\.6%\), is presented as an area that may warrant further, exploratory review rather than a confirmed design weakness\. Discussion The results suggest that a structured instructional\-design approach was associated with positive learner perceptions in this agriculture MOOC, while cognitive\-load management in slide design may merit further, cautious attention in future course iterations\.

## [Forecasting Voltage Time Series under Anomalies Using a WGAN Model With Lipschitz Control and Progressive Kernel Critic Strategy](../publications/898c4ee22dbc45cc208e.md)

Najmieh Sadat Safarabadi

In time\-series forecasting tasks, the use of recursive forecasting on high\-dimensional data substantially increases the complexity of the prediction process\. The main challenge is that long\-term dynamics becomes harder to model, since the sequences show greater temporal variability\. To counteract this limitation and improve the modeling of long\-term dynamics, and more importantly, address high\-dimensional recursive forecasting, this paper uses a Wasserstein GAN equipped with a progressive Lipschitz penalty and an adaptive kernel\. This model is capable of taking a window of the data stream and forecasting the next values, subsequently reconstructing the time\-series stream and dynamically adapting its kernel to each new window\. The proopsed model is a deep learning framework based on a Wasserstein GAN \(WGAN\-CLP\) with an adaptive kernel to model alterations in streaming voltage time series\. To establish the methodological foundation, we review the WGAN\-LP formulation another variant model in this class and extend its framework through an adaptive kernel critic model\. We then evaluate this extended model using power ratios, correlation coefficient \(CC\), and relative root mean squared error \(RRMSE\)\. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms benchmark methods in both accuracy and robustness\. The evaluation shows promising performance of the WGAN\-CLP with an adaptive kernel framework in forecasting sequence alterations across the voltage and energy time\-series datasets\.

## [Association between xerostomia and peri‐implant health: A retrospective cohort study](../publications/898eb286fafa761f8259.md)

Shahad Alhazmi; Sahar Baniameri; Parham Hazrati; Yousef Taha Y\. Amrou; Fatemeh SamavatiJame; Hom‐Lay Wang; Muhammad H\. A\. Saleh

BACKGROUND: Dental implants are a long\-term and reliable solution to replace missing dentition, but subject to different patient\-related and biological changes that could alter its success\. Xerostomia, or the alteration of the normal salivary flow, can impair oral function and potentially affect the success of any treatment, including implant outcomes\. The purpose of this study is to study the association between xerostomia and peri\-implantitis\. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using records of patients who received dental implants between 2010 and 2023 at the University of Michigan School of Dentistry\. The patients were divided into two groups: the xerostomia group and the non\-xerostomia group\. Implant level assessment included the presence of peri\-implantitis and marginal bone loss, restoration type, cement\-retained or screw retained, and the depth of restoration margin\. Patient\-level assessment included sex, age, smoking history, medical conditions, and maintenance visit frequency\. Univariable and multivariable mixed\-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between peri\-implantitis and patient\-level and other implant\-related variables\. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were reported, and statistical significance was defined as p &lt; 0\.05\. RESULTS: A total of 173 patients were included, with 46 patients reporting xerostomia\. The results showed no independent association between xerostomia and peri\-implantitis in either univariable or multivariable analyzes\. The history of periodontitis and cement\-retained restorations were significant predictors for peri\-implantitis\. Age was significant in univariable analysis but lost significance in the adjusted model\. The frequency of maintenance visits was associated with peri\-implantitis in univariable analysis but lost significance in multivariable analysis\. Sex, smoking, and diabetes mellitus were not significantly associated with peri\-implantitis\. CONCLUSION: Xerostomia alone does not increase the risk of peri\-implantitis\. A history of periodontitis, the use of cement\-retained prosthesis, and longer follow\-up duration after prosthetic loading were associated with unfavorable implant outcomes\.

## [Effect of Rare‐Earth La Addition on Inclusion Modification Mechanism in 42CrMo Steel](../publications/89923b3826cebc525930.md)

Hong\-bin Ji; 王建梅; Yuehui Wang; Yanwei Li; Chen Chen

Rare‐earth lanthanum \(La\) improves the strength–ductility synergy of steel through inclusion modification\. This study investigates 42CrMo steels containing 0–0\.013 wt% La using SEM–EDS, thermodynamic calculations, and first‐principles calculations, clarifying the mechanism of La in improving the strength and ductility\. With increasing La content, inclusions gradually transform from elongated MnS and MnS/Al 2 O 3 composites to La‐containing inclusions\. At 0\.009 wt% La, the inclusions are effectively modified into fine, spherical La 2 O 3 –La 2 O 2 S–La 3 S 4 composites, whereas excess La \(0\.013 wt%\) causes coarsening and agglomeration into chain‐like or irregular morphologies\. Combined SEM–EDS observations and thermodynamic calculations suggest an evolution pathway of La 2 O 3 → La 2 O 2 S → LaAlO 3 → La 3 S 4 , while preformed Al 2 O 3 is difficult to modify by La\. The dominant La‐modified inclusions exhibit lower elastic moduli and hardness and better matrix compatibility\. Fine and dispersed La‐containing inclusions refine prior‐austenite grains from 32\.15 to 17\.21 μm through heterogeneous nucleation and Zener pinning, while optimized inclusion morphology alleviates local stress concentration\. At 0\.009 wt% La, the steel exhibits optimal comprehensive properties, with yield strength, tensile strength, and elongation increasing by 11\.2%, 14\.4%, and 37\.4%, respectively, compared with La‐free steel\. This study elucidates La‐induced inclusion modification and strength–ductility synergy mechanisms, providing a theoretical basis for high‐performance steel design via rare‐earth microalloying\.

## [Artificial intelligence in immovable cultural heritage research: a bibliometric and knowledge mapping review](../publications/89930a48b99807ade505.md)

Yating Wen; Marzudi Md Yunus

Abstract In recent years, the application of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in immovable cultural heritage research has expanded rapidly, supporting new approaches to heritage documentation, condition assessment, conservation, management, and public communication\. In this study, immovable cultural heritage primarily refers to historic buildings, archaeological sites, monuments, cultural landscapes, and other heritage places with fixed spatial locations\. Movable cultural objects, museum collections, and intangible cultural heritage are not systematically examined unless the relevant studies directly address the documentation, monitoring, restoration, conservation, or management of immovable heritage\. Despite the growing volume of research, existing studies have largely focused on individual technical applications, while comprehensive bibliometric analyses and knowledge\-structure mapping from a global perspective remain limited\. To address this gap, this study retrieved 382 English\-language publications from the Web of Science Core Collection covering the period from 1 January 2015 to 1 October 2025\. Using bibliometric methods and analytical tools including VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and ArcGIS, the study examines publication trends, geographical distribution, disciplinary categories, major authors, institutional affiliations, collaboration networks, thematic evolution, and emerging research topics\. The results show that publication output increased substantially after 2020\. China, Italy, and Spain were among the most productive countries and occupied important positions in the international collaboration network\. Major research themes included digital heritage, structural health monitoring, virtual reconstruction, deep learning, remote sensing, and sustainability\-related applications\. These findings indicate that AI\-related research on immovable cultural heritage is strongly represented in engineering, conservation science, computer science, remote sensing, and related technical fields\. However, this pattern should not be interpreted as evidence of a general disciplinary shift across cultural heritage studies as a whole\. Rather, it reflects the technological orientation of the literature captured by the present search strategy, which was limited to English\-language publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection\. This study maps the development and knowledge structure of AI applications in immovable cultural heritage research and provides quantitative evidence for identifying major research areas, collaboration patterns, methodological tendencies, and future research needs\.

## [Can emotions be professional? A decolonial reframing of professional identity formation](../publications/89aa9063a224126c16c9.md)

Sofia Camargo Collet; Ligia Maria Cayres Ribeiro; Wieke E\. van der Goot; Marco Antonio de Carvalho Filho; Francisco Manuel Olmos‐Vega

Medical professionalism has long been associated with rationality, emotional detachment, and self\-control\. Although often presented as universal standards of professional conduct, these norms are historically shaped by Western and individualistic epistemologies that frame emotions as threats to objectivity and ethical judgment\. Such expectations shape Professional Identity Formation \(PIF\), often generating tensions between learners’ lived experiences and institutional norms\. We argue that emotions are essential resources that qualify decision\-making by helping us understand ourselves, the other, and the context, and anticipate the consequences of our decisions, thereby being essential for learning and professional identity formation\. We draw on three decolonial perspectives\. First, research on queer identities shows how trainees act as care weavers, transforming their own experience of marginalization into a relational capacity for empathy and clinical insight\. Second, the South African philosophy of Ubuntu positions compassion and humanness not as soft skills but as constitutive markers of professional conduct grounded in communal interdependence\. Third, rooted in Freire&\#x27;s critical pedagogy, the Pedagogy of Connection defines professionalism through presence—an openness to patients’ suffering that qualifies clinical reasoning and positions the physician as an agent of social justice\. Drawing on transformative learning theory, we suggest that emotionally challenging experiences can prompt reflection and shifts in perspective that are central to professional identity formation\. Building on these perspectives, we propose reconnecting professionalism with emotions\. We argue that emotional engagement is constitutive of professional identity formation, while its expressions and legitimate forms are shaped by the contexts in which physicians learn and practice\.

## [A multi\-scale framework for identifying and validating managed aquifer recharge sites in semi\-arid Kazakhstan](../publications/89b4a4f12de422a8df9d.md)

Zhuldyzbek Onglassynov; S\. A\. Kulbekova; Raushan Amanzholova; Aldiyar Abyshev; Айгерим Алимгазина; И\.К\. Рахметов; Malis K\. Absametov

Managed Aquifer Recharge \(MAR\) has emerged as an effective approach for enhancing groundwater resources in water\-scarce regions under increasing climate variability and growing water demand\. However, most GIS\-based MAR studies are limited to regional suitability mapping, whereas the hydrogeological feasibility of identified sites is rarely verified under field conditions\. This study presents a multi\-scale framework integrating regional GIS\-based screening with detailed site\-scale verification to improve the reliability of MAR suitability assessment in southeastern Kazakhstan\. This research was conducted within the Zhetysu Alatau–Balkhash First\-Order Hydrogeological Basin to develop and evaluate a multi\-scale framework for identifying suitable MAR sites\. Regional suitability assessment combined Geographic Information Systems \(GIS\), the Analytic Hierarchy Process \(AHP\), Monte Carlo simulation, Fuzzy Gamma analysis, remote sensing, and regional hydrochemical data\. Based on the regional assessment, the Byzhy River Basin was selected as a representative site for detailed hydrological, hydrogeological, hydrochemical, LiDAR\-based, and field investigations to verify regional suitability under actual hydrogeological conditions\. The regional suitability assessment identified 21\.82% \(58\.41 km 2 \) of the representative study area as highly suitable for MAR, while Monte Carlo simulation and Fuzzy Gamma analysis confirmed the robustness of the suitability model\. Hydrological assessment indicated a positive long\-term mean potential water balance of 27\.69 mm·year −1 , suggesting sufficient water resources for MAR\. Three double\-ring infiltration tests yielded a mean field\-saturated hydraulic conductivity of 1\.92 m·day −1 \(range: 1\.86–1\.96 m·day −1 \), indicating high infiltration capacity of the Quaternary alluvial deposits\. Groundwater mineralization remained below 1 g·L −1 , and hydrogeological investigations confirmed a 50 m thick Quaternary alluvial aquifer suitable for MAR\. Long\-term daily river discharge records indicated a potential annual recharge volume of 17\.44 million m 3 , representing only 2\.33% of the effective aquifer storage capacity \(746\.8 million m 3 \), demonstrating substantial storage potential\. The close agreement between the regional suitability assessment and field investigations demonstrates that the multi\-scale framework substantially reduces uncertainty in GIS\-based MAR site identification\. By integrating regional suitability mapping with hydrological, hydrogeological, hydrochemical, LiDAR, and field investigations, the framework provides a transferable methodology for identifying and verifying MAR sites in arid and semi\-arid regions, supporting groundwater management and long\-term water resource planning\.

## [High\-throughput screening model of ilmenite flotation collectors via quantum chemistry and machine learning](../publications/89c1131c24096debe9a6.md)

Yan Long; Junhan Yang; Lanlin Yu; Fanfan Zhang; Yijun Cao; Peng Li; Jianyong He; Guixia Fan

The efficient separation between ilmenite and forsterite is critical for improving titanium resource utilization\. However, the development of novel flotation collectors still heavily relies on inefficient trial\-and\-error experimentation\. In this work, a high\-throughput computational framework integrating Quantum Chemistry \(QC\), Machine Learning \(ML\), and Molecular Dynamics \(MD\) simulations was established for the design and screening of selective collectors\. A dataset comprising 66 reported collectors was compiled, and 15 QC\-derived descriptors were calculated at the PBE0/Def2\-TZVP level\. Among the evaluated ML algorithms, Gradient Boosting Regression achieved the optimal predictive performance, confirming a pronounced nonlinear structure–activity relationship between collector binding energies and their electronic descriptors\. Feature importance analysis further identified the electron\-donating ability of primary bonding atoms \(EN DA1 \) and vertical ionization potential \(VIP\) as the dominant descriptors governing the interactions with Ti 4\+ , Fe 2\+ , and Mg 2\+ sites, revealing that electron\-donating capacity and charge distribution play decisive roles in flotation selectivity\. Accordingly, unsaturated hydroxamic acid collectors featuring C=C double bonds, including 2\-OcHA \( trans \-2\-Octenohydroxamic acid\), 2\-DeHA \( trans \-2\-Decenohydroxamic acid\), 2\-DdHA \( trans \-2\-Dodecenohydroxamic acid\), 2\-DyHA \( trans \-2\-Dodecynohydroxamic acid\), 9\-HHA \( trans \-9\-Hexadecenohydroxamic acid\), and 9\-OdHA \( trans \-9\-Octadecenohydroxamic acid\), were screened, exhibiting superior chelation selectivity toward Ti 4\+ \. MD simulations further elucidated the adsorption configurations, interfacial interaction energies, and dynamic adsorption behaviors that are inaccessible to conventional flotation experiments, corroborating the selective adsorption of the identified collectors onto ilmenite at the molecular level\. This work not only provides an efficient computational methodology and model for flotation reagent screening but also elucidates the critical collector characteristics governing ilmenite flotation performance, offering a theoretical foundation for the molecular design of novel high\-performance collectors\.

## [Investment Feasibility Analysis of the Palembang–Indralaya Toll Road](../publications/89c9ba2f6f37dd65ea08.md)

Erza Adhitya; Farida Rachmawati

The Palembang–Simpang Indralaya Toll Road, spanning 21\.93 km, is a strategic component of the Trans\-Sumatra Toll Road network, intended to improve regional connectivity and reduce logistics costs in South Sumatra\. However, average daily traffic between 2017 and 2024 reached only 26%–45% of projected levels, raising concerns about the project&\#x27;s financial viability\. This study evaluates the financial feasibility of the existing financing structure and compares alternative schemes, including the tariff\-based Base Case, Availability Payment \(AP\), 30% Viability Gap Funding \(VGF\), and asset divestment at 49%, 51%, and 100%\. Using a capital budgeting approach, financial performance was assessed through Net Present Value \(NPV\), Internal Rate of Return \(IRR\), and Payback Period \(PP\)\. Under the tariff scheme, the project generates an IRR of 10\.98%, an NPV of IDR 1\.37 trillion, and a payback period of 16 years\. The 30% VGF scheme provides the strongest financial results, increasing the IRR to 12\.41% and NPV to IDR 2\.01 trillion while reducing the payback period to 14 years\. Conversely, the AP scheme records an IRR of 4\.17% and a negative NPV of IDR 635\.43 billion, indicating financial infeasibility\. Asset divestment also weakens financial performance as the divested share increases\. These findings identify 30% VGF as the preferred financing alternative for improving investment feasibility and addressing risks arising from lower\-than\-expected traffic volumes\. The results highlight the importance of targeted public financial support in sustaining infrastructure investment under persistent demand uncertainty\. This assessment offers practical guidance for policymakers and investors selecting financing arrangements for comparable toll road developments\.

## [On the Bias Distribution of Pseudo‐Linear Regression Algorithms for Recursive Identification](../publications/89dcdf9871806cf93f47.md)

Bernard Vau; Henri Bourlès

ABSTRACT This paper presents a detailed analysis of the asymptotic bias distribution of recursive identification schemes based on Pseudo‐Linear Regression\. As shown in a previous article, the criterion asymptotically minimized is the variance of a non‐measurable signal \(called the equivalent prediction error\) when the system to be identified is in the model set\. We prove a similar but slightly weaker \(however still relevant\) result when the true system does not belong to the model set, provided that the resulting bias remains small: if the bias tends towards 0, the stationary condition of the variance of the equivalent prediction error becomes identical to that of the criterion minimized by PLR\. It is also shown that the open‐loop output error algorithm obtained with Pseudo‐Linear Regression provides a limit model which has the same bias distribution as the one obtained by the Instrumental Variable algorithm with auxiliary model\.

## [Propuesta conceptual de un modelo adaptativo basado en inteligencia artificial para la detección de fraude en transacciones internacionales: innovaciones, riesgos emergentes y aplicabilidad en PYMES de Latinoamérica](../publications/89e9bd9b55f1121dfa4a.md)

Vanessa Sanchez Del Castillo

El crecimiento de las transacciones digitales internacionales ha incrementado la exposición de las pequeñas y medianas empresas \(PYMES\) al fraude financiero, en un contexto en el que la inteligencia artificial \(IA\) puede emplearse tanto para combatir como para perpetrar este delito\. En México, se reportaron pérdidas aproximadas de 17,400 millones de pesos durante el primer semestre de 2025\. Este trabajo propone, a nivel conceptual, un modelo adaptativo de detección de fraude bajo la modalidad de Software como Servicio \(SaaS\) dirigido a PYMES latinoamericanas\. Se empleó una metodología mixta de alcance exploratorio\-descriptivo, que combinó una revisión documental narrativa, el análisis descriptivo de registros operativos agregados de una organización de remesas \(octubre de 2024 a enero de 2025\) y el diseño de una arquitectura de entrada, procesamiento y salida de datos\. En el caso analizado, 103\.720 llamadas fueron derivadas al área de fraude y solo el 33,53 % se confirmó como tal, lo que evidencia la fricción que generan los sistemas basados en reglas fijas\. El modelo propuesto combina aprendizaje supervisado, aprendizaje no supervisado y revisión humana, y está diseñado para reducir esa fricción sin descuidar la seguridad\. Su desempeño no fue medido en este estudio y requiere validación empírica posterior\.

## [The cognition of dynamic evaluation of operating room environmental quality among medical staff: a qualitative study](../publications/89f656ade0083c4880c1.md)

Yanan Li; Tong Zhang; 边冬梅

Objective This qualitative study, guided by the Donabedian three\-dimensional quality model, aimed to explore the real perceptions of multidisciplinary healthcare professionals regarding the dynamic evaluation of the operating room environment quality\. The ultimate goal was to identify current management deficiencies and propose evidence\-based strategies for optimization\. Method Using a descriptive qualitative design with a hybrid analytic orientation, purposive sampling recruited 7 operating\-room nurses, 6 surgeons, 5 anesthesiologists, and 2 infection\-control specialists from 4 tertiary Grade A hospitals\. After ethics approval, formal semi\-structured interviews were conducted in March 2026\. Interview data were transcribed, manually coded, and analyzed in NVivo 15\.0 using Colaizzi&\#x27;s method\. The Donabedian model informed the interview guide and later organization of evaluation\-related categories\. Results Three core themes were extracted: \(1\) the four\-dimensional connotation of operating\-room environmental quality, comprising physical, chemical, biological, and humanistic dimensions; \(2\) nine preliminary candidate indicators for dynamic evaluation, grouped across structure, process, and outcome domains; and \(3\) healthcare professionals&\#x27; perceptions of potential safety and health implications for staff and patients\. These findings highlight a gap between current static monitoring practices and the dynamic nature of intraoperative environmental risks\. Conclusion Participants&\#x27; accounts suggest that a preliminary candidate framework for dynamic evaluation could incorporate structural conditions, process monitoring, and outcome\-related feedback\. Integrated management that considers both occupational health and patient safety represents a practice implication to be empirically evaluated\. This study provides a qualitative foundation for subsequent Delphi consultation and psychometric or empirical validation of a dynamic OR environmental assessment framework\.

## [Chemical Equilibrium Modulated Crystallization of 2D Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance and Robust Dual‐Mode Photonic Detection](../publications/8a11676c3fc303c3b708.md)

Kailian Dong; Yan Zhang; Hongling Guan; Wenlong Shao; Haipeng Di; Guoyi Chen; Hongyi Fang; Zhou Shun; Fancheng Meng; Weijun Ke; Guojia Fang

ABSTRACT 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum‐well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection\. However, synergistically driving efficient carrier extraction and rapid radiative recombination within monolithic single crystals \(SC\) remains a fundamental challenge\. Herein, a room‐temperature chemical equilibrium‐modulated crystallization strategy is demonstrated to synthesize centimeter‐scale 2D \(PA\) 2 PbBr 4 \(PPB\) SCs\. The use of a hygroscopic acid‐base reactive agent precisely regulates the solvent evaporation kinetics, suppressing stochastic nucleation and yielding high‐quality SCs with suppressed light scattering\. Consequently, planar PPB photodetectors \(PDs\) exhibit a notable and robust UV response, featuring a large on/off ratio of 2\.77 × 10 4 , a wide linear dynamic range of 159 dB, and an ultra‐low limit of detection of 3\.5 nW cm −2 \. Simultaneously, the intense exciton confinement endows the PPB SCs with strong radioluminescence and robust radiation stability\. Both SCs and flexible film scintillators demonstrate excellent practical x‐ray imaging capabilities\. Crucially, the absence of grain boundaries inherently mitigates internal light scattering, enabling SC scintillators to achieve an impressive spatial resolution up to 26\.5 lp mm −1 , representing one of the highest values among the reported metal halide SC scintillators\. This work establishes a kinetically control for high‐quality SCs synthesis and provides valuable insights for high‐performance and robust dual‐mode photonic detection\.

## [Ultrasound‐Triggered piRNA Delivery Using Biomimetic Phase‐Changeable Nanoparticles for Theranostics of Myocardial Infarction](../publications/8a1ea8bb7a70ad986e31.md)

Yajun Zhang; Hongzhao Qi; Yanyan Yang; Feng Wang; Tiantian Han; Yanbei Lei; Xiaolu Li; Zhibin Wang; Hua Qu; Tao Yu; Pin Sun

ABSTRACT Myocardial infarction \(MI\) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity, and effective strategies to prevent adverse remodeling are limited\. Here, we identify piR‐1873 as a cardioprotective piRNA that is down‐regulated in MI patients, mouse models, and H 2 O 2 ‐treated cardiomyocytes\. Serum piR‐1873 levels correlated with MI biomarkers, suggesting its potential as a complementary biomarker, with an area under the curve \(AUC\) of 0\.8389\. Mechanistically, piR‐1873 directly targeted Usp2 and inhibited RIP1/RIP3/MLKL‐mediated necroptosis\. To achieve efficient delivery, we developed ultrasound \(US\)‐responsive piRNA nanoparticles \(piR‐NPs\) consisting of a perfluorohexane \(PFH\) phase‐change core loaded with piR‐1873 and coated with a cardiomyocyte membrane shell\. In vitro, piR‐NPs enhanced piR‐1873 delivery and suppressed cardiomyocyte necroptosis, with US further improving these effects\. In MI mice, piR‐NPs accumulated in infarcted myocardium, and US enhanced nanoparticle retention, resulting in improved cardiac function, reduced fibrosis, and attenuated necroptosis without detectable systemic toxicity\. Collectively, this study reveals the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of piR‐1873 and establishes a biomimetic, US‐triggered piRNA delivery platform for MI treatment\.

## [ANALISIS ALGORITMA RANDOM FOREST DAN SURVIVAL ANALYSIS TERHADAP FAKTOR YANG MEMPENGARUHI WAKTU PENYELESAIAN PERKARA DI PENGADILAN AGAMA LUBUK PAKAM KELAS 1A \- DELI SERDANG](../publications/8a31e39d1be3cbaea48a.md)

Nur Azizah Harahap; Muhammad Iqbal; Rian Farta Wijaya

The increasing number of cases in religious courts poses challenges in maintaining consistency in case resolution time\. This study aims to analyze factors affecting case resolution time using Random Forest and Survival Analysis methods\.The dataset consists of case records from the Religious Court of Lubuk Pakam Class IA, Deli Serdang, covering March 2025 to March 2026\. Random Forest is used to classify case duration and identify dominant variables, while Survival Analysis with the Cox Proportional Hazards model is applied to examine the effect of variables on resolution time\.The results show that the Random Forest model achieves an accuracy of 66%, with the number of hearings identified as the most dominant factor \(feature importance = 0\.634\)\. Survival Analysis indicates that the number of hearings has a hazard ratio of 0\.78, suggesting that an increase in hearings tends to prolong case resolution time\. The concordance value of 0\.70 indicates a reasonably good predictive performance\.These findings indicate that operational factors, particularly the number of hearings and the presence of parties, significantly influence case resolution time\.

## [The glycolysis–neurotransmitter axis: a missing link in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma biology](../publications/8a36e9ea2ab27ec04beb.md)

Vinay Bisen; Ashmita Das; Yogita Dhurandhar; Ashok Kumar Varma; Gauri Misra; Kamta Prashad Namdeo

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma remains a major clinical challenge because of its high rates of recurrence, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance despite advances in treatment\. Enhanced glycolysis and neurotransmitter signalling are independently recognised as key drivers of tumour progression; however, their mechanistic relationship remains poorly understood, highlighting the need for an integrated framework that explains how metabolic reprogramming influences neural signalling in tumour progression\. Building on the established fields of cancer metabolism and cancer neuroscience, we propose a focused, HNSCC\-specific extension of these frameworks: aberrant glycolytic reprogramming is hypothesised to function as a key upstream regulator of neurotransmitter remodelling, contributing to tumour progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance\. To keep the model testable, we narrow our primary focus to the lactate–HIF\-1α–GPR81–NGF/BDNF axis and its influence on adrenergic \(sympathetic\) signalling, treating cholinergic and glutamatergic contributions as secondary, exploratory components\. Glycolysis\-induced metabolic alterations, including lactate accumulation, intracellular metabolite availability, and tumour microenvironment acidification, are hypothesised to regulate neurotransmitter synthesis, release, and receptor\-mediated signalling, creating a self\-reinforcing neuro\-metabolic feedback loop that enhances tumour aggressiveness, although non\-metabolic drivers such as autonomic nerve activity and psychological stress are also acknowledged as potential contributors to this signalling\. This hypothesis can be evaluated using complementary molecular, cellular, and translational approaches by correlating glycolytic activity with neurotransmitter expression and assessing the biological consequences of glycolytic modulation; quantification of glycolytic markers and neurotransmitter profiles, together with functional analyses and clinical correlation studies, would determine whether glycolysis acts as an upstream regulator of neurotransmitter remodelling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma\. The proposed glycolysis–neurotransmitter axis thus provides a biologically plausible and experimentally testable framework that integrates metabolic and neural mechanisms in this cancer; if validated, this model could offer preliminary support for metabolism\-associated neurotransmitter biomarkers and help inform future, rigorously validated metabolism\-directed therapeutic strategies; such translational applications remain speculative and contingent on further experimental and clinical validation\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in Construction Management Enhancing Decision Making A cross a Project Life Cycle: throught A Machine Learning Method](../publications/8a4727d9c426e97fd1d8.md)

Nedjwa Elafri; Abdallah Lalmi; Badr\-Eddine BOUMALI; Koudoua Ferhati

The construction industry, which creates 13% of the world’s GDP, suffers from cost overruns of 28% and delays of over 42%, yet is still undigitized\. AI has the promise of transforming management in the areas of cost, time and safety\. This research provides a systematic review of AI applications and performs an original machine learning analysis on seven algorithms, i\.e\., Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, K\-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Stacking Ensemble, Artificial Neural Networks, and XGBoost on 139 Indian road projects with 44 risk factors\. XGBoost performed the best with 82\.50% accuracy and 84\.21% F1\-score\. The most important concerns were the delay in decision\-making \(0\.152\), cash flow problems \(0\.082\) and cost underestimate \(0\.071\)\. Case studies demonstrate AI’s capabilities: 98\.7% accurate cost estimation, 94\.36% delay prediction via deep learning, and 97% safety monitoring with computer vision\. These findings underscore the importance of ensemble ML in proactive, data\-driven risk management, bringing projects into a predictive framework rather than reactive\.

## [From conversation to green intention: how perceived AI chatbot empathy shapes sustainable travel](../publications/8a4b9c124d04b6e9e850.md)

Sohail Ahmad; Muhammad Ashfaq; Jing Song; Sai Yan

Recent developments in artificial intelligence \(AI\) have expanded the role of conversational agents in hospitality and travel service encounters\. However, it remains unclear how the conversational characteristics of AI become psychologically meaningful and relate to travelers’ sustainable decision\-making\. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory \(CAT\), this study examines the associations between Chatbot Conversational Quality \(CCQ\) and Green Travel Intention \(GTI\) through the sequential roles of Perceived Chatbot Empathy \(PCE\) and Green Travel Motivation \(GTM\), while considering Eco\-Friendly Customer Innovativeness \(EFCI\) as a boundary condition\. Survey data from 400 travelers show that CCQ is associated with PCE, which in turn is associated with stronger GTM and, subsequently, higher GTI\. EFCI strengthens the PCE\-GTM relationship but does not significantly moderate GTM\-GTI, suggesting greater relevance during motivation formation than motivation\-to\-intention translation\. The findings show how conversational AI interactions can acquire socio\-emotional meaning in hospitality contexts and highlight customer heterogeneity in sustainability\-related decisions\.

## [Digitalisasi Pembayaran UMKM Desa Salohe: Pendampingan Pembuatan QRIS dalam Perspektif Maqashid Syariah untuk Peningkatan Inklusi Keuangan](../publications/8a5ea6452f6b1fe39a58.md)

Andi Jahnur Itsnaieni Kaffah; Hikma Ramadhani; Nur Indah Sari; Aulia haerunnisa; Munawarah; Muhammad Fahrul; Najmi Raehani; Nasrullah; Gita; Nursalam

Kesenjangan adopsi pembayaran digital masih menjadi tantangan bagi pelaku usaha mikro, kecil, dan menengah \(UMKM\) di wilayah perdesaan\. Survei awal terhadap tujuh pelaku UMKM di Desa Salohe, Kecamatan Sinjai Timur, Kabupaten Sinjai, menunjukkan bahwa enam pelaku belum pernah menggunakan pembayaran digital, sedangkan satu pelaku telah mengetahui QRIS tetapi belum mendaftarkan usahanya\. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan mendampingi pelaku UMKM dalam pembuatan dan penggunaan Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard \(QRIS\) serta menelaah relevansinya dengan prinsip maqashid syariah\. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 13 Agustus–23 September 2026 melalui empat tahapan, yaitu survei kebutuhan, sosialisasi program, pendampingan pendaftaran melalui DANA Bisnis, serta pelatihan dan pendampingan penggunaan\. Dari tujuh UMKM yang disurvei, tiga berhasil menyelesaikan pendaftaran dan verifikasi QRIS\. Empat lainnya belum mengaktifkan QRIS karena kendala dokumen identitas atau pilihan untuk tetap menggunakan transfer bank manual dan uang tunai\. Tiga pelaku yang memiliki akun aktif mengikuti simulasi penerimaan pembayaran, pemeriksaan notifikasi, dan pengecekan riwayat transaksi\. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pendampingan teknis dapat membantu sebagian pelaku usaha mengakses pembayaran digital, meskipun adopsi belum merata\. Dalam perspektif maqashid syariah, riwayat transaksi digital berpotensi mendukung perlindungan harta \(hifz al\-mal\), sedangkan perluasan kesempatan mengakses layanan pembayaran mencerminkan orientasi keadilan \(al\-‘adl\)\. Namun, kegiatan ini tidak mengukur perubahan pendapatan atau inklusi keuangan pada tingkat populasi\.

## [Fast Matrix Multiplication for Database Query Processing](../publications/8a6288bdcd3784306ba3.md)

Xiao Hu

Motivation : Modern data analytical workloads – from graph processing to machine learning – have evolved significantly, increasingly combining JOIN with additional relational\-algebra operators and aggregate functions \(e\.g\., PROJECT and COUNT\)\. Traditionally, database query processing has been dominated by discrete, logicbased primitives such as for\-loops \[9, 10, 13\], tree decompositions \[4\], and data partitioning \[6, 8\], which are fundamentally combinatorial \. However, the landscape changes when examining graph analytics, where algebraic algorithms – which treat query processing as a series of high\-dimensional tensor or matrix operations – have achieved strictly lower theoretical complexity than the best\-known combinatorial counterparts\. Fast matrix multiplication \(FMM\) bridges this gap\. As modern data systems increasingly integrate dedicated linear algebra kernels \(e\.g\., for ML\), repurposing these optimized algebraic engines for classical query processing offers immense potential\. This drives the core insight of our research: a comprehensive exploration of FMM within database query engines, bringing the theoretical power of algebraic techniques to practical data systems\.

## [Three LiDARs, Twenty\-Five Datasets: Cross\-Source Generalization in Tree\-Species Recognition](../publications/8a694de7491eaccb75b9.md)

Jae Joong Lee; Bedrich Benes

FOR\-species20K is the largest public LiDAR benchmark for tree\-species classification, pooling 25 independently collected terrestrial, mobile, and airborne laser\-scanning datasets across 33 species\. We introduce a multi\-resolution, multi\-view ConvNeXtV2 model that improves official hidden\-test accuracy from 79\.5% to 85\.0%, ranking first at the time of submission\. We then examine what this score measures\. Because the hidden test is species\-balanced, its overall accuracy is more comparable to a macro metric than to accuracy under the public set&\#x27;s long\-tailed distribution\. Moreover, the official random split places every source dataset in both training and evaluation\. A logistic probe recovers source identity from out\-of\-fold model probabilities with 69% accuracy, while geometric features identify the source above 90% within two widely shared species; 18 of the 33 species occur in only one source\. Under a source\-species\-cell holdout, evaluated on 5,566 trees from eight eligible species that retain the same LiDAR\-type training support in other sources, the unweighted species mean falls from 82% to 36%, and tree\-weighted accuracy falls from 95% to 60%\. Count\-matched retraining and experiments with two alternative backbones indicate that this gap is not explained by reduced training support alone, while an external PureForest experiment shows a smaller but consistent grouped\-split effect\. These results establish the 85% leaderboard score as strong in\-distribution performance, but not as an estimate of source\-disjoint generalization, motivating balanced metrics and source\-aware evaluation\. The code is available at: https://github\.com/JaeLee18/FOR20K\-lidar\-tree\-species

## [INFLAMMATION AND IMMUNE\-MEDIATED DISEASES IN COMPANION ANIMALS: PATHOLOGICAL MECHANISMS, DIAGNOSTIC APPROACHES AND EMERGING PERSPECTIVES](../publications/8a6a325ff40446a73a3f.md)

Nancy Bajaj; Anushri Tiwari; Prateek Mishra; Drishti Jain; Surya Gond

Inflammation is a crucial defense mechanism against infection, tissue damage, and other harmful stimuli\. However, persistent or dysregulated inflammation can lead to tissue damage and immune\-mediated disease\. Significant inflammatory and immune\-mediated disorders in dogs and cats include immune\-mediated hemolytic anemia \(IMHA\), immune\-mediated thrombocytopenia, immune\-mediated polyarthritis, chronic inflammatory enteropathies, dermatological conditions, renal disease, and inflammatory disorders of the nervous system\. These conditions include complex interactions between innate and adaptive immunity, cytokines, genetic susceptibility, environmental factors, and the microbiome\. Histopathology is an essential diagnostic method even if immunohistochemistry, molecular diagnostics, and inflammatory biomarkers provide additional information\. Emerging technologies like digital pathology, artificial intelligence, spatial biology, and multi\-omics may improve future treatment strategies and disease characterization\.

## [From simulation to reality: Empirical validation of the superiority of da in indexing sensitivity in recognition\-memory experiments\.](../publications/8a74ff6e32b26cc4fb04.md)

Adva Levi; Caren M\. Rotello; Yonatan Goshen‐Gottstein

The selection of an accuracy \(sensitivity\) measure is a pivotal decision faced by researchers who use binary judgments\.An abundance of measures has been developed to index sensitivity independent of participants&\#x27; bias\.However, recent Monte Carlo simulations ran in our lab found that all commonly used measures confound sensitivity with bias, with the exception of our proposed version of the signal\-detection measure d\-sub\-a \(denoted d a \), based on confidence ratings rather than binary responses\.Nevertheless, empirical confirmation in real\-world experiments is needed to validate any measure\.To this end, we ran two large\-scale recognition studies that can serve as a proof of concept to all binary tasks\.Sensitivity was not manipulated at encoding, while we manipulated bias at test\.When comparing these iso\-sensitive conditions, valid measures should yield erroneous significant results at approximately 5% \(or α\)\.Using resampling, we repeatedly ran the experiment to derive rates of Type\-I errors\.Only d a , but not P r , A′, or d′, demonstrated the desired 5% rate of Type\-I errors across different experimental designs, sample sizes, and number of trials\.We also used our data to assess statistical power\.We compared d a &\#x27;s ability to detect genuine sensitivity differences and found detection rates similar to all other measures tested\.Combined with our simulation results, these empirical findings provide compelling evidence that d a is a valid and powerful sensitivity measure\.Our findings offer a validated measure that can reduce the hazards of the measurement crisis that plague recognition\-memory research\.Our large data sets, available online, provide opportunities for future analyses\.

## [Exploring Students&\#x27; Perceptions of Using the ChatGPT Voice Conversation Feature for Informal English\-Speaking Practice](../publications/8a757739616a4629897b.md)

Rizki Rayana

The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), especially with generative AI chatbots, is opening innovative options for autonomous language learning\. This qualitative descriptive study investigates university students’ impressions of utilizing the ChatGPT Voice Conversation function for informal English speaking practice\. Twelve Indonesian university students of English education major who used the feature to practice speaking by themselves for four weeks were selected by purposive sampling technique and then interviewed using semi\-structured interview\. The data collected were examined using Braun and Clarke thematic analysis methodology\. The preliminary data suggest that students view the ChatGPT Voice Conversation feature as a low\-anxiety, highly accessible and interactive tool that helps them improve speaking fluency and learn vocabulary\. However, several significant shortcomings were detected including technical constraints such as occasional odd prosody, conversational disconnects and the absence of non\-verbal cues\. The study suggests that AI speech features, while useful as scaffolding for informal conversation, should be used to supplement, not substitute for, human\-human contact in language instruction

## [B\-bKM &amp; LDP: a secure, cost\-effective and efficient key management system for social internet of vehicles](../publications/8a7d715934dfcfbe5b20.md)

Maham Iftikhar; Munam Ali Shah; Hasan Shojaa Alkahtani; Sidra Tahir

The Social Internet of Vehicles \(SIoV\) combines vehicular networks with social networking principles to support advanced services such as entertainment, personalized recommendations, and smarter route planning\. Despite its potential, SIoV faces major challenges due to its highly dynamic environment, including secure key management, protection of location privacy, scalability, and communication latency\. Additionally, adaptability, scalability, and efficient resource discovery remain major challenges in SIoV environments\. To overcome these issues, this article introduces B\-bKM, a blockchain\-based key management framework strengthened with Local Differential Privacy \(LDP\)\. The proposed approach redesigns the traditional blockchain architecture by incorporating three key features: \(i\) a lightweight miner election mechanism to reduce overhead, \(ii\) personalized transaction chains that allow vehicles to securely manage and migrate cryptographic keys, and \(iii\) LDP\-based location perturbation to safeguard users’ privacy\. Unlike cloud\-dependent solutions, B\-bKM distributes trust across the network and removes single points of failure by limiting blockchain operations to cluster heads\. Extensive simulations using real vehicular mobility data show that B\-bKM significantly lowers communication latency and transmission costs while improving throughput and achieving stronger k\-anonymity compared to existing baseline schemes\. These results demonstrate that B\-bKM offers a secure, efficient, and privacy\-preserving key management solution suitable for large\-scale SIoV systems\.

## [Individualized Theta Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Modulates Mnemonic Discrimination and ERP Responses to Positive Information in Individuals With Elevated Depressive Symptoms](../publications/8a7ec522187b7389a420.md)

Xinyu Huang; Min Zhou; Chun Wang; Yuxin Huang; Wenchang Wang; Jianfei Shao; Junyu Mao; Jiaqi Li; Zhang Lei; Rong Ye; Chunyan Zhu; Yanghua Tian; Kongliang He; 余凤琼; Kai Wang

Individuals with elevated depressive symptoms often show impairments in positive memory processing\. This randomized, double\-blind study investigated whether individualized theta\-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation \(tACS\) using an OFC\-oriented montage modulates mnemonic discrimination and ERP responses to positive information\. Sixty\-one individuals with elevated depressive symptoms received either real or sham stimulation before completing an emotional mnemonic discrimination task\. Behavioral results showed that lure discrimination increased following real stimulation but not sham stimulation\. EEG results showed that real stimulation modulated ERP responses during positive memory encoding and retrieval, as reflected by increased late positive potential \(LPP\) amplitudes during encoding and altered early retrieval\-related ERP amplitudes\. ## [A Juridical Review of Sharia Financial Technology Dispute Resolution in Indonesia](../publications/8a7eceda4068e87ee908.md)

Nabilah Azmi Lubis; Cahaya Permata

The development of sharia\-based financial technology \(fintech\) in Indonesia has experienced significant growth in line with the increasing demand for digital financing services that operate in accordance with Islamic sharia principles\. Data from the Financial Services Authority \(OJK\) indicate that, as of early 2025, dozens of Information Technology\-Based Joint Funding Services \(Layanan Pendanaan Bersama Berbasis Teknologi Informasi/LPBBTI\) providers were operating based on sharia principles, while consumer complaints in the financial services sector processed by the Alternative Dispute Resolution Institution for Financial Services Sector \(Lembaga Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa Sektor Jasa Keuangan/LAPS SJK\) also included a significant proportion from the fintech sector\. Cases of payment defaults and business activity restrictions affecting sharia\-based fintech peer\-to\-peer lending providers in late 2025 underscore the urgent need for effective dispute resolution mechanisms\. This study aims to analyze the relevant laws and regulations, examine dispute resolution mechanisms, and assess the effectiveness of regulations and dispute resolution institutions for sharia\-based fintech in Indonesia\. This study employs a normative juridical method using statutory and conceptual approaches, supported by secondary data consisting of laws and regulations, fatwas issued by the National Sharia Board of the Indonesian Ulema Council \(DSN\-MUI\), Constitutional Court decisions, and legal literature, which are analyzed using a qualitative\-descriptive method\. The results show that the legal framework for dispute resolution in sharia\-based fintech is dispersed across Law Number 4 of 2023, Financial Services Authority Regulation Number 40/POJK\.03/2024, and Financial Services Authority Regulation Number 61/POJK\.07/2020, with a tiered mechanism ranging from internal dispute resolution, mediation and arbitration through LAPS SJK, to litigation before the Religious Courts\. This study also identifies problems concerning the unclear jurisdiction of dispute resolution institutions, limited availability of human resources with sharia certification, and the limited enforceability of alternative dispute resolution decisions, which hinder the effectiveness of legal protection for sharia\-based fintech consumers\.

## [Strategic piano practice in cognitive and metacognitive regulation](../publications/8a8f7a649c6e7347a9a1.md)

Yiling Li

This integrative review synthesizes evidence on how cognitive, metacognitive, and repetition\-regulation processes shape strategic piano practice\. The review corpus comprised 63 empirical, review, and theoretical sources spanning music education, cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and motor learning; the original corpus was re\-screened and updated through September 2026\. Piano practice is defined here as intentional work undertaken to prepare, stabilise, evaluate, or adapt a performance, including keyboard rehearsal, score analysis, mental rehearsal, and recording\-based review\. The synthesis focuses primarily on advanced and professional pianists working in Western classical solo and studio traditions, while evidence from children, novices, and broader instrumental settings is used to identify developmental and contextual boundaries\. Findings indicate that segmentation, tempo manipulation, hands\-separate work, auditory imagery, goal setting, self\-monitoring, and delayed self\-assessment become effective when they are selected and revised in response to performance evidence\. Unvaried repetition may produce immediate fluency that does not necessarily predict durable retention, whereas strategically varied trials can expose errors and strengthen adaptability\. The proposed model aligns these processes with cyclical self\-regulated learning: forethought guides strategy choice, performance generates evidence, and self\-reflection updates subsequent goals and repetitions\. The review supports explicit strategy instruction while cautioning that effects depend on expertise, task, repertoire, feedback source, and musical goal\.

## [Early Dual\-path Detail Preservation for Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation with U\-Net](../publications/8a967518360b072d97e7.md)

Lukman Hakim; Mochammad Lutfi; Cahya Bagus Sanjaya; Setiawan Cahyono Putro; Muthu Subash Kavitha; Qien Yu

Thin retinal vessels can be attenuated during early encoder downsampling while contributing little to conventional overlap scores\.We propose Dual\-Path Detail Preservation \(DPD\), a low\-overhead U\-Net modification that retains max\-pooling and adds zero\-initialised, phase\-resolved residuals beside the first two encoder reductions\.Standard U\-Net and DPD were compared over three training seeds on the official DRIVE test set and by datasetspecific out\-of\-fold \(OOF\) evaluation on STARE and subject\-grouped CHASE\_DB1\.On DRIVE, DPD increased sensitivity from 0\.8251 to 0\.8377 and reduced thin\-vessel false negatives by 5\.52%\.A two\-way seed\-and\-case bootstrap retained confidence intervals excluding zero for sensitivity and thin\-vessel false\-negative reduction, whereas missed\-branch and coverage effects became seed\-sensitive\.The primary recovery direction also persisted across 11 prespecified structural\-diagnostic settings and both DRIVE manual annotations\.STARE and CHASE\_DB1 showed smaller, mixed, seed\-dependent effects, with all two\-way OOF intervals including zero\.DPD adds 0\.95% trainable parameters and approximately 2\.70% convolutional GMACs\.The evidence supports a targeted, dataset\-conditional improvement in thin\-vessel recovery rather than universal pixel\-level superiority\.

## [Hospital and health\-center bed expansion and persistent relative mismatch across geometry\-stable non\-district Chinese counties, 2015–2023](../publications/8a9c829cdd307e5b08f5.md)

Kai Dai; Ziao Chen; Ling Wang; Zihao Lin; Yiqiang Feng

Introduction Territorial health equity depends not only on expanding health resources but also on aligning local capacity with territorial planning contexts\. We examined whether changes in hospital and health\-center bed allocation were associated more strongly with territorial planning context or local fiscal\-economic capacity\. Methods We analyzed a 2015\-2023 panel of 1,787 geometry\-stable non\-district counties in China\. The analysis combined county and province\-by\-year fixed effects, long\-difference models, block\-level Shapley decomposition, high\-mismatch\-state transitions, spatial diagnostics, discrete\-time exit models, and adjacent\-county pair comparisons\. Results Median beds per 10,000 registered residents increased from 35\.1 in 2015 to 54\.0 in 2023, whereas the distribution of relative planning\-supply mismatch changed little\. Planning\-context and capacity blocks explained similarly small shares of annual variation in total beds\. For bed density, the larger baseline planning\-context share was driven primarily by the negative population coefficient and did not indicate allocation aligned with observed healthcare need\. Higher initial capacity was associated with greater cumulative bed\-density growth, lower relative mismatch, and a higher probability of exiting the high\-mismatch state\. Among county\-years previously classified as high\-mismatch, 84\.0% remained in that state in the following year\. Relative mismatch remained spatially clustered, but prefecture boundaries did not significantly amplify capacity\-related bed\-density gaps\. Discussion Aggregate expansion, relative territorial alignment, and recovery from persistent high mismatch represent distinct health\-system outcomes\. The findings support context\-sensitive allocation, capacity\-sensitive financing, and duration\-sensitive monitoring, while remaining associational rather than causal\.

## [Impacto de la inteligencia artificial generativa en procesos de creación de animación digital e ilustración\.](../publications/8a9ca2f0a4f6be40ed55.md)

Julieth Alejandra Gamboa Chan; Damián Uriel Rosado Castellanos; Farid Yehoshuah Mendicuti Gómez; César Iván De la Cruz Tec

La inteligencia artificial \(IA\) generativa ha llegado a cambiar las reglas en la creación de imágenes, transformando los flujos de trabajo tradicionales y redefiniendo la ontología del artista\. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el impacto de las herramientas algorítmicas en los procesos de creación de la animación digital y la ilustración desde un enfoque teórico\-conceptual\. Se ejecutó una revisión sistemática de la literatura con un enfoque cualitativo, fundamentada en las directrices de la declaración PRISMA\. La búsqueda se realizó en las bases de datos Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Dialnet e IEEE Xplore, conformando una muestra documental definitiva de 50 artículos científicos revisados por pares\. Los hallazgos se estructuraron en dos macro\-categorías: el impacto técnico y el impacto humano\. Por un lado, se evidencia una reconfiguración operativa del pipeline mediante la automatización del modelado 3D, el control de movimiento 2D y la eficiencia del renderizado en la nube\. Por otro lado, se devela una mutación en el proceso creativo que desplaza el esfuerzo manual hacia la curaduría visual, forzando la reconfiguración de las prácticas pedagógicas en la educación superior y desatando severas tensiones tecno\-éticas debido al vacío legal sobre los derechos de autor y la propiedad intelectual\.

## [A multi\-objective synergistic optimization framework for gas distribution quality and output performance in proton exchange membrane fuel cells](../publications/8aa5840359817803afea.md)

Mu Qing; Haolong Li

Proton exchange membrane fuel cells \(PEMFCs\) are promising electrochemical energy conversion devices for hydrogen\-based power generation\. However, their output performance and internal oxygen distribution are highly sensitive to operating conditions, making it challenging to simultaneously maintain electrochemical output, oxygen supply sufficiency, and gas distribution uniformity\. To address this issue, this paper proposes a synergistic optimization framework that integrates interpretable machine learning, surrogate modeling, and multi\-objective optimization\. First, a Random\-Forest\-based local interpretable model is developed to quantify the effects of operating parameters on key performance indicators and to identify the decision variables for subsequent optimization\. Then, the mean oxygen concentration in the catalyst layer, the oxygen concentration standard deviation, and the output current density are selected as optimization objectives to represent oxygen supply sufficiency, oxygen distribution uniformity, and electrochemical output capability, respectively\. An iTransformer\-inspired variable\-token regression model is further constructed to characterize the nonlinear mapping between operating parameters and performance responses, thereby reducing the computational cost of repeated multiphysics simulations\. Based on 2,000 samples, the proposed surrogate achieves the lowest mean normalized RMSE of 0\.2920±0\.0105% over 10 repeated data partitions among the six compared surrogate models\. The three\-dimensional multiphysics model is further validated against experimental polarization measurements under the baseline operating condition, achieving an R2 of 0\.9939 and an RMSE of 0\.0106 V\. Quantitative comparisons based on hypervolume, inverted generational distance, and spacing support the use of NSGA\-II for Pareto search\. Entropy\-weighted LINMAP is subsequently employed to identify one load\-dependent preferred compromise operating condition at each prescribed voltage\. Three\-dimensional back\-calculation shows that the maximum surrogate\-to\-model deviations for the three optimization objectives remain below 1\.11%\. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for coordinating oxygen supply, gas\-distribution uniformity, and electrochemical output under different PEMFC operating conditions\.

## [Machine Learning\-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK\-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple\-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells](../publications/8aa65fe0c1edc9d58670.md)

Wanxin Cao; Bin Jiang; Xiangyin Chi; Wan Li; Hong Yang; Xiaoxue Li; Yuxuan Zhao; Xu Zhang; Rui Meng; Yanyu Cang; Guanhua Du; Jinhua Wang

Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase \(MELK\) is a cell cycle\-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies that has been controversially pursued as an anticancer target\. Here we applied an integrated computational workflow combining four machine learning regressors \(Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM\), hierarchical Glide docking \(HTVS to SP to XP\), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation to a \~15\.58 million\-compound commercial library, yielding 12 prioritized candidates\. Three commercially available compounds \(CPD4, CPD6, CPD10\) were evaluated in an antiproliferative panel\. CPD6 emerged as the most active hit, with IC50 values of 1\.44 μM in MDA\-MB\-468 and 1\.66 μM in H1299, modestly exceeding the reference compound MELK\-8a under the same assay conditions \(2\.48 and 2\.51 μM, respectively\)\. Cellular thermal shift assay in cell lysates provided biochemical evidence of MELK engagement, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations supported a plausible computationally predicted binding mode in the MELK kinase domain\. Colony formation, EdU incorporation, and cell cycle analyses demonstrated dose\-dependent antiproliferative effects and G2/M arrest, with concomitant downregulation of CDC25C, CDK1, and Cyclin B1\. These findings support CPD6 as a structurally novel, cell\-active antiproliferative lead with a chemically distinct scaffold, evidence of MELK target engagement, preferential activity against cancer cells, and a clear G2/M arrest phenotype; reduced MELK substrate phosphorylation and partial rescue by MELK overexpression further support MELK\-dependent activity, warranting further hit\-to\-lead optimization and selectivity profiling\.

## [Adaptive Interfacial Recognition Through Proton‐Coupled Force Reconfiguration in MOF@COF Composites](../publications/8aae9cf71d6c3d05e132.md)

Zhen Zhang; 张新忠; Zimo Huang; Xuemei Wang; Xinzhen Du; Xiaoquan Lu

ABSTRACT Achieving dynamic, in situ switchable molecular recognition in porous composites remains challenging due to the difficulty of precisely modulating interfacial noncovalent interactions at the atomic level\. Here, we demonstrated that proton‐coupled interfacial force reconstruction served as a general and efficient regulatory strategy to control adsorption‐desorption behaviors in a metal‐organic framework \(MOFs\)‐based covalent organic framework \(COF\) composite, NH 2 ‐UiO‐66@COF‐TpDBA \(NU@FC\)\. Reversible protonation‐deprotonation at carboxyl sites induced precise redistribution of the interfacial noncovalent force field, thereby endowing switchable molecular capture and markedly improving the utilization efficiency of interfacial active sites, constructing a stimuli‐responsive adsorption platform featuring molecular capture and release\. This atomic‐scale regulation, coupled with solvent‐ triggered microenvironment modulation, allowed adaptive recognition of polychlorinated biphenyls \(PCBs\) under diverse environments\. Combined with the mechanically reinforced sheath‐tube‐protected solid‐phase microextraction device \(STP‐SPME\), this proton‐responsive interfacial regulation strategy was extended to an in situ, low‐cost, anti‐interference sample pretreatment system, achieving reliable identification and efficient extraction of trace organic pollutants from complex environmental matrices\. Beyond device‐level performance, this study established proton‐coupled force reconstruction as a general design principle for constructing intelligently responsive MOF‐COF composites, bridging atomic‐scale interfacial modulation with expansive environmental analysis\.

## [EMO: A Closed\-Loop Test\-Time Computation Framework via Alternating Context Optimization and Logits Steering](../publications/8abdc1e044e581c66a28.md)

Wei Xia; Yehui Tang; Zhi\-Hong Deng

Test\-time context optimization adapts frozen language models through textual feedback, but ordinary conditional generation provides no separate control over how strongly to reinforce the distributional changes induced by a context update\. We introduce EMO, a training\-free framework inspired by expectation\-\-maximization that alternates question\-specific context estimation \(E\-step\) and distribution refinement \(M\-step\)\. The E\-step revises a system context using textual gradients from an external judge without access to gold answers\. The M\-step contrasts next\-token distributions under the revised and preceding contexts at a shared prefix to construct a confidence\-constrained logit correction\. Feedback on the steered response drives the next context update, coupling adaptation across rounds with intervention within each generation\. Theoretically, we connect parameter and context optimization through a shared target\-KL objective and additive logit representations, and derive the steering vector from context\-induced logit displacements\. Under context\-improvement and faithful\-steering assumptions, we prove a one\-round decrease in target KL divergence for sufficiently small steering strength\. Under greedy decoding across eight models and six benchmarks, EMO improves the zero\-shot baseline in 39 of 40 aggregated settings, averaging $\+9\.10$ percentage points\. With the same judge, it adds $\+1\.53$ points on average over context\-only optimization \(TextGrad\), with consistent MMLU\-Pro gains across models\. At matched target\-model generation budgets, accuracy advantages over best\-of\-$N$ are strongest on Llama, while oracle coverage is higher in most comparisons despite fewer candidates\. The coverage\-\-selection gap motivates allocating test\-time computation jointly to candidate generation and verification\.

## [The Role of English Language Education in Promoting Peace and Social Harmony](../publications/8ac6c2278339d0058598.md)

Muhammad Ahmad; Abdul Raheem; Abdullah Shah; Asma Bibi; Abid Hussain

This study investigated the role of English language education in promoting peace and social harmony among university students in Bahawalpur, Pakistan\. Using a quantitative descriptive design, data were collected through a structured questionnaire containing demographic items and 59 close\-ended statements covering peace, tolerance, cooperation, empathy, and social harmony\. The population comprised BS students of English Literature, English Linguistics, and English Language Teaching \(ELT\) from four higher education institutions\. Purposive sampling selected 347 male and female students across different semesters\. The questionnaire was pilot\-tested with 15 students, validated through expert review, and demonstrated good reliability \(Cronbach’s Alpha = 0\.83\)\. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27, including descriptive and inferential statistics\. Findings indicated that English language education promoted cultural respect, peaceful communication, teamwork, empathy, and cooperation\. However, limited classroom time, large classes, language barriers, and insufficient teacher training hindered peace education\. The study recommends teacher training, curriculum improvements, and interactive teaching methods to strengthen tolerance, understanding, and social harmony\.
