## [Dynamic Stability and Learning Rate Selection in Deep Neural Networks Using an Empirical Indicator](../publications/8aced296528b6a80c431.md)

Julio Paredes Rojas

La selección de la tasa de aprendizaje en redes neuronales profundas suele realizarse mediante procedimientos empíricos que no siempre permiten comprender la dinámica del entrenamiento ni reducir eficientemente el espacio de búsqueda\. En este trabajo se analiza dicha dinámica mediante un indicador empírico de estabilidad construido a partir de la evolución temporal de la función de pérdida, utilizado como proxy de sensibilidad del entrenamiento\. El estudio combina análisis dinámico, evaluación del desempeño predictivo y comparación entre selección tradicional y criterio dinámico\. Para ello, se examina la relación entre tasa de aprendizaje, estabilidad relativa y rendimiento en redes multicapa sobre MNIST y FashionMNIST, y luego se extiende el análisis a arquitecturas de distinta profundidad, al conjunto CIFAR\-10, a distintos optimizadores, a una evaluación multi\-dataset con conjuntos tabulares y a una validación multi\-seed\. Los resultados muestran que la tasa de aprendizaje modifica de manera sistemática la estabilidad relativa del entrenamiento y que los mejores desempeños tienden a concentrarse en regiones intermedias del indicador\. En los experimentos multi\-dataset, el criterio dinámico permitió reducir la región de búsqueda entre 30 % y 60 %, manteniendo desempeños finales comparables a los obtenidos mediante exploración exhaustiva\. En conjunto, los hallazgos sugieren que el análisis dinámico puede complementar la selección de hiperparámetros y aportar una herramienta útil para estudiar la estabilidad del aprendizaje en redes neuronales profundas\.

## [Large language models for depression assessment from brief daily diaries](../publications/8ad427ead14245d89155.md)

Whitney R\. Ringwald; Aman Taxali; Mike Angstadt; Colin E\. Vize; Chandra Sripada; Aidan G\.C\. Wright

Abstract Closely tracking changes in depression is important for clinical research and practice\. However, intensive longitudinal depression assessment relies on self\-report surveys that have major limitations\. Scoring depression from natural language with large language models \(LLMs\) could resolve these shortcomings\. This study tested the validity of depression rated by LLMs from daily video diaries\. We studied 108 participants selected for mental health treatment status \(45% in treatment\)\. Participants completed a clinical interview and 14\-21 days of depression surveys and video diaries\. Daily depression scores were estimated by LLMs from diary transcripts\. LLM ratings converged with self\-report depression within\-person \( r = \.45;95% CrI\[\.40, \.49\]\) and when averaged across days for an overall depression score \( r = \.61;95% CrI\[\.43,\.75\]\)\. Averaged LLM ratings correlated with depression symptom severity ascertained by clinical interview \( r = \.53;95% CrI\[\.35, \.68\]\)\. LLM\-rated depression and self\-report had similar profiles of associations with daily functioning variables \(profile r = \.98 within\-person; r = \.94 between\-person\)\. Multivariable regression results showed LLM ratings predicted daily functioning variables \(partial $$\\beta s$$ β s =\|\.12 \| \- \| \.28 \| \) and interview\-rated depression \(partial $$\\beta$$ β =\.33;95% CrI\[\.07, \.58\]\) over and above self\-reports, suggesting LLMs capture clinically\-relevant information that self\-reports miss\. Findings establish a strong foundation for a depression assessment approach that addresses shortcomings of self\-reports while satisfying the unique demands of intensive longitudinal monitoring\.

## [GIS\-Based Assessment of Potential Emergency Assembly Areas: A Staged Planning Framework and Population\-Coverage Analysis](../publications/8ad80d5b668a450e89cd.md)

Ceren Yağcı

Emergency assembly\-area planning requires distinct assessments of safety, accessibility, capacity, and operational readiness\. This study combines a literature\-informed planning framework with a GIS\-based analysis of potential population coverage\. The framework is structured around six stages: hazard screening, accessibility assessment, demand–capacity analysis, operational preparedness evaluation, comparison of feasible alternatives, and scenario\-based testing\. The accessibility stage was demonstrated in the Odunpazarı and Tepebaşı districts of Eskişehir, Türkiye, using a 2024 WorldPop gridded population dataset and 444 selected urban parks\. Euclidean buffers of 300 m, 500 m, and 800 m were generated and dissolved at each threshold to avoid double\-counting populations in overlapping service areas\. Estimated population coverage increased from 66\.9% within 300 m to 78\.7% within 500 m and 82\.5% within 800 m\. The relatively small increase beyond 500 m indicates diminishing coverage gains as the assumed spatial reach expands\. These estimates represent potential spatial coverage only; they do not demonstrate pedestrian accessibility or operational suitability\. Thus, the case study illustrates the population\-coverage component of the staged framework, while hazard exposure, usable capacity, operational preparedness, and performance under disrupted network conditions remain to be evaluated\. The study provides a structured basis for identifying the further assessments required before potential locations can be designated as suitable emergency assembly areas\.

## [Securing real\-time traffic analytics with a privacy\-preserving edge and cloud computing framework](../publications/8aea7028670bc25bad69.md)

Kuldoshbay Avazov; Zhuldyz B\. Kalpeyeva; Raissa Uskenbayeva; Aizhan Kassymova; Sadoqat Tursunova; Dilshoda Kurbonalieva; Akmalbek Bobomirzaevich Abdusalomov; Young Im Cho

The recent demand for real\-time traffic management in urban environments has led to the adoption of edge and cloud computing, which improve the efficiency, scalability, and security of traffic analytics\. Nevertheless, the privacy and confidentiality of traffic data remain important issues\. In this study, a privacy\-sensitive real\-time traffic analytics system is proposed that combines edge computing for local\-area data processing and cloud computing for large\-scale analytics\. This system uses blockchain, encryption, and differential privacy to safeguard sensitive traffic information and ensure information integrity and confidentiality\. The proposed system was evaluated through a set of simulation experiments and compared with existing models, namely BFRT, FedTSE, FLAGCN, and VehiCast\. The results indicate that the suggested system is more successful at reducing latency, power consumption, and load balancing, and at improving data security, achieving 30% latency reduction and 15\-30% power reduction\. In addition, the system was highly scalable, able to process an increasing number of edge devices and cloud servers without significant performance impairment\. The work overall offers a scalable, robust real\-time traffic control platform and insight into integrating the edge\-cloud computing system into intelligent transportation systems \(ITS\) with privacy\-preserving technologies\.

## [Construction of A Path for Matching and Improving The Supply and Demand of Financial Technology Talents from The Perspective of Industry\-to\-Edal Education Integration](../publications/8aecec79479535385ec3.md)

Jingjing Huang

The continuous development of the digital economy has promoted the financial industry to accelerate the transformation to digitalisation and intelligence\. Artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, cloud computing and other technologies are constantly integrated into payment, credit, investment, risk control and other business scenarios\. The demand of financial institutions for composite talents with financial knowledge and digital technology capabilities continues to expand\. Big\. The traditional talent training model has obvious disadvantages, and there is a structural deviation between the supply of financial technology talents and job demand\. The integration of industry and education can use the resource linkage between universities and financial technology enterprises to convey industrial needs to the talent training link, and promote the connection between the curriculum system, practical teaching and evaluation mechanism and job ability requirements\. Based on this, the article analyses the actual requirements and impact mechanism of the supply and demand matching of financial technology talents from the perspective of industry\-education integration, and puts forward an optimisation path around the training goals, curriculum system, practical education and collaborative platform, thereby improving the quality of financial technology talent training and providing talent support for the digital transformation of the financial industry\.

## [ЦИФРОВІ ПЛАТФОРМИ В СИСТЕМІ ЕКОНОМІЧНОЇ БЕЗПЕКИ: ФУНКЦІОНАЛЬНА КЛАСИФІКАЦІЯ ІНСТРУМЕНТІВ ТА ДОСВІД ЄС І США](../publications/8aed844dac091bdf3e96.md)

S\. V\. Logvynenko

Стаття присвячена порівняльному аналізу цифрових технологічних архітектур механізмів реагування Європейського Союзу \(ЄС\) і Сполучених Штатів Америки \(США\) на глобальні загрози в економічній сфері\. Встановлено, що технологічна архітектура є невід’ємним конту\- ром будь\-якої сучасної системи реагування, без якого нормативно\-правова рамка залишається функціонально неповноцінною\. Проаналізовано ключові технологічні платформи європейської архітектури: Агентство ЄС з кібербезпеки \(European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, ENISA\), Гельсінський центр передового досвіду з питань гібридних загроз \(European Centre of Excellence for Countering Hybrid Threats, Hybrid CoE\), цифрова платформа скринінгу прямих іноземних інвестицій \(ПІІ\), Єдиний консолідований санкційний список ЄС, Регламент про штучний інте\- лект \(AI Act\) 2024/1689\. Виявлено три структурні характеристики європейської технологічної архітектури: спеціалізована платформізація, нормативна впорядкованість і захисна орієнто\- ваність\. Досліджено американські технологічні платформи: Мережа з протидії фінансовим злочинам \(FinCEN\), Об’єднана міжвідомча кіберслідча група \(National Cyber Investigative Joint Task Force, NCIJTF\), Агентство з кібербезпеки та захисту інфраструктури \(Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, CISA\), систему автоматизованого санкційного скринінгу Управ\- ління з контролю за іноземними активами \(Office of Foreign Assets Control, OFAC\) і Основи управління ризиками штучного інтелекту \(AI RMF\) Національного інституту стандартів і технологій \(National Institute of Standards and Technology, NIST\)\. Запропоновано авторську функціональну класифікацію цифрових інструментів механізмів реагування за п’ятьма кате\- горіями: інструменти моніторингу, аналізу, підтримки прийняття рішень, імплементації та адаптації\. Виявлено спільний патерн обох систем: інструменти моніторингу і аналізу є най\- більш розвиненими, тоді як інструменти адаптації залишаються найбільш фрагментованими\. Встановлено три структурних відмінності між моделями: архітектура даних, регуляторна філософія щодо автоматизованих рішень, механізми технологічного співробітництва\. Визна\- чено чотири ризики цифровізації без інституційної реформи і сформульовано п’ять принципів продуктивного технологічного розвитку безпекової функції, що є методологічним орієнтиром для формування технологічного компонента системи реагування України, що кореспондує з цілями Стратегії економічної безпеки України \[3\]\.

## [Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration](../publications/8aeef9186465b5deed36.md)

Majid Ramedani; Jaya C\. Terli; Ole H\. Martensen; Tobias Strauß; Katharina Buerger; Peter Dechent; Emrah Düzel; Klaus Fließbach; Maria Gemenetzi; Wenzel Glanz; Julian Hellmann‐Regen; Stefan Hetzer; Enise Irem Incesoy; Daniel Janowitz; Marie Theres Kronmüller; Christoph Laske; Falk Lüsebrink; Robert Perneczky; Oliver Peters; Lukas Preis; Josef Priller; Boris\-Stephan Rauchmann; Ayda Rostamzadeh; Anja Schneider; Björn H\. Schott; Sebastian Sodenkamp; Annika Spottke; Eike Jakob Spruth; Sophia Stöcklein; Jens Wiltfang; Frank Jessen; Stefan J\. Teipel; Martin Dyrba

Abstract Purpose: The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer’s disease from structural MRI scans\. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age\-related bias and unreliable probability estimates\. Specifically, we investigated in\-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age\-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy\. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations\. Methods: Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts \(ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE\) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline\. Age\-related bias was addressed using two in\-processing strategies, adversarial training \(CF\-Net\) and GLM\-based feature residualization \(PMDN\), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network \(CNN\) framework\. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning\. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration\-specific metrics\. Results: PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy \(0\.71\) and improved calibration \(Brier $$\\approx $$ ≈ 0\.22\), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF\-Net\. PMDN effectively removed age\-related bias, achieving near\-zero age prediction correlation; CF\-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing\. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods \(isotonic regression and Bayesian binning\) yielding the lowest calibration errors \(MCE $$\\approx $$ ≈ 0\.21−0\.24\)\. Conclusion: This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness\. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF\-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups\. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration\.

## [Imaging\-based biological age estimation predicts competing mortality risk in lung cancer screening](../publications/8af1941328022fcdda5b.md)

Bellingan; Georgia Bullock; Graham Robinson; Gulistan Keskinbicak; Gulten Geneci; Harriet Sorrell; Hasti Robbie; Helen Kiconco; Helen Victoria Bowyer; Henna Makwana; Hina Pervez; Houda Benmebarek; James Rusius; Jane Rowlands; Janine Zylstra; Jeannie Eng; Jhanara Begum; Jon W\. Teague; Joseph Jacob; Judy Airebamen; Julian McKee; Karen Parry\-Billings; Karen Sennett; Kate Davies; Kate H\.C\. Gowers; Kaylene Phua; Kim Sorley; Kitty Chan; Kylie Gyertson; Laila Ahmed; Laura Farrelly; Laura Green; Lucas Clarke; Lynsey Gallagher; Magali N\. Taylor; Malavika Suresh; Mamta Ruparel; Marie Calligaris; Marilyn Ijeomah\-Orji; Mark Clark; Maureen Browne; Mehran Azimbagirad; Miguel Ferreira; Milica Rajkov; Moksud Miah; Monika Sommerrey; Navinah Nundlall; Nazim Miah; Neil Songsong; Nick Beech; Nick Screaton; Nikita Sharma

Abstract Lung cancer screening \(LCS\) participants have a high competing risk of non\-lung cancer related death, which limits screening benefit\. We hypothesized that imaging\-based biological age can identify individuals at higher risk of non\-lung cancer mortality\. Low dose computed tomography scans from a large LCS trial were retrospectively analyzed\. Bone density loss, muscular fat infiltration, vascular calcification, and visceral fat mass were calculated using segmentations from a nnU\-Net based deep learning segmentation model\. Each participant’s age gap, defined as the difference between their estimated biological age and chronological age, was estimated with disease course mapping using a Bayesian mixed\-effects model\. Disease course map construction used all available longitudinal scan data, whilst individual biological age prediction used baseline scan data only\. The performance of age gap as a parameter in competing risk models for non\-lung cancer related death versus lung cancer diagnosis was evaluated, following the TRIPOD \+ AI reporting guideline\. We included 29,745 scans from 12,478 participants in the final analysis\. Median follow\-up was 5 years, representing 58,284 person\-years at risk\. Multivariable survival models of competing risks were constructed, including the estimated age gap\. The subdistribution hazard ratio \(sHR\) for each decade of age gap for non\-lung cancer related death was higher \(sHR = 2\.0, 95% CI 1\.8–2\.3\), compared to lung cancer diagnosis \(sHR = 1\.3, 95% CI 1\.2–1\.5\)\. Addition of age gap improved model concordance of non\-lung cancer death compared to a model with clinical variables alone \(pooled C\-index = 0\.69 vs 0\.73, difference \+ 0\.04, 95% CI 0\.03–0\.04, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Biological age estimation using an imaging\-based disease progression model improves prediction of non\-lung cancer related death in lung cancer screening\.

## [LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training](../publications/8b050653d0bec9161f33.md)

Max Zhu; Bohang Sun; Pietro Lio; Jialin Yu

Lossless tensor compression could reduce memory usage during training, but training requires tensors to be repeatedly re\-encoded\. We introduce Losslessly Compressed Tensors \(LCT\), a GPU execution framework designed for this repeated encode\-decode regime\. LCT exploits the natural redundancy in floating point data to reduce storage for weights, activations and optimizer states\. Highly optimized GPU kernels implement Huffman coding with precomputed codebooks for low compression and decompression overhead, essential for training\. Our analysis characterizes LCT&\#x27;s storage costs and adaptation to magnitude shifts\. LCT achieves a compression ratio of up to $1\.455\\times$, and is demonstrated in training and finetuning settings\. On a 162M\-parameter NanoGPT, LCT reduces memory usage by $24\.6\\%$ for a $7\.2\\%$ step\-time increase\. In Qwen3\-4B fine\-tuning, LCT saves up to $23\.8\\%$ of peak memory, enabling a $3\.5\\times$ larger context length in training on the same GPU\.

## [Plug\-and\-play predictive energy management for fuel\-efficient platooning of gasoline\-powered autonomous vehicles](../publications/8b0cf77d0bebfd0f87e1.md)

Behrouz Samieiyan; Anjali Awasthi

In this paper, we present a plug\-and\-play predictive energy management framework for fuel\-efficient platooning of gasoline\-powered autonomous vehicles\. Unlike existing approaches that target electric or hybrid drivetrains, the proposed architecture addresses the nonlinear thermodynamic and aerodynamic challenges inherent to internal combustion engine \(ICE\) vehicles\. The framework integrates an Adaptive Neuro\-Fuzzy Inference System optimized via Teaching\-Learning\-Based Optimization \(ANFIS\-TLBO\) with Model Predictive Control \(MPC\) and a Quantum\-inspired Long Short\-Term Memory \(QLSTM\) network that broadcasts a 10\-second leader state prediction horizon to all follower vehicles simultaneously\. A cooperative power\-sharing mechanism and a predictive gap policy are superimposed as a lightweight supervisory layer that leaves the internal structure and parameters of each local controller entirely unchanged, modifying only its reference inputs \(predicted leader trajectory, desired gap, and coordinated fuel\-cut activation\)\. The framework is validated across four standardized driving cycles, HWFET, US06, Artemis HW130, and Artemis HW150, in both 4\-vehicle and 6\-vehicle homogeneous platoon configurations, each subjected to 20 statistically independent runs incorporating stochastic wind \(Weibull\) and road grade \(Rayleigh\) disturbances\. Under the HWFET cycle, the proposed method achieves an average per\-vehicle fuel consumption of 6\.64 L/100 km \(4\-vehicle platoon\) and 6\.61 L/100 km \(6\-vehicle platoon\), outperforming all benchmarks including Adaptive MAB, Pure ANFIS, Pure MPC, and Pure TLBO\. NOx emission reduction rates from leader to last follower reach 5\.74% and 6\.23% in the respective configurations, the highest recorded across all methods, reflecting a trade\-off in which the leader operates at a higher absolute NOx level to sustain tighter velocity tracking, while followers benefit disproportionately from predictive power management\. The plug\-and\-play architecture is validated on a 6\-vehicle platoon with zero controller retuning, confirming scalability across platoon sizes without local\-controller modification\.

## [AI for Poststroke Epilepsy: Scoping Review of Imaging\-Based Prediction Models and Implications for African Settings](../publications/8b0ecb9ac486858970dc.md)

Bashemera Brenda Birungi; Rahman Sanya; Suzan Nakasendwa; Joyce Nakatumba Nabende

Background: Poststroke seizures \(PSS\) and poststroke epilepsy \(PSE\) are important neurological complications associated with poorer functional recovery, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life after stroke\. Neuroimaging plays a central role in identifying patients at increased risk, and recent advances in AI have enabled the development of imaging\-based prediction models that may improve individualized risk stratification\. However, the current evidence remains fragmented, and the extent to which these approaches are applicable to African health care settings is unclear\. Objective: This scoping review aimed to chart the existing global evidence on the development of imaging\-based prediction models that can help in predicting PSS and PSE, especially AI\-based ones\. The purpose was to look into the imaging techniques, computational algorithms, and validation methodologies used and the representation of African populations\. Methods: This scoping review was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework, and the results were presented based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews \(PRISMA\-ScR\) framework\. Articles searched using databases such as PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar involved the application of computed tomography \(CT\), magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\), angiography imaging techniques, radiomic markers, or multimodal neuroimaging techniques in statistical and AI\-based prediction models for seizure\-related outcomes after stroke\. Results: Twenty\-three studies published between 2005 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria\. The evidence demonstrated a clear methodological evolution from conventional imaging\-based prediction models to radiomics, machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, and multimodal approaches\. MRI and CT were the predominant imaging modalities, with cortical involvement, lesion location, infarct volume, hemorrhagic transformation, and quantitative radiomic features emerging as the most frequently reported imaging predictors\. Most AI models relied on internal validation, while relatively few underwent external validation\. The evidence base was concentrated in East Asia, Europe, and North America, with no eligible imaging\-based AI models having been developed or externally validated using African datasets\. Conclusions: Imaging\-based AI for predicting PSS and PSE has progressed rapidly, but important methodological and geographical gaps remain\. Limited external validation, heterogeneous reporting, and the absence of African development and validation cohorts restrict confidence in the generalizability of existing models\. Future research should prioritize the development of explainable imaging\-based AI models using representative African neuroimaging datasets and their external validation in multicenter studies\.

## [COMET: Decoupled Distillation, Routing, and Capacity Control for Task\-Agnostic Continual Vision\-\-Language Learning](../publications/8b104bcb700cf1ae6e22.md)

Seungyoon Woo; Keonhee Park; Gunhee Kim

Vision\-language models \(VLMs\) such as CLIP retain zero\-shot recognition ability, but their open\-world use often requires task\-agnostic continual learning: tasks arrive sequentially, past data are unavailable, task identity is unknown, and the backbone cannot be retrained\. We argue that this setting fails VLMs through three coupled pressures beyond the stability\-plasticity tradeoff: \(1\) modal\-consistency drift, \(2\) representation\-space interference, and \(3\) per\-task capacity shortfall\. We propose COMET \(Collaborative Mixture\-of\-Expert Transfer\) to resolve these three issues respectively as follows\. A frozen teacher provides only a feature reference on a shared image\-text pool; Tri\-Affinity Distillation preserves image\-image, text\-text, and image\-text geometry; and Student\-Aware Cross\-Expert Distillation aligns new experts with compatible prior experts so routing errors degrade gracefully\. We design COMET to keep capacity and inference separate: a contextual bandit keeps or merges full per\-task experts using post\-training signals, while a reconstruction router selects sparse experts at test time without teacher semantics\. On the X\-TAIL benchmark, we show that each proposed component improves continual learning performance\. COMET shows that continual vision\-language adaptation can preserve multimodal geometry, coordinate accumulated experts, and allocate capacity jointly when feature reference, expert shaping, routing, and capacity control are separated by construction\.

## [Long\-term spatiotemporal dynamics, hotspot persistence, and extreme AOD days over Bursa, Türkiye](../publications/8b1161dbe2ab39e331c9.md)

Burak Çalışkan

Satellite\-based aerosol optical depth \(AOD\) enables long\-term monitoring of atmospheric aerosol loading in regions with sparse ground\-based observation networks\. In this study, the spatial and temporal variability of 550 nm AOD over Bursa during 2003–2025 was investigated using Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer \(MODIS\) Multi\-Angle Implementation of Atmospheric Correction \(MAIAC\) MCD19A2 Collection 6\.1 data at 1 km spatial resolution\. Annual and seasonal composites were used to evaluate long\-term trends, seasonality, the persistence of high\-AOD areas, and extreme aerosol days\. The common analysis domain covered 83\.20% of the provincial area\. The area\-weighted annual AOD series showed a small negative trend in the full\-period analysis \(Theil\-Sen slope = \-0\.510 × 10 − 3 AOD year − 1 ; p = 0\.035\)\. The negative slope direction remained consistent across the regional trend sensitivity analyses, whereas statistical significance at p &lt; 0\.05 was not retained under several annual\-coverage and leave\-one\-year\-out scenarios\. After correction for multiple testing, 1,550 pixels exhibited significant trends, of which 1,539 showed decreases\. AOD was highest in summer and lowest in winter, while none of the seasonal trends was significant\. Persistent high\-AOD areas were concentrated along the northern plain and urban corridor, with 102 pixels remaining in the annual upper\-decile class throughout all 23 years\. No robust trend was detected in the frequency of extreme AOD days\. Overall, the different dimensions of the aerosol record did not evolve in parallel: mean AOD showed a modest negative long\-term tendency, the spatial structure of recurrent high\-AOD areas remained persistent, and extreme\-day frequency showed no detectable trend\.

## [Data\-driven static position modeling of a parallel tendon\-actuated soft continuum robot using artificial neural networks](../publications/8b1498e6856c2e776130.md)

Seraphima Sami Hanna; A\. M\. M\. Abdelhaleem; S\. El\-Naggar; Haitham El\-Hussieny

Abstract Parallel soft continuum robots combine the compliance and adaptability of soft structures with the structural advantages of parallel mechanisms, offering promising capabilities for complex robotic applications\. However, their highly nonlinear behavior presents significant challenges for accurate and computationally efficient modeling\. This study presents a data\-driven approach for static end\-effector position modeling of a parallel tendon\-actuated soft continuum robot using an artificial neural network \(ANN\)\. A physics\-based model of the robot is developed in the SoRoSim MATLAB framework using the Geometric Variable\-Strain \(GVS\) formulation, with gravity incorporated into the static simulations\. Simulation data are then used to train the ANN to learn the nonlinear mapping between the tendon actuation forces and the Cartesian position of the end effector\. The trained ANN demonstrates close agreement with the SoRoSim\-generated positions over the investigated input domain while providing considerably faster position predictions than direct SoRoSim evaluations\. This computational advantage highlights the potential of the proposed data\-driven model for applications requiring repeated and rapid model evaluations, particularly in future control\-oriented implementations\. The presented results establish the ANN as an efficient surrogate for the considered SoRoSim\-based static position model, while the current evaluation remains simulation\-based\.

## [Do fungal pathogens exploit HLA\-G\-mediated immune tolerance?](../publications/8b169aaeb2d0e2d32fcf.md)

Abdullah AlSaleh; Eman Farid

Fungal pathogens employ diverse strategies to evade host immunity and establish persistent infection, yet the contribution of immune checkpoint pathways to fungal pathogenesis remains incompletely understood\. Human leukocyte antigen\-G \(HLA\-G\) is a nonclassical major histocompatibility complex class I molecule with potent immunoregulatory properties\. It is capable of suppressing innate and adaptive immune responses through interactions with inhibitory receptors\. Although HLA\-G\-mediated immune tolerance is increasingly recognized in cancer, transplantation, and persistent viral and parasitic infections, its role in fungal disease remains largely unexplored\. This review examines the hypothesis that fungal pathogens may exploit HLA\-G\-mediated immune tolerance to facilitate infection and persistence\. Particular attention is given to interleukin\-10 and transforming growth factor\-β, two immunoregulatory cytokines linked to HLA\-G expression that are prominently induced during various fungal infections\. The convergence of these pathways provides a mechanistic framework connecting fungal\-induced immune regulation with potential HLA\-G activity\. Establishing this relationship could reveal an underrecognized mechanism of fungal immune evasion and identify opportunities for host\-directed therapy\.

## [Monitoring groundwater nitrate concentrations using geodetector\-based geofactors and neural network approach in the Wanka Watershed, Ethiopia](../publications/8b1717abc54f784e2c90.md)

Asnakew Mulualem Tegegne; Adugnaw Tadesse; Tadesual Asamin Setargie; Ayenew Desalegn Ayalew; Tarun Kumar Lohani

Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6 \(Clean Water and Sanitation\) and Goal 3 \(Good Health and Well\-Being\) is reliant on having access to safe drinking water\. Groundwater is the main sources of drinking water in rural and urban areas\. However, water quality is still poorly monitored in Ethiopia&\#x27;&\#x27;s rural areas, including the Wanka Watershed\. Improper land use and agricultural growth, nitrate contamination is a growing concern for groundwater, endangering human health and water sustainability\. High nitrate concentration \(NO 3 \-N\) pose serious health risks such as blue baby syndrome, cancers, and neural tube defects\. However, routine monitoring is limited because laboratory analysis is expensive, logistically difficult, and often inaccessible in remote communities\. Hence, the primary objective of this research is to develop suitable statistical methods and apply appropriate machine learning algorithms to estimate the current status of nitrate concentration in data\-limited area \(Wanka watershed\), upper Blue Nile basin, Ethiopia\. Therefore, geodetector\-based geofactors and neural network methods have been applied to predict the nitrate level in the groundwater\. Forty\-one groundwater nitrate concentration samples were used as the training dataset in 2013, whereas 12 nitrate concentration samples were collected from the same well locations in 2022 for validation\. Nitrate influencing factors were quantified as factor detector output such as recharge \(0\.210\), static water level \(0\.015\), transmissivity \(0\.119\), lithology \(0\.079\), mean air temperature \(0\.021\), Topographic Wetness Index \(0\.078\), soil \(0\.115\), and land use \(0\.232\) as input variables\. The results revealed that land use, recharge, transmissivity, and soil have a strong power of influence on changing the nitrate concentration of shallow groundwater in agriculturally intensified areas, compared with lithology, static water level, and temperature have a weak power of influence\. Geofactors and neural network \(NN\) were acceptable with respect to metrics such as, RMSE \(0\.39, 0\.53\), MAE \(0\.26, 0\.33\), RSSE \(1\.83, 3\.37\), and R 2 \(0\.995, 0\.99\), respectively\. Comparatively, geofactors has a better performance for nitrate monitoring in this study area\. The predicted results of NO3\-N \(in mg/L\) have been mapped for monitoring and management in the agriculturally intensified areas\. It has a better implication for policymakers regarding to water resources protection\.

## [BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed\-Forward Networks](../publications/8b1f40bed18c8bbecfe4.md)

Max Zhu; Bohang Sun; Pietro Lio; Jialin Yu

Reducing memory use in large language model \(LLM\) training is an ongoing challenge\. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations\. The reemergence of sparse $\\relu$ and $\\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself\. We present BitSparse, a GPU\-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations\. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass\. Bfloat16 \(BF16\) and FP8 activations are supported\. Optional sign\-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit\. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum\. BitSparse lowers per\-token VRAM by 31\\% and 30\\% Modded\-NanoGPT and Nemotron\-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\\% at practical sequence lengths\. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated\.

## [YOLOv8\-P2\-CBAM\-NWD: High\-Precision Small\-Target Drone Detection in Complex Visual Airspace via Shallow Attention Routing and Normalized Wasserstein Distance](../publications/8b1f8f37cc01949dad57.md)

Layeq Ali; Iftikhar Ahmed Khan; Shahid Yousaf

Optical ground\-to\-air detection of small unmanned aerial vehicles \(UAVs\) supports perimeter security and airspace safety, but a distant UAV may occupy fewer than 16 × 16 pixels, which is 0\.0625% of a 640 × 640 detector input\. Strided downsampling makes such objects harder to detect, and Intersection over Union \(IoU\) based box losses are highly sensitive to pixel\-level shifts\. This paper evaluates YOLOv8\-P2\-CBAM\-NWD, a nano\-scale version of YOLOv8 with a stride\-4 P2 detection head, a Convolutional Block Attention Module \(CBAM\) on the shallow P2 branch, and a box loss that combines Complete IoU \(CIoU\) with the Normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance \(NWD\)\. Each model was trained only once on 800 single\-class drone images and compared against a YOLOv8n baseline\. On 200 validation images, the proposed model reached a mean average precision at an IoU of 0\.5 \(mAP@0\.5\) of 89\.8%, which is below the 92\.5% of the baseline\. On a sentry test set of 2,500 frames \(1,800 drone frames and 700 cloud or clear\-sky frames\) at a confidence threshold of 0\.1, it increased frame\-level precision from 96\.94% to 98\.35% and specificity from 92\.14% to 95\.86%, and it decreased false alarms from 78\.57 to 41\.43 per 1,000 negative frames, a 47\.3% relative reduction\. Frame\-level recall went down from 96\.78% to 96\.11%\. Thus, the main advantage is fewer false alarms rather than higher object\-level accuracy\. Since the threshold was selected on the test set and the frames were not grouped by video, these results are preliminary\.

## [Pou2f2 enhances retinal ganglion cell survival and axon regeneration after optic nerve injury](../publications/8b289246707c1bb30d8d.md)

D\. N\. Stavropoulos; Chia\-Chun Liu; Shining Wang; Chi\-Yu Chen; Mishal Rao; Laman Mirzaliyeva; Hui\-Chun Cheng; Ya\-Ling Lin; Andrew M\. Williams; Yuan Pan; Takaaki Kuwajima; Jeffrey Louis Goldberg; José‐Alain Sahel; Kun‐Che Chang

Retinal ganglion cell \(RGC\) degeneration and the limited regenerative capacity of mammalian central nervous system axons result in irreversible vision loss in optic neuropathies\. Identifying intrinsic regulators that promote both neuroprotection and axon regeneration is critical for developing effective therapies\. This study identified POU domain class 2 transcription factor 2 \(Pou2f2\) as a previously unrecognized regulator involved in RGC biology\. Single\-cell RNA sequencing analysis of developing mouse and human retinas showed that Pou2f2 is enriched in RGC clusters and suppressed by an RGC fate suppressor in the mouse retinal progenitor cell culture\. Pou2f2 protein was detected in mouse RGCs and optic nerves, where its expression decreased following optic nerve crush \(ONC\)\. In primary RGC cultures, AAV2\-mediated Pou2f2 overexpression enhanced neurite outgrowth, whereas Pou2f2 knockdown reduced neurite length\. In vivo, intravitreal injection of Pou2f2 overexpression AAV2s increased axon regeneration, improved RGC survival, and partially preserved RGC function after ONC\. Bulk RNA sequencing data revealed early activation of cytoskeletal growth pathways and later upregulation of DNA repair\-associated genes, whereas immunostaining and in vitro analyses suggested activation of AKT/mTOR signaling following Pou2f2 overexpression\. Together, these findings identify Pou2f2 as a promising molecular target for gene\-based therapies for RGC degenerative diseases, including glaucoma and other optic neuropathies\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO COMBATE À RESISTÊNCIA ANTIMICROBIANA](../publications/8b2ac1496b74e415c94b.md)

Giulia Portilho Pereira; Ítalo Fernandes Ferreira; Brunna de Paula Campos; Mariana Xavier Cânara; Rubens Carlos Ribeiro

A resistência antimicrobiana constitui uma das principais ameaças contemporâneas à saúde pública global, tendo sido diretamente responsável por 1,14 milhão de óbitos em 2021 e associada a 4,71 milhões de mortes nesse mesmo ano, com projeções indicando aumento para 1,91 milhão de mortes diretamente atribuíveis até 2050 caso a trajetória atual não seja revertida \(GBD 2021 ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE COLLABORATORS, 2024\)\. Diante do relativo estancamento da descoberta de novas classes de antibióticos pelos métodos tradicionais de triagem química, a inteligência artificial e o aprendizado de máquina têm emergido como ferramentas capazes de acelerar substancialmente múltiplas etapas dessa cadeia, desde a descoberta de novos compostos até o diagnóstico e a vigilância epidemiológica\. Modelo de rede neural profunda treinado para prever atividade antibacteriana identificou a halicina, molécula estruturalmente divergente dos antibióticos convencionais, entre mais de cem milhões de compostos avaliados computacionalmente, demonstrando eficácia contra patógenos multirresistentes em modelos animais \(STOKES et al\., 2020\)\. Abordagem semelhante, aplicada especificamente contra o patógeno multirresistente Acinetobacter baumannii, identificou a abaucina, composto capaz de controlar infecções em modelo murino por meio de mecanismo de ação distinto dos antibióticos já existentes \(LIU et al\., 2023\)\. Paralelamente, algoritmos de aprendizado de máquina aplicados a dados de sequenciamento genômico completo têm alcançado desempenho preditivo elevado para determinação de perfis de resistência bacteriana, ao passo que modelos aplicados a espectros de espectrometria de massas MALDI\-TOF têm demonstrado potencial de reduzir drasticamente o tempo necessário para determinação fenotípica de suscetibilidade antimicrobiana em relação aos métodos convencionais baseados em cultura \(WEIS et al\., 2022\)\. Este capítulo revisa criticamente as principais aplicações da inteligência artificial no combate à resistência antimicrobiana, incluindo descoberta e desenho de novos compostos, predição genômica de resistência, diagnóstico rápido, otimização do uso clínico de antimicrobianos, e os desafios técnicos e translacionais que ainda limitam a incorporação plena dessas tecnologias à prática clínica\.

## [THE EFFECT OF SEMANTIC PAUSING ON LISTENING COMPREHENSION AND PERCEIVED COGNITIVE LOAD AMONG A2 EFL LEARNERS](../publications/8b30db4330bbdd6d1923.md)

Aikhan Torekeldi; Гулдана Сейдалиева; Aikhan Torekeldi; Guldana Seidaliyeva; Гулдана Сейдалиева

Abstract\. The study examines the effect of semantic pausing on listening comprehension and perceived mental effort among A2\-level EFL learners\. The study involved 24 first\-year students aged 15\-16 from a vocational college\. A counterbalanced within\-subject design was employed, in which participants listened to two A2\-level texts in both an original condition and a semantic\-pause condition\. The semantic\-pause versions contained additional one\-second pauses inserted at predetermined semantic boundaries, while the lexical, grammatical, and informational content remained unchanged\. After each listening task, participants completed a 10\-item comprehension test and provided a 9\-point rating of perceived mental effort\. The results showed a statistically significant improvement in listening comprehension in the semantic\-pause condition compared with the original condition\. However, the difference in perceived mental effort was not statistically significant, although a slight descriptive reduction was observed\. The findings suggest that semantic pausing may provide A2\-level learners with additional processing time and support their comprehension of spoken English without necessarily reducing their subjective perception of mental effort\. The study contributes to research on temporal modifications of spoken input and suggests that strategically placed pauses may be a practical way of adapting listening materials for lower\-proficiency EFL learners\.

## [Enhanced detection of polymicrobial bloodstream infections with 16S rDNA PCR library amplicons and clinical relevance](../publications/8b33cb9086e51b087d9d.md)

Guangqi Li; Geng Wu; He Yin; Kendall A\. McGraw; Jia Hou; Zhijun Zhao

Introduction Polymicrobial bloodstream infections \(BSIs\) are clinically challenging because conventional blood culture may fail to recover all causative microorganisms, particularly in patients with low microbial burden, prior antimicrobial exposure, or infections caused by fastidious organisms\. This study evaluated a 16S rDNA PCR library construction strategy based on cloning and Sanger sequencing as a complementary approach to conventional blood culture and compared its microbial detection profile with that of direct 16S rDNA amplicon high\-throughput sequencing\. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 16,970 blood culture specimens collected at a hospital in northwestern China to characterize the clinical distribution and epidemiological features of BSIs\. In a retrospective cohort of 295 patients with culture\-confirmed BSI, clinical predictors associated with blood culture\-defined polymicrobial BSI were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analyses, with particular emphasis on white blood cell \(WBC\) count and procalcitonin \(PCT\) levels\. In a separate molecular comparison cohort of 20 patients, cell\-free DNA \(cfDNA\) was analyzed using two 16S rDNA\-based workflows: a clone\-based approach involving PCR amplification, gel purification, cloning, amplified ribosomal DNA restriction analysis \(ARDRA\), and Sanger sequencing, and a direct 16S rDNA amplicon high\-throughput sequencing approach\. Results Among the 16,970 blood culture specimens, 1,321 were positive, including 45 polymicrobial BSI cases\. Escherichia coli was the most frequently identified pathogen, followed by coagulase\-negative staphylococci and Brucella spp\. Compared with monomicrobial BSI, polymicrobial BSI was associated with higher WBC counts and PCT levels\. In multivariable analysis, both WBC count and PCT were independently associated with polymicrobial BSI, and their combination showed good discriminatory performance \(AUC = 0\.927\)\. In the separate molecular comparison cohort of 20 patients, the three methods showed distinct detection ranges\. Blood culture detected 0–1 microbial taxon per patient, with one pathogen identified in 17 patients and negative results in 3 patients\. The clone\-based method detected a broader microbial spectrum, identifying 0–5 taxa per patient, whereas direct 16S rDNA amplicon sequencing showed the broadest detection range, with more than five taxa detected in 9 patients\. In contrast, 16S rDNA high\-throughput sequencing generated broader taxonomic profiles but showed lower agreement with blood culture\. Compared with conventional blood culture, the 16S rDNA PCR library method showed an overall percent agreement of 80\.0%\. Conclusion WBC and PCT may help identify patients at increased risk of polymicrobial BSI and may support the selection of patients for additional molecular testing\. The cloning\-based 16S rDNA PCR library strategy provides a complementary approach to conventional blood culture and may offer a balance between broader microbial detection and more focused sequence\-level interpretation compared with direct amplicon high\-throughput sequencing\. Its potential utility may be particularly relevant in selected patients with culture\-negative or clinically suspected polymicrobial BSI\.

## [COMUNICAÇÃO E SAÚDE, HUMANIZAÇÃO E INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NOS PROJETOS PEDAGÓGICOS DE MEDICINA DO RIO GRANDE DO SUL](../publications/8b33de262c60230254f7.md)

Lucas Petrich; André Petrich; Helena de Moraes Fernandes

A formação médica demanda a integração entre humanização do cuidado, comunicação em saúde e incorporação crítica e ética da Inteligência Artificial \(IA\)\. Este estudo analisou a inserção dos eixos Comunicação e Saúde, Humanização e Inteligência Artificial nos Projetos Pedagógicos de Cursos \(PPCs\) de Medicina de sete Universidades Federais do Rio Grande do Sul: FURG, UFCSPA, UFFS, UFPel, UFRGS, UFSM e UNIPAMPA\. Trata\-se de estudo documental descritivo, realizado a partir dos PPCs vigentes entre 2023 e 2025\. Foi elaborado um dicionário lexical com termos, variações morfológicas e sinonímias\. Os documentos foram processados em Python, utilizando expressões regulares e cálculo da densidade lexical\. Foram analisadas 380\.892 palavras e identificadas 1\.860 ocorrências: 1\.135 \(61,0%\) de Humanização, 531 \(28,5%\) de Comunicação e Saúde e 194 \(10,4%\) de Inteligência Artificial\. A hierarquia Humanização &gt; Comunicação e Saúde &gt; Inteligência Artificial foi observada\. Na Humanização, predominaram “ética” e “bioética”, enquanto “empatia” e “escuta ativa” foram pouco frequentes\. Em Comunicação e Saúde, prevaleceram termos genéricos\. Na IA, 82,1% das ocorrências concentraram\-se em “tecnologia”, e “inteligência artificial” apareceu uma única vez\. Os resultados evidenciam inserção assimétrica dos eixos, com IA ausente como campo curricular específico\. A Resolução CNE/CES nº 3/2025 reforça a necessidade de atualização dos PPCs\.

## [Formulation and Optimization of Sustained\-Release Gastroretentive Microspheres of Vonoprazan Using Box– Behnken Design](../publications/8b43438fd796825e662a.md)



Background: Vonoprazan is a novel potassium\-competitive acid blocker \(P\-CAB\) with potent acid\-suppressive activity; however, its therapeutic efficacy may be limited by rapid gastric emptying\.The present study aimed to formulate and optimize sustained\-release gastroretentive microspheres of vonoprazan using the ionotropic gelation technique to prolong gastric residence time and achieve controlled drug release\.Methods: Gastroretentive microspheres were prepared using sodium alginate and HPMC K100M as matrixforming polymers and calcium chloride as the cross\-linking agent\.A three\-factor, three\-level Box\-Behnken design was employed to optimize sodium alginate concentration \(1\-3% w/v\), HPMC K100M concentration \(0\.5\-1\.5% w/v\), and calcium chloride concentration \(2\-6% w/v\)\.The formulations were evaluated for encapsulation efficiency, particle size, percentage yield, drug loading, swelling index, floating behavior, and in vitro drug release\.Numerical optimization was performed using the desirability function approach\.Results: The encapsulation efficiency ranged from 85\.18% to 94\.21%, particle size varied between 171 and 221 nm, and cumulative drug release after 12 h ranged from 66\.7% to 79\.8%\.ANOVA confirmed that the developed models were statistically significant \(p &lt; 0\.05\), with sodium alginate concentration significantly affecting encapsulation efficiency, while sodium alginate and HPMC K100M significantly influenced particle size and drug release\.The optimized formulation contained 3\.0% w/v sodium alginate, 1\.5% w/v HPMC K100M, and 4\.123% w/v calcium chloride, with predicted values of 93\.55% encapsulation efficiency, 172\.83 nm particle size, and 79\.80% drug release, achieving a desirability of 0\.945\.The optimized microspheres also demonstrated excellent floating ability, high swelling capacity, and satisfactory stability\.Conclusion: The optimized gastroretentive microspheres of vonoprazan successfully provided sustained drug release with high encapsulation efficiency and desirable physicochemical characteristics\.The Box\-Behnken design proved to be an effective optimization tool for developing a robust gastroretentive delivery system with potential to improve the therapeutic performance of vonoprazan\.

## [Research on the Innovation of School\-Local Collaborative Education Mode for Rural Smart Culture and Tourism Vocational Education in Hubei Ethnic Minority Areas](../publications/8b4fd5955e44ec4722c5.md)

Driven by the dual strategies of in\-depth integration of culture and tourism and digitalization of vocational education, rural smart culture and tourism has become a core industrial driver for rural revitalization in ethnic minority areas of Hubei Province, while the insufficient supply of localized skilled talents has become a key bottleneck restricting the quality improvement and upgrading of the industry\. Taking Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Changyang Tujia Autonomous County and Wufeng Tujia Autonomous County of Yichang City as the core research fields, this study systematically sorts out the research context and theoretical basis of school\-local collaborative education for rural smart culture and tourism vocational education by comprehensively adopting methods such as literature research, field investigation and case analysis\. It further diagnoses the practical dilemmas existing in the current school\-local collaborative education in Hubei ethnic minority areas, including insufficient subject collaboration, disconnection between talent training and industrial demand, low integration of ethnic culture and smart technology, and lack of long\-term operation mechanism\. On this basis, this study constructs an innovative school\-local collaborative education mode for rural smart culture and tourism vocational education featuring &quot;four\-dimensional linkage, three\-stage progression, and two\-way empowerment&quot;, and clarifies the rights\-responsibility boundaries and collaborative logic of four main subjects, namely the government, vocational colleges, rural communities, and cultural and tourism enterprises\. Furthermore, it designs specific implementation paths from five dimensions: joint major construction, integrated curriculum development, co\-construction of training bases, joint cultivation of teaching staff, and sharing of research outcomes, and puts forward a four\-in\-one guarantee mechanism covering policy, organization, resources and system\. The research results can provide theoretical references and practical schemes for cultivating localized rural smart culture and tourism talents and promoting the long\-term implementation of school\-local collaborative education in Hubei ethnic minority areas, and also offer reference for the reform of culture and tourism vocational education in similar ethnic minority areas in central China\.

## [Post\-Deployment Monitoring of Prediction\-Error Deterioration in Machine Learning Models Using a Two\-Channel Exponentially Weighted Moving Average Chart](../publications/8b554467811fe6155d24.md)

Quynh Pham Ba; Du Nguyen Huu; Son Ta Anh; Hoa Le Thanh

This study develops a forward\-cross\-fitted two\-channel EWMA \(FCF\-DS\-EWMA\) chart for post\-deployment monitoring of predictionerror deterioration in continuous\-response machine\-learning models\. Temporally held\-out Phase\-I residuals are transformed into robust signed and magnitude channels, and an equal\-share rule uses channel\-specific finite\-horizon limits whose common marginal exceedance level is selected jointly\. In a unified Monte Carlo study with 𝑅 = 1000, the native false\-alarm probability \(PFA\) is 0\.176–0\.196 for the in\-sample\-residual chart and 0\.094–0\.097 for FCF\-DS across the three in\-control environments\. Six deterioration mechanisms are compared on a common ΔMSE scale\. The signed and magnitude channels specialize to different changes, while equal\-share calibration restores directional sensitivity relative to a common\-limit maximum \(abrupt\-shift detection probability 𝑃𝐷 = 0\.724 versus 0\.582\)\. One\-factor analyses of native PFA identify serial dependence, inadequate block length, and monitoring horizon as the clearest sources of false\-alarm inflation\. An oracle diagnostic shows that the temporary\-model/final\-model reference mismatch mainly shifts the operating point by a small amount\. The ethanol study illustrates channel attribution and reference\-location sensitivity, and paired perturbations of actual post\-Phase\-I Metro traffic residual windows provide quantitative evidence in a second regression domain\.

## [An Alignment\-Driven Approach for Constructing SPARQL Federated Queries](../publications/8b5b3630c69994229c4c.md)

Moussa Abdenour Beldi; Sihem Klai; Karima Mecheri; Seif Eddine Bouziane

Integrating complementary information across distributed SPARQL endpoints remains a significant challenge\. While query federation enables access across multiple endpoints, constructing federated queries requires both SPARQL expertise and knowledge of the underlying ontological schemas\. Current query rewriting techniques primarily focus on vocabulary translation to retrieve equivalent data, often overlooking the integration of complementary information spread across sources\. To address these limitations, we propose an alignment\-driven approach that assists users in constructing federated queries by leveraging ontology alignments\. Our approach joins class paths – user\-selected sequences of ontology classes and relationships – from source and target ontologies, guided by alignment\-based filtering, into a unified path that serves as the foundation for generating federated SPARQL queries capturing complementary aspects of the user’s intent\. An experimental evaluation using OAEI Conference track datasets demonstrates that the generated queries consistently match reference queries in both structure and data retrieval across simple and complex mapping types, confirming the approach’s effectiveness in integrating complementary data from heterogeneous sources\.

## [A research framework for evaluating upstream multimodal sarcopenia risk domains in older adults](../publications/8b75b8d275e7d6add222.md)

Nackhwan Kim

Established sarcopenia definitions identify clinically important impairment, but their thresholds are not designed to characterize all biological changes associated with subsequent muscle decline\. Whether additional measurements improve assessment before these thresholds are reached remains uncertain\. This structured narrative review proposes a research framework for evaluating upstream, multimodal sarcopenia risk domains in older adults\. It integrates diagnostic consensus statements with mechanistic, observational, diagnostic\-accuracy, prognostic, and intervention literature identified through purposive searches and citation tracking\. Candidate domains comprise circulating biomarkers, creatine\-pool\-based muscle mass estimation, neuromuscular measurements, imaging and bioelectrical measures, and digital mobility assessments\. The evidence supporting these domains is heterogeneous\. Cross\-sectional differences and biological plausibility do not establish prediction of incident sarcopenia, incremental clinical value, or differential treatment benefit\. Neuromuscular abnormalities may reflect aging rather than sarcopenia specifically, and measures commonly grouped as muscle quality assess distinct constructs\. The proposed domains are therefore nonexclusive and nonsequential; no diagnostic stages, validated multimodal score, or biomarker\-guided treatment algorithm are proposed\. Conventional clinical assessments provide reference phenotypes, while falls, disability, fractures, quality of life, hospitalization, and mortality remain separate validation outcomes\. The principal contribution is an evidence\-to\-validation framework that distinguishes demonstrated measurement capabilities from untested applications\. Priorities are longitudinal assessment, reproducibility, external validation, incremental prediction beyond inexpensive clinical measures, and trials of clinical utility before implementation\.

## [Investigating the transfer of physical stimuli to the dreamed body: A comparative study of muscular, vestibular, and haptic stimulation on dream incorporation](../publications/8b7c217cc8873126d540.md)

Emma Peters; Jakob Poehlmann; Xinlin Wang; Kathrin Fischer; Stefano Maraschin; Gian Jäger; Gabriel Bolliger; Ralf Kredel; Simon Maurer; Martin Dresler; Daniel Erlacher

The relationship between the dreamed body and the physical body remains an open question in sleep and dream research\. This study examined whether somatosensory stimulation applied during REM sleep modulates the corresponding dream content under controlled conditions\. Using a within\-subject design, we compared three stimulation modalities\-electrical muscular, galvanic vestibular, and haptic vibration\-each paired with a modality\-specific sham stimulation\. Twenty\-four participants completed one adaptation night followed by three consecutive experimental nights in the sleep laboratory\. Dream reports were collected following rapid eye movement sleep awakenings after stimulation or sham periods, yielding a total of 120 reports\. Dream incorporation of bodily sensations and actions was observed across all conditions; however, generalized linear mixed\-effects analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between stimulation and sham conditions for any modality\. No evidence for reliable modality\-specific dream incorporation was observed under rigorous sham\-controlled conditions\. Rather than demonstrating robust stimulation\-specific effects, these findings suggest that contextual and expectancy\-related influences substantially contribute to bodily dream content under laboratory conditions while highlighting methodological challenges in dream incorporation research\. By combining multiple somatosensory stimulation modalities with rigorous sham\-controlled procedures, the present study provides a methodological benchmark for future investigations of dream incorporation and dream engineering\.

## [MBOAT7 \-Associated Intellectual Developmental Disorder\-57 with Global Developmental Delay: A Whole Exome Sequencing Case Report](../publications/8b7e256305a37c662546.md)

NV Sundarachary; Madhavi Kondepudi; Ramya Rachamanti

Intellectual developmental disorder\-57 \(MRT57\) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the MBOAT7 gene\. The disorder is characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, severe speech impairment, behavioral abnormalities, and variable motor dysfunction\. Due to overlapping clinical manifestations, affected patients are commonly misdiagnosed with cerebral palsy or nonspecific developmental delay before genetic confirmation\. We report a 7\-year\-old male child who presented with delayed speech and language development and delayed developmental milestones\. Due to persistent developmental concerns and the presence of a similarly affected sibling, a hereditary neurodevelopmental disorder was suspected\. Whole exome sequencing \(WES\) found a homozygous frameshift variant in the MBOAT7 gene, c\.168del \(p\. Ile57Serfs\*52\)\. The same variant was detected in the affected sibling, supporting autosomal recessive inheritance\. This case shows the importance of considering genetic causes in children presenting with delayed speech, language impairment, and developmental delay\. Molecular diagnosis through WES enabled definitive diagnosis, appropriate genetic counseling, and informed clinical management\.

## [A Novel Non Invasive Approach for Jaundice Detection and Photo Therapy System](../publications/8b7faf2c3c1c79698a7e.md)



Jaundice is a significant condition in new born that leads to yellowing of the skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels\.While various underlying conditions can contribute to this issue, it typically arises from the underdeveloped liver function of infants\.In the past five years, 60% of new born experienced jaundice, resulting in a yellow tint to their skin and eyes\.Thanks to improved screening and management practices, the proportion of affected infants with severe jaundice requiring treatment has dropped by approximately 20% over the last five years\.This condition generally occurs as the infant&\#x27;s liver matures and starts processing bilirubin more efficiently\.This study introduces and validates a non\-invasive device known as the &quot;Golden Hue Detector&quot; for the identification of neonatal jaundice\.Infants often experience jaundice, a condition that requires prompt and precise diagnosis to prevent complications such as kernicterus\.Conventional methods of detecting jaundice rely on blood tests, which can be stressful for babies and demanding on healthcare resources\.These conventional approaches often necessitate multiple blood samples, raising the risk of infection and causing significant distress to the infants\.

## [Beyond Gross Motor Function: The Association Between Fine Motor Skills and Cognitive Development in Treated SMA Type 1](../publications/8b8557408ed4fea3b195.md)

Background: Disease\-modifying therapies \(DMTs\) have transformed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy \(SMA\) type 1, revealing heterogeneous developmental trajectories and renewing interest in cognitive and language outcomes beyond gross motor function\. Within an embodied cognition framework, sensorimotor experience, object manipulation, and interactions with the environment may shape early cognitive development\. This study aimed to describe the cognitive, language, and motor development of treated children with SMA type 1 and to explore associations between gross motor abilities and neurodevelopmental outcomes\. Methods: A retrospective observational study included 32 children aged 18–30 months with confirmed SMA type 1\. Participants were assessed using the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia Infant Test of Neuromuscular Disorders \(CHOP\-INTEND\) at baseline \(T0\) and both CHOP\-INTEND and the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition \(BSID\-III\) at the time of neurodevelopmental assessment \(T1\)\. Associations among Fine Motor, Cognitive, Language, and Gross Motor scores were examined using Spearman’s correlations and multivariable rank\-based regression\. Results: Fine Motor scores showed inter\-individual variability and were correlated with Cognitive \(ρ = 0\.647, p &lt; 0\.001\) and Language \(ρ = 0\.753, p &lt; 0\.001\) scores\. The association between Fine Motor and Cognitive performance remained robust even after adjustment for gross motor function, assessed by CHOP\-INTEND, indicating that fine motor ability is linked to cognitive outcome irrespective of overall motor severity\. Conclusions: In our cohort, fine motor ability was associated with cognitive and language outcomes, regardless of gross motor severity\. These findings suggest the important role of neurodevelopmental components, beyond gross motor function alone, supporting their systematic integration into the clinical characterization of children with treated SMA type 1\.

## [Long\-chain fatty acid\- and acylcarnitine\-bound oxygenated myoglobin interactions with outer mitochondrial membrane](../publications/8b8657b339ea0e0139bd.md)

Andriy Anishkin; Sangita Kachhap; Kiran Kumar Adepu; Ryan Sturms; Vaidehi Ulaganathan; Sree Vamsee Chintapalli

Introduction Oxygenated myoglobin \(oxy\-Mb\) releases oxygen \(O 2 \) during interactions with the outer mitochondrial membrane \(OMM\) and is shown to bind hydrophobic metabolic substrates like palmitate \(PLM\) and palmitoylcarnitine \(PLC\)\. However, it remains unclear how the binding of these specific lipids influences oxy\-Mb interaction with the OMM\. Methods We employed molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulations to evaluate PLM\- and PLC\-bound oxy\-Mb/membrane interactions in two settings: an average\-composition OMM and a cardiolipin\-enriched contact\-site OMM \(CS\-OMM\)\. Following steered MD\-assisted contact establishment, we assessed unrestrained membrane\-association stability and steered detachment forces\. Results Both PLM\- and PLC\-bound oxy\-Mb, unrestrained after attachment to the membrane, demonstrated a strong preference for the CS\-OMM, showing 2\.3\- to 2\.7\-fold increases in stability compared to the average\-OMM\. However, the bound lipid influenced membrane\-contact persistence and resistance to steered detachment\. PLM\-bound oxy\-Mb was 10%–20% more stable overall and required approximately twice the detachment force of the PLC\-bound complex\. During steered detachment, it required roughly twice the force of the PLC\-bound complex and preferentially interacted with cardiolipin\. Conversely, PLC\-bound oxy\-Mb exhibited weaker membrane association and preferentially engaged phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylinositol\. Discussion The identity of the bound lipid actively modulates oxy\-Mb’s membrane stability, phospholipid preference, and membrane facing orientation\. PLM promotes a more mechanically robust membrane association, whereas PLC produces a distinct and weaker interaction pattern\. These structural differences may influence the accessibility of the heme region at the mitochondrial surface; however, O 2 release and lipid transfer were not directly measured in the present simulations\.

## [Pregnancy Health Monitoring System Using Artificial Intelligence: A Review](../publications/8b950fc9e34e10874b4c.md)

Anbazhagan R; Dr\. Susitha N

Pregnancy\-related complications such as gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, preterm birth, and fetal distress remain major causes of maternal and perinatal morbidity, and timely detection depends on regular, accurate monitoring that many women cannot easily access\. Advances in wearable sensing, mobile health, and artificial intelligence \(AI\) have made continuous, data\-driven pregnancy monitoring technically feasible\. This paper presents a structured narrative review of AI\-based pregnancy health monitoring, drawing mainly on recent systematic, scoping, and narrative reviews together with selected primary studies\. It examines the data sources and sensing modalities used, the machine learning and deep learning techniques applied, and the main application areas: gestational diabetes and preeclampsia prediction, fetal monitoring through cardiotocography, preterm birth and imaging, and wearable and IoT\-based remote monitoring\.The review finds that AI methods show consistent promise across these areas, but that the evidence base is limited by small single\-centre datasets, geographic concentration of research, class imbalance, scarce external validation, and an unresolved tension between accuracy and interpretability\. Privacy, sensor accuracy, and user compliance further constrain real\-world deployment\. The paper proposes a five\-layer reference architecture for an AI\-based pregnancy health monitoring system and outlines research directions relevant to resource\-constrained settings such as India\.

## [Environmental impact of a radiology department: greenhouse gas emissions and primary energy accounting and strategies for sustainable practice](../publications/8b9ae98984ccc6e8e4c9.md)

Stefania Rizzo; Christoph Ruesch; Marco Budin; Rolf Wyttenbach; Ermidio Rezzonico; Filippo Grande

OBJECTIVES: To assess the environmental impact of a radiology department&\#x27;s operations \(primary energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions \(GHG\); to identify the main levers for reduction\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data collection included measured and calculated energy consumption of imaging machines \(2 MRI, 2 CT, 1 interventional radiology \(IR\) suite, 2 US, 3 radiography machines\), workstations, lighting, ventilation; cooling and heating for imaging systems and rooms; materials/pharmaceuticals; external services \(e\.g\. laundry and information technology \(IT\)\)\. The electrical energy consumption of building systems, lighting, and IT equipment was primarily determined through measurements; other energy consumption figures were estimated using technical data and meteorological data\. For the calculation of GHG emissions and primary energy consumption, a specialised tool using specific conversion factors from established environmental databases was developed\. RESULTS: Our hospital switched from coal\-based electricity to renewable electrical energy \(hydropower\), leading to a reduction in primary energy consumption \(\-64%\) and GHG emissions \(\-92%\) of the radiology department\. Following this change, without a reduction in direct energy consumption, the MRI systems showed a marked reduction in primary energy consumption, although still having the highest primary energy consumption per exam \(49\.2 kWh compared to 13\.9 kWh \(CT1\) and 48\.9 kWh \(IR\)\)\. After the transition to renewable energy, the major source of GHG emissions shifted from electrical energy toward materials/pharmaceuticals\. CONCLUSION: Our findings support the transition to renewable energy sources for electricity, as a key strategy for reducing GHG emissions and primary energy demand of radiology departments\. Following this shift, selecting materials and pharmaceuticals with lower emissions and primary energy factors can further mitigate the environmental impact\. KEY POINTS: Question Radiology departments are significant sources of energy consumption and GHG emissions\. Findings Adoption of renewable energy reduces primary energy consumption and GHG emissions\. Critical relevance statement GHG emissions in a radiology department can be significantly reduced by transitioning to renewable energy sources\. After this shift, emissions will mainly depend on the materials and pharmaceuticals used, such as disposable supplies and contrast agents\.

## [Cryptococcal meningitis\-associated cerebrovascular injury presenting with sequential multifocal cerebral infarctions and prominent autonomic dysfunction in a non\-HIV patient: a case report and focused literature review](../publications/8ba2c7d2be584e637ead.md)

Lijin Liu; Lijin Liu; Fanxin Kong; Jinfang Li; Jianjun Wang; Wei Li; Yong Jiang; Lanying Liu; Lanying Liu; Xiude Qin

Cryptococcal meningitis \(CM\) can occur in patients without human immunodeficiency virus \(HIV\) infection and may be complicated by genuine cerebral infarction, creating a powerful diagnostic anchor toward primary cerebrovascular disease\. We report a 66\-year\-old non\-HIV man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and no documented major immunosuppressive condition who initially presented with dizziness and mild headache\. Brain MRI showed restricted diffusion in the left brainstem, and acute ischemic stroke was diagnosed\. Over the following weeks, neurological deterioration continued despite stroke\-directed treatment\. Repeat MRI demonstrated new infarctions involving the left cerebellar vermis, corpus callosum, and left thalamus, while the patient developed rapid cognitive decline and prominent autonomic manifestations, including orthostatic hypotension, urinary retention, constipation, vomiting, and severe sleep disturbance\. Cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) examination revealed an opening pressure &gt;300 mmH 2 O, leukocytes 128 × 10 6 /L, protein 964 mg/L, and glucose 1\.28 mmol/L\. India ink staining was suspiciously positive, and Cryptococcus neoformans was confirmed by fungal culture and metagenomic next\-generation sequencing\. Serial lumbar punctures and antifungal treatment with amphotericin B and fluconazole were followed by substantial clinical improvement\. To contextualize the case, we conducted a focused review of published non\-HIV or apparently immunocompetent reports of CM\-associated cerebral infarction\. The literature shows a recurring pattern of deep perforator, brainstem, cerebellar, callosal, and multifocal ischemic injury, with both small\- and large\-vessel mechanisms reported\. However, sequential infarctions across multiple territories accompanied by a prominent progressive autonomic syndrome remain poorly documented\. This case supports early CSF investigation when recurrent infarction, encephalopathic progression, and multisystem neurological features are discordant with an isolated vascular diagnosis\.
