## [Dual‐Branch Model‐Driven Intelligent Diagnosis of Osteoarthritis via Multidimensional Raman Spectral Data Fusion](../publications/8ba6628e486d93d382e7.md)

Hui Yang; Hongze Xu; Xiaoyi Lv; Chen Chen; Chen Chen; Jianhui Zhu; Cheng Chen; Cheng Chen

ABSTRACT Osteoarthritis is a chronic disease, and early diagnosis is critical for clinical intervention\. Raman spectroscopy is a non‐invasive and sensitive method for molecular fingerprinting and has recently proved promising for biomedical sensing and disease diagnosis\. However, the peak overlap of complex biological samples often limits feature extraction accuracy\. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose a novel dual‐branch convolutional neural network architecture \(DBCM\)\. By feeding one‐dimensional raw spectra and two‐dimensional spectral data simultaneously, one‐dimensional branch captures fine variations in peak intensities, and two‐dimensional branch mines nonlinear spatial correlations between frequency bins\. The complementary multidimensional features effectively disentangle the overlap information\. Experimentally using five‐fold cross validation results show that the DBCM provides diagnostic accuracy of 0\.9142 and 0\.9734 on osteoarthritis and alcohol dependence data respectively\. To further improve the robustness of feature representation, we incorporate Inception module to optimize the network architecture, employing multi‐scale convolutional kernels to extract features across different frequency widths in parallel\. Improved DBCM obtains accuracy of 0\.9689 and F1 score of 0\.9792 on the osteoarthritis dataset\. Our results suggest that DBCM deeply integrates multidimensional Raman features which provides a high precision tool for early osteoarthritis diagnosis and a new model paradigm for deep learning applications in biomedical spectral analysis\.

## [Computation\-through\-Dynamics Toolkit: Simulated datasets and quality metrics for dynamical models of neural activity](../publications/8bb3c33c7d31d72447b8.md)

Christopher Versteeg; Jonathan McCart; Mitchell Ostrow; David M\. Zoltowski; Clayton B\. Washington; Laura N\. Driscoll; Olivier Codol; Jonathan A\. Michaels; Scott W\. Linderman; David C\. Sussillo; Chethan Pandarinath

A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal\-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation\. A powerful framework for understanding neural computation uses neural dynamics \- the rules that govern how neural activity evolves over time \- to explain how goal\-directed input\-output transformations occur\. As dynamical rules are not directly observable, we need computational models that can infer neural dynamics from recorded neural activity\. We typically validate such models using synthetic datasets with known ground\-truth dynamics, but unfortunately existing synthetic datasets don&\#x27;t reflect fundamental features of neural computation and may therefore be poor proxies for neural systems\. Further, the field lacks validated metrics for quantifying the accuracy of the dynamics inferred by models\. The Computation\-through\-Dynamics Toolkit \(CtDToolkit\) addresses these critical gaps by providing: 1\) synthetic datasets that reflect computational properties of biological neural circuits, 2\) interpretable metrics for quantifying model performance, and 3\) a standardized pipeline for training and evaluating models with or without known external inputs\. In this manuscript, we demonstrate how CtDToolkit can help guide the development, tuning, and troubleshooting of neural dynamics models\. In summary, CtDToolkit provides a necessary framework for model developers to better understand and characterize neural computation through the lens of dynamics\.

## [Case Report: Smith\-Magenis syndrome with bilateral high\-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, and seizure in infancy](../publications/8bb87e695dd131551904.md)

Yun Cheng; Xunwei Liu; Lingyun Yang; Jinwen Xu

Smith\-Magenis syndrome \(SMS\) is a rare neurodevelopmental and multisystem disorder caused mainly by 17p11\.2 deletions involving RAI1\. Because the characteristic behavioral and sleep phenotype may not yet be apparent, diagnosis in infancy can be challenging\. We report a 9\-month\-old boy with recurrent febrile urinary tract infection, bilateral hydronephrosis with ureteral dilatation, hypothyroidism, global developmental delay, hypotonia, brachydactyly, dysmorphic features, phimosis, and short penis\. Voiding cystourethrography demonstrated bilateral grade IV vesicoureteral reflux \(VUR\)\. Renal scintigraphy showed focal right renal cortical defects; DTPA effective renal plasma flow was 180\.33 mL/min in the left kidney and 133\.77 mL/min in the right kidney, corresponding to split function of 57\.4% and 42\.6%\. Trio whole\-exome sequencing with copy\-number\-variant analysis identified a de novo 3\.63\-Mb deletion at 17p11\.2 encompassing RAI1, confirming SMS; a maternally inherited heterozygous DUOX2 likely pathogenic variant was also detected, but its contribution to hypothyroidism remains unproven\. Infection improved with antibiotics, levothyroxine was resumed, and amoxicillin/clavulanate prophylaxis was initiated\. Surgery for phimosis was postponed after an afebrile sleep\-related seizure\. Follow\-up showed improved renal indices, no recurrent urinary tract infection, normalized thyroid function, and no definite abnormality on video\-electroencephalography, although developmental delay persisted and brief seizure\-like ocular events remained under evaluation\. This case shows that high\-grade bilateral VUR with recurrent infection and a syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotype can be an early presentation of SMS and warrants copy\-number analysis, renal protection, and coordinated endocrine, neurologic, developmental, and urologic follow\-up\.

## [Mental health, resilience, and culturally congruent care among Muslim and Arab American women in the United States: a scoping review](../publications/8bbd7d32e3c9d278c9dc.md)

Lina Mohammad

The purpose of this scoping review was to explore the evidence regarding mental health outcomes, wellbeing status, help\-seeking patterns, and culturally congruent care for Muslim American, Arab American, and Arab Muslim American women within the U\.S\. healthcare system\. The review was guided by the Arksey and O&\#x27;Malley framework and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews \(PRISMA\-ScR\) checklist\. The search was guided by the Population, Concept, and Context \(PCC\) framework\. Articles were sought from PubMed Central, CINAHL, and Scopus, targeting peer\-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026\. Data were analyzed through narrative synthesis\. The review included 29 studies, and five overarching themes emerged: \(1\) high mental health burden across multiple domains; \(2\) multi\-level barriers to help\-seeking and care access; \(3\) discrimination, Islamophobia, and provider bias as structural stressors; \(4\) mental health vulnerabilities and unmet care needs during the perinatal period; and \(5\) resilience, faith, and culturally congruent care as protective factors\. Mosque\-based, culturally congruent, faith\-integrated interventions have demonstrated good acceptability, although evidence of their effectiveness remains preliminary\. These findings highlight the need for greater investment in cultural humility training for providers, disaggregated national data on mental health, and intersectional longitudinal studies to improve equitable mental health care for these populations\.

## [Public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of the use of ChatGPT for self\-diagnosis, health information, and medication use: a cross\-sectional study](../publications/8bc13e58320432e3a2ce.md)

Mohammad S\. Alzahrani; Daniyah A\. Almarghalani; Alaa M\. Hammad; Adnan S\. Alharbi; Manar khaled Alhayfani; Mohammed Saad AlHarthi; Tahani Momenah; Khulood Almehmadi; Amal Hamdan Alzahrani; Daniyah Mansour Alazwari; Ahdab Safar Althobaiti; Mjd A\. Alkhudaidi; Ekram Saad Aljudayi; Dimah Zuwayyid Alsufyani; Hawazin S\. Alsufyani

Background The increasing availability of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) tools, such as ChatGPT, has changed the ways individuals access health information\. While these technologies offer rapid, convenient access to information, concerns remain about their accuracy, safety, and potential influence on health\-related decision\-making\. Understanding public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions toward ChatGPT is essential to support its safe and responsible use in healthcare contexts\. Objective To assess the use of ChatGPT for health\-related purposes and examine demographic, knowledge, attitude, perception, and risk–reward appraisal factors associated with its use among adults recruited from the Western Region of Saudi Arabia\. Methods In this cross\-sectional study, 735 participants completed an online questionnaire\. The instrument selected constructs from the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology \(UTAUT\) and was informed by the technology acceptance model \(TAM\), which captures demographics, health literacy, ChatGPT use, and multi\-item Likert scales measuring knowledge, attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal\. We applied descriptive statistics, chi\-square tests, t tests, ANOVA, and multivariable binary logistic regression\. Results Overall, 66\.3% of the participants reported using ChatGPT for health\-related purposes\. The participants demonstrated good awareness of ChatGPT’s limitations, particularly the importance of consulting healthcare professionals for accurate diagnosis and safe medication use \(mean = 4\.58 ± 0\.74\)\. Attitudes toward ChatGPT were moderate, whereas perceptions of its usefulness and accessibility were generally positive\. Compared with nonusers, ChatGPT users presented significantly higher attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal scores \(all p &lt; 0\.01\), whereas knowledge scores were comparable between the two groups\. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, compared with participants aged ≥45 years, those aged 18–24 years \(aOR = 5\.37, 95% CI: 2\.34–12\.34, p &lt; 0\.001\) and 25–44 years \(aOR = 2\.28, 95% CI: 1\.32–3\.96, p = 0\.003\) had higher odds of reported use\. Participants with a bachelor’s degree \(aOR = 1\.82, 95% CI: 1\.15–2\.89, p = 0\.011\) or postgraduate education \(aOR = 2\.80, 95% CI: 1\.34–5\.85, p = 0\.006\), as well as students \(aOR = 2\.56, 95% CI: 1\.29–5\.09, p = 0\.007\), also had higher odds of use\. Higher total perception scores were independently associated with reported ChatGPT use \(aOR = 1\.19, 95% CI: 1\.12–1\.26, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion ChatGPT is widely used for health\-related purposes, particularly among younger and more educated individuals\. Despite good awareness of its limitations, more favorable perceptions were independently associated with reported use, emphasizing the need for digital health literacy and guidance for safe AI use in healthcare\.

## [Pharmacoepigenetics: from epigenetic regulation to personalized therapeutics](../publications/8bc2d63adf5dab7af82c.md)

Ashley M\. Nguyen; Tamer E\. Fandy

Pharmacoepigenetics is an emerging field of precision medicine that examines how epigenetic modifications influence interindividual variability in drug response\. This review discusses the clinical utility of epigenetic therapy in personalized medicine\. Current FDA\-approved epigenetic drugs including DNA methyltransferase inhibitors, histone deacetylase inhibitors, EZH2 inhibitors, mutant IDH inhibitors, and menin inhibitors are reviewed along with emerging therapies such as BET inhibitors, LSD1 inhibitors, precision epigenetic editing, and combination treatment strategies\. Despite notable advances, challenges such as target selectivity, dose\-limiting toxicity, epigenetic variability and lack of biomarkers for predicting response or selecting patients continue to limit broader clinical implementation of epigenetic drugs\. Continued progress is expected to expand the role of pharmacoepigenetics and improve treatment across a growing range of diseases other than oncology\.

## [Trajectory generation for 3D fly\-by transitions using analytically constrained Bézier curves](../publications/8bdfdec63bbf5f89ed59.md)

Zoe Mbikayi; Agnes Steinert; Florian Holzapfel; Hugh H\. \-T\. Liu

Abstract Conventional trajectory generation remains inadequate for high\-accuracy aircraft guidance because Dubins\- and clothoid\-based turn transitions contain discontinuities in curvature or curvature derivative\. As a result, even when high\-order guidance laws are used to reduce tracking error, the reference trajectory itself does not provide suitable higher\-order feedforward commands\. Existing solutions are also unsatisfactory because they either recover higher\-order smoothness only approximately through post\-processing, rely on numerical optimization, which is unsuitable for deterministic airborne systems, or do not actively account for aircraft dynamic constraints\. This paper closes these gaps with a closed\-form method for generating three\-dimensional turn trajectories as ninth\-order Bézier curves\. The curve is constructed analytically from smoothness requirements and aircraft dynamic constraints, yielding a high\-order reference trajectory that is both dynamically consistent and deterministic\. The methods presented are integrated into an operational trajectory generation system and validated analytically and through flight testing on a 700 kg medical evacuation eVTOL aircraft\.

## [ЕЛЕКТРОННІ ТА ОНЛАЙН\-СЛОВНИКИ ЯК ЗАСІБ ФОРМУВАННЯ ФРАЗЕОЛОГІЧНОЇ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТІ МАЙБУТНІХ ФІЛОЛОГІВ \(НА МАТЕРІАЛІ НІМЕЦЬКОЇ МОВИ\)](../publications/8be3f9bf7689527323fe.md)

Оксана Сивик

У статті досліджено дидактичний потенціал електронних і онлайн\-словників як ефективного засобу формування фразеологічної компетентності майбутніх філологів у процесі вивчення німецької мови\. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена інтенсивною цифровізацією сучасної вищої освіти, упровадженням інформаційно\-комунікаційних техно\- логій у мовну підготовку студентів та необхідністю оновлення традиційних методичних підходів до засвоєння фра\- зеологічного фонду німецької мови\. Обґрунтовано, що саме фразеологічна компетентність є важливим складником професійної іншомовної підготовки майбутніх філологів, оскільки забезпечує адекватне розуміння образних мовних одиниць, сприяє розвитку міжкультурної комунікації та формуванню навичок ефективної мовленнєвої взаємодії\. Проаналізовано функціональні можливості сучасних німецькомовних лексикографічних ресурсів, зокрема Duden Online, Digitales Wörterbuch der deutschen Sprache \(DWDS\), Redensarten\-Index, PONS і Dict\.cc, визначено їхні переваги для роботи з фразеологічними одиницями, ідіомами та стійкими словосполученнями\. Встановле\- но, що використання цифрових словників забезпечує доступ до автентичних мовних контекстів, етимологічних довідок, стилістичних характеристик і граматичних особливостей фразеологізмів, що сприяє глибшому розу\- мінню їхньої семантики та специфіки функціонування в сучасному німецькомовному дискурсі\. У роботі запропоновано методичний підхід до інтеграції електронних словників у практику навчання німець\- кої мови, який охоплює пошуковий, аналітичний і продуктивний етапи роботи з фразеологічним матеріалом\. Доведено, що систематичне використання цифрових лексикографічних ресурсів сприяє розвитку навчальної автономії студентів, удосконаленню їхніх дослідницьких умінь, формуванню критичного ставлення до викорис\- тання автоматизованих перекладачів і генеративних систем штучного інтелекту, а також підвищує точність розуміння та доречного вживання фразеологічних одиниць у професійному мовленні\. Обґрунтовано доцільність упровадження сучасної електронної лексикографії як невід&\#x27;ємного компонента професійної підготовки майбут\- ніх філологів в умовах цифрової трансформації вищої освіти\.

## [The All of Us dataset in scientific research: a bibliometric study of its utilization through 2024](../publications/8c0069000897a0c17124.md)

Yuqi He; Abrielle Spaletta

Objective: This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research publications utilizing the All of Us Research Program dataset to characterize publication trends, collaboration networks, key research topics, and compliance with All of Us publication and presentation policies through December 2024\. Methods: A total of 561 publication titles were collected from the All of Us Publications Directory\. Titles were then searched across Web of Science \(WoS\), Scopus, and PubMed, with WoS \(475 publications identified\) selected as the primary source for analysis\. Productivity metrics, including publication growth, journal distribution, author productivity, and word frequency, were analyzed using Biblioshiny\. Co\-authorship and keyword co\-occurrence networks were visualized in VOSviewer to reveal collaboration structures and emerging research themes\. Results: Among the 475 analyzed publications, 2,803 authors were identified across 211 journals\. The annual number of All of Us publications increased by 82\.45% from 2015 to 2024\. Major research themes included epidemiology, chronic conditions, genomics, and health disparities, with dermatology emerging as a particularly active area\. Network analysis revealed strong intra\-institutional ties and some cross\-institutional collaborations, primarily among R1 universities\. Conclusions: This bibliometric study demonstrates a rapid rise in scholarly activity leveraging the All of Us dataset, characterized by concentrated author and institutional engagement\. These findings highlight both the growing impact of the All of Us dataset and opportunities to foster broader collaborations and diversify participation across the research community\.

## [Metabolic oncology: clonal selection and the pre\-existing origins of cancer resistance](../publications/8c1388b262404840cbc1.md)

Cesar A\. Perez; Annette R\. Khaled

Treatment resistance remains the principal cause of cancer mortality, conventionally modeled as an adaptive response arising under therapeutic pressure\. However, a substantial component of resistance is plausibly established before therapeutic exposure, determined by the metabolic environment of the tissue in which the malignancy arises\. This article advances the hypothesis that chronic metabolic dysregulation constitutes a selective pressure acting on premalignant tissue\. Hyperinsulinemia and increased bioavailable IGF\-1 sustain PI3K–AKT–mTOR and RAS–MAPK signaling in tissues where insulin resistance has preserved mitogenic sensitivity, creating an environment permissive to clonal selection\. Metabolic intermediates serve as obligate substrates for chromatin\-modifying enzymes, coupling metabolic state to the epigenome across the years of subclinical dysregulation that precede diagnosis\. Within this landscape, hypoxia stabilizes G9a and promotes locus\-specific H3K9 methylation at apoptotic and differentiation loci, whereas one\-carbon and S\-adenosylmethionine status determine the available H3K9me1 substrate pool\. The consequence is an elevated apoptotic threshold and enrichment of epigenetically primed, apoptosis\-resistant cells before a tumor is histologically apparent or clinically detected\. The argument is fundamentally Darwinian: the metabolic environment selects its survivors before any therapeutic intervention\. Clonal dynamics subsequently attributed to therapy may therefore reflect, in part, selection of a pre\-existing, resistance\-primed population\. This is advanced not as an alternative to clonal evolution, of which selection of pre\-existing clones is a constituent process, but as a determinant of the pre\-treatment resistance heterogeneity upon which therapeutic pressure acts\. Existing data on metabolic intervention are discordant, and the discrepancies appear more consistent with differences in intervention potency, timing, and trial design than with failure of the proposed mechanism\. Much of the supporting evidence remains indirect and derives from heterogeneous experimental settings\. The observations that would distinguish this framework from reverse causation and treatment\-induced plasticity are specified, together with its central untested prediction: that pretreatment metabolic state correlates with baseline subclonal architecture, chromatin state, and treatment outcome\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL, GESTÃO DO CONHECIMENTO E APRENDIZAGEM](../publications/8c1c53d2da616bda409b.md)

Clodomir de Jesus Chaves Neto; Ana Rute Mendes Pereira; Jose de Ribamar Rodrigues Junior; Midiã do Rosário Martins Conde Monteiro; Nivaldo Ferreira Mousinho; Wilany Chagas Cardoso Esposito

Este estudo analisa o impacto da inteligência artificial na gestão do conhecimento e na inovação dentro das organizações, a partir de uma abordagem qualitativa e bibliográfica baseada em artigos recentes sobre o tema\. O trabalho busca compreender como a IA tem modificado os processos internos, a circulação das informações e a forma como o conhecimento é produzido e compartilhado no ambiente corporativo\. A literatura demonstra que a inteligência artificial, ao ser integrada à rotina das empresas, não apenas automatiza tarefas, mas transforma a cultura organizacional, influencia comportamentos e estimula a aprendizagem contínua\. Além disso, evidencia\-se que a tecnologia pode fortalecer a tomada de decisão, a produtividade e a criatividade, desde que utilizada com responsabilidade, ética e sensibilidade humana\. Conclui\-se que o futuro das organizações depende da capacidade de equilibrar o uso da IA com o desenvolvimento humano, promovendo uma gestão do conhecimento baseada em cooperação, reflexão e inovação constante\.

## [Development and In\-Vivo Evaluation of Rivastigmine\-Loaded PLGA Nanoparticles for Brain Targeting in Alzheimer’s disease](../publications/8c2ed3f42980bbb592ea.md)



Alzheimer disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that is marked with memory lapse and cognitive dysfunction\.Rivastigmine is a dual acetyl\-and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitor and is commonly used in symptomatic therapy, but its clinical activity is severely restricted due to short half\-life, low blood\-brain barrier permeability and systemic side effects\.This current research was to design and test rivastigmine\-impregnated poly \(lactic\-co\-glycolic acid\) nanoparticles to target the brain better in the case of Alzheimer disease\.The emulsionsolvent evaporation method was used to prepare nanoparticles and optimize them in terms of particle size, zeta potential, drug loading and encapsulation efficiency\.The optimized formulation was in the form of nanoscale size with narrow distribution and spherical morphology which made it stable and suitable to deliver to the brain\.In vitro drug release experiments showed sustained and controlled release behavior as opposed to pure rivastigmine\.Pharmacokinetics assessment showed that nanoparticle formulations had higher maximum plasma concentration, longer time to peak plasma concentration, higher area under curve and longer half\-life, which is an indication of better bioavailability\.Biodistribution studies revealed that there was a high level of accumulation of the drug in brain tissue and the brain targeting index was high in comparison to the pure drug\.Animal model behavioral assessment of an Alzheimer disease model established better learning and memory performance of nanoparticlestreated groups over traditional rivastigmine\.These results indicate that poly \(lactic\-co\-glycolic acid\) nanoparticles are effective brain delivery systems to rivastigmine, which leads to a higher pharmacokinetic effect, targeted biodistribution, and therapeutic effect\.The nanoparticulate system developed provides a prospective approach to addressing the shortcomings of the traditional therapy and it can serve as a better method in the management of the disease Alzheimer by means of sustained and targeted delivery of the drugs\.

## [Encoded but Exposed: Language Embeddings can Reveal More Than They Should in Recommender Systems](../publications/8c2f27d033da8e665dea.md)

Linda Beková; Rodrigo Alves

Language embeddings are increasingly used in recommenders to represent item content, but their privacy risks remain poorly understood\. We study whether item embeddings can reveal item identities when an adversary has access to auxiliary item text from external sources\. We show that a simple cosine\-similarity attack can recover item identities with high mean reciprocal rank across language models and candidate\-set settings on two real\-world datasets\. Leakage is strongest when the adversary&\#x27;s partial information overlaps with the victim representation, but it also persists through semantic alignment between independently sourced descriptions\. We further show that item leakage can propagate to user re\-identification from sparse ratings\. Finally, we evaluate obfuscated descriptions as a mitigation and find a clear leakage\-utility tradeoff\.

## [Practical competencies required for professional practice in industrial engineering](../publications/8c5179276e0b0221f485.md)

Zdenka Gyurak Babelova; Augustín Stareček; Natalia Zazova

The main task of process engineers is to optimize processes, whether in terms of efficiency, quality, or costs\. For this important role, it is necessary that industrial engineers and managers possess the required skills that consider all aspects of the work in industrial engineering\. In addition to the ability to design and manage technical solutions, ensure production, and maintain the standard course of processes taking place in manufacturing, the skills of industrial engineers should also reflect the demands of implementing changes, project management, leadership, team management, ensuring occupational fire protection and health and safety requirements, as well as innovation and improvement\. The diversity of requirements placed on industrial engineers leads to the need for an interdisciplinary set of skills\. Therefore, in the present study, we focused on identifying which competencies, in addition to technical ones, are required of professionals in the field of industrial engineering and industrial management\. The analysis revealed differences in competency profiles across the analyzed positions, with managerial positions emphasizing resource optimization and project management, while technical positions placed greater emphasis on proficiency in industrial engineering methods and process optimization\. These findings provide valuable information for employers, higher education institutions, and human resources professionals who seek to align talent development and educational programs with the changing demands of modern industrial practice\. Keywords: competencies; engineering; industry; management; requirements

## [Conductive Polymers in Microbial Fuel Cells for Bioelectricity Generation](../publications/8c533d57a05eda125c27.md)

Zahraddin Zubair Mahmud; Maryam Muawuya Dauda; Umar Dahiru; Zainab Garba Musa; A Umar

Microbial fuel cells \(MFCs\) offer simultaneous wastewater treatment and electricity generation, but their practical performance is limited by inefficient extracellular electron transfer \(EET\) and interfacial losses at the electrode–biofilm interface\. Conductive polymers \(CPs\), particularly polyaniline \(PANI\), polypyrrole \(PPy\), and poly\(3,4\-ethylenedioxythiophene\) \(PEDOT\), have therefore been investigated as electrode modifiers because their electrical, electrochemical, and surface properties can be tailored to support biofilm development and electron transfer\. This review critically evaluates reported evidence for CP\-modified MFC electrodes, with emphasis on electrochemical performance, EET\-related mechanisms, microbial interactions, real\-wastewater applications, stability, and scale\-up limitations\. Laboratory studies demonstrate substantial performance improvements under controlled conditions\. For example, PANI nanofiber\-modified carbon cloth reached 1,091 mW m⁻², PPy/MXene\-modified graphite felt reached 264 mW m⁻² \(vs\. 45 mW m⁻² for bare graphite felt\), and a PEDOT\-modified graphite\-felt system treating palm oil mill effluent reported a maximum current density of 3\.5 A m⁻² and a Coulombic efficiency of 51%\. However, these results are difficult to compare directly because studies differ in electrode architecture, reactor configuration, substrate, inoculum, and performance normalization\. Evidence for specific CP\-mediated EET mechanisms also remains limited, particularly for distinguishing direct, mediated, and long\-distance electron\-transfer contributions\. More importantly, long\-term operation with real wastewater and pilot\-scale CP\-modified systems remains insufficiently investigated\. Existing pilot\-scale MFC studies without CP modification demonstrate that performance under real wastewater conditions can differ substantially from laboratory results\. Future research should therefore prioritize standardized performance reporting, matched real\-wastewater comparisons, long\-term stability testing, pilot\-scale validation, mechanistic EET characterization, and fabrication\-cost assessment\. Overall, CPs show considerable potential for improving MFC electrode performance, but their practical and economic advantages over conventional electrodes remain to be established under realistic operating conditions\.

## [Ethical leadership and job crafting: the role of intrinsic motivation and job feedback](../publications/8c5bee42267a7f9ab02a.md)

Pei Wang; Yu Zhang; Kun Yu

Introduction Drawing on Self\-Determination Theory \(SDT\) and its sub\-theory Cognitive Evaluation Theory \(CET\), the present study examines how ethical leadership relates to employees’ job crafting through intrinsic motivation, and how this indirect relationship is contingent on job feedback\. We proposed that ethical leadership is positively related to job crafting via intrinsic motivation, and that job feedback moderates this indirect effect by providing competence\-relevant informational cues\. Methods We tested our hypotheses using two\-wave data collected from 102 employees in the customer service department of a gaming company in northern China\. Results The results provided preliminary evidence of a moderated mediation pattern, suggesting that the indirect association between ethical leadership and job crafting through intrinsic motivation varied as a function of job feedback\. Discussion These findings extend research on ethical leadership and job crafting by clarifying intrinsic motivation as the motivational mechanism and job feedback as a key boundary condition\. The theoretical and practical implications are discussed\.

## [AR\-LRX: Robustness of Adaptive Residual Linear Regression\-XGBoost Forecasting Across Pharmaceutical and Retail Demand Regimes](../publications/8c5c356b9705cd6f2436.md)

Wahyu Ramadhan; Edi Noersasongko; Abdul Syukur; Moch Arief Soeleman

Residual hybrids that combine a linear model with gradient boosting are widely reported to improve demand forecasting, yet published comparisons mix different splits, preprocessing pipelines and target scales\.This study asks whether such a hybrid is robust and what its robustness depends on\.A single experimental contract is applied to every model, and eight baselines from recent forecasting work are retrained under it instead of quoted\.We propose AR\-LRX, which aligns the first stage with the structure of the data, trains the residual learner on cross\-fitted first\-stage predictions, and weights its correction by a gate selected on the validation fold\.On a 1,115\-outlet drugstore panel AR\-LRX attained a test RMSE of 954\.90, 5\.45% below the strongest retrained baseline, and led the tree baselines at four forecast origins and five seeds\.On pharmaceutical series the gate closed in 17 of 32 configurations, reducing mean degradation from 1\.77 to 0\.22 percent\.

## [Why Anthropologists Should Study Dogs](../publications/8c625a4986c51a37d2d9.md)

Kyle C\. M\. Smith

While primates have traditionally been a focus of evolutionary anthropologists, the domestic dog represents a valuable complementary model due to its long shared evolutionary history with humans\. The advantages of studying dogs are particularly evident in four key areas: \(1\) analyzing evolutionary adaptations, \(2\) understanding humanity&\#x27;s past, \(3\) examining humanity&\#x27;s cultural diversity, and \(4\) assessing factors that influence human health\. Dogs have convergently evolved social cognition and local adaptations \(including altitude adaptations and the ability to digest starches and lactose\) that parallel those of humans, making them valuable models for testing evolutionary hypotheses\. The global spread of dogs also illuminates human population histories, and isotopic analyses of dog remains can be proxies for human dietary data when sampling human remains is infeasible or inappropriate\. Dogs&\#x27; near\-universal presence across human societies and exposure to the same real\-world environments further make them uniquely powerful models for studying cultural variation and health\.

## [PRODUÇÃO CIENTÍFICA MUNDIAL SOBRE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL APLICADA À ELETROENCEFALOGRAFIA NO DIAGNÓSTICO E MONITORIZAÇÃO DA EPILEPSIA: ESTUDO BIBLIOMÉTRICO DE 2020 A 2025](../publications/8c6df33b29fc4d4c7d0c.md)

Gabriela Evaldt Espindola; Jair Henrique de Siqueira Mendes; Merisandra Côrtes de Mattos

Introdução: A epilepsia é uma doença neurológica caracterizada pela ocorrência recorrente de crises epilépticas, cujo diagnóstico e acompanhamento dependem frequentemente da avaliação do eletroencefalograma \(EEG\)\. A análise manual dos registros eletroencefalográficos apresenta limitações relacionadas ao grande volume de dados e à variabilidade entre avaliadores, impulsionando o desenvolvimento de métodos automatizados baseados em inteligência artificial \(IA\)\. Nesse contexto, algoritmos de aprendizado de máquina e profundo vêm sendo investigados para a análise automatizada do EEG, com aplicações na detecção de padrões epileptiformes e no suporte à avaliação de pacientes com epilepsia\.Objetivo: Analisar a produção científica mundial sobre a aplicação de inteligência artificial na eletroencefalografia para diagnóstico e monitorização da epilepsia entre 2020 e 2025\.Métodos: Estudo bibliométrico realizado na base de dados PubMed\. A estratégia de busca incluiu os termos “epilepsy”, “EEG” e “deep learning”\. Foram incluídas publicações entre janeiro de 2020 e dezembro de 2025\. Foram avaliadas características da produção científica, incluindo número de publicações por ano, periódicos e países de origem\.Resultados: Foram identificadas 780 publicações entre 2020 e 2025\. Observou\-se crescimento expressivo da produção científica ao longo do período analisado, passando de 76 publicações em 2020 para 212 em 2025, o que representa aumento aproximado de 179%\. Os periódicos com maior número de publicações foram Scientific Reports \(n=48\), Epilepsia \(n=43\) e Journal of Neural Engineering \(n=36\)\. Os países com maior contribuição científica foram Estados Unidos \(n=422\) e China \(n=403\), seguidos por Canadá \(n=130\) e Austrália \(n=125\)\. A concentração da produção em países com elevado investimento em pesquisa e inovação tecnológica demonstra o papel central dessas nações no avanço de ferramentas computacionais aplicadas à neurologia\. O crescimento observado reflete o interesse crescente em métodos capazes de automatizar a análise de sinais eletroencefalográficos, classificação de padrões elétricos, auxiliar na detecção de crises epilépticas e otimizar a monitorização contínua de pacientes\.Conclusão: A produção científica mundial sobre inteligência artificial aplicada ao EEG na epilepsia apresentou crescimento substancial entre 2020 e 2025\. Esse aumento evidencia a consolidação da IA como área emergente na neurologia, impulsionada pela busca por métodos mais rápidos, reprodutíveis e escaláveis para interpretação de exames\. Os achados sugerem que a pesquisa atual está direcionada ao desenvolvimento de ferramentas com potencial para aprimorar o apoio diagnóstico, reduzir o tempo de análise dos registros eletroencefalográficos e contribuir para uma abordagem mais eficiente no manejo de pacientes com epilepsia, embora sua incorporação clínica ainda dependa de validação e padronização\.

## [Comprehensive Analytical Study on Spatial Reasoning and Adaptation of Human Brain Versus Artificial Intelligence \- A Review Report](../publications/8c77bea76f186ebb48fd.md)

Sahasra V\.; Yukaciny S\.; Nithiyasri V\.; Santhanalakshmi V\.; Logeshwari \.; D\. P\. Sivasakti Balan; R\. J\. Thayumanaswamy

Recent advances in computer vision, spatial computing, robotics, and embodied artificial intelligence \(AI\) have substantially improved machine capabilities in visual perception, navigation, spatial reasoning, and object manipulation\. However, performance on structured benchmarks and controlled environments does not necessarily demonstrate equivalence to human spatial intelligence in complex real\-world situations\. This review examines whether current AI systems can reproduce the breadth and flexibility of human spatial and embodied intelligence, with particular emphasis on their implications for the potential replacement of humans by AI\. The review synthesizes theoretical and empirical literature on human spatial cognition, embodied AI, vision\-language\-action models, robotics, and relevant AI capability benchmarks\. The evidence is organised around four dimensions: \(1\) biological sensorimotor coupling and proprioception, \(2\) zero\-shot spatial problem\-solving and dynamic affordance recognition, \(3\) physical common\-sense reasoning and adaptation, and \(4\) energy\-efficient and context\-sensitive spatial processing\. Existing research indicates that AI systems have achieved considerable progress in perception, navigation, planning, and manipulation, but continue to encounter challenges involving unfamiliar environments, occlusion, uncertainty, dynamic obstacles, changing object configurations, physical interaction, long\-horizon adaptation, and generalisation beyond training distributions\. Human spatial intelligence, in contrast, integrates perception, proprioception, embodied experience, contextual knowledge, physical intuition, memory, and flexible real\-time decision\-making as an interconnected system\. The reviewed evidence therefore suggests that current AI can augment and extend human spatial capabilities but cannot yet reproduce the breadth, adaptability, embodied experience, and contextual flexibility of human spatial intelligence\. Spatial ability consequently represents an important dimension of human irreplaceability and supports a future paradigm of human–AI complementarity rather than complete human substitution\.

## [Dopamine](../publications/8c9af41c6a2f7bb221f9.md)

Kaushik Mitra

Dopamine is a chemical messenger \(neurotransmitter\) in the brain and a circulating hormone in the blood\.While popular culture commonly describes it as the &quot;feel\-good&quot; chemical, neuroscientists categorize it differently\.Rather than producing the sensation of pleasure, dopamine generates an overwhelming urge to seek out things that provide pleasure or assure survival\.

## [Classification\-constrained retrieval of PM 2\.5 vertical profiles from fluorescence\-raman\-mie polarization lidar](../publications/8ca4e335bc5ea9c59aa8.md)

Siying Chen; Yingjie Shu; He Chen; Pan Guo; Yurong Jiang; Guoxing Hu; Xiaolei Zhang; Haokai Yang; Mengjun Feng; Yue Cao; Kaitong Zhang

Abstract\. The vertical distribution of PM2\.5 during urban haze events is jointly affected by aerosol composition, boundary\-layer structure, and regional transport\. Empirical PM2\.5 retrievals based on lidar\-derived extinction coefficients can be biased by the optical contribution of coarse\-mode mineral particles\. This study used fluorescence–Raman–Mie polarization lidar observations in Beijing to identify anthropogenic pollution aerosols \(APA\), desert dust \(DD\), and mineral dust \(MD\) using the particle depolarization ratio \(PDR\) and fluorescence capacity \(Gf\)\. The classification results were incorporated into the construction and application of an empirical extinction–PM2\.5 relationship\. For mixed\-aerosol samples, the APA component fraction and its associated extinction contribution were estimated before retrieving the vertical PM2\.5 distribution\. To quantify the effect of classification constraints, three linear models were developed: a model without aerosol\-type constraints, a PDR\-only screening model, and a model constrained by combined PDR–Gf classification\. Near\-surface, date\-separated validation using 411 hourly samples from 69 observation dates showed that the combined\-classification model achieved an RMSE of 17\.32 µg m−3, an MAE of 13\.54 µg m−3, and a Bias of 3\.30 µg m−3\. Compared with the model without aerosol\-type constraints, the RMSE, MAE, and Bias decreased by 38\.2 %, 45\.0 %, and approximately 83\.0 %, respectively\. Uncertainty analysis showed that classification end\-member and aerosol\-type\-dependent lidar\-ratio perturbations affected the quantitative PM2\.5 estimates under mixed\-aerosol conditions, whereas the residual scatter and parameter stability of the empirical extinction–PM2\.5 relationship were the dominant sources of prediction uncertainty\. For a mixed\-to\-pollution aerosol evolution episode in Beijing in November 2024, the classification\-constrained PM2\.5 vertical structure was physically consistent with temperature stratification, wind fields, and backward trajectories\. Seasonal testing showed no stable and consistent improvement from season\-specific fitting\. The proposed method provides classification\-constrained estimates of the PM2\.5 vertical structure under APA\-dominated conditions in Beijing\. Model parameters should be recalibrated using local observations when applied to regions, seasons, or aerosol conditions with substantially different composition\.

## [RECENT ADVANCES IN DIRECT SEEDED RICE: PHYSIOLOGICAL ADAPTATION, CROP MANAGEMENT, AND GENETIC IMPROVEMENT](../publications/8cab6b2ccbe8a45ecf5c.md)

Vaishnavi\. T S; N\. Sritharan; V Ravichandran; Suresh\. R; Kannan\. P

Owing to insufficient water, labour shortages and accelerating climate change, direct seeded rice \(DSR\) has emerged as a feasible and resource\-efficient alternative to conventional transplanted puddled rice \(TPR\) systems, conserving water and reducing methane emissions\. However, the initial growth phases are frequently impeded by inadequate seedling emergence, intensive weed competition, nutritional deficiencies and exposure to variable soil moisture and aeration conditions in some DSR systems, including low nitrogen use efficiency, which can impair the establishment of a healthy crop stand and stability of its yield under DSR\. Identifying and phenotyping rice germplasm for critical physiological traits is essential for developing cultivars that thrive in DSR environments\. The physiological basis of genotypes adaption to DSR conditions need to be integrated with phenotyping and breeding strategies\. This review synthesizes the knowledge of the physiological traits that facilitate DSR adaptation evaluates both conventional and high\-throughput phenotyping \(HTP\) techniques — digital imaging, canopy temperature measurement, chlorophyll fluorescence analysis, and remote sensing technologies to precisely evaluate these traits in field and controlled environment and examines how quantitative trait loci \(QTL\) mapping, genome\-wide association studies \(GWAS\), and marker\-assisted selection \(MAS\), significantly facilitates the development of rice varieties suitable for DSR\. The review highlights the importance of multi\-trait phenotyping frameworks and multi\-environment testing in accelerating genetic improvement and ensuring sustainable rice production in direct seeded agricultural systems\.

## [Dynamic weight quantization for embedded federated learning in LoRa mesh networks: A case study](../publications/8cb3262b7cd688090b19.md)

Nil Llisterri Giménez; Fèlix Freitag

The integration of federated learning \(FL\) into resource\-constrained devices promises a re\-trainable distributed Machine Learning \(ML\) intelligence in Internet of Things \(IoT\) networks\. However, in low\-power wide\-area network \(LPWAN\) technologies such as LoRa, the extremely limited and dynamically varying bandwidth at each node poses a major obstacle to the practical deployment of FL\. While static model quantization has been proposed to reduce communication overhead, it cannot adapt to changing network conditions\. This paper investigates dynamic weight quantization \(DynQuant\) as a communication\-aware strategy for embedded federated learning over LoRa networks\. DynQuant enables both clients and the server to flexibly select the quantization bit width at each FL round based on dynamic system and network conditions\. We first explore the design space of dynamic quantization through extensive simulations, analyzing the tradeoff between model accuracy, quantization strategy, and communication cost\. Subsequently, we validate the practical feasibility of the approach through a prototype implementation on real microcontroller\-based nodes interconnected via a LoRa mesh network\. Our results show that dynamic quantization can significantly reduce the volume of transmitted data and communication time, while only slightly affecting the final model accuracy\. For instance, early quantization achieves an 8\.6% reduction of communicated model data and the asymmetric 6 → 8 quantization strategy achieves a 12\.5% reduction in communicated model data compared to static 8\-bit quantization\. These findings support dynamic quantization as a practical and effective mechanism for tailoring federated learning to dynamic, low\-data\-rate IoT networks\.

## [Convergence bounds for fixed, adaptive, and stochastic gradient methods under Polyak–Łojasiewicz geometry](../publications/8cb708eba28fc5c92160.md)

Yousef Farhang; Betül Öztel; Samet Yıldırım; Şaban Onur Viga; Mehmet Akif Çifçi; Fazlı Yıldırım

The Polyak–Łojasiewicz \(PL\) inequality offers a useful way to study gradient\-based optimization beyond the setting of strong convexity, while still allowing linear convergence under suitable smoothness conditions\. This study develops a unified descent\-based analysis for fixed\-step gradient descent, safeguarded objective\-gap step rules, Armijo backtracking, and mini\-batch stochastic gradient descent\. For the deterministic methods, the analysis provides explicit contraction bounds that show how convergence depends on smoothness, gradient domination, and step\-selection parameters\. In the stochastic setting, conditional unbiasedness together with a bounded conditional variance leads to a finite\-time expectation bound and an upper estimate for the asymptotic residual neighborhood\. The analysis is further extended to generalized gradient inequalities\. Smooth explicit gradient descent yields linear or polynomial convergence depending on the exponent, whereas superlinear behavior for exponents below one half is established separately for an implicit decrease sequence\. This distinction avoids transferring continuous\-time behavior directly to explicit discrete gradient iterations\. For continuously differentiable squared\-error models, uniform spectral bounds on the Jacobian Gram matrix are used to derive regional gradient domination relative to the zero\-loss target\. A complementary path\-length argument gives a sufficient condition for trajectory containment and establishes convergence to zero loss under the stated regional assumptions\. Numerical illustrations based on quadratic objectives, power functions, implicit recurrences, stochastic models, and a constant\-kernel least\-squares example are used to examine the theoretical bounds, accepted Armijo steps, backtracking costs, convergence regimes, and stochastic uncertainty\.

## [Achieving sustainable desertification control: insights from symbiosis between the Taklamakan Desert\-fringe shelter\-belt enclosure project and desert\-based industries](../publications/8cb8849661f2ddb36425.md)

Hua Li

There is an inherent trade\-off between ecological restoration goals and the survival needs of inhabitants in desertification control\. From an ecological perspective, large\-scale planting of trees and grasses, sand fixation through enclosed forest cultivation, and rotational cropping are core measures for curbing shifting sands, restoring soil and water, and building robust ecological barriers to prevent further desertification\. From an economic perspective, local residents in desert areas rely heavily on traditional grassland grazing, desert reclamation, and the harvesting of desert shrubs for fuel and forage\. This gives rise to the tangible dilemma of “ecological restoration versus subsistence survival” in desertification control\. Desert\-based industries are considered conducive to addressing the trade\-off dilemma between ecological restoration and economic gain\. This study was conducted through a multi\-case study of the symbiosis between the Taklamakan Desert\-fringe Shelter\-belt Enclosure Project \(TDSEP\), a part of China’s Three Norths Shelterbelt Program \(TNSP\), and six types of desert\-based industries embedded in the TDSEP, including the Yutian rose industry, Kunyu jujube industry, Hetian walnut \+ jujube industry, Shache Eucommia Industry, Shaya centralized photovoltaic industry, and Shaya “saxaul \+ cistanche deserticola \+ distributed photovoltaic” industry\. It was found that the factors and mechanisms impacting the symbiosis between TDSEP and industry\-based industries are categorized into three categories: the symbiotic environment and material factors of production, the technological factors of production, and the transformative agencies enabling symbiosis, thus responding to the research questions proposed in the introduction section\. Therefore, policy insights and implications may involve fostering a favorable environment for symbiosis, selecting adaptable symbiotic units, promoting technological advancements, and forming an inclusive participating network among stakeholders\.

## [Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large\-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study](../publications/8cc1236bac30a4f52b77.md)

Yunfeng Chen; 芮云云

Background The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure\. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging\. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics\. Methods This multicenter cohort study included 3000 patients with acute appendicitis\. Following rigorous data reduction using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, eight supervised machine learning algorithms were constructed\. The optimal predictive algorithm was comprehensively evaluated across training, internal testing, and independent external validation cohorts\. The SHapley Additive exPlanations framework was utilized to provide transparent model interpretability, and the final algorithm was deployed as a dynamic digital calculator\. Results Six independent predictors were identified, including the Systemic Immune Inflammation Index, C\-reactive protein to albumin ratio, glucose to lymphocyte ratio, Prognostic Nutritional Index, periappendiceal fluid, and the sonographic loss of the submucosal echogenic layer\. The Random Forest model demonstrated the highest discriminative performance among the evaluated algorithms, achieving an area under the curve of 0\.914\. The model’s discrimination, calibration, and decision\-analytic performance were consistently evaluated in the internal testing and external validation cohorts\. SHAP analysis indicated that systemic inflammatory indices and sonographic features reflecting local disease severity made important contributions to the model’s predicted risk of septic shock\. These findings should be interpreted as predictive associations rather than evidence of biological causality or synergy\. Conclusion This multicenter study developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early risk stratification of septic shock\. The publicly accessible calculator may support individualized risk assessment; however, prospective impact evaluation is required to determine whether its clinical implementation facilitates earlier resuscitation or improves patient outcomes\.

## [Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation](../publications/8cd257cc89b8d70a92b1.md)

Zhenwei Tang; Jintao Liu; Di Bai; Xidong Wu; Xinwu Cheng

Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs \(SIDs\)\. Ranking from SIDs alone has two appeals: SID prompts are far shorter than the matched item text, and although item codes are fixed from content, the backbone learns their token embeddings in part from user\-item interaction sequences, so the tokens can carry behavioral signal that item text lacks\. That training targets next\-item generation, and whether it supports ranking a supplied slate from SIDs alone is untested\. We build ReRankID, a controlled testbed in which models reason and rank from a history and slate shown only as SIDs, varying item rendering, history length, and slate size one at a time\. On this testbed, such models often copy the input order instead of reranking, and readable metadata does not repair the failure\. We compare supervised fine\-tuning, rejection\-sampled self\-training, on\-policy distillation, and verifier\-based reinforcement learning as post\-training methods and find that they elicit the missing behavior\. The strongest post\-trained model, the 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward, gives the best SID\-only ranking and matches strong text\-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer\. It ranks above random with no history at all, where a caption\-reading reference does not, and it keeps its gains at long histories, where text prompts pass 50k tokens and the caption\-reading reference stops improving\. In a paired rationale audit, this model argues trade\-offs better than that reference but describes items less accurately\. The common post\-training methods we test thus elicit ranking from SIDs but not faithful item descriptions, which calls for post\-training that improves the reasoning itself, not only the ranking it produces\.

## [Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans](../publications/8ce1bc10661a15627205.md)

Joyce Oerlemans; Ricardo J\. Alejandro; Dimitri Hemelsoet; Eva Genbrugge; Katie Bouche; Luc Defreyne; Veerle De Herdt; Clay B\. Holroyd

Abstract The reward positivity \(RewP\) is an event\-related brain potential \(ERP\) component associated with feedback and goal completion\. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex \(ACC\), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem\. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram \(EEG\) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’\. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude\. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial\-and\-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP\. Non\-parametric voxel\-based lesion\-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’ significantly attenuated RewP amplitude\. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors\.

## [How extensive and coordinated is farmers’ participation in agricultural value chains in China? Evidence from contractual–digital chain coupling](../publications/8ce6ec0ce8b9d9c34929.md)

Rashid Latief; Yuanyuan Peng; Xuanheng Wu

Integrating smallholders into modern agricultural value chains is essential for agricultural modernization and rural development\. Using survey data from the China Rural Revitalization Survey \(CRRS\), this study examines farmers’ participation in contractual and digital chains\. An entropy\-based index system is constructed to measure the depth of participation in both chains, and a coupling coordination model is employed to evaluate their interaction and coordinated development\. The results indicate that the participation levels of Chinese farmers in both contractual and digital chains remain relatively low, although participation in digital chains is generally higher than that in contractual chains\. The degree of coupling coordination between the two chains falls within the category of “slightly unbalanced,” suggesting considerable scope for improving systemic coordination\. Further analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity in contractual\-chain participation among farmers, whereas digital\-chain participation exhibits comparatively lower inequality, despite persistent disparities in the distribution of digital engagement\. However, the disparity in the coupling and synergistic development between the contractual and digital chains is relatively limited\. These differences are associated with farmer heterogeneity and regional variation in chain participation\. Within the surveyed sample, eastern regions demonstrate relatively higher participation in digital chains but comparatively weaker participation in contractual chains, resulting in lower levels of coupling coordination\. In contrast, southern regions, benefiting from relative advantages in both chains, exhibit higher levels of coupling coordination\. This study clarifies the developmental stage of farmers’ participation in contractual and digital chains and their coupling coordination, offering new insights into Chinese agricultural practices and the process of agricultural modernization\.

## [Kebijakan dan program peningkatan kompetensi guru PAI dalam upaya meningkatkan mutu pendidikan di madrasah](../publications/8d017178dc2aac3ba1bb.md)

Ayu Windarsih; Tasman Hamami

This research is motivated by the strategic role of the competence of Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) teachers in improving the quality of madrasah education in Indonesia, but its implementation still faces various obstacles in the field\. The purpose of this study is to analyze national education policies and the effectiveness of PAI teacher competency improvement programs in improving the quality of madrasah education, especially in the context of challenges in the 3T \(Frontier, Outermost, and Disadvantaged\) areas\. The research method used is qualitative descriptive with a literature study approach and content analysis techniques to relevant policy documents and scientific literature\. The results of the study show that policies such as the National Education System Law, the Regulation of the Minister of Religion Number 60 of 2015, the Teacher Professional Education Program \(PPG\), and the Independent Teaching Platform have provided the basis for strengthening the competence of PAI teachers, but their implementation still faces obstacles in the form of inequality of access to training, limited technological infrastructure, and low distribution of resources in the 3T area\. In addition, the policy approach that tends to top\-down causes the program to not fully comply with the contextual needs of madrasas in the regions\. The conclusion of this study emphasizes that improving the quality of madrassas requires a more adaptive, inclusive, and local needs\-based policy reformulation through strengthening School\-Based Management \(SBM\), equitable access to teacher training, and effective infrastructure and madrasah leadership support so that improving the competence of PAI teachers can run more sustainably and fairly\. Abstrak Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh peran strategis kompetensi guru Pendidikan Agama Islam \(PAI\) dalam meningkatkan mutu pendidikan madrasah di Indonesia, namun implementasinya masih menghadapi berbagai kendala di lapangan\. Tujuan penelitian ini, untuk menganalisis kebijakan pendidikan nasional serta efektivitas program peningkatan kompetensi guru PAI dalam meningkatkan mutu pendidikan madrasah, khususnya dalam konteks tantangan di wilayah 3T \(Terdepan, Terluar, dan Tertinggal\)\. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif dengan pendekatan studi pustaka dan teknik analisis isi terhadap dokumen kebijakan serta literatur ilmiah yang relevan\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kebijakan seperti Undang\-Undang Sistem Pendidikan Nasional, Peraturan Menteri Agama Nomor 60 Tahun 2015, Program Pendidikan Profesi Guru \(PPG\), dan Platform Merdeka Mengajar telah memberikan dasar penguatan kompetensi guru PAI, namun implementasinya masih menghadapi kendala berupa ketimpangan akses pelatihan, keterbatasan infrastruktur teknologi, serta rendahnya pemerataan sumber daya di wilayah 3T\. Selain itu, pendekatan kebijakan yang cenderung top\-down menyebabkan program belum sepenuhnya sesuai dengan kebutuhan kontekstual madrasah di daerah\. Simpulan penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa peningkatan mutu madrasah memerlukan reformulasi kebijakan yang lebih adaptif, inklusif, dan berbasis kebutuhan lokal melalui penguatan Manajemen Berbasis Sekolah \(MBS\), pemerataan akses pelatihan guru, serta dukungan infrastruktur dan kepemimpinan madrasah yang efektif agar peningkatan kompetensi guru PAI dapat berjalan lebih berkelanjutan dan berkeadilan\.

## [Ultrasonic Sensing Systems: From Hardware Design to Interactive and Physiological Applications](../publications/8d0755c3fcec52077dcb.md)

Shirui Cao

This research investigates the design and implementation of ultrasonic sensing systems that allow everyday devices to perceive and interpret signals beyond the audible spectrum\. By integrating advancements in hardware design, firmware optimization, signal processing, and machine learning, the work advances ultrasonic sensing from foundational system architectures to high\-level applications in interaction and human physiology\. The first part presents a six\-layer HDI PCB designed for a battery\-powered wearable device featuring an 8\-microphone array\. The accompanying firmware supports real\-time ultrasonic beamforming and signal analysis, enabling high\-resolution spatial sensing within a compact and energy\-efficient form factor\. Next, the thesis examines how commodity smartphones can be repurposed to support enhanced ultrasonic sensing\. Through modifications to the Android audio stack that increase system sampling rates, the platform achieves improved accuracy and unlocks new sensing applications—using only the device’s built\-in microphones and speakers\. Extending the exploration of consumer audio platforms, a multi\-modality fusion model is developed for headphones, combining audible and ultrasonic features\. This model enables whisper\-level and silent\-speech keyword detection, providing a privacy\-preserving and noise\-robust interface that broadens the possibilities for future auditory computing devices\. Finally, the research introduces a through\-skin ultrasonic sensing system implemented on smartphones, capable of detecting subsurface physiological signals such as blood flow\. This demonstrates the feasibility of transforming mobile devices into accessible, non\-invasive biomedical sensors\. Together, these projects establish a unified framework for ultrasonic sensing systems, bridging hardware design, software adaptation, and intelligent signal processing to support both interactive and physiological applications\.

## [WHEN SILOED MARKETING TEAMS RAISE ACQUISITION COSTS: THE PRICE OF ANARCHY INSIDE A SINGLE ADVERTISER](../publications/8d0d1eeae9272c0f70c7.md)

Igor I\. Ivitskiy

Firms that divide customer acquisition among product, regional or channel teams can see the total cost per lead rise even when each team meets its own target\. The subject of the study is the customer acquisition system of a single advertiser whose teams draw leads from a shared pool of prospects, and the gap between the equilibrium reached by independent teams and the cost\-minimizing allocation\. The purpose of the paper is to specify when this situation forms a congestion game, to quantify its coordination cost and to translate the known remedies of such games into advertising management\. Methodology\. The study applies the theory of atomic splittable congestion games\. The model assumes homogeneous, deduplicated leads and fixed quotas, with the volume of each team raising the cost of comparable leads for the others; because Google Ads keeps campaigns within one account from bidding each other up, the cost increase comes from depleting the shared pool rather than from auction prices\. A closed\-form benchmark is derived analytically and checked by numerical simulation, and two conditional extensions draw on Braess&\#x27;s paradox and on the bullwhip effect\. Results\. The paper introduces the Funnel Coordination Gap, the share of acquisition cost that coordination can avoid\. A single team produces no gap and each additional team widens it: in the benchmark, ten teams spend 22% more than a coordinated firm, the avoidable share approaches 25% as teams multiply, and independent teams take up to twice the cost\-minimizing volume from the shared pool\. Known bounds for this class of games cap the avoidable share at one quarter for identical teams and at one third for teams with different quotas\. A personal internal charge per lead, an established toll mechanism, makes the cost\-minimizing allocation an equilibrium\. Under stated conditions, a costless link between funnel stages can raise total cost by one third, and lower bounds on lead variance multiply across stages unless end\-customer conversion data are shared\. Conclusions\. The internal team structure of an advertiser is a measurable source of acquisition cost, and its size depends on the number of teams and on how sharply the cost of the shared pool rises with volume\. Practical implications\. Managers obtain a diagnostic of team structure, an internal price for shared sources, a holdout test for channel removal and a controlled experiment that could falsify the central assumption\. Value / originality\. The paper contributes the conditions under which acquisition inside a firm is a congestion game, a closed\-form advertising benchmark placed against exact bounds, and a translation of known pricing mechanisms into management instruments\.

## [Reduced Stacking Classifier Model with Optimized feature Selection for Efficient Phishing Website Detection](../publications/8d1158d1a74491368a7b.md)

I\. N\. Thompson; Victor Thomas Emmah; D\. Mathias

Phishing websites remain an effective vehicle for credential theft and financial fraud, while machine\-learning detectors must increasingly balance predictive performance against the cost of deployment\. Stacking ensembles can improve classification by combining diverse learners, but large ensembles operating on full feature sets increase inference cost\. This paper examines an HHO–GWO reduced stacking model for phishing website classification\. It uses Harris Hawks Optimisation \(HHO\) for feature selection, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting classifiers, and Grey Wolf Optimiser \(GWO\) weights for combining classifier probabilities\. The model was evaluated on the UCI Phishing Websites dataset and the Mendeley Web Page Phishing Detection dataset using five random seeds, and compared with individual classifiers, unoptimised stacking, a replicated nine\-classifier stacking baseline, and ablated configurations\. It obtained mean accuracies of 94\.40% and 96\.38% and mean F1\-scores of 94\.53% and 96\.31% on UCI and Mendeley, respectively\. It used an average of 23\.2 of 30 UCI features and 65\.0 of 87 Mendeley features\. Relative to the nine\-classifier baseline, mean inference latency declined from 1\.924 ms to 0\.465 ms on UCI and from 1\.457 ms to 0\.271 ms on Mendeley, corresponding to reductions of 75\.8% and 81\.4%\. The associated accuracy differences were 0\.47 and 0\.39 percentage points\. The findings position HHO–GWO reduced stacking as a practical accuracy–efficiency alternative for offline phishing classification experiments\. Its suitability for live URL screening or evolving attack streams requires further validation\.

## [Single\-cell multi\-omics in IPF and COPD: from atlas to impact](../publications/8d1ee98c533c96769316.md)

Puja Mehta; Chao He; Connar M\. Mawer; Xiting Yan; Iván O\. Rosas; Naftali Kaminski

Single\-cell and spatial multi\-omics technologies are transforming our understanding of the normal lung cellular repertoire as well the molecular and cellular networks of chronic lung diseases\. In this review we focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis \(IPF\) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\)\. We briefly review technologies and discuss technical and analytical challenges, including strategies to optimise batch correction, dataset integration, and sample\-aware differential gene expression; we describe global lung reference atlases, enabled by large\-scale data\-sharing, providing accessible frameworks for cross\-study validation, lineage and trajectory inference, and inter\-disease comparisons; and we outline the major findings in COPD and IPF\. In IPF, mechanistic insights include: \(i\) loss of the normal alveolar niche \(ii\) aberrant basaloid epithelial cells linked to failed regeneration, expansion of \(iii\) profibrotic SPP1\+ macrophages and \(iv\) disease\-associated CTHRC1 \+ and HAS1 hi fibroblast subtypes, that localise to fibrotic niches, and \(v\) extensive vascular and immune remodelling\. In COPD these approaches demonstrate: \(i\) loss of aerocytes; \(ii\) expansion of MMP \-expressing macrophages, \(iii\) activated neutrophil influx and \(iv\) B\-cell lymphoid follicle activation and endothelial inflammation \(iv\) some overlapping features with IPF\. We highlight gaps and future opportunities, including under\-representation of early disease stages, incomplete resolution of neutrophils, tissue\-resident immune compartments, and cross\-organ integration\. Looking forward, integration with clinical phenotypes and imaging is accelerating translation towards precision medicine, enabling biomarker discovery, cellular endotyping, and therapeutic prioritisation\. Advances in multimodal profiling, computational pipelines, next generation technologies, open science initiatives and artificial intelligence will propel the field toward predictive, patient\-specific insight and mechanistically informed, stratified trial design\.

## [Controlled Evaluation for Numeric\-Field Forgery Detection in SROIE Receipts using Fine\-Tuned EfficientNetV2\-S](../publications/8d28361bedbd8b00b088.md)

Tousi Adak; Priyanshu Mukherjee; Sudipta Das; Jahir Paik

Altered amounts, dates, and identifiers on retail receipts represent a practical source of expense and tax fraud\. However, public receipt datasets such as Scanned Receipts OCR and Information Extraction \(SROIE\) contain authentic receipts but do not provide forged counterparts, limiting controlled evaluation of receipt\-forgery detection methods\. Chakraborty \(2025\) reported 97\.1% accuracy using a convolutional neural network \(CNN\)\-based receipt\-forgery detection framework\. Building on this research context, the present study investigates forgery detection at the numeric\-field level, focusing on receipt components that directly carry financial information\. Using SROIE, a receipt\-grouped benchmark of paired authentic and synthetically forged numeric\-field crops is constructed\. Two controlled forgery mechanisms are considered: splicing a donor numeric field from the same receipt and erasing and re\-rendering a field with a specified proportion of its digits changed\. Authentic and forged crops undergo the same Joint Photographic Experts Group \(JPEG\) compression procedure, and receipt\-level grouping is used for training, validation, and test partitioning at approximately 70/15/15\. An ImageNet\-pretrained EfficientNetV2\-S is fine\-tuned end\-to\-end using linear warm\-up, cosine learning\-rate decay, and exponential moving average \(EMA\) weights, with model selection based exclusively on validation accuracy\. On the held\-out test set of 4,602 crops, comprising 2,301 authentic and 2,301 forged samples, the reference detector achieves 98\.09% accuracy, 99\.42% precision, 96\.74% recall, an F1\-score of 0\.9806, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve \(AUC\) of 0\.9971 at a fixed decision threshold of 0\.5 in a single run with seed 42\. Most remaining errors correspond to missed forgeries\. The reported accuracy is numerically higher than the 97\.1% reported by Chakraborty \(2025\), but direct comparison is limited by differences in datasets, sample construction, and evaluation protocols\. Gradient\-weighted Class Activation Mapping \(Grad\-CAM\) analysis indicates attention to numeric text regions but also, in some cases, to crop boundaries and background regions, suggesting that synthetic generation artifacts may contribute to the observed performance\. As the study relies on synthetic forgeries without multiple baseline architectures, ablation experiments, multiple random seeds, or real\-world forged\-receipt evaluation, the findings are limited to the defined synthetic tampering processes rather than general real\-world forgery\-detection performance\.

## [Algorithm or Assembly? An Experimental Study of Recommendations by AI Versus Deliberative Mini\-Publics in Democratic Decision\-Making](../publications/8d32841e0a8816887295.md)

Nuri Kim; Myojung Chung; S\. Mo Jones\-Jang; Sangwon Lee; Jihyang Choi

Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) renewed debates about who—or what—can legitimately contribute to democratic processes\. While both AI and deliberative mini\-publics can supplement citizens’ efforts to form judgments about issues, little is known about how citizens evaluate policy advice from these sources\. In an online survey experiment with U\.S\. adults \(N = 502\), participants read a mock news story reporting a policy recommendation, attributed either to an AI system or a deliberative citizens’ assembly\. Opinion climate was orthogonally varied to assess contextual influences\. Results were split: citizens’ assemblies were rated fairer and more satisfying, but AI was perceived to be more useful\. Opinion climate cues had no moderating effects\. Further analysis indicated that acceptance of AI versus citizens’ assembly recommendations depends on individual factors, such as prior attitudes toward the issue and trust in AI\. Findings offer theoretical and practical implications for designing democratic decision support systems\.

## [Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human\-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales](../publications/8d35dd8229812495b71a.md)

Christiane Attig; Christiane B\. Wiebel\-Herboth; Patricia Wollstadt; Tim Schrills; Mourad Zoubir; Thomas Franke

As human–AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human–AI interaction are needed\. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale \(PCS\), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale \(TPS\), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory\. The PCS captures an agent’s perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support\. Both scales were adapted for human–human cooperation to enable cross\-agent comparisons\. Across three studies \(complete N=409\) encompassing a cooperative card game \(N1=94\), LLM interaction \(N2=182\), and a decision\-support system \(N3=133\), analyses of dimensionality, reliability, and validity indicated that both scales successfully differentiated between cooperation partners of varying cooperative quality and showed construct validity in line with expectations\. The scales provide a basis for empirical investigation and system evaluation across a wide range of human–AI cooperation contexts\.

## [Turismo Perú 360 hacia un modelo competitivo, inclusivo y regenerativo](../publications/8d3f8f998dd8486f1359.md)

El libro Turismo Perú 360\. A través de seis ejes fundamentales —gobernanza, talento humano, desarrollo territorial, mercados, transformación digital e investigación—, el autor examina las limitaciones estructurales que dificultan el aprovechamiento del potencial turístico del país\. Asimismo, aborda temas como la diversificación de la oferta turística, la inteligencia artificial, la profesionalización del sector y el turismo regenerativo\.
