## [Effects of Combined Drought and Salinity Stress on Oxidative Damage and the Antioxidant Enzyme System in Aronia \(Aronia melanocarpa L\.\) ‘Nero’ under In Vitro Conditions](../publications/8d3fd77345553ba278ce.md)

Çağlar Kaya

This study investigated the effects of single and combined drought \(10% PEG\-6000\) and salinity \(100 mM NaCl\) stress on oxidative injury, antioxidant defense, and physiological responses of aronia \(Aronia melanocarpa L\.\) ‘Nero’ under in\-vitro conditions\. After 14 days, combined stress induced markedly stronger biochemical disruption than individual treatments\. Malondialdehyde \(MDA\) increased from 8\.4 nmol g\-1 FW in the control to 14\.7 \(PEG\) and 16\.2 \(NaCl\), reaching 24\.8 nmol g\-1 FW under combined stress\. Hydrogen peroxide \(H2O2\) rose from 3\.2 to 11\.6 µmol g\-1 FW in the dual treatment, indicating intensified reactive oxygen species accumulation\. Antioxidant enzymes were strongly upregulated in response to stress\. SOD activity increased from 62\.4 to 138\.6 U mg\-1 protein under combined stress, while CAT \(21\.8 U mg\-1 protein\), APX \(13\.2 U mg\-1 protein\), GR \(9\.7 U mg\-1 protein\), and POD \(29\.4 U mg\-1 protein\) also showed their highest activities in the dual treatment\. Non\-enzymatic antioxidants followed a similar pattern: proline increased nearly fivefold \(1\.8 to 8\.7 µmol g\-1 FW\), total phenolics rose from 5\.4 to 13\.8 mg GAE g\-1 FW, flavonoids reached 5\.2 mg CE g\-1 FW, and DPPH scavenging activity increased from 38\.6% to 64\.3%\. Despite enhanced antioxidant responses, oxidative markers remained elevated under combined stress\. Relative water content declined from 91\.4% to 61\.3%, and SPAD values decreased from 42\.5 to 28\.9, indicating impaired water status and chlorophyll stability\. Simultaneous osmotic and ionic stress, therefore, imposes a substantially greater redox and physiological burden than single stress exposure in aronia ‘Nero’\. Future studies should evaluate different stress intensities and exposure durations across various aronia cultivars and under field conditions, while also investigating the molecular and metabolic mechanisms underlying tolerance to combined stress\.

Priyanka Kiran Khawale

## [The algorithmic artrepreneur: rethinking creative entrepreneurship under platform governance](../publications/8d5b755dcd6687a3ea82.md)

Maria Susan Mathew; Jaya Jacob; Ann Mariya Cyriac; Ajimon George; Ajo Andrews; Jerome Varghese; Jibil K John

Digital platforms have revolutionized creativity in many ways, offering new possibilities for audiences to access, discover, engage with, and purchase artistic work\. Meanwhile, the platformization of the production of creative content has introduced algorithmic systems that increasingly mediate visibility, content circulation, audience reach, and economic opportunity\. This Mini Review brings together research on arts entrepreneurship, creative work, platformization, algorithmic governance and creator labor to discuss the impact of these changes on the agency of arts entrepreneurs\. It highlights the possibility of platforms to lower some traditional obstacles to artistic entrepreneurship, but also to create new forms of infrastructural dependence, namely in terms of algorithmic visibility, metricisation, platform norms and monetization systems\. The review suggests that contemporary artrepreneurs operate through constrained and negotiated agency, interpreting, adapting to, and sometimes challenging platform conditions\. The notion of the algorithmic artrepreneur is introduced to describe an artrepreneur whose entrepreneurial agency is reconfigured through continuous negotiation with algorithmically mediated platform infrastructures affecting visibility, audience access, content circulation and value creation\. This mini review conceptualizes this agency through four interrelated dimensions: creative agency, platform agency, relational agency and entrepreneurial agency\. Three tensions are highlighted: the tension between visibility as an entrepreneurial opportunity and as a form of labor, the tension between platform adaptation as an entrepreneurial strategy and as a creative constraint, and the tension between digital access as a democratization and as an infrastructural dependence\. There is a need to look into algorithmic agency, visibility labor, inequality, platform diversification and sustainable creative careers in the future\.

## [The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Portfolio Performance: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Traditional Portfolio Optimisation Approaches](../publications/8d737d4b6b6aa0cf19a0.md)

S Reshma; V Narendra

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are now being used in investment products, but it remains uncertain whether these tools consistently outperform established portfolio optimisation methods or control risk more effectively\. This study compares three AI/ML\-oriented exchange\-traded funds—AIEQ, QRFT and AMOM—with three funds following minimum\-variance or low\-volatility strategies—USMV, SPLV and ACWV\. The comparison covers 2021–2025 and relies on secondary data for annual total returns, the S&amp;P 500 total\-return benchmark and the three\-month Treasury bill rate\. Performance is assessed using returns, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, and the worst annual loss\. Risk\-management efficiency is represented by a combined measure based on volatility, downside capture, worst\-year loss and beta\. The analysis uses chi\-square tests, one\-way and two\-way ANOVA, multiple regression and mediation testing\. Traditional funds recorded stronger risk\-management efficiency \(F = 67\.9, p = 0\.001\), while the difference in average annual returns between the groups was not statistically significant \(10\.8% for ML\-based funds and 7\.8% for traditional funds; p = 0\.622\)\. Although the regression model was significant overall \(R² = 0\.76\), market conditions were the only significant individual predictor\. Results also indicate that the relative performance of the two approaches changes with the market: ML\-based funds did better in rising periods but experienced substantially larger losses in 2022\. Risk\-management efficiency did not significantly explain returns, and the proposed mediation effect was not supported\. Given the limited sample, these findings should be treated as preliminary rather than conclusive\.

## [Artificial intelligence policy, digital industry agglomeration, and industrial land intensive use: evidence from a quasi\-natural experiment in China](../publications/8d7b6ac3df2c62d1c3d2.md)

Ning Wang; Yunpeng Fu; Zhihong Liu

Against the backdrop of the deep integration of the digital economy and artificial intelligence, whether and how AI policies can enhance the intensification of industrial land use is a critical issue concerning the efficiency of land resource allocation and urban sustainable development\. Using the development of China’s National new Generation Artificial Intelligence Innovation and development pilot zones as a quasi\-natural experiment, this study employs an overlapping difference\-in\-differences model based on panel data from 271 prefecture\-level and higher cities in China from 2010 to 2023 to systematically evaluate the impact, transmission mechanisms, and policy synergies of artificial intelligence policies on the intensification of industrial land use\. The study found that: first, AI policies significantly improved the intensification of industrial land use in pilot cities, a conclusion that withstood a series of robustness tests; second, the clustering of digital industries played a significant partial mediating role, revealing the transmission mechanism of “AI policies → digital industry clustering → intensification of industrial land use\.” third, there is a significant positive synergy between AI policies and public data openness policies; the combined implementation of these two policies yields greater promotional effects on both the intensification of industrial land use and the clustering of digital industries than either policy alone, indicating that the combination of digital and AI policies can produce a “1 \+ 1 &gt; 2” amplification effect\. This study provides a theoretical basis and policy guidance for optimizing the allocation of industrial land, promoting the coordination of digital and intelligent policies, and achieving the efficient use of land resources\.

## [Machine Learning\-based Ayurvedic Body Type Prediction with Suggestive System](../publications/8d7e133e053885c0af07.md)

Naganidhi U; Mrs\.Sowmya D; Varsha Dixit K G; Vikas T S; Vivek V\. Shet

Ayurveda, the ancient Indian system of medicine, classifies human beings into three primary body types, or Prakritis: Vata, Pitta, and Kapha\. These body types are determined by the balance of three fundamental biological energies called Doshas\. Understanding an individual&\#x27;s body type is crucial for recommending lifestyle habits, dietary preferences, and preventive healthcare strategies\. Traditional methods for determining Prakriti rely on subjective questionnaires and expert evaluation, which can often be inconsistent and time\-consuming\. This project aims to leverage machine learning techniques to predict an individual&\#x27;s Ayurvedic body type accurately and efficiently\. By analyzing physiological, psychological, and lifestyle data, the system can classify users into one or more dominant Doshas\. Furthermore, the project incorporates a suggestive system that provides personalized recommendations on diet, exercise, and daily routines based on the predicted Prakriti\. The integration of machine learning enhances prediction accuracy, provides a scalable solution, and bridges traditional knowledge with modern technology, making Ayurvedic health insights more accessible to the general population\.

## [Robotics and Artificial Intelligence: Emerging Educational Needs and Essential Skills for Students in the 21st Century](../publications/8d7f62f7255997e7efff.md)

Rohit Gandhe; DR\. SWEETY DODWANI

Robotics and Artificial Intelligence: Emerging Educational Needs and Essential Skills for Students in the 21st CenturyRohit GandheAssistant Professor MIST, Indore M\.PEmail: rohitgandhe@mistindore\.comDr\. Sweety DodwaniAssistant Professor, Idyllic Institute Of ManagementEmail: sweetydodwani\.idyllic@icoeducation\.co\.inAbstractRobotics and Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) are transforming education, employment, communication, healthcare, manufacturing, and other areas of modern society\. As these technologies become increasingly integrated into everyday life, students need more than traditional academic knowledge\. They require digital literacy, computational thinking, problem\-solving, creativity, collaboration, ethical awareness, and the ability to use intelligent technologies responsibly\. This paper examines the educational significance of robotics and AI, identifies the competencies students need to develop, and proposes practical approaches for integrating these technologies into school education\. The study adopts a conceptual research approach based on a review of selected policy documents and educational literature\. It explores opportunities such as personalized learning, project\-based education, interdisciplinary learning, and career preparation, while also examining challenges related to infrastructure, teacher training, privacy, algorithmic bias, academic integrity, and unequal access to technology\. The paper proposes a gradual, inclusive, and human\-centred framework for introducing robotics and AI into educational institutions\. It argues that students should not merely learn how to operate technological tools but should also understand their limitations, evaluate their outputs, and use them to solve meaningful real\-world problems\. The study concludes that robotics and AI education should become an integral component of future\-oriented education, supported by appropriate teacher preparation, curriculum development, ethical guidelines, and equitable access to learning resources\.Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Robotics Education, Digital Literacy, Computational Thinking, STEM Education, Student Competencies, Educational Technology, 21st\-Century Skills

## [PGTNet: a physiology\-guided parallel Graph\-Transformer network for multimodal fatigue recognition of aviation maintenance engineers](../publications/8d929c9e569e18fc9ad2.md)

Guocai Li; Tiantian Yang; Huan Cai; Chengye Dai; Pengyue Huang; Runxia Guo

Fatigue severely degrades operational reliability in high\-risk operational settings such as aviation maintenance\. Although multimodal physiological signals support objective fatigue assessment, many existing models emphasize temporal patterns without explicitly modeling dependencies among physiological features across modalities\. We propose a Physiology\-Guided Parallel Graph–Transformer Network \(PGTNet\) for multimodal fatigue recognition, which incorporates physiologically motivated fatigue\-related features derived from multimodal physiological signals\. Parallel DGCN and Transformer branches jointly model physiological feature relationships and long\-range temporal dependencies, and their representations are integrated through a bidirectional cross\-attention mechanism\. Under the predefined subject\-independent partition, PGTNet achieves an Accuracy of 0\.8778 and a Macro\-AUC of 0\.9648\. Eight\-fold subject\-wise cross\-validation yields an average Accuracy of 0\.8592 ± 0\.0112 across the eight held\-out subjects\. These results support the effectiveness of PGTNet within the present dataset\.

## [Anti\-obesogenic potential of curcumin, disulfiram, and their synergistic effects in HFD\-fed obese Swiss albino mice](../publications/8da1c2aa3565efcfc085.md)

Jitendra Kumar Patel; Raghunath S\. More; Alakh Narayan Singh; Anurag Gupta

Aims This study aimed to investigate the preventive anti\-obesogenic effects of disulfiram and curcumin, including their potential synergistic effects, in a high\-fat diet\-induced obese and diabetic mouse model by evaluating body weight gain, food intake, glycaemic control, lipid profile, insulin and leptin levels, liver injury markers, and histopathological changes\. Diabetes and obesity are dual pandemics affecting millions of people worldwide\. Curcumin, commonly used in Indian kitchens, and the repurposed drug Disulfiram, previously used for other purposes, are evaluated to assess their anti\-obesogenic properties\. Materials and methods Inducing obesity and diabetes through an HFD in Swiss albino mice provides a suitable strategy for testing the preventive effects of supplements or drugs against obesity\. To achieve this, we established five groups: one fed a control diet, one fed an HFD, and three treatment groups that received curcumin, Disulfiram, or both simultaneously by oral gavage\. We measured food intake, weight gain, the Lee obesity index, lipid profiles, liver injury enzymes, insulin and leptin levels, and liver histopathological changes\. Results These results suggest that treating high\-fat diet \(HFD\)\- fed mice with either Curcumin or Disulfiram alone, or combining both simultaneously, for 12 weeks effectively controls weight gain, improves glucose metabolism, reverses abnormal lipid profiles, and reduces Insulin and Leptin resistance\. Conclusion The combination treatment with Curcumin and Disulfiram shows a synergistic effect and a significantly enhanced anti\-obesogenic effect\. However, treatment with Curcumin alone also shows greater effectiveness compared to Disulfiram alone\.

## [Changes in plasma CGRP levels and clinical outcomes following acupuncture in episodic migraine: a prospective pilot study \(the AcuCGRP study\)](../publications/8daeea9e1d6f118734b8.md)

Valentina Favoni; Lorenzo Giusti; Fiorina Bartiromo; Alessandra Poini; Calogero Calabrò; Elena Merli; Barbara Polischi; Flavia Baccari; Corrado Zenesini; Davide Mascarella; Giulia Pierangeli; Carlo Maria Giovanardi; Sabina Cevoli

Background Manual acupuncture is an established non\-pharmacological treatment for migraine, with efficacy comparable to conventional prophylactic therapies\. Calcitonin gene\-related peptide \(CGRP\) plays a central role in migraine pathophysiology and has been proposed as a biomarker for treatment response\. This study aimed to investigate changes in plasma CGRP levels in patients with episodic migraine undergoing a course of manual acupuncture\. Methods Fifty\-two patients with episodic migraine received 10 sessions of standardized manual acupuncture\. Clinical assessments and plasma samples were collected at baseline and one week after treatment completion\. The primary outcome was the change in plasma CGRP levels\. Secondary outcomes included changes in migraine frequency, pain intensity, acute medication intake, and HIT\-6\. Results No statistically significant change in plasma CGRP levels was observed \(baseline: 60\.9 pg/ml; after treatment: 62\.4 pg/ml; p = 0\.841\)\. Significant clinical improvements were observed, in migraine frequency \(median decrease of 1\.5 days/month, p &lt; 0\.001\), pain intensity \(1\-point decrease on a 10\-point scale, p &lt; 0\.001\), acute medication use \(2 units/month, p &lt; 0\.001\), and HIT\-6 score \(−6 points; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions This is the first study to investigate changes in plasma CGRP levels following acupuncture in patients with episodic migraine\. While CGRP levels remained unchanged, patients experienced reductions in headache frequency, intensity, medication use, and disability\. Although these improvements may be attributable, at least in part, to acupuncture, the single\-arm design precludes causal inference\. Peripheral plasma CGRP may not be a straightforward biomarker of clinical changes in this setting\. Controlled studies are warranted\.

## [Simuladores interactivos y resolución de problemas: Mediaciones pedagógicas para el aprendizaje de la física](../publications/8db8cccf62b050cf5d1d.md)

Victor Daniel Trillos Miranda

Problem\-solving is a core competency in the education of students and individuals; at the same time, it is one of the challenges encountered when teaching physics\. This article reflects on the role of interactive simulators as pedagogical tools to strengthen this competency, integrating recent evidence on PhET, guided inquiry, problem\-based learning, digital literacy, artificial intelligence, and virtual laboratories\. A literature review of recent research and academic studies was conducted\. The findings indicate that simulations facilitate the visualization of abstract concepts, the manipulation of variables, and immediate feedback; however, their effectiveness does not depend solely on the technology itself\. Improvement occurs when the use of the simulator, in conjunction with activities proposed by the teacher, guides students to test their own hypotheses, rather than merely observing a result\. Limitations related to teacher training, infrastructure, cognitive load, and the risk of purely demonstrative uses were also identified\. We conclude that the value of simulators lies in their ability to transform problem\-solving into an activity involving modeling, inquiry, and argumentation, provided they are integrated through a deliberate and assessable instructional sequence\.

## [A Comprehensive Review \- Approaches to Advance Drug Discovery for Neglected Tropical Diseases](../publications/8dbdcf3b3fb358a5f232.md)

Asha Nandabaram; Niharika Konka; Rajaputana Lakshmi Manisha; Bhavani Bachu; Sudhakar Muvvala

Background: Neglected tropical diseases \(NTDs\) represent a group of more than 20 infectious conditions that disproportionately affect impoverished populations in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide\. Despite collectively afflicting over 1\.7 billion people globally, NTDs remain severely underfunded and underrepresented in mainstream pharmaceutical research pipelines\. Objective: This review critically examines the multifaceted scientific, technological, and structural approaches that have emerged to accelerate drug discovery and development for NTDs, addressing both scientific and access\-related barriers\. Methods: A comprehensive literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Clinical trials\.gov, covering publications from 2000 to 2024\. Search terms included &quot;neglected tropical diseases,&quot; &quot;drug discovery,&quot; &quot;phenotypic screening,&quot; &quot;computational drug design,&quot; &quot;drug repurposing,&quot; and related terms\. Results and Discussion: Eight major strategic approaches are identified and discussed: \(1\) target\-based drug discovery exploiting validated molecular targets; \(2\) phenotypic and whole\-organism screening; \(3\) drug repurposing and repositioning; \(4\) natural product\-based drug discovery; \(5\) computational approaches including artificial intelligence and machine learning; \(6\) open\-access drug discovery and collaborative models; \(7\) advanced drug delivery systems; and \(8\) public–private partnerships and product development partnerships \(PDPs\)\. Importantly, lessons from biologic drug discovery in autoimmune diseases including precision immunotherapy platforms validated for pemphigus vulgaris, generalized myasthenia gravis, and psoriasis offer translatable frameworks applicable to NTD drug development\. Conclusion: Advancing drug discovery for NTDs requires a paradigm shift integrating innovative science with sustainable funding models, open data sharing, and equitable access policies\. The convergence of computational biology, open\-source drug discovery, and product development partnerships represents the most viable pathway toward safe, effective, and affordable medicines for the world&\#x27;s most vulnerable populations\.

## [Design and Chemical Fabrication of MoxMn1\-xFe2O4/g\-C3N4 Nanocomposite for Photocatalytic Degradation of Direct Green 6 Dye: Environmental Cleaner Approach](../publications/8dbf52fdcf4b7e6731fc.md)

Azqa Amjad; Shumaila Kiran; Muhammad Bilal Qadir; Shazia Abrar; Muhammad Naveed Anjum

MoₓMn₁₋ₓFe₂O₄/g C₃N₄ nanocomposites were successfully synthesized via the hydrothermal method by incorporating mixed spinel ferrite \(MoₓMn₁₋ₓFe₂O₄\) nanoparticles onto graphitic carbon nitride \(g C₃N₄\) sheets to enhance visible light\-driven photocatalytic performance\. XRD, SEM, TEM, FT\-IR, and UV\-Vis were used to characterize the synthesized nanocomposites, and the successful formation of the heterostructure with an enhanced surface area and modified bandgap was observed\. The MoₓMn₁₋ₓFe₂O₄/g C₃N₄ catalysts effectively showed improved photocatalytic degradation of Direct Green 6 \(DG 6\) dye under visible light irradiation, which is superior to g C₃N₄ and ferrite\. The performance of the composite is enhanced due to the synergistic effect between MoₓMn₁₋ₓFe₂O₄ and g\-C₃N₄ parts, where efficient separation of electron hole pairs and long light absorption take place\. The degradation reaction of DG 6 was found to be of pseudo\-first order, and the radical trapping experiments suggested that the major reactive oxygen species in the photocatalytic reaction were the superoxide radicals \(•O₂⁻\)\. The results show the potential of MoₓMn₁₋ₓFe₂O₄/g\-C₃N₄ nanocomposites as an efficient visible light photocatalyst working for wastewater treatment applications\.

## [Interaction Patterns and Embodied Design Processes Using an AI Robotics Kit for K–12 Education](../publications/8dc0a04d0aff1cee1f09.md)

Anssi Lin; Henriikka Vartiainen; Anssi Salonen; Matti Tedre

This multidisciplinary study explores how children interact with a low\-cost robotics educational tool designed to teach machine learning \(ML\) concepts through hands\-on making\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and ML are increasingly integrated into K\-12 education, yet tangible approaches are not extensively studied\. We conducted three researcher\-led interventions with children aged 10, 11 and 13, each tasked to build an AI\-enhanced robot using the robotics kit\. Interventions were analyzed both qualitatively and with process mining methods to gain an in\-depth view of the interactions\. Findings indicate that designing and building were very central throughout the interventions, with the affordances guiding the design process forward\. Children exhibited emerging data\-driven thinking and ownership of their design process, while still requiring tailored scaffolding throughout the design process\. We identify a general structure of the design process from all the interventions and emphasize the importance of building and designing activities\. This study provides a new methodological lens to analyzing the interactions between children and embodied AI\-educational tools while also contributing to the current body of knowledge on designing and effectively leveraging embodied learning tools\.

## [An explicit Eulerian vortex solution of the compressible Euler equations at large Mach numbers resolves the classical problem of turbulence](../publications/8dc345c476b27d226c18.md)

S\. G\. Chefranov; Artem  S\. Chefranov

A statistically closed analytical theory of compressible vortex turbulence is developed based on an explicit Eulerian classical vortex solution of the three\-dimensional \(3D\) inviscid Burgers equations or, equivalently in the large\-Mach\-number limit, of the compressible 3D Euler equations\. The finite\-time blow\-up of the solution is avoided, and the solution becomes globally smooth without introducing any additional hyperviscous dissipation at small scales, either through supercritical homogeneous linear friction or after stochastic averaging over a homogeneous Wiener process representing an arbitrarily small effective viscosity\. Thus, in contrast to the known counterexample to the Clay Millennium Prize Problem in the incompressible case, the fundamental question of whether ordinary viscous dissipation can suppress the singularity arising from non\-linear vortex stretching for any smooth initial data is positively resolved within the present compressible model\. A rigorous assessment of the range of validity of the Millionshchikov hypothesis and of Onsager&\#x27;s dissipative anomaly, or Kolmogorov&\#x27;s zeroth hypothesis, is also obtained in arbitrary spatial dimensions\. In particular, the strong dissipative anomaly is found to be valid only in six dimensions, whereas in the three\-dimensional case only the weak dissipative anomaly is possible\. ## [The influence of mutant genes APP and PSEN1 on hippocampal asymmetry in 5xFAD mice, transgenic model of Alzheimer disease](../publications/8dc36a637f9680559ba2.md)

Eugeny Yu\. Brusentsev; И\. Н\. Рожкова; V\. S\. Kozeneva; I D Chekashov; T\. A\. Rakhmanova; Oleg B\. Shevelev; Sergei Ya Amstislavsky

Alzheimer’s disease \(AD\) is an age\-related neurodegenerative pathology and one of the primary causes of dementia associated with memory and cognitive impairment\. The dentate gyrus \(DG\) of the hippocampus plays a crucial role in learning and memory encoding, and it undergoes significant changes in AD\. To study the underlying mechanisms of AD and to test new therapeutic agents, mouse models of this pathology are developed\. One of the most popular and relevant models for AD research is the 5xFAD transgenic mouse strain carrying mutant human genes, specifically: amyloid beta precursor protein \( APP \) and presenilin\-1 \( PSEN1 \)\. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of mutant APP and PSEN1 transgenes on the microstructure of the hippocampal DG in six\-month\-old heterozygous male 5xFAD transgenic mice using diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging \(DTI\-MRI\) combined with immunohistochemical analysis\. A special emphasis was placed on assessing hippocampal asymmetry, which had not been previously investigated in 5xFAD mice\. In the hippocampal DG of both hemispheres in male 5xFAD mice, an elevated level of betaamyloid was detected compared to the wild\-type control group, combined with a higher density of microglia, but no differences were found in the level of neurogenesis\. Along with this, hippocampal asymmetry was discovered in male 5xFAD mice, manifesting as an increased volume of the right hippocampus, a decreased level of fractional anisotropy in the right hippocampal DG, and a reduced neuron density in the left DG compared to the wild\-type\. Based on our results, it can be concluded that mutant human APP and PSEN1 genes cause alterations in the hippocampal DG, which may open new possibilities for the early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease\. The identified changes in hippocampal volume and its asymmetry could become important biomarkers characterizing this pathology\.

## [POLYMERIC NANOSPHERES FOR ORAL DRUG DELIVERY: EMERGING FORMULATION TECHNOLOGIES, TRANSLATIONAL CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE CLINICAL PERSPECTIVES](../publications/8dc73c52d78bb685b5f0.md)



Oral drug delivery remains the most widely preferred route of drug administration owing to its convenience, patient compliance, cost\-effectiveness, and suitability for long\-term therapy\.However, the oral delivery of many therapeutic agents is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility, low intestinal permeability, gastrointestinal degradation, extensive first\-pass metabolism, and efflux transporter activity, resulting in inadequate bioavailability and inconsistent therapeutic outcomes\.Polymeric nanospheres have emerged as a promising nanotechnology\-based platform capable of overcoming these physiological and biopharmaceutical barriers through enhanced drug protection, controlled release, improved mucosal interaction, and targeted intestinal absorption\.The selection of appropriate biodegradable polymers, together with advances in formulation technologies such as nanoprecipitation, solvent evaporation, microfluidics, and continuous manufacturing, has considerably improved the physicochemical properties and therapeutic performance of oral nanosphere formulations\.Furthermore, recent developments in surface engineering, stimuli\-responsive polymers, artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted formulation design, machine learning \(ML\), and Quality by Design \(QbD\) have accelerated the optimization and translation of polymeric nanospheres from laboratory research toward industrial manufacturing\.This review comprehensively summarizes the fundamental principles, classification, formulation strategies, characterization techniques, drug release mechanisms, surface functionalization approaches, and smart polymeric nanosphere systems developed for oral drug delivery\.In addition, recent therapeutic applications in cancer, diabetes, infectious diseases, inflammatory disorders, neurological diseases, and biological therapeutics are critically discussed\.The review also highlights current translational challenges, regulatory considerations, clinical perspectives, and future research directions with particular emphasis on intelligent nanomedicine, precision drug delivery, and sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing\.Overall, polymeric nanospheres represent a versatile and rapidly evolving oral drug delivery platform with significant potential to improve drug bioavailability, therapeutic efficacy, and patient outcomes while facilitating the development of next\-generation oral nanomedicines\.

## [When inequality looms large: the cumulative impacts of discrimination on sexual minorities’ late life experiences](../publications/8dc88455d0b414347dff.md)

Lisa R\. Miller

Introduction Research suggests that older sexual minorities face distinctive challenges in late adulthood compared to their heterosexual counterparts\. However, attention to the role that lifelong discrimination plays in the aging experiences of older sexual minorities has been insufficient\. Methods Utilizing life story interview data with older \(55\+\) sexual minorities, I examine how lifelong exposure to structural inequality contributes to aging\-related challenges and the development of unique assets in late adulthood\. Results The results suggest that older sexual minorities face three distinct challenges in late adulthood: economic marginalization, medical distrust and subsequent rejection of medical care in long\-term care facilities, and suicidal thoughts and intent\. In addition, participants possessed unique assets for confronting aging\-related challenges, namely community\-centered care approaches\. Discussion Taken together, the results suggest that much greater attention should be paid to cumulative inequality processes in the lives of older sexual minorities, including how this population can avoid the accumulation of disadvantage over time\.

## [Advancing Machine Learning for Resource\-Constrained Environments](../publications/8dd2a09f523c0468006b.md)

Kunjal Panchal

This dissertation addresses the fundamental challenge of enabling machine learning intelligence on resource\-constrained systems\. These systems include embedded edge devices, mobile platforms, and robots operating under both on\-device and cloud\-based paradigms\. The resource\-constrained systems must perform low\-latency, memory\-efficient, and privacy preserving intelligence close to users and their data\. Such systems are essential for personalized on\-device learning, autonomous task execution in everyday environments, and user\-adaptive multimodal assistants\. However, ML on resource\-constrained devices face three characteristic challenges that distinguish it from traditional ML settings: \(1\) heterogeneous data that varies across devices, users, and time; \(2\) strict hardware budget with limited compute and memory; and \(3\) stringent runtime efficiency requirements under dynamic environments\. Efficient ML system design must tailor to these characteristics\. The dissertation first introduces a work which addresses heterogeneity across edge devices, where each device&\#x27;s local data distribution differs from others\. It demonstrates that dynamically adapting model parameters per device and per data instance improves prediction accuracy across all clients\. The second work addresses temporal heterogeneity, where each device’s local data distribution can change over time \(concept drift\)\. It introduces drift\-aware optimization, which effectively maintains model performance as data evolves under a dynamic environment\. Next, the dissertation tackles the challenge of strict memory constraints on resource\-constrained devices using forward\-mode automatic differentiation \(FmAD\) to train large language models\. This method enables low memory consumption during training while achieving accuracy comparable to backpropagation\-based methods\. Building on insights from FmAD, the dissertation further examines the trade\-offs of FmAD and other memory\-efficient gradient estimation methods as alternatives to backpropagation\. It uncovers constraints on the computation, runtime, and convergence of the gradient estimation methods that inform the design of future algorithms\. Finally, it targets the challenge of runtime\-efficiency under dynamic environments for multi\-agent planning tasks, where several physical or simulated robots must coordinate to complete shared objectives\. The dissertation introduces a runtime\-efficient planning framework that combines symbolic constraints with LLM\-based reasoning\. This approach reduces plan failures and execution time, while improving task success in dynamic environments\.

## [Explainable Machine Learning for Punching Shear and Post\-Failure Integrity](../publications/8dd8b88ae5785fde8523.md)

Ahmed N\. Elbelacy; Hassan Ibrahim; Mina A\. Mikaeel; Andrew G\. Gouda

Punching shear is a brittle failure mode in reinforced\-concrete slab–column connections, requiring predictive models with explicit validity limits\. This study develops a mechanics\-informed machine\-learning workflow using 1068 quality\-controlled specimens from 111 literature sources\. XGBoost achieved R2 = 0\.932 under a specimen\-random five\-fold benchmark, while leakage\-safe nested source\-grouped validation yielded R2 = 0\.858 and a fully source\-disjoint holdout yielded R2 = 0\.793\. Performance was substantially weaker for scarce edge and corner connections than for interior connections, demonstrating configuration\-dependent transfer limitations\. Predictive\-importance analyses identified geometry and loading as the dominant variable blocks; these associations were not causal\. Conformal prediction provided marginal predictive\-uncertainty diagnostics, including 97\.90% coverage with a 507\.14 kN mean interval width on the source\-disjoint test, but does not establish configuration\-conditional coverage or structural reliability\. Bounded perturbations were likewise interpreted as sensitivity analysis rather than reliability assessment\. A separate nine\-specimen geogrid program provided complementary post\-failure evidence; quantitative post\-peak conclusions were restricted to the three specimens with complete records\. The workflow supports validation\-aware research screening within the represented domain while emphasizing source separation and configuration\-specific applicability\.

## [A Framework for Identifying and Addressing Bottlenecks in Government Administrative Approval Processes](../publications/8ddf9a0546d9acc5bd46.md)

Yaddehi Arachchilage Oshani Ayeshika Kalapriya

Many government offices in Sri Lanka now handle files through digital workflow systems, yet the record of how files move is rarely used to study delay\. This paper presents a simple and reusable framework for identifying and addressing bottlenecks in government administrative approval processes\. The framework was developed and tested on one six\-stage file approval process carried out in five government offices\. Because system event logs were not available, a structured questionnaire was used: Subject Officers copied the stage\-by\-stage dates from files they had personally closed, giving 150 file records \(30 per office\)\.

## [Automated speech analysis for psychosis detection: a systematic comparison of task efficiency and feature groups](../publications/8de436bf06f92fb6cda1.md)

Norio Zimmermann; Jonathan Heitz; Anna Steiner; Noemi Dannecker; Roya Melanie Hüppi; Giacomo Cecere; Wolfgang Omlor; Werner Surbeck; Philipp Homan; Nicolas Langer

Abstract This study investigates the effectiveness of automatic speech analysis in differentiating between patients with psychotic disorders and healthy control individuals with low or high levels of schizotypy within a German\-speaking cohort\. A range of acoustic and linguistic features was extracted from audio recordings and transcriptions obtained through structured interviews, open discourse, and picture description tasks, in which each participant described at least six pictures\. These features served as input to train Random Forest classifiers, with linguistic features achieving consistent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of around 0\.8–0\.9 across all interview formats\. In contrast, acoustic features performed significantly worse, particularly in the picture description task\. Using linguistic features, we showed that increasing the number of described pictures significantly improved model accuracy, with performance plateauing after the combination of three pictures\. Subsequent feature importance analysis revealed that patients produced simpler language, shorter sentences, less speech overall, and exhibited lower semantic coherence compared to healthy controls\. These findings highlight the potential of automatic linguistic analysis as a scalable and objective tool for the detection of psychotic disorders in German\-speaking populations\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NO PODER JUDICIÁRIO: RISCOS, TIPOLOGIA E IMPACTOS SOBRE O ACESSO À JUSTIÇA](../publications/8de53ab675263830ff99.md)

Igor Makio Brasil Kanehira; Luiz Guilherme Eliano Pinto; Allan Teixeira Nogueira

A inteligência artificial generativa \(IA Gen\) vem sendo incorporada ao Poder Judiciário no contexto da transformação digital do Estado, destacando\-se por sua capacidade de gerar conteúdos novos a partir de padrões probabilísticos, o que amplia suas aplicações, mas também introduz desafios de previsibilidade, explicabilidade e controle\. O estudo analisa criticamente sua utilização no Judiciário, com foco na identificação e categorização dos riscos operacionais, interacionais e sistêmicos, bem como sua relação com o acesso à justiça\. Metodologicamente, adota\-se abordagem qualitativa, descritivo\-analítica, baseada em revisão bibliográfica e documentos normativos, com método dedutivo voltado à construção de uma tipologia aplicável ao contexto judicial brasileiro\. Conclui\-se que a IA Gen não deve ser avaliada apenas sob a ótica da eficiência, mas à luz de seus impactos sobre garantias processuais e direitos fundamentais, especialmente o acesso à justiça, exigindo governança e limites institucionais adequados\.

## [A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI](../publications/8de769ccb9e639b6ec16.md)

Vivek Sharma

The complexity of today&\#x27;s transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging\. Intelligent Transportation Systems \(ITS\) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision\-making\. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges\. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management\. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver\-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions\. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability\. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems\. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road\-safety management from reactive measures to data\-driven approaches\.

## [POR QUE ACREDITAR NA RESPOSTA? : CONFIANÇA E AUTORIDADE EPISTÊMICA NO ENSINO JURÍDICO DIANTE DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA](../publications/8ded8304bc4fbe062343.md)

Leonardo Peteno Magnusson; Olívia Inocêncio; Caio Cezar Pontim Scholz

O artigo examina as condições sob as quais um estudante de Direito deve conceder crédito a respostas produzidas por sistemas de inteligência artificial generativa, a partir do problema mais geral da confiança epistêmica na formação jurídica\. Parte\-se da constatação de que a autonomia intelectual não pressupõe autossuficiência, pois o conhecimento jurídico depende estruturalmente de fontes, autoridades e testemunhos que o próprio sujeito não pode integralmente verificar\. O artigo delimita deliberadamente seu referencial teórico em torno de duas linhas, a epistemologia do testemunho e da autoridade epistêmica, e a literatura sobre confiança calibrada em sistemas automatizados e sobre confiança apropriada, evitando cobertura panorâmica em favor de aprofundamento vertical\. Sustenta\-se que a inteligência artificial generativa desloca a confiança epistêmica ao converter propriedades da apresentação discursiva, como fluência e segurança linguística, em substitutos práticos dos critérios pelos quais a autoridade deveria ser reconhecida\. O objetivo consiste em identificar esse deslocamento e propor critérios para uma confiança epistemicamente calibrada no uso educacional da inteligência artificial\. Adota\-se abordagem qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica, com finalidade exploratória e analítica e raciocínio predominantemente dedutivo\. Os resultados indicam que a plausibilidade discursiva de uma resposta generativa não constitui, por si mesma, razão suficiente para lhe atribuir autoridade epistêmica\. Conclui\-se que a formação jurídica deve desenvolver, além da capacidade de avaliar informações, a capacidade de calibrar a confiança segundo quatro dimensões articuladas: a diferenciação da tarefa e da proposição, a rastreabilidade das razões e da autoridade, a proporcionalidade da verificação e a revisabilidade da confiança concedida\.

## [Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute](../publications/8e04d80d8a6036062ccb.md)

Sima Zahedi Fard; Paolo Tiso; Parisa Omidvar; Marc Serra‐Garcia

Designing metamaterials that compute is challenging; the space of possible geometries is very large, and the relation between structure and function is complex\. Perturbative metamaterials, consisting of weakly interacting unit cells, can be efficiently designed by combining simple geometric building blocks\. However, perturbative metamaterials are conventionally defined in terms of linear wave physics, which prevents their use in information\-processing applications that require nonlinearity\. Here, we introduce a nonlinear formulation for perturbative metamaterials that allows us to identify material geometries that perform target computations\. The design is enabled by a nonlinear, localized map connecting metamaterial deformations to a discrete tight\-binding model that encodes the computation\. We demonstrate the generality of this approach by designing three information\-processing metamaterials based on three different computing paradigms: an Ising machine that solves combinatorial optimization problems through energy minimization, a mechanical racetrack device for in\-memory computing, and a speech classification metamaterial based on analog neuromorphic computing\. Elastic metamaterials provide opportunities for implementing computation tasks, yet generality provides a major challenge with respect to the design of metamaterial geometry\. Here, the authors introduce a two\-step metamaterial design strategy embedding first the computation functionality in a tight\-binding model and subsequently tailoring a metamaterial geometry\.

## [Printcrete: Upgrading shotcrete](../publications/8e0cdca1e7a144ded43e.md)

Yong Yuan; Jiao\-Long Zhang; Yaxin Tao

Abstract Printable concrete \(hereafter printcrete\) is a promising additive construction technology and a novel alternative to conventional shotcrete for tunnel engineering, offering advantages such as eliminating rebound and enhancing flexibility\. Despite its potential, challenges remain in upscaling, performance, and applicable equipment\. This paper consolidates the prior research on printcrete carried out by the authors, while also offering insights into the advancement of printcrete technology from both sustainable and intelligent perspectives\. It begins by addressing the mixture design at both the concrete and paste levels to reduce the carbon footprint of printcrete\. The advantages of incorporating coarse aggregates in reducing binder content, along with the associated challenges in processing, are discussed\. Additionally, various reaction mechanisms based on low\-carbon, fast\-setting binders, such as aluminate\-based cement and other supplementary cementitious materials, have been studied for printcrete, enabling the decoupling of productive strength from service strength to improve its sustainability\. Based on these reaction mechanisms, a twin\-pipe pumping technology has been developed to balance the conflicting requirements of pumpability and buildability\. This highlights the need for novel indices and standardized testing methods to characterize the early\-age hydration and rheological evolution, addressing the accurate time\-dependent demands of printcrete\. Lastly, a detailed discussion on smart construction is presented, emphasizing its importance in extreme environments, where automated equipment integrated with artificial intelligence is essential for real\-time monitoring and adaptive decision\-making\.

## [A synthetic\-data and machine\-learning digital shadow foundation for end\-of\-life magnet recycling](../publications/8e11a97540f6965494b0.md)

Nikolaos Sifakis; Alexandros Chachalis; George Tsinarakis; Maria Aryblia; Dimitrios Cholidis; George Arampatzis

ABSTRACT Digital twins need data that are physically consistent, temporally realistic and honest about uncertainty\. For end\-of\-life permanent\-magnet recycling, central to rare\-earth supply security yet poorly characterised, they are absent\. Generated data can substitute, but resemblance, utility and privacy criteria are defined against the missing data themselves, so a synthetic foundation cannot be certified\. This study builds one for an eleven\-process neodymium\-iron\-boron and ferrite recycling chain\. The generator combines autoregressive noise, dual seasonality, a wear trend, noisy conversion ratios and two\-pass mass\-balance conservation over 500 replicates\. Seven structural fits recover the configured ratios to within 0\.11% \(R² 0\.979\-0\.999\), and 85\.4% of an 82\-model screen satisfy five diagnostic criteria \(best\-per\-process R² 0\.24\-0\.98\)\. Four machine\-learning families all degrade mean R² \(0\.000\-0\.041\), as a linear generating process predicts; this linearity\-recovery test is proposed as a within\-synthetic criterion of internal consistency, not of external validity\. Chain demand is 442\.1 kWh per hour and energy intensity 9\.58 kWh per kilogram of magnet product against 1\.19 for ferrite; no saving against primary neodymium is claimed, the pellet&\#x27;s composition being unresolved\. Relative dispersion rises from 3\.46% to a 4\.62\-4\.69% plateau, so conservation bounds variance propagation\. Its cost follows in closed form: renormalisation attenuates each stage&\#x27;s injected dispersion by a factor set by its conversion ratios, producing the near\-unit coefficients of determination and erasing the specified seasonal and wear\-trend structure\. With near\-uniform dispersion, a binary\-knapsack reallocation of the control budget funds high\-throughput upstream stages, not the energy\-dominant Furnace: the uncertainty and energy layers order the chain oppositely\.

## [Mechanical Performance and Compost‐Soil Degradation of Uncompatibilized PLA / PBAT / PCL Blends](../publications/8e185a3e74e052be1e8d.md)

Najwa Ibrahim; M\. Mariatti; Azzah Dyah Pramata; Hiroshi Uyama

ABSTRACT The persistence and fragmentation of conventional petroleum‐based plastics used in agricultural and soil‐contact products have increased the need for biodegradable alternatives that can provide adequate mechanical performance during service while reducing long‐term persistence after disposal\. This study investigated uncompatibilized poly\(lactic acid\) \(PLA\)/poly\(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate\) \(PBAT\)/poly\(ε‐caprolactone\) \(PCL\) binary and ternary blends to evaluate the balance between initial mechanical performance and subsequent degradation under compost‐soil conditions\. The PLA content was fixed at 60 wt%, while the relative proportions of PBAT and PCL were varied to determine the influence of blend composition on mechanical, thermal, and degradation behavior\. Among the investigated formulations, the ternary blend containing 60 wt% PLA, 20 wt% PBAT, and 20 wt% PCL \(P6B2C2\) exhibited the most balanced initial mechanical performance\. P6B2C2 achieved approximately 73% of the tensile strength and 95% of the tensile modulus of neat PLA without the use of a compatibilizer\. DSC analysis revealed distinct component‐specific thermal transitions, confirming the immiscible nature of the blends\. The PLA melting temperature remained relatively stable at approximately 148°C–155°C, while PCL retained its characteristic melting peak near 56°C\. During 60 days of compost‐soil burial, distinct composition‐dependent degradation responses were observed\. The binary PLA/PCL blend \(P6C4\) exhibited approximately 46% weight loss, accompanied by extensive surface deterioration, cavity formation, and substantial loss of mechanical integrity\. In comparison, P6B2C2 exhibited approximately 22% weight loss and retained greater structural integrity throughout the exposure period\. SEM observations revealed progressive interfacial deterioration and matrix fragmentation, while FTIR spectra retained the characteristic ester bands without showing substantial formation of new functional groups\. The combined weight‐loss, mechanical retention, and physicochemical analyses demonstrate that the degradation response of PLA‐based biodegradable blends can be tailored through blend composition\. These findings highlight the potential of ternary PLA/PBAT/PCL blending to balance mechanical performance with soil degradation, providing a material level basis for developing biodegradable alternatives for short life agricultural and soil contact applications\.

## [Machine\-Learning Classification of Topological Materials Using Crystallographic and Compositional Descriptors for Pre\-DFT Screening](../publications/8e1dcde06bc1ab7dd4d5.md)

Sammy S\. Dan; Joseph Bassey Emah; Sylvester Andrew Ekong

Identifying topological insulators and semimetals among inorganic crystalline materials traditionally requires density functional theory \(DFT\) calculations with spin–orbit coupling, a computationally expensive process that limits high\-throughput screening\. This study examined whether machine learning models trained on ground\-state crystallographic and compositional descriptors, obtainable without DFT or space\-group information, could reliably classify materials as topologically non\-trivial, trivial, or semimetallic\. A dataset of 1,391 labelled crystalline entries \(230 semimetal, 781 topological, 380 trivial\), curated from the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database and the Topological Quantum Chemistry database, was cleaned, including manual correction, via direct ICSD lookup, of a systematic lattice\-parameter data\-entry artefact \(an Excel auto\-fill error that had propagated a single genuine c\-parameter value across 1,208 rows, identified by cross\-validation against unit\-cell volume\), prior to a further, now pipeline\-integrated audit that removed 47 true\-duplicate ICSD entries and attempted live TQC API resolution of 10 conflicting\-label ICSD groups, none of which returned a match, so the first\-encountered row was conservatively retained in each case \(net reduction from 1,450 to 1,391 entries\), and used to engineer 31 structural and compositional features motivated by the physics of spin\-orbit\-coupling\-driven band inversion\. Six classifiers, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Support Vector Machine, an Artificial Neural Network, and a soft\-voting Ensemble, were trained and optimised using nested stratified cross\-validation, Bayesian hyperparameter search, and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique \(SMOTE\)\-based class rebalancing applied strictly within each training fold\. XGBoost produced the highest observed test\-set performance \(macro\-F1 of 0\.744, accuracy of 78\.1%, macro\-AUC\-ROC of 0\.896\), narrowly ahead of LightGBM \(macro\-F1 0\.721, accuracy 74\.9%, macro\-AUC\-ROC 0\.887\), though the difference was not statistically significant \(McNemar&\#x27;s test, p = 1\.000, Bonferroni\-corrected\); LightGBM was retained as the primary model for interpretability and screening on the basis of its lower cross\-validation variance and better\-behaved post\-hoc probability calibration\. Shapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\), permutation, and impurity\-based feature importance analyses converged on a consistent predictor hierarchy: number of constituent elements, mean ionisation potential, electronegativity range, maximum atomic number, and mean atomic radius, corroborated by polymorph\-level diagnostics providing evidence that the model exploits structural, not merely compositional, information in most cases, although structural signal proved insufficient in at least one hard case\. Applied to the full dataset, LightGBM ranked 424 entries as Tier 1 \(P\(Topological\) ≥ 0\.80\) high\-confidence topological predictions within the labelled dataset, of which 419 corresponded to already\-known topological labels — a precision of 98\.8% against known labels \(retrospective validation precision, not prospective discovery precision\)\. Interpretability analysis was also used as a data\-quality diagnostic, motivating a closer investigation that, together with cross\-validation against unit\-cell volume and a subsequent ICSD/TQC provenance audit, uncovering and correcting a latent artefact in an earlier version of the model&\#x27;s most important feature\. These findings demonstrate that pre\-DFT structural and compositional descriptors carry physically plausible and interpretable predictive signal for topological classification, offering an inexpensive pre\-screening tool to prioritise candidate materials for further investigation\.

## [Data\-Driven Supply Chain Practice and Sustainable RMG Performance: The Mediating Roles of Organizational Agility and Eco\-Efficiency Moderated by Green Absorptive Capacity](../publications/8e20901e056709309f3e.md)

S\.K\. Md\. Anik Hassan Rabby; Nashita Mumtahina; Sharjil Khan

Abstract Amidst rapid global scaling of Bangladesh&\#x27;s RMG industry, achieving sustainability via effective digital transformation unlocks immense potential for accelerating SDG goal attainment progress to ensure long\-term competitiveness\. Grounded in the Dynamic Capabilities View and Absorptive Capacity Theory, this research examines the mechanisms where data\-driven supply chain practices \(DDSCP\) influence sustainable RMG performance \(SRP\) through the mediating role of organizational agility and eco\-efficiency\. Employing a quantitative, cross\-sectional design, data from 215 supply chain and operational managers in Bangladesh were analyzed using PLS\-SEM\. The findings challenge deterministic technological narratives where DDSCP directly affects SRP and is notably minimal\. Instead, the true value of digitalization is realized through the significant mediating roles of organizational agility and eco\-efficiency\. Importantly, while Green Absorptive Capacity directly enhances sustainable performance, it does not moderate the DDSCP\-SRP relationship, acting as an independent operational baseline rather than a digital synergist in this developing context\. This research advances supply chain literature by demonstrating that digital tools alone are insufficient, they require agile organizational reconfiguration and rigorous eco\-efficient routines to achieve sustainable excellence\. These insights provide actionable strategies for manufacturers and policymakers navigating stringent global compliance paradigms\.

## [Close Enough is Nowhere Near: Fidelity\-Consumability Decoupling in KV Caches](../publications/8e253122ce5441db36f5.md)

Adam Deng; Shicheng Liu; Yada Zhu

Multi\-agent LLM systems communicate in text, which is lossy and wasteful: the sender throws away the reading it already did\. A growing literature instead transmits the KV cache, the natural carrier of that reading\. We study the most appealing form of the idea: both models stay frozen and the sender&\#x27;s cache is substituted for the reader&\#x27;s with nothing trained\. It does not work, and the obstruction belongs to the reader\. A frozen transformer reads only caches close to the one it would have written itself, a region we call its tolerable set\. We show that geometric similarity to that cache does not predict whether the reader can use it, and the failure is not gradual, so a more faithful substitute is not the remedy it appears to be\. We explain this phenomenon with competitive attention\. Experimentally, we test eight diverse substitution methods against two measured anchors: an uninformative cache baseline and the reader&\#x27;s own accuracy from having read the passage\. All sit at the baseline\. That turns a long tail of separate negative results into one outcome with a stated condition for overturning it\. A different design does work: if the reader keeps its own cache and attends over the sender&\#x27;s as extra context, adapting only its queries, it beats its own baseline, and also clears the baseline with eight senders pooled where undirected attention over the same union falls below it\. We offer this as a characterization on one probe, not a leaderboard claim\. Our central contribution is a redirection: pursuing faithful substitute caches is the wrong target; adding a cache to what the reader already has is the promising one\.

## [Digital Footprint Detection: A Client\-Side Browser Security Framework for Real\-Time Tracker Auditing, Device Fingerprint Mitigation, and Dynamic Privacy Risk Assessment](../publications/8e29a2195f2484eee975.md)

Syed Bahauddin; V\. Aruna

Modern web applications subject end\-users to pervasive tracking mechanisms, including third\-party stateful cookies, persistent local storage beacons, cache\-based ETag tracking, cross\-site script injections, and stateless hardware fingerprinting\. While conventional privacy extensions rely predominantly on static blocklists, they often fail to quantify real\-time data exposure, lack transparent risk metrics, and offer minimal visibility into sophisticated device fingerprinting and DNS leakage\. This paper presents the design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of Digital Footprint Detection, an advanced client\-side browser security extension engineered on Google Chrome’s Manifest V3 service\-worker architecture\. The framework introduces a multitier detection engine combining DOM\-level Canvas and WebGL API interception, dual\-layer DNS leakage detection via DoH resolvers \(Cloudflare and Google/Akamai\), behavioral biometric telemetry, and automated token cryptanalysis \(including JWT decoding\)\. Furthermore, the extension formulates a dynamic multi\-factor risk assessment model that computes a composite 10\- point privacy score across seven weighted attributes per cookie and tracking vector\. To actively safeguard user privacy, an automated countermeasure subsystem enforces real\-time header stripping, ad\-domain network blocking, automated high\-risk cookie remediation, and synthetic canvas noise injection\. Experimental validation across high\-traffic commercial and media domains demonstrates that the proposed framework reliably intercepts 100% of tested canvas fingerprint attempts, successfully neutralizes cross\-site tracking vectors, and delivers low\-overhead, real\-time privacy auditing without degrading page render performance\.

## [The Academic Operating System](../publications/8e323164943c6fee8fe2.md)

Susan L\. Stansberry

The Academic Operating System: Successfully Navigating Doctoral Education&\#x27;s Hidden Curriculum is an interactive open educational resource designed to support current and prospective doctoral students by making the implicit expectations of graduate education explicit\. Recognizing that success in doctoral programs depends on more than coursework and research, the resource illuminates the often\-unspoken norms, practices, and expectations that shape the doctoral experience while providing practical guidance for navigating common challenges along the way\.Developed with students in PhD and EdD programs in education and human sciences in mind, the resource draws on experiences from learning, design, and technology programs while offering strategies and insights applicable across a wide range of academic disciplines\. Interactive activities, reflective prompts, and practical resources encourage readers to develop the skills, habits, and confidence needed to thrive throughout their doctoral journey\.

## [Multiobjective Optimization of Heat‐Treatment Pathways for SK85 Steel: Integrating NGBoost and NSGA‐II for Tailored Properties](../publications/8e346b8cd3e9f2173737.md)

Attasit Wiangkham; Atthaphon Ariyarit; Prasert Aengchuan; Nipon Taweejun; Tanabodee Praditja; Patiphan Juijerm; Wanna Homjabok; Apilak Koptonglang; Narongsak Thammachot

Optimizing the mechanical properties of high‐carbon steels requires precise control over complex phase transformations driven by heat‐treatment pathways\. This study develops a novel data‐driven framework integrating natural gradient boosting \(NGBoost\) for probabilistic surrogate modeling and the non‐dominated sorting genetic algorithm II \(NSGA‐II\) for multiobjective optimization to design quenching–tempering \(Q‐T\) and austempering–tempering \(A‐T\) sequences for JIS SK85 high‐carbon steel\. A systematic experimental dataset linking process parameters to microstructural and mechanical responses was constructed\. The NGBoost model accurately predicted tensile properties and hardness while quantifying predictive uncertainty, outperforming conventional regression methods\. Global sensitivity analysis via Sobol indices identified austempering and tempering temperatures as dominant factors governing mechanical performance\. Multiobjective optimization using NSGA‐II revealed that the A‐T route at 320 °C delivers the optimal strength‐ductility balance, attributed to the formation of lower bainite with finely dispersed carbides\. K‐means clustering and TOPSIS were employed to select practical Pareto‐optimal solutions\. Experimental validation confirmed the model&\#x27;s high accuracy, with errors below 5%\. This work demonstrates an effective AI‐aided methodology that reduces trial‐and‐error in designing high‐performance heat treatments for advanced high‐carbon steel components\.
