## [From AI\-enabled materials informatics to sustainable innovation in Asian global value chains: the bridging role of inter\-organisational collaboration](../publications/8e515434f3046dd8cc3a.md)

An\-Chin Cheng

The twin transition of digitalisation and sustainability requires manufacturers in Asian global value chains \(GVCs\) to convert internal artificial intelligence \(AI\) capability into outcomes that depend on cross\-boundary coordination\. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities View and GVC governance research, this study examines how AI\-enabled materials informatics \(MI\) capability relates to sustainable innovation performance \(SIP\) through inter\-organisational collaboration\. Survey data from 205 senior technology executives in Taiwan&\#x27;s high\-technology manufacturing sector were analysed using a complementary quantitative dual\-analytic strategy combining PLS\-SEM and fsQCA\. PLS\-SEM shows positive associations between AI\-enabled MI capability and collaboration capability \(β = 0\.612, p &lt; \.001\), collaboration capability and SIP \(β = 0\.485, p &lt; \.001\) and AI\-enabled MI capability and SIP \(β = 0\.215, p = \.002\)\. The specific indirect association is significant \(β = 0\.297, p &lt; \.001\), and sensitivity analysis excluding SIP\_2 yields materially unchanged results\. fsQCA identifies three sufficient configurations for high SIP, including an Eco\-Collaborative pathway combining weak internal AI capability with strong data\-governance and regulatory\-sensing practices\. The findings highlight complementary net\-association and configurational perspectives on sustainable innovation\.

## [Exploring sense of belonging in medical students: A scoping review](../publications/8e51aed142e71d8875e6.md)

Stephanie Bull; Lynelle Govender; Agalya Ramanathan; Laura Knight; Katie Scott; Sukhi Ubhi; Jo Horsburgh

BACKGROUND: Sense of belonging is increasingly discussed in health professions education and predominantly recognised as a necessary state for students&\#x27; success\. This study aims to synthesise the evidence and consider what it means to belong as a medical student, what impact it has on students and what influences its development\. METHODS: A scoping review using the Arskey and O&\#x27;Malley&\#x27;s five\-step framework was conducted\. MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsychINFO, GlobalHealth, LILACS and Sabinet were searched for research articles relating to sense of belonging in medical students until 12 December 2025\. RESULTS: Three hundred ten articles were identified\. One hundred sixty\-two used the term belonging and 148 a closely related term\. One hundred thirty\-six of these did not provide a definition\. The number of articles from authors in high\-income countries was 25\-fold and 50\-fold higher than that of authors from lower\-middle income and low\-income countries, respectively\. Well\-being was the most cited effect of belonging \(130 articles\), followed by increased learning and professional identity formation\. Only 10 articles considered the impact of sense of belonging on student attainment\. Demographic factors such as ethnicity and socio\-economic background influenced students&\#x27; sense of belonging\. Features of the learning environment were also important, including inclusive practice, diversity and representation, student support, facilitating student connection and meaningful involvement in clinical practice\. Recommendations made to promote belonging mirrored the influencing factors\. Only 26 articles presented initiatives designed to promote sense of belonging among medical students\. DISCUSSION: When considering the influences, impacts of and recommendations for developing sense of belonging, the collated evidence supports some commonly held narratives but is also lacking in some areas, with lack of definitions of belonging also creating ambiguity\. The deficit of study participants from lower\-middle and low\-income countries means that care needs to be taken when applying these findings to those settings\.

## [Information behaviour in legal decision\-making: a literature review of models relevant to street\-level bureaucrats](../publications/8e5a33bcbfb57c8ab9db.md)

Norma Fötsch; A\.A\.J\. van Helvoort

Introduction\. We investigated the information behaviour of street\-level bureaucrats \(individuals in public services\)\. Our two objectives were: first to develop a theoretical framework that supports interdisciplinary research on legal decision\-making processes, and second to deepen our understanding of how these individuals collect and use information in contexts such as asylum decision\-making\. Method\. We conducted a comprehensive literature review, systematically searching for relevant publications and empirical studies related to the information behaviour of street\-level bureaucrats\. Following a thorough selection process, we identified 34 relevant publications\. Analysis\. For our qualitative analysis, we first coded the process\-based models identified in the publications, followed by the findings from the empirical studies\. We then compared the resulting codes to categorise the elements of information behaviour, merged them, and grouped them into three clusters\. Results\. We regard these clusters as components: activities, users, and information\. Together with their respective elements, these components form a new framework and provide a methodological contribution to the study of legal decision\-making processes\. The framework was then applied to analyse the use of country of origin information by Dutch asylum caseworkers, informed by findings from a previous literature review on their information behaviour\. Conclusion\. The developed conceptual framework may serve as a basis for future empirical research into the information behaviour of street\-level bureaucrats, particularly asylum caseworkers\. This \(future\) research on information behaviour introduces a valuable and novel perspective on legal decision\-making processes\. Gaining greater insights into how decision\-makers seek, select, create, interpret, and communicate information facilitates a more comprehensive understanding of legal decision\-making processes\.

## [BIOECOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS, DISTRIBUTION RANGE, CHEMICAL COMPOSITION AND MEDICINAL PROPERTIES OF BOG BILBERRY \(VACCINIUM ULIGINOSUM L\.\)](../publications/8e623d49390e0f4b617e.md)

Zilola Jabborova

The article analyses the scientific literature on the bioecological characteristics, distribution range, chemical composition and medicinal properties of wild bog bilberry \(Vaccinium uliginosum L\.\), which grows in the cold regions of the Northern Hemisphere, and of the closely related cultivated species, highbush blueberry \(V\. corymbosum L\.\)\. Methods of systematic literature review, comparative analysis and generalisation were applied\. Bog bilberry is a circumboreal species that is highly frost\-hardy and thrives only on acidic \(pH 3\.5–5\.5\) peaty soils\. Per 100 g, the berries contain 57 kcal of energy, 14\.49 g of carbohydrates, 2\.4 g of dietary fibre, 9\.7 mg of vitamin C and 77 mg of potassium; in addition, they contain anthocyanins, flavonols, chlorogenic acid, iridoids and triterpenes\. Clinical and experimental evidence on the reduction of visual fatigue, the improvement of cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, and neuroprotective, anti\-inflammatory and antitumour effects is summarised\. The safety of bog bilberry, its contraindications, the storage conditions of the berries and the problem of V\. uliginosum and V\. corymbosum being referred to by the same name in the scientific literature are also considered separately\. The need to grow blueberries in containers on an acidic substrate and to conduct local introduction studies under the calcareous soils and hot climate of Uzbekistan is substantiated\.

## [Digital twin\-driven surrogate optimization for maximum power point tracking of photovoltaic systems under partial shading conditions](../publications/8e63441fb064670417f1.md)

R\. Gohila; P\. Veena

Photovoltaic systems under partial shading develop multimodal power\-voltage characteristics that render conventional gradient\-based MPPT algorithms ineffective\. Bio\-inspired metaheuristic approaches overcome local\-maxima entrapment but introduce a structural scan\-phase energy loss: each search iteration physically evaluates a candidate duty cycle on the PV hardware, dissipating real energy at every shading event\. This paper presents the Digital Twin\-Driven Surrogate\-Optimized MPPT \(DTSO\-MPPT\) model, which substantially reduces hardware scan losses by decoupling the global search from the physical PV system and limiting hardware interaction to VTC\-based verification\. The proposed four layer architecture has a physics calibrated Digital Twin with Recursive Least Squares, a surrogate PV surface builder to evaluate the calibrated model, an Orangutan Optimization algorithm to search the surrogate for the global optimum and finally a validation and transfer controller to verify the accuracy conditions\. The proposed model was implemented and numerically evaluated in MATLAB R2024b/Simulink 24\.1 under five partial\-shading conditions\. The simulation results exhibit the proposed model tracking efficiency as 99\.1%, GMPP convergence in 0\.14s, steady\-state power oscillation averaging approximately 0\.53 W and remaining within 0\.42–0\.58 W across the five evaluated cases\. The scan\-loss reduction energy efficiency metric of 99\.4% obtained by the proposed quantifies the reduction in scan\-loss, which represents the principal advantage over conventional hardware\-coupled MPPT methods\.

## [From pixels to prevention: Can artificial intelligence transform the endoscopic management of colorectal neoplasia?](../publications/8e6971e6b28665416666.md)

Muhammad Abdul Haseeb Khan; Abdullah Saeed; Hafiz Hanzala Tufail; Bakhtiar Ameer Tahir; Ehtezaz Khan Ali Zai

In this literature narrative review of artificial intelligence \(AI\) technologies for colorectal endoscopy \(PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library, January 2015 to June 2026, with supplementary hand\-searching\), the &quot;pixels\-to\-prevention&quot; paradigm \-image interpretation → detection → characterization → clinical decision → treatment quality → surveillance → prevention \-is employed to examine whether the well\-evidenced performance characteristics of AI can actually be tied to effective cancer prevention rather than merely listing out the different types of applications of AI that were reported in previous reviews\.Colorectal cancer prevention is strongly connected to colonoscopy but is limited by lesion miss rates, endoscopist variability, and interpretation of the results into management\.Computer\-aided detection enhances the adenoma detection rates and reduces the lesion miss rate, but the higher adenoma detection rates is just a surrogate and does not directly contribute to cancer prevention: AI\-assisted colonoscopy prefers the detection of diminutive and non\-neoplastic lesions rather than advanced neoplasms\.This review traces the evolution from computer\-aided detection to computer\-aided characterization and optical diagnosis, highlighting their recent applications for quality control of resection, prediction of recurrence development, and individualized surveillance based on risk stratification where we distinguish advances in metrics of performance from clinical utility \(interval colorectal cancer, unneeded resections, surveillance burden\)\.The review considers the questions related to the problem of false positives, algorithm bias, dataset variability, lack of external validation, automation bias, interpretability, workflow, and regulation\.Asking ourselves how intelligent endoscopy could help us going beyond the discovery of lesions through the use of artificial intelligence, we propose an agenda for research that focuses on validation and patient outcome\.

## [Transfer dynamics and spectral cascades in graph\-coupled Kuramoto networks](../publications/8e6f8aa1bf5adef12ad7.md)

Marcin Kowalczyk; Pietro Liò; Zbigniew R\. Struzik

Abstract This work introduces a spectral transfer formalism for nonlinear synchronisation dynamics to resolve how internal dynamical activity redistributes across network scales, moving beyond traditional global observables like the Kuramoto order parameter\. By projecting Kuramoto phase dynamics onto the eigenbasis of the graph Laplacian, we construct a time\-dependent transfer matrix and derive novel network metrics, including the spectral flux, which quantifies directional redistribution between structural dynamical scales rather than physical transport across nodes\. Numerical simulations on modular networks reveal structured, intermittent cascade\-like redistribution in graph\-spectral space, directional reversals, and complex interaction geometries\. Crucially, we demonstrate a clear separation between macroscopic coherence and microscopic spectral interactions, showing that highly organised, fluctuating internal redistribution dynamics persist even beneath nearly stationary and featureless global synchronisation states\. This framework extends conventional synchronisation analysis and establishes a multiscale approach for interpreting network dynamics as an evolving process of spectral reorganisation\.

## [Industrial IoT for Predictive Maintenance: Addressing Key Research Gaps in Industrial Deployment](../publications/8e71064037c6eaf3e6f7.md)

Arpit Verma; Sarvesh Kumar Srivasatava; Ashish Gupta; Ashish Singh

Many studies have already been conducted on the replacement of reactive and schedule maintenance with predictive maintenance in the context of the Industrial Internet of Things, and the reported results are very promising\. However, after a careful inspection of this literature, several gaps emerged: most of the systems rely on a single sensor, all the data used are laboratory\-based, the detection, diagnosis and prognosis phase do not communicate with each other, predictions in deep learning are not easy to explain, deployment is costly for small and medium sized industries, and action\-oriented recommendations are still only a concept and not yet a reality\. Rather than repeating these gaps, we are proposing an actual framework designed to address each gap\. It combines vibration, thermal, acoustic, and oil\-condition signals into a single edge sensor, executes detection, diagnosis and prognosis under one single pipeline and avoids needing to involve three individual models, provides explainable AI \(XAI\) layer to enable the prediction with a reason attached, and is based on low\-cost, off\-the\-shelf hardware to ensure that small industrial users do not get priced out\. The paper then describes the working process, the machine learning methods used, a case scenario, and the expected benefits and limitations, and concludes with the next steps towards fully prescriptive maintenance\.

## [Examining West African Regional Integration on the Scale of Anglophone\-Francophone Linguistic Strain](../publications/8e786bc060b6d4269133.md)

Anita Tolulope Olugbemi

The hope of the eventual transformation of the Economic Community of West African States into a cohesive regional union, accentuated with the dynamism and transformation of the institution from 1975 to the present, reflects evolving exigencies\. However, five decades down the line, the dream of a fully integrated West African community remains a pipe dream\. The nascent nationalism manifesting as a military uprising in the sub\-region further obfuscates attempts at characterising the milieu within globalisation and regionalism contexts\. There is palpable relapse in the auspicious ECOWAS of Peoples initiative, with deep\-seated colonial legacies, specifically the persistent Anglophone/Francophone linguistic blocs\. The animosity it produces has not received adequate attention\. This study examines how the persistent linguistic strain continues to inhibit regional integration\. The study adopts a Descriptive Method in analyzing data from dual sources\. This study argues that the linguistic divide is deeply entrenched and will endlessly weigh down integration, because while multilingualism serves a centripetal purpose in the European Union for example, it is the reverse in the ECOWAS\. Linguistic Relativity also known as the ‘Sapir\-Whorf Hypothesis,’ was used to explain the linguistic phenomenon\. It recommends a more robust socio\-cultural and multilingual approach which emphasises globalism epitomized in democracy despite the essential economic and political asymmetries\.

## [Immediate Hemodynamic Effects of Pulmonary Artery Flow Restrictors in Univentricular Circulation: Hypothesis\-Generating Insights from High\-Fidelity Physiologic Streaming Data Using Machine\-Learning](../publications/8e88d141712b0e230ef6.md)

J\. L\. Fox; Alan William Nugent; Conor P\. O’Halloran; Paul Tannous; Michael Evans; Rohit S\. Loomba

Hypoplastic left heart syndrome has been historically palliated with the surgical Norwood or hybrid procedures\. Transcatheter placement of pulmonary flow restrictors \(PFR\) with prostaglandin to maintain an unobstructed ductus arteriosus has emerged as an option for single\-ventricle patients that are poor surgical candidates\. High\-fidelity physiologic data has been used to predict outcomes in interstage patients\. This study aimed to characterize the acute hemodynamic effects of transcatheter flow restrictors on pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio using physiologic data\. A single\-center retrospective review of 10 patients who underwent transcatheter flow restrictor placement was performed\. High\-fidelity physiologic data \(1\-second resolution\) from before, during, and after flow restrictor placement were utilized\. Data were aggregated with the Sickbay Clinical Platform\. An autoregressive integrated moving average model was used to compare variables of interest before, during, and after flow restrictor placement\. A total of 10 patients were included in the study for a total of 123,509 patient seconds of monitoring\. A statistically significant decrease in pulmonary\-to\-systemic blood flow ratio, systemic saturation, and renal oxygen extraction, and an increase in blood pressure, were observed during and after PFR placement\. Flow restrictor placement is associated with an acute decrease in calculated pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio and an increase in calculated renal oxygen extraction ratio \(related to an increase in systemic oxygen delivery\)\. More importantly, this study demonstrates that high\-fidelity physiologic data platforms can be used for real\-time assessment of the effect of pulmonary artery flow reducers\. Eventually, clinical decision algorithms may be able to guide the pulmonary artery flow reducer strategy, both intra\-procedurally and afterward\.

## [O&\#x27;ZBEK TILIDAGI MODAL MA&\#x27;NOLARNI SUN&\#x27;IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA AVTOMATIK TASNIFLASH MODELI](../publications/8e9273b4d8b64d869423.md)

Xayrulloyеva Gulasal Fayzullo qizi

Annotatsiya\. Maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi epistemik, deontik, dinamik, volitiv va evidensial modal ma’nolarni avtomatik aniqlash uchun lingvistik qoidalar hamda transformer reprezentatsiyasini birlashtiruvchi gibrid model taklif qilinadi\. В статье предлагается гибридная модель автоматического распознавания эпистемических, деонтических, динамических, волитивных и эвиденциальных модальных значений узбекского языка\. Модель объединяет лингвистические правила и трансформерные представления\. Описываются этапы обработки, система признаков и результаты анализа примеров\. Ключевые слова: модальность, искусственный интеллект, трансформер, классификация, аннотация, корпус, прагматика\. Abstract\. ## [Transtorno do Espectro Autista: do Diagnóstico à Intervenção Neurocognitiva e Sensorial](../publications/8e9639cade06ba095130.md)

Monica dos Passos Nascimento Roveran; Lincoln Brasil Silva Rosa

Introdução: O Transtorno do Espectro Autista \(TEA\) tem apresentado um crescimento expressivo em sua prevalência, exigindo abordagens terapêuticas e educacionais fundamentadas nas neurociências\. Desenvolvimento: O estudo visa analisar a intersecção entre o diagnóstico de TEA, os mecanismos de neuroplasticidade, a integração sensorial e a ludicidade no processo de aprendizagem e desenvolvimento da linguagem\. Metodologia: A pesquisa constitui\-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, abordando conceitos teóricos sobre neuroplasticidade, processamento sensorial e intervenções comportamentais baseadas em evidências\. Os resultados indicam que a compreensão da neuroplasticidade e o fornecimento de estímulos estruturados são essenciais para a aprendizagem\. A ludicidade atua como mediadora central na intervenção precoce, enquanto a regulação sensorial atua como base para a mitigação de comportamentos disruptivos e o desenvolvimento da linguagem\. Conclusão: O desenvolvimento da criança com TEA exige uma intervenção precoce baseada no tripé clínico interdisciplinar \(Psicologia, Fonoaudiologia e Terapia Ocupacional\), unindo estratégias para maximizar as habilidades comunicativas, sensoriais e sociais de forma integrada e lúdica\.

## [Smart Ads\-Smart Ads for Smart City](../publications/8e9936997b91c0643b3c.md)

T Dr Santhosh; B M Srushti; S Amulya; S Sanika; s hiremath S Shreyash

Traditional advertising methods, such as paper posters, banners, and hoardings, require manual design, printing, installation, and maintenance\. These activities increase operational effort, material consumption, and the difficulty of updating advertisements\. This paper presents SmartAds, a web\-based artificial intelligence\-powered digital advertisement management platform developed to simplify advertisement creation, pricing, payment\-record management, approval, scheduling, and display\. The system enables users to generate promotional descriptions and slogans from product details using large language model services\. A fallback mechanism involving Groq, an optional local Ollama model, and rule\-based generation supports content creation when an AI service is unavailable\. Users can select poster or video formats, choose display slots, calculate advertisement costs, and track their submissions\. Administrators can approve or reject advertisements before they are scheduled for display\. The platform also includes payment\-record management, receipt generation, notifications, optional AI avatar\-video generation through D\-ID, and a browser\-based virtual LED display\. SmartAds was implemented using Python, Flask, SQLAlchemy, HTML, Bootstrap, and JavaScript\. Functional testing documented in the project report covered 45 test cases, all reported as passing\. The system demonstrates the feasibility of integrating AI\-assisted content generation with digital advertisement workflow management in a controlled proof\-of\-concept environment\.

## [Virulence determinants in multidrug\-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii: comparative phenotypic and genomic analysis of clinical and patient\-environmental isolates](../publications/8ea17e26e15b57ca248a.md)

Preethi Basavaraju; Rashmi Padmanabha Mahale; Morubagal Raghavendra Rao; Suchitra M Shenoy

Introduction Acinetobacter baumannii is a major cause of healthcare\-associated infections owing to its ability to acquire multidrug resistance and express multiple virulence determinants that facilitate persistence in both clinical and hospital environments\. However, comparative studies evaluating the phenotypic expression of virulence factors alongside their genomic determinants in paired clinical and patient\-environmental isolates remain limited\. This study investigated the phenotypic virulence characteristics and corresponding genomic distribution of virulence\-associated genes among multidrug\-resistant \(MDR\) A\. baumannii isolated from clinical specimens and patient environmental surroundings\. Methods A total of 110 non\-duplicate MDR A\. baumannii isolates, comprising 55 clinical and 55 corresponding patient\-environmental isolates, were included\. Biofilm formation, haemolytic activity, proteolytic activity, and siderophore production were evaluated using standard phenotypic assays\. Whole\-genome sequencing was performed on all isolates using the Illumina MiSeq platform, followed by genome assembly, annotation, and identification of virulence\-associated genes using the Virulence Factor Database \(VFDB\)\. Comparative analyses were performed between clinical and environmental isolates\. Results Clinical isolates demonstrated significantly higher frequencies of strong biofilm formation \(34/55, 61\.8% vs\. 6/55, 10\.9%\), haemolytic activity \(29/55, 52\.7% vs\. 13/55, 23\.6%\), and siderophore production \(31/55, 56\.4% vs\. 17/55, 30\.9%\) than environmental isolates \(P &lt; 0\.05\), whereas proteolytic activity was comparable between the two groups \(36/55, 65\.5% vs\. 33/55, 60\.0%\)\. Whole\-genome sequencing revealed a high prevalence of virulence\-associated genes involved in biofilm formation, haemolysis, proteolysis, and iron acquisition among phenotypically positive isolates\. Several virulence\-associated genes were also detected in a subset of phenotypically negative isolates, indicating a phenotype–genotype discordance and suggesting that gene carriage alone does not necessarily predict phenotypic expression\. Discussion Clinical MDR A\. baumannii isolates exhibited greater virulence than corresponding patient\-environmental isolates; however, environmental isolates retained multiple virulence\-associated genes, highlighting their potential role as reservoirs for persistence and transmission within healthcare settings\. Integrating phenotypic virulence assays with whole\-genome sequencing provides a comprehensive understanding of the virulence potential of MDR A\. baumannii and underscores the importance of continuous environmental surveillance and infection prevention strategies to limit the dissemination of highly virulent strains\.

## [A geographic grid\-based research on the spatiotemporal network of intangible cultural heritage and its impacting elements: The case of Pearl River Basin, China](../publications/8ead3776a37cd6933d9d.md)

Xingmeng Ma; Yanlong Guo

This study examines 976 intangible cultural heritage items within the Pearl River Basin\. It aims to reveal their static spatial distribution characteristics, dynamic evolution patterns, and influencing factors, laying a foundation for cultural preservation and regional sustainable development in the basin\. Employing ArcGIS geographic information systems and methodologies, including Lorenz curves, nearest neighbor indices, kernel density analysis, and geographic concentration indices, the study systematically analyzes the spatial diffusion patterns and dynamic evolution processes of intangible cultural heritage while investigating their influencing factors\. Results indicate that at the static distribution level, intangible cultural heritage across categories and provinces exhibits uneven spatial clustering\. The basin as a whole forms a spatial structure comprising two cores, two foci, and one trend belt\. Among the ten major categories, Guangdong and Fujian rank first in quantity, with the northeastern region serving as the overall distribution core\. At the dynamic evolution level, the distribution center first shifted northwestward, then eastward, and finally westward\. The number of intangible cultural heritage nominations reached its peak in 2008, with Guangdong Province submitting the highest number of nominations\. Regarding influencing factors, intangible cultural heritage tends to be distributed in areas with favorable natural conditions, concentrating in regions with gentle slopes, lower altitudes, and suitable climates, and is not constrained by economic factors\. The optimized abstract clearly presents the core research objectives, methodology, key findings, and central conclusions, significantly enhancing structural coherence and readability\. We will conduct further verification to ensure precise and concise expression\.

## [Healthy digital learning environments relate to faculty wellbeing through technological adaptation and perceived organizational support](../publications/8eb370351b34e1c09bdf.md)

K\. D\. V\. Prasad; Shivoham Singh; Hemant Kothari; Ridhi Rani; Ved Srinivas; Debanjan Nag

Digitally mediated teaching practices have changed faculty occupational behaviors and working conditions, exposing faculty to greater demands associated with always\-on connectivity, extended screen\-time, sedentary work posture, and technology\-mediated occupational stressors\. The current research explored associations between healthy digital learning environments \(HDLE\) and faculty well\-being via the proposed moderators of technological adaptation and perceived organizational support\. The researchers posited digitally mediated faculty scholarly work as an issue of occupational health and public health\. The data was collected from a sample of 500 faculty who were employed at colleges and universities in and around Hyderabad India\. Using Socio\-Technical Systems Theory as a foundation and the Job Demands–Resources Model as a guide, the researchers tested relationships using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, and bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples\. HDLE was significantly and positively associated with technological adaptation \(β = 0\.463, p &lt; \.001\) and perceived organizational support \(β = 0\.374, p &lt; \.001\)\. The researchers found a non\-significant direct association between HDLE and faculty well\-being \(β = 0\.019, p = \.912\)\. Perceived organizational support was a significant predictor of faculty well\-being \(β = 0\.309, p &lt; \.001\) and technological adaptation was a significant predictor of faculty well\-being \(β = 0\.167, p = \.002\)\. HDLE had a significant indirect association with faculty well\-being when tested through both technological adaptation and perceived organizational support \(full mediation\)\. Faculty who worked in environments with healthier technology use reported greater adaptive capacities to technology, higher levels of perceived organizational support, and greater well\-being\. The current study highlights organizational support and technological adaptation as relevant workplace resources and establishes potential occupation\- and mental\-health implications of human\-centered digital learning environments\. Future research should include longitudinal designs\.

## [Shift and Increase in Tidal Modulation of Seismicity in the Ridgecrest Fault Zone Before and After the 2019 Magnitude 7\.1 Earthquake](../publications/8ebdabf9105291f58377.md)

Éric Beaucé; Piero Poli; F\. Waldhauser; Benjamin Kamine Holtzman; Christopher H\. Scholz

ABSTRACT We studied the tidal modulation of the rate of seismicity in the Ridgecrest, California area between 2008 and 2024, thus including the 2019 Mw 7\.1 earthquake\. We combined machine\-learning\-enhanced earthquake detection and location with a novel methodology to characterize tidal modulation\. We identified significant modulation of seismicity in the Ridgecrest fault zone and in the neighboring regions, the Coso volcanic field and the Garlock fault, but tidal modulation in the fault zone exhibits a unique temporal evolution\. Modulation in the fault zone shifts, around 2014–2015, from a stress\-controlled regime where peak seismicity occurs at peak tidal stress to a stress\-rate\-controlled regime where peak seismicity occurs at peak tidal stress rate\. In contrast, peak seismicity in Coso and along the Garlock fault consistently occurs at peak tidal stress throughout time\. Moreover, the strength of tidal modulation in the fault zone increases before the 2019 Mw 7\.1 earthquake, unlike in its surroundings\. A possible interpretation based on experimental and theoretical work suggests that some characteristic frictional time scale \(the nucleation time or the critical period of the fault\) becomes shorter than the dominant tidal period after 2015\. This change implies that the fault loading rate increases, which may be accompanied by a decrease in effective normal stress\. Reduced effective stress, fault zone resonance, or increased mechanical compliance could cause the increase in modulation strength\. We propose that these changes manifest a preparation phase before a large earthquake\.

## [Species distribution of nontuberculous mycobacteria identified at a national reference laboratory in Ecuador from 2019 to 2024](../publications/8ec1cb8086995359ee54.md)

Greta Franco\-Sotomayor; Elsy Carvajal; Eva Nicola; Camilo Cardenas Franco; Andrea Belén Salcedo Maldonado; Solon Alberto Orlando; Miguel Ángel García\-Bereguiain

Nontuberculous mycobacteria \(NTM\) are clinically relevant opportunistic pathogens\. However, epidemiological data on NTM in low\- and middle\-income countries like Ecuador remain scarce\. This retrospective study characterized the species distribution of NTM identified by molecular methods in the 225 isolates processed at the “Instituto Nacional de Salud Pública e Investigación” in Ecuador from 2019 to 2024\. Most isolates were recovered from pulmonary samples \(205/225; 91\.11%\)\. Their geographic distribution was heterogeneous, with the highest numbers recorded in El Oro, Pichincha, and Los Ríos\. However, because all isolates were processed at a single national reference laboratory, this distribution may reflect referral patterns and access to laboratory services\. It should not be interpreted as representative of Ecuador’s national NTM epidemiology\. Overall, 11 different NTM species were identified, with M\. fortuitum , M\. intracellulare , M\. kansasii , and M\. abscessus predominating in pulmonary isolates, while M\. fortuitum and M\. abscessus predominated in extrapulmonary isolates\. The relatively small number of NTM isolates identified over the six\-year study period, together with the scarcity of national data, suggests that NTM infections may be underdiagnosed in Ecuador\. Strengthening surveillance and diagnostic capacity for NTM in Ecuador is strongly recommended\.

## [Environmental enrichment as a multisystem modulator of neurotransmitter function: mechanisms, plasticity, and therapeutic implications](../publications/8ec872be2bbaa8f376b0.md)

Gaurav Singhal; Bernhard Theodor Baune

Environmental enrichment \(EE\) has emerged as a powerful non\-pharmacological strategy for reshaping brain function through experience dependent plasticity\. By integrating sensory, cognitive, motor, and social stimulation, EE provides a biologically relevant framework for understanding how external environments influence neurotransmitter systems that govern mood, cognition, stress adaptation, and neurodegeneration\. In this review, we examined the effects of EE on major neurotransmitter pathways, including serotonergic, dopaminergic, glutamatergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, adrenergic, and histaminergic systems\. We conducted a structured narrative search of PubMed, supplemented by Google Scholar reference list searching and informed by PRISMA reporting principles\. The literature search covered studies published through 4 September 2026\. The initial search, completed in February 2025, included 136 articles\. A supplemental update screened 108 PubMed records and identified seven additional eligible primary studies, resulting in an updated evidence synthesis comprising 143 articles\. Across predominantly preclinical studies, EE was consistently associated with enhanced neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, stress resilience, and improved behavioral and cognitive outcomes, accompanied by neurotransmitter related changes across multiple brain systems\. The most robust evidence supported modulation of serotonergic, dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic pathways, whereas adrenergic and histaminergic effects were less well characterized and often indirect\. Mechanistically, these effects converged on altered receptor and transporter expression, neurotrophic signaling, CREB dependent transcriptional regulation, and epigenetic remodeling\. Collectively, the evidence positions EE as a multisystem regulator of neurotransmitter function with potential relevance to mood disorders, neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, stroke, addiction, and cognitive decline\. Nevertheless, the field remains limited by the predominance of animal data and by substantial heterogeneity in enrichment paradigms\. Future translational and clinical studies are needed to define the most effective EE components, timing, and intensity for therapeutic application in humans\.

## [Isothankunic acid from Centella asiatica targets signalling inducing caspase\-3 activation and cell cycle arrest in PA\-1 ovarian teratocarcinoma cells](../publications/8edfc59afa5c63f0b8f2.md)

Nawaf Alshammari; Mamdouh Alshammari; Malvi Surti

Ovarian cancer remains a major cause of mortality due to chemoresistance and apoptosis evasion\. This study evaluated the anticancer activity of a methanolic extract \(ME\) of Centella asiatica against PA\-1 ovarian teratocarcinoma cells\. The ME exhibited concentration\-dependent cytotoxicity, with an IC₅₀ of 89\.89 μg/mL\. Apoptotic cells increased from 8\.54% in controls to 66\.3% following treatment, accompanied by increased active caspase\-3 expression and a G2/M\-arrest phenotype, indicating inhibited cell survival and proliferation\. LC‒MS profiling identified multiple phytochemicals within the extract, which were subsequently evaluated using molecular docking, ADMET profiling and molecular dynamics simulations\. Isothankunic acid has emerged as a potential bioactive candidate with favourable predicted interaction with estrogen receptor alpha\. Overall, the ME demonstrated cytotoxic and pro\-apoptotic effects in PA\-1 cells, while isothankunic acid remains an analytically identified and computationally prioritized candidate requiring isolation and direct experimental validation\.

## [Referral Delay and Admission Hypothermia among Outborn Neonates at PHQ Hospital Gilgit](../publications/8ef499a8bb45066f10a3.md)

Amara Akram; Zainab Muhammad Hussain; Umair Riaz; Dr\. Hassan Shah; Shazia Batool; Dr\. Muhammad Hamid

Objective: To assess whether a longer delay between referral advice and hospital arrival was linked with a lower admission temperature and greater severity of hypothermia in outborn neonates\. Methods: This prospective observational study included 240 referred neonates aged 0–28 days who arrived at PHQ Hospital Gilgit between 1 November 2025 and 28 August 2026\. Referral time, arrival time and the first rectal temperature recorded within two hours of arrival were noted\. WHO temperature categories were used\. The relationship between referral delay and admission temperature was examined using Kruskal–Wallis testing, Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression, with adjustment for gestational age, admission weight, sex and documented thermal protection\. Results: Median referral delay was 5\.85 hours \(interquartile range 4\.20–8\.20\), and mean admission temperature was 36\.02 ± 0\.61°C\. Hypothermia was recorded in 190 neonates \(79\.2%\): 90 had mild and 100 had moderate hypothermia\. Median delay was 4\.2 hours among normothermic neonates, 5\.5 hours among those with mild hypothermia and 8\.2 hours among those with moderate hypothermia \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. Longer delay correlated with lower temperature \(ρ=−0\.63; p&lt;0\.001\)\. Each additional hour was associated with a 0\.120°C lower temperature after adjustment \(95% confidence interval −0\.137 to −0\.103\)\. Documented thermal protection was associated with a 0\.510°C higher temperature \(95% confidence interval 0\.380–0\.640\)\. Conclusion: Longer referral delays were associated with lower early admission temperatures\. These findings highlight the importance of timely transfer and continuous thermal care, although this observational study cannot prove that delay itself caused the fall in temperature\.

## [The roadmap of quantum many\-body physics : from exact diagonalization to machine learning](../publications/8efaf0c5a26fdb333514.md)

Yilun Gao

The study of interacting quantum many\-body systems is constrained by the exponential growth of the Hilbert space with system size, which limits both numerical simulations and theoretical understanding\. This thesis explores how the interplay between disorder and interactions shapes localization and ergodicity in quantum many\-body systems, using the exact diagonalization method, and how machine learning can serve as an alternative approach for studying these systems\. We first investigate the many\-body localization problem in a one\-dimensional SU\(2\)\-invariant random antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using exact and sparse matrix diagonalization methods\. By analyzing energy level gap\-ratio statistics, participation ratio, entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectral parameter as a function of disorder strength under di\!erent random coupling distributions, we identify clear qualitative di\!erences from the widely studied random field Heisenberg chain\. For system sizes up to L = 24, signatures of localized behaviour are much less pronounced than in the case of the random field model\. Motivated by the limitations of conventional numerical methods, we examine machine learning as a scalable paradigm for many\-body physics\. Using the Bose\- Hubbard model in one and two dimensions as a benchmark, we test HUBBARDNET, a deep neural network architecture, by replacing standard stochastic gradient descent with adaptive moment estimation \(ADAM\), adjusting the learning rate for improved optimization, and introducing physics\-informed output activations that can resolve extremely small wave\-function amplitudes\. This approach yields ground\-state energy errors reduced by orders of magnitude and wave function fidelities exceeding 99%, remaining robust across four decades of interaction strength and over superfluid, Mott\-insulating, and quantum chaotic regimes\. Beyond energy prediction, the trained models accurately reproduce generalized inverse participation ratios and multifractal dimensions for ground and excited states, capturing localization, delocalization, and multifractality across the spectrum, with excited\-state training explicitly guided by fractal dimensions that encode the multifractal properties of the wave functions\.

## [Once\-weekly insulin icodec in type 1 diabetes: Are we ready for children?](../publications/8f01b5ec40bcd0f397e3.md)

Pragati Sisodia

During my fellowship training in pediatric endocrinology, my understanding of the ambulatory care of type 1 diabetes \(T1D\) evolved considerably\.I had initially viewed the basal\-bolus regimen and a so\-called prescribed diabetic diet as the major pillars of management\.In the diabetes clinic, however, I learned that successful care extends far beyond insulin prescription and diet adjustments\-asking about insulin doses taken during the school hours, identifying hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia patterns, checking injection technique, understanding social challenges, and helping families obtain insulin and glucose\-monitoring supplies\.In the developing world, clinicians are still struggling to educate parents/caregivers and children on the importance of adhering to a basal\-bolus insulin regimen, regular blood glucose level monitoring, emphasis on the use of continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\), and the need to administer bolus insulin for meals consumed during school hours\.Attempts to reduce the immediate burden and cost of glucose checks and insulin injections may ultimately come at the expense of suboptimal glycemic control and its resultant long\-term complications\.In this background, one of the major developments in diabetes care this year has drawn my attention\-the US Food and Drug Administration \(FDA\) approval of insulin icodec \(Awiqli\), the first once\-weekly basal insulin, on March 26, 2026, for use in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2D\)\.For a pediatric endocrinologist, this raises an intriguing question: &quot;Could once\-weekly basal insulin someday ease the treatment burden for children and adolescents with T1D?&quot;

## [Pengembangan Model Intervensi pada Ibu Hamil Berisiko Dalam Rangka Pencegahan Preeklamsia](../publications/8f04cdbeb99da7869a94.md)

Sri Handayani, S\.Si\.T,M\.Kes\.; Triani Yuliastanti; Yuni Puji Widiastuti; Novita Nur Hidayati

Latar Belakang : Preeklamsia merupakan penyebab utama morbiditas dan mortalitas ibu dan bayi\. Berbagai intervensi farmakologis, nonfarmakologis, perubahan gaya hidup, dan teknologi digital telah dikembangkan sebagai upaya pencegahan\. Tujuan : Menganalisis efektivitas berbagai intervensi pencegahan preeklamsia pada ibu hamil berisiko\. Metode: Systematic Literature Review menggunakan pedoman PRISMA 2020 dan kerangka PICOS \( Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Study Design \) \. Populasi adalah ibu hamil berisiko preeklamsia; intervensi meliputi farmakologis, nonfarmakologis, edukasi, perubahan gaya hidup, skrining, dan teknologi digital; outcome mencakup kejadian preeklamsia, kepatuhan, luaran maternal\-neonatal, dan deteksi dini\. Penelusuran dilakukan pada Scopus, PubMed, dan Google Scholar untuk publikasi 2020–2025\. Dari 314 artikel yang diidentifikasi, 50 artikel memenuhi kriteria inklusi dan dianalisis secara naratif\. Hasil : Aspirin dosis rendah dan suplementasi kalsium merupakan intervensi dengan bukti paling konsisten\. Vitamin D dan L\-arginin menunjukkan manfaat pada kelompok tertentu\. Intervensi edukasi, skrining trimester pertama, perubahan gaya hidup, serta aplikasi digital meningkatkan deteksi dini dan kepatuhan\. Simpulan: Pencegahan preeklamsia memerlukan pendekatan multidimensi yang mengintegrasikan intervensi farmakologis, nonfarmakologis, edukasi, dan teknologi digital\.

## [Topology\-aware and constraint\-guided deep reinforcement learning for climate\-resilient control of urban stormwater systems](../publications/8f20fe865058832c122e.md)

Kaiyu Jing; Mohammed Abubakor Baljon; Ghanshyam G\. Tejani

Introduction Urban stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by extreme precipitation events, leading to hydraulic surcharge when system capacity is exceeded\. Traditional rule\-based control \(RBC\) is reactive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning \(DRL\) does not explicitly exploit drainage‐network topology or ensure physically consistent control\. This study introduces Constraint\-guided Graph\-PPO \(PIG‐PPO\), a topology‐aware reinforcement learning framework designed to improve stormwater control under extreme precipitation conditions\. Methods PIG‐PPO integrates a graph convolutional network \(GCN\) state encoder with proximal policy optimization \(PPO\)\. A soft mass\-balance residual penalty is incorporated into the reward function to encourage physically consistent control\. The framework was trained on 20 moderate design storms and evaluated on 30 held‐out extreme storms and 20 long‐duration monsoon‐like events\. Performance was assessed across 10 independent PPO seeds, with comparisons against RBC and a topology‐agnostic MLP‐PPO ablation\. Few‐shot adaptation, cross‐topology validation using a second PyStorms scenario after retraining, and parameter‐count analysis were also conducted\. Results Across 10 independent PPO seeds, PIG‐PPO reduced mean overflow by 31\.2% relative to RBC and reduced the control‐effort metric by 78\.3% relative to the MLP‐PPO ablation, with Holm‐adjusted p‐values below 0\.001\. Few‐shot adaptation reduced overflow during monsoon\-like events by 58\.8% relative to zero‐shot transfer\. Parameter‐count analysis demonstrated a 106\.69\-fold encoder‐size advantage over a flat MLP at 1,000 nodes\. However, this result reflects parameter efficiency rather than direct validation at city scale\. Discussion The results indicate that topology‐aware state encoding and constraint\-guided reward shaping can improve stormwater control performance and support adaptation to previously unseen precipitation regimes\. Cross‐topology evaluation provides additional evidence of the framework’s applicability beyond the initial network configuration\. Nevertheless, the climate‐resilience implications are limited to performance under synthetic extreme precipitation regimes designed to emulate intensifying rainfall patterns associated with climate change; direct validation against observational climate\-projection datasets was not conducted\.

## [Resource subsidies mediated by non\-native species: a review](../publications/8f27b6a58823d5d55fb7.md)

Letícia Alves; Janeide de Assis Guilherme Padilha; Phillip Joschka Haubrock; Amanda L\. Subalusky; Ronaldo Sousa

Non\-native species are recognized as one of the major drivers of biodiversity change globally, with profound impacts on ecosystem functions and services\. Despite the high number of studies on non\-native species published, mainly in the last two decades, an often\-overlooked aspect is their role as mediators of resource subsidies \(the cross\-boundary movement of energy, nutrients, or materials\)\. This topic may have theoretical and empirical implications because non\-native species may play a major role in ecosystem connectivity by transporting—or interrupting the transport of—energy and organic matter\. Therefore, the main aims of this review were to \(1\) assess temporal trends, geographic distribution, and methodological approaches in research on resource subsidies mediated by non\-native species; \(2\) synthesize how non\-native species alter the magnitude, direction, and dynamics of resource subsidies across ecosystems and their implications for ecosystem functioning; and \(3\) identify key gaps in current knowledge and define future research priorities\. The review retrieved 143 publications, resulting in 212 case studies, that collectively show that non\-native species can both reduce and increase resource flows across ecosystem boundaries, with implications for ecosystem dynamics and connectivity\. Although terrestrial and freshwater connectivity accounted for the majority of published case studies \(56%\), many ecosystem linkages remain underexplored\. A significant geographic bias was found, with Africa being severely understudied \(2\.8% of all publications\), followed by Asia \(7\.7% of all publications\)\. Taxonomic representation was also skewed, with the majority of studies focusing on non\-native plants \(28\.8% of case studies\), non\-native fish \(25\.5% of case studies\), and mammals \(21\.7% of case studies\), whereas fungi \(0\.9%\) and bacteria \(2\.4%\) were largely neglected despite their fundamental roles in decomposition processes\. Key priorities for advancing this field include long\-term monitoring, the application of emerging molecular and analytical tools \(e\.g\., telemetry, eDNA, metabarcoding, and isotopic tracers\), and the integration of artificial intelligence to synthesize large datasets\. The findings provide the first synthesis of resource subsidies mediated by non\-native species\. This information is crucial for biodiversity conservation and the effective management of ecosystems and their connectivity\.

## [A BERT\-based multi\-task learning framework for social media opinion mining with risk detection](../publications/8f33b392a5012ffbbbaf.md)

Wei\-Wei Liu

Abstract This paper proposes a BERT\-based multi\-task learning framework for social media mining and risk detection\. Unlike traditional open\-loop architectures, the proposed system establishes a closed\-loop feedback mechanism among crawling, analysis, and alerting modules, focusing on high\-accuracy negative sentiment detection for social risk detection\. A dataset of 4,238 texts is constructed, covering eight topic categories and three sentiment labels\. A BERT\-based multi\-task framework with shared encoder and two task\-specific heads jointly optimizes topic classification and sentiment analysis\. Training uses AdamW \(learning rate 2e\-5, batch size 16, max length 128\) for three epochs\. The multi\-task BERT model achieves 97\.97% F1 for topic classification and 99\.89% F1 for sentiment analysis\. Negative sentiment detection reaches 100% accuracy\. Compared to single\-task models \(98\.34% and 99\.76%\), the multi\-task model maintains comparable topic performance while improving sentiment analysis\. Removing pre\-training fine\-tuning reduces training time by 7\.9% with stable performance\. The model performs two tasks in one inference, reducing deployment complexity while enabling reliable negative sentiment detection for social media opinion monitoring\.

## [ОСНОВНІ ПРОТИРІЧЧЯ У СУЧАСНИХ КОНЦЕПЦІЯХ СОЦІУМІВ, ЩО ПРИПУСКАЮТЬ СУБ&\#x27;ЄКТНІСТЬ ЗАГАЛЬНОГО ШІ](../publications/8f3bb7f7ce084d5aba85.md)

Stanislav BESKARAVAINYI

Потенційне створення штучних інтелектів, що не будуть поступатися людині, так званих «Загальних ШІ» \(AGI\), робить реальною участь роботів у соціальному житті суспільства\. Але форма соціальних структур, які може створювати інтелектуальна техніка, залишається маловивченою\. Більшість прогнозів, що описують гетерогенний, людино\-машинний соціум, можна віднести до трьох концепцій: гуманістичної, трансгманістичної і постгуманістичної\. Але антропоцентричні чи контр\-антропоцентрические причини міркувань призводять до внутрішніх протиріч у створюваних моделях соціуму\. Необхідно описати протиріччя в актуальних футурологічних прогнозах про людино\-машинні соціуми та показати методологічні підстави їх подолання\. Гуманістична концепція людино\-машинного соціуму розглядається в роботах К\. Шваба, М\. Хардта та А\. Негрі, С\. Жижека, а також сумі авторів, що досліджують напрямок «Human\-Robot Interaction»\. Трансгуманізм розглянутий у роботах М\. Срничека, А\. Вільямса Н\. Ленда, К\. Ярвіна, та суми авторів, що досліджує модель коеволюції людини та машини\. Постгуманізм – у роботах Н\. Бострома, Ю\. Харарі, Ф\. Феррандо, Р\. Брайдотті, Ж\.\-М\. Шеффера\. Висновки: показано, що антропна модель суб&\#x27;єкта імпліцитно використовується як зразок суб&\#x27;єкта у рамках гуманістичних, а й трансгуманістичних і постгуманістичних концепцій\. Спроби створення моделей соціуму з використанням редукованих моделей техногенних суб&\#x27;єктів, із запозиченням моделей поведінки тварин або простих моделей з теорії ігор, призводять до перманентного змішування соціальних, технологічних та біологічних факторів у описі поведінки техногенного суб&\#x27;єкта\. Тобто неантропоморфна модель соціальних взаємодій не формулюється\. Показано, що «акторно\-мережева теорія» \(М\. Каллона, Б\. Латура\), концепції «асамбляжів» \(М\. Деланда\) та «комунікації» \(Н\. Лумана\) – не дозволяють оцінювати гетерогенний людино\-машинний соціум\. Ймовірно, лише створивши цілісну модель техногенного суб&\#x27;єкта, можна розпочати повноцінного моделювання постлюдських соціумів\. Можливо, лише завдяки створенню цілісної моделі техногенного суб’єкта вдасться розпочати комплексне моделювання постлюдських суспільств\. Доведено, що антропна модель суб’єкта неявно використовується як еталон суб’єктності загалом – не лише в межах гуманістичної соціальної парадигми, а й, подекуди, у трансгуманістичній та постгуманістичній парадигмах; спроби відмовитися від антропної моделі призводять до змішування соціального, психологічного, техногенного та біологічного під час моделювання нових суб’єктів\. Довільно обрана поведінкова модель \(наприклад, людина в суспільстві, тварина в зграї, раціональний гравець\) поширюється на всю потенційну соціальну сферу та на всі типи суб’єктів, акторів, автономних агентів тощо\. Це унеможливлює аналіз культурної специфіки суспільства або прогнозування дій суб’єкта\.

## [Distributional signatures of computation: inferring mechanisms from computation time distributions](../publications/8f3f53805de537b8a8d7.md)

Céline van Valkenhoef; Catherine Schuman; Nikolaus Kriegeskorte; Philip Walther

Computational complexity theory provides a framework for analysing abstract models of computation, whereas computational systems operate as finite physical implementations whose behaviour is shaped by their architecture and physical substrate\. In such systems, computational organisation cannot be directly characterised from algorithms or internal representations\. Building on the use of reaction time distributions to constrain mechanisms in cognitive science, we introduce an empirical framework for investigating computation in physical systems by inferring computational mechanisms from observable computation time distributions\. The framework combines empirical benchmarking, which characterises computational efficiency through the scaling of computation time with problem size, with distributional analysis, which treats computation time distributions as signatures of the stochastic dynamics generated by different computational mechanisms\. We demonstrate the framework using a scalable visual search paradigm, comparing human performance with three computational models that employ distinct mechanisms of evidence accumulation\. Benchmarking reveals broadly similar scaling behaviour for the models and human observers, whereas distributional analysis distinguishes between these models\. We show that computation time distributions provide an empirical level of description linking observable computational behaviour to underlying computational mechanisms\. This framework complements computational complexity theory by extending the empirical study of computation from measuring computational performance to characterising computational organisation\. It provides an empirical approach for comparing finite computational systems across diverse physical implementations, including biological, classical, neuromorphic, and quantum systems, without requiring access to their internal algorithms or architectures\.

## [Integrasi Framework Laravel dan Android pada Sistem IoT untuk Monitoring Parameter Fisika\-Kimia di Greenhouse](../publications/8f43038019e9e37fad9a.md)

Ramadanzah Ramadanzah; Dodi Yudo Setyawan; Nurfiana Nurfiana; Refi Arioen

Pengembangan teknologi pertanian presisi \(precision agriculture\) pada ekosistem greenhouse menggunakan sistem hidroponik menghadapi tantangan teknis dalam menjaga stabilitas parameter lingkungan mikro secara simultan\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengintegrasikan framework Laravel dan platform Android ke dalam sistem Internet of Things \(IoT\) untuk memantau parameter fisika\-kimia lingkungan, meliputi suhu udara, kelembaban, intensitas cahaya, dan kadar karbon dioksida \(CO2\), pada budidaya pakcoy \(Brassica rapa L\.\) di greenhouse hidroponik\. Fokus utama penelitian ini terletak pada perancangan arsitektur backend RESTful API menggunakan Laravel untuk mengelola penyimpanan basis data riwayat jangka panjang serta menyinkronkan transmisi data dari multi\-sensor \(DHT22, LDR, dan sensor gas CO2\) yang memiliki karakteristik sampling rate berbeda\. Di sisi pengguna, aplikasi Android dan antarmuka web dikembangkan sebagai frontend yang mengonsumsi data melalui serialisasi format JSON menggunakan metode polling HTTP GET real\-time, serta menyediakan tiga mode kendali aktuator, yaitu manual, otomatis berbasis ambang batas sensor, dan penjadwalan\. Pengujian fungsionalitas dan kinerja sistem dilakukan melalui visualisasi antarmuka pada dasbor situs web neliti\-sk\.darmajaya\.ac\.id serta evaluasi transmisi data nirkabel\. Infrastruktur backend berbasis Laravel terbukti stabil dalam menangani fluktuasi frekuensi data sensor yang kompleks\. Berdasarkan evaluasi log data selama 24 jam pengujian kontinu pada rentang 14 Agustus 2026 \(00\.00–23\.00 WIB\), sistem berhasil merekam seluruh 24 titik data per jam \(100%\) tanpa satupun jam yang terlewat\. Integrasi ini menghadirkan solusi pemantauan sekaligus pengendalian pertanian presisi yang andal, terintegrasi, dan memiliki skalabilitas tinggi bagi operator greenhouse, meskipun masih memerlukan mekanisme offline logging untuk mengantisipasi gangguan konektivitas atau pemadaman listrik di masa mendatang\.

## [Institutional policies for responsible generative AI use in Saudi higher education: a policy review and gap analysis of national\-to\-institutional implementation](../publications/8f50938686611ec2ae35.md)

Fouad Ahmed Atallah

Saudi Arabia has established a comprehensive national\-level governance landscape for generative artificial intelligence through the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority \(SDAIA\), including the AI Ethics Principles \(2023\), Generative AI Guidelines \(2024–2025\), the AI Adoption Framework, and the Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications, alongside broader strategic directions under Vision 2030\. This study employed systematic documentary analysis combined with gap analysis to examine eight national\-level policy and strategic documents, focusing on governance principles, operational mechanisms, and their relevance to Saudi higher education\. The analysis reveals three critical findings: \(1\) national frameworks articulate detailed governance principles, organizational responsibilities, and operational guidance for responsible AI use, although the regulatory status and degree of prescriptiveness vary across documents; \(2\) national documents reference Islamic values and cultural alignment but generally lack explicit integration of Maqasid al\-Shariah principles into governance language or operational mechanisms; and \(3\) an institutional audit of 17 purposively selected Saudi universities identified publicly accessible formal AI governance policies or guidelines at six institutions, indicating substantial variation in the publicly documented institutional translation of national AI governance frameworks\. The findings suggest that translating national principles into operational institutional frameworks may benefit from three key components: higher\-education\-specific policy translation mechanisms, clearly defined accountability structures with appropriate monitoring indicators, and explicit consideration of Islamic ethical dimensions\. Documentary analysis combined with institutional policy auditing and gap analysis provides a systematic approach to identifying discontinuities between national governance frameworks and publicly documented institutional policy development\. The findings contribute to understanding AI governance challenges in Saudi higher education and highlight the importance of institutional\-level policy architecture for connecting national governance principles with educational practice\. The research also has implications for other Arab and Muslim\-majority higher education systems seeking to align emerging global AI governance standards with local Islamic and cultural values\.

## [Association between infant crawling characteristics and fundamental movement skill development in preschool children](../publications/8f5b1a0c421ed961b328.md)

Yuehui Zhou; Huizi Yin; Yingxiang Fang; Bingao Chen; Juhua Wu; Yang Yuan

This study examined the associations between infant crawling experience and crawling characteristics and fundamental movement skill \(FMS\) development in preschool children to characterize population\-level associations and generate hypotheses for prospective research\. A retrospective cross\-sectional design was used, including 557 children aged 3–6 years from kindergartens in Qufu, Shandong Province, and the surrounding areas\. Infant crawling experience and crawling characteristics were collected retrospectively through guardian questionnaires, and FMS was assessed using the Test of Gross Motor Development–Third Edition \(TGMD\-3\)\. Children with a total FMS score below the 25th percentile were classified as having relatively insufficient FMS development, and a multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to examine these associations\. Compared with children with relatively sufficient crawling experience, those with insufficient crawling experience had lower locomotor skill and ball skill scores, as well as lower total FMS scores\. These findings suggest that insufficient crawling experience and selected crawling characteristics, particularly daily crawling duration and crawling\-posture diversity, are statistically associated with relatively insufficient FMS development in preschool children; however, their significance requires further confirmation in prospective studies\.

## [Graph Serializations for Reasoning LLMs: A Study Across Knowledge Extraction and Structural Reasoning](../publications/8f5b6dd7d3d7504f8da0.md)

Julien Yu; Mihaela Bornea; Avirup Sil; Katrin Kirchhoff

The way a knowledge graph is serialized as text for inclusion into LLM context can substantially affect downstream LLM performance, with prior work reporting tens of percentage points variations across formats\. However, existing studies consider only a limited set of representations and predate frontier reasoning models, which now offer stronger reasoning, instruction\-following, and long\-context capabilities\. We evaluate 15 graph representation formats across nine frontier LLM configurations on ontology\-based knowledge extraction and structural graph reasoning tasks\. While knowledge extraction is relatively insensitive to different serialization formats, the choice of the optimal format for structural reasoning tasks significantly affects accuracy\. We demonstrate that the optimal representation choice depends on model, query, and task and propose to approach graph serialization as a dynamic orchestration decision\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE SYSTEM OF MASTER PLAN DEVELOPMENT AND ADJUSTMENT](../publications/8f6de2349d799d7d6ba8.md)

Egor Nakaryakov; Mihail Lavrenenkov

The development and adjustment of a master plan involve processing a considerable amount of heterogeneous spatial information, including data from the Unified State Register of Real Estate, territorial and urban zoning documents, information on existing development, engineering and transport infrastructure, and zones with special land\-use conditions\. As the digital information base expands, the analytical work of planners becomes more complicated, since it requires not only collecting data but also identifying relationships, restrictions, and contradictions between different datasets\. The purpose of the study is to determine the role of artificial intelligence technologies in the development and adjustment of master plans and to propose a model for their integration into urban planning analysis\. The methodological framework combines systems and comparative analysis, cadastral interpretation and spatial data comparison, as well as an analysis of Russian and international research in digital urban planning and GeoAI\. The study identifies preliminary territorial classification, detection of spatial inconsistencies, land\-use change analysis, identification of territorial reserves, and scenario modelling as the most relevant areas for artificial intelligence application\. A sequential model is proposed in which intelligent analysis is performed after the spatial database has been created and verified but before the final planning decision is selected by experts\. Within this approach, artificial intelligence does not replace the specialist but reduces routine data processing and helps identify areas requiring in\-depth analysis at an earlier stage\. The results can be used to develop digital tools for information and analytical support of territorial planning\.

## [Model Stability Evaluation Under Random Seed Variation Using SSI and RRS](../publications/8f81b24b8b2804431ae0.md)

Nurul Chamidah; Azwa Abdul Aziz

Machine learning models are commonly evaluated using a single experimental run, implicitly assuming that performance remains stable under fixed conditions\. However, many machine learning algorithms involve stochastic processes that may cause performance variability across different random seed configurations\. We examine how sensitive tabular classifiers are to the choice of random seed\. Multi\-Layer Perceptron \(MLP\), Random Forest, Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), and XGBoost were each trained and tested under 30 seeds on three public benchmark datasets\. To assess robustness, this study introduces two complementary stability measures: Stability Sensitivity Index \(SSI\) and Relative Robustness Score \(RRS\)\. Stability was measured on three metrics: Accuracy, F1\-score, and ROC\-AUC\. The results demonstrate that model performance can vary substantially across random seed configurations; on the smallest dataset, the accuracy of a single run differed by up to 7\.9 percentage points depending on the seed\. XGBoost achieved the highest mean performance on the two large datasets and, in most cases, also the lowest variability there, whereas SVM was the most stable model on the small Breast Cancer dataset\. MLP was generally the most seed\-sensitive model on the large datasets, and Random Forest on the small one\. F1\-score varied considerably more than Accuracy and ROC\-AUC, particularly under class imbalance\. Furthermore, the smallest dataset generally exhibits greater variability than the larger datasets\. These results argue for reporting seed\-level variability, not only mean scores, as a routine part of model evaluation\. The proposed SSI and RRS metrics can support stability\-aware model selection and reproducibility\-oriented evaluation in applications requiring consistent predictive performance\.

## [Balay\-Odao, Ejercito Mangawa: Artificial intelligence and academic integrity in nursing education: a thematic analysis of Filipino nurse educators’ perspectives](../publications/8f90f7a021f465563eaf.md)



\_AI and Society\_:1\-16\. forthcomingAs technology advances, artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational settings, raising important questions about its impact on learning and academic integrity\. This study describes the perspectives of Filipino nurse educators on the role of artificial intelligence in maintaining academic integrity\. A descriptive qualitative design was used, with a two\-phase data collection process employing purposive sampling\. In Phase 1, open\-ended online responses were collected via Google Forms from 23 nurse educators to elicit initial perspectives on AI and academic integrity\. In Phase 2, findings from the online responses informed a focus group discussion with 19 participants, enabling deeper exploration, clarification, and expansion of emerging issues\. Data from both phases were integrated and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six\-step thematic analysis framework\. Through iterative coding and theme development, 148 initial codes were generated, consolidated into 14 subthemes, and organized into four major themes: “Policy Gaps: Need for Agile Ethical Frameworks,” “Critical AI Literacy: Essential for Students and Educators,” “AI as a Double\-Edged Sword in Nursing Education,” and “Balancing AI Use and Human Learning\.” This study concludes that AI is a valuable educational tool but may compromise academic integrity and critical thinking, highlighting the need for institutional policies, ethical guidelines, and user training in higher education\. \(direct link \)

## [Danışman, Arkadaş, Asistan: Üniversite Öğrencilerinin Perspektifinden Yapay Zekânın Sosyo\-Bilişsel Rolü](../publications/8f9cce882d2a41e06f41.md)

Emine ARSLAN KILIÇOĞLU; Eda Sezerer Albayrak

Dijital dönüşüm sürecinin en dinamik unsurlarından biri olan Yapay Zekâ \(YZ\) teknolojileri, yükseköğretim ekosisteminde öğrenme ve sosyal etkileşim pratiklerini kökten dönüştürmektedir\. Bu çalışma, üniversite öğrencilerinin YZ teknolojileriyle kurdukları etkileşimi, bilişsel, duygusal ve etik boyutlarıyla fenomenolojik bir perspektiften incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Nitel araştırma yöntemiyle yürütülen çalışma kapsamında, kartopu örnekleme tekniği ile belirlenen farklı disiplinlerden 41 üniversite öğrencisiyle derinlemesine görüşmeler gerçekleştirilmiştir\. Tematik analiz sonucunda elde edilen bulgular, öğrencilerin YZ’yi salt teknik bir yazılımın ötesinde; akademik süreçlerini yöneten bir asistan, kararlarını rasyonalize eden bir danışman ve yalnızlık hissiyle baş etmelerine yardımcı olan bir arkadaş olarak konumlandırdıklarını ortaya koymuştur\. Araştırma sonuçları, öğrencilerin YZ deneyimlerinde &quot;araçsal bir mesafe&quot; ile &quot;sosyo\-duygusal bağlılık&quot; arasında paradoksal bir denge kurduklarını göstermektedir\. Katılımcılar bilgiye hızlı erişim ve zaman yönetimi gibi konularda YZ’nin verimlilik artırıcı etkisini vurgularken, aynı zamanda mahremiyet ihlalleri ve bilişsel körelme riskine dair ciddi etik kaygılar taşımaktadır\. Özellikle stres ve kriz anlarında YZ’nin &quot;yargılamayan bir muhatap&quot; olarak deneyimlenmesi, teknolojinin sosyo\-bilişsel bir ortak olarak hayatın merkezine yerleştiğini kanıtlamaktadır\. Bu bulgular, yükseköğretim kurumlarının YZ okuryazarlığını etik ve psikososyal boyutları da kapsayacak şekilde genişletmesi ve dijital etik müfredatlarını bu yeni insan\-makine ortaklığına göre yeniden yapılandırması gerektiğini göstermektedir\.

## [Single\-Cell Whole\-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual\-Cell Models](../publications/8f9ce30ebdcc49c584e7.md)

Xudong Liu; Bo Zhang; Kefei Zou; Ruikai Wan; Qiangyuan Zhu

Single\-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-enabled virtual\-cell models with scalable, gene\-level descriptions of cellular state\. Yet prevalent poly\(A\)\-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape\. Here, “single\-cell whole\-transcriptome detection” denotes sequencing\-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly\(A\)\-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias\. We compare RNA\-capture scope, transcript\-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions\. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models\. We then examine cell\-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models\. Total\-RNA assays reveal additional non\-coding RNAs, long\-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics\. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene\-count inputs requires matched, task\-specific model comparisons\. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions\. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held\-out samples while testing feature ablations, out\-of\-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes\. Together, high\-throughput poly\(A\)\-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth\.

## [Can Simple MRI Characteristics Predict Molecular Subgroups in Paediatric Medulloblastoma?](../publications/8fbe0c2269a723090187.md)

Nigel McGregor; Wilson Tao; J\. A\. Prat\-Matifoll; Robert Paul Goetti

INTRODUCTION: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant paediatric central nervous system \(CNS\) tumour and is classified using molecular subgroups: WNT, SHH and non\-WNT/non\-SHH\. Subgroup identification guides prognosis and treatment, but requires molecular testing, which is not universally available\. MRI is routine in assessment of CNS tumours, and the MRI characteristics may serve as surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subgrouping\. This study aims to use simple MRI surrogate markers identified by Perreault et al\., against local medulloblastoma cases and their final molecular outcome\. METHOD: Retrospective cohort study of paediatric medulloblastomas at a single tertiary children&\#x27;s hospital between January 2015 and October 2025\. MRI studies were reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a radiology registrar in consensus\. Tumours were classified by location \(cerebellar hemisphere, cerebellopontine angle/cerebellar peduncle \(CP/CPA\), or midline/fourth ventricle\) and enhancement pattern \(minimal/none = &lt; 10%, heterogeneous = 10%\-90%, solid = &gt; 90%\)\. Associations between MRI features and molecular subgroup were assessed\. RESULTS: Twenty\-two cases were analysed: SHH 22\.7% \(5/22\), WNT 13\.6% \(3/22\) and non\-WNT/non\-SHH 63\.7% \(14/22\)\. Most tumours were midline \(90\.9%\), with two hemispheric lesions and no CP/CPA\. Enhancement patterns were heterogeneous \(54\.5%\), solid \(36\.4%\) and minimal/none \(9\.1%\)\. Hemispheric location was associated with SHH tumours \(p = 0\.043\), and all WNT tumours demonstrated solid enhancement \(p = 0\.036\)\. No other statistically significant associations were identified\. CONCLUSION: MRI characteristics offer promising surrogate markers for medulloblastoma subtype\. The only strong predictor we found corresponding with Perreault et al\. is that hemispheric lesions are correlated with SHH\-activated medulloblastoma\. This supports further investigation of MRI markers as non\-invasive and preoperative medulloblastoma subgroup prediction\.

## [Debates about the IT work of the future at Faculty of Exact Sciences, UNICEN](../publications/8fd56657017e946738fb.md)

Joaquín Ezequiel Palacios; Claudio Aciti

El presente trabajo sistematiza los debates surgidos en la jornada organizada por la Facultad de Ciencias Exactas \(UNICEN\), donde especialistas de diversos sectores de la comunidad informática analizaron las transformaciones derivadas del auge de la Inteligencia Artificial \(IA\)\. Los disertantes trataron los impactos de las nuevas tecnologías en el trabajo informático, los nuevos perfiles y nuevas posibilidades que se abren a partir de ello, los impactos en la formación y las nuevas demandas educativas, las cuestiones éticas que aparecen cómo corolario de su uso, y el impacto que tienen estas tecnologías en la soberanía nacional\. En el presente trabajo se desarrollan los puntos tratados en la disertación, y se elaboran algunas reflexiones alrededor de esas temáticas, con el foco puesto en la necesidad de que los espacios de encuentro y diálogo conduzcan a un consenso de planificación para el desarrollo nacional de una industria estratégica de gran importancia\.
