## [Uluslararası öğrenci algıları: Kalıpyargı içerikleri, rekabet ve sosyal yakınlaşma](../publications/8fdaef1262b2ce23ea6e.md)

Şeydanur TEZCAN ÖZER

Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de artan uluslararası öğrenci çeşitliliği bağlamında kampüs toplulukları arasındaki karşılıklı algıları Kalıpyargı İçerikleri Modeli \(KİM\) çerçevesinde incelemektedir\. Araştırmanın amacı, farklı ulusal gruplara yönelik sevecenlik ve yetkinlik algılarının, sosyal yakınlaşma eğilimini ne ölçüde yordadığını ortaya koymaktır\. Karabük Üniversitesi’nde yürütülen kesitsel, nicel ve ilişkisel tasarım kapsamında 498 katılımcıdan veri toplanmıştır\. Analizlerde tek yönlü varyans analizi \(ANOVA\) ve post\-hoc testlerinin yanı sıra korelasyon ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon yöntemleri kullanılmıştır\. Bulgular, KİM ile uyumlu biçimde, sevecenlik algısının tüm ulusal gruplar için sosyal yakınlaşmanın en güçlü ve tutarlı yordayıcısı olduğunu göstermektedir\. Yetkinlik algısının yordayıcı gücü ise hedef gruba göre farklılaşmıştır\. Ortadoğulu öğrenciler, Türkler ve Uzakdoğulular için yetkinlik algısı sosyal yakınlaşmayı anlamlı biçimde yordarken; Afrikalı öğrenciler ile Türk Cumhuriyetleri vatandaşlarına yönelik sosyal yakınlaşmada yetkinlik algısının etkisi sınırlı kalmıştır\. Türk Cumhuriyetleri öğrencileri, yüksek sevecenlik algılarıyla öne çıkan gruplardan biri olurken; Afrikalı öğrenciler özellikle sevecenlik boyutunda olumlu bir profil sergilemiştir\. Elde edilen bulgular, kampüs bağlamında sosyal yakınlaşmanın öncelikle ilişkisel ve duygusal değerlendirmeler üzerinden şekillendiğini, bilişsel yeterlik atıflarının ise bağlama duyarlı bir rol üstlendiğini göstermektedir\. Çalışma, gruplar arası algıların sabit grup özelliklerinden ziyade, sosyal etkileşimlerin niteliğiyle biçimlenen ilişkisel örüntüler sergilediğine işaret etmekte; üniversite ortamlarında olumlu temas ve sevecenliği güçlendiren uygulamaların sosyal yakınlaşmayı destekleyebileceğini ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Integrating MaxEnt and explainable AI to assess habitat suitability and conservation gaps of Przewalski&\#x27;s gazelle \(Procapra przewalskii\) in the Qinghai Lake region](../publications/8fe30ae47f124400ec25.md)

Fan Guo; Feng Jiang; Pengfei Song; Xunchao Zhang; Qichao WEI; Shuai Wang; Chengbo Liang; Haifeng Gu; Bin Li; Meng Zhang; Tongzuo Zhang; Zhenyuan Cai

Habitat suitability assessment and conservation gap identification are critical for endangered species conservation\. Using Przewalski&\#x27;s gazelle \(Procapra przewalskii\), an endangered ungulate endemic to China, we assessed habitat suitability, key environmental predictors, and conservation gaps in the Qinghai Lake region\. Based on 1597 field occurrence records collected from 2020 to 2025, we integrated the Maximum Entropy \(MaxEnt\) model with explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\), including SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) and Partial Dependence Plots \(PDPs\), and GAP analysis\. The selected MaxEnt model showed high discriminatory ability within the surveyed region \(mean test AUC = 0\.972 ± 0\.003\)\. The Human Influence Index \(HII\), mean temperature and precipitation of the driest quarter, elevation, and vegetation type were key predictors associated with habitat suitability, while mean diurnal range and HII had the highest mean SHAP importance\. Suitable habitats were concentrated around Qinghai Lake and in the northern Gonghe Basin\. The Qinghai Lake Basin represented the current core distribution area, whereas the Gonghe Basin contained extensive currently predicted suitable habitat and may represent an important conservation opportunity\. GAP analysis showed that 71\.83% of suitable habitat and 52\.34% of the current distribution range lay outside the protected\-area boundaries assessed in this study\. Fence occurrence in the Hubei population area was significantly associated with relatively high predicted habitat suitability and showed marked spatial clustering\. These findings provide spatially explicit evidence for protected\-area optimization and habitat management of Przewalski&\#x27;s gazelle\.

## [Deep Learning for Skin Cancer Classification Using Data Augmentation and Pre\-Trained CNN Models](../publications/8fe858cc305ed2130ffb.md)

Pa Pa Min; Fang Yong Lim; Jashila Nair Mogan; Astie Darmayantie

Skin cancer is one of the most common forms of cancer worldwide, and its early detection is critical for effective treatment and improved survival rates\. In recent years, advancements in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), particularly deep learning, have shown great promise in enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis\. This study aims to develop a non\-invasive, AI\-powered diagnostic system for the early detection and classification of skin cancer using dermoscopic images\. The proposed approach leverages deep learning techniques to automatically recognize and differentiate between various types of skin lesions, including both malignant and benign cases\. The project focuses on the end\-to\-end development of this system, beginning with the acquisition and preprocessing of a publicly available dataset of annotated skin lesion images\. The images undergo enhancement and normalization processes to improve model performance\. Pre\-trained Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\) architecture is designed and trained to classify the lesions based on visual features\. The model’s performance is evaluated using an independent validation set\. By providing a reliable and accessible screening tool, this work aims to support dermatologists in early diagnosis and decision\-making, potentially reducing the burden on healthcare systems and improving patient care\. The study demonstrates the potential of integrating deep learning into medical diagnostics for skin cancer, paving the way for future research and clinical implementation\.

## [Accuracy, Usefulness, and Expert\-Perceived Clinical Impact of Response Variability in ChatGPT\-4o for Hyperlipidemia\-Related Questions](../publications/8feeac86563e5092bb56.md)

Sharmon P\. Osae; Robin L\. Southwood; Devin L\. Lavender; Rebecca H\. Stone; Sarah Grace White; Russ H\. Palmer; Richard Lamb; Lorenzo Villa Zapata; Joshua Caballero

ChatGPT\-4o, an advanced Artificial Intelligence based large language model, has demonstrated utility for providing medical information\. Data regarding its accuracy and usefulness for hyperlipidemia pharmacotherapy are limited\. Additionally, the clinical implications of variability in responses generated from simultaneous identical prompts across multiple sessions remains poorly understood\. This research aimed to \(1\) assess accuracy, \(2\) evaluate usefulness, and \(3\) examine perceived impact variability of ChatGPT\-4o generated responses to hyperlipidemia\-related clinical questions\. Five questions addressing hyperlipidemia management and patient counseling were developed\. Responses to the questions were collected simultaneously from three independent ChatGPT\-4o sessions initiated in separate, newly opened ChatGPT windows\. A modified Delphi technique using clinical pharmacy faculty evaluated responses for accuracy, usefulness, and impact variability\. Scores were evaluated using a 3\-point Likert scale\. After initial scoring, responses were collected, collated, and redistributed to faculty for review and optional revision\. Final evaluations and consensus were facilitated by a moderator during a virtual panel\. Consensus was reached for all responses\. Evaluations of response accuracy ranged from poor to good, while usefulness ranged between somewhat useful and very useful\. Impact variability ranged from none to high across responses, which faculty concluded could impact patient management\. Response variability may have potential clinical implications; however, the present study evaluated expert\-perceived potential impact rather than actual patient outcomes\. Users should be aware concurrently generated ChatGPT responses can differ in accuracy and usefulness\. Clinical judgment and patient\-centered multidisciplinary collaboration remain essential\. Future directions include using a larger data set to corroborate findings\.

## [Plasma microbial cell\-free DNA metagenomic sequencing for early detection of infection after liver transplantation: a prospective cohort study](../publications/9003986794bf49ceb9b0.md)

Yongseop Lee; Eun‐Ki Min; Yu Jin Park; Deok\-Gie Kim; Dong Jin Joo; Myoung Soo Kim; Saeam Shin; Seung\-Tae Lee; Jae Geun Lee; Su Jin Jeong

Introduction Microbial cell\-free DNA \(mcfDNA\) metagenomic next\-generation sequencing \(mNGS\) is a promising technique for diagnosing infectious diseases\. However, research on mcfDNA\-based mNGS for diagnosing infections in liver transplantation \(LT\) recipients remains limited\. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of plasma mcfDNA mNGS during the early post\-LT period\. Methods In this prospective diagnostic cohort study, adult LT recipients underwent plasma mcfDNA mNGS on postoperative days 7 and 14\. The findings were compared with results of the blood cultures and other conventional microbiological tests at the species level\. Results Among 193 LT recipients, mNGS positivity was observed in 14\.5% on day 7 and 21\.8% on day 14\. The concordance between mNGS and blood culture for bacterial pathogens was modest on days 7 \(35\.0%\) and 14 \(14\.3%\) but increased substantially when other clinically relevant specimens were included \(80\.0% and 71\.4%, respectively\)\. mNGS identified additional pathogens not detected using blood culture in 59\.3% and 74\.2% of cases on days 7 and 14, respectively\. Viral pathogens, including cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, varicella\-zoster virus, and roseolovirus, were also detected\. Among the 13 discordant cases \(blood culture\-positive and mNGS\-negative\), two \(15\.4%\) were classified as contamination/colonization, five \(38\.5%\) as weak positives, and six \(46\.2%\) as not detected by mNGS\. Conclusion Plasma mcfDNA mNGS demonstrated substantial concordance with conventional microbiological testing when clinically relevant specimens were considered\. mNGS may serve as a useful adjunct tool for early pathogen detection and clinical assessment of LT recipients\.

## [Higher intraoperative arterial\-to\-end\-tidal carbon dioxide gradients are associated with postoperative respiratory morbidity after lung cancer resection: a retrospective INSPIRE cohort study](../publications/901a5d27495d8046ff40.md)

Long Li; Dan Wang; Qingyi Zhou; Bin Shang

Background The arterial\-to\-end\-tidal carbon dioxide gradient may reflect impaired gas exchange during thoracic surgery\. We examined its association with postoperative respiratory morbidity after lung cancer resection\. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using INSPIRE version 1\.4\.2\. Each intraoperative arterial carbon dioxide \(PaCO 2 \) measurement was paired with the nearest positive end\-tidal carbon dioxide \(EtCO 2 \) measurement within 10 min, and the primary exposure was each patient&\#x27;s median gradient\. Respiratory morbidity was defined from new respiratory diagnoses and qualifying postoperative ventilation records during the index admission\. We used multivariable regression, repeated\-measurement analyses, sensitivity analyses, and exploratory internally validated prediction models\. Results Among 2,665 eligible patients, 85 \(3\.2%\) had respiratory morbidity\. A valid gradient was available in 2,527 patients; the primary complete\-case analysis included 2,436 patients and 80 events\. Each 5 mmHg higher gradient was associated with greater morbidity \(adjusted odds ratio 1\.53, 95% confidence interval 1\.17–2\.00; adjusted risk ratio 1\.48, 1\.14–1\.91\)\. Standardised risk increased from 2\.28% at the first gradient quartile to 3\.46% at the third, a difference of 1\.18 percentage points \(0\.49–1\.83\)\. In a post hoc comparison, adding the gradient to a model already containing PaCO 2 and clinical covariates did not materially change internally cross\-validated discrimination \(AUROC 0\.7324 vs\. 0\.7325\)\. Conclusion A higher intraoperative PaCO 2 –EtCO 2 gradient was associated with postoperative respiratory morbidity after lung cancer resection, but its incremental prognostic value beyond PaCO 2 was limited in exploratory analyses\. Prospective external validation is required before clinical use\.

## [Endoscopic therapy for gastrointestinal bleeding in Klippel–Trénaunay syndrome: a case report and literature review](../publications/901d0800eeaeefd80f23.md)

Ruoxi Zhang; Wen Shi; Xi Wu; Aiming Yang; Yang Chen

Background Klippel–Trénaunay syndrome \(KTS\) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly characterized by capillary malformation, underlying low\-flow venous/lymphatic malformations, and bone\- and/or soft\-tissue limb hypertrophy of the affected extremity\. At present, there is no consensus on the optimal management of KTS, particularly in the context of gastrointestinal bleeding\. Case presentation We describe a case of gastrointestinal bleeding in a patient with KTS who presented with colorectal venous malformations with phleboliths, multiple splenic vascular malformations, penile varicosities, and hypertrophy of the right lower extremity and the right buttock\. A colonoscopy revealed a circumferential mucosal elevation with bluish discoloration extending from 15 cm above the anal verge in the colorectum, and active bleeding was observed at 12 cm from the anal verge\. Endoscopic submucosal sclerotherapy with 1–1\.5 mL of lauromacrogol \(1%\) per site and a total volume of 30 mL, combined with band ligation using six bands, was performed\. This approach has rarely been reported and resulted in significant relief from bleeding\. At the 6\-month follow\-up, the patient&\#x27;s symptoms and hemoglobin levels remained stable, with no other complications\. Conclusion Although KTS remains incurable, early endoscopic recognition facilitates diagnosis, and endoscopic therapy may serve as an important treatment modality for gastrointestinal involvement\.

## [Sustainable Materials for Reducing the Environmental Footprint of Artificial Intelligence Data Centers in the United States](../publications/9029758f2a0230f0355f.md)

R\. Gandhimathi

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is expanding data\-centre infrastructure in the United States, increasing demand for electricity, cooling water, semiconductor materials and electronic equipment\. This review examines how sustainable materials and integrated engineering strategies may reduce environmental pressures across the AI data\-centre life cycle\. It considers operational energy demand, greenhouse\-gas emissions, direct and indirect water consumption, critical\-material requirements, thermal management, renewable\-energy integration, storage technologies and end\-of\-life equipment management\. High\-thermal\-conductivity materials, electrically insulating ceramics, thermal\-interface composites and phase\-change materials can support heat transfer and temperature control\. Direct\-to\-chip liquid cooling and immersion cooling offer additional options for high\-density computing, although material compatibility, leakage, toxicity, durability and recyclability require careful assessment\. Renewable electricity can be complemented by supercapacitors, lithium\-based batteries, redox\-flow systems, hydrogen and thermal storage, with technology selection guided by the timescale of power demand\. Measures such as modular design, longer server service life, repair, component reuse and recovery of critical materials may reduce embodied impacts and electronic waste\. The review emphasises that improvements in one environmental metric can increase burdens elsewhere, particularly across the energy–water–carbon nexus\. Accordingly, the assessment of sustainable AI infrastructure requires a life\-cycle perspective, transparent facility\-level reporting, responsible material sourcing and coordination between materials engineering, electricity supply, cooling design and circular management\. No individual material or technology is sufficient to address these interdependent impacts\.

## [Dendrimers for Solubility Enhancement of Poorly Soluble Drugs: A Comprehensive Analysis of Key Determinants, Molecular Properties, and Formulation Challenges](../publications/902be23ca2348dcccaba.md)



Poor aqueous solubility remains a significant obstacle in the development and clinical translation of many promising drug candidates, limiting their absorption, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy\.In recent years, dendrimers have emerged as a novel and highly adaptable class of nanocarriers capable of enhancing the solubility of poorly water\-soluble drugs through multiple mechanisms\.These synthetic, hyperbranched, and monodisperse macromolecules offer a well\-defined architecture, consisting of a central core, iterative internal branching layers, and terminal functional groups\.Such structural precision allows for fine\-tuning of dendrimer properties to achieve optimal drug\-carrier compatibility and solubility enhancement\.This review provides a comprehensive exploration of the structural attributes of dendrimers, focusing on core architecture, generation level, surface functionality, and internal cavities, and their direct implications on drug solubilization capacity\.Particular emphasis is placed on understanding how the dendrimer generation and molecular weight influence encapsulation efficiency and solubilization performance\.The solubility\-enhancing mechanisms, including encapsulation, surface adsorption, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic complexation, and covalent conjugation, are thoroughly discussed\.Additionally, case studies of various drug, dendrimer formulations are presented to demonstrate their practical relevance and effectiveness\.Despite their significant potential, challenges such as generation\-dependent cytotoxicity, synthetic complexity, and regulatory uncertainty continue to hinder the broader clinical adoption of dendrimeric systems\.The review also highlights recent innovations in dendrimer design, such as biodegradable constructs, stimuliresponsive systems, and ligand\-functionalized carriers, that aim to overcome these limitations\.By addressing current gaps and future prospects, this review underscores the strategic role of dendrimers in transforming solubility\-limited drug development pipelines and facilitating the formulation of next\-generation therapeutics\.

## [HIF\-1α–Nrf2 crosstalk in myocardial ischemia–reperfusion injury: a potential preconditioning\-responsive protective network](../publications/90324cebbebfd48c0c33.md)

Xiaoqiang Guo; Chaojie Wang; 张舒岩; Mengqi Li; Chen Chen

Myocardial ischemia–reperfusion injury \(MIRI\) is a dynamic pathological process in which metabolic and mitochondrial disturbances during ischemia predispose the myocardium to oxidative damage upon reperfusion\. This temporal coupling poses a fundamental limitation to single\-pathway cardioprotection, as interventions directed at one stage of injury may fail to adequately address the evolving pathophysiological cascade\. Hypoxia\-inducible factor\-1 α \(HIF\-1 α \) and nuclear factor erythroid 2\-related factor 2 \(Nrf2\), key regulators of hypoxic adaptation and cellular redox homeostasis, respectively, may constitute an interconnected protective network that spans the ischemia–reperfusion transition\. HIF\-1 α promotes metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial adaptation during ischemia, thereby reducing oxidative susceptibility, whereas Nrf2 enhances glutathione metabolism, peroxide detoxification, and resistance to lipid peroxidation during reperfusion\. Emerging evidence further suggests the possibility of reciprocal crosstalk between these pathways, with HIF\-1 α reported to facilitate Nrf2 activation and Nrf2 to support HIF\-1 α transcriptional availability and protein stability\. This coupling may enable preconditioning to establish metabolic and mitochondrial adaptation before ischemia while simultaneously building an antioxidant defense reserve for reperfusion, while sustained metabolic adaptation during early reperfusion provides transitional support for the recovery of oxidative metabolism, thereby limiting secondary oxidative injury\. Compared with isolated pathway activation, coordinated HIF\-1 α –Nrf2 regulation may therefore provide broader and more temporally integrated cardioprotection by simultaneously reducing oxidative susceptibility and enhancing resistance to reperfusion stress\. Pharmacological and non\-pharmacological preconditioning studies further support the therapeutic potential of this network\-based strategy, highlighting HIF\-1 α –Nrf2 crosstalk as a promising framework for optimizing cardioprotection in MIRI\.

## [Microencapsulation of sardine fish oil using different molecular weight chitosan and polymer blends: a comparative study on oxidative stability and encapsulation characteristics](../publications/9033b9b91b85b315f173.md)

A\. Jeyakumari; Vinod Abhiroop; K\. Elavarasan

Fish oil is a valuable source of long\-chain omega\-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids; however, it is more prone to oxidative degradation which limits its incorporation into food and nutraceutical products\. Microencapsulation offers an effective strategy to protect these bioactive lipids by creating a physical barrier against environmental stressors\. In the present study, low\- and medium\-molecular\-weight chitosan, in combination with bovine gelatin and maltodextrin, were evaluated as wall materials for encapsulation of sardine fish oil by spray drying\. The four different sardine fish oil emulsion formulations \(SE1–SE4\) were prepared and spray dried\. The resulting microencapsulates were stored under both ambient and refrigerated conditions, and their oxidative stability was monitored for 21 days\. The moisture content of the encapsulated powders ranged from 2\.49 to 4\.23%, while encapsulation efficiency varied between 53\.26 and 82\.06%\. Powder flow characteristics differed significantly \(p&lt;0\.05\) among the formulations, with SE3 exhibiting the most desirable flow properties, as indicated by the lowest Carr’s Index \(26\.93\) and Hausner ratio \(1\.37\)\. Storage studies further demonstrated that SE3 provided superior protection against lipid oxidation under both storage conditions, as evidenced by lower thiobarbituric acid reactive substances \(TBARS\) values throughout the storage period\. The findings highlighted that among the formulations evaluated, medium\-molecular\-weight chitosan in combination with bovine gelatin, maltodextrin and fish oil \(0\.5%\) produced microencapsulates showed enhanced encapsulation efficiency, improved powder characteristics, and greater resistance to oxidative deterioration\. These results suggested that sardine fish oil encapsulates prepared in the study possess significant potential for the formulation of stable omega\-3\-enriched functional foods and nutraceutical products\.

## [Who is in the data? Demographic and geographic reporting in public datasets used to develop artificial intelligence for neurosurgery: protocol for a meta\-research audit](../publications/90382c0aad07f704bb8c.md)

Omar Farghal; Mohammad Al\-Darawsheh; Mohammad Telfah; Leen Basha

Protocol for a cross\-sectional meta\-research audit of how public datasets used to develop artificial intelligence \(AI\) for neurosurgery report patient demographics and data origin\. The frame comprises 110 datasets: the 84 unique datasets catalogued by Chan et al\. \(J Clin Med 2025\) and 26 pre\-specified, widely used datasets\. Fourteen items are extracted from each descriptor paper, including age, sex, race/ethnicity, socioeconomic status, country of data origin and inclusion of children\. A large language model produced a first\-pass extraction with verbatim quotes\. Two investigators verify every item independently and reconcile any disagreements, and two further reviewers double\-extract a random 20% sample\. Countries are mapped to World Bank income groups\. This record time\-stamps the protocol, codebook, sampling frame and analysis code before human verification began\. The AI outputs and verification workbooks are withheld until verification is complete, to keep the second reviewers blind\.

## [An open\-source, physics\-aware, data\-driven tool for automated particle image velocimetry post\-processing](../publications/903d2cf154f6b46f123c.md)

Arefe Ghazi Nezami; Blair Johnson; Joseph P\. Vantassel

Particle image velocimetry \(PIV\) is a powerful diagnostic tool for analyzing the properties and structures of laminar and turbulent flows\. Modern PIV systems provide high spatial and temporal resolution measurements, often generating hundreds of gigabytes of raw data\. Before these data can be used for flow analysis, they must be post\-processed to identify and remove erroneous velocity vectors\. Post\-processing techniques typically require substantial manual intervention by highly trained analysts, making the process tedious, time\-consuming, and inherently subjective\. To address these challenges, we developed a physics\-aware, data\-driven framework for automated PIV post\-processing\. Our machine learning\-based tool, PIVPostProcess, employs an ensemble of gradient\-boosted decision trees trained on real experimental PIV datasets and is validated using direct numerical simulation data with synthetic noise\. The fully trained model achieves excellent performance, with an F1 score—a performance metric that combines precision and recall—of 0\.991 on the testing dataset\. To evaluate generalization beyond the training distribution, we apply the model to six additional experimental datasets featuring previously unseen flow fields\. The model achieves a mean F1 score of 0\.990 across tested experimental datasets, demonstrating robust predictive capability\. Importantly, this automated technique processes each dataset significantly faster compared to manual post\-processing\. By substantially reducing processing time while maintaining high accuracy, this tool accelerates and standardizes PIV vector validation approaches\.

## [Trust in artificial intelligence at the bedside: a qualitative interview study with neonatologists](../publications/905781c5f9129363b61d.md)

Lotte Schuitmaker; Jojanneke Drogt; Sarah Dewi Hartman; Karin Rolanda Jongsma

Abstract Background Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) promises to improve patient outcomes, increase efficiency, and reduce healthcare costs\. While AI has demonstrated success in imaging fields like radiology, its application is expanding into other data\-rich medical domains, including neonatology\. Nonetheless, a disparity persists between technical advancements of AI and its practical use in clinical care\. A significant obstacle for integrating these systems into bedside decision\-making is physicians’ difficulty in determining when AI can reasonably be trusted\. Methods We explored the perspectives of neonatologists at a Dutch academic hospital on trust in AI via in\-depth, semi\-structured interviews \( n = 17\)\. Thematic analysis was used to identify key themes\. Results Three overarching themes emerged: \(1\) Trusting AI in practice, \(2\) Maintaining control over trusted AI systems, and \(3\) Limits of trust\. Overall, AI in neonatal clinical settings was welcomed\. The concept of trust was delineated as being distinct from that of confidence and reliance\. For trusting AI, it was deemed important that AI’s role would be supplemental to the role of the physician\. Also, AI validation and adequate oversight were considered essential for physicians’ trust\. Preserving human expertise while working with AI in clinical settings was deemed important\. Concerns about overreliance and incompatibility of clinical intuition with AI in practice were frequently mentioned as reasons to lose trust in AI\. Conclusion This study offers practical insights into how trust in medical AI is conceptualized by neonatologists and highlights key considerations for its acceptance\. Clarifying what is expected of physicians in terms of reliance on AI at the bedside and formulating concrete guidance for trust in AI is recommended\. Trial registration Not applicable\. The research protocol was reviewed by the research quality control committee of the University Medical Center Utrecht and was deemed exempt from the Medical Research Involving Humans Act \(research proposal no\. 23U0364\)\.

Henry Kautz

Abstract Even while AI based on large language models makes enormous advances, many AI researchers and pundits argue that it LLMs are an inadequate basis for AI because they do not support exact logical and probabilistic reasoning\. ## [BridgeAfford: Bridging Query\-Target Gap for Generalizable 3D Affordance Grounding](../publications/90796cab4a62d544b380.md)

Yijie Su; Yakun Zhu; Yi Bin; Pengpeng Zeng; Liang Chen; Guoqing Wang; Jingkuan Song; Heng Tao Shen

Language\-guided 3D affordance grounding aims to localize functional regions on 3D objects according to interaction intents\. However, existing methods exhibit poor generalization to unseen objects\. One challenge is the query\-target gap: a semantic discrepancy between query features encoding interaction intents and target\-region features, leading to inaccurate grounding\. End\-to\-end training favors query representations tailored to seen objects, limiting their compatibility with shifted target\-region features on unseen objects\. To address this issue, we propose BridgeAfford, a framework that reduces the query\-target semantic gap from two complementary perspectives\. First, Interaction Region Alignment \(IRA\) promotes cross\-object alignment among geometrically similar interaction regions during training\. This enables structures on unseen objects that resemble previously observed ones to produce representations similar to those learned during training, facilitating target\-region recognition\. Second, Visual Evidence Aggregation \(VEA\) leverages a 2D affordance model to refine the attention distribution and guide the query toward the correct region, yielding more target\-aware queries\. Extensive experiments on the LASO and PIAD datasets demonstrate that BridgeAfford outperforms existing methods, particularly on unseen objects, highlighting its robust generalization ability\.

## [INCRETIN\-BASED THERAPIES AND DEMENTIA: RECONCILING EPIDEMIOLOGICAL PREVENTION SIGNALS WITH NEGATIVE DISEASE\-MODIFYING TRIALS IN EARLY SYMPTOMATIC ALZHEIMER&\#x27;S DISEASE](../publications/907f2da437c66b8dd65c.md)

Joao Fernandes Floriano; María Elizabeth Menezes

Glucagon\-like peptide\-1 receptor agonists \(GLP\-1RAs\) and dual glucose\-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide \(GIP\)/GLP\-1 receptor agonism have been proposed as candidate interventions against cognitive decline\. This structured critical review appraises clinical, epidemiological, pharmacological and biomarker evidence through 23 September 2026 and examines why favourable prevention signals diverge from negative disease\-modification trials\. Pooled cardiovascular\-trial data and a later, partly overlapping randomized\-trial meta\-analysis suggest fewer dementia events, recorded as secondary or safety outcomes, with GLP\-1RAs, whereas target\-trial emulations remain vulnerable to channelling, surveillance and residual confounding\. A quantitative E\-value sensitivity analysis shows marked variation in robustness across key observational estimates, from weak confidence\-bound robustness in several comparisons to effect estimates so large as to be causally implausible and compatible with structural bias\. In EVOKE and EVOKE\+ \(n=3,808\), oral semaglutide did not slow Clinical Dementia Rating\-Sum of Boxes progression at 104 weeks despite modest changes in cerebrospinal\-fluid Alzheimer\-related biomarkers\. The phase 2b liraglutide trial in AD and the phase 3 exenatide trial in Parkinson&\#x27;s disease were also negative on their primary outcomes\. We compare four competing explanations \(disease stage, insufficient central exposure, confounded epidemiology and indirect vascular mediation\) and specify evidence capable of discriminating among them\. We further formalize a hypothesis\-generating, stage\-dependent Metabolic Window Hypothesis with explicit predictions and refutation conditions, and propose a Precision Incretin\-Neurodegeneration Framework as a provisional operational scaffold for biomarker\-stratified research\. Neither semaglutide nor tirzepatide is an established therapy for preventing or treating Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease or dementia\.

## [AI Behind the Adult, Not in Front of the Child: A Design Framework for Adult\-Mediated AI in Early Childhood](../publications/9081a454b90bb2df6be7.md)

Elif Öztürk

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) in education has largely been positioned as a child\-facing tutor, conversational agent, or content\-delivery system\. In early childhood, this orientation warrants particular caution because executive functions, self\-regulation, and social\-emotional competencies develop through responsive relationships, play, embodied experience, and co\-regulation with adults\. This theory\-informed conceptual design study addressed three questions: which developmental, pedagogical, and ethical principles should structure AI use in early childhood; how these principles can be translated into a system architecture; and what validation pathway is required before such a system can make defensible claims\. Drawing on four evidence streams \(executive\-function and social\-emotional development, ecological and embodied learning, human\-centered AI ethics, and measurement and implementation science\), the study proposes the Behind\-the\-Adult AI framework, an adult\-mediated design framework initially specified for children aged 4–6 years\. Six design principles were derived and operationalized in a layered architecture: brief, bounded, non\-conversational digital developmental tasks generate behavioral indicators under transparent adaptation rules; a provisional, non\-diagnostic profile organizes longitudinal information; and AI operates only behind the adult, synthesizing observations from center, home, and school into hypotheses for human review\. A five\-stage validation pathway with explicit decision gates separates design claims from evidence claims\. The paper argues that developmentally responsible AI in early childhood should be evaluated not by how convincingly it replaces human interaction but by how effectively it strengthens the adults and environments surrounding the child, and it offers a transferable design heuristic for researchers, developers, and policymakers\.

## [Radiation\-Induced Esophagitis: From Clinical Observation to Precision Management](../publications/9086f95e69e9e2ff3ee7.md)

Yaqi Song; Biao Gu; Gang Ma; 宋旭东; Wubi Zhou; Changsong Xu; Honglei Luo; Jingjing Dai

For the past seven decades, radiation\-induced esophagitis \(RE\) has been a major dose\-limiting acute toxicity of thoracic radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients&\#x27; quality of life and their ability to complete planned treatment courses\. Research on RE has progressed from phenomenological reporting to multidimensional quantification and, more recently, toward precision\-driven intervention\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current research on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, predictive modeling, prevention, and treatment of radiation\-induced esophagitis\. Dose\-volume parameters established an important quantitative framework for risk assessment, while more recent advances in genomic profiling, functional imaging, and artificial intelligence have supported the development of integrative multi\-omics predictive models\. Pharmacological prophylaxis has shown limited success in randomized trials, whereas technical refinements in radiation delivery and emerging regenerative approaches offer promising alternatives\. Persistent knowledge gaps remain, including the need for prospective multicenter validation of omics\-derived models, re\-evaluation of RE risk in the immunotherapy era, investigation of chronomodulated treatment scheduling, and translation of tissue\-engineering strategies into clinical practice\. The review is intended to provide clinicians and investigators with a comprehensive reference and to support future research in thoracic radiation oncology\.

## [A Student\-Centered Model for Ethically Evaluating AI Integration in Learning Support Services and Beyond](../publications/908aad9011206fc7e8f0.md)

Cristina Caputo; Bruels, Raymond, III; Alexis Rivera

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) reshapes higher education, learning support centers are uniquely positioned to intentionally assess whether if and how to best integrate AI tools into academic services\. This session presents a 6\-week project framework that was designed to: • Review the literature on critical AI literacy and training • Benchmark current best practices in AI policy, use, and integration alongside human\-centered academic services • Examine student AI knowledge and use \(needs assessment\) • Identify and evaluate relevant AI tools or platforms The framework was developed within the Academic Success Center \(ASC\) at Nevada State University where Center peer educators \(student employees\) served as project leads and evaluators\. This model offers a practical, research\-informed pathway for institutions seeking to lead responsibly in AI\-integrated learning support or other student services\. Session activities include a walkthrough and discussion of the model structure, tools, challenges, and recommendations\. Attendees will leave with: \(1\) a sample 6\-week project roadmap, \(2\) a student\-centered model for AI evaluation and pilot design, \(3\) learning frameworks grounded in critical AI literacy, \(4\) adaptable resources for assessment and decision\-making, and \(5\) strategies for positioning students as co\-creators in institutional/unit change

## [A Neural Processing Unit\-Accelerated Monocular Perception Pipeline for Remotely Operated Underwater Vehicle Station Keeping](../publications/9090e41dbedf5a5f9fcc.md)

Gyan Louisin; Vinh La The; Trung Ngo Lam; Nga Nguyen Thi Thanh; Dung Nguyen Anh; Duc Dương Minh; Hiep Hoang Van

Holding a stable viewpoint is a prerequisite for observation tasks performed by remotely operated underwater vehicles, yet it is difficult to achieve when the only sensor is a monocular camera and all computation must run on board\. This work reports the deployment of a complete visual stationkeeping perception pipeline on a Qualcomm QCS8550 platform using its Hexagon HTP/NPU accelerator, in which two networks\-\-\-an INT8 object detector and a dense monocular depth model\-\-\-share a single accelerator\. A per\-stage latency breakdown shows that the throughput difference between an accelerated and a CPU\-executed configuration is attributable to one stage: moving depth inference alone to the accelerator makes it 27 times faster and carries the pipeline from 0\.46 to 8\.47 frames per second, with depth inference still occupying two thirds of the frame budget afterwards and the accelerator occupied at least 69\\% of wall\-clock time\. We document two deployment failure modes that are silent rather than loud: an output polarity that must be established empirically, and a normalisation choice that destroys the range signal\. The two available range cues are combined by an analytic fusion rule\-\-\-the square root of the tracked bounding box area and the depth output both vary inversely with distance, so the two are directly combinable once anchored on a reference captured at target selection, without training data or knowledge of the target dimensions\. On the rigid targets evaluated here the zero\-cost geometric term carries more of the distance signal than the depth network that consumes two thirds of the frame budget, and the two cues degrade unequally on immersion, which makes their relative weighting an operating parameter rather than a constant\. Evaluation is open\-loop; closed\-loop validation was prevented by a degenerate thruster configuration\.

## [Inteligencia artificial, gestión aduanera y competitividad del comercio exterior mexicano \(2019\-2026\)](../publications/909c7250186d80e4addc.md)

Rubén Rodríguez Carrizal

Mexican customs services currently face persistent challenges in terms of time and efficiency: the Time Release Study conducted by Mexico&\#x27;s Tax Administration Service \(2019\) documented that, when goods are subject to physical\-documentary customs inspection, clearance time multiplies up to 14\-fold compared to an operation without inspection, reaching up to 218 hours at the port of Manzanillo\. This article aims to analyze, through a theoretical and documentary review, the role that artificial intelligence \(AI\) plays in the modernization of customs management and its potential impact on the competitiveness of Mexican foreign trade, given that such trade amounted to more than 369 billion dollars in exports during the first half of 2025\. The study draws on administrative modernization theory applied to customs management, which explains how the adoption of information technologies affects inspection, tax collection, and trade facilitation\. Methodologically, it is conducted through a qualitative, documentary, and descriptive study that draws on international organization reports, peer\-reviewed academic literature on the Mexican case, and official data from the Tax Administration Service\. Findings suggest that Mexico has a solid track record of customs technology modernization, but no public measurement currently isolates the specific effect of artificial intelligence on clearance times, which constitutes both a research gap and an opportunity to strengthen national customs competitiveness, as well as evidence of the need to create regulations to govern the use of AI in customs processes\.

## [Development and evaluation of eduvate CBT as an integrated artificial intelligence powered assessment ecosystem](../publications/90a37d5de9d8ea0074fd.md)

Peace Awofesobi; Obiseye Obiyemi

The growth of digital assessment has intensified concerns about examination integrity, grading efficiency, fairness, and responsible artificial intelligence \(AI\)\. This study evaluates Eduvate CBT, an integrated role\-based assessment ecosystem combining examination administration, AI\-assisted proctoring, automated objective grading, reviewable violation evidence, and learning analytics\. A four\-week quantitative evaluation covered 250 undergraduate examination sessions across four computing courses, with usability data from 15 instructors and 5 administrators\. At the session level, proctoring achieved 94\.8% accuracy \(95% CI 91\.3–96\.9\), 94\.6% precision, 96\.6% recall, and an F1\-score of 95\.6%\. Automated grading agreed with instructor consensus for 742 of 750 sampled responses \(98\.9%; 95% CI 97\.9–99\.5\) and processed the cohort in under 10 s, compared with an estimated 23\.1 h of manual grading\. The aggregate System Usability Scale score was 87\.4 \(SD = 5\.8; 95% CI 84\.7–90\.1\)\. Analytics identified six low\-performing items in algorithmic complexity, demonstrating how assessment evidence can prompt instructional review\. The findings support the feasibility of the integrated workflow, although generalisability is limited by the single\-institution design, absence of a competing\-system control, and unavailable formal inter\-rater reliability estimates\.

Alison Knopf

Congenital TORCH infections are known to injure the fetus, but little is known about their contribution to neurodevelopmental outcomes\. ## [Evaluating Educational Policy and Administration: A Weighted Scoring Method Analysis of Performance Dimensions](../publications/90b62d15a9cce9ca084d.md)

Mani Devipriya; M Ramachandran; Saravanan Libiya

This study evaluates education policy and management using the Weighted Scoring Method \(WSM\) across five domains: education leadership, management, administration, planning, and public education policy\. Four equally weighted dimensions—policy effectiveness, equity, collaboration, and student allocation—were considered\. The findings indicate that education planning ranked first with a priority score of 0\.72991, demonstrating excellent collaboration and equity performance\. Education management secured second place \(0\.70486\), reflecting balanced performance across the dimensions\. Education leadership ranked third \(0\.56527\), achieving the highest equity score but requiring improved collaboration\. Public education policy placed fourth \(0\.55337\), demonstrating strong policy effectiveness but weaker student allocation\. Educational administration ranked last \(0\.40102\), highlighting the need for comprehensive improvements\. The normalized data and weighted decision matrix identified the relative strengths and weaknesses of each domain\. the study emphasizes strengthening collaboration, promoting equitable resource distribution, and integrating policy effectiveness with efficient student allocation to improve educational governance and management\.

## [Learning Adaptation in Artificial Intelligence‐Enabled Nursing Education: A Network Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Literacy, Self‐Regulated Learning and Academic Resilience](../publications/90b73478e8d968470f46.md)

Xueqing Gong; Xiao Zemei; Dan Chen; Danyan Li; Xiahui Xiao

AIMS: To examine the interconnections among artificial intelligence literacy, self\-regulated learning strategies, and academic resilience in undergraduate nursing students, and to conduct an exploratory comparison of network characteristics between students with and without clinical practice experience\. DESIGN: A cross\-sectional survey\. METHODS: Using convenience sampling, 1784 undergraduate nursing students were recruited from five universities in Hunan Province, China, between March and May 2026\. Participants completed a demographic questionnaire and three validated scales\. Network analysis estimated node strength, bridge strength, and predictability\. Bootstrap procedures assessed network accuracy and stability, and the Network Comparison Test was used to conduct an exploratory comparison between students with and without clinical practice experience\. RESULTS: The 10\-node network contained 35 non\-zero edges and had a mean predictability of 62\.6%\. Artificial intelligence evaluation showed the highest node strength, followed jointly by monitoring learning strategies and cognitive maturity\. Evaluating and revising learning strategies showed the highest bridge strength, followed by cognitive maturity\. In the exploratory subgroup analysis, the overall network structure differed between students with and without clinical practice experience, whereas global strength did not\. CONCLUSIONS: Artificial intelligence evaluation, monitoring learning strategies and cognitive maturity showed relatively high node strength, whereas evaluating and revising learning strategies and cognitive maturity showed relatively high cross\-domain bridge strength\. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION: Findings may inform nursing curricula integrating artificial intelligence literacy, learning regulation, and academic adaptation\. IMPACT: This study addressed fragmented understanding of these capacities\. It identified dimensions with relatively high node strength and bridge strength, providing exploratory evidence for future nursing education research\. REPORTING METHOD: This study was reported in accordance with the STROBE statement\. NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not involve patients, service users, caregivers, or members of the public\.

## [Global Trends and Emerging Research Themes in Patient\-Reported and Patient\-Centered Outcomes after Cataract Surgery: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis](../publications/90c66832e4dbb24d751f.md)

Dilber Keskinel; Gülcan Dürüst Sakallı

BACKGROUND/AIMS:Research on cataract surgery outcomes has increasingly expanded beyond visual acuity to include visual function, quality of life, patient satisfaction, and other patient\-reported and patient\-centered outcomes\.This study aimed to examine global research trends and emerging themes in patient\-reported and patient\-centered outcomes following cataract surgery using bibliometric and science mapping methods\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A literature search was conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection on 11 September 2026 using the topic field\.Following document\-type screening, 2,704 article and review article publications were analyzed using the bibliometrix package in R\. Scientific production, citation characteristics, sources, authors, countries, institutions, collaboration patterns, keywords, and trend topics were evaluated\. RESULTS:The dataset comprised 2,704 publications from 472 sources published between 1980 and 2026\.The mean number of citations per document was 26\.42, the annual scientific production growth rate was 11\.57%, and the international co\-authorship rate was 22\.15%\.The United States was the most productive country \(n=477\); the University of London was the most productive institution \(n=271\); and Pesudovs K was the most productive author \(n=53\)\.Research themes progressed from visual outcomes and quality of life to visual function, patient satisfaction, spectacle independence, newer intraocular lens technologies, and patient\-reported outcome measures\.Psychometric properties and Rasch analysis were also prominent methodological themes\. CONCLUSION:Research on cataract surgery outcomes has demonstrated substantial growth and an expanding focus on patient\-reported and patient\-centered outcomes\.Standardized patient\-reported outcome measures and greater international, multicenter collaboration may strengthen future research in this field\.

## [Nonlinear pluggable optics: Digital signal processing\-free Intensity Modulated Direct Detection links using analog photonic Next Generation Reservoir Computing](../publications/90c929bb01be832798e2.md)

Nicholas Cox; Joseph Murray; Ross T\. Schermer; Shuo S\. Pang; Christopher Long; Gajadhar Joshi; Nicholas A\. Nobile; Raktim Sarma; Brandon Redding

In this work, we propose a Nonlinear Pluggable Optic \(NLPO\) transceiver that combines the low latency and low power consumption of Linear Pluggable Optics \(LPO\) with the range and robustness of digital signal processing \(DSP\)\-based transceivers\. The proposed NLPO uses an analog photonic Next\-Generation Reservoir Computing \(NGRC\) architecture, constructed on a photonic integrated circuit \(PIC\), to compensate for electrical\-domain distortions as well as optical\-channel impairments from chromatic dispersion and Kerr nonlinearity\. Focusing on a simulated 50 GBd PAM\-4 link, we find that the NGRC\-based NLPO not only extends the range of LPO, but actually outperforms DSP\-based solutions as well\. Our simulations reveal two key advantages compared to DSP\-based Intensity Modulation/Direct Detection \(IM/DD\) links: \(1\) the NGRC can take advantage of the optical phase information without requiring a local oscillator and \(2\) the NGRC can optically sample the transmitted data well above the symbol rate without requiring high\-bandwidth electronics\. This work showcases the potential for photonic NGRCs to outperform state\-of\-the\-art digital solutions in real\-world applications and opens a path to low\-latency, lower\-power IM/DD links at ranges of 10s of km\.

## [Escala de autoeficacia en inteligencia artificial generativa \(EAIAG\) para contextos académicos: Diseño y validación psicométrica](../publications/90d07f509f247f739a3c.md)

María Antonieta Elvira\-Valdés; Emilse Durán\-Aponte

La expansión de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior demanda instrumentos psicométricos que evalúen la autoeficacia del estudiantado ante estas tecnologías\. Este estudio tuvo como objetivo diseñar y validar la Escala de Autoeficacia en Inteligencia Artificial Generativa para contextos académicos \(EAIAG\) en una muestra de 251 estudiantes universitarios hispanohablantes de España \(n = 107\) y Latinoamérica \(n = 144\)\. Se adoptó un diseño instrumental en tres fases\. La validez de contenido, evaluada con seis jueces expertos, fue excelente\. El análisis factorial exploratorio evidenció una estructura tridimensional que explica el 55,3 % de la varianza, con un ajuste satisfactorio en el análisis factorial confirmatorio \(CFI = ,938; TLI = ,934; RMSEA = ,069\)\. La versión final consta de 17 ítems en tres dimensiones: gestión de prompts, integración adaptativa y evaluación crítica y ética\. La fiabilidad fue excelente \(α = ,931; ω = ,953\)\. Los valores HTMT \(&lt; ,85\) respaldaron la validez discriminante; la AVE fue adecuada en gestión de prompts e integración adaptativa, e inferior a ,50 en evaluación crítica y ética\. Se obtuvieron correlaciones positivas con la escala PEIIA, un instrumento de autoinforme teóricamente próximo \(r = ,360 a ,581; p &lt; ,001\)\. La invarianza factorial mostró equivalencia escalar entre España y Latinoamérica \(ΔCFI ≤ ,005; ΔRMSEA ≤ ,001\)\. Estos resultados aportan evidencias iniciales favorables sobre la validez y fiabilidad de la EAIAG, con utilidad potencial para la investigación y la identificación de necesidades formativas en educación superior hispanohablante\.

## [Sociologia da educação inclusiva na Espanha](../publications/90f43a3fe48c49aaad96.md)

Anabel Paramá\-Díaz; Enrique Fernández Vilas; Olga Jedrysiak Gutowska; Blanca García \-Gómez; Susana Gómez\-Redondo; Marcos Iglesias Carrera; Juan R\. Coca

A partir de un diseño de métodos mixtos, este artículo analiza cómo el profesorado comprende la discapacidad y la educación inclusiva como fenómenos socioeducativos\. Los datos de un cuestionario \(n = 502\) mostraron actitudes generalmente favorables hacia la inclusión, aunque con claras diferencias generacionales: el profesorado más joven declaró mayor confianza y apoyo a las prácticas inclusivas que sus colegas de mayor edad\. Al mismo tiempo, el profesorado identificó barreras estructurales y actitudinales persistentes, como la insuficiencia de recursos, la escasa formación especializada y la falta de materiales y espacios adaptados\. Los resultados cualitativos profundizaron este panorama, destacando demandas por más profesionales de apoyo, reducción de ratios de alumnos por clase, infraestructuras accesibles y tiempo para planificar pedagogías diferenciadas\. En conjunto, los resultados sugieren que el profesorado percibe diferencias importantes entre los principios de la educación inclusiva promovidos en los marcos normativos y su implementación en las prácticas escolares cotidianas\.

## [Machine learning\-based prediction of malignant transformation within 5 years in patients with oral leukoplakia: A retrospective cohort study](../publications/90fed53d391d7e4072af.md)

Qingmo Yang; Mimi Zhou; Chang Zhang; Ye Lu; Qingying Lan; Pan Wei; Hong Hua

BACKGROUND: Oral leukoplakia \(OLK\), a potentially malignant oral disorder, has 7\.2 \- 9\.8 % transformation rate\. Identifying high\-risk patients within 5 years can reduce the oral cancer burden\. OBJECTIVE: In this retrospective study, we aimed to identify the factors associated with malignant transformation in Chinese patients with OLK and develop and evaluate machine learning \(ML\) models for predicting malignant transformation within 5 years\. METHODS: In total, 672 OLK patients \(203 showing transformation; 469 with no transformation\) were included\. Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, GBDT, XGBoost, and LightGBM ML algorithms were used to develop models based on 17 clinicopathological features and evaluated using an internal test set and a temporal validation cohort of 73 patients \(24 showing transformation; 49 with no transformation\)\. RESULTS: LightGBM showed the best overall performance in the internal test set \(accuracy, 82\.65 %; area under the curve \(AUC\), 0\.8524\), and it maintained good discriminative performance in the temporal validation cohort \(AUC, 0\.7959\) when 17 clinicopathological features were used\. XGBoost showed the best performance in both the internal test set \(AUC, 0\.8081\) and temporal validation cohort \(AUC, 0\.8092\) when five clinicopathological features were used\. While predicting malignant transformation within 5 years, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0\.8505 in the internal test set\. However, the temporal validation results should be interpreted with caution because of limited sample size\. CONCLUSION: ML models may predict malignant transformation within 5 years in patients with OLK and may assist in individualized risk stratification\. Further validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical application\.

## [Synthetic humanitarianism and algorithmic witnessing: generative AI and the politics of humanitarian representation](../publications/91035b738155e89ae29e.md)

Marco Scalvini

Humanitarian organisations have begun deploying generative AI imagery in their campaigns, a practice this article terms synthetic humanitarianism\. The article asks what conceptual framework is required to analyse the ethical and communicative implications of this practice\. Drawing on witnessing theory, decolonial critiques of humanitarian visibility, and technocolonialism, I argue that synthetic humanitarianism is not a novel disruption but an intensification of extractive and colonial logics that have structured humanitarian communication since its institutional emergence\. I develop the concept of algorithmic witnessing to name the communicative condition in which generative AI systems produce the relations of testimony and moral address without any act of witnessing having taken place and without the participation of those represented\. The framework specifies four dimensions, testimonial fabrication, epistemic extraction, delanguaging, and stereoscopic automation, and I apply it to thirteen documented cases of generative AI image use in humanitarian communications between 2022 and 2025\. The analysis demonstrates that these dimensions form a mutually reinforcing system in which the elimination of situated meaning\-making enables fabricated testimony and the computational encoding of colonial visual archives produces automated stereotype\. I argue that the most significant consequence of synthetic humanitarianism is political rather than epistemological\. The displacement of situated meaning\-making by algorithmic production eliminates the last structural point at which affected communities could intervene in their own representation\.

## [Mandatory manuscript submission policies and authors’ rights and capabilities from a diversity, equity, inclusion, and access perspective: A prototype proposal](../publications/91040852dde3a9a8ff97.md)

Jaime A\. Teixeira da Silva; Timothy P Daly; Maryna Nazarovets

Several academic journals have explicitly articulated goals related to diversity, equity, inclusion, and access \(DEIA\)\. Their mandatory online submission policies, however, introduce final structural hurdles that we believe have the potential to infringe upon authors’ freedom of expression by wasting time and restricting their freedom to impart information and opinions, contrary to DEIA principles\. In this case\-based prototype opinion paper, we classify mandatory submission\-related requirements into three categories: necessary and reasonable; burdensome, but still rationally understandable; excessive, intrusive or dubiously justified\. We also examine the intersection between DEIA and authors’ rights and capabilities in scholarly publishing, arguing that excessively rigid or unjustifiable submission policies may undermine equitable participation and efficiency\. Finally, we advocate for an approach that prioritizes accessibility, fairness, and intellectual merit over bureaucratic formalities, proposing three alternative models that we contend could reduce unnecessary burdens on researchers during the submission process\.

## [PGM‐Free Catalysts for Oxygen Evolution Reaction for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers](../publications/9108758f0ddad66e2aab.md)

Shichen Guo; Minghao Xie; Chukwunwike O\. Iloeje; Di‐Jia Liu

ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer \(PEMWE\) holds a promise for large‐scale and highly efficient hydrogen production through electrocatalytic water splitting\. Its widespread commercial adoption, however, is hindered by its reliance on expensive and scarce platinum group metals \(PGMs\) as the electrode catalyst materials\. This is particularly the case at the PEMWE anode where the costly iridium is required to promote oxygen evolution reaction \(OER\)\. This article provides a brief review of the recent progresses and challenges in searching for PGM‐free OER catalysts as the low‐cost replacement of PGM catalysts, as well as our perspectives on future research directions from rational catalyst design to their potential industrial deployment\.

## [Putting others first: testing a model of prosociality and performance](../publications/91167951e6952f4113e7.md)

Anna Viragos; M\. Davis; D\. Leach

Abstract Employees reshape their roles to help others; yet existing theories explain either proactive self\-directed job redesign or prosocial behavior within existing role boundaries\. We introduce Prosocial Job Crafting \(PSJC\), a distinct form of role\-based job crafting through which individuals proactively modify their jobs’ task, relational, and cognitive boundaries to create opportunities to benefit others\. PSJC draws on the three dimensions of prosociality, linking perceived prosocial impact, prosocial motivation, and prosocial behavior\. The paper presents two empirical studies: in Study 1, we develop and validate a new scale measuring PSJC with data collected from employees in the USA \( N = 500\), and in Study 2, we test our theoretical model with matched data collected from Hungarian academic library employees \( N = 262\) and performance rating from their direct supervisors \( N = 8\)\. Perceived prosocial impact predicted all three forms of PSJC; however, only task PSJC positively predicted performance\. Findings suggest that the dimensions of PSJC have distinct behavioral implications and PSJC is not a uniform phenomenon\. We establish Job Crafting as not exclusively pro\-self, and that prosociality can be enacted through proactive job redesign\.

## [Mapping the Landscape of Integrated Reporting: Cross‐Industry Insights and Global Perspectives From a Topic Modeling Approach](../publications/9117cd12029949cabab5.md)

Francesca Culasso; Edoardo Crocco; Edoardo Borlatto; Elisa Truant

ABSTRACT This study investigates how companies across different industries emphasize themes within Integrated Reporting \(IR\), as promoted by the International Integrated Reporting Council \(IIRC\)\. As IR gains relevance for advancing Corporate Social Responsibility \(CSR\) and Environmental, Social, and Governance \(ESG\) disclosure, understanding sectoral reporting patterns becomes essential\. Building on dialogic accounting, we frame IR as a continuum between monologic disclosure—where reporting remains finance‐led and stakeholder dialog is effectively “closed down”—and dialogic accountability, where multiple value dimensions are connected and trade‐offs are made visible\. Using topic modeling \(Latent Dirichlet Allocation\), multidimensional scaling, and ANOVA tests, the analysis examines 425 best‐practice integrated reports from Corporate Register and the Integrated Reporting Example Database of the IFRS Council\. Results show substantial cross‐industry variations; however, the analysis also highlights three overarching patterns that are not implied by industry differences alone\. First, finance‐centered discourse remains structurally dominant even within best‐practice IR\. Second, sustainability‐related discourse appears comparatively bounded, suggesting compartmentalization rather than diffusion across reporting domains\. Third, the “connectivity of information” central to the IR promise emerges as empirically weak, as indicated by the persistent distance between sustainability and financial‐performance topics\. These findings challenge the implicit assumption that IR best practices naturally approximate integrated thinking and instead suggest a systematic tendency toward monologic reporting structures\. The study contributes to CSR and environmental management literature by offering empirical, data‐driven insights into how industry context shapes reporting priorities and by providing a scalable text‐analytic protocol that can support regulators and practitioners in monitoring whether integration improves as CSRD‐ and ISSB‐related disclosure regimes diffuse\.

## [Aerobic\-Component Training and Blood Pressure Variability in Women: A Scoping Review](../publications/911c561ed0e97231b1aa.md)

Marcio Lemos Rodrigues; Fernanda Tabita Barroso Zeidan; Janaina de Oliveira Brito Monzani; Nathaniel Gomes Oliveira; Vitoria Rodrigues Demetrio; Cristiano Teixeira Mostarda

Blood pressure variability \(BPV\) is an independent cardiovascular risk marker associated with target\-organ damage, cardiovascular events, and mortality\. In women, however, it remains unclear whether aerobic\-component training meaningfully modifies BPV and whether BPV\-focused intervention studies report hard cardiovascular outcomes\. This scoping review mapped and synthesized indexed literature on BPV responses to aerobic\-component training in adult women\. The review followed PRISMA\-ScR and updated Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and was registered in the Open Science Framework \( https://doi\.org/10\.17605/OSF\.IO/R2D4K \)\. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, the Virtual Health Library, and SciELO, without language or date restrictions, using Population\-Concept\-Context eligibility criteria\. Women aged 18 years or older exposed to interventions with a predominant aerobic component were eligible when BPV was explicitly assessed with a validated method\. Among 552 identified records, 527 unique records were screened and four reports were included, representing approximately 151 women from predominantly postmenopausal and selected clinical populations\. Available studies suggest reductions in mean blood pressure and selected autonomic markers, whereas chronic BPV findings were heterogeneous\. One pilot study reported a greater reduction in 24\-hour systolic BPV with supervised exercise than with a home\-based program\. No included BPV\-focused intervention study reported cardiovascular mortality or major cardiovascular events\.

## [Protocol for a cohort study of comprehensive intervention of psoriasis and diabetes comorbidity prevention and control using traditional Chinese medicine of blood\-activating and stasis\-dissolving method](../publications/91222364d0bba3866201.md)

Qingyun Wang; Jing\-wen Yeap; Pengbo Gao; Jiale Chen; Jiao Wang; Liu Liu; Jingjie He; Xiaoying Sun; Xin Li

Background Psoriasis is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease associated with an increased risk of metabolic dysfunction, including type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\)\. Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation may contribute to this association\. Blood\-activating and stasis\-dissolving therapies in traditional Chinese medicine \(TCM\) have shown potential anti\-inflammatory and metabolic benefits\. This study aimed to evaluate an integrated TCM\-based intervention in patients with psoriasis at high risk of T2DM\. Methods Participants aged 18–80 who met predefined diagnostic criteria for psoriasis vulgaris and blood\-stasis syndrome will be recruited\. Individuals identified as being at high risk for T2DM using a validated multifactorial diagnostic model will be allocated to two groups according to clinical assessment and treatment preference\. The conventional strategy group \(CSG\) will receive guideline\-based conventional psoriasis treatment, while the integrated strategy group \(ISG\) will receive standard care combined with Taodan granules \(TDG\), fish oil supplementation, and a structured aerobic exercise programme\. The primary analysis will employ linear mixed\-effects models with a difference\-in\-differences approach to compare changes in outcomes between groups\. Propensity score matching will be performed as a sensitivity analysis to balance baseline characteristics\. Outcomes The primary outcome is the change in insulin resistance from baseline to Week 16, assessed using the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance \(HOMA\-IR\)\. Key secondary outcomes include changes in psoriasis severity assessed by the psoriasis area and severity index \(PASI\), including PASI 50, PASI 75, and PASI 90 response rates\. Exploratory outcomes include the incidence of new\-onset T2DM and changes in circulating inflammatory biomarkers, including IL\-1β, IL\-6, TNF\-α, IL\-17A, and FGL1, to explore potential mechanisms underlying the effects of the integrated intervention\. Conclusion This study aims to evaluate the effects of an integrated TCM\-based intervention on dermatological and metabolic outcomes in patients with psoriasis at high risk of T2DM\. The findings may provide clinical evidence to support policymakers in developing management strategies for psoriasis and related metabolic comorbidities\. Trial registration This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials\.gov \(ID: NCT06402760\)\.

## [Ordinal measurement invariance of three retained GAEU\-1 dimensions in Chilean and Ecuadorian university samples](../publications/912b76b8b7c4ec35a805.md)

Xinglong Pang; Lin Zhou; Jin\-Ho CHO

Meaningful cross\-national comparisons of self\-regulated learning \(SRL\), motivation, and related learning\-regulation constructs require evidence that the measurement model operates comparably across groups\. We tested this requirement for three GAEU\-1 dimensions previously retained in Chile and Ecuador using the open Version\-5 dataset \( N = 1,316; Chile n = 631; Ecuador n = 685\)\. Fifteen ordered indicators representing the GAEU\-1 SRL factor, conscious motivational strategies, and deep learning techniques were analyzed with WLSMV, followed by a Wu\-Estabrook multigroup ordinal invariance sequence and complementary DIF analyses\. Country\-specific fit was mixed: CFI and SRMR were relatively favorable, whereas RMSEA indicated residual misspecification, especially in Chile \(CFI = 0\.947, SRMR = 0\.059, RMSEA = 0\.094; Ecuador: CFI = 0\.952, SRMR = 0\.059, RMSEA = 0\.085\)\. In the multigroup models, equality constraints on thresholds, loadings, and intercept\-related parameters produced no meaningful deterioration in approximate fit, and met the study&\#x27;s prespecified incremental\-fit criteria for proceeding to latent comparison within the retained scoring representation\. Several items showed FDR\-adjusted DIF signals, but none reached the prespecified 0\.020 practical\-effect criterion\. Post hoc diagnostics localized the largest residual association to GA7\-GA8 in both samples; a one\-factor model fit appreciably worse than the retained three\-factor representation \(Delta CFI = −0\.059 in Chile and −0\.069 in Ecuador\)\. Polychoric HTMT values were all below 0\.85, although Fornell\-Larcker diagnostics remained unfavorable for factor pairs involving the GAEU\-1 SRL factor\. Observed and latent standardized sample contrasts differed only modestly and are interpreted descriptively because the samples differed markedly in university sector and gender composition\. The two planned sensitivity analyses and a post hoc private\-university\-only sensitivity analysis preserved the main comparability result\. Overall, the three retained GAEU\-1 dimensions showed stable measurement parameters across these Chilean and Ecuadorian university samples, while broader structural and country\-level interpretations remain outside the evidence provided here\.

## [JACKKNIFE EMPIRICAL LIKELIHOOD FOR INFINITE\-ORDER U \-STATISTICS](../publications/912e242d509b884e1674.md)

Qing Wang; Yichuan Zhao; Ting Zhang

Infinite\-order U \-statistics play a vital role in modern statistics\. However, given their degree k n $k\_n$ k Subscript n depends on the sample size n , quantifying their variability is quite challenging, as fixed\-degree theories cannot be directly adopted\. In this article, we propose a jackknife empirical likelihood \(EL\) framework that can be used to construct confidence intervals for an infinite\-order U \-statistic\. We establish sufficient conditions for the limiting chi\-squared distribution of the JEL ratio statistic and introduce an efficient partition\-sampling realization for practical implementation\. To evaluate the performance of the proposed methodology, we conduct simulation studies in the context of subsampling\-based ensemble methods and the maximum test, respectively, comparing its performance with four competing methods\. The simulation studies yield satisfactory results across the board\. Finally, we demonstrate the practical application of our method using a United States Forest Service timber auctions dataset to predict the highest bid at an auction\.
