## [Version Control for Surgical Data Science: A Primer on Git and GitHub](../publications/914acfe1cb8c2b835baf.md)

Andrew C\. Kuo; Marissa C\. Kuo; Paul C\. Kuo

Surgical research increasingly relies on computational analysis of large clinical datasets, and major journals now request code availability statements for publication\. Yet most surgical trainees and faculty receive no formal training in software version control, despite its central role in reproducible research\. This article provides a practical introduction to Git, a widely used version control system in academic and industrial software development, and GitHub, a leading hosting platform\. The presentation implements workflows specific to surgical research, including retrospective registry analysis, multi\-institutional collaboration, and reviewer reproducibility requests\. Core concepts covered include the four mental models that are the basis for Git usage \(repository, commit, branch, and remote\), the daily edit\-stage\-commit cycle that is the dominant workflow, and the use of branches and pull requests for collaboration\. Attention is given to clinical data security: identifiable patient data must never enter a version\-controlled repository, and the article details the use of a\.gitignore file to prevent inadvertent commits\. The article also illustrates the installation of community\-developed tools through a worked example involving Stash, an open\-source persistent memory layer for artificial intelligence \(AI\) research assistants\. Three recovery scenarios are demonstrated: restoring deleted code, reproducing the exact state of a manuscript at submission, and resolving merge conflicts\. This allows surgical researchers to adopt version control practices that protect their work, support reproducibility, and meet emerging standards for transparent computational research\.

## [Identification of Macrophage Polarization\-Related Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma Using Integrated Bioinformatics](../publications/9151a12aa87bd87148bf.md)

Ran Wang; Jingwei Zhang; Jing Qi; Yizhi Jiang; Nana Wang; Jun Huang; Sisi Tang; Yuanfeng Wei; Yu Xiang; Hesheng He; 黄来全; 韦中玲

Multiple myeloma \(MM\) is an incurable hematologic neoplasm with heterogeneous prognosis\. Within the bone marrow microenvironment, macrophage polarization \(MP\) contributes to immune remodeling and may influence disease progression, yet MP\-related prognostic biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized\. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic data from UCSC Xena \(n = 844\) and GSE4581 \(n = 414\) to identify differentially expressed genes between immune\-hot and immune\-cold MM samples stratified by single\-sample gene set enrichment analysis \(ssGSEA\)\-derived immune scores\. Weighted gene co\-expression network analysis \(WGCNA\) and intersection with published MP\-related genes yielded candidate genes, which were further refined using univariate Cox regression combined with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator \(LASSO\), eXtreme gradient boosting \(XGBoost\) and support vector machine recursive feature elimination \(SVM\-RFE\) machine learning algorithms to construct a prognostic model\. An eight\-gene signature \(LGALS3, IL2RG, ADAM8, MERTK, ACSS1, ARSK, CBX6 and SOCS3\) was established, demonstrating acceptable discriminatory ability for 1\-, 2\-, and 3\-year overall survival \(AUC 0\.666\-0\.736 in training cohort\)\. Risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration patterns, predicted drug sensitivity, and survival outcomes\. A predicted competing endogenous RNA \(ceRNA\) network centered on MERTK and SOCS3 was also constructed\. These findings identify eight MP\-related hub genes as candidate prognostic biomarkers and provide a risk model with acceptable predictive performance, offering insights into the immune\-metabolic interplay in MM and suggesting potential avenues for personalized therapeutic strategies\.

## [Proof\-of\-concept for a deep learning\-based automated system for deep\-sea fish stomach content analysis](../publications/91709c348596bd715cb6.md)

Akira Eto; Ryusuke Miyamoto; Masashi Yokota

In fish dietary analysis, reducing the substantial time and effort required is essential for accelerating the accumulation of ecological knowledge\. Recent advances in machine learning have enabled development of highly accurate object detection models\. Here, we aimed to establish a foundational technology for automating stomach content analysis by developing an automated prey detection system based on YOLO, a general\-purpose object detection model\. Stomach contents from demersal fish collected by bottom trawling were photographed using a stereomicroscope, and a training dataset comprising 682 images \(1655 instances\) across 18 classes was constructed\. The developed model successfully detected prey items across a wide range of digestion states, including highly degraded and amorphous prey that are difficult to identify visually\. Despite the challenging nature of this task, the class\-average precision, recall, and class assignment error rate were 41\.3% ± 8\.4%, 37\.2% ± 7\.6%, and 34\.1% ± 7\.2%, respectively\. Among all classes, precision was highest for the ‘Fish\(eye\)’ class at 88\.3%, whereas recall was highest for ‘Decapoda\(shrimp\)’ at 70\.5%\. In addition to these conventional metrics, we introduced a novel metric, Identification to Higher\-level Taxon \(IdHT\), to account for taxonomic\-level inconsistencies common in dietary analyses\. The class\-average IdHT was 19\.5% ± 5\.3%\. Inter\-class confusion occurred frequently, particularly among crustacean classes, likely due to texture bias inherent in convolutional neural networks\. This study represents the first application of deep learning–based object detection to dietary analysis across multiple prey taxa, providing a foundational framework for efficiently conducting large\-scale deep\-sea food\-web studies in the future\.

## [Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings](../publications/917aa5df2a6f4ffc52b1.md)

Ilia Davarashvili; Ariel Israel; Shlomo Vinker; Hila Hochler

Background SARS\-CoV\-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population\. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community\-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients\. In this retrospective population\-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID\-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings\. Methods We conducted a retrospective population\-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025\. Women with COVID\-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID\-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics\. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group\. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed\. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID\-19 and control groups\. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint \(0\.15% vs\. 0\.15%; OR 1\.00, 95% CI 0\.27–3\.74\)\. Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis\. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID\-19 than among matched controls \(6\.88% vs\. 4\.87%; OR 1\.45, 95% CI 1\.19–1\.75; 13\.8% vs\. 11\.8%; OR 1\.20, 95% CI 1\.05–1\.37; p = 0\.007 respectively\)\. Conclusions Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID\-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications\.

## [ML\-Based Intrusion Detection System with Intrusion Prevention System](../publications/917abdb4dd5d81c2bd64.md)

Prathysh N; Rajesh H S; Purushothama M; Chandrashekar Y; Syeda Ayesha Unisa

This paper presented a hybrid rule\-based and machine\-learning system that intercepts navigation at the browser and blocks phishing, malware, ransomware, and DGA\-style malicious destinations in real time, without requiring network\-level packet capture\. A Random Forest classifier trained on eight lexical and structural URL features reached 95\.83% accuracy and a 95\.52% F1\-score on a held\-out test set, at an inference cost of under 6 ms per request, well within the latency budget of a normal page navigation\. More importantly, a real false\-positive failure was found, measured, and fixed: restricting an entropy rule from the full URL to the hostname alone, combined with removing a spurious pattern from the training corpus, reduced false blocks on ordinary websites from 7 of 10 to 1 of 12 with no loss of true detections\. A live per\-attack\-type accuracy view complements the usual offline benchmark by scoring every trained algorithm against real traffic as it happens, and a per\-class confusion matrix shows the two remaining error types clearly enough to prioritize future work: at the current dataset scale, missed detections \(2 of 34\) matter more than false alarms \(1 of 38\), which argues for growing the malicious\-class training data before anything else\. Taken together, these results suggest that a browser\-level hybrid detector is a practical, lightweight complement to network\-level intrusion detection for the individual users and small deployments that flow\-based systems do not reach\.

## [ADMP\-GCN: Interpretable Adaptive Message Passing Graph Learning for Patient\-specific EEG Seizure Prediction with Human\-in\-the\-Loop Validation](../publications/918b2ce2875baf908c12.md)

Ashwini B\. Patil; Megharani Patil

Automated seizure prediction based on multichannel Electroencephalography \(EEG\) using Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is a challenging task that mandates accurate and interpretable results for improved clinical decisionmaking\.However, brain connectivity modelling on the evolving patient\-specific and seizure\-dynamic EEG signals makes the problem highly complex\.Recently, Graph Neural Network \(GNN\)\-based approaches have shown promising results for improved seizure prediction by modelling brain functional connectivity and inter\-channel interactions\.However, they employ redundant channel representations and a fixed propagation mechanism, which potentially limit their practicality\.To address these potential limitations, this paper introduces a unified framework that employs an explanation\-constrained topology\-aware graph learning model\.In this context, a novel Adaptive Depth Message Passing Graph Convolutional Network \(ADMP\-GCN\) is introduced that models topology\-conditioned message propagation to enable heterogeneous receptive fields within EEG connectivity graphs while considering channel reduction for improved efficiency and robustness\.Following model training, multilevel post hoc explainability is performed using SHAP, Integrated Gradients \(IG\), and GNNExplainer to interpret feature, layer, and graph\-level contributions to seizure prediction\.Finally, a human\-aligned composite supervision is introduced that balances prediction accuracy and explanation quality\.The proposed model is validated using the CHB\-MIT dataset, and it is found that the proposed model results in improved accuracy of 95\.10% and sensitivity of 96\.33% compared to existing graph\-based seizure prediction models\.In conclusion, the results reveal a viable and clinically relevant seizure prediction that balances performance and applicability\.

## [Crop\-associated differentiation of rhizosphere microbial communities and soil functional traits in saline\-alkaline farmland](../publications/91a8a962796345935d91.md)

Xiaoling Zhang; Yuhao Yuan; Yanpeng Shi; Siyuan Chen; Zhijun Gao; Qinghua Yang; Hanghang Hou; Baili Feng

Introduction Saline\-alkaline soils constrain crop production, yet it remains unclear how different crops shape rhizosphere conditions, plant ion allocation and microbial communities when grown under the same field background\. Methods We compared eight crops under uniform saline\-alkaline field and management conditions and integrated rhizosphere physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, plant nutrient and ion traits, and bacterial and fungal community characteristics using a multivariate framework\. Results Crop identity was associated with pronounced differences in nutrient status, salinity, moisture, enzyme activity and Na \+ and K \+ allocation, and explained 78\.1% and 83\.5% of bacterial and fungal community variation, respectively\. Multiple factor analysis further separated the eight crops into two stable multivariate profiles, one characterized mainly by nutrient and enzyme traits and the other by higher salinity and greater contributions from Na \+ allocation traits\. Discussion These findings demonstrate that crop\-associated differentiation in saline\-alkaline farmland reflects coordinated variation among soil conditions, plant ion regulation and microbial organization, providing an integrated basis for crop comparison and saline\-alkaline soil management\.

## [Forest bathing as a pathway toward ecological identity: a community case study](../publications/91ab0c34da4fef5925f5.md)

Kelly G\. Guilbeau; Kathryn Dietzway

Climate and ecological disruption can affect wellbeing, social relationships, and connection to place; when experienced across generations, these widespread disruptions can lead to collective trauma, becoming culturally embedded in identities shared at a community\-level\. This paper proposes a theoretical model demonstrating the reciprocal relationship between collective trauma and ecological dissociation, defined as diminished capacity for relational connection with the more\-than\-human world\. We then present Acadiana Forest Bathing, a free, community\-based initiative in south Louisiana, as an application of forest bathing to operationalize the theoretical underpinnings of this reciprocal cycle\. Inviting self\-guided and group\-based sensory experiences in outdoor settings, the program aims to cultivate ecological identity through embodiment, agency, belonging, and connection at individual, community, and ecological scales\. Initial lessons learned and suggestions for future programming are explored, as well as discussion of feasibility to systematically evaluate the conceptual application of the theoretical model, such that this place\-based programming can integrate lived experiences with community\-level interventions to address the ecological dissociation resulting from collective trauma\.

## [Global Food Safety Challenges and Their Public Health Consequences: A Systematic Review](../publications/91acaba3939121bc708d.md)



Background: Foodborne illness is the effect of consumption of contaminated food which can carry bacteria, viruses, parasites, chemical residues &amp; toxins or physical hazards and can range from acute gastroenteritis to invasive infection organ damage neurological disease &amp; cancer\.Ninety\-seven report 2018 WHO foodborne disease estimates for the first time in this special issue, which show that contaminated food is still an enormous global health burden, but with differential effects between populations and regions\.This review addresses two related questions: how frequently are specific food\-safety challenges identified in current global literature, and what are their direct and indirect pathways to public health?Methods: A qualitative systematic review following applicable PRISMA 2020 principles \(Page et al\., 2021\) was conducted and reported\.Hazards were then classified into microbial and parasitic hazards, chemical hazards, antimicrobial resistance and food fraud, climate change and environmental effects \(direct or indirect to human health\)\.This is an opportunity to design riskbased regulation that targets the hazards that are most threatening to health, while providing smaller producers and vendors with a degree of leeway in achieving achievable standards\.Future research should increase the evidence from under\-represented regions, disentangle climate stress and chemical exposure impacts, enhance source attribution for AMR and assess interventions in real market scenarios\.

## [Tianwang Buxin Dan regulated PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway to improve constipation and emotional disorders in rats](../publications/91b75499b4bf7b8b9881.md)

Heng Wang; Xinran Li; Zhaoyu Chen; Li Ji; Shaoliang Li; Haihua Qian; Dan Zhang

Background Functional constipation \(FC\) is frequently comorbid with anxiety and depression, yet pharmacological strategies targeting both gastrointestinal and emotional symptoms remain limited\. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of Tianwang Buxin Dan \(TWBXD\), a classical Chinese herbal formula, in treating FC with emotional disturbances using an integrated strategy combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vivo validation\. Methods TWBXD chemical constituents were characterized exclusively by UHPLC\-MS/MS, yielding 650 compounds for network pharmacology\. Targets were predicted via TargetNet and intersected with disease\-associated genes from GeneCards\. Common targets underwent PPI network analysis, GO/KEGG enrichment, and molecular docking\. In vivo , a rat model was established by CUMS plus diphenoxylate and treated with TWBXD \(low, medium, high doses\) or positive drugs \(mosapride plus fluoxetine\) for 28 days\. Therapeutic effects and pathway regulation in colon and hippocampus were evaluated by behavioral tests, gastrointestinal function assessment, histopathology, transmission electron microscopy, Western blotting, and qPCR\. Results Network pharmacology identified 473 drug targets and 308 disease\-overlapping targets\. KEGG enrichment highlighted PI3K\-Akt, MAPK, IL\-17, and neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction pathways, while PPI analysis identified Akt1, IL\-6, and TNF as hub genes\. Molecular docking showed quercetin, luteolin, and tanshinone IIA bound stably to Akt1, IL\-6, and JUN \(binding energies ≤ −6\.6 kcal/mol\)\. In vivo , TWBXD dose\-dependently improved fecal water content, intestinal transit, sucrose preference, and open\-field performance, and attenuated colonic mucosal injury, hippocampal neuronal damage, and mitochondrial disruption\. Mechanistically, TWBXD was associated with increased PI3K/Akt/mTOR phosphorylation in colonic and hippocampal tissues and with reduced JNK expression in the hippocampus\. No organ toxicity was observed\. Conclusion TWBXD alleviates constipation\-related gastrointestinal dysfunction and comorbid anxiety/depression\-like behaviors in rats, and these effects are associated with activation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling in colonic and hippocampal tissues and with modulation of JNK signaling in the hippocampus\. Although the concordance between computational predictions and multi\-level in vivo validation supports TWBXD as a multi\-target therapeutic candidate for functional constipation with emotional comorbidities, the causal contribution of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, and the extent to which the peripheral and central changes are functionally coupled through the gut–brain axis, remain to be established\.

## [Post\-traumatic stress and psychological well\-being in children with type 1 diabetes: An Indian perspective](../publications/91bb0a6cc2c9e94bc798.md)

Praveen George Paul; Satya Raj

The diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus \(T1D\) is frequently recalled by families as one of the most frightening moments of their lives\.What follows is not a single crisis but a chronic one: Relentless glucose monitoring, insulin dosing, and the ever\-present fear of hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis\.It is increasingly recognized that this burden can cross the threshold from ordinary adjustment stress into post\-traumatic stress symptoms and, in a subset, frank posttraumatic stress disorder \(PTSD\) \-affecting not only the child but the caregiver who carries the round\-the\-clock vigilance of disease management\.In this issue, Shah et al\. present findings from a study examining probable PTSD among children with T1D and their caregivers, reporting a prevalence of approximately 10%\-a figure the authors note is nearly twice that reported in earlier United States cohorts\.\[1\] What makes this striking is the context: 88% of participants were on insulin pumps, 97% had access to continuous glucose monitoring \(CGM\), mean hemoglobin A1c \(HbA1c\) was 7\.5%, and nearly all had public or private insurance\.The lesson is an important one\-trauma related to a chronic, life\-threatening childhood illness is not fully mitigated by technology, tight glycemic control, or financial access\.The emotional weight of living with T1DM appears to persist independent of resource level\.If probable PTSD persists at this rate even under near\-optimal resource settings, the Indian scenario invites a different and arguably more layered set of stressors\.Insulin pump and CGM penetration remain low, and most children are managed on multiple daily injections with selfmonitoring of blood glucose that is frequently curtailed by cost or by the pain of repeated fingerpricks\.This directly translates into unpredictable hypoglycemia and glycemic swings\-an Indian cohort using retrospective CGM found a mean HbA1c of 8\.0%, yet time\-in\-range averaging only 41%, with none of the children meeting recommended glycemic targets\.\[2\] Layered onto this is genuine financial insecurity: A North Indian survey found families spending roughly ₹55,000 a year on glucose monitoring, insulin, and investigations alone, with over 30% of families spending more than half their household income on diabetes care, more than a third borrowing money to sustain treatment, and fewer than 12% receiving any organized financial support\-many families depend on out\-of\-pocket purchases or non\-governmental organization\-supplied strips and insulin\.\[3\] For an Indian family, then, the traumatic burden of T1D is not only the fear of the disease itself but also the compounding weight of unaffordability, technology denied, and the visible dejection of an HbA1c far above target despite best efforts\.This is consistent with Indian data specifically on caregivers\.The IDREAM study found that high caregiving burden nearly doubled the probability of severe depression and low well\-being https://ispae\-jped\.com/

## [Role Of Social\-Media In Social Inclusion And Self\-Reliance Of Disabled People – A Sociological Study Based On Mentally And Physically Disabled Adults Of Kanpur Nagar](../publications/91c6e713dacc5a5080f0.md)



For centuries, disability has been misunderstood in multifarious cultures\.People with disabilities often face stigma, exclusion, and stereotypes that prevent them from fully participating in society\.In traditional communities, where physical ability is closely tied to social status, these challenges have been even greater\.However, the rise of social media has started to change this narrative\.Digital platforms like Instagram, YouTube etc\., have given people with infirmities a space to tell their own stories, break down stereotypes, and build supportive communities\.Instead of being defined by outdated cultural beliefs, individuals with disabilities can now control how they are seen by the world\.Social media is not just a tool for entertainment\-it is a powerful force that is shifting attitudes, raising awareness, and advocating for change\.This research paper examines how social media may contribute to social inclusion and self\-reliance among young adults with disabilities\.It assumes a sample of 100 respondents from Kanpur Nagar comprising 50 mentally disabled adults and 50 physically disabled adults aged 18\-25 years\.The paper argues that accessible digital platforms can strengthen social participation, peer interaction, access to education, employment information, entrepreneurship, and civic engagement while also highlighting barriers such as affordability, digital literacy and accessibility\.

## [TriRouter: Sparse\-to\-Dense Electrode\-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding](../publications/91e3ce3d38565a99d3fc.md)

Ying Zhou;  Yaoxin; Mengting Liu

Motor imagery brain\-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages\. We propose TriRouter, an electrode\-space routing framework with discriminative\-preservation, mask\-robustness, and latent\-compensation paths\. A validation\-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete\-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness\. In BNCI2014\-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic\-spatial\-filtering corrupted\-EEG baseline\. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted\-EEG baseline by 3\.68, 4\.02, and 6\.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low\-channel dataset evaluation\.

## [Regulating the Digital Divide: Policy Interventions for Equitable Access to AI\-Enabled E\-Learning Platforms](../publications/91eee4b82a5a1e2b7ac7.md)

Chukwudum Collins Umoke

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is rapidly transforming global education systems, offering unprecedented opportunities for personalization, efficiency, and adaptive learning\. However, the integration of AI in education has also deepened existing digital divides, particularly in under\-resourced communities lacking adequate infrastructure, policy support, and inclusive design\. This study proposes the Equity\-Centered AI Learning Access Model \(ECALAM\)—a conceptual framework developed through a qualitative synthesis of recent literature and policy reports—to understand and address systemic barriers to equitable AI adoption\. ECALAM identifies four interrelated domains: structural inequities, AI accessibility challenges, inclusive design adaptation, and policy governance\. Findings indicate that AI\-enhanced learning systems, when deployed without attention to algorithmic fairness, linguistic diversity, and access equity, risk reinforcing educational stratification\. Inclusive design principles, adaptive technologies, and regulatory frameworks are shown to play a pivotal role in enabling just and accessible learning environments\. The study concludes with policy recommendations for governments, educators, and technology developers, emphasizing the need for anticipatory governance and inclusive pedagogical integration\. ECALAM offers a diagnostic and strategic tool for guiding ethical and equitable AI implementation in education, particularly across diverse and underserved global contexts\.

## [Structural optimization and environmental response analysis of modular buildings based on BIM](../publications/91f589f88f0aa0aba417.md)

Jiaming Zhang

Despite the benefits of efficiency and fast construction associated with modular steel structures, the structural design of modular buildings is faced with unique challenges concerning the connection properties between modules during different loads\. This paper proposes a comprehensive BIM\-driven approach integrating multi\-objective optimization of the structure and assessment of the multi\-physics environmental response to the building, namely a six\-story modular steel building in Changsha, China\. The parametric design carried out by using Autodesk Revit software, incorporating the attributes of wind, earthquake, and temperature effects, was utilized for analysis purposes\. When combined with the finite element analysis via automatic IFC exchange, the NSGA\-II algorithm provides a Pareto front consisting of 22 non\-dominated solutions between steel usage and lateral stiffness; the adopted balanced solution demonstrates a reduction in the steel mass by 8\.2%, compared to the un\-optimized one, as well as the improved drift behavior\. The environmental impact analysis for the optimized solution under wind loads, seismic excitations, and thermal conditions indicates that although the connection region of modules complies with all international standards, there is an increased wind stress concentration by 20\.7%, seismic dynamic magnification of 2\.16 at the horizontal module junction, and condensation potential in winter due to the temperature lower than the dew point at the inner surface of the connection junction\. These vulnerabilities at the level of the connections, which cannot be detected using standard optimization strategies based on global performance indicators, prove the need to combine optimization with a multiphysics environmental evaluation strategy using a BIM model\. Supplementary connection, stiffness\-transition, thermo\-mechanical, and thermal\-bridge checks were added to clarify the robustness and limitations of the reported results\.

## [ЕЛЕКТРОННІ ДОКАЗИ У ЦИВІЛЬНОМУ ПРОЦЕСІ УКРАЇНИ: ПРОБЛЕМИ ТЕОРІЇ ТА ПРАКТИКИ ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ](../publications/920cad51d21417416be8.md)

V\. Zinukhova

У статті здійснено комплексний теоретико\-прикладний аналіз актуальних проблем використання електронних доказів у цивільному процесі України в умовах глобальної циф\- рової трансформації судочинства\. Досліджено правову природу електронної інформації, її специфічні ознаки та визначено чільне місце електронних доказів у сучасній системі засо\- бів доказування\. Детально проаналізовано процесуальний порядок подання, дослідження, оцінки та забезпечення цифрових даних, а також розкрито механізми функціонування інсти\- туту електронного правосуддя\. Методологічне підґрунтя дослідження становить комплекс загальнонаукових і спеціаль\- но\-юридичних методів пізнання\. За допомогою діалектичного методу простежено еволюцію та тенденції розвитку інституту доказування під впливом інформаційних технологій\. Фор\- мально\-юридичний аналіз дав змогу всебічно дослідити норми Цивільного процесуального кодексу України та спеціального законодавства, що регулює сфери електронного докумен\- тообігу й електронних довірчих послуг\. Системно\-структурний підхід сприяв визначенню взаємозв’язку між окремими елементами процесуального механізму роботи з цифровими даними, а порівняльно\-правовий метод дав змогу зіставити вітчизняне процесуальне зако\- нодавство із передовими європейськими стандартами e\-Justice\. У результаті дослідження встановлено, що найбільші практичні труднощі під час роз\- гляду цивільних справ виникають під час встановлення автентичності, цілісності, належ\- ності та допустимості електронних даних\. Окрему увагу приділено специфіці фіксації й оцінки відомостей, що містяться в електронному листуванні, мобільних месенджерах, матеріалах вебсайтів, соціальних мережах, цифрових аудіо\- та відеозаписах\. Обґрунтовано, що підвищення ефективності використання електронних доказів вимагає комплексної уні\- фікації судової практики, належної матеріально\-технічної модернізації судів, широкого впро\- вадження кваліфікованого електронного підпису та розроблення чітких алгоритмів проце\- суального закріплення цифрових слідів\.

## [GNN\-Guided Local Refinement for Efficient Layout Decomposition with DSA\-MP](../publications/92193c4314664e15628a.md)

Yu Feng; Liyi Zhou; Haoyu Wang; Yiming Xu; Hao Geng; Shaozhi Deng; Ningsheng Xu; Shisheng Xiong

Multiple patterning lithography \(MPL\) has been widely used to improve lithography resolution in advanced nodes, but it faces cost limits as feature sizes shrink\. Directed self\-assembly \(DSA\) offers a cost\-effective complement, extending the resolution of optical lithography to sub\-10 nm and beyond\. Integrating DSA into MPL \(DSA\-MP\) further enhances the resolution of contact/via patterning\. Nevertheless, growing design complexity exposes the limits of existing decomposition methods, which struggle to balance solution quality and runtime, and neglect edge\-to\-edge spacing constraints of DSA templates, compromising manufacturability\. To address these issues, we introduce a new conflict graph model capturing the previously overlooked constraints and develop a local refinement strategy powered by the graph neural network, enabling efficient and scalable layout decomposition\. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves higher solution quality with faster convergence than state\-of\-the\-art methods, while maintaining robustness across layout scales, design styles, technology nodes, and varying mask counts\.

## [Sequential Dissolution Demolding for the Replication of Multifunctional High‐Aspect‐Ratio Copper Micropillar Arrays](../publications/921dfca299ea880b4dc7.md)

Sheng\-Yun Chen; Ruiqi Cheng; Zhaofeng Xue; Yue Zhang; Yu Shu; Chengqun Gui; Hao Cao

Nanoimprint lithography \(NIL\) is widely used to pattern material surfaces for functional modification\. To advance this capability, we develop a sequential dissolution demolding \(SDD\) technique based on selective material solubility, enabling two consecutive, stress\-free demolding processes\. This approach capitalizes on the differential solubility of positive photoresists, which withstand non\-polar solvents but dissolve readily in alkaline aqueous solutions following UV exposure\. Utilizing this mechanism, the high\-aspect\-ratio \(HAR\) micropillar arrays \(aspect ratios up to 20:1\) on photoresist masters were successfully replicated into lipophilic polystyrene \(PS\) films, yielding intermediate templates comprising deep microcavities\. These cavities were subsequently metallized via an electroplating process\. By dissolving the PS template in a non\-polar solvent, high\-quality, free\-standing HAR copper \(Cu\) micropillars were isolated without inducing mechanical strain\. Furthermore, these engineered Cu structures exhibited valuable multifunctional properties, including anti\-reflective and antibacterial characteristics\. This stress\-free demolding strategy provides a robust pathway to broaden the applicability of NIL in complex nanofabrication\.

## [The Effect of AI\-Supported Coding Instruction on 21st\-Century Skills](../publications/922c7ae07e3a221e8d0e.md)

Osman Kayhan

The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction on students’ 21st\-century skills\. A quantitative research approach employing a pretest–posttest quasi\-experimental design with a control group was used\. The study group consisted of high school students\. While the experimental group received artificial intelligence\-supported coding instruction, the control group continued with coding instruction based on the existing teaching method\. Data were collected using a 21st\-century skills scale\. To examine within\-group changes, a paired\-samples t test was conducted, and to determine between\-group differences, ANCOVA was performed by controlling pretest scores\. The findings indicated that both the experimental and control groups showed significant increases in their 21st\-century skills scores\. When pretest scores were controlled, no statistically significant difference was found between the posttest scores of students who received artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction and those who received coding instruction based on the existing teaching method\. The results demonstrate that both the existing teaching method–based coding instruction and artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction are effective in developing students’ 21st\-century skills\. Accordingly, it is recommended that different instructional approaches used in coding education be planned in a way that supports targeted 21st\-century skills and that teaching processes be structured using a holistic approach\.

## [Construcción de la actitud de riesgo suicida a lo largo del curso de vida: una mirada desde personas mayores en Santiago de Chile](../publications/923520a7de2e55e9a72d.md)

Introduction: Suicide in old age is a complex phenomenon built over the life course, shaped by cumulative biopsychosocial factors\. Objective: To explore protective and risk factors shaping the risk attitude towards suicide attempts among older adults enrolled in the Older Adult Health Program \(PSAM\) at a Family Health Center in Santiago, Chile\. Methodology: A qualitative, exploratory study with a narrative approach, using the biographical method\. Twenty\-seven in\-depth interviews were conducted with individuals aged 65 to 91, analyzing experiences from childhood to late adulthood\. Results: Protective factors included emotional support, community engagement, self\-care, and stable support networks\. ## [MASTERING THE MATH MINDSET: NAVIGATING THE GAP BETWEEN WHAT TEACHERS KNOW AND WHAT THEY TEACH](../publications/9242d2f51b53b866405e.md)

Nurideen Yakubu Gbegini; Mohammed Yikehere Marifa; Bismark Basigi; Patrick Alade; Johnson Kwadwo Ankomah; Daniel Kudjo Adiku; Collins Oteng; Dennis Offei Kwakye

In Ghana, Senior High School mathematics curriculum standards strongly advocate for inquiry\-based and problem\-centered pedagogies\. However, empirical evidence regarding how teachers’ pedagogical knowledge translates into classroom practice remains scarce, particularly in marginalized administrative regions\. This study investigated the self\-reported knowledge levels, classroom instructional practices, and the theory\-practice alignment amongst public SHS mathematics teachers in the Wa Municipality of the Upper West Region, Ghana\. Adopting a quantitative descriptive survey design, data were collected from N = 76 mathematics teachers using a self\-developed structured questionnaire\. Descriptive statistics \(means and standard deviations\) and inferential statistics \(paired\-samples t\-test\) were utilized for data analysis\. Findings revealed high overall self\-reported knowledge \(M = 3\.27, SD = 0\.72\) and implementation levels \(M = 3\.23, SD = 0\.70\)\. Teachers reported highest competence in assessing learner reasoning processes \(M = 3\.49\) and selecting real\-world problems \(M = 3\.34\) but demonstrated lower scores in theoretical underpinnings \(M = 3\.11\) and providing extension activities \(M = 3\.17\)\. The paired\-samples t\-test indicated no statistically significant difference between teachers’ perceived knowledge and instructional practices, t\(70\) = 0\.34, p = \.738, d = 0\.06, revealing strong self\-efficacy alignment\. Continuous professional development should focus on strengthening foundational theoretical frameworks and diagnostic formative assessment strategies\.

## [Cooperative metaheuristic feature selection and out\-of\-fold weighted ensemble learning for chronic kidney disease prediction from a reduced attribute panel](../publications/924441254da6dee29ba0.md)

Amaresh Ayyanahalli Math; Ananda Murthy Meenakshi Sundaram

Chronic kidney disease is diagnosed from a broad laboratory panel whose size and composition are open to optimization\. This study pairs a cooperative hybrid metaheuristic for attribute selection with a weighted voting ensemble\. Genetic, swarm, and annealing sub\-populations evolved in parallel over one shared fitness landscape, exchanged elites every five iterations, and were refined by annealing applied as a local search on the incumbent; the attributes retained across the elite band formed the subset, which fed four heterogeneous learners whose probabilities were fused using weights tuned from out\-of\-fold predictions only\. Imputation, search, learners, and weights were confined to the training partition of a 10 times five\-fold cross\-validation, and every single\-operator variant, four classical selectors, and the unreduced panel were evaluated under that identical protocol\. The ensemble reached 99\.00% accuracy, an area under the curve of 0\.9994, and an F\-measure of 99\.19% from 11 of the 24 attributes, dropping 53% of the assays at a cost of two\-thirds of a percentage point that is not statistically significant once the dependence between cross\-validation folds is modeled\. Accuracy held at 98\.00% when a further fifth of all values was deleted, and an independent cohort of 200 records recorded as discretized intervals returned 98\.00%\. The pipeline is statistically equivalent to the strongest single learner and to the strongest classical selector while using fewer than half the attributes\.

## [Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search\-Free Planning in Latent Space](../publications/92496835700d02b14a6b.md)

Guanchen Du; Jinhao Du; Yanpeng Sun; Shan Zhang; Na Zhao; Zechao Li

Latent world models learn action\-conditioned state transitions in a compact representation space, providing a predictive model for visual planning and control\. However, planning with these models typically requires costly test\-time optimization over action sequences\. We propose to replace this online search with a goal\-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations\. A key challenge is that action prediction alone neither ensures that goal representations encode action\-relevant information nor that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent prediction model\. We introduce Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning \(HIJP\), a search\-free framework that addresses both aspects during training\. HIJP relabels future observations along offline trajectories as goals, providing action supervision across multiple temporal horizons\. By retaining gradients through the goal representations, this supervision directly shapes the visual representation\. HIJP further feeds predicted actions into the latent predictor model and aligns the resulting next\-state representations with encoded successor observations, enforcing action\-transition consistency\. At inference time, the inverse dynamics model and latent predictor models are applied alternately to generate multi\-step action sequences without online search\. Across four visual control tasks, HIJP achieves 86\.8% overall success and a 1\.9\-16\.5x planning speedup over search\-based planning\.

## [MULTIMODAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR PREDICTING HAIR FOLLICLE SURVIVAL AND AESTHETIC OUTCOMES FOLLOWING HAIR TRANSPLANTATION SURGERY](../publications/926bc746805860ccadb6.md)

Jawad Jahangir; Ali Raza

Background: Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has considerable potential to support outcome assessment in hair transplantation; however, its clinical reliability depends on the availability of complete, standardized, and appropriately linked patient\-level data\. Despite growing interest in AI\-assisted aesthetic and clinical assessment, the readiness of currently reported hair\-transplantation data for predictive and multimodal modelling remains insufficiently characterized\. Objective: This study aimed to quantitatively assess the completeness, consistency, and multimodal readiness of literature\-derived hair\-transplantation data, with particular emphasis on hair survival, patient satisfaction, follow\-up reporting, and the availability of clinical and trichoscopic imaging features\. Methods: A descriptive data\-readiness assessment was conducted using 36 literature\-derived records extracted from three published studies\. An additional 1,000 simulated records were maintained separately for technical testing and excluded from all clinical summaries\. Data completeness, variable availability, outcome distributions, and reporting inconsistencies were examined using descriptive statistics\. No missing values were imputed, and no predictive model was trained or validated\. The analysis therefore focused on characterizing the strengths and limitations of the available data for future AI development\. Results: Numerical hair\-survival values were available for 26 of the 36 literature\-derived records \(72\.2%\)\. Among these records, mean hair survival was 85\.30% \(standard deviation \[SD\], 10\.60\), with a median of 85\.90% and a range of 45\.1%–96\.8%\. Satisfaction information was available for 27 records, comprising 17 classified as mostly satisfied, seven as very satisfied, and three as dissatisfied\. Although 24 of these 27 records carried favorable satisfaction labels \(88\.9%\), differences in reporting and the absence of a standardized assessment instrument limit direct clinical interpretation\. Follow\-up information was recorded for 27 records, but some entries represented study\-level reporting intervals rather than verified patient\-specific assessments\. Most importantly, no original clinical or trichoscopic images were available in the analyzed dataset, and key imaging\-derived features including vascularity, fibrosis, and trichoscopic characteristics were absent\. These limitations restrict outcome comparability and prevent the construction of a genuinely linked multimodal dataset from the available records\. Conclusion: This study identifies a substantial data\-readiness gap between the potential of AI in hair transplantation and the structure of currently available literature\-derived data\. Although reported hair\-survival values provide a preliminary descriptive benchmark, incomplete outcome reporting, inconsistent assessment definitions, uncertain patient\-level follow\-up alignment, and absent linked imaging data constrain robust predictive modelling\. Progress toward clinically credible AI systems will require standardized outcome definitions, source\-verified patient\-level data, harmonized follow\-up schedules, and prospectively linked clinical and trichoscopic images\. The findings provide a practical basis for designing future datasets and validation studies before predictive AI claims can be justified\.

## [Predictive Analytics in Talent Acquisition: Evaluating Digital Selection Frameworks and Internal Marketing at HDFC Life Insurance](../publications/92717f3bf91ee990c3e5.md)

Prof\. Ketaki Kukde Hina Wasudeo Dhawas

The contemporary insurance sector, characterized by high attrition and intense competition for specialized talent, necessitates a paradigm shift from reactive recruitment to proactive, data\-driven talent acquisition\. This research investigates the integration of predictive analytics and digital selection frameworks at HDFC Life Insurance, examining their dual impact on operational recruitment efficiency and internal employer branding\. Utilizing a mixed\-methods approach comprising quantitative HRIS data analysis and qualitative employee sentiment evaluation, this study develops a machine\-learning\-informed conceptual model for predicting candidate success and tenure\. The findings suggest that algorithmic candidate profiling not only accelerates the time\-to\-hire by 28% but also significantly aligns candidate values with the organizational culture, acting as a potent tool for internal marketing\. Furthermore, the deployment of transparent, AIdriven selection processes enhances perceived organizational justice, thereby strengthening the employer brand from within\. This paper provides a comprehensive framework bridging human resources technology and strategic marketing, offering actionable insights for optimizing the employee lifecycle in the financial services industry\.

## [Graph neural networks for transmission grid topology control: Busbar information asymmetry and heterogeneous representations](../publications/928067f2b05a285ea1d4.md)

Matthijs de Jong; Jan Viebahn; Yuliya Shapovalova

Factors such as the proliferation of renewable energy and electrification contribute to grid congestion which is a pressing problem\. Topology control is an appealing method for relieving congestion, but traditional approaches for topology discovery have proven too slow for practical applications\. Recent research has focused on machine learning \(ML\) as an efficient alternative\. Due to their ability to model the graph structure of power grids, graph neural networks \(GNNs\) are particularly well\-suited for topology control applications\. This study investigates different graph representations of the power grid for topology control with GNNs\. We identify an information flow problem inherent to the popular homogeneous graph representation and propose a heterogeneous graph representation that resolves said problem\. We apply GNNs with both graph representations and a fully connected neural network \(FCNN\) baseline to an imitation learning task\. The models are evaluated by classification accuracy and the percentage of successful grid operation days\. We find that heterogeneous GNNs perform the best, followed by FCNNs, and lastly, homogeneous GNNs\. We also find that both GNN types generalize better to unseen network configurations than FCNNs\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Digital Image Forgery Detection](../publications/92814960a2a5416b775e.md)

Shreyas Shinde; Sanika Lomate; Shreya Matkar; Prof\. Vijaya Jadhav

With the growing use of digital images in online communication and social media, verifying whether an image is authentic has become increasingly important\. Image manipulation techniques such as copy\-move, splicing, inpainting, and object removal can change the meaning of visual information\. At the same time, JPEG compression and repeated recompression can weaken the forensic traces that are useful for detection\. This review looks at two AI\-based approaches for detecting digital image forgery\. The first study combines Error Level Analysis \(ELA\) with the VGG\-16 convolutional neural network to classify images as original or tampered\. The second study focuses on compressed images shared through social networks and uses a modified ShuffleNet V2 architecture for lightweight forgery classification\. The two studies are reviewed based on their objectives, datasets, preprocessing or feature representation, deep learning architecture, compression conditions, findings, and limitations\. The comparison shows that ELA with VGG\-16 can help expose compression\-related manipulation artifacts, while the modified ShuffleNet V2 approach focuses on the practical challenge of detecting forgery after JPEG and social\-network recompression\. The review highlights dataset diversity, compression robustness, computational efficiency, and generalization across different manipulation and sharing conditions as important research gaps\. Keywords— Artificial Intelligence, Digital Image Forgery, Deep Learning, Error Level Analysis, VGG\-16,ShuffleNet V2, Image Compression\.

## [Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts](../publications/928da03a928627ef9288.md)

Alina Khaybullina

Which inputs drive a language model&\#x27;s financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20\-day momentum, non\-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus\. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families \(0\.49\-7\.61B base parameters\) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct\-answer Q8\_0 protocol\. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes\. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion\. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer\-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities\. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from \-0\.19 to 86\.80 percentage points\. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5\. Natural\-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51\.0 to 95\.8 percent\. Answer\-encoding, wording, context, and conversion controls qualify these results\. The experiment measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition; it establishes neither an internal reasoning mechanism nor realized return predictability\. Public benchmark prompts, recorded scores, and an interactive recorded\-results explorer accompany the study\.

## [Case Report: Spinal cord herniation associated with ankylosing spondylitis](../publications/92912c7ec9b04fc4bec1.md)

Zekai Ke; Chunguang Duan

Background Spinal cord herniation \(SCH\) is a rare clinical entity characterized by the ventral displacement of the spinal cord through a dural defect\. While often classified as idiopathic, SCH associated with ankylosing spondylitis \(AS\) is exceedingly rare\. The pathogenesis in such cases remains unclear, and treatment strategies are not well standardized\. Case presentation Herein, we report a series of four patients with long\-standing ankylosing spondylitis who presented with SCH between August 2018 and August 2021\. All patients exhibited severe thoracolumbar kyphosis and restricted spinal mobility\. Uniquely, the herniations occurred at the vertebral body level rather than the disc level, and one patient presented with rare multilevel herniations\. Two patients underwent pedicle subtraction osteotomy \(PSO\) with spinal fusion\. In both surgical cases, direct dural repair was avoided; stabilization was achieved through indirect cord relaxation via spinal column shortening\. Postoperative imaging showed successful kyphosis correction and stabilization of the herniation\. Conclusion SCH in patients with AS is a distinct entity secondary to inflammatory and biomechanical changes\. PSO with fusion is a viable surgical option that addresses both deformity and cord tethering through an indirect mechanism\.

## [FlexUMM: Flexible Representation Learning for Unified Multimodal Models](../publications/9292ace37b5435053851.md)

Yinyi Luo; Haoyue Bai; Yi Ge; Nilton Cesar Rojas Vales; Marios Savvides; Jindong Wang

Unified multimodal models \(UMMs\) can integrate understanding and generation within a single backbone\. However, it is commonly known that these two capabilities can cause conflicting representations, leading to a central question: how representation and computation should be shared across functionalities? Existing UMMs often rely on a largely fixed structure, where different inputs and functionalities follow the same depth and parameter\-sharing pattern\. We argue that this assumption is too restrictive: more effective unification requires sharing the computation that supports cross\-functional communication while specializing the capacity that becomes task\- or input\-specific\. We introduce FlexUMM, a flexible UMM framework that dynamically decides when to preserve shared computation, when to route specialized capacity, and when to stop further processing\. Evidence shows that this flexible allocation improves UMMs along two complementary axes\. It improves accuracy by reducing harmful competition between functionalities, and it improves efficiency by avoiding unnecessary computation once an input representation is sufficiently mature\. Beyond simple architectural unification from the pre\-trained models, FlexUMM works as a model\-agnostic, functional plug\-in to make existing UMMs more unified, stronger, and efficient\. Code is available at: https://github\.com/AIFrontierLab/TorchUMM/tree/main/src/umm/post\_training/flexumm\.

## [Professional Readiness and Implementation Barriers for Non\-invasive Neuromodulation Among Attendees of an Educational Module in Mexico: An Exploratory Cross\-sectional Survey](../publications/92932a849759e8152d69.md)

Eleonora Ocampo\-Coronado; Daniel San‐Juan; Paola Denisse Ascencio\-Ceja; Alan Hinojosa Godínez; Carlos Trenado; Cristina Nachely Subia\-Castro; Luis Fernando Díaz\-López; Jesús Alejandro Aldana\-López; Alejandro Velasco\-Hernandez; Manuel Zorrilla\-Hernandez

Background: Non\-invasive neuromodulation is increasingly used in selected neuropsychiatric disorders, but implementation depends on professional readiness, training, access, perceived legitimacy, and local feasibility\. This study assessed knowledge, perceptions, barriers, baseline willingness to recommend neuromodulation, and future implementation or referral intention among attendees of an educational neuromodulation module in Mexico\. Methods: We conducted an exploratory cross\-sectional survey among attendees of an in\-person educational neuromodulation module at a specialized academic congress in Mexico\. Anonymous, real\-time items assessed baseline familiarity; perceptions of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, transcranial direct current stimulation, and transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation; perceived barriers; baseline willingness to recommend neuromodulation; and future implementation or referral intention\. Analyses used descriptive statistics, non\-parametric tests, Spearman correlations, and exploratory univariate logistic regression\. Results: A total of 111 participants answered at least one item\. Baseline familiarity was limited: 22\.2% reported basic knowledge, and 84\.6% strongly disagreed that they had personal equipment\. Baseline willingness to recommend neuromodulation was 63\.2% and was associated with basic knowledge \(OR = 2\.90; 95% CI = 1\.44–5\.84; p = \.003\), prior exposure \(OR = 1\.58; 95% CI = 1\.07–2\.35; p = \.023\), and perceived sufficiency of evidence \(OR = 1\.91; 95% CI = 1\.21–2\.99; p = \.005\)\. The main barriers were cost/accessibility \(78\.0%\), patients’ lack of knowledge \(36\.6%\), and lack of technical training \(29\.3%\)\. Final\-block implementation\-intention findings were exploratory because of the small effective denominator\. Conclusions: Among attendees of an educational neuromodulation module in Mexico, receptivity toward non\-invasive neuromodulation was favorable, but operational readiness was limited\. Responsible implementation may benefit from competency\-based training, referral pathways, patient education, regulatory literacy, and sustainable access models\.

## [RESULTS OF SURGICAL TREATMENT OF PRIMARY MALIGNANT AND METASTATIC TUMORS OF THE HUMERAL DIAPHYSIS](../publications/92aab5ca401e2fbabab4.md)

Volodymyr V\. Protsenko; V\.V\. Voloshin A\.E\. Volkov; Yuriy L\. Sobolevskiy; Andrii S\. Kukharuk; Yevgen Solonitsyn

Introduction\. The view on the surgical treatment of primary malignant and metastatic tumors of the diaphyseal zone of the humerus after resection of the malignant tumor is ambiguous, the optimal choice of reconstructive method remains debatable due to the risk of complications and recurrence\. Aim\. To evaluate the results of treatment of patients with tumors of the humerus diaphysis in order to select methods of surgical treatment of tumors of this location\.Materials and methods\. We present 29 patients from three clinical groups who underwent different surgical treatment methods for primary malignant and metastatic bone tumors with damage to the diaphysis of the humerus\. The functional outcome of the limb was determined by the MSTS scale, the degree of pain syndrome was determined by the R\.G\. Watkins scale, the quality of life of patients was determined by the EORTC QLQ–C30 questionnaire, and patient survival was determined by the Kaplan\-Meier method\.Results\. The functional outcome of the operated upper limb \(according to the MSTS score\) after endoprosthetic replacement of the humeral shaft ranged from 84% to 91\.2%; after reinforced metal osteosynthesis, from 70% to 86%; and after transosseous extrafocal osteosynthesis using a rod external fixation device, from 66% to 72\.4%\. Patients’ quality of life \(according to the EORTC QLQ\-C30\) improved after endoprosthetic replacement of the humeral shaft from 30 to 80 points, after reinforced osteosynthesis from 40 to 72 points, and after transosseous extrafocal osteosynthesis from 30 to 66 points\. The three\-year overall survival rate of patients in the group after endoprosthetics was 81\.8±13\.6%, in the group after reinforced osteosynthesis – 62\.7±15\.8%, in the group after the use of external fixation devices – 12\.2±11\.1% \(p&gt;0\.05\)\.Conclusions\. Segmental resection of the humeral shaft followed by reconstruction using an individual segmental endoprosthesis is indicated for primary malignant tumors\. Metal osteosynthesis using a rod external fixation device is indicated for multiple bone metastases when a pathological fracture has occurred, in order to allow radiotherapy to the metastatic lesion in the humerus and subsequent limb\-sparing reconstructive surgery\.

## [Gender sensitivity and its implementation in inpatient cardiology: a mixed\-methods study of patient and healthcare professional perspectives](../publications/92c0260b1dc5f4db3641.md)

Sophia Sgraja; Judith Mollenhauer; Martina Kloepfer; Ute Seeland; Clarissa Kurscheid; Volker Eric Amelung

Background Gender\-sensitive personalized care \(GSC\+\) is a core component of people\-centered healthcare and health equity\. Evidence from cardiovascular research demonstrates relevant sex\- and gender\-related differences in symptom presentation, diagnostics, treatment response, and outcomes\. These differences are increasingly acknowledged in clinical practice guidelines and nursing expert standards\. However, despite growing integration into guideline recommendations, translation into routine clinical practice remains inconsistent\. Empirical data integrating both patient and healthcare professional perspectives on guideline\-based gender\-sensitive care are still limited\. Methods This exploratory mixed\-methods study synthesizes findings from the German health services research project HeartGap \(funding number: 01VSF22030; DRKS00031317\)\. The study comprised \(1\) a scoping review on measures, facilitators, and barriers to implementing GSC\+, \(2\) qualitative expert interviews and focus groups with physicians and nurses, and \(3\) nationwide surveys with physicians \( n = 155\), nurses \( n = 111\), and cardiology inpatients \( n = 390\)\. Gender sensitivity among healthcare professionals was assessed using the Nijmegen Gender Awareness in Medicine Scale \(N\-GAMS\), alongside measures of perceived implementation of GSC\+\. Patient perspectives were analyzed descriptively and using multivariate regression models\. Results Healthcare professionals demonstrated moderate to high gender sensitivity \(physicians: M = 3\.95, SD = 0\.73; nurses: M = 3\.46, SD = 0\.76\)\. Perceived implementation of GSC\+ was substantially lower, particularly among physicians \( M = 2\.45, SD = 0\.59\), compared with nurses \( M = 2\.91, SD = 0\.81\) and patients \( M = 3\.04, SD = 0\.65\)\. Higher gender sensitivity did not correspond with higher perceived implementation, indicating a disconnect between attitudes and practice\. Although guideline\-based knowledge on sex\- and gender\-related aspects was moderate to high, its translation into routine clinical practice remained limited\. Patients evaluated GSC\+ positively and reported comparatively low additional needs\. Across methods, structural constraints, insufficient operationalization of guideline recommendations, and limited institutional embedding emerged as key barriers\. Conclusion Organizational, structural, and systemic barriers were consistently identified across study components as relevant factors associated with implementation gaps in GSC\+ rather than by negative attitudes or lack of awareness among healthcare professionals\. Strengthening the evidence base, operationalizing gender\-sensitive recommendations, and embedding GSC\+ into organizational routines and education are essential to advance people\-centered, equitable, and safe cardiology care\.

## [A responsabilidade civil médica no Brasil sobre erro de diagnóstico assistido por Inteligência Artificial](../publications/92e4103acdce9e670648.md)

Luísa de Castro Bezerra

This study analyzes medical civil liability in Brazil for diagnostic errors assisted by Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)\. There is a growing use of AI in the healthcare sector, where,through databases and pattern recognition, it is possible to reach diagnoses within minutes\. Although the benefits of innovation are widely recognized, concerns about regulating its use—especially in high\-risk activities such as healthcare—are increasing\. This research adopts an exploratory and qualitative approach, aiming to provide aninitial understanding of a still underdeveloped topic\. The analysis is based on relevant national sources, with emphasis on Bill No\. 2,338/2023, which proposes a regulatory framework for Artificial Intelligence in Brazil, as well as international references such as European Union legislation and recommendations from the World HealthOrganization \(WHO\)\. The examined documents highlight challenges to traditional civil liability\. These include the control problem, as AI systems operate autonomously andmay evolve unpredictably; opacity, which hinders understanding of the decisionmaking process; and the multiplicity of agents involved, which dilutes the attribution of responsibility\. Such factors render the application of classical civil liability models insufficient\. The Brazilian proposal establishes strict liability for high\-risk AI systems,distributed according to each party’s contribution to the harm\. However, proving such contribution may be excessively burdensome\. Therefore, although there is a tendency for legal systems to adapt, definitive answers remain uncertain, and this study aims to support further reflection and future research\.

## [Algorithmic management and gig workers&\#x27; workplace wellbeing: the moderating role of psychological resilience](../publications/92e909c04911cfc1024a.md)

Zha Xiaofang; Zhang Yue; Dan Zhang; Feng Xinying; SUZIANA MAT YASIN

This study examines how algorithmic management in the gig economy is related to gig workers&\#x27; workplace wellbeing\. Specifically, we explore how algorithmic management corresponds with \(positive\) challenge appraisal and \(negative\) threat appraisal\. We also examine the moderating role of psychological resilience in these relationships, as well as the implications of appraisal processes for workplace wellbeing\. Data were collected from 389 food delivery workers in China\. We find that algorithmic management is positively associated with both challenge appraisal and threat appraisal\. Challenge appraisal is positively associated with workplace wellbeing, whereas threat appraisal is negatively associated with workplace wellbeing\. Psychological resilience strengthens the challenge\-appraisal pathway and the corresponding positive indirect relationship with workplace wellbeing, but it does not significantly buffer the threat\-appraisal pathway\. These findings show that algorithmic management is associated with both positive and negative appraisal processes and that psychological resilience may play different roles across these pathways\. The study therefore offers a more nuanced explanation of the relationship between algorithmic management and gig workers&\#x27; workplace wellbeing\.

## [الإسراء والمعراج وأدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تمثيل الأوصاف المادية&quot;](../publications/92f055e7a0cee267229c.md)

سوسن عباس حسين; هدى سعيد مهدي الشهرستاني

تعد حادثة الاسراء من معجزات الله سبحانه وتعالى وآياته التي خص بها نبيه الكريم محمد \(صلى الله عليه واله وسلم\) وذلك تكريما وتعظيما لمقامه، وقد بدأت رحلة الرسول الكريم \(صلوات الله عليه وسلامه\) من المسجد الحرام الى المسجد الأقصى، بصحبه جبريل \(عليه السلام\)، ثم عرج به الى السماء السابعة، وهناك شهد فيها عجائب الله تعالى، والتقى بالأنبياء الذين سبقوه، وقد رفعه الله الى مقام الاعلى وكلمه بدون حجاب، وقد أشار القران الكريم صراحة الى هذه الحادثة في سورة الاسراء بقوله تعالى ﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾

## [Building Educational Excellence through Competency\-Based Talent Acquisition for Educators and Educational Staff](../publications/92fca9be612b3dfcc66b.md)

Mahrus Ali; Zainul Mun’im; Zohaib Hassan Sain

This study aims to construct a Competency\-Based Talent Acquisition model as a strategy for fostering educational excellence through the management of educators and educational staff that is oriented toward competencies and the strategic needs of educational institutions\. This study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design to construct the Competency\-Based Talent Acquisition model for fostering educational excellence\. The research was conducted over a period of one month at SMP Negeri 3 Rogojampi, Banyuwangi, involving four informants selected through purposive sampling: the principal, the vice principal for curriculum, a senior teacher, and the head of administrative staff\. Data were collected through semi\-structured interviews, non\-participant observation, and documentation\. Data analysis utilized the interactive model proposed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through open coding, axial coding, and selective coding, with data validity ensured through triangulation and member checking\. The results of this study indicate that Competency\-Based Talent Acquisition is an effective strategy for building educational excellence through three main components: competency mapping, strategic talent identification, and continuous talent development\. These three components form an integrated talent management system, ranging from mapping competency needs and identifying talent based on competencies to continuous professional development\. These findings expand the perspectives of Competency\-Based Human Resource Management and Strategic Talent Management by constructing a Competency\-Based Talent Acquisition model as a framework for human resource management in educational institutions\. This model offers practical implications for the development of talent acquisition policies that are more systematic, adaptive, and oriented toward the continuous improvement of quality\.

## [Readability, reliability, and quality of AI\-Generated responses on pelvic congestion syndrome: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT, gemini, and perplexity](../publications/930ac36bcf4314bba321.md)

Emre Sertel

Objective Pelvic congestion syndrome \(PCS\) is a vascular cause of chronic pelvic pain arising from ovarian and pelvic venous insufficiency, typically presenting as dull, aching pelvic pain that worsens with prolonged standing, physical activity, and the premenstrual period, and is particularly common among multiparous women of reproductive age\. Online health information on this condition is frequently accessed by both patients and healthcare professionals\. This study aimed to evaluate the readability, quality, and reliability of responses generated by three popular artificial intelligence \(AI\) chatbots—ChatGPT\-4o, Gemini, and Perplexity—regarding the most commonly asked questions on PCS\. Methods From 25 PCS\-related keywords identified through Google Trends, duplicates and irrelevant terms were excluded, yielding a final set of 18 keywords\. These were separately submitted to the three AI chatbots\. Readability was assessed using the Gunning Fog Index \(GFOG\), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook \(SMOG\), and Flesch Reading Ease Score \(FRES\), among other indices, calculated via two independent readability tools\. Quality was measured using the Global Quality Score \(GQS\) and the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients \(EQIP\) tool, while reliability was assessed with the Journal of the American Medical Association \(JAMA\) benchmark criteria and the modified DISCERN instrument\. Results Readability analyses revealed that all chatbot responses significantly exceeded the sixth\-grade level recommended by the AMA and NIH \(p &lt; \.001\)\. ChatGPT\-4o achieved the highest readability on the CLI and ARI, whereas Gemini performed better on the remaining indices, and Perplexity consistently produced the most complex responses\. Among the three evaluated freely accessible platforms, Perplexity achieved the highest scores on several quality and reliability measures \(JAMA, DISCERN, and GQS\), while Gemini outperformed the others on EQIP scoring\. Conclusion Although AI chatbots hold promise for providing accessible information on PCS, their readability levels remain above recommended standards, and overall quality scores are suboptimal\. Producing clearer, more balanced, and more reliable content could enhance the contribution of these technologies to public health\.

## [DECISÕES ESTATAIS AUTOMATIZADAS E O DEVIDO PROCESSO CONSTITUCIONAL: LIMITES DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO EXERCÍCIO DA FUNÇÃO ADMINISTRATIVA](../publications/93136223c459fc688847.md)

Camile Costa Leite Sousa; Clóvis Marques Dias Júnior

O presente artigo analisa os limites constitucionais impostos ao uso da inteligência artificial no exercício da função administrativa, tendo como problema central identificar que limites o devido processo constitucional impõe às decisões administrativas automatizadas, especialmente quanto à motivação, ao contraditório, à ampla defesa e à impessoalidade\. A pesquisa examina experiências documentadas de automação administrativa, com destaque para o reconhecimento automático de direitos pelo Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social e para os sistemas de análise e seleção utilizados pela administração tributária, e as confronta com a Constituição Federal, a Lei nº 9\.784/1999, a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados, a jurisprudência do Supremo Tribunal Federal e referências do direito comparado\. Os parâmetros propostos são então aplicados ao caso do reconhecimento automático de direitos, com base em relatório de auditoria do órgão\. Utiliza\-se o método dedutivo, mediante pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, com exame de doutrina de direito administrativo e de direito digital, de legislação, de jurisprudência e de documentos institucionais\. Os resultados indicam que a automação pode contribuir para a eficiência e a padronização, mas não afasta os deveres jurídicos de motivação, transparência, possibilidade de contestação, supervisão humana e responsabilização\. Conclui\-se que o emprego de sistemas automatizados pela Administração Pública é juridicamente possível, desde que estruturado segundo parâmetros de explicabilidade, acesso aos critérios relevantes, auditoria, avaliação de impacto e revisão humana proporcional ao risco e à natureza do ato administrativo\.

## [Adoption of robot\-assisted minimally invasive surgery across surgical specialties in France: a nationwide population\-based study](../publications/93191124d7e9d6e0df63.md)

Anaïs Havet; François Bettega; Violaine Fernandez; Clara Bouvard; Cécile Payet; Jean‐Christophe Lifante; Christophe Trésallet; Laurent Brunaud; Xavier Armoiry; Marie Viprey

Robotic minimally invasive surgery has been used in France for nearly two decades, with monitoring enabled by the National Health Data System \(SNDS\) since March 2020\. No French study has comprehensively described robotic procedures, including ENT, at a fine geographical scale\. We aimed to assess the use of robotic and non\-robotic minimally invasive surgery over time and across French departments \(administrative subdivisions\), describe patient and healthcare facility characteristics and investigate determinants of robotic surgery use\. We identified adults undergoing robotic or non\-robotic minimally invasive procedures in urology, gynaecology, digestive, thoracic, and ENT specialties between January 2017 and June 2023\. From July 2020, robotic surgery use was described by specialty, quarter and department, and temporal trends were assessed using SARIMA models\. Determinants of robotic surgery use were identified by specialty using multivariable logistic regression models\. Between January 2017 and June 2023, 914,350 minimally invasive surgeries were performed, including 432,505 from July 2020 onwards, of which 19\.2% were robotic\. This proportion varied by specialty \(urology: 63\.6%, thoracic surgery: 18\.5%, ENT: 16\.8%, gynaecology: 9\.7%, digestive surgery: 6\.5%\)\. Across all specialties, the proportion of robotic surgeries increased by 0\.66% points per quarter\. Minimally invasive surgery volume and robotic surgery use varied substantially across departments\. Robotic surgery use was associated with patient sociodemographic characteristics and facility characteristics \(facility type, number of beds and surgical volume\)\. Robotic surgery use is increasing in France, with substantial variation across specialties, departments, patient and healthcare facility characteristics\. Further studies on safety and effectiveness are needed to complement real\-world monitoring\.

## [The Tensed Computer Improviser and the workmanship of risk: Small\-dataset machine learning and real\-time interactive musical improvisation](../publications/9321c22b3ad611cae860.md)

Taylor Brook

Abstract Generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) has entered music overwhelmingly by way of large industrial models trained on vast corpora, in which the outcome is fixed in advance by an apparatus that the musician neither controls nor understands\. This article argues that the essential machine\-learning operations of dataset assembly, feature extraction and model fitting can instead be utilised transparently as part of an artist’s creative practice\. Looking to David Pye’s concepts of workmanship of certainty and workmanship of risk , this article examines the design of the Tensed Computer Improviser \(TCI\), an open\-source machine improviser built in Max with the Fluid Corpus Manipulation \(FluCoMa\) toolkit, which trains models from a small audio corpus of the user’s own choosing, with no pretrained component and no external training stage\. Situating the TCI within a genealogy of machine improvisation using small data, the article analyses its design through the vocabulary of craft where the corpus curation and training are integrated into the creative act and the characteristic errors of small data are welcomed as tool\-marks\.
