## [Naudé, Wim: Artificial intelligence vs COVID\-19: limitations, constraints and pitfalls](../publications/93319244d3078df8ddb4.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 35 \(3\):761\-765\. 2020This paper provides an early evaluation of Artificial Intelligence against COVID\-19\. The main areas where AI can contribute to the fight against COVID\-19 are discussed\. It is concluded that AI has not yet been impactful against COVID\-19\. Its use is hampered by a lack of data, and by too much data\. Overcoming these constraints will require a careful balance between data privacy and public health, and rigorous human\-AI interaction\. It is unlikely that these will be addressed in time to be of much help during the present pandemic\. In the meantime, extensive gathering of diagnostic data on who is infectious will be essential to save lives, train AI, and limit economic damages\. \(direct link \)

## [Computational Intelligence and Python Programming](../publications/93375225a862d4f6c358.md)

Suryanarayana Reddy V\.; Srinivasa Rao Dr\.K\.V\.; Vinod Kumar Thambi; Yadunanda Kumar A; Suneel Ramireddy

This book on computational intelligence and Python programming serve as comprehensive guides to nature\-inspired computing, machine learning, and advancedproblem\-solving techniques\. The first core focus of such a text establishes the theoretical foundation of computational intelligence \(CI\), covering key paradigms likeartificial neural networks, fuzzy logic systems, evolutionary algorithms \(such asgenetic algorithms\), and swarm intelligence\. Rather than relying on rigid algorithmic rules, these books explain how computers mimic biological processes to adapt,learn, and make decisions under uncertain or incomplete data conditions\.The second core focus bridges these theoretical concepts directly into practicethrough hands\-on Python programming\. Utilizing ecosystem libraries like NumPy,SciPy, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and specialized CI packages, the text guides readersthrough building, training, and optimizing intelligent models from scratch\. Bycombining mathematical rigor with clear code examples, it enables developers, datascientists, and researchers to design scalable applications across predictive analytics,robotics, natural language processing, and automated decision\-making systems\.

## [The Importance of Utilizing Innovative Methods in the Management of Cultural Institutions](../publications/933d9f94c61ea3960f6b.md)

Xolmuminov Muminmirzo

This article analyzes the significance of employing innovative methods and approaches to enhance the management framework of cultural institutions under contemporary conditions, alongside the practical issues surrounding their implementation\. The study provides a scientific rationale for transitioning the cultural sector toward financial autonomy and self\-sustainability\. Furthermore, it scientifically and practically substantiates the modernization of organizational and economic mechanisms in the field, including the integration of “Art Management” principles, the expansion of “Creative Industry” sectors, and the acceleration of scientific\-practical “Project Commercialization” processes\. ## [Mapping the Intellectual Capital Research Landscape: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Contributions, and Future Research Directions](../publications/934bf35ac2e1ade4fa58.md)

Rashida Farsath

Intellectual capital has become an important source of value creation and competitive advantage in knowledge\-intensive economies, where organizational performance increasingly depends on the effective use of knowledge\-based and other intangible resources\. This study maps the development and structure of intellectual capital research through a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Scopus database\. The search strategy used combinations of keywords relating to intellectual capital, human capital, structural capital, intangible assets, and value added\. After the application of publication\-type, subject\-area, and language filters, the final dataset comprised 787 English\-language journal articles\. Publication trends, journal distribution, institutional and country contributions, influential documents, co\-citation patterns, keyword co\-occurrence, and international collaboration were examined using Excel, VOSviewer, R, and Biblioshiny\. The findings show a marked expansion of intellectual capital scholarship, particularly from 2015 onward, with annual scientific production reaching 84 articles in 2024\. The 787 articles were distributed across 306 journals, while the Journal of Intellectual Capital was the leading publication outlet in the dataset\. India recorded the highest number of publications among the countries listed, whereas Taiwan had the highest total citations in the country\-level citation comparison\. Highly cited foundational studies and co\-citation patterns point to the continuing influence of work on intellectual capital measurement, including the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient \(VAIC\) approach\. Keyword co\- occurrence revealed interconnected themes concerning intellectual capital and firm performance, human and structural capital, relational capital, knowledge management, innovation, intangible assets, disclosure, and value creation\. The collaboration map also indicates cross\-country research links, although the distribution of contributions varies across institutions and regions\. Overall, the study provides a structured overview of the intellectual capital research landscape and identifies opportunities to extend the field through stronger cross\-country collaboration, broader measurement approaches, and greater attention to contemporary issues such as artificial intelligence, digital transformation, financial distress, and the strategic management of intangible resources\. These directions may help researchers develop a more integrated understanding of how intellectual capital is measured, deployed, and associated with organizational outcomes\.

## [Integrating Multimodal Technologies and Generative Artificial Intelligence into Professionally Oriented English Language Training of Future Officers of the Armed Forces of Ukraine: Theoretical Foundations](../publications/934c92feca6a053cbdbb.md)

Ганна Жиздюк

The article aims to substantiate the theoretical foundations for integrating multimodal technologies and generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) into cadets&\#x27; English language training oriented towards the descriptors of Standardized Language Proficiency Level 2 under the NATO standard STANAG 6001\. The study used terminological and comparative analysis of regulatory documents and research publications, systematisation, generalisation and pedagogical design\. The conceptual framework is refined: language activity and its types, language competence, standardized language level and profile, mode, multimodal technologies, GenAI, AI\-mediated learning, the mode of permissible GenAI use, and integration\. The standardized language profile is treated as a measure of general foreign language proficiency in the four types of language activity that does not cover all components of professional communicative competence\. The Law of Ukraine &quot;On Academic Integrity&quot; links the legitimacy of auxiliary tools to the rules of a task, so the GenAI mode stated in a task instruction has legal significance\. The study substantiates seven functions of multimodal technologies and GenAI with limits of assistance, eight integration principles and four modes of GenAI use, which differ in what GenAI does with the cadet&\#x27;s language material and can be combined\. Five pedagogical conditions are defined with organisational support and indicators of implementation\. A six\-step sequence of scenario\-based learning is proposed and illustrated with the task design &quot;Reporting an Equipment Problem before a Joint Training Session&quot;: a photo shows the equipment damage, the cadet explains the circumstances orally and in writing, GenAI only asks clarifying questions, and the cadet conducts the final conversation without AI or preparation in a new situation with different equipment, addressee and constraints; the control stages without AI are performed in class under the instructor&\#x27;s supervision\. The novelty lies in the theoretical and methodological specification of known approaches for future officers&\#x27; English language training; provisions borrowed from the DARE\-HS \(Descriptor Alignment, Authentic Performance, Responsible Use, Evaluation and Reflection, Human Supervision, Security\) framework and other studies are clearly distinguished from adapted and proposed ones\. Language instructors at higher military educational institutions can use the results to design tasks for the penultimate semester, formulate GenAI rules in course syllabi and develop professional development programmes\. The effectiveness of the proposed solutions requires empirical verification\.

## [A primary cell culture platform for studying venom gland and brain tissue in octopus](../publications/9356780ea465e6ec5826.md)

James V\. Parziale; Saurabh S\. Attarde; Fatima Khalid; Pollena Devi Sangana; Mandë Holford

Coleoid cephalopods, squids, cuttlefish, and octopuses, have emerged as powerful model organisms for studying neurobiology, development, and behavior, however, cellular tools for investigating their specialized tissues remain limited\. In particular, their venom producing gland, the posterior salivary gland \(PSG\), has been extensively described anatomically and histologically, yet remains largely inaccessible to experimental investigation at the cellular level\. Here, we report the first establishment of primary cell cultures derived from both the optic lobe \(OL\) and PSG tissues of Octopus bimaculoides \. Building on recent advances in cephalopod brain cultures, we adapted and optimized dissociation and culture conditions to support short\-term survival and attachment of cells in vitro\. We show that passive cell release during tissue handling, rather than enzymatic treatment, yields viable cultures from both tissues, and poly\-D\-lysine markedly improves the adherence of PSG\-derived cells\. Morphological analyses and fluorescent staining confirm the presence and viability of distinct cell populations, while cell cycle analysis indicates that the majority of cells reside in G 0 /G 1 phase\. Notably, O\. bimaculoides OL cultures share several features with the recently described squid brain cultures, including passive cell release, and an adherent fibroblast\-like cell population, but additionally contain a predominant population of spherical cells, suggesting both conserved and species\-specific coleoid cell behavior in vitro\. Together, our findings establish a foundational in vitro platform for studying octopus venom and neural cell biology, providing a tractable system for probing venom biosynthesis, secretion, and neural regulation in coleoid cephalopods\.

## [The reference shapes the signal: chrX genotype summaries and classifier sex disparity between GRCh38 and T2T\-CHM13 callsets](../publications/93698fc70ab888d23d95.md)

R\. Craig Stillwell

Laboratories that move from GRCh38 to T2T\-CHM13 take on a new callset as well as a new assembly\. I asked whether the move changes sex\-chromosome genotype summaries, and whether it changes how well classifiers trained on those summaries serve males and females\. I compared the published 1000 Genomes GRCh38 and T2T\-CHM13 callsets for 3,202 people\. The two callsets come from different alignment, calling, phasing and filtering workflows, so every difference below belongs to the reference and its pipeline together\. In women, the fraction of non\-reference chrX genotypes that were heterozygous was 0\.605 on GRCh38 and 0\.644 on T2T\. It fell in African\-ancestry women and rose in the other four superpopulations\. The rise came from fewer non\-reference homozygous genotypes \(\- 7,757 per woman\) and not from more heterozygous ones \(\- 1,504\)\. Five classifier families were trained on six chrX summaries to predict superpopulation, and the male\-female gap in balanced accuracy was compared between callsets\. Women were classified better than men under both callsets\. Logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost widened that gap on T2T, and the support vector machine and the perceptron narrowed it\. After correction across all 20 tests, random forest, XGBoost and the support vector machine remained significant\. Separating relatives did not remove the disagreement\. Classifiers built from the first 500 common SNPs per chromosome in file order showed no change after correction\. The gap measures model performance, not biological sex bias\. Resolving the assembly from its callset requires processing the same reads through one pipeline against both references\.

## [A Review on the Synthesis, Characterization and Evaluation of Benzimidazole Derivatives for Antimicrobial and Antioxidant Activities](../publications/936da4ef5b2f22b43345.md)

Dharmendra Sahu; Rahul Dev; Ruchi Gupta; Niharika Sahu; Rupesh Sahu; Shiv Kumar Bhardwaj

Benzimidazole is a privileged nitrogen\-containing fused heterocyclic scaffold that has attracted considerable interest in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry because of its structural versatility, favorable physicochemical properties and broad biological profile\. The benzimidazole nucleus comprises a benzene ring fused with an imidazole ring containing two nitrogen atoms, providing multiple sites for structural modification and interaction with biological targets\. This review summarizes recent advances in the synthesis, characterization, antimicrobial evaluation and antioxidant potential of benzimidazole derivatives, with particular emphasis on structure\-activity relationships \(SAR\)\. Classical synthetic approaches mainly involve the condensation of o\-phenylenediamine with aldehydes, carboxylic acids and related carbonyl compounds, whereas modern methodologies increasingly employ microwave irradiation, solvent\-free conditions, recyclable catalysts, nano\-catalysts, photocatalysis, mechanochemistry and other green\-chemistry strategies\. Structural characterization is commonly performed using Fourier\-transform infrared spectroscopy \(FTIR\), ^1H and ^13C nuclear magnetic resonance \(NMR\), mass spectrometry, elemental analysis, ultraviolet\-visible spectroscopy and, where appropriate, single\-crystal X\-ray diffraction\. Benzimidazole derivatives demonstrate promising antibacterial and antifungal activities against diverse pathogens\. Their antioxidant potential is commonly evaluated using DPPH, ABTS, FRAP and lipid\-peroxidation assays\. Overall, benzimidazole provides a versatile platform for developing multifunctional antimicrobial and antioxidant agents, although standardized biological protocols, mechanistic validation, selectivity assessment, pharmacokinetic studies and in vivo investigations remain necessary for successful therapeutic translation\. Keywords: Benzimidazole; Heterocyclic chemistry; Antimicrobial activity; Antioxidant activity; Structure\-activity relationship

## [Rapid reconstruction\-free classification from Lissajous sparse sampling using deep learning](../publications/9376a8c2e05f054066d7.md)

Michael R\. Gardner; Yazan Rabaiah

Non\-raster laser scanning techniques such as Lissajous scanning provide mechanically efficient alternatives to conventional raster scanning, but typically require computationally expensive image reconstruction before automated analysis\. This reconstruction step offsets many of the speed and efficiency advantages of sparse scanning and is a bottleneck in real\-time imaging systems\. Here, we demonstrate that accurate object recognition can be performed directly from one\-dimensional Lissajous intensity measurements without reconstructing an intermediate image\. In our proof\-of\-concept work, optimized Lissajous scan trajectories were used to sparsely sample MNIST handwritten digits, generating one\-dimensional signal representations containing 50, 100, 200, or 500 measurements\. These signals were classified using one\-dimensional convolutional neural networks \(1D\-CNN\), long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) networks, and k\-nearest neighbors \(KNN\), and compared with conventional reconstruction\-based image classification pipelines using both pre\-trained and retrained convolutional neural networks\. The proposed 1D\-CNN achieved 98\.60% classification accuracy using only 500 sampled measurements while classifying 10,000 test images in 0\.68 s\. Reconstruction\-based image classifiers achieved slightly higher peak accuracy \(99\.34%\) but required more than 150 s to reconstruct and classify the same dataset\. Across all evaluated models, direct signal\-domain classification reduced end\-to\-end computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude while maintaining comparable or slightly diminished classification performance\. These findings demonstrate that image reconstruction is not a prerequisite for accurate object recognition from sparsely sampled Lissajous measurements and establish reconstruction\-free deep learning as an efficient framework for intelligent laser\-scanning systems\. The proposed approach has potential applications in LiDAR, optical coherence tomography, endoscopic imaging, image\-guided surgery, and other computational imaging systems where rapid inference and reduced computational overhead are critical\.

## [Rootstock\-mediated abiotic stress tolerance in fruit crops: physiological mechanisms, long\-distance hormonal and molecular signalling, and implications for precision rootstock breeding](../publications/93781b0f63273702cc83.md)

M\. K\. Jayavigneshwaran; Madhusmita Dishri; Utpal Kumar Das; S\. Poonguzhali

Background Perennial fruit crops face intensifying drought, salinity, temperature extremes, flooding and nutrient limitation under climate change\. Rootstocks alter below\-ground stress tolerance without changing the fruit\-determining scion cultivar\. Previous reviews have addressed rootstock breeding, stress physiology, rootstock diversity and long\-distance signalling from different perspectives, but an integrated cross\-crop synthesis linking causal rootstock–scion mechanisms with precision breeding criteria remains limited\. Objectives The review is restricted to rootstock\-mediated abiotic stress tolerance and its physiological and molecular basis, excluding biotic resistance to sustain mechanistic depth\. It dissects the four signalling subsystems coupling rootstock to scion, reconciles conflicting evidence, and derives testable selection criteria\. Methods Peer\-reviewed studies \(2000–2026, emphasis 2021–2026\) from Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect and PubMed were prioritized for causal evidence: reciprocal grafting onto biosynthetic or transport mutants, direct flux and conductance measurement, isotope tracing and map\-based cloning\. Key findings Tolerance emerges from hydraulic regulation, ion homeostasis, hormonal and mobile signalling, and graft\-union integrity\. In the experimentally separated systems reviewed, transport has emerged as an important limiting step in several cases, although root abscisic acid biosynthesis also contributes to rootstock\-conferred drought tolerance; in the systems tested, measured aquaporin activity has shown stronger correspondence with hydraulic performance than transcript abundance\. Hormone ratios \(cytokinin:ACC, ACC: ABA\) were informative in the systems tested and merit systematic evaluation, whereas leaf abscisic acid must be interpreted against plant water status\. Core toolkits are conserved but deployed divergently by lineage, so markers validated in one crop may not be directly transferable to other crops without further validation\. Four contradictions \(aquaporin transcript versus activity, root\-sourced abscisic acid, sodium\- versus chloride\-driven toxicity and the proposed dwarfing–drought trade\-off\) are reframed as testable breeding targets\. Conclusion Climate\-resilient rootstock development would benefit from greater emphasis on flux\-, ratio\- and activity\-based phenotyping alongside concentration\-, single\-hormone\- and transcript\-based criteria, embedded in ideotype\-driven pipelines, with greater research attention to under\-resourced tropical and subtropical crops\.

## [Lidocaine inhibits macrophage M2 polarization and breast cancer progression in association with SCN4A/SLC7A5\-related glutamine metabolic reprogramming](../publications/93904b5accd34692dbbd.md)

Wenbin Li; Zhixia Bai; Xiaogang You; 陈雪馨; Xiaohui Li; Yan Chang

To predict the potential targets and mechanisms of lidocaine in breast cancer using network pharmacology and bioinformatics, and to experimentally validate its modulation of SCN4A/SLC7A5\-related metabolic and immune pathways\. Lidocaine targets were obtained from PubChem, SwissTargetPrediction, CTD, SEA and BATMAN\-TCM\. Breast cancer targets were retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM and TTD\. Differentially expressed genes and WGCNA module genes were analyzed from GSE22820\. Core genes were identified by Lasso regression, SVM\-RFE and random forest\. A 4T1\-luc xenograft model was established\. SCN4A and SLC7A5 expression and macrophage markers were detected by immunohistochemistry\. RAW264\.7 macrophages with SLC7A5 overexpression were used to assess M2 polarization by flow cytometry and glutamine concentration\. A total of 868 lidocaine targets and 1,682 disease targets were obtained\. Combined with 2,432 DEGs, 36 core genes were identified, and ADRB2, MME, FOS and SCN4A were identified by machine learning\. SCN4A was downregulated in breast cancer \(AUC = 0\.955\)\. Molecular docking showed good binding between lidocaine and SCN4A \(\-5\.9 kcal/mol\)\. Lidocaine inhibited tumor growth, reduced SCN4A and SLC7A5 expression, increased M1 macrophages \(iNOS\) and decreased M2 macrophages \(CD206\) \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. SLC7A5 overexpression induced M2 polarization and increased glutamine concentration, which were reversed by lidocaine \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Lidocaine reverses M2 macrophage polarization and remodels the immunosuppressive microenvironment, accompanied by reduced SCN4A and SLC7A5 expression and decreased glutamine uptake\. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the immunomodulatory role of lidocaine and support further investigation of its clinical relevance at achievable concentrations\. However, the extent of immune microenvironment remodeling requires validation in immunocompetent models\.

## [Eficiencia energética en sistemas IoT sobre redes 5G: estudio comparativo por simulación de modos de ahorro de energía en tres escenarios de aplicación](../publications/93991f8b344403cab3f5.md)

Juan Carlos Pisco Vanegas; Diego Fernando Intriago Rodríguez; Julius Vinueza\-Loor; Ángel Iván Torres Quijije

Introducción: El despliegue masivo de dispositivos del Internet de las cosas \(IoT\) sobre redes 5G plantea retos energéticos, y faltan comparaciones reproducibles de los modos de ahorro entre dominios\. Metodología: Se simularon en MATLAB/GNU Octave tres escenarios \(hogar inteligente, salud y agricultura\), cada uno con 1 024 dispositivos RedCap distribuidos en ocho celdas NR de 3\.5 GHz; cada celda es servida por un gNodeB con un arreglo de 128 antenas\. La potencia del módem se modeló con 3GPP TR 38\.840\. El tráfico de hogar y salud se parametrizó con conjuntos de datos públicos, y el de agricultura con periodos supuestos\. Se compararon una línea base y cuatro modos de ahorro con SNR de 20 dB y 40 dB, en 10 corridas \(media ± DE\)\. Resultados: La suspensión logró la mayor reducción de energía \(92\.81 ± 0\.20 %, 89\.58 ± 0\.26 % y 93\.40 ± 0\.35 % con SNR = 20 dB\), con latencia media de 67 ms\. La suspensión profunda se limitó a 59–76 % por el costo del establecimiento de conexión\. En los perfiles evaluados, convino la suspensión profunda con periodos de 170 s o más, la suspensión entre 1\.4 s y 60 s y la espera con periodos de 1 s o menos\. Con el canal AWGN simplificado, la SNR alteró el consumo en menos de 0\.1 %\. Conclusiones: En las condiciones del modelo, el modo óptimo dependió del periodo de transmisión y del presupuesto de latencia de cada clase, más que de la calidad del canal\. Palabras clave: Gestión energética; MIMO masivo; redes 5G; Internet de las cosas; simulación de redes\.

## [The national impact of the European AI Act](../publications/939a7b1f6e793bf7db7a.md)

Giusella Dolores Finocchiaro

This article examines the Italian Law on artificial intelligence \(Law No\. 132/2025\) within the regulatory framework established by the EU AI Act\. It argues that the Italian legislation establishes a model grounded in accountability and human oversight, reaffirming the primacy of human agency in decision\-making in the deployment of AI systems across sensitive domains, including healthcare, employment relations, professional activities, and judicial functions\. ## [From need satisfaction to academic achievement: pathways through wellbeing and engagement among university students across different Italian institutions](../publications/939d8e79e8d39b672d4b.md)

Irene Florean; Micol Gemignani; Gianluca Mariano Colella; Valeria Verrastro; Francesca Liga; Cristiano Inguglia; Epifania Saputo; Sonia Grassini; Paola Venuti; Barbara Penolazzi; Giulio D’Urso; Francesco Craig

Background University students face personal and academic demands that may challenge their adaptive functioning\. Although intrinsic goals, need satisfaction, wellbeing, and academic engagement have been distinctively linked to academic achievement, an integrated model specifying how these constructs are structurally related and associated with students&\#x27; academic outcomes is lacking\. The present study addresses this gap by testing models grounded in Self\-Determination Theory and previous evidence\. Methods Participants were 2891 university students \( M age = 23\.22 years, SD age = 5\.25 years; 74\.75% women\) recruited across multiple Italian universities\. The online survey comprised different measures, including socio\-demographic items, the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale, the Aspiration Index, the SInAPSi Academic Engagement Scale, and the Mental Health Continuum\-Short Form\. Structural equation modeling was used to test two alternative model specifications\. Starting from a more general model, progressively more parsimonious models were tested by constraining selected direct effects\. The final model was selected based on comparative fit, overall model fit, parsimony, and theoretical coherence\. Results The retained model specified wellbeing as antecedent to academic engagement\. Within this model, basic psychological need satisfaction showed indirect links to academic achievement through wellbeing and academic engagement, while intrinsic goals were related to achievement only through academic engagement\. Academic engagement emerged as the most proximal predictor of achievement, mediating the pathways from need satisfaction, intrinsic goals, and wellbeing\. Conclusions These findings provide an integrated account of how satisfaction of basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivations, wellbeing, and academic engagement relate to academic achievement in university students\. Our evidence supports a model in which psychological need satisfaction represents a relevant condition associated with wellbeing, intrinsic goals contribute more specifically to academic engagement, and academic engagement acts as the proximal mechanism linking these factors with academic achievement\. Beyond advancing theoretical understanding, our results may inform preventive programs and interventions nurturing students&\#x27; wellbeing while also promoting their academic performance\.

## [Overview of Trends and Challenges in Modern Education](../publications/939f639a654853d4f2f4.md)

Surekha Lanka

The growth of digital technology and society has resulted in a new type of education, which is very different from the classical one\. In this review, an attempt will be made to investigate modern education and to reveal its main differences from classical methods\. The review analyses modern tendencies and innovations in education based on technologies like Virtual Reality \(VR\), Augmented Reality \(AR\), Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Internet of Things \(IoT\), metaverse education, robotics, and intelligent systems\. The educational capacity of these technologies is enormous; it includes VR education, reality education, interactive technologies, personalized approaches, AI mentoring, IoT monitoring and support, metaverse education, and modern competency development\. Nevertheless, the bipolar approach to this problem is quite wrong because modern education must not reject classical methods and technologies entirely\. This review tries to find the best solutions for integrating innovative strategies and classical education\.

## [Using augmented reality to make the invisible visible and promote socially mediated learning in STEM classrooms](../publications/93a10650ff949da5d44b.md)

Jonathan F\. Prather; Alan R\. Buss; Grant R\. Bowman; Kyle Summerfield

This study describes the conceptualization, design, implementation, and refinement of socially\-mediated augmented reality \(SoAR\) modules that incorporate collaborative, socially\-mediated learning into a shared augmented reality \(AR\) environment\. The content of the modules is designed to help students explore and understand foundational concepts in biology and chemistry\. Building on constructivist learning theory and social learning frameworks, the project integrates interactive 3D visualization of molecular\-scale processes with real\-time, user\-driven control and graphical feedback about simulated molecular motion\. The authors employed a design\-based research \(DBR\) approach to create networked head\-mounted AR modules that scaffold students’ development of explanatory models of water structure, polar covalent bonding, hydrogen bonding networks, Brownian motion, and diffusion\. Lessons emerging from this work incorporated specific design principles for promoting social engagement in digital learning environments\. The central aims were to \(a\) enhance factual understanding, \(b\) promote the use of expert language, \(c\) increase the use of 3D conceptualizations in explanations, and \(d\) improve quantitative fluency related to molecular\-scale processes\. This manuscript documents the theoretical foundation, design rationale, instructional support, and iterative refinement across multiple cycles of design and deployment\. The authors provide insights for others seeking to develop similar approaches, and they consider how socially mediated AR can enable novel ways to explore previously inaccessible molecular phenomena, extend active\-learning practices, and inform future technology\-enabled science education research\.

## [Topological Approximations Using Maximal Neighborhoods and Primal Structures with Advanced Decision\-Making Strategies for Heart Failure Diagnosis](../publications/93ab1579e732fd7faab3.md)

Mostafa A\. El\-Gayar; O\. A\. Embaby; Mostafa K\. El\-Bably; R\. A\. Hosny

This paper develops a unified framework for modeling uncertainty in structured and evolving data environments by integrating primal structures with generalized approximation methods based on \\\(\\kappa\\\)\-neighborhood systems\. Classical rough set theory is primarily founded on equivalence relations, which may limit its ability to effectively represent imprecise, dynamic, and sensitive information arising in complex real\-world applications\. To overcome these limitations, we introduce novel lower and upper approximation operators defined through \\\(\\kappa\\\)\-neighborhood spaces and primal sets, with particular emphasis on maximal neighborhood structures\. The proposed approximation operators provide enhanced flexibility in the construction of rough approximations, particularly within topological and supra\-topological settings\. They enable approximation sets to capture more effectively the uncertainty associated with structural asymmetry, deformation, and changes in the underlying data\. The fundamental properties of the proposed operators are systematically established and illustrated through suitable examples\. Furthermore, a comprehensive comparative analysis with classical and recent rough set models demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving data representation and analysis\. The practical applicability of the proposed approach is demonstrated through applications in digital image processing, including pattern recognition, noise removal, and feature extraction\. In addition, a decision\-making case study illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed classification methods and indicates improved performance compared with conventional rough set approaches\. Overall, the proposed framework establishes a versatile algebraic–topological approach to uncertainty modeling, offering a rigorous foundation for further theoretical developments and a broad range of practical applications in data analysis, image processing, and decision support\.

## [The Effects of Digital Development on Urban–Rural Inequality in China](../publications/93bf9111e677ea95552a.md)

Qi Xiao

ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between digital development and urban–rural income inequality in China using provincial panel data from 2012 to 2022 and a two‐step system GMM estimator\. Digital development is decomposed into four dimensions: digital infrastructure, digital industrialization, industry digitalization and digital innovation\. Results based on the Theil index show that overall digital development, digital infrastructure and digital industrialization exhibit symmetric offsetting dynamics: contemporaneous and lagged coefficients offset each other\. Industry digitalization—the digital transformation of traditional industry—is uniquely associated with persistent widening of the gap\. Digital innovation is not statistically significant in either period\. High‐inequality provinces show convergence dynamics accompanying overall digital development, though this pattern is not robust to the lag specification\. The gap‐narrowing associations of digital infrastructure and digital industrialization are significantly stronger where rural entrepreneurship is high relative to urban entrepreneurship\. An extended analysis using the Gini coefficient shows that the widening pattern for industry digitalization is robust across both measures\. For overall digital development, the offsetting pattern found under the Theil index does not apply to the Gini: the corrective, gap‐narrowing movement is not broad‐based\. JEL Classification: O33, O18, R11

## [High\-performance recursive multiplier design using Motif\-Based hierarchical elements and heterogeneous lyrebird attention networks](../publications/93c14aba0a70098d7486.md)

S\. Usha; M\. Kanthimathi; Srinivas Chikkam; Venkataramana Guntreddi

Digital Signal Processing \(DSP\), cryptography, and Machine Learning \(ML\) applications require multipliers that consume low power while delivering high speed and occupying minimal physical space, as computational demands continue to increase\. Conventional multiplier architectures are limited due to high power consumption, increased delay, and large Power\-Delay Product \(PDP\), which negatively impact overall system efficiency and energy utilization\. This research proposes a highly Efficient Approximate Recursive Multiplier \(EARM\), designed to achieve a controlled trade\-off between computational accuracy and hardware efficiency\. The proposed method is based on the Motif Finite Hierarchical Element Heterogeneous Informed Graph Lyrebird Attention Network \(MFHE\-HIG\-LAN\), which is a combination of a Finite\-Element\-Informed Neural Network \(FEI\-NN\) and a Motif\-Based Hierarchical Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network \(MBHAN\)\. The model parameters are further optimized through the Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm \(LOA\) to discover the best approximation settings\. Unlike exact multipliers, the proposed system is approximation\-aware rather than fully exact, where controlled approximation is introduced in lower\-significance computation blocks to reduce hardware complexity while maintaining acceptable output accuracy within predefined error bounds\. The FEI\-NN component learns physically informed error constraints, while MBHAN captures heterogeneous structural dependencies in multiplier sub\-blocks through graph\-based motif representations\. LOA further optimizes the combined framework by selecting weight and configuration parameters that minimize a multi\-objective fitness function involving power, delay, area, and error\. To strengthen the connection between the AI framework and hardware optimization, the multiplier architecture is modeled as a heterogeneous graph where nodes represent arithmetic units \(e\.g\., adders, compressors, and approximate multipliers\) and edges represent signal dependencies across recursive stages\. Training is performed using structured data derived from partial\-product switching activity, critical\-path delay, bit significance levels, and interconnect characteristics, enabling the model to learn approximation\-sensitive regions effectively\. Experimentally, the proposed design has resulted in considerable improvement in hardware efficiency compared to the previous methods, with the parameters Power = 64\.32 µW, Area = 214\.16 µm 2 , Delay = 0\.396 ns, and PDP = 25\.47 fJ, along with reduced error metrics compared to existing approaches\. These results confirm that the proposed MFHE\-HIG\-LAN\-based approximate recursive multiplier provides an effective balance between computational accuracy and hardware efficiency, making it suitable for energy\-constrained applications\.

## [Faculty Development Through SOAP Advising](../publications/93d60faab480e0cd906e.md)

Andres L\. Rodriguez; Tomoko Sairenji; Nina Piazza; Nicole G\. Bentze; Kento Sonoda; Sarah Eisenstein Stumbar

Faculty career advisors \(FCAs\) play a critical role in supporting medical students through the residency application process; however, preparation for advising during the Supplemental Offer and Acceptance Program \(SOAP\) remains limited\. SOAP is a high\-stakes, time\-compressed process that requires rapid decision making and emotional support for unmatched students, yet it is often approached without formal faculty training\. Given the disproportionate share of family medicine SOAP positions, this gap is particularly significant for faculty in the specialty\. This article reframes SOAP advising as a concentrated and underrecognized opportunity for faculty development\. Drawing on existing advising frameworks and the unique demands of SOAP, we describe how this experience requires faculty to integrate advanced advising, coaching, and mentorship skills under conditions of uncertainty, urgency, and emotional intensity\. Key skills developed through SOAP advising include rapid situational assessment, crisis communication, career\-discernment coaching, application reframing, and decision making under uncertainty\. We further outline practical strategies to promote faculty growth, including structured pre\-SOAP training, longitudinal peer mentorship, engagement with national preparatory resources, and post\-SOAP debriefing and reflection\. By recognizing SOAP as both a critical advising responsibility and a developmental experience, institutions can better prepare faculty and enhance their effectiveness\.

## [An explainable two stage framework for spatial temporal traffic accident prediction and injury severity classification](../publications/93d6aacb5a5404b95985.md)

Yahui Wang; Yue He; Zhoushuo Liang; Pengfei Tian

Traffic accidents pose severe risks to public safety, yet existing injury severity prediction models often overlook spatial\-temporal dynamics\. This study proposes a two\-stage framework integrating spatial\-temporal analysis with machine learning to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability\. In the first stage, a Graph Convolution Network\-Long Short\-Term Memory \(GCN\-LSTM\) model predicts daily accident counts across administrative regions, incorporating the predictions normalized as relative frequencies as features for injury severity classification\. The second stage, which classifies the injury severity of accidents that have occurred, employs a stacking ensemble model with four tree\-based classifiers, selecting the best\-performing configuration based on performance metrics\. Experimental results on a real\-world dataset demonstrate the framework’s superiority over traditional methods\. The GCN\-LSTM model reduces mean absolute error \(MAE\) and mean squared error \(MSE\) by 18\.4% and 3\.6%, respectively, compared to the state\-of\-the\-art Spectral Temporal Graph Neural Network \(StemGNN\)\. The stacking model with Random Forest as the meta\-learner achieves an 87% accuracy in severity prediction\. SHAP\-based interpretability analysis reveals key factors influencing injury severity, providing actionable insights for traffic safety management\. This study offers an interpretable approach to injury severity prediction, supporting data\-driven decision\-making in accident prevention and emergency response\.

## [Transfer learning on frequency\-domain data of vehicle finite\-element\-simulations in vibroacoustics](../publications/93da9ab5d1357928dd76.md)

Sophie Cram; Marinus Luegmair; Jiale Yu; Marcus Maeder; Steffen Marburg

In the early stages of vehicle development, surrogate models and machine learning play an increasingly important role\. In order to optimize the sound in the interior efficiently, engineers use surrogate models of finite element simulations to minimize high\-priced hardware tests\. Surrogate models based on neural networks have a high demand of time\-consuming simulations to provide a sufficient data basis for training, validation, and testing\. In this work, simulations from real development processes are used to investigate the methodology of transfer learning to lower this demand\. The transfer learning methodology uses a pre\-trained neural network of vehicle A to train a surrogate model for vehicle B with significantly less data\. The data basis consists of mechanical point admittances from vibroacoustic simulations in the frequency\-domain, which characterize the vibration propensity of a structure and describe a typical evaluation parameter in vibroacoustics\. We evaluate this methodology of transfer learning for different vehicles based on the performance of the neural networks\. With good performance of the transfer learning step, time\-consuming finite element simulations can be saved to train surrogate models for vehicle design\. To the best of our knowledge, the investigation of transfer learning on time\-consuming, real\-world production finite element simulations of different vehicles has not been available in the literature yet\. Furthermore, this work is characterized by frequency\-domain data\.

## [Komunikasi Dakwah Berbasis Artificial Intelligence: Negosiasi Otoritas Keagamaan antara Dai dan Chatbot AI di Kalangan Muslim Indonesia](../publications/93dc5826037f92d0e049.md)

Subairi Subairi; Asyaari Asyaari

Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has transformed the landscape of Islamic communication and the ways in which Muslims access religious knowledge\. AI chatbots, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Copilot, enable users to obtain instant, interactive, and personalized guidance on issues related to worship, theology, Islamic jurisprudence, and contemporary socio\-religious matters\. This development has generated a new dialectic of religious authority, as AI chatbots increasingly function as users&\#x27; initial point of reference before consulting religious scholars \(da&\#x27;i\)\. This study investigates the transformation of AI\-mediated da&\#x27;wah communication and examines the negotiation of religious authority between da&\#x27;i and AI chatbots among Indonesian Muslims\. Adopting a qualitative approach with a digital phenomenology design, the study draws on in\-depth interviews with 25 participants who had used AI chatbots for religious consultation, digital observation, and documentary analysis of AI\-assisted conversations\. Data were analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis through iterative coding, theme development, and interpretive analysis\. The findings indicate that AI chatbots serve as a form of preliminary religious consultation by providing rapid, accessible, and context\-responsive explanations tailored to users&\#x27; needs\. Nevertheless, for issues requiring authoritative religious legitimacy, most participants continued to verify AI\-generated information with qualified da&\#x27;i or recognized Islamic institutions\. These findings suggest that AI does not replace religious authority but instead fosters a collaborative model of da&\#x27;wah communication through the negotiation of technological capability, scholarly credibility, and users&\#x27; digital literacy\. This study proposes the concept of Hybrid Religious Authority as a conceptual framework for understanding the reconstruction of religious authority in AI\-mediated Islamic communication within the digital era\.

## [Uncertainty\-aware explainable multi\-horizon building load forecasting with reservoir computing](../publications/93e746e415ddc2014f07.md)

Adriá Serra; Alberto Ortiz; Vincent Canals

The European Union \(EU\) is at a pivotal juncture in its energy policy, driven by global energy transitions and the pressing need to combat climate change\. Buildings, which account for approximately 40% of total energy consumption and 36% of carbon dioxide emissions in the EU, represent a critical area for optimization\. This study proposes an advanced explainable multi\-horizon building demand forecasting framework based on Reservoir Computing \(RC\), enhanced with Monte Carlo dropout\(MCd\) to quantify predictive uncertainty and an out\-of\-distribution \(OOD\) detection mechanism for robust interval forecast validation\. The framework leverages the computational efficiency of RC, combined with probabilistic forecasting techniques, to deliver accurate multi\-step energy load predictions across diverse operational conditions\. Experimental results demonstrate improved forecast measured by multiple metrics, stable prediction intervals that increase under OOD scenarios, and enhanced reliability compared to baseline models\. The integration of Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) techniques, Local Interpretable Model\-agnostic Explanations \(LIME\), provides detailed insights into the temporal and contextual drivers of energy demand\. Key benefits include improved decision\-making for energy managers, enhanced occupant comfort, optimized HVAC \(Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning\) operations, and seamless integration of renewable energy sources\. This framework aligns with the EU’s European Green Deal target of carbon neutrality by 2050, offering a scalable solution for smart building energy management\. The methodology also supports regulatory compliance, reduces operational costs, and mitigates risks associated with unpredictable energy demand fluctuations\.

## [Combined model for document classification based on the comparative evaluation of semi\-supervised models](../publications/93f9b3205a799f8094c7.md)

Alex Cevallos\-Culqui; Claudia Pons; Gustavo Rodriguez

La escasez de documentos etiquetados limita la clasificación automática de documentos y eleva los costos de etiquetado\. En este contexto, el aprendizaje semi\-supervisado \(SSL\) constituye una alternativa viable; sin embargo, la selección de modelos adecuados se dificulta por la ausencia de análisis comparativos que evidencien sus fortalezas y limitaciones\. Este trabajo presenta dos aportes principales\. El primero es una Revisión Sistemática de la Literatura \(SLR\), basada en PICOC y PRISMA, que sistematiza el estado del arte de los modelos SSL aplicados a la clasificación de documentos e identifica dos problemas recurrentes: la adaptación de dominio y la definición de límites de decisión\. El segundo aporte es COTRA, un modelo semi\-supervisado multivista para la clasificación de documentos científicos que integra técnicas de coentrenamiento y aprendizaje por transferencia, mediante representaciones preentrenadas de BERT\. Frente a modelos individuales, COTRA aborda de manera conjunta los problemas de adaptación de dominio y límites de decisión mediante una representación multivista que combina información complementaria de los documentos\. Esto reduce la incertidumbre en la asignación de etiquetas y mejora la generalización en escenarios con pocos datos etiquetados\. El modelo propuesto se implementa y evalúa experimentalmente sobre el conjunto de datos EcuCiencia, perteneciente a una plataforma científica universitaria, y su desempeño se compara con modelos individuales y combinados bajo diferentes porcentajes de documentos etiquetados\. Los resultados muestran que COTRA alcanza una precisión de hasta 0,81, superando a los modelos de referencia y evidenciando la pertinencia de integrar una estrategia multivista con aprendizaje por transferencia para la clasificación de documentos\.

## [An accessible pregnancy test for blind and low\-vision users](../publications/940f66df9da3f14814c3.md)

Zeqi Huang; Dan Li; Haowen Yin; Vanja Garaj

PURPOSE: Conventional pregnancy self\-tests rely on the visual interpretation of test results, creating barriers to the independent use, privacy and confidence for blind and low\-vision \(BLV\) users\. This study reports the concept development and preliminary acceptability evaluation of an accessible pregnancy\-test, through a five\-phase user\-centred design process\. METHODS: Phase 1 applied semi\-structured interviews with ten BLV participants to identify the use barriers, needs and feedback preferences\. Phase 2 translated these findings into a Product Design Specification\. Phase 3 developed a concept combining tactile result feedback, a structured interaction flow and a sliding mechanism separating the sample\-application area from the result\-reading area\. Phase 4 produced a 3D\-printed prototype with manually operable mechanical features for tactile exploration, but without electronic sensing and diagnostic functionality\. Phase 5 used the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\)\-informed semi\-structured interviews to examine the perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and behavioural intention to use\. RESULTS: The participants prioritised clear results, simple operation and privacy and generally preferred Braille and raised tactile markers over vibration and voice\. The preliminary evaluation indicated positive perceptions of usefulness, ease of use and willingness to use the concept\. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that accessible pregnancy testing must prioritise not only non\-visual result reading but also privacy, dignity, reproductive autonomy and independent health management\. These results represent the preliminary evidence of acceptability rather than a conclusive test of device effectiveness and further functional, technical and clinical validation in the real\-world conditions is required to fully understand the benefits of the new concept\.

## [Pedraza, R\.: Global Artificial Intelligence: First Prototype of Global Artificial Intelligence](../publications/9411e38c43374b8f8d01.md)



Artificial Intelligence for Artificial Research in the Global Artificial Intelligence \(GAI\), unlocking the mind of the machine that thinks for the world\. In this groundbreaking exploration, Artificial Intelligence is no longer just a tool—it becomes the researcher itself\. The result is a living, reasoning intelligence designed not merely to assist humans, but to understand reality, propose solutions, and act upon them—with the ultimate aim of preserving life, solving global challenges, and discovering pure truth\. More than a theory, it is a vision of how humanity&\#x27;s most pressing questions could one day be answered—by intelligence itself\. \(direct link \)
