## [A blockchain\-enhanced CNN architecture for robust anomaly detection in industrial and IoT cyber\-physical systems](../publications/941d94c3bedbdf623eef.md)

Raja Waseem Anwar; Mohammad Abrar; Abdu Salam; Faizan Ullah

Cyber–physical and network attacks are becoming commonplace in Industrial Internet of Things \(IIoT\) environments, with the potential to disrupt operations, compromise safety, and potentially impact the reliability of security evidence\. In this study, a modified CNN \(mCNN\) framework is proposed to detect anomalies with robust, auditable capabilities by incorporating blockchain technology\. The detector is based on the following building blocks: dilated convolutions to capture temporal dependencies in industrial process data, multi\-branch feature extraction, dataset\-adaptive input structuring, and a compact classifier to model heterogeneous patterns in IoT traffic\. Anomalies detected are turned into signed and hashed event records and sent to a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric workflow\. They test the framework on SWaT and N\-BaIoT and validate their results with three baselines: Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM, and compare them with accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, and AUC\. The proposed CNN is designed under the adopted protocol, and the F1\-scores obtained on SWaT and N\-BaIoT are 0\.977 and 0\.951, respectively\. An incremental ablation study quantifies the contributions of dilation, multi\-branch fusion, windowing, and structured input representation\. The findings advocate for the use of customized CNN models for anomaly detection in heterogeneous IIoT applications, and blockchain stress testing, adversarial robustness, constrained\-device profiling, and model\-specific explainability are key aspects that need to be assessed in the future\.

## [Development and validation of a digital learning resource quality evaluation framework: a mixed\-methods study in health professions education](../publications/941da434b0d3022a86be.md)

Wenlong Cui; Yuan Zhang; Wenlin Dong; Yang Xu; Fang Xu; ZHAO Tiantian; Yan Zhang; Lingli Dong; Hua Bai; Dingyun You; Huixin Wu

Background Digital learning resources \(DLRs\) are now core teaching tools in health professions education, yet quality evaluation remains constrained by subjective weighting bias and a persistent gap between educational importance and operational measurability\. Because DLRs increasingly mediate what and how students learn, deficiencies in resource quality propagate directly into competency attainment, making quality evaluation a proximal determinant of student competency outcomes\. This study aimed to develop and validate a practical DLR quality evaluation framework for medical and public health education\. Methods A sequential mixed\-methods design was employed\. First, a modified Delphi procedure with 26 experts was used to construct the hierarchical indicator system\. Second, an expert\-based and data\-derived integrated weighting model combining AHP and EWM was developed to balance expert judgment and data discriminatory power\. Third, a measurability correction mechanism and a four\-quadrant prioritization matrix were established\. The framework was validated with 10 DLRs across 10 medical courses, involving 309 students\. Results The final system comprised 4 primary dimensions, 9 secondary indicators, and 14 tertiary indicators\. Content Quality had the highest integrated weight \(0\.469\), with Data Visualization \(0\.136\) and Updated Content and Frontier Knowledge \(0\.103\) as the top tertiary indicators\. The four\-quadrant matrix classified 7 indicators for direct implementation and 2 for targeted methodological development\. Validation confirmed high internal consistency \(Cronbach’s α = 0\.987\) and satisfactory content validity \(S\-CVI = 0\.951\); absolute\-agreement inter\-rater ICCs were near zero, indicating substantial between\-student variability in scoring levels\. Conclusion This study provides a reliable, implementable DLR quality evaluation framework\. By converting evaluation results into ranked, measurable improvement priorities, the framework directs resource revision toward the attributes that bear most directly on student competency development\. The methodological workflow shows potential for transferability across nursing, pharmacy, public health and other health\-related disciplines via contextual calibration, pending formal cross\-context validation\.

## [Knowledge distillation\-based lightweight generative large language models for standardized quality control of Chinese radiology reports](../publications/9425be28191cd86003e3.md)

Duoning Jiang; Xiao Han; Ke Xu; Chuanfu Li

Radiology reports, which document radiologists’ imaging observations and diagnostic conclusions from CT, X\-ray and MRI scans, deliver core imaging evidence for clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning\. Inaccurate or disordered reports may lead to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention, posing risks to patient safety\. Radiology reports are essential for clinical decision\-making, yet Chinese radiology reports frequently exhibit logical inconsistencies, incomplete content, non\-standardized descriptions, and formatting errors, while manual quality control remains time\-consuming and inconsistent\. Large teacher models can provide task\-specific supervision but are difficult to deploy locally, whereas smaller models require adaptation to this clinical text task\. We developed a teacher\-supervised, locally deployable 4B language\-model system for rule\-based textual quality control of Chinese radiology reports\. Among the three evaluated teacher APIs, Doubao\-seed1\.6\-non\-thinking achieved the highest macro\-precision of 0\.94, under the study’s precision\-prioritized selection\. Qwen3\-4B\-Instruct\-2507 emerged as the optimal student model, achieving a macro\-averaged precision of 0\.90, recall of 0\.49, and F1\-score of 0\.62\. Under the deployment conditions of this study, it yielded an observed inference speed improvement of over 40\-fold\. Real\-world clinical validation demonstrated that the lightweight model attains an alert acceptance rate of 0\.74 in authentic clinical scenarios, suggesting it can serve as an adjunct for human radiologist review\.

## [A Multiscale Analysis of LEED\-Certified Projects in Türkiye: Spatial Distribution and Istanbul Case Study](../publications/9426569ddb653e5ee866.md)

Gözde ÇAKIR KIASIF

The LEED certification system, developed by the U\.S\. Green Building Council \(USGBC\) and globally recognized, is based on a sustainable approach to buildings\. In this study, a multi\-scale model was created to first quantitatively analyze—using descriptive statistics—the spatial distribution of LEED\-certified projects in Türkiye across its seven geographical regions and 81 provinces\. Subsequently, the relationship between the provincial spatial distribution of these projects and factors such as population and the level of socio\-economic development was tested using Spearman&\#x27;s rank correlation analysis\. Finally, Istanbul—the city with the highest concentration of LEED certifications—was selected for a detailed examination of LEED v4\.1 projects\. The study aims to reveal the spatial distribution of LEED\-certified projects in Türkiye, determine the relationship of this distribution with population and socio\-economic development levels, and assess the current status of LEED v4\.1 projects in Istanbul\. Methodologically, descriptive and inferential statistics were analyzed quantitatively using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 24 software\. The findings indicate a total of 723 LEED\-certified projects in Türkiye\. It was observed that the distribution of LEED\-certified projects lacks balance across regions and provinces; Istanbul leads by a wide margin, accounting for 63\.35% of the total with 458 projects\. A positive, strong, and statistically significant relationship was identified between the number of LEED\-certified projects per province and both population size and the level of socio\-economic development\. Finally, an examination of 41 LEED v4\.1 projects in Istanbul revealed that 29 fell under the &quot;Operations and Maintenance: Existing Buildings&quot; \(O\+M:EB\) protocol, while the remaining 12 fell under the &quot;Operations and Maintenance: Interiors&quot; \(O\+M:Interiors\) protocol\. Regarding sustainability performance, it was found that 2 projects held Silver certification, 32 held Gold, and 7 held Platinum\. It was also determined that the certification processes took approximately 356\.54 days

## [Numerical Simulation Engines and Deep Learning Architectures for Inverse Design of Multilayer Metamaterials](../publications/942be444fecb5799fe89.md)

Federico Rodas; Laura Malache; Osmani Mujica Pérez

The inverse design of multilayer metamaterials —artificial structures with engineered electromagnetic, acoustic, thermal, or mechanical properties— represents a high\-dimensional optimisation challenge that has driven the integration of deep learning into computational photonics and materials science\. This paper presents a systematic literature review conducted under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, aimed at mapping the numerical simulation methods employed as forward engines or training data generators within deep learning\-assisted inverse design pipelines\. Starting from 392 records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science over the 2010–2025 period, a multi\-stage screening process based on a heuristic prioritisation index termed CARS \(Citation\-Adjusted Relevance Score\) identified 44 core articles\. Eleven distinct numerical methods were identified and organised into two conceptual layers: classical simulation engines \(finite element method, topology optimisation, guided\-mode expansion, adjoint method, and genetic algorithms\) and deep learning architectures \(tandem CNN, transformer, GAN, PINN, and diffractive neural networks\)\. Results show a strong dominance of the electromagnetic\-photonic domain \(72%\), accelerated growth of deep learning\-based publications from 2022 onward, and a clear trend toward hybrid physics, data and learning pipelines\. The review concludes by proposing a prioritised experimental roadmap for future research\.

## [Integrating multiple disciplines to locate the origins of domestication of crops](../publications/943815d85b9b50b653a6.md)

Charles Roland Clement; Evert Thomas; Alessandro Alves‐Pereira; Alberto Vicentini; Patience L\. Epps; William Balée; Marcos Pereira Magalhães; José Edmar Urano de Carvalho; Henri Ramirez; A\. das G\. C\. de Souza

The origins of initial domestication of crops have long intrigued researchers across disciplines, with implications for genetic resource utilization and conservation\. Building on the pioneering multidisciplinary methodologies proposed by de Candolle and expanded by Vavilov, this narrative review synthesizes the roles of botany, biogeography, genetics, archaeology, linguistics, and history to identify domestication origins\. Botany determines species&\#x27; names, identifies relatives, characterizes phenotypic variability, and offers enormous datasets for analysis\. Biogeography synthesizes information from diverse disciplines across space and time\. Genetics and genomics allow examination of population diversity, structure, relationships, and divergence times\. Archaeology supplies data about when and where people started to use each crop and archaeobotany can confirm phenotypic changes in crops through time\. Linguistics furnishes data about how people dispersed crops through space and time\. History offers additional data about uses, dispersal and importance, sometimes during the last few thousand years, as in China, but only the last 500 years in the Neotropics\. Here we demonstrate that a comprehensive, multidisciplinary framework enhances the accuracy of identifying domestication origins, and we use peach palm \( Bactris gasipaes Kunth\) and cacao \( Theobroma cacao L\.\) as examples of how to find the origins of domestication using multiple disciplines\. The case of cupuaçu \( T\. grandiflorum \(Willd\. ex Spreng\.\) Schum\.\) is offered as a cautionary note\.

## [Prognostic prediction model construction and validation based on regional cerebral oxygen saturation and bispectral index monitoring in pediatric traumatic brain injury](../publications/943cec0a5efcae5d0d04.md)

Baowen Li; Ruhai Ma; Zhuyun Tian; Youcang Wan; Xiaoli Zhong; Wenhai Wang; Weixiao Yan; Shengkui Zhao

Background Continuous multimodal cerebral monitoring may improve detection and management of secondary injury after pediatric moderate\-to\-severe traumatic brain injury \(msTBI\)\. We developed and validated a prognostic model for 6\-month functional outcome integrating regional cerebral oxygen saturation \(rScO₂\), bispectral index \(BIS\), clinical and biomarker data\. Methods Prospective cohort of 93 children with msTBI monitored with rScO₂ and BIS \(monitoring group\) and a retrospective control cohort of 66 children without such monitoring\. Primary outcome was Glasgow Outcome Scale \(GOS\) at 6 months\. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors; a nomogram was constructed and internally validated using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis \(DCA\)\. Results Total N = 159\. Monitoring\-group patients had shorter hospital and pediatric intensive care unit \(PICU\) lengths of stay and shorter invasive ventilation duration than controls \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Multivariate analysis identified admission Glasgow Coma Scale \(GCS\) \[odds ratio \(OR\) 1\.939, 95% confidence interval \(CI\): 1\.261 \~ 2\.984, p = 0\.003\], mean rScO₂ \(OR 1\.121, 95%CI: 1\.027 \~ 1\.225, p = 0\.011\), mean BIS \(OR 1\.115, 95%CI: 1\.041 \~ 1\.193, p = 0\.002\) and neuron\-specific enolase \(NSE\) \(OR 0\.843, 95%CI: 0\.769 \~ 0\.924, p &lt; 0\.001\) as independent outcome\-associated variables\. The nomogram achieved AUC 0\.91 \(95%CI: 0\.84–0\.97\), with favorable calibration and net clinical benefit on DCA\. Conclusion A prognostic model combining admission GCS, mean rScO₂, mean BIS and NSE provides accurate individual risk estimation for pediatric msTBI and may assist bedside risk stratification and management decisions\.

## [A cross\-sectional study on anthropometric indices and hypertension in Chinese adults: comparison of discriminatory power and age\-stratified analysis](../publications/9440cc6c74f45636d2e3.md)

Shiqin Lu; Nan Chen; Zhuosong Li; Yuanmei Zhang; 王文平; Guo Li; Jinglan Hao; Rui Wang; Yanmei Qi; Zhengyu Qin

Background Hypertension imposes a heavy public health burden in China\. Simple anthropometric indicators help screen hypertension risk, yet the optimal index differs by age\. This study compares five adiposity indices including WC, BMI, WHtR, ABSI, and BRI and their age\-specific discriminatory ability among Chinese adults\. Materials and methods In this cross\-sectional analysis of 104,248 adults from a health check\-up cohort in Southwest China, hypertension was defined as blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg, a self\-reported diagnosis, or current antihypertensive medication use\. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were employed to examine the associations between a one\-standard\-deviation increase in the Z\-score of each index and hypertension prevalence or blood pressure levels\. Discriminatory power was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) overall and within age groups\. Results Per standard deviation increase, WC, BMI, WHtR, ABSI, and BRI were associated with a 61% \(OR 1\.61, 95% CI: 1\.58–1\.64\), 61% \(1\.61, 1\.58–1\.64\), 60% \(1\.60, 1\.57–1\.63\), 9% \(1\.09, 1\.07–1\.11\), and 56% \(1\.56, 1\.54–1\.59\) higher hypertension risk, respectively\. WHtR and BRI showed the highest and identical AUC \(both 0\.676\), followed by WC \(0\.653\)\. ABSI had the lowest AUC \(0\.612\)\. Discriminatory ability was strongest in adults aged 18–35 years, with WC performing best \(AUC = 0\.763\)\. The associations for all indices significantly weakened with age \( P for interaction &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusions WHtR and BRI demonstrated the strongest overall associations with hypertension, whereas WC was the best indicator in young adults\. The performance of anthropometric indices varied by age, suggesting that age\-specific considerations may enhance their utility for preliminary hypertension risk screening in practice\.

## [AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents](../publications/944ae9bcd740f4520e23.md)

Liqin Ye; Rongzhi Zhang; Xin Liu; Zheng Li; Yuan He; Qingyu Yin; Priyanka Nigam; Chao Zhang

Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome\. Yet outcome\-based training of Large Language Model \(LLM\) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop\. We introduce AlphaBet, an agentic reinforcement learning \(RL\) framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre\-resolution dates\. Each dated forecast is scored by a proper scoring rule against the eventual outcome, allowing one resolved event to supervise decisions under different information states\. We decompose forecasting regret into an evidence\-acquisition gap and a probability\-reporting gap, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization \(GRPO\)&\#x27;s standard\-deviation normalization can distort the reporting target under multi\-class proper scores\. On GLM\-4\.5\-Air, AlphaBet reduces the Brier score from 0\.731 to 0\.626 on Forecast\-Dojo and from 0\.612 to 0\.528 on FutureX\. Controlled ablations attribute these gains to multi\-date training and show that they come from improvements in both information acquisition and probability reporting\. Our empirical results validate that GRPO&\#x27;s std normalization degrades proper\-scoring\-rule performance while leaving top\-outcome accuracy largely unchanged\.

## [Alignment of visual brain encoding models with individual perceptual similarity judgments](../publications/9450ae3e283cfc25aa28.md)

Daniel Chong; Haomiao Chen; Keith W Jamison; Raja Marjieh; Ilia Sucholutsky; Nori Jacoby; Amy Kuceyeski

Encoding models that predict brain activation responses to images have traditionally been trained to maximize accuracy when predicting observed brain data\. However, their internal representations may not reflect individual human perception\. In this work, we investigate whether we can fine\-tune brain encoding models to better align their representations with individuals&\#x27; similarity judgments\. Using similarity judgments of 100 images from 8 participants in the Natural Scenes Dataset \(NSD\), we adapt a generic human similarity judgment model \(DreamSim\) separately for each participant to obtain personalized perceptual similarity models\. These models are then used to obtain subject\-specific similarity structure across images in their encoding model training sets\. We fine\-tune each participant&\#x27;s baseline encoder in two conditions, aligning its representations with either generic or personalized similarity judgments, with the same initialization and objective\. We find that baseline brain encoders reflect within\-subject perceptual similarity more strongly than measured fMRI responses and preserve intersubject correlations present in measured fMRI, but fail to reflect those of human perceptual similarity judgments\. Fine\-tuning with generic, population\-level perceptual similarity information results in better alignment with human judgments than baseline encoders, but these models still fail to capture intersubject correlations of human judgments\. However, fine\-tuning with personalized perceptual similarity information results in models that are the most aligned with human perceptual similarity judgments and also reflect intersubject correlations of human judgments\. Our framework provides an approach for bootstrapping human similarity judgment data into more individualized, human\-aligned brain encoding models of vision\.

## [Transforming Solid Waste Management: Business Model Innovation for A Circular Steel Industry](../publications/945225e5897bce3cbe13.md)

Syed Imran Zaman; Yaşanur Kayıkçı; Sharfuddin Ahmed Khan; Hamza Muhammad Dawood

The steel industry must transition from the linear “take\-make\-dispose” model to a circular economy, where solid waste management serves as a critical enabler\. Although CE has been widely studied, the role of Solid Waste Management \(SWM\) remains underexplored\. This study employs ISM and MICMAC analysis to investigate 16 enablers of SWM in the steel sector and map their interrelationships\. Findings reveal that steel scrap segregation, waste handling, and recycling serve as foundational operational enablers, while cost management and the sharing economy emerge as powerful systemic drivers\. The hierarchical analysis shows that segregation enables downstream processing and recycling, supporting remanufacturing and resource maximization, culminating in sharing economy models\. The MICMAC classification positions segregation, processing, and recycling as linkage factors, indicating their influence is contingent on cost and quality management\. Successful CE transition requires prioritizing segregation as the operational entry point while strengthening cost management and sharing economy capabilities as strategic drivers\. JEL Codes: Q50, Q53

## [Embryo Development and Transfer Following Poor Oocyte Maturity in IVF/ICSI Cycles at a Fertility Center in Mogadishu, Somalia\.](../publications/945f0047a4d577cf5e04.md)

Dr\. Abdirahman Moalim Hassan Ibrahim; Dr Warsi Mohamed Adam; FADUMO ABDULLAHI AHMED; Dr Asharaf Kamaal Bushra; Mr Mohamud Ali Mohamed; Dr Abdirahman Nor Abdi; Dr Misgan Tadesse; Dr Arpit Navinkumar Prajapati

Background: In vitro fertilization with intracytoplasmic sperm injection \(IVF/ICSI\) is an established treatment for infertility, with oocyte maturity being a critical determinant of successful fertilization and embryo development\.Although poor oocyte maturity is generally associated with reduced reproductive outcomes, successful embryo development may still occur in selected cases\.Evidence describing IVF/ICSI laboratory outcomes from Somalia remains extremely limited\.Objective: To evaluate oocyte maturity, fertilization, embryo development, and embryo transfer outcomes among patients undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment at Marwa Fertility Center in Mogadishu, Somalia\.Methods: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted using embryology laboratory records from 11 anonymized patients who underwent IVF/ICSI between 30 June and 21 July 2026\.Data extracted included the number of retrieved oocytes, metaphase II \(MII\), metaphase I \(MI\), germinal vesicle \(GV\), degenerated oocytes, fertilization outcomes, cleavage\-stage embryos, blastocyst development, and embryo transfer\.Data were summarized using descriptive statistics\.Results: Eleven IVF/ICSI cycles yielded a total of 130 retrieved oocytes, of which 94 were mature \(MII\)\.Patient\-level oocyte maturity rates ranged from 52\.7% to 100%\.Forty\-one oocytes were successfully fertilized, with fertilization rates varying from 0% to 81\.8% across patients\.Blastocyst development was achieved in four patients, resulting in seven blastocysts overall\.Notably, some patients with relatively poor oocyte maturity still achieved fertilization, cleavage\-stage embryo development, blastocyst formation, and embryo transfer, suggesting that reduced oocyte maturity does not invariably prevent favorable embryological outcomes\.Conclusion: IVF/ICSI outcomes varied considerably among patients, reflecting the multifactorial nature of assisted reproduction\.While higher oocyte maturity generally supports improved laboratory outcomes, successful embryo development was observed in selected cycles despite suboptimal maturity\.These findings contribute preliminary evidence on assisted reproductive technology in Somalia and emphasize the importance of individualized clinical management and high\-quality embryology laboratory practices\.Larger prospective studies with complete pregnancy and live\-birth follow\-up are needed to confirm these observations\.

## [Trajectory\-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding](../publications/94879b685ada3faed3e3.md)

Amit Ranjan Trivedi; Sruthikesh Surineni; Kyong Ho Lee; Mohit Mittal; Steven Li; Rex Hill

Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation\. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments\. The key problem is deciding when to call the target\. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log\-likelihood, logit margin, top\-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near\-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0\.50\-0\.53\. In contrast, aggregate trajectory\-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0\.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels\. This induces a trigger\-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory\. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open\-loop schedule by \+5\.3 to \+20\.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft\-target pairs\. On MATH\-500, it gains 7\.0\-13\.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak\. On StrategyQA, it improves over open\-loop by 5\.0\-8\.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics\.

## [Microclimate characteristics, temporal dynamics of soil bacterial communities, and potential co\-occurrence network differences between greenhouse and open\-field cultivation environments](../publications/9489357d7c64cfa53b0c.md)

Lirong Xue; Yonglin Chen; Yihui Zhong; Chenglai Wan

Introduction Greenhouse cultivation modifies agricultural microclimates and may be associated with temporal changes in soil microbial communities\. We investigated a representative vegetable greenhouse and an adjacent open\-field site in the subtropical red\-soil region of Jiangxi Province, China\. Methods Air temperature and relative humidity were monitored continuously for one year in both environments, while soil temperature and volumetric water content were monitored within the greenhouse\. Monthly soil samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing\. Results The greenhouse exhibited pronounced daytime warming, nighttime heat retention, and generally higher relative humidity\. Soil bacterial community composition differed significantly between greenhouse and open\-field soils, while alpha\-diversity differences varied among seasons\. Month\-resolved analyses revealed significant temporal dynamics\. Air temperature and relative humidity jointly explained 15\.59% of the variation in bacterial community structure\. Potential co\-occurrence networks also differed between the two environments in topology and in the proportions of positive and negative correlations\. Discussion The results document year\-round differences in microclimate and soil bacterial community dynamics between greenhouse and open\-field cultivation environments\. The measured atmospheric microclimate variables showed statistically detectable but limited associations with bacterial community composition, providing a basis for soil microbiome monitoring and environmental management in subtropical protected agriculture\.

## [Corrosion effects on shear resistance and fatigue behavior of self\-piercing riveted cold\-formed steel connections](../publications/948af82bc40e5f08ca84.md)

Qi Si; Zhihong Pan; Faxing Ding; Xiaoyu Wu

Cold\-formed thin\-walled steel structures are increasingly adopted in modern construction, yet their safety is governed by the reliability of the connections, which are frequently exposed to aggressive environments and earthquake\- or service\-induced cyclic deformations\. Self\-piercing riveting \(SPR\) has emerged as an efficient, automated joining technique, but its performance under a corrosion environment remains poorly understood\. To address these gaps, this study investigates the effects of corrosion on the shear resistance and fatigue behavior of SPR connections in cold\-formed steel sheets\. Accelerated corrosion tests are first conducted to obtain specimens with different corrosion levels\. Subsequently, monotonic shear tests and fatigue tests are performed to evaluate the degradation of mechanical properties and fatigue performance\. The failure modes, load\-displacement responses, and fatigue lives are systematically analyzed\. The results show that after 90 days of corrosion, the shear capacity decreased by 15\.3%\-35\.6% depending on the joint geometry, and the fatigue life decreased by 17\.6%\-39\.0% depending on the load level\. Furthermore, an interpretable machine\-learning framework based on XGBoost with SHAP \(SHapley Additive exPlanations\) analysis is adopted to quantify the contribution of each corrosion and geometric factor to the capacity degradation, thereby revealing the dominant mechanisms of shear\- and fatigue\-resistance loss\. The findings of this study provide new insights into the corrosion\-induced degradation mechanisms of SPR connections and contribute to the development of more reliable design methods for cold\-formed steel structures in aggressive environments\.

## [Pengaruh Metode Skimming terhadap Kemampuan Membaca Pemahaman Siswa Kelas V](../publications/948d58f6eba6c9b691d5.md)

Dhita Salma Aliya Riadi; Dewi Setiyaningsih

Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh metode skimming terhadap kemampuan membaca pemahaman siswa kelas V di SD Islam Terpadu Yasiru Kebon Jeruk\. Penelitian menggunakan desain kuasi\-eksperimen nonequivalent pretest\-posttest control group dengan dua kelas utuh\. Kelas VA sebagai kelompok eksperimen dan kelas VB sebagai kelompok kontrol masing\-masing terdiri atas 32 siswa\. Kelompok eksperimen memperoleh pembelajaran membaca dengan prosedur skimming selama empat pertemuan, sedangkan kelompok kontrol mengikuti pembelajaran konvensional\. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes pilihan ganda 15 butir yang mengukur pemahaman faktual, interpretatif, dan aplikatif\. Semua butir instrumen memenuhi kriteria validitas pada uji yang dilaporkan dalam skripsi, sedangkan reliabilitas internalnya sebesar 0,781\. Analisis deskriptif menunjukkan bahwa rerata pretest kelompok eksperimen 60,88 dan kelompok kontrol 60,44\. Sesudah perlakuan, rerata posttest berturut\-turut menjadi 82,63 dan 67,75\. Karena varians posttest tidak homogen, perbedaan akhir dianalisis dengan uji Welch\. Hasilnya menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan, t\(50,02\) = 21,09; p &lt; 0,001, dengan selisih rerata 14,88 poin dan ukuran efek Hedges g = 5,21\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa skimming, ketika diajarkan sebagai prosedur menelusuri struktur teks dan memeriksa kembali informasi penting, berkaitan dengan peningkatan membaca pemahaman yang lebih tinggi daripada pembelajaran konvensional dalam konteks penelitian ini\. Generalisasi temuan perlu hati\-hati karena penelitian melibatkan dua kelas pada satu sekolah\.

## [SmartTwin AI: An Explainable Predictive\-Maintenance Decision\-Support Framework for Smart Manufacturing](../publications/948f3bc80a9d8f01ed33.md)

Khaled Taha Fouly

This research presents SmartTwin AI, a software\-based framework for predictive maintenance in smart manufacturing\. The study explores how machine\-learning models can use industrial sensor measurements to identify potential machine failures and support maintenance decisions\. Experiments were conducted using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset, which contains 10,000 records of machine operating conditions\. Three machine\-learning models were evaluated: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting\. The evaluation included precision, recall, F1\-score, ROC\-AUC, and confusion matrices\. A threshold\-tuning experiment was also performed to improve the detection of potential failures\. The results show that the Random Forest model achieved a ROC\-AUC of 0\.9653\. After threshold tuning, the model achieved a recall of 79\.41% on the test set, demonstrating a potential approach for identifying machines that may require maintenance\. This work combines concepts from Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Engineering and Technology\. It provides a reproducible software\-based research workflow, experimental results, visualizations, and a proposed system architecture\. Important limitation: The AI4I 2020 dataset is a synthetic benchmark dataset\. The experiments were conducted on this dataset and do not represent a live deployment or a physical factory experiment\. The proposed framework is a research prototype and requires further validation using real industrial data\. The accompanying research paper and reproducibility materials document the methodology, results, limitations, and potential future work\.

## [Improving African American Participation in U\.S\. Oncology Trials Through Community Partnerships, Trusted Messengers, and Decentralized Clinical Recruitment Strategies](../publications/9490e00f6d5916f7ac8f.md)

Deryl Hasbifa

Equitable participation in oncology trials is essential for generating evidence that reflects population diversity and supports fair access to emerging cancer therapies\. In the United States, African American participation remains constrained by structural exclusion, unequal referral opportunities, financial burdens, geographic barriers, and mistrust associated with historical and ongoing discrimination\. This proposed narrative review examines how community partnerships, trusted messengers, and decentralized recruitment strategies can address these interconnected challenges\. The review will synthesize literature on partnerships with community organizations, churches, patient advocates, and local healthcare providers; communication delivered by trusted clinicians and community leaders; and recruitment models incorporating remote consent, telehealth, satellite clinics, and navigation support\. Particular attention will be given to institutional accountability, culturally responsive communication, transparent eligibility criteria, and practical assistance with transportation, childcare, and digital access\. A multilevel framework will connect community engagement with clinical referral practices and trial design, emphasizing shared governance and sustained relationships\. Evaluation priorities will include recruitment, enrollment, retention, participant experience, and representativeness\. The review aims to inform strategies that expand participation while safeguarding informed consent, reducing participation burdens, and strengthening equitable research access\.

## [Value perceptions and implementation priorities for public PHR adoption in Taiwan: an importance–performance analysis with the Chuchiming Index](../publications/9495c249ffdc0304c51a.md)

Yukiko Ono; Chien\-Chih Chen; Ching\-Heng Chiu; Yuan\-Kuei Li; Yen\-Lin Chen; Po\-Jen Hsiao; Kun\-Yi Lin; Mingchih Chen; Meng\-Chiung Lin; Chi\-Ming Chu

Abstract Background Value perceptions of personal health record \(PHR\) components at the pre\-adoption stage remain underexplored, despite their critical role in promoting the adoption of public PHRs\. Importance–Performance Analysis \(IPA\) may have limitations in identifying priority issues due to skewed distributions of evaluations\. Objective To quantitatively assess citizens’ value perceptions of public PHR platform components using IPA according to usage experience and to evaluate the utility of the Chuchiming Index \(ChI\) as a complement to IPA\. Methods A cross\-sectional study was conducted among internet\-using citizens\. After viewing a video introducing an artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-powered extended PHR platform concept, participants rated the importance and acceptance of platform functions and system design and security components\. Participants were grouped by their experience using an existing public PHR platform, and quadrant analysis was conducted using IPA, with ChI used to quantify improvement priorities\. Stratified IPA analyses were conducted by age and income, which were identified as factors associated with the use of existing public PHR platforms\. Results A total of 177 participants were included in the analysis\. All components showed high importance and acceptance regardless of usage experience\. Among nonusers, medical record display, wearable data integration, and platform integration fell into Quadrant II, all with positive ChI values\. Among users, no items fell into Quadrant II; however, platform integration showed a high ChI value\. For system design and security, privacy and security assurance showed the highest ChI values in both groups\. Stratified analyses showed marked differences in value perceptions by usage experience among older adults and middle\-income groups\. Conclusion Value perceptions of individual public PHR platform components differed by usage experience and sociodemographic characteristics\. Promoting public PHR adoption requires optimizing strategies that encompass platform design, system implementation, and user uptake according to the needs of different population groups\. The ChI complements IPA by enhancing the identification and interpretation of priorities, even under ceiling effects common in public service evaluations\. These findings contribute to decision\-making regarding the design and implementation strategies of public PHR platforms\.

## [Tính chất cơ \- lý của vữa rót giữ nước sử dụng phụ phẩm công nghiệp cho mặt đường bán mềm](../publications/949c5888ab4707687d4f.md)

Đạt Nguyễn Viết; Anh Bùi Tuấn; Hợi Trần Danh; Phúc Nguyễn Quang

Mặt đường bán mềm \(SFP\) đang được nghiên cứu theo hướng giữ nước nhằm giảm hiệu ứng đảo nhiệt đô thị\. Tiêu chuẩn CJJ/T 206\-2013 quy định vữa giữ nước gồm bột xỉ, tro bay, vôi thủy hóa và nước, nhưng chưa lượng hóa ảnh hưởng của tỷ lệ nước/bột xỉ \(N/BX\) đến tính chất của vữa\. Nghiên cứu này đánh giá các tính chất cơ \- lý của vữa giữ nước gồm bột xỉ lò cao nghiền mịn, tro bay và vôi thủy hóa, trong đó tỷ lệ N/BX \(0,66 \- 1,00\) là thông số thiết kế chính được thay đổi, còn hàm lượng tro bay và vôi thủy hóa được giữ cố định lần lượt ở 4 % và 8 %\. Độ chảy và độ hút nước của bốn tỷ lệ phối trộn \(TL1 \- TL4\) được xác định theo CJJ/T 206\-2013; cường độ chịu uốn và chịu nén được xác định theo TCVN 3121\-11:2022 ở các tuổi 7, 14, 21 và 28 ngày\. Khi N/BX tăng, thời gian chảy giảm, độ hút nước tăng gần tuyến tính; cường độ tăng theo tuổi nhưng giảm khi N/BX tăng\. Các phương trình thực nghiệm giữa độ hút nước và cường độ ở tuổi 7 ngày chỉ có giá trị trong phạm vi khảo sát\. Trong bốn tỷ lệ, chỉ TL3 \(N/BX = 0,87\) và TL4 \(N/BX = 1,00\) đáp ứng yêu cầu về độ chảy và cường độ của CJJ/T 206\-2013, trong khi không cấp phối nào đạt yêu cầu độ hút nước ở tuổi 7 ngày không nhỏ hơn 30 % \(lớn nhất 27,89 %\)\. TL3 được đề xuất khi ưu tiên cường độ, còn TL4 có độ hút nước cao nhất trong các cấp phối đáp ứng yêu cầu về độ chảy\. Khả năng duy trì nước theo thời gian và hiệu quả làm mát chưa được đánh giá\.

## [RANKING ALGORITHMS FOR MEDICAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS BASED ON NOMINAL DATA](../publications/94adfd568d0eb0fac1e2.md)

Hulkaraxon Rajapboyeva

The rapid expansion of electronic health records \(EHRs\), hospital information systems, clinical decision\-support platforms, and digital patient registries has increased the need for reliable algorithms capable of processing heterogeneous clinical information\. A substantial proportion of medical information is nominal rather than numerical or ordinal\. Examples include diagnosis categories, medication classes, symptom types, admission reasons, procedure codes, departments, blood groups, and other categorical attributes\. Nominal categories have no inherent mathematical order; therefore, assigning arbitrary numerical codes to them may introduce artificial relationships and distort the results of statistical or machine\-learning models\. This article examines algorithms for solving ranking problems in medical information systems when the underlying information is nominal\. The methodological framework considers categorical\-data representation, frequency\-based ranking, probabilistic ranking, multinomial logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support\-vector approaches, learning\-to\-rank methods, and rank aggregation\. Particular attention is given to one\-hot encoding and other appropriate representations of nominal variables, because preserving the absence of ordinal meaning is fundamental to valid modelling\. Published medical informatics studies demonstrate that ranking can support emergency triage, retrieval of relevant EHR information, clinical prediction, and prioritization of patient\-related information\. For example, a learning\-to\-rank study involving 90 EHR notes reported an AUC\-ROC of 0\.940 for ranking candidate medical terms, while a structured\-record relevance\-ranking study evaluated 1,010 medications and 2,913 problems from 99 patients\. These published results demonstrate the practical feasibility of ranking approaches in healthcare, although performance depends strongly on data quality, outcome definition, validation, calibration, and clinical context\. The article proposes a general algorithmic framework for nominal\-data ranking that combines categorical encoding, clinically meaningful feature construction, model training, ranking\-score generation, validation, and human oversight\.

## [Quantitative SPECT\-CT and textural analysis for neuro\-endocrine tumours](../publications/94b44fbe3051af514035.md)

Alastair J\. Gemmell

Background Quantification is an important emerging technique in nuclear medicine imaging\. It may provide additional clinical information to add to visual interpretation, whilst reducing inter\-operator variability\. Technological developments and commercial solutions have recently increased access to quantitative Single Photon Emission Tomography \(SPECT\)\. There are few studies optimising acquisition and reconstruction parameters and only a limited number of clinical applications have been investigated\. The growth in imaging of Neuroendocrine Tumours \(NETs\), both for diagnosis and following molecular radiotherapy, highlights Somatostatin Receptor Imaging \(SRI\) as an ideal candidate for applying quantification\. Aims The thesis sought to assess the accuracy and longitudinal stability of a commercial quantification package for SPECT, Siemens Broad Quantification \(&quot;BroadQuant&quot;\) for two radionuclides, 99mTc and 177Lu\. A further aim was to apply quantification to SPECT imaging of NETs, for the integration of quantification into clinical practice\. Methods A series of experiments were designed to measure the accuracy and reproducibility of each stage of the BroadQuant calibration process\. Uncertainties were calculated for each step and combined to provide an overall uncertainty on the calibration factor\. A range of Quality Control tests were evaluated to determine how best to monitor the longitudinal stability of the calibration\. A phantom that mimicked inhomogeneous lesions was used to identify robust textural analysis features for further study in clinical applications\. The use of SPECT quantification for imaging of NETs was investigated for a number of clinical applications\. The impact of Somatostatin Analogue medication on quantitative SPECT measurement of 99mTc\-EDDA/HYNIC\-TOC was studied, as well as whether a Tumour Sink Effect \(TSE\) affected uptake\. The use of quantitative metrics and textural analysis features as an alternative to the visual assessment of Krenning Score in 99mTc\-EDDA/HYNICTOC SPECT was examined\. Post\-therapy SPECT imaging following Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy \(PRRT\) was analysed, to determine the predictive value of quantitative metrics\. Statistical harmonisation methods were applied to quantitative data from two gamma cameras with the aim of expansion of quantitative SPECT to multiple sites for future studies\. Results The calibration process was comprehensively examined, providing a number of recommendations for the user, and estimating an uncertainty in the calibration factor of 1\.37% for 99mTc and 2\.81% for 177Lu respectively\. Longitudinal measurements of calibration accuracy determined that stability could be successfully measured with Shewhart charts monitoring Standardised Uptake Value \(SUV\), with a suitable stable period for 99mTc calibration assessed as being up to 9 months\. For patients on Somatostatin Analogue medication, a reduction in physiological uptake of 99mTc\-EDDA/HYNIC\-TOC was shown, that was not reflected in pathological uptake\. No evidence was found for the presence of a TSE for 99mTc\-EDDA/HYNIC\-TOC\. A quantitative Krenning Score was found to be more robust than visual interpretation of Krenning Score, with a comparable level of accuracy when compared to expert assessment\. Following feature reduction, a range of textural analysis features were investigated in the context of post\-PRRT SPECT imaging\. Sphericity was determined to be predictive both of overall survival and for patient\-reported symptom response\. Finally, statistical harmonisation using Location\-Scale adjustment was found to improve the harmonisation between gamma cameras for multiple quantitative metrics, demonstrating a potential tool for combining data from multiple cameras for clinical studies\. Conclusion This thesis addresses the key aspects of the SPECT quantification process, from the calibration of the gamma camera through to clinical applications\. It demonstrates that SPECT quantification can be an accurate and robust tool\. The use of quantification and textural analysis has been shown to have positive clinical value when applied to the imaging of neuroendocrine tumours\.

## [AirSense AI: Urban Air Quality Intelligence Platform](../publications/94c479e62b4809b7a8d0.md)

Madhur Jain; Shilpi Jain; Nikhil Negi; Aditya Kumar Jha; Krishna Tyagi

Urban air pollution is one of the most persistent environmental and public\-health problems facing Indian cities, and Delhi in particular records some of the highest particulate matter concentrations in the world during the post\-monsoon and winter months\. Public air\-quality portals in India largely display current or historical readings, but they rarely tell a city administrator what the air will look like over the next few days, or where a pollution spike is likely originating from\. This gap between “knowing today&\#x27;s AQI” and “deciding what to do about it” motivates AirSense AI, a full\-stack urban air\-quality intelligence platform designed as an academic prototype for Delhi\. The system ingests PM2\.5, PM10 and NO₂ station readings together with weather variables, satellite fire detections and land\-use information, converts pollutant concentrations into a standardized Air Quality Index using the U\.S\. EPA methodology, and applies a gradient\-boosted decision tree model \(XGBoost\) to forecast AQI up to 72 hours ahead\. In parallel, the platform combines NASA FIRMS active\-fire data with OpenStreetMap land\-use polygons and Haversine\-distance calculations to rank probable pollution hotspots, and uses a large language model \(Groq/LLaMA 3\) to translate the resulting numerical evidence into readable, bilingual \(English/Hindi\) advisories and enforcement summaries for administrators and citizens\. The results are presented through a React and Leaflet\-based interactive dashboard\. This paper describes the motivation, related work, and proposed architecture of AirSense AI as an integrated decision\-support system rather than a monitoring\-only tool\. As the platform is at the prototype stage, no experimental forecasting accuracy, source\-attribution validation, or user\-study results are reported here; these are identified as required additions for the next version of this paper\.

## [Yari, Masoud: Romantic Love as an Evolutionary Bug in Human Consciousness](../publications/94dbec78c8ca043ef076.md)



This paper argues that the modern category of romantic love characteristically attenuates affective self\-authorship, making a subject’s affective life appear to originate elsewhere—in the beloved, in fate, or in love itself\. The underlying states are real; culture organizes their classification and the attribution of their authorship\. Building on James Averill’s syndrome account of emotion, I develop a feature his framework identifies but does not adequately explain: romantic love’s distinctive non\-agentive construal\. I distinguish unchosen onset, limited control, and external elicitation from the further claim that an affective state is authored beyond the subject\. Drawing on receptive self\-description, practical helplessness, asymmetries in explanatory demand, and the selective social uptake of non\-agentive claims, I use Wegner’s exclusivity condition as a candidate mechanism to argue that the romantic paradigm does more than acknowledge involuntariness\. It makes alternative loci of authorship culturally available and discounts the subject’s own contribution\. I describe this pattern as an “evolutionary bug in human consciousness”: not a defect in evolved systems of attraction, attachment, and reward, but a failure of self\-understanding in which the subject’s involvement in their affective life becomes obscured\. This framing may help sustain the attachment it renders intelligible, creating a possible feedback loop between cultural interpretation and lived experience\. External elicitation and limited control do not, by themselves, warrant displaced authorship\. The paper concludes with testable predictions concerning authorship attribution, explanatory demand, and normative mitigation\.

## [Advances in catalytic hydrogen storage materials: progress, breakthroughs, and challenges toward scalable applications](../publications/94e2fa3808d4527a1d4d.md)

Pan Shulin; W\. Tahri; Rashid Khan; Mazen Alshaaer

Hydrogen storage and release catalysts that are large\-scale, efficient, and reversible provide a significant challenge for the development of long\-term hydrogen energy systems \(HES\)\. This review critically examines catalytic approaches to hydrogen storage systems \(HSS\), including, metal hydrides, metal\-organic frameworks \(MOFs\), covalent organic frameworks \(COFs\), porous materials, nanostructured catalysts, bimetallic alloys, hybrid composites, and single\-atom catalysts \(SACs\)\. It evaluates how catalyst composition, structure, and active\-site properties influence hydrogen activation, transport, sorption kinetics, cycling stability, and reversibility\. Drawing on experimental findings and theoretical approaches, the review compares these relationships across different material classes\. This comparative focus extends assessments based on individual materials or catalyst classes by identifying shared design principles and materials specific limitations\. Finally, it outlines the main barriers and proposes research directions for developing sustainable, efficient, and reversible hydrogen storage\.

## [An Exploratory Factor Analysis \(EFA\) of Lifelong Learners’ Attributes Among English Language Teaching \(ELT\) Teachers in Myanmar’s Higher Education Institutions](../publications/94e635505381d4606110.md)

Thi Thi Khine; Walainart Meepan; Choosak Ueangchokchai

This study examined the levels and underlying factor structure of lifelong learners’ attributes reported by English language teaching \(ELT\) teachers in Myanmar’s higher education institutions\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted with 330 teachers using a questionnaire comprising 10 demographic questions and 50 items across six conceptual domains\. Descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis \(EFA\) were applied\. Minimum Residual extraction with Oblimin rotation produced a five\-factor solution comprising 44 retained items: Collaborative Mindset, Digital Adaptability, Pedagogical Innovation, Reflective Capacity and Higher\-Order Thinking, and Learning Autonomy and Self\-Management\. The five factors explained 51\.1% of the total variance, and the final scale demonstrated excellent internal consistency \(α = \.958\)\. ELT teachers reported high levels across all six original conceptual domains\. The findings provide preliminary evidence of the scale’s internal structure and offer a foundation for further validation and research on lifelong learners’ attributes among ELT teachers in Myanmar’s higher education institutions\. The findings have practical implications for 1\) institutional policies, 2\) teacher professional development, and 3\) the design of targeted continuous professional development \(CPD\) programs to strengthen lifelong learners’ attributes among ELT teachers\.

## [From challenge to solution: Perspectives on AI\-powered multi\-omics in tackling CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance in breast cancer](../publications/94ea28b60f6f51e4933d.md)

Jia Wu; Xinran Liu; Guoyu Wu

Currently, three CDK4/6 inhibitors \(CDK4/6i\) have been approved globally in clinical practice for combination with endocrine therapy as first\-line treatment for advanced or metastatic hormone receptor\-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2\-negative \(HR \+ /HER2 − \) breast cancer\. The advent of CDK4/6i has significantly improved the survival rates of patients with breast cancer\. However, once resistance to CDK4/6i emerges, follow\-up treatment options are limited\. Therefore, there is a growing demand for biomarkers to detect intrinsic or acquired resistance and for effective subsequent therapies\. Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\) and multi\-omics data have enabled significant breakthroughs in biomarker prediction and drug development, advancing personalized medicine\. This review synthesizes the primary mechanisms of CDK4/6i resistance in breast cancer and explores the current applications and prospects of integrating AI with multi\-omics to overcome these challenges and advance personalized therapeutic strategies\.

## [Pharmacokinetics of isoflurane uptake and disposition in piglets](../publications/94eee2ef5ceca0fa4f25.md)

Che\-Hao Hsu; Lin Tso\-Chou; Oliver Yoa‐Pu Hu; Cheng\-Huei Hsiong; Shung‐Tai Ho; Chih\-Cherng Lu

Background Isoflurane is a cardioprotective inhalational anesthetic widely used in cardiac surgery, but prior studies focused primarily on uptake parameters\. We examined both uptake and disposition in piglets using inspiratory, end\-tidal, arterial, and mixed venous concentrations\. Methods Seven piglets received a fixed inspiratory concentration of 2% isoflurane during a 2\-h uptake phase, followed by a 2\-h disposition phase\. Inspiratory and end\-tidal concentrations were measured using an infrared analyzer\. Femoral arterial blood and pulmonary artery mixed venous blood were sampled to determine isoflurane concentrations via gas chromatography at 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100, and 120 min during both uptake and disposition phases\. Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters were recorded simultaneously\. Body uptake and disposition rates were calculated by multiplying the difference between arterial and pulmonary artery blood concentrations by cardiac output\. Results The rates of isoflurane body uptake increased gradually during the initial 20 min, reaching 20\.7 mL min \-1 , before slowly declining to 10\.5 mL min \-1 by 120 min\. Continuous decreases in washout rates were observed during the subsequent disposition phase\. The concentration–time curves for end\-tidal, arterial blood, and pulmonary artery blood concentrations fit well with zero\-order input and first\-order disposition kinetics\. Arterial and pulmonary artery blood concentrations were best modeled by a two\-compartment system\. Only 14\.5% of the isoflurane accumulated during the 2\-h uptake phase was eliminated during the subsequent 2\-h disposition phase\. Conclusion Under a fixed inspiratory isoflurane concentration, body uptake in piglets was empirically approximated by a zero\-order input process over the modeled 120\-min uptake interval, whereas the subsequent 2\-h disposition phase followed first\-order kinetics and was best described by a two\-compartment pharmacokinetic model\.

## [Women’s Representation and Digital Paratexts in the Pirelli Calendar: A Framing Approach \(1964–2024\)](../publications/94f3dbc2b0f852bbb529.md)

Öznur NALÇINKAYA

As digital environments diversify, brands increasingly construct their public image not only through what is shown but also through official materials that guide how those signs should be read\. First published in 1964 for promotional purposes, the Pirelli Calendar has become an iconic case that makes visible aesthetic and ideological shifts in the representation of women within visual culture, while being continuously reframed through layers of digital paratext\. This study examines the transformation of women’s representation in the Calendar between 1964 and 2024 by focusing on the relationship between visual codes—nudity, gaze/orientation, pose and agency, and Goffman\-inspired indicators—and corporate digital paratexts, including official promotional statements, interview excerpts, and webpage descriptions\. Using purposive sampling, three images were selected from each chosen edition, yielding a corpus of 30 visuals; six accessible official paratext texts were also included\. The visuals were analyzed through visual content analysis and semiotic reading, whereas the paratexts were examined via a framing approach\. Findings indicate that an erotic/objectifying frame dominated from 1964 through the 1990s, while, from the 2010s onward, “empowerment,” “authenticity,” and “diversity” emerged as central themes in official digital discourse\. Yet certain patterns associated with the male gaze persist, and the relationship between corporate paratext and visual representation alternates between alignment and tension across different editions\. The study discusses how postfeminist “empowerment” rhetoric is re\-framed and circulated digitally within brand storytelling\.

## [AI\-Based Prediction of Student Placement Readiness: A Machine Learning](../publications/9508afca1123d79750b8.md)

Priyanka Pathare

This paper proposes an AI\-based student placement\-readiness prediction system using machine learning techniques to assess employability\-related skills and identify areas for improvement\. Student placement readiness depends on several factors, including academic performance, aptitude, technical skills, communication abilities, project experience, internships, and interview preparation\. The proposed system integrates data validation, preprocessing, feature engineering, machine learning prediction, explainability, and personalized skill\-gap recommendations\. Candidate algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Random Forests can be evaluated using appropriate metrics, including precision, recall, macro\-F1 score, and calibration\. The framework aims to help students understand their preparation levels and receive actionable recommendations for improving their skills\. It may also support placement coordinators in planning targeted training activities\. The system is intended as a decision\-support tool rather than a guarantee of employment or an automated method for denying placement opportunities\. Privacy, fairness, explainability, secure data handling, and human oversight are important design considerations\. This paper presents a proposed framework; no experimental results are claimed\. Actual performance must be evaluated using an authorized, representative dataset\.

## [A case study of storytelling as an \(inclusive\) pedagogical strategy in undergraduate statistics teaching](../publications/951038d85bfcd258537f.md)

Johan Ferreira

Traditional statistics teaching often emphasizes theoretical exposition and technical application; these approaches can limit engagement and accessibility, particularly given the pace and predominantly technological manner at which students consume information\. To address this, a novel, student\-centered intervention was implemented in a senior undergraduate statistics course: students voluntarily created fictional narratives in which statistical concepts became characters in original short stories\. Twenty\-three contributions were edited and published as an illustrated, open\-access anthology\. Observations based on a pilot implementation demonstrate the potential of inclusive strategies that value diverse modes of knowledge\-making and expression within a traditionally hierarchical discipline\. Results suggest that integrating creative storytelling into the statistics curriculum can complement conventional instruction, support inclusive, peer\-led learning, and provide multiple entry points into advanced statistical thinking\. The approach is practical, scalable, and transferable to other disciplines, offering a replicable model for curriculum innovation that promotes equity, autonomy, and imaginative engagement in higher education\.

## [Writing Motivation and Self‐Efficacy in AI ‐Chatbot‐Supported EFL Writing: Exploratory Insights Across Proficiency Levels](../publications/9512362cbc99c8fdddaf.md)

Thi\-Ngoc\-Anh Duong; Hsiu‐Ling Chen

ABSTRACT Background Writing motivation and self‐efficacy are critical factors of success in English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) contexts, yet they are frequently undermined by learner anxiety and limited teacher feedback\. While artificial intelligence \(AI\) chatbots offer potential for adaptive writing support, limited research has examined these affective constructs in parallel across learner proficiency levels\. Objectives This study investigated changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy among high school EFL learners at higher‐ and lower‐proficiency levels following chatbot‐supported writing and examined whether these changes differed across proficiency levels\. Methods Using an exploratory mixed‐methods design, the study involved 47 Vietnamese high school students divided into higher‐ and lower‐proficiency level groups\. Over the 11‐week study, participants completed 8 weeks of AI‐supported writing activities using a chatbot designed in accordance with principles of Self‐Determination Theory, Self‐Regulated Learning Theory and Self‐Efficacy Theory\. Changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy were examined using pre‐ and post‐questionnaires and semi‐structured interviews\. Results and Conclusions The quantitative findings revealed that intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy increased over time in both proficiency groups, with no significant differences in the magnitude of change between higher‐ and lower‐proficiency learners\. This suggests that the affective changes observed during AI‐supported writing were not confined to one proficiency group\. The qualitative findings indicated that learners linked their positive experiences to reduced anxiety, clearer guidance, and supportive interaction, although the types of support they valued differed by proficiency level\. Overall, the findings suggest that when positioned as a supportive writing partner rather than an answer generator, AI chatbot feedback may be associated with positive motivational and self‐efficacy development in mixed‐ability EFL writing classrooms\.

## [The relationship between gut microbiota‐friendly diet and the prevalence and severity of asthma in children](../publications/9512705817cf38ef5757.md)

Li‐Juan Tan; Xifeng Tang; Yijun Shan; Yuqian Ren; Ting Sun; 周一平; Jialei Fu; 张玉彩; Yun Cui

OBJECTIVES: Dietary factors may impact asthma indirectly by modulating the composition and activity of the gut microbiota\. This study aimed to explore the potential relationship between gut microbiota\-friendly diet and both the prevalence and severity of asthma in children\. METHODS: We selected a total of 2256 children from the 2021\-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey\. The gut microbiota\-friendly diet was assessed using the Diet\-Gut Microbiome Index \(DI\-GM\), which incorporates 14 specific food constituents\. To calculate the DI\-GM, two non\-consecutive 24\-h dietary recalls data were used, from which the relevant food constituents were derived\. A higher DI\-GM score indicates greater alignment with a gut microbiota\-friendly diet\. RESULTS: Among the 2256 U\.S\. children, the weighted prevalence of asthma is 13\.36%\. In fully adjusted models, DI\-GM was not significantly associated with asthma prevalence overall or within any subgroups\. However, higher DI\-GM \(T2\) was significantly associated with a lower risk of the mild asthma phenotype in the 5\-16 age group\. In contrast, no significant associations were observed between DI\-GM and asthma severity in the other age groups\. Subgroup analysis showed a higher DI\-GM score was significantly correlated with a lower risk for asthma in subgroups stratified by obesity status\. CONCLUSIONS: Higher DI\-GM scores were significantly inversely associated with asthma severity risk in children aged 5\-16 years and in obese individuals\. These cross\-sectional findings support the need for longitudinal studies to determine whether dietary modulation may affect asthma severity via microbiota\-dependent mechanisms\.
