## [Neurological Basis of Learning Among Persons with Intellectual Disability](../publications/959c937ed15a3fc2cb64.md)

B\. Suresh Lal

Learning is a complex neurobiological process involving the coordinated functioning of multiple brain systems responsible for attention, perception, memory, executive functioning, emotion and motor activity\. Contemporary neuroscience has demonstrated that learning is accompanied by changes in neural connectivity and brain function through mechanisms of neuroplasticity\. Understanding these mechanisms is particularly important in the context of persons with intellectual disability\. In persons with intellectual disability there are differences in cognitive and adaptive functioning that may influence attention, working memory, executive functioning &amp; language, problem\-solving and the acquisition &amp; generalization of new skills\. This review examines the neurological basis of learning and considers the relevance of Brain\-Based Learning \(BBL\) as a neuroscience\-informed educational framework for learners with intellectual disabilities\. A narrative review of peer\-reviewed research, systematic reviews, meta\-analyses and scholarly books was undertaken\. The literature was thematically synthesized around brain structures involved in learning, neuroplasticity, memory, attention, executive functioning, emotional processing and the cognitive characteristics associated with intellectual disability\. The review further examines major principles of Brain\-Based Learning, including multisensory instruction, active engagement, meaningful learning, emotional support, repetition, individualized instruction and inclusive classroom practices\. The reviewed literature indicates that learning is facilitated when instruction is meaningful, appropriately challenging, emotionally supportive and responsive to individual differences\. This article contributes to improved engagement, knowledge acquisition, memory retention and participation among learners with intellectual disability\.

## [Anàlisi espacial de la severitat d&\#x27;incendis forestals a la Comunitat Valenciana mitjançant teledetecció i machine learning](../publications/95a7a4e37582f0df72cc.md)

Giancarlo Gómez Lucero

\[ES\] Este trabajo analiza la interacción entre diversas variables ambientales y el daño producido por el fuego para optimizar la gestión forestal\. El objetivo principal consiste en estructurar la base de un modelo predictivo espacial orientado a evaluar la severidad de los incendios en la Comunitat Valenciana\. La metodología emplea computación en la nube mediante Google Earth Engine para el procesamiento masivo de series temporales de imágenes satelitales Sentinel\-2, extrayendo índices espectrales de severidad y estrés hídrico previos y posteriores a cada evento\. Posteriormente, a través de programación en Python, se ejecuta el cruce espacial y temporal topológico de estas métricas con Modelos Digitales de Elevaciones, cartografía de usos del suelo y registros meteorológicos históricos\. Esta convergencia paramétrica facilita el cálculo de la Humedad del Combustible Vivo \(HCV\), un indicador biofísico que constituirá un insumo para la fase predictiva con técnicas de Machine Learning\. La consolidación de esta robusta infraestructura geoespacial posee gran utilidad práctica para la protección civil y ordenación territorial, siendo clave para anticipar el comportamiento del fuego, priorizar la prevención silvícola y optimizar los recursos de extinción\.

## [Co\-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM\-1, KPC\-2, IMP\-1, and AFM\-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient](../publications/95a9ca07839620b0d991.md)

Yi Zhang; Zhirong Zhang; Senhong Ying; 王三荣; Rong Xiang

Background Carbapenem\-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare\. Methods Metagenomic next\-generation sequencing \(mNGS\) and whole\-genome sequencing \(WGS\) were performed on a bronchoalveolar lavage fluid \(BALF\) sample from a patient with severe pneumonia\. Results Four carbapenemase genes— bla AFM\-1 , bla NDM\-1 , bla IMP\-1 , and bla KPC\-2 —were simultaneously detected in a single specimen\. Three carbapenem\-resistant isolates were recovered: an ST11 K\. pneumoniae carrying bla KPC\-2 and virulence\-associated genes, an S\. algae strain with an assembly\-based tandem chromosomal bla NDM\-1 arrangement, and a P\. stutzeri strain co\-harboring bla AFM\-1 and bla IMP\-1 \. Genomic analysis revealed complex mobile genetic contexts associated with these resistance determinants\. Conclusion The coexistence of four carbapenemase genes within one clinical sample highlights the complexity of polymicrobial carbapenem resistance and underscores the importance of genomic surveillance\.

## [Improved Swin Transformer\-based fine\-grained human motion understanding approach driven by simulation\-based augmentation for intangible cultural heritage in sports](../publications/95abb97a3aed67b91123.md)

Xiaofang Yang; Xiwen Huang; Linghui Yu; Bo Dai

Fine\-grained human motion understanding for Intangible Cultural Heritage \(ICH\) in sports faces challenges such as high similarity in posture between motion categories and significant differences in temporal rhythms within categories\. Existing spatiotemporal motion models suffer from insufficient feature discrimination under small sample conditions and severe degradation in generalization ability when migrating from the simulation domain to the real domain\. This paper proposes an improved Swin Transformer\-based fine\-grained human motion understanding method driven by simulation\-based data augmentation for ICH\. The method reconstructs the 3D skeleton of ICH motions using the Unity3D simulation engine combined with the OptiTrack motion capture system, and generates multimodal simulation samples by applying random perturbations to lighting, viewpoint, and body shape parameters\. Addressing the limitation of the original Swin Transformer window self\-attention mechanism lacking inter\-frame temporal awareness, a Temporal Difference Attention \(TDA\) module is embedded after each Stage attention layer\. This module explicitly models the rhythmic motion changes of ICH motions through the differential response of feature maps from adjacent frames\. A cross\-domain alignment loss, \\\(\\:\{\\text\{L\}\}\_\{\\text\{MMD\}\}\\\) , based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy \(MMD\), is introduced at the top of the feature pyramid to force the convergence of high\-level semantic feature distributions between the simulation and real domains, enabling cross\-domain transferability of spatiotemporal representations\. The overall framework is jointly trained end\-to\-end to complete closed\-loop modeling from simulation generation to real\-world action classification and stage localization\. Experiments are conducted on the public datasets NTU RGB \+ D 120 \(hereinafter referred to as “NTU”\) and Kinetics\-400 for system validation\. The accuracy rates for fine\-grained human action recognition reach 88\.6% and 79\.3%, respectively\. The mean average precision \(mAP\) in cross\-domain scenarios reaches 81\.2%; the MMD distance converges to 0\.038; the temporal intersection over union \(tIoU\) for action stage localization reaches 0\.76\. Further generalization analysis is conducted on the SICHA\-Derived sports ICH action test dataset \(covering 8 categories of traditional actions such as Tai Chi and martial arts routines, totaling 1,240 annotated videos\) derived from NTU\. The proposed method achieves a Top\-1 accuracy of 82\.4%, a 10\.6% point improvement over the strongest baseline, validating the framework’s practicality in the sports ICH scenario\. Notably, under extreme small\-sample conditions with only a single real sample per class, the framework achieves 71\.6% accuracy, substantially exceeding both the simulation\-only variant at 52\.4% and real\-data\-only fine\-tuning at 18\.3%, demonstrating the practical value of the simulation\-based augmentation and cross\-domain alignment mechanisms for real\-world sports ICH scenarios where annotations are inherently scarce\.

## [Feasibility and proof\-of\-concept of a cervical cancer prevention edutainment webisode for African American women in Houston, Texas](../publications/95bd9d5262eae8ce3349.md)

Chakema C\. Carmack; Nawar Ahmed; Antonia Marinoni; Terra Ousley; Angelica M\. Roncancio

Objectives African American women in Harris County, Texas, have a cervical cancer mortality rate higher than other racial/ethnic minorities\. Educational interventions designed to increase women’s participation in cervical cancer screening are needed\. The present study examined the feasibility and preliminary proof\-of\-concept for a culturally tailored cervical cancer prevention edutainment webisode intervention intended to influence knowledge, screening intentions, and HPV vaccination intentions\. Methods N = 40 African American females were administered a pre\-test, completed the edutainment intervention, and completed the post\-test 1 week later\. Results The intervention was feasible regarding recruitment, engagement, retention, and acceptability\. Cervical cancer knowledge, susceptibility, and intentions to screen \(p &lt;0 \.01\) showed positive signal detection in the expected direction, indicating proof\-of\-concept\. Most participants found the edutainment film acceptable for various age groups and public health venues\. Conclusion The intervention demonstrated suitability for future pilot testing and subsequent randomized controlled trial testing to demonstrate efficacy and effectiveness\. To mitigate the cervical cancer disparities among African American women, this population should be informed, motivated, and supported through culturally tailored, effective interventions and public health messaging\.

## [THE EFFECT OF INITIAL LEARNING ABILITIES AND LEARNING INTERESTS ON PAI LEARNING OUTCOMES \(CORRELATIONAL STUDY ON STUDENTS OF SDN CEMPAKA BARU 03 PAGI CENTRAL JAKARTA\)](../publications/95c3e40051ea84351375.md)

Khairun Nasbi; Farhana Farhana

Islamic Religious Education \(PAI\) learning outcomes at the elementary school level often show variations in achievement influenced by students&\#x27; cognitive readiness and motivation\. This study aims to analyze the influence of initial learning abilities and learning interests, both partially and simultaneously, on students&\#x27; PAI learning outcomes at SDN Cempaka Baru 03 Pagi, Central Jakarta\. A quantitative approach with a correlational survey method was used to test the correlation between variables in a sample of 60 students from a total population of 178 students, determined using the Slovin formula and proportional random sampling technique\. Data were collected through calibrated questionnaires for initial abilities and learning interests, as well as multiple\-choice tests and official grade documentation for PAI learning outcomes\. The results showed that the average scores for initial abilities \(97\.85\), learning interests \(89\.32\), and PAI learning outcomes \(82\.37\) were in the high category\. Partial hypothesis testing showed that the variables of initial abilities \(t = \-0\.466; p = 0\.643\) and learning interests \(t = 1\.359; p = 0\.179\) did not significantly influence PAI learning outcomes\. Simultaneous testing yielded an F value of 1\.148 \(p = 0\.325\) with a coefficient of determination \(R2\) of 0\.039, meaning the two variables only contributed 3\.9% to the variation in PAI learning outcomes\. The study&\#x27;s conclusion confirms that students&\#x27; initial learning abilities and learning interests do not have a significant direct influence on PAI test scores at the elementary school level\.

## [Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Chinese Herbal Medicine: Understanding Its Mechanisms and Efficacy](../publications/95d29f578fd6255acfe1.md)



Chinese Herbal Medicine \(CHM\) has been widely used for centuries and remains an important component of healthcare systems worldwide\.The increasing integration of Chinese herbal medicine into modern medicine has intensified interest in understanding its pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics and their contributions to therapeutic efficacy\.This review aims to summarize current knowledge regarding the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, mechanisms of action, therapeutic applications, and safety considerations of Chinese Herbal Medicine\.A comprehensive literature review was conducted using peer\-reviewed articles retrieved from major scientific databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar\.Relevant studies addressing absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, pharmacological mechanisms, herb\-drug interactions, and advanced analytical approaches were evaluated and organized into thematic categories\.Evidence indicates that Chinese Herbal Medicine exerts therapeutic effects through complex multi\-component and multi\-target interactions\.Pharmacokinetic processes influence the bioavailability and disposition of herbal constituents, whereas pharmacodynamic mechanisms involve modulation of receptors, enzymes, signaling pathways, and gene expression\.Emerging approaches such as network pharmacology, chinmedomics, and pharmacometabolomics have improved the understanding of the molecular basis of Chinese Herbal Medicine efficacy\.However, challenges related to standardization, quality control, and herb\-drug interactions remain significant\.Integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic evidence provides a scientific foundation for understanding the efficacy and safety of Chinese Herbal Medicine\.Future advances in systems biology, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine may facilitate the development of more effective and personalized herbal therapies\.

## [Feature Engineering for Biological Sequence and Protein Structure Prediction](../publications/95d65bf3e1594b12f8de.md)

Filip Markovic

Feature engineering remains central to predictive modeling in computational biology, governing how DNA, RNAand protein sequences are converted into numerical forms amenable to machine learning\. The field hasprogressed from compact composition based descriptors such as amino acid composition \(AAC\) and dipeptidecomposition \(DPC\) to correlation based representations \(pseudo amino acid composition, PseAAC, pseudoK\-tuple nucleotide composition, PseKNC\), evolutionary profiles \(position specific scoring matrices, PSSM\), and,more recently, to deep representation learning and biological foundation models\. This narrative review focuseson biological sequence prediction, with particular emphasis on proteins and structure derived features\. Webegin with Chou&\#x27;s five step framework for predictor construction, benchmark curation and redundancyreduction using CD\-HIT and MMseqs2, and the specific challenges of multi label and hierarchical prediction\. Wethen survey handcrafted descriptors, feature selection and dimensionality reduction, and the adaptation ofnatural language processing methods to biological sequences, including k\-mer embeddings, convolutional andrecurrent architectures, and protein and genomic foundation models, including Transformer models such asESM\-2 and DNABERT\-2, the ESMFold structure predictor, and Hyena based genomic models\. We distinguishthree common adaptation strategies: frozen embedding extraction, full fine tuning and parameter efficient finetuning \(PEFT\) \- and discuss hybrid fusion of handcrafted and learned features, structure founded encodings\(DSSP, Foldseek 3Di, ProstT5, SES\-Adapter\), and the role of explainable AI \(SHAP, LIME, Integrated Gradients\)\.Throughout we emphasize homology evaluation, nested validation to avoid selection leakage, confidencebased use of predicted structures, and cautious interpretation of attribution\. We close with practical guidelinesfor choosing a representation under different data and compute regimes and outline open challenges\.

## [Howard, John: Artificial Versus Natural Intelligence \- The Algorithm Conjecture \(Revision One\)](../publications/95dc13ffa747bb02cd08.md)



This paper investigates the conceptual foundations of intelligence and examines the distinctions between natural and artificial forms of intelligence\. This paper presents an algorithmic model of the mind, and a model of intelligence, and introduces the Algorithm Conjecture\. The Conjecture is used as a framework for analyzing various forms of artificial intelligence and robotics, followed by a discussion of potential methods for enhancing the performance and capabilities of AI systems\. The paper concludes by proposing a significant experimental approach aimed at advancing the empirical study of human consciousness\.

## [Single\-stage joint diffusion of sky images and clear\-sky index for ultra\-short\-term irradiance forecasting: what the frame\-to\-irradiance stage discards](../publications/95dc7b984889fc061096.md)

Kanawut Suwandee; Suwichaya Suwanwimolkul

Sky\-image irradiance forecasting is dominated by a two\-stage design: a video\-prediction model forecasts future sky frames, and a separately trained regressor maps those frames to irradiance\. We propose a single\-stage alternative that co\-denoises the future sky\-image and clear\-sky\-index sequences in one diffusion process, with an irradiance head that reads a denoised preview of the future sky rather than the noised diffusion state\. The forecaster needs no regression stage and runs from sky images and deterministic covariates alone, with no measured irradiance at its input \-\-\- the situation at a site with a camera but no pyranometer\. On 2023 SIRTA data the model reaches a pooled RMSE of $104\.1$\~W\\,m$^\{\-2\}$ and a skill score of $\+0\.34$ on the continuous ranked probability score \(CRPS\) against smart persistence, higher than any of twelve baseline configurations, and retains that skill when retrained on 2021\-\-2022\. On the model&\#x27;s own generated frames, a separately trained regressor reaches $150\.6$\~W\\,m$^\{\-2\}$ against the joint head&\#x27;s $104\.1$: roughly $46$\~W\\,m$^\{\-2\}$ that joint training recovers and a cascade discards\. Point accuracy is competitive but not best: a deterministic network that also reads measured irradiance attains $97\.6$\~W\\,m$^\{\-2\}$\. The model&\#x27;s CRPS skill leads that network&\#x27;s in every sky\-condition tertile, by $0\.26$ to $0\.30$\.

## [ANALISIS KOMPARATIF AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT DAN KINERJA BISNIS CONTENT CREATOR PADA KONTEN BERTEMA CLAUDE AI DAN NON\-CLAUDE AI DI YOUTUBE](../publications/95e0fe3d5e612bdf05f6.md)

224010232 Andini Elya Siswandari; Dr\. Erik Syawal Alghifari, SE\.,MM, Pembimbing

ABSTRAK Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence mendorong semakin beragamnya konten bertema Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) di YouTube, salah satunya konten mengenai Claude AI\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan membandingkan audience engagement serta kinerja bisnis content creator antara konten Claude AI dan Non\-Claude AI di YouTube\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode deskriptif dan komparatif\. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 200 video dari delapan channel YouTube, yaitu 100 video Claude AI dan 100 video Non\-Claude AI yang dipilih menggunakan purposive sampling\. Audience engagement diukur melalui views, likes, dan comments, sedangkan kinerja bisnis content creator diukur melalui estimated earnings\. Data dianalisis menggunakan Mann Whitney U\-test dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara konten Claude AI dan Non\-Claude AI pada indikator views, likes, dan estimated earnings, sedangkan pada indikator comments tidak ditemukan perbedaan yang signifikan\. Secara umum, konten Claude AI menunjukkan performa yang lebih tinggi pada views, likes, dan estimated earnings dibandingkan konten Non\-Claude AI\. Kata Kunci: Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Claude AI, Audience Engagement, Content Creator, Kinerja Bisnis, YouTube\.

## [Spatially Constrained Self\-Organizing Maps for Seismic Facies Analysis](../publications/95ead63cdc03bbbae056.md)

Cun Yang; Xinming Wu; Guozhang Fan; Qingyuan Qi; Yintao Lu; Hongping Wang

Abstract Understanding and characterizing seismic facies is essential for reconstructing depositional settings, identifying stratigraphic boundaries, and supporting reservoir evaluation in both exploration and development contexts\. In this study, we present a spatially constrained self\-organizing map \(SOM\) framework for seismic facies analysis that integrates multi\-attribute information while incorporating local spatial consistency during training\. Unlike conventional SOM approaches that rely solely on attribute similarity, the proposed method introduces a spatial regularization term into the best matching unit \(BMU\) assignment, promoting consistent mapping among neighboring samples while preserving discontinuities associated with structural or stratigraphic boundaries\. The spatial constraint is implemented through a local weighting function that reflects structural continuity; in this implementation, seismic coherence is used as an indicator, although the formulation is not restricted to a specific attribute\. Following SOM training, the attribute manifold is further represented using a geodesic\-based one\-dimensional ordering that captures intrinsic relationships among SOM nodes, providing a continuous representation of facies variability and improving interpretability\. Application to a deep\-water 3D seismic dataset demonstrates that the proposed framework reduces local instability in facies mapping, enhances spatial continuity, and preserves boundary sharpness compared with conventional SOM\-based workflows\.

## [PERSONALIZED DIAGNOSTICS AND TREATMENT OF ACUTE SURGICAL AND UROLOGICAL PATHOLOGY \(BASED ON THE RESULTS OF PLANNED RESEARCH\)](../publications/95f47da3c15f8aeea661.md)

V\. Polovyi; Ruslan I\. Sydorchuk; V\. S\. Zaitsev; O\. Rotar; О\. С\. Федорук; K\. A\. Vladychenko; P\. M\. Volyanyuk; І\. І\. Ілюк; Р\. П\. Кнут; A\. S\. Palianytsia; Петрюк Богдан Васильевич; O\. M\. Plehutsa; S\. I\. Railianu; Yu\.M\. Myshkovskyi; Yurii М\. Solovei

Urgent surgical and urological diseases possess a leading position in the structure of pathologies\. At the same time, the existing healthcare system, which is based on the use of therapeutic approaches that have proven effective in other patients, is insufficiently effective, prompting the development of personalized treatment tactics\. Aim of the work – to summarize the results of the planned scientific research of the Department of General Surgery and Urology for 2022\-2027, scientifically substantiate and improve existing and develop new methods of personalized diagnosis and treatment of acute surgical and urological pathology\. Materials and methods\. The study is combined \(clinical\-experimental, prospective, cohort\)\. The experimental part was conducted on 280 white nonlinear rats using the method of polarization tomography of birefringence of the polycrystalline component of histological sections and blood films during modeling of peritonitis and abdominal sepsis of varying severity\. The clinical block covers 1039 patients: 696 \(66\.99%\) with acute abdominal pathology, 198 \(19\.06%\) with non\-abdominal surgical pathology \(including 123 patients with diabetic foot syndrome – DFS\), 145 \(13\.95%\) patients with acute purulent\-inflammatory diseases of the urinary system\. For analysis and formation of personalized algorithms, methods of variation statistics, special software, and auxiliary artificial intelligence tools were used\. Results\. The polyetiological nature of urinary system lesions was confirmed with dominance of E\. coli and S\. aureus, but the pathogen was not identified in 13\.48% of cases\. In surgical treatment of DFS, the high technical effectiveness of balloon angioplasty \(94\.3%\) was proven and the expansion of individual indications for revascularization was substantiated\. According to polarization tomographic mapping of blood films of experimental animals, a scenario of necrotic destruction of optical anisotropy was revealed corresponding to the severity of peritonitis\. The use of developed personalized approaches to determine the timing and stages of interventions allowed reducing the frequency of postoperative complications by 28\.1% and shortening the length of hospital stay by 14\.08%\. Conclusions\. The conducted scientific research allowed a comprehensive assessment of the main parameters of acute surgical and urological diseases, to develop new and improve existing methods of diagnosis and treatment\. It was shown that acute surgical and urological diseases dominate in the structure of pathologies treated in the clinic of general surgery and urology\. Integration of clinical, laboratory, and instrumental parameters into a single prognostic algorithm using AI tools can be the basis for optimizing treatment\. The obtained data allow asserting that personalized diagnostic and therapeutic approaches have development potential and require active implementation\.

## [Lessons learned from recruitment and implementation of the Perceived Diet Quality Study](../publications/95fe43004f6e7f845281.md)

Tameka I\. Walls; Alicia S\. Landry; Fatemeh Malekian; Gabriela E\. Rodriguez; Jessica Lee Thomson

Background Online surveys offer rapid, cost\-effective, and convenient tools for data collection\. However, online survey research carries risk, particularly for fraudulent behavior\. The objective of this study was to describe lessons learned from implementing an online survey designed to test and validate a comprehensive tool for measuring perceived diet quality\. Methods Participants were recruited via flyers posted at various community organizations\. Recruitment flyers contained a QR code to access the recruitment survey\. The study consisted of two surveys, the Perceived Diet Quality Questionnaire \(PDQ\-Q\) and Diet ID TM , a dietary assessment, tool\. Email reminders were sent to participants who had not completed the surveys within specified time frames\. Chi square tests were used to determine whether participant characteristics differed by reminder status \(no reminder vs\. ≥1 reminder\)\. Results Of the 1,337 recruitment surveys submitted, 962 individuals were enrolled in the study, with 605 \(63%\) and 591 \(61%\) valid and complete PDQ\-Q and Diet ID TM surveys submitted\. Majority reasons for not enrolling 375 individuals in the study included duplicate name, email address or telephone number \(73%\) and suspicious or invalid contact information \(15%\)\. The mean number of reminders sent to participants who completed the PDQ\-Q and the Diet ID TM was 1\.8 \(SD = 0\.9\) and 1\.7 \(SD = 1\.4\)\. For both surveys, the percentage of participants who needed ≥1 reminder increased as age increased \(PDQ\-Q: 21% for 18–29 years vs\. 35% for ≥60 years; Diet ID TM : 10% for 18–29 years vs\. 22% for ≥60 years\)\. Conclusions While QR codes and mobile\-first surveys increase accessibility and reduce participant burden, they also introduce risks to data integrity resulting in the need for verification checks\. Incorporating verification procedures may reduce redundant submissions and improve efficiency\. The observed pattern of diminishing returns after two completion reminders indicates that reminder schedules can be optimized to balance participant engagement\. Participant characteristics associated with the need for reminders suggest that fully digital protocols may disadvantage some groups\. Future research may involve testing recruitment and retention strategies, evaluating cost\-effectiveness of number of email reminders vs\. completion percentage, and examining how tailored engagement influences participation among underrepresented populations\.

## [Artificial intelligence and the rebalanced hemostasis of chronic liver disease: From viscoelastic testing to digital twins](../publications/9609277ca7859abc02c7.md)

Ahmed Salman

Chronic liver disease, particularly cirrhosis, produces a fragile, rebalanced hemostatic state\.Patients may develop bleeding or thrombosis\.The international normalized ratio and platelet count incompletely reflect concurrent procoagulant and anticoagulant changes and poorly predict procedural bleeding\.Viscoelastic testing and thrombingeneration assays assess hemostasis more broadly\.Randomized trials support viscoelastic testing\-guided reductions in blood product use, but these trials do not establish prediction of later bleeding or thrombosis\.Machine\-learning models address gastrointestinal bleeding outcomes, variceal hemorrhage, portal vein thrombosis \(PVT\), and transfusion requirements using clinical records, imaging, or elastography\.Most cirrhosis models address one outcome, omit direct hemostatic measurements, and have limited external validation\.Within the English\-language eligibility criteria and focused queries of a PubMed update on July 29, 2026, no adult model jointly estimating future bleeding and PVT in cirrhosis was identified\.This structured narrative minireview evaluates the evidence for both outcomes and specifies research requirements for paired\-risk models and a possible digital twin of the coagulation\-portal axis\.Treatmentspecific predictions would require additional causal validation\.

## [Non‐invasive diagnosis of endometriosis: From expert imaging to molecular and artificial intelligence‐enabled pathways](../publications/960d2b783fe03610168d.md)

Rana Mondal; Mouli Nandi

Endometriosis affects approximately one in 10 women and people assigned female at birth of reproductive age, yet diagnosis is still delayed by years, historically because confirmation required laparoscopy\. This review synthesizes which non\-invasive tools\-expert ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\), molecular and microRNA \(miRNA\) biomarkers, and artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-are ready for clinical use and which have so far been evaluated only in research settings and proposes a pragmatic clinical pathway\. This is a narrative review and not a systematic review\. Major guidelines now endorse a clinical and imaging\-based diagnosis without mandatory laparoscopy\. Expert transvaginal ultrasound and MRI identify ovarian endometrioma and deep endometriosis with high specificity and map disease for surgery, but a normal scan does not exclude endometriosis because superficial peritoneal endometriosis remains largely invisible\. No blood, urinary, or endometrial biomarker meets criteria for clinical use; circulating miRNA panels have failed independent validation, and a salivary miRNA signature still needs independent, lower\-prevalence validation\. Radiomics and AI remain investigational pending external validation, calibration, and demonstrated clinical utility\. Non\-invasive diagnosis is best framed not as one replacement test but as a multimodal, staged pathway in which each tool is used according to how far its evidence has progressed, which shortens diagnostic delay, targets specialist care, and interprets a negative scan safely\.

## [Using Temporal Convolutional Autoencoders for Sound\-Based Fault Detection in Industrial Machinery](../publications/962bc6bf29a0c2610366.md)

Igor Assunção; Rodrigo de Paula Monteiro; Andrea Maria Nogueira Cavalcanti Ribeiro; Diego Pinheiro

We propose using two deep autoencoder architectures, i\.e\. the Temporal Convolutional Network Autoencoder \(TCN\-AE\) and Wasserstein Autoencoder with Generative Adversarial Network \(WAE\-GAN\), to perform anomaly detection in the industrial context\. In this work, we detect anomalies by introducing a feature engineering pipeline that structures univariate acoustic signals into sequential multivariate representations via Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients \(MFCCs\)\. The trained models were evaluated using 10\-fold cross\-validation, and their performances were assessed through an empirical analysis of hyperparameter sensitivity, mapping prominent structural configurations for each neural architecture\. The optimized TCN\-AE showed superior performance, achieving an average AUC\-ROC of 0\.8716 for pump devices and 0\.7834 for fan devices, thereby surpassing state\-of\-the\-art literature benchmarks, while also demonstrating robust performance for the slider device with an average AUC\-ROC of 0\.9646\. Both architectures presented limitations with the valve device due to its highly transient behavior\. The results achieved confirm the effectiveness of sequential reconstruction\-based models for continuous machine operations while highlighting specific open challenges in acoustic industrial monitoring\.

## [Do Financing and Investment\- Based Courses Influence the Gen\-Z Investment?](../publications/962cfbef4eaae1c833e6.md)

Eneng Nur Hasanah; Sudarso Kaderi Wiryono; Deddy Priatmodjo Koesrindartoto

The number of young investors in Indonesia has grown significantly in recent years, marking a notable shift in the country’s investment landscape\. Although the total assets of younger investors are smaller compared to those of older investors, their increasing participation has positively influenced the development of the investment sector and improved financial literacy among younger generations\. Based on this phenomenon, the purpose of this study is to examine the attitudes of Generation Z as the young investors towards business and management programs, the use of investment applications, and robo\-advisor services\. The research focuses on two distinct groups: students who have had prior exposure to finance and investment\-related courses, and those who have not had such courses\. The method used was structured focus group discussions to explore students’ knowledge and experiences, then supplemented with a survey questionnaire to validate findings and provide deeper insights\. The research concluded that there were no significant differences between the two cohorts regarding their interest in understanding and the importance of investments\. Some participants had already started investing without formal financial education, while others explored unconventional investments such as collectible hobby items\. Moreover, participants generally trusted risk assessments provided by robo\-advisors, but many of them were hesitant to follow the recommendations\. They expressed a greater confidence in their ability to make independent investment decisions\.

## [Factors Influencing the Sustainability of Microenterprise Projects Supported Through Government Assistance Among DSWD\-SLP Beneficiaries](../publications/962f68878a058d64756a.md)

Bevirly Habacon

This study examined the influence of entrepreneurial competencies and marketing strategies on the perceived sustainability of microenterprises among beneficiaries of the Department of Social Welfare and Development – Sustainable Livelihood Program \(DSWD\-SLP\) in Barangay San Jose, Antipolo City, Rizal, Philippines\. Anchored in Human Capital Theory, the Resource\-Based View, and Market Orientation Theory, the study employed an explanatory sequential mixed\-methods design\. Quantitative data were collected through a survey and analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression, while qualitative data were gathered through focus group discussions\. Results revealed very high levels of entrepreneurial competencies \(M = 4\.751\), marketing strategies \(M = 4\.720\), and perceived microenterprise sustainability \(M = 4\.910\)\. Regression analysis indicated that the overall model was statistically significant \(R² = 0\.141, F = 8\.590, p &lt; \.001\)\. Entrepreneurial competencies significantly predicted perceived sustainability \(p = \.004\), whereas marketing strategies did not demonstrate a statistically significant effect \(p = \.089\)\. The model explained 14\.1% of the variance in perceived sustainability, suggesting that other factors also contribute to enterprise continuity\. Qualitative findings highlighted decision\-making, communication, perseverance, adaptability, customer relations, pricing, promotion, and product accessibility as important business practices\. However, beneficiaries faced challenges involving limited capital, competition, fluctuating demand, irregular income, and gaps in technical and digital skills\. The study recommends strengthening capacity\-building initiatives in entrepreneurial and financial management, alongside institutional support and market development interventions, to enhance the sustainability of livelihood\-assisted microenterprises\.

## [Reconfigurable Floating‐Gate van der Waals Phototransistor With Asymmetric Contact Geometries for Bio‐Inspired Multi‐Stage Visual Tasks](../publications/96373a6f879d9b98ec4b.md)

Jun Xie; Shuang Ge; Xiaoning Zhao; Ya Lin; Zhongqiang Wang; Ye Tao; Haiyang Xu; Yichun Liu

ABSTRACT Bio‐inspired optoelectronic devices with in‐sensor neuromorphic computing capability are promising for artificial visual applications\. However, the biological visual system possesses simultaneous sensing and multi‐stage processing capability through the retina and visual cortex\. Different device types and materials are required to emulate specific visual functions, which will unavoidably pose complexity in integration and limit the scalability\. Herein, we report a WSe 2 /h‐BN/Graphene reconfigurable floating‐gate van der Waals phototransistor \(RFGPT\) featuring a laterally asymmetric contact geometry\. The device exhibits reconfigurable optoelectronic functionality via gate voltage modulation, including photodetection mode with bipolar photoresponse and optoelectronic synapse mode with short‐term memory\. The RFGPT fulfills versatile neuromorphic image processing functions, including retina‐level pre‐processing \(edge extraction\) and cortex‐level processing \(image recognition\)\. The RFGPT provides a fundamental unit to develop artificial visual hardware with reduced fabrication complexity and enhanced scalability for efficient in‐sensor computing\.

## [TrajOnco: a multi\-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi\-cancer early detection](../publications/9640f0739e9742a14ded.md)

Sihang Zeng; Young Won Kim; Wilson Lau; Ehsan Alipour; Ruth Etzioni; Meliha Yetisgen; Anand Oka

Abstract Accurate estimation of cancer risk from longitudinal electronic health records \(EHRs\) could support earlier detection and improved care, but modeling such complex patient trajectories remains challenging\. We present TrajOnco, a training\-free, multi\-agent large language model \(LLM\) framework designed for scalable multi\-cancer early detection\. Using a chain\-of\-agents architecture with long\-term memory, TrajOnco performs temporal reasoning over sequential clinical events to generate patient\-level summaries, evidence\-linked rationales, and predicted risk scores\. We evaluated TrajOnco on de\-identified Truveta EHR data across 15 cancer types using matched case\-control cohorts, predicting risk of cancer diagnosis at 1 year\. In zero\-shot evaluation, TrajOnco achieved AUROCs of 0\.64–0\.80, performing comparably to supervised machine learning in a lung cancer benchmark while demonstrating better temporal reasoning than single\-agent LLMs\. The multi\-agent design also enabled effective temporal reasoning with smaller\-capacity models such as GPT\-4\.1\-mini\. The groundedness of TrajOnco’s output was supported by human evaluation\. Furthermore, TrajOnco’s interpretable reasoning outputs can be aggregated to reveal population\-level risk patterns that align with established clinical knowledge\. These findings highlight the potential of multi\-agent LLMs to execute interpretable temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHRs, advancing both scalable multi\-cancer early detection and clinical insight generation\.

## [InRegPep: a web server for modeling of parallel beta\-sheet fibrillar aggregates of amyloidogenic peptides](../publications/9646ceea18f832f18d93.md)

Wojciech Puławski; Szymon Niewieczerzał; Andrzej Koliński; Grzegorz Firlik; Michał Koliński

Predicting the structures of peptide or protein aggregates that assemble into amyloid protofilaments remains one of the most challenging tasks in computational structural biology\. Computational difficulties arise mainly from the large size of the modeled systems and the extensive timescales of aggregation processes\. The InRegPep web server is designed for the multiscale structural modeling of peptide aggregates that preferentially adopt in\-register parallel β\-sheet architectures\. The method employs the coarse\-grained CABS model, which enables the assembly of a large number of aggregates composed of five interacting peptides\. The best models are selected using clustering techniques combined with energy\-based and model\-symmetry criteria\. Top\-scoring models are subsequently refined at the all\-atom level and further assessed using molecular dynamics simulations\. Finally, short protofilament structures are assembled for conformationally stable aggregates\. The performance of the InRegPep server was evaluated using a benchmark dataset comprising 15 experimentally determined protofilament structures\. For 10 of the 15 systems, the best\-performing model among the 10 top\-scoring predictions achieved an RMSD below 5 Å\. The resulting models provide a valuable foundation for subsequent studies, including investigations of conformational polymorphism, mutational design, and downstream experimental or computational validation\.

## [Modes of Engagement with AI\-Generated Feedback: A Case Study of Three Pre\-Service EFL Teachers](../publications/9654d4b3f560cfc90b20.md)

Raigul Zheldibayeva

Generative AI \(GenAI\) feedback tools are increasingly used to support formative writing instruction, yet most research reports feedback effects in aggregate, offering little insight into how individual learners actually engage with AI\-generated feedback\. This exploratory case study examines three pre\-service EFL teachers&\#x27; engagement with feedback from CyberScholar, a rubric\-aligned AI feedback platform, during revision of a short reflective essay on AI in English language education\. Drawing on a larger pilot dataset, three contrasting cases were purposively selected to illustrate distinct modes of engagement: regenerative rewriting, in which the participant produced an almost entirely new text in a markedly more formal register; minimal, selective engagement, in which only a narrowly targeted mechanical issue was addressed while conceptual feedback was left unaddressed; and partial, uneven engagement, in which some rubric criteria were revised while others remained unchanged\. Comparing participants&\#x27; draft\-to\-draft changes, the AI\-generated feedback they received, and the resulting rating changes, the study develops a preliminary typology of engagement modes rather than a claim about writing\-quality improvement\. Findings suggest that the same feedback instrument can prompt qualitatively different revision behaviors depending on how learners interpret and act on it, with implications for how AI feedback tools are designed and how teacher educators might scaffold students&\#x27; critical use of such tools\. The study contributes a fine\-grained, learner\-centered perspective that complements aggregate analyses of AI feedback effectiveness\.

## [BioInteract combines residue\-level cross\-attention with protein\-language and physicochemical priors for interpretable drug–target interaction prediction](../publications/966971570a2470f8a830.md)

Shengnan Wang; Qi Zhang; Xucheng Liu; Zixuan Wang; Jiangke Cheng; Zhi Zhen Huang

Accurate prediction of drug–target interactions \(DTIs\) can support the prioritisation of candidate pairs, yet published models are usually compared through numbers quoted across papers whose protocols differ, and their attribution outputs are rarely accompanied by an explicit statement of where the model may be trusted\. We present BioInteract, a DTI framework combining a chemistry\-aware molecular graph encoder, an ESM\-2/physicochemical protein residue encoder with a configured domain\-label channel, and bidirectional cross\-attention, and we evaluate it inside a matched\-protocol benchmark on the Davis kinase inhibitor dataset in which every model is trained with one shared partition, seed, optimiser, schedule and threshold rule\. The comparison is a three\-model ladder that changes one component at a time, so that adding the frozen ESM\-2 representation and then replacing concatenation with cross\-attention can be read separately\. Both steps help, but by protocol\-dependent amounts: the protein language model adds 0\.120 and 0\.063 AUPRC under the random and Target\-ID\-held\-out protocols, whereas cross\-attention adds 0\.067 and 0\.201 AUPRC under the same two protocols\. A breadth check across two further architecture families places these differences in context: on the random split the five architectures tested fall within a narrow band, so the controlled Target\-ID\-held\-out ladder carries the informative contrast\. We audit chemical and sequence similarity across all partitions, evaluate exact\-sequence\-grouped cold\-start protocols, and report leakage\-aware diagnostic controls\. On a strict exact\-entity\-novel BindingDB cohort, whose construction is documented as a complete row\-level filtering waterfall for both the curated\-articles snapshot and the full BindingDB release, the frozen Davis checkpoint achieved an AUROC of 0\.560 and an AUPRC of 0\.340; an applicability\-domain analysis attributes this limited transfer principally to ligand and target novelty relative to Davis\. The attribution analyses generate hypotheses about model\-relevant atoms and residues, but, in line with evidence from models trained with explicit non\-covalent interaction supervision, unsupervised attention is not treated here as a recovered interaction mechanism\. BioInteract therefore contributes an audited, reproducible and domain\-of\-applicability\-aware DTI reference rather than a new architectural principle\.

## [Load\-Dependent Wiener Degradation Modeling and Life Prediction of Wire\-Driven Minimally Invasive Surgical Instruments](../publications/966a8d20af0ec5792416.md)

Yuan Xing; Tong Niu; Rui Zheng; Yuxuan Zhao; Xiangyun Ren; Han Liu

This paper investigates the fatigue degradation and life prediction of a wire\-driven parallel mechanism for minimally invasive surgical instruments under different external loads\. Fatigue tests are conducted under 0 N, 0\.5 N, and 1 N loads, and the trajectory radius loss of the end\-effector is selected as the degradation indicator\. The results show that the degradation rate increases with load, and ANOVA confirms that the load effect is statistically significant\. A load\-dependent Wiener degradation model is then established to describe the stochastic process\. Compared with the conventional Wiener model, the proposed model shows better fitting performance\. Based on a soft failure threshold and the first\-passage\-time distribution of the Wiener process, reliability, lifetime distribution, and mean remaining life are analytically predicted\. The results indicate that higher loads significantly shorten the service life of the mechanism\. The proposed method provides a basis for reliability evaluation and maintenance decision\-making of wire\-driven minimally invasive surgical instruments\.

## [Datenraumdiplomatie und differentielle Erosion: Wenn Künstliche Intelligenz über Kulturen spricht](../publications/9671d24414b0e03ef060.md)

Stephan U\. Breu

Dieses Konzeptpapier führt die Begriffe Datenraumdiplomatie \(Dataspace Diplomacy\) und differentielle Erosion \(Differential Cultural Erosion\) ein, bestimmt ihren Gegenstand und grenzt sie von benachbarten Konzepten ab\. Es dient der begrifflichen Grundlegung\. Die ausführliche wissenschaftliche Herleitung, die Aufarbeitung des Forschungsstands und die empirische Untersuchung erfolgen in einer späteren Monografie\.This concept paper introduces the terms Dataspace Diplomacy \(Datenraumdiplomatie\) and Differential Cultural Erosion \(differentielle Erosion\), defines their subject matter, and distinguishes them from related concepts\. ## [The Growing Impact of CiteScore as a Bibliometric Indicator: A Global Contextual Analysis of Adoption, Reliability, and Influence on Academic Publishing](../publications/96799a85e872ba22398a.md)

Samaya Pillai

CiteScore became an influential metric in academic publishing when Elsevier introduced it in late 2016\. Coverage of journals within the CiteScore dataset increased by approximately 38% during the same time frame \(from 22,615 in 2017 to 31,138 in 2024 and to 50,040 in 2026\)\. Accordingly, regression analyses used data on yearly increases in the number of journals included in each subsequent year&\#x27;s dataset\. The results indicated a very strong linear correlation \(Pearson r = 0\.9901\) between year and journal coverage with a very high level of explanation for this association \(R² = 0\.9804\)\. Because t\(8\) = 18\.69 is statistically significant \(p &lt; 0\.001\), these findings provide clear evidence supporting hypothesis one \(H1\) and confirm that CiteScore adoption will continue at a consistent pace\. The reliability of CiteScore was assessed in relation to Journal Impact Factors \(JIFs\) and other various disciplinary categories\. Results showed that correlations between CiteScore and JIFs were similar across disciplines\. For example, medical journals had a Spearman ρ = 0\.91, indicating that these two measures of impact were ranked very similarly within this field\. These results provide support for hypothesis two \(H2\) and suggest that CiteScore may serve as a viable alternative to existing measures of impact\. Finally, we also examined trends in open access publishing\. Our results show that both CiteScore and JIF\-tracked journals have similar proportions of open access articles\. However, our examination did not find that either type of journal disproportionately benefits from CiteScore relative to JIF tracking\. Ultimately, our findings emphasize the need for future investigations into CiteScore&\#x27;s effects on journal behavior, author submission patterns, and other aspects of the broader research evaluation ecosystem\.

## [Adaptive Education Platforms for Development of Algorithmic Thinking in Corporate Environment: Criteria for Selection of Experimental Environment](../publications/968121424f6de0a318ca.md)

Tsvetelina Rashkova; Gencho Stoitsov

This article develops a methodological framework for screening and subsequently verifying adaptive learning platforms intended to support algorithmic and critical thinking among adults in corporate settings\. It combines a conceptual analysis of selected literature, document analysis, and multi\-criteria modelling\. Six criteria are operationalized through five\-level descriptors, provisional normative weights, and non\-compensatory thresholds\. Documentation for five platforms is examined to distinguish vendor claims from demonstrated functionality and secured access rights\. A separate numerical example using five hypothetical profiles illustrates weighted aggregation and sensitivity to weights and input assumptions; it is not an empirical ranking of the products\. A schematic corporate case provides separate indicators for algorithmic thinking, critical thinking, and transfer\. The main contribution is a two\-stage procedure linking documentary screening to technical and expert verification\. The framework requires validation\. No intervention study is reported, and no platform\-specific educational effect is established\.

## [Modelos econométricos y estadísticos basados en datos de la SUNAT, el BCRP y el INEI](../publications/968253f34fafbce111e0.md)

Carolina Montes Lizárraga; Raúl Yajahuanca Huancas; Ana Cristhina Blanco Napuri De Martínez; Evelyn Esteffany Ordinola Lama; Edwin Johny Asnate Salazar; Bebeto Juan Pizarro Marcos

Este libro de investigación aborda la necesidad de superar las limitaciones de los agregados macroeconómicos tradicionales y los desfases temporales en el análisis cuantitativo de la economía peruana, caracterizada por su alta informalidad y heterogeneidad estructural\. Con el propósito de desarrollar, estimar y validar un conjunto de modelos econométricos y estadísticos avanzados utilizando microdatos y datos agregados provenientes de la SUNAT, el BCP y el INEI, se empleó una metodología cuantitativa e híbrida que integró microdatos de facturación y cumplimiento fiscal de la SUNAT, métricas de transaccionalidad, liquidez y comportamiento crediticio del BCP, e indicadores oficiales de PBI, inflación y empleo del INEI, procesados mediante modelos econométricos de series de tiempo \(VAR, VEC, ARIMA\), datos de panel y algoritmos de machine learning como XGBoost y Random Forest\. Los resultados evidencian que la facturación electrónica y la transaccionalidad bancaria funcionan como indicadores adelantados \(leading indicators\) altamente efectivos que anteceden entre 30 y 60 días a las cifras oficiales de consumo e inversión del INEI, reduciendo significativamente el error cuadrático medio \(RMSE\) en las estimaciones del PBI trimestral y mejorando la identificación de brechas de informalidad regional\. Se concluye que la articulación analítica de fuentes tributarias, financieras y estadísticas oficiales proporciona una arquitectura predictiva superior y de alta frecuencia, indispensable para fortalecer el diseño de políticas públicas, la gestión del riesgo crediticio y la toma de decisiones estratégicas en los sectores público y privado del Perú\.

## [A Computationally Efficient Radar Sensor Modeling Methodology Incorporating Rain\-Induced Propagation Attenuation for Virtual Validation of Autonomous Driving Systems](../publications/96851f2cde8a6dce6bee.md)

Seunghwan Chung; Chan\-Jung Kim

This paper presents a computationally efficient radar sensor modeling methodology incorporating rain\-induced propagation attenuation for simulation\-based validation of autonomous driving systems\. The proposed framework combines the classical radar equation with the rain attenuation model specified in ITU\-R Recommenda\-tion P\.838\-3 to estimate received signal power degradation and target\-range estimation errors under rainfall conditions\. A stochastic False Alarm Probability Generation \(FAPG\) algorithm is also introduced to reproduce intermittent tar\-get detection according to user\-defined probabilities of false alarm and detection\. The proposed methodology was implemented through real\-time co\-simulation between MATLAB/Simulink and IPG CarMaker\. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed framework successfully reproduced rain\-induced propagation attenuation, target\-range estimation errors, received signal power degradation, and stochastic target detection behavior while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for real\-time simulation\.

## [Data analytics and AI in ESG, climate change and sustainability: A practitioner&\#x27;s handbook](../publications/968c32799cd62be2a96b.md)

Harry Patria; Yudhy Muhammad Riandhy Anindika; Zulkifli Muhammad

This handbook began as a course module and grew into something more urgent\.When the Task Force on Climate\-related Financial Disclosures published its recommendations in 2017, thesustainability community gained a shared vocabulary for risk\. When the Corporate SustainabilityReporting Directive came into force in Europe and the International Sustainability Standards Board issuedits inaugural disclosure standards in 2023, that vocabulary became mandatory for tens of thousands oforganisations\. And when the UN Climate Change Conferences from Paris to Dubai produced nationallydetermined contributions that required hard measurement, the gap between ambition and evidence becamethe defining professional challenge of our time\.That challenge is a data challenge\. Organisations that cannot measure their emissions cannot crediblycommit to reducing them\. Investment portfolios that cannot quantify biodiversity exposure cannot claim tomanage it\. Governments that cannot track deforestation in near\-real time cannot enforce the policies theyhave signed\. The missing link between ambition and accountability is analytics, and increasingly it isartificial intelligence\.This handbook is written for the practitioners who occupy that gap: the analyst pricing carbon risk into acredit model, the sustainability manager selecting a reporting framework, the data engineer building thepipeline that feeds the board dashboard, and the senior leader deciding how much of the analytical frontiertheir organisation should reach for\. It assumes numeracy but not specialist training in any single domain\. Itdraws on three currents simultaneously: sustainability science, data analytics and artificial intelligence\.The handbook is organised around a four\-layer framework\. The first layer is Data: the infrastructure,open\-source tools and measurement conventions that make everything else possible\. The second layer isAnalytics: the ESG metrics, decision frameworks and geospatial methods that transform rawmeasurements into insight\. The third layer is AI: the machine learning, natural language processing andforecasting methods that amplify analytical reach\. The fourth layer is Impact: the reporting standards, SDGinvestment frameworks and organisational capabilities that turn insight into durable institutional change\.Each chapter opens with a single Core Proposition stated before any story, follows a deductive argumentthrough theory and worked example, and closes with reflective exercises that require the reader to applythe chapter&\#x27;s ideas to their own context\. The Clinical Vignettes are composites; the Field Narratives usereal, documented cases with full attribution\. Every cited work appears in the reference list\.A note on the open\-source tools\. The GitHub repositories featured in Part I and Part II are real, maintainedand freely usable\. The authors have no commercial relationship with any of them\. They are featuredbecause practitioners should know they exist, what they do reliably, and where they sit in the broaderanalytical stack\.A note on the I\-ESG framework\. This handbook integrates the Integrated ESG \(I\-ESG\) philosophydeveloped by two of the present authors through years of practice in high\-hazard industries\. I\-ESGrecognises that Governance is not a third pillar alongside Environment and Social, but the closed\-loopcontrol system that anchors Process Safety Management, Asset Integrity Management and OperationaliiExcellence to ESG outcomes\. Practitioners from the oil and gas, mining and heavy manufacturing sectorswill find this framing directly applicable to their operating reality\.The authors are grateful to the sustainability practitioners, engineers and data scientists across multiplesectors and jurisdictions whose questions shaped these chapters, and to the researchers whose workprovides the evidential foundation for every claim made here\. We are equally grateful to our institutionalhomes—PT Artificial Intelligent Indonesia and Convergeni by Patria &amp; Co\.—for the intellectual freedomand practical challenge that made this handbook possible\.Harry Patria, Riandhy, and Zulkifli Jakarta, October 2026

## [Testing minimally invasive imaging methods for phenotypic sex determination in immature frogs](../publications/9698b3281368e585bc50.md)

Nikolett Ujhegyi; Veronika Bókony; Árisz Ziszisz; Noémi Kovács; Ildikó Horváth; Maya Zsófia Rozsnyik; Richárd Limboczki; Ákos Benedek Lini; Gábor Berkei; Edina Nemesházi; Andrea Kásler; Zsanett Mikó; Domokos Máthé; Krisztián Szigeti; Emese Balogh

Amphibians are regularly encountered in exotic veterinary practice, and knowledge of their sex can be extremely important for various programs for breeding and species conservation, as well as for veterinary care\. However, sex identification remains challenging because many amphibians lack secondary sexual characteristics until reaching maturity, and genetic sex may not always correspond to phenotypic sex\. Consequently, visual inspection of the gonads is often the most reliable method for identifying sex in amphibians\. However, non\-invasive imaging methods for gonad examination have not been formally validated in juvenile amphibians, where the small size of the gonads may limit visualization success\. In our study, we attempted to determine the phenotypic sex of small\-sized, immature and mature agile frogs \( Rana dalmatina \) using three non\-invasive imaging methods: general veterinary ultrasound, native computed tomography \(CT\), and magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\)\. Ovaries in immature females were not unambiguously recognizable with any of the tested methods, but became clearly visible during oocyte development, enabling identification in mature females with MRI and ultrasonography\. Testes were identifiable in both immature and mature males by MRI but not by ultrasonography or CT\. Weighing the costs and benefits of each method in light of our results, we make recommendations for further research into non\-invasive sexing of juvenile amphibians\.

## [Tendências de Uso e Cobertura do Solo e seu Impacto no Escoamento Superficial em uma Microbacia no Semiárido de Pernambuco](../publications/969ab9a43339d560026c.md)

Fabricio David Simplicio Aniceto; Diêgo Cézar dos Santos Araújo; Jaime Joaquim da Silva Pereira Cabral

As modificações no uso e cobertura do solo, impulsionadas pela expansão urbana desordenada, têm provocado alterações no ciclo hidrológico das bacias hidrográficas\. Diante disso, este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as mudanças no uso e cobertura do solo e avaliar seus impactos no escoamento superficial na microbacia do riacho Salgado, em Caruaru – PE, entre 1988 e 2025\. Para tanto, foram utilizadas imagens dos satélites Landsat, classificadas por meio da Análise de Imagens Baseadas em Objetos \(OBIA\), e o aplicou\-se o método Natural Resource Conservation Service – Curve Number \(NRCS\-CN\) para estimar o escoamento\. Os resultados indicaram aumento de 39,5% na área urbanizada, com consequente redução nas formações campestres e savânicas\. Essa substituição elevou os valores de CN, refletindo a intensificação da impermeabilização do solo e do escoamento superficial\. A classe de escoamento “muito alto” aumentou 39,1% no período analisado, evidenciando maior suscetibilidade aos alagamentos\. Portanto, os dados obtidos reforçam a influência da expansão urbana na intensificação do escoamento superficial, destacando a necessidade de estratégias voltadas à mitigação de riscos hidrológicos na região\.

## [Performance Pressure Effect on Knowledge Hiding: A Perspective of Chinese Education Culture](../publications/96a474b8e8215fcb8ff8.md)

Yanhong Tan; Shengxiang She; Pharatt Run

Knowledge sharing is a critical aspect of information and communication interactions and significantly influences teacher performance\. In the context of Chinese academia, cultural values such as collectivism, respect for hierarchy, and social harmony shape knowledge sharing among teachers\. This study investigates how performance pressure affects teacher knowledge hiding, with a psychological contract breach as a mediator and teacher psychological resilience as a moderator\. Four hundred twenty university teachers across 14 cities in Guangxi, China, a region known for its ethnic diversity and rapid educational development, filled out the questionnaire\. Structural equation modeling \(SEM\) was used to examine the proposed research hypotheses\. The results show that performance pressure significantly increases psychological contract breach and knowledge hiding\. Additionally, psychological contract breach partially mediates the relationship between performance pressure and knowledge hiding\. Psychological resilience moderates the effects of teachers&\#x27; performance pressure on psychological resilience and knowledge hiding\. These results confirm that teachers&\#x27; performance pressure from school management is critical to both psychological well\-being and knowledge exchange behavior\. In the Chinese cultural context, values such as group cohesion help facilitate knowledge sharing among teachers and reduce the tendency toward knowledge hiding\.

## [Transformer\-based architectures for anomaly detection in solar\-wind integrated energy infrastructures](../publications/96aeb3b1c06cb7fa29ab.md)

Ritika Asati; Vikas Khare

The growing incorporation of variable solar and wind power in electrical grids leads to serious issues concerning reliability due to the complexity of spatial and temporal behavior caused by factors like variations in environmental conditions, degradation of equipment, failures of sensors, and exceptional operating conditions\. Therefore, we develop an innovative transformer\-based deep\-learning approach for anomaly detection in integrated solar\-wind energy systems using real\-life multivariate time series datasets from a renewable energy facility situated in Kayathar, Tamil Nadu, India\. The framework proposed in this paper consists of data preparation and normalization, sliding window conducted as a set of sequences, anomaly data creation based on domain knowledge, transformer encoder enhanced with multi\-head self\-attention technology and the attention mechanism\-based data interpretation\. The effectiveness of the framework is compared with LSTM, GRU and CNN\-LSTM using MSE, accuracy and ROC\-AUC\. The obtained results indicate the sufficient performance of the transformer model with the lowest MSE value of 0\.00641 in comparison to 0\.00831, 0\.00859 and 0\.00792 achieved for LSTM, GRU and CNN\-LSTM respectively\. The transformer model has also achieved the value of accuracy equal to 95% together with ROC\-AUC of 0\.89\. However, at the default classification threshold, this accuracy was driven almost entirely by the majority \(normal\) class, and the model failed to identify any of the 10 labelled anomalies in the confusion\-matrix evaluation \(recall = 0% for the anomaly class\), reflecting a severe 18\.8:1 class imbalance in the test set\. The correlation and attention analysis performed in the study shows that the model is capable of revealing significant interdependence among various environmental parameters and renewable power generation rates such as solar radiation and solar energy production \( r = 0\.84\) and wind speed and wind energy production \( r = 0\.90\)\.

## [Evaluation of Two Combined Analytical Approaches to Assess the Impact of Rare Variants on Severe COVID\-19](../publications/96af006fb80f07e1d6b8.md)

Francesca Rosamilia; Giada Recchi; Davide Cangelosi; Sergio Decherchi; Francesca Lantieri; Stefania Croci; Carlo Salvarani; Andrea Cavalli; Marta Rusmini; Isabella Ceccherini; Paolo Uva

Severe COVID\-19 displays substantial inter\-individual variability that cannot be fully explained by common genetic variants, suggesting a contribution of rare functional variation\. We performed whole\-genome sequencing in 191 Italian patients \(96 moderate, 95 severe\) to investigate rare coding variants \(minor allele frequency &lt;1% and &lt;5%\) via complementary network\-based and machine learning approaches\. Classical single\-variant and burden tests did not identify significant associations after multiple testing correction\. However, Network\-based Heterogeneity Clustering \(NHC\) revealed that multiple gene clusters were enriched in severe cases, particularly those involving RNA polymerase II–mediated transcription, RNA metabolism, and vesicle\-mediated transport pathways\. Gene\-level rare variant analysis via the variable threshold method identified five genes significantly associated with severe disease \(FDR &lt; 0\.05\), namely, EIF4G3, GTF2F2, LY96, COX6A1, and STK11, which are involved in transcriptional and translational regulation, innate immune signaling, and mitochondrial function\. Unsupervised biclustering significantly stratified patients by severity, and a decision tree model highlighted the burden of DOCK10 variants as a key discriminator between phenotypes\. Convergence between the network\-based and machine learning results further supported the robustness of the identified signals\. Overall, our integrative framework underscores the contribution of rare variants to COVID\-19 severity and highlights the coordinated perturbation of interconnected molecular pathways as a determinant of clinical outcome\.

## [Grafik Tasarımın Genişleyen Ekosistemi: Uluslararası Tasarım Platformlarının Hesaplamalı İçerik Analizi \(2020–2026\)](../publications/96afa682497eb33974c1.md)

Onur Aşkın

Grafik tasarım uzun yıllar afiş, logo, kitap ve ambalaj gibi nesne merkezli görsel ürünler üzerinden tanımlanmış; ancak 2020–2026 döneminde disiplinin sınırlarını yeniden şekillendiren önemli bir dönüşüm yaşanmıştır\. Bu çalışma, söz konusu dönüşümü ortaya koymak amacıyla uluslararası tasarım medyası, araç geliştiricilerinin blogları, marka yayınları, kullanıcı deneyimi \(UX\) platformları ve yapay zekâ laboratuvarları dâhil olmak üzere 66 kaynaktan derlenen 4\.396 editoryal içeriği çok etiketli tematik kodlama, zamansal eğilim analizi, eş\-görünüm analizi ve kaynak ekolojisi yaklaşımıyla incelemektedir\. Bulgular, üretken yapay zekânın 2022 sonrasında grafik tasarım söyleminde belirgin bir kırılma yarattığını ve marka kimliği, kullanıcı deneyimi \(UX\), hareketli grafik, tasarım sistemleri, tipografi, eğitim ve iş akışı gibi alanları birbirine bağlayan yeni bir tasarım ekosistemi oluşturduğunu göstermektedir\. Aynı dönemde kaynak ağı da önemli ölçüde genişlemiş; 2020&\#x27;de yedi kaynaktan oluşan yapı, 2026&\#x27;da kırk beş kaynağa ulaşmıştır\. Bununla birlikte, yapay zekâ söyleminin coğrafi ve kurumsal dağılımı dengeli değildir; dönüşüme ağırlıklı olarak ABD merkezli şirketler ve araştırma laboratuvarları yön vermektedir\. Ek analizler, 2026 yılında yayın sayısı artmasına rağmen yapay zekâ odaklı içeriklerin oransal olarak azaldığını göstermektedir\. Bu durum, yapay zekânın olağanüstü bir yenilik olmaktan çıkarak grafik tasarım pratiğinin yerleşik bir bileşeni hâline geldiğine işaret etmektedir\. Sonuç olarak çalışma, hesaplamalı içerik analizinin grafik tasarım disiplinindeki güncel dönüşümleri geniş ölçekli veri üzerinden incelemek için güvenilir ve ölçeklenebilir bir araştırma yaklaşımı sunduğunu ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Combining Generative Drawing and Explaining Activities for Chemistry Learning: Exploring the Role of Prior Knowledge](../publications/96b6b78638913576c920.md)

Runzhi Chen; Jennifer G\. Cromley

Abstract Generative strategies such as drawing, self\-explaining, and explaining to others promote active learning, but evidence on their combined effects is mixed, and the role of prior knowledge remains unclear\. The authors investigated the effects of drawing, self\-explaining, and explaining to others, alone and in combination, in a multiple representation domain, chemistry\. A total of 134 undergraduate students who had completed introductory chemistry were randomly assigned to one of six conditions using a 2 \(drawing/no drawing\) x 3 \(self\-explaining, explaining to others, no explaining\) experimental design\. Participants completed a pretest, studied learning materials while applying their assigned strategies, revised their products against instructor\-provided examples, and then completed a posttest\. Results showed no significant main effects of drawing or explaining\. However, prior knowledge moderated the impact of conditions on the posttest: drawing benefitted students with moderate prior knowledge, while combining drawing with explaining to others was particularly effective for students with lower prior knowledge\. These findings highlight boundary conditions for dual generative strategies and underscore the importance of aligning strategy use with learner characteristics\.

## [Case Report: Ankle fracture caused by anterior\-posterior horizontal force: a report of two cases](../publications/96b9c50506fc546e10bf.md)

Bang Dou; Jiaxun Zhao; Wenqian Ma; Junshuai Lu; Jiong Mei

Background Ankle fractures caused by violence in the anterior\-posterior horizontal direction are very rare in clinical practice\. Few literatures report on the characteristics and mechanisms of this type of fracture, which should be studied to guide clinical treatment\. Case presentation We presented two cases of ankle fractures caused by horizontal violence in the anterior\-posterior direction, and these fractures presented a distinctive morphological pattern\. After injury, the affected limbs showed significant swelling, and case 2 had developed osteofascial compartment syndrome, and immediate reduction and incision decompression had been performed\. After the soft tissue swelling subsided, an open reduction and internal fixation surgery was performed\. We fixed the tibial fractures first and then the fibular fractures, and fixed tibial fractures in anterior and medial biplane, which achieved good clinical efficacy\. Conclusion Ankle joint fracture caused by horizontal force in the anterior\-posterior direction may be a flexion/extension injury, which is rare and unstable and needs further research on the mechanism of injury\. This type of ankle fracture may be accompanied by osteofascial compartment syndrome, which needs careful examination and timely treatment\.

## [Maize Inositol Polyphosphate 5‐phosphatase Gene Family Analysis Reveals Zm5PTase25 as a Negative Regulator of Low Phosphate‐Induced Leaf Senescence](../publications/96c00c8630bed5381ce5.md)

Huijuan Li; Yini Wang; Yu Lu; Zhubing Hu; Juanjuan Feng; Guoyong An

ABSTRACT Phosphate \(Pi\) deficiency promotes premature leaf senescence in plants through complex molecular networks; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood\. Inositol polyphosphate 5‐phosphatases \(5PTases\) are key regulators of inositol phosphate metabolism, but the maize \( Zea mays L\.\) 5PTase gene family and its roles in low Pi \(LP\)‐induced leaf senescence have not been systematically investigated\. Here, we identified 31 members of the Zm5PTase family in the maize genome\. Phylogenetic and structural analyses revealed marked divergence among clades\. Among these genes, Zm5PTase25 was preferentially expressed in senescing leaves and significantly downregulated under LP stress\. Functional analyses indicated that Zm5PTase25 negatively regulates LP‐induced leaf senescence\. Silencing Zm5PTase25 accelerated leaf senescence, promoted anthocyanin accumulation, altered Pi distribution between old and young leaves in a manner consistent with enhanced Pi remobilisation, and upregulated senescence‐ and ribonuclease‐associated genes and repressed photosynthesis‐related genes\. Conversely, overexpression of Zm5PTase25 delayed leaf senescence\. In vitro assays showed that Zm5PTase25 bound and hydrolysed soluble InsP 3 and InsP 4 \. The PHR1‐like transcription factor ZmPHL6 was identified as a potential upstream transcriptional repressor of Zm5PTase25 \. Moreover, silencing ZmPHL6 produced phenotypes opposite to those of Zm5PTase25 ‐silenced plants\. Collectively, our findings suggest that the ZmPHL6 ‐ Zm5PTase25 regulatory module may modulate LP‐induced leaf senescence, potentially by influencing source to sink Pi remobilisation, providing insights into molecular mechanisms coordinating leaf senescence with maize adaptation to Pi starvation\.
