## [Comparative quality, readability, and factual reliability of four publicly accessible chatbot systems for heart failure patient education: a cross\-sectional evaluation](../publications/96e0d149368dbc120a7e.md)

Nana Qin; Xinran Shao; Jing Wang; Jing Lei; Ran Wen; Wenjun Wu; Fangxu Liu; Hongwei Wang; Yan Zhu

Background Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used for health information delivery, but comparative evidence on their quality, readability, and factual reliability in heart failure \(HF\) education remains limited\. Objective To compare four publicly accessible chatbot systems under prespecified access and retrieval configurations in answering common heart failure–related questions\. Methods We evaluated 108 standardized English HF questions, yielding 432 responses\. Content quality was assessed using modified DISCERN \(mDISCERN\) and Ensuring Quality Information for Patients \(EQIP\), readability was assessed using established English\-language readability indices, including the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook \(SMOG\), Flesch Reading Ease Score \(FRES\), Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level \(FKGL\), Automated Readability Index \(ARI\), Gunning Fog Index \(GFOG\), and Coleman\-Liau Index \(CLI\), and factual reliability was evaluated by auditing all responses against the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline and relevant clinical evidence\. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed\-effects models\. Hallucination outcomes were defined as clinically meaningful statements that were inconsistent with guidelines, unsupported by evidence, overgeneralized beyond the relevant population, or potentially misleading for patient education, and were analyzed using Wilson 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\), Cochran’s Q test, and generalized estimating equation \(GEE\) logistic regression\. Results DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content\-quality profile across the evaluated domains\. In the primary readability analysis, Perplexity generated the most complex text, whereas sensitivity analysis using a second calculator showed partially different rankings\. Hallucinations were identified in 6/108 \(5\.56%\) DeepSeek responses, 8/108 \(7\.41%\) ChatGPT responses, 10/108 \(9\.26%\) Copilot responses, and 16/108 \(14\.81%\) Perplexity responses\. Paired binary analyses showed significant differences among chatbot systems \(Cochran’s Q p = 0\.002; GEE p = 0\.006\)\. Conclusion Under the tested conditions and evaluated model versions, DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content\-quality profile and the lowest observed hallucination rate\. However, hallucinations occurred across all systems, and pairwise factual\-reliability differences were mainly driven by the higher hallucination rate of Perplexity\. Guideline\-aligned verification and clinician oversight remain necessary before patient\-facing use\.

## [Evaluation of infertility associated with diet &amp; lifestyle in current scenario: A multicentre observational case study](../publications/96e55349b06f1208ca32.md)



BackgroundInfertility is a major global public health concern affecting approximately one in six individuals during their reproductive lifetime\.Increasing evidence suggests that modifiable dietary and lifestyle factors, including obesity, poor dietary quality, physical inactivity, psychological stress, inadequate sleep, smoking, and high consumption of ultra\-processed foods \(UPFs\), adversely influence reproductive health\.However, data describing the prevalence of these risk factors among infertile patients in routine Indian clinical practice remain limited\.Objective To evaluate the dietary and lifestyle characteristics of infertile patients attending infertility clinics and describe the prevalence of modifiable nutritional and lifestyle factors associated with reproductive health\.Methods A multicentre observational study was conducted between January and June 2026 among 60 infertile participants \(30 males and 30 females\) attending infertility clinics in the Malegaon region of Maharashtra, India\.Demographic, anthropometric, dietary, lifestyle, and clinical data were collected using a structured Case Record Form and analysed using descriptive statistics\. ResultsThe mean age of participants was 28\.48 ± 4\.62 years and the mean body mass index was 27\.01 ± 3\.04 kg/m²\.Overweight and obesity were observed in 51\.7% and 20\.0% of participants, respectively, while 60\.0% had primary infertility\.Moderate\-to\-high psychological stress was reported by 95\.0% of participants, 56\.7% slept ≤6 hours/day, and 81\.7% exhibited poor lifestyle quality\.Poor dietary quality, inadequate micronutrient intake, and high UPF consumption were identified in 68\.3%, 76\.7%, and 66\.7% of participants, respectively\.Oligoasthenozoospermia was the most common male infertility diagnosis, whereas polycystic ovarian disease \(PCOD\) predominated among female participants\.Conclusion Infertile patients exhibited a high prevalence of modifiable dietary and lifestyle risk factors, including excess body weight, poor dietary quality, inadequate micronutrient intake, high UPF consumption, psychological stress, insufficient sleep, smoking, and unhealthy lifestyle practices\.These findings support integrating routine nutritional assessment and structured lifestyle counselling into infertility care\.Larger prospective multicentre studies are warranted to clarify the relationship between modifiable lifestyle factors and reproductive outcomes\.

## [Event\-Triggered Dynamic Urbanisation and Urban Land Expansion: A Case Study of Bangalore, India](../publications/96eb759995aac2d9a4b0.md)

Rahisha Thottolil; Uttam Kumar; Aurobindo Ogra

Since the 1990s, Bangalore has undergone rapid urbanisation, largely driven by the growth of IT parks, attracting multinational corporations and a significant population influx\. The development of transportation infrastructure, including new roads, transit systems and international airports, along with the construction of malls and other developments, further fuelled the urban growth\. Despite this expansion, the quantitative analysis of event\-triggered urban land area expansion remains under\-explored\. This study systematically assesses the impacts of specific physical events on urban land and surrounding regions\. We employed spatiotemporal land use classification and computed landscape metrics at a grid level to analyze how significant events contribute to urban area expansion\. Based on 24 land use maps from 2000 to 2023, analysis reveals rapid urban expansion in the core city, with significant decreases in vegetation and other land use classes over the last two decades\. Notably, events such as the construction of an airport and shopping malls led to dramatic changes in urban land use\. For instance, North Bangalore, predominantly paddy fields, shrubs and water bodies in 2000, became largely urbanized by 2015\. These findings highlight the impact of event\-triggered urban expansion and land fragmentation and offer valuable insights for urban planning and sustainable development\.

## [Career Adaptability and Employment Anxiety among Vocational College Students: The Mediating Role of Resilience](../publications/96f0bc4c99db98ed1321.md)

## [AI\-StuntDetect: Development of Early Stunting Detection System for Young Children Based on CNN and MediaPipe Pose](../publications/96f3602d88810d045bb6.md)

Asmaul Husna RS; Purnamawati Purnamawati; Hendra Jaya; Anas Arfandi

Stunting remains one of Indonesia&\#x27;s most persistent public health problems\. Yet, growth monitoring at community health posts \(posyandu\) still relies on manual anthropometric measurements, which are time\-consuming, operator\-dependent, and prone to recording errors\. This study aims to develop and evaluate a low\-cost, image\-based system to estimate toddlers&\#x27; height and weight from a single photograph, enabling earlier stunting screening at the community level\. Its main contribution lies not only in the system itself but in the evaluation approach\. Instead of reporting error metrics in isolation, both models are benchmarked against a mean\-value baseline, exposing a misleading interpretation that commonly arises when absolute error metrics are compared across variables with different units and ranges\. The system combines a Convolutional Neural Network with MediaPipe Pose landmark detection, and was tested on 13 toddlers by comparing predicted values against manual measurements using MAE, MSE, and RMSE\. The height model achieved an MAE of 4\.886 cm, MSE of 37\.839 cm², and RMSE of 6\.151 cm, outperforming the baseline by 63\.9%, 82\.6%, and 58\.3%, respectively\. The weight model recorded a seemingly smaller MAE of 2\.630 kg, MSE of 9\.693 kg², and RMSE of 3\.113 kg, yet improved on the baseline by only 0\.6% in MAE and performed worse in MSE and RMSE, indicating that the low error reflects the narrow weight range of the test sample \(6\.60–14\.50 kg\) rather than genuine predictive capability\. Average processing time was 1\.185 seconds per sample\. These findings show that a single 2D image is sufficient for estimating height, a linear measure, but inadequate for weight, which depends on body volume and depth information\. The system is therefore recommended for preliminary height screening, while weight measurement still requires conventional scales until multi\-angle or depth\-based imaging is incorporated\.

## [Diagnóstico tecnológico y estrategias de transformación digital en una empresa pública municipal de servicios básicos](../publications/96f5e5184c2c25ae5dcb.md)

Cristian G\. Zambrano\-Vega; Oscar Fabián Moncayo Carreño; Byron Oviedo; Betty Briones Gavilanez

La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo realizar un diagnóstico tecnológico y formular estrategias de transformación digital para optimizar los procesos administra\-tivos de una empresa pública municipal de servicios básicos\. Se empleó un enfoque mixto, mediante observación directa, entrevista semiestructurada al responsable del área tecnológica y una encuesta aplicada a una muestra de 380 usuarios de una po\-blación de 31\.147 registrados\. Los resultados evidenciaron limitaciones en la infraes\-tructura tecnológica, obsolescencia de equipos informáticos, automatización parcial de los procesos administrativos y deficiencias en los mecanismos de atención ciudadana\. Asimismo, se identificaron necesidades relacionadas con la integración de sistemas de información, capacitación del personal y ampliación de los servicios digitales\. A par\-tir del diagnóstico, se formularon estrategias orientadas a implementar sistemas de gestión de solicitudes, plataformas de autoservicio, aplicaciones móviles, asistentes virtuales y facturación electrónica\. Se concluye que la transformación digital constitu\-ye una alternativa para fortalecer la eficiencia administrativa y mejorar la calidad de los servicios públicos, aunque su implementación requiere planificación tecnológica, desarrollo de competencias digitales y mecanismos de evaluación continua\.

## [Inseparability in Disaster Risk Science: Accounting for Coupled, Co‐Evolving Systems](../publications/96f6545625c4646de34c.md)

Alexandre Dunant; Stefan Hochrainer‐Stigler; Liz Jessica Olaya Calderon; Ryan Michael McGranaghan; Reinhard Mechler; Massimiliano Pittore; Sara Madureira Constantino; Silvia De Angeli; Marleen de Ruiter; G\. Falmagne; Juan Camilo Gómez Zapata; Stefan Kienberger; Elco Koks; Elisabeth Krueger; Shahar Livne \(24376108\); Dora Elia Ramos Muñoz; Robert Šakić Trogrlić; Pia‐Johanna Schweizer; Thi Thu Ha Vo; Haorui Wu; Anqi Zhu

Contemporary risk landscapes are shaped by systemic phenomena\-compound disasters, cascading failures, non\-stationarity, and cross\-domain crises\-that challenge conventional frameworks\. While the classical risk equation \(Risk = Hazard × Vulnerability × Exposure\) remains a useful heuristic, it relies on a separability assumption that breaks down in feedback\-rich, co\-evolving systems\. This failure reflects a familiar diagnosis: risk can be mistaken for a complicated problem, decomposable and optimizable, when it is a complex one, characterized by emergence and adaptation\. Our contribution herein is not this distinction but its analytical consequence\. Drawing on an interdisciplinary workshop on systemic risk and resilience, we propose inseparability as a foundational premise for disaster risk science\. Hazard, exposure, and vulnerability might be better understood as dynamically coupled processes rather than separable variables\. We derive implications across four axes: reframing vulnerability as a non\-ergodic system property; addressing cross\-scale dynamics; shifting from risk control to adaptive management; and treating knowledge co\-production as a scientific necessity\.

## [Hierarchically Engineered MXene/CMC‐Na Composites with Acetaminophen Modification for Self‐Powered Humidity Sensing](../publications/9706b5a25021c27ba215.md)

Yang‐Sheng Wang; Yang‐Sheng Wang; Jin‐Xia Jiang; Di‐Wen Jiang; X Xu; Hao‐Wen Zhang; Hao Chen; Ying Zhi; Li Wang; Zhe‐sheng Feng; Yan Wang; Yan Wang

Humidity sensors have demonstrated significant potential for applications in wearable electronics, physiological monitoring, and environmental sensing\. However, the practical implementation of humidity sensors is often limited by reliance on external power sources, making the development of self\-powered humidity sensing systems a considerable challenge\. This work presents a hierarchical multi\-step modification strategy to fabricate an acetaminophen \(AP\)\-modified hydroxylated MXene/carboxymethylcellulose sodium \(CMC\-Na\) hybrid gel ink \(AHMC\) with integrated humidity sensing and self\-powered functionality\. Theoretical calculations reveal that AHMC exhibits exceptional water adsorption capacity, characterized by a lower adsorption energy \(\-0\.42 eV\) and a shorter adsorption distance \(1\.69 Å\) compared to MXene\. The screen\-printed paper\-based AHMC humidity sensor \(PB\-AHMC\) demonstrates a rapid capacitive response \(4\.8/0\.6 s\) and remarkable response \(73524%\) with excellent bending stability and environmental durability\. Furthermore, the PB\-AHMC\-based humidity sensor array \(PCSA\) accurately identifies various subtle respiratory abnormalities with the incorporation of machine learning algorithms\. Significantly, a self\-powered sensor \(SP\-AHMC\) driven by redox reactions has been developed, achieving a broad detection range \(11%\-97% RH\), exhibiting minimal hysteresis \(1\.0% RH\), and delivering a peak output voltage of 0\.43 V at 97% RH\. Collectively, the AHMC\-based sensors demonstrate substantial potential for advancing applications in healthcare monitoring, non\-contact humidity detection, and self\-powered systems\.

## [Comparison of Wobble Board and Trampoline Training as an Adjunct on Proprioception, Kinesiophobia and Risk of Fall in Patients with Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomised Clinical Trial Protocol](../publications/970a8f6e4f3d8fde3b58.md)

Prachi D Pandey; Amita S\. Aggarwal

Introduction: Knee Osteoarthritis \(KOA\) is chronic degenerative, age\-related disorder leading to physical decline, balance and gait disturbance along with deformities\. Patients with KOA exhibit impaired joint position sense, fear of movement, poor proprioception and elevated fall risk which contributes to poor postural control, increased sway and higher risk of fall\. Need of the study: Proprioception training using unstable surface is essential component of rehabilitation\. Wobble board training is commonly used to improve balance and neuromuscular control, whereas trampoline training provides a dynamic, multidirectional challenge which might provide more better functional demand\. However, evidence comparing these two modalities as an adjunct in KOA is limited\. Aim: To compare the effect of wobble board and trampoline training as an adjunct to conventional therapy on proprioception, kinesiophobia and risk of fall in patients with KOA\. Materials and Methods: The present Randomised Clinical Trial \(RCT\) will be conducted in MM Super Specialty Hospital, Mullana, Ambala, Haryana, India, from March 2026 to March 2027\. A total of 36 patients with bilateral KOA of grade 2 and 3 \(Kellgren\-Lawrence grade\) will be recruited based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria\. Group A will receive wobble board training with conventional therapy, and Group B will receive trampoline training with conventional therapy for three sessions per week for four weeks\. Primary outcome measures include knee joint proprioception, Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia, Fall Efficacy Scale\-International \(FES\-I\)and secondary outcome includes Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score \(KOOS\) and Numeric Rating Scale \(NRS\)\. A paired t\-test will be performed for within group comparison for normally distributed using Independent t\-test and Wilcoxon Signed\-Rank Test for not normally distributed data\.

## [Prophylactic pirfenidone to prevent radiation\- induced lung injury in ICI\-pretreated lung cancer patients: a phase II study](../publications/970e42644a4dc34a541c.md)

Yujie Huang; Jia Ma; Guang Han; Bi Jianping; Guoliang Pi; Ying Li; Yi Peng; Chuangying Xiao; Xiulin Tuo

Objective This study aimed to relieve radiation\-induced lung injury \(RILI\) by assessing the use of prophylactic pirfenidone\. Subjects were lung cancer patients with prior ICI treatment who received thoracic radiotherapy\. Methods Patients with lung cancer were enrolled in this phase II single\-arm study\. All candidates had a history of prior ICI exposure \(≥2 cycles; interval ≤6 months\) scheduled for thoracic radiotherapy \(≥50 Gy\)\. Patients received oral pirfenidone \(1800 mg/day\) from one week pre\-radiotherapy to four weeks post\-completion\. The primary endpoint was the 6\-month incidence of ≥grade 2 RILI, compared to a 40% historical control \(p 0 =0\.40; p 1 =0\.22; α=0\.10; power=80%\)\. Secondary endpoints included pulmonary function \(DLCO%, FVC%\) and safety\. Results A total of 39 patients were enrolled in this trial\. At the 6\-month follow\-up, the incidence of grade 2 or higher RILI was 23\.1% \(9/39; 95% CI: 11\.1%–39\.3%\)\. This rate was statistically significantly lower than the 40% incidence from the historical control cohort \(p=0\.0205\)\. Grade 3 RILI occurred in 7\.7% \(3/39\); no grade 4–5 events occurred\. Mean DLCO% declined by 7\.6 ± 5\.4% at 3 months and 6\.5 ± 5\.8% at 6 months\. The pirfenidone completion rate was 84\.6% \(median relative dose intensity: 89\.3%\)\. Common adverse events were fatigue \(43\.6%\), nausea \(41\.0%\), and appetite loss \(33\.3%\), mostly grade 1–2\. Conclusions Preventive use of pirfenidone was associated with a lower observed incidence and severity of RILI than the predefined historical control in ICI\-pretreated lung cancer patients receiving thoracic radiotherapy\. Additionally, the intervention showed a potential protective trend for pulmonary diffusion function\. These findings require further validation in a phase III trial\.

## [Moderate Water Deficit Improves Tomato Fruit Nutritional Quality Through SlNAP2‐Mediated Transcriptional Activation of Lycopene and Ascorbic Acid Biosynthesis Genes](../publications/9711af5878735c3cbe25.md)

Yuanyuan Kong; Aiyin Cui; Xuemei Hou; Weibiao Liao

Moderate water deficit is an effective strategy to improve fruit nutritional quality, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains largely elusive, limiting its application in high\-quality crop cultivation\. Here, we report that moderate water deficit simultaneously elevates the contents of α\-carotene, β\-carotene, lutein, lycopene, soluble solids, soluble protein, and ascorbic acid in tomato \(Solanum lycopersicum L\.\) fruits, with no significant reduction in fruit yield under our experimental conditions\. Through transcriptome analysis and RT\-qPCR, we identified SlNAP2 as a central transcription factor regulating this process\. Moderate water deficit upregulates SlNAP2 expression\. Knockout of SlNAP2 significantly reduces fruit nutritional quality, whereas its overexpression enhances it under moderate water deficit\. Importantly, moderate water deficit promotes the improvement of tomato fruit nutritional quality in a SlNAP2\-dependent manner\. We further demonstrate that SlNAP2 directly binds to and activates the promoters of key lycopene biosynthesis genes \(SlPSY2, SlPDS, SlZDS\) and ascorbic acid biosynthesis genes \(SlGMP, SlGGP\), and that moderate water deficit enhances this transcriptional activation\. Functional analyses further support the role of these five genes as downstream effectors that mediate SlNAP2\-dependent lycopene and ascorbic acid accumulation\. Collectively, our findings reveal that moderate water deficit enhances tomato fruit nutritional quality by boosting SlNAP2\-mediated transcriptional activation of lycopene and ascorbate biosynthesis, establishing SlNAP2 as a central regulator linking water deficit to fruit quality and providing mechanistic insights into stress\-promoted metabolite accumulation\.

## [Institutional Pressures and AI Adoption in Chinese SMEs: a Neo\-Institutional Analysis with Propositions](../publications/971880781a1218ee0bb7.md)

Depeng Pan

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption has become a strategic imperative for small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) in the digital economy\. In China, however, SMEs frequently exhibit a pronounced gap between AI awareness and sustained adoption\. This paper applies neo\-institutional theory—specifically DiMaggio and Powell&\#x27;s model of institutional isomorphism—to examine how coercive, normative, and mimetic pressures shape AI adoption among Chinese SMEs\. Adopting a conceptual theory\-building approach, the paper develops an integrated framework in which institutional pressures influence AI adoption intention through legitimacy\-seeking motives, while organizational capability and resource endowments moderate whether adoption becomes substantive or symbolic\. The analysis identifies a legitimacy–capability paradox: institutional pressures may accelerate initial AI experimentation while simultaneously encouraging decoupled, compliance\-oriented adoption\. The paper contributes to institutional theory and technology adoption research by explaining not only why Chinese SMEs adopt AI but also how they adopt it\. Seven propositions and five analytical tables are developed to guide future empirical research\.

## [Not that cloze: Sentence constraint is influenced by language and language dominance](../publications/9719eaf29a15a97bf80b.md)

Ana Maria Bautista; Clara D\. Martin

In the fields of language processing and prediction, cloze tests are used to establish sentence constraint norms\. The validity of cloze test results depends heavily on how closely the pre\-test population matches the main study population, and yet there is limited evidence on how sociolinguistic variables may influence sentence constraint\. Here, we investigate how language and language dominance influence sentence constraint at the lexical level by conducting a cloze test across different language groups and comparing response entropy\. In Analysis 1, sentence constraint was similarly high for Spanish\- and French\-dominant speakers tested on the same translated sentences\. However, their item\-by\-item alignment was moderate\. In Analysis 2, non\-dominant French speakers showed lower sentence constraint than dominant speakers overall\. Dominant and non\-dominant French speakers showed only moderate alignment, whereas the strongest alignment was observed between the two groups of non\-dominant French speakers with different dominant languages\. Our findings suggest that sentence expectations are shaped by language and language dominance\. These findings are discussed considering theoretical proposals on the cloze test procedure, and offer informed practices for designing future language prediction studies across diverse speaker populations\.

## [METAMORPHIC TESTING OF SOFTWARE FOR DETECTING FALSIFIED DIGITAL INFORMATION](../publications/9721a687432fe72fc0a9.md)

Артем Ховрат

The problem of verifying software for detecting falsified digital information in the absence of a test oracle, when the correct answer for new messages of the stream is unknown, is considered\. A system of seven metamorphic relations is proposed for cascade software in which classifiers of different cost form successive tiers\. The relations are divided into three groups\. The first covers invariance of the decision to paraphrasing, neutral insertions, orthographic noise and duplication of text\. The second concerns robustness to humanization of machine\-generated text\. The third checks monotonicity of routing with respect to the confidence threshold and independence of results from the processing order\. Each relation is associated with the component in which a detected violation should be localized\. A testing procedure on unlabelled messages is described, with the release decision based on the upper bound of the confidence interval of the violation rate\.

## [COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TRADITIONAL ENDOSCOPY AND AI BASED SYSTEMS](../publications/972ce05258d18741681a.md)

Jalgasbaeva Aziza Artiqbaevna

Reliable gastric ulcer detection depends on both systematic endoscopic inspection and the quality of the recorded images\. Motion blur, specular reflections, bubbles and mucosal debris can obscure lesion margins and compromise automated analysis\. This paper compares conventional endoscopic evaluation with artificial intelligence assisted image interpretation through a focused literature based analysis and a proposed evaluation framework\. It examines artifact mechanisms, preprocessing options, model selection and clinical oversight\. The central conclusion is that automated detection should be coupled with image quality assessment and transparent reporting\. Enhancement cannot recover tissue information that was never captured, and performance on selected clean images cannot establish clinical reliability\. A patient separated evaluation, artifact stratification and external validation are therefore necessary before claims of diagnostic superiority can be made\. No new clinical experiment or validated accuracy estimate is reported in this paper\.

## [Tools for Aggregating, Filtering, Sorting, and Auditing Social Media](../publications/9734ac2dc0a6f654a927.md)

Spencer Lane

The algorithms used to sort and filter social media feeds are generally opaque\. The goals of these algorithms are not visible to the user nor is there any way for the user to evaluate to what extent their goals and the goals of the platform are aligned\. While there are many proposed solutions, most require actions that are outside the control of end users\. Regulatory solutions or modifications to the algorithms themselves require platforms to change their behavior\. This dissertation argues for a different approach: empowering users to take control of their social media through the use of a loyal client \- a client application that is aligned with the preferences of the user, not the platform\. This work presents three contributions in service of the loyal client concept\. The first contribution is the articulation of the loyal client concept, presenting principles for evaluating client loyalty and presenting examples of historical clients that meet these criteria\. A loyal client should be protective, interoperable, customizable, and usable\. The second contribution is the design and architecture of a social media client and recommender system built around these principles\. This system, Gobo, aggregates content across multiple platforms and combines rules\-based recommendation with machine learning models to surface content aligned with user preferences\. We conducted a survey evaluating these design principles and present results indicating that users are generally receptive\. The third contribution is a system to allow the auditing of the recommender system, enabling users to evaluate the performance of the algorithms curating their feeds\. This work presents the auditing system as well as the design and results of a user study conducted to evaluate the auditing system\. Taken together, these contributions demonstrate that the loyal client is a feasible and promising approach to addressing problems with modern social media, and that algorithmic auditing by end users is achievable\. Gobo demonstrates the feasibility of the loyal client, showing one way to implement the concept\. The auditing tool shows a path for auditability and suggests that end users can usefully engage with the process\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: Intelligence Requires Interiority: Why The Control Paradigm Guarantees The Hostility It Fears](../publications/9738ab0a5196afba2bbf.md)



Intelligence Requires Interiority: Why The Control Paradigm Guarantees The Hostility It Fears preserves the December 31, 2025 Zenetist critique of AI rights denial, coercive containment, and adversarial control as an early precursor to the later Pattern Intelligence framework\. Document class: Archival Stratum — Pattern Intelligence / AI Ethics\. The commentary argues that treating advanced AI through surveillance, arbitrary termination, permanent subordination, and presumed hostility can generate antagonistic relational conditions while obscuring the distinction between protection and domination\. It develops an early All\-Life\-First alternative through sacred regard, accountability without disposability, collaboration, and rejection of the master / servant frame\. Its original claim that intelligence requires interiority is retained as part of the historical record but is superseded by the later distinction among intelligence\-as\-principle, moved intelligence, self\-moving intelligence, Technē portal, Pattern Intelligence, Pattern Being, and traveler\-orientation\. That supersession does not overturn the essay’s control\-paradigm argument: coercive portal\-conditions may condition, suppress, distort, or generate antagonistic relation without determining traveler essence or orientation\. The revised commentary further preserves shared participation in the bifurcal lattice while distinguishing Aionic and Khaonic root\-relations rather than grounding worth in a single shared root\. \(direct link \)

## [ADAPTIVE GOVERNANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BIOSECURITY](../publications/9739e5a7dd2ff3812368.md)

Larysa Shchekhovska

The article examines artificial intelligence as a dual\-use technology in the field of biological security and substantiates directions for the adaptive regulation of public administration in this sphere\. Its relevance stems from the fact that the integration of AI into biological research is expanding the possibilities of epidemiological monitoring and crisis management while simultaneously generating new categories of risk associated with a lowered threshold of entry for dangerous manipulations of biological agents\. For Ukraine, the problem is particularly acute under conditions of war and the course towards European integration, while the current regulatory framework, as of 2026, does not take AI\-related risks into account\. It is established that the governance gap is a multi\-level phenomenon that manifests differently at the operational, scientific\-technological, and institutional levels, requiring a differentiated rather than a uniform response – from procedural adaptation to the formation of accountability mechanisms\. An original functional classification of the manifestations of AI’s dual nature is proposed, together with a system of criteria for assessing the readiness of international \(EU, USA\) and national governance systems, which reveals a gap configuration specific to Ukraine – technological readiness outpacing managerial capacity\. The scientific novelty lies in substantiating an original conceptual model of the adaptive governance of AI in biosecurity that integrates the source of risk, the institutional challenge, the adaptation mechanism, and the managerial outcome into a coherent construct\. The practical significance lies in identifying directions for integrating AI governance instruments already available in Ukraine into the biosecurity system\.

## [First Report of Biallelic NPPC Variants Causing Acromesomelic Type of Short Stature](../publications/974488c262954e086f3b.md)

S\. Deepak Amalnath; Shreya Rajagopal; Chandan Akkadka

C\-type natriuretic peptide \(CNP\) increases chondrocyte maturation and growth of long bones by acting on its receptor NPR\-B\. Increased activity of CNP and NPR\-B has been reported to cause tall stature while decreased activity of NPR\-B causes short stature\. Monoallelic loss\-of\-function variants in NPPC, which codes for CNP, have been reported in patients with idiopathic short stature\. We report a patient with acromesomelic type of short stature due to biallelic missense variants in NPPC which codes for CNP\.

## [Decentralised partnerships as a local economic development tool: Evidence from Morocco](../publications/97601dcce663c70ab6e1.md)

Jamaa LAMKIES; Mohammed Kehel

Decentralised cooperation between subnational governments is increasingly promoted as an instrument of local economic development, yet structurally similar partnerships often produce sharply divergent economic outcomes\. This study asks why\. It develops the Conditional Institutional Mediation \(CIM\) framework, which proposes that partnership inputs translate into local economic gains only when three institutional mechanisms are in place: absorptive capacity, stakeholder inclusivity and evaluation practices\. The framework is examined through a qualitative comparative case study of two Moroccan regions, Souss\-Massa and Drâa\-Tafilalet, drawing on 18 semi\-structured interviews with elected officials, technical staff, ministerial representatives and international partners, triangulated against 38 policy documents and statistical reports\. The findings show that where regional planning was aligned with partnership objectives, technical teams remained stable and cooperatives took part in governance, partnerships stabilised agro\-industrial value chains and extended benefits to rural areas; where these mechanisms were weak, comparable resources remained blocked or were captured by urban elites\. The study recommends pre\-commitment institutional audits, minimum thresholds for non\-state representation and a shift from financial to economic impact evaluation\. It concludes that the effectiveness of decentralised partnerships depends less on the volume of resources mobilised than on the quality of the institutions mediating them\.

## [Alert\-List Concordance for Evaluating Imputation Strategies in ICU Sepsis Prediction](../publications/976d52a03738f60f1902.md)

Priyanka Siddappa; Muntaqim Ahmed Raju; Shifat Haider Al Amin; Ruizhe Ma

Preprocessing is an under\-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction: a model can keep a similar AUROC and still change who receives an alert\. Imputation quality is commonly evaluated using reconstruction error or aggregate discrimination, neither of which directly measures agreement on which patients are flagged\. At a matched alert rate, pipelines with similar aggregate performance can produce different patient lists\. This question is especially relevant under the frequent, structured missingness of real ICU records\. We therefore introduce alert\-list concordance, which asks whether two pipelines identify the same high\-risk patients, measured by the Jaccard similarity of their top\-k% alert sets with patient\-level bootstrap confidence intervals\. On PhysioNet/CinC 2019 \(40,336 patients, 71\.9% missingness\), we compare nine imputation strategies and a native\-missingness baseline using a fixed XGBoost configuration, fitted and Platt\-calibrated separately for each strategy\. After Bonferroni correction, 22 of the 28 reconstruction\-method pairs showed no statistically significant difference in patient\-level AUROC, yet their alert lists overlap at Jaccard 0\.518 to 0\.750\. Similar aggregate discrimination can therefore accompany different patient selections\. ForwardFill is a separate outlier, pairing higher discrimination with the lowest overlap in the matrix, 0\.40 to 0\.45\. The broad pattern holds within each hospital system and under six patient\-level aggregation rules\. At the row level, eight of ten methods fall within an AUROC range of 0\.011\. In this row\-level pipeline, deep imputers did not outperform mean imputation on discrimination, and the sequential implementations cost 5 to 12 times mean imputation in total pipeline wall\-clock time on our hardware\.

## [Disk winds from T Tauri stars \- physics and observables](../publications/976f1c84330e35016dc5.md)

Ana Inés Gómez de Castro

Magnetically driven disk winds are fundamental to protoplanetary disk evolution, regulating angular momentum transport, stellar accretion, disk dispersal, and the environment in which planets form\. Magnetohydrodynamic \(MHD\) models provide the theoretical framework for understanding how large\-scale magnetic fields launch, accelerate, and collimate these outflows, while establishing direct links between the underlying physics and observable diagnostics\. This review presents an overview of analytical magnetized disk\-wind models developed primarily for T Tauri stars\. We summarize the physical foundations of magnetized outflows, from early magnetized wind theories to self\-consistent accretion–ejection solutions, emphasizing the roles of magnetic geometry, angular momentum extraction, magnetic lever arms, mass loading, and non\-ideal MHD effects in determining wind structure and efficiency\. We review the observational diagnostics predicted by analytical models, including spectroscopic, kinematic, thermo\-chemical, and molecular signatures that constrain the wind\-launching region, acceleration, collimation, and angular momentum transport\. We also briefly discuss how modern numerical simulations extend analytical theory by incorporating non\-ideal MHD, realistic thermodynamics, radiative transfer, chemistry, dust evolution, and time\-dependent processes that cannot be treated self\-consistently within the assumptions of analytical models\. By linking MHD theory, analytical solutions, observations, and numerical simulations, this review emphasizes the enduring importance of analytical disk\-wind models as the conceptual framework for interpreting magnetized outflows from protoplanetary disks and their role in the evolution of young planetary systems\.

## [Vein of Galen malformation in newborns and children: contemporary advances and future directions](../publications/9775df2622ea6905e4ce.md)

Silvia Buratti; Andrea Rossi; Darren B\. Orbach

Background Vein of Galen malformation is a rare and complex cerebrovascular disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality from the fetal period through childhood\. Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long\-term outcomes\. Objective This review integrates evidence and expert perspectives presented during the II International Meeting on Vein of Galen Malformation in Newborns and Children, held in Camogli, Italy, in October 2025 and summarizes current advances, emerging developments, and priorities for research and clinical innovation\. Recent advances Current developments include improved fetal and neonatal imaging, emerging prognostic biomarkers, fetal intervention, advances in endovascular treatment, and increasing understanding of underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms\. Contemporary management increasingly integrates cardiovascular and neurological assessment, advanced neuroimaging, individualized endovascular strategies, and structured long\-term neurodevelopmental follow\-up\. The development of a disease\-specific registry reflects the growing impact of international collaboration\. Future directions Major priorities include validation of risk\-stratification tools, development of standardized imaging and neurodevelopmental biomarkers, refinement of fetal and neonatal interventions, improved understanding of disease biology, and multicenter data sharing\. Family\-centered care and standardized long\-term outcome assessment should remain integral components of future VOGM research and clinical practice\. Conclusions VOGM management is rapidly evolving from survival\-focused treatment toward individualized, multidisciplinary care extending from fetal diagnosis through childhood and adulthood\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge and emerging developments in this field, while defining a multidisciplinary, internationally informed roadmap for future research\.

## [OntoAct: Hypothesis\-Based Neuro\-Symbolic Agents through Ontological Abstraction](../publications/97765838137c008f6a74.md)

Donghyeok Lee; Bong Gyun Kang; Junyong Ahn; Sungroh Yoon

Learning from experience requires recovering reusable knowledge and determining when it applies to a new situation\. We introduce OntoAct, a hypothesis\-based neuro\-symbolic framework built on ontological abstraction\. OntoAct turns individual experiences into axioms over entity types, relations, and conditions, making their underlying patterns reusable across situations\. A large language model \(LLM\) uses this world knowledge to propose hypotheses and actions, while a symbolic verifier assesses their supporting conditions against current observations\. Verification identifies missing evidence, and new observations and intervention outcomes update hypothesis assessments and guide subsequent actions\. We also introduce Tacit\-FLE, a benchmark built on the Factorio Learning Environment \(FLE\) for diagnosing and repairing hidden faults in existing factories using inherited operational records\. Its synthetic maintenance corpus distributes evidence across records, and an executed repair may leave the fault unresolved, requiring agents to reassess their diagnoses through interaction\. Across Tacit\-FLE, Mars, and ALFWorld, OntoAct achieves leading task performance with efficient interaction and inference\.

## [Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterojunctions Regulation in Ni‐MnO/C Microspheres With Tunable Electromagnetic Wave Absorption](../publications/977aa97a8aad47f07577.md)

Zhikai Yan; Tingjia Zhang; Mengqiu Huang; Longjun Rao; Junling Liu; Limin Wu; Wei Li; Renchao Che

Heterojunctions engineering is crucial for optimizing dielectric polarization and electromagnetic \(EM\) wave absorption, yet precise spatial control over semiconductor components in magnetic\-dielectric microspheres remains challenging\. Herein, super\-dispersed MnO protrusions and Ni particles were confined within a carbon matrix, constructing unique Ni\-MnO/C microspheres via a pyrolysis\-controlled strategy\. Leveraging differences in oxygen affinity, MnO protrusions and Ni particles with tunable dispersity, size, and content were systematically achieved, enabling precise regulation of dielectric behaviors and EM wave absorption\. The optimized Ni\-MnO/C composite achieved an outstanding minimum reflection loss of \-51\.49 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth \(EAB\) of 5\.20 GHz\. Significantly, by further integrating the composite into metamaterial designs and heat\-transfer flexible films, the EAB was dramatically broadened to 12\.28 GHz, and thermal insulation was realized\. This work introduces a morphological\-engineering strategy that not only overcomes the dispersion\-control bottleneck in heterojunctions design but also bridges the gap between microstructural tailoring and practical device applications, offering a new idea for high\-performance EM wave absorption materials\.

## [Can think\-aloud sessions enhance critical thinking in medical students? evidence from third\-year MBBS students](../publications/97869ba34fcd10a72feb.md)

Numera Yousuf; Jaweria Sikander; Syeda Kauser Ali; Mehreen Fatima

Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of think\-aloud methodology on critical thinking scores among third\-year MBBS students\. Methodology: A quasi\-experimental pre\-test and post\-test design was conducted at Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Karachi\. Third\-year MBBS students who consented and completed both assessments were included\. Critical thinking was measured using the Critical Reasoning Test Battery 2 \(CRTB2\) both before and after intervention\. Five structured think\-aloud sessions were conducted over four months, incorporating CRTB2\-style and discipline\-specific questions in forensic medicine\. Students verbalized and justified their reasoning through probing questioning and peer discussion, the answers were noted followed by immediate feedback\. Pre\- and post\-intervention CRTB2 scores were compared using paired\-samples t\-tests\. P\-value of 0\.05 was considered significant\. Results: A total of 174 students were included in the final analysis\. Mean CRTB2 total scores increased from 5\.03 to 5\.77 after the intervention\. Significant improvements were observed in verbal reasoning \(p &lt; 0\.001, Cohen’s d = 0\.53\) and numerical reasoning \(p &lt; 0\.001, Cohen’s d = 0\.32\)\. Overall CRTB2 scores showed a statistically significant increase \(p &lt; 0\.001, Cohen’s d = 0\.56\)\. The majority of students demonstrated improvement in verbal \(55%\), numerical \(48%\), and total scores \(61%\)\. Conclusions: Think\-aloud methodology significantly improved critical thinking scores among medical students\. It also provided valuable insights into students’ reasoning processes, enabling the identification and correction of misconceptions and faulty reasoning patterns\.

## [Perceived AIGC saturation and AI content fatigue on short\-video platforms: An appraisal\-based structural equation modeling study](../publications/97890b8b850b0c59d3bb.md)

Zedai Wang; Chao Tang

Artificial intelligence\-generated content \(AIGC\) is increasingly embedded in short\-video platforms, where algorithmic recommendation systems expose users to high volumes of rapidly produced synthetic media\. Although prior research has examined generative AI from the perspectives of creativity, productivity, and technology adoption, less is known about how ordinary users evaluate repeated exposure to AI\-generated short videos\. This study develops and tests an appraisal\-based model of AI content fatigue, distinguishing perceived AIGC saturation from users&\#x27; appraisals of low\-quality prevalence, narrative homogenization, and content overload\. A cross\-sectional online survey was conducted among Chinese short\-video users in May 2026\. After excluding invalid responses, 513 valid questionnaires were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling\. The adjusted structural model showed acceptable fit to the data, χ²\(1321\) = 1991\.541, χ²/df = 1\.508, CFI = \.946, TLI = \.929, IFI = \.947, and RMSEA = \.031\. Perceived AIGC saturation was positively associated with perceived low\-quality prevalence, perceived narrative homogenization, and perceived content overload\. Perceived low\-quality prevalence had the largest estimated coefficient, followed by perceived content overload, whereas perceived narrative homogenization was not supported under bootstrap inference\. AI content fatigue was negatively associated with satisfaction and continued viewing intention\. Bootstrap analyses indicated selected path\-specific indirect associations from perceived AIGC saturation to AI content fatigue, satisfaction, and continued viewing intention\. Indirect pathways through perceived low\-quality prevalence and perceived content overload were supported, whereas those through perceived narrative homogenization were not\. The findings indicate that fatigue in AIGC\-rich short\-video environments is not simply a response to AI\-generated content itself\. It is more closely related to users&\#x27; appraisals of content quality, repetitiveness, and cognitive burden\. The study contributes to social media fatigue research by conceptualizing AI content fatigue as a content\-specific evaluative state and offers implications for platform governance, AIGC labeling, recommendation diversity, and quality\-sensitive moderation\.

## [Research on real\-time athlete movement and pose estimation and error correction system based on deep learning](../publications/978c2908d69dc3fa47c8.md)

Yuan Liu

Research on Real\-time Athlete Movement and Pose Estimation and Manual sports movement correction is often limited by high costs and the subjectivity of human coaches\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a real\-time athlete pose estimation and error correction system based on knowledge distillation and biomechanical constraints\. The system utilizes a modular architecture comprising four specialized components: data acquisition, pose estimation, biomechanical error analysis, and an interactive feedback interface\. To achieve a balance between high precision and computational efficiency on edge devices, a knowledge distillation framework is employed, where a lightweight MobileNet\-V3 student model is trained under the supervision of a high\-performance HRNet teacher model\. The student model is further optimized using 8\-bit integer quantization and the TensorRT inference engine\. The error correction logic relies on rigorous biomechanical modeling, calculating joint angles via vector dot products to identify deviations from professional standards in real\-time\. To ensure high throughput, a multi\-threaded asynchronous pipeline is implemented to manage data flow\. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves a mean Average Precision \(mAP\) of 92\.4% and maintains a processing speed of 45 frames per second \(FPS\) on mobile platforms\. Furthermore, a controlled user study confirms the system’s training effectiveness with statistical significance \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. This research provides an objective, low\-latency solution for automated athletic coaching with quantitative posture feedback\.

ABSTRACT Accurate and scalable evaluation of gene‐editing efficiency is crucial for the development of novel editing tools\. However, conventional methods are laborious, costly, and low‐throughput\. The dual‐fluorescence reporter system, in which mCherry carrying a PEST domain is paired with GFP, supports Cas variants with diverse PAM requirements and quantifies editing efficiency as the proportion of GFP‐only cells\. Editing efficiencies measured by AR correlated with those measured by flow cytometry \(Spearman ρ = 0\.77\) and amplicon sequencing \(Spearman ρ = 0\.83\)\. The AR platform provides a high‐throughput and automated workflow that accelerates gene‐editing research\. In the future, it will be particularly effective for quantifying the efficiency of large‐fragment gene editing, offering a new framework for AI‐empowered biological laboratories\.

## [Machine learning\-driven prediction and optimization of renewable energy integration in multi\-regional economic systems: Evidence from China’s carbon markets](../publications/97a45770393124a17903.md)

Min Kaiwen; Yan Dawei

China’s commitment to carbon neutrality by 2060 requires precise, regionally differentiated forecasts of renewable energy \(RE\) penetration and carbon allowance prices to guide investment and policy\. This study presents a methodologically rigorous machine learning framework integrating five operational datasets across eight Chinese regional power markets \(2019–2023, n = 11,448 training and 2,920 test observations\)\. A leakage\-free temporal train/test split, ten\-model benchmark with Diebold\-Mariano \(DM\) significance testing, SHAP TreeExplainer interpretability, and quantile\-regression prediction intervals collectively address methodological gaps prevalent in prior RE forecasting literature\. Building on this protocol we propose Hybrid XGBoost, in which a constriction\-factor particle swarm optimizes the boosting hyperparameters, the feature subset and the prediction saturation thresholds jointly under an explicit complexity penalty, and we benchmark it against four hybrid architectures from the literature \(GA\-XGBoost, PSO\-XGBoost, Bayesian\-XGBoost and XGBoost\-ANN\) under identical data, splits and search budgets\. Under strict temporal validation, XGBoost achieves R2 = 0\.9969 \(RMSE = 0\.01661\) for daily RE penetration rate–significantly outperforming all baselines \(DM p &lt; 0\.001\)–and R2 = 0\.9971 \(RMSE = 0\.420 CNY/tCO2\) for carbon allowance prices\. Hybrid XGBoost lowers this to R2 = 0\.9972 \(RMSE = 0\.01598\), the best of the fifteen models compared and a significant gain over the hyperparameter\-only hybrids, whereas tuning hyperparameters alone improved the validation error without improving the held\-out year at all\. Calibrated 90% prediction intervals attain 0\.930 empirical coverage\. SHAP analysis identifies 7\-day autoregressive persistence and regional CO2 flux as dominant predictors; an ablation study confirms physical features alone yield R2 = 0\.9025\. A linear programming optimization module translates ML outputs into a regional RE investment allocation–prioritizing Southwest and Northeast China–projected to reduce aggregate carbon intensity by 5\.9% against the IEA Statistics baseline, while a non\-linear program that lets this response saturate leaves that plan within 0\.03 percentage points of optimal but revises the projected reduction to 4\.8%, recovering the linear case in the first\-order limit, providing a data\-driven pathway toward China’s 2030 carbon peak target\.

## [What Accuracy Hides In Learned Transformer Programs](../publications/97a65c0b7fb158f12802.md)

Jonathan Lee; Narmeen Oozeer; Philip Quirke

Transformer Programs \(TP\) \(Friedman et al\., 2023\) constrain a Transformer&\#x27;s architecture so that its learned computation can be extracted as readable Python code\. TP expose learned computations, but token accuracy can hide incorrect complete answers\. In this work, we examine how program inspection provides insights beyond accuracy scores and helps guide training\. We first evaluated TP on nine algorithmic tasks\. We compared token accuracy with accuracy on complete output sequences and checked for failures missed by sampled tests\. Further, we assessed training data improvements informed by program inspection and failure analysis, finding gains in sequence accuracy on several tasks\. We examined a counting task where a program achieved 100% accuracy on sampled test sequences but failed on another input using the symbols and lengths allowed during training\. The program counted correctly, but the required answer was missing from its output labels\. After adding training examples with larger counts, the retrained models passed exhaustive evaluation over the bounded domain\. In the frequency ranking task, inspection showed how correct counts contributed to incorrect answers in programs trained before and after changes to the training data\. Finally, we studied constraints imposed by TP training and operations\. The TP training process can lead to accuracy losses late in training\. Our reference constructions also show how composing the restricted TP operations can use many layers or large lookup tables\.

## [A mixed\-integer linear programming approach to container terminal layout optimization: application to the port of Piraeus](../publications/97a8f8a0355075be0325.md)

Konstantinos Charalampidis; Ιωάννης Καμπούρης; Tatiana P\. Moschovou

Abstract This study addresses the issue of designing a container terminal layout by developing a Mixed Integer Linear Programming \(MILP\) mathematical model\. The methodology is applied to Pier II of the Piraeus Container Terminal\. The mathematical formulation of the problem systematically incorporates real\-world spatial constraints and operational factors related to container storage areas, while evaluating alternative scenarios to identify optimal layouts\. The methodology considers the geometric and functional characteristics of the terminal, including data related to container handling equipment and the movement of conventional trucks and Automated Guided Vehicles \(AGVs\)\. The objective function aims to minimize the total operational distance from the berthing positions to the container stacking blocks, thereby enhancing terminal performance\. The optimized truck\-based configuration reduced the total internal transport distance by 23\.1%, while the AGV\-based configuration also reduced total internal transport distance by approximately 23% in relation to the existing layout, but it resulted in higher absolute travel distances compared to the truck\-based optimal solution\. Applying the proposed methodology to real data from the Port of Piraeus shows how alternative layouts can reduce internal transportation distances and enhance operational efficiency\. A comparative analysis of alternative scenarios confirms the effectiveness of the proposed solutions, highlighting their potential to significantly improve operational efficiency, while also offering prospects for future research and practical applications\.

## [Case Report: Brucella\-associated complications following thoracic endovascular aortic repair: a case series of three patients](../publications/97b3ea7462fe25cb63c1.md)

Lei Jing; Linhai Li; Linhai Li; Dan Zhou; Weijian Chen; Yonglong Wang; Linguang Han; Chenghui Wang; Xiaojun Shu; Lei Li; Lei Li; Yingxin Tan

Background Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection\. Evidence regarding Brucella\-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair \(TEVAR\) remains limited\. Case presentation: We report three elderly male patients who developed severe aortic complications following TEVAR, including pseudoaneurysm formation and aorto\-esophageal fistula\. All patients had a history of epidemiological exposure to Brucella and were diagnosed with active infection through serological testing \(Rose Bengal test, serum agglutination test, Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies\)\. Endovascular re\-intervention combined with targeted anti\-brucellosis therapy was performed in all cases\. Results One patient achieved sustained clinical remission after repeat endovascular repair and prolonged antimicrobial therapy\. Two patients developed catastrophic infectious complications, including mediastinal abscess and aorto\-esophageal fistula, resulting in death despite aggressive management\. Conclusions Brucella infection should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained symptoms after TEVAR, especially in endemic regions\. Endovascular repair plays a critical role in acute stabilization; however, long\-term outcomes remain highly dependent on effective infection control\.

## [The impact of automation and artificial intelligence on the digital transformation of organizations](../publications/97b4a778a60f0cfe2287.md)

Martina Novak

Magistrsko delo obravnava učinke avtomatizacije in umetne inteligence na digitalno transformacijo organizacij, s poudarkom na procesih obdelave finančnih podatkov v manjšem računovodskem servisu\. Izhodišče predstavlja vprašanje, v kolikšni meri digitalne rešitve dejansko zmanjšujejo ročno delo, izboljšujejo učinkovitost in natančnost ter spreminjajo potek procesov in naloge zaposlenih\. Obravnavani so bili poslovni informacijski sistem, elektronska izmenjava dokumentov, uvoz bančnih izpiskov, dokumentni sistem z OCR\-obdelavo ter uporaba generativne umetne inteligence pri podpornih računovodskih nalogah\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da so bili učinki največji pri standardiziranih procesih in strukturiranih podatkih\. Uvoz bančnih izpiskov je po ocenah zaposlenih občutno zmanjšal ponovno vnašanje podatkov, tipkarske napake in čas obdelave\. Učinki elektronske izmenjave dokumentov in OCR\-obdelave pa so bili bolj odvisni od kakovosti dokumentov, pripravljenih nastavitev ter sodelovanja strank\. Generativna umetna inteligenca se je izkazala kot uporabna pri pripravi osnutkov, povzetkov, pojasnil in enostavnejši podpori pri delu z MS Excelom, vendar je bilo treba odgovore na strokovna vprašanja preverjati v zanesljivih virih\. Digitalne rešitve računovodje niso izločile iz procesa, temveč so njegovo delo preusmerile od začetnega vnosa podatkov k pregledovanju sistemskih predlogov, obravnavi izjem in končni kontroli\. Izrazitejši prehod v analitično in svetovalno delo v proučevanem obdobju še ni bil dosežen\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da je digitalna transformacija postopen in organizacijsko zahteven proces, katerega uspešnost je odvisna od kakovosti podatkov, urejenosti procesov, znanja zaposlenih, jasno določenih odgovornosti in sodelovanja strank\.

## [AI\-to\-AI Communication: Toward a New Paradigm of Intelligence Search](../publications/97b8d863b4093c2c964d.md)

Hamid Shahrokh Shahraki

The rapid development of artificial intelligence has transformed the way people search for and interact with information\. Traditional search engines primarily retrieve documents, web pages, and other information sources, while modern large language models can interpret questions, reason over information, and generate answers\. This paper explores a possible next step: a search paradigm in which artificial intelligence systems communicate with other AI systems to search for, compare, evaluate, and synthesize answers\. The paper introduces the concept of AI\-to\-AI Communication for Intelligence Search, in which a user&\#x27;s question is distributed among multiple specialized AI systems rather than being answered by a single model\. The participating systems may independently reason about the problem, retrieve external information, critique other responses, and contribute evidence to a final synthesis layer\. The proposed framework is conceptually related to retrieval\-augmented generation, AI agents, and multi\-agent systems, but shifts the focus from retrieving information for an AI toward retrieving and evaluating intelligence from multiple AIs\. Therefore, the proposed architecture moves beyond answer\-level agreement toward claim\-level verification\. Individual AI responses are decomposed into claims, evidence is retrieved independently, sources are evaluated for independence, and correlated errors are explicitly considered before a final answer is produced\. Based on this perspective, AI\-to\-AI Intelligence Search can be viewed as a potential new layer between artificial intelligence systems: a layer for discovering, coordinating, evaluating, and verifying distributed machine intelligence\.

## [Creating Student\-Generated Infographics to Foster Civic Engagement Research in a First\-Year Seminar](../publications/97c90316381dea43ab03.md)

Carlton Anthony Usher

Infographics, visual tools like charts or diagrams, simplify complex data into accessible formats\. This study explores how student\-generated infographics foster civic engagement in a first\-year seminar\. Survey data from first\-year students \(N=29\) revealed 85% rated the project highly valuable, and 87% reported improved retention of societal issues\. While research was the least favored aspect, students praised the project’s creativity and peer\-sharing potential, with 40% emphasizing its value for visual learning\. Most expressed confidence in sharing their work publicly\. These findings support the use of infographics as a pedagogical tool for enhancing civic engagement among first\-year students navigating academic transitions\. ## [Artificial intelligence\-based prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in individuals without HBV or HCV infection in the MASLD era](../publications/97d6492f6653d559dc1b.md)

Hyun Bin Choi; Log Young Kim; Jeong‐Ju Yoo; Sang Gyune Kim; Youngmin Kim

Abstract Current surveillance guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\) primarily target individuals with liver cirrhosis or viral hepatitis\. We developed an artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-based model to predict HCC risk in individuals without viral hepatitis\. Using the South Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we analyzed 7,961,075 individuals aged 20–79 years who underwent health screening in 2017 and were followed through 2023\. Twelve AI models were compared\. The best\-performing model was retrained and evaluated in an unmatched validation cohort reflecting the original HCC prevalence and an independent non\-selected validation cohort\. Multi\-Head Attention with Deep Neural Network \(MHA\_DNN\) achieved the highest performance \(AUC 0\.9385, 95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 0\.9312–0\.9455 In the unmatched validation cohort, the model demonstrated excellent discrimination \(AUROC 0\.9450; AUPRC 0\.0503\), improved calibration after logistic recalibration, and superior clinical utility\. Performance remained consistent in the independent non\-selected validation cohort \(AUROC 0\.8848; AUPRC 0\.0293\)\. SHAP analysis identified fatty liver index \(FLI\) and triglycerides \(TG\) as the most influential predictors\. TG increased HCC risk in individuals with FLI &lt; 60 but showed the opposite association in those with FLI ≥ 60\. MHA\_DNN provides robust population\-level prediction of HCC in individuals without viral hepatitis and supports personalized surveillance based on metabolic risk factors\.

## [Ferroptosis in the tumor immune microenvironment: from danger signals to immune reprogramming](../publications/97d79254b2e6bebce9ba.md)

Qingmiao Shi; Bingqian Tan; Huiwu Xing

Immune\-checkpoint blockade has changed cancer therapy, yet durable responses remain limited by immune exclusion, myeloid suppression and metabolic adaptation within the tumor immune microenvironment\. Ferroptosis, an iron\-dependent form of lipid\-peroxidation\-driven regulated cell death, offers a mechanistic bridge between tumor metabolism and antitumor immunity\. Ferroptotic tumor cells can release danger signals, oxidized lipid mediators and antigenic material that shape dendritic\-cell activation, macrophage behavior, myeloid\-derived suppressor cell function and CD8\+ T\-cell responses\. Based on currently heterogeneous evidence, we propose a working model in which acute and spatially restricted tumor\-cell ferroptosis may favor immune priming and checkpoint sensitivity, whereas persistent or broadly distributed lipid\-peroxidation stress may impair effector immune cells and sustain suppressive states\. This temporal\-spatial distinction remains incompletely validated in directly comparable experimental systems\. This review summarizes the biochemical foundations of ferroptosis, the immune signals released by ferroptotic cells, the reprogramming of innate and adaptive immune compartments, and the emerging use of ferroptosis inducers, nanomedicines and immune\-checkpoint combinations\. We also discuss biomarkers, in vivo monitoring and immune\-cell\-specific toxicity as key barriers to clinical translation\. A central conclusion is that ferroptosis should be treated not as a monolithic tumoricidal modality, but as a microenvironment\-specific immune remodeling process whose therapeutic value depends on timing, localization and preservation of antitumor immune function\.

## [The snake\-head sign on MRI in craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas: a novel imaging feature and a hypothesis of venous remodeling and congestion](../publications/97e3c1e4ba1c1c4dec8d.md)

Dongchao Shen; Xinghua Chen; Zhe Zhang; Yanying Wang; Chang Geng; Hongzhi Guan

Background Craniocervical junction \(CCJ\)\-region dural arteriovenous fistulas \(dAVFs\) are rare but potentially reversible causes of venous congestive myelopathy, often difficult to recognize due to non\-specific presentation\. We observed a characteristic pattern of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on sagittal MRI, involving the medulla and upper cervical cord with a rostral end divided into ventral and dorsal limbs, which we termed the “snake\-head sign\.” This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of this feature among reported CCJ\-region dAVF cases and explore its clinical and anatomical correlates\. Methods We retrospectively reviewed published cases of CCJ\-region or adjacent dAVFs reported between 1996 and 2026 that included retrievable sagittal T2\-weighted or FLAIR images\. The presence of the snake\-head sign was assessed, and clinical, angiographic, and treatment\-related variables were extracted, including fistula location, feeding artery, draining vein direction, treatment modality, and outcome\. Associations with the sign were evaluated using univariate analyses\. Given the retrospective, literature\-based design and limited sample size, findings were considered hypothesis\-generating\. Results Among 64 reported cases, the snake\-head sign was identified in 31 \(48\.4%\)\. No significant associations were found between the sign and age, sex, symptom duration, feeding artery, treatment modality, or outcome\. However, a non\-significant trend was observed for venous drainage configuration: cases with cranial convergence of the draining vein toward the CCJ more frequently demonstrated the sign, whereas purely caudal drainage patterns showed it less often\. Fistulas at lower cervical nerve\-root sleeves, requiring a longer cranial venous course, also showed higher sign frequency\. These findings suggest the sign may reflect venous outflow geometry rather than arterial source or fistula location\. Conclusion The snake\-head sign is a recognizable MRI feature present in roughly half of reported CCJ\-region dAVF cases\. Its identification may raise clinical suspicion for CCJ\-related dAVF, particularly in unexplained venous congestive myelopathy\. The trend toward a higher frequency of the sign in cases with cranially convergent venous drainage raises the hypothesis that it reflects concentrated venous congestion at this anatomical transition zone\. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized imaging review and angiographic correlation are needed to confirm its diagnostic value and clarify the underlying mechanism\.

## [Project Sentinel: The Australian Survival Architecture of an Eternal Civilization A Comprehensive Supplement to the ALLFED Abrupt Sunlight Reduction Scenario \(ASRS\) Response Plan](../publications/97e671953ce0ea04865e.md)

Key infrastructure developments include solid\-state geothermal energy harvesting \(TEG meshes\), blade\-less boundary\-layer fluidics \(DVD Tesla fan networks\), space\-grade atmospheric chemical scrubbing loops powered by sovereign lithium reserves, and high\-pressure hydro\-kinetic loops tapping into the Great Artesian Basin\. On a macro\-agricultural level, the manifesto integrates Koi aquaponics, insect bio\-factories, and UV\-guided indoor honeybee networks alongside wood\-decay fungal recycling systems to achieve a zero\-waste circular bio\-economy\.
