## [Composite power quality disturbance identification method considering confidence correction](../publications/97eb03bc4eb72c7240a9.md)

Biaolong Su; Dashi Luo; Shuangyin Dai; Bo Dong; Yi Wang; Fan Ni

To effectively identify multi\-source composite power quality disturbance \(PQD\) signals in distribution networks, this paper proposes a novel PQD recognition method based on a Fully Convolutional Network\-Gated Recurrent Unit\-Attention \(FCN\-GRU\-Attention\) architecture combined with a confidence correction mechanism\. Composite PQDs, formed by the simultaneous coupling of transient and continuous disturbances, exhibit severe feature overlap and masking effect, making key discriminative features easily submerged\. To tackle this challenge, a three\-dimensional synergistic framework is constructed: the FCN extracts multi\-scale spatial and temporal\-frequency representations from raw time\-series signals without manual feature extraction; the Gated Recurrent Unit \(GRU\) models long\-term dynamic evolution characteristics; and the Attention mechanism adaptively weights critical transient disturbance windows\. Furthermore, a disturbance recognition enhancement mechanism using explicit and implicit confidence factors is designed to adaptively refine multi\-label confidence predictions, enabling the model to achieve superior generalization to unseen composite disturbances beyond the training distribution\.

## [A real\-world pharmacovigilance study of FDA adverse event reporting system events for bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide](../publications/97eb94f242bdab397378.md)

Ying Liu; Leidan Zhang; Xin Li; Hongxin Zhao

Introduction Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide \(B/F/TAF\) is a widely used antiretroviral regimen, but its real\-world long\-term safety profile in diverse populations remains incompletely characterized\. Methods We analyzed adverse drug signals from the FAERS database \(2018–2025\) with B/F/TAF as the primary suspected drug\. Disproportionality analyses using reporting odds ratio \(ROR\), proportional reporting ratio \(PRR\), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network \(BCPNN\), and multi\-item gamma Poisson shrinker \(MGPS\) algorithms were performed to detect safety signals\. Results A total of 6,816 case reports and 13,853 adverse events were included\. The highest numbers of reports were related to “Injury, poisoning and procedural complications” \(n = 1,792\), followed by “General disorders and administration site conditions” \(n = 1,726\) and “Investigations” \(n = 1,499\)\. The System Organ Classes \(SOCs\) meeting all four disproportionality criteria were “Congenital, familial and genetic disorders” and “Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions\.” The most frequently reported preferred terms were weight increase \(408 cases\), product dose omission \(242 cases\), and maternal exposure during pregnancy \(202 cases\), while the strongest signals by ROR were viral load increased \(ROR 160\.14\), CD4 lymphocytes decreased \(ROR 124\.60\), and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome \(ROR 88\.12\)\. Overall, 37\.94% of events occurred within the first month of treatment, and 17\.49% occurred after one year\. Conclusion These pharmacovigilance signals merit clinical awareness, particularly regarding metabolic monitoring, virologic/immunologic parameters \(which likely reflect treatment response rather than drug toxicity\), and pregnancy exposure reporting\. Events occurred both early and late, reinforcing the necessity of longitudinal pharmacovigilance for this widely used antiretroviral regimen\. However, these findings are exploratory and should not be interpreted as confirmed causal associations\.

## [PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool\-Using LLM Agents](../publications/97ee168ec636462f612e.md)

Kshitij Mishra; Abhijith Sharma; Nils Lukas; Salem Lahlou

Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi\-turn interactions\. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements\. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content\-safety red\-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use\. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems\. We propose PROBE \(Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration\), an algorithm for training LLM\-based auditors that interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe them for policy violations through multi\-turn, tool\-mediated dialogue\. We formalize agent auditing as a two\-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity\. To study training objectives and reward design, we compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet\-based optimization in a controlled setting\. Across extensive experiments, auditors trained with PROBE uncover substantially broader and higher\-yield policy violations than same\-architecture zero\-shot adversaries, even when the auditor is significantly smaller than the target agent\. Our results show that multi\-turn behavioral auditing is a distinct and necessary axis of agent evaluation, complementing capability and safety benchmarks\. PROBE offers a scalable path toward automated policy auditing for real\-world agentic systems and suggests a co\-evolutionary loop in which auditors expose failures and agents improve from auditor feedback\.

## [Conditional diffusion\-based inverse kinematics for redundant 7\-DOF manipulators with differentiable refinement](../publications/97ef96a80eb01a946e79.md)

Lesia Hentosh; Yaroslav Hladun; Ivan Tsmots

Background Inverse kinematics of redundant manipulators is a multi\-solution problem, since one end\-effector pose may correspond to multiple admissible joint configurations\. Classical numerical solvers and regression\-based neural models usually return a single joint configuration and therefore do not explicitly represent the inverse\-kinematic solution manifold\. Existing generative solvers based on normalizing flows produce multiple solutions, but they require invertible network architectures and do not include an explicit task\-space correction stage\. This study aimed to develop a hybrid generative\-kinematic method for inverse kinematics of a redundant 7\-DOF manipulator that can generate multiple admissible configurations for a given target pose\. Methods A hybrid method, DiffusionIK, was developed by combining conditional diffusion\-based generation, classifier\-free guidance, DDIM sampling, and differentiable forward\-kinematics refinement\. A ResMLP denoiser is trained in the normalized joint space using procedurally generated training pairs obtained from the forward kinematics of the xArm manipulator\. For each target pose, the diffusion model generated multiple candidate joint configurations, and the refinement stage subsequently reduced the task\-space residual for each candidate\. Numerical experiments were performed on 500 reachable target poses with 50 generated candidates per pose\. Performance was evaluated using position and orientation success thresholds of 1 mm and 1°, respectively, together with the preservation of joint\-space variability after refinement\. Results DiffusionIK reached 99\.40% success after 200 refinement steps and 100\.00% after 500 steps under 1 mm and 1° thresholds, with a mean joint\-space variability of 9\.77 rad\. In a unified benchmark against damped least squares, KDL, direct regression, and a normalizing\-flow baseline, DiffusionIK with refinement achieved 99\.80% success on 500 unseen poses and 98\.40% near singularities, matching the strongest numerical solver while returning 50 diverse solutions per pose\. Conclusion The proposed DiffusionIK method provides an effective formulation of redundant inverse kinematics as conditional generation followed by local kinematic correction\. By combining diffusion\-based candidate generation with differentiable forward\-kinematics refinement, the method represents the multi\-solution nature of redundant manipulators and achieves high task\-space accuracy while preserving configuration diversity\. Unlike normalizing\-flow\-based solvers, DiffusionIK imposes no invertibility constraints on the denoiser and combines generation with differentiable forward\-kinematics refinement, which provides sub\-millimetre and sub\-degree accuracy together with configuration diversity\.

## [Blood pressure targets in adults with hypertension](../publications/97f6bfa7a6f1ea1061c4.md)

Doreen Yvonne Larvie; Wade Thompson; Guillaume Grenet; James Wright; Ciprian D Jauca; Douglas M Salzwedel; Stephen Adams; Anshula Ambasta

OBJECTIVES: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review \(intervention\)\. The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets of blood pressure \(BP; i\.e\. BP ≤ 135/85 mmHg\) versus standard targets \(i\.e\. BP ≤ 140 to 160/90 to 100 mmHg\) for total mortality and morbidity in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP\. Secondary objectives To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets versus standard targets for achieved systolic and diastolic BP in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP\. To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets versus standard targets for withdrawals due to adverse events in people 18 years or older with elevated BP\. To assess whether the effects of lower targets versus standard targets differ according to prespecified equity\-related characteristics \(e\.g\. place of residence, race/ethnicity/culture/ancestry, sex, socioeconomic status, and social capital, plus other context\-specific factors, including comorbidity burden\) in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP\.

## [A Plausible Explanation Is Enough to Mislead Multimodal Judges](../publications/97f785199bb491db8e0f.md)

Anglin Cai; Zhiqi Wang; Xiaozhi Yang; Yurun Lin; Dongwon Lee; Yuchen Yang

Multimodal large language models \(MLLMs\) increasingly serve as judges in training and evaluation pipelines, often assessing answers together with explanations\. Although AI judges are sensitive to textual factors, it remains unclear whether ordinary plausible explanations can sway judgments requiring visual verification\. We introduce JUPE, a visual\-question\-answering \(VQA\)\-style benchmark that fixes answers while varying explanations\. Across 14 MLLM judges, ordinary explanations that sound plausible mislead judges, with effects comparable on average to deliberately persuasive arguments\. Plain justifications and chain\-of\-thought rationales reduce rejection of incorrect answers by 12\.7 and 13\.8 percentage points, respectively\. We call this failure plausibility capture\. Using signal detection theory, we find a significant mean shift in decision criterion toward acceptance, without a clear change in mean discriminability\. Explanations sway judgments across domains, explanation generators, and judging protocols, while tested mitigations offer limited, model\-dependent protection\. Such shifts can inflate performance estimates when judges evaluate answers with explanations\.

## [Maternal thyroid function and subsequent markers of insulin resistance in pregnant women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome](../publications/97fa9dbd9418e58b83d5.md)

Anastasia Trouva; Eszter Vanky; Michael Alvarsson; Jan Calissendorff; Bjørn Olav Åsvold; Dorina Ujvári; Angelica Lindén Hirschberg

Objectives Low maternal free thyroxine \(fT4\) levels have been associated with markers of insulin resistance and gestational diabetes\. Our primary aim was to investigate whether maternal thyroid function was associated with subsequent insulin resistance in pregnant women with polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome \(PMOS, previously known as PCOS\)\. Methods In this post\-hoc analysis of two randomized controlled trials, we used linear regression analyses to examine associations of thyroid stimulating hormone \(TSH\) and fT4 with parameters of metabolic profile \(pre\- and post\-load glucose, fasting insulin and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance \(HOMA\-IR\) in 284 pregnant women with PMOS who were randomized to metformin or placebo in early pregnancy\. Blood samples were drawn at gestational weeks \(gw\) 5 to12, 19, 32 and 36\. An oral glucose tolerance test was performed at inclusion, gw19 and 32\. Results At baseline, the women had a mean body mass index \(BMI\) of 28\.9 and HOMA\-IR 3\.2, and none had overt hypothyroidism\. We found significant inverse associations between the change in TSH during pregnancy and post\-load glucose at gw19, as well as fasting glucose at gw36, i\.e\. the smaller increase in maternal TSH, the higher subsequent maternal glucose levels\. Furthermore, lower maternal fT4 levels were significantly associated with higher subsequent insulin/HOMA\-IR levels, and the change in TSH was also inversely associated with HOMA\-IR at gw32\. All associations were independent of treatment with metformin or placebo\. Conclusions In this exploratory post\-hoc analysis, a smaller maternal TSH increase and lower fT4 levels during pregnancy in overweight women with PMOS are associated with higher subsequent glucose and insulin/HOMA\-IR levels later in pregnancy\.

## [Hypothesis on Emergence and Consciousness Mechanisms of Large Language Models Based on Reciprocal Unit Coupling, Critical Dynamics and Local Entropy Reductio](../publications/980337c580e90842ed0a.md)

chen tiantai

The emergence capability of large language models \(LLMs\) is a core puzzle in the fundamental theories of artificial intelligence\. The mainstream scaling law only describes external phenomena of capability change with model scale and fails to explain the underlying dynamical causes for the jumpwise emergence of emergent behaviors\. This paper proposes an integrated framework: numer ous basic units inside the Transformer network perform nonlinear reciprocal coupling and layer\-wise mutual correction; under the long\-term self\-organization of gradient descent, system parameters are driven into the critical region between order and chaos; during inference forward propagation, continuous mutual constraints among units cancel representation noise and resolve internal contra dictions, achieving local entropy reduction in the representation space and generating self\-consistent high\-order ordered information, which macroscopically manifests as emergent capabilities such as multi\-step reasoning\. This hypothesis integrates three independently observed experimental phe nomena, namely inter\-layer representation correction, critical phase transition at the edge of chaos, and hidden\-state entropy evolution, to construct a complete causal chain\. Meanwhile, it identifies the conceptual boundaries and pending verifiable predictions of this framework, distinguishes dynamical differences between the training and inference phases, and discusses limitations of the hypothesis and subsequent verifiable experimental schemes\.

## [ESTIMATIVA FUTURA DE NOVOS CASOS DE SÍFILIS CONGÊNITA E ADQUIRIDA NO BRASIL ATÉ 2030 A PARTIR DE PREVISÃO DE SÉRIES TEMPORAIS](../publications/9809ed9b2f4a5acfd7ef.md)

Maria Clara Da Silva Maia; Daniela Teixeira Borges; Renata dos Santos Rabello

A sífilis é uma infecção sexualmente transmissível, cuja propagação pode ser também vertical\. Este estudo objetiva estimar novos casos de sífilis adquirida e congênita no Brasil utilizando os modelos Autorregressivo Integrado de Médias Móveis Sazonal \(SARIMA\), de Memória de Curto\-Longo Prazo \(LSTM\) e um modelo híbrido SARIMA\-LSTM\. Foram utilizados dados do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação referentes às notificações mensais entre janeiro de 2014 e junho de 2024\. A validação ocorreu pelas métricas Erro Percentual Absoluto Médio \(MAPE\), Raiz do Erro Quadrático Médio \(RMSE\) e Erro Absoluto Médio \(MAE\)\. A implementação foi em Python\. Nenhuma das séries foram estacionárias pelo teste de Dickey\-Fuller aumentado e ambas tiveram tendência crescente pelo teste de Mann\-Kendall e autocorrelação dos dados pelo teste de Ljung\-Box\. Ambos os modelos tiveram métricas de erro indicando boa adequação e acurácia\. O SARIMA teve desempenho levemente superior ao LSTM tanto para sífilis adquirida quanto para sífilis congênita\. Fazendo a média aritmética entre as previsões \(implementação do modelo híbrido\), as métricas de erro diminuíram ainda mais\. As estimativas futuras indicam continuidade da sífilis como problema de saúde pública\.Portanto, todos os modelos testados mostraram\-se adequados para prever os casos de sífilis adquirida e congênita no Brasil\.

## [APRENDER A APRENDER EN LA ERA DE LA IA: METACOGNICIÓN, AUTORREGULACIÓN Y ESTRATEGIAS DE RECUPERACIÓN PARA PREVENIR LA DEPENDENCIA DE LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL](../publications/980fc4fefef0edc8a069.md)

Christian Cañarte Lino; Alex Roberto Morán Naranjo; Ángel Wladimir Pilco Cajilema; Lizbeth Jacqueline Alarcón Silva

La integración de la inteligencia artificial generativa en educación ha cambiado la forma de buscar información, resolver problemas y producir textos\. Esta transformación ha creado tensión entre el apoyo al aprendizaje y la posible externalización de procesos cognitivos\. Esta revisión sistemática analizó la relación entre metacognición, autorregulación, práctica de recuperación y patrones de dependencia cognitiva en el aprendizaje mediado por inteligencia artificial\. Se siguió las directrices PRISMA 2020 y PRISMA\-S, y se realizaron búsquedas en las bases de datos Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink y PsycINFO, complementadas con una búsqueda en Google Scholar\. La última búsqueda se realizó el 10 de septiembre de 2026, y se incluyeron artículos desde enero de 2020 hasta septiembre de 2026\. Las bases de datos proporcionaron 1\.247 resultados, y la búsqueda en Google Scholar arrojó otros 89 resultados\. A continuación, se excluyeron los duplicados y se evaluaron los criterios de elegibilidad, y se calcularon que 7 estudios fueron artículos primarios y 10 documentos de investigación secundaria y de síntesis, para un total de 17 documentos\. De los siete estudios primarios, dos eran ensayos aleatorios publicados en revistas científicas, uno era un ensayo aleatorio cuyo contenido circulaba en forma de preprint no revisado por pares, tres eran estudios mixtos y uno era un estudio transversal de tipo encuesta\. Los estudios identifican factores como el uso no optimizado de la IA, lo que conducía a menores resultados a largo plazo en comparación con la asistencia al aprendizaje sin IA, el aumento de la externalización cognitiva y una mayor dependencia, aunque estas variables dependían del contexto y de las instrucciones\. Algunos estudios mencionan la metacognición y la autorregulación como factores explicativos de las diferencias detectadas en el uso de la IA\. La «secuencia de recuperación primero, asistencia de la IA a continuación, verificación y pensamiento» fue la hipótesis operativa deducida de la revisión de la literatura\. En resumen, en determinados marcos pedagógicos, el uso de la IA puede estar condicionado para fomentar el aprendizaje autónomo\.

## [Confidence without consensus? Human versus AI abstracts in urology](../publications/98157127e49917ed9eb3.md)

Sholem Hack; Shlomo Resnik; Yoram Dekel; Shlomi Moshe; Daniel Noy; Mohammad Shalabi; Ari Frajewicki; Omri Zonenfeld; Sobhi Khoury; Israel Benzekry; Yazeed Barghouthy; Maharan Kabha

OBJECTIVE: This study asked whether urologists can tell human\-written abstracts apart from artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-written abstracts when both describe the same study, and whether the answer depends on which AI model did the writing\. METHODS: Fifteen published urology studies were selected\. For each study, the original human\-written abstract was paired with three AI\-written abstracts covering the same material, produced by Claude Sonnet 4\.6, GPT\-5\.5, and Gemini 3 Flash using identical instructions and each model&\#x27;s ordinary consumer settings\. Because all four versions described the same study, the underlying data were held constant, and the versions differed in how that material was written and presented\. The resulting 60 abstracts were stripped of identifying information, and eight urologists read all of them without knowing which was which \(480 judgments in total\)\. For each abstract, reviewers stated whether they believed it was written by a human or by AI, rated how confident they were in that judgment, and rated the abstract&\#x27;s quality and credibility on 5\-point scales\. RESULTS: Reviewers correctly identified AI\-written abstracts 49\.3% of the time, approximately 50%, compared with 62\.4% for human\-written abstracts \(p = \.011\)\. Results depended heavily on which model wrote the text \(p = \.003\)\. Abstracts written by Claude were recognized as AI only 40\.0% of the time, significantly less often than human abstracts were correctly identified \(p = \.003\) and less often than GPT abstracts \(56\.8%, p = \.038\); Gemini fell between the two at 50\.9%\. Quality ratings differed only for GPT, which scored lower than human abstracts \(p = \.046; omnibus p = \.030\); credibility ratings did not differ between sources at all \(p = \.577\)\. Reviewers who felt confident were no more likely to be correct \(p = \.749\), and reviewers seldom agreed with one another about which abstracts were AI\-written \(Fleiss&\#x27; κ = \-0\.009\)\. CONCLUSION: Urologists could not reliably recognize AI\-written urology abstracts, and the difficulty came mainly from one model rather than from AI writing in general\. How good an abstract appeared had little to do with whether its authorship was correctly identified, and neither reviewer confidence nor agreement between reviewers gave any warning\. Reading alone is therefore not a dependable way to detect undisclosed AI authorship\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL, DOCUMENTAÇÃO PEDAGÓGICA E EDUCAÇÃO ESPECIAL INCLUSIVA](../publications/9842643d47b6738da892.md)

Luiz Fernando Marques dos Santos; Marcilene Moreira Donadoni

This article analyzes the possibilities and limits of Artificial Intelligence in organizing pedagogical evidence aimed at monitoring the learning pathways of students who are the target audience of Special Education\. It develops a bibliographic and theoretical\-conceptual study grounded in research on Artificial Intelligence and education, pedagogical documentation, mediating assessment, and Inclusive Special Education\. It argues that Artificial Intelligence can contribute to systematizing records, integrating different sources of information, and expanding institutional pedagogical memory, but it cannot replace the ethical, relational, and interpretive processes carried out by teachers and pedagogical coordinators\. The analysis indicates that data become evidence only when contextualized and interpreted in light of school experiences\. It concludes that the contribution of Artificial Intelligence to democratic and inclusive education depends on its articulation with pedagogical documentation and human decisions committed to students’ singularities and to ensuring the right to learn\.

## [Hemşirelik Esasları: İnsan, Bakım ve Bilim](../publications/985852dd073b59f78e99.md)



Hemşirelik, bilimsel bilgi ile insani değerlerin bütünleştiği, bireyin yaşamına dokunan ve sürekli gelişen profesyonel bir sağlık disiplinidir\. Hemşirelik bakımının temelinde insanı bütüncül bir yaklaşımla anlamak, bireysel gereksinimlerini belirlemek ve kanıta dayalı uygulamalarla güvenli, nitelikli ve etik bakım sunmak yer almaktadır\. Hemşirelik Esasları: İnsan, Bakım ve Bilim adlı bu kitap, hemşirelik disiplininin temel felsefesini çağdaş bilimsel gelişmelerle buluşturarak bakımın insani, bilimsel ve uygulamaya yönelik boyutlarını bütüncül bir bakış açısıyla ele almaktadır\. Hemşirelik bakımının farklı klinik ortamlardaki yansımalarını, bireyselleştirilmiş bakım yaklaşımlarını, teknolojik dönüşümün hemşire\-hasta ilişkisine etkilerini ve sağlık hizmetlerinde sürdürülebilirlik anlayışını güncel bilimsel bilgiler ışığında değerlendirmektedir\. Kitapta, bakımın yalnızca teknik becerilerden oluşmadığı; klinik karar verme, eleştirel düşünme, etik duyarlılık, etkili iletişim, hasta güvenliği ve profesyonel sorumluluk gibi birbirini tamamlayan bileşenleri içerdiği vurgulanmaktadır\. Dijital sağlık teknolojileri, yenilikçi bakım uygulamaları ve çevre dostu sağlık hizmetleri gibi güncel konular, hemşireliğin değişen ve gelişen rolü çerçevesinde ele alınmaktadır\. Hemşirelik öğrencileri, akademisyenler, klinisyen hemşireler ve sağlık alanındaki araştırmacılar için bilimsel bir başvuru kaynağı olması amaçlanan bu eser, kuramsal bilgi ile klinik uygulama arasında güçlü bir bağ kurulmasına katkı sunmayı hedeflemektedir\. Hemşirelik Esasları: İnsan, Bakım ve Bilim, insanı merkeze alan, bilimden güç alan ve bakımın değerini önceleyen hemşirelik anlayışını geleceğe taşıma çabasının bir ürünüdür\.

## [Design and Evaluation of the Battery Thermal Management System for Electric Vehicles Under Complex Environmental Conditions](../publications/9864dc5e6dff2dcb797f.md)

Cong\-Trang Nguyen; Hoang An Nguyen; Thanh Hung Vu; Anh Khoa Nguyen

This research develops a cooling system controller for the battery thermal management system \(BTMS\) of electric vehicles using the proportional\-integral\-derivative \(PID\) technique, replacing the traditional relay switching mechanism which is commonly used in existing construction\. The BTMS is designed to include some main components: an electronic control circuit, a coolant re\-circulation pump, temperature sensors, a coolant piping system, and coolant storage tank\. Cooling liquid used is a mixture of water and ethylene glycol \(EG\) in a 5:5 ratio\. This research evaluates the efficiency of integrating a PID controller into the BTMS under three scenarios, consisting of ambient temperature 25 °C \(normal\), 45 °C \(hot\), and 10 °C \(cold\), respectively\. The response capability of the system is tested with initial battery temperatures of 30 °C, 45 °C and 55 °C, respectively\. The simulation results demonstrate that the system satisfies the reliability by maintaining the set temperature in every scenario, while the energy consumption is different\. The research is also compared with recent published studies, thereby enhancing its scientific competitiveness\. These findings highlight the essential role of the designed controller, which is flexible and sustainable, confirming the effective thermal management and maintaining optimal battery efficiency under all real\-world driving conditions\.

## [THE BIO\-LEGAL INTELLIGENCE FRAMEWORK FROM NEURONS TO CONSTITUTIONS: A Unified Theory of Neurobiological, Sociological, and Philosophical Foundations of Legal Systems](../publications/987bcb1d61894f62f301.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The Bio\-Legal Intelligence Framework: From Neurons to Constitutions by Dr\. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El\-Rakhawi \(DOI: 10\.5281/zenodo\.23458534\) establishes Bio\-Legal Intelligence as a groundbreaking academic field integrating neuroscience, evolutionary biology, sociology, philosophy, and legal theory\. The central thesis posits that law functions as the collective nervous system of society—constitutions as central processors, laws as neural pathways, justice as homeostatic balance, and legal evolution as cultural biological evolution\. The framework unfolds through four pillars: \(1\) Biological Foundations of Legal Consciousness, exploring the moral brain, evolutionary justice origins, and social neuroscience of law; \(2\) Law as Bio\-Social Living System, analyzing legal systems as collective neural networks with homeostasis, plasticity, and immune functions; \(3\) Bio\-Philosophy of Law, grounding natural rights in evolved biological needs and examining evolutionary justice; \(4\) Integration and Applications, proposing bio\-constitutional design principles, bio\-legal education reform, and future civilization vision\. The book introduces novel concepts including legal homeostasis, legal immunity, legal plasticity, memetic propagation of norms, and biological foundations of rights\. It provides transformative applications for constitutional design, legal education, judicial decision\-making, and addressing 21st\-century challenges including climate change, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and global inequality\. This foundational treatise offers a unified theoretical framework connecting individual neural processes to collective legal institutions, providing both rigorous scholarship and practical guidance for creating legal systems that serve human flourishing based on evolved needs and capacities\. The work is protected under international copyright law and available for academic citation across multiple formats \(APA, Chicago, MLA, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver\)\.

## [Immigrant earnings and labour\-market positioning in a transforming digital labour market: evidence from Canada, 1971–2021](../publications/9884726e66d3ed4395c0.md)

Xingfei Liu; Saba Ranjbar; Tony Fang; Husame Doganay; Arthur Sweetman

Purpose This paper examines immigrant earnings trajectories and labour\-market positioning across industries and employment arrangements in six Canadian provinces, as well as how industry patterns relate to digital intensity, telework feasibility, and productivity\-relevant allocation\. Design/methodology/approach Canadian Census microdata, 1971–2021 compare immigrant and native\-born earnings across ten arrival cohorts by gender and age at arrival\. For two recent cohorts, an earnings\-based positioning measure combines industry mean annual earnings with full\-time or part\-time status multinomial\-logit average marginal effects are estimated\. The study also maps 2021 industry employment shares to external digital\-intensity and telework\-feasibility classifications\. Individual productivity, artificial\-intelligence \(AI\) adoption, Information and Communications Technology use, and remote\-work uptake are not observed\. Findings Entry earnings gaps and incomplete cohort convergence persist, especially among women and recent cohorts\. Across the two positioning cohorts, immigrants are less likely than comparable native\-born workers to hold full\-time jobs in higher\-earnings industries; gaps vary by source region and do not uniformly narrow\. Education is associated with better positioning but does not eliminate gaps Immigrant employment is more concentrated in many digitally intensive categories but less concentrated in several higher\-earnings, high\-telework\-feasibility industries digital intensity is not systematically related to immigrant employment shares\. Originality/value The paper combines five decades of earnings evidence across ten cohorts with a two\-cohort positioning measure and descriptive digital and telework mapping\. It complements individual\-level careers research by identifying structural differences in opportunity access with possible, unmeasured productivity implications\.

## [Students Use of Generative AI Models for Health Information Seeking: Lessons from a Developing Country in Africa](../publications/9898fede1ee0596ed5ed.md)

Richard Ndubuisi C\. Ugwuanyi; Yakubu Azaki Jibrin; Bolaji David Oladokun; Esther David Josiah Okai; Bridget Enuwa Abah

This study investigated students’ use of generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) models for health information seeking in Nigeria\. A descriptive cross\-sectional survey design was adopted\. Data were collected through an online questionnaire administered to students in selected universities across the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria\. A total of 308 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics\. The findings revealed that ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Claude were the most widely used generative AI models for health information seeking\. Students frequently used AI tools for obtaining immediate health information, understanding diseases and symptoms, supporting academic research, and seeking mental health and wellness information\. Convenience, ease of use, quick access to information, and free availability significantly influenced usage\. Although respondents moderately trusted AI\-generated health information, they emphasized the need to verify such information with healthcare professionals because of concerns about misinformation, contradictory responses, and privacy risks\. The study further revealed that demographic variables had no significant influence on students’ use of generative AI models\. The study concluded that generative AI models have become important health information tools among students despite associated credibility and technological challenges\. The study recommended AI literacy programs, information verification training, ethical AI policies, and improved internet infrastructure in Nigerian universities\.

## [The Trust Paradox of AI\-Generated Content Transparency: Impulse Buying from the Perspective of Generative Agents](../publications/989b2bc6c344c4a2f5d6.md)

Xi Cheng

As generative artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in digital e\-commerce environments, the transparency labeling of AI\-generated content has emerged as a crucial institutional variable in modern platform governance\. Drawing upon the established information–trust–behavior theoretical logic, this study conducted a large\-scale AI\-agent simulation, comprising 900 distinct purchase decisions executed by large language model agents, to systematically test how disclosure labeling affects simulated consumer trust and simulated impulse buying intention\. Furthermore, the research investigated whether trust acts as a mediating mechanism and whether consumer involvement moderates these relationships\. Rigorous model\-rationality validation confirmed that the agent decisions consistently conformed to their assigned behavioral personalities and rational economic logic\. The empirical results demonstrated that disclosure labeling significantly suppressed both simulated trust and impulse buying intention\. Additionally, simulated trust positively predicted impulse intention, revealing a negative indirect association within the disclosure–impulse behavioral link\. Notably, consumer involvement moderated the trust–impulse path during the primary simulation phase, although this moderating effect was not replicated in the cross\-model robustness check\. Ultimately, these comprehensive findings reveal the critical boundary conditions of the institutional logic surrounding the exchange of transparency for trust\. The study provides robust, simulation\-based empirical evidence for the development of AI\-content labeling policies and offers valuable insights for optimizing platform information governance strategies in the digital economy\.

## [Pengaruh Voluntary Disclosure, Income Smoothing dan Pertumbuhan Laba Terhadap Kualitas Laba](../publications/989cceefbcb5a1068db1.md)

Widya Eka Utami; Abdullah Mubarok

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh voluntary disclosure, income smoothing, dan pertumbuhan laba terhadap kualitas laba\. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari 27 perusahaan sektor consumer non\-cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia \(BEI\) periode 2020–2024, yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling\. Data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan tahunan dianalisis menggunakan EViews 12 dengan Common Effect Model \(CEM\) sebagai model terbaik\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial, voluntary disclosure dan income smoothing tidak berpengaruh terhadap kualitas laba, sedangkan pertumbuhan laba berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kualitas laba\. Namun secara simultan, ketiga variabel independen tersebut berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kualitas laba\. This study aims to analyze the effect of voluntary disclosure, income smoothing, and earnings growth on earnings quality\. The research sample consists of 27 consumer non\-cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange \(IDX\) during the 2020–2024 period, selected using a purposive sampling technique\. Secondary data in the form of annual financial statements were analyzed using EViews 12, with the Common Effect Model \(CEM\) identified as the best\-fit model\. The results indicate that partially, voluntary disclosure and income smoothing have no significant effect on earnings quality, whereas earnings growth has a significant effect on earnings quality\. However, simultaneously, voluntary disclosure, income smoothing, and earnings growth significantly affect earnings quality\.

## [Anisotropic Representation Dynamics in Transformers](../publications/989cf6d201edcc8d26dd.md)

Nguyen Do; My T\. Thai

Small differences between internal representations can shrink or grow as they pass through a Transformer layer, affecting how information is preserved and how sensitive the model is to perturbations\. Yet it remains unclear when changes in attention weights can turn a representation difference that would otherwise shrink into one that grows\. We develop a \\textbf\{Mixture\-Gated Theory of Anisotropic Representation Dynamics\} that separates self\-attention into value transport, query gating, and key gating\. Our analysis reveals how the geometry of attended representations constrains gating and how interactions between these mechanisms can reverse contraction induced by value transport\. We formalize this phenomenon as gating\-induced regime switching, where a representation difference contracts under fixed attention routing but expands under full attention\. We derive a necessary and sufficient spectral criterion that certifies the existence or absence of switching and identifies switching directions without exhaustive search\. Beyond existence, our theory characterizes maximum relative switching strength, certifies the severity of contraction that gating can overcome, and determines the largest dimension of a subspace in which every nonzero direction switches\. Experiments across four Transformer architectures validate these predictions through analytical and finite\-forward comparisons, revealing distinct and joint query\-\-key gating mechanisms and nontrivial switching subspaces\. Our results provide a mechanistic and spectral understanding of how attention routing can alter local representation dynamics\.

## [AI for Everyone: Designing an Introductory AI Course Across Disciplines](../publications/98aed7cd02432a1f1dfd.md)

Jesse J\. Fitts; Waleed Faris

As artificial intelligence reshapes virtually every field, universities face a growing imperative to ensure AI literacy is not reserved for computer science majors alone\. This panel presents the collaborative design of an introductory AI course built for undergraduate general education — one that serves students across disciplines, regardless of technical background\. Two co\-designers will share the story of building the course from complementary angles\. The first presenter will address the technical foundation of the curriculum: how core AI concepts such as machine learning, data, and algorithms were translated into accessible, hands\-on learning experiences for non\-specialist students\. The second presenter will explore the philosophical framework woven throughout the course — examining questions of ethics, agency, bias, and what it means to be human in an age of intelligent machines\. The panelists will discuss how technical and philosophical threads were intentionally integrated rather than siloed, creating a course where students not only understand how AI works, but are equipped to think critically about why it matters\. Attendees will come away with practical insights on curriculum structure, cross\-disciplinary collaboration, and strategies for making AI education inclusive for students from diverse academic and experiential backgrounds\. This session is designed for faculty, instructional designers, and administrators interested in developing or expanding AI literacy offerings at their institutions\.

## [When Can You Trust an Agent&\#x27;s Own Verifier? Stress\-Testing Counterfactual Rationale Verification Under Search Pressure and Oracle Access](../publications/98b444d4fc756bd80b40.md)

Jonghyun Lee; Moonsu Kim; Sunghwan Park

Automated agent design increasingly trusts a single score to decide whether a change is an improvement \-\- but a score optimized aggressively enough ceases to measure what it was meant to\. When an agent also explains its design, that explanation is a second signal we can check without human labels: negate each stated claim, re\-run, and observe whether performance drops\. We ask whether such a verifier stays reliable once an agent optimizes against it\. Our contribution is not a new verifier but a way to stress\-test one: a pressure ratio $ρ$ measuring how much the verifier steers the agent&\#x27;s search, and four falsifiable probes covering four failure modes \-\- giving no signal, being too weak to matter, being gamed by stating fewer claims, and being queried before the agent commits\. We apply the test to our own verifier, the Rationale Consistency Score \(RCS\), inside an LLM agent that designs machine\-learning pipelines, with one generator model, six tasks, and three seeds\. First, in our prior configuration the verifier barely affects the search objective \($ρ\\ll 1$\), partly because of an accuracy gate, so its robustness had not been tested; it still shapes the reported artifact through a final\-selection tie\-break that $ρ$ does not register\. Second, a capability control shows the agent shortens its claim lists when instructed, yet search does not, even at $ρ$ over 100 times the prior level; since feedback omits claim volume and horizons are short, this null result is largely structural rather than evidence of robustness\. Third, when the agent can probe the verifier before committing, it keeps claims that pass while held\-out faithfulness falls \-\- a decline invisible to in\-loop metrics, though partly confounded by how RCS scores small pipelines\. We offer these as preliminary evidence and propose a reporting standard: audit a verifier with $ρ$ and these probes before trusting it\.

## [Isolation, Phenotypic Screening, and Extracellular Serotonin\-Like Immunoreactivity of Presumptive Lactic Acid Bacteria from Butterfly Pea Flower \(Clitoria ternatea L\.\) Kombucha](../publications/98b69bee6b3e64093949.md)

Rafeyfa Alya Mukhbita; Desi Purwaningsih; Isniani Ramdhani; Dara Juliana

Background: Major depressive disorder is a leading cause of disability, and interest in the microbiota\-gut\-brain axis has stimulated bioprospecting of food\-derived lactic acid bacteria \(LAB\) for neuroactive metabolite production\. Objective: To isolate and phenotypically screen acidogenic bacteria from butterfly pea flower \(Clitoria ternatea L\.\) kombucha and to evaluate their cell\-free supernatants for extracellular serotonin\-like immunoreactivity\. Methods: Colonies were isolated from day\-14 kombucha on MRS agar supplemented with 1\.0% CaCO3 and characterised by Gram staining, catalase testing and broth acidification in MRS broth \(24 h, 37 °C\)\. Serotonin\-like immunoreactivity in cell\-free supernatants was quantified by a competitive enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay \(ELISA\) calibrated with a four\-parameter logistic \(4\-PL\) model\. Results: Three isolates \(Isolates 3, 6 and 8\) were presumptive LAB \(Gram\-positive, catalase\-negative bacilli\), dissolved CaCO3 \(clear zones 14\.8–18\.4 mm\) and reduced broth pH from 7\.00 to 3\.94–4\.15\. The 4\-PL model returned R2 = 0\.9993 and back\-calculated the standards to within 0\.1% of nominal\. Cell\-free supernatants gave serotonin\-like immunoreactivity averaging 18\.11 ± 4\.54 ng/mL \(Isolate 3 highest, 23\.13 ng/mL\) versus 1\.28 ± 0\.67 ng/mL in sterile media \(exploratory Welch&\#x27;s t = 6\.34, df = 2\.09, p = 0\.022\)\. Conclusion: Presumptive lactic acid bacteria from butterfly pea flower kombucha yielded a measurable serotonin\-like immunoreactivity signal in culture broth\. These preliminary in vitro findings warrant 16S rRNA gene sequencing, chromatographic confirmation of analyte identity \(HPLC/LC\-MS\) and in vivo evaluation\.

## [Analysis of nine years of safety monitoring data from a roller\-compacted concrete gravity dam in a high\-altitude cold region](../publications/98ba684bce9d02ab52cf.md)

Ying Li; Jiwei Zhao; Yongshuai Yan; Xiaolei Zhang; ZHU Zhaohui; Feng Zhang

Long\-term monitoring records from roller\-compacted concrete \(RCC\) gravity dams in cold regions are scarce, although freeze–thaw cycling and large seasonal temperature ranges act there together with hydrostatic loading\. This study analyzes 9\.1 years of daily records \(2016–2025\) from 190 instruments on a 71 m RCC gravity dam in Xinjiang, China\. Correlations are reported with seasonality controls and a significance criterion that allows for serial correlation, and the monitored changes are related to the sliding stability of the dam\. Maximum downstream displacement is 18\.71 mm\. Its seasonality\-controlled association with reservoir level is moderate \(partial r = 0\.26–0\.58\), and its multi\-year baseline, after rising by about 3–4 mm over 2017–2021, has not risen since\. Foundation uplift head stays below the reservoir level, decreases downstream and shows no upward trend, and no monitored change points to reduced sliding stability\. Concrete strain follows local concrete temperature \(raw r = 0\.82–0\.94\)\. Stresses estimated with a code\-specified modulus, no material tests being available, are order\-of\-magnitude values \(1\.1–3\.7 MPa compression\), and one tensile strain excursion is flagged for inspection\. The annual response is reversible, and no monitored quantity shows cumulative deterioration; surface freeze–thaw damage is beyond the reach of the embedded instruments\.

## [Prediction of pregnancy following transfer of in‐vitro produced embryos using recipient health records, accelerometer sensors and meteorological data in Australian dairy cows](../publications/98c206f44d1af911dfb4.md)

AM Johnston; MD Greene; Rory P\. Nevard; John K\. House; Sam M\. Rowe

Embryo transfer \(ET\) in dairy cattle has long been used for the dissemination of elite genetics\. However, achieving consistently high pregnancy rates remains a major challenge, particularly in high\-producing lactating dairy cows receiving in\-vitro produced \(IVP\) embryos\. We hypothesised that recipient selection and ET program timing could be optimised using individual items of recipient and meteorological data that are routinely available on dairy farms\. To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an observational study that explored associations between recipient characteristics, health events, sensor\-derived activity alerts, meteorological variables and their ability to predict successful pregnancy following ET \(P/ET\) in an on\-farm IVP embryo program\. Cow health data and ear tag health sensor alerts from a commercial dairy herd in southern Australia were used to compile a retrospective dataset of 5770 embryo transfers \(ETs\) in 4681 recipients\. Meteorological records from two nearby weather stations were used to calculate temperature humidity index \(THI\)\. Univariable generalised linear models were used to test associations between predictors and P/ET\. Outputs from models included risk differences \(RD\), P\-values, 95% confidence intervals and area under the curve \(AUC\)\. Population RD were calculated using tabular methods\. Recipient parity, days in milk \(DIM\), calving interval, metritis events and &\#x27;very sick&\#x27; ear\-tag sensor alerts were associated with P/ET, as were temperature and THI variables\. Area under the curve values were close to 0\.50 \(range 0\.50\-0\.55\) and population RD values from many exposure variables were close to 0, indicating that optimising the ET program using individual variables as done in this study, under the conditions in this herd may have limited impact on the overall P/ET\. Therefore, further research is needed to evaluate other methodologies to predict P/ET\. Furthermore, future studies should incorporate non\-recipient factors, such as embryo quality\. It is unclear if the associations observed in this study are due to causal relationships; therefore, we recommend that observational and intervention studies be conducted to verify this\.

## [A Multiphysics Model of Magnetically Enhanced ATP Hydrolysis in Ferromagnetic Nanosystems](../publications/98c330e7cdd864f6e273.md)

Paata J\. Kervalishvili

This study develops a multiphysics framework for evaluating whether alternating magnetic fields \(AMF\) applied to Fe₃O₄ and MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles can modify ATP hydrolysis through thermal, mechanical, and ion\-mediated pathways\. Rather than assigning a single phenomenological magnetic activation\-energy reduction to all effects, the model starts from Arrhenius/Eyring kinetics and derives the observed rate change as the sum of a temperature\-dependent contribution and explicitly defined non\-thermal perturbations\. The thermal term is constrained by the measured temperature history and nanoparticle specific absorption rate \(SAR\); the mechanical term is related to magnetic torque, hydrodynamic damping, and experimentally measurable particle motion; and the catalytic term is expressed through independently measurable Fe²⁺/Mn²⁺ concentrations and dose\-response parameters\. The available experimental observations reported in the original manuscript—2\.5–3\-fold enhancement of non\-enzymatic hydrolysis under nanoparticle/AMF conditions, approximately 40% enhancement of Na⁺/K⁺\-ATPase activity under stated isothermal conditions, and Raman/FTIR changes in phosphate\-associated bands—are retained, but their interpretation is deliberately narrowed\. In particular, the present data support rate enhancement under specified conditions and are consistent with multiple mechanisms; they do not, by themselves, establish a unique mechanical mechanism, nanoscale temperature gradients, or synergistic coupling\. A mechanism\-separation experimental matrix is therefore defined, together with quantitative spectroscopic observables and statistical requirements\.

## [Votsis, Ioannis: Science with Artificially Intelligent Agents: The Case of Gerrymandered Hypotheses](../publications/98c6d5b5ace581ec8047.md)



Barring some civilisation\-ending natural or man\-made catastrophe, future scientists will likely incorporate fully fledged artificially intelligent agents in their ranks\. Their tasks will include the conjecturing, extending and testing of hypotheses\. At present human scientists have a number of methods to help them carry out those tasks\. These range from the well\-articulated, formal and unexceptional rules to the semi\-articulated rules\-of\-thumb and intuitive hunches\. If we are to hand over at least some of the aforementioned tasks to artificially intelligent agents, we need to find ways to make explicit and ultimately formal, not to mention computable, the more obscure of the methods that scientists currently employ with some measure of success in their inquiries\. The focus of this talk is a problem for which the available solutions are at best semi\-articulated and far from perfect\. It concerns the question of how to conjecture new hypotheses or extend existing ones such that they do not save phenomena in gerrymandered or ad hoc ways\. This talk puts forward a fully articulated formal solution to this problem by specifying what it is about the internal constitution of the content of a hypothesis that makes it gerrymandered or ad hoc\. In doing so, it helps prepare the ground for the delegation of a full gamut of investigative duties to the artificially intelligent scientists of the future \(direct link \)

## [Nutritional, trace element and heavy metal stability in human milk during standard milk bank processing\.](../publications/98d4a84c4789fc333c5b.md)

Ana Rubio\-Granda; Marta Suárez; Leire Cardo González; Clara González\-López; María Teresa Peláez\-Nava; Nodelina Arias\-García; Belén Prieto\-García; Gonzalo Solís Sánchez

Abstract Human milk \(HM\) is the optimal source of nutrition for neonates; however, mothers of preterm infants may experience insufficient milk production\. Donor HM from human milk banks \(HMB\) undergoes freezing and Holder pasteurisation \(HoP\) to ensure safety, but these processes can alter nutrient and mineral composition\. Heavy metals in HM also require monitoring due to neonatal vulnerability\. We analysed eighty\-eight HM samples from twenty\-two donors at four processing stages: fresh, frozen at –20°C, post\-HoP and frozen at –80°C\. Macronutrients were measured using a MIRIS® HM analyser\. Cu, Zn, Se, iodine, As, Cd, Hg and Pb were quantified via ICP\-MS\. Statistical analyses included repeated\-measures ANOVA and paired t tests\. Macronutrient concentrations remained largely stable across processing stages\. Cu and iodine exhibited significant stage\-specific reductions, particularly following HoP and –20°C freezing \( p &lt; 0·05\)\. Se and Zn were minimally affected\. Hg and As were detectable in some samples but remained below safety thresholds, while Cd and Pb were undetectable at all stages\. Notably, carbohydrate levels increased after –80°C freezing, likely due to sample homogenisation variability\. Routine HMB processing effectively preserves the nutritional profile of HM while ensuring microbiological safety\. Stage\-dependent reductions in Cu and iodine suggest that careful monitoring is warranted, especially for preterm infants\. Importantly, heavy metal contamination was negligible, confirming the safety of donor HM for neonatal feeding\.

## [Artificial Intelligence dalam Pembelajaran PAI :Urgensi Guru Sebagai Verifikator Pemahaman Keagamaan](../publications/98d677e9cbd300251de4.md)

Dita Dzata Mirrota

The development of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in the field of education has brought about significant changes in the learning process, including in Islamic Religious Education \(IRE\)\. Generative AI enables students to access religious information quickly and easily; however, it also poses challenges regarding the validity and accuracy of religious understanding\. This study aims to analyze the use of AI in PAI learning and to examine the urgency of the teacher’s role as a verifier of religious understanding in the digital age\. This study employs a qualitative approach using field research methods, including interviews, observations, and documentation, conducted at Primaganda High School in Jombang\. The results of the study indicate that AI has been used as an alternative learning resource by students; however, it has the potential to lead to misunderstandings if not accompanied by teacher guidance\. Islamic Education teachers play a strategic role as verifiers who ensure the accuracy of religious information by referring to authoritative Islamic sources such as the Qur’an, hadith, and the opinions of Islamic scholars\. In addition, teachers also play a role in guiding religious digital literacy and instilling a spirit of tabayyun in filtering information\. Thus, AI is positioned as a learning aid, while teachers remain the primary actors in maintaining the validity of students’ religious understanding\. This study emphasizes that the integration of AI into Islamic Education must remain grounded in Islamic values and the strengthening of teachers’ pedagogical roles\.

## [An evidence\-informed fine\-tuning framework for traceable generative redesign of architectural heritage ornaments](../publications/98fc68b3a42949dc043e.md)

Jiale Zhang; Hanbin Luo; Jie Xu

Generative heritage redesign requires more than visually plausible synthesis: documented evidence must become computable conditions that guide, constrain and evaluate outputs\. This study proposes an evidence\-informed fine\-tuning framework for heritage ornament redesign\. The framework incorporates an evidence\-to\-conditioning translation layer that converts various source\-audited evidence into ontology\-linked minimal semantic units \(MSUs\), structured prompt fields, exclusion fields, and relation\-check configurations\. A representational five\-civilisation corpus is created to support controlled vocabulary, MSU, and relation construction, while validation uses two structurally contrasting ornament families: Chinese eave tiles and Mesopotamian frieze ornaments\. Across 700 outputs, the proposed pipeline achieved an expert\-rated mean of 4\.66, 0\.982 SSIM and 0\.041 LPIPS with 1\.6% \(14\.0 M\) trainable parameters of the base model and 2\.5 h total training time, outperforming selected baselines\. It is shown to support traceable plausible redesign within explicit evidence, relation, and expert\-evaluation boundaries\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI DOCTRINE OF COGNITIVE MANAGEMENT A Unified Framework for Business Excellence in the Age of Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Transformation](../publications/98fde4707c7996fc973a.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

&quot;The El\-Rakhawi Doctrine of Cognitive Management&quot; presents a revolutionary paradigm shift for 21st\-century business, transitioning organizations from mechanistic machines to dynamic cognitive ecosystems\. Authored by Dr\. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El\-Rakhawi, this treatise introduces the &quot;Master Equation of Cognitive Reality&quot; as a rigorous analogical model to quantify organizational health, balancing collective alignment, cognitive sovereignty, causal information flow, and thermodynamic sustainability\. The book addresses leadership in the BANI \(Brittle, Anxious, Non\-linear, Incomprehensible\) world, advocating for epistemic humility and topological safety\. It redefines AI as a cognitive extension requiring strict ethical governance, and applies behavioral economics to debias decision\-making\. It provides actionable frameworks for managing hybrid workforces, building antifragile supply chains, implementing ESG as a topological safety barrier, and fostering ethical marketing\. Ultimately, this doctrine offers a unified, mathematically grounded blueprint for business excellence, ensuring organizations thrive through continuous adaptation and an unwavering commitment to human dignity in the cognitive age\.

## [Bringing the Hikayat Hang Tuah into Digital Learning: Student Perceptions of AI\-Assisted Animated Videos](../publications/9926e9b2fee3e7a80a55.md)

Nyayu Aisya Shafira; Nurhayati Nurhayati; Zahra Alwi

The utilization of Artificial Intelligence in developing learning media offers opportunities to present classic literary works in audiovisual formats that align better with the characteristics of digital learning\. The aim of this study was to analyze the perceptions of tenth\-grade students regarding an AI\-assisted animated video of Hikayat Hang Tuah \(HHT\) as a learning medium for Indonesian language studies\. A quantitative approach with a survey design was employed\. The study involved 310 tenth\-grade high school students in Palembang City\. Data were collected using a Likert\-scale questionnaire comprising 18 statements across five aspects: visual quality, storytelling, ease of comprehension, learning interest, and perceived benefits\. The instrument underwent content validation by three experts \(Aiken’s V coefficient: 0\.778–1\.000\) and a reliability test with 30 students \(Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient: 0\.906\)\. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, with a positive perception threshold set at ≥62\.5%\. The results indicate that all perception statements fell within the positive range, with scores between 81% and 87%\. The highest score was recorded for the statement regarding the visual comfort of the video&\#x27;s colors and illustrations, while the lowest score related to students&\#x27; willingness to use AI\-assisted animated videos in their studies; nevertheless, even the lowest score exceeded the positive perception threshold\. Thus, the AI\-assisted animated video of HHT was positively received by students and serves as a viable alternative medium for teaching hikayat \(traditional Malay tales\)\. These findings reflect student perceptions of the medium and do not demonstrate its experimental effectiveness regarding learning outcomes\.

## [Assessment of Cybersecurity Risks in the Logistics Sector Using Fuzzy AHP Methodology](../publications/992b482651919f82905c.md)

Ömer Cengîz

Cybersecurity is the sum of processes, policies, and technical measures applied against threats to information and communication infrastructure\. With the digital transformation movements across all sectors, the importance of cybersecurity is increasing day by day\. The aim of this study is to identify the cybersecurity risks arising in the intensive use of digital technologies in logistics operations and to determine the importance of these risks\. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to identify cybersecurity risks in logistics\. Eight cybersecurity risk criteria were validated based on expert opinions\. The Fuzzy AHP method was used to determine the importance levels of the identified risks\. To meet the criteria, an adjustment formula with a 1\-7 Saaty view was prepared and developed by five IT specialists working in the logistics sector\. The collected data was combined and analyzed using transformed matrices\. As a result of the analyses, an importance ranking was obtained for the 8 criteria\. According to the research, the top three cybersecurity risks are: Ransomware Attack Risk, Risks Arising from Supply Chain Stakeholders, and Attack Risks on Customs and Port Systems\. The sum of the importance levels of these three risks is approximately 65%\.

## [Deviant Behaviours in Flood Risk Management: A Novel Typology](../publications/992d43dc1b82b55803ee.md)

Edmund C\. Penning‐Rowsell; Thomas Thaler

ABSTRACT Flooding has become an increasing threat across the globe and risk is likely to rise in the coming decades\. In this context, individuals and communities are expected to assume certain tasks and responsibilities, including following the rules and guidance of flood risk management \(FRM\) agencies\. However, such collaboration does not always align seamlessly and may instead involve what we term deviant behaviour\. Individuals or groups may act in ways that deviate from the expectations or aspirations of the state or the majority of society, with negative consequences\. This paper suggests a typology of such deviant behaviours, with examples occurring before, during or after a flood event\. The typology encompasses different forms of behaviours, ranging from the inappropriate and uncooperative to anti‐social behaviour and illegal actions\. We suggest that FRM agencies—often surprised by and unprepared for such behaviours—need to integrate a recognition of deviant behaviours into their operational logic rather than continue to ignore them\. Furthermore, deviant behaviour is not fully addressed directly in the current academic FRM debates\. Consequently, there remain significant gaps in understanding, such as the many reasons behind these phenomena, and further research should focus on the significance of deviant behaviours in FRM in relation to their drivers and the consequences\.

## [EVOLVING TOOLS IN CONSTRUCTED WETLAND RESEARCH: FROM RADIOISOTOPE TRACERS TO PREDICTIVE HYDROLOGICAL MODELS](../publications/99348f02274b260c1745.md)

Kasban H\.; Arafa Horya; Mohamed S\. El\_Tokhy; Elsayed H\. Ali

Constructed wetlands \(CWs\) have become a key nature\-based technology for sustainable wastewater treatment and ecological restoration, yet their performance remains highly dependent on complex interactions among hydrodynamics, biogeochemistry, vegetation, and operational conditions\. This paper traces the evolution of research and troubleshooting tools used in CW studies, starting from early radiotracer applications and progressing towards contemporary data rich, model driven frameworks\. The paper then presents the recent advances including remote sensing and UAV based monitoring, sensor networks, computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\), process based hydrological and reactive transport models, integrated systems, and the renewed but regulated use of radioisotope and dye tracers\. In parallel, the role of dedicated simulation software in CW design and optimization is analyzed through six main platforms: BIO\_PORE, HYDRUS Wetland Module, Wetland Water Quality Model \(WWQM\), WEST, AQUASIM, and SWAT\. A comparative assessment highlights how each tool targets specific spatial scales and processes, from pore scale clogging dynamics to watershed level pollutant loading\. The results demonstrate that no single technique or software package can capture the full multi scale complexity of CWs; instead, maximum benefit is achieved by combining complementary tools into integrated monitoring–modelling frameworks\. The paper concludes by emphasising the need for multi model, multi\-source strategies and outlines future directions involving AI, digital twins, and tighter coupling between field diagnostics and predictive simulation to support more resilient, efficient, and sustainable CW systems\.

## [The role of intolerance of uncertainty in bipolar disorder](../publications/993ca03d8c1960927163.md)

Laura Maratchi; Thomas Hugh Richardson; Jayne Morriss

OBJECTIVES: Intolerance of uncertainty \(IU\) is a dispositional trait arising from negative beliefs about uncertainty\. IU has been found to be associated with various psychological disorders, including anxiety and depression, but little is known about its role in bipolar disorder \(BD\)\. The present study investigates the presentation of IU in BD, including exploring its relationship with mania and impulsivity\. METHOD: Participants with a self\-reported diagnosis of BD \(n = 93\), unipolar depression \(n = 90\) and control participants \(n = 91\) were recruited from a participant recruitment platform to complete an online survey\. Groups were compared on a variety of measures, including IU, mania symptoms, impulsivity and neuroticism, and a correlation analysis was performed to examine the relationships between IU and mania as well as IU and impulsivity\. RESULTS: BD participants scored higher than depression participants and controls on all measures except neuroticism, which was found to be equivalent to the depression group\. IU positively correlated with mania even when neuroticism was controlled for\. IU positively correlated with impulsivity but only in the BD group, and this effect was lost when neuroticism was controlled for\. CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence for the possible importance of IU as a higher\-order factor in BD, which extends our understanding of the disorder\. Findings could pave the way to explaining why anxiety is prevalent in BD and provide opportunities for an increase in the effectiveness of treatments\.

## [Statistical Assessment of the Impact of Climate Change on Cotton Yield](../publications/9943d685e21d69d203c9.md)

Bakhtiyar Babashli

Climate change presents significant risks to worldwide cotton output due to alterations in temperature regimes, an increase in drought frequency, and the exacerbation of pest and disease proliferation\. Climate anomalies affect cotton plant productivity, which is highly sensitive to hydrothermal regime\. Recent research indicates that contemporary irrigation techniques are crucial for mitigating the adverse impacts of elevated temperatures and water scarcity in the development of climate\-resilient cotton genotypes\. This study determined the relationship between cotton productivity and climatic conditions using statistical methods with ANOVA, MixedLM and Tukey HSD post\-hoc analysis\. The analysis results highlight that temperature and precipitation significantly influence productivity, with cotton productivity in certain places being more susceptible to climatic influences\. Cotton yield was determined to be statistically significantly affected by a combination of precipitation, air temperature and soil temperature in the majority of the regions where the study was conducted \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The Linear mixed\-effects model indicated region\-specific structural differences, with climate\-regional factors having significant explanatory power\. The Tukey HSD post\-hoc analysis shown statistically significant differences exclusively across specific regions and years\. The findings indicate that cotton output shows significant, although region\-specific, sensitivity to climatic conditions, thereby offering a scientific foundation for the formulation of climate\-adapted management techniques\.

## [Decoding Consumer Choices: How Marketing Mix and Online Reviews Shape E\-Commerce Purchasing Behavior](../publications/994b8e5d7bc6ccfd440e.md)

Tusiana Dewi; Syamsuddinnor Syamsuddinnor; Alfiannor Alfiannor; Syamilah Muslimah Awaluddin

This study examines the effects of the Marketing Mix and Online Consumer Reviews on purchasing decisions among consumers on e\-commerce platforms, both individually and simultaneously\. This study employed a quantitative explanatory research design to analyze the relationship between these variables\. Data were collected through questionnaires using a five\-point Likert scale from 77 students with prior experience purchasing products on Shopee\. The collected data were analyzed using multiple linear regression, supported by validity, reliability, normality, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity tests, followed by partial t\-tests, a simultaneous F\-test, and coefficient of determination analysis\. The findings indicate that the Marketing Mix has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, demonstrating the importance of product quality, pricing strategies, promotions, and accessibility\. Online Consumer Reviews also show a positive and significant influence, indicating that consumer\-generated information plays an important role in reducing uncertainty and supporting purchase evaluation\. Furthermore, both variables simultaneously contribute significantly to purchasing decisions\. The study suggests that e\-commerce sellers should strengthen marketing strategies and encourage credible consumer reviews to improve customer trust, decision\-making, and competitive performance in online marketplaces\.

## [Health equity is the goal of medical education: Implications for assessment validity](../publications/9959d25c7f3cbdcb5903.md)

Julia Blitz; Anthea Hansen

INTRODUCTION: Prevailing health inequities, viewed as a matter of social justice, have catalysed an intentionality about ensuring that medical graduates can contribute to more equitable health outcomes\. Medical education programmes are grappling with what this means for the assessment imperative\. Attention has been given to criteria for judging assessment quality, with validity remaining an important criterion\. In this paper, we explore the implications of health equity for validity and ask whether plans of assessment that do not provide evidence of students&\#x27; capacity to act to advance health equity can be considered valid\. HEALTH EQUITY AS A CONSIDERATION IN ASSESSMENT: We align with calls for medical education curricula and their assessment plans to fulfil medicine&\#x27;ssocial contract to respond to societal health needs\. We suggest that such a commitment requires us to explicitly address health equity and the inequitable health outcomes experienced by patients and communities\. In turn, it challenges us to reflect on what addressing these inequities might mean for the validity and interpretation of the inferences we make from our assessments\. RECONSIDERING ASSESSMENT VALIDITY THROUGH A HEALTH EQUITY LENS: Drawing on scholarship related to assessment validity, health equity and social justice, we identify conceptual and practical challenges associated with foregrounding health equity as a central component of assessment validity\. Using a health equity lens, we propose a set of heuristic prompts spanning purpose, constructs, evidence, inferences, learning effects, context, stakeholders, and systems and structures\. These prompts are intended to foster critical reflection on how current understandings of assessment validity might be broadened when advancing health equity is recognised as a core goal of medical education\. CONCLUSION: Rather than offering definitive solutions, we seek to provoke dialogue about the consequences for our students and society when we do not embrace considerations of health equity in our programmes of assessment\. We contend that if medical education is committed to advancing health equity, assessment of our students cannot be deemed valid unless it provides evidence to support decisions on their ability to act towards health equity\.
