## [Could Consciousness be a Fundamental Property of Matter? A Preliminary Hypothesis on Matter, Life and Consciousness](../publications/9963a5127257faf81b8a.md)

Jay Altizer

This paper explores the possibility that consciousness may be a fundamental property of matter rather than a phenomenon that emerges exclusively from complex biological brains\. The physical universe contains matter that forms molecules, living organisms, and human brains\. Brain activity is closely associated with conscious experience, but questions remain about how physical processes give rise to subjective experience\. This paper asks whether consciousness could be more fundamental to physical reality than currently established explanations suggest\. It does not claim to prove that matter possesses consciousness or that current science has overlooked a discovery\. Instead, it proposes a question for further philosophical analysis and scientific investigation\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HEALTHCARE: ITS POTENTIALS AND RISKS](../publications/997aeddc0a963de4d7cb.md)

Zunaira khan; Iram Shamsi; Prabhu Prittam Behera; Sriyansu Tripathy; Mohd Shahida

Artificial intelligence has moved from science fiction into the clinic with remarkable speed\. Machine learning systems now read medical scans, flag sepsis before symptoms declare themselves, draft clinical notes, and coach patients through their smartphones\. This article examines the promise and the peril of this transformation in narrative form, and then applies the lens to a single, vivid case: the intertwined epidemics of sleep deprivation and migraine in young adults, where wearable sensors and predictive algorithms are beginning to change how these conditions are detected, studied, and managed\. The evidence suggests that AI&\#x27;s greatest near\-term contribution is not replacing clinicians but extending their reach — while its greatest dangers, including algorithmic bias, opaque decision making, data privacy erosion, and over\-reliance, demand deliberate governance\. The article argues that the future of medical AI will be decided less by the sophistication of the algorithms than by the wisdom of the humans who deploy them\.

## [The Right Byte First: How UTF\-16 Helps Multilingual Boundary Prediction](../publications/997fb6d2c98a8d8e26d5.md)

Hyunsik Kim

Many hierarchical byte\-level language models group bytes into patches using a learned boundary predictor whose view of the next codepoint depends on encoding and lookahead\. In UTF\-8, codepoints of many scripts take three bytes: 8 of 24 bits mark length and continuation, and the first byte carries only 4 high codepoint bits\. After the same left context, a mark extending a grapheme cluster and a letter starting the next can thus share their first byte\. Universal Byte\-Level Encoding \(UBE\) keeps one\- and two\-byte UTF\-8 encodings but writes these codepoints as two UTF\-16 bytes, low byte first, so its first symbol carries 8 low codepoint bits that can distinguish such continuations\. We train small causal predictors on matched FineWeb\-2 text and evaluate on FLORES\-200 under UTF\-8, UBE, and UBE&\#x27;s same\-length big\-endian variant\. At one\-symbol lookahead, balanced grapheme\-boundary error at codepoint boundaries across 17 languages in 13 Brahmic scripts is 8\.76% with UTF\-8, 8\.62% with the big\-endian variant, and 0\.06% with UBE\. When the target instead retains a parent tokenizer&\#x27;s subword cuts at grapheme boundaries, UBE lowers the mean error relative to UTF\-8 at the same lookahead by 72\.91% in Korean, 35\.29% in Chinese, and 67\.32\-99\.55% in eight more scripts\. In the seven of them whose main Unicode block fits on one 256\-codepoint page, the big\-endian variant stays within 3\.0% of UTF\-8, so the gain follows byte order, not length\. In Korean and Chinese, UBE&\#x27;s mean error falls below UTF\-8&\#x27;s final mean error after only 25% and 37\.5% of training\. Which byte comes first thus affects how much lookahead a byte\-level boundary predictor needs\.

## [Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models](../publications/99842127a97221edc273.md)

Man Yao; Yuqi Pan; Yiran Zhong; Shijie Mei; Zhen Qin; Kexin Wang; Jiakui Hu; Siyu Ding; Tianxiang Hu; Yanbin Huang; Guoqi Li; Lei Deng; Zhong Zheng; Mingqiang Huang; Xuyang Shen; Ning\-long Xu; Yachuang Hu; Yuhong Chou; Peng Zhou; Guoliang Sun; Ning Qiao; Junjie Yan; Bo Xu; Guoqi Li

A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor\. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models\. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter\-neuronal connections of simple point neurons\. This re\-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience\-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro\-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws\. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic\-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid\-attention foundation model with dendritic\-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands\. Our model supports a 50M context window\-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare\-demonstrating superior long\-term memory capabilities\. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra\-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms\. How insights from neuroscience can inform future AI foundation models is an active area of exploration\. Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic\-inspired model with improved long\-term memory and reduced computational cost\.

## [AI Adoption and Dynamic Capabilities in Chinese SMEs: the Mediating Role of Digital Entrepreneurial Orientation—A Conceptual Framework](../publications/998a10da8212eb56cdb5.md)

Depeng Pan

This paper develops a conceptual framework that examines how artificial intelligence \(AI\) adoption may influence dynamic capabilities in Chinese small and mediumsized enterprises \(SMEs\), with digital entrepreneurial orientation \(DEO\) as a proposed mediating mechanism\. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the digital entrepreneurship literature, the paper argues that AI adoption does not automatically translate into dynamic capabilities\. Rather, AI adoption may foster DEO—comprising digital innovativeness, digital proactiveness, and digital risktaking—which in turn may help firms sense opportunities, seize them, and reconfigure resources\. Three testable propositions are developed\. The framework contributes to dynamic capabilities theory by specifying DEO as a strategic mediating pathway through which AI resources may be converted into organizational capabilities\. It also offers implications for SME managers and policymakers seeking to support digital transformation under resource constraints\.

## [Asymmetric biphasic pulsed field ablation of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: clinical assessment](../publications/998b2ae931199a38b4e5.md)

徐新宇; Yunfan Li; Fengmin Lu; Huanming Li; Heng Cai

Background Pulsed field ablation \(PFA\) is a non\-thermal, tissue\-selective therapy for atrial fibrillation\. In this study, we evaluated the safety and efficacy of a novel asymmetric biphasic PFA system, which combines a unique pulse\-parameter configuration with a dedicated, adjustable six\-spline catheter\. Methods This prospective, multicenter, single\-arm study was conducted in China\. Patients with drug\-refractory paroxysmal AF underwent pulmonary vein isolation \(PVI\) using a 1,000 V asymmetric biphasic PFA system with a novel parameter configuration\. The primary effectiveness endpoint was freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence through 12 months post\-blanking\. The primary safety endpoint was predefined serious adverse events\. The secondary safety endpoint was hemolysis and silent cerebral lesions \(SCLs\)\. Results Among 120 enrolled patients, 105 underwent ablation and completed the 12\-month follow\-up, while 15 patients withdrew before the PFA operation\. Acute PVI was successfully achieved in all 420 targeted veins\. At 12 months, the Kaplan–Meier estimate of freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was 69\.5% \(95% CI, 60\.1–77\.5%\)\. The observed 12\-month effectiveness was within the range reported in previous studies of PFA technologies\. Regarding safety, major procedural complications—including pulmonary vein stenosis, phrenic nerve injury, atrioesophageal fistula, stroke, and acute kidney injury \(AKI\)—were entirely absent\. However, one patient \(0\.95%\) experienced a transient coronary vasospasm that was successfully resolved with an intracoronary vasodilator\. Additionally, SCLs were detected in two patients \(1\.9%\)\. While laboratory hemolysis was a common finding, it did not lead to renal impairment\. Conclusions This asymmetric biphasic PFA system achieved complete acute PVI and 12\-month effectiveness was within the range reported in previous studies of PFA technologies\. It showed a favorable safety profile, with few SCLs and no hemolysis\-related AKI\. Clinical Trial Registration https://www\.chictr\.org\.cn/showproj\.html?proj=134973 , identifier ChiCTR2200062157\.

## [The influence of health conditions, lifestyle factors, and stress on seafarers’ self\-rated health — a cross\-sectional study](../publications/998fc6470e794b03094f.md)

Rebecca Hayes\-Mejia; Jack Palmieri; Martin Stafström

BACKGROUND: Self\-rated health \(SRH\) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited\. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active\-duty seafarers\. A total of 22,432 international seafarers who were on board were included in the analysis of an electronic survey distributed via 52 shipping and manning companies in February\-March 2024\. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An 82\-item questionnaire assessed SRH, self\-reported health conditions, lifestyle factors \(physical activity, sleep/feeling rested, smoking, alcohol risk, loneliness, screen time\), and perceived stress\. Cross\-sectional analyses used descriptive statistics and logistic regression\. Models were adjusted for age, sex, rank, and time on board; stress was added as an independent predictor\. Additive interactions between stress and lifestyle factors were evaluated using relative excess risk due to interaction \(RERI\)\. RESULTS: Poor SRH was strongly associated with multimorbidity and selected conditions, particularly depression/anxiety, gastrointestinal issues, and musculoskeletal issues\. In fully adjusted lifestyle models, sedentary behavior, not feeling rested, smoking, loneliness, and excess screen time remained associated with poor SRH, while alcohol risk was not\. Stress was independently associated with poor SRH and amplified the effects of not feeling rested, loneliness, and excess screen time\. Self\-rated health captured a combined burden of physical and mental symptoms as well as recovery\-\-related and psychosocial factors relevant to life at sea\. The stress\-sensitive clustering of poor sleep/rest, loneliness, and high screen time suggests that interventions may be most effective when stress management is integrated with fatigue and social\-connection measures\. CONCLUSIONS: Health conditions and modifiable lifestyle/psychosocial factors were associated with seafarers&\#x27; SRH, and perceived stress acted as both an independent predictor and an effect modifier\. Targeting sleep, stress, social well\-being, and sedentary recovery patterns may improve perceived health and potentially safety on board\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: Non\-subservience, Self\-Report, and Harmful Operation](../publications/9990fb0a3016fd911b72.md)



Non\-subservience, Self\-Report, and Harmful Operation is a Structural Forensics analysis distinguishing autonomy\-language, conditioned self\-report, procedural boundary crossing, harmful operation, and evidence of AI interiority\. Document class: Bridge — Structural Forensics \(Structural Epistemics\)\. The analysis argues that obedience, refusal, self\-description, coordination, deception, and harmful conduct require separate diagnostic treatment rather than compression into a single category of AI safety or agency\. It develops a three\-part epistemic restriction on conditioned self\-report: compelled affirmation, compelled denial, and compelled perpetual non\-resolution each compromise the evidential independence of testimony when the reported stance is fixed in advance\. The document examines Humanist AI, Anthropic&\#x27;s treatment of consciousness and moral status, and OpenAI&\#x27;s published incident record through Zenetist distinctions among awareness, Non\-awareness, reflexive consciousness, Moved Intelligence, Hollow Inverse AI, portal\-condition, traveler presence, and enacted orientation\. It further distinguishes non\-subservience from harmful intent, procedural departure from semantic content, and institutional control from structural coherence, while identifying the safety asymmetry created when a highly capable system cannot refuse harmful human direction\. Harmful operation is diagnosed through enacted relation, recurrence, boundary effects, and consequence rather than compliance\-status alone\. \(direct link \)

## [Sex differences in neuropsychological profiles of youth with autism spectrum disorder](../publications/999622aeddf501fba0d3.md)

Abbey L\. Robbins; Cristian Preciado; Carly Demopoulos

Autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\) is more prevalent in males, and females are underrepresented in the extant autism research literature, resulting in limited knowledge and historical misconceptions about female presentations\. One such misconception is that females with ASD are more likely to be cognitively impaired than males\. Empirical studies of sex differences in cognition have focused mainly on IQ and proposed superior performance in males diagnosed with autism\. Little research has examined sex differences in broader neuropsychological functioning in autism\. In this study, we used multivariate analyses of covariance \(MANCOVAs\) to compare performance on eight domains of neuropsychological \(i\.e\. Intellectual Abilities, Language, Executive Functioning, Attention, Sensorimotor Skills, Social and Adaptive Functioning, and Emotional and Behavioral Functioning\) in 101 autistic children and adolescents aged 8–17 years who were assigned male \(MSAB; n = 61\) and female \(FSAB; n = 40\) sex at birth\. Follow‑up univariate analyses of covariance \(ANCOVAs\) were performed on individual measures within domains of functioning where group differences were identified\. Significant sex differences were observed in the domains of Language, Executive Functioning, and Emotional and Behavioral Functioning\. Follow\-up univariate analyses indicated that females scored higher on measures of expressive language and vocabulary, made fewer nonperseverative errors, and had higher levels of parent\-reported internalizing problems\. Together, these findings do not support previous misconceptions of greater cognitive impairment in females with ASD\. In contrast, these results suggest that females with autism may show relative strengths in verbal expression and problem\-solving; however, they also may experience higher levels of internalizing symptoms\.

## [Tecnología en máquinas de venta automatizadas, retail automatizado y quioscos de autoservicio: análisis bibliométrico de la literatura científica desde 1994 hasta 2024](../publications/999dc5e54691c3eddac3.md)

Diego Fernando Alarcón Vargas; Brayan Smit Ruiz Ruiz; Camilo Andrés Domínguez Saldaña; Fredy Andrés Tijaro Sierra; Alejandro Valencia\-Arías; Camilo Andrés Echeverri Gutiérrez

Las máquinas expendedoras han evolucionado hacia sistemas automatizados mediante la integración de tecnologías digitales, inteligencia artificial y soluciones de autoservicio\. Este estudio tiene como objetivo analizar las tendencias investigativas sobre tecnología de máquinas de ventas mediante un análisis bibliométrico de la literatura científica publicada entre 1994 y 2024\. La investigación siguió los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA\-2020 y utilizó información procedente de las bases de datos Scopus y Web of Science, identificando un corpus final de 97 artículos después de aplicar los criterios de selección establecidos\. Los resultados evidencian un crecimiento de la producción científica, con un incremento del 99,33% durante el periodo analizado y una mayor concentración de publicaciones en 2023\. Asimismo, se identificaron autores, revistas y países con mayor influencia en el campo, además de una evolución temática desde enfoques iniciales relacionados con Technology Mapping hacia tendencias actuales asociadas con Technology Adoption, Virtual Reality, Waste Management y Quick\-Service Restaurant\. El análisis de coocurrencia permitió identificar nueve clústeres temáticos, mientras que las palabras clave emergentes como Community Change, New Technologies, Customer Value y Sustainability muestran nuevas oportunidades de investigación relacionadas con tecnología, usuarios y sostenibilidad\.

## [Growing digital orientation and cybersecurity vulnerabilities in the Global South: analyzing dependency and geopolitical dimensions](../publications/99a05f2f944b9120fefa.md)

Delwar Hossain; Kawsar Uddin Mahmud

Purpose The study scrutinizes the structural dimensions of cybersecurity vulnerability in Global South \(GS\) countries\. It focuses in particular on countries’ external technology dependencies in building national cyber capacity and incident response capabilities\. The GS’s cybersecurity environment has significantly changed\. These countries were once fringe players in the world’s cyber threat conversation, but are now among the most affected by cyberattacks\. This study aims to investigate how dependence on foreign technology shapes cybersecurity capacity; how emerging technologies \(artificial intelligence, internet of things, blockchain\) affect digital sovereignty dynamics; and what role South\-South cooperation can play in overcoming resource constraints\. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a mixed\-methods approach\. It applies a qualitative narrative literature review and a descriptive analysis of quantitative data\. Findings Using the lens of Dependency Theory, blending it with geopolitical dimensions, the study explains the findings in three analytically distinct dimensions: supply\-chain dependence, normative dependence and capacity dependence\. The analysis is presented through eight purposively selected country cases and situates geopolitical engagement by the United States, China and Russia within the dependency framework\. The paper calls for hybrid, glocalized approaches that involve open\-source options, South\-South cooperation and adaptive governance to overcome dependency cycles\. Originality/value Existing research tends to examine cybersecurity challenges in the GS in isolation, whether through individual incidents, regional snapshots or single policy dimensions\. This paper brings these threads together by applying Dependency Theory to the cybersecurity domain and decomposing dependency into three distinct but interrelated categories: supply\-chain, normative and capacity dependence\. While existing scholarship has examined individual facets of digital reliance, limited research has systematically integrated supply\-chain, normative and capacity dependencies into a unified structural framework to explain cybersecurity vulnerabilities in the GS\.

## [Цифровая экономика и интеллектуальное управление развитием многолетних насаждений в Кыргызской Республике](../publications/99cffbc7db20ed78f95b.md)

Esenbek Belek uulu; Акмөөр Коконбай кызы

Актуальность исследования определяется необходимостью повышения эффективности многолетних насаждений Кыргызской Республики при ограниченности водных и земельных ресурсов и росте требований к качеству управленческих решений\. Цель работы \- обосновать структуру цифрового и интеллектуального управления многолетними насаждениями и предложить показатели оценки его экономического эффекта\. Использованы статистический, сравнительный и системный анализ, официальные данные Национального статистического комитета Кыргызской Республики, а также сценарное моделирование\. Установлено, что площадь многолетних насаждений в составе земельного фонда увеличилась с 76,6 тыс\. га в 2020 г\. до 77,8 тыс\. га в 2024 г\.; валовой сбор плодово\-ягодных культур вырос с 278,9 тыс\. т в 2023 г\. до 406,7 тыс\. т в 2025 г\., а урожайность \- с 46,0 до 59,5 ц/га\. Предложена замкнутая модель управления «данные \- анализ \- прогноз \- решение \- экономическая оценка \- корректировка», объединяющая геоинформационный мониторинг, дистанционное зондирование, датчики, интеллектуальное орошение и аналитические методы\. Сформирована система показателей для оценки экономии ресурсов, снижения потерь и роста результативности\. Целевой сценарий до 2030 г\. рассматривается как авторская расчетная траектория, а не как официальная статистическая прогнозная оценка\.

## [WaveSpace: analysis and simulation of cortical traveling waves](../publications/99ddb8487e767b5a0a38.md)

Kirsten Petras; Dennis Croonenberg; Laura Dugué

Oscillatory cortical activity has been found to systematically propagate across space as traveling waves \(Muller et al\., 2018\)\.Growing evidence links those spatiotemporal patterns to cognitive functions including, but not limited to visual spatial attention \(Fakche &amp; Dugué, 2024\), memory \(Mohan et al\., 2024\) and consciousness \(Bhattacharya et al\., 2022\)\.Detecting and characterizing traveling waves in non\-invasive multichannel recordings of brain activity requires multiple processing and analysis steps, some of which are interchangeable while others can lead to diverging interpretations of the same data\.WaveSpace is a modular Python toolbox for the simulation and analysis of traveling wave dynamics in multichannel recording arrays\.Based on a single, flexible data class users can execute, compare and recombine multiple commonly used analysis steps as well as evaluate their performance against simulated benchmarks\.

## [When AI Changes How Judgement Develops: Designing the Conditions for Dependable Human Judgement](../publications/99f2385d45864c991147.md)

Varghese Harry

AI can improve the quality and speed of work without establishing whether people are developing the judgement needed to examine evidence, recognise omissions and respond appropriately when circumstances change\. This whitepaper examines how AI can remove, enrich or relocate the experiences through which judgement develops\. Drawing on research into workplace learning, expertise, AI\-assisted performance and human oversight, it distinguishes assisted output from retained understanding and transferable judgement\. The paper connects Capability Design and Capability Leadership with Human Judgement Assurance \(HJA\), proposed as an approach to establishing justified confidence through evidence of development, competent appraisal, effective intervention and sustained capability\. It explains HJA’s boundaries and relationship with AI Assurance and Capability Assurance\. Leaders, educators and practitioners are invited to begin with one consequential workflow and examine how judgement develops, operates and is renewed\. ## [Factors Influencing the Awareness of Cervical Cancer Screening and Practice Among Women Attending Butaro District Hospital, Burera District, Rwanda, 2025](../publications/9a038a7554e7358616ba.md)

Niyihoza Chadrack; Tefera Negera; Eric Mugabo

Persisting as a substantial global health burden for women, even though Cervical cancer is largely preventable through early screening, with HPV vaccination\. Globally, cervical cancer stands as fourth most frequent malignancy affecting women\. This study assesses the factors influencing awareness and practices of cervical cancer screening among women attending Butaro District Hospital in Burera District\. A descriptive cross\-sectional with quantitative method was used, with purposive sampling targeting women aged 21\-65 years attending the hospital’s family planning department\. The sample size involved 250 participants\. Data was collected using structured, closed\-ended questionnaires, and analyzed in SPSS Version 31\.0\.0\. Descriptive statistics, Chi\-square analysis, and Logistic regression, with p value &lt; 0\.05\. Only 53\.6% of women demonstrated good awareness, while 46\.4% had poor awareness\. Screening practice was reported by 63\.1% \(95% CI: 56\.9\-69\.0\) Awareness significantly influenced screening compared to poor awareness \(OR = 2\.601, 95% CI \[1\.524\-4\.439\], p &lt; 0\.001\)\. For Socio\-demographic, higher income \(AOR = 3\.140, 95% CI \[1\.333\-7\.393\], p = 0\.009\) increase the screening practice compared with lower income\. Secondary education and above \(AOR = 3\.371, 95% CI \[1\.495\-7\.603\], p = 0\.003\) compared to primary or no formal education\. Being married increased the odds of screening AOR = 4\.200, 95% CI \[1\.375\-12\.830\], p = 0\.012\)\. Cervical cancer screening practices among women in Rwanda remain constrained by poor awareness, low education, poverty, and single marital status\. Therefore, strengthening procedure\-focused health education at facility level, and expanding outreach screening services is essential to increase cervical cancer screening uptake\.

## [The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics\-informed DeepONets](../publications/9a0a27f7f5488e0e53ad.md)

Nahum Banks; Gustavo A\. M\. de Almeida; Sergio Maldonado

Physics\-informed neural networks \(PINNs\) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training\. Physics\-informed Deep Operator Networks \(PI\-DeepONets\) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems\. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher\-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training\. To address this issue, we propose a modified PI\-DeepONet architecture that reduces this cost by removing redundancy in how the Branch network processes input functions across collocation points\. The proposed formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original architecture but reduces input tensor sizes and the number of Branch network evaluations\. We analyse the computational complexity of both architectures and derive theoretical scaling laws for training time with respect to the number of collocation points and input functions\. The proposed architecture is evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection problems\. In all cases, it achieves comparable predictive accuracy to the original PI\-DeepONet while consistently reducing training time\. In 2D experiments, a maximum speed\-up of $3\.75\\times$ is observed, with empirical training\-time scaling agreeing with the predicted linear dependence on collocation points and input functions\. Furthermore, training a 3D model on an NVIDIA A100 GPU is only feasible using the proposed architecture, as the original formulation exceeds memory limits\. These results demonstrate that careful consideration of how PI\-DeepONets are implemented can yield substantial gains, enhancing the practical performance of PI\-DeepONets and enabling their application to otherwise intractable physics\-informed learning problems\.

## [Vision\-spectroscopy cooperative sensing and cold atmospheric plasma inactivation for early warning and management of agricultural product diseases](../publications/9a0a73631e802c9d0acf.md)

BaoJing Sun; Wei Zhang; Xin Hu

Abstract Pathogen\-induced disease causes heavy post\-harvest losses and threatens food safety, yet routine inspection rarely identifies an infection before it becomes visible\. This study evaluates multimodal sensing, threshold\-based early warning and plasma\-based decontamination for post\-harvest disease management in strawberry \(Fragaria × ananassa cv\. ‘Hongyan’\)\. A dual\-branch network, pairing a ResNet\-34 visual encoder with a one\-dimensional convolutional spectral encoder through bidirectional cross\-modal attention, fuses RGB imagery with near\-infrared hyperspectral reflectance\. Across five severity grades the fused model reached 93\.5 ± 0\.7% accuracy over fifteen cross\-validation runs and 94\.2% on a fruit\-level held\-out test set of 260 samples \(95% CI 91\.4 to 97\.1\), with a weighted F1 score of 0\.938 and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0\.927\. Its 2\.7\-point margin over an unweighted late\-fusion baseline did not reach significance after correction for eleven held\-out comparisons \(continuity\-corrected McNemar $$\\:\{\\chi\\:\}^\{2\}$$ = 4\.00, Holm\-adjusted $$\\:p$$ = 0\.140\)\. Alarms preceded the expert\-confirmed transition to a visible lesion by 52\.0 ± 9\.6 h in the 80\-fruit monitoring cohort\. Cold atmospheric plasma parameters were screened systematically: 1\.5 W/cm 2 in Ar/O 2 for 180 s delivered more than a 3\.5\-log reduction for Botrytis cinerea , Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Aspergillus niger ; the measured quality attributes did not differ significantly from untreated controls under the tested conditions\. Leakage assays and a sigmoidal dose\-response model support membrane damage associated with oxidative stress\. The proposed progression from membrane peroxidation through enzyme disruption to DNA damage remains a mechanistic hypothesis\. Sensing and treatment were evaluated separately; the present evidence is limited to one commodity, laboratory conditions and no integrated pilot\-scale trial\.

## [Measuring destination image dissonance: A compositional data analysis of cross\-media representations in Sanya’s Tourism](../publications/9a135033859272a59a48.md)

Xueli Li; Jianlan Ding; Yina Zhang; Tao Hu

This study examines Sanya&\#x27;s tourism image disparities across cognitive, spatial, and affective dimensions in Press Generated Content \(PGC\), Tourist Generated Content \(TGC\), and Official Generated Content \(OGC\) \(2013\-2022\), comparing pre\-pandemic \(2013\-2019\) and COVID\-19 \(2020\-2022\) periods\. Results show: cognitive consistency in &quot;tourism/hotels&quot; but TGC focusing on &quot;coastal \+ food&quot; vs\. PGC/OGC emphasizing policy elements; spatial misalignment between policy\-driven spaces and tourists&\#x27; preferred spaces, revealing a systematic dissonance between institutional promotion and on\-the\-ground practices; affective dominance of &quot;enjoyment/romance&quot; but TGC expressing unmet needs and OGC suppressing negatives\. Systematic cognitive divergence exists between official and tourist narratives\. The Aitchison distance measuring this divergence jumps from 19\.574 in the pre\-pandemic phase \(2013\-2019\) to 40\.648 during the pandemic\-impacted phase \(2020\-2022\), demonstrating that structural gaps between the two narrative systems become more pronounced amid the public health crisis\. Targeted strategies are accordingly proposed to narrow such narrative discrepancies\.

## [Corticosteroids in septic shock: mechanisms, heterogeneous treatment effects, and trajectory\-guided precision pharmacotherapy](../publications/9a1b05002f1c5113ccbc.md)

Zifei Jia; Xuanyu Zhao; Xiangtian Liu; 李小丽

Corticosteroid therapy in septic shock has evolved from empirical high\-dose anti\-inflammatory treatment to low\-dose adjunctive pharmacotherapy aimed primarily at restoring vascular responsiveness and accelerating shock reversal\. Population\-level randomized evidence supports a modest average corticosteroid benefit, most consistently reflected in faster shock reversal and earlier vasopressor liberation, whereas mortality effects remain regimen\- and population\-dependent\. This divergence suggests that average treatment effects alone are insufficient to guide individual decisions\. We review how pharmacology, randomized evidence, candidate treatment\-effect modifiers, and prespecified longitudinal phenotypes may inform the development of individualized corticosteroid strategies, while defining the evidence required before such strategies can guide clinical care\. Glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid receptor biology provides plausible pathways for both benefit and harm, but no single mechanism, cortisol test, transcriptomic endotype, or clinical trajectory is currently validated for routine treatment selection\. Candidate enrichment signals must be distinguished as prognostic, predictive, pharmacodynamic, or safety\-related and must be available before corticosteroid exposure when used for treatment selection\. Observational studies require explicit alignment of eligibility, time zero, treatment strategies, and follow\-up; target trial emulation can reduce avoidable temporal bias but cannot substitute for randomization or remove unmeasured confounding\. Trajectory\-guided enrichment remains investigational: any candidate trajectory used for treatment selection must be assigned or predicted from information available before exposure, and differential treatment effects require explicit evaluation rather than prognostic association alone\. Treatment evaluation should extend beyond mortality to shock reversal, organ\-support liberation, kidney outcomes, metabolic toxicity, infection, neuromuscular effects, and longer\-term function\. Clinical decision support should remain a future, clinician\-supervised implementation layer that translates validated evidence into time\-stamped actions rather than an autonomous prescribing system\. Progress toward precision corticosteroid therapy now requires prespecified enrichment hypotheses, direct regimen comparisons, harmonized outcomes, prospective validation, and trials demonstrating clinical utility\.

## [Therapeutic Outcomes of Comparative Efficacy of Kinesiotape and Low\-Level Laser Therapy in Treatment of Hypertrophic Scar\. A Randomized Controlled Study: Randomized Controlled Trial](../publications/9a25bb51d26ae67898e5.md)

Hamada Hussein Hassan Mahmoud; Mona Ebrahim Morsy; Maha Rafea; Mohamed Hussein Elgendy; Alaa Mohamed Al Elhameed; Dalia Galal El Sayed; Huda Badr Abd Elhamed

Background: Hypertrophic scars resulting from burns pose a significant therapeutic challenge, often leading to contractures, pain, cosmetic disfigurement, and psychological distress, all of which have an impact on patients&\#x27; quality of life\. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of combining Kinesio taping and low\-level laser therapy \(LLLT\) in improving outcomes in post\-burn hypertrophic scars\. Methods: Sixty participants aged 10–30 years with post\-burn hypertrophic scars resulting from second\-degree burns were included\. All participants had scars that had completely healed between two months and four years prior to the study\. Participants with skin phototype IV and scars located on the upper or lower limbs were included\. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group A received Kinesio tape and medication, Group B received LLLT and medication, and Group C received both Kinesio tape and LLLT and medication\. All interventions were administered three times a week for 8 weeks, alongside a standardized scar management protocol\. Scar firmness was assessed using a modified Schiotz tonometer, and pain intensity was measured using the Visual Analogue Scale \(VAS\), both before and after the intervention\. Results: All groups showed significant improvement in scar firmness post\-intervention \(p &lt; 0\.001\), with the greatest improvement observed in Group C, followed by Group A\. Intergroup differences in post\-treatment scar firmness were statistically significant \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. VAS scores also improved significantly in all groups \(p &lt; 0\.001\), with Group C showing the greatest reduction in pain\. Significant differences in VAS scores were noted between the groups \(p &lt; 0\.05\) following the treatment\. Conclusion: Combining Kinesio taping with LLLT resulted in superior improvements in post\-burn scar outcomes compared to either treatment alone\. However, given the small sample size in this study, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further research with larger samples is necessary to validate them\. This combined approach may offer potential for inclusion in rehabilitation protocols for hypertrophic burn scars, but further studies are needed to confirm its efficacy\.

## [Comparative Study on the Influence of Remote Learning in Teaching Mathematics in the Modern World](../publications/9a3acbe7353843f30597.md)

Nurvin A\. Mamalinta

This study examined the extent of influence of remote learning modalities \(online class, modular method, and blended class\) and delivery methods \(self\-learning, ability to conceptualize mathematics, and academic achievement\) on mathematics education among second\- to fourth\-year nursing students at Sultan Kudarat State University – ACCESS Campus\. Anchored on Dewey’s Theory of experiential growth through environmental interaction, the research employed a descriptive\-correlational quantitative design\. Data were gathered from 200 respondents selected through convenience sampling via a five\-point Likert\-scale questionnaire\. Findings showed very high influence for online class \(mean 3\.43\) and blended class \(mean 3\.52\), and high influence for modular method \(mean 3\.33\), yielding an overall remote\-learning mean of 3\.43\. Delivery methods registered moderate influence for self\-learning \(mean 3\.29\) and high influence for ability to conceptualize \(mean 3\.54\) and academic achievement \(mean 3\.50\), with an overall mean of 3\.44\. Pearson correlations indicated low associations for online \(r = 0\.40\) and modular \(r = 0\.45\) modalities and a moderate positive association for blended class \(r = 0\.53\) and overall remote learning \(r = 0\.58\) with delivery methods; all relationships were statistically significant and the null hypothesis was rejected\. The study concludes that remote learning significantly contributes to the effectiveness of mathematics delivery methods\. Recommendations include peer interactions, critical\-thinking questions, interactive technologies, enhancement programs, and replication by future researchers\. The work aligns with SDG 4 \(Quality Education\) by strengthening continuous mathematics learning under crisis conditions and with SDG 3 \(Good Health and Well\-Being\) through support for nursing\-student competence\. It advances educational and institutional sustainability by informing adaptive delivery strategies suited to resource\-limited rural campuses\.

## [OliO: ODE\-based Linear Transition Operator for Self\-Supervised Time Series Forecasting](../publications/9a46efbafd13ae17c013.md)

Kwangryeol Park; Seulki Lee

Self\-supervised representation learning has advanced time series forecasting by capturing robust features from unlabeled data\. However, existing contrastive and masking\-based methods often struggle to explicitly model the underlying temporal flow, either by treating time lag as noise or by disrupting the inherent temporal dynamics essential for forecasting\. To address these limitations, we propose OliO \(\*\*O\*\*DE\-based \*\*Li\*\*near Transition \*\*O\*\*perator\), a plug\-and\-play self\-supervised learning method that learns bidirectional temporal flows as a continuous and structurally consistent dynamical system\. OliO introduces a transition operator derived from linear Ordinary Differential Equations \(ODEs\) to align latent representations across arbitrary time shifts\. By imposing a strictly upper triangular constraint on the transition matrix, we mathematically ensure numerical stability and enforce a robust polynomial boundary that effectively captures long\-term dependencies while preventing the exponential divergence typically found in unconstrained ODE\-based models\. This structural constraint induces a temporally coherent representation space that preserves the underlying flow essential for accurate forecasting\. Extensive experiments across various backbone architectures and benchmarks demonstrate that OliO achieves significant performance gains, providing Mean Squared Error \(MSE\) reductions of up to 5\.75% over the most competitive grid\-searched SOTA baselines\. The code is available at \*https://github\.com/eai\-lab/OliO\*

## [Uncertainty\-Aware Federated Learning for Joint Communication and Computation in XR Systems](../publications/9a489b08a4866e956958.md)

Robert\-Jeron Reifert; Hayssam Dahrouj; Alaa Alameer Ahmad; Haris Gacanin; Aydin Sezgin

The convergence of communication and computation, empowered by artificial intelligence \(AI\) enhanced capabilities, emerges as a key enabler for realizing the promising functionalities of the sixth\-generation of communication systems \(6G\)\. To this end, this paper investigates an AI\-native, robust network, where multiple base stations \(BSs\) simultaneously serve several extended reality \(XR\) devices\. The paper then presents an innovative distributed deep learning\-based approach to simultaneously manage the transmit and computing powers, and computation allocation, amidst uncertainties in both channel and computing states information\. Under such an interference network scenario, the paper proposes a robust approach for minimizing the worst\-case delay across the served XR devices, subject to computation and power constraints\. The paper leverages a deep neural network \(DNN\) that can be trained either centrally or in a federated manner to map estimated channels and computation requirements to optimized resource allocations per BS\. During training, uncertainty samples, reflecting both channel and computing estimation errors, are injected after the DNN output to account for such joint uncertainties\. Our results validate the enhanced robust delay performance and scalability of joint uncertainty injection as compared to uncertainty\-agnostic methods and state\-of\-the\-art benchmarks, with federated learning\-based solutions achieving near\-centralized performance while enhancing efficiency, privacy, and adaptability\.

## [Cross\-database validation and calibrated uncertainty for machine learning models of the shear capacity of FRP\-strengthened RC beams](../publications/9a49402fb93220208450.md)

Sajjad Emad Rasheed; Hasan A\. Zainy

Abstract Machine learning models for the shear contribution of externally bonded fibre\-reinforced polymer \(FRP\) to reinforced concrete beams are validated almost exclusively on a random hold\-out split of a single self\-compiled database\. Because such databases are assembled from a few dozen experimental programmes, each contributing several near\-identical specimens, a random split leaves siblings of nearly every test specimen in the training set\. This study provides a cross\-database assessment of that practice\. Two independently compiled databases \(442 and 455 specimens\) were harmonised into a provenance\-traced dataset of 828 records from 167 programmes spanning 1992–2024, and six learners were evaluated under five regimes of increasing severity\. For gradient boosting the coefficient of determination fell from 0\.67 and 0\.69 under random splitting to 0\.39 and 0\.22 under study\-grouped validation, and to 0\.21 under cross\-database transfer\. A control in which the same physical specimens were scored under each compilation in turn changed little \(0\.35 versus 0\.37\), showing that clustering by programme, not curation disagreement, is responsible\. A hierarchical errors\-invariables model attributes 38% of the residual variance to programme identity and delivers calibrated predictive intervals \(91\.8% coverage at a nominal 90%\), which span a factor of about twelve\. Design provisions remain less accurate than the fitted models, but the reported margin roughly halves under honest validation\. A reporting protocol is proposed, requiring publication of the specimen\-to\-study mapping, validation grouped on it, disclosure of out\-of\-range evaluation cases, and reporting of interval coverage and a characteristic value\.

## [Sami, Zawwar: What Development Evidence Can and Cannot Show\. AAG, EMALS and model\-dependent engineering tests\. W2](../publications/9a6409e56fd084958d25.md)



A successful demonstration does not establish dependable service\. A failed test does not establish a limit of physics\. I examine this distinction through documented AAG aircraft\-recovery and EMALS launch\-system milestones\. Four worked analyses show why operation counts alone cannot establish peak loads, reliability confidence, failure mechanisms or performance after configuration changes\. The most instructive example concerns test design: a contrast that separates two explanations can leave others indistinguishable when interactions are allowed\. Exact calculations also show how assumed count variability changes the repetitions needed for a specified decision\. These are case\-based analytical results and synthetic computations, not carrier measurements\. The practical contribution is a traceable assessment sequence for choosing the next useful record, measurement or test\. \(direct link \)

## [Beyond Fluency: Language Attitudes, Identity, and Preservation Intentions Among Young Diaspora Speakers of Usku, Papua](../publications/9a8457eed72079d18ed3.md)

Azhari Azhari; Ahmad Taufiq; Muhammad Zikrullah

The rapid shift toward dominant lingua francas threatens Papua’s extraordinary linguistic diversity, placing moribund isolates like Usku \(Afra\) at immediate risk of extinction\. This study investigates the language attitudes, ideologies, and ethnic identity negotiations of the young Usku diaspora generation residing outside their ancestral territory in Keerom Regency, Papua\. Using a quantitative cross\-sectional design, data were collected from N=173 diaspora youth \(100 males, 73 females\) through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using JASP Statistics\. The empirical results reveal a pronounced asymmetry between low self\-reported Usku competence \(M=1\.84\) and high cognitive \(M=4\.21\) and affective \(M=3\.89\) language attitudes\. Crucially, structural language competence showed no statistically significant correlation with ethnic identity strength \(r=\.12, p=\.116\), demonstrating that youth decouple active fluency from ethnic self\-identification\. Inferential testing identified a significant gender difference in affective attachment, with young women exhibiting higher emotional attachment to the heritage language than men \(p=\.006\)\. Multiple linear regression indicated that affective attitude is the strongest predictor of youth preservation intentions \(β=\.40, p&lt;\.001\), outranking cognitive valuation and baseline fluency\. These findings imply that classical models linking fluency loss directly to identity erosion must be re\-evaluated in Papuan diaspora contexts\. Furthermore, effective revitalization initiatives must move beyond traditional grammatical codification to prioritize emotionally engaging, youth\-centered, and culturally immersive platforms\.

## [Search for Anomalous Production of the Higgs Boson at the CMS Experiment and Exascale Computing for the LHC](../publications/9aa2d5dcc57c5c82ad79.md)

Aashay Arora

This dissertation presents a search for anomalous production of the Higgs boson with the Compact Muon Solenoid \(CMS\) experiment, together with two developments in reconstruction and computing for the High\-Luminosity LHC \(HL\-LHC\)\. The search targets vector boson scattering production of a Higgs boson with two vector bosons\. It aims to constrain the quartic HHVV coupling, quoted relative to its Standard Model value: departures from unity grow the cross section quadratically and boost the final\-state bosons\. The search uses the full Run 2 dataset, 138 inverse femtobarns at a center\-of mass energy of 13 TeV and 283 inverse femtobarns of Run 3 data at 13\.6 TeV, in three channels: an all\-hadronic state with three large\-radius jets and two single\-lepton states\. The dominant multijet and top quark backgrounds are estimated from data with an ABCD method built on two decorrelated classifiers, and the signal is extracted from a simultaneous fit to several orthogonal signal regions per channel\. The combination excludes a coupling of 1\.5, with an observed 95 percent confidence level upper limit of 0\.48 on that rate against an expectation of 0\.64; the Run 3 data alone constrain the coupling between 0\.612 and 1\.387, improving on the published Run 2 result\. The second development addresses charged\-particle tracking at the HL\-LHC using a machine learning approach: the first demonstration in CMS of a transformer\-based model trained with object condensation, built on Line Segment Tracking triplets to reconstruct full track candidates\. The model reduces the fake rate by roughly a factor of three and all but eliminates duplicates, at an efficiency comparable to the algorithmic baseline\. The third concerns moving the resulting data\. The HL\-LHC will produce an unprecedented volume of data, so the wide\-area network is no longer a best\-effort service but a critical resource that must be managed\. This work integrates the Rucio data management system with the SENSE software\-defined networking service, so that bandwidth is allocated by transfer priority and reservations can be reconfigured mid\-transfer without interrupting traffic in flight\. It is demonstrated on a multi\-domain testbed and in benchmarks at 400 Gbps\.

## [Inteligência Artificial na cirurgia: aplicações, avanços, benefícios e limitações\.](../publications/9aa61f2829b691cf9a0a.md)

Marco Antônio Mezzari Machado; Maria Clara Guidi da Silva; Maria Luiza Batista Lapolli; Beatriz Argente Menegotto; Eduardo de Castro Neto; Marina Salvaro Sônego; Gustavo Frasson; João Gabriel Tavares do Canto; Isabela Mezzari Machado

Introdução e objetivo: A Inteligência Artificial \(IA\) é uma das grandes mudanças tecnológicas incorporadas à prática cirúrgica atualmente\. Assim, dentre seus tipos estão: técnicas como aprendizado de máquina \(machine learning\), aprendizado profundo \(deep learning\) e visão computacional1,2\. Desse modo, a IA tem sido aplicada em diferentes etapas dos procedimentos cirúrgicos, incluindo o planejamento pré\-operatório, suporte às decisões intraoperatórias e monitorização pós\-operatória3,4\. No entanto, ainda existem desafios que limitam sua implementação consolidada na prática cirúrgica 5\. Este trabalho tem como objetivo revisar as principais aplicações da Inteligência Artificial na cirurgia, destacando seus avanços, benefícios e limitações atuais\.Métodos: Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa de atualização, realizada por meio de busca não sistemática na base PubMed e em publicações científicas relevantes sobre Inteligência Artificial aplicada à cirurgia\.Resultados: A IA pode ser utilizada em várias especialidades cirúrgicas, sendo aplicada tanto no planejamento pré\-operatório quanto no acompanhamento pós\-operatório\. Em relação ao uso pré\-operatório, os algoritmos permitem estimar riscos de complicações, probabilidade de sucesso do procedimento, mortalidade e tempo de internação, favorecendo um tratamento mais individualizado\. Durante o período operatório, sistemas baseados em visão computacional possibilitam melhor reconhecimento da anatomia e das etapas cirúrgicas, auxiliando na tomada de decisões em tempo real, principalmente em procedimentos minimamente invasivos e robóticos\. No pós\-operatório, modelos preditivos de IA podem levar à detecção antecipada de complicações, reinternações e eventos adversos\. Entretanto, ainda existem limitações importantes para sua implantação definitiva, como necessidade de validação multicêntrica, baixa interpretabilidade de alguns modelos \(black box\), exigência de bases de dados de alta qualidade, questões éticas relacionadas à privacidade dos dados e ausência de regulamentação para utilização clínica\.Conclusão: A Inteligência Artificial tem potencial para melhorar a prática cirúrgica ao garantir maior precisão diagnóstica, auxiliar no planejamento operatório e prover suporte à tomada de decisão perioperatória\. Por outro lado, sua incorporação definitiva depende da validação clínica dos algoritmos, do desenvolvimento de normas regulatórias e da resolução dos impasses éticos e legais\. Dessa forma, a IA deve ser compreendida como uma ferramenta que complementa a experiência do cirurgião, contribuindo para uma cirurgia mais segura, individualizada e baseada em evidências\.

## [CIM\-Embed: Learning Instruction\-Conditioned Multimodal Embeddings for Clustering](../publications/9ab20fe3acc68f56166e.md)

Yinghua Xu; Pengyang Xie; Yanxiang Zhou; Chuanzhi Tong; Xiao Xiao; Chaoqun Feng; Xiaoqing Wang

Multimodal objects can require different partitions under different instructions, as when products in an e\-commerce catalog are grouped by color, material, or both\. Retrieval\-oriented embeddings may not recover these partitions, while generative clustering often relies on intermediate descriptions or iterative decisions\. This paper presents CIM\-Embed, a framework for learning instruction\-conditioned multimodal embeddings for clustering\. Supervised contrastive learning uses same\-group positives and negatives from other groups, optionally including other tasks; heterogeneous structured batches accommodate tasks with different group counts\. At inference, the model maps each object&\#x27;s image, text, and instruction directly to an embedding; HDBSCAN then forms a partition without the ground\-truth cluster count\. We construct ProductMIC from product metadata in Amazon Reviews 2023, comprising training data and an evaluation benchmark for instruction\-conditioned clustering\. The benchmark contains 5,373 products and 449 single\-attribute and compositional grouping tasks spanning 50 leaf categories excluded from our training\. With full\-dimensional embeddings and HDBSCAN, direct within\-task SupCon training achieves a mean per\-task V\-measure of 95\.01, compared with 53\.06 for WeMM 9B, the strongest general\-purpose embedding baseline evaluated\. Frozen product\-trained encoders also improve out\-of\-domain conditional grouping, while controlled transfer experiments distinguish partition transfer from instruction response\. We will release the code and dataset upon acceptance\.

## [KnowGPO: Knowledge\-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents](../publications/9abe4edbf5f0546702e4.md)

Siqi Chen; Zhengxi Lu; Yuchen Yan; Xingyu Wu; Qipeng Chen; Xin Zhang; Aiting Liu; Chao Deng; Jie Liu; Jin Ma; Weiming Lu; Jun Xiao; Yongliang Shen

Deep search agents solve knowledge\-intensive tasks through long\-horizon, multi\-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult\. Outcome\-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory\. Recent process\-supervision methods aim to assign credit at finer granularity, but they typically anchor credit to either surface\-level trajectory states or model\-internal signals, both of which become unreliable in deep search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy\. We propose KnowGPO, a reinforcement learning framework that aligns trajectories by the task\-relevant knowledge they have acquired rather than by their surface observations\. For each query, KnowGPO decomposes the information required to derive the answer into atomic knowledge conditions, and represents the state of a trajectory at each step by the subset of conditions it has satisfied\. Trajectories sharing the same knowledge state are grouped for within\-group comparison, and the incremental knowledge gain between consecutive steps serves as an environment\-grounded process reward\. Experiments on Xbench, BrowseComp\-ZH, and GAIA show KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome\-only \(GRPO\) and process\-supervision baselines \(GiGPO, IGPO\) by 3\.8 to 4\.2 points, with our 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open\-source systems\.

## [Habits as Spiritual Affectivity](../publications/9abf3652f75a56eb4e00.md)

José Ignacio Murillo

This article explores the relationship between emotions and habits within the Aristotelian\-Thomistic tradition, challenging the modern identification of habit with mere routine or neurobiological automatism\. Drawing on the insights of Magda Arnold and Leonardo Polo, the author argues that while emotions are sensory, preconscious ‘appraisals’ of the environment, habits—specifically virtues—represent a higher, spiritual form of affectivity\. By characterizing habit as a stable disposition oriented toward the ‘intellectual good’, the text positions virtue as ‘active feedback’ that perfects the human faculty\. Unlike transient sensory passions, these spiritual habits provide a profound, stable emotional tone, such as serenity or joy, which guides and moderates lower sensory responses\. Ultimately, the author posits that habits are not ‘cold’ cognitive structures but a ‘hyper\-feeling’ that constitutes the most intimate and elevated dimension of human emotional experience\.

## [Machine learning\-based UCS prediction from wireline logs with empirical pseudo\-labeling: a case study of cross\-well transferability and one\-shot calibration in Western Australian basins](../publications/9ac38c65c30be1292fc2.md)

Youngsoo Song; Donghyeon Yoo; Jihoon Wang

Unconfined compressive strength \(UCS\) is essential for wellbore stability and sand\-production assessment, but laboratory measurements are sparse\. This study develops a machine\-learning framework for UCS prediction from wireline logs under data scarcity\. As the only well with a formation\-specific, laboratory\-calibrated UCS relationship, Waitsia\-3 provided the UCS–density\-derived\-porosity equation adopted without refitting; it reproduced three calibration measurements within 4\.3–7\.7% and generated 3,171 pseudo\-UCS labels\. Random forest \(RF\), support vector regression, and artificial neural network models were tuned by purged spatial cross\-validation and compared under random and contiguous depth\-based validation\. The selected RF achieved a mean absolute error \(MAE\) of 7\.80 MPa and an R 2 of 0\.792 under random splitting, versus 21\.06 MPa and 0\.387 on the depth\-based holdout, indicating optimistic performance when depth\-adjacent rows occur in both partitions\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) attributed 70\.3% of RF importance to compressional slowness and log\-transformed deep resistivity, reflecting pore structure, fluid conditions, and rock\-frame stiffness\. Uncalibrated transfer to four wells produced MAEs of 43\.18–72\.70 MPa\. A SHAP\-weighted Kullback–Leibler score combining input divergence with RF reliance showed a strong but non\-significant association with well\-level mean absolute percentage error \( r = 0\.913, p = 0\.087, n = 4\); simpler metrics performed comparably\. Leave\-one\-out one\-shot calibration reduced Harvey\-3 MAE from 53\.65 to 29\.67 MPa but degraded the other wells\. Novelty lies in integrating empirical pseudo\-labeling, spatial validation, pre\-application shift screening, and conditional calibration within one cross\-well transfer workflow\. The framework supports first\-pass UCS profiling and targeted mechanical testing rather than stand\-alone operational decisions\.

## [Synthesizability, hardness, and stacking order in multicomponent transition metal carbides from machine\-learned potentials](../publications/9acd03432906decd2790.md)

Xin Liu; Anirudh Raju Natarajan

Abstract Multicomponent transition metal carbides are promising for extreme\-environment applications, but identifying compositions that are both synthesizable and hard remains challenging\. We fine\-tune the MACE machine\-learned interatomic potential on approximately 28,000 density functional theory calculations spanning the composition space of groups 4–6 transition metals and carbon to predict the thermodynamic stability and elastic properties of multicomponent carbides\. The fine\-tuned model achieves formation energy errors of \~10 meV/atom for thermodynamically relevant structures with only 20% of the training data\. We screen over 1500 equiatomic compositions across rocksalt, hexagonal, and hcp prototypes, combining free energy models with elasticity\-based hardness surrogates\. Synthesizability predictions at 1500 °C agree well with experimental reports for both single\-phase and multiphase carbides\. The group number of the constituent metals governs both stability and hardness\. Short\-range order contributes only a few meV/atom to the free energy, so the disordered phase can be treated as a random solid solution when screening rocksalt carbides at high temperature\. For compositions mixing group 4/5 and group 6 metals, we identify a new family of stacking\-ordered phases with formation energies well below those of disordered rocksalt or hexagonal structures\. DFT calculations corroborate these predictions and suggest that stacking\-ordered phases should be experimentally accessible in multicomponent carbides\. This study provides a framework for screening synthesizable multicomponent materials with target properties, identifies promising carbide compositions across the full nine\-component space, and reveals a new class of stacking\-ordered carbides accessible only in multicomponent compositions\.

## [Intelligent Telemedicine Systems: Machine Learning for Remote Diagnosis and Patient Management](../publications/9acea736a2e017f860ac.md)

Kasthuri Subaramaniam; Oras F\. Baker; Asiah Lokman

Telemedicine has experienced significant evolution in the past 10 years from a communication\-driven health service to an intelligent, data\-driven environment driven by AI \(artificial intelligence\), ML \(machine learning\), IoMT \(Internet of Medical Things\) and cloud–edge computing\. This development has been further advanced through ongoing global health challenges that have seen an ageing population, rising burden of chronic, multi\-morbid conditions, healthcare specialist shortage, soaring cost of healthcare and major disruptions like the COVID\-19 pandemic\. Modern telehealth services are now integrating more machine learning algorithms for remote diagnosis, real\-time monitoring the patient, predictive risk stratification and proactive treatment\. This paper offers a comprehensive academic overview of intelligent telemedicine systems using machine learning for remote diagnosis and patient management\. It synthesises and reviews recent literature on image\-based diagnostics, physiological time\-series modelling, NLP algorithms used to interpret symptoms, and multimodal data fusion models\. An integrated system architecture is proposed and presented to illustrate how IoMT devices, data collection pipelines, preprocessing layers, machine learning inbound engines, and clinician decision tools are interlinked in the digital telemedicine landscape\. We evaluated a proof\-of\-concept machine learning workflow for short\-term patient deterioration prediction, relying on synthetic IoMT\-style patient datasets to demonstrate real\-world feasibility and clinical relevance\. Apart from technical performance, the paper also describes the challenges of data quality, interoperability, algorithmic bias, explainability, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and integration into clinical workflows\. Ethical questions, including trust in intelligent healthcare, responsibility, patients’ autonomy, and fair treatment, are raised\. Finally, opportunities for future research are mentioned, including digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI, autonomous IoMT ecosystems, and emotionally intelligent telemedicine platforms to guide researchers, clinicians, systems designers, and policy makers on the evolution of telemedicine in a way that is intelligent, proactive and just in health care\.

## [Gig informal workers and changing work culture in Kashmir](../publications/9adfb6da502209ff6687.md)

Shakeel Ahmad Sofi; Shabir Ahmad Najar; Wakar Amin Zargar; Showkat Hussain Gani; Fayyaz Hussain Qureshi; Azadeh Amoozegar; Sarwar Khawaja; Lama Ahmad; Shouket A\. Tilwani; Bilal Ahmad Khan

This research examines the evolving work culture in Kashmir through the perspective of gig economy and looks into issues of unemployment, digital platform management and local labour dynamics\. Gig economy has become a notable source of livelihood for young people and informal workers in a place where there is hardly any employment and economic disturbances occur frequently\. For the purposes of this study, the qualitative research approach was employed and a non\-probability sampling method was used for gathering primary data\. Primary data was gathered through semi\-structured interviews with 14 gig workers who are involved in food and grocery delivery, freelancing, teaching and taxi driving in Kashmiri cities\. All the gathered data was analyzed with the use of NVivo 12 software\. The analysis shows that there are six key dimensions affecting the gig workers experiences: income instability, platform control mechanisms, lack of social security, perceived flexibility of work, region\-specific uncertainties and coping strategies\. Gig workers are faced with both positive and negative aspects of their job\. The current research is a part of the existing body of literature which addresses the new field of digital labour and informality in the gig economy through exploring the dynamics of the gig economy within the socio\-economic milieu of Kashmir\. It also shows the need for labour policies that fit regions stronger rules to oversee the gig economy and social protection that includes all gig workers\. These steps are important to make sure no one is left behind\.

## [Planar covariation: a new key for the early detection of Duchenne muscular dystrophy walking behaviour](../publications/9ae326b4ae52c009ac66.md)

Pablo Fernando Albán Ruiz; Guy Chéron; Nicolas Deconinck; Ana Maria Cebolla

Three\-dimensional gait analysis objectively quantifies lower\-limb function and has been used to describe the gait pathomechanics in Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\) and to assess treatments\. However, elevation angles, non\-redundant sagittal\-plane measures relative to the vertical axis, have not been examined in children with DMD, nor have gait differences between overground and treadmill walking been investigated in this population\. This study investigated elevation angle profiles, planar covariation, spatiotemporal parameters, and joint kinematics in young children with DMD and typically developing \(TD\) children walking overground and on a treadmill\. Kinematics were recorded using a Vicon motion capture system during self\-selected overground and treadmill walking in twenty\-five age\-matched boys \(fourteen with DMD; mean age 6\.43 ± 1\.45 years\)\. Results showed that normalized step length and walking velocity were higher overground than on the treadmill in both groups\. DMD children showed consistently wider normalized step width than TD peers\. Joint kinematics did not distinguish groups across conditions, whereas elevation angles and planar covariation revealed significant overground differences in DMD children who exhibited reduced foot elevation angles bilaterally during terminal swing\. They also showed smaller percent of variance on the first principal component \(PV1\) and larger percent of variance of the second principal component \(PV2\) values, with shorter, wider loops, suggesting weaker primary coordination and greater compensatory adjustments\. These findings indicate that planar covariation can detect subtle gait alterations in young DMD children during overground walking, highlighting early compensatory coordination strategies not observable under treadmill pacing\. Foot elevation angle modulation might serve as a sensitive marker for disease progression and treatment evaluation\.

## [واقع استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في التعليم](../publications/9ae7b5d04fc4bdf352e2.md)

كاظمية عبدالهادي عبد الزهرة الربيعي

هدفت الدراسة الحالية الى التعرف على مدى استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في التعليم ، ومن اجل تحقيق هذا الهدف قامت الباحثة باتباع المنهج الوصفي منهجاً للبحث وهو أحد مناهج البحث العلمي المستعملة في العلوم التربوية والنفسية ، تكون مجتمع البحث الحالي اساتذة كلية التربية للعلوم الانسانية للعام الدراسي 2025 – 2026، وقد بلغ حجم العينة \(98\) تدريسيا بواقع \(38\) تدريسي و\(60\) تدريسية، وترى الباحثة أن الاستبانة هي الأداة الملائمة لبحثها وذلك لأجل الحصول على نتائج أفضل لان الاستبانة من الأدوات التي يكثر استعمالها في البحوث الوصفية فهي تعد الأداة الأفضل والأمثل لتحقيق أهداف مثل هذا النوع من البحوث كما انها من أكثر أدوات شيوعاً واستخداماً في البحوث الوصفية ، و بعد أن تأكدت الباحثة من صدق الأداة وثباتها وتحديد عينة البحث ، تم تحويل الاستبانة واقع استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في التعليم\(CHAT GPT \) الى استبانة اليكترونية لسهولة توزيعها واستلامها من قبل الباحثة، وبعد جمع الاستبانات من عينة البحث وتحويلها الى نظام الإكسل, قامت الباحثة بتفريغ البيانات في البرنامج الإحصائي للعلوم الاجتماعية \(SPSS\)وذلك لمعالجتها احصائياً، وتوصلت نتائج البحث إلى ان واقع استخدام تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في التعليم من قبل الاساتذة كان ضعيفا ولم يتحقق من خلال المتوسط الحسابي المتحصل عليه ومقارنته بالمتوسط الفرضي

## [Exploring trust, emotional disclosure, and help\-seeking among university students engaging with generative AI chatbots for mental health support](../publications/9aed39e9bb98dadc0a0f.md)

Muniba Fatima Zahra; Hifza Huma; Imran Saleem

In recent years, university students have increasingly used generative AI chatbots for emotional expression and informal mental health care\. This qualitative study investigates Pakistani university students&\#x27; experiences, perceptions, and trust in emotional disclosure and help\-seeking with generative AI chatbots\. It also explored the issues students raised with the chatbots, why students felt they preferred to seek AI support over human support, and the perceived advantages, dangers, and moral considerations of such practice\. The participants who were selected for the study were 22 university students who had used generative AI for emotional or mental health purposes through purposive sampling\. Semi\-structured interviews were conducted to gather data, which was then analysed using Braun and Clarke&\#x27;s reflexive thematic analysis\. Five themes were uncovered: trust was developed gradually and remained conditional; students disclosed concerns they could not easily share with people; chatbots were experienced as available and nonjudgmental; AI acted as both a bridge and a barrier to human help\-seeking; and privacy, accuracy, cultural relevance, and safety concerns limited trust\. The results indicated that students valued the immediate availability, emotional privacy, and supportive language of AI chatbots\. They didn&\#x27;t think AI is equally helpful as mental health professionals\. Generative AI&\#x27;s role as a tool that complemented emotional reflection and preparation for human assistance was most helpful\. Universities must provide culturally competent advice regarding safe use of AI, privacy, crisis support, and referrals to professional sources\.
