## [Serum biochemical and hematological responses of broiler chickens to herbal\-origin anticoccidial supplementation during experimental Eimeria infection](../publications/9afc47fdbe856590a6cd.md)

Vilma Vilienė; Asta Racevičiūtė\-Stupelienė; Daria Murawska; M\. Gesek; Paulius Matusevičius; Zoja Miknienė; Monika Nutautaitė

Introduction Coccidiosis is one of the most economically important diseases in poultry production, prompting increasing interest in natural alternatives to conventional anticoccidial drugs\. The aim of this study was to evaluate the biochemical and hematological response of broiler chicken serum to an herbal anticoccidial supplement during experimental Eimeria infection\. Methods A total of 1,200 Ross 308 broilers were assigned to four groups \( n = 300\): non\-infected \( − \) and infected \( \+ \) birds receiving either conventional chemical anticoccidials \(UC\) or the herbal\-origin anticoccidial additive \(HA\)\. Blood samples were collected on days 10 and 35 to assess serum biochemical parameters, differential leukocyte profiles and lymphocyte morphology\. Results Age significantly affected total protein, albumin, AST, GGT, calcium and iron concentrations \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. A significant group effect was observed for ALT activity \( p = 0\.036\) and magnesium concentration \( p = 0\.013\), while a significant G x A interaction was found for urea concentration \( p = 0\.040\)\. Significant differences between the groups were also identified band and segmented heterophils, lymphocytes and monocytes, while lymphocyte morphology differed significantly among groups and sampling periods \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Discussion The study results indicate that the use of a herbal anticoccidial additive was associated with changes in certain serum biochemical and hematological parameters during experimental Eimeria infection, without causing adverse changes in the physiological condition of the broilers\. These results suggest that herbal anticoccidial supplements may be a promising natural strategy to support the immune response during coccidiosis\.

## [Network pharmacology–driven identification of PTP1β and rational design of simufilam\-based allosteric inhibitors for neuroprotection in Alzheimer’s disease](../publications/9b00040c12f81e59b370.md)

Vishnu Kumar Malakar; Rajeshkumar Raman; Antony Justin; Dhanabal SP; Dhritiman Roy; Chandi C\. Malakar; Dipen Purohit; Pratap Chand Mali

Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that predominantly affects elderly people and is characterized by cognitive decline and dementia\. Protein tyrosine phosphatase\-1B \(PTP1B\) is known to modulate pro\-inflammatory mediators, and its overexpression in the brain has been implicated in AD\-associated neuroinflammation\. This study explores the mechanism of A20, A26, and co\-crystal\-designed compound targeting non\-competitive allosteric PTP1B enzyme inhibition for AD therapy using network pharmacology and computational studies\. Protein\-protein interaction was designed for 128 active targets by STRING database and Cytoscape software\. Further, active target\-associated pathways analysed using ClueGO plugin Cytoscape software and the Reactome online public domain server\. The non\-competitive allosteric PTP1B inhibition through the design of Simufilam derivatives, with particular emphasis on A20, which is predicted to bind at the non\-competitive allosteric site of the PTP1B protein \(PDB ID: 1T49\), involves α3, α6, and α7 helices that influence the WPD loop orientation\. The proposed non\-competitive allosteric binding mode is based on computational evidence and for that further experimental validation would be required to conclusively confirm binding of the designed compounds within this regulatory region\. Using in\-silico approaches, including molecular docking, identified A20 with the most favourable predicted binding energy score \(\-10\.8 kcal/mol\) compared to other derivatives\. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated structural stability of the PTP1B\-A20, 26, and co\-crystal complex, with consistent RMSD, RMSF, H\-bond, Rg, and SASA\. Principal component analysis suggested that A20 restricts conformational flexibility; hence MM\-PBSA analysis displayed its stable binding free energies\. Density functional theory \(DFT\) calculation characterized the polarity, stability, and reactivity of A20 studies supported its favourable electronic configuration\. Overall, A20 displayed superior calculated binding energies, trajectory stability, and predicted drug\-likeness, positioning it as a promising lead candidate for future empirical validation in AD research\. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi\.org/10\.1007/s13205\-026\-05086\-2\.

## [Phenotypic antimicrobial resistance structure among Enterobacterales circulating at the turkey–environment interface in a small\-scale poultry production system](../publications/9b029c68642322f9f9ff.md)

Alex Yauyo; Alejandra Castro; Brenda Ayzanoa; Marcelo Cardenas; Guillermo Salvatierra R\.

Introduction Antimicrobial resistance is a major One Health challenge affecting human, animal, and environmental health\. Poultry production systems may contribute to the maintenance and dissemination of multidrug\-resistant \(MDR\) Enterobacterales through interactions among animals and their environment\. Conventional analytical approaches may have limited capacity to characterize the complexity of phenotypic resistance profiles\. This study aimed to characterize phenotypic antimicrobial resistance patterns and explore resistance clustering among Enterobacterales isolated from turkeys and their production environment in Lima, Peru\. Methods A descriptive cross\-sectional study was conducted using Enterobacterales recovered from cloacal swabs and environmental samples collected in a small\-scale poultry production system\. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method; intermediate results were classified as susceptible for analytical purposes\. Multiple correspondence analysis \(MCA\) combined with k\-means clustering was applied to explore the multivariate structure of phenotypic resistance profiles\. Results A total of 50 Enterobacterales isolates were recovered from cloacal swabs \( n = 38; 76\.0%\) and environmental samples \( n = 12; 24\.0%\)\. Predominant species included Escherichia coli \( n = 39; 78\.0%\), followed by Klebsiella spp\. \( n = 7; 14\.0%\) and Citrobacter spp\. \( n = 4; 8\.0%\)\. All isolates were classified as MDR\. The most frequent resistance profile included kanamycin, tetracycline, neomycin, cefuroxime, and amoxicillin–clavulanic acid\. One E\. coli isolate exhibited resistance to 18 antimicrobials, while a Citrobacter spp\. isolate recovered from the environment showed resistance to 17 antimicrobials, including imipenem\. MCA revealed a structured distribution of resistance phenotypes, with the first two dimensions explaining 45\.3% of the total inertia and identifying three clusters with distinct resistance spectra\. One cluster contained all carbapenem\-resistant isolates and exhibited the broadest resistance profile\. Discussion These findings highlight the circulation of heterogeneous MDR populations and support surveillance strategies in poultry production environments\.

## [A biomarker\-derived injury score integrating inflammatory cytokines and mitochondrial vitality may predict short\-term injury risk in football](../publications/9b0be51446faecf8bc71.md)

Dominik Ziehe; Björn Koos; Patrick Thon; Hartmuth Nowak; Nadine Hennigs; Kaspar Schepanek; Patrick Ingelfinger; Andreas Schlüter; Holger Holthusen; Martin Meichelbeck; Mark Sandfort; Kristina Gebhardt; Fabian Maria Stuby; Karsten Krüger; Michael Adamzik

Background To determine whether a biomarker\-derived injury score integrating exercise\-induced cytokine responses with mitochondrial and bioenergetic readouts improves short\-term injury risk stratification in professional football players compared with normalized TPL and high\-intensity running distance \(HIRD\)\. Methods Prospective observational cohort study in elite professional football\. Twenty\-one professional male football players \(German 2nd Bundesliga, 2023/2024 season\) were assessed immediately pre\- and post\-training\. Serum cytokines \(IL\-6, IL\-8, IL\-10, TNF\-α\) were measured using a multiplex immunoassay\. PBMC ATP content was quantified via a luciferase\-based assay, and mitochondrial vitality was approximated by the TFAM/TFB2M interaction using a proximity ligation assay\. ROC analysis with Youden index was applied to derive biomarker cut\-offs associated with injuries occurring within 10 days\. Each exceeded cut\-off contributed one point to a composite Injury score \(0–6\)\. Predictive performance was compared with normalized total player load \(TPL\) and, in an exploratory sensitivity analysis, high\-intensity running distance \(HIRD; the sum of velocity\-band 5 and 6 distances\)\. Results Six of 21 players sustained an injury within 10 days\. Normalized TPL showed weak discriminatory performance \(AUC = 0\.577\), and HIRD showed similarly weak discrimination in an exploratory analysis \(AUC = 0\.532; 95% CI 0\.247–0\.817\)\. In contrast, the biomarker\-derived Injury score demonstrated high discrimination \(AUC = 0\.939; 95% CI 0\.828–1\.000\)\. Using a threshold of &lt;4 versus ≥4, scores &lt;4 were associated with a 93% probability of remaining injury\-free \(13/14\), whereas scores ≥4 were associated with injury occurrence in 71% of cases \(5/7\)\. Conclusion A biomarker\-based Injury score integrating inflammatory and mitochondrial responses to exercise showed promising performance for short\-term injury risk stratification and showed higher apparent discriminatory performance than normalized TPL and HIRD in this cohort\. These findings suggest that individualized biological responses to training stress may provide clinically relevant information for injury risk assessment in professional football\. Further prospective validation in larger cohorts is required\.

## [The Relationship between Brokers, Insureds, and Insurers: Duties, Distribution, and Value Creation in a Changing Global Insurance Market](../publications/9b0cb69eff4191dd78e5.md)

Ben Kajwang

Purpose: This paper critically examines the relationships among insurance brokers, insureds, and insurers, focusing on professional duties, market distribution, contractual authority, and economic value creation\. Methodology: A qualitative literature review approach was adopted, synthesizing scholarly studies, legal frameworks, and international insurance market reports, primarily published between 2020 and 2025\. The review was guided by Agency Theory and Stakeholder Theory, with evidence organised into five thematic areas\. Findings: Findings revealed that insurance intermediaries remained essential in reducing information asymmetry, facilitating risk transfer, and enhancing customer protection\. However, dual agency, remuneration arrangements, and overlapping contractual obligations created potential conflicts of interest\. Digitalization and alternative risk\-financing mechanisms further transformed intermediary responsibilities, increasing the importance of professional competence and regulatory accountability\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Based on the reviewed literature, the paper informs intermediary governance and advisory practices and supports clearer contractual authority, remuneration transparency, and stronger consumer protection regulations in contemporary insurance markets\.

## [Beyond usefulness: cognitive and emotional correlates of AI use intentions among HR professionals](../publications/9b198ecbc54ed9538e44.md)

René Arseneault; Houssem Eddine Ben Messaoud

Purpose Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is transforming human resource management \(HRM\), yet the cognitive and psychological factors associated with human resource \(HR\) professionals’ intentions to use AI remain incompletely understood\. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) and appraisal perspectives, this study examines the relative associations of Cognitive Evaluation, AI\-Use Anxiety, AI\-Related Job Insecurity, organizational AI use across HR functions, and AI Knowledge with behavioral intention to use AI\. It also explores whether AI Knowledge moderates these relationships\. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 285 HR professionals\. Confirmatory factor analyses assessed the measurement structure of the study constructs, followed by hierarchical moderated regression analyses examining their unique associations with behavioral intention and the exploratory moderating role of AI Knowledge\. Findings Cognitive Evaluation, reflecting perceived usefulness and ease of use, showed the strongest unique association with behavioral intention to use AI\. AI\-Use Anxiety demonstrated a smaller negative association, whereas AI\-Related Job Insecurity, AI Use Across HR Functions, and AI Knowledge did not explain significant unique variance once the competing predictors were considered simultaneously\. The comprehensive model explained 66\.8% of the variance in behavioral intention\. The exploratory interaction analyses provided no clear evidence that AI Knowledge systematically moderated the relationships examined\. Practical implications Organizations implementing AI in HR should address both employees’ evaluations of the technology and apprehension surrounding its use\. Implementation strategies should demonstrate the practical usefulness and usability of AI through role\-specific examples, hands\-on training, and opportunities to experiment with AI tools in realistic HR contexts\. Organizations should also recognize AI\-use anxiety as a distinct potential barrier by providing accessible support, low\-risk opportunities for familiarization, and clear communication throughout implementation\. These strategies may help create conditions that support employees’ willingness to use AI\. Originality/value This study extends research on AI use intentions by examining cognitive, emotional, knowledge\-related, and organizational\-exposure factors simultaneously rather than in isolation\. The findings show that HR professionals’ intentions to use AI are most strongly associated with evaluations of its usefulness and usability, while AI\-use anxiety represents a smaller but distinct negative correlate\. By distinguishing AI\-use anxiety from AI\-related job insecurity and individual AI knowledge from organizational AI exposure, the study provides a more differentiated account of the factors associated with HR professionals’ intentions to use AI\.

## [Generative AI Decision Support in B2C E\-Commerce: A Consumer Buying Behaviour Framework](../publications/9b230cfe1b081996d12c.md)

Galina Ilieva

Decision making in business\-to\-consumer \(B2C\) e\-commerce connects company and consumer activities before, during and after purchase, whereas many existing generative artificial intelligence \(GAI\) applications focus on specific tasks or functions\. This article develops a conceptual framework linking employee responsibilities, consumer choices, GAI support, information sources, permissions and two\-sided evaluation through the five\-stage Consumer Buying Behaviour \(CBB\) process\. It connects need clarification, information gathering, feasible\-offer comparison, transaction review and post\-purchase assessment through decision gates and bounded support functions\. Five employees and three consumers participated in a fixed\-order ChatGPT 5\.6 demonstration to examine the administration and perceived value of the proposed decision\-support approach\. Following a brief GAI introduction, participants observed ordinary prompt\-response support and then a structured CBB\-guided sequence within the same general e\-commerce decision context\. Questionnaire ratings were generally more favourable following CBB guidance, particularly for perceived comparison support and mental effort\. The study\-specific items are descriptive indicators, and fixed ordering confounds condition with practice, familiarity, novelty, fatigue, expectancy and task\-set effects\. The contribution is strictly conceptual and methodological; the eight\-participant exercise supplies procedural illustration and design input, without establishing effectiveness, deployment readiness or validated system behaviour\. Future evaluation requires an implemented system, versioned tasks and outputs, independently scored task\-level records, and randomised or counterbalanced comparison\.

## [MANIFESTO OF CONSCIOUSNESS: Where It Begins, How It Evolves, and What It May Become](../publications/9b24f200658849db892c.md)

Mykola Iabluchanskyi; Andriy Yabluchanskiy

abluchanskyi M\., Yabluchanskiy A\., MANIFESTO OF CONSCIOUSNESS: Where It Begins, How It Evolves, and What It May Become, 2026, 15,095 words\. Consciousness remains the biggest unresolved scientific problem of the twenty‑first century not because we lack data, but because we hide different phenomena under a single word\. This book offers an ontological definition of consciousness as the union of subjectivity \(“what it is like”\) and reflection \(self‑monitoring of one’s own states\), and systematically draws demarcation lines between consciousness, sentience, irritability, and complex cognitive behavior\. At the intersection of philosophy, neuroscience, and clinical medicine, the authors reconstruct the evolutionary threshold of consciousness, examine the octopus as a living demarcation line, reconsider the Cambridge, New York, and Vienna declarations, and show why embodiment is a necessary condition of any conscious experience\. A separate part of the book turns to future forms of consciousness—from embodied robots to hybrid bio‑silicon systems—and formulates the principles of graded moral status and the presumption of consciousness as the basis for a new ethics in a world where human consciousness is not a final authority but only one stage in an open evolutionary process\.

## [ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ACADEMIC WRITING: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND ETHICAL GUIDELINES FOR HIGHER EDUCATION](../publications/9b2de0c08cdde05ecbc9.md)

Bobur Suyunov

The rapid development of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has significantly transformed academic writing, creating new opportunities for students, researchers, and university teachers\. AI\-powered applications can assist users in generating ideas, organizing arguments, improving grammar, expanding vocabulary, paraphrasing sentences, and editing academic texts\. However, the integration of these technologies into higher education also raises important questions concerning academic integrity, authorship, originality, critical thinking, and the reliability of automatically generated information\. This article examines the role of AI in academic writing, focusing on its educational benefits, methodological limitations, and ethical implications\. The study employs a qualitative, descriptive\-analytical approach based on a review of relevant academic literature and international guidelines on generative AI in education and research\. The analysis suggests that AI can support the development of academic writing when it is used as an assistive instrument rather than a substitute for independent intellectual work\. Particular attention is paid to the responsibilities of students, researchers, and educational institutions in ensuring transparent and responsible AI use\. The article argues that effective integration requires AI literacy, critical evaluation of generated content, appropriate disclosure practices, and assessment methods that recognize the importance of human reasoning\. It concludes that the educational value of AI depends not simply on technological availability but on the principles governing its application in academic contexts\.

## [Validating LLM\-generated political networks with survey\-reported partisan exposure](../publications/9b35d5c52bea9fed5aaf.md)

Marco Tonin; Michele Tizzoni; Bruno Lepri; Luca Maria Aiello

Large language models \(LLMs\) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in social science research, including decisions, interactions, and social relationships\. However, in network formation tasks, existing evaluations often focus on aggregate network properties, while networks with plausible structural properties may still fail to reproduce individuals&\#x27; social and political environments\. Here, we generate LLM\-based political networks using personas sampled from the nationally representative ANES 2020\-\-2022 Social Media Study and use respondents&\#x27; survey\-reported partisan exposure as an empirical benchmark for the political environments generated for the corresponding personas\. We first characterize the structural properties and political assortativity of the generated networks, and then compare ego\-level partisan exposure with the survey\. We find that the structure and political assortativity of the generated networks vary across experimental configurations\. More importantly, when comparing generated partisan exposure with the survey, some models generate stronger separation between Democratic and Republican egos than reported in the survey, with higher same\-party and lower cross\-party exposure, while others mainly underestimate Republican exposure across ego groups\. Moreover, networks with similar political assortativity can still generate different partisan environments around the same personas, including among networks with plausible structural properties\. Finally, generated networks show group\-specific errors, under\- or overestimating exposure to either Democrats or Republicans for specific social groups\. These findings show that evaluating LLM\-based social simulations only through aggregate outcomes can hide errors in the local environments through which those outcomes emerge, highlighting the importance of validation at both aggregate and individual levels\.

## [Toward a Civil Security Orientation: Bridging Research and Practice in Homeland Security and Emergency Management\. Insights from the 2nd Pracademic Emergency Management and Homeland Security Summit](../publications/9b36611f0eff760ae2eb.md)

Alexander Siedschlag

Abstract This article synthesizes proceedings and outcomes from the 2nd Pracademic Emergency Management and Homeland Security Summit, hosted virtually by Embry\-Riddle Aeronautical University’s Worldwide Campus College of Arts &amp; Sciences and its Virtual Collaboratory for Security and Resilience Education, Research, and Engagement\. Drawing on contributions from an international and interdisciplinary group of scholars, practitioners, students, policymakers, and professional organizations representing higher education, government, industry, and operational practice, the summit examined emerging challenges and future directions across homeland security, emergency management, resilience, public health, homeland defense, disaster planning, information disorder, artificial intelligence, ethics, and standards development\. Several cross\-cutting findings emerged\. First, preparedness and resilience increasingly require adaptive, inclusive, and whole\-community approaches grounded in trusted communication, social capital, functional needs inclusion, and meaningful stakeholder engagement\. Second, while artificial intelligence, remote sensing, and advanced decision\-support systems offer substantial operational promise, their implementation demands stronger attention to ethical oversight, interoperability, governance, and consensus\-based standards capable of translating technical capability into operational relevance\. Third, increasingly complex threat environments reinforce the need for critical thinking, scenario\-based learning, ethical reasoning, and career\-long professional development to prepare leaders to operate across institutional boundaries and under incomplete information\.

## [Functional Imaging of Hippocampal Layers Using VASO and BOLD on the Next Generation \( NexGen \) 7T Scanner](../publications/9b420e314137b8b14a1b.md)

Suvi Häkkinen; Alexander J\. S\. Beckett; Erica Walker; Laurentius Huber; David A\. Feinberg

Spatial accuracy and venous biases are a central concern in mesoscale fMRI, with subcortical brain regions facing additional challenges due to lower sensitivity, high physiological noise, and complicated vasculature\. Here, we optimized CBV VASO on the NexGen 7T scanner for layer\-specific investigations of the human hippocampus\. Both VASO and BOLD \(from the same acquisition\) detected significant hippocampal activation during an established autobiographical memory task\. At the macroscale, activation patterns converged, showing pronounced memory task activation in the anterior hippocampus and consistent engagement across the frontoparietal neocortex\. At the laminar scale, however, differences in depth\-dependent profiles emerged within the subiculum: BOLD exhibited a pronounced bias toward the inner layers, consistent with the known venous drainage pattern in the subfield\. Finally, the optimized effective TR of 3\.2 s allowed exploratory study of retrieval stages and neocortical functional connectivity, which both supported hippocampal anterior\-posterior dissociation using either VASO or BOLD\. Thus, hippocampal fMRI allows mapping layer function with high accuracy and can provide deeper insights into a number of neuropsychological phenomena and disorders\.

## [21\. Yüzyılda Kentsel ve Çevresel Dönüşüm: Politikalar, Uygulamalar ve Güncel Yaklaşımlar](../publications/9b6369c38b1f0397c6d8.md)



21\. yüzyıl, kentlerin yalnızca fiziksel olarak büyüdüğü değil; aynı zamanda ekonomik, toplumsal, teknolojik ve çevresel açıdan hızlı ve çok boyutlu bir dönüşüm geçirdiği bir dönemdir\. Hızlı kentleşme, iklim değişikliği, çevresel sorunlar, artan hareketlilik gereksinimleri, dijitalleşme ve değişen toplumsal ihtiyaçlar, kentlerin planlanması ve yönetilmesine ilişkin geleneksel yaklaşımların yeniden ele alınmasını gerekli kılmaktadır\. Bu süreçte kentsel ve çevresel dönüşüm, yalnızca yapıların veya fiziksel çevrenin yenilenmesiyle sınırlı olmayan; yaşam kalitesi, sürdürülebilirlik, yönetişim, teknoloji, ulaşım ve çevresel politikalar gibi farklı boyutları birlikte içeren kapsamlı bir süreç olarak değerlendirilmektedir\. “21\. Yüzyılda Kentsel ve Çevresel Dönüşüm: Politikalar, Uygulamalar ve Güncel Yaklaşımlar” başlıklı bu editörlü kitap dört bölümden oluşmaktadır\. Birinci bölümde; Adnan TETİKOL, “21\. Yüzyılda 24 Saatlik Kent: Kentsel Hizmetler ve Gece Yönetişimi İçin Bütünleşik Bir Yaklaşım” başlıklı çalışmasında, 21\. yüzyılın 24 saatlik kenti için zamansal erişilebilirlik, hizmetler arası eşgüdüm ve gece yönetişiminden oluşan üç düzeyli bütünleşik bir yaklaşım önermiştir\. İkinci bölümde; Ali KİRİKTAŞ, “Çin’in Latin Amerika’da Ekolojik Modernleşme Yaklaşımı: Kentsel Çevre Politikalarının Dönüşümü” başlıklı çalışması ile Çin’in Latin Amerika ve Karayipler \(LAK\) bölgesindeki ekolojik modernleşme stratejileri ve bu stratejilerin kentsel çevre politikaları üzerindeki dönüştürücü etkilerini kapsamlı bir analitik çerçeveyle incelemiştir\. ## [Resilient Event‐Triggered Control of Interval Type‐2 Fuzzy Systems via Functional Observers](../publications/9b713bfe882dce741f70.md)

Jie Yang; Shaoyan Gai; Feipeng Da

ABSTRACT This article addresses the resilient output‐feedback control problem for discrete‐time interval type‐2 \(IT2\) Takagi–Sugeno \(TS\) fuzzy systems operating under imperfect measurement and modeling uncertainties\. First, an adaptive saturation mechanism driven by an a priori predicted output is introduced to construct a saturation‐protected measurement signal and avoid algebraic‐loop issues in real‐time implementation\. Then, an admissible unknown‐input functional observer is developed to estimate the required augmented‐state function, and a rank‐condition‐based criterion is established for the solvability of the observer matching equations\. Next, a dynamic event‐triggered fuzzy controller is designed using the estimated functional variable, which compensates for the unknown‐input‐related component while reducing unnecessary signal transmissions\. Finally, by constructing a descriptor closed‐loop representation that incorporates the plant dynamics, observer error, transmission error, saturation residual, and MF mismatch, sufficient linear matrix inequality \(LMI\) conditions are derived to guarantee asymptotic stability and mixed performance\. The proposed framework offers an implementable solution for resilient unknown‐input functional‐observer \(UIFO\) based event‐triggered control of IT2 fuzzy systems\.

## [Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey](../publications/9b721734e5dc8ef7f0bf.md)

Ou Wu

Large language models \(LLMs\) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years\. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation\. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data\-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era\. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs&\#x27; training and application processes\. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other\. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs&\#x27; data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency\. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs&\#x27; training and inference\. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs&\#x27; data properties\. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others\. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories\. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs&\#x27; data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches\.

## [Dark Pattern Finder for Consumer Protection Web Extension](../publications/9b84c437c238cce3a013.md)

Mrs\. MANIMEGALA M; Madhusree M; Sangeetha M; SANMATHI PRIYA K S

The rapid growth of e\-commerce platforms and web\-based services has increased the use of user interface techniques designed to influence online decision\-making\. Among these techniques, dark patterns are deceptive or manipulative design practices that can mislead users, encourage unintended actions, or make it difficult to understand and control their choices\. Identifying such patterns manually across different websites is time\-consuming and requires considerable awareness of deceptive interface designs\. To address this challenge, this project titled “Dark Pattern Finder” presents an intelligent browser\-based system that automatically detects and identifies potential dark patterns present in web pages\.The proposed system utilizes Artificial Intelligence and machine learning techniques to analyze webpage content and identify suspicious interface patterns\. A browser extension collects relevant webpage information, including DOM elements, visible text, user interactions, and other behavioral evidence\. The collected information is processed by a backend detection system developed using Python and FastAPI\. A machine learning\-based classification model analyzes the extracted content and categorizes potential dark patterns such as scarcity and urgency, deceptive messages, forced actions, and other manipulative interface practices\. The system also provides confidence scores and supporting evidence to improve the transparency and interpretability of the detection results\.To enhance the reliability of detection, the proposed system integrates multiple analysis approaches, including DOM\-based analysis, behavioral observation, and state\-change information\. The detected patterns are presented directly through the browser extension using visual overlays and user\-friendly notifications, enabling users to understand potentially manipulative elements while browsing\. The system can also associate detected patterns with relevant legal and regulatory information to provide additional awareness regarding potentially deceptive practices\.

## [Remimazolam versus propofol for elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery: a randomized trial concentrating on delirium and hemodynamic stability](../publications/9b87f759ea7702f3a4ad.md)

Hongna Fan; Xiaotong Chen; Linlin Xu; Bin Zou; Da Li; Cheng Zhang; Jianyu Zu; Yugang Diao

Background Postoperative delirium \(POD\) is a common complication in elderly surgical patients that can impede recovery\. While remimazolam offers superior hemodynamic stability compared to propofol, its impact on POD incidence remains unclear\. This randomized trial aimed to determine whether two induction doses of remimazolam are more effective than propofol in reducing POD and improving hemodynamic stability in older patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery\. Methods In this prospective trial, 186 patients \(aged 60–80 years\) were randomized to receive anesthesia induction with remimazolam 0\.15 mg/kg \(R1\), remimazolam 0\.3 mg/kg \(R2\), or propofol 1\.5 mg/kg \(P\)\. The primary endpoint was the incidence of POD within 5 days post\-surgery, assessed using the 3\-Minute Diagnostic Interview for Confusion Assessment Method\. Secondary endpoints included hemodynamic parameters, recovery times, and adverse events\. Results The incidence of POD was 12\.9% in the R1 group, 11\.3% in the R2 group, and 6\.5% in the P group \( P = 0\.467\)\. Both remimazolam groups exhibited significantly higher mean arterial pressure following induction and intubation \(both P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Furthermore, remimazolam was associated with a lower incidence of treated hypotension \( P = 0\.010\), fewer bradycardia events \( P &lt; 0\.001\), and reduced vasopressor requirements \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. However, the time to loss of consciousness \( P &lt; 0\.001\) and extubation time \( P &lt; 0\.001\) were longer with remimazolam\. Conclusions Remimazolam at induction doses of 0\.15 mg/kg and 0\.3 mg/kg did not reduce the incidence of POD compared with propofol\. Nevertheless, the study was not adequately powered to exclude a clinically relevant difference in POD incidence given the substantially lower\-than\-expected event rate, as no statistically significant between\-group difference was detected\. In addition, remimazolam at these doses was associated with higher post\-induction blood pressure, fewer hypotensive events, and lower vasopressor requirements compared with propofol\. Therefore, remimazolam at these induction doses may serve as suitable alternatives for this vulnerable patient population\. Clinical trial registration https://www\.chictr\.org\.cn , Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400082176\.

## [STIMULI\-RESPONSIVE POLYMERS: DESIGN PRINCIPLES, POLYMER ARCHITECTURES, AND CONTROLLED FUNCTIONAL RESPONSES](../publications/9ba5360b7fbd4658f159.md)

Pradip Karale; Dipali Pagar; Agasti Ware; Seema Gosavi; Amit Narang; Nitin Sutar; Nilesh B Chaudhari; Saloni Borse; Anushka Pholane; Raosaheb S\. Shendge

Smart polymers undergo reversible physicochemical changes in response to stimuli such as magnetic fields, temperature, pH, light, and external reagents\. Advanced polymerization techniques, including reversible addition fragmentation chain transfer \(RAFT\), atom transfer radical polymerization \(ATRP\), and ring opening polymerization, enable precise control over polymer architecture and functional group placement, allowing the design of tailored responsive materials\. These polymers are widely explored in biomedical applications, drug delivery, biosensing, cosmetics, and soft robotics due to their ability to adapt dynamically to environmental conditions\. Poly\(N\-isopropylacrylamide\) is a well\-known thermoresponsive polymer extensively studied for drug delivery and sensing\. Responsive polymers exist in linear, block, graft, and cross\-linked forms, with activation depending on interactions between structural motifs and stimuli\. Despite promising results, challenges remain, including immunogenicity, batch variability, synthesis complexity, scalability, and limited understanding of in vivo stimulus accessibility\. Covalent adaptable and interpenetrating polymer networks enhance mechanical strength, biocompatibility, and stimuli responsiveness\.

## [Pink, Sarah ; Quilty, Emma ; Grundy, John &amp; Hoda, Rashina: Trust, artificial intelligence and software practitioners: an interdisciplinary agenda](../publications/9bb6d048ddae4b02ccdd.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 40 \(2\):639\-652\. 2025Trust and trustworthiness are central concepts in contemporary discussions about the ethics of and qualities associated with artificial intelligence \(AI\) and the relationships between people, organisations and AI\. In this article we develop an interdisciplinary approach, using socio\-technical software engineering and design anthropological approaches, to investigate how trust and trustworthiness concepts are articulated and performed by AI software practitioners\. We examine how trust and trustworthiness are defined in relation to AI across these disciplines, and investigate how AI, trust and trustworthiness are conceptualised and experienced through an ethnographic study of the work practices of nine practitioners in the software industry\. We present key implications of our findings for the generation of trust and trustworthiness and for the training and education of future software practitioners\. \(direct link \)

## [Digital Enforcement and Dignity Disequilibrium: A CARE\-Capability Perspective on Digital Public Services](../publications/9bbaa31e25a22d71eb8e.md)

Parijat Upadhyay; Manas Paul; Baidyanath Biswas

Digital technologies are essential to modern governance, as governments rely on them to deliver vital public services\. Although these initiatives aim to enhance efficiency, scalability, and transparency, they also raise concerns about digitally mediated access for citizens with varying levels of capability\. When access to entitlements depends on technology, barriers can arise that constrain citizens’ freedom to realise their entitlements and affect their sense of dignity\. Despite increasing focus on digital inequality, the dignity implications of digitally enforced public services remain unexplored in Information Systems \(IS\) research\. Drawing on CARE Theory and Sen’s Capability Approach, this study examines how digitally mediated governance reshapes citizens’ freedoms and generates dignity tensions\. Through an interpretive multiple\-case study of two large\-scale public digital governance systems in India: the CoWIN vaccination platform and the Jeevan Pramaan digital life certificates, we develop the concept of digital enforcement to explain how institutional reliance on digital infrastructure reconfigures access to benefits\. The findings uncover a mechanism in which narratives of reform translate into technology\-conditioned access that limits capability conversion and creates a dignity disequilibrium\. The study advances IS research by extending CARE Theory to digital governance and conceptualising digital enforcement as a governance mechanism shaping citizens’ lived experiences\.

## [A New Branch of Physics for the Age of Artificial Intelligence \- Nothingness as Temporal Singularity: Beyond Big Bang and Planck Epoch \-\-\- Theory of Everything](../publications/9bc726843b77fed8c165.md)

Khalid Masood

This paper introduces Meta AI Physics \(Meta Physics\) — a new branch of physics for the Age of Artificial Intelligence\. We propose a fundamental re\-interpretation of cosmological origin\. We argue: There is no Big Bang or bangs\. What existed was not infinite density at $10^\{32\}$ Kelvin compressed to subatomic scale\. Instead, Nothingness — as a singularity of time — serves as the foundation for creation, spanning from eternity to eternity\. This process continues incessantly\. Mass, energy, time, and nothingness — or simply &\#x27;nothing&\#x27; as a singularity of time — are interconnected\. We define: 1\. \* $c$ as $v\_T$:\* The constant $c$ is not speed of light, but speed of Time itself \(TER Theory\)\.2\. Photon: Quantum of a Moment \( $Q\_m$\)3\. Nothon \( $N\_0$\): Quantum of Nothingness, proposed Fifth Force and foundation of quantum vacuum equilibrium\. We firmly argue the so\-called Planck epoch \( $0$ to $10^\{\-43\}$ seconds\) does not actually exist\. The interval from zero to Planck time is an illusion\. ## [Feature\-token clinical transformer for 24\-h landmark mortality risk stratification in critically ill patients with heart failure: development and multicenter external validation](../publications/9bcd87e2cf53ecbf5b03.md)

Mianxian Li; Yuefei Zhou; Chun Li

Background The first 24 h after ICU admission in critically ill patients with heart failure yield heterogeneous EHR evidence across vital signs, laboratory tests, treatments, organ support, and nurse\-charted monitoring\. Conventional scores and flat\-vector ML models may not preserve individual variable identity or context\. Methods We developed FTCT, encoding each predictor recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission as a clinically tagged token \(value, missingness, identity, group\)\. MIMIC\-IV \(2008–2019\) served for development, validation, and internal testing; eICU\-CRD \(2014–2015\) served for external validation\. Included were adults with heart failure, a complete 24\-h ICU observation window, and known discharge status\. The endpoint was in\-hospital all\-cause death\. Results MIMIC\-IV included 11,156 stays and 1,484 deaths, partitioned into training \( n = 7,809\), validation \( n = 1,673\), and internal test \( n = 1,674\) sets\. eICU\-CRD included 9,837 stays and 1,319 deaths\. FTCT achieved an AUROC of 0\.849 \(95% CI, 0\.835–0\.863\) internally and 0\.804 \(0\.788–0\.820\) externally\. Patient\-paired AUROC differences vs\. XGBoost were 0\.027 \(0\.011–0\.043\) internally and 0\.032 \(0\.014–0\.050\) externally\. A matched FT\-Transformer\-style baseline achieved an external AUROC of 0\.781 \(0\.760–0\.801\)\. In eICU\-CRD, FTCT achieved an AUPRC of 0\.296 \(0\.278–0\.314\), Brier score of 0\.091 \(0\.085–0\.097\), and expected calibration error of 0\.036 \(0\.030–0\.042\)\. In a post hoc cohort\-specific descriptive operating analysis targeting approximately 85% specificity, external sensitivity was 0\.662 \(0\.636–0\.687\), positive predictive value 0\.406 \(0\.385–0\.427\), negative predictive value 0\.942 \(0\.937–0\.947\), and F1 score 0\.503\. Removing feature\-token encoding produced the largest ablation loss in external AUROC \(−0\.031\)\. Conclusions FTCT combines established feature\-token Transformer modeling with clinical\-group embeddings, explicit missingness representation, and group\-aware pooling for 24\-h landmark mortality risk stratification from structured EHR data recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission\. Its external validation and ablation results support prospective investigation, but do not yet demonstrate clinical utility, workflow integration, admission\-time applicability, or autonomous use\.

## [MCH\-02, a synthetic macamide analog with in vitro FAAH\-inhibitory activity, modulates hippocampal endocannabinoid system and BK channel expression without preventing PTZ\-induced progressive seizure susceptibility in rats](../publications/9bf1df5cb5705532f5a5.md)

Yessenia Yauri\-Huaman; Rodrigo Caceres\-Robles; Christell Becerra Flores; Miguel Garay\-Malpartida; Carlos Medina\-Saldivar; Luis F\. Pacheco‐Otálora

Epilepsy remains a major neurological disorder, with about 30% of patients showing drug resistance despite the availability of multiple antiseizure medications\. The endocannabinoid system \(ECS\) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target due to its role in regulating neuronal excitability\. This study examined the effects of a new macamide\-derived fatty acid amide hydrolase \(FAAH\) inhibitor, N \-\(8Z\-heptadecen\-1\-yl\)\- O \-\(3\-pyridylmethyl\) carbamate \(MCH\-02\), on seizure development, cognition, and hippocampal molecular markers in a chronic pentylenetetrazol \(PTZ\) kindling model in rats\. Behavioral measures \(Racine scale, survival, Barnes maze, and novel object recognition\) and molecular analyses \(RT\-qPCR and Western blot of CA1, CA3, and dentate gyrus\) were conducted\. MCH\-02 did not prevent PTZ\-induced progressive seizure susceptibility and initially worsened seizure severity\. Survival probability did not differ significantly among groups, and we observed no evidence of a protective effect on survival\. On a molecular level, MCH\-02 increased FAAH, Cnr1, and Napepld mRNA levels in the CA1 region\. It altered CB1 receptor and BKα1 subunit protein levels in the hippocampus, suggesting ECS remodeling and changes in potassium channel regulation\. Despite these molecular changes, behavioral protection was inconsistent, suggesting a complex and context\-dependent relationship between ECS function and intrinsic excitability\. Overall, MCH\-02 modulates molecular pathways associated with hippocampal endocannabinoid signaling and BK channel remodeling but does not demonstrate antiepileptogenic efficacy in the PTZ\-kindling model\. However, the surprising worsening of seizures highlights the importance of further research incorporating electrophysiological and pharmacokinetic studies to determine optimal dosing and therapeutic timing for FAAH inhibitors in chronic epilepsy models\.

## [AI\-Based Predictive Maintenance System for Electric Motor Fault Detection](../publications/9c0019656444e3b0f9c2.md)

Harshitha S, Keerthana B, Kruthika B Y, Prof\. Ravi Y C

The proposed work develops a cost\-effective IoT and artificial\-intelligence\-based predictive maintenance system for electric motor fault detection\. A BO geared DC motor is monitored using an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with DHT11, INA219, and MPU9250 sensors to measure temperature, current, voltage, and vibration parameters\. The collected sensor data are processed using time\-domain statistical features and transmitted through Wi\-Fi to a local server for analysis\. Machine learning models, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost, are employed and combined using a soft\-voting approach to improve fault classification\. The system categorizes the motor condition into normal, highcurrent, and maintenance\-required states\. In addition, vibration, current, and temperature trends are analyzed to provide early warnings before critical thresholds are reached\. Blynk IoT is used for remote monitoring, while automatic email notifications are generated when abnormal conditions persist\. The study demonstrates the feasibility of implementing an affordable real\-time predictive maintenance solution suitable for laboratories, small industries, and academic applications\.

## [Patient\-Derived Vs IPSC\-Derived Organoids: Complementary Platforms for Translational and Regenerative Medicine](../publications/9c003ee4463cf305e233.md)

Muhamad Farid Zulkifle; Roslina Husaini; Norodiyah Othman

Three\-dimensional \(3D\) organoid cultures have transformed the way researchers bridge the gap between conventional two\-dimensional \(2D\) systems and living tissue\. Here, we compare the two organoid platforms that now dominate biomedical research—patient\-derived organoids \(PDOs\) and induced pluripotent stem cell \(iPSC\)\-derived organoids—and consider how combining their strengths might shape the future of translational and regenerative medicine\. PDOs retain a donor&\#x27;s genetic, histopathological and phenotypic features, which makes them well suited to rapid, clinically relevant modelling of cancer, infectious disease and fibrosis; their main drawbacks are limited tissue availability, dependence on animal\-derived matrices, and an incomplete tumour microenvironment\. iPSC\-derived organoids, by contrast, can be expanded almost indefinitely and are readily amenable to genetic manipulation, making them attractive for developmental and rare disease research, although they tend to remain immature and are costly to produce\. We review several emerging approaches that address these shared limitations—co\-culture and organoid\-on\-a\-chip systems, multi\-omics integration, and vascularised assembloids—alongside the ethical and regulatory questions that both platforms raise\. Rather than competing technologies, we argue that PDOs and iPSC\-derived organoids are best treated as complementary tools, and that hybrid models combining patient specificity with scalability offer a promising way forward\. We also discuss the limitations of this narrative review, including its non\-systematic search strategy\.

## [FDUNet\-LRSA: efficient frequency\-adaptive segmentation for automated crop disease inspection](../publications/9c0a2f3e2ccafbe76b11.md)

Ru Han; Lei Shu; Grzegorz Cielniak; Yan Zhu; Jucheng Yang; Fan Yang; Weihan Song; Qian Zhang; Kai Huang

The transition toward industrialized and automated agriculture requires reliable machine vision for high\-throughput crop health monitoring and field decision support\. Automated sweetpotato disease inspection, however, remains challenging because field images exhibit substantial variations in leaf scale, appearance, illumination, occlusion, and background complexity\. Conventional U\-shaped networks rely primarily on fixed convolutional kernels and local feature aggregation, whereas Transformer\-based alternatives often introduce considerable computational overhead\. This article proposes FDUNet\-LRSA, a frequency\-adaptive segmentation network that integrates frequency\-domain dynamic convolution, low\-resolution self\-attention, and boundary\-aware refinement\. Frequency\-domain dynamic convolution reconstructs input\-dependent spatial kernels to improve feature adaptation under changing imaging conditions\. Low\-resolution self\-attention captures long\-range contextual dependencies in a fixed compact feature space, while boundary\-aware refinement preserves irregular leaf contours during mask reconstruction\. Under the reported evaluation protocol, FDUNet\-LRSA achieved a mean test foreground IoU of 0\.94 and a Dice coefficient of 0\.97, with 3\.72 GFLOPs\. Additional experiments indicate that task\-oriented moderate augmentation improves generalization compared with stronger augmentation\. The proposed network provides an efficient visual perception approach for automated crop inspection systems\.

## [Minimax\-optimal Scaling Laws in Ridge Regression via Transfer Learning](../publications/9c2930d2fa4d79292bf3.md)

Yalda Shabanzadeh; Diyuan Wu; Marco Mondelli

Pretrained models are often reused across downstream tasks, motivating the question of whether this transfer learning procedure can provide a substantial performance improvement, namely, in terms of the scaling law\. We address this question in the prototypical setting of high\-dimensional regression, where \(i\) a pretrained \\emph\{source\} model is trained via ridge regression, and \(ii\) a fine\-tuned \\emph\{target\} model is regularized via the $L\_2$ distance from the source estimator\. First, we establish a deterministic equivalent for the risk of this two\-step procedure under both model and covariance shift\. Next, by specializing the deterministic equivalent to a shared regression function and commuting power\-law covariance spectra, we identify a regime where the resulting scaling law achieves the minimax\-optimal exponent\. Notably, in this regime, the optimal source regularization depends on source data only, indicating its universality across all targets\. Furthermore, we show that the same optimal rate is achieved by performing the fine\-tuning step via one\-pass stochastic gradient descent\. We support our theoretical analysis via experiments on both synthetic settings and language models\.

## [Pathophysiology of REM sleep behaviour disorder](../publications/9c2cf27609dff2306a41.md)

Nita E Alpin; Kristijan D\. Jovanoski; Pietro‐Luca Ratti; David A\. Menassa; Laura Parkkinen

Abstract REM sleep behaviour disorder \(RBD\) is a parasomnia characterised by loss of muscle atonia and dream enactment behaviour during REM sleep\. RBD is recognised as a significant prodromal marker of α\-synucleinopathies, but characterising its unique neuropathological features is challenging due to reliance on individual case reports\. Additionally, RBD is not a terminal illness, and data generalisability is limited by the high co\-occurrence of α\-synucleinopathies\. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms responsible for altered REM sleep regulation in RBD, incorporating evidence from human postmortem histological analyses, structural and functional neuroimaging data on patients with RBD, and pharmacological studies\. We explore the risks, biomarkers, and mechanisms of phenoconversion from RBD to α\-synucleinopathies, drawing on data from large longitudinal patient cohorts, and we consider disease remission\. Lastly, we propose several promising directions for future studies\.

## [The minipig as a programmable translational platform for experimental oncofertility](../publications/9c377bc2c4a5e2ea350c.md)

Rodrigo Albertho Almeida Wedy; Lucas Damé Simões; Bruna Silveira Pacheco; Priscila Marques Moura de Leon; Fabiana K\. Seixas; Ligiane Leme; Luciano Abreu Brito; Ernesto Goulart; M\.L\. Dagli; Tiago Veiras Collares

Experimental oncofertility remains fragmented across models of cancer biology, treatment\-associated gonadotoxicity, fertility preservation, and reproductive recovery\. We propose extending the Oncopig concept into a translational platform that reconnects these states within one genetically defined, cancer\-bearing host\. The Oncopig provides the oncologic backbone, combining programmable cancer in an immunocompetent large\-animal host with clinically scaled intervention and longitudinal sampling\. High\-resolution porcine genomics, CRISPR\-based genome engineering, somatic\-cell nuclear transfer for line generation, comparative experimental pathology, and mature reproductive biotechnology extend this architecture toward reproductive endpoints\. Here, programmability refers to deliberate specification of the cancer state—genotype, cell lineage or induction strategy, and timing—whereas the reproductive phenotype is measured longitudinally rather than programmed\. Distant\-cancer modules can test whether cancer status modifies gonadotoxicity, while reproductive\-organ modules require disease\-specific alleles, appropriate cell\-of\-origin targeting, and pathology\-led validation\. Because porcine and human reproduction align in several endocrine and gonadal processes but differ in cycle organization, implantation, placentation, and pregnancy, translation should emphasize process\-level endpoints rather than numerical equivalence\. The platform is particularly suited to unresolved questions involving targeted therapies and immunotherapies, preservation timing, and pediatric or prepubertal patients\. Porcine reproductive biotechnology provides functional endpoints from gonadal tissue and gametes to embryos and offspring\. Rather than replacing rodent or human\-based models, the Oncopig framework adds an integrated translational layer for questions requiring clinically scaled intervention, longitudinal physiology, and functional reproductive recovery\.

## [SQL Injection: A Study of Attacks and Prevention Techniques](../publications/9c3cc8ee65532e79c033.md)

Amar S\. Ingle Prof\. Rana Afreen Sheikh; Prathamesh R\. Malviya

SQL injection is a database security vulnerability in which untrusted application input changes the meaning of an SQL statement\. The vulnerability occurs when an application allows user\-controlled values to become part of query structure rather than treating them only as data\. A successful attack can expose confidential information, alter records, or enable unauthorized database access\. This paper reviews the causes, consequences, attack classifications, detection approaches, and prevention techniques associated with SQL injection\. The literature indicates that no single detection or prevention mechanism addresses every attack condition\. Static analysis, runtime validation, automated testing, and behavior\-oriented detection address different stages of the problem, while parameterized queries provide the central application\-level defense\. Input validation, carefully designed stored procedures, controlled error handling, and least\-privilege database accounts provide additional protection

## [Gillies, Donald: Artificial Intelligence and Scientific Method](../publications/9c43f3578421c3da90ab.md)



Artificial Intelligence and Scientific Method examines the remarkable advances made in the field of AI over the past twenty years, discussing their profound implications for philosophy\. Taking a clear, non\-technical approach, Donald Gillies shows how current views on scientific method are challenged by this recent research, and suggests a new framework for the study of logic\. Finally, he draws on work by such seminal thinkers as Bacon, Gödel, Popper, Penrose, and Lucas, to address the hotly\-contested question of whether computers might become intellectually superior to human beings\. \(direct link \)

## [Robustness of neural networks for CMB polarization foreground removal](../publications/9c4f9c4f2ac5a605d25f.md)

Luca Gomez Bachar; Cora Dvorkin; Alberto Daniel Supanitsky

The detection of Cosmic Microwave Background primordial $B$\-mode polarization would constitute a \`\`smoking gun&quot; signal of primordial gravitational waves\. However, this measurement requires accurate removal of polarized Galactic foregrounds to avoid systematic biases when estimating the tensor\-to\-scalar ratio\. Methods based on Machine Learning techniques \(ML\), such as Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\), have recently been proposed as alternative foreground cleaning techniques, but their applicability to real data relies on their ability to generalize beyond the models assumed during training\. In this work, we focus on a variety of foreground models \(FMs\) used for training and conduct a systematic study of the generalization properties of a CNN\-based method\. We train various CNN architectures on simulations generated from different Galactic FMs, and test their performance on models not used during the training\. By characterizing the statistical properties of the FMs using variance, skewness, and Shannon entropy, we define a statistical complexity hierarchy among them\. We show that training on the more complex FMs reduces bias and improves precision when testing on unseen FMs, whereas training on the simplest model could introduce systematic errors\. These results evidence that a lack of generalization is a relevant source of systematic uncertainty, and emphasize the importance of understanding the impact of the models assumed during training in ML\-based methods before applying them to real data\.

## [Reinforcement learning deficits in at\-risk mental state for psychosis: the role of primary negative symptoms](../publications/9c545a6f27ce771a8009.md)

Anson Kai Chun Chau; James A\. Waltz; Joe Kwun Nam Chan; Tracey Chi Wan Chan; Hoi Ching Lee; Sui Fung Wo; Cheuk Fei Wong; Suet In Chan; Sanyin Chiu; Christy Lai Ming Hui; Sherry Kit Wa Chan; Edwin Ho Ming Lee; Eric Yu Hai Chen; Wing Chung Chang

Negative symptoms such as amotivation begin to emerge in the at\-risk mental state for psychosis \(ARMS\), and in some cases, these symptoms are idiopathic \(i\.e\., primary negative symptoms, PNS\)\. While deficits in reinforcement learning \(RL\) are evident in patients with first\-episode and chronic schizophrenia and are associated with the severity of negative symptoms, whether these deficits are present during ARMS warrants further investigation\. Additionally, it is unclear whether these deficits, especially those driven by rewards, are particularly characteristic of ARMS individuals with PNS\. This study compared 97 ARMS individuals and 37 healthy controls \(HC\) on probabilistic RL\. We then compared ARMS individuals with PNS \(n = 15\), those without PNS \(n = 82\), and HC on probabilistic RL\. Reward\- and punishment\-driven RL \(both trial\-by\-trial and procedural\) and value\-guided choice were assessed using two probabilistic RL tasks: Go/NoGo \(GNG\) and Gain vs\. Loss\-Avoidance \(GLA\) tasks\. Compared with HC, ARMS individuals showed impairments in overall procedural RL on both RL tasks, as well as subtle, task\-specific alterations in value\-guided choice\. Furthermore, ARMS\-PNS individuals, relative to HC, showed particular deficits in reward\-driven RL \(trial\-to\-trial RL on GLA task and procedural RL on both tasks\), as well as impaired positive expected value representations to guide decision\-making on GLA task\. Extending the results in patients with established psychosis, our findings indicate that deficits in RL exist before the onset of a psychotic disorder\. With a modest sample of ARMS\-PNS individuals, preliminary evidence suggests that deficits in reward\-driven RL may be more specific to PNS\.

## [Adopting Smart Technologies for Sustainable Tourism: Challenges and Opportunities for Nashik Kumbh Mela](../publications/9c5712d4105e46ced90e.md)

Chandrashekhar Pawar; Yogesh Gaikwad

Adopting Smart Technologies for Sustainable Tourism: Challenges and Opportunities for Nashik Kumbh Mela Chandrashekhar Pawar Research Scholar, MET’s Institute of Management \(Affiliated to Savitribai Phule Pune University\), Nashik, Maharashtra, India Dr\. Yogesh Gaikwad Professor &amp; Research Guide, MET’s Institute of Management \(Affiliated to Savitribai Phule Pune University\), Nashik, Maharashtra, India Abstract Tourism is the key tool for socio\-economic development\. The Nashik Kumbh Mela is one of India’s major religious gatherings, attracting millions of pilgrims and creating substantial demands on transportation, sanitation, accommodation, public safety, waste management, and environmental resources\. This study examines the adoption of smart technologies for promoting sustainable tourism during the Nashik Kumbh Mela, with particular emphasis on both opportunities and implementation challenges\. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, Internet of Things \(IoT\), smart mobility systems, GIS\-based crowd monitoring, digital payment platforms, mobile applications, and data analytics can improve visitor management, resource efficiency, safety, and tourist experiences\. Their integration may also support waste reduction, traffic control, energy conservation, and effective destination governance\. The inadequate digital infrastructure, implementation costs, cybersecurity risks, digital literacy gaps, interoperability issues, and stakeholder coordination remain significant challenges\. The study highlights the need for an integrated smart\-tourism framework combining technological innovation, environmental sustainability, inclusive governance, and community participation to facilitate efficient and sustainable management of the Nashik Kumbh Mela\. Keywords: Smart Tourism, Sustainable Tourism, Nashik Kumbh Mela, Smart Technologies, Artificial Intelligence, IoT, Crowd Management, Destination Governance

## [Admission METS\-IR in relation to severe acute pancreatitis among patients with hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/9c5d6462dfd6a78962ae.md)

Ziyi ZHANG; Changwei Peng; Hong Peng; Zhu Yuanxia; Chenghu Huang; Li Rong

Background Hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis \(HTG\-AP\) is accompanied by significant metabolic abnormalities, but few studies have investigated whether a composite measure of this metabolic burden is associated with severe acute pancreatitis \(SAP\)\. The metabolic score for insulin resistance \(METS\-IR\), derived from fasting glucose, high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and body mass index, can be calculated from routinely available clinical data without requiring an insulin assay\. However, its association with SAP in HTG\-AP remains poorly characterized\. Objective This study investigates the association between admission METS\-IR and SAP in patients with HTG\-AP and assesses the robustness of this association through subgroup and sensitivity analyses\. Methods We retrospectively assembled a single\-center cohort of 456 adults admitted with HTG\-AP between January 2019 and July 2025\. Logistic regression evaluated METS\-IR as a continuous exposure and in quartiles\. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed\. Exploratory ROC analyses compared apparent discrimination with TyG, TyG\-BMI, and BISAP\. Results SAP occurred in 78 of 456 patients \(17\.1%\)\. Median METS\-IR was 69\.99 \(IQR, 61\.92–83\.67\) in the SAP group and 58\.18 \(IQR, 51\.47–66\.46\) in the non\-SAP group\. In Model 3, each one\-point increase in METS\-IR was associated with higher odds of SAP \(OR, 1\.06; 95% CI, 1\.04–1\.08\)\. After additional adjustment for TG, TG/HDL\-C, and TyG, the estimate was attenuated \(OR, 1\.03; 95% CI, 0\.997–1\.064; P = 0\.073\)\. Apparent AUCs were 0\.730 for METS\-IR, 0\.720 for TyG, and 0\.758 for BISAP; neither paired comparison showed a statistically significant difference\. In the three\-category analysis, the METS\-IR association was stronger for SAP vs\. MAP than for MSAP vs\. MAP\. Conclusion Higher admission METS\-IR was independently associated with higher odds of SAP in patients with HTG\-AP\. METS\-IR may provide a readily available measure of metabolic burden for early clinical assessment of patients with HTG\-AP, although its clinical utility requires confirmation in prospective multicenter studies\.

## [Routing Optimization for The Traveling Salesman Problem with Drones \(TSP\-D\) in Medical Supply Distribution](../publications/9c776c23f54eadbb503f.md)

Yutong Ha; Tae Seung Kim

The integration of drones into last\-mile logistics has emerged as a transformative solution to address the inefficiencies of traditional truck\-based delivery in smart cities\. This study investigates the Traveling Salesman Problem with Drones \(TSP\-D\) specifically within the context of medical supply distribution in Qingdao, China\. A hierarchical two\-stage optimization methodology is proposed: first, the service area is partitioned into optimal subregions using the k\-means clustering algorithm, with the number of clusters determined by the silhouette coefficient\. Second, a mixed\-integer programming model is formulated and solved using Gurobi to optimize synchronized routing within each cluster\. Based on a dataset of 169 customer locations, computational experiments demonstrate that the framework identifies seven efficient clusters and significantly enhances delivery performance\. The findings indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to reduce response time and improve operational efficiency in medical supply distribution\.

## [Learning Rational Strategies for Temporal Objectives in Multi\-Agent Systems](../publications/9c8320e27060362d1c9e.md)

Omar Adalat; Edwin Hamel\-De le Court; Francesco Belardinelli

We study rational synthesis for stochastic multi\-agent systems with unknown dynamics, where each agent is equipped with its own probabilistic temporal objective specified using Probabilistic Linear Temporal Logic on Finite Traces \($\\mathsf\{PLTL\}\_f\}$\)\. We impose solution concepts \(e\.g\., Nash equilibrium, subgame\-perfect equilibrium\) as constraints on the joint strategy profile, using payoffs derived from each agent&\#x27;s probability of satisfying its temporal objective\. In particular, we formulate per\-agent rational synthesis as finding a strategy profile \-\- if one exists \-\- such that \(i\) the designated agent&\#x27;s probabilistic temporal constraint is satisfied, and \(ii\) the profile represents a stable solution under a chosen solution concept\. We give conditional convergence guarantees for tabular Nash\-Q learning, certify satisfaction with simultaneous finite\-sample confidence bounds, and assess strategic stability with approximate best\-response checking\. Our approach operates in a stochastic \\emph\{Multi\-Agent Reinforcement Learning\} \(MARL\) environment, where model\-free learning algorithms attempt to attain extremal satisfaction probabilities for temporal objectives automatically compiled into reward automata\. Our approach is empirically validated using 8 general\-sum concurrent stochastic games\.

## [Design and Implementation of an Integrated Cross\-Platform Privacy Management Architecture Using a Rule\-Based Privacy Enforcement Algorithm \(RBPEA\) for Cross\-Platform Social Media Systems](../publications/9c86213af797e28ef13b.md)

Sabir Umar Danillela

The widespread use of multiple social media platforms has increased user exposure to privacy risks due to fragmented and complex privacy controls\. Users are required to configure separate privacy settings across different platforms, often leading to inconsistent configurations, privacy fatigue, and unintended data disclosure\. Existing privacy mechanisms remain largely platform\-specific and do not provide unified or user\-centred control across platforms\. This study aims to design, implement, and evaluate an integrated architecture for protecting user privacy across social media platforms\. The proposed system employs a Rule\-Based Privacy Enforcement Algorithm \(RBPEA\) to translate user\-defined privacy preferences into platform\-specific enforcement actions\. Using the Design Science Research methodology, a modular, web\-based prototype was developed, incorporating secure user authentication, centralized privacy rule management, and cross\-platform enforcement through platform adapters\. The system was evaluated based on enforcement consistency, usability, and system performance\. Results indicate improved consistency of privacy settings across platforms, reduced user effort in privacy configuration, and enhanced transparency through audit and feedback mechanisms\. The findings demonstrate that algorithm\-driven, integrated privacy management is both feasible and effective for improving user privacy control in multiplatform environments\. This study contributes an empirically evaluated architectural model and algorithmic approach for cross\-platform privacy protection, addressing a significant gap in existing privacy management solutions\.

## [ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD\-BASED PREDICTIVE APPROACHES FOR HOSPITAL READMISSION: A STRUCTURED REVIEW OF SOCIOECONOMIC VARIABLES AND ALGORITHMIC EQUITY](../publications/9c8aa4c3c4f90cfc9a92.md)

Maciej Kamil Majchrzak; Faustyna Magdalena Kołodziej; Krzysztof Konopka; Mateusz Lis; Zuzanna Julia Komin; Maryan Liasota; Eliza Zofia Kabat; Jakub Juskowiak; Alicja Kwiatkowska; Michalina Justyna Kozłowska

Background: Hospital readmission rates are often used to judge the quality of care and how well healthcare systems are working\. Predictive models based on electronic health records \(EHRs\) can help estimate which patients are at higher risk, but when they don’t properly reflect socioeconomic realities, they can unintentionally reinforce existing inequalities \(Obermeyer et al\., 2019\)\. This review looks at how well these EHR\-based models predict 30\-day readmissions, how Social Determinants of Health \(SDOH\) are included, and what this means for fairness and health equity in real\-world use\. Methodology: A structured literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar\. It included peer\-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2026, focusing on model validation studies, retrospective cohort analyses, and research on bias and fairness in predictive healthcare models\. Results: Synthesis reveals that incorporating unstructured and structured SDOH variables yields mixed impacts on discriminatory performance \(Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve changes ranging from \-0\.01 to \+0\.04\), yet significantly rectifies systemic algorithmic underestimation of risk for marginalized demographics\. Unadjusted models consistently show racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic bias, often because they rely on proxy variables embedded in historical healthcare data \(Gianfrancesco et al\., 2018\)\. As a result, preventive transition\-of\-care resources can be systematically directed away from the patients who need them most \(Pierson et al\., 2021\)\. Conclusion: To make predictive healthcare tools truly useful in practice, it is not enough to focus only on accuracy\. They also need to account for fairness, real clinical context, and the actual consequences of their use in everyday healthcare settings \(Wiens et al\., 2019\)\. Policy\-level interventions must mandate standardized SDOH extraction alongside equity\-focused calibration algorithms before widespread clinical deployment \(Ghassemi et al\., 2021\)\.

## [Redefining Audit Efficiency: A Model for Streamlined Financial Reporting in Nigerian Chartered Accounting Practices](../publications/9c8cc08fcd60acb335e1.md)

Ifeoma E\. Okoli

This critical review examines how Nigerian chartered accounting practices can redefine audit efficiency and streamline financial reporting\. It applies a structured thematic synthesis of 250 DOI\-verified, peer\-reviewed and institutional sources published through 2022, coding the evidence across four dimensions: conceptual definition, causal mechanism, empirical support, and implementation constraint\. Grounded in agency theory, audit\-quality theory, institutional \(isomorphism\) theory, and lean process\-efficiency theory, the synthesis shows that efficiency in Nigerian audit practice follows from standardized workflows, risk\-focused procedures, independent audit\-committee oversight, staff capability, and timely review, while professional judgment continues to protect audit quality where formal controls are weak\. Unlike prior single\-determinant studies of Nigerian audit quality, which typically isolate one governance variable at a time, this review&\#x27;s contribution is an integrative operating model that connects audit inputs, workflow design, review discipline, reporting accuracy, and engagement performance into a single framework, together with four testable propositions and a Nigeria\-specific research agenda for stronger validation, transparency, and institutional comparison\. The review also proposes a repositioned role for chartered accounting firms as active drivers, rather than passive recipients, of digital transformation, continuous auditing, and regulatory reform in Nigeria&\#x27;s financial reporting ecosystem\.
