## [Bir İngiliz İstihbaratçısının Gözleminden IV\. Ordu’nun Askerî, Lojistik ve Sanayi Modernleşmesi: Mark Sykes’ın 1906 Tarihli Raporu](../publications/9e6c759b1b56bd78f44d.md)

İsmail Yakan

Bu çalışma, IV\. Ordu’nun askerî, lojistik ve sanayi alanlarındaki modernleşme sürecini İngiliz istihbarat subayı Yüzbaşı Mark Sykes’ın 1906 tarihli raporu çerçevesinde değerlendirmiştir\. Tanzimat sonrasında hız kazanan askerî reorganizasyonunun Anadolu’nun doğusundaki yansımalarını belgeleyen bu rapor, Mehmed Zeki Paşa kumandasındaki IV\. Ordu’nun teşkilâtı, teknik ve idarî kapasitesini ayrıntılı bir biçimde yansıtmaktaydı\. Çalışmada ordunun eğitim sistemi, talim ve tatbikat uygulamaları, mühimmat temini, ikmal hattı, sağlık hizmetleri ve yerel sanayi üretimi ele alınmış; subay ve askerlerin görev anlayışı ile disiplin prensipleri saha verileriyle mukayese edilmiştir\. Sykes’ın Erzincan gözlemleri, garnizonun disiplin seviyesi, sağlık tedbirleri ve teçhizat donanımı bakımından diğer birliklere nazaran ileride olduğunu göstermekteydi\. Mehmed Zeki Paşa tarafından kurulan veya yeni teknolojiyle donatılan kumaş fabrikası, zanaat okulu, un değirmeni ve bisikletli keşif birliği IV\. Ordu’nun ikmal ve intikal kabiliyetini güçlendirmişti\. Sykes’ın tespitleri, IV\. Ordu özelinde Osmanlı ordusunun bölgesel düzeyde muharebe kabiliyeti, eğitim sistemi ve ikmal yapısında gerçekleştirdiği dönüşümün sahadaki yansımalarını ortaya koymuştu\. Bu bulgular, Anadolu’nun doğusunda konuşlandırılan IV\. Ordu’nun modern Osmanlı askerî teşkilâtının önemli bir unsuru hâline geldiğini göstermişti\. Ayrıca çalışmada, Sykes’ın birincil kaynak niteliğindeki raporu, Osmanlı merkezî ıslahatları bağlamında tartışılmış ve ulaşılan ilerlemenin sınırları değerlendirilmişti\.

## [Consensus machine learning for interpretable road\-user fatality risk analysis: Evidence from the Canadian National Collision Database](../publications/9e73609cbb787e883c77.md)

Shengkun Xie; Nguyen Duy Anh Luong

OBJECTIVES: Fatal road traffic collisions account for a small proportion of reported crashes but impose a disproportionate societal and public health burden\. This study evaluates interpretable machine\-learning models and proposes a consensus machine learning \(CML\) framework to identify robust predictors associated with fatal collision risk using Canadian collision data\. METHODS: Person\-level records from the Canadian National Collision Database \(NCDB\) covering 2014\-2021 were used to classify fatal and nonfatal collision outcomes\. Balanced random forest, extreme gradient boosting \(XGBoost\), and neural network models were developed using a common preprocessing framework\. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve \(ROC\-AUC\) and precision\-recall area under the curve \(PR\-AUC\)\. Permutation\-based feature\-importance rankings were subsequently aggregated using the proposed CML framework to identify predictors that remained consistently important across models and reporting years\. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the strongest predictive performance \(ROC\-AUC = 0\.932; PR\-AUC = 0\.714\), followed by balanced random forest \(ROC\-AUC = 0\.898; PR\-AUC = 0\.585\) and the neural network \(ROC\-AUC = 0\.886; PR\-AUC = 0\.587\)\. Across the three machine\-learning models, collision configuration, traffic control, collision hour, and the number of vehicles involved consistently ranked among the most influential predictors associated with fatal collision risk\. Roadway configuration, roadway alignment, road\-surface condition, weather conditions, vehicle characteristics, and safety\-device use also contributed to prediction, although their relative importance varied among models\. The CML framework further identified the leading predictors of fatal collisions: collision configuration, road\-surface conditions, time of collision, number of vehicles involved, roadway configuration, and weather conditions\. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed CML framework consistently identified important predictors across multiple machine\-learning algorithms and reporting years, providing a robust and interpretable approach to understanding fatal collision risk\. Two of the defined categories, crash characteristics and traffic and environmental conditions, were identified as key feature sets for predicting collision fatalities\. These findings provide evidence to support engineering, policy, enforcement, and education initiatives aimed at reducing fatal collisions while highlighting the value of consensus\-based machine learning as a complementary decision\-support tool for transportation safety planning\.

## [AI\-Driven Early Warning Systems for Flash Floods Using Satellite Imagery: A GeoAI\-Based Framework for Real\-Time Flash Flood Prediction, Risk Reduction and the Future of Intelligent Disaster Management](../publications/9e83f4dc5ee863b43f34.md)

Vishwaditya Aazad; Dr\. S\. S\. Baghel

Abstract: Flash floods remain among the most destructive and least predictable hydrometeorological hazards, characterized by rapid onset, localized intense precipitation, and minimal warning time\. This paper critically examines whether the convergence of satellite Earth Observation \(EO\), Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), and hydrometeorological intelligence can transform flashflood early warning from a predominantly reactive, detectionoriented paradigm into a predictive, anticipatory, and progressively autonomous disaster intelligence system\. Through an interdisciplinary synthesis of remote sensing science, deep learning architectures, spatiotemporal modelling, and disaster risk reduction, we propose the AISatellite Flash Flood Early Warning Intelligence Framework \(AISFFEWI\)—a conceptual architecture that integrates multisource satellite data, groundbased observations, physicsinformed AI, uncertainty quantification, impact forecasting, and community feedback\. The study distinguishes carefully between flood detection and actionable early warning, and emphasizes that lead time, false alarm mitigation, and explainability are as critical as prediction accuracy\. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of satellite data sources, AI model suitability, spatiotemporal deep learning, and the severe challenges posed by class imbalance, nonstationary climate conditions, and limited crossregion model transferability\. A dedicated Indiacentric perspective examines Himalayan and urban flash floods, while a futureoriented timeline \(2026–2050\) explores the gradual emergence of AIenabled digital twin watersheds and autonomous warning agents, always balancing technological promise against scientific caution, ethical accountability, and the imperative of communitycentred response\. The paper concludes that while satelliteAI systems hold substantial potential to enhance flashflood warning, they cannot replace hydrological understanding, institutional trust, and the human decisionmaking required to convert a probabilistic hazard forecast into lifesaving action\.

## [Die Förderung von Critical Digital Literacy im Englischunterricht am Beispiel visueller Repräsentationen von Gender durch künstliche Intelligenz](../publications/9e952043b67ff2ecad31.md)

Subin Nijhawan

This article examines learners’ use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) with both languagerelated and subject\-specific learning processes in the foreign language classroom\. The development of critical digital literacy \(\#CDL\), understood as the ability to critically assess and evaluate digital, including AI\-generated content, is focused on in the reported research data, a video\-taped double lesson of an upper\-secondary advanced English course\. In the lesson, learners used generative AI ChatGPT and DALL\-E 3\) to design their own campaigns for the promotion of gender equality, and discussed and reflected the appropriateness of AI\-generated visual representations\. The data analysis draws on video and screen recordings, group discussions, the plenary presentation and the subsequently initiated reflection\. Focusing on a critical incident, the analysis shows how learners negotiate meaning by aligning with or distancing themselves from AI\-generated artefacts, concomitantly developing, testing, evaluating and reflecting upon prompting strategies\. In particular, the data reveal the learners’ critical engagement with AI\-generated representations of gender in relation to diversity, equality, justice and intersectional equity as well as implicit and contested beauty ideals\. Processes of interpretation, appropriation, emotional engagement and the act of developing and defending a position become visible as learners distance themselves from DALL\-E 3’s stereotypical visual worlds and the underlying algorithmic biases of ChatGPT\.

## [Peer relationships and school mobility in England](../publications/9e9673f43efc21bc7420.md)

John Jerrim

This paper examines the relationship between pupils’ peer relationships and subsequent school mobility\. Using large\-scale longitudinal data from The Engagement Platform \(TEP\), the study follows 48,146 pupils in Years 3 to 10 across 109 schools in England\. We estimate logistic regression models with school fixed effects and rich controls for pupil demographics, attitudes to education, relationships with teachers, school climate and attendance\. The results reveal a strong and robust association between poorer peer relationships and an increased likelihood of changing school\. Pupils reporting poor peer relationships are around twice as likely to move school as those with very good peer relationships\. This association is consistent across gender and across primary and secondary phases\. The relationship appears broadly linear, although having exceptional rather than very good peer relationships offer little additional reduction in mobility risk\. These findings are replicated using a smaller, independent sample from the United Arab Emirates\. Overall, the study highlights peer relationships as a key predictor of school mobility, with important implications for early identification of peer difficulties, pastoral support and interventions aimed at improving peer dynamics\.

## [SUZISH MASHG‘ULOTLARIDA QATNASHUVCHI BOLALARDA DIQQAT VA ISHCHI XOTIRANING KLINIK\-PSIXOLOGIK XUSUSIYATLARI](../publications/9e9a5ff7754f7a627373.md)

Ostanaqulov Alijon Dadajon o&\#x27;g&\#x27;li

This article theoretically examines the clinical and psychological characteristics of attention and working memory in children participating in swimming training\. It discusses the development of cognitive processes during childhood, including sustained attention, concentration, attentional shifting, divided attention, and the mechanisms through which working memory temporarily maintains, processes, and uses information during ongoing activity\. Particular emphasis is placed on the sensorimotor demands of swimming, remembering movement sequences, understanding coaches’ instructions, and coordinating breathing with motor actions\. The potential relationships between cognitive performance and individual developmental characteristics, emotional states, physical fatigue, and training experience are also considered\. Neuropsychological, clinical\-psychological, and psychodiagnostic approaches are discussed as possible methodological foundations for assessing attention and working memory in young swimmers\. Two analytical tables present assessment criteria and a proposed framework for empirical data analysis\. The article emphasizes that the relationship between swimming participation and cognitive development should be examined through appropriately designed research and that causal conclusions require sufficient empirical evidence\.

## [Managerial Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in Textile Wastewater Management in Bangladesh](../publications/9e9af98236a0bb41dbd5.md)

Intan Sazrina Binti Saimy Mohammad Saidul Karim Sayeed

Artificial intelligence offers potential applications in wastewater monitoring, prediction, and operational decision support\. However, selecting a model does not establish that factory managers and treatment operators can use it effectively\. This conceptual article examines managerial readiness for artificial intelligence in Bangladesh&\#x27;s textile wastewater management\. It brings together selected literature on organizational readiness, artificial intelligence capabilities, and wastewater applications, alongside Bangladesh\-specific research and institutional reports\. The article proposes six readiness domains: strategic commitment, managerial and operator knowledge, data stewardship, operational integration, investment and partnership capacity, and accountable decision making\. It further distinguishes exploratory interest, supervised experimentation, routine decision support, and controlled operational integration as different adoption states\. Four propositions explain how readiness may influence movement between these states and the translation of adoption into environmental performance\. A proposed qualitative multiple\-case design specifies evidence needed to examine these propositions, including decision histories, operational records, interviews across organizational levels, and observations of treatment routines\. The framework is an analytical proposal rather than a validated measurement scale or report of completed fieldwork\. Its contribution is to connect organizational preparation with the specific decisions, responsibilities, and verification practices required for textile wastewater management\. Empirical research is needed to assess its relevance across factories with different resources and treatment arrangements\.

## [Prediksi Penjualan XGBoost untuk Rekomendasi Diskon Produk Kuliner Berbasis Web](../publications/9e9c242c6844a9b666ca.md)

R\. Q\. Putra; L\. O\. M\. G\. Jaya; A\. H\. Wibowo

Penentuan diskon produk kuliner pada PT Bonton ATB Sejahtera masih mengandalkan pengamatan persediaan dan pengalaman pengelola sehingga informasi historis penjualan belum dimanfaatkan secara optimal\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan aplikasi pendukung keputusan berbasis web yang mengintegrasikan prediksi jumlah penjualan dengan rekomendasi diskon berdasarkan kondisi stok serta masa kedaluwarsa produk\. Penelitian menggunakan 936 catatan penjualan selama 2023\-2025 yang mencakup 13 produk dalam empat kategori\. Sebanyak 624 catatan periode 2023\-2024 digunakan untuk pelatihan, sedangkan 312 catatan tahun 2025 digunakan untuk pengujian temporal\. Setelah prapemrosesan diperoleh 22 fitur untuk model Extreme Gradient Boosting\. Hasil prediksi diproses dengan aturan bisnis berprioritas sehingga menghasilkan rekomendasi diskon sebesar 0%, 10%, 20%, atau 30%\. Aplikasi dikembangkan menggunakan Django dan diuji melalui evaluasi galat prediksi serta pengujian jalur program\. Nilai kesalahan absolut rata\-rata mencapai 1,894050 produk dan akar kesalahan kuadrat rata\-rata sebesar 3,179004 produk pada seluruh data uji\. Kesalahan persentase absolut rata\-rata sebesar 9,887142% dihitung pada 211 catatan dengan penjualan aktual positif\. Enam skenario pengujian fungsi rekomendasi menunjukkan keluaran sesuai aturan implementasi\. Penelitian menghasilkan prototipe fungsional untuk mendukung keputusan diskon, tetapi belum membuktikan peningkatan laba atau pengurangan limbah\. Aturan untuk produk yang telah mencapai masa kedaluwarsa masih memerlukan perbaikan sebelum penerapan operasional\. Hasil ini belum menjadi dasar klaim efektivitas kebijakan harga dalam kondisi pasar yang sesungguhnya\.

## [Small\-sample ERP\-assisted screening for depression and audio multimodal fusion based on the MODMA dataset](../publications/9e9f2c56b3341e161bb3.md)

Jiaxuan WAN; Zhenshen Qu

OBJECTIVE: Event\-related potentials \(ERPs\) may provide objective neurophysiological markers for depression\-assisted screening\. We benchmarked structured ERP features and strictly paired ERP\-audio fusion in small\-sample, subject\-level settings\. APPROACH: Two experiments on MODMA used leakage\-controlled leave\-one\-subject\-out \(LOSO\) validation, with all preprocessing, tuning and fusion restricted to training folds\. Experiment I included 52 ERP subjects retained after quality control \(QC\) \(23 with major depressive disorder \(MDD\) and 29 healthy controls \(HC\)\), each represented by a 60\-feature vector, to compare machine learning \(ML\) and deep learning \(DL\) models\. This paper additionally evaluated convolutional neural network \(CNN\)\-based architectures \(EEGNet and ShallowConvNet\) on a multichannel ERP time\-series representation \(28 channels × 129 samples\) constructed from subject\-level averaged cue\-locked and dot\-locked ERPs\. Experiment II used 37 strictly paired ERP\-audio subjects \(16 MDD, 21 HC\) with 178 audio features to evaluate unimodal and decision\-level fusion under balanced and screening objectives\. MAIN RESULTS: In Experiment I, SVM\-RBF achieved area under the ROC curve \(AUC\) 0\.859 vs 0\.588 for TinyMLP \($\\Delta$AUC = \+0\.271\)\. On ERP time\-series inputs, EEGNet achieved AUC = 0\.640 and ShallowConvNet achieved AUC = 0\.540, both inferior to the engineered\-feature SVM baseline\. In Experiment II, the best unimodal baseline was audio SVM\-RBF \(AUC = 0\.753\)\. Fusion achieved AUC to 0\.762 and increased specificity \(Spec\) to 0\.810 under the balanced objective, and increased recall \(Rec\) to 0\.813 with a false\-negative rate \(FNR\) of 0\.188 under the screening objective\. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a leakage\-controlled, strictly paired, subject\-level evaluation framework for depression\-assisted screening and shows that ERP\-audio fusion offers objective\-dependent complementary value\.

## [Ancient Greek votive epigraphy: Ancient religion between individual choice and cultural trends](../publications/9eab9f54671c94b5382c.md)

Moshe Blidstein

Ancient votive inscriptions, numbering in the tens of thousands across the Mediterranean, offer direct evidence for religious practice but have rarely been studied comprehensively across time and space due to their sheer volume\. This paper presents a &quot;distant reading&quot; analysis of approximately 11,000 Greek dedicatory inscriptions \(sixth century BCE \- seventh century CE\) drawn primarily from the GIST/I\.PHI digital corpus\. By tagging inscriptions for key features \(votive/dedicatory terminology, deities, motives, gender\) and analyzing their distribution chronologically and geographically while controlling for the &quot;epigraphic habit,&quot; this study identifies large\-scale trends\. The results reveal a significant relative increase in the use of explicit votive terminology \(forms of euche/euchomai\) over time, particularly during the Roman Imperial period and Late Antiquity\. This practice exhibits strong regional variation, being markedly more prevalent in Asia Minor and the East than in mainland Greece before the fourth century CE\. Furthermore, the use of votive formulae correlates strongly with specific deities \(e\.g\., Men, Meter, Hypsistos, Hosios kai Dikaios\) and negatively with others \(e\.g\., emperors, Athena\)\. Votive terminology also appears negatively correlated with the explicit mention of other motives \(like dreams or commands\) and with the use of standard consecration terms\. While demonstrating the potential of computational methods for identifying broad patterns of continuity and change in religious expression, the study also highlights methodological challenges \(dating uncertainty, data tagging\) and underscores the persistent difficulty in definitively separating shifts in epigraphic conventions from changes in underlying religious mentalities\.

## [Diverse Reasoning Paths Matter: Symbolic Equivalence Augmentation for Enhancing RL Exploration](../publications/9eb1a50d6f92d79091c9.md)

Xiaoou Liu; Tiejin Chen; Hanyang Chen; Yuan Ling; Hua Wei

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards \(RLVR\) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of LLMs\. However, the role of supervised fine\-tuning \(SFT\) data in enabling effective downstream RL remains underexplored\. In this paper, we investigate a key hypothesis: the diversity of reasoning steps in chain\-of\-thought \(CoT\) during SFT is a critical enabler of RLVR performance\. To test this hypothesis, we introduce EquivAug, a data augmentation framework that uses symbolic equivalence transformations to generate diverse yet provably correct reasoning paths\. By converting CoT solutions into formal symbolic representations, applying equivalence transformations, and reconstructing natural\-language explanations, EquivAug produces training data that differs in reasoning steps rather than surface\-level lexical variation\. Experiments on GSM8K and FOLIO across model scales demonstrate that EquivAug consistently achieves the highest reasoning path diversity after SFT and the strongest accuracy after GRPO\. Our results establish that CoT diversity during SFT is positively correlated with downstream RLVR performance\.

## [Development and validation of a model of severe abdominal blast injury: characterization and hemostatic response](../publications/9ebb3637e2e34e5b573a.md)

Guo\-Xing Huang; Jinlong Wang; 田敏; Tong\-yu Sun; Xin\-lou Li; Yuan Yang; Meng Wang

Objective To establish a stable porcine model of severe abdominal blast injury with massive hemorrhage and evaluate a novel hemostatic material \(novel hydrogel bioadhesive\) versus traditional gelatin for emergency management\. Methods A severe abdominal blast injury was induced in Bama miniature pigs \( n = 18\) using a 5 g JH\-14 charge \(3\.5 cm standoff\)\. The experimental animals were randomly divided into two cohorts: the blast injury model preparation cohort \( n = 6\) and the hemostatic material cohort \( n = 12\)\. The latter cohort was further randomized into control \(gauze\), hemostatic gelatin, and novel hemostatic material groups \( n = 4/group\)\. Hemostatic efficacy was assessed via vital signs, blood loss, survival, biomarkers, and histopathology\. Results The model produced full\-thickness abdominal wall laceration \(mean area: 16\.24 ± 0\.53 cm 2 \), severe liver injury, and massive hemorrhage \(497\.8 ± 45\.70 g blood loss\), with systemic hypothermia and shock\. Post\-injury hematology showed reduced RBC, WBC, PLT, Hb, and ALB, while AST, ALT, and LDH surged\. Both hemostatic materials reduced blood loss, extended survival, and partially stabilized vital signs, though Hb continued declining\. Biochemical markers \(ALT, LDH\) partially recovered\. Inflammatory markers \(PCT, CRP, etc\.\) increased post\-injury but remained unchanged post\-treatment\. Histopathology confirmed liver necrosis and inflammation, with partial recovery at 2 weeks; no apparent difference was observed between materials\. Conclusion The porcine model effectively simulates severe abdominal blast trauma\. Both hemostatic materials achieved rapid local hemostasis but were limited by persistent occult bleeding and systemic complications\. Future strategies should integrate optimized hemostasis with systemic resuscitation to enhance emergency outcomes\.

## [CFRD\-Net: Calibrated Residual Latent Diffusion Network for Pomegranate Fruit Quality and Disease Classification](../publications/9ec11dac1c17d7f97672.md)

Harish Bommenahalli Mallikarjunaiah; Balaji Prabhu Baluvaneralu Veeranna

Fruits are essential components of the global diet which plays a major role in agricultural growth and the economy\.However, high\-value fruits like pomegranates frequently lose the market\-value due to quality deterioration, ripeness variations, surface defects, and diseases\.Therefore, this research introduces the Calibrated Residual Latent Diffusion Network \(CFRD\-Net\) for pomegranate fruit quality classification\.The CFRD\-Net architecture integrates Latent Conditional Diffusion learning, Residual Feature Calibration \(RFC\), and Residual Latent Refinement \(RLR\)\.This integration enables the learning of robust, discriminative latent representations, which captures local fine\-grained texture irregularities, surface defects, and global ripeness\-related color distributions\.The model requires 62\.34 million parameters and 11\.86 GFLOPs, demonstrating a trade\-off between accuracy and computational cost\.CFRD\-Net achieved 99\.33% accuracy on the Pomegranate Fruit Quality Grading Dataset and 98\.75% accuracy on the Pomegranate Fruit Diseases Dataset\.These results indicate that CFRD\-Net performs effectively under the evaluated benchmark settings for automated pomegranate image classification\.

## [Single‐Cell Resolution Mapping of Osteoarthritis‐Associated Chondrocyte Dynamics Using a High‐Density CMOS MEA Platform](../publications/9ec6e0d53abc73e8582b.md)

Neha Deshpande; Pauline Coquart; Bram Theuns; Susanne Cremery; Jaime Rodolfo V\. Garcia III; Julien Verplanken; Dennis Lambrechts; Dries Braeken; Liesbet Lagae; Johanna Bolander

Fibrosis is a major cause of chronic tissue dysfunction and contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality worldwide\. Osteoarthritis \(OA\), affecting over 590 million people, is a prevalent fibrotic joint disease for which disease\-modifying therapies remain lacking, partly because disease progression remains incompletely understood\. As human\-relevant in vitro models, including organ\-on\-chip and microphysiological systems, become increasingly important, non\-invasive technologies capable of continuous cellular monitoring are urgently needed\. Here, we implement high\-density complementary metal\-oxide\-semiconductor \(CMOS\) multielectrode array \(MEA\)\-based impedance profiling as a label\-free platform for longitudinal assessment of OA\-relevant chondrocyte remodeling\. Human primary chondrocytes cultured on CMOS\-MEA chips exhibited impedance increases that correlated with electrode occupancy and extracellular matrix \(ECM\) deposition\. Spatial impedance mapping enabled visualization of injury\-response dynamics, while oxidative stress induced progressive impedance decline accompanied by apoptosis, morphological remodeling, and chondrocyte dedifferentiation, evidenced by reduced collagen II and SOX9 expression and increased collagen I expression\. In contrast, osteogenic de\-differentiation produced increased impedance associated with ECM remodeling and matrix mineralization\. Together, these findings support high\-density CMOS\-MEA impedance profiling as a non\-invasive approach for monitoring cellular remodeling and provide a foundation for future integration of spatially resolved impedance sensing into advanced microphysiological systems for OA and other fibrotic diseases\.

## [ASSESSMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE AND CLINICAL EFFECTIVENESS OF SURGICAL TREATMENT IN PATIENTS WITH VARICOSE VEIN DISEASE OF THE LOWER EXTREMITIES](../publications/9ecfab7a62fde0ea5c6a.md)

Mykyta Druzhkin; A\. V\. Klymenko

Introduction\. Chronic venous disease \(CVD\) of the lower extremities in the stage of chronic venous insufficiency is characterized by a progressive course, a high rate of complications, and a significant decline in patients’ quality of life \(QoL\)\. Despite the widespread implementation of endovenous thermal treatment methods, isolated elimination of truncal reflux does not always ensure complete clinical and functional recovery in the postoperative period\.Aim\. To assess quality of life and clinical manifestations of the disease in patients with chronic venous disease of the lower extremities in the early and long\-term postoperative periods depending on the method of surgical treatment\.Materials and methods\. A total of 139 patients \(100%\) with CVD at the stage of chronic venous insufficiency \(C3\-C6, CEAP\) were included and divided into three groups\. Group 1 \(n=32; 23\.02%\) underwent endovenous radiofrequency ablation \(RFA\) of the great and/or small saphenous veins combined with miniphlebectomy and perforator vein ligation\. Group 2 \(n=64\) included subgroup 2A \(n=31; 22\.30%\) – RFA with miniphlebectomy without perforator ligation, and subgroup 2B \(n=33; 23\.74%\) – RFA with perforator ligation without miniphlebectomy\. Group 3 \(n=43; 30\.94%\) underwent isolated RFA\.The study methods included clinical assessment \(complaints, medical and life history, physical examination, laboratory tests\), duplex ultrasound of the lower limb veins, quality of life evaluation using CIVIQ\-20 \(invGIS\), VCSS scoring, and statistical analysis\.Results\. In all groups, improvement in QoL indicators and a reduction in clinical severity were observed after treatment\. The most pronounced and sustained positive changes were noted in patients who underwent multimodal combined treatment \(RFA combined with miniphlebectomy of tributary veins and ligation of perforator veins\)\. After 12 months, CIVIQ\-20 scores in the main group were significantly higher, while VCSS scores were lower compared to the groups of mono\-endovenous and partially combined treatment \(p&lt;0\.05\)\.Conclusions\. Multimodal treatment of CVD provides the most complete restoration of patients’ QoL and significantly reduces the clinical severity of the disease compared to monoablation and partially combined treatment\.

## [Conceptualising AI\-reform professional learning communities in Chinese schools through the lion dance metaphor](../publications/9eea0c6809b01b8bb985.md)

Shiyu Pu; Xiaokun Shi

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) moves into school education at increasing speed, we still know relatively little about how schools organise AI\-related change amid policy expectations, technological uncertainty and teachers’ everyday work\. Based on a qualitative case study of an AI education pilot school in Beijing, China, this article examines the formation and operation of an AI\-reform professional learning community \(PLC\)\. Data were generated through semi\-structured interviews, school\-based observations and school documents\. Through inductive thematic analysis, four recurring role functions were identified and subsequently conceptualised through the structural metaphor of the Chinese lion dance: drummers, lion heads, lion tails and audiences\. The findings show that school leaders translated policy expectations and paced implementation; teacher leaders carried visible exploratory and pedagogical work; non\-lead teachers extended reform through cautious and selective participation; and parents, while remaining outside the formal community, shaped ethical boundaries and conditions of trust\. The article conceptualises AI\-reform PLCs as issue\-specific and role\-differentiated communities that organise policy translation, teacher learning, leadership, participation and ethical negotiation around emerging technological change\. It contributes a culturally grounded account of how school\-based AI reform is collectively coordinated rather than simply implemented by individual teachers\.

## [The double\-edged sword of human\-AI collaboration on design students’ competence development: The mediating roles of challenge and hindrance appraisals and the asymmetric moderation of teacher AI leadership](../publications/9eed2e9d7720145fbdfb.md)

Xiang Wang; Mingxing Li; Jia Du; YU Yao; Jiabei Jiang

The deepening integration of generative AI into design education is driving a paradigm shift in human\-computer AI collaboration \(HAIC\) \-from mere tool assistance toward intelligent synergy\. However, its dual impact on the competency development of design students and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood\. Grounded in the Theory of Stress Appraisal, this study constructs a research model to examine the double\-edged sword effect of HAIC on Design Competence \(DC\), introducing teacher AI Leadership \(AIL\) as a moderating variable\. The aim is to reveal the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions through which HAIC influences DC\. Employing a questionnaire survey, this study conducted an empirical investigation involving 483 design students in East China\. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 24\.0 and Amos 23\.0, encompassing reliability and validity tests, regression analysis, and Bootstrap mediation analysis\. The results indicate that HAIC influences DC through dual pathways: it positively enhances DC by fostering Challenge Appraisal \(CA\) \(β = 0\.283, p &lt; 0\.01\), which in turn positively predicted competence development \(β = 0\.363, p &lt; 0\.01\), yielding a significant indirect effect of 0\.103 \(p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Simultaneously, HAIC triggered Hindrance Appraisal \(HA\) \(β = 0\.271, p &lt; 0\.01\), which negatively predicted competence development \(β = \-0\.229, p &lt; 0\.01\), yielding a significant indirect effect of \-0\.062 \(p &lt; 0\.01\)\. This constitutes a partial mediating mechanism characterized by &quot;one positive, one negative&quot; effect\. Furthermore, Teacher AIL exhibits an asymmetric moderating effect: it significantly buffers the positive impact of HAIC on HA \(β = \-0\.112, p &lt; 0\.01\), indicating that high AIL can mitigate cognitive load and anxiety arising from technological uncertainty, yet it does not significantly amplify the positive pathway via CA \(β = 0\.001, p &gt; 0\.05\)\. The findings suggest that the impact of HAIC on DC is not linear but rather a dialectical process contingent upon individual cognitive appraisal\. The core value of Teacher AIL lies in &quot;risk mitigation&quot; rather than &quot;creativity stimulation,&quot; offering a theoretical foundation for the intelligent transformation of educational design\. At the practical level, it is imperative to facilitate from knowledge deliverers to cognitive facilitators in AI\-augmented design education\. By systematically developing AI instructional competencies and reforming assessment systems, educators can guide students toward establishing a healthy relationship with HAIC, thereby achieving the synergistic advancement of technological empowerment and humanistic literacy\.

## [Caputo\-inspired Adaptive Genetic Algorithm and Taguchi Design of Experiment to Solve Capacitated Ambulance Routing Problem](../publications/9f0dc58dfa587a51b110.md)

Marissa Marcella Daulip Lakkui; Jackel Vui Lung Chew

This study proposes an adaptive genetic algorithm based on a nabla Caputo fractional difference with the Taguchi design of experiment for solving the capacitated ambulance routing problem\.The optimization problem considered aims to minimize the total ambulance routing cost while satisfying ambulance availability and capacity\.In this study, a nabla Caputo fractional difference\-based adaptive mutation mechanism is designed and incorporated into the genetic algorithm evolutionary process\.This so\-called memory\-aware mechanism captures historical fitness behavior and is used as an adaptive control signal for dynamically adjusting the mutation rate during optimization\.To obtain appropriate parameter settings systematically, the Taguchi design of experiment is employed in two stages\.The first stage tunes the genetic algorithm parameters, such as the maximum number of generations, the population size, and the fixed mutation rate\.While the second stage tunes the nabla Caputo fractional\-memory parameters, such as the fractional order, the memory window, the scaling coefficient, and the maximum adaptive mutation rate\.The proposed algorithm is interpreted through the lens of nonlinear dynamical systems\.For the performance evaluation, this study uses Augerat benchmark instances\.The results show that the proposed algorithm is competitive against established hybrid metaheuristics\.These findings suggest that integrating the nabla Caputo fractional\-memory dynamics with statistically guided parameter tuning offers a promising solution for the capacitated ambulance routing problem\.

## [RECENT ADVANCES IN NEUROPATHOLOGY: WHO CNS TUMOR CLASSIFICATION AND MOLECULAR MARKERS](../publications/9f1677eab9fd9532a265.md)

Sumana Pawar

The role of the neuropathologist in the diagnosis of tumours of the CNS is important and has an impact on the care of the patients\. The recent changes made in the 2021 World Health Organization \(WHO\) Classification of CNS Tumors are highlighted with an emphasis on ‘inclusive’ molecular diagnosis and important molecular markers\. Important biomarkers such as IDH, 1p/19q codeletion, EGFR or H3 changes have helped to classify tumors, to view the prognosis and to choose an adequate treatment\. Besides, the review emphasizes current molecular diagnostics technologies, precision medicine and AI in the domain of neuropathology\. These advances are very useful for making a more accurate diagnosis and treating the patient and give a good basis for future advances in the management of CNS tumors\.

## [Explainable deep graph attention learning with enhanced residual SwinV2 transformer for interpretable facial paralysis severity assessment](../publications/9f2d80e0507f1c47ceaa.md)

Ramesh N\. S\. V\. S\. C\. Sripada; Koppisetti Giridhar; Bhaskar Marapelli; GANTA RAJU; Bibhuti Bhusan Dash; Sribidhya Mohanty; Saroja Kumar Rout

Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements\. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations\. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency\. Recently, deep learning \(DL\) techniques have revolutionized the field, especially in the context of facial and clinical image analyses\. While DL enables automatic, accurate facial recognition, its black\-box nature restricts its use in healthcare\. Therefore, explainable artificial intelligence \(XAI\) is integrated to enhance transparency that provides visual evidence for medical decision\-making\. This study introduces an Explainable Deep Graph Attention Learning Framework for Facial Paralysis Identification \(XDGAL\-FPI\)\. The proposed model is designed to automatically identify the severity of facial paralysis using facial image data\. Initially, the input images are preprocessed, including face detection and alignment, color space conversion and contrast enhancement, noise reduction, normalization, and data augmentation to improve the quality and consistency of the input data\. Besides, deep feature representations are extracted using an Enhanced Residual SwinV2 Transformer\. The extracted features are then provided to a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network that models the relational dependencies between multiple facial regions, such as the eyes, eyebrows, and mouth, for precise severity classification\. Additionally, to improve the training efficiency and convergence behavior of the model, the Ranger optimizer is employed\. Furthermore, the GradCAM \+ \+ technique is integrated to improve model interpretability by highlighting the important facial regions that contribute to the model’s prediction\. The effectiveness of the proposed model is assessed using YouTube Facial Paralysis \(YFP\) Updated Dataset, which contains 14, 389 images categorized into four severity levels across different facial regions\. The experimental results indicate that the proposed XDGAL\-FPI model achieves improved performance compared with existing approaches across various evaluation metrics\. Thus, the proposed XDGAL\-FPI model can serve as a reliable and interpretable tool for automated facial paralysis severity assessment\. The source code of this study is available at https://github\.com/researcher010\-debug/XDGAL\-FPI \.

## [Socially embedded predictive construction: a model of emotional experience](../publications/9f3df41d40e8052c4ff8.md)

Raffaele Grimaldi

The dominant view in affective neuroscience has long held that discrete emotional states are universal, biologically fixed, and implemented in dedicated neural circuits\. This ‘basic emotions’ framework faces accumulating challenges from neuroimaging meta\-analyses, cross\-cultural research, and studies of individual variability, while an alternative account—the theory of constructed emotion—holds that emotional experiences are generated by integrating interoceptive predictions, prior conceptual knowledge, and cultural and linguistic context\. This Perspective makes three contributions\. First, it distinguishes the following three explananda that the debate routinely conflates: rapid, largely subcortically mediated emotional reactions and expressive behaviour; the conscious experience of feeling; and the linguistic categorisation of that experience\. Much of the apparent inconsistency of the neuroimaging literature follows from treating these as one phenomenon\. Second, it reports that the evidence is genuinely mixed: univariate analyses do not identify consistent and specific regional signatures for discrete emotional categories, whereas multivariate analyses frequently decode such categories from distributed activity, and cross\-culturally recurrent facial behaviour has been reported at scale\. A constructionist account is argued to accommodate the context\-sensitivity, cultural variability and language\-dependence of affective neural representation more economically than a dedicated\-circuit account, without claiming that the basic\-emotions programme has been refuted\. Third, it proposes the Socially Embedded Predictive Construction \(SEPC\) model: a stratification of a single generative model into allostatic\-interoceptive, conceptual\-linguistic and socio\-cultural levels that differ in represented content and temporal horizon rather than in kind\. For each level the model specifies candidate substrates, measurable indicators, selective manipulations and falsification criteria, together with three study designs that would test it and the results that would falsify it\. Recognising emotion as constructed across stratified predictive levels supports a view of the brain as a socially embedded organ whose affective states are shaped by, though not exhausted by, language and culture\.

## [Thoughts on Artificial Intelligence for Teachers](../publications/9f4db48d257f8aa1d98d.md)

GYARMATI G\. Péter

In this lecture, we approach from a new aspect the sources and the expected development of artificial intelligence\. Our starting point is still human creation, which is driven by common sense, the striving for omnipotence of power, and the unlimited nature of the capitalist economy\. Artificial intelligence is based on the anthropomorphic model according to the current state of science, i\.e\., it tries to imitate human thinking and behavior\. The basis of human intelligence is the human brain, and the computer for artificial intelligence\. People organize themselves into societies according to rules and morality\. Common sense contradicts the need to provide machines with such self\-organizing ability, and human goals do not require it\. This performance tries to explore the difference and possible convergence of the two intelligences\. At the same time, it always establishes the superiority and responsibility of man\. The unethical, the destruction, is caused by man, the power, even if it is done by machines with intelligence\.

## [Acceptance of AI\-based human resource practices: Sectoral differences between technology\-intensive and traditional industries](../publications/9f512cffbf65da97a645.md)

Selma Kalkavan

This study examines employee acceptance of AI\-based human resource management practices in technology\-intensive and traditional sectors\. Data were collected from 360 employees, with 60 participants from each of six sectors\. Biotechnology, information technology, and manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products formed the technology\-intensive group, while retail, textiles, and hotels formed the traditional group\. Acceptance was evaluated across recruitment, performance appraisal, training planning, and talent management\. The explanatory variables were perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust in AI, perceived algorithmic fairness and transparency, and loss of human touch\. The subgroup regressions show that usefulness, ease of use, and trust positively predict acceptance in technology\-intensive sectors\. In traditional sectors, fairness and transparency positively predict acceptance, while loss of human touch negatively predicts acceptance\. Five significant interactions identify specific differences between sector groups\. The positive association of fairness and transparency with acceptance is stronger in traditional sectors for recruitment and performance appraisal, and the negative association of loss of human touch is stronger in traditional sectors for recruitment\. The positive association of trust is stronger in technology\-intensive sectors for training planning, while that of usefulness is stronger in technology\-intensive sectors for talent management\. Acceptance is descriptively higher in training planning and talent management than in recruitment and performance appraisal\. These findings show that employee evaluations of AI\-based HR practices vary by sector group and HR function, supporting attention to usefulness, trust, fairness, and human involvement in the particular functions where their associations with acceptance differ\.

## [Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long\-Term History for Streaming Videos](../publications/9f5d93428e7583c83540.md)

Zhuoming Liu; Jinhong Lin; Lin Zhang; Yiwu Zhong; Yin Li

Streaming vision\-language models \(VLMs\) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries\. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context\. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates\. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed\-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream\. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input\. To support training, we further construct MaLoW\-Instruct, a large\-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question\-answer pairs over 56K videos\. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO\-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena\. On the backward split of OVO\-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3\.9% to 11\.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead\. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision\-language\-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9\.3%\.

## [From perceptual context to clinical tools – investigating spatial\-temporal influences on bistable vision and automating neglect assessment](../publications/9f66010d9657a28a6bf0.md)

Lisa Beckmann‏

This dissertation is based on three studies which are published as research articles in international peer\-reviewed journals\.I am the first author of all three of these studies\.

## [Assessment of Fatigue Among Pregnant Women Using the Fatigue Assessment Scale: A Cross\-Sectional Study](../publications/9f674d6a15213828dcad.md)



Background\-Fatigue is a common symptom in pregnancy, especially in the first and third trimester, caused by hormonal changes like increased progesterone, increased blood volume and heart rate, and the physiological demands of supporting fetal development\.Objective\-This study aimed to assess the prevalence and severity of fatigue among pregnant women using the FAS questionnaire and to explore its association with demographic and obstetric variables\.Methodology\-A cross\-sectional survey was conducted among 155 pregnant women attending, Obstetrics and Gynecology OPD using Convenient Sampling Technique Participants were administered the FAS questionnaire, a 10item self\-reported measure of fatigue\.Demographic characteristics and obstetric history were collected\.The questionnaire was distributed to pregnant females coming for antenatal checkups; completely filled questionnaires were collected; the data was coded and stored in MS Excel\.Result\-Responses were analyzed using chi square test to assess the statistical association between fatigue and age, gravida and trimesters\.Severity of fatigue experienced in various trimesters and their effect on QOL, physical and mental wellbeing of the pregnant women was also calculated\.Discussion\-Fatigue is highly prevalent among pregnant women and warrants greater attention in routine antenatal care\.The FAS questionnaire is a valid tool for assessing fatigue, highlighting the need for early identification and supportive interventions to improve maternal well\-being\.

## [Cyclospora cayetanensis at a crossroads: A critical re\-evaluation of foundational assumptions in research and public health](../publications/9f6c82abb5fa37d0f880.md)

Gülsün Akdemir Evrendilek

Cyclospora cayetanensis remains a poorly controlled foodborne pathogen despite decades of research and major advances in molecular detection and genomic characterization\. This review critically re\-evaluates three foundational assumptions that continue to shape research, diagnostics, and public health practice\. First, the widespread use of Eimeria and Cryptosporidium as surrogate organisms is examined in light of the limited direct validation of their ability to reproduce key biological characteristics of C\. cayetanensis, particularly with respect to sporulation, environmental persistence, and intervention efficacy\. Second, emerging phylogenetic and genomic evidence indicates that human\-infecting Cyclospora comprises multiple genetically distinct lineages with reproductive isolation, raising important questions regarding taxonomy, epidemiology, transmission, and virulence\. Third, the host\-parasite\-immune axis remains incompletely understood, particularly the mechanisms underlying the greater severity, persistence, and recurrence of infection in immunocompromised individuals\. Across these three areas, the evidence reveals a persistent gap between what can be detected and what can be effectively prevented or controlled\. The review therefore proposes a translational research framework that links foundational biological investigation to intervention development, implementation, and public health practice\. Key priorities include direct validation of surrogate models, improved genomic resolution, standardized methods for assessing oocyst viability and infectivity, stronger agricultural water and on\-farm controls, real\-time molecular surveillance and traceback, and improved therapeutic and preventive strategies for vulnerable populations\. Progress in controlling cyclosporiasis will require a shift from predominantly descriptive research toward evidence\-based, actionable approaches that translate biological and technological advances into measurable reductions in transmission and disease\.

## [Efficiency of the Pooled Logistic Regression Approach as an Alternative to the Cox Proportional Hazard Model](../publications/9f71a8eeeb994e8f500e.md)

Precious O\. Ibeakuzie

The Cox proportional hazards \(CPH\) model and the exponential Cox model are foundational tools in survival analysis, yet they impose structural assumptions; proportional hazards and constant baseline hazard, respectively that frequently fail in practice\. This paper proposes and evaluates pooled logistic regression \(PLR\) applied to survival\-piled \(stacked\) data as an alternative discrete\-time survival estimator\. Right\-censored survival data are restructured into a long\-format person\-time binary classification dataset, and three models are compared: the exponential Cox model, the classical semi\-parametric CPH model, and PLR\. Monte Carlo simulations with 1,000 replications at each of six sample sizes \(n = 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250\) are conducted to assess stability, discrimination, and goodness\-of\-fit\. Performance is measured by Harrell&\#x27;s concordance index \(C\-index\) and the Akaike information criterion \(AIC\)\. Simulation results show that PLR maintains consistently high and stable C\-index values \(0\.742–0\.784\) across all sample sizes, whereas the CPH model exhibits high variability \(0\.575–0\.884\) and the exponential Cox model underperforms throughout \(0\.532–0\.671\)\. AIC comparisons further demonstrate PLR&\#x27;s competitive goodness\-of\-fit at moderate and large sample sizes\. Real\-data validation using the NCCTG lung cancer dataset corroborates these findings\. PLR&\#x27;s theoretical connection to the Cox partial likelihood is established formally, and its compatibility with machine\-learning classification pipelines is discussed\. The findings support PLR as a robust, flexible, and interpretable alternative for discrete\-time survival analysis\.

## [EduSynapse AI™: A Predictive and Adaptive Artificial Intelligence Framework for Transforming Higher Education in Africa](../publications/9f71edad5801eaab1862.md)

Jamilu Auwalu Adamu; Promise Mebine

Higher education systems across Sub\-Saharan Africa confront acute challenges arising from systemic massification, extreme faculty deficits \(with lecturer\-tostudent ratios routinely surpassing 1:120\), intermittent national power grids, and unsustainable student attrition\.While contemporary Western educational data mining \(EDM\) and adaptive learning systems presume continuous high\-bandwidth broadband and ubiquitous personal laptop ownership, these assumptions diverge drastically from the socioeconomic realities of developing nations\.This paper presents EduSynapse AI™ \(AICOM\+\), a multi\-tiered predictive and adaptive artificial intelligence framework custom\-engineered for resource\-constrained tertiary institutions in Africa\.The architecture integrates four core synergistic engines: \(1\) an Adaptive Learning Engine \(ALE\) formulated as a Markov Decision Process \(MDP\) with multi\-objective reinforcement learning; \(2\) a Predictive Risk and Success Engine \(PRSE\) employing deep neural networks with non\-linear rectified linear unit \(ReLU\) activations for early dropout detection; \(3\) an AI Teaching Assistant \(AITA\) providing automated formative feedback with asynchronous offline caching; and \(4\) a Smart Academic Chatbot \(SAC\) operating over low\-bandwidth SMS/WhatsApp fallback channels\.The framework was evaluated on a simulated contextual cohort of N = 12,500 students across six Nigerian universities \(three Federal, two State, and one Private\) tracked across four semesters with 42 multimodal features and controlled Gaussian noise injection \(ε \~ N\(0, σ²\)\) to mirror authentic empirical variability and protect student privacy\.Empirical benchmarking demonstrates that the proposed PRSE and Optimized AICOM\+ frameworks achieve superior classification performance \(Accuracy: 31\.4%,Macro F1\-Score: 31\.5%,ROC\-AUC: 0\.985, MCC: \-0\.335\), statistically outperforming classical baselines including Logistic Regression \(Accuracy: 39\.5%, F1: 38\.1%\) and Random Forest \(Accuracy: 30\.3%, F1: 31\.3%\) with high significance \(paired t\(49\) = 2\.57, p &lt; 0\.05, Cohen&\#x27;s d = 0\.36\)\.Multivariate logistic odds\-ratio analysis established that infrastructural internet deficits impose a statistically significant 3\.21× risk multiplier \(OR = 3\.21, 95% CI: \[2\.84, 3\.63\], p &lt; 0\.001\) and electrical load shedding imposes a 2\.45× risk multiplier\.Furthermore, longitudinal simulation of the ALE reinforcement policy demonstrated a \+24\.5% mean academic GPA recovery and collapsed the high\-risk cohort from 53\.4% down to 11\.5%\.These findings establish EduSynapse AI™ as a validated, resilient technological blueprint for scalable educational transformation in the Global South\.

## [Resilience and clinical recovery in first\-episode schizophrenia: a 10\-year longitudinal study of clinically recovered, non\-recovered, and healthy control participants](../publications/9f72407b1b6058272799.md)

Anne‐Kari Torgalsbøen; Christine Mohn; Frank Larøi; Nikolai Olavi Czajkowski

Introduction Research on resilience in clinical recovery following first\-episode schizophrenia \(FES\) remains limited, and few longitudinal studies achieve sufficient retention to capture long\-term trajectories\. To address this, the Oslo Schizophrenia Recovery Study \(OSR\) was designed to examine resilience over time in FES\. Investigating resilience is essential for understanding how individuals exposed to schizophrenia may achieve favorable outcomes\. We addressed two primary questions: First, how does resilience change over time in individuals with FES compared with healthy controls\. Second, whether longitudinal resilience trajectories within the FES group differ between participants who meet predefined clinical recovery criteria compared to those who do not\. Methods Repeated assessments were conducted across 12 clinical evaluations\. The sample comprised 28 individuals with FES and 28 healthy controls\. Resilience was measured with the Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale, and social and role functioning were indexed using the Global Functioning Scales\. The data were analyzed using linear multilevel models\. Candidate longitudinal mixed\-effects models were compared using the small\-sample corrected Akaike Information Criterion \(AICc\), with parameters estimated by maximum likelihood\. Results At 10\-year follow\-up, retention was 79%\. Half of the FES group achieved clinical recovery\. Model estimates indicated increasing resilience over time in the FES group, whereas resilience in healthy controls remained relatively stable, although statistical support for differential trajectories between groups was limited\. Clinically recovered individuals showed a steeper increase in resilience\. In contrast, non\-recovered individuals exhibited only modest, gradual improvements, with resilience levels remaining lower at study completion\. Conclusion Different resilience trajectories were observed between clinically recovered and non\-recovered individuals with FES, with greater improvements in resilience associated with recovery\. Although causality remains uncertain and differences to healthy controls were less robust, these findings highlight the value of repeated longitudinal assessments of resilience in FES, both to more precisely characterize resilience trajectories and to reduce drop\-out rates\.

## [PENGARUH EDUKASI KESEHATAN MELALUI BOOKLET TERHADAP PENINGKATAN PENGETAHUAN ASAM URAT PADA LANSIA DI DESA LAM UJONG BAITUSSALAM BANDA ACEH](../publications/9f83cf3e197219aa6b29.md)

Nuliyana; Gadis Halizasia; Ully Muzakir

Asam urat \(gout\) banyak dialami lansia dan dapat menurunkan kualitas hidup, sedangkan pengetahuan lansia tentang pengelolaannya masih terbatas\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui pengaruh edukasi kesehatan melalui booklet terhadap pengetahuan lansia tentang asam urat di Desa Lam Ujong, Kabupaten Aceh Besar\. Penelitian kuantitatif ini menggunakan desain pre\-eksperimental one group pretest\-posttest\. Sebanyak 55 lansia dipilih dengan purposive sampling\. Pengetahuan diukur dengan kuesioner sebelum dan sesudah edukasi, kemudian dianalisis dengan uji Paired Sample t\-Test\. Sebelum edukasi, sebagian besar responden memiliki pengetahuan cukup \(56,4%\) dengan rerata skor 11,24 ± 2,11\. Sesudah edukasi, 80,0% responden berada pada kategori baik dengan rerata skor 17,69 ± 1,48\. Rerata skor pengetahuan meningkat 6,45 poin \(95% CI 5,81–7,10; p &lt; 0,001\)\. Edukasi kesehatan melalui booklet diikuti peningkatan skor pengetahuan lansia tentang asam urat pada kelompok penelitian ini\. Karena penelitian tidak menggunakan kelompok kontrol, pengaruh booklet perlu dikonfirmasi melalui penelitian dengan kelompok pembanding\.

## [ENDURING MEMORIES: THE IMPACT OF UNPLEASANT EXPERIENCES ON STUDENTS](../publications/9f85f009aeafa95c70e3.md)

Azza Syaikha Zulfa; Gavin Waradana Lesmana; Khalesa Mothea Rahman; Naufal Abyan; Salsabila Hendrawan Harahap; Maria Ulfah Handayani

Unpleasant experiences experienced by students, such as bullying, academic failure, unfair treatment, or the loss of someone close, can contribute to the formation of long\-term memories that affect psychological development and the learning process\. The urgency of this study is supported by data from the Indonesia–National Adolescent Mental Health Survey \(I\-NAMHS\), which shows that anxiety is the most prevalent mental health problem among Indonesian adolescents, at 28\.2% among females and 25\.4% among males, followed by hyperactivity, depression, behavioral problems, and post\-traumatic stress\. This situation indicates that psychological difficulties among adolescents are an issue requiring attention in educational settings\. This study aims to analyze the influence of unpleasant experiences on the formation of long\-term memories and their implications for students&\#x27; psychological, social, and academic aspects\. The study uses a Systematic Literature Review \(SLR\) with a qualitative\-descriptive approach\. Data were obtained by searching scientific articles in Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and SINTA databases published during 2016–2026\. Articles meeting the inclusion criteria were analyzed using content analysis to identify consistent patterns of findings\. The results show that experiences involving negative emotions are more easily stored in long\-term memory through the involvement of the amygdala and hippocampus in emotional memory processing\. Such memories contribute to various effects, including increased anxiety, reduced self\-confidence, concentration problems, low learning motivation, difficulties in social interaction, and decreased academic achievement\. These findings emphasize the importance of collaboration among schools, teachers, and parents in creating a safe, supportive, and responsive learning environment that addresses students&\#x27; psychological needs, minimizes the negative effects of traumatic experiences, and optimally supports students&\#x27; academic development and psychological well\-being\.

## [Hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects of Arctium lappa root extract in valproic acid–induced toxicity: biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analysis](../publications/9f8f797f7d5db937e587.md)

Mukul Shyam; Sabina Evan Prince

Introduction Valproic acid \(VPA\) is a widely used antiepileptic drug; however, its clinical use is limited by hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis, primarily mediated through oxidative stress and inflammation\. Arctium lappa root extract \(ALRE\) has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties that may confer protection against VPA\-induced organ toxicity\. Methods Phytochemical profiling of ALRE was performed using GC\-MS and HPLC\. In vitro cytotoxic effects were assessed in Hep3B and PANC\-1 cancer cell lines, while safety was assessed in THLE\-2 normal hepatic epithelial cells and H6C7 normal pancreatic ductal epithelial cells using the MTT assay\. The hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects were investigated in VPA\-induced toxicity in male Wistar albino rats through biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological analyses\. Results ALRE exhibited low cytotoxicity towards THLE\-2 and H6C7 cells, with IC50 values of 1,084\.92 and 1,174\.62 μg/mL, respectively\. VPA administration markedly increased serum levels of ALT \(127\.67 ± 4\.34 U/L\), AST \(153\.67 ± 4\.91 U/L\), ALP \(178\.67 ± 5\.21 U/L\), GGT \(7\.67 ± 0\.09 U/L\), amylase \(47\.33 ± 2\.91 U/L\), and lipase \(49\.00 ± 3\.79 U/L\) compared with the control group \(p &lt; 0\.05\)\. These enzyme levels were considerably lowered by ALRE administration, especially at 500 mg/kg\. Furthermore, ALRE restored antioxidant defences \(SOD, CAT, and GSH\), malondialdehyde levels were decreased, and the histological architecture of the liver and pancreas was improved\. Conclusion ALRE effectively attenuated VPA\-induced hepatic and pancreatic injury through antioxidant and cytoprotective mechanisms while exhibiting minimal toxicity towards normal hepatic and pancreatic cells\. These findings support the potential therapeutic application of A\. lappa as a natural protective against VPA\-associated hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis\. Further studies are warranted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and pharmacokinetic interactions underlying the protective effects of ALRE\.

## [Definition of childhood visual impairment: A systematic overview of reviews and authoritative sources across clinical, research, and policy contexts](../publications/9f93c47f20c06aded29b.md)

Martina Micai; Letizia Gila; Francesca Fulceri; Angela Caruso; Mara Sabbioni; Els Ortibus; Elisa Maria Fazzi; Corinna Bauer; John Ravencroft; María Luisa Scattoni

AIMS: To identify, synthesize, and compare current terminologies and definitions of cerebral visual impairment \(CVI\) in children across clinical, research, educational, and policy settings\. METHOD: We conducted a systematic overview of systematic reviews and authoritative documents registered in PROSPERO \(CRD420251025233\) and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines\. We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, ProQuest Health and Medical, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for records published from 1st January 2015 to 10th April 2025, without language restrictions\. Records were screened independently by pairs of reviewers\. We performed manual searches of websites from governmental organizations, national health authorities, CVI societies, and international professional bodies\. RESULTS: Forty\-eight systematic reviews and 26 authoritative documents were included\. CVI was most commonly defined using World Health Organization\-based or International Classification of Diseases\-based distance visual acuity thresholds, typically defining visual impairment as a visual acuity worse than 6/12 in the better\-seeing eye and blindness as visual acuity worse than 3/60\. Visual field loss and near visual impairment were incorporated less consistently\. Systematic reviews tended to prioritize measurable criteria, typically visual acuity in the better\-seeing eye, whereas authoritative documents more frequently linked visual impairment to functional consequences for learning and daily activities\. CVI was described in a subset of sources as brain\-based visual dysfunction not fully explained by ocular pathology, but definitions and severity criteria varied widely\. Few documents included structured functional vision assessment\. INTERPRETATION: CVI definitions remain heterogeneous and incompletely reflect real\-world visual functioning, especially for CVI and functional vision\. Consensus is needed on child\-centred, multidimensional definitions integrating ocular and brain\-based causes, multiple visual functions, and functional impact across sectors\. A working definition of CVI is needed and has been proposed in this review\.

## [PROCEEDINGS BOOK OF THE XXXII SYMPOSIUM “BIOINFORMATICS AND COMPUTER\-AIDED DRUG DISCOVERY”](../publications/9f95fe73377bebdf2f89.md)



The materials of the XXXII International Symposium Bioinformatics and Computer\-Aided Drug Discovery \(Virtual, October 19–21, 2026\) are presented\. The Symposium is dedicated to addressing the emerging challenges and opportunities in in silicodrug discovery\. It covers contemporary areas of biomedical science focused on analyzing normal and pathological states of the organism and elucidating pathological processes at the cellular and molecular levels\. The main topics include the development and practical application of computational methods for identifying and validating new pharmacological targets, in silico design of potent and safe pharmaceutical agents, optimization of the structure and properties of drug\-like compounds, and rational approaches to the use of pharmacotherapeutic agents in medical practice\. It may also be of interest to undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate students specializing in related fields\.

## [Digital tokens reshape ownership, control, and labor: organizing logics in DAOs](../publications/9f98907259adf11cfac2.md)

Nina\-Birte Schirrmacher; Michel Avital; Johannes Rude Jensen; Omri Ross

We study three decentralized autonomous organizations \(DAOs\) to explain how governability is sustained when ownership claims, decision rights, and contribution rewards are bundled through digital tokens\. Unlike conventional organizations where separating capital, management, and labor is a core design principle for sustaining governance through checks and balances, DAOs cannot rely on formal roles, hierarchical authority, or employment contracts\. DAO contributors must continually negotiate stake, authority, reward, and belonging through governance processes\. The absence of conventional governance structures should make DAOs difficult to govern\. Yet our qualitative analysis reveals three organizing logics through which contributors address this challenge: valorization, which sustains contribution by linking it to token\-based value; distribution, which organizes token\-based authority for collective action; and collective constitution, which defines the collective to which authority and rewards are oriented\. The study contributes to research on DAOs by explaining how digital tokens recombine ownership, control, and labor, thereby creating distinctive organizational tensions\. The study further shows how these tensions are mitigated through recurrent organizing logics that render collective governance sustainable\.

## [Tokamak Pedestal Region Profile Prediction in Transport\-Limited Regimes](../publications/9fa04f6c0542d8a36fac.md)

Steven Molesworth

Accurately predicting temperature and density profiles in the near\-edge region—roughly the outer 10% of closed flux surfaces—is critical for modeling tokamak performance because fusion power scales with the square of pedestal\-top pressure\. Building upon an existing framework for accelerated core transport solutions, this dissertation presents a workflow for self\-consistently solving transport\-limited pedestals using 1D, steady\-state flux matching\. Inverse scale lengths are represented using an asymmetric hyperbolic tangent parameterization, anchored at the separatrix\. Modular near\-edge physics including neutral and impurity penetration are added to account for their effects on source terms in the flux matching solution\. Diamagnetic and neoclassical terms in the rotation profile are self\-consistently updated, while the toroidal velocity is held constant at this stage\. Neoclassical and turbulent transport models developed for core plasmas were chosen to determine their range of validity\. Five discharges spanning L\-mode, H\-mode at contrasting collisionalities, negative triangularity, and I\-mode are used to test the workflow\. Only the NT result falls within the desired sub\-10% error in pedestal\-top pressure for reactor predictions, while the remaining cases miss the experimental pedestal\-top pressure by 17–84%\. That error is attributed to three factors: uncertainties in the separatrix boundary conditions, degeneracy between solver objective and pedestal values, and transport model limitations most severe in the region that most strongly determines pedestal shape\. Together, these errors do not exclude flux matching as a solution to the transport\-limited pedestal prediction problem, but do suggest limitations of the approach, particularly until an accurate near\-edge turbulence model can be made tractable within an iterative framework\. This work is thus a step toward a unified, self\-consistent treatment of core\-edge coupling suitable for integrated tokamak modeling\.

## [Chudnoff, Elijah: A Priorism in Moral Epistemology](../publications/9fb510117f169e989c8b.md)



\_Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy\_\. forthcomingA priorism in moral epistemology holds that at least some moral judgments can be justified independently of sensory experience, by reason alone\. This article surveys the surrounding debates\. It begins with two influential arguments in favor of a priorism: an epistemic regress argument from Ewing and the British intuitionist tradition, and Kant’s argument from the metaphysics of morals\. Next up are two challenges to the regress argument\. The first derives from recent defenses of moral Inferentialism, the second derives from recent defenses of moral empiricist views on which moral judgments can be based on moral perception or emotion\. The article then compares rival explanations of a priori justification \(pure reasoning, epistemic necessity, understanding, and intuition\) and identifies the burdens each faces, such as how beliefs get based on understanding and the problem of morally abhorrent intuitive appearances\. It next examines how metaethical views, including non\-naturalism, primitivism, analytic naturalism, and constructivism, bear on a priorism\. Finally, it asks whether a priori justification has distinctive theoretical or practical significance, taking into account recent discussions of whether the a priori/a posteriori distinction is epistemically shallow\.

## [A Review of Liquidity Risk Management and Stress Testing Practices in Global Financial Institutions](../publications/9fb6650057e7984680fa.md)

Kofi Okyere Mensah

This critical review examines how global financial institutions manage liquidity risk and design and validate liquidity stress tests, synthesizing theory, regulatory design, stress\-testing methodology, and institutional implementation practice into a single, integrative account\. The review screened 250 supplied sources against explicit inclusion criteria \(topical scope, publication date through 2020, verifiable indexing, and citation\-balance limits\) and applied thematic coding, rather than statistical meta\-analysis, to a core working set of approximately 50 DOI\-verified studies, organized around liquidity resilience, scenario design, and contingency funding\. The synthesis shows that funding\-liquidity risk and market\-liquidity risk interact through fire\-sale and network\-contagion channels that neither the Liquidity Coverage Ratio nor the Net Stable Funding Ratio fully internalizes on its own, that stress\-testing methodology \(scenario design, cash\-flow modeling, and model validation\) has advanced unevenly relative to regulatory design, and that implementation outcomes, governance quality, data infrastructure, and cross\-jurisdictional practice, explain more of the variation in institutional resilience than compliance with any single formal metric\. Beyond synthesizing this evidence, the review integrates regulatory buffers, stress severity, governance quality, and contingency\-funding capacity into a single decision\-cycle framework, develops four testable propositions connecting these elements, and sets out a research agenda emphasizing longitudinal, cross\-jurisdictional, and validation\-focused designs capable of testing them\.
