## [Identification of potential donors for bruchid \(Callosobruchus maculatus\) resistance in blackgram through multi\-environments phenotyping and biochemical profiling](../publications/9fc0545cfdd8ccbf39fe.md)

Shailja Jaiswal; Rakesh Pandey; Ajit Pandey; Brajrajsharan Tiwari; Chirag; Pradyum Maurya; Ashutosh Rai; Surendra Kumar Singh; Mukesh Kumar Mishra; Awnindra Kumar Singh; Bhupendra Kumar Singh; CHANDRA MOHAN SINGH

Among the various threats limiting the blackgram production, bruchids \( Callosobruchus spp\.\) are a serious concern, particularly under storage conditions\. The present experiments were carried out with 258 Vigna accessions belonging to V\. mungo and V\. umbellata to identify the potential donors for bruchid \( Callosobruchus maculatus \) resistance\. The studies on biological parameters revealed that the percent damage ranged from 0\.0 to 95\.0%\. The results indicated that two blackgram \(SYNP\-2, BLU\-1\) and two ricebean wild accessions \(PRR 2008\-2, PRR 2008\-2\-sel\) were identified as highly resistant \(HR\) on the basis of percent damage\. Further, based on the stability index and GGE biplot analysis, it was demonstrated that these genotypes have the potential of resistance over the year/ environments, considered as stable genotypes\. Biochemical analysis showed that tannin, total phenol and flavonoid contents were higher in resistant genotypes compared to susceptible genotypes\. These potential donors will serve as genetic stock in a breeding programme for improving the bruchid resistance\.

## [Quantitative Trading Algorithm Based on Systematic Optimization of Decision Thresholds](../publications/9fc3c07684e319907e27.md)

Matías Adell; Javier Balda; Facundo Casas; Antonio Quintero\-Rincón

El análisis de los mercados financieros, tales como el Nasdaq, el S&amp;P 500, las acciones de Apple y el Bitcoin, plantea desafíos significativos debido a su elevada volatilidad y a la compleja interacción de estos activos con diversos indicadores macroeconómicos de Estados Unidos\. En el presente estudio se propone un algoritmo cuantitativo de trading que optimiza los umbrales de decisión de compra y venta en los mercados financieros, utilizando ocho indicadores macroeconómicos, en particular la tasa de interés y la inflación\. Con el propósito de abordar la complejidad y la elevada dimensionalidad de los datos, se evaluaron comparativamente cinco métodos de reducción de dimensionalidad \(PCA, t\-SNE, LDA, PPCA y VSD\), identificándose a PCA como el procedimiento con mayor eficiencia computacional y mejor desempeño global\. Posteriormente, se implementó un esquema de backtracking para determinar los umbrales óptimos de compra y venta que maximizan el rendimiento de la inversión bajo las condiciones de mercado consideradas\. La aplicación de estos umbrales a los distintos activos financieros analizados generó resultados sobresalientes, con rendimientos del 98,92 % en el Nasdaq, 109,44 % en el S&amp;P 500 y 160,27 % en Apple, en un horizonte temporal aproximado de cuatro años\. Sin embargo, el modelo evidenció una eficacia sustancialmente menor en el caso de Bitcoin, fenómeno atribuible a su baja correlación con los indicadores macroeconómicos incorporados en el análisis\. Estos resultados preliminares indican que el algoritmo propuesto presenta una capacidad sólida para identificar puntos de entrada y salida del mercado en las acciones analizadas\.

## [From Dyadic Reciprocity to Giant Interaction Engines](../publications/9fcc88e87d3bca5c0459.md)

Rita Tamara Vallentin; Britta Schneider

In this paper, based on posthumanist theory and posthumanist linguistics, we discuss specific elaborations of the term interaction as found in linguistics and sociology, where interactivity, reciprocal awareness and agency are discussed as possible characteristics of human interaction\. We problematise to what extent this is distinct from interaction between humans and machines\. We bring these discussions in relation to illustrative observations on how users of ChatGPT report on their experiences with large language models, drawn from Reddit threads\. We show that the concept of interaction is ‘under construction’, not only because we have new interactional partners but also because meaning\-making is now intertwined with the changing and individually customised and at the same time collectivised media affordances of machine\-learning technologies\. Interaction is no longer perceived as typically taking place between two humans but as embedded in and distributed across time and space in large networks of speaking subjects, massive historical and ever\-changing data sets, and algorithmic affordances\.

## [Financial toxicity profiles and associated factors among lung cancer patients receiving immunotherapy: a latent profile analysis](../publications/9fcd6e39dc1457e4b8d8.md)

Jing Nie; Peijuan Hu; Wei Qian; Xiaoyan Lu; Yulong Tan

Objectives To identify latent profiles of patient\-reported financial toxicity and factors associated with profile membership among lung cancer patients receiving immunotherapy\. Methods A total of 331 lung cancer patients receiving immunotherapy were recruited by convenience sampling\. Financial toxicity, perceived social support, and psychological resilience were assessed using the Comprehensive Score for Financial Toxicity \(COST\-PROM\), Perceived Social Support Scale \(PSSS\), and Connor\-Davidson Resilience Scale \(CD\-RISC\), respectively\. Latent profile analysis \(LPA\) based on the 11 COST\-PROM items was used to identify financial\-toxicity profiles\. Factors associated with profile membership were examined using the Mplus three\-step R3STEP procedure, which accounts for classification uncertainty\. A conventional multinomial logistic regression based on most\-likely class assignment was used as a sensitivity analysis\. Additional analyses examined the robustness of the LPA solution, an R3STEP model including all available covariates, collinearity, and possible nonlinear effects of PSSS and CD\-RISC\. Results Three profiles were identified: Severe Financial Toxicity \(28\.7%\), Moderate Financial Toxicity \(39\.9%\), and Mild Financial Toxicity \(31\.4%\)\. In R3STEP analyses, lower monthly income, out\-of\-pocket payment, and non\-working status were associated with higher odds of Severe Financial Toxicity profile membership \( p &lt; 0\.05\), whereas higher PSSS and CD\-RISC scores were associated with lower odds \( p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The modal\-assignment sensitivity analysis yielded materially consistent findings\. The three classes differed mainly in overall severity, with broadly parallel item profiles\. Average posterior probabilities were 0\.989, 0\.982, and 0\.992 for the Severe, Moderate, and Mild classes, respectively\. Both alternative LPA models retained three classes, and the additional multivariable R3STEP model produced similar results\. Conclusion Patient\-reported financial toxicity was heterogeneous among lung cancer patients receiving immunotherapy\. Socioeconomic vulnerability and psychosocial characteristics were associated with profile membership\. Routine financial\-distress screening and financial navigation may be considered for patients with greater financial toxicity, while psychosocial intervention strategies require prospective evaluation before their effectiveness can be inferred\. The classes mainly reflected different levels of financial toxicity rather than distinct response patterns\.

## [Chronic Electroconvulsive Shock Disrupts Hippocampal Physiology and Impairs Associative Memory in Mice](../publications/9fe28b5d14afd38d087b.md)

T\. Zhang; Nicholas P\. Vyleta; Isaac Schwein; Baran Askari; Matthew B\. Cooke; F\. Vila‐Rodriguez; Jason S\. Snyder

ABSTRACT Electroconvulsive therapy \( ECT \) is a highly effective treatment for depression but it has undesirable side effects on various aspects of cognition, including memory\. Patients may display retrograde amnesia for autobiographical events and anterograde amnesia in tests of recall and recognition memory\. These amnestic effects are likely to depend, at least in part, on changes in the hippocampus\. ECT ‐induced volume increases in the hippocampus and dentate gyrus subregion in particular correlate with the cognitive deficits\. However, the precise cellular and behavioral effects of ECT remain poorly understood\. Here, we therefore subjected male and female mice to chronic electroconvulsive shock \( ECS \) and examined effects on hippocampal physiology and memory\. Perforant path inputs onto dentate gyrus neurons were examined using whole cell patch clamp recordings in hippocampal slices\. In the intact slice, perforant path stimulation did not result in any synaptic or spiking differences in mice given sham versus ECS treatments\. However, GABA A blockade increased EPSPs and spiking in sham, but not ECS ‐treated, mice\. Voltage clamp recordings further revealed weaker perforant path excitation of dentate gyrus neurons in ECS ‐treated mice\. Extrapolating these findings to the intact animal, we then used Fos expression as a proxy for neural activity and found that ECS blunted exploration‐induced hippocampal activation, which was most pronounced in the dentate gyrus\. Finally, recognition memory tasks revealed that ECS impaired memory for object‐context associations but not memory for objects or locations\. Collectively, these experiments reveal that a clinically relevant schedule of ECS disrupts synaptic and circuit functions of the hippocampus and causes anterograde amnesia in a test of episodic‐like associative memory\.

## [Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment](../publications/9fea22a54fd253139c42.md)

Rachana Mahadevan; Naomi Kristin Giesers; Thomas Liman; Karsten Witt; Andrea Hildebrandt; Mandy Roheger; Stephanie Rosemann

Mild cognitive impairment \(MCI\) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread\. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance\. Sixty adults \(30 MCI, 30 healthy controls\), aged 50\-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI\. Whole\-brain voxel\-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups\. However, targeted region\-of\-interest ROI analyses demonstrated lower right amygdala and bilateral hippocampal volumes in patients with MCI\. Cortical thickness analyses identified two regions with lower thickness in MCI: the right superior parietal lobule and the left posterior insula\. A significant Group × Sadness interaction indicated that the association between left superior parietal gray matter volume and sadness recognition differed between groups\. Follow\-up analyses of the extracted values showed a positive association in MCI, although this within\-group association did not reach statistical significance, and a significant inverse association in HCs\. These findings suggest that early MCI involves selective thinning in association cortices supporting attention and salience processing\. The sadness\-specific interaction indicates that patients with MCI may rely on preserved superior parietal structure during sadness recognition, a pattern that is consistent with structural reserve accounts, although this interpretation remains speculative given the cross\-sectional design\.

## [Thickness‐Gradient Liquid Metal Connectors for Seamless Electrophysiological Sensors](../publications/9fec48135e91186de3b0.md)

Jinyoung Kim; Jaejun Lee; Christopher E\. Tabor; Vladimir V\. Tsukruk

High\-fidelity electrophysiological monitoring requires wearable bioelectronic devices with mechanical properties closely matched to human skin\. However, current approaches focus primarily on electrode design and performance, while overlooking mechanical compliance and interfacial continuity with complex and dynamic human skin\. Mechanical mismatches across electrodes, connectors, and interconnects often lead to interfacial noise, motion artifacts, and electrical instability\. In order to overcome these critical issues, we introduce a thickness\-gradient liquid metal \(LM\)/SEBS connector that enables seamless interfacial integration with skin, electrode, and interconnector interfaces through gradual mechanical compliance matching and manually activated metal network formation\. The activated LM forms continuous and robust conductive networks, maintaining electrical stability under large tensile strain \(∼1100%\) and for repeatable deformation cycles\. Skin\-mimetic conformal integration suggested here suppresses interfacial void formation and stress concentration and thereby preserves stable electrical pathways under dynamic skin deformation\. As a result, the proposed system delivers markedly improved signal amplitude and signal\-to\-noise ratio, along with substantially lower noise, relative to conventional connector platforms\. By systematically aligning mechanical compliance across sensor components, this mechanically adaptive design preserves seamless electrical pathways and minimizes motion\-induced artifacts under dynamic conditions, providing a robust platform for reliable electrophysiological monitoring in long\-lasting wearable bioelectronics\.

## [The Influence of Storytelling Marketing, Content Quality, and Influencer Credibility on Purchase Decision\[EJ1\.1\] Through Purchase Intention as an Intervening Variable on Time Phoria Products by a \[o2\.1\]Dosen Kecantikan](../publications/a0021afc410c2b66ef87.md)

Ersa Juliana; Nikma Yucha

This research is motivated by the increasingly important role of influencers in marketing cosmetic products through social media, particularly for relatively new brands such as Time Phoria\. This study aims to analyze the influence of storytelling marketing, content quality, and influencer credibility on purchase intention and purchase decisions, as well as the role of purchase intention as an intervening variable\. A quantitative approach with a descriptive method was employed\. The study population consisted of Dosen Kecantikan&\#x27;s followers who had purchased Time Phoria, with a sample of 153 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on an a priori power analysis using G\*Power\. Data were collected using a five\-point Likert\-scale questionnaire and analyzed with PLS\-SEM in SmartPLS 4\. The results indicate that all three independent variables have a positive and significant effect on both purchase intention and purchase decisions\. However, purchase intention does not significantly affect purchase decisions are more directly influenced by storytelling marketing, content quality, and influencer credibility\.

## [Cross\-sectional associations of Kidney deficiency, Phlegm\-stasis, and Heat\-toxin syndrome patterns with disease severity in Alzheimer’s disease: an exploratory study](../publications/a0083597d371af2e75b9.md)

Limin Zhang; Hong‐Mei An; Min\-Rui Ding; 于晓飞; Feng Yan; Chao Gu; Xia Li

Background Current Alzheimer’s diagnostics lack integration with Traditional Chinese Medicine’s syndrome differentiation framework, making it difficult to fully capture the clinical heterogeneity and multidimensional nature of the disease\. Methods This cross\-sectional study analyzed 236 AD patients stratified by CDR into early\-stage \( n = 127\), moderate \( n = 66\), and severe \( n = 43\) groups\. Using the SHA\-03\-W1 diagnostic instrument and Tian Jinzhou Scale, patients were classified into three TCM syndrome patterns: Kidney essence deficiency \( n = 87\), Phlegm\-stasis obstructing the orifices \( n = 93\), and Heat\-toxin obstructing the collaterals \( n = 56\)\. Data collected included demographics, cognitive scores \(MMSE, MoCA\), activities of daily living \(ADL\), and plasma biomarkers \(GFAP, NfL, p\-tau181, p\-tau217, Aβ42/40\)\. Statistical analyses involved intergroup comparisons \(Chi\-square and Kruskal\-Wallis tests\), Spearman correlation analysis between dementia severity/TCM patterns and clinical measures, logistic regression to examine factors associated with disease severity, and exploratory ROC analysis to describe discriminatory performance within this development sample\. Results Across the three CDR\-defined severity groups \( n = 236\), MMSE, MoCA, ADL and estimated symptom duration differed significantly \( p &lt; 0\.05, q &lt; 0\.05\)\. Dementia severity correlated strongly with MMSE \( r = −0\.779\), MoCA \( r = −0\.785\) and ADL \( r = 0\.742\) \( p &lt; 0\.001\), and only weakly with estimated symptom duration \( r = 0\.384, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. TCM syndrome distribution patterns differed across severity stages, with kidney essence deficiency being most prevalent in the early\-stage group \(48%\), Phlegm\-stasis in the moderate group \(54\.5%\), and Heat\-toxin in the severe group \(60\.5%\)\. In multivariable multinomial logistic regression \(reference: early\-stage AD\), MMSE and ADL scores were associated with AD severity \(MMSE: moderate vs\. early, OR = 0\.844, 95% CI 0\.774–0\.921; severe vs\. early, OR = 0\.485, 95% CI 0\.351–0\.671; ADL: moderate vs\. early, OR = 1\.128, 95% CI 1\.065–1\.196; severe vs\. early, OR = 1\.280, 95% CI 1\.150–1\.425; all p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Among TCM syndrome elements, Heat\-toxin was associated with both moderate and severe AD \(Moderate vs\. Early\-stage: OR = 1\.177, 95% CI 1\.046–1\.324, p = 0\.007; Severe vs\. Early\-stage: OR = 1\.498, 95% CI 1\.205–1\.861, p &lt; 0\.001\) and Phlegm\-stasis with moderate AD only \(OR = 1\.198, 95% CI 1\.079–1\.329, p = 0\.001\)\. In an exploratory ROC analysis, single indicators showed modest discriminatory performance for Heat\-toxin syndrome, with CDR \(AUC = 0\.709\) &gt; ADL \(AUC = 0\.690\) &gt; MMSE \(AUC = 0\.683\), whereas AUCs for Kidney deficiency \(≤0\.633\) and Phlegm\-stasis \(≤0\.581\) were close to chance\. In a sensitivity analysis excluding participants with CDR 0\.5 \( n = 186\), the cognitive, functional and Heat\-toxin associations were essentially unchanged, but the Phlegm\-stasis score was associated with both moderate and severe AD, with comparable effect sizes \(Moderate vs\. Early\-stage: OR = 1\.26, 95% CI 1\.12–1\.42, p &lt; 0\.001; Severe vs\. Early\-stage: OR = 1\.25, 95% CI 1\.02–1\.54, p = 0\.032\), indicating that its restriction to moderate AD was not robust\. Discussion In this cross\-sectional single\-center sample, TCM syndrome distributions and scores differed across concurrent CDR\-defined severity groups, with kidney essence deficiency predominating in early\-stage AD \(48\.0%\), Phlegm\-stasis in moderate AD \(54\.5%\), and Heat\-toxin in severe AD \(60\.5%\)\. Heat\-toxin scores were associated with greater concurrent cognitive and functional impairment, whereas plasma biomarkers showed limited and inconsistent associations\. These findings do not establish temporal syndrome transitions or validated diagnostic utility outside this development sample, but provide hypothesis\-generating evidence for future prospective investigations\.

## [Urban growth\-induced surface thermal dynamics: an integrated deep learning assessment for Colombo, Sri Lanka](../publications/a015a869aa0415bfc275.md)

Farasath Hasan; Xintao Liu

Abstract Urban growth is a major driver of land surface temperature \(LST\) change, yet most LST forecasting studies do not explicitly incorporate future urban expansion\. To address this gap, we develop an integrated deep learning \(DL\) framework that couples urban growth simulation with LST prediction for Colombo, Sri Lanka, and benchmark our proposed ResNet\+Transformer model against six comparison models \(four DL architectures and two machine learning methods\) across both tasks\. For urban growth simulation, the ResNet\+Transformer achieves the highest accuracy \(0\.908\), F1 score \(0\.8691\), Figure of Merit \(0\.7684\), precision \(0\.9152\), and recall \(0\.8274\), while also yielding the lowest quantity and allocation disagreement\. The simulated urban growth maps for 2035 and 2045 were then incorporated as dynamic drivers in LST prediction\. In this second task, the ResNet\+Transformer again outperformed all benchmark models, achieving the lowest RMSE \(0\.951 $$^\\circ $$ C\) and MAE \(0\.651 $$^\\circ $$ C\), and the highest $$R^2$$ \(0\.7412\)\. The projections indicate a 2\.22 $$^\\circ $$ C increase in mean LST between 2025 and 2045, while surface urban heat island \(SUHI\) intensity rises from 4\.73 $$^\\circ $$ C in 2035 to 5\.06 $$^\\circ $$ C in 2045\. Hotspot analysis reveals strong spatial clustering of warming \( $$r&gt;0\.90$$ \), and sensitivity analysis identifies urban growth as the dominant driver of future LST \(2\.357–2\.396 $$^\\circ $$ C\), far exceeding other environmental factors\. The proposed framework provides a robust tool for identifying future thermal risk and supporting climate\-responsive urban planning\.

## [The Impact of Technology Use in Teaching English as a Second Language at Educational Institutions in Sabha City](../publications/a02a51fcc5bb414536a4.md)

منير أحمد ناصر المشري; Monir Ahmed Naser Elmeshri

هدفت الدراسة الحالية إلى الكشف عن أثر استخدام التكنولوجيا في تدريس اللغة الإنجليزية بوصفها لغةً ثانية في المؤسسات التعليمية بمدينة سبها، من خلال تحليل أبعاد هذا التوظيف وانعكاساته على المخرجات اللغوية للمتعلمين\. وتمحورت مشكلة البحث حول الفجوة القائمة بين السياسات التعليمية المعلنة والممارسة الميدانية الفعلية، والتفاوت بين الإمكانات التقنية المتاحة والكفاءة البشرية اللازمة لتوظيفها، فضلًا عن التحديات البنيوية والمؤسسية التي تحدّ من فاعلية الدمج التكنولوجي\. وانطلقت الدراسة من فرضية رئيسة مفادها وجود أثر ذي دلالة إحصائية لاستخدام التكنولوجيا في المخرجات اللغوية عند مستوى دلالة \(α ≤ 0\.05\)، تفرّعت عنها ثلاث فرضيات فرعية تتصل بأثر توظيف الأدوات التكنولوجية في المهارات اللغوية الأربع، والعلاقة بين الكفاءة الرقمية للمعلم وفاعلية الدمج، ووجود فروق تُعزى إلى التحديات المؤسسية\. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، ووظّفت الاستبانة أداةً لجمع البيانات من عينة بلغت \(209\) مشاركين من المعلمين والمتعلمين في \(18\) مؤسسة ومركزًا تعليميًا\. وأظهرت النتائج مستوى مرتفعًا لتوظيف الأدوات التكنولوجية بمتوسط حسابي \(4\.02\)، وعلاقة إيجابية قوية بين التكنولوجيا وتنمية المهارات اللغوية بمتوسط \(4\.17\)، كما فسّر المتغير المستقل ما نسبته \(49\.8%\) من التباين في المخرجات اللغوية\. وأوصت الدراسة بتطوير البنية التحتية الرقمية، وتصميم برامج تطوير مهني متخصصة، والتوسع في توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي، وبناء شراكات استراتيجية، ووضع سياسات مؤسسية تنظّم التحول الرقمي في تعليم اللغات\.

## [Repositioning standardisation: artificial intelligence and the recentring of professional value in television audiovisual documentation](../publications/a03db592ff8f68fc571e.md)

Jorge Caldera\-Serrano

Abstract The expansion of artificial intelligence in archives, documentation systems and media archives has intensified a transformation that cannot be understood solely as technical innovation or task automation\. In television audiovisual documentation, this shift is particularly visible because of the convergence of high production volumes, time pressure, continuous editorial reuse, descriptive granularity and multiplatform circulation\. Drawing on a critical\-conceptual approach supported by documentary analysis and based on a comparative reading of recent academic literature, broadcaster\-sector studies, and professional and institutional documents, this article examines the loss of sufficiency of standardisation as the exclusive centre of professional documentary value\. The argument advanced is that standardisation remains indispensable as an infrastructure of consistency, interoperability and retrievability, but that professional value increasingly tends to be recentred around documentary judgement, contextualisation, provenance and traceability, access mediation, and the critical governance of automation and AI\.

## [ADVANCES IN AI\-BASED PERSONALIZED HEALTHCARE](../publications/a0403343aab9538b65d3.md)

Gopi Jesadiya; Hemani Mistry; Maryam Meer; Satyajit Sahoo; Dhananjay B Meshram

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly changing the way healthcare is delivered by supporting a more personalized and patient\-centered approach to medicine\. Personalized medicine combines information such as genetics, genomics, medical history, lifestyle, laboratory results, medical images, and continuous health data to help healthcare professionals make better decisions for individual patients\. Its applications include disease risk prediction, AI\-assisted medical imaging, genomic data interpretation, biomarker identification, personalized drug selection, pharmacogenomics, adaptive drug dosing, treatment response prediction, and remote patient monitoring through wearable and mobile health technologies\. However, successful implementation requires careful data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, model development, validation, and continuous monitoring\. Despite its benefits, AI\-driven personalized medicine faces important challenges, including data privacy and security, poor data quality, limited diversity in datasets, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, high implementation costs, and regulatory and ethical concerns\. Future developments such as digital twins, generative AI, precision oncology, multi\-omics integration, federated learning, and real\-time adaptive treatment systems may further strengthen personalized healthcare\. Overall, AI should complement rather than replace healthcare professionals, providing evidence\-based support while keeping patient safety, fairness, privacy, and clinical judgment at the center of care\.

## [Efficient Pairwise Difference Learning: A Comparative Study of Encoding Strategies and Training Pair Selection](../publications/a04ee23a28821c77d7a8.md)

Bernard Georges; Mohamed Karim Belaid; Manuel Rodrigues

Pairwise Difference Learning for Classification \(PDC\) enhances supervised learning in low\-data regimes by training a binary similarity classifier on pairs of instances rather than individual samples, effectively inflating the training set from $n$ to $O\(n^2\)$ examples\. However, the PDC framework leaves critical implementation choices underspecified, particularly regarding input representation and pair selection strategies\. This work systematically investigates these design decisions through extensive empirical evaluation\. We compare four feature encoders \(paired features, triplet with relative difference, absolute difference, and a novel triplet with absolute difference\) alongside four pair selection strategies ranging from exhaustive to kernel\-thinning\-based schemes\. Experiments across nearly 200 benchmark classification datasets using Decision Tree, Multilayer Perceptron, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Classifier as base models reveal that the proposed triplet with absolute difference encoder \($φ\_\{\\mathrm\{3dabs\}\}$\) achieves the highest average F1 scores\. More notably, restricting training to upper\-triangle pairs reduces computational time by approximately 40% with negligible accuracy loss\. Kernel thinning\-based selection provided no accuracy benefits while substantially increasing computational overhead\. Overall, PDC configurations outperformed base models in 94% of tested cases, though no single configuration dominated universally, suggesting dataset\-specific optimization remains an open challenge\.

## [Behavioral Financial Signals and Explainable AI in Credit Risk Assessment: Evidence from Utility Arrears and Gambling Activity](../publications/a05427498605554065e4.md)

Shynara Sarkambayeva; Aliya Turegeldinova; Marat Sultangaziyev; Yerkezhan Mussabayeva; Satyanand Singh

Traditional consumer credit scoring models frequently fail to identify rising default risks in transition economies because they rely almost exclusively on formal macroeconomic indicators and unchanging demographic data\. This paper offers a preliminary empirical assessment of digital gambling participation and utility payment arrears as stand\-in risk indicators in Kazakhstani consumer credit scoring\. Using a unique survey\-derived dataset from Kazakhstan \(N = 41 survey respondents, yielding a finalized modeling cohort of N = 233 active borrowers\), we develop, tune, and evaluate five predictive models—Logistic Regression \(LR\), Decision Trees, Artificial Neural Networks \(ANNs\), Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\)\. Models were optimized using stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation on the training partition \(N ≈ 163\) and benchmarked across both a SMOTE\-balanced evaluation pool \(Deval, N = 473\) and an empirical 30% holdout test set \(Demp, N ≈ 70\)\. The results provide localized baseline evidence on incorporating non\-traditional behavioral data into credit evaluation frameworks in data\-constrained emerging economies\. While the raw empirical cohort \(𝒟emp\) exhibits a dominant majority distribution with an 88\.84% default/late\-payment rate, a balanced resampled evaluation pool \(𝒟eval, N = 473\) was constructed to ensure unbiased model optimization\. The empirical results show that tree\-based ensemble structures considerably outperform conventional methods, establishing a clear performance hierarchy\. With an accuracy of 83\.1% and an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve \(AUROC\) of 0\.854, the classical LR baseline has the lowest predictive power and is unable to map complex, interactive behavioral hazards\. On the other hand, the best architecture is the improved XGBoost ensemble engine, which achieves an AUROC of 0\.976 on the balanced evaluation pool \(𝒟eval\)\. The XGBoost framework successfully reduces institutional asymmetric loss constraints, according to a micro\-structural audit of the underlying confusion matrix\. Evaluated on 𝒟eval, the model achieves a specificity of 97\.4% \(TN = 228\) and a sensitivity of 96\.2% \(TP = 230\), reducing catastrophic FNR underwriting errors while preserving high loan onboarding efficiency\. Furthermore, comparative testing directly on the unadjusted empirical cohort \(𝒟emp\) confirms strong diagnostic robustness, demonstrating that high class\-separation performance generalizes effectively to skewed real\-world credit distributions\. These findings demonstrate that incorporating real\-time behavioral abnormalities into regularized ensemble pipelines offers a very reliable method of reducing risk\. In conclusion, this research provides emerging market financial institutions and regulators with an empirical guide to enhance credit underwriting accuracy, strike a compromise between inclusive lending and capital preservation, and shield the retail banking portfolio from localized default contagion\. Although the size of the available dataset does not allow us to attain a definitive conclusion, these results point to a promising direction to further investigate with the same methods proposed in this work and larger datasets\. Indeed, they suggest that behavioral data has the potential to enhance traditional credit\-scoring techniques when properly vetted and integrated with machine\-learning techniques\.

## [Choroid plexus volume in metabolic syndrome: a cross\-sectional neuroimaging study](../publications/a057d6713b7de2f46f82.md)

Xiunan Huo; Tao Chen; Zhenyu Cheng; Boyao Chen; Fushuai Zhang; Yiwen Chen; Pengcheng Liang; Nan Zhang; Yena Che; Changhu Liang; Lingfei Guo; Meng Li

Objectives Our investigation aimed to explore the associations between choroid plexus \(CP\) volume and metabolic syndrome \(MetS\) components and cognitive\-motor performance in a cross\-sectional sample\. Methods A total of 211 participants \(73 with MetS and 138 non\-MetS controls\) were included in this study\. CP volume was automatically segmented from 3D T1\-weighted images using a 3D nnU\-Net\. CP volume was normalized to estimated total intracranial volume \(eTIV\) and expressed as the CP/eTIV ratio\. Multivariable linear regression analyses and Spearman correlation analyses were used to examine associations among the CP/eTIV ratio, MetS components and cognitive\-motor domains\. The Boruta algorithm was applied for exploratory feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis was used to evaluate the discriminative capacity of the selected variables for identifying participants with lower global cognitive\-motor performance \(lowest 25th percentile of global cognitive\-motor composite\)\. Results Participants with MetS exhibited a higher CP/eTIV ratio than non\-MetS controls, and higher CP/eTIV was independently associated with lower high\-density lipoprotein cholesterol \(HDL\-C\) levels \( FDR q = 0\.024\) after full adjustment and FDR correction\. In unadjusted analyses, the CP/eTIV ratio was correlated with multiple cognitive\-motor domains\. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for confounders\. Boruta analysis identified CP/eTIV, white matter hyperintensity \(WMH\) volume/eTIV, and BMI as key variables, and the combined model yielded an AUC of 0\.787 \(95% CI: 0\.718 to 0\.854\) for discriminating participants with lower global cognitive\-motor composite\. DeLong&\#x27;s test showed that the combined model did not significantly outperform CP/eTIV alone \(0\.742 vs\. 0\.787; FDR q = 0\.084\) or the model of WMH/eTIV and BMI \(0\.729 vs\. 0\.787; FDR q = 0\.084\)\. Conclusion A higher CP/eTIV ratio was associated with MetS and lower HDL\-C levels, but was not independently associated with cognitive\-motor performance after multivariable adjustment\. CP structural variation may represent an imaging correlate of metabolic disturbance, and its relevance to cognitive vulnerability requires prospective validation\.

## [Backward and Hopf bifurcations in a human papillomavirus–cancer model with imperfect vaccination and waning immunity](../publications/a0658baba689ed20c245.md)

Din Prathumwan; Kingkan Sunthonphong; Sirawit Phakmee; Inthira Chaiya; Kamonchat Trachoo

Introduction Human papillomavirus \(HPV\) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the cause of virtually all cervical cancer, yet elimination is complicated by two features of real vaccination programmes: available vaccines are imperfect, leaving vaccinated individuals partially susceptible, and naturally acquired immunity wanes\. We ask whether reducing the basic reproduction number below unity is sufficient for elimination when both mechanisms are present\. Methods We formulate and analyse a six\-compartment \( SEIRVC \) deterministic model combining an imperfect vaccine and waning immunity with explicit progression to an HPV\-related cancer class\. We establish positivity, boundedness, and an invariant region; derive R 0 by the next\-generation matrix method; characterize the equilibria and their stability using Routh–Hurwitz criteria, Lyapunov functions, and the geometric approach of Li and Muldowney; and analyse the bifurcation structure, supported by sensitivity indices and simulation\. Results The reproduction number decomposes additively into a susceptible and a vaccine\-breakthrough route, and the disease\-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable precisely when R 0 &lt; 1, and globally so under an explicit condition\. Reducing the endemic equilibria to the roots of a quadratic shows that a leaky vaccine together with waning immunity produces a backward bifurcation, so that R 0 &lt; 1 is necessary but not sufficient for elimination and control must clear a turning point R 0 c &lt; 1 \. Above threshold the unique endemic equilibrium can lose stability through a Hopf bifurcation, giving sustained oscillations whose amplitude is magnified in the cancer class, which varies by a factor of order 10 2 within a cycle under constant parameters\. Both phenomena require both mechanisms and vanish when the vaccine becomes perfectly protective or immunity permanent, the limit in which global stability of the endemic equilibrium is proved; two\-parameter continuation shows the two regimes to be disjoint alternatives\. Discussion Sensitivity analysis gives sgnΥ β = sgn\(θ−λ H \) so scaling up an insufficiently protective vaccine raises R 0 , while the waning rate has zero elasticity yet determines both non\-classical regimes\. Threshold quantities alone are therefore an unreliable guide to HPV control, and surveillance must track prevalence over time\.

## [TECNOLOGIAS DIGITAIS NA GESTÃO DO CUIDADO: DESAFIOS E PERSPECTIVAS PARA OS SISTEMAS DE SAÚDE: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA](../publications/a067fc1390e0aad121ff.md)

Nayane Regina Silva Araújo; Rafaelle Serejo Machado; Jennyfer Lacerda Teles; Rafael Rodrigues Gonçalves; Paula Lyra Dias de Oliva; Ana Laura Moraes da Silveira; Edivaldo Bazilio dos Santos; Jacineidy de Moura Sousa; Josyane Rebouças da Silva; Paula De Vasconcelos Pinheiro; Marialdo Dias Barroso Mendonça; Evilda Rodrigues de Lima; Itamar dos Santos Fonseca; Jomacs Costa da Silva

Objetivo: sintetizar as melhores evidências científicas sobre a incorporação de tecnologias digitais na gestão do cuidado em saúde, evidenciando efeitos sobre a organização do trabalho, a qualidade e a continuidade da assistência, o acesso e a equidade, bem como os desafios de implementação nos sistemas de saúde\. Método: revisão integrativa conduzida segundo Whittemore e Knafl e reportada conforme o PRISMA 2020, com busca reprodutível em PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, LILACS, SciELO e BVS, complementada por documentos institucionais da Organização Mundial da Saúde, da Organização Pan\-Americana da Saúde e do Ministério da Saúde\. Adotaram\-se descritores DeCS e MeSH combinados por operadores booleanos e recorte temporal de 2020 a 2026\. A qualidade e o nível de evidência foram classificados conforme Melnyk e Fineout\-Overholt, seguidos de análise temática\. Resultados: vinte estudos compuseram o corpus, predominando revisões sistemáticas de países de alta renda e um conjunto relevante de experiências brasileiras no Sistema Único de Saúde\. As evidências convergem para ganhos em continuidade, coordenação e acesso, condicionados à interoperabilidade, à usabilidade, ao letramento digital e à governança de dados; a carga de documentação e o burnout emergem como efeitos adversos recorrentes\. Considerações finais: as tecnologias digitais qualificam a gestão do cuidado quando integradas a processos de trabalho redesenhados, competências profissionais e políticas de equidade, exigindo protagonismo da enfermagem e da equipe multiprofissional na mediação tecnológica do cuidado\.

## [GENIE\-IDS: Failure\-steered Closed\-loop Generative\-discriminative Learning for Long\-tailed Network Intrusion Detection](../publications/a08ef8edfd876d0757f2.md)

Amanpreet Singh; Rakesh Kumar; Meenu Gupta

Rare attack families remain the weak point of learned network intrusion detection\.Established remedies allocate synthetic samples by class frequency, so a class that is scarce but already separable is treated exactly like one whose examples sit inside a region occupied by a dominant class\.This paper presents GENIE\-IDS, in which that allocation follows the detector&\#x27;s own failure geometry: a calibrated model is trained first, and its margin deficit, temperature\-scaled uncertainty and attraction toward competing head classes pool into a class\-and\-region failure map that spends a fixed budget of accepted synthetic flows on underlearned minority regions\.A conditional tabular generator is queried only for those regions, and a four\-stage gate screens validity, local conformity, multivariate dependence and duplication before accepted flows re\-enter training with a reliability weight\.Under group\-aware partitions on four benchmarks, against ten baselines sharing the split, feature space, tuning allowance and both an equal accepted\-sample and an equal generator\-call budget, the model the declared stopping rule selects reaches macro\-F1 0\.789, 0\.759, 0\.679 and 0\.868, with tail\-tier gains of 4\.6 to 8\.0 points\.Holm correction over 72 per\-class blocks separates it from all ten baselines, but a dependence\-aware re\-analysis treating the dataset as the cluster cuts the effective sample size to about twelve, so the twenty independent dataset\-seed runs are adopted as the primary inferential basis and keep the advantage over every baseline; the within\-dataset Wilcoxon signed\-rank test against each dataset&\#x27;s strongest baseline then separates the method on three of the four datasets, the exception being CSE\-CIC\-IDS2018 against BA\-REG \(p = 0\.084\)\.Removing region\-level failure localisation costs more than removing any other component\.

## [Student Course Recommendation System Using Semantic Aware Temporal Gating With Time Transformer](../publications/a091b706dd2d212b26bd.md)

Joshi Vinay Kumar; Dahlia Sam; N\. Kanya

Course recommendation system works by analyzing users’ interests and recognizes their historical behavior such as course enrollment and previously watched videos to recommend relevant courses\. However, the existing course recommendation systems in Massive Open Online Courses \(MOOCs\) face challenges in capturing complex semantic information, which impacts student requirements with an unsatisfied recommendation\. By combining historical behaviors without temporal awareness, the model does not provide a proper recommendation and it lacks sequential dependencies\. This research proposes Semantic Aware Temporal Gating \(SATG\) with Time Transformer \(TT\), which dynamically weights historical learning interactions by cross\-referencing elapsed time with content\-based Knowledge Graph \(KG\) semantics\. The SATG helps capture sequential dependencies between historical user behaviors; hence, the relevant course is recommended by the model\. Additionally, SATG preserves long\-term, semantically relevant connections while suppressing irrelevant past behaviors\. The proposed SATG\-TT achieves a Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain \(NDCG\) of 54\.82 and 51\.02% at @5 as well as @10 on the MOOCCube and XuetangX datasets, respectively\. These results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits competitive performance compared to existing baseline models such as Knowledge Sequence Course Recommendation \(KSCR\)\.

## [Sustainable agro\-waste ash reinforced aluminium matrix composites with emerging potential of nano\-banana peel ash in Al7075](../publications/a094087278ec693be704.md)

Ch\. V S R Satya Prasad; N\. Rao

Abstract The development of sustainable aluminium matrix composites using agricultural waste\-derived reinforcements provides an alternative approach to utilizing biomass residues in advanced engineering materials\. In this study, nanoscale banana peel ash \(Nano\-BPA\) was synthesized through dehydration, calcination, and high\-energy ball milling and incorporated into an Al7075 alloy by stir casting\. Nano\-BPA was characterized using particle size analysis \(PSA\), scanning electron microscopy \(SEM\), energy\-dispersive spectroscopy \(EDS\), and thermogravimetric analysis \(TGA\)\. The Al7075 base alloy and composites containing 2 and 4 wt% Nano\-BPA were fabricated and evaluated under dry sliding wear, Charpy impact, and immersion corrosion conditions\. Particle size analysis yielded a D50 value of 20\.2 nm, with D10 and D90 values of 12\.4 and 33\.8 nm, respectively\. The specific wear rate decreased from 1\.160 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/\(N·m\) for Al7075 to 8\.456 × 10⁻⁵ and 3\.315 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/\(N·m\) for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano\-BPA composites, respectively\. The absorbed impact energy increased from 5\.5 ± 0\.20 J for Al7075 to 7\.0 ± 0\.25 and 8\.0 ± 0\.30 J for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano\-BPA composites, respectively\. After 72 h of immersion in a 3\.5 wt% NaCl solution, the measured corrosion rate decreased from 0\.649 ± 0\.027 mm/year for Al7075 to 0\.460 ± 0\.027 and 0\.203 ± 0\.014 mm/year for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano\-BPA composites, respectively\. Among the investigated compositions, the 4 wt% Nano\-BPA composite exhibited the best overall measured performance\. These results demonstrate the feasibility of Nano\-BPA as a sustainable reinforcement for improving the experimentally evaluated wear, impact, and corrosion performance of Al7075 composites\.

## [Requisites for applying adaptive control of safety lead time](../publications/a0a1771be9a1e053b662.md)

Helena Forslund; Lisa Hedvall; Joakim Wikner; Mats I\. Johansson; Stig‐Arne Mattsson

Purpose A fundamental manufacturing challenge is how to dimension safety buffers effectively, particularly in today’s challenging competitive environment with increased focus on delivery capability and cost\-efficiency\. An adaptive approach is suggested to overcome such challenges, but no approach is effective unless applied\. The purpose of this study is to explore the requisites for applying adaptive control of safety lead time in manufacturing companies\. Design/methodology/approach An interactive, case\-based research approach identified requisites – practical aspects to consider – for developing and applying adaptive control of safety lead time among four manufacturing companies\. Findings A framework was developed comprising nine propositions on interlinked requisites for understanding cause\-and\-effect relationships, metrics and measuring, balancing performance variables and organizing for control\. The framework is the first step of theory\-building\. Research limitations/implications The framework complements the literature beyond the conceptual idea of an adaptive control approach, positioned within the production planning process\. Extending performance management literature to safety buffer control contributes to understanding and terminology\. A metric, balancing delivery capability risk and cost risk to support application, is proposed\. Practical implications The framework, with provided examples, enables practitioners to understand how to apply adaptive control of safety lead time, thereby increasing the potential real\-world impact on delivery capability and cost\. Originality/value An interactive and longitudinal research approach enabled deep insights into the practical development of applying adaptive control of safety lead time\.

## [An explainable deep learning framework for multi\-class malicious URL classification using priority\-coefficient analysis](../publications/a0a6100a2b7c47523f56.md)

Nguyễn Gia Như; Tran Minh Bao; Arshpreet Kaur; Kumar Shashvat; Dac‐Nhuong Le

The increasing complexity of cyber\-attacks requires URL classifiers that are both accurate and transparent\. This paper presents X\-URL, a pipeline\-level framework for four\-class URL classification \(Benign, Defacement, Malware, and Phishing\)\. A Quantitative Feature Analysis \(QFA\) branch computes URL length, digit density, special\-character frequency, Shannon entropy, Information Gain, and a normalized Priority Coefficient using training data only\. These QFA variables are used for independent statistical validation and class\-specific interpretation; they are not concatenated with character embeddings and do not modify the neural loss\. The predictive path receives only padded character sequences and uses a character\-level Bidirectional Long Short\-Term Memory \(BiLSTM\), class\-frequency weighted cross\-entropy, and Bayesian model selection based on validation macro\-F1\. SHAP DeepExplainer is applied post hoc to the fixed trained model and does not feed back into training or hyperparameter optimization\. On the cleaned training partition, stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation yields 98\.53 ± 0\.03% accuracy for the optimized weighted BiLSTM, compared with 97\.74 ± 0\.20% for the raw BiLSTM, 98\.16 ± 0\.02% for BiLSTM–Random Forest, 97\.93 ± 0\.05% for BiLSTM–XGBoost, and 96\.03 ± 0\.08% for Char\-CNN\. A separate hold\-out snapshot \( n = 130,236\) yields 97\.73% accuracy and 97\.72% weighted F1\. Because production throughput, temporal generalization, domain\-disjoint performance, adversarial robustness, and expert validation were not evaluated, the results support further operational assessment rather than a claim of deployment readiness\.

## [Performance Analysis of Hybrid Deep\-Transfer Learning Approaches with Machine Learning Methods for Face Recognition](../publications/a0aefae3e4b0f7a2125b.md)

Mohsen Mohammadagha; Atena Khoshkonesh; Shayan Sharifi; Vahid Ghanbarizadeh; Farbod Bigdeli

This study addresses the pressing challenge of supervised face recognition under unconstrained conditions by systematically integrating classical machine learning, deep learning, and transfer learning approaches\. While existing literature demonstrates significant progress, particularly with hybrid and transfer learning models, a gap remains in unified, detailed benchmarking across diverse techniques\. The primary objective is to holistically compare Support Vector Machines \(SVM\) with PCA, Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\), XGBoost, a custom Convolutional Neural Network \(CNN\), MobileNetV2\-based transfer learning, and stacked hybrid meta\-models using the Labeled Faces in the Wild \(LFW\) dataset\. The methodology encompasses data preprocessing, parallel feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, ensemble learning, and interpretability analysis\. Experimental results show that stacking hybrid models achieves the highest test accuracy \(87\.9%\) and macro ROC\-AUC \(0\.983\), with MobileNetV2 transfer learning also excelling in sample efficiency and performance\. Future research should expand interpretability diagnostics and benchmark these pipelines on more diverse or occluded datasets for greater real\-world applicability\.

## [Hantavirus emergence through a One Health lens: ecological dynamics, human exposure and integrated surveillance](../publications/a0be84a52df717e06745.md)

Xinyu Wang

Abstract Hantaviruses are rodent\-borne zoonotic viruses that cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas\. Although human hantavirus infections are usually recognised clinically, infection risk is affected by upstream factors including reservoir\-host ecology, environmental variability and human exposure\. Evidence from China, Europe and the Americas shows that the incidence of hantavirus may depend on rodent population dynamics, climate conditions, land use, agricultural practices, housing environments and recreational or travel\-related exposure\. In China, the seasonal pattern of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, including a major autumn–winter peak and a smaller spring or spring–summer peak in many endemic areas, illustrates how virus–host ecology and agricultural labour jointly affect the human risk\. In Europe, bank vole population cycles have been shown to influence Puumala virus epidemics, while studies in the Americas have linked rainfall, rodent abundance and human exposure in domestic, occupational and recreational settings\. This mini review synthesises evidence on the ecological drivers, exposure pathways and surveillance challenges for hantavirus diseases through a One Health lens\. We suggest that One Health approaches should move beyond general calls for multisector collaboration towards evidence\-informed surveillance linking rodent, environmental and human data to setting\-specific prevention, such as issuing seasonal risk warnings and reinforcing exposure\-reduction measures before harvest periods in endemic agricultural regions\.

## [In Quest of the Mythical Mate](../publications/a0bfa2452766c868a14d.md)

Ellyn Bader; Peter Pearson

Written by pioneers in the field of couples therapy, the classic edition of In Quest of the Mythical Mate presents Dr\. Ellyn Bader and Dr\. Peter Pearson&\#x27;s methodology for analyzing how couples&\#x27; relationships develop and grow over time\. They provide practical intervention strategies that promote both individual development and relationship strengthening\. Originally published in 1988, this foundational couples therapy text introduces the Developmental Model of Couples Therapy \(also known as the Bader\-Pearson Model\)\. It provides a structured yet flexible approach to understanding and treating relationship issues\. It offers practical diagnostic tools and treatment strategies that therapists can use with couples in distress including questionnaires, innovative assessment techniques, and specific therapeutic interventions\. This essential book is intended for marriage and family therapists, psychologists, counselors, and other mental health professionals who treat couples\.
