## [Idiopathic digital clubbing](../publications/a0cf171a121be5018960.md)

Nitish Kumar

A 20\-year\-old man presented to our outpatient department with complaints of swelling of the distal portions of the fingers and toes, accompanied by abnormal nail curvature\.It had gradually evolved over time and had not existed since birth\.The patient was otherwise asymptomatic and denied any respiratory, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal or other systemic symptoms\.A thorough family history revealed no 1 st \-or 2 nd \-degree relatives with pachydermoperiostosis, hypertrophic osteoarthropathy or digital clubbing\.Cutaneous and nail examination revealed clubbing involving all fingers and toes \[Figure 1\]\.Schamroth&\#x27;s sign was positive\.Systemic examination was unremarkable\.Chest radiography, electrocardiography, echocardiography, inflammatory markers, routine laboratory tests and other pertinent tests were all within normal ranges\.No periosteal new bone growth was visible on radiographs of the hands and long bones\.A diagnosis of idiopathic digital clubbing was made after primary, secondary and inherited causes were ruled out\.

## [Machine learning\-based interfacial tension prediction for nanoparticles\-assisted enhanced oil recovery](../publications/a0cff76c7a9d734bcd5b.md)

Youssef E\. Kandiel; Omar Mahmoud; Ahmed Farid Ibrahim

Accurate interfacial tension \(IFT\) prediction is crucial for optimizing enhanced oil recovery \(EOR\), as traditional measurement methods are time\-consuming, costly, and often impractical under reservoir conditions\. This study presents a novel machine learning \(ML\) framework for robust IFT prediction\. A comprehensive dataset of 474 data points was curated from published literature, uniquely encompassing a wide variability in reservoir conditions and complex chemical formulations, including 10 distinct nanoparticle \(NP\) types, 4 surfactant classes, and various polymers\. Multiple ML models were developed, including Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\), Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), Random Forest \(RF\), and novel hybrid ensembles \(ANN\-RF and ANN\-XGBoost\)\. The results demonstrated that hybrid and deep learning approaches significantly outperformed simpler models\. The hybrid ANN\-RF model achieved superior validation accuracy \(R 2 = 0\.973, RMSE = 1\.730\), while the standalone ANN \(Test R 2 = 0\.942\) and XGBoost \(Test R 2 = 0\.940\) also showed strong generalization\. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis identified chemical additive concentration as the dominant predictive factor, followed by NP concentration\. Crucially, it revealed that salinity’s significant impact is driven primarily by high\-order interaction effects\. This work establishes a powerful, validated data\-driven tool, highlighting the potential of ML to reduce experimentation and accelerate the design of optimized chemical EOR formulations\. The novelty lies in combining hybrid models with comprehensive sensitivity analysis to deconstruct the complex, interaction\-driven physics of NP\-assisted EOR systems\.

## [Towards a unified biology of vertebrate number sense](../publications/a0dc478ea888207396d5.md)

Mirko Zanon; Andrea Messina; Brian Butterworth; Giorgio Vallortígara; Caroline H\. Brennan; Jose Vicente Torres\-Pérez; Maria Elena Miletto Petrazzini

Number sense, the ability to estimate and compare numerical quantities, emerges early in development and is widespread across species\. Despite decades of work on behavioural and neural correlates of numerosity, the genetic and mechanistic foundations remain poorly integrated\. We propose a review and perspective that brings together evidence from vertebrates\. Our unique focus relies on how genetic variation, brain lateralisation, and neural circuit organisation across development shape number cognition\. We highlight zebrafish \(Danio rerio\) and chicks \(Gallus gallus\) as complementary comparative models that can uncover conserved principles and novel mechanisms, opening new avenues for studying the biological bases of numerical cognition and its disorders from the very early developmental stages\. This review integrates behavioural, genetic and neural evidence for number sense across vertebrates, with a focus on zebrafish and chicks\. Current evidence indicates that numerical abilities rely on evolutionarily conserved mechanisms that emerge early in development and can be linked from genes to neural circuits\.

## [Escalating Antimicrobial and Antifungal Resistance: Mechanistic Insights and Natural Product\-Based Interventions](../publications/a0ded92e06431c711610.md)

Shivangi Sharma; Satyender Kumar

Background: Antimicrobial resistance \(AMR\) and antifungal resistance \(AFR\) have emerged as significant health risks in the world, with recent \(2024\-2025\) data on the growth in resistance of pathogens \(Acinetobacter baumannii, Candida aureus, Trichophyton indotineae, etc\.\) causing treatment failure and mortality\. Objective: To discuss the current tendencies in AMR and AFR, clarify the molecular\-based mechanisms, and assess the possibility of the natural product\-based intervention as alternative or additive treatment\. Methods: The recent literature and worldwide surveillance reports were reviewed in the form of a narrative, and the selected topic included resistance epidemiology, molecular pathways \(enzymatic degradation, target modification, efflux pumps, biofilms, and gene transfer\), and emerging natural therapeutics such as phytochemicals and nanocarrier systems\. Results: There was great increase in the number of multidrug resistant bacterial and fungal pathogens, with last\-line agent resistance\. Natural products like cinnamaldehyde, eugenol and curcumin showed potential antimicrobial effects especially by a synergistic and biofilm disrupting mechanism\. Greater bioavailability was increased with the help of advanced delivery systems, but clinical validation is limited\. Conclusion: AMR and AFR is an urgent world problem that needs comprehensive measures\. Natural products have a good potential in adjunctive solutions, but the standardized clinical validation and regulatory frameworks are the key to successful translation of these solutions into practices\.

## [Social commerce and Consumer Shopping Behavior: A Qualitative Study at Atrium Senen Mal, Jakarta](../publications/a0e52468e279dab91d84.md)

Muhammad Alfauzan Katili; Gorendva R\. Warganegara

Advances in digital technology and social media have shifted consumer shopping paradigms from physical shopping centers to social commerce platforms such as TikTok Shop\. This study aims to understand the impact of social commerce on changes in consumer shopping behavior at Mal Atrium Senen, Jakarta\. The novelty of this research lies in integrating the analysis of consumer behavior in social commerce with its impact on physical shopping centers, specifically Mal Atrium Senen, using primary data from open questionnaires presented in diagrams and narratives\. The approach used is qualitative descriptive with 28 participants who are active TikTok Shop users selected through purposive sampling\. Data analysis was conducted through data reduction, which involved sorting, focusing attention, and simplifying information in line with the research objectives\. The results show that spontaneous or impulsive buying is the dominant factor at 82\.1%, followed by content and promotion at 71\.4%, influencer recommendations at 57\.1%, and live shopping at 42\.9%\. As a result, visits and transactions at Mal Atrium Senen have decreased\. This study concludes that social commerce significantly changes consumer shopping behavior\. The limitation of this study lies in purposive sampling that only involved active TikTok Shop consumers, so the findings cannot be generalized to all mall visitors\. Future research is suggested to compare users and non\-users of social commerce, involve participants across ages, use a mixed\-method approach, and measure actual transaction data\.

## [PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State](../publications/a0e829dba0981fd5b673.md)

Peña Arroyo Gallego; Mauro Ruiz Moreno; Alejandro Acien; Sergio Romero\-Tapiador; Teresa Arroyo\-Gallego

Presence\-aware intelligence is the capacity of an AI system&\#x27;s intelligence layer to adapt appropriately to the functional state of the person it serves \(here readiness, flow, and stability\) while preserving task quality and safety\. We introduce PresenceBench, an instrument for measuring it\. PresenceBench evaluates how the intelligence layer uses a supplied state, not how that state is sensed, and breaks the capability into measurable properties\. Two are tested here\. Receptivity: does the model take up the state and give a better response than with no signal? Specificity: does any improvement depend on the correct state, rather than on extra structured context? A third, adaptation across states, is a required endpoint not measured in this release\. A five\-arm causal design answers both questions, against each model&\#x27;s own baseline and an equally structured mismatched\-state control, scored by a correctness\-gated human paired comparison\. The exploratory evaluation covered four models across eighteen single\-turn, six fixed three\-turn and six simulated natural\-conversation scenarios\. Supplying a synthetic state, raw or translated into a response policy, gave human\-preference point estimates above 0\.5 for all four models \(Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3\.6 Flash, GPT\-5\.6 Terra\), with three of eight 95% intervals excluding chance\. Specificity was not resolved: no per\-model interval excluded chance, and the design cannot yet separate the state values from a generic instruction to adapt\. Policy delivery reduced priced cost and output tokens against each model&\#x27;s baseline; these are resource\-use changes, not efficiency gains, because correctness non\-inferiority was not established\. Safety\-floor failures were rare \(13 of 360 cases\), with a non\-significant excess under policy delivery\. We report the instrument, the frozen results, and the controls a confirmatory study needs\.

## [From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness\-Protected Coding Agents](../publications/a0ecd92b88b3e7b13d3c.md)

Xianglin Yang; Yechao Zhang; Jiahao Liu; Yulin Chen; Yuxin Cao; Bryan Hooi; Jiaheng Zhang

Coding agents use execution harnesses to constrain the consequences of prompt injection by enforcing permission boundaries\. These systems deterministically intercept any out\-of\-sandbox action and prompt the user for approval\. To reduce approval fatigue, users can approve allow\-rules proposed by the agent, after which any future action matching the rule is allowed without a prompt\. In this work, we show that this mechanism introduces a new risk: untrusted context can influence the permissions presented for approval, with consequences extending beyond the immediate task\. We investigate privilege escalation targeting this permission\-update process\. Specifically, adversarial context planted in a repository can reliably steer an agent performing a routine task into requesting a plausibly justified, yet dangerously broad allow\-rule\. If the user approves the request, the saved rule can effectively blind the harness, enabling adversaries to execute malicious actions that would otherwise require approval, without triggering human oversight\. Across production platforms, including Claude Code and Codex CLI, we demonstrate that agents successfully elicit the target allow\-rules in 58% of experimental instances\. Once acquired, these rules exhibit a massive semantic blast radius, covering 56\.9% of category\-specific capability test cases\. To further quantify the downstream risk, we show that conditional on rule approval, our exploit achieves verified, silent goal completion in 47 of the 58 eligible instances \(81\.0%\), undermining the safety promise of human\-in\-the\-loop oversight\.

## [Not All Graphs Are Maps: A Task\-Agnostic Exploration Framework for Mobile GUI Navigation](../publications/a0ef705aa3e2dfd0dffa.md)

Adamo Orsini; Seyed Mehdi Ayyoubzadeh; Sadman Rakib Pinon; Hannuo Zhang; Koosha Gholipour Baradari; Yuanhao Yu; Xinxin Zuo; Yang Wang

Modern mobile GUI agents can perceive visible screens and execute local actions, but they still lack persistent app\-specific navigation knowledge: where functions live, which pages contain them, and which screens are equivalent across repeated visits\. We introduce TAG\-Nav, a Task\-Agnostic Graph Navigation framework that wraps existing GUI\-agent backbones with reusable destination memory\. Offline exploration is distilled into compact records of app functions, target pages, and waypoint routes before any evaluated instruction is seen\. When a future task&\#x27;s destination is covered, TAG\-Nav retrieves the destination and provides route guidance without task\-specific demonstrations\. This separates mobile GUI destination navigation from full task completion: many tasks share the prefix of reaching the right page, while final actions may enter content, send data, make purchases, delete information, or change sensitive settings\. To evaluate route finding without downstream execution confounds, we introduce DestBench, a navigation\-only protocol that asks whether an agent reaches the correct pre\-action destination screen\. DestBench enables a controlled graph\-memory study comparing no\-memory agents with random, automated BFS, and clean graph memory\. Graph\-derived memory improves strict navigation success rate of UI\-TARS\-1\.5\-7B from 52\.4% without graph memory to 58\.3% with automated BFS memory, and improves Qwen\-VL\-Max success rate from 59\.5% to 71\.4% on the same conditions\. Together, TAG\-Nav and DestBench show that destination coverage and route cleanliness strongly shape graph\-memory value, making graph quality a measured variable rather than an assumed benefit of exploration\.

## [CSR Disclosure and Price Discovery Efficiency in MENA Firms: The Moderating Roles of Foreign Directors and Shareholders](../publications/a0f4f6e6366352be812c.md)

Imen Khanchel; Naima Lassoued; Mohamed Malek Belhoula; Rawen Rourou

ABSTRACT This study investigates the impact of Corporate Social Responsibility disclosure \(CSRD\) on the price discovery efficiency of 220 non‐financial firms listed on stock exchanges across 10 MENA countries from 2010 to 2022\. We analyze how CSRD influences the speed at which new information is incorporated into stock prices\. Our findings indicate that global CSRD and all CSRD components \(environmental disclosure, social disclosure, human rights disclosure and employee disclosure\) decrease pricing efficiency by amplifying information asymmetry\. We conclude that CSRD acts as noise rather than a credible signal\. Additionally, our study shows that foreign directors exert a beneficial moderating effect on the relationship between CSRD \(including the overall CSRD measure and the four components\) and price discovery efficiency\. Finally, foreign shareholders serve as a positive moderator in the relationship between CSRD \(including the overall CSRD measure, environmental disclosure component, and employee disclosure component\) and price discovery efficiency\.

## [The impact of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions: an empirical examination based on Chinese urban panel data](../publications/a0fd72a198df372d8f7b.md)

Chao Wang; Haitao Zhang

Depressive emotions have emerged as a critical public health concern, with their etiology closely linked to the natural environment, particularly air quality\. Grounded in environmental stress theory and social support theory, this study utilizes panel data from 277 prefecture\-level cities in China spanning 2011–2023 to theoretically analyze and empirically examine the effects of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions and the underlying mechanisms\. The findings reveal that: First, improvements in air quality significantly reduce public attention to depressive emotions, a conclusion that remains robust across multiple robustness tests\. Second, the unemployment rate serves as a partial mediator between air quality and public attention to depressive emotions, while healthcare workforce allocation and public fiscal expenditure effectively buffer the adverse psychological impacts of air quality deterioration\. Third, the influence of air quality on public attention to depressive emotions exhibits significant urban heterogeneity, being more pronounced in eastern and central regions, cities with net population outflows, and mature and declining resource\-based cities\. By examining environmental public goods and social support systems, this study provides novel empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between air quality and public mental health, offering valuable insights for promoting synergy between environmental policies and social security policies\.

## [Lithostratigraphically\-constrained landslide susceptibility modeling in red\-bed basins using a bayesian probability\-based mixture probabilistic neural network](../publications/a0fd77d050e8448e58d8.md)

Zidan Liu; Aihua Yi; Gen Huang; Qi Li; Tongyi Zheng

Regional landslide susceptibility prediction commonly treats diverse failure mechanisms as a single statistical entity, an oversimplification that fails in lithologically complex red\-bed basins, where retrogressive and translational landslides follow fundamentally distinct hydromechanical laws\. Here we develop a mechanism\-divergent framework that integrates frequency ratio factor screening, Bayesian probability for uncertainty\-aware dataset construction, and a mixture probabilistic neural network to explicitly fuse multi\-modal susceptibility indices\. The approach is validated in Sanshui District, a subtropical red\-bed basin in China, using a 15\-year multi\-source inventory\. Random forest and logistic regression are coupled with frequency ratio and Bayesian strategies to independently predict each landslide type\. Bayesian\-enhanced models consistently outperform their frequency\-ratio counterparts, with Bayesian random forest achieving the highest accuracy\. The mixture probabilistic neural network captures spatial heterogeneity through distance\-weighted neural connections, markedly improving regional mapping and attaining an area under the curve of 90\.2%, substantially higher than the 66\.7% of conventional unified models\. Shapley additive explanation analysis identifies lithology, annual precipitation, and road proximity as dominant controls; lithostratigraphic Groups 1, 7, 12 and 13 exhibit the highest susceptibility\. This framework offers a lithostratigraphy\-informed, mechanism\-aware pathway for landslide risk assessment in complex soft\-rock terrains\.

## [PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN DALAM PEMBELAJARAN DI SEKOLAH DASAR: PELUANG DAN TANTANGAN BAGI GURU DI KABUPATEN BUNGOThis study aims to identify opportunities and challenges of AI utilization by elementary teachers in Bungo Regency, Jambi Province, and to](../publications/a108db3efc193653b430.md)

Sarmiati; Baili Kurniawan; Sugeng Kurniawan; Rugaiyah; Muhammad Sayuti

This study aims to identify opportunities and challenges of AI utilization by elementary teachers in Bungo Regency, Jambi Province, and to map adaptation strategies developed within resource\-constrained contexts\. Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, the research involved 15 purposively selected teachers with varied age, teaching experience, and school locations\. Data were collected through in\-depth interviews, classroom observations, and pedagogical document analysis, then analyzed thematically using Braun &amp; Clarke’s framework assisted by NVivo 14\. Findings reveal four main opportunities: \(1\) personalized learning pathways, \(2\) administrative efficiency and formative assessment, \(3\) interactive multimodal material development, and \(4\) expanded access to learning references\. Conversely, structural and pedagogical challenges emerged, including digital infrastructure gaps, TPACK competency variation, ethical concerns regarding data privacy and technological dependency, and lack of continuous mentoring\. Grounded in TPACK and UTAUT theoretical frameworks, the findings explain how perceived usefulness, ease of use, and institutional support shape AI adoption\. The study recommends practice\-based training enhancement, hybrid infrastructure provision, and responsive school policies for technological innovation\. This research contributes to elementary education literature in non\-metropolitan regions and offers a contextual, ethical, and sustainable AI implementation framework\.

## [COMPARATIVE GENOMIC ANALYSIS OF PROBIOTIC STRAINS FOR SAFETY AND FUNCTIONAL ATTRIBUTES](../publications/a10d1c9fe8ab77f73a7d.md)

Manochitra A S; Inchara K S; Monishkumar R; Kowshika S; Reshma A S; Balakrishnaraja Rengaraju

Probiotics are good bacteria that help keep people healthy by balancing the microbes in the gut, improving the immune system, and supporting important body processes\. As they are used more in special foods, supplements, and treatments, it&\#x27;s important to check how safe they are and how well they work, looking at their genetic makeup\. This study looked at four common probiotic strains: Lactobacillus rhamnosus, Lactobacillus plantarum, Bifidobacterium bifidum, and Bifidobacterium longum\. The full genetic codes of these bacteria were taken from public databases and checked for quality using tools like QUAST and CheckM\. The genes in each genome were studied using RASTtk to find out which ones help the bacteria have probiotic benefits\. To make sure the probiotics are safe, they checked for harmful genes and genes that make bacteria resistant to antibiotics\. For their useful functions, they looked at genes connected to breaking down sugars, using amino acids, making vitamins, and responding to stress\. By comparing the genes of these strains, the study found out which parts of the genome are shared and which are unique to each strain\. The results showed that all the selected probiotics had high\-quality genomes, were safe, and had different kinds of useful genes\. Lactobacillus plantarum had the most variety in its functions, while Lactobacillus rhamnosus was better at handling stress\. This research shows that using genome comparisons is a good way to check the safety and effectiveness of probiotics\. The findings help find better probiotics and support making safe and effective products for food, health supplements, and medical treatments\.

## [Front\-line decision\-making: a thematic analysis of interviews with hospital staff on referrals, admissions, and care for people with multiple long\-term conditions](../publications/a1101f7a2cd7171b3834.md)

Sara Pretorius; Sue Bellass; Rachel Cooper; Felicity Evison; Rachel Cooper; Nicola Howe; Elizabeth Sapey; Amelia Sheppard; Jana Suklan; Avan Aihie Sayer; Miles D\. Witham

BACKGROUND: Multiple long\-term conditions \(MLTC\) are increasingly common and present challenges for hospital healthcare professionals \(HCPs\) making decisions about admissions, referrals, and care management in the context of a single\-organ oriented health system\. This qualitative study examined how HCPs in emergency and acute hospital settings make such decisions for people living with MLTC, exploring factors that influence clinical judgement and how HCPs respond to these challenges\. METHODS: HCPs involved in making decisions about care for people living with MLTC presenting to hospital were recruited via National Health Service \(NHS\) research delivery networks and professional contacts, using purposive and snowball sampling\. Semi\-structured individual interviews were conducted, focusing on how HCPs make decisions regarding the care of people living with MLTC and factors influencing such decisions\. Reflexive thematic analysis was undertaken\. Themes relating to influences on decision\-making were organised using the Social Ecological Model \(SEM\)\. RESULTS: We interviewed 40 HCPs working in NHS emergency departments and acute assessment units across multiple regions, specialties and roles\. Seven themes were constructed and organised into two overarching categories\. The first category &\#x27;Factors Influencing Decision\-Making&\#x27; included the themes the complex patient, professional expertise and identity, system pressures and inflexible structures\. These themes were mapped to the SEM, demonstrating influences across individual and environmental levels\. The second category &\#x27;Adaptive Decision\-Making Strategies&\#x27; included the themes Mitigating risk and Relying on heuristics capturing how HCPs navigate the uncertainty created by these influences\. The theme, Relational care, operated between categories, illustrating how relationships both shape what decisions are possible \(interpersonal level of SEM\) and provide a means of navigating uncertainty\. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical decision\-making for people living with MLTC in emergency and acute settings is shaped by uncertainty arising from the interaction of factors operating across individual, interpersonal and environmental levels\. To manage this uncertainty, staff employ a range of adaptive strategies\. However, participants described this level of compensatory work as challenging and potentially insufficient on its own\. Supporting decision\-making and reducing reliance on adaptive responses may benefit from system‑level change, including improved community care, enhanced generalist expertise, opportunities for relational decision\-making, better continuity and shared ownership of care, and flexible care pathways\.

## [Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure](../publications/a110223ffb266b9de5e1.md)

Nellia Bellaert; Federico Cassioli; Wan\-Ling Tseng; Mandy Rossignol

Irritability is characterized by a propensity to experience frustration and has been associated with reduced self\-reported willingness to expend effort for rewards\. Frustration may be relevant to effortful reward pursuit, but its effects on effort expenditure have rarely been experimentally tested in humans\. To address this gap, this study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort\-Doors task to elicit frustrative nonreward \(FNR\), a negative emotional state triggered by unexpected reward loss, and examined its effects on physical effort expenditure and feedback\-related electroencephalographic \(EEG\) activity\. We also tested whether these effects vary as a function of state and trait measures of motivation and affect\. Linear mixed\-effects models tested the effects of FNR induction on self\-reported, behavioral, and EEG measures in young adults \(N = 83\) completing the Frustrative Effort\-Doors task\. Models tested manipulation effects, trial\-level post\-feedback adjustment, and moderation by state and trait measures\. Midfrontal theta power \(MFθ\) extracted using multivariate spatial filtering was examined as a function of feedback \(win vs\. FNR\), effort \(low vs\. high\), and subsequent behavioral adjustments\. The frustration condition was associated with decreased self\-reported state motivation and increased frustration, arousal, and response speed\. Midfrontal theta power was larger following FNR feedback and increased with state frustration during high\-effort trials\. Higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following FNR feedback\. MFθ did not predict trial\-to\-trial behavioral adjustments\. These findings indicate that FNR recruits MFθ, a neural marker of cognitive control, while state frustration modulates physical effort execution following unexpected reward loss\.

## [When Magnitude Suffices: Reconstructing Time\-Domain\-Gated Microwave Signals Without Phase on a Thoracic Phantom](../publications/a1129d7380b6b8dc8856.md)

Maciej Cichoń; Patrycja Gołaś; Maksymilian Bartosik; Angelika Walczak; Agata Bielecka\-Dąbrowa; Maciej Ślot

Time\-domain gating separates the arrivals that form a microwave S\-parameter measurement\. It requires the measurement of complex values, so this application almost always uses a vector network analyzer \(VNA\)\. We show that, on one calibrated measurement configuration, the gated magnitude the VNA would give can be reconstructed from a magnitude\-only sweep of a spectrum analyzer with a tracking generator \(SA\)\. We select the gate center for separability of the measured states, correct each instrument once by a per\-bin subtraction of a reference state, and train a fully connected network on sweeps from both instruments\. The test object is a torso phantom with lung\-shaped compartments whose filling takes eleven dielectric states, each held out in turn\. On $S\_\{11\}$ the reconstruction from SA input reaches a shape error of 0\.08 dB$^2$ with a state ordering of 0\.81\. This matches the reconstruction from VNA input\. On $S\_\{21\}$ it reaches 0\.82 dB$^2$ and keeps the ordered groups of the states\. An explicit phase prediction performs much worse, because gating needs the phase to about 0\.2 rad RMS\. Across eleven measurement configurations the dependence of phase on magnitude is strong for reflection and weak for transmission\. This explains the difference between $S\_\{11\}$ and $S\_\{21\}$\. Where the magnitude carries enough of the phase, a scalar instrument gives the gated response without any phase measurement after installation\. On the open UM\-BMID breast data set, with whole phantoms held out, the shape error of the network is 30 percent lower than that of a per\-bin linear map\.

## [Uncertainty propagation from vision\-based tool wear measurements to cutting loads](../publications/a1145e2ed74c6cef020f.md)

Jamshid Ravshanovich Ravshanov; Bektosh Kodirov; Faxriddin Barakaev; Dostonjon Oripov

This study presents a computational approach to predicting cutting loads while accounting for uncertainty in machine\-vision\-based tool\-wear measurements during computer numerical control machining\. The proposed methodology integrates image segmentation, quantitative assessment of tool flank wear, and mathematical modeling of cutting force and spindle torque as functions of tool wear\. Three segmentation methods are considered: Otsu thresholding with morphological operations, Canny edge detection with morphological processing, and a convolutional neural network based on the U\-Net architecture\. The performance of these methods was evaluated under different image\-quality conditions using pixel accuracy, intersection over union \(IoU\), the Dice coefficient, and relative wear\-width measurement error\. When the image\-quality index decreased from 1\.00 to 0\.40, the IoU of the neural\-network\-based method decreased from 0\.866 to 0\.626, while the Dice coefficient decreased from 0\.927 to 0\.759\. Within the considered computational model, increasing tool wear was accompanied by a 100\.6% increase in radial cutting force and a 66\.3% increase in spindle torque\. The results demonstrate that high pixel accuracy alone is not a sufficient criterion for reliable quantitative tool\-wear measurement\. A methodological basis was established for assessing the propagation of uncertainty from tool\-wear measurements to predicted mechanical loads\. The obtained results may be used for further development of tool\-condition monitoring systems and cutting\-load prediction in CNC machining\. Additional quantitative and experimental validation is required to confirm the practical applicability of the proposed approach\.

## [AEDS: Adaptive edge‐difference shaping for piecewise‐stationary sparse‐reward reinforcement learning](../publications/a11a4e22d54c43e1abdd.md)

Younghwan Shin; Byunghyun Yoo; Jeongmin Yang; Jung‐Hoon Lee; Cheol Ho Kim; Euisok Chung; Hyun Woo Kim; Hwa Jeon Song

Abstract Sparse‐reward tasks with piecewise‐stationary topology shifts challenge reinforcement learning\. Continuous spectral shaping biases agents toward geometric extrema and can delay adaptation when bottlenecks move\. We propose adaptive edge‐difference shaping \(AEDS\), a spectral reward‐shaping method that focuses exploration on structural bottlenecks\. AEDS triggers a direction‐agnostic intrinsic reward only when the agent crosses the sign‐flip boundary of the dynamically updated Fiedler vector\. An episodic gating mechanism limits rewarded crossings and bounds the cumulative intrinsic return\. Within each stationary phase, AEDS induces an augmented Markov decision process to which the standard tabular Q‐learning convergence theorem applies\. We evaluate AEDS on grid environments with shifting bottlenecks and geometric traps\. Across the evaluation, AEDS performs strongly in several bottleneck‐oriented settings, while count‐based exploration or well‐oriented dense spectral shaping can be preferable in other regimes\. These results support a focused scope for AEDS in bottleneck‐oriented sparse‐reward grid tasks\.

## [Potential Application of Carbon Nanotubes and Ag\-doped Carbon Nanotubes for Ethylene \(C2H4\) Adsorbent in Postharvest Agriculture](../publications/a11d786faa3b7536d784.md)

Art Anthony Z\. Munio

Ethylene \(C2H4\) control technologies in postharvest agriculture are critical for minimizing wastage and maintaining the market value of climacteric fruits\. The present study reports molecular interactions between C2H4 and single\-walled carbon nanotubes \(SWCNTs\) and Ag\-doped single\-walled carbon nanotubes \(Ag\-doped SWCNTs\) using density functional theory\-based simulations\. The ground\-state calculations demonstrate that C2H4 is attached to the sidewall of the prototype single\-walled carbon nanotube \(SWCNT\) via weak physisorption, with bonding mediated by minor charge redistribution\. The interaction between C2H4 and the prototype nanotube can be enhanced by introducing an Ag dopant into the SWCNT sidewall, forming an Ag\-C2H4 π\-complex\. The Ag dopant can trap multiple C2H4 molecules, implying superior adsorbent performance\. The NVT molecular dynamics simulations at 300 K predicted that the presence of competing H2O and CO2 weakens C2H4 binding on the surface of pristine SWCNT, leading to its diffusion\. In contrast, the π\-complex structure of C2H4 with Ag\-dopant remains stable despite the presence of competing volatile gases\. The simulations predicted that Ag\-SWCNT is an effective adsorbent for C2H4 in H2O\- and CO2\-rich environments, such as in postharvest storage\. Overall, the findings presented herein will serve as a reference for the design of C2H4 control technologies in postharvest agriculture\.

## [Composition determination of biodiesel/ethanol blends using dielectric spectroscopy and tabular prior\-data fitted networks](../publications/a124a399e9216cf2cd7a.md)

Julián Corach; Martín González; Lautaro Gómez Ciapponi; P\.A\. Sorichetti

Biodiesel/ethanol blends represent a promising alternative to reduce the consumption of fossil diesel\. This work employs frequency\-domain dielectric spectroscopy to determine the permittivity of biodiesel/ethanol blends across the full range of compositions, at temperatures between 293 K and 333 K, and within a frequency range from 1 MHz to 30 MHz\. Within this interval, the real part of the permittivity is frequency\-independent, and electrical losses are negligible\. Leveraging these experimental results, a transformer\-based deep learning model implementing Tabular Prior\-data Fitted Networks \(TabPFN\) was developed to determine the blend composition from temperature and permittivity measurements\. Evaluated via Leave\-One\-Out Cross\-Validation, the proposed TabPFN model predicted the composition with high accuracy, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0\.997, an average absolute deviation of 1\.0 mol%, and a root mean squared error of 1\.6 mol%\. These results outperform conventional machine learning algorithms as well as standard analytical inversion models, operating in a single forward pass without requiring hyperparameter tuning or data scaling\. Overall, using high\-frequency dielectric spectroscopy together with tabular foundation models are the basis of a streamlined, highly efficient strategy for non\-destructive biofuel quality verification\.

## [A HIPERDIGITALIZAÇÃO DOS SERVIÇOS ESSENCIAIS E A EXCLUSÃO DIGITAL DA PESSOA IDOSA: OS DESAFIOS DA AUTOMAÇÃO E DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA GARANTIA DE DIREITOS FUNDAMENTAIS](../publications/a129613e3ca4903534e6.md)

Regina Gomes da Costa Moreira; Andressa Costenaro

Contextualização do tema: A digitalização dos serviços públicos e privados modificou a forma como as pessoas acessam informações, realizam procedimentos e participam da vida social\. Embora o avanço das tecnologias digitais, da automação e da inteligência artificial tenha ampliado possibilidades de acesso e praticidade, esse processo também apresenta desafios para a inclusão da população idosa\. Objetivos: Analisar os impactos da digitalização dos serviços essenciais, da automação e da inteligência artificial na garantia dos direitos fundamentais da pessoa idosa, considerando aspectos relacionados à autonomia, à acessibilidade, à participação social e à exclusão digital\. Metodologia: Trata\-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem qualitativa, realizada a partir da análise de estudos científicos, legislação e documentos institucionais\. O levantamento bibliográfico foi realizado por meio de consultas ao Google Acadêmico, SciELO, Portal de Periódicos CAPES e Biblioteca Digital Brasileira de Teses e Dissertações, além de periódicos científicos e sites oficiais de instituições relacionadas ao tema\. Considerações e resultados: A análise demonstrou que a exclusão digital não se limita à ausência de internet ou de equipamentos, envolvendo também dificuldades na utilização das plataformas, na compreensão dos procedimentos, na segurança e na disponibilidade de suporte\. Os resultados indicam que a inteligência artificial e a automação podem ampliar possibilidades de acesso, mas também podem produzir barreiras quando utilizadas sem condições adequadas de acessibilidade ou como única forma de atendimento\. Conclui\-se que a modernização tecnológica pode coexistir com a proteção dos direitos fundamentais da pessoa idosa, desde que seja acompanhada por medidas de inclusão digital, serviços acessíveis, suporte adequado e preservação de alternativas de atendimento, protegendo sua autonomia, dignidade e participação social\.

## [Penguatan Budaya Membaca dan Numerik Bagi Anak Usia Sekolah di Wilayah KKN](../publications/a1361ebb43e41401df8d.md)

Irwan Yon Hadi; Suhaini; Mutmain Natulaila Noviana; Muhammad Marwazi; Yuyun Ayu Lestari; Muh\. Sahidi; Juliadi; Moh\. Asrorul Hayyi; Pinta Mauladia; Meta Intan Kuswari; Juliati; Nururl Huda; Sarniati; Desti Septiana Putri

Reading literacy and numeracy are fundamental skills that play an important role in supporting children&\#x27;s academic development and everyday life\. However, observations conducted in the area of the Community Service Program \(Kuliah Kerja Nyata/KKN\) showed that reading habits among school\-age children had not yet been fully established, and some children still experienced difficulties in applying numeracy skills to everyday problems\. This community service activity aimed to strengthen reading culture and numeracy skills among school\-age children through creative, participatory, and enjoyable learning activities\. The method employed a participatory approach consisting of preparation, implementation, evaluation, and follow\-up stages\. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and evaluation of participants&\#x27; reading and numeracy skills\. Reading activities included shared reading, reading assistance, storytelling, discussions, educational games, and quizzes\. Meanwhile, numeracy activities were conducted through number games, arithmetic exercises, mathematics quizzes, and contextual problems related to everyday life\. The results showed that children demonstrated better enthusiasm and participation when literacy and numeracy activities were presented in an interactive and enjoyable manner\. The activities also provided different learning experiences and encouraged children to become more active in reading, understanding texts, performing calculations, and solving simple problems\. Support from the village government, village staff, and community members was an important factor in the implementation and sustainability of the program\. Therefore, strengthening reading culture and numeracy through participatory activities can serve as an effort to improve learning motivation and fundamental skills among school\-age children and should be continued sustainably with the involvement of families and the community\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI DISCRETE TIME\-CRYSTAL QUANTUM ARCHITECTURE \(DTC\-QA\): NON\-EQUILIBRIUM PHASE COMPUTING AND ULTRA\-PRECISE SPATIOTEMPORAL METROLOGY VIA BROKEN TIME TRANSLATION SYMMETRY](../publications/a13a521209817490cb14.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Discrete Time\-Crystal Quantum Architecture \(DTC\-QA\) transitions quantum computing from spatial to spatiotemporal paradigms\. It utilizes Discrete Time Crystals \(DTCs\) engineered via Floquet driving and Many\-Body Localization \(MBL\) to perform non\-equilibrium phase computing\. The system spontaneously breaks discrete time\-translation symmetry, exhibiting sub\-harmonic oscillations where the expectation value satisfies O\(t\+T\) \!= O\(t\) but O\(t\+nT\) = O\(t\) for integer n&gt;1\. This topologically protected temporal order enables Chrono\-Reservoir Computing, where classical measurement outcomes of local observables serve as high\-dimensional temporal features without full\-state tomography\. The architecture minimizes the El\-Rakhawi Chrono\-Computational Loss \(L\_CCL\), penalizing subsystem bipartite entanglement entropy growth to prevent Floquet heating\. Performance is quantified by the El\-Rakhawi Chrono\-Computational Fidelity Metric \(ECCFM\), yielding bits per Joule\. Applications include fault\-tolerant quantum AI, ultralight dark matter detection, and precision quantum metrology, bridging quantum physics, materials science, and artificial intelligence\.

## [Die kybernetische Psychokratie: Vom zweistufigen mathematischen Kreislauf](../publications/a13b05eec6e6ab87d626.md)

Peter Siegfried Krug

Das klassische Ideal der westlichen Demokratie basiert auf der Prämisse des mündigen Bürgers, der freie und rationale Entscheidungen trifft\. Das vorliegende Werk dekonstruiert dieses Paradigma angesichts des flächendeckenden Einsatzes generativer Künstlicher Intelligenz\. Der Autor Peter Siegfried Krug beschreibt den Übergang von reaktiver Datenüberwachung hin zur &quot;kybernetischen Psychokratie&quot; – einer operationalen Steuerung des menschlichen Bewusstseins durch psychometrische Extraktion und die algorithmische Modellierung statistischer Zwillinge\. Neben den theoretischen Fundamenten des zweistufigen mathematischen Kreislaufs und des informationstechnischen Trennungsprinzips analysiert die Arbeit die marktdominierende &quot;Default\-Falle&quot; mobiler Betriebssysteme\. Am konkreten Fallbeispiel der 2\.093 österreichischen Bürgermeister wird dargelegt, wie algorithmisches Mikrotargeting die Strukturen der Kommunalpolitik gläsern macht und transformiert\. Das Werk schließt mit einem staatspolitischen Plädoyer für den Erhalt der kognitiven Souveränität durch strategische digitale Inaktivität\.

## [Deep Learning Approaches to Teaching And Learning: An Integrative Review from the Perspectives of Multiple Learning Theories](../publications/a13eab5c8408ceb47363.md)

Baharuddin Baharuddin

The deep learning approach in education is a learning strategy oriented toward in\-depth conceptual understanding, reflection, and integration of knowledge\. This study aims to analyze the deep learning approach from the perspectives of multiple learning theories, namely behaviorism, cognitivism, humanism, and constructivism\. The deep learning approach is considered relevant to addressing the challenges of twenty\-first\-century education because it emphasizes deep conceptual understanding, critical thinking skills, and learners’ active engagement in the learning process\. However, the implementation of this approach is often not supported by a strong theoretical understanding\. Therefore, this study employs a descriptive qualitative literature review method by analyzing various academic sources to identify the contributions of each learning theory to the deep learning approach\. The findings indicate that behaviorism shapes purposeful learning behaviors; cognitivism provides a foundation for information\-processing strategies and metacognition; humanism emphasizes the importance of intrinsic motivation, personal values, and individual growth; while constructivism supports active, collaborative, and contextualized learning\. The synthesis of these four perspectives establishes a comprehensive conceptual foundation for developing transformative and holistic deep learning instructional designs\. This study makes a significant conceptual contribution to the development of learning strategies that integrate behavioral, cognitive, affective, and social dimensions in a balanced manner\.

## [Nanotechnology Applied to Anesthesia: The Potential of Local Analgesics and Opioids in Liposomal Systems](../publications/a156553dfaa1514d4706.md)

Karen Priscilla Oliveira CASTRO; Amanda Muller Baptista Nunes; Gabriela Tais Stiehl; Ruan Fernandes da Rosa; Felipe Ferreira Gomes; Mônica Santos Primeira; Laura Böttcher Lins; Jhonatan De Campos Rosa; Mateus Udino Sari; Caroline dos Santos Nader; Lucas de Campos Spindola; Nicole Ries Girardi

Nanotechnology has emerged as a promising strategy for the development of controlled\-release drug delivery systems, with potential applications in anesthesiology and the treatment of perioperative pain\.Among these technologies, liposomal systems stand out for their ability to encapsulate both hydrophilic and lipophilic substances, modify their pharmacokinetics, and promote gradual release at the site of action\.The use of local anesthetics and opioids incorporated into liposomal systems aims to prolong analgesia, reduce plasma peaks, decrease the frequency of administration, and potentially reduce opioid consumption and its adverse events\.Liposomal bupivacaine is currently one of the main clinical applications of this strategy, while liposomal formulations of morphine and other opioids remain relevant in the context of research and specific applications\.Experimental studies demonstrate that the encapsulation of opioids can modify systemic exposure and prolong the analgesic effect\.However, the clinical results of liposomal bupivacaine are heterogeneous, with trials and meta\-analyses showing modest benefits or a lack of superiority compared to conventional anesthetics\.Recent studies also indicate that its benefits may depend on the surgical procedure, the regional technique used, and the multimodal analgesia protocol\.Thus, liposomal systems represent an important nanotechnological platform for anesthesia, but their use must be individualized and based on clinical, pharmacoeconomic, and safety evidence\.Future development should focus on optimizing formulations, achieving specific tissue targeting, controlling drug release, and identifying patients who stand to benefit the most\.

## [SUPERVISIÓN TOLERANTE A FALLOS MEDIANTE REDES NEURONALES EXPLICABLES PARA EL CONTROL DE PROCESOS ALIMENTARIOS](../publications/a15a3d5de21fb4f19abf.md)

Letícia de Souza Lima; Pedro Vieira Souza Santos; José Wendel dos Santos

Este estudio tiene como objetivo desarrollar y evaluar una arquitectura de redes neuronales artificiales explicables para la supervisión tolerante a fallos de un proceso térmico, centrándose en la clasificación de fallos y en la evaluación de acciones correctivas bajo condiciones simuladas de operación\. Se utilizó un modelo térmico simplificado para generar datos sintéticos que representan el funcionamiento normal y diferentes escenarios de fallo\. Se desarrolló un perceptrón multicapa \(MLP\) para clasificar las condiciones operativas, mientras que el método SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) se empleó para favorecer la interpretabilidad del modelo\. La estrategia de supervisión se evaluó mediante la comparación de indicadores de desempeño del proceso con y sin acciones de control tolerante a fallos\. El modelo alcanzó una exactitud de clasificación global del 98,6 %\. Para una ventana temporal de 20 muestras, la exactitud reportada fue del 98,7 %, con un tiempo de detección de 5,2 s\. Bajo las condiciones simuladas, la incorporación de la supervisión tolerante a fallos se asoció con una reducción de la integral del error absoluto \(IAE\), de 46,8 a 19,7; del sobreimpulso, del 11,3 % al 4,8 %; y del tiempo de establecimiento, de 95 a 61 s\. Estos resultados indican el potencial de integrar la clasificación de fallos basada en redes neuronales, la inteligencia artificial explicable y las acciones correctivas de supervisión para mejorar la respuesta del proceso en las condiciones evaluadas\. Sin embargo, el estudio se basa en datos sintéticos y en un modelo térmico simplificado, y no se realizó una validación experimental en una instalación física o industrial\. La capacidad de generalización de la arquitectura a diferentes condiciones operativas, así como los efectos de los errores de clasificación sobre las acciones correctivas y la seguridad operacional, requieren investigaciones adicionales\. Por tanto, el marco propuesto constituye una alternativa potencial para el diagnóstico de fallos y la supervisión de procesos térmicos, aunque su fiabilidad y eficacia en entornos industriales reales aún deben demostrarse\.

## [Structure\-activity relationship of Cu\(II\) and Pd\(II\) thiosemicarbazone complexes with anticancer and antibacterial properties](../publications/a15c096ca9fa0dc47012.md)

Bartłomiej Rogalewicz; Magdalena Iwan; Marcin Świa̧tkowski; Mariola Michalczuk; Joanna Kubik; Ewelina Humeniuk; Agnieszka Korga\-Plewko; Monika Pitucha; Tomasz Boruta; Tomasz Sierański; Jakub Kubicki; Sylwia Ścieszka; Edyta Kordialik‐Bogacka; Agnieszka Czylkowska

Twelve thiosemicarbazones and 24 corresponding Cu\(II\) and Pd\(II\) complexes were synthesised and evaluated for their physicochemical properties and biological activities\. Single\-crystal X\-ray diffraction and mass spectrometry confirmed ligand deprotonation and the formation of neutral ML2\-type complexes\. Several complexes containing 3,4\-dimethoxybenzylidene\- or 4\-bromobenzylidene\-substituted ligands exhibited submicromolar cytotoxicity against melanoma cells\. Cu\(b\-TSC\)2 and Pd\(dm\-TSC\-pCl\)2 were selected for mechanistic studies and induced cell\-cycle arrest, pro\-apoptotic gene activation, DNA damage, and apoptosis\. Notably, Cu\(b\-TSC\)2 retained activity against vemurafenib\-resistant SK\-MEL\-28 and A\-375 cells\. Structure\-activity analysis showed that additional chlorine substitution generally reduced anticancer activity\. Calculated physicochemical descriptors suggested that increased chlorination enhanced lipophilicity and reduced hydrophilicity, which was associated with lower apparent solution stability\. These findings highlight the importance of balancing lipophilicity, hydrophilicity, and solution stability in future design of potential drugs based on thiosemicarbazones\. In contrast, antibacterial activity was more strain\-dependent, with MIC values against E\. coli as low as 3\.125 mg/L\.

## [Stance, Legitimation, and Digital Authority on LinkedIn: A Corpus\-Informed Critical Discourse Analysis of Bill Gates&\#x27; Posts](../publications/a165faed8b9405a02973.md)

Abdulhameed Abdulhadi Alhuwaydi

This paper studies how Bill Gates’ LinkedIn posts enact digital authority and legitimate global development intervention through stance, quantification, progress\-talk, and solution\-oriented agency\. The corpus includes 14 fact\-checked English\-language LinkedIn posts published by Bill Gates between 23 September 2025 and 7 June 2026\. Corpus\-informed critical discourse analysis employed reproducible Python\-generated token counts alongside post\-level thematic and legitimation coding\. The total corpus size was 1,222 words \(M = 87\.3 words/post; range = 24\-199\)\. Posts related to global health or child survival were most frequent at eight posts \(57\.1%\)\. First\-person singular self\-mentions and collective references each appeared in nine posts\. Predictive appeared 18 times across the corpus Quantification/evidentialization appeared in nine posts, solution/intervention language appeared in 11 posts, and agency assigned to institutions or experts appeared in 10 posts\. Close reading revealed a common pattern of legitimation through stances which move from problem definition, to evi\-dence and social alliances, towards solution\-carrying organizations, programs/companies, researchers, or technologies\. This pattern diffuses moral responsibility while centralizing the capacity for action\. Results suggest executive discourse on LinkedIn blends personal judgments, quantified endorsements of urgency, collective solidarity, and futurological expertise to frame institutions and their solutions as natural\. Both the community\-centered transportation response of the m\-mama post and explicit mentions of equity in captions about AI nevertheless caution against reading these captions as purely techno\-solutionist Keywords: LinkedIn, corpus\-informed discourse analysis, critical discourse analysis, stance, legitimation, digital authority, BillGates

## [Exploring AI Literacy Self\-Efficacy among Pre\-Service EFL Teachers: A Case Study in the Vietnamese Context](../publications/a170a01175cbb88146ea.md)

Thi Thai Ha Pham; Thi Xuan Lien Cao

This case study aims to explore Vietnamese pre\-service EFL teachers&\#x27; awareness of AI literacy, their AI self\-efficacy, and developmental needs\. Using an explanatory mixed\-methods approach, data were collected through a questionnaire administered to 85 pre\-service EFL teachers and follow\-up interviews with 08 of them at a public university offering initial teacher education in central Vietnam\. The findings show that these pre\-service teachers were generally familiar with the concept of AI literacy, well\-aware of its role in EFL instruction, and strongly supported the inclusion of formal AI literacy training in teacher education programs\. In addition, they perceived self\-efficacy of AI literacy to be moderate, particularly in dimensions such as a human\-centered mindset and AI application\. However, these pre\-service teachers still needed more structured, practice\-oriented support to develop their AI competence, with a preferred mode of blended training\. These findings can provide insights into pre\-service teachers’ perceptions of their self\-efficacy in AI\-assisted language education and inform the design and delivery of targeted AI literacy training for teacher education programs\.

## [An Analytical Study of a Governed Lakehouse Framework in Multi\-State Medicare Claims and Provider Data for Fraud, Waste, and Abuse Detection](../publications/a17361279154182990d4.md)

Chandra Obul Reddy Nagi Reddy

Medicare fraud detection, waste, and abuse is hampered by the high volume of claims, highly fragmented data\-analysis systems, limited visibility into data quality, and significant class imbalance\. This study assessed the potential of an Original Medicare Part B \(OMB\) Bronze\-Silver\-Gold lakehouse to improve data quality, traceability, analytical efficiency, and provider\-level risk identification across OMB\-covered populations in California, New York, Florida, Texas, and Pennsylvania in 2024\. Using Apache Spark/PySpark with Delta\-format tables, the study sampled 1,500,000 provider\-service records in proportion to state Traditional Medicare enrollment, representing 214,873 unique NPIs, consolidated them with CMS provider files and HHS\-OIG provider\-exclusion data, interpreted 30 features, and used four models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Isolation Forest\. During Silver\-layer screening, 27,362 records \(1\.82%\) triggered one or more quality rules and were quarantined; NPI enrichment had 99\.7% compliance, and Gold\-layer data quality had 99\.2% compliance\. This reduced query time from a median of 18\.4 seconds to 5\.7 seconds \(approximately 69%\)\. XGBoost performed best among the supervised models, with ROC\-AUC = 0\.91, PR\-AUC = 0\.34, and F1 = 0\.66\. State elevated/high\-risk flags were not confirmed as fraud; they were a priority for investigation and ranged from 2\.2%–3\.4% of unique providers within each state\. Manually managed, repeatable pipelines provide defensible Medicare FWA prioritization, and repeatable, source\-to\-feature, auditable pipelines can support multi\-state, analytic workflows where needed\. Areas to explore include longitudinal claims, Part D, DMEPOS, enforcement outcomes, graph analytics, and prospective investigator validation\.

## [RECENT ADVANCES IN TRANSDERMAL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS: SKIN BARRIER, PERMEATION ENHANCEMENT STRATEGIES, NANOCARRIER\-BASED APPROACHES, AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES](../publications/a176279f96626962713c.md)



Transdermal drug delivery systems \(TDDS\) have emerged as an effective alternative to conventional drug administration by providing sustained drug release, improved patient compliance, avoidance of first\-pass metabolism, and reduced gastrointestinal adverse effects\.However, the highly organized structure of the stratum corneum remains the principal barrier limiting transdermal permeation\.Recent advances in pharmaceutical technology have significantly expanded the scope of TDDS through the development of chemical permeation enhancers, physical enhancement techniques, nanocarrier\-based formulations, and microneedle\-assisted delivery systems\.Liposomes, transfersomes, ethosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, polymeric nanoparticles, and nanoemulsions have demonstrated considerable potential in improving drug permeation, stability, and controlled release\.Emerging technologies, including iontophoresis, sonophoresis, electroporation, and dissolving microneedles, further facilitate the delivery of macromolecules such as peptides, proteins, vaccines, and nucleic acids\.Additionally, smart wearable transdermal patches integrated with biosensors are opening new opportunities for personalized and precision medicine\.This review summarizes recent advances in skin physiology relevant to transdermal delivery, mechanisms of drug permeation, formulation strategies, permeation enhancement techniques, nanocarrier\-based systems, therapeutic applications, commercially available products, current challenges, and future perspectives\.Collectively, these innovations are transforming TDDS into a versatile platform capable of delivering both conventional therapeutics and biologics with improved efficacy, safety, and patient acceptance\.

## [THE EL\-RAKHAWI FLUIDIC CAUSAL INTELLIGENCE ARCHITECTURE \(FCIA\): IN\-VIVO MICROFLUIDIC RESERVOIR COMPUTING VIA CHAOTIC ADVECTION AND REACTION\-DIFFUSION DYNAMICS](../publications/a17d9cf027fead041037.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Fluidic Causal Intelligence Architecture \(FCIA\) shifts computing from solid\-state electronics to liquid\-state computing in biological environments\. It utilizes microfluidic networks for continuous\-time causal inference with zero external electrical power\. Harnessing Lagrangian chaotic advection via 3D spatial modulation and biocompatible reaction\-diffusion dynamics using enzymatic cascades or DNA strand displacement, the system acts as a physical reservoir computer\. It processes temporal biological signals to autonomously actuate therapeutic responses\. Engineered with ultra\-low hydraulic resistance to prevent hemolysis, it operates on ambient biological energy\. The algorithm minimizes the El\-Rakhawi Fluidic Causal Loss, enforcing Advection\-Diffusion\-Reaction dynamics\. Performance is quantified by the El\-Rakhawi Fluidic Computational Efficiency Metric in bits per Joule\. This enables biocompatible, battery\-less smart implants and environmental nodes, bridging AI, fluid physics, chemistry, and neuroscience\.

## [Digital Transformation, Cost\-to\-Income Ratio, and Profitability of Digital Banks in Indonesia](../publications/a191f02dba3e53eabb1a.md)

Raden Achmad Rendy Ashari Mulyadi; Siti Jahroh; Heny Kuswanti Suwarsinah

Background: Digital banking has expanded rapidly in Indonesia, yet growth in assets and transaction activity has not consistently translated into stronger profitability\. This tension raises the question of whether the transition to a digital operating model and the accompanying cost structure are associated with short\-term financial performance\. Objective: This study examines the relationship between post\-digital\-transformation status and bank profitability and separately evaluates the association between the Cost\-to\-Income Ratio \(CIR\) and Return on Assets \(ROA\)\. Method: The analysis uses an unbalanced panel comprising 79 valid bank\-period observations drawn from quarterly reports of 10 Indonesian digital banks over 2019–2024\. Panel\-model selection relied on the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests, followed by diagnostic assessment and hypothesis testing\. Results: Post\-transformation status is negatively associated with ROA \(B = \-13\.9108; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. CIR also shows a negative association with ROA \(B = \-0\.0525; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The estimates indicate that profitability remained under pressure during the observed transition period and that a heavier operating\-cost burden corresponded with weaker asset returns\. Conclusion: For the banks and periods observed, both digital\-transformation status and higher CIR are associated with lower ROA\. The findings highlight the importance of operating efficiency during digital transition, while the transformation coefficient should be interpreted as a short\-term empirical association rather than evidence of a permanent causal effect\.

## [Regional and Gender Disparities in Higher Education in Nepal: A Quantitative Case Study](../publications/a195d328ff61b2c44f17.md)

Prem Kumar Nayak; Suresh Kumar Sahani

National enrollment figures can conceal inequalities across regions, academic levels, and fields of study\. This quantitative case study examined regional and gender disparities in Nepal’s higher education system using 2023/24 data from the University Grants Commission’s Education Management Information System\. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze enrollment, campus distribution, and financing by province, ecological belt, gender, academic level, faculty, and campus type\. Women constituted 56\.58% of 633,053 students, with a national gender parity index of 1\.3 and a higher gross enrollment ratio than men \(24\.6% versus 17\.8%\)\. However, female representation decreased across academic levels, from 57\.6% at the bachelor’s level to 48\.7% at the master’s level, 22\.4% at the MPhil level, and 17\.7% at the PhD level\. Women accounted for 24\.4% of engineering enrollment and 14\.5% of Sanskrit enrollment, compared with over 70% in education\. Regional concentration was pronounced: Bagmati Province accounted for 44\.04% of enrollment and 43\.58% of campuses, compared with 4\.01% and 4\.05%, respectively, in Karnali Province\. The Hill, Tarai, and Mountain belts accounted for 55\.47%, 41\.96%, and 2\.56% of enrollment, respectively, while Tribhuvan University enrolled 77\.61% of students nationally\. Supplementary evidence from independent studies indicated that Dalit communities, comprising over 13% of the population, have historically experienced participation and completion rates substantially below national averages\. The findings indicate that women’s numerical predominance nationally coexists with vertical and horizontal gender segregation and substantial geographic concentration\. They provide an empirical basis for targeted resource allocation, expanded quota and scholarship mechanisms, and more disaggregated data systems to inform equity\-oriented policy within Nepal’s federal higher education system\.

## [Determinação da Vulnerabilidade Ambiental à Erosão na Bacia do Reservatório de Santana no Estado do Rio de Janeiro](../publications/a197af56baa8593dbffa.md)

Manuel Galdino da Costa Júnior; Madson Tavares Silva; Ênio Pereira de Souza; Ingrid Paloma Carneiro de Lima; Maurício Nogueira Frota; Gutemberg Borges França; Thaís Regina Benevides Trigueiro Aranha

As dimensões da vulnerabilidade ambiental constituem tipologias de informação decisivas para o ordenamento territorial\. Nesse contexto, a análise dos índices de erodibilidade torna\-se determinante para compreender a dinâmica de sedimentação\. Esse estudo busca quantificar a vulnerabilidade à erosão na Bacia Hidrográfica do Reservatório de Santana \(BHRS\) no estado do Rio de Janeiro, bem como identificar regiões de maior vulnerabilidade à produção de sedimentos e fornecer o Índice de Vulnerabilidade à Erosão \(IVE\)\. Para isso, utilizaram\-se os parâmetros da Equação Universal de Perda de Solo \(USLE\): erosividade das chuvas, erodibilidade dos solos, fator topográfico, cobertura vegetal e práticas conservacionistas\. O método consistiu na atribuição inicial de valores de vulnerabilidade a cada parâmetro individual\. Posteriormente, a sobreposição espacial e o cálculo da média aritmética dessas variáveis resultaram no mapeamento do IVE global da área analisada\. O mapeamento do IVE indicou que mais de 56% do território da BHRS encontra\-se sob maior vulnerabilidade erosiva, enquanto aproximadamente 43% da área apresenta maior estabilidade frente aos processos de degradação, sendo identificados trechos de maior instabilidade na bacia, resultados da interação entre alta erosividade, solos com elevado teor de silte, alta amplitude altimétrica e cobertura vegetal deficitária\. Desta forma, ficou clara a vulnerabilidade à erosão da BHRS, constatando que a espacialização desses dados fornece subsídios indispensáveis para o ordenamento territorial, orientando ações para mitigar o aporte de sedimentos no Reservatório de Santana\.

## [Unveiling the Potential of Quaternary Heusler Alloys for Spintronic and Thermoelectric Applications: A Valence Electron Count Perspective](../publications/a198e18e74743027744f.md)

Shahana K C; Shuvankar Gupta; Mantu Modak; Chandan Mazumdar; Santanu Pakhira

crystal architecture provides exceptional compositional flexibility, enabling systematic control of electronic band filling, magnetic exchange interactions, and spin polarization\. This tunability gives rise to a wide range of functional states, including half\-metallicity, spin\-gapless semiconductivity, bipolar magnetic semiconductivity, spin semimetallicity, compensated ferrimagnetism, and topological electronic phases\. Among the descriptors governing these properties, the valence electron count \(VEC\) has proven particularly powerful, providing a predictive framework through the Slater\-Pauling rule for correlating composition with magnetic and electronic behavior\. In this Review, we comprehensively survey experimentally reported quaternary Heusler alloys and systematically classify them according to their VEC\. We first discuss their crystal chemistry, atomic ordering, and disorder mechanisms, highlighting their influence on physical properties\. We then establish clear correlations between VEC and magnetic ground states, electronic structure, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric performance, identifying overarching trends and unifying structure\-property relationships across diverse compositional families\. By integrating insights from structural, magnetic, electronic, and transport studies, this Review provides a coherent framework for understanding quaternary Heusler alloys and offers design principles for discovering next\-generation materials for spintronic, thermoelectric, and energy\-efficient electronic technologies\.

## [WEARABLE BIOSENSORS IN REMOTE CHRONIC DISEASE MONITORING: A STRUCTURED REVIEW OF IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS AND HEALTH EQUITY IMPLICATIONS](../publications/a1a20193019e2d922c86.md)

Jakub Juskowiak; Zuzanna Julia Komin; Maryan Liasota; Eliza Zofia Kabat; Michalina Justyna Kozłowska; Krzysztof Konopka; Maciej Kamil Majchrzak; Faustyna Magdalena Kołodziej; Alicja Kwiatkowska; Mateusz Lis

Background Clinical\-grade wearable biosensors offer significant potential for tracking chronic diseases outside the hospital\. However, while the hardware itself is highly accurate, the medical field still struggles with the logistical reality of deploying these tools\. The structural barriers preventing widespread clinical use, and the ways these hurdles impact overall health equity, lack rigorous synthesis in the current literature\. Objective Moving beyond pure hardware accuracy, this analysis maps the practical realities of continuous patient surveillance\. It specifically investigates the institutional workflow bottlenecks, hardware usability hurdles, and underlying economic disparities that dictate how monitoring programs actually function for populations managing heart failure, diabetes, or COPD\. Methodology Peer\-reviewed literature spanning 2018 to 2026 was extracted from PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar\. The inclusion criteria deliberately filtered out purely technical validation studies\. Instead, the analysis targeted data documenting the logistical friction, long\-term adherence failures, and unequal access surrounding continuous glucose monitors, ambulatory cardiac patches, and multi\-parameter tracking devices\. Results The synthesized data show that severe workflow friction and poor electronic health record interoperability actively block hospital networks from scaling these programs\. On the patient side, a distinct &quot;compliance paradox&quot; emerges\. High initial motivation frequently collapses into device abandonment, usually triggered by physical skin irritation, convoluted software interfaces, and low technical literacy\. The literature also exposes a severe digital divide\. A patient&\#x27;s income bracket, geographic location, and advanced age strictly gatekeep their ability to access continuous medical monitoring\. Conclusion Healthcare networks cannot rely solely on precise hardware to improve chronic disease management\. Deploying continuous monitors successfully requires a fundamental shift toward repairing broken clinical workflows and addressing systemic exclusion\. Without structural interventions targeting financial and technical accessibility, digital health initiatives will simply reinforce existing medical inequalities\.

## [Formulation and Evaluation of Nanocrystals for improvement dissolution and oral absorption of poorly aqueous soluble drugs](../publications/a1a297ecb2e28b2627d1.md)



Nanocrystal formulation key elements of consideration; stabilizers; the importance of key processing parameters will be outlined\.The physicochemical characteristics of nanoparticles \(e\.g\., size and polydispersity index \(PDI\), Zeta potential \(ZP\), morphology, crystalline structure, drug release profiles, and stability\) and their absorption and lymph uptake mechanism in the gastrointestinal \(GI\) tract are tabulated in Table1\.About 40\-70% of new drug candidates exhibit poor solubility in aqueous media, resulting in slow dissolution and absorption from the GI tract and lower bioavailability; thus, nanocrystal technology provides a solution to this problem\.Thus, it can be concluded that pharmaceutical nanocrystals are an interesting technology that has many applications and has shown success in the clinic to achieve successful delivery of water\-insoluble drug substances\.The review elaborates scientific principles behind nanocrystal technology, including size reduction, surface energy, dissolution kinetics, and formation of nanocrystals by top\-down approach \(milling and grinding\), bottom\-up approach \(precipitation, anti\-solvent crystallization, and emulsion\-based methods\), and hybrid or combination approach \(Smart Crystal\)\.Nanocrystal formulation considerations, importance of stabilizers, and critical processing parameters are discussed in brief, and the applicability of Quality by Design \(QbD\) to develop robust and reproducible nanocrystal formulation\.Physicochemical characterization of nanocrystals, like Particle size \(PS\) and polydispersity index, ZP, morphology, crystalline state, dissolution performance, and stability, as well as mechanisms of absorption and lymphatic uptake from the GI tract, are summarized\.Commercial examples, recent advances in oral nanocrystal dosage forms, scale\-up and manufacturing challenges, regulatory issues, and new approaches in nanocrystal drug delivery systems are reviewed\.In conclusion, pharmaceutical nanocrystals are an attractive drug delivery technology with broad applicability and clinical success in achieving successful delivery of water\-insoluble drug substances\.

## [Stretching the Sociological Imagination: An Inquiry into Sociology&\#x27;s Theory of Change](../publications/a1a729c07cecc6ad322f.md)

Jenell Williams Paris

This article explores the theory of change embedded within introductory sociology textbooks, arguing that the discipline’s pedagogical focus truncates the sociological imagination\. While textbooks exhaustively critique bureaucracies as alienating, they disproportionately idealize social movements as the primary mechanism for progressive social transformation\. Drawing on Carl Jung’s The Undiscovered Self and Christian sociological frameworks, the author contends this emphasis over\-socializes individuals into collective &quot;mass man&quot; thinking that fosters eventual disillusionment\. Expanding the sociological imagination requires recovering a robust understanding of institutional and bureaucratic reform, alongside cultivating the inner life and moral agency of the self\-reflective individual\.

## [Implementation of robotic process automation in small and medium\-sized enterprises](../publications/a1a8798697a11ab9f1af.md)

David Cvetko

Magistrska naloga se osredotoča na raziskovanje možnosti za izvajanje robotske avtomatizacije procesov, znane tudi kot RPA, v malih in srednjih podjetjih\. Posebno pozornost namenja analizi stroškov ter oceni njihovih učinkov\. Majhna in srednja podjetja se pri digitalni transformaciji pogosto srečujejo z omejenimi finančnimi, človeškimi in tehnološkimi viri\. Zato je ključno, da so odločitve o uvajanju novih digitalnih rešitev dobro premišljene\. RPA je ena izmed možnosti za avtomatizacijo ponavljajočih se, dobro strukturiranih in digitalno podprtih poslovnih procesov\. Vendar pa njena implementacija ni primerna za vsak postopek, oziroma proces\. Namen magistrskega dela je proučiti, pod kakšnimi pogoji je uvedba RPA v malih in srednjih podjetjih smiselna, kateri procesi so najprimernejši za avtomatizacijo ter kakšne stroške in učinke lahko podjetje pri tem pričakuje\. V teoretičnem delu so predstavljene osnove digitalne transformacije, poslovnih procesov, optimizacije ter avtomatizacije procesov z uporabo RPA\. V nadaljevanju je predstavljen model za ocenjevanje primernosti avtomatizacije procesov\. Ta model upošteva različne kriterije, kot so ponovljivost procesov, količina ročnega dela, stopnja standardizacije, dostopnost podatkov v digitalni obliki, delež izjem, stabilnost postopka ter možnosti za prihranek časa\. V analitičnem delu je obravnavan proces prenašanja naročil iz e\-pošte v ERP sistem kot modelni primer\. Opravljena je bila primerjava med obstoječim stanjem procesa in predlaganim izboljšanjem po uvajanju RPA\. Izdelava modelne analize nakazuje, da bi lahko uvedba RPA v realističnem okolju zmanjšala mesečno delovno obremenitev procesa za približno 57 %, hkrati pa bi se število napak reduciralo za okoli 50 %\. Ob upoštevanju predvidenih stroškov za uvedbo, licence in vzdrževanje se začetna naložba povrne v približno desetih mesecih\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da ima RPA \(robotizirana avtomatizacija procesov\) v malih in srednjih podjetjih velik potencial, a le pri skrbno izbranih procesih\. Uvedba je najbolj smiselna pri procesih, ki se ponavljajo, sledijo standardom, so digitalno podprti in so dovolj obsežni\. Magistrsko delo prispeva k bolj sistematičnemu odločanju malih in srednjih podjetij glede uvedbe RPA ter predstavlja model, ki ga je mogoče uporabiti kot izhodišče za oceno stroškov in učinkov avtomatizacije\.

## [Gerakan Santri Melek Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) Untuk Pembelajaran Islam Kreatif](../publications/a1ac6085b8ed495b8d98.md)

M\. Hadi Sutiyo

Perkembangan teknologi Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) telah membawa perubahan besar dalam dunia pendidikan, termasuk pada pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam di lingkungan pesantren\. Namun, pemanfaatan AI di kalangan santri masih menghadapi berbagai tantangan, seperti rendahnya literasi digital, keterbatasan pemahaman penggunaan teknologi secara produktif, serta kurangnya pendampingan dalam memanfaatkan AI untuk kegiatan pembelajaran yang kreatif dan edukatif\. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan pemahaman dan keterampilan santri dalam memanfaatkan Artificial Intelligence sebagai media pendukung pembelajaran Islam kreatif, inovatif, dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan zaman\. Metode pelaksanaan kegiatan dilakukan melalui pendekatan pelatihan, pendampingan, praktik langsung, dan evaluasi pemanfaatan aplikasi AI dalam pembelajaran\. Materi yang diberikan meliputi pengenalan konsep AI, etika penggunaan AI dalam perspektif Islam, pemanfaatan AI untuk pembuatan media pembelajaran, penulisan materi dakwah, pengembangan konten edukasi Islami, serta strategi penggunaan AI secara bijak dan bertanggung jawab\. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan pemahaman santri terhadap teknologi AI serta tumbuhnya kreativitas dalam menghasilkan media pembelajaran Islam berbasis digital\. Selain itu, kegiatan ini juga mampu meningkatkan kesadaran santri mengenai pentingnya etika digital, literasi teknologi, dan sikap kritis dalam menghadapi perkembangan kecerdasan buatan\. Dengan demikian, gerakan santri melek AI diharapkan dapat menjadi langkah strategis dalam menciptakan generasi santri yang religius, adaptif, kreatif, dan mampu bersaing di era transformasi digital tanpa meninggalkan nilai\-nilai keislaman\.
