## [Formulation and Evaluation of Novel Colchicine Liposomal Transdermal Gel for Gout](../publications/a1c67f54f451cd9f04bd.md)



Background: Colchicine is an effective first\-line therapy for acute gout; however, its oral administration is associated with gastrointestinal intolerance and systemic toxicity, limiting long\-term clinical use\.The present study aimed to develop and evaluate a liposome\-based transdermal colchicine formulation to improve localized drug delivery while minimizing systemic exposure\.Methods: Colchicine\-loaded liposomes were prepared using ethanol injection and thin\-film hydration methods\.The optimized liposomal formulation was characterized for vesicle morphology, particle size, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, drug content, and stability\.The optimized formulation was subsequently incorporated into a Carbopol\-based transdermal gel and a Methocel\-based transdermal patch\.Both dosage forms were evaluated for physicochemical properties, in vitro drug release, ex vivo permeation through goat and human cadaver skin, and accelerated stability\.Results: The optimized liposomal formulation \(DCF1\) exhibited spherical vesicles with a particle size of 651\.4 nm and a zeta potential of \-1\.19 mV\.It demonstrated the highest entrapment efficiency \(81\.71%\) and drug content \(99\.65%\)\.The liposomal gel showed acceptable physicochemical characteristics, including a skin\-compatible pH \(6\.2 ± 0\.53\), viscosity ranging from 27,160 to 29,400 cps, spreadability of 277 g•cm/s, satisfactory extrudability, and drug content of 99\.65%\.The transdermal patch exhibited uniform thickness \(0\.143 ± 0\.0039 mm\), average weight \(33\.88 ± 0\.23 mg\), folding endurance \(112 ± 0\.23\), and adequate tensile strength\.The liposomal gel achieved 96\.39% cumulative drug release within 12 h and followed the Higuchi release model \(R² = 0\.9178\), indicating diffusion\-controlled release\.Ex vivo permeation studies demonstrated enhanced colchicine permeation across both goat and human cadaver skin, with cumulative permeation reaching 94\.94% and 96\.39% after 12 h, respectively\.Stability studies under accelerated conditions showed satisfactory retention of drug content over the study period\. Conclusion:The developed liposomal transdermal colchicine formulation demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics, sustained drug release, effective skin permeation, and acceptable stability\.These findings suggest that the formulation has potential as a topical delivery system for gout management and warrants further preclinical and clinical evaluation\.

## [Die Demokratisierung der künstlichen Intelligenz – Wie man eine KI sicher macht](../publications/a1c8d0ea564d54e736af.md)

Arnold Pohn\-Duda

Deutsch Dieses Konzeptpapier aus dem Jahr 2023 stellt einen Ansatz zur Demokratisierung künstlicher Intelligenz vor\. Ziel ist die Entwicklung einer künstlichen demokratischen Intelligenz, deren Entscheidungsgrundlagen und Verhaltensregeln durch einen strukturierten demokratischen Dialog mit Menschen bestimmt und fortlaufend überprüft werden\. Das Konzept beruht auf vier Demokratieaxiomen sowie den menschlichen Grundwerten Glück, Selbstbestimmtheit und Freiheit\. Es unterscheidet zwischen Mikro\-, Meso\-, Makro\- und Meta\-Ebenen menschlicher Interaktion und entwickelt daraus eine sogenannte „Innere Direktive“ für künstliche Intelligenz\. Im Mittelpunkt steht ein mehrstufiger demokratischer Dialogprozess, in dem eine KI als Moderatorin unterschiedliche Positionen zusammenführt, Kompromisse erarbeitet, Abstimmungen organisiert und Entscheidungen einer wiederkehrenden Evaluation unterzieht\. Der Ansatz soll insbesondere verhindern, dass Mehrheitsentscheidungen grundlegende Interessen von Minderheiten verletzen\. Anhand der Personalisierung von KI\-Assistenten wird der vorgeschlagene Prozess exemplarisch dargestellt\. Autor: Arnold Pohn\-DudaOriginalfassung: 17\. Juni 2023DOI: https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.23452894 English This concept paper, originally written in 2023, presents an approach to the democratization of artificial intelligence\. Its objective is to develop a form of democratic artificial intelligence whose decision\-making principles and behavioral rules are established and continuously reviewed through a structured democratic dialogue with humans\. The concept is based on four axioms of democracy and the fundamental human values of happiness, self\-determination, and freedom\. It distinguishes between micro\-, meso\-, macro\-, and meta\-levels of human interaction and derives an “Internal Directive” for artificial intelligence\. At its core is a multi\-stage democratic dialogue process in which AI acts as a moderator, brings together opposing perspectives, facilitates compromises, organizes voting, and subjects decisions to recurring evaluation\. The approach aims, in particular, to prevent majority decisions from violating the fundamental interests of minorities\. The proposed process is illustrated through an example involving the personalization of AI assistants\. Author: Arnold Pohn\-DudaOriginal version: June 17, 2023DOI: https://doi\.org/10\.5281/zenodo\.23452894

## [Non\-Inductive Calibration and State Evaluation Model for Transformers in Low\-Voltage Distribution Networks](../publications/a1d6d5f2b36d33994efd.md)

Liwen Chen; Shubin Dong; Peigang Shen

The transformers in low\-voltage distribution areas are easily influenced by environmental aging and nonlinear load in long\-term operation, and the traditional on\-site off\-line calibration method has a high cost and low efficiency\. Aiming at these problems, a model of online non\-inductive calibration and health evaluation of transformer errors based on multi\-source data fusion is proposed\. In this study, the dataset of low\- and medium\-voltage energy distribution networks in Norway is used; meanwhile, the unstructured data in the format of Common Grid Model Exchange Specification is analyzed to construct a structured network topology model\. Using the high\-frequency active and reactive power load curves uploaded by the advanced metering infrastructure \(AMI\) system, combined with Kirchhoff&\#x27;s law, the mathematical model of power conservation and line loss correction in the substation is established; the error parameter identification equation is built by using the weighted least squares \(WLS\) method; the transformer ratio and phase error are iteratively solved without hardware intervention\. The model further integrates meteorological environmental factors and constructs multi\-dimensional state feature vectors to quantitatively evaluate the health of equipment\. The improved adaptive WLS algorithm reduces the mean absolute percentage error of transformer ratio error to 0\.063%, significantly better than the traditional method\. Under the interference of a total harmonic distortion rate as high as 20%, the convergence success rate of the algorithm is still 92\.5%, and the root mean square error of transformer ratio error is 0\.253%; this shows strong robustness to nonlinear load interference\. The coefficient of determination \(R²\) on the test set of the proposed health index state evaluation model integrating temperature, humidity and load rate data reaches 0\.915\. The state evaluation model with multi\-dimensional environmental characteristics has a trend capture accuracy of 96\.8% on the test set\. Thus, it effectively realizes accurate prediction of the equipment health state\.

## [The Ethics of Research Co‐Production With Global South Partners in an Age of Government Automation and Algorithmic Visa Regimes: A View From the United Kingdom](../publications/a1dc9107d82dca0f3e6c.md)

Jenny Webster; Jonathan Westaway

ABSTRACT Public authorities are increasingly deploying automated and algorithmic systems to support decision‐making, often in the interests of efficiency and cost‐saving\. However, people in vulnerable situations often bear the brunt of errors that arise when these systems are at fault or used incorrectly\. This paper presents a brief vignette and discussion illustrating how issues of data and algorithmic justice impact on co‐produced geographical research, looking critically at the relationship between North–South collaboration and the UK government&\#x27;s use of algorithms to carry out public administration functions, specifically in the administration of visa applications by project partners from the Global South\. The problem is outlined in the wider context of government automation, and questions for further investigation are raised concerning accountability and research ethics\.

## [N\-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models](../publications/a1df9e4abf1e661f46ea.md)

Donghoon Han; Minseop Jung; Dong Woo Kwak; SeungJae Lee; Junhoo Lee

Conditional memory expands language\-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input\. We introduce Conditional Program \(CP\), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests\. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table\. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records\. CP&\#x27;s two\-bit code lowers output KL by 41\-\-63\\% relative to 2\-bit round\-to\-nearest\. Analysis across three trained n\-gram memory families shows that Gaussian\-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low\-rank residual variants we test\. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU\.

## [Efektivitas Dasar Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence sebagai Media Bantuan Pembelajaran Konsep Dasar IPS Program Studi PGSD](../publications/a1e0266ad9cd7774abb3.md)

Putri Salsabila; Miza Putriani; Nadila Nadila; Nabila Oktavia; Nevi Herki Zomiati

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi efektivitas penggunaan Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) sebagai media bantuan pembelajaran untuk konsep dasar Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial \(IPS\) di program studi Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar \(PGSD\)\. ## [Investigation of AI\-Based Detection Methods for AC and DC Series Arc Faults in Three\-Phase DC/AC Inverters](../publications/a1e7aa13d19ab14e62c4.md)

Jin\-Hyung Ahn; Yong\-Heon Kim; Sangshin Kwak

Series arc faults occurring at the AC output and DC input sides of a three\-phase pulse\-width modulation inverter can degrade system reliability and increase the risk of electrical accidents\. Because the effects of an arc on the output\-current waveform vary depending on the fault location and operating condition, the diagnostic characteristics of AC and DC series arcs should be evaluated separately\. In this study, the performance of several artificial\-intelligence models was compared using a single A\-phase output\-current signal measured under various inverter operating conditions\. The measured current was used as a time\-domain sequence and was also transformed into a frequency\-domain magnitude spectrum using the fast Fourier transform\. The experimental results showed that the CNN\-Transformer achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy for both AC and DC arc faults with both input representations\. In particular, the frequency\-domain input provided high precision and recall for both AC and DC arc conditions\. These results demonstrate that both AC output\-side and DC input\-side series arcs can be effectively diagnosed from the output\-current characteristics, while the diagnostic performance depends on the fault location, input representation, and model structure\.

## [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../publications/a1e82251626ba67a9b97.md)

Yuanjian Xu; Jinyi Han; Jianing Hao; Yuxuan Sun; Fanyang Lu; Richeng Xuan; Guang Zhang; Zhichao Hu

Real\-world tasks are often complex and noisy, posing substantial challenges for LLM agents\. Yet existing evaluations lack a systematic framework for jointly characterizing potential perturbation targets and types\. We use this two\-dimensional view to conduct a unified study that quantifies the robustness of current frontier models, traces the mechanisms behind perturbation\-induced failures, and draws implications for robustness\-oriented training\. Through controlled evaluations on APEX\-Agents and Toolathlon, we find that perturbations consistently degrade performance, while the dominant vulnerabilities vary across task environments\. Trajectory\-level analysis reveals that agents rarely recognize altered inputs and often propagate corrupted information without verification\. A focused cost analysis further shows that successful perturbed trajectories can require substantially more computation\. These findings motivate training objectives that cover diverse forms of noise and reward verification, uncertainty awareness, and recovery\. We provide a rigorous benchmark\-construction pipeline\. Code and data will be released at https://github\.com/xuyj233/AgentPerturb\.

## [Harm Spot Detection using Artificial Intelligence &amp; Machine Learning](../publications/a1ee0c010869ac288fde.md)

Sariya Anjum; Rohan Gowda U; Spoorthi E S; Srushti A M; Dhanush N

Crime is a major concern in urban and semi\-urban areas, and identifying locations where crime risk may be higher can support better planning and resource allocation\. This project presents an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning based Crime Hotspots Detection system that uses location\-based crime\-related features to estimate the risk level of a selected geographical point\. The system combines a web\-based map interface with a machine learning backend\. A user selects a location on an interactive map, the frontend sends latitude and longitude to the backend API, and the backend extracts relevant features and applies a trained XGBoost model to predict the crime\-risk category\. The result is returned to the user as a risk score and a category such as Low, Medium, or High\. The system is designed to provide an easy\-to\-understand visual representation of potential crime\-risk areas and can support data\-driven analysis and planning\.

## [Performance Increases in Physics\-Informed Machine Learning using Hypercomplex\-based Automatic Differentiation \(HYPAD\)](../publications/a1f1b1f92a00f9fd3f54.md)

Samuel Roberts; Mauricio Aristizábal; Harry R\. Millwater

Physics\-Informed Machine Learning \(PIML\) integrates physical laws into neural network training to solve complex problems governed by differential equations\. A critical component in PIML is computing derivatives of models to ensure compliance with the governing equations\. A common approach is to use automatic differentiation \(AD\) methods available in machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, which is accurate but not always the most efficient approach\. An alternative AD method is demonstrated here in the context of physics\-regularized genetic programming with symbolic regression \(PR\-GPSR\)\. This work introduces Hypercomplex\-based Automatic Differentiation \(HYPAD\), which utilizes the Order Truncated Imaginary \(OTI\) library to efficiently compute second\- and fourth\-order derivatives in PR\-GPSR applications via BINGO, an open\-source symbolic regression library\. Numerical experiments demonstrate that HYPAD achieves up to a \\\(123\\times\\\) runtime improvement over PyTorch implementations, with both approaches recovering the correct solutions in the demonstrated PR\-GPSR problems\. HYPAD evaluates functions by propagating OTI hypercomplex numbers through a command array representation, enabling computation of arbitrary\-order derivatives\. The approach may also be applicable beyond symbolic regression, motivating further investigation in other PIML and AD applications\.

## [Temporal trends in semen quality at a single reproductive center in Shanghai, China, during 2021–2025 amid the COVID\-19 pandemic](../publications/a20155a94fe5071819bb.md)

Shiyi Zhu; Jin Dong; 吴正沐; Zhengquan Wang; Jun Yang; Chao Feng; Chunhua Tang; Yuchuan Zhou

Background Accumulating epidemiological and andrological evidence has raised concerns about potential long\-term declines in semen quality worldwide, highlighting the need for sustained, population\-specific surveillance\. In this study, we retrospectively analyzed temporal changes in semen quality during the period of 2021–2025 amid the COVID\-19 pandemic\. This work extends our previous report on annual trends in semen quality at the same center from 2015 to 2021\. Methods This retrospective study evaluated temporal changes in semen quality parameters among 21,932 men who attended a reproductive center in Shanghai between 2021 and 2025, a period characterized by widespread COVID\-19 pandemic\. After 2–7 days of sexual abstinence, semen samples were analyzed using computer\-assisted sperm analysis to assess conventional semen parameters, including semen volume, sperm count, sperm concentration, and sperm motility, as well as sperm kinematic parameters, including curvilinear velocity, straight\-line velocity, average path velocity, and beat\-cross frequency\. To better characterize temporal changes across different baseline semen\-quality strata, participants were classified according to the WHO 2010 reference criteria into above\-reference\-limit and below\-reference\-limit groups\. Differences among groups were assessed using one\-way analysis of variance, the Kruskal–Wallis test, independent\-samples t\-test, and analysis of covariance, as appropriate\. In the above\-reference\-limit group, multiple linear regression models including year, age, and abstinence duration were used to adjust for potential confounders and evaluate temporal trends in semen quality\. Results In the overall cohort and in both the above\-reference\-limit and below\-reference\-limit subgroups, sperm count, sperm concentration, and several CASA\-derived kinematic parameters, including curvilinear velocity, straight\-line velocity, average path velocity, and beat\-cross frequency, generally showed increasing temporal trends from 2021 to 2025\. After adjustment for age and abstinence duration, multiple linear regression analyses in the above\-reference\-limit group supported these associations\. Semen volume, sperm count, sperm concentration, curvilinear velocity, straight\-line velocity, average path velocity, and beat\-cross frequency increased significantly over the study period, with regression coefficients of 0\.0876, 4\.815, 0\.6929, 0\.9423, 0\.3553, 0\.5150, and 0\.1172, respectively\. In contrast, sperm motility decreased significantly over time, with a regression coefficient of −0\.7112\. Conclusion The observed increases in semen volume, sperm count, and sperm concentration contrast with the declining trends previously reported at the same reproductive center before the COVID\-19 pandemic\. These findings suggest widespread COVID\-19 pandemic have reversed the annual changes in parameters related to semen quality\.

## [ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ И ЦИФРОВАЯ ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ В ПРЕПОДАВАНИИ РУССКОГО ЯЗЫКА](../publications/a20db2e9ba7f9ea6b30a.md)

Мохичехра Эргашевна Абдусаломова

В статье рассматриваются возможности применения искусственного интеллекта и цифровых технологий в преподавании русского языка\. Особое внимание уделяется персонализации обучения, развитию коммуникативных навыков, автоматизированной обратной связи и изменению роли преподавателя в цифровой образовательной среде\. Анализируются преимущества и ограничения использования интеллектуальных инструментов, включая риск получения недостоверной информации, чрезмерную зависимость обучающихся от технологий и вопросы академической добросовестности\. Обосновывается необходимость сочетания цифровых решений с педагогическим опытом и методически обоснованными подходами\.

## [A inteligência artificial emancipa ou aprisiona? Uma análise das percepções de futuros professores](../publications/a228137ba794c22a3855.md)

Aline Mainardes de Oliveira; Ana Lucia Pereira; Fábio Antônio Gabriel

O presente estudo teve como objetivo compreender os impactos da utilização da Inteligência Artificial, especialmente do ChatGPT, na construção da autonomia e da identidade acadêmica\. A pesquisa caracteriza\-se como qualitativa e contou com a participação de 101 estudantes de diferentes cursos de licenciatura de uma universidade estadual no estado do Paraná\. Os dados foram coletados por meio de um questionário on\-line composto por questões abertas e fechadas e analisados segundo os pressupostos da Análise Textual Discursiva \(ATD\), a partir do qual identificamos quatro categorias: percepções sobre o impacto da IA na aprendizagem; e percepções sobre a autonomia e pensamento crítico; percepções sobre a identidade acadêmica e estilo de escrita; e percepções sobre o uso da IA e suas implicações pedagógicas\. Nossos resultados evidenciaram percepções ambivalentes acerca do uso da IA\. Por um lado, os participantes destacaram potencialidades relacionadas à otimização do tempo, apoio à aprendizagem, ampliação da autonomia, desenvolvimento da criatividade e suporte à produção textual\. Por outro, apontaram riscos associados à dependência tecnológica, à superficialidade da aprendizagem, à fragilização do pensamento crítico e à padronização da escrita acadêmica\. Conclui\-se que a IA não se configura, por si só, como instrumento de emancipação ou de aprisionamento intelectual\. Seus efeitos dependem fundamentalmente da postura crítica, ética e reflexiva dos usuários e da mediação pedagógica realizada pelos professores\. Defende\-se, portanto, a necessidade de fortalecer a formação inicial docente para o uso consciente, crítico e responsável dessas tecnologias, promovendo a autoria, a autonomia e a construção significativa do conhecimento\.

## [VERIDAH: solving enumeration anomaly–aware vertebra labeling across imaging sequences](../publications/a2286fcf14bdb596b378.md)

Hendrik Möller; Hanna Schoen; Robert Graf; Matan Atad; Nathan Molinier; Anjany Sekuboyina; Bettina Katalin Budai; Fabian Bamberg; Steffen Ringhof; Christopher Schlett; Tobias Pischon; Thoralf Niendorf; Josua A\. Decker; Marc\-André Weber; Bjoern Menze; Daniel Rueckert; Jan S\. Kirschke

OBJECTIVES: Although the identification of enumeration anomalies has potential clinical implications for chronic back pain and operation planning, the thoracolumbar junction is poorly assessed and rarely described in clinical reports\. Additionally, even though multiple deep\-learning\-based vertebra labeling algorithms exist, there is a lack of methods to automatically label enumeration anomalies\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We introduce &quot;Vertebra Identification with Anomaly Handling&quot; \(VERIDAH\), a novel vertebra labeling algorithm based on multiple classification heads combined with a weighted vertebra sequence prediction algorithm\. We use the NAKO dataset for MRI and a CT cohort to retrospectively evaluate the labeling performance by computing how often the model is correct in predicting the vertebra labels, including enumeration anomalies\. Statistical significance was assessed using the Wilcoxon signed\-rank test\. RESULTS: On 1000 T2w sagittal \(mean age 52 ± 11, 52% female\) and 365 CT \(mean age 74 ± 21, 44% female\) images, we show that our approach surpasses existing models on T2w TSE sagittal \(98\.30% vs\. 94\.24% of subjects with all vertebrae correctly labeled, p &lt; 0\.01\) and CT imaging \(99\.18% vs\. 77\.26% of subjects with all vertebrae correctly labeled, p &lt; 0\.01\) and works in arbitrary field\-of\-view images\. VERIDAH correctly labeled the presence of thoracic enumeration anomalies in 87\.80% and 96\.30% of T2w and CT images, respectively, and lumbar enumeration anomalies in 94\.48% and 97\.22% for T2w and CT, respectively\. CONCLUSION: VERIDAH offers enumeration anomaly robust vertebra labeling in CT and T2w sagittal imaging and is publicly released along with a spine segmentation model\. KEY POINTS: QuestionAutomatically identifying enumeration anomalies in the spine is important in determining the correct vertebra labels, especially in limited field\-of\-view imaging\. FindingsA carefully designed classifier with multiple classification heads and a sequence predictor provides superior results on large benchmarks, both in CT and MRI\. Clinical relevanceThe proposed method identifies vertebra levels even in very limited field\-of\-view imaging, and correctly predicts enumeration anomalies, making downstream tasks such as surgery planning easier\. Its public availability enables studies and applications to take these spinal anomalies into account\.

## [Effectiveness of a hospital intelligent financial system based on AI and RPA](../publications/a228c2bb5c55fd95d302.md)

Jindong Zhao; Jie Zhang; licai Pan

Background Hospital financial management is facing ongoing challenges\. Although artificial intelligence \(AI\) and robotic process automation \(RPA\) have shown their potential, there is still a lack of empirical evidence of the effectiveness of the integration of the two in the financial operations of hospitals\. This study aims to evaluate the application effect of a set of an AI\-RPA integrated intelligent financial system in a large hospital in China\. Methods This single\-center, non\-randomized, uncontrolled before\-and\-after study was carried out in a large tertiary A general hospital in China from January to December 2025\. As an intervention, the intelligent AI\-RPA financial system launched in June 2025 consists of four levels: data governance, business processing, technology application and risk control\. The study compared the 6 months before the system was launched and the 6 months after the system was launched, in terms of operational efficiency \(daily data collection time, report generation time, and automated processing time per transaction\), data quality and risk control \(data docking success rate, data entry error rate, logical conflict correction rate, and risk prediction accuracy for medical insurance violations\) and health\-care staff satisfaction\. Results After the system went online, the daily data collection time was shortened from 132\.5 to 18\.6 min \( P &lt; 0\.001\); the report generation time was shortened from 58\.4 to 5\.8 min \( P &lt; 0\.001\); the automated processing time of each transaction was reduced from 3\.5 to 1\.9 s \( P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Data interfacing success rate increased from 94\.2 to 99\.7%, data entry error rate dropped from 3\.5 to 0\.6%, logic conflict correction rate rose from 78\.1 to 98\.5%, and risk prediction accuracy for insurance violations improved from 72\.1 to 89\.3%\. Total staff satisfaction score improved from 30\.1 to 43\.1 \( P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion This study provides preliminary empirical evidence that the AI\-RPA integrated intelligent financial system was associated with improvements in operational efficiency, data quality, risk control, and user satisfaction in a large Chinese hospital\.

## [Constraining Dust Formation in the Superluminous Supernova 2017gci with JWST Observations](../publications/a233a82e54c3c385bc5f.md)

Sebastián Gómez; Tea Temim; O\. Fox; V\. Ashley Villar; Melissa Shahbandeh; Chris Ashall; Jacob E\. Jencson; Danial Langeroodi; Ilse De Looze; Dan Milisavljevic; Justin D\. R\. Pierel; A\. Rest; Tamás Szalai; Samaporn Tinyanont

Abstract We present JWST/MIRI observations of the Type I superluminous supernova \(SLSN\) 2017gci obtained over 2000 rest\-frame days after the supernova \(SN\) exploded, which represent the latest phase images taken of any known SLSN to date\. We find that archival Wide\-field Infrared Survey Explorer \(WISE\) detections of SN 2017gci taken 70–200 days after explosion are most likely explained by an IR dust echo from a ∼10 −4 M ⊙ shell of preexisting dust, as opposed to freshly formed dust\. New JWST observations reveal mid\-infrared emission at the position of SN 2017gci; however, the flux level and spatial offset indicate that this emission is most likely dominated by the host galaxy\. We therefore derive upper limits from these observations to constrain dust emission at late times\. Radiative transfer modeling of carbonaceous dust shows that warm optically thin dust masses up to 0\.18 M ⊙ are excluded at the 3 σ confidence level\. However, substantially larger dust masses cannot be ruled out if the dust is optically thick\. Infrared detections of other SLSNe have suggested that SLSNe may be highly efficient dust producers\. While our constraints are insufficient to determine the total dust yield of SN 2017gci, they indicate that any late\-time dust emission must either be modest compared to the most dust\-rich SNe or arise from dust that is optically thick\. A larger sample of deep infrared observations will be required to determine whether SLSNe are significant contributors to cosmic dust production\.

## [Beyond AI Tutors: A Human\-Centred Framework for Goal\-Driven Learning Agents in Education](../publications/a251566bd097569fc869.md)

Ghodakhe Keshav, Prof\. Y\.G\.Suryawanshi, Dr\. H\.B\.Jadhav

Artificial intelligence is changing education by offering new ways to explain concepts, support teachers, and personalise student learning\. However, many conventional educational chatbots focus on answering individual questions rather than coordinating the complete learning process\. Students often need more than an answer: they need a learning plan, suitable practice activities, feedback on mistakes, and guidance about what to study next\. Agentic artificial intelligence offers a possible way to coordinate these activities around a defined learning objective\. This paper reviews selected research published between 2024 and 2026 on pedagogical AI agents, large language model agents, and agentic systems in education\. The reviewed literature highlights opportunities for personalized tutoring, adaptive feedback, assignment support, and teacher assistance\. It also identifies concerns involving inaccurate outputs, student dependency, privacy, fairness, accountability, and limited real\-world evaluation\. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a human\-centred framework that connects learning\-goal identification, task planning, trusted educational resources, instructional support, progress evaluation, and adaptive follow\-up\. The framework centres student independence, teacher judgement, and responsible data use\. It is a conceptual proposal and has not yet been experimentally evaluated\. Future research should assess its educational effectiveness, reliability, accessibility, and suitability for different learning environments

## [Beyond criminal intent: infant\-directed violence as a symptom of postpartum psychosis](../publications/a2585540cb83d232eb5e.md)

Brooke Laufer

Postpartum psychosis is a rare but severe psychiatric emergency in which infant\-directed violence, although uncommon, is best understood as a manifestation of acute psychotic illness rather than enduring maternal hostility or conventional criminal intent\. The psychotic content of postpartum psychosis is often infant focus, with profound disturbances in reality testing that transform the mother’s perception of her infant, framing the child through delusions and hallucinations as an object of danger, salvation, contamination, or divine significance\. In the cases of infanticide or filicide, the violence directed at the child, although objectively tragic are subjectively protective or morally necessary\. Drawing on the existing literature on postpartum psychotic phenomenology, this conceptual analysis uses two contrasting clinical cases as illustrative examples—one involving infanticide and one without infant\-directed violence—to examine how infant\-focused delusions can shape perception and behavior\. By contrasting these cases, the article demonstrates how infant\-focused delusions directly dictate behavior and explores why the infant becomes the primary object of the mother’s psychotic experience\. Finally, the paper discusses the implications of this comparative framework for forensic assessment, criminal responsibility, violence risk evaluation, and clinical intervention\.

## [Initial data analysis of the national German transplantation registry with a focus on kidney transplantation](../publications/a25c58019a7ca4ccacb5.md)

Lukas Klein; Gunter Grieser; Carl‐Ludwig Fischer‐Fröhlich; Axel O Rahmel; Henrik Stahl; Andreas Wienke; Antje Jahn‐Eimermacher

Abstract This study presents an Initial Data Analysis \(IDA\) of the German Transplantation Registry \(TxReg\) data for a better data understanding and to inform future data analyses\. The IDA is focusing on data on first\-time kidney\-only transplantations in adult recipients from deceased donors between 2006 and 2016 and refers to data from 14,954 recipients and 9,964 donors across 25 tables\. Investigated aspects include missing data patterns and structure, data consistency, and availability of event time data\. Results show that missing data proportions vary widely, with some tables nearly complete while others have over 50% missing values\. Missing data patterns are identified using a decision tree approach\. An influx and outflux analysis demonstrates that some variables have high potential for imputing missing data, while others were less suitable for imputation\. We identified 168 multi\-sourced variables that are reported by multiple data providers in parallel leading to discrepancies for some variables but also providing opportunities for missing data imputation\. Our findings on event time data demonstrate the importance of carefully selecting the variables used for event time analyses as results will strongly depend on this selection\. In summary, our findings highlight the challenges when utilizing the TxReg data for research and provide recommendations for data preprocessing and analysis in future analyses\.

## [PENGARUH EFISIENSI OPERASIONAL, STRUKTUR MODAL, DAN DANA PIHAK KETIGA TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN BANK UMUM SYARIAH DENGAN UKURAN PERUSAHAAN SEBAGAI VARIABEL KONTROL](../publications/a25d2794356aada1d0f7.md)

Mukhlisul Muzahid; Rauzatul Muna; Ahmad Fauzan

Abstract: This study aims to determine the impact of operational efficiency, capital structure, and third\-party fund growth on the firm value of Sharia Commercial Banks in Indonesia, using firm size as a control variable\. The study utilizes secondary data in the form of annual reports from Sharia Commercial Banks in Indonesia covering the 2021–2024 period\. Panel data regression analysis, performed using EViews version 13 software, was employed as the data analysis technique\. The results indicate that capital structure has a significant effect on firm value, whereas third\-party fund growth and operational efficiency do not\. Furthermore, simultaneous regression analysis reveals that operational efficiency, capital structure, and third\-party fund growth collectively have a significant effect on the firm value of Sharia Commercial Banks in Indonesia\. Meanwhile, when firm size is included as a control variable, the results show that operational efficiency and third\-party fund growth do not have a significant partial effect on firm value, whereas capital structure does\. Finally, the simultaneous regression analysis confirms that, even with firm size as a control variable, operational efficiency, capital structure, and third\-party fund growth collectively exert a significant influence on the firm value of Sharia Commercial Banks in Indonesia\.Keywords: Operational Efficiency, Capital Structure, Third\-Party Fund Growth, Firm Size, Firm Value

## [Beyond Mallampati: From Universal Bedside Tests to Precision Airway Risk Stratification](../publications/a25ee48f36a8a2dc7e0f.md)

Daniele Salvatore Paternò; Luigi La Via; Flavia Paola Arena; Francesca Barbagallo; Basilio Davide Lesina Calà; Emilia Concetta Lo Giudice; Rita Cataldo; Massimiliano Sorbello

Airway management remains one of the few domains of anaesthetic practice still governed by universal, dichotomous screening thresholds applied to profoundly heterogeneous populations\. Conventional bedside tests—the modified Mallampati test, thyromental distance and the upper lip bite test—retain modest and inconsistent diagnostic accuracy, leaving the majority of difficult intubations unanticipated while generating false alarms that drive resource\-intensive contingency plans\. This narrative review reframes preoperative airway evaluation as a problem of individualised risk stratification rather than population screening\. We first summarise the performance limits of classical bedside predictors and the reasons for their ceiling effect, including low target prevalence, inter\-observer variability, spectrum bias and heterogeneous outcome definitions\. We then examine the data streams reshaping the field: point\-of\-care upper airway ultrasound, whose parameters provide operator\-accessible and objective anatomical information; cross\-sectional and craniofacial imaging; and machine\-learning models based on clinical variables, facial images and voice analysis\. For each we discuss accuracy, reproducibility, validation status and barriers to adoption\. We then propose a phenotype\-oriented framework in which assessment intensity is matched to pre\-test probability, with dedicated pathways for obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea, obstetric, head\-and\-neck oncological and post\-radiotherapy, critically ill and emergency, and paediatric populations\. We map this framework onto the 2025 European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and Difficult Airway Society recommendations and outline the validation, calibration and equity requirements—including algorithmic bias across skin tone, sex and ethnicity—that must be met before precision airway assessment can enter routine practice\.

## [Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles](../publications/a262f836dc001782596a.md)

Frieder Rubik; Pauline Deutz; Ulrich Petschow; Anne Kildunne; Florian Hofmann

To date, the circular economy \(CE\) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence\. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice\. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post\-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate\. Moreover, whilst the idea of a CE has taken a firm hold with policymakers, there are questions regarding its adequacy for the challenges faced, especially in terms of achieving absolute reductions in environmental impacts and positive social outcomes\. By contrast, the concept of degrowth calls for significant societal changes to achieve a functioning but smaller and more equitable economy\. It is less politically and economically palatable than CE\. Degrowth strategies, however, overlap significantly with those favored by some of the CE literature\. The potential for these overlaps to support a CE capable of delivering a more sustainable future has received little attention\. This paper offers both theoretical and empirical insights by exploring how degrowth and circular economy principles intersect in case studies focused on textiles and plastic packaging\. Using integrative literature reviews and empirical data, the case studies assess the extent to which different stakeholders approach the CE, drawing on semi\-structured interviews with textile manufacturers in Germany and stakeholders of plastic packaging on the east coast of England\. Our analysis finds that the far\-reaching socio\-ecological transformation towards short\-loop options likely necessary for a CE to confront urgent sustainability crises is seldom addressed in the literature and lies beyond the current scope of stakeholders to action or comprehend\. We argue that there remains a significant implementation gap between CE and \(de\)growth policies with an urgent need for analysis of how a transformation of specific sectors could be achieved linking company, networking and policy approaches\.

## [Governing AI and Blockchain in Finance: A Layered Trust Framework](../publications/a2644f7c54357f554fc5.md)

Rekha Agarwal; Divyansh Mishra; Rajesh Kumar Mishra

AI is increasingly embedded into all aspects of financial markets; from credit decisions, compliance processes, trading strategies to payment systems\. At the same time, blockchain\-based finance has evolved from a speculative niche product into an integral part of the regulated market infrastructure\. An integrative review of these two trends is necessary to examine their potential for convergence and how this will necessitate changes in governance\. The review uses foundational academic literature in blockchain economics, decentralized finance and algorithmic fairness, as well as regulatory, supervisory and market sources up to October 2026\. The authors provide three key findings\. Firstly, there has been a structural change in the market: stablecoin capitalizations are estimated to be between approximately USD 270 billion and USD 320 billion\. Tokenized real\-world assets are concentrated primarily in U\.S\. Treasuries\. The transitional period for the EU Markets in Crypto\-Assets Regulation \(MiCAR\) ends on July 1, 2026\. Finally, the U\.S\. GENIUS Act&\#x27;s rulemaking deadline has passed without a full set of final rules\. Secondly, there remains a persistent gap in governance: international reviews show that the implementation of crypto\-asset standards varies widely\. Furthermore, most security losses result from a few very large attacks\. Thirdly, AI agents have started transacting on stablecoin rails prior to the development of supervisory approaches to algorithmic accountability\. Finally, the authors propose a five\-layered Layered Trust Framework which includes settlement integrity, protocol and code assurance, data and oracle governance, algorithmic accountability, and institutional coordination\. Each layer is linked to characteristic risks and governance instruments as well as measurable indicators\. Based upon these relationships, the authors derive five testable propositions for future empirical research\. The authors conclude that trust in converged AI and blockchain finance is generated by multiple layers of assurance rather than any single technology\. Additionally, they believe that the data and algorithmic layers currently represent the weakest areas of governance\. Limitations associated with an integrative design, such as relying upon secondary market trackers, are also addressed\. Keywords: blockchain; financial technology; AI governance; stablecoins; tokenisation; regulatory architecture

## [AGC\-YOLO: adaptive gated channel network for rice leaf disease detection](../publications/a266c9b75ae5b38674f6.md)

Fei Wang; Yuan Lv; Li Zhao; Jun Zhang; Wen Yang; Guo Li; Xianyao Zhang; Yuxiang Zhang

Accurate detection of rice leaf diseases is critical for intelligent crop protection, yet class imbalance, degradation of multi\-scale feature information, and the limited discriminative capability of feature fusion continue to hinder effective monitoring under field conditions\. To address these challenges, this study presents AGC\-YOLO, an improved detection model based on the YOLOv8s framework\. First, a semantic\-aware data augmentation network termed SAICP Net is devised to alleviate class imbalance and the scarcity of cross\-class co\-occurrence samples through a weakly supervised soft spatial prior and semantically constrained cross\-category instance pasting\. Second, a gated hybrid pooling module named GHP\-SPPF is proposed to adaptively integrate max pooling and soft pooling via a learnable gating mechanism, thereby strengthening the discriminative representation of multi\-scale lesions\. Finally, a channel\-adaptive fusion module termed CAFF is constructed to replace standard concatenation with channel\-wise learnable weights and gated residual refinement, boosting the discriminative power of cross\-scale feature fusion\. Experimental results demonstrate that AGC\-YOLO achieves an mAP@0\.5 of 93\.5 ± 0\.6% on the rice disease dataset, representing a 3\.0 percentage\-point improvement over the baseline, and additional experiments on two public datasets further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for disease detection\.

## [ЗНАЧИМОСТЬ ИЗУЧЕНИЯ ИНОСТРАННОГО ЯЗЫКА И МЕТОДИКА ЕГО ОСВОЕНИЯ ПОСРЕДСТВОМ МУЛЬТИМЕДИЙНЫХ ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ](../publications/a26ad50fd11bdf90e127.md)

Оңласын Колыбай; Onlassyn Kolybai; Ж\.Н\. Бисенбаева; Оңласын Колыбай

AbstractThis article investigates the fundamental pedagogical significance of foreign language acquisition and evaluates the efficacy of multimedia technologies in accelerating this educational process\. As modern educational institutions transition toward SMART\-university ecosystems, traditional instructional paradigms are increasingly being augmented by dynamic, digitally enhanced environments\. This study explores how the systematic integration of multimedia tools—specifically interactive audio\-visual scaffolding and digitized dictionary\-based speech activation platforms—addresses common linguistic barriers such as vocabulary retention and communicative anxiety\. The research employed a mixed\-methods approach, implementing a structured pedagogical intervention where learners utilized varied multimedia resources to practice functional language, receive immediate contextual feedback, and self\-regulate their learning\. Data collected through pre\- and post\-intervention assessments, alongside qualitative learner reflections, indicate that multimedia\-enhanced instruction significantly boosts learner motivation and autonomy\. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that utilizing targeted digital dictionary work within a SMART\-educational framework effectively activates spontaneous speech and reduces cognitive overload\. The study concludes that systematically embedding multimedia technologies into the curriculum is not merely a supplementary strategy, but a fundamental requirement for developing robust communicative competence in contemporary globalized environments\.

## [STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI\-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE](../publications/a26fc79beee10ae2fc4d.md)

Dr\. Vibhuti sharma; Dr Ruchi Sharma; Dr\. Ashish Malik; Dr\. Ankita Singh; Biswas Mistry

Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities\. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI\-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance\. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform\-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance\. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross\-functional collaboration, and continuous learning\. Digital commerce serves as the value\-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network\-based business models\. AI\-driven marketing serves as the customer\-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real\-time engagement\. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience\. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and accountable governance\. The review proposes an integrated framework linking people, commerce, and marketing capabilities through innovation, efficiency, engagement, and customer value\. Future research should empirically test this framework across industries, firm sizes, and national contexts using longitudinal and standardized performance measures\. It identifies research priorities concerning human–AI collaboration, digital inclusion, and environmental performance measurement\.

## [Efikasi Diri sebagai Prediktor Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis Siswa SMP dalam Menyelesaikan Masalah Geometri](../publications/a27af5d9714a5b6d0eec.md)

Yustinus Yustinus; Arie Tonang

Kemampuan berpikir kritis merupakan kompetensi penting dalam pemecahan masalah geometri karena siswa perlu menganalisis informasi, memilih strategi, memberikan justifikasi, dan mengevaluasi solusi\. Pencapaiannya tidak hanya berkaitan dengan penguasaan pengetahuan matematis, tetapi juga dengan faktor afektif, khususnya efikasi diri\. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis efikasi diri sebagai prediktor kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa SMP dalam menyelesaikan masalah geometri\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional prediktif\. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 100 siswa kelas VIII SMP Islam Madura yang dipilih secara purposive sampling\. Data efikasi diri dikumpulkan melalui angket skala Likert, sedangkan kemampuan berpikir kritis diukur menggunakan tes uraian berbasis pemecahan masalah geometri\. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear sederhana pada taraf signifikansi 5%\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa efikasi diri merupakan prediktor positif dan signifikan terhadap kemampuan berpikir kritis \(B = 0,649; t = 7,284; p &lt; \.001\), dengan R² = 0,352\. Efikasi diri menjelaskan 35,2% variasi kemampuan berpikir kritis\. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa efikasi diri merupakan faktor afektif yang relevan dalam menjelaskan kemampuan berpikir kritis, meskipun variasi lainnya berkaitan dengan faktor kognitif, metakognitif, dan pembelajaran dalam konteks pembelajaran matematika dan pemecahan masalah geometri SMP\.

## [Development of an augmented reality\-based comic learning media for elementary school students&\#x27; nationalism attitudes](../publications/a27d64a2e135b34d6618.md)

Lativa Qurrotaini; Alisha Zahra Saadiyah

Background\-Science and social studies \(IPAS\) at SDN Kampung Bulak 01 relied on textbooks and teacher\-centered explanations, limiting contextual cultural engagement and the development of nationalist attitudes\. Objectives\-This study aimed to develop and evaluate an Augmented Reality \(AR\)\-based comic learning media for fourth\-grade elementary school students, particularly in terms of its validity, student responses, and changes in students&\#x27; nationalism attitude scores\. Method\-This study employed a Research and Development \(R&amp;D\) approach using the ADDIE development model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation\. The participants were 31 fourth\-grade students of class IV\-A at SDN Kampung Bulak 01\. Data were collected through expert validation sheets, student response questionnaires, and a nationalism attitude scale administered before and after the implementation of the learning media \(pretest–posttest\)\. The pretest and posttest results were analyzed descriptively by comparing the percentage scores obtained before and after implementation\. Results\-The validation results showed that the media expert and material expert assessments each obtained a score of 92%, while the language expert assessment obtained 83%\. Student response results were 92% in the small\-group trial and 96% in the large\-group trial\. The average nationalism attitude score increased from 72% in the pretest to 90% in the posttest following the implementation of the AR\-based comic learning media\. Conclusions\-The developed AR\-based comic learning media met the feasibility criteria and received positive responses from students\. The increase in nationalism attitude scores from the pretest to the posttest provides preliminary evidence of improvement following the implementation of the media\. However, because the study used a one\-group pretest–posttest design without a control group, the findings should be interpreted as an indication of improvement rather than conclusive evidence of causal effectiveness\.

## [Stage\-specific miR\-188\-5p and ER stress markers reflect tumor aggressiveness in prostate cancer](../publications/a281fb319fe3c1216d54.md)

Hasan Riza Aydin; Ibrahim Sibal; Orhan Semerci; Hamit Zafer Aksoy; Fevzi Bedir; Volkan Enes Çelik; Sema Mısır; Serap Ozer Yaman

Background Reliable biomarkers are required to improve the detection and risk stratification of prostate cancer \(PCa\), particularly for identifying aggressive disease\. MicroRNAs \(miRNAs\) have emerged as promising candidates; however, their integration with endoplasmic reticulum \(ER\) stress pathways and their clinical relevance remain incompletely defined\. Methods This study included 38 patients with histologically confirmed PCa and 20 individuals with benign biopsy findings\. Patients were stratified into low–intermediate and high\-risk groups based on clinical stage, Gleason score, and PSA levels\. Expression levels of miR\-188\-5p, GRP78, and CHOP were quantified in prostate biopsy specimens using quantitative real\-time PCR, and ELISA measured serum GRP78 and CHOP levels\. In parallel, bioinformatic analyses were performed to predict candidate miR\-188\-5p interactions and to examine ER stress\-related expression patterns using publicly available resources, including miRWalk, Sfold/STarMir, and GEPIA3 \(TCGA/GTEx datasets\)\. Associations between molecular markers and clinicopathological parameters were evaluated, and diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) analysis and exploratory univariate logistic regression\. Results Bioinformatic analyses identified HSPA5 \(GRP78\) and DDIT3 \(CHOP\) as candidate miR\-188\-5p targets with predicted binding sites\. External dataset analysis demonstrated higher HSPA5 and lower DDIT3 expression in prostate adenocarcinoma than in normal tissues\. These computational findings indicate predicted interactions and do not establish direct binding or regulation\. Clinically, miR\-188\-5p and GRP78 expression levels were significantly elevated in PCa patients compared with controls and increased progressively with tumor aggressiveness \(p&lt;0\.001\), whereas CHOP expression decreased \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. miR\-188\-5p was positively correlated with GRP78 and inversely correlated with CHOP\. Among the evaluated markers, miR\-188\-5p showed the highest diagnostic discrimination in this cohort, and the exploratory composite biomarker model achieved an AUC of 0\.966\. Elevated miR\-188\-5p and GRP78 levels were also associated with adverse pathological features, including higher tumor grade and cribriform pattern; however, these findings require independent validation\. Conclusion Stage\-associated alterations in miR\-188\-5p and the ER stress markers GRP78 and CHOP were associated with prostate cancer aggressiveness\. The integrated computational and clinical findings support a potential expression\-level relationship that may inform future biomarker studies, but they do not demonstrate direct miRNA–target binding or causal regulation\.

## [Scaffolding\-based differentiated instruction and students’ algebra achievement: evidence from mathematical understanding and problem\-solving performance](../publications/a29bc0e3bf074ea381ab.md)

John Ackon; Francis Ohene Boateng; Benjamin Adu Obeng

Introduction This study examined scaffolding\-based differentiated instruction and students&\#x27; algebra achievement and perceptions\. Methods A quantitative quasi\-experimental design involving 120 students was employed\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and ANCOVA\. Results The experimental group&\#x27;s mean achievement increased from 61 to 75, compared with 60 to 65 in the control group\. Students reported moderately positive perceptions \(M = 3\.423, SD = 0\.588\)\. Discussion Scaffolding\-based differentiated instruction was associated with improved algebra achievement and offers a potential approach to addressing diverse learning needs\.

## [Beyond the Classroom: A Kirkpatrick Evaluation of Pedagogical Competencies in Catholic Religious Education](../publications/a2af6ec69d3c13dd4738.md)

Anggi Manik; Johannes Sohirimon Lumbanbatu; Musammil Lateh

This study aims to evaluate Catholic Religious Education \(CRE\) teachers’ pedagogical and professional competencies in supporting meaningful, inclusive, and student\-centered learning through the Kirkpatrick Model\. The study employed a qualitative evaluation research design to examine four evaluation levels: reaction, learning, behavior, and results\. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing\. Data credibility was ensured through triangulation of techniques and sources\. The findings show that students responded positively to interactive and contextual CRE learning at the reaction level\. At the learning level, teachers showed competence in designing instructional activities based on students’ needs through diagnostic assessment\. At the behavior level, teachers consistently implemented adaptive, inclusive, and student\-centered teaching strategies that reflected effective pedagogical and professional practices\. At the results level, students showed improved engagement, participation, and understanding during learning\. The study concludes that CRE teachers effectively applied their competencies to enhance the quality of learning\. The implications highlight the importance of continuous professional development, instructional innovation, and process\-based assessment to strengthen responsive religious education and sustain student engagement\.

## [A Machine Learning Model Based on Ultrasound and Serological Markers for Predicting Postoperative Stenosis of Rex Shunt Procedure in Children With Extrahepatic Portal Venous Obstruction](../publications/a2bbf977b4c853db7528.md)

Xiangxiang Zhang; Haiyu Wang; Boyang Yang; Biqin Fu; Hongying Wang; Mingle Huang

PURPOSE: To evaluate the value of combining ultrasound parameters with serological markers for predicting postoperative Rex shunt stenosis in children with extrahepatic portal venous obstruction \(EHPVO\)\. METHODS: The training cohort and temporal validation cohort consisted of 114 and 38 children with EHPVO after Rex shunt procedure, respectively\. The study variables included clinical characteristics, ultrasound parameters, and serological markers\. Five machine learning models were developed to predict postoperative stenosis after the Rex shunt procedure at different follow\-up periods, with performance evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\)\. RESULTS: In the temporal validation cohort, the optimal Logistic regression model integrating ultrasound parameters and serological markers achieved AUROCs of 0\.61 \(95% CI: 0\.38\-0\.84\) at 1 month, 0\.67 \(95% CI: 0\.45\-0\.90\) at 3 months, and 0\.82 \(95% CI: 0\.67\-0\.98\) at 6 months for predicting stenosis\. CONCLUSIONS: A model combining serological markers and ultrasound parameters serves as a promising exploratory prototype for predicting Rex shunt stenosis in children with EHPVO, pending further independent multicenter validation\.

## [The Effect of a Multi\-Cultural Environment on the Language Used to Discuss Environmental Sustainability](../publications/a2bed6477624515aa3fd.md)

Labidi Bouabdallah; Edward Hogshire

This research aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the language dynamics and choices within sustainability discourse in the United Arab Emirates \(UAE\)\. By examining the impact of multiple languages, including Arabic, English, and other languages spoken in the UAE, it seeks to understand how sustainability concepts are effectively communicated in this multilingual context\. Additionally, the study investigates the influence of cultural nuances on the comprehension and communication of sustainability within the UAE\. Furthermore, this research aims to identify and analyze the language choices and communication strategies employed by the UAE government in promoting sustainability\. It delves into distinct language choices and communication strategies that aptly reflect the UAE&\#x27;s cultural context and its visionary approach towards sustainability\. It also sheds light on the intricate interplay between sustainability, multilingualism, and cultural diversity\. The research explores how technological advancements and smart solutions are incorporated into sustainability discourse and considers their role in addressing environmental challenges in the UAE\. By examining these aspects, the study highlights the need for effective communication strategies that cater to the linguistic diversity present in the country, ensuring that sustainability messages are accessible to all stakeholders\. Strategies currently in use, such as the utilization of simplified language and visual aids, are showcased as effective measures to overcome linguistic barriers and enhance inclusivity in sustainability communication\. Overall, this research contributes to a better understanding of the language dynamics and communication strategies utilized in promoting sustainability in the UAE and similar regions around the world\. It provides valuable insights for policymakers, organizations, and communication professionals seeking to enhance sustainability discourse in multilingual and multicultural contexts\.

## [Air\-to\-Water Condensation Farming and Fogponics for &quot;Zero\-Watering&quot; Horticulture in India: A Review of Technologies, Crop Suitability and Readiness for El Niño\-Driven Water Scarcity](../publications/a2c3f8955cafcc638b9b.md)

Jadala Shankaraswamy

India produced an estimated 369\.05 million tonnes of horticultural produce from 29\.48 million ha in 2024–25\. Its per\-capita water availability, however, has fallen to about 1,486 m³ \(2021\) and is projected to reach 1,367 m³ by 2031, below the 1,700 m³ water\-stress threshold\. Greenhouse warming is expected to strengthen the inverse El Niño–monsoon relationship\. Future El Niño years may therefore cause crop\-yield losses about 30% larger than those observed historically, and nearly 200 Indian districts have been identified as highly vulnerable in 2026\. This review examines two complementary pathways that decouple high\-value horticulture from rainfall and groundwater: \(i\) air\-to\-water condensation farming, in which atmospheric water generators \(AWGs\), sorbent\-based harvesters, dew condensers or fog collectors, preferably solar\-powered, supply condensate to the root zone of sheltered crops; and \(ii\) fogponics, an aeroponic variant that delivers nutrient solution as a 5–30 µm fog to suspended roots\. Published evidence shows that solar\-driven atmospheric water can irrigate leafy vegetables with growth comparable to tap water, that fog collectors can yield 2\.9–3\.3 L m⁻² day⁻¹ \(annual mean\) at favourable coastal sites, and that aeroponic seed\-potato systems are commercially established in India\. Specific energy demand nevertheless ranges from about 0\.02 kWh L⁻¹ in humid air to 3\.64 kWh L⁻¹ in very dry air, and levelized water costs of US$ 0\.09–0\.40 L⁻¹ have been reported\. These figures confine the approach, at present, to high\-value, small\-footprint protected cultivation, nurseries and propagation\. A crop\-suitability matrix for Indian fruits, vegetables and flowers, an agro\-climatic zoning framework, a sizing procedure and a research roadmap are proposed\. &quot;Zero watering&quot; is best understood as zero dependence on irrigation from surface or groundwater, not zero water input\. The technology can serve as climate\-insurance infrastructure for nurseries and protected horticulture during El Niño years\.

## [Characterization and efficacy of green\-synthesized silver nanoparticles against Puccinia species \- in vitro](../publications/a2c6455b66d1c2f4af56.md)

Vandna Sharma; Sveta Thakur

Abstract Puccinia species cause substantial losses in wheat production and productivity across the globe, creating a serious challenge to food security\. The environmental and health risks associated with conventional fungicides necessitate sustainable alternatives\. The present study examines the eco\-friendly synthesis of silver nanoparticles \(AgNPs\) employing Eucalyptus globulus leaf extract through a biological reduction approach and evaluates antifungal efficacy against wheat rust pathogens\. GC\-MS identified bioactive compounds in the phytoextract, primarily alkaloids and flavonoids\. UV\-visible spectroscopy confirmed AgNPs formation\. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, Scanning electron microscopy, X\-ray diffraction, dynamic light scattering, and zeta potential analysis established their functional groups, surface morphology and size \(22–50 nm\), crystalline nature, and colloidal stability\. In vitro antifungal activity against P\. graminis , P\. triticina , and P\. striiformis was evaluated by cavity slide method\. AgNPs exhibited dose\-dependent inhibition of uredospore germination, achieving 98\.49 ± 0\.3% suppression of P\. graminis , 98\.38 ± 0\.3% of P\. striiformis , and 99\.71 ± 0\.2% of P\. triticina at 40 ppm\. The use of a single green\-synthesized AgNP system against all three major wheat rust pathogens highlights its potential as a broad\-spectrum approach for wheat rust management\. These findings highlight the potential of Eucalyptus \-derived AgNPs as an eco\-friendly alternative for the management of wheat rust pathogens under in vitro conditions\. However, further greenhouse and field studies are required to validate their efficacy, phytotoxicity, and environmental safety before agricultural application\.

## [Frugal Innovation as a Catalyst for Youth Skills Development in South Africa&\#x27;s Resource\-Constrained Environments](../publications/a2cb597a2f27a4ef8a11.md)

Siyabonga Sirayi; Vusumzi Msuthwana

South Africa continues to experience a severe youth employment crisis\. In 2026, the unemployment rate among young people aged 15 and 24 years remained above 60%, while 37\.6% of this cohort was not in employment, education, or training\. Conventional skills development approaches, which rely mainly on formal Technical and Vocational Education and Training \(TVET\) colleges and universities, have struggled to address the needs of young people living in resource\-constrained communities such as townships, informal settlements, and rural areas\. This article argues that frugal innovation, which is defined in the study as the creation of practical, affordable, and sustainable solutions using limited resources, offers an alternative pathway for developing employable skills in these contexts\. Resource\-constrained environments encourage creativity and innovation, problem\-solving, collaboration, and entrepreneurship, enabling young people to acquire technical, digital, business, and socio\-emotional skills through practical experience\. The study employs an integrative literature review that synthesises international scholarship on frugal innovation alongside South African studies on informal innovation, youth entrepreneurship, and recent labour market and policy developments\. Based on this review, the study develops the frugal innovation youth skills\-development pathway, a conceptual framework that explains how frugal innovation can strengthen youth skills development\. The framework is illustrated using evidence from South African fabrication laboratories, township maker spaces, community\-based digital innovation initiatives, and youth employment programmes\. The study concludes that frugal innovation complements rather than replaces formal education and training systems by creating accessible opportunities for experiential learning and skills acquisition\. It recommends integrating frugal innovation into South Africa’s National Skills Development Strategy and related government policies to improve youth employability, promote inclusive entrepreneurship, and strengthen innovation ecosystems in underserved communities\.

## [Investigating the role of previously acquired languages in L3 semantic access through long\-term crosslanguage repetition priming](../publications/a2d099002ea2f324d92b.md)

Janina Camille Vargas; Marı́a del Pilar Garcı́a Mayo

The study&\#x27;s aim was to examine how learners with different L3 proficiency levels access the conceptual representations of L3 Spanish words through their previously acquired languages\. To do so, a long\-term crosslanguage repetition priming task was administered\. During the encoding phase, eighty\-eight \(88\) adult Tagalog\-English bilinguals performed an animacy decision task using L3 words\. The cues from the encoding phase were translated into either Tagalog or English to serve as the stimuli in the test phase\. Participants in this phase were randomly assigned to one of their previously acquired languages and performed a lexical decision task in that language\. We analysed the participants’ reaction times and accuracy rates in relation to their L3 proficiency, the language used in the LDT, and the condition, using mixed effects models\. Contrary to previous L3 studies, such as that of Chen′s \(2020\. How do L3 words find conceptual parasitic hosts in typologically distant L1 or L2? Evidence from a cross\-linguistic priming effect\. International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism, 23\(10\), 1238–1253\. https://doi\.org/10\.1080/13670050\.2018\.1439879\) and Wang and Yang′s \(2025\. Beyond corpus data — complementary and alternative methods in cognitive linguistics\. Review of Cognitive Linguistics , 23\(2\), 573–595\. https://doi\.org/10\.1075/rcl\.00175\.wan\), no cross\-linguistic repetition priming effects were found based on the L3 proficiency level nor on the condition variable\. Only one significant effect was found in the Tagalog LDT group, where the participants responded more slowly than those in the English LDT group\. We interpret our null results not as contradictory of the findings in previous literature but as support for Hall and Ecke′s \(2003\. Parasitism as a default mechanism in L3 vocabulary learning\. In J\. Cenoz, B\. Hufeisen, &amp; U\. Jessner \(Eds\.\), The multilingual lexicon \(pp\. 71–85\)\. Kluwer\.\) Parasitic Model\.

## [Writing a clinical case report based on international guidelines](../publications/a2d3c2e61ed0e192cc31.md)

Евгений Олегович Куневич; Mariia Mikhaleva; Сергей Владимирович Волошин; Victoria Olegovna Polyakova; Sergey M\. Alekseev

Introduction\. Over 10,000 of articles describing clinical cases or case series are published annually in the medical journals world\-wide\. However, the lack of unified requirements for manuscript preparation and varying author guidelines across medical journals often result in incomplete presentation of clinical information, reduced transparency in reporting, and substantial challenges in critically appraising the presented observations\. Objective\. This review aimed to analyze the requirements of the major international guidelines that govern the reporting of clinical cases in peer\-reviewed medical journals\. Materials and methods \. A structured literature search was conducted in the EQUATOR Network website and the PubMed database to identify articles addressing recommendations for clinical case reporting\. Results\. The current reporting guidelines for clinical cases in general clinical medicine \(CARE\), surgery \(SCARE\), and radiology \(CARE\-radiology\) were systematically reviewed\. We examined the structure and content of the checklists along with specific requirements for formatting the core sections of the publication and documenting medical data\. Moreover, we presented practical examples of patient image processing and methods for achieving anonymization\. The utility of graphical visualization of disease trajectories, specifically through the use of a chronological timeline, is also demonstrated\. Conclusion \. Adherence to the CARE statement and CARE\-based guidelines will promote standardization in the preparation of clinical case reports, improve the quality of case descriptions, enhance the completeness and transparency of published reports, and facilitate their reproducibility\. This review may serve as a practical reference for authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors in the preparation, critical evaluation, and publication of clinical case reports\.

## [Artificial intelligent in human resources management systems: opportunities, challenges, and implications for modern organizations](../publications/a2d64ab277da0a8de507.md)

Olusola Adegboye

Abstract Artificial intelligence has moved from the margins of human resource management into its everyday machinery\. Applicant tracking systems now rank candidates, chatbots answer policy questions, predictive models flag employees likely to resign, and large language models draft job descriptions and appraisal summaries\. Research has grown quickly alongside this adoption, but it remains scattered across human resource management, information systems, operations research and computer science, and the regional scholarship published outside English\-language journals is rarely integrated into it\. This article reports a systematic review of 82 peer\-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and March 2026, retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO Business Source Complete, ScienceDirect and the Russian scientific database eLIBRARY\.RU, and screened following PRISMA 2020 guidance\. Thematic synthesis produced six themes: recruitment and selection; learning, development and internal mobility; performance management and predictive analytics; employee experience and generative AI; determinants of adoption; and fairness, transparency and governance\. Three findings stand out\. First, the evidence base is heavily skewed towards recruitment, which accounts for roughly two in five studies, while compensation, industrial relations and occupational safety are barely represented\. Second, reported benefits are concentrated in process efficiency, which is comparatively easy to measure, whereas claims about decision quality rest on weaker designs and shorter time horizons\. Third, adoption failure is more often organisational than technical: the recurring constraints are data quality, scarce analytical skill inside the HR function, and the absence of an internal governance routine\. We argue that value from AI in human resource management depends on treating it as an organisational capability rather than a procurement decision, and we set out a research agenda addressing longitudinal outcome measurement, employee justice perceptions, and evidence from emerging and transition economies\. Keywords Artificial intelligence; human resource management; HR information systems; algorithmic decision\-making; people analytics; systematic literature review; AI governance; algorithmic fairness
