## [CRobot\-SECOND: an improved SECOND\-based 3D point cloud object detection method for safety inspection robots in building construction sites](../publications/a2e6827787f9fba70e07.md)

Jiarong Li; Chunyong Feng; Junqi Yu; Xuyang Zhu; Peng Du; Kaiwen Wang; Ben Wang; Zhenping Dong

Abstract In safety inspection tasks in building construction sites, 3D point cloud object detection is a key technology for safety inspection robots to perceive construction workers, construction vehicles, and surrounding obstacles\. However, sparse low\-channel Light Detection and Ranging \(LiDAR\) point clouds, dynamic\-object interference, and deployment on resource\-constrained robotic platforms make it difficult to improve detection accuracy without compromising detector\-level inference efficiency\. To address this problem, this study proposes CRobot\-SECOND, a 3D point cloud object detection method that combines point cloud input enhancement with lightweight backbone optimization\. First, a point cloud fusion method based on ground constraints and dynamic object compensation is constructed to improve point cloud density and geometric completeness while suppressing ghosting artifacts\. Then, the Partial Convolution \(PConv\) module and the Simple Parameter\-Free Attention Module \(SimAM\) are introduced into the two\-dimensional Bird’s\-Eye\-View \(BEV\) backbone of Sparsely Embedded Convolutional Detection \(SECOND\) to reduce redundant computation and enhance key\-region feature representation\. Finally, a construction\-site point cloud dataset containing construction workers and construction vehicles is established, and comparative, ablation, and multi\-seed experiments are conducted\. The experimental results show that the proposed fusion method improves point cloud density while maintaining high fusion quality\. Across five independent training seeds, CRobot\-SECOND achieves 3D average precision \(AP\) values of \(57\.77 ± 0\.50\)% for construction workers and \(82\.84 ± 0\.37\)% for construction vehicles, compared with \(53\.09 ± 0\.44\)% and \(81\.08 ± 0\.32\)% for SECOND, respectively, where the results are reported as mean ± standard deviation\. The category\-averaged 3D AP increases from \(67\.08 ± 0\.35\)% to \(70\.31 ± 0\.43\)%, with a mean paired improvement of 3\.22 ± 0\.10 percentage points\. The detector\-only network inference speed increases from 75\.19 Hz to 92\.08 Hz\. Overall, these results show that coordinated point cloud input enhancement and lightweight detector optimization improve frame\-level 3D detection of construction workers and construction vehicles under the collected construction\-site conditions without increasing model scale\. These frame\-level detection results provide a basis for exploring CRobot\-SECOND as a perception component for construction\-site safety monitoring, robot path planning, and obstacle avoidance\.

## [Trends in glaucoma diagnosis and medical management in Germany: A nationwide claims data analysis over 10 years](../publications/a2e8727c6ec2e46c2f24.md)

Somar M\. Hasan; Leonore Bovy; Maike Below; Kerstin Klimke; Alexander Karl\-Georg Schuster; Jan Darius Unterlauft; Carl Erb; Argyrios Chronopoulos; Robert Patrick Finger

PURPOSE: Analysing longitudinal trends in recorded diagnosis and medical management of glaucoma in Germany over a 10\-year period\. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using nationwide outpatient claims and prescription data from the German statutory health insurance system\. Patients with documented glaucoma or glaucoma suspect \(ICD\-10 H40\.\*\) between 2014 and 2023 were included\. Analyses assessed annual diagnosed glaucoma patients, demographic characteristics, proportions of medically treated patients and prescribing patterns of glaucoma medications\. Trends in medication classes and number of active ingredients per patient were evaluated\. RESULTS: In 2014, 2 065 065 glaucoma patients were registered\. Documented patient numbers increased until 2019, reaching 2 129 673 and subsequently declined after the pandemic year to 2 025 226 in 2023\. Mean patient age increased from 71\.0 to 72\.4 years\. The proportion of medically treated patients increased from 68% to 71\.5% across all glaucoma subtypes, except for primary open\-angle glaucoma, where it remained stable \(86\.2%\-86\.1%\) and primary angle\-closure glaucoma, where it decreased \(68\.7%\-65\.6%\)\. Among treated patients, monotherapy declined from 54\.8% to 46\.8%, while the proportion on two medications increased from 30\.7% to 33\.7%, three medications from 10\.3% to 12\.3%, four medications from 3\.2% to 4\.9% and 5 or more from 1\.0% to 1\.9%\. Among patients receiving multiple agents, fixed\-combinations increased from 75\.7% to 80\.5%\. Prescribing patterns shifted towards greater use of prostaglandin analogues and reduced use of beta\-blockers\. CONCLUSION: After increasing until 2019, the number of documented glaucoma patients in Germany declined despite an ageing population\. Concurrently, treatment strategies shifted towards intensified medical therapy with greater use of multiple medications and fixed combinations, particularly prostaglandin\-based regimens\.

## [Intellectual property in design\-driven industries: A bibliometric and thematic analysis \(2000–2025\) with insights for the Jewellery Industry](../publications/a2ebc4a78fbec0b51d71.md)

Xia Du; Nor Azlina Mohd Noor; Khadijah Mohamed

This study aims to systematically examine the intellectual property \(IP\) research in design\-driven industries through a bibliometric and thematic analysis of publications from 2000 to 2025, and further derives implications for the jewellery industry\. With the rapid development of the creative economy and digital transformation, IP protection has become an important pillar for innovation and market competitiveness in design\-intensive industries\. However, current research lacks a systematic and holistic review of this interdisciplinary field, and evidence specific to the jewellery remains limited\. To fill this gap, a bibliometric and thematic analysis was conducted based on 359 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection \(WoSCC\) database\. Descriptive statistics were processed using Microsoft Excel, while publication trends, global research patterns, thematic structures, and emerging research frontiers were analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer\. The findings indicate that intellectual property research in design\-driven industries has maintained continuous growth and gradually formed an interdisciplinary integration trend\. Among the valid publications, &quot;Law&quot; is the dominant subject category, followed by &quot;Business&quot; and &quot;Management&quot;, with insufficient attention to &quot;Cultural Studies&quot; and &quot;Art&quot;\. Geographically, the USA and England are core hubs, with the USA leading in publications, citations and collaboration; China is an emerging contributor\. IP law journals dominate in publication volume like Journal of Intellectual Property Law, while interdisciplinary journals such as Strategic Management Journal exhibit higher citation impact\. Reliable keyword clustering identifies copyright, IP and innovation as core keywords, with three main thematic areas\. Accordingly, this study offers relevant implications for the jewellery industry, emphasizing integrated IP strategies and adaptive responses to digital and AI\-related challenges\. It provides a systematic knowledge map and supports future research and innovation in design\-driven industries\.

## [Human myometrial cell fate under chronic oxidative stress for leiomyomagenesis](../publications/a30916f08fa2206751ce.md)

Jian‐Jun Wei; Matthew John Schipma; Yue Feng; Wenan Qiang; David R\. Gius; J\. Julie Kim

Uterine Leiomyoma are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age\. Studies show that both leiomyoma and adjacent myometrium exist in a state of high oxidative stress, characterized by reactive oxygen species \(ROS\) production and impaired antioxidant defenses including defects of manganese superoxide dismutase \(MnSOD\)\. Oxidative stress has been linked to leiomyoma initiation by promoting oxidative DNA damage leading to mutations in MED12 and leiomyoma growth\. We hypothesize that chronic oxidative stress in human myometrial cells induces cellular remodeling and genomic alterations that promote adaptation and contribute to early events in leiomyoma development\. To test this hypothesis, we generated stable human myometrial cell lines \(Myo\-hTERT\) of wild type, MnSOD 68K and mutant MnSOD 68Q that impairs MnSOD antioxidant activity thereby imposing sustained oxidative stress\. Experiments were performed both in vitro using three\-dimensional spheroid cultures and in vivo using xenograft models in immunocompromised mice, with some studies extending up to 10 months to model chronic oxidative stress\. Cells were exposed to the oxidative inducer paraquat \(PQ\) and analyzed using cellular and molecular approaches including spatial transcriptomics and MED12 mutational analysis\. Cells expressing MnSOD 68Q exhibited increased intracellular ROS and oxidative DNA damage, as indicated by accumulation of 8\-hydroxy\-deoxyguanosine \(8\-OHdG\)\. Transcriptomic analysis revealed activation of pathways associated with oxidative stress responses including collagen/extracellular matrix, cellular senescence and IGF/AKT signaling\. Xenografts of primary myometrial cells subjected to prolonged oxidative stress demonstrated similar molecular responses and showed an increased frequency of MED12 mutations\. These changes were accompanied by modest increases in cell proliferation with minimal induction of cell death\. Together, these findings provide mechanistic evidence that sustained oxidative stress can drive molecular and genomic changes in myometrial cells and support a causal role for chronic redox imbalance in the initiation of uterine leiomyomas\.

## [Administrative Law Innovation For Automated Artificial Intelligence Social Assistance Governance](../publications/a30c39facdd58273c08d.md)

Azilfi Fatma; Abelia Rahma Ananda; Syaita Novidia; Fathia Dwi Maharani; Melyana Melyana; Wandari Syahputri

General Background The integration of digital technologies into government systems aims to optimize public service precision and national resource distribution\. Specific Background The INA Digital portal accelerates the distribution of safety nets in Indonesia using automated decision\-making systems to minimize targeting errors and prevent state budget leakage\. Knowledge Gap Although computational processing offers efficiency, the existing regulatory framework experiences a significant vacuum regarding algorithmic auditing mechanisms, the obligation to provide logical explanations, and digital objection schemes\. Aims This study analyzes the readiness of national administrative jurisprudence instruments to govern the utilization of electronic agents in determining welfare recipient eligibility\. Results Normative legal analysis reveals that current legislations are inadequate to independently oversee automated machine decisions\. The absence of human verification within the data matching system risks violating the General Principles of Proper Governance and triggers bureaucratic authority defects\. Novelty This research specifically proposes the formulation of governmental algorithmic accountability regulations that mandate human intervention principles within legally binding digital policies\. Implications Establishing new legislative instruments coordinated by relevant institutions is essential to guarantee system operational transparency, jurisprudential certainty, and the constitutional rights protection of affected citizens\. Highlights Bureaucratic decision\-making without human verification triggers potential violations of jurisprudential certainty principles\. Existing regulations lack necessary mechanisms for digital objections and public computational system audits\. The state requires new legislative instruments mandating operational transparency for integrated public service portals\. Keywords Administrative Law Innovation; Artificial Intelligence Governance; Automated Decision Making; INA Digital Portal; Algorithmic Accountability

## [Factors associated with generative AI chatbot acceptance among medical students with prior academic use: a cross\-sectional study based on an extended technology acceptance model](../publications/a325b4f9104fb53f2430.md)

Hesamaddin Kamalzadeh; Elham Boushehri; Mohammad Hosein Hayavi\-Haghighi; Mohammad Saeed Salari; Samireh Abedini

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) chatbots are becoming increasingly embedded in medical education, providing students with on\-demand support for learning, clinical reasoning, and academic tasks\. However, the psychological and technological factors that shape medical students’ acceptance of these tools remain insufficiently understood\. This study examined acceptance among medical students with prior academic use of GenAI chatbots by extending the Technology Acceptance Model \(TAM\) to include AI literacy \(AIL\) and perceived security and privacy \(PSP\), and by examining their associations with perceived ease of use \(PEOU\), perceived usefulness \(PU\), attitude toward using GenAI \(ATG\), and behavioral intention to use GenAI \(BIG\)\. A cross\-sectional online survey was conducted among medical students at Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences \(HUMS\), Iran, between May and June 2026\. Eligibility required prior academic use of a GenAI chatbot\. Data were collected using a structured, self\-administered questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. The measurement model was assessed for reliability and validity, while the structural model was evaluated using path coefficients \(β\), coefficients of determination \( R ²\), and effect sizes \( f ²\)\. Of the 292 students invited, 267 completed the survey, and 252 participants with prior academic use of GenAI chatbots were included in the final analysis \(mean age, 22\.64 ± 2\.28 years; 147 \[58\.3%\] female\)\. The measurement model demonstrated adequate reliability and validity\. AIL was positively associated with PEOU \(β = 0\.479, p &lt; 0\.001\), while PSP was positively associated with PU \(β = 0\.157, p = 0\.005\)\. PEOU and PU were positively associated with ATG, and ATG showed the strongest association with BIG \(β = 0\.524, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The model explained 38\.7% of the variance in BIG, with R ² values ranging from 0\.229 to 0\.387 across the endogenous constructs\. The findings indicate that medical students’ acceptance of GenAI chatbots is associated with AIL and PSP alongside the core TAM constructs of PEOU and PU, with ATG showing the strongest association with BIG\. Strengthening AIL and establishing clear privacy and security policies may support the informed and responsible integration of GenAI chatbots into medical education\.

## [Vehicle Type Heterogeneity in Battery Electric Vehicle Energy Consumption: A Multi\-Perspective Analysis Using Real\-World Fleet Data](../publications/a330506db77286835234.md)

Liangying Luo; Haichao Huang; Yizhou Wang; Hongdi He

Real\-world energy consumption of battery electric vehicles \(BEVs\) varies with trip conditions, driving behavior, and vehicle state\. Treating vehicle type merely as a control variable may mask substantial heterogeneity in energy consumption mechanisms\. This study treats vehicle type as a source of mechanism heterogeneity and examines how the determinants of energy consumption rate \(ECR\) differ among sedans, logistics vehicles, and buses\. Using 41,933 trips in China, we combined statistical analysis, machine learning, and CausalForestDML\. Statistically, ECRs of sedans and logistics vehicles decrease as trip distance increases, but trip distance is nearly irrelevant for buses\. Aggressive driving raises logistics vehicle ECR by 22\.2% yet barely affects sedans\. For prediction, permutation importance further reveals the divergence: trip distance and duration dominate sedan prediction, whereas energy recovery ratio and accelerator\-pedal, which are marginally important for sedans, become primary predictors for logistics vehicles and buses\. Causal estimates confirm that directional divergences persist after conditioning on covariates\. For example, trip duration has opposite effects on buses versus sedans and logistics vehicles\. Moreover, the causal framework decomposes each factor’s effects across its value range, revealing patterns beyond correlation alone\. These findings provide actionable guidance for vehicle\-specific eco\-driving strategies and battery management system optimization\.

## [Exploring the Lives of HRM Graduates in Their Workplaces](../publications/a33686f52850f37e874e.md)

Joshua Ong; Rene D\. Osorno

This study explored the lived experiences of Bachelor of Science in Hotel and Restaurant Management \(BSHRM\) graduates in their workplaces, focusing on rewarding experiences, professional challenges, coping strategies, personal and professional development, and recommendations for improving hospitality education\. Using a descriptive phenomenological research design, the researcher conducted structured interviews with ten BSHRM graduates employed across four hotels in Cebu\. Ethical principles, including beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, and respect for autonomy, were observed throughout the research process\. Findings revealed that graduates experienced positive aspects of employment, including tangible rewards, career advancement, guest satisfaction, relationship building, and personal and professional growth\. However, they also encountered challenges involving difficult guests, interpersonal conflicts, communication barriers, demanding workloads, and workplace pressures\. To address these difficulties, graduates employed coping strategies such as establishing professional boundaries, prioritizing rest, maintaining a proactive mindset, strengthening communication skills, and demonstrating adaptability, maturity, and professionalism\. Their workplace experiences further contributed to developing advanced technical, managerial, cognitive, and interpersonal competencies essential for hospitality careers\. Participants emphasized the importance of specialized instruction, practical and hands\-on training, comprehensive health and safety standards, and stronger collaboration between academic institutions and hospitality establishments\. The study highlights the importance of aligning hospitality education with actual industry expectations to better prepare graduates for professional responsibilities\. These findings provide valuable insights for educators, curriculum developers, and hospitality stakeholders in enhancing instructional approaches, strengthening industry partnerships, and developing relevant training programs that promote graduate employability, workplace readiness, professional competence, and sustainable career development within the hospitality industry\.

## [Food allergy and attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children: evidence and implications for pediatric allergy practice](../publications/a33b281f5986449c5085.md)

鲁冰雪; Yongmei Xie

Families of children with food allergies \(FA\) and attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\) often ask whether the conditions are related and whether dietary changes could improve their children&\#x27;s attention or behavior\. This narrative review examines FA\-specific evidence and its implications for pediatric allergy practices, drawing on observational studies, reviews, clinical guidance, and contextual mechanistic research\. One small FA\-specific meta\-analysis found no statistically significant association, whereas several individual observational studies reported positive associations\. Differences in diagnostic definitions, reporting sources, temporal assessment, and confounder adjustment limited the ability to make comparisons\. Studies of broader allergic phenotypes and Mendelian randomization provide no FA\-specific causal estimate, and proposed microbiota–immune–brain pathways remain unconfirmed in humans\. Restrictive or elimination diets should not be routinely recommended for ADHD because evidence of sustained benefit is limited, and additional restriction may compromise nutrition or worsen feeding difficulties, particularly in children already avoiding allergens\. Pediatric allergy care should verify the FA diagnosis, preserve tolerated foods, monitor growth and dietary adequacy, and refer persistent attention or behavioral concerns for appropriate assessment\. This review distinguishes direct FA evidence from broader allergy findings and relates these uncertainties to practical decisions about diagnosis, dietary restriction, and coordinated care\.

## [Weisbrod, Victor: Philosophical Foundations of AI Certification](../publications/a33c71b91b1b35f82fc3.md)



\_Certified Ai Project\_\. 2026This white paper conducts a systematic inquiry into the philosophical foundations of AI certification, that is, into the basic assumptions of the institutionalised endeavour to assess AI applications as ethically good or bad\. It identifies and examines two paradigms of AI governance: the dominant principles paradigm and the alternative systems paradigm\. By clarifying and problematising the foundational assumptions of both paradigms, the white paper elucidates their respective strengths and weakness\. The principles paradigm provides an administratively legible, legally predictable, and standardised framework for product\-level auditing\. However, it encounters significant challenges regarding underdetermination, value arbitration, narrow artefact boundaries, and ethics washing\. The systems paradigm approaches AI applications in a manner that aims to capture these as embedded in complex ecological, social, and economic systems with inherent standards of good functioning\. In turn, it faces significant hurdles concerning system unboundedness, data opacity, normative projection, and temporal bottlenecks\. Ultimately, by explicating the implicit assumptions and limitations of both paradigms, the white paper aims to deepen our understanding of AI certification as a complex governance practice, and to provide foundational insights for future research, standard\-setting, and policymaking in this field\.

## [An Efficient AES\-128 CMOS Architecture with Round Reuse and Composite Field S\-Box to Secure IoT Devices](../publications/a3483c3870f2e52905cb.md)

Salman Ahmed; Nabihah Ahmad; Chessda Uttraphan; Ardhi Wijayanto; Abdinasir Hirsi

The rapid growth of the Internet of Things \(IoT\) has intensified the demand for lightweight cryptographic solutions that deliver high security without compromising energy and area constraints\. This paper presents a highly efficient AES \-128 hardware architecture specifically optimised for resource\-constrained IoT devices\. The proposed design employs reusing a 128 \-bit AES framework resource, enabling an extensive reduction in functional units across all transformation stages\. Additionally, the elimination of intermediate registers and the reuse of a single round computation block for all encryption rounds significantly reduce area while balancing the trade \-offs between throughput, frequency and power\. A key innovation in this work is the implementation of a compact S\-box using composite Galois Field GF28 arithmetic to enhance the substitution efficiency while maintaining cryptographic strength\. The physical layout implemented on 32 nm technology reveals that the proposed architecture achieves a core area of only 0\.015 mm , an operating 2 frequency of 200 MHz, with 0\.014 Gbps throughput, and a low power consumption of 1\.4 mW , offering a well\-balanced trade\-off among performance, security, and hardware efficiency\. A comparative analysis with state\-of\-the\-art designs demonstrates the superiority of this approach for achieving low\-cost, energy\-aware cryptographic protection\. The proposed solution is highly suitable for secure resource constrained IoT deployments\.

## [INCIDENCIA DE VARIABLES TECNOLÓGICAS EN LA RENTABILIDAD DE UNA PLANTA DE ETANOL DE BAGAZO DE CAÑA DE AZÚCAR](../publications/a34bbfb0b160c43b9afc.md)

Adiánez Sánchez González; Eulogio Castro Galiano; Leyanis Mesa Garriga; Erenio Gónzalez Suárez; Yailet Albernas Carvajal; Geidy Díaz Hernández

Introduction:The production of bioethanol from lignocellulosic biomass faces economic challenges due to technological and market uncertainties\.Objective:To evaluate the impact of the main technological and economic variables on the profitability of a second\-generation \(2G\) ethanol plant, considering different capacities and process variants\.Materials and Methods:A base plant with a capacity of 500 hL/day of ethanol was designed, including four variants\. Investment and operating costs were estimated, applying univariate sensitivity analysis and the Plackett–Bürman design\. Profitability \(NPV, IRR, PBP\) was assessed for ethanol production capacities of 500, 3500, and 5000 hL/day\.Results and Discussion:At 500 hL/day, none of the variants are profitable, although Variants 3 and 4 \(175 °C, furfural as a coproduct\) show better indicators\. Fixed capital is the most significant variable\. Fractionation and enzymatic hydrolysis account for 85–95% of equipment costs\. At 3500 and 5000 hL/day, Variants 3 and 4 are highly profitable \(positive NPV, IRR &gt; 60%, PBP of 1\.5–2 years\)\.Conclusions:Ethanol production from sugarcane bagasse is not profitable at a small scale without high\-value coproducts\. Furfural \(pretreatment at 175 °C\) is key to economic viability\. Fixed capital is the most influential variable; therefore, the design and energy integration of the fractionation and enzymatic hydrolysis stages must be optimized\. Variants with integrated saccharification and fermentation are technically and economically superior\.

## [Evaluating the Effectiveness of an AI\-Assisted Personalized Learning Pathway in Mobile\-Supported Online Physical Education](../publications/a357db60ef5e63d6227f.md)

Xia Wan; Libing Fu

This study evaluates the effectiveness of an AI\-assisted personalized learning pathway in mobile\-supported online physical education\. To overcome issues of homogeneous content and delayed feedback, a system integrating cognitive knowledge, physical fitness, and motor skills was developed\. Reinforcement learning dynamically adapted learning pathways, while edge\-based computer vision enabled real\-time feedback on low\-end mobile devices\. A randomized controlled trial with 120 students over eight weeks compared the proposed system to conventional video\-based instruction\. Results showed low inference latency \(34\.8 ms\) and a 61\.2% reduction in movement variability\. NASA\-TLX scores revealed lower mental demand and frustration, with high learner engagement\. The findings highlight the effectiveness of AI\-assisted personalization and mobile feedback in improving learning outcomes and experiences in online physical education\.

## [Aging Characteristics and Mechanisms of CMDB Propellants Under Vacuum Conditions](../publications/a35d4de07a512764c36b.md)

Hanyu Deng; Zhandong Wang; Wenhe Liao; Peizhe Gao; Yuqing Tang; Yichao Yuan; Linwei Li

ABSTRACT In order to explore the aging characteristics of CMDB propellants under vacuum conditions relevant to spacecraft storage or ground‐based applications, comparative accelerated aging tests were conducted under three conditions: vacuum 60°C, atmospheric 60°C and 70°C\. Specimens were tested for uniaxial tensile strength, hardness, an NMR‐derived cross‐linking‐related parameter, and component content\. The results show that under atmospheric 60°C, NG decreases by only 1\.68%, stabilizer by 0\.188%, cross‐linking density reduces by 0\.196 Mc, maximum tensile strength declines by 2\.169 MPa, maximum elongation decreases by 3\.85%, and hardness increases by 1 HA\. These changes are more obvious at 70°C, but the propellant remains viscoelastic\. In contrast, under vacuum 60°C, NG drastically reduces from 36% to 19\.54%, stabilizer reduces by 0\.55%, cross‐linking density increases to 2\.405 Mc, maximum tensile strength increases by 3\.163 MPa, maximum elongation plunges by 11\.984%, hardness increases by 4\.13 HA, and the propellant exhibits brittle characteristics\. The results indicate that vacuum conditions accelerate the migration and volatilization of liquid components \(NG and stabilizer\), increasing intermolecular forces of NC\. Meanwhile, H \+ generated from thermal decomposition of NG creates a more acidic environment in the lower liquid component environment, inducing ‐OH groups on NC molecular chains to react and form ‐O‐ bonds, leading to chemical cross‐linking between adjacent NC molecules\. These phenomena fundamentally cause the distinct vacuum aging behavior compared to atmospheric pressure\.

## [Adultcentrism in the moral instruction of Di Zi Gui: proposed psychological mechanisms and implications for children’s autonomy](../publications/a35f7d769003bc4570bf.md)

Hui Liu; Pinghua Liu

Di Zi Gui , a Qing\-era moral primer, is discussed in contemporary Chinese family education, school moral education, and classical\-recitation initiatives\. Existing accounts document heterogeneous uses but do not establish their current prevalence or effects on children’s autonomy\. This Hypothesis and Theory article develops a conditional model through close reading of 34 purposively selected precept groups from one modern working edition and comparison with psychological research from other contexts\. Textual evidence, theoretical inference, and predictions requiring empirical testing are distinguished throughout\. Adultcentrism identifies a possible asymmetry in interpretive authority; self\-determination theory supplies the core distinction between controlled compliance and endorsed commitment\. The proposed developmental focus is middle childhood, approximately 8–12 years, without assuming that findings from other age groups transfer directly\. Three candidate pathways concern the permitted form of action, the motivational basis of conformity, and the legitimacy and expression of affect: behavioral standardization, compliance reinforcement, and emotional suppression through moral absolutization\. Their operation is hypothesized to depend on enactment and children’s acceptance, negotiation, reinterpretation, selective appropriation, strategic compliance, or resistance\. Autonomy is treated as a culturally situated, relational capacity, not as independence from family obligations\. Five propositions specify an exposure\-only baseline comparison, distinct mediators and moderators, and autonomy\-related outcomes\. Philosophy for Children is considered a possible moderator only when children’s contributions can consequentially alter interpretation or practice\. The article offers an auditable interpretive framework, not evidence of established mechanisms: it contains no original participant data, direct observations of current teaching, or estimates of prevalence or effect size\. Its contribution is a differentiated research agenda for testing how the same text may be enacted and understood differently\.

## [The clinimetric properties of an extended version of the brief approach/avoidance coping questionnaire in the Danish population: the BACQ\-14](../publications/a35f819b7fff73f180c3.md)

Isabella P\. R\. Holst; Dorte Ejg Jarbøl; Sonja Wehberg; Tina Birgitte Wisbech Carstensen; Kirubakaran Balasubramaniam; Lisa Maria Sele Sætre

Objective To describe the expansion of the three\-dimensional Brief Approach/Avoidance Coping Questionnaire \(BACQ\) from a 12\-item scale \(BACQ\-12\) to a 14\-item scale \(BACQ\-14\) covering four dimensions and to examine its clinimetric properties including reliability and validity\. Methods A thorough developmental process for the BACQ\-14 was performed\. Pilot tests were conducted to evaluate content validity\. A field test comprising both test and retest was performed\. Structural validity was evaluated using Exploratory Factor Analysis \(EFA\) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis \(CFA\)\. Internal consistency was evaluated by Cronbach’s alpha and item\-to\-rest Pearson correlation\. Hypothesis testing was based on health\-related variables, whereas test–retest reliability was evaluated using Bland–Altman \(BA\) plots\. Results The BACQ\-14 showed good content validity\. The EFA \( n = 150\) showed that both a three\- and a four\-factor\-model could be suitable for the BACQ\-14, but the CFA \( n = 360\) demonstrated that the four\-factor model had a substantial better fit\. Cronbach’s alpha for the dimensions in the four\-factor model ranged from 0\.66 to 0\.88\. The BA plots showed that the 95% limits of agreements were approximately \[−5;5\] for the four subscales, indicating large random variation\. Conclusion The BACQ\-14 covering four dimensions had slightly better clinimetric properties than the BACQ\-12 and is suitable for questionnaires where a brief assessment of coping is warranted\. However, its sensitivity to detect small changes in coping is constrained which may limit its utility in clinical practice\.

## [Assessing the effect of elevated CO2 on wheat leaf rust severity: insights from a free\-air carbon dioxide enrichment \(FACE\) experiment](../publications/a364915e3d2cfdd344d1.md)

Jasper Krößmann; Lars Großhans\-Kretschmer; Lisa Waßmann; Bernd Rodemann; Lorenz Kottmann; Sven E\. Weber; Rod J\. Snowdon; Albrecht Serfling; Andreas Stahl

Introduction The continuous increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) concentrations is a major driver of global climate change and may alter plant growth and host–pathogen interactions\. Understanding how elevated CO 2 affects disease development is therefore important for future crop production and resistance screening\. This study investigated the effect of elevated CO 2 on wheat leaf rust \( Puccinia triticina \) in Central European winter wheat genotypes under field conditions\. Methods Free Air Carbon Dioxide Enrichment \(FACE\) field experiments were conducted over two growing seasons, exposing winter wheat to an atmospheric CO 2 concentration of approximately 600 ppm\. Leaf rust development was assessed using the Area Under the Disease Progress Curve \(AUDPC\) and Average Ordinate \(AO\)\. Genotypic effects, CO 2 treatment effects and their interaction were analysed across the tested genotypes and growing seasons\. Results Elevated CO 2 was associated with a general tendency towards higher leaf rust severity, although the magnitude of this response varied between growing seasons and genotypes\. Genotype effects were highly significant, whereas the genotype × CO 2 interaction was comparatively weak, providing limited evidence for differential responses among the tested genotypes\. Under the conditions of this FACE experiment, the relative ranking of genotypes for leaf rust severity was largely maintained under elevated CO 2 \. Discussion The results indicate that elevated CO 2 may affect the expression of wheat leaf rust resistance, while the relative differences among genotypes remained largely consistent under the tested conditions\. However, the limited number of independent CO 2 treatment environments, particularly following the exclusion of one elevated CO 2 ring in 2023, restricts the strength of treatment\-level inference\. The findings should therefore be interpreted as observations specific to the experimental conditions rather than as general evidence for stable leaf rust resistance under elevated atmospheric CO 2 \. Nevertheless, they highlight the importance of considering changing atmospheric CO 2 concentrations when evaluating and screening disease resistance in future wheat breeding programmes\.

## [Prediction of Marine Engine Wear Using Topological Data Analysis of Lubricating Oil](../publications/a371b198325ed663f0c1.md)

Екатерина Мазур; Pavel Shcherban

Predicting marine engine wear based on the analysis of used lubricating oil samples is an important task in predictive maintenance\.However, conventional forecasting methods are often ineffective in this context because of irregular sampling intervals, the limited number of observations available for establishing reliable relationships, and the apparent &quot;improvement effect&quot; in oil condition caused by oil replenishment or changes in engine operating conditions\.This study proposes a methodological approach based on topological data analysis\.Its distinctive feature is the identification of hidden relationships under conditions of critically incomplete data and a &quot;blind start,&quot; when no sufficiently representative historical dataset is available\.The proposed integrated algorithm includes preliminary parameter normalization and feature\-space dimensionality reduction using principal component analysis\.The Density\-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise algorithm is applied to identify dense regions corresponding to stable operating states and to detect noise points\.The resulting multidimensional space of diagnostic indicators is then transformed by the Mapper algorithm into a topological graph representing the chronological degradation trajectory\.Mapper identifies persistent groups of observations that are interpreted as graph nodes\.These nodes correspond to characteristic system states, while the graph edges represent possible transitions between them\.Geometric graph metrics are used to calculate the cumulative wear path, the system condition index, and the remaining useful life\.The introduction of an additional calculated parameter, degradation intensity, makes it possible to estimate the topological rate of wear per unit of operating time and to adapt the model to nonlinear degradation processes\.The proposed method makes it possible to develop an interpretable model of the engine state space\.Such a representation facilitates accurate assessment of the current condition and prediction of wear progression\.Modeling results obtained from real\-world data demonstrated that the approach is capable of identifying normal operating states and anomalous transitions\.The resulting information provides a reliable basis for predictive wear assessment and the optimization of maintenance processes\.

## [Network\-Wide Freeway Speed Nowcasting and Forecasting from Sparse Fixed Sensors with a Probe\-Supervised Graph Convolutional Recurrent Network](../publications/a37330d7ea8b45f56e04.md)

Ran Tu; Zihao Li; Arash Mirzaei

Traffic agencies need current and near\-future speeds on every link of their network, but their fixed sensors cover only part of it\. We study joint nowcasting and next\-hour forecasting of hourly speeds on all 4\{,\}127 directional freeway links of the Dallas\-\-Fort Worth region from sensors on 643 links \(15\.6%\)\. Historical probe\-vehicle data supervise every link in training; only sensor readings are used at inference\. We call this setting probe\-supervised sparse sensing\. We propose GCRN\+, a graph convolutional recurrent network that predicts deviations from a historical speed profile\. It combines a parameter\-free, direction\-aware kernel interpolation of sensor anomalies, used as input features and as an output baseline, with a diffusion\-convolutional GRU on the directed road graph, a low\-rank adaptive graph and learnable link embeddings\. It scales linearly with network size and trains on a CPU\. Sensor readings are emulated from probe speeds, which isolates spatio\-temporal inference from detector calibration\. On four held\-out test days, GCRN\+ attains an RMSE of 2\.21\~mph for the current hour and 2\.39\~mph for the next hour on unsensored links, against 3\.23\~mph for the historical average\. The best baselines that use the same interpolation features reach 2\.53 and 2\.75\~mph\. Adapted recent models without these features \(STID, STAEformer, ImputeFormer, MoGERNN\) reach at best 2\.54 and 2\.53\~mph; this comparison is between complete pipelines rather than architectures\. GCRN\+ is best in every distance band except links not connected to any sensor through the road graph\. Ablations within one recurrent backbone attribute most of the gain to the link embeddings and the adaptive graph, which can be trained because probe labels exist for every link\. For congestion detection on unsensored links, recall rises from 77\\% \(historical average\) and 86% \(best competitor\) to 89% at aprecision of 0\.94\.

## [Triglyceride\-glucose\-Chinese visceral adiposity index \(TyG\-CVAI\) outperforms other TyG\-derived indices in predicting 5\-year advanced cardiovascular\-kidney\-metabolic syndrome: a prospective community\-based cohort and machine learning study in China](../publications/a37f188f24413216ad2b.md)

Yezhou Wu; Qiuhua Wei; Lingyu Ye; YeMei Mo; Yushuang Wei; Fuxiang Fang; Huannan Wei; 张秋玲; Mingli Li; Zengnan Mo

The Cardiovascular\-Kidney\-Metabolic \(CKM\) syndrome is a recently proposed integrated disease concept\. Its advanced stages \(Stages 3–4\) are characterized by subclinical or clinical cardiovascular disease, severe chronic kidney disease, and significantly elevated mortality risk\. Triglyceride\-glucose\(TyG\) and TyG\-derived indices can comprehensively reflect insulin resistance \(IR\) and obesity; however, the predictive performance of these indices for advanced CKM syndrome has not been systematically compared\. This study aimed to compare the predictive value of 10 TyG and TyG\-derived indices for 5\-year advanced CKM syndrome and to identify the optimal index\. This prospective community\-based cohort study \(Yulin, Guangxi, China\) included 2072 participants free of advanced CKM at baseline \(median follow\-up: 54\.7 months\)\. Ten TyG and TyG\-derived indices were calculated \(TyG, TyG\-WC, TyG\-WHtR, TyG\-BMI, TyG\-BRI, TyG\-WWI, TyG\-LAP, TyG\-ABSI, TyG\-VAI, TyG\-CVAI\)\. Restricted cubic spline \(RCS\) regression assessed dose–response relationships, and Cox proportional hazards regression estimated effect sizes\. Incremental predictive value was evaluated using a clinical reference model \(Model Clinical\) and a simplified model \(Model 2\) as a sensitivity analysis\. IDI and time\-dependent AUC were the primary metrics, with NRI as secondary \(1000 bootstrap resamples\)\. Three feature selection methods \(LASSO, Boruta, and RF\-RFE\) were jointly applied within the training set to identify the optimal TyG index, and their stability was assessed using 1000 bootstrap resamples\. Six machine learning algorithms \(RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, MLP, AdaBoost, and Bagging\) were used to construct prediction models\. The optimal model was selected based on test\-set discrimination, calibration \(Hosmer–Lemeshow P ≥ 0\.05\), and clinical utility, with the Youden index used for threshold determination\. Model performance was assessed using AUC, calibration plots, Brier score, and decision curve analysis \(DCA\)\. A risk stratification cutoff was derived from the training set using the Youden index and applied to the test set\. SHAP was used to interpret the final optimal model\. Internal validation used 10\-fold cross\-validation and bootstrap optimism correction \(1000 resamples\); sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of censoring weighting \(IPCW\), exclusion of participants with hypertension, diabetes, or medication use, additional adjustment for baseline CKM stage, and separate analyses for Stage 3 and Stage 4 outcomes, and redefinition of advanced CKM excluding Stage 3 events defined solely by eGFR &lt; 30 mL/min/1\.73 m 2 \. Multiple comparison corrections \(FDR and Bonferroni\) were applied\. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess consistency across age, gender, smoking, drinking, and exercise strata\. After a 5\-year follow\-up, 247 of the 2,072 participants developed incident advanced CKM events \(incidence density: 2\.79 per 100 person\-years\)\. RCS analysis revealed that, except for TyG\-ABSI, which exhibited a U\-shaped non\-linear association \( P for nonlinearity = 0\.037, crossing points: 0\.651 and 0\.712\), the remaining nine indices showed significant linear dose–response relationships with advanced CKM risk \(all P for overall &lt; 0\.05, all P for nonlinearity &gt; 0\.05\)\. In the fully adjusted model, TyG\-CVAI demonstrated the largest effect size \(per 1\-SD increase: HR = 1\.290, 95% CI 1\.143–1\.456, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. In the incremental predictive analysis using Model Clinical, TyG\-CVAI showed the highest continuous NRI \(0\.363, 95% CI 0\.198–0\.493, P &lt; 0\.001\) and a modest but statistically significant IDI \(0\.009, 95% CI 0\.001–0\.022, P = 0\.016\)\. At 60 months, adding TyG\-CVAI yielded a small yet statistically significant increase in AUC \(from 0\.789 to 0\.799; ΔAUC = 0\.010, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. This was the largest improvement among all indices\. All three feature selection methods consistently identified TyG\-CVAI as the optimal index\. Based on comprehensive evaluation of test set AUC, calibration curves, and Brier score, the XGBoost model \(AUC = 0\.839, 95% CI 0\.796–0\.883, Brier score = 0\.084, Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0\.200\) achieved the best balance between discrimination and calibration and was selected as the final optimal model\. Internal validation showed a 10\-fold cross\-validated AUC of 0\.855 ± 0\.038 and a bootstrap optimism\-corrected AUC of 0\.870, indicating low overfitting risk\. DCA demonstrated positive net benefit of the XGBoost model compared to the &quot;treat all&quot; strategy within the threshold probability range of 0\.10–0\.40\. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes\. SHAP analysis of the final six\-feature XGBoost model illustrated the contributions of age, gender, hypertension, diabetes, LDL\-C, and TyG\-CVAI\. Using a cutoff of 0\.14, the test set was stratified into low\- and high\-risk groups, with 5\-year cumulative incidences of advanced CKM of 5\.9% vs\. 38\.1% \(HR = 8\.356, 95% CI 5\.105–13\.676, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across strata \(all P for interaction &gt; 0\.05\)\. Sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with hypertension, diabetes, or medication use, additional adjustment for baseline CKM stage, and separate analyses for Stage 3 and Stage 4, yielded consistent results\. These findings remained robust after FDR and Bonferroni correction, and TyG\-CVAI was selected in 100% of bootstrap resamples\. Among the 10 TyG and TyG\-derived indices evaluated, TyG\-CVAI demonstrated superior predictive performance for 5\-year advanced CKM syndrome, with the largest effect size and highest continuous NRI, although its incremental value beyond established clinical predictors was modest\. These findings were internally consistent across multiple machine learning approaches\. TyG\-CVAI may serve as a low\-cost auxiliary tool for identifying individuals at high risk of advanced CKM in community settings, pending external validation\.

## [Explainability Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection from Genomic Data](../publications/a381cee5442e65ac2f15.md)

Puvaneswari Subramaniapillai; Indirani Govindasamy; Revathy Gurumurthy

Genetic disorders affect millions worldwide, posing major challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatments\. New developments in genomic technologies, especially Next\-Generation Sequencing \(NGS\), have enhanced the classification of genetic modification and improved diagnostic abilities\. Moreover, the Machine Learning \(ML\) and Deep Learning \(DL\) methods emerged as efficient tools for evaluating the intricate genomic data and determining the patterns, which can be generally complex to identify by employing conventional analytical techniques\. Additionally, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence \(XAI\) has developed as a significant constituent in the analysis of genomic data by enhancing the interpretability of DL methods and showing the contribution of main genetic features involved in the detection of genetic disorders\. This study presents an Explainability\-Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection \(XHTGT\-AGDD\) approach\. The primary objective of the proposed model is to improve the reliability and accuracy of genetic disorder detection from genomic data by integrating advanced techniques\. Initially, preprocessing is performed using quantile transformation to normalize the input data for robust analysis\. Following preprocessing, feature selection is performed using the fire hawk optimizer to identify the most informative feature subsets from the genomic data\. Besides, the classification task is accomplished using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer, which captures complex relationships and temporal dependencies among genomic features\. To further refine the learning process, hippopotamus optimization algorithm is employed for model optimization\. In addition, an explainability mechanism based on SHAP is incorporated to interpret the model predictions and highlight the individual genetic features toward the final decision\. The experimental result analysis of the XHTGT\-AGDD model is performed using a benchmark dataset\. The simulation results reported the enhanced results of the XHTGT\-AGDD technique in terms of several measures, achieving an accuracy of 99\.12%\. Therefore, the proposed model provides reliable and effective performance for automated genetic disorder detection from genomic data\.

## [Lifetime exposure to nitrogen dioxide and ozone and pediatric asthma](../publications/a3847cadf35f52184fd9.md)

Wenli Ni; Hilary L\. Zetlen; Sheryl L\. Rifas‐Shiman; Heike Luttmann Gibson; Emily Oken; Diane R\. Gold; Mary Berlik Rice

Abstract Short\-term exposure to nitrogen dioxide \(NO2\) and ozone \(O3\) worsens pediatric respiratory health, but impacts of lifetime exposure on asthma development are less clear\. We examined associations of early\-life and cumulative NO2 and O3 exposure with asthma from mid\-childhood through mid\-adolescence among participants in Project Viva, a pre\-birth cohort enrolled in eastern Massachusetts, USA, from 1999 to 2002\. We estimated residential NO2 and O3 at 1×1 km resolution using geospatial models and calculated average concentrations in the first year of life and cumulatively through mid\-childhood and early teens\. Asthma was reported by questionnaire in mid\-childhood \(mean age 7\.9 years, n=1,174\), early teens \(13\.3 years, n=979\), and mid\-teens \(17\.8 years, n=665\)\. Using logistic regression adjusted for child age and sex, maternal education, and household smoking, we assessed odds of asthma per interquartile range \(IQR\) increase in exposure\. Higher NO2 in the first year of life \(IQR 10 ppb\) and cumulatively through midchildhood \(IQR 9 ppb\) was associated with higher odds of asthma in mid\-childhood \(odds ratio\[OR\] 1\.34, 95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 1\.05\-1\.71; OR 1\.32, 95% CI: 1\.01\-1\.73, respectively\)\. We did not observe associations for O3\. Even at relatively low levels, early\-life and cumulative NO2 exposure may increase childhood asthma risk\.

## [Addressing unmet clinical needs in treatment\-resistant breast cancer: expanding the diagnostic–prognostic landscape through next\-generation inflammatory signatures](../publications/a3871bdee31ba6080b04.md)

Emmanuel Ifeanyi Obeagu

Treatment\-resistant breast cancer remains a major clinical challenge because conventional clinicopathological and molecular biomarkers incompletely capture the dynamic interactions between tumour cells, immunity, inflammation, and the systemic host response\. Next\-generation inflammatory signatures offer an opportunity to expand the diagnostic–prognostic landscape by integrating cellular, molecular, immune, and thromboinflammatory indicators with established tumour characteristics\. This narrative review critically examines emerging evidence for neutrophil\-to\-lymphocyte ratio, platelet\-to\-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune\-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, C\-reactive protein, cytokines, tumour\-associated macrophages, myeloid\-derived suppressor cells, neutrophil extracellular traps, coagulation biomarkers, and liquid\-biopsy\-derived measures in treatment\-resistant breast cancer\. Particular attention is given to sources of heterogeneity, including population characteristics, tumour subtype, treatment exposure, comorbid inflammation, sampling time, specimen processing, analytical platforms, and inconsistent biomarker thresholds\. The review further evaluates the transition from biomarker discovery to clinical decision support, highlighting the need for prospective multicentre validation, standardised analytical procedures, external validation of computational models, and integration with molecular subtyping, circulating tumour DNA, imaging, and immune profiling\. Rather than interpreting inflammation as a static prognostic variable, longitudinal inflammatory trajectories may provide earlier signals of biological treatment resistance and complement conventional measures of disease progression\. Future research should establish clinically actionable inflammatory combinations and evaluate biomarker\-guided anti\-inflammatory strategies alongside standard therapies\. Ultimately, integrating inflammatory phenotypes with tumour molecular characteristics may facilitate earlier recognition of resistance and more precise, dynamic, and equitable breast cancer management\.
