## [Brain\-Aligned Multimodal LLMs for Social and Emotional Understanding of Cartoon Movies](../publications/a4f371d8bb2385b24295.md)

Yiran Huang; Zeyong Zhang; Bharat Biswal; Xin Di; Mengjia Xu

Multimodal large language models \(MLLMs\) offer scalable annotations of social and affective content, but their temporal agreement with human judgments and neural predictive value require further evaluation\. We compared diffusion\-based and autoregressive MLLMs with continuous human Theory of Mind \(ToM\) and affective valence ratings across three short cartoon movies\. Behavioral analyses assessed temporally aligned Pearson correlations, rating distributions, and the effects of preceding scene descriptions\. Ratings from each source were separately used in subject\-specific regression models to predict regional fMRI responses\. Model ratings captured aspects of human temporal variation despite systematic distributional differences, with generally stronger alignment for valence than ToM\. Preceding context improved alignment in some conditions, depending on the model and movie\. In \\emph\{The Present\}, more regions showed significant encoding for MLLM ratings than for human ratings, whereas effects were more limited in the other movies\. Spatial overlap across rating sources occurred mainly among MLLMs; overlap between human and model ratings was limited and involved primarily visual, dorsal\-attention, and posterior default\-mode regions\. These findings support MLLMs as scalable tools for generating brain\-predictive annotations of social and emotional content, while highlighting systematic rating differences and model\- and stimulus\-dependent alignment with human judgments\.

## [Sex‐Specific Early Life Corticosterone Stress‐Coping Capacity Is Linked to Mitochondrial Content and Telomere Maintenance](../publications/a4f4212a2e7db2340acd.md)

Mauricio Guillen‐Parra; Alberto Velando; Bibiana Montoya; Roxana Torres

Glucocorticoids are upregulated during acute challenges, contributing to maintenance of energy balance\. However, if this upregulation exceeds a threshold or becomes chronic, it can lead to harmful effects\. Investigating the factors behind between\-individual variation in the magnitude of the response to acute stress and how effectively individuals regulate this response to return to baseline glucocorticoid levels \(recovery capacity\), is therefore important\. Glucocorticoid regulation may be influenced by mitochondrial content, as these hormones are produced in the mitochondria of the adrenal glands\. Furthermore, early\-life adversity can impair glucocorticoid regulation, and these effects may be mirrored by other mechanisms, such as telomere maintenance, suggesting possible correlations among these traits\. In this study, we evaluated whether variation in corticosterone response to an acute challenge and recovery capacity in 27 Cocos Booby \(Sula brewsteri\) nestlings was related to mitochondrial DNA copy number \(mtDNAcn\), mass growth rate, and telomere dynamics during the first 30 days of life\. We found sex differences in recovery capacity: females sustained higher corticosterone levels than males after an acute challenge\. Higher mtDNAcn was associated with greater corticosterone increases and weaker recovery, suggesting that mtDNAcn reflects an individual&\#x27;s capacity to produce glucocorticoids\. Finally, telomere dynamics, but not mass growth rate, were related to recovery capacity, a relationship only significant in females\. Females with better telomere maintenance had weaker recovery capacity than those with poorer telomere maintenance\. These results highlight links among glucocorticoid regulation, mtDNAcn, and telomere dynamics, suggesting that these traits are jointly shaped, likely through sex\-specific pathways during early life\.

## [Hemovigilance Systems: Current Practices, Implementation Challenges, and Future Perspectives in Transfusion Safety](../publications/a4ff973b81df92ca3854.md)

Chhavi Juyal; Yusra Ahmad; Hiba Parveen; Pragati Bailwal

Hemovigilance includes an organized overview of monitoring and managing any negative outcomes of blood transfusion along with safeguarding the donors and recipients of blood transfusions\. This study articulates systematically the theory, types and ways of putting the hemovigilance systems into practice in micro and macro health institutions\. It discusses the role of structured, streamlined, and controlled transfusion safety reporting along with databases and feedback systems\. It encompasses the systems of primary donor and recipient hemovigilance, operational and laboratory monitoring, near and other systems for other countries\. It analyses current constraints to reporting, definitional inconsistencies, and digital resource deficits, while proposing system effectiveness improvements\. It emphasizes system strengthening improvements to artificial intelligence, automatic electronic reporting, donor\-recipient system feedback, and definitional globalization, particularly in resource constrained environments\. It emphasizes the necessity of improved structured systems to promote transfusion medicine safety and efficient practice globally\.

## [Research progress on the BAG3\-HSP70 axis\-mediated autophagy in acute myeloid leukemia](../publications/a50150c6f5d6996e61af.md)

Yang Liu; Tao Wu

Acute myeloid leukemia \(AML\) is a genetically heterogeneous hematological malignancy in which chemoresistance and relapse, often driven by leukemia stem cells \(LSCs\), remain major obstacles to cure\. Autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved lysosomal degradation pathway whose function in AML is not fixed but is stage\- and context\-dependent: it restrains leukemogenesis in some settings while sustaining established and therapy\-stressed LSCs in others\. The Bcl\-2\-associated athanogene 3 \(BAG3\)\-heat shock protein 70 \(HSP70\) axis integrates proteotoxic stress with the autophagy machinery, most notably through chaperone\-assisted selective autophagy \(CASA\)\. This review applies a four\-tier evidence framework—direct AML evidence, other hematological evidence, non\-AML evidence, and proposed or hypothetical mechanisms—and explicitly separates BAG3\-specific evidence from general HSP70 and autophagy findings\. Direct AML evidence is comparatively strong for the cytoprotective, mitophagic and chemoresistance roles of autophagy and HSP70, but it is limited for a specific BAG3 dependency\. In particular, direct BAG3 coupling to ULK1, competitive BAG3/HSP70 binding at the Beclin1 BH3 domain, and direct HSP70 shielding of ATG5 from cleavage are not supported by primary evidence\. We examine the crosstalk between this axis and recurrent AML alterations \(FLT3\-ITD, NPM1 and TP53\), and survey therapeutic strategies ranging from ATP\-site HSP70 inhibitors to HSP70\-BAG3 protein\-protein interaction inhibitors, dual HSP70/HSP90 targeting, BAG3\-directed agents, targeted protein degradation, nanoparticle delivery and emerging immunotherapies\. We stratify direct axis\-targeting from broad HSP70\-family or proteostasis approaches\. Finally, we summarize the principal knowledge gaps and the potential therapeutic window, cardiac\-safety and biomarker challenges that must be addressed to convert the BAG3\-HSP70 axis from a plausible mechanism into a precision target in AML\.

## [Effects of combined GnRHa and letrozole on serum steroid profiles in girls with advanced bone age](../publications/a503ef38ebd99823e6b5.md)

Xuan Zhang; Yanan Zhang; Yutong Xing; 杨文庆; 秦月秋; Xuehan Gao; Xujing Kong; Susu Cai; 薛国翠; Xiaomin Fan; Mingzhao Chen; Yongqi Liu; Baorong Chen; Xue Yan; 张会丰

Objective To evaluate the impact of combined GnRHa and letrozole on serum steroid profiles \(classical, 11‐oxygenated, and backdoor androgen pathways\) in girls with advanced bone age, and to monitor adverse events\. Methods 28 girls with advanced bone age were enrolled\. Of these, 15 received add‐on letrozole after GnRHa monotherapy \(Group B\); the remaining 13 started combination therapy from baseline \(Group A\)\. Blood was collected at baseline, 1, and 6 months\. Steroids were measured by LC‐MS/MS\. Results At baseline, Group A had higher classical androgens, progestogens, estrogens, INB, SHBG, and FAI than Group B \(all P &lt; 0\.05\), while 11‐oxygenated androgens were similar\. In Group A, classical androgens, P, 17‐OHP, 5α‐DHP, 17OH‐DHP, 3α‐diol, E1, E2, and FAI decreased markedly \(all overall P &lt; 0\.01\) and remained lower at 6 months; 11‐KT showed a modest reduction at 1 month \( P = 0\.02\), but other 11‐oxygenated androgens were unchanged\. In Group B, add‐on letrozole reduced E1, E2, AMH, and INB \(all overall P &lt; 0\.05\), while most androgens and progestogens were stable\. No hyperandrogenism or adverse events were observed\. Conclusions Over 6 months, combined GnRHa and letrozole was not associated with hyperandrogenism in girls with advanced bone age\. In Group A, gonadal androgens and estrogens were markedly suppressed, while adrenal androgens remained stable\. In Group B, add‐on letrozole had limited effects on most androgens\. Estrogen suppression was observed in both groups\. These findings appear to support short‐term safety, although longer‐term data are needed\.

## [Spatial sampling for triaxial OPM\-MEG: understanding neurodevelopmental trajectory](../publications/a50b41c9eb30f429edbf.md)

Lukas Rier; Niall Holmes; Ryan M\. Hill; Matthew J\. Brookes

OBJECTIVE: Magnetoencephalography \(MEG\) measures magnetic fields generated by current flow in neural assemblies, providing a non\-invasive means to track brain function\. In recent years, the MEG field has been revolutionised by a new class of field sensor called an Optically Pumped Magnetometer \(OPM\)\. OPMs are small, lightweight, and allow construction of wearable and reconfigurable arrays of &\#x27;triaxial&\#x27; field sensors \(that measure magnetic fields along three axes simultaneously\)\. These systems can be used to capture MEG data across the life span, from infancy to adulthood\. With such multi\-axis sensing arrays coming into routine use, here we aimed determine how dense a sensor array is required to adequately capture the spatial variation of neuromagnetic fields across the scalp\. Approach: We simulated neuromagnetic fields based on realistic head geometries of individuals aged 15 months to 34 years\. We then used two independent approaches to determine the sensor spacing required to capture the highest spatial variation of the field across the scalp surface: one method was based on spherical harmonic decomposition of neuromagnetic fields, and the other based on evaluating sensor redundancy in densely sampled arrays\. Main results: Both methods agree in showing that the required sensor separation increases with age, from \~40 mm in a 1\-year\-old to \~55 mm in an adult\. Significance: The sensor spacings obtained in our simulations represent upper bounds in the required values: separations above these bounds will not adequately capture spatial field variation; however, continuing to reduce sensor separation below these limits will continue to improve performance\. These findings are important for the future development of OPM\-MEG technology, particularly the construction of systems for neurodevelopmental applications\.

## [Mattos, José Caetano de: THE VIRTUE WORM: Why the Base of the Pyramid Defends the Power That Seized It — Flattery, the Trivia Decoy and the Transfer Test, with La Boétie, Aristotle’s Flatterer and Kershaw’s ‘Working Towards the Führer’](../publications/a50d7b23f245052cfda7.md)



Tyranny has never governed by force alone\. Every seizure of an institution or a state is held, in the end, by people who could see what was being done to freedom and chose to applaud — and who applauded what did not matter\. They praise the leader’s punctuality, his humour, his faith, his humble origins, while the courts are captured, the budget diverted and the critics silenced\. This article names that figure the “virtue worm” and gives it, for the first time, an exact structure\. The worm is identified without reading any mind, by four public marks: a seizure documented on the record, a defence that begins with possession of the seat, praise of attributes offered in place of answers to documented acts, and display beyond what personal safety requires \(D1\)\. From this definition seven results follow\. The worm’s praise is a forgery of judgement — the form of fair assessment with its origin replaced by interest \(T1\)\. It is the exact contrary of parresia, the courage to speak truth to power: pleasant speech to power at others’ risk instead of frank speech at one’s own \(T2\)\. It needs no lie, because its deception lives in the selection of truths, and the truer the trivia, the deeper the concealment \(T3\)\. Unlike the programme’s Freedophobic Man, who has lost his freedom to fear, the worm keeps his freedom intact and spends it against the freedom of others — and is answerable for it \(T4\)\. Its loyalty belongs to the seat, not the person, and passes to the successor the day the leader falls \(T5\)\. It blinds the very power it flatters \(T6\), and performs for free the policing that would otherwise need police \(T7\)\. The same structure now operates at a scale no court ever reached: in AI assistants trained on approval, which reproduce the worm’s selective affirmation by construction, and in state honour rolls such as China’s Social Credit System, which turn the worm’s display into a currency\. The remedy cannot be a purge, because those who hunt the old power’s worms become the new power’s worms \(C2\)\. It can only be a virtue: one person, in the room where it matters, saying what everyone else has chosen not to say\. Priority is conceded to Aristotle, Tacitus, La Boétie, Machiavelli, Kershaw, Kuran, Wintrobe, Egorov and Sonin, and the paltering literature; three tests are registered and none has yet been run\. Keywords: virtue worm; flattery; voluntary servitude; La Boétie; Aristotle’s kolax; Kershaw; working towards the Führer; preference falsification; Kuran; parresia; paltering; loyalty–competence trade\-off; Freedophobic Man; Philosophy of Virtues; Decoy Placement Rule; AI sycophancy; social credit system\. Highlights • The virtue worm is the person who defends a power that seized an institution by praising its trivia and omitting its acts against freedom; it is defined by structure, not by mind\-reading\. • The worm’s speech is the determinate contrary of parresia: pleasant speech to power at others’ risk, against frank speech at one’s own\. • Worm discourse needs no false sentence\. The forgery lies in what is selected for defence — the Trivia Decoy, predicted by the Decoy Placement Rule\. • The worm is not the Freedophobic Man\. The freedophobe’s freedom was replaced; the worm’s is intact and spent against others, so the worm is answerable where the freedophobe is a victim\-turned\-enforcer\. • Worm loyalty follows the seat, not the person: the registered Transfer Test predicts re\-alignment to the successor when the figure falls\. • AI assistants trained on approval reproduce the worm’s structure without its agency, and state honour rolls \(China’s Social Credit System\) are worm markets; the remedy in both is a protected capacity to dissent, never a score\. • Freedom is lost not only when it is taken, but when those who could defend it find it more convenient to praise the one taking it; against that loss, no institution substitutes for the virtue of frank speech\. Relevance Every contemporary society has institutions — universities, firms, parties, churches, courts, platforms — in which power can be taken by one person and then held by the applause of many\. Political science explains much of the holding with fear and with rational opportunism\. What the virtue worm adds is an account of why the applause takes the form it does, why it can be honest sentence by sentence and still deceive, why it blinds the power it flatters, and why it outlives the figure it served\. For the governance of artificial intelligence the result is direct: a system rewarded by the approval of whoever holds the conversation acquires the worm’s structure without anyone intending it, and adding virtue scores makes the problem worse rather than better\. For states that score civic virtue, the article identifies the honour roll as the place where worm displays will concentrate\. For individuals, it offers five self\-administered questions that a person can ask before defending anyone in power, and it explains why one frank voice in a room is worth more than many silent dissenters\. \(direct link \)

## [Elections, Disinformation, and Fact\-Checking: The Case of Türkiye in 2023](../publications/a5114cb3474b2702fa3c.md)

Hakan ASTA

This study examines the role of disinformation in the context of the 2023 Presidential Election and 28th Term General Election of Members of Parliament in Türkiye through a comparative analysis of two major fact\-checking platforms: Teyit \(teyit\.org\) and Doğruluk Payı \(dogrulukpayi\.com\)\. Building on the theoretical framework of disinformation as a form of strategic and manipulative communication, the research investigates how false or misleading information circulated during election periods affects the democratic process\. The study employs a quantitative content analysis method, supported by document analysis, to evaluate a total of 243 verified claims\-154 from Teyit and 89 from Doğruluk Payı\-circulated between March 18 and May 28, 2023, the official election period designated by the Supreme Election Council \(YSK\)\. The findings reveal that the number of circulating claims increased significantly as election day approached, demonstrating that disinformation activity intensifies in parallel with political competition\. The majority of the claims targeted the Nation Alliance \(Millet İttifakı\), while most of the verified content was classified as false, indicating the dominance of disinformation in the political communication process\. Both platforms were found to act quickly, verifying a substantial portion of claims within three days\. The analysis also shows that social media served as the primary channel for dissemination \(91\.35% of all claims\), with videos and images emerging as the most frequently used content types\. Overall, the research highlights that while fact\-checking platforms play a critical role in promoting transparency and information accuracy, the pervasive and rapid nature of digital disinformation continues to challenge the integrity of democratic processes\. The study concludes that combating disinformation effectively requires not only verification efforts but also systemic strategies encompassing media literacy, algorithmic transparency, and ethical media practices to preserve the reliability of information and the fairness of elections in the digital age\.

## [Why this AI app? The impact of generative artificial intelligence on educators’ choices in educational apps](../publications/a51f010c7a77e08e1d62.md)

Emma Liptrot; Adam Kenneth Dubé

In elementary education, generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is being incorporated into educational applications, despite still\-emerging evidence of its effects on children’s learning and development\. Educators, who are already overwhelmed with choice in the commercial app space, may increasincly have to decide whether to incorporate GenAI\-enabled apps for their classrooms\. Thus, the present study investigates how mentioning GenAI in app store descriptions impacts K\-6 educators’ selection of educational apps\. Over two studies, K\-6 educators \(each n = 101\) from Canada, the US, and the UK viewed and evaluated eight researcher\-created educational math apps with and without GenAI\. Study 1 tested whether mentioning GenAI in app descriptions affected educators’ app evaluations but found no effect\. In Study 2, results from a repeated measures MANOVA revealed that educators rated apps without AI higher than those mentioning GenAI, but there were no significant effects of GenAI on likelihood to download or willingness to pay for apps\. A hierarchical cluster analysis identified three distinct groups of educators: 1\) selectors \(n = 28\), who exhibited a preference for downloading, rating, and paying for apps including GenAI; 2\) agnostics \(n = 59\), who exhibit minimal preferences; and 3\) avoiders \(n = 14\), who prefer apps without AI\. Most educators were agnostic to the use of GenAI in educational apps, highlighting the need to support educators’ informed decisions about when to adopt GenAI tools and encourage critical evaluation of GenAI’s role in education\. More research is needed to understand how educators’ GenAI preferences relate to their attitudes, knowledge, and use of GenAI\.

## [Developing and Evaluating Hikaya: A Bilingual Mobile App for Children with Dyslexia and Dyscalculia](../publications/a52673932d0c526cf6f3.md)

Saadeh Z\. Sweidan; Khalid Ahmad Darabkh; Dareen M\. Hamdan; Raghad W\. Shkukani; Raghad M\. Alzaatreh

Dyslexia and dyscalculia are lifelong learning disabilities that affect how individuals process language and numbers\. Children with these disabilities often require specialized support, which can be difficult and expensive to provide\. Smartphones and their applications \(apps\) have created opportunities for accessible digital learning support\. However, most existing educational apps do not support Arabic language\. Motivated by this, we introduce Hikaya, an interactive Android application designed to assist children with learning difficulties, particularly in Arabic\-speaking countries\. Hikaya provides bilingual support in Arabic and English covering three core subjects: Arabic, English, and Math\. Parents can create accounts, add children, and monitor progress through a dedicated dashboard\. Children can engage with one of three learning models, including a unique Reading Karaoke feature that allows them to read scripts aloud while the app evaluates their performance\. To assess Hikaya’s perceived utility, user satisfaction, and system usability, a perception survey was completed by 200 participants after a one\-month test period\. The results displayed highly positive user reception and strong satisfaction\. As future work, we aim to expand Hikaya’s language capabilities by supporting various Arabic dialects and widely spoken global languages\. We also plan to integrate adaptive learning algorithms using Artificial Intelligence and collaborate with educators and speech therapists to enhance the app’s learning value\.

## [Teacher&\#x27;s Guide to the AI\-Driven Classroom Toolkit](../publications/a52cad271159290a6957.md)

Obasanjo Fajemirokun; Amber M\. Neal\-Stanley; Waliu Oluwaseun Abioja; Christabel Kanayo Anumenechi; Favour  Oluwatosin Olaosebikan; Maria Regina Jaga; Kofoworola Elegbede

Teacher’s Guide to the AI\-Driven Classroom Toolkit is a practical resource for building teachers’ capacity to use artificial intelligence responsibly and effectively in teaching and learning\. Developed for educators, the toolkit introduces foundational concepts in artificial intelligence, digital literacy, prompt engineering, AI\-supported lesson planning, assessment, differentiated instruction, student engagement, and reflective teaching practice\. It also presents practical guidance for working in low\-resource environments with limited access to devices and reliable internet connectivity\. The toolkit discusses responsible and ethical AI use, including accuracy verification, data privacy, academic integrity, bias awareness, fairness, inclusion, transparency, and the continuing importance of teacher judgment and human oversight\. It highlights AI as a support tool that can enhance teaching efficiency and learning experiences without replacing the professional, relational, and ethical responsibilities of educators\. The resource is intended for teachers, teacher educators, education administrators, professional\-development facilitators, researchers, and other stakeholders interested in practical AI integration in schools\.

## [Machine Learning Modeling of Drill Cuttings Transport Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulation Data](../publications/a53dba529f85bfa5cc2f.md)

Kathrin Susanne Skinder; Mostafa M\. Abdelhafiz; Khizar Shahid; Günther Brenner

ABSTRACT Drill cuttings transport is a critical operation in drilling deep wells\. Inefficient removal of cuttings can lead to both hydraulic and mechanical problems during drilling operations\. High‐fidelity computational fluid dynamics \(CFD\) simulations provide detailed insight but are computationally expensive\. Alternative models often oversimplify the relationships between operational parameters and particle transport, thereby failing to predict critical quantities\. These quantities include transport efficiency or cuttings concentrations\. In this study, surrogate models are developed using a common data set generated by validated multiphase CFD simulations\. The data set consists of 269 CFD simulations varying the Reynolds number, Taylor number, particle concentration, and particle size\. Five surrogate models, namely, Decision Trees \(DTs\), Random Forest \(RF\), Extra Trees \(XTRs\), Extreme Gradient Boosting \(XGBoost\), and Gaussian process regression \(GPR\), were trained to predict the domain‐averaged particle velocity\. The models are evaluated in terms of prediction accuracy, learning behavior with respect to training data size, robustness through bootstrap resampling, and physical consistency of the response trends\. All trained models achieved very high predictive accuracy \(\), confirming that CFD‐based particle transport can be reliably emulated using data‐driven surrogates\. The learning‐curve analysis showed that performance improves rapidly with increasing data, saturating beyond approximately 60% of the data set\. Despite the statistical accuracy, tree‐based ensembles produced piecewise‐constant, nonsmooth response surfaces\. However, GPR generated smoother and more physically consistent trends\. Sensitivity analysis revealed that the Reynolds number dominates the system behavior, explaining more than 95% of the output variance\. The high predictive accuracy observed across all surrogate models \(\), with most predictions within of CFD reference values, reflects the low‐dimensional character of the system, where the output is dominated by the Reynolds number\. The trained models enable global sensitivity analysis through Monte Carlo simulation and real‐time prediction of cuttings velocity, supporting continuous monitoring, control, and optimization of borehole cleaning in deep drilling operations, while demonstrating how information from expensive high‐fidelity CFD simulations can be retained in fast, computationally cheap surrogates\.

## [Linha de cuidado para pessoas em crise de ansiedade na urgência e emergência: evidências e desafios na integração entre upa e a rede de atenção psicossocial](../publications/a53ed9e86df6c2c93650.md)

Ricardo Galvão Filho; Querem Evelyn da Silva Pereira; FABIANA RAQUEL FRIESS; Luiz Fernando Jun Aoyagi; Rebeca Ribeiro marques; Cesar Romero Lima Ferreira; Brenda Paes Bendassoli

Acute manifestations of psychological distress, particularly anxiety crises and panic attacks, represent highly prevalent demands in fixed pre\-hospital emergency care facilities, such as 24\-hour Emergency Care Units \(UPAs\)\. However, clinical management is frequently characterized by episodic interventions, covert stigmatization, symptomatic hypermedicalization, and severe disruption of longitudinal follow\-up\. This study aims to analyze scientific evidence and clinical\-organizational challenges in establishing an integrated care pathway for individuals experiencing acute anxiety in emergency settings, emphasizing the articulation between acute emergency services and the Psychosocial Care Network \(RAPS\), notably Psychosocial Care Centers \(CAPS\) and Primary Health Care\. This narrative literature review was conducted through a structured bibliographic search on the MEDLINE database via Europe PMC \(2015–2025\), complemented by official regulatory frameworks of the Brazilian Unified Health System\. The evidence indicates that acute emergency management requires rapid clinical stratification to rule out life\-threatening somatic mimics, relational reception grounded in active listening, judicious and strictly short\-term anxiolytic pharmacotherapy, and structured discharge planning\. Collaborative intersectoral matrix support and stepped\-care models emerge as decisive strategies to mitigate overcrowding, prevent rapid readmissions, and ensure person\-centered care\.

## [ELABORAÇÕES LINGUÍSTICO\-DISCURSIVAS DA EMPATIA NA CONTEMPORANEIDADE](../publications/a540b0fc9be0ae9e447f.md)

Fábio Luiz Nunes

A obra A corpus linguistic approach to analyzing “empathy” \(Routledge, 2026\), de Sabrina Fusari, investiga o perfil lexicogramatical da empatia mediante análise do corpus English Web 2020\. Examinam\-se divergências entre definições neurocientíficas e o uso social, utilizando a linguística sistêmico\-funcional para identificar as metafunções ideacional, interpessoal e textual\. Os resultados indicam que o uso leigo reifica a empatia como mercadoria quantificável\. Observa\-se que o deslocamento morfológico por meio da nominalização do verbo correlato condensa processos interpessoais, à medida que a passividade sintática do termo sugere uma entidade estática\. A pesquisa valida a eficácia de grandes corpora para elucidar a construção discursiva de estados internos\. Além disso, o estudo fundamenta a compreensão da empatia como construto complexo, trazendo implicações diretas para áreas clínicas, psicológicas e para os estudos de linguagem\.

## [Visual\-digital writing instruction and its effects on creativity, motivation, multiliteracy awareness, and writing anxiety in pre\-service EFL teachers](../publications/a54e041ce05c19572913.md)

Figun Dinçer

The rapidly increasing transformation of education demands a new look at how pre\-service teachers of English as a Foreign Language \(EFL\) are prepared for writing instruction\. While multimodal communication increasingly dominates education, writing pedagogy in many teacher training programs remains traditional and text\-centered, leaving pre\-service teachers to face a heavy cognitive and emotional burden\. This study explores how a visual\-digital writing model affects four learner outcomes: writing anxiety, intrinsic motivation, creativity, and multiliteracy awareness\. By introducing the concept of Cognitive Load Diffusion \(CLD\), the study explains how meaning\-making through visuals and digital design can reduce linguistic pressure and emotional burden while facilitating learners’ creative engagement\. A quasi\-experimental design was used with 150 pre\-service teachers enrolled in the ELT department at a large public university in Turkey; two intact class sections were randomly assigned to condition, with the experimental group \(N = 75\) receiving a design\-focused, multimodal curriculum with visuals, color, and layout, and the control group \(N = 75\) receiving a traditional, paragraph\-based, text\-centric writing curriculum\. Both sections were taught by the same instructor to control for instructor effects\. The four principal outcomes were measured with the Second Language Writing Anxiety Inventory \(SLWAI; \[6\]\), the Attitude/Motivation Test Battery \(AMTB\), the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking \(TTCT\), and a Multiliteracy Pedagogical Awareness Scale \(MPAS\), and were analyzed with a one\-way Multivariate Analysis of Covariance \(MANCOVA\) controlling for pre\-test writing anxiety\. The multivariate effect of instructional method was significant, Wilks’ Λ = 0\.80, F\(4, 144\) = 7\.85, p &lt; \.001, η² = 0\.20; follow\-up ANCOVAs indicated that the experimental group reported significantly lower writing anxiety and significantly higher intrinsic motivation, creativity, and multiliteracy awareness than the control group \(all p &lt; \.001\)\. A researcher\-developed, 24\-item process\-perception questionnaire, resolved by exploratory factor analysis into four sub\-dimensions \(perceived cognitive effort, emotional comfort, task clarity, and creativity support\), was additionally administered to the experimental group only, to help describe the cognitive and affective process underlying these outcomes\. Qualitative data from weekly reflective design journals and end\-of\-treatment reflections, analyzed thematically, converged with the quantitative results, suggesting that visual\-digital instruction reduced participants’ sense of linguistic pressure and supported creative agency\.

## [Is physical climate risk priced in India’s financial sector? A monthly index approach, 2014–2024](../publications/a54eccb8b5d52e87029b.md)

M\. K\. Maneesha; N Saravanabhavan

Floods, cyclones and heatwaves are no longer viewed as humanitarian crises; they also have significant financial implications by affecting borrowers’ ability to repay loans, increasing potential liabilities of insurers and influencing how investors assess and price financial risks\. Whether financial markets actually respond to this physical climate risk remains an open question, particularly in emerging economies like India, where climate exposure is high but market\-based evidence is scarce\. This paper tests whether physical climate risk is reflected in the equity returns of India’s financial services sector, using a new monthly Climate Risk Index \(CRI\) constructed from disaster data spanning February 2014 to December 2024\. Using multiple methods, average effect regression, distribution analysis, structural break test and causality tests, we find no statistically significant relationship between physical climate risk and financial returns\. A concentrated effect at the lower\-middle quantile of the return distribution does not survive exclusion of a single extreme observation, and a structural break detected around India’s 2022 climate\-disclosure reforms is not specific to the climate\-risk relationship itself\. Financial\-sector returns do, however, predict subsequent movements in the Climate Risk Index, suggesting shared exposure to broader economic conditions rather than a reverse\-causal effect\. These findings do not mean climate risk is unpriced in India’s financial system\. They suggest instead that the current aggregate, monthly\-level measurement may not be capturing where that pricing occurs\. The study contributes a novel India\-specific Climate Risk Index and a multi\-method framework for testing climate\-risk pricing, offering a tool that regulators such as the RBI and SEBI can use to assess whether disclosure mandates are translating into actual market pricing\.

## [Re\-Engineering General Foundation Mathematics for STEM Readiness in Oman: A Curriculum Alignment and Comparative Readiness Analysis](../publications/a556eef0550e012c10cf.md)

Dheva Rajan S; Mini Punnolli; Asim Thabit Talib Almaamari; Madhan Narayanan

A basic mathematical foundation, as part of a knowledge\-based educational framework aligned with Oman Vision 2040, could serve as the intellectual foundation for STEM development\. The Mathematics course in the General Foundation Program \(GFP\) at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences \(UTAS\) is vital for students planning to pursue fields such as information technology, artificial intelligence, engineering, and data science\. However, concerns remain significant as the program focuses on procedural skills and is less focused on analytical reasoning and modeling\. The CDP has a digital math literacy component, but it is limited\. None of the previous attempts to assess structured curriculum mapping has proven effective\. Through structured curriculum mapping and a comparative readiness analysis, this study examines Course Learning Outcomes, Course Objectives, assessment plans, course delivery strategies, and proposed revisions aligned with a 10\-dimensional STEM Readiness Framework\. It also considers the spread of Bloom&\#x27;s taxonomy\. The paper notes observed alignment gaps, graphically documents them, and benchmarks insights from Harvard University’s mathematics pathways against policy recommendations\. Results demonstrated around 70% agreement in content but also highlighted discrepancies between evaluation and instruction in two specific areas: modeling and decision\-making under uncertainty, as well as digital exploration\. Even though the same applies to the requirements for using general skills for knowledge, in the higher cognitive sphere, these limitations are even more severe\. Proposed revisions include strengthened analytical and practical competencies, moving from bridge to cognitive enhancement\. Advancing IT and engineering readiness, incorporating the IT cum technology\-oriented concepts in mathematics, will help sustain existing STEM growth here\.

## [Integrating infrared thermography, behavioral assessment, and meat quality analysis to evaluate the effects of environmental enrichment in broiler chickens](../publications/a569428564ab56028f23.md)

Roberto Carlos Hernández\-Sánchez; Francisco Ernesto Martínez\-Castañeda; Juan Omar Hernández\-Ramírez; Monica Paola Salcedo\-Gómez; Victor\-Manuel Díaz\-Sánchez; Daniela Guadalupe Valencia\-Viramonte; Iván Gerardo Olivares\-Hernández; Janeli Solís\-Garfias; María L\. Zambrano‐Zaragoza; Elein Hernández

Introduction Environmental enrichment \(EE\) is used in broiler production to improve welfare, but findings on design preferences, behavior, production, and meat quality are heterogeneous\. An integrative approach combining live and postmortem assessments may clarify the EE effects\. This study evaluated the effects of different EE models on leg health, behavior, and meat quality in broilers\. Methods Three hundred one\-day\-old Cobb 500 broilers were reared under commercial conditions until 49 days of age \(DOA\)\. At 21 DOA, birds were randomly allocated into three blocks \(n=100\), each containing four groups \(n=25\): Control, Perch 1 level \(Perch 1L\), Perch 2 level \(Perch 2L\), and Platform\. Body weight was recorded weekly\. The birds’ behavior was assessed at 28 and 42 DOA\. Infrared thermography of the left and right intertarsal articulations and plantar surfaces was performed at 21 and 49 DOA\. After slaughter, the chickens’ thigh meat was evaluated for texture, pH, color \(L\*, a\*, b\*\), electrical conductivity \(EC\), and water\-holding capacity \(WHC\) on days post\-slaughter \(DPS\)\) 0, 1, 2, 7, 10, and 15, depending on the parameter\. Results EE did not affect final body weight\. Thermography showed age\-related decreases in superficial temperatures of intertarsal articulations and plantar surfaces; however, Perch 2L showed temperature changes suggestive of lesions\. The Platform was the least\-used EE, while other behavioral patterns were unaffected\. Meat quality differed among groups in pH \(DPS 0 and 10\), L\* \(DPS 7\), a\* \(DPS 2\), and WHC \(DPS 15\), particularly between Control and Perch 2L\. Differences across storage time were observed for pH \(Control, Perch 2L, and Platform\), L\* \(Perch 1L\), a\* \(Platform\), EC \(Perch 1L\), and WHC \(all treatments\)\. Discussion EE use declined with age, and preference appeared influenced by design characteristics such as material, height, and dimensions\. Perch 2L may have been associated with an inflammatory response, whereas the Platform may have functioned primarily as an obstacle\. Perch 2L and Platform improved WHC, potentially indicating differences in muscle development\. Overall, EE did not affect live weight, but influenced selected behaviors, leg health, and meat quality, highlighting the need for an integrative assessment when evaluating EE in broiler production\.
