## [From Single\-Modal Signal Recognition to Multidimensional Precision Detection: Breakthroughs and Innovations of Multi\-Modal Sensors in Tumor Biomarker Detection](../publications/a5743106a292225f90d8.md)

Ruimiao Chang; Jin Wang; Yong Li; Shuai Jia; Liping Li; Ruiping Zhang

The sensitive detection of tumor markers is of great significance for clinical diagnosis\. Due to the extremely low abundance of early tumor biomarkers and severe background interference from biological matrices, traditional single\-modal atomolar biological testing generally has limitations such as high false positives and narrow linear ranges, making it difficult to meet the clinical needs of precise diagnosis and treatment\. This has driven the iterative development of biosensing technology from a single signal readout mode to multi\-modal collaborative analysis, significantly improving the sensitivity and accuracy of complex biological sample detection\. Dual\-modal sensors integrate two complementary sensing mechanisms, whereas multi\-modal sensors produce three or more independent signal outputs\. By combining such mechanisms, for example electrochemistry and optics, these platforms can establish a signal cross\-validation and self\-calibration detection system\. This multidimensional analysis strategy can mitigate interference caused by environmental factors and human operational errors to a certain extent, lowering detection limits and broadening the linear range, thereby potentially providing higher\-reliability data support for early tumor diagnosis\. This work systematically reviews the technological evolution and performance differences in tumor biomarker sensors from single\-mode to multi\-mode in recent years, with a focus on summarizing the cutting\-edge research progress in this field\. It provides a comprehensive reference for researchers and facilitates further applications of multi\-modal sensors in point\-of\-care detection, and artificial intelligence\-assisted analysis\.

## [Group emotion awareness in socially shared regulation of learning: a conceptual framework and process model](../publications/a578f5ffbae3c7e9ba52.md)

Jiawen Chen; Xiangdong Chen; Sihan Song; Chen Guo; Chunlei Liang; Ruijun Zhao

In collaborative learning environments, fostering positive emotional experiences and effective emotional management is of paramount importance for creating a supportive and productive learning atmosphere\. A fundamental prerequisite for achieving this goal is the cultivation of timely and effective emotional awareness within collaborative groups\. A growing body of research suggests that group emotional awareness during the collaborative process is critical to both the quality of team interaction and Socially Shared Regulation of Learning \(SSRL\)\. Drawing upon the characteristics of SSRL, this study proposes a conceptual framework for group emotional awareness by analyzing the specific emotional information required across different stages of shared regulation and their respective functional dimensions\. To integrate emotional awareness into the SSRL process, this paper further constructs a corresponding process model and achieves its practical embedding through the design of instructional scaffolding and the integration of existing technological tools\. Addressing the research question of how to implement group emotional awareness models in collaborative scenarios, this study adopts a theory\-driven evidence\-chain synthesis approach to integrate representative empirical findings\. It synthesizes key conditions and process evidence—ranging from the externalization of emotional cues and shared interpretation to the formation of shared problem representations—thereby elucidating the feasible paths and applicable boundaries of the proposed model in supporting learners to enhance emotional awareness and conduct emotional attribution inquiries\. Moving beyond previous research that predominantly focused on emotional measurement techniques or tool development, this paper advances the implementation framework for group emotional awareness in collaborative learning from the dual perspectives of theoretical modeling and evidence\-chain support\.

## [A critical review of barriers to achieving net\-zero emissions in the information technology\-enabled services sector](../publications/a5840985e3b0250c0469.md)

Suhasini Jindal; Harshita Jain; Lovepreet Singh

Information Technology\-Enabled Services \(ITeS\) have typically been viewed as producing less carbon emissions than sectors that are energy\- and material\-intensive\. However, the rapid expansion of cloud computing, data centres, artificial intelligence, platform\-based services, and globally distributed digital operations is increasing the sector’s electricity demand and associated greenhouse gas emissions\. This systematic review synthesises 78 studies to identify the principal barriers that constrain the transition of the ITeS sector towards net\-zero emissions\. The review finds five recurring and interdependent barriers: the high energy intensity of digital infrastructure, dependence on carbon\-intensive electricity grids, insufficient sector\-specific carbon accounting and reporting, fragmented policy and regulatory incentives, and weak corporate commitment and stakeholder alignment\. The analysis also highlights the importance of Scope 3 emissions, particularly those linked to ICT hardware, cloud services, semiconductor supply chains, telecommuting, and e\-waste\. In response, the review identifies key transition pathways, including energy\-efficient infrastructure, renewable electricity procurement, carbon intelligence platforms, circular ICT practices, science\-based target\-setting, supplier engagement, and climate\-smart digital infrastructure\. By integrating these findings through a systems perspective, the study contributes a sector\-specific understanding of how technical, organisational, policy, and governance barriers interact to delay decarbonisation\. The review provides practical implications for ITeS organisations, policymakers, and researchers seeking to strengthen carbon accountability, prioritise high\-impact interventions, and accelerate credible net\-zero transitions in the digital services economy\.

## [AI literacy: Gen Z expectations vs\. organisational practices in India&\#x27;s dynamic job market](../publications/a592f96514aa8595d097.md)

Kumkum Tripathi; Aastha Patidar; Shine David

The mismatch between Generation Z&\#x27;s \(Gen Z\) high expectations of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and organisational AI practices has profound implications for vocational well\-being in India&\#x27;s job market\. This research explores the structural path between Gen Z’s AI Expectations, Organisational AI Practices, and AI Literacy\-Driven Vocational Well\-being, with Skills Velocity as a key contextual variable in a rapidly changing, technology\-driven landscape\.This research used a mixed\-methods approach\. A structured questionnaire was administered to 203 Gen Z professionals and HR managers in AI\-heavy industries \(IT, BFSI and manufacturing\) in Tier\-1 and Tier\-2 cities in India\. Structural Equation Modelling \(SEM\) using the lavaan package in R was used to test the path model\. We triangulated our findings with 20 semi\-structured interviews\. The sample was skewed towards males \(70:30 male\-to\-female\) and non\-normal\.Based on the findings, the model fit was satisfactory\. Gen Z&\#x27;s AI Expectations positively impacted Organisational AI Practices \(β = 0\.608, p &lt; \.001\) and AI Literacy\-driven Vocational Well\-being \(β = 0\.449, p &lt; \.001\)\. Organisational AI Practices also significantly and positively influenced Vocational Well\-being \(β = 0\.418, p &lt; \.001\)\. The variance in Organisational AI Practices and Vocational Well\-being explained by the model was 36\.9% and 60\.4%, respectively\.The research suggests that matching organisational AI practices to Gen Z expectations is crucial to improving AI literacy\-based vocational well\-being in India&\#x27;s ever\-evolving labour market\. The findings reveal the important role of Gen Z as a driver for change in organisations and the need for forward\-looking, skills\-velocity\-sensitive human resource management strategies such as AI upskilling and training, ethical AI policies and lifelong learning opportunities to enhance retention and workforce preparedness\.

## [A design space for AI integration in early\-stage production plant planning](../publications/a59f528aa5f20b64aaed.md)

Sibel Talyat Hyusmen; Jürgen Bock

Early\-stage production plant planning is characterised by evolving requirements, incomplete process definitions, and information distributed across documents, engineering models, and planning tools\. Introducing artificial intelligence in this setting raises a fundamental question: what must be considered before a specific application, data model, or technical solution can be defined? Existing research typically starts from an already identified planning task, a selected artificial intelligence method, or an available technical infrastructure\. It therefore provides limited guidance for structuring the initial need and determining how artificial intelligence should enter planning work\. This paper develops a design space that addresses this early decision problem\. Literature from factory planning, production planning, collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence, semantic technologies, and digital planning was compared to derive five dimensions: planning scope, information structure, authority to modify planning results, connection to planning tools and data, and functional contribution\. Data quality, organisational roles, governance, and interaction are considered as additional conditions\. Application to process failure mode and effects analysis shows how the appropriate configuration changes as preliminary process information develops into a maintained planning record\. The design space helps planners, artificial\-intelligence specialists, and system engineers specify implementation requirements before selecting a particular technical solution\.

## [The social influence ecosystem and foreign language proficiency among students in higher education institutions in Malaysia](../publications/a5a81e659f58beeec51a.md)

Nur Najmina Najwa Mat Noor; Mohd Mahzan Awang

Foreign language proficiency has become increasingly important in higher education, as graduates are expected to communicate effectively across cultures, adapt to the global labour market, and establish international academic and professional networks\. Nevertheless, the level of foreign language proficiency among university students continues to vary despite their participation in formal foreign language courses\. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the social influence ecosystem, encompassing family support, peer influence, lecturers, and digital media, and its relationship with foreign language proficiency among students in higher education institutions \(HEIs\) in Malaysia\. To achieve this objective, the study employed a quantitative approach using a survey research design\. A total of 464 HEI students enrolled in foreign language courses participated as respondents\. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 29 through descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analysis\. The findings revealed that the level of social influence was high, whereas the level of foreign language proficiency was moderate\. Furthermore, the correlation analysis indicated a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between social influence and foreign language proficiency\. These findings demonstrate that support from family, peers, lecturers, and digital media plays a crucial role in fostering students&\#x27; motivation, confidence, and opportunities to use foreign languages\. From a theoretical perspective, the study reinforces Vygotsky&\#x27;s Sociocultural Theory and Gardner&\#x27;s Socio\-Educational Model, both of which emphasise the importance of social interaction and motivation in language acquisition\. In terms of practical implications, the study recommends that higher education institutions expand collaborative learning, authentic communication activities, and the integration of digital media to enhance students&\#x27; foreign language proficiency\.

## [Multiclass Software Defect Prediction Using an Optimized LLM CodeSentinel\-BERT Based Framework](../publications/a5b933ec228afa0297df.md)

Vijayarajan S M\.; Ponnalagar V\.; Ravikrishnan R\.; Sarguna Gokul R\.

The prediction of software defects is important to detect defects in source codes prior to their deployment but traditional techniques use selected features and limited binary classification\. This research work proposes DefectGuard, a transformer\-based multiclass software defect prediction system for C/C\+\+ source code that utilizes CodeBERT fine\-tuning\. This custom dataset consists of 2,000 samples of manually collected and labeled C/C\+\+ source codes and includes nine classes of defects, namely syntax, semantic, logic, linker, and runtime\-related defects\. The proposed pipeline includes preprocessing, stratified splitting, sub\-word tokenization, CodeBERT representation learning, and multiclass classification\. The experimental results show the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1\-score of 98\.8%, 96\.4%, 95\.8%, and 96\.1%, respectively, on the test set\. Additionally, ROC\-AUC and confusion\-matrix metrics are used to evaluate the class\-level discrimination\. Moreover, the proposed model is implemented in a real\-time Flask\-based web application, which can classify the source code into defect labels with confidence scores and language detection to provide the interpretation feedback\.

## [INFLUENCE OF POLYPROPYLENE IMPLANTS COATED WITH TANTALUM AND ITS DERIVATIVES ON INFLAMMATION AND REGENERATION PROCESSES](../publications/a5ce49a892123c54af77.md)

O\. V\. Kyslov; Оксана Анатоліївна Наконечна; Liudmyla D Popova; С\. А\. Денисенко; Ievgen Ivanov

Introduction\. Polypropylene implants are widely used in surgical practice; however, some authors point to numerous postoperative complications after their use, the main cause of which is the development of aseptic inflammation\. This necessitates the search for effective anti\-inflammatory coatings\.Aim\. To evaluate the influence of polypropylene implants coated with tantalum and its derivatives on inflammation and regeneration processes\.Materials and methods\. The study used 40 male rats, divided into 6 groups: intact \(1\); with surgical intervention without an implant \(2\); with an uncoated polypropylene implant \(3\); with a tantalum\-coated implant \(4\); with a tantalum pentoxide\-coated implant \(5\); with a tantalum nitride\-coated implant \(6\)\. Morphological and immunohistochemical studies were performed\.Results\. In rats of groups 3 and 6, pronounced neutrophilic infiltration, purulent exudate, and a thin layer of immature granulation tissue were detected\. Multinucleated foreign body giant cells were often observed in the granulation tissue\. In rats of groups 4 and 5, neutrophilic infiltration was absent, granulation tissue was mature, and its layer thickness was one\-third greater compared to groups 3 and 6\. In rats of groups 4 and 5, a greater number of Ki\-67 positive and a smaller number of p53 positive cells were detected, and a higher proliferative\-apoptotic ratio \(Ki\-67/p53\) was found compared to rats of groups 3 and 6\.Conclusions\. Polypropylene implant induces aseptic inflammation, leading to increased apoptosis and decreased regeneration\. Coating the implant with tantalum or tantalum pentoxide prevents inflammation, reduces apoptosis, and increases cell proliferation\. Coating the implant with tantalum nitride does not change it, while coating with tantalum or tantalum pentoxide improves its biointegration\.

## [Efficient CPU\-GPU collaborative MoE inference via Adaptive Expert Assignment](../publications/a5ddfbacbbf75b25bc4f.md)

Wenhui Lv; Yunming Liao; Hongli Xu; Yang Xu; Junhao Cheng

Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) models reduce inference computation through sparse expert activation, but their large expert memory footprint often exceeds GPU capacity, making expert offloading necessary for memory\-constrained inference\. However, existing systems typically handle GPU\-missed experts by either transferring them to the GPU, incurring substantial PCIe transfer latency, or executing them on the CPU, making the slower CPU computation the bottleneck\. To address these limitations, we present \\method, a CPU\-GPU collaborative MoE inference system that adaptively assigns these missed experts to the CPU or GPU for efficient execution\. By exploiting differences in expert token\-loads, \\method selectively transfers high\-load experts to the GPU while executing low\-load experts on the CPU\. To minimize inference latency, \\method adaptively adjusts expert assignments to balance the CPU computation path against the GPU transfer\-and\-computation path, allowing both execution paths to complete as early as possible\. Extensive experiments on three representative MoE LLMs show that \\method improves prefill speed by up to 51\.9\\% and decode throughput by up to 39\.5\\% over the strongest baseline across the evaluated batch sizes, with consistent gains under different GPU\-memory budgets\.

## [Dexmedetomidine Evaluation for Reducing Cognitive Complications after Neurosurgery \(DECCAN\) \- Study Protocol of a Randomised Controlled Trial](../publications/a5dfa9e203451b7300b2.md)

Sriganesh Kamath; Suparna Bharadwaj; Sangeetha Akula; Sahana Raj Kandiraju; Nishant Sadashiva; Shantala Hegde; N\. Nandakumar; Monojit Debnath

Background: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders of Emergence Delirium \(ED\), Postoperative Delirium \(POD\), delayed Neurocognitive Recovery \(dNCR\), and postoperative Neurocognitive Disorder \(pNCD\) occur with varying incidences after anaesthesia and surgery\. Considering their adverse impact on patient outcomes, several interventions are being explored\. Dexmedetomidine has shown promise in reducing perioperative stress and lowering the incidence of POD\. This study aimed to compare intraoperative dexmedetomidine versus saline infusion for postoperative cognitive complications after brain surgery\. Methods: This prospective, single\-centre, randomised controlled trial, funded by the Department of Science and Technology, India, was conducted in adult patients undergoing elective brain surgery under general anaesthesia over a 3\-year period\. Intraoperative dexmedetomidine started at 0\.5 μg/kg/h was compared to saline infusion at a similar infusion rate after standard anaesthetic induction\. A block randomisation was performed using a computer\-generated random number table with a 1:1 allocation ratio\. Patients, anesthesiologists, data collectors, and analysts were blinded to study interventions\. Results: This trial was approved by the institute&\#x27;s ethics committee and is registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, and eligible patients are recruited\. The primary outcomes are the incidence of ED within the first 60 minutes and the incidence of POD within the first 3 postoperative days\. Secondary outcomes included postoperative sleep, biomarkers of surgical stress, acute and chronic pain, dNCR, pNCD, and quality of life at 1, 3, and 6 months\. Conclusions: It is anticipated that dexmedetomidine will reduce adverse postoperative cognitive outcomes\. The findings will be disseminated through conference presentations and scientific publications\.

## [Al\-Qur’an dan Keseimbangan Antara Artificial Intelligence dan Spiritual Intelligence: Rekonstruksi Tekno\-Spiritualitas dalam Perspektif Quranic Worldview](../publications/a5eb71b0de89a551f0c1.md)

Mohammad Nizar; Ahmad Zain Sarnoto

Ekskalasi teknologi kecerdasan buatan \(Artificial Intelligence/AI\) pada era modernitas akhir telah membawa transformasi multidimensional yang tidak hanya menyentuh aspek teknis\-utilitarian, melainkan merambah ranah eksistensial, antropologis, dan epistemologis manusia\. Kecenderungan peradaban modern yang didominasi oleh cara berpikir belahan otak kiri yang bercorak mekanistis, kalkulatif, dan reduksionis berisiko mengikis kesadaran transendental serta memicu krisis kehampaan spiritualitas \(spiritual emptiness\)\. Artikel jurnal tingkat doktoral ini bertujuan merekonstruksi secara komprehensif paradigma keseimbangan antara Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) dan Spiritual Intelligence \(SI\) melalui kacamata pandangan hidup Al\-Qur&\#x27;an \(Quranic Worldview\)\. Menggunakan metode tafsir tematik konseptual \(maudhu’i\) yang diintegrasikan dengan hermeneutika filosofis dan pendekatan maqāṣid al\-syarī‘ah, penelitian ini membedah status ontologis, batas epistemologis, dan orientasi aksiologis AI dan SI\. Eksplorasi teks suci difokuskan pada dialog arketipikal kekhalifahan Nabi Adam as\. dan kritik teknofetisisme patung anak sapi emas Samiri, yang diperkuat dengan analisis eksegetis terhadap beberapa ayat ayng lain\. Penelitian ini juga merumuskan pilar\-pilar kecerdasan spiritual Qur&\#x27;ani: kesadaran diri, transendensi, makna hidup, nilai etis, dan kesadaran holistik\. Hasil kajian menyimpulkan bahwa AI secara ontologis berstatus instrumen profan aksidental \(khādim\) yang terikat pada hukum komputasi simbolik dan probabilistik, sehingga klaim transhumanisme mengenai kesadaran mesin \(ensoulment\) ditolak secara mutlak karena ketiadaan hembusan rūḥ ilahiah dan fakultas qalb\. Keseimbangan peradaban tercapai manakala lompatan AI ditundukkan di bawah kepemimpinan aksiologis SI yang berakar pada tauhid, keadilan \(‘adl\), kemaslahatan \(maṣlaḥah\), dan kesadaran human\-in\-the\-loop, guna mengarahkan sains menuju terwujudnya martabat manusia seutuhnya \(al\-insān al\-kāmil\)\.

## [Local Skill Exchange Network: An AI\-Powered Location\-Based Platform for Skill Sharing and Personalized Learning](../publications/a5efab29cb88c0a8b984.md)

Vanita Zambare Vaishnavi Navale; Mrs\. Manisha Aswale Pranjal Khambekar

The Local Skill Exchange Network is a proposed web\-based platform designed to connect individuals who want to learn new skills with people who possess relevant knowledge and expertise\. Traditional learning platforms often focus on structured courses, while local communities may have difficulty discovering nearby individuals who can provide personalized guidance or participate in reciprocal skill exchanges\. The proposed system addresses this challenge by integrating skill discovery, location\-based search, intelligent recommendations, session booking, real\-time communication, online payments, and a skill barter mechanism into a unified application\. Users can register as skill providers, learners, or both, create skill profiles, specify availability, and search for suitable learning opportunities\. The recommendation module ranks potential matches using factors such as skill relevance, geographical proximity, ratings, price, experience, and availability\. Google Maps integration supports geographical discovery, while a payment gateway facilitates paid sessions\. The barter module enables users to exchange skills without requiring monetary transactions\. Administrative and moderation modules support user management, content review, dispute handling, and platform analytics\. The proposed application follows a modular monolithic architecture with a web frontend, backend REST APIs, and a relational database\. The system aims to improve access to community\-based learning, encourage knowledge sharing, and provide a scalable foundation for personalized skill development\. Its effectiveness can be evaluated through functional testing, recommendation relevance, booking success rate, response time, and user feedback

## [Dual\-energy computed tomography pulmonary angiography for pulmonary embolism: a three\-tier evidence framework to guide individualized low\-iodine scanning](../publications/a600b1108d0fa0662b22.md)

Qinwei Jiang; long Qian

Dual\-energy computed tomography \(DECT\) pulmonary angiography \(CTPA\) is widely studied for pulmonary embolism \(PE\) evaluation, but heterogeneity in protocols, platforms, and study designs complicates its clinical positioning\. This narrative review, with structured search elements adapted from the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses 2020, synthesized evidence from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure \(January 2016\-June 2026\); 28 studies were eligible \(26 of 1,287 screened records and 2 identified through citation tracing\)\. Evidence was organized into a three\-tier framework \(image quality, diagnostic performance, and clinical outcomes\)\. Low\-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging at 40\-50 keV improves vascular attenuation and enables iodine load reduction to approximately 6 g in selected protocols\. Pooled meta\-analytic evidence shows no consistent diagnostic advantage of DECT over single\-energy CT\. The right ventricular/left ventricular diameter ratio remains the most stable prognostic indicator; DECT perfusion metrics have not surpassed it for mortality prediction\. Iodine\-map hypoperfusion in distal arteries is suspicious for, but not morphologically confirmed as, subsegmental PE; such findings carry a risk of overdiagnosis and warrant caution before anticoagulation\. A body mass index\- and estimated glomerular filtration rate\-stratified protocol table with Oxford Centre for Evidence\-Based Medicine 2011 evidence\-level annotations is provided, and knowledge gaps in photon\-counting CT, artificial intelligence, and cross\-platform standardization are identified\.

## [СИСТЕМА СУБ’ЄКТІВ ПУБЛІЧНОГО АДМІНІСТРУВАННЯ У СФЕРІ ВПРОВАДЖЕННЯ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ В МЕДИЦИНІ](../publications/a60e75085d487166bc8c.md)

Андрій Вікторович Сидорук

У статті на основі аналізу конституційних положень і галузевого законодавства України досліджується формування системи суб’єктів публічного адміністрування у сфері впровадження технологій штучного інтелекту в медицину\. Метою дослідження є визначення інституційної структури публічного адміністрування, спроможної забезпечити нормативне, організаційне й управлінське супроводження процесів цифровізації охорони здоров’я\. Автор окреслює потенційне коло органів публічної влади, які відповідно до чинного законодавства можуть входити до системи суб’єктів публічного адміністрування у зазначеній сфері, зокрема органи виконавчої влади та органи місцевого самоврядування\. З огляду на проведений аналіз обґрунтовується багаторівнева модель інституційної організації публічного адміністрування, що охоплює центральний, галузевий, регіональний і локальний рівні реалізації державної політики у сфері охорони здоров’я\. За результатами дослідження зроблено висновок про необхідність формування узгодженого адміністративно\-правового механізму регулювання цифровізації медицини та впровадження технологій штучного інтелекту, що має забезпечувати ефективну координацію діяльності суб’єктів публічного адміністрування та належні правові гарантії безпеки пацієнтів

## [NuXLApp : Interactive data analysis and visualization for protein‐nucleic acid crosslinking mass spectrometry](../publications/a62a8406c426d00c8b9e.md)

Arslan Siraj; Sergei A\. Moshkovskii; Tom David Müller; Henning Urlaub; Oliver Kohlbacher; Timo T\. Sachsenberg

Protein\-nucleic acid \(protein\-Nu\) interactions are crucial for many cellular processes and biological functions\. Crosslinking mass spectrometry \(XL\-MS\) has emerged as a powerful method for identifying these interactions\. However, the analysis of protein\-Nu XL\-MS data requires an integrated workflow from raw data processing to results inspection and validation\. Existing workflows for protein\-Nu XL\-MS often require switching between tools and considerable manual processing\. Here, we introduce NuXLApp, an interactive web\-based application for data processing and results visualization in protein\-Nu XL\-MS studies\. NuXLApp integrates the protein\-Nu crosslink search engine &quot;NuXL,&quot; machine\-learning models for peptide property prediction, and interactive result visualization within a reproducible workflow\. It enables rapid validation of false discovery rate\-controlled crosslink spectrum match\-level identifications and facilitates collaboration and intuitive exploration of experimental results\. In addition, NuXLApp generates a spectral library from identified protein\-Nu crosslinks to enable quantitative analysis of crosslinks using data\-independent acquisition \(DIA\)\. NuXLApp supports discovery\-driven identification of protein\-nucleic acid crosslinks and enables DIA\-based follow\-up experiments for their quantitative analysis\. NuXLApp is open\-source and available via the OpenMS WebApps platform at https://nuxl\.webapps\.openms\.de/\.

## [Competitive phenotype and metabolite repertoire of the endophytic Diaporthe sp\. PBS30\-7](../publications/a62c3df2cd19a979d9b7.md)

Ling Yang; Chuancheng Wei

Endophytic fungi represent potential sources of antifungal agents, but the phenotypic and chemical basis of their interactions with competing fungi remains incompletely understood\. Here, physiological characterization, time\-resolved confrontation assays, cell\-free culture\-filtrate testing, untargeted chemical profiling, and molecular docking were integrated to characterize the competitive phenotype of the endophytic fungus Diaporthe sp\. PBS30\-7, isolated from the medicinal plant Pereskia bleo \(Kunth\) DC\., and to prioritize candidate metabolites for subsequent investigation\. Diaporthe sp\. PBS30\-7 exhibited condition\-dependent growth and a temporally asymmetric competitive phenotype against two Penicillium species, characterized by sustained colony expansion, progressive restriction of target\-fungal growth, and pronounced hyphal abnormalities\. Cell\-free culture filtrates retained antifungal activity against both target fungi, supporting a contribution of extracellular chemical factors to the overall antagonistic phenotype\. Feature\-based molecular networking of a culture\-associated agar–mycelium extract resolved a chemically diverse repertoire that included putatively annotated beauvericin\-type cyclodepsipeptides, diketopiperazines, and unresolved molecular families\. Molecular docking further prioritized this candidate chemical space, with beauvericin derivatives displaying particularly favorable target\-dependent docking profiles toward CYP51, Fks1, and the ABC transporter, whereas cyclo\(L\-Tyr\-L\-Tyr\) emerged as a notable diketopiperazine candidate\. Together, these findings prioritize candidate metabolites potentially associated with the competitive phenotype of Diaporthe sp\. PBS30\-7 and provide a foundation for future mechanistic studies of endophytic fungal antagonism\.

## [ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN INVESTMENT DECISIONS](../publications/a62d1edb2ff1893b8a47.md)

Shakthipriya R V; Dr\. D\. Sumathi

Investment behaviour has changed as a result of artificial intelligence \(AI\), which replaces human judgment with data\-driven insights\. Investors may analyse big information, spot trends, and optimize portfolios with the help of technologies like machine learning, robo\-advisors, and predictive analytics, increasing productivity and lowering emotional biases\. Adoption of AI is not without its difficulties, though, such as algorithmic bias, a lack of transparency, expensive costs, and problems with data quality\. Automation bias and market volatility may increase if automated systems are overused\. This study highlights AI’s impact on investor behaviour and emphasizes the importance of a balanced, responsible approach to effectively integrate AI into investment decision\-making processes\.

## [Deep learning\-based profanity detection in social media: a survey in the context of toxic language detection](../publications/a62f8ac5679e29495bed.md)

Luong Vuong Nguyen; Dang Huy Le; Van Hon Nguyen; Thuy\-Trang PHAM; Rin Vy Nguyen; O‐Joun Lee

The spread of toxic and profane language across online platforms has necessitated the development of advanced automated detection systems to maintain safe online environments\. This survey comprehensively explores the progression of profanity language detection techniques, focusing on datasets, feature extraction methods, and model architectures\. Through a thorough examination of key developments in the field, the study outlines the evolution of detection systems across four distinct phases\. It offers a taxonomy of approaches that have shaped the current landscape\. We review various high\-performing models, highlighting their effectiveness in addressing challenges such as context understanding, multilingual data, and identifying subtle forms of toxicity\. The article further explores the strengths of these models, including their ability to capture long\-range dependencies and nuanced features, while also discussing their limitations, such as computational efficiency and generalization across datasets\. By analyzing the current state of toxic language detection and the latest advancements in feature extraction and modeling techniques, we provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners\. Additionally, the article outlines future research directions, emphasizing the importance of lightweight, adaptive models and real\-time optimization techniques to enable scalable, practical deployment across diverse platforms and environments\.

## [Wireless bioelectronic control architectures for muscle\-powered biohybrid robotic systems](../publications/a632f4cfef1ba46903f5.md)

Hiroyuki Tetsuka; Minoru Hirano

Wireless bioelectronic interfaces are increasingly used to control tissue\-engineered, muscle\-powered biohybrid robotic systems\. However, a unifying engineering framework linking device design to system\-level control remains underdeveloped\. Here, we formulate wireless control in biohybrid robotics as a coupled co\-design problem integrating signal delivery, spatial selectivity, scalability, sensing and feedback, controller implementation, biological life support, and interface stability\. We analyze three representative actuation and control strategies\-wireless electrical stimulation, wireless optoelectronic stimulation, and neuromuscular integration\-which operate in distinct regimes with characteristic trade\-offs\. Across these modalities, the tissue\-device interface emerges as a key constraint governing the interplay among electrical or optical signal delivery, circuit performance, sensing, and biomechanical response\. We outline practical design principles spanning electromagnetic field distribution, circuit architecture, actuator mechanics, multi\-actuator addressing, and closed\-loop control\. Rather than treating neural organoids as an inevitable end point, we compare conventional electronic controllers, neuronal culture\-silicon interfaces, and organoid\-microelectrode array systems as alternative trajectories toward closed\-loop autonomy\. This system\-level perspective provides design guidelines for stable, scalable, and application\-driven biohybrid robotic systems\.

## [Reflections on the prospects for western Atlantic coral reefs](../publications/a64c0c6c76f016fc05c0.md)

Jeremy B\. C\. Jackson

Ever more frequent and severe heat waves and resulting coral bleaching threaten to drive reef corals to extinction unless they can rapidly increase resilience against rising temperatures\. This is especially true in the Western Atlantic where the unique geographic features of the region and long history of intense exploitation and pollution have made corals especially vulnerable\. Fortunately, there is considerable evidence that thermal resilience is increasing through shuffling of relationships among corals and their symbionts, and by natural selection\. Moreover, experiments have shown that assisted reproduction can increase the pace of increasing resilience\. However, these promising signs will come to naught unless overexploitation, pollution, and development are rapidly and severely reduced\.

## [MSFANet: a multi\-scale feature aggregation network for tobacco pest recognition](../publications/a64f6318947bafd5af7e.md)

Shun He; Sifan Li; Xinjian Li; Qianqian Luo; Dong Sufen; Lu Lei; Xingjiang Chen; Liuti Cai; Jian‐Yu Meng; Ning Lu; Hancheng Wang

Introduction Tobacco is a globally significant economic crop, and pest infestation represents one of the primary factors contributing to declines in both yield and quality\. However, tobacco pests encompass a wide variety of species that differ substantially in morphology and scale\. Field\-captured images are frequently subject to complex background interference and class imbalance, presenting considerable challenges for automated recognition\. Existing deep learning approaches remain limited in their capacity for multi\-scale feature extraction and discriminative feature representation under such conditions\. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi\-Scale Feature Aggregation Network \(MSFANet\) for tobacco pest recognition, formulated here as a single\-label image classification task\. Methods To address scale variation and complex field backgrounds, two task\-oriented modules were developed\. The Multi\-Scale Pyramid Pooling \(MSPP\) module aggregates contextual information across multiple receptive fields through parallel feature extraction and adaptive cross\-branch fusion\. The Hierarchical Feature Fusion Block \(HFFB\) subsequently refines the feature representations through spatial gating and partial convolution\. An auxiliary classification head and Focal Loss were incorporated during training to provide intermediate supervision and address class imbalance, respectively\. Results The effectiveness of MSFANet was evaluated on a dataset comprising 13 tobacco\-associated pest and natural\-enemy categories\. The model achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1\-score of 97\.63%, 97\.89%, 97\.59%, and 97\.71%, respectively, with a parameter count of 1\.21 M\. Among the models trained from random initialization, MSFANet shared the highest accuracy while using the fewest parameters\. Discussion By combining multi\-scale contextual aggregation with hierarchical feature refinement, MSFANet achieved accurate classification across the 13 tobacco\-associated categories under complex field conditions\. The proposed method provides effective technical support for automated and precision\-oriented pest monitoring in tobacco fields, offering practical value for advancing precise pest management and the broader development of smart agriculture\.

## [Diagnosing GNN Failure Modes with Layer\-Wise Probe Entropy](../publications/a651223b01f2dedd2f19.md)

Shanzi Bao; Mar Gonzàlez I Català; Pietro Liò

Graph neural networks \(GNNs\) are typically evaluated only at their final layer, obscuring how task\-relevant information evolves during message passing\. We introduce a post\-hoc diagnostic that freezes a trained GNN, fits an independent linear probe to each layer, and tracks probe accuracy alongside normalized predictive entropy\. Across real and synthetic graph settings, layer\-wise probe entropy distinguishes beneficial, neutral, and harmful smoothing, a capability not demonstrated by existing geometric measures\. Moreover, by comparing shallow and deep models, we show that the onset of entropy degradation separates the two main GNN failure modes: structural mismatch under heterophily, which appears from the earliest layers even in shallow models, and excessive\-depth oversmoothing, which emerges only as propagation depth increases\. These results establish probe\-entropy trajectories as a tool for analyzing information flow in GNNs and motivate future work on adaptive depth selection and early\-exit mechanisms\.

## [Is it psychologically dangerous to live in a rich area? Evidence from census\-matched micro data on UK suicides](../publications/a66837d2cfd9cbcab529.md)

Caspar Kaiser; Ekaterina Oparina; Andrew J\. Oswald

This paper uses micro data on UK suicides to implement a new test of relative\-deprivation theory\. Research into the potential consequences of relative comparisons had in the past had to rely on subjective data on wellbeing or on particular types of biomarker information\. With information that was released under strict confidentiality requirements by the Office for National Statistics, we here report the first econometric results that are able to draw upon full census\-matched micro\-level records with register data on suicides in the United Kingdom\. The paper’s key result is that suicide risk is greatest, ceteris paribus, in rich areas\. Thus the long\-standing belief that it is hazardous to live in a deprived place appears to be incorrect\. For reasons explained in the paper, we believe it is possible that our estimates may understate the extent of the suicide risk\.

## [Longitudinal Assessment of Fluoride Concentrations in Public Drinking Water Supplies in New Zealand: Implications for Epidemiological Studies](../publications/a670e196a12059ec357c.md)

Frank Dean; Tim James Chambers; Christina Pike; Matthew Hobbs; Jonathan Mark Broadbent

OBJECTIVES: To establish a national longitudinal database of fluoride concentrations in public drinking water supplies in New Zealand \(NZ\) and investigate the potential implications of different fluoride exposure classifications for epidemiological studies evaluating the effects of community water fluoridation \(CWF\) on population health outcomes\. METHODS: Fluoride concentrations in NZ public drinking water supplies were assessed longitudinally from 2000 to 2021\. Fluoride sample results obtained from all 67 Territorial Authorities and drinking water regulators were cleaned, standardised to water distribution zones \(WDZs\), aggregated to weekly values, and imputed where missing\. A synthetic birth cohort of 10 000 children followed from birth to age four was developed to simulate individual\-level fluoride exposure histories and evaluate different exposure classifications, including binary fluoridation status and mixed exposure resulting from residential mobility\. RESULTS: Fluoride concentrations in fluoridated WDZ had a median of 0\.74 mg/L \(range 0\.00\-1\.04\), while non\-fluoridated WDZ had consistently low fluoride concentrations \(median 0\.05 mg/L; range 0\.00\-0\.42\)\. Substantial temporal variability was observed, with only 40% of WDZ\-observation years having fluoride concentrations above 0\.7 mg/L for at least 90% of the year\. In the synthetic cohort, exposure misclassification arising from naturally occurring fluoride concentrations or sub\-optimal dosing appeared minimal\. In contrast, residential mobility between fluoridated and non\-fluoridated areas represented a more substantial source of potential bias, with approximately 30% of individuals experiencing mixed fluoridation exposure over 4 years\. CONCLUSION: The findings highlight the importance of longitudinal and quantitatively derived exposure measures for future research evaluating the oral health impacts of CWF\.

## [Unintended childbearing and child cognitive outcomes: does gender matter?](../publications/a6748b978359e34586c4.md)

Astghik Mavisakalyan; Rachma Indah Nurbani; Silvia Salazar

Abstract Do unintended pregnancies have implications for children’s cognitive outcomes, and does this vary by gender? We address this question using rich longitudinal data from Indonesia − a country where nearly 3 million in every 8 million annual pregnancies are estimated to be unintended\. Exploiting the random assignment of child gender, we identify a significant girl penalty specific to children born after an unintended pregnancy\. Although girls in Indonesia generally outperform boys on cognitive tests, girls born after an unintended pregnancy show lower numerical and language abilities during adolescence compared to boys born under the same circumstances, a gap not observed among intended children\. This penalty is robust to a wide range of household and child characteristics and to checks for selection on unobservables\. Potential mechanisms point to lower parental investment in girls relative to boys within the unintended group, reflected in reduced private school enrollment and poorer early childhood health\.

## [Machine Learning\-Enabled Behavioural Analytics for Cyber Threat Detection in SCADA\-Based Operational Technology Environments](../publications/a68c625c7d41b9056ff6.md)

A\. Chandra Sekaran

The integration of digital technologies in SCADA systems has made it easier to monitor and automate the industrial process, but at the same time, it has made the OT environment vulnerable to cyberattacks\. The OT environment based on SCADA systems has unique operational requirements, has heterogeneous devices, continuous flow of data, and also has safety considerations\. As a result, it becomes hard to detect any threats to the environment in a timely manner\. Conventional approaches of intrusion detection rely heavily on predefined rules, signatures, and static behavioral models that might not be enough to identify unknown attacks and behavioral changes in devices and networks\. In this research paper, an approach for detecting cyber threats using behavioral analytics through machine learning in SCADA\-based OT environments has been suggested using a combination of Liquid Neural Networks \(LNNs\), Hypergraph Neural Networks \(HGNNs\), and Deep Evidential Learning \(EDL\)\. The LNN is employed to capture the temporal changes in the behavior of the system through its operations and data flows\. The HGNN component is used to capture complex dependencies between devices, communication activities, network activities, and other interconnected entities in the OT environment, where conventional pairwise representation may fail to model dependencies between several entities\. Proposed framework examines behavioral patterns in SCADA\-related datasets and uses temporal patterns, high order dependencies, and evidential information to separate normal operational behavior from any potentially malicious behavior\. Evaluation of the proposed framework provided 97\.29% accuracy in identifying cyber threat patterns in the investigated SCADA\-based OT environment

## [Factors contributing to high\-performance competitive swimsuits: a review from materials science and engineering principles](../publications/a69a9a04b8754350e899.md)

Shengxuan Yuan

High\-performance competitive swimsuits are designed and manufactured to enhance athletic performance mainly through the combined effects of drag reduction and optimized body compression\. This review synthesizes current research on the key factors in high\-performance competitive swimsuits that enhance swimmers&\#x27; performance, including optimal fiber composition and proportion, warp\-knitting techniques, microfiber adoption, surface modification for enhanced hydrophobicity and drag reduction, compression systems, unimpeded thermal exchange, positive sensory and psychological feedback, and advanced manufacturing techniques such as ultrasonic welding and three\-dimensional cutting\. The analysis indicates that these factors do not operate in isolation but rather function as interdependent and coupled mechanisms, collectively contributing to improved performance, although the size of that contribution has not been quantified\. Nonetheless, a small number of factors involve trade\-offs that require careful balancing, although their overall influence appears to be relatively minor\. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the complex design principles of high\-performance competitive swimsuits and offers insights for future material innovation and engineering optimization\.

## [Toward a population\-level public health approach to support families living under continuous traumatic stress](../publications/a69bfdb0eb6dce538143.md)

Abigail H\. Gewirtz; Mor Keleynikov; Hadar Eliash; Nehama Lewis; Jessica Gale; Shir Itzhaky\-Wruble; Adena Hoffnung\-Assouline; Anastasia Viner

Since October 2023, families across Israel have been living under conditions of continuous traumatic stress \(CTS\): ongoing, unresolved threat due to repeated rounds of regional conflict\. Demand for mental health support has far outstripped the capacity of clinician\-delivered services, leaving many families without evidence\-based help\. This community case study describes the development and early implementation of ADAPT\-Israel\. To our knowledge, this is likely to be the first population\-level, parenting\-centered public health approach designed for families living under CTS\. The initiative uses a tiered model to provide parenting support across layers of care: \(i\) a universal layer of brief, trauma\-informed public health messages and a self\-directed, interactive online parenting program \(with an optional AI avatar guide\); \(ii\) a selective layer of facilitator\-delivered ADAPT groups for live higher\-risk families, beginning with families of long\-serving military reservists; and \(iii\) an indicated layer of individual telehealth support for families experiencing clinical levels of difficulty\. The approach adapts Adaptive Parenting Tools/ADAPT, an evidence\-based program grounded in Social Interaction Learning theory and validated in a different context – for military families in the United States across three randomized controlled trials with nearly 1,000 military families\. We describe the rationale, the methodology used to develop each tier, and early implementation experience\. Feasibility and acceptability indicators from initial pilot groups are promising, including high group completion and positive participant reports of improved parenting and family relationships, though these are small\-sample, self\-report, early\-stage findings rather than effectiveness evidence\. We discuss practical implications, lessons learned, and the model’s potential utility in settings of protracted conflict and chronic threat\.

## [Saint\-Bonnet Doppler waveform classification system: a scoping review and evidence\-based appraisal using AGREE II and AGREE\-REX](../publications/a69c7bc98284f5ed2cc9.md)

Hamidah Mabruk Alodayni; Alodaini Fatimah; Alun Davies; Pasha Normahani

Background Doppler waveform interpretation is central to the diagnosis and surveillance of lower limb peripheral arterial disease \(PAD\)\. Despite widespread clinical use of duplex ultrasound \(DUS\) and hand\-held Doppler \(HHD\), waveform terminology remains highly variable and non\-standardised across institutions\. The Saint\-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine \(CEMV\), offers a structured eight\-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity\. Its evidence base and methodological quality have never been formally appraised\. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta\-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews \(PRISMA\-ScR\)\. MEDLINE \(Ovid\) and Embase \(Ovid\) were searched from 1946 to November 2025\. Studies describing, applying, validating, or evaluating the Saint\-Bonnet classification were eligible\. Data were extracted using a standardised form\. Methodological quality was appraised using AGREE II \(six domains\) and AGREE\-REX \(three domains\), independently by two reviewers \(H\.A\. and F\.A\.\)\. Results Seven studies met the inclusion criteria; all published between 2017 and 2022 from a single French vascular research group\. The Saint\-Bonnet classification achieved a categorisation rate of 98\.2% across 1,033 waveforms, outperforming alternative systems\. Inter\-rater reliability was moderate \( κ ≈ 0\.55\)\. Waveform grade independently correlated with maximal walking distance, and waveform\-guided ankle–brachial index \(ABI\) selection achieved near\-perfect agreement with guideline standards \( κ up to 1\.00\)\. Automated neural network classification reached κ = 0\.79, approaching expert agreement\. AGREE II appraisal revealed high scores for Clarity of Presentation and Scope &amp; Purpose \(97% and 83%\), but low scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability \(44% and 40%\)\. AGREE\-REX demonstrated high Clinical Applicability and Implementability\. Conclusion The Saint\-Bonnet classification is a promising and practical framework for Doppler waveform interpretation, with consistent findings across the available studies\. Low AGREE II scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability reflect gaps in its documented development and reporting rather than evidence against its clinical performance\. However, all supporting evidence originates from a single, non\-independent French research group, and the classification has not undergone external validation; broader adoption should await independent, multicentre confirmation of these findings\.

## [Automated Segmentation of Wound Bed Tissue from Clinical Photographs: A Benchmark of Five Deep Learning Architectures Under a Shared Protocol](../publications/a6a16cbb90449ba61946.md)

David Reifs; Lorena Casanova\-Lozano; Jordi Solé‐Casals; Andrea Coda

Accurate characterisation of the wound bed, the relative proportions of granulation, slough and necrotic tissue described by the red\-yellow\-black model, is central to monitoring healing and guiding debridement in chronic\-wound care, yet in routine practice, it is judged visually and is poorly reproducible between clinicians\. We investigated automatic, pixel\-level segmentation of these three classes within the wound region of interest\. A corpus of 404 photographs was curated from a public wound image collection and densely annotated by wound care clinicians with a purpose\-built, cluster\-assisted labelling tool\. Five deep learning architectures spanning convolutional, transformer, hybrid and ensemble families were trained on one frozen data split under a largely shared pipeline, with limited, fully documented architecture\-specific tuning, and scored on a shared 62\-image test set\. The models fell within a narrow mean intersection\-over\-union band \(0\.748\-0\.818\)\. The strongest single model, a purely convolutional network, was statistically indistinguishable from the best ensemble, and simply averaging already\-trained convolutional and transformer models matched that ensemble at no additional training cost\. Slough remained consistently the hardest tissue\. Translated into clinical units, per\-wound tissue percentages were recovered with small mean bias \(within ± 5 percentage points\) but wide single\-image limits of agreement \(about ± 25\-50 percentage points\), so the measurement suits aggregate and longitudinal assessment rather than single\-image reading\. Within this dataset, split and training protocol, the choice among the strong hierarchical architectures was not decisive: a single strong model is the pragmatic option for clinical deployment, with an ensemble reserved for maximal accuracy and class balance\.

## [From Individual Songs to Music Corpora: Evaluating Explainable Harmonic Decision\-Making on HookTheory](../publications/a6ac70f5fd0d06bee40a.md)

Josef Pavlíček; Martin Pelikán

Automatic melody harmonization is often evaluated through individual compositions or data\-driven corpus models\. This study examines whether an explainable harmonic decision model developed for individual songs can be applied to independently collected human annotations without changing its rules\. We evaluate a frozen Explainable Melody Harmonizer \(EMH\) on selected HookTheory excerpts containing aligned melody and chord annotations\. EMH generates chord sequences from melody alone using explicit criteria for melodic compatibility, harmonic function, persistence, cadence, meter\-aware segmentation, and Viterbi\-like optimization\. Human chords are withheld during generation and used only for post\-hoc comparison\. Nineteen excerpts yielded 439 evaluable harmonic segments\. Exact chord agreement reached 20\.50%, chord\-root agreement 31\.66%, and harmonic\-function agreement 47\.62%, with functions assessed relative to the key inferred by EMH\. Decision\-level analysis identified 203 segments \(46\.24%\) where the human chord lay outside the model&\#x27;s candidate vocabulary and 146 \(33\.26%\) where it was available but not selected\. These findings distinguish representational limitations from differences in chord selection without treating the human reference as the only musically valid solution\. The study demonstrates a reproducible, interpretable approach to corpus\-based evaluation of harmonic decision\-making\.

## [Conditional Derivative GANs for Parameter\-Conditioned Synthesis of Gravitational Waves from Core\-Collapse Supernovae](../publications/a6b2471db5c01b80e14d.md)

Jossian A\. García; Vicente Sierra; Claudia Moreno; Javier Mauricio Antelis

Abstract Gravitational wave signals from core\-collapse supernovae encode critical astrophysical information, including key astrophysical parameters such as the ratio of rotational kinetic to gravitational potential energy at bounce, pre\-collapse differential rotation, and the nuclear equation of state\. However, the limited number of observed core\-collapse supernovae events makes it challenging to build robust data\-driven models\. The generation of synthetic gravitational wave signals from core\-collapse supernovae can therefore provide a valuable tool for data augmentation in machine learning pipelines, particularly for the training and testing of detection and parameter estimation algorithms\. Although recent efforts have explored the use of generative models to synthesize waveform\-like data, existing approaches lack the ability to condition outputs on specific astrophysical parameters\. To address this, we propose a model capable of generating gravitational wave signals conditioned on astrophysical parameters of core\-collapse supernovae rotation\. The proposed conditional derivative generative adversarial network is trained on the Richers et al\. catalog, which contains 1,824 simulated time\-series gravitational wave waveforms and their corresponding physical parameters\. Quantitative evaluation using time\-domain similarity and distributional metrics shows that the generated signals reproduce the key statistical and morphological features of the original dataset\. This work introduces a conditional generative framework for rotating core\-collapse supernovae gravitational wave signals, that enables fast, low\-cost data augmentation and parameterized modeling, improving ML\-based detection and parameter estimation\.

## [Análisis de Emparejamiento Óptimo: aplicaciones novedosas en la intersección entre la demografía y los estudios de cambio climático](../publications/a6b24a201e3c5a3d2f3a.md)

Karla Arlae Sánchez Guijosa; Guillermo Nicolás Murray Tortarolo; Mario Martínez Salgado

El cambio climático reconfigura los ecosistemas, las economías y las trayectorias de vida, pero la investigación rara vez captura su carácter dinámico y procesual\. Este artículo presenta una revisión conceptual y metodológica orientada a sintetizar y discutir el potencial del Análisis de Emparejamiento Óptimo \(OMA por sus siglas en inglés: Optimal Matching Analysis\) para el estudio de respuestas demográficas al cambio climático desde una perspectiva temporal\. A partir del análisis de las aplicaciones del OMA en demografía y estudios ambientales, se pudo observar que esta técnica permite identificar grupos socialmente vulnerables, integrar dimensiones temporales y espaciales en el análisis de la adaptación y vincular trayectorias de vida con variabilidad climática\. Asimismo, evidencia su utilidad para analizar procesos de movilidad, cambio de uso de suelo y salud en contextos de riesgo\. Se concluye que el OMA constituye un marco analítico innovador para avanzar en investigaciones interdisciplinarias y para transitar de enfoques reactivos hacia mecanismos sociales, políticos y económicos orientados a la anticipación y la preparación frente a los impactos climáticos\.

## [Developing GenAI\-Based Feedback Through Iterative Prompt Design: An Exploratory Study of Online Students’ Cognitive, Affective, and Behavioral Perceptions](../publications/a6b59501da1ba4c45bf8.md)

Meva Bayrak Karsli; Sinem Çilligöl Karabey; Muhammed Guler; Ömer Arpacık; Melike Aydemir Arslan; Engin Kurşun; Ebubekir Kaba

This study reports the iterative prompt\-engineering development of Generative Artificial Intelligence \(GenAI\)\-based feedback in an online graduate course and examines students’ cognitive, affective, and behavioral perceptions\. Grounded in the Student–Feedback Interaction Model, a qualitative case study involved 14 graduate students in a 14\-week fully online course on open and distance learning\. Students completed forum\-based formative activities and received instructor\-reviewed GenAI feedback\. Informed by expert review, instructor observations, and student reflections, prompts evolved through three stages: checklist\-style criterion verification, criteria\-anchored synthesized explanations, and personalized diagnosis of strengths and weaknesses\. Semi\-structured interviews were analyzed through qualitative content analysis\. Students reported improved feedback comprehensibility, detail, tone, and timeliness, valuing personalized, explanatory, criterion\-based comments\. However, inconsistencies between AI comments and instructor scores, limited conceptual evaluation, and lack of emotional presence weakened trust\. GenAI therefore functions best as a draft\-generation layer requiring sustained, active instructor oversight rather than as a stand\-alone source of formative feedback\.

## [Consistency and correlation of a domestic Kehua serum free light chain assay with two imported analytical systems](../publications/a6b64be056cc9cfb5721.md)

Yansong Ren; Shoulei Wang; Limin Han; 王艳生; Qian Ren; Mengxin Wang; Yonghui Xia; Guoqing Zhu

Background Serum free light chain \(sFLC\) testing is central to the diagnosis and monitoring of plasma cell disorders, but assay availability and implementation can vary by laboratory setting\. We evaluated a domestic latex\-enhanced immunoturbidimetric Kehua serum sFLC assay against Freelite and N Latex systems\. Methods Residual serum samples from 133 adults with suspected or established monoclonal gammopathies were measured in parallel by Kehua and Freelite; 122 were also tested by N Latex\. Precision was assessed with low\- and high\-level serum controls\. Method agreement was evaluated using correlation, Passing\-Bablok regression, Bland\-Altman analysis, qualitative concordance and comparator\-defined ROC analysis\. Results Kehua within\-run CVs were &lt;5% for κ and λ controls\. Agreement with Freelite was excellent for FLC\-κ, FLC\-λ and κ/λ ratio \(Pearson r = 0\.988\-1\.000; CCC = 0\.983\-0\.999\), with Passing\-Bablok slopes close to unity\. Agreement with N Latex was also strong \(r = 0\.991\-0\.998\), although κ/λ ratio showed proportional bias\. Total qualitative concordance was 89\.47\-93\.23% versus Freelite and 83\.61\-91\.80% versus N Latex, with Cohen’s κ of 0\.67\-0\.85\. Comparator\-defined ROC AUCs were 0\.994\-0\.999 for elevated FLC\-κ or FLC\-λ and 0\.796\-0\.869 for κ/λ ratio abnormality\. Conclusion The Kehua serum assay demonstrated acceptable precision and good clinical agreement with two imported methods\. It may serve as a domestic option for routine serum sFLC quantification, provided method\-specific intervals are maintained and the same platform is used for serial monitoring\.

## [Optimality of Quasi\-Monte Carlo Methods and Suboptimality of the Sparse\-Grid Gauss–Hermite Rule in Gaussian Sobolev Spaces](../publications/a6b883e2d2cd632c334a.md)

Yoshihito Kazashi; Yuya Suzuki; Takashi Goda

Abstract\. Optimality of several quasi\-Monte Carlo methods and suboptimality of the sparse\-grid quadrature based on the univariate Gauss–Hermite rule are proved in the Sobolev spaces of mixed dominating smoothness of order \[Formula: see text\], where the optimality is in the sense of worst\-case convergence rate\. For sparse\-grid Gauss–Hermite quadrature, lower and upper bounds are established, with rates coinciding up to a logarithmic factor\. This common algebraic rate is found to be only \[Formula: see text\] with \[Formula: see text\] function evaluations, although the optimal rate is known to be \[Formula: see text\]\. The lower bound is obtained by exploiting the structure of the Gauss–Hermite nodes and is independent of the quadrature weights; consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate \[Formula: see text\]\. In contrast, several quasi\-Monte Carlo methods with a change of variables are shown to achieve the optimal rate, some up to, and one including, the logarithmic factor\.

## [Engineering the Ir─O─Ni Interface Bonds in Ir@Ni‐MOF to Accelerate Li 2 O 2 Formation and Decomposition for High‐Reversibility Li‐O 2 Batteries](../publications/a6ba74ad2b3ab5b2cf1e.md)

Yuan Qiu; Yinjing Sun; Yajing Li; Tong Lv; Nuo Zhou; Lei Wang; Qingliang Lv

ABSTRACT Aprotic lithium‐oxygen \(Li‐O 2 \) batteries have attracted considerable interest due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy density, yet their practical application is severely limited by slow cathode reaction kinetics and large voltage hysteresis\. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy to construct ultrafine Ir nanoparticles anchored on Ni‐based metal‐organic framework \(Ir@Ni‐MOF\) as an efficient bifunctional cathode catalyst for Li‐O 2 batteries\. Experimental and theoretical calculations reveal the formation of interfacial Ir─O─Ni chemical bonds, inducing significant charge redistribution and downshifting the d‐band center of Ir@Ni‐MOF\. This electronic modulation weakens the adsorption affinity toward the LiO 2 intermediate, thereby enhancing a solution‐mediated discharge pathway to form nanosheet‐like Li 2 O 2 with intimate interface contact and rapid charge/mass transfer, which facilitates reversible decomposition during charging\. As a result, the Ir@Ni‐MOF cathode delivers a remarkably low overpotential of 0\.76 V, an extended cycling stability over 400 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , outperforming most reported MOF‐based and noble‐metal catalysts\. This work provides a promising avenue for designing high‐performance Li‐O 2 batteries and beyond through precise electronic structure engineering\.

## [POLVIZX: un prototipo multiplataforma para la construcción y la exploración de árboles de posturas](../publications/a6c76038c24834227066.md)

Tobías Afonso; Gabriela Andrea Diaz; Carlos Iván Chesñevar; Ana Gabriela Maguitman

Opinion polarization in social media challenges public discourse and informed decision\-making\. POLVIZ, a prior web prototype, analyzed polarized opinions through stance detection, topic modeling, argument synthesis, and visual analytics\. This paper presents POLVIZX, a cross\-platform extension offering both desktop web and mobile applications for exploring polarized opinion spaces on any dataset\. POLVIZX organizes opinions into hierarchical stance trees, grouping arguments by topic and stance \(pro/anti\), to help users navigate debates and identify polarization patterns, with a pipeline supporting partial execution and reuse of intermediate results for iterative analysis\. Each application offers interaction and visualization strategies suited to its platform, while Firebase\-based authentication enables cross\-device synchronization, stance tree sharing, and collaborative exploration\. This extension broadens access to opinion polarization tools and supports emerging e\-deliberation scenarios\.

## [Protective factors against burnout in police officers: a review of research](../publications/a6c772cda16692611cf4.md)

Karin Miklič

V zaključnem delu so bili s pregledom znanstvene literature obravnavani zaščitni dejavniki pred izgorelostjo\. Namen dela je bil prepoznati ključne individualne in organizacijske dejavnike, ki so pomembni za preprečevanje izgorelosti\. Uporabljena je bila deskriptivna metoda pregleda literature\. V pregled je bilo vključenih 11 empiričnih raziskav\. Raziskave so poročale predvsem o rezultatih kvantitativnih presečnih raziskovalnih načrtov, manj pogosto pa so bili uporabljeni tudi kvalitativni, eksperimentalni in longitudinalni raziskovalni načrti\. Pri pregledu raziskav je bilo ugotovljeno, da preprečevanje izgorelosti temelji na medsebojni povezanosti organizacije in zaposlenih\. Med pomembnejše zaščitne dejavnike lahko uvrstimo psihološko odpornost, čuječnost, telesno dejavnost, različne tehnike spoprijemanja s stresom ter socialno in organizacijsko podporo\. Ugotovitve so pokazale tudi, da so kakovostno vodenje, podporno delovno okolje in preventivni programi za krepitev duševnega zdravja policistov prav tako pomembni dejavniki za preprečevanje izgorelosti\. V slovenskem okolju bi bilo smiselno krepiti strategije spoprijemanja s stresom in odpornost na individualni ravni, na organizacijski ravni pa dostopno psihološko podporo in podporno vodenje\.

## [Generative AI as a cognitive partner: personalised GPTs and differentiated learning in undergraduate teacher education](../publications/a6f1b391ce9b25d3bc7c.md)

Jason Zagami

Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly framed as a catalyst for deeper learning rather than simple automation\. This design\-based study investigated how personalised GPT agents were used as cognitive partners by pre\-service teachers in an undergraduate Initial Teacher Education course in Digital Technologies within a Bachelor of Education \(Secondary\) programme\. Drawing on distributed cognition, constructivism, cognitive load theory, and critical AI literacy, the intervention embedded personalised GPT agents within a university Canvas Learning Management System\. Fourteen students configured and used agents aligned to curriculum goals, teaching contexts, pedagogical preferences, and weekly Prompt–Reflect–Refine tasks\. Data included approximately 7,000 AI interactions, reflective journals, assessed lesson and assessment artefacts, and tutorial\-group discussions\. A hybrid inductive–deductive thematic analysis identified four recurrent functions in students’ use of the agents: conceptual tutor, co\-designer, reflective mirror, and cognitive challenger\. Across data sources, students reported clearer conceptual support, iterative planning, and reflective prompting, alongside risks of over\-reliance, factual drift, and culturally narrow exemplars\. The study contributes a context\-specific model for LMS\-integrated generative AI that foregrounds partnership, personalisation, judgement, and ethical reflexivity\. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study was small\-scale, single\-site, and partly reliant on self\-reported reflection\.

## [A Mathematical Analysis of the Present Status and Challenges of Higher Education in Nepal](../publications/a6fb858d794040d203a8.md)

Partiva Kumari Sahani; Suresh Kumar Sahani

Rapid expansion of higher education in Nepal has been accompanied by uneven institutional development and persistent structural weaknesses\. This study examined the sector’s scale, distribution, and growth trajectory to identify key challenges and inform policy priorities\. The analysis drew on enrolment records from the University Grants Commission and the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, supplemented by case studies of Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu University, and Pokhara University\. Methods included descriptive statistics, ratio analysis, compound annual growth rate estimation, log\-linear regression modelling, and market\-concentration measures\. National enrolment increased from approximately 407,000 students across 12 universities and academies in 2015/16 to 749,392 students across 30 universities and academies operating 1,608 campuses in 2025/26\. Conditional on the continuation of observed trends, the regression model projected enrolment of approximately 983,000 students by 2030\. Institutional concentration remained pronounced: Tribhuvan University accounted for approximately 61% of national enrolment, whereas Kathmandu University and Pokhara University together accounted for less than 8%, despite having substantially lower student\-to\-staff ratios\. No\-Objection Certificate issuance, used as a proxy for outward student mobility, indicated that more than 100,000 Nepali students sought overseas study in a recent fiscal year\. Five interlinked challenges emerged: institutional concentration and limited diversification, funding that lagged behind enrolment growth, increasing outward student mobility, fragmented and inconsistently implemented quality assurance, and geographic and gender disparities\. These findings indicate that sectoral expansion has coexisted with substantial structural imbalances\. The study provides a quantitative basis for policy responses to these challenges while emphasizing that inconsistencies across official and secondary data sources constrain interpretation and evidence\-based planning\.

## [COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF ACORUS TATARINOWII RHIZOMA: MEDICINAL HISTORY, BOTANICAL SOURCES, GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION, EXTRACTION AND ISOLATION METHODS, AND ANTI\-MICROBIAL ACTIVITY](../publications/a6fe70eff63703e28196.md)

Rojalini Samanta; Amitder Nath Chatterjee

Objective: The dried rhizome of Acorus tatarinowii Schott\., a perennial herb of the Acoraceae family, is known as Acorus tatarinowii Rhizoma \(ATR\), or Chinese Sweet Flag\. The objective of this study is to determine the pharmacological potentiality, phytochemical constituents, and assessment of safety of ATR\. It also aims for assessment of its conventional usage, therapeutical effectiveness and validation study for modernized therapeutical applications\. Methods: A systematically review of traditional literature and modernized scientifical study was conducted\. The analysis mainly highlighted the identification of bioactive phytochemical composition of ATR, which majorly includes presence of phenylpropanoid\-groups, terpenoid\-groups, lignan\-groups, flavonoidal contents, alkaloidal contents and organic acids along with their therpaeutical importance and pharmacological activities\. Results: Modern plant research has found more than 160 active ingredients, such as phenylpropanoids, terpenoids, lignans, flavonoids, alkaloids, and organic acids\. These substances are responsible for helping with epilepsy, preventing seizures, fighting cell damage, calming the body, fighting cancer, and reducing swelling\. Overall, Acorus tatarinowii is considered to be a healing plant which has been in use for a long time and even today, it interests the scientists and researchers\. Conclusion: ATR has also been used in clinical settings to treat neurological, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and respiratory problems, including epilepsy, depression, anxiety, and related cognitive deficits\. Despite of treating various health disorders, still there are possibilities of various types of side effects caused by some of the main parts of the plant\. This suggests that the amount of the plant part used must be controlled closely as well as its safety and efficacy must also be carefully tested\.

## [Ori: Drift\-Aware Streaming $k$\-PCA for Very Low\-Rank LLM Training](../publications/a700b27af9142370634c.md)

Xinyu Luo; Jincheng Zhou; Mengbo Wang; Zilin Shen; Nadia Atallah Lanman; Petros Drineas; Bruno Ribeiro; Brian Bullins

A prominent family of low\-rank LLM optimizers, pioneered by GaLore, performs gradient\-subspace projection: at each step, they project the gradient into a low\-dimensional subspace and map the update back to the full model\. Most existing work either recomputes the gradient subspace at certain intervals, or performs post\-hoc adaptation to catch up to the moving subspace\. In this work, we explicitly identify in practice the slow, stable manner in which LLM gradient subspaces drift across time\. To this end, we propose Ori, a novel low\-rank optimizer for training LLMs that captures the shifting principal gradient directions over time to achieve state\-of\-the\-art accuracy under stringent low\-rank constraints\. Ori employs a streaming $k$\-PCA algorithm inspired by Oja\+\+, whose low per\-step cost enables high\-frequency, on\-the\-fly subspace tracking\. In practice, Ori reduces the performance gap of the state\-of\-the\-art low\-rank optimizers to full\-rank optimizers by up to 69\.3\\% on a 1B LLaMA pretraining task, and achieves the best performance on 10 out of 16 task scenarios in Roberta\-Base fine\-tuning\. Together, these contributions allow Ori to further push the performance and efficiency frontiers of gradient\-projecting optimizers, narrowing the gap to full\-rank training for LLMs\. Code can be found at https://anonymous\.4open\.science/r/Ori\-Submission\-2132\.
