## [MetaPaCS: A Novel Meta‐Learning Framework for Pancreatic Cancer Subtype Identification](../publications/a710b5a5ba2cbbf69db4.md)

Nick Boos Peterson; Mengtao Sun; Xinchao Wu; Jieqiong Wang; Shibiao Wan

Pancreatic cancer \(PaC\), the third leading cause of cancer related deaths in the United States, is a highly heterogenous malignancy with a multitude of potential subtypes\. Each PaC subtype has unique molecular pathways and therapeutic characteristics, which can be used in downstream patient risk stratification and tailored treatment design\. Conventional wet‐lab approaches for PaC subtyping \(microdissection, histopathological studies, etc\.\) are laborious, costly, and time‐consuming\. To address these concerns, we present MetaPaCS, a novel meta‐learning framework to accurately identify PaC subtypes based on transcriptomics data\. Specifically, after preprocessing, the transcriptome‐based feature vectors are classified by multiple base machine learning classifiers, whose diverse prediction outputs are combined with the initial preprocessed feature vectors to constitute a new set of ensemble feature vectors for a meta‐learning classifier\. Leave‐one‐out cross‐validation demonstrates that MetaPaCS performs remarkably better optimized individual base classifiers\. We believe that MetaPaCS is a promising tool for downstream risk stratification and personalized treatment design\.

## [Effectiveness of the SEFT teaching model on the clinical practice competence of surgical residents: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/a7281c56b961a2bc2ece.md)

Xiang Jin; Weihong Zhao; Xinye Lin; Xiaomei Xie; Xinli Mao; 李卫林

Background This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the SEFT teaching model in improving surgical residents’ clinical practice competencies, so as to provide a basis for optimizing training strategies\.Methods This single\-center, non\-randomized retrospective cohort study included 38 residents\. The 2019 cohort \(n = 19\) was the control group, receiving traditional demonstration and practice\-based training, while the 2020 cohort \(n = 19\) was the intervention group, trained via the SEFT teaching model\. Scores across five core competencies were compared using the Wilcoxon rank\-sum test\.Results The intervention group scored significantly higher than the control group across all five assessment domains \(all p &lt; 0\.05\): medical history taking \(90\.43 ± 3\.83 vs\. 84\.29 ± 10\.63, p = 0\.039\), physical examination \(91\.20 ± 4\.88 vs\. 83\.76 ± 11\.51, p = 0\.017\), initial medical record documentation \(90\.61 ± 4\.98 vs\. 84\.20 ± 4\.97, p &lt; 0\.001\), and clinical reasoning and decision\-making \(87\.00 ± 3\.64 vs\. 80\.76 ± 9\.24, p = 0\.039\)\.Discussion The SEFT teaching model, with its closed\-loop structure and targeted feedback, showed promising potential to enhance surgical residents’ clinical practice competencies\.

## [Local proxies for memory\-efficient training](../publications/a72af046cf1f197bb923.md)

Wu S\. Zihan; Brian A\. Yuan; Guillaume Bellec

Local learning algorithms can reshape resource requirements of artificial intelligence\. The memory bottleneck of standard end\-to\-end backpropagation lies in the need to store all network activations until the loss gradient has been propagated back through\. Local learning avoids this, but typically at a cost in accuracy\. We study how to achieve accurate and memory efficient local learning in transformers\. For each transformer block, we train a local proxy network to predict the global network output via distillation\. Gradients can be independently propagated through this local proxy while estimating well the backpropagation gradients\. In theory, this approach is exact for deep linear networks; in non\-linear residual models, the gradient error can be bounded when using the appropriate residual proxy\. We verify this numerically and demonstrate that optimizing the distillation loss improves gradient estimation\. Evaluating the performance of proxy propagation on CIFAR\-100 in vision transformers, we find that it achieves a better accuracy/memory trade\-off compared to other local algorithms\. Finally, we show that the method is further relevant for fine\-tuning large language models on a small memory budget\. Our method trains faster and achieves higher performance than memory\-efficient zeroth\-order learning algorithms with comparable memory cost\.

## [AI\-Based Waste Classification and Smart Waste Management Systems: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions](../publications/a732afdd9bd0b8f10e1b.md)

Mohammed Zain\. I; Mohammed Hashir; Mohammad Zuhaib Wani; Md Yusuf Ali; Kavitha D D

Rapid urban growth and the corresponding rise in municipal solid waste have intensified the need for efficient and scalable waste management solutions\. Conventional segregation practices, which largely rely on manual intervention, are often time\-consuming, inconsistent, and unsuitable for handling large volumes of waste\. In recent years, advancements in Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), Machine Learning \(ML\), and Deep Learning \(DL\) have facilitated the development of intelligent systems capable of automating waste classification and monitoring processes\. This survey provides a detailed review of 13 research studies published between 2021 and 2025, with a focus on AI\-driven approaches for waste management\. It examines a range of techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\), object detection frameworks, and hybrid learning models, along with the datasets, evaluation metrics, and system designs employed in these works\. A comparative assessment is carried out to analyze the performance, advantages, and limitations of the existing methodologies\. The review further identifies critical research gaps, such as the absence of standardized benchmark datasets, limited real\-time implementation, lack of multimodal sensor integration, and insufficient emphasis on model interpretability\. Based on these findings, the paper outlines potential future directions, including the adoption of edge\-based AI systems, integration with IoT\-enabled smart infrastructure, and the use of advanced detection models to support scalable and efficient waste management in smart city environments\.

## [Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book III: WaveModules\. Source\-Native Construction of Intelligent Systems](../publications/a733338685bf16c56815.md)

B\. Petersen

Coherence\-Driven Intelligence, Book III: WaveModules\. Source\-Native Construction of Intelligent Systems develops a constructive, source\-explicit realization of the Coherence\-Driven Intelligence \(CDI\) framework\. Book I establishes the mathematical foundations of CDI, and Book II develops the source\-to\-endpoint bridge connecting finite coherence\-memory organization with familiar machine\-learning architectures\. Book III turns the direction around: rather than beginning with an endpoint architecture and asking what Source structure may underlie it, this volume constructs intelligent computational systems while deliberately retaining selected Source\-side organization in explicit, measurable, editable form\. The resulting reference architecture is called WaveModules\. WaveModules is not presented as a competing species of machine learning or as the definition of CDI\. It is a finite computational realization in which presentation, local views, module boundaries, memory responses, closure, target geometry, measurement, collection, replay, editing, growth, pruning, composition, and regulation can remain separately addressable\. The architecture is representation\-agnostic: wave, spectral, complex, graph, temporal, relational, symbolic, learned, and hybrid realizations may occupy the same computational roles\. The volume develops computational Source presentations, registration and invariance, local WaveModule interfaces, explicit memory geometry, closure mechanisms, static response basins, dynamical recovery, memory diagnostics, open\-set and ambiguous states, collective memory, memory insertion and removal, replay and preservation, growth and pruning, continual memory, hierarchical and relational memory, associative activity, endogenous cues, finite internal regulation, self\-state memory, and self\-regulated replay\. It maintains explicit distinctions between static closure and genuine dynamical recovery, terminal task output and internal memory condition, memory removal and residual statistical recoverability, and finite computational Source representations and complete Coherence Geometry Sources\. The later parts provide a constructive experimental program\. Reference demonstrations include geometric registration, explicit complex memory fields, post\-formation memory editing, removal and restoration, sequential confusion\-guided memory growth, and self\-regulated associative replay\. The final reference\-software section organizes these mechanisms within one shared Python source tree and treats experiments, configurations, saved outputs, tests, and figure generation as reproducible computational contracts\. A companion source\-code package is included with this Zenodo release\. It contains the WaveModules reference implementation, experiment scripts, configurations, tests, selected saved results, validation materials, and figure\-generation resources corresponding to the computational realization described in the book\. This release is a Working Reference Text, Version 0\.1, and has not undergone external editorial or peer review\.CGI Internal ID: CGI\-BKS\-0007

## [ENHANCING THE DETECTION OF PHISHING WEBSITE USING SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE AND SIMULATED USER BEHAVIOUR IN MATLAB ENVIRONMENT](../publications/a7340e367c3d2ab7e58d.md)

Gilbert Ugwuanyi

Background: However, the incorporation of behavioural features introduced a novel method of detecting phishing websites which offers valuable insights into user interaction patterns\. Objective: The increasing daily presence on the internet has exposed users to several cybercrimes; among them, phishing has emerged as the most prevalent and damaging attack\. Methods: The introduction of behavioural features, such as mouse movement intensity and click frequency, in combination with static attributes like URL length and the number of dots, created a more robust detection model\. The research findings showed that while static features are significant in detecting phishing sites to a maximum of 97\.54% accuracy, the incorporation of behavioural features complemented insights which enabled the developed model to detect phishing attempts in real\-time with 100% accuracy\. The simulated real\-time web traffic showed that whenever the model is applied in real life settings, good accuracy, precision, recall, and zero false positive rates for both the baseline and integrated models were achieved\. Results: The results from this research adds to the wealth of knowledge in the field of cybersecurity as it enhances phishing detection systems and creates opportunities for future exploration of machine learning algorithms that combine dynamic user behaviors to achieve better solutions to cyber threats\. Conclusion: This research is on enhanced phishing website detection system which combines Support Vector Machines \(SVMs\) with simulated user behaviour in a MATLAB environment\.

## [Low\-Cost AI\-Based Wearable Rehabilitation Monitoring System for Upper\-Limb Stroke Patients](../publications/a7392e0b4b62f49a2700.md)

Anisha N\.; Ushus S\. Kumar

The low cost wearble monitoring framework for the automatic evaluation of exercises for stroke recovery of the upper limb with special attention to discrimination between the intended and compensatory motion of the elbow joint is designed\. The monitoring framework utilizes a 9 degrees\-of\-freedom IMU combined with the ESP32\-based data acquisition and transmission device to obtain the motion of the forearm at 100 Hz\. The signals are processed using the fourth order Butterworth filter, orientation estimation by Madgwick algorithm, quaternion representation, fixed window segmentation, and features extraction\. A stacked 128\- and 64\-unit LSTM network is used to identify the characteristics of movements for the four classes of correct elbow flexion, correct elbow extension, compensatory flexion, and compensatory extension\. The proposed system obtains an accuracy of 93\.25%, precision of 93\.3%, recall of 93\.25%, F1\-Score of 93\.2%, and an AUC\-ROC macro average of 0\.822\. Processing time and communication time are estimated at 312 ms, and the estimated cost for wearable hardware is USD 27\.40\. The system combines movement classification and correction feedback and offers an efficient system for inexpensive rehabilitation monitoring\.

## [ORBITAL SELECTION FOR SPACE\-BASED DATA CENTERS: A COMPARATIVE MULTI\-PHYSICAL AND TECHNICAL PERFORMANCE TRADE\-OFF AMONG LEO, DAWN\-DUSK SSO, AND GEO](../publications/a746e0f0a269b380120f.md)

Dafnhê Thor Castro de Martins Barros; Felipe Augusto Trancoso Fernandes

The scaling of terrestrial data centers dedicated to massive artificial intelligence workloads faces severe electrical power grid saturation and evaporative cooling water constraints\. Orbital Data Centers \(ODCs\) offer a compelling sustainable paradigm by harvesting continuous extraterrestrial Air Mass Zero solar irradiance \(1,361 W/m²\) in the space vacuum\. However, orbital trajectory selection decisively dictates boundary conditions for thermal stress, radiation damage, and data throughput\. This paper establishes a rigorous analytical and multi\-physical comparative evaluation among three candidate trajectories: Conventional LEO \(500 km, 53°\), Dawn\-Dusk SSO \(700 km, 98\.2°\), and Equatorial GEO \(35,786 km, 0°\)\. The investigation focuses strictly on four technical axes: launch mass decomposition and dry specific weight \(kg/kW\); 10\-year subsystem lifetime reliability under Total Ionizing Dose \(TID\), battery fading, and Coffin\-Manson thermal fatigue; sustained AI compute throughput \(orbital PUE and thermal throttling\); and communications performance \(RTT latency and RF/FSO daily throughput\)\. Coupled physical modeling and annual 365\-day orbital propagations demonstrate that Dawn\-Dusk SSO constitutes the optimal design alternative: it slashes specific launch mass to 48\.24 kg/kW \(a 28\.5% saving relative to LEO and 35\.4% relative to GEO, with compute IT hardware explicitly modeled at 10\.0 kg/kW\), confines eclipses to brief seasonal solstice windows \(281 days/year 100% eclipse\-free and max 18\.8 min eclipse\), retains 88\.5% battery capacity over 10 years, preserves BGA solder joint reliability at 96\.8%, achieves an orbital PUE of 1\.15 with 98\.8% sustained throughput, and delivers an agile 9\.5 ms geometric RTT \(21\.5 ms end\-to\-end\) with 150\.2 TB/day downlink volume per 100 Gbps optical node over polar ground stations\. Saaty&\#x27;s canonical AHP evaluation \(CR = 0\.000 &lt; 0\.10\) ratifies SSO as the superior regime with a composite score of 0\.5158\.

## [Ağız yoluyla endoskopik miyotomide yapay zekâ: Kişiselleştirilmiş miyotomiye, daha güvenli eğitime ve reflü tahminine doğru: AI in POEM](../publications/a751efff47a7112982ab.md)

MD Ahmed Abdallah Salman; Ahmed Abdallah

Peroral endoscopic myotomy \(POEM\) is an established treatment for achalasia and selected spastic esophageal motility disorders, but several aspects of care remain highly operator\-dependent\. These include early diagnosis, patient selection, procedural planning, myotomy length, intra\-procedural safety, training assessment, and prediction of post\-procedure reflux\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) may help address these limitations by integrating endoscopic video, high\-resolution manometry, timed barium esophagram, EndoFLIP, clinical variables, procedural data, and follow\-up outcomes into more personalized decision\-support tools\. This narrative review critically examines the evidence for AI across the POEM pathway and distinguishes direct achalasia or POEM evidence from adjacent and conceptual applications\. Early AI applications are most likely to emerge in achalasia detection during diagnostic endoscopy, automated motility interpretation, video\-based procedural assessment, and prediction of clinical response or post\-POEM reflux\. More ambitious applications, such as real\-time tunnel orientation, vessel recognition, mucosal injury alerts, and personalized myotomy planning, remain largely investigational\. Most AI\-specific POEM applications remain at an early or conceptual stage and require multicenter validation, standardized outcomes, and careful clinical governance\. AI should support, rather than replace, expert judgment, and an AI\-derived reflux estimate cannot replace standard follow\-up or objective reflux assessment\.

## [High\-accuracy crude oil purity detection using a non\-invasive microwave sensor with proximity\-coupled patch antennas](../publications/a76c660d2fc39e443d13.md)

Sepehr Zarghami; Ali Roshani; Parsa Askarian Chayjan; Peshawa Jamal Muhammad Ali; Gholam Hossein Roshani

This paper presents a non\-invasive microwave\-based sensor for high\-precision purity detection of crude oil based on the proximity\-coupled rectangular microstrip patch antennas\. The sensor employs mutual electromagnetic coupling between two closely placed slotted rectangular\-shaped antennas in order to extract dielectric metrics from oil\-water mixtures\. This design contrasts with more traditional single\-antenna sensors, which rely entirely on S 11 or return loss, as our design utilizes additional scattering parameters \(S 21 , S 22 \) for improved sensitivity and selectivity when characterizing oil purity\. This antenna system operates in two primary frequency bands, specifically 6\.9–7\.6 GHz for detecting dielectric\-based bandwidth variation and 1\.6 GHz for characterizing signal transmission\. The sensor is fabricated on the FR4 substrate and experimentally validates its capabilities with a wide range of water\-oil mixtures\. The results showed good agreement with simulated and measured data, and validated the high accuracy of the proposed sensor\. To improve sensing precision and decrease nonlinearity due to operation at higher frequencies, artificial neural networks \(ANN\) models are used in the data processing step\. Altogether, the ANN model increased prediction accuracy and model reliability for oil clarity classifications\. Measured results indicate an S11 &lt; − 10 dB in the 6\.9–7\.6 GHz with peak gain of 7\.6 dBi, and the ANN regression yielded R²=0\.995 with low prediction error, confirming enhanced detection accuracy\.

## [Development of a conceptual integrated approach combining cluster analysis and machine learning for credit risk assessment](../publications/a76f8c97e2bf64514ab0.md)

N\. S\. Lyoshin; Д\.А\. МЕЛЬНИКОВА; Liliya Valerievna ERMOLINA

In the context of the rapid growth in volume and complexity of financial data, classical credit scoring models face limitations in forecast accuracy and sustainability\. At the same time, clustering and machine learning methods are evolving, enabling the identification of latent borrower segments and the integration of this additional information directly into predictive models\. This paper addresses the methodological gap between data segmentation and machine learning in credit risk assessment\. The goal of the study is to develop a concept of a hybrid model that combines clustering analysis and gradient boosting algorithms by incorporating cluster meta\-features into the feature space of a scoring model\. The methodological framework includes an analysis for existing approaches to credit scoring, the design of a sequential data\-processing pipeline, and the construction of a feature set that reflects the borrower’s structural position in the data space\. In addition, the study evaluates the stability of clustering results with respect to the choice of metric, the number of clusters, and sample characteristics, as well as compares different ways of encoding cluster information\. The proposed approach is aimed at improving model discriminatory power by accounting for latent customer segmentation\. The expected deliverable is enhanced default prediction quality and expanded model interpretability, which increases their practical value for credit risk management and decision support in financial institutions\.

## [Structure–Reactivity Relationships in Methylaluminoxane: Ionization Potentials Across Compositions and Morphologies](../publications/a76fc38b7d1f276a9136.md)

Xiaotong Mao; Wei Hu; Scott Collins; Mikko Linnolahti

Methylaluminoxane \(MAO\) is the most widely used cocatalyst in metallocene‐catalyzed olefin polymerization, yet its structural basis for reactivity remains poorly understood\. Here, we present a computational survey of ionization potentials across 118 MAO species with the general formula \(AlOMe\) n \(AlMe 3 \) m \( n = 4–10\), covering over 1100 aluminum sites classified by local coordination environment\. The analysis is extended to experimentally relevant sizes through evaluation of sheet and cage models up to n = 18, including an ovalene‐type sheet model and crystallographically characterized 26,9 species\. All energies are evaluated at the RI‐MP2 level\. Ionization potentials become systematically more negative with increasing oligomer size, and sheet structures are more reactive than cages across the sizes studied\. At experimentally relevant sizes, the reactive site landscape converges to two characteristic types: one for methide abstraction and one for dimethylaluminum cation cleavage, with the latter pathway becoming exceptionally favorable for the ovalene‐type sheet topology that matches the crystallographically confirmed MAO structure\. The identification of specific sheet‐type species as the most reactive MAO components is consistent with the experimental observation that the catalytically active component of MAO is a minor species within the bulk material, providing a quantitative basis for understanding structure–reactivity relationships in this industrially important cocatalyst\.

## [Operationalizing AI Governance for Defense SMEs: A Modular, Generative\-AI\-Assisted Framework for NIST SP 800\-171 and CMMC Compliance](../publications/a781f16730ad787d846b.md)

Rizwan Virani

This praxis investigates how artificial intelligence \(AI\) governance can be integrated into the cybersecurity compliance workflows of United States defense small and mid\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\)\. These firms are navigating the transition to the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification \(CMMC\) 2\.0 program and the foundational requirements of National Institute of Standards and Technology \(NIST\) Special Publication \(SP\) 800\-171\. Existing AI risk guidance, such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework \(AI RMF\), does not provide implementation\-focused direction suited to the resource constraints of smaller firms\. This praxis therefore describes a control mapping method consistent with the overlay logic of NIST&\#x27;s Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems \(COSAIS\) concept paper\. It uses that method to develop the Modular AI Governance Framework \(MAGF\), a &quot;comply once, satisfy many&quot; governance framework and toolkit\. My research uses a convergent mixed\-methods design guided by five research questions\. Four ask how practitioners map AI risk categories to control families, which families they identify most often, how feasible they judge lightweight governance artifacts to be, and what barriers and enablers shape implementation\. The fifth asks to what extent the resulting framework is practical, scalable, and audit\-aligned\. In the first phase, 38 practitioners mapped six AI risk categories onto the 14 NIST SP 800\-171 control families through a structured survey\. They prioritized &quot;auditability gaps&quot; in data integrity and model transparency, yet many reported lacking the specialized staff to document these areas manually\. Qualitative analysis of their open\-ended responses produced eight empirically grounded design requirements, including control family anchoring, traceability\-first evidence, change control for probabilistic systems, and a dual\-purpose evidence pattern\. Inspired by operational &quot;playbooks,&quot; the MAGF defines governance tasks as structured modules with goals, actions, and lightweight evidence artifacts\. The modules model the work already required in defense cybersecurity and span the AI lifecycle from initiation and data collection to production deployment and monitoring\. A prompt library provides engineered prompts for generative AI chatbot tools like Google&\#x27;s Gemini and Microsoft&\#x27;s Copilot to support human\-reviewed drafting of artifacts such as bias assessment records and model/prompt change logs\. No output of that prompt library was evaluated in this study\. I evaluated the framework through a structured expert review rather than a measured field deployment\. A panel of 13 qualified reviewers, six of whom identified primarily as assessors, rated the framework and its artifacts against defined criteria\. The results were encouraging but bounded\. Reviewers judged the framework relevant, clear, and valuable as assessment evidence\. Their reservations centered on the feasibility of the most measurement\-intensive artifacts for the smallest firms\. Only 30\.8% of reviewers were favorable on scalability, which marks the boundary of what this study establishes\. An illustrative estimate anchored to published federal compliance cost figures and peer\-reviewed evidence on generative writing productivity suggests a meaningful reduction in recurring drafting effort while human review remains constant\. The estimate is not a measurement, and it does not assert that any requirement or practice is satisfied\. It also shows that careful coordination is needed to keep documentation bloat and fatigue from eroding the benefit and slowing certification\. This praxis contributes a method for compliance\-aligned and resource\-optimized AI governance design and applies it to build an integrated toolkit for defense SMEs\. Future work can examine the generative AI assistance in greater detail and apply the framework to other emerging regulatory environments\. The method offers a replicable template for integrating emerging technologies into highly regulated and risk\-averse operations, helping small firms remain competitive while safeguarding national security\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Supported Personalized Learning: Examining Its Impact on Students&\#x27; Critical Thinking, Learning Engagement, and Academic Achievement in Higher Education](../publications/a7831a1052a36e22f420.md)

Mia Siti Nurazizah; Endan Hamdan Ridwan; Ahsen Yılmaz; Syalaisha Renaisse Fathiha; Mehwish Kaleem

Artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-supported personalized learning provides adaptive instructional content, individualized feedback, and differentiated learning pathways, although its educational outcomes remain inconsistently established\. This study examines the relationships between AI\-supported personalized learning and students&\#x27; critical thinking, learning engagement, and academic achievement in higher education\. A structured integrative literature review was conducted using 24 scholarly publications from 2022–2026\. Qualitative thematic synthesis examined technological mechanisms, reported educational outcomes, and pedagogical conditions while distinguishing empirical findings from conceptual interpretations\. The findings identify adaptive questioning, reflective feedback, and individualized cognitive challenges as potential mechanisms supporting critical thinking, although direct evidence of measurable improvement remains limited\. Personalized instructional support is associated with learning engagement through relevance, motivation, and sustained participation, while adaptive assessment, individualized feedback, and self\-regulated learning are linked to reported academic achievement\. These relationships vary according to instructional design, learner autonomy, digital competence, and educational context\. The reviewed evidence does not establish causal relationships among the three outcomes\. The bounded literature corpus, heterogeneous research designs, and absence of a standardized quality appraisal limit generalizability\. The review contributes an integrated interpretation distinguishing reported educational associations from proposed mechanisms and identifies priorities for longitudinal, comparative, and outcome\-specific empirical investigation\.

## [Pancasila Sebagai Etika Keutamaan: Tinjauan Kritis Atas Tantangan Moral Globalisasi Digital di Indonesia](../publications/a784789d1f286db71016.md)

Putri Nadia Utami; Indah Nomi Varya Ningsih; Najua Sifa; Indry Okuli Sitio; Sarmika Perangin\-angin; M\. Tata Alfarizi

Globalisasi dan kemajuan teknologi digital telah mengubah pola interaksi, komunikasi, dan pengambilan keputusan moral manusia\. Perubahan tersebut membawa manfaat, tetapi juga memunculkan persoalan seperti informasi keliru, sikap tidak toleran, perundungan daring, pelanggaran privasi, polarisasi digital, dan dilema etika kecerdasan buatan\. Di Indonesia, Pancasila berperan bukan hanya sebagai dasar negara, melainkan juga sebagai sistem nilai yang menuntun perilaku etis dalam kehidupan bermasyarakat, berbangsa, dan bernegara\. Kajian ini bertujuan menelaah Pancasila sebagai sistem etika melalui sudut pandang deontologis, teleologis, dan etika keutamaan; mengidentifikasi tantangan moral akibat globalisasi digital; menelaah hambatan internal dan eksternal dalam memperkuat etika Pancasila; serta merumuskan kedudukan konseptual Pancasila dalam menjawab persoalan moral masa kini\. Penelitian ini memakai pendekatan kualitatif dengan tinjauan literatur kritis/naratif\. Sumber yang digunakan meliputi buku filsafat dan etika, artikel jurnal ilmiah, serta dokumen kelembagaan yang relevan\. Analisis isi dan tematik diterapkan untuk mengelompokkan literatur\. Hasil kajian memperlihatkan bahwa Pancasila tidak dapat dipersempit menjadi satu teori etika tertentu\. Nilainya mencakup kewajiban moral, pertimbangan akibat, dan pembentukan karakter\. Kaelan dan Notonagoro menegaskan Pancasila sebagai sistem nilai yang saling terhubung, sedangkan etika Jawa Magnis\-Suseno memperkaya dimensi keutamaan melalui kebijaksanaan dan harmoni sosial\. Dalam menghadapi globalisasi digital, Pancasila dapat berfungsi sebagai kerangka normatif untuk menilai kemajuan teknologi sambil menjunjung kemanusiaan, persatuan, musyawarah, dan keadilan sosial\. Meski demikian, efektivitasnya bergantung pada kemampuan menerjemahkan nilai abstrak ke dalam persoalan moral konkret serta memperkuat literasi digital\.

## [Liquid\-Phase Electrochemical Determination of Methyl Ethyl Ketone Using CuO/HAp\-like Modified PGE](../publications/a7850bab14dcaff55fff.md)

Selin Işık; Filiz Kara; Selda Güney; Emir Baki Denkbaş

Monitoring of Methyl Ethyl Ketone \(MEK\) is essential for industrial safety and biomedical diagnostics, serving as a reliable biomarker for metabolic disorders\. Conventional detection techniques require bulky, expensive instrumentation, limiting portable use\. In this study, a low\-cost and disposable electrochemical sensor was fabricated using a Pencil Graphite Electrode \(PGE\) modified with a porous Hydroxyapatite\-like \(HAp\-like\) interlayer and Copper Oxide \(CuO\)\. The HAp\-like scaffold minimized the copper agglomeration and increased the electroactive surface area, with SEM and EDX confirming homogeneous CuO distribution\. Toward MEK, the sensor exhibited a “signal\-off” response, systematically suppressing the anodic peak current\. This is consistent with a steric\-hindrance mechanism where analyte adsorption blocks interfacial electron transfer\. Evaluated via square\-wave voltammetry \(SWV\) in phosphate buffer \(PBS, pH 10\.0\), the sensor demonstrated dual linear ranges \(0\.1\-5\.0 mM and 5\.0\-50 mM\) with a 1\.04 mM limit of detection\. The sensor demonstrated consistent reproducibility with an overall relative standard deviation \(RSD\) of 2\.83% \(n=15\) and an inter\-day RSD of 1\.94%, while retaining 107\.2% of its initial response after a 14\-day storage period\. Validated in PBS pH 10\.0, this CuO/HAp\-like/PGE platform is presented as a proof\-of\-concept for liquid\-phase MEK detection, establishing a foundation for future monitoring under simulated physiological conditions\.

## [Sub‐Second Ratiometric Fluorescence Imaging of Histamine Dynamics in Living Cells via a Supramolecular Probe](../publications/a79c3a114508f9f1ddb2.md)

Chenming Chan; Yujie Han; Yufei Song; Chunlei Jiang; Qi‐Wei Zhang

ABSTRACT Histamine \(HA\) is a critical neurotransmitter, yet its intracellular dysregulation remains difficult to monitor due to the slow kinetics and environmental sensitivity of traditional fluorescent probes\. Herein, we report a supramolecular ratiometric probe engineered via the host–guest self‐assembly of cationic fluorophores with cucurbit\[7\]uril \(CB\[7\]\)\. By precisely modulating the cationic locus within the guests, we achieved a 2:1 \(host:guest\) stoichiometric complex \( CB\[7\] 2 ⊃GA‐1 \) that displays a distinct 60 nm bathochromic shift\. Functioning via a competitive displacement mechanism, this probe demonstrates exceptional selectivity and an ultrafast response time of 0\.96 s \( k obs = 3\.56 s − 1 \)\. We successfully utilized this system to visualize real‐time HA fluctuations in living mast cells with sub‐second resolution\. Notably, our imaging revealed a quantitative correlation between nigericin‐induced cytoplasmic HA elevation and mast cell rupture\. These findings validate the probe&\#x27;s efficacy in tracking cellular inflammatory responses and highlight its potential as an early‐warning indicator for drug‐induced cytotoxicity\. Consequently, this work offers a robust tool for dissecting HA‐related pathophysiology and establishes a generalizable design paradigm for the rapid, ratiometric sensing of biologically relevant analytes\.

## [Watson, Jeffrey J\.: A Knowledge Argument Without “Knowledge”](../publications/a79d59ad1e8bff4e988e.md)



\_Analytic Philosophy\_\. forthcomingI offer a variation on the Knowledge Argument, the “Resemblance Argument,” which argues that the accuracy conditions for representations of qualia require qualitative resemblance to the mode of presentation, whereas those for representations of physical states do not\. The Resemblance Argument resists a number of popular current responses to the Knowledge Argument, including the Ability hypothesis, the Acquaintance hypothesis, and the “New Knowledge of an Old Fact” strategy\. Because these responses focus on the concept of knowledge, but the Resemblance Argument makes no claims about knowledge, these responses fail\. Some physicalist responses nonetheless survive the Resemblance Argument intact, including Illusionism and the Incomplete Physical Knowledge Strategy\. \(direct link \)

## [Post\-Purchase Emotional Collapse: LLM\-Assisted Analysis of Online Consumer Complaint Narratives](../publications/a7a18abd4e1b997afa89.md)

Eren Temel

Online shopping environments involve interactions shaped by trust, responsiveness, speed, and personalization\. When post\-purchase service failures occur, customer reactions may extend beyond dissatisfaction to cumulative emotional disruption, including regret, frustration, exhaustion, perceived betrayal, and trust erosion\. Despite extensive research on service failure and complaint behavior, limited attention has been given to progressive emotional breakdowns across digital consumption journeys\. Addressing this gap, the study introduces post\-purchase emotional collapse \(PPEC\), defined as a cumulative emotional breakdown resulting from repeated service failures and unresolved negative experiences across customer touchpoints\. Using a qualitative content analysis design, the study analyzes 1,000 consumer complaints from sikayetvar\.com via Large Language Model \(LLM\)\-assisted emotional coding, touchpoint identification, metaphor analysis, and narrative classification, with human validation on a subsample\. Findings suggest delivery failures as the most frequently coded rupture point, with anger, disappointment, and regret as the most frequently coded primary emotions\. Complaint narratives include metaphors of deception, battle, and destruction, which are compatible with a reading of cumulative deterioration\. The study contributes by conceptualizing PPEC and illustrating the potential and the limits of LLM\-assisted qualitative analysis in consumer research; it also offers managerial implications for emotionally responsive complaint management systems\.

## [How Model Choice Obscures Forecast Uncertainty: The Rashomon Effect and the 2026 Senate](../publications/a7a87a8fd35b2e6d2103.md)

Jack T\. Rametta; Christopher Hare

Election forecasts report ostensibly precise predictions that depend on modeling choices\.These include the size of the incumbency advantage, the weight on state partisan lean, and how strongly national conditions move individual races\.We show that the record of Senate elections between 2010 and 2024 is insufficient to adjudicate such choices\.While hundreds of Senate races provide information about racelevel relationships, the role of shared national conditions must be learned primarily from comparisons across only eight election cycles\.Indeed, of 120 plausible models varying these weights, 117 predict past elections similarly well\.This &quot;Rashomon set&quot; illustrates how different assumptions can produce comparable predictive performance but distinct substantive findings\.Our reference model predicts a 50\.6% chance of Democratic control of the 120th Senate with 50\.5 expected seats \(90% interval 45\-56\)\.The 117\-model Rashomon set, however, puts the chances of Democratic control anywhere between 43\.2% and 57\.6%\.We recommend reporting this range alongside conventional predictive intervals from a single model\.

## [DEEP LEARNING ENSEMBLES FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF ENDOSCOPIC LESIONS](../publications/a7abad50cc7c72fe9904.md)

Breno Augusto Tamanini; Danilo Maia de Oliveira; Marcos Raffael Almeida Amorim; Felipe da Costa Mota; José Leal Rodrigues; Genilson Vieira Martins; João Otávio Bandeira Diniz; Luiz Otávio de Oliveira Souza Júnior

Gastrointestinal lesions represent a significant public health concern, where early detection reduces mortality despite the subjectivity of manual endoscopic image analysis\. This work proposes DeepEnsemble\-Endo, a weighted soft voting ensemble with weights optimized via grid search\. After evaluating 11 pre\-trained CNNs via transfer learning and selecting the top\-5 \(DenseNet121, ResNet50, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB2\), weights were systematically optimized, achieving 96\.63% accuracy and 97\.25% F1\-score \- outperforming simple ensembles from the literature and demonstrating potential as automated clinical decision support\.

## [Leveraging Large Language Model Token Probabilities for Literature Review Abstract Filtering](../publications/a7b89cab9409c842c83a.md)

Philip Mitchell; Baptiste Andrieu; Mehrnoosh Heydari; Jonathan M\. Cullen; André Cabrera Serrenho

Grasping the latest knowledge in any field has become increasingly challenging given the rapid pace of modern publishing\. Recent advances in artificial intelligence \(AI\), particularly embedding models and large language models \(LLMs\), provide promising tools to aid researchers in the filtration and identification of the most relevant literature\. However, there is little practical guidance on how to incorporate LLMs into literature reviews, and there are not yet direct comparisons of embedding models versus generative approaches\. In this work, we compare these methods using small local LLMs for literature screening on both a simple dataset containing distinct categories and a more complex example with abstracts obtained from the Web of Science\. We find that embedding models perform strongly for simple, well\-separated queries due to their robustness and computational efficiency\. For more complex filtering tasks, generative approaches based on token probabilities can achieve competitive or superior performance, but only when properly calibrated and when token\-level outputs are interpreted as continuous scores rather than binary decisions\. However, we show these methods are highly sensitive to prompt formulation, token conventions, and threshold selection\.

Do not claim a visual or interaction test passed unless it was actually performed\. \#\# Change policy Prefer reporting defects before editing\. Fix only clearly demonstrated UI defects that can be corrected without changing approved scope or security assumptions\. Keep changes small and inspect the diff afterward\. If a change could affect authorization, privacy, business rules, or the established Git baseline, stop and report it instead\. \#\# Final report State: \- Whether the portal was actually opened and visually inspected\. \- Which desktop and mobile checks were performed\. \- Results for navigation, buttons, prototype states, console, and assets\. \- Any defects found and exact files changed\. \- Git status before and after, including whether anything was staged\. \- Remaining limitations and the recommended next task\. Do not begin Supabase integration in this task\.

## [Lexical Evidence for Malicious and Benign Envy: The Affective Structure of Japanese Emotion Words](../publications/a7c7ca7183ae47346331.md)

Ayaka Nakai; Naomi Watanabe; Takashi Hattori; Tessei Kobayashi

Abstract Although there is debate over how envy is conceptualized, one prominent view is that envy comprises two subtypes—malicious and benign envy—that differ in their emotional and motivational natures\. Previous research has shown that people can experience both types regardless of whether their language lexically distinguishes them\. However, it remains unclear how, and to what extent, these subtypes are reflected in the lexical and affective structure of emotion words within a single language\. We examined the affective structure of Japanese emotion words expressing envy and related emotions, such as jealousy, resentment, and admiration\. In two surveys, 22,819 participants rated 3,021 words for valence \(positive, negative, or mixed\) and classified each word into an emotion category \(e\.g\., anger, sadness\), with at least 100 ratings per word\. By visualizing the affective space of these words, we analyzed how 11 words referring to envy clustered into two distinct subgroups\. Results showed that one subgroup consisted of words perceived predominantly as negative and classified as disgust or anger \(e\.g\., netamashii \), whereas the other consisted of words characterized by more ambivalent valence and showing no single dominant emotion category \(e\.g\., urayamashii \)\. These subgroups correspond to theoretical distinctions between malicious and benign envy, respectively\. In addition, the word for jealousy clustered with malicious envy, while the words for resentment and admiration formed separate groups\. These findings demonstrate that perceived Japanese affective\-semantic structure reflects both malicious and benign envy, highlighting nuanced similarities and differences among envy\-related emotions and offering a lexical perspective on envy’s dual structure\.

## [Dikey Çekilen Dizilerde Sinematografik Görünüm: Zirvede Dizisi Örneği](../publications/a7d104d566a94b3050f8.md)

Büşra Urlular Öncü; Fatih Şahinoğlu; Ersin AYCAN

Bu çalışmanın amacı, geleneksel sinema anlayışının dönüşümüyle ortaya çıkan dikey formatlı yeni görsel dilin dikey dizilerde nasıl yansıdığını incelemek ve gelecekte yeni bir perspektif oluşturacağı öngörülen dikey çekimli eserlerin daha iyi anlaşılmasını sağlamaktır\. Bu doğrultuda dikey olarak çekimleri yapılan Zirvede \(2024\) adlı dizinin ilk üç bölümü sinematografik açıdan incelemeye alınmıştır\. Nitel araştırma yöntemlerinden içerik analizi ve karşılaştırmalı analiz kullanılarak sinematografik yapısı incelenen bu dizinin, geleneksel sinematografik uygulamalara kıyasla nasıl farklılaştığı yorumlanmıştır\. Akıllı telefon kullanımının artmasıyla birlikte 9:16 oranına sahip mobil ekranların, özellikle sosyal medya kullanımı üzerinden izleyici alışkanlıklarını etkilediği aşikârdır\. Bu durum, görsel çerçeveleme anlayışının yeniden tanımlanmasına neden olmakta ve geleneksel sinemada kullanılan çerçeve oranlarının \(1,33:1, 1,85:1, 2,35:1, 2,40:1\) yatay genişliğe sahip kadraj anlayışının aksine daha dar ve dikey bir çerçeveleme oranını \(9:16\) izleyiciye dayatmaktadır\. Analiz sonuçlarına göre dikey formatın, geleneksel yatay çerçevelemeye kıyasla mekânsal genişliği sınırladığı ve böylece karakter odaklı kısıtlanmışlık estetiğine dayalı, dikey derinliği ön plana çıkaran özgün bir görsel anlatım sunduğu söylenebilir\. Ayrıca sosyal medya estetiğinden ödünç alınan ‘Zoom Efekt’ ve ‘Donmuş Kare’ gibi uygulamalarla birlikte &\#x27;Split Screen&\#x27; tekniğine yer verilmesinin, dikey dizilerde geleneksel yatay sinema formunun ağır ve akışkan yapısına alternatif olarak daha hızlı ve vurgu odaklı yeni bir anlayış geliştirdiği saptanmıştır\. Diğer taraftan dikey kadrajın dar yatay düzlemi nedeniyle özellikle orta ölçekli çekimlerde ani bir hareket yaptığında karakterin kadrajda tutulmasının zorlaştığı, bu sebeple de oyuncu hareketlerinin kısıtlandığı görülmüştür\.

## [Learning Rewards in Strategic Games](../publications/a7dfc646c4bf75f89d3a.md)

Antoine Bergerault; Cyrille Kone; Giorgia Ramponi

Understanding the objectives that drive agents&\#x27; behavior is crucial in strategic environments, where multiple agents interact and adapt to one another\. This challenge arises in domains such as cybersecurity, autonomous driving, and online markets, where agents&\#x27; underlying incentives are typically unknown and must be inferred from their observed behavior\. Inverse reinforcement learning \(IRL\) provides a natural framework for this problem, but extending IRL to strategic multi\-agent settings introduces a fundamental challenge: a reward that explains observed behavior does not necessarily induce optimal strategies when used for decision\-making\. In this work, we study this problem through the lens of \\emph\{strategic identifiability\}, and show that learning from a fixed policy pair can be insufficient to strategically identify rewards, independent of the number of expert samples $K$\. Motivated by this, we introduce an active IRL algorithm for two\-player repeated Stackelberg games, in which the leader adaptively selects policies to elicit informative responses about the follower&\#x27;s reward\. Combining maximum\-likelihood estimation with experimental design, we derive finite\-sample guarantees on the Stackelberg sub\-optimality induced by the learned reward, matching up to polylogarithmic factors a new minimax learning rate of $K^\{\-1/2\}$\. Finally, we evaluate our approach in a realistic anti\-poaching setting, demonstrating the benefits of active exploration for reward recovery and downstream strategic performance\.

## [Asking Smarter Questions: Targeted Active Preference Learning for Underspecified Rewards](../publications/a7e0207c5b4e0fe68105.md)

Helena Merker; Nick Walker; Andreea Bobu

Reward learning typically assumes the human&\#x27;s input covers everything that matters for the task\. In practice, humans can only attend to so much at once, so their teaching naturally captures some features\-\-\-or aspects of the task\-\-\-better than others\. Prior work has shown how the robot can identify which features were poorly supervised directly from its teaching data\. But the current solution is to ask the human to try again, putting the burden on someone who already struggled to convey those features\. We propose shifting this burden to the robot\. Our key insight is that the same information that tells the robot what it doesn&\#x27;t know can help it ask better questions\. Preference queries offer a low\-effort channel for resolving this uncertainty, but only if the robot knows where to direct them and the human knows what to attend to when answering\. We act on this insight in two ways: we build an informed prior that targets preference queries at the features that need resolving, and we accompany each query with an explanation that focuses the human&\#x27;s attention on exactly those features\. In simulation, the informed prior beats the standard active preference learning baseline by up to $30\.8\\%$ in the low\-query regime, where reducing human effort matters most\. In a user study, the informed prior and explanations each significantly improve reward recovery and amplify each other\.

## [BULANIK WENSLO VE BULANIK TOPSIS İLE DEPO YERİ SEÇİMİ: TÜRKİYE’DEKİ 3PL HİZMET SAĞLAYICI BİR FİRMADA VAKA ÇALIŞMASI](../publications/a7e07e3fa4036cbb22e6.md)

Sündüs Dağ; Nihan Kabadayı

Depo yeri seçimi, işletmelerin tedarik zinciri operasyonel maliyetlerini, hizmet seviyesini ve genel performansını doğrudan etkileyen stratejik bir karar sürecidir\. Bu kararın, işletmelerin rekabet stratejileri ve tedarik zinciri yapılarıyla uyumlu bir şekilde ele alınması sürdürülebilir başarı için kritik bir öneme sahiptir\. Özellikle 3PL \(üçüncü parti lojistik\) hizmet sağlayıcı firmalar açısından, farklı sektörde faaliyet gösteren müşterilerinin tedarik zinciri gereksinimlerini karşılayabilecek uygun depo lokasyonularının belirlemesi; müşteri memnuniyeti, operasyonel verimlilik ve uzun vadeli karlılık için stratejik bir zorunluluktur\. Depo yeri seçimi, çok sayıda alternatifin birden fazla kriter doğrultusunda değerlendirilmesini gerektiren tipik birçok kriterli karar verme \(ÇKVV\) problemidir\. Kriterlerin veya alternatiflerin değerlendirilmesinde belirsizlik ve uzman görüşüne dayalı yargılar söz konusu olduğunda, bulanık mantık temelli yöntemler etkin sonuçlar üretmektedir\. Bu çalışmada, belirsizlik ortamında stratejik karar alma süreçlerini destekleyecek entegre bir bulanık karar destek sistemi geliştirmek amaçlanmıştır\. Çalışmanın uygulama bölümünde Türkiye’deki uluslararası bir 3PL hizmet sağlayıcı firmanın İstanbul’daki depo yeri seçimi problemi ele alınmıştır\. Burada depo yeri seçim karar kriterlerinin önem ağırlık değerleri Bulanık WENSLO \(Weighted Sum with Normalized Levels of Satisfaction\) yöntemi ile belirlenmiş, ardından aday depo lokasyonlarının değerlendirilmesinde Bulanık TOPSIS \(Technique for Order Performance by Similarity to Ideal Solution\) yöntemi kullanılarak en uygun alternatif tespit edilmiştir\.

## [The World&\#x27;s Youngest Billionaires](../publications/a7ed5ad48a8a3419b320.md)

Zen Revista

This study examines the ten youngest billionaires on the 2026 Forbes World’s Billionaires List—the five youngest women and the five youngest men—as a lens through which to investigate the dynamics of extreme wealth formation in the twenty\-first century\. Drawing on Thomas Piketty’s r &gt; g framework and the empirical literature on intergenerational wealth transmission, the analysis reconstructs, verifies, and independently re\-verifies the demographic, geographic, and institutional profiles of the 2026 billionaire cohort under the age of 30, which comprises a record 35 individuals with a combined net worth of $92\.4 billion\. The findings reveal a strongly bimodal structure of youth wealth\. Of the 35 billionaires under 30, 23 owe their positions to inheritance concentrated in a small number of family\-controlled enterprises, including WEG, Nexon, Ferd, Boehringer Ingelheim, and EssilorLuxottica\. The remaining 12 self\-made billionaires, representing the largest such cohort ever recorded by Forbes, derive their fortunes almost exclusively from artificial intelligence ventures and prediction markets\. This group includes the three 22\-year\-old founders of Mercor, the youngest self\-made billionaires in the history of the list\. Every fortune in the inherited\-wealth group is consistent with the mechanism described by Piketty’s r &gt; g framework, whereby returns on existing capital outpace economic growth, enabling dynastic wealth to accumulate across generations\. By contrast, the self\-made group illustrates how equity valuations in venture\-backed companies can compress the time required to attain billionaire status, allowing substantial paper wealth to accumulate within a single entrepreneurial cycle\. The study also presents an original source\-verification exercise documenting five factual discrepancies between a widely circulated Portuguese\-language infographic depicting the 2026 ranking and Forbes’ primary data\. The implications for theories of wealth concentration, the geographic and gender distribution of early\-life wealth, and inheritance\-tax policy are examined, alongside the methodological limitations of billionaire rankings as measures of economic inequality and wealth accumulation\.

## [Integrated sensor engineering and AI\-assisted peptide design to target the Zika virus NS2B\-NS3 protease](../publications/a7f26cca755f09fbc5a8.md)

Alejandro Cadillo\-Valverde; Ana Sanchez\-Castro; Pohl Milón

Abstract Zika virus NS2B\-NS3 protease \(ZVP\) is an essential enzyme for viral replication and a promising antiviral drug target\. However, peptide\-based inhibitor design remains challenging\. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining a recombinant FRET\-based protease sensor with AI\-driven peptide inhibitor design\. The engineered PEprot ZIKV sensor, containing the ZVP cleavage sequence between two fluorescently labeled domains, enabled quantitative activity assays\. PEprot ZIKV showed \~ 5\.5\-fold higher catalytic efficiency \( k cat / K m = 49 ± 7 × 10 6 M −1 s − 1 \) and a lower K m \(4 nM\) than a chemically synthesized substrate \(22 nM\) bearing the same cleavage sequence, with comparable catalytic turnover\. Structural hotspot mapping of 53 ZVP crystal structures and multiple sequence alignment of flaviviral polyprotein motifs guided de novo peptide generation using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN\. Computational filtering \(docking, AlphaFold\-3 co\-folding, MD simulations and MM/PBSA\) prioritized short peptides for testing\. Biochemical screening with PEprot ZIKV identified three candidate inhibitors, with peptide 715 showing the strongest activity \(IC 50 = 214 µM\), followed by 630 and 701\. Structure\-guided peptide elongation improved 630\-derived variants \(e\.g\., 630\_03, IC 50 = 224 µM\) but reduced potency for 701\- and 715\-derived sequences\. This integrated approach offers a generalizable framework to accelerate the discovery of peptide inhibitors against ZVP and other viral proteases\.

## [Out of Support, Not Out of Reach: In\-Context Learning with Unsupported Instructions and Composed Tasks](../publications/a7f285fdfbecd6498431.md)

Xuhan Tong; Yuchen Zeng; Jiawei Zhang

In\-Context Learning \(ICL\) enables pretrained LLMs to adapt to downstream tasks from a small set of input\-output demonstrations, without parameter updates\. Yet existing theory primarily explains ICL as identifying a latent task already represented in pretraining, leaving unclear whether ICL can succeed when either the instruction or the target task falls outside the pretraining support\. We develop a theoretical framework under mild assumptions that separates these two forms of distribution shift\. For target tasks represented in pretraining, we show that demonstrations can identify the task and reduce sensitivity to pretrain\-supported prompt templates as their number increases\. For an unsupported instruction, we show that under a fixed model\-induced reference extension, demonstration evidence can dominate an $N$\-independent instruction shift while preserving the exponential identification rate\. We then use the same ICL framework as an interpretive lens for long\-horizon target tasks that are not represented in pretraining but admit a plan that decomposes them into pretraining\-supported subtasks\. Applying the supported\-task analysis step by step yields a standard accumulated\-error bound and clarifies how invoking familiar subtasks along an intermediate\-state trajectory can avoid directly selecting the unsupported complete task\. Together, our results characterize when demonstrations, instructions, and task decomposition can support ICL beyond the corresponding pretraining supports\.

## [Technology readiness in maintenance: an Industry 4\.0 case study in the Swedish sawmill sector with Industry 5\.0 human\-centric insights](../publications/a7f68430d8b738371561.md)

Mirka Kans; Kristina Maria Eriksson; Liselott Lycke; Tinh Sjökvist

Abstract The sawmill industry presents unique opportunities for adopting emerging technologies due to its capital\-intensive operations and dependence on high reliability\. However, despite increasing digitalization, there remains limited understanding of how maintenance organizations can assess and develop technology readiness, particularly with respect to organizational and human factors\. Understanding these factors is important not only for operational efficiency but also for supporting the human\-centric, sustainable, and resilient ambitions of Industry 5\.0\. This paper investigates the technology readiness of maintenance operations in a Swedish sawmill\. The study is based on a qualitative case study involving 21 in\-depth interviews and three workshops with personnel from the maintenance organization \(technicians, engineers, coordinators, and managers\) and related functions \(production, operations development, health and safety, and management\)\. Findings reveal that while the organization demonstrates strengths in technology adoption and operational structure, challenges remain in areas such as strategic integration, workforce competence, and data utilization\. The study highlights that advancing technology utilization and work processes alone is insufficient for successful development of maintenance\. Thus, the study emphasizes human\-centric perspectives such as leadership visibility, shared responsibility, cross\-functional communication, and long\-term planning, are critical for achieving technology readiness\. The study concludes that technology readiness in maintenance depends on the combined development of technological, organizational, and human capabilities\. Maintenance can serve as a strategic entry point for this transformation, enabling improved sustainability, resilience, and safer operations\. Further research is recommended to combine methods and explore how human\-centric factors influence the successful adoption of smart technologies\.

## [Agricultural Communication](../publications/a82160b019b5d5c71430.md)

Meetali Bharti; Bhavnesh Jaint; Rohitashw Kumar; N\. R\. Chaithra; Vijay P\. Singh

Agricultural Communication: Advances in Agricultural Knowledge and Information Systems examines the transformative role of communication technologies in modern agriculture\. It highlights the critical need for effective dissemination of agricultural knowledge and technologies to farmers, addressing the challenges posed by poor linkages between research and advisory services\. The book explores the integration of indigenous technical knowledge \(ITK\) with advanced information and communication technologies \(ICT\) to empower farmers, enhance decision\-making, and promote sustainable agricultural practices\. Covering topics such as precision agriculture, drones, artificial intelligence, and mobile technology, it emphasizes the importance of timely and accurate information in overcoming market complexities, climate change, and resource constraints\. Examines emerging trends such as robotics, AI, and precision farming, emphasizing their potential to revolutionize agriculture and address global challenges like climate change and food security\. Addresses real\-world challenges faced by small farmers, offering actionable knowledge on decision\-making, market dynamics, and resource optimization to improve livelihoods\. Highlights the importance of ITK, showcasing its role in sustainable farming practices and its integration with modern technologies for enhanced agricultural productivity\. Offers best practices for different agroclimatic zones\.

## [परथमक ककषओ म द भष शकषण क परभव बनन मशटल एव AI आधरत ससधन क भमक: एक अधययन](../publications/a8221eacc4fc89ff5144.md)

तिवारी मानसी

वितमान समय में शििा के िेत्र में तिशिटल िकनीक और कृतत्रम बुशिमत्ता \(Artificial Intelligence–AI\) का प्रयोग िेिी से बढ़ र ा ै। प्राथतमक स्तर पर त िंदी भाषा शििण में इन सिंसाधनोिं का उपयोग बच्ोिं के सीखने को अतधक रोचक, सरल और प्रभावी बनाने में स ायक ो सकिा ै। राष्ट्रीयशििानीति \(NEP\) 2020 एविंराष्ट्रीयपाठ्यचयातकीरूपरेखा \(NCF\-SE\) 2023 मेंशििण\-अतधगमप्रतियाकोप्रभावी, रोचकएविंगुणवत्तापूणतबनानेकेशलएतिशिटलिकनीककेसाथतकउपयोगपरबलतदयागया ै।प्रस्तुि अध्ययन में प्राथतमक किाओिं में त िंदी भाषा शििण के शलए तिशिटल बोित, PPT, िैतिक वीतियो, ऑतियो, ऑनलाइन क्विज़, तिशिटल वकतिीट िथा तचत्र आधाररि गतितवतधयोिं के प्रयोग की सिंभावनाओिं पर तवचार तकया गया ै। साथ ी, AI की स ायिा से क ानी एविं कतविा तनमातण, ि􀉨ावली अभ्यास, व्याकरण सिंबिंधी प्रश्न, व्यक्विगि स्तर की वकतिीट िथा शििक के शलए पाठ\-योिना और गतितवतध तनमातण िैसे कायों के उपयोग पर चचात की गई ै। अध्ययन य स्पष्ट् करिा ै तक तिशिटल एविं AI आधाररि सिंसाधन तवद्यातथतयोिं की सतिय भागीदारी, सीखने में रुतच, रचनात्मकिा िथा व्यक्विगि सीखने में स ायिा कर सकिे ैं। ालािंतक, इनके प्रयोग के साथ िकनीकी सुतवधाओिं की उपलब्दिा, AI द्वारा िैयार सामग्री की िुििा, शििक प्रशििण, स्क्रीन पर अत्यतधक तनभतरिा िथा बच्ोिं की तिशिटल गोपनीयिा िैसी चुनौतियााँ भी िुडी ैं। अिः इन सिंसाधनोिं का प्रयोग शििक के तवकल्प के रूप में न ीिं, बक्वि स ायक साधन के रूप में तकया िाना चात ए। शििक द्वारा सामग्री की िााँच, आयु\-उपयुि सामग्री का चयन और पारिंपररक िथा तिशिटल शििण के बीच सिंिुलन इस प्रतिया को अतधक प्रभावी बना सकिा ै। त िंदी सत ि भारिीय भाषाओिं के शलए गुणवत्तापूणत और तवश्वसनीय AI आधाररि सामग्री का तवकास भी समय की आवश्यकिा ै।

## [Digital Technology for Health Service Management and Well\-Being in Later Life in Canada: A Critical Analysis Using an Anti\-Oppressive Lens](../publications/a82a1ed16a06a6922cea.md)

Mir Nabila Ashraf; Natasha L\. Gallant; M\. Rebecca Genoe

Healthy aging plays a crucial role in a country&\#x27;s economic growth\. However, older adults face health challenges, resulting in financial pressure on a country&\#x27;s healthcare systems, a situation worsened during the pandemic\. Amidst these challenges, digital health, such as telehealth, mHealth, and eHealth, emerged to address limited healthcare resources during and following COVID\-19\. This paper critically analyzes the current landscape of digital health for later life in Canada and the initiatives promoting it\. A critical narrative review of 38 sources, including peer\-reviewed studies, policy documents, and grey literature, was conducted\. Thematic analysis identified four domains: access and utilization, structural barriers, digital ageism, and policy responses\. Digital health expanded access and continuity of care, but significant inequities persist, including limited digital literacy, affordability constraints, and uneven infrastructure\. Digital ageism operates across individual, institutional, and technological levels\. Addressing these challenges requires equity\-centred policies, inclusive design, and system\-level interventions to support healthy aging\.

## [The Plant Defense Web: Decoding Convergent Mechanisms of Tolerance to Multiple Abiotic Stresses and Building Climate\-Resilient Crops](../publications/a83201fce2b9628dfb73.md)

Isharani Acharya; Preetam Kumar Senapati

Plants are continuously exposed to an increasingly complex combination of environmental constraints rather than to individual stresses occurring in isolation\. Drought, heat, salinity, flooding, chilling, high light, ultraviolet\-B \(UV\-B\) radiation, nutrient imbalance, heavy metals and atmospheric pollutants can occur simultaneously or sequentially, creating stress combinations that profoundly alter plant growth, metabolism and productivity\. Conventional stress biology has predominantly examined individual stresses, but increasing evidence demonstrates that the response to combined stress cannot simply be predicted by adding the responses to individual stressors\. Instead, plants employ an integrated defense network in which stress perception, calcium signalling, reactive oxygen species \(ROS\), reactive nitrogen species, phytohormones, protein phosphorylation, transcriptional regulation, metabolic reprogramming, antioxidant defense and epigenetic memory interact dynamically\. This review proposes a conceptual framework termed the Plant Defense Web \(PDW\), in which multiple abiotic stresses converge on a limited number of regulatory hubs\. Stress\-induced perturbations in membrane integrity, cellular hydration, redox balance, temperature, photosynthetic electron transport and ion homeostasis generate early calcium and ROS signatures\. These signals activate protein kinases, transcription factors and hormonal networks, which subsequently regulate stomatal behavior, osmotic adjustment, antioxidant metabolism, repair of damaged macromolecules, secondary metabolite biosynthesis and growth\-defense trade\-offs\. Particular attention is given to the integration of abscisic acid, jasmonates, salicylic acid, ethylene, brassinosteroid, auxin, cytokinins, melatonin and Strigolactones\. The review further examines flavonoids, phenolics, proline, soluble sugars, polyamines and antioxidant enzymes as components of the biochemical defense shield\. UV\-B perception through UVR8 and the relationship between light signalling and redox defense are discussed as important examples of stress\-specific signalling converging with general defense mechanisms\. Finally, the emerging importance of stress priming, epigenetic regulation, small RNAs, multi\-omics, genome editing, nanotechnology and machine\-learning\-assisted phenotyping is discussed for developing crops capable of tolerating realistic combinations of environmental stresses\. The proposed Plant Defense Web model shifts the conceptual focus from isolated stress tolerance genes toward network\-level resilience, providing a framework for understanding and engineering crops capable of maintaining productivity under increasingly unpredictable climate conditions\.
