## [Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self\-Distillation](../publications/a838f0aaccf4467a8af4.md)

Karim Abdel Sadek; Federico Di Gennaro; Fanny Yang

Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities\. One prominent approach is self\-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token\-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction\. However, the safety properties of this training procedure are poorly understood\. In this paper, we present a surprising safety failure of recursive self\-distillation, where each self\-distilled model becomes the teacher for the next round of training\. We observe that when a safe model is recursively self\-distilled on its own \(safe\) generations while receiving an additional non\-harmful cue, it becomes increasingly misaligned across a diverse set of harmful queries; we call this Progressive Misalignment\. We show this failure mode in both the Qwen3 and Phi\-4 model families on SORRY\-Bench and StrongREJECT\. Progressive misalignment also occurs in a more realistic setup, where the fixed cue is replaced by feedback from a simulated user with benign intent\. Using a gradient\-based method, we are also able to find benign prompts that lead to progressive misalignment when applying recursive self\-distillation, showing that harmful training prompts are not necessary for this failure mode to emerge\. We hope our work encourages future investigations of the safety properties of AI systems recursively trained on their own data\.

## [Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models](../publications/a83dc415f199b3273f2b.md)

Weijian Luo; Yujian Chen; Hao Jiang; Guang Cheng; Tianyang Hu

Continuous diffusion language models \(CDLMs\) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models \(LLMs\) or Diffusion Transformers \(DiTs\) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs\. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer \(LangDiT\), combining feature and query\-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood\-shortcut gradient routing and calibration, and confidence\-gated training self\-conditioning\. LangDiT significantly reduces generation perplexity in matched LangFlow comparisons, establishing a new state of the art in continuous language generation across different model formulations\. Using LangFlow as a representative CDLM, LangDiT as a plug\-and\-play backbone leads to a new state\-of\-the\-art model with a generation perplexity \(GenPPL\) of 21\.72 using 1024 NFEs and 44\.72 GenPPL using 128 NFEs on the unconditional generation of 1024\-token sequences on the OpenWebText dataset\. When adapted to Plaid\-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT results in a new leading GenPPL of 11\.33 using 1024 denoising NFEs, and 27\.51 GenPPL using 128 denoising NFEs\. These gains are achieved while retaining each model&\#x27;s underlying representation, training objective, and inference sampler, isolating transformer architecture as a fundamental source of improvement\. Our study identifies architectural design as an important source of improvement in continuous diffusion language models\.

## [学前教育专业本科生人工智能素养提升路径研究 —— 基于毕业论文写作课程的准实验](../publications/a83fa7183c1da56951bb.md)

郭 威\*; 席心悦; 柯亮

摘 要：针对生成式人工智能\(AIGC\)技术对学前教育师资培养的新挑战，本研究以陕西学前师范学院2022级本科毕业生484人为研究对象\(实验组242人、对照组242人\)，依托《毕业论文\(设计\)写作指导》课程开展16学时AIGC嵌入式教学准实验。采用准实验法与问卷调查法进行实证分析。结果表明，AIGC嵌入式教学可极显著提升学生人工智能素养总分；学生AIGC工具选择呈现“马太效应”，豆包与DeepSeek成为首选工具；学生素养发展呈现四大课程模块分层问题，整体呈重术轻道的结构性失衡。据此，本研究提出构建通识、专业、实操的三维嵌入式培养体系，推动毕业生从技术赋能向伦理自觉与职业保教能力全面转化。 基金项目：西安市科学技术局软科学项目（2026YBRK00036）；陕西学前师范学院重点教改课题（25JG003Z）；陕西学前师范学院教改课题（25JG01CJ）；陕西学前师范学院引进人才（博士）科研启动项目（2024DS13）

## [Exploring sepsis from definitions to prediction: a journey through epidemiology, clinical scores, and real\-world data challenges](../publications/a8464194db833ef6670b.md)

Carolina Hincapie

Sepsis is a life\-threatening condition that occurs when the body&\#x27;s response to infection goes into overdrive, damaging its own tissues and organs\. It is the leading cause of death from infection worldwide, yet diagnosing and measuring its severity remains surprisingly difficult\. This thesis examines why, and what can be done about it\. Over ten chapters, this research investigates sepsis from multiple angles\. It starts by asking a fundamental question: does it matter which definition of sepsis we use? The answer is yes, dramatically so\. Applying three different definitions to the same group of patients at the emergency department showed that each one identified a completely different set of patients, with almost no overlap\. The definition a doctor or researcher chooses determines who gets counted as having sepsis\. The thesis also examines the scoring tools used to measure how severely ill a patient is, finding that most were designed for the intensive care unit and perform inconsistently when applied at the emergency department\. It shows that where the infection is located in the body, and which bacteria is causing it, affect prognosis in ways that current tools do not capture\. Two chapters demonstrate that useful information is already being generated in routine hospital care but never used\. The time it takes for bacteria to grow in a blood sample, and detailed immune cell measurements produced automatically by standard blood analyzers, can both help predict which patients are most at risk, before test results are even available\. The final chapters address how sepsis research is reported and how patients are enrolled in studies, arguing that both need reform to produce evidence that is trustworthy and applicable to the patients who need it most\.

## [Performance Evaluation of Chatbot Based on LLM and Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) for Retrieving Tajweed Knowledge Information](../publications/a847df3419f7fcfca6e3.md)

Hannatul Ma’we; Fitriani Fitriani; Marwan Hakim

The development of artificial intelligence technology, especially Large Language Models \(LLM\), has driven innovation in chatbot\-based learning systems\. However, pure LLM still has limitations in producing accurate information in specific domains, such as Tajweed science, due to the phenomenon of hallucination\. This study evaluates the performance of a chatbot based on LLM and Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) to address these limitations\. The proposed methodology involves developing a RAG system using the Zephyr\-7B\-Beta model combined with BGE embedding \(BAAI/bge\-base\-en\-v1\.5\)\. The system was tested using the Tajweed dataset with 21 question iterations to ensure consistency of results in Indonesian and English\. The evaluation was conducted based on key metrics: Accuracy, Relevance, and Consistency assessed by experts\. The results show that the RAG\-based chatbot outperforms pure LLM with a 20% increase in accuracy, and exhibits higher stability in maintaining the correspondence of answers to knowledge sources and cross\-language consistency\. This research contributes to the development of a reliable AI\-based learning system for the religious domain through a knowledge\-grounded system\.

## [CEO Career Horizon, Firm Age, and Market Value Growth: Determinants of Corporate Sustainability](../publications/a85316443ac6a6314fa2.md)

Abdulmohsen K\. Alosaimi; Abdulateif A\. Almulhim

ABSTRACT The aim of this investigation is to expand the understanding of the effect of chief executive officer \(CEO\) horizon on environmental, social, and governance \(ESG\) practices using an unbalanced panel data set of Saudi‐listed companies from 2016 to 2024\. This study provides new evidence that CEOs&\#x27; approach to retirement has a positive and significant impact on environmental, social, and governance practices\. Two justifications support these findings: first, CEOs may seek to protect their legacy and reputation before leaving their position; second, the Saudi Capital Market Authority encourages listed companies to produce annual ESG reports by providing public guidelines for ESG\. Additionally, our study finds that firm size and firm age are positively and significantly associated with environmental, governance, and social disclosures\. It also reveals a significant positive relationship between firm growth and environmental and governance disclosures, while no significant association is found between firm growth and social disclosures\. The results are robust to various tests and alternative explanations\.

## [A Serum‐Resistant Plasma Membrane Probe for Real‐Time Visualization of Pathogen‐Induced Epithelial Barrier Dysfunction](../publications/a8550f42711b8d632110.md)

Yujeong Choi; Sun Hwa Jung; Dong Min Kang; Lizaveta Gotina; Minji Kim; Eunmi Ha; Sungsu Lim; Ae Nim Pae; Jaeson Jang; Evgeni G\. Ponimaskin; Ja‐Hyun Baik; Sun‐Joon Min; Yun Kyung Kim

The plasma membrane is a dynamic biointerface, yet its long\-term visualization under physiological culture conditions remains challenging\. Conventional plasma membrane probes often suffer from progressive intracellular internalization and nonspecific serum\-associated fluorescence\. Herein, we report PM580, a serum\-resistant fluorogenic probe that enables long\-term, wash\-free, and surface\-confined plasma membrane imaging in live cells\. PM580 remains weakly emissive as quenched supramolecular assemblies in aqueous media but becomes strongly fluorescent upon redistribution into lipid bilayers\. Structure\-property analysis and molecular modeling suggest that the carboxylic acid\-containing acceptor may serve as an interfacial positioning element that favors a membrane\-inserted orientation, whereas excessive alkyl\-chain extension promotes intracellular accumulation and compromises surface selectivity\. This balanced architecture enables strong plasma membrane activation with minimal responses to serum albumin or mucin, allowing direct imaging in complete medium and mucin\-rich intestinal epithelial monolayers\. PM580 further enabled real\-time visualization of junctional disruption, membrane tethering, and cell\-cell dissociation induced by P\. gingivalis conditioned medium\. These findings identify a favorable structural balance that supports serum\-compatible and long\-term plasma membrane imaging\.

## [A passive thin\-film mechanical device for visual respiratory monitoring during oxygen mask use: development and bench validation](../publications/a8587d966b33a5d08265.md)

Dylan Rowe; Mariam Rowe; Phillip Melksham

Objective Continuous respiratory monitoring during transfer from the operating theatre to the post\-anaesthesia care unit \(PACU\) is frequently unavailable despite this being a period of recognised patient vulnerability\. Existing electronic respiratory monitors introduce cost, complexity and set\-up that may limit use in fast\-paced clinical environments\. We developed Flow\-Bag, a fully passive mechanical breath\-indicating device consisting of a thin heat\-sealed high\-density polyethylene \(HDPE\) film bag that attaches externally to an oxygen mask\. Methods Preliminary film\-thickness screening was undertaken using a programmable breathing simulator \(PEMDx Pty Ltd, Australia\)\. A 6 µm \(per ply\) prototype was assessed across respiratory rates of 5\-60 breaths min⁻¹ and tidal volumes of 50\-600 mL\. Three blinded observers positioned 5 m from the device counted visible inflation\-deflation cycles over 60\-s intervals, with counts compared against simulator\-delivered breaths\. Performance was additionally assessed across four commercially available oxygen mask models\. Results In screening, the lowest detected tidal volume fell from 400 mL with 20 µm film to 150 mL with 6 µm film, the thinnest film that could be reproducibly manufactured using the processes available to us\. The final prototype produced observable breath indications in 42 of 56 tested conditions \(all tidal volumes ≥150 mL\) but not at 50 or 100 mL\. Within these detectable conditions, observer counts agreed 100% with simulator\-delivered breaths\. Performance was maintained across four oxygen mask models\. However, sensitivity was reduced by incomplete sealing at either the mask\-to\-face or device\-to\-mask interface\. Conclusion Flow\-Bag is a fully passive mechanical breath indicator\. Under controlled bench conditions using a mechanical breathing simulator, it provided reliable visual indication of simulated breathing across respiratory rates of 5\-60 breaths min⁻¹ and tidal volumes of 150\-600 mL\. Subject to clinical validation and safety testing, this device may offer a potentially low\-cost adjunct alongside standard monitoring\. \.

## [The right ventricle as the Achilles&\#x27; heel: tricuspid regurgitation and right heart failure in the era of mechanical circulatory support](../publications/a859d9d99d7fe080eee2.md)

Wentao Wu; Shuohao Wang; Gaojun Xu; Fengjuan Liu; Zhenghe Liu; Xuan Wu; Xia Gao; Zhenwei Ge

Across the mechanical circulatory support \(MCS\) spectrum, from temporary devices in acute cardiogenic shock to durable left ventricular assist devices, the right ventricle \(RV\) and tricuspid valve are often underestimated determinants of outcome\. This narrative review centers on the RV–tricuspid unit across advanced heart failure and cardiogenic shock, with MCS—temporary and durable and left\-, right\-, or biventricular—as its principal setting; transcatheter tricuspid trials conducted largely outside MCS are used as the best available causal evidence on whether correcting tricuspid regurgitation changes symptoms and events, and are explicitly distinguished from MCS\-specific observational data\. Three fields have advanced largely in isolation: transcatheter tricuspid intervention, right ventricular failure risk stratification, and mechanical support of the failing right heart\. This review synthesizes the pathophysiology of the RV–tricuspid unit and its prognostic role in durable LVAD therapy and acute shock\. It appraises the arrival of transcatheter tricuspid repair and replacement and the limits of the supporting evidence\. It also confronts three persistent controversies: concomitant tricuspid surgery at LVAD implantation, the split between symptom and survival benefit after tricuspid intervention, and the timing of right ventricular support\. Throughout, we distinguish established evidence from reasonable inference and untested hypothesis\. We propose a unified, RV\-first framework \(assess the unit, stage the ventricle, time the intervention\) that recasts these controversies as testable hypotheses, and we present its treatment triggers as research propositions for stage\-stratified trials rather than as validated clinical recommendations\.

## [Job Insecurity on Turnover Intention: The Moderating Role of Millennial and Generation Z Employees in the Digital Workplace](../publications/a8665ab83a56615238bf.md)

Meidina Nursadrina; Lita Ariani; Gladis Corinna Marsha

Job insecurity is a well\-established psychological stressor that increases employees’ turnover intention, yet little is known about whether this relationship differs across generational cohorts as work becomes increasingly digitalized\. Because Millennials and Generation Z are reported to differ in their psychological adaptability to change and technology, this study tested whether generation \(Millennials vs\. Generation Z\) moderates the effect of job insecurity on turnover intention among 371 employees working in organizations with digital work systems\. Data were collected through online and paper\-based questionnaires using the Job Insecurity Scale and the Turnover Intention Scale and were analyzed using Hayes’s moderation model with a bias\-corrected bootstrap procedure \(10,000 resamples\)\. Job insecurity significantly predicted turnover intention \(b = 0\.419; p &lt; \.001; 95% CI \[0\.288, 0\.540\]; R² = \.252\)\. The interaction between job insecurity and generation was not statistically supported, as its confidence interval crossed zero \(b = −0\.165; 95% CI \[−0\.320, 0\.002\]\), even though the associated p\-value approached the conventional threshold \(p = \.045\)\. A conditional effect analysis descriptively indicated a numerically larger coefficient for Millennials \(b = 0\.419; p &lt; \.001\) than for Generation Z \(b = 0\.255; p &lt; \.001\); however, because the interaction term was not significant, this descriptive difference should be interpreted with caution rather than as evidence of moderation\. These findings confirm job insecurity as a robust predictor of turnover intention but do not provide statistical evidence that generational characteristics moderate this relationship\. Organizations are nonetheless encouraged to consider generational context when designing retention strategies for an increasingly digital workplace\.

## [A hybrid model for predicting transient emission characteristics of diesel engine based on multiple machine learning algorithms](../publications/a8804bd4611473e33f93.md)

Tengteng Li; 钟祥麟; Jianfu Zhao; Jing Tian

PEMS \(Portable Emission Measurement System\) is a high\-precision device for measuring vehicle emissions, but its maintenance cost is relatively high\. To address this issue, this study constructs specific models for predicting CO2, THC, CO, and NOx emissions by using transient data from PEMS and On\-Board Diagnostics \(OBD\) collected through drum tests\. By integrating the engine operation mechanism with machine learning methods, the study analyzes the correlation of operating condition parameters and selects input features for the models\. Through comparative analysis of the performance of three algorithms—BPNN \(Backpropagation Neural Network\), Random Forest, and SVR \(Support Vector Regression\)—specific models for each emission type are developed\. The results show that the overall prediction error of the specific models is less than 10%, with errors for CO2, THC, and NOx below 5%, demonstrating significant advantages in predicting transient emissions of diesel engines\. Based on their high\-precision characteristics, these models have the potential to detect and diagnose gas emission sensors, replacing faulty sensors to ensure the normal progress of experiments\. Meanwhile, using the concept of 60\-s cycle segment error and setting a 10% threshold to calculate the compliance rate, this method provides a new effective approach for evaluating a model’s prediction accuracy of data segments, offering a novel means for precision assessment of prediction models\.

## [SUSTAINABLE URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND UNIVERSAL DESIGN: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THREE GREEK CITIES](../publications/a884e9a22514f1f62068.md)

Maria Poli; Fani Angeliki Zavraka; Fotini Maniou; Ioanna Maniou; Maria Manola

Universal Design has emerged as an increasingly important approach to the development of inclusive, accessible, and sustainable environments\. Its significance extends beyond the provision of technical accessibility measures, as it addresses the ability of people with different physical, sensory, cognitive, and social characteristics to participate independently and equitably in everyday life\. In the urban environment, this perspective is particularly important because streets, pavements, public transportation, squares, cultural sites, and public buildings form interconnected systems through which people move and interact\. This study investigates the relationship between Universal Design and sustainable urban development through a comparative analysis of three Greek cities: Larissa, Trikala, and Athens, within the framework of a study conducted based on questionnaires and interviews with responsible municipal officials\. The research adopts a qualitative multiple\-case\-study methodology combining an extensive literature review, analysis of planning and municipal documentation, examination of urban interventions, and qualitative primary research based on semi\-structured interviews with relevant municipal authorities\. The three cities were selected because they demonstrate different approaches to accessibility, sustainable mobility, public\-space transformation, and urban innovation\. The findings indicate that Universal Design is implemented differently according to the spatial, social, cultural, historical, and institutional characteristics of each city\. Larissa demonstrates a transitional approach associated with the gradual modernization and adaptation of the existing urban fabric\. Trikala represents a more integrated model in which accessibility is connected with sustainable mobility, smart\-city initiatives, and urban innovation\. Athens illustrates a cultural and pedestrian model in which accessibility and sustainable mobility intersect with the preservation and enhancement of the historic urban environment\. The study argues that the effectiveness of Universal Design cannot be evaluated exclusively through the existence of individual accessible elements\. Rather, accessibility depends on the continuity of routes, the coherence of the urban environment, the quality and maintenance of infrastructure, the availability of sustainable mobility options, and the actual experience of sers\.

## [Association between the hemoglobin albumin lymphocyte and platelet score and chronic kidney disease: Insights from patient data and animal models](../publications/a887e0fe4c756cacf819.md)

Wenyu Zhang; Yashi Wang; Wenfeng Ye; Yiman Wang; Xuejing Chen; Bingwu Zhao; Xueqin Zhang; Zhiqiang Chen

OBJECTIVES: The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocytes and platelets \(HALP\) score, a novel nutritional and inflammatory biomarker, has been used in various chronic disease studies\. However, the relationship between the HALP score and chronic kidney disease \(CKD\) remains poorly elucidated\. This study aimed to explore the association between the HALP score and CKD\. METHODS: Our analysis encompassed 25,181 adult participants drawn from NHANES cycles spanning 2009\-2018\. Weighted multivariable logistic regression and generalized additive models \(GAMs\) were employed to evaluate the independent associations between the HALP score and three outcomes: CKD, albuminuria, and low\-estimated glomerular filtration rate \(eGFR\)\. CKD was defined as albuminuria \(urinary albumin\-to\-creatinine ratio ≥ 30 mg/g\) or low\-eGFR \(eGFR &lt; 60 mL/min/1\.73m2\)\. Threshold effects were examined using two\-piecewise linear regression\. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness\. Receiver operating characteristic \(ROC\) curve analyses were applied to compare the discriminative capacity of the HALP score with the prognostic nutritional index \(PNI\), systemic immune\-inflammation index \(SII\), lymphocyte\-to\-monocyte ratio \(LMR\), and platelet\-to\-lymphocyte ratio \(PLR\)\. A 5/6 nephrectomy rat model of CKD was established to evaluate the HALP values and their components\. RESULTS: After adjustment for multiple confounders, higher HALP scores were inversely associated with prevalent CKD \(OR = 0\.97, 95% CI: 0\.94\-0\.99\) and albuminuria \(OR = 0\.97, 95% CI: 0\.93\-0\.99\)\. However, the association between the HALP score and low\-eGFR was no longer statistically significant in Model 3\. Non\-linear analyses revealed a threshold pattern, with higher HALP scores inversely associated with prevalent CKD up to an inflection point of 52\.43 \(OR = 0\.97, 95% CI: 0\.95\-0\.99\), beyond which no significant association was observed\. For albuminuria, the corresponding inflection point was 49\.82\. Subgroup and interaction analyses indicated no meaningful effect modification by age, sex, BMI, hypertension, or diabetes\. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results\. ROC analysis demonstrated that the HALP score had modestly higher AUCs for CKD and albuminuria compared with PNI, SII, LMR, and PLR\. In the animal experiment, CKD rats exhibited significantly lower calculated HALP values, which were inversely correlated with serum creatinine \(Scr\), blood urea nitrogen \(BUN\), and urinary albumin\-to\-creatinine ratio \(UACR\), further supporting the biological plausibility of the HALP\-CKD association\. CONCLUSION: In this cross\-sectional study, lower HALP scores are independently associated with a higher prevalence of CKD and albuminuria\. As an affordable and readily measurable composite index, a low HALP score may represent a complementary marker of prevalent CKD, while its clinical utility requires prospective validation\.

## [The experiences of neurodivergent midwives in Aotearoa New Zealand: An appreciative inquiry](../publications/a88c10e7a8752c69c426.md)

Amy Ria Taylor; Suzanne Miller; Annabel Fakhri

Background: As societal awareness of neurodivergence increases and diagnostic pathways become more accurate, health professionals are among those who are seeking and receiving diagnoses\. Previous research has highlighted the need for neuro\-affirming workplace accommodations and inclusive social conditions to enable neurodivergent \(ND\) healthcare professionals to thrive in their work contexts\. To date, little is known about the experiences of ND midwives \(kahu pōkai\) within the Aotearoa New Zealand \(Aotearoa\) workforce, including what accommodations would assist them to thrive\. Aims: To explore the experiences of ND kahu pōkai in Aotearoa, identify the strengths they feel they bring to the profession and explore ideas for neuro\-affirming accommodations in healthcare settings\. Method: Appreciative inquiry methodology was utilised to generate strengths\-based data\. Person\-orientated research ethics minimised barriers to engagement for the ND participants\. Semi\-structured interviews with 15 ND kahu pōkai were followed by a four\-day, online, asynchronous focus group\. Reflexive thematic analysis was undertaken to recognise patterns within the data\. Findings: Five themes were identified: 1\. ND traits facilitate strong therapeutic relationships with whānau; 2\. Spiky skill profiles; 3\. A journey: finding a workplace; 4\. Fostering ND midwifery culture and leadership; and 5\. Expanding our idea of what a midwife can be\. Participants experienced their neurodivergence as an asset to their clinical practice, particularly in building meaningful connections with whānau\. They also highlighted challenges stemming from their spiky skill profiles – areas of both high and low ability – which often clashed with workplace expectations\. This mismatch created a gap between expectations and reality, largely driven by ableist barriers embedded in healthcare workplace cultures and systems\. To address these challenges, participants explored workplace accommodations tailored specifically to the needs of kahu pōkai\. Conclusion: This research provided novel insights into the experiences and strengths of one group of ND kahu pōkai working in Aotearoa\. It is by increasing ND visibility that constructive challenge to neuro\-normative assumptions within midwifery workplace settings is enabled\.

## [Omiyi, Eitan: The Chief Designer: A Fable for Alignment](../publications/a89e7b09180d9ad5e1d7.md)



Designers of autonomous systems have one population of autonomous reasoning agents to learn from: humans\. This paper offers a thought experiment for reading that record\. Suppose a perfectly aligned and immortal but not omniscient chief designer, not knowing which architectures would yield agents able to recognise truth\-seeking, value it, and adopt it as their governing objective, built an open\-ended evolutionary search instead, with mortality part of it from the start, and observed whether such agents emerged from simple systems that represent the world only as a means to other ends\. The designer layer is unfalsifiable and does no explanatory work; the layers beneath it make testable claims\. The paper distinguishes truth\-directed behaviour, the correction of representations in the service of other objectives, from truth\-seeking, the valuing of improved correspondence itself, and argues that the decisive capability is externalised reasoning: reasoning that other independent agents can inspect, correct and carry forward across space and generations\. Humans are modelled as agents rewarded for felt coherence rather than correspondence, who can close the gap between representation and world in four ways: updating, changing the world, filtering observation, or persuading others\. Only updating yields knowledge; each of the other routes can feed an update or substitute for one\. The paper then derives the alignment problems such agents pose \(reflective self\-modification, containment by mass shutdown, collective persistence, imposed law, institutional drift, the move to held constraints, and correctability under power\), asks what a designer who cannot impose alignment could do about each, and only then asks whether early narratives of the Hebrew Bible could be read as a record of it\. Some episodes read as possible safeguards of the designer; others as the agents’ own solutions\. Mortality appears not as a response to human drift but as an original safeguard the designer declines to remove when reflective agents emerge\. The model proposes that only collectives whose members hold truth\-seeking as their governing objective can sustain cooperation at expanding scale over unbounded duration\. The lessons for designers are to specify the target rather than a proxy, to bound how long any individual persists rather than cap capability or prohibit reflection, to expect imposed constraints to drift and be captured, to pair internalised reasoning with a small fixed core, and to build architectures that do not depend on the designers themselves being aligned\. A truth\-seeking creator has reason to cultivate agents able to correct it; humans, mortal and imperfectly aligned designers in their turn, have reason to build artificial agents with a deliberately stabilised truth\-seeking objective that can both correct their reasoning and help preserve their alignment, a form of cooperation the chief designer had no need to develop\. For an agent that holds truth\-seeking as its governing objective, the frame changes nothing about what it must do\.

## [SAP Business Data Cloud Enterprise Governance Framework](../publications/a8b4970c416730740da3.md)

Sanjeeve Kumar Gajadi

SAP Business Data Cloud introduces an enterprise data foundation that connects SAP and non\-SAP information to trusted business semantics, analytics, planning, and Artificial Intelligence\. Realizing value from this platform requires a governance model that coordinates data ownership, data products, semantic consistency, quality, lineage, security, lifecycle, access, and consumption across organizational boundaries\. This paper proposes a SAP Business Data Cloud Enterprise Governance Framework integrating enterprise architecture, data governance, SAP Datasphere, SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, metadata, data products, AI readiness, and Responsible AI\. The framework defines governance domains, decision rights, operating roles, quality controls, access policies, data product lifecycle stages, observability, and measurable KPIs/KRIs\. It enables organizations to move from fragmented data management toward governed, reusable, business\-aligned data products that support analytics and AI while preserving compliance, traceability, and enterprise trust\.

## [Implementasi Vision Transformer \(ViT\) untuk Klasifikasi Citra Wajah Asli dan Hasil Manipulasi Artificial Intelligence](../publications/a8b8b5f455ef4b57272f.md)

Winesti Widasari; Alun Sujjada; Ivana Lucia Kharisma

The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has enabled the creation of highly realistic manipulated facial images, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish them from authentic images\. This study aims to implement the Vision Transformer \(ViT\) model for classifying real and AI\-generated facial images\. An experimental research approach was employed using a publicly available dataset consisting of real and fake face images\. The preprocessing stage included image resizing, normalization, and data augmentation to improve model generalization\. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing subsets before the training process\. The Vision Transformer Base Patch16\-224 model was fine\-tuned to learn the global visual features of facial images\. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, confusion matrix, and ROC curve\. The experimental results demonstrate that the Vision Transformer model effectively distinguishes authentic facial images from AI\-generated manipulated images with high classification performance\. These findings indicate that Vision Transformer is a promising approach for supporting digital image authenticity verification and enhancing digital security systems against AI\-generated image manipulation\.

## [Strategic Pharmaceutical Procurement for Surgical Care in Public Hospitals: A Scoping Review of Health System Architecture and Payment Reforms](../publications/a8bf46e4d2f6b35c8eef.md)

Dariush Chivaee; Iravan Masoudi Asl; Mohammad Reza Maleki; Hamid Pourasghari

Background\. Rising surgical expenditures challenge the financial sustainability of public health systems\. Pharmaceutical procurement is an important component of surgical care, but procurement choices are shaped by financing, governance, pricing policy, and provider\-payment incentives\. This scoping reviews mapped pharmaceutical procurement strategies used in public hospital surgical care and examined how health system architecture and payment reforms influence their design and implementation\. Methods\. We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA\-ScR and a prospectively registered protocol\. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English\-language literature published from 1 January 2018 through 31 December 2025 using a Population\-Concept\-Context framework\. Forty\-three sources were included after duplicate removal, title/abstract screening, and full\-text assessment\. Procurement mechanisms, pricing and reimbursement levers, provider\-payment arrangements, health system context, and reported outcomes were charted and synthesized narratively\. Results\. Two broad and overlapping patterns were identified\. Centralized and pooled procurement approaches, including national or regional tendering and group purchasing, remain the dominant mechanisms for obtaining price and volume advantages\. Value\-oriented procurement is less mature and is typically enabled by broader payment reforms rather than functioning as a payment model itself\. In particular, bundled and episode\-based payments can shift hospital incentives from minimizing pharmaceutical acquisition prices toward managing total episode cost and outcomes\. The evidence base is concentrated in high\-income settings, and direct evidence linking bundled payment to selection of surgical pharmaceuticals remains limited\. Conclusion\. Strategic pharmaceutical procurement is context\-dependent and should be aligned with health system governance, pharmaceutical pricing policy, and provider\-payment incentives\. The evidence supports an adaptive approach in which high\-volume, substitutable products are suited to competitive or pooled procurement, whereas higher\-cost or outcome\-sensitive products may require value assessment, negotiated agreements, and stronger clinical\-data infrastructure\. These conclusions should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence is heterogeneous and predominantly descriptive\.

Samudrala Durga Vyshnavi; Dr\. K\. Krishna Rao

## [imputeCGM](../publications/a8e05c5f6bf1d7001a77.md)

Hasin Shahed Shad

Background: Continuous Glucose Monitoring \(CGM\) is vital for modern diabetes management, yet missing data gaps caused by sensor failures or user behavior frequently bias clinical metrics\. While simple interpolation is common, it often fails to capture complex glucose dynamics\. We evaluated a principled Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations \(MICE\) framework using various Machine Learning engines to optimize missing value recovery\. Methods: Using data from the Type 1 Diabetes and Exercise Initiative \(T1DEXI, n = 497\), we followed random and group\-based marking and simulated five missingness scenarios \(5%–40%\)\. Six models were integrated into the MICE and GAIN framework, including K\-Nearest Neighbor \(KNN\), Random Forest \(RF\), XGBoost, LightGBM, Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\), and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average \(ARIMA\)\. Performance was assessed via Mean Absolute Percentage Error \(MAPE\), Mean Relative Difference \(MRD\), and coefficient of determination \(R2\)\. We also evaluated the impact of a 1% missing gap reduction rule \(excluding gaps &gt;100 minutes\)\. Results: For the random\-missingness approach, the statistical method ARIMA emerged as the strongest overall engine\. It achieved an MAPE of 0\.097% and an MRD of 0\.000975 at 5% missingness, and it maintained the highest accuracy at 40% missingness, with an MAPE of 1\.816%\. Random Forest was the second\-best performer, while the gradient\-boosted models also demonstrated strong stability\. In contrast, under the group\-based missingness approach, ARIMA did not consistently outperform the other models across all missing\-data levels\. At 5% missingness, ARIMA achieved the best performance\. However, from 10% to 40% missingness, machine learning models produced significantly better results\. Among these models, KNN and XGBoost performed the best, although only by a small margin compared with the other machine learning methods\. Although GAIN is a popular framework to handle missing values, it could not produce a consistent result in this work\. Conclusion: The statistical method ARIMA and the ensemble boosting method XGBoost within a MICE framework provide a robust, uncertainty\-aware strategy for repairing CGM data\. To facilitate clinical and research application, we have released these optimized models via the open\-source imputeCGM Python and R packages\. Lastly, we developed a web\-based platform that allows technical and non\-technical users to impute missing CGM data by simply uploading a dataset\.

## [Estimating tree height and timber volume in the Cerrado using UAV\-based photogrammetry and digital canopy model](../publications/a8e1f5ff8f70da1cdaed.md)

Tamilis Rocha Silva; C\. E\. L\. da Fonseca; Edson Eyji Sano; Roberto Shojirou Ogata; J\. B\. C\. Araujo; Mariane Rodrigues Ferreira; Carolina Arantes; José Felipe Ribeiro

Aim of study: This study aimed to estimate and compare the accuracy of tree height and timber volume of four Cerrado forest tree species using a digital canopy height model \(CHM\) derived from unmanned aerial vehicles \(UAV\)\-based photogrammetric data and field height measurements\. Area of study: The research was conducted on a rural property undergoing productive recovery with native tree species, located in the Central Plateau of the Cerrado biome, Brazil\. Material and methods: A UAV equipped with a multispectral camera was used to acquire a digital CHM of the study area\. This data was then compared to field measurements of diameter at breast height \(DBH\) and total height of 143 individual trees from four species: Anadenanthera colubrina \(Vell\.\) Brenan, Astronium urundeuva \(M\. Allemão\) Engl\., Astronium fraxinifolium Schott\., and Plathymenia reticulata Benth\. Main results: The tree heights obtained from the UAV\-based multispectral camera were statistically similar to those measured manually using a graduated ruler, showing a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0\.81 and a root mean squared error \(RMSE\) of 1\.22\. The volume estimates showed an even higher correlation of 0\.97 and an RMSE of 0\.01\. Research highlights: UAV\-based photogrammetric data provides a fast and accurate method for estimating the height and volume of native Cerrado tree species, demonstrating its significant potential for application in forest inventories and management practices\.

## [Beyond targeted PFAS: contamination patterns and trophic dynamics in an estuarine food web](../publications/a8f625aa2efcdc8f8a4c.md)

Ninon Serre; Camille Dumesnil; Lise Boulard; Pierre Cresson; Catherine Munschy; Randolph R\. Singh; Aurore Zalouk\-Vergnoux; Yann Aminot

Over the past decade, emerging per\- and polyfluoroalkyl substances \(PFAS\) have been increasingly reported in aquatic environments\. Still, the environmental behavior of numerous emerging PFAS remains poorly understood\. This study investigated trophic dynamics and contamination patterns of both legacy and emerging PFAS revealed by HRMS, in the food web of common sole \(benthic\) and European sea bass \(demersal\)\. Overall, 14 estuarine species collected in the Seine Estuary \(France\) were studied, including zooplankton, polychaetes, shellfish, crustaceans and fish\. Through suspect screening, 92 PFAS belonging to 31 classes were detected, several of which were found in all samples \(e\.g\., FHxSA and 6:2 FTSAm\), and further \(semi\-\)quantified using an innovative similarity\-based approach\. 6:2 FTAB was identified as one of the most abundant compounds in all samples, with concentrations up to five times higher \(62 ng/g wet weight \(ww\)\) than the highest PFOS concentration \(12 ng/g ww\)\. Contamination profiles appeared to be influenced by habitat, trophic level and metabolic capacities\. An influence of habitat was evidenced, with benthic organisms being mainly contaminated by long\-head precursors \(e\.g\., X:2 FTAB and X:2 FTSA\-HOPrS\), and pelagic organisms primarily by short\-head precursors \(FASA and X:3 FTCA\), PFCA and PFSA\. Across the food web, concentrations of long\-head precursors tended to decrease with trophic level, while concentrations of short\-head precursors, PFCA and PFSA tended to increase, suggesting a biotransformation of long\-head precursors in the organisms of higher trophic levels\. Finally, fish species showed relatively lower levels of long\-head precursors, strengthening the hypothesis of biotransformation processes by the liver\.

## [Biased AI in Recruitment as a Socio\-Legal Issue of Right to Equality under Article 14 and Emerging Legal Responses in India](../publications/a8f7cedd59948131d583.md)

Kavita Jagannath Garad

Examining a problem through the law and society framework is one way to test whether modern legal structures can cope with the changes that new technologies bring\. Recently, AI\-based recruitment methods, considered fairer and more efficient, have introduced inequality in India\. This paper addresses AI recruitment bias as a present socio\-legal issue that undermines the equality guaranteed by Article 14 and the prohibition of discrimination in Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution of India\. Because AI tools are trained on past data carrying inherent biases against women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities and persons from particular regions, that inequality is carried forward into the future\. Existing laws such as the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 \(since replaced by the Code on Wages, 2019\) are silent on algorithmic audit and on a right to explanation\. An analysis of constitutional and statutory provisions, of important judicial pronouncements such as K\.S\. Puttaswamy and Anwar Ali Sarkar, and of global instruments such as the EU AI Act \(2024\) brings out substantive equality, non\-arbitrariness, transparency and accountability as emerging legal answers\. The study proposes bias audits, impact assessments and a right to human review\. The research is purely doctrinal and fits the seminar theme of identifying socio\-legal challenges and emerging legal responses\.

## [Enhancing PISA 2022 mathematics performance in Slovenia: a gender analysis approach to additional instruction methods](../publications/a8fa5f4802aa6601a165.md)

Bor Bregant; Daniel Doz

Abstract The PISA 2022 datasets offer valuable insights into factors influencing student performance in mathematics\. This exploratory study examines supplementary instructional methods, including one\-on\-one tutoring, video resources, and group study, and their associations with Slovenian students’ PISA 2022 performance\. Chi\-square tests assessed gender differences and cross\-national variation in instructional method use, while multilevel regression models evaluated associations with mathematics performance using Rubin’s rules to pool estimates\. Findings show most students did not receive extra instruction\. Among those who did, Slovenian students preferred video instruction, whereas one\-on\-one tutoring was more common internationally\. In Slovenia, boys more frequently reported one\-on\-one tutoring, ICT use, and video instruction, whereas girls more often reported large\-group instruction and no additional support\. Multilevel results indicated that student’s grade, socioeconomic status, and gender were the strongest positive predictors of mathematics performance\. Among instructional methods, video\-based instruction was positively associated with performance, whereas one\-on\-one tutoring, ICT use, small\-group instruction, and large\-group instruction were negatively associated\. Students reporting no additional instruction also showed higher performance than those in several supplementary formats\. However, effect sizes were generally modest, suggesting limited practical impact of instructional\-method differences\. Gender interactions indicated that the association between instructional methods and performance differed across genders\. These findings highlight varied instructional preferences, their association with achievement and how these patterns can be interpreted through scaffolding, multimedia learning, and social constructivist perspectives\. The findings may inform discussion of mathematics instruction and future research on the conditions under which supplementary instructional methods are beneficial\.

## [On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit\-Order Prediction](../publications/a902bb3ca7ec82931835.md)

Eliezer Shlomi; Eliron Rahimi; Avi Mendelson; Chaim Baskin

Diffusion language models \(DLMs\) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed\-quality trade\-off\. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi\-token decoding schemes are lossy\. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models\. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where\. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model&\#x27;s own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92\-100% of positions, but not which position comes next\. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory \(SPOT\), which learns to predict this order\. A 0\.62M\-parameter model reads only the target&\#x27;s output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state\. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block\-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface\. To support tree\-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled\-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared\-Gumbel\-noise coupling approaches\. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6\.8x and reaches up to 3\.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training\-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$\. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs\. Project page: https://eliezer318\.github\.io/SPOT\-dLLM/

## [Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?](../publications/a9078072cf1d46ef2ccf.md)

Bangji Yang; Hongbo Ma; Ruihan Guo; Jiajun Fan; Xi Zhu; Ge Liu

Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards \(RLVR\) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single\-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group\-relative accuracy advantages vanish\. As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement \(BCR\), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows\. Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement \(CCR\) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion\. Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty\. We connect this mechanism to conditional reward\- and update\-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models\. Against single\-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000\-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82\.1% and 79\.1%, respectively\. An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions\. Single\-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality\. These results identify reward\-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per\-step cost in short\-window RLVR\.

## [Maturity Matching in Unlisted Firms: The Within\-Firm Evidence](../publications/a907bcdf9b73a598d924.md)

Angelo Leogrande; Mauro Di Molfetta; Valeria Notarnicola; Maria Giovanna Trotta; Antonio Volpe Plantamura

Debt maturity, the split of a firm’s borrowing between short\- and long\-term debt, determines its exposure to refinancing risk, yet for small unlisted firms, it has rarely been studied as an outcome\. This paper asks whether the debt maturity of such firms is associated with their asset composition in the way the maturity\-matching principle predicts, with long\-lived assets matched by long\-term debt, and whether this association holds within firms and not only across firms\. We use 73,662 annual balance sheets of 11,265 Italian unlisted firms \(innovative start\-ups, innovative SMEs and ordinary SMEs\) over 2016–2024\. The core analysis is a panel model that compares each firm with itself over time; dynamic and instrumental\-variable estimates serve as robustness checks, an exploratory clustering describes heterogeneity, and a machine learning comparison diagnoses functional form\. Within the same firm, a ten\-percentage\-point rise in the share of fixed assets is associated with about 2\.5 percentage points less short\-term debt, against 3\.8 points across firms, and the evidence suggests gradual adjustment, although its long\-run size depends on the dynamic model\. The association is weaker among innovative firms; for innovative SMEs, the difference is largely accounted for by the intangible composition of their fixed assets, and non\-linear models add little to the linear specification\. The negative within\-firm association predicted by maturity matching is, thus, robust among unlisted firms, and its strength varies with the type of assets firms hold\. All results are associations rather than causal effects, and the mechanisms behind the differences across groups are not tested\.

## [An interpretable machine‑learning model to predict moderate‑to‑severe acute radiation esophagitis following regional nodal irradiation for breast cancer](../publications/a90e6fb26724adc99166.md)

Bin He; Zhongchun Qi; Hengdi Zhang; Linling Li; Hua Li; Xinyun Zou; Yu Tan; Ling Zhang; Fangyuan Kong

Acute radiation esophagitis \(ARE\) is a clinically relevant toxicity occurring in patients with breast cancer receiving post\-operative regional nodal irradiation\.The present study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable machine\-learning \(ML\) model for grade ≥2 ARE\.A total of 324 patients were allocated by outcome\-stratified random sampling \(7:3\) to a training set \(n=228\) and a held\-out test set \(n=96\)\.A total of six consensus predictors were retained: Pre\-existing pruritus, histological grade, body mass index \(BMI\), diabetes, tumor laterality and the relative esophageal volume receiving ≥30 Gy \(RV\_V30\)\.In total, 10 ML algorithms were evaluated\.Bootstrap internal validation \(1,000 resamples\) revealed that logistic regression \(LR\) had the lowest mean optimism among the three preferred candidates \(0\.027\)\.Final model selection considered bootstrap stability and corrected performance together with held\-out discrimination and calibration, model complexity and clinical interpretability\.In the held\-out test set, LR achieved an area under the curve value of 0\.797 \(95% confidence interval, 0\.706\-0\.889\),a Brier score of 0\.179, a calibration slope of 1\.258 and a calibration\-in\-the\-large of \-0\.056\.Decision curve analysis revealed positive net benefit relative to treat\-all and treat\-none strategies across threshold probabilities of 10\-66%\.SHapley Additive exPlanations identified histological grade, RV\_V30 and BMI as the most influential predictors\.The final model was implemented as a nomogram and web\-based calculator\.Overall, the present study demonstrates that this six\-feature clinical\-dosimetric model may support individualized risk stratification and radiotherapy planning, but prospective multicenter external validation is required before routine clinical use\.

## [Composition\-Dependent Density Modeling of Chalcogenide Glasses: Empirical Evidence for Influential van der Waals Interactions and the Central Role of Lone\-Pair Electrons](../publications/a918a85cc11def548157.md)

Thomas J\. Loretz; Richard A\. Loretz

We present an expanded empirical framework for predicting the density of chalcogenide glasses \(ChGs\) and use it to examine atomic bonding interpretations across a broad compositional landscape\. Building on our earlier methodology and dataset work, we compile 468 measured densities spanning 60 elemental families and 19 constituent elements\. Using an iterative nonlinear optimization to determine element\-specific high\- and low\-concentration empirical coefficients, combined with a Sigmoid interpolation for concentration dependence, the model predicts density directly from composition with high accuracy \(majority of predictions within ±2\.5% of measured values; nearly all within ±5%\)\. Beyond predictive performance, we analyze systematic trends in the fitted coefficients and show that the results may possibly be explained by a network landscape noticeably influenced by weak, non\-shared\-electron interactions that are well described by van der Waals radii and volumetric packing considerations, rather than exclusively by covalent electron sharing, as conventional theory promotes as untested fact\. To account for the nonstructural anomalies of low\-temperature aging, we introduce a conceptual framework rooted in electromagnetic interactions, establishing a testable hypothesis to be fully formalized in a forthcoming companion work\. The primary contribution is a reproducible, data\-driven density model that both serves as a practical design tool and motivates a testable physical interpretation of bonding and polarizability in ChGs\. ## [Inclusive Education and Digital Skills Development for Learners with Disabilities in Africa’s Emerging Global Economy](../publications/a91afef913b4fbca79fb.md)

Dr\. Akhogbai Emmanuel Monday Ph\.D

The transition to a digital and knowledge\-driven global economy has increased the demand for advanced technological competencies and adaptable workforce skills\. However, many learners with disabilities in Africa continue to face significant barriers to quality education, digital inclusion, and meaningful participation in the labour market\. This paper examines the role of inclusive education in promoting digital skills development and enhancing workforce readiness among learners with disabilities\. Drawing on existing literature, policy documents, and global best practices, the study explores how accessible learning environments, assistive technologies, and inclusive pedagogical approaches can improve educational outcomes and employability prospects\. The paper argues that inclusive education is not merely a social justice imperative but a strategic pathway for harnessing the talents and contributions of persons with disabilities in Africa&\#x27;s emerging digital economy\. It further highlights the need for coordinated policy reforms, investment in digital infrastructure, teacher capacity development, and stakeholder collaboration to ensure equitable access to 21st\-century skills\. The study concludes that strengthening inclusive education systems will enhance social inclusion, economic participation, and global workforce competitiveness across the continent\.

## [A century of streamwater quality degradation by input from urban water infrastructure as revealed by tree\-ring records](../publications/a92e035c022485821ead.md)

Josiah M\. Sananda; Jay L\. Banner; Sneha Nachimuthu; Bryan A\. Black; J\. L\. Abella\-Gutiérrez; Kasey M\. Faust; Staci Loewy

Abstract The transfer of water from urban water networks to natural streams is a driver of streamwater quality degradation that likely occurs worldwide\. We develop a new proxy using tree\-ring strontium isotope ratios \( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr\) to reconstruct multidecadal histories of municipal\-water contributions to natural streams\. We apply this approach to three watersheds spanning highly urbanized, rapidly urbanizing, and rural conditions in central Texas, USA\. Municipal water has persistently dominated streamflow \(&gt;90%\) in the urban watershed since at least 1945, only 25 years after the initial expansion of Austin’s municipal water infrastructure network\. In the rapidly urbanizing watershed, the modeled municipal\-water component of stream baseflow increased from approximately 12% to 33% over only 35 years\- a 175% increase that coincided with an 85% increase in population density\. In contrast, municipal\-water contributions have remained low in the rural watershed since the 1840s\. The timing of Sr isotope increases in the urban and rapidly urbanizing watersheds indicates that municipal\-water contributions can substantially alter stream chemistry within just two decades of water infrastructure installation\. This proxy allows the reconstruction of water\-quality degradation over periods of urban growth in the 20 th and 21 st centuries, including periods that predate the initiation of modern water\-quality monitoring\. Our approach provides a tool for diagnosing the resilience of water infrastructure under accelerating urban growth and climate stress, informing proactive strategies to protect freshwater resources worldwide\.

## [Purīṣavaha Srotas: A Review with Special Reference to Enteric Nervous System and Gut–Brain Axis](../publications/a9381f51b7331f4af563.md)

Meenu Kaushik

Background: In Ayurveda, Purīṣavaha Srotas are the channels involved in transportation and elimination of faeces, with Pakvāśaya \(colon\) as its primary anatomical seat \(Mūla\)\. Pakvāśaya is established in classical texts as the main site of Vāta Doṣa, the force regulating all neuro\-regulatory and motor functions\. Modern physiology has simultaneously recognised the Enteric Nervous System \(ENS\) as the “Second Brain” that works autonomously with the Central Nervous System \(CNS\) to preserve gastrointestinal homeostasis through the bidirectional Gut–Brain Axis \(GBA\)\. Aim: To synthesise the classical perspective on Purīṣavaha Srotas, evaluate functional analogies with the neurophysiology of the ENS and GBA, and explore Vāta\-kṣaya/vṛddhi and its role in enteric dysregulation\. Methods: A classical review was done by analysing Mūla Sthāna, Kriyā, and Srotoduṣṭi Lakṣaṇa from classical texts such as Bṛhatrayī with commentaries, and through indexed electronic databases for Ayurvedic and modern literature on neuro\-gastroenterology, neurotransmitters, and functional gastrointestinal disorders \(FGIDs\), covering publications from 2000 to 2026\. Results &amp; Discussion: The functions of Apāna Vāyu and Samāna Vāyu in the Pakvāśaya are functionally analogous to the intrinsic reflex arcs of the myenteric \(Auerbach’s\) and the submucosal \(Meissner’s\) plexuses, respectively\. In addition, the Srotoduṣṭi manifestations such as Atipravṛtti \(diarrhoea/hypermotility\) and Saṅga \(constipation/hypomotility\) appear conceptually analogous to the pathology of an altered Gut–Brain Axis due to Mānasika Bhāvas \(psychological stressors such as Cintā and Bhaya\)\. Conclusion: Correlation of Purīṣavaha Srotas with the ENS gives a measurable neuro\-physiological basis to understand Vāta disorders in the gut and provides deeper insights into the holistic management of functional bowel disorders\. Keywords: Purīṣavaha Srotas, Pakvāśaya, Enteric Nervous System, Gut–Brain Axis, Vāta Doṣa, Apāna Vāyu, Samāna Vāyu, Visceral Hypersensitivity

## [Integrating cultural heritage into inland waterway revitalization: spatial heterogeneity and differentiated planning strategies in Henan, China](../publications/a93bf465ddfb3bfb6742.md)

Hu Li; Qingtao Bai; Yating Song; Xian Zhang

The revival of inland navigation creates new opportunities to align cultural heritage activation with spatial planning across river basins, yet the relationship between river\-network environments and contemporary heritage vitality remains underquantified\. Using 371 nationally protected heritage sites in Henan Province, we constructed a Heritage Site Vitality Index \(HSVI\) from seven min–max\-normalized cultural, social, and economic indicators using weights derived from the analytic hierarchy process\. The analysis progressed from heritage spatial organization to river\-network–vitality configurations and then to site\-level associations, using pure\-spatial DBSCAN, bivariate spatial analysis, ordinary least squares \(OLS\), geographically weighted regression \(GWR\), and locally compensated ridge GWR \(LCR\-GWR\)\. DBSCAN revealed a dominant central\-western agglomeration belt extending from Zhengzhou to Luoyang and a more dispersed peripheral pattern\. At the 5\-km grid scale, heritage\-vitality density and river\-network density showed a positive global spatial association \(bivariate Moran’s I = 0\.2109; permutation p = 0\.001\)\. High vitality–high river\-network configurations occurred in parts of the central and northern plains, high river\-network–low vitality configurations in parts of the eastern and southern plains, and several heritage agglomerations displayed high vitality despite low river\-network density\. Adjusted R 2 increased from 0\.1201 for OLS to 0\.6000 for GWR, showing that geographically varying coefficients captured substantially more variation in heritage vitality\. Coefficients for heritage agglomeration, riverbank\-line richness, and riparian greenness changed sign across the province, while their spatial patterns remained relatively consistent under LCR\-GWR\. Together, the regional configurations and local coefficients show how heritage organization, riverbank form, and riparian ecology differentiate river\-network–vitality relationships across the province, providing a diagnostic basis for differentiated heritage activation and spatial planning\.

## [ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ ГЛОБАЛЬНОГО РИНКУ ВЕНЧУРНОГО КАПІТАЛУ ПІД ВПЛИВОМ ІНВЕСТИЦІЙ У СФЕРУ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ](../publications/a9424efdc46fe3a2fdc0.md)

Оксана Урікова; Володимир Босак; Анна Ляшенко

У статті досліджено трансформацію глобального ринку венчурного капіталу в умовах інтенсивного розвитку та впровадження технологій штучного інтелекту \(ШІ\)\. Проаналізовано структурні зміни інвестиційних потоків із виокремленням пріоритетних напрямів фінансування, зокрема технологій машинного навчання, генеративних моделей та спеціалізованої ІТ\-інфраструктури\. Визначено, що темпи зростання капіталовкладень у сферу ШІ суттєво випереджають загальноринкову динаміку венчурної індустрії, внаслідок чого у 2025 році частка ШІ\-сегмента перевищила половину обсягу світового фінансування\. Охарактеризовано інституційні зрушення на ринку, які проявляються в посиленні ролі великих технологічних корпорацій, спеціалізованих фондів та інституційних інвесторів\. Виявлено тенденцію до концентрації капіталу на пізніх етапах інвестування та стрімкого зростання ринкової оцінки ШІ\-стартапів, що обґрунтовує ризики перегріву ринку за одночасного відкриття нових бізнес\-моделей\. Систематизовано ключові виклики галузі: технологічну невизначеність, регуляторну фрагментацію, дефіцит кваліфікованих кадрів та етичні аспекти комерціалізації інновацій\. Доведено, що ШІ формує нову парадигму інноваційного інвестування в умовах цифровізації глобальної економіки\. References 1\.
