## [Association between preoperative E/e′ and early left ventricular systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting](../publications/a9467aa4be37c8b241cc.md)

Jungsuk Choi; Hee Kyung Kim; Joon Kyu Kang

Background In patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, the degree of systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting \(CABG\) is heterogeneous\. We assessed whether routine preoperative transthoracic echocardiography \(TTE\) indices—particularly E/e′—are associated with early postoperative improvement in left ventricular function\. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing isolated CABG at a single tertiary center \(April 2019 to July 2025\)\. Eligibility required a preoperative left ventricular ejection fraction \(LVEF\) of &lt;50%\. Emergency/salvage operations, 30\-day deaths, and patients without an evaluable early postoperative TTE were excluded\. The primary outcome was an absolute increase in the LVEF of ≥10 percentage points\. Because of the limited number of outcome events, the primary association analysis used a single\-predictor logistic regression model with preoperative E/e′\. Sensitivity analyses excluded patients with preoperative atrial fibrillation \(AF\) and modeled postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome adjusted for baseline LVEF\. Results Of 75 otherwise clinically eligible patients, three lacked an evaluable early postoperative TTE, leaving 72 patients for outcome analysis; 17 \(23\.6%\) achieved an LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points\. A higher preoperative E/e′ was associated with early LVEF improvement \(OR 1\.155 per 1\-unit increase; 95% CI 1\.04–1\.28; p = 0\.005; N = 66; 16 events\)\. The apparent AUC was 0\.700; after 1,000\-resample bootstrap internal validation, the estimated optimism was 0\.004 and the optimism\-corrected AUC was 0\.696 \(95% bootstrap CI 0\.526–0\.885\)\. The association persisted after excluding patients with AF \(OR 1\.14; 95% CI 1\.02–1\.27; p = 0\.025\)\. In a sensitivity analysis using postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome, E/e′ remained associated with postoperative LVEF after adjustment for baseline LVEF \( β = 0\.31 percentage points per 1\-unit increase; 95% CI 0\.01–0\.61; p = 0\.042\)\. Conclusion A higher preoperative E/e′ was associated with early improvement in LV systolic function after CABG among patients with a preoperative LVEF of &lt;50% who survived to undergo early postoperative echocardiographic assessment\. Given the small number of events and the single\-center retrospective design, these findings are hypothesis\-generating and require external validation\.

## [ІСТОРІЯ ФІЗИЧНОЇ КУЛЬТУРИ І СПОРТУ КРІЗЬ ПРИЗМУ ГЛОБАЛІЗАЦІЇ І СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ](../publications/a94fd0f5e1e8fb50e89b.md)

Natalia Volodymyrivna Semal

Актуальність дослідження в тому, що елобальні соціальні трансформації докорінно змінюють традиційне бачення історичної ролі фізичної культури і спорту\. Цифрова цивілізація змінює не лише сучасний спорт, а й способи інтерпретації його історичної еволюції\. Російсько\-українська війна посилює необхідність переосмислення історичної ролі фізичної культури як чинника суспільної консолідації, реабілітації та післявоєнного відновлення держави\. \. Саме тому актуальним науковим і практичним завданням є переосмислення історії фізичної культури і спорту крізь призму глобалізації та сталого розвитку як багатовимірного цивілізаційного феномена, що інтегрує історичний, соціокультурний, аксіологічний, освітній і гуманістичний виміри розвитку суспільства\. Цивілізаційна перспектива засвідчує, що цифровізація стає одним із ключових чинників модернізації сучасної фізичної культури та спорту\. Метою статті є комплексне історико\-філософське дослідження еволюції фізичної культури і спорту крізь призму глобалізації та сталого розвитку, виявлення закономірностей їх історичної трансформації, обґрунтування ролі фізичної культури і спорту як соціокультурного й цивілізаційного феномена\. Результати дослідження\. Проаналізлвано теоретико\-методологічні засади деволюції історії фізичної культури і спорту та досліджено основні етапи історичної еволюції фізичної культури і спорту та закономірності трансформації соціальних, культурних, освітніх і гуманістичних функцій у різні історичні періоди\. Розкрито вплив глобалізаційних процесів на розвиток фізичної культури і спорту та особливості інтернаціоналізації, комерціалізації та інституційної модернізації спортивної діяльності\. Обґрунтовано взаємозв&\#x27;язок фізичної культури і спорту з концепцією сталого розвитку, визначити їхній внесок у досягнення Цілей сталого розвитку\. Сформовано авторське концептуальне бачення історії фізичної культури і спорту як багатовимірного цивілізаційного феномена, що інтегрує історичний, соціокультурний, аксіологічний, людиноцентричний, інституційний і безпековий виміри\. Практичне значення отриманих результатів полягає в можливості використання запропонованої концепції для вдосконалення історико\-спортивних досліджень, формування сучасної державної політики у сфері фізичної культури і спорту, розвитку спортивної освіти, соціальної інклюзії, молодіжної політики та програм відновлення людського потенціалу\.

## [The Lagrangian Structure of Cost\-Penalized Active Feature Acquisition](../publications/a95d31dbf971e54f443e.md)

Joseph Bingham

Active Feature Acquisition \(AFA\) sequentially selects features to maximize predictive accuracy under an acquisition budget\. A natural heuristic greedily maximizes Expected Information Gain minus a cost penalty, EIG\(j\|x\_S\)\-lam\*c\_j \(EIG\-Cost\), but its theoretical guarantees are unclear\. We provide an a\-posteriori certificate decomposing the gap to the optimal hard\-budget policy into a budget\-slack term and a greedy\-suboptimality term Del\_lam\. The certificate is computable when the penalized optimum is tractable; on small heterogeneous\-cost instances, we verify it exactly, finding Del\_lam near zero across 4,000 solved cases\. On the large clinical task, Del\_lam is not computable, so the decomposition is diagnostic rather than a numerical guarantee\. Our analysis identifies EIG\-Cost as one\-step greedy optimization of the Lagrangian relaxation of expected\-cost AFA, with lam as its dual multiplier\. For equal costs, we prove Del\_lam &lt;= exp\(\-gam\*I\(Y;X\_\[d\]\)\), where gam is the submodularity ratio, yielding a structural guarantee in the near\-submodular regime\. Supporting results establish an adaptive chain\-rule identity showing that cumulative stepwise EIG optimizes transcript information, and prove that A \-&gt; I\(Y;X\_A\) need not be submodular, even for jointly Gaussian variables\. This rules out a direct Nemhauser\-Wolsey\-Fisher bound; naive Bayes restores submodularity\. We also bound the randomization gap between hard\-budget and expected\-cost optima, analyze sensitivity to dual\-multiplier error under local smoothness, and derive a conditional CVAE generator\-shift bound given a bound on forward predictive KL\. We treat this KL as a diagnostic quantity, not as a transform of training loss\. Experiments cover synthetic Gaussian settings, AFA benchmarks, and clinical differential diagnosis on MIMIC\-IV\. On MIMIC\-IV, EIG\-Cost achieves macro\-F1 0\.180 \+/\- 0\.012 at a $30 budget, using 6\.6% of full\-panel cost\.

## [Rehabilitation after selective dorsal rhizotomy in cerebral palsy: world experience in literature review](../publications/a9667cc0d464dc0ac068.md)

D\. B\. Kurmanova; Туруспекова Сауле Тлеубергеновна; V\. S\. Lisnic; G\. A\. Mukhambetova; М\.Р\. Рабандияров; Azamat Zhailganov; Г Н Касенова

One of the surgical methods used to correct muscle spasticity in cerebral palsy \(CP\) is selective dorsal rhizotomy \(SDR\)\. The effectiveness of this method depends on the patient’s individual rehabilitation program \(IRP\), as well as on the timeliness, quality, and duration of rehabilitation interventions\. This review presents a historical overview of SDR development, summarizes global experience in post\-SDR rehabilitation for patients with CP, and highlights the key factors influencing its effectiveness\. The success of SDR largely relies on a well\-designed rehabilitation program that includes early initiation of physical therapy, optimal training intensity, and a multidisciplinary approach\. The paper outlines the main stages of SDR evolution, analyzes current rehabilitation strategies, and provides examples of international protocols defining the frequency, duration, and sequence of therapeutic interventions\. Special attention is given to postoperative kinesiotherapy, physiotherapy, neurodevelopmental techniques, and psychological support for families\. The review emphasizes the need for standardization of rehabilitation programs and increased patient adherence to long\-term therapy\. The analysis confirms that combining surgical correction with comprehensive rehabilitation ensures optimal functional outcomes, promotes independence, improves quality of life, and strengthens the evidence base for developing national rehabilitation protocols\.

## [Associations between accumulated weekly external load and technical match actions in elite soccer](../publications/a974a04b5712b198ce8c.md)

Alexandre Oliveira; María Calegari; Lucas Figueiredo; Filipe Clemente; Robert Trybulski; Gustavo De Conti Teixeira Costa; Lorenzo Laporta; Henrique de Oliveira Castro

This study investigated the associations between accumulated weekly external load metrics and match technical performance in elite male players\.19 outfield players from a Brazilian first\-division club \(25\.7 ± 3\.9 years; 80\.4 ± 6\.6 kg; 181\.3 ± 6\.7 cm\) were monitored across 208 sessions \(170 training sessions and 38 official matches\) during a full competitive season\.External load was quantified, capturing total distance \(TD\), PlayerLoad \(PL\), high\-speed running distance \(HSRD\), total accelerations \(ACC\), and repeated high\-intensity efforts \(RHIE\)\.Match technical performance was categorized into defensive and offensive indicators\.Results showed several negative associations between accumulated weekly external load and technical performance indicators\.TD was negatively associated with Clearances \(β = \-0\.310\)and Successful Forward Passes \(β = \-0\.213\),while PL was negatively associated with Clearances \(β = \-0\.315\)and Aerial Duels Won \(β = \-0\.216\)\.Additionally, HSRD and RHIE were negatively associated with Interceptions \(β = \-0\.273;β = \-0\.284\)\.Finally, ACC was negatively associated with Interceptions \(β = \-0\.241\),Offensive Volume \(β = \-0\.220\),and Successful Total Passes \(β = \-0\.207\)\.These results suggest that weeks characterized by higher training volumes and intensities may negatively affect offensive and defensive technical performance in subsequent matches\.Consequently, coaches should consider the adequacy of the weekly load composition, specifically managing neuromuscular stress and exposure to high intensity before matches, to balance offensive readiness with technical precision and defensive efficiency\.An integrated approach combining external load and technical\-tactical monitoring can optimize training prescription and help maintain performance throughout the competitive season\.

## [Sheep pulmonary image recognition \(SPIRO\): An explainable deep learning framework for macroscopic assessment of ovine pulmonary lesions](../publications/a97a43bff1e74b1faced.md)

Muhammad Furqan Arshad; Tesfalem Mehari Berhe; Giovanni Lai; Ludovica Mura; Antonio Varcasia; Maria Luisa Pinna Parpaglia; Elisabetta Antuofermo; Marta Polinas; Marina Antonella Sanna; Maria Giovanna Cancedda; Md Sabbir Ahmed; Delaram Ghadir; Setayesh Ghadir; Stefano Giordano; Ciriaco Ligios; Davide Adami; Giovanni Pietro Burrai

Accurate detection and classification of pulmonary diseases in sheep are critical for ensuring animal welfare, food safety, and effective disease surveillance in abattoir settings\. In this study, we propose a two\-stage, explainable, histopathology\-informed deep learning framework for the automated classification of ovine lung lesions\. The dataset comprises 1052 sheep lung images, annotated through a dual\-level diagnostic process involving macroscopic inspection and histopathological confirmation, and classified as healthy, inflammatory, or neoplastic\. Four convolutional neural network architectures\-VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0\-were benchmarked under identical conditions\. EfficientNetB0 achieved the highest observed standalone performance and was integrated into a two\-stage pipeline, in which YOLOv11 first localized lung regions and EfficientNetB0 subsequently classified the cropped images\. Model interpretability was evaluated using Gradient\-weighted Class Activation Mapping \(Grad\-CAM\)\. The YOLOv11\-EfficientNetB0 pipeline achieved an overall test accuracy of 90% and a weighted F1\-score of 0\.88\. Neoplastic lesions were classified with the highest performance, reaching precision, recall, and F1\-score values of 0\.98, 0\.99, and 0\.99, respectively, while healthy and inflammatory lungs achieved F1\-scores of 0\.83 and 0\.82, respectively\. Grad\-CAM visualizations indicated that predictions were mainly driven by diagnostically relevant pulmonary regions\. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of explainable artificial intelligence for objective, scalable, and biologically grounded post\-mortem assessment of sheep lungs, with potential applications in abattoir surveillance, veterinary pathology, and flock health monitoring\.

## [Frequency of incidentally detected pulmonary nodules and their association with smoking history among adult liver transplant candidates](../publications/a97bd5e88825ba62bd64.md)

Sarah Jawed; Mushtaq Haroon; Maaz Suhail Rana

Background and Objectives: Lung cancer carries a huge burden of global deaths\. Routine imaging done frequently for other reasons detects pulmonary nodules which when carefully evaluated, may support in early recognition and management of early malignancies\. This study aims to determine the frequency of incidental pulmonary nodules detected in pre\-transplant patients and to evaluate the association between the presence of nodules and smoking history\. Methodology: This study was conducted at Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute and Research Center, including 139 pre\-transplant patients evaluated over a period of six months\. Pre\-transplant CT scans and clinical data were reviewed\. Pulmonary nodules were identified and statistical analysis, including Fisher exact test, was applied to determine the association between smoking history and nodule presence\. Results: A total of 139 pre transplant patients were included in the study, with a mean age of 50\.9\+/\-10\.4 years\. Mainstream of the patients were male \(74\.0%\) and lung nodules were detected in 9 patients \(6\.4%\)\. 16 patients had a history of smoking \(11\.5%\)\. It was found from the study that smokers had a significantly higher prevalence of lung nodules than non\-smokers \(31\.3% vs\. 3\.3%, Fisher exact test, p=0\.001\)\. Conclusion: A significant trend towards higher prevalence of pulmonary nodules was observed among smokers\.

## [Demokratik Meşruiyet Krizi: Görünürlükten Açıklanabilirliğe Kamusal Alanın Dönüşümü](../publications/a986688e63204433e1b4.md)

Ayse Okumus; Fatih DEĞİRMENCİ; Emre OKUMUŞ

Bu çalışma, çağdaş demokrasilerde giderek derinleşen meşruiyet krizini, kamusal alanın dönüşümü ve dijitalleşme bağlamında incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır\. Araştırmanın kapsamı; demokratik meşruiyet, görünürlük odaklı yeni medya pratikleri ve platform kapitalizminin algoritmik yönlendirmeleri arasındaki ilişki ile sınırlandırılmıştır\. Çalışmada nitel ve kuramsal\-yorumlayıcı bir araştırma tasarımı benimsenmiş; siyasal meşruiyet, kamusal alan kuramı ve dijital iktidar literatürü sistematik olarak taranarak kavramsal ve eleştirel bir metin analizi yürütülmüştür\. Yürütülen analiz sonucunda üç temel bulguya ulaşılmıştır: İlk olarak, demokratik kurumlarda siyasal karar alma süreçlerindeki şeffaflık ve söylemsel gerekçelendirme eksikliği meşruiyet algısını yapısal olarak zedelemektedir\. İkincisi, kamusal alan rasyonel müzakere zemininden uzaklaşarak, medyatik görünürlüğün ve duygusal tepkilerin egemen olduğu seyirlik bir yapıya dönüşmüştür\. Üçüncüsü, dijital platformlar etkileşimi niceliksel olarak artırsa da &quot;algoritmik opaklık&quot; ve kâr odaklı doğaları gereği demokratik denetimi güçleştirmekte, meşruiyet açığını derinleştirmektedir\. Araştırmanın sonucunda; çağdaş demokrasilerde meşruiyetin yeniden inşası için salt seçim ve katılıma dayalı kurumsal modellerin yetersiz olduğu görülmüştür\. Krizin aşılabilmesi için kamusal alanın hukuki olarak desteklendiği, dijital iletişimin insan hakları temelinde güvence altına alındığı ve özellikle algoritmik karar mekanizmalarının topluma karşı hesap verebilir ve &quot;açıklanabilir&quot; kılındığı yeni bir demokratik yaklaşıma geçiş yapılması gerektiği sonucuna varılmıştır\.

## [Biodiversity, trophic position, and nutritional ecology of euphausiid species in the Benguela upwelling system](../publications/a99624cba7fd1fe2fe9c.md)

Tine Jordan; Anna Schukat; Tim Dudeck; Sabrina Dorschner; Holger Auel

Lantern shrimp \(krill, Euphausiacea\) play a key ecological role in the Benguela Current coastal upwelling system \(BUS\) off Namibia and South Africa due to their high biomass, their physiological plasticity, and their position as a link between primary production and higher trophic levels\. In total, 15 krill species were identified\. Euphausiid species composition was variable at spatial scales between nearshore and offshore areas and between the northern and southern Benguela upwelling subsystems \(nBUS and sBUS\)\. Euphausia lucens was the most dominant species in both subsystems in terms of biomass and distribution range\. In the nBUS, Hansarsia megalops and Euphausia hanseni were predominantly found\. Euphausia similis occurred in the sBUS\. Offshore stations were dominated in both subsystems by Euphausia recurva \. Biodiversity increased from coastal to oceanic waters\. Krill species in the BUS occupy multiple trophic levels because of species\-specific feeding behaviors that range from herbivory via omnivory to exclusive carnivory\. Stable isotope and fatty acid biomarker analysis revealed trophic positions \(TP\) between 2 and 3\.7 and carnivory indices \(CI\) between 1\.7 and 19\.5 for krill species in the BUS\. Furcilia larvae and small juveniles \(&lt;10 mm\) were predominantly herbivorous, specified by low TPs of 1\.9\-2\.2 and low mean CI of 2\.3\. E\. recurva and E\. lucens were predominantly herbivorous to partially omnivorous indicated by elevated proportions of the diatom marker fatty acid 18:1\(n\-7\) \(2\.7–4% of total fatty acids \(TFA\)\)\. A high proportion of the carnivory marker fatty acid 18:1\(n\-9\) supported an omnivorous feeding behavior with a tendency toward carnivory for E\. hanseni \(10\.4–12\.5% TFA\)\. CI and TP of H\. megalops and E\. similis suggested trophic plasticity and a tendency to a carnivorous life style \(mean CI of 3\.5/3\.2 and TP of 2\.1\-3\.4\)\. Species of the genus Stylocheiron were exclusively carnivorous \(TP of 2\.7\-3\.8 and mean CI of 15\.6\)\. Only H\. megalops had fatty alcohols indicating the production of wax esters as storage lipids\. This study shows that the ecological role of krill is more complex than just linking primary production to higher trophic levels\. For realistic food\-web models, the different functional groups within the krill taxon should be considered\.

## [Data sharing Ba: A unified digital framework for tacit knowledge management in SMEs](../publications/a99dc2936d3a8dba4733.md)

Sajjad Vojdanian; S\.S\. Barnes

This study addresses knowledge management \(KM\) gaps in small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\), specifically the lack of systematic approaches to managing tacit knowledge and preventing knowledge loss when employees depart\. While SMEs typically operate with informal, human\-centric KM practices due to their flat structures and close social ties, these approaches limit their ability to utilize knowledge for innovation\. Building upon Nonaka&\#x27;s Socialization, Externalization, Combination, and Internalization \(SECI\) model, this research proposes a reconceptualization through a novel &quot;Data Sharing Ba&quot; framework that integrates digital capabilities with organizational culture\. Unlike conventional implementations that maintain separate spaces \(Ba\) for each knowledge conversion mode, this unified model creates a centralized digital ecosystem where tacit and explicit knowledge continuously interact\. The framework prioritizes tacit knowledge as the primary driver of value creation while incorporating anonymization mechanisms to foster trust and encourage sharing\. By transforming how SMEs capture, store, and convert knowledge artifacts, the model bridges theoretical and practical gaps in KM implementation\. The research contributes theoretically by expanding the SECI model to accommodate contemporary digital contexts while preserving the contextual integrity of knowledge exchanges\. Practically, it offers SMEs an adaptable solution that aligns with their flexible structures yet provides systematic knowledge retention\. Though empirical validation remains necessary, this framework represents a step toward enabling SMEs to harness their collective intelligence for sustained innovation and competitive advantage in increasingly digital business environments\.

## [Attending to control? International parliamentary institutions and parliamentary oversight of foreign affairs](../publications/a99ffc655f7bb1d32246.md)

Philipp Bien

Abstract Traditionally dominated by the executives, parliaments increasingly push for a more active role in multilateral affairs through International Parliamentary Institutions \(IPIs\)\. Conceptual research has argued that IPIs improve the democratic legitimacy of IOs by strengthening the accountability of IOs, as they allow parliamentary oversight over executives\. Empirically, it remains unclear if IPIs are accomplishing this task\. This paper provides further evidence in this regard\. I theoretically derive the hypothesis that IPIs help legislators to hold the executives from their own country to account within the context of an IO\. This happens by way of improved access to otherwise scarce information\. I test this hypothesis on a novel dataset including three IOs \(NATO, OSCE, Council of Europe\) and their respective IPIs\. For the German case, I show that legislators who are part of an IPI delegation ask more questions to the foreign ministries, but that this effect is likely driven by self\-selection\. Further exploratory qualitative interview evidence suggest that legislators do not attend IPIs to improve their parliamentary oversight capacity, but rather to engage in informal diplomacy\. My findings add further nuance to our understanding of IPIs as source of information for MPs active in foreign affairs and their role in extending multilateral diplomacy\.

## [Integridad Académica y Toma de Decisiones en la Educación Superior en Línea: Una Revisión Narrativa y un Marco Multinivel en la Era de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa](../publications/a9a0ce783dcf229b253b.md)

Adriana María Cadena León; Alexander Javier Montes Miranda

La expansión de la evaluación en línea en la educación superior ha intensificado las preocupaciones sobre la integridad académica, particularmente a medida que la inteligencia artificial generativa \(IAG\), la supervisión remota de exámenes y la analítica del comportamiento transforman tanto las oportunidades de incurrir en conductas indebidas como las respuestas institucionales\. Esta revisión narrativa sintetiza críticamente 29 estudios y revisiones publicados predominantemente entre 2024 y 2026, junto con fuentes metodológicas e institucionales seleccionadas\. La evidencia se organizó en cinco ámbitos: diseño de evaluaciones y psicometría; detección estadística de la colusión y de patrones de respuesta anómalos; analítica del comportamiento, aprendizaje automático y supervisión remota de exámenes; desafíos relacionados con la IAG; y gobernanza institucional y toma de decisiones humanas\. En la literatura revisada, las conductas indebidas autoinformadas, los comportamientos digitales sospechosos, las anomalías estadísticas y las alertas automatizadas representan constructos diferentes y no deben considerarse indicadores intercambiables de fraude académico\. El rediseño de las evaluaciones, las versiones múltiples de los exámenes, el análisis de los tiempos de respuesta, los algoritmos de detección de colusión, la supervisión remota y la monitorización basada en inteligencia artificial abordan vulnerabilidades específicas, pero presentan limitaciones en cuanto a precisión, generalización, privacidad y alcance\. La síntesis sugiere que los indicadores automatizados son más defendibles cuando se utilizan como señales de apoyo a la toma de decisiones que requieren interpretación humana contextualizada, en lugar de considerarse pruebas independientes para imponer sanciones disciplinarias\. A partir de la evidencia revisada, el artículo propone un marco de decisión de cinco capas que integra la gobernanza institucional, el diseño de las evaluaciones, la supervisión proporcional, la analítica multimodal y la revisión humana con garantías procedimentales\. Este marco replantea la integridad académica como un problema de toma de decisiones sociotécnicas y prioriza la prevención, la proporcionalidad, la transparencia y la disponibilidad de evidencias creíbles del aprendizaje individual en la era de la IAG\.

## [Freeze\-thaw model for compressive strength of flowable solidified soil based on machine learning](../publications/a9a1225ed765117f5c37.md)

Baolin Wang; Jinggan Shao; Yunjun Huang; Cong Li; Tingting Han; Bingsen Fan

Freeze\-thaw cycling is a critical factor triggering durability degradation of flowable solidified soil in cold\-region engineering, and its damage evolution process is affected by multi\-factor coupling with obvious nonlinear characteristics\. Based on experimental compressive strength data of flowable solidified soil under freeze\-thaw cycles, four influencing factors, namely solidifier dosage \(SD\), admixture dosage \(AD\), water\-solid ratio \(WS\) and freeze\-thaw cycle number \(F\-T\), are selected as input variables\. Four machine learning algorithms including Decision Tree \(DT\), BP Neural Network \(BP\), Support Vector Regression \(SVR\) and XGBoost are adopted to establish freeze\-thaw damage prediction models for the compressive strength of flowable solidified soil\. The SHAP interpretable framework is further employed for feature sensitivity analysis to quantify the contribution and nonlinear effect of each input factor on prediction results\. The results reveal that the DT model suffers severe overfitting with drastic error fluctuations on the test set; BP and SVR achieve a high test‑set R 2 yet show noticeable prediction deviations; the ensemble tree model XGBoost presents well‑balanced fitting capacity and satisfactory overall prediction stability with low error dispersion\. SHAP analysis indicates the feature importance ranking: F\-T &gt; SD &gt; AD &gt; WS\. Freeze\-thaw cycle number \(F\-T\) acts as the dominant control factor, and high/low values of each factor impose distinct positive and negative effects on model outputs\. The proposed modeling and interpretive analysis method can provide technical references for rapid prediction of mechanical indices of similar flowable solidified soil specimens and identification of primary influencing factors\.

## [FuzzInsight: Navigating the Efficiency\-Effectiveness Trade\-off in Coverage\-Guided DNN Fuzzing](../publications/a9a21cf9e1b2ab33650e.md)

Vivek Vekariya; Fathiyeh Faghih; Alexander Pretschner

Collecting and labeling diverse test datasets for evaluating Deep Neural Networks \(DNNs\) is costly and time\-consuming\. This has motivated coverage\-guided fuzzing techniques that generate defect\-revealing corner cases from limited test data\. However, their effectiveness depends heavily on configuration choices, particularly coverage criteria and seed\-selection strategies\. We present a configuration\-oriented analysis and decision guidelines for scalable DNN fuzzing targeting two bottlenecks: inefficient seed utilization and the cost of coverage guidance\. Our analysis shows that existing seed\-selection strategies repeatedly prioritize a small subset of inputs, leaving many collected seeds unexplored\. To address this issue, we propose Equalized Sampling, a constraint\-based strategy that increases mean seed queue utilization to 77%, improving on prior approaches by 13 percentage points\. We further evaluate 84 fuzzing configurations on four benchmark datasets: MNIST, SVHN, GTSRB, and CIFAR\-100\. Results show that the non\-structural criteria LSCD, LSC, and MDSC achieve coverage outcomes comparable to structural and alternative non\-structural criteria while requiring substantially less computation\. These criteria also promote broad behavioral exploration of the DNN under test, reducing the need to monitor multiple coverage metrics\. Among them, LSCD provides a modest but consistent runtime advantage\. Finally, we show that retraining with generated corner cases improves generalization robustness by up to 77 percentage points on average without degrading performance on the original test distribution\. Together, these findings provide a practical blueprint for selecting fuzzing configurations that balance efficiency, behavioral exploration, and model hardening\.

## [Servicios E\-Learning en la satisfacción de los usuarios](../publications/a9a3630853f5f2a39e54.md)

Jhanina Inés Chávez Quevedo; Manuel Eduardo Vilca Tantapoma

El E\-Learning se ha convertido en una herramienta fundamental para el desarrollo profesional y la continuidad educativa, especialmente tras la pandemia por COVID\-19\. El objetivo de esta revisión sistemática fue analizar los factores asociados a la satisfacción de los usuarios en plataformas virtuales\. Se realizó una búsqueda en Scopus, Redalyc, Dialnet y SciELO, siguiendo la metodología PRISMA y considerando publicaciones de los últimos cinco años\. Se identificaron 243 estudios, de los cuales 50 cumplieron los criterios de inclusión\. Los resultados evidencian que la satisfacción del usuario depende principalmente de la infraestructura tecnológica, calidad de la información, capacitación docente, planificación académica y la interacción en el entorno virtual\. Asimismo, la retroalimentación oportuna y la usabilidad de las plataformas influyen positivamente en la experiencia formativa\. La conclusión de la investigación es que la integración adecuada de factores tecnológicos, pedagógicos y humanos es esencial para garantizar una experiencia de E\-Learning de calidad\.

## [Chemical ecology in conservation biological control: status and emerging challenges](../publications/a9a5d7a35db508815183.md)

Stefano Colazza

Over the past decade, chemical ecology has become increasingly integrated into the development of biological control programs, particularly Conservation Biological Control \(CBC\)\. Conservation Biological Control exploits a set of habitat manipulation practices to maintain and enhance the reproduction, survival, and efficacy of arthropod natural enemies that prey upon or parasitize insect pests\. Specifically, chemical cues that convey information between living organisms, named semiochemicals, can enhance the management of herbivore populations by mediating interactions among plants, herbivores, predators, parasitoids, and their surrounding habitats\. Nevertheless, translating mechanistic knowledge of chemically mediated interactions into reliable control of pest insect populations remains a major challenge\. A central constraint is the persistent gap between results obtained under simplified laboratory conditions and outcomes observed in dynamic agroecosystems, where background odors, meteorological conditions, crop phenology, and multispecies interactions can modify semiochemical production and transmission, receiver responses, and ultimately, biological control agent efficacy\. Additional priorities include moving from the study of individual compounds to ecologically realistic blends of bioactive volatiles; identifying non\-target and food\-web effects; integrating semiochemical\-based interventions with habitat management and selective crop\-protection practices; and developing standardized field metrics that connect natural enemy recruitment with predation, parasitism, herbivore population control, and reduction in crop damage\. Progress will therefore require multiscale experimentation, closer integration of analytical chemistry with behavioral and field ecology that balance efficacy, ecological safety, and operational feasibility\. From this perspective, CBC involves more than enhancing the abundance or activity of arthropod natural enemies: it requires the deliberate management of information flow across multitrophic levels to establish a more predictive and mechanistically grounded framework for biological herbivore population control\. Here, are reviewed the principal issues that chemical ecology should address to advance CBC, focusing on how semiochemical production, transmission, and perception vary across plant genotypes, herbivore communities, natural\-enemy guilds, microbiomes, agricultural practices, and landscape contexts\.

## [Effect of frequency\-dependent dielectric properties features on the accuracy of cancerous liver tissue identification](../publications/a9c33ced8c638134d3ab.md)

Xiao Wang; Guofang Xu; Chunyou Ye; Yinhao Ren; Xuefei Yu; Jijun Han

Differences in the dielectric properties of normal and cancer tissues provide invaluable information for distinguishing them\. The open\-ended coaxial probe technique is a recognized method for measuring the dielectric properties of normal and cancerous tissues\. Machine learning is widely used to classify these tissues on the basis of their dielectric properties\. However, the current classification technique is error‑prone, as selecting an insufficient number of features may result in diminished accuracy, whereas selecting an excessive number can lead to overfitting in classification models\. This study systematically investigated the impact of noise and individual variability, with particular emphasis on how the number of frequency points, which represents the features, influences the accuracy of cancer identification\. The K\-nearest neighbor \(KNN\) algorithm was used to analyze the dielectric properties, and the model was generalized to phantoms\. Results demonstrate that as the number of frequency points increases, accuracy stabilizes and improves\. However, accuracy gradually plateaued and slightly decreased with excessive frequency points, suggesting potential overfitting\. A comprehensive analysis recommends using 20 frequency points for accurate tissue identification\. When generalized to phantom dielectric properties data, the model misclassified only one phantom\. The dielectric properties offer valuable insights into medical diagnostics\. The KNN was effective in distinguishing between normal and cancer tissues\. This study also provides practical recommendations for cost\-effective dielectric properties analysis\.

## [Relationship of Work Environment on Novice Nurses’ Turnover Intentions](../publications/a9c45111f55a2eb887dc.md)

Jubee Joseph; Bala Seetharaman

Objectives A supportive and well\-organised work environment is crucial for reducing nurse turnover, particularly among novice nurses in India\. Challenges such as heavy workloads, lack of recognition, inadequate support systems, and poor work–life balance contribute to job dissatisfaction and drive many nurses to seek opportunities abroad\. This study examined whether the work environment influences turnover intentions among novice nurses\. Material and Methods The study used a descriptive correlational design\. Purposive sampling was used to find new nurses with ≤1 year of work experience\. 51 qualified nurses who provided complete responses were used in the analysis\. A baseline proforma was used to begin data collection, and then the Practice Work Environment Scale and the Nurse Turnover Intention Scale were given out\. Results Although it was not statistically significant, a negative correlation between practice work environment and nurse turnover intention was found \(r = –0\.201, p = 0\.157\), suggesting that better practice environments were linked to somewhat lower turnover intentions\. According to regression analysis, there was a slight decrease in turnover intention for every unit rise in practice environment score; the effect size was tiny\. Conclusion The negative correlation observed clearly advocates the influence of the work environment on nurse retention, though the relationship was weak\. The findings from the turnover scale emphasise that workload, salary dissatisfaction, and external opportunities are the decisive factors that lead to nurses’ intention to leave\. While factors like resource allocation, staffing inadequacy, and interprofessional collaboration remain important, targeted strategies addressing staffing, fair compensation, and career development are essential to strengthen workforce stability\.

## [Effect of Gnrh Administration at Artificial Insemination and on Day 6 Post Insemination on Pregnancy Outcomes in Holstein Friesian Cows](../publications/a9d0b08a76bf874f24b7.md)

Muhammad Waqas; Huzaila Mudassar; Huzaima Qaiser; Rana Muhammad Haroon; Haseeb Ullah Saad; Baqir Hussain Shah\.; Dr Abdul Salam

This study aimed to compare the effects of GnRH treated at artificial insemination \(AI\), at day 6 post\-AI and at both times on pregnancy success in Holstein Friesian cows\. The experiment was carried out at Aslam and Sons Dairy Farm at Dijkot, Faisalabad, Pakistan from February to June 2026\. Eighty second parity cows were randomly divided into 4 groups \(20 cows per group\)\. G1 were the controls, G2 were treated with GnRH at AI, and G3 and G4 were treated with GnRH at AI and at 6 days post\-AI\. Each administration consisted of 5 mL of Conceptal intramuscularly, equivalent to 20 µg of buserelin\. Artificial insemination was performed approximately 12 hours after the onset of natural estrus\. Pregnancy diagnosis was performed using ultrasonography on days 28 and 45 post\-AI to evaluate pregnancy establishment and maintenance\. Overall, 45/80 cows \(56\.25%\) were pregnant on day 28\. Pregnancy rates were 45%, 60%, 55%, and 65% in G1, G2, G3, and G4, respectively; differences among groups were not statistically significant \(χ² = 1\.778, p = 0\.620\)\. Of the 45 initially pregnant cows, nine \(20%\) experienced subsequent pregnancy loss by day 45\. Pregnancy loss was 33\.33% in G1, 25\.00% in G2, 18\.18% in G3, and 7\.69% in G4, with no significant difference among groups \(p = 0\.481\)\. Maintained pregnancy rates per inseminated cow were 30%, 45%, 45%, and 60%, respectively \(χ² = 3\.636, p = 0\.304\)\. In conclusion, combined GnRH administration at AI and on day 6 post\-AI produced the most favourable numerical outcomes for pregnancy establishment and maintenance\. However, these differences were not statistically significant, warranting further investigation in larger studies\.

## [Transcriptome of atopic dermatitis patients as a biomarker for response to dupilumab](../publications/a9d48522118171c2f226.md)

Martina Krušič

Atopijski dermatitis \(AD\) je najpogostejša kronična vnetna kožna bolezen heterogene narave, kar se odraža tudi pri razlikah v odzivu na zdravljenje\. Kljub vedno večjemu naboru bioloških zdravil se določen delež bolnikov na zdravljenje odziva nezadostno\. Posledično se je povečala težnja po identifikaciji bioloških označevalcev, ki bi omogočili napoved odziva na zdravljenje in s tem personaliziran pristop k zdravljenju\. V okviru našega dela smo si prizadevali identificirati nabor morebitnih bioloških označevalcev, s katerimi bi lahko napovedali odziv bolnikov z zmerno do hudo obliko AD na zdravljenje z dupilumabom\. Uporabili smo inovativen tristopenjski pristop, s katerim smo iz podatkov najprej izločili gene, ki se spremenijo zaradi samega zdravljenja, nato še gene, povezane z vnetjem – tako nam je ostal nabor genov, ki potencialno napovedujejo odziv na zdravljenje\. Omenjen pristop združuje analizo diferencialno izraženih genov, analizo genske ontologije, analizo omrežij soizražanja genov in ciljno genomsko profiliranje\. Identificirali smo osem kandidatnih genov \(RPL18A, RPS28, FAU, MASTL, AURKA, TAF2, BUB1B in RNF135\) in genomskih različic v omenjenih genih, ki so povezani z odzivom na zdravljenje z dupilumabom pri slovenskih bolnikih z zmerno do hudo obliko AD\. S tem smo naredili korak k personaliziranemu pristopu k zdravljenju, vendar so za uporabo označevalcev v klinični praksi potrebne nadaljnje raziskave za potrditev naših ugotovitev\.

## [Evaluation of the safe operating space during low flow for water allocation and climate change scenarios in the Danube](../publications/a9d91b02b11ff499fe41.md)

Martin Glas; T\. Graf; F\. Monji; Mario Klösch; Max Preiml; Andrei Toma; Albert Scrieciu; J\. ter Maat; Helmut M\. Habersack

A basin\-to\-local evaluation framework, quantifying safe operating space \(SOS\) for low\-flow water allocation and climate change along the Danube, is presented, linking basin hydrology to local operations for navigation, ecology, run\-of\-river hydropower, drinking water, and nuclear power plant cooling\. The water allocation model \(RIBASIM\), forced by the hydrological model \(wflow\_sbm\), embeds explicit demands on the mainstem under ‘what\-if’ scenarios, while the numerical model \(RSim\-3D\) simulates corresponding water levels at an Upper Danube case study\. SOS was determined with sector\-specific indicators and thresholds, such as the number of days per year with interruptions or disconnections\. The results show competing demands and upstream\-downstream effects, even for local abstractions\. Navigation interruptions increase \(on top of morphodynamic challenges\), and side channel connectivity decreases under ‘what\-if’ scenarios\. A reconnection measure improves, whereas bed degradation reduces side channel connectivity, worsening SOS\. Hydropower production declines, with seasonal shifts mitigating winter deficits\. Nuclear power plant cooling was sensitive to low flow, extending under a more extreme climate scenario, while SOS for drinking water was not exceeded at the investigated cities\. Across sectors, the interaction of water allocation and sediment management with fairway depths, lateral connectivity, sediment continuity, hydropower production and cooling\-water reliability under changing climate and demand needs to be discussed\.

## [A cross\-temporal individual\-level framework for identifying, associating, and counting multiple mounting events for dairy cow in estrus monitoring](../publications/a9db10f55130c40d29ca.md)

Seri Azi; Haowen Pan; Xiangfeng Kong; Yuhan Wu; Chunhui Geng; Zhiwen Song; Huaibo Song; Zuojing Zhang

In vision\-based estrus monitoring, mounting behavior serves as a key indicator\. However, reliance on a single mounting event may cause false positives because non\-estrous cows may also exhibit mounting behavior\. To address this issue, a cross\-temporal individual\-level framework was proposed to identify, associate, and count multiple mounting events of the same cow over time\. The framework combines an improved You Only Look Once Version 11\-nano \(YOLO11n\) model with an improved baseline variant of the HiT lightweight hierarchical vision transformer tracking model \(HiT\-Base\)\. The artificial intelligence contribution comprises improved detection and tracking\. For detection, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss was integrated with Complete Intersection over Union loss to improve small\-target detection, and a lightweight Golden Cudgel Block \(GCBlock\) was designed to enhance feature representation under complex farm conditions\. For tracking, a plug\-and\-play detail\-enhanced convolution \(DEConv\) module was designed to strengthen boundary and fine\-grained features, improving target discrimination and tracking stability\. The engineering application contribution lies in reducing reliance on isolated observations and providing more reliable behavioral evidence through cross\-temporal association and counting of multiple mounting events\. Experimental results showed that the proposed detection model achieved 96\.42% average precision and 94\.74% balanced F\-measure \(F1\-score\) for cow in estrus, with an inference speed of 265\.96 frames per second\. The proposed tracking model achieved an area under the curve of 70\.76%, a normalized precision of 88\.73%, and an average overlap of 70\.74%\. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for real\-time estrus monitoring and its potential for precision dairy farming\.

## [Appraising Artificial Intelligence Studies in Dental and Maxillofacial Imaging: A Task\-Routed Framework for Reporting Completeness and Risk of Bias](../publications/a9e2db24a783d7a77ca5.md)

Volodymyr Kachmar; Roksolana Mikhlin; Tamara Danko; Alina Shmal

Artificial intelligence studies in dental and maxillofacial imaging use different designs and endpoints, but reviews often apply a single adapted appraisal instrument across them\.Recent updates to reporting guidelines and risk\-of\-bias tools have clarified their respective scopes\.This narrative methodological review proposes an appraisal framework in which the review question, study design, and each eligible evaluation determine the instrument used\.Diagnostic accuracy estimates are assessed using appropriate criteria, with comparative accuracy evaluations assessed separately according to relevant methodological guidance\.Diagnostic or prognostic multivariable models are evaluated for risk of bias and methodological quality, with model development quality and evaluation risk of bias reported separately\.Structural segmentation, localization, registration, and image\-enhancement evaluations receive a declared descriptive appraisal where the framework provides no established task\-specific risk\-of\-bias route\.Reporting completeness is assessed separately using the relevant reporting guidelines\.Hybrid reports may contribute to more than one route, with evaluations and estimates linked to the underlying study and dataset\.Results are presented by route, with explicit denominators, rather than combined into a single quality score\.The proposed extraction items address annotation provenance, patient\-level separation between data partitions, within\-patient clustering, dataset reuse, clinical exclusions, and modality\-specific acquisition characteristics\.The review also identifies limitations concerning general\-purpose multimodal models and certainty\-of\-evidence assessment\.The framework offers practical guidance and a proposed minimum reporting set for authors, reviewers, and editors\.Its routing reliability has not been evaluated; therefore, the framework is intended to improve transparency and comparability and requires empirical testing\.

## [A Study on The Influence of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) Literacy on Career Readiness Among Young Adults in Chennai](../publications/a9e627d81f9a1d3d86b2.md)

Akila S Jagadeshwaran S

The study “A Study on the Influence of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) Literacy on Career Readiness Among Young Adults in Chennai” aims to establish a connection between the level of awareness about AI and career readiness\. The influence of artificial intelligence is increasing in all fields of activity, especially in the educational and professional spheres\. Therefore, understanding the characteristics of this technology is becoming a vital skill for achieving employability in the future\. The study uses a descriptive research design, with a primary data collection method\. The data was gathered by distributing questionnaires among one hundred respondents who were selected using a convenience sampling technique\. The data analysis involved the percentage analysis of the results, the weighted average of the responses, multiple linear regression, and Pearson’s correlation\. The analysis focused on investigating the level of AI literacy, the factors that contribute to it, and the relationship between AI literacy and career readiness\. The results of the study showed that the mean score for AI literacy is 3\.61, while that of career readiness is 3\.33\. According to multiple regression analysis, such variables as peer, social, and professional interaction, and personal curiosity and self\-learning were statistically significant predictors of AI literacy, with a score of approximately 66%\. The results also showed that AI literacy and career readiness were positively correlated \(r = 0\.819, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The study established the significance of improving the level of knowledge and skills about artificial intelligence among young adults, which will increase their chances of being employed\. This information can be useful for academic organizations and young people who intend to gain knowledge about AI to enhance their employability\.

## [Individual perching, a potential reproductive strategy of Melipona stingless bee males](../publications/a9e8a1039d58217dd625.md)

José Javier G\. Quezada‐Euán; Roger O\. Guerrero\-Herrera; Rosendo Arturo de J\. Aragón\-Pech; Luis Ancona\-Lizarraga; Fernando A\. Fleites‐Ayil; Humberto Moo‐Valle

There is a wide gap in the knowledge of the reproductive behaviour of males of the Meliponini or stingless bees, the richest group of species within the corbiculate bees\. To date two general reproductive strategies have been reported in the males of stingless bees, both involving the formation of large congregations of individuals\. Here, we describe a newly observed potential reproductive behaviour of stingless bee males, that contrast with the large clustering reported in all species studied so far: individual perching\. Across ten months we documented the frequency of Melipona beecheii males perching nearby colonies\. We performed bioassays to verify sexual activity and the capacity of perching males for detecting and mating with gynes\. We also assessed body size differences, comparing perching males and males produced in colonies\. Males perching were present across the study\. In controlled bioassays, they detected gynes and attempted mounting, which has not been observed at congregations\. These evidences indicate that this behaviour is not occasional and may represent a mating strategy\. Noteworthy, the thorax width of perching males was not different to colony males, suggesting that unlike other bees, this behavior may not be driven by body size differences\. We discuss possible explanations and implications of this newly reported behaviour\.

## [The role of dynamic data in credit risk assessment and early detection of corporate insolvency: a study of selected cases](../publications/aa0ced20256a50982f10.md)

Primož Potočnik

V magistrskem delu obravnavamo problematiko bonitetnega ocenjevanja podjetij z vidika vključevanja dinamičnih podatkov\. Tradicionalni pristopi, ki temeljijo predvsem na statičnih podatkih oziroma računovodskih izkazih, pogosto ne omogočajo pravočasnega zaznavanja finančnih težav podjetij, saj odražajo preteklo stanje in so lahko podvrženi prilagoditvam\. ## [Putting AI to the test: Evidence from a large\-scale RCT in rural China](../publications/aa11427d602f25d8dfa5.md)

Yue Ma; Tianli Feng; Robert W\. Fairlie; Chengfang Liu; Prashant Kumar Loyalka; Scott Rozelle; Xinwu Zhang

The emergence of artificial intelligence \(AI\) has heightened interest in personalizing computer assisted learning \(CAL\) programs to tailor their instruction to individual students\. Despite the proliferation of AI\-driven CAL programs, evidence for their effectiveness remains limited\. We present findings from a field experiment in rural China examining whether an AI\-driven personalized CAL program improves student achievement\. We randomly assign 8647 students from 315 primary school classes to one of three treatment arms: \(i\) AI\-CAL, \(ii\) non\-personalized CAL \(active control\), and \(iii\) non\-CAL educational activities \(pure control\)\. Results indicate that AI\-CAL does not significantly improve achievement, with estimates precise enough to rule out non\-trivial positive effects\. This finding holds across the difficulty of assessment items and across the baseline achievement of students\. If anything, AI\-CAL might be less effective than non\-personalized CAL for students in the middle tercile of baseline achievement\. These findings call for caution when scaling AI\-driven educational technologies\.

## [Kent ve Çevre Bilimlerinde Yeni Yaklaşımlar](../publications/aa14ec156e13aa4fea74.md)



Kentler; iklim değişikliğinin, kaynak baskısının, göç hareketlerinin, toplumsal eşitsizliklerin ve hızlı teknolojik dönüşümün en görünür hâle geldiği mekânlardır\. Bu karmaşık tabloyu tek bir disiplinin araçlarıyla açıklamak giderek güçleşmekte; kent ve çevre bilimleri, mekânı, toplumu, teknolojiyi, siyaseti ve doğal sistemleri birlikte düşünmeyi gerektirmektedir\. Elinizdeki kitap, bu ihtiyaçtan hareketle hazırlanmış dört bölümden oluşmaktadır\. Kitap, Abidin Kemeç&\#x27;in &quot;Dijital Çağın Sürdürülebilir Kent Modelleri: Döngüsel Kent, Akıllı Eko Kent ve Veri Odaklı Kent&quot; başlıklı bölümüyle kavramsal bir çerçeve sunarak açılmaktadır\. Hasan Ege Söğüt&\#x27;ün &quot;Digital Infrastructure Ecosystems in Smart City Strategies: A Comparative Analysis of Konya Metropolitan Municipality and Bucharest Sector 5&quot; başlıklı bölümü, dijital altyapı yatırımlarının kurumsal öğrenme kapasitesi ve çok aktörlü yönetişimle desteklenmedikçe dönüştürücü olmadığını göstermektedir\. Özgür Bayraktar&\#x27;ın &quot;Kent Siyasetinde Süreklilik ve Değişim: Genel ve Yerel Seçimler Işığında Karaman&\#x27;ın Siyasal Görünümü \(1991–2024\)&quot; başlıklı bölümü, kentin siyasal zeminini seçim verileri üzerinden ele almaktadır\. Son olarak Fatma Calayır, Sema Kaptanoğlu ve Ali Rıza Kul&\#x27;un &quot;The Interaction Between Global Fire Dynamics and Climate Change: Causes, Consequences, and Future Strategies&quot; başlıklı bölümü, tartışmayı küresel ölçekte iklim krizi ve orman yangınları ilişkisine taşımaktadır\. Bölümler birlikte okunduğunda ortak temalar belirginleşmektedir: Teknoloji tek başına yeterli değildir; kurumsal kapasite, katılım ve veri etiği gereklidir\. Küresel normlarla yerel bağlam arasında süregelen bir gerilim vardır\. Sürdürülebilirlik ise ancak sosyal adalet ve ölçekler arası iş birliğiyle mümkündür\.

## [TMEM59 modulates TREM2\-regulated microglial responses in ischemia and serves as a potential therapeutic target](../publications/aa24c15d22a58f77c60a.md)

Jinghui Wang; Zihao Zhao; Jian Meng; Ziqian Tang; Yunxia Lu; Zhongding Li; Jian Zhang; Naizhen Zheng; Jing Cao; Yong Wang; Kun Li; Xian Zhang; Hong Luo; Yingjun Zhao; 李徽徽; Yun‐wu Zhang

Abstract Microglial responses mediated by the triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 \(TREM2\) play a crucial role in ischemia, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear\. Herein, we found that TREM2 and its interacting protein, transmembrane protein 59 \(TMEM59\), had opposite expression dynamics in microglia from mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion \(MCAO/R\) and HMC3 cells treated with oxygen–glucose deprivation/reoxygenation \(OGD/R\), with TREM2 expression gradually increased, whereas TMEM59 expression increased first and then gradually decreased after ischemia modeling\. We confirmed that TREM2 deficiency deteriorated neurological function impairments, cell apoptosis, microgliosis, and neuroinflammation in MCAO/R mice\. Notably, TMEM59 haploinsufficiency dramatically attenuated the exacerbated impairments in TREM2\-deficient mice with MCAO/R\. Mechanistically, TMEM59 deficiency suppressed aberrant autophagy activation and neuroinflammation in microglia following MCAO/R and OGD/R\. Moreover, both microglia\-specific and systemic deletion of TMEM59 ameliorated neurological function impairments, cell apoptosis, microgliosis, neuroinflammation, and aberrant autophagy in MCAO/R mice\. Finally, we developed a peptide targeting TMEM59 to promote its degradation and showed that treatment with this peptide reduced TMEM59 protein levels and effectively rescued neurological impairments and related pathologies in MCAO/R mice\. Our findings establish TMEM59 as a key negative regulator of TREM2 function in microglia and a key driver of maladaptive microglial autophagy and neuroinflammation in ischemia, indicating that TMEM59 reduction represents a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemia treatment\.

## [Multi\-predator feeding aggregations: understanding dynamic communities through functional niches and demographic analysis tools](../publications/aa2eef262d9c47e84ccf.md)

Wednesday Davis; Rochelle Constantine; Gaia Dell’Ariccia

Multi\-predator feeding aggregations \(MPFAs\) are ocean events whereby two or more species forage on the same or co\-occurring prey\. Such communities are dynamic, with community structure reflecting the connections between species and the benefits and costs of associations\. The analysis of MPFAs provides an overview of ecosystem health, with social networks reflecting prey and available resources\. Demographic analyses of MPFAs can act as process\-based indicators of community responses to rapid change\. To understand complex community dynamics, we identified community types in MPFAs using hierarchical clustering and determined the social associations and roles of the different species present\. We collected data on 179 MPFA events, recording 55\.4 hours of behavioural observations from 33 843 individuals belonging to 19 seabird and three cetacean species in the Hauraki Gulf, New Zealand\. Eight MPFA community types were identified, representing planktivorous, scavenger or polytrophic aggregations\. Seabird\-cetacean and seabird\-seabird associations dominated species associations\. We interpret the species&\#x27; roles by combining our observations of behavioural states with knowledge from the literature\. The study of marine MPFAs offers a community\-level perspective for understanding community dynamics and food\-web organization under future ecosystem changes\. Using social network analyses, we advance the understanding of species interconnectedness to better inform ecosystem\-based conservation management\. This article is part of the theme issue &\#x27;Multi\-predator feeding aggregations in the pelagic waters&\#x27;\.

## [SENTINEL\-X: Evaluating Context\-Aware SOC Alert Decision Reliability Under Cross\-Environment and Temporal Distribution Shifts](../publications/aa3ae20dd43822626b5d.md)

Nikhil Bhardwaj

The Security Operation Centers \(SOCs\) are using artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) more and more for detecting and prioritizing security alerts\. While these methods could prove to be effective, there are still issues regarding the shifting distributions and changing realities in which the solutions still need to be tested\. This poses a challenge in terms of generalization and long\-term effectiveness of AI\-driven security operations centers in Security Operation Center \(SOC\)\. To deal with this, we introduce SENTINEL\-X, an experimental framework designed to evaluate the robustness of context\-aware Security Operation Center \(SOC\) decision\-making under distribution shift\. The scope of this research encompasses two primary modalities of distribution shift: environmental discrepancies and time\-based data evolution\. Our framework provides a holistic evaluation of the SOC decision\-making process, spanning threat detection, context driven prioritization, uncertainty estimation and the final determination to either automate actions or escalate them to a security analyst\. To ensure operational realism, SENTINEL\-X bypasses basic classification metrics to directly measure alert ranking, decision trustworthiness, automation coverage, erroneous actions and analyst workload\. We put different setups head\-to\-head to find out if context builds a more resilient AI and if a smart “defer” button can stop automated mistakes before they happen\. The objective of this research is to establish a comprehensive, unified evaluation of AI\-driven SOC workflows under shifting conditions, thereby exposing critical limitations that static or single\-environment test beds fail to reveal\.

## [HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGING IN FRUIT QUALITY ASSESSMENT: SPECTRAL ANALYSIS, MACHINE LEARNING AND APPLICATIONS](../publications/aa3b4a70a7c35ea023de.md)

S\. Manikandan; S\. Parveen; P\. Rajkumar; Balaji Kannan; R\. Kannan

Fruit quality assessment is important for maintaining postharvest quality, reducing losses and improving the efficiency of sorting and grading operations\. Conventional destructive methods provide reliable measurements of physicochemical, chemical, mechanical and microbiological attributes, but generally require sample preparation, laboratory analysis and destruction of the fruit\. Non\-destructive techniques such as visual inspection, machine vision, near\-infrared spectroscopy, multispectral imaging, thermal imaging and electronic nose systems have been increasingly used for fruit quality evaluation, although their ability to provide detailed spatial and spectral information simultaneously is limited\. Hyperspectral imaging \(HSI\) combines imaging and spectroscopy to acquire spatially resolved spectral information from intact fruits, allowing both internal quality attributes and external defects to be assessed\. This review discusses the development and working principles of HSI, scanning and illumination modes, and the major steps involved in spectral data processing, including preprocessing, feature extraction, wavelength selection and dimensionality reduction\. Applications of HSI for internal quality attributes such as soluble solids content, pH, firmness and total soluble solids, as well as external defects and fungal diseases, are reviewed with emphasis on spectral range, data analysis methods and machine\-learning models\. The major challenges include limited and cultivar\-specific datasets, environmental variability, laboratory\-to\-field transferability, insufficient external validation, high\-dimensional data and the lack of standardized protocols\. Future research should focus on compact and portable HSI systems, real\-time inspection, artificial intelligence, multimodal sensing, transfer learning, standardized datasets and commercial\-scale validation to support reliable and practical fruit quality assessment\.

## [Toward Recreating the Breath of Cities in the Atmospheric Simulation Chamber SAPHIR](../publications/aa3c40c8fd63d5a97b25.md)

Yizhen Wu; Ralf Tillmann; Eva Y\. Pfannerstill; Peeyush Khare; Andrea Carolina Marcillo Lara; Achim Grasse; Franz Röhrer; Milan Roska; Clémence Depp; Max G\. Adam; Sarah Albertin; Rabbia Asgher; Thomas J\. Bannan; Shawon Barua; Kelvin H\. Bates; David M\. Bell; Birger Bohn; Steven S\. S Brown; Angela Buchholz; Yanfang Chen; Changmin Cho; Hugh Coe; Matthew Mitchell Coggon; Michelle Färber; Sana Farhoudian; Juliane L\. Fry; Hendrik Fuchs; M\. Graus; Imad El Haddad; Quanfu He; Thorsten Hohaus; Siddharth Iyer; Vlassis A\. Karydis; Avinash Kumar; Markus Sebastian Leiminger; Lu Liu; Emily Matthews; Gordon B\. McFiggans; Ann M\. Middlebrook; Markus Müller; Aki Nissinen; Anke Christine Nölscher; Anna Novelli; Farhan Ramadzan Nursanto; Sébastien Perrier; Andrê S\. H\. Prévôt; Iida Pullinen; Eka Dian Pusfitasari; Tobias Reinecke; Matti P\. Rissanen; Matthieu Riva; Michael A\. Robinson; Siegfried Schobesberger; Chelsea E\. Stockwell; Jens Top; Alexandra P\. Tsimpidi; Netta Vinkvist; Aristeidis Voliotis; Andreas Wahner; Yuantao Wang; Yuwei Wang; C\. Warneke; Robert Wegener; Boxing Yang; Georgios I\. Gkatzelis

Abstract Atmospheric simulation chambers are essential for studying oxidation processes, yet many experiments rely on single\-precursor systems at concentrations that limit their representativeness for the chemical complexity of urban air\. Here, we present a framework linking emission inventories, chamber experiments, and field observations by constructing emission fingerprints of major urban sources, including vegetation, volatile chemical products, cooking emissions, and gasoline and diesel exhaust\. Applied during the CHANEL campaign in the SAPHIR outdoor chamber, these fingerprints advanced toward reproducing gas\-phase mixtures representative of Los Angeles \(gasoline\-dominated traffic\), a diesel\-dominated city, and a future low\-vehicle\-emission scenario\. The resulting mixtures generated peroxy\-to\-hydroperoxy radical ratios \(RO2/HO2\) close to unity, bimolecular RO2 lifetimes comparable with urban atmospheric observations, although lower NO levels favored RO2 \+ HO2 over RO2 \+ NO reactions\. Comparison with aircraft measurements over Los Angeles using ammonium \(NH4\+\) chemical ionization mass spectrometry showed reasonable agreement, with 465 organic product ions detected in both data sets, representing 78% of the product ions observed in the ambient air\. Furthermore, 87% of common product ions agreed within a factor of 3 of the linear correlation, demonstrating that chamber experiments can capture key aspects of both atmospherically relevant radical chemistry and the oxidation product diversity of urban air\.

## [Surrogate\-assisted machine learning framework for performance enhancement of Rb2CuSbF6 perovskite LEDs with MoO3/WO3 charge transport layers](../publications/aa3cbfc4f3bd28aedfbb.md)

Mangey Ram Nagar; Niraj Agrawal; Mohd Sazid; Anil Kumar Gautam; Neha Gupta

Machine learning has become an impressive method to speed up the design and performance prediction of optoelectronic devices, by making the exploration of efficient high\-dimensional and highly nonlinear parameter spaces\. In this paper, we propose a surrogate\-assisted machine learning model to train a performance enhancement of lead\-free Rb 2 CuSbF 6 perovskite light\-emitting diodes \(PeLEDs\) using MoO 3 and WO 3 as hole\- and electron\-transport layer, respectively\. This is done by physics\-based simulations of devices to undertake a systematic parametric sweep of fourteen important material and device parameters producing over 11,000 samples and provides the variation in four important performance measures indicating electrical and optical efficiency\. Several machine learning regression models are developed and tested to build a good surrogate model that is sufficiently accurate to predict the nonlinear interactions among all input parameters and the performance of the device\. The trained surrogate model is subsequently used for rapid prediction and design\-space screening across the multidimensional parameter space, enabling identification of high\-performing combinations of transport\-layer properties at substantially lower computational cost than repeated physics\-based simulations\. The suggested framework has a strong predictive potential and rapid prediction action plan in the design and development of perovskite LEDs\. This paper shows how surrogate\-assisted machine learning solutions can be an efficient and scaled route to creating high\-efficiency, environmentally common\-place lead\-free perovskite light\-emitting devices\.
