## [ABA RENEWAL OF FENTANYL SEEKING USING A DRUG\-PRIME AND PEER STIMULUS IN RATS](../publications/aa4cf29094a9f9429d83.md)

Meagan Blanchard

People with opioid use disorder can experience craving and relapse to use when exposed to cues that were previously paired with the drug\-taking environment\. These cues can be both social and non\-social in nature\. This study aimed to explore the effect of a peer cue and a drug\-prime cue, both together and separately\. First, rats were trained to self\-administer fentanyl in Context A \(peer and drug present\)\. Then, rats extinguished this behavior in Context B \(no peer and no drug present\) while self\-administering saline instead of fentanyl\. Lastly, rats underwent 4 different renewal test conditions \(control, peer only, drug only, peer \+ drug\) in order to determine renewal of drug\-seeking\. It was found that rats renewed drug seeking under the peer only and peer \+ drug conditions, but not the drug only condition\. This suggests that the social cue overshadowed the effect of the nonsocial, drug cue\.

## [Explainable Feature Selection and Hybrid Computational Intelligence Models for Predicting Chloride Penetration in Concrete](../publications/aa4e6e8ec9c435f8efa7.md)

Morteza Khorshidi; Amirehsan Teimortashlu; Ehsan Afaridegan

The Rapid Chloride Permeability Test \(RCPT\) is widely used to assess the durability of concrete against chloride ion ingress; however, this test is time\-consuming, costly, and highly sensitive to laboratory conditions\. Consequently, developing accurate and reliable predictive models has become an attractive alternative to experimental measurements\. In this study, an advanced data\-driven framework is proposed for predicting RCPT values by integrating hybrid machine learning models with robust feature selection strategies\. A comprehensive database comprising 483 experimental samples was compiled from previous studies\. In addition to the primary mix design parameters, a set of ratio\-based and interaction features was generated to better capture complex nonlinear relationships among the variables\. Feature selection was carried out using two complementary approaches, namely Q\-learning–Decision Tree \(Q\-learning–DT\) and NSGA\-II–Decision Tree \(NSGA\-II–DT\)\. The results demonstrate that NSGA\-II–DT achieves superior performance by identifying only five key input variables while maintaining high predictive accuracy\. Subsequently, four hybrid models—CatBoost–SWOA, NGBoost–WOA, TabNet–EVOA, and TabPFN–HEOA—were developed and evaluated using multiple statistical performance indices and Taylor diagrams\. Among the developed models, CatBoost–SWOA exhibited the best predictive capability on the testing dataset, achieving an R 2 value of 0\.966 with the lowest RMSE\. Uncertainty analysis based on residual bootstrapping further confirmed the robustness and stability of this model, yielding the narrowest confidence intervals and the lowest uncertainty measures\. In addition, SHAP\-based interpretability analysis revealed that curing temperature and fly ash content are the most influential parameters governing RCPT values\. The findings indicate that the proposed framework provides an accurate, reliable, and interpretable tool for RCPT prediction and offers a practical alternative to labor\-intensive experimental testing in concrete durability assessment\.

## [Security and Privacy Challenges in Multi \-Cloud Environments : A Comprehensive](../publications/aa528fe4b70b0b757789.md)

Kavita Yadav; Sheshang Degadwala

The rapid adoption of multi \-cloud computing in which organizations distribute workloads and data across two or more cloud service providers \(CSPs\) has introduced a distinct and rapidly evolving class of security and privacy problems that differ materially from those of single \- provider or simple hybrid \-cloud deployments\. This paper presents a review of the security and privacy challenges that arise in multi \-cloud environments synthesizing recent academic literature and industry research published primarily between 2018 and 2026\. The review is organized around six pillars: data security and confidentiality, identity and access management \(IAM\) network security and attack \-surface expansion, privacy \-preserving computation, regulatory compliance and data sovereignty and the emerging role of Zero Trust Architecture \(ZTA\) as a unifying defense paradigm\. For each pillar representative studies are summarized, compared and critically discussed, culminating in a analysis table that maps challenges to proposed solutions and their limitations\. The review concludes by identifying research gaps, including the lack of standardized cross \-CSP security interfaces the shortage of empirically validated Zero Trust deployments in production multi \-cloud settings and the unresolved tension between regulatory data \- sovereignty requirements and the operational flexibility that motivates multi \-cloud adoption in the first place\. This review is intended as a foundation for researchers and practitioners seeking to design resilient privacy \-preserving and regulation \- compliant multi \-cloud architectures\.

## [Explosive protection mechanism of aircraft fuel tank cooling based on minimum ignition energy](../publications/aa5a69932023c010984f.md)

Kelin Ma

Abstract To investigate the cooling and explosion prevention mechanism of aircraft fuel tanks, this study develops an intelligent quantitative model based on Minimum Ignition Energy\. The model integrates Back Propagation Neural Networks, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Grey Wolf Optimizer, and Entropy Weight Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution\. It estimates Minimum Ignition Energy together with temperature and concentration distributions, optimizes cooling conditions, and assesses explosion safety, thus uncovering the connections between them\. The results show that the proposed model achieves root mean square errors of 0\.020 mJ and 0\.12 °C、0\.15%VOL in prediction\. The scheme based on Grey Wolf Optimizer increases Minimum Ignition Energy by 67\.94% and maintains the maximum fuel tank temperature within 35 °C to 45 °C\. Meanwhile, explosion safety is improved by 281\.31% compared with the non\-cooling condition, and the score dispersion is only 0\.021\. This shows that the cooling and explosion prevention of aircraft fuel tanks occur through lowering the temperature of the fuel tank, preventing vaporization, and raising the Minimum Ignition Energy of the fuel\-air mixture\. The proposed model makes possible the process of prediction, optimization, and evaluation simultaneously, ensuring that there will be a scientific, reliable, and objective basis and technique for the design of parameters of aircraft fuel tank cooling and explosion protection systems\.

## [Transparency and compliance of artificial intelligence systems with the EU regulatory framework \(AI Act &amp; GDPR\) : legal and technical approaches](../publications/aa82271b768a8ee6ab26.md)

Σάββας Δανιήλογλου

Η αυξανόμενη χρήση συστημάτων Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και μηχανικής μάθησης σε διαδικασίες λήψης και υποστήριξης αποφάσεων έχει αναδείξει σημαντικά ζητήματα σχετικά με την αλγοριθμική μεροληψία, τη δίκαιη μεταχείριση διαφορετικών πληθυσμιακών ομάδων και τη δυνατότητα ερμηνείας των παραγόμενων προβλέψεων\. Παράλληλα, η εφαρμογή του ευρωπαϊκού ρυθμιστικού πλαισίου, και ειδικότερα του AI Act και του GDPR, ενισχύει την ανάγκη σύνδεσης των νομικών απαιτήσεων με πρακτικές διαδικασίες τεχνικής αξιολόγησης\. Σκοπός της παρούσας διπλωματικής εργασίας είναι η διερεύνηση της σχέσης μεταξύ αλγοριθμικής μεροληψίας, αλγοριθμικής δικαιοσύνης, επεξηγησιμότητας και του ευρωπαϊκού ρυθμιστικού πλαισίου, μέσω του συνδυασμού θεωρητικής και νομικής ανάλυσης με την ανάπτυξη ενός εργαλείου απόδειξης εφικτότητας \(Proof\-of\-Concept, PoC\)\. Για το πειραματικό μέρος χρησιμοποιείται το German Credit Dataset και αναπτύσσεται μοντέλο δυαδικής ταξινόμησης πιστωτικού κινδύνου με τον αλγόριθμο XGBoost\. Η αξιολόγηση πραγματοποιείται σε δύο ανεξάρτητα σενάρια, με ευαίσθητα χαρακτηριστικά την ηλικία και το φύλο\. Η συμπεριφορά του μοντέλου εξετάζεται μέσω των μετρικών αλγοριθμικής δικαιοσύνης Disparate Impact Ratio, Demographic Parity Difference και Equal Opportunity Difference, σε συνδυασμό με μετρικές προβλεπτικής απόδοσης\. Στη συνέχεια εφαρμόζεται η τεχνική Reweighing στο σύνολο εκπαίδευσης και συγκρίνονται τα αποτελέσματα πριν και μετά την παρέμβαση\. Η αξιολόγηση συμπληρώνεται με τη χρήση του TreeSHAP για την τοπική ερμηνεία μεμονωμένων προβλέψεων και με τη δημιουργία δομημένου αρχείου καταγραφής ελέγχου για την τεχνική καταγραφή της πειραματικής διαδικασίας\. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι η επίδραση μιας τεχνικής μετριασμού της μεροληψίας εξαρτάται από το ευαίσθητο χαρακτηριστικό και τις μετρικές που εξετάζονται\. Στην περίπτωση της ηλικίας, το Reweighing οδήγησε συνολικά σε βελτίωση των εξεταζόμενων μετρικών αλγοριθμικής δικαιοσύνης, με μικρή μείωση της προβλεπτικής απόδοσης\. Αντίθετα, στην περίπτωση του φύλου δεν παρατηρήθηκε αντίστοιχη συνολική βελτίωση της αλγοριθμική δικαιοσύνη, ενώ η προβλεπτική απόδοση παρουσίασε μικρή αύξηση\. Τα ευρήματα αναδεικνύουν ότι η αξιολόγηση της αλγοριθμική δικαιοσύνη δεν μπορεί να βασίζεται σε μία μόνο μετρική και ότι η εφαρμογή μιας τεχνικής μετριασμού της μεροληψίας \(mitigation\) δεν εγγυάται τη βελτίωση όλων των διαστάσεων της συμπεριφοράς ενός μοντέλου\. Συνολικά, η εργασία υποστηρίζει ότι η προβλεπτική απόδοση, η αλγοριθμική δικαιοσύνη, η επεξηγησιμότητα και η τεχνική τεκμηρίωση πρέπει να εξετάζονται συνδυαστικά\. Οι τεχνικές μετρήσεις μπορούν να παρέχουν χρήσιμα στοιχεία για την αξιολόγηση ενός συστήματος ΤΝ, χωρίς όμως να αποτελούν από μόνες τους απόδειξη ότι το σύστημα είναι συνολικά «δίκαιο» ή νομικά συμμορφούμενο\.

## [Mattos, José Caetano de: THE DENOUNCING WORM: How the Communist Party\-State Turned Flattery into Complicity — the Floor Ratchet, the Spiral of Proof and the Worm Inflation of the Harvest Record](../publications/aa995a1f90188e865b1e.md)



Every tyranny has had its flatterers\. The communist party\-state did something no court before it had done on such a scale: it turned flattery into denunciation, denunciation into complicity, and complicity into conviction, and it did so across a third of humanity for most of a century\. This article shows how, by joining three results of the Philosophy of Virtues that have so far stood apart: the abolition of the verifier \(The Communist Paradise, Forged, \#130\), the forged gift \(Bread for Silence, \#131\) and the virtue worm, the person who defends a seized power by praising its trivia \(The Virtue Worm, \#132\)\. The cost was paid in lives, in virtues and in freedom\. In lives: the communist party\-states caused deaths counted in tens of millions — about 27 to 64 million in the documented episodes of six countries alone \(\#130, §7\.1\)\. The famine of the Great Leap Forward killed between about 15 and 45 million people, and its harvest records were written not only by officials who feared to report less than the plan but by officials who competed to report more\. In the Great Terror of 1937–38 some 680,000 to 750,000 people were shot, and regional leaders petitioned Moscow for larger quotas of executions than they had been assigned\. In virtues: a regime that could not tell loyal praise from interested praise demanded proofs of loyalty that only harm to others could supply, and so taught whole societies to prove their fidelity by betraying their neighbours, their colleagues and their parents — and left behind a trust between persons that was still measurably lower a generation after the regimes fell\. In freedom: every act of frank speech acquired a price, every denunciation a reward, and the people who could have checked the power were converted, one proof at a time, into its accomplices\. The article establishes six results\. The worm is a negative verifier \(D1\): unlike a silent captured channel, which adds nothing to the detection of a forgery, worm display subtracts from it and adds to the reliance placed on the forged record\. Worm inflation \(T1\): the inflation of a harvest report has a compelled part, the target an official must report, and a worm part, the excess he reports to be seen; the worm part alone can cross the threshold of famine, and when next year’s target is set from this year’s report, the worm’s excess becomes the next official’s floor\. The floor ratchet \(T2\): wherever display is rewarded by rank, the floor of safety rises by the worms’ own excess, so that worm status is unstable and yesterday’s zealot becomes today’s laggard\. The spiral of proof \(T3\): praise is cheap, so it soon carries no information; a power that must still verify loyalty is driven to demand displays that destroy the displayer’s outside options, and the cheapest such displays are harms to others — denunciation, then complicity\. Conversion by complicity \(T4\): the acts the spiral demands are those that turn opportunists into believers\. The chain \(C2\): discretion over forged gifts is the wage the power pays its middle layer for display, so worming upward and gift\-forging downward are one transaction\. The article states where the mechanism does not run — where a verifier survives, where praise keeps its information, where loyalty is fixed by birth, where display is demanded only as submission, and where allocation is by rule — and shows that at the peak of terror, when intensity no longer separates the worm from the frightened, initiative still does: the regional leaders who asked Moscow for larger quotas of executions in 1937 were raising the floor, not standing on it\. The mechanism is not peculiar to communism; National Socialist and military regimes ran it too, and the article says so\. Its thesis is narrower and harder to answer: the Leninist party\-state was the only regime type that removed every boundary of the mechanism at once — it made itself the sole dispenser of livelihood, defined orthodoxy by a line that moved so that anyone could fall from it, taught denunciation to children as a virtue, and abolished every verifier that could have stopped the spiral\. Its catastrophes were therefore not the work of a few bad leaders, nor the excesses of local zealots, nor the product of fear alone\. They were the output of a structure its founders chose to build\. The article is also an instrument against that structure\. Its results give a diagnosis that can be applied from documents — the initiative criterion identifies the agents who raised the floor of repression rather than standing on it\. Its five boundaries are five defences, each of which stops the spiral: an independent verifier, allocation by public rule, plural sources of livelihood, protection for speech that goes up against power and no reward for reports that go sideways against peers, and the opening of archives after the regime falls\. And its results answer, one by one, the four defences on which apologists for communist rule still rely: that its founders meant well, that its crimes were local excesses, that its people were merely afraid, and that its evils were the work of a few\. The same structure now has new bodies, in the states that communist parties still govern, in states that score civic conduct and reward the reporting of others, and in artificial systems that make praise costless at scale\. Three tests are registered; none has been run\. Keywords: communism; denunciation; complicity; flattery inflation; cult of personality; virtue worm; costly signalling; Great Leap Forward; famine; launching satellites; Lushan Conference; Pavlik Morozov; clientelism; brokers; preference falsification; verification; Philosophy of Virtues; social credit system; AI sycophancy\. Highlights • The communist party\-states caused deaths counted in tens of millions — about 27 to 64 million in the documented episodes of six countries alone — and destroyed the trust between persons on which every shared virtue depends\. • The communist party\-state did not merely tolerate flatterers\. It converted flattery into denunciation and denunciation into complicity, and it did so because it could no longer tell its friends from its flatterers\. • A virtue worm is a negative verifier: its praise does not merely fail to expose a forged record, it consumes the attention that could expose it and increases the reliance placed on it\. • The Great Leap’s harvest records had two authors: the official who feared to report less than the plan, and the official who competed to report more\. The second alone could push a county past the threshold of famine, and his excess became his neighbours’ target the following year\. • Where praise is rewarded by rank, the floor of safety rises by the worms’ own excess\. Yesterday’s zealot becomes today’s laggard, and the ratchet eats its own worms\. • When praise carries no information, proof of loyalty migrates to acts that burn the displayer’s bridges\. The cheapest bridge to burn is another person: denunciation first, complicity after\. • Complicity makes believers\. The regime that demanded proofs in order to find true believers manufactured them, and they did not transfer their loyalty when the regime fell\. • The middle layer of a single\-dispenser state is paid in discretion\. Each intermediary is a worm towards those above and a dispenser of forged gifts towards those below\. • The spiral has boundaries: it stalls where a verifier survives, where loyalty is fixed by birth, where display is demanded only as submission, and where allocation is by rule\. • At the peak of terror the worm is found by initiative, not intensity: the regional leaders who petitioned for larger quotas of executions in 1937 were raising the floor, not standing on it\. • Communism did not invent the mechanism\. It was the only regime that removed all its boundaries at once, and so the only one in which it ran without a brake for generations\. • The apologist’s four defences fail: good intentions do not change a structure, local excess became national obligation through the target, initiative shows more than fear, and the mechanism needed millions of intermediaries, not a few bad men\. • The boundaries are the defences: keep one verifier out of the power’s reach, allocate by public rule, keep livelihood plural, protect speech that goes up against power and never reward reports that go sideways against peers, and open the archives when the regime falls\. • Scoring states that reward the reporting of others, and artificial systems that make praise costless, rebuild the conditions of the spiral\. The defence is the same as in the twentieth century: verifiers the power does not control, and help it cannot withdraw for a vote\. • Freedom dies not only when it is taken but when people are paid to prove their loyalty by taking it from one another; against that loss, the virtue of frank speech has no institutional substitute\. Relevance The question why so many ordinary, intelligent people under the communist states denounced their neighbours, inflated their reports and took part in campaigns they privately doubted has usually been answered with fear\. Fear explains a great deal, but it does not explain the excess: the official who reported a yield ten times the plan, the colleague who denounced before he was asked, the believer who was made rather than born\. This article explains the excess structurally, without assuming that the people concerned were unusually wicked, and it shows how the excess killed\. The answer matters for the present for three reasons\. First, the mechanism is not historical: every institution that rewards displayed loyalty and cannot verify it is under the same pressure to demand costlier proofs, and every institution that rewards the reporting of colleagues is building the first step of the spiral\. Second, states that score the conduct of their citizens, such as China’s Social Credit System, publish the floor of safety as a number and attach rewards to exceeding it; the floor ratchet predicts what follows\. Third, artificial intelligence now makes praise effectively free to produce in any quantity\. By the spiral of proof, a power that wishes to read loyalty will be pushed faster towards proofs that cost the prover something real, and in political life the costliest proofs have always been paid by other people\. The answer also matters because communism is not over\. Communist parties still hold power over about a fifth of humanity, and the apologetics of the twentieth\-century regimes — that their founders meant well, that their crimes were the excesses of local zealots or of a few bad leaders, that their peoples were merely afraid — are still taught\. This article gives the reader a structural answer to each, and a set of defences derived from the mechanism itself \(§11\.1\), so that what destroyed so many lives can be recognised at its first step and stopped before its last\. For individuals the article offers what the programme offers throughout: a description of the act before which a person can stop\. The spiral begins with a sentence of praise that costs nothing and ends with a signature beneath another person’s name\. Every step in between is taken by someone who could have spoken frankly instead\. \(direct link \)

## [Functional brain activity in cancer\-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies](../publications/aab1df3412f665d3d705.md)

Barbara Johanne Thomas Nordhjem; Laura Maria Toftekær Rothschild; Clotilde Rose Honoré; Anders Thyge Steen Larsen; Martin Kaj Fridh; Lisa Lyngsie Hjalgrim

Cancer\-related cognitive impairment \(CRCI\) is reported across the cancer trajectory, yet its neurobiological basis remains incompletely understood\. Electroencephalography \(EEG\) provides a temporally precise method for assessing brain activity at rest and during cognitive processing, but its application in CRCI research has not been systematically mapped\. This scoping review characterized how EEG has been used to study cognitive functioning in people with cancer, including populations studied, EEG paradigms and analytic approaches employed, and cognitive outcomes assessed\. Following PRISMA\-ScR guidance, we searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science from inception to February 2025 for studies using EEG to examine cognitive functioning\. Sixty articles were included\. Most were small and cross\-sectional, with publication output increasing markedly after 2015\. Task\-based event\-related potentials, particularly from oddball and attention tasks, were used most frequently, whereas quantitative EEG approaches, including spectral power and connectivity analyses, were less common\. In populations with cancers outside the central nervous system \(CNS\), longer P300 latency and lower amplitude were common, but opposite and null findings also occurred\. Evidence from primary CNS and other intracranial tumor populations was sparse\. Across cancer contexts, quantitative EEG findings showed limited convergence across articles\. Associations between EEG measures and cognitive outcomes were inconsistent and often not tested directly\. Overall, EEG provides a complementary approach to investigating cognition in people with cancer, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous\. Larger longitudinal studies, more consistent cognitive outcome selection, and closer integration of neural and cognitive measures are needed to establish reproducible findings and evaluate their potential clinical utility\. Systematic review registration https://www\.crd\.york\.ac\.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251084951 \.

## [Improving detection of candidates for botulinum toxin therapy in spasticity: an interprofessional screening approach](../publications/aab85ada2678d8b39e9f.md)

Melanie Rudelstorfer; B\. Mayr\-Pirker; Eugen Trinka; Bernhard Iglseder; Richard Friedrich Radlberger

Background Spastic movement disorders \(SMD\) are commonly treated with botulinum toxin, however, many patients who may benefit from treatment remain unrecognized in routine clinical practice\. Early identification is particularly challenging in non\-specialized settings\. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of interprofessional screening tools for identifying patients with clinically relevant SMD requiring referral for specialist assessment\. Methods In this prospective, two\-phase, single\-center study, 124 patients who received care by departments of neurology and geriatrics were included\. In phase 1, the Spastic Movement Disorder decision tree \(SMD\-DT\) was applied independently by nurses, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists and compared with the clinical assessment of an experienced neurologist as the reference standard\. Based on the findings, a simplified nursing screening tool, the Salzburg Nursing Questionnaire \(SNQ\), was developed and subsequently evaluated in independent cohorts in phase 2 of the study\. Results The SMD\-DT demonstrated high agreement with the reference standard in neurological rehabilitation settings, with a high degree of consistency across all professional groups compared with the expert, but showed substantially lower performance among nurses in non\-specialized geriatric settings\. In contrast, the SNQ consistently achieved high diagnostic accuracy in these settings \(sensitivity of 1\.00 and specificity of 0\.96\) considering treatment recommendation\. Conclusion The diagnostic performance of screening instruments for SMD depends strongly on both clinical context and professional background\. These findings support the implementation of profession\-specific screening strategies to improve early recognition of clinically relevant SMD, facilitating timely referral for specialist evaluation, and optimize access to botulinum toxin therapy in routine clinical practice\.

## [Distill Until Divergence: Error\-Truncated Hindsight Distillation for Agentic RL](../publications/aac1844158fe227af264.md)

Yibin Huang; Conghui Zhu

Long\-horizon interaction requires agents to make multiple decisions in a changing environment\. Outcome\-based GRPO lacks fine\-grained guidance for intermediate decisions\. Recent methods distill completed trajectories into reusable skills and use hindsight\-conditioned OPD to provide dense token\-level credit\. However, skill\-induced probability shifts do not necessarily represent reward\-aligned credit; especially after an erroneous action changes subsequent interaction states, skill\-conditioned supervision may become mismatched with the current state\. To address this mismatch, we propose \\methodname\{\}, which routes two complementary hindsight skills according to trajectory outcomes and error boundaries: Positive skills capture successful workflows to reinforce successful trajectories and pre\-error decisions, while Negative skills capture failure\-specific corrections to target decisive errors\. The post\-error suffix is optimized exclusively by GRPO, retaining outcome\-based learning without extending potentially mismatched hindsight supervision\. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive task performance and support effective fine\-grained credit allocation\.

## [Similar perceived availability but lower use of physical activity spaces among Chilean adults with disabilities](../publications/aac4caa2095cc5a6e3b1.md)

Josivaldo de Souza\-Lima; Ciro Winckler; Jurgi Olasagasti\-Ibargoien; Rodrigo Alejandro Yañez Sepulveda; Cristian Godoy\-Tapia; Maribel Parra\-Saldías; Daniel Michel Duclos Bastías; Andrés Esteban Roberto Godoy\-Cumillaf; Eugenio Merellano\-Navarro; José Bruneau\-Chávez; Tomás Reyes\-Amigo; Claudio Farías‐Valenzuela

Background Adults with disabilities are less physically active than the general population, yet the environmental point at which this disparity emerges is rarely identified in national surveillance\. We examined perceived availability, use, and barriers to the use of physical activity spaces among Chilean adults with and without disabilities, and estimated the association of disability with physical inactivity and with non\-use of available spaces\. Methods Cross\-sectional analysis of the 2024 National Survey of Physical Activity and Sports Habits \(ENAFyD\), a probabilistic national sample of adults in Chile \( n = 8,653\)\. Self\-reported disability was classified into mutually exclusive categories \(sensory only, physical only, cognitive only, multiple types, other only, none\) and cross\-classified with perceived availability of spaces near the home, their use, reported barriers among non\-users, and the survey physical activity index\. Group differences were tested with weighted Poisson regression with robust variance, reported as crude prevalence ratios \(PR\) with 95% confidence intervals and p values; adjusted models included sex, age group, and socioeconomic status, selected a priori as confounders using a directed acyclic graph\. Results The weighted prevalence of disability was 9\.3%\. Perceived availability of spaces did not differ between groups \(92\.1% vs\. 91\.4%; crude PR 1\.01; 95% CI 0\.99\-1\.03; p = 0\.478\)\. However, among adults with available spaces, only 29\.9% \(95% CI 25\.4\-34\.8\) of those with disabilities used them, compared with 42\.7% \(40\.8\-44\.6\) of those without \(crude PR for non\-use 1\.22; 1\.16\-1\.29; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The largest differential barriers were distance or difficulty of access \(14\.0% vs\. 7\.7%; PR 1\.82; 1\.44\-2\.31\) and lack of companionship \(25\.9% vs\. 16\.8%; PR 1\.54; 1\.31\-1\.80\)\. In adjusted models, disability was associated with physical inactivity \(PR 1\.22; 1\.11\-1\.33\) and with non\-use of available spaces \(PR 1\.14; 1\.08\-1\.20\), with the largest estimate among adults reporting multiple disability types \(PR 1\.47; 1\.35\-1\.60\)\. Conclusions In Chilean adults, the disability gap in physical activity is concentrated in the use of spaces rather than in their perceived availability, and access\- and companionship\-related barriers were more frequently reported by non\-users with disabilities\. Policies should prioritize the usability of existing spaces, through accessibility, safe access, and social support, alongside new construction\.

## [3D printed spinal fusion devices: Technological breakthroughs, clinical challenges and intelligent future](../publications/aaddc2292c6a5ab22a58.md)

Anning Su; Rong Zhou; Zanrong Huang; Licheng Cai; Hao Chen; Qingguo Zhao; Jia Xu; Linfeng Xie

Three\-dimensional \(3D\)‑printed spinal fusion devices have emerged as a transformative solution to the limitations associated with conventional spinal implants, including mechanical mismatch, limited biocompatibility, and insufficient bioactivity\. This review summarizes recent advances in the development of 3D‑printed spinal fusion devices and discusses how additive manufacturing technologies address key shortcomings of traditional implants\. Recent evidence demonstrates that additive manufacturing enables the fabrication of patient‑specific implants with optimized porous architectures—such as triply periodic minimal surface \(TPMS\) structures—that closely replicate the mechanical characteristics of native bone while promoting osseointegration\. In addition, the integration of bioactive materials and functional coatings enhances biological performance and introduces multifunctional capabilities, including localized drug delivery and improved interface stability\. Another important development is the application of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in implant design and surgical planning, enabling personalized structural optimization and biomechanical matching\. Overall, the convergence of 3D printing and AI is accelerating the transition toward intelligent and personalized spinal implants with the potential to substantially improve surgical outcomes\. However, widespread clinical translation will require long‑term safety validation, cost reduction, and the establishment of standardized regulatory frameworks\.

## [Perceived Social Support dan Post\-Traumatic Growth Remaja yang ditinggalkan Orang Tua](../publications/aaeec1fc3ad8141dd442.md)

Alifiah Matano Dita; Aisyah Putri Rawe Mahardika

Perceived Social Support merupakan salah satu bentuk dari dukungan sosial yang dapat mempengaruhi pertumbuhan psikologis seseorang setelah mengalami peristiwa traumatis atau disebut dengan Post\-traumatic growth\. Dukungan secara emosional dan materil dalam berbagai situasi memiliki peran penting membentuk seorang remaja terkhususnya remaja yang telah ditinggalkan oleh orang tua\. Penelitian dilakukan di Kabupaten Sumbawa dengan melibatkan 100 sampel remaja yang kehilangan orang tua karena meninggal dunia\. Hipotesis pada penelitian ini yakni, Ha diterima dan H0 ditolak yang menunjukkan bahwa terdapat pengaruh perceived social support terhadap post\-traumatic growth pada remaja yang ditinggalkan orang tua\. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa terdapat pengaruh signifikan sebesar 40,6% \(sig\. p\-value = &lt; 0,001, R2 = 0,406\), dengan arah positif \(β = 0,594\) yang artinya semakin tinggi perceived social support maka, akan semakin tinggi juga post\-traumatic growth remaja\. Implikasi praktis dari penelitian ini ialah, remaja yang mengalami kehilangan orang tua diharapkan mampu mengenali dan memanfaatkan dukungan dari lingkungan sekitar guna membantu proses pemulihan dan menghadapi pengalaman kehilangan\.

## [Physical and mathematical model of display requirements for ai monitoring of educational content](../publications/aaf426356ae6d69ff69b.md)

Victor Vasilyevich Belyaev; Yu\. Obydenkov; A\. I\. Rulev; V\. I\. Ermolaev; A\. V\. Lukyanovich; A\. A\. Hetagurov; S\. A\. Kochemirov; Anatoly Vitalyevich Litvin; N\. A\. Konovalova

Aim \. The work aims to develop a physico\-mathematical model that links the physical and technical characteristics of a display – namely spatial resolution, refresh rate, color gamut, and image output latency, taking into account material parameters – with the productivity of a teacher who checks digital educational materials using AI tools for compliance with the requirements of the Federal State Educational Standards \(FSES\)\. Methodology \. The starting point was the well\-studied limitations of the human visual system: the angular resolution of the eye, the critical flicker fusion frequency, and thresholds for color discrimination\. Based on this data, the authors determined which display parameter values should be considered minimally acceptable and which should be considered desirable\. Next, an efficiency objective function W disp was introduced, comprising three components: time spent, number of errors made, and subjectively perceived workload \(according to the NASA TLX methodology\)\. In addition, a review was carried out of publications on how pixel density, frame refresh rate, and color accuracy affect the user&\#x27;s cognitive load\. Results \. Based on physiological limitations of vision, the following set of display parameters is justified for AI monitoring tasks: pixel density of about 300 PPI, refresh rate of 120 Hz, sRGB color space coverage of at least 99%, and response time not exceeding 8 ms\. The form of the efficiency objective function is formulated\. Calculations show that when working on a display with the above characteristics, the value of W disp is approximately 30–35% higher than when using a standard office monitor\. Research implications\. The proposed model makes it possible to translate display equipment requirements into quantitative indicators, which is especially relevant for educational institutions where AI monitoring systems are already being implemented or are planned for implementation\. The findings can be applied in two directions: first, in developing standards for equipping schools with technical means, and second, in compiling methodological materials and recommendations addressed directly to practicing teachers\. It is shown what physical properties of the material affect the parameters of the information display device\.

## [Research on Micro\-Regeneration Design of Historic Districts Based on the Resilient City Concept](../publications/aaf8f8a4550b7e2b458c.md)

Jinxun Ruan

Against the backdrop of accelerating urbanization and frequent environmental crises, building resilient cities has become an urgent priority\. As carriers of urban memory, historic districts are facing new challenges in micro\-renewal\. Grounded in the concept of resilient cities, this study targets the integration of energy sustainability and urban adaptability, drawing on theories of urban ecology and building adaptability\. Adopting methods such as field investigation and interdisciplinary analysis, it conducts in\-depth research into historic districts\. The study finds that rational layout of new energy facilities can improve energy self\-sufficiency, and constructing flexible spaces enables districts to cope with disasters\. The contribution lies in providing an innovative model for historic district renewal, with the unique strength of organically integrating energy, adaptability and historical culture, balancing conservation and development, and promoting urban sustainability\.

## [Procalcitonin\-guided antibiotic discontinuation after ADAPT\-Sepsis: a national survey of current practice and readiness for implementation](../publications/ab07df6069b04817334c.md)

Richard O&\#x27;sullivan; Thomas Knight; Daniel Edward Horner; Paul M Wilson; Jo C Dumville; Tim Felton; Paul M Dark

Procalcitonin \(PCT\)\-guided antibiotic discontinuation is increasingly supported by evidence, but current UK practice remains uncertain\. We conducted a national survey of acute healthcare staff to describe current PCT use and organisational readiness for implementation of PCT\-guided antibiotic discontinuation\. Eighty\-six responses were analysed\. PCT was mostly measured occasionally in selected patients, while 28% of respondents reported rarely or never measuring PCT\. Nearly half wished to increase their use of PCT\-guided antibiotic discontinuation, while almost a third wanted further information before making practice changes\. Organisational readiness scores were generally favourable\. Ongoing implementation may be supported by national guidance, local protocols and education\.

## [A Starfish‐Inspired Hierarchical Multimodal Flexible Sensor for Decoupled Thumb Motion Perception and Virtual Human–Machine Interaction](../publications/ab0909200b55747005b7.md)

Lu Liu; Zengbai Ouyang; Mengze Zhang; Jiantao Yao; Xiaoli Jia; Peng Zhang; Bo Han; Yu Gu; Yundou Xu

ABSTRACT Wearable human–machine interfaces \(HMIs\) require sensing systems that combine high accuracy, mechanical compliance, and low system complexity\. Here, we present a starfish‐inspired, hierarchically decoupled multimodal flexible sensor for high‐fidelity thumb motion perception and virtual human–machine interaction\. Inspired by the distributed sensing mechanism of starfish tube feet, the architecture integrates radially distributed strain channels with spatially isolated pressure nodes\. This design enables simultaneous sensing of global deformation and localized tactile stimuli while minimizing mechanical coupling\. Finite element simulations and experimental characterization demonstrate effective strain amplification, low interchannel coupling, stable electromechanical performance, and long‐term durability\. Combined with a Light Gradient Boosting Machine \(LightGBM\) classifier, the system achieves validation and test accuracies of 99\.82% and 99\.27%, respectively, for six thumb motions, with strong cross‐subject generalization\. The decoded motions enable intuitive, real‐time control in a virtual environment without bulky sensor gloves or external tracking systems\. This work establishes a bioinspired strategy for structurally decoupled multimodal flexible sensing and provides a promising platform for wearable HMIs and intelligent robotics\.

## [Predicting](../publications/ab0d28f26695790291b4.md)

T1\.Faker 

Speech comprehension relies heavily on predictive processing, enabling listeners to predict upcoming information before it is heard\. While extensive research has demonstrated predictive processing at the linguistic level, it remains unclear whether listeners also anticipate properties of the upcoming speaker during speech comprehension\. The present study investigated whether listeners pre\-activate phonological information and speaker\-related information using electroencephalography \(EEG\) and representational similarity analysis \(RSA\)\. Sixty\-two native Mandarin speakers listened to four\-character Chinese idioms produced by one male and one female speaker\. We constructed three types of trial pairs: \(1\) phonology\-related pairs \(pairs that predict similar phonological information from distinct speakers\), \(2\) speaker\-related pairs \(pairs that predict the same speaker despite different phonological information\), and \(3\) unrelated pairs \(different phonological forms produced by different speakers\)\. Prior to the onset of the idiom\-final segment, both phonology\-related pairs and speaker\-related pairs elicited greater neural pattern similarity than unrelated pairs, with phonology\-related effects emerging earlier than speaker\-related effects\. These findings showed that listeners pre\-activated both phonological information and speaker\-related information before the onset of upcoming speech, with the phonological similarity effect emerging earlier than the speaker\-related effect\. This suggest that anticipatory representations during speech comprehension may involve multiple types of information\.

## [Development of Dual\-Target Protein Kinase Inhibitors for Tau Hyperphosphorylation in Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease\.](../publications/ab1065f28ef264c5762b.md)

Rekha Pathak

Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease with a course of progressive cognitive dysfunction, failure of synapses functions, and a loss of neurons; mostly related to the deposition of amyloid\-β plaques \(Aβ\) and hyperphosphorylation of tau protein\. Glycogen Synthase Kinase\-3β \(GSK\-3β\) and Cyclin\-Dependent Kinase\-5 \(CDK5\) are important kinases involved in tau\-related processes: promoting neurofibrillary tangle formation and neuronal degeneration, respectively\. In the present study, a series of inhibitors of GSK\-3β and CDK5 were screened to identify new dual\-target inhibitors for AD treatment, focusing on the ability to inhibit hyperphosphorylation of tau\.In the present study the ability of a series of GSK\-3β and CDK5 inhibitors to inhibit hyperphosphorylation of tau was assessed and has led to the identification of novel dual\-target inhibitors as potential therapeutic candidates for the care of tau hyperphosphorylated in AD\. A computational integrated approach to drug discovery, including protein modeling and preparation, high throughput virtual screening, sequential dual docking, molecular dynamics simulation, binding free energy prediction and ADMET prediction, was used in the process\. To optimize the X\-ray crystal structure for docking studies, X\-ray crystal structures of GSK\-3β and CDK5 were taken from PDB are shown in figure graphical abstract\. Ambiguity Library of structurally diverse ligands was screened against both kinase targets to search for high structure similarity for two targets, meaning compounds with strong dual inhibitory activity\. Out of the shortlisted molecules, Compounds 08, 09, 05, and 10 showed very good docking scores along with stable hydrogen bonding interactions and good hydrophobic contacts with the ATP\-binding pockets of the both kinases\. The structural stability and stability of protein–ligand interactions under physiological conditions were confirmed by molecular dynamics simulation and the binding free energies were calculated with MM\-PBSA with good scores\. In silico studies including ADMET and permeability across blood–brain barrier also showed that chosen compounds had good pharmacokinetics, CNS permeability, metabolic stability, and had low predicted toxicity\. The identified dual inhibitors showed highly promising potential to inhibit tau hyperphosphorylation by targeting both GSK\-3β and CDK5 and provide a potential multi\-target based therapeutic approach to Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease\. The findings suggest that the identified lead compounds are worth further testing and optimization and could be used to create effective anti\-Alzheimer drugs\.

## [Peningkatan User Experience Website SIP Dispendukcapil Jember Melalui Evaluasi UEQ Dan SDLC Waterfall](../publications/ab1aa0a321899b095b28.md)

Nurulia Ainur Rohmah; Henny Wahyu Sulistyo; Habibatul Azizah Al Faruq; Nur Qodariyah Fitriyah; Qurrota A&\#x27;yun

Website SIP Dispendukcapil Jember merupakan media pelayanan administrasi kependudukan berbasis web yang masih memerlukan peningkatan pada aspek pengalaman pengguna, terutama terkait kemudahan penggunaan, navigasi, dan tampilan antarmuka\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi user experience menggunakan User Experience Questionnaire \(UEQ\) serta mengembangkan website melalui Software Development Life Cycle \(SDLC\) model Waterfall\. Evaluasi dilakukan berdasarkan enam dimensi UEQ, kemudian hasilnya digunakan sebagai dasar penyusunan kebutuhan sistem\. Setelah pengembangan selesai, dilakukan evaluasi ulang menggunakan instrumen yang sama\. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan seluruh dimensi UEQ mengalami peningkatan, dengan kenaikan terbesar pada dimensi Novelty sebesar 0,632 dan Dependability sebesar 0,387 setelah implementasi pengembangan sistem\. Berdasarkan UEQ Benchmark, dimensi attractiveness, efficiency, dependability, dan novelty berada pada kategori Excellent, sedangkan perspicuity dan stimulation berada pada kategori Good\. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa penerapan UEQ sebagai dasar pengembangan melalui SDLC Waterfall mampu meningkatkan kualitas user experience Website SIP Dispendukcapil Jember\.Kata Kunci: User Experience ; UEQ; SDLC; Waterfall; Website

## [Augment the Cache, Replace the Activation: A 2x2 Study of Internal\-State Sharing](../publications/ab1edf126c8543f7ad39.md)

Adam Deng; Shicheng Liu; Yada Zhu

Multi\-agent systems built from frozen language models communicate through text, which discards the internal state the sender already computed and makes the receiver pay to rebuild it\. Work on internal channels avoids that cost, framing the problem as transfer: agent A sends information to agent B\. Every agent pair that must communicate needs its own transfer bridge, and every agent added to a system needs a new bridge fitted against each previous agent\. We reframe this problem as sharing: an agent publishes its internal state once into a pool, and every peer reads that pool through a single mechanism fitted to no sender in particular, so adding an agent adds a publisher and no new bridge\. Whereas the carrier of the internal state and the fusion mechanism are usually chosen independently in the literature, our main finding is that these two choices are coupled; the deciding factor is where the carrier enters the receiver&\#x27;s computation\. Consumability is a property of the receiving computation rather than of the representation\. We find that the key\-value \(KV\) cache must be augmented rather than swapped in: the receiver cross\-attends over a peer&\#x27;s cache while keeping its own, and with only a small query\-side adapter trained, matches the accuracy it gets from reading the source document\. Activations invert this\. They are best written straight into the receiver, with no bridge, no adapter and no training, which beats exposing them alongside the receiver&\#x27;s own, though that advantage rests on knowing where in the receiver the state belongs\. The rule is augment the KV cache, replace the activation, established under one protocol with a shared control ladder\. One adapter, trained once, also serves publishers it never trained on, and a pool of several at once, but only those whose internal state lies close to the receiver&\#x27;s own\.

## [Flat optics for analog computing: From fundamental mechanisms to advanced meta\-processors](../publications/ab250c2f2c226e047c47.md)

Tingting Liu; Jumin Qiu; Xintong Shi; Qiegen Liu; Shuyuan Xiao

As the explosive growth of visual data increasingly strains the latency and energy limits of conventional electronic computing, optical analog computing has re\-emerged as a disruptive paradigm for zero\-power, speed\-of\-light information processing\. Propelled by the unprecedented wave\-manipulation capabilities of optical metasurfaces, this field is undergoing a rapid transition from macroscopic physical optics to ultra\-compact, on\-chip meta\-processors\. This Review examines the fundamental mechanisms of metasurface\-empowered optical computing spanning Fourier\-domain, nonlocal spatial\-domain, and interferometric architectures that perform mathematical operations, with a particular focus on spatial differentiation and edge detection as representative computing tasks\. By emphasizing recent breakthroughs, we highlight the evolution of meta\-processors from static, linear regimes to dynamically reconfigurable, nonlinear, and quantum\-assisted multidimensional platforms\. We also envision how the synergy of AI\-driven inverse design and the integration of analog meta\-front\-ends with optical neural networks will synergistically revolutionize next\-generation intelligent machine vision\.

## [Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection](../publications/ab3169a9bc9fc9a350a4.md)

Dixi Yao; Tahseen Rabbani; Tian Li

Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) enhances the capabilities of large language models \(LLMs\) by querying external structured knowledge\. However, it can also introduce privacy risks by leaking sensitive information from the retrieval datastore\. We propose a simple method to preserve datastore privacy in RAG systems via random projection\. By applying the same projection to both datastore embeddings and query embeddings, our method provably preserves semantic similarity between queries and retrieved items while substantially mitigating data extraction attacks\. Across multiple RAG architectures and datasets, we show that this lightweight approach achieves superior retrieval and generation performance compared to prior methods which leverage formal differential privacy \(DP\) guarantees, while exhibiting comparable empirical privacy under strong attack models\. Our results for the first time suggest that random projection can serve as a competitive and practical baseline for privacy\-preserving RAG systems\.

## [Analysis of the Relationship Between Disease Self\-Management and Psychosocial Adjustment of Celiac Patients](../publications/ab4bdc353dfb17f9c91e.md)

İ̇lknur Bodur; Hilal Tüzer

BACKGROUND/AIMS:In this study, it was aimed to analyze the relationship between disease self\-management and psychosocial adjustment of celiac patients\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study was designed as descriptive and correlational\.The data for the study were collected from 279 individuals with celiac disease between 25 July 2024 and 25 October 2024\.In our study, the psychosocial adjustment levels of patients with celiac disease were evaluated with respect to various socio\-demographic factors \(such as gender, marital status, income level, and education level\)\.RESULTS: Analyses indicated that female patients had worse psychosocial adjustment than male patients\.Single patients had higher scores on the sub\-dimensions of domestic environment and psychological distress than married patients\.Participants who had another family member diagnosed with celiac disease demonstrated better healthcare orientation\.Increasing age was associated with greater acceptance of chronic disease and better treatment compliance\.The results reveal that factors such as gender, marital status, and income level are significant determinants of self\-management and psychosocial adjustment among patients with celiac disease\. CONCLUSION:To improve the psychological adaptation and self\-management among patients with celiac disease, support programs should consider factors such as income, gender, marital status, and age\.Financial support should be provided to cope with the economic burden of the diet, and educational programs should be organized not only for patients but also for their families so that they can be supportive in this process\.

## [Reconstructing the Fiqh of Time](../publications/ab4bf940a35e4cc0fb35.md)

Rohendi Rohendi; Neng Sarah; Abdul Manaf Lubis

Time is an important dimension of Islamic law because certain legal rulings depend on specific temporal conditions\. However, existing studies generally examine time within specific fields of Islamic jurisprudence or as a factor in legal change, without an integrated framework that explains its role in Islamic legal reasoning\. This study reconstructs Fiqh of Time as a conceptual framework for temporal legal analysis, rather than as a new branch of Islamic jurisprudence\. Employing doctrinal legal research with conceptual and comparative approaches, the study analyzes normative sources, classical juristic works, and contemporary scholarship through qualitative content analysis, doctrinal interpretation, and conceptual synthesis\. The study develops three analytical functions: Temporal Activation, in which temporal conditions activate legal applicability through sabab or sharṭ; Temporal Limitation, in which temporal boundaries determine the scope or termination of legal consequences; and Temporal Adaptation, in which changes in temporal conditions, as part of changing realities, are evaluated through ‘illah, maṣlaḥah, and maqāṣid al\-sharī‘ah before legal application is retained or adjusted through ijtihad\. The model connects textual norms, temporal facts, ḥukm waḍ‘ī, changing realities, and maqāṣid within a single analytical process\.

## [Stress Distribution Prediction in front of the crack tip using Artificial Neural Networks: A Data\-Driven Approach in Fracture Mechanics](../publications/ab52d19651b59652a6d8.md)

Khairul Anam; Anindito Purnowidodo; Pavan Kumar Asur Vijaya Kumar; Heinz E\. Pettermann

Understanding the stress distribution in front of the crack tip is essential because this region experiences high stress concentration that can control crack initiation and propagation\. This study proposes an artificial neural network \(ANN\) model as a computationally efficient surrogate model for predicting the stress distribution and stress values in front of the crack tip in a simple cracked geometry\. The proposed ANN model complements conventional finite element method \(FEM\) analyses by enabling rapid stress prediction once the model has been trained\. The results show that the ANN model can capture the general relationship between the stress intensity factor, radial distance, angular position, and crack\-tip stress\. However, its predictive performance strongly depends on the magnitude of the stress intensity factor\. At low K values, the ANN model shows significant discrepancies in both stress values and contour visualization, and it cannot accurately reproduce the theoretical butterfly\-shaped stress distribution\. At higher K values, the predicted stress distribution is closer to the analytical solution, and the contour shape is more consistent\. These findings indicate that the present ANN model should be regarded as a proof\-of\-concept surrogate model with limitations, rather than a replacement for analytical LEFM solutions or FEM analysis\.

## [The Predictive Role of Instructional Leadership in Polytechnic Change Management Amidst TVET Reform: Integrating Hallinger&\#x27;s Model and McKinsey&\#x27;s 7\-S Framework](../publications/ab53980d0f9968059c76.md)

Wan Hanim Nadrah Wan Muda; Nur\` Aqilah Ab Rahim

Technical and Vocational Education and Training \(TVET\) transformation in Malaysian polytechnics requires effective instructional leadership and strategic change management\. This study examined the perceived levels of instructional leadership and change management among polytechnic administrators and investigated the predictive role of instructional leadership in change management within southern\-zone polytechnics\. The conceptual framework draws on Hallinger’s Instructional Leadership Model, operationalised through the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale \(PIMRS\), and McKinsey’s 7\-S Framework for change management\. A quantitative, cross\-sectional survey design was employed using an online questionnaire\. The target population comprised 163 higher\-level administrators, including directors, deputy directors, heads of departments, heads of units, and heads of programmes, across eight polytechnics in Malaysia’s southern zone\. A total of 108 valid responses were obtained\. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and simple linear regression\. The findings revealed high levels of perceived instructional leadership and change management among polytechnic administrators\. Instructional leadership was significantly and positively associated with change management and emerged as a significant predictor of change management\. These findings suggest that instructional leadership, particularly through the dimensions of Hallinger’s Instructional Leadership Model, plays an important role in supporting change management, while the McKinsey 7\-S Framework highlights the broader organisational factors that shape institutional change\. Thus, the findings reinforce the importance of aligning instructional leadership with organisational elements to support effective TVET transformation in Malaysian polytechnics\.

## [EVIDÊNCIAS SOBRE OS EFEITOS DO TREINAMENTO MOTOR\-COGNITIVO DE DUPLA TAREFA NA MOBILIDADE FUNCIONAL EM IDOSOS COM DOENÇA DE ALZHEIMER: REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA](../publications/ab5da92d63f21c46c3fc.md)

Luana Lima Carvalho; Alessandra Gomes Mesquita

Introdução: A Doença de Alzheimer \(DA\) pode comprometer funções cognitivas e motoras relacionadas à marcha, ao equilíbrio e à mobilidade funcional\. O treinamento motor\-cognitivo de dupla tarefa associa simultaneamente demandas motoras e cognitivas e tem sido investigado como estratégia de intervenção nessa população\. Objetivo: analisar as evidências científicas disponíveis na literatura sobre os efeitos do treinamento motor\-cognitivo de dupla tarefa na mobilidade funcional de pessoas idosas com DA\. Metodologia: revisão integrativa da literatura, com buscas nas bases PubMed, SciELO, PEDro, LILACS e Portal de Periódicos CAPES, além de busca complementar manual\. Foram incluídos estudos primários publicados entre 2012 e 2026, em português ou inglês, que investigaram intervenções motor\-cognitivas de dupla tarefa em pessoas idosas com DA e avaliaram desfechos relacionados à mobilidade funcional\. Após o processo de identificação, triagem e elegibilidade, sete estudos primários compuseram a síntese final\. Resultados e Discussão: os estudos apresentaram potenciais efeitos favoráveis em componentes da mobilidade funcional, especialmente marcha, equilíbrio e desempenho em testes funcionais\. Entretanto, os efeitos não foram uniformes entre todos os desfechos, e foram observadas diferenças quanto aos protocolos de intervenção, características das amostras, instrumentos de avaliação e qualidade metodológica dos estudos\. Conclusão: o treinamento motor\-cognitivo de dupla tarefa apresenta potencial para melhorar componentes da mobilidade funcional em pessoas idosas com DA\. Contudo, a heterogeneidade metodológica e o número reduzido de estudos específicos exigem cautela na interpretação dos resultados\.

## [Time\-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces for integrated sensing, communication and security with generative artificial intelligence design](../publications/ab6079d83d45fad3c26e.md)

Zhihao Tao; Athina P\. Petropulu; H\. Vincent Poor

We propose a physical layer security approach for integrated sensing and communication \(ISAC\) systems, where targets may act as eavesdroppers\. A time\-modulated intelligent reflecting surface \(TM\-IRS\) preserves data integrity at legitimate communication users \(CUs\) while scrambling transmissions in other directions\. The TM\-IRS design leverages a generative flow network \(GFlowNet\) to learn a stochastic policy for sampling high\-performing configurations from a large discrete parameter space\. We formulate the achievable sum rate for legitimate CUs and beam pattern gain toward the target, constructing rewards that jointly capture communication and sensing performance\. The TM\-IRS design is modeled as a deterministic Markov decision process, where each terminal state represents a complete configuration\. GFlowNets, parameterized by deep neural networks, sample configurations with probability proportional to reward\. Experimental results demonstrate effective sensing, communication, and security integration, with significantly higher sampling efficiency than exhaustive search and improved robustness over existing benchmarks\.

## [Advanced Variance Reduction Methods for Monte Carlo Particle Transport: A Comprehensive Review](../publications/ab6d4c5eccdf33d2390c.md)

Dengjian Wu; Junjun Gong; Zifu Hao; Junxiang Mao; Yuhang Zhang; Chengqiang Liang

The Monte Carlo \(MC\) method is the reference approach for particle transport simulation in complex three\-dimensional geometries and continuous\-energy problems, where it avoids the phase\-space discretization required by deterministic methods; yet its 1/N convergence rate renders brute\-force computation infeasible for deep\-penetration shielding and full\-core fixed\-source problems\. Variance reduction \(VR\) methods address this bottleneck by modifying particle sampling or transport while preserving estimator unbiasedness, concentrating computational resources on high\-contribution phase\-space regions\. This review systematically surveys VR methods for Monte Carlo particle transport, organized into three categories: classical techniques, advanced local variance reduction \(LVR\), and advanced global variance reduction \(GVR\)\. Using Zero\-Variance Theory as the unifying framework, the review elucidates that all VR methods are fundamentally distinct approximations to the optimal importance function\. A multi\-dimensional classification system is proposed that traces the evolution from manual, heuristic parameter tuning to automated generation, from single\-technique application to multi\-solver collaborative integration, and from empirical rules to mathematically rigorous efficiency optimization\. Key future directions include the rigorization of global efficiency theory, machine\-learning\-assisted importance function construction, and multi\-solver collaborative adaptive frameworks\. The field is progressing toward a hierarchical complementarity of local and global VR, jointly advancing VR methodology from academic research to engineering practice\.

## [Psychology of passwords as a vulnerability of modern security systems](../publications/ab6f25eeb3347da4ee1d.md)

Maria\-Nikolina Baketarić

V magistrskem delu je bila proučena povezanost psiholoških dejavnikov z varnostnim vedenjem uporabnikov pri ustvarjanju, uporabi in upravljanju gesel\. Posebna pozornost je bila namenjena zaznavanju tveganja, kognitivni obremenitvi in uporabniškim navadam\. Empirični del je bil izveden kot kvantitativna presečna spletna anketna raziskava, v analizo pa je bilo vključenih 205 ustreznih zapisov\. Proučene so bile uporaba različnih gesel, izogibanje osebnim podatkom in predvidljivim vzorcem, uporaba upravljalnikov gesel ter večfaktorska avtentikacija\. Ugotovljeno je bilo, da psihološki dejavniki niso enako povezani z vsemi oblikami varnostnega vedenja\. Kot najdoslednejši dejavnik so se pokazale nevarne oziroma ustaljene uporabniške navade, povezane z redkejšo uporabo različnih gesel in slabšim izogibanjem predvidljivim vzorcem\. Večja kognitivna obremenitev je bila povezana z nekaterimi manj varnimi praksami, konkretno prepoznavanje nevarnosti ponovne uporabe gesel pa z nekaterimi varnejšimi oblikami vedenja\. Splošna zaznava verjetnosti zlorabe ali resnosti njenih posledic sama po sebi ni zadostovala za pojasnjevanje proučevanega vedenja\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da varnosti gesel ni mogoče obravnavati zgolj kot tehničnega vprašanja\. Pri oblikovanju varnostnih ukrepov je zato smiselno zmanjševati kognitivno in praktično obremenitev, spodbujati uporabo izvedljivih varnostnih rešitev ter podpirati spreminjanje ustaljenih vedenjskih vzorcev uporabnikov\. Tak pristop lahko prispeva k doslednejšemu in dolgoročno varnejšemu ravnanju uporabnikov\.

## [Electrochemical Detection of PFAS Contaminants Across Environmental and Pharmaceutical Matrices:Sensing Mechanisms, Nanomaterial Platforms, Biological Monitoring, and Regulatory Convergence](../publications/ab6f2c0dab81eb1cb09e.md)



PFAS are a class of over 14,000 synthetic compounds characterized by a stable carbon\-fluorine bond that confers resistance to thermal and biological degradation, resulting in common contamination of various aquatic matrices at concentrations ranging from sub\-parts per trillion to parts per billion\.Demand for directly deployable sensitive quantification methods has been spurred by increasingly stringent regulatory responses such as the U\.S\. Environmental Protection Agency \(EPA\) proposed maximum contaminant levels of 4 ppt for PFOA and PFOS in 2024 under its third Fourth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule and sub\-parametric values recommended by the EU Drinking Water Directive\.Conventional liquid chromatography\-tandem mass spectrometry provides the required sensitivity but is still limited by centralized infrastructure and slow sample preparation that prevents point\-of\-care or real\-time surveillance\.Another critically understudied dimension includes pharmaceutical matrices, where PFAS can act as formulation excipients or derive from the synthesis of fluorinated active pharmaceutical ingredients and pharmacokinetically interfere with albumin binding and hepatic CYP450 activity in exposed populations\.The current review summarized the existing electrochemical sensing strategies, including molecularly imprinted polymers, aptasensors, and CRISPR\-Cas12a biosensors, and state\-of\-the\-art electrode structures, including metal\-organic frameworks, MXenes, and covalent triazine frameworks, for targeting PFAS in environmental and biological matrices\.While some of these can be implemented analytically with detection below 1 ppt, critical benchmarking using regulatory thresholds reveals that 10% of sensor studies validate their performance in non\-spiked field or clinical matrices\.This highlights the need for multi\-analyte array development to allow standardized sensor validation frameworks across environmental and pharmaceutical quality monitoring\.

Recommendation systems can reduce information overload, improve product relevance and support customer decision\-making\. Their effectiveness, however, depends on factors such as recommendation frequency, perceived helpfulness and perceived accuracy\. This study examines consumer purchase behaviour using the publicly available Amazon Consumer Behaviour Dataset hosted on Kaggle\. The dataset contains 602 observations and 23 variables covering demographics, purchase frequency, browsing behaviour, personalized recommendations, recommendation helpfulness, rating accuracy, reviews, Save\-for\-Later activity and shopping satisfaction\. The study follows a quantitative, explanatory secondary\-data design\. Reported statistical analyses of the same dataset show significant positive associations between purchase frequency and browsing frequency, Save\-for\-Later frequency and review helpfulness\. Recommendation\-specific analysis reports a positive association between personalized recommendation frequency and rating accuracy\. Because the dataset contains Purchase\_Frequency rather than a direct Purchase\_Intention measure, the findings are interpreted as evidence of consumer purchase behaviour\. ## [Efektivitas Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif terhadap Hasil Belajar Peserta Didik: Meta\-Analisis Studi Eksperimen dan Kuasi\-Eksperimen](../publications/ab8406c81e9bee93fbbb.md)

Roy Marthin Sihombing; Yeremia Christoper Sihotang; Anggina Pertiwi Nasution; Balqis Hijriaulia; Siska Anzani; Yosua Nathanael Nainggolan; Daldi Altamerando Suramana Sembiring; Elsa Sabrina

Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis secara kuantitatif pengaruh penggunaan kecerdasan buatan generatif \(GenAI\) terhadap hasil belajar peserta didik serta mengidentifikasi karakteristik intervensi yang berkaitan dengan variasi pengaruh tersebut\. Metode yang digunakan adalah meta\-analisis atas studi eksperimen dan kuasi\-eksperimen yang terbit pada 2021–2026 dengan pelaporan mengikuti PRISMA 2020\. Pencarian dilakukan pada Scopus, ResearchGate, dan Google Scholar, dan sebanyak 20 studi dengan total 3\.005 peserta didik disertakan dalam sintesis\. Ukuran efek gabungan diestimasi dengan model efek acak, disertai analisis subkelompok dan analisis sensitivitas\. Hasil menunjukkan pengaruh positif pada kisaran sedang menuju besar \(Hedges’ g = 0,707; interval kepercayaan 95%: 0,339–1,074\) dengan heterogenitas tinggi \(I² = 93,1%\)\. Pengaruh cenderung lebih besar pada penggunaan GenAI yang terstruktur dengan panduan pedagogis \(g = 0,839\) daripada penggunaan tanpa panduan \(g = 0,034\), serta pada perbandingan dengan pembelajaran tanpa GenAI \(g = 0,861\) daripada dengan umpan balik manusia \(g = 0,200\)\. Disimpulkan bahwa efektivitas GenAI berkaitan dengan rancangan pedagogis dan konteks penerapannya, sehingga integrasinya perlu dirancang secara terarah\.

## [Testing the Planning Claims of LLM\-Based Agents against Formal Semantics](../publications/ab8ca387f14d55af4853.md)

Oriol Miro\-Lopez\-Feliu; Oscar Miró López\-Feliu; Victor Gimenez\-Abalos; Javier Vazquez\-Salceda; Victor Carballo Araruna; Sergio Alvarez\-Napagao

LLM\-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions\. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain\-of\-thought, search\-based prompting, self\-refinement, reflection, critics and tool\-using loops\. Yet these claims are usually supported by end\-to\-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers\. We test LLM planning against formal semantics\. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all\. Across five domains \(two of them new, all released with the paper\), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state\. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain\. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures\. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces\.

## [Development of pH\-Responsive Polymeric Nanoparticles for Targeted Doxorubicin Delivery in Breast Cancer: Advances, Design Strategies, and Future Perspectives](../publications/ab96bb8f8023c7cbe08d.md)

Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer\-related mortality among women worldwide\. Although doxorubicin is widely used in chemotherapy, its clinical application is limited by cardiotoxicity, systemic toxicity, and non\-specific drug distribution\. pH\-responsive polymeric nanoparticles offer a promising approach for targeted drug delivery by releasing doxorubicin in the acidic tumor microenvironment while maintaining stability under physiological conditions\. Biodegradable polymers, including PLGA, PEG, chitosan, and poly\(β\-amino esters\), have been investigated for developing these nanocarriers\. Preclinical studies indicate improved intracellular drug delivery, enhanced antitumor activity, and potential reductions in systemic toxicity\. This review highlights recent advances in the design, development, and therapeutic applications of pH\-responsive polymeric nanoparticles for doxorubicin delivery in breast cancer, along with challenges in safety, clinical translation, and regulatory approval\.
