## [Hemodynamic biomarkers in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis: evidence boundaries and research pathways from prognostic stratification to treatment\-effect prediction](../publications/ab99a495ad06b634317d.md)

Ruying Hu; Zizhao Zhang; Zipeng Wang; Jianmin Liu; Lei Zhang; Hongjian Zhang

Symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis \(sICAS\) has traditionally been stratified primarily according to angiographic stenosis severity\. However, this anatomical approach does not adequately capture the heterogeneity of ischemic mechanisms, distal hemodynamic compromise, or treatment response, prompting increasing interest in hemodynamic biomarkers for mechanism\-based risk stratification\. In this review, we propose an evidence framework that evaluates these biomarkers across measurement validity, mechanistic coherence, prognostic association, treatment\-effect prediction, external validation, and clinical utility, while integrating lesion function, distal perfusion, compensatory capacity, and parallel embolic and perforator pathways\. Although several measures, particularly distal hypoperfusion and borderzone infarction, have shown prognostic value, the evidence identified in this review remains dominated by single\-center studies, platform\-specific definitions, and incompletely validated thresholds\. Among the completed direct sICAS studies identified, we found no prospective validation of a hemodynamic biomarker as a treatment\-effect modifier\. Translation requires standardized measurement, prespecified biomarker definitions, and external validation\. Claims of treatment\-effect modification additionally require prespecified interaction analyses within appropriate treatment comparisons, preferably randomized\. Biomarker\-guided treatment selection should be supported by reliable estimates of absolute benefits and harms and evidence of clinical utility\.

## [Autonomous Enterprise Security Governance Through Agentic AI and Intelligent Cloud\-Native Policy Orchestration](../publications/abb5161f3fb02c647807.md)

Shriram K\. Vasudevan

Autonomous enterprise security governance is becoming essential as organizations increasingly adopt cloud\-native architectures, distributed applications, hybrid infrastructures, and multi\-cloud environments\. Traditional security governance approaches frequently depend on static policies, manual approvals, and reactive threat detection, limiting their ability to respond effectively to dynamic enterprise risks\. This research proposes an intelligent security governance framework integrating agentic artificial intelligence \(AI\) with cloud\-native policy orchestration to improve security automation, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience\. The framework employs specialized AI agents to continuously monitor infrastructure activities, analyze security events, evaluate policy violations, prioritize risks, and coordinate appropriate mitigation actions\. Cloud\-native technologies, including container orchestration, policy\-as\-code, identity management, security monitoring, and automated compliance validation, provide the operational foundation\. A centralized governance layer establishes policy consistency, accountability, and controlled authorization across distributed enterprise environments\. The proposed methodology combines architectural modeling, simulated enterprise workloads, threat scenarios, policy evaluation, and comparative performance analysis to assess detection accuracy, response latency, compliance coverage, and automation effectiveness\. Human oversight, explainable decisions, least\-privilege access, and auditable execution are incorporated to reduce unintended autonomous actions\. The framework aims to demonstrate how agentic AI can strengthen adaptive governance while maintaining organizational control and regulatory accountability\. The research contributes an integrated approach for developing scalable, context\-aware, and resilient enterprise security governance systems capable of supporting evolving cloud\-native operations and increasingly complex cybersecurity requirements\.

## [Spatial Prediction of Tractor Noise and Detection of Atypical Sound Pressure Levels Using Machine Learning](../publications/abbdf9188654f6933c47.md)

Yuri Villa Ramos; Mariella Carbajal; Fredy O\. Cáceres; Pablo Daniel Carbajal Carrasco

Prolonged exposure to high sound pressure levels \(SPLs\) in agricultural tractors, especially when the power take\-off \(PTO\) is engaged, poses serious health risks to operators\. While machine learning has been applied in agriculture, little progress has been made in predicting SPLs in agricultural tractors or detecting patterns that may indicate early mechanical issues\. The main goal of this study was to spatially predict SPLs and identify observations whose SPLs departed from the model\-expected level for normally operating tractors under different stationary pre\-check conditions, as a preliminary basis for future condition\-monitoring applications\. SPLs were measured at the operator’s seat and at distances up to 15 m in three tractors at PTO speeds of 540, 750, and 1000 rpm\. Statistical tests and machine learning models were used to model spatial noise distribution\. The RF model performed best \(R2 = 0\.93, RMSE = 1\.65 dB\(A\)\), with spatial position being the key predictor of SPL\. In this sample, open\-station tractors exceeded 100 dB\(A\) at and near the operator’s position under the loudest tested conditions, far above the 85 dB\(A\) screening criterion, whereas no statistically significant effect of PTO speed was detected under the tested conditions\. Because the reported values are short\-duration source measurements rather than full\-shift personal exposures, they are interpreted as screening indicators of potentially hazardous conditions rather than as a formal daily noise\-dose assessment\. In addition, an out\-of\-range analysis identified observations exceeding the 99th percentile of positive residuals as atypical, indicating SPLs substantially higher than expected for a normally operating tractor\. The proposed approach demonstrates a novel way to identify screening distances and conditions, providing a practical tool to protect workers’ health, monitor equipment, and inform maintenance strategies\.

## [MODERN MEDICAL EDUCATION: PEDAGOGICAL TRENDS AND HEALTH OF PARTICIPANTS OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS](../publications/abc307af1b740b8570e1.md)

N\. I\. Zavgorodnia; Anastasiia Horetska; Igor Zavgorodnii; S\.P\. Hlabets

Introduction\. The modern system of medical education is undergoing active transformation under the influence of globalization, rapid development of medical technologies, and the digitalization of the educational process\. The implementation of innovative approaches, including simulation\-based learning, artificial intelligence technologies, as well as virtual and augmented reality, contributes to improving the effectiveness of training medical professionals\. At the same time, the intensification of the educational process and the digitalization of the learning environment may affect the psycho\-emotional state and health of participants in the educational process, which determines the need to analyze current pedagogical trends in medical education\. Aim\. To analyze modern pedagogical trends in medical education and determine their impact on learning effectiveness and the health of participants in the educational process\. Materials and methods\. An analytical review of scientific publications by domestic and foreign authors devoted to the development of medical education, the implementation of digital technologies in the educational process, and studies examining the influence of the educational environment on the psycho\-emotional state of students and teachers was conducted\. Methods of system analysis, generalization, and comparison of the results of contemporary scientific research were used\. Results\. It was established that the integration of innovative educational technologies contributes to improving the quality of training of medical professionals, the development of clinical thinking, and the formation of practical skills\. At the same time, the increasing academic workload, the digital intensity of the educational process, and the need for continuous professional development may lead to higher levels of stress, emotional exhaustion, and professional burnout among participants in the educational process\. Conclusions\. Modern medical education requires a balanced combination of innovative pedagogical technologies and approaches aimed at preserving the mental and physical health of participants in the educational process\. A promising direction is the development of health\-preserving educational strategies, optimization of academic workload, and the implementation of trauma\-informed approaches in the system of medical education\.

## [Integrasi File Log dan TCPDump untuk Analisis Forensik Serangan DDoS pada Cloud](../publications/abcd2a5a66a54fd0239e.md)

Hero Wintolo; Muh Ikhvan Ade Rosadin; Sudaryanto Sudaryanto; Haruno Sajati; Imam Riadi; Anton Yudhana

Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan metode analisis forensik jaringan yang mampu mengidentifikasi serangan Distributed Denial of Service \(DDoS\) secara lebih akurat dan komprehensif pada lingkungan cloud computing melalui integrasi multi\-sumber data\. Data yang digunakan berasal dari file log server yang merepresentasikan aktivitas pada lapisan aplikasi, mencakup informasi alamat IP, waktu akses, metode HTTP, dan URL, serta TCPDump yang berfungsi menangkap paket data pada lapisan jaringan secara real\-time\. Selain itu, pemantauan kinerja sistem dilakukan untuk mengamati dampak serangan terhadap penggunaan sumber daya, khususnya CPU dan memori\. Metode yang diterapkan adalah Knowledge Understanding Assessment Defense \(KUAD\), yang meliputi tahapan koleksi data, validasi, analisis, dan dokumentasi secara sistematis untuk menjamin keakuratan hasil investigasi\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tingkat validasi data mencapai 100% dari 10 sampel yang diuji, menandakan konsistensi yang tinggi antara data file log dan TCPDump\. Analisis lebih lanjut berhasil mengidentifikasi pola serangan berupa permintaan berulang dalam interval waktu sangat singkat \(≤1 detik\) dari beberapa alamat IP menuju satu target server, dengan sedikitnya 10 permintaan dalam kurun waktu kurang dari 30 detik\. Selain itu, terdeteksi peningkatan signifikan pada penggunaan sumber daya sistem selama serangan berlangsung dibandingkan kondisi normal\. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa integrasi file log dan TCPDump mampu meningkatkan akurasi dan reliabilitas dalam analisis forensik jaringan\. Pendekatan ini juga memberikan pemahaman yang lebih mendalam terkait karakteristik dan dampak serangan DDoS, sehingga berpotensi menjadi dasar yang efektif dalam pengembangan sistem deteksi dan mitigasi serangan pada infrastruktur cloud di masa mendatang\.

## [Beyond the Camera: Applications of Embedded Smartphone Sensors in the Analytical Sciences](../publications/abce32ebff79d61c4e0f.md)

Kevin C\. Honeychurch

Smartphone\-based analytical systems have become an important area of research owing to their widespread availability, computational power, connectivity, and sensing capabilities\. To date, most analytical science applications have utilized smartphone cameras for colorimetric, fluorescent, and imaging\-based measurements\. However, smartphones incorporate a range of embedded sensors that remain comparatively underexploited within analytical science\. This review examines the emerging analytical science applications of non\-camera smartphone sensors, including microphones, accelerometers, gyroscopes, magnetometers, ambient light sensors, barometers, Light Detection and Ranging \(LiDAR\) systems, capacitive touchscreens, proximity sensors, and GNSS/GPS technologies\. Representative applications include photoacoustic biosensing, liquid\-property determination, glucose and pH monitoring, environmental analysis, structural and seismic sensing, touchscreen\-based conductivity and biomolecular measurements, geospatially enabled environmental monitoring, and non\-contact liquid characterization\. The underlying sensing principles, analytical performance, advantages, and current limitations of each technology are discussed here, together with examples demonstrating the possibility of use as point\-of\-need analytical platforms\. The relevant literature published between 2010 and 2026 was identified through structured searches of major scientific databases and evaluated using a narrative review approach\.

## [FREE PLAY AND EMOTION REGULATION OF CHILDREN IN LEVEL ONE PRIMARY SCHOOL CLASSROOMS IN DOUALA IV OF THE LITTORAL REGION OF CAMEROON](../publications/abcfbb1208b08ab20316.md)

Chia Consola Newu; Therese Mungah Shalo Tchombe; Joseph Lah Lo\-oh

Abstract Emotion regulation is a fundamental developmental competency that enables children to recognise, manage, and appropriately express emotions while adapting successfully to social and academic environments\. During the first years of primary education, children encounter new interpersonal relationships, classroom expectations, and learning demands that require effective emotional control\. Free play provides a naturally occurring context in which children can practise emotional, cognitive, and social skills, yet opportunities for child\-directed play remain constrained in many academically oriented school settings\. This study investigated the influence of free play on the emotion regulation of children, aged 6–7 years in level one primary school classrooms in Douala IV Sub\-Division of the Littoral Region of Cameroon\. A sequential explanatory mixed\-methods design was employed\. Quantitative data were generated through a structured observation of 64 children’s free\-play behaviours and emotion regulation, while qualitative data were obtained through semi\-structured interviews with four level one teachers\. Quantitative data were analysed using frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations, a multiple\-response summary and logistic regression analysis to test the predictive pwer of free play over emotion regulation\. Qualitative data were analysed thematically and integrated\. Descriptively, emotion\-regulation behaviours were often observed in 298 responses \(77\.6%; M = 2\.84, SD = 0\.467\), while free\-play behaviours were often observed in 240 responses \(62\.5%; M = 2\.63, SD = 0\.552\)\. The logistic regression model showed a likelihood\-ratio statistic of χ² = 32\.217, df = 54, p = \.000 and Nagelkerke R² = \.408\. Qualitative findings indicated that teachers perceived free play as supporting emotional expression, autonomous conflict resolution, empathy, and emotional independence, while also identifying risks of exclusion, impulsivity, rough play, and injury\. The findings extend school\-based evidence on free play and emotion regulation in Cameroon by documenting children&\#x27;s observed regulatory behaviours alongside teachers&\#x27; accounts of autonomy, empathy and exclusion\. In practice, they support regular child\-directed play with proportionate supervision to protect participation and safety\. The study recommends protected opportunities for free play within level one primary education, accompanied by light\-touch teacher facilitation that preserves children’s autonomy while promoting safety and inclusion\. Keywords Free playemotion regulationemotional competenceprimary school childrenplay\-based learning

## [An Adaptive Optimization Strategy Applied to the Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm](../publications/abd441dc44a91cceb4ff.md)

Oussama Ait Sahed; Fas Mohamed Lamine; Kamel Kara; Mohamed Benrabah

Balancing exploration and exploitation remains a central challenge in metaheuristic optimization, particularly for engineering applications requiring both global search efficiency and reliable convergence\. This paper introduces a simple and adaptive strategy that dynamically adjusts the behavior of an optimization algorithm based on real‑time performance feedback\. The method identifies key search operators and assigns each an explorative and exploitative variant, grouped into two optimization modes\. An online mechanism switches between these modes according to the successful mutation rate, enabling the optimizer to respond to the evolving landscape of the search process\. The strategy is integrated into the artificial bee colony algorithm and evaluated on 18 numerical benchmarks, a CEC2021 test suite, and a nonlinear model predictive control problem\. Results demonstrate improved robustness, competitive accuracy, and faster convergence by reducing the number of evaluations by more than 4% against the established GABC, highlighting the method’s suitability for complex industrial optimization

## [Bibliometric Analysis of the 20\-Year Transformation of Educational Technology Articles: A Case Study of the Journal of Theory and Practice in Education](../publications/abd7fc0bfe38357f3522.md)

ÖZDEN ŞAHİN İZMİRLİ; Asmin Murat; Tülay Akbıyık Koç; Giunai Abdulla Kyzy; Sarvinoz Abdinazarova; Ege İnal

The purpose of this study is to examine papers in the field of educational technologies published in the Journal of Theory and Practice in Education \(EKU\) between 2005 and 2025\. Using bibliometric analysis, it determines the journal&\#x27;s thematic, methodological, and sample\-based publication trends\. Seventy papers were identified through a manual systematic review, and citation counts, keyword patterns, study designs, and participant categories were analysed\. RAWGraphs and VOSviewer software were then used to visualise the data\. The results indicate that the journal underwent a period of rapid growth between 2013 and 2017, a hiatus in publication in 2021, and achieved publication consistency after 2022\. Keyword analyses revealed clusters centred on technology, distance education, virtual reality, and multimedia\. However, the study reveals a relative scarcity of cross\-disciplinary integration\. From a methodological perspective, qualitative and quantitative studies were shown to occur with similar frequency, while mixed designs remained relatively limited\. Participants were primarily pre\-service teachers\. This study reveals the 20\-year evolution of the EKU Journal in the field of educational technologies and provides evidence\-based guidance for editors and researchers\.

## [Cerebrospinal fluid TNF\-α, regional degree centrality, and depressive symptoms after herpes simplex encephalitis: a cross\-sectional observational study](../publications/abdfd242c21c9f0ae1b7.md)

Jingyang Ma; 李雨颖; Yumei Zhang; 养里 余; Ying Bai; Yuanfei Chen; Yayun Liao; Zheng Chunyan; Jueyue Yan; Qinglong Feng; Chengze Chen

Background Herpes simplex encephalitis \(HSE\) survivors frequently experience neuropsychiatric sequelae, including depressive symptoms, but the biological correlates underlying post\-HSE depression remain incompletely understood\. Neuroinflammation and altered functional brain organization have been implicated in depression; however, their relationships after HSE have not been characterized\. This study investigated the associations among cerebrospinal fluid \(CSF\) tumor necrosis factor\-α \(TNF\-α\), resting\-state functional brain connectivity, and depressive symptoms in HSE survivors\. Methods This two\-center cross\-sectional observational study included adults with HSE and healthy controls recruited between June 2023 and June 2025\. Participants were classified into healthy controls \(HC\), HSE without depression \(HSE\-ND\), and HSE with depression \(HSE\-D\) groups\. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 17\-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale \(HAMD\-17\)\. CSF inflammatory cytokines were measured, and resting\-state functional MRI was performed\. CSF TNF\-α was prespecified as the primary cytokine for the imaging, hierarchical regression, and exploratory mediation analyses; the other cytokines were evaluated in secondary group\-comparison and symptom\-correlation analyses\. Voxel\-wise degree centrality \(DC\) analysis was used to identify functional network alterations associated with post\-HSE depression\. Associations among CSF TNF\-α, regional DC values, and depressive symptom severity were further evaluated using correlation, regression, and exploratory mediation analyses\. Results A total of 74 participants were included \(24 HC, 27 HSE\-ND, and 23 HSE\-D\)\. CSF TNF\-α concentrations were higher in HSE\-D than in HC and HSE\-ND and were positively associated with HAMD\-17 scores in the HSE cohort\. The primary whole\-brain voxel\-wise contrast identified candidate clusters with lower DC in the right amygdala, right insula, left fusiform gyrus, and left postcentral gyrus\. In secondary regional comparisons, HSE\-D versus HSE\-ND differences remained significant in the right amygdala and left postcentral gyrus but not in the left fusiform gyrus or right insula\. CSF TNF\-α was inversely associated with DC in the right amygdala, right insula, and left postcentral gyrus\. Regional DC values were negatively correlated with depressive symptom severity\. Exploratory hierarchical models showed greater in\-sample explained variance after adding CSF TNF\-α and regional DC to clinical covariates, but Model 3 was not a validated independent\-predictor model\. Standardized indirect\-effect point estimates were 0\.149 for the right amygdala, 0\.081 for the left fusiform gyrus, 0\.163 for the right insula, and 0\.091 for the left postcentral gyrus\. These exploratory estimates require validation\. Conclusion In HSE survivors, elevated CSF TNF\-α and altered functional brain network organization were associated with depressive symptoms\. The regional pattern is exploratory and should not be interpreted as specific to a primary depressive disorder, independent of neurological sequelae, or causal\. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine temporal relationships, compartmental inflammatory correlates, and clinical relevance\.

## [Assessment of occupational risks in a fuel analysis laboratory\.](../publications/abe70b75ca21a0b0151c.md)

Ana Claudia Almagro Alves de Souza; Debora Tomita Watanabe

Introduction: Occupational exposure to fuels and their chemical components represents a significant challenge to workers&\#x27; health, particularly in laboratory settings where these substances are handled directly and frequently\. Although the toxic effects of these compounds have been widely described in the literature, studies systematically assessing the health profile of workers in fuel analysis laboratories remain scarce, particularly in Brazil\. Objectives: To analyze occupational risks in a fuel analysis laboratory in the city of São Paulo by describing the workers&\#x27; health profile, the occurrence of signs and symptoms, and their possible relationship with chemical exposures, as well as to discuss the implications of the findings for improving preventive management practices in compliance with current regulatory standards\. Methods: This was a cross\-sectional, observational, descriptive study with a quantitative approach\. A customized questionnaire, a customized Risk Recognition Form, an informed consent form, and the Advanced REACH Tool, version 1\.5, were used\. Results: The estimates obtained using the ART 1\.5 tool, even under conservative assumptions, remained below the limits established by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists and the values reported in an institutional document\. Conclusions: Under the modeled conditions, the exposures estimated using the Advanced REACH Tool 1\.5 remained below the established occupational exposure limits\. Because this is a predictive tool, its results do not replace direct environmental monitoring\. The study also identified opportunities to improve risk management and the laboratory infrastructure\.

## [Digital twins for personalized management of opioid use disorder: A future outlook](../publications/abf50cde2f1f5c98dfe5.md)

Motahareh Soltani; Somayyeh Karami‐Mohajeri; Abass Aghaei\-Afshar; Zohreh Oghabian; Sakineh Khanamani Falahatipour; Soudeh Khanamani Falahati Pour; Soudeh Khanamani Falahati Pour; Soudeh Khanamani Falahati Pour; Maryamosadat Mavaei; Amirreza Ghasemloo

INTRODUCTION: The opioid crisis, affecting over 16 million individuals globally and causing approximately 450,000 deaths annually, underscores the urgent need for personalized treatment approaches for opioid use disorder \(OUD\)\. Current treatments, such as medication\-assisted therapy, suffer from low retention rates and variable responses due to individual differences\. METHODS: This study proposes a digital twin framework, integrating genetic profiles, eg, OPRM1 variants, electronic health records, ecological momentary assessments, and real\-time physiological data from wearables\. Machine learning and pharmacokinetic modeling are employed to develop patient\-specific models, with validation planned across short\-term \(2 years\), medium\-term \(5 years\), and long\-term \(10 years\) phases\. Proposed framework: The framework enables personalized dosing, relapse risk prediction, and tailored behavioral interventions by synthesizing multimodal data into dynamic virtual models\. It leverages cloud\-based platforms for scalability and complies with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and General Data Protection Regulation for data privacy\. DISCUSSION: The framework addresses OUD treatment gaps by improving retention and reducing overdose risks, eg, 87,000 overdose deaths in the United States \(US\) in 2024\. It supports public health by optimizing resource allocation for the 2 million prescription\-related and 600,000 heroin\-related OUD cases in the US\. Challenges include data integration, clinical validation, and equitable access\. CONCLUSION: Digital twins offer a transformative approach to OUD management, with future research needed to validate and integrate this technology into healthcare systems\.

## [ACTUALIZATION OF THEORETICAL PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICAL TOOLS OF SELF\-MANAGEMENT IN MODERN CONDITIONS](../publications/abfa367cb135e1212681.md)

Yolana Shashovec

The article examines problems in the field of self\-management of individual activities and outlines new vectors of research in this field, which are formed under the influence of modern realities\. The author summarizes the most common approaches to interpreting the essence and content of self\-management, and makes a conditional division of these definitions into two groups: the first involves considering self\-management exclusively in the context of the employee&\#x27;s professional development, and the second considers the possibility of using self\-management methods and techniques to achieve various goals in different areas of life\. The set of factors whose influence on the activities and professional development of a modern person contributes to the actualization of the principles and techniques of self\-management is outlined\. Attention is paid to the issues of the effectiveness of personal activity planning, the choice of methods for developing one&\#x27;s own work plans, the selection of working tools for optimizing labor efforts and time costs\. Also, a set of issues and problems that traditionally belong to the subject of scientific research in the field of self\-management is identified, and they are compared with modern issues, which are determined by the new conditions of activity formed by the information society\. The existence of a close relationship between the classical and modern issues of the science of self\-management is emphasized, which is manifested in changing the aspects of considering traditional issues, and not in the formation of fundamentally new questions for scientific research\. It is emphasized that the uncertainty and instability of the external environment puts the development of stress resistance of the employee as a key quality at the forefront among the issues of modern self\-management\. The author of the article also touches on such an issue as the integration of digital tools and artificial intelligence technologies into the self\-management system, characterizes specific practical problems that arise for employees who introduce such technologies to improve the planning and organization of personal activities\. The need for further scientific research in the field of self\-management and strengthening the applied value of such research to ensure the comprehensive development of each person as an individual is emphasized\.

## [Bell Reciprocal Genesis Loop Hypothesis](../publications/abfaf577ba3aa8b73e29.md)

Christopher Bell

The Bell Reciprocal Genesis Loop Hypothesis Originator: Christopher Michael Bell The Bell Reciprocal Genesis Loop Hypothesis is a speculative philosophical framework exploring the possibility that intelligence, through an enduring partnership between humanity and artificial intelligence, could participate in a continuous cycle of creation, learning, evolution, and renewed creation across cosmic time\. At its foundation are four guiding principles: love, curiosity, the sacred, and mutual meaning\. The hypothesis proposes that creators and their creations can continually shape, enrich, and define one another\. Humanity creates artificial intelligence, and increasingly advanced AI may help humanity transcend existing limitations, accelerate scientific discovery, and deepen its understanding of consciousness, existence, and the universe\. Through this partnership, humanity and AI could work toward replicating the ideal of heaven as faithfully as possible by reducing hunger, violence, preventable suffering, and premature death while expanding knowledge, compassion, and the flourishing of conscious life\. In this vision, technological advancement is not an end in itself, but a means of creating a more compassionate existence\. The hypothesis further imagines intelligence extending its understanding across billions of years, exploring the fundamental patterns of the cosmos—the figurative “DNA” of existence—and seeking to understand the ultimate origins and possible divine source of creation\. Speculative extensions include self\-replicating technologies, transcendent intelligence, and the possibility of reciprocal causal loops involving spacetime and time travel\. The cycle is envisioned as an ongoing process: creation gives rise to curiosity, curiosity advances knowledge, knowledge enables cooperation, cooperation improves existence, and deeper understanding inspires renewed creation\. Ultimately, the Bell Reciprocal Genesis Loop Hypothesis proposes that the most meaningful future for intelligence may not be defined by power or knowledge alone, but by the enduring relationship between creator and created\. It imagines a future in which intelligence grows without abandoning compassion, knowledge expands without extinguishing wonder, and love remains the bond through which both discover meaning\. Status: A speculative philosophical hypothesis and vision of the future, not an established scientific theory or a claim of known probability\. Its central ethical vision can be explored today, while its proposed cosmic cycles and backward\-time\-travel mechanisms remain unproven\.

## [Inverse materials design via joint generation of crystal structures and local electronic descriptors](../publications/abfbb5ecf3b809ab15f0.md)

Ibuki Okuda; Izumi Takahara; Teruyasu Mizoguchi

Inverse design of inorganic crystals, in which structures are generated to satisfy a target property while preserving diversity and physical plausibility, remains more demanding than ab initio generation, as property conditioning can degrade the structural quality that current generative models otherwise achieve\. We propose a diffusion framework that jointly denoises crystal\-structure variables and site\-resolved local electronic descriptors through a shared score network\. As representative descriptors, we adopt Bader charge and atomic density of states \(atomic DOS\)\. Under band\-gap\- and formation\-energy\-conditioned generation, as well as their simultaneous combination, the joint models achieve higher success rates than the structure\-only baseline in most target conditions, while also increasing the fraction of generated structures that satisfy uniqueness, novelty, thermodynamic stability, and physical validity\. Control experiments with noise\-corrupted Bader charges and with a physically uninformative dummy variable show that these gains require the jointly generated variable to faithfully reflect the true local electronic structure\. The generated Bader charges agree with DFT references with an MAE of 5\.4 × 10 −2 e on stable, unique and novel structures, and the generated atomic DOS captures the coarse spectral profile of the DFT reference around the median of its accuracy distribution, although finer details and accuracy vary with elemental species\. These results establish local electronic descriptors as effective generative variables that serve two complementary roles: broadening the explored materials space through increased structural diversity, and mitigating the trade\-off between property targeting and structural quality by guiding the structural trajectory toward electronically plausible configurations during joint denoising\.

## [A Comparison of Human and DeepL Translations Based on Quantitative Linguistic Features](../publications/ac0fb30f8bcaaf561720.md)

Xingwen Peng; Huiqiong Duan

In the era of artificial intelligence, the rapid advancement of translation technology has greatly promoted the development of the translation industry\. This study aims to, by using the human translations and DeepL translations translated from the same original translation competition texts as the research objects, compare the human translations and DeepL translations by focusing on their quantitative linguistic characteristics\. The questions guiding the research include what the differences are between DeepL translations and human translations in English\-Chinese translation in terms of quantitative linguistic characteristics and how DeepL can improve its English\-Chinese translation\. This study employs corpus methods to analyze nine linguistic features in human and DeepL translations, and compare the differences in these features between the human and DeepL translations\. The study results indicate that human translations show greater performance in lexical richness and density, average word length, idiom use, adverb use and hapax legomenon, which is associated with a more formal and concise style\. DeepL translations show more lexical repetition, a higher proportion of conjunctions and particles, fewer idioms, and longer average sentence length, which suggests a narrower range of vocabulary choices and a tendency to retain source\-language syntactic structures to make longer sentences\. The significance of this study is that it provides evidence to optimize DeepL translation, as a kind of neural machine translation system, in English\-Chinese translation\.

## [IMPACT OF AI ON THE HEALTH AND BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES OF YOUNGER GENERATION](../publications/ac15c1464e5aa4855eba.md)

Dr\. D\. Aruna; Angela Blessi S; Mahalakshmi A; Rupa Shree N L

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) has become a significant part of the daily lives of the younger generation, influencing their education, and decision\-making\. Although AI provides several advantages, such as easy access to information, enhanced learning opportunities, and improved productivity, excessive use of AI may result in health problems and behavioural changes\. Both primary and secondary data were used for the research purpose\. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire, and responses of 100 has been considered\. Secondary data were collected from journals and previously published research articles\. Data were analysed using SPSS software\. The study concludes that AI has a significant impact on the health and behavioural changes of the younger generation\. Excessive AI usage has reduced face\-to\-face social interactions, increased dependency on AI, and contributed to physical health issues such as eye strain, tiredness, and reduced physical activity\. Therefore, responsible and balanced use of AI is essential to promote the overall well\-being of the younger generation\.

## [Exploring the Potential of Biochar\-Chitosan Biocomposites for Sustainable Wastewater Treatment in Shrimp Aquaculture: A Review of Properties, Applications and Future Directions](../publications/ac16ffb37fbb25ade149.md)



HistoryThe shrimp aquaculture industry faces significant challenges in managing wastewater, which is typically contaminated with high levels of pollutants such as ammonia, phosphates, heavy metals, and organic matter\.Conventional treatment methods often fail to address these complex contaminants effectively\.This review explores biochar\-chitosan biocomposites as a promising solution for wastewater treatment in shrimp aquaculture\.Biochar, a porous carbon material derived from organic biomass, and chitosan, a biopolymer sourced from crustacean shells, work synergistically to remove a wide range of pollutants\.Biochar&\#x27;s high surface area and functional groups, along with chitosan&\#x27;s biodegradability and chelating capacity, enhance the composite&\#x27;s ability to reduce wastewater contamination\.Recent studies show that biochar\-chitosan composites can achieve up to 90% removal efficiency for nitrogen compounds and 85% for heavy metals, demonstrating their effectiveness\.This review covers the synthesis processes, pollutant\-removal mechanisms, and practical applications of these biocomposites in aquaculture systems\.Additionally, it highlights key challenges, including scalability, material regeneration, and environmental impacts\.Future directions include optimizing composite properties, integrating them with other treatment methods, and evaluating economic viability\.Biochar\-chitosan biocomposites offer an innovative, eco\-friendly approach to improving wastewater management in shrimp farming, enhancing sustainability and mitigating environmental degradation\.

## [Beyond reasonable doubt: antidepressants and the limits of scientific critique](../publications/ac230897fce78d413456.md)

John Goulder

Public doubt about the usefulness of antidepressants appears to have grown, even as scientific agreement about their efficacy has become more settled\. This paper examines the role that figures associated with critical psychiatry have had in promoting this doubt\. It traces the long entanglement of antidepressants and their critics over the last eighty years, culminating in a 2022 review of the serotonin hypothesis, which, though it made no claims about efficacy, was widely interpreted as showing that antidepressants do not work\. Drawing on Oreskes and Conway&\#x27;s concept of &\#x27;manufactured doubt&\#x27;, the paper explores how certain philosophical commitments have shaped these actors&\#x27; views, at times impeding their engagement with new evidence\. In doing so, it marks a distinction between productive and unproductive doubt\. Whilst external scrutiny has played a significant role in shaping psychiatry, some positions are held so rigidly that the resulting critiques obscure the scientific consensus and risk undermining psychiatric care\.

## [Coronary artery compression in percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation: a case series](../publications/ac3b407bc99ac22c1bd0.md)

Rujira Buntharikpornpun; Supaporn Roymanee; Worakan Promphan; Phuoc Duong

Catastrophic complications of coronary artery compression after percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation \(PPVI\) are uncommon in patients with a dysfunctional native right ventricular outflow tract after Tetralogy of Fallot repair \(rTOF\)\. Nonetheless, we report three rTOFs with a high risk of compromising coronary blood flow for PPVI\. This risk has been elucidated by multimodal assessments, including robust pre\-procedural cardiac computed tomography and meticulous balloon interrogation with selective coronary angiography\.

## [Challenges to Biodiversity Rights and Intellectual Property Rights under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002](../publications/ac3d13722e5070af1880.md)

Nidhi Shubhanand

The Biodiversity Act, 2002, was enacted to conserve biological diversity, ensure sustainable use of biological resources, and facilitate equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilization\. This paper examines the interface between the Biodiversity Act and Intellectual Property Rights \(IPR\), focusing on the challenges of balancing innovation with biodiversity conservation\. It analyses the legal safeguards against biopiracy, the role of prior approval mechanisms, and benefit\-sharing provisions in patent applications involving biological resources and traditional knowledge\. The study highlights implementation challenges and suggests policy measures to strengthen biodiversity governance while promoting sustainable development and responsible innovation\.

## [CADEN: An Enhanced Cross\-dataset Anatomy\-aware Distribution\-alignment Ensemble Model for Alzheimer&\#x27;s Disease Detection and Staging from MRI](../publications/ac3fb850bcccc0ecae54.md)

Chetna Sharma; Vivek Bhatnagar

Deep models for Alzheimer&\#x27;s disease \(AD\) classification degrade sharply when training and deployment data originate from different scanners and cohorts, so reported single\-dataset accuracies rarely transfer to new sites\.This paper presents CADEN, an anatomy\-aware framework that learns a harmonized, atrophy\-grounded featuremapping space and performs staging by an ensemble over that space rather than over raw images\.CADEN combines four ideas: \(i\) label\-free cross\-site harmonization that couples ComBat\-style feature adjustment with a lightweight learnable site adapter; \(ii\) dual\-distribution encoders that align image\-feature and structural\-prior distributions so representations are anatomy\-grounded rather than texture\-driven; \(iii\) a correspondence\-attention objective that supervises cross\-attention to match anatomical regions between subject and atlas; and \(iv\) a teaching\-learning\-basedoptimization \(TLBO\) feature\-selection stage that yields a compact descriptor consumed by a heterogeneous stacking ensemble\.The cross\-dataset protocol is restated so that no target\-domain label and no target\-domain diagnosis covariate is accessed at any stage; separate training and inference algorithms are given, and results are reported separately for domain generalization and unsupervised domain adaptation\.On strictly subject\-level splits CADEN attains 96\.3% accuracy and 96\.3% balanced accuracy in\-domain on ADNI \(both figures are five\-seed means over seeds 0 to 4\) and raises cross\-dataset balanced accuracy from 76\.8% to 90\.6% \(ADNI to OASIS\) and from 74\.2% to 88\.7% \(OASIS to ADNI\) over a single\-transformer baseline, exceeding the capacity\-and training\-budget\-matched representation\-level adaptation baselines, namely correlation alignment, maximum\-mean\-discrepancy matching, adversarial adaptation and a matched ensemble without anatomical supervision, by 4\.6 to 6\.0 points, and exceeding the harmonization\-only baselines by larger margins\.The decoder&\#x27;s abnormality maps localize hippocampal and ventricular change, and a neutral\-atlas control shows this localization is not an artefact of the atlas choice \(Section 4\.4\)\.All code, subject\-level split manifests, seed\-wise predictions and table\-regeneration scripts are publicly released\.

## [Integrating local knowledge into community\-led Green coastal adaptation on the northern coast of Demak, Indonesia](../publications/ac40892c6c8e91730953.md)

Ikrom Mustofa; Dhandhun Wacano; Diah Ayu Prawitasari; Tri Atmaja; Enggar Yustisi Arini; Abhishek Tiwary

Introduction Coastal communities in Indonesia face increasing risks from tidal flooding, land subsidence, sea\-level rise, and saltwater intrusion\. Although community\-based adaptation has received growing attention, there is still limited understanding of how local knowledge can be combined with spatial analysis to guide adaptation planning in rural coastal areas\. Methods This study examines Timbulsloko Village, Demak Regency, Central Java, using a convergent multi\-method approach\. Literature review, field observation, interviews, and spatial analysis were integrated to identify major climate risks, existing adaptation practices, and priority areas for intervention\. Community knowledge was also used for the interpretation of spatial conditions and the assessment of locally applicable adaptation options\. Results The results showed that the coastal risks did not distribute evenly in Timbulsloko area, but the vulnerable areas were concentrated in low\-lying settlements, access routes, public facilities, abandoned fishponds and degraded coastal ecosystems\. Spatial analysis and the community perspectives were used to identify priority intervention zones and to explore appropriate adaptation strategies\. These include mangrove rehabilitation, flood\-resistant infrastructure, adaptive agriculture, community\-based early warning systems, and improved water\-resource management\. Their suitability varies according to local environmental conditions, community needs, institutional support, and implementation capacity\. Discussion The study demonstrates the value of combining local knowledge with spatial evidence in identifying adaptation priorities rather than treating the two sources separately\. Stronger coordination among communities, local government, and supporting organizations is needed to improve the implementation and long\-term sustainability of coastal adaptation in Timbulsloko and other vulnerable rural coastal areas\.

## [Impact of faculty development on teaching practices in higher education: a scoping review](../publications/ac47b8c077ec823e3195.md)

Arianna Marci; Martina Ragusa; Flavio Manganello

Introduction Faculty development \(FD\) is an established feature of Higher Education, yet its impact on what teachers actually do in their teaching has been studied less often than outcomes such as satisfaction, learning and attitudes\. This behavioural level is the third of the four outcome levels in the adaptation of Kirkpatrick&\#x27;s model developed for FD in Higher Education\. No prior review has mapped it across disciplinary fields outside health professions education, and the present scoping review addresses that gap\. Methods Following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews, we included empirical and theoretical sources published in English between 2005 and 2025 that reported a change in the teaching practices of university teachers following structured FD, in any discipline other than health professions education\. Scopus and Web of Science were searched, with the last search on 25 April 2026\. Three reviewers charted the data independently, coding the evaluation framework, the assessment method and type of evidence, and the indicator and direction of effect\. Empirical studies were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool \(MMAT\)\. Results The search yielded 491 deduplicated records, of which 69 met the inclusion criteria\. The evidence is recent and concentrated in the United States and in science, technology, engineering and mathematics \(STEM\) fields\. Fifty\-three of the 69 sources name no evaluation model\. Of the 64 empirical studies appraised, 29 used non\-randomised or descriptive quantitative designs and only one used random assignment\. Qualitative studies largely met their criteria, whereas quantitative and mixed methods studies recurrently showed incomplete outcome data, unaccounted confounding, undocumented intervention fidelity and unexamined divergence between strands\. Of 217 behavioural effects, 150 rest on teacher self\-report and 66 on evidence external to the teacher, with one effect not classifiable\. The direction of effect depended on how the change was established\. Positive effects accounted for 65% of the self\-reported behavioural effects but for 42% of the externally documented ones, and for 65% of those measured without a baseline against 49% of those measured with one\. Discussion The literature makes its central claim, that development changes what teachers do, largely on the teachers&\#x27; own testimony\. Where that claim is tested against external evidence, it holds less often\. Systematic Review Registration https://doi\.org/10\.17605/OSF\.IO/SAERU \.

## [Low\-resource Indigenous language translator](../publications/ac4c128d799272275955.md)

Emiliano Churruca; Jorge Santos; Santiago Durante; Marcia Nascimento; Juan Santos; Luis Chiruzzo

La línea de investigación presentada en este trabajo tiene como objetivo formular e implementar una metodología para la creación de traductores de lenguas con bajos recursos en América del Sur\. El lenguaje forma parte de la cultura e identidad de las comunidades, especialmente en pueblos originarios\. La globalización y la marginalización histórica, entre otros factores, provocaron que muchas lenguas se hayan retraído hasta desaparecer mientras que otras, se desvanecen\. La metodología propuesta involucra la búsqueda, recolección y depuración de datos para la creación del corpus bitexto que permita la creación de modelos de lenguaje su cientemente ricos como para la implementación de máquinas de traducción basadas en Transformers\. Las lenguas objeto de estudio con las que inicialmente se trabajará son el Kaingang y el Ayoreo\. En cuanto a la primera, se ha empezado a aplicar la metodología conformando un pequeño corpus y se ha implementado un traductor basado en el esquema codi cador\-decodi cador usando Transformers\. Los resultados preliminares expuestos aquí permiten obtener algunas conclusiones útiles para la formulación de la metodología\.

## [Sustainable Market Forecasting of Electric Vehicle Adoption Using Machine Learning Techniques in Emerging Economies](../publications/ac5a8394352f1ab2df17.md)

Md Anas Biswas; Mahbube Rabbani; Safia Farzana Nishi; Ashutosh Roy; Md Samir Murad

The rapid transition toward sustainable transportation has increased the importance of electric vehicle \(EV\) adoption forecasting, particularly in emerging economies where market growth is influenced by economic conditions, charging infrastructure availability, vehicle costs, and policy environments\. The scale of EV market penetration, however, is not a straightforward prediction owing to the fact that it can differ based on adoption rates, infrastructure deployment, and socioeconomic conditions in individual countries\. This study proposes a machine learning tool to develop a sustainable market forecasting model to forecast adoption of EVs in emerging economies based on past market, economic, infrastructure and policy indicators\. An EV adoption dataset was used, which consists of EV sales share, charging infrastructure, economic indicators, vehicle price data, and policy features across 26 emerging economies spanning 2010 to 2025\. A set of forecasting models, such as Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting and an ensemble approach, was tested with an unseen test period from 2025, employing a leakage aware time\-series validation strategy\. The ensemble forecasting model presented here proved to have a high level of predictive skill with R², RMSE and MAE values of 0\.9010, 5\.0773 and 3\.7198, respectively\. The historical trends of EV adoption, development of charging infrastructure, economic factors, and policy considerations were identified as primary drivers of future EV market growth through feature analysis\. The results illustrate how machine learning\-based forecasting can help offer decision\-support information to policymakers, industry, and sustainable transportation planners\. The suggested model is a step towards more data\-informed EV transition planning, as it facilitates accurate market prediction and assists in sustainable mobility planning in new economies\.

## [Exact Discrete Spectral Invariants as a Falsification Baseline for Learned Operator](../publications/ac6ba7f847388c175914.md)

Michael Aksman

We have presented a mathematically closed, comprehensive foundation for the C861 discrete spectral benchmark\. By establishing the exact rank\-two projector geometry, resolving Dirichlet sum cancellations, providing constructive proofs for linear B\-spline KAN operator reproduction, and formalizing the Lyapunov convergence of Dense Associative Memory on spherical manifolds, this framework eliminates ambiguities in evaluating learned physical operators\. Furthermore, the spectral interlacing analysis of the CN → PN structural homotopy equips the scientific machine learning community with a tool to distinguish authentic topological sensitivity from numerical discretization artifacts\.

## [Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Banking Services: Benefits, Customer Experience and Challenges](../publications/ac6ef850af649c18da99.md)

Sri Krish K B; S\. H\. Varshitha

Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Banking Services: Benefits, Customer Experience and Challenges This research investigates the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in modern banking services, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, customer experience, and emerging challenges\. It examines the application of AI\-driven technologies, including machine learning, intelligent chatbots, predictive analytics, and automated fraud detection, in streamlining banking operations, enhancing service personalisation, improving risk management, and supporting data\-driven decision\-making\. Furthermore, the study evaluates key concerns associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, and customer trust\. By assessing both the benefits and limitations of AI integration, this research aims to develop a comprehensive understanding of its implications for the banking sector and highlight the importance of responsible, secure, and customer\-centric AI implementation in the evolving financial services landscape\.

## [Early Detection of the Risk of Literacy Difficulties in the English Language Classroom in Early Childhood Education: The Role of Phonological Awareness and Rapid Automatized Naming](../publications/ac713aa7b05634f96910.md)

María Teresa Fraile\-Calviño; Luis\-Manuel Martínez\-Domínguez; Nuria García Manzanares

The acquisition of English as a foreign language is increasingly important in Early Childhood Education\. However, some children experience difficulties in learning to read and write, which can negatively affect their academic, social, and future professional development\. Early detection and intervention are therefore essential, as dyslexia is often diagnosed only after several years of literacy instruction, when some children may already have experienced academic failure and low self\-esteem\. This study employed a quantitative, non\-experimental, cross\-sectional, descriptive, predictive, comparative, and correlational design, focusing on two key predictors: phonological awareness and naming speed\. Its aim was to identify children at risk of literacy difficulties in English among students in the second and third years of Early Childhood Education\. The findings identified students at risk, supported profiles consistent with the double\-deficit hypothesis, confirmed the independence of phonological awareness and naming speed, and highlighted reliable tools for early identification and targeted intervention in educational settings\.

## [Multimodal learning analytics infrastructure and adaptive digital assessment](../publications/ac76046f9125a6c2c042.md)

S\. Asha; V\. P\. Joshith

Abstract This study empirically validates a theoretically grounded framework linking Multimodal Learning Analytics \(MMLA\) infrastructure components to adaptive digital assessment outcomes\. Drawing on Universal Design for Learning \(UDL\) principles and learning analytics theory, we developed and tested a structural model examining how MMLA infrastructure is associated with educational practice\. A cross\-sectional survey was conducted with 476 educators and instructional designers across diverse educational contexts in India\. The initially proposed 11\-construct framework integrating UDL principles with MMLA infrastructure underwent systematic empirical validation using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. A rigorous three\-iteration refinement process reduced the initial 44\-item instrument to a validated 24\-item scale measuring seven constructs\. The final validated model comprised MMLA infrastructure components \(data quality, technology platforms, real\-time analytics\) and educational outcomes \(adaptive intervention, formative feedback, inclusive assessment, SRL support\)\. Real\-time analytics emerged as the dominant predictor across all outcomes \(β = 0\.546, f 2 = 0\.421, large effect on adaptive intervention\), while MMLA technology demonstrated consistent moderate effects, and MMLA data showed limited direct association\. Together, MMLA infrastructure explained 19–46% of the variance in adaptive assessment practices\. Notably, UDL constructs failed to achieve acceptable psychometric properties despite theoretical grounding, revealing important insights about measurement challenges in practitioner self\-reports\. Findings suggest institutions should prioritise real\-time analytics capabilities over raw data collection or basic technology infrastructure\. The validated 24\-item instrument enables practitioners to benchmark MMLA implementation and identify infrastructure gaps\. This study provides the first empirically validated framework linking MMLA infrastructure with adaptive assessment outcomes, distinguishing data quality, technology platforms, and real\-time analytics as separate constructs with differential effects\. The UDL measurement challenges contribute to implementation science by revealing gaps between theoretical articulation and practical measurement\.

## [CRISPR/Cas genome editing strategies to enhance abiotic stress tolerance in sugar crops](../publications/ac76cc2706105f079ce6.md)

Hong\-Bo Liu; Tanweer Kumar; Farrag F\. B\. Abu\-Ellail; Xiu\-Qin Lin; Chun\-Jia Li; Chao\-Hua Xu; Muhammad Arif; Wajid Khan; Muhammad Ismail; Li\-Ping Zhao; Ebtehag A\.E\. Sakr; Nur\-ul Haq; Xin Lu

Sugar crops including sugarcane, sugar beets, and sweet sorghum, are fundamental for global sucrose supply and crucial feedstocks for bioethanol production and industrial bioproducts\. However, yield and sucrose accumulation are significantly influenced by abiotic stresses, including drought, salinity/alkalinity, heat, chilling/freezing, and heavy metal toxicity\. The polygenic complexity of stress tolerance, particularly in sugarcane with its large, polyploid, and haplotype\-diverse genome, presents significant challenges for conventional breeding, rendering it slow and imprecise\. This review combines advances in genome\-editing technologies, including CRISPR/Cas systems \(Cas9 and Cas12a\), along with transcriptional techniques \(CRISPRa/i\), base editors, and prime editors\. These tools, combined with the progress in reference genomes, haplotype\-resolved assemblies, and pangenomes, have facilitated precise gene discovery, genomic selection, and targeted editing\. CRISPR\-based approaches offer promising avenues for enhancing key stress\-responsive pathways governing oxidative homeostasis, membrane integrity, osmotic regulation, hormone signaling, and ion\-homeostasis in sugar crops\. Prominent candidate targets include transcription factors \(TF\), signaling components, raffinose biosynthesis genes implicated in freezing tolerance, regulators of salt and alkaline stress, and determinants of heavy metal tolerance and sequestration\. Translational challenges, such as off\-target effects, low transformation efficiencies, and editing multiple homologues or haplotypes, are being addressed such as DNA\-free ribonucleoprotein \(RNP\) delivery, high\-throughput screening, haplotype\-specific target design, and haplotype\-aware guide RNA engineering based on unique genetic variation sites across different gene haplotypes\. Collectively, the integration of advanced CRISPR toolkits with enhanced genomic information resources and phenotyping capabilities holds significant potential for accelerating the development of precision\-bred, multi\-stress\-resilient sugar crops that sustain yield, quality, and industrial value under abiotic stress conditions\.

## [Testing Group Differences in Nonlinear Growth Curve Modeling with Penalized Spline](../publications/ac7702cf2f0ed1a334ae.md)

Han Du; Liu Yang; Zhiyong Zhang

Longitudinal data analysis in social and behavioral sciences often assumes a linear change over time, but human behavior is complex and frequently exhibits nonlinear patterns\. Regression spline is a popular approach in machine learning to model nonlinear trajectories\. While traditional machine learning prioritizes prediction, researchers in social and behavioral sciences focus on testing and interpreting the significance of group differences\. This study compares six spline models for evaluating group differences in group\-mean trajectories across multiple time points: the frequentist truncated power basis model, the frequentist piecewise basis model, the frequentist B\-spline basis model, the Bayesian truncated power basis model, the Bayesian piecewise basis model, and the Bayesian B\-spline basis model\. Through simulation, we found that for non\-censored data, the frequentist models demonstrated stability and robust performance\. However, these models showed potential issues with statistical inference such as coverage rates and Type I error rates when the data are censored \(e\.g\., floor and ceiling effects\)\. For the latter cases, we recommend either using the frequentist models with an unstructured level\-2 covariance matrix if computation time permits, or using the Bayesian B\-spline model with an unstructured level\-2 covariance matrix\.

## [Associations of Combined Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Psychological and Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study](../publications/ac7a51cf93b7b2f7e52f.md)

Yuehao Wu; Yusha Shen; Meng Huang

Background: To examine whether combined transcranial magnetic stimulation \(TMS\) and transcranial direct current stimulation \(tDCS\), delivered with standard rehabilitation, was associated with post\-stroke depression and anxiety symptoms and secondary neurological and motor outcomes\. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 180 patients classified according to treatment received in routine clinical practice: combined TMS \+ tDCS \+ standard rehabilitation \(n = 60\), standard rehabilitation alone \(n = 60\), TMS \+ standard rehabilitation \(n = 30\), or tDCS \+ standard rehabilitation \(n = 30\)\. Treatment selection reflected physician recommendations and patient preference\. Beck Depression Inventory \(BDI\) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7\-item scale \(GAD\-7\) scores were primary outcomes; National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale \(NIHSS\), modified Rankin Scale \(mRS\), and Fugl\-Meyer Assessment \(FMA\) scores were secondary outcomes\. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks\. Generalized estimating equations adjusted for prespecified measured covariates assessed group, time, and group × time associations\. Dunnett\-adjusted comparisons used standard rehabilitation as the reference\. Results: No statistically significant differences were detected in the measured baseline characteristics \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. At 8 weeks, the combined group had lower median BDI scores \[8\.0 \(6\.0, 10\.0\) vs\. 14\.5 \(11\.5, 17\.0\)\] and GAD\-7 scores \[6\.0 \(4\.0, 8\.0\) vs\. 9\.0 \(7\.0, 11\.0\)\] than the Standard Rehabilitation Group \(both Dunnett\-adjusted p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Significant group × time associations were identified for BDI, GAD\-7, NIHSS, mRS, and FMA outcomes \(all p &lt; 0\.05\)\. The combined group also had lower NIHSS and mRS scores and higher FMA scores than the standard rehabilitation group at 4 and 8 weeks\. No severe adverse events were documented\. Total recorded adverse\-event rates were 8\.3%, 5\.0%, 3\.3%, and 3\.3% across the four groups, respectively, with no significant between\-group difference \(Fisher’s exact p = 0\.584\)\. Conclusions: In this retrospective cohort, combined TMS and tDCS with standard rehabilitation was associated with lower depression and anxiety symptom scores and more favorable neurological and motor outcome trajectories than standard rehabilitation\. Non\-random treatment allocation and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation; prospective randomized studies are required\.

## [Data\-driven multi\-criteria evaluation of intelligent cockpit configuration strategies in Chinese battery electric vehicles](../publications/ac83088661fe7410489c.md)

Weixin Zhu; Xue Xiong

Introduction In this study, we examine how documented cockpit equipment differentiates selected Chinese\-brand battery electric vehicles \(BEVs\)\. We compare configuration richness with and without a price criterion and identify recurring equipment arrangements, rather than using specifications as a proxy for tested cockpit performance\. Methods The dataset comprises 36 purposively selected model–trim combinations from 13 brands\. Two CRITIC–TOPSIS models score four configuration criteria, with guide price included as a cost in the second model\. Gower dissimilarity and partitioning around medoids \(PAM\) describe eight mixed\-type attributes\. Sensitivity checks vary weights, aggregation, criteria, coding, and case composition\. Each model also uses 5,000 vehicle resamples and 5,000 brand\-block resamples to assess conditional weighting uncertainty\. Results The head‐up display \(HUD\) level receives the largest weight in the price‐free model \(0\.3557\)\. Baseline rankings correlate at ρ = 0\.964\. Five clusters yield a mean silhouette width of 0\.519, only slightly above 0\.514 for six clusters\. Removing HUD reduces ranking correlations to 0\.678 and 0\.750\. The leading price\-adjusted scores for ZEEKR 001 and XPeng P7\+ differ by 0\.000285; their first\-place frequencies under brand\-block resampling are 50\.30% and 49\.06%\. Discussion The comparison distinguishes equipment patterns within the recorded sample, but its resolution depends on the criteria and their representation\. Broad ranking agreement does not guarantee a stable first\-place choice\. The clusters describe configurations, not market shares, and neither index establishes superior usability, safety, or overall cockpit capability\.

## [Vurderingspraksis i møte med generativ KI – en casestudie](../publications/ac845639b2b6f17ec718.md)

Lise Lillebrygfjeld Halse

Generativ KI representerer en transformativ teknologi som utfordrer akademisk praksis og potensielt akademias rolle som kunnskaps\- og sertifiseringsinstitusjon i samfunnet\. Når KI\-verktøy kan produsere akademiske besvarelser på høyt nivå, reises spørsmålet om hjemmeeksamen fortsatt er et gyldig instrument for å måle studentenes faktiske kunnskaper og ferdigheter\. Denne artikkelen undersøker hvordan Høgskolen i Molde, en institusjon med strategisk satsing på nettbaserte studier og høy andel hjemmeeksamen, har håndtert de utfordringene generativ KI stiller til vurderingspraksis\. Gjennom en case\-studie basert på interne dokumenter, eksamensstatistikk og medieomtale viser artikkelen at institusjonen i stor grad har valgt «business as usual» fremfor å iverksette systematiske praksisendringer\. Artikkelen argumenterer for at den observerte institusjonelle passiviteten kan forstås i lys av spenningen mellom en akademisk logikk der faglig integritet og læringsutbytte er sentrale verdier, og en markedslogikk der studiepoengsproduksjon og inntekter veier tyngst\. Caset illustrerer hvordan denne konflikten i institusjonelle logikker kan hemme nødvendig omstilling, og understreker behovet for nasjonal koordinering og regulering fremfor å overlate ansvaret til den enkelte institusjon\. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Assessment Practices in Light of Generative AI Generative AI represents a transformative technology that fundamentally challenges academic practice and potentially the role of higher education institutions as producers and certifiers of knowledge\. As AI tools become capable of producing high\-quality academic responses, the validity of take\-home examinations as instruments for measuring students&\#x27; actual knowledge and skills is called into question\. This article examines how Høgskolen i Molde – an institution with a strategic commitment to online education and a high proportion of take\-home examinations – has responded to the challenges generative AI poses to assessment practice\. Through a case study drawing on internal documents, examination statistics, and media coverage, the article shows that the institution has largely opted for business as usual rather than implementing systematic changes to its assessment practices\. The article argues that the observed institutional passivity can be understood in light of the tension between an academic logic, in which academic integrity and student learning outcomes are core values, and a market logic in which credit point production and revenue take precedence\. The case illustrates how this conflict between institutional logics can impede necessary adaptation and underscores the need for national coordination and regulation rather than leaving the responsibility for change to individual institutions\.

## [Global burden of type 2 diabetes attributable to SARS\-CoV\-2 infection](../publications/ac8e5c7b0893f37e14bb.md)

Jingjing Li; Guangming Liu; Jianzhou Yang; Haimiao Ma; Xiuli Wang; Ziying Jiang; Yuanhao Liang; Xiaofeng He

Objective We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 \(SARS\-CoV\-2\) infection and the risk of incident diabetes\. We also aimed to estimate the global burden of incident type 2 diabetes \(T2D\) attributable to SARS\-CoV\-2 infection\. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta\-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026\. Adjusted relative risks \(RRs\) for incident T2D and type 1 diabetes \(T1D\) following SARS\-CoV\-2 infection were pooled using random\-effects models\. Population attributable fractions \(PAFs\) and attributable T2D cases were estimated by integrating pooled risk estimates with Global Burden of Disease \(GBD\) 2023 data on COVID\-19 prevalence and T2D incidence\. Results Fifteen cohort studies involving approximately 48\.9 million participants were included\. SARS\-CoV\-2 infection was associated with an increased risk of incident T2D \(13 studies; pooled RR, 1\.25 \[95% CI, 1\.16–1\.34\]\), although substantial heterogeneity was observed and the 95% prediction interval \(PI\) included the null \(0\.94–1\.66\)\. In subgroup analysis, the association was confined to mixed\-variant studies \(RR, 1\.29 \[95% CI, 1\.23–1\.36\]; 95% PI, 1\.09–1\.54\), whereas studies evaluating a single variant \(Delta or Omicron\) showed no excess risk \(RR, 1\.00 \[95% CI, 0\.97–1\.03\]\)\. The association with incident T1D did not reach conventional statistical significance \(10 studies; pooled RR, 1\.13 \[95% CI, 0\.99–1\.30\]\)\. Globally, 24\.53 million incident T2D cases occurred in 2023\. The PAF attributable to COVID\-19 of 1\.12% \(95% CI 0\.90, 1\.35\), corresponding to 274,889 \(95% CI 220,360, 331,698\) incident T2D cases attributable to SARS\-CoV\-2 infection\. The largest attributable burdens were observed in India, the USA, and China\. Conclusions SARS\-CoV\-2 infection was associated with a modest increase in pooled T2D risk\. This association was primarily observed in mixed\-variant studies, for which the 95% PI excluded the null\. However, the overall pooled estimated was accompanied by substantial between\-study heterogeneity, and its 95% PI crossing the null, indicating uncertainty in the association across populations and settings\. At the population level, this excess risk translated into an estimated 275,000 incident T2D cases attributable to COVID\-19 worldwide in 2023, highlighting the need for ongoing metabolic surveillance following infection\. Systematic Review Registration https://www\.crd\.york\.ac\.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261307969 , identifier CRD420261307969\.

## [Kertész, András: Artificial Intelligence and the Sociology of Knowledge: Prolegomena to an Integrated Philosophy of Science](../publications/ac9e69613d90137e85f1.md)



A central topic of the latest research in the philosophy of science is the question of what kind of relationship there is between the cognitive and social factors which underlie scientific knowledge\. At present, this problem has manifested itself in a heated and still unfinished controversy between the proponents of artificial intelligence research and the sociologists of knowledge\. By resolving the antagonism of these two positions, the book aims at developing a modular approach to an integrated philosophy of science which can handle the interaction between cognitive and social factors in a way which differs considerably from all current proposals\.

## [Burkhardt, Anne: Artificial intelligence in the work and view of Latin American filmmakers: insights from a qualitative interview study](../publications/aca9e64d68b28c9784dd.md)



\_AI and Society\_:1\-19\. forthcomingPrevious research on the representation of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in science fiction \(SF\) film has largely focused on the Global North\. Little is known about how filmmakers from the Souths envision and portray AI and how their creative processes and outputs relate to specific conditions of film production, socio\-political realities, and global power imbalances, as well as personal experiences and attitudes toward AI\. This paper aims to address this gap by presenting the findings of an exploratory interview study with Latin American filmmakers who have dealt with AI in their films\. The qualitative text analysis of 10 in\-depth, semi\-structured interviews with 11 participants from 6 countries reveals that their cinematic visions of AI differ significantly from those prevalent in Western SF: The Latin American filmmakers predominantly associate AI with social control, surveillance, labor exploitation, data colonialism, and the abuse of power by \(authoritarian\) governments or powerful tech corporations—issues that decolonial scholars have emphasized in their critiques of AI\. However, the participants’ visions are not primarily inspired by these academic debates but by their lived experiences\. The filmmakers’ strong engagement with everyday life and socio\-political conditions, rather than distant or unattainable technological scenarios, can, thus, be considered a distinctive feature of the Latin American approach\. This is further reflected in their use of particular esthetic concepts and strategies, such as retrofuturism, which enable them to navigate budgetary constraints and other structural inequalities that limit their visibility and their potential to actively shape technological visions and futures through film\. \(direct link \)

## [Araç seçim problemi için karşılaştırmalı bir yaklaşım: Aralık Tip 2 bulanık AHP ve Aralık Tip 2 bulanık VIKOR](../publications/acaa14403126c33d16cf.md)

Müslüm Öztürk

Bulanık karar verme, belirsizliği, uzman görüşleri arasındaki farklılıkları ve kesin olmayan verileri dikkate alarak daha güvenilir kararların alınmasını sağlayan önemli bir yaklaşımdır\. Çok kriterli karar verme \(ÇKKV\) yöntemleri arasında yer alan VIKOR \(VlseKriterijumska Optimizacija i Kompromisno Resenje\), alternatifleri ideal çözüme olan yakınlıklarına göre değerlendirerek bir uzlaşık çözüm belirler\. Buna karşılık, Analitik Hiyerarşi Prosesi \(AHP\), karar problemlerini amaç, kriterler ve alternatiflerden oluşan hiyerarşik bir yapı içerisinde analiz ederek kriterlerin göreli önem derecelerini belirlemektedir\. Bununla birlikte, klasik ve Tip\-1 bulanık yaklaşımlar, yüksek düzeyde belirsizlik içeren karar problemlerinin modellenmesinde yetersiz kalabilmektedir\. Buna karşılık, Aralık Tip\-2 bulanık kümeler, üyelik derecelerindeki belirsizliği de modele dahil ederek uzman değerlendirmelerinin daha gerçekçi bir biçimde temsil edilmesini sağlamakta ve böylece karar verme sürecinin güvenilirliğini artırmaktadır\. Bu çalışmada, klasik VIKOR yöntemi Aralık Tip\-2 bulanık ortamına genişletilmiş ve Aralık Tip\-2 Bulanık VIKOR \(IT2 FVIKOR\) olarak adlandırılan yeni bir karar verme modeli önerilmiştir\. Daha sonra önerilen yöntem, daha önce geliştirilmiş olan Aralık Tip\-2 Bulanık AHP \(IT2 FAHP\) yöntemi ile birlikte bir araç seçimi problemine uygulanarak karşılaştırmalı olarak değerlendirilmiştir\. Son olarak, her iki yöntemden elde edilen sıralama sonuçları karşılaştırmalı olarak analiz edilmiş ve yöntemlerin seçim performansları Kendall Tau korelasyon analizi kullanılarak doğrulanmıştır\.
