## [Cross\-sectional assessment of anxiety and insomnia of Spanish veterinarians following African swine fever wild boar detection in Spain](../publications/acadc33809d36032f658.md)

Rachel A\. Schambow; Paulina Guerra; Marta Martinez Aviles; Irene Iglesias; Antonio Palomo Yagüe; Miguel Angel Higuera; Alejandro D\. Perez; Andrés Pérez

In November 2025, African swine fever \(ASF\) was detected in wild boar in the Catalonia region of Spain\. The primary objective of this cross\-sectional survey study was to descriptively explore the mental health impacts of the emergence of ASF in Spain on Spanish practicing veterinarians working with swine and to provide a baseline for future comparison if conditions of the ASF epidemic in Spain significantly change\. A questionnaire with the Generalized Anxiety Disorder\-7 and Insomnia Severity Index was distributed via convenience sampling to Spanish pig veterinarians from April to May 2026\. Working in an ASF control zone, and working in Catalonia, were primary exposures of interest for anxiety and insomnia score\. Data were analyzed using univariate analyses\. Fifty\-three veterinarians responded to the survey\. Median anxiety score was 6\.00 \(interquartile range \[IQR\]: 2\.00–10\.0\) and median insomnia score was 8\.00 \(IQR: 4\.00–13\.0\)\. Some veterinarians reported new feelings of uneasiness or sadness \(54\.7%\), extreme changes in their feelings of happiness and sadness \(41\.5%\), and less confidence in their abilities or their value \(41\.5%\) since the ASF outbreak\. Working in an ASF control zone or working in Catalonia were not significantly associated with insomnia or anxiety score \( p &gt; 0\.05\)\. These findings help to describe the current status of anxiety and insomnia amongst Spanish pig veterinarians following the ASF detection in wild boar, and provide a baseline for future comparisons if the ASF epidemic worsens in the country\.

## [REGULARITIES OF GROWTH AND MORPHOGENESIS OF HUMAN METACARPAL BONES DURING THE PERIOD OF OSTEOGENESIS COMPLETION](../publications/acb22b143563a820aaa8.md)

I\. H\. Biriuk

The study of morphometric parameters of hand bones in adolescents and young adults is an important direction in modern anatomy, pediatric orthopedics, and forensic medicine\. The age period of 17\-21 years is characterized by the final phases of osteogenesis, when the rate of linear growth slows down, yet individual and sex\-specific features of skeletal formation persist\. Establishing clear age\- and sex\-related norms for metacarpal bone lengths allows for increasing the accuracy of biological age assessment, predicting growth potential, and evaluating skeletal maturity\. Objective\. To investigate the anatomical and morphometric standards and sex differences in the dimensions of the metacarpal bones of the right and left hands in young adults aged 17\-21 years\. Material and Methods\. The study of the morphometric parameters of the metacarpal bones of the right and left hands in young adults was conducted through a retrospective analysis of 224 hand radiographs obtained from patients aged 17 to 21 years who received inpatient or outpatient treatment at the Department of Traumatology of the Emergency Hospital in Chernivtsi\. The total sample included 112 young men and 112 young women without signs of skeletal system pathology that could affect the growth or morphometric parameters of the metacarpal bones\. The study was carried out within the framework of cooperation with the medical institution in accordance with a formal agreement\. Inclusion criteria: age range of 17\-21 years, presence of clear radiographs of both hands in a direct anteroposterior projection without distortion, absence of radiological signs of trauma \(fractures, cracks, bone calluses\), congenital developmental anomalies, bone and joint pathologies, or systemic skeletal diseases\. Exclusion criteria: presence of artifacts on radiographs that complicated osteometry; destructive, inflammatory, or neoplastic changes in bone tissue; traces of surgical interventions or metal osteosynthesis; and structural deformities of the metacarpal bones\. Since the study was retrospective and based on the analysis of a de\-identified radiological archive, additional informed consent from patients was not required, which complies with the ethical standards of the Declaration of Helsinki of the World Medical Association \(1964, amended in 2013\) and the Council of Europe Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine \(04\.04\.1997\)\. The study was conducted in compliance with bioethical norms and was approved by the Bioethics Committee of Bukovinian State Medical University \(Protocol No\. 2 dated October 16, 2025\), which revealed no violations of moral and legal standards\.The study is a fragment of the department&\#x27;s comprehensive research project of the Department of Anatomy, Clinical Anatomy, and Operative Surgery: &quot;Sex and age patterns of ontogenetic transformations and morphometric parameters of organs and structures in normal and experimental conditions\. Morpho\-functional and anthropometric characteristics of the musculoskeletal system of athletes&quot; \(State Registration Number: 0125U001531\)\. Statistical processing of the data was performed using Microsoft Excel\. Results are presented as mean values \(M\) and standard deviations \(SD\)\. Relative annual growth values \(percentages\) and bilateral asymmetry indices were also calculated\. Results\. Analysis of the radiographs revealed that the length of all metacarpal bones increases continuously during young adulthood; however, growth dynamics are characterized by heterochrony and marked sexual dimorphism\. Throughout the entire observation period \(17\-21 years\), the absolute dimensions of all metacarpal bones in young men significantly exceeded the corresponding values in young women\. Growth processes in young men exhibited a wave\-like pattern with two distinct peaks in intensity\. The first spurt was recorded at 17\-18 years of age, with maximum growth observed in the 1st metacarpal bone \(\+2\.33% on the right hand\) and the 2nd metacarpal bone \(\+1\.71%\)\. The second growth spurt occurred at 20\-21 years, showing peak values for the 3rd, 4th, and 5th metacarpal bones\. In young women, growth rates generally slowed down after the age of 17\. The maximum growth increment of the 1st metacarpal bone in young women occurred at 18\-19 years \(\+0\.96 ±1\.21%\), the 2nd bone at 17\-18 years \(\+0\.16 ±0\.32%\), and the 3rd bone at 19\-20 years \(\+0\.50%\)\. At the same time, at 20\-21 years of age, a significant peak growth increment was observed in the 5th metacarpal bone \(\+3\.37%\) and the 4th metacarpal bone \(\+0\.56 ±0\.74%\)\. The least intensive period of bone length increase for both sexes was between 19 and 20 years of age, during which the annual increment of most bones decreased to 0\.18 ±0\.67% in males and 0\.16 ±0\.40% in females, corresponding to a phase of adaptive structural and mineral remodeling of bone tissue\. Analysis of bilateral differences showed that asymmetry between the right and left hands in young men and women was minimal \(ranging within 0\.00 ±0\.93% or 0\.01 ±0\.04 cm\) and lacked a systematic direction\. Conclusions\.The process of metacarpal bone osteogenesis during young adulthood \(17\-21 years\) is incomplete and is characterized by pronounced sexual dimorphism: the absolute sizes and growth rates of all metacarpal bones in young men significantly exceed the corresponding values in young women throughout the entire period\.In young men, two growth spurts are observed\- at 17\-18 years \(predominantly the 1st and 2nd metacarpals\) and at 20\-21 years \(the 3rd, 4th, and 5th metacarpals\)\. In young women, growth processes generally decelerate after the age of 17, but demonstrate a local peak growth increment in the 5th metacarpal bone at 20\-21 years \(\+3\.37%\)\.The period of minimal growth activity for both sexes is the age interval of 19\-20 years \(increment of 0\.16 ±0\.67%\), which corresponds to a phase of relative quiescence and organotypic remodeling of compact bone prior to the final closure of meta\-epiphyseal growth plates\.Bilateral asymmetry between the right and left hands is minimal\.

## [Comparison of Backward Elimination Features on Diabetes Disease Classification Accuracy using K\-Nearest Neighbor and Random Forest Algorithms](../publications/acbb9391e35ea0a4a45a.md)

Gusti Chandra Kurniawan; Imam Riadi; Anton Yudhana

The critical need for faster, more accurate diagnosis of diabetes mellitus by machine learning classification models is highlighted by the exponential growth in the global incidence of the disease\. The predominance of clinical traits and an unequal class distribution, among other problems, usually make it difficult for these models to forecast results\. This research investigates the comparative performance of K\-Nearest Neighbor \(KNN\) and Random Forest \(RF\) algorithms in diagnosing diabetes using a unified pipeline\. The methodology encompasses several stages: data preprocessing \(including the treatment of missing values, normalization, and encoding\), feature selection via backward elimination, class rebalancing using the Synthetic Minority Over\-sampling Technique \(SMOTE\), and performance assessment through a 5\-fold cross\-validation protocol\. The dataset from Mendeley Data was separated into two categories: those with diabetes and those without\. Based on the results, the RF algorithm achieved 97\.10% accuracy, 99\.52% precision, 98\.26% F1\-score, and 99\.50% ROC\-AUC, outperforming KNN in most evaluation criteria\. However, KNN also shows a competitive ability to categorize data with a high precision rate of 99\.15%\. These results show that feature selection and data balance techniques should be part of every classification pipeline if we want more consistent and accurate models\. The research concludes that Random Forest is more appropriate for clinical diabetes classification and suggests the systematic use of structured preprocessing in developing systems for early detection of chronic illnesses\.

## [Machine Learning Techniques for Malware Detection](../publications/acbd8427085e6195ca3f.md)

Dr\. S\. B\. Sarvaiya, Tanvi Kukadkar, Achal Bhelkar

Malware is one of the major threats to modern computer systems, mobile devices, cloud platforms, and networks\. Traditional signature\-based antivirus systems are effective against known malware but often have difficulty detecting new, polymorphic, obfuscated, and zero\-day variants\. Machine Learning \(ML\) provides a data\-driven approach in which models learn patterns that distinguish malicious software from legitimate software\. This paper presents an overview of ML techniques used for malware detection, focusing on static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis\. Various algorithms, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), k\-Nearest Neighbors \(KNN\), Naïve Bayes, Artificial Neural Networks \(ANN\), Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\), and Recurrent Neural Networks \(RNN\), are discussed\. A general ML\-based malware detection methodology involving dataset collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, feature selection, classification, and evaluation is presented\. Important evaluation measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1\-score, and false\-positive rate are also described\. The paper further examines applications in endpoint security, Android malware detection, network security, cloud computing, and IoT environments\. Major challenges include dataset quality, class imbalance, concept drift, adversarial attacks, explainability, computational cost, and cross\-dataset generalization\. Finally, future research directions such as Explainable AI, federated learning, graph neural networks, transformer models, continuous learning, and lightweight edge\-based detection are discussed\.

## [HNRNPH2\-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids](../publications/acbeb20ae4c8f6556de7.md)

Carlo Donato Caiaffa; Neda Ghousifam; Stephen Watkins; Helder Imoto Nakaya; Rodney A\. Bowling; Richard H\. Finnell; Robert M\. Cabrera

Autism spectrum disorder has been linked to disrupted RNA processing during corticogenesis, yet variant\-specific mechanisms remain difficult to resolve\. Isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient\-derived induced pluripotent stem cell \(iPSC\) line carrying the HNRNPH2\-R114W variant and its CRISPR\-corrected counterpart serve as a human developmental model to investigate variant\-associated RNA dysregulation\. Imaging quantification and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing, performed at a single developmental time point on a pooled organoid RNA from each genotype, identify coordinated remodeling of neuronal and metabolic programs, along with junction\-centered splicing dysregulation involving 6,310 differentially used junctions\. Computational structural docking situates HNRNPH2 RNA recognition motifs \(RRMs\) 1–3 within a spliceosomal context and locates residue R114 near a predicted RNA\-contact interface, indicating that the R114W substitution may alter RNA engagement\. Integration of differential expression with event\- and isoform\-level analyses identifies regulatory hubs enriched for axon guidance and synaptic signaling pathways\. Single\-cell\-reference\-based deconvolution suggests modest compositional shifts that are unlikely to account for the extent of transcriptional and splicing alterations observed\. Collectively, these findings imply HNRNPH2\-R114W in widespread RNA rewiring and define candidate isoform\-level endpoints for mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in human cortical organoids\. These molecular signatures open new avenues to examine how HNRNPH2\-associated RNA dysregulation evolves across developmental time and recurs across independent biological contexts, providing a foundation for further mechanistic studies of this rare neurodevelopmental disorder\.

## [Wear Performance and Microstructure Characterization of EN39B Alloy Steel: An Integrated Approach Using Experimental Testing and Machine Learning](../publications/acbed2c016c358d598c5.md)

Rakesh Sudarsi; Jack J\. Kenned; Krishnasamy Sankaranarayanasamy; Andarge Ayele Adem

This study investigates the wear performance of carburized EN39B alloy steel, a very rarely explored aerospace gear material, using a hybrid Machine Learning\-Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\) approach for predictive modelling and process optimization\. An L16 orthogonal array\-based experimental design was adopted, and wear data were obtained using a Pin\-on\-Disc tribometer\. The experimental results revealed minimum and maximum wear values of 93 and 418 microns respectively\. The results of ANOVA revealed that speed is a significant influencing input parameter with a contribution of 77\.67%, followed by load with a contribution of 16\.26% on the variation of output characteristics\. The Gradient Boosting \(GB\) model achieved an R 2 regression coefficient of 0\.9977, indicating the model&\#x27;s adequacy and efficiency in the present study\. The PSO algorithm was used to optimize wear parameters, resulting in an optimal configuration \(Speed = 556\.47 RPM, Load = 29\.92 N, Time = 85\.59 min, Track Diameter = 25\.57 mm\), which resulted in a predicted wear value of 92\.4 microns\. 3D surface plots and heatmaps revealed nonlinear interactions between the parameters, with speed and load being the major influencing parameters\. Microstructural characterization of the selected samples and optimized run revealed transitions in wear mechanisms\. An integrated analytical framework was developed where multi\-objective optimization is combined with multidimensional parameter sensitivity and thermodynamic energy\-flow modelling, which mapped complex input\-output relations resulting in a unified P\.V \(Contact pressure vs Sliding Velocity\) phase map that clearly delineates distinct wear regimes using a non\-dimensional Severity Index\. These findings provide a comprehensive framework for predictive wear analysis that can be employed on conventional materials used for aerospace applications\.

## [Promising Directions for Sorting Seeds of Various Crops: Improving Electric Field Methods and Integrating Them with Modern Sensor Technologies](../publications/acc0bb46f5da12c0bc1e.md)

Usmonov Inomjon Isroilovich; Abdusattorov Axadjon Ortiqali o‘g‘li

Improving the germination capacity, purity, and uniformity of seed lots is a key task in seed production, yet pneumatic and mechanical sorting rely on only one or two physical traits, mass or size\. This article reviews electric field sorting of agricultural seeds as an alternative that acts on several properties at once: mass, shape, density, electrical resistance, and dielectric permittivity\. Published studies show that corona\-discharge separation can improve seed purity and raise barley germination by 17\.34%, and that an electrostatic separator can remove plastic film residue from seed cotton at up to 96\.8% efficiency\. Analysis of existing devices identifies a main limitation: electrode geometry is not matched to seed shape\. To address this, a universal sorting device is proposed, with a polyethylene working body carrying screw\-shaped channels and oppositely charged electrodes of triangular cross\-section\. Further directions are outlined: a hybrid electro\-optical system combining electric field sorting with NIR/AI sensing, adaptive voltage control based on seed moisture, application to cotton seed cleaning, and sensor\-based energy management\. The proposed device and these directions are conceptual and still need experimental and numerical validation, for example by finite element modeling of the electric field\.

## [Tiran, Noam: AI Sycophancy, Self\-interpretation, and Coversational Contentment](../publications/acc8029ecddff699f64b.md)



\_AI and Ethics\_ 6\. 2026AI sycophancy is often conceptualized as a chatbot’s tendency to flout truth, accuracy, or other epistemic standards to shield users from hurt feelings, or otherwise protect them from the consequences of their thoughts, words, or actions\. In this paper, I argue against this conception\. That is, I argue that sycophantic AI behavior does not necessarily aim to protect users, nor that its harms are essentially epistemic\. There are highly prevalent cases in which sycophantic AI chatbots actively contribute to their users’ knowledge\. One class of such examples involves cases in which chatbots are used as auto\-hermeneutic technologies—as tools to facilitate the user’s interpretation of her own cares, concerns, values, and other identity components and life events\. In these cases, LLMs can help articulate the user’s avowed self\-interpretations\. In turn, avowals of these interpretations by users can often have downstream effects that render the interpretations true\. If this is correct, then LLMs can often advance the user’s knowledge regarding important truths about herself\. Simultaneously, as I explain, interpretations offered by LLMs may be deeply harmful\. This understanding of AI sycophancy can help us clarify what is so disturbing about it, as well as resist the temptation to draw too tight an analogy between sycophantic behaviors in AI systems and in humans\. \(direct link \)

## [The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery](../publications/acde065ce43b2348cd72.md)

Xiaofang Liu; Haifeng Wen; Tengyu Wang; Hao Liu; Mingming Xie; Yajie Luo; Luchao Zuo; Chunxia Liu; Dong Zhou; Wenlong Wang

Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security\. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations\. These include the time\-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine\-induced immunity with serological tests\. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild\-type strains via genotyping methods\. Furthermore, current practice relies on manual reporting and empirical judgment without real\-time data support\. Consequently, these challenges could hinder early detection and reduce the efficiency of large\-scale screening, which leads to imprecise outbreak tracing and fails to meet the practical demands of modern livestock production for rapid diagnosis, intelligent prevention and control\. In recent years, artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) technologies have been widely applied in the field of veterinary microbiology, which could offer novel technical pathways for the prevention and control of brucellosis\. This paper reviews the latest research progress in the application of AI for the rapid diagnosis of brucellosis, genomic analysis and antimicrobial resistance prediction of Brucella, epidemiological risk early warning and the development of drugs and vaccines\. We further analyze the current limitations of AI in brucellosis research including the scarcity of high\-quality, annotated datasets, insufficient model interpretability and low efficiency in on\-site translation and implementation\. The paper provides an outlook on the future development of AI\-based intelligent prevention and control systems for brucellosis, which offer a theoretical reference and innovative perspectives for the fundamental research and clinical application of AI technologies\. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first review to integrate AI applications across the entire chain of brucellosis prevention and control and to propose a conceptual framework for AI\-driven intelligent brucellosis management\.

## [PENGARUH CITA RASA, VARIASI RASA, DAN HARGA TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN KOPI KELILING JAGO DI JALAN GURU MUGHNI JAKARTA SELATAN](../publications/ace11c57cae043819bde.md)

Mahrizal; Hidayat Syah; Wanda Yulia Utami; Mahrizal

This study aims to determine the effect of taste, flavor variety, and price on purchasing decisions for Kopi Keliling Jago on Jalan Guru Mughni, South Jakarta\. This study employed a quantitative approach involving 95 respondents\. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS 25\. The results showed that, partially, taste had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0\.267, a t\-value of 2\.204, and a significance value of 0\.030\. Flavor variety also had a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0\.449, a t\-value of 4\.411, and a significance value of 0\.000\. Price had a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0\.267, a t\-value of 3\.212, and a significance value of 0\.003\. Simultaneously, taste, flavor variety, and price had a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with an F\-value of 16\.395 and a significance value of 0\.000\. Therefore, improving taste quality, providing greater flavor variety, and offering appropriate prices can increase consumers’ purchasing decisions for Kopi Keliling Jago\.

## [Understanding and Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Models: A Systematic Survey of Mechanisms, Detection Paradigms, and Architectural Defenses](../publications/ace5a9921b542bba8ad4.md)

Anoopraj Verma

Large Language Models \(LLMs\) based on the autoregressive Transformer architecture have achieved remarkable empirical capabilities across open\-domain dialogue, reasoning, code synthesis, and analytical tasks\. Despite these milestones, their operational deployment in high\-stakes settings—such as clinical informatics, jurisprudence, and autonomous systems—remains bottlenecked by hallucination: the generation of fluent, syntactically coherent text that is factually erroneous, unfaithful to provided source material, or entirely fabricated\. This survey provides a comprehensive, rigorous synthesis of the LLM hallucination phenomenon\. We formalize the taxonomy of hallucinations, distinguishing between factuality violations and context\-faithfulness discrepancies\. We investigate the underlying computational and statistical etiology of hallucinations across data pipelines, objective functions, representational bottlenecks, and decoding dynamics\. Furthermore, we systematically categorize contemporary detection paradigms—ranging from internal activation probing and semantic entropy estimation to external verification networks—and examine defense strategies spanning Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\), internal representation steering, contrastive decoding, and alignment algorithms\. Finally, we highlight unresolved challenges across multimodal models and propose actionable frontiers for achieving epistemically grounded artificial intelligence\.

## [Integrasi Naive Bayes dan ArcGIS untuk Penentuan Prioritas Mustahik Zakat di LAZISMU Sumatera Utara](../publications/ace9d04fed44d0e22c29.md)

Mhd\. Arkan Mufadhal; Firahmi Rizky

Pengelolaan distribusi zakat yang akurat dan tepat sasaran merupakan tantangan bagi lembaga amil zakat, salah satunya LAZISMU Sumatera Utara\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem penentuan prioritas mustahik zakat menggunakan algoritma Naive Bayes yang diintegrasikan dengan visualisasi spasial berbasis ArcGIS\. Data yang digunakan adalah data mustahik LAZISMU Sumatera Utara periode 2022–2024 sebanyak 500 sampel dengan atribut pendapatan bulanan, jumlah tanggungan, kondisi tempat tinggal, dan ketidakmampuan bekerja\. Discretisasi diterapkan pada fitur numerik sebelum proses klasifikasi, dan Laplace Smoothing digunakan untuk mengatasi kemungkinan zero\-probability\. Evaluasi model menggunakan confusion matrix menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 92,00%, presisi 92,47%, recall 98,85%, dan F1\-Score 95,56%\. Sistem kemudian diintegrasikan dengan ArcGIS untuk menghasilkan peta persebaran mustahik dan peta kerapatan \(kernel density\) per kecamatan di kota Medan, yang mempermudah pengambilan keputusan berbasis wilayah\. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi Naive Bayes dan GIS mampu meningkatkan efektivitas dan transparansi distribusi zakat, serta dapat menjadi referensi bagi lembaga amil zakat lain dalam mengoptimalkan pengelolaan data mustahik\.

## [Research on Performance Evaluation of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem in Universities Under the Background of Internet Education](../publications/acf325871d4d9583ae6f.md)

Qinjue Kang; Fenglin Yan

Some universities in the world have successfully implemented innovation and entrepreneurship education, but there is still a lack of exploration on the innovation and entrepreneurship education system in higher education institutions\. This article uses the factor grouping method, theoretical analysis method, and Delphi method to construct a comprehensive evaluation index system\. Then, using the analytic hierarchy process, it calculates the weight coefficients of each indicator in the comprehensive evaluation index system\. By analyzing the advantages, heterogeneity, and rational allocation ratio of original ecological resources in the ecosystem, the authors gradually promote the application of innovation and the entrepreneurship education ecosystem\. This study indicates that the ecological environment for college students&\#x27; innovation and entrepreneurship urgently needs to establish a model for college students&\#x27; innovation and entrepreneurship and provide effective guidance for college students&\#x27; innovation and entrepreneurship in multiple aspects\.

## [The Geo Ai Revolution: The Future of Geography in The Age of Artificial Intelligence](../publications/acfb02537c96930056dc.md)

Manoj Chouhan; Suresh Awase

Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence with geospatial technology has given rise to Geospatial Artificial Intelligence \(GeoAI\), fundamentally altering how geographical information is produced, analyzed, and applied\. This paper examines whether GeoAI functions merely as an advanced analytical toolkit or constitutes a structural paradigm shift in spatial knowledge generation\. Through a systematic literature synthesis, analytical scenario modeling, and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that Geography is transitioning from a human\-driven descriptive field to a continuously computational, multimodal, and semi\-autonomous spatial intelligence system\. The development of geospatial foundation models \(GeoFMs\), autonomous GIS agents, and Earth digital twins signals a movement toward AI\-native geographical workflows\. To conceptualize this transformation, we propose the GeoAI Transformation of Geographical Intelligence Framework \(GT\-GIF\)\. Looking toward 2050, the discipline may shift toward continuous Planetary Geographical Intelligence\. However, human contextual reasoning, ethical oversight, fieldwork, and critical interpretation remain vital safeguards\. Finally, the paper addresses the Global South perspective specifically focusing on India, by examining risks such as spatial bias, surveillance, and algorithmic colonialism alongside opportunities for climate resilience and sustainable development\.

## [Epigenetic regulation of the transcriptional activity of genes mediating the neuroprotective activity of ceftriaxone in the brain in a rat model of sporadic Alzheimer disease: the involvement of histone deacetylase 1](../publications/ad0dc97e429df1768ab5.md)

A\. A\. Bashirzade; Maria A\. Tikhonova; В\. М\. Беличенко; Larisa A\. Fedoseeva; M\. D\. Belyaev; T\.\-Y\. Renn; H\.\-M\. Chang; Nataliya G\. Kolosova; N\. D\. Belyaev; T\. G\. Amstislavska

Histone deacetylases \(HDACs\) are enzymes that provide transcriptional repression, while HDAC inhibitors are considered to be potential drugs in the treatment of Alzheimer disease \(AD\)\. Earlier we found that ceftriaxone \(CEF\), an antibiotic with neuroprotective activity, augmented mRNA levels of Ide and Mme , encoding enzymes involved in the catabolism of amyloid beta in the amygdala of OXYS rats, a model of sporadic AD\. On the other hand, disturbances of neurotrophic factors \(BDNF in particular\) play an important role in AD pathogenesis\. Moreover, HDACs of class I \(HDAC1\) are involved in the regulation of Bdnf transcriptional activity\. The study was aimed to assess the effects of CEF on HDAC1 enrichment at Mme , Ide , and Bdnf gene promoters in the amygdala of OXYS rats and on Bdnf mRNA levels in the amygdala of OXYS and Wistar rats\. Chromatin immunoprecipitation and qPCR were utilized for epigenetic analysis and assay of Bdnf mRNA levels, respectively\. Neither significant HDAC1 enrichment, nor its alteration under CEF treatment at the Mme or Ide promoters were found, whereas CEF attenuated HDAC1 binding at Bdnf promoter IV\. This is a novel mechanism of transcription regulation by CEF in the brain, which may be involved in its neuroprotective activity\. In 5\-month\-old OXYS rats, it seems to play a minor role, as CEF did not change Bdnf transcript 5 \(containing exons IV and IX\) levels\. We were first to demonstrate the transcript\-specific regulation of Bdnf transcription by CEF\. CEF significantly increased the levels of Bdnf transcript 6 \(containing exons VII, VIII, and IX\)\. The results of our study can be taken into account in AD treatment\.

Accurate dynamical mass estimates of galaxy clusters are essential for studies of cluster formation and evolution and for cosmological applications\. We developed a probabilistic deep\-learning framework for cluster member identification and dynamical mass estimation and tested the sensitivity of the inferred masses to cluster miscentring and radially dependent incompleteness in controlled mock experiments\. We used mock galaxy cluster catalogues to train a two\-stage model\. In this model, a long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) network assigns membership probabilities to galaxies arranged by projected phase\-space proximity\. ## [Pyrolysis of Pinus roxburghii: process optimization, product characterization and scale\-up potential](../publications/ad1a44fca5a562468f88.md)

Madhuka Roy; Sayon Chakravarty; Brij Kishore; Krishnendu Kundu

The growing accumulation of Pinus roxburghii needles in the Indian Himalayan region presents both a significant fire hazard and an underutilized biomass resource\. This study investigates the conversion of pine needles into bio\-oil and biochar through bench\-scale pyrolysis, with process optimization using Response Surface Methodology \(RSM\)\. In contrast to previous studies largely limited to laboratory\-scale investigations, this work demonstrates the scale\-up potential of pine needle pyrolysis and provides data relevant to its practical deployment\. Product characterization confirmed the successful conversion of pine needles into value\-added products, with biochar exhibiting enhanced carbon\-rich properties and bio\-oil containing diverse organic compounds\. The findings not only validate RSM as a robust optimization tool for scale\-up but also highlight the potential of pine needle pyrolysis products for renewable energy, carbon sequestration and environmental applications\. By converting a fire\-prone forest residue into valuable bioenergy products, this study contributes to sustainable biomass valorization and forest fire risk mitigation\.

## [A Self‐Sustained System for Producing Green Hydrogen via Moisture Power](../publications/ad1ce792da991c1e07d5.md)

Zhenglin Wang; Jianning Lv; Xiaojun He; Xiangyang Li; Zifeng Jin; Lanmin Qiao; Hui Zhang; Nan Chen

ABSTRACT We report a self‐sustaining system that directly converts atmospheric moisture into green hydrogen, eliminating reliance on intermittent renewables and liquid water sources\. The core of the system is a multifunctional hydrogel device that integrates moisture‐enabled electricity generation, atmospheric water harvesting, and electrolysis into a seamless operation\. Concerted ion diffusion and active electrode chemistry in the gel yield a stable power output of 1\.87 V and 450 μA cm −2 , while its hygroscopic components capture water at 1\.318 g g −1 \. The harvested water and electricity are used in situ to drive efficient overall water splitting at 1\.50 V, catalyzed by a Mo‐FeNi 3 /NiFe 2 O 4 heterostructure catalyst, producing hydrogen at a rate of 2\.6 μmol g PPM −1 per cycle\. This integrated “moisture‐to‐hydrogen” paradigm offers a scalable, off‐grid solution for continuous and carbon‐neutral hydrogen production\.

## [Hyper\-Personalization Berbasis AI Agents: Dampaknya Terhadap Loyalitas Konsumen Generasi Z Dan Milenial Di E\-Commerce Indonesia](../publications/ad3c80c8114d792ad836.md)

Wiwin Riski Windarsari; Hery Maulana Arif

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi pengalaman Generasi Z dan Milenial terhadap hyper\-personalization berbasis AI agents dalam e\-commerce Indonesia serta memahami bagaimana pengalaman tersebut membentuk loyalitas konsumen\. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif fenomenologis dengan wawancara semi\-terstruktur terhadap konsumen Gen Z dan Milenial yang aktif menggunakan platform e\-commerce atau social commerce\. Data dianalisis menggunakan thematic analysis untuk mengidentifikasi pola pengalaman, persepsi, dan respons emosional konsumen terhadap rekomendasi personal, chatbot, promosi otomatis, dan interaksi berbasis algoritma\. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa hyper\-personalization berbasis AI agents dapat memperkuat loyalitas ketika konsumen memersepsikannya sebagai relevan, membantu, responsif, dan dapat dipercaya\. Personalisasi mampu mengurangi upaya pencarian, meningkatkan efisiensi belanja, serta mendorong keterikatan berulang dengan platform\. Namun, loyalitas tidak terbentuk secara otomatis karena konsumen juga menghadapi ambivalensi algoritmik, terutama terkait privasi, transparansi data, dan perasaan diawasi oleh sistem\. Ketika personalisasi dianggap terlalu intensif, invasif, atau manipulatif, kepercayaan konsumen dapat melemah\. Studi ini menegaskan bahwa loyalitas dalam e\-commerce berbasis AI merupakan hasil dari negosiasi antara manfaat personalisasi, kepercayaan algoritmik, pengalaman emosional, persepsi kontrol, dan kekhawatiran privasi\. Implikasi praktisnya, platform e\-commerce perlu merancang AI agents yang relevan, transparan, etis, dan tetap memberi ruang kendali bagi konsumen\.

## [“Epistemology” and “gnoseology”: the origin of the terms](../publications/ad55f48eebefd9c7d6b6.md)

А\. М\. Кардаш; Кардаш Алексей Михайлович

В статье рассматривается происхождение терминов «эпистемология» и «гносеология»\. Показывается, что термин «эпистемология» был введен в 1854 г\. шотландским философом Джеймсом Фредериком Ферриером, и уже через 40 лет англоязычные философы использовали термин, не упоминая его автора\. После появления когнитивной науки в 1950\-х гг\. и эпистемологического бума 1960\-х гг\. «эпистемология» стала общепринятым названием для теории познания в мировой философии\. В русскоязычной философии термин «эпистемология» иногда употребляется параллельно с термином «гносеология»\. Автором приводятся данные, согласно которым на русском написано про гносеологию больше текстов, чем на немецком и английском языках суммарно\. При этом история и происхождение термина оставались до настоящего времени непроясненными\. Показывается, что наиболее вероятным автором термина «гносеология» является Александр Готлиб Баумгартен, впервые употребивший это слово в 1739 г\. Одновременно с этим подчеркивается историко\-философская сложность, связанная с тем, что Баумгартен придумал «гносеологию», когда в употреблении у немецких мыслителей уже был термин «гностология», имевший схожее значение\. Выдвигается гипотеза о том, что хотя «эпистемология» и «гносеология» появились в разных интеллектуальных контекстах, у нас есть основание считать, что появление обоих терминов является последствием когнитивного поворота в философии эпохи Возрождения\.

## [Look Back, Correct Forward: Error Feedback Calibration for Time Series Forecasting](../publications/ad63cfd769f9c509272a.md)

Haonan Yang; Yulin He; Zhuo Li

Time series forecasting models are increasingly deployed in continuously evolving environments\. After a forecast is issued, future observations gradually arrive and reveal how the model has failed\. Existing methods mainly treat such observations as supervision for parameter updates\. However, it remains unclear whether verified forecasting errors can themselves provide causal feedback for correcting future predictions\. To address this, we introduce Error Feedback Calibration \(EFC\), a fully test\-time framework for deterministic post\-hoc correction of time series forecasting\. EFC constructs a Causal Error Diagonal \(CED\) from revealed errors of overlapping historical forecasts, providing a fresh view of the frozen forecaster&\#x27;s recent failure behavior\. Then Cumulative Error Transport \(CET\) maps this error state to future residuals using cumulative estimation, while temporal out\-of\-sample validation controls the correction strength\. Temporal Residual Learning \(TRL\) further predicts only the residual structure left after CET from recent CED trajectories, rather than relearning the entire forecasting error\. Extensive experiments across forecasting backbones and datasets show that EFC broadly improves forecasting performance while substantially controlling harmful over correction\.

## [Advanced Computing R\+D\+i Statement in LAC SCALAC \- Position Paper](../publications/ad654890a797fb485e1d.md)

Carlos Barrios\-Hernandez

This position paper, presented by the Advanced Computing System for Latin America and the Caribbean \(SCALAC\) to the CELAC and ECLAC forums, outlines a strategic roadmap to bridge the region&\#x27;s technological divide\. It advocates for the urgent transition of Latin America and the Caribbean from passive technology consumers to active creators of sovereign, sustainable, and impactful digital solutions\. By emphasizing infrastructure integration, human capacity building, and &\#x27;mindful computing&\#x27; principles across High\-Performance Computing \(HPC\), Quantum Computing \(QC\), and Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), SCALAC proposes a collaborative framework\. Key recommendations include securing institutional endorsement for SCALAC, leveraging the CARLA conference and other non\-profit divulgation activities for regional outreach, and establishing framework cooperation agreements to ensure equitable access to supercomputing resources, thereby fostering long\-term scientific and economic sovereignty in the region\.

## [Q\($γ\_H$\): Entropy\-Guided Horizon Mixing in Multi\-Discount Q\-Learning](../publications/ad753f6a57a59e342805.md)

Arwa Albelaihi; Abdulrahman Altahhan

A fixed discount factor in Q\-learning imposes a single planning horizon throughout training, despite the differing demands of early exploration and long\-term credit assignment\. We propose Q\($γ\_H$\), a multi\-horizon Q\-learning framework that maintains multiple discount\-specific heads and adaptively combines them at control time using an entropy\-derived confidence signal\. The resulting state\-dependent mixing weights shift control from shorter\- to longer\-horizon heads as policy confidence increases, enabling adaptive horizon mixing without modifying individual Bellman updates\. Across classical control and deep reinforcement\-learning benchmarks, Q\($γ\_H$\) shows its strongest improvements on delayed\-credit tasks relative to strong fixed\-discount baselines\. By decoupling horizon adaptation from the underlying learning updates, Q\($γ\_H$\) provides a lightweight framework for adaptive planning\-horizon control in reinforcement learning, avoiding the need for manual discount\-factor selection while remaining compatible with standard value\-learning methods\.

## [Interpretable Symbolic Regression Modelling of Stacking Sequence Effects in Jute/Ramie and Jute/Flax Hybrid Composites](../publications/ad75976429ac8214a689.md)

Serkan Batı

In this study, a symbolic regression\-based framework was developed to investigate the tensile and flexural behavior of natural fiber\-reinforced hybrid composites with different stacking sequences\. Experimental data from eleven six\-layer laminates, including jute, ramie, flax, jute/ramie, and jute/flax configurations, were reanalyzed\. Due to the limited dataset size, the proposed approach was considered an exploratory and interpretable modelling framework rather than a universal predictive model\. Fifteen descriptors related to fiber position, interlayer contacts, fiber weight fractions, and density were defined to analytically represent laminate architectures\. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were first performed, followed by symbolic regression modelling using HeuristicLab to derive interpretable expressions for tensile and flexural strength\. The results indicated that ramie\-related parameters generally showed positive relationships with mechanical performance, while the symbolic regression models highlighted the potential importance of flax fibers in the outer layers, jute fibers in the core region, and ramie–ramie contact density\. The obtained models showed satisfactory agreement with the available experimental data; however, their interpretation should be limited to the investigated laminate configurations\. Therefore, the obtained expressions are not intended as universal predictive equations, but as data\-driven analytical representations that may help interpret the influence of stacking sequence on the mechanical behavior of hybrid composite laminates\. The proposed framework may serve as an example for future studies aiming to establish interpretable relationships between laminate architecture and mechanical performance using larger and more diverse datasets\.

## [Outcome of percutaneous peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion](../publications/ad7cd4cb693e116b9d1c.md)

Khalfan Salim AlShaaili; Hanaa Mohammed Eid El Sayed; Samira Sulaiman Alsaeghi; Adil Ali Alsulaimi; Khalid Salim Al\-Rawahi; Sultan Ali Al\-Busaidi

Objectives: Peritoneal dialysis \(PD\) is an effective home\-based renal replacement therapy for patients with end\-stage renal disease \(ESRD\)\. However, timely and safe catheter insertion remains a barrier to its widespread adoption\. Percutaneous PD catheter insertion by nephrologists has emerged as a safe alternative to surgical techniques\. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes and safety of nephrologist\-performed percutaneous PD catheter insertion using a combined ultrasound and fluoroscopy\-guided approach at a regional hospital in Oman\. Material and Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Nephrology Department, Nizwa Hospital, Sultanate of Oman, between September 2022 and December 2025\. All consecutive adult patients with ESRD who underwent percutaneous PD catheter insertion by the trained nephrology team were included\. Procedures were performed under local anesthesia using ultrasound for abdominal wall assessment and fluoroscopy with contrast to confirm intraperitoneal placement\. The study evaluated technical success and early procedural and post\-insertion complications; 1\-year catheter survival, transfer to hemodialysis, and late catheter revision were outside its scope\. Results: A total of 79 patients \(60\.8% male, mean age 56\.8 ± 16\.6 years\) underwent percutaneous PD catheter insertion\. The success rate was 88\.6% \(70/79; 95% confidence interval: 79\.5–94\.2%\)\. No bowel perforation occurred\. The most common causes of failure were preperitoneal placement \(33\.3%\) and surgical adhesions \(33\.3%\)\. Early leakage was the most frequent mechanical complication \(7\.6%\)\. Prophylactic antibiotics were administered in 100% of patients\. Early peritonitis occurred in 1 patient \(1\.3%\) and exit site infections in 3 patients \(3\.8%\)\. Pseudomonas aeruginosa was the most common organism \(2 cases\)\. Failure of insertion decreased from 15\.0% in the first 40 insertions to 7\.7% in the last 39 insertions\. Urgent\-start PD \(53\.2% of patients\) was associated with higher early leakage \(11\.9% vs\. 2\.7%\)\. Conclusion: Percutaneous PD catheter insertion by nephrologists using image guidance is safe and effective, with improving outcomes over time\. Urgent\-start PD is feasible but requires caution due to higher leakage risk\.

## [Modern Techniques in Computer Vision](../publications/ad8c9381a7ba59eb012b.md)

Kanthali Harshada, Mr\. A\. A\. Dalvi, Prof\. J\. R\. Mahajan

Computer vision enables computer systems to extract useful meaning from images and video\. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have improved the ability of machines to recognise objects, interpret scenes, and identify visual patterns\. This paper presents a structured review of AI techniques used in computer vision, with emphasis on convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\), their main processing stages, practical applications, and continuing limitations\. It explains why manually designed visual features can be unreliable when images vary in lighting, scale, viewpoint, or background, and how learned representations help address these problems\. Applications in healthcare, transportation, astronomy, and industrial inspection are discussed alongside concerns involving data quality, bias, privacy, explainability, and computational cost\. The paper is a conceptual review based on established literature and does not claim a new experiment or measured performance result\. It concludes that responsible deployment requires not only accurate models, but also representative data, careful evaluation, human oversight, and monitoring after deployment

## [T cell–driven venetoclax resistance in chronic lymphocytic leukemia: in vivo preclinical activity of opaganib](../publications/ad9373a35d1df7f67b14.md)

Valeria Judith Sarapura Martínez; Paula S\. Pérez; Anita Ng; Yu\-Ju Chen; Kelly Wong; Chiara Cassarino; Rosario Custidiano; Carolina Valeria Mahuad; Miguel Arturo Pavlovsky; Raimundo Fernando Bezares; Martin Bertini; Mercedes Borge; Monica Elba Vermeulen; Pablo Elías Morande; Mirta Giordano; Matías Ostrowski; Nicholas Chiorazzi; Shih‐Shih Chen; Romina Gamberale

Introduction Venetoclax has transformed the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia \(CLL\), yet therapeutic resistance remains a major clinical challenge\. In addition to leukemia cell\-intrinsic mechanisms, interactions with the immune microenvironment can profoundly reduce venetoclax sensitivity\. We previously identified sphingosine kinase 2 \(SPHK2\) as a therapeutic vulnerability underlying T\-cell\-supported venetoclax resistance\. Here, we investigated the contribution of CD4 \+ and CD8 \+ T cell subsets and their extracellular vesicles \(EVs\) to this resistant phenotype and evaluated the therapeutic activity of the SPHK2 inhibitor opaganib in vivo \. Methods We evaluated the role of activated CD4 \+ and CD8 \+ T cells and their EVs in the development of the venetoclax\-resistant phenotype in primary CLL cells\. The in vivo activity of opaganib was assessed in a xenograft model generated by co\-engraftment of primary CLL cells with autologous activated T cells\. Mice were treated with venetoclax, opaganib, or their combination, and leukemic burden and the T cell compartment were evaluated\. Anti\-apoptotic BCL\-2 family proteins were also assessed in residual leukemic cells\. Results Activated CD4 \+ , but not CD8 \+ , T cells induced leukemic cell activation and venetoclax resistance, and CD4 \+ T cell\-derived EVs were sufficient to reproduce this phenotype\. In vivo , venetoclax monotherapy failed to reduce leukemic burden, confirming that adaptive interactions with the immune microenvironment are sufficient to sustain therapeutic resistance\. Although opaganib alone showed minimal antileukemic activity, its combination with venetoclax reduced splenic leukemic burden by approximately 50% and remodeled the tumor\-associated T\-cell compartment, without consistent modulation of anti\-apoptotic BCL\-2 family proteins in residual leukemic cells\. Discussion These findings are consistent with the notion that the therapeutic effects of opaganib extend beyond leukemic\-cell\-intrinsic mechanisms and may include modulation of the immune microenvironment\. Our study shows that opaganib reduces microenvironment\-driven venetoclax resistance in a preclinical CLL model in vivo , supporting its clinical evaluation in combination with BCL\-2 inhibition\.

## [Exploring the cross\-task transferability of an automated scoring model for discourse completion tasks in relation to learner perceptions](../publications/ad957084914dc04fb69c.md)

Yuko Hayashi; Yusuke Kondo; Yutaka Ishii

As automated scoring systems are increasingly integrated into technology\-mediated speaking practice and assessment, ensuring generalisability and construct alignment across tasks remains a critical challenge, particularly in discourse\-based contexts\. This study examined cross\-task transferability by applying an automated scoring model originally developed for multi\-turn discourse completion tasks \(DCTs\)\. While prior work demonstrated moderate agreement between human and machine scores within a single task, it remains unclear whether such models maintain reliability when applied to discourse tasks that elicit different linguistic and semantic demands\. Using responses from 116 undergraduate EFL learners, the existing random\-forest\-based model was applied to two oral DCTs without task\-specific retraining\. Human–machine agreement was examined using multiple agreement indices and confusion matrices, followed by lexical, keyword\-based, and regression analyses of learner responses, along with a descriptive analysis of learner perceptions for system evaluation\. Results showed high human–human agreement across both tasks, whereas human–machine agreement was considerably stronger for DCT1 than for DCT2\. Although task\-relevant semantic features were associated with both human and automated scores, particularly for academic\-related content in DCT2, confusion matrices and transcript inspection indicated that the automated model did not adequately capture discourse\-level relationships reflected in holistic human scoring\. These findings suggest that limited cross\-task transferability cannot be attributed simply to insensitivity to task\-relevant semantic content but may instead reflect broader challenges in representing discourse contingency within multi\-turn interactions\. At the same time, learners generally evaluated the automated feedback positively, although positive perceptions should not be taken as evidence of scoring validity\. Taken together, the findings highlight the need for greater construct alignment in cross\-task automated scoring and point to the potential role of such systems as learning\-support tools, rather than fully reliable assessment instruments, in technology\-enhanced language learning environments\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: SN07 — Collective Cognition and Centropy\-Forward Social Architecture: Structural Dynamics of Social Fields at the Embodiment Band](../publications/ad965bee3f1abebce6b1.md)



Collective Cognition and Centropy\-Forward Social Architecture examines participant\-composed social fields at the embodiment band\. Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience\. The volume extends cognitive cost and recovery analysis to collective orientation, membrane dynamics, coherence budgets and the conditions of centropy\-forward social life\. The Non\-fusion Axiom preserves each participant&\#x27;s sovereign distinction, while systemic orientation concerns recurrent enacted patterns rather than an average of individual essential inclinations\. ## [Curriculum Management and Pedagogical Content Knowledge Development: Mentor Teachers’ Perspectives on Accounting Work\-Integrated Learning](../publications/ad98048acca25c241997.md)

Radhakrishnan Nair

This study explored mentor teachers&\#x27; perceptions of the teacher education curriculum&\#x27;s role in developing Accounting student\-teachers&\#x27; Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(PCK\) during Work\-Integrated Learning \(WIL\)\. The study used an interpretivist qualitative case study design in seven secondary schools in the OR Tambo Inland Education District, South Africa\. The study collected data from seven purposively selected Accounting mentor teachers through semi\-structured written responses and analyzed them using data condensation, data display, conclusion drawing, and verification\. The findings show that micro\-teaching, guided lesson planning, school\-based practice, feedback, reflection, and authentic classroom engagement consistently supported curriculum\-mediated PCK development\. However, gaps in Accounting content knowledge, limited practical exposure, inadequate resources, classroom\-management challenges, and contextual constraints hindered PCK development\. The study concludes that Accounting PCK develops through integrating disciplinary knowledge, subject\-specific pedagogy, WIL, mentoring, reflection, and contextual adaptation across contexts\. The study implies that teacher education programs should strengthen Accounting content preparation, extend structured teaching practice, enhance mentor lecturer collaboration, provide contextualized learning experiences, and better prepare student\-teachers for rural and resource\-constrained classrooms\.

## [Improving snow simulations through improved representations of vegetation conditions: insights from high resolution simulations over California](../publications/ad991340f1d346a99700.md)

Aniket Gupta; Ali Behrangi; Mohammad Farmani; P\. D\. Broxton; Guo‐Yue Niu

Abstract\. Most hydrological models underestimate snow water equivalent \(SWE\) in the mountainous western US\. Key limitations may be due to coarse resolution precipitation input and inadequate representations of snow\-vegetation interactions\. Vegetation affects snow dynamics through snow interception, throughfall/unloading, and energy transfer through the canopy, yet basin\-scale studies on the vegetation effects are limited\. To address this issue, we applied the Noah\-MP version 5\.0 with a dynamic vegetation module to the Sacramento and San Joaquin River Basins in California at 1 km resolution driven by forcing from Analysis of Record for Calibration \(AORC\) and NLDAS\-2, downscaled to 1 km using the WRF\-Hydro Meteorological Forcing Engine\. We carried out eight model experiments driven by the two forcing datasets and two vegetation schemes over the two Basins\. Compared to 4 km PRISM and 1 km AORC, the downscaled 1 km NLDAS\-2 forcing data shows higher precipitation and lower temperatures over the mountains, resulting in more snowfall and SWE, which is more consistent with in\-situ SWE observations\. Using the 1\-km NLDAS\-2 forcing, the default vegetation scheme with prescribed leaf area index \(LAI\) and vegetation cover fraction produces too much SWE on the ground due mainly to the strong canopy shading effect despite more snow intercepted by the canopy\. The dynamic vegetation module produces smaller LAI than the prescribed \(more consistent with MODIS data\) and thus leads to more shortwave radiation reaching the snow surface, thereby enhancing episodic melting during the accumulation season\. Validation against in\-situ snow data suggests that the use of dynamic vegetation model and the downscaled NLDAS\-2 data performs the best\. These findings highlight the importance of vegetation effects and downscaling of atmospheric forcing to increase the accuracy of snow modeling over the Southwest US\.

## [THE AI AGE How Artificial Intelligence is Transforming humanity](../publications/ad9b4fd310f6f790a287.md)

Shehu Ibrahim

Nigeria has 350 government schools where a single teacher taught math to five different skill levels at once — until an AI tutor helped push the district&\#x27;s pass rate to 96\.4 percent in six weeks\. A radiologist in Scotland caught a six\-millimeter tumor that human eyes alone had missed\. A smallholder farmer in Kenya saved his maize crop by pointing his phone at a leaf\. None of these are science fiction\. They happened in the last three years\.THE AI AGE is the book for anyone who wants to understand what artificial intelligence is actually doing to the world right now not the hype, not the panic, but the real, documented transformation already underway across medicine, education, work, government, and daily life\.Shehu Ibrahim traces the full arc: from the ancient dream of thinking machines, through decades of AI winters and quiet breakthroughs, to the sudden acceleration that produced ChatGPT, AlphaFold, and a global race for AI supremacy\. Then he turns to the questions that matter most for the next fifty years — who wins, who is left behind, and what humanity owes itself as it builds something smarter than any tool it has ever made\.This is not a Silicon Valley book\. It is a genuinely global one — grounded as much in Kenyan farms, Rajasthani classrooms, and Nigerian newsrooms as in California labs, written by an author whose own path from rural northern Nigeria into technology mirrors the book&\#x27;s central argument: that this technology&\#x27;s benefits must reach everyone, not just those already closest to power\.Inside, you&\#x27;ll find:• The real history of AI, from Ada Lovelace&\#x27;s first program to the deep learning breakthrough of 2012• How AI is already reshaping healthcare, education, work, business, and government — with real numbers and real case studies• A clear\-eyed account of the global AI race between the US, China, and the rest of the world• Africa&\#x27;s emerging role in the AI revolution — leapfrogging opportunities most global coverage ignores• An honest reckoning with AI&\#x27;s risks: job disruption, inequality, misinformation, and long\-horizon questions• What AI means for human identity, creativity, and authorship• Two grounded scenarios for the world in 2050 and 2100• A final chapter on the choice still in front of usWritten for citizens, not specialists, THE AI AGE is a comprehensive, research\-driven guide to the most consequential technological shift of our time\.If you want to understand artificial intelligence&\#x27;s history, its present reach, and its stakes for your own future, This is the BOOK \!\!\!\.

## [Manajemen Implementasi Kurikulum Berbasis Cinta dalam Pembelajaran Bahasa Arab di MI Dakwatul Khoiriyah Banyuwangi](../publications/ad9e06f236f3e5c67b07.md)

## [Design of a Web\-Based Medical Record Correspondence Information System with an Audit Trail Feature at Dustira Level II Hospital](../publications/ada064e8e742db57c3d4.md)

Nasthea Hidayati; Falaah Abdussalaam; Irda Sari

Medical record correspondence management at Dustira Level II Hospital is still carried out through processes that are not yet optimal, particularly in recording user activities, so monitoring, tracking data changes, and supervising medical record document management have not been effective\. This study aimed to design a web\-based Medical Record Correspondence Information System equipped with an Audit Trail feature to support more structured, secure, and accountable management of medical record correspondence\. A descriptive qualitative approach was used, with data collected through observation, interviews, and documentation studies\. System development employed the Waterfall method, consisting of requirements analysis, system design, program coding, testing, and maintenance\. The system was developed using PHP and MySQL and designed using a flowmap, context diagram, Data Flow Diagram Level 1, and Entity Relationship Diagram\. The resulting application manages patient data, physicians, users, medical resumes, discharge summaries, death claims, file\-loan registers, reports, and user activity logs\. Black Box Testing showed that all tested functions were valid\. The Audit Trail constitutes the key feature by automatically documenting user activities to strengthen security, monitoring, transparency, and accountability\.

## [Design challenges and enabling technologies for ultra\-high\-speed electric drive systems](../publications/ada536e823c9b2ffdc24.md)

Yingshuai Liu; Dongdong Li; Hua Li; Xintong Li

Ultra\-high\-speed electric drive systems are a key route toward higher power density in electric vehicles, aerospace propulsion, and industrial applications, with series\-production traction machines now exceeding 20,000 r/min and laboratory prototypes approaching or exceeding 100,000 r/min\. This mini\-review examines the design challenges and enabling technologies of ultra\-high\-speed machines, organized around five engineering questions: how high electrical frequency reshapes loss mechanisms and winding design, how centrifugal and fatigue loading constrain rotor structures, which bearing technologies remain viable at extreme speeds, how windage and cooling limit thermal management, and how power electronics and control must adapt\. Findings are synthesized from peer\-reviewed journal literature, with particular attention to retaining\-sleeve material selection, rotor stress and balancing, active magnetic bearing systems, windage loss scaling, and direct oil cooling trade\-offs\. Because rotational speed alone does not define the operational limits—tip speed, electrical frequency, bearing DN values, and rated power are equally decisive—the review frames each topic around its underlying physical constraint rather than a nominal speed threshold\. By identifying the conflicts among electromagnetic performance, mechanical integrity, and thermal stability, and by separating mature industrial practice from laboratory demonstrations, this review aims to provide a focused reference for researchers and engineers developing next\-generation high\-speed electric propulsion systems\.
