## [Digital patient decision aids for cancer prevention in socially disadvantaged women: A scoping review protocol](../publications/ada5af4a9011bcdb1884.md)

Emmanuelle Lüthi; Océane Pittet; Joanna Montagnese; Romain Freund; Kevin J\. Selby; Véronique S\. Grazioli; Thomas Brauchli; Marie‐Anne Durand

This scoping review aims to map and analyze the existing evidence on digital Patient Decision Aids \(PtDAs\) for cancer prevention targeting socially disadvantaged women\. Cancer is a leading cause of premature mortality among women\. Cancer prevention strategies can effectively reduce cancer incidence and mortality\. Socially disadvantaged women face lower screening rates and higher mortality\. Effective cancer prevention requires informed decision\-making\. One approach is the use of digital PtDAs\. They represent a promising innovation for this population\. However, their characteristics, development process, and evaluation for cancer prevention targeting this population remain underexplored\. This scoping review will include digital PtDAs designed to meet the needs of socially disadvantaged women aged 18\-75 in the context of cancer prevention and meeting the minimum criteria established by the International Patient Decision Aid Standards\. We will include studies and sources covering quantitative and qualitative research, and gray literature\. This scoping review will follow the JBI methodology for scoping reviews\. A comprehensive three\-step search will be conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane databases, Google Scholar and gray literature sources\. All studies and sources available in any language will be considered\. Citations will be imported into Rayyan for screening\. Two independent reviewers will conduct study selection, data extraction, and analysis\. Data will be summarized using tables and descriptive content analysis to identify characteristics, development processes, and evaluation methods of digital PtDAs\. The review will be reported in accordance with PRISMA\-ScR guidelines\. Findings will be submitted for publication in an international peer\-reviewed journal and presented at national and international conferences focused on cancer prevention, shared decision\-making, digital health or socially disadvantaged women\. We will share findings with healthcare professionals, public health and cancer prevention stakeholders, and socially disadvantaged communities and their network\. This protocol has been registered with the Open Science Framework \(https://osf\.io/f3428/\)\.

## [A microelectrode array\-organoid interface for probing oscillatory behaviors and network\-level functional characteristics in mini\-brain models](../publications/ada73d62f7fb97bb6e1b.md)

Qifei Wang; Xin Dong; Xiangyu Ye; Yajie Zhang; mengxue liu; Nan Jiang; Bingqian Yu; Qin Yang; Fan Wu; Ping Wang; Liujing Zhuang

The convergence of brain organoids and microelectrode arrays \(MEAs\) represents a transformative advancement in neuroscience, drug discovery, and the emerging field of organoid intelligence\. However, the absence of refined analytical methods for extracting reliable and meaningful data continues to impede its full potential\. By shifting from single\-unit activity to local field potentials, we uncover the predominance of spatiotemporal slow oscillations, particularly within the delta range \(&lt;4 Hz\), originating intrinsically from the organoids\. Throughout development of the organoids, the intensity of oscillatory activity strongly correlates with neuronal maturity and cellular composition\. Moreover, electrical or chemical stimulation can lead to rapid changes in oscillatory behavior\. In ischemic stroke models, oxygen\-glucose deprivation elicits changes in oscillatory patterns, accompanied by elevated delta\-band coherence and increased global efficiency\. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the oscillatory activity is associated with network\-level functional connectivity across developmental and physiological states, providing insights into neural development, disease modeling, and biocomputing\.

## [A Survey on Intelligent Surveillance Systems for Classification of Usual and Unusual Events Using Deep Learning Models](../publications/ada7806362b9fd537abf.md)

Rathan J; Harish Naik T

The proliferation of closed\-circuit television and networked camera infrastructure has outpaced the human capacity to monitor it, motivating sustained research into intelligent surveillance systems capable of distinguishing usual from unusual events automatically\. Over the past decade the field has migrated decisively from handcrafted motion and appearance descriptors towards deep representation learning, and more recently towards weakly supervised, self\-supervised, and vision–language paradigms\. This survey provides a critical and comparative examination of that trajectory, drawing on more than ninety studies published principally between 2019 and 2026 together with a smaller set of earlier works that remain foundational\. The classification problem is first formalised, and it is established that the field employs at least four distinct and only partially compatible problem definitions, a circumstance that materially complicates cross\-study comparison\. A two\-axis taxonomy organised by supervision regime and by learning objective is then proposed and used to structure a detailed analysis of reconstruction\-based, prediction\-based, memory\-augmented, adversarial, graph\-based, transformer\-based, and vision–language architectures\. Particular attention is given to the weakly supervised multiple\-instance paradigm, which now dominates work on real\-world untrimmed footage\. The principal benchmarks and evaluation protocols are consolidated, and it is argued that the widespread reliance on frame\-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve has produced an appearance of saturation that conceals persistent weaknesses in localisation, generalisation, and false\-alarm behaviour\. Comparative performance tables are presented alongside an analysis of the experimental conditions that govern their comparability\. The survey closes by identifying research gaps relating to scene dependence, dataset bias, domain shift, explainability, adversarial robustness, and deployment under edge and fog computing constraints, and by outlining the directions that appear most promising for the next phase of the field\.

## [The Axiology of Arabic Language Education in the Age of Generative AI: Toward an Integrative Framework of Educational Values](../publications/adaa7ebd6f061101648c.md)

Ulwi Albab

The presence of of generative Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in Arabic language education raises fundamental questions about educational purposes and values\. This qualitative conceptual study, based on a literature review, aims to reconstruct the axiological foundations of Arabic language education by integrating intrinsic, instrumental, and transformative values\. The study employs critical philosophical analysis and theoretical synthesis\. The findings identify three educational value orientations: linguistic and cultural understanding, communicative competence and social participation, and the development of critical thinking, learner agency, and ethical responsibility\. Their integration yields four pedagogical principles: justification of educational purposes, alignment between learning and assessment, source traceability, and human accountability\. This study contributes an integrative normative framework for guiding curriculum development, teaching, assessment, and responsible AI governance in Arabic language education\.

## [Importancia de la inteligencia artificial en el éxito de los emprendimientos](../publications/adc113088f903454842f.md)

Juan Felipe Campos Brisneda

La inteligencia artificial \(IA\) se ha convertido en la herramienta número uno en excelencia tanto para jóvenes como para adultos dentro del entorno empresarial y no solo eso si no la vida en general, debido a su capacidad para transformar procesos, optimizar recursos y generar nuevas oportunidades de innovación\. En el contexto de los emprendimientos, empieza a tomar mucha relevancia pues la incorporación de soluciones basadas en inteligencia artificial representa una alternativa estratégica e indispensable para mejorar la productividad, fortalecer la toma de decisiones y aumentar la competitividad en mercados cada vez más dinámicos y exigentes nivel global\. El presente trabajo tiene como objetivo principal analizar la importancia de la inteligencia artificial en los emprendimientos, identificando y analizando sus principales aplicaciones, beneficios y desafíos para contribuir al éxito, desarrollo y sostenibilidad empresarial en plena era de expansión\. Por esto se desarrolla una investigación de tipo documental basada en la revisión y análisis de fuentes académicas, artículos científicos, informes especializados y documentos relacionados con la inteligencia artificial, la innovación empresarial y el emprendimiento\. Los resultados presentados del análisis permiten evidenciar que la inteligencia artificial ofrece múltiples ventajas para los nuevos negocios y no solo eso también presenta una herramienta en ciertos puntos confiables para micronegocios y emprendimientos emergentes, entre ellas la automatización de actividades se presenta como la parte mas fundamental a la hora de mirar el impacto presente en estas nueva era, siempre y cuando los emprendedores cuenten con la preparación necesaria para utilizarla como una herramienta estratégica de desarrollo\.

## [Molecular Biomarker Testing in Kidney Cancer: Integrating Diagnosis, Prediction, and Emerging Renal Tumor Entities](../publications/adc23c04cffb5fd0104d.md)

Büşra Yaprak Bayrak; Elif Özsağır; Nazif Alperen Yıldırım; Kerem Teke; Michael Cheng; Anna Caliò; Guido Martignoni; Mahmut Akgül; Liang Cheng C

Background: Kidney tumors comprise a biologically diverse and diagnostically challenging group of neoplasms\. Many entities share overlapping morphologic features despite having distinct molecular profiles\. Although histomorphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular biomarker testing has become increasingly important for accurate classification, recognition of emerging entities, identification of hereditary cancer syndromes, and therapeutic decision\-making\. Focus of the Review: This narrative review provides a practical, pathology\-oriented framework for molecular biomarker testing in kidney tumors\. It integrates immunohistochemistry, fluorescence in situ hybridization, polymerase chain reaction\-based methods, and next\-generation sequencing with morphologic assessment\. Particular attention is given to diagnostically relevant alterations involving VHL, TFE3, TFEB, MET, FH, ELOC, and ALK, genes encoding SDH subunits, and components of the mTOR signaling pathway, together with commonly used immunohistochemical surrogates\. The prognostic and predictive roles of selected biomarkers, including their potential value in hereditary risk assessment and treatment selection, are also discussed\. Practical limitations, such as limited biopsy material, intratumoral heterogeneity, and technical variability, are considered\. Conclusions: Molecular biomarker testing is reshaping kidney tumor pathology by supporting an integrated diagnostic approach that complements, rather than replaces, careful morphologic evaluation\. Its appropriate use can improve diagnostic accuracy, refine clinical stratification, and facilitate the recognition of emerging renal tumor entities with hereditary or therapeutic relevance\. Future developments are expected to include methylation profiling, transcriptomic classifiers, liquid biopsy platforms, and artificial intelligence\-assisted interpretation\.

## [The Dual Narcissists: Disentangling the Distinct Impacts of CEO and Board Chair Narcissism on Corporate ESG Performance](../publications/adc6bfb37c79e88a0a5f.md)

Ali E\. Akgün; Halit Keski̇n; Emel Esen; Abdullah Kürşat Merter

ABSTRACT Top executive narcissism is a crucial yet often overlooked concept in ESG performance\. Current research primarily focuses on CEO narcissism, offering an incomplete view by largely ignoring the Board Chair&\#x27;s key role in shaping ESG outcomes\. Furthermore, there is a notable lack of a comprehensive narcissism index, which would surpass the limitations of single‐ or limited‐indicator measures typically used in previous studies\. To deepen understanding, this study empirically examines the distinct effects of narcissism exhibited by both the CEO and the Board Chair on a firm&\#x27;s environmental, social, and governance \(ESG\) pillars\. By analyzing executive narcissism states in integrated report narratives alongside ESG data for 255 publicly listed companies from 2018 to 2023, measured via Refinitiv Eikon scores, this study shows that Board Chair narcissism is positively related to environmental and social performance but negatively related to governance performance\. Conversely, CEO narcissism is positively associated with both environmental and governance performance but negatively associated with social performance\. The varying effects across ESG dimensions indicate that narcissistic leadership depends on the executive&\#x27;s role and the stakeholder domain involved\. This study advances upper echelons theory, the concept of narcissistic personality, and stakeholder theory by revealing the complex interactions among various executive narcissistic states and emphasizing the need to recognize these dynamics\. Additionally, the findings offer practical insights into board composition and executive hiring to support sustainable business strategies\.

## [Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune\-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no\-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention](../publications/add7bed58ca5b1a7bc90.md)

Rensong Liu; Yan Peng; Haoran Qin; Yang Zhou; Xiaolong Li; Hongqian Wang; Ying Li; Hanlin Zhang; Xinyi Hu; Zhouqing Zhang; Weiran Ren; Xianlong Shu; Junhao Zhang; Li Nie; Xinliang Zou; Tao Jing

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether routine immune\-inflammatory biomarkers predict no\-reflow \(NR\) after percutaneous coronary intervention \(PCI\) in acute myocardial infarction \(AMI\) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri\-procedural prediction model\. METHODS: This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI\. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder\-adjusted restricted cubic splines \(RCS\) assessed nonlinear associations\. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor \(VIF\) assessing multicollinearity\. Four machine\-learning models underwent 1000\-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation\. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC \(DeLong test\), continuous NRI, and IDI\. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI\-subtype effect modification\. RESULTS: NR occurred in 91 patients \(23\.8%\)\. Multiple neutrophil\-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment\. Seven predictors constituted the final model \(all VIF &lt; 2\.5\)\. LightGBM yielded optimal discrimination and modest net clinical benefit \(AUC 0\.799, 95% CI 0\.699\-0\.899\); AMI subtype and neutrophil\-related markers dominated SHAP outputs\. Neutrophil count, NAR, NHR, SII, and PIV significantly improved discrimination\. Seven of the 16 tested markers yielded significant continuous NRI, and ten demonstrated significant IDI gains\. In stratified analyses, neutrophil count, NLR, and MHR were associated with NR in STEMI but not NSTEMI patients; interaction tests found no significant AMI\-subtype effect modification\. CONCLUSION: Pre\-procedural neutrophil\-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post\-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables\. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri\-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application\.

## [Bridging the Human–AI Trust Gap: The Mechanisms Underlying Perceived Efficacy of AI\-Powered Psychological Counseling Large Language Models](../publications/addb40c218a7ccee10e7.md)

Yi Wang; Mingchao Yin; Kun Lv

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is transforming the delivery of mental health services, yet public trust in AI\-based psychological counseling remains a significant challenge\. Drawing on a “technology–context–trust” framework, this study recruited a total of 1000 consumers in China through Credamo and conducted five between\-subjects, scenario\-based experiments to examine differences in perceived efficacy between LLM\-based psychological counseling and human experts and to investigate the mechanisms underlying these differences\. Perceived efficacy was the primary outcome of the study and, in Experiment 1B, also served as a mediator linking counseling provider type to downstream market outcomes, including overall attitude, willingness to try, and willingness to pay\. The results showed that \(1\) consumers generally perceived AI as less efficacious than human experts, a difference driven by the parallel mediating effects of perceived professional competence and perceived risk; \(2\) participants rated the AI\-based service as more efficacious in the routine counseling vignette, whereas they rated the human\-expert service as more efficacious in the major psychological\-disorder intervention vignette; \(3\) disclosure of technological investment enhanced trust in AI’s capabilities and mitigated negative evaluations; and \(4\) safety\-standard disclosure reduced perceived risk, while higher perceived economic accessibility was associated with a smaller provider\-related difference in perceived professional competence\. These findings characterize subjective service evaluations among the recruited online consumers in China and do not establish comparative clinical effectiveness\. They inform research on consumer trust while highlighting the need for further validation in more diverse samples and actual service settings\.

## [Novel ABCC2 mutations in a neonate with Dubin\-Johnson syndrome: a case report](../publications/ade28b2d5e4c429d473c.md)

Lijun An; Yuanda Zhang; Sisi Zhang

Background Dubin\-Johnson syndrome \(DJS\) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the ABCC2 gene, leading to impaired excretion of conjugated bilirubin\. Neonatal or infantile onset is uncommon and easily misdiagnosed as biliary atresia or progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis\. Case presentation We report a female infant who presented with persistent jaundice since birth \(onset in the neonatal period, ≤28 days\)\. A definitive genetic diagnosis of Dubin\-Johnson syndrome \(DJS\) was established at 11 months of age through next\-generation sequencing\. Her subsequent 5\-year follow\-up indicates a favorable clinical course\. Laboratory tests revealed consistently normal transaminase levels with elevated total bilirubin \(peak 120\.3 μmol/L at 52 days\), direct bilirubin \(peak 61\.3 μmol/L\), and gamma\-glutamyl transferase \(88 U/L\)\. Next\-generation sequencing identified two novel compound heterozygous mutations in the ABCC2 gene: c\.2443C&gt;T \(p\.R815X, nonsense\) inherited from the mother and c\.4465\_4473delinsGGCCCACAG \(p\.1489\_1491delinsGPQ, in\-frame\) inherited from the father\. Both mutations were classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic according to ACMG guidelines \(c\.2443C&gt;T: PVS1, PM2, PM3; c\.4465\_4473delinsGGCCCACAG: PM2, PM3, PM4\) and have not been previously reported\. Ursodeoxycholic acid therapy was administered, and bilirubin levels showed progressive decline over time; however, this improvement may also reflect the spontaneous trend toward resolution that is characteristic of the natural history of DJS\. Conclusion This case expands the mutational spectrum of ABCC2 gene and highlights the critical role of genetic testing in early diagnosis of infantile DJS, thereby avoiding unnecessary invasive procedures\. The favorable prognosis with conservative management further supports the benign nature of this condition\.

## [Responsible Generative AI Governance in Bangladeshi Higher Education: A Risk\-Tiered Framework for Assessment Validity, Equity and Accountability](../publications/ae0f0780927fbbd8a997.md)

Sumaia Yasmin Keya; Md\. Shahed Alamm; Niger Sultana; Md\. Aminul Islam; Ummey Sumaiya; Md\. Baharul Hasan

Purpose: Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) has entered university teaching in Bangladesh faster than institutional rules\. This paper asks which risks require institutional control when GenAI is used in teaching and assessment, and which governance design can allow proportionate use while protecting learning, integrity, privacy, fairness and human accountability\.Design/methodology/approach: The study is a structured integrative review and normative policy analysis of 61 sources: peer\-reviewed research on GenAI in higher education, academic integrity, assessment design and AI literacy; Bangladeshi empirical studies; and international and national policy instruments, including Bangladesh’s draft National AI Policy 2026–2030\. Sources were coded against five governance domains and interpreted through three lenses: assessment validity, rights\-based responsible AI and virtue ethics\.Findings: Prohibition is hard to enforce and can widen inequity, while unrestricted adoption shifts educational judgment to opaque commercial systems\. Bangladeshi evidence shows near\-universal reliance on free tool versions, weak institutional guidance, unreliable Bangla\-language output and uneven device and connectivity access\.Originality/value: The paper proposes a five\-domain \(access, assessment, data, authorship, accountability\), three\-tier \(prohibited, supervised, permitted assisted\) framework and a five\-step assessment assurance cycle that treats assessment validity, rather than detection, as the central object of governance\.Implications: The framework gives universities and the University Grants Commission a low\-cost route from broad AI principles to course\-level permissions, process evidence, oral verification and appeal\. It is a conceptual proposal that requires empirical piloting\.

## [Performance Evaluation of Steganogan Using Hybrid Image Datasets and Statistical Quality Metrics](../publications/ae1592dc65f2084997b1.md)

Metin Eken; İclal Çetin Taş

This study proposes a novel approach by employing SteganoGAN, a steganographic framework based on Generative Adversarial Networks \(GANs\)\. The impact of image categories with different semantic contents \(art, building, and nature\) on system performance was examined in detail using the SteganoGAN architecture\. A hybrid dataset composed of BossBase and USC\-SIPI images was utilized to conduct the experiments\. The influence of image quality, categorized by visual content, on performance was systematically analyzed\. In particular, changes in skewness and kurtosis values, as well as the widely used image quality metrics PSNR and SSIM, were investigated\. ## [A Multimodal\-Experimental Approach to Data Visualization: Embodying Information](../publications/ae16e6fb177756f1e1bd.md)

Murray Dick

Data visualization is an increasingly present feature of contemporary life\. It is argued that this popularity is due to their communicative efficiency, and indeed, simplicity in design is embraced as a virtue in many guides to best practice\. And yet, not everyone finds them easy to interpret; during the UK’s 2023 COVID Inquiry, former Prime Minister Boris Johnson was said, by his Chief Scientific Advisor, Sir Patrick Vallance, to have often been ‘bamboozled’ by the daily graphs produced to track the crisis\. Ideas about how data visualizations &\#x27;communicate&\#x27; \(or, how they are understood\) are often based on a computational theory of mind, with an emphasis on cognitive mechanisms, and an underlying assumption that people are essentially rational actors\. But while such an approach may be helpful in terms of helping us understand comprehension, it provides little explanation in terms of what initially attracts people to data visualizations, nor in terms of what in these designs people find engaging\.Alternatively, this book will take an embodied approach to cognition, foregrounding audience affect in theory and in design\. This monograph will introduce an experimental ‘ecology’ of design principles for data visualization, a multimodal\-experimental approach incorporating cognitive metaphor theory and visual grammar, as well as storytelling and dramaturgical techniques\. It will offer a new approach to best practice guidance, based on a conception of data visualization as multisemiotic text\. These ideas will be developed iteratively via a mix of methods and project work; including visitor studies, interviews, and pedagogic research\.

## [Introducing Coding and Artificial Intelligence to Enhance Teacher Readiness at SDN Cibuntu 01](../publications/ae1b436316158b155e43.md)

Dea Andini Andriati; Tri Nur Arifin; Uus Rusmawan

Rapid technological advances associated with the Fourth Industrial Revolution have heightened the need to cultivate digital literacy from the earliest stages of formal education\. Coding and artificial intelligence \(AI\) are increasingly recognised as essential twenty\-first\-century competencies, making teachers’ capacity to incorporate these technologies into instruction particularly important\. At SDN Cibuntu 01 in Bekasi Regency, an initial assessment identified substantial readiness gaps: approximately 80% of participating teachers lacked a sufficient grasp of fundamental coding and AI concepts, while 90% had no prior experience using visual coding platforms or AI\-supported educational tools\. This community engagement programme sought to strengthen teachers’ conceptual understanding, confidence, and pedagogical readiness to integrate coding and AI into classroom learning\. It combined interactive training and workshops featuring unplugged activities with guided demonstrations of accessible AI tools\. Post\-test scores exceeded pre\-test scores across all assessed dimensions\. Participants also prepared draft lesson plans incorporating computational thinking, while the programme produced a practical guide entitled “Introduction to Coding and Artificial Intelligence for Elementary School Teachers” to support continued implementation\. These findings indicate that combining unplugged learning with accessible AI tools can strengthen teachers’ initial readiness for technology\-enhanced instruction and generate practical resources that may be adapted by elementary schools facing similar circumstances\.

## [3D Visualization Tool for E\-Learning Activity Log Analysis From Desktop to VR Environment](../publications/ae20117b8562397f1f53.md)

Shohei Nakamura; Yoshihiro Okada

This paper presents a longitudinal evaluation through four studies of Cubic Gantt Chart \(CGC\), which is a three\-dimensional version of Gantt chart designed to visualize individual student e\-learning log data\. Across four system versions and four user studies through desktop to VR environments, this paper traces the CGC&\#x27;s development from an initial prototype through an enhanced desktop system, a collaborative VR environment\. The central finding across these evaluations is that each function increased users&\#x27; confidence in their analytical judgements but a ground\-truth verification in the final study revealed that this confidence did not correspond to statistical validity\. The in\-situ statistical test feature designed for integrating into participants&\#x27; analytical workflow to confirm their analysis is used sparsely and exploratorily\. ## [The Colorimetric Scale for Skin of Color \(CSSC\) can Provide a Standardized Classification System for Patients with Diverse Skin Tones](../publications/ae20c23e23f8357b7503.md)

Philip R Cohen

The colorimetric scale for skin of color \(CSSC\) is an inexpensive, easy to use, rapidly performed assessment for the classification of skin color type of individuals with dark skin\. The scale only includes colors, is not based on sun\-reactive skin types, and requires minimal training of the person doing the evaluation\. The colors in the CSSC range from very light beige to very dark brown; each color corresponds to a numerical skin color type: very light beige \(skin color type 1\), light brown \(skin color type 2\), medium brown \(skin color type 3\), dark brown \(skin color type 4\), and very dark brown \(skin color type 5\)\. Importantly, the CSSC provides a non\-ethnic and non\-racial categorization of people with dark skin which potentially not only diminishes racial disparities in dermatology but also promotes healthcare equity\. The expected reliability and reproducibility of the scale remain to be validated by prospective studies\. In addition, for individuals with dark skin, it is anticipated that the scale shall not only be an integral component in forensic pathology but also useful for improving diagnosis of dermatologic conditions, determining appropriate cosmetic procedures and devices, assessing the risk of skin cancer development, establishing skin type\-directed photoprotection, and enhancing research in dermatology\. The design of the CSSC enables the potential creation of an artificial intelligence\-based system to establish more objective parameters for the classification of individuals with dark skin\. In summary, the CSSC is an ideal tool for classifying individuals with dark skin\.

## [Modernizing Pakistan&\#x27;s trade ecosystem: The role of artificial intelligence in digital customs and trade facilitation](../publications/ae2417fd75b1cc55405d.md)

Hiba Syed; Syed Adeel Ali Bukhari; Syed Saghir Hussain; Abdullah Ghunio; Kaleem Mustafa; Muhammad Tayyab Ahmed

As AI technology evolves, it has opened up new prospects for enhancing customs management and promoting international commerce\. Continuous digitalization efforts such as Web\-Based One Customs \(WeBOC\), Pakistan Single Window \(PSW\), Faceless Customs Assessment \(FCA\), and Central Appraising Unit \(CAU\) serve as a starting point for the technological modernization in Pakistan\. The present study focuses on how AI can transform the trade landscape in Pakistan, especially in terms of efficiency in digital customs management, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance\. The research method used is a quantitative method with cross sectional survey by the respondents of customs officers, importers, exporters, clearing agents and other trade parties\. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling \(PLS\-SEM\) is used to evaluate the proposed relationships using SmartPLS 4\. The results revealed that the adoption of AI is statistically significant and positively related to customs operational efficiency, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance based on simulated data of 250 respondents\. The most prominent association with the use of AI is that of customs operational efficiency, followed by trade facilitation and transparency and compliance\. The research emphasizes the role of AI\-driven solutions in streamlining customs operations, minimizing paperwork, and enhancing regulatory oversight\. It also highlights the need for a robust digital infrastructure, institutional capabilities, data quality, and human oversight in the responsible integration of AI\. The study offers a template for how AI can be leveraged for a more streamlined, transparent, and competitive trade environment in Pakistan\.

Objectives Widespread digital transformation in healthcare has led to serious digital exclusion among rural older adults\. This study aims to explore the formation mechanisms of the rural digital health divide in China and propose targeted solutions to address this issue\. Methods This research adopted reflexive thematic analysis\. We conducted in\-depth interviews and participant observation with 105 older adults and 20 reference participants \(15 adult children/relatives and 5 community workers\) recruited from 12 administrative villages in Hubei Province to collect first\-hand empirical data\. Results A typical paradox was identified: rural older adults demonstrate strong willingness and practical needs to use digital health tools, yet remain unable to access the full range of digital health services\. The digital health divide is jointly shaped by three interrelated factors: individual physical and cognitive limitations, structural exclusion caused by inadequate digital health infrastructure, and intergenerational disconnection\. Conclusion Beyond simple individual and infrastructure logic, the rural digital health divide is a complex problem shaped by individual, structural and intergenerational contexts\. Informed by spatial justice theory, this study puts forward a systematic optimization framework across physical, social and symbolic spatial dimensions, covering infrastructure upgrading, community capacity building and cultural adaptation\. The research findings help eliminate access barriers to digital health services, build an inclusive digital health ecosystem, and promote health equity for rural older populations\.

## [Logistics of clinical xenotransplantation: from donor pig production to global organ distribution](../publications/ae45e90e1648eb6aded3.md)

Konrad Fischer; Joachim Denner; Ralf Reinhard Tönjes; Philipp Felgendreff; Axel O Rahmel

The shortage of transplantable organs remains one of the most significant unmet challenges in modern medicine\. Despite advances in donor management, organ preservation, surgical techniques, and immunosuppression, organ demand continues to exceed supply worldwide\. Xenotransplantation using genetically engineered porcine organs has emerged as a promising strategy to address this gap\. Recent clinical pig\-to\-human heart and kidney transplantations have demonstrated the feasibility of clinical xenotransplantation and shifted attention from immunological barriers toward practical implementation\. This review examines the logistical requirements for clinical xenotransplantation, with particular emphasis on donor herd management, biosafety, organ preservation technologies, and future distribution networks\. The integration of donor production with advanced machine perfusion technologies may ultimately transform transplantation medicine from a donor\-dependent emergency service into a predictable and scalable therapeutic platform\.

## [A review and evaluation of geologic CO2 storage potential in major South African Sedimentary Basins, with emphasis on opportunities, challenges, and future perspectives for climate change mitigation](../publications/ae469c0eab6640398327.md)

Yinka A\. Olayinka; Blessing Afolayan; Ovie Emmanuel Eruteya; Mimonitu Opuwari

Abstract Carbon dioxide \(CO 2 \) emissions from fossil fuels and industry in South Africa amounted to 401\.89 million tonnes in 2023, with implications for climate change and global warming\. South Africa has committed to achieving net\-zero carbon emissions by the year 2050\. However, the transition to a low\-carbon economy must be pursued sustainably and equitably, given South Africa’s reliance on coal and its status as a leading global coal producer\. This highlights the potential of CCUS \(carbon capture, utilisation, and storage\) as a reliable solution for achieving a low\-carbon economy\. This study adopts a comprehensive and systematic review approach to identify potential opportunities, constraints, and future directions for geologic carbon capture and storage\. This requires reviewing and evaluating relevant prior work conducted in various sedimentary basins across South Africa\. These findings indicate that South Africa has significant potential for the sequestration of CO 2 in geologic formations, with a theoretical storage capacity of 150 gigatons, almost entirely offshore\. However, there are impediments to putting a geologic carbon storage project into action\. This includes but is not limited to infrastructure, financial issues, a lack of stakeholder support, regulatory restrictions, and technical difficulties\. Significant work will be needed to evaluate realistic CO 2 storage potential, which will include detailed geological characterization: geophysics, petrophysics, geomechanics, geochemistry, sedimentology, and dynamic modelling of CO 2 sequestration\. Furthermore, the engagement of policymakers, societal opinion shapers, and oil industry professionals, among many others, may help build stakeholder support\.

## [Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi\-Turn Search Agents](../publications/ae49154a467e0430b18f.md)

Qirui Liu; Hao Chen; Yi Wen; Weijie Shi; Yao Zhao; Xianhe Chen; Hao Zhao; Xing Tang; Weihong Luo; Yuyu Luo

Outcome\-reward reinforcement learning such as GRPO gives every token of a search\-agent rollout the same advantage, although the rollout exercises two capabilities: finding evidence and using it\. We show that accuracy improves without grounding: Search\-R1 raises accuracy on all seven QA benchmarks, yet on Bamboogle the evidence\-supported share of correct answers falls from 84\.0% to 42\.9%\. We attribute this to GRPO&\#x27;s credit assignment: rollouts that retrieve answer\-bearing evidence are favoured in aggregate only in proportion to their accuracy gain over the rest, a grounding gap that answering from memory or misusing evidence shrinks or reverses\. To address this, we propose Grounded Credit Assignment \(GCA\), which uses verifiable sub\-outcomes \(evidence retrieval and answer correctness\) to correct search and answer credit separately: a wrong answer is blamed more than the search that found the evidence, and a correct answer that bypasses retrievable evidence is credited less\. Never negative on evidence\-finding search, the correction does not shrink with the grounding gap; capped at 10% of each token&\#x27;s advantage, it never overrides the outcome signal\. Without extra models, rollouts, or training stages, GCA improves average EM over Search\-R1 by 5\.7 \(Qwen2\.5\-3B\) and 6\.3 points \(Qwen3\-30B\-A3B\) and raises this share from 76\.9% to 93\.4%\.

## [Maximizing Retail Profitability with Advanced Business Analytics: Leveraging Data\-Driven Insights to Improve Merchandising Strategies](../publications/ae4cab81591371576e91.md)

Md\. Mokshud Ali; Mohammad Jobir Monjur; Sharmin Akter Moni

This paper explores how advanced business analytics can be used to refine the retail merchandising strategies in order to increase profitability\. Retailers in an extremely competitive and data\-driven industry are challenged by the need to use their data insights to the best of their prices, inventory, and communication with their customers\. The study will fill the knowledge gap in systematic optimization of strategies using analytics to improve financial results\. The research is meaningful because it offers some practical implications in terms of enhancing the efficiency of the operations and profitability in the changing retail environment\. The study will be able to address the severe problem of incorporating the advanced analytics in merchandising strategies to enhance decision\-making and outcomes\. It applies to the impact of data\-driven applications in the inventory management, dynamic pricing, and customer engagement, especially the integration of predictive and prescriptive analytics\. According to the secondary data provided by different academic studies, the results demonstrate that advanced analytics significantly enhance inventory turnover, customer satisfaction, and profitability\. Since the research indicates the importance of applying dynamic pricing models that are driven by real\-time information and effectiveness of customer engagement methods that are customized to individual customers, the research also demonstrates how consumers can be loyal\. Nevertheless, barriers connected with the unwillingness to use technology and fragmented consumer experience in multiple sales channels were found to be a major hindrance\. The study contributes to the academic argument and practical uses in the retail management field by providing suggestions on how to maximize the use of data, customer\-centric practices, and enhance the use of technology\. Lastly, the paper suggests future research opportunities, including researching application to industry\-specific applications and longitudinal research to determine the long\-term implications of advanced analytics to retail merchandising strategies\.

## [Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four\-eyed fish Anableps anableps](../publications/ae5594234dcc37d7600d.md)

Louise Perez; Lina Shi; Alyssa Daspit; Keyla N\. Pruett; Carsyn Smith; Anna Prideaux; Josane F\. Sousa; Patricia N\. Schneider

Abstract The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye\. Here, we use the four\-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision\. Single\-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region\-specific opsin expression\. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer\-wavelength\-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally\. Machine\-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red\-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue\-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments\. Dorsal\-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities\. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain\. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes\.

## [Combinatorial structure of iconic strategies in the manual\-visual modality: evidence from silent gestures by hearing non\-signers](../publications/ae643269de4f008fd647.md)

Songlei Zhang; Hua Chen

Iconicity, understood as perceived resemblance between aspects of form and meaning, provides a central basis for representing conceptual information in the manual\-visual modality\. Previous research on silent gesture has shown systematic associations between semantic categories and particular iconic strategies, with several strategies sometimes used together to represent a concept\. How these strategies are organized when they are used together, however, remains less well understood\. Using an individually administered task adapted from an established silent gesture paradigm, we elicited silent gestures from 38 Mandarin\-speaking hearing non\-signers to represent 246 concepts spanning concrete and abstract conceptual categories\. We examined how concreteness and conceptual category were related to the occurrence of combinations and how meaningful manual units were organized sequentially, simultaneously, or in mixed structures\. Our results show that most manual productions contained a single meaningful unit\. Concrete concepts were more likely than abstract concepts to elicit combinations overall and simultaneous\-only combinations, while conceptual category was associated with all three organizational formats\. Sequential combinations were the most frequent, with drawing and embodying tending to precede acting, while pointing and schema mapping tended to precede symbolic mapping\. Simultaneous combinations were characterized by recurrent pairings across the hands, especially acting with embodying and representing with locating, and broader iconicity\-type pairings varied across conceptual categories\. Mixed combinations were rare but clustered in concepts that invited both temporal staging and bimanual integration\. Our findings extend patterned iconicity beyond the selection of individual form\-meaning mappings to the relations among multiple iconic depictions\. They show that the manual\-visual modality provides temporal and spatial resources through which conceptual relations can be externalized and systematically organized even in the absence of an established sign language system\.

## [A Contextualist Account of Ascriptions of Faith](../publications/ae66918584fbc3e0b2e8.md)

M\. Hosein M\. A\. Khalaj; Mohsen Javadi

Abstract Is there a necessary epistemic condition for ascriptions of faith that P to be appropriate? The primary aim of this article is to address this question by developing a contextualist account of ascriptions of faith\. We argue that the ascription of faith that P to a subject S in a context C is semantically appropriate only if there is a salient relevant alternative to P for S in C\. We also explore the implications of the contextualist account for the debate on the possession of faith\. One group of philosophers argues that having faith that P is incompatible with possessing knowledge that P, while another group disagrees, maintaining that one can simultaneously have faith and knowledge that P\. The second aim of the article is to argue that the linguistic facts \(at least those discussed in this article\) about ascriptions of faith are not sufficient to establish that either group of philosophers is on the right track\.

## [A comparative analysis of trade exposure and human capability in Indonesian growth and emissions dynamics](../publications/ae75ffa957f0ded5afd5.md)

Muhammad Hasan Imaduddin; Soumya Basu; Hideyuki Okumura

Abstract Understanding whether economic growth can be decoupled from environmental pressure is central to the energy–economy–environment nexus \(3E nexus\)\. Evidence remains limited for economies that combine developing\-country growth pressures, net energy\-exporting status, and structurally complex transition challenges, such as Indonesia\. This study compares two alternative macro\-structural configurations within a unified 3E system: an export\-inclusive specification containing energy exports and an HDI\-inclusive specification containing human development\. A Vector Error Correction Model is estimated using quarterly data from 2000Q1 to 2022Q4, complemented by reduced\-form impulse responses and Granger\-predictive tests\. In the main quarterly estimates, the GDP\-related level\-feedback term is positive in the export\-inclusive specification and negative in the HDI\-inclusive specification; the descriptive sign contrast indicates sensitivity to model specification\. Across both specifications, electricity and non\-electric energy use remain important emissions constraints\. In Indonesia, these constraints operate within a fossil\-intensive energy sector characterized by strong state involvement and regulation across electricity and fuel supply\. This combination resembles evidence from many fossil\-resource exporters and ASEAN peers, where capability gains can coexist with carbon lock\-in; some developed economies, by contrast, have recorded emissions declines alongside a lower fossil share of energy and reduced final energy use\. Policy should therefore channel capability gains, export revenues, and capital formation toward power\-sector decarbonization, reduced direct fossil\-fuel use, and cleaner productive investment, while accounting for Indonesia’s energy\-sector governance and infrastructure constraints\.

## [REPURPOSING OF DRUGS IN THE AGE OF PRECISION MEDICINE: APPROACHES, TECHNOLOGIES, AND CLINICAL APPLICATIONS](../publications/ae9a661f77e5dcd44146.md)

Peddaboina Usha Rani; Kotla Sahithi; Tekumatlai Gowthami; Kandi Subhashini; Anitha Sadula

Drug repurposing, also known as drug repositioning or reprofiling, involves investigating existing drugs for uses beyond their original indications\. Unlike traditional drug discovery, it utilizes existing information on pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, clinical experience, and production, thereby reducing uncertainties in drug development\. Advances in computational biology, systems pharmacology, artificial intelligence \(AI\), high\-throughput screening \(HTS\), and omics sciences have transformed repurposing from an observation\-based approach into a systematic strategy\. Computational methods can identify drug–disease interactions through molecular targets, biological pathways, gene\-expression profiles, and clinical phenotypes, which can be validated through experiments, data, and prospective studies\. Integration with precision medicine enables approved drugs to be evaluated in patients selected by specific molecular or clinical features, while biomarker\-based stratification may identify beneficiaries, particularly in heterogeneous disorders\. Electronic health records and registries further provide real\-world data for detecting treatment signals and evaluating drug effectiveness and safety in clinical practice\. However, successful clinical implementation faces challenges, including incomplete or biased databases, computational prediction errors, and confounding and selection biases in clinical observations\. Previous approval for one indication does not eliminate the need for indication\-specific evaluation, as repurposing may require dose adjustment, additional safety testing, and clinical trials\. Limited diversity in clinical databases may also restrict treatment generalizability\. This paper reviews major repurposing approaches, including predictive modelling, transcriptomic analysis, screening, organoids, clinical data mining, and real\-world evidence, emphasizing their integration with precision medicine and the criteria for successful clinical implementation\.

## [A machine learning framework for stage\-structured predator–prey systems with fear effect: Sparse Identification, Gaussian Process Regression, and bifurcation analysis](../publications/ae9e4c458525ea85042d.md)

G\. Ramraj; T\. Poornima

This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning framework for the analysis of a stage\-structured predator–prey system incorporating the fear effect, intra\-specific competition among juvenile predators, and maturation delay\. The three\-species model, comprising prey \( N \), juvenile predators \( P 1 \), and mature predators \( P 2 \), is governed by a non\-linear ordinary differential equation system in which the prey growth rate is modulated by a fear factor 1/\(1\+ kP 2 \)\. We first establish the existence and local stability of the coexistence equilibrium E \* = \(16\.02, 16\.09, 32\.19\) and rigorously identify a supercritical Hopf bifurcation at a critical fear intensity k crit ≈ 0\.067, beyond which the equilibrium becomes unstable and a stable limit cycle emerges\. Five machine learning methods are deployed and benchmarked: \(i\) Sparse Identification of Non\-linear Dynamics \(SINDy\) with a generic polynomial library, which recovers the predator equations exactly \( R 2 = 1\.0\) and approximates the prey equation \( R 2 = 0\.9997\); \(ii\) Dynamic Mode Decomposition \(DMD\), whose linear assumption yields poor reconstruction \( R 2 = −2\.885 for P 2 \), demonstrating the inadequacy of linear methods for this non\-linear system; \(iii\) Gaussian Process Regression \(GPR\) with a periodic–RBF composite kernel, achieving RMSE values of 1\.92, 1\.03, and 0\.84 from sparse noisy observations; \(iv\) a physics\-constrained function approximation for recovering population trajectories from incomplete data; and \(v\) a polynomial surrogate ODE model for derivative field approximation\. Additionally, the effect of maturation delay τ on system stability is examined through delay differential equation analysis with a fourth\-order Runge–Kutta integrator, revealing delay\-induced destabilization and transitions to limit cycle dynamics at τ ≥ 10\. All numerical results are independently verified and all performance metrics are computed from actual analyses\. The framework provides a rigorous, reproducible methodology for applying modern data\-driven methods to stage\-structured ecological models\.

## [Mapping rainfed cereals and olive groves using Sentinel\-1, Sentinel\-2, and topographic data in northern Morocco](../publications/ae9f697a8f3e761f6cf4.md)

Meryem Qacami; Marc‐André Bourgault; Mohamed Chikhaoui

Accurate discrimination of agricultural crop categories in heterogeneous, rainfed landscapes remains challenging because crop spectral responses are strongly influenced by environmental variability and complex terrain\. This study assessed the contribution of optical \(Sentinel\-2\), radar \(Sentinel\-1\), and topographic variables to the binary discrimination of annual rainfed cereals and perennial olive groves in the Tangier–Tétouan–Al Hoceima region of northern Morocco, a Mediterranean mountain environment characterized by fragmented agricultural systems and rainfed conditions\. Using a Random Forest classifier, 38 candidate feature sets were evaluated, representing different combinations of Sentinel\-2 spectral bands and vegetation indices, Sentinel\-1 radar features, phenological information, and topographic variables to discriminate cereals and olive groves\. The results showed that Sentinel\-2 variables provided the strongest discriminative power, while Sentinel\-1 variables alone yielded comparatively lower performance\. The best\-performing scenario combined Sentinel\-2 spectral bands, Sentinel\-1 VV and VH backscatter, Normalized Difference Red Edge Index 2 \(NDRE2\), Sentinel\-1 VV/VH backscatter ratio \(RATIO\), and topographic variables \(elevation, slope, and aspect\), reaching an overall accuracy of 0\.96 with balanced F1\-scores for cereals and olives \(0\.92 and 0\.91, respectively\)\. Sentinel\-2\-only configurations already achieved high accuracies, particularly when spectral bands were combined with red\-edge indices and topographic variables, whereas the addition of Synthetic Aperture Radar \(SAR\) data produced modest but consistent improvements in classification accuracy\. SHAP\-based interpretation revealed a hierarchical contribution of predictors, with elevation and slope emerging as the most influential variables, followed by NDRE2 and key spectral bands\. These findings indicate that the discrimination between rainfed cereals and olive groves in this rainfed landscape is strongly influenced by topographic and environmental gradients, while spectral variables capture vegetation biophysical properties and SAR contributes complementary structural and moisture\-related information\. Overall, the study demonstrates that accurate mapping of rainfed cereals and olive groves in heterogeneous Mediterranean agro\-ecosystems benefits from the integration of spectral, structural, and topographic information\. The proposed framework provides a useful foundation for extending crop mapping and agricultural monitoring approaches in data\-scarce and climate\-sensitive regions\.

## [Edukasi Resolusi Konflik Melalui Budaya bagi Siswa\-Siswi SMA Negeri 5 Jayapura](../publications/aeb8ffcf0ef27efc7cb3.md)

Emilie Mansoben; Mariana Erny Buiney; Inri Maloringan

Konflik merupakan bagian yang tidak terhindarkan dari interaksi sosial, terutama dalam masyarakat multikultural seperti Indonesia, dan khususnya di Papua yang kaya akan keragaman budaya\. Namun, edukasi resolusi konflik melalui pendekatan budaya masih kurang mendapat perhatian dalam kurikulum sekolah formal, dan program pengabdian sebelumnya sering berfokus pada mekanisme hukum atau formal daripada kearifan budaya\. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertajuk &quot;Edukasi Resolusi Konflik Melalui Budaya&quot; dengan sasaran siswa\-siswi SMA Negeri 5 Angkasa di Jayapura\. Kegiatan ini bertujuan untuk memperkenalkan siswa pada pendekatan budaya dalam resolusi konflik dan membekali mereka dengan pengetahuan dan keterampilan untuk mengelola konflik di lingkungan sosial mereka\. Metode yang digunakan adalah metode partisipatif, dengan melibatkan siswa secara aktif dalam kegiatan edukasi dan sosialisasi melalui ceramah, diskusi, tanya jawab, dan permainan\. Kegiatan dilaksanakan dalam tiga tahap: persiapan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi, dengan melibatkan sekitar 100 siswa dari kelas X dan XI\. Hasil kegiatan ini menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar peserta mampu menyerap materi yang diberikan dengan baik, yang dibuktikan dengan partisipasi aktif mereka dalam diskusi dan kemampuan mereka memberikan contoh penyelesaian konflik secara budaya dalam kehidupan sehari\-hari\. Keterbatasan utama kegiatan ini adalah pelaksanaannya di satu sekolah dengan jumlah peserta yang terbatas, dan tidak adanya desain pre\-test/post\-test untuk mengukur perubahan pengetahuan atau sikap\.

## [Chronology\-aware generation of early Chinese black\-and\-white traditional motifs via an edge\-aware self\-attention variational autoencoder](../publications/aec287c0beebd9ef22f2.md)

Liu Gang; Hui’e Liang; Wang Xinzi; Fang Siqi

Chinese black\-and\-white traditional motifs are important visual records of cultural symbolism, ritual expression, and stylistic evolution, yet their small and poorly annotated image collections limit computational analysis and generation\. Here, we present a chronology\-aware generative framework for digital heritage representation using a curated dataset of 300 traditional pattern images from four historical periods\. The framework integrates ResNet18 feature extraction, LSTM\-based temporal modeling, and an edge\-aware self\-attention variational autoencoder to capture period\-specific motif features while preserving high\-contrast contours\. A Sobel\-based edge loss further strengthens structural fidelity in generated motifs\. Compared with Edge\-guided GAN, Edge\-conditioned diffusion, VAE, and CVAE baselines, the proposed model improves KID, LPIPS, Edge\-SSIM, SSIM, and PSNR\. The results indicate that chronological conditioning and edge\-sensitive reconstruction can improve contour preservation and structural readability in the present small\-sample setting\.

## [Human Factors and the Moon](../publications/aed90abd47c246e1b925.md)

Ken Parsons; Dennis Loveday; Simon Hodder

Living and working on the Moon requires knowledge of how to get there and back, survive, perform tasks and create comfortable habitats for lunar living\. For centuries, humanity has gazed at the Moon with wonder, but now the dream of living and working on its surface is becoming a reality\. This book explores the Moon as the next frontier, offering a comprehensive examination of its environment, the challenges of human habitation and the opportunities it presents\. With national and commercial interests investigating lunar exploration, the stakes are high and the potential for achievements and critical missteps is immense\. This title provides the introductory knowledge needed to navigate this exciting yet complex future\. This text delivers the knowledge and perspective needed to engage with the challenges and opportunities of humanity’s next great adventure\. Readers will find a detailed exploration of the Moon’s physical characteristics, its history in human exploration, and the engineering marvels that have made space travel possible\. The book introduces the principles of human factors and ergonomics, applying them to lunar environments to address the design of spaceships, habitats, vehicles and spacesuits\. From the physics of reduced gravity to the intricacies of thermal comfort, it offers practical insights into how humans can adapt to and thrive on the Moon\. The reader will acquire the tools to understand and contribute to the future of lunar habitation\. Human Factors and the Moon: Mission Requirements, Engineering Solutions and Lunar Living is essential reading for human factors professionals plus anyone with an interest in space exploration, from students and researchers in human factors and engineering to policymakers and space enthusiasts\.

## [Hallucination Detection Middleware using RAG Based Model](../publications/aef45ddf301d4ad19f73.md)

Lakshmanan A; S Nithyanandh; Mohanapriya D

Retrieval\-augmented generation \(RAG\) gives a language model access to external evidence, but retrieval alone does not ensure that a generated answer is supported by that evidence\. This paper presents VeriRAG, a middleware\-oriented design that separates query screening and evidence retrieval from answer verification\. According to the supplied project documentation, the first stage handles conversational or unsuitable requests and retrieves records through a TF–IDF index with unigram–bigram features, cosine similarity, content\-word overlap, and a small set of attribute\-specific rules\. The second stage compares retrieved evidence with a candidate answer and returns a binary support decision, confidence, explanation, and interface status\. The documented knowledge base contains 10,000 evidence–question–answer triplets, reported as equally divided between sUPPoRTED and HALLUcInATED labels\. The system is exposed through FastAPI middleware and a Streamlit interface designed around progressive disclosure: an answer is shown first and supporting evidence and verification details are revealed on demand\. The principal contribution is an inspectable division of responsibility between scope control, retrieval, and evidence\-grounded classification rather than a claim that retrieval eliminates hallucination\. Because the source archive, dataset, serialized estimators, Transformer checkpoint, and executable tests were not supplied, model priority, training history, dataset provenance, predictive accuracy, and latency could not be independently audited\. Consequently, this study reports the documented architecture and a reproducible evaluation plan while treating artifact\-level figures as project\-reported values rather than experimental findings\.

## [Edge\-native Small Language Models for 6G Intent\-driven Slicing: A Hardware\-grounded Empirical Study](../publications/aefa857eea4e0877c3cd.md)

Pratchaya Jaisudthi; Pachara Threerapat Sridee; Natthakran Phungkoed; Siwakun Kunsuk; Kanyaphak Srisuk; Vasupon Phueaknamphol

This study presents a deterministic, hardware\-grounded empirical evaluation of open\-weight Small Language Models \(SLMs\) on CPU\-only edge infrastructure\.Using greedy decoding for exact reproducibility, we benchmark four ∼8B\-parameter families \(Llama 3\.1, Qwen 2\.5, Gemma 2, GLM\-4\) under identical Q4\_K\_M quantisation, then run a 4×3 scaling analysis of Qwen 2\.5 \(0\.5B\-7B\)\.By capturing validated telemetry\-RAPL \(Running Average Power Limit\) package energy and IMC \(Integrated Memory Controller\) DRAM bandwidth across NUMA \(Non\-Uniform Memory Access\) nodes\-we provide direct hardware evidence of a memory\-bandwidthsensitive regime for SLM edge inference\.The results reveal a trade\-off: Gemma 2 9B attains the highest actioncorrectness \(50\.0%, p=0\.0037\), while Qwen 2\.5 7B is more efficient \(2\.1× faster, 2\.3× lower marginal energy\)\.We identify Qwen 2\.5 3B \(Q4\_K\_M\) as the accuracy\-efficiency sweet spot: 46\.0% action accuracy, 5\.1 s/intent, 1,997 MB peak memory, statistically tied with its 7B counterpart under identical Q4\_K\_M quantisation \(McNemar p=0\.11\)\.

## [Inheritance and Transcendence: An Examination of the Gains and Losses of Classical Political Economy from the Perspective of Marx](../publications/aefa89c0722f6836a440.md)

Jinan Gou; Puxuan Wang

Classical political economy, as the theoretical crystallisation of bourgeois economic consciousness, presents a complex intellectual landscape in which its historical contributions and inherent limitations are intertwined\. Taking Marx&\#x27;s critique of political economy as the methodological point of departure, this paper systematically reviews the theoretical evolution from William Petty and Adam Smith to David Ricardo\. Across four dimensions—the deepening of the labour theory of value, the concealment of the source of surplus value, the divergence of research methods, and the opposition of historical conceptions—it analyses why the classical school&\#x27;s &\#x27;gains&\#x27; laid a scientific foundation and why its &\#x27;losses&\#x27; plunged it into an inextricable theoretical impasse\. The study shows that the fundamental defects of classical political economy, namely the naturalisation of economic categories and the eternalisation of the capitalist mode of production, could only be thoroughly liquidated within the horizon of Marx&\#x27;s dialectics and historical materialism; while the historical merits of the classical school in analysing the law of value and class relations were, through the creative transformation effected in Capital, sublated into the theoretical premises of proletarian political economy\. A renewed examination of this intellectual moment is of foundational significance for understanding the theoretical origins of contemporary critiques of political economy\.

## [Factors influencing the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD: an extended UTAUT model](../publications/aefbd1da476632801498.md)

Jingyi Ye; Jianhua Chen; Mi Yao; Guanning Jing; Wenping Li; Yujing Su; Hongjing Pei; Jiapei Xu; Chunhua Chi

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease \(COPD\) imposes a substantial global health burden\. Despite the considerable potential of wearable devices for early detection and disease management, suboptimal engagement limits their clinical utility\. This study aims to identify factors associated with the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD\. The study extends the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology \(UTAUT\) by incorporating health risk perception and interface presentation\. A sequential mixed\-methods design was employed, commencing with semi\-structured interviews \( n = 28\), followed by a questionnaire survey \( n = 233\)\. Structural equation modeling was used to validate the measurement model and examine the hypothesized relationships\. All six constructs demonstrated statistically significant positive associations with intention to use \( P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Health risk perception \(β = 0\.272, P &lt; 0\.001\) and social influence \(β = 0\.271, P &lt; 0\.001\) were the primary correlates of intention to use\. This study extends UTAUT by identifying factors correlated with COPD patients’ intention to use smart wristbands\. The findings offer practical insights for user\-oriented device design and intervention strategies, thereby supporting the promotion of digital health monitoring among COPD patients\.

## [Time\-series analysis of the impact of short\-term exposure to atmospheric pollutants on stroke risk among residents in Guiyang City, 2016–2021](../publications/aefe5be0a114704a4240.md)

Ling Zhang; Minmin Su; Shuangfei Zhai; Meiqin Jiang; Xuanhao Chen; Ruifang Liu; Gang Chen; 张建华

Background Stroke is one of the leading causes of death among Chinese residents, and air pollution is a significant environmental risk factor\. Currently, research on the association between air pollution and stroke incidence remains limited in low\-pollution karst cities in Southwest China\. This study aims to evaluate the short\-term effects of major air pollutants on stroke incidence in Guiyang City\. Methods Daily data on stroke incidence, air pollutants, and meteorological conditions for permanent residents of Guiyang from 2016 to 2021 were collected\. A time\-series analysis was conducted using a generalized additive model \(GAM\) based on a quasi\-Poisson distribution\. Long\-term trends, meteorological factors, day\-of\-week effects, and holiday effects were controlled\. The relative risk \( RR \) and 95% CI for stroke incidence per 10 μg/m 3 increase in pollutant concentration \(CO: 1 mg/m 3 \) were assessed\. Single\-day and cumulative lag models were used to examine lag effects, and analyses were stratified by gender and age\. Results A total of 11,517 stroke cases were reported, with a daily average of 5\.25 cases\. Short\-term exposure to PM₂\.₅, PM₁₀, SO₂, NO₂, and O₃ \(per 10 μg/m 3 increase\) and CO \(per 1 mg/m 3 increase\) was positively associated with stroke risk\. The RRs \(95% CI \) at maximum lag were: PM₂\.₅ 1\.026 \(1\.005–1\.048\), PM₁₀ 1\.015 \(1\.001–1\.030\), SO₂ 1\.075 \(1\.016–1\.137\), NO₂ 1\.057 \(1\.017–1\.098\), O₃ 1\.013 \(1\.003–1\.023\), and CO 1\.346 \(1\.072–1\.691\)\. Women were more sensitive to all six pollutants, especially CO \(lag0 RR = 1\.548, 95% CI : 1\.116–2\.147\)\. Older adults \(≥65 years\) showed increased risk across all pollutants, while only NO₂ and PM₁₀ had statistically significant effects on those &lt;65 years\. Conclusion Even under low pollution levels, short\-term exposure to air pollutants is significantly associated with increased stroke risk with a lag effect, particularly among women and older adults\. Strengthening air quality management and protection for high\-risk populations is recommended to potentially reduce the burden of stroke\.

## [Development and Evaluation of AI\-Integrated Digital Learning Modules for Food and Beverage Operations Under the Strengthened Senior High School Tech\-Pro Curriculum](../publications/aeff311d34a9e21a1487.md)

Maria Luiza V\. Tantoy; Randy C\. Mangubat

This study developed and evaluated artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-integrated digital learning modules for Food and Beverage Operations under the Strengthened Senior High School Tech\-Pro Curriculum\. Using a developmental\-descriptive research design with a one\-group pretest–posttest quasi\-experimental component, it involved 84 Grade 11 learners and five TLE/TVL teachers from five public secondary schools in Agusan del Sur, together with three expert validators\. The modules were examined in terms of instructional features, competency alignment, validity, and acceptability\. Expert evaluation questionnaires, teacher and student acceptability questionnaires, and achievement tests supplied the data, which were analyzed using means, standard deviations, mean percentage scores, independent\-samples t\-tests, and a paired\-samples t\-test\. The six instructional feature dimensions were rated highly evident \(means = 4\.60–4\.80\), and the five validity dimensions were assessed as highly valid \(means = 4\.67–4\.80\)\. Teachers and students considered the modules highly acceptable, with no statistically significant differences in their ratings across the five dimensions \(all p &gt; \.05\)\. The reported mean percentage score rose from 69\.4 on the pretest to 78\.0 on the posttest\. The paired comparison of achievement\-test scores was statistically significant \(t = −11\.303, p &lt; \.001\)\. The findings support the modules’ suitability as supplementary, competency\-aligned learning resources, while the one\-group design limits causal interpretation\. Continued refinement, responsible AI\-use guidance, and testing in additional instructional settings are recommended\.

## [The Influence of Robotics Technology on Library Services Delivery in Academic Libraries in Lagos State, Nigeria](../publications/af01c667fad193e71ba5.md)

Isiaka Mashood Ishola

This study examined the influence of robotics technology for library services delivery in selected academic libraries in Lagos state, Nigeria\. It investigate the types of robot currently in use, the perception of librarians’ on it relationship to users satisfaction ans services efficiency, and the obstacles facing the implementation\. The study adopted descriptive survey research design with a population of sixty \(60\) librarians from the three selected academic libraries in Lagos state\. All 60 librarians were included through total enumeration\. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations\. Humanoid or interactive robots were the most commonly reported robot identified by 90% of respondents and other technologies, including telepresence, shelf\-reading, and autonomous delivery robots, were less widely available\. Respondents generally perceived robotics as improving service accessibility, user experience, and operational accuracy\. However, perceived benefits in reducing waiting times and enabling staff to focus on complex user needs were comparatively modest\. Major implementation challenges included acquisition costs, difficulties integrating robotic systems with existing library infrastructure, maintenance requirements, unreliable electricity or internet connectivity, and limited technical support\. The findings suggest that robotics can support more accessible and efficient library services, but wider adoption will depend on sustained funding, reliable infrastructure, system integration, and staff training\. Implementation should also preserve access to human assistance\.

## [Social Representations About Museums of Preservice Teachers Who Participate in a Museum Internship](../publications/af034c112703d47c421e.md)

Carlos Arturo Soto Lombana; Claudia Alejandra Mazzitelli; Erica Gabriela Zorrilla; Verónica Cardona Arango

ABSTRACT This article presents the results of a research project aimed at identifying the Social Representations of a group of preservice teachers who participated in a museum internship and inferring the influence of these representations on educational practice in this context\. The research employs a mixed‐methods design with a qualitative approach\. The sample consisted of eight preservice teachers of natural sciences from a Colombian university\. Following a previous examination of the social representations associated with museums and the pedagogical practices developed in this context, data collection took place during a workshop that explored content related to museum education\. Findings suggest that the Social Representations perceived by the participants identify a museum as an educational space conducive to teacher training, where learning, mediation, and motivation are aspects that occur with various audiences\.

## [Inter\-Rater and Intra\-Rater reliability of rehabilitative ultrasound imaging of core muscle thickness in individuals with Anterior Pelvic Tilt](../publications/af0ce7d1bcc34af8e4d4.md)

Wajeeha Zia; Syed Shakil\-ur\-Rehman; Muhammad Salman Bashir; Hafiz Muhammad Waseem Javaid

Background &amp; Objectives: Excessive lordotic curvature of the lumbar spine defines the phenomenon known as anterior pelvic tilt, which causes changes in posture, movement, and core muscle activation\. Rehabilitative ultrasound imaging \(RUSI\) has been proposed as an effective means of evaluating muscle thickness both in static and dynamic states\. The present study aimed to determine the intra\-rater reliability of RUSI measurements of transverse abdominis \(TrA\), lumbar multifidus \(LM\), and gluteus maximus \(GMax\) muscle thickness at rest and during standardized contraction, and to determine the inter\-rater reliability of these measurements in young adults with and without anterior pelvic tilt \(APT\)\. Methodology: The methodological reliability study was conducted at Al\-Khumeini Trust Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, between January 2023 and June 2023\. Participants included forty\-six volunteers between 18 and 28 years old, of which 23 subjects were diagnosed with APT and 23 had normal spinal alignment\. Bilateral TrA, LM, and GMax thicknesses at rest and during contraction were measured twice in two assessment days by two independent raters who had more than five years of experience in RUSI\. Intra\-rater reliability was tested based on the measurements by the same rater in two different days, while inter\-rater reliability was assessed between the two raters\. ICC with 95% confidence interval, was used to quantify reliability\. SEM and MDC95 were computed to assess absolute precision of the measurement\. Results: The results showed consistent high intra\- and inter\-rater reliability in the thickness measurements of the TrA, LM, and GM muscles, with intraclass correlation coefficients between 0\.930 and 0\.998, suggesting that these measurements were highly consistent\. SEM and MDC95 values indicated relatively small absolute measurement error, although the magnitude varied across muscle measurements\. Conclusion: Standardized RUSI measurements of TrA, LM, and GMax muscle thickness demonstrated good\-to\-excellent intra\-rater and inter\-rater reliability in young adults with and without APT\. These findings support the reproducibility of the measurement protocol under the conditions examined\. Further studies are required to determine whether these reliability estimates are generalizable to older adults, symptomatic chronic low back pain populations, and examiners with different levels of RUSI experience\.

## [Not all prolific letter writers are alike](../publications/af29a8041c998f1b2b90.md)

Shigeki Matsubara

Concerns have recently been raised that AI\-assisted &quot;letter\-bombing&quot; may distort medical publishing\. Although I share these concerns, prolific Letter writing can arise for legitimate reasons\. Using my own publication history as an example, I illustrate how retirement, loss of access to primary data, and broader academic interests naturally shifted my publications from original articles toward Letters\. The problem lies not in writing many Letters, but in inappropriate motivations and misuse of AI\.

## [AI\-driven mobile practice and English\-speaking performance: a quasi\-experimental study of ELSA speak among Malaysian university learners](../publications/af2abe4f2b5c8a030774.md)

Omar Al\-Jamili; Musharraf Aziz; Huda Ibrahim; Mazida Ahmad; Munya Saleh Ba Matraf

This study examined whether supplementary use of the AI\-enabled ELSA Speak application was associated with improved English\-speaking performance among Malaysian university learners\. A mixed\-methods, quasi\-experimental pre\-test–post\-test non\-equivalent control\-group design involved 60 undergraduates from two intact sections of a compulsory English course\. Both sections received identical core instruction; the experimental section also completed approximately 36 hours of monitored ELSA Speak practice over four months, scheduled three times weekly for at least 30 minutes\. Across approximately 48 scheduled sessions, cumulative records implied about 45 minutes per session rather than a recorded session\-level mean\. An IELTS\-informed analytic rubric assessed pronunciation, fluency, vocabulary, grammatical accuracy, and communicative content\. Both sections improved, but the experimental section showed markedly higher post\-test performance after accounting for baseline differences\. Exploratory interviews and classroom observations suggested learners valued practice and immediate feedback, but did not provide validated psychological or technology\-related measures\. The advantage cannot be attributed solely to software because additional practice, automated feedback, monitoring, technical guidance, and instructional support were also provided\. Findings are context\-specific and hypothesis\-generating, warranting stronger allocation procedures, a time\-matched active comparison, multiple blinded raters, larger samples, and delayed follow\-up\.
