## [Epidemiology and outcomes in pediatric neuroblastoma: a US population\-based study](../publications/af31bf5cd0d43cd119c3.md)

Shruti Wadhwani; Nikita Wadhwani; Vignesh Krishnan Nagesh; Izage Kianifar Aguilar; Behzad Amoozgar; Sindhu Avvari; Kousik Surya Sridharan; Aman Siddiqui; Urveesh Sharma; Olga Velichko; Kwangha Baek; Auda Auda; Valentino O\. Baldeo; Tirth Bhavsar; Georgia Souza; Harman Antaal; Florchi Furman; Priya Rokade; Gopal Mondal; Pavan T\. Vaddera; Divya Bhagavathi; Sumreen Nazly; Dessislava Papantoniou; Grace John; Dhanush K\. Aruljothi; Reshma Radhakrishnan; Juilee V\. Dongre

Purpose Neuroblastoma is a heterogeneous pediatric malignancy with variable outcomes\. This study aimed to evaluate survival outcomes and identify independent prognostic factors using a large population\-based cohort\. Methods The Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results \(SEER\) database was used to identify 863 patients diagnosed with neuroblastoma between 2000 and 2017\. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to assess predictors of overall and cancer\-specific mortality\. Results The cohort included nearly equal numbers of males and females, with most patients diagnosed before 10 years of age\. The majority of patients were non\-Hispanic White, followed by Hispanic and non\-Hispanic African American patients\. In univariate analysis, race/ethnicity showed differences in mortality; however, these were not significant after multivariable adjustment\. Increasing age at diagnosis was strongly associated with worse survival, with infants \(&lt;1 year\) demonstrating the best outcomes and adolescents \(10–19 years\) the highest mortality risk\. Distant metastatic disease was independently associated with increased mortality\. Surgical resection was associated with improved overall survival, whereas chemotherapy was associated with higher mortality, likely reflecting confounding by indication due to treatment selection in high\-risk disease\. Conclusion Age at diagnosis and disease stage are the strongest independent predictors of survival in pediatric neuroblastoma\. Race/ethnicity was not independently associated with outcomes after adjustment\. Observed associations between chemotherapy and mortality likely reflect underlying disease severity rather than treatment effect\.

## [A Hybrid Computational Intelligence Framework for Automatic Calibration of Catchment Scale Hydrodynamic Flood Models](../publications/af31ea82af02a522b493.md)

Mahdi Sedighkia; Barry Croke; Roslyn Tamara Prinsley

Abstract This study presents a novel automated framework for the calibration and validation of rain\-on\-grid \(RoG\) hydrodynamic models at the catchment scale, with specific application to the TUFLOW HPC platform\. The proposed approach establishes an integrated and automated workflow that links rainfall input directly to flood response, enabling efficient calibration of key hydraulic parameters, including Manning’s roughness, initial loss, and continuous loss\. The framework combines ensemble\-based parameter sampling, automated model execution, data\-driven surrogate modelling, and evolutionary optimization algorithms \(EAs\) to systematically explore parameter combinations within the defined calibration ranges\. Three modelling techniques—Random Forest \(RF\), Gaussian Process Regression \(GPR\), and Gradient Boosting \(GB\)—are employed to approximate model responses from an ensemble of hydrodynamic model simulations, thereby accelerating the calibration process and reducing computational costs\. Furthermore, three EAs, consisting of Particle Swarm Optimization \(PSO\), Invasive Weed Optimization \(IWO\), and Differential Evolution \(DE\), are applied\. The optimization objective is defined as minimizing the discrepancy between simulated and reference inundation extents, quantified through total inundated area derived from benchmark inundation datasets\. The entire process is implemented in a MATLAB\-based script that automatically controls TUFLOW simulations, iteratively adjusts parameters, and evaluates model performance without manual intervention\. The framework is tested in a small catchment case study under multiple design rainfall events \(50\-, 100\-, and 500\-year return periods\)\. Results demonstrate close agreement between the simulated and reference inundation areas, with differences of less than 1% across all scenarios\. These findings indicate satisfactory predictive performance within the studied calibration range\. The key novelty of this study lies in the integration of surrogate\-assisted optimization within a fully automated calibration environment tailored for RoG models\. Furthermore, the developed MATLAB code is made publicly available via GitHub, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and potential broader application in hydrodynamic flood modelling\.

## [Allen, Colin: Real Traits, Real Functions?](../publications/af36a84007f17247c6f1.md)



In Andre Ariew, Robert Cummins &amp; Mark Perlman, Functions: New Essays in the Philosophy of Psychology and Biology\. New York: Oxford University Press\. pp\. 373\. 2002Discussions of the functions of biological traits generally take the notion of a trait for granted\. Defining this notion is a non\-trivial problem\. Different approaches to function place different constraints on adequate accounts of the notion of a trait\. Accounts of function based on engineering\-style analyses allow trait boundaries to be a matter of human interest\. Accounts of function based on natural selection have typically been taken to require trait boundaries that are objectively real\. After canvassing problems raised by each approach, I conclude with some facts that satisfactory notions of trait must respect\. \(direct link \)

## [КОМПЛЕКСНА МЕТОДИКА ВИЗНАЧЕННЯ ДЕФОРМАЦІЙНИХ ХАРАКТЕРИСТИК ҐРУНТІВ ДЛЯ МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ ВЗАЄМОДІЇ З БУДІВЕЛЬНИМИ КОНСТРУКЦІЯМИ](../publications/af37b456aa916b2e4402.md)

ОЛЕНА БАГРІЙ; ОЛЕКСАНДР ДОРОФЄЄВ

The design of spatial building structures in modern software systems requires the use of numerical methods capable of accounting for the physical and geometric non\-linearities of materials\. One of the most complex tasks in this process is the correct modeling of the interaction between the structure and the soil environment, the reliability of which depends on the accuracy of the specified physical and mechanical parameters of the base\. Soil is a discrete medium with a significant manifestation of internal friction, the deformation laws of which depend on the magnitude of the average compressive stress\. Standard laboratory techniques, such as compression in a rigid holder or testing in classical stabilometers, have technical limitations and often do not allow determining the non\-linear deformation characteristics required for modern non\-linear calculation models with sufficient accuracy\. The article theoretically substantiates a comprehensive methodology of parallel testing of discrete media to establish the parameters of non\-linear deformation models\. To find elastic characteristics, in particular the deformation modulus and Poisson&\#x27;s ratio, the combined use of compression and loading of a thick\-walled cylindrical sample with internal radial pressure is applied\. The developed approach to the study of plastic deformation regularities ensures the independent variation of principal stresses while maintaining the constancy of the average compressive stress\. The proposed loading regime eliminates the shortcomings of traditional triaxial compression devices and makes it possible to obtain a family of deformation curves\. The combination of these curves describes a single deformation surface in the stress\-strain space\. The use of the characteristics determined by this methodology as input data for computer\-aided design systems opens the way to a significant increase in the reliability of numerical modeling of the joint behavior of building structures with a soil base\.

## [From groups to teams: applying Team Academy methodology in organisational development](../publications/af3c768aeac924417dba.md)

Nina Swaddle; Heikki Toivanen

Purpose Team Academy, known in Finnish as Tiimiakatemia, is a well\-known method for team\-based learning in education, but rarely studied as a tool for organisational development \(OD\)\. This article asks whether Team Academy methodology can help organisations move from groups to genuine teams, and whether human collective learning will become a key organisational strength as artificial intelligence changes what individuals can do\. Design/methodology/approach The article combines a literature review, drawing on the learning organisation \(Senge\), knowledge creation \(Nonaka and Takeuchi\) and selfmanaged learning \(Cunningham\), with three semi\-structured interviews\. The practitioners interviewed had each introduced Team Academy methodology inside a large organisation: an industrial technology and logistics company, a telecommunications company and a financial services company\. The three cases are discussed together, theme by theme, using thematic analysis\. Findings Thematic analysis identified eight cross\-case themes, including person\-dependent adoption, partial uptake of Team Academy tools, letting go of hierarchical control and middle management as a friction point\. Rather than one shared model, the cases show a repeating pattern: a committed individual applies parts of the methodology, meets resistance and builds trust through small steps\. A six\-phase framework is proposed\. Originality/value Team Academy methodology has been widely studied in education, but very little academic work has looked at its use in OD\. This article addresses that gap using original practitioner interviews from three sectors, and connects Team Academy to a topic not previously explored: artificial intelligence in the workplace\. The resulting six\-phase framework offers a new, practical starting point for organisations and researchers\.

## [INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL, RESPONSABILIDADE JURÍDICA E PROTEÇÃO SOCIOAMBIENTAL](../publications/af44930af0c469c9e324.md)

Mestra Em Saúde e Ambiente; Ana Paula Felismino da Silva; Eduardo De Siqueira de Negreiros; John Willian Vieira Martins; Daniel Souza TABOSA; Lucas Luiz Castro De Souza

O uso crescente de inteligência artificial \(IA\) suscita debates sobre a atribuição de responsabilidade jurídica por danos de decisões automatizadas, em cenário de opacidade algorítmica e de impactos coletivos e ambientais\. Objetivo: Sintetizar a literatura científica sobre responsabilidade jurídica e IA e propor caminhos cíveis, criminais e socioambientais para a lacuna legislativa brasileira\. Metodologia: Revisão narrativa da literatura, qualitativa, com 14 trabalhos com DOI \(2016 a 2026\) localizados em outubro de 2026 por busca não sistemática; normas e doutrina apoiaram as propostas, fora do corpus\. Resultados: Os estudos convergem quanto à opacidade e à dispersão de agentes como obstáculos à imputação, divergem sobre a existência de lacunas de responsabilidade e apontam responsabilidade compartilhada, revisão do conceito de defeito, seguro e facilitação da prova\. Para um caso hipotético de crédito discriminatório, propõem\-se responsabilidade civil objetiva com facilitação probatória e responsabilização penal por omissão imprópria, e o regime da responsabilidade ambiental serve de modelo para danos coletivos\. Conclusão: A proteção de quem sofre dano exige critérios de imputação e de prova adaptados à IA, mesmo antes da aprovação do Projeto de Lei 2\.338/2023\.

Jamal MENNACH; Prof\. Chakib BOUKNANI

L&\#x27;émergence de l&\#x27;intelligence artificielle a profondément transformé le monde des affaires et a même bouleversé les principes sur lesquels repose le droit classique des sociétés\. Des systèmes autonomes assurent certaines fonctions de gestion, des algorithmes prennent des décisions, tandis que des actifs immatériels acquièrent de la valeur\. ## [Opinion dynamics model based on temporal higher\-order networks](../publications/af4baed5c241e5d85690.md)

CHEN Lei; XIAO Haibing; Feng Hu; Zike Zhang

揭示社交网络中的信息传播规律，是实现网络空间治理所面临的核心挑战。针对现有意见动力学模型难以还原信息传播过程中用户在线\-离线动态演化以及高阶交互的局限，本文构建融合用户在线\-离线状态切换机制的时序社交超网络，并在此基础上提出耦合“个体\-圈层\-群组”三层影响机制的连续意见动力学模型。通过理论分析，探究模型中立单稳态的局部渐进稳定边界条件，并揭示非对称分岔机理与多稳态涌现规律。通过在合成网络上的参数敏感性分析，以及在三类实证社交超网络上的实验验证，表明所提模型能够较好地捕捉舆情演化中的多稳态现象。研究结果为复杂社交环境下的信息监管提供理论支撑与治理启示。

## [Working‐Time Demands and Work–Family Conflict: The Gendered Role of Informal Childcare Support in Germany](../publications/af5cfffc2cd9df3c834b.md)

Alina Maria Pavelea; Anna Matysiak; Anna Kurowská

ABSTRACT Objective This study examines how perceived availability of informal childcare support moderates the associations between work‐time demands and time‐based work–family conflict \(tWFC\) for mothers and fathers in dual‐earner families in Germany\. Background Increasing work‐time demands, including job‐related time pressure, long hours, and evening work, contribute to tWFC, particularly for parents\. Informal childcare support, such as assistance from grandparents or other relatives, may help parents manage work and family obligations\. However, the moderating role of informal childcare support has received limited research attention\. Method We use data from three waves \(6, 8, and 10\) of the Panel Analysis of Intimate Relationships and Family Dynamics \(PAIRFAM\), including 753 mothers and 678 fathers in dual‐earner couples with at least 1 child aged 10 or younger\. To examine associations between work‐time demands and tWFC, as well as interactions with informal childcare support, we use random‐effects linear regression models\. Results Higher work‐time demands are associated with tWFC for mothers and fathers, with gender differences in magnitude\. Mothers report higher tWFC from longer working hours, while fathers&\#x27; tWFC is associated with job pressure\. Informal childcare support moderates these associations: maternal grandmother support is linked to lower tWFC for mothers, whereas fathers benefit more from support from grandfathers, siblings, and other relatives\. Implications Findings underscore the gendered nature of tWFC and gender differences in the role of informal childcare support\. Policies ensuring access to flexible childcare and supporting care provided by extended family members may help parents manage work and family responsibilities under demanding work‐time conditions\.

## [Strawberry \(Fragaria × ananassa\) cultivation in India: A critical review of status, constraints and future directions](../publications/af61a24cb2d654ef754c.md)

A Dharshni; C\. P\. Ravindran; S\. Muthulakshmi; S\. Shenbagavalli; T Anitha

Strawberry \(Fragaria × ananassa Duch\.\) is an economically important berry crop worldwide, due to its distinctive flavour, nutritional value and health benefits\. In recent years, it has been cultivated not only in temperate regions, but also in subtropical and tropical regions\. It has become one of the high\-value horticultural crops in India, due to the growing consumer demand and good returns to farmers\. This review critically examines the trends in yield, constraints and technological factors influencing strawberry cultivation across major strawberry producing states such as Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and other emerging regions in India\. Evidence from existing studies indicates that the adoption of improved cultivation practices such as balanced fertilisation, integrated pest management, mulching, protected cultivation and soilless systems has substantially improved fruit yield and quality compared to conventional open\-field methods\. Despite these advancements, productivity remains limited by climatic sensitivity, pest and disease factors, soil and nutrient management constraints and postharvest losses due to the highly perishable nature of the fruit\. Moreover, disparities in technology adoption and the lack of cold\-chain infrastructure continue to constrain sectoral growth\. Emerging technologies such as precision agriculture and decision\-support systems offer considerable potential to improve resource\-use efficiency and sustainable production\. The review discusses the status of strawberry production in India and its integration with production trends, challenges and future research in the field\. It also points out gaps in the current knowledge and limited production systems and also outlines the future technological interventions needed to enhance the productivity, profitability and sustainability of strawberry production under Indian conditions\.

## [Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent\-State Design](../publications/af73ba4410cc0cb8828b.md)

Benhao Huang; Chufan Shi; Junlin Chen; Shicheng Wen; Zhengzhong Liu; Eric Xing; Xuezhe Ma

Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization\. We isolate these axes in models trained from scratch at matched parameter scale, logical depth, and token budgets, and then test whether the resulting design principles transfer to resident\- and active\-parameter\-matched Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) models\. The prelude\-recurrent block\-coda sandwich architecture consistently improves performance on context extraction and reasoning\-intensive tasks\. Input injection primarily enhances knowledge retrieval and context utilization, whereas random initialization and separate H/L recurrent states provide mixed or negative returns\. Taken together, these results favor the Huginn\-style design: at the 730M\-parameter and 336B\-token scale, the complete Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks\. The advantages of Huginn over Ouro transfer to MoE models\. At the 8BA0\.8B \(32BA3B when unrolled\) scale trained on 500B tokens, Huginn outperforms Ouro on nearly all benchmarks spanning knowledge, reasoning, and coding, while also exhibiting more balanced expert routing\. Under matched training and inference FLOPs, the Huginn\-style model uses 75% fewer resident parameters than a 112\-layer feedforward MoE baseline\. Despite its smaller physical parameters, it outperforms the feedforward baseline on DROP and GSM8K, matches it on MATH500, and remains competitive on the other benchmarks\.

## [Parametric Resonance in Primal\-Dual Learning for Slowly Non\-Stationary Constrained MDPs](../publications/af755bd62c83b0d454ce.md)

Maxime Baelde

Primal\-dual methods for constrained Markov decision processes are analyzed under a two\-timescale assumption, with non\-stationarity entering through two channels\. In the additive channel, where the constraint level oscillates, the dual oscillation saturates at a floor set by the moving optimum and is amplified linearly by the timescale ratio\. In the parametric channel, where the constraint sensitivity oscillates, a coherent modulation carries no resonant forcing at any depth: the dual update&\#x27;s stiffness modulation cancels the primal update&\#x27;s damping modulation\. Instability instead comes from a mismatch between the constraint estimate used by the primal update and the measurement used by the dual update, producing a parametric resonance at twice the pair&\#x27;s natural frequency\. The tolerated mismatch grows with the square root of the forcing bandwidth and collapses with the square root of the dual\-to\-primal step\-size ratio\. These results hold on the tangent linear\-quadratic reduction around an active saddle, for one constraint and for $K$ constraints under a common modulation and an isotropy condition\. Driving both updates from the same estimate removes the resonant forcing but introduces a stationary offset equal to the estimator&\#x27;s bias\. In a Lagrangian soft actor\-critic agent, the multiplier locks onto the sub\-harmonic at the timescale ratios its identified linear loop predicts and a coherent cost critic suppresses the lock\-in, while a proportional \(PID\) term, predicted to leave the lock\-in in place, suppresses most of it through the projection of the multiplier\.

## [AI in daily cardiology and structured multidisciplinary care](../publications/af7b61f8dbec6be830de.md)

Pim van der Harst

This issue of the Netherlands Heart Journal includes three original articles, Dutch endorsement of the 2025 ESC pregnancy guideline, and a perspective on artificial intelligence \(AI\) in the outpatient clinic\.In a national survey among 120 hospital\-based professionals, Aertsen\-van der Kuip et al\. found that 97% considered palliative care and advance care planning in chronic heart failure important, but only one third provided it regularly \[1\]\.While 78% recognised palliative care needs, only 23% felt sufficiently skilled\.Education and time remain key barriers\.Van Vreeswijk et al\. describe EmbRACE, a national network on atrial cardiomyopathy \[2\]\.Seven work packages combine biobanking, molecular profiling and AI\-based modelling with interventional trials\.The aim is to define thresholds and determine whether targeting the atrial substrate improves outcomes\.Van der Zwaan et al\. present the NVVC endorsement of the 2025 ESC pregnancy guidelines \[3\]\.Women with cardiovascular disease should undergo mWHO 2\.0 risk assessment\.Women above class II are counselled and followed by a Pregnancy Heart Team\.The Dutch addendum includes recommendations on single\-embryo transfer and ethical deliberation\.Okken et al\. developed an AI tool that detects complications of pulmonary vein isolation, coronary intervention and TAVI from health records \[4\]\.In 6,564 patients, sensitivity was 94\.4\-100% and specificity 99\.4\-100%\.Flagged cases still require review, but registration no longer relies solely on manual reporting\.Meijer and De Jong describe the Epic\-integrated ambient AI scribe at OLVG \[5\]\.They observed more patient attention and about 30% less documentation

## [Push and pull factors of relocation in the coastal zone: what matters most?](../publications/af8dac986f380fead013.md)

Anamaria Bukvic; Mingang Kim

Abstract Permanent relocation is increasingly proposed as an effective long\-term strategy for coastal areas affected by recurrent flooding\. While the literature on coastal relocation has been steadily growing—particularly on policy processes, financial mechanisms, and lived experiences—less attention has been given to understanding the reasoning behind relocation decisions\. This study provides empirical evidence on the factors that drive willingness to relocate from a telephone survey administered in high\-risk coastal settings on the Delmarva Peninsula in Maryland and Hampton Roads, Virginia\. Drawing on data from 182 completed surveys, we examined prior flood exposure and reported impacts, willingness to relocate, push and pull factors, preferences for relocation destinations, and socioeconomic characteristics\. The most common push factors were disastrous hurricane flooding and financial considerations \(i\.e\., higher taxes, living costs, and insurance rates\), and pull factors were low crime rates and proximity to family, friends, and healthcare services\. All highly rated intervening factors were related to the relocation process, including assistance tailored to individual needs, a straightforward and transparent program implementation, the opportunity to participate in the planning process, monetary compensation, and moving assistance\. The regression analysis identified nine predictors of relocation, including five push factors related to flooding and its secondary impacts on quality of life, and changes in social support\. Other predictors included proximity to friends, living outside the FEMA floodplain, free legal and technical advice on moving options, and a preference for a community with conservative policies\. These quantitative results can inform policy development, advance spatially explicit modeling of coastal mobility, and help design buyout programs that address comprehensive household needs while aligning with broader community land use and development goals\.

## [Strategies for widening participation in the biomedical science at London South Bank University—a case study](../publications/af9080fa17d9ca695d78.md)

Ruth Gyereh Dogwul; Bernadine Idowu; Eiman A\. Aleem

Introduction and context Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic \(BAME\) professionals make essential contributions to UK healthcare, biomedical science research, academia, and the life sciences industry, yet remain underrepresented in senior roles\. Three barriers recur: limited access to the discipline, a weak sense of belonging, and few visible role models\. This study presents targeted strategies implemented within London South Bank University&\#x27;s Biomedical Science Programme \(BMS\) to address these barriers at key stages of students&\#x27; career development journey\. Aims This case study had two linked Aims: \(1\) to describe strategies addressing these barriers, and \(2\) to examine, through a survey of BMS alumni and students, whether barriers were experienced, whether strategies reached them, and what remained unmet\. Methods Initiatives included the Black in Biomed conference, providing role models and networking; STEM workshops for school pupils; and BMS Day outreach, offering hands\-on engagement and diverse representation\. An anonymous Qualtrics survey examined the same three areas: role models and mentors, when students first learned about biomedical science careers, support and inclusion and how the course prepared them for their careers\. Results The Black in Biomed conference was valued for early career exposure, mentorship, and representation\. Among survey respondents, 76% were BAME, 94% rated the course positively, and 78% reported access to BAME role models or mentors\. Forty percent had attended a widening participation event and reported positive influence\. However, 63% first learned about biomedical science at sixth form or college, while 33% reported financial constraints\. Conclusion Programme strategies address barriers to access, belonging, and representation, while the survey identifies where these persist\. Inclusive, career\-focused initiatives embedded within the curriculum may support equity and representation\. Priorities include earlier career guidance, relatable role models, hands\-on experience, and financial support\. The initiatives presented in this work could be easily introduced to other programmes\.

Veri çağında, geleceği anlamak ve kararları yeniden şekillendirmek için yapay zekânın gücünü keşfedin\! Ham verinin karmaşasından doğru ve güvenilir kararlara ulaşmak, günümüz bilgi çağının en temel arayışıdır\. Bu eser, söz konusu sorumlulukları arka plana itmeden, teknolojiyi bütüncül ve eleştirel bir bakış açısıyla ele alıyor\. ## [Explainable artificial intelligence reveals spatially divergent effects of global change on mammals](../publications/af95ce134446b726bd8d.md)

Lei Song; Amy E\. Frazier; Peter Kedron; Diogo S\. A\. Araujo; Diyang Cui; Brian Joseph Enquist; César Hinojo‐Hinojo; Joana Madeira Krieger; Brian Maitner; Cory Merow; Gabriel Massaine MOULATLET; Efthymios I\. Nikolopoulos; Patrick R\. Roehrdanz

Abstract Understanding how global change reshapes species distributions remains a central challenge in ecology, yet most global assessments treat environmental drivers as static, uniform, or aggregate influences\. This obscures where, why, and how specific drivers generate ecological risk or opportunity\. Here, we apply explainable machine learning to assess how climate averages, variability, extremes, and land cover are projected to reshape future distributions of 1,992 terrestrial mammals\. Using Shapley Additive Explanations with species distribution models, we quantify the directional contribution of 16 environmental drivers and track how these contributions change over space and time\. We propose two ecological diagnostics, directional turnovers and favorability shifts, that reveal where drivers switch from favorable to unfavorable, or the reverse, and where their influence strengthens or weakens without sign reversal\. While not designed to infer causation, our framework assesses whether projected spatial patterns align with ecological expectations\. We show that climate extremes impose intense but spatially restricted impacts, temperature\-related drivers dominate exposure patterns, particularly for specialist species, and the same driver can impose risk in one region while creating opportunity in another\. By decomposing projected biodiversity change into driver\-specific signatures, our framework advances biodiversity forecasting toward a more actionable understanding of ecological risk and opportunity\.

## [Machine Learning Approach for Cardiovascular Disease Risk Stratification Using Ensemble Classifiers and Dimensionality Reduction](../publications/af9c6e5fa65aaa525e13.md)

Alejandro Posada\-Castellanos; Miguel Angel Gómez\-Aristizabal; Carlos Manuel Orrego\-Franco; E\. Restrepo\-Parra; Luis Eduardo Lopez\-Betancur

Cardiovascular disease \(CVD\) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, motivating data\-driven tools that complement established clinical risk criteria\. We present a two\-pathway machine learning framework for CVD risk assessment\. Pathway I is a brief rule\-learnability verification, a four\-level risk label is generated by a deterministic MEWS/Framingham\-inspired scoring rule, and because the label is a deterministic function of the inputs, its near\-perfect recovery by the classifiers is only a consistency check, not predictive evidence\. Pathway II, the focus of the study and the main contribution of this work, is a hybrid pipeline that combines unsupervised preprocessing \(K\-Nearest Neighbors imputation, PCA/UMAP dimensionality reduction, K\-Means phenotyping\) with supervised ensemble classifiers \(Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM\), trained on an ≈70,000\-record Kaggle cohort and externally validated on an independent 219\-patient cohort using the same prevalent\-CVD definition\. On the external cohort the six pipelines performed comparably \(accuracy 70–74%, external\-cohort AUC 0\.82–0\.85\); paired McNemar tests showed no significant difference between UMAP\- and PCA\-based pipelines \(all p&gt;0\.5\), and a power analysis indicates the cohort is too small to distinguish them, so no configuration is claimed to be superior\. An unsupervised phenotype analysis is included as a descriptive, hypothesis\-generating step; its association with the outcome is statistically significant but of negligible effect size\. The framework offers a reproducible, clinically interpretable methodology for CVD risk categorization\.

## [Comparative Assessment of Machine Learning and Statistical Models for Agricultural Drought Forecasting and Driver Attribution in the North China Plain](../publications/af9ce863ed02a1f408e4.md)

Zeeshan Zafar; Jingwei Wu; Shiqiang Zhang; Guoqing Lei; Yuanyuan Zha

ABSTRACT Drought severely threatens agricultural productivity and water resources in the North China Plain \(NCP\)\. This study provides a spatiotemporal analysis and prediction of agricultural drought from 2001 to 2024 using the Vegetation Health Index \(VHI\) derived from satellite data\. Meteorological \(air temperature, precipitation\) and environmental variables \(soil moisture, evapotranspiration, leaf area index, enhanced vegetation index\) were analysed\. A multi‐method approach, including trend analysis, wavelet coherence, Granger causality, and structural equation modelling \(SEM\), revealed that air temperature is the dominant negative driver of vegetation health \( β = −0\.444, p &lt; 0\.001\), while soil moisture \( β = 0\.297, p &lt; 0\.001\) and vegetation greenness, particularly EVI \( β = 0\.906, p &lt; 0\.001\), exert significant positive influences\. The northern and central NCP were identified as persistent drought hotspots\. Three prediction models, Long Short‐Term Memory \(LSTM\), Random Forest \(RF\), and ARIMAX, were evaluated\. LSTM showed the best overall performance, achieving the lowest RMSE \(3\.23\) and highest R 2 \(0\.781\), indicating its potential to capture complex temporal dynamics, while ARIMAX exhibited relatively higher forecast uncertainty\. Feature importance analysis consistently identified temperature, evapotranspiration, and vegetation as important drivers across all models\. This research highlights LSTM as a promising approach for agricultural drought prediction in the NCP and emphasises the roles of thermal stress and soil moisture deficit in supporting drought mitigation and sustainable water management\.

## [Aluminium Downstreaming Business Development in Indonesia: a PESTEL and Stakeholder Mapping Approach](../publications/afa015e45933ff4bc329.md)

Muhammad Rahmat; Feriansyah; Eduardus Budi Nursanto; Fadhila Maulida; Rezky Hermawan; Azrina Rahmah

Background: Downstreaming is an industrial strategy to increase value added from natural resources, and in Indonesia aluminium has strong potential due to large bauxite reserves and rising global demand, yet its downstream development remains constrained by limited alumina capacity and low diversification into higher value\-added products\.Purpose: The study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how Indonesia’s aluminium business model can be strengthened by analyzing external factors influencing downstreaming development and mapping the roles of key stakeholders within the aluminium value chain\.Design/methodology/approach: The study employs a qualitative analytical approach by integrating PESTEL analysis to assess key political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal factors influencing aluminium downstreaming, alongside stakeholder mapping to identify actor roles, interests, and interrelationships within the industry ecosystem\. Data are collected through desk studies, FGDs, and in\-depth interviews, with findings synthesized to inform strategic and policy recommendations for strengthening Indonesia’s aluminium industry\.Findings/Result: The results show that government downstreaming policies, increasing global aluminium demand, and domestic bauxite availability support industry development\. However, major constraints include high energy requirements, technological dependence, environmental compliance, and regulatory complexity\. Stakeholder mapping indicates that effective coordination among government institutions, energy providers, investors, and local communities is essential\.Conclusion: This study concludes that integrated industrial planning, clean energy utilization, regulatory clarity, and stakeholder coordination are required to support sustainable aluminium downstreaming in Indonesia\.Originality/value \(State of the art\): This study applies an integrated approach combining PESTEL analysis and stakeholder mapping to provide a comprehensive assessment of external factors and actor interactions, offering a framework for policy and collaborative governance in Indonesia’s aluminium downstream industry\. Keywords: alumunium downstreaming, business development, industrial policy, PESTEL analysis, stakeholder mapping

## [Effect of Dispersion Morphology of Graphene in Polyoxymethylene/Polyurethane Multiphase System on Wear Resistance Properties](../publications/afa36390cdf489949eb2.md)

Yiting Que; Xingrui Su; Hongli Xie; Shibing Bai

ABSTRACT Polyoxymethylene \(POM\) features inherent self‐lubrication, excellent chemical resistance, and low cost, making it a common matrix for wear‐resistant polymer composites\. In the modification research of POM, the thermoplastic polyurethane elastomer \(TPU\) toughening of POM has been industrialized, yet it only slightly improves wear resistance\. Therefore, in this study, solid‐state shear milling technology \(S 3 M\) was used to modify the multi‐phase system of POM/TPU with graphene, changing the dispersion degree of graphene in both phases to make a significant enhancement of wear‐resistant properties of the composites\. The mechanism of its wear‐resistant properties was investigated\. The results showed that, after graphene was decarboxylated via silane coupling agent KH‐570, S 3 M drives graphene to migrate from the TPU dispersed phase into the POM continuous matrix\. The spherical POM/TPU hybrid microstructures are consequently formed on friction interfaces, acting as microscale ball bearings converting sliding friction into rolling friction\. This structural evolution significantly lowers the friction coefficient and specific wear rate of composites\. Additionally, due to the decarboxylation of graphene, the thermal properties of the multiphase composites relatively increase\. The friction coefficient is reduced from 0\.32 to 0\.15, and the specific wear rate is reduced from 6\.28 × 10 −6 mm 3 /\(N·m\) to 5\.5 × 10 −6 mm 3 /\(N·m\), which greatly improves the wear performance\.

## [From Relevant Memories to Sufficient Evidence: Rethinking Memory Utilization in LLM Agents](../publications/afa40d1bf240fe4ee231.md)

Shixuan Li; Wei Yang; Peiyu Zhang; Anzhe Cheng; Heng Ping; Xiaole Zhang; Jesse Thomason; Xuezhe Ma; Yue Zhao; Paul Bogdan

Long\-term memory enables LLM agents to reuse past experiences, yet retrieving relevant memories does not necessarily provide sufficient evidence for answering a query\. Essential information may remain fragmented across memory records, obscured by abstraction, or disconnected from the relations required for reasoning\. We identify this relevance\-sufficiency gap and propose QEMem, a framework that reformulates memory utilization as the construction of query\-specific evidence sets, shifting the focus from individual retrieval relevance to collective evidential support\. QEMem integrates three complementary mechanisms: query\-guided discovery retrieves evidence across multiple memory granularities; source\-grounded reification organizes it into structured ViewCards with explicit evidential roles and source references; and sufficiency\-guided refinement selectively recovers missing information\. Operating on existing memory stores without modifying memory formation, QEMem achieves 91\.43% LLM\-judge accuracy on LoCoMo with Claude Opus 4\.5, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline, MemR$^3$, by 7\.6 percentage points and NEMORI by 10\.7 points under a shared memory store\. Further analyses demonstrate improved evidence coverage and strong performance on questions requiring cross\-session evidence integration\.

## [Trends in the Implementation of Forensic Auditing in Colombia](../publications/afa85c51e9e4115fa837.md)

Danna Alexandra Rosales Cañizares; Sara Elizabeth Yela Eraso

Forensic auditing represents a relevant tool for the prevention and detection of financial fraud and the strengthening of control processes within organizations; however, in Colombia there are still conceptual, training, technological and methodological challenges that limited its implementation and development\. In this context, the research aimed to analyze the trends related to the implementation of forensic auditing in Colombia, considering its evolution, main methodologies, tools and contributions to the prevention and detection of fraud\. Methodologically, the study was developed under the positivist paradigm, with a quantitative approach, empirical\-analytical method and descriptive type of research, through a systematic review of literature based on the Kitchenham protocol\. The population was constituted by scientific production related to forensic auditing, after applying criteria of inclusion, exclusion and quality studies retrieved through Redalyc, Google Scholar, DOAJ and ScienceDirect, 50 articles published between 2020 and 2025 were selected; for the collection and organization of the information, a data extraction matrix was used\. The results showed trends towards a preventive approach, integration with internal control and risk management, and the incorporation of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence\. It was concluded that forensic auditing advanced towards preventive, technological, and interdisciplinary approaches to strengthen fraud detection and organizational control\.

## [Alfalfa\-Yolo: a boundary\-aware lightweight framework for real\-time weed detection in alfalfa fields](../publications/afb75d2b625c8ad9b6a6.md)

Jingyi Wang; Kai Li; Tao Zhou; Yuanjun Xu; Yiwen Gao; Changzhong Li; Yanhua Zhao

Accurate weed detection in alfalfa fields is hindered by morphological similarity between crops and weeds at the seedling stage, substantial scale variation across weed targets, and degradation of fine spatial information during feature resampling\. To address these challenges, Alfalfa\-Yolo is proposed as a boundary\-aware compact detection framework integrating three complementary components\. The Edge\-Perception Global Transfer Network \(EPGTNet\) uses bidirectional Sobel responses and cross\-layer transmission to preserve edge\-related high\-frequency cues in deeper semantic features\. The Multi\-Scale Adaptive Feature Pyramid Network \(MSAFPN\) replaces static concatenation with attention\-guided aggregation to adaptively regulate multi\-scale contributions\. The Enhanced Channel Shuffle Upsampling Module \(ECSM\) combines depthwise convolution, channel shuffle, and spatial shift to enhance local spatial representation after upsampling\. On the self\-constructed alfalfa\-field dataset comprising 1,100 independent original field images, Alfalfa\-Yolo achieves 77\.6% mAP@0\.5 and 55\.9% mAP@0\.5:0\.95 with 2\.67 M parameters\. Independent\-dataset benchmarking on CottonWeedDet12 and ImageWeeds confirms that the architecture remains competitive after target\-dataset retraining, while a separate zero\-shot cross\-dataset protocol directly evaluates transfer without target\-domain training\. Deployment tests on NVIDIA RTX 4090, NVIDIA Orin NX, and RK3588 further characterize the accuracy\-efficiency trade\-off under different hardware and quantization settings\. These results indicate that Alfalfa\-Yolo provides a compact and practically deployable solution for real\-time weed localization in alfalfa fields\.

## [Multi\-Perspective explainability in traffic prediction: A neuro\-symbolic approach using CNN\-LSTMs and concept lattices](../publications/afb834971c42fb521d0c.md)

Suraya Syazwani Mohamad Yusof; Hadhrami Ab Ghani; Nurul Izrin Md Saleh; Nurulaqilla Khamis

The rapid urbanization and continuous growth of vehicle ownership have escalated traffic congestion into a critical socioeconomic challenge, resulting in massive productivity losses and environmental degradation\. To establish effective Intelligent Transportation Systems \(ITS\), reliable and accurate traffic forecasting is paramount\. While deep learning \(DL\) algorithms, particularly Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) and Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNN\), have established themselves as state\-of\-the\-art for spatiotemporal sequence forecasting, their inherent “black\-box” nature severely limits their practical deployment in high\-stakes traffic management\. Decision\-makers require transparent, qualitative reasoning behind algorithmic forecasts\. Current post\-hoc numerical Explainable AI \(XAI\) methods, such as SHAP and Integrated Gradients \(IG\), quantify feature attribution but fail to provide structured, human\-readable rule mapping\. To bridge the gap between predictive performance and model transparency, this paper proposes a novel Neuro\-Symbolic Explainable Deep Learning framework\. We integrate the statistical learning power of a hybrid CNN\-LSTM architecture \(the ’Neural’ component\) with the rigorous logical reasoning of Formal Concept Analysis \(the ’Symbolic’ component\)\. Validated on an extensive real\-world, five\-year multivariate dataset from PLUS Malaysia Berhad \(encompassing 73,891 aggregated records across multiple vehicle classes\), the CNN\-LSTM consistently outperforms standalone LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU baselines, achieving the lowest Root Mean Squared Error \(RMSE\) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error \(MAPE\)\. Furthermore, the synthesis of FCA with SHAP, LIME, and IG establishes a consensus view of feature importance, explicitly proving that the hybrid predictive\-symbolic framework yields robust, highly accurate, and thoroughly interpretable forecasts suitable for modern ITS architectures\.

## [ZAPP: a zero\-aware photovoltaic power prediction framework](../publications/afb8d948137e8d9c3845.md)

Ahmet Gürhanlı; Vedat Esen

Predicting photovoltaic power generator outputs is not easy, especially when the values are near zero, because even very small errors can lead to large percentage errors\. We introduce a new forecasting framework, ZAPP \(Zero\-Aware Photovoltaic Power Predictor\), that handles near\-zero errors while maintaining high prediction accuracy\. The model does not rely on a single unified regression model but instead attaches two refinement stages to a base regression model\. The first stage, called ZeroGate, predicts whether the output should be zero\. The second refinement stage, the low\-power MAPE reducer, fine\-tunes the non\-zero outputs near the zero level without significantly affecting scale\-dependent regression metrics\. The datasets are divided into training, validation, and test sets in chronological order, ensuring that test data is not used during model development, threshold tuning, ensemble weighting, or calibration\. Experimental evaluation included base models such as Persistence, Ridge, XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, and a hybrid Ridge–XGBoost model\. Two separate datasets are employed to strengthen the quality of the results\. For the hybrid model, sMAPE fell from 60\.57% to 11\.07% on Dataset 1\. Its final MAE, RMSE, and R 2 were 22\.37, 60\.72, and 0\.9637, respectively\. On Dataset 2, sMAPE decreased from 63\.30% to 11\.92%, with MAE = 52\.24, RMSE = 144\.60, and R 2 = 0\.9559\. The zero\-aware correction mainly reduced percentage errors without weakening the overall regression results\.

## [Psycho\-social correlates of prosocial\-productivity in a sample of entrepreneurs in Peru](../publications/afcda8401ad38b694ef1.md)

Ángela Vera Ruíz; César Andrés Llanco Gonzales; Agustín Espinosa

This study examines a dual\-path structural model suggesting that similar prosocial\-productivity outcomes may emerge from psychologically distinct configurations\. prosocial\-productivity is conceptualized as entrepreneurial behavior that deliberately integrates social and economic value creation\. A cross\-sectional survey of 506 entrepreneurs operating in Peru employed validated measures of personality traits, personal values, empathic concern, appreciation for sustainable practices, and prosocial\-productivity\. Correlational and path analyses identified two differentiated structural routes\. The “genuine” pathway is associated with compassion, self transcendence values, empathic concern, and sustainability orientation, reflecting a coherent prosocial psychological configuration\. In contrast, the “dark shortcut” pathway links prosocial\-productivity to narcissism and self enhancement values, suggesting an instrumental configuration in which socially oriented outcomes may align with self promotional tendencies\. Although both pathways converge behaviorally, they diverge in their underlying psychological structure, revealing an ethical tension\. Interpreted within a Latin American context marked by inequality and institutional fragility, these findings underscore the situated nature of prosocial\-productivity and provide correlational evidence of heterogeneous psychological configurations underlying value integrative entrepreneurship\.

## [A case report of intracardiac cement embolism after percutaneous kyphoplasty](../publications/afdb15d5791c1ca68db1.md)

Qi Shu

Leakage of bone cement is a common complication after percutaneous kyphoplasty, and this complication has a wide time window: symptoms may appear immediately after surgery, or develop days, months, or even years later\. Although intracardiac cement embolism is extremely rare, reporting such cases can provide reference for similar clinical cases in the future\. A 68\-year\-old female patient developed abdominal distension, chest tightness and dyspnea 5 days after undergoing percutaneous kyphoplasty\. Comprehensive analysis of preoperative and postoperative imaging indicated that these symptoms were possibly related to bone cement leakage from the 7th thoracic vertebra \(T7\), which occurred after the patient received surgery at another hospital three months prior, although a definitive causal relationship could not be established based on the available evidence\. The patient was immediately transferred to the intensive care unit \(ICU\) for symptomatic supportive treatment\. After receiving treatment in the ICU, her symptoms resolved, but she declined the recommendation for further surgery\. At the 3\-month and 6\-month follow\-up appointments after discharge, the patient had returned to normal life and reported no subjective discomfort\. This case highlights the risk of bone cement\-induced cardiac embolism after PKP, and suggests that routine chest X\-ray examination should be performed, with further echocardiography and chest CT examinations arranged when necessary\. This approach can help identify asymptomatic patients with pulmonary or intracardiac cement embolism, and thus prevent the development of severe cardiopulmonary failure\.

## [Availability\-Aware Multitask Learning for Robust Clinical Prediction from Incomplete Electronic Health Records](../publications/afdc4ef6b911ac61ba43.md)

Zhainagul Khamitova; Gulmira Omarova; Akerke Akanova; Aliya Abdukarimova; Kuanysh Kadirkulov; Bagdat Satayev; Aliya Beissegul; Abdugani Kholbekov; Gulnoz Dzhiyanmuratova; Aizat Amirbay

This study presents NORIA, an availability\-aware multitask learning framework for clinical prediction from incomplete electronic health records \(EHRs\)\. We analyzed a public dataset of 77,724 patients and 107 numerical features\. To prevent temporal leakage, predictors were grouped by availability, and training\-only feature selection identified three baseline and two first\-year variables\. NORIA jointly predicts baseline and updated glycemic control, an HbA1c change index, and 21 medication labels using shared representations, masked training, and stage\-specific prediction updates\. Comparators included classical machine learning, gradient boosting, deep tabular models, and multitask architectures \(MMoE and PLE\)\. On the internal test set, NORIA achieved AUROCs of 0\.8554 and 0\.8888 for baseline and updated glycemic control, respectively, and medication macro\-AP of 0\.1854 versus 0\.1879 for CatBoost\. The predefined medication improvement criterion was not met\. With 20% of baseline features artificially masked, updated\-control AUROC declined by 0\.0271 for NORIA, versus 0\.0510 for CatBoost and 0\.0542 for FT\-Transformer\. Ablation analyses indicated that masked training provided the clearest robustness benefit\. NORIA thus demonstrated competitive accuracy and robustness in selected simulated missing\-data scenarios, without establishing overall superiority\.

## [Everything but the Signature: A Proposal for AI\-Born Journals](../publications/b005f313031c34f6c405.md)

Luciano Floridi

A journal’s distinctive contribution to scholarly communication lies neither in dissemination nor in storage, nor even in certification considered alone, but in the act by which certification is bound to the durable trust accumulated by the journal and to the reward conferred by its imprimatur: an act grounded in the judgement of the journal’s referees and editorial board, for which named editors accept answerability under uncertainty\. I call that binding the editorial signature , and argue that its irreducible core is not the cognitive judgement that goes into it, which artificial intelligence \(AI\) may match or surpass, but the answerability of those who sign it, which no advance in capability can assume on their behalf\. What surrounds the signature is infrastructure , and it is costly: on my estimate, an author spends 17 to 18 h formatting and feeding submission systems for each published paper, which comes to tens of millions of researcher\-hours a year, and an AI\-born workflow could bring the per\-paper figure to about an hour\. Since 2001, the cumulative labour in my baseline scenario amounts to some 700 million hours, or around 350,000 person\-years, comparable in magnitude to Battelle’s estimated direct job\-years from US human genome sequencing and its associated industry\. AI is the first technology, since the modern journal apparatus took shape, that can absorb this infrastructure while leaving the signature in human hands, because it can do the delegable labour but cannot bear the answerability\. Therefore, I propose a new class of AI\-born journals , defined by necessary architectural features and governance controls, and I set out what such journals would owe their authors, reviewers, and readers\.

## [Multiple strategies to improve the therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell‑derived exosome transplantation in ischemic stroke \(Review\)](../publications/b008800f821f4b421bb2.md)

Xu Yan; Xiaolei Zhou; Wenhui Zeng; Jiabing Wang; Lin Zhou; Lincai Li; Zhengwei Zou; Cixiang Chen; Yichi Zhang; Zhengyi He; Junsong Ye

Ischemic stroke \(IS\) is a common cause of physical disability and death worldwide\.Although it has been indicated that mesenchymal stem cells \(MScs\) can treat IS through mechanisms such as immunomodulation, angiogenesis and neuroprotection, their clinical application is limited by inherent drawbacks, such as immune rejection risk and tumorigenic potential\.Notably, MSc\-derived exosomes \(MSc\-Exos\) possess advantages, such as a smaller volume, low immunogenicity and low tumorigenicity, enabling therapeutic effects similar to those of the parent cells\.Furthermore, MSc\-Exos can carry various bioactive substances and cross the blood\-brain barrier \(BBB\), thus indicating their potential in the diagnosis, treatment and prognostic assessment of IS\.The present review comprehensively elaborates on the principles by which MSc\-Exos may treat IS through mechanisms such as inhibiting inflammatory responses, suppressing apoptosis, promoting angiogenesis, regulating ferroptosis and maintaining BBB integrity\.However, the therapeutic efficacy of MSC\-Exo monotherapy is restricted by its low brain bioavailability, short lesion retention time, insufficient in vivo stability and inability to remain at the lesion site for an extended period of time to exert its effect\.Furthermore, the review summarizes the recent optimization strategies involving the combination of MSc\-Exos with microRNAs, traditional chinese medicine, hydrogels, exosome pretreatment and electroacupuncture to enhance the efficacy of MSc\-Exo therapy for IS, and systematically reviews their synergistic therapeutic mechanisms\.In addition, the current status of clinical translation, technical breakthrough obstacles and future development directions for MSc\-Exo combination therapies in neurological diseases is outlined, providing a theoretical reference for innovative treatments of IS\.

## [Multi\-parameter optimization of recombinant protein secretion in Bacillus subtilis: a review](../publications/b0184f201f29cf966e96.md)

Askar Kholikov; Khushnut Vokhidov; Алимова Барно Хасановна; Ozodakhon Pulatova; Yulong Zhang; Shihui Yang; Guimin Zhang; Yihua Chen; Махсумханов Ахмаджан Аъзамханович

Abstract Bacillus subtilis is widely recognized as one of the most robust and versatile hosts for recombinant protein production\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the protein secretion pathway in B\. subtilis , detailing its mechanistic basis and key limiting steps\. We discuss the structural features of signal peptides \(SPs\) that govern efficient translocation and highlight recent advances in de novo promoter and signal peptide engineering\. A particular focus is placed on the integration of artificial intelligence \(AI\) to predict and design optimal genetic elements\. Drawing on findings from combinatorial and multi\-parameter studies, we propose that future engineering strategies should move beyond maximizing individual parameters\. Instead, achieving a dynamic balance across transcriptional, translational and secretion layers is essential to sustain high productivity while minimizing cellular secretion stress\. This review offers a roadmap for systems\-level engineering of B\. subtilis as a next\-generation protein production platform\.

## [Shape\-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid\-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning](../publications/b019836ca8ae433bcdd7.md)

Yanming Zhou; Yuchen Liu; Ahmed H\. Qureshi

Rigid\-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments\. This coupling makes planning chal\- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry\. We propose Shape\- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics\-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel\-time, or cost\- to\-go, representation for rigid\-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions\. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling\-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses\. We evaluate the framework across 2D and 3D rigid\- body planning tasks and non\-prehensile manipulation through object pushing in diverse environments\. Results show substantial improvements in planning success and inference efficiency over physics\-informed neural planning baselines, while remaining competitive with classical sampling\-based planners at significantly lower planning times\. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of both the learned representation and the proposed planning strategy\. Finally, closed\-loop pushing experiments under execution deviations and external disturbances demonstrate that fast replanning enables reactive and adaptive task execution\.

## [Rivera\-Novoa, Angel &amp; Duarte Arias, Daniel Augusto: Generative Artificial Intelligences and Extended Cognition in Science Learning Contexts](../publications/b0254a0184c2bbeb37cb.md)



\_Science &amp; Education\_ 2025:1\-22\. 2025This paper philosophically examines the impact of generative artificial intelligence on learning processes from the perspective of extended cognition\. The central problem addressed is how these technologies can transform students into passive or active learners, influencing the development of cognitive skills\. It will be argued that generative artificial intelligence presents risks of diminishing cognitive activity among students, as it is likely to substitute—rather than complement—the cognitive subject\. It will also be argued that there are ways to leverage generative artificial intelligence so that learners are not passive but rather active cognitive subjects\. Three cases will be presented, with empirical support, to show how this leveraging is possible: the production of feedback, assistive technologies, and gamification\. In these cases, generative artificial intelligence is a complementary cognitive artifact rather than a substitutive one\. To achieve this goal, the paper presents the framework of the extended mind thesis as a conducive scenario for analyzing the relationship between generative artificial intelligence and learning contexts, and it analyzes specific cases of science education\. An analysis of the types of cognitive artifacts will also be conducted to examine how generative artificial intelligence intervenes in learning in both substitute and complementary ways\.

## [Reconstructing Palladian Symmetry: Quotient Trees and House\-and\-Wing Morphospace](../publications/b02a90f1e5b30b086e3a.md)

Sabri Gökmen

Abstract Palladio’s villas have long been interpreted through proportion, harmonic ratios, typology, and generative rules, yet wings and barchesse remain less developed as computational objects than the compact house plans\. This article presents an inside\-out graph method for constructing and comparing symmetry in sixteen villa and country\-house plans traced from I quattro libri dell’architettura \. Unlike justified access graphs rooted in space syntax studies, the method begins at the central sala or an identified principal symmetry root and reconstructs formal relations toward rooms, porticoes, wings, and estate\-scale dependencies using quotient trees\. Two measures are defined for the resulting morphospace analysis: symmetry propagation depth, which records the mean depth of quotient tree leaves, and Symmetry Reticulation Index, which records surplus relations in the collapsed quotient graph\. The results separate outward extension from quotient\-graph reticulation\. Barbaro propagates deeply while remaining tree\-like, Ragona is comparatively compact but highly reticulated, and Thiene combines maximum propagation with substantial surplus structure\. The framework therefore identifies Palladian symmetry as an inside\-out relational morphology whose extension and reticulation can be measured independently\.

## [Electronic System\-Level Optimization of Network Slicing and Resource Allocation for 6G URLLC Applications](../publications/b02c839e77646a951f65.md)

Luma Abd Al\-Kareem Hussein

In this paper, we propose a complete mathematical framework for optimizing network slicing and resource allocation at the electronic system\-level \(ESL\) of 6G ultra\-reliable low\-latency communication \(URLLC\)\. We present a multi\-dimensional, non\-convex mixed\-integer stochastic optimization problem that jointly optimizes slice admission control, radio resource block \(RRB\) allocation and transmit power distribution, computation offloading decisions, reconfigurable intelligent surface \(RIS\) phase\-shift beamforming configurations and fronthaul/backhaul capacity partitioning under heterogeneous traffic demands and stringent quality\-of\-service \(QoS\) constraints\. The proposed model incorporates finite block length \(FBL\) information theory, Lyapunov drift\-plus\-penalty stochastic control, and deep reinforcement learning \(DRL\)\-assisted dynamic orchestration\. Numerical results confirm reliability and low end\-to\-end latency across heterogeneous slice types\.

## [A study on three\-stage integration of generative artificial intelligence in architectural design based on human\-in\-the\-loop](../publications/b0301fc61fee88739dc6.md)

Shuangbo Ren; Yawei Liu; Rumei Liu

The swift advancement of artificial intelligence has posed new demands on the architectural industry’s transformation\. Generative AI \(GAI\) enables the digitization of architectural design experience, offering fresh inspiration for architectural scheme generation\. This study develops a human\-in\-the\-loop three\-phase framework that distinguishes concept generation, scheme deepening, and result expression while adding explicit decision gates and cross\-cutting controls for architectural knowledge, performance verification, data provenance, and professional accountability\. This study starts by leveraging VOSviewer software to visualize and analyze keyword co\-occurrences in GAI\-related literature, summarizing GAI’s development trends and hotspots\. Then, it outlines GAI’s application stages in architectural design, namely concept generation, scheme deepening, and result expression\. It also lists 20 generative design software useful for architectural scheme design\. Subsequently, taking Midjourney, NOAH, and Stable Diffusion as examples, it explores GAI’s specific application scenarios across these three design stages\. Finally, it proposes a new architectural design model shaped by GAI\. The contribution is not a new sequence of conventional design stages, but an operational phase\-control matrix that specifies inputs, outputs, human decisions, verification requirements, and feedback loops\. It accelerates inspiration image generation, thereby influencing design thinking and processes, meanwhile it provides a cautious, reproducible framework for selecting and governing GAI tools in architectural design\.

## [Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on\-charger coordination](../publications/b03d943aa1cc8fb6dc87.md)

Yehui Li; Xueyuan Cui; Chongqing Kang; Thomas Morstyn; Yue Wang

The large\-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging\. Here, we show that on\-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle\-grid coordination\. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource\-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization\. Validated on a high\-fidelity hardware\-in\-the\-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber\-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96\.1% and communication overhead by 74\.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme\. Moreover, unlocking this hardware\-level flexibility achieves a 10\.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation\. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040\. Uncoordinated electric vehicle charging strains microgrids, yet advanced control exceeds charger hardware limits\. Here, the authors develop a lightweight on\-charger coordination framework that unlocks vehicle flexibility with low memory and communication needs\.

## [R\-spondins suppress adipogenic differentiation in fibro\-adipogenic progenitors via autocrine WNT/β\-catenin signaling](../publications/b04084beda0658584bf7.md)

Jennifer Fransisca; Younjeong Oh; Bagus Sarmito; Nurkyz Alymkulova; Yongsung Hwang; Jeong Kyo Yoon

Introduction Fibro‐adipogenic progenitors \(FAPs\) are muscle‐resident stromal cells that support skeletal muscle regeneration and homeostasis but can drive pathological adipogenesis\. In this study, we investigated the role of R‐spondins \(RSPOs\), a family of WNT signaling modulators, in FAP adipogenic differentiation\. Methods FAPs were differentiated in adipogenic induction medium \(AIM\) supplemented with RSPO2 or RSPO3 in combination with WNT3A, followed by assessment of adipogenic differentiation using western blot and Oil Red O \(ORO\) analyses\. siRNA‐mediated knockdown of Rspo 2, Rspo 3, and Ctnnb1 , as well as constitutive activation of β\-catenin, was performed to investigate their roles in FAP adipogenesis\. For in vivo validation, a mixture of recombinant RSPO3 and WNT3A was injected into glycerol‐injured tibialis anterior muscles, followed by assessment of adipogenesis and transcriptomic analysis\. Results Here, we identify Rspo 2 and Rspo 3 as key autocrine regulators of FAP fate through modulation of WNT/β‐catenin signaling\. Their siRNA‐mediated knockdown markedly enhances FAP adipogenic differentiation\. Conversely, RSPO2 and RSPO3 synergize with WNT3A to suppress FAP adipogenesis, an effect dependent on β‐catenin as demonstrated by attenuation following Ctnnb1 knockdown\. Constitutive β‐catenin activation similarly restrains adipogenic differentiation\. In vivo , intramuscular delivery of recombinant RSPO3 and WNT3A proteins significantly reduces ectopic adipogenesis induced in glycerol‐injured tibialis anterior muscle, accompanied by downregulation of adipogenic markers and transcriptional programs\. Discussion Collectively, these findings establish RSPO2 and RSPO3 as previously unrecognized suppressors of FAP adipogenesis acting through canonical WNT/β‐catenin signaling\.

## [AI\-Powered Scoring System for Detecting Drug\-Drug Interaction Insights from Scientific Literature](../publications/b042b506dd9ba40bc2b3.md)

Charbel Alhelou; Nour Allam

Background and Objective: Drug\-drug interactions \(DDIs\) present major challenges in clinical care, impacting patient safety and therapeutic outcomes\. Traditional detection methods, often based on curated databases, may miss newly emerging interactions or require frequent manual updates\. Recent advances in natural language processing \(NLP\) and artificial intelligence \(AI\) offer novel tools for real\-time, automated DDI detection directly from biomedical literature\. This study introduces an AI\-powered approach to identify DDIs, assign relevance scores to publications, and benchmark performance against conventional databases\. Methods: We developed an NLP pipeline incorporating sentence classification to detect safety and interaction\-related content, and named entity recognition \(NER\) to extract drug\-drug interaction types, their clinical impact, and patient features\. The sentence classification module is based on a BERT architecture fine\-tuned from microsoft/BiomedNLP\-BiomedBERT\-baseuncased\-abstract\-fulltext, and the NER module uses the open\-source model d4data/biomedical\-ner\-all\. A DDI relevance score was designed to quantify each article’s significance based on weighted parameters derived from model outputs, with weights informed by domain experts \(title relevance: 50 points, DDI impact: 40 points, publication type: 10 points\)\. The system was validated on a manually curated dataset\. We applied ANOVA and sensitivity analyses, and evaluated performance using recall, precision, and F1\-score, comparing our method to established DDI resources\. Key Content and Findings: The pipeline was validated on 7,751 articles across 15 query types\. ROC analysis identified a relevance score threshold of 75%\. Drug\-family queries achieved the highest F1\-score \(0\.872\), followed by single\-drug \(0\.731\) and drug\-drug queries \(0\.684\)\. ANOVA and Tukey post\-hoc analysis confirmed statistically significant differences in relevance scores between annotation groups \(p &lt; 0\.05\), with full stratification across all three groups for drug\-drug family queries\. Compared with manually compiled expert reference lists, our system retrieved substantially more relevant articles without requiring manual updates\. Conclusion: AI\-driven NLP approaches can enhance clinical decision support systems by providing comprehensive, evidence\-based DDI detection and prioritization, offering scalable support for safer pharmacological decision\-making\. Keywords: Drug\-drug Interactions; Natural Language Processing; Artificial Intelligence; Pharmacovigilance; Clinical Decision Support\.

## [How crime data incompleteness shapes ethnic disparities in predictive policing: evidence from Chicago](../publications/b0499e8e854bf9e18e57.md)

Mengqin K\. Jiang; Federico Liberatore; Alun D\. Preece

Purpose: Fairness in Predictive Policing \(PP\) has been explored by many researchers\. However, to the best of our knowledge, no work has quantified the impact of event\-level data incompleteness in spatio\-temporal prediction on each ethnicity\. In this paper, we propose a model to quantify the impact of recorded crime data incompleteness on ethnic disparities in policing\. We also examine whether these disparities depend on where in the city data are missing\. Methods: We introduce a neighbourhood\-level method that allocates PP prediction errors \(false positives as potential over\-policing, false negatives as potential under\-policing\) to ethnic groups in proportion to their share of the neighbourhood population\. Using Chicago crime records \(2022\-2024\), census data, and HAGEN \(a state\-of\-the\-art spatial\-temporal PP model\), we explore data incompleteness by reducing the original crime data at varying ratios in two settings: \(i\) 25\-100% reductions in neighbourhoods with low racial diversity; \(ii\) 50% or 100% reductions in communities dominated by a single ethnicity \(Hispanic, Non\-Hispanic Black, Non\-Hispanic White, or Non\-Hispanic Asian\)\. Enforcement bias outcomes are then compared across ethnicities and scenarios\. Results: Removing records from a single\-ethnicity\-majority community generally reduces predicted over\-policing and increases predicted under\-policing for that ethnicity across the whole study area, with Asian\-majority scenarios a consistent exception\. In low\-diversity neighbourhoods, greater missingness amplifies prediction bias against Non\-Hispanic Black residents specifically: predicted over\-policing falls and predicted under\-policing rises, with the opposite holding for other groups\. The largest overall shifts occur when data are removed from Black\-majority communities\. Conclusions: Incomplete crime records could propagate into substantial, ethnically unequal disparities in model\-predicted policing exposure, whose direction depends on where missingness concentrates\. The findings motivate auditing missingness and its demographic distribution as a prerequisite for deploying event\-level PP systems\.

Olha Honchar; Ігор Миколайович Скрипник; O\. Ye\. Akimov

Introduction\. Non\-Q\-wave myocardial infarction is accompanied by changes in nitric oxide metabolism and the stress response\. The biochemical effects of adding temgicoluril to standard treatment require clarification\.Aim\. To assess changes in nitric oxide synthase isoform activity, nitrite, peroxynitrite and cortisol concentrations during standard therapy with or without temgicoluril\.Materials and methods\. The prospective study included 40 patients \(mean age 62\.9±11\.7 years, mean±standard deviation\), divided into two groups of 20\. Both groups received standard therapy and multidisciplinary rehabilitation\. Group 2 additionally received temgicoluril, 500 mg three times daily for one month\. Blood biochemical parameters were assessed before and after treatment and compared with those of 20 control participants\.Results\. Biochemical values are means ± standard errors\. Before treatment, both patient groups had lower endothelial enzyme activity and higher neuronal enzyme activity, nitrite, peroxynitrite and cortisol concentrations than controls\. Baseline values did not differ significantly between treatment groups\. Endothelial nitric oxide synthase activity increased in both groups during treatment, while nitrite, peroxynitrite and cortisol concentrations decreased\. After treatment, nitrite concentrations were 1\.25±0\.04 nmol/L in group 1 and 1\.00±0\.04 nmol/L in group 2\. Endothelial enzyme activity was lower in group 2 than in group 1 \(0\.34±0\.005 versus 0\.41±0\.001 µmol/min per g protein\)\. Inducible and neuronal enzyme activities were higher in group 2, whereas peroxynitrite concentrations did not differ significantly between groups\. Cortisol decreased from 252\.2±9\.2 to 67\.2±1\.2 nmol/L in group 1 and from 278\.5±10\.8 to 126\.2±3\.4 nmol/L in group 2\. Endothelial enzyme activity remained below the control value in both groups\.Conclusions\. Both regimens were associated with changes in nitric oxide metabolism and a decline in cortisol\. Temgicoluril use was associated with lower post\-treatment nitrite but higher cortisol concentrations than standard therapy alone\. These biochemical differences do not establish superior endothelial recovery or a clinical advantage of the additional treatment\.

## [Oxytocin signaling bidirectionally modulates serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus](../publications/b08955073616f74689eb.md)

Ja Eun Choi; Yoon Kyoung Kim; Yongmin Sung; Dong Il Choi; Jooyoung Kim; Chaery Lee; Jisu Lee; Nam‐Kyung Yu; Han Kyoung Choe; Bong‐Kiun Kaang

The involvement of oxytocin in social behavior is well established, yet its interaction with neuromodulatory systems, such as serotonin and dopamine, remains incompletely understood\. Here, we utilized immunohistochemistry, anatomical tracing, chemogenetic, and ex vivo electrophysiological approaches primarily in male mice, with female mice used only for an additional anatomical tracing control experiment, investigate how oxytocin modulates serotonergic and dopaminergic neuronal populations\. Employing the dual\-eGRASP tool, we visualized oxytocinergic projections from the paraventricular nucleus \(PVN\) to the serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons in dorsal raphe nucleus \(DRN\)\. Blocking oxytocin receptors in the DRN attenuated social interaction behavior\. Additionally, analysis of c\-Fos levels and neuronal excitability revealed that oxytocin inhibits serotonergic neurons while activating dopaminergic neurons in the DRN\. Our findings suggest a bidirectional regulatory role of oxytocin signaling in the DRN serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons\. Significance Statement Social behavior relies on interactions among neuromodulatory systems, yet how oxytocin communicates with serotonin and dopamine circuits remains unclear\. We identify the DRN as a functionally relevant target of hypothalamic oxytocin neurons during social approach\. Using dual\-eGRASP, we visualize contacts from PVN oxytocin neurons onto both serotonergic and dopaminergic DRN\. Blocking oxytocin receptors in the DRN reduces social interaction without affecting locomotion\. Moreover, oxytocin suppresses serotonergic neuronal activity while increasing dopaminergic neuronal activation, revealing opposing control of two prosocial neuromodulatory populations within the same region\. These findings provide a circuit framework for how oxytocin coordinates social behavior through bidirectional modulation of dorsal raphe neuromodulators\.
