## [THE NATURE OF THE SOUL \(Volume 8 \)](../publications/b1b8b9e5a8af787c12e5.md)

Majid Karimi Baghmaleki

The eighth volume confronts the most forward\-looking dimension of the project\. Human beings are increasingly capable of modifying memory, attention, cognition, emotion, personality, neural activity, identity, and the relationship between biological and technological systems\. Brain–computer interfaces, artificial intelligence, neurotechnology, biotechnology, cognitive enhancement, memory engineering, personality modification, artificial consciousness, and hybrid human–machine systems raise a fundamental question: Can the architecture of the soul itself be engineered? If the answer is partially yes, then technological progress becomes more than an engineering problem\. It becomes a problem of personhood\. What happens when memory can be modified? What happens when personality can be redesigned? What happens when agency can be technologically enhanced or manipulated? What happens when artificial systems potentially acquire subjective organization? And what happens when biological and technological components become so deeply integrated that the distinction between human and machine becomes philosophically unstable? The final volume therefore develops principles concerning autonomy, cognitive liberty, mental sovereignty, identity security, agency preservation, consciousness integrity, hybrid personhood, artificial consciousness, and responsible soul engineering\. Its ultimate concern is not whether technology should simply be accepted or rejected\. It is whether future technologies can be developed without destroying the very subject whose capacities they are intended to enhance\. The final question of the eight\-volume work is consequently also its most demanding: How can humanity transform the soul without losing the person?

## [Artificial intelligence is not enough to enhance organizational performance](../publications/b1bcae89d25f554ecc50.md)

Michael Wang

This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), supply chain visibility, supplier integration, and organizational performance through the lens of Organizational Information Processing Theory \(OIPT\)\. Drawing on empirical data from UK\-based organizations that have adopted AI technologies, we employ structural equation modeling along with mediation and moderation analyses to test our hypotheses\. The findings indicate that AI does not have a significant direct effect on performance; instead, its impact is fully mediated through supply chain visibility and supplier integration\. This supports the view that AI\-driven supply chain visibility acts as an information\-processing mechanism that enhances firms&\#x27; ability to coordinate, collaborate, and integrate with supply chain partners, thereby improving organizational performance\. Furthermore, supply uncertainty positively moderates the relationship between supplier integration and performance, amplifying the benefits under conditions of higher uncertainty\. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying AI&\#x27;s indirect role in driving performance and highlighting the importance of embedding AI within broader organizational capabilities\. It also offers practical insights for managers seeking to leverage AI to enhance supply chain integration and organizational effectiveness\. • AI does not directly enhance organizational performance\. • AI\-enabled supply chain visibility strengthens supplier integration\. • Supply chain visibility and supplier integration jointly mediate the AI–performance link\. • Supplier integration contributes more strongly to performance under high supply uncertainty\. • The findings extend Organizational Information Processing Theory in AI\-enabled supply chains\.

## [EFFECTIVENESS OF VARIOUS FORMS OF ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION TREATMENT IN MEN WHO HAVE SUFFERED FROM THE CONSEQUENCES OF COMBAT](../publications/b1be3e1c08e1266fd229.md)

Mykola Z\. Vorobets; Dmytro Z\. Vorobets; Р\. В\. Фафула; Oksana V\. Melnyk; Mariia Kushynska; Zinoviy D\. Vorobets; Орест Мирославович Чемерис

Introduction\. The long\-term consequences of severe injuries sustained by combatants have a significant impact on quality of life and sexual function\. Post\-traumatic stress disorder, which develops as a result of injuries, is associated with the development of erectile dysfunction, decreased sexual desire, and premature ejaculation\.Aim\. Analysis of erectile function and quality of life indicators in men of different age groups injured as a result of combat operations before and after the end of treatment\.Materials and methods\. The study included the results of treatment and a questionnaire survey of 136 men with combat injuries and concomitant sexual dysfunction before and after treatment of the dysfunction\. To determine the health\-related quality of life, a questionnaire survey was conducted using the SF\-36 questionnaire\. The second criterion in differentiating the severity of ED was the sum of the scores of the answers to the questions of the International Index of Erectile Function\-5 \(IIEF\-5\) questionnaire\. According to the form of erectile dysfunction, patients were divided into two groups: Group 1 – patients with psychogenic erectile dysfunction after combat trauma; Group 2 – patients with erectile dysfunction of mixed genesis\.Results\. In patients of group 1 with a psychogenic form of ED, after treatment, a significant increase in the average score of the domains of general health, role\-physical functioning and role\-emotional functioning was observed\. With a mixed form of ED, as a result of treatment, patients observed significant improvements in role\-physical functioning and pain sensation\. After comprehensive treatment, in men with psychogenic ED, the average scores of the IIEF\-5 questionnaire domain regarding satisfaction with sexual life significantly increased from 2\.8 to 5\.5 and erectile function from 7\.2 to 16\.7\. In men with a mixed form of erectile dysfunction, erectile function increased the most during treatment, by 7\.3 scores\.Conclusions\. In men, after suffering combat injuries, both psychogenic and mixed forms of erectile dysfunction develop\. As a result of the treatment of erectile dysfunction of both psychogenic and mixed forms, general health, role\-physical and role\-emotional functioning improve\. After comprehensive treatment, men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction of both age groups significantly increased their indicators of satisfaction with sexual life and the erectile function domain\.

## [Reference study for biogenic carbon storage in the residential building stock](../publications/b1c282807d60572328f2.md)

Oana Iliescu; Ilmari Talvitie; Ali Amiri; Seppo Junnila

The built environment is both a major source of greenhouse gas emissions and an important area for climate mitigation through material choices, design and long\-term use\. Wood products can reduce emissions by substituting more carbon\-intensive construction materials while also storing biogenic carbon in buildings\. However, these benefits depend on how long buildings remain in use and how much carbon they retain over time\. This study examines residential buildings in Helsinki, Finland, to estimate observed stock survival, quantify cumulative biogenic carbon storage in the residential building stock, and compare the results with estimates based on replacement cycles and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s \(IPCC\) default 35\-year half\-life for harvested wood products \(HWP\)\. Results indicate high residential stock survival, with 92% of floor area still in use from the earliest study periods \(1921–39\)\. Timber buildings account for 40% of total biogenic carbon storage, despite representing only 10% of the gross floor area \(GFA\)\. The existing stock stores an estimated 266–285 kt C compared with 123 kt C predicted by the IPCC’s default half\-life estimation\. The results show that the IPCC’s default decay assumption produces substantially lower estimates when applied to long\-lived residential building components\. POLICY RELEVANCE This study provides empirical evidence on the survival of residential buildings and the associated long\-term storage of biogenic carbon in wood materials\. Helsinki’s existing residential stock stores approximately 266–285 kt C, indicating that long\-lived buildings form a relevant urban carbon stock\. The results also show that residential building survival is shaped not only by materials but also by stable housing demand as well as by institutional factors such as planning regulations, zoning, renovation programmes and heritage protection\. For policymakers, better empirical data on building survival and component replacement can improve assumptions used in whole\-life carbon assessment and evaluations of wood use in construction\. The comparison with the IPCC’s default 35\-year half\-life further shows the importance of distinguishing broad HWP accounting assumptions from the behaviour of long\-lived wood products in residential buildings\.

## [Clustering Provinces by IPTV Users’ Viewing Profiles](../publications/b1c3924e4356996855e9.md)

Ahmet Sari; Üstün Özen

One\-sided and terrestrial broadcasting, which the audience can influence only by changing channels, has taken on a different understanding by IPTV service taking the audience&\#x27;s preferences and tendencies into consideration\. The one\-way transmission from the broadcasting channel to the audience in traditional television broadcasting turns into an interactive environment that provides a space for movement for the audience&\#x27;s preferences in IPTV technology\. In the study, the data set was compiled to cover Türkiye between February and May 2018\. However, after the examination of The Set Top Box \(STB\) logs raw data, only one week period \(31 March \- 06 April 2018\) could be analysed because of the data quality, completeness, and representativeness\. A huge and non\-classified IPTV STB log data has been observed, End Distributor Server \(POP Point, approximately 31 000 records\) data is re\-classified in compliance with the Turkish Statistical Institute \(Turkstat\) Statistical Regional Units Classification \(NUTS\)\. The average duration of viewing of IPTV national channels in Turkey is 4 hours and 28 minutes per day, Furthermore, it was determined that the average amount of television watched per person in Turkey during prime time \(18:00\-23:00\) is 52 minutes\.As a result of cluster analysis by category viewing times and rates, Ağrı, Amasya, Çankırı, Düzce, Hakkâri, Iğdır, Şırnak and Zonguldak provinces differed from the others\. By using the category viewing time per active user at the provincial level, Cluster analysis was applied to the provinces with the k\-means method and the results were shown on the map\.

## [The development and use of Contextual Knowledge \(XK\) within the TPACK framework among secondary school English language teachers in Indonesia](../publications/b1cb0ac497ec257a63c2.md)

Monica Ella Harendita

This study investigated the development and use of teacher Contextual Knowledge \(XK\) within the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge \(TPACK\) framework among secondary school English teachers in Indonesia\. Data were gathered from 14 in\-service teachers across six schools in three regions through in\-depth interviews informed by teachers&\#x27; lesson plans and digital artefacts\. Thematic analysis of the data revealed that teachers articulated XK regarding three layers of context \(micro, meso and macro\) in varying detail\. The development of their XK occurred mainly through informal and formal professional learning\. Finally, the use of XK in their technology\-mediated instruction aimed at improving student learning\.

## [Pinus heldreichii and Pinus peuce forests of the Pirin Mountains in Bulgaria](../publications/b1d6b6f6b45cedae8a51.md)

Veradina Nacheva; Gianmaria Bonari; Kalina Pachedjieva; Vladimir Vulchev; Chavdar V\. Gussev; Veselin V\. Shivarov; Anna Ganeva; Rossen T\. Tzonev

We investigated the forest communities of Pinus heldreichii and Pinus peuce in the Pirin Mountains in Bulgaria\. Both Pinus species are sensitive relicts with a very limited range, primarily in the Balkan Peninsula\. Anthropogenic activities and global climate change pose serious challenges to their conservation\. We have subjected 189 published and unpublished relevés from newly conducted field research to numerical analysis\. Then we corroborated them by comparison with the previously identified and published syntaxa in neighbouring countries\. The results indicated that the Pinus heldreichii communities form part of the Festuco penzesii\-Pinetum heldreichii ass\. nov\. with two subassociations: typicum and seslerietosum coerulantis subass\. nov\. These communities are distinctly oromediterranean, characterised by their floristic composition and occurrence on marbles\. In contrast, we classified the Pinus peuce communities in the Pirin Mts\. at the community level as the Festuca valida\-Pinus peuce community\. These extrazonal boreomontane communities are also distributed at high elevations, but in contrast to the Pinus heldreichii communities, they occur on silicate terrains\. Pinus heldreichii associations have a limited range, and due to their canopy openness and occurrence on marbles and serpentine terrains, they support many regional and even local endemics\. Although Pinus peuce communities are also divided into geographically isolated groups, the high constancy of characteristic species of boreomontane forests calls this classification into question, suggesting that a comprehensive revision of Pinus peuce forests within their range is needed\.

## [Strong AI and the method of explication](../publications/b1d6cce64949e1151439.md)

Anton Alexandrov; Sebastian Sunday Grève

This paper argues that the concept of human mindedness may be employed as a Carnapian explicatum that enables progress to be made in the debate about strong AI, that is, the thesis that ‘the appropriately programmed computer really is a mind’\. It is shown that a holistic notion of human mindedness – conceived as all of what may typically occur in the mental life of a human being – yields greater precision without sacrificing simplicity or similarity to ordinary psychological concepts, including consciousness and intelligence, which were formerly central to the debate\. The alternative approach is assessed by reference to Carnap’s four criteria of adequacy – similarity, precision, fruitfulness, and simplicity – and defended against Strawson’s charge of changing the subject\. The paper concludes that explication provides a methodologically superior framework for testing strong AI and promises progress on further issues in the philosophy of AI\.

## [Multi\-response optimization of flexural performance in additively manufactured carbon fiber\-reinforced PLA composites](../publications/b1e2b7bd95f42101c121.md)

Emanoil Linul; ION MIRON; Manjunath Patel Gowdru Chandrashekarappa; Harsha Henchinamane Murthy

Abstract Additively manufactured carbon fiber\-reinforced polylactic acid \(CF\-PLA\) composites are increasingly used for lightweight components that require improved flexural performance\. However, their mechanical response is strongly governed by the combined effects of printing parameters, making systematic modeling and multi\-response optimization essential\. In this study, the flexural behavior of CF\-PLA composites was investigated using a central composite design \(CCD\) based on four material extrusion parameters: printing speed \(PS\), printing temperature \(PT\), layer thickness \(LT\), and number of outer shells \(OS\)\. Eight flexural responses were analyzed to describe stiffness\-, strength\-, strain\-, and energy\-related performance indicators\. The results showed that PT, LT, and OS had dominant but response\-dependent effects, whereas PS exhibited a comparatively lower influence\. Flexural stress at break was significantly affected by interaction terms, indicating strong process\-parameter interdependencies, while flexural strain at break showed a more independent response, with no significant interaction effects\. The developed response surface models showed high predictive accuracy, with coefficients of determination \(R 2 \) ranging from 93\.06 to 96\.64%\. To account for the unequal importance of the flexural responses, MEREC and CRITIC objective weighting methods were integrated with Grey Wolf Optimizer \(GWO\) and Desirability Function Approach \(DFA\)\. Among the investigated strategies, GWO\-MEREC\-DFA achieved the highest composite desirability value \(0\.9899\), outperforming GWO\-CRITIC\-DFA \(0\.9756\) and equal\-weight optimization \(0\.9751\)\. The optimized condition also produced superior flexural performance and the most compact, least disrupted damage morphology\. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of hybrid GWO\-based approaches for optimizing MEX\-printed CF\-PLA composites\.

## [Orthodontic\-Surgical Management of Skeletal Class III Malocclusion: A Case\-Based Approach](../publications/b1f15457d08e7606ee65.md)

Nandhini Kalyanasundaram; Murali Patla; Sony Jacob; Jagadish Chandra

Skeletal Class III malocclusions in adults pose significant treatment challenges due to the involvement of complex skeletal discrepancies such as maxillary deficiency, mandibular prognathism, or a combination of both\. This case report highlights two adult patients with distinct skeletal Class III presentations, one with mandibular prognathism and chin deviation, and the other with midfacial retrusion accompanied by an anterior open bite\. Both patients underwent comprehensive treatment involving presurgical orthodontic decompensation using MBT appliances, followed by orthognathic surgery\. Surgical interventions included Le Fort I osteotomy for maxillary advancement and bilateral sagittal split osteotomy \(BSSO\) for mandibular setback\. Post\-treatment outcomes revealed marked improvements in occlusion, facial aesthetics, and overall patient satisfaction\. These cases emphasize the importance of a coordinated orthodontic\-surgical approach for achieving functional stability and aesthetic harmony in adult patients with severe skeletal Class III malocclusions\.

## [X\-RIC: An Agentic RAN\-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning](../publications/b1f4df5910f8e09bcd98.md)

Adhwaa Al\-Chaab; Ayman Younis; Dario Pompili

The O\-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI\-driven control\. While the RAN Intelligent Controller \(RIC\) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability\. We propose eXplainable RIC \(X\-RIC\), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O\-RAN architectures\. X\-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning \(RL\) with strategic agentic reasoning through: \(i\) automated Behavioral Cloning \(BC\) using domain heuristics for sample\-efficient training, \(ii\) a Telecom Language Model \(TLM\), a transformer\-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and \(iii\) closed\-loop co\-adaptation within the Near\-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement\. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX \(Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN\), a domain\-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics\. We validate X\-RIC on SLA\-aware network slicing in simulation and O\-RAN\-compliant testbed deployments\. X\-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance\.

## [Meta\-Bayesian Fusion Adaptation for Evacuation Prediction: A Hybrid XGBoost–Graph Neural Network Framework for the Mentawai Megathrust Scenario](../publications/b1f9b03d723432bf5950.md)

Sularno Sularno; Wendi Boy; Putri Anggraini; Dio Prima Mulya; Rexcharles Enyinna Donatus

Continuous monitoring of physiological conditions in intensive care units generates complex multivariate time\-series data that can support early clinical decision\-making\. However, conventional hybrid models combining Long Short\-Term Memory networks and XGBoost generally learn correlational patterns and may experience performance degradation under non\-stationary conditions, sensor artifacts, and changes in patient characteristics\. Moreover, these models are typically designed for outcome prediction rather than treatment\-effect estimation\. Therefore, a framework capable of integrating temporal forecasting, representation disentanglement, uncertainty estimation, and treatment\-response analysis is required\. Purpose: This study aims to develop a Causal Multi\-Task Fusion Engine \(CMTFE\) for forecasting future vital\-sign trajectories and estimating individualized treatment effects in IoT\-supported ICU monitoring\. Methods/Study Design/Approach: The proposed framework integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network for multivariate vital\-sign encoding, a β\-Variational Autoencoder for separating outcome\-relevant and confounding representations, a Transformer decoder for probabilistic trajectory forecasting, and propensity\-weighted XGBoost regressors for treatment\-effect estimation\. Experiments were conducted using 487,000 observation windows derived from 38,200 ICU stays in the MIMIC\-IV dataset\. The data were chronologically divided into training, validation, and testing sets at proportions of 70%, 15%, and 15%, respectively\. Forecasting performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error, and Continuous Ranked Probability Score\. Treatment\-effect estimation was evaluated on a semi\-synthetic test set using Precision in Estimation of Heterogeneous Effect and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve\. Results/Findings: CMTFE achieved an MAE of 0\.281, RMSE of 0\.390, and CRPS of 0\.218, outperforming the evaluated LSTM, TCN, Transformer, LSTM–XGBoost, and TCN–XGBoost baselines\. Under the constructed distribution\-shift scenario, the model exhibited a relative MAE increase of 4\.2%, compared with 9\.5% for TCN–XGBoost\. For semi\-synthetic treatment\-effect estimation, CMTFE obtained a PEHE of 0\.187 and an AUC of 0\.842\. The ablation analysis further indicated that representation disentanglement, contrastive regularization, propensity\-score weighting, and temporal convolution each contributed to the model’s performance\. Novelty/Originality/Value: The principal contribution of this study lies in integrating temporal forecasting, disentangled representation learning, uncertainty quantification, and propensity\-adjusted treatment\-effect estimation within a unified ICU\-monitoring framework\. Unlike conventional hybrid models that combine neural and tree\-based predictions through passive aggregation, CMTFE uses learned outcome\-relevant representations to support both forecasting and intervention\-response analysis\. Nevertheless, the treatment\-effect findings are based on semi\-synthetic outcomes and should be interpreted as experimental decision\-support evidence rather than validated clinical recommendations\. External, prospective, and clinician\-centered validation is required before real\-world deployment\.

## [Use of Private 5G Networks for Industrial Systems](../publications/b210f6354951f9bd92e4.md)

JURE VUČKO

Z vse večjimi željami industrije po napredku, hitrosti in robotizaciji je treba hitro razvijati in izboljševati omrežja\. Tehnologija pete generacije predstavlja pomemben preboj na področju brezžičnih komunikacij ter odpira nove možnosti za razvoj in implementacijo robotskih sistemov\. Digitalna transformacija industrije in razvoj koncepta Industrije 4\.0 povečujeta pomen zanesljive, nizkolatenčne in varne komunikacijske infrastrukture, ki predstavlja ključni pogoj za učinkovito delovanje robotov v proizvodnih in drugih zahtevnih okoljih\. Namen dela je analizirati delovanje zasebnega omrežja 5G za industrijske aplikacije ter ovrednotiti njene tehnične, varnostne in ekonomske vidike\. Omrežja 5G temeljijo na napredni, programsko podprti arhitekturi, ki omogoča visoko prilagodljivost in optimizacijo omrežnih virov glede na potrebe posamezne aplikacije\. Posebno pomemben je storitveni profil URLLC, ki zagotavlja izjemno nizko zakasnitev in visoko zanesljivost prenosa podatkov\. Robotski sistemi zahtevajo natančno sinhronizacijo med senzorji, aktuatorji in krmilnimi enotami\. To je trenutno odvisno od žične povezave, katere težava je fleksibilnost in nemobilnost sistema\. Uporaba tehnologije 5G omogoča brezžično povezljivost, s čimer je mogoče zmanjšati oziroma odpraviti navedene omejitve\. ## [Assessing the Socio\-Economic Implications of GST Reforms 2\.0 on Growth, Inflation and Consumption in India](../publications/b2185aef19b5ea850785.md)

Abhishek Gopal Satpute; Pralhad Rathod

This study examines the socio\-economic impacts of India’s Goods and Services Tax \(GST\) reforms, with a focus on the post\-2021 period and their alignment with the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision\. Using secondary data from the Reserve Bank of India, the GST Council, and the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, the study employs descriptive and trend analysis to evaluate the relationship of these reforms with GDP growth, inflationary trends, and consumer behaviour\. The manuscript argues that GST reforms have enhanced digital compliance and tax administration, supported post\-pandemic recovery, and stabilized revenue collections\. Although inflation continues to be influenced by broader macroeconomic factors, the enhanced GST framework is described as reducing tax cascading and improving cost transparency\. The study considers these reforms important for economic formalization and inclusive growth, and discusses their relevance to India’s long\-term development goals and macroeconomic stability\.

## [Multi\-modal intelligent driving decision\-making in complex traffic scenarios integrating DDQN and DDPG](../publications/b2328327d9ba1ac327e8.md)

Li He

In complex traffic environments, the interaction between vehicles is highly dynamic and significantly nonlinear, which poses a challenge to the coordinated optimization of safety and stability in intelligent driving decision\-making\. To enhance adaptability and decision\-making accuracy in complex scenarios, a multi\-modal intelligent driving decision model integrating continuous control and discrete decision\-making is developed\. The model is based on a longitudinal continuous control model with deep deterministic policy gradient to achieve adaptive acceleration adjustment, and introduces a multi strategy particle swarm optimization mechanism to improve the convergence stability of the strategy\. On this basis, a hierarchical decision\-making structure is constructed by combining dual deep reinforcement learning methods, where high\-level discrete behavior decisions and low\-level continuous motion control are collaboratively optimized through temporal modeling and priority experience learning\. The research results show that in terms of car following control, the average distance between vehicles reaches 20\.1 m, which is about 8\.1% higher than the comparison model\. The collision rate drops to 1\.3%, which is more than 55% lower than the benchmark model\. The average headway is 1\.95s, with significantly reduced fluctuations\. The average acceleration decreases to 0\.72 m/s 3 , a decrease of about 23%\. The comfort satisfaction rate increases to 93\.8%, and the safety constraint satisfaction rate has reached 96\.5%\. The research shows that the constructed model achieves significant improvements in safety, stability, comfort, and real\-time performance, which can provide effective support for intelligent driving in complex traffic scenarios\.

## [Klasifikasi Gambar Asli dan Buatan AI Menggunakan SE\-ResNet18 dan SE\-ResNet50](../publications/b235b5e83caf46b3b326.md)

Aurelia Catherine Lay; Yuni Yamasari

Perkembangan model generatif, seperti Generative Adversarial Networks \(GAN\) dan Diffusion Models, yang menghasilkan gambar berkualitas tinggi buatan AI yang sulit dibedakan dari gambar asli, menjadi pendorong utama penelitian ini\. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah menggunakan arsitektur SE\-ResNet50 dan SE\-ResNet18 untuk membuat model klasifikasi yang mampu membedakan antara gambar asli dan gambar buatan AI\. Teknik class weight dan optimasi hyperparameter yang memanfaatkan Optimasi Bayesian digunakan untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan data\. Dataset Chameleon, yang berisi 26\.033 gambar—11\.170 gambar buatan AI dan 14\.863 gambar asli digunakan\. Berdasarkan hasilnya, SE\-ResNet50 menunjukkan kemampuan generalisasi yang unggul dan mencapai akurasi 88,33%, presisi 91,60%, recall 87,58%, f1\-score 0,88 ketika dipadukan dengan class weight dan Optimasi Bayesian\. SE\-ResNet18 mencapai akurasi 88,75%, presisi 0,9095%, recall 0,8917%, F1\-score 0,88% pada skenario tanpa class weight dan Optimasi Bayesian\. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa arsitektur berbasis Squeeze\-and\-Excitation, yang dipadukan dengan teknik penyeimbangan data dan Optimasi Hyperparameter, terbukti menjadi pendekatan yang handal untuk klasifikasi gambar buatan AI ketika data tidak seimbang\.

## [Pemanfaatan Digital Marketing dan Inovasi Produk sebagai Strategi Pengembangan UMKM Sandwich dan Pisang Coklat Lumer](../publications/b2393bbd2b61782e6252.md)

Khairani Alawiyah Matondang; Putri Kemala Dewi Lubis; Khirunnisa Br Marpaung; Ellyka Evitasari Purba; Adika Sanjaya

Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah \(UMKM\) memiliki peran penting dalam mendukung perekonomian masyarakat, khususnya melalui pengembangan usaha kuliner\. Namun, keterbatasan modal, promosi yang belum optimal, dan minat konsumen yang tidak selalu stabil menjadi tantangan bagi UMKM dalam mempertahankan dan mengembangkan usahanya\. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan pemanfaatan digital marketing, mengidentifikasi kendala pemasaran, serta menganalisis peluang inovasi produk sebagai strategi pengembangan UMKM YICI SENLY\. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan metode studi kasus\. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara langsung dengan pemilik usaha, dan dokumentasi yang dilakukan pada 1 Oktober 2026\. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif untuk menggambarkan kondisi usaha, kegiatan pemasaran, dan alternatif strategi pengembangan yang sesuai dengan kemampuan UMKM\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa UMKM YICI SENLY menawarkan sandwich reguler seharga Rp10\.000, sandwich ayam seharga Rp13\.000, dan pisang coklat lumer seharga Rp10\.000, dengan modal awal sekitar Rp200\.000\. Kondisi tersebut menunjukkan perlunya strategi pemasaran yang efisien dan inovasi produk yang mempertimbangkan keterbatasan sumber daya usaha\. Pemanfaatan digital marketing direkomendasikan melalui media sosial, foto dan video produk, informasi harga yang jelas, serta promosi yang dilakukan secara konsisten\. Selain itu, inovasi Sandwich Pisang Sambal diusulkan sebagai alternatif pengembangan menu dengan perpaduan rasa manis, pedas, dan gurih\. Inovasi ini masih memerlukan pengujian rasa, penerimaan konsumen, penentuan harga, dan perhitungan biaya produksi\. Dengan demikian, digital marketing dan inovasi produk berpotensi menjadi strategi pengembangan UMKM apabila diterapkan secara terencana dan dievaluasi berdasarkan respons konsumen serta kondisi usaha\.

## [Advancing Responsible and Trustworthy AI Using Human\-Centered Methods](../publications/b23f321d05392a554db8.md)

Aimen Gaba

Data\-driven systems that use machine learning are now embedded in high\-stakes domains including healthcare, hiring, and the criminal justice system, yet they routinely exhibit biases that cause real harm, generate stigmatizing language about marginalized groups, and encode discrimination into consequential decisions\. A growing body of work has focused on detecting and mitigating these biases at the algorithmic level, but a critical question remains underexplored: when does AI bias actually become visible to the humans who interact with these systems? This dissertation argues that bias legibility, whether a person can perceive and interpret the bias present in an AI system&\#x27;s outputs, is not a fixed property of the bias itself\. It is co\-determined by two forces that have rarely been studied together: how AI outputs are visually and linguistically presented, and who is doing the perceiving\. This dissertation presents three empirical studies that each isolate a different point in the human\-AI interaction loop where bias legibility is shaped\. First, I examine how natural language shapes the visualization design space for data comparison tasks\. Through a design study with visualization experts and non\-experts, followed by a crowdsourced preference study, I show that the cardinality and concreteness of a comparison utterance systematically influence which visualization designs users prefer, and that this variation is not accounted for in how existing natural language interfaces are designed\. Second, I investigate how visual design choices affect people&\#x27;s trust in ML models and their perception of model fairness\. Across three controlled experiments with over 1,500 participants, I find that presenting model performance as text rather than bar charts increases the likelihood that people prioritize fairness, that women and men weigh accuracy\-fairness trade\-offs differently given identical visual information, and that explicitly labeling a model as biased has a stronger effect on trust than showing its biased history\. These findings demonstrate that visualization design is not a neutral communicative medium; it shapes what people attend to and how they reason\. Third, I examine how gender identity shapes the perception of bias in large language model outputs\. Through 25 in\-depth interviews with participants across gender identities, I find that non\-binary and transgender participants consistently identified harms, including condescension, identity erasure, and stereotyping, in ChatGPT outputs that cisgender men characterized as neutral or realistic\. These differential perceptions reflect knowledge derived from lived experience with systems that have historically erased or stereotyped their identities, knowledge that technical fairness metrics and aggregate user feedback are not designed to capture\. Together, these studies make the case that bias legibility is determined at three distinct points in the human\-AI interaction loop: how users express analytical intent in language, how AI outputs are visually rendered, and who is reading those outputs\. Current approaches to AI fairness focus predominantly on algorithmic properties of models, but this dissertation shows that the human side of the loop, the interface, the design, and the perceiver, plays a significant and underappreciated role\. Building AI systems that people can genuinely evaluate for fairness requires design choices informed by how visualization and language shape reasoning, and by centering the perspectives of the users most likely to be harmed\.

## [The rise and fall of anti\-corruption agencies in Indonesia’s emerging democracy](../publications/b243c74e123de1402973.md)

Ahmad Khoirul Umam; M\. Adil Khan

The article critically discusses the tensions between political power, institutional independence and the persistence of corruption by examining the historic development of several anti\-corruption initiatives in Indonesia and the problems faced by Indonesia’s anti\-corruption agencies in fighting corruption\. Using qualitative research methods, it contends that anti\-corruption agencies initially thrive in reform\-oriented political coalitions but are institutionally vulnerable when their enforcement activities threaten entrenched political\-economic interests\. Instead of viewing institutional decline as a consequence of organisational design, this article demonstrates a more comprehensive governance perspective where effectiveness of anti\-graft measures is conditioned by changing elite coalitions, political incentives and resilience of democratic accountability mechanism\. Drawing on Indonesia’s experience, especially the rise and fall of the contemporary KPK, Indonesia’s central corruption control agency, the article demonstrates the fragility of institutional reforms under entrenched power and elite opposition\. The findings suggest that the effectiveness of anti\-corruption measures depends not only on the formal design of institutions, but also on the broader political configuration in which agencies operate, in particular elite alignments, sustained political commitment, the capacity of civil society and the role the media can play in mobilising public support in building accountability\. This article contributes to the comparative governance literature by conceptualising anti\-corruption agencies as politically embedded institutions, whose developmental trajectories are shaped by the relationship between institutional autonomy and elite power\. It offers a generic analytical framework to account for the cyclical rise, consolidation, and decline of anti\-corruption agencies in the Global South, where democratic institutions coexist with resilient networks of elite capture\. The article ends with the conclusion that effective and durable anti\-corruption control depends on operational autonomy and transparent public administration, but also on the presence of sustained reform coalitions that are able to withstand elite backlash and maintain democratic accountability\.

## [The Production, Characterization, and Biodegradation Kinetics of Bioplastics From Starch Extracted From Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta Tubers](../publications/b24912ce3330c9ffb041.md)

John Onyebuchi Ogbodo; Irene Okechukwu‐Okoro; Parker Elijah Joshua; Obinna Aru Oje; Ikechukwu N\.E\. Onwurah; Simeon Ikechukwu Egba

ABSTRACT The accumulation of non‐biodegradable plastics is driving the search for environmentally friendly, low‐cost alternatives\. This study investigated the production of biodegradable bioplastics using starch extracted from Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta tubers\. The tubers were pulverized, and starch was extracted\. Bioplastic was produced by reacting the starch with ethanoic, methanoic, and propanoic acids in the presence of glycerol and water at 80°C for 25 min\. The starch yield and the physicochemical, mechanical, and degradability properties of the bioplastics were determined\. The results showed starch yields \(57\.5%; 52\.26%\), moisture content \(12\.38%; 13\.74%\), pH \(6\.9; 6\.7\), amylose content \(20\.4%; 20\.67%\) and amylopectin content \(79\.6%; 80\.2%\) for Ipomoea batatas and Manihot esculenta tubers, respectively\. The mass of bioplastic produced was directly proportional to starch content and the number of carbon chains present in the organic acid\. The mechanical properties showed that tensile strength was significantly \( p &lt; 0\.05\) higher than that of the control, except for the 15 g bioplastic produced\. Shear strength also showed a trend similar to tensile strength\. The elongation/break properties significantly \( p &lt; 0\.05\) increased in the methanoic acid‐derived bioplastic\. The bioplastic degradation rates were \(0\.0059, 0\.0056 and 0\.0043 mg/ml/h\) for Ipomoea batatas and \(0\.0099, 0\.0098 and 0\.0091 mg/ml/h\) for Manihot esculenta‐derived biodegradable plastic, respectively , using Pseudomonas aeruginosa \. The results of this study show that starches from Ipomoea batata and Manihot esculenta tubers could be a good source for bioplastic production because they are inexpensive, renewable, and readily biodegradable when disposed of in the environment\.

## [The Role of Digital Leadership and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Tourism Strategies: Evidence from Turkey](../publications/b249627012d955152324.md)

Elif Savaşkan

This study investigates how digital leadership and artificial intelligence \(AI\) contribute to the development of sustainable tourism strategies, focusing on the context of the Turkish hospitality industry\. The central research question examines how digital leadership practices guide the strategic use of AI technologies toward sustainability\-oriented outcomes\. Grounded in digital leadership theory and the triple bottom line sustainability framework, the study adopts a qualitative multiple case study design\. Data were collected through document analysis of sustainability reports, strategic plans, and publicly available digital transformation materials from four leading hotel groups in Turkey: Rixos Hotels, Titanic Hotels, Maxx Royal Hotels, and The Marmara Hotels\. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and strategic practices\. The findings reveal that AI\-enabled applications support sustainability by enhancing operational efficiency, enabling personalized service delivery, and improving environmental management practices, particularly in areas such as energy efficiency, resource optimization, and carbon footprint reduction\. Furthermore, the results indicate that the alignment of digital leadership with ethical responsibility, innovation orientation, and employee digital capability development strengthens organizational competitiveness and long\-term sustainability\. The study contributes to the literature by offering an applied strategic framework that conceptualizes digital leadership as a governance mechanism directing AI technologies toward sustainability objectives\. Beyond academic contributions, the findings provide practical insights for managers and policymakers seeking to integrate digital transformation initiatives with sustainable tourism strategies, especially in emerging tourism economies\.

## [Carbon Quantum Dots‐Decorated Mn 0\.5 Cd 0\.5 S/BiOBr S‐Scheme Heterojunction With Interfacial Bi─S Bonding as an Efficient Piezocatalyst for Aqueous Cr\(VI\) Reduction](../publications/b2539f3efe48b6222063.md)

Darya Shorsh Hamad; Hawkar Ahmed; Omid Amiri; Kamran Heydaryan

ABSTRACT Hexavalent chromium \[Cr\(VI\)\] is a serious environmental problem that needs to be removed efficiently from water without the need for reagents\. A two‐step hydrothermal/solvothermal method was employed to synthesize a ternary piezocatalyst of carbon quantum dots \(CDs\) coupled with Mn 0\.5 Cd 0\.5 S \(MCS\) and BiOBr \(BOB\), denoted MBC, with an interfacial Bi─S bond and tested for the piezocatalytic reduction of Cr\(VI\) under dark and ultrasound‐assisted conditions\. BOB microsphere architecture which was also uniformly decorated with cauliflower‐like MCS aggregates and had a systematic increase in carbon content from 12\.5 to 25\.9 wt\.% as the nominal loading of CDs in the BOB was increased from MBC‐1 to MBC‐3\. In the case of Cr\(VI\), all three ternary MBC composites showed significant removal efficiency of the target ion compared to the respective BOB and MCS, with MBC‐2 showing the best removal efficiency \(89%\), whereas the control without the catalyst removed 5\.2% of the Cr\(VI\), which indicates that the removal of Cr\(VI\) is not a sonolytic effect but a true piezo‐driven effect\. Based on these results, an S‐scheme charge‐transfer mechanism that involves the interface between chemically bonded Bi─S and anchored CDs is proposed\.

## [Reservoir dynamic evolution and drainage optimization in deep saturated coalbed methane of Shenfu Block](../publications/b268f79d923be6134427.md)

Ya Juan Wang; Hao Xu; Yi nan Liu; LIU Yan Cheng; Heng Wu; Ding Liu; Xiao zhuo Wu; Yu Dong; Xue Jing Song; Jin wei Wang

China possesses vast deep coalbed methane \(CBM\) resources, However, the dynamic evolution of reservoir pressure and permeability during the production process remains unclear, which restricts their efficient development\. This study conducted to reveal the dynamic evolution of coal reservoir pressure and permeability under different production rates and its influence on the productivity of deep saturated CBM wells, so as to provide a theoretical basis for efficient development\. Based on actual production data from deep saturated CBM vertical wells in the Shenfu Block, and considering positive and negative effects on coal reservoirs during drainage, this study utilizes reservoir pressure and permeability prediction models and derives from production dynamics to characterize the variations of reservoir pressure and permeability under different drainage rates, and analyzes their impacts on well productivity\. The gas production curves of deep saturated CBM wells in the Shenfu Block can be classified into two types: decline type and stable type\. The results show that the initial pressure drop rate is the key factor leading to productivity differentiation\. Stable\-type wells exhibit a lower initial pressure drop rate, a wider propagation range of reservoir pressure, and a permeability improvement of 5\.4%, enabling sustained and efficient CBM production\. In contrast, decline\-type wells experience an excessively rapid initial pressure drop rate, resulting in slow reservoir pressure decline, limited permeability enhancement of only 0\.9%, and a significant drop in productivity at later stages\. To achieve high and stable production of deep saturated CBM wells, a strategy of &quot;slow drainage and controlled pressure&quot; should be adopted\. It is recommended to control the bottomhole flowing pressure drop rate within 160 kPa/d during the initial production stage; appropriately increase the rate by 50\-100 kPa/d during the gas production increase stage to promote gas desorption; and adjust it back to around 50 kPa/d during the later decline stage to maintain production\.

## [A low\-cost environmental monitoring framework for climate\-sensitive disease surveillance in the Peruvian Amazon](../publications/b2ab38427259bbf692db.md)

Bryan Fernandez\-Camacho; Edson J Ascencio; Antony Barja; Luis C\. Revilla; Diego Villa; P\. Brou; Yomali Ferreyra; Lucia Bartolini\-Arana; Rachel Lowe; Gabriel Carrasco‐Escobar

Abstract Malaria, dengue and leptospirosis are endemic in the Peruvian Amazon, where routine surveillance operates without village\-scale environmental observation\. We report the yield of that monitoring framework, the completeness of its meteorological record, and its cost, operated at village scale alongside notifiable disease surveillance\. Across ten villages along the Iquitos–Nauta Highway, we operated drones, automatic weather stations, low\-cost particulate monitors and acoustic recorders, inspected terrain and geolocated cases\. Co\-creation with the regional health directorate and villages governed deployment and data handling\. Streams were harmonized into a spatial database at daily to annual resolution\. Nine quarterly campaigns between March 2023 and March 2026 covered 14 flight areas, 14 km 2 per round, and produced 756 orthomosaics from 1\.16 million images\. Sensors returned 678,564 meteorological and 2,778,363 air\-quality records and 4349\.75 h of audio\. Completely missing outdoor\-temperature weeks ranged from 5\.1 to 61\.4% across sites\. Of 10,883 notified individuals, 1489 \(13\.7%\) were georeferenced, with coverage of 8\.3% in 2010–2015 and 31\.1% in 2021–2025\. Capital outlay was about USD 22,050, each campaign about USD 3660\. The harmonized series is intended to inform vector control and case detection for local health authorities and stakeholders\.

## [From cubic semen profiles to body form: linking seminal dynamics with LAS\-derived zoometrics in Murciano\-Granadina bucks](../publications/b2c636b8f4571ca49e87.md)

María Pía Peláez Caro; Ander Arando Arbulu; Juan Vicente Delgado Bermejo; José Manuel León Jurado; Javier Fernández Álvarez; Francisco Javier Navas González

Introduction Selection of Murciano\-Granadina goats has traditionally relied on Linear Appraisal Systems \(LAS\) to evaluate morphometric traits associated with dairy productivity\. However, the relationship between LAS\-derived traits and male reproductive performance remains insufficiently explored\. This study aimed to assess the association between morphometric characteristics and semen quality parameters in bucks under standardized breeding conditions\. Methods A total of 6,868 ejaculates were recorded, of which 1,901 ejaculates from 77 bucks with complete LAS data were included in the analysis\. The sample was balanced by age \(≤2 years: 53\.25%; &gt;2 years: 46\.75%\), allowing age\-stratified inference\. Ten morphometric traits were evaluated alongside semen parameters, including ejaculate volume, sperm concentration, total motility, progressive motility, acrosome integrity, and endosmosis\. Multicollinearity diagnostics confirmed independence among explanatory variables \(all VIF &lt; 5\)\. Associations were assessed using cubic regression models and correlation analyses\. Results Cubic regression models explained up to 72% of the variance in ejaculate volume, which showed strong positive correlations with chest width \(r = 0\.61, p &lt; 0\.01\) and rump width \(r = 0\.58, p &lt; 0\.01\)\. Sperm concentration was positively associated with stature \(r = 0\.55, p &lt; 0\.05\) and chest width \(r = 0\.49, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Motility parameters exhibited dynamic patterns, with progressive motility primarily explained by quadratic effects and total motility by cubic trends, particularly influenced by chest width and rump depth \(r = 0\.46 \-0\.52, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Acrosome integrity showed strong baseline and cubic effects, while endosmosis followed a linear trend \(R² = 0\.41\)\. Processed semen traits reduced variability, whereas real added volume preserved biologically meaningful differences\. Discussion LAS\-derived morphometric traits \-\-especially chest width, rump width, rump angularity, general angularity, and stature \-\-demonstrated consistent and biologically meaningful associations with semen quality, although effect sizes were moderate\. These findings highlight the potential of integrating morphometric evaluation with reproductive assessment to enhance both dairy and reproductive performance in Murciano\-Granadina goats\. Incorporating reproductive indicators into LAS\-based selection frameworks could improve breeding efficiency and genetic progress\.

## [The longitudinal interplay among L2 writing self\-efficacy, self\-regulated writing strategies, and writing performance: a three\-wave cross\-lagged panel study of Chinese EFL learners](../publications/b2c671ff9a11684dc8de.md)

Dongliang Ding; Ahmad Muhyiddin Bin Yusof

Writing in a second language \(L2\) is a complex cognitive activity that demands sustained self\-regulation and a strong sense of personal capability\. Although cross\-sectional studies have linked writing self\-efficacy, self\-regulated writing strategies, and writing performance, the directional and reciprocal nature of these relationships remains insufficiently understood\. This three\-wave longitudinal study examined the temporal dynamics among L2 writing self\-efficacy \(L2WSE\), self\-regulated writing strategies \(SRWS\), and writing performance \(WP\) over one academic semester\. A total of 368 Chinese EFL learners \(Mage = 19\.2 years, SD = 1\.1; 62\.2% female\) from a public university in central China completed self\-report measures of L2WSE and SRWS at three time points \(Week 1, Week 8, and Week 16\) and produced a timed writing task at each wave\. Confirmatory factor analyses supported the three\-factor measurement model, and tests of measurement invariance confirmed configural, metric, and scalar invariance across waves\. A cross\-lagged panel model \(CLPM\) revealed that \(a\) L2WSE prospectively predicted SRWS from T1 to T2 \( β = 0\.21, p &lt; 0\.001\) and from T2 to T3 \( β = 0\.19, p &lt; 0\.01\), \(b\) SRWS prospectively predicted WP from T1 to T2 \( β = 0\.16, p &lt; 0\.01\) and from T2 to T3 \( β = 0\.18, p &lt; 0\.01\), and \(c\) WP prospectively predicted L2WSE from T1 to T2 \( β = 0\.17, p &lt; 0\.01\) and from T2 to T3 \( β = 0\.15, p &lt; 0\.05\)\. A random\-intercept cross\-lagged panel model \(RI\-CLPM\) sensitivity analysis yielded directionally consistent within\-person effects, with slightly attenuated standardized coefficients\. The findings suggest a temporally ordered, sequential chain in which self\-efficacy beliefs prospectively predict greater strategic engagement, which in turn predicts higher subsequent writing outcomes, while successful writing experiences predict higher subsequent self\-efficacy\. These model\-implied longitudinal associations extend Bandura’s social cognitive theory to L2 writing contexts and highlight the pedagogical importance of nurturing both motivational beliefs and strategic competence in EFL writing instruction, although the observational design precludes causal conclusions\.

## [Cystine as an Ionophore: Redox‐Controlled Anion Transport and Toxicity Toward Triple Negative Breast Cancer Cells](../publications/b2dbcbfc7c65762f3623.md)

Smriti Subir Mukherjee; Satyarthi Mishra; Tanja Junkers; Ramray Bhat; Nandita Madhavan

Synthetic molecules that selectively transport anions across cellular membranes are an emerging class of therapeutics against cancer\. Peptide\-derived transporters are attractive for cancer therapy due to their biocompatibility\. A disulfide tether is employed here to position two anion\-binding hydrophobic tryptophan motifs in close proximity, thereby enhancing membrane insertion and anion selectivity\. The tryptophan\-flanked cystine functions as an anion carrier with a preference toward nitrate and chloride ions\. Reduction of the disulfide to the corresponding free thiol substantially decreases anion transport activity\. In situ reduction in vesicular systems, is governed by the membrane uptake of the disulfide\. This loss in activity upon reduction to the corresponding cysteine establishes a unique class of anionophores that is active as the oxidized species rather than one activated by reduction\. Extension to a cellular context showed a depletion in viability of triple negative MDA\-MB\-231 breast cancer cells by 50 µM of the transporter compared with untransformed MCF\-10A breast cells\. In co\-cultures, the transporter shifted competitive viability in favor of the untransformed cells\. These results establish cystine\-based peptides as a chemically programmable class of anionophores that translate potentially into cancer\-selective biological activity\.

## [Case Report: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke: a diagnostic challenge and biomarker\-based clarification](../publications/b2e1b63d2e92c4a0ddfe.md)

Wenjie Hao; Xuan Zhou; Meixia Wang; Wenming Yang; Ting Cheng

Background Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease \(sCJD\) is a rare and uniformly fatal prion disorder characterized by rapidly progressive dementia and heterogeneous neurological manifestations\. Early sCJD may be misinterpreted as cerebrovascular disease, particularly when focal neurological deficits, unilateral diffusion abnormalities, and vascular risk factors coexist\. Case presentation We report a 76\-year\-old man with a history of hypertension who initially presented with dizziness and gait instability, followed by progressive right\-sided weakness, and was initially diagnosed with ischemic stroke in the setting of intracranial arterial stenosis\. Despite antiplatelet and vascular management, the patient experienced rapid cognitive decline, psychiatric disturbances, aphasia, and progressive hemiparesis\. Follow\-up MRI demonstrated progressive, non\-territorial cortical ribbon\-like diffusion restriction predominantly involving the left insular, parietal, frontal, and temporal cortices\. CSF analysis revealed markedly elevated total tau \(4553\.50 pg/mL; laboratory\-reported cutoff: &lt; 399 pg/mL\), phosphorylated tau \(66\.93 pg/mL; laboratory\-reported cutoff: &lt; 50 pg/mL\), and 14\-3\-3γ protein \(50515 AU/mL; laboratory\-reported cutoff: &lt; 20,000 AU/mL\)\. Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies and metagenomic next\-generation sequencing were negative\. PRNP genetic testing detected no pathogenic variant in the patient and his son\. EEG showed diffuse slowing without periodic sharp wave complexes\. According to the 2017 International CJD Surveillance Network criteria, the diagnosis was classified as probable sCJD on the basis of rapidly progressive cognitive impairment, two clinical features \(documented cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal signs\), characteristic MRI abnormalities, and positive CSF 14\-3\-3; the typical EEG criterion was absent and RT\-QuIC was not performed\. Conclusion This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of early sCJD initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke in the presence of coexisting vascular pathology\. Recognition of non\-vascular diffusion patterns, careful reassessment of atypical clinical progression, and adjunctive CSF biomarker assessment may facilitate timely diagnostic reconsideration and help avoid unnecessary interventions\.

## [Causal Edit Serialization](../publications/b2ed416ea7c2311345da.md)

Louis Robinson

Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated\. Causal Edit Serialization \(CES\) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream\. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly\. A lightweight localization head and dual\-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask\. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model\-generated edits and repeated text\. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean\-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models\. Supervised and reinforcement\-learning post\-training provide a grammatical\-error\-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference\-blind model judging\. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained\. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer\-addressed transformations\.

## [The Connection between Flares and Starspots on M Dwarfs Based on TESS Photometry](../publications/b2f863afa462a2643766.md)

Chunxiang Wang; Jiaxin Wang; Yanjun He; Heyu Sun; Yu Pan; Xianju Zhou; Shichang Li; Yirong MA

Abstract This study uses Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite photometry to investigate the relationship between flare characteristics and starspot features on M dwarfs\. From the light curves, we identified 12,661 flare events on 2699 M dwarfs\. For these flares, we extracted parameters such as flare energy, rise time, and decay time\. Additionally, we applied a spot model to light curves exhibiting spot modulation to derive the photometric amplitude and spot distribution complexity\. Our analysis revealed four correlations: \(1\) flare energy is positively correlated with spot size; \(2\) the flare rate initially increases steeply, then declines gradually as spot size increases, a trend whose robustness is confirmed through Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis and independent flare frequency distribution power\-law fits; \(3\) there is no significant correlation between flare energy and spot complexity distribution; and \(4\) most importantly, the flare rate increases with spot distribution complexity before reaching a peak and subsequently showing a slow decline\. These results suggest that spot size is associated with flare energetics, while the spatial distribution of spots, which may reflect the large\-scale magnetic field configuration, could play a role in determining the flare rate\. These correlations provide an observational clue to the influence of large\-scale magnetic field structure on flare triggering\.

## [Team signal detection theory: objective team performance measurement using simulation telemetry](../publications/b3195e38edde38a480e9.md)

Ryan Thomas Villarreal; Gregory J\. Funke; Denny Yu

Current methods for evaluating team performance rely primarily on simple outcome measures and subjective ratings, which offer limited insight into the decision processes driving performance\. This study extends signal detection theory \(SDT\) to teams, deriving sensitivity \(d′\) and response bias \(c\) from simulation telemetry\. Twenty three\-person teams completed five virtual reality tasks varying in interdependence and time pressure while self\-reported workload, conventional and SDT metrics, and verbal communication were collected\. Team\-level sensitivity distinguished conditions that conventional metrics did not\. High time pressure reduced sensitivity relative to baseline before task scores declined, suggesting sensitivity may indicate early performance degradation\. Response bias became more conservative under combined high interdependence and time pressure, reflecting team strategy shifts\. SDT metrics correlated with workload, particularly team\-task balancing demands \(rs=−0\.68 for d′\)\. Together, sensitivity and bias characterise team performance more completely than accuracy alone by separating discriminative ability from decision strategy\.

## [An entropy\-guided dynamic lightweight network for identification of wild edible vegetables of BTR](../publications/b32362b709033bd6228f.md)

Tania Sarkar; Pranav Kumar Singh; Parag Bhuyan; Anshuman Kalla

Wild edible vegetables of Bodoland Territorial Region \(BTR\) are the species of plants that grow naturally and are commonly consumed as food by the indigenous communities\. These plants are important sources of nutritional and therapeutic properties and are essential for food security and socio\-economic development of rural communities\. Therefore, sustainable conservation and utilization of these unique plant resources are of great significance\. Developing an efficient and accurate automatic identification system is an essential conservation strategy for them\. Current plant identification methods are mainly based on classical machine learning \(ML\) methods and deep convolutional neural network \(CNN\) architectures for recognition and classification\. These methods are effective for images taken under controlled or pristine conditions, but the performance is often far from ideal in the complex and natural environments of forest and grassland, where wild edible plants are found\. This paper proposes an entropy\-guided dynamic lightweight deep learning architecture for automatic detection of wild edible vegetables in BTR\. The proposed model employs adaptive computation with Dynamic Kernel Selection \(DKS\), Region\-wise Adaptive Feature Routing \(RAFR\), Ultra\-Light Context Encoding \(ULCE\), and Entropy\-Guided Global Pooling \(EGGP\) to capture multi\-scale plant characteristics efficiently and reduce redundant computations\. The novelty of our proposed framework lies in its coordinated integration of these modules that is designed to reduce computational overhead without compromising with performance\. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves excellent classification accuracy of 90\.69% with significantly reduced parameter complexity and floating\-point operations \(FLOPs\), which is well\-suited for real\-time precision agriculture and low\-resource edge deployment applications\.

## [BALANCING GROWTH AND NATURE: UNDERSTANDING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN KARACHI’S COASTAL AREAS: A CASE STUDY OF DHA PHASE VII–VIII AND THE MALIR RIVER DELTA](../publications/b324b366e8e7fd05153b.md)

Muhammad Abrar Khokhar; Maaz Bin Qasim

Coastal areas give cities great economic, social, and environmental value, yet rapid building on them often damages the very nature that makes them valuable\. This paper studies sustainable development along the coast of Karachi, Pakistan, using the case of Defence Housing Authority \(DHA\) Phase VII–VIII and the neighbouring Malir River Delta\. The study follows the three\-pillar idea of sustainability environment, society, and economy and asks whether coastal growth in Karachi keeps these three in balance\. It uses a mixed approach: a review of recent research, comparison of land\-use maps from 1984 and 2017, field visits, and interviews with a marine scientist, estate agents, restaurant visitors, and fishermen from Ibrahim Haidri village\. The findings show a clear imbalance\. Economic growth from ports, luxury housing, and restaurants is strong, but land reclamation has cleared mangroves and marshlands, reduced fish stocks, cut public access to the shore, and raised the risk from storms and sea\-level rise\. Weak enforcement of environmental laws makes the problem worse\. The paper argues that development cannot and should not be stopped, but it must be made sustainable through balanced planning, mangrove restoration, protection of fishing livelihoods, marine spatial planning, and honest governance\. The Hong Kong Chek Lap Kok airport case shows that damaged coastal habitats can be restored when mitigation is taken seriously\.

## [Early experience with the SHURUI single port serpentine arm robotic system with an auxiliary port in gastrointestinal surgery: a descriptive case series](../publications/b32a6442e2b69c17debd.md)

Dipesh Kumar Yadav; Yuncheng Luo; Zhangwei Yang; Yi Huang; Hanzhang Huang; Sisi Lin; Min Li; Dandan Bao; Yiren Hu

Background The SHURUI single\-port \(SP\) robotic system is a novel platform with serpentine instruments designed for reduced\-access surgery\. Clinical experience in gastrointestinal malignancies remains limited\. This exploratory, descriptive case series reports initial technical experience with the SHURUI SP system in a consecutive series of gastric and colorectal cancer resections\. Methods This retrospective case series included six consecutive patients who underwent SP robotic gastrointestinal cancer surgery between November 2025 and December 2025 at a single tertiary center\. Procedures comprised rectal cancer resection with total mesorectal excision \( n = 2\), left hemicolectomy \( n = 1\), right hemicolectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy \( n = 1\), distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy \( n = 1\), and total gastrectomy with extended D2 lymphadenectomy \( n = 1\)\. All cases used a single periumbilical incision \(3–4 cm\) and a 12 mm auxiliary port for energy devices and staplers\. Outcomes included operative parameters, complications \(Clavien\-Dindo\), pathological metrics, and hospital costs\. Results All six procedures were completed without conversion\. Median operative time was 332\.5 min \(155–402\); median estimated blood loss was 70 mL \(10–200\)\. No intraoperative complications or transfusions occurred\. Postoperative Grade II complications occurred in two patients \(33\.3%\): anastomotic bleeding requiring transfusion and wound infection\. Grade I transient fever occurred in two additional patients \(33\.3%\)\. No Grade III–V complications, reoperations, or 30\-day mortality occurred\. All resections achieved R0 margins; median lymph node yield was 18\.5 \(12–28\)\. Median hospital stay was 14 days \(12–20\)\. Mean total hospital cost was ¥30,573 ± ¥14,725, exclusive of robotic platform and instrument fees, which were waived during this initial evaluation period\. Conclusions In this initial series, the SHURUI SP robotic system achieved complete resection without conversion in all six cases\. R0 resection was obtained in every case with no severe early complications; however, the small sample size precludes definitive safety assessment, and oncologic adequacy requires long\-term follow\-up\. The system proved technically feasible for complex gastric and colorectal cancer resections, though the absence of an integrated energy channel necessitated an auxiliary port in all cases, and operative times reflected an early learning curve\. Larger comparative studies with long\-term follow\-up are needed to define the role of this platform\.

## [Articulación de estrategias y viabilidad proyectada de un desarrollo multifamiliar dirigido al segmento “NIDO VACÍO del NSE A](../publications/b332cdb038d829b5f0db.md)

Elisa Eliana Suárez Granados

Los proyectos inmobiliarios dirigidos a segmentos residenciales específicos deben conciliar la diferenciación del producto con un mercado potencial delimitado y con la necesidad de mantener una comercialización y una estructura de financiamiento coherentes\. El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar cómo la articulación de las estrategias de producto, posicionamiento, comercialización y financiamiento sustentó la viabilidad proyectada de la primera etapa del proyecto multifamiliar El Pedregal, dirigido a hogares del NSE A en etapa de nido vacío\. Se desarrolló un estudio de caso aplicado, de alcance evaluativo y proyectivo, mediante el análisis de la configuración económica del producto, la oferta comparable, los supuestos comerciales, la estructura de financiamiento y los flujos económico y financiero\. Bajo las condiciones del mercado limeño de 2015–2016, el escenario base alcanzó un margen neto sobre ventas de 11\.76%, una TIR económica anual de 27% y un VAN económico de US$391,381, calculado con un COK anual de 12%\. El análisis de sensibilidad mostró que la velocidad de ventas produjo la mayor variación del VAN financiero entre las variables examinadas\. Se concluye que el caso presentó viabilidad proyectada bajo los supuestos históricos establecidos y que sus resultados dependieron de la articulación entre la configuración del producto, su comercialización y la programación del financiamiento\.

## [Advanced AI/ML Analysis of AQI to Study the Crowd Density Effect](../publications/b337f937a407c383c457.md)

Ashish B\. Jirapure; Komal Mahalle; Swejal Tembhare; Aniket Tayde; Shruti Sarode

Public environments can experience rapid changes in person density, particularly during festivals, weekends, and special occasions\. These changes may influence carbon dioxide concentration, particulate matter, temperature, humidity, and the resulting air\-quality condition\. This paper presents an integrated framework that combines camera\-based person counting with environmental sensing and artificial intelligence and machine learning analysis\. A vision module estimates the number of people and crowd density from video frames, while environmental observations are collected with synchronized timestamps\. The combined dataset is preprocessed, aligned, and analyzed to identify relationships between crowd density and air\-quality indicators\. The framework also supports dashboard\-based visualization and alert generation for practical monitoring\. The proposed approach is intended to provide a common analytical view of occupancy and environmental conditions in public premises\.
