## [An Improved DSC‐Based Fixed‐Time Resilient Tracking Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems With Full‐State Constraints](../publications/b347cd6a0684c60637a4.md)

Bocheng Yan; Shuai Liu; Xianfu Zhang

ABSTRACT This article addresses the fixed‐time resilient tracking control problem for state‐constrained unknown nonlinear systems under deception attacks\. First, within the backstepping framework, a state‐dependent function is introduced at each design step to enforce asymmetric state constraints\. This approach eliminates the feasibility conditions on virtual controllers required by barrier Lyapunov function \(BLF\)‐based methods\. Second, an enhanced dynamic surface control \(DSC\) technique is proposed to circumvent the differentiation explosion inherent in backstepping while overcoming stability analysis challenges from state‐dependent function‐induced residual terms\. By integrating these components, a fixed‐time resilient control strategy is developed that \(1\) guarantees the fixed‐time convergence of the output tracking error; \(2\) ensures strict adherence to prescribed state constraints\. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm\.

## [Refining risk prediction in geriatric heart failure: the emergency heart failure mortality risk grade‑BI model under scrutiny](../publications/b34a897d897880b7c9bf.md)

Kianoush A\. h\. Saberi L\.; Durdona Alimova; Sherzod Niyazov; Kholmurod Qayumov; Parvina Gaffarova; Xamida Juraqobilova; Zaynura Kadirova

Risk stratification is critical for managing acute heart failure in older adults, yet existing tools often underperform in geriatric populations\. Özdemir recently introduced the EHMRG‑BI model, integrating brain natriuretic peptide and endotracheal intubation with the Emergency Heart Failure Mortality Risk Grade score to improve 30‑day mortality prediction\. While the model demonstrates improved discrimination in a single‑center derivation cohort, several methodological considerations warrant attention\. The inclusion of intubation, a treatment decision rather than a baseline characteristic, may introduce bias and limit its utility as an arrival‑time tool\. The absence of key geriatric domains such as frailty, functional status, and cognitive impairment may result in residual confounding\. Additionally, modelling BNP as a linear predictor disregards its well‑documented non‑linear association with mortality\. This Matters Arising offers a perspective on these challenges and proposes refinements, including external validation, integration of geriatric assessments, and flexible BNP modelling, to strengthen the model&\#x27;s clinical applicability\.

## [When AI Gives the Feedback: Evaluative Outsourcing and Learner Agency in the English Writing Classroom](../publications/b34b70be0021c7574992.md)

Anwar Farhan Mohamad Marzaini; Shahazwan Mat Yusoff; Nur Syahirah Ibrahim; Lijie Hao

Generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) is increasingly used to provide feedback and support revision in English writing\. Existing debate has largely examined the quality, accuracy, and effectiveness of AI\-generated feedback\. This conceptual paper argues that such concerns risk overlooking a more fundamental pedagogical issue: the redistribution of evaluative work between learner and system\. Drawing on feedback literacy and evaluative judgement, the paper introduces evaluative outsourcing to describe the delegation of interpretive, judgemental, and decision\-making work in feedback engagement to AI\. It argues that GenAI can enable substantial textual improvement while requiring limited learner participation in the evaluation underlying revision, creating an AI feedback paradox in which better revision does not necessarily indicate better judgement\. The paper proposes four principles for retaining learner evaluative agency: making evaluative decisions visible, designing for comparison, preserving consequential decisions for learners, and creating opportunities for evaluative transfer\.

## [Banerjee, Parthasarathi &amp; Bhardwaj, Krishna K\.: Constructivist Management of Knowledge, Communication and Enterprise Innovation: Lessons from Indian Experience](../publications/b36a9369c818689df46a.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 16 \(1\):49\-72\. 2002Prime movers of enterprise innovation are inside the organisation\. The enterprise NIIT, studied in this paper, tells us how elicitation and recognition of knowledge and its contents set an enterprise on the move\. Recognised knowledge is actionable\. Each act of recognition is an addition to knowledge content, and such additions took place in NIIT through acts of communications and self\-searching\. These contents form a large collage that cannot be strewn into a single novelistic episode\. Perspectives and context, motives and suggestions render to each member of the enterprise different disjoint appearances of knowledge\. There are thus many knowledge systems and multiple narrations, each with small episode\-like finality\. Enterprise innovation is achieved not through any grand episodic integration of all knowledge contents, but by constructively eliciting further new contents of knowledge, and encouraging acts of communications and discourses on this new knowledge\. Constructive management of knowledge and communication towards enterprise innovation has thus been defined\. Through such constructive management, NIIT enabled itself innovationally and empowered its members in eliciting knowledge and acting communicatively\. A critical feature of knowledge work is that it requires multidisciplinary expertise and mutual learning in order to achieve a complex synthesis of highly specialised state\-of\-the\-art technologies and knowledge domains\. A convivial work culture and a culture of communicative acts enable sharing of the non\-informatised yet recognised contents of knowledge\. \(direct link \)

## [Youth Unemployment and Economic Growth in Developing Economies: A Review of Structural Drivers and Policy Interventions](../publications/b36e98945155640c0616.md)

Dennis Sebastian Haldar

Youth unemployment remains a major socioeconomic challenge in developing economies, constraining productivity, increasing poverty, and limiting the potential contributions of young people to sustainable economic growth\. This review examines the structural drivers of youth unemployment and evaluates policy interventions designed to improve youth employment outcomes and promote inclusive economic development\. It explores the interconnected roles of skills mismatches, inadequate education and vocational training, limited access to finance, rapid population growth, informality, weak industrial development, gender inequalities, and insufficient employment opportunities in shaping youth labor market outcomes\. The review also considers how macroeconomic instability, technological transformation, and institutional constraints influence the capacity of developing economies to generate decent and sustainable jobs for young people\. Furthermore, it assesses key policy interventions, including technical and vocational education and training, entrepreneurship development, youth enterprise financing, active labor market programs, digital skills development, industrialization, and public–private partnerships\. The review indicates that isolated interventions are often insufficient to address the multidimensional nature of youth unemployment, particularly where economic growth fails to generate adequate productive employment\. Instead, coordinated strategies that align education and skills development with labor market demand, strengthen private\-sector job creation, expand access to productive resources, and promote inclusive economic diversification are essential\. The review also highlights the importance of institutional effectiveness, gender\-responsive policies, and targeted support for disadvantaged youth in improving employment outcomes\. It concludes that reducing youth unemployment requires an integrated, long\-term policy framework that connects employment creation with structural economic transformation, human capital development, and equitable access to economic opportunities\. Such an approach can strengthen productivity, stimulate aggregate demand, reduce socioeconomic inequalities, and enhance the contribution of young people to sustainable economic growth in developing economies\.

## [Recognition–decision–execution: a new design principle for intelligent antimicrobial systems](../publications/b36f12f6ece849d8cad4.md)

Jingwen Ma; Min Feng; Si Li

The continued rise of antimicrobial resistance highlights fundamental limitations of prevailing antibacterial strategies, which remain largely dominated by continuous, non\-directed killing\. Although combination therapies and multifunctional materials are frequently described as synergistic, many reported effects primarily reflect pharmacokinetic enhancement or local concentration increases, rather than genuine reprogramming of antibacterial behavior\. As a result, most current approaches still impose sustained selective pressure and offer limited control over timing, location, and intensity of killing\. Here, we propose the Recognition\-Decision\-Execution \(RDE\) framework as a function\-driven organizational principle for antibacterial system design\. In this framework, antibacterial activity is decomposed into three orthogonal yet logically coupled modules: pathogen recognition, decision\-making, and killing execution\. Recognition modules provide contextual information regarding pathogen identity, microenvironmental state, and infection dynamics; decision modules interpret these inputs to authorize action with defined spatiotemporal and intensity constraints; and execution modules eliminate pathogens only upon conditional approval\. This architecture transforms antibacterial activity from a default, always\-on process into a programmable, event\-driven intervention that may reshape rather than universally reduce selective pressure\. We discuss how functional decoupling enables a clear distinction between apparent \(pseudo\-\) synergy and true mechanistic synergy, and how regulatory\-execution interactions can qualitatively reshape killing mechanisms rather than merely amplifying them\. Importantly, functional roles are not intrinsic to specific agents: antimicrobial peptides, nanomaterials, and nucleic acid aptamers can dynamically interchange between regulatory and execution functions depending on system architecture\. The aptamer\-nanomaterial\-antimicrobial peptide triad serves as a minimal closed\-loop example illustrating how sensing, decision\-making, and execution can be independently optimized yet synergistically integrated\. By emphasizing system logic, modular verifiability, and conditional authorization of killing, the RDE framework offers a unifying conceptual language for the design of programmable and adaptive antibacterial therapies\. It should be emphasized that the RDE framework represents a unifying conceptual paradigm and set of testable design hypotheses\. Most reported antibacterial examples only achieve partial pairwise functional slices rather than fully\-validated ternary closed\-loop RDE architectures\.

## [p\-adic geometry of finite and infinite type](../publications/b371075f307c96647227.md)

Jack Jerry Garzella

In this thesis, we present four results: in the first, we give a fast algorithms for calculating the quasi\-F\-split height of Calabi\-Yau hypersurfaces in characteristic p\. In the second, we give a fast algorithm for calculating the zeta functions of projective hypersurfaces in characteristic p\. In the third, we show that Berkovich’s affinoid algebras and dagger algebras are F\-instersection flat \(and thus contain big test elements\)\. In the fourth, we consider the problem of the nullstellensatz of perfectoid Tate algebras\. We give a result and a counterexample; we establish a limitation on what the possible quotient fields, and we generalize a counterexample due to Gleason\.

## [CoTA\+\+: Understanding the Repeat Curse in dMLLMs from an Information Flow Perspective](../publications/b37be19cc831d3712889.md)

Qiyan Zhao; Xiaofeng Zhang; Xu\-Yao Zhang; Shijie Han; Zhepeng Li; Shunzhi Zhu; Da\-Han Wang

Diffusion\-based multimodal large language models \(dMLLMs\) decode by iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, which precludes the standard autoregressive key\-\-value cache\. Practical deployments therefore rely on approximate caching that reuses intermediate states across denoising steps\. Such caching, however, often makes a response repeat one token at adjacent positions in a run that breaks the sentence, a failure we term the \\emph\{Repeat Curse\}\. Tracing the context\-token information flow reveals three disruptions\. Within a step, caching disperses the attention that anchors a position on nearby context tokens\. Across steps, similarity\-based refresh is not staleness\-aware, so some positions are decoded against stale key\-\-value states\. Across layers, the deep\-layer entropy of the context fails to converge where repetition arises\. We accordingly propose CoTA\+\+, a training\-free, plug\-and\-play framework that counteracts each disruption where it originates: Context\-Token Attention Re\-anchoring re\-forms the attention routing against the current context, Decode\-Aware Refresh reserves part of the cache&\#x27;s refresh budget for the positions about to be committed, and Context\-Token Entropy\-Guided Voting discounts the confidence of a position by the deep\-layer entropy of its context, which reorders the unmasking\. The three components act at non\-overlapping stages of a decoding step and compose freely with existing dMLLMs and caches\. Across three dMLLMs and two caching backends, CoTA\+\+ reduces the sample repetition rate of long responses from up to 99\.6\\% to at most 17\.0\\%, recovers most of the accuracy lost to caching on nine benchmarks, and keeps the speedup of caching at under 15\\% overhead, making approximate caching reliable for dMLLMs\.

## [Analisis Sentimen Kepuasan Masyarakat terhadap Pelayanan Aplikasi Mobile JKN Menggunakan Algoritma Naïve Bayes](../publications/b389b4d1c966e5a3935d.md)

Muhammad Diaz R Rambe; Martiano

Program Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional \(JKN\) yang diselenggarakan oleh BPJS Kesehatan sedang memasuki masa transisi kebijakan Kelas Rawat Inap Standar \(KRIS\) berdasarkan Peraturan Presiden Nomor 59 Tahun 2024\. Perubahan kebijakan tersebut memunculkan beragam tanggapan masyarakat yang tersebar pada ulasan aplikasi Mobile JKN di Google Play Store, namun tanggapan tersebut belum diolah menjadi informasi yang dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan evaluasi layanan\. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengklasifikasikan sentimen ulasan pengguna aplikasi Mobile JKN menggunakan algoritma Naïve Bayes serta mengimplementasikan hasil klasifikasi ke dalam sistem informasi berbasis web\. Data dikumpulkan melalui teknik web scraping terhadap 4\.000 ulasan berbahasa Indonesia pada periode 15 Juli sampai dengan 15 Agustus 2026 dan menghasilkan 2\.675 ulasan hasil seleksi\. Pelabelan dilakukan menggunakan pendekatan rating pengguna dan kamus sentimen InSet dengan verifikasi manual pada ulasan yang kedua pendekatannya berbeda, sehingga diperoleh 751 ulasan berlabel positif dan negatif\. Data diproses melalui cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, dan stemming, kemudian dibobotkan menggunakan TF\-IDF\. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan model Naïve Bayes memperoleh accuracy 90,07%, precision 90,57%, recall 90,07%, dan F1\-score 89,99%, sedangkan 10\-fold cross validation memperoleh rata\-rata akurasi 90,68% dengan simpangan baku 2,60%\. Sebaran sentimen menunjukkan 403 ulasan \(53,7%\) bersentimen negatif dan 348 ulasan \(46,3%\) bersentimen positif, dengan keluhan pengguna terpusat pada proses autentikasi, khususnya pengiriman kode OTP dan verifikasi akun\. Sistem informasi berbasis web yang dibangun berhasil melewati seluruh 12 skenario pengujian Black Box dan dapat digunakan secara berulang untuk menganalisis ulasan pengguna tanpa harus membacanya satu per satu\.

## [Lightweight Hybrid CNN\-Transformer Network for Robust Maize Leaf Disease Detection and Edge Deployment](../publications/b38caa5ab9f58f42fcdd.md)

Awwab Mohammad; Punith kumar; Bhavani K; Sailee N\. Panchbhai; Sagarkumar S\. Badhiye; Manoj Kumar S B; Dharamvir; Sumit Kumar Sar; Rani Chhagan Dalvi; Yogesh Harishchandra Bhosale

Early and accurate detection of maize leaf diseases is essential for improving crop productivity and supporting precision agriculture\.However, deep learning models trained on controlled leaf\-image datasets often experience performance degradation under real\-world agricultural conditions because of illumination variation, background clutter, occlusion, leaf orientation, and imaging noise\.To address these challenges, this study develops a lightweight deep learning framework for robust maize leaf disease classification and edge\-oriented deployment\.The framework employs MobileNetV3\-Small for efficient extraction of disease\-discriminative visual features and investigates lightweight feature\-learning strategies for improving classification under challenging field conditions\.Experiments were conducted using PlantVillage\-Maize and Field\-Maize datasets comprising 6,188 images from four categories: Maize Leaf Blight \(MLB\), Common Rust, Healthy, and Leaf Spot\.The image\-only MobileNetV3\-Small model achieved 97\.8% accuracy and a 97\.4% F1\-score on the controlled PlantVillage\-Maize dataset, while its performance decreased to 86\.1% accuracy and an 83\.9% F1\-score on Field\-Maize, highlighting the domain gap between controlled and real\-field imagery\.Robustness was further evaluated under Gaussian noise, illumination variation, and partial occlusion, together with computational\-efficiency and edge\-deployment analyses\.The findings demonstrate the importance of lightweight and robust visual feature learning for practical maize disease diagnosis under real\-world agricultural imaging conditions\.

## [CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi\-agent Reinforcement Learning](../publications/b39eefb27f32146ec4d6.md)

Tianmeng Hu; Biao Luo; Ke Li

Designing RNA sequences that reliably fold into specific secondary structures is essential for understanding their biological functions but remains a challenging computational problem\. We propose CocoRNA, a cooperative multi\-agent reinforcement learning framework for RNA inverse design\. CocoRNA simplifies the design task by decomposing it into smaller sub\-problems, each solved collaboratively by multiple agents\. This approach reduces the complexity of the problem and improves the exploration of design policies\. During training, a centralized critic uses global structural information to guide the agents, enabling them to jointly optimize their design strategies\. As a result, CocoRNA learns high\-quality RNA design policies that generalize effectively to unseen structures without additional training\. Experiments on the Rfam dataset demonstrate that CocoRNA substantially outperforms state\-of\-the\-art methods in both success rate and design speed\. Further experiments on other biological sequence design tasks highlight the effectiveness and broad potential of CocoRNA for complex design tasks\.

## [Nanotechnology in orthopedic surgery: Advances, applications, and future directions](../publications/b3a9b55b1c52d9bd7045.md)

Rashwan A\. Elmeligy

Nanotechnology has emerged as a promising platform in orthopedic medicine, offering potential solutions to persistent challenges in implant integration, bone regeneration, cartilage repair, and oncologic drug delivery\. This narrative review summarizes recent advancements in orthopedic nanotechnology and critically evaluates their translational readiness\. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science \(2010–2026\), including peer\-reviewed English\-language studies on implant surface modification, bone tissue engineering, cartilage and meniscus regeneration, and targeted cancer therapeutics\. Most available evidence remains preclinical \( in vitro and animal studies\), with limited human clinical data\. Nanostructured surfaces have demonstrated improved osteoblast adhesion and early osseointegration in preclinical models\. Nanofibrous scaffolds enhance mechanical strength and guide stem\-cell differentiation, while stimuli\-responsive nanocarriers promote chondrogenesis and support meniscal repair\. In orthopedic oncology, functionalized nanocarriers enable passive and active tumor targeting and may overcome multidrug resistance\. Future progress will depend on standardized safety guidelines, scalable manufacturing approaches, and the integration of artificial intelligence\-driven nanomaterial design an emerging field in which machine\-learning models are increasingly used to predict nanoparticle behavior, optimize surface chemistry, and accelerate biomaterial discovery\.

## [AGRICULTURAL CROP\-RESIDUE WASTE CONVERTED INTO ELECTRICITY IN INDIA](../publications/b3b7e77b03755d94e344.md)

RAJU KRISHNA CHALANNAVAR; Hosamani PA; Deepika Gupta; Ravindra Balappa Malabadi

The importance of adopting a “waste\-to\-wealth” approach lies in reusing waste as a valuable resource rather than an economic burden and environmental issue\. India’s agricultural residues have the potential to generate over 18,000 MW of power annually\. Biogas plants are a progressive step taken by the Government of India to curb crop burning to prevent pollution\. In India, as agriculture plays a pivotal role in ensuring food and nutritional security, it also generates significant waste during cultivation, harvesting, and processing\. Agricultural waste is generated throughout the journey from farm to food plate\. Inadequate management of agricultural waste has become a substantial source of environmental contamination affecting air, soil, and water\. Agricultural waste management in India presents both significant challenges and opportunities\. Traditional practices, particularly crop residue burning, although ingrained, are often unsustainable and environmentally damaging\. Residue burning leads to the depletion of soil nutrients, degradation of soil health, and the emission of greenhouse gases\. The implementation of advanced waste valorization methods, like thermochemical and biochemical processes, can transform agricultural waste into valuable products, contributing to the circular economy and sustainable development\. Various agricultural wastes are generated in large amounts with different compositions, which plays an important role in selecting suitable velarization methods\. Addressing the technical, financial, social, cultural, and institutional barriers is crucial for the successful implementation of sustainable waste management\. Effective policy implementation is crucial for promoting sustainable agricultural waste management practices in India\.

## [Associação entre contágios de COVID\-19, vulnerabilidade social e população indígena no Norte Grande do Chile: uma análise multiescalar municipal e intraurbana](../publications/b3bd71e780a264361f86.md)

JUAN JOFRE; Gustavo Henrique Naves Givisiez

Diante da escassez de dados individuais sobre o impacto da pandemia na população indígena, analisouse a associação entre a taxa de casos ativos de COVID\-19, a vulnerabilidade social e a proporção de população indígena\. O estudo adotou um desenho ecológico misto multiescalar: nacional \(municípios\) e urbana \(dados espacializados em quadrantes de Arica, Iquique\-Alto Hospício, Calama e Antofagasta\)\. Utilizaramse testes de Qui\-quadrado e Tau\-b de Kendall, integrando uma análise de colinearidade que revelou a sobreposição entre etnia e vulnerabilidade no Norte Grande\. A frequência dos dados foi reforçada pela ponderação populacional, método que conferiu maior estabilidade às associações\. Os resultados revelaram padrões de contágio que se tornaram mais nítidos durante os picos epidemiológicos\. Embora a natureza dos dados agregados exija cautela para evitar a falácia ecológica na interpretação dos resultados, os achados fornecem indícios de um impacto desproporcional na população indígena\. Concluise que a segregação socioespacial e a transição epidemiológica polarizada atuaram como determinantes fundamentais na carga de contágios em contextos urbanos\.

## [Automotive Engineering in the Age of AI and Software\-Defined Vehicles](../publications/b3c76f5a891d570efa92.md)

Milan Bjelica; Bogdan Pavković; Ivan Kaštelan

Automotive engineering is undergoing a transition in which software, connectivity and artificialintelligence increasingly determine vehicle functionality throughout the complete product lifecycle\. The softwaredefinedvehicle extends development beyond the traditional point of production, as functions, operationalknowledge and customer\-facing features can continue to evolve after deployment through over\-the\-air updates\.Artificial intelligence adds another dimension to this development\. AI is becoming relevant not only for perception inadvanced driver assistance and automated driving, but increasingly for decision making and more integrated endto\-end approaches\. These developments create significant opportunities for vehicle functionality and customerexperience, while at the same time increasing the importance of systematic verification, safety engineering andlifecycle management\. This paper provides an editorial perspective on this changing automotive engineeringlandscape\. Particular attention is given to AI safety, verification pipelines, continuous engineering, software\-definedvehicle architectures, over\-the\-air updates and the emerging use of end\-to\-end AI\. The central observation is thatthese topics are closely connected\. Vehicles are becoming continuously evolving cyber\-physical products, whilesafety arguments have traditionally been developed around controlled configurations and well\-defined engineeringbaselines\. Future automotive engineering therefore requires development, verification, monitoring and updateprocesses that can preserve engineering evidence across repeated product changes\. AI further extends thisrequirement because its behaviour depends on data, operational conditions and statistical performance in additionto conventional software correctness\.

## [Nonlinear threshold responses of agroecosystem water use efficiency to increasing vapor pressure deficit](../publications/b3cac2d01095d9f27b11.md)

Youli Ma; 王明昌 Wang Mingchang; Xunhua Zheng; Hongchao Fan; Fengyan Wang

Increasing vapor pressure deficit \(VPD\) alters ecosystem carbon and water exchange, but agroecosystem water use efficiency \(WUE\) may respond nonlinearly to rising atmospheric evaporative demand\. The VPD levels at which these nonlinear transitions occur, their spatial consistency, and the factors associated with spatial variation in breakpoint magnitude remain poorly understood\. We therefore examined nonlinear WUE responses to increasing VPD and assessed how breakpoint magnitude varied across croplands in relation to environmental and agricultural characteristics\. Using multisource observations from 111 sub\-basins of the Songhua River Basin during 2002–2024 and independent eddy covariance observations from cropland sites, we identified a nonlinear WUE–VPD relationship\. The first derivative of the generalized additive model fit indicated a point of maximum WUE sensitivity to VPD at approximately 0\.27 kPa, whereas piecewise linear fitting identified the primary basin\-scale breakpoint at approximately 0\.41 kPa\. Repeated subsampling indicated that the basin\-scale breakpoint was robust to sampling variation, while local breakpoint estimates varied across sub\-basins\. Statistically supported breakpoints were detected in 59 of the 111 sub\-basins, and site\-level screening retained breakpoint estimates for 20 of the 28 evaluated cropland flux sites\. The mean breakpoint estimate across the 20 retained flux sites was approximately 0\.43 kPa\. Sub\-basin breakpoint magnitude was negatively associated with leaf area index, soil bulk density, and mean growing\-season precipitation total, and positively associated with C4 crop proportion\. Above the basin\-scale breakpoint, the sensitivity of gross primary productivity to VPD increased significantly, whereas the sensitivity of evapotranspiration showed no significant change, indicating an asymmetric carbon–water response\. At the retained flux sites, higher Bowen ratios and lower evaporative fractions above the site\-specific breakpoints were consistent with a relative shift in energy partitioning toward sensible heat\. The approximately 0\.41\-kPa breakpoint characterizes the basin\-scale WUE response to increasing VPD but does not represent a universal local threshold\. Spatial variation in breakpoint magnitude was associated with climate, vegetation structure, soil properties, and crop composition, although the observational design precludes direct causal attribution to individual management factors\. These findings clarify spatial variation in nonlinear agroecosystem WUE responses to increasing VPD and underscore the importance of local environmental context when interpreting carbon–water responses to atmospheric drying\.

## [A cumulative biochemical profile of low uric acid and high total bilirubin is associated with hemorrhagic transformation after intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study](../publications/b3d4980b99c42907c187.md)

Huan Liang; Baiyu Zeng; Jingquan Wang; Lizhen Yi; Linxing Huang; Ziyan Lin; Cai Zhou; Zenghui Yue

Background and objective Uric acid and bilirubin are endogenous redox\-related metabolites, but their joint association with hemorrhagic transformation \(HT\) after intravenous thrombolysis \(IVT\) remains uncertain\. We examined whether relatively low uric acid and high total bilirubin define a cumulative biochemical profile associated with hemorrhagic risk\. Methods In this single\-center retrospective cohort, we analyzed 733 patients with verifiable pretreatment uric acid and total bilirubin measurements from an IVT registry\. Low uric acid \(≤278 μmol/L\) and high total bilirubin \(≥12\.67 μmol/L\) contributed one point each to a 0–2 adverse\-feature score\. Any HT was the primary outcome; parenchymal hematoma \(PH\) and database\-defined symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage \(sICH\) were secondary outcomes\. Analyses used logistic regression, Firth bias\-reduced regression, multiple imputation and restricted cubic splines\. Results HT occurred in 79/733 patients \(10\.8%\)\. Observed HT rates were 7\.0%, 13\.6% and 26\.5% across zero, one and two adverse features\. Each additional feature was associated with higher odds of HT after covariate adjustment \(OR 1\.76, 95% CI 1\.19–2\.60; P = 0\.004\)\. PH occurred in 30/733 patients \(4\.1%\), and database\-defined sICH occurred in 33/664 patients with observed status \(5\.0%\)\. Continuous spline analyses in 731 patients showed evidence of an overall association for uric acid \( P overall=0\.044\) and total bilirubin \( P overall=0\.040\), without strong evidence of nonlinearity \( P nonlinear=0\.193 and P nonlinear=0\.704, respectively\)\. No multiplicative interaction between the continuous biomarker terms was detected \(OR 0\.99, 95% CI 0\.77–1\.28; P = 0\.938\)\. Conclusions Relatively low uric acid and high total bilirubin defined a cumulative biochemical profile associated with greater odds of HT after IVT\. The association requires external validation and should not be interpreted as evidence of causality or as a clinical treatment threshold\.

## [Case Report: transient migratory pulmonary nodules with bronchial artery malformations in an autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease patient: a case of recurrent hemoptysis](../publications/b3d5ed0c9f3364da4ef8.md)

Yi Hu; Jie Zhang; Ting Wang; Bing Xue

Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease \(ADPKD\) is associated with vascular malformations, but bronchial artery involvement with migratory pulmonary nodules has not been reported\. We describe an 81\-year\-old man with recurrent hemoptysis and migratory nodules on chest CT\. Digital subtraction angiography revealed tortuous, dilated bronchial arteries; embolization controlled bleeding and nodules resolved\. He had polycystic kidney and liver disease, a prior intracranial aneurysm, and a PKD1 missense variant \(c\.8426C &gt; T\)\. Common causes of hemoptysis were excluded\. This case describes co\-occurrence of bronchial artery malformation, recurrent hemoptysis and migratory pulmonary nodules in a patient with genetically confirmed ADPKD, raising the possibility that bronchial arterial involvement could be a rare, under\-recognized vascular manifestation associated with ADPKD\.

## [Yaratıcı işler üretken yapay zekâya devredilirken: Reklamcılıkta mesleki muhakeme](../publications/b3e218ea9902b58f1d54.md)

Mustafa Okay

This thesis examines how practitioners in advertising and related creative\-content work describe the reorganization of creative work through delegation to generative artificial intelligence \(AI\) and considers the implications for professional skill and judgment\. The interpretive qualitative study draws on fifteen semi\-structured interviews with sixteen practitioners in 2025\. Thematic analysis used a codebook informed by the literature and interviews\. Participants used AI for production, search, consultation, comparison, and preliminary checking\. They continued to interpret assignments, set direction, revise material, and decide what to deliver\. AI enabled some participants to attempt or complete work requiring more time, resources, or technical knowledge and to understand unfamiliar terms, workflows, and problems\. Preparing inputs, correcting outputs, and integrating material added work\. Using each participant’s earlier workflow for comparison, the study distinguishes what AI did, what it replaced, and what it added\. It then examines opportunities for practice, correction, guidance, and feedback in the reorganized work\. This connects research on AI\-assisted creative work with research on practice, learning, and assisted performance\. Opportunities for exploration sometimes narrowed, while other forms of practice continued and participants reported learning from AI\-generated examples\. Reported changes concerned particular capacities and varied in direction within individual interviews\. Interviews did not independently measure capacity or establish how wider professional judgment changed over time\. Most participants developed expertise before using generative AI, leaving limited evidence on newcomers’ professional formation\. Policy implications concern occupation\-specific capacity, the conditions for its use, process\-wide evaluation of AI adoption, and clear project responsibility\.

## [Regularized free deconvolution for spectral repair of resampling distortion in high\-dimensional particle filters](../publications/b3e3ebf3f59279e698df.md)

Deming Song; Chi\-Kin Lam; Kefeng Li; Hui Yu; Xilin Li; Huagang Lin

Resampling is the standard remedy for weight degeneracy in particle filters, but in high dimensions it distorts the spectrum of the ensemble covariance in a way that is computable from the importance weights\. This paper studies the inverse problem: recovering the pre\-resampling spectrum from the observed weights and the empirical spectrum alone, and using it without biasing the filter\. We first show that the forward spectral law extends to random importance weights once one conditions on the weights together with the realized offspring counts, rather than on the weights alone\. We then construct a regularized free\-deconvolution estimator, prove its consistency with an explicit error budget at a fixed resolution scale, and certify model mismatch through a computable forward residual\. The repaired spectrum enters the filter only as the preconditioner of a Metropolis\-adjusted rejuvenation move, so that spectral error affects mixing efficiency but not the invariant target\. For the full filtering cycle, we derive a geometrically summable error recursion under stable scalar dynamics and an explicit law for the cost of abstaining from repair\. Pre\-registered simulations show that the inversion reduces the spectral error by an order of magnitude, that the corrected preconditioner recovers about 90% of the oracle&\#x27;s sampling efficiency in an anisotropic regime, and that the cost of abstention depends on when abstentions occur rather than on how many\. The repair recovers eigenvalue laws, not eigenvectors, and is certified only within an explicitly stated exogenous\-weight regime\.

## [A transformer\-based attention network for high\-precision soil moisture retrieval using CYGNSS data](../publications/b3f07c81d30526cff5a1.md)

Xiangle Li; Feng Wang; Dong Wang; Weixin Li; Dandan Wang; Lei Yang

In recent years, NASA’s Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System \(CYGNSS\) has attracted significant attention for soil moisture \(SM\) retrieval through reflected signal analysis\. The improvement of SM retrieval accuracy has long been a hot spot in this field\. Most research restricts the utilization of the Delay\-Doppler Map \(DDM\) to peak power, which cannot fully capture the characteristics of the DDM\. A model named Transformer\-Neural Network \(TNN\) is proposed in this paper to improve SM retrieval accuracy\. The proposed model comprises a Vision Transformer \(ViT\) alongside a neural network\. Feature extraction through ViT enables more effective acquisition of overall DDM information\. The extracted DDM information is used to establish the connection with SM through a neural network, which improves SM retrieval accuracy\. The results show that high\-precision SM retrieval is achieved with our proposed model, in comparison with other machine learning \(ML\) models\. The value of R reaches 0\.88, and the value of root mean square error \(RMSE\) is as low as 0\.04\. The proposed model also exhibits good performance across various land cover types\. Moreover, the SM values predicted by the model show better consistency with the Soil Moisture Active Passive \(SMAP\) observations\. The proposed model effectively adopts the ViT image\-processing strategy, providing a new method to improve the precision of GNSS\-R SM retrieval\.

## [Improving Environment\-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding](../publications/b3f11c7c4bfcb00c878e.md)

Sergey Rodionov

Stronger language models may increasingly construct useful procedures for themselves, reducing the advantage of developer\-supplied scaffolding\. We investigate why this advantage persists and whether an environment\-agnostic agent can be improved without environment\-specific engineering\. We evaluate a Codex\-based agent in two nearly identical prompt variants on ARC\-AGI\-3, AGI Maze, and Terminal\-Bench\. Each variant is deployed with unchanged code, prompts, and general\-purpose tools across environments, receiving environment\-specific information as input\. Changing only an instruction to encourage reporting difficulties and returning control for automatic continuation improves mean scores on both ARC\-AGI\-3 and AGI Maze, while Terminal\-Bench shows small, mixed changes\. Yet the general agent remains below an ARC\-AGI\-3\-specific reference, including with GPT\-5\.6\-sol\. The reference prescribes organization and control rather than supplying new game rules or solutions\. To investigate this gap, we transfer reset decisions to a scripted controller that follows a convention already given to the agent\. This small change recovers part of the specialized agent&\#x27;s advantage\. A complementary AGI Maze experiment shows that additional tutorial experience can reduce performance\. Together, these findings highlight the distinction between having information and tools available and using them effectively\. Supplied procedures still matter for the models tested here\. The performance gains also come with higher token\-based cost\. The experiments do not separate better use of information and procedures from additional or differently allocated inference\. We provide the EnvTraverse framework and an evaluated baseline agent for testing whether further environment\-independent changes improve performance in some environments without degrading it in others\.

## [Adaptation of Computer Use Agents to New Software with User Manuals](../publications/b3f611b335cd16f1ff8a.md)

Chulhoon Yoon; Kyungri Park; Jinyeong Yun; Daeyun Jeong; Sukmin Yun; Woohwan Jung

Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have significantly improved the ability to operate real\-world software through graphical user interfaces \(GUIs\) using visual observations and natural language instructions\. However, maintaining strong performance on unseen applications remains challenging, as practical tasks often require long\-horizon procedural knowledge and application\-specific operation patterns\. In addition, constructing executable tasks and collecting corresponding trajectories for training still heavily rely on human\-annotated data, incurring substantial cost\. In this paper, we propose MAGE \(Manual\-augmented computer use AGent Execution and learning\), a framework that leverages user manuals as a scalable source of procedural knowledge to improve both inference and training\. During execution, MAGE retrieves task\-relevant manual content and uses a planner to generate explicit procedural guidance for CUAs\. To further account for the discrepancies between manuals and actual GUI environments, such as version differences or user settings, MAGE also adapts the agent policy through environment interaction\. During training, MAGE converts manuals into executable task\-plan pairs and uses the plans to guide environment rollouts toward task\-relevant states; the resulting trajectories are then used to optimize the policy without human\-authored demonstrations\. This unified design enables effective utilization of manuals for both task execution and training, reducing reliance on human\-authored training data\. Experimental results across six applications demonstrate improvements in task success rates over strong baselines, highlighting the effectiveness of manual\-guided planning and policy adaptation in new software environments\. We provide the code and reproduction scripts at https://github\.com/ku\-autoai/MAGE\.

## [Thinking With, Not Through, AI: Philosophical Counseling and Ethical Self\-Authorship in Teacher Education](../publications/b3fe19cbe6799e7fe8de.md)

Rotem Waitzman; Sivan Sarid Goldfisher

Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used to interpret professional situations, formulate arguments, and consider responses to ethical dilemmas\. Although these systems can broaden reflection, their persuasive outputs may encourage moral outsourcing, defined as transferring substantive elements of ethical interpretation, justification, or judgment to an external system without adequate examination, endorsement, or responsibility\. This conceptual article asks how generative AI can be integrated into philosophical counseling and ethical reflection in teacher education without undermining ethical self\-authorship\. Drawing on philosophical counseling, moral development, relational autonomy, professional ethics, and AI literacy, it develops the Ethical Self\-Authorship Cycle\. The model comprises five iterative stages: articulating the dilemma, pluralizing perspectives, interrogating assumptions, testing reasons and consequences, and reclaiming moral authorship\. Its contribution is threefold\. First, it distributes deliberative functions between the human participant and AI by specifying what the system may contribute and what it cannot establish at each stage\. Second, it requires the process to conclude with a human\-formulated justification rather than an AI\-generated recommendation\. Third, it treats ethical self\-authorship as a developing capacity requiring pedagogical scaffolding and ethically and digitally prepared teacher educators\. An illustrative case demonstrates the model’s application to a dilemma involving student use of AI in assessment\. The article argues that AI may generate material for ethical inquiry, but it cannot represent affected people, determine which values should prevail, or assume professional responsibility\. Moral authorship and answerability must remain human\.

## [Design and Empirical Evaluation of Erhu Teaching Aid System Based on Virtual Reality](../publications/b408246742644b105709.md)

Li Han

Digital technology facilitates traditional cultural inheritance, and virtual reality \(VR\) provides innovative approaches for ethnic musical instrument teaching\. This paper constructs a three‑module VR‑assisted Erhu teaching system to solve issues of one‑way instruction, delayed feedback, and single learning scenarios in conventional Erhu teaching\. Supported by motion capture and audio analysis, the system delivers real‑time playing correction\. An eight‑week controlled experiment with 120 learners shows that the VR group achieves higher fingering accuracy, lower pitch deviation, and better learning engagement than the traditional‑teaching control group\. Still, the system faces hardware‑related defects, and the study has limitations such as uncertain long‑term skill retention\. VR serves as an auxiliary rather than a replacement for Erhu instruction\. Future optimizations include lightweight Web‑XR adaptation and intelligent teaching resources to advance popularized, personalized VR Erhu education\.

## [β\-Boswellic Acid Suppresses Migration and Invasion and Attenuates TGF\-β1\-Induced EMT\-Related Changes in PC\-3 Prostate Cancer Cells](../publications/b40cc764726b0727254a.md)

Kaixin Song; Kunpeng Zang; Zihan Yang; Zhirong Tan; Xiaohui Geng; Jiale Wang; Lixi Zhu; Sijie He; Sian Pan

β\-Boswellic acid \(BA\) has potential antitumor activity, but its effects on migration, invasion, and epithelial–mesenchymal transition \(EMT\)\-related phenotypes in prostate cancer cells remain unclear\. In this study, we integrated public transcriptomic data, candidate molecule prediction, machine learning, functional association analysis, and molecular simulations with MTT, wound\-healing, Transwell, qPCR, Western blotting, transcriptomic analysis, and data\-independent acquisition proteomics to evaluate BA effects on PC\-3 cells and explore its potential molecular basis\. We identified 22 candidate BA\-related molecules and prioritised DPP4, MME, and ABL1 for further analysis\. Higher BA concentrations reduced PC\-3 cell viability\. At the same time, BA suppressed wound closure, migration, and invasion and attenuated TGF\-β1\-induced EMT\-related changes, accompanied by increased E\-cadherin and decreased N\-cadherin, Snail, and ZEB1 levels\. DPP4, MME, and ABL1 also exhibited BA\-associated expression changes\. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses suggested that BA\-associated molecular alterations involved the cell cycle, DNA replication, cell adhesion, cytoskeletal remodelling, and TGF\-β\-related processes\. In conclusion, BA suppresses migration and invasion in PC\-3 cells and attenuates TGF\-β1\-induced EMT\-related changes\. Candidate molecules including DPP4, MME, and ABL1, together with the multi\-omics findings, provide exploratory clues for further investigation of the potential molecular basis of BA activity\.

## [Clozapine‐Associated Neutropenia With COVID‐19 Infection and the Role of Filgrastim](../publications/b40f2cdac409f563e3e7.md)

Devender Singh Yadav

ABSTRACT Clozapine is the gold standard, evidence‐based treatment of choice for treatment‐resistant schizophrenia\. However, clozapine can induce serious, life‐threatening adverse effects, including neutropenia and agranulocytosis\. There is accumulating evidence to suggest that rechallenging with clozapine should be considered in most patients with clozapine‐associated neutropenia \(mild to moderate neutropenia\) who do not respond to other treatments\. Ruling out other causes of coincidental neutropenia is important when the neutropenia occurs after 2 years of treatment on clozapine, as the risk of developing neutropenia becomes negligible after 2 years and becomes nonspecific to clozapine\. When our patient developed neutropenia whilst taking clozapine during Covid‐19 infection, she benefitted from Filgrastim \[a Granulocyte‐Colony Stimulating Factor \(G‐CSF\)\], which provided symptomatic treatment\.

## [A Comprehensive Literature Review on Factors Affecting Timing, Contrast Media Volume, and Flow Rate in Cardiovascular CT Imaging](../publications/b41020b9e78654fb698f.md)



This literature review is a general overview about the most important factors affecting timing, volume and flow rate of contrast media \(CM\) during CT examination especially regarding image quality, sensitivity of diagnosis and patient safety\.The review covers the effects of the bolus timing methods, injection settings and patient\-related factors on enhancement of the contrast and radiologic outcomes\.In automated bolus tracking, test bolus strategies, and consideration of patient habitus have been noted as top priority in the optimization efforts of CM delivery\.Much emphasis is put on the relationship between rate of injection and contrast time and effects of incorrect loading of the contrast such as ineffective vascular visualization or unwarranted radiations\.The characteristics of the action of contrast media in the physicochemical aspect, the impact of the size of cannulae and the point of administration and their effect on the dynamics of contrast are also covered by the review\.The brief discussion of new technologies in artificial intelligence \(AI\) and automation in CT contrast administration administration is presented\.New tools are promising to individualize the protocols and improve similarity between various imaging centers\.Further studies should work to confirm the effectiveness of AI\-based bolus monitoring systems, in addition to defining patient\-oriented standards that will help guarantee the best achievable image quality and reduce contrast dose and side\-effects\.

## [A lightweight hybrid network with inverted residuals and state space model for remote sensing image segmentation](../publications/b41557bce69ada3f84d1.md)

Qixuan Tang; Ming Zhang; Liuye Yu; Yinghao Fan; Xuanwen Liu

Abstract In current research on semantic segmentation, the majority of studies primarily focus on utilizing traditional CNNs and Transformer\-based architectures\. However, CNNs are limited in capturing long\-range dependencies and accurately modeling global context information because their receptive fields are confined to local regions\. Although Transformer can effectively achieve global context modeling through the self\-attention mechanism, overcoming the limitations of local receptive fields, they inevitably introduce a computational burden that grows quadratically with the input size\. In recent years, Mamba based on state\-space models \(SSMs\) has received increasing attention due to its strong ability to capture global context while maintaining low computational complexity\. However, in the field of remote sensing image segmentation, existing Mamba\-based network architectures seldom achieve a balance between modeling long\-range dependencies and extracting finegrained local features\. Therefore, this paper proposed IRUM\-Net, a novel hybrid architecture that integrates Mamba and CNN for semantic segmentation of remote sensing images\. Specifically, the encoder of IRUM\-Net adopted inverted residual blocks \(IR Block\) as its basic building units, it is designed to extract rich image features with low computational cost\. Subsequently, we proposed a decoder module named Multi\-Scale Local and Global Mamba Module \(MLGM\)\. This hybrid module effectively combines Mamba and CNN, allowing for the simultaneous modeling of global contextual dependencies and multi\-scale local spatial details\. At the same time, a Gated Enhanced Fusion \(GEF\) module was designed\. It can connect and fuse the output of the previous decoder with the corresponding feature map in the encoder&\#x27;s skip connection at the same stage through a gating mechanism\. This process yielded a refined feature representation enriched with multi\-level information, which is then fed into the subsequent decoder stage\. We conducted extensive experiments on two public datasets, Vaihingen and Potsdam, achieving 81\.9% mIoU and 92\.2% OA on the Vaihingen dataset, and 84\.5% mIoU and 94\.2% OA on the Potsdam dataset\. Moreover, the overall network only has 1\.98M parameters and 6\.53G floating\-point operations\. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed IRUM\-Net outperforms most semantic segmentation networks while maintaining low computational overhead, achieving excellent segmentation accuracy\.

## [Design and Thermal Performance Analysis of a Multilayer Coolbox with Polyurethane as the Primary Insulation for Portable Fish\-Hold Applications](../publications/b41802113778a753f466.md)

Mustopa Kamal

Post\-harvest handling of fresh fish by small\-scale fishermen is highly dependent on effective temperature control to minimize quality deterioration during storage and transportation\. This study aimed to design, fabricate, and evaluate the thermal performance of a 70\-L portable coolbox using rigid polyurethane foam as the primary thermal insulation material\. The coolbox was constructed using a 3\-cm\-thick multilayer composite wall consisting of fiberglass \(1\.0 cm\), meranti plywood \(0\.5 cm\), aluminum foil \(0\.5 cm\), and rigid polyurethane foam \(1\.0 cm\)\. A rubber sealing strip and clamp locks were incorporated to reduce heat infiltration through the lid interface\. Thermal performance was evaluated experimentally over 168 h under two loading conditions: 30 kg of block ice and a combination of 30 kg of block ice and 20 kg of fresh fish\. A one\-dimensional steady\-state heat conduction model was also applied to estimate the thermal resistance and equivalent thermal conductivity of the composite wall\. The results yielded a total thermal resistance of 0\.4291 K/W and an equivalent thermal conductivity of 0\.0606 W/\(m·K\)\. Polyurethane contributed approximately 84\.15% of the total thermal resistance, indicating that it was the dominant insulating layer in the composite structure\. During the first 72 h, the internal temperature remained within approximately 0–4 °C under both loading conditions\. After 72 h, the internal temperature gradually increased as the ice load decreased, reaching 18–19 °C by the seventh day\. The total material cost for fabricating one prototype was IDR 1,445,000\. These findings indicate that the multilayer polyurethane\-based coolbox can provide effective passive thermal insulation for short\-term chilled fish storage in small\-scale fishing operations\.

## [Multi\-direction shift RWKV and frequency\-aware semantic network with for Ultrasound Image Segmentation](../publications/b41a180ad32fb87c3927.md)

Jiangxiong Fang; Yiming Ge; Danjiang Huang; Wenbin Ji; Youyao Fu; Huaxiang Liu; Jie Jin

Abstract Ultrasound image segmentation plays an important role in computer\-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support\. Accurate delineation remains difficult because ultrasound images commonly exhibit speckle noise, low contrast, blurred boundaries, and substantial variation in lesion morphology\. Convolutional neural networks are effective at extracting local patterns but have limited capacity for modeling long\-range interactions, whereas Transformer\-based methods may incur high computational cost and lose fine local details\. To address these challenges, we propose a Multi\-Direction Shift RWKV and Frequency\-Aware Semantic Network \(MDS\-RWKV\) for ultrasound image segmentation\. First, a Multi\-Direction Shift RWKV \(MS\-RWKV\) module combines linear\-complexity WKV recurrence with multi\-direction spatial shifting, enabling each token to incorporate two\-dimensional neighborhood information before recurrent modeling\. Second, a Spatial and Spectral Cross Aggregation \(SSCA\) module integrates multi\-scale spatial features with Fourier\-domain representations to enhance lesion\-boundary and texture discrimination under speckle interference and weak contrast\. Third, a Global and Local Feature Decoder \(GLFD\) progressively fuses high\-level semantic context with fine\-grained spatial details for accurate mask reconstruction\. Experiments on three public ultrasound datasets, BUSI, BUS\-BRA, and TN\-SCUI, produced mIoU values of 71\.27%, 84\.18%, and 79\.87%, respectively\. The aggregate results show improved region overlap and boundary accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines, while the complete model should be regarded as a moderate\-size network rather than a lightweight architecture\.

## [Language modeling on tabular data: a survey of foundations, techniques and evolution](../publications/b429871cc352ba48dbf4.md)

Yucheng Ruan; Xiang Lan; Jingying Ma; Yizhi Dong; Kai He; Mengling Feng

Tabular data, a prevalent data type across various domains, presents unique challenges due to its heterogeneous nature and complex structural relationships\. Achieving high predictive performance and robustness in tabular data analysis holds significant promise for numerous applications\. Influenced by recent advancements in natural language processing, particularly Transformer architectures, new methods for tabular data modeling have emerged\. Early techniques concentrated on pre\-training Transformers from scratch, often encountering scalability issues\. Subsequently, methods leveraging pre\-trained language models like BERT have been developed, which require less data and yield enhanced performance\. The recent advent of large language models, such as GPT and LLaMA, has further revolutionized the field, facilitating more advanced and diverse applications with minimal fine\-tuning\. Despite the growing interest, a comprehensive survey of language modeling techniques for tabular data remains absent\. This paper fills this gap by providing a systematic review of the development of language modeling for tabular data, encompassing: \(1\) a categorization of different tabular data structures and data types; \(2\) a review of key datasets used in model training and tasks used for evaluation; \(3\) a summary of modeling techniques including widely\-adopted data processing methods, popular architectures, and training objectives; \(4\) the evolution from adapting traditional Pre\-training/Pre\-trained language models to the utilization of large language models; \(5\) an identification of persistent challenges and potential future research directions in language modeling for tabular data analysis\. GitHub page associated with this survey is available at: https://github\.com/lanxiang1017/Language\-Modeling\-on\-Tabular\-Data\-Survey\.git \.

Sekiteri Patience Sametu; Ogunobo Romanus; Umar Adam Isah
