## [The role of artificial intelligence in energy systems development: A comparative analysis of national strategies and future directions](../publications/b431295a81a83db335ed.md)

Armin Razmjoo; Pedram Asef; Poul Alberg Østergaard

Artificial intelligence is expanding rapidly across energy systems, offering tools for renewable integration, forecasting, grid reliability, and demand management while also increasing electricity and infrastructure demand\. Yet evidence of its energy\-system benefits remains fragmented across national contexts and is often synthesised without accounting for differences in evidence quality or governance\. This study addresses that gap through a systematic review of 146 peer\-reviewed studies and authoritative reports published from 2010 to 2026, supplemented by earlier foundational methodological sources dating back to 1994\. It compares the United States, India, South Korea, and Sweden, selected to represent contrasting market\-led, emerging\-economy, state\-directed, and mature low\-carbon contexts\. The analysis combines an evidence\-tiered comparison across 14 energy\-system indicators, a city\-level deployment index covering ten urban centres, and a four\-pillar governance framework\. Reported studies indicate improvements in renewable\-energy forecasting performance, while CNN\-based and explainable machine\-learning approaches have been applied to power\-system fault detection; however, country\-specific quantitative validation remains uneven\. Northern Virginia/DC ranks first with an unrounded AECDI score of 83\.00, followed closely by Stockholm at 82\.95; both scores round to 83 for presentation, but they achieve these results through different pathways: infrastructure scale and grid deployment in Northern Virginia/DC, and low\-carbon electricity integration and institutional maturity in Stockholm\. Across the four cases, technical performance and investment alone do not ensure sustainable outcomes; grid carbon intensity, institutional capacity, cybersecurity, explainability, and equity shape how benefits are realised\. The study contributes a transparent and replicable approach that links evidence quality, sub\-national deployment patterns, and measurable governance priorities, providing practical guidance for more effective and equitable integration of artificial intelligence into energy systems\.

## [A self\-organizing developmental framework for the head direction ring attractor](../publications/b438c8d61c8b5d9f6367.md)

Shujia Liu; Bailu Si; J\. Michael Herrmann

The head direction \(HD\) system provides a continuous representation of the animal&\#x27;s facing direction and is a core component of the spatial navigation network\. Although mature HD circuits have been studied extensively, their developmental origin remains unclear, particularly because young animals already show attractor\-like internal coherence before stable visual anchoring is established\. Here we propose a developmental computational framework of the lateral mammillary nucleus and dorsal tegmental nucleus \(LMN\-DTN\) circuit, in which a functional HD ring attractor emerges through staged self\-organization without preconfigured topology or early external supervision\. In the model, a randomly connected LMN network first generates stable travelling waves through relative refractoriness\. These waves provide a temporal scaffold for subsequent learning\. Local STDP\-like and structural plasticity then consolidate wave\-based statistics into locally enhanced recurrent connectivity, followed by direction\-selective shift\-feedback learning in the DTN→LMN pathway\. At a later stage, recruited long\-range inhibition transforms the travelling\-wave manifold into a stable single activity profile \(bump\) attractor\. Visual input acts mainly as a late calibration signal for global integration gain: it improves short\-timescale path integration, but does not remove long\-term drift\. The framework provides a testable account of the developmental dissociation between early internal organization and later sensory anchoring\. More broadly, it suggests that key components of classical ring attractor models, including local recurrent structure, direction\-selective shift feedback, and late stabilizing mechanisms, can arise through a staged developmental process rather than relying on a preconfigured network architecture\.

## [Multi\-view context learning for human\-object interaction detection](../publications/b43a0c7f6db72c016e13.md)

Akmalbek Abdusalomov; Utkir Xudoynazarov; Umidjon Ruziev; Mukhriddin Mukhiddinov; Narziev Nosir; Alpamis Kutlimuratov; Cüneyt Şamil Oğurlu; Abror Shavkatovich Buriboev; Heung Seok Jeon

Understanding how humans interact with objects in complex visual scenes is fundamental to human\-centric artificial intelligence\. Yet, current Human\-Object Interaction \(HOI\) detection frameworks often falter when faced with visual occlusions, vague interaction semantics, and scenarios that extend beyond predefined categories\. We present Multi\-View Context\-Aware Disentangled Interaction Network \(MCD\-Inet\), a unified framework designed to robustly detect HOIs under these challenging, open\-world conditions\. Our approach integrates a novel Multi\-View Context Fusion mechanism that synthesizes fine grained spatial cues and broad semantic information across instance, interaction, and global levels\. To decouple the learning of object localization from interaction semantics, we introduce a Disentangled Interaction Decoder, enabling clearer task specific representations\. Complementing this, our Bilateral Knowledge Adaptation module bridges high\-resolution spatial features from the visual backbone with abstract semantics from a pre\-trained vision language model\. To overcome the challenge of occluded interactions, we design an Occlusion\-Robust Enhancement module, which extrapolates missing regions and mines contextual cues to recover interaction evidence\. Finally, MCD\-INet leverages multi\-modal prompts incorporating both textual templates and visual exemplars to extend its detection capabilities to unseen HOI triplets\. Extensive evaluations on HICO\-DET, V\-COCO, and the HICO\-Ambiguous datasets confirm the superiority of our approach, achieving a new state\-of\-the\-art mAP of 40\.7% and demonstrating significant resilience in occluded and zero\-shot scenarios\. MCD\-INet offers a powerful step toward generalizable, context\-aware HOI detection in real\-world visual environments\.

## [Comparative assessment of household plastic waste segregation, disposal practices, and recycling awareness in Ghana, Sierra Leone, and Zambia](../publications/b448bbf254356e3eabf0.md)

Elijah Afeliga; Michael Ato Essuman; Inusah Hamidu; Kwame Asamoah; Hastings Munyenyembe; Odis Adaora Isabella; Ernest Daniel Max Lavalie

The global increase in plastic usage has highlighted the urgent need for sustainable waste management practices, especially in developing countries\. Research indicates that shifting from a linear “take\-make\-dispose” model to a circular system could mitigate the growing plastic waste issue\. This study comparatively assesses household plastic waste generation, segregation, and disposal practices and their implications for plastic packaging recycling systems in Ghana, Sierra Leone, and Zambia—three Sub\-Saharan African countries facing significant plastic waste challenges\. This study employed quantitative research methods\. Data were collected from households and individuals in Ghana, Sierra Leone, and Zambia using a structured questionnaire containing open\-ended and closed\-ended two\-point Likert scales\. The sample comprised 216 respondents, distributed across the three countries: Ghana, Sierra Leone, and Zambia\. The data collected was then validated and analyzed using statistical tools such as the Chi\-square test and the Kruskal\-Wallis H test, and descriptive statistics\. The findings indicate that while households in these countries are generally willing to segregate waste, substantial barriers remain\. These include limited awareness of recycling symbols, inadequate waste segregation infrastructure, and insufficient economic incentives\. Most households dispose of plastic waste in garbage bins, with burning as the second most common method\. Also, interventions such as household goods exchange for plastic waste, segregation buckets, and periodic visits by officials could effectively increase household waste segregation\. The study concluded that while there is no significant difference between the three countries regarding the effectiveness of interventions like household goods exchange for plastic waste and segregation buckets, there is a clear need for better regulations, monitoring, and management of plastic waste\.

## [Cyber Threat Detection and Forensics for Ethereum Cryptocurrency Transactions](../publications/b44a39d6982d69adc83d.md)

Bhairab Sarma; Anupam Dutta; Prazna Lahkar; Chayanika Sarmah; Sangita Das

Objectives: To detect suspicious fraudulent activities in Ethereum wallet transactions using a graph\-based machine learning and anomaly detection techniques\. Method: From the Ethereum transaction graph, graph structure signals, timing cues, and node level attributes, have been analyzed using unsupervised models like Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor, and One\-Class SVM to flag irregular wallet patterns\. Finally, based on the transaction tracing pattern, illicit transactions are figure out for forensics actions\. Findings: This work successfully found some suspicious Ethereum wallet behaviors by mixing graph analytics with unsupervised anomaly detection techniques\. Graph\-based signals such as PageRank, clustering coefficient, transaction frequency and entropy, boosted the capture of strange transaction behaviors that point out as suspicious operation\. Isolation Forest did well at isolating the most extreme outliers, while LOF and One\-Class SVM highlighted wallets with odd local density, plus a clear behavioral mismatch observed\. Overall, the framework worked with the Ethereum transaction dataset from Kaggle, where wallet addresses\. Out of 4000 transaction history, top 20 are figure out as may be fraudulent transaction based on their behaviors\. Novelty: The study integrates graph analytics, blockchain forensics, and unsupervised machine learning to detect anomalous Ethereum wallet behavior without requiring labeled cryptocurrency fraud datasets\. Here, only 0\.5 percent Ethereum transaction are categorized as suspicious on this study\. Keywords: Blockchain Tracing, Cryptocurrency Transactions, Ethereum, Fraud Detection, Graph Neural Network \(GNN\)

## [From Food to Skin: Understanding Nutritional Dermatoses through the Ayurvedic Concept](../publications/b45289afde12e1ff43d6.md)

Rishita Gohel; Anita Ratnavat

Background: Nutritional status is fundamental to maintaining the structural and functional integrity of the skin\. As a metabolically active organ, the skin requires adequate proteins, essential fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, and other micronutrients for epidermal differentiation, cutaneous barrier maintenance, collagen synthesis, antioxidant defence, immune regulation, and wound healing\. Nutritional dermatoses comprise a heterogeneous group of cutaneous manifestations resulting from inadequate intake, impaired absorption, altered metabolism, increased physiological requirements, or excessive nutrient loss\. Objective: To review nutritional dermatoses and their clinical manifestations and explore their possible correlation with the Ayurvedic concepts of food, digestive fire and the formation of various tissues\. Methods: A narrative review was undertaken using contemporary concepts of nutritional dermatology concerning nutrient deficiencies, restrictive dietary patterns, malabsorption, chronic systemic disorders, and altered nutrient availability\. These concepts were examined alongside classical Ayurvedic principles related to digestion, transformation, nourishment, and tissue maintenance\. Results: Nutritional disturbances may manifest as xerosis, dermatitis, hyperkeratosis and many other conditions\. Ayurveda emphasizes food as a fundamental determinant of nourishment and health, with Agni governing the transformation and utilization of consumed food\. Metabolism and tissue formation \(Dhātu Poṣaṇa\) provide a conceptual framework for understanding the sequential nourishment of body tissues\. These concepts may offer a broader perspective on the relationship between dietary intake, digestion, metabolism, tissue nourishment, and skin health, although they cannot be directly equated with individual biochemical pathways\. Conclusion: Understanding nutritional dermatoses through both contemporary nutritional dermatology and Ayurvedic principles may provide an integrative perspective on nutrition\-related skin manifestations\. Further interdisciplinary research is warranted to explore these conceptual correlations systematically\. Keywords: Nutritional dermatoses, Dhātu Poṣaṇa, Nutritional deficiency

## [PURWARUPA KONTROL DAN MONITORING KANDANG AYAM PETELUR BERBASIS ESP32](../publications/b46de191f522a32e45fd.md)

Rega Priyanggara

Industri peternakan ayam petelur membutuhkan sistem pengelolaan kandang yang efektif untuk menjaga kondisi lingkungan dan meningkatkan produktivitas\. Pengelolaan kandang yang masih dilakukan secara manual sering menimbulkan permasalahan seperti ketidakstabilan suhu, keterlambatan pemberian pakan, serta proses pengumpulan telur yang kurang efisien\. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan membangun purwarupa sistem kontrol dan monitoring kandang ayam petelur berbasis Internet of Things \(IoT\) menggunakan mikrokontroler ESP32\. Sistem ini mengintegrasikan sensor suhu DHT22, sensor kapasitas pakan ultrasonik, dan sensor proximity untuk mendeteksi telur, serta menggunakan aktuator berupa relay, motor stepper, dan motor DC\. Sistem juga dilengkapi dengan penjadwalan berbasis RTC dan platform IoT menggunakan Blynk dan ThingSpeak untuk monitoring jarak jauh\. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu melakukan monitoring dan kontrol kandang secara otomatis sesuai perancangan\. Kata kunci: ESP32, Internet of Things, kandang ayam petelur, sistem monitoring, sistem kontrol\.

## [B2B influencer marketing collaborations: A relational governance perspective](../publications/b46eb9add31266ae3cec.md)

Heini Vanninen; Joona Keränen; Joel Mero

Influencer marketing has grown rapidly in business markets, yet existing research remains largely rooted in consumer contexts and organization\-centric perspectives\. Little is known about how B2B influencers perceive collaborations with companies\. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes B2B influencer collaboration as an interactionally constituted governance process and examines how governance mechanisms are interpreted by internal and external influencers\. Drawing on relational governance and role theory, we analyzed 27 interviews with B2B influencers\. The findings show that collaborations emerge through ongoing negotiation in which firms and influencers balance competing demands across collaboration stages\. We identify two distinct role logics that explain why similar governance mechanisms are interpreted differently and are associated with different collaboration dynamics\. The study contributes by framing B2B influencer collaboration as negotiated governance and introducing a role logics perspective to explain governance interpretations, with authenticity emerging as an outcome that can be enabled or constrained by governance arrangements\.

## [Toward modeling ecosystem responses to drought through coupled dynamical state representations](../publications/b46ef9a404d91288e716.md)

Junyi Liu; Xiang Zhang

Increasingly frequent and persistent drought disturbances are reshaping terrestrial ecosystems, making Modeling Ecosystem Responses to Drought \(MERD\) increasingly important not only to quantify ecosystem impacts but also to understand the mechanisms governing ecosystem trajectories\. Advances in satellite observations, ecological monitoring, and artificial intelligence have greatly improved the ability within MERD to detect drought impacts and predict ecosystem responses across large spatial and temporal scales\. However, an important remaining challenge is to connect environmental observations, statistical relationships, and process\-specific understanding within representations that explicitly describe how coupled vegetation\-water interactions generate ecosystem trajectories through time\. Here, we argue that MERD would benefit from complementing observation\-centered descriptions with dynamical representations of ecosystem state evolution\. We propose that ecosystem drought responses can be represented as evolving coupled dynamical states, complementing analyses based on individual environmental observations\. Within this representation, observations constrain the estimation of ecosystem states, while ecological feedbacks provide the mechanisms governing their trajectories\. We further introduce a coupled vegetation\-water dynamical representation as a prototype for encoding ecological mechanisms into state evolution\. This perspective provides a unified dynamical language through which resilience, recovery, response thresholds, dynamical transitions, legacy effects, carbon loss, and model\-based counterfactual scenarios can be interpreted as different manifestations of ecosystem dynamics\. We envision that future developments in MERD will increasingly integrate Earth observations, geospatial information, artificial intelligence, ecological theory, and mechanistic dynamical representations to move beyond predicting drought impacts toward explaining how ecosystem trajectories emerge\.

## [Implementation of the smart tourism concept and its impact on the intellectual potential of the region](../publications/b470807a4332fe7171b6.md)

Tatyana E\. Gvarliani; N\. V\. Frolova

Global economic development requires new approaches to regional management in the field of tourism\. In the context of digitalization, smart tourism stands out, which relies on the implementation and grouping of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, digital platforms, big data, and virtual and augmented reality\. This concept has gone beyond simple service automation, becoming a central element of regional innovation systems that significantly impact the development of territories and stimulate economic growth\. The article explores how smart tourism technologies are being implemented in the tourism ecosystems of Russian regions, and how the level of digitalization in these regions is affecting this process\. The study highlights the key components of this trend, including infrastructure, technology, social aspects, and institutional frameworks, and identifies key areas for strengthening smart tourism in the region\. The proposed Smart Tourism Readiness Index \(STRI\) has been considered, which is designed to assess the region&\#x27;s readiness for implementing the concept of smart tourism\. The comprehensive approach to creating tourist ecosystems focuses on both digital infra\-structure and the development of attractive tourist areas\.

## [From publication to action: connecting science, policy, and public attention for ocean\-related climate mitigation](../publications/b47790ddf70444552c21.md)

Devi Veytia; Laurent Bopp; Vicky Martí Barclay; Simon P\. Neill; Marie Bonnin; Daniela M\. Carranza; Joachim Claudet; Adrien Comte; Gaël Mariani; Yunne\-Jai Shin; Olivier Thébaud; Christian Robert Voolstra; Frédérique Viard; Jean‐Pierre Gattuso

Ocean\-related options \(OROs\), including marine renewable energy and ocean\-based carbon dioxide removal, are emerging as promising climate mitigation actions\. OROs vary widely in technological maturity and risk acceptability, yet as scientific literature exponentially increases, synthesising the current state of evidence is a major challenge\. Using causal inference across diverse datasets from scientific publications, policy and legislation documents, social media posts, and deployment metrics, we identify scientific publications and social media attention as direct drivers of action\. However, when social media attention overtakes research, actions may advance ahead of science – underscoring the need for responsive and robust policy development\. Through a narrative analysis of three case studies, we identify that at a global scale, coordinated and well\-designed policy with decisive implementation is key for catalysing step\-changes in ORO progress\. Together, our findings reveal the dynamic relationships linking science to action and highlight pathways for the effective and responsible scaling of OROs in the coming decades\.

## [INDÚSTRIA 4\.0 PARA MELHORIA DO DESEMPENHO DE PROCESSOS PRODUTIVOS](../publications/b484692ca75ea19efa3a.md)

Millena França Araujo Silva; Ana Carolina Vasconcelos Martins da Silva; Giovana Trindade do Nascimento; Maria Eduarda Ferreira Alves Pereira; Renato de Oliveira Lopes; Jonathan Silva dos Santos; João Pedro Cordeiro Salfemoser

A transformação dos processos produtivos promovida pela Indústria 4\.0 está diretamente relacionada ao avanço da digitalização, da automação e da comunicação entre sistemas e equipamentos\. Diante desse cenário, esta pesquisa busca compreender de que maneira a utilização de tecnologias associadas à Indústria 4\.0 pode favorecer o desempenho das operações produtivas, considerando tanto as oportunidades proporcionadas por sua aplicação quanto as dificuldades encontradas pelas organizações durante sua implementação\. Para o desenvolvimento do estudo, será realizada uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório, contemplando publicações produzidas no período de 2013 a 2026 e disponíveis em bases de pesquisa científica, entre elas o Portal de Periódicos da CAPES, SciELO, Scopus, Web of Science e Google Acadêmico\. A pesquisa contemplará diferentes recursos tecnológicos empregados no contexto da Indústria 4\.0, como Internet das Coisas, Big Data e Analytics, inteligência artificial, sistemas ciberfísicos, robótica, computação em nuvem, manufatura aditiva, sistemas MES e gêmeos digitais\. A partir da análise da literatura selecionada, verifica\-se que a utilização combinada dessas tecnologias apresenta potencial para aprimorar a produtividade e a qualidade dos processos, possibilitando também maior acompanhamento das operações, redução de desperdícios e utilização de estratégias de manutenção preditiva\. Entretanto, a adoção desses recursos também poderá ser condicionada por fatores como custos de implementação, necessidade de qualificação dos trabalhadores, proteção das informações, compatibilidade com tecnologias já existentes e adaptação das equipes às mudanças organizacionais\. Assim, a análise realizada permite compreender que a contribuição da Indústria 4\.0 para o desempenho produtivo não dependerá exclusivamente da incorporação de novas tecnologias\. Os resultados estarão associados, sobretudo, à capacidade da organização de integrar os recursos tecnológicos aos seus processos, às competências de seus profissionais e às práticas de gestão adotadas\.

## [GENETIC INSIGHTS INTO А KAZAKHSTANI FAMILY WITH MULTIPLE NEUROLOGICAL CONDITIONS: A CASE REPORT](../publications/b4868f6ed0d980da2931.md)

Aidana Gabdulkayum; Zhanel Z\. Mirmanova; Asset Z\. Daniyarov; Zh\. Medetbekova; A\.S\. Kudaibergenov; Saya Amangeldikyzy; Azhar Giniyat; Adil Y\. Yerezhepov; Akbota M\. Aitkulova; Ainur R\. Akilzhanova; Dauren Yerezhepov

Introduction\. Neurological disorders \(ND\) are diseases that affect both the central nervous system \(CNS\) and peripheral nervous system \(PNS\)\. The aetiology of neurological disorders is highly diverse and may involve genetic, environmental, metabolic, infectious, immune\-mediated, and acquired factors\. Epilepsy, cerebral palsy \(CP\), and autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\) are clinically and genetically heterogeneous neurological and neurodevelopmental conditions that frequently manifest during childhood\. Although these disorders have distinct core clinical features, considerable phenotypic overlap and comorbidity are observed, suggesting they may share underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms\. Methods\. Recruitment of the family, interview and clinical data acquisition, as well as blood sample acquisition, took place at the “National Center for Children&\#x27;s Rehabilitation” NJSC\. DNA was isolated using commercially available kits\. Whole\-exome sequencing \(WES\) was performed using DNA Prep with Exome 2\.0 Plus Enrichment Kit on the NovaSeq\-6000 platform\. All sequencing reads were mapped to the human reference genome assembly GRCh38 \(hg38\) using the DRAGEN Platform\. Variant annotation was performed using VEP release 116\.0\. Results\. We recruited a family with multiple neurological conditions\. The parents were a Kazakh male and female with no family history of neurological or neurodevelopmental conditions\. Marriage is non\-consanguineous\. There are three probands in the family diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder \(ASD\), focal symptomatic epilepsy, and \(ASD\) and ataxic cerebral palsy \(CP\), respectively\. Bioinformatic analysis revealed pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in IL10, CDKN2B, GALC, and SLC12A3 genes\. In addition, we identified variants of uncertain significance \(VUS\), loss\-of\-function \(LoF\), compound heterozygous, X\-linked, and single de novo mutation, in many genes involved in neurological or neurodevelopmental conditions\. Conclusion\. Overall, our findings demonstrate substantial genetic heterogeneity within a single family presenting with different neurological and neurodevelopmental phenotypes\. The results highlight the challenges of interpreting rare and uncertain variants identified by whole\-exome sequencing and emphasize the importance of integrating variant classification, inheritance patterns, segregation analysis, clinical phenotype, and available gene–disease evidence\. Further functional studies and accumulation of additional clinical cases will be required to determine the contribution of the identified candidate variants to autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, and other neurological manifestations in this family\.

## [Intrinsically Spin‐Exchange‐Field‐Modulated Two‐Dimensional Sensor with Platinum Single Atoms for High‐Performance Hydrogen Peroxide Monitoring](../publications/b495744ab0e8a9f66ca2.md)

Hongjian Dai; Zhen Tang; Huijie Yu; Tiantian Su; Yun Xiu; Zhaojie Huang; Wenjie Lu; Xin Gong; Wenxuan Gu; Peiyan Yu; Yuxiang Xian; Guangchao Zang; Yuchan Zhang

ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts \(SACs\) offer broad prospects in catalysis and sensing due to their maximum atom efficiency and tunable coordination\. However, the performance of Pt‐based SACs in electrochemical hydrogen peroxide \(H 2 O 2 \) sensing remains kinetically limited\. To overcome this, we propose a magnetic engineering strategy that introduces Fe/Co atoms adjacent to Pt sites\. Through in situ pyrolysis, magnetized Pt SACs \(mag‐Pt SACs\) were stably anchored on a 2D electrode\. This approach uses the intrinsic magnetic moments of Fe/Co to induce local spin polarization, thereby modulating the electronic structure of Pt without an external field\. Compared to PtN 4 and Fe‐Co diatomic catalysts, the mag‐Pt SACs‐modified electrode exhibited significantly enhanced sensitivity—by 1\.80‐ and 2\.14‐fold, respectively\. Mechanistic studies reveal that the induced spin polarization generates a net magnetic moment and unpaired electrons at Pt, which optimizes the d ‐band center and weakens the over‐strong adsorption of reaction intermediates, thus lowering the H 2 O 2 reduction barrier and boosting sensing kinetics\. Based on this spin‐polarization enhancement, the mag‐Pt SACs biosensor achieved highly sensitive and selective real‐time monitoring of H 2 O 2 fluctuations from MSB/VK3‐stimulated cancer cells\. This work introduces spin behavior into electrocatalytic kinetics, providing a new paradigm for designing high‐performance SAC‐based electrochemical sensors\.

## [Analysis of The Malfunction And Handling of The Access Control Intercom At An Airport Boarding Lounge](../publications/b499a1247059b2d3dc0b.md)

sari nastiti nalurita; Juvinal Ximenes Guterres; Ade Irfansyah; Teguh Imam

The access control intercom is part of an airport&\#x27;s physical security system that connects Aviation Security \(AVSEC\) officers in the field with the On Duty \(OD\) monitoring room through a structured cabling network\. On 24 January 2025, a malfunction was found in the intercom at Boarding Lounge Garbarata Way Gate B5, Terminal 1B \(BL GW B5\) of Soekarno\-Hatta International Airport, where the device could not place a call to the AVSEC OD room\. This article aims to analyze the cause of the malfunction and document the repair process\. The method used was field observation and systematic troubleshooting, consisting of inspecting the intercom&\#x27;s condition, conducting a comparative test on a similar unit, and checking the LAN cable network using a LAN Tester\. The inspection showed that the comparison intercom functioned normally, while the LAN Tester test on the faulty unit showed only two of nine pins lit \(eight data pins and one ground pin\), indicating a broken cable path\. Further tracing found that the LAN cable on the intercom side was severed, which was attributed to termite damage and is consistent with the minimal maintenance during the approximately four years Terminal 1B was not in operation after the pandemic\. The repair was carried out by re\-crimping the LAN cable, and the test results showed all pins functioning normally and a successful call to the AVSEC OD room\. This case study emphasizes the importance of preventive maintenance and network infrastructure monitoring for rarely used facilities to maintain the reliability of airport access control systems\. The study is limited to a single case, and photographic evidence of the cable damage is not presented\.

## [Beyond Compliance: Rethinking Pedagogy and Creative Epistemologies in Nigerian Postgraduate Education](../publications/b4a68ad135f01fd3437d.md)

Ademola Omoniyi Ajibade

Nigerian postgraduate education drives the nation&\#x27;s research capacity, yet it risks pedagogical inertia when quality assurance, including the National Universities Commission&\#x27;s minimum academic standards and accreditation, is reduced to procedural compliance\. This paper rethinks postgraduate education by shifting attention toward pedagogies that foster intellectual agency, dialogue, epistemic plurality and context\-sensitive knowledge production\. Drawing on critical pedagogy, decolonial theory, Ubuntu and Igwebuike, and situated\-learning theory, it uses a critical\-integrative conceptual method and a purposive review of policy documents and Nigerian, African and international literature\. The evidence is strongest for structural constraints on supervision and staff retention and for the Eurocentric orientation of methodological training in African research, but thin or inferential for prevailing pedagogy and examination practice; these claims are therefore advanced as nine testable hypotheses rather than established facts\. The paper proposes four connected commitments \(relational supervision, epistemic plurality, creative rigour and public relevance\), operationalised through the CARE model \(Criticality, Agency, Relationality and Epistemic creativity\)\. It argues that standards should be an enabling floor rather than an intellectual ceiling, that resourcing rather than intent is the main obstacle to reform, and that CARE can be adopted through a staged, low\-cost, workload\-neutral pathway viable for early\-career supervisors and under\-funded state universities\.

## [Mihal, Jan &amp; Black, C\. F\.: Flowing with AI: Towards a New Jurisprudence](../publications/b4aea570b4668b854e66.md)



This Element introduces a new jurisprudence for exploring artificial intelligence \(AI\) and law in an open and creative way\. Drawing upon the backgrounds of, respectively, an Indigenous jurisprudent and poet \(Black\) and a legal philosopher \(Mihal\), the Element develops a &\#x27;mythosophical&\#x27; approach informed by narrative theory, Indigenous jurisprudence, and original interpretations of stories from the past\. To imagine possible lawful futures with AI, the Element weaves a stream of what it calls &\#x27;flows&\#x27;, designed to allow readers openness and flexibility as they engage with the ideas underpinning this new jurisprudence\. As worldwide changes sweep us into a vortex of ceaseless innovation, the Element provides a cultural scaffolding through which to relate to AI as an autonomous, cunning, &\#x27;non\-human&\#x27; intelligence in lawful terms\. It offers insights both old and new which assist in reconceptualising problems and aligning with the paradigm\-shattering changes of the present day\. \(direct link \)

## [Fostering Healthy Digital Practices: Exploring the Conceptual Relationship between Netiquette and Mental Well\-being among Prospective Teachers](../publications/b4b8988683f5a320fd39.md)

Hrishikesh kushwaha; Shefali Jaiswal

Digital communication now sits at the centre of how prospective teachers learn, collaborate and prepare for the profession, yet the courtesy norms that govern those exchanges, commonly called netiquette, are seldom examined as a matter of psychological health\. This conceptual paper examines how netiquette and mental well\-being may be related among prospective teachers\. It draws on a synthesis of seventeen sources on netiquette, digital citizenship, cyber incivility, digital well\-being and teacher education\. The paper first clarifies the key constructs and then reviews what is known about how online conduct shapes emotional experience in educational settings\. The synthesis shows that the evidence connecting the two domains is indirect and unevenly distributed: studies of netiquette rarely measure well\-being, and studies of well\-being rarely isolate netiquette\. To bridge this gap, the paper proposes a conceptual model in which netiquette knowledge, netiquette practice and the netiquette climate of a learning community influence well\-being through psychological safety, communication competence and emotional regulation, with gender, digital confidence, cultural context and institutional policy as possible moderators\. Five testable propositions and a research agenda follow, together with implications for teacher education programmes, including those operating under India&\#x27;s National Education Policy 2020\. The paper argues that netiquette education should be reframed from an exercise in rule compliance into a well\-being\-oriented competence for future teachers\.

## [Using artificial intelligence to manage business processes](../publications/b4b8f770537ce0e9526c.md)

Jan Duler

Umetna inteligenca predstavlja hitro razvijajoče se področje, katerega uporaba se vse bolj širi tudi na področje upravljanja poslovnih procesov\. Organizacije strmijo k temu, da se poslovni procesi izvajajo čim bolj učinkovito, nenehno izboljšujejo ter da se prilagajajo spremembam v poslovnem okolju\. Pri tem se pojavljajo nove možnosti uporabe umetne inteligence za podporo in izboljšanje upravljanja poslovnih procesov\. Magistrsko delo najprej obravnava področje umetne inteligence, njen razvoj skozi čas, etične dileme ter izbrane tehnike in pristope, med katere sodijo strojno učenje, robotska avtomatizacija procesov, prepoznavanje govora, obdelava naravnega jezika in računalniški vid\. V nadaljevanju je predstavljeno upravljanje poslovnih procesov, pri čemer so obravnavani njegovi ključni elementi, življenjski cikel, notacija za modeliranje poslovnih procesov ter sistemi za upravljanje s poslovnimi procesi\. Osrednji del magistrskega dela povezuje obe področji ter predstavlja tehnike in pristope umetne inteligence pri upravljanju s poslovnimi procesi, ter možnosti njihove uporabe v posameznih fazah življenjskega cikla\. Obravnavane so tudi funkcionalnosti in izzivi razvoja z umetno inteligenco podprtih sistemov za upravljanje poslovnih procesov\. Rezultati pregleda in analize literature so pokazali, da je področje uporabe umetne inteligence pri upravljanju poslovnih procesov že razmeroma dobro raziskano ter da obstajajo številni konkretni pristopi in možnosti njene uporabe\. Dosedanje raziskave kažejo na pozitiven vpliv umetne inteligence na upravljanje poslovnih procesov, predvsem z vidika njihove avtomatizacije, analize, optimizacije in podpore pri odločanju\. Ugotovljeno je bilo tudi, da je različne tehnike umetne inteligence mogoče uporabiti skozi celoten življenjski cikel upravljanja s poslovnimi procesi\. Njeno vključevanje v sisteme za upravljanje s poslovnimi procesi dodatno razširja njihove zmogljivosti in omogoča razvoj naprednejših sistemov\. Kljub številnim možnostim in prednostim pa področje še vedno spremljajo različni izzivi, zaradi česar ostaja veliko prostora za nadaljnji razvoj in raziskovanje\.

## [Exploring Perceptions of Digital Currency: A Sentiment Analysis and Islamic Perspective](../publications/b4c74f31b64faa4b6094.md)

Aam Slamet Rusydiana

Digitalization in the economic and financial sectors is currently advancing at a very rapid pace\. Topics concerning cryptocurrencies, bitcoin, ethereum, and other blockchain\-based assets have become significant and compelling issues\. One particularly crucial topic today relates to digital currency\. The decentralized nature of these digital currencies presents a myriad of opportunities and challenges\. This study investigates contemporary views on digital currencies through sentiment analysis and evaluates them from an Islamic legal perspective\. By analyzing 100 Scopus\-indexed academic articles using the SentiStrength software, the study categorizes the sentiment into 45% neutral, 39% negative, 12% positive, and 4% highly negative\. Neutral sentiment suggests a balanced scholarly stance, while negative views emphasize concerns over volatility, regulation, and security\. From an Islamic viewpoint, digital currencies like Bitcoin are generally viewed as non\-compliant due to speculation, gharar \(uncertainty\), and high risk\. However, opinions vary depending on usage context\. The study highlights the need for greater regulatory clarity and improved digital literacy\. It offers valuable insights for scholars, policymakers, and Muslim stakeholders seeking to navigate the ethical and financial implications of these assets\. This research uniquely contributes to the literature by combining computational sentiment analysis with Shariah evaluation, urging future research on practical applications and religious acceptability of digital currencies\.

## [Key Success Factors in CRM Implementation: A Case Study of Salesforce](../publications/b4c8f102d8ab0bfd3bc9.md)

Tjaša Duh

Učinkovito upravljanje odnosov s strankami predstavlja pomemben dejavnik uspešnega poslovanja podjetij\. CRM\-rešitve omogočajo celovito upravljanje podatkov o strankah ter učinkovito podporo prodajnim, marketinškim in storitvenim procesom\. Uspešna implementacija CRM\-rešitve pa presega zgolj tehnološki vidik, saj je v veliki meri odvisna tudi od obvladovanja organizacijskih, procesnih in človeških dejavnikov\. Magistrsko delo obravnava ključne dejavnike uspešne implementacije CRM\-rešitev s poudarkom na rešitvi Salesforce CRM ter preučuje njihovo vlogo v poslovni praksi na primeru podjetja X\. V teoretičnem delu so predstavljeni razvoj in temeljne značilnosti CRM\-rešitev, njihove vrste, arhitektura, prednosti ter sodobni razvojni trendi\. Posebna pozornost je namenjena procesu implementacije CRM\-rešitve ter dejavnikom, ki pomembno vplivajo na njegovo uspešnost\. Empirični del temelji na analizi implementacije rešitve Salesforce CRM v podjetju X in se osredotoča na tri ključna področja: razloge za implementacijo rešitve, potek implementacije ter analizo ključnih dejavnikov uspeha\. Obravnavane so najpomembnejše odločitve in aktivnosti v posameznih fazah implementacije ter dejavniki, ki so vplivali na uspešnost projekta\. Med njimi so zlasti podpora vodstva, kakovost in migracija podatkov, integracija z obstoječimi informacijskimi sistemi, testiranje ter vključevanje in usposabljanje uporabnikov\. Ugotovitve kažejo, da uspešna implementacija CRM\-rešitve zahteva celovito in usklajeno povezovanje poslovnih potreb, procesov, podatkov, tehnologije in uporabnikov\. Analiza primera podjetja X kaže, da lahko premišljeno načrtovana in učinkovito izvedena implementacija prispeva k izboljšanju poslovnih procesov, vzpostavitvi celovitejšega pogleda na stranko, učinkovitejšemu upravljanju storitvenih procesov ter večji sprejetosti rešitve med zaposlenimi\. Raziskava potrjuje, da implementacije CRM\-rešitve ni mogoče obravnavati zgolj kot tehnološki projekt, temveč kot celovit proces poslovnih in organizacijskih sprememb\. Za uspešno implementacijo rešitve in doseganje dolgoročnih poslovnih koristi je zato ključnega pomena usklajeno obravnavanje tehnoloških, organizacijskih, procesnih in človeških dejavnikov\.

## [The esophageal microbiome–helicobacter pylori axis in gastroesophageal reflux disease and its therapeutic implication](../publications/b4cb9c4271ab78f798c1.md)

Syed Rafiq Hussain Shah; Bakhtawar Khan; Tanveer Khan; Muhammad Ajmal Khan; Moeen Khan; Liqing Zhao

Gastroesophageal reflux disease \(GERD\) is a chronic gastrointestinal disorder caused by the reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus, leading to symptoms such as heartburn, regurgitation, and dysphagia\. Persistent reflux can result in complications including reflux esophagitis \(RE\), non\-erosive reflux disease \(NERD\), Barrett’s esophagus \(BE\), and esophageal adenocarcinoma \(EAC\)\. Besides gastric acid exposure and lower esophageal sphincter dysfunction, emerging evidence suggests that alterations in the esophageal microbiome play an important role in GERD pathogenesis and progression\. This review summarizes the clinical spectrum, inflammatory mechanisms, and microbial alterations associated with GERD, with particular focus on the role of Helicobacter pylori and esophageal dysbiosis\. Differences between healthy and diseased esophageal microbiota, along with the influence of factors such as diet, obesity, smoking, antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors, and probiotics, are discussed\. The review also highlights the involvement of inflammatory pathways, including Toll\-like receptor and NF\-κB signaling, in reflux\-associated mucosal injury\. Finally, potential therapeutic strategies targeting microbiome modulation, including probiotics, prebiotics, bacteriocins, and anti\-inflammatory approaches, are explored\. Understanding the interaction between the esophageal microbiome and GERD may provide new insights for improved diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of esophageal diseases\. Graphical abstract

## [Floridi, Luciano &amp; Nobre, Anna C\.: Anthropomorphising Machines and Computerising Minds: The Crosswiring of Languages between Artificial Intelligence and Brain &amp; Cognitive Sciences](../publications/b4da187cc4124432b27a.md)



\_Minds and Machines\_ 34 \(1\):1\-9\. 2024The article discusses the process of “conceptual borrowing”, according to which, when a new discipline emerges, it develops its technical vocabulary also by appropriating terms from other neighbouring disciplines\. The phenomenon is likened to Carl Schmitt’s observation that modern political concepts have theological roots\. The authors argue that, through extensive conceptual borrowing, AI has ended up describing computers anthropomorphically, as computational brains with psychological properties, while brain and cognitive sciences have ended up describing brains and minds computationally and informationally, as biological computers\. The crosswiring between the technical languages of these disciplines is not merely metaphorical but can lead to confusion, and damaging assumptions and consequences\. The article ends on an optimistic note about the self\-adjusting nature of technical meanings in language and the ability to leave misleading conceptual baggage behind when confronted with advancement in understanding and factual knowledge\. \(direct link \)

## [Digital Technologies in Undergraduate Dental Education: A Scoping Review](../publications/b4dc914eca956b94421d.md)

Dimitar Kirov; Ilia Liondev; Мариана Димова\-Габровска; Todor Ts\. Uzunov; Aleksandar V\. Naydenov; Ivet Dzhondrova

Digital technologies are becoming increasingly embedded in undergraduate dental curricula, with the potential to support learning and skills development\. This scoping review mapped recent evidence on the implementation and educational applications of contemporary digital technologies in undergraduate dental education\. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify studies published between 2021 and 2025\. The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA\-ScR reporting guidelines and included studies investigating digital technologies in undergraduate dental education\. A total of 24 studies met the inclusion criteria\. The identified technologies included virtual reality and simulation\-based learning systems, digital and 3D\-printed educational models, digital assessment and feedback systems, web\-based learning platforms, artificial intelligence applications, CAD/CAM technologies, and digital clinical devices\. Across the included studies, the reported educational outcomes most commonly concerned practical performance, knowledge acquisition, student engagement, self\-assessment, and satisfaction, with many studies focusing on short\-term preclinical or learner\-reported outcomes\. Virtual simulation and digital assessment systems were the most extensively investigated technologies\. The available evidence suggests that digital technologies may support undergraduate dental education when used as adjuncts to conventional teaching methods\. However, the effectiveness of specific blended\-learning models requires direct comparative evaluation\. Future research should prioritize longitudinal and methodologically rigorous studies examining long\-term knowledge retention, clinical competence, educational quality, and the transfer of acquired skills to professional practice\.

## [Remote Video Assessment of Ataxia via SARA home : Correlation of Pose‐Derived Endpoints with Clinician Severity Ratings](../publications/b4e1087f780cec608ba4.md)

Rabia Aziza; Elisa Ferrer\-Mallol; Fereshteh Poursaeed; Vivian Maas; Jennifer Faber; Arian Taheri Amin; Katharina Hill; Matthis Synofzik; Lisa H\. Graf; Dagmar Timmann; Andreas Gustafsson Thieme; Paola Giunti; Héctor García‐Moreno; Magda M\. Santana; Jeannette Hübener‐Schmid; Elin Haf Davies; Thomas Klockgether; Marcus Grobe‐Einsler

Abstract Background Remote assessment of ataxia is increasingly important for patient‐centered care and clinical research\. SARA home , a validated video‐based adaptation of the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia \(SARA\), enables self‐administration of key motor tasks at home\. Objective The aim was to evaluate the correlation of pose‐derived gait and stance endpoints from SARA home videos with clinician‐rated severity\. Methods In a multisite observational study, participants recorded SARA home tasks on consumer mobile devices via the Atom5 TM app\. Clinicians rated videos using standardized criteria, blinded to automated outputs\. Kinematic measures were extracted via pose estimation and aggregated to video‐level features\. Videos were aggregated per participant before correlation using Spearman&\#x27;s ρ and Kendall&\#x27;s τ , with 95% cluster‐bootstrap confidence intervals\. Results We analyzed 5418 gait and stance videos from 58 participants across 4 sites \(gait n = 2205, stance n = 3213\)\. Score distribution was skewed toward lower severity\. For gait, clearance variability \( ρ = 0\.52 \[0\.37–0\.64\]\) and median‐normalized base of support \( ρ = 0\.51 \[0\.35–0\.66\]\) correlated most strongly with item ratings, followed by shoulder sway root mean square \( ρ = 0\.43 \[0\.24–0\.60\]\)\. Adjusted foot clearance \(worse limb\) correlated negatively \( ρ = −0\.35 \[−0\.52 to −0\.15\]\)\. For stance, anteroposterior sway \( ρ = 0\.51 \[0\.36–0\.65\]\), leg alignment variability \( ρ = 0\.51 \[0\.36–0\.65\]\), and composite sway \( ρ = 0\.48 \[0\.32–0\.62\]\) were most associated with severity\. Base of support widened monotonically with severity and was the most reliable gait feature \(intraclass correlation coefficient \[ICC\] = 0\.88\)\. Conclusions Pose‐derived digital endpoints from home‐captured SARA home videos show robust, clinically interpretable correlation with severity, supporting scalable remote phenotyping\. Findings motivate longitudinal validation toward clinical and regulatory utility\.

## [Multidimensional spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanisms of soil erosion in a mountainous small watershed: an ST\-TransUNet\-R framework](../publications/b4e337ff8115ac0c65bc.md)

Hui Miao; Hao Zhang; Zhengyang Deng; Ning Hao; Wenzhong Zhu; Jiran Zou

Soil erosion threatens ecological security and water conservation in mountainous small watersheds\. To improve pixel\-level assessment under complex terrain and incomplete multi\-source raster inputs, we developed ST\-TransUNet\-R, a deep\-learning framework that integrates a ResNet\-50 encoder, a Transformer module, a joint\-validity mask, and masked mean squared error loss\. The framework was applied to the Xikouwai Small Watershed upstream of the Miyun Reservoir for five assessment years between 2005 and 2020 and achieved R² = 0\.87, RMSE = 2\.08, MAE = 1\.15, and PBIAS = − 3\.13%\. Multidimensional analysis showed that the 600–900 m elevation band contained 48\.0% of the eroded area, whereas zones above 1100 m produced disproportionately high soil loss per unit area\. Slopes &gt; 35°, vegetation cover &lt; 30%, unused land, and skeletal soils were consistently erosion\-sensitive\. SHAP analysis identified slope as the dominant predictor, followed by slope length and vegetation cover, indicating that terrain\-controlled runoff concentration and surface protection jointly shaped spatial erosion heterogeneity\. These findings provide a high\-resolution basis for prioritizing erosion\-control measures in mountainous water\-source protection areas\.

## [Digital Innovation as an Entry Point for Enhancing Operational Sustainability: The Intermediary Role of Reverse Logistics in a Textile and Knitting Factory in Wasit](../publications/b4e70a63ce165666c1ab.md)

Asst\. Prof\. Azhaar Murad Aujah

The purpose of this study is to investigate the mediating effect of reverse logistics on the connection of digital innovation adoption with operational sustainability\. The study consisted of three primary variables and their sub\-dimensions\. The independent variable \(digital innovation\) was measured in four dimensions: digital infrastructure, application of digital technologies and solutions, digital work environment and digital skills and capabilities\. The mediating variable \(reverse logistics\) had four aspects, namely product acquisition, recycling, reuse and remanufacturing\. The dependent variable \(operational sustainability\) consisted of three dimensions: energy efficiency, sustainable packaging and process automation\. The study topic is the knowledge and application gap on how to use digital technologies and technology solutions to support operational sustainability mechanisms through reverse logistics practices in the studied facility\. The population of the field study was determined from the administrative, supervisory and technical staff of the Wasit Textile and Knitting Factory, which amounted to \(180\)\. The statistically needed sample size of 123 respondents was calculated using Thompson’s technique\. The researcher sent out 140 questionnaires, of which 133 were returned\. After the review, 5 questionnaires were discarded as invalid and the statistical analysis was performed on a total of 128 valid questionnaires, with a response rate of 91\.4%\. The data were analysed and the hypotheses were tested by a descriptive\-analytic technique, using the statistical software SPSS version 26 and AMOS version 24\. Advanced statistical procedures were used, namely: confirmatory factor analysis \(CFA\), normality test, Cronbach’s alpha coefficient, structural equation modelling \(SEM\), path analysis and Sobel’s test to validate the significance of the mediation effect\. The study found that digital innovation plays a substantial and crucial role in improving operational sustainability indirectly through the mediation of reverse logistics\. This mediation raised the explanation power of the structural model to 62 % \. Based on these findings, the study recommended the management of the factory under investigation to incorporate modern digital technologies with recycling and manufacturing practices to recover resources, optimise energy consumption and automate processes to ensure the highest level of operational sustainability\.

## [Suspected atrioesophageal fistula complicated by coronary air embolism after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: direct angiographic visualization and catheter aspiration in a case report](../publications/b4f4be122ca05f80c8eb.md)

Chao Yang; Xiaobin Zeng; Shihai Wang; Chaoju Wang; Jianjun Lan; Yahong Wen; Zaiyong Zheng

Atrioesophageal fistula is a rare but fatal complication of catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation\(AF\)\. It may present with infection, dysphagia or other swallowing\-related symptoms, neurologic events, and systemic air embolism; coronary air embolism is even less common\. Case summary An 84\-year\-old woman was admitted with recurrent palpitations lasting 1 h, approximately 1 month after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation and left atrial appendage closure\(RFCA &amp; LAAC\)\. On admission, she was in sinus rhythm and had a normal cardiac troponin level\. Four hours after admission, she abruptly became unresponsive and developed fever and severe respiratory abnormalities\. Electrocardiography subsequently showed ST\-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF\. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated gas in the mid right coronary artery with TIMI 0 distal flow, and catheter aspiration was performed\. Computed tomography \(CT\) of the head and chest revealed gas at multiple sites, including the intracranial compartment, cardiac chambers, and great vessels\. Blood cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus and other streptococci\. Given the recent left atrial ablation, acute neurologic and myocardial ischemic manifestations, multisite intravascular gas, and bacteremia with organisms associated with the oropharyngeal or gastrointestinal flora, an atrioesophageal fistula complicated by systemic air embolism was strongly suspected\. Her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she developed cardiac arrest and died approximately 27 h after admission\. Conclusion Atrioesophageal fistula and coronary air embolism should be considered in patients who develop fever, impaired consciousness, or acute ST\-segment elevation within several weeks of atrial fibrillation ablation\. Coronary angiography can directly visualize intracoronary gas and allow catheter aspiration; however, the certainty of an atrioesophageal fistula diagnosis should remain commensurate with the available imaging evidence\.

## [A multilingual heterogeneous knowledge graph framework for curriculum–vacancy–MOOC alignment: edge\-weight regression with heterogeneous graph transformers for educational recommendation](../publications/b4f9f1c30fdd2da3e185.md)

Sandugash Serikbayeva; Madina Sambetbayeva; Valiya Ramazanova; Zhanar Lamasheva; Aigerim Yerimbetova; Valentina E\. Makhatova; Zhanna B\. Sadirmekova

Introduction Digitalisation and artificial intelligence have widened the gap between competencies certified by university curricula and skills demanded by employers\. MOOCs could close this gap, but existing recommenders rarely connect what a programme teaches, what the market requires, and what online courses develop within a single semantic structure\. Methods We built a multilingual heterogeneous knowledge graph \(KG\) that integrates university programmes, IT vacancies from hh\.kz, and Coursera MOOCs in English, Russian, and Kazakh\. A property\-graph ontology was formalised and instantiated automatically\. Skills were aligned with a fine\-tuned multilingual Sentence Transformer \(paraphrase\-multilingual\-mpnet\-base\-v2\), and agglomerative clustering formed skill communities\. Recommendation was cast as edge\-weight regression over a competency\-to\-course relation and solved with GraphSAGE, HAN, and HGT encoders\. Results On a held\-out 20% test graph, HGT achieved the best ranking quality \(NDCG@10 = 0\.714; with short meta\-paths NDCG@10 = 0\.987, RMSE = 0\.108\), outperforming GraphSAGE and HAN\. Applied to the “Information Systems” programme of a Kazakhstani university, the system expanded the market\-aligned competency profile by \+36\.2% with five top\-ranked courses and by \+170% with the full catalogue\. Discussion Edge\-weight regression on a cross\-domain heterogeneous KG produces front\-loaded, actionable course recommendations for curriculum alignment\. All datasets, models, graph snapshots, and code are released for reproducibility\.

## [TRANSFORMASI PEMBELAJARAN MELALUI PENDEKATAN DEEP LEARNING DAN QUESTION PROMPT SCAFFOLDING BERBANTUAN AI](../publications/b50fd9ceb9a46932faaf.md)

Adinda Sekar arum Cahyani; Qurrotu Inayatil Maula; Jesika Yulianti; Nadia Putri; Dea Alya Agustina

Elementary/madrasah ibtidaiyah students are generally still accustomed to learning by memorizing facts, so they are less trained in understanding meaning, connecting concepts to real experience, and thinking critically\. This condition runs counter to the spirit of the Merdeka Curriculum, which promotes the implementation of deep learning that is joyful, meaningful, and mindful\. This activity aims to analyze the effectiveness of an AI\-assisted Deep Learning and Question Prompt Scaffolding approach in improving deep understanding, critical thinking skills, and learning engagement among fifth\-grade students at MI An\-Nuriyah, by integrating the context of Madurese local wisdom\. The activity was carried out through a participatory mentoring approach using a descriptive qualitative design\. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using an interactive model comprising data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, with data validity obtained through source and method triangulation\. The results show that students&\#x27; initial understanding was still superficial and they were not yet accustomed to reflective thinking\. After being introduced to a graded series of AI\-assisted question prompts, students showed a livelier learning process, especially when questions were connected to Madurese local wisdom they were familiar with, which increased their confidence and courage to ask questions\. Obstacles found included some students&\#x27; difficulty answering analysis\- and reflection\-level questions, as well as limited access to devices and the internet at home\. This activity concludes that a practice\-based approach using AI\-assisted graded questioning is more effective in building meaningful understanding than one\-way explanation, although its success depends on consistent teacher mentoring and sustained, adequate technological support\.

## [Carboni, David: Barthes&\#x27;s Punctum as Anti\-Bliss Epiphany: Toward an Ontology of Photographic Wounding](../publications/b52c009fc2bb7b725147.md)



Roland Barthes&\#x27;s concept of punctum—the photographic detail that &quot;pierces&quot; the viewer—remains one of aesthetics&\#x27; most influential yet under\-theorized concepts\. While Barthes provides a rich phenomenology of the wounding experience, he cannot explain why punctum must be unintended, why it always returns to mortality, or what distinguishes piercing recognition from subjective projection\. This paper argues that punctum is best understood as a specific instantiation of anti\-bliss epiphany, a structure in which trauma\-prepared consciousness recognizes patterns of emergence and dissolution compressed into legible signals\. The personal thread of connection—trauma\-calibrated receptivity—transduces universal fractal patterns into lived experience, producing the wound Barthes documents\. Photography&\#x27;s indexical structure, temporal dislocation, and detail\-excess create optimal conditions for this recognition, but the wounding mechanism extends beyond photography to any medium achieving sufficient pattern\-fidelity\. This framework not only resolves Barthes&\#x27;s enduring puzzles but also opens new avenues for inquiry into visual ethics, the phenomenology of loss, and the structure of aesthetic experience itself\. Keywords: Barthes, punctum, pre\-grief, photography, phenomenology, mortality, pattern recognition, anti\-bliss epiphany, syntactic care

## [Sentence\-Level Topic Modeling with Lexical and Contextual Evidence](../publications/b52db1655fdb8045e05a.md)

Federica Granese; Serena Villata; Charles Bouveyron

Topic modeling faces a fundamental granularity dilemma: probabilistic topic models assign topics at the word level, whereas transformer\-based methods operate at the document level\. The latter overlooks that real\-world documents typically cover multiple topics, whereas the former relies on individual words, which rarely provide sufficient context to identify them\. We introduce SentenceETM, a neural topic model that assigns a topic to each sentence by jointly using lexical and contextual evidence\. Each topic is described both by a distribution over the vocabulary, defined through word embeddings, and by a Gaussian over sentence embeddings concentrated on a topic\-specific low\-dimensional subspace\. The topic of a sentence generates both its words and its embedding and is marginalized exactly, so that its posterior combines the two sources of evidence\. Document proportions are inferred with amortized variational inference, while the Gaussian parameters are re\-estimated in closed form\. Experiments show that SentenceETM consistently improves sentence\-level topic assignment over state\-of\-the\-art approaches, and a case study of a presidential debate shows how sentence\-level topics reveal how candidates handle the same subjects\.

## [Multimodal Evidence\-Based License Compliance Verification for KOGL Open Government Works on the Web](../publications/b530d8957b1303978965.md)

Seyoung Jang; Byeongchan Park; Youngmo Kim; Sun\-jib Kim

The reuse of open government works on the web has increased rapidly with the expansion of public data policies and artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-assisted content utilization\. In Korea, Korea Open Government Licenses \(KOGLs\) permit the reuse of public works under conditions such as attribution, non\-commercial use, and no\-derivatives\. However, these conditions are frequently violated or misunderstood in web pages, advertisements, social media posts, and reused digital content\. Since compliance\-related evidence is distributed across textual descriptions, captions, license metadata, embedded image text, visual changes, and page\-level context, manual inspection, and single\-modal analysis are not sufficient for scalable web\-based compliance review\. This paper proposes a multimodal evidence\-based method for KOGL license compliance risk prediction in web environments\. The proposed method combines textual context, KOGL metadata, optical character recognition \(OCR\) extracted image text, and visual features to classify four risk types: attribution risk, non\-commercial use risk, no\-derivatives risk, and false KOGL claim risk\. A lightweight sequential context model captures the contextual flow of compliance\-related cues, while the decision module produces both risk probabilities and evidence\-based explanations\. Experiments on a KOGL\-oriented dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy, macro\-F1, and area under the curve \(AUC\) than text\-only, image\-only, and simple fusion baselines\. The results demonstrate that multimodal web evidence improves compliance risk prediction and provides practical support for human review in public content management, open government data curation, and AI training data inspection\.

## [Immunohistochemical and morphometric assessment of carotid body remodeling under conditions of chronic hypoxia and hypertension](../publications/b53249a3fd766a6d5aa8.md)

Elena Sergeevna Ganina; Julia Grigoryeva; V\.N\. Sevryukova; Galina Nikolaevna Suvorova; Alexander V\. Bormotov; Ваньков Владимир Александрович

The comorbidity of arterial hypertension and hemodynamically significant carotid artery stenosis presents a serious clinical challenge\. The carotid body is a peripheral chemoreceptor that plays an important role in blood pressure regulation, but its structural changes in this comorbid condition remain poorly understood\. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in the histoarchitecture of the carotid body in patients with the combined pathology of arterial hypertension and hemodynamically significant common carotid artery stenosis using the morphometric and immunohistochemical markers PGR9\.5 and S\-100\. Research methodology: Ten carotid body preparations from healthy controls and ten preparations from patients with verified hypertension and hemodynamically significant common carotid artery stenosis were studied\. Immunohistochemical staining with PGR9\.5 and S\-100 markers was used, followed by morphometric analysis in ImageJ\. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Shapiro\-Wilk, Mann\-Whitney, and Student&\#x27;s t\-tests, as well as Spearman&\#x27;s correlation analysis\. The results of the research: In the group with hypertension and hemodynamically significant stenosis, a significant reduction in the number of supporting cells was observed\. Against this background, compensatory hypertrophy of chief cells was observed, manifested by an increase in their overall area, nucleus, and nuclear\-cytoplasmic ratio\. Correlation analysis in the comorbid group demonstrated the disappearance of significant correlations for PGR9\.5 and S\-100 previously observed in the control group, as well as the emergence of new pathological associations, indicating a profound disruption of tissue regulation\. Conclusions: The obtained data suggest a new pathophysiological mechanism for carotid body dysfunction in hypertension and common carotid artery stenosis, based on the disconnection of functional elements within the organ&\#x27;s parenchyma\. Disruption of cooperation between cell populations creates the basis for persistent chemoreceptor hyperactivation, which contributes to elevated blood pressure and the progression of hypertension\.

## [Metropolis\-scale resilient and trustworthy traffic flow inference using multi\-source data](../publications/b5347540d4e4b6f37a9d.md)

Qishen Zhou; Yifan Zhang; Michail Makridis; Anastasios Kouvelas; Yibing Wang; Simon Hu

Inferring network\-wide traffic states from sparse observations with high accuracy and trustworthy uncertainty quantification is essential for intelligent transportation systems, yet it remains challenging due to the underdetermined nature of the problem, multifaceted disturbances in sensing networks, and the inherent conflicts among multiple inference subtasks when modeled jointly\. We propose the Task\-Aware Attentive Neural Process \(TA\-ANP\), a unified probabilistic framework for resilient and trustworthy global traffic state inference \(GTSI\) by fusing floating car data \(FCD\) with sparse fixed\-detector measurements\. By casting GTSI as a stochastic process, TA\-ANP leverages the meta\-learning properties of neural processes to adapt rapidly to changes in sensing configurations without retraining\. A task\-aware multi\-query attention module with distinct spatiotemporal inductive biases is introduced to jointly handle three GTSI subtasks—real\-time estimation at unobserved locations, forecasting at both observed and unobserved locations—while mitigating cross\-task interference\. For uncertainty quantification, we combine neural processes with Monte Carlo Dropout to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty\. To support metropolis\-scale evaluation, we construct the Metropolitan Multi\-Source Traffic Dataset \(MMTD\), integrating fixed\-loop sensor measurements, FCD statistics, and OpenStreetMap road\-network data over an urban network of 26,166 road segments, including 2371 fixed\-sensor\-equipped segments used for quantitative evaluation\. Experiments across multiple independently generated sensor configurations show that TA\-ANP achieves best performance across all subtasks under deterministic and probabilistic metrics\. The resulting well\-calibrated uncertainties enable more efficient fixed\-sensor placement with fewer sensor deployments\. Under a Damage–Repair–Addition sensing lifecycle, TA\-ANP demonstrates superior resilience in terms of disturbance absorption, performance recovery, and adaptability to unseen sensing configurations\.The code and processed datasets are publicly available on GitHub and Zenodo , respectively\.

## [A Corpus based Comparison of Human and Machine News Translation Styles](../publications/b53901006183eb635cfc.md)

Yidong Ju

This study compares the styles of news translations produced by human translators, neural machine translation system, and large language model\. Using a corpus\-based approach, it examines lexical, syntactic, and discourse features across the three sets of translations\. Type–token ratios, mean word length, mean sentence length, and readability scores reveal no clear stylistic differences\. The findings suggest that advances in machine translation have made human and machine translations difficult to distinguish on stylistic grounds in this news corpus\.

## [Acute viral encephalitis syndrome in paediatric patients: Clinical profile and laboratory correlation](../publications/b53f6f59992a1356dd7f.md)

Deepika Shivakumar Pujari; Sudhindrashayana Raghunanadan Fattepur; Keerthidarshini Khanappanavar; Vinod Hanumant Ratageri

Objectives: Acute encephalitis syndrome \(AES\) poses a significant public health challenge in India, particularly in children\. The aetiological spectrum varies regionally, with viral agents being predominant\. This study evaluates the clinico\-virological profile of AES in children at a tertiary care centre in North Karnataka\. Material and Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted among children aged 6 months to 12 years presenting with AES, defined as acute fever with altered sensorium and/or seizures\. Detailed clinical evaluation, neuroimaging and laboratory investigations were performed\. Immunoglobulin M enzyme\-linked immunosorbent assay testing for herpes simplex virus type \(HSV\)\-1, HSV\-2, mumps, dengue, chikungunya and Japanese encephalitis \(JE\) virus was used to determine viral aetiology\. Outcomes were assessed at discharge\. Results: Among 41 children, 58\.5% were male and most were from low socioeconomic backgrounds\. Fever and altered sensorium were present in all cases; seizures occurred in 68\.3%\. Mumps \(22%\), HSV\-1/2 \(17%\), dengue \(14\.6%\) and JE \(4\.9%\) were the major viral causes identified, while no aetiology could be determined in 51\.2% of cases\. Neuroimaging was abnormal in 34\.2%, and hypoxia, low Glasgow Coma Scale and need for ventilation were associated with poorer outcomes\. The mortality rate was 17%\. Conclusion: A substantial proportion of AES cases remained aetiologically undiagnosed, underscoring the limitations of current diagnostic tools\. Regional epidemiological data and enhanced viral testing are essential for developing targeted public health strategies, improving early detection and preventing long\-term morbidity and mortality among affected children\.

## [Bongo Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature\-inspired Metaheuristic Approach for Efficient Optimization](../publications/b54592de2fe3355fb34f.md)

Zeinab Montazeri; Mohammad Dehghani; Raed Abu Zitar; Omar Almomani; Kei Eguchi

Metaheuristic algorithms have attracted much attention in recent years due to their ability to solve complex optimization problems\.However, striking a good balance between exploration and exploitation remains a major challenge in designing these algorithms\.In this paper, a new algorithm, the Bongo Optimization Algorithm \(BOA\), is introduced, which is inspired by the natural behavior of Bongo in searching for food resources and selecting highquality resources\.In BOA, the behavior of Bongo&\#x27;s extensive movement in the habitat to explore different areas is used as the basis for designing the exploration phase, while the behavior of selective browsing of high\-quality food is used to focus on promising areas and improve existing solutions, which forms the basis for the exploitation phase\.This structure allows for an effective balance between global search and local refinement\.In order to evaluate the performance of BOA, a set of 23 standard benchmark functions including unimodal test functions \(F1\-F7\), highdimensional multimodal test functions \(F8\-F13\), and fixed\-dimensional multimodal test functions \(F14\-F23\) has been investigated\.The performance of BOA has been compared with 9 well\-known metaheuristic algorithms and the statistical measures of mean, standard deviation \(std\), and rank have been used to analyze the results\.In addition, the search behavior of BOA has been investigated through visual analysis, convergence curve, population diversity, exploration, and exploitation percentage\.The simulation results show that BOA has obtained the first\-best optimizer rank in all 23 benchmark functions F1\-F23 and has provided 100% successful and competitive performance compared to the investigated algorithms\.Also, the analyses have confirmed the ability of BOA to maintain appropriate diversity in the early stages and increase exploitation in the final stages of optimization\.The findings of this study show that BOA has been introduced as a powerful metaheuristic optimizer with high power in balancing exploration and exploitation and has the potential to be used in a wide range of optimization problems in science and real\-world applications\.Future studies can focus on developing multi\-objective, binary versions and applying BOA to complex engineering problems\.

## [Directing Neuronal Differentiation via Calcium‐Chirality Synergy in Supramolecular Nanofibers](../publications/b54c8b9bf2bbae410ce2.md)

Shuhan He; Xin Wang; Si Li; Hengwei Lin; Jianping Yang

ABSTRACT While chiral supramolecular nanofibrous networks \(NFNs\) show promise in regulating cell fate, precisely directing differentiation pathways remains challenging\. This study systematically investigates the influence of various chiral supramolecular NFNs on neural cell differentiation\. A series of chiral supramolecular NFNs was synthesized using L/D‐amino acids and their derivatives as building blocks, including L/D‐lysine \(L/D‐Lys\), L/D‐histidine \(L/D‐His\), L/D‐arginine \(L/D‐Arg\), and L/D‐glutamic acid derivatives \(Fmoc‐L/D‐Glu\)\. The regulatory effects of these NFNs on the NG108‐15 were evaluated during the differentiation process\. Our findings demonstrate that the chiral microenvironment established by D‐Lys‐gel significantly enhances NG108‐15 differentiation and correlates with robust activation of the Ca 2\+ signaling pathway\. To further elucidate the relationship between supramolecular chirality and metal ions, we synthesized chiral supramolecular NFNs from L/D‐Lys‐Ca 2\+ ‐gel and L/D‐Lys‐Mg 2\+ ‐gel\. Notably, the supramolecular NFNs derived from D‐Lys‐Ca 2\+ ‐gel exhibited superior capacity to promote neurite outgrowth and maturation compared to their L‐enantiomer and Mg 2\+ ‐incorporated counterparts\. Proteomics analysis revealed that the chiral supramolecular NFNs obtained from D‐Lys‐Ca 2\+ ‐gel enhance neuronal differentiation by upregulating key effectors involved in both axon guidance and calcium signaling pathways, particularly the Camkk2‐Tiam1 cascade\. This study provides valuable insights into the design of chiral biomaterials and proposes novel strategies for neural regeneration and tissue engineering\.
