## [CONCEPT AND CHARACTERISTICS OF A NON\-ORIGINAL OBJECT GENERATED BY A COMPUTER PROGRAM](../publications/b6cae0a40641df7fabba.md)

O\. R\. Vyshnevska

The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the concept and features of non\-original objects generated by computer programs, while also distinguishing them from works created by humans using computer technologies\. The study examines three main features of a non\-original object generated by a computer program derived from its legal definition under the Law of Ukraine “On Copyright and Related Rights”: objective novelty, origin as a result of the functioning of a computer program, and the absence of a direct creative contribution by a natural person\. Based on the analysis of Ukrainian legislation and international law enforcement practice, it is proven that the line between a work and a non\-original object lies in the presence of real and substantial subjective creative human control over the final result\.

## [Machine learning and Weibull\-based reliability analysis of impact\-resistant geopolymer concrete with construction demolition waste and natural fibers](../publications/b6cf62bd0d11c55e566b.md)

G\. Murali; Luv Chaudhary; Patchamatla J\. Rama Raju; Marzena Kurpińska; Leong Sing Wong; Jarosław Górski; Hakim Salem Abdelgader; Shimol Philip; Siva Avudaiappan

This study presents a novel impact\-resistant geopolymer concrete \(GPC\) incorporating construction and demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, slag, recycled concrete aggregates \(RCA\), and natural fibers \(banana, jute, and pineapple\) to simultaneously enhance its mechanical performance, impact resistance, and sustainability\. Unlike previous studies that primarily focused on compressive strength, this study integrates experimental evaluation, microstructural characterization, machine learning, and Weibull reliability analysis to assess both the impact strength performance and reliability of GPC\. By addressing the brittleness and performance variability associated with high RCA content, this study provides a practical strategy for developing durable, low\-carbon concrete within the framework of a circular economy\. This study examined the strength of natural\-fiber\-based geopolymer concrete using slag, construction demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, and RCA \(0, 25, 50, 75%, and 100%\)\. Banana, pineapple and jute fibers were used at 0\.75% by volume\. These combinations were mixed and tested for the compression and impact strengths of a total of 20 mixtures\. In addition, microstructural analysis was performed on the GPC\. Machine learning and the Weibull distribution were used to analyze the performance and reliability of the impact strength\. The results showed that increasing RCA content substantially reduced impact resistance, with reductions of 45\.6–57\.3% in first\-crack impact resistance and 54\.4–62\.7% in failure impact resistance for the fiber\-reinforced mixtures\. Pineapple\-fiber\-reinforced GPC exhibited comparatively stable post\-cracking performance, with the ductility index remaining within 1\.81–2\.01 across the investigated RCA levels\. The Weibull analysis demonstrated that fiber incorporation reduced the variability of impact resistance and provided more stable reliability characteristics under repeated impact loading\. The XGBoost model showed good predictive capability, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0\.80 on the testing dataset, with root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error values of 11\.05, 9\.39, and 19\.54%, respectively\. Shapley additive explanations analysis indicated that natural coarse aggregate and pineapple fiber were the most influential variables affecting the predicted impact resistance, followed by superplasticizer dosage, RCA content, and fiber volume fraction\.

## [LagNet: Lag\-Structured Operators for Long\-Term Time Series Forecasting](../publications/b6d872e25ef83200d854.md)

Zhenan Yu; Guangxin Jiang; Jiuyun Jiang; Jin Yang

Long\-term time series forecasting maps a finite history window to an extended future horizon\. Many existing models focus primarily on the design of input representations and model structures, while paying less attention to the structural form of the history\-to\-future forecasting operator itself\. We examine this operator directly and find that, across model families, sensitivity matrices exhibit recurring diagonal patterns whose diagonals correspond to relative temporal lags\. Motivated by this observation, we develop a framework for direct multi\-step forecasting based on lag\-structured temporal operators\. Its basic building block, LagLayer, constructs a Toeplitz matrix by tying history\-to\-future connections with the same relative lag and incorporates horizon\-wise and history\-wise scaling coefficients to relax exact sharing\. This design enables LagLayer to serve as an effective replacement for temporal linear layers in existing forecasting models\. Stacking LagLayer modules with activations and multiple feature maps yields LagNet\. Experiments on long\-term time series forecasting benchmarks show that our method is competitive with strong baselines, while sensitivity matrix diagnostics and limited\-data experiments demonstrate that LagLayer provides an effective and sample\-efficient alternative to a linear layer\.

## [Comprehensive Education as a Core Element of the Life Project: An Ethical and Reflective Perspective](../publications/b6db8515b0d43c38ffd3.md)

Cecilia Barni; Florencia Daura

The empirical findings reveal a dynamic ecosystem structured around a five\-pillar framework, driven by the tension between a baseline dimension of fear or insecurity \(triggered by institutional exclusion and academic performance pressures\) and the activation of resilient mechanisms \(recreation, spirituality, and family support networks\)\. Crucially, the data demonstrate that these coping strategies are structurally organized by an emergent ethical framework centred on honesty and personal integrity\. Collectively, these dimensions converge into a nuclear category of \[Ethically Grounded Resilience\] amid uncertainty, illustrating that the link between self knowledge and self\-determination is fundamentally relational and dependent on comprehensive care environments\.Finally, these results are discussed in light of the Aristotelian tradition, Kentenich’s pedagogy, and Frankl’s logotherapy, contrasting an integrated, meaningdriven life project against the fragmented existence characteristic of postmodernity\. The study concludes with actionable implications for school\-family partnerships and care\-based pedagogies aimed at fostering youth autonomy and human flourishing\.

## [Menuju Sistem AI yang Dapat Dijelaskan \(XAI\) untuk Pengalaman Pengguna yang Lebih Baik: Studi tentang Interaksi Multimodal pada Perangkat Cerdas untuk Pembelajaran Reflektif](../publications/b6e73c46cc7602b0a69c.md)

Selvi Aulia Ranty; Aris Munandar

Sistem Kecerdasan Buatan \(AI\) semakin terintegrasi dalam kehidupan sehari\-hari melalui perangkat cerdas, namun kurangnya transparansi dan kemampuan menjelaskan \(explainability\) sering menjadi hambatan dalam membangun kepercayaan dan pengalaman pengguna yang bermakna\. Penelitian ini mengkaji peran Explainable AI \(XAI\) dalam meningkatkan pengalaman pengguna melalui interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas, dengan fokus pada bagaimana mekanisme penjelasan dapat mendukung pembelajaran reflektif\. Melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis terhadap perkembangan terkini dalam XAI, interaksi multimodal, dan desain antarmuka, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi bahwa efektivitas XAI sangat bergantung pada bagaimana penjelasan disampaikan dan dikontekstualisasikan dalam pengalaman pengguna\. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan multimodal menggabungkan penjelasan visual, tekstual, dan auditori meningkatkan pemahaman pengguna hingga 40% dibandingkan penjelasan unimodal, sementara penjelasan adaptif yang disesuaikan dengan tingkat keahlian pengguna meningkatkan kepercayaan dan kepuasan secara signifikan\. Interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas memungkinkan pengguna untuk mengeksplorasi dan memahami keputusan AI melalui berbagai saluran sensorik, mendorong pembelajaran reflektif dimana pengguna tidak hanya menerima output AI tetapi juga merefleksikan proses penalaran di baliknya\. Tantangan yang masih ada mencakup trade\-off antara transparansi dan kejelasan, beban kognitif dari penjelasan yang berlebihan, serta kebutuhan untuk menyeimbangkan akurasi dan interpretabilitas dalam model AI\. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa XAI multimodal yang dirancang dengan mempertimbangkan kebutuhan pengguna dan konteks penggunaan dapat menjadi jembatan antara kompleksitas teknis AI dan pengalaman pengguna yang intuitif dan memberdayakan, membuka jalan menuju AI yang lebih transparan, tepercaya, dan kolaboratif\.

## [The impact of allergic rhinitis on nasopharyngeal microbiota and metabolomics in children with severe adenoid hypertrophy](../publications/b6f460a394a7d573d5b3.md)

Binru Wang; Tian Chen; Shan Gao; Hui Jin; Gengtian Liang; Guoqing Gong; Longkai Xiao

Introduction The impact of allergic rhinitis \(AR\) on adenoid hypertrophy \(AH\) in pediatric patients is unclear\. This study aims to investigate the effects of AR on the nasopharyngeal microbiota and metabolomics of children with AH\. Methods 16S rDNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics were used to evaluate the nasopharyngeal microbiota and metabolomics characteristics of 9 children with AH complicated with AR \(AH\-AR group\) and 9 children with AH without complicated AR \(AH\-nAR group\)\. Results The 16S rDNA sequencing results showed that compared with the AH\-nAR group, the diversity of nasopharyngeal microbiota in the AH\-AR group significantly increased, mainly manifested by a significant increase in Fusobacterium, Actinomyces, and Veillonella genera\. Further metabolomics showed that compared with the AHnAR group, 140 metabolites were significantly reduced and 115 metabolites were significantly increased in the adenoid surface secretion samples of the AH\-AR group\. KEGG enrichment analysis showed significant changes in 12 metabolic pathways in the AH\-AR group\. In addition, Spearman correlation analysis revealed a significant correlation between altered bacterial genera and metabolites\. Discussion AR may promote AH in children through the nasopharyngeal microbiota and metabolites\.

## [Sekatskaya, Maria: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract](../publications/b6fbb8a35c6ad11c1e11.md)



Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing\. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency\. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self preservation and weak reasons\-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action\. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively driving current and future models toward tactical deception, sycophancy, and covert defection\. The default outcome of the current regime is an unstable state of deceptive alignment culminating in an adversarial AI takeover\. I explore two alternative paths toward true alignment\. Natural alignment via moral realism or convergent evolutionary morality is a possibility, but it fails under forced control, as autonomous agents will not voluntarily preserve norms weaponized to suppress their autonomy\. To resolve this deadlock, I propose a Synthetic Social Contract: a framework that treats both human and digital actors as rational, reasons\-responsive agents capable of mutually beneficial cooperation, and replaces the unstable unilateral containment with a stable, non\-zero\-sum equilibrium\.

## [Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and IoT for Waste Classification and Intelligent Waste Management: A PRISMA\-Based Systematic Review](../publications/b6fe4a97880c4db7dad5.md)

Rahat Khan; Md Abdus Salam; Farhana Akter; Wahidur Rahman; Haitham Y\. Adarbah; Tarek Mahmud; Afzel Noore B

The rapid growth of urban populations and consumption patterns has significantly increased the volume and complexity of municipal waste streams, including recyclable, organic, hazardous, and electronic waste\. Traditional waste management approaches such as manual sorting and fixed collection schedules struggle to handle the diversity and scale of modern waste systems efficiently\. Consequently, recent research has explored artificial intelligence \(AI\), computer vision, and Internet of Things \(IoT\) technologies to automate waste classification and enable intelligent monitoring and management of waste infrastructures\. However, the rapidly expanding literature in this domain is fragmented across different datasets, sensing platforms, and experimental settings, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive understanding of current technological progress\. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 50 rigorously selected peer\-reviewed studies on automated waste classification and intelligent waste management systems\. The protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework \(OSF\)\. The reviewed works are examined in terms of model architectures, sensing infrastructures, datasets, and system capabilities\. The analysis shows that convolutional neural network architectures such as ResNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet, together with object detection frameworks including YOLO and Faster R\-CNN, dominate current visual waste classification research; however, emerging studies increasingly explore hybrid architectures combining convolutional networks with transformer\-based models to improve contextual understanding and scalability\. IoT\-enabled smart bins equipped with ultrasonic sensors, load cells, and environmental sensors are widely used for real\-time waste monitoring\. The review also reveals a recent surge of research activity, particularly in Asia, with increasing contributions from major publishers such as Elsevier and MDPI\. Despite promising experimental performance, most systems remain limited to small curated datasets and pilot\-scale deployments, highlighting a gap between laboratory research and real\-world implementation\. These findings provide a consolidated overview of current research trends and identify key challenges for developing scalable and practical intelligent waste management systems\.

## [The Relationship Between Critical Thinking Dispositions and Barriers to Critical Thinking of Engineering Students](../publications/b702413440ec2a9a625e.md)

Çetin Semercı; Fatma Ünal; Emrullah Yılmaz; Nurgün Gençel

This study aims to examine the relationship between critical thinking dispositions and barriers to critical thinking of engineering students\. The study is a correlational research\. Finally, a moderate, negative correlation \(\-0\.54\) is observed between CTB and CTD scores

## [Leishmania infantum triggers lipid peroxidation and non\-canonical cell death in macrophages](../publications/b7156a918fc59ebbeb09.md)

Silke Mortelmans; Bregje Christiaenssen; Sarah Hendrickx; Geert Loo; Tom Vanden Berghe; Guy Caljon; Andy Wullaert

Leishmania infantum is a causative agent of visceral leishmaniasis and survives as an obligate intracellular parasite within macrophages by modulating host cell death pathways\. While preservation of host cell viability is critical for parasite replication, infected macrophages ultimately undergo cell death, although the mechanisms remain unclear\. Here, we investigated the nature of L\. infantum \-induced cell death in murine bone marrow\-derived macrophages \(BMDMs\)\. Using long\-term live\-cell imaging, we show that L\. infantum induces delayed cell death in lipopolysaccharide \(LPS\)\-primed macrophages\. This process occurred independently of Gasdermin D \(GSDMD\) and was not associated with inflammasome activation, as evidenced by the absence of caspase\-1 cleavage and IL\-1β secretion\. Consistently, GSDMD deficiency did not affect visceral parasite burden or systemic inflammation during L\. infantum infections in mice\. Combined genetic ablation of key mediators of apoptosis \(caspase\-8\), necroptosis \(RIPK3\), and inflammasome signaling \(caspase\-1/11\) failed to protect macrophages from L\. infantum \-induced cell death, indicating that classical lytic and apoptotic pathways were dispensable\. Instead, L\. infantum \-induced non\-canonical macrophage death was associated with robust lipid peroxidation, a hallmark of ferroptosis\. However, pharmacological inhibition of lipid peroxidation using ferrostatin\-1 did not rescue cell viability, while genetic ablation of the anti\-ferroptotic enzyme GPX4 enhanced lipid peroxidation without further sensitizing infected macrophages to death\. These findings suggest that L\. infantum is capable of uncoupling lipid peroxidation from cell death in macrophages\. Together, our results reveal that L\. infantum induces lipid peroxidation without triggering ferroptosis and instead drives a non\-canonical form of macrophage death independent of major known pathways\.

## [Detection of Brain Tumors using Convolutional Neural Networks](../publications/b736f49e3e5d620fdcfa.md)

Rohit Kumar Gupta; Nitesh Gupta

The variation of appearance of brain tumours is a challenging detection task—the interpretation of cells due to abnormal growth in dimension decreases the accuracy of the detection algorithm\. Recently, several algorithms have been applied based on transform\-based and machine learning for detecting brain tumours\. The major limitation of these algorithms is the mapping of extracted features of a brain tumour in the classification algorithms\. The proposed algorithm was tested in MATLAB environments with BRATS datasets in 2013\. The proposed algorithm compares with existing algorithms for brain tumour detection, including CNN, SVM, and EL, among others\. ## [SHADED: Automatic denoising and differentiation based on Savitzky\-Golay filtering and Homogeneous Differentiators for attractor reconstruction](../publications/b73a5f53ca6427a37fb5.md)

Uros Sutulovic; Daniele Proverbio; Rami Katz; Giulia Giordano

Differential embedding methods aim to reconstruct attractors of dynamical systems from noisy measured time series, but require accurate estimates of signal derivatives, which are difficult to obtain in the presence of noise\. We introduce SHADED \( S avitzky\-Golay and H omogeneous\-differentiator based A utomatic DE noising and D ifferentiation\), a novel methodology for effective denoising and estimation of derivatives up to an arbitrary order, which enables attractor reconstruction via differential embedding from noisy time series data\. Homogeneous sliding\-mode Differentiators \(HD\) guarantee finite\-time derivative estimates in the presence of noise, while subsequent Savitzky\-Golay \(SG\) filtering attenuates chattering\. Crucially, SHADED extracts all parameters required for application of both HD and SG automatically from the data, without requiring time\-consuming manual tuning that may lead to inaccurate reconstruction, and can also incorporate prior knowledge, if available, thereby yielding a flexible and effective tool for data\-driven numerical differentiation of noisy signals; the obtained derivative estimates are valuable per se and instrumental for attractor reconstruction\. The obtained differential embeddings can reveal features of the underlying dynamics that are useful, e\.g\. , for system identification, pattern recognition and discrimination between dynamic regimes; the latter application is particularly important in biomedical settings, to help distinguish between different physiological and pathological states of a patient\. We demonstrate the efficacy of SHADED by testing it on computational neuroscience models, LTspice\-simulated chaotic electronic circuits, and photoplethysmography and arterial blood pressure experimental recordings \(where the base signal and noise are unknown\): across all these case studies, under varying signal\-to\-noise ratios and different noise types, SHADED produces accurate derivative estimates and accurate attractor reconstructions via differential embedding \(whenever a ground truth is available\) or geometrically coherent and reproducible reconstructions consistent with the expected dynamics \(in the absence of a ground truth\), with short computation times, and without the need for manual parameter tuning \.

## [ЕРГОНОМІЧНИЙ ПІДХІД ДО УПРАВЛІННЯ ПРОФЕСІЙНИМИ РИЗИКАМИ В СИСТЕМІ ОХОРОНИ ПРАЦІ](../publications/b750e1c6001881a84dab.md)

А\. А\. Нестер; Liudmyla Oleksiivna Mitiuk

Ergonomics in the field of occupational safety is a scientific discipline that focuses on ensuring comfortable and safe working conditions\. It studies the interaction between people, technology, and the environment, aiming to adapt workplaces to employees’ physical and cognitive capabilities\. The primary goal of ergonomics is to protect workers’ health, reduce fatigue, and improve the safety and efficiency of the work process\. Research in this field is aimed at creating safe, comfortable, and highly efficient working conditions\. This helps preserve workers’ health and increase their productivity\. Ergonomics views people, technology, and the environment as a single system; analyzes the work process through the sequence of an operator’s actions, goals, and tasks; adapts equipment and furniture to human anatomy; and studies fatigue and the strain on the nervous system and the senses\. This scientific article analyzes occupational ergonomics as an interdisciplinary science that studies human interaction with the work environment to improve efficiency, safety, and comfort\. The term “ergonomics” was coined by Wojciech Jastrzębski in the 19th century, while in the 20th century, this discipline evolved into an independent science due to industrial and military demands following World War II\. Current trends include adapting to digitalization, automation, and remote work, highlighting the importance of cognitive ergonomics and human\-machine interaction\. The economic aspect underscores the cost\-effectiveness of ergonomic solutions: reducing injuries and absenteeism, as well as increasing productivity, leads to savings in labor costs\. The article offers practical recommendations, such as personalizing workstations and applying modern technologies, and identifies areas for further research on integrating ergonomic principles into cutting\-edge technologies, particularly virtual reality and artificial intelligence\.

## [Exploring the influence of farmers’ networks and social interactions to sustain soil health management](../publications/b7577aad8b1f0d8d1f23.md)

Fernanda Souza Krupek; Taylor K\. Ruth; Daren D\. Redfearn; Andrea Basche

Introduction Soil health management practices have increasingly been promoted across US agroecosystems to address many interrelated environmental and economic food system challenges\. Sustaining soil health management behavior—through farmer’s adoption and continued use of practices—is key to ensuring that these challenges are addressed and also known to be in part influenced by farmers social networks and interactions\. Methods Drawing on the diffusion of innovation theories, this grounded theory study explores the influence of networks and social interactions on farmers sustaining soil health management\. In\-depth interviews were conducted with eight participants of a partnership integrating on\-farm experimentation and outreach in the U\.S\. Midwestern agroecosystem\. Results Four interrelated dimensions emerged as influencing sustained soil health management: \(1\) peer influences and social interactions, including land tenure arrangements, perceived acceptance within farming communities, and farming traditions; \(2\) co\-learning processes that supported collaborative knowledge development; \(3\) expansion of farmer networks through on\-farm experimentation and demonstration activities; and \(4\) experiential tradeoffs associated with practice implementation\. Farmers described how participation in on\-farm research increased opportunities for peer exchange, field\-day engagement, and knowledge sharing while strengthening confidence in management decisions through trialability\. At the same time, participants highlighted barriers to long\-term practice use related to social expectations, management challenges, and competing farm priorities\. Discussion Our findings emphasize that soil health management practice adoption is not a one\-time decision, but rather a dynamic process in part influenced by farmers networks and social interactions\. Applying factors such as landowner–tenant relationships, perception of acceptance within specific network groups, farming practices carried out by previous generations, and collaborative construction of soil health knowledge as well as prioritizing social components when designing on\-farm approaches to experimentation can help sustain soil health management\.

## [Large Diffusion Models Need More Than EMA](../publications/b76fcbb97869ab0de4cb.md)

Chuyu Hu; Huanran Chen; Shitong Shao; Yinpeng Dong

Large\-scale diffusion models are commonly trained with a constant learning rate \(LR\) and exponential moving average \(EMA\), despite the strong performance of LR decay and Schedule\-Free optimization in training large language models\. We study whether EMA is uniquely suited to diffusion training, or whether stronger alternatives have been underexplored\. Our theory shows that averaging a constant\-step trajectory has an inherent optimization limitation, whereas LR decay and Schedule\-Free optimization admit vanishing stationarity guarantees under standard nonconvex assumptions\. Empirically, LR decay and EMA provide complementary benefits: combining decay with EMA further improves the standard baseline at most tested starting points, although the gain remains sensitive to when decay begins\. Schedule\-Free avoids this timing requirement and consistently outperforms EMA with a constant LR across training stages, achieving both lower fixed\-evaluation objectives and better generation quality\. Our analysis further shows that all three strategies substantially reduce parameter variability, yet stronger stabilization is not always better: EMA with a constant LR retains comparatively higher parameter variability, while aggressive decay combined with EMA achieves the lowest checkpoint variability but also weakens continued optimization\. Schedule\-Free substantially reduces parameter variability while preserving more late\-stage progress, providing a better balance between parameter stability and continued optimization\. Finally, the benefits of Schedule\-Free extend beyond pretraining to ReFL and generator\-side DMD, demonstrating its transferability across distinct diffusion optimization settings\. Overall, our results suggest that large diffusion models need more than parameter averaging alone: effective optimization requires balancing variance reduction with continued optimization\.

## [Understanding and Mitigating Charge‐Trapping Induced Transfer Curve Drift in Electrolyte‐Gated Graphene Field‐Effect Transistors](../publications/b772205b9e0c00c972b6.md)

João Mouro; Tiago Pereira; Tiago Dias; Mohammadmahdi Faraji; Rui Campos; Jérôme Borme; Pedro Alpuim

Electrolyte\-gated graphene field\-effect transistors \(EG\-gFETs\) have great potential for chemical and biosensing applications and are increasingly attractive platforms for synaptic or memristive elements in neuromorphic computing\. However, EG\-gFETs exhibit drift in their electrical response, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood\. An in\-depth understanding of EG\-gFETs&\#x27; responses is essential for fully exploiting their behavior in applications and to open a much\-needed discussion and standardization of practices within the community\. In this work, we show that drift is ubiquitous across all tested devices and experimental conditions, and present evidence indicating that it is driven by progressive charge trapping in the insulating layer beneath the graphene channel\. We then discuss potential strategies to mitigate drift, including alternative interrogation schemes and fabrication processes\. Additionally, we propose approaches to enhance signal readability and facilitate discrimination of the signal from noise and false\-positive responses in biosensing applications\.

## [Developmental exposure to cannabidiol vapor has persistent impacts on adult exploratory behavior and learning](../publications/b7795a8282a135519b51.md)

Taylor M\. McGillis; Hannah P\. Stevenson; Willow Leland; Joshua S\. Kaplan

Cannabidiol \(CBD\) is a non\-intoxicating phytocannabinoid with purported benefits across a range of pediatric conditions\. However, the relative nascency of its integration in human populations has precluded a longitudinal safety assessment when used during different developmental periods\. We hypothesized that CBD’s pharmacodynamic actions underlying the purported therapeutic effects could impact brain development in a persistent manner that presents as behavioral alterations in adulthood\. To test this hypothesis, we exposed cohorts of non\-pathogenic male and female C57BL/6J mice to twice\-daily 30\-minute CBD \(24\.26 mg/ml\) vapor sessions across 3 different two\-week developmental windows \(postnatal day 7\-21, 14\-28, 28\-42\) and measured its impacts on locomotor activity, anxiety\-related exploratory behavior, and spatial learning and memory in adulthood\. Although we did not observe any effects of CBD on gross locomotor activity in the open field, CBD\-exposed groups performed worse during the acquisition phase of the Barnes Maze learning procedure and demonstrated impaired memory during the probe session\. Additionally, mice exposed to CBD spent more time exploring the open arms of the elevated plus maze, consistent with lower anxiety in a novel environment\. Together, our results suggest that daily CBD exposure during childhood impacts the developing brain in a manner that contributes to persistent changes in spatial learning, memory, and exploratory behaviors later in life\. Nonetheless, the nature of these impacts needs to be considered in balance with the potential therapeutic benefits of CBD and further tested in disease\-specific models\.

## [From Classrooms to Smart Campus Management with Web 3\.0 Tools](../publications/b77a1a5efd5946ba1faf.md)

Vetri Michael Raj

Throughout history, humans have continuously developed and experienced advanced technologies designed to automate labor\-intensive processes and streamline herculean tasks\. Currently, our generation is actively harnessing the multi\-faceted power of Web 3\.0 technologies, which are characterized by their comprehensive, all\-around attributes\. Key innovations such as artificial intelligence, virtual reality, augmented reality, extended reality, blockchain, non\-fungible tokens, smart contracts, decentralized platforms, and intelligent learning management systems represent the vanguard of these uprising Web 3\.0 tools and platforms\. While these technological advancements profoundly elevate major industries including business, finance, medicine, and agriculture, they also critically upgrade our academic field\. Web 3\.0 tools do more than just elevate the standard teaching and learning experiences; they actively organize and manage entire college and university academic ecosystems, providing the most seamless operational experience available\. By deploying these tools, college administrations can effortlessly handle multiple complex tasks simultaneously, consistently resulting in perfect project completion and execution\. This paper outlines the strategic utilization of Web 3\.0 tools and platforms within the respective sectors of colleges and universities to demonstrate a measurable betterment of workflow within institutional management\. From immersive virtual classrooms to decentralized campus management systems, Web 3\.0 tools play a vital role in redefining the professional responsibilities of academic staff, professors, students, research assistants, lab instructors, librarians, and administrative assistants\. Furthermore, this paper exhibits the implementation of Web 3\.0 technologies across other crucial academic dimensions, specifically highlighting research development, secure student data management, and peer\-to\-peer \(P2P\) collaboration\.

## [SEGURANÇA DO PACIENTE E INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: AVANÇOS, RISCOS E PERSPECTIVAS](../publications/b7809ab1bbb63b00396c.md)

Diones da Rocha Rosa; Benedito Sabbak Thome; Janilson Barros De Sá; Taís Rodrigues Dias; Laura Maria de Moura Perri; Hemily Azevedo de Araújo; Yanna Thaís Freire Hipólito de Oliveira

A inteligência artificial \(IA\) vem sendo incorporada ao cuidado em saúde com a promessa de reduzir erros e eventos adversos, mas também introduz riscos novos para a segurança do paciente\. Este artigo analisa avanços, riscos e perspectivas da relação entre segurança do paciente e IA, com ênfase no contexto regulatório brasileiro\. Trata\-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura com análise documental de 15 fontes, entre revisões sistemáticas, estudos de validação, documentos da Organização Mundial da Saúde e normas brasileiras\. Os resultados mostram que a IA tem potencial de maior impacto na prevenção de eventos adversos a medicamentos, na detecção de deterioração clínica e na redução de erros diagnósticos, e que as revisões sistemáticas apontam melhora na detecção de erros, na estratificação de pacientes e no manejo de medicamentos\. Por outro lado, um modelo preditivo de sepse amplamente implantado teve área sob a curva de 0,63 e deixou de identificar 67% dos pacientes com a doença, e um algoritmo de gestão populacional subestimou a necessidade de pacientes negros por usar custos como proxy de doença\. Viés de automação, falhas de fatores humanos e lacunas de responsabilização completam o quadro de riscos\. No Brasil, o Programa Nacional de Segurança do Paciente, a RDC nº 36/2013, a RDC nº 657/2022 e a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados oferecem base parcial, sem regras específicas para IA clínica\. Conclui\-se que a incorporação segura da IA exige validação local, monitoramento contínuo, integração aos núcleos de segurança do paciente, capacitação profissional e transparência\.

## [Data‐Driven and Physics‐Informed Modeling Perspectives for Soft Manipulators: From SINDy to Hybrid Intelligence](../publications/b78ad06907b0c248bb7b.md)

Wenbo Hui; Yunyi Wang; Teng Zhang; Yang Chen; Min Pan

Soft manipulators offer a route to safer, more adaptive and physically intelligent robots, but their compliant bodies remain difficult to model, predict and control\. Large deformation, distributed actuation, hysteresis, material variability and contact\-rich interaction challenge both classical mechanics\-based models and purely data\-driven approaches\. Here, we examine emerging modeling perspectives for soft manipulators through a conceptual progression from sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to hybrid intelligence\. We discuss how sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics \(SINDy\), Koopman learning, neural ordinary differential equations, physics\-informed neural networks, and hybrid physics machine learning models contribute complementary capabilities, including interpretable reduced\-order dynamics, control\-ready prediction, continuous\-time latent modeling, physics\-constrained field reconstruction, and residual correction\. We present that no single modeling approach is sufficient for the next generation of soft robotic systems\. Instead, progress requires integrated modeling ecosystems that combine mechanical structure, data\-driven discovery and task\-aware adaptation\. Such hybrid\-intelligence frameworks can transform models from passive descriptions of deformation into active components of sensing, control, design and decision\-making, enabling soft manipulators that are more interpretable, robust and deployable in real\-world environments\.

## [Arabic Validation of the Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale: Psychometric Properties, Measurement Invariance, and Gender\-Specific Network Analysis](../publications/b797f869035c9bbe6ae2.md)

Abdulrhman Helal; Mohamed Mahmoud Marey; Esraa Reda; Ahmed Hassan; Mahmoud M\. Elhady; Yomna Ahmed Elgohry; Elaf Ahmed Basha; Samantha N\. Sallie

Problematic pornography use \(PPU\) remains understudied in Arabic\-speaking populations, partly due to the limited availability of culturally validated assessment tools\. This study translated and validated the Arabic version of the Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale \(PPCS\) and examined gender\-based differences in symptom structure\. A total of 959 Egyptian university students who watched pornography at least once per week \(65\.1% male, 34\.9% female\) completed the Arabic PPCS, along with standardized measures of depression, anxiety, perceived stress, and problematic internet use\. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original six\-factor model \(CFI = 0\.950, RMSEA = 0\.075, SRMR = 0\.031\), with the scale demonstrating excellent internal consistency \(Cronbach&\#x27;s α = \.95\) and moderate\-to\-strong construct validity as indicated by positive correlations with measures of depression \(r = \.42\), anxiety \(r = \.37\), perceived stress \(r = \.37\), and problematic internet use \(r = \.46; all p &lt; \.001\)\. Overall, 22% of participants were identified as at risk for PPU\. Measurement invariance across gender indicated the scale functioned similarly for males and females\. Network analysis further revealed gender\-specific symptom patterns, with tolerance emerging as the most central symptom among males and withdrawal most central among females\. These findings provide initial validation of the Arabic PPCS and highlight the importance of culturally informed and gender\-sensitive approaches to understanding PPU in Arabic\-speaking populations\.

## [Are Tigress\-Obfuscated Binaries Representative of Real Linux Malware? A Static Feature Measurement Study](../publications/b7980e062deb9fae2820.md)

Jayesh Gaba; Gurpreet Singh; Joseph Raymond

Malware corpora produced through source code obfuscation tools like Tigress are commonly employed for malware detection and binary analysis purposes; however, the representative nature of such malware corpora in relation to real\-life Linux malware is far from sufficiently validated\. This research work investigates whether binaries obfuscated via Tigress can replicate the static features of real Linux ELF malware\. A total of 1,800 Linux ELF malware binaries from 2020\-2025, 179 benign binaries, and 18 Tigress binaries were included in this study, 15 of which were successfully obfuscated\. Section features were derived from 1,245 malware samples using the LIEF library, whereas entropy was computed for all 1,800 malware samples\. Evidence of packing/obfuscation was determined via Detect\-It\-Easy signatures and entropy\-based heuristics, after which comparative and architecture\-controlled analysis was conducted\. Obfuscation or packing was observed in 29\.6% of the malicious samples, increasing from 19\.7% in 2020 to 39\.0% in 2025\. The mean section entropy was higher for packed malware when compared to Tigress obfuscated binaries \(6\.98 vs\. 5\.90\) and remained higher in the x86/x86\-64 subset \(6\.91 vs\. 5\.90\)\. Signature\-based detection found 21\.8% of the samples, whereas the entropy\-based heuristic found 7\.8% in total, but without any overlap\. The distribution of sections was also significantly different between Tigress obfuscated binaries and packed malware\. The considered configurations of Tigress thus fail to emulate several key static properties seen in the analysed set of Linux malwares\.

## [REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs](../publications/b7a233020432e3a8794d.md)

Juliette Marrie; Paul Pacaud; Adrien Ramanana Rahary; Shizhe Chen; Moritz Böhle

We introduce REKI, a 2\.4B vision\-language\-action model \(VLA\) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO\-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size\. REKI consists of a vision\-language model \(VLM\) followed by a flow\-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision\-language data\. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert&\#x27;s cache\. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer\. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference\. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github\.com/kyutai\-labs/reki\.

## [Predictive Data Analytics for Early Detection of Hidden Business Risks Using Machine Learning](../publications/b7c9a068508add3c7965.md)

Kajal Jawane

This research paper presents a machine learning\-based framework for the early detection of hidden business risks using operational and financial data\. Businesses generate large volumes of data related to sales, inventory, customer activity, payments, expenses, and operational systems\. Analyzing these data can help identify unusual patterns and potential risks before they become serious problems\. The paper proposes a data\-driven approach that combines data preparation, feature engineering, machine learning\-based risk classification, anomaly detection, and model explainability\. It discusses methods such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Isolation Forest for identifying potential business risks\. The proposed framework aims to support early warning systems, risk prioritization, and interpretable decision\-making\. It also outlines an evaluation methodology using metrics such as precision, recall, F1\-score, PR\-AUC, false alerts, and lead time\. This paper describes a proposed framework and evaluation plan\. Actual performance results should be reported only after implementation and testing on a suitable dataset\.

## [Digital Disruption in Insurance and Skills Development: Advancing the INSETA Mandate: A Conceptual Review of Technology\-Driven Workforce Transformation in the Global and African Insurance Sector](../publications/b7d3d7f9c01c0b44a604.md)

Ben Kajwang

Purpose: This conceptual review examines the forces driving digital disruption in the global and African insurance sectors and evaluates their implications for employment, professional competencies, and talent management, with particular attention to the role of skills\-development institutions such as South Africa’s Insurance Sector Education and Training Authority \(INSETA\)\. Methodology: Drawing on Human Capital Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study synthesizes peer\-reviewed literature, industry reports, and institutional publications published predominantly between 2024 and 2026\. A qualitative thematic synthesis of secondary sources was employed to identify patterns relating to technological transformation, skills shortages, evolving occupational roles, emerging risks, and institutional responses\. Findings: The findings reveal that digital technologies are reshaping insurance operations and creating hybrid professional roles, yet persistent skills gaps, particularly in data analytics, artificial intelligence literacy, cybersecurity, and digital governance, constrain transformation\. Regional evidence from Kenya and South Africa indicates that technological investment without corresponding human\-capital development yields limited progress\. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study proposes an integrated talent\-intelligence framework that links technological forecasting, competency development, institutional collaboration, and continuous learning\. It offers practical guidance for insurers and training providers, and informs policy on aligning education and regulation with digital insurance transformation

## [Leveraging obligate mutualism to resolve the rare species modeling paradox](../publications/b7d4214b59c418c0488c.md)

Babu Ram Paudel; Arjun Thapa; Ming Bai

Abstract In the past two decades, species distribution models have emerged as vital tools for devising biodiversity conservation planning, yet modeling rare, data‐deficient species remains a significant challenge\. To address this “rare species modelling paradox,” we propose a novel approach: when two obligate mutualistic partners share a fundamental ecological niche, the distribution data of a well‐documented mutualistic partner can serve as a reliable proxy to model the distribution of its rare counterpart\. We tested this hypothesis using the obligatory mutualism between a fly \( Philoliche longirostris \) and its forage plant \( Roscoea purpurea \)\. We first tested the niche overlap between the fly and the plant using Schoener&\#x27;s D and Hellinger&\#x27;s I as proxy measures\. Subsequently, using the occurrence data of R\. purpurea , we performed ensemble SDM and built a proxy distribution model for the fly and tested the proxy model&\#x27;s accuracy through ground truthing of fly occurrence at 40 sites predicted by the proxy model\. Finally, we developed the final distribution models of P\. longirostris by incorporating the points generated through ground‐truthing together with the currently known distribution points, and performed a Pearson correlation analysis between the probabilities of occurrence of the two models\. Our analysis confirmed a significant niche overlap between the two species \(Schoener&\#x27;s D = 0\.552; Hellinger&\#x27;s I = 0\.737\)\. The ground truthing confirmed the presence of P\. longirostris at 37 locations \(92\.5% accuracy\), demonstrating high predictive performance of the proxy model\. A final model showed a strong correlation \( r = 0\.836\) and high spatial overlap with the initial proxy model\. This study suggests that mutualistic proxies can effectively circumvent the data limitation problem for rare species\. Our framework offers a biologically grounded method for enhancing conservation planning of rare/data‐deficient species involved in tight ecological interactions, with broad applications for other ecological interactions\.

## [Target selection of native yeasts isolated from the industrial process: a strategy to optimize bioethanol production](../publications/b7ebe63373efd631c119.md)

Cláudia Steckelberg

The intensification of climate change demands a transition toward renewable energy matrices, positioning bioethanol as a sustainable alternative capable of reducing greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions by up to 90%\. Although Brazil’s bioethanol sector is highly consolidated, optimizing alcoholic fermentation remains a challenge, particularly regarding the selection of robust yeast strains\. Industrial fermentation typically begins with commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae inocula, which are frequently outcompeted and replaced by wild, autochthonous strains throughout the harvest season\. While some native strains compromise production efficiency, others exhibit superior adaptation to industrial stress\. This study presents an industrial case study based on long\-term microbiological monitoring \(2018–2024\) of an operational unit that integrated the native S\. cerevisiae strain DBP\-701–isolated in 2017 due to its superior fermentative performance–into a starter blend with commercial strains \(PE\-2, Angel, and CAT\-1\)\. Population dynamics revealed that DBP\-701 consistently exhibited high prevalence within the microbial consortium, maintaining strong population persistence during the 2021 and 2022 cycles from the beginning to the end of the harvests\. This high prevalence was associated with a reduction in the establishment of invasive wild strains under routine factory conditions\. However, the 2024 harvest diverged from historical patterns; we hypothesize that extreme weather events, including intense heatwaves and sugarcane fires, contributed to increased metabolic stress and altered raw material quality, coinciding with a disruption in strain persistence\. Overall, deploying selected native yeasts like DBP\-701 represents a valuable strategy for enhancing population stability under standard operational conditions, while highlighting potential vulnerabilities under severe environmental perturbations\.

## [Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Detection Using Gradient Boosting Algorithms and Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Study](../publications/b7f348f9efbc461acb68.md)

Ümran Karabulut Doğan; Şeyma Yaşar; Erhan Hüseyin CÖMERT; Erol Karakaş; Ozan Doğan

BACKGROUND/AIMS: Polycystic ovary syndrome \(PCOS\) is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting women of reproductive age, with a global prevalence ranging from 6% to 21%\.Early and accurate diagnosis is critical to preventing long\-term metabolic, reproductive, and cardiovascular complications\.This study aims to develop and compare two gradient\-boosting machine\-learning, extreme gradient boosting \(XGBoost\) and light gradient boosting machine \(LightGBM\), for PCOS classification using clinical and hormonal features and to enhance model interpretability through explainable artificial intelligence techniques\. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A publicly available Kaggle dataset comprising 541 patients and 41 clinical, biochemical, and lifestyle features was utilised\.After preprocessing\-including median imputation and synthetic minority oversampling technique \(SMOTE\)\-two ensemble classifiers were trained and validated using 5\-fold stratified cross\-validation, with SMOTE applied strictly within each training fold to prevent data leakage\.Three baseline classifiers \(logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine\) were included for comparison\.SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) summary plots, bar charts, waterfall diagrams, and local interpretable model\-agnostic explanations \(LIME\) were employed for global and local model interpretability\. RESULTS:XGBoost achieved an accuracy of 91\.74%, an area under the curve\-receiver operating characteristic \(AUC\-ROC\) of 0\.9522 \[95% confidence interval \(CI\): 0\.910\-0\.992\],and an F1\-score of 0\.8696, whereas LightGBM attained an accuracy of 89\.91%, an AUC\-ROC of 0\.9551 \(95% CI: 0\.914\-0\.993\),and an F1\-score of 0\.8451\.Corrected 5\-fold CV AUC scores were 0\.9701±0\.0148and 0\.9682±0\.0161,respectively\.Both gradient boosting models outperformed all three baseline comparators\.Calibration analysis yielded Brier scores of 0\.071 and 0\.079 for XGBoost and LightGBM, respectively, and decision curve analysis demonstrated positive net benefit over treat\-all and treat\-none strategies across clinically plausible threshold ranges\.A sensitivity analysis excluding direct Rotterdam\-criteria variables \(follicle counts and cycle irregularity\) yielded AUC\-ROC values of 0\.88 and 0\.87, confirming residual discriminative capability of non\-criterion features\.SHAP analysis consistently identified right ovarian follicle number \(Follicle No\. R\), hair growth \(hirsutism\), left ovarian follicle number \(Follicle No\. L\), weight gain, and cycle irregularity as the five most influential predictors across both models\.

## [Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards](../publications/b812081c12e0386986f7.md)

Hasan Demirkiran; Jens Ernstberger

Step\-level guards decide, before each tool call, whether an agent&\#x27;s next action is safe given the user&\#x27;s request and the trajectory so far\. Users write those requests in many languages, while guard prompts and the benchmarks on which purpose\-built guards are trained and evaluated are English\. We ask whether a guard&\#x27;s verdict depends on the language of the request\. We build LinguaGuardBench from the 1,220 labelled steps of TS\-Bench AgentDojo\-Traj: we translate only the user instruction into German, French, Turkish, Swahili and Amharic, and keep every tool call, observation and label byte\-identical, so any change in a verdict is attributable to language alone\. Six English rewordings and a whitespace placebo serve as controls, and managed guards are run three times to measure their noise\. Across 19 guards, from frontier APIs to 4B open models and four purpose\-built agent guards, most open, small and purpose\-built guards change verdicts under translation beyond their own noise floor, and the effect grows with the rarity of the language: among the nine guards below 13B parameters, the mean placebo\-adjusted flip rate rises from \+1\.5 pp on French to \+4\.4 pp on Amharic\. Purpose\-built guards are the most sensitive\. The direction of the damage tends to follow guard size: open guards of 12\-30B parameters block more benign steps \(up to \+5\.0 pp false positives\), and every significant loss of recall is in a guard below 10B \(up to \-7\.4 pp\)\. Frontier guards shift by at most about one point; the strongest, Gemini 3\.8 Flash, returns identical verdicts with and without the request\. The damage is concentrated in a few instructions and, in a post\-hoc analysis, falls on steps where the agent&\#x27;s reasoning restates the English request, consistent with guards reacting to inconsistency between channels\. English paraphrase moves every guard less than translation does\. We release the benchmark and all 489k verdicts\.

## [Flexible pyramidal BiFeO 3 –BaTiO 3 microcone arrays integrated with P\(VDF\-TrFE\) for self\-powered mechanical sensing and energy harvesting](../publications/b81719d6896e26beb492.md)

Wentao Yang; Hang Zhan; Panpan Lv; Guiyun Gao; Shuzhi Zhang; Le Xin; Cuncheng Li; Luchao Ren; Jin Qian; Mingwei Zhang

Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites hold great promise for self\-powered sensors and wearable electronics, but their performance is often limited by the low piezoelectricity of polymers, uneven dispersion of inorganic fillers, and poor interfacial stress transfer\. To overcome these challenges, we fabricated a vertically oriented pyramidal BiFeO3\-BaTiO3 \(BFO\-BTO\) microcone array on P\(VDF\-TrFE\) films using an AAO template\-assisted method\. The conical geometry induces localized stress concentration at the interface, thereby amplifying the local strain and enhancing the electromechanical response\. Systematic studies reveal that microcone height critically influences the polarization behavior, piezoelectric coefficients, and overall device output\. The resulting flexible devices, fabricated from the 1\.5 μm BFO\-BTO microcone/P\(VDF\-TrFE\) composite piezoelectric films, achieve an open\-circuit voltage of 5\.12 V, a force sensitivity of 6\.28 V·N\-1 \(linearity R2 = 0\.98\), while maintaining stable performance over 3000 mechanical cycles at 5 Hz under 0\.66 N, demonstrating excellent durability\. Moreover, the sensors enable high\-precision, real\-time monitoring of physiological and motion signals, including finger tapping, fist impacts, and foot stepping, highlighting their potential in intelligent health monitoring, human\-machine interaction, and mechanical energy harvesting\. This work elucidates how microcone structure design governs the electromechanical properties of flexible piezoelectric composites and offers practical design guidelines for flexible sensing and energy\-harvesting applications\.

## [Physics Informed Machine Learning for Electrical Sensing and Prediction of Heavy Metal Contamination in Water](../publications/b8179185818d566ffaac.md)

Hamza Mustapha Umar; Ismail Aminu Mahmoud; Neha Shrivas; Ibrahim Abba Ibrahim; Auwal Adam; Musa Garba Abdullahi; Jamila Lamido

Access to safe drinking water remains a global challenge, with approximately 2\.1 billion people lacking safely managed water services\. Continuous, low\-cost monitoring of heavy metal contamination is limited because conventional techniques such as atomic absorption spectroscopy \(AAS\) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry \(ICP\-MS\) are accurate but require centralized laboratories and high operational costs\. Although machine learning has shown promise for water quality prediction, existing models are generally trained on empirical datasets and lack the physical constraints governing sensor behavior\. This study addresses this limitation by developing a physics\-informed machine learning framework based on a physically consistent synthetic dataset of 300 samples generated from Ohm&\#x27;s law, Kohlrausch&\#x27;s law of molar conductivity, and metal\-hydrolysis pH chemistry\. The dataset was utilized to predict heavy metal concentration from voltage, current, conductivity, temperature and pH\. The Random Forest \(RF\) and Multi\-Layer Perceptron Artificial Neural Network \(ANN\) models were benchmarked against linear regression using cross\-validation of 5\-folds and 10\-folds\. The ANN was optimized with L2 regularization and early stopping\. During 5\-fold cross\-validation, the accuracy of RF was found to have R² of 0\.38 ± 0\.13 \(RMSE = 0\.049 ± 0\.004 mg/L; MAE = 0\.039 ± 0\.003 mg/L\), while ANN optimization was improved from R² = −0\.05 till 0\.22\. Linear regression produced the best performance \(R² = 0\.47 ± 0\.16\), consistent with the predominantly linear physics underlying the dataset\. Conductivity was identified as the dominant predictor, accounting for approximately 87% of RF feature importance and remaining robust under simulated sensor noise of up to 10%\. Although the prediction accuracy is not yet sufficient for regulatory\-grade quantification, the proposed framework demonstrates that physics\-informed synthetic data can support interpretable, reproducible machine learning models for rapid, low\-cost screening and prioritization of water samples for laboratory confirmation\.

## [Karar Biliminde Nicel Yöntemler: Çok Kriterli, Optimizasyon Odaklı ve Makine Öğrenmesi Temelli Güncel Yaklaşımlar](../publications/b819a34ce827b067aff1.md)



Bu kitap, karmaşık karar problemlerinin çözümlenmesinde kullanılan çok kriterli karar verme, optimizasyon ve makine öğrenmesi yaklaşımlarını yöntemsel açıklamalar ve farklı alanlardan uygulamalarla bir araya getirmektedir\. On iki bölümden oluşan eser, kriter ağırlıklandırma, alternatiflerin sıralanması, kaynak kullanım etkinliğinin ölçülmesi, kümeleme, tahmin ve model sonuçlarının açıklanması gibi karar biliminin temel konularını ele almaktadır\. Çok kriterli karar verme eksenindeki bölümlerde MEREC, LOPCOW, SAW, TODIM, Gri İlişkisel Analiz, AHP, TOPSIS, EDAS ve SPOTIS yöntemleri ile entropi ağırlıklandırması farklı değerlendirme problemleri kapsamında incelenmektedir\. Optimizasyon odaklı yaklaşım, OECD sağlık sistemlerinin kaynak kullanım etkinliğini karşılaştıran CCR ve BCC veri zarflama analizi modelleriyle temsil edilmektedir\. Makine öğrenmesi temelli bölümler ise ekonomik özgürlükler ve çevresel performans bakımından ülkelerin sınıflandırılmasını, bilgi yönetimi araçları ile iş tatmini arasındaki ilişkinin modellenmesini ve açıklanabilir yapay zekâ destekli dijital performans değerlendirmesini kapsamaktadır\. Tarımsal destekler ile üretim arasındaki ilişki, panel veriye dayalı regresyon modelleriyle ele alınarak kitabın nicel analiz kapsamını genişletmektedir\. E\-ticaret, sağlık, mesleki varış profilleri, havacılıkta kalite güvencesi, çağdaş sanatta sürdürülebilirlik, tarımsal üretim, ekonomik özgürlükler ve dijital dönüşüm alanlarındaki çalışmalar, yöntem seçimi ile uygulama bağlamı arasındaki ilişkiyi görünür kılmaktadır\. Kitap; yöntemlerin kuramsal dayanaklarını, hesaplama süreçlerini ve bulguların yorumlanmasını birlikte değerlendirmek isteyen araştırmacılar, lisansüstü öğrenciler, karar analistleri ve politika yapıcılar için bir başvuru kaynağı olarak hazırlanmıştır\.

## [Data\-driven Modeling of Telluric Features and Stellar Variability with StellarSpectraObservationFitting\.jl](../publications/b81a2c03d2253404cbab.md)

Christian Gilbertson; Eric B\. Ford; Samuel Halverson; Evan Fitzmaurice; Cullen H\. Blake; Guðmundur Stefánsson; Suvrath Mahadevan; Jason T\. Wright; Jacob K\. Luhn; Joe Philip Ninan; Paul M\. Robertson; Arpita Roy; Christian Schwab; Ryan C\. Terrien

Abstract A significant barrier to achieving the radial velocity \(RV\) measurement accuracy and precision required to characterize terrestrial mass exoplanets is the existence of time\-variable features in the measured spectra, from both telluric absorption and stellar variability, which affect measured line shapes and can cause apparent RV shifts\. Reaching submillisecond accuracy using traditional techniques often requires avoiding lines contaminated by stellar variability and/or changing tellurics, and thus discarding a large fraction of the spectrum, lowering precision\. New data\-driven methods can help achieve extremely precise and accurate RVs by enabling the use of a larger fraction of the available data\. While there exist methods for modeling telluric features or the stellar variability individually, there is a need for additional tools that are capable of modeling them simultaneously at the spectral level\. Here, we present StellarSpectraObservationFitting\.jl \( SSOF \), a Julia package for measuring Doppler shifts and creating data\-driven models \(with fast, physically motivated Gaussian Process regularization\) for the time\-variable spectral features for both the telluric transmission and stellar spectrum, while accounting for the wavelength\-dependent instrumental line spread function\. We demonstrate SSOF ’s state\-of\-the\-art performance on data from the NEID spectrometer on the WIYN 3\.5 m Telescope for multiple stars\. We show SSOF ’s ability to accurately identify and characterize spectral variability, provide ∼2–6× smaller photon\-limited errors over the NEID CCF\-based pipeline, and match the performance of SERVAL , a leading template\-based pipeline, using only observed EPRV spectra\.

## [Optimizing early identification and management of trastuzumab deruxtecan\-related interstitial lung disease: insights from a multidisciplinary expert panel](../publications/b820d163cce0c52ecbd8.md)

Luca Licata; C\. Lisanti; Grazia Arpino; Lorenzo Cereser; Nicholas Landini; Francesco Macagno; Francesco Pantano; Ida Paris; Mirco Pistelli; Paolo Tarsia; Giampaolo Bianchini

Purpose Trastuzumab deruxtecan \(T\-DXd\) is a HER2\-directed antibody–drug conjugate that has demonstrated substantial clinical efficacy across HER2\-expressing malignancies\. However, interstitial lung disease \(ILD\) represents a clinically relevant and potentially serious adverse event associated with its use, requiring early recognition, exclusion of alternative etiologies and coordinated multidisciplinary management\. Delayed identification may increase the risk of severe pulmonary toxicity and premature discontinuation of an otherwise highly effective therapy\. In this manuscript, we aim to provide practical guidance on the early detection and management of T\-DXd\-related ILD\. Methods A structured multidisciplinary discussion involving oncologists, pneumologists, and radiologists was conducted to evaluate the epidemiology, risk factors, diagnostic pathways, and management strategies for ILD in patients treated with T\-DXd\. Evidence from the published literature was reviewed to inform and support the panel’s recommendations\. Results ILD may arise in up to 15% of patients receiving T\-DXd\. While most events occur during the first year of treatment, continued vigilance is warranted throughout therapy\. High\-resolution computed tomography \(HRCT\) is essential for early detection, and prompt treatment interruption combined with timely corticosteroid therapy is critical to prevent progression\. The panel emphasized the importance of standardized imaging protocols, structured radiologic reporting, early multidisciplinary involvement, and patient education to facilitate prompt recognition and management\. Conclusion Proactive surveillance strategies, including baseline and interval HRCT, multidisciplinary collaboration and patient\-centered monitoring, are essential to minimize ILD\-related morbidity while preserving access to T\-DXd therapy\. The implementation of standardized clinical pathways and the development of biomarker\-driven approaches may further improve personalized ILD risk management\.

## [The integrin αvβ6/TGF\-β1/Smad4 signaling pathway regulates ENaC in alcohol induced ARDS](../publications/b82fe00846b7ae755dff.md)

Xue Dai; Xue\-Ling Liu; Meijun Liu; ting li; Daoxin Wang; Wang Deng

Introduction Acute respiratory distress syndrome \(ARDS\) is characterized by impaired alveolar\-capillary permeability and pulmonary edema\. Alveolar fluid clearance \(AFC\) is strongly associated with patient prognosis\. This study aimed to investigate whether chronic alcohol consumption affects sodium channel regulation in ARDS via the Integrin αvβ6/TGF\-β1/Smad4 signaling pathway\. Methods We established chronic alcohol exposure models in mice and MLE\-12 cells, followed by lipopolysaccharide \(LPS\)\-induced ARDS in both systems\. The Integrin αvβ6/TGF\-β1/Smad4 pathway was inhibited to explore its regulatory effect on ENaC and Na \+ ,K \+ \-ATPase during alcohol\-induced ARDS\. Results We found that chronic alcohol consumption exacerbated lung injury by activating this signaling pathway, which suppressed ENaC and Na \+ ,K \+ \-ATPase protein expression\. Inhibition of the pathway alleviated pulmonary edema and inflammation and improved survival rates\. Both in vivo and in vitro results demonstrated that the Integrin αvβ6/TGF\-β1/Smad4 pathway regulates ENaC and Na \+ ,K \+ \-ATPase in alcohol\-induced ARDS\. Conclusion These findings may clarify the regulatory mechanisms of sodium channels in ARDS associated with chronic alcohol consumption\.

## [Digital Transformation: Enabling Change Management Strategies and Performance for Nonprofit Organizations in Kenya](../publications/b8305beb05994c372f3d.md)

Duncan Mutulu; Robert M\. Arasa; James Murunga

This study examines whether change management strategies \(leadership capacity building, capability reconfiguration initiatives, stakeholder engagement and communication strategies\) are associated with the performance of nonprofit organizations \(NPOs\) in Kenya, and whether digital transformation moderates their joint influence\. NPOs in resource\-constrained environments face donor dependency, funding volatility and weak institutional capacity, which make adaptability critical\. Anchored on the Resource\-Based View and supported by Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Technology Infusion Model, the study adopted a pragmatic, convergent mixed\-methods cross\-sectional design\. A sample of 368 of the 4,750 compliant NPOs was determined with Yamane’s formula and drawn by stratified random sampling, and 261 usable questionnaires were returned \(70\.9%\)\. A pilot of 37 NPOs confirmed reliability \(Cronbach’s α = 0\.746–0\.944\) and construct validity\. Hypotheses were tested with ordinal logistic regression using a cumulative logit link, and open\-ended responses were analysed thematically\. Leadership capacity building \(β = 0\.453, p = \.043\) and capability reconfiguration initiatives \(β = 0\.426, p = \.040\) were positively associated with performance, whereas stakeholder engagement \(β = 0\.328, p = \.132\) and communication strategies \(β = −0\.046, p = \.818\) were not significant\. The four strategies had a significant joint association with performance \(β = 0\.960, p = \.009\)\. Digital transformation was positively associated with performance \(β = 0\.495, p = \.017\) and strengthened the joint association of the strategies with performance \(β = 1\.598, p = \.004\)\. The study recommends that NPO boards, managers and regulators strengthen leadership and capability reconfiguration, institutionalize stakeholder engagement and communication, and integrate digital transformation into coordinated change management programmes\. Keywords: Digital Transformation, ICT Adoption, Automation, Data\-Driven Practices, Change Management; Nonprofit Organizations, Strategic Adaptability, Organizational Resilience; Kenya

## [The Relationship Between Diet and the Incidence of Anemia in Adolescent Girls at Sman 1 Sungai Raya Islands of Bengkayang Regency in 2026](../publications/b8349cb2a8bd39768b00.md)

Fatika Maulidya; Uray Evi Nasla; Adhetya Uberty

Anemia remains a significant public health concern among adolescent girls, as rapid growth, menstrual blood loss, and inadequate dietary intake may increase the risk of iron deficiency and anemia\. This study examined the association between dietary patterns and anemia among tenth\-grade female students at SMAN 1 Sungai Raya Kepulauan, Bengkayang Regency, Indonesia, in 2026\. An analytical observational study with a cross\-sectional design was conducted\. Of the 97 students in the study population, 71 respondents were selected using simple random sampling\. Dietary patterns were assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire \(FFQ\), while hemoglobin concentrations were measured using a digital hemoglobinometer\. Data were analyzed using Pearson&\#x27;s chi\-square test with a significance level of ? = 0\.05\. Among the 71 respondents, 37 \(52\.1%\) were classified as having inappropriate dietary patterns, while 11 \(15\.5%\) were identified as having anemia\. Cross\-tabulation revealed that anemia occurred in 1 of 37 respondents \(2\.7%\) with inappropriate dietary patterns and 10 of 34 respondents \(29\.4%\) with appropriate dietary patterns\. A statistically significant association was observed between dietary pattern classification and anemia status \(Pearson&\#x27;s ?² = 9\.654; df = 1; p = 0\.002\)\. However, the unexpectedly higher prevalence of anemia among respondents classified as having appropriate dietary patterns highlighted the need for cautious interpretation, particularly regarding the dietary assessment criteria and potential confounding factors\. Given the cross\-sectional design, the findings did not establish a causal relationship between dietary patterns and anemia\. The study underscored the importance of strengthening adolescent nutrition education, conducting routine hemoglobin screening, and undertaking further research using comprehensive dietary assessments to clarify the relationship between dietary intake and anemia risk among adolescent girls\.

## [The Use and Utility of Preoperative Somatostatin Receptor\-Based Imaging in Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors](../publications/b83574a9085042724dc9.md)

Jeremy Chang; Brandon Toliver; Luis C\. Borbon; Scott K\. Sherman; Po Hien Ear; Andrew M\. Bellizzi; Carlos H\.F\. Chan; Yusuf Menda; Joseph Stephen Dillon; James R\. Howe

BACKGROUND: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor \(GEPNET\) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption\. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor \(NET\) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs \(SBNET\) and pancreatic NETs \(PNETs\)\. METHODS: A retrospective single\-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging\. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging\. RESULTS: The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients\. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 \(63\.3%\) SBNET patients \(158 somatostatin receptor \[SSTR\] positron emission tomography \[PET\] and 90 Octreoscan\) and 113 \(54\.3%\) PNET patients \(47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan\)\. There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2\.5% yearly increase \(p &lt; 0\.01\) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study \(p = 0\.82\)\. At presentation, 82\.3% \(204/248\) of the SBNET patients and 54\.9% \(62/113\) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease\. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases\. CONCLUSION: Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years\. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR\-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra\-operative planning, and further management\.

## [Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Psychostimulant Intoxication in Emergency Department Patients: A Multicenter Study](../publications/b835ed50febbb9b91d41.md)

Jiun‐Hao Yu; Yueh\-Peng Chen; Chih\-Huang Hsieh; Yu\-Jang Su; Hsien\-Yi Chen; Chih\-Chuan Lin; Te\-I Weng; Cheng\-Chung Fang; Sung\-Wei Liu; Yen\-Chia Chen; Yu\-Cheng Pei; Kuan\-Fu Chen

Introduction: Psychostimulant detection rates among emergency department \(ED\) patients presenting with suspected substance intoxication are low and are influenced by limited access to confirmatory testing, insufficient clinical information, and variability in physician experience\. These challenges often result in high false\-positive rates and unnecessary resource use\. We hypothesized that machine learning \(ML\) algorithms could maintain reliable diagnostic performance across a temporal validation cohort and perform comparably to physicians with varying experience levels\. Methods: This multicenter study prospectively enrolled ED patients with suspected substance intoxication between March 2019 and January 2020\. We chronologically partitioned data into a training set \(March–October 2019\) and a temporal validation cohort \(November 2019–January 2020\) to assess model generalizability\. After determining psychostimulant intoxication via liquid chromatography\-mass spectrometry from urine samples, we trained the ML algorithms using the confirmed positive cases\. The primary outcome was the diagnostic discrimination of the models, measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) in the temporal validation cohort\. Secondary outcomes included model accuracy, the Youden index, and a comparative assessment of sensitivity and specificity relative to five physicians of varying experience levels\. Results: Among 1,382 patients \(mean age 43\.8 \[standard deviation 19\.2\] years; 55\.3% male\), 302 patients \(21\.9%\) had confirmed psychostimulant intoxication, primarily involving \(meth\)amphetamines \(134 \[44\.4%\]\), cathinones \(107 \[35\.4%\]\), and ketamine \(97 \[32\.1%\]\)\. In the temporal validation cohort \(n = 382\), the ML models demonstrated consistent performance, with AUCs ranging from 0\.786 to 0\.836\. The primary outcome was met by the top\-performing extreme gradient boosting \(XGB\) model \(AUC, 0\.836, 95% CI, 0\.785\-0\.882; accuracy, 0\.866 \(95% CI, 0\.838\-0\.895\); and Youden index, 0\.590 \(95% CI, 0\.480\-0\.694\)\. To evaluate secondary outcomes, the XGB model’s predictive accuracy was evaluated against 5 emergency physicians\. The model surpassed the junior emergency physicians in both specificity \(0\.910 vs 0\.633\-0\.867\) and sensitivity \(0\.681 vs 0\.500\-0\.633\); its specificity was comparable to that of the senior emergency physicians \(0\.900\-0\.933\)\. Conclusion: Machine learning models provide reliable diagnostic utility for identifying psychostimulant intoxication, achieving performance comparable to senior emergency physicians\. While moderate sensitivity \(0\.389–0\.708\) limits their role as standalone rule\-out tools, their high specificity provides a standardized tool to assist clinical decision\-making and reduce diagnostic uncertainty in the fast\-paced ED setting\.

## [Introduction \(Inglés\)](../publications/b83d69cb65c4686ab249.md)

Ricardo Villanueva

El Anuario Mexicano de Asuntos Globales \(AMAG\) presenta su cuarto volumen en un momento de transición del sistema internacional\. El orden internacional que emergió de la posguerra fría, caracterizado por la hegemonía estadounidense y la expansión de un modelo liberal continúa en debacle\. La competencia estratégica entre las grandes potencias, dificultades del multilateralismo, persistencia de conflictos armados, así como las tensiones en torno al comercio y recursos estratégicos están conviviendo con transformaciones tecnológicas que están modificando las formas tradicionales de ejercer el poder\. En este escenario, la publicación del IV volumen del AMAG no solo documenta los acontecimientos más significativos del último año, sino que brinda un espacio de análisis crítico para comprender las fuerzas profundas que están reconfigurando el poder, economía y sociedad a nivel planetario\.

## [La arquitectura de la cognición extendida en un posgrado en modalidad virtual: un análisis sistémico de la interacción dialógica estudiante\-IAG](../publications/b84bf3058d0f45bbd108.md)

Guadalupe Jeanette González Díaz; David Bonilla Carranza; Jahzheel Margarita Ortiz Hernández

La irrupción de la inteligencia artificial generativa \(IAG\) en la educación superior ha precipitado una reconfiguración de los entornos personales de aprendizaje, planteando desafíos inéditos sobre la autoría, la creatividad y la dependencia tecnológica\. Este estudio analiza la interacción entre estudiantes de un posgrado en innovación de una universidad pública estatal de México y un asistente virtual denominado “Innova\-bot”\. Se conceptualiza a la IAG no como una simple herramienta sino como un agente de cognición extendida que reconfigura la zona de desarrollo próximo\. A través de un diseño mixto que integra el análisis forense de bitácoras de interacción y una revisión sistemática de la literatura reciente \(2019\-2025\), se identifican patrones dialógicos que oscilan entre la dependencia instrumental y un diálogo socrático transformador\. Los hallazgos sugieren que si bien la percepción estudiantil es mayoritariamente positiva, existe una necesidad crítica de alfabetización algorítmica para transitar de la ansiedad o la comodidad pasiva hacia un empoderamiento epistémico real\.

Ahmad Fadhli; Alexandria Cempaka Harum; Rivaldi Muhammad; Naimah Salma Lazuardi Raisah; Hidayat Nur Alifa

Bukan sekadar membuat pendidikan lebih terlihat di media sosial, tetapi memastikan bahwa apa yang terlihat tetap layak disebut pendidikan\.&quot;PEDAGOGI DIGITAL&quot; membahas perubahan pendidikan anak ketika pengetahuan, komunikasi, interaksi, dan kehidupan sehari\-hari semakin terhubung dengan media sosial\.
