Di dalamnya bekerja pula strategi komunikasi, budaya partisipasi, ekonomi perhatian, data, algoritma, serta kepentingan dan tata kelola platform\. Buku ini mempertemukan perspektif pendidikan anak, pedagogi digital, komunikasi edukatif, literasi, etika, dan budaya platform untuk membangun cara pandang yang lebih utuh terhadap praktik pendidikan di media sosial\. Pembahasan mencakup perkembangan dan hak anak dalam lingkungan digital, proses belajar di ruang publik dan informal, storytelling dan produksi konten edukatif, microlearning, multimodalitas, engagement dan analytics, kredibilitas, personal branding, kecerdasan artifisial, komodifikasi, datafikasi, hingga politik visibilitas\. Alih\-alih menawarkan formula untuk mengejar viralitas, buku ini mengajak pembaca mempertanyakan hubungan antara perhatian dan pendidikan: apakah konten yang banyak dilihat selalu bernilai edukatif, apakah engagement menunjukkan pembelajaran, dan bagaimana pengetahuan tetap dapat dikomunikasikan secara menarik tanpa kehilangan tanggung jawab pedagogis dan etis\. Pembahasan diperkaya dengan studi kasus 1\.290 unggahan Instagram @kaksetosahabatanak periode 2020\-2026, yang memperlihatkan bagaimana pedagogi digital diproduksi, dipersonalisasi, berinteraksi dengan beragam praktik komunikasi, dan memperoleh tingkat visibilitas yang berbeda\. Buku ini ditujukan bagi pendidik, dosen, peneliti, praktisi komunikasi, kreator edukatif, pengelola lembaga dan komunitas, orang tua, serta siapa pun yang ingin memahami pendidikan dalam budaya media sosial secara lebih kritis dan bertanggung jawab

## [Sustainable finance versus non\-sustainable finance and environmental sustainability: evidence from selected OECD economies](../publications/b861ec7d8f8cccc4fc94.md)

Daniel Balsalobre‐Lorente; Magdalena Radulescu; Niu Rong; Syed Ale Raza Shah; Naila Abbas

This study aims to examine the role of sustainable finance vs\. nonsustainable finance in environmental sustainability using OECD nations from 2012 to 2023\. Surprisingly, the data characteristics provide a clear guide to choose an appropriate set of estimators\. For instance, all variables are integrated at first difference, which compels this study to adopt the Johnson cointegration approach\. In addition, to address cross\-sectional dependence and serial correlation problems, this study employs the Driscoll\-Kraay Standard Error estimator\. To break the suspense, this study considers total factor productivity, urbanization, technology \(including information &amp; communication technology and artificial intelligence\), green innovation, public‒private partnerships \(PPPs\), sustainability, and nonsustainable finance as environmental determinants\. The obtained results remain fascinating for the specified nations\. For instance, outcomes reveal an inverse relationship between total factor productivity, urbanization, and green innovations with carbon emissions\. In addition, information and communication technology, artificial intelligence, and public‒private partnerships contribute to emissions\. Similarly, sustainable finance \(SF\), including green bonds and green foreign direct investment, plays a significant role in addressing environmental issues\. In contrast, nonsustainable finance increases emissions, except for financial stability and financial efficiency\. Additionally, this study offers a moderate effect of SF on PPPs and green innovations, which does not support the sustainability theme\. A heterogeneity view yields awe\-inspiring results concerning environmental proxies, including CO2 emissions, ecological footprint, and load capacity factor\. Finally, cross\-country analysis describes fascinating outcomes under the proposed theme\. Regarding outcomes, the present study offers imperative implications for becoming clean and green shortly\.

## [Martínez\-Roget, Fidel ; Rodríguez, Xosé A\. &amp; Pestana Mourão, Luis: Artificial intelligence and employment in the hospitality sector: an analysis of the determining factors in the digital age](../publications/b86e0570ef4b7eb1558c.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 41 \(4\):4013\-4024\. 2026This research is based on an empirical analysis of the determinants for job\-level employment in hotels\. The study takes data from 60 hotels in the Porto and Northern Portugal region, to conduct an empirical analysis based on a sample of 1560 observations, using a Tobit model\. It considers how the various types of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\)—mechanical, thinking and feeling—influence employment\. The research reveals that employment in hotels is positively influenced by internal characteristics such as the presence of female employees and having an own brand, as well as by worker\-related factors such as professional experience and specialised training in tourism\. The use of the various types of intelligence also has a positive impact on employment across various hotel jobs\. The results demonstrate the coexistence of the three types of intelligence in the hotel jobs and a greater marginal effect on employment in roles that require emotional intelligence\. This study is novel as in addition to traditional variables, it also considers AI as a determinant of employment in hotels\. Furthermore, it analyses employment in a disaggregated manner across different hotel jobs, taking into account the intelligence associated with the tasks of each role and the current use of AI\. \(direct link \)

## [Evaluating LLMs for named entity recognition: a cost\-benefit analysis in the legal domain](../publications/b870cad43beee889f57f.md)

Shefali Singhal; Eoin O’Connell; Niall McCarroll; Niamh Keogh; Mary Doherty; Vishva Munasinghe; Sujata Rani; Kevin Curran; Eugene McNamee; Angela Clist; Andrew Brammer

Abstract Within the legal domain, named entity recognition \(NER\) is an essential pre\-processing tool for important tasks such as information extraction and redaction\. Research to date has focused on rule\-based approaches or machine learning strategies that require significant time and effort to train through labelled corpora\. Large, multi\-purpose generative large language models \(LLMs\) have been successfully employed on natural language processing \(NLP\) tasks with no prior supervised training and may represent a way forward in addressing these existing bottlenecks\. Despite promising results in certain NLP use cases, the Few\-Shot LLM performance on unfamiliar, domain\-specific NER tasks has, to date, remained uncertain\. In this legal clause NER task, we evaluate a Few\-Shot, Chain\-of\-Thought \(CoT\) prompting strategy for OpenAI’s GPT\-4 LLM on a new CUAD\-NER dataset that we have repurposed for the task of Person and Organisation entity identification\. In a comparative study, we demonstrate that the GPT4 \+ Few\-Shot CoT prompt strategy outperforms existing state\-of\-the\-art models, achieving a 5% percentage point improvement in Micro F1 score over the best performing BERT base \(cased\) competitor\. This study also takes the novel approach of assessing the business feasibility of deploying each of these machine learning models through a detailed cost–benefit analysis that measures the trade\-off between performance metrics and low and high usage running costs\.

## [Hard Instances on Demand](../publications/b87d33c58c19b566c372.md)

Jamie Fravel; Martin Koutecký; Pavlo Tsitsei

The conclusions of an experimental study of algorithms are only as good as the instances they are run on\. Benchmark libraries for well\-studied problems took decades to curate, while evaluations of new problems often fall back on random instances, which are known to be misleading: they may say more about the random generator than about the algorithmic question at hand\. We treat instance generation as an optimization problem: parameterize the instance space, take the solver&\#x27;s running time as the objective, and let a black\-box optimizer search for hard instances\. We develop a widely applicable workflow built on the Nevergrad optimization platform and demonstrate it on four NP\-hard problems: satisfiability, traveling salesperson, Hamiltonian cycle, and non\-permutation flow\-shop scheduling\. The search needs only the solver, an instance encoder, and a compute budget\. Our evolved instances beat the hardest instance of a budget\-matched random draw in all four case studies, by an order of magnitude or more in three\. They are often competitive with long\-curated benchmark sets: our SAT champion is harder \(for a three\-solver portfolio\) than 78% of the 498 SAT Competition formulas in its size class; our 20\-city TSP champions take several times longer than the hardest measured classical TSPLIB instance \(229 cities\); and our flow\-shop champion takes 238\.6 seconds of CP Optimizer time to solve to proven optimality \(versus 4\.5 seconds for the hardest of 100,000 random draws\) while denying CP\-SAT an optimality proof\. The optimizer even recovers known structure from running time alone: it locates a SAT clause/variable ratio near the phase transition and finds structurally different champions for the two scheduling engines\.

## [Tathmini ya Mipango ya Vyuo Vikuu katika Fursa za Lugha Kwenye Sera ya Elimu Iliyoboreshwa: Mifano Kutoka katika Mitaala ya Kiswahili](../publications/b88cc63706574914c2c9.md)

Bertha Benitho; Mussa Omari Amanzi

Makala haya yanatathmini mipango ya Vyuo Vikuu katika maboresho ya mitaala ya Kiswahili kufuatia utekelezaji wa Sera ya Elimu na Mafunzo ya 2014 \(Toleo la 2023\) nchini Tanzania\. Sera hii imefungua fursa mpya za kuimarisha matumizi ya Kiswahili katika elimu, maendeleo ya taaluma na soko la ajira, hivyo kuhitaji Vyuo Vikuu kuboresha mitaala na programu zake ili kuendana na mahitaji mapya ya kitaifa na kijamii\. Utafiti ulitumia mkabala wa kimaelezo wa ubora na kuongozwa na Nadharia ya Uamilifu wa Kijamii ya Émile Durkheim\. Data zilikusanywa kupitia usaili wa ana kwa ana na uchambuzi wa nyaraka kutoka kwa wahadhiri na wakuu wa idara za Kiswahili katika Vyuo Vikuu vitatu nchini Tanzania\. Data zilichambuliwa kwa kutumia uchambuzi wa maudhui kwa kuzingatia malengo ya utafiti\. Matokeo yanaonesha kuwa vyuo vikuu vimeanza kufanya maboresho ya mitaala kwa kuanzisha programu na kozi mpya zinazohusiana na tafsiri, ukalimani, uhariri, uandishi, Kiswahili cha Biashara na matumizi ya Teknolojia ya Habari na Mawasiliano \(TEHAMA\)\. Aidha, Vyuo vimeimarisha mbinu za ufundishaji zinazolenga kukuza stadi za vitendo, ubunifu na umahiri unaohitajika katika soko la ajira\. Hata hivyo, utekelezaji wa mipango hiyo unaendelea kukabiliwa na changamoto za rasilimali, wataalamu na miundombinu ya kiteknolojia\. Makala haya yanahitimisha kuwa mafanikio ya utekelezaji wa sera mpya ya elimu yanategemea uoanishaji madhubuti kati ya sera, mitaala na mahitaji ya maendeleo ya taifa\. Hivyo, inapendekezwa kuimarishwa kwa uwekezaji katika maendeleo ya mitaala, rasilimali za kufundishia, utafiti na mafunzo ya wataalamu ili kuongeza mchango wa Kiswahili katika maendeleo ya kijamii, kiuchumi na kielimu nchini Tanzania\.

## [MAPPING FORENSIC ACCOUNTING’S SCHOLARLY LANDSCAPE IN NIGERIA: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF FRAUD DETECTION AND PREVENTION RESEARCH](../publications/b88e832b687652f0f665.md)

Abdullahi Giza Abubakar; Teinye Joseph Duke

Nigeria’s persistent exposure to financial fraud and systemic corruption has intensified the demand for robust investigative tools, with forensic accounting emerging as a critical mechanism for enhancing transparency, accountability, and institutional integrity\. Despite its theoretical promise, the scholarly engagement with forensic accounting in Nigeria remains fragmented and underdeveloped\. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 138 peer\-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2025, retrieved exclusively from the Scopus database, to examine the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and research gaps in forensic accounting and fraud\-related scholarship\. Using the Bibliometrix package in RStudio, the study maps publication trends, identifies prolific authors and institutions, visualises co\-authorship networks, and explores keyword co\-occurrence and thematic clusters\. The findings reveal a steady growth in scholarly output, with international collaboration moderately present but Nigerian contributions notably sparse despite the country’s high corruption index\. Dominant themes include fraud detection, forensic audit techniques, and data analytics, while emerging areas such as blockchain, smart contracts, and AI\-driven fraud prevention remain underexplored\. This study underscores the need for context\-specific frameworks, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strategic investment in Nigeria&\#x27;s forensic accounting education and research infrastructure\. This can be achieved by illuminating the structural dynamics and intellectual gaps within the field\. This study offers actionable insights for scholars, policymakers, and anti\-graft institutions seeking to leverage forensic accounting to combat financial crime\.

## [Designing Culturally Grounded Mindful Learning for Social Moderation in Elementary Schools: A Qualitative Needs Analysis in a Pandalungan Context](../publications/b8a3b6b1ab68d98c13a6.md)

Arief Tukiman Hendrawijaya; Muhammad Irfan Hilmi; Niswatul Imsiyah; Muhammad Shulton Masyhud; Derirista Rindriani; Kunti Kunanti; Novika Herlinasari

Elementary classrooms are formative social spaces in which children learn how to interpret difference, regulate responses, participate fairly, and handle disagreement\. This qualitative needs analysis examined how culturally grounded mindful learning could be designed to support social moderation in upper\-grade elementary classrooms in Jember, East Java, Indonesia\. The study formed the Analysis phase of an iterative ADDIE project and drew on written semi\-structured interview responses from eight teachers and two principals\. Reflexive thematic analysis combined deductive domains with inductive coding and translated themes into provisional design requirements\. Participants described culturally and linguistically diverse classrooms in which coexistence was generally positive but was periodically disrupted by teasing, peer\-group exclusion, accent\-related sensitivity, reactive emotions, and uneven use of local culture\. They valued stories, dialogue, visual media, games, reflection, perspective taking, collaboration, and social action, while also identifying risks of stereotyping, insufficient facilitation skill, and weak implementation support\. The analysis generated five design principles: behavioural translation of moderation values, plural and non\-hierarchical cultural representation, structured perspective taking, explicit safeguarding boundaries, and whole\-school implementation support\. These principles informed the provisional SADAR sequence: Siapkan perhatian \(attend\), Amati pengalaman budaya \(observe cultural experience\), Dialogkan perbedaan \(dialogue across difference\), Ambil perspektif dan refleksikan \(take perspective and reflect\), and Realisasikan aksi sosial \(enact social action\)\. The study contributes a traceable bridge from practitioner needs to instructional design rather than evidence of intervention effectiveness\. It argues that mindful learning for diverse classrooms should move beyond individual self\-regulation toward culturally responsive noticing, dialogic judgement, and safe collective action\.

## [Climate change impacts on the Mediterranean biogeographic patterns of macrofungal diversity](../publications/b8a4d485b4c32546790a.md)

Albert Morera; Kabir Peay; Juán Martínez de Aragón; José Antonio Bonet; Sergio de‐Miguel

Abstract Macrofungal diversity plays a central role in forest ecosystem functioning, contributing to nutrient cycling, plant performance, and food web dynamics\. Despite its ecological importance, spatially explicit assessments of macrofungal diversity remain scarce due to limited long\-term data\. Here, we combine one of the largest plot\-based datasets of macrofungal fruiting body abundance with machine learning models and high\-resolution climate data to quantify current and future biogeographic patterns of macrofungal alpha and beta diversity across pine forests in Catalonia, a western Mediterranean region spanning a broad altitudinal and bioclimatic gradient\. Our results indicate that climate change will differentially affect fungal communities across environmental gradients, leading to declines in species richness and abundance\-weighted diversity \(alpha diversity\), particularly at higher elevations, while the strongest shifts in community composition \(beta diversity\) are projected at lower elevations\. These changes are highly dependent on greenhouse gas emission scenarios, with severe impacts under high\-emission pathways and limited effects under mitigation scenarios\. Importantly, we show that macrofungal responses vary among ecological lifestyles\. While both mycorrhizal and saprotrophic fungi are projected to decline in alpha diversity in cooler environments, saprotrophic taxa may increase under warmer conditions at lower elevations\. Overall, our findings highlight the sensitivity of macrofungal communities to climate change and provide novel insights into how future warming may reshape fungal diversity patterns and trophic structure across Mediterranean ecosystems\.

## [Condition Knowing: A Nursing Approach to Addressing Health Injustice](../publications/b8bd12cecf9ee9f042ae.md)

Katrina Fyers; Karen McBride‐Henry; Martin Woods

AIM: To explore how registered nurses understand, use, and communicate their knowing of contemporary societal and political issues that impact the health and wellbeing of those they care for in practice\. DESIGN: The research employed a critical constructivist methodology, which presupposes that the relationship between the knower and what is to be known is a process developed through experience and shaped by interactions with societal structures\. METHODS: Twenty\-six registered nurses from various clinical and educational settings in Aotearoa New Zealand participated in interviews, focus groups and key informant interviews\. Data were analysed through the lenses of communicative action, epistemic injustice and critical constructivism\. RESULTS: The findings suggest that registered nurses&\#x27; relationship with socio\-political knowing can unintentionally support existing systems and practices\. This happens when socio\-political understanding is shaped by limited resources, institutional racism, emotional distress, epistemic injustices, and a sense of disconnection from the wider nursing profession\. Building on the interpretation of the findings, we propose Condition Knowing as an essential epistemological approach to addressing health injustice\. CONCLUSION: Nurses can rebuild the disjuncture between social and political knowing by identifying how and where nursing knowledge interests are subsumed and critiquing the influence of systematic and administrative mechanisms that disrupt meaningful practice for social justice\. Communicating meaningfully involves recognising and talking openly about the forces that shape this knowing\. This means going beyond what we know we value, who we know we are, and how we know\. It means acting as a professional group to claim agency over our socio\-political ways of knowing\. IMPACT STATEMENT: Condition Knowing involves recognising the conditions that tie, obscure and fragment nursing knowledge interests in health care systems and disrupt meaningful action for change\. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This research examined registered nurses&\#x27; understanding of socio\-political knowledge\. Participants provided feedback on the transcripts and analyses throughout various stages of the research process, as outlined in the manuscript\. This approach was consistent with the study&\#x27;s objectives, methodology and ethical approvals\. There was no further involvement from patients, caregivers, or members of the public in the research processes\.

## [Challenges and opportunities in higher education: the use of artificial intelligence in sport management subjects](../publications/b8c5267cf2b9ca14689e.md)

Jerónimo García Fernández; Ali Sevilmiş; Salvador Angosto Sánchez; Efi Tsitskari

Purpose This paper explores the effects of artificial intelligence \(AI\) on university teaching in sport management subjects\. It investigates how AI\-driven tools, such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and other generative systems, are reshaping pedagogical models, fostering innovation in curriculum design, and enhancing the personalization of learning experiences within higher education institutions\. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was adopted, involving semi\-structured interviews with 17 professors from eight European universities offering sport management programs\. Data were analyzed using thematic content analysis with AI\-assisted coding through MAXQDA software to identify key dimensions of educational transformation, faculty perceptions, and ethical concerns\. Findings Results reveal that AI enhances personalized learning, supports data\-informed decision\-making, and facilitates real\-time feedback in sport management education\. Educators view AI as a valuable tool for simulating real\-world scenarios, optimizing resource management, and improving student engagement and creativity\. However, persistent concerns emerge regarding ethical governance, data privacy, and the potential over\-reliance on AI\-generated content\. The study emphasizes the urgent need to strengthen AI literacy, ethical awareness, and institutional guidelines for responsible adoption\. Originality/value This research is among the first to examine AI integration in sport management education from a European academic perspective\. It contributes by linking theoretical insights on AI pedagogy with practical applications, highlighting the ethical and professional implications of emerging technologies in a digitally transforming field\.

## [H\-HQNN: Hybrid quantum\-classical neural network with feature selection by heuristics to predict heart failure](../publications/b8c6159e3b77df1a0121.md)

Neeraja Peddinti; M\. Sowmya Vani

Cardiovascular diseases are the most dominant cause of mortality across the entire world, claiming 17\.9 million lives every year\. According to recent trends, the mortality rate as a result of heart failure continues to increase particularly in low\- and middle\-income areas which means that early diagnostic tools desperately need to be discovered\. Conventional biomarkers like NT\-proBNP, troponins and creatinine levels are useful, although their sensitivity and specificity are low, particularly in identifying heart failure onset before it is actually clinically apparent\. We suggest addressing these issues by proposing the following Hybrid Quantum\-Classical Neural Network with Heuristics\-Based Feature Selection that can be used to predict the onset of heart failure: H\-HQNN: A Hybrid Quantum\-Classical Neural Network with Heuristics\-Based Feature Selection\. Given this, SMOTE is used to balance the clinical data and reduce class imbalance, whereas the most informative cardiac biomarkers and clinical features are selected using a two\-stage process in which Recursive Feature Elimination \(RFE\) first prunes redundant attributes, followed by a dual\-phase optimization where PSO refines the feature subset and Cuckoo Search \(CS\) enhances global exploration to avoid local minima, resulting in a compact and highly relevant feature set\. These features are then represented in a variational quantum circuit \(4 qubits\) and are implemented as ZZFeatureMap, Pauli\-Z gates, EfficientSU2, and RealAmplitudes, which are combined in a hybrid quantum\-classical neural network\. Performance was estimated using stratified 5\-fold cross\-validation on a single public dataset; external validation on independent cohorts has not yet been performed\. The average accuracy of our model is 96\.62% ± 3\.45 with precision of 96\.11, recall of 96\.10, F1\-score of 96\.54 and AUC = 0\.9604\. The most efficient fold has 98\.30% accuracy and AUC = 0\.9872 with a confusion matrix of almost perfect balance in true positive and true negative rates\. H\-HQNN is more efficient and interpretable as it achieves better discriminative power, with fewer features, compared to classical baselines \(e\.g\., Random Forests, deep neural networks\)\. H\-HQNN presents an opportunity toward novel methodology of identifying early heart failure by utilizing quantum\-classical hybrid modeling and heuristic feature selection to ensure progress in preventative cardiology and therapeutic intervention in particular where advanced imaging studies or invasive measurements of biomarkers are not feasible\.

## [Understanding anxiety disorders among Iranian mothers and their children exposed to conflict using an extended transactional model of stress and coping](../publications/b8cfde26cf2029548198.md)

Nie Ni; Zahra Osati; Zeinab Zaremohzzabieh; Seyedali Ahrari; Haslinda Binti Abdullah

Objective The psychological impact of war on families is profound\. However, the mechanisms linking war\-related stressors to anxiety among mothers and their children remain insufficiently understood, particularly in Middle Eastern contexts\. Grounded in an extended transactional model of stress and coping, this study examined the direct and indirect relationships between war\-related stressors, cognitive appraisal, coping strategies, and anxiety among Iranian mothers and their children following a recent military conflict\. The study also investigated the mediating roles of appraisal and coping processes and the moderating roles of religiosity and social support\. Method A cross\-sectional design was employed approximately three months after a major military escalation\. A stratified proportional sample of 343 Iranian mothers \(aged 24 years and older\) with at least one child aged 5–10 years living in conflict\-affected areas completed validated self\-report measures\. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS\-SEM\)\. Results The extends model explained substantial variance in maternal anxiety \( R ² = \.80\) and child anxiety \( R ² = \.72\)\. War\-related stressors were significantly and positively associated with both maternal anxiety and child anxiety\. In addition, maternal anxiety was significantly associated with child anxiety\. Challenge appraisal, problem\-focused coping, and cognitive restructuring mediated the relationship between war\-related stressors and maternal anxiety\. Emotion\-focused coping positively mediated the relationship between war\-related stressors and child anxiety\. Religiosity and social support were found to buffer the association between war\-related stressors and maternal anxiety, such that higher levels of religiosity and social support weakened the positive relationship between war\-related stressors and anxiety among mothers\. Conclusions This study extends the transactional model of stress and coping by supporting an integrated framework within a conflict\-affected Middle Eastern population\. The findings indicate distinct pathways linking war\-related stressors to maternal and child anxiety and highlight the importance of interventions that address cognitive appraisal, strengthen adaptive coping strategies, and mobilize spiritual and social resources in conflict\-affected families\.

## [Empathy shortens perceived time in association with visual attention but not physiological measures](../publications/b8d0ccbc5d7ec75c397a.md)

Soroosh Golbabaei; Mina Hosseinnezhad; Zahra Karami; Khatereh Borhani

Abstract Recent work suggests that empathic engagement can influence perceptual processes, yet its impact on time perception remains unclear\. Whereas internal clock models predict that empathy\-induced physiological arousal lengthens perceived duration, other frameworks predict the opposite\. Specifically, findings that empathy reduces perceived distance, along with motivational dimensional theory, predict that empathy shortens perceived duration\. To disentangle this, we employed an empathy\-for\-pain and duration estimation task, while measuring participants’ heart rate and skin conductance, to investigate how empathy and physiological arousal influence time perception\. Further, we measured eye\-movements to examine whether visual attention is associated with the possible effect of empathy on time perception\. Crucially, we also assessed whether these effects are modulated by individual differences in trait empathy, alexithymia, and trait autism\. Our findings show that empathy shortens estimated duration\. Despite increases in physiological arousal during empathy, arousal was not associated with changes in time perception\. Rather, greater visual attention to the eyes was related to stronger alteration in time perception\. Furthermore, trait empathy and autism quotient modulated this effect, whereas alexithymia did not\. These results provide the first empirical evidence that empathy alters time perception, elucidate the contribution of physiological and visual mechanisms to this phenomenon and extend current theories of time perception and empathy\.

## [ТРАДИЦИОННЫЕ МЕТОДЫ И МЕТОДЫ, ОСНОВАННЫЕ НА ИСКУССТВЕННОМ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТЕ, В ОБУЧЕНИИ РЕШЕНИЮ ТЕКСТОВЫХ ЗАДАЧ ПО ШКОЛЬНОЙ МАТЕМАТИКЕ: СРАВНИТЕЛЬНОЕ ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ С ТОЧКИ ЗРЕНИЯ РАЗВИТИЯ НАВЫКОВ РЕШЕНИЯ ЗАДАЧ У УЧАЩИХСЯ](../publications/b8ff1bf1d0fc8a33a604.md)

Салтанат Бахитжановна Ерназарова; Диёра Аюбханқызы Талипова

Digitalization of education creates new opportunities for mathematics teaching\. Solving word problems requires not only mathematical knowledge but also analytical skills, logical reasoning, and the ability to choose an appropriate solution strategy\. Therefore, comparing traditional teaching methods with artificial intelligence\-based approaches is becoming increasingly relevant\. This article examines traditional and artificial intelligence\-based approaches to teaching word problems in school mathematics\. Their potential for developing students problem\-solving skills is compared\. Particular attention is given to understanding the problem statement, constructing a mathematical model, and selecting a solution strategy\. The development of digital tools in mathematics education is also considered\. The study uses scientific literature analysis, comparative analysis and theoretical generalization\. The main characteristics of traditional and artificial intelligence\-based approaches are identified\. Traditional methods provide systematic development of mathematical knowledge and allow teachers to monitor the learning process\. Artificial intelligence can provide immediate feedback and adapt support to individual student needs\. However, the use of ready\-made solutions may reduce students independent thinking \. Therefore, artificial intelligence should be used as an additional learning tool rather than as a replacement for the teacher or students independent work\.

## [Content analysis of general surgery residency personal statements: implications for holistic review](../publications/b8ffd9e70f765344e230.md)

Usman Younis Panni; Tiffany K Brocke; Angela Hill; Ariana Naaseh; Catherine N\. Zivanov; Nikki E\. Rossetti; Oluseye Oduyale; Sabrya Jalal; Shinji Rho; Angela Colbeck; Maddie Houdos; Christa M\. Donald; Jennifer Yu; Paul E\. Wise

Abstract Purpose With general surgery residency becoming increasingly competitive and traditional metrics like Step 1 scores carrying less weight, there is a growing push to adopt holistic application review processes that better identify applicants suited for training\. Personal statements provide insight into applicants’ traits and experiences, but they also bring subjectivity and potential bias\. In this study, 24 distinct codes were identified from personal statements across six categories, and their variation in frequency and emphasis was examined\. Methods We performed a retrospective qualitative content analysis using a predefined coding framework that had been developed inductively\. Each statement was reviewed by two reviewers, and 24 codes across 6 categories were identified\. A comparative analysis assessed the frequency and strength of these codes by self\-designated gender and URiM status, as well as those offered an interview at our program\. Results On average, each personal statement contained ten codes\. The most frequent codes across all applicants were self\-discovery , mastery , working in teams , compassion , and responsibility \. Applicants who identified as men more frequently expressed the code of application of science to patient care \. URiM applicants more frequently expressed justice , cultural competence , and resilience \. Applicants invited to interview more frequently expressed intellectual curiosity and application of science to patient care \. Conclusions Our findings suggest that personal statements contain identifiable codes that vary in frequency and emphasis across applicant groups\. Applicants invited to interview more frequently emphasized intellectual curiosity , while URiM applicants more frequently emphasized cultural competence and resilience \. These findings demonstrate differences in how applicants communicate their values and experiences through personal statements\.

## [CAN ARTIFICIAL INFLUENCERS BE AUTHENTIC? THE ROLE OF AI DISCLOSURE IN THE AUTHENTICITY–TRUST–PURCHASE INTENTION PARADOX IN SOCIAL COMMERCE](../publications/b9029e92f9e21ee207ce.md)

 Mr\. Mohammed Saadh; Dr\. Shriram K Ms\. Swetha L

The rapid emergence of Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) in social media has introduced Artificial Influencers as a new form of digitally constructed endorser, challenging conventional assumptions about authenticity, trust, and consumer behaviour\. Unlike human influencers, Artificial Influencers are technologically created personas whose appearance, personality, communication, and interactions can be deliberately designed and controlled\. This raises an important question: Can consumers perceive an Artificial Influencer as authentic when they are aware of its artificial nature? The present study examines the role of AI disclosure in shaping perceived authenticity and explores how authenticity relates to consumer trust and purchase intention in the context of social commerce\. The study specifically addresses an emerging authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox, whereby consumers may recognise an influencer as artificial, perceive limitations in its authenticity, and nevertheless remain willing to trust its recommendations or consider purchasing promoted products\. A quantitative, exploratory, and cross\-sectional research design was adopted\. Primary data were collected through a structured online questionnaire from 30 social\-media users using non\-probability convenience sampling\. The questionnaire examined respondents’ social\-media exposure, awareness of Artificial Influencers, perceptions of AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention\. Frequency and percentage analysis were used to describe response patterns, while Spearman’s rank\-order correlation was employed to examine associations among the principal constructs\. Given the small sample size, the study is positioned as an exploratory investigation and does not seek to establish population\-level generalisation or definitive causal relationships\. The findings indicate that AI disclosure has a dual significance in consumer evaluation\. While 73\.3% of respondents supported AI disclosure always or in most cases, disclosure was also associated with increased scrutiny of recommendations and greater concerns regarding genuineness\. At the same time, 73\.3% of respondents indicated that an Artificial Influencer could be perceived as authentic under certain circumstances, particularly when communication was relatable and consistent\. However, 70\.0% reported that awareness of AI generation reduced their perception of authenticity to some degree\. Consumer trust appeared to be conditional rather than automatic, with respondents emphasising transparency, credibility, consistency, product relevance, and information verification\. Purchase intention was similarly cautious, with respondents indicating that willingness to purchase depended on the product and the credibility of the recommendation\. The study concludes that artificiality and authenticity should not be treated as mutually exclusive concepts\. Consumers may simultaneously recognise the technological construction of an Artificial Influencer, experience reduced perceptions of genuineness, and still regard the influencer as sufficiently credible to support trust and purchase consideration\. The findings therefore provide preliminary support for the authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox and suggest that AI disclosure functions not simply as a mechanism that reduces authenticity, but as a transparency cue that can coexist with scepticism\. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI\-mediated influencer marketing by integrating AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention within a single exploratory framework\. For marketers, the findings highlight the importance of transparent disclosure, credible and verifiable product information, consistent communication, and responsible consumer engagement when deploying Artificial Influencers in social commerce\.

## [AI\-Powered CRM Development for Smarter Sales Management](../publications/b91b36eb1e29ffb6caf4.md)

PAVINBALA

Managing customer relationships becomes difficult when sales teams depend on spreadsheets, disconnected communication tools, and manual follow\-ups\. A well\-planned CRM can bring customer information, sales activities, and business opportunities into one platform\. Businesses exploring this approach can learn more from this guide on building a CRM with AI lead scoring and sales predictions, which explains how AI can support lead prioritization and revenue forecasting\. Why Businesses Are Adopting AI\-Powered CRM Software Traditional CRM systems help businesses store customer details and track sales pipelines\. However, employees may still need to review records manually and decide which prospects deserve immediate attention\. As lead volumes grow, this process can become time\-consuming and inconsistent\. AI\-powered CRM software can analyze customer interactions, engagement patterns, company details, and previous sales outcomes\. These insights help teams prioritize opportunities instead of treating every lead equally\. Businesses looking for tailored solutions can explore CRM software development services to understand how custom workflows can support their sales operations\. How AI Lead Scoring Improves Sales Productivity AI lead scoring assigns a score to each prospect based on the likelihood of conversion\. The system can consider factors such as industry, company size, inquiry source, website activity, email responses, and previous interactions\. For example, a prospect who requests a product demonstration and responds to follow\-up emails may receive a higher score than someone who has only viewed a general webpage\. Sales representatives can use this information to organize daily tasks and contact high\-intent prospects sooner\. Businesses can initially use rule\-based scoring, where specific actions receive predefined points\. Once sufficient historical data becomes available, machine learning models can identify patterns from successful and unsuccessful sales opportunities\. Using Sales Predictions for Better Planning Sales forecasting helps managers estimate future revenue and understand whether their teams are likely to achieve business targets\. An AI\-enabled CRM can evaluate deal values, pipeline stages, previous conversion rates, sales cycles, and recent customer interactions\. These predictions can help managers identify deals that may require additional attention\. If several high\-value opportunities remain inactive, the system can highlight the risk and encourage timely follow\-ups\. Forecasts should be treated as estimates rather than guaranteed outcomes\. Comparing AI predictions with historical results and simpler forecasting methods helps businesses assess whether the system is genuinely useful\. Essential Features of an Intelligent CRM A practical CRM platform should include contact management, lead capture, sales pipeline tracking, task reminders, reporting dashboards, and automated lead assignment\. Email, messaging, calendar, and telephony integrations can reduce repetitive data entry\. Advanced implementations may include AI\-generated call summaries, personalized outreach suggestions, customer segmentation, deal risk alerts, and predictive revenue reporting\. These features should be introduced according to business requirements rather than added simply because they use AI\. Building a CRM Around Business Requirements CRM development begins with understanding how the sales team manages leads, qualifies prospects, communicates with customers, and closes deals\. Developers then define the data structure, user roles, integrations, reporting requirements, and automation rules\. Data quality is particularly important for predictive features\. Inconsistent sales stages, missing outcomes, duplicate contacts, and incomplete activity records can reduce prediction reliability\. Businesses should establish clear data standards before introducing machine learning\. Security must also be considered from the beginning\. Role\-based permissions, encryption, audit logs, secure integrations, and appropriate consent management help protect customer information\. Measuring CRM Performance After deployment, businesses can track lead\-to\-customer conversion rates, response times, sales cycle duration, forecast accuracy, and employee adoption\. These measurements show whether automation and AI are improving everyday sales activities\. A company can begin with essential CRM modules and transparent scoring rules, then introduce advanced predictions as reliable data accumulates\. This phased approach helps control complexity while allowing the platform to grow with the business\. Businesses exploring digital transformation can also visit Nextwebi to learn more about software development solutions for different operational needs\. FAQs 1\. What is an AI\-powered CRM? It is a customer relationship management system that uses AI to analyze sales data, prioritize leads, automate selected tasks, and support business decisions\. 2\. What is AI lead scoring? AI lead scoring estimates which prospects are more likely to become customers using available customer data and engagement signals\. 3\. Can AI predict sales revenue? Yes\. AI models can estimate deal outcomes and future revenue, provided the business has suitable historical data and consistent sales records\. 4\. How long does CRM development take? Timelines depend on the number of modules, integrations, user roles, and AI capabilities required\. 5\. Can a custom CRM integrate with existing tools? Yes\. It can connect with supported email systems, websites, communication platforms, accounting software, and other business applications through suitable integrations\.

## [Mapping the Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of fNIRS\-Gait Research: A Systematic Bibliometric and Network Visualization Analysis](../publications/b91d5321b1e2f14091e6.md)

Yunis Akkaş; Senem Güner; Naime Uluğ

Background: Functional near\-infrared spectroscopy \(fNIRS\) has emerged as an essential optical neuroimaging modality in human locomotion, yet a comprehensive computational mapping of its structural and thematic evolution remains absent\. This study provides a systematic, data\-driven scientometric evaluation of the global fNIRS\-gait research landscape across a quarter\-century \(2002–April 2026\)\. Methods: A refined corpus of 348 peer\-reviewed documents from the Web of Science Core Collection was computationally analyzed using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix\. Results: The literature exhibits a 12\.53% compound annual growth rate, shifting from stationary motor imagery toward ecologically valid overground walking\. The United States leads global outputs, supported by European collaborative corridors and Chinese national infrastructures\. Healthy aging \(27\.30%\), Parkinson’s disease \(10\.92%\), and stroke \(9\.20%\) represent the primary clinical subdomains, centering on prefrontal cortex hyper\-activation during dual\-task walking \(20\.11%\)\. Frontiers have migrated toward multimodal Mobile Brain/Body Imaging \(MoBI\) integrating virtual reality, exoskeletons, and machine learning\. However, technical integration is hindered by severe signal processing heterogeneity and unstandardized short\-separation channel regressions\. Conclusions: Establishing standardized preprocessing pipelines and short\-separation regressions may prove pivotal for transitioning mobile neuroimaging into objective, closed\-loop clinical neurorehabilitation\.

## [Tsyganov, Vladimir: Artificial intelligence, public control, and supply of a vital commodity like COVID\-19 vaccine](../publications/b92516e6767e4db96024.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 38 \(6\):2619\-2628\. 2023The article examines the problem of ensuring the political stability of a democratic social system with a shortage of a vital commodity \(like vaccine against COVID\-19\)\. In such a system, members of society citizens assess the authorities\. Thus, actions by the authorities to increase the supply of this commodity can contribute to citizens&\#x27; approval and hence political stability\. However, this supply is influenced by random factors, the actions of competitors, etc\. Therefore, citizens do not have sufficient information about all the possibilities of supplying, and it is difficult for them to make the right decisions\. Such citizen unawareness can be exploited by unscrupulous politicians to achieve personal targets\. Therefore, it is necessary to organize public control to motivate politicians to use all available opportunities in supplying\. The goal of the paper is to build such a digital mechanism of public control of the politicians by citizens, which would best assess and stimulate the activities of the authorities to improve the supply of a vital commodity\. In the age of artificial intelligence, such digital public control in the face of uncertainty can be based on digital machine learning\. In addition, it is necessary to take into account and model the activities of politicians associated with the presence of their own targets that do not coincide with public ones\. Such politicians can use the learning of citizens for their own targets\. The objective of the article is to build an optimal digital mechanism of public control in a two\-level model of a democratic social system—a digital society\. At its top level, there is the Citizen, who gives an assessment for the Politico located at the lower level\. In turn, the Politico can influence the supplying of a vital commodity\. Political stability is guaranteed if the Citizen regularly approves of the Politico’s actions to increase this supply\. However, the Politico may not use the opportunities available to him to offer a commodity to achieve a personal target\. To avoid this, the Politico’s control mechanism is proposed\. It includes the procedure for digital learning of the Citizen, as well as a procedure for assessing the Politico activity\. Sufficient conditions have been found for the synthesis of such the Politico’s control mechanism, at which stochastic possibilities of increasing the supply of a vital commodity are used\. The example of such the Politico’s control mechanism is considered on the case of supply of the COVID\-19 vaccine in England\. \(direct link \)

## [Flujo explicable para clasificar péptidos antimicrobianos con modelo pequeño de lenguaje de proteínas](../publications/b928cda01d866b425513.md)

Chavelys Fernández Quintero; Miguel Angel Fernández; Daniela Fuentes Morales; Christian David Castellanos Isern; Reydel Fanjul Evora; Daniel Alejandro Alfonso Bermúdez; Alejandro Cespón Ferriol; Daliana Cabrera Grau; Deborah Galpert Cañizares

Antimicrobial resistance has driven the development of computational strategies to accelerate the identification of peptides with antimicrobial activity\. This study designed a reproducible and interpretable workflow for their binary classification based on vector representations derived from a protein language model\. The methodology integrated data preprocessing, embedding generation with ProtFlash, training of three architectures \(multilayer perceptron, one\-dimensional convolutional network, and bidirectional recurrent network\), external validation, and explainability analysis using integrated gradients and Shapley values\. The corpus used comprised 40,358 sequences, distributed across training \(19,548 sequences – 9,767 negative and 9,781 positive\), validation \(5,125 sequences – 2,561 negative and 2,564 positive\), and test \(15,685 sequences – 10,771 negative and 4,914 positive\) sets\. During internal validation, the architectures demonstrated competitive performance: the multilayer perceptron achieved the highest Matthews correlation coefficient \(0\.8247\), while the convolutional network led in accuracy \(0\.9112\) and the accuracy\-coverage balance \(0\.9086\)\. In the external validation, the recurrent configuration demonstrated greater resilience and the best overall balance \(Matthews correlation coefficient = 0\.6506\)\. The developed workflow demonstrated that the computationally efficient representation of the small protein language ProtFlash enabled the training of competitive classifiers and, when combined with explainability techniques, facilitated a transparent interpretation of the patterns associated with biological activity\. The integration of semantic representations with deep architectures and explainable artificial intelligence modules constitutes a robust and transparent strategy for the computational screening of bioactive candidates\.

## [Impact of revised antral follicle count threshold on PCOS diagnosis: A comparative clinical study](../publications/b92b596cff4e3a4470c4.md)

Saloni Kamboj; Neena Malhotra; Reeta Mahey; Taruna Katyal Arora; Aditi Goyal; Snigdha Soni; Anshu Jyoti; Spondita Banerjee; Rintu Kutum

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical impact of the revised antral follicle count \(AFC\) threshold on polycystic ovary syndrome \(PCOS\) diagnosis\. METHODS: A retrospective cross\-sectional observational study including women diagnosed using the Rotterdam criteria, stratified by AFC: 12\-19 \(low AFC\) and ≥20 \(high AFC\)\. Clinical, metabolic, and hormonal parameters were compared against controls and amongst low and high AFC group\. RESULTS: Of 336 PCOS women, 208 \(62%\) had an AFC between 12 and 19 and would not meet the revised ≥20 follicle threshold for the diagnosis of polycystic morphology\. CONCLUSION: Excluding low AFC women may misclassify patients who require clinical care\.

## [Gestió i desenvolupament d una solució d intel·ligència artificial per a la predicció de la qualitat de frits produïts en forns de fusió](../publications/b936232b1eee1d66bb76.md)

Eduardo Gómez Fernández

\[ES\] Este Trabajo Final de Máster se enmarca en el contexto de la industria 4\.0 y aborda la aplicación de técnicas avanzadas de inteligencia artificial en un entorno industrial del sector cerámico\. En estos entornos ya existen muchos procesos en el que la disponibilidad de datos históricos, variables de proceso y sistemas de sensorización avanzada permiten desarrollar soluciones orientadas a la mejora de la eficiencia productiva y la toma de decisiones en planta\. El objetivo principal del trabajo es diseñar, gestionar e implementar una solución inteligente capaz de predecir en tiempo real si la calidad de la frita producida será apta o no apta, alineando los requisitos técnicos del sistema con los objetivos operativos y de negocio del entorno industrial\. La metodología propuesta combina la gestión integral del proyecto con el desarrollo técnico de la solución\. Se contemplan fases de planificación, definición de la arquitectura, coordinación de equipos, seguimiento de hitos, gestión de riesgos y despliegue\. Desde el punto de vista técnico, se desarrollarán pipelines de datos para la ingesta, limpieza y procesamiento de información procedente de sensores y sistemas internos, así como modelos predictivos basados en técnicas de machine learning y deep learning\. La solución incluirá una arquitectura software formada por un backend en Python y un frontend de visualización\. Como resultado esperado, se pretende obtener un sistema funcional que permita anticipar la calidad del producto en tiempo real, visualizar variables críticas del proceso y apoyar la toma de decisiones, contribuyendo a la optimización del proceso productivo y a la reducción de incidencias de calidad\.

## [Data Science for the Next Millennium: A Ubiquitous Review](../publications/b9368e658c3078ee1b2e.md)

Miss\. S\. B\. Avhad Miss\. Warale Tejasvi Narsinha; Prof\. J\. R\. Mahajan

Data science has become a practical foundation for understanding complex information and supporting decisions across modern society\. Digital services, connected devices, scientific instruments, business systems and public platforms continuously generate structured and unstructured data\. This review examines data science as an interdisciplinary process that combines statistics, computing, domain knowledge, data engineering, machine learning and communication\. It discusses the typical lifecycle of a data science project, major analytical techniques, commonly used tools, and applications in education, healthcare, business, environmental monitoring, transportation and public services\. The discussion is informed by a review of literature published mainly between 2018 and 2023, including the review by Anwar and colleagues, while also drawing on established books and methodological publications\. Rather than presenting a new experiment, the paper synthesizes recurring themes and practical considerations reported in the literature\. The review highlights that useful outcomes depend not only on advanced algorithms but also on data quality, appropriate problem formulation, reproducibility, privacy, fairness, and communication of uncertainty\. It concludes that the future of data science will be shaped by responsible automation, accessible analytical platforms, stronger interdisciplinary collaboration and governance that keeps human needs at the centre of data\-driven decisions\.

## [Attentional emotional bias in Huntington’s disease: The “Hyper\-Positive” effect](../publications/b94159bf3493e37f3010.md)

Stefania Righi; Viola Benedetti; Agnese Zonino; Gioele Gavazzi; Elena Giachi; Elena Capacci; Maria Pia Viggiano; Francesco Rotella; Lapo Pierguidi; Camilla Ferrari

In addition to motor symptoms, Huntington&\#x27;s disease \(HD\) is associated with cognitive deficits, including the ability to recognize emotions \(fear, disgust, and anger\) from faces and voices, while happiness and neutral expressions are relatively preserved\. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear\. We investigated both explicit emotion recognition and implicit attentional biases in manifest HD patients to assess whether altered attentional orienting may explain the selective deficit in negative emotions\. To our knowledge, this represents the first study of its kind in HD\. Twenty patients with manifest HD and 25 controls completed an explicit facial emotion recognition task \(neutral, disgust, fear, and happiness\) and two dot\-probe tasks \(100 ms and 500 ms SOAs\) to dissociate automatic and controlled attentional processes\. Attentional Facilitation Index \(AFI\) and Disengagement Index \(DI\) were calculated\. Huntington&\#x27;s disease patients showed reduced accuracy and slower reaction times in recognizing negative emotions \(fear and disgust\)\. At the 100\-ms SOA in the dot\-probe task, they exhibited reduced attentional facilitation for fearful faces and greater facilitation for happy faces compared with controls, with a similar pattern observed for attentional disengagement\. No significant differences emerged at 500 ms SOA\. These findings reveal a &quot;hyperpositivity effect&quot; in HD: an early automatic prioritization of positive stimuli alongside reduced attentional capture by negative ones\. This pattern, which parallels the positivity bias in normal aging, may contribute to the selective impairment in negative emotion recognition\. A plausible underlying mechanism involves striatal dopaminergic dysregulation\. Longitudinal studies in premanifest gene carriers are needed to clarify this bias&\#x27;s development\.

## [Luz invisible que revela moléculas: el papel de la radiación infrarroja en la química](../publications/b94c5fdb759f9761bbfb.md)

Fernando Ortega‐Jiménez

Infrared \(IR\) radiation is a part of the electromagnetic spectrum that is invisible to the human eye but very important for the chemical sciences\. Using IR, particularly IR spectroscopy, chemists can identify compounds, verify product quality, or monitor the progress of a chemical reaction without destroying samples\. This article provides a clear explanation of the operating principles of IR, as well as its applications in modern chemistry and its potential future developments, with examples ranging from the food industry to space exploration\.

## [Matrix‐Based Analytical Method for Failure Mode Identification and Uniform‐Failure Seismic Design of Prestressed Column](../publications/b965e72c7833ccb520e5.md)

Jian Zhong; Hao Ye; Longfei Shi; Biao Wei; Dewang Yang

ABSTRACT Resilient seismic design requires that structures exhibit excellent seismic performance and small residual deformation\. Unbonded prestressed reinforced concrete \(UBPRC\) columns, with prestressed strands serving as self‐centering components, can effectively reduce residual displacement, which is of great significance for the seismic resilience of bridges\. Compared with a traditional reinforced concrete column, the presence of prestress may change the failure mode of the UBPRC column\. To quantitatively study the failure mode of UBPRC columns, two failure modes in the complete damage state were defined, and a matrix‐based analytical model was proposed\. First, two failure modes were defined: crushing of the core concrete and tensile fracture of the longitudinal steel bars\. On this basis, the uniform‐failure state was defined as the two failure modes occurring almost simultaneously\. Then, an analytical model for the failure mode, including eight structural and material parameters, was proposed\. The failure mode can be identified by inputting the values of these parameters into the analytical model\. According to the proposed analytical model, the effects of various parameters on the failure mode of UBPRC columns were investigated\. The parameter design was carried out using transverse and longitudinal reinforcement ratios, and the prestressing force ratio as examples, based on the uniform‐failure state\. The proposed analytical model can be applied to identify the failure modes and to perform preliminary parameter design of the UBPRC column\.

## [Normative functional network localization of gray matter alterations in idiopathic generalized epilepsy](../publications/b966b7c92374e103b14f.md)

Xiang Wang; Zhipeng Zhang; Bo\-Chao Zheng; Lu Liu; Gen\-Di Wang; Hucheng Yang; Liang\-Liang Ma

Objective Idiopathic generalized epilepsy \(IGE\) has traditionally been considered a non\-lesional epilepsy syndrome on conventional MRI, yet voxel\-based morphometry \(VBM\) studies have reported subtle gray matter \(GM\) abnormalities across diverse brain regions\. These findings remain spatially heterogeneous and difficult to reconcile\. We aimed to characterize the normative functional connectivity patterns associated with reported GM alterations in IGE using functional connectivity network mapping \(FCNM\), and to explore whether these spatially heterogeneous findings show a reproducible pattern of observed network overlap\. Methods We systematically identified 18 whole\-brain VBM studies of IGE, including 111 reported peak coordinates from 1,492 participants\. Coordinates reflecting both increased and decreased GM were pooled in the primary analysis to characterize normative connectivity patterns associated with reported GM alterations irrespective of alteration direction\. Using resting\-state functional MRI \(rs\-fMRI\) data from a normative discovery cohort \(Human Connectome Project, N = 1,093\), we mapped the functional connectivity of these GM coordinates to identify a convergent IGE\-related network\. The reproducibility of the observed spatial pattern was explored using an independent, cross\-scanner validation cohort \(Southwest University Adult Lifespan Dataset, N = 329\) and two alternative seed sizes \(1\-mm and 7\-mm radii\)\. Results Reported GM alterations in IGE were associated with an observed distributed normative functional connectivity pattern involving the bilateral middle temporal gyri, bilateral thalami, left superior frontal gyrus, and right putamen\. In the HCP discovery analysis, this network showed the greatest observed overlap with the subcortical network \(overlap proportion = 42\.77%\) and secondary correspondence with the default mode network \(DMN; overlap proportion = 11\.06%\)\. Analysis using the independent SALD connectome showed a similar descriptive pattern, with the greatest observed overlap again involving the subcortical network \(overlap proportion = 43\.98%\), whereas DMN correspondence was weaker\. Conclusion Reported GM alterations in IGE converge most robustly onto a subcortical normative functional network involving the thalamus and putamen, with additional DMN involvement observed primarily in the HCP discovery analysis\. These findings provide preliminary, descriptive evidence that reported GM alterations in IGE are associated with a reproducible subcortical normative connectivity pattern across two connectome datasets, although the available analyses do not establish above\-chance or disease\-specific network convergence\.

## [Case Report: Solitary fibrous tumor \(SFT\) of cerebellum: report of 2 cases](../publications/b967d43a910548d80490.md)

Gaochao Guo; Zongzong Ma; Liming Zhao; Tao Gao; Yuxue Sun; Ziqiang Liu; Yang Liu; Chaoyue Li

Objective To elucidate the neuroradiological characteristics, clinical manifestations, and surgical outcomes of intracranial cerebellar solitary fibrous tumors \(SFTs\) to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic strategies\. Method A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of two histopathologically confirmed cases of cerebellar SFT, supplemented by a review of the relevant literature\. Results Both patients underwent total surgical excision followed by postoperative radiotherapy\. At the latest follow\-up, neither patient showed radiological evidence of tumor recurrence \(Case 1: 18 months; Case 2: 12 months\]\)\. Given the potential for late recurrence in SFTs, long\-term surveillance is mandatory\. Conclusion Intracranial cerebellar SFTs are rare neoplasms that are frequently misdiagnosed despite exhibiting distinctive magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\) features\. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses\. In this study, MRI demonstrated T1\-weighted imaging \(T1WI\) hypointensity or isointensity, T2\-weighted imaging \(T2WI\) heterogeneity, and inconsistent post\-contrast enhancement\. Immunohistochemical evaluation revealed positivity for CD34, CD99, and STAT6\. Prompt surgical intervention accompanied by adjuvant therapy was associated with a favorable prognosis\.

## [Psychiatric and substance use disorder polygenic scores are associated with the exposome in youth](../publications/b968b74470b14200c4cb.md)

I‐Tzu Hung; Nathaniel Thomas; David W\. Sosnowski; Julia W\. Felton; Ran Barzilay; Tyler M\. Moore; Elina Visoki; Nathan A\. Gillespie; Danielle M\. Dick; Brion S\. Maher; Jill A\. Rabinowitz

Gene\-environment correlations \(rGE\) present challenges for accurately estimating the individual and joint contributions of genetic and environmental influences on risk for psychiatric and substance use disorders\. The present study examined rGE between polygenic risk scores \(PGS\) for psychiatric and substance use disorders and environmental exposures \(i\.e\., exposome factors\) using multi\-level data spanning youth\- and parent\-reports, as well as objective measures of the built environment\. Participants included 4,797 genetically similar to European reference populations, 1,585 genetically similar to African reference populations, and 2,012 genetically similar to Admixed American reference populations from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development \(ABCD\) Study\. The ABCD study was conducted at 21 sites across the U\.S and used a stratified probability sampling design to ensure the cohort recruited was demographically diverse\. Based on factor\-analytic work conducted by Moore et al\. \(2022\) in the ABCD study, the exposome included 6 factors: household adversity, neighborhood adversity, positive day\-to\-day experiences, state conservatism/ruralness, family values, and pregnancy/birth complications\. Disorder\-specific PGS for psychiatric \(e\.g\., major depressive disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder\) and substance use conditions \(e\.g\., alcohol use disorders, cannabis use disorders\), as well as PGS for common liability for externalizing and general substance use disorders, were used to examine genetic associations with the exposome factors\. After adjusting for participant sex, age, log income\-to\-needs ratio, and genetic ancestry principal components, higher PGS for psychiatric \(e\.g\., broad externalizing liability, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder\) and substance use disorders \(e\.g\., general substance use disorders, cannabis use disorder\) were positively associated with household adversity and negatively associated with positive day\-to\-day experiences\. Our results indicate that polygenic risk for psychiatric and substance use disorders correlate with environmental factors in adolescence at multiple levels, most notably household adversity and positive day\-to\-day experiences\. Findings underscore the importance of investigating rGE when examining these environmental exposures with genetic risk for psychiatric and substance use disorders\.
