## [PANORAMA DA IA NA EDUCAÇÃO: DESAFIOS E PERSPECTIVAS](../publications/b96ea5b31edbad6bf371.md)

Maria Elenice Alves Pereira; Ivone Maria Alves Soares; Geane de Souza Vieira; Luseir Montes Campos; Edelma Costa de Paiva Vaz; Ana Maria Ferreira; Edileusa Francisca Machado; Bonivaldo Pedro Silva

A Inteligência Artificial \(IA\) vem ampliando sua presença na educação, incorporando novas possibilidades aos processos de ensino, aprendizagem e gestão educacional\. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar as contribuições, os desafios e as formas de utilização da IA na educação, com atenção especial à sua adoção nas redes públicas brasileiras e às iniciativas desenvolvidas pela Secretaria de Estado da Educação de Goiás \(SEDUC\-GO\)\. Trata\-se de uma pesquisa de abordagem qualitativa, de caráter bibliográfico e exploratório, complementada pelo levantamento e análise de iniciativas de IA implementadas em redes públicas de ensino\. A discussão aborda a evolução da IA, suas aplicações educacionais, a personalização da aprendizagem, o apoio ao trabalho docente e o uso de plataformas digitais\. Os resultados do mapeamento identificaram 121 iniciativas relacionadas à IA em 23 estados brasileiros, envolvendo 71 empresas e fornecedores e contratos que totalizam aproximadamente R$ 3,1 bilhões\. As iniciativas concentram\-se principalmente nas áreas de aprendizagem, apoio docente e gestão educacional\. No contexto da SEDUC\-GO, destacam\-se plataformas e recursos como Letrus, Google para Educação, Gemini, SIGE, Portal Educa e NetEscola\. Conclui\-se que a IA apresenta possibilidades relevantes para apoiar as práticas educacionais, mas sua utilização requer mediação docente, formação profissional, proteção de dados, transparência e avaliação de seus efeitos sobre a aprendizagem\. Dessa forma, a incorporação dessas tecnologias deve estar articulada às finalidades pedagógicas e às necessidades dos contextos educacionais\.

## [FIRM: Fisher\-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning](../publications/b96eb7a64bac3b2e935c.md)

Reeyansh Shah; Maram Hasan; Subhasis Chaudhuri; Biplab Banerjee

Federated LLM unlearning addresses targeted knowledge removal when forget and retain data remain distributed across private clients and are inaccessible to the server\. The resulting locally trained adapters encode conflicting objectives, making their aggregation fundamentally different from conventional federated optimization\. A key failure mode is magnitude explosion, whereby unnormalized cross\-client aggregation increases the merged update magnitude and degrades retained utility under stronger unlearning\. We propose FIRM \(Fisher\-Informed Retention Merging\), a single\-round framework for stable and retention\-aware server\-side aggregation\. FIRM uses client\-local Fisher statistics as a unified sensitivity signal to construct a Fisher\-normalized base merge and impose explicit control over retain\-sensitive parameters\. Its second\-order retention projection admits a unique minimum\-distance solution, while the corresponding dual scales with the number of retain clients rather than the model dimension\. Experiments across WMDP, TOFU, and MUSE\-HP using Zephyr\-7B and Llama\-3\-8B show utility gains at comparable forgetting on WMDP and MUSE\-HP, with metric\-dependent trade\-offs on TOFU\. Controlled comparisons support benefits of the combined base merge and additional retention correction at selected operating points\.

## [Value frameworks as federated digital platforms for digitalised road infrastructure](../publications/b9726652eed0becd004e.md)

M\. R\. Mahendrini Fernando Ariyachandra; Piranavan Sivasothy; Ashan Senel Asmone

Digital transformation of road infrastructure is accelerating, yet efforts remain fragmented by inconsistent data governance, technological silos, and weak alignment between digital investment and value creation\. Existing approaches emphasise either technical integration or high\-level strategy, leaving no structured pathway linking data quality, federated interoperability, and outcomes across the lifecycle\. This study develops and expert\-validates a Federated Digital Platform Value Framework \(FDPVF\) for digitalised road infrastructure\. The framework introduces a closed\-loop data\-to\-value hierarchy integrating two dimensions: Digital Asset Quality \(DAQ\), which operationalises data\-quality constructs for federated ecosystems, and Technology\-Enabled Metrics \(TEM\), which translate validated data into indicators of safety, efficiency, resilience, sustainability, and collaboration\. A mixed\-method approach combined literature synthesis with expert evaluation from industry, government, and academia, analysed descriptively and interpretively\. Findings show strong acceptance of the FDPVF, highlighting its potential to strengthen federated interoperability, align data governance with performance metrics, and support cross\-sector collaboration\. Neutral responses reflect implementation uncertainty rather than disagreement, signalling a need for clearer operational guidance\. Contributions: \(1\) a socio\-technical value framework integrating economic, public, and data value within federated architecture; \(2\) a governance\-aware diagnostic assessing digital asset quality and value realisation; and \(3\) actionable recommendations for pilot deployment, AI integration, and application in developing\-country contexts\.

## [AI\-Based Women Safety Clip: Literature Survey and Proposed System](../publications/b9780ba23343330edf87.md)

Riddhima Patil, Tejal Chaudhari, Vaishnavi Zambare; Prof\. S\.S Momin Sanskruti Ahire

Women&\#x27;s safety systems have increasingly used wearable devices, IoT communication, sensors, cameras, and machine learning to provide faster emergency assistance\. This paper reviews existing research on wearable women safety systems, automatic activity detection, sensor\-based monitoring, camera\-based verification, and wireless alert communication\. Existing systems mainly depend on manual emergency activation or physiological monitoring, while some recent systems introduce AI\-based detection\. However, there is still a need for a compact wearable system that can automatically identify predefined unusual activity patterns and reduce false alarms through verification\. The proposed AI\-Based Women Safety Clip uses a camera and MPU6050 IMU connected to an ESP32\-based controller\. The collected data is processed and analysed using AI/ML techniques to classify activity as Normal or Unusual\. A verification stage is used before sending an alert through Wi\-Fi to a smartphone\. The smartphone obtains GPS location and shares the alert with a trusted contact\.

## [ALGORITHMIC GOVERNANCE AND CROSS\-JURISDICTIONAL REGULATORY INTELLIGENCE: DOCTRINAL, ARCHITECTURAL, AND EMPIRICAL FOUNDATIONS](../publications/b97f38faa9626604ffc8.md)

Kostiantyn Pavroz

This study develops a jurisprudential, algorithmic, and systems framework for automated regulatory intelligence within the structurally fragmented administrative environment of the United States\. Mechanical and HVAC regulation is used as a test domain because a single field operation may simultaneously implicate federal environmental rules, state licensing regimes, county or municipal permitting, locally adopted building codes, technician credentials, and address\-specific inspection procedures\. Comparative analysis of Illinois, Texas, North Carolina, and Arizona therefore treats the United States not merely as a geographical setting, but as an empirical governance laboratory for examining how artificial intelligence can mediate rules that vary by authority, location, and time\. The analysis addresses three related problems\. First, Home Rule, Dillon&\#x27;s Rule, and state preemption distribute local regulatory authority differently across the four states, creating materially different operational pathways \(Baker &amp; Rodriguez, 2009; Briffault, 2018; Briffault et al\., 2020; Diller, 2017; Mead, 2019; Richardson, 2011; Stahl, 2024\)\. Second, the federal HFC phasedown and EPA Technology Transitions program interact with state and local code\-adoption cycles; this interaction may create sequencing gaps or administrative uncertainty, but it should not be characterized as a universal direct conflict or as a federal mandate to use one specific A2L refrigerant \(U\.S\. EPA, 2026a, 2026b\)\. Third, digitally generated compliance records require provenance, temporal reconstruction, qualified certification, and notice procedures if they are later offered under Federal Rules of Evidence 901 or 902\(13\)/\(14\); cryptographic hashing alone does not establish admissibility \(Krishnamurthy, 2025; U\.S\. Courts, 2017\)\. By combining constitutional and administrative analysis, point\-in\-polygon jurisdictional resolution, temporal knowledge graphs, constrained generative AI, human\-in\-the\-loop governance, and cryptographic provenance, the study proposes a scalable research architecture rather than claiming a completed production platform\. The U\.S\. HVAC case also provides a bridge to Metaverse governance: it demonstrates how physical territory can first become machine\-readable, then algorithmically mediated, and comparable to an electronic jurisdiction in which digital space, identity, activity, and time determine the applicable governance regime \(Kostenko et al\., 2022, 2024, 2025\)\.

## [An Efficient Approach to Beetle Damage Detection of Banana Using Deep Learning](../publications/b9829ef56b6216608e5b.md)

Md\. Mehedi Hasan Naeem; Ishtiyak Ahmmad Araf; Md\. Arefin Haque Mahir; Tushar Kanti Saha

Visible surface damage of banana fruits by Basilepta subcostata \(the banana fruit scarring beetle\) can reduce their market value\. Here, manual inspection of Banana fruits is subjective and difficult to scale\. This study presents a lightweight framework based on YOLOv8n deep learning model for locating individual bananas and classifying their visible surface condition as healthy or unhealthy\. The term beetle damage in the paper title is used operationally for the locally observed scar\-like surface condition; the model does not identify a specific beetle species or biological cause\. A custom dataset of 2,473 images containing 5,827 annotated banana instances was prepared from local\-market imagery in Bangladesh\. The reported experiment used an 80/20 protocol with 1,982 training images and 491 test images\. A pretrained YOLOv8n model was trained at 640x640 resolution for 50 epochs with a batch size of 4\. On the test partition, it achieved 81\.36% precision, 74\.30% recall, 77\.67% F1\-score, 87\.04% mAP@0\.50 and 59\.33% mAP@0\.50:0\.95\. A YOLOv8s comparison gave slightly lower F1 and mAP while using a substantially larger checkpoint\. The YOLOv8n checkpoint occupied 5\.96 MB and required 6\.54 ms/image for inference on an NVIDIA Tesla T4\. The results support YOLOv8n as a compact baseline for instance\-level banana surface inspection within the studied acquisition conditions\.

## [Automated surveillance of primary outcome reporting in clinical trials: Development and validation of a scalable screening pipeline](../publications/b98912c48f43218a3b4e.md)

Hayden Farquhar

Background: Detecting discrepancies between registered and published trial outcomes currently requires manual expert review, limiting surveillance to small samples\. No scalable automated system exists for continuous monitoring of outcome reporting integrity across the clinical trial literature\. We aimed to develop and validate an automated screening pipeline for primary outcome discrepancies and to characterise its performance at scale\. Methods: We developed an automated pipeline that retrieves trial registrations from ClinicalTrials\.gov, matches them to publications via PubMed and screens for primary outcome discrepancies using a term\-matching algorithm\. We applied the pipeline to all 46,365 completed interventional trials with posted results \(2015–2025\) and validated performance against manual expert review of 123 trial\-publication pairs, with independent large language model re\-review as a second rater\. Results: The pipeline processed 46,365 trials in under 48 h, matching 27,555 \(59\.4%\) to publications and confirming 13,595 pairs via trial identifier verification\. Automated screening classified 10,231 \(75\.3%\) as concordant and flagged 3353 \(24\.7%\) for review\. Against manual review of 123 pairs, the screen achieved 100% specificity and 16\.7% sensitivity \(1 of 6 discrepancies\); the flag’s positive predictive value could not be estimated because the validation sample contained only one flagged pair\. Independent large language model re\-review showed 99\.2% agreement \(Cohen’s kappa = 0\.91\)\. Manual review estimated a true discrepancy rate of 4\.9% \(95% confidence interval = 1\.6%–8\.9%\), predominantly minor modifications \(timeframe extensions, operationalisation changes\) rather than substantive outcome switching\. Automated flag rates were not associated with primary outcome statistical significance \(21\.0% vs 20\.6%; p = 0\.745\)\. Discussion: Automated screening can efficiently triage tens of thousands of trials for outcome reporting surveillance, deprioritising 75% of pairs as concordant and concentrating manual review on the flagged subset\. The pipeline provides a foundation for continuous, near\-real\-time monitoring of outcome reporting integrity that could be integrated into journal peer review or regulatory workflows\.

## [Phytochemical composition and acaricidal potential of Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis extracts against Varroa destructor in Apis mellifera colonies](../publications/b995163e9dccf17ddfbd.md)

Jesús Humberto Reyna\-Fuentes; Miguel Corona

The ectoparasitic mite Varroa destructor is one of the main sanitary threats to Apis mellifera colonies worldwide, prompting the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic acaricides\. This study evaluated the effects of hydroethanolic extracts from Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis on phoretic V\. destructor infestation and mite fall under field conditions\. Extracts were applied at concentrations of 10%, 15%, and 20%\. In addition, total phenolic compounds, flavonoids, condensed tannins, and antioxidant activity were quantified to further characterize the phytochemical profiles of the extracts\. The effects of these extracts on mite fall, reduction of phoretic infestation, and honey production were evaluated in thirty\-five productive honey bee colonies, which were randomly assigned to seven experimental groups, each consisting of five colonies\. Six groups received botanical treatments, while one group served as a vehicle control and received 70% ethanol without plant material\. Our results showed that botanical treatments increased mite fall and significantly reduced phoretic V\. destructor infestation compared with the vehicle\-control colonies, demonstrating a clear concentration\-dependent response\. A\. mexicana exhibited the highest concentrations of phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and condensed tannins as well as the strongest antioxidant activity\. However, plant species did not significantly affect the estimated effectiveness in reducing phoretic infestation\. Honey species did not significantly affect honey production or extract concentration \(p = 0\.088\); however, acaricidal effectiveness was positively correlated with honey production \(r = 0\.794, p &lt; 0\.0001\)\. These findings demonstrate the biological activity of the tested botanical preparations against V\. destructor under field conditions and support further investigation into their use in integrated management strategies\.

## [From Agro\-Food By\-Products to Precision Nutraceuticals: Bioactive Compounds, Molecular Mechanisms, Bioavailability and Clinical Translation](../publications/b9a68267d484ea7691d3.md)

Stefano Ruga

The valorization of agro\-food by\-products represents a potential strategy to address both environmental sustainability and the growing demand for innovative health\-promoting products\. Traditionally considered waste materials, agro\-food residues are now recognized as valuable sources of bioactive compounds, including polyphenols, flavonoids, carotenoids, terpenoids, peptides, and other phytochemicals with potential nutraceutical applications\. This review aims to provide a critical synthesis of the transition from agro\-food by\-product recovery to the development of evidence\-based precision nutraceuticals\. Particular attention is given to the chemical diversity of bioactive compounds obtained from representative agro\-food sources, including citrus, olive, grape, tomato, and pomegranate residues, highlighting their biological activities and therapeutic potential\. The molecular mechanisms underlying their health\-promoting effects are discussed, focusing on key pathways involved in oxidative stress \(Nrf2\), inflammation \(NF\-κB\), metabolic regulation \(AMPK/SIRT1\), mitochondrial homeostasis, autophagy/mitophagy, and apoptosis\. Beyond the description of biological activities, this review critically addresses the main challenges limiting the translation of agro\-food\-derived bioactives into effective nutraceutical products, including bioavailability, bioaccessibility, intestinal metabolism, standardization of extracts, variability of raw materials, dose optimization, and the gap between preclinical findings and clinical evidence\. The translational bottleneck is examined in detail, emphasizing the need for robust clinical validation and regulatory compliance\. Finally, future perspectives are discussed, highlighting the potential of emerging technologies, including precision extraction, omics approaches, artificial intelligence, and personalized nutrition, to overcome current limitations and to enable the development of sustainable, safe, and effective nutraceutical interventions\. By integrating advances in food science, molecular pharmacology, and human health research, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on how agro\-food by\-products can be transformed into scientifically validated nutraceutical platforms, supporting the development of sustainable and personalized strategies for disease prevention and health promotion\. Despite promising preclinical evidence, clinical validation remains limited: most human studies are small, of short duration, and none have evaluated hard clinical endpoints\.

## [GENERATIVE AI IN MODERN EDUCATION: ETHICAL IMPLICATIONS AND ACADEMIC INTEGRITY](../publications/b9aa397fd7981d189f55.md)

Abdusalomova Barchinoy Jo&\#x27;rabek qizi

The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has significantly transformed contemporary education by introducing new opportunities for teaching, learning, assessment, and academic research\. AI\-powered systems can generate written texts, explain complex concepts, provide personalised feedback, and support independent learning\. However, their increasing use has raised important ethical concerns regarding academic integrity, plagiarism, authorship, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the reliability of AI\-generated information\. This article examines the role of generative AI in modern educational environments, focusing on its pedagogical benefits, ethical implications, and influence on academic standards\. It explores the responsibilities of students, teachers, researchers, and educational institutions in promoting the transparent and responsible use of AI technologies\. The article argues that generative AI should be integrated into education through clear institutional policies, effective digital literacy programmes, and assessment methods that emphasise critical thinking, creativity, and independent understanding\. Responsible AI integration can support educational innovation while preserving the fundamental principles of academic integrity and intellectual responsibility\.

## [Digital Skills and Human Capital Development: Bridging the Gap in Nigeria’s Workforce](../publications/b9aa6e305ec71c0c6ea1.md)

Glory Chibuzo Agu; Kelechi Clara Anyanwu; Ogochukwu Nancy Nwedu; Kehinde Adedayo  Olajuwon

Youth unemployment remains one of Nigeria&\#x27;s most pressing structural economic challenges, persisting against the backdrop of a rapidly expanding digital economy\. This study investigates the effect of digital skills on human capital development in Nigeria over the period 2000 to 2025\. Human capital development is the dependent variable proxied by youth unemployment with specific focus on three explanatory variables: digital literacy, internet penetration, and ICT contribution to real GDP\. Annual time series data were sourced from the World Bank World Development Indicators, International Labour Organization, the International Telecommunication Union, and the National Bureau of Statistics\. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag \(ARDL\) bounds testing framework was adopted, given the mixed order of integration \-I\(0\) and I\(1\) \- established by the Augmented Dickey\-Fuller unit root tests\. The bounds F\-statistic of 9\.594 substantially exceeds the upper critical bound at the 5% significance level, confirming a stable long\-run cointegrating relationship among the variables\. The error correction term is negative and significant at \-0\.729, indicating that approximately 72\.93% of short\-run deviations from equilibrium are corrected annually\. Long\-run estimates reveal that internet penetration and ICT contribution to real GDP exert negative and statistically significant effects on youth unemployment, conforming to a priori expectations\. Digital literacy, however, exerts a positive and significant effect in both the short and long run, reflecting a structural skills\-surplus condition whereby the supply of digitally trained youth outpaces the absorptive capacity of Nigeria&\#x27;s formal labour market\. Post\-estimation diagnostics confirm the absence of serial correlation, heteroskedasticity, non\-normality, and parameter instability\. The study recommends demand\-driven alignment of digital training curricula, accelerated broadband infrastructure rollout in underserved regions, and deliberate ICT sector deepening through targeted fiscal incentives as complementary strategies to reduce youth unemployment in Nigeria\.

## [Experimental Evaluation of Retrieval Strategies in RAG Architectures Applied to the Judicial Domain](../publications/b9d4db6860c6fc2f8316.md)

Julio César Bossero

Este trabajo presenta el diseño, implementación y evaluación experimental de un sistema Retrieval\-Augmented Generation \(RAG\) aplicado al dominio judicial penal\. El objetivo principal fue analizar el desempeño del componente de recuperación semántica en un entorno completamente local, seguro y reproducible, utilizando un corpus real compuesto por 2\.592 sentencias judiciales y 46\.382 fragmentos vectorizados\. El pipeline implementado integra segmentación textual mediante Recursive Character Text Splitter, embeddings densos generados con all\-mpnet\-base\-v2, almacenamiento en ChromaDB y generación contextual con un modelo LLM ejecutado localmente\. La evaluación se centró exclusivamente en el módulo de retrieval, empleando métricas estándar de Information Retrieval como Precision@5 y Mean Reciprocal Rank \(MRR\), complementadas con análisis de similitud coseno y evaluación manual experta de relevancia\. Los resultados muestran alta coherencia temática en la recuperación, pero limitaciones en la discriminación de fundamentos jurídicos específicos, especialmente ante variaciones lingüísticas en las consultas\. Se identifican como líneas de mejora la incorporación de embeddings jurídicos especializados, técnicas de re\-ranking con cross\-encoders y optimización del esquema de chunking\. El estudio aporta evidencia empírica sobre los desafíos estructurales de los sistemas RAG jurídicos y establece un baseline reproducible para investigaciones futuras\.

## [The Dilemma of Multilateral Cooperation and Institutional Innovation Paths in Global Digital Governance](../publications/b9d8e18461277012b260.md)

Jian Zhan

The rapid diffusion of digital technology is profoundly reshaping the global governance landscape\. However, the current global digital governance system faces significant structural difficulties, including the increasing fragmentation of regulatory frameworks, the continued widening of the digital divide, and the persistent inefficiency of existing multilateral mechanisms\. This article systematically analyzes the three core dilemmas currently hindering multilateral cooperation in global digital governance\. Specifically, it examines how the supply of international rules lags behind rapid technological iterations, how strategic competition among major nations squeezes the available space for multilateral negotiation, and how the blurring of rights and responsibilities among multiple stakeholders complicates consensus\-building\. Following this analysis, the study explores feasible pathways for institutional innovation\. The research posits that, marked by the establishment of the World Data Organization, a dual governance model and modular agreement design emphasizing both rules and standards provide new institutional frameworks for breaking through the current deadlock in multilateral cooperation\. Furthermore, the concept of inclusive multilateralism offers crucial directional guidance for constructing a global digital governance architecture that is both highly representative and operationally effective, ultimately fostering sustainable and equitable digital development worldwide across diverse economic and social contexts\. By addressing these critical challenges, this paper contributes to the broader academic discourse on international relations and technology policy, offering actionable recommendations for policymakers\.

## [Phenolic Profiles of Nelumbo nucifera from Manipur Against Neurodegenerative Inflammation](../publications/b9dd88b840fadcdb2fb7.md)



Background: Natural phenolic compounds have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their antioxidant and anti\-inflammatory effects\.Neuroinflammation is a pivotal factor in the etiology of neurodegenerative disorders\.Although Nelumbo nucifera is widely utilized in traditional medicine for neurological ailments, its phenolic composition and the associated neuroprotective mechanisms are predominantly uninvestigated\.Objective: This study sought to employ ultra\-high\-performance liquid chromatography\-tandem mass spectrometry \(UHPLC\-MS/MS\) to analyze the phenolic compounds of N\. nucifera from Manipur and to assess its neuroprotective potential by evaluating its anti\-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities in BV2 microglial cells activated by lipopolysaccharide \(LPS\)\.Methods: UHPLC\-MS/MS was utilized to identify and quantify phenolic chemicals\.The neuroprotective activity was evaluated by quantifying tumor necrosis factor\-α \(TNF\-α\), interleukin\-1β \(IL\-1β\), nitric oxide \(NO\), and intracellular reactive oxygen species \(ROS\) generation\.Western blotting was utilized to evaluate the expression levels of NF\-κB p65, phosphorylated p38 MAPK, phosphorylated JNK, cyclooxygenase\-2 \(COX\-2\), and inducible nitric oxide synthase \(iNOS\)\.M1 \(iNOS and CD86\) and M2 \(Arg\-1, CD206, IL\-4, and IL\-10\) markers were utilized to assess microglial polarization\.Results: UHPLC\-MS/MS profiling revealed that the predominant phenolic compounds were myricetin \(18\.64 ± 0\.82 mg g⁻¹ DW\), quercetin \(15\.27 ± 0\.74 mg g⁻¹ DW\), and kaempferol \(11\.83 ± 0\.56 mg g⁻¹ DW\), along with rutin, catechin, gallic acid, and chlorogenic acid\.Compared to LPS\-treated cells, N\. nucifera extract markedly decreased the generation of TNF\-α \(66\.17%\),IL\-1β \(68\.32%\),NO \(68\.54%\), and ROS \(64\.80%\) at a dose of 100 μg mL⁻¹ \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\.The extract induced a phenotypic shift in microglia from the pro\-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the neuroprotective M2 phenotype by enhancing the synthesis of Arg\-1, CD206, IL\-4, and IL\-10, while significantly suppressing the activation of NF\-κB p65, phosphorylated p38 MAPK, phosphorylated JNK, COX\-2, and iNOS\.Conclusion: The results demonstrate that N\. nucifera from Manipur is a considerable source of bioactive phenolics with notable neuroprotective characteristics\.The extract reduced neuroinflammation by promoting anti\-inflammatory microglial polarization and lowering oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokine production, and NF\-κB/MAPK signaling\.These findings demonstrate N\. nucifera&\#x27;s potential as a natural therapeutic alternative for the prevention and treatment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative illnesses, offering mechanistic validity for the plant&\#x27;s traditional medicinal uses\.

## [Is Influencer Identity a Key Cue? The Sequential Process of Message Acceptance in Issue\-Based Communication on Social Media](../publications/b9dd8f1070a37983b9a4.md)

Chenwei Yang; Shih\-Chia Wu; Yushan Jiang

Despite the growing use of virtual influencers \(VIs\), their persuasive effectiveness relative to human influencers \(HIs\) in issue\-based social media communication remains underexplored\. Drawing on social identity theory and Computers Are Social Actors \(CASA\) framework, Study 1 used a 2 x 2 x 2 between\-subjects experiment and found higher message acceptance \(MA\) in the VI condition\. Perceived social closeness \(PSC\) positively mediated the effect of influencer identity on MA, whereas trust functioned as a negative mediator\. The serial pathway through PSC and trust was positive\. Study 2 found no significant direct effect of influencer identity on MA, but identified perceived humanness as an upstream mediator shaping PSC, trust, and MA\. Trust also worked as a negative mediator within competing mechanisms\. The findings suggest that influencer identity shapes MA through layered perceptual and relational processes rather than through identity categorization alone and provide practical insights for issue\-based communication\.

## [Sustainable Business Model Innovation Research: Bibliometric Structures and the Emerging Frontier of Regenerative Business Models \(2016–2025\)](../publications/b9df8e6f046452e3a85c.md)

Merzoug Fetah; Boukhatem Lakhdar; Vincenzo Basile; Yassine Remache

ABSTRACT This study presents a bibliometric mapping of sustainable business model innovation \(SBMI\) research, analysing 961 Scopus‐indexed documents \(2016–2025\) retrieved via a title‐field Boolean query and a four‐stage screening protocol\. Circular, regenerative, and resilient business models are treated as distinct, related perspectives rather than sequential stages\. The corpus shows a three‐phase growth trajectory: emergence, acceleration, and consolidation, with an overall compound annual growth rate of 24\.5%\. Knowledge production concentrates in European institutions, led by Sweden, the UK, and Italy, anchored by Lund University\. Co‐citation \(four clusters\) and keyword co‐occurrence \(five clusters\) analyses reveal a field anchored in Osterwalder and Pigneur&\#x27;s business model canvas\. The regenerative perspective remains bibliometrically marginal, appearing as an author keyword in only 2 of 961 documents\. The study clarifies the boundaries separating these perspectives and proposes a structured research agenda, positioning regeneration as an emerging, not accomplished, frontier for sustainable business model innovation scholarship\.

## [MetaEarth3D: Spatially Scalable Generative Modeling for World\-scale 3D Scenes](../publications/b9e86c08fa1782f47ac8.md)

Jinqi Cao; Zhiping Yu; Baihong Lin; Chenyang Liu; Zhenwei Shi; Zhengxia Zou

Abstract Recent generative AI models have achieved remarkable breakthroughs in language and visual understanding\. However, although these models can generate realistic visual content, their spatial scale remains confined to bounded environments, preventing them from capturing how geographic environments evolve across thousands of kilometers or from modeling the spatial structure of the large\-scale physical world\. This limitation poses a critical challenge for ultra\-wide\-area spatial intelligence in Earth observation and simulation, revealing a deeper gap in generative AI: progress has relied primarily on scaling model parameters and training data, while overlooking spatial scale as a core dimension of intelligence\. Here, motivated by this missing dimension, we investigate spatial scale as a new scaling axis in foundation models and present MetaEarth3D, the first generative foundation model capable of spatially consistent generation at world scale\. Taking optical Earth observation simulation as a testbed, MetaEarth3D enables the generation of multi\-level, unbounded, and diverse 3D scenes spanning large\-scale terrains, medium\-scale cities, and fine\-grained street blocks\. Built upon 10\.2 million globally distributed real\-world training images, MetaEarth3D demonstrates both strong visual realism and geospatial statistical realism\. Beyond generation, MetaEarth3D serves as a generative data engine for diverse virtual environments in ultra\-wide spatial intelligence\. We argue that this study may help empower next\-generation spatial intelligence for Earth observation\.

## [IntelliMirror: User Evaluation of an IoT Smart Mirror for Health Awareness and Mood Tracking](../publications/b9ed0e4b4176b5a1e9c6.md)

Marwa Ali Hamdan AL Jabri; Rasheeda Hamed Sultan ALBadi; Amani Hilal Said AL Saeidi; Saleem Raja Abdul Samad; Pradeepa Ganesan; Singaravelan Murugan

Objectives: Integrating Internet of Things \(IoT\) technologies in healthcare creates opportunities to develop intelligent, non\-invasive, and user\-friendly systems for continuous health monitoring\. These advancements can simplify healthcare\-related tasks, improve patient monitoring, and enable more personalized healthcare services\. This study presents IntelliMirror, an IoT\-based smart mirror for mood and health monitoring, which provides an interactive platform for accessing health\-related information and mood\-related conditions\. Method: The experiment is conducted in three phases, comprising a baseline pre\-survey, active IntelliMirror design and development, and interaction\. Finally, the post \-implementation evaluation\. The experiment aims to incorporate user’s needs into the design to increase the system&\#x27;s trust and usability\. Fifty participants completed the survey\-based evaluation\. The baseline survey identified user’s perceptions of the system before development, focusing on perceived health benefits, interest in mood monitoring, technological comfort, trust in data handling, and willingness to use the technology\. Findings: The evaluation results show that 60% of participants perceived potential health benefits, 70% expressed interest in mood monitoring, and 62% were willing to use an intelligent mirror in a healthcare environment\. The evaluation demonstrated generally favourable user perceptions, with positive responses exceeding 80% across the evaluated system features\. The results indicate that IntelliMirror has promising potential as a user\-centered IoT platform for integrating health and mood monitoring into an interactive smart\-mirror environment\. Novelty: This study explores user’s perception of an Intelligent Mirror before and after development\. Based on pre\-survey findings IntelliMirror was designed as a user centered IoT platform integrating healthcare and mood monitoring into a smart mirror environment\. Post\-development result indicates potential for smart technology adaptation in personalized healthcare\. However, the research needs to include technical validation, clinical comparison, and long\-term evaluation to ensure reliability and clinical applicability\. Keywords: IntelliMirror, Smart Mirror, Internet of Things, IoT Healthcare, Mood Monitoring, Health Monitoring, User Acceptance, Smart Healthcare, Human–Computer Interaction

## [Towards useful AI in remote sensing](../publications/b9f1554793dbd0f92ed3.md)

Ziheng Sun

Remote sensing has never lacked algorithms\. What it still lacks is work that travels\. Artificial intelligence and machine learning now appear in roughly half of recent titles or abstracts in International Journal of Remote Sensing \(IJRS\)\. That shift is real, and it is welcome\. However, frequency is a poor proxy for useful AI\. Useful, here, means a result another laboratory can reproduce and that an operational user could begin to apply, not a new network scored on a private split and closed with an aspirational application sentence\. A reading of IJRS titles and abstracts from 2020 to 2025, across more than a thousand papers that use learning methods, finds reuse language scarce and accuracy claims dominant\. Keep building new methods\. However, stacking methods on private datasets should not be treated as progress towards useful remote sensing AI\.

## [Des carrières linéaires aux trajectoires dynamiques : cartographie algorithmique des compétences et reconfiguration des parcours professionnels dans les organisations d&\#x27;Afrique subsaharienne](../publications/ba00b4e7f1b2874acf3e.md)

BELINGA BESSALA Jacob Patrick

Cet article élabore un cadre conceptuel théoriquement fondé reliant la cartographie des compétences par l&\#x27;intelligence artificielle à la reconfiguration des parcours professionnels dans les organisations d&\#x27;Afrique subsaharienne \(ASS\)\. Il introduit l&\#x27;Échafaudage de Carrière Algorithmique \(ECA\), défini comme le degré auquel les systèmes fondés sur l&\#x27;IA fournissent des repères de carrière structurés, visibles et portables, se substituant à l&\#x27;orientation traditionnellement assurée par les hiérarchies formelles\. Une revue intégrative \(Torraco, 2005, 2016\) synthétise quatre couches théoriques complémentaires — marchés internes du travail et capital humain, carrière protéenne et sans frontières, technologies IA\-compétences, construction de carrière et auto\-efficacité — ancrées dans des données institutionnelles de l&\#x27;OIT et de la Banque mondiale couvrant plusieurs pays d&\#x27;ASS\. Cinq propositions falsifiables en sont dérivées : l&\#x27;ECA se substitue aux repères structurels manquants \(P1\), favorise l&\#x27;orientation protéenne modérée par la littératie numérique \(P2\), renforce l&\#x27;orientation sans frontières en contexte de promotion interne limitée \(P3\), dépend de la qualité de l&\#x27;infrastructure de données \(P4\), et opère via l&\#x27;auto\-efficacité de carrière comme médiateur de la satisfaction professionnelle \(P5\)\. L&\#x27;article fournit le premier cadre conceptuel articulé, dans la littérature évaluée par les pairs, entre la cartographie algorithmique des compétences et la théorie de la carrière dans le contexte institutionnel subsaharien\.

## [HOW MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON ARCHITECTURE AND TRAINING HYPERPARAMETERS AFFECT PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE IN UAV\-BASED SOYBEAN PHENOTYPING](../publications/ba0aa58a4f23dc261816.md)

João Agostini Netto; Paulo Sousa; Paulo Eduardo Teodoro; Leonardo Lopes Bhering

Multilayer perceptron \(MLP\) models have been increasingly applied to high\-throughput phenotyping using unmanned aerial vehicle \(UAV\)\-derived multispectral imagery\. However, the effects of network architecture and training hyperparameters on predictive performance remain poorly understood\. This study evaluated the number of neurons, hidden layers, training epochs, and cross\-validation folds, as well as the performance of different combinations of these factors in MLP models to predict soybean phenotypic traits using vegetation indices\. A total of 32 soybean genotypes were evaluated over three growing seasons, generating 384 experimental plots\. Seven vegetation indices derived from UAV\-based multispectral imagery were used to predict plant height \(PH\), first pod insertion height \(FPIH\), days to maturity \(DM\), and grain yield \(GY\)\. Under the conditions evaluated, increasing network width improved predictive performance up to a plateau, whereas additional hidden layers provided no consistent advantage\. Likewise, under the conditions studied, extending training from 10,000 to 30,000 epochs improved prediction accuracy, but further increases produced only marginal gains\. Models evaluated using 15\-fold cross\-validation consistently achieved the highest predictive performance\. The effects of architectural and training parameters also depended on the biological nature of the target trait, with PH and FPIH showing higher predictive performance than DM and GY\. Overall, the results demonstrate that optimizing architecture and training parameters can improve model performance, but the extent of this improvement depends on the ability of vegetation indices to represent the target phenotypic trait\. These findings provide practical guidance for configuring MLP models in UAV\-based high\-throughput soybean phenotyping\.

## [Intensity\-Measure\-Driven Prediction of Equivalent Seismic Responses for Deep\-Water Bridge Pile\-Group Foundations](../publications/ba12c5409ee8f78ff504.md)

Xiaowei Wu

Abstract Rapid seismic screening of deep\-water bridge pile\-group foundations requires evaluation of ground\-motion intensity, site condition, water depth, and foundation geometry\. This study develops an intensity\-measure\-driven workflow for predicting responses from an equivalent dynamic model without using original acceleration time histories as inference inputs\. A subset of 461 records from 82 Next Generation Attenuation\-West2 events is combined with water depths of 30, 60, and 90 m, yielding 1,383 samples\. One acceleration realization is shared across the three depths of each record\. Its coefficients are calibrated to peak ground acceleration, peak ground velocity, and spectral accelerations at 0\.2, 1\.0, and 3\.0 s; median relative errors for all five measures remain below 0\.003%\. Twelve regression models are assessed using an event\-independent test set and target\-wise normalized metrics\. Long short\-term memory \(LSTM\) achieves the lowest complete\-input normalized mean absolute error \(NMAE\) of 0\.0090 and normalized root mean square error \(NRMSE\) of 0\.0155\. Three\-seed tests confirm this ranking, with LSTM attaining an NMAE of 0\.0101 ± 0\.0016\. The five\-measure input set lowers three\-seed NRMSE from 0\.0852 for peak ground acceleration alone to 0\.0166\. When 20%–60% of features are set to training means, the latent\-relation residual variant lowers NMAE by 1\.45%–2\.11% relative to LSTM while adding 16 parameters\. Thus, combined intensity measures govern complete\-input accuracy, whereas relation\-residual mixing provides a bounded benefit under incomplete conditions\. The labels remain limited to a linear equivalent oscillator and a parameterized foundation family\. Within this scope, the workflow enables rapid equivalent\-response screening across conditions without AT2 records as prediction inputs\.

## [Exploring the association between brief evaluation of psychosis symptom domains and HbA1c in patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder](../publications/ba1457c84a00bc6bc71e.md)

Genki Koyama; Riku Yonezawa; Masaki Nakano; Riko Wakisaka; Taketo Takata; Hiroyuki Uchida; Michitaka Funayama

BACKGROUND: Patients with schizophrenia have an elevated burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus \(T2DM\), but the relationship between psychiatric symptom domains of schizophrenia and glycemic status has been less well established\. This study aimed to investigate the association of clinical factors with HbA1c in this population, particularly focusing on Brief Evaluation of Psychosis Symptom Domains \(BE\-PSD\), a symptom scale easy to use in routine clinical practice\. METHOD: This retrospective observational study included patients aged 18 years or older with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder admitted to the psychiatric ward of Ashikaga Red Cross Hospital between April 2021 and November 2025\. A linear mixed\-effects model was fitted with HbA1c as the dependent variable, clinical factors including the five BE\-PSD symptom domains as fixed effects, and a random intercept for patient ID\. RESULTS: The primary analysis included 369 admissions of 249 patients\. Of the 249 patients, 44 \(17\.7%\) had a history of T2DM\. Older age \(p = 0\.0013\), higher body mass index \(p = 0\.028\), and greater BE\-PSD mania/excitement symptoms \(p = 0\.038\) were significantly associated with higher HbA1c\. Mania/excitement symptoms were not associated with HbA1c in the sensitivity analyses\. CONCLUSIONS: Older age, higher body mass index, and greater BE\-PSD mania/excitement symptoms were associated with higher HbA1c, although the mania/excitement association was not statistically significant in the sensitivity analyses and should be interpreted as exploratory\. Further studies are necessary to establish the relationship between symptoms of schizophrenia and glycemic status, and to examine whether BE\-PSD can help characterize symptom\-metabolic relationships in routine care\.

## [From Biomarker Measurement to Clinical Utility: Lessons From Six Established Biomarkers](../publications/ba1dda6e0a0f6db6606d.md)

Elsa Faviou; Christina Economidou; Melina E Baltogianni; Nikolaos Baltogiannis

Biomarkers are increasingly used to support diagnosis, risk stratification, therapeutic selection, monitoring, and prognosis\.Advances in high\-sensitivity assays, molecular diagnostics, multi\-omics, and artificial intelligence have accelerated biomarker discovery, but improved measurement does not necessarily translate into improved care\.A biomarker may be analytically robust and strongly associated with disease while adding little to clinical decision\-making\.This narrative review examines the progression from analytical validity and clinical association to incremental value, actionability, clinical utility, and net clinical benefit\.Six familiar biomarkers were selected as illustrative case studies because each represents a different point at which biomarker translation may succeed or fail\.D\-dimer shows how clinical context and pretest probability can transform a nonspecific marker into an efficient diagnostic tool\.Procalcitonin demonstrates that utility often depends on the management algorithm attached to the result\.Highsensitivity cardiac troponin illustrates both the benefits and the interpretive burden created by detecting smaller degrees of myocardial injury\.Point\-of\-care C\-reactive protein testing shows that clinical value does not require technological novelty\.Conversely, N\-terminal pro\-B\-type natriuretic peptide demonstrates that strong prognostic value does not necessarily validate biomarker\-targeted therapy, while cancer antigen 125 screening for ovarian cancer shows that earlier detection and stage shift cannot be assumed to improve mortality and may expose patients to downstream harm\.Taken together, these examples suggest that the clinically relevant unit is not the biomarker in isolation but the biomarker\-enabled decision pathway\.Biomarker research should therefore move beyond association and discrimination toward evidence that testing changes meaningful decisions and that the resulting strategy provides greater benefit than harm compared with current care\.
