## [Conceptualizing One Health governance for leptospirosis control through a bivariate spatial analysis of risk factors in East Java province, Indonesia](../publications/ba3153bfb4b889d9a142.md)

Forman Novrindo Sidjabat; Nanda Ferlyansin Tersandy

Objective: Effective management requires a One Health strategy integrating epidemiological and environmental data to guide intersectoral coordination\. This study aimed to analyze local spatial associations between leptospirosis and risk factors using the Bivariate Local Indicator of Spatial Association \(BiLISA\) and to develop a One Health Cooperation Map for targeted control\.Methods: An ecological cross\-sectional study was conducted across 38 regencies/cities in East Java using 2024 data\. Variables included leptospirosis incidence, climate, flooding, agriculture, and socio\-demographics\. Global Moran’s I and BiLISA were used to identify spatial clusters\. Significant clusters were mapped to construct a governance framework assigning intervention responsibilities to relevant non\-health sectors\.Results: Global spatial autocorrelation was weak, but BiLISA revealed significant local heterogeneity\. The analysis distinguished &quot;hotspots&quot; \(High\-Low\) from critical &quot;silent risk&quot; areas \(Low\-High\)\-regions where low reported cases coexist with high environmental vulnerability \(e\.g\., Sidoarjo, Lamongan\)\. Nineteen priority regencies were identified\. These findings were translated into a One Health Governance Map, explicitly linking specific spatial risks to mandated actions for agencies such as Public Works and Housing\.Conclusion: Leptospirosis in East Java exhibits distinct local clustering driven by specific determinants\. By translating statistical evidence into a practical governance tool, this study operationalizes One Health\. This shift from siloed approaches to determinant\-led collaboration enables policymakers to prioritize &quot;silent risk&quot; areas and implement targeted infrastructure\-based prevention strategies\.

## [Human Capital to National Competitiveness: Talent Management in India’s IT Sector by 2047](../publications/ba34499b1ad4ca14bc4b.md)

Anamika Sen; Prateek Verma

India’s aspiration to emerge as a developed nation by 2047 hinges critically on the evolution of its digital economy, with the Information Technology \(IT\) sector at its core\. India’s rapidly growing digital economy and IT industry have greatly increased the need for skilled employees\. Therefore, talent management has become very important for the growth of both organisations and the country\. This study focuses on the main processes of talent management such as recruitment, employee growth, employee engagement, employee retention, leadership development, and workforce diversity\. The research is based on secondary data collected from government reports, industrial reports, different research papers, and policy documents\. The study analyses the main factors that affect talent management, such as new government policies, technological changes, workforce diversity, employee well\-being, educational reforms, and the continuous need to learn new skills\. Along with this, the study also examines the role of government initiatives like Skill India, Digital India, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana \(PMKVY\), and the National Education Policy, which help in reducing skill gaps and increasing employment opportunities\. The conclusion states that effective and inclusive talent management is not only important for the growth of the IT sector but also necessary for India’s social, economic, and technological development\. A future\-ready, skilled, and continuously learning workforce will help India achieve its Vision 2047 goals and make the country a leading nation in the global digital economy\.

## [Deep\-Economic Dispatch: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Optimal Power Generation Scheduling in Real\-Time Electricity Markets](../publications/ba407fd556f41eccde8f.md)

Ekeriance Dominic Evanson; Cherukei Agbara

The increasing complexity of real\-time electricity markets and fluctuating load demands challenges traditional economic dispatch methods, which often fail to balance cost efficiency and system reliability\. This study presents a Deep Reinforcement Learning \(DRL\) framework for real\-time power dispatch, enabling adaptive and intelligent scheduling of generation units\. By leveraging state\-value and action\-value functions, the agent learns optimal dispatch policies directly from system interactions without requiring explicit system models\. The framework integrates real\-time reward signals, constraint penalties, and gradient\-based policy updates to minimize total generation costs while maintaining generator limits and demand\-supply balance\. A six\-unit case study demonstrates the model’s performance, achieving peak cost reductions of $23,780 during high\-demand periods and overall economic improvements of 10–15% compared to traditional Classical Economic Dispatch \(CED\)\. The DRL agent consistently maintains reliability at 100% across varying load conditions \(700–2010 MW\), while respecting operational boundaries and avoiding violations\. Policy probabilities adapt flexibly to changing generation requirements, ensuring both efficiency and robustness\. These results confirm that DRL not only reduces operational costs but also provides a scalable, intelligent approach to real\-time electricity market management, outperforming conventional static methods\. The study highlights the potential of integrating learning\-based techniques into modern smart grids for adaptive, cost\-effective, and reliable power generation scheduling\.

## [The use of digital tools among roofers in slovenia](../publications/ba408d6e31876636e019.md)

Anja Miško

Magistrsko delo obravnava uporabo digitalnih orodij med krovci v Sloveniji\. V teoretičnem delu so opredeljeni pojmi digitizacije, digitalizacije in digitalne preobrazbe, predstavljene so posebnosti digitalizacije gradbene panoge ter izzivi in koristi digitalnih orodij za obrtnike\. Kontekst dopolnjujeta oris slovenske krovske dejavnosti s statističnimi podatki in študiji dveh primerov dobre prakse, platforme Moj mojster in spletne aplikacije Renoto\. Empirični del temelji na spletni anketi med 100 slovenskimi krovci ter treh polstrukturiranih intervjujih s soustanoviteljem platforme Moj mojster, soustanoviteljema spletne aplikacije Renoto in takratnim predsednikom sekcije kleparjev in krovcev pri Obrtno\-podjetniški zbornici Slovenije\. Rezultati kažejo, da je najbolj uveljavljeno orodje elektronska pošta, sledijo mobilne aplikacije proizvajalcev, Facebook in lastna spletna stran, orodja umetne inteligence pa uporablja 15 % anketiranih\. Od dvanajstih raziskovalnih hipotez, razporejenih v tri skupine, smo štiri sprejeli in osem zavrnili

## [Beyond Forestry: Women&\#x27;s Multidimensional Contributions to Rural Development in Forest Villages \(Türkiye/Afyonkarahisar Example\)](../publications/ba45bbca3e6ac7f2476b.md)

Murat Köse; Emre Can Kuytu

ABSTRACT Despite growing recognition of women&\#x27;s contributions to rural development, limited evidence exists on the multidimensional factors shaping their roles in forest villages\. This study addresses this gap by examining the determinants of women&\#x27;s contributions to rural development in 26 forest villages in Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye, using survey data from 260 women\. Factor analysis, multiple linear regression, and non‐parametric tests were employed to identify key dimensions, determinants, and socio‐demographic differences\. Six dimensions explaining approximately 69% of the total variance were identified, with agricultural participation and household responsibilities emerging as the dominant contributors\. Regression results showed that women&\#x27;s contributions are strengthened by financial management, decision‐making, and diversified livelihood activities rather than forestry alone\. The findings highlight women&\#x27;s central role in sustainable rural development and demonstrate the need for integrated, gender‐responsive policies that improve access to productive resources, financial inclusion, and participation in local decision‐making\.

## [Feasibility of diffuse reflectance spectroscopy for tumor border detection in colorectal cancer surgery](../publications/ba46f051ed905949aca9.md)

Joris T\. Hepkema; Isis Boeije; Arend G\. J\. Aalbers; Brechtje A\. Grotenhuis; Marinke Westerterp; Freija Geldof; Behdad Dashtbozorg; Theo J\. M\. Ruers

Adequate distal resection margins \(DRM\) in colorectal cancer surgery are critical for oncological safety while preserving sphincter function\. Current intra\-operative DRM assessment methods are limited or have major drawbacks, leaving surgeons without real\-time guidance\. Diffuse reflectance spectroscopy \(DRS\) offers a potential solution using rapid optical feedback on tissue characteristics\. In this study, continuous measurements were performed on freshly excised colorectal specimens using a broadband DRS system \(400–1600 nm\)\. A binary classification approach was applied to discriminate between non\-tumor and tumor locations\. Multiple feature extraction strategies were evaluated in combination with different classifiers and hyperparameter tuning was performed\. A total of 39,741 spectra \(22,451 non\-tumor, 17,290 tumor\) from 86 patients were included\. Using the first derivative of the spectra paired with a radial basis function \(RBF\) support vector machine achieved good results, reaching a mean Matthews Correlation Coefficient \(MCC\) of 0\.76 ± 0\.27 across patients\. Sensitivity and specificity were 0\.93 ± 0\.13 and 0\.88 ± 0\.17, respectively\. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using DRS combined with machine learning to distinguish tumor from non\-tumor regions in colorectal cancer surgery\. Future work should focus on prospective validation of distal margin assessment and exploring probe designs with deeper penetration to enhance intra\-operative applicability\.

## [NVIDIA Stock Price Forecasting in 2025 Using a Time\-Series Based LSTM Model](../publications/ba4d0853c52c9558f9d2.md)

Sheila Nur’Aeni Afidah; Adik Nur Halimah; Febri Liantoni

Advances in computing technology, artificial intelligence, and graphics accelerators have driven significant growth in the value of NVIDIA Corporation \(NVDA\) shares over the past decade\. The high volatility and non\-linear patterns in NVDA&\#x27;s stock price require the use of forecasting methods that can capture long\-term dependencies in time\-series data\. This study proposes a Long Short\-Term Memory \(LSTM\) model to predict NVDA&\#x27;s stock price using historical daily data up to 2025\. The training process was carried out using a two\-layer LSTM architecture, Adam optimizers, and a 60\-day time window\. The evaluation results show that the model is capable of achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error \(MAPE\) of 4%, which indicates a high level of accuracy in predicting price movement patterns\. Visualization of the prediction results confirms that the model successfully follows actual trends consistently, with relatively small deviations at extreme fluctuation points\. Additionally, the model was used to project NVDA stock prices ten steps ahead, showing that price movement trends remain consistent with historical patterns\. These findings contribute methodologically to studies on high\-risk stock forecasting through deep learning approaches and provide a basis for data\-driven decision\-making in the modern financial sector\.

## [Hartwig, Tilman ; Ikkatai, Yuko ; Takanashi, Naohiro &amp; Yokoyama, Hiromi M\.: Artificial intelligence ELSI score for science and technology: a comparison between Japan and the US](../publications/ba4ef48ad1a91aaaf673.md)



\_AI and Society\_ 38 \(4\):1609\-1626\. 2023Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has become indispensable in our lives\. The development of a quantitative scale for AI ethics is necessary for a better understanding of public attitudes toward AI research ethics and to advance the discussion on using AI within society\. For this study, we developed an AI ethics scale based on AI\-specific scenarios\. We investigated public attitudes toward AI ethics in Japan and the US using online questionnaires\. We designed a test set using four dilemma scenarios and questionnaire items based on a theoretical framework for ethics, legal, and social issues \(ELSI\)\. We found that \_country\_ and \_age\_ are the most informative sociodemographic categories for predicting attitudes for AI ethics\. Our proposed scale, which consists of 13 questions, can be reduced to only three, covering ethics, tradition, and policies\. This new AI ethics scale will help to quantify how AI research is accepted in society and which area of ELSI people are most concerned with\. \(direct link \)

## [Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test\-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers](../publications/ba5ab224c36cd0f982ae.md)

Srinivasan Iyengar

A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers\. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it\. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers \(unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models\) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes\. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb\. We introduce SPLIT, which makes them from a small labelled pilot\. It rests on an exact formula for the probability of submitting a correct answer under accept/reject and top\-score selection that accounts for varying task difficulty, blind spots shared across models, and correlated repeated verifier calls\. SPLIT fits the formula by empirical Bayes and uses it to plan budgets on unseen tasks\. Across seven benchmarks spanning math, science QA, code and software\-engineering agents, 26 models, 175 agent systems and six kinds of real verifiers, all from public releases, SPLIT lands within 0\.02\-0\.8 percentage points of the best allocation in hindsight, while every fixed rule we test loses at least 2\.5 points in some setting\. Regret depends only on how well SPLIT ranks configurations, and it stays near\-optimal under compute, price and latency costs and online\. The formula also explains when asking more LLM judges lowers precision\. As a forecaster far beyond the pilot, SPLIT beats power\-law fitting when the verifier caps success, and we report where it loses\.

## [AI sycophancy, self\-interpretation, and conversational contentment](../publications/ba5cea35edb256120b84.md)

Noam Tiran

Abstract AI sycophancy is often conceptualized as a chatbot’s tendency to flout truth, accuracy, or other epistemic standards to shield users from hurt feelings, or otherwise protect them from the consequences of their thoughts, words, or actions\. In this paper, I argue against this conception\. That is, I argue that sycophantic AI behavior does not necessarily aim to protect users, nor that its harms are essentially epistemic \. There are highly prevalent cases in which sycophantic AI chatbots actively contribute to their users’ knowledge\. One class of such examples involves cases in which chatbots are used as auto\-hermeneutic technologies —as tools to facilitate the user’s interpretation of her own cares, concerns, values, and other identity components and life events\. In these cases, LLMs can help articulate the user’s avowed self\-interpretations\. In turn, avowals of these interpretations by users can often have downstream effects that render the interpretations true\. If this is correct, then LLMs can often advance the user’s knowledge regarding important truths about herself\. Simultaneously, as I explain, interpretations offered by LLMs may be deeply harmful\. This understanding of AI sycophancy can help us clarify what is so disturbing about it, as well as resist the temptation to draw too tight an analogy between sycophantic behaviors in AI systems and in humans\.

## [Confianza y juicio técnico frente a la inteligencia artificial en la formación en Ingeniería en Alimentos](../publications/ba79dca64e299cc159bb.md)

Jonathan Alexis Tapia Chamba; Odalis Kassandra Gonzalez Duarte; Jessica Lisbeth Parrales Cedeño; Belén Marín Palacios

La posibilidad de evaluar las respuestas que la inteligencia artificial generativa entrega ante una solicitud exige un examen de sus fundamentos y suficiencia mediante conocimientos disciplinares que los estudiantes todavía están consolidando\. En torno a lo anterior, el objetivo del presente estudio fue analizar la asociación entre la capacidad autopercibida para evaluar estas respuestas y el acierto al clasificarlas, en estudiantes de Ingeniería en Alimentos de la Universidad Técnica Estatal de Quevedo, Ecuador\. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, transversal y descriptivo\-correlacional, con muestreo no probabilístico por accesibilidad\. Participaron 127 estudiantes de cuarto a décimo semestre; el análisis principal incluyó 125 registros completos\. El cuestionario, administrado presencialmente mediante Google Forms, reunió cinco ítems de autopercepción, cinco casos alimentarios y la primera acción declarada ante cada respuesta\. El desempeño se puntuó por coincidencia exacta con una clave técnica\.

## [Building a domain\-specific large language model for Chinese ancient books: a case study on epitaph modelling](../publications/ba7f48442847e4c09475.md)

Minjie Yu; Haoyue Jin; Shiliang Xue

Introduction\. With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence technology, large language models \(LLMs\) are expected to play an important role in improving access to and the use of library collections\. This study constructs and develops a generative conversational large language model tailored specifically to epitaphs, overcoming traditional research paths and systems of digitisation\. Method\. Based on the Chinese epitaph database built by the Zhejiang University Library and some commercial epitaph databases, an epitaph generative dialogue large language model was constructed using Doubao as the base model through pre\-training, supervised fine\-tuning, and other full process trainings\. Analysis\. This study used human evaluation, in which experts, researchers, or general users assessed the quality of model\-generated outputs\. The evaluation included the epitaphs of Cui Yi, Liu Yi, and Lihua in the Tang dynasty\. Results\. The model successfully performed intelligent interpretation of epitaphs, automatic information extraction, and other knowledge\-based services, thereby providing new ideas for constructing an ancient literature corpus from excavated materials represented by epitaphs\. Conclusion\. A large\-scale domain\-specific foundational model tailored for library applications was successfully developed\. The study offers innovative approaches for processing historical texts and suggests new directions for AI integration in library knowledge systems\.

## [Experimental Comparison of Tire Tread Wear Performance on Conventional and Electric Vehicles under Controlled Road Conditions](../publications/ba8ff8fe73a0b05dca3e.md)

Melih GELBAL; Mustafa Umut Karaoğlan

The replacement of internal combustion engine \(ICE\) with electric motor by electric vehicles \(EVs\) technology is one of the most comprehensive transition in the automotive industry for recent decades\. EVs technology causes fundamental changes in vehicle architecture and dynamics including increased overall weight due to battery packs, altered torque delivery, and regenerative braking systems\. These changes have significant implications on tires because of the direct interaction of vehicle and road\. Therefore, tire performance characteristics are influenced by the type of powertrain\. According to the distinctive operating conditions of EVs comparing with the conventional vehicles, determination of the tire tread wear behavior has become a critical challenge for tires\. The higher mass and unique driving characteristics of EVs cause fast and unevenly distributed tire wear\. This study aims to evaluate the investigation of passenger car tire tread wears for conventional and electric vehicles under controlled road testing\. Four commercially available tires are selected for the tests using conventional vehicles on Route\-1 and EV testing on Route\-2\. Key indicators such as average tread depth reduction, wear uniformity, and wear pattern distribution are measured to assess the impact of vehicle type\. The results indicate that EVs consistently impose higher tread wear than conventional vehicles\. For the tested tire specifications, tread\-wear\-based mileage on electric\-vehicle platforms was markedly lower than on conventional platforms, with the strongest reduction observed on the front axle\. Depending on tire type, the estimated mileage reduction from ICE to EV ranged from approximately 35 % to 62 %\. The findings indicate that the combined effect of higher vehicle mass, instantaneous torque delivery and regenerative braking intensifies wear severity and front/rear imbalance, especially under urban and stop\-go EV duty cycles\. These results support the need for EV\-oriented tire compounds, axle\-specific design strategies and validation procedures that reflect route severity and real operating conditions\.

## [Artificial Intelligence Capabilities and Organizational Sustainability of Retail Outlets in Port Harcourt: A Drive for Renewable Hope in Smart Economies](../publications/ba9030f5f90d69cdea62.md)

Happiness Nwanyi Elekwachi; Blessing Onwuanaku; Ibim Taribo Amachree

The study examined artificial intelligence capabilities and organizational sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt\. The objectives of the study were to examine the relationship between dimensions of artificial intelligence capabilities such as CCTV analytics, chatbots and automated processing; and measures of organizational sustainability in terms of Environmental sustainability and Economic sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt\. Thus, the study was anchored on Diffusion of Innovation theoretical foundation\. The study adopted the cross\-sectional survey research design\. The accessible population of the study was Sixteen \(16\) retail outlets currently operating in Port Harcourt\. The entire population was used as the study sample\. Thus, the study was census research which involves using the entire population rather than drawing a sample from it\. Structured questionnaire served as the instrument for data collection\. A total of sixty\-four \(64\) copies of the validated questionnaire were distributed to the targeted audience\. The researcher was able to retrieve fifty\-six \(56\) copies of the entire validated questionnaire distributed\. Arithmetic mean and standard deviation were used for the research question analyses, while the test of hypotheses was done using Spearman rank order correlation with the aid of SPSS Version 24\.0\. It was found that there is a significant positive relationship between artificial intelligence capabilities and organizational sustainability of retail outlets in Port Harcourt\. It was concluded that leveraging artificial intelligence powered tools such as CCTV analytics, chatbots and automated processing, retailers can enhance operational efficiency, improve customer experiences and gain valuable insights into market trends\. Consequently, it was recommended that operators of retail outlets should utilize automated system to track inventory level, reduce waste and optimize stock replenishment\.

## [Kamera Görüntülerinde Sigara Tespiti için SAHI Destekli YOLO Tabanlı Model Seçimi ve Sabah Saatleri İçin Zaman Bazlı Senaryo Analizi](../publications/ba9314378b8f67bfaa2b.md)

Bedirhan Bedir; Gökalp Tulum

Bu çalışmada, kamera görüntülerinden sigara tespitine yönelik olarak senaryo temelli bir veri düzeni, çok aşamalı model seçimi ve SAHI \(Slicing Aided Hyper Inference\) destekli çıkarım yaklaşımı birlikte değerlendirilmiştir\. Çalışmanın çıkış noktası, sigaranın görüntü içinde çoğu zaman küçük ve ince bir nesne olarak yer alması, buna ek olarak çekim ortamının çok sayıda pencere, koruma demiri, demir yüzeylerin ortama yakın renkleri ve gün içinde değişen ışık koşulları nedeniyle zorlayıcı bir yapıda olmasıdır\. Bu nedenle yalnızca tek bir model sonucu raporlamak yerine, önce temel YOLO tabanlı karşılaştırma yapılmış, daha sonra küçük nesne görünürlüğünü artırmak amacıyla SAHI ile ikinci bir karşılaştırma yürütülmüş, ardından seçilen aday modeller daha uzun çevrimlerde yeniden değerlendirilmiştir\. Veri yapısı kamuya açık veri ile araştırmacı tarafından oluşturulan yerel verinin birlikte kullanıldığı bir düzende kurulmuştur\. Yerel veri tarafında 4\.060 sigara içeren görüntü, 3\.840 yalnızca ortamı gösteren görüntü, yanlış alarm üretmeye yatkın 1\.954 görüntü, 2\.178 farklı kişi odaklı pozitif görüntü ve 1\.542 kişi odaklı yanlış alarm örneği kullanılmıştır\. Çalışma senaryo bazlı tasarlanmış, zaman ekseninde ise sabah saatleri 09\.00–14\.00 aralığı ana değerlendirme bölgesi olarak belirlenmiştir\. Temel YOLO karşılaştırmasında YOLO11m ve YOLO8m öne çıkmış; SAHI destekli ikinci aşamada da YOLO11m en yüksek başarıyı sürdürmüştür\. Daha uzun çevrimli değerlendirmeler ve Optuna ile yapılan ayar iyileştirmesi sonunda nihai aday yine YOLO11m olmuştur\. Saat bazlı sonuçlarda 11\. saat en güçlü, 14\. saat ise en zayıf aralık olarak belirlenmiştir\. Örnek çerçeveler üzerinden yapılan kutu düzeyi doğrulama, performanstaki bozulmanın yalnızca kutu yerleşiminden değil, bazı saatlerde adayın yeterince bulunamamasından da kaynaklandığını göstermiştir\. Ayrıca yanlış alarm incelemesi, ayar sıkılaştırması ile belirgin bir iyileşme elde edildiğini, ancak yanlış alarm probleminin tamamen ortadan kalkmadığını ortaya koymuştur\. Elde edilen bulgular, sigara tespitinin yalnızca bir nesne bulma problemi olarak değil, çevresel koşullardan ve zaman bazlı değişkenlikten etkilenen bütüncül bir izleme problemi olarak ele alınması gerektiğini göstermektedir\.

## [A Combined Molecular Dynamics and Experimental Study on the Processing and Property Modification of UHMWPE / HDPE Blends by CaSt 2](../publications/baa46ec096d66a14adfe.md)

Jie Liu; Ning Han; Gonghao Wang; Shengxue Qin

ABSTRACT High melt viscosity limits the processability of ultra‐high‐molecular‐weight polyethylene \(UHMWPE\)\. Here, UHMWPE/high‐density polyethylene \(HDPE\) blends modified with calcium stearate \(CaSt 2 \) were studied by combined molecular dynamics \(MD\) simulation and experiment\. MD results show that 0\.5 wt% CaSt 2 maximizes the fractional free volume and diffusion coefficient, with increases of 8\.06% and 27\.17%, respectively\. Interaction strength increases monotonically with CaSt 2 content, while chain mobility peaks at 0\.5 wt%, indicating that excessive interactions restrict segmental motion at higher loading\. Experimentally, CaSt 2 increases the melt flow rate by 23\.53%, reduces processing torque, improves extrusion stability, and increases tensile strength and crystallinity by 4\.01% and 5\.18%, respectively\. These results show that appropriate CaSt 2 incorporation improves melt processability while maintaining mechanical performance\.

## [Artificial Intelligence for Net\-Zero and Climate\-Resilient Sustainable Cities: Technologies, Challenges, and Future Perspectives](../publications/baa7892b4ee36c8a6fd4.md)

Rakesh Ashok Afre; Bhavana B\. Thakre; Radha Panchal; Sandhyatai Kadam

Urbanization, climate change, increasing energy demand, and rapid infrastructure development have created significant challenges for achieving sustainable and resilient cities\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) has emerged as a transformative technology that enables data\-driven decision\-making, intelligent automation, and efficient resource management, making it an important enabler of net\-zero and climate\-resilient urban systems\. This narrative review examines AI applications relevant to urban climate mitigation and adaptation, drawing on literature identified through Google Scholar and ScienceDirect\. The review examines the role of machine learning, deep learning, Internet of Things \(IoT\), big data analytics, cloud computing, digital twins, and generative AI in improving urban energy systems, sustainable transportation, environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, and smart governance\. The study also discusses how these technologies contribute to carbon emission reduction, renewable energy integration, climate adaptation, disaster preparedness, and efficient urban planning\. In addition, major challenges associated with AI implementation are critically analyzed, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, lack of interoperability, high energy consumption of AI systems, digital inequality, and governance issues\. Emerging research trends such as explainable AI, green AI, AI\-enabled digital twins, federated learning, and human\-centered smart governance are highlighted as important directions for future research\. Based on the reviewed literature, the study proposes future research priorities that emphasize interdisciplinary collaboration, responsible AI governance, standardized urban data frameworks, and sustainable policy development\. Overall, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition toward intelligent, low\-carbon, and climate\-resilient cities\. The synthesis is qualitative and non\-exhaustive, with limitations arising from unavailable original search and screening records and differences between study settings and outcome measures\. However, the successful implementation of AI will depend on integrating technological innovation with ethical governance, public participation, and long\-term sustainability planning to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals\.

## [Biossegurança em hospitais materno\-infantis: desafios e perspectivas](../publications/baab5c5a59751ba09c56.md)

Thais Cardoso Guerra; Higor Luan Silva Almeida; Maísa Miranda Coutinho; Natália Ferrini Laviola Pereira; Clara Mônica Figueredo de Lima; Israel Souza Ribeiro; William Rodrigues de Freitas

O objetivo do presente estudo foi analisar os desafios e as perspectivas da biossegurança em hospitais materno\-infantis, enfatizando a aplicação prática de normas, infraestrutura, resistência microbiana e a influência da cultura organizacional\. Revisão integrativa realizada na base de dados LILACS, na Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde e na biblioteca eletrônica SciELO, contemplando publicações de 2015 a 2025, tendo sido incluídos quatro estudos após aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade\. Considerando artigos científicos e documentos oficiais que abordam barreiras e estratégias para implementação de práticas de segurança\. Foram identificados obstáculos como infraestrutura insuficiente, falta de treinamento contínuo e aumento da resistência antimicrobiana em ambientes hospitalares\. A análise destaca a importância da modernização da infraestrutura, do investimento em tecnologias inovadoras e da capacitação profissional contínua como medidas essenciais para a prevenção de infecções relacionadas à assistência à saúde\. Além disso, enfatiza\-se o papel central da cultura organizacional no fortalecimento das práticas de segurança, bem como a necessidade de programas de gestão de antimicrobianos, melhorias nos sistemas de ventilação e descontaminação e políticas públicas eficazes\. Portanto, a biossegurança em hospitais materno\-infantis requer uma abordagem multidisciplinar, integrando educação continuada, infraestrutura adequada e protocolos específicos\. O fortalecimento da cultura de segurança, juntamente com o investimento em tecnologia e treinamento, é fundamental para garantir um ambiente hospitalar seguro para pacientes e profissionais\. Palavras\-chave: Arquitetura hospitalar\. Cultura organizacional\. Segurança do paciente\. Serviços de saúde materno\-infantil\. Abstract: The objective of this study was to analyze the challenges and perspectives regarding biosafety in maternal and child hospitals, emphasizing the practical application of standards, infrastructure, microbial resistance, and the influence of organizational culture\. An integrative review was conducted using the LILACS, Virtual Health Library, and SciELO databases, covering publications from 2015 to 2025; four studies were included after applying eligibility criteria\. The review considered scientific articles and official documents addressing barriers to and strategies for implementing safety practices\. Obstacles identified included insufficient infrastructure, a lack of continuous training, and rising antimicrobial resistance in hospital settings\. The analysis highlights the importance of infrastructure modernization, investment in innovative technologies, and continuous professional training as essential measures for preventing healthcare\-associated infections\. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the pivotal role of organizational culture in strengthening safety practices, as well as the need for antimicrobial stewardship programs, improvements in ventilation and decontamination systems, and effective public policies\. Therefore, biosafety in maternal and child hospitals requires a multidisciplinary approach that integrates continuing education, adequate infrastructure, and specific protocols\. Strengthening the safety culture, combined with investment in technology and training, is fundamental to ensuring a safe hospital environment for both patients and healthcare professionals\. Keywords: Hospital architecture\. Organizational culture\. Patient safety\. Maternal\-child health services\. Resumen: El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los desafíos y perspectivas en materia de bioseguridad en hospitales materno\-infantiles, haciendo hincapié en la aplicación práctica de normas, la infraestructura, la resistencia microbiana y la influencia de la cultura organizacional\. Se realizó una revisión integradora utilizando la base de datos LILACS, la Biblioteca Virtual en Salud y SciELO, abarcando publicaciones desde 2015 hasta 2025; se incluyeron cuatro estudios tras aplicar los criterios de elegibilidad\. La revisión consideró artículos científicos y documentos oficiales que abordaban las barreras y estrategias para la implementación de prácticas de seguridad\. Entre los obstáculos identificados se encuentran la infraestructura insuficiente, la falta de capacitación continua y el aumento de la resistencia a los antimicrobianos en el entorno hospitalario\. El análisis destaca la importancia de la modernización de la infraestructura, la inversión en tecnologías innovadoras y la capacitación profesional continua como medidas esenciales para prevenir las infecciones asociadas a la atención de salud\. Asimismo, el estudio subraya el papel fundamental de la cultura organizacional en el fortalecimiento de las prácticas de seguridad, así como la necesidad de programas de uso racional de antimicrobianos, mejoras en los sistemas de ventilación y descontaminación, y políticas públicas eficaces\. Por tanto, la bioseguridad en los hospitales materno\-infantiles requiere un enfoque multidisciplinario que integre la educación continua, una infraestructura adecuada y protocolos específicos\. Fortalecer la cultura de seguridad, junto con la inversión en tecnología y capacitación, resulta fundamental para garantizar un entorno hospitalario seguro tanto para los pacientes como para los profesionales de la salud\. Palabras clave: Arquitectura hospitalaria\. Cultura organizacional\. Seguridad del paciente\. Servicios de salud materno\-infantil\.

## [Development and validation of a minimum data set for a male sexual health assessment registry system](../publications/bab75319432f2b39cb52.md)

Mohsen Shafiee; Alireza Baghrobehbahani; Noorollah Tahery; Zahra Asghari Varzaneh; Hadi Kazemi\-Arpanahi

Men’s sexual health is an important aspect of public health that requires focused attention and thorough analysis\. A comprehensive evaluation must consider various health issues from multiple perspectives\. Clinical registries are vital for tracking male sexual health and follow\-up data; however, the absence of a standardized data collection tool hinders the systematic documentation of male sexual health from an information management standpoint\. As a result, the data collected often lacks comparability, which limits the generalizability of the findings\. This study aims to develop a minimum data set \(MDS\) as an initial step toward creating a male sexual health registry\. This study was conducted from January 8, 2024, to March 20, 2025, using a multi\-phased approach\. We began by compiling a list of potential data items through a search of scientific databases, a review of grey literature, and an examination of existing information systems, forms, and websites related to male sexual health\. Next, we applied a modified Delphi technique, which involved a two\-round survey with a panel of 27 experts in clinical practice and research focused on male sexual health\. These experts rated the importance of each candidate data item for inclusion in the MDS using afour\-point Likert scale\. Items that received an agreement level of 80% or higher were accepted for inclusion in the final MDS\. Finally, we evaluated the content validity of the developed MDS using the content validity ratio \(CVR\) and the content validity index \(CVI\) criteria\. The finalized MDS for male sexual health assessment comprises 105 items, organized into six distinct categories, including sociodemographic factors, relationship status, sexual behaviors and functions, awareness of sexual self\-examination, sexual protective behaviors, and clinical history\. This MDS is developed to assist registry designers and administrators in selecting the necessary data items for a male sexual health assessment registry system\. Its purpose is to facilitate the design and implementation of a standardized registry and support the systematic collection of high\-quality data\. The MDS may also provide a useful foundation for improving the availability and consistency of information relevant to male sexual health care\. However, further research is needed to evaluate its implementation, feasibility, and potential impact on clinical decision\-making and quality of care\.

## [R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self\-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self\-Play within a Skill\-Internalization Loop](../publications/babb9a9e204915f4d6b6.md)

Mingda Zhang; Yun Huang; Qiang Huang; Yanjin Li; Rui Qian; Qichao Zhao; Tiesunlong Shen; Na Zhao; Jian Wang; Xiaoying Tang

In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks\. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand\-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task&\#x27;s rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score\. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self\-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self\-play that improves the orchestrator on self\-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves\. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn\. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self\-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it\. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero\-skill deployment\. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks\.

## [Verification of the breeding periods of two clawed salamander species \(Onychodactylus koreanus and O\. sillanus\) using environmental DNA analysis and field surveys](../publications/babfb1b36d34b0b487b8.md)

Daesik Park; Jaejin Park; Jongsun Kim; Jiho Park; 주나래; Hahyun Nam; Jaebeom Jeong; Young\-Guk Kim; Min\-Woo Park

Determining the breeding frequencies and breeding periods of species that spend part or all of their lives underground is challenging because of limited population surveys\. Environmental DNA \(eDNA\) analysis can be performed to address this issue\. eDNA analysis and population surveys were combined to verify and compare the breeding frequencies and breeding periods of Onychodactylus koreanus and O\. sillanus in mountain valley streams, which are their typical habitats in the Republic of Korea, between April 2024 and May 2025\. Both species externally fertilize their eggs\. Adult O\. koreanus appeared at the sites during two periods, from April to June and from October to early December, whereas adult O\. sillanus was not detected despite similar survey efforts\. eDNA concentrations detected in the upper, middle, and lower streams differed; however, the major eDNA detection patterns were largely consistent\. In O\. koreanus , two major eDNA detections occurred in early May and early December, whereas in O\. sillanus , eDNA detections occurred between January and June\. These results suggest that the two species have different breeding frequencies and breeding periods\. However, whether these differences are species\- or habitat\-specific needs to be further explored\.

## [Composition\-Controlled Hydrogen\-Bond Restructuring and Interfacial Transport in Glycerol–Ethanol Mixtures for Orange Essential Oil Separation: Experiments and Multiscale Modeling](../publications/bac03e3f3b0116cb27da.md)

Guoxiao Cai; Ruiyao Zhang; Fuqiang Qiu; Wei Xiong; Songlin Zhou; Fang Hao; Chang Yi Kong

Abstract Hydrogen\-bonded glycerol–ethanol \(Gly–EtOH\) mixtures are promising biodiesel\-derived solvents for orange essential oil \(OEO\) separation\. However, how solvent composition governs equilibrium and transport properties and selectivity remains unclear\. We combined rotational rheometry, ReaxFF molecular dynamics \(ReaxFF\-MD\), density functional theory \(DFT\), COSMO\-RS, Redlich–Kwong equation of state \(RK EoS\), and machine learning to establish structure–property–separation relationships\. ReaxFF\-MD and RK EoS reproduced the composition\-dependent density behavior with AARDs of 4\.6% and 2\.0%, respectively\. Rheometry validated the ReaxFF\-MD\-predicted decrease in viscosity with increasing ethanol content\. ReaxFF\-MD and DFT reveal that ethanol reorganizes the glycerol\-dominated hydrogen\-bond network by altering O···O coordination and O···H correlations, while COSMO\-RS reveals a composition\-dependent shift toward weakly polarized surface segments\. Polynomial ridge regression and Gaussian process regression were used to interpolate density and viscosity, respectively\. Source\-separated and grouped cross\-validation showed that composition interpolation was more reliable than prediction at a completely unseen temperature\. Interfacial MD simulations further indicate that solute–solvent affinity, interfacial organization, and diffusivity contrast jointly govern linalool enrichment, with the highest simulated selectivity at x1 = 0\.5\. These findings establish a composition\-controlled mechanism connecting hydrogen\-bond restructuring, bulk transport, and interfacial separation, enabling rational design of sustainable biomass\-derived solvents\.

## [Evaluation of psychosocial benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients](../publications/bad5104476182af09620.md)

Vipin Chandra; Ramakant Dixit; Manudev Mehta; Mukesh Goyal

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \(COPD\) is associated with significant symptom burden, impaired quality of life, and psychosocial morbidity\. Pulmonary rehabilitation \(PR\) is a recommended non\-pharmacological intervention, but evidence focusing on its psychosocial benefits remains limited\. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of hospital\-based outpatient PR on psychosocial parameters and health\-related quality of life in patients with COPD receiving standard pharmacotherapy\. This before\-after interventional study included 50 male patients with stable COPD who underwent a structured outpatient PR program for 24 weeks in addition to standard medical therapy\. Assessments were performed at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks\. Psychosocial outcomes were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale \(HADS\), and quality of life was assessed using the COPD Assessment Test \(CAT\) and the St\. George&\#x27;s Respiratory Questionnaire\-COPD\-specific version \(SGRQ\-C\)\. Statistical analysis was performed with significance set at p&lt;0\.05\. PR led to significant improvements in psychosocial and quality\-of\-life outcomes\. Mean HADS anxiety and depression scores showed significant reductions at 12 and 24 weeks compared to baseline \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. Quality\-of\-life scores improved significantly, with reductions in CAT and SGRQ\-C scores at follow\-up \(p&lt;0\.001\)\. A marked reduction in COPD exacerbations and hospital admissions was also observed during the study period\. Hospital\-based outpatient PR significantly improves psychosocial well\-being and health\-related quality of life while reducing morbidity in patients with COPD, supporting its routine integration into comprehensive COPD care\.

## [Piceatannol enhances polymyxin B efficacy against Escherichia coli O157:H7 via inhibition of biofilm formation](../publications/bad8c1dc604bd98ae13d.md)

Jing Xu; Yaxin Zhou; Wenkui Bao; Zhanqing Ma; Zixuan Shang; Hongxing Zhang; Weiwei Wang; Bing Li; Yubin Bai; Jiyu Zhang

Introduction Escherichia coli O157:H7 \( E\. coli O157 \) poses a severe global health threat, particularly due to its ability to form recalcitrant biofilms and the paradoxical exacerbation of life‑threatening haemolytic uraemic syndrome by conventional antibiotics\. This study identifies piceatannol as an effective agent that suppresses E\. coli O157 biofilm formation in vitro and acts as an adjuvant to enhance antimicrobial efficacy\. Methods The effects of piceatannol on biofilm formation, swarming motility, and exopolysaccharide \(EPS\) and protein production were evaluated in vitro \. Pharmacological screening identified an effective combination with polymyxin B, which was validated in a murine infection model by assessing bacterial loads in visceral organs \(liver and spleen\), ileal villous morphology, and survival rates\. Results Piceatannol suppressed biofilm formation by inhibiting swarming motility and reducing EPS and protein production, thereby weakening biofilm integrity and enhancing antimicrobial efficacy\. In vivo , the piceatannol–polymyxin B combination reduced bacterial loads in visceral organs, restored ileal villous morphology, and improved survival more effectively than monotherapy\. Discussion These findings establish piceatannol as an effective adjuvant that enhances polymyxin B efficacy against E\. coli O157\. By disrupting biofilm integrity and sensitizing bacteria to polymyxin B, the piceatannol–polymyxin B combination represents a promising strategy for treating E\. coli O157 infections\.

## [A dynamic pyramidal model of teaching excellence in higher education: a critical analytical reflection](../publications/bada34cdc1329b8dabca.md)

Ariel Torres; Paloma González; Gisselle Trujillo; Mario Alomía; Martha Fors

Teaching excellence in higher education is often conceptualized through isolated dimensions such as instructional quality, assessment practices, or technological integration\. However, these approaches may overlook the dynamic and interdependent nature of educational processes\. This study presents a critical analytical reflection aimed at synthesizing high\-level evidence and proposing an integrative conceptual model of teaching excellence\. An interpretative synthesis was conducted using 35 high\-level studies \(systematic reviews, meta\-analyses, umbrella reviews, and scoping reviews\) published between 2015 and 2025, complemented by five international policy reports\. The analysis followed a thematic and iterative approach supported by an analytical matrix, coding procedures, and conceptual triangulation\. The findings reveal convergence across five interrelated dimensions: teacher–student interaction, higher\-order cognitive processes, pedagogical strategies, formative and authentic assessment, and digital technologies\. These dimensions are conceptualized as interconnected elements embedded within teaching and learning processes rather than as independent components\. Based on this convergence, the study proposes the Dynamic Pyramidal Model of Teaching Excellence, which conceptualizes excellence as an integrative construct organized through the interaction and alignment of multiple educational dimensions\. The model integrates relational, cognitive, pedagogical, evaluative, technological, contextual, and individual factors within a dynamic system characterized by continuous feedback\. The proposed framework integrates dimensions commonly addressed separately in the literature and provides a conceptual basis for future empirical validation across diverse higher\-education contexts\.

## [Digital sociality and the reshaping of network participation: the emergence of phatic imbalances](../publications/baec1e2cf28e308e95ac.md)

João Vasco Coelho

This article theorizes phatic imbalances as emergent effects of how participation and presence are reorganized in contemporary digital sociality\. It argues that participation in digital networks has become increasingly transactional and positional, oriented toward sustaining visibility and availability rather than exchanging meaning\. Drawing on work on networked sociality, weak ties and deep mediatization, the article conceptualizes phaticity and phatic work as priori conditions of digital participation\. It introduces digital proxemics as the sociotechnical production of presence, distance and relational positioning in environments structured by telepresence, virtuality and AI\-infused affordances\. Phatic imbalances arise when infrastructural demands for continuous phatic presence exceed the cognitive and temporal capacities of subjects, producing overload, hollowed presence and machine\-modulated rhythms of interaction\. By linking participation, phaticity and digital proxemics, the article offers a diagnostic lens for understanding how digital infrastructures reshape attention, presence and communicative agency in AI\-saturated environments\.

## [From minds to machines](../publications/baed5fc7ae03767664f6.md)

Hang Li

Recent progress in generative and multimodal machine learning has produced models capable of synthesizing high\-quality text, images, and code\. While these systems often exhibit behaviors that resemble human understanding, their impressive surface\-level fluency does not reliably indicate the presence of stable, grounded, or systematically reusable internal representations\. Empirical evidence suggests that this &quot;illusion of understanding&quot; reflects a critical tension: models that achieve strong benchmark performance can still suffer from brittle failures, semantic drift, and a heavy reliance on shortcut correlations\. This dissertation investigates the structural conditions required to bridge the gap between statistical mimicry and robust semantic reasoning, moving from empirical audits of current systems to the design of cognitively inspired architectures\. We approach machine understanding not as a binary property, but as a set of structural conditions that can be empirically evaluated\. Taking the concept as the unit of analysis, we introduce three diagnostic dimensions to characterize semantic integrity: availability, invariance, and robustness\. Availability examines whether high\-level concepts are explicitly encoded within a model&\#x27;s internal geometry in an interpretable form\. Invariance evaluates whether these representations preserve their identity across modalities and architectures\. Robustness tests whether representations support compositional reasoning and resist degradation under counterfactual or relational perturbations\. The first stage of this research presents a series of empirical audits and interventions based on these dimensions\. We demonstrate that diffusion models encode interpretable semantic structure within internal bottleneck representations, or $h$\-space\. We propose a self\-supervised optimization framework for discovering and manipulating these semantic directions to improve model fairness and safety without requiring manual annotations\. We then analyze semantic consistency at the vision\-\-language interface, showing that meaning often degrades during cross\-modal translation\. To address this, we introduce a cycle\-consistent fine\-tuning framework that enforces bidirectional semantic preservation between image\-to\-text and text\-to\-image models\. Finally, we develop a generative hard\-negative mining pipeline that synthesizes fine\-grained counterfactuals, compelling models to move beyond global statistical shortcuts and yielding substantial improvements in compositional reasoning\. These empirical findings underscore a fundamental limitation: while post\-hoc interventions can improve model behavior, the &quot;semantic fragility&quot; of current systems is often rooted in unstructured, monolithic design\. This observation motivates the second stage of the research, which shifts from auditing machines to drawing inspiration from the functional organization of the human mind\. We explore architectural inductive biases as a necessary complement to large\-scale learning\. We introduce the Tensor Brain framework, which decouples symbolic indexing from subsymbolic representation and helps resolve the conflation of logic and probability in general\-purpose models\. Furthermore, we demonstrate a biologically inspired neural path\-finding mechanism that achieves constant\-time relational reasoning, providing evidence that structural constraints derived from cognitive systems can significantly improve the efficiency and systematicity of machine cognition\. In summary, this dissertation advances the analysis of semantic representations by providing both a mechanistic understanding of existing models and a roadmap for their architectural evolution\. By systematically evaluating the availability, invariance, and robustness of internal concepts, we identify the specific failure modes of modern generative AI and provide targeted methods for repair\. Beyond these interventions, we demonstrate that incorporating structural principles from cognitive science, specifically the separation of symbolic indexing and relational navigation, offers a path toward more stable and reliable systems\. These contributions provide a technical foundation for building a new generation of artificial intelligence that is not only high\-performing but also semantically grounded, systematically robust, and human\-aligned\.

## [A non\-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity](../publications/baef57a4a2e2c21882e1.md)

F\. M\. Filbey; C\. Tyler Short; A\. Leazure; N\. E\. Nekoui; T\. Brown; S\. Kroener; C\. Liu

Background Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation \(taVNS\) has shown promise for enhancing cognition and emotion regulation\. To date, most human studies have focused on narrow learning paradigms that limit our understanding of how taVNS influences complex, integrative cognitive operations\. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms of taVNS are still not well understood\. Objective Building on preclinical findings that vagus nerve stimulation enhances cognitive flexibility and memory in animal models, this study investigated whether acute taVNS can modulate executive function and neural connectivity in healthy adults\. Methods Using a quasi\-experimental design, forty healthy participants received either active or sham taVNS while completing executive function tasks and adaptive cognitive training \(BrainHQ\)\. High\-density electroencephalography \(EEG\) was recorded during stimulation to assess cortical activity and functional connectivity across frequency bands\. Results Multivariate analyses demonstrated significant effects of taVNS on cognitive function and EEG\. Post\-hoc group comparisons showed that compared to sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with improved BrainHQ performance and decreased delta\-band connectivity in left frontal, central, and parietal regions\. Delta\-band connectivity during active taVNS was positively associated with pre\-to\-post improvements in mood\. No difference in executive function tasks was found between active and sham taVNS\. Sensitivity analyses using adjusted models showed that these effects were sensitive to age, sex, and education\. Conclusion By evaluating multiple dimensions of executive function, these exploratory findings suggest that active taVNS may influence selected aspects of executive performance and frontal–parietal delta connectivity, potentially reflecting enhanced neural efficiency arising from the interaction between vagally mediated neuromodulation and continuously adaptive cognitive demands\. However, these effects did not survive multiple\-comparison correction and should therefore be interpreted cautiously and replicated in larger, prospectively powered studies\.

## [ThetreStageAI: Multi\-View Retrieval\-Augmented Generation for Structured Bengali Theatre Production Planning](../publications/baf523d75b661b887130.md)

Md\. Mehedi Hasan Naeem; Mst\. Kamrunnahar Ruma; Shakila Sultana; Nafiza Anjum; Nasreen Jannatun Nemu; Md\. Sujan Ali

Staging a theatre performance requires coordinating dialogue, actor movement, stage directions, lighting focus, cue timing, and equipment constraints within the same production plan\. This work presents ThetreStageAI, a retrieval augmented framework for structured Bengali theatre production planning\. Rather than retrieving from one mixed corpus, the system maintains separate scene, actor\-blocking, and lighting views\. Bengali text is embedded with BGE\-M3 and indexed in view\-specific Qdrant collections\. Retrieved references are combined with a production brief and passed to Gemini, which generates schema\-constrained JSON containing characters, scenes, dialogue, stage directions, blocking, lighting, and optional sound cues\. Structural and semantic checks are applied before acceptance, with at most one constrained repair attempt\. We also construct a human\-guided, LLM\-assisted synthetic dataset of 500 short Bengali theatre records that expands to 1,500 retrieval documents\. Dataset diagnostics confirm consistent identifiers and valid lighting fields while also revealing substantial dialogue repetition\. A paired camera\-ready evaluation compares single\-combined and full multi\-view retrieval under matched settings\. The source code, dataset, and evaluation materials are publicly available\.

## [Use of Machine Learning to Predict Mental Health Disorders Using EEG Data: Selected Research Excerpts](../publications/bb05011558f8d53894f4.md)

Aiwanseosa Israel Omo\-Imade

This record contains selected, unedited excerpts from research completed in 2024 as part of an MSc in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Wolverhampton\. The study investigated the use of machine\-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and a Soft Voting Ensemble, for predicting mental health disorders using electroencephalography \(EEG\) data\. The selected excerpts cover the research rationale, methodology, model evaluation, interpretation of findings, clinical implications, methodological limitations and recommendations for future work\. This public portfolio edition has been prepared as a concise research and analytical writing sample\. It does not represent the complete dissertation and has not undergone peer review\.

## [From Testing to Deployment: A Comparative Approach to the Regulation of Autonomous Vehicles](../publications/bb08838b6aae3ed2bb25.md)

Ranko P\. Sovilj; Sanja Stojković\-Zlatanović

The rapid development of autonomous vehicles challenges traditional driver\-centred legal frameworks and raises important questions concerning safety, responsibility, and regulatory certainty\. This article examines whether existing legal frameworks adequately address the regulation of autonomous vehicles and identifies regulatory approaches relevant to Serbia\. Drawing on comparative and normative legal methodology, it analyses regulatory models in the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, Germany, France, and Australia, before assessing the Serbian regulatory framework\. The findings indicate a shift towards ex ante safety assurance, institutional responsibility, lifecycle oversight, and adaptive regulation\. Serbia, however, remains focused primarily on the testing of autonomous vehicles and lacks comprehensive rules governing authorisation, responsibility, insurance, data governance, and continuous oversight\. The article therefore identifies key elements for the development of a comprehensive regulatory framework for autonomous vehicles in Serbia\.

## [Evaluating the Effect of Numerical Solvers on Learning in Neural ODEs](../publications/bb0f1ed0793774451274.md)

Gavin Lee Goodship; Luis Miralles‐Pechuán; Stephen O’Sullivan

\# Evaluating the Effect of Numerical Solvers on Learning in Neural ODEs \*\*Supplementary code and reproduction guide\*\* \*\*Paper:\*\* \*Transactions on Machine Learning Research\* \(TMLR\), October 2026 \*\*Authors:\*\* Gavin Lee Goodship, Stephen O&\#x27;Sullivan, and Luis Miralles\-Pechuán \*\*Paper and review record:\*\* https://openreview\.net/forum?id=Mopa70gMnp \#\# Overview This archive accompanies the TMLR paper \*Evaluating the Effect of Numerical Solvers on Learning in Neural ODEs\*\. It provides PyTorch experiment scripts and supporting documentation for investigating how fixed\-step Runge–Kutta methods influence the coarse numerical maps learned by Neural ODE classifiers\. The paper asks whether a Runge–Kutta method&\#x27;s \*\*external scalar stability polynomial\*\* is sufficient to characterize solver\-dependent learning\. Two controlled comparisons address this question: varying the Gegenbauer parameter while holding formal order and computational conditions fixed, and comparing ESRKG\-15 with LSRKG\-15, which have numerically matched external scalar stability polynomials but different internal tableaux and higher\-order nonlinear B\-series coefficients\. The results support the conclusion that external stability structure matters but \*\*does not determine the complete nonlinear Runge–Kutta update\*\*\. Further experiments use frozen\-weight solver replacement and common\-reference numerical refinement\. A checkpoint may classify well under its training\-time coarse discretization yet perform very differently when its learned vector field is numerically resolved\. For example, on the fixed 1,000\-image CIFAR\-10 refinement subset, the paper reports an ESRKG\-15 checkpoint changing from \*\*85\.4% native accuracy to 12\.1% resolved accuracy\*\*\. This is a representative checkpoint\-level result, not an assertion that all trained models show the same change\. The third\-order augmented Neural ODE exposes velocity, acceleration and third\-order forcing for descriptive numerical diagnostics\. Those diagnostics are \*\*not\*\* proposed as intrinsic geometric invariants, exact spectral quantities or stability certificates\. First\-order Neural ODE controls are also included\. \#\# Contents The original supplementary ZIP has the following layout\. Folder and filenames below follow the archive exactly\. \| Location \| Contents \| Paper connection \| \| \-\-\- \| \-\-\- \| \-\-\- \| \| \`CIFAR 10/\` \| RK4, ESRKG\-15, ESRKG\-21 and LSRKG\-15 training/evaluation scripts; experiment PDF \| Section 4\.3, CIFAR\-10 \| \| \`CIFAR100/\` \| Corresponding CIFAR\-100 solver scripts and PDF \| Section 4\.3, CIFAR\-100 \| \| \`Tinyimagnet/\` \| Tiny\-ImageNet experiments and dataset\-path instructions \| Section 4\.3, Tiny\-ImageNet \| \| \`Gegenbauer/\` \| ESRKG\-15 parameter variants and \`visual\.py\` stability\-region plot \| Section 4\.4\.1 \| \| \`Realization/\` \| \`real\.py\` for external stability\-polynomial and internal\-stage amplification comparisons \| Section 4\.4\.2 \| \| \`Swap/\` \| Frozen\-weight solver replacement at integration horizons 10 and 20 \| Section 4\.5 \| \| \`Refinement/\` \| Common\-reference solver\-refinement experiments for CIFAR\-10 and CIFAR\-100 \| Section 4\.6 \| \| \`Appendices/\` \| First\-order solver\-swap and numerical\-metric controls \| Appendix experiments \| \| \`Documentation\_for\_code\.pdf\` \| Overall supplementary documentation \| Archive guide \| Each experiment directory also contains a PDF with more detailed instructions\. \*\*Datasets, pretrained weights/checkpoints and generated experiment results are not bundled in this ZIP\*\*; the supplied material consists of code and documentation\. ## [ENTRE TÉCNICA E RESPONSABILIDADE: SOFT LAW E GOVERNANÇA DA IA NA EDUCAÇÃO E PESQUISA](../publications/bb13e3a50f33a2c1af18.md)

Karen Lowhany Costa Da Silva; Débora Sabatini Fabiano; Wendys Mendes da Silva; Kléber Abreu Sousa; Marli Terezinha Vieira

A incorporação da inteligência artificial generativa \(IAG\) no ensino superior transformou as dinâmicas de ensino, aprendizagem e pesquisa, ampliando possibilidades e suscitando desafios éticos, riscos operacionais e questões relacionadas à autoria e à integridade científica\. Objetivo: Analisar o potencial dos instrumentos de soft law como referências orientadoras para o desenvolvimento do letramento em governança da inteligência artificial na academia\. Metodologia: Pesquisa qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, realizada mediante procedimentos bibliográficos e documentais\. O corpus compreendeu produções teóricas publicadas entre 2019 e 2025 e documentos normativos, com destaque para as diretrizes da UNESCO e o manual de recomendações da Universidade Federal de Uberlândia \(UFU\)\. Resultados: Os achados indicam que o letramento digital de caráter predominantemente técnico é insuficiente diante da complexidade dos modelos generativos, evidenciando a necessidade de um letramento em governança da IA voltado à capacidade decisória e à responsabilidade humana\. A soft law apresenta potencial pedagógico e flexível diante da dinâmica dos marcos regulatórios formais, oferecendo parâmetros para transparência, supervisão humana e integridade\. Conclusão: Instrumentos de soft law podem atuar como pontes formativas para a autonomia crítica no ensino superior, orientando decisões sobre quando, por que e sob quais condições utilizar a inteligência artificial\.

## [The Impact of Adopting Artificial Intelligence Techniques on Accounting information Systems\` Reliability](../publications/bb176d6955dd6de83b04.md)

ايناس ابو فرحة

The Impact of Adopting Artificial Intelligence Techniques on Accounting information Systems\` Reliability Abstract This study examines how using Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) techniques affects accounting information system \(AIS\) reliability\. Additionally, this study aims to bridge a gap in the literature by establishing the impacts of utilizing AI technology on the major reliability factors and how those factors impact commercial banks and Islamic banks listed on the Amman stock exchange\. The study used a descriptive analytical research design and employed a structured questionnaire as the means for collecting responses from a sample of 15 banks\. A total of 236 valid responses were obtained from the survey participants\. Data analysis was conducted using SMART PLS4 software for evaluating the relationship of AI implementation with the dependability of AIS\. The findings of this study suggest that the application of AI transforms the overall dependability of an AIS by accounting for nearly a third \(34%\) of the differences seen in various metrics used to assess reliability\. Therefore, the availability of Artificial Intelligence is viewed as providing opportunities for improving both the dependability and the value of an organization’s AIS\. In addition, this work adds to the knowledge base on the effect that adopting AI has on the reliability of an AIS within a financial institution\. The study contributes to the existing literature by demonstrating the relationship between AI adoption and AIS reliability in the context of the banking sector, in conjunction with a well\-established infrastructure for an AIS, and also advocates for providing management and staff with specialized training to assist them in the effective deployment of these new AI tools\. The results also suggest that organizations aiming to improve their AIS through new technology can utilize these findings as a basis for a planning strategy to do so\. Key Words: Artificial Intelligence Techniques, Reliability of Accounting Information Systems, and Banks\.
