## [The resource theory of causal influence and knowledge of causal influence](../publications/bb2532343da37d3026a0.md)

Marina Maciel Ansanelli; Beata Zjawin; David Schmid; Yìlè Yīng; John Harry Selby; Ciaran Gilligan\-Lee; Ana Belen Sainz; Rob W Spekkens

Abstract Understanding and quantifying causal relationships between variables is essential for reasoning about the physical world\. A challenge to this is the fact that different functional causal models can induce the same conditional probability distribution over observed variables while encoding different amounts of causal influence\. Motivated by this observation, we study the underlying functional mechanisms, including uncertainty over them, as meaningful objects in their own right and develop a resource\-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence\. We focus on the simplest nontrivial setting\-\-\- two variables that are causally ordered, meaning that the first has the potential to influence the second, without hidden confounding\. First, we introduce the resource theory that directly quantifies causal influence of a functional dependence in this setting and show that the problem of deciding convertibility of resources and identifying a complete set of monotones has a relatively straightforward solution\. Following this, we introduce the resource theory that arises naturally when one has uncertainty about the functional dependence\. We describe a linear program for deciding the question of whether one resource \(i\.e\., state of knowledge about the functional dependence\) can be converted to another\. Then, we focus on the case where the variables are binary\. In this case, we identify a triple of monotones that are complete in the sense that they capture the partial order over the set of all resources, and we provide an interpretation of each\.

## [Design and Development of an AI\-Assisted Medical Laboratory Report Analysis and Decision\-Support System](../publications/bb371cf98d329aece12c.md)

Vivek Kumar; Nitish Pal; Prince Munna Yadav; Akash Verma

Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) is becoming an important part of modern healthcare by helping organize medical information, improve data accessibility, and support more efficient workflows\. Medical laboratory reports contain valuable information about a person&\#x27;s health, including test names, measured values, units, and reference ranges\. However, understanding these reports can be challenging for individuals who are unfamiliar with medical terminology\. Manually reviewing and organizing laboratory data can also be time\-consuming, particularly when reports are available in different formats, such as digital PDFs, scanned documents, and images\. This research paper presents the design of a proposed AI\-assisted Medical Laboratory Report Analysis and Decision\-Support System that aims to make laboratory information easier to process, organize, and review\. The system focuses on combining document processing, Optical Character Recognition \(OCR\), data extraction, validation, normalization, and visualization within a structured workflow\. Its primary goal is to improve the accessibility and consistency of laboratory report information while supporting the identification of results that may require further attention\. The proposed system begins by accepting laboratory reports in supported digital or scanned formats\. When a report contains image\-based text, OCR technology can be used to convert the visible information into machine\-readable text\. For digital PDF files containing an accessible text layer, document\-parsing techniques can be used to extract relevant information directly\. The extracted content is then processed to identify important laboratory parameters, numerical values, measurement units, and reference intervals\. After extraction, the system applies preprocessing and validation techniques to organize the collected information\. This stage is important because laboratory reports may contain inconsistent formatting, different parameter names, missing values, unclear units, or variations in table layouts\. The system is designed to preserve the original information wherever possible and identify uncertain or incomplete fields for manual verification rather than making unsupported assumptions\. Data normalization helps present the extracted information in a more consistent and structured format\. The next stage focuses on comparing laboratory results with the reference intervals provided in the original report\. Based on these intervals, the system can categorize a value as being within the supplied range, below the supplied range, or above the supplied range\. If the reference interval or measurement unit is missing, ambiguous, or incompatible, the result should be flagged for manual review\. This approach aims to make the analysis process more transparent by showing the extracted values and the reference information used for comparison\. A user\-friendly dashboard is proposed to display the organized laboratory information in a clear and accessible manner\. By presenting relevant parameters and highlighting potentially out\-of\-range values, the dashboard can help users locate important information more easily\. The system also emphasizes traceability, allowing extracted information to be checked against its original source wherever practical\. These features are intended to reduce the effort involved in locating and organizing relevant details within laboratory reports\. An important aspect of this research is the responsible use of AI in healthcare\-related applications\. A result outside a laboratory&\#x27;s reference interval does not necessarily indicate a disease, and a result within that interval does not guarantee that a person is healthy\. Therefore, the proposed system is intended to support the review of medical information rather than provide autonomous diagnoses, prescribe treatments, or replace the professional judgment of qualified healthcare practitioners\. Human verification, clear communication of uncertainty, and appropriate interpretation of laboratory findings remain essential\. The research also considers privacy, data security, and the reliability of extracted information\. Medical reports may contain sensitive personal data, making it important to use appropriate access controls, secure data handling practices, file validation, and suitable data\-retention policies\. For development and evaluation, synthetic, de\-identified, or appropriately authorized datasets can be used to reduce privacy risks\. The proposed evaluation framework includes measures for extraction accuracy, classification performance, processing time, robustness across report formats, and usability\. Actual performance results must be obtained through systematic testing before the effectiveness of the implemented system can be established\. The proposed system follows a modular architecture consisting of a user interface, document\-processing or OCR component, preprocessing and validation layer, data\-normalization module, reference\-range comparison mechanism, and dashboard for presenting the results\. This modular structure provides a foundation for future improvements, including multilingual laboratory report processing, better handling of complex tables, visualization of changes across multiple reports, explainable AI techniques, and enhanced tools for professional review\. The main contribution of this research is the proposed integration of report extraction, data validation, normalization, reference\-range comparison, and visualization into a traceable workflow\. Rather than presenting automated output as a definitive medical conclusion, the approach emphasizes transparency, verification, and human oversight\. Its practical value will depend on implementation quality, dataset coverage, systematic evaluation, and the ability to handle different report layouts reliably\.

## [From population equality to demographic alignment: normative benchmarks and institutional governance of health workforce allocation in China, 2012–2024](../publications/bb4ab49a65f5bb0d73d4.md)

Tong Lyu

Background The health workforce is a constrained health\-system input, and allocation decisions often rely on workforce\-to\-population indicators\. Although transparent and readily comparable, these indicators may obscure heterogeneity in demographic demand across provinces and health subsystems\. We examined whether provincial health workforce distributions in China became more closely aligned with subsystem\-relevant demographic proxies between 2012 and 2024\. Methods We conducted a provincial longitudinal ecological study covering 31 mainland provincial\-level units and 403 province\-year observations\. Four prespecified relationships were assessed: hospital workforce vs\. older population, primary healthcare workforce vs\. older population, maternal and child health \(MCH\) workforce vs\. child population, and MCH workforce vs\. a birth\-demand proxy\. Alignment was assessed using provincial workforce and demographic\-proxy shares, together with annual distributional mismatch, dispersion, β\-convergence, rank persistence, regional alignment, and sensitivity analyses\. Results Hospital–older\-population mismatch decreased from 0\.116 in 2012 to 0\.077 in 2024, with β\-convergence \(β = – 0\.0435, q &lt; 0\.001\)\. Primary healthcare showed no consistent convergence relative to the older\-population proxy: D remained 0\.076 at both endpoints, whereas the primary healthcare–total\-population benchmark decreased by 36\.3%\. For MCH, mismatch relative to child population decreased by 31\.7%, with β\-convergence \(β = – 0\.0396, q = 0\.031\), although unweighted cross\-provincial dispersion did not decline\. MCH mismatch relative to the birth\-demand proxy decreased by 18\.9% but showed no consistent convergence and widened again after 2021\. Conclusions General\-population equalization did not translate into similar demographic alignment across health subsystems\. Subsystem\-specific demographic benchmarks function as alternative normative criteria for interpreting workforce allocation under demographic change, revealing patterns not apparent from total\-population indicators\. They should be interpreted as descriptive distributional measures, not as estimates of staffing adequacy or allocative efficiency\.

## [Self\-Reflective Chain\-of\-Thought \(SRCoT\): Evidence\-Based Text Generation via a Closed\-Loop Retrieve\-\-Reflect\-\-Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs](../publications/bb620535a43b915f61e0.md)

Fabian Broszio; Michael Hoffmann; Adrian Paschke

Large language models \(LLMs\) can generate fluent outputs that lack source support or conflict with local operational constraints\. We introduce Self\-Reflective Chain\-of\-Thought \(SRCoT\), a modular architecture that organizes generation as a closed Retrieve\-\-Reflect\-\-Revise loop\. SRCoT separates environment state, persistent knowledge, accumulated experience, and short\-term memory into provenance\-labeled stores\. BM25 retrieval supplies local context; subsequent passes expose intermediate drafts, missing\-information markers, follow\-up queries, and optional claim\-\-evidence mappings\. These artifacts inform retrieval, revision, clarification, or abstention decisions\. We examine the architecture through qualitative, trace\-based case studies in two fully synthetic settings: emergency medical services and Munich\-Sim, an emergency\-operations simulation\. Local prototype runs on an Apple M4\-family laptop with 128 GB memory illustrate source\-labeled documentation, explicit gap marking, and structured dispatch\-style outputs\. The traces also reveal provenance\-assignment errors, incomplete evidence coverage, and unsafe assumptions that remain possible despite prompting constraints\. These cases demonstrate report\-level inspectability and local execution, not comparative superiority, hallucination reduction, clinical validity, or operational safety\. The architecture separates retrieval and control from the model interface, but behavior across different models remains to be evaluated\. SRCoT is a research proof of concept requiring human review, with its principal contribution lying in an inspectable control procedure rather than a new model\.

## [SpecLLM: LLM\-based VNIR spectral interpretation](../publications/bb6cd45de0ac0a3e6af0.md)

Michał Romaszewski; Anna Strzoda; Marzena Halama; Przemysław Głomb; Piotr Masłowski

Abstract Visible and near\-infrared \(VNIR\) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities\. Recent machine\-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature\-level descriptions\. Meanwhile, LLM\-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences\. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models \(LLMs\) through compact, feature\-based representations\. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma\-separated values \(CSV\), JavaScript Object Notation \(JSON\), or extensible markup language \(XML\), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema\. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON\. We evaluate prototype\-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open\-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset\. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra\. The natural\-language format provides a human\-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full\-spectrum encodings\. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable\.

## [Naključno učenje iz znanstvenega novinarstva](../publications/bb746f0e91e1334265d8.md)

Christian Ameseder; Iztok Devetak; Darija Skubic

Austrian non\-experts in health sciences often lack the scientific knowledge to make informed decisions that affect their daily lives and society as a whole\. In general, their interest in current scientific knowledge is low, so it is unlikely that they will actively seek out information\. Adult non\-experts therefore need to acquire relevant scientific information incidentally, e\.g\., by reading journalistic articles\. Journalistic articles traditionally follow an inverted pyramid structure, presenting the most important information first, while narratives unfold events chronologically with intentionally acting characters\. Journalistic science narratives provide information that is usually missing in inverted pyramids\. This additional information may increase situational interest in journalistic science narratives\. Most people are confronted with narratives more often than with explanatory texts in everyday life and can therefore process them better\. Due to the linear structure, relevant information elements are automatically activated at the same time, which further facilitates processing\. An online study in the context of online science journalism on nutrition topics was conducted in Austria with 461 adult non\-experts in health sciences recruited via online platforms\. The dependent variables comprehension, cognitive load and situational interest were investigated using a multipletier test and self\-reports\. The results indicate significantly higher comprehension and general situational interest and significantly lower cognitive load after reading journalistic science narratives compared to inverted pyramids\. However, situational interest in journalistic science narratives was significantly lower after participants had read the first paragraph\. It then increased and was significantly higher than that for inverted pyramids for the rest of the article\. Therefore, journalistic science narratives with a strictly chronological structure should be used with caution\. When initial situational interest is low, individuals may stop reading before they have enough information to fully comprehend the content\. In addition, higher situational interest is correlated with a lower perception of cognitive load\.

## [Quality of life before and after sympathectomy in primary hyperhidrosis: a recall\-based paired analysis of 94 patients](../publications/bb7e117f109c446d7e53.md)

Yazeed A\. Alrodiman; Qais A\. Almuhaideb; Nasser M\. AbuDujain; Khalid M\. AlGhamdi

Objectives Primary hyperhidrosis substantially impairs quality of life\. Sympathectomy is an established treatment for severe focal hyperhidrosis; however, patient\-reported outcomes in Arab populations remain limited\. This study evaluated recalled preoperative and current postoperative quality of life after sympathectomy using validated Arabic instruments\. Methods We conducted a secondary, recall\-based paired analysis of a cross\-sectional survey of 94 participants with primary hyperhidrosis who reported having undergone bilateral sympathectomy\. Participants completed an Arabic electronic survey between May 2024 and April 2025\. Current postoperative quality\-of\-life scores were compared with retrospectively recalled preoperative scores using the Arabic Hyperhidrosis Quality of Life Index \(HidroQoL©\); severity was assessed using the Arabic Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Scale\. Wilcoxon signed\-rank tests were primary; paired t tests were sensitivity analyses\. Results The mean participant age was 30\.7 ± 8\.9 years, and 63\.8% were men\. At the recalled preoperative assessment, 55 participants \(58\.5%\) reported Grade 4 disease severity\. All 94 participants provided complete paired data\. The mean daily\-life score decreased from 8\.5 ± 2\.8 to 4\.9 ± 4\.5 \[mean paired change −3\.6; 95% confidence interval \(CI\) −4\.5 to −2\.8; d z = −0\.88\]\. The mean psychosocial score decreased from 16\.9 ± 5\.5 to 8\.8 ± 8\.7 \(−8\.1; 95% CI −9\.7 to −6\.4; d z = −0\.97\)\. The total score decreased from 25\.4 ± 7\.5 to 13\.7 ± 12\.8 \(−11\.7; 95% CI −14\.1 to −9\.3; d z = −0\.98\); all p &lt; 0\.001\. Thirteen participants \(13\.8%\) reported a higher total score after surgery\. Conclusions Participants reported substantially lower hyperhidrosis\-related daily\-life and psychosocial impairment after sympathectomy\. Recall bias may affect the magnitude and direction of these differences, which do not establish causal treatment effects\. Prospective studies incorporating true preoperative baseline assessment, operative details, compensatory sweating, and longer follow\-up are needed to confirm the magnitude and durability of these improvements\.

## [Machine learning models of noninvasive tests to predict metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis stage](../publications/bba0f0e584a3b8373cda.md)

Rohit Loomba; Rebecca Taub; Dominic Labriola; Jan Priel; Krishna Padmanabhan; W\. Ray Kim

BACKGROUND: Fibrosis stage in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis \(MASH\) is currently diagnosed by liver biopsy in clinical trials\. Using noninvasive tests, no consensus method exists for staging fibrosis or diagnosing MASH\. We aimed to develop machine learning \(ML\) methods to predict fibrosis stage and MASH with F2/F3 fibrosis using noninvasive biomarkers\. METHODS: Data from 1970 biopsy\-confirmed patients screened for phase 3 resmetirom trials \(MAESTRO\-NASH, MAESTRO\-NAFLD\-1\) were retrospectively analyzed\. Outcomes were fibrosis stage and MASH with F2/F3 fibrosis \[NAFLD Activity Score \(NAS\) ≥4 with moderate to advanced noncirrhotic fibrosis\], modeled from 37 clinical, laboratory, and imaging predictors\. Random forest models were developed, including a full model using all 37 predictors and “Lean” models using subsets of predictors routinely available in clinical practice\. These models were evaluated by 4\-fold cross\-validation using AUC\. RESULTS: For three\-class fibrosis staging \(F0/F1 vs\. F2/F3 vs\. F4\), one\-versus\-rest cross\-validation mean AUCs were 0\.76, 0\.75, and 0\.94 for the full model and 0\.83, 0\.78, and 0\.89 for the best\-performing Lean model\. Liver stiffness measures \(LSM\) and MASH composite algorithms, such as the Fibrosis\-4 Index \(FIB\-4\) and FibroScan\-AST, were among the most important predictors\. For MASH with F2/F3 fibrosis, the full and best\-performing Lean models achieved AUCs of 0\.75 and 0\.79, respectively\. Parsimonious top\-k models retaining LSM preserved much of this performance\. CONCLUSION: ML models using routinely available noninvasive biomarkers discriminated fibrosis stage and MASH with F2/F3 fibrosis with strong performance, supporting patient selection for clinical trials or practice\. Lean predictor models that incorporated LSM outperformed models limited to blood\-based biomarkers or a combination of FIB\-4 and LSM\. These proposed ML models need additional external and prospective validation before deployment for clinical use\.

## [Game Startup Business Sustainability Through Strategy, Innovation, and SDGs Orientation: A Bibliometric Analysis](../publications/bbb70dea6005712a749a.md)

Nur Azizah; Vanessa Gaffar; Lili Adi Wibowo; Tutik Inayati

Background: The digital creative industry requires game startups to achieve business sustainability while responding to technological change, market uncertainty, platform dependence, and sustainability demands\. However, literature remains fragmented across strategic management, innovation, entrepreneurship, competitive advantage, and Sustainable Development Goals \(SDGs\), leaving the integrated structure of game startup sustainability insufficiently mapped\. Objective: This study aims to map the development, conceptual structure, thematic evolution, and collaborative landscape of game startup business sustainability research through strategy, innovation, competitive advantage, and SDGs orientation\. Methods: A descriptive quantitative design using bibliometric analysis was employed\. The dataset comprised 1,269 scientific publications retrieved from the Dimensions database for 2017–2026\. Bibliographic metadata were analyzed using VOSviewer through annual publication trends, keyword co\-occurrence, density visualization, temporal overlay analysis, and collaboration networks involving countries, authors, and organizations\. Results: Publication output increased from 25 articles in 2017 to 275 in 2025, indicating growing scholarly attention\. Keyword mapping identified interconnected themes involving business models, capabilities, performance, entrepreneurship, policy, investment, innovation, and sustainable development\. Temporal analysis revealed emerging attention to artificial intelligence, transformation, governance, policymaking, investment, resilience, and infrastructure\. International collaboration was broad, although contributions remained concentrated among established research systems, while Indonesia occupied a comparatively less central position\. Conclusion: Game startup business sustainability constitutes a multidisciplinary research domain integrating strategic management, innovation, digital entrepreneurship, institutional ecosystems, and sustainable development\. The findings provide a conceptual foundation for future empirical research on sustainable adaptive strategy, sustainable business model innovation, competitive advantage, and sustainability outcomes, particularly in emerging economies and policy development in Indonesia\.

## [Metabolic and inflammatory traits and depression: a Mendelian randomization study with late\-adolescent population\-based and clinical triangulation](../publications/bbba0a2acc4fc35a0894.md)

Yanping Wu; Zhenyu Xu; Daolin Wu

Objective Metabolic dysfunction and systemic inflammation have been associated with adolescent depression, but their causal relevance remains uncertain\. We examined whether insulin resistance, proxied by the triglyceride\-glucose \(TyG\) index, and high\-sensitivity C\-reactive protein \(hs\-CRP\) show genetically proxied associations with major depressive disorder \(MDD\), and evaluated their observational relevance in late adolescents from the general population and in a clinical adolescent sample\. Methods We performed bidirectional two\-sample Mendelian randomization \(MR\) using genome\-wide association study \(GWAS\) summary statistics for the TyG index, hs\-CRP, body mass index \(BMI\), and MDD, with inverse\-variance weighting as the primary method, supplemented by sensitivity and multivariable MR analyses\. Observational corroboration was sought in 327 late adolescents aged 18–19 years from the pooled 2015–2016 and 2017–March 2020 pre\-pandemic cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey \(NHANES\) and in a retrospective cohort of 224 adolescents with depression and 200 frequency\-matched controls\. Results Genetically predicted higher TyG index \(odds ratio \[OR\] 1\.08, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] 1\.03–1\.14, P = 0\.001\) and hs\-CRP \(OR 1\.11, 95% CI 1\.05–1\.16, P&lt;0\.001\) were associated with higher odds of MDD; reverse MR analyses did not show statistically significant associations\. In the late\-adolescent NHANES sample, each 1\-SD higher TyG index \(adjusted OR 1\.28, 95% CI 1\.01–1\.63\) and each 1\-SD higher log\-transformed hs\-CRP \(adjusted OR 1\.33, 95% CI 1\.03–1\.71\) were associated with higher odds of moderate\-to\-severe depressive symptoms \(Patient Health Questionnaire\-9 score ≥10\)\. In the clinical cohort, the TyG index \(adjusted OR 1\.35, 95% CI 1\.15–1\.58\) and hs\-CRP &gt;3\.0 mg/L \(adjusted OR 2\.55, 95% CI 1\.60–4\.06\) were associated with higher odds of depression\. In a multiple\-imputation sensitivity analysis retaining all 561 exposure/outcome\-complete NHANES participants, both NHANES associations remained directionally consistent with the primary complete\-case estimates\. Conclusion Converging but methodologically distinct lines of evidence—genetic, population\-based, and clinical—are directionally consistent with a contribution of insulin resistance and systemic inflammation to depression across adolescence and late adolescence\. These findings support further prospective and interventional evaluation of metabolic\-inflammatory pathways rather than immediate clinical translation\.

## [Carbon dots derived from traditional Chinese medicines: a novel therapeutic strategy for ocular diseases](../publications/bbd5f8bac4ed509aa27c.md)

Tingyu Yang; Zongqi Feng; Xiao Zhang; Lihui Zhang; Yu Su; Ruihua Liu; Rina Sa; A Lamusi

Carbon dots \(CDs\) represent a novel category of zero\-dimensional carbon\-based nanomaterials featuring favorable biosafety in vitro and in acute animal studies\. They also exhibit distinctive optical properties and diverse pharmacological activities\. Synthesized via eco\-friendly green routes using traditional Chinese medicines \(TCMs\) and their extracts, TCM\-derived carbon dots \(TCM\-CDs\) display distinct properties compared to conventional nanocarriers\. Benefiting from their inherent nanostructures, abundant surface functional groups, and nanozyme\-like activity, TCM\-CDs can deliver intrinsic therapeutic effects without loading exogenous drugs or relying on residual herbal ingredients\. They possess multiple bioactivities, including antioxidant, anti\-inflammatory, antibacterial and neuroprotective effects, which make them potential non\-invasive therapeutic candidates for refractory ocular disorders\. A growing body of studies has validated the promising therapeutic efficacy of TCM\-CDs in animal models against autoimmune uveitis, retinal lesions, and optic nerve injuries, highlighting their encouraging preclinical findings that warrant further investigation toward clinical translation\. Focusing on the intrinsic therapeutic capacity of TCM\-CDs, this review systematically summarizes their core functional mechanisms and research progress in ocular disease intervention, discusses prevailing academic controversies and unresolved research bottlenecks in this field, and proposes prospective developmental directions\. This work intends to offer comprehensive theoretical evidence and guidance directions for subsequent mechanistic investigations and clinical translation of TCM\-CDs in ophthalmic research\.

## [Physiological reserve and early recovery across oncologic and non\-oncologic abdominal surgery: a prospective multicenter interaction analysis](../publications/bbdad85a840ac9922559.md)

Sergii Girnyi; Francesco Giovinazzo; Elena Montanari; Eugenia Semeraro; Alessandra Marano; Jarosław Skokowski; Tomasz Cwalinski; Mathias Schlögl; Mirko Barone; Archil Aladashvili; Mahmoud Al\-Balas; Virginia Boccardi; Mauro Santarelli; Luigi Marano

Background Frailty and low handgrip strength are established markers of limited physiological reserve, but it is uncertain whether their prognostic meaning differs between oncologic and non\-oncologic surgery\. We examined whether oncologic indication modifies the associations of preoperative frailty and baseline handgrip strength with early postoperative outcomes\. Methods This secondary analysis used a prospective cohort conducted at participating surgical centers between January 2023 and June 2025\. Frailty was classified using the Fried phenotype, and handgrip strength was measured at admission\. The primary outcome was prolonged length of stay \(LOS &gt;10 days\); secondary outcomes were any postoperative complication, major complications, and log\-transformed LOS\. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms in multivariable logistic models adjusted for age and sex\. Because no prolonged stays occurred among fit patients in the non\-oncologic stratum, categorical frailty models used Firth penalized logistic regression\. Results Among 222 clinically characterized participants, 118 \(53\.2%\) underwent oncologic surgery\. Prolonged LOS occurred in 41/118 \(34\.7%\) oncologic and 7/104 \(6\.7%\) non\-oncologic patients\. The complete\-case primary analysis included 216 patients and 45 events\. In an additional ordinal main\-effects model, increasing frailty \[odds ratio \(OR\) 2\.91 per category, 95% confidence interval \(CI\) 1\.57–5\.38\], lower handgrip strength \(OR 0\.95 per kg, 95% CI 0\.90–0\.99\), and oncologic indication \(OR 8\.97, 95% CI 3\.47–23\.19\) were associated with prolonged LOS\. However, categorical frailty\-by\-oncology interaction was not supported \(global p = 0\.341\), nor was handgrip\-strength\-by\-oncology interaction \( p = 0\.739\); the joint interaction test was not statistically significant \( p = 0\.525\)\. No convincing effect modification was observed for complications or continuous LOS\. Conclusions Oncologic surgery was associated with a substantially higher early postoperative burden, while frailty and handgrip strength retained prognostic relevance\. No clear evidence of multiplicative interaction by oncologic indication was detected, but clinically meaningful effect modification cannot be excluded\. Physiological reserve assessment should therefore be considered across elective abdominal surgery rather than restricted to the oncologic setting\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI QUANTUM COLLECTIVE OPTICAL RESONANCE SPECTROSCOPY SYSTEM \(E\-QCORS\) A Femtosecond Near\-Field Optical Architecture for Real\-Time Observation of Quantum Collective Electron Behavior in Two\-Dimensional Materials](../publications/bbdfa1befdd019582de7.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Quantum Collective Optical Resonance Spectroscopy System \(E\-QCORS\) is a revolutionary five\-layer femtosecond near\-field optical architecture for real\-time observation of quantum collective electron behavior in two\-dimensional materials\. Combining ultrafast pump\-probe spectroscopy \(10 fs effective temporal resolution via attosecond\-precision delay\-stage scanning\), scanning near\-field optical microscopy \(10 nm spatial resolution\), and dual\-mode detection, E\-QCORS overcomes fundamental limitations of transport measurements, conventional optical spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy\. The system operates across a wide temperature range \(4K\-300K\) with in\-situ control of magnetic field \(0\-9T\), strain \(0\-2%\), and carrier density\. The core innovation is the Quantum Collective Coherence Index \($\\Xi\_\{QCC\}$\), a strictly bounded dimensionless metric computed from the third\-order nonlinear optical susceptibility using causal transfer entropy decomposition combined with constrained microscopic modeling \(GW\+BSE\)\. This enables unambiguous discrimination between single\-particle and collective quantum behavior while preventing mathematical singularity\. The automated quantum phase classification system identifies superconducting, quantum Hall \(at cryogenic temperatures &lt;10K\-30K\), exciton condensate, spin liquid, and charge density wave phases through machine learning trained on distinctive nonlinear optical signatures with explicit temperature and field constraints\. Real\-time quantum phase mapping with nanoscale resolution accelerates quantum materials discovery by 10\-100x compared to traditional methods\. E\-QCORS provides the first practical pathway to direct, real\-time observation of quantum collective phenomena, enabling rapid development of quantum electronics, discovery of novel quantum materials, and fundamental tests of quantum many\-body theories\. Patent pending \(DOI: 10\.5281/zenodo\.23438932\)\.

## [Polymer Sorbents for Wastewater Treatment: Structure–Performance Relationships and Adsorption Mechanisms](../publications/bbe62d8cb542936f4757.md)

Ch\.M\. Seyidova; H\.F\. Aslanova; Nigar Shikhverdiyeva; Nargiz Tahmasib Rahimli; Jamila Guliyeva; Aytaj Javadzada; Ulviyya Mammadova; Mehpara Nadiri; Nizami Allahverdi Zeynalov; Parvana Movsumova

ABSTRACT Industrial effluents containing heavy metals, synthetic dyes, per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances \(PFAS\), pharmaceuticals, and endocrine‐disrupting compounds remain a major challenge for wastewater treatment\. Conventional adsorbents, including activated carbon and zeolites, often show limitations in selectivity, regeneration, or adsorption capacity for complex wastewater systems\. Polymer sorbents offer an alternative because their chemical structure and surface functionality can be tailored for specific separation and adsorption applications\. This review examines studies published between 2021 and 2025, with particular attention to the relationship between polymer structure and adsorption performance\. The discussion considers the effects of crosslinking density, pore architecture, and functional‐group modification on adsorption behavior across different classes of polymer sorbents\. Representative examples include molecularly imprinted polymers for selective recognition, poly\(ionic liquid\)‐based materials for PFAS removal, stimuli‐responsive hydrogels with swelling‐dependent transport properties, and magnetic polymer nanocomposites that combine adsorption with straightforward separation\. The review also discusses regeneration efficiency, structural stability during repeated adsorption–desorption cycles, and the balance between mechanical strength and biodegradability\. Although substantial progress has been reported at the laboratory scale, pilot‐scale investigations and studies involving multi‐component wastewater remain relatively limited\. Recent work applying machine learning to polymer design is briefly considered as a promising direction for accelerating material development\. By bringing these aspects together, this review provides an updated overview of current polymer sorbent technologies and identifies priorities for future research and practical wastewater treatment applications, with the aim of supporting informed material‐selection decisions by treatment‐plant operators, regulators, and technology managers\.

## [CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning](../publications/bc01c159712568a3a8d2.md)

Ling\-Xiang Zhang; Tao Hu; Da\-Wei Zhou

Multimodal Large Language Models \(MLLMs\) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet real\-world applications often require them to continually acquire new capabilities from sequential tasks, i\.e\., Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning \(MCIT\)\. In typical MLLMs, a projector is employed to align visual representations with the language model\. However, existing methods primarily protect the language model from forgetting while continuously updating the projector across tasks\. Such asymmetric adaptation can cause substantial representation drift in the projector, increasing the mismatch between the projector and language model and consequently exacerbating catastrophic forgetting\. To address this issue, we propose Compatible Routing \(CART\), which explicitly coordinates the adaptation of the projector and language model\. Specifically, CART maintains task\-specific experts for both modules and combines them through weighted mixtures\. CART jointly infers their weights by considering both expert relevance and cross\-module compatibility, thereby promoting coordinated adaptation between the two modules\. To further control model growth, we introduce relevance\-guided expert consolidation, which merges experts exhibiting similar relevance profiles across samples within each module\. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CART achieves state\-of\-the\-art performance\.

## [Research advances of magnesium and magnesium alloys worldwide in 2025](../publications/bc11a5f9ab7c6e9a43a8.md)

Yan Yang; Xiaoming Xiong; Jia She; Yuan Yuan; Shuangshuang Tan; Yangfan Lu; Wenhui Yao; X\. Chen; Xiaoyuan Zhou; Xiaodong Peng; Daolun Chen; Fusheng Pan

Research on magnesium materials has achieved rapid development in 2025, with a total of 6124 related papers indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, where China contributes 50\.89% of the global output, occupying a leading position in international magnesium research\. Bibliometric analysis indicates that microstructure evolution, mechanical performance, and corrosion resistance remain the mainstream research focuses of magnesium alloys\. Meanwhile, functional magnesium material systems, including biomedical magnesium alloys, hydrogen storage media, and rechargeable magnesium batteries, have witnessed remarkable breakthroughs\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) and machine learning \(ML\) techniques are increasingly integrated into magnesium research workflows, supporting multi\-performance forecasting, inverse alloy composition design and interpretable property regulation, which provides an innovative paradigm for the customized optimization of magnesium alloy properties\. The continuous drop in primary magnesium prices further facilitates scaled industrial deployment of magnesium products\. This review systematically summarizes the full spectrum of magnesium research advances in 2025 and highlights prevailing bottlenecks together with prospective research pathways for magnesium\-based materials\.

## [Rethinking GRPO for Large Reasoning Model Safety Alignment](../publications/bc13526b245d871a7d54.md)

Jiawei Chen; Yi Zhang; Jiawei Du; Zhonghou Lv; Tairan Chen; Junyuan Shang; Jinchang Hou; Xiao Yang; Yu Tian; Chenfu Bao; Chao Yu; Zhaoxia Yin

Large reasoning models \(LRMs\) exhibit strong reasoning capabilities but remain vulnerable to unsafe outputs\. While Group Relative Policy Optimization \(GRPO\) is widely used for safety alignment, its group\-relative optimization may provide insufficient safety\-directed learning signals\. In this paper, we identify two failure modes: advantage collapse, where homogeneous rollout groups yield vanishing advantages, and unsafe diversification, where unsafe behaviors persist and become increasingly diverse\. Our theoretical analysis reveals that behavioral consistency weakens within\-group safety contrasts, while entropy regularization can diversify unsafe responses when relative signals vanish\. To address these challenges, we propose Beacon, comprising Safety Signal Recovery \(SSR\) and Safety\-Utility Decoupled Alignment \(SUDA\)\. SSR combines advantage\-guided trajectory filtering and safe reference supervision to recover effective safety learning signals, while SUDA employs category\-aware rewards and benign\-only KL anchoring to mitigate over\-refusal without compromising safety\. Experiments across four Qwen3 and DeepSeek\-R1\-Distill variants and eight benchmarks show that our framework achieves the best average safety and reasoning performance, reducing average safety error by up to 32\.83 percentage points while maintaining low over\-refusal\.

## [blockchain\-based cryptocurrency in Developing Economies: Unveiling Usability, Usefulness, Risk, Online Social and Commercial Interactions Factors in Cryptocurrency Online Trading\.](../publications/bc1fa6e628b75ecc86d1.md)

د عاهد الحرايزة

Abstract: This study seeks to identify aspects linked to the adoption of a blockchain\-based cryptocurrency from the viewpoint of individuals&\#x27; behaviors in emerging markets like Jordan\. A study framework has been created to explore how perceived ease of use, perceived benefits, perceived risks, and intention to use cryptocurrency are interconnected\. This investigation will consider factors like online social and commercial interactions\. The research sample comprises individuals aged 18 and above from Jordan with internet skills \(4686 participants\)\. The study aims to achieve its objective through an analytical method\. It involves procedures in two stages; measurement model analysis and an explanatory model of cryptocurrency usage intention \(structural model analysis\)\. The study evaluates the fit of the model and examines the path coefficient to address the research hypotheses put forward in this study\. The study discovered that all aspects of the suggested model play a role in influencing the decision to use cryptocurrency technology online trading\. Additionally, the study has made contributions by shedding light on the intention to use cryptocurrency trading platforms in developing economics like Jordan\.

## [Decoupling the Conductivity–Seebeck Trade‐Off in N‐Type MXene/Conjugated Polyelectrolyte Thermoelectric Bilayers](../publications/bc20fff5152b2cf5e0a5.md)

Xiang‐Ren Chen; Tzu\-Ling Ma; Haim Kwon; Min‐Chi Fu; Tsu‐Ting Lu; Yu‐Jane Sheng; Han Young Woo; Cheng‐Liang Liu

ABSTRACT To decouple the Seebeck coefficient from electrical conductivity in metallic thermoelectric \(TE\) systems, we investigated bilayer heterostructures of MXene \(Ti 3 C 2 T x \) and conjugated polymers with anionic \(–SO 3– Na \+ , CPE‐Na\), neutral \(CP\), and cationic \(–N \+ \(CH 3 \) 3 Br–, CPE‐Br\) side chains\. Strong electrostatic anchoring between the cationic ammonium side chains and electronegative MXene terminations induces a previously unreported Coulombic trap‐induced filtering mechanism, distinct from conventional energy filtering\. The resulting localized potential wells selectively trap low‐energy carriers to enhance the Seebeck coefficient, while concurrent lattice stiffening suppresses electron–phonon scattering and preserves high‐energy carrier transport\. This decoupling raises Hall mobility from 1\.01 to 5\.40 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and the Seebeck coefficient from –8\.6 to –19\.0 µV K −1 while maintaining a metallic conductivity of 5291\.9 S cm −1 \. The optimized MXene/CPE‐Br film, processed with a halogen‐free solvent, achieves a record power factor of 190\.5 µW m −1 K −2 and a peak figure of merit \( zT \) of 0\.0279\. Strong interfacial adhesion further imparts good electromechanical durability under repeated bending to a flexible TE generator, providing an effective strategy to address the transport limitations of n‐type MXene‐based TE materials\.

## [Optimizing Academic Success for OTD Students: A LASSI\-Based Pre/Posttest Study on Intervention Effectiveness](../publications/bc2896e405d91204cc68.md)

Mica Rutschke; Dailen Castillo; Lauren Peyton

Graduate students frequently experience heightened anxiety that can interfere with academic performance, well\-being, and persistence in graduate programs\. This pilot study explored the effectiveness of a targeted academic intervention for Occupational Therapy Doctorate \(OTD\) students using the Learning and Study Strategies Inventory \(LASSI\) as a pre/post assessment tool\. Ten first\-year OTD students completed the LASSI at program entry and again after participating in a faculty\-led intervention focused on growth mindset and anxiety management strategies\. The intervention included a lunch\-hour educational session on evidence\-based techniques, such as mindfulness, test\-taking skills, cognitive reframing, and stress regulation\. Faculty advisors also used individualized LASSI data to guide one\-on\-one academic coaching\. Statistical analysis revealed a significant improvement in students’ Anxiety scores, with a large effect size \(Cohen’s d = –0\.93\), suggesting that the intervention had a meaningful impact on students’ perceived ability to manage academic anxiety\. Findings support the use of growth mindset principles and structured faculty engagement in improving mental health and academic readiness\. While limited by sample size and lack of a control group, results provide preliminary evidence for integrating LASSI\-informed advising and targeted interventions into OTD curricula to enhance student success\.

## [Bank\-Promoted Insurance Companies After The 2025 Legal Reforms: Corporate Control, Board Independence and Regulatory Coordination](../publications/bc297f133f14a4cb46b7.md)

Harisudhan S

Banks which own insurance companies operate in the interface of two regulatory systems, and the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha \(Amendment of Insurance Laws\) Act, 2025 modifies the conditions of such an interface\. In this paper, I attempt to explore the manner in which the Act modifies the relationship between the bank promoters and the control of the insurance affiliates they have, whether the independence of the boards is sufficient in dealing with the problems of bancassurance, and how effectively the Reserve Bank of India \(RBI\) and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India \(IRDAI\) coordinate\. This study analyzes the modified insurance laws along with the banking, company, and securities laws\. I argue that, by the enactment of this Act, the scope for foreign investment is expanded and the independent\-board requirement is dispensed with for insurers having substantial foreign investment while the sole provision seeking to address the problems of overlapping of boards of insurers and banks, Section 32A, has not been notified\. The statutes also fail to allocate supervisory responsibilities among RBI and IRDAI\.

## [Applying ICH E9\(R1\) Sensitivity Analysis to an FDA Substantial\-Evidence Standard: An Allogeneic Cell Therapy Case Study in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy](../publications/bc322f138201c93811d7.md)

Anushree Siddharth Sheladia; Peivand Pirouzi

The statutory standard of substantial evidence of effectiveness is often discussed in general terms, but its practical meaning is best understood through the specific sensitivity analyses a regulator applies to a contested result\. This article examines a representative allogeneic cardiosphere\-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy \(DMD\), whose pivotal trial produced a sponsor\-reported, statistically significant functional benefit that collapsed toward non\-significance once a regulator applied its prespecified missing\-data handling rules to the sponsor&\#x27;s own revised analytic model, a robustness failure the article argues is the clearest practical illustration available of what the substantial\-evidence standard actually demands for a mutation\-agnostic therapy relying on a clinical functional endpoint rather than a validated surrogate\. The article develops the mechanism, the full analytic dispute, and the regulatory history this produced, situates the case within ICH estimand methodology, and proposes a real\-world evidence framework designed specifically around robustness and prespecification\. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs professionals designing statistical strategy for functional\-endpoint programs in rare disease\.Keywords: substantial evidence of effectiveness; sensitivity analysis; estimands; Duchenne muscular dystrophy; allogeneic cell therapy; regulatory artificial intelligence

## [Dynamic experiments: deconstructing the body in feminist experimental film and performance](../publications/bc339cdde4fa32b8771d.md)

Zhuoran Zhang

This study is situated at the intersection of two fields: the exploratory practices of female experimental artists and the speculative extension of the female body in imagery and philosophical texts\. Employing textual analysis alongside examples from visual texts, this research reconstructed and critiqued structuralist and postmodernist interpretations to explore deconstructive misreadings and reflections of the female body within temporal and spatial dimensions in experimental film works\. In doing so, the study offers innovative and diverse perspectives on the theoretical expression possibilities available to avant\-garde female artists, as Illustration as on the multidimensional elements within philosophical practice texts\. This includes the entanglement and contradictions betien bodily imagery and postmodernist texts, alongside a decentralised reconstruction of the social and natural realities of the body\. The project&\#x27;s theoretical framework was grounded fundamentally in the works of Michel Foucault and Gilles Deleuze, with significant reference to Rosi Braidotti, Judith Butler, Donna J\. Haraway, and Giorgio Agamben\. The analysis explored the malleability of bodily autonomy practices across time and space, proposing a future state of self\-awareness for the body that transcends gender\-centricity, and underscoring the significance of constructing social networks of embodied existence\.

Boymirzayev Zokirjon Mashrabboyevich

Maqolada raqamli iqtisodiyot va sun&\#x27;iy intellektning kichik biznes samaradorligiga ta&\#x27;sir etish mexanizmlari nazariy va statistik jihatdan tadqiq etilgan\. ## [Consumer Decision‐Making Styles Across Product Involvement Levels: A Mixed‐Methods Study of Online Flash Sale Events](../publications/bc3e39c7e3fd537d695a.md)

T Low; X Zhu; NS Butt

ABSTRACT Online flash sale events create urgency, scarcity and deep‐discount conditions, yet little is known about how consumer decision‐making styles vary across product involvement levels and how they are associated with situational involvement\. Grounded in consumer decision‐making styles and involvement theory, this sequential exploratory mixed‐methods research examines these variations across high‐, medium‐ and low‐involvement product categories and associations with situational involvement\. A preliminary study identified package holidays, high‐street clothes and takeaway food vouchers as high‐, medium‐ and low‐involvement categories, respectively\. Semi‐structured interviews with 28 UK online shoppers were analysed using content analysis with intercoder reliability assessment\. Questionnaire data from the package holidays \( n = 464\), high‐street clothes \( n = 521\) and takeaway food vouchers \( n = 420\) were analysed using structural equation modelling\. Brand consciousness, perfectionism, price consciousness and web security were positively associated with situational involvement across all three categories\. Fulfilment and impulsiveness were positively associated, and inertia negatively associated, for high‐street clothes and takeaway food vouchers\. Fashion consciousness was positively associated for high‐street clothes, whereas health consciousness for takeaway food vouchers and safety for package holidays were not significantly associated\. The findings qualify product‐neutral applications of consumer decision‐making styles by identifying category‐invariant, partially shared and category‐specific dimensions\. Retailers can use these patterns to tailor product information and communication to the decision‐making styles relevant to each product category\.

## [STETOSKOP DIGITAL DALAM MENINGKATKAN AKURASI DIAGNOSTIK AUSKULTASI JANTUNG](../publications/bc45447b11d592efcb54.md)

Zulfi Chumaidi; Dwi Hastuti; W\. Wijaya

Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan mengimplementasikan stetoskop digital guna meningkatkan akurasi diagnostik pada auskultasi jantung\. Stetoskop konvensional memiliki keterbatasan dalam sensitivitas suara, kemampuan reduksi noise, serta tidak mendukung perekaman dan analisis data secara digital, sehingga berpotensi menurunkan kualitas diagnosis\. Oleh karena itu, pengembangan stetoskop digital berbasis sensor akustik, penguat sinyal, konversi analog\-ke\-digital \(ADC\), dan mikrokontroler menjadi solusi yang menjanjikan\. Metode penelitian meliputi perancangan perangkat keras dan pengujian kinerja alat dengan membandingkan hasil pengukuran denyut jantung terhadap standar pemeriksaan ECG 12 lead\. Pengujian dilakukan pada lima responden laki\-laki dengan rentang usia 26–46 tahun, serta melibatkan tiga tenaga medis sebagai penguji\. Hasil pengukuran menunjukkan bahwa pada responden pertama diperoleh nilai 85–90 bpm dibandingkan ECG 90–91 bpm, responden kedua 77–80 bpm dibandingkan 79–81 bpm, responden ketiga 80–85 bpm dibandingkan 81–85 bpm, responden keempat 90–94 bpm dibandingkan 90–92 bpm, dan responden kelima 101–112 bpm dibandingkan 100–105 bpm\. Secara keseluruhan, selisih pengukuran berada pada rentang 1–7 bpm dengan rata\-rata deviasi yang rendah, menunjukkan tingkat akurasi yang baik dan konsistensi antar penguji\. Selain itu, stetoskop digital mampu meningkatkan kualitas sinyal melalui fitur penguatan dan penyaringan noise, sehingga memudahkan identifikasi suara jantung\.

## [Characterization of Optical and Mechanical Properties of Nanocellulose from Oil Palm Empty Fruit Bunch Biomass Using Acid Hydrolysis](../publications/bc4fede099538a73e512.md)

Wahyu Dian Laksanawati; Ranti An Nisaa; Advent Triyanti Halawa; Novika Aszyiamilatul Utami

This study aims to investigate the optical and mechanical properties of nanocrystalline cellulose \(NCC\) derived from oil palm empty fruit bunch \(OPEFB\) as a renewable lignocellulosic biomass for sustainable functional materials\. NCC was synthesized through sequential delignification, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis at concentrations of 30 wt% and 40 wt%\. The resulting NCC was characterized using UV–Vis spectroscopy and tensile testing\. UV–Vis analysis showed absorption peaks at 292, 291, and 289 nm for commercial NCC, OPEFB\-derived NCC hydrolyzed with 30 wt% H₂SO₄, and OPEFB\-derived NCC hydrolyzed with 40 wt% H₂SO₄, respectively\. Tauc plot analysis yielded estimated optical band gap energies of 4\.25, 4\.26, and 4\.29 eV, respectively\. Tensile testing showed that the commercial NCC exhibited the highest tensile strength and Young’s modulus, whereas the OPEFB\-derived NCC showed lower mechanical performance\. The NCC hydrolyzed with 30 wt% H₂SO₄ exhibited a tensile strength of 9\.65 MPa and a Young’s modulus of 0\.330 GPa, while the 40 wt% H₂SO₄ sample exhibited values of 3\.99 MPa and 0\.176 GPa, respectively\. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration resulted in a slight increase in the estimated optical band gap but a decrease in tensile strength and Young’s modulus\. Among the hydrolysis conditions investigated, 30 wt% H₂SO₄ provided a more balanced combination of optical and mechanical properties\. These findings indicate that OPEFB can serve as a renewable precursor for the development of cellulose\-based functional materials and provide a basis for further investigation of their structural and functional properties\.

## [Análisis bibliométrico de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación médica entre 2021 y 2026](../publications/bc53d1628ace81a0f137.md)

Mario Alexander Aguilar Balseca; Joane Nicole Aguilar Balseca; Daniel Alberto Hidrovo Moreno; Laura Katheryne Hernández León

Introduction: Generative artificial intelligence burst into medical education and led to accelerated growth in publications on its integration into the training of health professionals\. The structure of this scientific output in terms of volume, origin, journals and thematic trends remains unknown\. Objective: To analyze the scientific output on generative artificial intelligence in medical education indexed in Scopus between 2021 and 2026\. Methods: A descriptive bibliometric study was conducted\. The universe comprised the documents indexed in Scopus that addressed generative artificial intelligence in medical education, retrieved through a search strategy applied to title, abstract and keywords\. Productivity, impact and thematic trend indicators were analyzed with descriptive statistics and keyword co\-occurrence analysis with routines developed in Python\. Results: The sample included 3 223 documents, with sustained growth since 2023 and 90,4 % published between 2024 and 2026\. Original articles predominated \(72,9 %\)\. The United States \(27,0 %\) and China \(12,7 %\) led the output, with marginal Ibero\-American participation\. JMIR Medical Education headed the journal list\. The documents accumulated 52 761 citations \(average of 16,4\) and the keyword network comprised 132 terms grouped into 4 thematic clusters\. Conclusions: The scientific output showed recent and accelerated growth, concentrated in a few countries and specialized journals, with a thematic shift toward the responsible use of these tools and research gaps in Latin America\.

## [Procesamiento térmico y acidificación: un ejercicio de laboratorio de grado](../publications/bc5cfd6b7e0e28326422.md)

José Chaves\-Quesada; Oscar Acosta\-Montoya

Food engineering programs should provide students with practical activities related to the analysis of unit operations, within the context of food processing\. Both effectiveness and efficiency should be evaluated, so students can recognize the importance of achieving an objective and quantifying resources employed to achieve the goal\. We describe an undergraduate\-level food engineering laboratory exercise divided in two sections\. Both use carrot cylinders in vinegar solutions, packed in glass jars with metal lids, thermally processed in boiling water\. In the first section \(thermal processing\) students collect time and temperature data during a heat penetration study\. The experimental variable is the process time, and the response variable is the accumulated lethality \(Tref = 93\.3ºC, z = 8\.9ºC\)\. In the second section \(acidification\), students collect time and pH data during an acidification study\. The experimental variables are the acetic acid concentration and the acidification time, and the response variable is the carrot cylinders’ pH\. In both sections, students perform basic statistical analyses, carrying out calculations related to non\-linear regression, prediction intervals, inverse prediction, and model verification\. This laboratory exercise can assist in illustrating concepts, techniques, measurements, calculations, model development, and statistical analyses related to thermal processing and acidification of food\.

## [Factors associated with HPV vaccination coverage before pregnancy: a cross\-sectional study in a cohort of Pregnant Women](../publications/bc6593268d5cfe30940f.md)

Claudio Fiorilla; Fabio Massimo Contarino; Francesca Bella; Ilaria Cosentini; Paolo Colombo; Valeria Longo; Noemi Aloi; Gaspare Drago; Silvia Ruggieri

Background\. Human papillomavirus \(HPV\) infection is a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers\. Despite the availability of effective vaccines, HPV vaccination coverage remains suboptimal in Italy, particularly among women of childbearing age\. Pregnant women represent a key population for investigating vaccine hesitancy and its determinants\. This study aimed to explore socio\-demographic, behavioural, and perceptual factors associated with HPV vaccination coverage prior to pregnancy, using data from the NEHO cohort in Southern Italy\. Methods\. A cross\-sectional analysis was conducted on 567 pregnant women enrolled between 2018 and 2020 in the Priolo National Priority Site\. HPV vaccination status was obtained from local immunization databases\. Risk perception indices \(HPI, EHPI, HRPI, RPI\), and information sources were assessed via structured questionnaires\. Logistic regression and Bayesian Weighted Quantile Sum \(bWQS\) models were used to identify associations between vaccination status and independent variables\. Results\. Only 7\.4% of participants had HPV vaccination coverage prior to pregnancy\. Vaccinated women were significantly younger, unmarried, and more likely to have lower educational levels\. Higher scores on environmental and exposure hazard perception indices \(HPI and EHPI\) were positively associated with vaccination uptake\. Vaccinated individuals were more likely to attribute health protection responsibility to national institutions and industry leadership\. bWQS regression confirmed the relevance of risk perception in shaping vaccination behaviour, with EHPI contributing most to the overall effect\. Conclusion\. The results of this study suggest that tailored public health strategies that address risk perception, institutional trust, and population\-specific dynamics are essential to increase HPV vaccination coverage and reduce health inequalities\.

## [Physics\-Data Co\-driven Reliability\-Based Robust Design for Rolling Bearings Under Small\-Sample Uncertainty](../publications/bc660712bcb112e80439.md)

张志斌; Weibin Guo; Juan Wang; Qilong Chu; Xiangdong He

This study proposes a physics\-data fusion framework for reliability assessment and reliability\-based robust design of rolling bearings under small\-sample uncertainty\. Hertzian contact theory and finite element analysis \(FEM\) are integrated using inverse\-variance weighted and Bayesian fusion strategies, followed by Gaussian Kriging surrogate modeling\. L\-moments are employed to characterize the unknown radial\-load distribution from limited measurements, while asymmetric Gauss\-Hermite quadrature is used to obtain the first four moments of the limit\-state function\. The Maximum Entropy Method \(MEM\) is then applied for reliability assessment, and a dual\-surrogate\-assisted NSGA\-II framework is established to simultaneously minimize bearing mass and reliability sensitivity under R ≥ 0\.999\. Results show that Bayesian fusion achieves R2 = 0\.9932 and an average relative error of 0\.359% relative to FEM\. Both Kriging models achieve R2 &gt; 0\.97 in leave\-one\-out cross\-validation\. The MEM results agree well with million\-sample Monte Carlo simulation\. The selected balanced compromise designs reduce bearing mass by 5\.00% and 6\.09% for weighted and Bayesian fusion, respectively, while satisfying R ≥ 0\.999 and substantially reducing reliability sensitivity\.

## [Spatial macrophage\-fibroblast interactions in osteoarthritis synovium: inflammatory and fibrotic niches](../publications/bc715daa8ae88dc9273c.md)

Wei Huacheng; Ming Lei; Chendeng Lao; Ronghe Gu

Synovial inflammation and fibrosis often coexist in osteoarthritis, but a transition from one to the other has not been established\. This Mini Review examines macrophage\-fibroblast interactions in the surface lining, perivascular regions, and collagen\-rich synovium\. We integrate human spatial and single\-cell studies with functional experiments and map reported cell states, markers, locations, and functions\. Experimental evidence is clearest for inflammatory amplification\. Signals from recruited macrophages can increase fibroblast chemokine and cartilage\-degrading enzyme production, while fibroblast secretions and extracellular vesicles influence macrophage recruitment and activation\. Oncostatin M can induce inflammatory responses without increasing collagen deposition\. Matrix synthesis and mechanical responses characterize fibrotic niches, which may also contain fibroblasts with immunoregulatory functions\. These findings favor a model of potentially coexisting niches with overlapping but partly separable inflammatory, matrix\-remodeling, and tissue\-maintenance functions\. Spatial proximity in human tissue identifies candidate signaling partners; it cannot establish their dependence on specific signals or an inflammation\-to\-fibrosis sequence\. We discuss experiments that link defined cellular sources to local responses and measure pain, collagen deposition, clearance of dying cells, and lubrication separately\.

## [Fractional Optimal Control of AI\-TPACK Learning Dynamics with FBSM Numerical Study](../publications/bc7245e0393238d3a504.md)

Moosa Ebadi

In this study, we develop a fractional optimal control model for teachers&\#x27; artificial intelligence\-based technological pedagogical content knowledge \(AI\-TPACK\)\. Four state variables: AI\-related technological knowledge \(AI\-TK\), technological content knowledge \(AI\-TCK\), technological pedagogical knowledge \(AI\-TPK\), and integrated AI\-TPACK are used in the model\. We used two bounded decision variables: technology\-integration workshops and specialized technology courses\. A direct\-method proof establishes the existence of an optimal pair\. Pontryagin conditions yield the fractional adjoint and the classical pseudo\-state system used numerically, as well as separate projection formulas for both interventions\. A local contraction theorem gives sufficient conditions for convergence of the relaxed forward\-backward sweep method \(FBSM\)\. The results support a staged policy: moderately stronger technology\-integration workshops, complemented by specialized courses, provide a more efficient pathway than either intervention component alone\. The scenario coefficients are used in this work to solve the AI\-TPACK optimal control model numerically\.

## [Prism Attention: Proposal\-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference](../publications/bc728d51c9d47e5dda6c.md)

Zhenxu Tian; Kebin Liu; Zhengwu Yang; Yi Su; Qingqing Dang; Yanlin Sha; Kaipeng Deng; Dianhai Yu; Yanjun Ma; Juntao Li; Min Zhang

Long\-context decoding in large language models \(LLMs\) is increasingly bottlenecked by the memory and computation required to attend over an ever\-growing Key\-Value \(KV\) cache at each autoregressive step\. Although token\-level sparse attention reduces this burden by restricting computation to a small subset of relevant past tokens, its practical gains are often offset by repeatedly recomputing layer\-wise sparse indices as the context grows\. A common remedy is to share sparse indices across layers by computing them only at designated anchor layers, but such static reuse ignores the layer\-wise evolution of attention patterns, causing the reused indices to progressively deviate from the layer\-specific optima and incur substantial attention loss\. By revisiting cross\-layer sparsity from the perspective of attention dynamics, we find that inter\-layer salient token shift is highly localized: although the exact top\-$κ$ indices differ across layers, the core high\-attention tokens remain stable, with changes concentrated near the expanded boundary of previously selected regions\. Motivated by this, we propose Prism Attention, a proposal\-refined sparse attention framework\. It replaces rigid cross\-layer index reuse with a coarse\-to\-fine strategy, preserving layer\-wise adaptability while retaining the efficiency benefits of cross\-layer sharing\. Extensive experiments show that Prism Attention achieves state\-of\-the\-art performance among mainstream sparse attention methods on both reasoning and long\-context benchmarks, while attaining a $3\.4\\times$ end\-to\-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context length\.

## [Resilience assessment and prediction of fresh agricultural product supply chains using variable fuzzy recognition and machine learning](../publications/bc86f8e288403927e5db.md)

Shangbing Gao; Anming Bai; Xinguo Sun; Anbang Peng; Shilan Li; Wei Zhao; Shuaifei Ma

Fresh agricultural products are highly perishable and sensitive to transportation, storage, and handling conditions, which makes their supply chains particularly vulnerable to disruptions\. Such disruptions can interrupt product flows and reduce both quality and availability\. Traditional risk analysis methods mainly focus on uncertainty and the probability of adverse events, but they do not adequately capture the ability of supply chains to recover and adapt following disruptions\. To address this limitation, this study develops a resilience evaluation and prediction framework for fresh agricultural product supply chains \(FAPSCs\)\. The framework is structured around three dimensions: production, transportation, and consumption\. A hybrid modeling approach is proposed by integrating variable fuzzy set theory with machine learning\. The variable fuzzy set model is used for dynamic resilience assessment, while a convolutional neural network \(CNN\) is employed to capture temporal dynamics and perform prediction\. Indicator weights are determined by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process \(AHP\) and the CRITIC method to improve robustness and interpretability\. Using panel data from 31 provinces in China from 2009 to 2023, the results show that the proposed framework effectively distinguishes different resilience levels across regions\. The CNN model captures temporal variations, including peak and off\-peak fluctuations, and outperforms baseline models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Linear Regression, particularly in modeling nonlinear patterns and high\-resilience cases\. Overall, the proposed approach demonstrates strong robustness under limited or noisy data conditions and provides practical support for early warning, risk mitigation, and decision making in FAPSC management\.

## [Digitalization and Environmental Quality in the OECD : A Structural‐Break Analysis of the Ecological Footprint and Load Capacity Factor](../publications/bc89fbb11e43d8b1f921.md)

Can Apaydın; Mustafa BİLİK

ABSTRACT This study examines how digitalization shapes environmental quality in OECD countries using the ecological footprint \(demand side\) and the load capacity factor \(supply side\) within a balanced panel dataset of 30 countries covering the 2002–2021 period\. Income, urbanization, natural resource rents, and renewable energy variables are each included, along with four indicators of digitalization \(fixed broadband, fixed‐line telephony, mobile cellular connections, and internet penetration\)\. Second‐generation tests employed in this process confirm the cointegration findings by accounting for cross‐sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, and structural breaks\. Common Correlated Effects Mean Group \(CCE‐MG\) estimates indicate that digitalization does not have a consistent impact on environmental quality\. The findings reveal that while income growth expands the ecological footprint \(≈0\.93–1\.00\) and reduces biocapacity \(−0\.77 to −1\.02\), renewable energy usage reverses both effects\. Analyses allowing for coefficient variation across regimes demonstrate that broadband and the internet reduce the ecological footprint \(−0\.084 and −0\.100\) and increase biocapacity \(0\.117 and 0\.148\), but only after a structural break occurring around the 2007–2009 financial crisis\.

## [Bio‐Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra‐Fast and Context‐Aware Human‐Robot Interaction](../publications/bc8d53ef11bf96cbdbea.md)

Jinhyeok Oh; Hun Jang; 최주성; Heejun Moon; Joonbum Bae

ABSTRACT Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution\. However, existing proprioceptive or vision‐based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions\. Here, we propose a human‐inspired tactile perception and reflex control framework that integrates a high‐performance single‐electrode triboelectric nanogenerator \(STENG\) tactile array, distributed microcontroller‐based reflex processing, and impact‐aware high‐level motion generation\. The STENG array, fabricated using optimized silicone and liquid‐metal printing, provides high‐bandwidth, high‐resolution mechanical sensing and robust surface conformability\. A lightweight neural classifier embedded directly in the reflex layer enables real‐time discrimination between human and object contact from raw triboelectric waveforms\. The distributed control architecture achieves a total reflex latency of 2\.2 ms, outperforming the centralized controller by more than a factor of five\. Experimental demonstrations show that the system can generate an immediate stop followed by high‐level retraction under human contact, while selectively modulating motion during object contact, providing context‐aware reflex actions\. The proposed architecture bridges the gap between ultra‐fast tactile sensing and high‐level motion intelligence, enabling fast, safe, and human‐friendly physical interaction for future human‐robot interaction \(HRI\) applications\.

## [Artificial intelligence\-driven imaging in sickle cell retinopathy: Advancing early detection, risk stratification, and precision ophthalmology](../publications/bc9b390ded687c5b678d.md)

Tarun Sahu; Deepankar Mondal; Yashwant Kumar Ratre; Henu Kumar Verma

Sickle cell disease \(SCD\) is a disorder of genetically inherited red blood cells \(RBCs\), wherein it is manifested clinically as sickling of RBCs, due to polymerization of hemoglobin S\. SCD patients frequently face RBCs clumping, blocking of blood vessels and capillaries along with persistent hemolysis\.Sickle cell retinopathy \(SCR\), is a SCD associated disorder in the peripheral retina, responsible for several features like vasoocclusion, ischemia, vitreous hemorrhage and neovascularization within the retina and adjoining regions\.While these are manageable features, some severe cases report retinal detachment and ultimately vision impairment in patients\.As early signs of SCR are not usually manifested visually, its early diagnosis becomes the limiting factor for devising effective management strategies in patients\.Artificial intelligence \(AI\) assisted deep learning models have very recently being utilized and provides a promising alternative in assisting early diagnosis, staging, and monitoring disease progression\.Traditional retinal imaging methods like fundus photography, fluorescein angiography, optical coherence tomography and optical coherence tomography angiography scans have always assisted ophthalmologists to make clinical decisions for patients\.Recently, these methods were being used to train AI models for easy and efficient analysis of such scans\.As a growing field, works in this area have transitioned our understanding of image analyses and promises a fast, objective and efficient interpretation\.This review discusses; how traditional methods captures structural damages to peripheral retina and summarizes recent research work done in this field to integrate AI driven models based on deep learning and machine learning\.We summarize here AI based strategies for SCR screening and diagnosis, while underlining their clinical applicability, utilities and future translational promises towards ascertaining personalized ophthalmology\.

## [Teaching and the acquisition of complex and opaque cultural skills and knowledge among the Koygu hunter\-gatherers and Nyangatom pastoralists of southern Ethiopia](../publications/bcaa97a0108d21fc2405.md)

Temechegn G\. Bira; Barry S\. Hewlett; Edward H\. Hagen

In order to adapt to diverse ecological and social settings, humans learn skills, norms, and knowledge from others\. These skills and knowledge range from relatively transparent skills to complex cultural norms and rituals\. The study utilized focal\-follow behavioral observations of 60 children aged 3–18 years, to evaluate cultural evolutionary and social learning predictions about the relationship between teaching and learning opaque and complex skills and knowledge in small\-scale cultures\. Each child was observed for 2 hours during daylight hours between 6:00 a\.m\. to 6:00 p\.m\. Data were gathered from the Koygu transitional hunter\-gatherer and Nyangatom pastoralist cultures in southern Ethiopia\. The study found that \(1\) teaching generally increased with child age, especially among the Nyangatom; \(2\) Nyangatom children were more likely to learn from their parents and other adults, whereas Koygu children were more likely to learn from other children, including siblings; \(3\) teaching was significantly related to the opacity of the skill or knowledge, but was not related to skill complexity, and \(4\) the relative proportion of transparent, complex and opaque skills or knowledge did not vary by child age\.
