## [Physics driven incremental meta\-learning rolling bearing fault diagnosis under few\-shot emerging conditions](../publications/bcb3c76a942c75527065.md)

Dongming Xiao; Hengshu Chen; Jiakai Ding; Xuanrui Zhang

Abstract Abstract: Traditional deep learning fault diagnosis methods rely on sufficiently labeled training data, which limits their ability to adapt to the continual emergence of new fault data\. Although continual learning methods can alleviate catastrophic forgetting to some extent, the model’s diagnostic performance is still significantly impacted under few\-shot emerging fault data\. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics\-driven incremental meta\-learning method \(PIML\) for rolling bearing fault diagnosis\. First, the method uses a physics model to generate multi\-condition bearing fault data, providing original training data for the meta\-training stage\. This approach effectively alleviates the problem of limited training data\. Then, under the model\-agnostic meta\-learning \(MAML\) framework, the model is meta\-trained using the simulated data, enabling the model to rapidly adapt to few\-shot emerging fault data under self\-labeling conditions\. Finally, the self\-labeling fault data are combined with historical data stored in the memory buffer through prototype replay\. Such a mechanism enables continual incremental diagnosis of bearing faults\. The proposed method in this paper was validated using existing datasets\. The experimental results show that under different situations of few\-shot emerging fault data, the accuracy of the proposed method is higher than that of other methods\.

## [Voice features in paediatric ADHD: baseline group differences and longitudinal change under methylphenidate](../publications/bcbeb14d07d6509477b5.md)

Rachel Bamberger; Gianna Kuhles; Leon D\. Lotter; Juergen Dukart; Kerstin Konrad; Thomas Günther; Michael Siniatchkin; Michael Fuchs; Georg G\. von Polier

Diagnosis and treatment monitoring of attention\-deficit/hyperactivity disorder \(ADHD\) largely rely on subjective assessments, highlighting the need for objective markers\. Voice features and speech embeddings represent promising candidates, as they may offer an objective, scalable and clinically valuable complement to current practice\. Yet it remains largely unclear which features are most informative for distinguishing ADHD and monitoring treatment effects, and which speech tasks best elicit these differences\. Twenty\-seven children with ADHD and 27 age\-matched neurotypical controls completed six speech tasks across two study visits\. Children with ADHD were unmedicated at baseline and were assessed under prescribed methylphenidate treatment at follow\-up, whereas controls underwent repeated assessment without intervention\. Established acoustic voice features and high\-dimensional speech embeddings were extracted and analysed using linear mixed models to examine baseline group differences and group\-by\-time interaction effects reflecting medication\-associated change patterns\. At baseline, children with ADHD showed a lower and more variable pitch \(F0 mean, F0 variability\), altered spectral properties \(MFCC1/MFCC2 variability\), and reduced rhythmic stability \(variability of voiced\-segment length\) compared to controls\. Group\-by\-time interaction effects indicated medication\-associated modulation in the ADHD group, including reduced loudness variability and normalization of first formant bandwidth toward control values\. Speech embeddings \(Whisper but not WavLM\) showed FDR\-significant baseline and interaction effects\. Free speech tasks, particularly picture description, yielded the most robust and consistent effects\. These findings support further investigation of speech\-based measures as potential digital biomarkers in ADHD, with picture description emerging as a particularly promising task for future clinical assessment protocols\.Clinical trial registration: German Clinical Trials Registry, registration no\. DRKS00030766, Registration Date: 12 December 2022\. Available: https://drks\.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00030766\.

## [Inteligencia Artificial en la Animación Digital: Impacto en el Mercado Laboral y la Toma de Decisiones Creativas](../publications/bcbf6ac2ef45bdf22b85.md)

Fernando Fernández Gómez; Julieta Hernández Ramírez; Viviana Yasmin Cahuich Cruz; Karen Itzel Cordero Martínez

Este estudio analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial \(IA\) en la toma de decisiones estratégicas de la animación digital y sus consecuencias laborales\. Mediante una revisión sistemática documental PRISMA de 50 artículos \(2021–2026\), se evalúa cómo la IA genera eficiencia operativa \(reducción de tiempos de renderizado, automatización de tareas repetitivas\) pero también desplaza empleos tradicionales, especialmente en México y América Latina, donde más de 200,000 animadores enfrentan riesgo de disrupción en cinco años\. Los hallazgos revelan polarización: algunos autores destacan la IA como herramienta colaborativa que potencia la creatividad; otros advierten sobre pérdida de empleos, homogeneización estética y erosión de la autonomía autoral\. Se concluye que la IA influye directamente en decisiones creativas \(estilos visuales, movimientos, optimización\), pero requiere un enfoque equilibrado: formación híbrida arte\-IA, marcos éticos y políticas de transición laboral para proteger la empleabilidad sin renunciar a los beneficios de la automatización\. La esencia del estudio es que el desafío no es rechazar la tecnología, sino integrarla preservando el talento humano\.

## [Association of ambient temperature and diurnal temperature range exposure during adolescence with adult IIEF\-5 and PEDT scores: a cross\-sectional study in China](../publications/bcc04421a05712cd1735.md)

Weiqian Zhang; Rui Qu; Jiayu Wang; Jingxuan Wang; Feng Zhang; Yiqiu Wei; Zihan Guo; Yan Zhang; Jue Liu; Tailang Yin; Dongdong Tang

Background Exposure to extreme temperatures and diurnal temperature range \(DTR\) has been linked to impaired male reproductive health, yet studies investigating the associations between such exposures during adolescence and adult male sexual function \(MSF\) remain limited\. Methods We analyzed data from 5,039 sexually active males across 31 provinces in China, drawn from a two\-stage quota\-sampled cross\-sectional online survey conducted in 2023\. Exposure periods included all adolescence \(10–19 years\), early adolescence \(10–14 years\), and late adolescence \(15–19 years\)\. Adolescent temperature and DTR exposures were retrospectively estimated using participants&\#x27; current adult residential addresses\. Generalized additive models and hierarchical linear models were employed to assess the associations between temperature and DTR exposure and self\-reported MSF, measured by the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool \(PEDT\) and the International Index of Erectile Function\-5 \(IIEF\-5\)\. Results Generalized additive models suggested U\-shaped and J\-shaped trends for ambient temperature and DTR with PEDT scores, respectively, and formal tests confirmed significant departure from linearity\. Exposure to extremely hot temperatures \(&gt; 90th percentile\) during early adolescence was associated with higher PEDT scores \( β : 0\.67, 95% CI: 0\.24–1\.10\) compared to moderate temperatures\. Higher DTR exposure \(&gt;80th percentile\) during all adolescence \( β : 0\.75, 95% CI: 0\.29–1\.22\), early adolescence \( β : 0\.75, 95% CI: 0\.28–1\.21\), and late adolescence \( β : 0\.48, 95% CI: 0\.00–0\.96\) was also associated with higher PEDT scores\. No significant associations were observed between temperature or DTR exposure and IIEF\-5 scores\. Conclusions Our study provides preliminary epidemiological evidence that adolescent exposure to extremely hot temperatures and higher DTR is associated with higher PEDT scores in adulthood, with no association observed for IIEF\-5 scores\.

## [ARES\-SI: adaptive reinforcement\-enhanced sampling for suicidal ideation](../publications/bcca63c9b336718be913.md)

Ross Jacobucci; Taylor A\. Burke; Ying Cheng; Brooke A\. Ammerman

Suicidal ideation \(SI\) fluctuates rapidly within individuals, but standard ecological momentary assessment \(EMA\) uses fixed schedules that miss critical risk windows\. We present ARES\-SI \(Adaptive Reinforcement\-Enhanced Sampling for Suicidal Ideation\), a reinforcement learning system that personalizes EMA timing to individual risk patterns\. ARES\-SI combines random forest models to predict active SI probability and non\-response likelihood with a Q\-learning algorithm to determine optimal assessment intervals \(30 min for high\-risk states, 3 h for low\-risk states, and next day to reduce burden\)\. We trained the system using EMA data from 98 participants across three studies with varied sampling frequencies \(4–15 assessments per day; 2359 positive active SI responses\) over 28\-day protocols\. In validation testing \( N = 34; 374 positive active SI responses\), the random forest models achieved an AUC of 0\.865 for active SI and 0\.750 for non\-response\. ARES\-SI demonstrated 65% higher action selection accuracy than random scheduling \(0\.781 vs\. 0\.474; macro F1 = 0\.650 vs\. 0\.377\), with stronger detection of high\-risk windows \(30\-min recall = 0\.810 vs\. 0\.392\) and efficient low\-risk scheduling \(3\-h precision = 0\.972 vs\. 0\.876\)\. These findings provide initial evidence that reinforcement learning can adapt assessment timing to momentary risk\.

## [A Data\-Driven Smart University Framework for Sustainable Internationalisation at Home: A PLS\-SEM Study in Vietnamese Higher Education](../publications/bcd0d9e7c422733eab9d.md)

Loc Thi My Nguyen; Tuong Sy Hoang

Internationalisation at Home is increasingly recognised as an alternative to conventional physical mobility, offering opportunities to broaden equitable access to knowledge and promote sustainable practices in higher education\. This study develops and empirically tests a data\-driven smart university framework as an integrative model for examining the structural relationships between technological foundations and the sustainable implementation of Internationalisation at Home\. A quantitative, cross\-sectional research design was employed, using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 312 managers and faculty members involved in transnational education programmes in Vietnam\. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling\. The findings support the proposed structural relationships within the model\. Specifically, integrated data infrastructure has a positive relationship with faculty digital competence\. An ethical data governance framework and the adoption of learning analytics and artificial intelligence are also positively associated with the quality of Internationalisation at Home\. In turn, the quality of Internationalisation at Home has a statistically significant positive relationship with perceived institutional sustainability\. The study provides empirical evidence of the structural links between digital technological innovation and the sustainability of higher education internationalisation\. The findings offer a basis for reconsidering institutional resource allocation strategies in developing countries, with greater priority given to integrated data architectures, digital capability development, and responsible data governance\.

## [Histopatoloji görüntülerinde anlamsal çekirdek segmentasyonu için ön işleme tekniklerinin karşılaştırmalı analizi](../publications/bcd1fe47e65e6552b540.md)

Abdulkadir Gulsen

Histopatolojik çekirdek segmentasyonu, bilgisayar destekli patoloji uygulamalarında temel bir bileşen olmakla birlikte, boyama protokolleri, tarayıcı farklılıkları ve doku hazırlama süreçlerinden kaynaklanan varyasyonlar, derin öğrenme tabanlı modellerin genellenebilirliğini olumsuz etkileyebilmektedir\. Bu çalışmada, MoNuSeg veri seti üzerinde SegFormer\-B2 mimarisi kullanılarak, yaygın önişleme bileşenlerinin anlamsal çekirdek segmentasyonu performansı üzerindeki etkisi kontrollü bir deneysel çerçevede incelenmiştir\. Tüm deneylerde model mimarisi ve eğitim prosedürü sabit tutulmuş, yalnızca önişleme adımları değiştirilmiştir; bu sayede önişleme bileşenlerinin göreli katkıları kontrollü ve yorumlanabilir biçimde analiz edilmiştir\. Bu kapsamda, boyama normalizasyonu \(Macenko\), kontrast iyileştirme \(CLAHE\), uzamsal filtreleme \(Gauss\) ve renk tabanlı veri artırmanın tekil ve birleşik kullanımlarını içeren K0–K7 önişleme konfigürasyonları karşılaştırmalı olarak değerlendirilmiştir\. Model performansı, bölge tabanlı örtüşmeyi değerlendiren Dice ve IoU ile sınır duyarlılığını yansıtan BF1 ve HD95 ölçütleri kullanılarak raporlanmıştır\. Elde edilen sonuçlar, önişleme adımlarının segmentasyon performansı üzerinde konfigürasyona ve bileşen etkileşimlerine duyarlı olduğunu göstermektedir\. Gauss tabanlı uzamsal filtreleme, tüm ölçütlerde dengeli iyileşmeler sağlayarak sınır kararlılığını desteklemiştir\. Renk tabanlı veri artırma bölge tabanlı ölçütlerde sınırlı fakat istikrarlı kazanımlar üretirken, CLAHE ve Macenko temelli normalizasyonların belirli konfigürasyonlarda performans düşüşlerine yol açabildiği gözlenmiştir\. Bu bulgular, önişleme tasarımının kritik bir değişken olduğunu ve daha fazla önişlemenin her zaman daha iyi segmentasyon performansı anlamına gelmediğini ortaya koymaktadır\.

## [Conceptual Design and Preliminary Embedded Applicability Evaluation of an AI\-Based Predictive Maintenance Residual Current Device Using Time\-Series Analysis of Leakage Current](../publications/bcd5714571b141c69e37.md)

Inju Jung; Hyungpyo Kim

This study proposes a conceptual AI\-based predictive maintenance architecture for residual current devices \(RCDs\) using time\-series analysis of leakage current and evaluates the preliminary embedded applicability of deep learning models\. Leakage current data were collected at 1 s intervals for 120 h using two ACS712 current sensors\. LSTM, GRU, and Transformer models were trained and evaluated using the same dataset configuration and evaluation framework\. Their performance was compared using MAE, RMSE, trainable parameter count, estimated FP32 weight memory, and CPU inference time\. LSTM and GRU showed lower prediction errors than the Transformer\. GRU achieved prediction accuracy comparable to LSTM while requiring the fewest parameters and the shortest CPU inference time, suggesting its potential as a lightweight candidate for future MCU\-based implementation\. Based on these results, the proposed architecture is designed to support early warning and predictive maintenance while retaining the conventional RCD protection function\.

## [Técnicas para el modelado y la generación de audio en trastornos del habla : evaluación comparativa de tecnologías de generación de voz para la síntesis de habla con disartria\.](../publications/bcd89cabd52734276594.md)

M\. \(Mathew\) Gutiérrez Montenegro

En la actualidad, el crecimiento acelerado de la inteligencia artificial ha abierto nuevos caminos para el procesamiento y generación de audios que imitan la voz\. Sin embargo, para la disartria, estos nuevos horizontes enfrentan un imponente desafío: la escasez de datos para el entrenamiento y evaluación de modelos de vanguardia\. Las personas con disartria presentan alteraciones motoras del habla, lo que puede afectar la inteligibilidad, la prosodia y la calidad acústica de la voz; esto provoca una limitación al desarrollar tecnologías orientadas a esta patología\. Bajo este enfoque, se propone la evaluación comparativa de tecnologías de generación y conversión de voz para la creación de datos sintéticos del habla disártrica\. En el capítulo 1 se presenta el problema, los objetivos, el alcance y el marco teórico relacionado con disartria, tecnologías generativas, conversión de voz y métricas objetivas\. En el Capítulo 2 se describe la metodología, incluyendo el uso del dataset TORGO, los procesos de limpieza, normalización, extracción de representaciones acústicas y ejecución de los modelos seleccionados\. En el Capítulo 3 se presentan los resultados de la comparación entre enfoques basados en redes generativas, modelos secuenciales y modelos de difusión, evaluados mediante métricas objetivas de inteligibilidad, calidad acústica y similitud espectral\. Finalmente, se exponen las conclusiones y recomendaciones orientadas a identificar qué tecnologías presentan mejores condiciones técnicas para futuras estrategias de aumento de datos sintéticos en datasets disártricos\.

## [Understanding Human\-AI Trust in Military AI Applications: A Multistage Human Factors Framework](../publications/bcdc30faafbf30fab818.md)

Kangwon Kim

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly used in military systems to support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, autonomous operations, logistics, command and control, and decision support\. Effective use, however, depends not only on technical performance but also on how operators perceive, interpret, evaluate, and rely on AI outputs under uncertainty, time pressure, and adversarial interference\. This study presents a conceptual integrative review informed by a structured supplementary literature search and synthesis\. It synthesizes human factors, human–automation trust, human–AI teaming, military AI, and industrial engineering literature to develop an iterative multistage framework of human–AI trust in military applications\. Trust is conceptualized as dynamic situational trust in a specific military AI system during task interaction, while dispositional, initial, and learned trust are treated as antecedent conditions\. The framework distinguishes four analytically separable but functionally interdependent stages—perception, interpretation, evaluation, and trust judgment and reliance decision—and identifies four military\-relevant moderators: system transparency, explainability, and behavioral predictability; data quality and information uncertainty; adversarial vulnerability; and operational and organizational context\. The framework clarifies conceptual pathways to calibrated reliance, overtrust, and undertrust, and derives implications for task analysis, interface evaluation, human\-centered design, operator training, and empirical validation\.

## [A two\-stage optimization method for wide\-range single\-electron quantum magnetic sensing](../publications/bceab40970931a2a6b60.md)

Shiqian Guo; Jianqing Liu; Thinh Le; Huaiyu Dai

Quantum magnetic sensing is a new paradigm for detecting ultra\-weak magnetic fields\. Its protocol design concerns the devise of optimal sensing parameters to estimate the underlying signals of interest \(SoI\)\. Existing studies mainly rely on adaptive algorithms based on black\-box AI models or formula\-driven principled searches\. However, when the SoI spans a wide range and the quantum sensor has physical constraints, these methods may fail to converge efficiently or optimally, causing prolonged interrogation times and reduced accuracy\. This work presents a new protocol using a two\-stage optimization method, consisting of a Bayesian neural network to first narrow the SoI range and a federated reinforcement learning agent to subsequently calibrate the SoI\. The protocol is developed and evaluated in the challenging context of an NV\-center spin system with single\-shot readout and limited sensing time; and yet it achieves significant improvements in both accuracy and resource efficiency compared to the state\-of\-the\-art\.

## [MEDIAÇÃO ALGORÍTMICA E REDUÇÃO DA VARIABILIDADE DECISÓRIA: UMA ANÁLISE JURÍDICO\-EMPÍRICA DA INFLUÊNCIA DA IA SOBRE A INDIVIDUALIZAÇÃO DA DECISÃO JUDICIAL](../publications/bcf0767325d0725eed2d.md)

Fabrício Santana Oliveira Santos; Rafael Bianchini Glavam; Chaiane Rebeca Silva de Sousa; Ígor Dias da Silva; João Artur de Souza

A crescente incorporação de sistemas de inteligência artificial à atividade judicial amplia a capacidade de recuperar precedentes, organizar informações, gerar fundamentações e identificar padrões decisórios\. Nesse contexto, o artigo analisa possíveis efeitos da mediação algorítmica sobre a individualização da decisão judicial, compreendida como a consideração efetiva das circunstâncias, fatos, argumentos, provas e diferenças juridicamente relevantes do caso concreto\. A pesquisa adota abordagem qualitativa, bibliográfica, exploratória e interpretativa, articulando estudos jurídicos, empíricos e técnicos sobre recuperação de informações, variabilidade decisória, sensibilidade factual, retroalimentação de sistemas e vulnerabilidades associadas ao prompt injection\. Os estudos analisados, embora desenvolvidos em contextos jurisdicionais e metodológicos distintos, apontam para uma tendência de redução da variabilidade e de maior uniformização em ambientes mediados por inteligência artificial\. Essa convergência pode produzir efeitos sobre a individualização, sobretudo quando padrões decisórios adquirem maior presença no ambiente informacional utilizado para a tomada de decisão\. Ao mesmo tempo, evidências empíricas indicam que julgadores humanos podem considerar elementos qualitativos e contextuais do caso concreto ausentes dos dados estruturados utilizados na modelagem algorítmica\. Conclui\-se que a redução da variabilidade associada à mediação algorítmica produz efeitos sobre a individualização das decisões, ao favorecer maior convergência decisória, ao mesmo tempo em que evidencia a relevância da atuação humana na consideração de elementos qualitativos e contextuais do caso concreto que podem não estar representados nos dados estruturados\. Os resultados, contudo, devem ser interpretados à luz dos modelos, versões, arquiteturas e contextos específicos investigados\. A rápida evolução dos sistemas de inteligência artificial impõe, ainda, um desafio adicional à pesquisa empírica, uma vez que evidências produzidas sobre determinada versão podem perder capacidade explicativa diante de modificações tecnológicas posteriores\.

## [From digital technologies to business sustainability: the central role of innovation in Thai SMEs](../publications/bcfec8b210204917e2e6.md)

Parinya Pattayanun; Sumaman Pankham; Somchai Lekcharoen

This study examines how AI\-chatbot usage, social media usage, and customer value anticipation are associated with business sustainability in Thai small and medium\-sized enterprises \(SMEs\) through an innovation\-centered capability pathway\. Drawing on a dynamic capabilities perspective, the model positions innovation as the central mechanism through which digital and customer\-sensing inputs are linked to network learning, business performance, and business sustainability\. The measurement instrument was initially validated through a Fuzzy\-Rough Set e\-Delphi procedure involving 23 experts, followed by covariance\-based structural equation modeling using 703 valid SME responses\. A pooled seven\-construct confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated satisfactory measurement\-model fit, reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity\. All 10 hypothesized structural relationships were statistically significant\. AI\-chatbot usage, customer value anticipation, and social media usage were positively associated with innovation, while innovation was associated with network learning and business sustainability\. Network learning, customer value anticipation, and social media usage were associated with business performance, which in turn was associated with business sustainability\. The model explained modest\-to\-moderate variance in the endogenous constructs\. The study contributes by extending prior SME capability research with AI\-chatbot and social media inputs and by showing how innovation provides a central pathway connecting digital engagement and customer sensing with learning, performance, and longer\-term business sustainability\.

## [A facet joint landmark\-guided approach for multi\-segmental DRG injection with limited bone removal in mice](../publications/bd052989e19aa17f2c44.md)

Ruohan Yan; Sike Sun; Zipeng Zhou; Lei Ma; Junhao Deng; Jinhui Zhang

Background Targeted gene delivery to the dorsal root ganglion \(DRG\) has been developed as a valuable approach for pain research\. Nevertheless, conventional DRG microinjection approaches suffer from notable drawbacks: vertebral bone resection and facet joint destruction induce spinal instability, extensive tissue adhesion impedes repeated surgery, and multi\-segment targeting remains challenging\. Methods To establish a multi\-segmental DRG injection workflow, we developed a vertebral counting scheme based on mouse anatomical dissection\. To guide our selection of target segments for viral delivery, Thy1\-YFP\-H transgenic mice was used to trace segmental DRG innervation patterns with good resolution\. Anatomical dissection was then performed to examine the precise spatial relationship between each target DRG and its neighboring facet joints\. With this anatomical roadmap, together with a custom designed temporary spinal stabilizer, we established a standardized injection procedure applicable to user\-specified levels\. Post\-operatively, animal behavior was serially assessed, and finally in vivo GCaMP calcium imaging was conducted to verify functional viral transduction\. Results Vertebral counting based on the V\-shaped white lines on the spinous processes enabled reliable identification of lumbar segmentation\. YFP tracing clarified distinct segmental innervation patterns: L1\-L2 fibers do not contribute to the sciatic nerve; L3\-L5 collectively form the sciatic nerve; L6 fibers, plus minor L5 branches, constitute the pudendal nerve\. Additional anatomical dissection confirmed that drilling at the base of the inferior articular process of the cranial vertebra provided a direct access route to the L3\-L6 DRGs\. Serial behavioral monitoring post\-injection revealed transient functional disturbances, most of which resolved by postoperative day 21\. Finally, concurrent jGCaMP8s imaging confirmed successful functional transduction: air\-puff stimulation elicited robust calcium responses in transduced DRG neurons, whereas no such signals were detected in wild\-type controls\. Conclusion We have established a reproducible viral delivery method that minimizes bone resection and avoids gross facet joint destruction through laminar drilling, while enabling multi\-segmental injection into mouse L3\-L6 DRGs\. The combination of longitudinal behavioral monitoring and stimulus\-evoked calcium imaging supported the surgical feasibility and functional transduction of this approach\. This method thus provides an experimental toolkit that should be useful for dissecting somatic\-visceral pain crosstalk through multi\-segmental DRG genetic manipulation\.

## [Carbon\-Aware Dynamic Data Routing in Cloud Pipelines](../publications/bd14a43eac5b41902b5f.md)

Pradeep Rao Vennamaneni; Sri Prudhvi Adusumilli; Naveen Shrivastava; Mahesh Marri; Sojy John; Venkata Phaneendra Reddi

As energy consumption in data centers and carbon emissions become more and more critical environmental issues for the information technology industry, energy consumption is accelerating\. In 2020, global data centres consumed about 200 TWh of electricity, representing a small fraction of global electricity demand of one per cent\. While absolute energy consumption has been relatively constant due to improvements in efficiency, the carbon intensity of energy consumption has emerged as the most important consideration as the percentage of renewables in the electricity supplied to the grid fluctuates significantly from one geographic area to another and one time period to the next\. In this paper, the authors will present the main research works prior to 2020 on carbon\-aware dynamic data routing in cloud pipelines: computational workloads are dynamically moved in real\-time to the data centre with the lowest instantaneous carbon intensity\. The synthesis considers the basics of energy consumption models, geographical load balancing algorithms, virtual machine consolidation heuristics, renewable energy integration frameworks and multi\-cloud carbon management strategies\. Literature provides quantitative evidence showing that carbon\-aware routing can cut carbon emissions by 30\-45% compared to latency\-first routing, with only a small latency increase of 3 to 8 milliseconds\. A maximum of 69 percent energy savings is possible using combined VM dynamic consolidation and carbon\-aware placement\. It also reviews incentive structures for colocation facilities and self\-adaptive scheduling algorithms, discusses the key architectural aspects, algorithmic bottlenecks, and future challenges in the field\.

## [Gait freezing onset and termination prediction in Parkinson disease using shank sensor acceleration data](../publications/bd16354e5e612c36d98f.md)

Preeti Khera; Ashok Kumar; Rajat Kapila

Motor impairment Freezing\-of\-Gait \(FoG\) is associated with reduced mobility leading to falls usually occurring in advancing Parkinson’s disease \(PD\)\. Cueing techniques have been successfully used to alleviate the event\. Although, FoG prediction is extensively studied but only paucity of work includes event termination detection\. Together with freezing, unfreeze event prediction is advantageous to reduce long\-term cueing effects\. The focus of carried work is to propose a machine\-learning based framework for prediction of freeze and unfreeze events\. Based on the Freeze Index \(FI\), a relabelling scheme is developed to represent four gait states, that are, no\-FoG, pre\-FoG, FoG, and pre no\-FoG using publicly available Daphnet dataset, comprising of 10PD patients\. Using nine extracted features from the shank sensor, Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 95\.5% using segmentation window of 2s\. While episode\-independent GroupKFold \(5\-fold\) and subject\-independent evaluation reported accuracy of \(91\.2 ± 0\.9\)% and \(86\.2 ± 4\.0\)% respectively representing more stricter independence constraints to generalize across episodes and, unseen subjects\. Following feature selection, a reduced set of five shank features are obtained using 2s segmentation window and accuracy of 96\.2% is achieved\. At event level, 197 of 237 annotated FoG episodes are successfully identified at onset, corresponding to per\-episode sensitivity of 83\.12%\. The predicted termination transitions achieved 63\.6% cue\-deactivation accuracy\. These results demonstrate that single shank sensor can provide information for both FoG onset and termination with relatively low sensing and feature\-processing requirements\. However, framework requires clinical validation and its effectiveness for real\-time cueing following prospective validation on larger and more diverse PD population\.

## [The impact of fatigue on lower limb neuromuscular control in female college soccer players](../publications/bd1967d3be424e759c44.md)

Tao Xiang; Tingzheng Zhu; Huiru Ma; Ziwen Mu; Zhiqiang Han; Kazuhiro Imai; Shaoshuai Shen; Zhiguang Guo; Xiao Zhou

Introduction Fatigue is a key risk factor for non\-contact lower\-limb injuries in female soccer players\. This study aimed to identify the impact of fatigue on lower limb neuromuscular control in female college soccer players\. Methods Twenty female collegiate soccer players performed the Yo\-Yo Intermittent Endurance Level 2 Test for fatigue induction\. Before and after fatigue, single\-leg landing \(SLL\), double\-leg landing \(DLL\), and zigzag running were assessed using surface electromyography \(sEMG\) and force plates\. Normalized sEMG amplitude \(%PEAK\), peak vertical ground reaction force \(vGRF, BW\), stabilization time, and center of pressure \(COP\) displacement area were analyzed\. Twenty participants performed the Yo\-Yo Intermittent Endurance Level 2 Test for fatigue induction\. Before and after the test, single\-leg landing \(SLL\), double\-leg landing \(DLL\), zigzag running, surface electromyography, force plates, and center of pressure analysis were used to assess neuromuscular and kinetic responses\. Fatigue altered sEMG amplitude in a task\-specific manner\. Results In DLL, normalized sEMG amplitude decreased significantly in the right vastus lateralis \( P = 0\.002; FDR\-adjusted P = 0\.024\), left vastus lateralis \( P = 0\.006; FDR\-adjusted P = 0\.036\), and right vastus medialis \( P = 0\.010; FDR\-adjusted P = 0\.040\)\. In zigzag running, a pre\- fatigue bilateral rectus femoris asymmetry \( P = 0\.037; exploratory, FDR\- adjusted P &gt; 0\.05\) was no longer significant post\-fatigue \( P = 0\.112\)\. In SLL, peak vGRF \(BW\) decreased bilaterally \(left: 2\.52 ± 0\.31–2\.34 ± 0\.27 BW, P = 0\.015; FDR\-adjusted P = 0\.045; right: 2\.69 ± 0\.36\-2\.40 ± 0\.30 BW, P &lt; 0\.001; FDR\-adjusted P &lt; 0\.003\)\. Discussion These findings provide insights into fatigue\-induced neuromuscular changes in female collegiate soccer players, with the DLL vastus muscles&\#x27; responses surviving FDR correction, while other findings remain exploratory and require confirmation\. The results offer preliminary theoretical support for targeted training and injury prevention strategies, though the fixed testing sequence and potential recovery effects limit strong causal conclusions\.

## [Deciphering Anomalous Luminescence in Highly Doped Transition‐Metal Phosphors: Spin‐Exchange, Unusual Site Occupancy, and Trace Impurities](../publications/bd22490391c5e22a2037.md)

Qiaoling Chen; Litian Lin; Qinshi Hu; Hui Wang; Chang‐Kui Duan

ABSTRACT Anomalous luminescence in phosphors highly doped with transition‐metal ions \(e\.g\., , \) has attracted significant interest for multifunctional optical materials and devices\. However, rational optimization and materials design have been hindered by controversial mechanisms\. Here, we establish a unified analytical framework for deciphering such complex emissions across a diverse range of host systems\. Our framework categorizes the possible origins into distinct classes— transition‐metal dimers or clusters, configuration‐associated isolated transition‐metal centers, and impurities\. We demonstrate that the various anomalous luminescence phenomena observed in highly doped transition‐metal phosphors cannot be explained by exchange‐coupled dimers alone, but instead arise from a variety of configuration‐dependent effects that arise at high doping levels \(e\.g\., unusual site occupancy, defect‐dopant complexes, or alternative valence states\), or trace impurities\. In particular, the intervalence charge transfer transition in transition‐metal dimers is expected to be predominantly non‐radiative due to the large structural relaxation energy involved\. This study provides a generalizable framework for deciphering complex luminescence in highly doped systems, reconciling long‐standing controversies and offering a mechanistic foundation for interpreting broadband near‐infrared emissions in highly doped phosphors for multifunctional optical applications\.

## [Memperkuat Kesehatan Mental Karyawan melalui Pengaruh Kondisi Kerja, Kesejahteraan di Tempat Kerja, dan Mediasi pada Manajemen Sumber Daya Manusia Hijau yang Berkelanjutan](../publications/bd28c988870b6648eb04.md)

Kurniawan Prambudi Utomo; Ananto Krisna Wardhana; Riris Lestiowati; Rachmat Fadly; Aprilia Puspasari; Nanang Kohar

Purpose – This study aims to analyze the influence of work condition harmonization and employee welfare on employee mental health through sustainable Green Human Resource Management \(Green HRM\) as an intervening variable\. Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative approach was used with survey data from 200 employees across various industries\. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling\-Partial Least Squares \(SEM\-PLS\)\. Findings – The results show that work condition harmonization and employee welfare positively and significantly affect employee mental health\. Sustainable Green HRM also significantly mediates the relationship by strengthening psychological stability and employee engagement\. Research limitations/implications – The study is limited by its cross\-sectional design and self\-reported data\. Practical implications – Organizations are encouraged to integrate sustainable Green HRM practices to improve employee well\-being and organizational sustainability\. ## [High\-throughput methods for identification of ClpC N\-terminal domain bait ligands for antibacterial targeted protein degradation drug discovery](../publications/bd323b652c4b4933dcef.md)

Helen E\. Erickson; Yahani P\. Jayasinghe; Zalak Sheth; Dylan B\. Wolfe; Julien Roche; Donald R\. Ronning

Introduction Antimicrobial resistance, which can be attributed to overconsumption of antibiotics, as well as a shortage of new, pathogen\-specific drugs, is a continually expanding global health crisis\. In 2023, one in six bacterial infections is caused by an antibiotic\-resistant strain, according to the World Health Organization\. With the intention of channeling a fresh perspective through the antibiotic drug discovery pipeline, we harnessed the ClpC N\-terminal domain, a regulatory ATPase within the caseinolytic protease pathway, as a biomolecular target widely conserved across bacterial pathogens\. The Clp protease complex consists of the ATP\-dependent unfoldase, ClpC, and the ClpP protease\. The ClpC\-NTD recognizes proteins tagged with a phosphorylated arginine residue as substrates marked for proteolytic degradation, thereby initiating ClpC/ClpP complex formation and protease activity\. Methods Here we describe protein thermal shift screening assays, synthesis and utilization of a phospho\-arginine fluorescent probe for fluorescence polarization assay development, X\-ray crystallographic and computational docking experiments to characterize possible binding modes of ligands to ClpC homologs\. Results and discussion We developed a fluorescence polarization displacement assay using a phospho\-arginine\-based probe, with Kd values ranging from 0\.1 µM to 0\.8 µM for multiple ClpC\-NTD homologs from a variety of pathogenic bacteria\. Putative ClpC\-NTD binders were identified using a protein thermal shift assay and cross\-examined across multiple homologs using our displacement assay\. Additionally, we solved the X\-ray structures of Staphylococcus aureus and Chlamydia trachomatis ClpC\-NTDs and docked a panel of binders against three ClpC\-NTD homologs, offering structural insight into possible allosteric receptor\-ligand interactions\. Taken together, these results can be leveraged for screening and validating species\-dependent competitive or noncompetitive ligands of this prominent bacterial drug discovery target and ultimately advance the development of bifunctional molecules for targeted protein degradation\.

## [Inteligencia artificial generativa en la enseñanza escolar: oportunidades y desafíos para docentes ecuatorianos](../publications/bd3655939a4d45d4024f.md)

Sandra Marlene Espinoza Barreto; Edison Ruben Yagual Quinde; Diana Isabel Campoverde Orrala; Eloisa Maria Tomala Cruz

La inteligencia artificial generativa se incorpora a la práctica escolar antes de que muchas instituciones dispongan de criterios consolidados para orientar su uso\. Este artículo analiza las oportunidades, los riesgos y las condiciones pedagógicas de su integración en la enseñanza de educación básica y bachillerato, con atención al contexto ecuatoriano\. Se desarrolló una revisión bibliográfica integrativa de investigaciones, revisiones sobre educación escolar y documentos institucionales publicados principalmente entre 2020 y 2026, complementados con aportes teóricos anteriores\. La síntesis examinó planificación docente, elaboración de materiales, retroalimentación, alfabetización en inteligencia artificial, evaluación, inclusión y protección de estudiantes\. Las fuentes muestran posibilidades para diversificar explicaciones, preparar recursos y apoyar tareas docentes, pero no permiten inferir mejoras generalizadas del aprendizaje por el simple acceso a asistentes generativos\. Un estudio experimental en matemáticas de bachillerato advierte que el desempeño asistido puede ocultar dificultades cuando desaparece el apoyo tecnológico\. Los marcos internacionales y las orientaciones ecuatorianas coinciden en conservar la mediación profesional, proteger los datos y adaptar cualquier herramienta a la edad del alumnado\. Se propone un esquema de implementación que combina verificación de contenidos, actividades de producción propia, transparencia sobre el uso de inteligencia artificial y alternativas no digitales\. Se concluye que el criterio de pertinencia no es la novedad tecnológica, sino la evidencia de aprendizaje, la equidad y la capacidad del docente para decidir cuándo utilizarla y cuándo prescindir de ella\.

## [Artificial Intelligence in the Assessment of Spasticity and Gait Disorders: A Critical Review of Methods, Sensors, and Clinical Integration](../publications/bd48a6914dc9385cf303.md)

Dimitrios Sakavalas; George A\. Papakostas

Spasticity and neuromuscular dysfunctions are common consequences of neurological conditions such as cerebral palsy, stroke, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord lesions, substantially impairing mobility and quality of life\. Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly employed to process surface electromyography \(sEMG\) signals, inertial\-sensor recordings, gait\-analysis data, and clinical information, supporting more objective characterization of neuromuscular impairments\. Following PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review synthesizes evidence from 78 studies published between 2010 and 2026, identified through an expanded multi\-database search of Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, and IEEE Xplore\. Most studies focused on lower\-limb applications, followed by upper\-limb assessment, whereas a smaller proportion addressed general neuromuscular impairments\. Classification was a predominant AI task across the reviewed literature\. Most studies relied on private or non\-public datasets, limiting reproducibility and external validation, while small or single\-center cohorts and heterogeneous methodological protocols were also frequent limitations\. This review synthesizes methodological trends, dataset variability, and clinical applicability and identifies persistent gaps in generalizability, multimodal and longitudinal integration, and clinically validated decision\-support capabilities\. Overall, AI shows substantial potential to support more objective and individualized neurorehabilitation; however, broader external validation, standardized data acquisition, and prospective clinical evaluation remain necessary before widespread clinical integration\.

## [The teaching\-research nexus under pressure: sustaining ideals in uneven and changing times across disciplines](../publications/bd48e24131a3bb9cc072.md)

Cecilie Hansen; Kjetil Egelandsdal; Marit Ulvik

Professors in higher education are commonly expected to combine teaching and research, yet the relationship between these activities remains contested\. This article explores how professors make sense of the teaching\-research nexus in their everyday academic work\. Drawing on semi\-structured interviews with 16 professors in philosophy, mathematics, law and medicine at two Norwegian research\-intensive universities, we explore professors&\#x27; meaning\-making with particular attention to the dialectical process between academic experiences and institutional structures\. Framed by mundane phenomenology, we find the nexus to be a core element of the academic role and central to how professors understand academic work\. The combination of teaching and research is sustained through professors&\#x27; understanding of the role as interconnected engagements within their disciplinary fields\. Research deepens teaching, and teaching can generate reflection, questions and, at times, new research ideas\. At the same time, organisational arrangements, such as course structures, workload models, funding mechanisms and research\-only positions, increasingly separate teaching and research in everyday practice\. The article contributes to research on the teaching\-research nexus by shifting attention from whether teaching and research are connected and from the possible effects of combining these activities, to how the connection as a social phenomenon is sustained through professors&\#x27; meaning\-making, but also increasingly challenged through organisational conditions\.

## [Association between female genital mutilation and sexually transmitted infection in sub‐Saharan Africa: Evidence from interpretable weighted machine learning](../publications/bd4f459350de06313aea.md)

Mei Wang; Huaiyue Xu; Huimin Ben; Jiahui Tong; Shouxin Peng; Yuxuan Tan; 赵秀丽; Qi Chen; Hao Xiang; Wei Liang

OBJECTIVE: Sexually transmitted infections \(STIs\) impose a heavy public health burden on low\- and middle\-income countries\. We aimed to examine the association between female genital mutilation \(FGM\) and STI and develop an interpretable machine learning framework for STI identification among women in Sub\-Saharan Africa\. METHODS: We analyzed Demographic and Health Survey \(DHS\) data from 57 548 women aged 15\-49 years across 10 Sub\-Saharan African countries\. Eighteen prespecified sociodemographic, behavioral, health\-related, symptom, and cultural features were included\. Data from nine countries were used for model development and internal validation, while Sierra Leone was reserved for independent external validation\. Weighted logistic regression, elastic net, random forest, and XGBoost incorporated individual\-level DHS sampling weights, with hyperparameters tuned using fivefold cross\-validation\. SHapley Additive exPlanations \(SHAP\) analysis was used for model interpretation, and survey\-weighted multivariable logistic regression quantified adjusted associations\. RESULTS: A total of 4144 women had STIs\. The selected weighted random forest model showed good discrimination in both the internal validation set \(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \[AUROC\] = 0\.863\) and the independent external validation set \(AUROC = 0\.878\)\. SHAP analysis identified history of abnormal genital discharge, history of genital sores, and FGM as the leading contributors to STI identification\. Survey\-weighted multivariable logistic regression showed that women with FGM had 82\.7% higher odds of STI than those without FGM \(adjusted odds ratio 1\.827, 95% confidence interval 1\.630, 2\.049\)\. CONCLUSION: Female genital mutilation and genital symptom histories were associated with STI\. Combining sociodemographic, behavioral, and symptom information might improve STI identification and highlight the sexual and reproductive health relevance of FGM in high\-burden settings\.

## [AMPK activation stabilizes HIF\-2α by disrupting VHL binding and promotes erythroid differentiation under anemic stress via the mTOR pathway](../publications/bd56a9c11996155250ab.md)

Yun Cen; Pingjing Cai; 蒋瑾瑾; 黄丽华; Yiwei Hua

Objective Anemia affects over two billion people globally, and ESA resistance poses major clinical hurdles\. HIF\-2α governs erythropoiesis, yet how AMPK/mTOR energy sensors regulate HIF\-2α in erythroid cells remains unclear\. This study explored whether AMPK activation stabilizes HIF\-2α via impaired VHL binding to boost erythroid differentiation under anemic stress through mTOR signaling\. Methods UT\-7/EPO cells were cultured under 1% O 2 with low EPO to mimic anemic stress, treated with AMPK/mTOR pharmacological modulators\. CHX chase and Co\-IP detected HIF\-2α stability and VHL interaction; Ser672 phosphorylation, erythroid and iron\-related genes, hepcidin and intracellular iron were measured\. Results Anemic stress suppressed cell viability, stabilized HIF\-2α, activated AMPK and inhibited mTOR, upregulated erythroid markers and triggered apoptosis\. AICAR extended HIF\-2α half\-life, disrupted HIF\-2α\-VHL binding and elevated Ser672 phosphorylation, while mTOR activator MHY1485 reversed these effects\. AMPK activation elevated EPOR, DMT1, FPN1, lowered hepcidin and ferritin, and restored intracellular iron; these effects vanished upon HIF\-2α knockdown or mTOR overactivation\. Conclusions AMPK stabilizes HIF\-2α by blocking VHL binding to facilitate erythroid maturation and iron homeostasis under anemic stress via mTOR\. The AMPK/mTOR/HIF\-2α cascade controls stress erythropoiesis, and targeting this axis may treat ESA\-insensitive anemia\.

## [Pengembangan Bahan Ajar Digital Interaktif Menggunakan Flip PDF Professional untuk Pembelajaran Geometri SMP](../publications/bd66685f7630e453e41b.md)

Fatqurhohman Fatqurhohman; Maulidina Chintia Maharani; Nike Novianti

The limitation of digital learning materials that remain predominantly PDF\-based is one of the challenges in providing interactive geometry learning\. This study aimed to develop an interactive digital learning material based on Flip PDF Professional for curved\-surface solids for eighth\-grade students at SMPN 4 Jember\. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model, comprising Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation\. Data were collected through a literature review, interviews, expert validation sheets, teacher and student response questionnaires, and a learning achievement test\. Data were analyzed descriptively using percentages\. The validation results showed scores of 80\.0% for language, 83\.3% for media, and 66\.7% for material, categorized as very valid, very valid, and valid, respectively\. The practicality assessment yielded responses of 84\.4% from the teacher and 95\.8% from students, both categorized as very practical\. ## [MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning\-to\-Action Security of MLLM\-Based Mobile Agents under Cross\-Modal Consistency Injection](../publications/bd669b72a27425b97cad.md)

Songping Wang; Peiyang Li; Yi Huang; Fengting Li; Xuhao Ran; Yueming Lyu; Chao Feng; Caifeng Shan

Multimodal large language model \(MLLM\)\-based mobile agents are rapidly evolving from conversational assistants into autonomous systems that perceive, reason over, and act on smartphone environments\. This capability also exposes a new security risk: adversaries can embed malicious objectives in cross\-application mobile content and steer agent behavior through indirect multimodal injection\. Although prompt injection has been studied in desktop and web settings, its cross\-modal properties in mobile ecosystems remain poorly understood, and existing security analyses are still limited\. To close this gap, we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning\-to\-action security risks\. MobileInject provides a high\-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security\-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances\. It further introduces Cross\-Modal Consistency Injection to exploit corroboration across modalities, two enhanced attack methods, Multi\-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning\-Camouflage Injection, to intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine\-grained failure analysis\. Systematic experiments show that mobile agents are broadly vulnerable to multimodal injection, and that many failures stem from reasoning hijacking at early stages\. These findings establish MobileInject as a systematic cross\-modal benchmark for studying and improving the security of mobile agents\. Code release details are provided in the Appendix Open Science section\.

## [Relational Knowledge Production in Architectural Design Doctorate at Istanbul Technical University](../publications/bd69ca4c047cf60cff3b.md)

Melike Nur ŞAHİN; Nurbin Paker Kahvecioğlu

Architectural design doctoral education increasingly incorporates practice\-based research, raising questions about which forms of knowledge become academically visible and recognized\. In the Turkish context, the epistemic structures through which doctoral knowledge in architectural design gains academic recognition remain insufficiently understood\. Prior bibliometric studies in architectural education have largely mapped trend topics\. However, they have not examined how these themes define different fields of recognition\. This study addresses this gap through keyword co\-occurrence network analysis and thematic coding of 190 doctoral dissertation abstracts produced at Istanbul Technical University \(ITU\), representing 41\.63% of the architectural design doctoral corpus in Türkiye\. Drawing on Bourdieu&\#x27;s theory of symbolic capital, the study interprets which research themes acquire visibility and recognition within the academic field\. The findings reveal that doctoral knowledge production does not expand through a linear accumulation of research themes\. Instead, it operates as a relational network of interconnected domains\. The analysis identifies five major epistemic domains: Theory and Criticism, Education\-Practice\-Reproduction, Spatial Objects and Semantics, Computation and Representation, and Design Epistemology\. These domains show differing centrality and connectivity, pointing to unsteady patterns of academic recognition\. The study reframes knowledge production as relational rather than cumulative\. This perspective offers an analytical lens for evaluating epistemic legitimacy in doctoral education and supports comparative and institutional self\-reflection across architectural doctoral programs internationally\.

## [https://impactfactor\.org/PDF/IJDDT/16/IJDDT,Vol16,Issue71s,Article191\.pdf](../publications/bd777499ed228db85d2c.md)

Gayathri G\. A; G\. Kalyani; Manikandan K; Neethu Asokan; Pushpendra Kuumar; Amitabh Shad; Mohan Prakash Sharma; S\. Deepan

The human gut microbiota has emerged as a critical regulator of drug metabolism, therapeutic efficacy, and adverse drug reactions, highlighting its pivotal role in personalized pharmacotherapy\. Comprising trillions of microorganisms with diverse metabolic capabilities, the gut microbiome functions as an additional metabolic organ capable of biotransforming numerous therapeutic agents through enzymatic processes such as reduction, hydrolysis, deconjugation, and demethylation\. These microbial activities can alter drug absorption, bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and toxicity, thereby contributing to significant interindividual variability in treatment outcomes\. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the bidirectional interactions between gut microbiota and drugs, emphasizing their implications for precision medicine and individualized therapeutic strategies\. A systematic literature survey was conducted using peer\-reviewed publications retrieved from major scientific databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, focusing on studies investigating microbiota\-mediated drug metabolism, pharmacomicrobiomics, and microbiome\-based therapeutic interventions\. The review discusses the composition and physiological functions of the gut microbiota, the molecular mechanisms underlying microbial drug metabolism, and clinically significant interactions involving cardiovascular drugs, antidiabetic agents, anticancer therapies, antibiotics, central nervous system drugs, and non\-steroidal anti\-inflammatory drugs\. Furthermore, recent advances in pharmacomicrobiomics, microbiome\-derived biomarkers, artificial intelligence, multi\-omics technologies, probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation are critically evaluated as emerging approaches for optimizing personalized pharmacotherapy\. Despite substantial progress, several challenges, including inter\-individual microbial variability, lack of standardized analytical methodologies, limited clinical validation, and regulatory constraints, continue to impede the clinical implementation of microbiome\-guided therapy\. Future research integrating microbiome profiling with pharmacogenomics, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence is expected to improve the prediction of drug response, minimize adverse drug reactions, and facilitate the development of precision medicine\. Overall, gut microbiota–drug interactions represent a promising frontier in pharmaceutical sciences, offering new opportunities to enhance therapeutic efficacy and advance individualized patient care\.

## [Case Report: Prenatal and postnatal clinical manifestations of 15q duplication syndrome: a single longitudinal case combined with pooled analysis of 35 prenatal cases](../publications/bd7a3644e140604aad9a.md)

Ziqing Xu; Mou Ufei; Hongbo Chen; Shuo Yang; Peijun Zou; You Lu; Fei Xiong; Jinrong Li

Background 15q duplication \(Dup15q\) syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by early\-onset hypotonia, developmental delay, intellectual disability, symptoms related to autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy\. In the absence of specific treatment, prenatal diagnosis is of important clinical significance\. However, most reported cases are postnatal cases, whereas prenatal cases are limited and often lack detailed clinical information, making prenatal recognition of this disorder challenging\. In this study, we integrated prenatal and postnatal clinical information from the present case with a pooled analysis of published prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases, providing additional insights into the prenatal\-to\-postnatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome\. Case presentation We report a case of Dup15q syndrome with both prenatal and postnatal clinical data\. Although prenatal ultrasound showed polyhydramnios, an abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile, and mild tricuspid regurgitation, no further prenatal genetic testing was performed\. After birth, the patient presented with early hypotonia and developmental delay, and the diagnosis was established by genetic testing after a poor response to rehabilitation\. We collected 34 prenatal Dup15q syndrome cases through literature review\. The results showed that non\-invasive prenatal screening \(NIPS\) may facilitate the prenatal identification of Dup15q syndrome\. Prenatal ultrasound findings included polyhydramnios, fetal growth restriction \(FGR\), cardiac abnormalities, dysmorphic features, and abnormal ultrasound soft markers\. The pooled analysis further provided an overview of the prenatal phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and suggested that FGR and polyhydramnios, particularly in the presence of additional ultrasound abnormalities, positive NIPS results, or a positive family history, may warrant further etiological evaluation\. Conclusions Dup15q syndrome exhibits prominent clinical heterogeneity with nonspecific prenatal manifestations, predisposing patients to missed or delayed diagnosis\. By integrating prenatal and postnatal clinical information with pooled prenatal cases, this study provides a broader understanding of the phenotypic spectrum of Dup15q syndrome and may facilitate prenatal counseling and early clinical recognition\.

## [Energy\-Aware Machine Learning: A Comparative Analysis of Predictive Performance and Computational Energy Consumption](../publications/bd7d4d0a3e25ddaa1e43.md)

Pawan Thakur

Although the increased use of machine learning \(ML\) has enhanced the accuracy of predictive models in several applications, the computational resources and energy needed by ML algorithms have become important constraints\. Past studies have primarily focused on either enhancing the predictive accuracy of ML algorithms or reducing their energy consumption\. However, there is research gap in conducting a systematic comparison of the six different ML algorithms in term of predictive performance while considering the computational energy and time consumed in a standard experimental setup\. This paper proposes an energy\-aware comparative study of six ML algorithms, namely, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine \(SVM\), XGBoost and Neural Network\. The current research will utilize publicly available datasets and standard experimental conditions to evaluate and compare the algorithms based on their prediction performance, computational energy consumption, execution time, CPU utilization and memory utilization\. The obtained results will be analysed to establish a relationship between the performance of the ML algorithms and their computational energy consumption to identify the trade\-off between accuracy and energy consumption\. The current research will provided insight into the need to consider computational costs apart from accuracy while developing machine learning models\. The findings of this study can facilitate the creation of energy\-efficient and sustainable machine learning models\.

## [A multimodal machine learning framework for assessing moisture and thermal damage in asphalt binder aggregate systems](../publications/bd80f8a92c713bc47df8.md)

Qiang Lu; Qing Yang; Masoud Ghasemi; Samia Elattar; H\. Elhosiny Ali; J\.E\. Gutierrez

Abstract Moisture and thermal degradation of asphalt binder and aggregate interfacial bonds is a major precursor to stripping, adhesion loss, and premature pavement deterioration, but conventional mixture level indicators often fail to capture early interface damage\. This study develops a multimodal learning framework for post\-conditioning diagnostic assessment of durability loss by integrating binder rheology, aggregate surface characteristics, conditioning variables, contact angle measurements, and image derived damage descriptors\. A 720\-record experimental dataset was assembled using eight asphalt binders, six aggregate sources, five conditioning states, and three replicates\. Target outputs included pull off adhesion strength, retained adhesion index, moisture damage probability, failure mode, interfacial durability score, and critical conditioning class\. Mean pull off adhesion strength decreased from 722\.0 kPa to 453\.1 kPa after saline thermal aging, while retained adhesion declined from 100\.0% to 61\.7%\. Contact angle increased from 77\.4° to 101\.9° and debonded area ratio increased from 5\.0% to 31\.8%, confirming progressive wetting related and morphological damage\. For post test diagnostic inference, the Multimodal Transformer and CatBoost fusion model achieved R² values of 0\.984 and 0\.968 for adhesion strength and retained adhesion, moisture damage classification accuracy of 0\.96, and failure mode macro F1 of 0\.90\. The reported multimodal performance therefore characterizes already conditioned interfaces and should not be interpreted as prospective prediction before environmental exposure or mechanical testing\.

## [Radial Tiny Golden Angle UTE \(tyGA‐UTE\) for Cardiac MRI in the Small Animal Model](../publications/bd92bf42a850737525e1.md)

Hao Li; Patrick S\. Metze; Pengxi Han; Benzheng Wei; Volker Rasche

Robust cardiorespiratory motion correction is critical for high\-quality ultra\-high\-field \(UHF\) preclinical cardiac magnetic resonance imaging \(MRI\)\. Whereas radial tiny golden angle \(tyGA\) sampling, data\-driven self\-gating \(sg\), compressed sensing \(CS\), and ultrashort echo time \(UTE\) are individually well\-established techniques, their integration into a unified acquisition and reconstruction pipeline, together with systematic validation at 11\.7 T remains insufficiently explored\. This study presents and validates a UHF\-optimized tyGA\-based UTE workflow that enables high\-temporal\-resolution sliding\-window dynamic imaging \(SW\-tyGA\-UTE\) and high\-spatial\-resolution cardiorespiratory self\-gated cine imaging \(Gated\-tyGA\-UTE\) from a single continuous acquired tyGA acquisition\. All experiments were performed on an 11\.7\-T small\-animal MRI system in 16 healthy wild\-type mice\. Cardiac functional parameters, image quality metrics \(signal\-to\-noise ratio \[SNR\] and contrast\-to\-noise ratio \[CNR\]\), and inter\-/intra\-observer reproducibility were systematically compared between the proposed tyGA\-UTE pipeline and two navigator\-gated reference techniques: retrospectively gated FLASH and UTE methodologies\. SW\-tyGA\-UTE and Gated\-tyGA\-UTE reconstructions yielded global left ventricular functional parameters comparable to those obtained with the reference methods \(all p &gt; 0\.05\)\. All functional metrics showed excellent intra\-observer \(ICC = 0\.94\-0\.99\) and inter\-observer \(ICC = 0\.90\-0\.98\) reproducibility, with ejection fraction showing the highest measurement consistency\. Image quality was evaluated using an image\-based within\-ROI noise quantification approach that captures both thermal noise and reconstruction\-related artifacts\. In this analysis, the Gated\-tyGA\-UTE protocol showed no statistically significant differences in left ventricular blood\-pool SNR, myocardial SNR, or CNR relative to the reference sequences\. In contrast, the high\-temporal\-resolution sliding\-window reconstruction showed significantly reduced image quality across all three metrics, consistent with the expected spatiotemporal trade\-off of undersampled dynamic imaging\. This study validates a robust, UHF\-optimized tyGA\-UTE imaging workflow that generates both high\-fidelity quantitative cine data and ultra\-fast dynamic cardiac images from a single acquisition\. The unified pipeline eliminates the need for sequential repeated scans, minimizes anesthesia\-related physiological variability, and improves experimental efficiency, providing a practical tool for preclinical cardiac phenotyping, longitudinal studies, and drug screening\.
