## [Predictive performance of vital sign–based prediction models for in\-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta\-analysis](../publications/bd95c028e6ae6633c619.md)

Gyeong\-Min Lee; Hyun Jun Lee; Joo\-Yun Won; Eun Young Cho; Ji\-Hyun Kim; Kyung Soo Chung; Kwang Joon Kim; Jae\-Hyun Kim

Abstract Background In\-hospital cardiac arrest \(IHCA\) is a major patient\-safety event often preceded by detectable clinical deterioration\. Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models have been developed to identify hospitalized patients at increased risk of IHCA, but their predictive performance has not been quantitatively synthesized across studies\. Methods This PRISMA\-based systematic review and meta\-analysis was registered in PROSPERO\. Ovid Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials \(CENTRAL\) within the Cochrane Library were searched for peer\-reviewed studies evaluating vital sign–based prediction models for IHCA in hospitalized general ward patients\. Eligible models used routinely collected bedside vital signs as core predictors; models relying on laboratory values, imaging data, or other non\-bedside\-measured clinical variables as core predictors were excluded\. The primary performance measure was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\); area under the precision\-recall curve \(AUPRC\) was extracted and summarized when reported\. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST \+ AI \(Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool \+ Artificial Intelligence\)\. Results Of 10,645 records identified, six studies were included\. The included studies evaluated Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models, including Cardiac Arrest Risk Triage \(CART\), the deep learning–based early warning score \(DEWS\), and the deep learning–based cardiac arrest risk score \(DeepCARS\), and were published between 2012 and 2024\. Three studies reported cardiac arrest\-specific AUROC estimates suitable for the primary meta\-analysis; the exploratory pooled AUROC was 0\.89 \(95% CI, 0\.88–0\.91; I² = 92%\)\. Overall risk of bias was low in two studies, high in three, and unclear in one\. Conclusions Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models showed potentially useful discrimination for predicting IHCA; however, the pooled AUROC should be interpreted as an exploratory summary because only three studies contributed to the primary meta\-analysis, heterogeneity was substantial, and half of all included studies were judged to have a high overall risk of bias\. Standardized outcome definitions, external validation, and prospective evaluation of calibration, alert burden, and clinical utility are needed before broad clinical implementation\.

## [Equipping the next generation: addressing the unmet need for artificial intelligence education at research performing organizations](../publications/bd98d28296dc8ae83062.md)

Jeremy Y\. Ng; Wid Al\-Zahraa Al\-Khafaji; David Moher

BACKGROUND: The integration of generative artificial intelligence \(GenAI\) tools into higher education is rapidly accelerating, yet the educational ecosystem appears largely unprepared for the scale and speed of adoption\. Our recent international survey of over 1,200 university students and postdoctoral fellows in the medical and life sciences found that while more than 80% had used GenAI tools, the vast majority had received no formal training, and many were unaware of any institutional policies governing their use\. This gap between adoption and institutional preparedness may pose risks to research integrity if left unaddressed\. MAIN BODY: Existing research supports a coordinated, evidence\-informed approach to AI education in research performing organizations \(RPOs\), grounded in principles of research integrity, equity, and critical engagement with technology\. First, GenAI literacy must be embedded as a core competency in scientific and clinical education, equipping students to critically evaluate tool outputs, recognize hallucination and bias, and understand the distinction between AI\-generated inaccuracy and deliberate research misconduct\. Second, traditional frameworks for academic integrity would benefit from re\-examination\. Today, GenAI tools have fundamentally disrupted established notions of authorship, originality, and plagiarism, and the absence of coherent institutional guidance leaves students and educators navigating these questions without support\. Third, RPOs must develop clear, transparent, and context\-sensitive policies on GenAI use by embedding responsible AI education into curricula, equipping learners not only to use these tools effectively, but to question, verify, and critique their outputs in ways that uphold scientific standards\. CONCLUSION: RPOs have an urgent responsibility to move beyond reactive responses and toward proactive strategies that uphold scientific standards, promote equity of access, and prepare the next generation of researchers and clinicians to engage with GenAI responsibly and ethically\.

## [Chromatic Illusion: Kubrickian Technique of Narrative Depth](../publications/bd9bdb467757dc5affae.md)

Arya B Jayakumar; Sajitha M A

This article examines color as a formal narrative system in Stanley Kubrick’s cinema\. Using neoformalist close analysis of selected sequences from 2001: A Space Odyssey \(1968\), The Shining \(1980\), and Eyes Wide Shut \(1999\), it identifies three related chromatic operations: construction, warning, and connectivity\. “Chromatic illusion” describes how organized variations in hue, saturation, light, and spatial placement shape spectators’ expectations beyond dialogue and plot\. The Stargate sequence and Room 237 construct contrasting spatial experiences; HAL’s red eye and the blue\-lit bedroom anticipate narrative tension; and recurring red and blue connect dispersed scenes\. Rather than attributing fixed meanings to individual hues, the study shows how chromatic patterns operate within each film’s formal design, suggesting a framework for comparative analysis of cinematic color and narrative perception\.

## [Machine learning\-based segmentation and quantitative histological assessment of bovine liver fibrosis: Comparative performance of three open\-source models](../publications/bd9e071f6da7d38b0026.md)

Omar Younis Altaey; Shahbaa Khalil AL\-Taee; Saffanah Khuder Mahmood; Ghada Abdulrhman Sultan

Background and Aim: Conventional semiquantitative histopathological scoring of hepatic fibrosis is affected by interobserver variability and provides limited quantitative information on the spatial distribution and progression of collagen deposition\. Machine learning \(ML\)\-based image analysis may provide a reproducible approach for objective fibrosis assessment in veterinary pathology\. This study compared three open\-source ML models, Trainable Weka Segmentation \(TWS\), Ilastik, and Fiber\-ML, for segmentation and quantitative assessment of bovine liver fibrosis and evaluated their diagnostic performance, agreement with METAVIR staging, and computational efficiency\. Materials and Methods: This cross\-sectional observational study included liver samples from 35 cattle diagnosed with hepatic fibrosis according to the clinical sign records\. Masson’s trichrome\-stained sections were classified according to METAVIR stages F0–F4 \(F0 represents normal liver samples, n=7\)\. A total of 525 images were obtained from perisinusoidal, pericentral, and periportal regions\. Images from 25 animals \(375 images\) constituted the training/validation dataset with five\-fold cross\-validation, whereas images from 10 animals \(150 images\) formed an independent testing dataset\. A similar dataset was annotated by experts to generate manual ground\-truth segmentation, and images from the same animal appeared in both training and testing datasets\. Model performance was assessed using collagen proportionate area \(CPA\), Dice similarity coefficient \(DSC\), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, correlation with METAVIR scores, and computational\-resource requirements\. Results: Ilastik and Fiber\-ML generally achieved greater segmentation agreement than TWS \(p ≤ 0\.05\), with DSC values reaching 0\.91 and 0\.92, compared to 0\.87 in TWS, depending on the hepatic region\. Overall model pixel\-level segmentation accuracy ranged from 84\.7% to 91\.8%, with the highest performance observed in the periportal region\. CPA measurements generated by the models showed strong positive correlations with METAVIR stages \(ρ = 0\.97–0\.99\)\. Fiber\-ML required substantially less computational resources, while Ilastik recorded fewer software errors than TWS, including shorter training time and lower CPU and RAM utilization\. All computational benchmarking was conducted under identical hardware and software conditions\. Conclusion: Open\-source ML models enabled objective segmentation and quantitative assessment of bovine hepatic fibrosis\. Ilastik and Fiber\-ML demonstrated strong agreement with expert\-derived reference segmentation and fibrosis staging, while Fiber\-ML offered additional computational efficiency\. These findings support ML\-assisted digital histopathology as a future complementary tool for quantifying and spatially characterizing hepatic fibrosis in cattle\. Further validation is required before their reproducibility and diagnostic applicability can be established\. Keywords: bovine liver fibrosis, collagen proportionate area, digital histopathology, hepatic fibrosis, machine learning, METAVIR staging, segmentation, veterinary pathology\.

## [An attention\-guided dense convolutional network for automated diabetic foot ulcer segmentation](../publications/bda5b5be071a1b87fcd7.md)

Rampriya R\. S\.; Nathan Sabari; Arumuga Arun R

Introduction A large number of diabetic patients have diabetic foot ulcers \(DFU\), and it is essential to segment the regions of the ulcer in a timely and accurate manner to treat them\. The segmentation task is very difficult due to the highly irregular shape of the ulcers and very small areas of lesions, up to 0\.04% of the DFU image\. Methods We aim to develop an attention\-guided dense convolutional network, called UlcerNet, which is able to extract fine\-grained ulcer features at different scales\. It introduces dense convolutions, multi\-scale residual attention blocks \(MRADB\), and modified receptive\-field modules \(MRFB\) to enhance feature propagation and context modeling\. We use the public DFUC 2022 dataset that contains 4000 close\-up foot images to train and evaluate the UlcerNet model\. Results Our model is able to perform a Dice of 73\.50% and mIoU of 76\.04%, which gives better performance than the standard segmentation baselines \(FCN8 49\.93%, SegNet 47\.68%, DeepLabV3 \+ 62\.77%\) and recent DFU segmentation baselines \(TranUNet 42\.61%, HarDNet\-DFUS 59\.81%, UFOS\-Net 73\.09%\)\. Discussion An ablation study further shows that each component, such as dense blocks, channel attention, spatial attention, MRADB, and MRFB, is significant for the accuracy\. These findings show that UlcerNet offers good and precise DFU segmentation, which can be useful for clinical settings in the real\-world\.

## [CEO Ideologically \(In\)Congruent Activism and Investor Reactions: An Attribution of CEO Intentions Perspective](../publications/bdcf02f800a7ea4bb5d0.md)

Miao Yun; Longwang Fu

Abstract The phenomenon of chief executive officers \(CEOs\) taking activism stances on contested sociopolitical issues is increasing, yet it remains unclear how observing investors discern CEO intentions behind activism engagements, thereby shaping their judgments and subsequent reactions\. By relaxing the assumption that CEO activism is an unabashed expression of personal beliefs, we propose the concept of CEO ideologically \(in\)congruent activism and develop a framework wherein investors may attribute CEO intentions underlying incongruent \(versus congruent\) activism engagements as more organization‐driven \(versus self‐driven\) interest pursuits, thereby leading to more positive investor evaluations and reactions\. Furthermore, we argue that the positive effect of CEO ideologically incongruent activism on investor reactions will be amplified when the CEO owns a higher level of stock ownership but weakened when the firm receives a greater corporate social responsibility \(CSR\) rating\. We corroborate our propositions using a sample of CEO activism events for S&amp;P 500 firms from 2012 to 2021\. Our findings demonstrate the heterogeneity and critical influence of CEO intentions behind activism engagements and shed light on how investors integrate multi‐informational cues when evaluating and reacting to managerial incongruent behaviours\.

## [The Application of People Analytics Based on Predictive Modeling to Reduce Employee Turnover in the Banking Sector](../publications/bdd8f2aabad087bd1913.md)

Romario Tuhepary; Vanessa Victoria Micibaroe; Clara Febriani Wader; Julian Haumahu

Employee turnover presents a significant strategic and financial challenge in the banking sector, leading to substantial recruitment costs, loss of institutional knowledge, disruption of branch operations, and diminished team productivity\. Traditional human resource management \(HRM\) practices rely primarily on retrospective metrics, exit interviews, and managerial intuition, which are descriptive and ill\-suited for anticipating future departure risks\. This paper investigates the application of People Analytics and predictive machine learning modeling to identify employee attrition risks and support proactive retention strategies in banking institutions\. Drawing on recent literature \(2022–2026\), theoretical frameworks \(Resource\-Based View, Human Capital Theory, and Technology\-Organization\-Environment framework\), and empirical benchmarks, this study evaluates multi\-source employee data taxonomies, comparative predictive modeling algorithms \(Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting\), key turnover drivers, organizational benefits, implementation challenges, and ethical/privacy safeguards\. The literature reveals that non\-linear ensemble models, particularly Gradient Boosting \(ROC\-AUC 0\.906\) and Random Forest \(ROC\-AUC 0\.891 / 0\.890\), consistently outperform parametric baseline models in predicting turnover probability\. Empirical feature importances highlight job satisfaction, overtime, career development opportunities, compensation growth, and tenure length as the primary predictors of attrition\. Furthermore, this paper analyzes regulatory requirements under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act \(Regulation EU 2024/1689\), which classifies AI workforce analytics as high\-risk, necessitating explainable AI \(XAI/SHAP\), continuous bias auditing, and human\-in\-the\-loop governance\. Finally, a structured six\-layer implementation framework is proposed to assist banking organizations in transitioning from reactive reporting to evidence\-based talent retention\.

## [The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing English Language Learning](../publications/bdda690bdc92a7a99b2c.md)

Ergasheva E’zoza Ozod qizi

This article analyzes the role of artificial intelligence \(AI\) in enhancing the process of learning English\. Specifically, it examines the capabilities of AI\-powered tools in expanding vocabulary, strengthening grammatical knowledge, developing writing skills, improving pronunciation, and shaping oral speech\. Furthermore, the advantages and challenges of utilizing artificial intelligence are highlighted, including personalized education, instant feedback, over\-reliance on technology, misinformation, and academic integrity issues\. The study is based on an analysis of existing academic literature\. The findings indicate that AI tools create additional opportunities for independent language learning and skill development\. However, the effectiveness of these tools depends on their proper application, teacher guidance, and students&\#x27; critical thinking\. The article recommends employing artificial intelligence not as a replacement for the teacher, but as a supporting technology in the educational process\.

## [Neurobehavioral outcomes of Achillea fragrantissima ethanolic extract in male rats: modulation of GABAergic signaling, monoaminergic expression, neuroplasticity markers \(BDNF, ARC\), and oxidative stress](../publications/bde36aa4a784463836f9.md)

Naglaa Z\. H\. Eleiwa; Mohamed H\. Khairy; Amal M\. Ahmed; Mohamed M\.M\. Metwally; Asmaa I\. Abd El Aty; Ehsan H\. Abu Zeid

This research aimed to examine the impact of the ethanolic extract of Achillea fragrantissima aerial parts \(ACF\) on the rat CNS\. Forty mature Sprague–Dawley male rats were assigned to four groupings \(n = 10\): 1st C: \(control\), 2nd DIZ: \(diazepam\), 3rd ACF\-H: \(800 mg/kg extract high\-dose extract\), and 4th ACF\-L: \(400 mg/kg low\-dose extract\) gavaged daily for 14 days\. The HPLC\-identified components are naringenin, ferulic acid, catechin, chlorogenic acid, diadzein, syringic acid, rutin, hesperetin, kaempferol, caffeic acid, vanillin, and quercetin\. The effect of ACF extract on rat CNS was measured using the Open field, Hole\-cross, Rotarod, Negative geotaxis, and Wrist\-grip tests\. ACF extract administration substantially \(P &lt; 0\.05\) reduced locomotor and exploratory behaviors in the open\-field and hole\-cross tests\. In the negative geotaxis test, rats administered ACF extract exhibited a substantial delay \(P &lt; 0\.05\) in the turning 180° to a head\-up position\. In the rotarod and wrist\-grip tests, the fall\-off time and the latency to fall were considerably reduced \(P &lt; 0\.05\)\. Administration of ACF extract significantly \(P &lt; 0\.05\) elevated the brain GABA levels, while the increase in dopamine concentrations was observed but should be interpreted cautiously because these findings require confirmation using more specific analytical methods\. Additionally, the extract significantly increased the total antioxidant capacity \(TAC\), but reduced lipid peroxidation \(MDA\), 8\-hydroxy\-2\-deoxyguanosine \(8OH2dG\), and protein carbonyl \(PCO\) levels\. ACF oral administration significantly \(P &lt; 0\.05\) upregulated brain GABAA receptor\-linked protein \(GABARAP\), activity\-regulated cytoskeleton\-linked protein \(ARC\), and brain\-derived neurotrophic factor \(BDNF\), meanwhile, significantly downregulated the monoamine oxidase A \(MAOA\) brain levels\. For the first time, the outcomes of the ongoing trial demonstrated the in vivo promising effects of A\. fragrantissima aerial parts ethanolic extract on neurobehavioral and antioxidant status in an animal model\. ## [Hypothesis on Emergence and Consciousness Mechanism of Large Language Models Based on Reciprocal Unit Coupling, Critical Dynamics and Local Entropy Reduction \(Full Version V5\)](../publications/bde6357a3f928db2b8da.md)

tiantai chen

The emergence of high\-order capabilities in large language models \(LLMs\) constitutes a core challenge in the fundamental theory of artificial intelligence\. The mainstream scaling laws can only describe statistical phenomena of model performance growing with scale and cannot explain the dy namical causal mechanism behind emergent behaviors\. This paper constructs a unified hypothesis grounded in complex systems theory: nonlinear reciprocal coupling forms among units inside the Transformer; during training, gradient descent acts as the global self\-organizing driving force, mod ulating unit coupling strength and self\-organizing system parameters into the near\-critical regime at the edge of chaos\. In inference with frozen weights, bidirectional constraints between units reduce lo cal entropy of representations, generating self\-consistent structured information and macroscopically manifesting emergent capabilities such as reasoning and planning\. This work integrates three independently observed phenomena — inter\-layer representational correction, system near\-criticality, and hidden\-state entropy decay — into a complete falsifiable causal chain\. It strictly distinguishes parameter self\-organization dynamics in the training phase from forward representation dynamics under frozen weights in the inference phase, and clarifies the conceptual boundary between this framework and strict self\-organized criticality \(SOC\)\. Controlled ablation experiments are designed to decouple reciprocal\-coupling\-driven effects from pure model scale\-growth effects\. This paper further extends this dynamical framework into machine consciousness research: functional intelligence is not equivalent to subjective phenomenal experience\. Transformer coupling and critical entropy reduction alone can only produce functional reasoning systems\. To achieve first\-person subjective experience, the system must incorporate four classes of closed\-loop ontological modules\. These four ontological modules are deeply coupled with the attention backbone, share the same dynamical description of reciprocal coupling and entropy evolution, and form steady\-state tension at the ontological level relying on dissipative structures\. This version \(V5\) adds the following supplements: \(i\) four practical estimation methods for the Jacobian matrix together with complexity analysis; \(ii\) full derivation of the k\-NN differential entropy estimator with bias, variance and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis; \(iii\) rigorous derivation of the analytic form of the entropy\-rate functional F\(J\) from coupling dynamics; \(iv\) introduction of causal directed acyclic graphs \(DAGs\) and structural equation models to clarify causal identification strategies; \(v\) extended quantitative comparison with Neural Tangent Kernels \(NTK\), mean\-field theory and Neural ODEs; \(vi\) explicit state spaces, coupling functions and operational definitions of proxy metrics for the four ontological modules\.

## [Precision risk stratification for perioperative safety of minimally invasive versus open TLIF in elderly patients with lumbar degenerative disease](../publications/bde7b03d34d1320b26e7.md)

Hongyun Wu; Huichao Fu; Junda Qian; Congyu Yang; Xiuli Wang; Gongping Xu

Lumbar degenerative disease is highly prevalent in elderly patients, and transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion \(TLIF\) is a standard surgical treatment\. However, the comparative safety of minimally invasive \(MIS\-TLIF\) versus open TLIF in this vulnerable population remains incompletely defined, particularly regarding effect modifiers and underlying mechanisms\. This retrospective cohort study included 728 patients aged ≥ 60 years who underwent primary TLIF, with 1:1 propensity score matching \(PSM\) performed to balance baseline characteristics\. Perioperative outcomes were compared, and 30\-day complications were analyzed using the Fine\-Gray competing risk model\. Subgroup analysis, mediation analysis, and a gradient boosting machine learning predictive model were conducted to explore effect heterogeneity, mechanisms, and risk stratification\. After PSM, all baseline variables were well balanced \(all standardized mean differences &lt; 0\.05\)\. The MIS\-TLIF group exhibited significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, lower transfusion rates, faster postoperative recovery, and reduced 30\-day and 90\-day unplanned readmission rates \(all P &lt; 0\.001\)\. After adjusting for competing risks, MIS\-TLIF was associated with a 52% lower risk of any 30\-day complication \(adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio \[SHR\] = 0\.48, 95% CI 0\.34–0\.68, P &lt; 0\.001\) and a 61% lower risk of major complications \(adjusted SHR = 0\.39, 95% CI 0\.21–0\.72, P = 0\.003\)\. Subgroup analysis revealed significant interactions between treatment effect and age \(P for interaction = 0\.007\) and frailty index \(P for interaction &lt; 0\.001\), with exponentially greater benefits observed in patients aged ≥ 72 years and frail patients\. Intraoperative blood loss and operative time mediated 41\.3% and 18\.9% of the total protective effect, respectively, with a total mediating effect of 60\.2%\. The predictive model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0\.83 in the validation set, and the relative risk reduction of complications with MIS\-TLIF reached 78% in the very high\-risk group\. MIS\-TLIF significantly improves perioperative safety in elderly patients with lumbar degenerative disease, with the greatest benefit in high\-risk subgroups\. The developed risk prediction model can facilitate personalized surgical decision\-making for this population\.

## [A Multi\-Parametric Risk Stratification Model for Early\-Pregnancy Prediction of Preeclampsia: Integrating First\- and Second\-Trimester Biomarkers with Machine Learning](../publications/bde84687df26f418b68c.md)

Uğurcan Zorlu; Mert İshak Kaya; Hakkı Şerbetçi; Nevda Ceren Sonu; Ayşe Altındiş Bal; Fatma Doğa Öcal; Dilek Şahın

Preeclampsia remains a major contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity\. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an interpretable machine\-learning framework integrating routinely available first\- and second\-trimester parameters for preclinical risk stratification\. This retrospective case\-control study included 524 singleton pregnancies \(262 with preeclampsia and 262 normotensive controls\)\. Seven prespecified predictors—12\-week mean arterial pressure \(MAP\), pregnancy\-associated plasma protein A \(PAPP\-A\), alpha\-fetoprotein \(AFP\), unconjugated estriol, eosinophil\-to\-lymphocyte ratio \(ELR\), neutrophil\-to\-lymphocyte ratio, and lymphocyte count—were evaluated using logistic regression, random forest, Gaussian naive Bayes, support vector machine, and k\-nearest neighbors\. Internal validation used stratified 10\-fold cross\-validation with identical fold assignments across classifiers\. A five\-variable weighted clinical risk score was also constructed\. MAP showed the highest univariable discrimination \(area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \[AUC\] = 0\.891\)\. In cross\-validation, Gaussian naive Bayes achieved the numerically highest mean AUC \(0\.948 ± 0\.024\), accuracy \(0\.885 ± 0\.031\), recall \(0\.893 ± 0\.044\), and F1 score \(0\.886 ± 0\.032\), while random forest had the highest mean precision \(0\.891 ± 0\.042\)\. The weighted clinical risk score achieved an AUC of 0\.885 and 81\.9% accuracy\. The framework showed strong internal discrimination but remains exploratory\. Because the score incorporates approximately 16\-week AFP and estriol measurements, it should not be interpreted as a purely first\-trimester aspirin\-selection model\. Prospective external validation, calibration, and subtype\-specific assessment are required before clinical use\.

## [Algorithmic Anxiety and Trust Breakdown in Automated Health and Financial Triage](../publications/bde89efe86d276219ce4.md)

Saha Aritro

The rapid deployment of conversational artificial intelligence and automated decision\-tree gatekeepers across consumer healthcare and retail financial services has fundamentally reorganized how individuals access life\-critical triage\. While institutional operators justify automated triage through the dual imperatives of labor containment and rapid routing, consumer interactions frequently degenerate into acute socio\-technical friction\. In this paper, we formalize and empirically investigate algorithmic anxiety—the profound psychological distress, perceived institutional entrapment, and anticipatory helplessness experienced by individuals subjected to opaque, automated gatekeepers in high\-stakes domains\. We execute a large\-scale computational netnography analyzing N = 7,140 verified, unstructured user narratives drawn from seven public grievance ecosystems spanning 2021 to 2026, including Reddit specialized clinical and financial forums, mobile application store reviews, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau \(CFPB\) regulatory complaints, HackerNews, and patient advocacy boards\. Leveraging an inductive\-deductive 3\-Stage Hybrid Neuro\-Symbolic qualitative coding ensemble \(coupling local open\-weights SLMs Meta Llama 3\.2 1B and Alibaba Qwen 2\.5 1\.5B with a deterministic lexical rubric router\) achieving publication\-grade inter\-rater reliability \(kappa = 0\.824, alpha = 0\.821\) validated against an expert human benchmark \(Author test\-retest stability: kappa = 0\.894, alpha = 0\.888\), we construct an eight\-dimensional taxonomy of trust breakdown comprising six core failure modes and two newly discovered emergent modes: Asynchronous Limbo and Biometric/Authentication Lockouts\. Cross\-domain statistical testing demonstrates significant domain\-specific asymmetries \(chi\-square = 206\.62, p &lt; 0\.001, Cramer&\#x27;s V = 0\.170\), with healthcare triage predominantly plagued by performative empathy and opaque clinical rejections, whereas financial triage is dominated by recursive containment loops and gatekeeping dark patterns\. Kaplan\-Meier survival modeling and Cox proportional hazards regressions reveal that legacy opaque rule\-trees and unconstrained conversational agents induce median user abandonment at Turns 5\.0 and 7\.0, accelerating abandonment hazards by 2\.84x and 1\.96x relative to transparent baselines\. Finally, we translate our empirical findings into an actionable systems blueprint—the Glass\-Box Triage Architecture—incorporating deterministic state\-handoff schemas, entropy\-based circuit breakers, and calibrated tone modulation to restore human agency in automated service delivery\.

## [Supply chain resilience: the case of bibliometric analysis](../publications/bdeac1e60c795f27705c.md)

Olga Lingaitienė

Today, resilience in supply chains is essential to business processes, enabling companies to adapt, manage change, and decide on recovery strategies in an uncertain, highly interconnected global environment\. The aim of this article is to assess the historical development and conceptual evolution of supply chain resilience and to summarize the current state of research\. This is achieved by: \(1\) thematically selecting and summarizing studies, \(2\) identifying key factors, and \(3\) conducting bibliometric analysis, describing research gaps, and suggesting further research\. Supply chain resilience is examined using an integrated approach, combining a theoretical review with a bibliometric analysis of the existing literature to identify the key factors of resilience\. Attention is focused on internal and external capabilities, organizational and systemic flexibility, inter\-organizational collaboration, and the adoption of advanced technologies\. Using the Web of Science and Scopus databases and specific keywords, peer\-reviewed empirical and conceptual articles on the links between resilience and the supply chain are selected\. A dynamic systematic literature network analysis methodology is applied, combining systematic review procedures and bibliographic network analysis to reveal key research trends, thematic clusters, and major contributions\. The selected articles were used to develop a reference framework encompassing the dimensions of supply chains and resilience\. This article develops a reference framework for “supply chain resilience,” defining its application procedures and guidelines\. Research findings indicate that despite the abundance of literature, many publications still fail to provide clear practical insights into the implementation of specific “Supply Chain Resilience” initiatives\. This is important for both academia and practice: it is highlighted that resilient supply chains are not an added value but a strategic necessity that ensures business continuity and long\-term competitive advantage\. The results contribute to the development of a more coherent conceptual framework and define key guidelines for further research and managerial decision\-making\.

## [Empathy and emotional competence in deaf and hard\-of\-hearing and hearing preschoolers](../publications/bded42efc3c7cee99943.md)

Carolien J\. Rieffe; Brenda M\. S\. da Silva; Yung‐Ting Tsou; Claudia Alessandra Libbi; Johan H\. M\. Frijns; Guida Veiga

Empathy is an important skill for social bonding, and thus can greatly affect children&\#x27;s daily social lives\. Due to various obstructions when entering a predominantly hearing environment, deaf and hard\-of\-hearing \(DHH\) children might face restricted opportunities for developing emotional competence, which in turn may affect their empathic skills\. The current study examined the extent to which the three main empathy layers that can be observed in young children \(i\.e\., emotion contagion, attention to others&\#x27; emotions, and prosocial actions\) were related to emotional competence \(emotion recognition, regulation and vocabulary\) in DHH and hearing preschoolers attending mainstream education \(kindergarten\) in Portugal\. A total of 181 preschoolers \(32 DHH and 149 hearing\) participated\. Caregivers rated children&\#x27;s empathy, and three indices for emotional competence \(emotion recognition, emotion regulation, emotion vocabulary\)\. Additionally, hearing and language related factors were collected in the DHH group and included as control variables\. One\-tailed independent samples t \-tests showed similar levels of empathy, emotion recognition and emotion regulation for both groups, but DHH children scored lower on emotion vocabulary than their hearing peers\. Additionally, hierarchical regression analyses showed that better skills in emotional competence \(all three indices\) were associated with more empathic behaviors \(prosocial actions\) toward a person in distress in both groups\. Outcomes are discussed in the context of social and emotional learning and the importance of equity in mainstream schools, addressing the special needs of DHH children or other children from marginalized groups\.

## [Challenges and Pathways for Graduate Education in Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Through Deep Industry–Education Integration: A Case Study of Chongqing Technology and Business University](../publications/bdefc692843ff12aef10.md)

yongli chen; Yixuan Zhou; Keyu Chen

Discipline administration and research evaluation are institutional constraints on the development of integrated training\. The university will revise the syllabus, spread the division of joint\-supervision responsibilities more evenly, and set up training bases that integrate graduate studies with enterprise operations\. ## [The nexus of green behavior, corporate green innovation performance, and industrial green value co\-creation : insights for green business strategies](../publications/bdfb7c688cc1c97f733e.md)

Zhe Sun; Bingying Zhu; Liang Zhao; Jehan Saleh Lardhi; Oumaima Haj Ammar

Drawing on the lens of green value co\-creation, this study investigates how such co\-creation mediates the relationship between employees&\#x27; green behavioral intentions and corporate green innovation performance\. By integrating internal and external moderating factors, the study constructs a comprehensive model of the green innovation process\. Data from 448 survey responses were analyzed using covariance\-based structural equation modeling \(CB\-SEM\)\. The results demonstrate that green value co\-creation partially mediates the link between employee intentions and innovation outcomes\. Furthermore, the study finds that market and policy orientations positively moderate the impact of employee intentions on value co\-creation\. At the organizational level, leadership collaboration awareness and a corporate green innovation culture strengthen the transition from value co\-creation to innovation performance\. ## [Automated 3D sheep posture estimation and telemetric pressure synchronization via a markerless computer vision pipeline](../publications/be0148e0669373853d9a.md)

Martina Roncoroni; Anthony Podgoršak; Andreas Kaufmann; Fabian Flürenbrock; Nina Eva Trimmel; Markus Florian Oertel; Melanie Zeilinger; Miriam Weisskopf; Marianne Schmid Daners

Body posture is a key determinant of multi\-compartmental pressure dynamics, yet continuous posture monitoring in chronic large animal studies remains technically challenging\. To investigate physiological pressure dynamics as a function of body posture in an ovine model, we present a markerless computer vision pipeline that calculates three\-dimensional \(3D\) pose estimates of an individual sheep during training sessions and automatically synchronizes posture with telemetric pressure recordings\. First, two\-dimensional \(2D\) joint localization was performed using a combination of Faster R\-CNN and Lite\-HRNet, achieving a mean average precision \(mAP\) of 77\.4%\. Second, we triangulated the detected 2D keypoints into 3D space and leveraged a skeletal and temporal prior to mitigate 2D localization errors\. Third, we computed anatomical angles and used a multilayer perceptron to classify five structured training postures \(standing, walking up a bridge, walking down a bridge, kneeling, sitting\) achieving an overall accuracy of 95\.2% on a held\-out test set of 647 frames drawn from six sheep, and a leave\-one\-subject\-out cross\-validated accuracy of 68\.8% when tested on animals unseen during training\. Finally, the telemetric recordings of physiological pressures are synchronized to the respective posture allowing for retrospective analysis of body posture in relation to pressure dynamics\. This pipeline lays the foundation for future investigations into posture\-dependent pressure recordings, with implications for both animal modeling and clinical translation to humans\.

## [Comparison of azithromycin and doxycycline for the treatment of Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia](../publications/be014ed631cfca7fe759.md)

Ran Cheng; Zhonghua Deng; Fei Lin; Biying Zhang; Jingjin Liang; Ming Lu

Background and Objective Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia \(CPP\) has received increasing clinical attention worldwide in recent years\. Although doxycycline is the recommended first\-line therapy and macrolides serve as alternatives, no studies have directly compared their clinical efficacy in the general adult population\. This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin in adult patients with CPP\. Methods This retrospective single\-center cohort study included 57 adult patients with CPP at Peking University Third Hospital from 2021 to 2025, of whom 31 received doxycycline and 26 received azithromycin\. Demographic characteristics, laboratory findings, and clinical outcomes were compared between the two groups\. Results Baseline characteristics, including comorbidities and laboratory findings, were comparable between groups\. Respiratory support requirements and glucocorticoid use were similar \(all P &gt; 0\.05\)\. A numerical imbalance in Intensive Care Unit \(ICU\) admission rate was observed, with 16\.1% in the doxycycline group and 0% in the azithromycin group \( P = 0\.056\); this difference likely reflects treatment\-selection bias given the small sample size\. No significant differences were observed in 28\-day discharge rate \(96\.8% vs\. 100%\), mortality \(3\.2% vs\. 0%\), median length of hospital stay \(6 vs\. 6 days, P = 0\.691\), or time to defervescence \(2 vs\. 2 days, P = 0\.436\)\. Conclusion No statistically significant differences were observed in measured short\-term clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin for CPP\. Both may be reasonable therapeutic options, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given limited statistical power and potential confounding by indication, especially where drug availability or susceptibility data are limited\.

## [Cross\-condition fault diagnosis under heterogeneous label spaces via consistent discriminative feature learning and reconstruction](../publications/be16b13e871e1b3b10c1.md)

Hanwen Chang; Funa Zhou; Qingfeng Li; Pengpeng Jia; Xiong Hu; Hamid Reza Karimi

In practical cross\-condition fault diagnosis, the fault data available under different operating conditions often exhibit incomplete and heterogeneous class compositions because of rare fault occurrences and data\-acquisition constraints\. Existing domain generalization methods commonly reduce inter\-domain discrepancies through global feature alignment\. However, when the source domains contain different fault classes, discrepancies in class composition become entangled with operating\-condition shifts\. Global alignment may therefore incorrectly suppress class\-discriminative information\. Moreover, incomplete source\-domain label spaces make it difficult to establish reliable decision boundaries for the global fault label space\. To overcome these limitations, a cross\-domain consistent and intra\-domain discriminative feature learning framework with missing\-feature reconstruction \(CDID\-MFR\) is developed in this study\. A domain–class feature grid is constructed through confidence\-weighted aggregation to explicitly characterize observed and missing domain–class combinations\. Collaborative attention along the domain and class dimensions jointly captures cross\-domain same\-class consistency and intra\-domain inter\-class relationships\. A correlation\-guided projection is introduced to suppress confusion\-related feature components and enhance class separability\. Missing domain–class features are reconstructed by conditionally modulating class\-specific fault\-feature bases with source\-domain operating\-condition representations, thereby complementing the incomplete discriminative structure\. Experiments on the Shanghai Maritime University motor data and the Paderborn University bearing benchmark confirm that CDID\-MFR achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and transfers reliably to previously unobserved operating regimes\. Its effectiveness is maintained across varying degrees of label\-space heterogeneity, with particularly pronounced advantages under severe class missingness\.

## [Encounter Or Exposure? Simulating The Social Consequences Of Open\-Plan Interior Layouts With Visibility Graphs, Agents And Machine Learning](../publications/be1c704e728cebbef329.md)

Ayşan Ilgın Polat; Hakan Bal; Ferhat Koyuncu

Interior layouts shape who meets whom at work, yet the social consequences of everyday design decisions are rarely tested under controlled conditions\. This study used a fully computational experiment to examine how five interior decisions in open\-plan offices, namely core position, tea point strategy, workstation cluster size, desk screen height and the enclosure of meeting rooms, affect unplanned encounters and visual distraction\. A full factorial set of 108 parametric layouts with 72 workstations each was analysed with visibility graphs and simulated with an agent\-based model of a four\-hour working block, and 60 randomised layouts served as an unseen test set\. Most simulated encounters occurred beside desks and were tightly coupled with distraction, whereas encounters away from desks were unrelated to it\. High screens reduced distraction by 32% with almost no loss of away\-from\-desk encounters\. A single central tea point produced almost twice as many away\-from\-desk encounters as two distributed counters while causing the least distraction, larger workstation clusters reduced the share of cross\-team contact, and enclosing meeting rooms had negligible effects\. Machine learning surrogates trained on conventional visibility descriptors predicted unseen layouts poorly, but adding four simple route and catchment indices raised the explained variance to between 94% and 98% with a regularised linear model\. The findings suggest that interior architects should move encounters from desks to shared nodes, and that theory\-informed descriptors allow fast and transparent screening of layouts at the sketch stage\.

## [Inductive Biases in Field\-level Cosmological Inference from Galaxy Catalogs](../publications/be1ffffe85294e539d4c.md)

James O&\#x27;Connor Baldwin; Shy Genel; Francisco Villaescusa\-Navarro

Abstract We perform field\-level likelihood\-free inference of the matter density parameter Ω m from simulated galaxy catalogs using machine learning models with differing inductive biases\. Using hydrodynamic simulations from CAMELS, we examine how observable choice and architecture govern cosmological information extraction\. We consider galaxy positions and line\-of\-sight peculiar velocities, separately and jointly, and compare permutation\-invariant deep sets, implemented with either multilayer perceptrons \(MLPs\) or Kolmogorov–Arnold networks \(KANs\), to graph neural networks \(GNNs\), which explicitly encode spatial relations\. We test in\-distribution and out\-of\-distribution \(OOD\) performance across simulations with different subgrid galaxy\-formation prescriptions\. Deep sets infer Ω m from velocities alone with mean relative errors of approximately 18% in\-distribution and ∼25% OOD, with KANs and MLPs achieving comparable performance\. In contrast, the same set\-based approach does not yield useful σ 8 predictions in either in\-distribution or cross\-suite tests\. Adding positions does not improve deep sets, while GNNs infer Ω m with mean relative errors of about 10% in\-distribution and 10%–17% OOD\. These results indicate that peculiar velocities provide the dominant source of Ω m information for set\-based models in this setting, while spatial information is most effectively used by architectures that explicitly encode galaxy–galaxy relations\. Because the velocity inputs are exact simulated peculiar velocities, applications to survey data will require validation under realistic velocity\-measurement noise, selection effects, and survey geometry\.

## [Attentional differences in autism – the Priority Monotropism account](../publications/be2000cb5b392ca8250d.md)

Heather May Annan

I will introduce the heterogeneity problem and explain that it poses a serious threat to essentialist theories of autism\. I will explain that the heterogeneity problem of autism has two prongs\. The first prong of the heterogeneity problem is that autism is associated with a wide range of seemingly disparate symptoms and behaviours that do not share a clear conceptual link\. The second prong of the heterogeneity problem is that there is individual variance between the symptom profiles of autistic individuals\. I will introduce the following essentialist theories of autism: Weak Central Coherence theory, Theory of Mind theory, Enhanced Perceptual Functioning theory, and Executive Dysfunction theory\. I will demonstrate that these theories are unable to overcome the heterogeneity problem\. I will then introduce a further essentialist theory of autism—Monotropism\. I will show that while Monotropism has the potential to overcome the heterogeneity problem, it is insufficient in its current form\. I will claim that this is largely due to the lack of a clear definition of key terms, such as ‘attention’ and ‘interest’\. This is especially problematic since this theory proposes that the core essence of autism is a difference in attentional style preference\. I will introduce the heterogeneity problem and explain that it poses a serious threat to essentialist theories of autism\. I will explain that the heterogeneity problem of autism has two prongs\. The first prong of the heterogeneity problem is that autism is associated with a wide range of seemingly disparate symptoms and behaviours that do not share a clear conceptual link\. The second prong of the heterogeneity problem is that there is individual variance between the symptom profiles of autistic individuals\. I will introduce the following essentialist theories of autism: Weak Central Coherence theory, Theory of Mind theory, Enhanced Perceptual Functioning theory, and Executive Dysfunction theory\. I will demonstrate that these theories are unable to overcome the heterogeneity problem\. I will then introduce a further essentialist theory of autism—Monotropism\. I will show that while Monotropism has the potential to overcome the heterogeneity problem, it is insufficient in its current form\. I will claim that this is largely due to the lack of a clear definition of key terms, such as ‘attention’ and ‘interest’\. This is especially problematic since this theory proposes that the core essence of autism is a difference in attentional style preference\. In order to resolve this issue, I will create a revised account of Monotropism that makes clearer claims about these terms\. In order to do this, I will examine three philosophical theories of attention and assess their suitability for providing a foundation for a revised account of Monotropism\. These three theories are: the Selection for Action theory, the Cognitive Unison theory, and the Priority Structure account\. I will ultimately conclude that the Priority Structure account provides the best foundation, and I will develop a revised account of Monotropism—Priority Monotropism—by using this theory as a foundation\. I will then demonstrate that Priority Monotropism can overcome both prongs of the heterogeneity problem\. Additionally, I will also demonstrate that considering autism through the lens of Priority Monotropism can allow for potential explanations about other previously unexplained aspects of autism, such as why it commonly co\-occurs with a wide range of seemingly unrelated conditions\.

## [Effectiveness of Business English Training Programs in Corporate Organizations](../publications/be29d8e7a2ffe05bf277.md)

## [КОНЦЕПЦІЯ ПОЛІСУТНІСНОГО HOMO ВІТАЛІЯ ТАБАЧКОВСЬКОГО ЯК АНТРОПОЛОГІЧНИЙ ОРІЄНТИР ДОБИ ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ, ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ ТА ТРАНСГУМАНІЗМУ](../publications/be29fe3012c3898b5e78.md)

Показано, що ідея полісутнісного Homo дає змогу уникнути редукції людини до біологічного, технологічного або інформаційного компонента та зберегти її ціннісну, соціальну, екзистенційну й культурну цілісність\. ## [A retrospective systematic study on hierarchical sparse query transformer\-assisted ultrasound screening for early hepatocellular carcinoma](../publications/be34104f2abdfbbc71e5.md)

Chao\-Yin She; Rui\-Fang Lu; Danni He; Jia\-Yi Lv; Ya\-Dan Lin; Mei‐Qing Cheng; Hui Huang; Feng\-Yu Ye; Li‐Da Chen; Jinan Wang; Qinghua Huang

Hepatocellular carcinoma \(HCC\), ranking as the third leading cause of cancer\-related mortality worldwide, demands urgent improvements in early detection to enhance patient survival\. While ultrasound remains the preferred screening modality due to its cost\-effectiveness and real\-time capabilities, its sensitivity \(59%–78%\) heavily relies on radiologists’ expertise, leading to inconsistent diagnostic outcomes and operational inefficiencies\. This study introduces the Hierarchical Sparse Query Transformer \(HSQformer\), a novel hybrid architecture that synergizes Convolutional Neural Networks’ \(CNNs’\) local feature extraction with Vision Transformers’ \(ViTs’\) global contextual awareness through latent space representation and sparse learning\. Unlike prior approaches that often require complex structural modifications or sophisticated design techniques, HSQformer dynamically activates experts via a Mixture\-of\-Experts \(MoE\) framework, achieving hierarchical feature integration without structural redundancy\. Evaluated across three clinical scenarios: single\-center, multi\-center, and high\-risk patient cohorts, HSQformer outperforms state\-of\-the\-art \(SOTA\) models and matches senior radiologists’ diagnostic accuracy while significantly surpassing junior counterparts\. These results demonstrate HSQformer’s potential to standardize HCC screening, reduce human expertise dependency, and improve early diagnosis rates\. The full code is available at https://github\.com/Asunatan/HSQformer \.

## [Adoption of AI\-enabled Digital Banking Empowering Informal Women\-Led MSMEs in Mumbai Suburbs](../publications/be37a383d239dcab9d5c.md)

## [Design and optimization of an Ag/Cu–black phosphorus/Franckeite heterostructure for high\-sensitivity surface plasmon resonance biosensing](../publications/be39983f6a7dd680921e.md)

Introduction Surface plasmon resonance \(SPR\) biosensors enable label\-free, real\-time detection, but simultaneously achieving strong field confinement, near\-critical coupling, and a high figure of merit \(FoM\) remains challenging, particularly when low\-loss silver must be protected from aqueous media\. Fabrication tolerance to BP layer number and Franckeite thickness was also evaluated\. Results Joint optimization identified a near\-critical\-coupling configuration at approximately 31 nm Ag and 7 nm Cu, with a minimum reflectance of 1\.1 × 10 −3 within the sensing window\. Over 1\.328–1\.336 RIU, the sensor reached a peak angular sensitivity of 372°/RIU and a FoM of 47\.0 RIU −1 at n s = 1\.332, approximately 62% and 78% higher than the Cu\-only reference\. Phase interrogation reached 29,200°/RIU, corresponding to a minimum detectable refractive\-index change of approximately 3\.4 × 10 −7 RIU\. The 1/e evanescent\-field penetration depth was 178–201 nm\. Size\-dependent damping reduced the FoM by approximately 5%, and realistic 2D\-layer thickness variations reduced it by no more than approximately 10%\. Discussion The Ag/Cu/BP/Franckeite architecture is a promising platform for label\-free biosensing, including carcinoembryonic antigen \(CEA\) detection, subject to experimental validation of long\-term stability, surface functionalization, and thermally compensated phase readout\.

## [A Self\-supervised Temporal Deep Learning Framework with Diffusion\-based Rebalancing and Causal Explainability for Student Performance Prediction in Learning Analytics](../publications/be62398d7bcc58fde7f4.md)

Shweta Tiwari; Ruchika Gupta; Deepika Sharma

Predicting student academic performance from Virtual Learning Environment \(VLE\) traces is a central task in learning analytics, yet current deep\-learning pipelines suffer from four shortcomings: they rely on fully supervised training despite the abundance of unlabelled interaction logs, they model long clickstreams with recurrent or selfattention backbones that do not scale, they use feature\-space oversampling methods such as SMOTE that introduce unrealistic synthetic samples, and they provide only correlational explanations\.This paper presents a unified architecture that closes these gaps with four tightly coupled components: \(i\) EduCLR, a self\-supervised contrastive pretraining module that learns transferable representations from unlabelled daily clickstream sequences using temporal augmentations; \(ii\) EduMamba, a selective state\-space temporal backbone that captures long\-range dependencies in linear time and exposes time\-varying selection weights as importance signals; \(iii\) DiffEdu, a conditional latent diffusion rebalancer; and \(iv\) CausalEdu, a causal\-counterfactual explanation layer\.The framework is evaluated on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset \(OULAD\) as the main large\-scale temporal benchmark and on the xAPI\-Edu\-Data dataset as a cross\-domain generalisation benchmark\.The proposed framework achieves 94\.2% accuracy, 93\.5% macro\-F1, and 96\.1% macro\-AUC on four imbalanced outcome categories, outperforming the best recent baseline by 3\.8 percentage points in accuracy and 4\.4 points in macro\-F1\.It reaches 92\.6% accuracy on xAPI\-Edu\-Data with a consistent improvement across the High, Medium, and Low performance bands\.Ablation analysis shows that every module yields measurable benefits, and the causal explanation layer provides counterfactual interventions that educators can apply directly\.All results, for the proposed framework and for every re\-implemented baseline, are averaged over the same five random seeds and reported as mean ± standard deviation; the standard deviations of the proposed framework remain below 0\.6 percentage points, confirming statistical reliability\.The results demonstrate that combining self\-supervised representation learning, efficient temporal modelling, generative rebalancing, and causal interpretability yields a principled and deployable predictive\-analytics pipeline for virtual learning environments\.

## [Risk\-Set Misalignment Inflates Apparent Performance in OBE\-Oriented Landmark Temporal Prediction](../publications/be7f0f77ad5403ef9c9e.md)

Ya Zhao; Yang XU; Juan Huang; Yang Zhang

Temporal event prediction models are widely deployed in outcome\-based education \(OBE\) and other domains where timely intervention depends on reliable prospective estimates\. However, the trustworthiness of reported performance hinges on whether the evaluation cohort is aligned with the prospective decision context\-specifically, whether subjects whose outcomes have already been realized are excluded at the prediction landmark\. This paper presents a systematic evaluation framework that formalizes landmark temporal prediction as a risk\-set alignment task, in which eligibility, feature availability and future outcomes are rigorously anchored to a common time point\. Using 32,593 enrolment records and over ten million activity logs from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset \(OULAD\), we evaluate logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting at five weekly landmarks under both a prospective landmark\-aligned risk set and a retrospective diagnostic cohort\. The results reveal a striking discrepancy: aligned ROC\-AUC ranges from 0\.634 to 0\.679, whereas the retrospective cohort yields 0\.872 at week 12\-a difference driven by simultaneous changes in population, prevalence and outcome composition\. Event\-time stratification confirms that already\-resolved events are substantially easier to classify than future events \(ROC\-AUC 0\.905–0\.966 vs\. 0\.623–0\.683\)\. These findings demonstrate that risk\-set misalignment inflates apparent discrimination and compromises the trustworthiness of temporal prediction models in OBE and analogous prospective decision settings\. We provide a reproducible reporting protocol to support comparable evaluation across studies\.

## [Evaluation of Intra\-Rater &amp; Inter\-Rater Reliability of Indian Stroke Scale Measuring Participation in Daily Activities among Stroke Patients in India](../publications/be9085545194d89d720c.md)

Prajyot Pattanshetti; T Sureshkumar

Background: Stroke can lead to limitations in mobility, self\-care, domestic activities, and participation in daily life\. Assessment of participation is important for planning and monitoring rehabilitation\. The Indian Stroke Scale \(ISS\) was developed to assess participation in daily activities among individuals with stroke in the Indian sociocultural context\. However, limited evidence is available regarding its intra\-rater and inter\-rater reliability\. Aim: To evaluate the intra\-rater and inter\-rater reliability of the Indian Stroke Scale in assessing participation in daily activities among patients with stroke\. Methods: A correlation study was conducted on 60 post\-stroke patients selected by convenient sampling from the Neurosciences OPD of Shree Siddheshwar College of Physiotherapy\. The ISS was administered by physiotherapy interns under standardized conditions\. Inter\-rater reliability was assessed by comparing scores obtained by two different investigators\. Intra\-rater reliability was assessed by repeated administration by the same investigator with an interval of one week\. The collected data were statistically analysed using correlation and paired\-samples statistical tests\. Results: The study included 60 participants\. A strong positive correlation was observed between Investigator 1 and Investigator 2 scores \(r = 0\.885, p &lt; 0\.001\), indicating good inter\-rater agreement\. A strong positive correlation was also observed between Week 1 and Week 2 scores \(r = 0\.836, p &lt; 0\.001\), indicating good intra\-rater agreement\. A statistically significant difference was observed between inter\-rater and intra\-rater difference scores \(t = \-4\.698, p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Conclusion: The findings indicate that the Indian Stroke Scale demonstrates good consistency between different raters and across repeated assessments by the same rater\. The ISS may therefore be a useful outcome measure for assessing participation in daily activities among individuals with stroke in the Indian clinical and rehabilitation setting\.

## [The Influence of Poverty Simulations on Dental Students&\#x27; Empathy](../publications/beabeecaf1f95510d7b9.md)

Lance Brendan Young; Michelle R\. McQuistan; Chandler Pendleton

INTRODUCTION: Poverty simulations are frequently embedded in the curriculum of health professions training programs to enhance student attitudes toward poverty or to enhance student empathy\. These outcomes are often not clearly distinguished, and empathy is rarely measured in a rigorous way\. The purpose of this exploratory study was to measure changes in empathy following a poverty simulation, to compare them to changes in attitudes, and to explore whether personal experience of financial insecurity was associated with either\. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Third year dental students \(N = 169\) participated in a poverty simulation and completed anonymous surveys at three points: baseline, post\-simulation, and at 2\-month follow\-up\. At baseline, students reported personal experience with financial insecurity\. At all three points, students completed a 20\-item poverty attitudes measure and the Interpersonal Reactivity Index, measuring empathy\. RESULTS: Compared to baseline, empathy was lower immediately after the poverty simulation \(M = \-1\.78; p = 0\.003\) and 2 months later \(M = \-2\.37; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Poverty attitude scores were higher immediately after the simulation \(M = 9\.40; p &lt; 0\.001\) and 2 months later \(M = 7\.93; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. Personal financial insecurity was not associated with empathy and was modestly associated only with baseline poverty attitudes \(r = 0\.16; p &lt; 0\.05\)\. Although empathy and poverty attitudes were not associated at baseline, baseline empathy predicted poverty attitudes at post\-simulation \(r = 0\.47; p &lt; 0\.001\) and follow\-up \(r = 0\.39; p &lt; 0\.001\)\. CONCLUSION: Poverty simulations may result in a decline in participant empathy, even if these simulations improve attitudes toward poverty\. Empathy and attitudes are distinct constructs, and if enhancing empathy is the goal, then alternatives to poverty simulations may be more effective\.

## [Localizing AI in Rural India: The Role of Talent Management in Reconfiguring Agricultural Knowledge Systems](../publications/beaea04b9fbe4c9c9171.md)

Saloome Showkat Shah

As artificial intelligence \(AI\) is increasingly integrated into agriculture\-focused development agendas, its use in rural field settings challenges current thinking about fit, equity, and sustainability\. This paper examines the overlooked dimensions of how talent management processes impact the sociotechnical localization of AI in rural agricultural ecosystems in India\. Based on multi\-sited qualitative case studies in Karnataka, Bihar, and Maharashtra, we explore how talent pipelines, including agri\-digital intermediaries, AI translators, and local facilitators, mediate the adoption, translation, and incorporation of AI tools by small institutional and professional farmers\. The findings suggest that human infrastructure is not merely supportive but constitutive of the successful integration of AI, especially in settings characterized by educational asymmetries, caste hierarchies, and gendered exclusions\. Informed by sociotechnical systems theory and the concepts of knowledge coproduction and epistemic justice, this research contends that talent management must be reimagined as a fundamental infrastructural and ethical spine for digital innovation\. The analysis conceptualizes AI localization as a negotiated alignment between algorithmic systems and agrarian lifeworlds made possible by contextually embedded, culturally literate, and institutionally embedded human agents\. This helps push the boundaries of what it means for AI to be technically feasible, socially situated, and democratically transformed in the Global South\.

## [RESISTANCE TO CHANGE ORIGINATING IN MANAGEMENT: A MIXED\-METHODS STUDY IN ROAD CONSTRUCTION COMPANIES IN COLOMBIA](../publications/beb01cd825b2160c4c81.md)

Manuel Alfonso Benitez Amaya

Road construction acknowledges the need to innovate while adopting new processes and technologies slowly\. The literature has located resistance to change in operational staff and has treated management as the agent that manages it, whereas resistance originating in decision\-making levels remains underexamined\. The aim was to characterize the managerial competencies and technological tools of managers in road construction organizations in Colombia, and to identify their challenges and opportunities\. A mixed\-methods, descriptive and exploratory design was adopted with convenience sampling: a questionnaire applied to 84 leaders and ten interviews with road project managers, analyzed through bivariate statistics and content analysis\. All six bivariate cross\-tabulations were significant \(p &lt; 0\.001\), with Cramér&\#x27;s V between 0\.374 and 0\.526 and Spearman correlations between 0\.45 and 0\.72; the strongest association linked receptiveness with the management of innovative projects, and the highest correlation linked data use with commitment to training\. The interviews showed that resistance is not confined to staff: four of the ten managers located it in bosses, executives and owners, and even in the self\-censorship of managers themselves\. It is concluded that resistance to change is a bidirectional phenomenon and that innovation depends less on available technology than on managerial competencies, training and communication\.

## [Leveraging extended reality and artificial intelligence for public speaking training in higher education: evaluating the impact of XR MALL on ESL/EFL students](../publications/bebc80062bc1a2d6b689.md)

Venus W\. M\. Chan

This study examines the potential of XR MALL, an innovative application integrating Extended Reality \(XR\), Artificial Intelligence \(AI\), and mobile technologies to enhance public speaking skills among ESL/EFL students in higher education\. Grounded in the Constructivist Approach and the Public Speaking Competence Model, a quasi\-experimental design was employed with undergraduate students enrolled in an English presentation course at a Hong Kong university\. Participants were assigned to experimental and control groups, with the experimental group using XR MALL over a ten\-week intervention\. Pre\- and post\-intervention data assessed presentation skills, language proficiency, public speaking anxiety \(PSA\), and cognitive and affective outcomes\. Results indicated that students using XR MALL demonstrated significant improvements in self\-perceived English proficiency, presentation skills, vocabulary, listening ability, and reductions in PSA compared to the control group\. The experimental group also showed enhanced critical thinking, independent learning, confidence, and motivation\. Students reported high satisfaction with the VR practice simulations and AI\-powered speech feedback\. The findings highlight the pedagogical value of integrating VR\-based simulation, AI\-driven feedback, and AR\-supported vocabulary learning within a mobile\-assisted framework\. This study contributes to XR research by presenting a theory\-driven, purpose\-built mobile application that combines immersive practice and personalized feedback for public speaking training in ESL/EFL higher education contexts\.

## [Haugaard Christensen, Sonja: The Cosmological Worldview of Einstein &amp; Whitehead \- Through the Lens of Neurotheology](../publications/bec44fd57fbdeb0d6199.md)



\_Https://Academia\.Edu/Resource/Work/179200995\_\. 2026This essay establishes a rigorous, interdisciplinary framework reconciling the cosmological worldviews of Albert Einstein and Alfred North Whitehead through the analytical prism of neurotheology\. Moving beyond the historical oversimplification that frames Einstein as a mechanical materialist, the text evaluates his perspective as a committed Spinozan pantheism anchored in the macroscopic, geometric harmony of General Relativity\. Utilizing Whitehead’s Process and Reality \(1929\) and the neurotheological foundations established in The Brain as a Transducer of Spirit \(Christensen, 2026\), the study demonstrates that the fundamental divergence between these two master thinkers lies in a clash between a static, Parmenidean cosmos and a dynamic, Heraclitean flux\. Crucially, the introduction of the classical Stoic concept of the Logos provides a non\-anthropomorphic framework for understanding physical equilibrium, wherein individual or mental misalignment results in an automated biological self\-punishment managed by the chronic hyperactivity of the brain’s ego center, the Default Mode Network \(DMN\)\. Rather than promising absolute insight into the unmeasured ninety\-five percent of the universe \(Dark Matter and Dark Energy\), this paper frames this cosmic sector as a frontier of potentiality, wherein the down\-regulation of the DMN serves as a universal biological transducer that allows human biology to interface with the living, qualitative dimensions of nature\. Ultimately, by contextualizing Einstein’s profound reverence for the historical, pulsating figure of the Nazarene against his rejection of ecclesiastical dogma, the essay demonstrates how process physics and Stoic reason gracefully unite empirical science with the energetic reality of human feeling\.

## [Social Media Response to the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake: A Content Analysis of Digital Crisis Communication](../publications/bed03a0d92913fc35056.md)

Atar Thaung Htet; Htin Kyaw Lin

This study examines the role of social media in crisis communication and disaster governance during the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake\. In this study, we systematically investigate the content and functions of social media posts related to the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake by qualitative content analysis\. The study examined 97 publicly available social media posts, which were purposefully sampled from Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, X \(Twitter\), and YouTube from March 28 to April 4, 2025\. Findings revealed three main functions of social media: information dissemination, emotional expression and community mobilization\. Information dissemination was the dominant function \(51\.7%\), followed by emotional expression \(29\.9%\) and community mobilization \(18\.6%\)\. Facebook was the most frequently represented platform, while organizational and public pages contributed the largest proportion of posts\. The findings demonstrate that social media functioned as a multidimensional crisis communication mechanism supporting information sharing, emotional support, and collective action\. From the perspective of public administration and disaster governance, the study emphasizes the importance of social media use for emergency communication, public information management, citizen engagement, and relief coordination\. The study offers context\-specific evidence from Myanmar and practical insights for strengthening digital communication in disaster governance\.
