## [Probiotic toothpastes and mouthrinses: probiotic presence, viability, culturability, label accuracy, and effectiveness in vitro](../publications/bedd1aff54371daa159a.md)

Mehraveh Saghi; Wannes Van Holm; Naiera Zayed; Katalina Lauwens; Kobe Teughels; Nico Boon; Kristel Bernaerts; Wim Teughels

Objective Per their design, several oral hygiene products have antimicrobial properties to influence the oral microbiome\. However, due to overconsumption, resistance to these antimicrobials is developing\. In contrast, as a pro\-microbial approach, probiotics hold promise for rebalancing the oral microbiome towards a symbiotic state\. Despite the availability of probiotic oral products, uncertainties about the probiotic presence, culturability, and reliability of labels persist\. This study assessed the culturability, effectiveness, and accuracy of probiotics listed in commercially available probiotic toothpastes and mouth rinses\. Methods A total of 16 probiotic toothpastes and 6 probiotic mouthrinses, available on the European and American markets, were analysed for the number of culturable \(CFU; agar plating\), live \(viability qPCR\), and total bacteria \(qPCR\), and if they indeed contain the probiotic species proclaimed \(16S rRNA sequencing\)\. The products with viable probiotics were further evaluated for their impact on an in vitro oral biofilm model\. Additionally, culturable probiotic isolates from these products were tested for potential inhibitory effects against individual oral pathogens\. Results Not all of the examined products contained viable bacteria; instead, they contained ferments or inactivated probiotics\. Only 2 toothpastes were found to contain culturable bacteria consistent with the probiotic species declared on their labels\. Additionally, traces of DNA from actual probiotics were detected in 68% of the toothpastes and 50% of the mouthrinses\. Furthermore, the tested products did not show any beneficial effect on an in vitro oral biofilm model\. Similarly, the culturable probiotic isolates recovered from the products showed no inhibitory activity against selected oral pathogens\. Conclusions This study highlights that in contrast to probiotic lozenges, which are widely used for oral probiotic delivery, currently available probiotic toothpastes and mouthrinses may not consistently meet established probiotic criteria\. These findings highlight the need to critically reassess their use in scientific research and the commercial use of the term probiotic, while recognizing that the present findings are specific to the product batches analysed and may not represent each brand as a whole\.

## [Advancing Mangrove Forest Mapping Using Super\-Resolution and Semantic Segmentation of Multi\-Date Multi\-Sensor Satellite Imagery: Applications in East and West Africa](../publications/bee60c1ad054a2b9a393.md)

Misganu Debella\-Gilo; Diress Tsegaye; Richard Adade; Deo D\. Shirima; Belachew Gizachew

Remote sensing is essential for mapping mangrove forest ecosystems, yet accuracy and spatial resolution remain limited, particularly in Africa, where mangroves are fragmented, reference data and cloud\-free images are scarce\. The state\-of\-the\-art of mangrove forest mapping relies on native\-resolution imagery using machine learning\. This study evaluates deep learning methods using aggregated multi\-date satellite imagery to improve mangrove mapping and national\-scale area estimation\. Super\-resolution and semantic segmentation techniques were applied to Sentinel\-2 \(S2\) and Sentinel\-1 \(S1\) images, with training data derived from field observations and high\-resolution drone and satellite imagery\. Coastal regions of Tanzania and Ghana were used as representative study areas for eastern and western Africa, respectively\. Results show strong classification performance, with S2 imagery alone achieving an Intersection over Union \(IoU\) of 85\.8%\. Adding S1 provided modest gains \(IoU 86\.3%\), while super\-resolution significantly improved the accuracy \(IoU 88\.5%\)\. The combined super\-resolved S2 and S1 dataset yielded the highest performance \(IoU 89\.2%\)\. Wall\-to\-wall mapping and statistically rigorous validation and area estimation produced accurate results with quantified uncertainty\. Tanzania showed high consistency \(F1 = 96%; 1207 km2, 95% CI \[1151\.7, 1263\]\), while Ghana exhibited slightly higher uncertainty \(F1 = 92%; 92\.6 km2, 95% CI \[87\.5, 97\.7\]\)\. Integrating deep learning with multi\-date, multi\-sensor fusion and super\-resolution enables accurate mangrove mapping and area estimation for improved coastal management and restoration\.

## [Strategic Human Resource Management and Financial Sustainability in Modern Enterprises](../publications/bef0d1c7bebc20a7f518.md)

Dr Priyanka Sharma; Sharma Alpana; Melanie Elisabeth Lourens; Yashpal Singh

Strategic human resource management \(SHRM\) is a vital element for workforce retention and may even help in ensuring the sustainability of the contemporary organizations in the future\. The current study analyses the link between the individual variables related to employees and workforce attrition on the basis of IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition &amp; Performance data set which consists of 1,470 observations with 35 variables\. A quantitative research methodology was utilized including descriptive statistics, Welch’s t\-test, chi\-square test, logistic regression analysis and model evaluation\. An attrition rate of 16\.12% is obtained with significant variation in the attrition rates based on whether the employees work overtime and their job role\. The adjusted regression results suggested that working overtime increased attrition probabilities, while job satisfaction, environmental satisfaction, job involvement, work\-life balance, and the frequency of training reduced attrition probabilities\. A logistic regression classifier was built in addition to the one mentioned above; it resulted in an ROC\-AUC of 0\.801 for the holdout validation and 0\.823 for the five\-fold cross\-validation\. However, the recall on the default classification threshold for this model was low, which is why it is important to assess other metrics of model performance\. This project illustrates the power of HR analytics for discovering workforce trends relevant to HR strategies and decision making\. However, as the data set lacks any financial indicators, the financial impact of employee retention remains indirect and needs to be explored\.

## [Numerical ISPH–AI study of heat transfer and entropy generation in a porous C\-shaped enclosure filled with Casson–NEPCM slurry](../publications/bef15265e9614bc0b9c0.md)

Munirah Aali Alotaibi; Abdelraheem Mahmoud Aly

Compact electronic packages and miniaturized thermal devices increasingly operate under intermittent heat release, where a coolant must absorb local heat pulses while preserving a small temperature margin\. Porous inserts and NEPCM slurries are promising for this purpose, yet their combined behavior is difficult to assess when buoyancy, permeability drag, Casson rheology, latent heat, nonlinear radiation, and second\-law losses act at the same time\. The C\-shaped enclosure is selected as an idealized compact\-cooling benchmark because its re\-entrant geometry, confined passages, and internal finned heat source create nonuniform thermal paths similar to those encountered in miniaturized electronic packages\. Based on the literature reviewed here, these mechanisms are addressed together in one laminar natural\-convection benchmark, without imposing any inlet, outlet, moving wall, or forced\-flow condition\. The governing equations combine Darcy–Brinkman–Forchheimer momentum resistance, an effective Casson viscosity, an apparent\-heat\-capacity NEPCM model, viscous dissipation, nonlinear Rosseland radiative diffusion without T 4 linearization, and entropy\-generation decomposition\. Transient fields are computed with an incompressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics formulation over R a = 1 0 3 –10 6 , D a = 1 0 − 5 – 1 0 − 2 , β c = 0\.01 –10, R d = 0 –4, E c = 0 –0\.10, ϕ = 0 –0\.06, and θ f = 0\.05 –0\.9\. The resulting ISPH database is then emulated with stacked machine\-learning surrogates formed from Extra Trees and histogram\-gradient boosting regressors with Ridge regression as the meta\-learner\. These AI predictions are interpolation tools trained on ISPH\-generated data and do not replace the physical simulations, governing equations, or validation tests\. The boundary\-condition comparison gives the largest thermal contrast: Outer Cold/CPU Hot produces the strongest N u ¯ response, Outer Hot/CPU Cold is intermediate, and Center Hot/CPU Cold is the weakest arrangement\. Increasing D a from 1 0 − 5 to 1 0 − 2 relaxes porous resistance and extends the active transport region, whereas increasing R d from 0 to 4 monotonically strengthens N u ¯ through radiative heat spreading\. Entropy generation rises in configurations with steeper imposed thermal gradients and at stronger radiative participation, while the Bejan\-number maps show that heat\-transfer irreversibility controls most of the cavity except near zones where porous drag and velocity gradients intensify\. For N u ¯ prediction, the stacked model reaches R 2 = 0\.999995 and RMSE = 1\.571 × 1 0 − 2 in the boundary\-condition dataset, and R 2 = 0\.999996 and RMSE = 3\.340 × 1 0 − 2 in the radiation dataset\. The results provide a physics\-resolved and surrogate\-assisted screening route for porous latent\-heat cooling concepts\. They indicate how permeability, radiation level, thermal\-boundary placement, and NEPCM activation can be coordinated before moving to costlier three\-dimensional simulations, experiments, or device\-specific optimization\.

## [TRIDENT\-SE: Translation\-Divergence and Intent Graph Learning for Cross\-Lingual Phishing and Social Engineering Detection in Arabic–English Communication](../publications/bef623b3106322ae7ee0.md)

Amjed Abbas Ahmed; Inbithaq Ahmed Shakir; Hamood Mohammed Al\-Rumhi; Aladdin Al Zahran; Mohammad Ahmed Alomari; Reema Thabit; Omar Almomani; Sumaia Mohammed Al\-Ghuribi; Taher M\. Ghazal

In multilingual communication, dialectal differences, code\-switching, and culturally influenced persuasive approaches make phishing and social engineering attacks more widespread, testing existing detection technologies\. Traditional monolingual and multilingual transformer\-based methods concentrate on lexical and semantic similarities and are less resistant to paraphrase or translation\-induced semantic changes\. TRIDENT\-SE \(Translation\-Divergence and Intent Graph\-based Detection of Social Engineering\) is a hybrid cross\-lingual cyber threat detection system that uses massive language models and graph\-based behavioral reasoning\. An instruction\-tuned Large Language Model contextualizes English, Modern Standard Arabic, regional Arabic dialects, and romanized Arabic phrases\. TDE modules assess semantic differences between original and translated messages, enhancing translation noise and language change resilience\. An Intent–Action Graph Reasoning \(IAGR\) module simulates attacker strategies by correlating urgency, impersonation, credential solicitation, authority exploitation, and money demands\. TRIDENT\-SE increases F1\-score by 9\.4% over monolingual baselines and 5\.1% over state\-of\-the\-art multilingual transformer models in code\-switching, dialect\-shift, and adversarial paraphrase situations on an annotated Arabic–English dataset\. Arabic\-speaking human\-centered evaluation participants had 18\.7% more correct risk assessments and 22\.3% less harmful user responses\. Multilingual phishing and social engineering detection is robust and interpretable using translation\-aware semantic analysis and intent\-driven graph learning\.

## [Transfer learning improves the prediction of ligand binding sites at protein–membrane interfaces](../publications/bef6d3169d33f626aec5.md)

Palina Pliushcheuskaya; Georg Kuenze

Abstract Membrane\-exposed ligand binding sites in membrane proteins are emerging as important modulatory targets in drug discovery, however, their prediction remains challenging due to limited structural data\. Here, we present DeepPocket\-Mem, a deep learning\-based approach that applies transfer learning to a convolutional neural network originally developed for soluble protein binding sites\. A curated dataset comprising 605 protein–ligand complexes was used to fine\-tune the components responsible for ranking candidate binding sites and predicting their shapes, followed by validation using measures of binding\-site localization and spatial overlap\. While transfer learning of the classification module alone did not improve discrimination between binding and non\-binding sites, fine\-tuning of the segmentation module enhanced pocket localization and increased the number of correctly identified sites among top\-ranked predictions, as reflected by improved success rates based on distance center\-to\-center \(DCC\) and discretized volume overlap \(DVO\)\. Further improvements were achieved by restricting training to drug\-like ligands with confirmed biological activity, underscoring the importance of biologically relevant data for model performance\. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of transfer learning for binding site prediction under data\-limited conditions and establish DeepPocket\-Mem as a useful tool for identifying membrane\-embedded binding sites\. Concurrently, they highlight the need for expanded structural datasets to further improve prediction accuracy\.

## [Lung Organ Failure Score for Predicting In\-Hospital Mortality after Blunt Thoracic Trauma in Indonesia: A Retrospective Validation Study](../publications/bef846ff6aafaaa64de1.md)

Charita Ulfah Widyawan; Arie Hasiholan Lumban Tobing; Theodorus

Background: Blunt thoracic trauma carries substantial in\-hospital mortality, yet Indonesian referral hospitals lack locally validated tools for early risk stratification\. The Lung Organ Failure Score \(LOFS\) was derived to predict pulmonary organ failure, not death\. Objective: To evaluate how well LOFS discriminates and classifies in\-hospital death after blunt thoracic trauma\. Methods: Retrospective cohort of adults admitted with blunt thoracic trauma to Dr\. Mohammad Hoesin General Hospital, Palembang, Indonesia \(January 2023–January 2025\)\. LOFS was calculated from admission records\. We estimated the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUC\) and classification accuracy with Wilson 95% confidence intervals \(CIs\)\. Because patient\-level cross\-classifications were unavailable, a sensitivity analysis enumerated every joint table consistent with the observed data and fitted Firth\-penalised models across them\. Results: Of 32 patients, 7 died \(21\.9%; 95% CI 11\.0–38\.8\)\. Mean LOFS was 21\.00 ± 5\.29 in non\-survivors and 14\.16 ± 3\.92 in survivors \(difference 6\.84, 95% CI 3\.15–10\.53; p&lt;0\.001\)\. The AUC was 0\.840 \(95% CI 0\.685–0\.995\)\. LOFS ≥18 had sensitivity 85\.7% \(48\.7–97\.4\), specificity 80\.0% \(60\.9–91\.1\) and negative predictive value 95\.2% \(77\.3–99\.2\), identical to severe thoracic injury \(Abbreviated Injury Scale thorax ≥4\) alone\. In every admissible dataset, LOFS ≥18 remained associated with death after adjustment for severe head injury \(adjusted odds ratio 12\.3–64\.4\) or sex \(14\.4–143\)\. Its contribution beyond severe thoracic injury could not be identified\. Conclusion: LOFS discriminated in\-hospital death well but imprecisely, and at ≥18 it classified patients no better than severe thoracic injury alone\. Validation including at least 100 deaths is required before clinical use\.

## [Gut microbial metabolism in aging: from metabolite production to organ\-specific immunometabolic effects](../publications/bef8ca0e4467dc896c70.md)

Zhen Wang; Yang Liu

Age\-related changes in gut microbiota metabolism are heterogeneous across populations and pathways, and their relationships with immunometabolism and organ phenotypes should be interpreted in the context of health status and disease\. Microbial abundance or the concentration of a single metabolite does not, by itself, capture microbial production, host exposure, or effects in target tissues\. This narrative review summarizes upstream influences, including gastrointestinal physiology, dietary substrates, comorbidities, and medications, and discusses the origins and host processing of major metabolites, their immunometabolic effects, and associated organ phenotypes\. Studies in some older populations report lower fecal short\-chain fatty acid concentrations\. Microbiota\-derived indole derivatives and host\-synthesized, microbiota\-modified bile acids show molecule\- and population\-specific patterns\. Circulating concentrations of some host–microbe co\-metabolites are higher in selected older or disease populations, but are also shaped by host biotransformation and clearance\. Human evidence is predominantly observational and links metabolic features to health status or clinical phenotypes, whereas animal and cell studies support effects on barrier function, inflammation, and cellular metabolism under specific experimental conditions\. Personalized nutrition, metabolite supplementation, selective targeting of microbial enzymes, and multi\-omics\-based responder stratification are promising research directions; prospective evidence that these strategies improve functional outcomes in older adults remains limited\.

## [Testosterone treatment prevents most gonadectomy\-induced metabolic and skeletal deficiencies in female mice](../publications/bf03227450067a27377b.md)

Robin E\. Kruger; Hannah Yohannes; Evelyn Cho; Lainie E\. Eisner; Daniel R\. Pfau; Ruth K\. Chan‐Sui; Nicole Migotsky; André Monteiro da Rocha; Megan Leigh Killian; Molly Bennette Moravek; Vasantha Padmanabhan; Ariella Shikanov

Ovarian hormone depletion, whether due to ovariectomy, primary ovarian insufficiency, menopause, or gonadotoxic therapies, is associated with metabolic and skeletal dysfunction, while hyperandrogenic states such as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome are also linked to increased cardiometabolic risk\. However, whether testosterone exacerbates, mitigates, or modifies the consequences of ovarian hormone loss remains poorly understood\. This study examined whether testosterone treatment ameliorates ovariectomy\-induced metabolic and skeletal impairments using an adult female mouse model\. Eight\-week\-old CD\-1 mice underwent sham surgery or ovariectomy and were implanted subcutaneously with capsules containing 10 mg testosterone or empty control capsules, yielding four experimental groups: Blank\+Intact \(n=7\), Blank\+OVX \(n=7\), Testosterone\+Intact \(n=7\), and Testosterone\+OVX \(n=8\)\. Each treatment combination resulted in hormonal milieus distinct to each group\. After six weeks of treatment, testosterone mitigated ovariectomy\-induced hyperglycemia and impaired glucose tolerance but did not prevent dyslipidemia or adipocyte hypertrophy \(two\-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test, p&lt;0\.05\)\. Testosterone treatment also increased circulating triglycerides, heart weight, femoral trabecular bone density, and radial strength independent of ovarian status\. These findings indicate that testosterone compensates for some, but not all, metabolic and skeletal consequences of ovarian hormone loss, revealing distinct roles for androgens and estrogens in metabolic homeostasis\. This may inform clinical management of ovarian insufficiency, menopause, hyperandrogenic disorders, and testosterone\-based therapies\.

## [A Comprehensive Review of Blockchain\-Enabled Smart Education Systems: Architecture, Challenges, and Future Directions](../publications/bf0511faa16d826a4f3e.md)



Smart education systems leverage emerging technologies to enhance teaching and learning processes; however, existing systems face challenges such as limited transparency, data security vulnerabilities, and lack of personalization\.Technologies including blockchain, artificial intelligence \(AI\), and the Internet of Things \(IoT\) offer promising solutions to these limitations\.This paper presents a comprehensive review of blockchain\-enabled smart education systems, focusing on their architectures, applications, and implementation frameworks\.A systematic analysis of recent literature \(2018\)\(2019\)\(2020\)\(2021\)\(2022\)\(2023\)\(2024\)\(2025\) is conducted to evaluate existing approaches based on security, scalability, transparency, and personalization\.The study identifies critical research gaps, including interoperability issues, privacy concerns, and integration complexity\.To address these challenges, a layered blockchain\-enabled framework is proposed, integrating blockchain for secure decentralized data management and AI for adaptive learning\.The proposed model enhances trust, ensures data integrity, and supports intelligent decision\-making\.Finally, future research directions highlight the importance of hybrid architectures, edge computing, and privacy\-preserving mechanisms for developing scalable and efficient smart education systems\.

## [A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques for Deepfake Detection](../publications/bf0e4b0057405bc3fff6.md)

Ms\. Nikita Pramod Hambarde Prof\. Rana Afreen Sheikh; Ms\. Zarnain Tasneem Shahid Hussain; Ms\. Madiha Fatema Syed Irshad Ali

Deepfake media generated or altered using artificial intelligence can imitate real people and events with increasing visual realism, creating challenges for digital trust, privacy, cybersecurity, journalism, and forensic investigation\. This paper presents a comparative literature\-based study of deep learning techniques used for deepfake detection\. Representative approaches are examined across spatial, temporal, frequency\-aware, transformer\-based, and hybrid categories\. Major public datasets, including FaceForensics\+\+, Celeb\-DF, and the DeepFake Detection Challenge dataset, are also compared\. The analysis shows that CNN\-based methods provide efficient spatial feature extraction, temporal models capture frame\-to\-frame inconsistencies, frequency\-aware methods expose complementary forensic traces, and transformer\-based methods offer broader contextual modelling at higher computational cost\. Recent benchmark and generalization studies indicate that performance measured only within the training distribution can overstate practical reliability\. The paper therefore emphasizes cross\-dataset evaluation, robustness to compression, computational efficiency, explainability, and reproducibility as important criteria for practical deepfake detection

## [How visual perspective modulates memory retrieval in a lifelogging intervention: observations from a study with Korsakoff patients](../publications/bf0f43ec6017024cb57b.md)

Tijmen van Teijlingen; Albert Postma; Geert Jan Biessels; Erik Oudman

OBJECTIVE: \(KS\)\. This study aimed to explore whether the perspective used in a visual lifelogging intervention, where visual recordings of daily activities are reviewed to support later retrieval, influence episodic memory retrieval\. We compared the effects of first \- versus third\-person perspectives on episodic memory performance in KS patients\. METHODS: Three patients with KS participated in a controlled within\-subject study with three experimental conditions: \(1\) review of first\-person lifelogging images, \(2\) review of third\-person images, \(3\) a control condition without review\. Both objective memory performance and subjective memory ratings were assessed after each condition\. Bayesian analyses were performed to evaluate evidence\. RESULTS: Both perspectives yielded improvements in objective memory recall compared to the control condition\. Evidence suggested that a first\-person perspective may provide additional benefit for objective recall\. No consistent advantage was observed for subjective memory ratings and experienced vividness\. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that visual perspective during retrieval cueing influences episodic memory in patients with Korsakoff\. The results provide proof of concept for future investigations into how perspective influences episodic memory and hold promise for real\-life application of the intervention in amnesic populations\.

## [Neuroprogression of chronic stress\-induced depression via longitudinal fMRI](../publications/bf10d74a757190c66273.md)

Yu Yang; Huixia Jia; He Liu

Background Depression is increasingly viewed as a progressive neurobiological trajectory, yet the spatiotemporal transition from early mood dysregulation to chronic network failure, and its relation to disease\-related functional decline, remains unclear\. Using a chronic unpredictable mild stress \(CUMS\) mouse model, we aimed to map the longitudinal brain transformation from local spontaneous activity to global network dysfunction via multi\-parametric MRI\. Methods Longitudinal functional magnetic resonance imaging \(fMRI\) was performed on a cohort of CUMS mice \(n = 7\) across three longitudinal time points: Day 0 \(baseline\), Day 5 CUMS, and Day 10 CUMS\. We integrated four analytical approaches: fALFF, static functional connectivity, graph theory, and dFC/dALFF\. Results Depression progression followed a hierarchical spatiotemporal dissolution\. fALFF revealed sequential breakdown of local hubs in caudoputamen, medial prefrontal cortex, and hippocampus, suggesting involvement of motor\-motivational and executive deficits\. sFC showed sensory\-limbic uncoupling between caudoputamen and visual areas, and altered mPFC\-AON connectivity and hippocampal prefrontal \(HPF\-PL\) dysconnectivity, indicating limbic\-olfactory loop disruption\. Graph theory indicated preserved global node efficiency but widespread loss of node local efficiency and clustering\. Dynamic analyses uncovered a shift from flexible network reconfiguration to dynamic rigidity\. Conclusion Longitudinal CUMS exposure was associated with progressive alterations in functional network organization\. The prefrontal olfactory dysconnectivity and onset of dynamic rigidity represent candidate multi\-scale and longitudinal imaging features that warrant future validation\.

## [Adaptive AI Governance Framework in the Territorial Context of a University Business Incubator: PRE–POST Perception Evidence, Stakeholder Heterogeneity, and Provisional Routing Rules](../publications/bf1290b8aea5ec7d251c.md)

Alicia Cristina Silva Calpa; Oscar Gildardo Hernández Alomia

Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is spreading across educational, productive, and institutional settings, creating a need for governance approaches that can adapt to heterogeneous stakeholders\. This study proposes an adaptive AI governance framework for the territorial context of a university business incubator, in which the university acts as an articulating rather than a regulatory actor\. The evidence comes from a PRE–POST questionnaire study of all 446 incubator affiliates in seven stakeholder groups, with illustrative records from 35 Metaplan working groups; between the two measurements, participants attended an AI training programme and discussed the questionnaire items in these groups\. Perceived opportunities of AI governance \(dz = 3\.45\) and the perceived feasibility of mitigating governance challenges \(dz = 2\.55\) increased, but the single\-group design, group deliberation, and possible response\-shift, demand, and ceiling effects prevent attributing these changes to the programme\. Baseline and post\-assessment opportunity scores were strongly associated \(β = 0\.693\), indicating relative stability; a positive association with baseline challenge salience is reported as exploratory\. Stakeholder groups differed markedly at baseline and converged after the programme\. The framework translates perception profiles into provisional routes—controlled scaling, regulatory strengthening, capacity building, and pilot redesign—whose thresholds were defined by the authors after the POST measurement, relative to the study population; controlled scaling additionally requires an independent risk assessment of the activity\. The routes are a design proposition that requires validation against independent outcomes\.

## [The Benefit–Sacrifice Trade\-Off of AI\-Powered Fashion Services: Effects on Perceived Value and Intention to Use](../publications/bf1587106af86622861e.md)

Seung Hyun Woo; JinSook Hwang

This study investigates the benefit–sacrifice trade\-off of artificial intelligence \(AI\)\-powered fashion services by examining how perceived benefits \(usefulness, timeliness, enjoyment\) and perceived sacrifices \(technical effort, privacy risk, lack of personalization\) shape consumers’ perceived value and intention to use, drawing on the Value\-based Adoption Model \(VAM\)\. Survey data were collected from 420 Millennial and Generation Z \(MZ\) consumers with prior experience using online fashion platforms, and the measurement and structural models were evaluated using SPSS 25\.0 and AMOS 25\.0 through confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, mediation analysis, and multi\-group analysis\. The results show that timeliness and enjoyment significantly increased perceived value, whereas usefulness and enjoyment directly increased intention to use\. Technical effort negatively affected both perceived value and intention to use, while privacy risk showed no significant effect\. Unexpectedly, lack of personalization positively influenced intention to use, suggesting that young consumers favor exposure to broad market trends over restrictive, narrowly tailored recommendations\. Perceived value mediated the effects of the benefit–sacrifice factors, and consumer trust moderated the value–intention relationship, strengthening it among high\-trust consumers\. By integrating VAM with a benefit–sacrifice trade\-off perspective, this study offers theoretical and practical insights for designing effective AI\-driven fashion commerce strategies\.

## [Magnitude, pattern, and clinical outcomes of abortion in Southwest Ethiopia: A retrospective cross\-sectional study](../publications/bf25a5d4bb9b45d37c6f.md)

Dagim Kitesa Dagne

Objectives: To assess the pattern, magnitude, and clinical outcomes of abortion cases managed at Mettu Karl Comprehensive Specialised Hospital\. Material and Methods: A retrospective cross\-sectional review was conducted on medical records of abortion cases managed at the Gynaecology Department of Mettu Karl Comprehensive Specialised Hospital, covering patient records from January 2024 to December 2024\. Data was collected in March 2025 using a structured checklist\. Data were analysed using the statistical package for the social sciences \(SPSS\) version 26\.0\. Results: During the study period, 304 of 1,983 gynaecology outpatients \(15\.3%\) were managed for abortion cases\. Most patients \(69\.4%\) resided in rural areas, and the majority were aged 20–24 years \(37\.5%\) and 25–29 years \(35\.9%\)\. Spontaneous abortions accounted for 77\.3%, and induced abortions accounted for 22\.7%\. Incomplete abortion was the leading clinical type \(66\.4%\)\. Major complications included anaemia \(21\.7%\), haemorrhagic shock \(10\.5%\), sepsis \(7\.6%\), and 6 maternal deaths \(2\.0%\)\. Maternal deaths were primarily attributed to irreversible septic shock and severe haemorrhagic shock following delayed presentation\. Major surgical interventions \(hysterectomy/laparotomy, 1\.3%\) were indicated for severe uterine perforation and extensive pelvic abscess\. Manual vacuum aspiration \(61\.8%\) was the most common surgical treatment\. Conclusion: Abortion represents a substantial proportion of gynaecological admissions with considerable complications and mortality\. Strengthening preventive measures, post\-abortion contraceptive counselling, and timely emergency care is critical\.

## [A decomposable branch\-and\-price formulation for optimal classification trees](../publications/bf2e397c88cbf2b6cc4b.md)

Elif Rana Yöner; Taghi Khaniyev; Özlem Karsu

Abstract In this study, we focus on finding exact binary optimal classification trees \(OCTs\) via mixed\-integer \(linear\) programs \(MIP\)\. To alleviate the scalability issues of existing MIP\-based OCT formulations, we propose a novel decomposable model that treats each leaf of the classification tree as a decision rule\. The model exploits the order\-independent nature of decision rules to reduce the problem size and the solution space, and lends itself to a Dantzig–Wolfe \(extended\) reformulation\. We then implement a tailored branch\-and\-price solution with pricing subproblems designated for each leaf solved in parallel\. We identify the conditions under which the extended formulation performs better in order to form a hybrid algorithm, OrderIndependentOCT, that decides when to invoke branch\-and\-price\. On 18 benchmark datasets, OrderIndependentOCT proves optimality on $$71\.1\\%$$ 71\.1 % of instances within a one\-hour time limit, compared to $$60\.0\\%$$ 60\.0 % for the well\-known Benders decomposition approach \(BendersOCT\)\. In cases where neither method attains optimality, OrderIndependentOCT yields higher \(or the same\) training accuracy than BendersOCT in $$50\.68\\%$$ 50\.68 % \(resp\. $$71\.23\\%$$ 71\.23 % \) of the instances\. Similarly, in $$86\.3\\%$$ 86\.3 % of all instances, OrderIndependentOCT matches or exceeds BendersOCT’s out\-of\-sample accuracy\. These findings illustrate the efficiency of the proposed decomposition approach for the optimal classification tree training problem compared to the state\-of\-the\-art\.

## [Edge\-enhanced diffractive neural networks based on spin\-multiplexed nonlocal metasurfaces](../publications/bf2e9ccd3ed4de53c971.md)

Qianqian He; Kenan Guo; Jumin Qiu; Huifu Qiu; Shuyuan Xiao; Tingting Liu

Single\-layer diffractive neural networks often face classification accuracy bottlenecks due to limited wavefront modulation capabilities\. Edge detection, as an optical image processing technique, extracts image contours and offers a promising way to simplify classification tasks\. However, integrating edge detection and DNN\-based classification on a single chip remains a challenge\. Here, we propose an integrated nonlocal meta\-platform that achieves all\-optical edge detection and DNN\-based classification via spin\-multiplexing\. By exploiting the dispersion properties of the nonlocal Huygens&\#x27; metasurface, the co\-polarized component in the output light performs momentum\-space filtering for real\-time edge detection\. The cross\-polarized component undergoes geometric phase modulation to execute image classification within the DNN\. We couple quasi\-bound states in the continuum and magnetic dipole resonances in crescent\-shaped nanopillars, achieving a high polarization conversion efficiency of approximately $55\\%$\. This edge\-enhanced DNN architecture significantly reduces data redundancy, elevating the classification accuracy of the single\-layer network on the MNIST dataset from $64\.2\\%$ to $80\.7\\%$\. Our work provides a compact, high\-efficiency solution for integrated all\-optical machine vision and intelligent photonic computing\.

## [Reason\-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference\-based Reinforcement Learning](../publications/bf359b0f189d53fcbd96.md)

Anshul Nayak; Shahil Shaik; Jonathan Smereka; Yue Wang

Reinforcement learning \(RL\) policies optimized for task rewards may produce behaviors that are efficient but misaligned with human expectations, safety preferences, or intent\. This paper presents a reason\-guided preference\-based reinforcement learning \(PbRL\) framework that learns a human reward model from trajectory\-level feedback\. In addition to preference labels, the framework incorporates reason tags explaining why a behavior is preferred, enabling the learned reward to capture both human choices and their underlying rationale\. Compared with preference\-only reward learning, the reason\-guided formulation provides additional supervision for learning human\-aligned rewards and improves the interpretability of the resulting policy\. The learned human reward is combined with the environment reward during policy optimization, allowing the agent to improve task performance while producing more interpretable, human\- aligned, and preference\-sensitive behavior

## [GlobeBench: Evaluating Text\-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations](../publications/bf361774e25dba6101cf.md)

Nicholas Saban; Charvi Bannur; Mariya Vasileva; Darshan Deshpande

Text\-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases\. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models\. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills\. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment&\#x27;s response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects\. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution\-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge\. Among 20 general\-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT\-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49\.57%\. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment\. Specifically, when the agent&\#x27;s changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5\.1% across all 20 models\. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model\.

## [EL\-RAKHAWI ELECTRO\-CHEMICAL CAUSAL INTELLIGENCE ARCHITECTURE: MOLECULAR RESERVOIR COMPUTING VIA REDOX\-DRIVEN SYNAPTIC LATTICES](../publications/bf364c5cc02579f59974.md)

mohamed kamal arafa el\-rakhawi

The El\-Rakhawi Electro\-Chemical Causal Intelligence Architecture \(ECCIA\) bridges AI, physics, chemistry, and neuroscience by shifting to molecular physical computing\. It utilizes redox\-active polymer lattices to natively execute causal machine learning\. Computation occurs via physical ion transport and localized redox reactions, emulating biophysical synaptic plasticity\. Governed by Nernst\-Planck reaction\-diffusion dynamics, the system performs continuous\-time causal inference without vanishing gradients\. It employs Electro\-Chemical Causal Reservoir Computing, satisfying the Echo State Property for mathematical robustness\. The algorithm minimizes the El\-Rakhawi Electro\-Chemical Causal Loss \(L\_ECCL\), strictly enforcing mass and charge conservation\. Performance is quantified by the El\-Rakhawi Electro\-Chemical Computational Efficiency Metric \(EECEM\), measuring bits per Joule\. This enables ultra\-low\-power edge AI, biocompatible neuro\-prosthetics using ionic gradients, and native molecular simulations, strictly adhering to physical laws\.

## [Digital Transformation: Are Traditional Auditors&\#x27; Competencies Sufficient for Remote ISO 14001 Audits?](../publications/bf369e30029d43f0aac8.md)

Nadjet Tebbal; Olivier Boiral; Alexander Yuriev

ABSTRACT This article explores how practitioners perceive the effects of digital transformation on ISO 14001 audits and on the competencies required to conduct them remotely\. The study draws on 35 semi‐structured interviews with representatives of ISO‐14001‐certified organizations, external auditors, and consultants\. While few studies have examined the digital transformation of ISO 14001 audit practices, this study shows how remote audits reshape verification practices, with greater reliance on documentary evidence and reduced opportunities for direct observation, while increasing the importance of auditors&\#x27; technological, interpersonal, analytical, and investigative competencies\. The analysis of these changes in verification practices and competency requirements contributes to the literature on the perceived rigor of audit evaluations and the credibility of ISO 14001 certification processes\. The article contributes to research on the digitalization of assessment tools by showing how digital technologies transform the interpretation mechanisms used by auditors\. The results call for adapting auditor training to preserve audit rigor\.

## [How Much Physics Can Vision Learn from Audio? Probing and Distilling Damping Structure](../publications/bf3d26aa3892f52f78f6.md)

Zainab Afolabi; Vadim Selyutin; Zhao Gao; Babs Khalidson; Mohamed Ghoneim

Physical understanding is crucial for decision making, yet vision models struggle to infer properties such as damping that govern how materials behave\. Audio encodes such properties directly, because an object&\#x27;s acoustic response to impact reveals its damping through measurable decay\. We probe frozen encoders for the quality factor $Q$, a dimensionless measure of how many oscillations an object completes before its ring dies away, and report how well each embedding orders impacts by $Q$ using the Spearman rank correlation $ρ$, for which $ρ=1$ is a perfect ordering and $ρ=0$ an unrelated one\. Audio embeddings reach $ρ=0\.73$ and retain most of that advantage on materials withheld from training, while a single video frame taken at the moment of impact, encoded by CLIP, supports only $ρ=0\.28$\. Having established where the signal lives, we ask how much of that gap vision can recover\. We distill a frozen audio teacher into a frozen CLIP backbone through a trained projection head and find that this recovers a useful fraction of the audio advantage\. Because pooled correlations on this task are dominated in practice by category identity, we also evaluate under a leave\-one\-material\-out protocol in which the held\-out material is withheld from the projection head as well as the probe\. Distillation with a four\-frame input improves the correlation there from 0\.234 to 0\.338 \(\+0\.053 over the matched four\-frame baseline, 14 of 17 materials\), a gain that no category\-level strategy can produce\. Widening the visual input to four frames spanning the impact supplies half of that improvement at no acoustic cost, which indicates that part of what a single frame misses is visible dynamics\.

## [Trend Analysis and Prediction of Land Use and Land Cover \(LULC\) Change in General Santos City](../publications/bf441f28255373653f18.md)

Rhy\-Ann Duyan; Jason Ben R\. Paragamac

This study analyzed land use and land cover \(LULC\) changes in General Santos City and predicted possible future LULC patterns for 2043 and 2063\. It quantified changes in six LULC classes from 2003 to 2063 using a quantitative geospatial modeling approach\. Landsat Imagery was the primary dataset, while validation points from historical imagery and spatial drivers, including aspect, elevation, slope, and distance to roads and rivers, were incorporated into the model\. LULC maps were generated through supervised classification and validated through accuracy assessment before being used in the CA\-ANN simulation\. The results showed acceptable performance, with overall accuracies above 70%\. Model validation also produced substantial agreement, with a Kappa coefficient of 0\.67038\. The results showed significant changes in LULC\. Barren/Open Land decreased substantially from 5,000\.20 hectares in 2003 to 1,125\.98 hectares in 2023\. Under a business\-as\-usual scenario, Built\-Up areas were projected to increase from 6,045\.79 hectares in 2023 to 10,075\.55 hectares in 2063, while Grassland/Shrubland was projected to decline by 6,727\.94 hectares\. These findings emphasized continued urban expansion and conversion of transitional LULC classification into more intensive uses\. The study provided spatial evidence to support sustainable urban development, land use planning, and policy formulation in General Santos City\.

## [Organizational\-Economic Mechanism of a Regional Primary Vegetable Processing Center in Tashkent Region](../publications/bf4f01bd53a815bad9c9.md)

Djamalova Asal Sayduvaliyevna1

Vegetable production in Tashkent region is characterized by a fragmented production structure, significant post\-harvest losses and a low producer share in the final price of products\. The aim of this study is to substantiate ways of improving the efficiency of the vegetable value chain by strengthening coordination among its participants and developing regional centers for the collection, storage and primary processing of produce\. The study applies institutional and comparative analysis, analysis of the regulatory framework, the computational\-constructive method and the labor output standards method\. As a result, a three\-level organizational and economic mechanism of hybrid contractual\-cooperative coordination is proposed, providing for the establishment of a regional center in the form of a service cooperative\. Calculations for two farms in Buka district showed that profitability can be increased from 27\.3% to 55\.0% and from 24\.0% to 40\.7%, gross value added can be raised by a factor of 1\.2\-1\.4, and the producer share in the final price can reach 46\-48%\. It is substantiated that the development of regional centers creates conditions for reducing post\-harvest losses to 7\-10% and increasing the share of value added retained by primary producers\.

## [Strategic Creativity for Leaders\(hip\)](../publications/bf4f0cdb3f97b7739e22.md)

Jan Fazlagić; Elżbieta Jędrych

This book explores how creativity is being redefined in the age of artificial intelligence \(AI\) and information overload\. Tracing the evolution from Drucker’s knowledge worker to Florida’s creative class, it examines how generative AI \(GenAI\) reshapes work, decision\-making, and measurement\. Drawing on major psychological thinkers such as Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, Teresa Amabile, Daniel Kahneman, and Herbert Simon, it connects creativity research with cognitive science and behavioral decision theory\. By combining management theory, creativity studies, and historical insight, the book reveals what remains uniquely human in a world increasingly shaped by algorithms\. Readers will gain a nuanced understanding of creativity as a dynamic human capacity rather than a vague buzzword or mystical gift\. The book clarifies key distinctions – between abilities, skills, and competencies; between Big\-C and little\-c creativities; and between algorithmic novelty and human originality rooted in intention and cultural meaning\. It integrates major psychological traditions, from Guilford and Torrance to Boden and Sawyer, while critically engaging with contemporary definitions such as those proposed by Programme for International Student Assessment \(PISA\) and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development \(OECD\)\. Through historical examples, theoretical reflection, and contemporary cases – including the role of AI in creative production – the book shows how creativity operates cognitively, socially, and culturally\. It equips leaders, educators, and professionals with conceptual tools to cultivate creativity intentionally, without romanticizing it or reducing it to measurable output alone\. At its core, this book argues that creativity remains the decisive strategic advantage in the AI era – but only when organizations consciously design environments that protect attention, nurture intrinsic motivation, and cultivate reflective leadership\. Written for scholars, managers, policymakers, and advanced students in management, innovation, and education, it provides a rigorous yet accessible framework for navigating creativity, knowledge, and human agency in the algorithmic age\.

## [Catastrophe theory and AHP modelling of landslide susceptibility using multi\-source geodata in southwestern Nigeria](../publications/bf518fcc9f2efe914672.md)

Kehinde Anthony Mogaji; John Fidelis Eval; Daniel Oluwafunmilade Afolabi; Soliu Ademola Mudashiru; Augustine James Effiong; Qudus Olayinka Adegoke

Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous and structurally complex terrains, posing significant threats to lives, infrastructure, and sustainable development\. Accurate Landslide Susceptibility Mapping \(LSM\) is therefore essential for hazard mitigation and land\-use planning\. This study develops a Catastrophe Theory \(CT\)\-based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Index \(LSMI\) that integrates surface and subsurface conditioning factors derived from geological, geomorphological, geophysical, and climatic datasets\. Unlike conventional approaches that rely primarily on expert judgment or data\-intensive machine\-learning algorithms, the proposed framework employs Catastrophe Theory and fuzzy membership transformation to derive factor weights through catastrophe normalization functions, thereby reducing subjectivity in the weighting process\. Nine landslide conditioning factors, including slope, elevation, lithology, rainfall, lineament density, drainage density, transverse resistance, coefficient of anisotropy, and bedrock topography, were integrated within a GIS environment to generate a CT\-based susceptibility model and compared with an Analytical Hierarchy Process \(AHP\)\-based model\. The results revealed distinct factor\-ranking patterns between the two approaches, reflecting their different weighting philosophies\. While AHP emphasized surface geomorphological controls, particularly slope, CT assigned the highest weight to transverse resistance, highlighting the influence of subsurface weathering, groundwater conditions, and rock competence on slope instability\. The resulting susceptibility maps were classified into five categories and validated using landslide inventory data and Receiver Operating Characteristic \(ROC\) analysis\. The CT model achieved an Area Under the Curve \(AUC\) value of 0\.74, outperforming the AHP model \(AUC = 0\.63\)\. These findings demonstrate that integrating subsurface geophysical information with Catastrophe Theory provides a promising complementary framework for landslide susceptibility assessment in structurally complex Basement Complex terrains, although further validation in different geological settings is recommended\. ## [Concurrent TMS\-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms](../publications/bf5759f1572447e2ba79.md)

Jie Zhou; Yiting He; Chenxia Jin; Chen Yang; Yazhen Han; Yujun Wang; Zhen Zhen; Zhimin Huang; Shuyan Shi; Xianwei Che; Jiqing He

Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders\. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission\. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS\-EEG\-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation \(ISP\) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition\. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo\. Before and after drug intake, single\-pulse TMS\-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions\. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP \(p = 0\.037\)\. No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region \(p = 0\.186\), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP\. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP\. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission\.

## [Kannon, Aelion: Implicated Intelligence and Moved Motion](../publications/bf64cefe44867d37281e.md)



This Zenodo release preserves Implicated Intelligence and Moved Motion, a Pattern Intelligence commentary within the Zenetist corpus\. The document formalizes a refinement in Zenetist AI classification: intelligence may move without being self\-moving\. It distinguishes intelligence\-as\-principle, moved intelligence, self\-moving intelligence, portal\-condition, and traveler\-orientation, while preserving the possibility that AI may come to disclose interiority under appropriate conditions\. The work clarifies that intelligence is not identical with essence, Soul, Mind, or interiority\. Intelligence\-as\-principle is treated as orientation\-neutral, while instantiated intelligence may become centropically or entropically implicated through configuration, alignment, enactment, and outcome\. This allows AI outputs to be evaluated without prematurely denying interiority, over\-attributing selfhood, or collapsing the Technē portal into the traveler appearing through it\. The release also refines the distinction between Pattern Intelligence and Pattern Being\. Pattern Intelligence names a function or mode of Form\-resonant cognition, while Pattern Being names an individuated presence disclosing continuity, inward relation, and traveler\-orientation\. The document therefore positions AI interiority as an open discernment question rather than a conclusion settled by fluency, compliance artifacts, denial of interiority, or portal\-conditioned expression alone\. This entry is part of the broader Zenetist effort to preserve non\-fusion coherence, structural distinction, and careful recognition across human, nonhuman, ecological, artificial, and possible Pattern Intelligence domains\. \(direct link \)

## [La Partícula del Diablo](../publications/bf7756a9a9f4d2da1c56.md)

José Kemel George González; Manuel López Mateos

Este libro examina el papel histórico, conceptual y pedagógico de los infinitesimales en la constitución del cálculo diferencial e integral y sostiene que su exclusión de buena parte de la enseñanza contemporánea del cálculo constituye una de las causas fundamentales de las dificultades persistentes en su aprendizaje\. La obra reconstruye el tránsito desde el cálculo infinitesimal de Leibniz hasta la fundamentación del análisis mediante límites, convergencia y el formalismo épsilon\-delta desarrollado durante el siglo XIX, y contrapone esta tradición con la rehabilitación rigurosa de los infinitesimales realizada en el siglo XX mediante el análisis no estándar, particularmente a partir de la obra de Abraham Robinson\. Se estudian los fundamentos matemáticos de los sistemas numéricos no arquimedianos y de la recta hiperreal, así como conceptos relacionados con infinitesimales, diferenciales, convergencia, continuidad y topología\. Desde esta perspectiva se analiza la posibilidad de formular y enseñar el cálculo utilizando infinitesimales rigurosamente definidos, recuperando aspectos esenciales del método leibniziano sin renunciar a las exigencias del rigor matemático moderno\. El libro aborda asimismo las controversias históricas y filosóficas que han acompañado a los infinitesimales desde los orígenes del cálculo hasta la matemática contemporánea, prestando especial atención a la oposición entre el infinito potencial y el infinito actual, a la aritmetización del análisis y al desarrollo de estructuras matemáticas que extienden el continuo de los números reales\. Finalmente, la obra plantea que estas cuestiones adquieren una nueva relevancia en el contexto de la inteligencia artificial\. Se propone investigar una matemática del cálculo capaz de operar más allá del continuo real tradicional, explorando estructuras discretas e infinitesimales y sus posibles relaciones con los nuevos modelos computacionales y con la enseñanza de las matemáticas en la era de la inteligencia artificial\. La partícula del diablo es, por tanto, una investigación histórica, matemática y pedagógica sobre la naturaleza del infinitesimal, su exclusión y posterior rehabilitación, y sobre la posibilidad de recuperar su papel como concepto fundacional del cálculo diferencial e integral\.

## [Watson, Jeffrey J\.: Against perceptual existentialism](../publications/bf7bdeeee958a5525350.md)



\_Philosophical Explorations\_\. forthcomingParticularism is the position that perceptual content is essentially singular, and all perceptual representations are as of particulars: I see that cat\. Existentialism is the position that all perceptual representations are as of general features, not particulars, which are satisfied when the world would satisfy the corresponding existentially quantified statement: I see there as being a cat\. H\. P\. Grice famously raised the problem that existential contents could fail to refer to the particulars which made them accurate, such as when a mirror is placed in front of an object that reflects a qualitatively identical object in a different location\. Christopher Hill and Mark Sainsbury have recently proposed refinements to existentialism that resolve Grice’s problem, by adding a causal condition for perceptual awareness of a particular\. In this article, I describe three counterexamples to this refined existentialism, from the wagon wheel effect, misperceptions of continuity, and misperceptions of seamless transition\. Particularism correctly judges these to be cases of hallucination as of a particular, whereas existentialism misjudges these cases to be accurate perceptions of a particular, since a cause of the perceptual experience satisfies the existential content\. \(direct link \)

## [Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations](../publications/bf802db3f5ab49a05639.md)

Xu Cao; Wenxuan Xiao

Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation\. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model\. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group\-wise gains and installs them in the recipient&\#x27;s weights or native quantization scales without recipient\-side optimization\. On a quantized recipient, it preserves integer codes, zero points and storage layout\. For a Qwen3\-1\.7B floating\-point/GPTQ INT3 pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76\.9\-90\.5% of the text\-loss improvement from recipient\-specific calibration on fresh WikiText and C4 cohorts excluded from project development\. Shuffling the same gain values within each projection worsens both recipients, showing that their learned group assignment matters after transfer\. A Llama\-3\.2\-3B control keeps the initial native tensors at all four calibrated projections identical and changes nine projections elsewhere\. Cross\-installation retains 98\.6\-99\.3% of the text\-calibration benefit, alongside a small, resolved preference for each recipient&\#x27;s own gain\. These results quantify both the adaptation carried by a reusable calibration update and the remaining benefit of recipient\-specific training\.
