## [Spastic Paraplegia Secondary to Spinal Metastasis in a Patient with Advanced\-Stage Breast Cancer: A Case Report](../publications/bf83f6f63a4cacfb22f1.md)

Fery Luvita Sari; Agus Taufiqurrohman

Introduction: Spinal metastasis in breast cancer patients can lead to severe pain, neurological deficits, and significant morbidity, impacting quality of life and chances of survival in breast cancer patients\. Case: A 48\-year\-old woman was referred to a neurologist because of lower extremity weakness\. Due to spinal cord compression, she had paraplegia with chronic progressive mixed\-type lower back pain, with radiating to the pelvis, accompanied by numbness, tingling, and burning from both feet to the subumbilical region, and impairment of defecation and urination\. She had a history of breast cancer with chemotherapy and radiotherapy\. Her numeric rating scale score was 7, ID pain score was 4, Karnofsky score was 40; neurological examination revealed spastic paraplegia, segmental hypoesthesia at and below the 11th spinal cord level, and urinary and bowel retention\. Radiologic examination showed kyphosis with osteolytic and osteosclerotic thoracic vertebrae\. Bone survey showed bone metastases in thoracic vertebral bodies 5–12, the right ilium, and the right proximal femur\. Discussion: The patient was diagnosed with spinal metastasis based on physical examination and supporting investigations, but further follow\-up was limited\. Early recognition of the clinical condition is expected to help prevent further deterioration of neurological deficits\. Conclusion: The patient was diagnosed with spinal metastasis from breast cancer and received analgesic and corticosteroid therapy\. The prognosis was poor\.

## [HardEval: An Execution\-Verified Benchmark for AI\-Driven Security Hardening and Compliance Remediation](../publications/bf916edeffc1f4ffe679.md)

Manohar Vellala; Soumya Banerjee; Sandip Roy; Ross Gore; Sachin Shetty

Implementing Security Technical Implementation Guide \(STIG\) controls remains a demanding operating\-system administration task\. Each natural\-language security requirement must be translated into a precise and persistent configuration change\. These changes span Secure Shell \(SSH\) configuration, authentication policy, audit rules, and kernel parameters\. Existing benchmarks do not measure whether a model can perform this task on a live system\. Code benchmarks evaluate isolated programs without persistent system state, while agent benchmarks largely focus on applications rather than operating\-system configuration\. In this paper, we introduce \\textbf\{HardEval\}, an execution\-verified benchmark for evaluating language\-model\-assisted security hardening\. HardEval is built from Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 STIG controls that fail on an unhardened baseline system\. Expert\-written reference remediations and Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language \(OVAL\) checks serve as hidden ground truth for grading; they are never shown to the model, and each task states only the required security outcome while withholding the implementation\. The model produces a Bash script, which is executed on a live virtual machine and graded from fail to pass using the corresponding OpenSCAP/OVAL compliance check\. Evaluation of fourteen frontier and open\-weight configurations reveals large and uneven capability differences across security domains\. A recurring failure mode is plausible security code that does not satisfy the exact compliance condition\. For four open\-weight configurations, multi\-run Wilson confidence intervals preserve the observed ordering\. HardEval is publicly available\.

## [Die Aktlosigkeit der Künstlichen Intelligenz](../publications/bf98c78ce5456fa1cc29.md)

Christian Wiesner

Der Beitrag untersucht Künstliche Intelligenz in der Psychotherapie aus der Perspektive Brentanos und der Strukturphänomenologie\. Psychotherapie wird als leiblich\-affektiver, intentionaler und responsiver Sinnvollzug verstanden\. Vorstellung, Urteil und Gemütsbewegung werden als Momente psychischer Akte gefasst, die sich in primärer Gerichtetheit und sekundärem Mitbewusstsein vollziehen\. Sprachmodelle vollziehen solche Akte nicht, sondern verarbeiten Tokens, Zahlenvektoren und Wahrscheinlichkeiten\. Diese Grenze wird an innerer Rede, visuellem Denken und der Differenz von Sinn und Bedeutung entfaltet\. Künstliche Intelligenz kann Bedeutungen ordnen, transkodieren und therapeutische Sprache simulieren, aber keine leiblich\-affektive Sinnumbildung oder therapeutische Beziehung tragen\.

## [EVALUASI EFEKTIVITAS INTERVENSI MOTIVASI BERPRESTASI BERBASIS ANALOGI GAME RPG DAN DESAIN VISUAL GAYA TEDx MENGGUNAKAN MODEL KIRKPATRICK PADA MAHASISWA BARU UNESA 5 MAGETAN: Bahasa indonesia](../publications/bfa569295e863d514d4e.md)

Khairunnisa Nur Fadhilah; Rusijono Rusijono

AbstrakPenelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi efektivitas intervensi motivasi berprestasi berbasis analogi game RPG dan desain visual gaya TEDx dalam memitigasi academic culture shock pada mahasiswa baru UNESA 5 Magetan\. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain post\-only dalam kerangka New World Kirkpatrick Model pada Level 1 \(Reaction\) dan Level 3 \(Behavior\)\. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 62 mahasiswa baru yang ditetapkan melalui total sampling\. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket skala Likert lima pilihan yang telah dinyatakan valid dan reliabel, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan uji One\-Sample t\-Test dengan Test Value = 18\. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan skor rata\-rata Level 1 sebesar 24,6290 \(indeks 4,10; kategori Sangat Puas\) dengan t\(61\) = 12,749 dan p = 0,000\. Skor rata\-rata Level 3, yang diukur setelah jeda retensi perkuliahan aktif selama empat minggu, mencapai 24,2097 \(indeks 4,03; kategori Sangat Tinggi\) dengan t\(61\) = 12,050 dan p = 0,000\. Dengan demikian, dapat disimpulkan bahwa intervensi ini efektif memperoleh penerimaan peserta sekaligus mempertahankan perilaku berprestasi mahasiswa baru tanpa penurunan antusiasme yang tajam\.Kata kunci: Intervensi motivasi berprestasi, gamifikasi RPG, desain visual TEDx, model evaluasi Kirkpatrick, academic culture shock, mahasiswa baru\.

## [Interactive effect of ESG performance on the earnings management, tax avoidance and financial performance relation: A bibliometric and empirical analysis](../publications/bfb8fe88d3de0bfa60db.md)

Hussein Mousa Ahmad Maabreh; Mara Ridhuan Che Abdul Rahman; Ainul Huda Jamil

This paper provides a bibliometric and analytical assessment of the salient works examining earnings management, tax avoidance, financial performance, and environmental, social, and governance \(ESG\) adoption\. The research is based on data obtained from the Scopus database between 2016–2026; VOSviewer was used to analyze trends in research, as well as co\-occurrence of keywords, citation patterns, and collaborations among countries\. The results indicate that previous research is quite focused on the study of earnings management related to financial performance, where few studies link tax avoidance with ESG performance \(Friede et al\., 2015; Kolsi et al\., 2023\)\. The results also suggest that while ESG performance has received increased attention in recent years as a predictor of financial performance/future cash flows or opportunistic behavior, its link to traditional accounting research streams appears weak\. Although a substantial body of research has examined earnings management, tax avoidance, financial, and ESG performance, their integrated relationships remain underexplored\. This study addresses this gap by developing a unified framework that examines ESG performance as a moderator of the relationships among the other three variables\. The conclusions of this study can provide theoretical and practical support for academic circles, enterprises, investors, regulators, and other relevant stakeholders\.

## [Subspace Accelerated Measure Transport Methods for Fast and Scalable Sequential Experimental Design, with Application to Photoacoustic Imaging](../publications/bfbd3ebb45a1820b6fb2.md)

Tiangang Cui; Karina Koval; Roland Herzog; Robert Scheichl

Abstract\. We propose a novel approach for sequential optimal experimental design \(sOED\) for Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive models with high\-dimensional unknown parameters\. This work focuses on designs that maximize the expected information gain \(EIG\) from prior to posterior, a task that is computationally very challenging in non\-Gaussian settings\. This challenge is amplified in sOED, as the incremental EIG \(iEIG\) must be repeatedly approximated across distinct stages, with both prior and posterior distributions being intractable\. To address this, we derive a general\-purpose, derivative\-based upper bound for the iEIG, which not only guides design placement but also enables the construction of projectors onto likelihood\-informed subspaces, facilitating parameter dimension reduction\. By combining this approach with conditional measure transport maps for the sequence of posteriors, we develop a unified sOED and amortized inference framework scalable to high\- and infinite\-dimensional problems\. Numerical experiments for two inverse problems governed by PDEs demonstrate the effectiveness of designs by maximizing the proposed bound\.

## [Effects of water saturation and impact load on the mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete](../publications/bfee33b49a5cd6958247.md)

Zhihang Wang; Dexian Zhao; Chaojia Liu; Chao Zhang; Mengyang Li; Erlei Bai

Abstract In terms of quality test, ultrasonic wave velocity test, static mechanical test and dynamic compression test, the physical and static mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete after water immersion for 180 d were studied, and the effects of water saturation and impact load on the mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete were analyzed\. The results show that the geopolymer concrete reaches the water saturated state after water immersion for 180 d, and the ultrasonic wave velocity of geopolymer increases after water saturation, while the compressive strength, splitting tensile strength and flexural strength decrease\. Water saturation increases the strength and stiffness of geopolymer concrete under impact load, while reducing its deformation capacity, with no significant effect on its energy consumption characteristics\. The dynamic compressive strength and dynamic elastic modulus of geopolymer concrete increase after water saturation, the dynamic peak strain and pre\-peak toughness decrease, and the impact toughness exhibits no significant alteration\. The dynamic compressive strength of geopolymer concrete after water saturation increases by 8\.61%\~19\.01%, the dynamic elastic modulus shows an average increase of 52\.20%, the dynamic peak strain shows a maximum reduction of 28\.88%, and the pre\-peak toughness decreases by 14\.07%\~43\.26%\. The dynamic increase factor \(DIF\) of geopolymer concrete increases significantly after water saturation, and the fractal dimension of fragments decreases\. The Comité Euro\-International du Béton \(CEB\) model can well predict the DIF of geopolymer concrete in dry state, but significantly underestimate the DIF value of geopolymer concrete in water saturated state\. Based on the test results, a DIF fitting formula for geopolymer concrete in water saturated state is proposed\.

## [Multimodal prediction of infliximab initiation within 6 months after initiation of conventional therapy in pediatric Crohn&\#x27;s disease: A multicenter algorithm development and validation study](../publications/bffde3eaff5b8ead18dc.md)

Seon Young Kim; Seung Ha Hwang; Dongjin Yeo; Juyeong Kim; Gyeom Hwangbo; Do Hyun Kim; Yoo Min Lee; Selin Woo; Jong Woo Hahn; Dong Keon Yon

OBJECTIVES: Early prediction of treatment course in pediatric Crohn&\#x27;s disease \(CD\) remains limited despite the importance of timely biologic therapy\. We developed and externally validated a multimodal model integrating colonoscopy images and clinical data to predict infliximab initiation within 6 months after conventional therapy\. METHODS: We collected data from children newly diagnosed with CD at three hospitals: Seoul National University Bundang Hospital for internal validation, Kyung Hee University Medical Center, and Soonchunhyang University Bucheon Hospital for external validation\. Each patient contributed 7 endoscopic images and 20 clinical variables\. An attention\-based multiple\-instance learning framework aggregated endoscopic images into a patient\-level representation and integrated them with clinical features\. The imaging encoder used a ResNet\-50 backbone pretrained with momentum contrastive learning on GastroNet\-5M, and clinical features were encoded using a multilayer perceptron\. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve \(AUROC\), balanced accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score\. Explainable AI was evaluated using attention maps \(image data\) and SHAP values \(tabular data\)\. RESULTS: Seventy\-seven children were included for model development and internal validation, with external validation performed in two independent cohorts \(n = 10 and n = 20\)\. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0\.839 and balanced accuracy of 0\.732 in the discovery cohort\. External\-validation AUROCs were 0\.857 and 0\.688\. SHapley Additive exPlanation analysis identified immunoglobulin G, body mass index, prealbumin, hematocrit, and age as key predictors\. Attention maps highlighted inflamed mucosa and ulcerative lesions\. CONCLUSION: A multimodal model integrating colonoscopy images with clinical data showed promising performance for predicting infliximab initiation within 6 months after conventional therapy in pediatric CD\. Multimodal information may support early risk stratification and identify patients who could benefit from earlier biologic intervention\.

## [Blinded professional ratings of artificial intelligence–generated and dietitian\-designed meal plans](../publications/c00220b08db13c6ff0dc.md)

Ellis Wollis Malta Abhulime; Diogo Thimóteo da Cunha; Vicente Monaco; Rafael de Melo; Fabiana Braga Benatti

OBJECTIVES: Artificial intelligence\-assisted systems increasingly produce personalized meal plans, but their value depends on whether clinicians judge those plans credible and usable\. We evaluated complete plans from a constrained artificial intelligence\-assisted pipeline under blinded professional review\. METHODS: In a cross\-sectional exploratory web study, 54 eligible anonymous evaluator records from Brazilian dietitians contributed 130 evaluations of five matched plan pairs, with one pipeline\-generated and one dietitian\-designed plan per persona\. Evaluators rated nine items across three domains and were offered an optional pairwise plan preference task\. The overall score required all nine items and was available for 124 evaluations\. RESULTS: Pipeline\-generated plans received a mean rating of 3\.67 \(standard deviation, 0\.57\) \(n = 59\) compared with 3\.11 \(standard deviation, 0\.73\) for comparator plans \(n = 65\) \(d = 0\.86\)\. Among 38 evaluator records with complete scores for both origins, 31 favored pipeline\-generated plans, 6 favored dietitian\-designed plans, and 1 had equal mean scores for both origins \(paired t\[37\] = 5\.32, P &lt; 0\.001\)\. Pipeline\-generated plans received higher ratings in all five persona pairs\. This pattern was descriptive because evaluator records overlapped across pairs\. Domain differences were \+0\.76 for nutritional adequacy, \+0\.69 for technical quality, and \+0\.21 for practical applicability\. In the optional task, 32 of 42 eligible pairwise choices selected the pipeline\-generated plan as more appropriate\. CONCLUSIONS: Under blinded presentation, practicing dietitians gave plans from the constrained pipeline a mean rating above the neutral anchor of the 5\-point scale\. These findings support prospective evaluation of a structured first draft workflow, with required clinician edits and patient\-relevant outcomes as endpoints\.

## [Provably Efficient Risk\-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents](../publications/c01183aca840aabab1fa.md)

Hanzhen Wang; Boxiang Lyu; Zhongxiang Dai; Siyang Gao; Dake Zhang; Shuang Qiu

Risk\-sensitive reinforcement learning \(RL\) addresses decision\-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes\. Learning risk\-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly\. Existing work on risk\-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped\. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk\-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent \(OCE\), a general class of risk measures\. We consider two formulations: dynamic\-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static\-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards\. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value\-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty\. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem&\#x27;s fundamental limits\. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least\-squares value\-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation\. We establish utility\-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$\. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic\- and static\-OCE RL\.

## [Ambient Artificial Intelligent Scribes in Oncology: Impact on Clinician Experience and Documentation Burden](../publications/c01208c58b344e4590fa.md)

Abigail Baldwin\-Medsker; Susan C\. Chimonas; Suryan P\. Goyal; Adam J\. R\. Watson; Fariha Ahsan; Gilad J\. Kuperman; Kenneth P\. Seier; Cardinale B\. Smith; Christina Ward; Gianna Zucotti; Allison Lipitz‐Snyderman

PURPOSE Ambient artificial intelligence \(AI\) scribes, widely implemented to reduce clinician burden and dissatisfaction, are not optimized for oncology\. We evaluated this technology at\-scale at a high\-volume cancer center\. METHODS This prospective mixed\-methods study used surveys, electronic health record \(EHR\), and utilization data to assess adoption, burden, and satisfaction with an ambient AI scribe that was implemented from June to September 2025\. Descriptive statistics categorized clinicians as adopters \(3\+ weeks of use\), attempted adopters \(1\-2 weeks\), and never\-users \(0 weeks\)\. Generalized estimating equations assessed the adoption&\#x27;s effect on the likelihood of closing notes on visit days and pajama time\. Pre\- and postimplementation surveys obtained clinicians&\#x27; insights into satisfaction and documentation burden\. RESULTS In all, 190 \(19\.8%\) of 958 clinicians used the tool, most often with new, video, and in\-person visits\. Adopters \(n = 124\) and attempted adopters \(n = 66\) were more commonly physicians from medicine and surgery\. Pre\- to post\-rollout, the likelihood of closing notes on visit days remained unchanged among never\-users \(70% v 70%\) and decreased among attempted adopters \(73% v 70%\) and adopters \(56% v 54%\)\. Pajama time remained unchanged among attempted adopters \(50\.6 v 50\.1 minutes per week\) and decreased among never\-users \(69\.5 v 62\.2\) and adopters \(86\.9 v 81\.4\)\. Clinicians completing both pre\- and postrollout surveys \(n = 45\) showed a decrease in high/excessive note\-writing time \(78% v 60%; P = \.043\)\. Postrollout surveys \(n = 77\) showed largely positive experiences, with 73% reporting they would recommend the tool to colleagues\. CONCLUSION This study of an ambient AI scribe at\-scale showed positive satisfaction but mixed burden outcomes among oncology clinicians\. Notably, despite enterprise\-wide implementation and training, adoption was low and varied by clinician and visit characteristics\. Future research should explore adoption barriers and tool optimization to support oncology documentation workflows\.

## [Neonatal Conjunctivitis with Gram\-Negative Diplococci Suggestive of Neisseria gonorrhoeae: A Case Report](../publications/c018e9039f0aff73f603.md)

Felicia Felicia; Ni Made Dwipayani; I Made Dwi Surya Wibawa; Putu Anindya Agrasidi; Komang Diah Kurnia Kesumaputri

Introduction: Gonococcal conjunctivitis in a neonate is a conjunctival infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae\. Transmission commonly occurs during vaginal delivery from an infected mother\. This serious infection can threaten vision if not promptly and properly treated\. Case: A 14\-day\-old female infant was brought to the ophthalmology clinic by her parents with a complaint of bilateral eye discharge that had been present since she was 2 days old\. The discharge was yellow, thick, and sticky\. Ocular examination revealed edema and erythema of the upper eyelids with profuse purulent discharge\. The tarsal conjunctiva was hyperemic with positive conjunctival vessel injection \(CVI\) and membrane formation\. Mild corneal edema was observed\. The direct pupillary light reflex was present\. Gram staining of conjunctival swab specimens obtained from both eyes demonstrated Gram\-negative diplococci\. The patient was presumptively diagnosed with gonococcal conjunctivitis based on the clinical findings and Gram staining demonstrating Gram\-negative diplococci\. Treatment included eye toilet with sterile cotton buds, a single intravenous dose of ceftriaxone 25 mg/kg body weight, 0\.3% ofloxacin eye drops administered six times daily to both eyes, and artificial tears administered six times daily to both eyes\. Discussion: The clinical findings and Gram\-stain results support a presumptive diagnosis of gonococcal conjunctivitis, an infection characterized by rapid progression and a high risk of corneal complications\. Management with a single dose of ceftriaxone plus topical therapy led to rapid clinical improvement\. Conclusion: Prompt diagnosis and treatment of neonatal gonococcal conjunctivitis with systemic and intensive topical antibiotic therapy resulted in a favorable clinical outcome and helped prevent serious ocular complications\.

## [Contemporary Islamic Thought In Indonesia: Opportunities, Challenges, And Future Directions](../publications/c01b22365253b71445fb.md)

Ayub Rohadi; Inayatulloh Abd Hasyim

Indonesia, as the nation with the world&\#x27;s largest Muslim population, has emerged as a significant arena for the development of contemporary Islamic thought\. Over recent decades, Indonesian Muslim intellectuals, educational institutions, and Islamic organizations have actively sought to reconcile Islamic teachings with democratic governance, religious pluralism, human rights frameworks, and the multifaceted challenges of globalization\. This article examines the evolution of contemporary Islamic thought in Indonesia by critically exploring the opportunities it presents for social transformation alongside the threats that potentially undermine its development\. Employing a qualitative approach grounded in library research and critical content analysis, this study draws upon scholarly books, peer\-reviewed journal articles, policy documents, and relevant historical sources to analyze major intellectual trends and contemporary debates\. The findings indicate that contemporary Islamic thought in Indonesia has contributed significantly to the promotion of religious moderation, democratic participation, educational reform, interfaith dialogue, and peaceful coexistence\. These developments have been supported by influential Muslim scholars and major Islamic organizations advocating contextual and inclusive understandings of Islam\. Concurrently, the study identifies several formidable challenges, including religious extremism, identity politics, digital misinformation, ideological polarization, and the growing influence of transnational religious movements\. These factors have created new tensions affecting the intellectual and social landscape of Indonesian Islam\. The article argues that the future of contemporary Islamic thought in Indonesia depends upon strengthening critical scholarship, revitalizing Islamic education, promoting digital literacy, and reinforcing the values of moderation, justice, and tolerance\. As a model of democratic and pluralistic Islam, Indonesia possesses significant potential to contribute meaningfully to contemporary Islamic discourse at both regional and global levels\.

## [Ginsenosides in hematopoietic homeostasis and hematological malignancies: context\-dependent pharmacological effects and translational limitations](../publications/c01cb37542b64260e50f.md)

Jinyu Gai; Bei Zhang; Xinyi Wan; Xiaoling Yu

Ginseng has long been used as a botanical drug in East Asian traditional medical systems, particularly in China and Korea, and as a food ingredient\. Ginsenosides are specialized metabolites of Panax species with diverse pharmacological activities reported in experimental studies\. Evidence regarding their effects in hematological contexts, however, is dispersed across studies using different materials, models, and exposure conditions\. This Mini Review synthesizes findings from purified ginsenosides and chemically characterized saponin fractions, focusing on hematopoietic and immune regulation in non\-malignant stress models and on malignant hematopoietic cell fate\. In non\-malignant models, selected metabolites and fractions were associated with reduced cellular injury and changes in peripheral blood, phenotypic, or colony\-forming endpoints\. In malignant models, effects on proliferation, apoptosis, differentiation, autophagy, and drug transport were reported mainly in cell lines\. Clinical evidence remains limited, while gaps in material standardization and pharmacologically relevant exposure constrain translation\. By comparing non\-malignant and malignant contexts, this review provides an integrated framework for interpreting heterogeneous findings and highlights how metabolite identity, experimental model, cellular context, and exposure may influence the reported effects\.

## [CONCEPTUALIZATION OF MULTIPLICITY IN ENGLISH AND AZERBAIJANI: A COGNITIVE\-DISCURSIVE ANALYSIS](../publications/c02349249981f9c4bb71.md)

Sevinj Mahmudova

Multiplicity is commonly associated with the grammatical contrast between singular and plural forms\. However, linguis\- tic expressions of multiplicity extend far beyond morphological number marking\. Speakers may construe a collection as a set of separate individuals, a unified group, an indefinite quantity, a distributive configuration, or a culturally salient social category\. The present article examines how multiplicity is conceptualized and discursively represented in English and Azerbaijani\. The study adopts a qualitative comparative approach combining insights from cognitive linguistics, discourse analysis, and contemporary research on plural semantics\. The analysis focuses on nominal plural markers, collective nouns, numerals, quantifiers, bare nouns, pronouns, agreement patterns, and context\-dependent interpretations\. English generally marks nominal plurality through the suffix \-s/\-es, although irregular forms, zero plurals, collective nouns, and mass\-count shifts contribute to a more complex system\. Azerbaijani mainly employs the suffixes \-lar/\-lər, selected accord\- ing to vowel harmony, yet plural meaning may remain morphologically unmarked after numerals and certain quantitative expressions\. The comparison demonstrates that morphological form alone does not determine plural interpretation\. In both languages, discourse context activates collective, distributive, generic, associative, and approximative readings\. Never\- theless, the two languages differ in how explicitly number is encoded\. English usually requires plural marking after numer\- als and reflects number distinctions in agreement, whereas Azerbaijani generally uses a morphologically singular noun following a cardinal numeral\. Azerbaijani plural morphology also develops pragmatic meanings such as respect, family association, approximation, and social grouping\. The article argues that multiplicity should be treated as a flexible concep\- tual domain constructed through the interaction of grammar, lexical semantics, cognition, and discourse\. This approach provides a more comprehensive account than analyses that restrict plurality to a binary singular–plural opposition\.

## [Supporting the Adoption of Digital Technology On\-Farm: Ten Tips for Extension](../publications/c02c0706f5fc28576d59.md)

David Christian Rose; Kayleigh Crouch; Lisa Blix Germundsson; Myriam Gaspard; Onno Giller; Livia Ortolani; Robert Strong

We held a symposium to exchange lessons from U\.S\. and European experts on how Extension can be best designed to support adoption of digital agricultural innovation\. We highlight 10 tips for an Extension audience in the United States: \(a\) ensure connectivity between all actors involved in agricultural innovation, \(b\) utilize the private sector, \(c\) advocate for adoption costs, \(d\) shape an enabling digital ecosystem, \(e\) create a service, not just a technology, \(f\) update Extension agents&\#x27; digital skills, \(g\) support farmer\-led innovation, \(h\) capture everyday farmer practices, \(i\) monitor and evaluate progress, and \(j\) offer long\-term support\.

## [Competitive Intelligence in the Age of Digital Transformation: Challenges and Opportunities: A Nigerian Perspective](../publications/c02e343d20e2c7b04d51.md)

BLESSING OMOTOSHO ONI; YACOB HALISO

This study analyses the impact of digital tools such as Artificial Intelligence \(AI\) and Big Data on the activities of Nigerian companies\. This process is called Competitive Intelligence \(CI\)\. The study also finds that though these tools offer great opportunities, there is an “Intelligence Paradox” in Nigeria\. It indicates that firms have a lot of data at hand but tend to grapple with leveraging it into proper business advice\. This is largely caused by bad infrastructure like poor power supply and expensive internet, plus new privacy laws, including the Nigeria Data Protection Act \(NDPA\) 2023\. To tackle these problems, the research recommends low\-cost methods such as Open\-Source Intelligence \(OSINT\) the use of free, public information, while ensuring humans are in charge of machines’ work\. To succeed in business in Nigeria, Nigerian firms must develop their own &quot;Compliant Intelligence&quot; using smart technologies that are compliant with the law, the paper concludes\. Mixing global technology with local knowledge helps businesses stay ahead in a tough economy\.

## [FoxWatch: A User‐Friendly Tool for Estimating Fox Abundance From Camera Traps Using Simultaneous‐Count Models](../publications/c02f77ad2afa73bbb771.md)

Duminda S\. B\. Dissanayake; Graeme Armstrong

ABSTRACT The red fox \( Vulpes vulpes \) is a major invasive predator in Australia, and camera traps are increasingly used to monitor it and evaluate control programs\. These devices generate large datasets, but turning them into abundance estimates requires statistical and programming skills that many land managers lack\. Detection data are therefore often reduced to naïve counts that ignore detection probability\. We developed FoxWatch, a Shiny R application that estimates fox abundance with Simultaneous‐Count Models through a guided point‐and‐click interface\. It sorts detection records into 10‐day blocks and fits the model by Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling, returning abundance estimates with quantified uncertainty\. We tested FoxWatch on 5 years of data from 35 camera traps at Oolambeyan National Park, Australia\. It processed the dataset in under 5 minutes, versus 2–3 hours by hand\. FoxWatch lowers the analytical barrier so practitioners without programming skills can assess fox abundance and support predator management\.

## [Stimulation\-stability and preclinical bench testing of a new auditory nerve interface](../publications/c02fa0b2df0988c340b2.md)

Taylor Stump; Stefan Strahl; Joseph D\. Crew; Moritz Leber; Keno Hübner; Sandeep Negi; Justin Vankirk; Meredith E\. Adams; Thomas Lenarz; Florian Solzbacher; Hubert Lim; Loren W\. Rieth

OBJECTIVE: Cochlear implants are the flagship sensory neural prosthetic, enabling improved hearing and speech perception in &gt;1 million patients with hearing loss\. Despite over three decades of active work and innovations in cochlear implants, hearing performance for complex tasks such as speech\-in\-noise and music appreciation are still quite limited, putatively due to the challenge of selectively stimulating the auditory nerve with intracochlear electrodes through the bony cochlear wall\. Our approach is to more selectively evoke hearing percepts through the development of an Auditory Nerve Implant \(ANI\) device that uses penetrating microelectrodes placed directly in the nerve for stimulation, and which will be evaluated through psychophysical testing as part of a first\-in\-human study\. Stability and integrity of ANI electrodes during passive soaking and stimulation are needed to support initiation of the clinical trial, which we evaluated through thermal accelerated saline soak testing and stimulation stability testing\. METHODS: The ANI electrode stability in saline was assessed by accelerated aging at ≥ 67 \[Formula: see text\]C with a 1\.5\-year equivalent endpoint using electrode impedance and microscopy to characterize outcomes\. Stimulation stability testing evaluated electrode integrity after 6\.3 billion pulses at 100 μA, which is the maximum clinical stimulation intensity, for a one\-year equivalent use, and 1200 μA, for a high\-dose protocol\. Electrode impedance, longitudinal stimulation voltage, and microscopy outcomes were used to the quantify results\. RESULTS: All electrodes had stable impedances around 2 kΩ at the end of the accelerated soak test, except for three with higher impedances but still below the 70 kΩ failure criteria\. All but one electrode survived stimulation stability testing\. Optical and electron microscopy largely showed little to no change during testing, indicating no observable tip degradation, with the exception of one soak\-test device\. CONCLUSIONS: The outcomes from the studies indicate that ANI electrodes exhibit a high degree of integrity and impedance stability\. Microscopy characterization proved effective for evaluating electrodes, providing complementary information to standard Backscattered Scanning Electron Microscopy \(BSEM\)\. This study suggests the ANI device tolerate a 1\.5 year in\-dwelling period for a 1 year perceptual study of stimulation evoked percepts, paving the way for clinical translation\.

## [Zero\-Shot Cross\-Modality Dose Prediction in Particle Therapy via Physics\-Informed Ensembles](../publications/c04459281ade5d9ba829.md)

Muhammed Emin Bedir

Purpose: Deep learning can accelerate radiotherapy dose prediction, but particle\-therapy datasets remain scarce\. We evaluated whether a physics\-informed ensemble trained exclusively on photon plans could predict proton and carbon\-ion dose distributions without particle\-dose training\.Methods: Using matRad, 90 reference plans \(photons, protons and carbon ions\) were generated for five anatomies and six beam configurations\. A 13\-channel tensor combining CT, structure masks and modality\-specific ray\-tracing/depth\-dose channels was input to SOTA\-UNet3D, Res\-UNet3D and Trans\-UNet3D; their voxel\-wise mean formed the Voltron ensemble\. Leave\-one\-anatomy\-out evaluation used four test anatomies with photon\-only training\. Performance was assessed with PyMedPhys gamma analysis \(3%/3 mm and 2%/2 mm; 10% low\-dose threshold\) and mean absolute error \(MAE\)\.Results: Across four held\-out anatomies, mean 3%/3 mm gamma pass rates were 23\.5% for photons, 23\.3% for protons and 21\.5% for carbon ions; 2%/2 mm rates were 15\.8%, 15\.5% and 14\.5%\. Mean MAE was approximately 5\.2–5\.3 Gy\. Gamma values reported in an earlier version of this work \(73\.2/70\.8/69\.1%\) were computed with a non\-standard lenient criterion; all values reported here use the standard gamma index\.Conclusion: Photon\-only training with physics\-informed inputs provides a reproducible feasibility baseline for zeroshot particle\-dose prediction\. Performance is not clinical\-grade, but the small cross\-modality degradation suggests that anatomical and geometric features learned from photon data can transfer to particle therapy\.

## [Catheter\-Associated Urinary Tract Infections: Epidemiology, Biofilm Pathogenesis, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Prevention Strategies—A Comprehensive Review](../publications/c04966b803589bcf86ca.md)



Catheter\-associated urinary tract infection \(CAUTI\) remains one of the most common healthcare\-associated infections worldwide and represents a significant burden on patient outcomes and healthcare systems\.The widespread use of indwelling urinary catheters, particularly in critically ill and long\-term hospitalized patients, contributes substantially to infection risk\.This review summarizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathogenesis, antimicrobial resistance patterns, diagnostic approaches, treatment challenges, and prevention strategies related to CAUTI\.Special emphasis is placed on the role of biofilm formation on catheter surfaces, which facilitates microbial persistence, reduces antibiotic efficacy, and promotes the emergence of multidrug\-resistant organisms\.Common pathogens include Gram\-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, many of which exhibit extended\-spectrum β\-lactamase and carbapenem resistance\.Accurate diagnosis requires correlation of clinical features with quantitative urine culture to distinguish true infection from asymptomatic bacteriuria and avoid unnecessary antimicrobial therapy\.Preventive strategies\-including appropriate catheter use, aseptic insertion techniques, early catheter removal, and antimicrobial stewardship\-remain the most effective methods for reducing CAUTI incidence\.Emerging therapeutic and preventive approaches such as antimicrobial\-coated catheters, anti\-biofilm strategies, bacteriophage therapy, and rapid molecular diagnostics are also discussed\.Strengthening infection control practices and surveillance systems is essential to limit the growing impact of antimicrobial resistance\.This review highlights current challenges and future directions for improved management and prevention of CAUTI in clinical settings\.

## [Integrating Proximal and Remote Sensing to Improve Characterization and Mapping of Soil Organic Carbon Stocks under Contrasting Land Uses](../publications/c050cf4621e1c830ec15.md)

Leonardo Augusto de Sousa; Fernanda Almeida Bócoli; Eduane José de Pádua; Luiza Maria Pereira Pierangeli; Junior César Avanzi; Bruno Montoani Silva; Carlos Victor Lima Albuquerque; Luiz Roberto Guimarães Guilherme; Marco Aurélio Carbone Carneiro; Nilton Curi; Sérgio Henrique Godinho Silva

Abstract Soils are fundamental to support ecosystem functions\. Therefore, understanding soil organic carbon stock \(SCS\) as a strategic environmental component for climate regulation, sustainable agricultural practices, and maximizing fertilizer application is essential\. This study aimed to predict and map the SCS at Palmital Farm, Minas Gerais state, using land use, parent materials, soil classes, proximal and remote sensing data as predictor variables\. A total of 76 soil samples were collected in the surface \(A\) and subsurface \(B\) horizons using a regular grid design \(200 × 200 m\)\. Carbon content was determined using the Walkley–Black method\. Prediction models were created via Random Forest algorithm and validated through leave\-one\-out cross\-validation\. Environmental and anthropogenic influences on SCS were analyzed statistically and spatially\. The highest mean SCS values were found at the surface horizon under native vegetation and pasture areas \(\~ 33 Mg ha⁻¹\), due to continuous organic matter deposition and lack of disturbance\. Charnockite\-derived soils showed higher SCS \(31\.24 Mg ha⁻¹, surface\)\. Among soil classes, Argissolos stood out reaching the highest SCS \(35\.86 Mg ha⁻¹\)\. Remote sensing data and terrain attributes yielded the best SCS prediction \(R²=0\.43\)\. The main factors influencing SCS were land use/management and soil texture\. Also, strong correlations were observed between vegetation indices, some terrain attributes and SCS\. This approach, combining multiple variables, indicated a moderate potential to achieve accurate SCS predictions using these data, demonstrating the high variability and complexity of SCS spatial variation in detailed\-scale mapping\.

## [AI‐Supported Research‐Led Teaching in Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning: Educator Questioning, Feedback, and Student Learning Outcomes in Authentic Industry Projects](../publications/c051bec32e0ea059ac78.md)

Phi Dinh Khuong; Duong Lam Thuy

ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence \(AI\) is creating new possibilities for connecting research‐led teaching with authentic industry projects, yet its educational value depends on how educators organize inquiry rather than on technological use alone\. This study examined the relationships among AI‐supported research‐led teaching \(AIRLT\), educator questioning \(EQ\), educator feedback \(EF\), student inquiry engagement \(SIE\), and authentic project learning outcomes \(APLO\) within Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning\. A quantitative cross‐sectional survey was conducted with 898 undergraduate students from 12 universities in Vietnam who had participated in authentic industry or organizational projects involving AI‐supported inquiry and educator guidance\. Partial least squares structural equation modeling \(PLS‐SEM\) showed that AIRLT was positively associated with EQ \( β = 0\.642\) and EF \( β = 0\.611\)\. Both EQ \( β = 0\.463\) and EF \( β = 0\.349\) were positively associated with SIE, which, in turn, showed a strong positive association with APLO \( β = 0\.689\)\. All six specific indirect effects were significant, indicating statistically significant indirect associations among AI‐supported teaching, educator guidance, student inquiry, and perceived authentic learning outcomes\. The findings contribute an educator‐mediated perspective to Syntegrative Education by showing that AI is most educationally meaningful when embedded in purposeful questioning, feedback, and sustained student inquiry\. The study highlights the importance of designing AI‐supported industry projects around evidence evaluation, iterative feedback, reflection, and active investigation of authentic problems rather than treating AI use as an educational objective in itself\.

## [A microexon regulatory code reveals autism\-linked genetic variation](../publications/c0527c1e0eeb664a19b7.md)

Guillermo E\. Parada; Hannes Bretschneider; Jack Daiyang Li; Jacob L\. Fine; Steven J\. Dupas; Jonathan D\. Ellis; Ulrich Braunschweig; Sophie Bonnal; Taykhoom Dalal; Worrawat Engchuan; Mehdi Zarrei; Wei Wei; Nadia Zafar; Martin Hemberg; Liliana Attisano; James Ellis; Manuel Irimia; Michael Wainberg; Brett Trost; Stephen W\. Scherer; Quaid Morris; Benjamin J\. Blencowe

Abstract Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology 1,2 \. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism\-like phenotypes 1,3,4 \. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated\. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype\-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense\-mediated mRNA decay\. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire\. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact\. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status\. They also converge on synaptic and other autism\-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism\. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders\.

Anthony Abou Mrad; Jayanth S\. Pratap; Aviona Conti; William Azar; Paola Vargas; Natalie Moreno; Joseph Cheaib; Mansour Riachi; Lisa Marie Knowlton; David P\. W\. Rastall; Gabriel A\. Brat; Melissa S\. Camp; Lilah F\. Morris; Anne Ehlers; Dana Alexa Telem; Peter Najjar; Andrew MacGregor Cameron; Jeffrey K\. Jopling

Informed consent is delivered inconsistently, and the comprehension it should produce is often poor\. We built ConsentAI, a conversational educational adjunct that guides patients through a surgeon\-authored consent form and gates progression on demonstrated understanding\. Before any patient\-facing trial, we asked how such an agent can be evaluated at scale, and which methods can be trusted\. Eight clinicians scored 50 simulated laparoscopic cholecystectomy sessions on a 10\-item rubric\. We tested four LLM judge architectures against this clinician reference under a pre\-specified, imbalance\-robust plan\. No single judge reproduced clinicians’ failure calls\. Only jury aggregation improved sensitivity \(0\.421; 95% CI, 0\.26–0\.61\), and no architecture reached a usable triage point\. A constant pass\-everything labeler topped raw agreement and AC1 yet scored zero on Matthews correlation and Cohen’s kappa\. Evaluating clinical conversational agents therefore requires multiple clinician ratings and imbalance\-robust metrics, treating clinician adjudication as a measurement layer, not ground truth\.

## [Long\-term dynamics and future trajectories of natural gas production: a global, regional, and Iranian assessment](../publications/c05cc0713ce24b8d909d.md)

Afshin Gholamalipour; Mohammadali Allahrabbi Shirazi; Hossein Yousefi

Natural gas plays an important role in sustainable energy supply and future planning\. This study examines trends in global natural gas production, Asia, the Middle East, and Iran, and outlines its outlook using several analytical methods\. Annual data for the period 1970\-2025 were examined using trend analysis and time series forecasting methods\. The significance of trends was determined using the Mann–Kendall test, and the rate of change was determined using Sen’s slope estimator\. Then, an ARIMA model was developed to forecast production up to 2035, and its accuracy was evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and MAPE criteria\. The results showed that production increased in all four ranges and was statistically significant \(p &lt; 0\.001\)\. The Z\-statistic values ​​were between 9\.69 and 10\.83\. Sen’s slope estimates showed annual increases in production in the world, Asia, the Middle East, and Iran of 594\.60, 295\.04, 145\.48, and 50\.39 TWh/year, respectively\. The ARIMA forecast also indicated that this increase would continue until 2035\. Global production would increase from 41,964\.71 TWh in 2025 to about 48,159\.54 TWh\. Production in Asia, the Middle East, and Iran in 2035 was also predicted to be about 18,096\.72, 9,348\.25, and 3,305\.26 TWh, respectively\. MAPE values below 10% indicate the model&\#x27;s accuracy in representing historical production behavior\. By examining trend significance, estimating growth rates, and forecasting, we can better understand long\-term changes in natural gas production\.

## [Effect of the CP@clinic program \(Community Paramedicine at Clinic program\) on health care utilization from administrative data during and after the intervention: a cluster\-randomized controlled trial](../publications/c0615c1aa70df48edf08.md)

Gina Agarwal; Melissa Pirrie; Manasvi Sai Vanama; Zheng Jing Hu; John Michael Paterson; Lehana Thabane; Ricardo N\. Angeles; Francine Marzanek

Introduction The study objective was to compare the effects of the Community Paramedicine at Clinic \(CP@clinic\) program versus usual care on building\-level health service utilization during a 12\-month trial period and 12 months post\-trial\. Methods This study employed a longitudinal, repeated cross\-sectional design within a cluster\-randomized controlled trial \(RCT\)\. It involved 30 apartment buildings across five Ontario communities, housing low\-income older adults\. Buildings were paired and randomized to receive either the CP@clinic intervention or continuing with usual care\. Data was derived from ICES\-maintained administrative health databases, linked using unique identifiers\. The sample included all residents aged 55 \+ in the study postal codes from the Ontario Health Insurance Plan \(OHIP\) Registered Persons Database \(RPDB\), excluding those aged 120\+, ineligible for OHIP, and those with no health care encounters within 7 years\. The primary health care utilization outcome was emergency department visits by ambulance and other outcomes included hospital admissions and primary care visits\. Results CP@clinic buildings showed significantly lower hospital admission rates during both the 12\-month RCT period \(adjusted incidence rate ratio \[aIRR\]: 0\.75 \[0\.61,0\.91\]\) and the 12\-month post\-RCT period \[aIRR: 0\.82 \(0\.70,0\.96\)\] compared to usual care buildings\. Primary care visits were lower in CP@clinic buildings during the RCT \(aIRR: 0\.93 \[0\.88,0\.99\]\) but higher in the post\-RCT period \(aIRR: 1\.05 \[1\.00,1\.10\]\)\. No significant differences were found in emergency department visits or the number of days admitted between groups in either period\. Discussion CP@clinic was linked to a sustained reduction in hospital admissions and an increase in primary care visits beyond the RCT time period, reflecting a shift from reactive to preventive care among older adults residing in social housing\. The lasting impact beyond the RCT period suggests that the CP@clinic Program can improve health system efficiency, primary care access, and reduce health inequities in vulnerable populations\. Trial registration ClinicalTrials\.gov, Identifier: NCT02152891

## [An Information\-theoretic framework for the peloric Lcyc epiallele in Linaria vulgaris: a synthetic demonstration](../publications/c064d8e0b2820dabb3a5.md)

Ildefonso M\. De la Fuente; Jose Carrasco\-Pujante; Leire Legarreta; Iker Malaina; Gorka Pérez‐Yarza; Luis Martínez; Jesús M\. Cortés; José I\. López

Introduction The peloric form of Linaria vulgaris , first described by Linnaeus in the eighteenth century, is a classical example of heritable epigenetic variation associated with a major change in floral morphology\. Wild\-type flowers exhibit bilateral symmetry, whereas peloric flowers exhibit radial symmetry\. This transition is associated with transcriptional silencing and increased DNA methylation of Lcyc, a CYCLOIDEA\-like gene involved in dorsoventral floral development\. Although the molecular association between the Lcyc epiallelic state and floral architecture is well established, a general framework for expressing differences between such methylation states in information\-theoretic units has not been developed\. Methods We developed an information\-theoretic framework in which potentially methylatable cytosines are represented as Bernoulli variables\. Because experimental cytosine\-level count data for the natural Lcyc epiallele were not available for direct reanalysis, the numerical demonstration uses a synthetic, literature\-constrained methylation matrix designed to reproduce the qualitative pattern reported for wild\-type and peloric Lcyc \. The framework quantifies maximum binary capacity, summed site\-wise Shannon entropy, directional Kullback–Leibler divergence, summed site\-wise Jensen–Shannon divergence, context\-specific contributions, and site\-wise dimensionality\. Results In the synthetic demonstration matrix, maximum binary capacity was 120 bits, summed site\-wise entropy was 39\.85 bits for the modeled wild\-type state and 101\.32 bits for the modeled peloric state, directional Kullback–Leibler divergence was 260\.30 bits, and summed site\-wise Jensen–Shannon divergence was 42\.31 bits\. These numerical values characterize the illustrative matrix under its specified assumptions and should not be interpreted as empirical estimates of the natural Lcyc epiallele\. Rather, they demonstrate how cytosine\-level methylation profiles can be translated into measures of uncertainty, statistical distinguishability, methylation\-context contribution, and the distribution of divergence across a locus\.

## [Quasi\-site\-specific probabilistic prediction of clay compression index with limited site data using SSM\-NGBayes model](../publications/c075eac51aadb17691ed.md)

Dianqing Li; Qin Ke; Xiao\-Song Tang; Sun Zi\-han; Hao Sun; Zheng Yu\-he

Clay data are typically multivariate, uncertain, site\-unique, sparse, and potentially anomalous\. These induce great challenges to data\-driven clay compression index \(Cc\) prediction\. To overcome these challenges, outlier detection by subsample scoring method \(SSM\), generic data learning by Natural Gradient Boosting \(NGBoost\) and site data learning by Bayesian approach are integrated in this study for quasi\-site\-specific probabilistic prediction of Cc\. In this methodology, SSM divides the clay data into univariate, bivariate and multivariate subspaces and constructs corresponding subsamples, then three base detectors are employed for subsample outlier detection and the obtained scores are collectively used to identify outlier samples\. Afterwards, NGBoost\-based probabilistic model is established by learning from the generic data, and its hyperparameters are optimised using a novel prediction interval\-oriented objective function\. The NGBoost model predictions on the site data are then served as prior information about Cc\. Finally, the Bayesian approach is adopted to produce posterior prediction of Cc based on the prior information and the observed site data\. This prior\-posterior prediction model named NGBayes model is validated on a global clay dataset\. Results show that the proposed SSM is more robust than traditional multivariate outlier detection methods by considering additional spaces\. The prior knowledge learned by the NGBoost model is highly informative, and it outperforms other probabilistic machine learning models in both mean prediction accuracy and prediction interval quality\. Moreover, the proposed SSM\-NGBayes prediction model exhibits satisfactory performance on various sites with limited data\.

## [The Eschatology of Light Cones: Cosmological Event Horizons, Existential Risk Mitigation, and the Metaphysics of Divine Judgment in 2 Peter 3:10](../publications/c077b2dd9d7f11cf30ce.md)

Edward Sitepu; Milisi Sembiring; Lasmawati Situmorang; Yonas Muanley

Modern physical cosmology, particularly the standard Lambda\-Cold Dark Matter \(ΛCDM\) framework, describes a universe in which accelerated expansion can establish cosmological event horizons and progressively restrict causal communication between sufficiently distant gravitationally unbound regions\. In long\-term existential\-risk analysis, this raises a provocative possibility: distributing civilization across increasingly independent causal domains could reduce the probability that one localized catastrophe destroys every descendant population\. This article examines whether such a physical strategy has any relevance to the eschatological claim of 2 Peter 3:10\. Through interdisciplinary textual\-critical exegesis, theological metaphysics, philosophy of causation, and a formal comparison of risk models, the study argues that cosmological isolation and eschatological judgment belong to different explanatory categories\. Event horizons constrain causal influence within spacetime; they do not constitute metaphysical barriers against a theological claim about the Creator’s judgment upon creation\. The argument is qualified in two directions\. First, ΛCDM is treated as a physical model rather than an unquestionable forecast of the universe’s ultimate destiny\. Second, divine action should not be described as a measurable faster\-than\-light signal, because doing so would incorrectly turn a theological doctrine of divine sovereignty into a physical mechanism\. The central thesis is therefore not that God “travels faster than light,” but that the explanatory scope of light cones is limited to physical causal relations within spacetime\. The article compares three readings of 2 Peter 3:10—cosmic dissolution, transformative judgment, and localized/biospheric judgment—and shows that only the third creates a possible conceptual space in which spatial dispersion might matter\. The theological conclusion is that eschatological security is not achieved through maximal cosmic distance but through the promise of “new heavens and a new earth” in which righteousness dwells \(2 Pet\. 3:13\)\.

## [Quantitative CT in the real\-world evaluation of progressive pulmonary fibrosis; the REVISE PPF multicentre observational study](../publications/c083098b7cb5028ba33f.md)

Ayodeji Adegunsoye; Anna J\. Podolanczuk; Teja Kulkarni; Christian Rennison\-Jones; Steven Rothenberg; Kristin Berger; YANA RABKOVA; Christine Wu; Lydia Chelala; Cathryn T\. RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVE: We assessed whether an FDA\-cleared quantitative CT \(qCT\) tool \(Brainomix, e\-Lung\) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis \(PPF\) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers\. METHODS: Multicentre retrospective study involving University of Alabama \(UAB\), Weill Cornell Medicine \(WCM\) and University of Chicago \(UChicago\); n = 509\. Prespecified progression thresholds were an absolute WRVS increase of ≥ 3 percentage points, an absolute TDE increase of ≥ 1\.5 percentage points, and a relative e\-Lung Volume decline of ≥ 10%, over less than 2 years\. RESULTS: Among 200 patients with PPF and serial HRCTs meeting the prespecified timing criterion, qCT identified progression earlier in 78% \(UAB\), 83% \(WCM\), and 47% \(UChicago\), with mean lead times of 434, 847, and 220 days, respectively\. Among 187 clinically stable patients meeting the same serial\-imaging criterion, progression thresholds were met in 67%, 56%, and 42%, respectively\. High\-risk baseline WRVS \(≥15%\) predicted future PPF \(OR 4\.09, 2\.48, and 2\.30\) and mortality \(HR 2\.03 pooled UAB/WCM; 2\.75 UChicago\)\. Per 1\-percentage\-point increase, adjusted mortality HRs were 1\.15 and 1\.19 for WRVS and 1\.05 and 1\.04 for TDE in pooled UAB/WCM and UChicago, respectively\. Threshold crossings were also associated with mortality \(WRVS: HR 6\.50 pooled UAB/WCM, 4\.05 UChicago; TDE: 7\.60 and 3\.26; e\-Lung Volume: 8\.20 and 2\.59\)\. CONCLUSION: qCT detects radiological progression months to years before clinical PPF diagnoses\. Integrating e\-Lung into ILD pathways could accelerate treatment decisions and personalize follow\-up\.

## [Bioactive Goat Milk Innovation for Lipstick and Lip Balm](../publications/c0862635ea811910d962.md)

Nicholas Renaldo; Achmad Tavip Junaedi; Nyoto Nyoto; Suhardjo Suhardjo; Marice Br Hutahuruk; Muhammad Pringgo Prayetno; Arih Dwi Prihastomo; Affilla Fetty Anggraheni; NIM\. 17105010058 INTAN PURNAMA; Luciana Fransisca

The growing demand for natural\-ingredient cosmetics creates opportunities to transform agricultural and livestock\-based resources into innovative, value\-added products\. This study proposes Bioactive Goat Milk Innovation for Lipstick and Lip Balm, an initiative to develop goat milk\-derived ingredients for two lip care applications\. The research employs an experimental development approach involving raw material preparation, formulation design, manufacturing, and product validation\. Goat milk powder is proposed as a characteristic ingredient, combined with cosmetic\-grade waxes, oils, butters, and approved pigments\. The lip balm formulation focuses on lip conditioning and moisture protection, while the lipstick formulation combines conditioning properties with decorative color\. Product evaluation will include organoleptic characteristics, homogeneity, physical performance, ingredient compatibility, microbiological quality, stability, packaging compatibility, and user acceptability, subject to appropriate safety requirements\. As the formulations have not yet been experimentally validated, product performance and commercial feasibility remain to be established\. The innovation has the potential to diversify goat milk utilization beyond conventional dairy products, create additional value for livestock producers, and support entrepreneurship at the intersection of livestock production and the cosmetics industry\. This research may also provide a foundation for future investigations into the potential role of goat milk\-derived bioactive ingredients in protecting lip tissue against oxidative stress and UV\-induced damage associated with lip cancer, although any cancer\-preventive effects must be established through rigorous scientific testing\. Further laboratory validation, regulatory assessment, and economic evaluation are required to determine its suitability for commercialization\.
